11166116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11166116.value: Vagal nerve stimulation (VNS) has been shown to enhance memory and cognitive functions in humans and rats. A preliminary study has shown that VNS could influence decision-making in epileptic patients. Neuroimaging data using human subjects have indicated a critical role for the prefrontal cortex and amygdala in selecting proper actions and calculating the expected value of loss- or gain-related, outcomes. Published data in rats suggested that the decision-making performances were relying on the functional integrity of the basolateral amygdala (BLA) and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). In this project we establish a rat model to monitor the effect of VNS on decision making using rat gambling task (RGT) and characterize the electrophysiological properties of ACC and BLA activated by VNS. We will show that moderate VNS does not affect rat’s general activity. VNS immediately following training sessions in RGT facilitates advantageous choices in rats that performed RGT. This animal study will provide evidence supporting the somatic marker hypothesis (SMH) that bioregulatory processes, including those that express themselves in emotions and feelings (somatic states), do play a role in influencing decisions. Brain neuronal oscillations play a basic role in coordinated activity, the field potential oscillations modulate local spike timing, and moreover, the theta band (frequencies among 4 and 10 Hz) has been acknowledged for a wide span of cognitive functions. Given the fact that synchronously discharging cells are more effective at driving neurons at subsequent processing stages next we will perform multi-electrodes recording of neural spike and local field potential (LFP) from neuronal ensembles in ACC and BLA simultaneously with RGT in behavioral animal to explore the neural mechanisms underlying the VNS-induced facilitation of decision making. First, we will identify the plasticity in the BLA-ACC synapse and demonstrate that VNS enhances synaptic transmission in this pathway. Then, we will clarify the spike field (theta oscillation) coherence and phase locking in BLA and ACC. Finally, cross-correlation analysis will show that VNS induces enhancements of synchronization between LFPs recorded in ACC and BLA, in particularly, in the theta range, which is consistent with an increase of neuronal communication between the two regions. Combination of multiple electrophysiological recording with rat gambling task in behavioral models in vivo should facilitate to identifying the putative mechanisms underlying the therapeutic VNS in cognitive impairment.

11166116.label: Realisation of objectives
11166116.value: We performed studies of implantation of vagus nerve cuff Electrode and implantation of recording electrodes. The Rat Gambling Task (RGT) has been developed to test the decision-making capacities of rats via a conflict between immediate and long-term gratification (food reward). During the training stage, rats gradually learned the association between the nose-poke action and the release of a food pellet. Electrical vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) was given to rats immediately after training10. Rats were free to make choices between four apertures (A–D), however, different choices were associated with different outcomes. The percentage of advantageous choices ((C + D)/(A + B + C + D) × 100%) made during the last 20 min and the food rewards obtained across the test were used to identify the decision-making behavior of rats. The average food intake per body weight was not significantly different between the two groups. The average body weights were not significantly different between the two groups and no difference was detected in the general activity - number of nose-pokes per min - (VNS, 11.37 ± 0.54 vs. control, 11.66 ± 0.44; t test, t(63) = 0.93, p > 0.05) or motivation (VNS, 25.96 ± 0.46 min vs. control, 25.75 ± 0.16 min; t test, t(63) = 0.25, p > 0.05, Fig. 1b) between two groups. The performance of the control rats and rats with VNS during the RGT test showed that. good decision-makers indicates those rats who chose randomly at first, then orientated their preference progressively toward more advantageous options and ended up making more than 70% advantageous choices during the last 20 min. Conversely, poor decision-makers developed a stable preference for the adverse options, making less than 30% advantageous selections during the last 20 min of the test. The number of choices of each option (A, B, C, D) of each rat are shown in Table 1 in the Supplementary Information as the percentages of advantageous choices during last 20 min. In the VNS group, the proportion of good decision-makers increased compared with the controls (VNS, n = 31 (83.7%) vs. control, n = 16 (57.1%)). The difference in the proportions of the three types of decision-making behavior (good, bad, undecided) between the two groups was significant (Mann-Whitney U test, U = 380.00, p = 0.018). The mean food reward obtained during the RGT by the VNS rats was significantly more than that of the controls (VNS, 206.0 ± 8.57 vs. control, 152.1 ± 6.09). Electrophysiological studies showed that VNS augmented theta activity. No significant changes in power were observed in the other frequency bands. Therefore, these data revealed that only theta band activity was influenced following VNS, suggesting that VNS affected the theta frequency band activity related to cognitive functions in basolateral amygdala (BLA) and (anterior cingulate cortex) (ACC). In the current study, spike-field coherence (SFC) was used to quantify the alteration in the spike timing-LFP relationship within the BLA and ACC before and after VNS. The SFC value is expressed in percentage and varies as a function of frequency. The SFC takes values from 0% to 100%, with 100% indicating all spikes follow a particular phase of oscillation in this frequency, while 0% reflects spikes firing completely at random. There were 71 neurons recorded in the BLA of 6 rats, including 5 neurons have spike(s) within 2 ms refractory period, and the mean percentage of spikes was 2.10% ± 0.32% within 2 ms (n = 5). The SFC distributions for various frequencies are presented in Fig. 3. We found a significant difference in the average SFC after VNS in the theta range (t(69) = 5.112, p < 0.001). SFC values were increased in the theta band from 2.028 ± 0.1669 before VNS to 3.214 ± 0.1804 after VNS. No significant changes were observed in the other three frequency bands. 60 neurons recorded in the ACC were used to calculate the SFC within the ACC. The mean percentage of spikes was 2.25% ± 0.23% within 2 ms (n = 4). No significant change was found in the theta band (t(58) = 0.456, p > 0.05). These results suggest that spike-field coherence in the theta band oscillations is changed in BLA after VNS. Moreover, we detected increased proportion of neurons phase-locked to theta oscillations within the BLA following VNS. As expected, we found that 22.5% of neurons fired spikes randomly to the phase of the LFP oscillations in the theta range before VNS and became phase-locked to the theta oscillations following VNS. The frequency with the maximal phase-locking in the Rayleigh test was 4.75 Hz. Example phase distributions of a neuron un-phase-locked before VNS and phase-locked after VNS are presented as polar-histograms. The un-phase-locked neuron displayed random firing. However, this neuron became phase-locked after VNS and showed most spikes firing close to 120° of the theta cycle with a mean-phase at 150°. Before VNS, 56.3% (40 of 71 neurons) showed phase-locking close to the trough of theta oscillation (Fig. 4c). In contrast, a significantly increased proportion of neurons (78.8%, 56 of 71 neurons, t(19) = 3.559, p < 0.01) showed phase-locking to the theta range following VNS. Together, the results indicate VNS causes an increase in the concentration of the distribution of the neuronal spikes in relation to the phase of the ongoing LFPs within the BLA. Finally, to further examine the functional connectivity between the ACC and BLA, we compared the LFP during 30 s spontaneous periods from before and after VNS in rats. Time-varying power spectra analysis revealed that the dispersed neuronal activities in the ACC and BLA became concentrated in the theta band following VNS. Cross-correlation analysis allows quantitative evaluation of the synchronization of activities in the LFP. We showed increased synchronization of theta activities in the ACC and BLA after VNS.

11166116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11166116.value: By employing a conscious rat model equipped with vagus nerve cuff electrode, we assess the role of chronic VNS on decision-making in rat gambling task (RGT). Simultaneous multichannel-recordings offer an ideal setup to test the hypothesis that VNS may induce alterations of in both spike-field-coherence and synchronization of theta oscillations across brain areas in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and basolateral amygdala (BLA). Daily VNS, administered immediately following training sessions of RGT, caused an increase in ‘good decision-maker’ rats. Neural spikes in the ACC became synchronized with the ongoing theta oscillations of local field potential (LFP) in BLA following VNS. Moreover, cross-correlation analysis revealed synchronization between the ACC and BLA. Our results provide specific evidence that VNS facilitates decision-making and unveils several important roles for VNS in regulating LFP and spike phases, as well as enhancing spike-phase coherence between key brain areas involved in cognitive performance. These data may serve to provide fundamental notions regarding neurophysiological biomarkers for therapeutic VNS in cognitive impairment.

11166116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11166116.value: Our behavioral animal, moderate VNS following training sessions facilitates decision making in rats. In parallel, we observed greater phase locking of the theta oscillations in the BLA to the ACC spikes immediately following VNS. Our findings suggest that theta synchrony may reveal more proficient trial and receive during gambling task training, and might also help endorse information into memory. These data are consistent with the theory that oscillatory synchrony, and particularly phase synchronization, is an overall principle for integrating information between different cortical and subcortical areas during complex cognitive processing. The data may serve as a basis to develop fundamental notions regarding neurophysiologic biomarkers for therapeutic VNS in cognitive impairment. Based these impotent findings our further studies will performed to identify the role of vagal afferent C-fibers in the mediation of Cholecystokinin-octapeptide (CCK)’s action on learned behavior that directly reflects the affective component of visceral pain.

11166116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11166116.value: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) can enhance cognitive functions in both rats and humans. Clinical studies have shown that VNS influences decision-making in epileptic patients. Neuroimaging data in humans have indicated a critical role for the prefrontal cortex and amygdala in decision-making. Studies in rats suggested that the decision-making performances rely on the basolateral amygdala (BLA) and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). In the current study, we established a rat model equipped with vagus nerve cuff electrode to assess the role of chronic VNS on decision-making in the Rat Gambling Task (RGT), and characterize the electrophysiological properties of the ACC and BLA. Electrophysiological brain recordings were used to test the hypothesis that VNS may alter neuronal activity across the ACC and BLA. Daily VNS administered immediately following training sessions of RGT caused an increase in ‘good decision-maker’ rats. It was found that neural activity in the ACC became synchronized with that in the BLA following VNS. Our results provide specific evidence that VNS facilitates decision-making and unveils the important role for VNS in regulating neural activity between key brain areas involved in cognitive performance.

11166316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11166316.value: The reciprocally interconnected network between the thalamus and cortex has been proposed to play an important role in memory consolidation during slow wave sleep, a phase of sleep where the network are dominated by high frequency bursts of spike firing. Nonetheless, evidence of memory related changes in thalamic neuronal activities is scarce. In several recent experiments, we found that the neuronal plasticity and long-term potentiation (LTP) in the auditory cortex are through cholecystokinin (CCK, ref 1). No corticocortical LTP, no thalamocortical LTP and no hippocampal LTP can be induced on CCK knockout mice. In the preliminary experiments using CCK-cre mouse and AAV-Dio-mCherry injection in the auditory cortex, we found that corticothalamic fibers/terminals are CCK-immunopositive. High-frequency stimulation of the auditory cortex could facilitate long-term auditory responses in the medial geniculate body (MGB). Based on the results of these experiments, we hypothesize that the auditory cortex can regulate synaptic plasticity and induce LTP in the MGB. The burst firing during slow wave sleep can function as an electrophysiological switch to enable the synaptic release of CCK and thus a lasting potentiation of corticothalamic fibers which will facilitate auditory memory of behavioural context cues during the wake state. In the proposed study, we will undertake four sets of experiments to further validate and test our hypothesis and address the following questions: 1) Whether specific pattern of stimulation of the corticotalamic neurons/fibers via electrical bursts are required for the induction of LTP in the MGB. 2) Whether selective activation of discrete sets of corticothalamic fibers through implanted optic fibers can induce LTP after AAV-DIO -ChR2-eYFP is injected into deep layers of the auditory cortex of CCK-Cre mouse. 3) By using the same pairing paradigm[1], we will examine whether tetanus burst stimulation of the cortex followed by auditory stimulus can facilitate the long-term auditory response in the thalamus. As the preliminary results were positive, we further hypothesize that consecutive pairings of the cortical stimulation and auditory stimuli in vivo will induce long-term changes for weeks in the thalamic tonotopic organization. The long-term impacts of the present study are two-fold. Corticothalamic plasticity would enable the thalamus to adapt based on the changing environment needs. The proposed experiments would unveil the mechanism leading to such plasticity. This study linking the high-frequency burst firing with the neuronal plasticity may also add on an important piece of the puzzle to unveil the mechanism how the thalamocortical oscillation facilitates the memory consolidation. 丘腦和皮層之間的相互投射的網絡在慢波睡眠過程中對記憶整固具有重要作用。在慢波睡眠過程中有一睡眠階段此網絡是由穗射擊高頻放電為主。但在丘腦神經元活動和記憶相關的證據是稀缺的。在最近的幾個實驗中，我們發現，內側顳葉可以通過膽囊收縮素（CCK）的釋放來調製聽覺皮層的神經元的可塑性，並引起長時程增強（LTP）。長時程增強是記憶的表現。在CCK敲除小鼠的無法誘導皮層到皮層 LTP，丘腦到皮層LTP，以及海馬的LTP。 在使用CCK-CRE小鼠注射AAV-DIO-mCherry到聽覺皮層的初步實驗中，我們發現，皮層丘腦纖維是CCK免疫陽性。我們還發現，聽覺皮層的高頻刺激可長期增強在聽覺丘腦，內側膝狀體聽覺​​反應。 基於這些實驗的結果，我們推測聽覺皮層可以調節內側膝狀體的突觸可塑性並誘導LTP。慢波睡眠期間突發放電可以作為一個電開關，以促進CCK的突觸釋放。皮層丘腦纖維的LTP將有利於在清醒狀態期間的聽覺記憶在睡眠過程中得以整固並起到持久保存的作用。 在我們提案的研究中，將進行四組試驗，以進一步驗證和檢驗我們的假設並解決以下問題：1）是否需要特定的放電模式來誘導皮層至丘腦神經元的LTP。 2）在聽覺皮層的第五層注入AAV-DIO -ChR2-EYFPCCK-CRE小鼠上，我們是否可以通過選擇性用激光來激活皮層丘腦纖維的辦法誘導出丘腦的LTP。 3）我們將研究皮層的突發刺激是否能夠促進丘腦對接下來的聽覺刺激反應。 4），我們將鑑定皮質的高頻激活和聽覺刺激的配對能否誘發在丘腦頻率特性的長期變化。 皮層丘腦可塑性將使丘腦根據環境需要適應。我們提案的實驗將揭開導致這種可塑性的機制。這項研究把高頻刺激與神經可塑性聯繫在一起，也可以增加我們對揭開丘腦振盪如何促進了記憶的鞏固的機制。

11166316.label: Realisation of objectives
11166316.value: Objective 1. We inserted a recording electrode array into the MGB (0.5-1.0 MΩ, FHC Inc.), obtaining a frequency-response function and the best frequency for a recorded neuron, selected the electrode for recording. And then we placed low impedance electrodes (<100kΩ, FHC Inc.) in the AC, then found the best stimulation location with similar best frequency in the auditory cortex, chose the electrode for stimulation electrode. Field excitatory postsynaptic potential (fEPSP) to the cortical electrical stimulation of different currents in the ACx was measured. Baseline recording of neuronal responses in both fEPSP and single-unit spikes to the cortical stimulation (with interstimulus interval of 10 s) were made in the MGB before. Next, HFS (8-s stimulation interval after 2-s HFS, 100Hz) were delivered to the auditory cortex for 40 s. After the HFS, neuronal responses to the cortical stimulation were recorded for more than 60 min. HFS induced a small yet significant LTP in the mice. The slope of fEPSPs that was measured 1 h after the HFS was potentiated by 6.7 ± 2.5% compared to the baseline before the HFS (p<0.05, N=11 mice). LFS (low frequency stimulation) could not induce corticothalamic LTP. Though the corticofugal LTP on the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) is not a subject of the present study, it is likely the LTP were also produced on the TRN neurons. TRN imposed inhibitory inputs on MGB neurons. Overall, the LTP detected in MGB was minimal but statistically significant. Objective 2. To exclude the possible TRN effect, we next used optogenetic methods to stimulate the corticothalamic fibers in the MGB only. In this experiment we examined whether corticothalamic LTP induced by using optogenetic methods on CCK-CRE mice. Viral vectors and stereotaxic surgeries for optogenetic approaches. AAV9-CaMKIIa-DIO-ChrimsonR-mCerry-WPRE-pA (Taitool) were used in this study for optical activation of the corticothalamic CCK-positive projection. CCK-cre mice were subjects in this objective. We infused the virus into deep layers of the auditory cortex. Mice could recover for 6 weeks during which the virus can effectively infect the neocortical projection fibers of the auditory cortex. fEPSP to the laser stimulation of different intensity in the MGB was measured. We adopted the intensity that evoked 40% of the maximal fEPSP as the testing current and 80% as the HFS intensity. Baseline recording of neuronal responses in both fEPSP and single-unit spikes to the Laser stimulation in the MGB. Next, HFLS (8-s stimulation interval after 2-s HFS, 50Hz) were delivered to MGB for 40 s. After the HFLS, neuronal responses to the laser stimulation were recorded for more than 60 min. The slope of fEPSPs that was measured 1 h after the HFLS was potentiated by 23.7±5.8% compared to the baseline before the HFLS (One-way ANOVA; 100.9±3.6% vs. 124.6±5.4 %, before vs. after HFLS; pairwise comparison, p<0.01, n=7). The potentiation induced by HFLS are greater than cortical HFS (23.7±5.8% vs. 6.7 ± 2.5%), indicating that the TRN effect were excluded. Objective 3. fEPSP to different intensity of sound and cortical electrical stimulation in the ACx was measured. We adopted the sound intensity that evoked 40% of the maximal fEPSP as the probe acoustic stimulus and 80% of the current that evoked the maximal fEPSP as the HFS current. Baseline recording of neuronal responses in both fEPSP and single-unit spikes to the acoustic stimulation. Next, HFS that is paired with acoustic stimuli (One burst of HFS, 100Hz × 5 pulses, paired with 5 acoustic stimuli in 1 Hz) will be delivered to the auditory cortex for 4 times in 0.1Hz. After the HFS, neuronal responses to the acoustic stimulation were recorded for more than 60 min. The Amplitude of fEPSPs that was measured 1 h after the HFS was potentiated by 36.6±6.0% compared to the baseline before the HFS (One-way ANOVA; 101.5±2.6% vs. 140.1±5.3%, before vs. after HFS; pairwise comparison, p<0.001, N=10 mice). LFS could not induce corticothalamic LTP (N.S., N=10). HFS of the ACx enables the LTP of ascending acoustic signal transmission in the MGB. The next step we examined whether corticofugal pathway exert influence on ascending acoustic signal transmission via CCK-positive projections by using optogenetic methods on CCK-CRE mice. Baseline recording of neuronal responses in both fEPSP and single-unit spikes to the auditory stimulation in the MGB. Next, HFLS that is paired with acoustic stimuli (One burst of HFLS, 100Hz × 5 pulses, paired with 5 acoustic stimuli in 1 Hz) were delivered to the MGB for 4 times in 0.1Hz. Then the neuronal responses to the acoustic stimulation were recorded for more than 60 min. As we expected, the Amplitude of fEPSPs that was measured 1 h after the HFS was potentiated by 63.9±15.3% compared to the baseline before the HFLS (One-way ANOVA; 101.4±3.8%vs. 165.3±15.0%, before vs. after HFLS; pairwise comparison, p<0.001, n=7). LFLS could not induce corticothalamic LTP (N.S., n=7). HF stimulation of the corticofugal CCK-positive pathway enables the LTP of ascending acoustic signal transmission in the MGB. From above results, we can infer that HF activation of the corticothalamic pathway exert much more influence on the ascending acoustic signal transmission in MGB than itself. Objective 4. We anesthetized the mouse, injected CCK8 and then delivered a supra-threshold tone stimulus for 200 trails. The tuning curves of the auditory neurons were measured before and after the intervention. CCK-8 did not cause the shift the characteristic frequency (CF) of the tuning curve to the frequency of the exposed tone. The responding threshold was significantly lowered to the frequencies near the exposed tone in the range with one octave in the auditory cortex of the experimental group with the CCK8 infusion, while the responding threshold was not lowered to any frequencies near the exposed tone in the shame control group with ACSF infusion (8.66±1.91dB at exposed frequency, p<0.001; 6.66±2.32dB P<0.001 and 5.33±1.33 dB, p< 0.05 at frequencies of 0.4 octave lower and 0.4 octave higher than the exposed frequency respectively; CCK, n=15; ACSF n=12, two-way ANOVA, p<0.001, post hoc: Tukey test, CCK-8S vs. ACSF, *p<0.05, **p<0.001), suggesting that the application of CCK-8 and the sound exposure induced LTP and led to the lowered response threshold near the exposed tone. In the next experiment, we adopted a prepulse inhibition acoustic startle test to examine the animal’s ability in frequency discrimination and long-term tonotopic reorganization. The prepulse inhibition (PPI) level indicates how well the animals perceive the frequency differences between the background tone and prepulse tone. The higher PPI means the mouse can differentiate the two frequencies better. Both CCK-8S and ACSF infused mice were exposed to tone stimulations (9.8 or 16.4 kHz) in a soundproof chamber immediately after the infusion. The frequency discrimination ability was tested by comparing the PPIs between the two groups at 24 h after exposure. The differences between the experimental and the control groups mainly appeared at the frequencies near the exposed frequency. The PPI showed a significant difference in detecting the prepulse tone with the 2% difference from the background tone. The PPI difference for both exposed frequencies reached > 18.8% when the difference of the exposed frequency and the prepulse frequency was 2%). This result indicates that CCK infusion and tone exposure at anesthesia enhanced ability for frequency discrimination near the frequency of the exposed tone and induced animal’s long-term tonotopic reorganization

11166316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11166316.value: During this report period, we unveiled the emerging role of a certain type of neuropeptide, cholecystokinin (CCK), originated from entorhinal cortex (EC) in the modulation of neural plasticity in many brain regions, including auditory cortex, hippocampus (Su et al., 2020) al and lateral amygdala (Feng, 2019). The transgenic CCK-knockout mutant mice show deficits in both electrophysiological and behavioral aspects, including the induction failure corticocortical LTP, thalamocortical LTP hippocampal LTP and the impairment in spatial memory, sound-sound associative memory and fear memory formation (Chen et al., 2019; Feng et al.,2020; Su et al., 2020). On the other hand, we found that the classical LTP induction protocol, theta burst stimulation, or tetanus burst stimulation (TBS), can induce the release of CCK from entorhinal projection terminals; And the endogenous or exogenous application of CCK both can induced LTP without TBS (Chen et al., 2019). In the present study, we hypothesized that CCK, which is expressed in the ACx, plays an essential role in enabling auditory long-term potentiation in the thalamus. We show here for the first time the HFS induced corticothalamic LTP in the MGB with in-vivo preparation. It seems that the cortical HFS could also induced LTP on the TRN neurons, which imposed inhibitory inputs on MGB neurons. In general, the LTP detected in MGB was minimal but statistically significant. To exclude the possible TRN effect, we next used optogenetic methods to stimulate the corticothalamic fibers in the MGB only. HF stimulation of the corticofugal CCK-positive pathway enables the LTP of ascending acoustic signal transmission in the MGB (Li et al., 2020). From above results, we can infer that HF activation of the corticothalamic pathway exert much more influence on the ascending acoustic signal transmission than itself. It suggested corticofugal fibers enable long-term modulation of ascending signal transmission via its CCK (Li et al., 2020). Our behavioral experiments showed that CCK infusion significantly increased the frequency discrimination ability by facilitating salubrious plastic changes induced by the passive tone exposure in adult animals. CCK induced plasticity may provide a possible treatment plan which can be applied to enhance the function of late cochlear implants in prelingually deaf children. We are developing CCKBR agonists for the purpose (Zhang et al., 2020). Our findings could be generalized in different sensory modalities, including, but not limited to perception, learning, and memory formation (Su et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2020)

11166316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11166316.value: Thalamus is important in relaying sensory information to cortex. In this study, we explored the role of corticothalamic induced MGB potentiation on thalamocortical transmission. CCK is essential in enabling auditory LTP in thalamus. It has been believed that reciprocal interconnection between cortex and thalamus is important in memory consolidation during slow wave sleep (SWS). In this certain phase of sleep, the neurals is dominated by high frequency bursts of spike firing. But how the thalamus cortex modulates neural plasticity is still unclear. Based on our findings, we believe that the burst firing during SWS can function as an electrophysiological switch to enable synaptic release of CCK. Thus a lasting potentiation of corticothalamic fibers will facilitate auditory memory of behavioral context cues during wake state. CCK-induced plasticity may provide a possible treatment plan which can be applied to enhance late cochlear implants performance in prelingual children. Neuroplasticity induced by the administration of cholecystokinin tetrapeptide and noise exposure can become a novel strategy for tinnitus treatment. Cholecystokinin administration also could lastingly rescue thalamocortical neuroplasticity. Thalamocortical plasticity not only participates in the refinement of the sensory cortices but also learning processes. Thus, our findings may involve different sensory modalities like perception, learning and memory.

11166316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11166316.value: Here, we investigated whether and how corticothalamic fibers modulated ascending acoustic signal transmission by its cholecystokinin (CCK). We found that a small yet significant corticothalamic LTP can be induced by High frequency stimulation of the corticofugal CCK fibers. And then the corticothalamic LTP facilitated ascending signal transmission in the MGB. CCK injection enhanced ability for frequency discrimination and induced animal’s long-term tonotopic reorganization.

11200116.label: Project Objectives
11200116.value: 1(a). To investigate multiclass classification for fast mode decision in HEVC. Video compression efficiency is improved by selecting the optimal mode from dozens of candidates for a coding module. To achieve this effectively and efficiently, the mode decision processes with multiple candidates can be modeled as multiclass classification problems (see Fig.2) and solved in a unified learning based framework (see Fig.1), where video blocks and mode candidates are treated as samples and classes. The goal is to develop learning based coding framework, explore multiclass classification for effective mode decision in HEVC, assign the number of classes and importance according to their similarities and distributions, develop decision strategies and model the cost/gain of the prediction for each class, so as to maximize decision efficiency and adaptability in diverse video contents. 1(b). To investigate recursive decision problems in HEVC. The CU decision and multi-layer joint optimization can be formulated as recursive classification with a multi-level hierarchical decision structure (see Fig.2). The mode candidates among different levels are inter-correlated and dependent, which lead to a conditional probability of neighboring levels. In addition, the increasing number of classes requires more powerful multiclass classifiers and comprehensive decision structures. The cost/gain of false/correct prediction shall be modeled in order to reasonably allocate the coding resources (e.g., bits, coding complexity and visual quality) among different decision levels and optimize the overall performance. 2(a). To explore effective features for the classification problems in HEVC. Representative features need to be explored for the multiclass classification problems modeled from the mode decision in HEVC. Feature extraction from raw video sequences and coding processes is required for bridging the gap between the video contents and the output modes. To explore useful information for a classification problem, feature selection is performed to construct a compact feature subset, and meanwhile adapt to diverse video contents and reduce the complexity overheads. Additionally, sample selection can be achieved by active learning so as to further reduce data redundancy and adapt to large-scale sample classification. 2(b). To develop effective learning schemes for HEVC. After feature construction, an effective learning scheme is desired to solve the classification problems in HEVC. Fuzzy rough set approaches with membership degrees are adopted, which construct multiclass classifiers with fuzzy outputs and soft boundaries. The robustness and adaptability of individual classifiers should be considered, so as to investigate the effectiveness of the learning algorithm. Finally, ensemble scheme can be employed by making use of multiple classifiers.

11200116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200116.value: High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) has attracted much attention due to the increasing need of compressing large-scale video data for storage and streaming over networks. It doubles the compression efficiency at the same video quality compared to its predecessor H.264/AVC standard, and demonstrates a great potential for High Definition (HD) video markets, such as IMAX movies, immersive video conferences, surveillance, ultra HDTV and 3D-TV. To achieve higher compression efficiency, HEVC divides video to a sequence of frames and subsequently partitions it into a number of smaller blocks size from 64x64 to 4x4 for better compression efficiency. This kind of partitioning can generally refer to mode decision problems in HEVC. The mode decision problems aim to minimize the bit rate as well to maximize the video quality based on a user designed rate distortion metric in HEVC, which are extremely complex and with high computational cost as they need to exhaust all the possible choices in order to come up with the optimal solution. Hand-crafted features and statistical-based methods are commonly used but they can hardly adapt to rapid change of the demands of today’s video especially with the dramatic increase of mode choices in HEVC and beyond. In this research, we propose a new unified framework based on learning which aims to resolve the mode decision problems in HEVC. Firstly, the mode decision processes in HEVC will be formulated as multiclass classification and recursive decision problems, and a machine learning based encoder framework and solutions will be developed, which tend to address future extensions of the coding standards. Secondly, representative features will be explored for the classification problems; feature selection and sample selection will be investigated to reduce data redundancy. Learning schemes will be developed to improve classification performance and adaptability in HEVC. This research will benefit large-scale video processing and boost the applications of HEVC for video transcoding, codec chip design, internet video, video communication and broadcasting, etc.

11200116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200116.value: High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) is the latest ongoing video coding standard developed by the Joint Collaborative Team on Video Coding (JCT-VC), which doubles the compression efficiency of H.264/MPEG-4 AVC high profile, i.e., half the transmission bit rate or storage space while maintaining the same video quality. SHVC, MV-HEVC and 3D-HEVC are the scalable, multiview and 3D extensions of HEVC standard, which aim to provide scalability, interactivity and high compression efficiency for streaming or 3D applications, respectively. In traditional model, the optimal mode among dozens of candidates for each module is selected by one-by-one sequential checking, which is extremely complex. To effectively reduce complexity, the determination of the optimal mode can be treated as a decision problem, which is prevalent in these coding modules and very challenging due to the diversity of video content and increasing number of modes. We have resolved this problem by developing a machine learning based framework which has been proved to be an effective method. Machine learning is a hotspot that has been widely applied to many application domains such as artificial intelligence, pattern recognition and signal processing. It learns from data of complex situations and gives the optimal discriminative solution. With this excellent property, this work proposed for machine learning based mode decision in H.264/AVC. The effectiveness of classification can then be fully exploited due to the lack of a general and optimal learning framework for these problems. Secondly, with the increase of mode candidates, more representative features are explored from the video content in order to improve the discriminability and reduce data redundancy.

11206216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206216.value: 自由立體顯示在過去的一個多世紀中已經成為重要的研究課題。它能為多個觀眾同時呈現雙目和運動視差，讓人們無需佩戴特殊的眼鏡便能看到3D圖像。在過去的十年中若干令人信服的系統已證實投影儀陣列非常適合用於自由立體顯示。但是，這種方法需要使用很多密集排列在一起的投影儀從各個不同的角度投影。這些系統成本高，設置複雜，校準費力，因此實現起來很有難度。迄今為止，還沒有相關研究提出在減少投影儀的數量的情況下，依然使投影儀陣列顯示系統保持較高的角度分辨率的方法。如果沒有這樣的方法，基於投影儀陣列的自由立體顯示系統就難以推廣，不能夠實際應用，因此也就無法對人們的生活帶來更大程度的潛在影響。 另一方面，高分辨率投影儀像素值的持續增長和價格的持續下降，使得將單個投影儀的影像分割成多個視圖成為可能，進而可以用單投影儀實現自由立體顯示。用鏡子陣列來配合實現該任務是簡單而有效的，而且使用鏡子陣列可以方便地重現密集排列的虛擬投影儀而不受真實投影儀的物理尺寸的限制，因此能夠使3D顯示系統具有很高的角度分辨率，這在現有的投影儀陣列中是難以實現的。本研究的主要挑戰是如何正確地設計一組鏡子陣列，在將投影儀光線準確地重新定向到顯示屏幕中心的同時保持不同的視角能夠觀察到不同影像的特性。我們需要設計一些方法來準確地認識不同的幾何參數之間如何相互影響以及相應的顯示效果，並且需要解決如何在有現實物理限制的約束條件下優化這些參數。 為了解決該問題，本研究將進行以下探索： a）設計相應的方法和幾何模型； b）用多種不同的配置來實現基於鏡子陣列的自由立體顯示系統； c）在實驗中驗證和評估我們提出的方法。 在我們提出的解決方案中，鏡子將會放在與橢球體相切的位置，投影儀和屏幕的中心則分別置於該橢球體的兩個焦點上。我們將會開發軟件工具包來自動生成優化的鏡子陣列模型，並直接應用3D打印等數字化製造手段來生產。 我們相信，這項研究將吸引研究者的注意力轉向利用折射反射的方法來實現自由立體顯示，這種方法是很有希望的，並且在許多方面還有很大的探索空間。本研究有很大的潛力擴展到其他應用中，比如在3D空間中增強現實、實時光場傳輸和遠程呈現，因此將會對3D顯示、人機交互和媒體藝術領域作出寶貴貢獻。

11206216.label: Realisation of objectives
11206216.value: All project objectives stated in the original application have been fully achieved. In particular, we have developed an ellipsoidal model which provides the mathematical foundation for designing the geometries of the horizontal parallax only (HPO), full parallax and 360 degrees viewable light field displays. The poses of system components, including the projector, the screen, and the mirrors, are defined by the ellipsoidal model. We have developed a parametric modeling tool to generate the 3D model of the light field display. User can easily re-configure the display settings to obtain the 3D geometry of the corresponding display. We have also experimentally verified our techniques by implementing several units of 3D displays and conducted user studies.

11206216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206216.value: In this project we have developed a set of methodologies to create a light field display using a single projector and an array of plane mirrors. Mirrors can reproduce densely arranged virtual projectors regardless of the physical size of the real projector, thus producing a light field display of very high ray density that is not achievable by real projector arrays. We propose an ellipsoidal geometric model and offset each row of mirrors to fully utilize both horizontal and vertical pixels of the projector in order to attain competitive ray density. We study the design space, formulate the system parameters, create a design pipeline, and implement the methods with parametric modelling to automate the generation of computer models of the mirror array for digital fabrication. Such high-density light field allows more than one ray depicting the same 3D point enters the pupil of the viewer’s eye at slightly different angles simultaneously, thus naturally driving the eye’s lens to focus at the depicted depth rather than the screen surface and thereby effectively alleviating the vergence-accommodation conflict (VAC), which is a very common problem of conventional stereoscopic and multiview 3D displays. We have conducted a user study to experimentally verify that the high-density light field generated by our display can evoke accommodation of the eye. We have reported these findings in Optics Express, a leading journal in optics. Bin CHEN, Lingyan RUAN and Miu-Ling LAM*, Light Field Display with Ellipsoidal Mirror Array and Single Projector, Optics Express, Vol. 27, Issue 15, pp. 21999-22016.

11206216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206216.value: This work has successfully obtained an award of US patent (US 10,869,022 B2). Our mirror array approach has a number of advantages over the conventional projector array approach, including low cost, flexible reconfiguration, simple setup and easy calibration. This work has high commercial potential. The mirror array light field displays can be applied in many application scenarios, such as computer-aided design, biomedical visualization, advertising, and creative art.

11206216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206216.value: In this work, we propose an easily reproducible and cost-effective approach to realize light field display. Viewers can perceive three-dimensionality without the need of wearing special glasses. We use a mirror array of special geometry to redirect light from a single, high-resolution projector. The optical paths of projector pixels reflected by the mirror array can be unfolded to mimic a large collection of rays projected from a dense array of virtual projectors in many different directions. Another powerful feature of the mirror array approach is the capability to create high ray density. High-density light field allows more than one ray depicting the same 3D point enters the pupil of the viewer’s eye at slightly different angles simultaneously, thus naturally driving the eye’s lens to focus at the depicted depth rather than the screen surface and thereby effectively alleviating the vergence-accommodation conflict (VAC), which is a very common problem of conventional stereoscopic and multiview 3D displays.

11207416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207416.value: Diamond, known as the hardest natural material in the world, is usually considered to be brittle and undeformable at bulk scale, however their mechanical properties at nanoscale were less studied. Recently, nanosized diamond structures, or nanodiamonds, have emerged as a new kind of carbon nanomaterials with many attractive applications in biomedicine, electronics, photonics etc., but the extremely low deformability and high brittleness of natural diamonds could potentially hinder their applications which involved larger deformations, such as flexible electronics and bio-nano interfaces. Despite that latest researches showed that diamonds’ hardness and toughness can be further improved by incorporating nanostructures (Nature 510, 250-253, 2014), such as nanocrystalline and nanotwinned structures, however, instead of being even harder, whether diamond could become more deformable, or even more elastic, while maintaining their high hardness/stiffness, should be of great practical and fundamental interests. In our preliminary investigations on diamond nanoneedles, a new form of one-dimensional (1-D) diamond nanostructures, we found that nanodiamonds could have significantly enhanced elasticity while maintained their ultrahigh strength. In addition, plastic deformation and enhanced hardness than that of bulk diamonds were also observed, while the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. So in this project, we aim to perform systematic nanomechanical study on various single/polycrystalline 1-D diamond nanostructures with well-defined orientations, geometries and loading mechanisms, assisted with our high-resolution in situ electron microscopy (SEM/TEM) characterization techniques. This project involved with three major parts, including the “rational fabrications of 1-D nanostructures of diamond with desired shape, dimensions and crystallographic orientation for different loading geometries”; “quantitative in situ nanomechanical characterizations of the as-fabricated single crystalline samples for their elastic and plastic deformation behavior”; and “investigation on the effects of nanocrystalline grain, nanotwin structure, loading rate/history, and doping in 1-D nanodiamonds as well as their respective influences on the plasticity and hardness”. The successful implementation of this project shall be of importance on the applications of 1-D diamond nanostructures in drug/gene delivery, nanophotonics and flexible electronics. The obtained quantitative insights can contribute to the deeper understanding on the mechanical behavior and deformation mechanisms of diamond cubic structured crystalline materials. The unprecedented mechanical properties, such as enhanced elasticity, of 1-D diamond nanostructures could also open up great opportunities for the emerging “elastic strain engineering” and many functional nanodevice applications. 作爲自然界最硬的材料，宏觀上鑽石通常被認爲是脆且不可變形的，然而他們在納米尺度下的力學性質則尚未被系統地研究。最近，納米尺寸的鑽石結構，或者叫納米鑽石，作爲一種新興的碳納米材料引起了越來越多研究者的關注，因爲他們所具有的在生物醫藥，電子學和光學方面的潛在應用。但是，極低的變形能力和高脆性，使得天然鑽石在這些潛在的需要大變形的應用領域，例如柔性電子器件，生物納米界面等的應用受到限制。因此，能否令鑽石變得更易變形，甚至具有彈性，將會具有十分重要的現實意義，也是很有意思的一個基礎科學問題。而在我們前期對鑽石納米針的研究中發現在納米尺度下鑽石具有顯著增強的彈性，並且維持其超高的強度。此外我們也發現其塑性形變的可能。所以，本項目將系統地對單晶和多晶的一維納米鑽石結構進行原位電鏡下的納米力學研究。 本項目將主要包含三個方面：“可控加工各種形貌和晶向的一維鑽石結構”，“原位定量納米力學測試和表征”，“深入理解晶體結構，加載條件等對其力學性質的影響”。成功執行該項目將有益于一維鑽石材料在藥物傳遞，基因輸送，納米光子學，柔性電子器件等方面的應用，以及深化對金剛石晶體結構的納米材料的機械性能和形變機制的理解。此外，這項研究還可能帶來更多的功能納米器件和“彈性應變工程”的應用。

11207416.label: Realisation of objectives
11207416.value: 1.We developed various microfabrication techniques and protocols for achieving various kinds of diamond micro/nanostructure samples (including diamond nanoneedles, diamond microbridges, and diamond bridge arrays) with well-controlled crystalline orientations, microstructures, and geometries for quantitative in situ nanomechanical testing (bending, compression, and tension). In 2018, we reported the discovery on ultralarge elasticity in the nanoscale diamond (Science 360, 300-302, 2018). We fabricated the nanoscale diamond needles by plasma-induced etching of diamond thin films deposited on Si substrates through bias-assisted chemical vapor deposition. The shape, size, crystallinity, and density of the nanoneedles were controlled by the appropriate choice of growth and etching parameters during deposition. We controlled the crystal orientation by etching the single-crystalline diamond nanoneedles from specific oriented diamond films. We successfully developed new platforms (“push-to-bend” and “compress-to-bend”) to carry out in situ mechanical testing for diamond nanoneedles. Moreover, reported in Science 371, 6524, 76-78, 2021, we developed advanced microfabrication processes producing high-quality diamond structures with micrometer dimensions and well-defined geometry, structure, and crystal orientations by focused ion beam (FIB) from bulk single-crystalline diamonds that were grown through microwave plasma-assisted chemical vapor deposition. 2. We obtained some essential understanding of the enhanced elasticity and origins of single crystalline diamond nanostructures and their underlying mechanism through in situ mechanical studies. We also investigated the effect of defects on diamond’s mechanical performance. For example, we demonstrated the fully reversible elastic deformation of nanoscale single-crystalline and polycrystalline diamond needles. For single-crystalline diamond, we realized the maximum tensile strains up to 9%, which approached the theoretical elastic limit, and the corresponding maximum tensile stress reached ~89 to 98 gigapascals. After combining systematic computational simulations and characterization of pre- and post-deformation structural features, we ascribe the concurrent high strength and large elastic strain to the paucity of defects in the small-volume diamond nanoneedles and the relatively smooth surfaces compared with those of microscale and larger specimens. Unlike those in single-crystalline needles, fracture surfaces in polycrystalline needles were nearly parallel to the substrate. The local (tensile) maximum principal strain from polycrystalline samples was considerably smaller, around 3.5%, which is approximately one-half the average for single crystal samples. In addition, we successfully realized the uniaxial tensile straining of single-crystalline diamond microbridge arrays with our homemade nanoindenter diamond gripper, allowing "strained diamond" device arrays. 3. Diamond shows elastic deformation during the whole loading-unloading tensile test. We then studied typical fracture morphologies of diamond bridges along [100], [101] and [111] directions. They have typical brittle fracture morphologies with no visible sign of plasticity or amorphization during tensile deformation, in which the fractured bridges retain the pristine single-crystalline structure. The fractured parts show typical distinct {111} cleavage surfaces, which are known to have the lowest surface energy and typically observed during brittle fracture of bulk diamonds. We also investigated the plastic deformation of wide-bandgap semiconductors including GaN and SiC, which are highly related with diamond and its crystalline structures. The size-induced brittle-to-ductile transition of GaN at room temperature was found, and GaN deformed plastically when the pillar size was smaller than 700-800nm. In situ TEM technique was used to study the plastic deformation mechanism of GaN at nanoscale. 4.We performed in situ bending experiments on polycrystalline diamond nanoneedles. Unlike those in single-crystalline needles, fracture surfaces in polycrystalline needles were nearly parallel to the substrate. The local (tensile) maximum principal strain from FEM simulation was between 3.51% and 3.54% (depending on friction coefficient) for the polycrystalline needle, which is approximately one-half the average for single crystals. The single-crystalline diamond nanoneedles generally achieved a much higher local maximum tensile strain than the polycrystalline ones. We achieved a mean maximum tensile strain of ~6% for the single-crystalline nanoneedles (maximum tensile strain of ~9%). The mean maximum tensile strain was ~3.3% for the polycrystalline nanoneedles, and the maximum tensile strain was 3.5%. Nevertheless, these elastic strains are also much higher than the previously reported bulk diamond elastic limit. We also conducted in situ lateral bending tests of diamond nanoneedles with nanotwins/stacking faults to assess the effect of defects on the mechanical properties of diamond (manuscript under preparation). Compared with single-crystalline needles, the needles that containing twins experienced a short range of elastic deformation and have fracture surfaces along {111} twin boundaries. The twin boundaries serve as planar defects and reduce the elasticity of diamond needles under the present loading geometry. On the other hand, according to recent reported works about nanotwin diamond, twin could strengthen the diamond depending on the configuration. In our cases, a few samples with nanotwin/stacking faults show considerable elastic deformation as well, which requires some further study. 5. We conducted the uniaxial tensile tests of diamond bridges with varied strain rates ranging from 1 × 10-3 s-1 to 6.25 × 10-3 s-1. Experimental results reveal that the deformations were fully reversible and hysteresis-free under loading-unloading tests with varied strain rates, and the diamond bridges all shows elastic deformation with typical brittle fracture, with no visible sign of plasticity or amorphization during tensile deformation, suggesting that the elastic limit is insensitive to strain rate in this range. Cyclic test was also performed to study the deformation behavior of silicon nanowires and monolayer 2D covalent crystals, such as graphene and h-BN. The results showed the deformation was essentially elastically during the tensile processes, but more systematic study remains needed to fully understand the fatigue behavior (if any).

11207416.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207416.value: Through the research of this project, we, for the first time, successfully achieved large elastic strain deformation of single-crystalline diamond nanoneedles with diameter ~300 nanometer and the maximum local tensile strains (up to 9%) approaching the theoretical elastic strain limit of diamond. The corresponding maximum tensile stress reached ~89 to 98 gigapascals approaching the ideal strength (Science 360, 300-302, 2018). After combining systematic computational simulations and characterization of pre- and postdeformation structural features, we ascribe the concurrent high strength and large elastic strain to the paucity of defects in the small-volume diamond nanoneedles and the relatively smooth surfaces compared with those of microscale and larger specimens. Moreover, we microfabricated single-crystalline diamond bridge structures by the focused ion beam. Experiment results found that diamond bridges of about 1 micrometer in length and 100 nanometer in thickness can sustain a highly uniform elastic strain distribution of about 7.5% across the sample. By further optimizing the sample geometry according to the American Society for Testing and Materials standard, we demonstrated that diamond bridge samples achieved a maximum tensile strain of up to 9.7%, which surpasses the local maximum strain value in our 2018 research and approaches to diamond theoretical strain limits. We can consistently achieve 6-8% sample-wide uniform elastic strains under uniaxial tensile loading along the [100], [101], and [111] directions (Science 371, 6524, 76-78, 2021). Based on the experimental results, the strain-induced electronic property changes of diamond under ultralarge strain are comparatively studied by DFT first principle calculations. Generally, the bandgap of diamonds for each direction decreases as the tensile strain increases. Straining along the [101] direction can induce a substantial calculated bandgap reduction as much as ~2 electron volts at 9% strain. An indirect-direct bandgap transition may be possible with tensile strains larger than 9% along the [111] direction. We also successfully microfabricated diamond array samples with multiple bridges and realized the large, uniform, reversible straining of diamond microbridge arrays to demonstrate the strained diamond device concept. Apart from diamond, micro/nanoscale mechanical properties and deformation mechanism of wide-bandgap semiconductors, such as GaN and SiC, which share similar crystalline structure as diamond, were also studied with in situ electron microscope techniques and HRTEM. Lastly, the elastic properties of 2D covalent crystals, such as monolayer graphene and h-BN, were investigated in this project for their nanomechanics and elastic strain engineering.

11207416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207416.value: The further development regarding this project is to experimentally explore the bandgap modulation by electronic measurements of the stretched diamond and the real application of strained diamond devices based on elastic strain engineering. According to our findings, including the ultralarge uniform tensile strain and calculated bandgap changes, the challenges of experimental bandgap characterization for stretched diamond remain, although we experimentally verified bandgap reduction using a T-shaped bending sample with nonuniform strain distribution by electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS). Electrical/optical detectors, including cathodoluminescence (CL), photoluminescence (PL), and Raman spectroscopy, can be coupled with our nanomechanical straining setup, and bandgap variation with increasing or decreasing of elastic strain would be measured in real-time. Therefore, we would systematically establish the strain-induced bandgap variation response for diamonds, critical for its practical applications. It inversely provides quantitative feedback that can calibrate theoretical calculations of DFT and an in-depth understanding of the mechanical and physical mechanisms of the strained diamond. In the long run, well-controlled microfabrication of the diamond nanostructures from bulk crystals, even at a wafer scale, would be necessary to bring such “strain engineering” device applications into reality. Other low-dimensional covalent crystalline solids can be also systematically investigated based on the outcomes and experiences obtained through this research for future application development.

11207416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207416.value: Diamond, known as the hardest natural material, is usually brittle and unbendable at a bulk scale; however, their mechanical properties at the nanoscale were less known. In this project, we, for the first time, experimentally found ultralarge tensile strain in nanoscale diamond needles (Science 2018), and later, we demonstrated that ultralarge, uniform elastic deformation can be indeed achieved through uniaxial tensile straining of microfabricated diamond bridges (Science 2021). Based on first-principle calculations and EESL characterization, the bandgap evolution/reduction with the increasing elastic strain was experimentally characterized, which, in some sense, turns the insulating diamond into a wide-bandgap semiconductor. Furthermore, the desired indirect-to-direct bandgap transformation under certain straining condition could make diamond direct-bandgap semiconductor, as comparable to GaN. Moreover, we demonstrated the strained diamond device concept by microfabricating diamond arrays with multiple bridges and realized the large reversible straining of diamond device arrays. Our research opens up new possibilities for tuning the diamond functional properties, such as electronic and optical properties, by using mechanical approach alone, leading to unprecedented application potential in electronics, photonics and quantum information technologies in the future. The obtained insights from this study can be potentially used for other 1D/2D semiconductors.

11211116.value: Experimentally demonstrate the proposed device concept of piezoelectric lamb wave mode MEMS magnetometers and formulate models to describe the magnetic field sensitivity in relation to film properties and device geometry. Investigate the frequency scalability of piezoelectric lamb wave mode MEMS magnetometers as a means to increase sensitivity through the use of higher order lamb wave modes.

11211116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211116.value: 本項目旨在通過實驗驗證一種新式的MEMS洛倫茲力磁力計。該磁力計採用成熟的工藝流程製造。同樣的工藝流程已經用於大規模生產智能手機中常見的MEMS慣性傳感器。 MEMS慣性傳感器是用於檢測運動的傳感器。目前，MEMS慣性傳感器的製造工藝已經非常成熟。與MEMS慣性傳感器不同的是，MEMS洛倫茲力磁力計仍處於研發的過程中，但它已經吸引了大量的關注。這是因為MEMS洛倫茲力磁力計可以用於製作智能手機中的電子羅盤儀。 MEMS洛倫茲力磁力計能夠檢測所在環境中的磁場強度。它的工作原理是將磁場所產生的洛倫茲力作用於機械振動結構，並檢測振動結構隨之產生的電信號輸出。將磁力計和慣性傳感器的組合起來能夠實現智能手機中的個人導航功能。目前使用的MEMS磁力計存在兩個問題。一個問題是一些MEMS磁力計需要真空封裝，因此組裝難度大，而且成本較高。另一個問題是能夠工作於大氣環境中的磁力計需要消耗額外的電流。本項目旨在通過解決這兩個問題進而推動MEMS磁力計的發展。本項目的創新點在於利用工作於Lamb波振動模式的壓電材料MEMS諧振器來檢測磁場產生的洛倫茲力。這種檢測方式能夠顯著提高磁力計在大氣環境中對磁場強度檢測的靈敏度。靈敏度的提高歸結於兩個原因：（1）採用壓電傳感方式能夠顯著提高洛倫茲力轉換產生的輸出電信號。 （2）採用Lamb振動模式能夠減小空氣阻尼對機械諧振器的影響。

11211116.label: Realisation of objectives
11211116.value: Objective 1: We have fully achieved the aims set out in this objective. On this aspect, we have experimentally demonstrated the concept on piezoelectric Lamb wave mode MEMS magnetometers. We have demonstrated several state of the art device concepts that have shown to be on par with or surpass the best MEMS magnetometers in terms of responsivity without the requirement for vacuum operation. The earliest conception was based on the width-extensional mode (published in Sens. Actuator A 2017). Later innovations with further improved performance included a square-extensional mode device (published in Appl. Phys. Lett. 2017) and the coupled radial contour mode (published in Sens. Actuator A 2018). For each of these novel modes, we have formulated and validated models that accurately describe the characteristics like responsivity of the device. Objective 2: We have fully achieved the aims set out in this objective. To this end, we have investigated the frequency scalability of piezoelectric lamb wave mode MEMS magnetometers as a means to increase sensitivity through the use of higher order lamb wave modes. We have validated this approach by experiments and actual devices as a means to boost responsivitiy. These exciting new results have formed the basis of a more recently funded GRF to look into this direction more extensively. The results were presented and published at the flagship Transducers 2019 conference in Berlin.

11211116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211116.value: 1/ We investigated an published on several device concepts for detecting out of plane magnetic fields, which were the sole focus of this project. We showed responsivities that surpassed the state of art without vacuum. The results have been published in several journals (Sens. Actuator A 2017, Appl. Phys. Lett. 2017, Sens. Actuator 2018) recogised in the field. 2/ Going beyond the scope of the project, we have also investigated and demonstrated device concepts for detecting in plane magnetic fields. These devices were implemented in the same standard process used to fabricated the out of plane B-field detection devices with the aim to show that these concepts are applicable to realized 3D field detection on a single chip with one process. These results have been published in journals (IEEE T Mag 2018, IEEE Trans. UFFC 2019). The relevant work presented at the joint EFTF IFCS conference in 2017 was shortlisted for the Best Student paper award. 3/ The bulk of the results arising from this project are delivered at an invited lecture at the 2018 IEEE NEMS conference and would also have been presented as an invited lecture at the MNE 2020 conference that was eventually cancelled due to the global pandemic. 4/ Through this project, a PhD student was trained and his PhD thesis was written on the topic of this project (see Part C of report). The student is now applying his training in piezoelectric MEMS to his scientific role at the Institute of Microelectronics in Singapore. 5/ We have also validated the efficacy of exploiting higher order Lamb wave modes to scale up both responsivity and bandwidth. The results were presented at the flagship Transducers 2019 conference (see attached paper in Part C). These results have formed the basis of a recently awarded GRF. As captured in Part C of this report, a total of 5 journal papers along with several conference papers have been published enabled by funding from this project.

11211116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211116.value: The research from this project have provided an invaluable foundation to build upon in a recently funded GRF that will look specifically at exploiting higher order mode topology designs as a means to scale up bandwidth and responsivity simultaneously. So there certainly will be further exciting research developments arising from this project with the fresh injection of funding. Funding from this completed project has enabled us to do the ground work concerned in device design, fabrication, characterization/calibration, and modelling.

11211116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211116.value: Miniaturized magnetometers are used in many applications, including smart phones, to measured magnetic fields. Existing solutions in the market are only available as discrete components. Given the trajectory of rising complexity of electronic devices that demand greater integration, there is a need to research device concepts that can be integrated with existing sensor technologies. Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) is an attractive solution but existing device concepts require proprietary vacuum packaging solutions. This project has investigated and demonstrated various novel device concepts based on piezoelectric transducers as an alternative and feasible pathway to eliminate such constraints but yet have been able to deliver higher responsivities than the state of the art.

11212216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11212216.value: 研究激子效應在聚合物光伏材料的限制

11212216.label: Project Objectives
11212216.value: To develop new experimental approaches to investigate the correction between the material dielectric properties and excitonic effect in an ensemble of polymeric photovoltaic materials. To develop nano-structured high-k materials that compatible with polymeric photovoltaic materials to form high-k composite films to reduce the excitonic effect. To develop photovoltaic cells using the high-k composite photovoltaic materials to demonstrate the reduced excitonic effect in device level, such as enhance photovoltage and reduced germinate recombination.

11212216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212216.value: Organic photovoltaic (OPV) has drawn a lot of attention during the last decade owning to its potential for low-cost and high-efficiency. The technology was triggered by the earlier breakthrough of the introduction of organic heterojunction that efficiently dissociate strongly bound excitons upon photo-excitation. The heterojunction structure has become the design rule for material synthesis and device architecture. Recently, having the efforts from both fine tuning of the electronic properties of the organic photoactive materials and device structures, over 10% power conversion efficiency (PCE) has been reported. However, in order to tackle the excitonic effect, the organic heterojunction requires an energy offset (>0.3eV) between the organic donor and acceptor materials, as a trade-off, the photovoltage and as a result of the PCE are significantly reduced by more than 30%. Recently the excitonic effect has been regarded as the major limitation on further improving the performance in OPV. Despite of the encouraging theoretical results and predictions on the ultimate PCE of 20% in OPV by reducing the excitonic effect, experimentally little success has been reported so far. There are two major obstacles in tackling this issue: 1) There is lack of systemic investigation on the correlation between the dielectric properties and excitonic effect in organic materials. It is still unclear how high the dielectric constant can completely diminish the exciton effect in the OPV processes. 2) There is lack of viable approach or demonstration to bring insight into reducing the excitonic effect. It is unknown whether the dielectric constant can be effectively increased by molecular structural modification or incorporating with other high-dielectric (high-k) materials. There are two key objectives in this proposed research: In materials, we will increase the dielectric constant of existing OPV materials by structural modifications and developing high-k composites. We are aiming at reducing the exciton binding energy in existing high-efficiency conjugated low-bandgap polymers. Ultimately, we will explore the possibility to realize free-charge generation without the heterojunction structure in OPV. In device physics, we will investigate the excitonic effect by developing techniques based on pump-probe and charge modulation spectroscopies to investigate the exciton to free-charge evolution in different material systems. We are aiming at quantitatively identify the contribution of the material dielectric properties on the excitonic effect. Therefore, the success of this project would not only bring insight into developing more efficient photovoltaic devices, but more fundamentally the excitonic effect in photo-carrier generation process in photovoltaic materials. 在過去的十年中，有機光伏材料由於其具備低成本及高效率等特點，在全世界範圍內引起廣泛關注。隨後，有機異質結的引入極大地提高了激子的分離效應，此技術的問世也成為有機光伏領域進步的一個里程碑。現階段有機異質結的設計已經成為有機光伏材料合成及器件製備的基本準則。通過對有機光伏材料電子性能及器件結構的不斷優化，現在有機太陽能電池的轉化效率已高達10%。然而，為了提高激子分離效率，一般要求電子給體和受體材料要有一定的能量差（>0.3eV），這就大幅度降低了有機太陽能電池的開路電壓和光電轉化效率（>30% ）。最近，更有報導指出激子效應就是直接限制有機太陽能電池性能的直接因素。計算得出通過降低有機光伏材料中的激子效應可以將有機太陽能電池的轉化效率突破20%。但至今未有實驗報導。目前通過降低有機光伏材料激子效應提高器件效率主要存在兩大問題：1）對於有機材料的介電性能和激子效應的關係至今未有系統地研究，而且一直都不清楚多高的介電常數才能有效地降低激子效應。 2）至今沒有一個切實可行的方案降低激子效應。另一方面也不清楚能否通過對有機分子結構進行修飾或者摻雜其他高介電常數材料等方法來提高有機光伏材料的介電常數。 本項目主要有兩大目標：1）材料方面，申請人將主要集中對目前已有的有機光伏材料結構進行修飾以達到提高其介電常數的目標，其次將研發一些具有高介電常數的有機複合材料。項目伊始，申請人希望能夠降低現有的共軛低帶隙的聚合物的激子結合能。最終，申請人將試圖開發無需異質結就能夠產生自由電荷的有機太陽能電池。 2）器件物理方面，申請人將基於泵浦-探測開發電荷調製吸收譜技術，用以研究在不同材料系統中激子向自由電荷轉變的過程。申請人最終將定量地給出介電常數對材料激子效應的影響機制。綜上兩方面，本項目的成功實施不僅能夠為今後開發高效的有機太陽能電池指明方向，更能從根本上了解有機光伏材料系統光生載流子產生過程中的激子效應。

11212216.label: Realisation of objectives
11212216.value: O1: To develop new experimental approaches to investigate the correction between the material dielectric properties and excitonic effect in an ensemble of polymeric photovoltaic materials. (100% completed) In this project, we developed several spectroscopy techniques to determine the dielectric and excitonic properties of a series of polymeric materials. We have found that the exciton binding energy in polymers has a second order dependence on their dielectric constant, it agrees with the hydrogen model. Our results also suggest that a dielectric constant of 5 in organic semiconductors can facilitate considerable amount of free carrier generation, it brings insight into developing more efficient materials with reduced recombination loss. O1.1. Dielectric constant – As mentioned in the mid-term reported, we compared the electrical impedance spectroscopy and optical ellipsometry for determining the dielectric constant of materials. Previously, there was debate in the community on the reliability of such electrical and optical techniques. In this project, we have found that both techniques can achieve mutual agreement by (1) eliminating the carrier injection effect in impedance measurement and (2) taking the dielectric value that converged in longer wavelength in ellipsometry measurement. Having this foundation, we further examined 15 organic photovoltaic materials and found that their dielectric constants span from 2.5 to 5.5. Surprisingly, we have found a material, SubNC, has a dielectric constant as high as 5.5 which is the highest reported among other organic photovoltaic materials. O1.2. Excitonic properties – We applied the external quantum efficiency (EQE) measurement and electroabsorption (EA) spectroscopy to investigate the excitonic properties of a series of organic photovoltaic materials. As mentioned in the mid-term reported, EQE can give access to the exciton binding energy, whereas EA can provide insight of the charge-transfer (CT) characteristics at different excitation energies. By further comparing a series of different materials. We have found that those materials with binding energy larger than 300meV can be readily extracted by the EQE techniques. However, the characteristic onset in the EQE spectrum cannot be resolved for materials with exciton binding energy smaller than that value. In this case, we have found that EA can complementarily resolve this issue by comparing the measured EA spectrum to the 1st and 2nd derivatives of the materials absorption spectrum. For example, materials such as PCBM and SubNC, with binding energy of around 200meV can be determined by the EA technique. In addition, we have also developed a generalized analytical model to analysis the EA spectrum. Using the model, we can accurately extract the polarizability and dipole moment of the materials, both are the key parameters in controlling the materials excitonic properties. More important, our model resolves the impact of optical effect in sandwiched thin film devices that has been overlooked in previous reports. O1.3. Correction between the dielectric and excitonic effect – Using the above-mentioned techniques, we have found that the exciton binding energy has a second order dependence on the materials dielectric constant, it agrees with the hydrogen model. Our results also suggest that a dielectric constant of 5 in organic semiconductors can facilitate considerable amount of free carrier generation. In addition, we found that the change in polarizability (p) and dipole moment (u) in different materials has no direct correlation with the exciton binding energy. Instead, we have found that the change in ratio between p and u (i.e. p/u) at different excitation wavelength are consistent with the EQE spectral characteristics. This interesting result would provide more in-depth understanding of the physical meaning of the two parameters. O2: To develop nano-structured high-k materials that compatible with polymeric photovoltaic materials to form high-k composite films to reduce the excitonic effect. (100% completed) We developed a series of high-k metal oxide nanoparticles (ZnO, AZO, SnO, NiO, perovskite, and GO) and tried to blend with polymers to reduce the exciton binding energy. Among those nanoparticles, ZnO, AZO and SnO can be well dissolved in the polymer solution. On the other hand, we have found that NiO, perovskite, and GO which primary dissolved in polar solvent are insoluble in the polymer solution. In addition, we have found that blending the ZnO, AZO and SnO with the polymer in solution would induce serious aggregation due to the miscibility issue between the nanoparticles and polymer. This issue was resolved by adding a small amount of amine as solvent additive in the blended solution to improve the dispersion between the two materials. By using the solvent additive technique, we have achieved homogeneous and smooth thin films as confirmed by the atomic force microscopy results. We measured the dielectric constant, exciton binding energy and exciton properties of the composite films using impedance spectroscopy, EQE and EA as described above. We have found that the dielectric constant of the composite films has been increased by 20% to 100% depending on the loading ratio of the high-k nanoparticles added into the polymer solution. We have also observed an increased in EQE value and CT characteristics in the EA spectrum, confirming the reduced exciton binding energy in the composite films. However, the reproducibility of the EQE results is challenging. Only around 10% of the fabricated devices showed increased EQE values. We suspected that there was still certain degree of aggregation of the polymer and nanoparticles in the resulting films. Further optimization of the process is required and different solvent additives would potentially solve this issue. O3: To develop photovoltaic cells using the high-k composite photovoltaic materials to demonstrate the reduced excitonic effect in device level, such as enhance photovoltage and reduced germinate recombination. (90% completed) We fabricated photovoltaic devices with the composite films and successfully achieved photovoltaic response as demonstrated in the mid-term report. The device had largely improved photovoltage and strongly suppressed recombination as compared to the pristine polymer devices. Further optimization of the device by varying the ratio between the polymer and nanoparticles were conducted. We found that the optimal ratio for achieving the best performance is around 1:1 for various composite films. It is the first time demonstration of working devices using polymer:nanoparticle composite, and it also brings insight into developing various organic electronic devices. However, as mentioned above, the devices were still suffered from material aggregation issue. Some of the devices were electrically insulating, suggesting the polymer were aggregated which could not form percolated charge carrier transport pathways. Further investigation on this issue is required to allow systemic assessment of the device performance and corresponding material science.

11212216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212216.value: In this project, the developed spectroscopy techniques are powerful tools which can be widely applied to extract the electronic properties in emerging semiconducting materials.[1-5] Particularly, we have found that the exciton binding energy in polymers has a second order dependence on their dielectric constant, which can be described by the hydrogen model. Our results also suggest that a dielectric constant of 5 in organic semiconductors can facilitate considerable amount of free carrier generation. The results bring fundamental insight into the understanding on molecular structure dependent electronic properties. In addition, the analytical electroabsorption model developed in this project resolves the previous issue of the impact of optical effect in sandwiched thin film devices. It provides an accurate assessment of the excitonic properties of various organic and inorganic electronic materials.[4] The high-k materials and the composite films with reduced excitonic effect developed in this project also demonstrate the feasibility of such new material system in optoelectronic device applications.[5]

11212216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212216.value: Although high power conversion efficiency over 18% in organic solar cells has been demonstrated, it is still questionable if the technology can be widely applied for energy conversion. One of the key concerns is the very high cost of the organic photovoltaic materials. On the other hand, the cost of metal oxide nanoparticles is typically ten to hundred times lower than the organic materials for the same amount. Therefore, the success of the polymer:nanoparticle composite would definitely a new avenue for organic electronic devices. As mentioned above, there is still certain degree of material aggregation in the composite films which affect the reproducibility of the device performance. Understanding the course and solving the aggregation issue are both scientifically and technologically important. It involves fundamental process of composite film formation and the corresponding variation of material optoelectronic properties. Based on our results, it is believed that the aggregation can be potentially resolved by incorporating solvent additive to increase the miscibility between the materials. Systemic investigation on composite film formation by adding additives with various dipole moment, viscosity, evaporation temperature, and solvent solubility would potentially trigger new findings and development.

11212216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212216.value: Organic solar cell is an emerging technology for energy conversion. Its unique properties of flexible and solution processable offer a great potential for developing the next generation low-cost and high-efficiency solar cells. However, existing organic solar cell materials are still in high cost and suffer from strong excitonic effect which limits the amount of photocurrent generation. In this UGC funded project, the research team devoted to developing spectroscopy technique to understand how photogenerated electrons and holes separate in organic materials. Meanwhile, the team also developed composite thin films with organic and inorganic materials to reduce the attractive force in the photogenerated carriers. By systemically study a series of organic materials, the team successfully found out the relationship between molecular structure and the ability of separating the photogenerated carriers. The team had also demonstrated an efficient solar cell with reduced carrier attractive force making use of the composite materials.
