11228316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11228316.value: We have successfully fabricated InAs nanowire biosensor as a platform for bio-sensing. The InAs NWs were of high quality, having length > 4 micron with diameter of less than 50 nm. Although the transport properties of the devices can be measured in PBS buffer, we discovered that the InAs nanowires exhibit moderate cytotoxicity to several cell lines. This result suggests that the as-grown InAs NWs cannot be directly used for any real-time bio-sensing purpose. Attempts were made to modify the surface of the InAs NWs by various thiol-containing organic molecules which are commercially available. While the cytotoxicity of the surface-modified InAs NWs can be significantly reduced, the gating properties of the FETs were compromised. We later explored other application of the FETs with surface-modified InAs NWs, and discovered that the surface of the InAs NWs plays a critical role in the enhancement of the negative photoconductivity. In line with our proposal to explore different bio-sensing platform based on nano-materials, we developed a nano-theranostic system, denoted as Ce6-CuS/MSN@PDA@MnO2-FA nanoparticles (NPs), which combines photodynamic therapy (PDT), photothermal therapy (PTT), magnetic resonance (MR) imaging with hypoxia-relieving and tumor-targeting functionalities. In vitro and in vivo measurements clearly demonstrated that all these functionalities worked synergistically as expected. The system, having a low dark cytotoxicity, can be effectively internalized by 4T1 cells and decrease the cell viability to 2% upon 660 nm/808 nm laser irradiation. Tumors in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice can almost be completely destroyed in 2 weeks via combined PDT/PTT. Moreover, several new anti-cancer systems were developed/explored in this project. We developed the synthesis of two series of phosphonium ring-fused bicyclic ruthenafuran and osmafuran complexes via a one-step synthesis procedure. The complexes were found to exhibit stronger cytotoxicity against several common human cancer cell lines compared with their corresponding metal precursors and the classic anticancer agent cisplatin, and are able to induce mitochondrial dysfunction in cells, which suggests that the metallafurans may potentially serve as alternative anticancer agents. A new series of ruthenium-indolizinone complexes with anticancer properties was also prepared by an unexpected alkyne activation pathways.

11228316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11228316.value: This project highlights the importance of the choice of organic molecules for surface passivation of the NWs. While the cytotoxicity of the NWs can be significantly reduced by various organic molecules with binding groups (e.g. thiol-groups in this project), it was discovered that there will be a trade-off between cytotoxicity and sensitivity of the devices. Therefore, the development of new and cost-effective passivation materials for the NWs would be the direction for further development. More specifically, research should focus on tailor-making organic or inorganic molecules for NW passivation, instead of just employing commercially available simple molecules. The effect of the passivating molecules on the surface state of the NWs should also be investigated carefully by various spectroscopic techniques.

11228316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11228316.value: Multi-nanowire field-effect transistor composed of InAs nanowires were fabricated to construct real-time bio-sensors. Although the InAs are cytotoxic and hampers the real-time bio-sensing, its toxicity can be significantly reduced by surface modification with thiol-containing molecules. While the cytotoxicity of the biosensor can be reduced, it was discovered that the sensing properties of the devices were also decreased, as the thiol-containing molecules affected the gating properties of the sensors. However, the devices were to have enhancement on the negative photoconductivity. This project highlights the importance of the choice of organic molecules for surface passivation. The future development on nanowaire-based bio-sensors should focus on the exploration of new and cost-effective organic or inorganic passivation materials which allows effective gating of field-effect transistors.

11234916.label: Project Objectives
11234916.value: To develop some easily-verified necessary and/or sufficient conditions for the state controllability of a general linear temporally switching network, in terms of the row-rank of the network controllability matrix. To develop some easily-verified necessary and/or sufficient conditions for the structural and strongly structural controllability of a general linear temporally switching network, in terms of temporal dilation, intersection and/or N-walks. To develop some easily-verified necessary and/or sufficient conditions for the state and structural observability of a general linear temporally switching network, in terms of matrix algebraic rank-checking and/or geometric graph-checking measures. Potential applications of the switching network observability to information source detection will be explored.

11234916.value: This proposal aims to study the controllability and observability of temporally switching directed complex networks with linear node dynamics. Both notions of state controllability and observability, as well as structural controllability and observability, will be studied. The main objective is to derive some precise and easily-verified algebraic as well as graph-theoretic controllability and observability conditions for such practical networks. To that end, some potential real applications of the temporally switching network controllability and observability will also be explored. 本項目研究時間切換線性節點有向網絡的能控性與能觀性，包括狀態能控能觀性和結構能控能觀性。主要目標是導出這類實用網絡的簡單明確而又容易驗證的能控能觀性的代數以及幾何條件。最後將探究時間切換有向網絡的能控性與能觀性的實際應用。

11234916.value: This project studied the controllability and observability of temporally switching directed complex networks with linear node dynamics. Both notions of state controllability and observability, as well as structural controllability and observability were studied. The completed objective derived precise and easily-verified algebraic as well as graph-theoretic controllability and observability conditions for practical networks. Some potential real applications of the temporally switching network controllability and observability have also be explored.

11237116.value: 基於數據驅動的物體結構自適應編輯

11237116.label: Project Objectives
11237116.value: To decompose a category of man-made models into groups of shapes with similar structures. To learn group-sensitive priors, including the inter-group and intra-group priors, to capture geometric and structural variations of shapes in the same category. To develop a structure-adaptive shape editing technique with the assistance of the learned group-sensitive priors. To develop various user interfaces to allow explicit control of structural variations. To thoroughly evaluate the usability and effectiveness of the proposed technique.

To learn group-sensitive priors, including the inter-group and intra-group priors, to capture geometric and structural variations of shapes in the same category.

To develop various user interfaces to allow explicit control of structural variations.
To thoroughly evaluate the usability and effectiveness of the proposed technique.

11237116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11237116.value: 3D modeling is a fundamental problem in 3D computer graphics. Although many 3D modeling techniques have been proposed, 3D modeling is still one of the bottlenecks for many applications such as virtual reality and 3D printing. In this project, we focus on the problem of interactive shape editing, which is a popular modeling paradigm and aims to generate new variations of a given shape via a moderate amount of user interactions. The recent efforts have been mainly put to the design of editing frameworks for man-made objects, which are highly demanded for 3D printing and the digitization of our real world. Most of the existing man-made shape editing techniques aim for the creation of geometric variations of a shape, typically through structure-preserving shape deformation. These techniques thus do not support either implicit or explicit exploration of structural variations during editing. The creation of new shape structures has been studied recently in context of synthesis from shape collections but is not directly applicable for editing a given shape. We observe that desired editing effects sometimes might be difficult to achieve without changing the shape structure of a shape. This motivates us to design a shape-adaptive editing framework which automatically decides whether to keep or change the shape structure to reflect user inputs. Our key idea is that possible geometric variations can be modeled by a group of shapes with similar structures, and possible structural variations can be determined by performing inter-group shape analysis. This leads to a data-driven approach with three key problems involved: How to cluster various shapes in the same category into structure groups? How to learn group-sensitive priors? How to adaptively edit shapes with the assistance of the learned group-sensitive priors? Our technique will automatically bring geometric and/or structural changes to a shape being edited dependent on user inputs. We believe that by allowing automatic adjustment of shape structures our technique will produce structurally more reasonable editing results. We also plan to explore various user interfaces to support a more explicit way for editing shape structures, making it possible to produce both geometric variations and structure variations when editing a single shape. With the growing accessibility of man-made objects, we expect that benefited from the rich knowledge embedded in the database, our structure-adaptive editing approach will enable both professional and novice users to easily produce new shapes, which are readily used by various applications. 三維建模是計算機圖形學中的一個基本問題。雖然許多三維建模技術已經被提出，但在很多應用中，例如虛擬現實和三維打印，對三維物體的建模仍是一個瓶頸。在本項目中，我們關注交互式的形狀編輯問題，這是一個流行的建模範式，即在給定的一個形狀中，通過添加適量的用戶交互，從而產生一系列新的形狀。 鑑於在三維打印和對真實世界物體的數字化強勁需求，近年來，人們的精力主要集中在設計針對人造物體的編輯框架。大部分針對人造形狀編輯技術，其主要目的是生成一個形狀的變形，典型的方法是通過結構保持的形狀變形。因此在編輯過程中，這些已有的方法並不以隱式或顯示的方式支持對結構形變的探究。從形狀集合的合成環境中生成新的形狀結構，該工作在最近得到研究，但該方法並不能直接地適用於編輯某一給定形狀。 在形狀編輯過程中，我們發現，不改變形狀結構而想得到理想的編輯效果，這往往非常困難。這促使我們設計一個形狀適應的編輯框架，它能夠在編輯過程中響應用戶的輸入，從而自動的決定保持或者改變形狀結構。我們的核心創新有兩點：組內相似的形狀結構能夠推斷出合理的幾何變形形狀；組間形狀分析可得到合理的幾何結構形狀。這引出了一個數據驅動方法，它涉及到三個關鍵性問題：針對相同種類而不同形狀的幾何集，如何按結構聚類？如何學習組別敏感的先驗知識？如何在已學習到的組別敏感先驗知識幫助下，適應性地編輯形狀？ 在形狀編輯過程中，我們的方法可根據用戶的輸入自動的產生幾何或結構上的改變，或兩者同時改變。允許自動的調整形狀結構，我們相信這一技術將使得編輯效果在結構上更加合理。與此同時，為了以更加直接的方式來編輯形狀結構，我們計劃開發多樣的用戶界面，使得在編輯某一形狀過程中，系統在幾何形狀和結構上都能夠產生豐富的變形。隨著人造物體變得越來越觸手可得，我們希望從蘊含在數據庫中的豐富知識中得到啟發，不管是專業人員還是新用戶，使用我們的結構自適應編輯方法都能夠使他們在各種應用中容易地創作出新的形狀物體。

11237116.label: Realisation of objectives
11237116.value: We have achieved all the objectives, as detailed below. We have designed and developed algorithms for decomposing man-made objects into groups of shapes with similar structures (Objective 1) and learning group-sensitive priors (Objective 2). Structure-adaptive editing (Objective 3) was first explored using a 3D human pose (represented as a 3D human skeleton) as the main interface (Objective 4). The advantage of using a human pose as the interface is that by describing the object affordance of individual 3D models against a 3D human skeleton, we can establish part-level correspondence between not only shapes with similar structures but also shapes from different categories. This allows us to synthesize new structures by recombining existing structures adaptively with respect to a given 3D human skeleton under a specific pose. To evaluate the effectiveness of our technique (Objective 5), we have compared it with state-of-the-art techniques and demonstrated its unique advantage. The results of these experiments have been presented in a research paper ([Journal 1] in Part C) published in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (the second-best journal in the field of computer graphics). We have also extended the above idea from shape synthesis to scene synthesis by analyzing groups of objects (Objective 1) and learning structural variations of objects (Objective 2) from a 2D floor plan database. We have focused on the synthesis of indoor scenes and our technique is able to adaptively explore proper indoor objects and their layouts for a given room and a few user-specified object categories with the learned priors from the 2D floor plans (Objective 3). We have developed a graphical user interface for users to control scene synthesis and perform scene editing (Objective 4). Finally, our method has been compared to the closely related works and its advantages have been demonstrated via extensive experiments (Objective 5). The results have been presented at SIGGRAPH Asia 2017 and the paper [Journal 2] has been published in a special issue of ACM Transactions on Graphics, which is the best journal in the field of computer graphics. The indoor scenes synthesized by the above technique have fixed layouts. To allow more explicit control of structure variations (Objective 4), we have introduced an interface for designing indoor scenes with convertible furniture layouts, which can automatically transform to each other to support multi-functions [Journal 4]. We have adopted relatively simple methods in the above papers for learning group-sensitive priors (based on multivariate linear regression) and learning structural variations of objects (mainly based on MeanShift clustering). Inspired by the recent advance of deep generative models, we have experimented with deep learning models to extract more useful information from existing shape exemplars (Objective 2) and design more intelligent structure-adaptive shape editing techniques (Objective 3). Specifically, we have introduced SDM-Net [Journal 3], a deep generative neural network that produces structured deformable meshes. Each structured deformable mesh is essentially a spatial arrangement of closed, deformable mesh parts, with its arrangement respecting the global part-level structure of a shape collection (e.g., chairs, airplanes). SDM-Net is essentially a two-level variational autoencoder (VAE), including PartVAE for encoding the geometry of deformable boxes, and SP-VAE for joint encoding of both part geometry and global structure such as symmetry and support (Objective 2). The structured deformable meshes produced by our generative model are immediately editable in a structure-aware manner (Objective 3), allowing explicit control of structure variations with our intuitive editing interface (Objective 4). The advantages of SDM-Net have been demonstrated in two applications, i.e., shape generation and shape interpolation, in comparison with the respective state-of-the-art methods (Objective 5). Structure-adaptive shape editing might suffer from ambiguities in certain scenarios. To enable more explicit control of structure variations (Objective 4), even for non-professional users, we have been exploring sketch-based interfaces, through which users can depict desired shapes for synthesis or during editing via freehand sketches, in terms of both geometry and structure. However, the structural information is not explicitly reflected by raw sketches. Asking users to manually annotating the structural information during the authoring process brings extra burdens to users. We thus have been developed deep learning-based solutions for semantic segmentation and labeling (i.e., part-level structures) of freehand sketches and achieved significant improvements over the existing techniques [Journals 5 and 6]. The interface demonstrated in [Journal 5] shows how explicit control of geometric and structural variations can be achieved via a sketch-based interface. While in the original proposal we were interested in studying structure-aware editing of man-made objects only, later we found that our ideas can be generalized to other domains. For example, human faces exhibit explicit geometric variations in individual face components and implicit/subtle structural variations among facial components. We thus have tried to extended the above ideas to the face domain by modeling face component manifolds using the aligned face components extracted from a large-scale face dataset (Objective 2) and using a feature mapping module to combine face components in a structured way. This leads to an end-to-end deep neural network and our DeepFaceDrawing system. In [Journal 7], which was presented at SIGGRAPH 2020, we show that DeepFaceDrawing is able to synthesize photo-realistic face images with rich geometric variations and subtle structural variations (Objectives 3 and 4) even from rough and incomplete sketched faces. The DeepFaceDrawing work is an important part of the Ph.D. thesis (see the submitted abstract in Part C) by my student, Mr. Wanchao Su, who is going to defending his thesis in the summer of 2021.

11237116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11237116.value: Man-made objects exhibit rich structural information, which can be captured by the relationships between object parts. Individual parts often exhibit rich geometric variations. Effective extraction of such geometric and structural variations from a collection of shapes in the same category can enable the effective synthesis of new shapes with geometric and structural variations. We have demonstrated how to achieve this goal using two different approaches: a more geometry-oriented approach leveraging certain prior knowledge (via a human pose) [Journal 1] and a deep learning-based approach [Journal 3]. Geometric and structural variations exist not only in man-made objects but also indoor scenes, where the structure variations are reflected by relative positions and orientations of scene objects. We have shown that it is possible to extract the structural knowledge from an existing 2D floor plan database and use such knowledge for helping synthesize new, structurally valid indoor scenes with limited input from users [Journal 2]. We have also shown that to facilitate multi-function usages, such scene layouts are not necessarily fixed, and we have designed a novel interactive system for designing convertible indoor scene layouts [Journal 4]. Since ordinary users are more familiar with 2D interfaces instead of 3D interfaces, we have explored sketch-based interfaces for explicit control of geometric and structural variations. To achieve this, we have to associate structural information with sketched objects. Since manually annotating such information is tedious, we have developed deep learning-based solutions for automatic segmentation and labeling of freehand sketches, including sketched man-made objects [Journals 5 and 6]. We have developed intuitive interfaces for sketch-based 3D modeling [Journal 5] and sketch-based face image generation [Journal 7]. The project led to in total 7 journal publications, including 4 in ACM Transactions on Graphics (the best journal in the field of computer graphics) and 2 in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (the second-best graphics journal). The papers [Journals 2, 3, and 7] were presented at SIGGRAPH Asia 2017, SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, and SIGGRAPH 2020, respectively (SIGGRAPH and SIGGRAPH Asia are the best graphics conferences). In addition, the paper in [Journal 5] received the Runner-up for the 2019 Best Paper Award by Computer Graphics & Applications.

11237116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11237116.value: There are multiple areas to be explored in the future. We have introduced various 2D and 3D interfaces for explicit control of structural variations in [Journals 1, 3, 5]. It will be interesting to reformulate the algorithms behind these interfaces for reconstructing rich shapes with details from images. We have shown the power of deep learning techniques for generating new shapes in the same category [Journal 3] and face images [Journal 7]. It will be exciting to investigate how to extend these techniques to encode shapes of different categories in a single deep network. In addition, structural refinement is formulated as a post-processing step in [Journal 3]. Achieving the same goal or even better performance using a sub-network module in our deep neural network would be interesting to explore.

11237116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11237116.value: Observing rich geometric and structural variations in shapes, especially in man-made objects, we have explored various techniques to capture such variations of shapes in the same category. We have also developed algorithms and interfaces for facilitating structure-aware shape editing and generation. It is shown that deep learning-based solutions are very effective for encoding not only the geometric information but also the structural information, since deep learning models have been proved effective for extracting both low-level and high-level features. To enable sketch-based interfaces for intuitive control of structural variations, we have developed novel sketch segmentation and labeling techniques, which are also made possible due to the recent advance of deep learning techniques. We have successfully extended such ideas to indoor scene synthesis and sketch-based face image generation. The presented techniques have demonstrated the importance of structural information for various applications such as shape editing, shape generation, shape interpolation, indoor scene synthesis, etc. We hope this research will not only lead to novel tools for shape modeling and processing but also inspire new research studies to exploit the structural information for new applications.

11242716.value: 有砟軌道系統是最常用和經濟的軌道系統。鐵軌的無損檢測已有大量的研究，商業技術（軌道和軌道幾何測量車以及超聲波檢測車）可以用來檢測鐵軌的水平，對齊，軌距以及起皺。然而，評估軌道道砟工作狀態的研究很有限。位於軌枕下的道砟損壞是不可能通過目視檢查鑑定出來。然而這種損壞會影響軌道的穩定性和減弱軌道的平穩性。當鐵路道砟有損壞，用來支撐軌枕的道砟剛度會減小。這會改變軌道系統的振動特性。所以，通過測量在動力荷載作用下的軌道振動和通過求解逆問題來計算道砟剛度來檢測位於軌枕下道砟的損傷是可能的。在這個方案投入使用之前，必須克服一些困難。第一，眾所周知，軌道的剛度是依賴於施加給軌道的荷載的大小。所以，如果測量的動力的大小和來自列車的荷載非常不同時，用所識別的軌道剛度來進行軌道安全監測就不可靠。為了確保所識別的軌道剛度的實用性，擬建項目推薦進行更加複雜的列車試驗。第二，軌道道砟自然特性是不確定的。必須採用概率論明確地處理這個不確定性問題。第三，車-軌耦合系統的建模很複雜。數值迭代法可以用於耦合系統振動分析，但分析結果對很多因素（車輛的懸掛系統，車輪（接觸面）和鐵軌的缺陷（縱剖面））很敏感。研究者必須小心選擇合適的列車-軌道模型。擬建項目將克服這些困難，並且開發出一種使用運營的列車荷載進行有砟軌道安全監測的方法。其理念是通過連續地測量列車和軌道系統的縱向振動和使用新開發的貝葉斯模型修正的方法識別軌道的動態剛度。

11242716.label: Realisation of objectives
11242716.value: All objectives were successfully achieved. Several classes of models were developed to capture the vibration characteristics of the ballasted track system in Objective 1. The ballast layer was modelled as a linear material resulting in a relatively simple model class at the beginning. Frequency- and modal- domain data can be employed for the model updating of the system owing to its linear and elastic nature. This class of models was modified by considering the nonlinear stress-strain behaviour of the ballast layer. Various nonlinear relationships were employed to form different classes of models. Owing to the inelastic nature of the system, time-domain data has to be employed in the model updating process. The original frequency- and modal- based Bayesian formulation was modified in this project to provide the necessary solid foundation for the determination of a general and reliable posterior probability density function (PDF) of the set of uncertain model parameters in Objective 3. Unlike most structural engineering applications of the Bayesian model updating framework, the uncertainties associated with the model parameters of the train-track system are very high in nature. Owing to the lack of measured data and the high complexity of the model class, model updating problems of this kind are usually classified as unidentifiable with a very complex and high-dimension manifold as the posterior PDF. The determination of such PDF is extremely difficult if not impossible for real world systems. In this project, this highly complex posterior (updated) PDF was approximated by samples generated from the newly developed multi-level Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation technique. This method allows the calculation of the posterior PDF without assuming that it follows a particular distribution. As a result, the solution method is general and it is appliable to model updating problems outside the field of train system safety. One main difficulty in the development of the MCMC-based Bayesian methodology for the approximation of the posterior PDF of uncertain model parameters is that there was no commonly accepted and theoretically rigorous way to determine the “length” of the Markov chain from the literature. This directly controls the number of sampling levels in the MCMC process. Most existing MCMC-based methods stopped the sampling process subjective or through ad hoc convergency check. It must be pointed out that if the number of sampling levels is too large, the samples will too close to each other that will underestimate the posterior uncertainties associated with the identified model parameters. On the other hand, if the number of sampling levels is too small, the samples have not yet arrived to the important region of the parameter space. The approximation of the posterior PDF will be very bad, and the posterior uncertainties associated with the identified results will usually be overestimated. To overcome this difficulty, a series of theoretically sound stopping criteria was developed in this project. This project focused not only on the time-domain but also the frequency- and modal- domain data. By extending the developed MCMC-based Bayesian method, a new modal identification method was developed though sequential sampling technique. This method contributes a lot in the field of structural health monitoring of civil engineering structures, such as bridges and buildings (see the published journal and conference papers). A set of measured data is essential for the proposed Bayesian model updating methodology. In Objective 2, the vibrations of both the train and the track were measured using accelerometers. A comprehensive sets of train-track vibration data were measured under various train speeds (with the in-kind support from MTR). The experimental setup consists of sensor installation on both the train (for measuring the vibration near the axle and the bogie) and the track (for measuring the vibration of the rails and the sleepers). From the literature, most research focused either the measurement of the train vibration or the track vibration, and it is difficult to find work simultaneously considers both the train and track vibrations. The two sets of data were synchronized through GPS to minimize the time lag between them. The problem of measurement noise is unavoidable, and it is explicitly addressed by following the Bayesian approach. Instead of pinpointing a set of model parameters, the methodology targets in calculating the posterior PDF of the uncertain parameters. It must be pointed out that this experimental setup is not only applicable for train-track system. The PI of this project successfully extend this experimental setup for the vibration monitoring of bridges, buildings and wind turbines (see the research outputs for the published journal and conference papers). Objective 4 is about the matching between the track stiffness identified from the proposed methodology to the records from MTR through meetings and discussions with the representative from MTR. With the help from Dr Wong MT, Permanent way engineer from MTR, a series of meetings were arranged. Good matching between the results from this project and the records from MTR were observed. As the records from MTR are confidential, it is impossible to published the results in this objective. Two undergraduate students were trained through the research activities of this project. One of them was financially supported by this project (Undergraduate student). The two students participated in a series of vibration tests (field tests). They contributed not only during the measurement but also in the planning and discussion of measured results. A presentation was given by the student (with financial support) in City University of Hong Kong on 26 January 2018 (with undergraduate students as audience).

11242716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11242716.value: The project was successfully completed with fruitful outcomes. A total of 6 journal papers tougher with at 10 conference papers were published for reporting the research findings from this project. Objective 1 focused on the development of model classes for capturing the vibration behaviour of the train-track system with particular concern on the track stiffness, and Objective 2 focused on the experimental design and implementation for obtaining the vibration data of the system for the purpose of model updating. A list of model classes were developed, and they were reported together with the experimental work in references (C2, C5, C8 and C10). Objective 3 is the most difficult part in the project. It is the development of an MCMC-based Bayesian model updating methodology. This project not only successfully developed the methodology, but also, extended the methodology such that it can be effectively applied under various situations. The research findings related to the frequency- and modal-domain data were presented in references (J4, J5, C3, C6 and C7), and the research findings related to the time-domain data were presented in references (C5, C8, C9, C10). It must be pointed out that references (C5 and C8) received the best presentation awards in the HKSTAM annual conference at 2018 and 2019, respectively. Objective 4 is about the matching between the track stiffness identified from the proposed methodology to the records from MTR through meetings and discussions with the representative from MTR. With the help from Dr Wong MT, Permanent way engineer from MTR, a series of meetings were arranged. Good matching between the results from this project and the records from MTR were observed. The experimental setup developed from this project was extended for wind turbine vibration monitoring. The research findings were published in a series of journal and conference papers including (J1, J2, J3, J6, C1 and C4). With the success of this project, the PI, Ir Dr Lam, has be invited to give many keynotes, invited lectures and distinguished lectures. Ir Dr Lam was also invited by Prof NI YQ, Chair Professor from the Hong Kong Polytechnical University, to submit a research proposal. The project “Enhancing safety, punctuality and ride comfort of railway transportation: From local metro system to global high-speed rail network” was successfully funded by UGC, Research Impact Fund (RIF) 2018/19 with a total grant of HK$ 5,892,320, and Ir Dr Lam has received HK$1,000,000 (Project number: 8799008).

11242716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11242716.value: The most important outcome of this project is the developed MCMC-based Bayesian model updating methodology. In general, the main purpose of this methodology is to identify a system conditional on a class of models utilizing a set of measured data. In this project, it was extended to cover the selection of the most plausible model class from a list of model classes conditional on a set of measured data. The outstanding feature of the developed methodology is the consideration of uncertainties induced from the modelling error of the selected class of models and the measurement error of the set of data. Unlike most existing methods, the proposed methodology doesn’t need to assume the prediction error to be normal distribution. The posterior probability density function (PDF) is approximated by samples generated by MCMC simulation. With some modifications, the methodology can be extended to be applied in various situations other than the safety of ballasted track. Currently, the methodology is extended to model updating in the field of bridges and buildings. Focusing on the field of railway safety, research work had been carried out in the funded RIF (8799008) in developing a Bayesian method to be applicable in high speed train systems.

11242716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11242716.value: Ballasted track system is the most popular and cost-effective railway track system. Extensive research has been carried out on non-destructive evaluation of the rails, and commercialized techniques are available for inspecting railway level and alignment, rail gauges and corrugation. However, research work for assessing the condition of railway ballast is very limited. This project focused on the non-destructive evaluation of railway ballast through vibration test of the track system. Some difficulties must be addressed before this method can be applied. The properties of railway ballast are uncertain in nature. The probability theory must be adopted to explicitly handle the uncertainty problem. The modelling of the train-track system is complicated and the analysis result is sensitive to many factors. Great care must be taken in the selection of an appropriate train-track model. The proposed project will address these difficulties and develop a ballasted track safety monitoring method utilizing operational measurements. The idea is to continuously measure the vertical vibrations of the train-track system, and identify the dynamic track stiffness by the newly developed Bayesian model updating method.

11247716.label: Realisation of objectives
11247716.value: Natural killer (NK)-92MI cells have been commonly regarded as one of the most active type of natural killer cells, which are capable of killing target cells rapidly within few hours in in-vitro experiments. With our various designs of microwells and microchannels, we showed the dynamics of NK cell activity within this cell line, and how their cytotoxicity can be adjusted by different level of microwell confinement and microchannel connections. Different sizes of microwells trapped different number of cells inside. In smaller microwells, NK cell cytotoxicity was significantly reduced due to their incapability of finding the “correct” target cell to kill; with increased microwell size, more complex interactions increase the probability of NK cells to form effective interaction pairs with target cells, resulting in promoted NK cell activity. Target cell death can also provide conditioned medium that decrease the viability of other target cells in the surrounding microenvironment through the bystander effect, resulting in significantly enhanced overall NK cell cytotoxicity in this region. Microchannel connections provided path for diffusion of cytokines and biomolecules and enhanced overall NK cell cytotoxicity. NK cell cytotoxicity in platforms with microchannel connections was much higher compared to NK cells confined in isolated microwells. These cells with different degrees of confinement showed much lower cytotoxicity than NK cells in typical culture dishes. Deficiency of NK cells in clinical trials compared to in-vitro experimental results has been a major roadblock in NK cell related cancer therapy. While most of the recent NK cell studies focus on population based or single cell interactions, cell interactions in small groups may be the missing link. Since cancer cells in tumor are separated into small groups by extracellular matrix, microwells with different sizes and connections can provide a better biomimetic platform for cancer immunology study. On the other side, high NK and target cell seeding densities were required in order to achieve homogeneous cell seeding in the microwells with different sizes. The NK-target cell interactions were complex and could have frequent z-direction movement, which made it difficult to identify all NK-target cell conjugations. The cells were also in contact or in close proximity with each other, which made it difficult to separate bystander killing from direct NK cell killing. In this case, extensive manual tracking of the cell behaviors was needed in this study due to the complex cell interactions that made it difficult to apply computer-assisted tools for cell viability analysis. The NK-92MI cell line utilized in this study was specifically modified for fast and effective cancer cell treatment, whereas further studies using normal NK cells isolated from peripheral blood in these connected microwells will be also be important. However, these analyses were effective in evaluating the effects of physical constraints on NK-target cell interactions and the dynamics of NK cell cytotoxicity in a systematical way. Thus the platforms presented here could provide insight for developing effective immunotherapy methods in the future. While most of the existing studies on NK cell migration focus on the establishment of cell polarization in accordance to localized chemokine concentration difference via various receptors on cell plasma, or the simple transmembrane invasion essay to evaluate cell migration ability, reproducible contact guidance effect is often underrated in the field. There were reports on lymphocyte cell migration on two dimensional or 3D platforms under specified chemotaxis gradient, where NK cell trajectories had a lot of side or even backward movements during the process, which could be related to topographical effect created by the gel matrix or cell-cell contact. In this paper, topographical effects on NK cell migration in microchannels with and without chemo-attractant were systematically studied. By simplifying NK cell migration track into one dimensional model using microchannel confinement, the results revealed that topographical modifications could affect chemotaxis NK cell migration by disrupting NK cell polarization through externally induced cell deformation. Moreover, such topographical modifications could even induce non-polarized NK cells to deform and migrate in specific orientation even without chemo-attractant. Transwell migration assay is currently the most widely used method for NK cell invasiveness characterization. Although it can help to evaluate cell deformability and responses to chemokine gradient, it fails to address the importance of topographical change to NK cell migration, which is emphasized in this paper. There are also many studies on lymphocyte migration in collagen gel with various porosities. While collagen gels can provide complex and biomimetic topographical effect which is reflected by the dynamic migration behavior of cells inside, extracellular matrix structures and dimensions could not be precisely controlled or reproduced which makes it difficult to evaluate the effects in detail. Thus the engineered platforms used in this project provided a good compliment to the current field of NK cell chemotaxis study and could lead to better understanding of the complex intra and extra-cellular process during chemotaxis induced NK cell migration.

11247716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11247716.value: Natural killer (NK) cells serve an important role in immune system by recognizing and killing the potentially malignant cells without antigen sensitization, and could be promising in cancer therapy. We have designed and fabricated microwell arrays with microchannel connections in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrates to study the interaction dynamics of NK-92MI cells with MCF7 breast cancer cells using time-lapse imaging by fluorescence microscopy for 15 h. Although cell seeding density was the same, NK cell cytotoxicity was found to be higher in larger microwells, which is manifested as increased target death ratio from 13.7±3.1% to 46.3±3.3% and shorter triggering time of first target lysis from 502±49 min to 391±63 min in 150×150 µm2 microwells comparing to 50×50 µm2 wells in 15 h. Mirochannel connection between adjacent microwells of the same size increased the overall target death ratio by >10%, while connection between microwells of different sizes led to significantly increased target death ratio and delayed first target lysis in smaller microwells. Our findings reveal unique cell interaction dynamics such as initiation and stimulation of NK cell cytotoxicity in a confined microenvironment, which is different from population-based study, and the results could lead to a better understanding of the dynamics of NK cell cytotoxicity. NK cells are lymphocytes which serve an important role in immune system by recognizing and killing potentially malign cells without antigen sensitization, and could be utilized in cancer therapy. NK cell migration is an essential process to find and kill target cells, which is well known to be driven by chemotaxis effect. NK cells also experience topographical effect induced by extracellular matrix (ECM) during their migration. However, topographical effect on NK cell locomotion in three-dimensional (3D) environment is not well studied yet. In this work, PDMS-based platforms containing microchannels with different types of perturbations and decorated with varies surface patterns were fabricated to systematically study the topographical effect on NK cell migration with and without chemotaxis effect. The results showed that perturbation sites in channels induced pauses and reversals in chemotaxis driven NK cell migration. Surface topography such as gratings in confined environment could introduce directional preference to NK cell movement even without chemo-attractant. These findings showed that NK cells migration could be controlled by contact guidance, which provides future possibility to manipulate NK cell migration in controlled in-vitro bioengineering systems. Results in this study showed that the complex topography of 3D microenvironment in ECM could have significant effects on NK cell migration in different tissues and organs, and provided insight for explaining dynamics of NK cell activities in clinical experiments.

11250716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11250716.value: Link traversal has been a usual practice for web page surfing. Similar practice on videos, nevertheless, is yet to be realized as audio-visual content are relatively difficult to edit than html pages. The idea of multimedia hyperlinking is to insert links between fragments of videos such that shared entities (e.g., object, person and event) are connected for efficient content navigation. Manual creation of hyperlinks, particularly for large and unfamiliar archive of multimedia content, is expected to be a tedious experience. The ambition of this project is to research techniques and algorithms to automate video hyperlinking – a timely problem in multimedia driven by applications such as detail-on-demand browsing and video advertising. Creation of hyperlinks involves two major steps. Starting from a large video collection, the process digs into underlying multimedia content shared among video fragments and subsequently establishes links among them for content-based navigation. Browsing behaviors are considered along the process such that, by traversing the links, user information need can be satisfied while diverse perspectives of the information are exposed to users. Different from information searching where relevant items are ranked with user search intent in mind, hyperlinking serves in the scenarios of detail-on-demand and exploratory browsing without user knowledge in advance. Hence, the created linkages are expected to be error-free as much as possible with diversification in content coverage, versus searching where right information are strived to be ranked as high as possible. Achieving this goal is by no means easy due to the need of techniques in reliable multimedia content mining and link selection, which remain largely open challenges. Yet this is achievable due to feasibility of million-scale visual entities mining demonstrated recently and new results from vision and database communities regarding meaningful nearest neighbor search, which can be applied for link selection. This project considers hyperlinking beyond search ranking by researching issues in mining of multi-modal entities and the statistical (i.e., hubness and local intrinsic dimensionality) and correlative properties of entities in leading to robust hyperlinking practical for different video browsing scenarios. The project targets for “linking things inside multimedia archive”, enabling video content more easily accessible and consumable – a problem becoming increasingly important due to massive video data growth. This project will contribute by investigating different aspects influencing the utility of hyperlinking, including anchor popularity, linking uncertainty, information coverage versus diversification, which are seldom studied and yet to be integrally explored in the literature. 在網頁瀏覽中，基於超鏈結的跳轉是非常普遍的操作。然而，相對於網頁中的超鏈結，在視頻中嵌入基於多媒體內容的超鏈結卻是相當困難的。多媒體超鏈結的創建一般是基於相同的實體對象，比如，物體，人物和事件。該類超鏈結的創建可以有效的提高瀏覽多媒體內容的效率。考慮到龐大而內容繁雜的多媒體視頻庫，人為的創建該類超鏈結將會是非常低效的。本項目的目標即是探索自動化的創建該類超鏈結的算法和技術。相關的研究成果可以有效的促進各種多媒體應用的發展，例如需求導向的視頻瀏覽系統和視頻廣告嵌入系統。 多媒體超鏈結的創建主要有兩個步驟。首先，基於視頻內容，對視頻數據庫中的各種實體對象進行挖掘。然後，對於分享相同實體對象的視頻片段進行鏈接從而便利視頻內容的快速瀏覽。在基於鏈結的瀏覽過程中，用戶的信息需求可以得到有效的滿足，同時，其他各種方面的信息也會進一步提供給用戶。傳統的視頻檢索系統通常是基於用戶的搜索意圖進行排名，然而，超鏈結的應用場景則是假設對於用戶的想法並不可知，通過需求導向和探索式搜索最終使得讓用戶快速獲取信息。基於此，多媒體超鏈結在盡可能準確的同時也要保證內容的多樣性。由於視頻內容挖掘和鏈接選擇技術仍然基本是一個未探索的領域，創建多媒體超鏈結會是一個非常困難的任務。同時，最近的百萬級別的實體對象挖掘技術的應用以及計算機視覺和數據庫領域的基於內容的近鄰搜索技術的發展讓我們看到了有效創建多媒體超鏈結的曙光。本項目計劃通過研究多媒體實體對象挖掘技術以及統計（例如，樞紐程度和本征維度）和實體對象的協從特徵對不同的視頻瀏覽情境來創建魯棒的多媒體超鏈結。 本項目通過對多媒體內容中的各種實體對象創建鏈結從而讓用戶可以快速的瀏覽視頻內容和獲取信息。基於當前網絡視頻內容的快速增長，該功能將會是非常迫切的需求。本項目將對多個鮮有觸及的領域進行系統的研究，包括，錨鏈結的流行度，超鏈結的不確定性以及信息的覆蓋程度和多樣化程度。

11250716.label: Realisation of objectives
11250716.value: We have studied the statistical properties of dataset for hyperlinking, specifically hubness and local intrinsic dimension, on a large video dataset Blip10000 which consists of 3,000 hours of videos. We have run intensive simulation on the dataset to verify the usefulness of hub and LID in uncovering the data characteristics of video segments for hyperlinking. Based on these findings, we have developed greedy algorithms and neural networks for video hyperlinking. Objective-1: Multimodal entity mining The main task here is to segment a video into fragments and each fragment is treated as a target candidate for linking. Initially, we treat a fragment as an uninterrupted speech sentence. Using the speech boundary, however, results in excessive number of very short fragments. On the other hand, speech boundary is undefined for silent video segments. Hence, the duration of a speechless fragment can be lengthy. To strike a balance, we propose a heuristic based speech-driven fragmentation algorithm. The basic idea is to merge short fragments based on the thresholding technique while uniformly splitting the fragments with only the visual streams. Experiments are conducted to study the use of different multi-modal features for fragment representation. For visual information, the features include concept histogram and the pool5 features extracted from convolutional neural networks (CNN). Five CNNs are trained separately on different datasets (ImageNet, ImageNet-Shuffle, Places, TRECVid MED and SIN). In addition to global features, local descriptors extracted from visual entities are also considered for 545 object classes. Each entity is represented by a box predictor feature derived from Faster R-CNN with Inception ResNet pre-trained on Open Image dataset. For speech transcripts, the features include bag-of-words and word2vec representation using the improved skip-gram model. Name entities recognition is also performed and the identified entities are also represented with word2vec. These features are combined in different ways to evaluate the similarity between an anchor and a target fragments. Objective-2: Risk and context aware hyperlinking Through the statistical analysis on Blip10000 dataset, we have quantified the appropriateness of link anchors and targets for hyperlinking. This is carried out by conducting simulation to study the hub phenomenon, the correlation among hubness, local intrinsic dimension and context, and the statistical differences between anchors and targets. The simulation involves 122 link anchors provided by the TRECVid organizers. The hub phenomenon is measured based on the skewness of hub distribution. Using different modalities and their combinations, the hub distribution is characterized by the popularities of video fragments measured using reverse k-nearest neighbor. While hubness defines the popularity of a fragment, its risk in hyperlinking is determined by the number of intrinsic dimensions computed based on the maximum likelihood estimation. The context is determined by diversity, which is computed by the mean pairwise distance of an anchor to its k-nearest neighbors. The correlation among these measurements (hubness, local intrinsic dimension, context) are investigated to quantify the difficulty of linking. The results are also leveraged for proposal of greedy algorithms in linking anchors and targets. We have also developed neural networks based on neighborhood structure preservation for video hyperlinking. We propose and develop a generalized multi-modal auto-encoder for cross-modal hyperlinking. The main idea is to learn the embeddings of visual and speech modalities using the paired visual-speech or visual-text training examples. Different from the conventional feature embedding approaches, the proposed embedding is learnt with the objective function to preserve the neighborhood structure of video fragments. Furthermore, the embedding is also expected to reconstruct a different modality when being decoded using the network. As local data characteristics of a dataset plays a critical role in hyperlinking, the proposed structure preserving network is found to be robust for video hyperlinking. In addition, learning cross-modal embedding also enables the aboutness measurement, where the linking between an anchor and a target is determined by multi-modal complementary beyond correlation. The proposed network also addresses the limitations of semantic representation network, the first version of the neural network developed in this project, which requires large amount of anchor-target pairs for model training. The developed multi-modal auto-encoder can be trained using off-the-shelf video-caption pairs available in the public datasets. Considering the network complexity, we also propose a simplified or light version of the network by detaching the decoder for modality construction from the model training. Objective-3: Hyperlinking presentation, visualization and application As TRECVid does not continue the benchmarking of video hyperlinking, we do not have enough labeled anchors and targets to investigate the effect of hyperlinking presentation and visualization on the Blip10000 dataset. We concentrate the study on interactive video search and the experiments are conducted on the IACC.3 and V3C1 datasets instead. Both datasets come along with ad-hoc and known-item search queries. Specifically, the videos are linked with various multi-modal features, including the hand-crafted and deep learning features, for interactive search. The search is started by user formulating a textual query and then the system retrieves a rank list of related and similar video fragments. User can interactively refine a query or select a retrieved fragment as anchor to further explore the linked targets. As search performance is highly dependent on the effectiveness of query formulation and refinement, we conduct a user study to evaluate the differences between the automatic and interactive query formulations. The study involves a total of 20 users who uses two different search systems to search the target videos of queries, and the search time for each query is limited to 6 minutes. The results of study are utilized to analyse how the users formulate queries, including the selection of fragments as anchors to quickly navigate the search results and the effectiveness of feature embedding for cross-modal search.

11250716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11250716.value: We have achieved satisfactory performance in the benchmarking of video hyperlinking organized by TRECVid. The first developed neural network, named as Semantic Representation Network, together with the greedy algorithms proposed based on the analysis of hubness and local intrinsic dimension [ICMR 2017], has attained the top performance in several measures including Precision@5 and mAP (mean Average Precision) [TRECVid 2017]. A better version of the network, named generalized multi-modal auto-encoder, attains even higher performance for this task on Blip10000 dataset. Comprehensive experiments are conducted to evaluate the effect of video fragmentations, use of various multi-modal features with different combinations, and variants of neural networks. The proposed generalized multi-modal auto-encoder achieves the overall best performance on this dataset on several measures including Precision@5, MAP and MAiSP (mean average interpolated segment precision). Further late fusing the result of the network with concept histogram and bag-of-text-words, we achieve the state-of-the-art performance in video hyperlinking on the Blip1000 dataset [TMM 2020]. In addition, the light version of the network also attains very competitive performance to the full version of the network. Through the experiments, we also conclude that there is no statistical difference between using the conventional fixed length video fragmentation and the algorithm proposed in this project (i.e., heuristic-based sentence-level segmentation). Aligning fragments with start and end times of speech may not be critical for boosting the recall performance. However, in terms of user experience, proper alignment indeed helps users in finding more relevant targets of an anchor. We also apply the results for benchmarking of interactive video search [VBS 2018-2020]. As query formulation plays a key role in search, a user study involving 20 users is conducted to investigate how users refine queries and select fragments as anchor to retrieve target fragments for browsing [TOMM 2020]. In general, a good searcher keeps refining queries within the first 30 seconds until reaching a page with potential target videos. A searcher may then perform browsing throughout the entire search session. One way exploited by user in the query refinement is by selecting candidate fragments as anchors and then browse the target fragments, either further selecting a target as anchor for search or simply browsing the targets to identify relevant videos of a query. In our analysis, although linking is able to contribute positive videos and speed up searching, most of the true positive video fragments contributed by linking can also be found by other search modes.

11250716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11250716.value: Video fragmentation remains a problem in video hyperlinking. Most of the researches assume static fragmentation, where the boundaries of fragments will not change regardless of anchors. This assumption makes video processing rather straightforward for requiring only offline fragmentation and indexing of video content for hyperlinking. The assumption, however, has oversimplified hyperlinking because a pre-fragmented target may be fully satisfied for an anchor but only partially relevant to another anchor. User experience could be frustrated for requiring fast forward or backward around a target to search for content of interest. In principle, the fragment boundary should be determined on-the-fly when a query anchor is presented. It is worth studying new algorithms that can adaptively adjust fragment boundaries during linking. The mining and indexing algorithms also need to be re-visited to deal with anchor-dependent fragment boundaries. Another issue is that the proposed neural networks can be extended to include attention mechanism to model aboutness within and across different modalities. Ideally, the mechanism will allow the network to selectively attend to different local entities and then link the entities to separate targets. The attention mechanism can also be applied at feature level to enhance the robustness of linking.

11250716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11250716.value: The aim of this project is to study new techniques and algorithms to enhance the accessibility of video content in large dataset through linking video fragments. The project first investigates the characteristic of data to quantify the risk of hyperlinking by local statistical properties of hubness, local intrinsic dimension and diversity. The study shows that both anchor and target fragments should have lower value of local intrinsic dimension, while the anchor fragments should have higher hub value than the target fragments. With these observations, the project proposes greedy algorithms to identify anchors and then to retrieve targets for the selected anchors. As the statistical properties of video fragments depends on the underlying multi-modal features, this project also proposes variants of neural networks that learn feature embedding by modeling the aboutness within and across different modalities of videos. Particularly, the networks are trained to preserve the local neighborhood structure of video fragments. Experimental results verify that the proposed networks can exhibit higher performance in video hyperlinking than using other hand-crafted and deep learning features. The project also explores interactive video search where user navigates the search space by following video links to efficiently find desired videos.

11253316.label: Project Objectives
11253316.value: The first objective is to design and fabricate a thermo-optic mode converter based on a 3D polymer-waveguide four-arm MZI. This device allows the conversion among the LP01, LP11a, LP11b, and LP21a modes, depending on the electric currents applied to the heating electrodes deposited on the four arms of the MZI. The second objective is to design and fabricate a four-mode (de)multiplexer based on a 3D polymer-waveguide structure, which can be a series of cascaded horizontal and vertical directional couplers or a set of adiabatic waveguide transitions formed in two layers. The mode (de)multiplexer is designed to spatially combine or separate the LP01, LP11a, LP11b, and LP21a modes. The third objective is to integrate a thermo-optic 3D multi-arm MZI with a matching 3D four-mode (de)multiplexer, so that any of the LP01, LP11a, LP11b, and LP21a modes launched into the MZI can be routed to any of the output ports of the mode (de)multiplexer to achieve spatial switching of the four modes.

11253316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11253316.value: The global demand for communication bandwidths is growing rapidly, which owes much to the continuous increase in the Internet traffic. There is an urgent need to largely increase the transmission capacities of optical networks to satisfy the market. Mode-division multiplexing (MDM), which allows different modes in a multimode fiber to carry different channels, is a particularly promising technology for enhancing the transmission capacity of a fiber, and is a focus of research in the field of optical communications worldwide. The goal of the project is to demonstrate a new and powerful optical waveguide platform for the implementation of mode-switching devices for reconfigurable MDM applications. The key waveguide structure to be considered is a three-dimensional (3D) thermally tunable Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) formed with four single-mode waveguide arms. The four waveguide arms are arranged in two layers and merged with waveguide branches into few-mode waveguides at both ends, where four spatial modes are supported. To achieve switching among the four modes, each waveguide arm of the MZI incorporates a heating electrode for tuning the phase of the light wave. By controlling the phases of the light waves in the four arms, any mode launched into the MZI can be converted into any other mode at the output of the MZI. While the 3D four-arm MZI itself is a very useful mode switch, it can be integrated with a matching 3D fixed four-mode (de)multiplexer to spatially separate the modes. This integrated device thus allows any input mode to be switched to any of the four output ports, a function that is important for a reconfigurable MDM system, where different mode channels are routed to different branches of the network, depending on the network traffic. In this project, these 3D devices will be designed and fabricated with polymer material. The polymer waveguide technology used in the project allows the formation of multilayer structures, which is essential for the realization of the proposed 3D devices. The large thermo-optic coefficient of polymer material also promises efficient thermal tuning, which is important for achieving the proposed switching functions. The project capitalizes on the long history of successes at CityU in the development of novel optical waveguide devices based on the polymer waveguide technology, including the recent works on fixed mode (de)multiplexers. The waveguide platform developed in the project serves to pave the path for the future development of reconfigurable optical networks based on the high-density MDM technology. 隨著互聯網流量的不斷快速增長，全球對網絡帶寬的需求也正在快速增長，大幅度提高光網絡的傳輸能力以滿足市場需求已是當務之急。模分複用技術允許不同模式攜帶不同的光信號在同一根多模光纖中傳輸，能夠成倍地提高光纖的傳輸能力，是一項非常有前景的技術，已成為當前全球在光通信領域的研究熱點。本項目的目標是研發並演示一種新型而又功能强大的光波導平臺，实现可重構模分複用系統的模式開關器件。 本項目所研制的一個關鍵器件結構是一個可以透過熱調控的三維四分枝馬赫曾德干涉儀。此結構由四個单模波導分枝组成，分兩組放置于上下兩層，在輸入和輸出端分別匯聚為一個支持四個模式的少模波導。為實現少模波導中四個模式的相互轉換，在四個分枝波導上分別配置獨立的加熱電極，用以調節各分枝波導中傳輸光的相位。通過獨立調控四個分枝波導的光相位，可使干涉儀輸入端進入的任意模式被轉變為輸出端的任意模式。此三維四分枝干涉儀可以單獨使用，實現模式開關功能，亦可以與另一個三維的四模式解複用器集成使用，將干涉儀輸入端少模波導的任意模式分配到解複用器輸出端的四個單模波導中的任意一個。這種動態解模分複用功能在未來可重構模分複用系統中將會大派用場，因為在這種系統中，不同模式信道需要根據網絡流量的改變被調配到不同的網絡分枝傳輸。本項目所提出的三維結構將會用聚合物材料來設計與製作。 本項目所使用的聚合物波導技術能夠製作多層立體結構，這正是實現三維波導器件所必需的。聚合物材料所具有的高熱光系數能夠提供高效的熱調控，也正是實現光開關功能的重要保證。我們多年來在香港城市大學利用聚合物波導技術成功開發了多種新型的光波導器件，包括最近完成的固定模式（解）複用器，這些工作為本項目的成功完成奠定了堅實的基礎。本項目所開發的波導平臺將為未來基於密集模分複用技術的可重構式光網絡的發展鋪平道路。

11253316.label: Realisation of objectives
11253316.value: All the project objectives have been addressed and achieved. Thanks to the 3D polymer waveguide technology established through the studies in the previous GRF project CityU 112113 “Design and fabrication of mode-division (de)multiplexers with polymer optical waveguides”, we were able to fabricate the 3D waveguide devices proposed in this project with well-controlled parameters. (1) Thermo-optic 3D four-arm Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) mode converters We successfully designed and fabricated thermo-optic 3D four-arm MZI mode converters with polymer material to achieve broadband polarization-insensitive switching among the first four spatial modes (the LP01, LP11a, LP11b, and LP21a modes) of a few-mode waveguide. Our typical fabricated device offers mode-extinction ratios higher than 14 dB at 1550 nm and a switching time shorter than 3.7 ms. The switching power for each arm of the MZI is about 10 mW. The structure is scalable for more modes, as it allows a large few-mode core to be divided into more layers and each layer can accommodate many arms. The first objective of the project has been fully addressed. (2) 3D mode (de)multiplexers We considered two types of 3D mode (de)multiplexers. The first type is based on adiabatic waveguide branches formed in two layers. This type works for four spatial modes (the LP01, LP11a, LP11b, and LP21a modes) and, therefore, can be integrated with the thermo-optic 3D four-arm MZI mode switch described above to form a four-mode router. The second type is based on cascaded vertical asymmetric directional couplers (DCs). Using five cascaded vertical DCs, we successfully designed and fabricated a six-mode (de)multiplexer with polymer waveguides. Our typical fabricated device, which has a length of 29 mm, shows coupling ratios varying between 61% to 90% and modal crosstalks between 29.0 to 12.5 dB in the wavelength range from 1530 to 1565 nm with weak polarization dependence. The proposed 3D structure is in principle scalable, as the number of the spatial modes that can be (de)multiplexed can be increased by simply increasing the number of the vertical DCs. It is the polymer waveguide technology that limits the length and the uniformity of the waveguides that can be achieved. The second objective of the project has been fully addressed. (3) Mode routers We designed and fabricated a broadband mode router by integrating a 3D thermo-optic MZI mode switch with a matching 3D mode (de)multiplexer based on adiabatic waveguide branches formed in two layers. The device can route any of the four spatial modes (the LP01, LP11a, LP11b, and LP21a modes) launched to the MZI into any of the four output ports of the mode (de)multiplexer to achieve spatial switching of the four modes. Our experimental device, fabricated with polymer material, shows crosstalks lower than −8.2 dB in the C-band. In addition, we successfully demonstrated another two thermo-optic mode routers. One is based on a thermally-induced long-period grating integrated with an asymmetric waveguide branch designed for two spatial modes. Our experimental device fabricated with polymer material shows a mode selectivity higher than 12 dB over the C+L band at a switching power of 198 mW. This study is part of the collaboration with the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China. The other one is based on the structure of cascaded vertical DCs that incorporate heater electrodes. Our experimental devices fabricated with polymer material show low switching powers (~20 mW), short response times (3 – 4 ms), and high extinction ratios (>14 dB) over the C band. These devices are polarization-insensitive and could find applications in reconfigurable mode-division-multiplexing systems. The third objective of the project has been fully achieved. (4) Additional studies In addition to the studies described above, we proposed and demonstrated a high-order-mode-pass mode (de)multiplexer based on the structure of a 3D waveguide directional coupler formed with a few-mode core and a single-mode core that has a higher refractive index. Unlike a conventional directional coupler, where the two cores have the same refractive index, the hybrid-core structure allows the design of a directional coupler to couple only the fundamental mode of a few-mode core to a single-mode core without affecting the high-order modes of the few-mode core. Our experimental device formed with polymer material has a length of 15 mm and a coupling ratio for the LP01 mode varying from 92.5% to 98.7% in the C band. The crosstalks to the single-mode core from the two high-order modes (the LP11a and LP11b modes) of the three-mode core are smaller than −13.8 dB in the C band. The performance of the device is polarization-insensitive. The proposed hybrid-core mode (de)multiplexer allows an effective control of the fundamental mode of a few-mode waveguide and thus opens up new possibilities for the design of mode-controlling devices, such as mode-group (de)multiplexers, mode-dependent-loss compensators, and mode add-drop multiplexers, for fiber-based mode-division-multiplexing applications. We also proposed and demonstrated an ultra-broadband mode filter based on the structure of a phase-shifted long-period grating formed along a few-mode waveguide terminated with two linear tapers. Our typical experimental device fabricated with polymer material, which has a length of 26 mm, provides polarization-insensitive 10-dB rejection of the LP01 mode against the LP11a and LP11b modes with bandwidths of ~190 nm (1440 – 1630 nm) and ~140 nm (1450 – 1590 nm), respectively. The proposed mode filter could serve as a general platform for the development of mode filters and mode-dependent-loss compensators for fiber-based mode-division-multiplexing applications. More recently, we successfully designed and fabricated a polarization-insensitive mode-independent optical switch based on a symmetric directional coupler formed with two identical two-mode waveguides, where the two modes in one waveguide can be simultaneously switched to the corresponding modes in the other waveguide by means of the thermo-optic effect. The proposed device could find applications in reconfigurable mode-division-multiplexing systems, where modes of different orders need to be switched together between two few-mode fibers.

11253316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11253316.value: In this project, we have proposed and experimentally demonstrated a wide range of mode-controlling devices with polymer waveguides that can find potential applications in fiber-based mode-division-multiplexing communication systems. The devices developed in the project are highlighted below: (1) Thermo-optic four-mode switch: This device is formed with a 3D four-arm Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) to provide broadband polarization-insensitive switching among the four spatial modes of a few-mode waveguide [J1]. (2) Six-mode (de)multiplexer: This device is formed with five cascaded vertical polymer waveguide directional couplers to provide the function of combining or separating the six spatial modes of a few-mode waveguide [J3]. (3) Thermo-optic mode-selective switch: This device is formed with two cascaded thermo-optically controlled vertical directional couplers to provide selective switching of the two higher-order modes of a three-mode waveguide into respective single-mode waveguides [J4],[C2]. (4) Four-mode router: This device is formed by integrating a thermo-optic 3D four-arm MZI with matching 3D waveguide branches to provide routing of any of the four input modes into any of the four output ports [C3]. (5) Ultra-broadband two-mode router: This device is formed by integrating a thermo-optic long-period waveguide grating with a waveguide branch to provide ultra-broadband routing of two spatial modes [J2]. (6) High-order-mode-pass mode (de)multiplexer: This device consists of a 3D waveguide directional coupler formed with a few-mode core and a single-mode core that has a higher refractive index [J5]. The hybrid-core structure allows an effective control of the fundamental mode of a few-mode waveguide, which opens up new possibilities for the design of mode-controlling devices. (7) Ultra-broadband mode filter: This device is formed with a phase-shifted long-period grating formed along a few-mode waveguide terminated with two linear tapers to provide filtering of a specific mode of a few-mode waveguide [J6], [C4]. (8) Mode-independent optical switch: This device consists of a symmetric directional coupler formed with two identical two-mode waveguides, where the two modes in one waveguide can be simultaneously switched to the corresponding modes in the other waveguide by means of the thermo-optic effect [J7]. The device could find applications in reconfigurable mode-division-multiplexing systems, where modes of different orders need to be switched together between two few-mode fibers. The results of the project have also been reported in invited talks at a number of international conferences [C1],[C5],[C6],[C7],[C8].

11253316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11253316.value: On completion of the project and a previous GRF project (CityU 112113), we have established an effective 3D polymer waveguide platform for the development of functional waveguide devices for fiber-based MDM applications. This platform can be further explored for the development of more powerful mode-controlling devices, such as devices that combine mode-controlling and wavelength-controlling functions for fiber-based MDM/WDM systems. A number of new MDM devices based on 3D waveguide structures are being pursued and we are actively looking for new funding sources and collaboration partners, including industrial partners. Another relevant research topic is the development of packaging techniques to facilitate coupling between optical fibers and 3D waveguide structures. It is hoped that the new 3D waveguide technology we have developed will eventually find its way in the manufacturing of some critical optical components to be used in practical MDM systems in the future.

11253316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11253316.value: Mode-division multiplexing (MDM), where different spatial modes of a few-mode optical fiber carry different signals, is emerging as a promising technology for increasing the transmission capacities of the existing wavelength-division-multiplexing systems based on single-mode fibers. The goal of the project is to develop fiber-compatible functional devices based on the 3D polymer waveguide technology for application in fiber-based MDM communication systems. On completion of the project, a range of mode-controlling integrated-optic devices have been proposed and experimentally demonstrated, which include, in particular, thermo-optic mode converters, mode-selective spatial switches, and mode routers. These devices are particularly useful for reconfigurable MDM systems, which involve dynamic routing of the modes of a few-mode fibers into different paths. The results of the project have been reported in six top-tier journal papers, as well as a number of international conference papers, which include five invited papers. The device structures and the associated fabrication techniques demonstrated in the project can greatly facilitate the development of practical mode-controlling devices for the deployment of fiber-based MDM systems.

11253716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11253716.value: 高熵合金（HEA）是以五種或以上的金屬元素以近乎平均的比例混合而成的新合金系列。雖然這些元素已知可以生成多種金屬間化合物，但很多高熵合金都出乎意料地是單相固溶結構。不同的熱力學，電子或幾何模型都曾被用作解釋其單相結構，但目前還沒有明確的結論。其中一種較獲普遍接受的解釋是基於原子隨機混合所產生的高混合熵。 與常規工程合金相比，高熵合金的晶格嚴重變形而且原子擴散緩慢。因此，即使組成元素中沒有耐高溫度金屬，高熵合金在室溫及高溫環境下都表現出高機械強度。由於高熵合金的研究只開展了約十多年，很多結構與性能的關係仍然未明確。為了使高熵合金可廣泛用於結構用途，關於熱機械處理對其結構和性能的影響的知識是至為重要。 電脈衝處理（EPT）是以密度大於每平方厘米一千安培的電流通過金屬達致控制工程合金微結構的迅速方法，而且過程中不會誘發很大的溫度上升。電脈衝處理的原理通常以'電子風'和晶體缺陷之間的相互作用解釋。因為高熵合金比常規合金有更多的畸變晶格，所以預期電子與晶格之間的相互作用更強。電脈衝處理應該能非常有效地控制高熵合金的結構，而相關的硏究對科技發展有重大意義。 在此研究計劃，研究人員旨在調查一系列以第三週期過渡元素組成的高熵合金經受各種熱機械處理後形成的微結構。除了傳統的熱處理，研究人員亦會嘗試以電脈衝處理為已變形的高熵合金進行快速和高效節能的再結晶和沉澱強化。預計當此項目完成後，我們會對高熵合金的顯微結構有比較清晰的認識，以及了解這類合金的晶體缺陷和變形行為的特點。所得結果將不僅有利於高熵合金作為結構材料的應用，更可闡明其變形機制和相變特性。

11253716.label: Realisation of objectives
11253716.value: A Postdoc Fellow was engaged to carry out experiments relating to the project. PhD students also participated in the project and they would include the work related to this project as part of their theses. Based on one of our previous extensive work on the phase formation and mechanical properties of 78 quaternary and quintenary HEAs, several series of alloys were selected for investigations in line with our approved objectives. The alloys (FeNiCrMn)100-xCox (x = 5, 10 & 20), CoCrFeNiAl0.3, and CoCrFeNiHfx (x = 0 – 0.4) were chosen for the examining the phase formation and the correlations between their microstructures and mechanical properties. All the samples were prepared by vacuum arc melting followed by drop casting. The microstructures of these samples were characterized with x-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy and electron backscatter diffraction. The phases formation in the as-cast alloy samples agreed well with prediction with parameters based on differences of atomic sizes or electronegativities of the constituent atoms, or valence electron concentration. The mechanical properties of the alloys with single phase FCC structures in general had moderate yield strengths with good ductility. However, when hard intermetallic phases existed in as-cast state or precipitated after thermal annealing, the strengths increased significantly while the ductility decreased. Friction-stir welding (FSW) is a solid-state joining method where the materials to be joined are heated by frictional heating and severely sheared by the action of the stir tool. The weld joint goes through complex thermomechanical processes and forms distinctive microstructures. Friction-stir welding was chosen as the process to investigate the effects of thermomechanical treatments on the structures and properties of HEAs for several reasons. Joining methods are important for applications where large or intricate structures have to be fabricated from simple structural members. There was no study of FSW of HEA before our work and our investigation could fill this gap. We established collaboration with Prof. Fujii’s group in Joining and Welding Research Institute of Osaka University, Japan on FSW. The postdoc-fellow and PhD students were sent to Osaka U to carry out the FSW processes. Three alloys, namely, CoCrFeNi, CoCrFeNiAl0.3, Co16Cr28Fe28Ni28, were used for the investigation of FSW. The processing windows for successful joining of the alloys by FSW were identified. The welding parameters including rotation speed and speed of translation of stir tool as well as the pressure exerted on the base metal plates through the stir tool can affect the heat input to the joint and the shear stress in the stir zone. The work relating to objectives 1 and 2 described above were promising and gave publishable results, while experiments on electropulsing treatments did not generate new results, as originally expected from ‘electron wind’ effect, beyond the effects of joule heating of the electric current. Efforts were therefore focused on effects of themomechanical treatments and FSW on microstructures and mechanical properties for the better use of the manpower and resources, especially in the second half of the project duration. With the publications and conference attendance listed in Part C, the objectives were considered to be achieved. In addition, a long term and fruitful collaboration with Prof. Fujii’s group has been established and new joint-project with them was still running on the date of the report.
