11253716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11253716.value: A series of (FeNiCrMn)100-xCox (x = 5, 10 & 20) high entropy alloys (HEA) were prepared to investigate the phase stability of the quintenary alloys after thermal annealing. The alloy compositions and the annealing treatment were designed to fill the gap of information on whether the phase structure of the as-cast HEAs are thermodynamically stable or metastable structures limited by kinetics. While all the as-cast alloys had single phase FCC structure, some of the aged ones contained chromium-rich sigma phase precipitates, which affects the mechanical properties. The sigma formation in these alloys agrees well with several rules based on compositions. The results were published in an international refereed journal paper (Item 1 in Part C), Section 8 and presented in a conference (Item 1 in Part C, Section 9). Technologies for joining of materials to fabricate complex structures are important for development of applications of the materials. Friction-stir welding (FSW) is a solid-state joining method and therefore does not result in shrinkage or other defects due to solidification. Three representative HEAs, namely, CoCrFeNi, Co16Cr28Fe28Ni28 and CoCrFeNiAl0.3, all having single phase FCC structure, were selected for friction-stir welding investigation. Since most of the HEAs retained their mechanical strength better than a lot of the conventional engineering alloys, FSW of HEAs is not a straightforward task. The processing windows for FSW of these alloys were identified for producing butt-joints of 2 mm to 3 mm thick alloy plates without welding defects. Collaborating with Prof. Fujii’s group in Joining and Welding Research Institute of Osaka University, we were the first in the world to report the success of FSW of HEAs. The microstructures of the welded regions in the three alloys were characterized in detail and correlated with the mechanical properties of the welded joints. The welded regions remained in single phase FCC structure. Unlike conventional fusion welding, the microstructures of the friction-stir welded region consisted of the stir-zone, the thermomechanically affected zone, and the heat-affected zone. The weld-joints were in general stronger than the base metals with various degrees of decrease in ductility, mainly due to grain refinement and higher dislocation density in the welded regions. These results were reported in three international refereed journal papers (Items 2,3 and 5 in Part C, Section 8) and presented in a conference (Item 2 in Part C, Section 9). Using the well-known CoCrFeNi alloy as a base system as stated in the first objective, quintenary CoCrFeNiHfx HEAs were prepared to investigate the effect of Hf, which has large atomic size differences and negative mixing enthalpies with the other four constituent elements, on the microstructures and mechanical properties of the alloys. Eutectic structures consisting of Ni7Hf2, Laves phase and the parent FCC phase were observed in the alloys with 0.1 < x < 0.4. Hardness and yield stress of the alloys increased rapidly with increasing x values, but tensile ductility dropped sharply from 45% for x = 0 to 6% for x = 0.2 and the samples with x > 0.2 were too brittle for tensile test. These results were published in an international refereed journal paper (Item 4 in Part C, Section 8).

11253716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11253716.value: The family of high entropy alloys represents almost infinite possibilities of alloy designs and properties. There are already literatures reporting HEAs with superb combinations of mechanical strength and ductility by ingenious composition design and proper thermomechanical treatments. So far, most of the composition spaces of these multicomponent alloys have not yet been explored. It is quite common to observe relatively good strength retention of HEA at high temperature and therefore the development of HEAs for high temperature applications should be a promising direction for further development. On the other hand, the establishment of processing windows for friction-stir welding of different HEAs can help expanding the scope of applications of the materials. Collaboration with JWRI was established and remained active for further developing optimal FSW processes for HEAs.

11253716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11253716.value: High entropy alloys are new families of engineering alloys with multiple ‘principal elements’. This alloy design approach has very short history compared with that of the use of metals by mankind and only a very small fraction of the possible compositions has been explored. In the project, the principal investigator contributed to this field by investigating the microstructure and properties of several series of high entropy alloys after different thermomechanical treatments. In order to expand the range of applications of the alloys, the PI and his collaborators were the first in the world to report the parameters for joining these alloys using a solid-state process known as friction-stir welding. The results from this project will enrich the repertoires of materials and related processing technologies available to engineers for designing structures or components.

11254616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11254616.value: There have been concerns that Electromagnetic exposure may affect the physiological and psychological reactions of humans particularly in neuro-psychological changes. The correlation between the Electromagnetic exposure and the brain wave activities has been explored for some time. Brain wave activity is a key parameter to all neuro-psychological changes and their relationship remains ambiguous; direct correlation between Electromagnetic waves and neuro-psychological changes, including psycological feeling such as anxiety and depression, are yet to be explored. This proposal is a pioneering investigation in exploring the above subjext matter, aiming at characterizing and quantifying the impact of the external EM waves by human brain activities, and then correlating the EM wave further directly to the neuro-psychological changes via the characteristics of the brain waves under EM exposure.

11254616.label: Realisation of objectives
11254616.value: All 3 original objectives as in section 5.1 has been achieved. Brain wave activities with driver neuro-psychological cognitive functions have been correlated with EMI exposure by controlled experiments, the effect and the changes are then summarised, with a conclusion of that there is an influence of the external Electromagnetic waves to the neuro-psychological changes of humans.

11255616.label: Project Objectives
11255616.value: To study the deterioration mechanism of FRP-bonded concrete system under the effect of stress field and water molecules from an atomistic and microscopic view. To study the coupled effect of both creep and moisture on the structural performance of the FRP-bonded concrete system at a beam level using an experimental fracture approach. To develop a predictive model which can describe the deterioration mechanism in the FRP-bonded reinforced concrete systems fundamentally and comprehensively using a multiscale simulation approach. To validate the newly proposed predictive model at a structural level using an appropriate nondestructive testing and structural health monitoring scheme.

To study the coupled effect of both creep and moisture on the structural performance of the FRP-bonded concrete system at a beam level using an experimental fracture approach.

11255616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11255616.value: While research on structural performance of fiber reinforced polymer (FRP)-bonded concrete systems has been conducted extensively for short-term mechanical characterization, long-term performance and deterioration behavior remain largely uncertain and unanswered. In particular, little is known with regard to the surrounding prolonged effect leading to the deterioration on bond properties and integrity of FRP-bonded concrete that would govern the effectiveness and life cycle of these systems. Prior research studies in this area have indicated that the deterioration mechanism is complex in which the critical region in the bonded systems may shift between bulk material substrate and the material interface, which has not been observed in short-term tests. The deterioration at the vicinity of the material interface is governed by the adhesion property of the adjoining constituent materials, in which the material limits are not necessarily attained at the failure stage. The objective of this research is to develop a predictive model which can describe the deterioration mechanism in the FRP-bonded concrete systems fundamentally and comprehensively using a multiscale simulation approach equipped with experimental monitoring. To approach the deterioration problem, the key two parameters, namely moisture and creep, are chosen here as the representatives of surrounding prolonged effects. It is proposed to investigate by means of a synergistic effort that consists of systematic and hierarchical material and interface fracture testing across different length scales, multiscale modeling of debonding under moisture and creep effects, numerical studies that consist of three-dimensional moisture diffusion simulation, structural performance monitoring based on novel techniques developed by the principal investigator (PI), integration of simulation and the experimental results to establish the predictive deterioration model of FRP-bonded concrete systems at a beam scale. The fracture-based approach will be adopted here with the aid of the multiscale modeling technique recently developed from a prior Early Career Scheme (ECS) research by the PI that is capable of describing mechanical properties of the tri-layer material problem consisting of FRP, epoxy, and concrete across different length scales. Synergizing the knowledge developed in these research tasks, this study will form the basis for augmenting existing design specifications for FRP-bonded concrete structures by including the quantitative design that accounts for moisture and creep effects in such system, leading to a much more reliable and sustainable design. It is envisioned that the proposed work will significantly advance scientific knowledge in the areas of deterioration mechanisms, coupled surrounding effects and the creep behavior of multi-layer bonded system. 盡管對纖維增強聚合物粘結混凝土材料系統的短期機械性能已經進行了廣泛的研究，然而其長期性能及退化行為仍處於未知狀態。尤其是所處環境對系統的粘結性能和結構完整性的影響所知甚少。結構的完整性對於系統的有效性和服役周期具有極其重要的影響。之前在此領域的研究表明系統的退化機理非常復雜且關鍵破壞部位可能從基底材料向材料界面轉變。這一轉變在短期的實驗測試中觀察不到。材料界面的退化是由相鄰材料之間的粘結力所控制，在系統破壞時材料可能並不會達到其極限強度。 本研究的目的是通過多尺度模擬技術結合實驗檢測來開發一個可以描述纖維增強聚合物粘結混凝土材料系統退化機理的預測性模型。為了研究系統退化問題，兩個關鍵的影響因子，水分和蠕變，在這裏代表環境對系統的長期影響。為了建立纖維增強聚合物粘結混凝土系統的預測性退化模型，擬通過以下一系列的實驗及模擬方法來完成，即材料和界面在不同尺度下的斷裂測試、水分和蠕變影響下剝離破壞的多尺度模擬、水分擴散的三維數值模擬以及主要研究者開發的結構健康監測技術。藉助多尺度模擬技術的斷裂力學分析方法也在此項研究中被采用。多尺度模擬技術是主要研究者在之前的傑出青年學者計劃中提出的，它能夠準確的描述包括混凝土，環氧樹脂以及纖維增強聚合物三層材料體系機械性能的變化。通過融合不同研究任務中得到的知識，這項研究在完善現有的纖維增強聚合物粘結混凝土材料的設計規範在水分和蠕變的影響方面提供重要基礎，從而得到更加可靠和可持續的設計。此項研究工作有望在多層粘結系統的退化機理、環境的藕合效應及蠕變行為領域大大推進科學知識的發展。

11255616.label: Realisation of objectives
11255616.value: Objective 1 has been achieved completely. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations have been conducted for FRP-bonded concrete system using full atomistic model. Coarse-grained (CG) model of cementitious materials (i.e. C-S-H) and advanced composites (i.e. FRP and epoxy) has also been constructed for studying the effect if stress field and moisture at the meso-scale level. Objective 2 has been achieved completely. A better understanding on the coupled effect of both creep and moisture on FRP-bonded concrete system has been obtained through the experimental approach. It is found that the coupled effect can bring a detrimental result to the FRP-bonded concrete system. Objective 3 has been achieved completely. The study of coupled effect has been conducted through both simulation and experiment. A hierarchical predictive model can describe the deterioration mechanism in the FRP-bonded concrete system has been proposed. Such predictive model, which consists of both full atomistic and coarse-grained models, allows transformation of information between atomistic and meso- scales in a seamless manner. Objective 4 has been achieved completely. In order to validate the newly proposed predictive model at a structural scale, nondestructive testing (NDT) and structural health monitoring (SHM) scheme, which are based on the concept of acoustic-laser technique, have been carried out for quantifying the deterioration of FRP-bonded concrete system. It is found that the extent of deterioration captured from NDT and SHM echoes with the results obtained from the predictive model.

11255616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11255616.value: The knowledge developed in this project is a fundamental step for understanding complex complex coupled effect of both creep and moisture on FRP-bonded concrete system at molecular level and contribute to the understanding at the macro-level design. Application and development for other type of substrates at larger scale is possible and this will help ensure public safety against unanticipated failure. In addition, this research has a strong intellectual component with potential to significantly advance scientific knowledge in the multi-disciplinary areas of experimental mechanics, molecular dynamics simulation for creep, and environmental effect in multi-layer material systems, involving polymeric and silica materials. This research forms the basis for the development of a new engineering and design paradigm for the solution of complex engineering problem.

11255716.value: 用于机器人手臂控制的注视跟踪: 标定, 注视点估测与跟踪

11255716.label: Project Objectives
11255716.value: To study the model of human eyes for 3D gaze. There are different modeling approaches for human eyes. The model complexity needs to be considered for feasibility in its calibration; To investigate the calibration method for the eye model and gaze. The set of parameters are needed for implementation. Both on-line and off-line approaches will be investigated for the calibration; To develop a gaze estimation method to obtain the point of gaze (POG) of human eyes in real time. The robustness and effectiveness are the key factors to consider for the estimation method; To set up a system and implement the methodology for gazing and tracking the target object in motion to obtain its motion trajectories. The trajectory will be presented via a descriptor for further recognition and reproduction in the subsequent robotic manipulations; To implement the proposed gaze based tracking method and system in case studies using a robot arm for manipulation tasks.

11255716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11255716.value: This project aims at developing the methodology and system in human gaze tracking for controlling a robotic upper limb for executing the intended actions by a handicapped person. The model of human eyes will be studied, and the method will be developed to detect the motion intention for the upper limb from the human eyes. An efficient gaze tracking method will be developed to achieve estimation of the points of gaze (POG) in real time. A suitable calibration approach will be investigated for the gaze tracking system. Different from traditional gaze estimations, the gaze based tracking of a target object will incorporate 3D gaze estimation. The goal in the gaze estimation is to locate the object of interest for further tracking and manipulation with a robotic arm. Furthermore, trajectory tracking of target object will be conducted in full 3D space. The tracked object trajectories will be described with a new invariant based method to for recognition and reproduction in further manipulation actions by the robotic limb. Through the study of this project, the theoretical framework will be established for hand-eye coordination for handicapped people with robotic upper limbs. The output of the project will be a novel solution to the control of a robotic limb by the intention of a physically handicapped person from his eyes. The results of the project will contribute to the development of technology and systems to provide better assistance to disabled people. The study will have significant impact on the theoretical development and the practical applications in gaze and motion tracking. With the effective methodology and system to develop, some urgent needs can be met in integrating robotic limb to a disabled person as an integral part of his body. This will be highly useful for improving the quality of life for handicapped or disabled people via adopting the methodology in the related fields including robot-assisted rehabilitation and robot-enhanced therapy. The project will also benefit the general works in human-robot interactions with the new interface provided by the gaze tracking. 本项目旨在研究一用于机器人手臂控制的人眼注视跟踪方法及系统,以便执行残障人士的动作.通过研究人眼模型,人的运动意向可被探测.以此可控制机械手臂的运动.为此,需要建立有效的注视跟踪方法以实现对注视点的实施跟踪.首先将对人眼及注视模型进行标定.不同于传统方法,本项目对注视点及其跟踪将立足于三维估测.对跟踪所获得的轨迹将进行描述以便其后的机器人动作复制.本项目将探讨手眼协调机制,以将机器人用于帮助残障人士的康复中.这将有利于使机器人成为康复系统中的一有机部分,以提高康复效率及人的生活素质.本项目的研究也将对探索人与机器人间的新的交互方法有所贡献.

11255716.label: Realisation of objectives
11255716.value: In realizing the proposed objectives, extensive studies were conducted on gaze system set up, calibration and gaze tracking. In the context of gaze modeling methods, the problems concern two-dimensional (2-D) and three-dimensional (3-D) issues that can be viewed as inferring 2-D epipolar lines and 3-D visual axes from eye monitoring cameras. To this end, per the objective 1 proposed, a simple local polynomial model [J8] is proposed to back-project a pupil center onto its corresponding visual axis. Based on this approximation, a homography-like relation is derived in a local manner, and via the Leave-One-Out cross-validation criterion, training gaze samples at a certain depth is leveraged to partition entire input space into multiple over lapping subregions. Then, the gaze data at another depth are utilized to recover the epipolar point, i.e., the image eyeball center. Thus, given a pupil image, the corresponding epipolar line can be determined by the resolved homography-like mapping and the epipolar point. By using the same partition structure, 3-D gaze prediction model can be inferred by solving a nonlinear optimization problem. To capture the smooth residual field unmodeled by the polynomial function, a sparse Gaussian Process using pseudo-inputs is adopted [J4]. In the gaze data acquisition method, Gaussian process regression incorporating the model prior knowledge is applied for registering the input space of the glint-pupil vectors with the output space of the image gaze points. In another investigation, the user's eye and the eye camera are modeled as a central catadioptric camera. Thus the epipolar geometry of the mobile gaze tracker can be described by the hybrid two-view geometry. The image gaze point viewed from different depths can be uniquely determined as the intersection of two epipolar lines calculated by binocular data [C1]. In yet another approach to eye modeling, the 3D eye model is built on the basis of eye images to determine gaze vectors [C4,C5]. The 3D gaze point is obtained through the calibrated gaze vectors, and the point cloud is generated from the RGBD camera in a special setup [C4]. The experimental results show that the proposed method work well. The set up system also presents a great improvement in depth measurement, which is sufficient for tracking users' visual attention in real scenes. In addressing Objective 2, several important issues were explored in the project. Among them, the tedious calibration procedures and parallax errors are typical. To this end, we proposed a two-step calibration method [C1,J4]. In the first step, instead of fixating at several pre-defined calibration points successively, the user is only required to change his or her head pose while gazing at one calibration marker and the correlation test was performed on the trajectories of the gaze and the image calibration point in order to gather the reliable training data. By adopting the “CalibMe” gaze data acquisition method, a sparse Gaussian Process using pseudo-inputs is used to capture the smooth residual field unmodeled by the polynomial function. Meanwhile, a distraction detection criterion is introduced to identify the moment when user’s attention is taken away from the calibration point thereby removing outliers. Then the sparse Gaussian process regression incorporating the model prior knowledge is applied for registering the input space of the glint-pupil vectors with the output space of the image gaze points. The second step involves recovering the epipolar geometry between HMGT and eyeball centers. Then a nonlinear optimization problem is formulated to search for the geometry parameter set which could well explain the detected virtual parallax resulting from changing the depth of calibration point location. The real image gaze point can then be estimated as the intersection of two epipolar lines calculated from the binocular data. To facilitate the subsequent gaze tracking, the proposed flexible calibration method was implemented to address two challenges in the typical head mounted gaze tracker, i.e., the tedious calibration procedure and the parallax error compensation. Objective 3 was addressed side by side with the calibration implementation. The gaze estimation in the mobile scenario often suffers from extrapolation and parallax errors. With the newly proposed calibration framework, it then becomes possible to achieve precise gaze estimation for the head-mounted gaze trackers [J4]. Within this framework, there are two steps for the tracking system to learn a point-to-point and a point-to-line relationship respectively. In the first step, we infer the relation between pupil centers and spatially constrained points of regard. Then a sparse Gaussian Process using pseudo-inputs is used to capture the smooth residual field unmodeled by the polynomial function. By combining with the point-to-point relation inferred in step I, the observed parallax errors are leveraged in step II to obtain a point-to-line relation, i.e., each pupil center will correspond to an epipolar line. Thus, the real image gaze point projected from different depths is predicted as the intersection of two epipolar lines inferred from binocular data. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the head-mounted gaze tracking. Relevant to Objective 4, the hardware gaze tracking systems were set up and implementation of the proposed methodologies for gaze tracking were fully carried out. Two types of gaze tracking systems were set up and tested. The first gaze tracking system developed in our lab have a scene camera and two eye cameras [J4]. The second gaze tracking system is a low-cost HMD developed in our laboratory. In this setup, we adopted an RGBD camera as the scene camera and two IR cameras as the eye cameras [C5]. During the calibration, subjects are encouraged to look at surroundings randomly, and there is no limitation on their head poses or standing position. With the target object motion tracked by the gaze tracker, its motion trajectories obtained are presented via a descriptor, for further tracking implementation. Here, a Rotation and Relative Velocity trajectory descriptor is proposed [J1]. A Dual Square-Root Function (DSRF) descriptor is introduced by calculating the gradient-based invariants for representing 6-D rigid body motion trajectories, which can offer substantial advantages over raw data of trajectories. Relevant to Objective 5, the proposed gaze tracking method and system were successfully implemented. In an effort to explore its application in robotics, we have taken as a case study of human robot interactions. In the relevant study, we propose a novel learning network for head pose estimation, as a way to understand human attention for attention recognition and human robot interactions [J11,J13]. In exploring the use of human attention for interacting with robots, we used attention guided combination of RGB and depth modalities[J5]. A novel framework is proposed to adopt the task-understanding knowledge of the RGB-induced saliency detection network to depth modality and fuse the deep representations of both two modalities adaptively. The problem of exploring complementary information from the counterpart is formulated as learning a cross-modal residual function[J2,J12]. To achieve efficient 3D measurements, we studied motion tracking with a binocular vision system to precisely record the target motion trajectories in Cartesian space [J6]. Precision visual sensing control feedback with motion tracking is also studied [J9]. Relevant methods were also developed for Imaging Enhancement for Industrial Robot Infrared Vision Sensing [J7], image reconstruction and recognition [J3,J10],

To this end, a simple local polynomial model [J8] is proposed to back-project a pupil center onto its corresponding visual axis. The problems in tedious calibration and parallax errors are solved with a new two-step calibration method [C1,J4]. In the first step, instead of fixating at several pre-defined calibration points successively, the user is only required to change his or her head pose while gazing at one calibration marker and the correlation test was performed on the trajectories of the gaze and the image calibration point in order to gather the reliable training data. A distraction detection criterion is introduced to identify the moment when user’s attention is taken away from the calibration point thereby removing outliers. This results in a flexible calibration method. The second gaze tracking system is a low-cost HMD where we adopted an RGBD camera as the scene camera and two IR cameras as the eye cameras [C5]. In this system, 3D eye model is built on the basis of eye images to determine gaze vectors [C4,C5]. 11255716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11255716.value: In this project, we developed two types of gaze tracking systems. The first one consists of a scene camera and two eye cameras. The problems in tedious calibration and parallax errors are solved with a new calibration method, where the user only needs to change his or her head pose while gazing at a calibration marker. A distraction detection criterion is introduced to identify the moment when user’s attention is taken away from the calibration point thereby removing outliers. This results in a flexible calibration method, which shows high potential for further development in gaze tracking applications. The second gaze tracking system is a low-cost HMD where we adopted an RGBD camera as the scene camera and two IR cameras as the eye cameras. The set up system also presents a significant improvement in depth measurement, which is sufficient for tracking users' visual attention in real scenes. A special feature for this type of gaze tracking system is the auto-calibration capability enabled by the setup and methodology developed. The prototype developed here will invite more explorations of such type of gaze trackers. We plan to patent such gaze tracking system in following up work.

11255716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11255716.value: Existing gaze trackers suffer from two major drawbacks: tedious calibration and lack of 3D functionality. To overcome these drawbacks, we developed new gaze tracking systems and methodologies. The problems in tedious calibration and parallax errors are solved with a new calibration method, where the user only needs to change his or her head pose while gazing at a calibration marker. This makes it easier for the user to calibrate a gaze tracker, which is important for practical applications. We also adopted an RGBD camera as the scene camera in a low-cost version of a gaze tracker. This setup system brings significant improvement in depth measurement, which is useful for tracking user visual attention for robotic applications. This gaze tracking system allows automatic calibration by the system itself. The prototype system developed here will have its impact on the applications gaze trackers in human-computer interface in general and in human-robot interactions in particular.

11256116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11256116.value: We have developed a tool for pan-genome scaffold comparison and rearrangement events. Using this tool, we analysis different strains of some bacteria Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli. We investigate the inversion events among different strains of the same species. We find an interesting phenomenon that long (larger than 10,000 bp) inversion regions are flanked by a pair of Inverted Repeats (IRs). This mechanism can also explain why the breakpoint reuses for inversion events happen. We study the prevalence of the phenomenon and find that it is a major mechanism for inversions. The other observation is that for different rearrangement events such as transposition and inverted block interchange, the two ends of the swapped regions are also associated with repeats so that after the rearrangement operations the two ends of the swapped regions remain unchanged. To our knowledge, this is the first time such a phenomenon is reported for transposition event. See [2] for publication. We have also designed algorithms and developed software packages for chromosomal haplotype assembly problem. One paper is for short reads and one paper is for long reads. See [1, 3] In [1], we proposes a new ILP model for the haplotype assembly problem and its all-heterozygous case, respectively. Experiments with both real and simulated datasets show that the new models can be solved within much shorter time by CPLEX than the previous bests. We believe that the models can be used to improve heuristic algorithms as well. In [2],we develop a progressive approach for SNP calling and haplotype assembly that works very well for the SMS data. Our method can handle more than 200 million non-N bases on Chromosome 1 with millions of reads, more than 100 blocks, each of which contains more than 2 million bases and more than 3K SNP sites on average. Experiment results show that the false discov- ery rate and false negative rate for our method are 15.7 and 11.0% on NA12878, and 16.5 and 11.0% on NA24385. Moreover, the overall switch errors for our method are 7.26 and 5.21 with average 3378 and 5736 SNP sites per block on NA12878 and NA24385, respectively. Here, we demonstrate that SMS reads alone can generate a high quality solution for both SNP calling and haplotype assembly. Source codes are available at https://github.com/guo feieileen/SMRT/wiki/Software.

11256416.value: 超高层建筑的风荷载, 结构健康监测及振动控制

11256416.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11256416.value: Prof Duan, Zhongdong Prof Fu, Xueyi Dr He, Yuncheng Dr Li, Hongwei

11256416.label: Project Objectives
11256416.value: Structural Health Monitoring. A novel strategy (called as elevation pre-adjustment or reservation) has been implemented in the design and construction of the PAFC, which modestly increased the lengths of vertical load-bearing elements to compensate for their accumulated shortenings. It is important to examine the effectiveness of this strategy by monitoring the vertical deformations of various vertical structural members along the building height based on the SHM system, especially to examine whether the elevation reservations match the accumulated vertical deformations and the strategy can effectively reduce the differential axial shortenings. The research results will offer useful guidelines for elevation pre-adjustment in the design and construction of super-tall buildings. In the service stage, structural health conditions will be assessed using data obtained from the SHM system and the results of numerical analysis of an updated finite element (FE) model, which will provide valuable information on the design of super-tall buildings. In addition, the SHM system will be used as a test bed to verify the effectiveness and limitations of SHM-related algorithms, and guidelines for choosing appropriate structural diagnosis algorithms to detect damage in high-rise structures will be proposed. Wind effects monitoring. Typhoons occur frequently in Shenzhen. Therefore, the use of the comprehensive SHM system to monitor the effects of wind on the tallest building in China under harsh typhoon conditions will offer very useful information for improvement of the wind-resistant design and habitability of super-tall buildings. This project aims to investigate the wind loads and the wind-induced vibration characteristics and serviceability of the high-rise structure. The field measurements will provide an important validation of design procedures and assurance of acceptable behavior. The findings will aid evaluation of the ability of current design codes and wind tunnel tests to realistically predict the effects of wind on super-tall buildings. Wind tunnel tests. Pressure measurement, force balance and aeroelastic model tests will be performed to investigate the effects of wind on the PAFC. Through comparing the pressures on the building model with the on-site measurements, this study will examine the capability of the model test for the generation of extremely high suction pressures on corners and leading edges of the building. Cross-comparisons of the overall wind loads from the three model tests will be performed to examine the effects of aerodynamic damping. In particular, the wind-induced acceleration and displacement responses obtained from the three tests will be compared with those from the accelerometers and Global Positioning System (GPS) in the SHM system to evaluate the accuracy of the model test results and the adequacy of the techniques used in the wind tunnel tests. Such a comparative study has rarely been conducted for super-tall buildings under typhoon conditions. Structural vibration control. The effectiveness of the ATMD system installed in the PAFC, the world’s largest such system, will be evaluated, and the optimal control strategy for vibration mitigation of super-tall buildings will be proposed through monitoring, wind tunnel tests and numerical analysis, as follows. (1) The performance of the ATMD system will be examined by comparing the field measurements of structural dynamic characteristics and wind-induced vibrations by the SHM system in two states of the ATMD system (locked and unlocked) under similar wind actions. (2) The wind loads determined in the wind tunnel tests will be applied to the computational model of the PAFC. Next, structural dynamic analysis will be conducted in the two states of the ATMD system, respectively. This will allow the effectiveness of the ATMD system to be evaluated straightforwardly. (3) Besides the control algorithm used in the ATMD system will be considered in the structural dynamic analysis, the performance of other control methodologies will be assessed to determine the optimal control strategy for suppressing the wind-induced responses of super-tall buildings.

11256416.label: Major findings and research outcome
11256416.value: Ping-An Financial Center (PAFC) with height of 600 m is currently the fourth tallest building in the world. The PAFC is equipped with an active tuned mass damper (ATMD) system to reduce its wind-induced vibration. A comprehensive structural health monitoring (SHM) system with 548 sensors has been installed in the PAFC for both in-construction and in-service monitoring. This research project uses the PAFC as a research platform to investigate several key scientific problems relating to the wind loading and structural response, SHM and vibration control of skyscrapers through a combined study of field measurement, wind tunnel testing and numerical analysis. The project includes four closely related tasks. Task 1 comprises an in-depth study of SHM and structural performance assessment based on the measurements obtained by the SHM system and the results of numerical analysis, which provide valuable information for the development of SHM-related techniques and the design of skyscrapers. Task 2 involves a comprehensive investigation of the effects of wind on the PAFC based on the measurements gathered by the SHM system under harsh typhoon conditions. The research findings enhance understanding of the wind loading and structural response characteristics of skyscrapers, and provide important validation of design procedures and assurance of acceptable behavior. Task 3 comprises a series of wind tunnel tests, including pressure measurement, high-frequency force balance and aeroelastic model tests, to investigate the wind loads and wind-induced responses of the skyscraper. The test results are compared with the field measurements obtained from the SHM system to verify and improve the experimental techniques. Task 4 involves an assessment of the performance of the ATMD system and an exploration of the optimal control strategy for suppressing the wind-induced responses of skyscrapers. The effectiveness of the ATMD system installed in the PAFC, the world’s largest such system, is evaluated to assess the benefits gained from the application of the active control technique. Furthermore, the optimal control strategy suitable for applications to wind-excited high-rise structures is proposed. The four tasks have been completed and a number of papers have been published in international journals and conference proceedings.

11256416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11256416.value: The established comprehensive structural health monitoring (SHM) system that comprises 548 sensors and integrates inter-disciplinary advanced technologies will be continuously used to monitor the wind effects on the skyscraper after this research project is completed. It is scheduled to conduct long-term (5-10 years) investigations on the basis of the SHM system.

11256416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11256416.value: A structural health monitoring (SHM) system that comprises 548 sensors and integrates inter-disciplinary advanced technologies has been installed in Ping-An Financial Center (PAFC) with 600 m in height in Shenzhen, the second tallest building in China. The PAFC is equipped with the world’s largest active tuned mass damper (ATMD) system, designed to reduce the building’s dynamic responses. This project uses the PAFC as a research platform to investigate several key scientific problems associated with the wind loading and structural response, SHM and vibration control of skyscrapers. The research project provides valuable information for the future development of SHM, enhance understanding of the effects of wind on skyscrapers, improve wind tunnel testing techniques and promote the further application of the active control technique. The outputs of the project are of utmost importance for the wind-resistant design of skyscrapers in tropical cyclone-prone regions. This is particularly relevant to Hong Kong’s environmental conditions as the city frequently experiences typhoons.

11257316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11257316.value: Viruses cause up to 15% of human cancers. Viruses persist in hosts through integrating their viral genome into the host cell genome, or by expressing proteins which segregate their genome into cells during cell partitioning. We are mainly interested in the integration of viral genomes into the host genome. Knowing exactly how an oncogenic virus transforms a host genome is important for us to understand how the virus compromises the host genome’s functions. The general availability of next generation sequencing (NGS) methods has made possible several large-scale studies to identify the integration profiles of oncogenic viruses in cancer samples. This paved the way for a natural step forward. That is, to investigate the exact mechanism for an oncogenic virus to transform its host genome—knowing this will help us understand the molecular and biological processes of virus integration, and the virus-host interaction in disease development. In this proposal, we develop algorithms and tools for the automatic reconstruction of integration sites in viral-infected genome from NGS data. We refer to the local portion of a host genome with the integrated virus as the virus integration local genomic map (LGM). Our algorithms and tools will accept as input NGS data from a host, and output probabilistically significant LGMs. An LGM consists of intervened genome segments from the host and the virus (integrant), modeled as a graph structure where the vertices represent short DNA segments. Compared to a linear structure, a graph structure is able to capture more details of the virus integration mechanism, and represents the current consensus among computational bioinformatians in referencing human genomes. Our approach will attempt to address the heterozygous problem in cancer tissues from NGS data, through probabilistic evaluation and the incorporation of additional information from other data sources such as PacBio, single cell data, or RNAseq data. Generalizing the LGMs will allow us to decode the core structure and pan structures for the integration mechanism of a specific virus across different hosts. We propose a model called consensus graph to capture these information, and develop algorithms and tools to construct such consensus graph out of multiple LGMs. Finally, we create tools that generate visualizations of the consensus graphs. Our tools will be made available to the research community through a web-based interface. We have plans to study four oncogenic viruses with the tools. The team has implemented a proof-of-concept system and performed preliminary investigations on the database. 病毒引起人類高達15％的癌症。病毒通過其基因組整合到宿主細胞基因組中。我們主要感興趣的是整合病毒基因組如何進入宿主基因組中。了解致癌病毒究竟是如何進入宿主基因組為我們了解病毒是如何妥協宿主基因組中的功能是非常重要的。下一代測序（NGS）方法在近幾年的成就了幾次大規模的研究，以確定腫瘤樣品中的致癌病毒的整合模式。這些方法這些成功鋪平了前進的方向，即要探討致癌病毒的確切機制如何改變其宿主基因組，知道​​這將有助於我們了解病毒整合的分子和生物過程。在這個提案中，我們制定NGS的算法和工具, 解釋整合位點在病毒感染的基因組中。一個宿主基因組的局部部分與整合病毒作為病毒融合本地基因組圖譜，或局部基因組圖譜（LGM）。我們的算法和工具，將接受來自宿主的NGS數據和輸出概率顯著的LGMs。一個LGM由來自主機和病毒（整合體）干預基因組區段，建模為一個圖結構，其中頂點表示短的DNA片段。我們的方法將試圖從其他數據源諸如PacBio，單細胞數據，或RNA測序數據處理中從NGS數據，通過概率模型評估癌症組織中的雜合的問題，以及附加信息的結合。 LGMs將允許我們解碼核心結構和平移的結構為在不同的宿主上的特定病毒的整合機制。我們提出了一個所謂共識圖形捕捉到這些信息，並開發算法和工具來構建這樣的共識圖形出多個LGMs的模式。最後，我們的工具將通過基於網絡的接口提供給研究團體。我們將研究至少有四個致癌病毒。該團隊已經實施驗證的概念系統和數據庫進行了初步調查。

11257316.label: Realisation of objectives
11257316.value: First, we proposed to use conjugate graph to model local genomic map of the virus integration sites. Oncovirus integrations could induce cancer genome instability, emerging as copy number variations and complex structural variations in local genomic regions. Adjacent genes at the integrated sites are frequently dysregulated, such as TERT in hepatocellular carcinoma and MYC in cervical carcinoma. LGMs (local genomic map) analysis could lay foundations to understand how oncovirus integrations emerge and compromise the functioning of host genome. To address this issue, computational model and algorithm is needed. We proposed a graph-based algorithm to construct LGMs at the oncovirus integration sites from whole genome sequecning data of cancer samples. Based on the breakpoints of SVs (structural variations), both of the host local genome and viral genome are divided into segments, as vertices in the graph model. Copy number (CN) of segments are considered as the weights of vertices. Junctions of SVs are modeled as directed edges connecting two vertices and their split-reads counts are converted to CN as the weights of the edges. Integer linear programming (ILP) was applied on the weights of vertices and edges to overcome segment depth fluctuations, as well as insufficient split-reads. As genome DNA has double strands, we further define that for each vertex/edge, there is a conjugate vertex/edge that represents its reverse complementary counterpart and shares the same weight. We then use an algorithm analogous to the Eulerian Circuits traversal rule to find available circular paths (called unit-cycle), and then merge them to construct the local genomic map consisting of host and virus segments. In our algorithm, the first upstream and last downstream host segments are called as source and sink vertex of the LGM, respectively. The algorithm firstly finds a main path, which starts from the source vertex and extends along the edges with non-zero weight until reaches the sink vertex. Each time one vertex/edge is included in the found path, its weight decreases by one. Then, starting at one vertex with non-zero weight, our algorithm forms a unit-cycle by random walking along edges with non-zero weight until the vertex itself is reached again. More unit-cycles can be found iteratively before the graph is drained. Finally, all unit-cycles are merged with the main path to get one putative LGM. Due to the random walking and megering of the unit-cycles, there could be multiple LGMs that exactly match the conjugate graph, and our algorithm will report all possible LGMs. We simulated a set of oncovirus integration LGMs at genomic loci of well-known hotspot genes, including HBV integrations (TERT, CCNE1, and KMT2B) and HPV integrations (LRP1B, FHIT, and MYC). Combining the different SV types, copy numbers, and viral segments, there are eight LGM simulated modes in each gene locus, such as substitutive integrations, inversed insertions, and complex tandem duplications. Totally, we prepared simulated sequencing data of 48 LGM cases for evaluation. The conjugate graph algorithm successfully recovered all simulated LGMs at HBV and HPV integrated sites. The integer linear programming obtained the copy number of all segments and junctions with zero offset from the expected values. Moreover, for complex structure with highly copied segments, the algorithm reported other possible candidate genomic maps that also satisfy the observed conjugate graph. The performance is good on simulated datasets. We have tested the algorithm on real datasets. Understanding virus integration mechanisms through probabilistic models. The virus can integrated randomly along the database. We integrated the local genomic map for different host into the same model. From which, we can infer the probabilities at different loci for integration. Common oncogenic viruses will be examined carefully. We applied the conjugate graph algorithm to analyze the LGM at HPV integration loci in four cervical carcinoma samples (T4931, T6050, HeLa, and SiHa). All samples have arm-level copy number changes at the HPV integrated chromosomes. The algorithm successfully constructed LGMs of all validated HPV integrations with most CN offsets less than one. The T4931 has the HPV16 integrations at gene GLI2 locus on chr2q, which is heterozygous pentaploid (minor CN = 2). Considering that the HPV integrations might locate on the minor or major alleles, the conjugate graph algorithm provides two LGM solutions The LGM on minor allele has less CN offests. This LGM includes two unit-cycles containing three VITs, virus circularization, one viral inversion, and one host tandem duplication. The chr8q of HeLa cell line shows asymmetric copy numbers at the HPV18 integrated sites: the upstream and downstream are tetraploid and hexaploid respectively, both of which are heterozygous (minor CN = 1). According to the haplotype previously reported1, one LGM is constructed on the major allele of the tetraploid. The LGM has three unit-cycles consisting of four VITs and the virus circularization. The unit-cycles are evenly distributed in the three copies of the major allele. This LGM has stuctures similar to that in the reported HeLa haplotype1. Both of the T6050 and SiHa have HPV16 integrations at chr13q, which appears as diploid with loss of heterozygosity (LOH). The LGM of T6050 contains one unit-cycle consisting of two VITs, virus circularization, and one host tandem duplication at the gene KLF12 locus. Interestingly, this unit-cycle has different copy times (two and three) in the remained diploid alleles, which implies the possible existence of circular extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA). The SiHa cell line has two unit-cycles in the LGM at the HPV16 integation sites (downstream of the gene KLF12, Supplementary Figure 4). The unit-cycles contain two VITs, virus circularization, one viral deletion, and one host deletion. The structure of the unit-cycles is as same as that in the previous report2. Moreover, the second unit-cycle shows different copies (one and two) in the diploid alleles. We have also studied the HBV induced liver cancers. The LMG of the HBV induced liver cancers are similar to the HPV induced the cervical cancers. Study the gene expressions for virus integrants. We have built a deep learning model to understand the gene expression from two aspects. First, a developed a learning model for gene expression data dimension reduction. Also, we build a model to infer the alternative splicing from the genomes. The virus integration may also led RNA editing. We developed algorithms to understand the gene editing and as well as gene editing database.

11257316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11257316.value: In this project, the significant finding is that we have proposed a conjugate graph model and applied it to understand the local genomic maps of genomes at the virus integration sites. Also, we can model omics data into a matrix. To understand the matrix, we designed a deep learning model to decompose the matrix. Genes can express differently at tumor sites; we developed another deep learning model to infer the alternative splicing from the mutated genome sequences. Bioinformatics needs data to operate. Hence, in this project, we also developed two databases of RNA data, SCDevDB and Scrofa RNA Editing database. To visualize the cancer genome and expression data at the virus integration site, we have also developed Oviz-Bio. Many types of visualization are widely used, most of which are static and require sufficient coding experience to create. Here, we present Oviz-Bio, a web-based platform that provides interactive and real-time visualizations of cancer genomics data. Researchers can interactively explore visual outputs and export high-quality diagrams. Oviz-Bio supports a diverse range of visualizations on common cancer mutation types, including annotation and signatures of small scale mutations, haplotype view and focal clusters of copy number variations, split-reads alignment, and heatmap view of structural variations, transcript junction of fusion genes, and genomic hotspot of oncovirus integrations. Furthermore, Oviz-Bio allows landscape view to investigate multi-layered data in samples cohort. All Oviz-Bio visual applications are freely available at https://bio.oviz.org/.

11257316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11257316.value: The conjugate graph can be extended for structural variations, as well as to understand the horizontal gene transfers in the microbiome. We have started to develop a model to understand the structural variations in the single-cell CN sequencing to data understand the lung cancers. The conjugate graph can resolve the complexity within the genomes and also determine the subclones. Horizontal gene transfer is to transfer one or more genome segments from one species to another species. Understanding the horizontal gene transfers can gain insights into the microbiomes. After applying the conjugate graph model to study the horizontal gene transfers in microbiomes, we found that the horizontal gene transfer is widespread in human gut microbiomes. Also, we developed the model to understand drug resistance.

11257316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11257316.value: Oncoviruses can insert their genomes into the human genome. Sometimes, insertions will lead to tumors or cancers. However, it isn't easy to resolve the genomic contents at the viral insertion sites along human genomes as the integration can contain complex structural variations along the human genome. In this project, we proposed an algorithmic model and also an implementation to determine the genomic contents from the next-generation sequencing data. We have applied the methods to study the HPV induced cervical cancers, and even the HBV caused liver cancers. We successfully resolved the genomic contents of instances for these cancers. With the genomic contents, we were able to decipher the factors that led the tumors. Visualization is critical to understand the cancer data. Here, we have developed a platform to visualize the cancer omics data. From which, practitioners may be able to generate intriguing figures within minutes rather than days. Also, better visualizations can provide insights into the cancers. Our platform offers visualization forms from different aspects. The same gene can have different alternative-splicing forms. Some alternative-splicing forms can lead to cancers. In this project, we also propose models to predict the possible alternative-splicing forms from the genes or genome contents.

11257816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11257816.value: Evacuation is crucial to the overall fire safety of a building. An inefficient evacuation system can lead to high fatality levels by exposing evacuees to an excessively smoke-filled environment. Evacuees who know the escape routes and exit locations well are fully aware of the direction they should follow in the case of evacuation. However, evacuees who are unfamiliar with the venue usually trace back their entry route when evacuating. Their wayfinding during evacuation also relies heavily on the emergency direction signs and exit signs of a traditional building evacuation system, which are considered insufficient in today’s mega buildings. In the past decade, human evacuation assistants (EAs) have been proposed to assist evacuees in the case of an evacuation. EAs act as leaders to guide evacuees to the exits. This is particularly important when the floor plan is very large and its layout highly complicated. Such buildings are not uncommon in today’s metropolitan cities. The EA system has been studied by pioneering researchers via simulations using cellular automata (CA) and social force (SF) models. However, such studies have not fully addressed the interactions between evacuees or between leaders and evacuees in the EA system. This project will develop an SF-based model with integrated interactions. Although it is realised that over-provision of EAs increases the number of occupants in the venue and jeopardises overall evacuation time, with too few EAs the system may be ineffective. Thus, the major objective of this study will be to find the optimum number of leaders to achieve minimum evacuation times in different situations (e.g. floor area, number of evacuees, walking speed, etc.). 人群疏散對於建築物整體消防安全至關重要。一個低效率的疏散系統可以令到撤離人員暴露於濃煙環境中並導致高死亡率。認識逃生路線的疏散人員當知道逃生方向。然而，不熟悉場地的人員在疏散中通常會追溯到其進入的路線撤離。他們找尋撤離路線過程中很大程度依賴於緊急方向標示和疏散系統的出口標示，這些標示在今天的大型建築物已經不足。在過去的十年中，人員協助疏散（EA）已被提出來協助撤離人員。EA就活像疏散中的帶領者，引導人員疏散到出口，對於大面積及高度複雜佈局的建築物尤為重要。這樣的建築在今天的大城市已不少見。前人利用自動機（CA）和社會力（SF）模型對該EA系統進行了開創性的研究。但是，這些前期研究還沒有完全解決EA領導和撤離人員之間的相互作用。此項目將開發一個具有集成該交互作用的SF-模型。 過度提供EA不但增加總疏散人員數量並可能增長整體的疏散時間，但太少EA亦會令致系統失效。因此，本研究的主要目標是跟據不同場境條件（例如，面積，疏散人員數目，行走速度等），找到最佳的EA數量來實現最短疏散時間。

11257816.label: Major findings and research outcome
11257816.value: 1. We developed an evacuation simulation model on the platform of traditional social-force model. It successfully to simulate the no-fire condition at which evacuees are cooperative and assisting each other to escape out of a room. With fire development inside the room, some of the evacuees becomes competitive. Such assisting evacuation breached and some evacuees when they are exposed to fire hazards becomes competitive. Our model successfully simulated the interactions between the cooperative and competitive evacuees in evacuation during fire outbreak. 2. ‘Fast-to-slow’ has been a norm in evacuation for a long time. In this study, we found that it is true for narrow door width (<800mm). When the door width is wide enough, the diminishing of the cooperated (assisted) evacuation may reduce the overall evacuation time. However, at the same time, body contacts and forces are possibly increased which was not studied in this research. 3. Our research also found that 100% evacuees with cooperative behavior or 100% evacuees with competitive behavior are not efficiency. Also, there should exist a mixing ratio of the two behaviors so that the evacuation time is minimized. The behavior of the evacuees can be changed by providing more information to them (e.g. signage, TV broadcasting, guidance from security guards, etc.) 4. Our model can also visualize the stress level of the evacuees who may require assistance for evacuation. The building managers, based on the simulation results, can provide suitable security guards at the locations for evacuation assistance.

11257816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11257816.value: 1. This project can further developed by carried out evacuation experiments to further calibrate the model parameters. Due to the COVID-19, carrying out evacuation experiment is very risky and was prohibited. When the pandemic situation improves to a satisfactory level, more experiments should be carried out to verify the model performance. 2. Intelligent fire alarm system and route choice system can be developed for enhancing the evacuation assistance system. The data of evacuees distribution can be collected by pattern recognition. Online optimization approach can be adopted to assist the evacuees to choose the most appropriate route for evacuation so that the overall performance of the assisted evacuation system can be improved. 3. Since the model was developed on the platform of social-force model, this project can be further developed to estimate the possible body forces between the evacuees when they are competing with others in front of an exist. It will be very useful to predict the occurrence of stampede so that the architect can adjust the architectural layout for preventing the accident.

11257816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11257816.value: We successfully developed a model to simulate building evacuation. It takes into account the human behaviors in evacuation during fire emergency when was not addressed by previous researches. Our model demonstrates how peoples assist and compete with each other under different exposures to fire hazards. It not only be able to predict a more realistic overall evacuation time, it can also be used to identify possible bottleneck areas of architectural layouts for architects to improve their design. Most importantly, the model can visualize the stress levels of the evacuees by which the stressful evacuees can then be identified and assisted.

11259116.value: To evaluate the strength of highly creep-resistant Mg-6Al-3Ca-3Ba (ABaX633) and Mg-1Zn-1Ca (ZX11) alloys at service temperatures (25-200 deg C) in compression and compare with the properties of other established and new magnesium alloys. 11259116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11259116.value: 工程界正在開發多種鎂 (Mg) 合金，用於輕質用途，包括作為汽車和航太設備部件，而且大部分是在鑄件形態下使用。為了做到高強度，這些合金加入了大量的合金添加物，例如鋁 (Al)、鋅 (Zn)、錫 (Sn)、錳 (Mn) 以及稀土元素。這些合金的高溫蠕變強度並不令人滿意，因此近期正在嘗試作進一步的合金處理。一些以 Mg-Al-Ba-Ca (ABaX) 系統和 Mg-Zn-Ca (ZX) 作為基礎的新合金已顯示出希望，因為鋇 (Ba) 和鈣 (Ca) 能夠形成具有熱穩定特性的金屬間化合物，可以比傳統的抗蠕變 Mg-Al-RE 合金更好地強化有關物料。鋇和鎂、鋁結合後，形成三元相的 Mg21Al3Ba2，而鈣則形成 (Al/Mg)2Ca，兩者均聚集於晶界上。鋇和鈣與稀土元素相比，是較便宜的合金元素，而且同樣具備阻燃功能。鑄件形態下的這些合金，有不平均沉澱物分佈、化學隔離、微小孔隙和鑄件瑕疵等問題。很多這些問題都可以用熱機械加工的方法克服，包括在優化條件下進行熱加工，以及進行熱處理等。 但是，含鈣的鎂合金是難以使其變形的，需要有受控加工的程序。近年，工程界研究出熱加工性能的優化技術，不但具體指出加工函數的準確組合，更提出關於微結構控制方法的建議。這些年來已普遍為人採用的其中一項相關技巧，就是加工圖。加工圖揭示出某些微結構機制具支配作用的若干領域，也同時指出一些限制因素或不受歡迎領域，例如裂解及流動不穩定性等。ABaX633 及 ZX11 合金與一些最為知名的鎂合金比較，已展示出十分卓越的抗蠕變特性；現獲選擇作為本項目研究之用，是因為加入鋇和鈣元素之後，雖然能夠提高強度，卻會減低其加工性。在本項目中，將通過闡述加工圖，來確定這些合金的熱加工特性。此外，將會確定在一系列熱加工條件下微結構演變的機制。那些合金將會在實驗室規模的鍛造工具設置下進行鍛造，以製作一個杯狀的部件，從而核實相關的加工圖所揭示的熱加工結果和安全工作電位視窗。這項研究將會帶來製作在强度、延展性和抗蠕變性方面比鑄造合金表現更佳的 ABaX633 及 ZX11 鍛造合金之技術，以供用於需要高强度和可靠性的輕質用途。

11259116.label: Realisation of objectives
11259116.value: The two selected magnesium alloys (alloy designations: ABaX633 and ZX11) were produced using conventional permanent mold casting method using pure elemental metals, with the help of Dr. N. Hort and H. Dieringa at the Magnesium Innovation Centre, Helmholtz-Zentrum Geesthacht, Germany. Disks were cut from the cast cylinders, and three samples were cut from the disk and each sample was embedded in resin, ground, polished and etched for obtaining the microstructure. The microstructures indicated limited porosity and minimum variation across the diameter, as can be expected with faster cooling rates associated with the chosen casting method. In the case of ZX11 alloy, the microstructure exhibited an average grain size of 144 microns and hardness of about 43 (HV5 scale). It was found that the grain size was the lowest compared to some of the other Zn-containing alloys we studied. Creep studies on this alloy indicated that it is among the best to offer creep resistance up to 200 °C with applied stresses of up to 180 MPa, which are the maximum service conditions for using magnesium alloys. On similar lines, studies were conducted on ABaX633 alloy. The alloy exhibited extremely fine size grains, with an average size of 22 microns and very high hardness of 65 (HV scale). The creep resistance is good and comparable to other alloys from ABaX system. Cylindrical specimens of 10 mm diameter and 15 mm height were machined from the disks of cast billets for compression testing. The specimens were tested in the service temperature range 25–250 °C for measuring their ultimate compressive strength (UCS). Both the alloys exhibited better strength compared to several other alloys containing Zn and/or calcium and started to show high plasticty level above 200 °C. The specimens of both the alloys were also subjected to uniaxial compression in the strain rate range of 0.0003–10 per second and temperature range of 260–500 °C using computer controlled servohydraulic testing machine for the purpose of studying their formability and developing processing maps. On the basis of flow stress obtained at different tested conditions and utilizing a dynamic materials modelling technique, processing maps were developed for both the alloys. The processed specimens have been cut and observed for the microstructural changes so as to confirm their favorable domains established based on the processing maps as well as those regimes that need to be avoided for processing these alloys. In addition, kinetic analysis was conducted to propose the underlying deformation mechanism of hot working under different processing conditions. Forging is one of the commonly used manufacturing process to convert cast or wrought alloys into various component shapes. A typical component shape was chosen to conduct semi-open die forging that generates both tensile and compressive stresses during the process. It may be noted that materials fracture more easily under tensile mode of loading compared to compressive type loading. Therefore, process conditions that enable successful forging of the selected shaped component clearly indicates high level of formability, and can be used to confirm/validate the findings of processing maps. A finite-element (FE) software, DEFORM-2D, was used to simulate the material flow during forging so that local variations of various parameters, such as stresses, strains, strain rates, etc. could be found out and used in the validation exercise. These forging studies have confirmed the established domains of formability and dynamic recrystallization leading uniform and finer grain structure in the components. The results obtained from these works have been used towards accomplishing the objectives 1, 2, and 4 of this project, and have been fully documented in the two papers that have been published and reported in Part C of this report. Finally, we compared the microstructural features, strength and formability of a large number of magnesium alloys, taken from our own research studies conducted over a decade through several research projects and those from the literature on calcium-containing magnesium alloys. This has established the superior role played by calcium in magnesium alloys, with the two alloys studied in this project being among the best in terms of mechanical properties. The details of this review paper is given in Part C of this report, and objective 3 is well accomplished.

11259116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11259116.value: The two chosen magnesium alloys in this project are ZX11 (ternary alloy) and ABaX633 (quaternary alloy), with calcium being the common alloying element that promotes creep resistance and strength. A full characterization of their microstructures obtained after casting these alloys included microstructure, creep resistance and mechanical strength over a the relevant range of temperature and stresses were carried out. The relevant results for ZX11 alloy, along with a comparison with some Zinc-containing magnesium alloys, were presented at TMS2017 Annual Meeting and published in Magnesium Technology 2017, with publication details as given in Part C (item 9) of the report (https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-52392-7_62). This dilute magnesium alloy has shown smallest grain size, excellent creep resistance and mechanical properties compared to others. Later, the study included compression testing of the alloy at relatively higher temperatures (260 - 500 deg C) that are commonly involved in hot working of such alloys over a large range of strain rate or speeds to generate flow curves for the alloy. Using the true stresses obtained from these flow curves, a processing map was developed on the basis of dynamic materials modelling. Later, semi-closed die forging process was used to study the conditions of successful formability of the alloy. In addition, finite-element simulation of the forging process under the chosen conditions of temperature and strain rate (relates to press speed) so as to estimate the material flow while the component shape being progressively developed to the final shape. The results obtained from the actual forging were compared with those obtained through simulation. It was found that the results not only agree with each other but also validate the developed processing map. This work was published in a journal is included as the first paper (http://dx.doi.org/10.3390/met7100405) in Part C (item 8) of the report. On similar lines, the characterization, hot workability, and forging of the other chosen alloy ABaX633 was carried out and the results obtained are published in the second journal paper (http://dx.doi.org/10.3390/met7110513) included in Part C (item 8). These essentially covered all the aspects mentioned in Objectives 1, 2, and 4. The results obtained on these alloys have been compared with a large number of Calcium-containing magnesium alloys, and the findings are published in the form of a review paper (https://doi.org/10.1002/adem.201701102) in an international journal, listed as the third paper in Part C (item 8). This essentially completed the realization of Objective 3 and the project.

11259116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11259116.value: The principal investigator has retired from regular academic faculty position and will not be able to further lead any related research projects. However, the contributions we made for a vast number of new magnesium alloys towards their successful development and thermo-mechanical processing will enrich the literature.

11259116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11259116.value: Magnesium (Mg) alloys are being developed for light-weight applications in automobile and aerospace. They are largely used in cast condition, and their creep strength is not satisfactory. Therefore, several alloy systems are being developed including addition of rare earth elements that are very expensive. We selected two alloys with 'Calcium' as the common element but from different magnesium alloy systems. While ZX11 (Zinc 1% - Calcium 1%) is a dilute alloy, ABaX633 has large level of alloying elements (Aluminium 6% - Barium 3% - Calcium 3%). These alloys are relatively easy to develop and economical. However, hard intermetallic phases in their microstructures pose difficulties while converting them into components through metal forming processes. This study characterized the microstructure, creep resistance, and mechanical strength of these cast alloys. Both these alloys developed fine grain sizes after casting, and offerred excellent creep resistance and strength within the service temperature range of up to 200 deg C. We developed processing maps for these alloys that provide windows of temperature and forming speed that should be utilized in industrial hot working processes such as forging, rolling, extrusion, etc. The findings are successfully validated by actual forging of components and finite-element simulation.

11259516.value: Lighting effects are important components in many multimedia applications, such as mobile game, Virtual Reality (VR), Augmented Reality (AR) and Mixed Reality (MR) applications, e.g., virtual tour, virtual meetings, smartglasses, etc. Although ray tracing can provide good visual results for high quality lighting effects, the computational loading of ray tracing is too heavy. This project has developed a number of techniques that can generate high quality lighting effects. In addition, their computational requirements are low and they are suitable to be realized in mobile devices. The following link shows our most updated result. https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sganLGp09gXl-7UxD4-QWAuAg35GaBIk/view?usp=sharing

11260016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11260016.value: Bode sensitivity integral relation, arguably the most important result in performance limitation studies, plays a central role in quantifying the intrinsic design constraints and performance limits in feedback design, of which a canonical objective is disturbance attenuation. Unfortunately, Bode integral relations and similarly, many other performance limitation results, cannot be applied to networked feedback systems, due to the inherent communication constraints present in the feedback loop. The impact of communication constraints on control performance calls for the incorporation of information and communication constraints into performance limitation studies, and in turn the integration of information and control theories for analysis and design of networked feedback systems. This project answers to these challenges and develops new information measures and correspondingly, an information-theoretic paradigm for analyzing the limitations and tradeoffs in networked feedback systems, enabled by a cohesive development of new information measures, Bode-type integral inequalities, and performance limits. We consider multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems with MIMO communication channels. The integral inequalities quantify the tradeoffs in disturbance attenuation for broad classes of networked feedback systems. The channel blurredness, a newly proposed information measure for the quality of communication channels, is used to characterize the effect of communication channel noises on the integrals and henceforth the tradeoffs in disturbance attenuation. Bounds on the power gain, a novel disturbance attenuation measure tailored for performance analysis of networked control systems, will provide the fundamental limits of disturbance attenuation achievable by networked feedback. The developments will seek to incorporate essential MIMO system characteristics such as directionality properties, and essential MIMO channel characteristics such as channel resource allocation. 波得灵敏函数积分关系在界定反馈设计中所存在的本质约束及性能极限起着举足轻重的作用，尤其是对于经典的扰动衰减性能，被广泛认为是反馈控制局限性研究中最重要的成果。然而由于反馈回路中内在的通讯约束，波得积分关系及其他相关的性能分析方法均不适合于网络反馈系统。为此，网络反馈系统的性能分析有必要考虑通讯约束对控制性能的影响，从而要求将信息论与控制理论有机地结合起来。本项目旨在回应这一挑战，通过提出新的信息测度、发展新的波得积分不等式及推导出网络反馈这一新情况下的性能极限，尝试发展一个基于信息论分析网络反馈系统局限性和设计取舍的理论框架。我们考虑具有多个通讯信道的多入多出系统。拟发展的积分不等式将可用来确定广泛类型的网络反馈系统中的扰动衰减在不同频段的取舍。信道模糊度，这一新提出的通讯信道质量指标，将用来界定通讯噪声对波得积分因之对扰动衰减性能的影响。而功率增益这一概念乃是为网络控制系统性能分析所专门打造，它使我们获得通过网络反馈可达致的扰动衰减的根本极限。本项目将特别注重多入多出系统及多通道信道的特质，如信号的方向性和信道资源分配问题。

11260016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11260016.value: 1. MIMO Bode Integrals and Power Bounds. Under this objective of the project, we have derived Bode-type integral relations and power attenuation bounds in the networked control setting, reported in Research Output [1, 2, 3, 7, 9, 12]. In this endeavor, we developed a general information-theoretic paradigm for analyzing the limitations and tradeoffs imposed by communication channels, with a particular focus on the disturbance attenuation of MIMO networked feedback systems. The integral relations quantify the tradeoffs in disturbance attenuation for broad classes of systems, including nonlinear time-varying systems with nonlinear time-varying communication channels. The channel blurredness, a newly developed information measure for the quality of multi-port communication channels, is used to characterize the effect of communication constraints on the integrals and henceforth the tradeoff in disturbance attenuation. Bounds on the best achievable power reduction of the disturbance are also derived for MIMO networked feedback systems, in which channel blurredness is seen to play a central role as well in quantifying the fundamental limit in power reduction of a networked feedback system. The systematic developments of this paradigm and fundamental theory are presented in the research monograph [2] and disseminated in the survey article [7]. 2. Networked Multi-Agent Systems. In another important objective of the project, we investigated networked multi-agent systems, an area of considerable research interest and enormous potential impact that builds directly on networked feedback control. Our research results in this direction are reported in the journal paper [4] and conference papers [3.4]. In doing so, we formulated and solved an optimal energy management problem for multi-agent systems under distributed control. At present, the overwhelming majority, if not all, of the multi-agent consensus algorithms have not addressed performance issues, and our work is among the first exploration into this open, more challenging problem area. We introduced a network approximation scheme in the energy minimization criterion, which ensures that a distributed optimal consensus algorithm always exists, for any given connected network topology. This distributed algorithm can be constructed by solving a single-agent-level parametric algebraic Ricatti equation. The performance of the optimal consensus algorithm can be determined accordingly. Moreover, we also contributed significantly to the study of bipartite and sign consensus problems for multi-agent systems, which are closely pertinent to opinion and social dynamics. Our results, while providing useful performance results for multi-agent systems, shed lights into the intrinsic limitations imposed by network topology.

11260016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11260016.value: The project has led to the growth into a comprehensive investigation of robustness and performance of time-delay systems, reported in the journal papers [6, 8, 10], where we studied in-depth the fundamental notion of delay margin. We launched a renewed effort focusing on the delay margin achievable by the famed PID control. The study has led to important discovery in the analytical design and tuning of PID controllers, showing that in achieving feedback robustness against uncertain system time delay, the proportional and integral control both have little effect, while the derivative control provides the desirable action required to compensate the degrading effect of the system delay. The project has also shown the potential for extension to an information-theoretic analysis of such optimal estimation algorithms as Kalman filtering, with the goal to characterize and quantify the fundamental limits of estimation using information-theoretic measures in a networked environment. Furthermore, there is a high likelihood to extend the Bode integrals and the power gain bounds to multi-agent systems. This highly challenging problem will usher us into the new domain of discovering the fundamental limitations and performance tradeoffs resulted from inter-agent interconnections, characterized by the network graph topology underpinning the multi-agent system.

11260016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11260016.value: Bode sensitivity integral relation, arguably the most important result in performance limitation studies, plays a central role in quantifying the intrinsic design constraints and performance limits in feedback design, of which a canonical objective is disturbance attenuation. Unfortunately, Bode integral relations and similarly, many other performance limitation results, cannot be applied to networked feedback systems, due to the inherent communication constraints present in the feedback loop. The impact of communication constraints on control performance calls for the incorporation of information and communication constraints into performance limitation studies, and in turn the integration of information and control theories for analysis and design of networked feedback systems. This project answers to these challenges and develops new information measures and correspondingly, an information-theoretic paradigm for analyzing the limitations and tradeoffs in networked feedback systems, enabled by a cohesive development of new information measures, Bode-type integral inequalities, and performance limits. Specifically, we proposed a new information measure for noisy communication channels, called channel blurredness, and developed accordingly Bode-type integral relations and power attenuation bounds in the networked control setting. These results provide fundamental insight and understanding in how communication constraints such as channel capacity, signal-to-noise ratio may constraint the control performance achievable.
