11260916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11260916.value: Secret key distribution is a procedure for two parties to agree on a key using public channels. It is essential for enabling encrypted communication applications. The key has information-theoretic secrecy if no eavesdropper can obtain it by computations. Recently, information-theoretic key distribution was realized using a concept called bounded observability. Two lasers under optical feedback were considered for scrambling a common noise with a sufficiently wide bandwidth that prevents complete observation. The laser emissions were processed into bit streams, which were successfully distilled into a secret key after exchanging the feedback parameters. Although the feedback was conveniently controlled, it often gives undesirable round-trip time-delay signatures (TDSs), potentially limiting the randomness and generation rate of the key. In this proposal, optically injected chaotic semiconductor lasers will be investigated for secret key distribution. As a common source, a laser is first perturbed by continuous-wave optical injection to emit a chaotic signal, which then optically injects two lasers into chaotic oscillations. The two lasers scramble the commonly injected signal into their own emissions, which are sent through nonlinear fibers, digitized electronically, and post-processed into two bit streams. The scrambling parameters are randomly switched over time so they occasionally coincide to allow chaos synchronization in the two lasers. Upon exchanging the parameters, synchronized segments of the two bit streams can be selected as the key. Though the optical injection is realized through a public channel, the common injection signal is chaotic and has a wide bandwidth that prevents complete recording. Advantageously, the proposed scheme provides information-theoretic security due to the impossibility for eavesdroppers to repeat the scrambling. The scheme eliminates the feedback loops for enabling reduction of the response time for synchronization. The scheme uses injection instead of feedback to avoid TDS-induced degradation of randomness. The research will first investigate synchronized random bit generation by common injection without feedback. Using chaotic sources with bandwidths exceeding 10 GHz, synchronized bit streams will be experimentally explored for high randomness and raw bit rates reaching 50 Gbps. Moreover, fast key distribution will be investigated by quickly switching the injection parameters, which could yield high key generation rates reaching 10 Gbps according to preliminary simulations. Furthermore, reduction of key errors will be investigated using fiber nonlinearities to increase the occurrences of high intensities, thereby reducing the effect of electronic noise. Overall, success of the research will contribute to the emerging developments in secret key distribution by bounded observability. 密鑰分發是用戶雙方通過公共信道實現密鑰共享的過程，在加密通信等相關應用中扮演著不可或缺的角色。如果第三方通過計算仍不能獲得密鑰，該密鑰則具備了信息理論安全。最近，基於信息理論的密鑰分發通過有限可觀測性得以實現。該方法採用兩個基於光反饋的激光器，混疊一個具有足夠帶寬的公共噪聲源，以實現阻止第三方完整觀測的目的。激光器輸出經處理生成比特序列，進而交換反饋參數以實現密鑰生成。儘管光反饋易於控制，但它不可避免的引入了反饋時延信息，潛在地限制了密鑰的隨機性和生成速率。 本項目提出採用光注入半導體激光器實現密鑰分發。首先將連續波光注入一個激光器，將其作為公共源，然後同時注入另外兩個激光器以實現混沌震盪。這兩個激光器將公共注入信號混疊至內部輸出，然後通過非線性光纖，數字化，以及後期處理生成兩個比特序列。因為混疊參數隨時間隨機轉換，所以在滿足一致性的條件下這兩個激光器可以實現混沌同步。通過交換參數，這兩個比特序列中同步的部分將被選出作為密鑰。雖然光注入發生在公共信道，但是公共注入信號處於混沌態並且具有很寬的帶寬，從而有效阻止了第三方的完整記錄。本項目的優勢在於，第三方偷聽不可能重現信號的混疊，因此該方案具備信息理論安全。本項目避免了反饋回路的使用，從而有效地減少了同步反應的時間。同時，用光注入替代光反饋也避免了反饋時延信息對隨機性的影響。 研究將首先探索採用無反饋的公共光注入實現同步隨機數生成。基於帶寬超過10 GHz 的混沌源，實驗生成原始比特率達50 Gbps的高質量同步比特序列。此外，通過快速轉換注入參數進行快速密鑰分發，基於初期仿真結果有望實現10 Gbps的密鑰生成。為了減少密鑰錯誤率，進一步提出採用光纖非線性促進高強度波形的生成，以達到減少電子噪聲影響的效果。總之，該項目的成功將會極大地促進有限觀測密鑰分發的發展。

11260916.label: Realisation of objectives
11260916.value: The project aims to investigate chaotic lasers under optical injection with the capability of key distribution. Conventional methods adopt optical feedback that often involves undesirable round-trip time-delay artifacts, which potentially limit the randomness and generation rates of the output bits. In this project, optically injected chaotic semiconductor lasers have been investigated for which the time-delay artifacts can be inherently eliminated. Using three optically injected chaotic semiconductor lasers, correlated random bit generation was developed with security ensured, as the response lasers produced bits that cannot be extracted using the information in the public channel. Then, through reconstruction of the phase space, the divergence of neighboring states was quantified. The divergence corresponds to the fundamental speed of generating the bits from the different scrambled states. Furthermore, by fiber propagation experiments, chaotic emission of a semiconductor laser was shown to be broadened optically and electrically, as an improvement of the waveforms for generating the secret bits. The objectives of the project have been addressed over the duration of the project as detailed below. Objective 1 was about synchronized random bit generation without optical feedback. Using a common chaotic laser source, two optically injected semiconductor lasers were illustrated for chaos synchronization, where the synchronized output waveforms were processed into nearly identical bit streams for secret key generation. To avoid any undesirable time-delay signatures (TDSs), the common chaotic laser source was subject to a continuous-wave optical injection instead of an optical feedback. It then unidirectionally and optically injected the pair of response lasers through a public channel. The two response lasers of identical parameters were synchronized and digitized in yielding correlated random bit streams at a tunable rate of up to about 2 Gbps. Verified to be sensitive to parameter mismatch between the response lasers, the best correlated bit streams corresponded to a low bit error ratio of less than 4%. Randomness was verified by a test suite of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Besides, the cascaded injection of the common and response lasers was experimentally extended for photonic millimeter-wave generation. Periodic oscillation was invoked with phase noise suppressed by the modulation for generating high-speed signals of up to 72 GHz, which resulted from tuning the injection conditions away from the chaotic region for the lasers in cascaded injection. Objective 2 was about investigating the speed by estimating the response time of the laser dynamics through phase space reconstruction as well as studying the period of switching supported by the dynamical scrambling. Although the laser dynamics determined the intrinsic statistics of the chaotic emission, the statistics of the output signals was found to be significantly affected by the process of detection. The statistical properties of chaotic signals were thoroughly analyzed, revealing the important roles of the different schemes of detection. Through reconstructing the detected state space, the divergence of neighboring states was quantified by the time-dependent exponent (TDE). Different schemes including low-passed direct detection, band-passed direct detection, and heterodyne detection were compared. As long as strong frequency components were avoided, the output statistics was found to approach the Gaussian distribution without much affecting the growth rate of the TDE, which corresponds to the detected response time of the laser dynamics. For instance, with a proper band-passed detection, the TDE growth rate of around 7.5 GHz was maintained for the laser with a bandwidth of about 10 GHz. Besides, intrinsic switching of the dynamical states was observed between stable and periodic states, where the periodic toggling between the states was experimentally measured to happen within a transient time of below 0.7 ns in supporting switches at high rates. Objective 3 was about utilizing nonlinear propagation in fibers for manipulating the waveforms containing high intensity signals, thereby broadening the chaotic bandwidths for applications. By sending the chaotic emissions of the lasers through fibers with nonlinearities, the waveforms for the bit generation were improved optically where broadening of the bandwidths and suppression of time-delay artifacts were achieved. The experiments were realized through propagation over a standard single-mode fiber for invoking self-phase modulation, together with anomalous group-velocity dispersion, which led to broadening the bandwidth by 6 times to above 100 GHz and suppressing the TDS by 10 times to below 0.04. When the input power launched to the fiber was increased to 340 mW for a 20-km fiber, the resultant high-intensity pulses enabled the nonlinear broadening effects. Additionally, the complexity of chaotic dynamics after propagation over the fiber was numerically analyzed by estimating the associated dimensions. Employing a careful state-space reconstruction yielded the correlation dimension of the laser that can be tuned through different combinations of injection and feedback. These optical approaches minimized the use of post-processing and so reduced potential distortions induced by electronic detections. Through addressing the above objectives, the project successfully illustrated the correlated distribution of the random bits through cascaded injection, where the inherent subnanosecond speed was quantified by state space reconstruction and the waveform manipulation was realized by nonlinear propagation in fibers. The investigation led to the exploration of cascaded injection for signal generation as well as the spontaneous periodic switching of states for future studies.

11260916.label: Major findings and research outcome
11260916.value: The research contributed to 5 journal publications and 4 conference papers. It also partially supported the training of 1 Ph.D. student. The major findings of this project are summarized as follows. Using unidirectional optical injection, correlated random bit generation was investigated in synchronized chaotic semiconductor lasers. Random output bit streams at a tunable rate of up to about 2 Gbps were verified using the NIST Special Publication 800-22 statistical tests. Security was ensured because a mismatch by merely 7% in the laser parameters was shown to drastically increase the bit error ratio from 4% to 30%, based on the rate-equation model. Moreover, due to the use of cascaded injection, an extension of the work was demonstrated for photonic millimeter-wave generation at 72 GHz. The results were documented in journal publications [1, 5] in Part C. By realizing the reconstruction of the phase space (or state space), the speed of generating the useful bits were quantified fundamentally using the TDE, which measures the divergence of neighboring states by the scrambling of the laser dynamics. The detection schemes were found to be important for generating an ideal Gaussian profile for the output intensity statistics. By studying low-passed direct detection, band-passed direct detection, optical heterodyne detection, and electrical heterodyne detection, Gaussian profiles could be yielded by excluding strong frequency components while maintaining the fast growth of the TDE. Estimated by the TDE slope, the fast rate of eliminating the influences of the previous states was about 7.5 GHz for generating the key bits. Also, an inherent switching of states was experimentally discovered and numerically verified through a long-cavity feedback, where periodic toggling between stable and oscillatory states was found with a transient time below 0.7 ns. The results were documented in journal publications [2, 4] and conference publications [2, 3] in Part C. As for manipulating the chaotic waveforms through nonlinear propagation, the emissions from the lasers were sent via standard single-mode fibers at power levels reaching up to 340 mW, where suppression of TDSs to below 0.04 and broadening of bandwidths to above 100 GHz were demonstrated. Besides, a time-delay dimensional analysis was implemented in yielding a tunable correlation dimension of within 8.6 and 15. Without relying on any post-processing by electronics, these increased bandwidths and complexities enable generation of random outputs at high rates. The results were documented in journal publication [3] and conference publications [1, 4] in Part C.

11260916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11260916.value: The project utilized cascaded injection of chaotic lasers for correlated random bit generation along with the estimation of the state-space properties. A number of extensions are enabled by this study. Firstly, the experimental setup of cascaded injection can be utilized in the periodic oscillatory state instead of the chaotic states. The differences in the resonance frequencies of the lasers were found to enable expansion of the modulation bandwidths, which allows for photonic generation of millimeter-wave frequencies. Secondly, the scrambling of the states led to the observation of the spontaneous switching behavior in the lasers. By applying feedback with a long delay, periodic switching between stable and unstable states was found experimentally. The theoretical analysis for explaining such a new dynamics is being developed. Additionally, based on further incorporating chaos into the switching oscillatory dynamics, preliminary experiments on realizing wireless distribution of the random bits are being actively pursued. The above results formed the basis of a Ph.D. thesis. Although interrupted by the unusual circumstance in 2019/20, the student will very soon submit his thesis for completion this year.

11260916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11260916.value: Generation of random bits along with their distribution though optical means has been a critical procedure in secure communication for commercial, civilian, and military applications, where two parties agreeing upon a set of random bits as the key can achieve message encryption. Recently, a number of secret key distribution schemes have been developed with high security based on the practical limitations of bounded observability by employing very fast generation of random bits. This project investigated the generation of random bit streams that are correlated through synchronizing chaotic lasers. The project investigated the unidirectional optical injection in cascade so that correlated random bits were generated at a tunable rate, where the randomness is verified by standardized tests. The fundamental speed for generating the random outputs was quantified through reconstructing the phase space that describes the states of the lasers, where any former information was found to be quickly scrambled in less than 1 ns by the dynamics. The chaotic waveforms were also improved through nonlinear propagation in optical fibers, resulting in the broadening of bandwidths and elimination of undesirable artifacts. Eventually, the results will physically improve the secure distribution of data based on laser dynamics.

11261216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11261216.value: 玻璃幕牆已經在現代高層建築中得到廣泛使用，以滿足人們對審美，提供透明度和光照的要求。然而，在火災中，幕墻玻璃的破壞會形成新的空氣循環，加速火焰的燃燒，並有可能形成在相鄰建築物之間的蔓延，從而造成嚴重的人員傷亡和材產損失。例如，2009年北京中央電視臺新辦公樓火災引起消防的賠償金高達2億元人民蔽。 玻璃在高溫下容易破碎和斷裂。因此可以通過控制溫度梯度的辦法改善玻璃的防火性能。為了降低熱梯度，本項目提出壹種可直接附著於玻璃表面的透明復合保護膜。其面層可以將熱量進行擴散，減少了對玻璃的熱負荷；第二層二氧化矽氣凝膠薄膜可阻隔熱量傳遞到玻璃上；最後壹層薄膜可使玻璃上的熱負荷更均勻的分佈以降低平面內溫度梯度。因此新型防護膜的使用可以對玻璃幕牆隔熱，耐火，防開裂以及機械強度起到重要作用。有限元法已經被應用於火災試驗模擬和數值研究中，然而有限元法在模擬裂紋擴展時表現出壹定的局限性，本研究將采用無網格法對玻璃幕墻火災下的力學性能進行模擬和優化設計，並將數值模擬的結果輔以試驗驗證，以提供更加高效和準確的解抉方案。

11261216.label: Realisation of objectives
11261216.value: In this proposed research project, all objectives have been realized. A new transparent thermally conductive film for the fire protection has been developed. Initially, the thermal-mechanical properties for the fire performance of glass facade were investigated to understand the fire proofing mechanism before proceeding with the experimental and theoretical research. We found that thermal radiation and convection are the two major effects of the heating-up of glass facades in fire environments. The heat flux imposed on glass and temperature discrepancy is important criteria for studying the thermal-mechanical properties and determining the initiation of glass crack and breakage. To predict the overall fire performance of glass, the thermal field of the glass facade was first determined by solving the system equation based on the green function method, integral transform method and thermal-elastic potential theory. The thermal stress-stain, crack initiation and breakage were then obtainable. The stress-stain state and glass failure generated by a residual stress or remote load were determined using the stress intensity factor. Partial differential equations based on energy conservation principles were discretized to sets of energy equations, and further solved to obtain the numerical solutions of the temperature field and thermal dilation of the glass. The heat balance expression of the thermodynamic equation was utilized to predict the breakage time of glass facades in a fire. Based on these work, the working mechanism of a glass facade under fire conditions was unveiled, and a thermal-mechanical model was developed for the simulation of thermal cracks and breakage in fires. For the fire protection of glass facades, a transparent thin film was fabricated. The proposed thin film was divided into three layers. The first and third layers are made of transparent Al2O3-based material while the middle layer is a SiO2 aerogel-based material. SiO2 aerogel is one of the lightest solid materials due to its nanoporous structure, low density, low dielectric constant, low thermal conductivity, high porosity, high specific surface and so on. The proposed transparent thin film can be attached directly to the glass surface. This film creates anisotropic thermal conductivity, leading to high thermal conductivity in parallel with, and low thermal conductivity perpendicular to, the glass surface. With respect to building energy efficiency, due to the existence of thermal resistance perpendicular to the glass, the film can prevent indoor thermal energy conduction in summer and winter, maintaining a comfortable indoor temperature. Additionally, its non-ageing characteristics under long-term UV exposure give it good practical applicability, as well as good weather and water resistance, tensile and compressive strength. A series of experiments on thermal-mechanical behavior of glass panels with different film arrangements and film-protected glass panels has been carried out. To evaluate the fire-protective efficiencies of glass facades covered with the aforementioned transparent thin film. Glass facades with different thicknesses of the transparent thin film layers were experimentally investigated, along with various loading cases and different installation formats, and comparison was made with conventional glass facades. The transparent thin film attached to one side to simulate indoor fire conditions was used for the tests. Temperature distribution on glass was monitored and measured throughout the process of crack initiations and propagation. Both the temperature on the ambient side and that on the side exposed to fire were recorded. It was found that the glass facades covered with transparent thin films exhibits improved crack initiation and breakage behavior in fire conditions. Additionally, the stress-strain states of the glass panes under fire were measured experimentally. Throughout the experiment, tests of the glass samples were first be carried out at room temperature and then in an increasingly hot environment, with the temperature set to 75, 100, 125, 150, 200, 300 and 400 oC. The experimental results provided useful guidelines for the establishment of a thermal-mechanical model and meshfree modeling framework for simulation of the crack and breakage behavior of glass facades with transparent thin films. The experimental results also provided a useful practical basis for the development of an optimization approach to the design of glass facades protected by transparent thin films. The overall thermal-mechanical behavior of film-protected glass facades under elevated temperatures was modeled. A general meshfree computational framework was established for simulation of the overall thermal-mechanical behavior of glass facades protected by transparent thin films. The established glass crack and breakage model that comprise radiation and conduction was incorporated into the meshfree framework for the numerical solutions. The simulation focused on the thermal-mechanical and fire-resistance properties conferred by these films. Stress singularity in the fracture meshfree approach was considered based on the approximation function enriched by a stress-field singular function. The developed meshfree modeling framework can also solve the non-continuity of cracks by employing a visibility criterion. The modeling work included dynamic analysis, in which the spatial domain and Newmark method were adopted for discretization in time domain. The thermal and mechanical field was coupled in the proposed meshfree framework to simulate the transient creep strain and thermal cracking to breakage. All simulation results were compared and validated by experiments. Additionally, an optimization algorithm for the fire-proof design of glass facades has been developed. To implement optimization, an objective function was built in consideration of such design variables as the layer thicknesses of the Al2O3 film, SiO2 aerogel, glass facade and fire resistance period. As a result, a general optimization and simulation computing system capable of modeling heat mass transfer, thermal-mechanical properties, and crack initiation and breakage phenomena was established. This research has led to 7 high-quality research papers being published in refereed international journals. A PhD student was trained under the research project.

11261216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11261216.value: A new transparent thermally conductive film that can be attached directly to the fire-exposed surface was developed. The film creates anisotropic thermal conductivity, leading to high thermal conductivity in parallel with, and low thermal conductivity perpendicular to, the glass surface. The film-protected glass facade enhances energy conservation, noise insulation, fire resistance, anti-crack properties and mechanical strength. The proposed film can lead to enhanced fire safety for commercial and residential buildings with glass facades. Fire-resistant film protected glass panels can help to confine and hence choke fires, thereby preventing their vertical and horizontal spread. The result will enhance safety and cost-effective solutions for achieving statutory fire ratings and reducing the risk of fire-induced losses of life and property. It can also enable the development of a new generation of fire-resistant film-protected glass panels, which will help the glass industry to develop new products and to create new job opportunities at a variety of levels. Based on the experimental results, a meshfree framework was developed to simulate the heat conduction and failure behavior of film-protected glass facades. This framework was compared and verified with data from the second test series and used for parametric studies. The stress distribution, crack initiation, propagation and breakage time was investigated to identify the degree of enhancement by the proposed thin films. Different parameters, including the thicknesses and arrangement of layers, were considered. Furthermore, an optimization process was implemented to find the optimal layer design. The development of the meshfree method for modeling crack initiation and propagation in film-protected glass at elevated temperatures can further be applied in alternative film-protected glass industrial applications. The above-mentioned points are the major findings and research outcome of this project.

11261216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11261216.value: The developed mesh-free modeling framework and experimental facilities will have the potential to be used for further investigation in fire research of film-protected glass facades. The mesh-free modeling framework can be used for predicting the heat conduction, failure behavior, stress distribution, crack initiation, propagation and breakage in consideration of different parameters, including the thicknesses and arrangement of layers. In the later work, uniform radiation and non-uniform fire loading conditions can be considered. The effects of different fixing formats on fire resistance can be determined based on the outcome of this research. The working efficiency of the developed transparent thin film for the fire resistance of glass facades at different stress states can be further investigated. Simulations will lead to the development of effective ways of predicting the breakage of the fire-resistant film-protected glass facade. Through the better understanding of glass facade breakage behavior in different fire loading conditions, installation forms, and stress states, it is expected safer and more innovative facades can be designed for use in building and construction.

11261216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11261216.value: We have developed a thin film that can be attached directly on the surface of glass panels for fire resistance. Fire-resistant film-protected glass panels can help to confine and hence choke fires, thereby preventing their vertical and horizontal spread. It can also enable the development of a new generation of fire-resistant film-protected glass panels, which will help the glass industry to develop new products. We have also developed a valuable framework for predicting the thermal-mechanical behavior of glass building facades and improving the fire resistance. The development of the simulation method for modeling crack initiation and propagation in film-protected glass at elevated temperatures can be applied in alternative film-protected glass industrial applications. This research will also serve as an important reference for the development of guidelines and standards.

11261516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11261516.value: Networked mobile robots have a great potential in military and industrial applications. In practice, networked mobile robots are often required to autonomously deploy themselves in a region of interest to execute distributed sensing tasks such as search and rescue, environment surveillance, and forest fire monitoring. An important yet challenging problem arising from such tasks is the so-called multi-robot deployment problem, that is, to design distributed cooperative control laws for mobile robots such that they finally reach an optimal configuration with respect to a given performance metric. During the past decade, considerable effort has been devoted to cooperative control for multi-robot deployment and significant progress has been made. However, recent literature review reveals that study on multi-robot deployment is still in its early stage of development. Many critical issues on deployment of networked mobile robots in real-world applications remain to be investigated. These issues include heterogeneity of mobile robots, limited interaction/communication range, complex environments, and communication constraints. These issues, if not well addressed, will significantly degrade the deployment performance of networked mobile robots, or even worse, lead to the failure of multi-robot deployment in real-world applications. This project, by addressing these issues, will investigate and develop novel approaches to distributed cooperative control for deployment of networked heterogeneous mobile robots. In particular, this project will focus on the issues of connectivity preservation, environments with varying roughness, and variety of communication constraints. The outcome of this project is expected to enrich theoretical foundation of cooperative control for multi-robot deployment, and moreover, the proposed approaches will provide control engineers with more solid analysis and design tools for autonomously deploying mobile robots in real-world applications.

11261516.label: Realisation of objectives
11261516.value: All the revised objectives of the project have been successfully achieved which can be evidenced by several publications in top-tier international journals. The PI and his students/research associates have developed a number of novel approaches to cooperative control for optimal deployment of heterogeneous mobile robots.

11261516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11261516.value: We have investigated and developed novel approaches to cooperative control for deployment of heterogeneous mobile robots with connectivity preservation and in environments with varying roughness. Several new approaches have been developed. One approach is developed to deal with the coverage control problem for networked mobile sensors on a line with different actuation limits and different roughness of each point on the line. The optimization objective is to minimize the largest time required for the sensor network to reach any point on the line via optimizing the sensors’ locations on this line. Distributed coverage control laws with input constraints are developed to drive the sensors to the optimal configuration while preserving their spatial ordering on the line. Another approach is developed to deal with the scenario where the communication range of each sensor is limited. In addition, one approach is developed to deal with the case when sensors have bounded position measurement errors. Two cases of coverage control with and without order preservation of the sensors respectively, are considered. For each case, the upper bounds on the measurement errors are employed to design an estimation algorithm for each sensor to estimate the difference between neighboring sensors’ positions. Then, distributed coverage control laws are developed for the mobile sensors by using the estimated difference. Under the proposed control laws, the sensor network is driven to a neighborhood of the optimal configuration minimizing the cost function and the effect of the measurement errors on the coverage performance is reduced or even eliminated. Furthermore, we have also developed an approach to leader-follower formation control of mobile robots with bearing-only measurements. Simulation studies have also been done to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches. Several papers as a result of the research effort have been produced.

11261516.value: Due to the budget cut of the approved project in comparison to the original proposal, the objective iii) of the original proposal, that is, cooperative control for deployment of heterogeneous mobile robots subject to various communication constraints, was removed from the revised objectives. The study of this objective warrants further effort as communication constraints are hardly avoidable.

11261516.value: Networked mobile robots have a great potential in military and industrial applications. In practice, networked mobile robots are often required to autonomously deploy themselves in a region of interest to execute distributed sensing tasks such as search and rescue, environment surveillance, and forest fire monitoring. An important yet challenging problem arising from such tasks is the so-called multi-robot deployment problem, that is, to design distributed cooperative control laws for mobile robots such that they finally reach an optimal configuration with respect to a given performance metric. Though considerable effort has been devoted to addressing this problem and significant progress has been made, several critical issues on deployment of networked mobile robots in real-world applications remain to be investigated. These issues include heterogeneity of mobile robots, limited interaction/communication range, complex environments, and communication constraints. This project has addressed some of these issues. In particular, this project has investigated and developed novel approaches to distributed cooperative control for optimal deployment of networked heterogeneous mobile robots by preserving connectivity under limited interaction range, by dealing with varying roughness and measurement errors in complex environments. 11263216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11263216.value: Exposure to fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) has been linked with various adverse health effects. Particle bound metals, especially transition metals, are hypothesized to initiate respiratory disease and trigger systemic inflammatory disease response. Understanding the role of metals in PM induced health effects is key to mitigate the impact of air pollution and protect public health. Iron is the most abundant PM transition metals from various sources including road dust, traffic, industrial and ship emissions. Many research studies have shown positive association between water soluble iron and the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) as the pathway to oxidative stress. However, the two different oxidation states of ferrous (Fe(II)) and ferric (Fe(III)) can be inter-converted in which photoreduction of Fe(III) to Fe(II) theoretically participates in a catalytic cycle to produce toxic hydroxyl radicals (·OH) and Fe(II) can also be oxidized to Fe(III) by molecular oxygen to generate superoxide anion O2- while Fe(III) plays an important role in various redox reactions. Currently, there is very little information on if and how this inter-conversion can happen in the atmosphere. The significant knowledge gap not only limits our understanding of bioavailability of iron as an essential nutrient that controls oceanic productivity, and impacts the global carbon budget and climate, but also hinders the further illustration of the mechanisms of atmospheric aging effect on PM toxicity on adverse health effect. This study will combine both real world field investigation to provide evidence-based knowledge on the particle bound water soluble iron speciation, and laboratory investigation to demonstrate the impact of atmospheric processing and aging on the conversion between Fe (II) and Fe (III). The findings from this study will be one of the first investigations of its kind, and we expect the results will form the basis to better understand the relation between particle metals and health effects. 人體長期接觸以及曝露在細顆粒物當中將會產生許多健康方面的問題。當金屬依附在顆粒物上時，尤其是過渡金屬，可能會導致呼吸類疾病的發生甚至會產生全身性炎性疾病。了解金屬在顆粒物中的形態對於空氣污染物的遷移所引起的健康問題以及對健康方面的保護就起到了至關重要的作用。鐵，是空氣顆粒物中含量最高的過渡金屬，其來源包括路邊灰塵，交通運輸，工廠以及輪船排放。現今為止已有許多的研究結果表明可溶性的鐵離子與活性氧作為氧化應激的產生有最直接的關系。而且，鐵離子兩種不同價態之間是會產生內部轉換的，比如在光解的條件下三價鐵離子會催化產生羥自由基，而三價鐵本身也會被還原成二價鐵離子；二價鐵離子在被氧化的情況下會轉換成三價鐵並同時產生超氧離子，三價鐵離子在氧化還原反應中就起到了關鍵性的作用。然而現在仍然很少有研究資料證明這種內部轉換反應是否存在於大氣當中以及它們之間的轉換情況。這部分重要理論的缺失不止會限制我們對於鐵作為必要營養元素在人體內的生物利用度，控制海洋生產力，影響全球碳收支以及氣候變化的了解與認知。並且會阻礙大氣演變基理對於顆粒物的毒性及對人體健康影響的例證研究。我們這項科研的進行會將真實大氣環境下，附著在固體顆粒物上可溶於水的鐵離子的演變過程和在可控制條件下的實驗室模擬相結合進行研究，來論證究竟是何種物質對於大氣中鐵離子價態的轉化起到至關的影響作用，從而進一步研究這種轉化在大氣中又是如何進行的。

11263216.label: Realisation of objectives
11263216.value: In this project, the investigations performed in this project included assessment of diurnal pattern of the soluble iron speciation, lab simulations of transformations between Fe(III) and Fe(II) and oxidative potential of particle iron based on air particle samples collected from Hong Kong, Xi’an and Beijing using a customized PM sampler designed in this study. Photo-irradiation was conducted in a chamber fitted with UV lamps to investigate possible photo-transformation reactions between Fe(III) and Fe(II). Water soluble PM extracts were used for the analysis of iron concentration and the measurement of reactive oxygen species (ROS). The results demonstrate the transformations between Fe(II) and Fe(III) in daytime and nighttime of urban atmospheric particulate matter in Hong Kong. The results showed a similar trend in soluble Fe(II) percentages between daytime and nighttime whereas there were very large differences in percentages for samples collected in daytime compared to nighttime. The percentage of soluble Fe(II) was higher in samples collected in the daytime than those at nighttime. Solar irradiation could be one of the important factors contributing to this phenomenon. Most values of the solubility of total iron detected in daytime were slightly higher than those at nighttime. The solubility of iron was found to be extremely low in summer but was relatively high in winter, possibly associated with the different sources of iron. Iron sulfates in oil fly ash (80%) were found to be significantly more soluble than were iron oxides and aluminosilicates in crustal species (<10%) in a series of leaching experiments conducted at a neutral pH. UV lab-simulation tests were carried out with samples collected from three different locations in China. The percentages of soluble Fe(II) of all samples showed an increasing trend within 48 hours of UV irradiation in Hong Kong, Xi’an and Beijing while some of the control samples (placed in dark), did not show obvious changes and the rest showed a decreasing trend. The concentration of total soluble iron increased with the increase in concentration of soluble Fe(II). Most of soluble Fe(III) levels were found to decrease when the concentration of soluble Fe(II) increased. However the relationship between most of the concentrations of soluble Fe(II) and the concentrations of soluble Fe(III) showed a very poor linearity. The result indicated that the transformation from Fe(III) to Fe(II) did not occur only in water soluble forms. After 48 h of UV irradiation, a small part of the soluble Fe(III) transformed into soluble Fe(II) while most of the soluble Fe(II) resulted from the transformation of Fe(III) and Fe(II) in solid phase into water soluble phase. In the determination of non-cellular ROS, the average of ROS produced during the daytime is ~34.3% higher compared to nighttime while the relationship between the concentration of soluble Fe(II) and ROS intensity did not show a good linearity. Fe alone can’t be the sole surrogate for ROS production, as the ambient PM usually consists of hydroxyl, hydroperoxyl and organic peroxyl radicals that are believed to contribute to the ROS generation in addition to Fe. Non-cellular ROS measurements were performed with standard solutions of Fe(II) and Fe(III), which showed a high coefficient of determination for Fe(II) standards calculated at different time intervals of Fe(II)-induced ROS production. However, Fe(III), which followed a slower reversible reaction resulted in a non-linear correlation between its concentration and ROS produced both in the presence and absence of H2O2. It is therefore considered that the Fe(III) reduction is a slower process than Fe(II) oxidation, and the amount of ROS measured in PM samples can be generated mainly from Fe(II) oxidation. In the UV irradiation results, the trends of increasing ROS were clear in the samples collected in Hong Kong, Xi’an, Beijing following the aging time of from 0 to 48 h. After using standard addition method to test the matrix effect, we found that Fe(II) only contributed about a quarter of the ROS in PM extracts; the rest of ROS was induced by other chemicals, such as other transition metals, organics, etc. After adding the DTPA to the extract, the result indicated that in addition to transition metals, the contributions to ROS of other materials in the PM extracts were very low based on our detection method. Finally, we summarized our findings that UV irradiation can induce the transformation between Fe(III) and Fe(II) to generate soluble Fe(II) from the solid phase to the liquid phase. The increasing concentration of Fe(II) can induce the increase in ROS intensity which have been linked to the genesis of pulmonary, cardiovascular injury, and other diseases. The other metal ions must have played a similar role in oxidant generating activity but their presence and contribution to urban air particles are much lower than iron.

11263216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11263216.value: This study provides an alternative view of secondary aerosol chemical characteristics from photochemical process with evidence showing the active dissolution of insoluble ironic ions into soluble fraction, and the soluble ferric and ferrous oxidation transformation, leading to significant contribution to the aerosol oxidative potential in generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Our results revealed that the ratios of soluble Fe(II) to total soluble iron fell by an average value of 63.7%, indicating that soluble Fe(II) dominated in water soluble iron, while this average ratio was 8.1% higher during daytime than nighttime. This may be due to exposure to solar radiation in daytime. The change in percentage of soluble Fe(II) was also found to be reflected as an aging process as indicated by the lab simulation of transformation between Fe(III) and Fe(II), where an increasing trend of Fe(II) was obtained in terms of UV irradiation compared to that without UV irradiation. These findings support the concept that Fe(II) and Fe(III) undergoes a rapid chemical change and is a key factor in influencing the transformation between Fe(III) and Fe(II). Our results further demonstrated that after 48 h of UV irradiation, only a small part of the soluble Fe(III) transformed to soluble Fe(II) whereas most of the soluble Fe(II) were from the transformation of Fe(III) and Fe(II) in solid phase depending largely on the form and structure of iron in PM samples. On average, ROS production was ~34.3% higher in samples collected during daytime than nighttime most plausibly due to the higher UV index and longer period of UV irradiation in daytime. Considering that Fe(III) reduction was a slower process compared to Fe(II) oxidation, the amount of ROS measured in PM samples could be mainly from Fe(II) oxidation. The ROS measurement for Fe(II) in highly purified water further proved that after UV irradiation ROS intensity increased with the increase in concentration of Fe(II). In addition, other soluble formation of chemicals in PM may be considered as minor contributors. Our experimental data also confirmed that almost all the ROS detected were induced by transition metals, i.e. Fe in this study, and UV irradiation plays a role in the transformation and generation of soluble Fe(II) from solid phase to liquid phase and thus contribute the increased formation of ROS.

11263216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11263216.value: For the transformation of iron, multiple sample collection from different locations and a long exposure time to identify the changes of Fe(II) in a continued time series could be desirable to expend in the further study. In the lab-simulation, since we found that the transformation between Fe(III) and Fe(II) to generate soluble Fe(II) from the solid phase to liquid phase, and this finding was based only on the water phase test due to time and instrumental limitation in this research, it is necessary to confirm whether this transformation occurred directly on the solid form of iron. Future studies could focus on refining our results using X-ray absorbance near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy in conjunction with our wet chemical method and with the LED based liquid waveguide capillary cell spectroscopy together to link the characterization of Fe(II) both in solid and liquid phases. Further studies on the nature of phase transformation of other transition metals, in addition to iron, in the liquid and solid states together with the expended experiment from a chemical ROS to the lung cells of ROS assay are desirable to better understand their environmental impacts and the potential risks to public health.

11263216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11263216.value: In scientific community, most of the research were focus secondary organic aerosol formation, while this study provides evidence that transition metals, i.e. iron, are instead the dominating factor in the induction of secondary aerosol toxicity initiated by the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Laboratory UV irradiation and real world solar irradiation on aerosol samples both demonstrated the same pathway of iron species transformation during photochemical process with initial dissolution of solid ironic components, followed by the conversion of soluble ferric to ferrous ions. Further, the products of the iron transformation are the dominant contributor to ROS in aerosol. This study shows the significance of transition metals in secondary aerosol and ROS formation as the initial step leading to adverse health effects.

11266416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11266416.value: The terahertz (THz) radiation, known as T-ray, is defined as the electromagnetic waves with frequency from 0.3THz to 3THz, which locates in the transition region between microwave and infrared in the electromagnetic spectrum. As early as 2004, THz technology was recognized as “one of the ten emerging technologies that will change the world”, owing to its promising applications in numerous areas including security, biomedicine, communication, astronomy, etc. Imaging, spectroscopy and high-speed wireless communications using T-rays are some application examples receiving a great deal of research interest and development efforts. It is projected that the THz market will grow at a compound annual growth rate of 26% and reach over US$380 million by 2022. However, there have been major fundamental challenges in implementing THz systems because the frequency is either too low or too high to employ traditional optical or electronic approaches, respectively. Despite of many other difficulties, it’s commonly agreed that the lack of appropriate radiating sources is the critical bottleneck holding up the progress of THz technologies. So far, most existing THz radiators are implemented using optics, quantum cascade lasers, or compound III-V semiconductor processes, which are expensive, bulky and of low integration level. Advanced nm-scale CMOS would be a potential solution for form factor and cost reduction, but the transistors’ cut-off frequency is lower than 300GHz such that neither fundamental oscillation nor power amplification can be employed for an efficient THz signal generation. Recently, frequency multiplication and harmonic oscillation techniques were proposed, boosting up the frequency to exceed 300GHz. However, theoretically these techniques suffer from severe loss due to the ultralow frequency conversion efficiency, resulting in limited output power. Moreover, for the signal radiation, the on-chip antennas are of low efficiency and low gain owing to the lossy silicon substrate. Off-chip antennas themselves feature better performance but their physical contacts with the chip would severely deteriorate the system performance. Consequently, state-of-the-art CMOS radiators can only achieve limited performance in terms of output power, EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power) and DC-to-THz power conversion efficiency. This project aims to explore new THz techniques including varactor-less frequency tuning for signal generators, distributed structure for antennas and hierarchical power combining for system integration. A CMOS radiator suitable for many THz applications will be implemented, targeting at generating 320GHz T-rays with 0-dBm output power, 12-dBm EIRP and 0.3% power efficiency. 太赫茲（ THz ）波，又稱為 T 射線（ T-ray ），是指 0.3THz 至 3THz 頻段內的電磁輻射 , 其波長介於傳統微波和紅外線之間。 太赫茲在國土安全、生物醫學、數據通信、天文學等領域均具有重要的應用價值。 早在2004年，太赫茲技術在美國已被譽為「未來改變世界的十大新興技術之一」。 當前，越來越多的資源正逐漸投入到太赫茲成像、頻譜儀及高速無線數據通信等相關技術的研發中。 據預測，太赫茲相關市場將以26%的年複合增長率增長並于2022年超越38億美元的規模。 但是，太赫茲的應用在技術方面仍存在一些制約性因素，其根本原因是由於太赫茲所在的頻段比較特殊，比較成熟的電學及光學方法均無法直接運用。 在諸多技術難點當中，國內外同行普遍認為缺乏合適的低成本太赫茲輻射源是目前制約太赫茲相關技術發展進步的一個瓶頸。 現有的太赫茲輻射器大多通常採用光學（如量子級聯鐳射）或基於III-V半導體工藝的解決方案，造價高昂、體積龐大、集成度較低。 近年來，隨著CMOS（互補式金屬氧化物半導體）製造工藝的特徵尺寸演進到深亞微米至納米級，國內外學者開始嘗試利用CMOS技術來實現低成本、高集成度的太赫茲系統。 一個問題是CMOS晶體管的截止頻率較低，無法採用基本振盪或者功率放大等手段輸出高功率的太赫茲信號。 最近，學術界提出採用倍頻技術或者諧波振盪技術來解決太赫茲信號的產生問題。 但是，由於功率轉換效率很低，這些方案得到的信號輸出功率普遍很低。 另外一個問題是太赫茲天線的實現。 片上天線的輻射效率和增益都比較低，而高性能的片外天線在與晶片互聯時會產生系統難以負擔的巨大功率損耗。 因此，現有的CMOS太赫茲輻射器在輸出功率、EIRP（等效全向輻射功率）、功率轉換效率等方面的性能均非常有限。 本項目以探索新穎的太赫茲相關技術為目標，具體包括用於信號發生器的非變容管頻率調諧機制，分佈式天線結構，及多層次系統功率合成架構。 以這些技術為基礎，項目將集成一款工作頻率約320GHz，輸出功率為0dBm，EIRP為12dBm，功率效率約0.3% 的太赫茲輻射器晶片。

11266416.label: Realisation of objectives
11266416.value: In this research project, we have successfully developed new CMOS injected-locked Terahertz (THz) radiator integrating a half-quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (HQVCO), four injection-locked frequency quadruplers (ILFQs), and a chip-and-package distributed antenna (DA). The results have been filed three US patents [2]-[4] and published one journal in IEEE JOURNAL OF SOLID-STATE CIRCUITS [1], which is the leading journal of IC applications and designs. These achieved results completely met with the defined project objectives of 1 to 4 in this GRF project. We proposed to use an architecture based on injection locking to allow individual optimization of the output power and the phase noise. Then, intrinsic-delay compensation and harmonic boosting techniques were proposed to optimize the phase noise of the HQVCO and the output power of the ILFQs, respectively. The proposed DA composed of four exciting elements on silicon chip and a primary radiator in low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) package features a wide bandwidth of 13% and a gain of 3.8 dBi without using lens at 312 GHz. Implemented in a 65-nm CMOS process, the radiator system occupying a core area of 0.36 mm2 achieves output frequency from 311.6 to 315.5 GHz and maximum equivalent isotropically radiated power (EIRP) of 10.5 dBm while consuming 300 mW. The output phase noise measures −109.3 dBc/Hz at 10-MHz offset and the dc-to-THz efficiency is 0.42%. In addition to THz CMOS development, this project also trained up two PhD graduates and other RF & antenna engineers. They invented some novel antenna designs for high-frequency applications. The inventions include a glass dielectric resonator antenna with liquid metal [5,6], a circularly-polarized dielectric rod antenna [7], a open-slot antenna array [8], a CPW-fed metasurface antenna [9]. These inventions have been published in IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters, and IEEE Access. The proposed antenna technologies can apply to the millimeter-wave and terahertz antenna designs. These achieved results with the trained PhD students completely met the defined project objective of 5 in this GRF project. 11267516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11267516.value: Currently, transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) are widely used as transparent conductors for thin film solar cells. Because of the potential of roll-to-roll, large-area processing on flexible low-cost substrates, flexible solar cells are a very attractive technology for the low-cost photovoltaic market. For flexible solar cells, an additional requirement for the transparent electrode is that the deposition must be carried out at temperatures lower than the deformation temperature of flexible polymer substrates. In this proposal we plan develop highly conducting and transparent CdO-based transparent conductors for flexible solar cell applications. This work built upon our prior efforts on the development of CdO-based TCOs for full spectrum solar cells. We have demonstrated that because of its high carrier mobilities, CdO can achieve a high conductivity of >30000 S/cm with transparency widow of 400-1500 nm. This makes them good candidates for full spectrum photovoltaic applications. However, our previous efforts focused on CdO-based TCOs deposited at elevated temperatures of 200-500C on glass substrates. Low temperature growth of most metal oxides resulted in amorphous or nano-crystalline materials, giving rise to degraded electrical and optical properties. Nevertheless, CdO is known to have a surface electron accumulation layer, suggesting that grain boundaries in CdO do not form barriers for electron transport. Hence it is expected that CdO thin films grown at low temperature can still achieve high electron concentration and mobility. Recently, a new class of low temperature grown amorphous oxides, the amorphous oxide semiconductors (AOSs) has been developed. They have the many unique properties including large electron mobilities ~10-20 cm^2/Vs and excellent surface flatness that can be exploited as TCOs for flexible solar cells. We note that since CdO and Ga2O3 crystallize in distinctly different crystal structure and they have very different band gap energies of 2.2 and 4.8 eV, respectively, co-depositing CdO and Ga2O3 at low temperature is expected to form amorphous alloys with a wide band gap span. Given the many desirable properties of CdO, Cd-Ga-O AOSs is also expected to be a good TCO material for flexible PV applications. In this proposal, the low temperature synthesis and properties of CdO as well as alloys of CdO-Ga2O3 over the entire composition range will be explored. In particular, we will optimize both CdO and Cd-Ga-O AOS films as transparent conductors on flexible substrates and demonstrate the improved performance of flexible solar cells fabricated on these new transparent conductors. 作為透明電極，透明導電氧化物 (TCO) 被廣泛應用於當今的薄膜太陽能電池技術中。因適宜卷對卷、大面積製備，塑料柔性基太陽能電池在低成本光伏市場極具吸引力。對於塑料基柔性光伏電池而言，透明電極的沉積溫度須低於塑料基底的熱形變溫度。在此項研究中，我們將開發基於CdO的高電導率的透明導體材料，并將其應用於柔性太陽能電池。該項研究是基於我們先前所發展的適用於全光譜太陽能電池的CdO透明電極材料之研究工作而開展。 我們先前的研究工作表明，由於其高的載流子遷移率，CdO的電導率可超過30000 S/cm，且在400-1500 nm光譜段表現出高的穿透率。該結果表明，CdO透明導電材料在全光譜太陽能電池中具有重要的應用價值。然而，我們先前在基於CdO導電材料方面的研究工作，僅集中於在玻璃基底上的高溫（200-500oC）沉積過程。對於大多數金屬氧化物而言，低溫生長的薄膜一般呈現出非晶態或納米晶態，從而使得其光電特性劣於其相應的晶態薄膜。不過，由於CdO表面電荷累積層的存在，其晶界將不會阻礙電荷的傳輸。因此，低溫生長的CdO薄膜有望呈現出高的載流子濃度及高的遷移率。 近來，人們研發出了一種新型低溫生長的非晶態氧化物半導體材料。該非晶態氧化物具有較高的電子遷移率（10-20 cm2/Vs）與良好的表面平整度，可作為透明導電氧化物而應用於柔性太陽能電池。由於CdO與Ga2O3晶體結構存在明顯差異，且其相應的帶隙分別為2.2 與4.8 eV，低溫共沉積CdO與Ga2O3有望形成寬帶隙跨度的非晶態合金材料。考慮到CdO具有不少優異的光電特性，基於Cd-Ga-O體系的非晶態氧化物半導體也有望成為一理想的可應用於柔性光伏電池的透明導電氧化物材料。 在該項研究計劃中，我們將探索低溫生長的CdO與CdO-Ga2O3之合金，并系統地研究其光電特性。特別地，作為柔性透明導電材料，我們將優化CdO與Cd-Ga-O體系非晶態薄膜的性能，並在其上展示出性能更為優良的柔性太陽能電池。

11267516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11267516.value: In this study, two new transparent amorphous conducting alloy semiconductor systems were developed using sputter deposition technique at room temperature. The amorphous composition range for both the CdxGa1-xO and CdxIn1-xO alloys were identified. Structural, electrical and optical properties of both crystalline and amorphous alloy films were thoroughly investigated. The amorphous alloy films of both of these systems were found to have electrical properties better than the existing amorphous conducting materials used in transparent flexible optoelectronic devices. In particular, these new alloy films have the advantages of high electron mobility and widely tunable band gap as well as electronic energy band edges. For example, the intrinsic bandgap of CdxGa1-xO ranges from 2.2 eV to 4.8 eV while their conduction band minimum can be tuned from 5.8 to 4.5 eV below the vacuum level. This is particularly important since matching the electronic bands in heterojunction devices is critical in the device performance. Furthermore, in order to determine if these films deposited on flexible substrates can be used for flexible electronics, the integrity of their electrical properties with mechanical bending is critical. We have carried out systematic investigations on the electrical resistivity variation of both crystalline and amorphous alloy films against mechanical bending as a function of the bending radius and number of bending cycles. We found that the amorphous CdxGa1-xO and CdxIn1-xO alloy films are very resistant to compressive bending down to a bending radius of 5 mm.

11267516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11267516.value: The ultimate goal of this project is to develop highly conducting, transparent and flexible amorphous thin films for flexible optoelectronic device applications. To test the suitability of the amorphous films we developed as transparent conductors (TC) on solar cells, we have fabricated perovskite solar cell structures using an amorphous CdInO layer as the top transparent conductor layer. This structure is directly compared to a solar cell using room temperature deposited ITO as the TC layer. Our preliminary results should improved fill factor as well as power conversion efficiency for the device using the amorphous CdInO layer. This can be attributed to the much improved conductivity of the CdInO layer. Our next step is to use our amorphous thin films as TC on perovskite or other organic solar cells fabricated on flexible substrates and test their performance when the cells are subjected to mechanical bending. In addition, due to their inherent high mobility, we also plan to modify the electrical properties of these amorphous thin films via doping and use them as active layers in thin film transistors.

11267516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11267516.value: Because of the potential of roll-to-roll, large-area processing on flexible low-cost substrates, flexible solar cells are a very attractive technology for the low-cost photovoltaic market. For flexible solar cells, the transparent electrode has to be highly conducting and transparent and at the same time be grown at low temperature so that the flexible plastic substrate would not deform. In this project, we developed new amorphous CdO-based alloy thin films with very high conductivity and visible transparency. These thin films were synthesized using the industry compatible sputtering method at room temperature on plastic susbtrates. More importantly, we also showed that these amorphous alloy films can be subjected to mechanical inward bending with a bending radius as small as 5 mm for multiple cycles without significant degradation in their electrical properties. The electrical, optical and mechanical properties of these amorphous films strongly suggested that they are suitable for transparent and flexible electronic device applications. Finally, these films were tested as a transparent conductor on an organic based solar cell structure and yielded reasonably high power conversion efficiency.

11267916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11267916.value: Magnetically actuated microrobots exhibit immense potential for many applications in the field of precision medicine, such as the delivery of targeted cells, microtissues, or drugs. Effective delivery of targeted materials for critical illnesses is still a major technical hurdle that has yet to be overcome. Several challenging problems that severely restrict the clinical applications of this novel technique include ensuring a large workspace with quantitatively controlled magnetic field density and gradient, designing microrobot structures that can successfully transport functional cells or targeted drugs to the disease site, and automatically controlling the precise position and orientation of microrobots in a 3D environment. This study aims to explore these challenging problems. We will develop a magnetically actuated microrobotic control system and hypothesize that such advancement will enable cell-cultured microrobots to navigate through body fluids (e.g., cerebrospinal fluid and blood or retinal vessels) and transport cells, microtissues, or drugs to target regions inside the body. Investigations will be conducted from four perspectives. First, the spatial distribution of the magnetic field will be modeled and identified through a laboratory-designed electromagnetic manipulation platform. The model will facilitate the quantitative characterization of the magnetic actuation field over the entire magnetic field, thereby enabling the magnetic agents to be operated in a substantially large workspace. Second, magnetic microrobot carriers will be designed and fabricated using a 3D laser writing tool (Nanoscribe), which will allow functional cells to be cultured and then readily delivered to the specified location for tissue fusion and vascularization. Third, a robust control approach will be designed to overcome environmental disturbances in the magnetic field and fluid flow, and model uncertainty, as well as achieve the precise position and orientation control of the microrobots in a 3D environment. Finally, a pre-clinical study utilizing the developed system and technologies will be conducted to deliver specialized cells in an animal body and explore their functional role in liver cancer. The success of this study will substantially advance the application of magnetic microrobotics in the field of precision medicine. This study will also facilitate the development of new technologies to enable automated cell surgery for various unforeseen applications that were thought to be impossible. 電磁驅動微機器人系統可以用來將細胞準確地傳送給體內的相關部位，從而對精准醫學的發展起到極大的促進作用。本項目主要從以下幾個方面對這一課題展開研究。首先，對於電磁驅動模型進行深入探討，重點解決如何擴大有效電磁驅動空間及相關磁場控制這一問題。其次，研究用於攜帶細胞的微機器人的結構和製造工藝等。然後，將對微機器人驅動的控制演算法進行研究，以實現對攜帶細胞的微機器人實現自動化控制。最後，對以上研究進行實驗論證。

11267916.label: Major findings and research outcome
11267916.value: This project was successfully completed in four aspects. First, we modeled quantitatively the spatial distribution of the electromagnetic field using the finite element method (FEM), and verified the validity of this model through comparison between modeling and experimental results. With this modeling information, we could successfully manipulate the microparticles effectively in a larger workspace than the central area only. Second, we designed a microrobot with a burr-like porous spherical structure (diameter 80-90 μm) for carrying and delivering targeted cells in vivo under a magnetic gradient field-driven mechanism. The robot was fabricated using three-dimensional (3D) laser lithography and coated with Ni for magnetic actuation and Ti for biocompatibility. Third, we developed a robust feedback control approach to precisely actuate the microrobots by using self-constructed electromagnetic coil system. A nonlinear high-gain observer was designed to estimate the velocity of the controlled microparticle and to eliminate the measurement noise amplified by the high observer gain. Finally, we performed both in-vitro and in-vivo tests of driving the microrobots with carried cells to the desired location and release cells. In the in vivo experiments, transparent zebrafish was used as the animal model so that the microrobot could be directly observed under an ordinary optical microscope. This work developed the world first magnetic microrobot that can carry and deliver cells to a desired site in vivo, which was reported in the top journal Science Robotics. The precise delivery of targeted cells will offer various applications in precision medicine in the future.

11267916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11267916.value: Further development of this research will focus on the in vivo imaging technology such that the experiments can be done inside the body with depth. We are currently studying the photoacoustic imaging technology and planning to use it to the in vivo tests on mice and rats. In addition, we also need to investigate the use of synthesis composite materials in making microrobots to meet the requirement of degradability, mechanical strength and magnetic actuation simultaneously.

11267916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11267916.value: In this project, we developed a magnetically-powered microrobotic system that can enable microrobots to navigate through body fluids for biomedical applications such as transporting cells to target site in the body. Investigations were conducted from four perspectives. First, the spatial distribution of the magnetic field was modeled and identified through a laboratory-designed electromagnetic manipulation platform. The model could facilitate the quantitative characterization of the magnetic actuation field over the entire magnetic field, thereby enabling the magnetic agents to be operated in a substantially large workspace. Second, magnetic microrobots were designed and fabricated using a 3D laser writing tool (Nanoscribe), which allowed functional cells to be cultured and readily delivered to the desired location. Third, a robust control approach was developed to overcome various environmental disturbances and model uncertainty and achieve the precise position control of microrobots in a 3D environment. Finally, a pre-clinical study utilizing the developed system and technologies was conducted successfully to deliver stem cells in the body of animal. The success of this study will substantially advance the application of magnetic microrobotics in the precision medical treatment.

11268616.label: Project Objectives
11268616.value: We will define a model for online scheduling with calibrations. We will give practical algorithms with guaranteed performance bounds. We will then extend these results to handle weighted jobs that can be prioritized, and multiple machines. We will examine the online model in the context of speed augmentation, allowing us to further understand the structure of the problem. We plan to find a tight tradeoff between speed augmentation and the approximation ratio. We will find lower bounds for the online calibration problem to help design better algorithms, and hopefully prove optimality of our results. When we are given a fixed budget of calibrations, we will give an offline algorithm to complete the jobs as quickly as possible within that budget. We hope to extend this algorithm to work with multiple machines and combine it with other calibration scheduling models (like calibrations taking time). When operating costs differ depending on the time when a machine is running, we hope to give an efficient dynamic programming solution. Depending on the practicality of the result, we may aim to find a more practical solution which gives a potentially less-than-optimal solution. We plan to give an algorithm solving the problem when machines can be calibrated all at once without increasing the cost. This has some connections to the single-machine setting, which we hope to explore. We are the first to consider the problem of batched calibrations to our knowledge.

11268616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11268616.value: Scheduling is an area of computer science which studies how to efficiently execute a series of tasks, or jobs. A scheduling algorithm decides when and where to run the jobs (possibly with some constraints) to minimize an objective function. Recent work has considered scheduling on machines that need to be calibrated. These machines are assumed to be high-performance and high-maintenance, and perform very precise tasks, for example, medical and healthcare equipment or embedded systems with input sensors. As such, they need to be calibrated before they can be trusted to perform a job. Performing these calibrations can be very expensive, possibly much more than the cost of running the machines. The calibrations are only effective for a set period of time, after which the machine may no longer be accurate, and must be (expensively) recalibrated before running more jobs. The goal of algorithms in this framework is to minimize the number of calibrations. This objective function has an interesting property: in most objective functions (say, minimizing total flow time, or maximizing number of jobs completed by a deadline), it is generally profitable to schedule a job as early as possible. However, to minimize calibrations, the algorithm wants to group jobs together as much as possible, possibly delaying some jobs considerably. The known algorithms in this framework are designed to effectively handle this tradeoff: grouping jobs for more efficient calibrations, while maintaining a reasonable schedule where jobs are not delayed too long. Our goal in this project is to extend the initial work on scheduling with calibrations. In particular, we want to generalize the model to give more algorithms that could be useful in practical situations (in a high-precision manufacturing plant, for example). As such, we want algorithms that perform well in minimizing the number of calibrations, while being practical to implement and run. Our initial results show that very simple---though difficult to analyze---algorithms can perform very well even with constraints that initially seem difficult to tackle. 在计算机科学中，调度研究的是如何有效的执行一系列的任务。调度算法会决定在满足一定限制情况下何时何处执行哪些任务来最优化某个目标函数。近几年出现了关于带校准的机器的调度问题。这些机器通常性能高但维护成本也高，比如医疗保健器械或带有传感器的嵌入式系统。他们在执行任务之前需要被校准以确保准确无误。而校准本身的成本相当高，通常高于执行任务的代价。而且一次校准只能保证一定时间内的精度，过了这段时间后又要重新校准。在该领域的调度问题以最小化校准次数为目标。这个目标有一个有趣的性质：在传统调度目标中（比如最小化总等待时间或最大化某个时刻前完成的总任务数），通常尽可能早的去做任务会比较好，而为了最小化校准的次数，人们通常需要把任务捆绑在一起，从而有可能延迟执行某些任务。目前已有的算法均试图平衡两者的关系：捆绑任务减少校准次数，而同时不要把任务延误太多。 在这个项目中，我们计划扩展带校准的调度模型。具体来讲，我们想要设计更多的在实际中用得上的算法（比如在高精度工厂当中）。所以我们会设计一些算法既能减少校准次数又容易实现。我们的初步结果显示非常简单（但是需要复杂分析才能证明性能）的算法已经可以表现很好，即使对于那些初看起来很难处理的限制条件。

11268616.label: Realisation of objectives
11268616.value: For objective 1, we have designed an online algorithm to solve the following three cases. Single machine, unweighted unit size jobs (where we proved an approximation ratio of 3). Single machine, weighted unit size jobs and multiple machines, unweighted unit size jobs (where we proved an approximation ratio of 12 for both). We also have a lower bound of 2 for the above scenarios. The results are published in SPAA 2017. We also studied the resource augmentation setting by introducing two types of calibrations, one with a normal speed and the other with a speed twice the normal speed. However, even this simple twist makes the problem extremely hard. We are only able to show optimal solutions for jobs with nested intervals and jobs with laminar structure. Due to this, the results are not sufficient to be published in a decent conference. Besides speed augmentation, we also studied the augmentation of calibrations. We found that by allowing more calibrations than the optimum, we could indeed design an algorithm to find a feasible schedule. Thus, we extend the results of the original work on the offline problem and achieve an 1+epsilon approximation algorithm (PTAS). This work is presented in SPAA 19. For objective 2, we studied the single machine case and designed a dynamic programming algorithm with running time O(Kn^3) where K is the number of calibrations allowed. We then can do binary search to find the best K which can minimize the objective studied in the online scenario. The results are published in SPAA 17. We then extend it to the multiple machine case, where the objective is to schedule a set of jobs such that the total weight is maximized on m identical machines with at most K calibrations. We present a (1/3) -approximation polynomial time algorithm when jobs have unit processing time. For the arbitrary processing time case, we give a ((1−ε)/3) -approximation pseudo-polynomial time algorithm and a ((1−ε)/18) -approximation polynomial time algorithm. The results are published in WADS 2019. Recently, we further improve the ratio 1/3 to 1-1/e but the results are still in submission. For objective 3, we started to explore the case with time slots cost and derived some initial results. As a byproduct, we also obtained FPTAS for another related scheduling problem where each calibration could support up to k jobs. The results are published in ISAAC 2017. We then study the calibration scheduling with time slot cost with an objective of minimizing calibration cost plus time slot cost. In this problem, other than calibration cost, a certain time slot cost will be incurred when the machine executes a job and such a cost is determined by the time slot that is occupied by the job in the schedule. We consider jobs with release times, deadlines and identical processing times. The objective is to schedule the jobs on a single machine and minimize the total cost while calibrating the machine at most K times. We investigate the structure of the optimal schedule and based on that we propose dynamic programs for different scenarios of the problem. At last, for another variant of the problem without the consideration of machine calibration, a greedy algorithm is proposed, which is based on matroid theory. The results are published in AAIM 2018 and later in Theoretical Computer Science. We also studied batch calibration where calibrations on different machines can be done in a batch. It is then not possible to perform any calibrations during a period of T after the previous batch calibration. We consider different cost function depending on the number of machines we calibrate at a given time. Moreover, jobs have release time, deadline and unit processing time. The objective is to schedule all jobs with the minimum cost of calibrations. We give a dynamic programming to solve the case with arbitrary cost function. Then, we propose several faster approximation algorithms for different cost functions. The results are published in COCOON 2019 and later in Theoretical Computer Science.

11268616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11268616.value: There are further directions that can be pursued. One direction is to study calibration scheduling for jobs with multiple feasible intervals, where each job can only be processed in its available time periods. A second direction is to study the calibration with probing where the duration of the calibration has some distributions and its exact length is known if an extra probing action is done at some cost smaller than the calibration cost. We could also study the stochastic setting where a calibration's duration has a distribution but it is known when one makes the calibration. The goal is then to minimize the expected number of calibrations to complete all the jobs in time.

11268616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11268616.value: Calibration is a very natural setting where the machine's normal operation period will end after some time. It can be used in many manufacturing scenarios like high precision production, weapon calibration, etc.. Because the calibration operation usually needs to be carried out by experts to whom we usually need to pay, minimizing the number of calibrations to finish all jobs then becomes vital in saving the cost. As such, this property of scheduling jobs within a limited number of calibration intervals as much as possible is quite interesting in the scheduling research community. On the other hand, the objective of maximizing the benefit of the completed jobs given the budget is also interesting. When there are multiple machines, batch calibration is of practical importance since inviting an expert to come over to calibrate multiple machines at the same time usually incurs similar cost as the case of calibrating one machine because the dominating cost of inviting the expert may lie in the air tickets which could dominate his hourly charging rate. The derived results from this project has provable performance guarantee and therefore can be used safely in practice.

11269216.value: To update the existing optical test rig to enable on-line measurements of film thickness. To characterize the influence of lubricant quantity on lubricating film building. To validate the load-carrying capacity of typical oil/air mixture films which occur with fragmented appearances under LLS conditions.
