11269216.label: Realisation of objectives
11269216.value: Obj.1 To enable on-line measurements of film thickness (*Details can be found in Peer-reviewed publication (1) in Part C.) A new approach was successfully developed to achieve on-line measurement of lubricating film thickness in a slider-on-disc contact. The inclination of the slider is obtained by Fourier transform and frequency estimation of the interferogram of the sliding contact. The developed algorithm that is based on optical flow calculation and dynamic time warping technique enables tracking a characteristic point with constant film thickness on the 1-D modulated intensity curve. Thus, on-line film thickness measurement is achieved. Obj.2 To characterize the influence of lubricant quantity on lubricating film building and friction. (*Details can be found in Peer-reviewed publication (3) and recognized international conference paper (1) in Part C.) Experiments were conducted with controlled lubricant supply and under full lubricant supply as well for comparison. Film thickness and friction of the slider bearings were measured at different speeds. At the lowest speed, all tests of different lubricant volumes generated almost the same film thickness, which was equal to the film thickness of full lubricant supply. At increased speed, the film thickness of limited lubricant supply deviated from those of full-supply. Further increase in speed, the film thickness remained nearly unchanged. In general, large lubricant volume presented high film thickness. It only departed from the corresponding film thickness of full lubricant supply at high speeds, wherein a region of rippled fringes appeared at the inlet of the bearing in the interferogram of the slider contact. Under limited lubricant supply, low speed interferograms for those of small supply volume presented a full film within the entire contact, showing adequate lubricant supply at the inlet. When speed was increased, the small lubricant volume could no longer provide full lubricant supply at the inlet of the contact and fragmented films (oil/air mixture) appeared. On the contrary to the increase in film thickness with the quantity of lubricant supplied, friction does not change much. The size of the full-lubricated area was measured. The starved hydrodynamic lubricating films were assumed to have a constant nominal viscosity, which was thus calculated based on the boundary conditions of the carrying load and the measured film thickness. The calculated viscous friction force is found well correlated with the experimental measurements. The magnitude of the nominal viscosity of the starved films is quite small, i.e. an order of magnitude less than that of the specimen lubricant. Hence, the viscous friction of starved lubricating films is small. Obj. 3 To validate the load-carrying capacity of typical oil/air mixture films which occur with fragmented appearances under LLS conditions. (*Details can be found in Peer-reviewed publication (3) in Part C.) To study the load-carrying capacity of the oil/air mixture films, some theoretical calculations were carried out and compared to the measurements. In the calculations, zero pressure was assumed to the boundary of full film region, and particularly the pressure in the starvation area was assumed to be zero. The size of the starvation area was extracted from the experimental images. The load was carried only in the area of full fringes. The smaller film thickness in the calculation implied less load-carrying capacity than that in the experiment. The load carried by the area of the full film in the experiments can be calculated by using the measured film thickness in the calculation of the Reynolds equation. If the calculated load is less than the applied load, the fragmented fringes can sustain some load. In the experiments of limited lubricant supply, the starvation area increased and the calculated load of the full film area was markedly less than the applied load, indicating that the load-carrying capacity of the oil/air mixture or fragmented area (starvation area). These results showed that the starvation areas presented load-carrying capacity. Obj. 4 To present an effective surface effect on driving the lubricant for localized lubricant replenishment and entrainment into bearing contact. (*Details can be found in Peer-reviewed publication (2, 5 and 6) in Part C.) A novel concept for regulating lubricant replenishment/supply by means of wettability gradient was established. The wettability gradient which is implemented on the two sides of the lubrication track. Two ideas, namely oleophobic coating and surface texture, were proposed and evaluated. The original surface of the bearing track is oleophilic (steel or glass) and sandwiched by the oleophobic-coated areas on the two sides. The design was evaluated with an elasto-hydrodynamic lubricated (EHL) contact [Paper (2)]. The wettability gradient on the two sides could drive the lubricant to form a stable oil reservoir leading to thick EHL films. The same idea of using oleophobic coating to facilitate wettability gradient was also appraised with hydrodynamic slider bearings [Paper (5)]. On the other hands, an oleophobic surface pattern was adopted to generate the wettability. A periodic comb-tooth-shaped pattern with anisotropic wetting capability was devised. Results show that the comb-tooth-shaped pattern enables the rearrangement of oil distribution, thereby escalating oil replenishment to the lubrication track. The effect is due to the unbalanced interfacial force created by the surface pattern. Surface patterns can be implemented using femtosecond laser ablation and they last much longer than oleophobic coatings in practice. [Paper (6)] Obj.5 To build a lubrication model (incorporating hydrodynamic effect, surface effect and partial oil/air mixture films) and develop an efficient numerical procedure to theoretically explain the experimental findings. (*Details can be found in Peer-reviewed publication (4) in Part C.) Hydrodynamic lubrication under limited lubricant supply conditions is modeled as a combination of fully flooded and starved conditions. A typical LLS interferogram shows two lubrication regimes co-exist in the bearing contact, which are signified with upright and rippled/fragmented interference fringes, respectively. The lubricating films are thus considered to have two parts. The full-film region is lubricated with the given specimen lubricant. Its viscosity is known beforehand. The starved region consists of mixture of oil/air films, which is simply assumed to be a single phase viscous fluid of a nominal viscosity. Using an appropriate value as the nominal viscosity of the starved films, the calculated results in film thickness and friction are well correlated to the experimental measurements. Thus, the developed model is validated.

11269216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11269216.value: 1. Update of the fixed-incline slider tester for on-line film thickness measurement The fixed-incline slider tester was invented by my research team in 2010. Its major drawback was the requirement of stopping the test and the slider falling through the lubricating film to get the film thickness. This project has successfully devised a robust algorithm based on Fourier transformation and frequency estimation to determine the slider inclination, and also realized the on-line film thickness measurement using optical flow calculation and the dynamic time warping technique. (Refer to Paper [1] in Part C) 2. Characterisation of limited lubricant supplied (LLS) and starved hydrodynamic film in slider bearing contacts We found that starved lubrication regime exists when the bearing speed has attained certain critical value which is dependent upon the oil volume at LLS. Beyond that, the bearing contact consists of two lubrication regimes, full-film and starved. Through experimental and theoretical studies, we obtained that the load support and friction of the bearing are largely relied on the full lubricating film. However, the starved regime also contributes. We successfully established a theoretical model for the co-existing lubrication regime in a bearing under LLS. (Refer Papers [3 and 4] in Part C.) 3. Enhancement of lubrication effect on bearings running at LLS or starvation conditions. A novel idea of using wettability gradient to enrich the oil replenishment to the lubrication track was successfully devised. Subsequently, the lubrication of bearing under LLS conditions can be enhanced. The same idea can also be applied to improve the starvation problems of running bearings. (Refer to Papers [2, 5 and 6] in Part C.) 4. Novel designs for wettability gradient by (a) oleophobic coatings and (b) micro/nano surface texture. Based on the phenomenon that a liquid drop tends to move towards the oleophilic region if it is put on the boundary of oleophobic and oleophilic regions. We treated the surrounding area of the lubrication track oleophobic while the track surface was oleophilic. Results from the experiments with a ball-on-disc and a slider-on-disc contacts proved the positive effects of the wettability gradient on lubrication. (Refer to Papers [2 and 5] in Part C) We also devised a comb-tooth-shaped pattern to facilitate wettability gradient. Two arrays of the pattern were formed as mirror images on the two sides of the lubrication track. They produce distinct effect on oil replenishment. (Refer to Paper [6] in Part C)

11269216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11269216.value: We studied the bearing lubrication under the limited lubricant supply condition using oleophobic-patterned coating in this project and found that good lubrication can be achieved using a limited amount of lubricant. However, the durability of the oleophobic coating is a problem and it hinders the application potential. Thus, we tried surface texture. We devised a three-dimensional comb-tooth groove texture which demonstrates unidirectional lubricant movement. The pattern can be readily produced by femto-laser ablation. We found that oil replenishment can be enriched by implementing the devised pattern on the two sides of the lubricant track. Its positive effect has been verified, but how and how good it works require further exploration. It is worth to gain in-depth understanding of the newly devised patterns for enabling unidirectional oil flow to enhance oil replenishment. The acquired knowledge will reduce the impact of the starvation problem and enable the optimal operation of bearing with limited lubricant supply.

11269216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11269216.value: Protecting the environment by reducing petroleum-based lubricant use has become a major universal concern. The oversupply of lubricant to machine elements is common in practice because individuals usually err on the side of caution. Oversupplying lubricant is more than an issue of wastage. The resistance generated by an excessive amount of lubricant may interrupt a running system, e.g. micro-machineries. This study investigated the fundamental relation between quantity of lubricant supply and the effective hydrodynamic bearing lubrication. Some operative strategies, by using tailored surface effects, were devised to facilitate effective lubrication with the optimal supply of lubricant. Two surface patterns were invented to produce wettability gradient that guides the exceeding oil around the bearing contact point back to the bearing running track for lubrication. The two patterns were, respectively, produced by chemical coating and physical surface texture. They generated positive effect on bearing lubrication and were able to make good use of the available lubricant. The knowledge acquired in the project is valuable to lubrication design for both classical industrial machineries and particularly, advanced miniature devices.

11270116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11270116.value: In the field of operations research and management sciences (OR/MS), mathematical models are often built to understand the system behaviors and to make decisions. These models have a wide spectrum of fidelity, from highly stylized models to complicated simulation models. Stylized models are often built on overly-simplified assumptions and admit elegant analytical formula. They are useful in understanding how systems work on a high level, in developing managerial insights and in making qualitative decisions. But they often perform poorly in predicting system performances and in making quantitative decisions. Simulation models, on the other hand, incorporate many details and often deliver credible predictions. But they are typically slow to run and, thus, it is difficult to construct the response surface (i.e., metamodeling) and conduct optimization (i.e., simulation optimization). In this project we propose to incorporate stylized models into stochastic kriging method, which is a popular and powerful tool for simulation metamodeling, and use the new combined model for prediction and optimization. Our preliminary results show that the idea works well for simple queueing simulation models. For the idea to work for more realistic problems, there are a number of research questions that need to be answered. In this project we will design hypothesis test to test whether the inclusion of stylized models improve the fitting quality, create indicators that measure the goodness of fit, develop algorithms for fast metamodeling so it may be used in simulation optimization algorithms, and study the convergence and rate of convergence of the new algorithms. We will also consider how to apply the new methods in queueing simulation problems, which include applications in manufacturing, supply chains and healthcare management. In particular, we will study how to develop appropriate stylized models for typical queueing situations and consider how to generate stylized models automatically in commercial simulation software packages such as Arena and Simio. 在运筹学和管理科学领域，数学模型往往用以理解系统行为和决策支持。这些模型逼真度的范围广泛，从高度程式化的模型到复杂的仿真模型，应有尽有。程式化模型往往需要过度简化的假设条件，有着优雅的解析形式。它们强于揭示系统中变量的相互关系，但弱于预测。而仿真模型往往可以提供可靠的预测，但运行速度缓慢，因此在曲面建模和优化中难以应用。在此项目中，我们建议将两种模型结合起来，并将其运用在制造业、供应链和医疗管理等领域的排队系统管理上。

11270116.label: Realisation of objectives
11270116.value: All the project objectives have been successfully achieved. In particular, we have developed stochastic kriging techniques to incorporate stylized models in simulation metamodeling, and studied statistical inference methods and goodness of fit indicators for model comparison and selection in metamodeling. We have also proposed fast algorithms for construct stochastic kriging metamodels when incorporating stylized models, and analyzed their asymptotic properties, including their variances, biases and mean squared errors. Application of the proposed method in queueing networks especially in patient flow management has been examined to demonstrate its value. More generally, the use of stylized model enhanced stochastic kriging in simulation optimization problems such as ranking and selection has been investigated and it turns out to be a promising simulation metamodeling tool. Convergent properties of the proposed simulation optimization algorithm have been established, and numerical testing based on queueing networks with application to hospital flow management has been conducted to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method and its relative merits compared to existing methods in the literature.

11270116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11270116.value: The research objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. We have developed stochastic kriging techniques to incorporate stylized models in simulation metamodeling, and studied statistical inference methods and goodness of fit indicators for model comparison and selection in metamodeling. We have also proposed fast algorithms for construct stochastic kriging metamodels when incorporating stylized models, and analyzed their asymptotic properties, including their variances, biases and mean squared errors. Application of the proposed method in queueing networks especially in patient flow management has been examined to demonstrate its value. More generally, the use of stylized model enhanced stochastic kriging in simulation optimization problems such as ranking and selection has been investigated and it turns out to be a promising simulation metamodeling tool. Some of the above findings have been published in two papers, titled "Enhancing stochastic kriging for queueing simulation with stylized models" and "A simulation-based estimation method for bias reduction", both published in a premier journal IISE Transactions. Some other relevant results, especially on the use of metamodeling in ranking and selection problems, have been published in the 2017 Winter Simulation Conference, titled "Ranking and selection with covariates" and "A new framework of designing sequential ranking-and-selection procedures", respectively. Moreover, two working papers, currently under review with INFORMS Journal on Computing, and Naval Research Logistics, include part of the results.

11270116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11270116.value: The idea of combining stylized models and traditional simulation metamodeling techniques may be found relevant in the interdisciplinary research areas between operations research and machine learning. Although an in-depth investigation along this line of research is beyond the scope of this project, the PI and co-PI will pursue in these directions in the years to come.

11270116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11270116.value: In many applications in operations research and management science, stylized models that admit closed-form solutions have been useful in providing managerial insights. However, at the operational level, stylized models may not be sufficiently accurate to capture the behavior of complex systems of interest, and simulation models may be preferred. However, implementing large-scale simulation models can be time consuming and simulation metamodeling techniques have been developed to accelerate its implementation. In this project, we leverage the advantages of both stylized models and simulation metamodels and propose a stylized-model enhanced stochastic kriging method, which may serve as a viable tool in simulation metamodeling when stylized models are available. It has been applied to queueing models in hospital operations management.

11271716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11271716.value: 建築及其相關活動產生了大量的能源消耗和溫室氣體排放，綠色建築則被認為是針對此問題的最優解。截止目前，雖然政府已經大力推動綠色建築發展，但成效尚不顯著。其遲緩發展主要歸咎於私營企業將綠色理念轉化為實際行動的動力不足。這也反映出在 “生態”與“經濟”的持續對立中，私營企業普遍認為綠色建築的額外成本和風險會損害公司績效。在未能證實綠色設計是否能夠轉化為經濟利益的前提下，開發商鮮有意願採用綠色設計和技術，因此嚴重阻礙了綠色建築的發展。 本研究基於已獲得香港綠色建築（HK-BEAM Plus）認證的住宅建築數據，考察不同類別綠色建築的價格溢價和成本溢價，以此幫助開發商選擇最低成本支出下的綠色建築設計方案及技術。研究者將從香港綠色建築議會（HKGBC）的記錄中抽取至少136座住宅，同時對比附近相近樣本數的非綠色建築住宅，來測算綠色建築的價格溢價。我們還將從香港經濟財產研究中心（Economic Property Research Center）獲得以上兩組樣本的交易信息，同時使用地理信息系統技術（GIS）刻畫住宅的結構，區位和社區特徵。這些信息將幫助我們評估HK-BEAM Plus評分系統中六個分項（選址，材料，能源使用，水資源利用，室內環境質量和創新及其他）的成本收益比。為了評估綠色建築的成本溢價， 研究者將從HKGBC的數據庫以及建築諮詢公司（如工程造價企業等）的成本資料庫中收集住宅成本信息，同時通過研習會和訪談形式從建築環保評估協會（BEAM society Limited），HKGBC和業界獲取更多的成本信息。研究針對綠色建築特徵而產生的成本和價格溢價進行優化，幫助地產商找到最優成本收益比的綠色設計，以此改進他們的開發方案。最後，研究者將設計出基於網絡平台或手機應用的軟體程序，幫助開發商選擇成本收益比最高的綠色開發方案。 本課題的研究成果旨在激勵開發商對綠色建築的投資與開發，以此推動綠色建築在私營領域中的發展。本課題也將提供給政府一個針對綠色設計和技術的更加精確的補貼方案，來推動政府的綠色建築發展目標。

11271716.label: Realisation of objectives
11271716.value: This project aims to provide concrete evidence on how to turn “green” into “gold”. The results of this project have both practical implications for the developers and policy implications for the decision-makers. On the one hand, the developers will be encouraged to participate in green building development. On the other hand, the green design methods or technologies that developers may underestimate will be identified by the Hong Kong government, so that appropriate corrective intervention policies (e.g., incentives) could be developed to achieve their future green goals. To realize the research objectives, the relationship between the costs and benefits of green features was first established. We have adopted the classic hedonic model to test the “price premium for green” effects of HK-BEAM Plus certification buildings. Then, we have evaluated the “cost premium for green”. After that, we constructed a conceptual model to optimize the dual effects of “Price Premium for Green” and “Cost Premium for Green”. In the end, a software program “GiG platform” has been developed to provide developers with optimal solutions to achieve the most cost-effective credits. During the research period, all of the three objectives have been fully achieved. As follows: 1. To model the “price premium for green” and calculate the cost premium of each attribute category of HK-BEAM Plus certified green buildings In order to model the “price premium for green” and calculate the cost premium of each attribute category of HK-BEAM Plus certified green buildings, the PI completed the modelling of “price premium for green” effects of HK-BEAM Plus certification buildings. Some of them are highlighted below. The classic hedonic model is adopted in this study to test the “price premium for green” effect of HK-BEAM Plus certification empirically by comparing with all-else-equal non-green residential buildings in the newly built housing market. It has been concluded in the preliminary meta-analysis that buildings with green labels can enjoy significant price premiums. In this research, we target the decomposed “price premium for green” effects of green building certification, i.e. the different effects of the six categories in the HK-BEAM Plus rating system. The decomposed data from the two versions of the HK-BEAM Plus rating system can be treated equally due to the similarity of both versions. Thus, variables of the six categories are introduced into the standard hedonic model. 2. To optimize the dual effects of “price premium for green” and “cost premium for green” and provide effectively as well as tailored solutions for developers on the choice of green technology/design methods by considering the current market conditions Examining the interplay of “price premium for green” and “cost premium for green” could help solve the puzzle of green building strategies for real estate developers, and meanwhile provide policy or regulatory suggestions for the government and industrial institutes. Some of them are highlighted below.  Content analysis Firstly, relevant publications on the subject of cost premium for green buildings were identified. A preliminary computer search was carried out using suitable keywords (“cost premium”, “additional cost”, or “incremental cost” for cost premium, with “green building” or “sustainable building” for green buildings) in the title and abstract, to select relevant publications from various databases, such as ABI/Inform, ISI Web of Knowledge, EBSCO, Emerald, and Google Scholar. A list of relevant articles, including 9 survey reports and 41 empirical studies published between 2000 and 2015, was established through these rigorous processes. Secondly, the selected studies were coded using content analysis. Thirdly, a series of statistical analyses were conducted on the data in the Excel file.  Impact factors on cost premium evaluation The impact factors of the evaluation of cost premium, including estimation methods, project types, BEAM models, green levels, and time effects, were examined by clustering and comparison. The principle of the meta-analysis method was adopted to calculate the weighted mean effect size in specific clusters of impact factors. In comparing the results by the unpaired two-sample t-test with unequal variance, it was found that, in terms of estimation methods, ex-ante and ex-post approaches provide different, but not statistically significant, results. Office and school buildings, except the residential buildings, are confirmed to have a significantly positive cost premium, with only small differences between the three types of green buildings. The BEAM models have a significant impact on the evaluation of cost premium, with sound green standards, high market maturity, and experience accumulation resulting in the average cost premium for green buildings with LEED or BREEAM certification being significantly lower.  Implementing a Green Strategy Plan (GSP) in China Knowing that the additional costs of green technologies are the main barrier for their application in China, it is important to devise solutions that address these constraints. We propose setting up a Green Strategy Plan (GSP) that is most appropriate in context of China, aimed at the proactive application of green technologies by engaging most of the stakeholders in the process. The proposed GSP is divided into four steps. Step 1: Setting an overall energy & resources (E&R) saving aim and separate E&R saving objectives; Step 2: Institutionalizing the green technologies and practices; Step 3: Implementation of a work plan for green technologies; Step 4: Green promotion and experience sharing scheme. 3. To develop a “GiG” platform to provide developers with optimal solutions to achieve most cost effective credits The “GiG” Platform (http://www.gig2020.top) has been developed, which aims to turn “green” into “gold” based on two “wheals”, i.e. “price premium for green” and “cost premium for green.” The website includes four main functions: 1) Green building feature display: Uses could have a quick knowledge about characteristics of the existing green buildings in Hong Kong, including the name, address, transaction price, construction cost and various sustainable indicators. 2) Price premium estimation: Transactional information on the sample (green and general buildings of similar location, type, attributes, neighbourhood characteristics, etc.) was extracted from the EPRC database and analysed for cost-effectiveness across the five indicators of the HK-BEAM Plus rating system (including site, materials, energy, water and indoor environmental quality). 3) Cost premium estimation: The premiums were estimated through the cost database of HKGBC, interviews and workshops with BEAM Society Limited and senior industry professionals, etc. 4) Multi-objective optimisation: Based on the given green building rating levels, a multi-objective optimisation algorithm was proposed to determine the reasonable weighting of each sustainability indicator for green buildings. The user can input the relevant characteristics of the green building, and therefore, he/she can obtain the corresponding price premium and cost premium values in real time. Moreover, when the user chooses different green building rating levels (1-4 corresponding to Copper; Silver; Gold; Platinum respectively), the GiG platform will show the optimal result of the sustainable indicators. And in the future, the GiG platform will incorporate more green building indicators into the evaluation scope, increase the sample data, optimise model settings, improve the accuracy of green price and cost premium estimation, and provide more refined and rationalised decision-making recommendations.

11271716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11271716.value: The PI and team members provided a strategic framework of water-saving measures for different phases of a construction project. Through a combination of content analysis and quantitative comparison using relative significance indexing, ten main water-saving measures were identified, and three strategies were finally proposed according to the features of these measures. Overall, the comparison of green building water-saving standards in different GBRTs provides a framework for improving water-saving efficiency (Wu, Z., Wu, Z., Li, H., Zhang, X., & Jiang, M., 2020). In addition, the PI and team members investigated the value of going green in the hotel industry. Using a unique dataset comprising 156 green hotels and matched comparable non-green hotels in Beijing, the results indicate that the rate of complaints about the indoor environmental quality of green hotels is roughly 19% lower than that for nongreen hotels. (Zhang, L., Wu, J., Liu, H., & Zhang, X., 2020). Li, H., Zhang, X., et al. (2018) identified 22 social sustainability indicators of public mega-projects in the Chinese context from a comprehensive literature review and evaluated their relative importance from a multi stakeholder perspective. The results uncover six sets of social sustainability indicators: improved quality of daily life, appropriate macro policies, harmonious connections with the surroundings, unique local identity, effective public participation, and others. The research findings are expected to benefit both the government and the construction industry at large for better addressing social concerns when delivering public megaprojects in China. Hazarika, N., & Zhang, X. (2019a, 2019b) provided quantitative evidence for exploring the key determinants that impact firms towards sustainability transition through increased process eco-innovative practices in the peculiar city of Hong Kong. They focus on the relationship between regulatory instruments, managerial concern, and organizational measures to that of eco-innovative practices using a dataset of 140 firms from the Hong Kong construction industry. Despite a great deal of research into precast production scheduling published in academic journals worldwide, little attention has been given to environmental performance related to precast construction transportation and assembly scheduling problems. Thus, the PI and the team investigated the Just-in-Time strategy for supply chain management of precast construction while considering time-dependent transportation time and on-site assembly time. The method developed is of practical value for precast building projects to help in the successful implementation of sustainable development (Kong, L., Li, H., Luo, H., Ding, L., & Zhang, X., 2018)

11271716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11271716.value: In future, we will focus on the life-cycle evaluation of green buildings from more perspectives with multi-source and fine-grained data. For instance, in the Energy Internet and smart city environment, the energy and resource consumption data of green buildings (including electricity, water, gas and heat) can be measured and collected by various sensors installed in buildings. Then, using advanced big data analytics and deep learning methods, the dynamic integrated energy consumption behaviors of different buildings and different appliances in buildings can be modelled. Combined with the interaction with demand response programs and the energy consumption forecasting, the energy consumption level and pattern of green buildings can be evaluated more comprehensively and more accurate. Therefore, the evaluation results will be conductive to the energy efficiency improvement of smart buildings.

11271716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11271716.value: The building sector has always been seen as one of the major areas of energy consumption and carbon emissions worldwide. However, the emergence and application of green buildings bring a new light for this industry. This is because green buildings not only provide a comfortable environment for people living and working in cities but also reduce pollution and energy consumption through advanced design concepts, green products and technologies, so as to achieve a sustainable ecological balance. But there is always a gulf between reality and theory with the huge challenges derived from economy, technology and policy. Thereinto, price and cost are the factors that green building developers concerned most, as no strong evidence could show whether “green” can turn into “gold” ever before. By modelling the “price premium for green” effects of HK-BEAM Plus certification buildings and examining the interplay of “price premium for green” and “cost premium for green,” the project could help solve the puzzles. Moreover, a “GiG” platform has been developed, which could offer developers with optimal solutions to achieve the most cost-effective credits and meanwhile provide policy or regulatory suggestions for the government and industrial institutes in real time.

11272216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11272216.value: 監測與信息技術的高速發展為製造業產生了大量的數據，其中很多數據與產品質量相關。在過去，這些數據通常只是簡單的隨機變量類型數據。最近幾十年來，複雜的監測系統逐步開始獲取信息含量更為豐富的輪廓類型質量數據。該類型數據描述了若干應變量與解釋變量之間的函數關係。在統計過程控制領域，已有大量的研究開始關注此類數據。這些研究基本都基於單維度的輪廓數據，然而多維度的數據卻在實際生產過程中變得越來越常見。多維度數據中同時存在的自相關和互相關因素，以及其大規模高維度的特點，使得針對此類數據的建模和監控非常困難。相關研究和工具的缺乏使得與此類數據相關的應用難以開展，大量寶貴的數據沒有被利用。在本課題中，我們將針對此類型數據提出一個廣泛有效的基於多維度相關高斯過程的建模框架。我們認為多維度相關高斯過程是處理此類數據的理想工具，可以用來克服前述的各種困難。我們將研究此類模型的統計性質以及其在實際應用中會遇到的若干問題。最後，我們的方法將被應用到若干實際問題中以檢驗其有效性。

11272216.label: Realisation of objectives
11272216.value: In this project, three research objectives were proposed. The realization of them is described one-by-one next. This project is first proposed by Dr. Qiang Zhou and next transferred to Dr. Zijun Zhang due to Dr. Qiang Zhou’s movement to the University of Arizona. However, such change stimulates a very exciting collaborations that Dr. Qiang Zhou’s team focuses on the theoretical studies of the proposed research tasks while Dr. Zijun Zhang’s team targets on implementing and adapting studied methods into a number of real applications. Successes have been achieved in both of theoretical and applications sides in this project. Objective 1 - Develop an effective and efficient model for characterizing multivariate quality profile data The research group has been dedicated to investigate the theoretical foundation of methodologies for characterizing multivariate quality profile data. Compared with the existing methods focusing on problems of univariate profiles, research contents carried out in activities for objective 1 in this project made a significant contribution from the methodological side, presenting an initial progress of studying methods for dealing with multivariate quality profile data. In this project, we have proposed a Multivariate Gaussian Process (MGP) for modeling multivariate profile data. Next, with MGP, we have studied modeling the random effect that captures variations of profiles. Selection of the covariance structure of the MGP has also been theoretically studied. We have examined cons and pros of two classes of covariance function, separable and non-separable, and selected the latter one as separable covariance function is restricted by assumptions which limit its practical value. Different examples of non-separable covariance functions have been discussed and analyzed. Details have been presented in our article published in a top journal Technometrics [2]. To further address the computational burden of applying MGP in modeling multivariate profiles, a novel non-parametric model for multivariate profiles based on a Linear Mixed Effects (LME) modeling framework, with a flexible random part described by Gaussian Process (GP)-controlled B-splines, is studied in this project. The proposed method works in a more flexible and efficient way. Theoretical explorations are presented in our article published in another top journal IISE Transactions [12]. Objective 2 - Investigate statistical properties of the proposed model and its parameter estimates Based on modeling method reported in our Technometrics paper, research activities have been carried out to explore the statistical properties of the proposed model and discuss appropriate method for estimating model parameters. The most challenging task is to estimate a super high dimension of parameters induced by selected covariance functions, typically the matrix of cross-correlation factors, T. To address such challenge, a pairwise estimation mechanism was adopted and extended. Firstly, a hypersphere decomposition method is introduced to re-parameterize T. Two critical properties of the HD have been reported: 1) it is a one-to-one mapping between original and alternative parameter spaces; 2) it enables a sequential construction of T using parameters in another space, Ω. Based on property 1), mapping functions can be defined. Based on property 2), we show that T can be sequentially determined and converted to parameters in Ω. After the hypersphere decomposition, the pairwise composite likelihood of MGP model can be derived. As each pair of GPs in MGP constitutes a bivariate GP, the pairwise composite likelihood can be easily obtained. However, its parameter estimation does not reduce the problem dimension. To address such problem, a new likelihood has been introduced in our reported study. Such component also links the parameter dimension reduction in the third objective. Based on former problem settings, the statistical properties have been thoroughly analyzed. Details of mathematics and proofs please refer to [2]. Simulation studies are conducted to demonstrate the performance of the proposed modeling and model estimation methods. We also further validate the modeling effectiveness of selecting non-separable covariance functions by benchmarking with selecting separable covariance functions. More explanations are also offered in the published [2]. Similar investigation of statistical properties has also been conducted in [12]. Objective 3 - Investigate the following implementation aspects of the proposed model: (1) model efficiency; (2) reduction of parameter dimension; (3) optimizing measuring strategy We have applied a simplified version of the proposed model into a real application and published in a top quality journal, Journal of Quality Technology [1]. Direct studies of three aspects in Objective 3 in implementation of the proposed model have been made in studies [2] and [12]. 11272216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11272216.value: Research findings are reported from the methodological and application sides. From methodological side, major research findings and outcomes are described as follows: Finding 1 – A multivariate Gaussian process for modeling multivariate profile data is first reported in the quality and statistical process control field. This theoretical study is published in Technometrics in 2018. Please refer to our Technometrics paper in Section C. Finding 2 – A Linear Mixed Effects (LME) modeling framework, with a flexible random part described by Gaussian Process (GP)-controlled B-splines, is first reported for modeling multivariate profile data. Details of this theoretical study please refer to our IISE Transactions paper listed in Section C. From applications side, major research findings and outcomes are described as follows: Finding 3 – A simplified version of our studied model has been successfully applied to model and monitor real data from dependent categorical process. Details please refer to our Journal of Quality Technology paper listed in Section C. Finding 4 – The studied modeling principle has been extended with incorporating data-driven ideas to model high-dimensional data from the wind energy industry and monitor the health of wind turbine systems. Research outcomes please refer to our papers published in IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid, IET Renewable Power Generation, Renewable Energy as listed in Section C. Finding 5 – We have studied methods for modeling high-dimensional information from image data collected from wind turbines, railway systems, and semiconductor manufacturing. Modeling methods are integrated with monitoring strategies to realize the vision based monitoring of these systems. Research outcomes please refer to our papers published in IEEE-ASME Transactions on Mechatronics, Transportation Research Part C, and International Journal of Production Research as listed in Section C. Finding 6 – The multivariate Gaussian process for modeling high-dimensional data has been extended to study the forecasting of solar radiances, which is reported to our another IET Renewable Power Generation paper listed in Section C. Finding 7 – We have applied and extended data-driven methods for modeling the energy profile of commercial buildings, which is reported in our paper published in Sustainable Cities and Society as listed in Section C.

11272216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11272216.value: The advancement of sensing and information technologies has enabled collections of a large volume of data of high dimensional parameters from different systems and processes. Novel approaches for modeling such high dimensional data and describing a broader map of system health and process quality are awaiting for further researches. This project has well studies GP based and data-driven methods for modeling quality or system health information contained from multivariate profiles. In the future, we aim to extend existing methodological findings to study modeling high-dimensional data from multiple data sources in addition to the numerical data, such as images, videos, etc. Besides, we will study more advanced monitoring mechanisms to better investigate abnormality and negative signals contained in such data. Moreover, we will also study the predictive monitoring paradigm for considered high-dimensional data and multivariate profiles to realize better application values.

11272216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11272216.value: Due to the rapid development of sensing and information technologies, the manufacturing industry has become a data-rich environment. A large amount of quality related process data has become available. In the recent decades, sophisticated inspection and sensory systems have started to generate quality profiles describing the functional relationship between response variable(s) and explanatory variable(s). In the area of statistical process control (SPC), extensive research has been done on monitoring the variations of these profiles. However, most of these works focus on univariate profile data, while in fact multivariate quality profiles are becoming increasingly common. There are some significant difficulties in modeling and monitoring the multivariate quality profiles due to presence of both within-profile autocorrelation and interprofile dependency, as well as the large-scale and high-dimensional nature of such data. Lack of effective tools for handling multivariate quality profiles seriously hinders its application in SPC, leaving the rich process information unexploited. In this project, we have addressed this issue by developing a general and efficient modeling framework for multivariate quality profiles based on multivariate (correlated) Gaussian processes (MGP). We have also investigated some statistical properties of the proposed model. The developed methodologies have been applied into several real world applications.

11272516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11272516.value: While a primary challenge addressed by earlier wireless standards was handling channel fading, the current challenge for 5G standardization comes from ever-growing number of smartphone users. This issue has aroused considerable interest in the dense small-cell networks to accommodate more spatially reusable spectrum. Promising theoretical results have been shown improved network sum-rate is possible. However, despite its theoretical success, this system suffers from substantially increased inter-cell interference. Advanced multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antennas techniques show that it is, nonetheless, possible to cancel out the interference, if all small-cells cooperatively design precoders/combiners by sharing global channel state information (CSI). However, it was very quickly revealed that sharing global CSI becomes infeasible as the network complexity increases. Moreover, there are many practical challenges that have to be addressed before any of the promised gain could be harnessed. At the front of them are questions about efficient distributed precoder/combiner adaptation and reliable local CSI estimation in the presence of interference. The distributed precoder/combiner adaptation employs an iterative forward-backward (F-B) directional training, exploiting channel reciprocity. In each direction, the receiver adapts its filter to the local CSI, estimated using pilot signals. In particular, high quality precoder/combiner should be extracted before the channel coherence time expires. However, as the numbers of small-cells and users in the network grow, the amount of interference accumulates. Consequently, the required number of F-B iterations and the pilot overhead in each F-B iteration, should increase, which can potentially overwhelms the channel coherence resource. This significantly deteriorates the achievable sum-rate promised by the dense small-cell systems because of less time left for data communications. Our goal is to tackle the above issue by providing efficient distributed precoder/combiner adaptation techniques for the dense small-cell MIMO networks. The system is constrained to only allow a fixed number of F-B iterations, while still improving the quality of filters. The novelty of the project mainly lies in introducing low-overhead, but reliable techniques that perform fully distributed rank adaptation and provide robust CSI estimates. It also exploits past pilot signals received over many coherence blocks to reduce the estimation error and provides initial filter alignment strategies that further enhance the performance. The adoption of the devised technique to the practical small-cell network will result in an upgraded cellular coordination that greatly scales the network sum-rate. Such a framework could serve as a reference for developing advanced small-cell systems that could potentially be evolved into the 5G wireless standards. 早前的無線通信標準主要處理信道衰弱這壹核心問題， 5G 標準的最大挑戰來自於與日俱增的智能終端用戶的數量。這個問題引發了人們對於利用高密度小型蜂窩網絡結構以容納更多的空間可重復使用的頻譜相當大的興趣。令人高興地是，理論結果已經證明了網絡總的傳輸速率是可以被大大改善的。盡管理論上很成功，我們也不能忽視系統的各個子蜂窩之間存在著極大的幹擾。 如果這些小蜂窩結構之間通過分享全局信道狀態信息來協同設計預編碼器和組合器，結合上先進的多輸入多輸出 (MIMO) 天線技術，這是有可能消除掉蜂窩之間的幹擾。然而分享全局信道狀態信息在大規模復雜的蜂窩結構裏面是不太現實的。如果想要獲得理想中的增益，還有許多的實際問題需要被提前解決。急需解決壹個問題是如何在幹擾存在的情況下可靠地估計局部信道和有效地分布式地設計預編碼器/組合器。分布式預編碼/組合適應采用的是壹種通過利用信道之間的相互性反復的前向-反向 (F-B) 來訓練實現的。 在每壹個訓練方向上，接收機根據引導信號估計的局部信道信息來調整自己的濾波器。值得註意的是，要想設計出高質量的濾波器，整個設計過程應該在壹個信道相幹時間間隙之內完成。但是隨著蜂窩結構和終端數量的增長，幹擾不斷地累積，這樣導致了所需要的前向-反向 (F-B) 反復訓練次數和引導信號的開銷大幅增長，從而有可能使得信道相幹時間的資源不夠支撐所需要的訓練開銷。用更少的時間資源來傳輸數據對高密度小蜂窩結構理論可取得的傳輸速率造成嚴重損害。 這個項目的目標是為高密度小蜂窩（MIMO）網絡設計有效的分布式的預編碼/組合適應技術來解決上面指出的問題。這個系統的目的是改善濾波器的品質並且將F-B的反復限定為壹個固定的次數。這個項目的創新性主要在於介紹壹種低消耗並且可靠的，完全分布式秩自適應的技術，以及提供具有魯棒性的信道狀態信息估計技術。同時，利用在多個信道相幹時間間隔內接收到的引導信號來降低估計誤差並且提供初始化濾波器對齊的策略，系統性能可以得到進壹步的提升。當高密度小蜂窩網絡結構采用我們設計的技術來提升蜂窩結構之間的協調作用，整個系統的傳輸速率將成倍的增加。該框架可以作為開發有潛力發展成為5G無線標準的先進高密度小蜂窩網絡系統的參考。

11272516.label: Realisation of objectives
11272516.value: The realization of the three objectives are summarized as follows: (1) For the first objective, we investigate fast converging distributed precoder/combiner adaptation techniques in fast varying channel environments. The technique we deploy is different from the conventional filter design methods namely minimum mean square error, but rather a new strategy based on sparse source separation. In this strategy, we incorporate distributed power allocation to accelerate the convergence while enhancing the quality of filter design. We introduce another filter design method by minimizing the transmit power subject to target signal-to-noise ratio. This approach can enhance the power efficiency. The power efficiency improvement of the proposed scheme is verified by simulation. This project objective is fully achieved. (2) For the second objective, different power adaptation schemes are investigated to improve the system performance. In this part, we develop optimal and suboptimal power allocation schemes for various systems, namely, distributed antenna systems and relay networks. The goal of the development is to improve the efficiency of power allocation. For distributed antenna systems, the new power allocation schemes can enhance the system capacity. For the relay system, the power allocation can significantly lower the bit error rate. Furthermore, we also consider to adapt the power to enhance the energy efficiency that is the ratio of the achievable rate to the total power consumption for different systems. Efficient optimal and suboptimal power allocation schemes are developed. This project objective is fully achieved. (3) For the third objective, we exploit the sparsity of channel state information (CSI) to improve the system performance. In this part, we develop a new sequential subspace method for channel estimation with reduced training signals and computational complexities, while providing accurate subspace information for channel estimation. With the CSI, we can design precoders to improve the efficiency of total transmit power and capacity of systems with multiple antennas and non-orthogonal multiple access. This project objective is fully achieved.

11272516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11272516.value: The major findings and research outcomes are summarized as follows: (1) Power-efficient distributed coordination techniques for designing linear filters and combiners in dense small-cell multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks are studied. The new scheme provides improved power efficiency over the existing works, where the linear filters are optimized by minimizing the transmit power subject to an SINR. The works have been published in journal paper [1], and conference paper [1]. (2) A coordinated channel allocation is proposed to incorporate into biased cell association to alleviate the severe cross-tier interference between small cells and macrocells. The proposed schemes can substantially improve the spectral efficiency of heterogeneous networks. The works have been published in journal paper [2]. (3) Efficient power allocation is proposed for the relay network with spatial modulation over multiple-input multiple-output channels. The system coverage and spectrum efficiency are significantly enhanced. The works have been published in journal paper [3]. (4) Efficient power allocation is proposed for distributed antenna systems with OFDM over frequency selective channels. The new scheme can improve the system coverage and capacity with low computational complexity. The works have been published in journal paper [4]. (5) Efficient power allocation is proposed for maximizing the energy efficiency of distributed multiple-input single-output systems with OFDM over frequency selective channels. This scheme has almost the same performance as the optimal scheme but with much lower computational complexity. An improved power allocation is developed for distributed MIMO systems with beamforming. The works have been published in journal papers [5] and [10]. (6) Effective subspace method is developed for low-rank matrix reconstruction and decomposition. This subspace method facilitates the development of an efficient sequential channel estimation method with lower training data overhead and more accurate channel estimate. The works have been published in journal papers [6], [8], and [11]. (7) With available channel state information, optimal precoder and power allocation can be derived for multi-cell transmission with non-orthogonal multiple access. The system capacity and connections are greatly enhanced. The works have been published in journal papers [7] and [9].

11272516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11272516.value: In this project, we have developed an efficient channel estimation for sparse channels such as millimeter wave (mmWave) channels and various power allocation techniques for MIMO systems. The research outcomes can be applied to develop efficient mmWave transmission systems for 5G and beyond.

11272516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11272516.value: Small cells are overlaid by the macrocell sharing the same system bandwidth forming a two-tier network. They can provide services to weak coverage and small range communications of low power consumption. This approach is considered as a promising technique to increase the system capacity manyfold for the next generation of wireless communications. However, the bandwidth sharing and the densification of small cells cause co-tier and cross-tier interferences in the two-tier heterogeneous networks. Theoretical studies have shown that the sum rate of the system can be considerably increased. However, the increase of the spectrum efficiency will be limited by the inter-cell interference. This project is to develop power-efficient distributed coordination techniques for designing linear filters and combiners in dense small-cell multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks. The new scheme provides improved power efficiency over the existing works, where the linear filters are optimized by minimizing the transmit power subject to a signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio. The robustness of the power distribution scheme relies on the accuracy of the channel state information. An efficient subspace method for channel estimation is proposed, which has low training data overhead and accurate channel estimates. The estimation method is particularly useful for millimeter wave channels with low computational complexity.

11272916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11272916.value: Among many kinds of uncertainties that affect the design and construction of geotechnical infrastructures in sand, the incomplete understanding of particle breakage behavior and its effect on the macro-mechanical properties of sand constitutes a major source of uncertainty. This has caused engineering failures of driven piles and large-scale rock-fill dams in China and other countries around the world in the past few decades. Concerning the fundamentals of the breakage mechanics, particle morphology is well known to play an important role in the sand crushing behavior. To date, however, very little is known about the intrinsic relationship between particle breakage and particle morphology evolution, and their influences on the macroscopic properties of sands. In view of the above deficiency, we propose an advanced investigation into the sand particle morphology and its influence on the particle breakage behavior and the macroscopic shear strength of sands using a combined experimental, theoretical and numerical approach. Specifically, the experimental investigation involves the use of nanofocus X-ray computed tomography (CT) in the visualization and characterization of sand particle morphologies and their evolution during the triaxial loading process. Then the theoretical investigation employs the spherical harmonics analysis (SHA) for the reconstruction of real sand particle morphologies acquired from the CT study and implement it in the 3D discrete element method (DEM) modeling of real sands. Finally, the numerical investigation establishes a probability-based DEM modeling approach for the realistic simulation of particle breakage and fragmentation behaviors. This innovative research will unravel the intrinsic linkage between particle morphology and particle breakage, and their relationship to the macroscopic shear strength of sands under the triaxial shearing condition. A novel probability-based DEM simulation method which can incorporate both actual sand particle morphologies and realistic particle breakage behavior will also be created. This will expedite the uptake of DEM in the geotechnical industry. The outcome of this research will produce both scientific and engineering impacts. The former comes from an improved understanding of the fundamentals of micromorphology and micromechanics of crushable sands and its possible contribution to the research on other related breakable granular materials. The latter is mainly reflected in the enhanced ability of engineers to make improved design and construction of geotechnical systems in crushable soils. This is very relevant in Hong Kong where highly decomposed granite or volcanic soils exhibit distinct breakage characteristics. 颗粒形状对于砂土的力学行为有着至关重要的影响。颗粒尺度的几何形状交错作用影响了颗粒材料准静态变形过程中的运动学和动力学性质。颗粒破碎显著提高了该问题的复杂性，因为颗粒形态的演化本身就是一个令人费解的问题。尽管已经有许多致力于研究可破碎砂土的微观力学工作，但是人们对于颗粒破碎和颗粒形状的演化之间内在关系，以及其对砂土的宏观性质的影响的认知仍然有限。 鉴于上述不足，我们提出了一种结合试验、理论和数值方法来研究砂颗粒形状，以及它对颗粒破碎和砂的宏观剪切强度的影响。具体来说，试验采用纳米级X射线计算机断层扫描（CT）研究和描述三轴加载过程中砂颗粒形状和他们的演化。然后，理论研究采用了球面谐波分析（SHA）对CT中获得的真实砂颗粒的形态进行描述和重建，并将其导入三维DEM模型中。最后，数值研究将建立基于概率的DEM模拟方法，模拟真实的颗粒破碎过程。每种技术的优势将得到充分的发挥并结合起来，从而对微观形状和可破碎砂微观力学进行一种新型的、前沿的研究。 这种创新的研究将解开颗粒形态和颗粒破碎，以及它们与三轴剪切条件下砂的宏观抗剪强度关系之间的内在联系。一种可以结合实际砂颗粒形态和颗粒破碎行为的新型基于概率的DEM模型也将被创建。 这项研究的结果将同时产生科学和工程方面的影响。前者来自对微观形态和可破碎砂土的微观力学的基础认识，并对相关的易碎颗粒状材料做出贡献。后者主要体现在帮助提升工程师在可破碎土体中进行岩土结构的设计和施工。这项工作在广泛分布着具有明显破碎特征的高风化花岗岩和火山土的香港是非常相关的。

11272916.label: Realisation of objectives
11272916.value: Objective 1: To couple fundamental mechanics, statistical methods and experimental measurements using micro-CT to study the characteristics of particle breakage and fragmentation morphology. This objective has been fully achieved. In order to perform the in-situ micro-CT investigation of sands, a miniature triaxial apparatus was firstly developed. The apparatus allows for triaxial testing of a miniature dry sample with a size of 8 mm × 16 mm (diameter × height). The inter-particle contact evolution of two sheared granular materials, i.e., a spherical glass bead (GB) specimen and an angular Leighton Buzzard Sand (LBS) specimen, was investigated non-destructively using X-ray micro-tomography. Full-field X-ray CT images of the two specimens are obtained at different shearing stages. A series of image processing and analysis techniques in combination with a particle-tracking approach is developed to detect the inter-particle contacts and determine the contact gain, loss, and movement, during each shear increment. It is found that the average coordination number (CN) experiences a strong change in the pre-peak shearing stage, and tends to reach a steady value after the peak. The average CN of particles with different sizes follows the same trend as the overall average CN as the shear progresses. Meanwhile, a widely used mesh-based method is also applied to the sand to acquire the strain results based on its particle displacements. The accuracies of both methods are evaluated by comparing the calculated local volumetric strain results with those from a voxel-based calculation. Both strain calculation methods are found to provide results that capture the overall trend of strain localization throughout the shearing, which follows the same trend as the evolution of particle kinematics. However, the results from the two methods exhibit significantly different degrees of strain localization. In parallel with the triaxial testing, one-dimensional compression on natural quartz sands with in-situ X-ray tomography was also conducted. The assembly-scale and particle-scale images were used to characterise particle failure patterns, e.g., chipping, major splitting and comminution. Image processing and analysis enable us to determine the failure patterns around the yield stress, and the influence of initial density and particle morphology on the particle survival probability. Objective 2: To develop advanced methods for characterizing multiscale particle morphology. This objective has been fully achieved. Particle morphological features at different scale levels hold the key to understanding the geological origin and mechanical behaviors of natural sands. In this context, it is necessary to characterize and quantify morphological features by defining a series of reasonable descriptors. In this study, based on X-ray micro-computed tomography (μCT) images collected from a series of image processing techniques, we firstly introduced spherical harmonic (SH) analysis to reconstruct the 3D realistic surface of sand particles. We then extended 3D sphericity, roundness and fractal dimension to define the global form, local features and surface textures of the particle morphology. Based on the SH-reconstructed surface, a novel framework was mainly established to measure the descriptors of 3D sphericity, roundness and fractal dimension. The 3D fractal dimension in this paper was an original descriptor to characterize the self-similar nature of the surface textures of real sand particle morphology. By using the proposed framework, these morphological descriptors were measured for two types of natural sand particles. The successful application and the results proved the capacity of the framework for measuring morphological descriptors. The finding of the correlation between different descriptors revealed a strong relevance between morphological features at different scale levels. Intrinsic flaws are an important factor affecting particle strength and breakage behavior and are closely related to the macroscopic behavior of granular soils, e.g., packing characteristics, strength, deformation, localization and failure behaviors, etc. In this paper, a novel DEM modeling approach for investigating the role of flaws on the particle crushing behavior is proposed. The idea is to use the realistic fracture surfaces obtained from the experiment as a basis for generating initial flaws in DEM in a statistical way. Firstly, nano-focus X-ray computed tomography technology was used to obtain the realistic particle information including particle morphology and a set of fracture surfaces. The particle information was then stored in several arrays and imported into the DEM to construct the particle model containing a reasonable set of initial flaws. The discrete element method simulation of mini-triaxial tests were also performed on sands with realistically shaped grains. It compares the results with physical experiments at multiple length scales including the macroscopic sample length scale and the particle scale. A series of image processing techniques were utilized to binarize, segment and label the raw data in images obtained from the mini-triaxial test. The images were obtained using an X-ray synchrotron radiation scanner. A spherical harmonic analysis was used to filter the image data and to reconstruct the natural particle morphology. A one-to-one discrete element model, where every particle in the physical experiment has its own numerical twin, was constructed. The discrete element model was contained by a numerically generated flexible membrane allowing free deformation of the specimen under a prescribed confining stress like in a physical triaxial test. Objective 3: To develop a probabilistic DEM model for simulating sand crushing behavior and validate the model using micro-CT measurements. This objective has been fully achieved. A probability-based model is developed to estimate particle crushing and the associated grading evolution in granular soils during isotropic compression and pre-peak shearing in biaxial tests. The model is based on probability density functions (PDFs) of inter- and intra-particle stress (i.e., particle normalized maximum shear stress and particle average maximum shear stress) derived from discrete element method (DEM) simulations of biaxial tests. We find that the PDFs of normalized maximum shear stress are dependent on the current sample grading, implying coupling effects between particle crushing and sample grading such that the particle crushing is affected by the current sample grading, and the grading change is also dependent on the current particle crushing extent. To incorporate these coupling effects into the model, particle crushing and grading change are calculated for each load increment, in which the crushing probability of a particle during any loading increment is denoted as the corresponding increment of probability of the internal maximum shear stress exceeding its maximum shear strength. The model shows qualitative agreement with published experimental data. The effects of the model parameters, including initial porosity, particle strength, initial grading, and crushing mode, on the calculated results are discussed and compared with previous studies. Finally, the strengths and limitations of the model are discussed. The broad aim of this work is to present the development of a theoretical model for the quantification and prediction of particle crushing within a granular sample undergoing biaxial shearing. The model is developed based on statistical data derived from DEM simulations, in which the particle crushing probability is related to the PDFs of inter- and intra-particle stress (i.e., the maximum particle shear stress). Through statistical analysis of these particle-scale stresses, we find that the PDFs of the shear stress index (i.e., normalized maximum particle shear stress) depend on the current sample grading. This means that the change in grading during biaxial shearing caused by particle crushing affects the PDFs of the shear stress index, which in turn affect the subsequent particle crushing.

11272916.label: Major findings and research outcome
11272916.value: 1. A detailed micro-CT investigation on the Leighton Buzzard sand (LBS) and highly decomposed granite (HDG) under one-dimensional compression was performed (Zhao et al. 2020). 2. A systematic and comprehensive set of micro-CT investigations on LBS and GB under triaxial shearing lead to the following major findings: • A miniature triaxial apparatus which allows for triaxial testing of a miniature dry sample was firstly developed (Cheng et al., 2020). • The particle volume-based particle tracking and particle surface area-based particle tracking are shown to have equally effective tracking performance. The presented particle-tracking method minimizes the effects of the initially incorrectly tracked particles (i.e., the incorrectly tracked particles in the initial matching where particle displacement is not involved) on the final tracking results (Cheng and Wang, 2018a). • The inter-particle contact evolution, i.e., the contact gain, contact loss, and contact movement, during the shearing process is quantitatively investigated by combing the inter-particle contact detection and a particle-tracking approach (Cheng and Wang, 2018b). • A convenient grid-based method is developed and applied to the computation of the strain field of a natural sand based on the X-ray CT measurement of particle kinematics (i.e., particle translations and particle rotations) (Cheng and Wang, 2018c). 3. A systematic and comprehensive set of theoretical and numerical modelling investigations on particle morphology lead to the following major findings: • Based on μCT scanning of sand particles and their SH-reconstructed surfaces, a practical approach was proposed to calculate the 3D sphericity and roundness of particles. The most significant contribution of this study was the establishment of a novel approach to calculate the 3D fractal dimension of real sand particles (Zhou et al., 2017). • A novel particle tracking method based on the multiscale matching of the morphological features of sand particles was developed (Zhou et al., 2018). • Real sand particle morphologies are characterized and generated using SHA-based methods (Zhao et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2018a and 2018b; Yang et al., 2019). • A novel DEM modeling approach for investigating the role of flaws on the particle crushing behavior utilizing micro-CT data is proposed (Wu and Wang, 2020). • A high- fidelity modeling approach for sands called SHDEM, which involves one-to-one mapping of every sand particle in the physical experiment, has been established (Wu et al., 2020). • Innovative pattern recognition techniques for matching and tracking crushed sand particles were developed (Wu and Wang, 2018 and 2019; Wang and Wu, 2020).

11272916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11272916.value: Based on the outcomes of this research, a comprehensive investigation on the intrinsic linkage between particle morphology and particle breakage, and their relationship to the macroscopic mechanical behavior of sands undergoing complex stress-path loading conditions will be conducted in future. Advanced tools for accurate reconstruction, tracking and modeling of real sand particles will be invented and used to unravel the particle-scale origin of the macroscopic sand behavior. The tools will open a new door towards the accurate and efficient simulation of real granular materials in both fundamental and applied geomechanics research, and expedite the uptake of DEM in industry.

11272916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11272916.value: The fundamental research on the particle-scale mechanisms of the mechanical behavior of granular materials has significant scientific, economic and societal impacts around the world. In the geomechanics community, substantial efforts have been devoted to exploring the particle-scale origin into the macroscopic sand behavior over the past few decades. However, a clear and complete understanding of the subject, particularly of the complex effects of particle morphology and particle breakage on sand behavior, is still lacking. In view of such a deficiency, a high-end research has been conducted to accurately reconstruct, track and model sand particles within a sand specimen undergoing triaxial shearing using nano-focus X-ray computed tomography (CT). Specifically, advanced mathematical methods, pattern recognition techniques and probabilistic theories were employed to precisely quantify particle morphology based on CT data and then incorporate it into three-dimensional discrete element method (DEM) modeling of sands. This innovative research has unravelled the intrinsic linkage between particle morphology and particle breakage, and their relationship to the macroscopic shear strength of sands under the triaxial shearing condition.

11273116.label: Realisation of objectives
11273116.value: Objective 1: To investigate the disinfection efficacy of coupling different UV-LED wavebands and maximize the synergistic effect of the UR-UVGI system. We designed and built a bench-top set up to investigate the inactivation of airborne bacteria by UV-LEDs. Three UV-LED modules with distinct peak wavelengths were compared, including a UVA-LED module (peak wavelength: 369 nm), a UVB-LED module (peak wavelength: 288 nm), and a UVC-LED module (peak wavelength: 271 nm). To investigate the synergistic effect of combined UV wavelengths, six distinct LED modules were built: 369 nm UVA alone; 288 nm UVB alone; 271 nm UVC alone; 369/288 nm; 369/271 nm; and 288/271 nm. The UV irradiances were measured by a high-resolution fiber-optic spectrometer. The synergistic effect was studied under the equivalent fluence of different UV-LEDs. Five strains of bacteria with different cell sizes and shapes were selected, Serratia marcescens (ATCC 6911), Pseudomonas alcaligenes (ATCC 14909), Escherichia coli O59:H21 (ATCC 10536), Staphylococcus epidermidis (ATCC 12228), and Salmonella Typhimurium (Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica, ATCC 53648). For each of the five tested bacteria, five different UV exposure times, together with a control (no UV exposure), were used. Each experimental condition was performed at least in triplicate. A first-order disinfection model was applied to fit the log-linear relationship between inactivation and fluence. The possible synergistic effect of combined wavelengths on bacterial inactivation was determined by comparing the results of log inactivation by combined UV-LEDs and the summed results of log inactivation by individual UV-LEDs. The inactivation rate constants, k-values of the five bacterial strains under exposure to different UV wavelengths were calculated. It was observed that S. marcescens was the bacterial strain most sensitive to 369 nm irradiation, while E. coli was the most sensitive to both 288 nm and 271 nm irradiation. Meanwhile, S. Typhimurium was the least sensitive under all three tested UV wavelengths. The potential synergistic effect of the coupled 369/288, 369/271, and 288/271 nm UV-LED modules were investigated. For the UVA/UVB (369/288 nm) combination, no significant synergy was observed compared with the sum of the two respective UV LEDs operating alone for any of the five tested bacteria. However, a synergistic effect was observed for the application of the UVB/UVC (288/271 nm) combination to three bacterial species. The log inactivation of E. coli, S. epidermidis, and S. Typhimurium by the 288/271 nm combination was higher than the sum of 288 nm and 271 nm in the dose range of 0.7–6.7 mJ/cm2. Namely, under the same experimental setups, synergy was found for three of the five tested bacteria, while the other two merely displayed additive effects. Besides, the k-values confirmed the synergistic effect for the above three bacteria, as the k-values by the 288/271 nm UV-LED were the highest among all modules tested. Objective 2: To study the disinfection efficacy of the pulsed mode of UV-LEDs. Experiments on Pulsed UV-LEDs for E. coli and S. epidermidis were performed to compare the inactivation efficiency of pulsed and continuous UV irradiation. Individual 288 nm UVB, 271 nm UVC, and a coupled 288/271 nm module were tested. Additionally, for the pulsed configurations, the frequency was fixed to 100 Hz, and three different duty cycles (20%, 50%, 80%) of LEDs were investigated. All modules showed comparable inactivation effects in continuous and pulsed power modes under equivalent UV fluence. In terms of the disinfection efficacy, there was no significant difference between the pulsed and continuous irradiations of UV-LEDs. Objective 3: To optimize the disinfection efficacy for systems developed in (1) and (2). Based on the results obtained from Objectives 1 and 2, the pulse operation of UVB/UVC was applied for E. coli. Comparing to the continuous operation, pulsed operation of coupled UVB/UVC gave no significant enhanced disinfection. Objective 4: To investigate the enhancement of disinfection performance by rotating the irradiation zone. The disinfection efficacy will be measured and compared to the conventional design. A novel and compact upper-room ultraviolet germicidal irradiation system with light-emitting diode sources (UR-UVGI-LED) was developed for disinfecting airborne microorganisms in a full-scale chamber. The UR-UVGI-LED system consisted of 10 individual UVC-LEDs and arranged in the form of a well-packed rectangular array (5 by 2 matrix). Compared with the conventional stationary design, a rotating UV-LED system was developed to enhance the disinfection performance. The UR-UVGI-LED system was fitted to an electricity-driven rotating platform, which could rotate horizontally (left and right) at 180 degrees. The E. coli was selected as the testing microorganism. Four scenarios were tested; stationary LED under well mixed; stationary LED under poorly mixed; rotating LED under well mixed and rotating LED under poorly mixed. Three irradiation levels in the full-scale chamber were tested, with corresponding mean irradiances of 0.316 μW/cm2, 0.382 μW/cm2, and 0.517 μW/cm2, respectively. There was no significant difference in the decay rate on using the stationary and the rotating UR-UVGI-LED systems under a well-mixed condition. Nevertheless, it can be seen that the UR-UVGI-LED system can be approximately 73% more efficient than the stationary system under the poorly mixed ventilation condition. Objective 5: To utilize AFM to reveal detailed 3-D surface topography. E. Coli was selected to be a microorganism to be further revealed by AFM. The images of collected microorganisms before and after UV treatments were taken successfully. Comparing to the controlled sample (without UV exposure), there was no significant difference between those samples with exposure under UVC. It is plausibly since UVC causes the damage within the DNA, thus no obvious topological change was detected. Objective 6: To develop a computational numerical model for rotating UR-UVGI. A computational numerical model has been developed using the software FLUENT and the geometry was selected based on the experimental chamber. In the simulation process, the rotating UVGI fixture was modeled as moving computational regions, whereas the other computational regions were treated as non-moving regions. The motion of the rotating UVGI fixture was prescribed motion where the subsequent motion can be specified with time. The measured spatial UV fluence rate and bacteria concentration were compared with the for the rotating UVGI fixture. Good matching between the computational and experimental results are found.

11273116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11273116.value: Upon completion of this project, some salient findings were observed: The results of UV-LEDs with different wavelengths showed that UVA irradiation has very low disinfection efficacy, while UVB and UVC irradiations both show a higher disinfection efficacy for individual operations. The coupling disinfection effects of UVA, UVB, and UVC were examined. There was no synergistic effect for UVA/UVB (369/288 nm) combination, while UVB/UVC combination showed a synergistic disinfection effect. In this study, we also investigated the microbicidal effect of a novel rotating UR-UVGI-LED system on airborne bacteria. A novel rotating the UR-UVGI-LED system was developed, which sweeps through the entire room rather than the straight-ahead irradiation of the stationary mode of the UR-UVGI-LED system. The efficacy of rotating the UR-UVGI-LED system under the poorly mixed ventilation condition was 73% better than that of the stationary scenario. In short, it is logical to conclude from the results that the rotating UR-UVGI-LED system is a promising, more efficient approach to upper room UVGI technology for air disinfection. The system can be very useful not only for residential environments but also air conditioning environments.
