11276816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11276816.value: To handle the exponential growth of content dissemination, many emerging network architectures along the direction of Information-Centric Networking have been proposed. Among them, one common trend is in-network content caching, by storing data in advanced network devices such as cache-enabled routers. The resulting benefits, including redundant network-wide traffic elimination and reduced content access latency, are well appreciated. However, due to the potentially wide attacking surfaces, caching data content in the increasingly untrustworthy networked environment inevitably raises new concerns on user privacy exposure and unauthorized data access. Simply encrypting the data before distribution is unsatisfying, as it would diminish the benefits of in-network caching by preventing network devices from accessing the data they need to inspect for their job. Existing encrypted protocols, such as HTTPS, either do not fully leverage in-network caching, or require decrypting the traffic in the middle, which violates the end-to-end security. To address these limitations, we propose to design a new networked system for secure and efficient content dissemination through encrypted in-network caching. For guaranteed confidentiality, we plan to encrypt all data content before distribution and keep them encrypted when cached in the network. To achieve the benefits of caching, we will further enable the network to securely identify and locate the cached encrypted data without revealing the plaintext requests or underlying content. Specifically, we plan to 1) design a compact, high-performance, yet encrypted content fingerprint index, which aims to provide the network with fully-controlled search capability over encrypted in-network cache, and 2) thoroughly explore its in-network deployment for building full-fledged network-assisted content dissemination. To move one-step further towards practice, we will consider the effective support of content dissemination from multiple providers to authorised users, and study how to efficiently enable authorised search across encrypted in-network content from multiple providers under their own different keys. To broaden the applications of our architecture, we plan to support advanced content-aware data dissemination scenarios by incorporating the content similarity detection into our encrypted in-network cache system. Our goal is to securely and effectively handle the generation/transmission of large amount of redundant data. The proposed research will greatly contribute to the roadmap of emerging Internet architectures and secure network function outsourcing. It provides guaranteed confidentiality against attackers with full access to in-network devices. The results can be easily adopted by content-intensive applications, including cloud social media, generic video/image distributions, and others. 為了應對網絡中呈指數級增長的數據內容傳播需求，許多圍繞著信息中心網絡的新興架構設計應孕而生 。這些設計的一個共同特點是網絡設備上的內容緩存，即將數據內容緩存在新興的帶存儲功能的網絡設備上，比如啟用高速緩存的路由器存儲數據。由此帶來的好處已被業界廣泛認可，包括消除冗餘的全網流量和減少數據內容的訪問延遲 。然而，緩存數據於網絡中也不可避免的帶來安全隱患。與日俱增的網絡威脅和潛在攻擊使得網絡中的安全環境令人擔憂。在這種環境下緩存數據內容，不可避免地產生新的用戶隱私洩漏或未經授權的數據訪問等潛在問題。在傳輸之前對數據進行加密是不能完全解決問題的。因為現有的設計中，網絡設備無法對加密後的數據內容進行處理和搜索的。因此，將加密數據緩存在網絡中的好處也就蕩然無存。現有的加密協議，例如HTTPS，要么沒有充分利用網絡緩存，要么需要中間設備的解密再加密。而後者並不能保證 HTTPS定義的傳統的端對端數據的傳輸安全。 為了解決這些限制，我們提出一系列全新的支持加密數據緩存的安全設計，並進而給出支持高效加密數據內容傳播的安全網絡架構。為了保密性，所有數據內容在傳輸之前均會在終端進行加密。在其通過的網絡設備的傳輸和緩存過程中，這些數據始終保持在加密狀態下。為了實現緩存的功效，我們將研究如何使得網絡，在不洩露明文內容的前提下，能夠安全地識別並找到緩存加密的數據。具體來說，我們計劃1）設計一個空間利用率高的，高性能的，針對加密數據內容的指紋索引。其目的是為網絡設備提供一種完全可控的，搜索加密數據緩存的能力； 2）深入探討如何將該設計部署在網絡設備中，來節省加密的冗餘數據傳輸，從而達到通過網絡緩存輔助提速數據傳輸的效果。更進一步，我們考慮加密緩存對多內容供應商的支持。緩存中的數據可能包括不同的內容供應商的密鑰加密的密文。如何有效支持用戶授權，並在盡量不需要頻繁交互的情況下，去跨域搜索網絡中來自多個供應商的加密數據內容？為了廣泛的應用場景，我們還計劃將內容相似性檢測引入到網絡加密緩存系統裡，以支持基於內容感知的數據優先傳播方案。我們的目標是安全有效地處理大量冗餘數據生成或發送的應用場景。我們的研究將極大地促進新興互聯網架構和安全的網絡功能外包。即便攻擊者對網絡設備具有完全訪問權限，我們的研究也能保證數據內容的保密性。這些結果也可在如下內容密集型應用場景所採用，比如雲社交媒體，一般的視頻/圖像的分佈等等。

11276816.label: Realisation of objectives
11276816.value: The mid-term progress has been reported before, with publications at IEEE-TIFS-2017, IEEE-Access-2016, IEEE-IWQoS-2017, IEEE-PAC-2017, etc. Below, we briefly conclude major achievements of the project objectives. #### Realisations of objective 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 ##### Towards Encrypted In-Network Storage Services with Secure Near-Duplicate Detection In-network storage is recognized as a vital component of many emerging network architectures, which facilitates high-quality and efficient content-centric services. In this trend, providing content-based near-duplicate detection (NDD) services among in-network storage becomes naturally necessary for network traffic alleviation and resource optimization. However, due to the increasing attacking surfaces, storing data in the networked environment inevitably raises new concerns about user privacy exposure and unauthorized data access. Therefore, we have designed a secure NDD service in the context of encrypted in-network storage. For efficiency, we first leverage the fingerprint techniques and locality-sensitive hashing to convert the problem of NDD into the keyword search. We then adopt an efficient multi-key searchable encryption scheme, which requires only one encrypted query from the user even when the data are from multiple content providers encrypted with different keys. As simply combining the above methods does not directly locate accurate results, we then devise a secure result refining scheme via Yao's garbled circuits to avoid user-side post-processing. Furthermore, we enhance our design to address the potential malicious behavior of in-network servers. Extensive evaluations of real world image dataset demonstrate that our design can achieve comparable accuracy to the plaintext with modest security overhead. These new findings are published in IEEE-TSC-2018(Part-C-8-[7]). #### Realisations of objective 1, 2 and 4 ##### Secure Content Redistribution in Encrypted Cloud Media Center The wide adoption of cloud greatly facilitates the sharing of explosively generated media content today, yet deprives content providers’ direct control over the outsourced media content. Thus, it is pivotal to build an encrypted cloud media center where only authorized access is allowed. Enforcing access control alone, however, cannot fully protect content providers’ interests, as authorized users may later become traitors that illegally redistribute media content to the public. Such realistic threat should have been seriously treated yet is largely overlooked in the literature. In this paper, we initiate the first study on secure media sharing with fair traitor tracing in the encrypted cloud media center, through a new marriage of proxy re-encryption (for secure media sharing) and fair watermarking (for fair traitor tracing). Our key insight is to fully leverage the homomorphic properties residing in proxy re-encryption to embrace operations in fair watermarking. Two protocols are proposed for different application scenarios. We also provide complexity analysis for performance, showing that our work can also be treated as secure outsourcing of fair watermarking, and thus kills two birds with one stone. We thoroughly analyze the security strengths and conduct extensive experiments to validate the effectiveness of our design. These new findings are published in IEEE-TDSC-2018(Part-C-8-[6]). ##### EncKV: An Encrypted Key-value Store with Rich Queries Distributed key-value stores have been widely adopted due to their superior performance. However, existing systems do not guarantee to provide strong protection of data confidentiality, and as a result fall short of addressing serious privacy concerns raised from massive data breaches. In this paper, we introduce EncKV, an encrypted key value store with secure rich query support. First, EncKV stores encrypted data records with multiple secondary attributes in the form of encrypted key-value pairs. Second, it leverages the latest practical primitives for searching over encrypted data, i.e., searchable symmetric encryption and order-revealing encryption, and provides encrypted indexes with guaranteed security to support exact-match and range match queries via secondary attributes of data records. Third, it carefully integrates these indexes into a distributed index framework to facilitate secure query processing in parallel. To mitigate recent inference attacks on encrypted database systems, EncKV protects the order information during range queries, and presents an interactive batch query mechanism to further hide the associations across data values on different attributes. For practical considerations, EncKV also enables secure system scaling in a minimally intrusive way. We implement an EncKV prototype on a Redis cluster, and conduct an extensive set of performance evaluations on the Amazon EC2 public cloud platform. Our results show that EncKV effectively preserves the efficiency and scalability of plaintext distributed key-value stores. These new findings are published in ACM-ASIACCS-2017(Part-C-9-[3]) and IEEE-TPDS-2019 (Part-C-8-[9]). ##### Privacy-Preserving Similarity Joins over Encrypted Data To support rich queries, we especially investigate privacy-preserving similarity join queries, i.e., a pivotal primitive of similarity search that finds pairwise similar data points across two data sets. We start from locality-sensitive hashing and searchable symmetric encryption, but the immediate combination of two techniques discloses the distribution of the query set. To enhance the security and scalability, we propose the frequency hiding query scheme, and design the result sharing query scheme, respectively. Rigorous security analysis and extensive experiments indicate the advance of the proposed query schemes. These new findings are published in IEEE-TIFS-2017 (Part-C-8-[5]). #### Realisations of objective 1, 4 and 5 ##### Secure Deduplication Techniques on Cloud Middleware and Enclave Applications Data deduplication is a vital component of current cloud storage systems for optimized space utilization, and we explore it in two popular real-world scenarios. First, in cloud storage systems, we observe that users cannot fairly enjoy the benefits of server-side deduplication. We thus design and implement a middleware system, namely UWare. It brings storage and bandwidth savings back to users, while preserving user data privacy. UWare starts from the message-locked encryption for efficient deduplication over encrypted data, and initiates the endeavor in leveraging the similarity characteristics of block-level deduplication to balance the effectiveness of secure deduplication and system efficiency. Also, UWare patches a practically feasible side-channel threat. Extensive experiments show that UWare greatly reduces storage and bandwidth cost. Second, for enclave applications, we consider that redundant computations occur commonly when handling the same input data. Therefore, we propose SPEED, a secure and generic computation deduplication system in the context of resource-limited Intel SGX. It allows SGX-enabled applications to identify redundant computations and reuse computation results, while protecting the confidentiality and integrity of code, inputs, and results. Extensive evaluations on an implemented prototype demonstrate the high performance of SPEED. These new findings are reported at IEEE-DSC-2018(Part-C-9-[4]) and IEEE-ICDCS-2019(Part-C-9-[5]). #### Realisations of objective 2 and 5 ##### Towards Trustworthy and Private Keyword Search in Encrypted Decentralized Storage Inspired by the emerging decentralized storage services atop the blockchain, such as Storj and Filecoin, we investigate searchable encryption techniques in the decentralized setting. However, it is hard to ensure the service integrity, since decentralized storage commonly faces severe threats from both clients and service peers. Service peers may return partial or incorrect results, while clients may intentionally slander the service peers to avoid payments. Hence, we utilize the smart contract to record the logs of encrypted search on the blockchain, and devise a fair protocol to handle disputes and issue fair payments. Using a dynamic-efficient searchable encryption scheme as an instantiation, we craft a concrete scheme that preserves encrypted search capability and enforces ecosystem healthiness, so that service peers are incentivized to make real efforts and jointly guarantee service reliability. We present a formal security analysis for the proposed architecture. We also implement our scheme in Python and Solidity, and test its search performance and transaction costs on Ethereum. These new findings are published in IEEE-ICC-2017(Part-C-9-[6]) and IEEE-TDSC-2018(Part-C-8-[8]).

11276816.label: Major findings and research outcome
11276816.value: The project has the follow major findings and research outcome. - Developed new methods of secure near-duplicate detection in the context of encrypted in-network storage. The proposed methods enable locating encrypted near-duplicates for authorized users from data repositories owned by multiple content providers. It also guides designing secure data duplication methods in the scenarios of encrypted cloud storage systems and enclave applications. The results were reported at IEEE-TSC-2018(Part-C-8-[7]), IEEE-DSC-2018(Part-C-9-[4]), IEEE-ICDCS-2019(Part-C-9-[5]) and IEEE-TMM-2017(Part-C-8-[3]). - Developed new methods of secure authorized media sharing in the encrypted cloud data center. The designs allow secure sharing of the outsourced media content to authorized users, and enable fairly tracing illegal content redistribution. About the fair tracing, it specifically studies two secure designs to cater for different application scenarios, which is beneficial to secure content dissemination in this project. The results were published in IEEE-TDSC-2018(Part-C-8-[6]). - Developed an encrypted and distributed key value store method with secure rich query support. The proposed method customizes the practical cryptographic primitives into the latest encrypted local index framework, which supports different types of queries over distributed encrypted data records with guaranteed security and linear scalability, laying foundations for encrypted in-network caching. The results were published in ACM-ASIACCS-2017(Part-C-9-[3]) and IEEE-TPDS-2019(Part-C-8-[9]). - Developed new methods of encrypted similarity search service in distributed settings. Similarity search techniques are widely adopted to handle massive and complex data records in the real world. However, how to achieve efficient and scalable similarity search over distributed, encrypted and complex data records is a challenging task. Our designs focus on this task and a specific case design which were published in ACM-IWQoS-2017(Part-C-9-[2]), IEEE-TIFS-2017(Part-C-8-[5]) and IEEE-TIFS-2017(Part-C-8-[4]). These similarity search methods are beneficial to support advanced content-aware data dissemination scenarios in this project. - Developed new methods of encrypted content dissemination with focus on targeted mobile coupon delivery dissemination. We study the privacy issues on model targeting, and propose our methods to securely deliver targeted coupons to eligible users whose behavioral profiles accurately satisfy the vendor's targeting profile. The findings were published in IEEE-ACCESS-2016(Part-C-8-[2]) and JCIN-2016(Part-C-8-[1]). - Developed new methods of trustworthy and private search service across encrypted decentralized storage with multiple providers. Our designs ensure the high quality of user experience with search result trustworthiness as well as service fairness, in the decentralized multiple-provider service model. Besides, we make efforts to improve the service robustness as the network grows. These results are published in IEEE-ICC-2017(Part-C-9-[6]), IEEE-PAC-2017(Part-C-9-[1]) and IEEE-TDSC-2018(Part-C-8-[8]).

11276816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11276816.value: There are quite a number of future directions that are worth pursuing. Below we list the two major ones. - Exploring the possibility of utilising trusted enclave, like Intel SGX or other equivalent, for the purpose of encrypted in-network caching. Compared to traditional cryptographic techniques, trusted enclave has the advantage of protecting data in-use with near native performance. The only extra requirement is the trust of hardware manufacturers. We believe that the potential of shifting to trusted enclave based approach might outweigh its extra trust requirement, and worth further exploration to achieve best possible designs. - Another direction is to explore the possibility of transforming the layer of encrypted in-network caching into a fully decentralised storage platform, with built-in support of data confidentiality, searchability, and more. Establishing such a platform has many potential benefits: 1) the first decentralised storage platform that respects data ownership with encryption and related key management; 2) establishing end-to-end data sharing and access control with technical enforcement, eliminating today's concern of untrusted third-party service providers; 3) laying foundations for end-to-end secure web applications.

11276816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11276816.value: As the in-network content caching becomes a common trend for data content caching, there is a growing challenge to protect the privacy of caching data and control data access, while preserving the functionality of in-network caching. To address the challenges, the research in this project designs a new networked system for secure and efficient content dissemination and access through encrypted in-network caching. The proposed designs protect data via at-rest encryption and support efficient encrypted data caching in the network. In addition, the proposed research enables authorized content-aware data dissemination and search from multiple providers for practicality. Specifically, two services are developed: 1) secure data duplication and dissemination services, where authorized data are efficiently disseminated and network bandwidth cost is greatly reduced, without leaking the underlying data content. 2) encrypted cache in-network identification and localization services, where users can efficiently search encrypted data records with the high quality of user experience, without exposing the plaintext requests. The research can find wide content-intensive applications, such as cloud social media, generic video or image distributions. It serves solid stepping-stones for further research along the direction of secure network function outsourcing.

11277116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11277116.value: The 5th generation mobile networks will support multi-gigabit data transmission to meet the huge growth of mobile data traffic for personal entertainment, investment, education, surveillance, and so on. All the existing mobile communication networks up to the 4th generation are operated at lower microwave frequency bands which are highly congested. As much wider bandwidth is required, the unlicensed 60 GHz band is very likely to be used in future mobile phones, tablets or personal computer for short-range high data rate transmission. In fact, some leading integrated-circuit manufacturers have developed 60 GHz chipsets to support the growth of this new technology. Atmospheric absorption is very strong at the 60 GHz millimeter-wave band. High power millimeter wave solid-state sources could be used to compensate the serious path loss, but they are costly and not durable. Alternatively, medium or high gain millimeter wave antenna arrays with beam steering capability are considered as a viable solution of the problem. Many 60 GHz planar antenna arrays with good directional property were developed recently. These antenna arrays are good in performance, in general, but their radiation beam cannot be steered electronically. There are two common approaches to develop steerable high-gain antenna arrays. The first approach is to incorporate a phase shifter to each antenna element for adjusting the phase differences between antenna elements electronically. Since 60 GHz phase shifter is expensive and has high insertion loss, this approach is not attractive for consumer product development. The second approach is to cascade a beam-forming network to the antenna array. For a network with N input and N output ports, N radiating beams, pointing to different directions over a range of angles, can be generated. Beam steering can be realized by adding switches to control the on/off states of the independent beams. This is an attractive approach for the 60 GHz band as low loss beam-forming networks can be implemented by substrate-integrated-waveguide technology and switches are not expensive compared with phase shifters. Recently, the principal investigator has developed a low-cost high-performance millimeter-wave electric dipole element which can be integrated easily with planar beam-forming networks. With this exciting result, a research on the development of multi-beam millimeter-wave antenna arrays of the newly proposed antenna element is highly desirable.

11277116.label: Realisation of objectives
11277116.value: The aim of this project is to develop end-fire millimeter-wave antenna arrays based on open-ended SIW-fed electric dipoles. All the objectives have been realized successfully. The project has also extended to the design of new wideband antenna arrays with coaxial-line feed. Based on the magneto-electric dipole concept, all the designed antenna arrays are not only wide in bandwidth, but all excellent in other electric characteristics. The details are as follows. Design guideline for the new SIW-fed wideband magneto-electric dipole has been obtained after a detailed parametric study. Detailed arrangement of the shorting vias in three layered structure for achieving excellent performance is obtained. One-dimensional multi-beam array of the proposed new magneto-electric dipole antenna element has been investigated. Different feed networks have been considered to achieve good scanning performance. Prototypes have been built for experimental verification. Two-dimensional multi-beam linearly-polarized antenna array with horizontal polarization has been designed. Again, it is designed with excellent wideband performance using the magneto-electric dipole technology. Technique for achieving wide scanned angles has been investigated. One-dimensional dual-polarized multi-beam antenna arrays have been developed. Antenna arrays with different feed networks including SIW and integrated coaxial line have been investigated. The designed structures can be used for developing two-dimensional dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole arrays.

11277116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11277116.value: With the assistance of several research students, the development of end-fire magneto-electric dipole antennas and arrays has been carried out smoothly. Several novel design structures and feeding techniques were demonstrated with excellent performance. After detailed parametric studies [1], design guidelines for the new SIW-fed end-fire magneto-electric dipole with vertical polarization have been obtained. For antenna array designs, different kinds of feed networks were considered. It is found that Butler matrix is more suitable to achieve wider bandwidth performance. Butler matrix is also easier to be realized in compact form. One-dimensional and two-dimensional end-fire magneto-electric dipole arrays with horizontal polarization have also been successfully developed with excellent performance [2]. This success enables us to combine the two designs to realize a one-dimensional dual-polarized end-fire magneto-electric dipole arrays with 18% bandwidth, 45 dB port isolation, and 82% radiation efficiency [3] A single-layer one-dimensional dual-polarized end-fire antenna array with 28.6% bandwidth and 18 dB port isolation was also developed [4]. Due to its thin profile structure, the array is suitable for compact mobile devices and can be used to realize two-dimensional arrays at low costs. In addition to use SIW as transmission line, asymmetrical substrate-integrated coaxial lines are employed as feed lines which can provide wider bandwidth. An ultra-wideband long-slot-excited phased array with end-fire vertically polarized radiation has been designed successfully with operating bandwidth of 3:1 with scan angle of up to 48 degree in the H-plane [5]. A wideband vertically-polarized end-fire magneto-electric dipole antenna fed by the coaxial line has also developed for multi-beam operation with wide bandwidth [6].

The proposed antenna arrays can also be modified with reconfigurable capability by incorporating switches. The work has high potential for further development.

11277516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11277516.value: Tissue engineering aims at using cell-based therapy to rebuild missing or damaged tissue. Many physiological functions, such as heart contraction, requires tissue alignment with specific left-right (LR) asymmetry. Recent evidences indicated that LR asymmetry should be originated from single cell’s LR biased motion, e.g. rotation or migration. However, how to guide LR asymmetry from single cells to tissue formation in a predictive manner is still a major challenge. If it is uncontrolled, such intrinsic cell behavior may lead to disorganized patterns and eventually malfunction the tissue construct. In this proposal, we aim at exploring an engineering strategy to guide the LR asymmetry in a type of tissue formation, skeletal muscle myogenesis. Recently we found that micropatterned substrate with decreased stiffness could reverse the LR polarity of cells located at the micropatterned interface. Importantly, based on our previous findings, the LR polarity may propagate from cells at the interface to cells remote from the interface, eventually leading to a coherent LR biased cell-cell alignment throughout the entire multicellular structure. Taking together, it suggests that micropatterned substrate with varying stiffness may be an approach, for the first time, to guide the LR asymmetry not only in single cells but also the associated tissue formation. To explore this possibility, we will hierarchically investigate how substrate stiffness can mediate the LR bias from 1) single cell’s torque to 2) its corresponding cell-cell alignment for 3) applications of guiding LR development in skeletal muscle myogenesis. First, we will apply the nanowire magnetoscope, our newly developed platform, to measure cellular torque representing single cell’s LR bias in response to substrate stiffness. Second, we will investigate how substrate stiffness can influence the propagation of LR bias using time-lapse nucleus rotation that automatically measures the long axis of stained nucleus in live cells to reveal the dynamics of cell-cell alignment. At last, we will apply the knowledge gained to a model of tissue formation, skeletal muscle myogenesis. Using C2C12 myoblasts, we will explore whether the changed substrate stiffness would switch the LR orientation of differentiated myotube, eventually controlling the LR direction of muscle orientation and contraction. Together, this integrated analysis on substrate stiffness will provide a valuable understanding of how LR asymmetry is formed from single cell to multicellular structure, opening up a new direction for controlling LR asymmetry in tissue formation in the future. 組織重建乃基於以細胞為本的治療方案，從而實現再造受創或損失的組織。很多的生理功能，例如心臟收縮，需要組織排列成特定的左右不對稱結構。近期研究發現此左右不對稱源自於單細胞具偏向性的動向，例如旋轉或遷徙。然而，如何在可預期的範疇中引導單細胞構成組織形貌的左右不對稱仍為主要挑戰。如果失控，此自發性的細胞行為可能導致紊亂的圖案生成，最終造成組織機能失常。在此計畫，我們致力於探索工程手段以引導骨骼肌組織的左右不對稱。近期我們發現，當細胞貼附於軟性材料上的微圖案邊界時，細胞會反轉其內建的左右極性。更重要的是，此左右極性可自位於邊界的細胞傳遞到遠方細胞，最終造成整體多細胞結構一致性的左右偏向排列。由此可見，微圖案結合不同基材硬度或可提供一種有效方案來指引單細胞以至組織的左右不對稱的生成。為了探索此可能性，我們將多層面地研究基材硬度如何協調（一）單細胞扭矩與（二）相對應之細胞排列於（三）骨骼肌組織形成之左右不對稱。首先，我們將採用本團隊近期研發之納米磁矩顯微鏡量測單細胞在不同基材硬度下的扭矩。接著，我們將用延時顯微鏡以自動量測細胞核長軸於活細胞中的轉動，進而揭示基材硬度如何影響左右不對稱於細胞排列的動態蔓延。最後，我們將利用獲取的知識應用於骨骼肌組織形成。基於 C2C12成肌细胞，我們將探索基材硬度是否可轉換分化後細胞的左右指向，進而控制肌肉組織的方向性與收縮性。總和來說，此針對基材硬度的整合性分析將提供對左右不對稱於單細胞至多細胞結構形成的深入了解，並對控制組織形貌發展的左右不對稱建立新方向。

11277516.label: Realisation of objectives
11277516.value: The objective 1 was proposed based on our previously developed nanowire magnetoscope that uses internalized ferromagnetic nanowires for measuring the chiral bias of cell rotation. Using this platform, we have found cellular torque with chiral bias depending on cell types. However, such measurement is limited because only very few cells can internalize nanowire internalization, which makes the characterization difficult and inconsistent. To overcome this, we have developed a new strategy by measuring the chiral bias of nucleus rotation and chiral pattern of actin filament. While nanowire is not used, such assay enables great number of cells for statistical analysis. Based on it, we found a direct evidence of different chiral bias of single cells on substrate with different stiffness. Such finding has been published in a peer-reviewed journal (Zhu, Ninghao, Kwong, Hoi Kwan, Bao, Yuanye & Chen, Ting-Hsuan* (8 Jun 2017). Chiral Orientation of Skeletal Muscle Cells Requires Rigid Substratee. Micromachines. 8/6. 181). In addition, same technique has been applied to other studies that shows a change of chiral bias upon lineage-specific induction. Specifically, cultured on circular micropatterns, hMSCs exhibited an anticlockwise (ACW) -biased nucleus rotation and swirling pattern of actin filaments. Interestingly, with adipogenic induction, the chiral bias was reversed to clockwise (CW) -biased, and such reversed chirality was consistently expressed in terminally differentiated adipocytes. This part has been published in an international journal (Bao, Yuanye, Wu, Siying, Chu, Lok Ting, Kwong, Hoi Kwan, Haranto, Hogi, Huang, Yaozhun, Lam, Miu Ling, Lam, Raymond H. W. & Chen, Ting-Hsuan* (4 Aug 2020). Early Committed Clockwise Cell Chirality Up-Regulates Adipogenic Differentiation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells. Advanced Biosystemss. in press doi:doi.org/10.1002/adbi.202000161) and the first author, Yuanye Bao, graduated in Jan 2019 with a PhD degree. In addition, using this technique, we have found that prior culture condition with high/low density can create remnant effects on cell chirality after reseeding. For cells cultured in circular micropatterns on rigid substrate, clear actin stress fibers can be observed. However, these filaments were dissembled on soft substrate, suggesting that actin is involved in the dependence of chirality on substrate stiffness. Such dissembled actin can be observed in cells after a series of low-density cultures which disorganize the formation of actin rings. To further explore this possibility, two actin inhibitors, Cytochalasin D that destroys actin microfilaments by inhibiting actin polymerization and Y27632 that inhibits Rho-associated kinase (ROCK), were used to treat the C2C12 cells. Here, by using high-density culture supplemented with inhibitors of actin polymerization, the effect of low-density cultures was recaptured, suggesting that the series of subcultures with high/low density may be an in vitro aging process that modifies the actin cytoskeleton, causing a remnant attenuation of cell chirality even after trypsin digestion and reseeding. Such finding has been published in a peer-reviewed journal (Kwong, Hoi Kwan, Huang, Yaozhun, Lam, Miu Ling & Chen, Ting-Hsuan* (4 Jun 2019). Remnant Effects of Culture Density on Cell Chirality After Reseeding. ACS Biomaterials Science & Engineering. 5. 3944 - 3953. doi:10.1021/acsbiomaterials.8b01364). We have achieved 85% for this objective 1. For objective 2, we have applied micropatterned stripes on different substrate to investigate the propagation of LR bias in cell-cell alignment. By comparing the cell orientation on rigid and soft substrate, we demonstrate that rigid substrate is required for the exhibition of LR-biased orientation of skeletal muscle cells. Using alternating micropatterned stripes of cell-adherent and cell-repellent regions on rigid substrate, we found that C2C12 skeletal muscle myoblasts oriented with significant LR bias. Importantly, such bias was reduced when cultured on soft substrates. In addition, through treatment of actin inhibitors, we demonstrated that actin stress fibers play a key role in the formation of LR asymmetry. Together, our finding of how LR asymmetry was affected by substrate stiffness offers a new approach for regulating the LR-biased orientation of skeletal muscle tissue. Importantly, to automate the analysis of cell orientation, we have carried out a new image analysis tool to investigate the cell chiral orientation. The analysis of chiral orientation has been difficult for cultures with high cell density because the region of nucleus overlaps. In this work, we demonstrate an image processing technique named “outline-etching method” that can segment densely-packed cell clusters into individual cells without affecting the cell orientation. Applying to a culture of C2C12 myoblasts, we found that chiral orientation was enhanced on glass substrate, which is consistently observed with increased intercellular alignment and independent of cell-cell distance or cell density, suggesting a role of intercellular alignment in such chiral orientation. Such finding has been published in a peer-reviewed journal (Huang, Yaozhun, Bao, Yuanye, Kwong, Hoi Kwan, Chen, Ting-Hsuan* & Lam, Miu Ling* (26 Jun 2018). Outline‐etching image segmentation reveals enhanced cell chirality through intercellular alignment. Biotechnology and Bioengineering. 115. 2595 - 2603. doi:10.1002/bit.26783). Like the chiral rotation of nucleus, the density of prior culture is also affecting the cell chiral orientation. After re-seeding on micropatterned stripes, we found that the cells with prior exposure to low-density culture exhibited a chiral cell orientation on glass substrate but not on PDMS substrate. In contrast, high-density culture enables cells to express stronger chiral orientation regardless the use of substrate material. More importantly, such change is associated with chiral rotation of single cells and the formation of actin ring, which were enhanced in cells from high-density culture. Our result suggests that culture density serve as a “dose” that results in a remnant effects on the cell chirality even after trypsin digestion and reseeding, suggesting a possible way to reconstitute the chiral morphology on different substrates. Such finding has been published in a peer-reviewed journal (Kwong, Hoi Kwan, Huang, Yaozhun, Lam, Miu Ling & Chen, Ting-Hsuan* (4 Jun 2019). Remnant Effects of Culture Density on Cell Chirality After Reseeding. ACS Biomaterials Science & Engineering. 5. 3944 - 3953. doi:10.1021/acsbiomaterials.8b01364). Together, we have achieved 100% for this objective 2. For object 3, we have applied our findings to construction of skeletal muscle tissue. Using micropatterned stripes with various widths as a platform for culturing C2C12 myoblasts, the LR asymmetry of cell orientation was investigated during myogenic induction to investigate the relationship between LR bias and myogenic differentiation. We found that cells on stripes with width of 50 μm and 80 μm showed a significant negative bias. During the subsequent myogenic differentiation, the bias was slightly reduced but still remained during myotube formation. In contrast, cells on 500 and 800 μm stripes had little bias before induction, but the LR bias emerged on day 8, suggesting that longer time is required for the appearance of LR bias on such wider stripes. This finding reveals that different widths of micropatterned stripes influence the formation of LR bias of C2C12 cells, and LR asymmetry could be inherited and carried forward to the subsequent myogenic differentiation, paving ways for reconstructing the muscle tissue in the future. Such finding has been published in a peer-reviewed international conference (Hin Sum Man, Siying Wu, Tiffany Ng, Fu Kin Ho, and Ting Hsuan Chen*, Reconstitution of Inherent Left-Right Asymmetry in Skeletal Myogenesis, The 12th IEEE International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine and Engineering, IEEE NANOMED 2018, Honolulu, USA, Dec 2018). We are working on collection of additional results for journal publication. We have achieved 80% for this objective 3.

11277516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11277516.value: The primary significance of this work is three-folds. First, the application of micro and nanotechnology provides a new standard for characterizing cell chirality. Assessment of cell chirality can be LR-biased cell polarity, orientation, morphology, and migration, which is nonstandard and sometimes controversial. Here, our results showed significant and consistent difference of cell chirality on different substrate. In addition, through treatment of actin inhibitors, we demonstrated that actin stress fibers play a key role in the formation of LR asymmetry. Together, our finding of how LR asymmetry was affected by substrate stiffness offers a new approach for regulating the LR-biased orientation of skeletal muscle tissue. Second, we have developed the “outline-etching method” as a new approach for image segmentation in analyzing the developmental dynamics of cell alignment. With the ability of extracting cell orientation from densely-packed cell clusters, our method allows the generation of massive information with improved accuracy and applicability, which is highly desired for obtaining statistical significance in different studies. Based on this technique, we discovered an improved intercellular alignment on glass substrate with broad range of cell-cell distance, suggesting an origin of the enhanced chirality on such substrate and make it independent of cell density. Based on the enriched information, our image analysis suggests a potential mechanism elucidating the development of LR asymmetry. Third, we found remnant effects of culture density on cell chirality. Recently, a profound experiment demonstrated that, with appropriate stiffness, muscle stem cells showed self-renewal in culture, and pertained its regenerative properties after being transplantation. Consistently, our result implies that culture density of the past environments can also be “memorized”, allowing a long term influence in cell’s chiral behavior. Our results clearly indicate the importance of culture condition for maintaining consistent cells behaviors. While low-density culture has been suggested to maintain cell phenotype since it avoids the contact inhibition and prevent cell differentiation, our results indicate the low-density culture may, on the other hand, attenuate the chiral behavior of cells, suggesting culture density as the key of how to reproduce and guide the chiral mechanics in an engineering context.

11277516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11277516.value: Engineering skeletal muscle sheet has drawn increasing attention because of its immense potential for repairing impaired muscle or building bionic machines. Spatial patterning cues have been widely used to align muscle precursors to facilitate their fusion and differentiation. Comparing to nano-topographic cues, micropatterning offers advantages in reproducing intricate patterns and greater length and alignment of myotubes. However, on micropattern, cells orient with a unidirectional slanting angle deviating from the pattern boundary. When uncontrolled, it can disorganize muscle fibers, creating significant difficulty when engineering skeletal muscle tissue. In this project, we found that the slanting angle of cell orientation is indeed due to an intrinsic chirality of cells. Here, combining our expertise in cell chirality and pattern formation, we would develop engineering skeletal muscle sheet with scalable, intricate and more importantly, controlled patterns of myotubes. We will design the orientation of micropatterned stripe with a “compensation angle” relative to the desired myotube direction. Finally, we can guide the formation of functional skeletal myotubes into desired, intricate, and function patterns by either compensating or suppressing the chiral orientation. We have applied for GRF 2020/21 and is recently approved (11215521). With the grant support, we will continue our exploration in 2021 -2023.

11277516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11277516.value: Do cells have chirality, or left-right asymmetry? If yes, how to measure and use it? It is a fundamental question in basic science. In recent years, researchers observe that cells can orient and migrate with left-right bias, or chiral bias, and such bias can later cause formation of tissue architecture with left-right asymmetry. As such, it is important to understand how cell chirality emerges and how it interacts with the microenvironment. However, observation of cell chirality is not easily accessible. Here, to tackle this question, we develop a series of microscopic techniques that can automatically extract the chiral rotation and orientation of cells. By characterizing such chirality of muscle cells, we found that cell chirality is dependent on substrate stiffness. However, such dependence is a remnant effect of culture density which reorganize the cytoskeleton. Finally, we have applied our understanding of cell chirality to reconstitution of skeletal muscle tissue. At the end, we expect to deliver a method for guiding the formation of functional skeletal myotubes into desired, intricate, and function patterns for tissue repair or bionic machines.

11278116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11278116.value: Smart materials which provide rapid responses to mechanical and magnetic stimuli hold the promise for future generations of sensors and actuators. Ferromagnetic shape memory alloys (FSMA), which exhibit such responses can transform a wide spectrum of transducer technologies in diversified fields such as aerospace, automotive, underwater navigation, biomedical, surveillance and consumer electronics. For many of these applications, it is desired that the FSMA components are able to respond to fast dynamic cycling under combined application of magnetic fields and stress. In order to design FSMAs outstanding cyclic responses and longer durability, it is necessary to comprehend, at the microscopic level, the magnetostructural phenomena in these materials at faster timescales (1 ms to 1 s), for which there is a large knowledge gap at the present. Under a current GRF, we have developed and demonstrated in-situ X-ray and neutron scattering techniques to determine the fundamental mechanisms for magnetoelastic coupling in FSMAs, which include twin-boundary motion and the rotation of magnetic moments under applied load or magnetic field. Here, we will improve on these techniques in order to probe in the dynamical regime of the magnetostructural responses in FSMAs in the ms-to-s timescales. Specifically, we propose to study the dynamic behavior of FSMAs with neutron and synchrotron X-ray scattering measurements under the following conditions: (a) combined magnetic field and cyclic mechanical stress, (b) pulsed magnetic field over ms timescales. The proposed study will extend our insights into the dynamic nature of the magnetostructural responsess, which will further shed light on the strong magnetoelastic coupling in FSMAs, thereby providing guidance for designing new materials for dynamic sensor and actuator applications. 对机械和磁等外场刺激具有快速响应的智能材料有望应用于下一代传感器和驱动器的制作。具有这种快速响应的铁磁形状记忆合金(FSMAs)能够被制作成一系列不同的传感器应用于各个领域。如可用于航空，汽车，水下导航，生物医学，监控和民用电子等领域。对于许多应用而言，都需要在磁场和应力共同作用下对FSMAs部件进行快速动态循环加载。为了设计出具有重复循环响应和更长寿命的FSMAs，需要在更快的时间尺度上来对这些材料的微观磁-结构现象进行理解。然而，目前人们对FSMAs的微观磁-结构的认识在1ms ~1 s尺度上尚存在较大断层。 此前，我们发展了原位X射线和中子散射技术，用于研究FSMAs中磁-弹耦合的基本物理机制。 分别确定了静态磁场和应力共同作用下孪晶界迁移和磁矩旋转过程。本课题中，我们将采用上述技术在ms-s的时间尺度上对FSMAs微观磁-结构现象进行研究，进一步扩展我们对其动态学本质的理解。我们将开发出可用于中子和X射线散射的原位实验设备来对该类材料的动态行为进行研究。原位实验主要在下面两种加载条件下开展：(a)在磁场下进行循环机械应力加载；(b)超过ms时间尺度的脉冲磁场加载。本研究将进一步拓展我们对微观磁-结构现象动态学本质的理解，而这正是FSMAs中强磁-弹耦合的起源。相关成果将为应用于动态传感器和驱动器的新材料的设计开发提供重要的指导。

11278116.label: Realisation of objectives
11278116.value: This project aims to probe the magnetostructural responses in ferromagnetic shape memory alloys in the ms-to-s timescales. Specifically, we proposed to study the dynamic behavior of FSMAs with neutron and synchrotron X-ray scattering measurements under the following conditions: (a) combined magnetic field and cyclic mechanical stress, (b) pulsed magnetic field over ms timescales. The proposed study will extend our insights into the dynamic nature of the magnetostructural responses, which will further shed light on the strong magnetoelastic coupling in FSMAs, thereby providing guidance for designing new materials for dynamic sensor and actuator applications. The Covid-19 pandemic, particularly the associated travel restrictions, has impacted neutron scattering experiments in the late stage of the project. In spite of these challenges, the project has met nearly all of its objectives. A key to the proposed experiments is a custom-built compact load frame that can be inserted into the magnet in a neutron beamline, allowing simultaneous application of stress and magnetic field. The load-frame was designed and built in collaboration with Dr. Yubin Ke, an instrument scientist at China Spallation Neutron Source, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Dongguan. Fig. 1 shows a photo of the load-frame labelled with scattering geometry and the magnetic field direction for proposed experiments. An invention disclosure has been filed. With this load-frame, a series of neutron scattering experiments were carried out at neutron scattering facilities world-wide. In each case, the compact load-frame was brought to the facilities and integrated into the data acquisition system of the neutron beamline. The load-frame was first tested at Australia Center for Neutron Scattering, using the WOMBAT beamline with polarized neutrons. This was an extremely challenging experiment, aiming to investigate the response of a ferromagnetic shape memory alloy under a combined mechanical load and magnetic field. With the use of polarized neutrons, the change in microstructure (twin growth) and magnetic moments could be determined simultaneously, which allows us to probe the coupling between the structure and magnetic moments. The experiment worked well, and a manuscript has been submitted for publication. Later, the load-frame was brought to Research Neutron Source Heinz Maier-Leibnitz (Forschungsreaktor München II), Germany, using the single crystal diffractometer POLI. After fine tuning, the load-frame worked more efficiently which led to high-quality results. In particular, the competition between magnetic field and applied stress was uncovered. Under a 1.0 T saturating magnetic field, twin reorientation could be activated by compressive stress and this was accompanied by a realignment of the magnetic moment, which followed the easy axis of the twin variant. On the other hand, compressive stress as small as 1.0 MPa could freeze the twin reorientation. The main results have been published in Applied Physics Letters. Building upon the success of these experiments, measurements under cyclic compressive stress have been planned. However, the pandemic limited travelling and the oversea neutron scattering facilities were closed to users. Alternate plans were made to use the China Spallation Neutron Source in Dongguan. Here, we proposed to adapt the magnetic reflectometer for single crystal measurements. The plan has been approved and beamtime secured. However, changes have been made to the beamline in order to accommodate the new experiment. The experiment will be carried out in the later part of 2021. For objective 2, measurements of the magnetic response under a pulsed magnetic field was performed using the SEQUOIA beamline at the Spallation Neutron Source in Oak Ridge National Laboratory, USA. The relaxation of the magnetic moments and twin boundary motion can both be affected by their interactions with microscopic defect centers such as random magnetic dipoles, ferromagnetic domain walls, dislocations and disconnections. The pulsed magnetic field at SEQUOIA can reach 30-40 Tesla over 4 ms, so it is ideally suited for the proposed experiment. Fig. 2 shows evolution of the (020) diffraction peak which is a signature of twin boundary rotation. However, no intensity change was observed within the expected time frame (to 1120 micro seconds before the next magnetic pulse comes in). The measurements were repeated at low temperature of 225 K, where a large ordered moment was expected, but the results were the same. On the other hand, within different regimes of the magnetic pulse, the intensity of (020) diffraction peak did show a change, which seemed to result from a change in magnetic field strength. These data are still being digested and analyzed. For the purpose of education and training, the project supported two postdocs over different period of times. • Dr. Yubing Ke, Postdoctoral Fellow • Dr. Honghui Wu, Postdoctoral Fellow They have travelled multiple times to neutron scattering facilities in Australia, Germany, and all have received ample training and experience on the use of neutron and synchrotron scattering techniques. Dr. Ke is now an instrument scientist at China Spallation Neutron Source. In addition, to support the proposed scattering experiments, real-space phase field simulation was performed to investigate the microstructure evolution and macro-response of a ferromagnetic shape memory alloy under stimuli of magnetic fields with different frequency and coupled magnetic-mechanical loading. The model development and example calculation results have been reported in J. Phys. D.

11278116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11278116.value: Polarized neutrons were used to unravel magneto-structural coupling of Ni2MnGa alloy under the application of stress and magnetic field. The measurements were performed using a single crystal diffractometer POLI at Heinz Maier-Leibnitz Zentrum (MLZ) in Germany. It was found that under a 1.0 T saturating magnetic field, twin reorientation could be activated by a compressive stress and this was accompanied by a realignment of the magnetic moment, which followed the easy axis of the twin variant. On the other hand, compressive stress as small as 1.0 MPa could freeze the twin reorientation. The evolution of the magnetic scattering amplitudes suggested that the change in magnetization was mainly achieved through the magnetic domain wall motion, while the twin boundary motion was blocked. The results have been reported in publication #2. A separate experiment conducted at Australia Center for Neutron Scattering confirmed the above-mentioned results. Furthermore, it was found that in addition to the ferromagnetic switching associated with twin reorientation, the magnitude of the ordered moment strongly depended on the lattice deformation. These experimental results demonstrated that stresses as small as a few MPa could effectively tune the magnetization vector in a ferromagnetic shape memory alloys in multiple steps, which then could be potentially used for sensing and nonvolatile information storage. The results have been submitted for publication. The above experiments were performed with a custom-built compact load frame, which could be inserted in to a electromagnet in a neutron beamline. An invention disclosure has been filed for the load-frame. The relaxation of magnetic moments under a pulsed magnetic field was studied using the SEQUOIA beamline at the Spallation Neutron Source, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, USA. The experimental results are somewhat unexpected and are still under analysis. Finally, the microstructure evolution and macro-response of a ferromagnetic shape memory alloy under stimuli of magnetic fields with different frequency and coupled magnetic-mechanical loading were investigated via a real-space phase field simulation. It was found that the coercive field was reduced with the increasing magnetic frequency. A concomitant domain wall motion and magnetization rotation were captured as well. Moreover, the simulation results demonstrated that, under the coupled magnetic-mechanical loading, the coercive field of the magnetic hysteresis loop could be reduced by applying a compressive strain perpendicular to the magnetic field direction. The results have been reported in publication #3.

11278116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11278116.value: The compact load-frame developed in this project is a enabler for new kinds of experiments, under combined stress and magnetic field, which will prove to be a valuable tool for the study of magneto-elastic coupling in ferromagnetic shape memory alloys. A follow-up study is planned at the China Spallation Neutron Source, i.e., with cyclic loading. The magnetic reflectometer at China Spallation Neutron Source will be modified to accommodate the new measurements involving single crystal samples. Beamtime has been secured, and the experiment will be carried out in the later part of 2021. The phase-field model established under this project will be further developed to study in detail effects of combined load and magnetic field, and to examine dynamics response of the material. This model will be useful in the design of future ferromagnetic shape memory alloys.

11278116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11278116.value: Ferromagnetic shape memory alloys exhibit fast responses to mechanical and magnetic stimuli and are considered for a wide spectrum of transducer technologies in diversified fields such as aerospace, automotive, underwater navigation, biomedical, surveillance and consumer electronics. The physical mechanism underlining the shape memory effect is the coupling between the magnetic moments and crystal lattice orientation. The former can be controlled by a magnetic field, whereas the latter by a mechanical load. In this project, we developed a compact load-frame which can be inserted into a magnet. This device allows us then to examine the competition between mechanical load and magnetic field. Moreover, with polarized neutrons, the change in microstructure and magnetic moments can be determined simultaneously. Experiments were carried out at world-leading neutron scattering facilities indicate that the applied stress plays a dominate role in the competition between mechanical load and magnetic field. Further experiments under cyclic loading condition will reveal the competition at fast time scales. In addition, a phase-field model was developed to simulate the response under combined mechanical load and magnetic field. The modelling results will help interpret the neutron diffraction data and aid the design of new smart materials

11278316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11278316.value: 基于非易失FPGA的高效物联网关键技术研究

11278316.label: Project Objectives
11278316.value: Understanding the impact of NVMs on FPGA design and synthesis steps. We will analyze the memory operations, i.e., read or write, in each step of FPGA synthesis flow and explore the desirable memory behaviors of NVM. Exploring the design space of NVMs in non-volatile FPGA systems. Considering different read/write patterns of various components in FPGA system, we will evaluate various decisions, such as selection of single level cells and multiple level cells, heavy/light write modes, to figure out the best memory settings for each FPGA component. Minimizing NVM write operations during the synthesis flow for non-volatile FPGAs. We will revisit system-level, logic level, and placing and routing level optimizations to achieve this goal. Balancing write operations across physical regions during FPGA synthesis. Due to the inherent variation in write patterns on different components of FPGA, write operations are significantly imbalanced. It may result in the endurance problem for non-volatile FPGA which needs frequent reconfigurations. We will also study the write balance issue during FPGA synthesis. Reducing reconfiguration cost of non-volatile FPGA. Reconfiguration mainly relates NVM writes. However, it is not effective to only considering bit-level flips like what have been done in NVM oriented research. In this project, we will investigate the similarities between consecutive configurations to reduce the cost. Performance estimation of hardware and software for System-on-Chip (SoC) implementations. In order to develop efficient system-level design consisting of both hardware and software based implementation, accurate performance estimation will be constructed. Efficient task partitioning and mapping for SoC system implementation. Tasks will be categorized based on the preferred implementation approach (FPGA or software), based on which a system-level design can be derived.

11278316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11278316.value: In order to keep its leading roles as the world’s financial center, it is essential for Hong Kong to utilize modern technologies to build a smarter city. FPGA, with excellent scalability and flexibility to customize in both hardware and software, is a promising technology for various smart city and Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, as the technology node scales under 20 nm, traditional SRAM-based volatile FPGAs are facing severe challenges such as high leakage power and process variations. To address this problem, non-volatile memory can be alternatively adopted in FPGAs as Look Up Tables (LUT) and other memory components to achieve high scalability, small form factor, and low power consumption. When NVMs are employed in FPGA, existing techniques need to be renovated due to the following reasons. First, traditional FPGA synthesize and reconfiguration techniques were optimized for SRAM-based memory components. Therefore, they did not take into consideration the inherently NVM characteristics such as read/write asymmetry. Thus the FPGA synthesize and reconfiguration procedures need to be redesigned to efficiently utilize NVM. Second, none of existing NVM optimizations are FPGA-specific. Thus, these techniques should be further improved by considering FPGA working patterns in NVM-based FPGAs. Third, different from SRAM, NVMs have the capability of storing more than one bit in a cell, which is known as Multiple Level Cell (MLC). While it certainly increases storage density and reduces FPGA size, it also complicates the design and configuration of NVM based FPGA. Thus, techniques to efficiently adopt MLC NVM in FPGA need to be developed. This project aims to fill these gaps and develop a long-lasting, fast-adaptive, reliable, and energy-efficient platform for future self-adaptive systems. Design issues will be studied with various optimization goals including write operation efficiency and endurance of NV-FPGA memory, reconfiguration cost reduction, access modeling of NV-FPGA, read optimizations through retention time aware mode selection, as well as system-level hardware/software co-design. With the proposed tasks, an efficient NV-FPGA platform as well as NVM characteristics aware FPGA synthesis/reconfiguration techniques will be developed. The success of this project will enable a new class of efficient non-volatile FPGA based embedded systems that can be utilized to build a smarter city for Hong Kong, with which we can provide better environmental monitoring, traffic management, smart buildings, and enhanced public safety. All of these will in turn help Hong Kong to maintain and advance its role as one of the world’s leading financial center. 作为世界金融中心，香港亟需利用先进的科学技术打造智慧城市建设。FPGA具有集成度和灵活性的优势，成为智慧城市中物联网应用的关键技术。然而随着生产工艺降到20nm以下，传统基于SRAM的FPGA在静态功耗和生产差异性方面面临着巨大挑战。为了弥补这些不足，研究者们提出使用非易失存储替代SRAM应用于FPGA中查找表和其他部分的存储单元，以达到高集成度、微小生产工艺和低功耗的目的。 非易失存储在FPGA中的应用将给现在的FPGA设计技术带来革新性的改变。这是因为：首先，传统的FPGA综合和重构技术是为SRAM设计和优化的，并没有集成非易失存储的特性，比如读写非对称性，因此FPGA的设计流程需要重新设计来有效地使用非易失存储；其次，现有的非易失存储优化技术都不是面向FPGA的，因此若将它们应用到非易失FPGA中还需要考虑FPGA的工作模式；再次，与SRAM不同，非易失存储可以以多级存储单元的方式用一个物理位存储多个比特。虽然这种使用方式增大了FPGA的集成度，减小了面积，但同时增加了非易失FPGA系统的设计和重构过程的复杂性。因此我们需要研究在非易失FPGA中，如何有效地使用多级存储层次的非易失存储。 该项目旨在填补这些空白，从而为将来的自适应系统建立持久、快速、稳定、高能效的平台。该项目将涵盖包括写操作效率、非易失FPGA的寿命、重构代价优化、非易失FPGA的访问模型、读操作模式选择和系统级软硬件协同设计在内的优化技术，搭建具有非易失存储特性认知能力的FPGA综合和重构技术。 该项目将引领香港未来智慧城市中基于非易失FPGA的新一代嵌入式系统，从而完善香港的环境监测、交通管理、智能建筑、公共安全等领域的建设，维持香港世界金融中心的领先地位。

11278616.label: Realisation of objectives
11278616.value: The objectives of this projected have been well realized in this study. We conducted a systematic study of neuronal chemo-sensation to a large-scale variety of molecular gradient proﬁles and revealed an enormous complexity of neuronal chemotaxis, especially in response to the steepness variation of different chemotactic cues. This study was made feasible by an innovative design of a microﬂuidic device that is capable of generating large-scale molecular gradients with different levels of steepness in a microarray format, providing a high-throughput solution for investigating the dependence of neuronal chemotaxis on steep-ness of molecular gradient. In addition, the device utilizes arrays of hydrogel cylinders as the basic assay units, rendering a 3D ex vivo model to recapitulate the in vivo neuronal growth pattern. Design of the microﬂuidic device: As its technical innovation, the microﬂuidic device relies on a simple diffusion process to establish molecular gradients in a well-designed 3D space. As outlined in the proposal, the device was ~1 cm in width and ~3 cm in length, and was based on a suspended array of Matrigel cylinders, each of which was measured as 200 µm in diameter and 250 µm in height, and was spaced by 200 µm from the neighboring ones. Each device was composed of three layers: a SOURCE layer, a suspended STENCIL layer (250 µm thick), and a DRAIN layer. The inlet of the bottom SOURCE layer was used to introduce guidance molecules (e.g., netrin-1, NGF and Sema3A). The height of the SOURCE layer was sufﬁciently small (~400 µm) to ensure that the molecules spread in this layer just by diffusion to establish a horizontal gradient in the X–Y plane, providing a gradually decreasing input concentration for each Matrigel cylinder within the suspended STENCIL layer. By further diffu-sion in the vertical direction, various gradients along the Z-axis were established within each of the hydrogel cylinders. Because of the large volume of culture medium in the DRAIN layer, the concentration at the top of each cylinder was approximately the same as the background level, which effectively resulted in descending gradient steepness in the hydrogel cylinders when their positions moved away from inlet of the SOURCE layer. When primary hippocampal neurons were cultured in the hydrogel cylinders by directly seeding them in the DRAIN layer, the device could be used to test tens of different gradient steep-ness (along X-axis) with multiple replicates (along Y-axis) in a single HT-ChemoChip. Characterization of molecular gradient: For an overall evalua-tion of the gradient generation principle in an HT-ChemoChip, we ﬁrst performed computational simulation to model the diffusion process and the resulted gradient proﬁles. In parallel, we also performed diffusion experiments with ﬂuores-cently labeled dextran (70 kDa) to validate and conﬁrm the strategy using confocal microscopy. When the imaging setting (e.g., laser power and scanning speed) was ﬁxed, a linear dependence between the dextran concentrations and ﬂuorescence intensities was achieved, and was used to calculate the actual concentrations from the ﬂuorescence values in later experiments. Steepness-dependent response to Sema3A. After an initial validation with the above chemoattractive cues, we focused on a chemorepellent molecule, Sema3A, and used the HT-ChemoChip to dissect the role of its gradient steepness in regulating different but coordinated cellular programs (neuronal migration and neurite guidance). Notably, this quantiﬁcation was only an approximate evaluation of the nonlinear concentration curves, but clearly demonstrated the feasibility of the HT-ChemoChip for generating large-scale 3D gradients of different steepness for high-throughput chemotactic assays. Application to 3D chemotactic assays: Because of a 3D conﬁguration, the HT-ChemoChip provides the capability to characterize neuronal growth with all 3D spatial information (Fig. 3a, Supplementary Movie 1), which is more preferable for recapitulating the in vivo conditions than many existing in vitro chemotactic assays performed using a 2D or cell-aggregate-based culture systems. Steepness-dependent response to Sema3A: After an initial validation with the above chemoattractive cues, we focused on a chemorepellent molecule, Sema3A, and used the HT-ChemoChip to dissect the role of its gradient steepness in regulating different but coordinated cellular programs (neuronal migration and neurite guidance). To analyze the level of neuronal differentiation and its relationship to Sema3A gradient steepness, we further performed immunostaining for axonal and dendritic markers (Tau-1 and MAP2) in neurons that were cultured in different Sema3A gradient. Involvement of STK11 and GSK3 in sensing gradient steepness: Focusing on Sema3A-regulated neuron migration and neurite repellence, we then examined speciﬁc signaling pathways related to this cue and tried to dissect the signals that are responsible for sensing the Sema3A gradient steepness in different cellular programs. Particularly, there have been extensive but sometimes contradictory reports about the involvement of STK11 and GSK3 in the regulation of axon/dendrite outgrowth and cell migration.

11278616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11278616.value: Many cellular programs of neural development are under combinatorial regulation by dif-ferent chemoattractive or chemorepulsive factors. Here, we describe a microﬂuidic platform that utilizes well-controlled three-dimensional (3D) diffusion to generate molecular gradients of varied steepness in a large array of hydrogel cylinders, allowing high-throughput 3D chemotactic assays for mechanistic dissection of steepness-dependent neuronal chemotaxis. Using this platform, we examine neuronal sensitivity to the steepness of gradient composed of netrin-1, nerve growth factor, or semaphorin3A (Sema3A) proteins, and reveal dramatic diversity and complexity in the associated chemotactic regulation of neuronal development. Particularly for Sema3A, we ﬁnd that serine/threonine kinase-11 and glycogen synthase kinase-3 signaling pathways are differentially involved in steepness-dependent chemotactic regulation of coordinated neurite repellence and neuronal migration. These results provide insights to the critical role of gradient steepness in neuronal chemotaxis, and also prove the technique as an expandable platform for studying other chemoresponsive cellular systems.

11278616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11278616.value: In this project, we conducted a systematic study of neuronal chemo-sensation to a large-scale variety of molecular gradient proﬁles and revealed an enormous complexity of neuronal chemotaxis, especially in response to the steepness variation of different chemotactic cues. This study was made feasible by an innovative design of a microﬂuidic device that is capable of generating large-scale molecular gradients with different levels of steepness in a microarray format, providing a high-throughput solution for investigating the dependence of neuronal chemotaxis on steep-ness of molecular gradient. In addition, the device utilizes arrays of hydrogel cylinders as the basic assay units, rendering a 3D ex vivo model to recapitulate the in vivo neuronal growth pattern. While this study is oriented to dissect the role of Sema3A gradient steepness, our results do not exclude more complexity of Sema3A-regulated neuronal chemotaxis that involves contribu-tion from both absolution concentration and gradient steepness of a particular chemotactic molecule. Using the same setup, the concentration-related regulation could be further explored in more details by adjusting the background concentration level of a guidance factor. We believe that the 3D high-throughput chemotactic assay platform provides an innovative experimental framework to advance the ﬁeld of neurobiology.

11278616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11278616.value: Chemotaxis refers to the movement of an organism in response to a chemical stimulus. It is well known that the concentration gradients of guidance molecules, such as netrin or semaphorin (Sema) proteins, play critical roles in embryonic neural development. Yet, how exactly the physical profiles of molecular gradients, e.g. the changing rate of concentration profiles (gradient steepness), interplays with neuronal development has long remained an unanswered question. Part of the reason was the lack of 3D devices that can recapitulate important features of brain tissues outside human body. Previous in vitro chemotactic assays are often 2D, low-throughput and lack fine gradient control. In response, we develop a new platform for performing the chemotactic experiments. They develop a hydrogel-based microfluidic platform for high-throughput 3D chemotactic assays, and use it to study neuronal sensitivity to the steepness of molecular gradient, shedding light on neural regeneration mechanism by recognizing subtle variation in the gradient profiles of guidance molecules. Using the new platform and rigorous statistical analysis, the team has revealed dramatic diversity and complexity in the chemotactic regulation of neuronal development by various guidance molecules. In particular, for Sema3A, we find that STK11 and GSK3 signaling pathways are differentially involved in steepness-dependent chemotactic regulation of coordinated neurite repellence and neuronal migration.

11278716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11278716.value: Nanomaterials usually show unconventional behavior under mechanical load due to size effect. Therefore, investigating the nanomaterials’ mechanical property has become essentially significant in many aspects, which could not only benefit our fundamental understanding of the material, but also provide guidance and reference for the practical application in industry. Among all the mechanical prosperity studies, torsion test is an extremely common test to elucidate the ability of the material against twisting forces before cracking or breaking. However, at current stage, the torsion property of the nanomaterial is rarely known since the testing has high requirement to the positioning, manipulation, and torque sensing ability of the testing device. Herein, in this project, we intend to propose a novel nano robot system to characterize the torsion prosperity of the nanomaterials. Firstly, we will develop the nano robot with 6-DOFs, including one rotation DOF, and integrate it with SEM. Then, we will fix the nanomaterial onto the robot and align it to the rotation axis of the robotic system. In addition, we will design a MEMS torque sensor to measure the torque applied on the nanomaterial. Finally, the torsion property of the nanomaterial will be investigated by controlling the movement of the nanorobotic system cooperatively. With this kind of experimental setup, the behavior of the nanomaterial under a torsion load can be studied in-situ, which would pave a new sight for the nanomaterial characterization and benefit both the fundamental research and the practical application as well. The successful implementation of this project will have long-term impacts in many aspects: Firstly, it provides the possibility for the in situ torsion test of micro/nano materials inside SEM for the first time; Secondly, in addition to torsion testing, the nanorobotic system will pave a novel way for the multi-directional imaging inside SEM; Thirdly, this project will deliver a novel type of MEMS torque sensor with the advantages of small dimension and high accuracy; Last but not least, this project will produce a practicable nano characterization system rather than a porotype in laboratory, thereby it has high potential for commercialization in the near future. Consequently, we believe this proposal will lead to an automatic, efficient, flexible and costless nanorobotic system for the torsion testing. It will not only promote the fundamental material research and practical industry application, but also produce a unique testing device for commercialization. 材料在微納尺度通常會體現出明顯的尺寸效應。研究材料在納米尺度的機械性能不僅能揭示材料的基本特性，也為其實際應用提供了指導和借鑒。在所有的機械特性研究中，扭轉測試是一種極為常見的測試，對揭示扭轉載荷對材料的開裂或斷裂有重要的意義。然而，受限於測量手段的限制，目前很難對微納尺度的材料進行扭轉測試。 本專案旨在提出一種新的微納機器人作業系統來實現對微納納材料的扭轉測試。首先，我們將開發具有6個自由度（包含旋轉自由度）的微納操作器並將其與顯微鏡系統整合。之後，我們將設計相應的MEMS扭矩感測器來測量施加在納米材料上的扭矩。最後，通過協同控制微納操作器系統的運動，來實現對納米材料的扭轉特性研究。該研究可以實現對微納材料扭轉特性的原位測量，為材料的力學特性研究提供了一種全新的方法，有重要的理論和實踐意義。

11278716.label: Realisation of objectives
11278716.value: All the objectives have been achieved and the outcomes have been presented in the forms of papers (9 SCI Journal, 3 International Conferences) and patents (1 CN patent). Objective 1: To develop a nanorobotic system to achieve the precise positioning and manipulation of the nano material. We have developed a nanorobotic system with 6-DOFs and integrated it with microscopy. The travel range, resolution and repeatability of the linear positioners are 20 mm, 1 nm and 50 nm; and the travel range, resolution and repeatability of the rotary positioner are 360° endless, 1μ° and 5% over full range, respectively. To hold the nanomaterial for torsion test, two sample holders were designed and assembled on the two manipulation units of the robot. Additionally, a specific connection port is also designed to control the robot by PC outside SEM’s chamber. With this kind of design, the sample alignment can be realized by adjusting the translational units and the torsion testing can be implemented based on the cooperation between the two robotic units. Specifically, the nano positioner can guarantee the positioning accuracy during the torsion testing. Objective 2. To realize the in-situ torque measurement by developing a MEMS based torsion sensor. The sensor was designed and optimized using the finite element method (COMSOL Multiphysics 5.4) and was fabricated through the silicon-on-insulator (SOI) MEMS manufacturing process. The sensor consists of two symmetrical parts: the released elements, i.e., the double-ended tuning forks (DETFs) and the finger beams; and the fixed components, i.e., the anchors and the electrodes. A spline was etched in the middle of the finger beam, which the cross-scale specimen could be inserted in. When the material is bent or twisted, the reaction force will be applied on the splines, then magnified and transmitted to the DETF resonators. The characteristic frequency of the resonator will be changed, where the applied torque will be transferred into forces acting on the tuning fork. Our microelectromechanical resonant torque sensor can provide an ultrahigh resolution up to 4.78 fN∙m within an ultrawide dynamic range of 123 dB, which is the highest reported resolution as we know. Objective 3. To automate torsion testing process, then to improve the operation accuracy and working efficiency. The automatic in situ torsion test is realized by the nanorobotic system and the self-developed microelectromechanical resonant torque sensor inside the SEM chamber. To ensure the operation accuracy, a controller and a field programmable gate array (FPGA)-based monitoring system are employed outside the chamber. Through the collaboration of the visual system, the manipulating system and the electrical system, we performed complex assembly under hybrid feedback control and carry out bending/torsion tests with micro/sub-micro scale specimens. With the supporting of the robotic manipulation, we finally obtained a positioning resolution as good as one pixel. Objective 4. To investigate the torsion property of the nanomaterials based on the developed testing platform. We have applied this system to the in-situ torsion test of several types of micro/nano materials, such as Si, glass, human hair, and so on. Taking the torsion test of Si as an example, we prepared a silicon dog-bone shaped specimen (width = 8.35 μm, length = 50 μm, and thickness = 1.23 μm) and assembled it on the nano robotic system. Then, we conducted the twisting test by applying different twisting angles of 40, 80, and 120 degrees respectively. The real-time SEM indicates that the Si exhibits a pure elastic deformation at this range. After applying a larger rotation angle (147 degree) on the sample, the Si belt fractured, and the measured stress is 2.7GPa. It suggests that the microbeams were five-fold stronger than their bulk counterparts, which gives us a new platform to study the mechanisms at the small scale.
