11278716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11278716.value: Nanomaterials usually show unconventional behavior under mechanical load due to size effect. Therefore, investigating the nanomaterials’ mechanical property has become essentially significant in many aspects, which could not only benefit our fundamental understanding of the material, but also provide guidance and reference for the practical application in industry. In this project, we proposed a platform combing the nano robotic system and MEMS torque sensor to characterize the torsion property of the micro/nano samples. The major findings and research outcome include: Firstly, a nano robotic manipulation system with 6-DOFs, including one rotation DOF, were developed and integrated with scanning electron microscope. Secondly, we proposed a sample alignment strategy to assemble and align the sample to the rotation axis of the robotic system, which achieved a high positioning accuracy approximate one pixel. Thirdly, we manufactured a torque sensor by MEMS technique to measure the torque applied on the nanomaterial, which is able to provide an ultrahigh resolution up to 4.78 fN∙m within an ultrawide dynamic range of 123 dB. Lastly, we characterized the mechanical property of several types of micro/nano sample during twisting and discovered some interesting features of the materials at the small scale. For instance, we found that the Si microbeams were five-fold stronger than their bulk counterparts. This research provides an effective platform for in-situ characterization, via which the behavior of the nanomaterial under a torsion load can be studied quantitatively. It would pave a new sight for the nanomaterial characterization and benefit both the fundamental research and the practical application as well. Moreover, this project also delivers a practicable nano characterization system that has high potential for commercialization in the future.

11278716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11278716.value: We have developed the nanorobotic manipulation system and torque sensor, and successfully realized the in-situ torsion test of the micro/nano samples. As the future work, this project can be extended further in the following two aspects: (1) To increase the flexibility of the robotic system further. The developed robotic system contains 6DOFs, which is adequate for the in-situ torsion test. In the future, more DOFs may be considered to give the robotic system more functions. For example, add two more manipulation units to allow it to test the electrical property at the same time. (2) To develop an integrated MEMS sensor with more functions. The developed MEMS in this project owes the ability to measure the torques and bending force in one direction. In the future, if the sensor with 6DOFs (3 torques and 3 forces) can be designed, we shall have a very powerful tool for the in-situ nano characterization.

11278716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11278716.value: Recent advances in in-situ characterization have enabled the impression, bending and stretching of micro/nanomaterials and then greatly expanded our understanding on the small world. Yet, as one of the standard test approaches at macro scale, torsion tests at a small scale remain a major challenge due to the lack of an ultrahigh precise torque sensor and the delicate sample assembly strategy. With the support of this project, we designed a microelectromechanical resonant torque sensor with an ultrahigh resolution up to 4.78 fN∙m within an ultrawide dynamic range of 123 dB. Meanwhile, we also developed a nanorobotic system to realize the precise assembly of microscale specimens with nanoscale positioning accuracy. As a result, we successfully realized the repeatable in situ pure torsion tests for the first time. We characterized the mechanical properties of several types of micro/nano materials and found out their unique features due to the size effect. This project pushes the limit of mechanical torsion tests and expands our knowledge on the behavior of micro/nanomaterials at various loads, which is expected to have significant implications for the eventual development and implementation of materials science.

11280216.label: Project Objectives
11280216.value: We will develop efficient algorithms that can provide more robust performance than AMP in a broader range of system settings. We will focus on systems with non-i.i.d. and/or non-Gaussian sensing matrixes. Our aim is to achieve optimized trade-off between data rate, residual mean square error, convergence speed and detection complexity. We will devise techniques for the analysis of new algorithms. We will apply the analysis techniques to design and optimize transmitter and receiver structures. We will study the applications of the new algorithms in coded communication systems based on a generalized amplitude, phase and spatial modulation strategy. We will develop a framework that can provide faster and more robust communication in large, complex channel environments.

11280216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11280216.value: Message-passing and compressed-sensing are two important techniques in signal processing and communications. They have been widely used for parameter estimation and signal detection problems. A conventional belief is that these two techniques are only applicable to systems that are sparse in either connection or signaling. It thus came as rather a surprise recently that the approximate message-passing (AMP) algorithm performs excellently in systems that are dense in both connection and signaling. The remarkable features of AMP have inspired extensive research effort on a wide range of applications, such as channel estimation, data detection, spectral estimation, source location, and imaging for radar, medicine, seismology and astronomy. AMP, however, has its limitations. First, AMP requires a special structure of sensing matrixes. Second, AMP has relatively slow convergence speed. These limitations constitute obstacles in some important applications such as channel estimation in transmission environment with rich dispersion or data detection in large rank deficient systems. In the proposed project, we will explore new ways to overcome the limitations of AMP. Specifically, we will study an orthogonal message-passing technique that can be applied to systems that do not meet the requirements for AMP. We will combine orthogonal message-passing with conventional turbo processing to achieve lower residual error and faster convergence speed. We will analyze the behavior of the new algorithms. The convergence analysis for a message-passing algorithm over a dense graph is generally a difficult issue. The recent progress on AMP offers valuable insights into the problem. We will investigate new mathematical treatments and develop theoretical analysis tools for the new orthogonal message-passing technique. We will also study a generalized spatial modulation scheme, in which information is encoded in the positions of non-zero symbols as well as their amplitudes and phases. We will develop detection techniques that can work with denser signaling and so achieve better compromise between information rate and receiver complexity. Recently, massive multiple-input multiple-output systems comprising large numbers of antennas have been identified as a key technology for the upcoming 5th generation cellular mobile networks. The costs related to channel estimation and data detection become a challenging issue for the success of large antenna systems. The outcomes of this project will provide fast, robust and low-cost solutions for signal processing in such large, complex system environments.

11280216.label: Realisation of objectives
11280216.value: We devised an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) for low-cost iterative signal recovery algorithm for linear system models. OAMP is an improved scheme based on approximate message passing (AMP). AMP is a very efficient signal processing schemes in dense systems. However, AMP has its limitations. In particular, AMP may become unreliable for non IID sensing matrixes, especially for ill-conditioned ones, which leads to poor performance. We conducted a comprehensive comparison between AMP, OAMP and conventional turbo algorithms in journal publication for coded linear systems. We showed that OAMP can potentially outperform both AMP and turbo algorithms in dense systems. These works address Objectives 1 and 2. They are reported in Journal publications [1, 8]. We studied a wide range of applications of OAMP. We developed an analogue spatially coupled scheme involving forward error control codes. This scheme can provide universally good performance at various different channel conditions. We investigated performance of iteration detection in massive MIMO systems. We showed that iterative joint channel estimation and decoding can provide significantly enhance throughput in massive MIMO. We devised detection techniques for orthogonal and non-orthogonal pilots. We showed that near-capacity performance is achievable with diminishing pilot overheads under joint iterative channel estimation and decoding. We investigated OAMP in forward error control (FEC) coded linear vector systems. We applied AMP and OAMP algorithms to such systems involving low-density parity check (LDPC) codes and developed a state evolution procedure based on both minimum mean square error (MMSE) and mutual information measures. These works address Objective 3. They are reported in Journal publications [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].

11280216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11280216.value: Approximate message passing (AMP) is a signal processing algorithm in dense systems. An open problem for AMP is that it may become unreliable for non IID sensing matrixes, especially for ill-conditioned ones. In this project, we devised an orthogonal AMP (OAMP) algorithm for low-cost iterative signal recovery algorithm for linear system models. Our work can be broadly divided into two parts. The first part is on theoretical analysis and the second part on applications. The theoretical study is reported in journal publication [1], where we showed that OAMP is more robust and versatile than AMP. OAMP involves a de-correlated linear estimator (LE) and a divergence-free non-linear estimator (NLE). We derived a state evolution procedure for OAMP and show numerically that the state evolution (SE) for OAMP is accurate for general unitarily-invariant matrices, including IID Gaussian matrices and partial orthogonal matrices. We further identified optimized structures for OAMP and show that OAMP can indeed outperform AMP in many situations. The application part leads to journal publications [1-7], where we studied AMP and OAMP for various applications. In journal publication [2], we developed an AMP based joint detection-decoding algorithm for analogue spatially-coupled (ASC) forward error control (FEC) codes. This scheme can provide universally good performance at various different channel conditions. In journal publications [3, 4], we investigated performance of AMP and OAMP based iteration detection in massive MIMO systems. We showed that such iterative joint channel estimation and decoding techniques can provide significantly enhance throughput in massive MIMO. Near-capacity performance is achievable with diminishing pilot overheads under joint iterative channel estimation and decoding. The systems in these works are all non-sparse and so AMP and OAMP can be used at the receiver side to overcome the correlation built-up during iterative detection. In journal publications [5, 6], we developed AMP and OAMP-based algorithms to overcome the clipping effect in OAMP systems. This provides a new solution to a well-known open problem in 4G and 5G wireless communication systems. In journal publication [7], we studied AMP and OAMP approaches for semi-blind channel estimation. Finally, we conducted a comprehensive comparison between AMP, OAMP and conventional turbo algorithms in journal publication [8] for coded linear systems. We showed that OAMP can potentially outperform the celebrated turbo algorithm in dense systems. In summary, we have well achieved the objectives set in the proposal. The findings of this project have opened a new direction for efficient signal processing algorithms and receiver designs.

11280216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11280216.value: OAMP have already find a wide range of applications in signal processing and communication applications. The outcomes of this project have attracted wide attention in the research community. In particular, journal publication [1] has already received 167 Google citations so far. These following works involve convergence analysis, deep-learning algorithms, inference networks, massive MIMO-NOMA, adaptive neural signal, artificial intelligence-aided receiver, MRI reconstruction, millimeter wave hybrid MIMO systems, just to name a few. We are also working on some interesting applications such as deep machine learning and massive random access.

11280216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11280216.value: OAMP has been widely discussed as a new solution for many signal processing, communication and deep-learning problems. We are encouraged by the enthusiasm in the following-works on OAMP for various applications. We are happy to see our effort has been well received by the research community. We have also been approached by industry on OAMP. In 2020, we secured a Guangdong Government strategic research fund (lead by ZTE) that involves the application of OAMP in beyond 5G and 6G wireless communication systems. These facts clearly indicate that this project has been very successful.

11302116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302116.value: In this project, we aim to develop new photofunctional transition metal complexes as novel synthetic substrates for protein tags including the SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, and HaloTag. The analysis and evaluation of protein functions have been greatly assisted by the development of protein tag technology. In this strategy, the protein of interest is tagged with a low-molecular weight protein or polypeptide, which is subsequently modified with a synthetic label such as an organic fluorophore or other targeting molecules. Currently, the three most widely used protein tags are the SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, and HaloTag. Although a number of fluorescent substrates for these tags have been developed, their use requires stringent washing after labeling because unlabeled probes remaining inside the cells can lead to strong background fluorescence. Thus, one of the current challenges is the development of fluorogenic probes that show fluorescence turn-on after bioconjugation. The protein tag technology has also facilitated the development of chromophore-assisted light inactivation (CALI). This technique employs a chromophore as a photosensitizer that produces reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as singlet oxygen upon irradiation; the latter can damage proteins in close vicinity of the chromophore. Although various protein tag substrates have been utilized, there is a lack of candidates that show high singlet oxygen production quantum yields and at the same time remain photostable upon irradiation. To date, nearly all of the fluorescent probes and photosensitizers developed as SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, and HaloTag substrates are organic dyes. Although the interesting luminescence properties of transition metal complexes have been widely utilized in biosensing and bioimaging as demonstrated by us and other research groups, the idea of using metal complexes as substrates for protein tags has not been explored. In this project, we will design new substrates for the SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, and HaloTag based on photofunctional transition metal complexes. The photophysical and photochemical properties of the complexes and their reactivity toward the protein tags will be investigated. Additionally, the cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, and bioimaging properties of the complexes, and their applications in CALI of proteins and intracellular biosensing will be examined. We believe that a combination of the specificity associated with the genetically encoded protein tags and the intriguing photophysical and photochemical properties of transition metal complexes will afford useful bioimaging, protein-inactivating, and biosensing reagents. Ultimately, we are very confident that the results generated from this project will lead to the development of biological and medical reagents with useful diagnostic and therapeutic applications. 這個項目的目標是開發新的具光功能過渡金屬絡合物作為蛋白質標記（包括 SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, 和HaloTag）的新型合成基質。蛋白質標記技術的發展為蛋白質功能的分析和評測帶來極大的幫助。在這策略中，目標蛋白質首先被低分子量蛋白質或多肽標記，然後被合成的標籤修改，例子句括有機熒光團或其他靶向分子。目前，三個最被廣泛應用的蛋白質標記是SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, 和HaloTag。雖然很多熒光探針已經被研發成這些蛋白質標記的基質，但是使用它們時需要嚴格的洗滌步驟，因為標籤後剩餘在細胞內的探針可能會導致強烈的背景熒光。因此，目前其中一個挑戰是開發能夠於生物耦合後自動亮起熒光的探針。此外，蛋白質標記技術也促進了發色團協助光滅活（CALI）的發展。這種技術採用一個發色團作為光敏劑，此分子於照射後能產生活性氧（ROS），例如單線態氧，可以破壞在其附近的蛋白質。雖然不同的蛋白質標記基質已被利用，但是目前還欠缺一些能提供高單線態氧生產量子產率，而同時具有良好光穩定性的探針。到目前為止，幾乎所有被發展為SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, 和HaloTag蛋白質標記基質的熒光探針與光敏劑都是有機染料。雖然過渡金屬絡合物有趣的發光特性已經被我們和其他研究小組廣泛地應用於生物傳感和生物成像，但是以金屬絡合物作為蛋白質標記基質的主題還沒有被探討過。在這個項目中，我們將設計具光功能的過渡金屬絡合物作為SNAP-tag, CLIP-tag, 和HaloTag蛋白質標記的全新基質，並研究它們的光物理和光化學特性及其對蛋白質標記的反應性。此外，我們還會研究該等絡合物的細胞攝取、細胞毒性、生物成像性能和它們被應用在蛋白質發色團協助光滅活和細胞內生物傳感的可能性。我們相信基因編碼蛋白質標記的特性以及過渡金屬絡合物的光物理和光化學性質的結合，將可以提供有用的生物成像、蛋白質失活和生物傳感的試劑。我們非常有信心這個項目的結果最終能發展成應用於診斷和治療的生物和醫學試劑。

11302116.label: Realisation of objectives
11302116.value: We exploited the use of 6-methyl-3-(2-pyridyl)tetrazine (py-Tz-Me) as a ligand for the synthesis of novel iridium(III) pyridyl-tetrazine complexes [Ir(N^C)2(py-Tz-Me)](PF6). Upon photoexcitation, the complexes displayed extremely weak emission due to quenching by the tetrazine unit. Upon addition of the strained cyclooctyne bicyclo[6.1.0]non-4-yn-9-ylmethanol (BCN) or bovine serum albumin (BSA) modified with a BCN moiety (BCN-BSA), significant emission enhancement appeared due to the conversion of the tetrazine unit into a non-quenching pyridazine derivative. The specific reaction of the complexes with BCN-BSA provided outstanding emission enhancement (128.1 to 1372.2). We applied the complexes to label specific target proteins in combination with the use of the protein tag HaloTag. The idea was to develop a wash-free approach for the luminogenic labeling of the HaloTag protein. Remarkably, a GST-HaloTag fusion protein treated with both BCN-C6-Cl and one of the complexes revealed emission enhancement of 2.17, whereas no similar emission change was observed in the negative controls. The results indicated that the GST-HaloTag fusion protein acquired the BCN functionality through its specific enzymatic reaction with BCN-C6-Cl, and this labeling was subsequently revealed by the bioorthogonal reaction of the BCN unit with the complex. The complex was further used to illuminate endogenous proteins containing a HaloTag in live cells. In another study, we developed a strategy to utilize iridium(III) nitrone complexes and SNAP-tag protein for the modulation of emission and singlet oxygen (1O2)-photosensitization in live cells. New iridium(III) nitrone complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-nitrone)](PF6) were designed as bioorthogonal phosphorogenic probes for a benzylguanine derivative BCN-BG, which is a specific substrate for the SNAP-tag protein. Upon reaction in aqueous buffer, the mixtures showed significant emission enhancement and lifetime extension (I/Io = 7.2 – 47.1, lifetimes = 0.28 – 0.58 us) as a result of the conversion of the quenching nitrone unit into a non-quenching isoxazoline derivative. The complexes exhibited greater emission enhancement (82.9 – 327.1 fold) (lifetimes = 0.43 – 1.14 us) upon reaction with the modified protein BCN-BSA. We also reacted BCN-BG with SNAP-tag protein and isolated the conjugate BCN-SNAP. As expected, the complexes also displayed more intense emission upon reaction with the conjugate, with the enhancement factors up to 10.6. CHO-K1 cells were transfected with phage UbiC SNAP-KDEL and pSNAPf that express endoplasmic reticulum-targeting and cytoplasm-enriched SNAP-tag, respectively. Confocal microscopy images indicated that strong emission signal was found only in cells that expressed SNAP-tag at ER and cytoplasm, confirming that the complexes were facile phosphorogenic probes for intracellular SNAP-tag. The complexes showed very low cytotoxicity toward HeLa cells in the dark. However, the cytotoxic activity increased significantly after the cells were transfected with the pSNAPf Vector that expresses SNAP-tag in the cytoplasm, followed by treatment with BCN-BG and upon excitation, impressive PI values of 9.0 – 115.9 were obtained. Thus, even more enhanced photogeneration of 1O2 occurred when BCN-BG and SNAP-tag were co-present. In other studies, we designed thiol-sensitive systems as new biological tools for controlled cytotoxicity and imaging. We synthesized three iridium(III) complexes bearing a 2,4-dinitrophenyl ether moiety [Ir(pq)2(bpy-O-C6H3(NO2)2)](PF6) as intracellular sensors for biothiols. These complexes were extremely weakly emissive due to the quenching dinitroaromatic moiety. However, after the moiety is attacked by a thiol nucleophile such as Cys, GSH, and H2S, the emission is turned on. One of the complexes showed facile cellular uptake and served as a phosphorogenic intracellular sensor for GSH and H2S. Through the incorporation of a benzylguanine or chlorohexane moiety into the complexes and the use of organelle-selective fusion proteins containing a SNAP-tag or HaloTag, the complexes could detect biothiols at specific organelles. To modulate the cytotoxicity of transition metal complexes, two iridium(III) PEG complexes with disulfide linkage [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-SS-PEG)](PF6) and a bimetallic iridium(III)-rhenium(I) complex [Ir(pqe)2(bpy-SS-py)(CO)3(Me4-phen)Re](PF6)(CF3SO3) were designed. Cell based assays on the mononuclear complex demonstrated that the addition of GSH to induce cleavage of the disulfide linker provided a more cytotoxic agent due to the release of the PEG pendant. The disulfur linkage of the dinuclear complex was also sensitive to thiols, and cleavage would lead to emission turn-on for both luminescent metal complex units. We developed luminescent transition metal complexes bearing a carbohydrate unit or a receptor for carbohydrate for bioimaging applications. Two ruthenium(II) complexes appended with a D-fructose unit, [Ru(N^N)2(bpy-fructose)](PF6)2 were synthesized. Their photophysical properties, lipophilicity, and cytotoxicity were also studied. The cellular uptake and intracellular localization of the Ph2-phen complexes toward MCF-7, MDCK, 3T3, and HeLa cells were investigated. These complexes displayed intense membrane staining toward MCF-7 cells. Confocal microscopy and flow cytometry suggested that the complexes were transported into cells via a glucose transporter (GLUT)-mediated pathway. Since cancer cells utilize their overexpressed sialylated antigens to propagate metastases, the development of probes for sialic acids has attracted much attention. Thus, we synthesized luminescent iridium(III) bipyridylphenylboronic acid (PBA) complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-TEG-PBA)](PF6), which were found to display higher binding affinity to the most common sialic acid N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac) compared with simple sugars. Notably, they can recognize cellular sialic acid residues, resulting in more efficient uptake than their PBA-free counterparts. Mesoionic sydnones have been discovered as new bioorthogonal reaction partners of alkynes in 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition reaction. Thus, we designed new bioorthogonal imaging reagents with environment-sensitive emission properties through the modification of sydnone with iridium(III) complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-NHCO-C6H4-sydnone)](PF6). These complexes displayed significant emission enhancement and lifetime elongation upon reaction with strained alkynes, and were utilized to label cyclooctyne-modified proteins and ceramide molecules in live cells with controlled photocytotoxicity. In another study, we designed luminescent molecular hybrids with eight cyclometalated iridium(III) polypyridine units grafted on a polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) core [POSS-{Ir(N^C)2(py-im)}8](PF6)8. The properties of these complexes were compared with those of their POSS-free counterparts. These hybrids showed much lower dark and light cytotoxicity compared to their POSS-free counterparts. In addition to protein tags, we have been interested in the modification of peptide tags with luminescent transition metal complexes for sensing, imaging, and photosensitizing applications. Thus, cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes appended with a perfluorobiphenyl (PFBP) moiety [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-CH2-OCONH-C2H4-S-C12F9)](PF6) were designed as bioconjugation and bioimaging reagents for cysteine-containing peptides. The PFBP complexes reacted readily with the pi-clamp sequence (Phe-Cys-Pro-Phe) to afford highly emissive bioconjugates. Confocal microscopy showed that all the complexes were diffusely distributed in the cytoplasmic region of the live HeLa cells with punctate staining, which appeared to be the mitochondria. These complexes showed a huge potential to be developed as organelle-selective bioimaging reagents and photocytotoxic agents. Overall, there were no significant difficulties encountered in this project. The largest obstacle would be weak binding of transition metal complexes to the protein tags if the substrates were directly linked to the metal complexes. Fortunately, this problem was circumvented by using a more efficient two-step approach, where the substrate was modified with a bioorthogonal group and the complexes were modified with the complementary reaction partner. Through a judicious choice of functional groups and quenching systems, we have successfully developed transition metal complexes that showed enhancement of luminescence intensities and 1O2-photosensitization efficiencies upon reaction with protein tags including HaloTag and SNAP-tag. A number of photofunctional transition metal complexes were developed in this project as cellular probes for small molecules, bioimaging reagents, and photocytotoxic agents. The project was also extended to the rational design of new reagents for bioorthogonal probes and peptide tags, which are anticipated to confer unique luminescence and cellular uptake properties on transition metal complexes for a range of biological applications.

11302116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302116.value: In this project, a number of new luminescent transition metal complexes appended with functional units were synthesized by different strategies, and fully characterized using a range of spectroscopic methods such as NMR, ESI-MS, IR, and elemental analyses. The fundamental UV-Vis absorption, photophysical, photochemical, and electrochemical properties of the complexes were examined. Additionally, the water solubility, lipophilicity, cellular uptake properties, and cytotoxic activity of all the complexes were investigated. In the first study, we synthesized novel iridium(III) pyridyl-tetrazine complexes that displayed extremely weak emission due to quenching by the tetrazine unit. However, these complexes exhibited significant emission enhancement upon reaction with strained alkyne derivatives. Using these complexes and BCN-C6-Cl (a strained-alkyne containing substrate for the protein tag HaloTag), we have developed a wash-free procedure for the luminogenic labeling of the HaloTag protein as well as proteins of interest that are fused to HaloTag. This strategy has also been applied to the sensing and imaging of endogenous proteins in live cells. In another study, we exploited the phosphorogenic properties of new iridium(III) nitrone complexes that are responsive toward strained alkyne derivatives and combined them with the applications of protein tags, with an aim to achieve targeted, controlled emission enhancement and photocytotoxicity. New iridium(III) nitrone complexes were designed, which showed greatly enhanced emission intensities and extended lifetimes upon reaction with strained alkyne derivatives. These complexes are responsive toward the benzylguanine analogue BCN-BG, which is also a specific substrate for the SNAP-tag protein. Thus, we modified SNAP-tag protein with BCN-BG and reacted the conjugate with the iridium(III) nitrone complexes to turn on their emission as well as photocytotoxic activity. We showed that live cells that express SNAP-tag fusion proteins can be readily imaged with our phosphorogenic iridium(III) nitrone complexes using the BCN-BG substrate. Hence, we demonstrated that the bioorthogonal reactivity and phosphorogenic property of the complexes and SNAP-tag protein can be exploited for the modulation of emission and 1O2-photosensitization in live cells. Inspired by these exciting results, we have also extended the studies to related systems including: 1) disulfide complexes that are sensitive to biothiols for controlled (photo)cytotoxicity and imaging; 2) carbohydrate systems where the metal complexes show specific localization due to binding to membrane proteins or reaction with surface-bound sialic acid residues; 3) mesoionic sydnone systems that show environment-sensitive photophysical and photochemical properties; and 4) perfluorobiphenyl complexes that display selective reactivity toward the pi-clamp amino acid sequence.

11302116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302116.value: We have demonstrated that the combined applications of protein tags and luminescent transition metal complexes modified with a bioorthogonal/quenching unit can realize biomolecular sensing, protein imaging, and controlled photocytotoxicity with high selectivity. The most important findings are that the phosphorogenic bioorthogonal reactivity of transition metal complexes can be utilized together with the selectivity associated with protein tags, which can be readily fused to proteins of interest. Our results will be valuable to the development of intracellular probes for endogenous proteins that are of diagnostic value. Additionally, the protein tag technology has a strong potential for the development of molecular oncological tools since it can realize cancer cell-targeting with substantially reduced toxicity. This is particular attractive in the context of photofunctional transition metal complexes because most metal complexes are efficient 1O2 photosensitizers that can contribute to photodynamic therapy. Additionally, photolabile complexes that are capable of releasing gaseous signaling molecules are known. Furthermore, a number of photoactivatable transition metal complexes with anticancer and other therapeutic properties are documented. We anticipate that a combination of these systems with the protein tag technology will further enhance the application potential of transition metal complexes in biological and medical science which is currently unexplored.

11302116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302116.value: The aim of this project was to develop new photofunctional transition metal complexes as novel synthetic substrates for protein tags. The protein tag technology has greatly facilitated the studies of protein functions through imaging and light inactivation. In this strategy, the protein of interest is tagged with a small protein or polypeptide, which is subsequently modified with a fluorescent dye or other targeting molecules with different functions. Despite the fact that fluorescent substrates for protein tags have been documented, almost all of the substrates reported thus far do not show fluorogenic responses, requiring stringent washing steps after labeling. Additionally, there is a lack of substrates that show efficient singlet oxygen-photosensitization and at the same time remain photostable upon irradiation. In this project, we have developed transition metal complexes that can indirectly interact with protein tags including SNAP-tag and HaloTag. We have also demonstrated that the hybridization of protein tags and luminescent transition metal complexes modified with a bioorthogonal/quenching unit can achieve phosphorogenic biomolecular sensing, protein imaging, and controlled photocytotoxicity with high selectivity. We anticipate that the protein tag technology will further enhance the application potential of photofunctional transition metal complexes in biological and medical science.

11303016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303016.value: The six Painleve equations are a series of second-order nonlinear ordinary differential equations which were first discovered and studied by Painleve, Gambier and their colleagues more than one century ago. Although these equations are nonlinear, they have very close relations with some linear differential systems. As a consequence, the solutions of these equations possess fascinating properties which are very different from the usual nonlinear ones. For example, when the parameters in the equations equal certain special values, there are hierarchies of rational solutions or one-parameter families of solutions expressible in terms of the classical special functions, such as Airy functions, Bessel functions and parabolic cylinder functions. Nowadays, due to their important applications in many physical branches including statistical mechanics, random matrix theory, nonlinear waves, quantum field theory and general relativity, these solutions are regarded as nonlinear special functions. To understand the Painleve equations in more detail, we will study properties of their solutions in this project. More precisely, we will derive the asymptotic expansions of the solutions on the real axis. Then, the connection formula, which is the relation between different asymptotic expansions of the same solution, will be established. We will also consider the behavior of the solutions in the complex plane and try to understand how their poles are distributed. 大約一個世紀以前，法國數學家Painleve, Gambier以及他們的同事發現了一些特殊的二階非線性常微分方程，即所謂的“Painleve 方程”。雖然這些方程是非線性的，但是它們与一些線性的微分系統有著非常緊密的聯係。因此，与普通的非線性方程相比，Painleve方程具有很多獨特的性質。舉例來說，當Painleve方程里的參數取某些特殊值的時候，它們的解可以用經典的特殊函數（比如Airy函數，Bessel函數以及拋物柱面函數）來表示。如今，由於Painleve方程的解在很多物理分支（比如隨機矩陣理論，非線性波，量子場論以及廣義相對論）都有重要的應用，它們被看作非線性的特殊函數。 為了更徹底的瞭解Painleve方程，我們計划在本項目中研究它們解的性質。更確切地説，我們會推導這些解在實軸上的漸進展開。然後我們會建立這些漸進展開之間的關係，也就是聯係公式。我們還計划考察這些解在復平面裏的性質并研究它們的極點是如何分布的。

11303016.label: Realisation of objectives
11303016.value: The main objective of this project is to study various properties of the Painleve transcendents, as well as their applications in mathematical physics. We first consider the inhomogeneous Painleve II equation. For the homogeneous case, it is well-known that there exist two families of solutions, namely the Hastings-McLeod solutions and the Ablowitz-Segur solutions, which have extensive applications in many areas of applied mathematics and mathematical physics. Both families of solutions are smooth on the real axis, but they have significantly different behaviours when x tends to negative infinity. Moreover, the Hastings-McLeod solutions are monotonic while the Ablowitz-Segur solutions are oscillatory on the real axis. For the inhomogeneous case, we proved that similar solutions exist. We also derived their asymptotics when the independent variable x tends to plus/minus infinity and the connection formulas. The starting point of our derivation is the integrable structure of the Painleve equations, i.e., the Lax pair, from which a 2x2 matrix valued Riemann-Hilbert problem is constructed. Then, applying the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest method for Riemann-Hilbert problems, the pole-free properties and the asymptotics are obtained via a series of delicate analysis. Moreover, based on the numerical observations in the literature, we rigorously proved the existence of the quasi-Hastings-McLeod solutions and the quasi-Ablowitz-Segur of the inhomogeneous Painleve II equation. Although they share the similar asymptotics as the classical ones when x is large, these solutions possess finitely many poles on the real axis. We showed how the number of poles depends on the inhomogeneous parameter, as well as the dynamics when the parameter changes. At the end, a family of singular solutions is studied, which possess infinitely many poles on the real axis. Via a modified Riemann-Hilbert approach, the singular asymptotics are also established rigorously. In addition, we consider the tronquée solutions, another family of solutions of the Painleve II equation, and the associated Hamiltonians. Comparing with the solutions mentioned above, the tronquée solutions possess infinitely many poles in the complex plane. Nevertheless, the location of the poles has nice structure, in the sense that they are confined in certain sectors in the complex plane. Interestingly, the associated Hamiltonians are pole-free on the real axis. In the literature of random matrix theory, integrals of these quantities play a significant role in the eigenvalue spacing problems. A major challenge in evaluating the integrals is to determine the integration constant explicitly. By observing nice structures of the Hamiltonians, we derived several crucial differential identities for the Hamiltonians, with respect to different parameters contained in the integrand. In such a way, we transform the integrals to the ones associated with the varying parameters. A key fact is that our asymptotic results are uniform for the parameters. Moreover, the detailed asymptotics about the Hamiltonians is known for special parameters. Therefore, one can determine the integration constants explicitly by integrating about the parameter instead. In a summary, our work is a systematic investigation about the asymptotics of the Painleve II equation. We believe this is an important contribution in the literature. Next, we focus on applications of the Painleve equations in random matrix theory. For the classical Gaussian unitary ensembles, it is well-known that the eigenvalue correlation kernel is expressed in terms of the Hermite polynomials. By letting the matrix size n tend to infinity (equivalently, the degree of the polynomials goes to infinity), the limiting kernels are the sine kernel and the Airy kernel. Note that, these limiting kernels arise for a large class of matrix models. They only depend on some general characteristic features, instead of the exact formulations of the matrix models. This phenomena are called “universality” in random matrix theory. If there are some singularities in the weight function, the local eigenvalue distribution will change significantly near the singular point. Under a double scaling limit, new limiting eigenvalue correlation kernels emerge, where the Painleve kernels are typical example. In this project, we consider Gaussian unitary ensembles perturbed by pole singularities near the soft edge. Under a multiple scaling limit, the limiting eigenvalue correlation kernel is given in term of the kernel involving a system of coupled Painleve XXXIV equations. We believe this is a novel universality class. With the limiting kernels obtained, we further consider the eigenvalue spacing properties in unitary ensembles. The Painleve II and Painleve III kernels are well-known kernels, which describe some important phase transitions in the random matrix theory. Since these kernels are integrable, it is possible to embed the Fredholm determinants of these kernels in matrix-valued Riemann-Hilbert problems. Note that the Fredholm determinants, as well as their derivatives, give us the probability that there are certain number of eigenvalues in a given interval. When the number is set to be zero, this is the well-known gap probability. It is an important quantity which describes the spacing of eigenvalues in random matrices. With the Riemann-Hilbert problem at hand, we applied the Deift-Zhou method to derive the so-called “large gap asymptotics”, i.e., the asymptotics that there is no eigenvalue in a large interval. Such kind of problems are one of the central problems in the study of random matrix theory. In addition, the explicit integral representations for the gap probabilities are obtained, which involves solutions to the coupled Painleve equations. The coupled Painleve equations are some higher order generalizations of the classical ones. Our integral formula for the gap probability can be viewed as the generalization of the celebrated Tracy-Widom distribution. Finally, due to the close relation among orthogonal polynomials and the Painleve equations, we studied properties of some polynomials orthogonal with asymptotic Freud-like weights, some q-orthogonal polynomials and the related Ramanujan type entire function. These results deepen our understanding about special functions and their relations to the Painleve equations and their generalizations.

11303016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303016.value: In this research project, we first thoroughly investigated the inhomogeneous Painleve II equations. Parallel to the homogeneous ones, several families of important solutions are studied, such as the Ablowitz–Segur solutions, the quasi-Ablowitz-Segur and quasi-Hastings-McLeod solutions, and the singular solutions. We derived their asymptotic properties on the real axis, as well as the connection formulas. The pole-free property of the Ablowitz–Segur solutions on the real axis is also established. For the quasi-Hastings-McLeod solutions and the quasi-Ablowitz–Segur solutions, there are finitely many poles on the real line. The number depends on the inhomogeneous parameter. We demonstrated the dynamics of the pole location when the parameter varies. This rigorously justifies numerical observations made by Fornberg and Weideman in the literature. The singular asymptotics of the inhomogeneous Painleve II equations are obtained as well. In addition, the total integrals of certain solution and Hamiltonians to the Painleve II equations are derived. The major difficulty in evaluating such kind of integrals is to determine the integration constants. This is one of the well-known questions in this research field. Making use of several differential identities with respect to different parameters or the independent variable x, we transform the integral about x to some auxiliary integrals about the parameters. Since our asymptotic formulas are uniformly valid for different parameters, we finally obtained the integration constant by integrating the formulas about the parameters. We also study some applications of the Painleve equations in the random matrix theory. By studying the Fredholm determinants of the well-known Painleve II and III kernels, we obtain their explicit integral representations in terms of the coupled Painleve equations. These equations are recently discovered and viewed as the novel fourth-order generalization of the classical ones. Some properties of their solutions are derived, including their asymptotic behaviour. These results are successfully applied to get the large gap asymptotics for a class of random matrix models, which are important for us to understand the eigenvalue spacing problems in these models. Last, we investigate some relations among orthogonal polynomials, the Painleve equations and random matrices. Some new and interesting results are achieved, such as the relation between a fermionic matrix model and related q-polynomials.

11303016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303016.value: Based on this project, there are several possible research problems in the future: i) The study of the coupled Painleve equations In the study of the Fredholm determinant of the Painleve II and Painleve III kernels, we realize that the integral representations are given in terms of solutions to the coupled Painleve equations. They are viewed as the fourth-order generalization of the classical ones. Although some of their properties have been obtained in this project, there are still a lot of unknown properties to be explored, such as special pole-free solutions, their asymptotics and total integrals on the real line, asymptotics for the related Hamiltonian and tau functions, and so on. ii) Properties of the coupled Painleve equations in random matrix theory When studying the deformed Airy kernels, one can see that their Fredholm determinants have the similar expression as the undeformed ones. They major difference is that a new family of solutions to the Painleve II equations replaces the role of the Hastings-McLeod solutions. We expect similar phenomena happen for the other kernels as well.

11303016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303016.value: The Painleve equations are six famous second-order nonlinear ordinary differential equations. They have significant applications in various branches of mathematics and physics. Their solutions, namely the Painleve transcendents, are regarded as the special functions in the 21st century. In this project, we systematically studied the inhomogeneous Painleve II equations and established a comprehensive understanding about their solutions. A novel fourth-order generalization of the classical Painleve equations are discovered and studied in this project, which has important potential for the further investigation due to their applications. We also successfully applied properties of the Painleve transcendents to study one of the central topics in random matrix theory, the eigenvalue spacing problems. The results obtained in this project deepen our understanding about the relations between these two important subjects (the Painleve equations and random matrix theory) in the modern mathematical physics.

11303316.label: Project Objectives
11303316.value: 1- First Objective: Elaborating the Stochastic Maximum Principle We consider that the dynamic programming approach is hopeless in general. Indeed, the state to be estimated is already infinite dimensional. In the methodology of dynamic programming, we should consider the conditional probability distribution of this infinite dimensional state. The value function becomes a functional of this state. It is thus a functional on a space which has a very primitive structure. The stochastic maximum principle is more promising. The adjoint variable can be defined as the solution of an infinite dimensional backward stochastic partial differential equation, as explained in the research plan. It has never appeared before, but at least can be formulated properly. 2- Second Objective: Studying particular cases In the classical situation of partial information without mean field, there are many cases which can be studied and solved. The basic one is the linear quadratic case. But there are many more, namely when the so called separation principle holds. It is thus promising to consider the possibility of a separation principle, for the mean field situation. Such particular cases can give the opportunity of one or several PhD dissertations 1- Third Objective: Discrete Time Our approach focuses on continuous time. It makes sense to consider discrete time. First, it may reduce some difficulties; second any attempt to go to numerical applications will require a good understanding of the discrete time situation. This could be the research topic of a PhD student.

11303316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303316.value: Mean field games have been introduced in 2006, independently by Lasry-Lions and Huang-Caines-Malhamé. Since then, this domain has attracted a considerable interest worldwide. This interest keeps growing, after almost a decade. The mean field community meets every other year and has become quite large. The domain is now constantly represented in all large conferences on control or applied mathematics. One reason is certainly due to the mathematical new challenges which appear continuously in the domain. Another one concerns the attractiveness of the concepts for applications. The idea that decision makers cannot act independently of large crowds of other individuals in which they are embedded is now obvious. At the same time, traditional tools in optimization, control theory are not adapted. Mean field theories, which incorporate ideas from physics, making an analogy between individuals in a large community and particles in a medium, provide a clear progress. At the same time, the new mathematical problems at stake are huge. The P.I. has benefited in 2013 of an RGC grant on mean field control, in which the objectives were first to provide a comprehensive approach to mean field games and mean field type control, and second to waive the limitation that players are identical. We now address a completely new topic. The decision makers do not have full information about the past and the present. They observe a signal, which is affected by measurement errors. This problem corresponds to concrete motivations, well known in the standard stochastic control framework. It has very little been addressed up to now, except in particular situations. Only recently Şen and Caines have studied nonlinear filtering for Mc Kean-Vlasov diffusions. An important aspect is to describe the uncertainties on the system itself. We consider two types of noise, the local noise and the common noise. This refers to the origin of mean field modeling. There is a large community of identical agents. The state evolution of each of them is affected individually by a local noise, and a common noise, which affects all of them. Think of the state of the economy, as an example. Our main effort will be to derive a stochastic maximum principle to characterize optimal decisions. Basically, we will try to extend to Mac Kean diffusions, what is known for ordinary diffusions. As described in the proposal, we are confident it can be done. There are, however, daunting mathematical challenges, which motivates our research. 自2006年起, 平均場博弈論分別由Larsy與Lions， Huang- Caines-Malhamé獨立引進。從那時起，這個領域已開始吸引了全世界不同學者的興趣，當中一個原因是由於這領域連續地向數學界提出各樣新的挑戰。我們現在討論一個全新的課題, 當中決策者沒有過去和現在的全部信息, 他們所觀察到的信息是帶有測量誤差的影響。除了Sen-Caines研究了在McKean-Vlasov 擴散下非線性濾波和在特定情況下，到現在為止這問題很少被討論， 我們將考察相關問題, 而模型當中亦考慮兩種類型的噪聲：個人的噪聲和共用的噪聲。我們的主要利用隨機最大值原理來表示最優決策，同時亦推擴一般在普通擴散已有的結果到McKean擴散情況中。

11303316.label: Realisation of objectives
11303316.value: FINAL REPORT 113 03 316 We have well explained in our interim report the various mathematical problems, which arise in mean field games and mean field type control, with full and partial information. On the one hand, thanks to the active research, which takes place worldwide in the community of mean field theory, significant progress is obtained. New ideas are introduced and it takes a long time to fully harness them. This is particularly the case of the lifting method approach of mean field theory. The problem is to solve the master equation. This is the key equation of mean field control and mean field games. The importance of the master equation is that it synthesizes completely the theory. In particular, from the master equation, we can recover the system of Hamilton Jacobi Bellman- Fokker Planck equations, which represents a major part of the theory. One of the key advantages of the master equation is that it is a deterministic equation, whereas the system of HJB-FP equations can be deterministic or stochastic, in which case it is a complex system of forward-backward stochastic PDE (partial differential equations). The drawback of the master equation is that it is an infinite dimensional PDE, in which the arguments are partly in R^n and partly in the probability measures on R^n . The natural functional space for probability measures is the Wasserstein space. A lot of effort worldwide is devoted to the analysis and control of dynamic systems, for which the state space is the Wasserstein space. The lifting procedure idea is an alternative to the Wasserstein space. It has been introduced by P.L. Lions. It relies on the strong and weak approaches of random variables. A random variable can be seen as a function on a probability space, or simply characterized by its probability distribution. To a probability measure, one associates a random variable, built on a convenient probability space. This allows replacing a metric space by a Hilbert space. Indeed, instead of the Wasserstein space, one can work with the space of square integrable random variables. We have devoted a lot of effort to make use of this brilliant idea, as much as possible, for mean field problems with full and partial observation. We have obtained significant results, which led to publications. Very often, this idea is only partly used. For instance, for Bellman equation of mean field type control, it is used just to write a viscosity interpretation of an infinite dimensional PDE. This is because viscosity theory is available for PDE on a Hilbert space, and not for PDE on the Wasserstein space. However, our goal has been much more ambitious. We want to make use of it, from the very beginning, at the formulation of the original problem. In the community, we are spearheading this research direction. In spite of successes, we have encountered unexpected difficulties. There is a way to work with Hilbert spaces, without introducing the set of square integrable random variables. It consists simply in working with probability measures, which have densities with respect to the Lebesgue measure on R^n, and assuming that the densities are square integrable. This is first quite restrictive, but more importantly, we need to extend the problem to functions, which are not normalized, the integral over R^n is not one. We have considered the linear quadratic case with this framework, and it was convincing that the normalization was important. The lifting procedure preserves the normalization, while using a Hilbert space as the basic argument space. We have developed intensively this set up, and presented results in a couple of papers. Unfortunately, we met unexpected hurdles. The first one is the collision of probability spaces. Indeed, the Hilbert space of square integrable random variables captures the uncertainty of the initial condition. However, the evolution of the state carries additional uncertainties, and we cannot avoid describing the correlation between the noises. Therefore, we cannot take the state space as any Hilbert space. This difficulty can be handled. However, we met a more serious one. When we differentiate twice on the Hilbert space, the synthetic advantage of the Hilbert space becomes a difficulty. The theory works nicely in the Hilbert space, but when we want to interpret the result in terms of the original problem, it does not work anymore, unless we remain at a formal level. This is excluded, since the introduction of the Hilbert space was for developing a smooth theory, and not to be formal. We worked a lot on this issue, but could not overcome it. After long efforts, we found a new approach. This new approach preserves the Hilbert space advantage, however changing the Hilbert space, and at the same time applies simply to the original problem. In other words, our discovery is that it is possible to embed the original problem into a problem, which can be formulated on a state space, which is a Hilbert space. Consequently, we obtain a rigorous theory for a more general problem, which covers the original one. We believe that this discovery is innovative, because it has not been presented in the literature. The cost in time has reduced the possibility of progressing in the partial information set up, which was our first objective. The theory so far is developed in the full information case. It represents a substantial contribution to this framework, alongside what has been done directly with the Wasserstein space. We certainly intend to address the partial information set up, after the closure of this grant. We have addressed the partial information set up in a particular case, which was our second objective. The classical stochastic control problem under partial information can be formulated as a control problem for Zakai equation, whose solution is the unnormalized conditional probability distribution of the state of the system, which is not directly accessible. Zakai equation is a stochastic Fokker-Planck equation. Therefore, the mathematical problem to be solved is very similar to that met in Mean Field Control theory. Since Mean Field Control theory is posterior to the development of Stochastic Control with partial information, the tools, techniques and concepts obtained in the last decade, for Mean Field Games and Mean field type Control theory, have not been used for the control of Zakai equation. With the power of these new tools, we have obtained new insights for the problem of stochastic control with partial information. We have obtained in this way an extension of the separation principle. This is surprising because the separation principle has been the object of intensive researches in the eighties and nineties. It was believed that this domain was fully covered. One must add that this extension necessitates an algorithm, which is much more elaborate than the Kalman filter, used in the standard formulation of the separation principle. In addition, in the context of applications, we have considered the so-called extended mean field control problem. Extended means that the probability distribution of the control enters in the model, alongside the probability distribution of the state. We have also studied another type of application, regarding risk management. The problem of risk management in stochastic control was outstanding, before mean field type control theory.

11303316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303316.value: Our first major finding concerns the way to implement the Hilbert space formulation of mean field games and mean field control, as an alternative to the natural approach of using the Wasserstein space of probability distributions. There were two concepts in the literature. The first one is simply to work with probability measures, which have densities with respect to the Lebesgue measure. The second one consists in implementing the idea of P.L. Lions, to associate to a probability distribution a random variable, and to work with the Hilbert space of square integrable random variables. This is the lifting method. These two approaches have advantages and drawbacks. We have found a third one, which keeps the advantages of the lifting approach, without the drawbacks. It is innovative, because it never appeared in the literature, and is quite promising. For lack of time, we have used it only in the case of full information, and not yet in the case of partial information. A second major finding concerns stochastic control with partial information. We have formulated the problem as a mean field type control problem, and used tools from this theory, which are available now. We were happy to obtain new results for the separation principle. This had been a very active domain of research in the nineties, and it was considered that all possible results were known. Mean field theory introduces new ideas and therefore new interesting results. Basically, we extended the domain of applicability of the separation principle, which is important. We also obtained significant results of Mean field control in applications. One concerns Risk Management. In the standard theory of stochastic control, the payoff, which is optimized, is always an average of the random cost. The average excludes the possibility of addressing risks. That would mean, at least, to take account of the variance of the random cost. Stochastic Control cannot handle higher moments. Mean Field Control can. This allows extending major relevant problems of economics and finance. A second important application concerns economic and management problems, where prices are defined endogenously and not exogenously. We have, in particular, considered the case of an energy grid, with solar panels. It is a situation where consumers can also be producers, and thus the price of electricity results from an equilibrium. We need extended mean field control to solve the problem. Another application concerns the management of exhaustible resources.

11303316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303316.value: The potential for further development is tremendous, both on the theory side and on the application side. From the results that we have obtained, we envisage the following extensions. Our Hilbert space method will be extended to the so-called common noise situation and to the partial information situation. For the separation principle, we believe that we can obtain results in many new situations. It will remain to consider situations where the separation principle does not hold. A general stochastic maximum principle can be obtained. On the application side, there is a huge potential for pricing management and endogenous prices. This is particularly motivated by special networks. However mean field type control raises an important issue, that of time consistency. In other words, the solution, which is obtained, depends on initial conditions, and not just on the current conditions, like in standard stochastic control theory. There is an interesting area of research, which is to optimize within the set of time consistent controls. We have started to look in this direction, in the domain of Risk Management. It is quite interesting to compare the solutions. Extended control has also a great potential for new research topics.

11303316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303316.value: Mean field games and mean field type control theory are extensions of stochastic control and differential games, with a lot of potential. The general idea is to apply concepts well known in physics, and deemed very useful, to social and economic sciences. The objective is to study the systemic risk, and more generally the influence on decisions of a large community of agents, with characteristics similar to the decision-maker. This impact is in general discarded, because of its complexity. Note that this is different from equilibrium theory in economics. In equilibrium theory, one takes decisions based on market prices. These prices reflect the interactions between all players, but they remain external to the agent, unlike in the mean field theory, in which the effect of the large community is endogenous. This theory is popular in many other domains, like traffic congestion, consumer behavior, or information technology. We have developed the applications to pricing management, in which prices are defined endogenously, and not exogenously as done usually. It turns out that the mathematical apparatus is able to handle problems of Risk Management. This is the situation where we want to optimize simultaneously the average and the variance of a random outcome.

11303616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303616.value: 作為一類在一些重要物理情形出現的典型現象 （如氣狀星體， 具有摩擦阻尼的可壓縮流體及淺水波)，聲速在氣體－真空介面附近為1/2-Holder 但非Lipschitz连续的物理真空奇性由于在物理上的重要性及非線性偏微分方程理論上的挑戰性，近年來受到極大關注。然而，由於在物理真空奇性下可壓縮Euler及Euler-Poisson方程在真空態附近高度蛻化，由Friedrichs-Lax-Kato發展的對稱雙曲組標準方法不再適用, 從而在研究上帶來極度挑戰， 對於氣體－真空介面自由邊界問題， 即使局部存在性也是近來才建立。 現有光滑解存在性理論多為短時間性質。據項目主持人所知， 僅有的關於光滑解或強解的時間整體結果限於帶耗散（如摩擦阻尼或粘性）的可壓等熵流體， 例如對於帶阻尼的等熵Euler方程由項目主持人及曾的一維結果及曾的三維球對稱結果， 由項目主持人，辛及曾的關於氣狀星體三維等熵Navier-Stokes-Poisson方程的球對稱解結果。 上述結果的分析強烈地依賴於由阻尼或粘性的耗散而引起的衰減。然而， 由於缺乏耗散機制，我們不能期望帶物理真空奇性的氣狀星體可壓縮Euler-Poisson方程自由邊界問題光滑解的整體存在性。可期望的最好結果為幾乎整體存在性。事實上，如果初始流不假設為無旋流， 因為渦度沒有衰減機制，我們甚至不能期望光滑解的幾乎整體存在性。氣狀星體的非旋轉平衡解由Lane-Emden方程給出， 關於其性質及穩定性的深入研究出現在天體物理文獻中。Lane-Emden解的一個特徵行為是在真空態附近的物理奇性。這是研究帶物理真空奇性的氣體－真空介面自由邊界問題的動機。本項目主要研究當初值為Lane-Emden解的小擾動時，三維帶物理真空奇性的氣狀星體可壓縮無旋流Euler-Poisson方程氣體－真空介面自由邊界問題的幾乎整體存在性。 第一部分將首先研究等熵流球對稱解的幾乎整體存在性，進而擴展到一般三維無旋流動。在本項目第二部分， 我們將研究非等熵流。因為熵的梯度只是隨著流線傳輸而不衰減，從等熵到非等熵情形的擴展極為不平凡。在本項目中， 除了由於所研究的偏微分方程在真空態附近的高度蛻化及非線性導致的分析上的困難外， 另一個主要問題為控制自由邊界的幾何。一般而言， 這一問題是流體自由邊界問題的一個極大挑戰。

11303616.label: Realisation of objectives
11303616.value: The objectives of this project are to investigate the large time existence (almost global or even global if possible) of solution to the gas-vacuum free boundary problem with physical singularity for gaseous stars modelled by PDEs of compressible Euler and related equations with physical effects of fields satisfying the Poisson equation, and study the role played by the variations of the entropy to the long time existence of solutions (e.g. almost global or global ) and evolution of the free boundaries. They fall in the broaden context of understanding the behavior of solutions of fluid equations with boundary effects, in particular, the free boundaries, and some related physical effects such as grivation, electric, magnetic and heat conductivity. Those physical effects are all important to the evolution of gaseous stars. First, the PI investigated the problem of the vacuum free boundary problem of gaseous stars, with the viscosity and variable transported entropy and thus non-isentropic. The global existence of strong solutions capturing the physical vacuum singularity was proved in the spherically symmetric case with nonlinear asymptotic stability of the stationary solution. In the special case that the entropy is a constant, the stationary solution reduces to the Lane-Emden solution. The results published on J. Differential Equations 265 (2018), no. 1, 177–236. The PI and his collaborators first studied the existence and properties of stationary solutions with variable entropy and physical vacuum singularity, by the shooting (time-map) method, and improved the previous result of the PI and J. Smoller obtained in Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 173 (2004), no. 3, 345–377. In order to prove the long time existence of solutions, we first adopted the Lagrangian formulation to reduce the free boundary problem to a fixed boundary problem restricted to the domain of the stationary solution using the mass conservation in the evolution. It was essential to build up uniform in time regularity near the vacuum states, by which the large time asymptotic uniform convergence of the vacuum free boundary capturing the physical singularity, density and velocity to those of the stationary solution was established. Compared with the isentropic case, the pressure for the variable entropy case depends on both the density and entropy, and the stationary density loses the monotonicity. These facts give rise to difficulties in the analysis. We used the stationary pressure, instead of the density, to characterize the degenerate boundary behavior of physical vacuum singularity in establishing the high order regularity uniform up to the vacuum boundary. The role of variable entropy played to the long time regularity of solutions near vacuum boundaries is realized by incorporating it in the higher order energy functional. This activity and the obtained results directly addressed the objective of the project. In order to understand the effects of the Poission term and physical boundary to the global existence of smooth solutions in the objective of the project. The PI investigated an initial boundary value problem for both compressible Euler-Poisson and Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in three spatial dimensions. In the spherical symmetry case, the global existence of solutions to compressible viscous equations with the Poisson term was proved with the large initial data. Without symmetry assumption, the global existence of smooth solutions for small data for both compressible Euler-Poisson equations and Navier-Stokes-Poisson with physicalboundary conditions was also established. The obtained results published in J. Differential Equations 269 (2020), no. 11, 9936–10001. One of the objectives of the project is to understand the long time existence of smooth irrotational flow solutions in three spatial dimensions. The role of irrotationality of flow to the long time existence of solutions was carefully studied for PDEs of thermal nonequilibrium gas dynamics for which the variable entropy evolves. The PDEs investigated here generalize the classical compressible Euler-equations to more realistic case. As one of is one of the objectives of the project , the time-evolution of entropy and its role to the long time existence of smooth solutions is investigated here too, The global existence of smooth equations of the three-dimensional irrotational flow was proved established, by establishing the uniform bound on derivatives of the entropy. Moreover, for those equations, in the presence of physical boundaries, the global existence and large time behavior of solutions are also obtained in one-dimensional case. Those results published in Ann. Inst. H. Poincare Anal. Non Lineaire 37 (2020), no. 1, 225–238. and J. Differential Equations 265 (2018), no. 5, 1875–1893. Understanding the evolution of free boundaries of Euler equations with physical stability conditions on the free boundary and some physical effects is a main issue of the project. For this purpose, the PI investigated for the free boundary problem of incompressible Euler equations of fluids coupled with magnetic fields. It should be noted that the magnetic field is an important physical effect of gaseous stars, contributing to many physical phenomena of gaseous stars such as solar flare. In this project, we showed the ill-posedness of the free boundary problem in two dimensions if the stability condition does is violated. This condition plays very similar role to the physical vacuum condition. This result published in Comm. Math. Phys. 376 (2020), no. 1, 259–286. The heat-conductivity is an important driving force to motions of fluid free boundaries of gaseous star. As noted in the paper “ N. R. Lebovitz, On the fluid dynamics of evolving stars}, Proc. Roy. Soc. London Ser. A 375 (1981), 249—269”, the heat-conductivity plays a crucial role to driving the evolution of a star in the phase of secular evolution. The heat-conductivity contributes to the variation of entropy both in time and space, and the evolution of the free boundaries, an issue to address in the project. For this, when the flow is highly supersonic and inviscid, the PI and his collaborator obtained the a priori estimates for geometric quantities of free boundaries and the Sobolev norms of fluid variables by investigating the coupling of the boundary geometry and the interior solutions. In this work, the PI and his collaborator developed and extended the geometric approaches, in particular, the one introduced by Christodoulou and Lindblad, to fluid free boundary problems losing more derivatives than the usual cases. This work is submitted and under review. In summary, most of the research results of this project have been published in important international journals. The objectives in the project have been successfully achieved. New analytic and geometric techniques are developed, which should be useful to the related problems of nonlinear fluids PDEs.

11303616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303616.value: For a vacuum free boundary problem of gaseous star, with the viscosity variable transported entropy and thus non-isentropic, the global existence of strong solutions capturing the physical vacuum singularity is proved in the spherically symmetric case. The nonlinear asymptotic stability of the stationary solution is also proved. In the special case that the entropy is a constant, the stationary solution reduces to the Lane-Emden solution. The results published on J. Differential Equations 265 (2018), no. 1, 177–236. The initial boundary value problems for both compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson and Euler-Poisson equations are considered on exterior domains. With the radial symmetry assumption, the global existence of solutions to compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations with the large initial data on a domain exterior to a ball in is proved. Moreover, without any symmetry assumption, the global existence of smooth solutions near a given constant steady state for both compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson and Euler-Poisson equations on an exterior domain in with physical boundary conditions is also established with the exponential stability. The equations considered can be used to model plasmas. The results published in J. Differential Equations 269 (2020), no. 11, 9936–10001. For gas dynamics equations in thermal nonequilibrium, the global existence and large time behavior of the classical solution to the Cauchy problem of the three-dimensional irrotational flow are established when the initial data are near the equilibrium state with an additional L1-norm bound. It should be noted the variable entropy does not decay. The uniform bound on derivatives of the entropy is obtained by using the a priori decay-in-time estimate on the velocity. For those equations, in the presence of physical boundaries, the global existence and large time behavior of solutions are also obtained in one-dimensional case. Those results published in Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire 37 (2020), no. 1, 225–238. and J. Differential Equations 265 (2018), no. 5, 1875–1893. For the free boundary problem of incompressible Euler equations of fluids coupled with magnetic fields modelling incompressible ideal magnetohydrodynamics, we show the ill-posedness in two spatial dimensions if the stability condition does not hold. This result published in Comm. Math. Phys. 376 (2020), no. 1, 259–286. For the free surface problem of highly subsonic heat-conducting inviscid flow in 2-D and 3-D, a priori estimates for geometric quantities and the Sobolev norms of fluid variables are proved by investigating the coupling of the boundary geometry and the interior solutions. This work is submitted and under review.

11303616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303616.value: For vacuum free boundary problems of gaseous stars with physical singularity, some other additional physical effects can be considered, for example, the effects of magnetic fields. In fact, magnetic fields are important to many interesting physical phenomena , for example, solar flare. However, there has been no well-posedness theory available of vacuum free boundary problems with physical singularity for compressible magnetohydrodynamics, to the best knowledge of the PI. For the free boundary problems for fluids (gas or incompressible fluids), it is important to consider the long-time existence and behavior of solutions without irrotational assumptions, to understand the role of vorticity, which in general does not decay for fluids equations without dissipations. Entropy is a very subtle concept near vacuum states, further understanding are needed. For the interface problems with interfaces separating compressible and incompressible fluids, it is important to investigate the well-posedness or ill-posedness of problems.

11303616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303616.value: The free boundary problems in fluids are challenging and important in many physical situation, such as in gaseous stars, water waves and magnetohydrodynamics. Those problems arise naturally in physics, astrophysics, engineering, medical sciences and etc. The study of those free boundary problems poses great challenges in both theoretical investigation and numerical simulations. It is in particular so to investigate long time existence and behavior of solutions. The system of partial differential equations of gaseous materials is highly degenerate near vacuum states. New ideas and techniques are needed to develop to solve those problems. Entropy is a very subtle issue in thermal dynamics, this is in particular the case near vacuum states. Part of this project is to understand the time evolution of variable entropy and its spatial derivatives. Those are non time-decay quantities which cause difficulties to establish the long time existence of solutions to the related problems. Some analytical ideas and techniques developed in this project should be useful to the related problems of nonlinear partial differential equations with free boundaries and fixed physical boundaries.

11310716.value: 計算真正的射影簇的同源性

11310716.label: Project Objectives
11310716.value: The only objective of this proposal is to design and analyze a new algorithm to compute the homology (Betti numbers and torsion coefficients) of a real projective variety given by a family of homogeneous polynomials. Algorithms to do this task already exist. But they are inefficient (the only explicit upper bound on their performance is doubly exponential in the number n of variables of the defining polynomials) and suspect of numerical instability when finite precision is used. The goal of our proposal is to design an algorithm that should be more efficient (hopefully its dependence on n will be single exponential) and numerically stable.

11310716.label: Realisation of objectives
11310716.value: The project only objective was completely achieved. Even though we originally set a deadline of 36 months for this completion we managed to do so in substantially less time. The main publication of the project (a 42-pages-long article in the highly prestigious journal "Foundations of Computational Mathematics") is not yet published on paper, it has already appeared online. A second article (in the Chinese Annals of Mathematics) has already been published. We therefore found that there is no reason to delay the submission of this completion report.
