rows: The only objective of this proposal is to design and analyze a new algorithm to compute the homology (Betti numbers and torsion coefficients) of a real projective variety given by a family of homogeneous polynomials. Algorithms to do this task already exist. But they are inefficient (the only explicit upper bound on their performance is doubly exponential in the number n of variables of the defining polynomials) and suspect of numerical instability when finite precision is used. The goal of our proposal is to design an algorithm that should be more efficient (hopefully its dependence on n will be single exponential) and numerically stable.

11310716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11310716.value: In the 1970s an algorithm called Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition was proposed that solved many computational problems in real algebraic geometry in a time that was doubly exponential in the dimension of the ambient space. Then, in the 1990s a new algorithm, known as the Critical Point Method, allowed to find single exponential time for most of the problems above. Among those for which the Critical Point Method failed to improve the complexity is the computation of homology groups (of real algebraic varieties). The main result in our project presents a new algorithm, based neither on Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition nor on the Critical Points Method, which computes these homology groups. Outside a set of input data of a vanishingly (i.e., exponentially) small measure, our algorithm works in single exponential time. That is, outside of this (essentially negligible) set, it works exponentially faster than all previous algorithms.

11310716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11310716.value: A possible extension of this result would be to sets defined by both polynomial equalities and inequalities (basic semialgebraic sets). We have applied for a GRF grant with this subject, which has been funded, and we are now progressing in this direction.

11310716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11310716.value: In many applications, we are interested in understanding the "shape" of a set. When the set lives in 3-dimensional space, a picture can help us but when the set lives in higher dimensional space, we need to do so analytically. Mathematicians developed a collection of formal objects (called Homotopy groups) that provide the most relevant information about this shape. In our project we have designed an algorithm that computes this objects (for a reasonably large family of sets) which works much faster than any previous algorithm for the same problem.

11319516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11319516.value: Cancer cells from solid tumors can disseminate into bloodstream and circulate either as single migratory circulating tumor cells (CTCs) or as multicellular clusters (CTC clusters) with highly metastatic ability. Technologies for detection, isolation and analysis of CTCs and CTC clusters will enable a broad range of clinical applications including prediction of drug response, monitoring of treatment outcomes, and early detection of recurrence. DNA mutation analysis of drug targets on single cells from CTCs and CTC clusters may also reveal the heterogeneity in metastatic tumors for precise selection of target-based drugs. However, there is a lack of techniques for capturing CTCs and CTC clusters from blood or other bodily fluids (such as plural fluid or ascites), for isolating single tumor cells from CTC and CTC clusters, and for analyzing target mutations and drug sensitivities. In our previous research and preliminary experiments, we have demonstrated the feasibility of using microfluidics to seize cells and cell clusters, to separate individual cells, and to carry out single cell mutation analysis. In this project, we propose to develop an integrated microfluidic system for capturing, isolating, and culturing single tumor cells from CTCs and CTC clusters for mutation analysis and drug sensitivity test at single cell level. Specifically, we will design and optimize three individual microfluidic modules, each with the functions of trapping and releasing CTCs and CTC clusters by varying gap dimensions in the channel and controlling flow directions, isolating single tumor cells from captured CTCs and CTC clusters by microvalves and filtering out non-cancerous cells, and testing dose-dependent response of anti-tumor drugs on single cells cultured in microwells, respectively. We will also integrate the three modules into one single platform once they are optimized and validated. The microfluidic system will provide an important tool for quantitative identification and analysis of CTCs and CTC clusters at single cell level, which will enable more precise clinical decision in treating cancer, and better understanding of the roles of CTCs and CTC clusters and intra-tumor heterogeneity in progression and metastasis of solid tumors. 本项目的目标是开发微流控芯片技术用于单细胞基因突变分析和循环肿瘤细胞药敏测试，包括微流控芯片捕捉循环肿瘤细胞和细胞簇，分离单细胞及分析单细胞基因突变，和测试肿瘤细胞药物敏感性。本项目的成果可应用于癌症的精准医疗。

11319516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11319516.value: In this project, three individual microfluidic modules have been designed and optimized, each with the functions of trapping and releasing CTCs and CTC clusters by varying gap dimensions in the channel and controlling flow directions, isolating single tumor cells from captured CTCs and CTC clusters by microvalves and filtering out non-cancerous cells, and testing dose-dependent response of anti-tumor drugs on single cells cultured in microwells, respectively. The microfluidic system for quantitative identification and analysis of CTCs and CTC clusters at single cell level were demonstrated. We developed a microvalve-based microfluidic module to isolate single tumor cells from captured CTCs and CTC clusters. Aarc-edge-cross-section monolithic valves (AMVs) chips were designed and fabricated, and large-scale liquid control for single cell detection, a sequence of microparticle manipulation processes for single cell isolation were well demonstrated. A single cell mutation analysis based on the designed microfluidic platform were also performed in this project. We used the single cancer cell isolation chip to retrieve individual lung cancer cells for mutation detection. For the clinical sample analysis, 5/20 and 4/20 cells carried L858R and T790M mutation, respectively, while 11/20 cells carried double mutation. The detection of T790M in the clinical sample to be associated with its drug-resistance status. The presence of both signal and double mutations in one pleural effusion sample clearly indicated the tumor mutation heterogeneity and may provide insight into the evolution of mutation spectrum. Please refer to Part C the publications part in detail. To achieve an integrated and high-throughput single-cell detection platform, we developed an efficient droplet-based microfluidic platform for manipulation and subsequent analysis of CTCs at single cell level. Real time RT-PCR was further carried out for H827 cell line and H1975 cell line based on the developed platform. The results showed H827 cell line occurred EGFR DEL mutation, while H1975 cell line was negative. Please refer to the Unpublished works part in detail.

11319516.value: In summary, we have developed three individual microfluidic modules, each with the functions of trapping and releasing CTCs and CTC clusters by varying gap dimensions in the channel and controlling flow directions, isolating single tumor cells from captured CTCs and CTC clusters by microvalves and filtering out non-cancerous cells. We further developed an efficient droplet-based microfluidic platform for capturing and isolating single tumor cells from CTCs and CTC clusters for mutation analysis at single cell level. Specifically, The microfluidic system for quantitative identification and analysis of CTCs and CTC clusters at single cell level were demonstrated, which enables more precise clinical decision in treating cancer, and better understanding of the roles of CTCs and CTC clusters and intra-tumor heterogeneity in progression and metastasis of solid tumors.

11320016.label: Project Objectives
11320016.value: To investigate the stability and instability criteria on the shear flow for both viscous and thermal layers in both 2D and 3D settings; To obtain stability and instability analysis on background states other than shear flow.

11320016.label: Realisation of objectives
11320016.value: The two objectives have been fully addressed and the research results were written in four research papers published/accepted by international refereed journals that including Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics, Journal of European Mathematical Society. Precisely, the stability and instability criteria for viscous and thermal layers are investigated under the influence of the self-induced magnetic field governed by either compressible or incompressible MHD systems. In some more general setting, the well-posedness of the boundary layer systems was considered in Gevrey function space with optimal Gevrey index implied by the instability analysis. More detail of the research results can be found in Section 6.1 about the major finding and research outcome.

11320016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11320016.value: In this project, we study the stability and instability of the boundary layers of fluid dynamics. The research results have been written in four research papers published in CPAM, JEMS, SIMA and JDE. Precisely, we first study the well-posedness theory for the MHD boundary layer. The boundary layer equations are governed by the Prandtl type equations that are derived from the incompressible MHD system with no-slip boundary condition on the velocity and perfectly conducting condition on the magnetic field. Under the assumption that the initial tangential magnetic field is not zero, we establish the local-in-time existence, uniqueness of solution for the nonlinear MHD boundary layer equations. This justifies the physical understanding that the magnetic field has a stabilizing effect on MHD boundary layer in rigorous mathematics. In the second paper, we study the well-posedness of the Prandtl system without monotonicity and analyticity assumption. Precisely, for any index in [3/2, 2], we obtain the local in time well-posedness in the space of Gevrey class in the tangential variable and Sobolev class in the normal variable so that the monotonicity condition on the tangential velocity is not needed to overcome the loss of tangential derivative. This answers the open question raised in the paper of D. Gerard-Varet and N. Masmoudi. The third paper aims to justify the high Reynolds numbers limit for the MHD system with Prandtl boundary layer expansion when no-slip boundary condition is imposed on velocity field and perfectly conducting wall condition on magnetic field. Under the assumption that the viscosity and resistivity coefficients are of the same order and the initial tangential magnetic field on the boundary is not degenerate, we justify the validity of the Prandtl boundary layer expansion. In the fourth paper, we are concerned with the motion of electrically conducting fluid governed by the two-dimensional non-isentropic viscous compressible MHD system on the half plane, with no-slip condition for velocity field, perfect conducting condition for magnetic field and Dirichlet boundary condition for temperature on the boundary. When the viscosity, heat conductivity and magnetic diffusivity coefficients tend to zero in the same rate, there is a boundary layer that is described by a Prandtl-type system. By applying a coordinate transformation in terms of stream function as motivated by the work on the incompressible MHD system, under the non-degeneracy condition on the tangential magnetic field, we obtain the local-in-time well-posedness of the boundary layer system in weighted Sobolev spaces.

11320016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11320016.value: The stability and instability study on fluid motion has a long history and many interesting and challenging mathematical problems remained unsolved. With the understanding on the well-posedness theories of the Prandtl equation in Gevrey function space with optimal index and the stability and instability analysis on the MHD system obtained in this project, one natural question is about the well-posedness of the boundary layer system for MHD without any structural assumption in Gevrey function space with optimal index, and the related justification of the vanishing viscosity and/or resistivity limits.

11320016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11320016.value: There is tremendous progress on the study on the Navier-Stokes equations either compressible or incompressible that describe the viscous fluid motion satisfying the conservation of mass, momentum and energy even though the Millennium problems on the Navier-Stokes equations about the existence with large data in three space dimensional space remains unsolved. On the other hand, the study on vanishing viscosity limit to inviscid fluid model such as Euler equations is important in physics, but challenging in mathematics, in particular, with no-slip boundary condition because of the lack of sufficient understanding on the boundary layer that governed by the Prandtl system. This project focuses on the stability and instability of boundary layer solution to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary condition that is governed by systems in the same spirit of Prandtl system derived from incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. We expect the mathematical theories developed in this project can be applied to explain some phenomena in fluid motion with boundary in physics.

11326016.label: Project Objectives
11326016.value: To verify the newly established photocharge-modulated photoemission spectroscopy (PMPES) and determine limits and scope of this technique. The energy change in charge-transfer state (measured with and without xenon lamp irradiation) of different donor/acceptor (D/A) pairs would be experimentally examined. These results will be comparing with charge-transfer exciton binding energy (EBCT) obtained from theoretical calculation and other reported results. To determine how the EBCT at a D/A junction can be affected by the junction properties (e.g. local charge transfer, energy level alignment and charge coupling, etc.). Successful implementation of this objective will give insight on designing and engineering of OPV devices with D/A junctions of small EBCT values so as to minimize the Voc loss in the OPV devices. To determine how the EBCT can be affected by device structure. For example, the effect of doping, formation of bulk heterojunction, work function tuning of the electrode will be studied. Results obtained from this objective would provide knowledge for minimizing loss in Voc and enhancing performance of OPV devices.

11326016.label: Realisation of objectives
11326016.value: In this reporting period, we have 1) demonstrated the validity of photocharge-modulated photoemission spectroscopy (PMPES) measurement; 2) studied charge-transfer exciton binding energy (EBCT) of donor / acceptor junctions; 3) studied how these energies can be affected by the device structures. Demonstrate the validity of PMPES Energy offset at the donor (D)/acceptor (A) interfaces play an important role on charge separation in organic photovoltaics (OPV). Its magnitude determines the charge separation process under illumination. Extensive studies have been carried out for elucidating the charge transfer (CT) process at different D/A junctions. It is expected that electronic structures and the charge behaviors at D/A interface should be different under photoexcitation, yet there is so far no direct experimental approach for probing the changes in electronic structures (i.e. Fermi level, vacuum level (VL), frontier molecular orbitals, etc.) upon photoexcitation. In this project, we successfully demonstrated that a PMPES system can probe the charge distributions and electronic interactions for different D/A heterojunctions under photoexcitation. In particular, CT states formation as a result of charge transfer at the copper phthalocyanine (CuPc)/ fullerene(C60) junction has been studied. Subsequent superposition of charge transfer and electron polarization effect increase the CuPc/C60 energy level offsets from 0.75 (ground state measured in dark) to 1.07eV (high lying state measured upon illumination). This energy change (~0.3 eV) is also verified with theoretical calculation. We showed that there is excess energy consumed for a subtle change in the energy level alignment of the CuPc/C60 junction under light illumination, suggesting a new insight for energy loss mechanism during the photocharge generation processes. The above results have been accepted for publication in ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces. (ref 1) Binding energy for different D / A system Apart from conventional D/A systems, D/ D or A/ A systems are also selected in current studies. For example, SubNc/SubPc OPV devices were found to exhibit much higher performance comparing to conventional D/A devices. To this end, PMPES studies are carried out on the SubNc/SubPc interface to examine its electronic structures. (Raw data included in mid-term report.) In our PMPES measurement, SubNc/SubPc shows Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO)- Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (LUMO) energy changes upon illumination. Yet, the energy offsets obtained from the PMPES do not show a strong correlation with their promising performance. To this end, we have further studied their physical and optical properties by using a hybrid modeling/experimental approach. This result further confirms that SubNc/SubPc does not work on the conventional P/N junction mechanism. This obtained result is consistent with our PMPES results showing that SubNc/SubPc behaves differently with CuPc/C60 heterojunction upon illumination. We conclude that SubNc and SubPc are in fact bipolar semiconductors capable of generating free carriers upon photoexcitation. The above works have been published in “Advanced Materials, 29, 1606909 (2017)” (ref 2). The effect of doping on binding energy in D/A system. There is a lack of the studies on Frankel excitons in actual blend devices, resulting in an incomplete understanding on the photovoltaic processes in organic electronic materials. To determine how the EBCT can be affected by device structures, effects of doping are investigated. The polarizability of Frankel exciton in both pristine donor and D:A blend films are studied. We observed that the polarizability of excitonic states in pristine donors can be dramatically increased when they are mixed with the n-type acceptor. We showed that the polarizability of Frankel excitons has direct correlation with the measured dielectric constant of the bulk heterojunction thin films. Our findings uncover the difference between the nature of Frankel exciton in pristine donor and that in D:A blend systems, revealing an important role of excitonic states on its dielectric constant (or EBCT) in OPV devices. This result is consistent with our PMPES findings, where polarizability changes induced by D:A mixing results in energy level offsets in the pristine donor film. Furthermore, the change in charge transfer state using different structures and measurement conditions are explored. The above works have been published in “ACS applied materials & interfaces 2018, 10 (8), 7256-7262” (ref 3) and “ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2020, 12 (33), 37384–37390” (ref 4). Other related work: Knowledge and insight from the above works have been further applied to perovskites solar cells. By modulating the charge interaction organic cations and inorganic layer in perovskite, minimizing their charge transfer energy, efﬁcient charge separation are achieved in both of the 1D and 2D perovskite. Above works have been published in “Adv. Mater. 2018, 30 (22), 1800710” (ref 5) and “J. Mater. Chem. A 2019, 7 (15), 8811-8817” (ref 6)

11326016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11326016.value: In this project, a PMPES system has been established to study the charge distributions and electronic interactions for D/A heterojunctions under photoexcitation. In particular, we observed CT states formed as a result of photocharge transfers at the CuPc/C60 junction. Subsequent superposition of charge transfer and electron polarization effects increase the D/A energy level offsets from 0.75 (ground state measured in dark) to 1.07eV (high lying state measured upon illumination). We showed that there is excess energy consumed for a subtle change in the energy level alignment of the CuPc/C60 junction under illumination, suggesting a new insight for energy loss mechanism during the photocharge generation processes. (Ref 1: Accepted by ACS applied materials & interfaces) By using a hybrid modeling/experimental approach (i.e. PMPES, theoretical calculation and device analysis), we found that the change in energy level upon illumination has an important implication to their charge transfer energy, which is a major cause for the Voc loss in general OPV devices. We also demonstrated that SubNc and SubPc can directly generate free carriers upon photoexcitation. Photoresponse of the SubNc/SubPc system is investigated and compared with other conventional OPV systems. (Ref 2: Advanced Materials, 29, 1606909 (2017) The effects of doping on binding energy in D/A system have been further investigated. We observed that the polarizability of excitonic states in pristine donors can be dramatically increased when they are mixed with the n-type acceptor. Also, the polarizability of Frankel excitons has direct correlation with the measured dielectric constant of the bulk heterojunction thin films. This result is consistent with our PMPES findings, where polarizability changes induced by D:A mixing results in energy level offsets in the pristine donor films. Furthermore, changes in charge transfer states in different structures and measurement conditions have also been explored. (Ref 3: ACS applied materials & interfaces 2018, 10 (8), 7256-7262 and Ref 4: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2020, 12 (33), 37384–37390. The obtained knowledge is further applied to perovskite devices. Different organic cations are selected to tune the binding energies of 2D perovskites (Ref 5: Adv. Mater. 2018, 30 (22), 1800710). Solar cells based on 1D perovskite also shows reduced exciton binding energy (Ref 6: J. Mater. Chem. A 2019, 7 (15), 8811-8817). These devices all show enhanced efficiency and stability.

11326016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11326016.value: The new measurement technique developed in this project has been successfully applied to probe electronic structures and charge behaviors in excited state upon illumination. As only a low-cost light source is need for modifying a conventional ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy (UPS) system. It is expected that the present approach would have wide applications for studying organic semiconductors under photoexcitation. However, the present approach does have limitation for studying fast dynamic processes due to the slow response time of most conventional UPS detectors. It is expected that the present approach can be further extended to studying dynamic processes by replacing the conventional detector with an ultra-fast detector or adding a pump-probe laser source.

11326016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11326016.value: Performance of many organic optoelectronic devices including OPV devices depends critically on properties of junctions formed between donors and acceptors in the devices. In many D/A junctions, CT state would be formed by electron transfer from a D molecule to an A molecule. Before excitation, the electron-hole pair in the CT state is bound by Columbic attraction. Upon excitation, they can separate as free carriers. However, there is so far no direct experimental approach for probing the changes in electronic structures (i.e. Fermi level, VL, frontier molecular orbitals, etc.) upon photoexcitation. Herein, a PMPES system has been developed by adding a solar simulator to a conventional ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy system to study the charge distributions and electronic interactions for a standard D/A heterojunction. With the newly developed equipment, the CT state properties, and the energy level alignment at D/A junction upon illumination have been studied in detail.

11329616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11329616.value: Now that numerical weather prediction is capable of providing accurate forecasts over moderately large scales, there is growing demand for improved forecasts of weather and air quality within cities. However, prediction on the scale of cities is difficult because small-scale heterogeneities such as buildings and pollutant sources (e.g. cars) exert a major influence on the behaviour at larger scales. Since the computational cost of building-resolving atmospheric models is extremely high, routine operational forecasts for a large city like Hong Kong are probably decades away. At present weather and air quality within cities are predicted using coarse-resolution atmospheric models. These models, which at best have a horizontal grid spacing of hundreds of metres, cannot represent urban areas explicitly, for buildings have features that are at least two orders of magnitude smaller. Consequently the effects of urban areas, e.g. that of buildings on winds, are modelled using urban canopy parameterisations (UCPs). Yet despite concerted efforts to improve their realism, current UCPs do not perform significantly better than simple bulk parameterisations that prescribe the velocity profile according to land use and roughness. Better UCPs are required. One possible explanation for the modest performance of the more sophisticated UCPs is that they model urban winds by analogy to molecular diffusion. This implies a single lengthscale or mixing length for the turbulent velocity field. Such an approach is questionable for urban flows, which change greatly with scale: there are major differences, for example, between winds on the scale of streets and neighbourhoods. Modelling small, subgrid scales in a way that respects the scale-dependence of urban winds should yield more accurate results. Multiscale methods have been developed to accomplish this in fluid dynamics and applied mathematics. This proposal describes a new multiscale approach to UCPs. Urban-scale turbulence will be parameterised using the energy transfer between resolved scales and distinguished subgrid-scale wavebands corresponding to specific flow features. Urban-scale passive pollutants will be parameterised using systematic coarse-graining over small scales. Data for the parameterisations will be obtained from building-resolving large-eddy simulations and discrete orthogonal wavelets. On the theoretical side, the proposal will introduce a new parameterisation framework and contribute to basic understanding of energy transfer in inhomogeneous urban domains; on the practical side, UCPs tailored to specific building geometries will be derived and tested within WRF, a popular atmospheric model. The long term impacts will include interdisciplinary research on urban parameterisation and improved forecasts of urban weather and air quality. 當前，數值天氣預報能夠對中尺度或稍大尺度的天氣進行準確的預測，對於提高城市尺度的天氣及空氣質量預報精度的要求而隨之不斷增加。然而，由於小尺度的非均質性，如建築物及污染源的分布（汽車廢氣），對大尺度的行為有很大的影響，城市尺度的預報是十分困難的。而且，求解建築物級精度的大氣模型的計算成本是十分驚人的，對於諸如香港這樣的大城市的常規預報需要數十年的時間，甚至更久。 目前，對城市尺度的天氣及空氣質量的預報主要採用較低網格精度的大氣模型。這類模型的水平網格精度最高也要數百米，對於其建築物尺度至少小兩個數量級的城市區域來說，是無法進行顯式描述的。因此，城市區域的影響，如建築物對風場的作用，主要通過城市冠層參數化方案來模化。盡管在實現和改進該參數化方案方面進行了大量的工作，目前的城市冠層參數化方案與根據土地使用及地表粗糙度而指定風廓線的參數化方案相比並沒有對預報效果起到顯著的改進。更優化的城市冠層參數化方案仍有待研究。 如此複雜的城市冠層參數化方案，其並效果卻並不顯著。一個可能的原因是，其通過類比分子擴散機理對城市風進行模化。這意味著在湍流速度場中需要引入單一尺度或混合尺度。而由於城市流動對尺度具有很強的依變性，如街道尺度與街區尺度的風場存在很大的差異，如上所述的城市冠層參數化方案其有效性尚有待商榷。如果在對小尺度及亞格子尺度進行模化的過程中能夠將城市風與尺度之間的依變關係予以考慮，將會獲得更精確的結果。為解決上述問題，在流體動力學及應用數學領域，多尺度方法應運而生。 該研究計畫為城市冠層參數化的實現提出了一種新的多尺度方法。對於特定的流動特徵，城市尺度的湍流將根據大尺度及亞格子尺度波段之間的能量傳遞予以參數化。城市尺度的被動標量污染物將通過對小尺度粗粒化的方法予以參數化。參數化所需要的數據將通過建築物級精度的大渦模擬以及離散正交小波來獲得。在理論層面上，該研究計畫將引入一種新的參數化框架並有助於理解非均勻城市域內的能量傳輸機理；在應用層面上，將針對特定的建築物拓撲特徵推演出對應的城市冠層參數化方案，並且使用目前頗受歡迎的大氣預報模型WRF予以驗證。該項計畫將涵蓋交叉學科的研究，對改進城市尺度的天氣及空氣質量的預報具有長遠的意義。

11329616.label: Realisation of objectives
11329616.value: The objectives were realised as follows by the following means: 1. Characterisation of interscale interactions. A wavelet formalism for analysing turbulence within the canopy layer of rough-wall boundary layers in general and inhomogeneous urban boundary layers in particular was developed. The great advantage of wavelets is that they allow for the scale dependence to be characterised as a function of location. Wavelets were previously applied to smooth-wall turbulence, in which energy transfers and scale interactions are not impeded by obstacles; the present work extended this to rough-wall boundary layers, for which the notion of scale is ambiguous as the canopy is multiply connected. Following intrinsic averaging in porous media theory, wherein the fluid and the medium may not be easily distinguished, spectra are calculated over domains that include fluid and obstacles. The present analysis of the kinetic energy and nonlinear (interscale) transfer was performed using data from large-eddy simulations (LES) of flow over different obstacle arrays. 2. Development of multiscale eddy viscosity. Leveraging the wavelet formalism of Objective 1, an eddy viscosity was calculated inside the canopy layer from the nonlinear subgrid transfer and kinetic spectra. The effects of scales below a nominal cut-off scale were parameterized by the nonlinear transfer between subgrid and resolved scales. This approach can be applied to a wide range of configurations because it does not rely on a priori assumptions about the turbulence and building geometry. 3. Development of subgrid-scale pollutant model. A subgrid-scale pollutant model was developed using wavelet-based numerical homogenisation. This is a multiscale modelling technique that had not been used in atmospheric science or urban pollutant dispersion. It allows for the effects of unresolved buildings on the resolved pollutant distribution at a given scale to be parameterized through successive coarse graining. The ultimate accuracy of the method, however, depends on the variability of small scales and the extent to which the scalar field is dominated by large-scale structures. Code implementing the numerical homogenisation was written and approximation procedures were developed to facilitate application to mesoscale models with horizontal resolutions of O(100-1000m) and buildings with dimensions of O(10m). 4. Implementation of the multiscale eddy viscosity. The eddy viscosities calculated for Objective 2 were applied to the parameterization of urban areas in an atmospheric mesoscale model, WRF. The multiscale eddy viscosity for an idealized urban geometry and specified cut-off scale (e.g. the horizontal mesoscale resolution) were used to parameterize the dynamics within a certain region or tile. Several implementations in WRF were examined, namely a constant eddy viscosity based on mean velocity and length scales and one allowing for dependence on the resolved mesoscale flow, i.e. a modification of WRF’s existing (Smagorinsky) subgrid-scale scheme to mimic the vertical dependence of the wavelet eddy viscosity. The objectives were fully achieved. 1. Characterisation of interscale interactions. A comprehensive analysis of turbulence statistics for flow over aligned and staggered arrays of identical cubic obstacles was performed. First, spatial averages and standard deviations of the kinetic energy and nonlinear transfer were calculated as a function of scale for different regions (e.g. the entire horizontal plane or the repeating units formed by the array). To complement the energy and transfer spectra, probability distributions of turbulence statistics at different scales were calculated to quantify spatial intermittency. Second, the underlying physical mechanisms were examined. The turbulent kinetic energy budget was analysed in wavelet space in order to link the turbulence structure and spatial intermittency to the inhomogeneous building geometry. 2. Development of multiscale eddy viscosity. Work on this objective extended that of Objective 1. The sensitivity to the cut-off scale and horizontal or vertical locations were quantified for the square and staggered arrays; additional geometries, namely non-uniform arrays and realistic urban topographies, were also examined as part of a student’s PhD thesis. The data covered a sufficiently wide range of horizontal scales (e.g. L=O(256m)) to allow for subgrid (urban) scales of a high-resolution mesoscale model to be parameterized. There was not enough time to repeat the wavelet analysis for a comprehensive range of configurations as each simulation required several months of wall-clock time. The strategy, therefore, was to examine conditions under which the turbulence statistics will be qualitatively unchanged from a regular obstacle array. This was done for different stratifications (i.e. bottom heating or cooling) and wind directions. 3. Development of subgrid-scale pollutant model. Numerical homogenisation was applied to a street canyon and building array. The homogenization procedure, which can be slow on account of the need to invert a large matrix, was optimized through approximation methods that exploit the spatial structure (i.e. periodicity) of the flow. Comparison of reconstructed and original scalar fields indicates that the approximate nonlocal diffusion operators perform acceptably according to standard validation metrics. Deriving separate subgrid-scale pollutant models for a large number of configurations or simulations was not practical. However, analysis of the approximation procedure implied that a comparable level of accuracy will be obtained if the spatial structure (i.e. scale dependence and variability) is similar. Therefore scalar fields for stratified flows and real urban topographies were also considered. 4. Implementation of the multiscale eddy viscosity. The eddy viscosities calculated for Objective 2 were averaged and nondimensionalised for use in the WRF atmospheric mesoscale model. A baseline WRF configuration for Hong Kong (with multiple nested domains, a minimum horizontal resolution of 200 m, and a simple bulk land surface scheme) was verified against meteorological observations from August 2020. Eddy viscosities derived from a square array, which are representative of a densely urbanised region, were applied to Kowloon. The effect of the parameterization on time series of surface winds was verified against observations and the structure of wind field compared to that for the baseline simulation.

11329616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11329616.value: (Reference numbering follows order in Part C.) 1. Characterisation of interscale interactions. We introduced a new wavelet-based methodology for the analysis of turbulence statistics within the urban canopy layer [4]. The conventional approach in fluid dynamics and boundary-layer meteorology is restricted to physical-space statistics. Using orthonormal wavelets, we showed that 1-D and 2-D scales can be meaningfully defined even when kinetic energy and transfer spectra include the obstacles. The analysis of flow over square and staggered arrays reveals that horizontal energy spectra below the obstacle scale obey the -5/3 law, but horizontal transfer spectra are strongly affected by vertical energy exchanges. Differences in the spatial intermittency of the energy and energy transfer are linked to the inhomogeneous geometry in general and the TKE budget in particular [4,5]. 2. Development of multiscale eddy viscosity. Conventional subgrid-scale turbulence parameterisations ignore topography. By exploiting the wavelet formalism developed in Objective 1, the effects of subgrid topography for different resolved grid sizes can be represented as an eddy viscosity. For the square and staggered arrays, the mean subgrid transfer is comparable to the resolved-scale transfer near the cut-off scale and the instantaneous backscatter (i.e. positive energy transfer) may be strong. Similar trends are found for different geometries and wind directions [3]. 3. Development of subgrid-scale pollutant model. We introduced a new method for representing the effects of subgrid-scale topography on the evolution of a passive scalar [1]. Conventional approaches neglect boundary effects and rely on turbulence phenomenology. Our results for idealized urban configurations show that acceptable results (pointwise concentration errors of ~30-40%) can be obtained when the original time-averaged scalar field is coarse-grained by a factor of 16x16x16. Analysis of scalar fields for realistic domains [2,6] indicate that the method should extend with a comparable level of accuracy. 4. Implementation of the multiscale eddy viscosity. A new parameterization of the effects of subgrid urban topography on mesoscale winds was implemented in the WRF atmospheric mesoscale model. Starting from a baseline WRF configuration for Hong Kong [6], 72-hour simulations of surface winds at the Hong Kong International Airport show small improvements (~2% for the mean wind speed and ~6% for the mean-square error) relative to the baseline simulation. The improvements are modest but comparable to that for typical changes in numerical weather prediction models. It is likely that larger improvements could be obtained if the eddy viscosities were derived using the actual building geometry rather than an idealised building array.

11329616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11329616.value: This project focused on the development of new multiscale modelling techniques for urban flows and pollutant dispersion. Only a relatively small number of configurations were examined in detail. In order to improve the performance for realistic applications, future research should consider more demanding tests. Important target problems include larger LES domains with greater variability in the topography and WRF (mesoscale) simulations for additional seasons. This direction represents a natural continuation of the current project and will be pursued over the next year. The findings from this project can also be developed in new and interesting directions. First, drawing on developments in climate prediction, a parameterization that abandons the eddy viscosity approach in favour of a stochastic backscatter model of energy transfer could account for intermittency and flow dependence. This could represent a major advance in realism compared to parameterisations based on the mean transfer or homogeneous turbulence. Second, the high numerical cost of numerical homogenisation could be avoided by using machine learning to avoid matrix inversion and construct an approximate nonlocal diffusion operator. In effect, a statistical procedure that aims to reproduce the benefits of homogenisation would be developed.

11329616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11329616.value: Although there is increasing interest in modelling weather and air quality for cities, current weather prediction models are incapable of representing urban inhomogeneities, namely buildings. Urban parameterisation schemes for atmospheric models partially address this limitation, but they do not explicitly take the multiscale nature of the atmosphere into account: the effect of unresolved scales on resolved ones is not calculated for turbulence or pollutants. Progress on the modelling of the urban atmosphere has been slowed in part by the lack of systematic approaches for representing the effects of the highly heterogeneous urban environment. In this project, multiscale parameterisations for urban flows and pollutant dispersion were developed for the first time by applying techniques from applied mathematics and fluid dynamics. This has been done for idealized cities with a regular arrangement of buildings and applied to a high-resolution numerical model for the Hong Kong region. Additional work will be required to tailor the parameterisations to real cities, in which there are significant variations in building height and shape. Nevertheless, this project represents a notable step towards the development of more accurate weather and air quality models that respect local inhomogeneities.

11331016.label: Project Objectives
11331016.value: An efficient large-scale multi-label classification framework will be developed, which incorporates information from both labels and predictors, allows for efficient computation, and attains desirable theoretical properties. The asymptotic estimation and selection consistencies will be established and numeric experiments will be conducted to support its effectiveness against the existing methods in literature. An efficient inexact alternating direction method of multiplier algorithm will be developed to tackle the large-scale optimization task. The computational cost shall be substantially reduced without sacrificing any estimation accuracy. The algorithm will be adapted to parallel computing nodes to further reduce the computational cost and to handle large-scale real dataset with size up to O(10^8). The proposed method will be extended to develop large-scale ranking and multivariate regression methods. The extended methods shall deliver superior performance against their competitors as well. The proposed multi-label classification method will be implemented and disseminated in a publicly available R package.

11331016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11331016.value: 本研究項目將針對文本摘要提出一個大規模多標籤分類框架，其主要目標是創造一個標籤集以抓獲原始文本文件的主要方面。一個新的針對文本標注的損失函數將被引入以測量實際與預測標籤集之間的差異。這個損失函數表示成一個對式間隔的加權和，其權重取決於每兩個標籤的相似度。在這個基礎上，一個正則化的經驗損失函數將被構造以集成部分語意信息，並最終確認一個標注器最大化對式間隔。這個框架一個顯著的特點是它能通過標籤間的相似度探測到那些在訓練集中未出現的新的標籤。這是其和大部分現有方法最大的不同。本項目將研究這個新方法的理論性質，並建立其標註錯誤率在大樣本及有限樣本的上界。本項目也將發展相應的有效優化算法以實現所需的大規模優化問題。這個算法將集成不精確交替方向乘子法（ADMM）以及並行計算平台。本項目提出的方法將被運用於摘要包含了800000條新聞故事的路透社數據集。

11331016.label: Realisation of objectives
11331016.value: In this project, the PI and his collaborators propose a novel multi-label classification framework based on a new tagging loss over a class of candidate tags. The new tagging loss is different from the popular 0-1 loss and symmetric difference loss, and measures the difference between the actual and predicted tag sets, which allows different lengths of tags. The loss is averaged over pairs of tags from the two tag sets, weighted by their pairwise degrees of similarity, with a high value indicating a high degree of similarity. This type of loss allows partial correctness of tagging. More importantly, this type of loss allows us to detect novel tags, because a novel tag in a candidate tag class can be identified in the presence of other tags if they have high similarity to the novel tag in a training sample. On this basis, the proposed method integrates the dependency structure in terms of word similarities, where regularization is imposed to incorporate linguistic knowledge for tagging. In practice, the pairwise degrees of similarity can be considered prior knowledge, and are estimated using existing semantic systems such as the WordNet system. The resultant optimization task can be efficiently solved by the inexact alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) method. The asymptotic estimation consistency of the proposed method is also established in terms of the tagging accuracy. The proposed method is also applied to analyze the original Reuters Corpus Volume I, which has 800 000 manually categorized news-wire stories. The proposed method is also extended to large-scale ranking problem. Particularly, the PI and his PhD student proposed a general U-process formulation for query-dependent ranking to admit different ranking functions for various queries. It allows to incorporate neighborhood structure among queries via various forms of smoothing weights to improve the ranking performance. One of its salient features is its capability of producing reasonable rankings for novel queries that are absent in the training set, which is commonly encountered in practice but often neglected in the literature. The proposed method is implemented via an inexact alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for each query parallelly. Its asymptotic risk bound is established, showing that it achieves desirable ranking accuracy at a fast rate for any query including the novel ones. Furthermore, simulated examples and a real application to the Yahoo! challenge dataset also support the advantage. Both proposed method are implemented in Python, and available upon request. As Dr. Ben Dai is in his last year of PostDoc training at University of Minnesota, we plan to wrap up all the implementations in both Python and R packages for dissemination in the coming year.

11331016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11331016.value: The major findings of this project is three-folds. First, the PI and his collaborators developed a novel multi-label classification framework based on a new tagging loss (Part C Output 1). The new tagging loss is averaged over pairs of tags from the two tag sets, weighted by their pairwise degrees of similarity, with a high value indicating a high degree of similarity, and thus allows us to detect novel tags. It is in sharp contrast to most existing tagging methods that can only produce observed tags, and thus provides an important addition to the literature on document tagging. Second, the proposed method is also extended to large-scale ranking and recommender system (Part C Outputs 4 & 5). The proposed method is built upon a general U-process formulation for query-dependent ranking, which admits different ranking functions for various queries. It also allows to incorporate neighborhood structure among queries via various forms of smoothing weights to improve the ranking and recommendation performance. Third, this project also develops tools to bridge classical machine learning framework to modern high-dimensional data analysis (Part C Outputs 2, 3, 7 & 8). Particularly, when we allow nonparametric regression function in the high-dimensional data, it can be well fit into the classical machine learning framework. The proposed large-scale multi-label classification and ranking methods played important foles in constructing the informative variables, which eventually lead to superior numerical performance and fast asymptotic convergence rates.

11331016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11331016.value: One potential development is to extend the multi-label ranking and recommendation methods to model directed networks. Directed networks have been popularly used to describe the interactions among objects, which can be naturally converted into a binary recommendation system. The PI and this another PhD student are now working on this extension, by fully utilizing the desirable properties of the latent factor model. The preliminary numerical experiments are very promising, and the required computational cost can be substantially reduced without any sacrifice of the estimation accuracy. The PI plans to admit another PhD student or a PostDoc to join the research team and complete the theoretical guarantees of these extensions.

11331016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11331016.value: This proposed research project develops novel statistical methods and computing algorithms for large-scale multi-label classification and ranking. All the objectives are achieved, and an efficient machine learning framework is developed, which is in sharp contrast to most existing methods in literature. The research findings have a wide spectrum of applications in practice, ranging from document categorization, image classification, to personalize recommendation. The proposed research not only develop a novel perspective of conducting multi-label classification and ranking, but also provide rich opportunities for Postgraduate students to participate in cutting-edge researches. With the support of this project, the PI and his collaborators published 8 research articles on leading statistics and machine learning journals, and trained one Ph.D. student Dr. Ben Dai, who is now PostDoc researcher at University of Minnesota. More importantly, this project also opens up a few potential directions for future research on learning complex structure in large-scale data.

11332816.label: Major findings and research outcome
11332816.value: The main objectives of this study are to (1) identify the characteristics of tropical cyclones (TCs) with large track forecast errors (TFEs) of operational warning centres, and their associated atmospheric conditions, and (2) to explain why the existence of such characteristics could lead to large TFEs. The International Grand Global Ensemble data are used to perform the study. Forty-four TCs in the western North Pacific during the period 2007 - 2014 with TFEs (+24 to +120 hours) larger than the 75th percentile of the annual error distribution (with a total of 93 cases) are identified. Four categories of situations are found to be associated with large TFEs. These include the interaction of the outer structure of the TC with tropical weather systems, the intensity of the TC, the extension of the subtropical high (SH) and the interaction with the westerly trough. The asymmetric flow structure of a TC appears to be a crucial factor when the TC is located near the neutral point between two high pressure systems. Moreover, a predicted TC that can withstand stronger vertical wind shear would have a smaller TFE. An erroneous prediction of the extension of the SH and the depth of westerly trough would lead to large TFEs of some models. Among the TIGGE model predictions, the models of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and the UK Met Office generally have a smaller TFE. The results have been published in Magnusson et al. (2019) and in another manuscript submitted for publication (Tang et al. 2020b). To further investigate how the size of the TC vortex might influence the TFE, three TCs with large TFEs are studied by performing simulations using the Weather Research and Forecasting model with a bogus vortex having different radii of 15 m/s (R15) but the same environmental flow. With a nearby strong monsoon trough, a TC with a smaller R15 merges with the cyclonic circulation within the trough leading to a larger outer circulation, which steers the TC to move more northward. On the other hand, in a weak monsoon trough situation, a TC with larger R15 interacts with the monsoon trough to cause the TC to move more westward. In the presence of a westerly trough, a TC with larger R15 interacts with the trough such that the TC moves more northeastward. The results have been published in Tang et al. (2020a).

11332816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11332816.value: Although this study represents the most comprehensive study on the reasons for large track forecast errors of most operational models, further studies are necessary. For example, a more in-depth investigation should be conducted on the effect of the interaction between the extension of the TC circulation and the nearby synoptic systems on the TC forecast track. Resolution of the NWP models and model physics may also be important factors leading to the large track forecast errors Further research into the sensitivity of model resolution on track forecast is clearly necessary. Moreover, due to data availability, only the years from 2007 to 2014 are studied in this project. Similar research using more recent datasets should be conducted to update the model performance.

11332816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11332816.value: The main objective of this study is to identify the reasons why forecasts of tropical cyclone (TC) track could sometimes have large errors. The main result is that errors from the predictions of the numerical models of either or both the characteristics of the TC and its surrounding flow are responsible for such large errors. Some models are consistently better than others. The reasons for the sources of such errors are investigated using numerical simulations. These results are useful for operational forecasters in selecting the better prediction model in different situations.

11332916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11332916.value: 此研究項目致力於發展高緯守恆律的數學理論， 特別是固體物質上的，比如說契形物和機翼，由定常歐拉方程決定的間斷可壓縮流體。 定常可壓縮歐拉方程是流體力學中的一個非常重要和經典的方程。 它可以用來刻劃很多非線性的物理現象， 比如說激波。所以對於由定常歐拉方程決定的間斷可壓縮流體的研究一直是流體和守恆律研究中的核心問題。而且這個項目的研究對於帶自由邊界的混合型耦合行方程有著重要的意義。 自上世紀八十年代以來，對於高緯守恆律的研究已經有了長足的進步。 然而幾乎所有的問題都集中在特定的問題上，如平面激波，稀疏波，具有特殊結構的定常或者自相似解的的存在穩定性。 比如定常超音速流體過契形物體時產生的斜激波的存在穩定性。 我們在相關的問題上做了幾年的研究。 最近，我們得到了無限長管道裡亞音速歐拉流體的全局存在性，過非直線邊界的契形物的激波機構的唯一性，以及雙曲守恆律柯西問題的幾何光學展開的適定性。 在這個項目中，我們會繼續發展解決這些問題中用到的方法。 直到現在，所有關於固體物上的二維定常間斷流體的數學結果，都集中於一個常狀態解的小擾動。 我們知道這裏有兩個常狀態解結構， 一個是強激波，一個是弱激波。 所以這裏有一個很自然的問題是哪一個解是真正物理上的解。 這是Courant-Friedrichs書上的一個公開問題。希望通過這個項目，我們能夠對這個公開問題有更深刻的理解和認識。

11334116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11334116.value: Hong Kong is dominated by busy and often polluted urban environments. Here high traffic flows have led to the construction of many walkways, which can in places develop into complex networks. Obviously such structures mean that pedestrian flow is safely segregated from the roadway, but there are also views that this lowers the roadside exposure to air pollutants. Air pollution exerts an important control on the health effects in urban populations and is a particular problem for the Pearl River Delta. It is thought to be responsible for the rapid increase in the number of people suffering from non-communicable diseases presents one of the biggest challenges to the health care systems in Hong Kong with its aging population. We proposed research will examine the potential exposure of people in the roadside environment and monitor the concentrations of carbon monoxide and fine particles at sufficient detail to map the concentrations in the walkways and their surroundings. The transfer of pollutants into the walkways will also be modelled by computational fluid dynamics and give an indication of features that affect transfer of air pollutants to their interiors. The project should help develop policy as part of Hong Kong desire to be a walkable city, but also offer guidance to the design and positioning of new walkways 香港城市环境多以由交通拥堵带来的污染环境为主。由于车流量的密集，大量人行道建成，并在各地形成了复杂网络。这样的城市结构很显然一方面起到保障行人交通安全的作用，但另一方面，也有观点认为其可以降低行人对道路空气污染的曝露。对城市人口的健康影响来说，空气污染起到重要的控制作用；在珠三角地区，此现象尤为特殊。伴随着香港人口老年化问题，非传染性疾病人数的快速增长给医疗保健系统带来了极大的挑战。空气污染需要为这一问题负一定责任。因此，我们提出此项研究来调查路边人群的潜在曝露和详细监测人行道及周边环境的一氧化碳和细颗粒物浓度，并绘制污染分布图。污染物从路边到人行道的转移也将基于计算流体动力学来建立模型，并指示性地给出影响这一过程的关键因素。这一项目将帮助香港制定政策，实现构建步行城市的愿景，同时也能够为新建人行道的设计和选址提供指导

11334116.label: Realisation of objectives
11334116.value: This project sought to determine the pollutant concentrations in and around elevated walkways in Hong Kong and determine the extent to which these expose pedestrians to high concentrations of air pollutants and estimate likely exposure of pedestrians adopting various routes through city streets. Although the vertical distribution of pollutants within idealized street canyons has been investigated in many earlier experimental and numerical studies relatively few address walkways. . Our in-situ measurements support the notion a decay away from the road, though the nature of the vertical dependence is complicated and reflects the influence of the building geometry. In particular In the horizontal, higher concentrations are found along the leeward wall of canyons for aspect ratios less than or equal to unity but multiple vortices at higher aspect ratios for >1.5 can give rise to the opposite situation. This was confrmed by a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (i.e. p < 0.001) on PM2.5 data we collected for a street with an aspect ratio of 2. This aligns with earlier work. As noted there are few studies of air pollution related to situations where walkways are present in street canyons. Measurements were made at a range of locations and for a number of idealised walkway designs in street canyons were also modelled. Field campaigns were conducted at a total of 17 sites; busy Hong Kong neighbourhoods in Mong Kok, Whampoa, Lai Chi Kok and Cheung Sha Wan). The walkway elevation is typically 6 m. A range of characteristic design elements of walkways were chosen: covered, uncovered; some with steel railings, some with concrete or others with glass walls. Some are covered to help protect pedestrians from sun and rain, but may trap pollutants inside. The sidewall material varies with steel, concrete or glass all being found. Our field measurements for PM2.5 in the walkway show that roadside PM concentrations usually exceed those on the walkway, but the ratio (which typically lies between 1 and 1.5) varies according to the walkway type. Only the covered walkways with steel railings and glass fences have a higher concentration than the sidewalks, although this is just by a few micrograms per cubic metre. The concentrations found in the walkway show less spread in the data than at the roadway, i.e. the date is more homogeneous. We examined the relationship between external pollutant concentrations and those inside the walkways as a function of meteorological conditions. The work explored the changes over 15 different occasions and on multiple times through a single day. The differences between the walkway and the surrounding roadway were relatively robust against diurnal changes in meteorological conditions. However, the measurements were mostly made at low wind speeds mostly between 1 and 3 m/s, though occasionally as high as 5 m/s. However, such low wind conditions are not atypical of densely populated urban areas. Large eddy simulation adopted the ﬁnite volume method and OpenFOAM to explore different walkway designs and elevations in a unit-aspect-ratio street canyon with external wind perpendicular to the canyon axis.to understand and model the dispersion of air pollutants around walkways. The presence of a walkway sets up distinct urban microenvironment where in place of a principal vortex extending through the canyon, smaller primary vortices appear above the walkway lid or below the walkway deck. Ventilation mechanisms for a ground-level pollutant source are qualitatively altered, such that mean concentrations immediately below the walkway at the pedestrian level and within the walkway interior may increase by up to 20% and 30% although we note that notably increased concentrations are found inside the walkway towards the leeward edge. We assessed the importance of walkways features that control the transfer of pollutants to their interior. Inside the walkway interior, modelling shows that ventilation depends on the mean ﬂow and turbulence. Although the mean ﬂow advects pollutants above the deck level, the streamlines diverge away from the walkway; hence ventilation requires lateral turbulent diﬀusion to transport pollutants into and out of the walkway interior. Distribution within the walkway depends on the complex interplay among mean ﬂow, drag and turbulence, which cannot be predicted a priori. This is manifested in a sensitivity to the walkway design. Naively one may expect the concentration within the walkway to increase due to trapping of pollutants by the lid; however, this is an oversimpliﬁcation and as noted in the field measurements it was open walkways that tend to be most polluted. Overall the project revealed that pedestrians using the walkway experience lower pollutant concentrations than those at the roadside. However, as walkaways may be used in Hong Kong for small social gatherings or even picnics, especially among domestic workers the study reveals that this is hardly a desirable place to remain. Pollutant concentrations are reduced only slightly, so the use of the walkway as a venues for people to meet, picnic or busk should be discouraged. The study can give guidance to future design of walkway as we observed and modelled the negative effect of walkway lids on the concentration of pollutants inside. Given that any improvements in pollutant concentrations over the roadside value are rather modest it would seem that closed walkways with some air conditioning or air filtration should be encouraged as such designs could and arrangement within the likely to minimise user exposure to street canyon pollutants More generally, we elucidate characteristics of the elevated walkway microenvironment

11334116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11334116.value: The concentration of particulate matter inside elevated walkways in Hong Kong are generally lower than the roadside below. The diﬀerences between the mean PM concentrations at the sidewalk and walkway, are typically positive, but these are generally modest, with an average over the sites of concentration differences of about 2.4µ gm−3 or 9%. However, the presence of a lid does not necessarily mean that that concentrations increase inside the walkway interior. There is no simple relationship between the walkway design and the concentration differences. A secondary ﬁnding from the field work suggests that the ratio (r) of the sidewalk PM2.5 concentration to the walkway PM2.5 concentration is consistent across all measurements sites in four different neighbourhoods, 17 sites and 15 measurements days: r = 1.22±0.13. These trends are also seen in subsets restricted to a single day highlighting the distance from the main road and the inﬂuence of traﬃc volume. This work suggests that displacing pedestrians from the street level to an elevated walkway does not necessarily decrease pollutant exposure. The walkway concentration depends on the walkway design and orientation relative to the street. From a practical perspective, the cost of building such a structure may not be justiﬁed if mean concentration is the primary concern. The measurements show modest decreases in mean and median PM concentration, though of course the magnitude of the eﬀect would be greater for high-pollution episodes. It is possible that diﬀerences in the age of pollutants between the street and the walkway could alter the relative concentrations of pollutants undergoing reactions. Practical recommendations aside, our work also shows that there is a distinct elevated walkway microenvironment. On account of the distortion of the canyon ﬂow and trapping of pollutants, PM concentrations inside a walkway are not determined simply by the (vertical) distance from the street, as in an idealised street canyon. Further more, basic features of this microenvironment appear to be independent of the details of the walkway structure or the local environment.

11334116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11334116.value: We are continuing to model various aspects of air pollution in street canyons so this work represents a continued inspiration towards our thinking on features of streets. In particular we have become interested in the ideas of completely closed walkway designs and the format of bus stop shelters which would reduce exposure of passengers waiting for buses. The work has further stimulated an interest in the role pollutant uptake by catalytic road surfaces may reduce pollutant concentrations in street canyons.

11334116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11334116.value: Overhead walkways aim to remove pedestrians from threats imposed by heavy traffic flows along roads. The most obvious threat is injury from impacts with pedestrians crossing roads, but there is also a potential risk from exposure pollutants. Overhead walkways increase the distance between pedestrian and traffic flows. This project has showed that in general the pollutant concentrations are about 10% lower on the walkways than at the curbside. Different walkway designs have little effect, although the open walkway, a simple bridge with no lid or canopy tends to be the most polluted. Walkways can also disrupt dispersion of air pollutants within street canyons of tall buildings so this study aids the thoughtful design of walkways. The height above the street can influence the degrees of dispersion of pollutants vertically within the street canyon.

11334516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11334516.value: 去乙酰化酶是在真核细胞中负责调控基因表达的关键酶。去乙酰化酶被广泛认为是一系列重要疾病的靶标，尤其是癌症，许多文献曾报道在不同癌症中观测到去乙酰化酶的异常表达。因其具有重要的生物学功能， 许多方法被开发出用于检测去乙酰化酶的活性，在不同的方法中， 荧光探针因其操作简便且具有高灵敏性，证明是可靠及最适合的方法。 但是， 绝大多数荧光探针需要多步反应完成荧光检测，极大地限制了它们在细胞环境中实时检测去乙酰化酶活性的生物应用。此外，目前尚缺乏能够能够特异性检测给定去乙酰化酶的荧光探针。 在此项目中，我们将设计并合成一系列含乙酰化赖氨酸和O-NBD基团的荧光探针用于检测去乙酰化酶的活性。当荧光探针与酶孵育后， 去乙酰化会导致探针中氨基的释放。产生的氨基会进一步与O-NBD基团反应从而“点亮”荧光。我们将详尽研究荧光探针的灵敏性及选择性。完成这些研究后，荧光探针将被应用于细胞成像实验。 接下来，我们会开发具有专一性荧光探针用于检测不同亚型去乙酰化酶的活性。我们将文献中报道的专一性多肽引入前述探针， 从而制得基于多肽的荧光探针。 此外，我们还将合成一个小的多肽探针文库来研究去乙酰化酶的底物选择性。 这些研究将有助于筛选出对给定去乙酰化酶具有特异性的荧光探针。 在此基础上，我们还将利用光交联基团二氮环丙烯发展具有双重功能的荧光探针，该探针不仅有助于我们实时监测细胞内去乙酰化酶的活性，同时能精确测量去乙酰化酶在不同生物样本中的表达量，我们预期此项研究将会产生能够系统表征去乙酰化酶的新型荧光探针并应用于生物医学研究。我们科研小组在荧光探针、多肽化学及定量蛋白组学具有广泛的研究经验，我们相信这项研究将能够成功完成并提供强有力的科研工具，从而进一步促进去乙酰化酶的研究及癌症药物的开发。

11334516.label: Realisation of objectives
11334516.value: Both objectives have been accomplished by the completion date. Specifically we have designed and synthesized a set of fluorescent probes by incorporating the Kac residue and the O-NBD moiety. The probes are capable of monitoring the enzymatic activity of HDACs in a continuous manner. Detailed experiments showed that the probes exhibit high sensitivity and selectivity towards HDACs, and the fluorescence turn on fold can reach up to 50 fold after enzymatic reaction. Subsequently we designed and synthetized a dual-function probe by employing photocrosslinking strategy. The designed probe can not only report enzymatic activity, but also identify and capture protein targets from the complex cellular environment.

11334716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11334716.value: Using solar energy to split water into H2 and O2 is a desirable and “clean” approach to resolving the energy crisis. It is particularly viable when a photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting technique is used. The technique would be effective if the photoelectrode material could efficiently absorb visible sunlight, transport charge carriers, and remain stable. A promising new candidate for such a material is graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN), according to our recent demonstration. While it is still necessary to achieve large-area thin film deposition, improved charge carrier mobility and full-spectrum absorption, this material also requires further development in order to reduce photocatalytic degradation in water splitting. To obtain strategies for reducing photocatalytic degradation, we propose in this project to systematically investigate the exciton dynamics and possible photoinduced chemical reactions of various g-CN nanostructures in water splitting under visible light. Towards the goal, we will use time-dependent density functional theory and its tight-binding approximation to perform the excited-state molecular dynamics simulations for the neutral and charged g-CN nanostructures. The simulation will be conducted at various possible temperatures (ranging from 230K to 320K) likely to be experienced in applications. We will do so in water containing OH- or H+ and sacrificial reagent (e.g. Na2S and triethanolamine) as well as in the presence of the O atoms and molecules generated from water splitting. The charged g-CN models will be used to simulate the electron rich and deficient cases due to n- and p-type dopings. We will examine the exciton generation, localization, and migration, and the related chemical reactions, in order to understand the photocatalytic degradation of g-CN. We will identify the atom and bond changes arising from the excitations and characterize the time evolution of the excited electron and hole distributions in the g-CN. In doing so we will pay particular attention to the possibility of inducing structural instability and deformation and the effects of the various possible species in the water environment. The excited-state chemical reactions we identify will then be quantitatively studied using transition state theory and the nudged elastic band method to derive their kinetic characteristics. We expect our simulations to reveal the degradation mechanism of g-CN due to the exciton generation in the g-CN and oxygen atoms and molecules generated on the electrode surface. This will allow us to propose strategies to minimize the degradation so as to contribute to the important development of PEC water splitting using g-CN. 高效節能的新型納米光催化劑的發展在光催化科學領域中至關重要。最近，一些諸如類石墨相氮化碳和石墨氧化物等層狀半導體材料由於其新穎的電子結構在這方面表現出巨大的潛力。它們的光催化反應動力學和機理以及性能的改進需要進一步深入的研究。本項目將通過分子水平的理論計算重點研究類石墨C3N4和石墨氧化物等層狀半導體材料電子性質和其結構調制對其光催化活性的影響。通過選擇性摻雜和表面功能化，將在分子水平上對材料的幾何結構和電子結構進行修改和設計。將分析它們由結構確定的物理化學性質以及決定它們的因素，以確定提高其光催化性能的方案。將用計及層間弱相互作用的含時密度泛函理論計算研究吸附離子和表面的相互作用、電荷轉移及催化反應動力學過程。此外，為揭示光催化機理，我們將研究層狀半導體材料涉及C-C鍵的π-π*躍遷吸收光譜；我們還將考查光生電子和空穴復合導致的熒光光譜。基於其微觀結構和決定光催化性能的因素，我們將預測這類材料的物理化學性質並提高其光催化反應活性，進而改進具有高活性和能量轉換效率的新型光催化材料的設計。

11334716.label: Realisation of objectives
11334716.value: The ultimate goal of this project is to reveal the possible degradation mechanism of g-CN due to the generation of the exciton in g-CN films so as to improve the photoelectrochemical property of the film in water splitting. Eventually, we have successfully achieved the goal by first demonstrating the computational approaches, in particular the excited state dynamics simulations by studying the excited state dynamics of the self-trapped exciton formation in silicon nanosheets. We moved on to further study the mechanism of charge separation and frontier orbital structure in graphitic carbon nitride and graphene quantum dots, exciton self-trapping in sp2 carbon nanostructures induced by edge adsorptions and/or saturations, and photoinduced water−heptazine electron-driven proton transfer and thus the perspective for water splitting with g‑C3N4. To complement the computational efforts, we experimentally studied the property tuneability of g-CN films by using melamine formaldehyde resin as a new precursor, proposing a pseudo-metal-free strategy for constructing high performance photoelectrodes, modifying the carbon concentration, and doping with boron. Combining computational explorations, we have achieved very good understanding of the structural-property relationship, in particular the water environment effects, degradation mechanism as well as doping effects, and eventually obtained g-CNs with record high water splitting photocurrent density and excellent stability.

11334716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11334716.value: We investigated the exciton formation dynamics of several model silicon nanosheets (SiNSs) using a time-dependent density functional tight binding method. While this study reveals that Si–Si bond breaking acts as an optical activity center and provides regulation of the self-trapped exciton formation time by the quantum confinement effect in SiNSs, the tool was demonstrated to be very useful and efficient for studying the exciton dynamics of low dimensional systems. [See C8-1] We uncovered the mechanism of charge separation and frontier orbital structure in graphitic carbon nitride and graphene quantum dots, providing an explanation for the origin of the enhanced photocatalytic performance of the former over the latter and their characteristic FOs localization. [See C8-2] We also obtained exciton self-trapping in sp2 carbon nanostructures induced by edge adsorptions and/or saturations. [See C8-3] Using excited-state nonadiabatic dynamics simulations, we uncovered the molecular-level picture of the decomposition of heptazine hydrogen bonded to water molecule(s) into heptazinyl and hydroxyl biradical products. We observed photorelaxation-induced water splitting by heptazine which proves the water-splitting reaction principle. [See C8-4] Combining experiments and computations, we worked on various strategies of tuning the property of g-CN films. Using melamine formaldehyde resin as a new precursor, we obtained crystal-face tailored graphitic carbon nitride films for high-performance photoelectrochemical cells. [See C8-5] We adopted different monomers and amounts to tailor carbon nitride based photoelectrodes with different colors and achieved colorful carbon nitride based photoelectrodes with satisfied photocatalytic activity. [See C8-6] We proposed a pseudo-metal-free strategy for constructing high performance photoelectrodes and [See C8-7] we modified the carbon concentration of g-CN films to boost the PEC performance by removing some N atoms from the g-CN networks with annealing treatment. [See C8-8] We further introduced boron heteroatoms into CN films (BCN) and explored the influence of the B heteroatom on the PEC performance. We found that B atoms favor substitution of carbon atoms at bay sites in BCN films and reduce the bandgap by raising the valence band edge as well as constructing optimal electronic structures for PEC hydrogen production with high g-CN film stability. [See C8-9] Eventually, we have achieved very good understanding of the structural-property relationship, in particular the water environment effects, degradation mechanism as well as doping effects, and obtained g-CN films with record high water splitting photocurrent density and excellent stability [See C8-5 to C8-9].

11334716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11334716.value: Using sunlight to decompose water is the most ideal hydrogen production technology. The material for hydrogen production by photolysis of water must not only meet the requirements of low cost, easy availability, and environmental friendliness, but also have appropriate band gap, effective carrier separation and migration, and good surface reactivity. Metal-free carbon nitride better satisfies these requirements. To reach the goal of practical application, our group has developed a thermal vapor condensation (TVC) method to synthesize large-area uniform carbon nitride films, with the photocurrent density reaching 0.12 mA/cm2 for pure g-CN film and up to 0.84 mA/cm2 for sulphur-doped g-CN. The boron-doped g-CN film prepared by TVC method shows a considerably high photostability and maintains 90% of initial photocurrent under 10h illumination. Further development must be made by designing g-CN films and manufacturing stable hydrogen production systems for efficient water splitting. Building on the findings of this project, we will establish the structure-property relationship of g-CN thin films, to clarify the charge transfer mechanism at the photoanode interface, to propose effective strategies for efficient charge transfer, and finally to industrialize the hydrogen production system and promote low carbon society.

11334716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11334716.value: Using solar energy to split water into H2 and O2 with a photoelectrochemical technique is a desirable and “clean” approach to resolving the energy crisis. Graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) has been a promising new candidate of the required photoelectrode material. Yet, its large-area thin films with improved charge carrier mobility and full-spectrum absorption are developed for efficient energy conversion and reduced photocatalytic degradation in water splitting. In this project, water-splitting reaction principle is uncovered by simulating the decomposition of heptazine hydrogen bonded to water molecule(s) into heptazinyl and hydroxyl biradical products, which reveals photorelaxation-induced water splitting by heptazine. Combining experiments and computations, we developed several strategies of tuning the property of g-CN films for optimal hydrogen generation by water splitting using photoelectrochemical cells. We achieved crystal-face tailored g-CN films using melamine formaldehyde resin as a new precursor, adopted different monomers and amounts to tailor g-CN based photoelectrodes with different colors, proposed a pseudo-metal-free strategy for constructing high performance photoelectrodes, modified the carbon concentration of g-CN films by removing some N atoms from the g-CN networks with annealing treatment, and further introduced boron heteroatoms into g-CN films which reduce the bandgap by constructing optimal electronic structures with high g-CN film stability.

11335316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11335316.value: 北大西洋风暴轴与乌拉尔山阻塞对东亚冬季风预测的影响误差

11335316.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11335316.value: Prof CHEN, Wen Prof Keenlyside, Noel Sebastian Dr Woollings, Tim

11335316.label: Project Objectives
11335316.value: To identify the key dynamic processes responsible for the formation and maintenance of Ural blocking in relation to the North Atlantic storm track; To analyze the biases of the North Atlantic storm track and the spatio-temporal characteristics of Ural blocking in the CMIP5 GCMs; To evaluate future changes of the spatio-temporal characteristics of Ural blocking and the North Atlantic storm track.

To analyze the biases of the North Atlantic storm track and the spatio-temporal characteristics of Ural blocking in the CMIP5 GCMs;
To evaluate future changes of the spatio-temporal characteristics of Ural blocking and the North Atlantic storm track.

11335316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11335316.value: 伴随着全球气候变暖，即使人们期望更温暖的冬天， 但由于最近在欧亚大陆不寻常和突然的寒冷天气已变得非常频繁，预估东亚冬季气候在全球变暖情景下的变化是非常具有挑战性。近十年来频繁的意外寒冷的冬天其实已经表明了急需要提高我们对冬季风机理分析和预测能力。 异常东亚冬季季风带来华南地区包括香港在内冬季极端天气。例如，香港天文台录得2008 年 1 月 24 日至 2 月 16 日自 1968 年以来最长 24天 连续寒冷天。在冬季，北大西洋风暴轴向东延伸与乌拉尔山/西伯利亚西部附近大气阻塞的频率相关。这种相互关系影响东亚冬季风强度，导致东亚地区发生寒潮。但是大气环流模式 (GCMs) 不能很好模拟风暴的轨道和阻塞的时空变异性。所以很好地验证北大西洋风暴轴和乌拉尔阻塞的偏差，对于评估东亚冬季风预测的不确定性是很重要的。 在此研究中，我们使用再分析数据集和参加第五阶段的大气环流耦合模型相互比较项目 (CMIP5)的模式数据，对北大西洋风暴轴与乌拉尔阻塞发生频次之间的关系提出了新颖分析方法。首先，我们将诊断乌拉尔阻塞和北大西洋风暴 的关系。第二，我们会选择 最佳模拟阻塞 — 风暴轴的关系的模式，然后我们将探讨在 RCP4.5 和 8.5情境下 运行的未来变化以及在每次模式运行的预估不确定性。最后，我们将在北大西洋进行不同的 SST 条件的数值实验来验证我们的假设。 通过本文的研究，我们将更好地理解模式间风暴轴/乌拉尔阻塞模拟的误差 及其对之后的东亚冬季气候变化的影响误差。这些结果对于气候变化下香港冬季极端条件的风险评估也应该是重要的。

11335316.label: Realisation of objectives
11335316.value: With the funding support, we hired some RAs to analyze observation data and CMIP5 model outputs. We have investigated the dynamical processes responsible for the monsoon system circulations and evaluated future change. We found the important role of the Stratospheric Polar Vortex and Tropospheric Blocking associated with a strong phase reversal of the Arctic Oscillation in Midwinter 2015/16. We emphasized the delayed impacts of the IOD on the cross-seasonal relationships between the IOD, Tibetan Plateau snow, and Asia precipitation. We also found that a remarkable link between projected uncertainties of Arctic sea ice decline and winter Eurasian climate. Therefore, we have published 11 SCI papers and achieved the project objectives.
