11335316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11335316.value: We have published 11 SCI papers, and found some significant results: 1. Remarkable link between projected uncertainties of Arctic sea-ice decline and winter Eurasian climate We identify that the projected uncertainty of the pan-Arctic sea-ice concentration (SIC) is strongly coupled with the Eurasian circulation in the boreal winter (December–March; DJFM), based on a singular value decomposition (SVD) analysis of the forced response of 11 CMIP5 models. In the models showing a stronger sea-ice decline, the Polar cell becomes weaker and there is an anomalous increase in the sea level pressure (SLP) along 60◦N, including the Urals–Siberia region and the Iceland low region. In the Mediterranean region, the anomalous circulation response shows a decreasing SLP and increasing precipitation. The anomalous SLP responses over the Euro-Atlantic region project on to the negative North Atlantic Oscillation–like pattern. Altogether, pan-Arctic SIC decline could strongly impact the winter Eurasian climate, but we should be cautious about the causality of their linkage. 2.A Strong Phase Reversal of the Arctic Oscillation in Midwinter 2015/16: Role of the Stratospheric Polar Vortex and Tropospheric Blocking In January 2016, Asia and North America experienced unusual cold temperatures, although the global average of surface air temperature broke the warmest record during a strong El Niño event. This was closely related to the remarkable phase transition of the Arctic Oscillation (AO), which can be explained by stratosphere‐troposphere interactions. First, the quasi‐biennial oscillation changed to its westerly phase in summer 2015 and the stratospheric polar vortex was stronger in early to midwinter 2015/2016. As blocking did not occur in December, the associated downward propagation signal resulted in a strongly positive AO in late December 2015. Second, after late December, the positive phase of Pacific‐North America pattern became apparent in El Niño event, which strengthened the Aleutian anticyclone in the stratosphere. In addition, an equivalent barotropic (“blocking”) anticyclone was established in the troposphere over Asia. The coexistence of blocking over Asia and North America characterized the negative AO and a strong zonal wave number 2 pattern. Due to stronger zonal wave number 2 signals from the troposphere, the stronger stratospheric polar vortex was elongated, with two cyclonic centers over Asia and the North Atlantic in January. The resultant southward displacement of polar vortices was followed by rare snowfall in the subtropical region of East Asia and a heavy snowstorm on the East Coast of the United States.

11335316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11335316.value: We may propose a CRF or RIF project based on the results. We believe our results can help evaluate the risk of cold extremes and improve stratosphere‐troposphere dynamical processes in climate models.

11335316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11335316.value: Under the global warming trend, cold extremes will very likely occur less frequently. It is thus important to identify the possible dynamic causes for their occurrence at different time scales. These advanced studies of stratosphere‐troposphere interactions will aid in understanding changes in large‐scale dynamics and would also be useful for improving extended‐range weather forecasts

11335816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11335816.value: 關於懸浮在非彈性粒子體系中的物體的動力學的研究

11335816.label: Project Objectives
11335816.value: Develop a numerical code to simulate objects embedded in inelastic particle systems. Carry out detailed numerical simulations for objects embedded in inelastic particle systems. Analyze the behavior of the embedded objects from numerical data. Develop theory for the dynamics of an object embedded in an inelastic particle system at low volume fraction. 11335816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11335816.value: When a small object embedded in a liquid or a gas, it experiences bombardment by fast‐moving atoms or molecules. This leads to random motion of the embedded object. Such random motion is called Brownian motion. Brownian motion has been widely used to model phenomena that involve random behavior. Brownian motion is the most fundamental building block in the mathematics of stochastic analysis. Over more than a century of development, many theoretical tools have been established to study and to analyze the Brownian motion. These include Maxwell distribution, diffusion equation, Ito calculus and martingale. However, none of these theoretical tools is applicable when one considers an object embedded in inelastic particle systems. Although phenomenologically the motion of the embedded object is also random due to the bombardment by the inelastic particles, the dynamics is very different from Brownian motion. Our preliminary study showed that even in the absence of external forces, the average net force exerted on the embedded object by the inelastic particles can be non‐zero. This is in sharp contrast to the corresponding cases in fluids or in gases. In fluids and gases, in the absence of external forces, the averaging net force on the embedded objects is zero and this property is independent of the shape of the object. In this proposal, we will study such surprising phenomena and investigate the fundamental mechanism that leads to such phenomenon. 懸浮在液體或氣體中的物體因受到快速運動的原子或分子的撞擊而產生布朗運動。布朗運動被廣泛地運用於描繪帶有隨機行為的現象。布朗運動也是數學領域裏隨機分析的基石。近百年來，人們發展了許多理論工具，以便在數學上分析布朗運動。其中包括麥克斯韋分布、擴散方程、伊藤引理和鞅論。可是，這些理論工具對於懸浮在非彈性粒子裏的物體來說都不適用。雖然非彈性粒子的碰撞對物體的運動也造成隨機性，但物體的動力學與布朗運動有很大的不同。我們初步的研究顯示，即使在沒有外力的情況下，非彈性粒子對物體產生的平均作用力可以不為零。這與物體懸浮在液體或氣體中的情況截然不同。在無外力的情況下，懸浮在液體或氣體中的物體所受的平均作用力為零。這個性質與物體的形狀無關。在本課題裏，我們將分析這個新奇的現象並研究導致這種現象的最根本的機制。

11336816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11336816.value: This project is concerned with the investigation of two new classes of high-valent transition metal complexes: (1) seven-coordinate metal oxo (M=O) species (M = Ru, Os), (2) d0 nitrido oxo species. Metal oxo species have long been used as oxidants in chemical and biological systems; and they usually have tetrahedral, square pyramidal or octahedral geometry. However, recently seven-coordinate ruthenium oxo species have been proposed as active intermediates in catalytic oxidation of water and organic substrates by a number of substitution-inert octahedral ruthenium(II/III) catalysts. These results suggest that seven-coordinate metal oxo species is a promising new class of highly active oxidants. Hence one of the main themes of this project is to isolate or generate new seven-coordinate metal oxo species from a series of substitution-inert, six-coordinate ruthenium and osmium complexes in +II or +III oxidation states. Our goals are to understand the factors that control their reactivity and to develop highly efficient catalytic systems for the oxidation of water and organic substrates based on seven-coordinate metal oxo intermediates. Our second main theme is concerned with the investigation of d0 metal nitrido oxo species as active intermediates for water and organic oxidation. Metal oxidation catalysts are usually in +II or +III oxidation states; in the presence of an external oxidant they can be oxidized to generate a high-valent oxo species as the active oxidant. However, we have previously discovered that d2 osmium(VI) nitrido complex bearing tetradentate Schiff base or simple chloride ligands are active catalysts for the oxidation of alkanes using hydrogen peroxide as the oxidant. Experimental and theoretical calculations suggest that the active intermediate is a d0 osmium(VIII) nitrido oxo species. Similarly we recently found that the d2 manganese(V) nitrido complex, [MnV(N)(CN)4]2-, is a highly active catalyst for the oxidation of water and alkanes. Mechanistic studies again suggest that the active intermediate is a d0 manganese(VII) nitrido oxo species. These results suggest that d0 metal nitrido oxo species are also a promising new class of highly active oxidants. Hence in this project we will design and synthesize new d2 nitrido complexes of manganese, ruthenium and osmium. The use of these complexes as oxidation catalysts will be investigated and we will attempt to isolate or characterize the metal nitrido oxo active intermediates. Our project should contribute to the understanding of coordination chemistry of these two classes of complexes, as well as the development of highly efficient oxidation catalysts. 本專案旨在研究兩類新型高價過渡金屬化合物:(1)七配位金屬氧化物(M=O, M = Ru, Os); (2) d0金屬氮氧化物。 金屬氧化物作為有效的水氧化和有機物氧化氧化劑,長期以來備受關注。 一般來說,金屬氧化物為四面體、方錐體或八面體構型。 近期,有科學家提出水氧化或有機物氧化中,七配位的八面體金屬釕氧化物為反應的活性中間體。 特別是孫教授課題組發表的二價釕化合物[RuII(bda)(L)2作為高效水氧化催化劑,催化頻數(TOF)高達300 s-1, 轉化數(TON)>50000。 在該體系中,孫教授提出七配位的五價金屬釕氧化物是該體系的活性中間體。 該研究表明,七配位的金屬氧化物極有可能是一類新型的高價活性中間體氧化劑。 因此,本專案重要目標之一即為設計並研究該類七配位的新型金屬氧化物,闡明該類活性中間體的特性,以達控制活性中間體活性進而控制催化體系活性。 本專案另一主要目標即為研究d0金屬氮氧化物中間體。 在本課題組前期工作中,成功利用含席夫堿配體的六價d2鋨氮化物作為催化劑,雙氧水作為氧化劑,將惰性烷烴高效氧化。 實驗和理論計算結果顯示該體系的活性中間體為d0的八價鋨氮氧化合物。 另外,在本課題組另一研究工作中,發現五價的d2錳氮化物是非常高效的水氧化和烷烴氧化催化劑。 理論計算顯示該體系的活性中間體為七價的錳氮氧化物。 綜上所述,d0金屬氮氧化物極有可能是新一類的高效活性中間體氧化劑。 本專案旨在研究該類型金屬氮氧化物特性,控制其活性、穩定性,以便設計發展更高效高活性的催化水氧化和有機物氧化體系。 本專案以七配位金屬氧化物和d0金屬氮氧化物活性中間體為切入點,致力於開發高效高活性的氧化催化劑、催化體系,填補了配位化學史上這兩類化合物的研究空白

11336816.label: Realisation of objectives
11336816.value: Overall speaking, the project objectives have been achieved. 1. A number of ruthenium complexes bearing various quaterpyridine ligands have been synthesized and their catalytic activities towards oxidation of various organic substrates have been studied. 2. A series of ruthenium complexes bearing hydroxyphenyl bipyridine ligands have been prepared and their catalytic activities towards water oxidation has been investigated. 3. A number of 7-coordinate osmium oxo complexes bearing quaterpyridine ligands have been synthesized and characterized. Oxidaiton of organic compounds by these complexes has been studied. 4. Osmium(VI) nitrido complexes bearing bidentate quinolinolato or pyridine carboxylate ligands have been synthesized. 5. A number of manganese(V) nitrido complexes bearing tetra-anionic ligands has been prepared and their reactivity towards organic substrates has been investigated.

11336816.label: Major findings and research outcome
11336816.value: Major findings: 1. A series of ruthenium complexes bearing various quaterpyridine ligands have been synthesized and characterized. Their catalytic activities towards oxidation of water and organic substrates has been investigated. 2. A series of ruthenium complexes bearing the hydroxyphenyl bipyridine ligand (dObpy) and derivatives have been synthesized and characterized. Their catalytic activities towards oxidation of water has been investigated. 3. A new 7-coordinate osmium(VI) nitrido complex bearing a quaterpyridine ligand has been synthesized and characterized. Its reactivity towards various organic substrates has been studied. 4. The osmium(VI) nitrido complex, OsVI(N)(quin)2(OTs) (1, quin = 2-quinaldinate, OTs = tosylate), is a highly selective and efficient catalyst for the ring hydroxylation of alkylbenzenes with H2O2 under ambient conditions. Oxidation of various alkylbenzenes occurs with ring/chain oxidation ratios ranging from 96.7/3.3 to 99.9/0.1, and total product yields from 93% to 98%. Moreover, turnover numbers (TONs) up to 6360, 5670 and 3880 can be achieved for the oxidation of p-xylene, ethylbenzene and mesitylene respectively. DFT calculations suggest that the active intermediate is an OsVIII nitrido oxo species. 5. A novel osmium(III) complex bearing the parent aminoguanidine, mer-[Os{NHC(NH2)(NHNH2)}(L)(CN)3]− (OsGNH2, HL = 2-(2-hydroxyphenyl)benzoxazole) has been generated from an osmium nitrido complex. The antioxidant properties of OsGNH2 have been investigated by reactions with various oxidants. 6. Various oxo and nitrido complexes prepared in this project are found to be activated by Lewis acids.

11336816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11336816.value: 1. The oxidizing properties of the ruthenium and osmium oxo and nitrido complexes can be further enhanced by varying the ancilliary ligands. 2. Activation of the oxo and nitrido complexes by Lewis acids should be further investigated. 3. In future, more efforts should be devoted to the design of oxidation catalysts based on cheap and earth abundant transition metals, such as iron, manganese, nickel and copper.

11337116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11337116.value: The proposal introduces a new concept on the spatial decoration of cocatalysts on photocatalysts that essentially allows the decoupling of Schottky barrier effect and that for surface charge transfer. This is to be achieved by spatially segregating the cocatalysts for each role and in an independent fashion. Cocatalysts with high work functions (Pt, Ir, Pd, Au) are to be deposited directly on the photocatalysts surface to maximise the charge separation across the Schottky barrier. The electron transfer cocatalysts (Pt, Ag, Pd/Co, Au/Pd and Ni/Fe) will be predeposited onto reduced graphene oxide prior to the attachment of the two components. To harness the wide spectrum of the solar irradiation, a range of wide and mid-bandgap oxide photocatalysts with suitable conduction band potentials (TiO2, SrTiO3, WO3, Ag3PO4, Ag3VO4, Bi2WO6, and BiVO4) will be synthesised and assessed as the base substrate for decoration with cocatalysts. Photocharge transport and the physicochemical properties will be characterized to verify the working mechanism of the advanced composite photocatalysts. The spatial deposition allows the selection of the best combinations of rational cocatalysts in surpassing the efficiencies of the conventional (but yet unsurpassed) single metal-deposited photocatalysts that practices the philosophy of “one cocatalyst fits all”. As such, the proposed strategy is a paradigm shift in terms of the architecture of high efficiency photocatalysts. In this proposal, the composite photocatalysts will be specifically designed for the solar abatement of a range of endocrine disruptors and antibiotics. Besides being emerging micropollutants with relevant global and regional concerns, the target substrates were carefully chosen to allow the studies of the efficacy of the photocatalysts in targeting certain molecular functional groups. Assessments will also be carried out as a function of water conditions, that is, water hardness, anions and cations, as well as the humic acid concentrations. Based on the laboratory-derived data and the measurement of action spectra of the photocatalysts, it will be possible to rationally construct the “rainbow photocatalysts” that maximize the coverage of the solar spectrum. Based on this, an outdoor reactor with flow over photocatalysts-coated corrugated plates will be constructed to showcase the abatement of the micropollutants to be assessed in real water samples collected from reservoirs in Hong Kong. The reactor will be engineered to maximize external and internal mass (reactants and products) diffusions into and out of the porous photocatalyst layer, effectiveness factor as well as solar light penetration. 此計劃於光觸媒上空間裝飾輔催化劑引入全新概念，這基本上容許把Schottky 屏障效應及表面電荷轉移分離，達致這功能全賴把輔催化劑為每個作用以獨立形式空間地分離。高功函輔催化劑 (鉑、銥、铅、金) 被直接沉積在光觸媒表面以於Schottky 屏障效應下把電荷分離最大化。這個電荷轉移輔催化劑 (鉑、銀、铅/鈷、金/铅及鎳/鐵) 將會在兩個組成部分附著前預先沉積在還原氧化石墨烯上。為了利用廣闊的太陽幅射光譜，一系列有合適導帶及中至闊能帶的氧化物光觸媒(TiO2, SrTiO3, WO3, Ag3PO4, Ag3VO4, Bi2WO6, and BiVO4 )將會為裝飾上輔催化劑作為基礎底材而合成及作出評估。同時亦會描述這個先進複合物光觸媒的光電荷傳輸及理化特性及證實其工作機制。 空間沉積容許選擇性把最佳合理的輔催化劑組合，這效率優於慣常單一萬用輔催化劑的傳統單金屬沉積光觸媒。確實，建議的策略乃高效光觸媒結構的典範改變。在這建議書，複合物光觸媒將會特別為以太陽能消除一系列內分泌干擾素及抗生素而設計。除了受全球及地區性關注的新的微污染物，為研究光觸媒對目標分子官能機的效能，目標底材亦會小心選擇。評估亦會以水的狀況為涵數，包括水硬度、陰離子及陽離子、及腐植酸的濃度。 基於實驗室獲得的數據及光觸煤的量度作用光譜，這將可能有理地建構出用於最大化太陽能光譜覆蓋的「彩虹光觸媒」，。建基於此，此計劃將會建造一個有光觸媒塗層的波浪形板戶外反應器，用於展示由香港水塘提取的真實水樣本的微污染物消除評估。這反應器亦會特別設計以達致最大化外在及內在質量(反應物及產物)於多孔光觸媒層的出入滲透、效用因子及太陽光滲透。

11337116.label: Realisation of objectives
11337116.value: Under the Objective 1, we developed a number of spatially-decorated photocatalysts that consisted of the supported cocatalysts on wide/mid-bandgap semiconductor metal oxides. These photocatalytic systems could be activated under visible light – the largest component of the freely-available solar spectrum. The spatial decoration of cocatalysts allowed for the modulation of the photocharge transport, while the suitable surface of the cocatalysts further promoted the otherwise slow step in surface charge transfer through various stoichiometric reactions. Under Objective 2, we characterized the relevant physicochemical and electrochemical properties of the photocatalysts to provide insights into the photoharge transport properties as well as to establish the properties-activity relationships. Under Objective 3, we demonstrated the high efficacy and in fact the recyclability of the catalysts in removing environmentally-relevant micropollutants. They include endocrine disruptors, pesticides, toxic metal ions, ammonia and carbon monoxide that are present at low concentrations and hence difficult to remediate using other existing means.

11337116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11337116.value: We developed a number of visible light photocatalysts with spatially-decorated cocatalysts for the abatement of different classes of micropollutants. These photocatalysts include Au nanoclusters/TiO2 (Output 8.1), Pd, Pt, Ag/BiVO4 (Output 8.3), Pt/MOx (TiO2, WO3) (Output 8.2), Mn-doped CdS/TiO2, (Output 8.6), Sn/FeOx (Output 8.5) and RGO/red P (Output 8.13). We found that the coupling of Pt, Pd and Ag cocatalysts to mid-bandgap photocatalysts such as BiVO4 and WO3 was essential to overcome the sluggish multielectron reduction (2H+ + O2 + 2e- -> H2O2; 4H+ + O2 + 4e- -> 2H2O) (Output 8.1, 8.3). Enhancing the rate of multielectron transfer de-bottlenecked the overall redox reactions, and this enhanced the overall rate of oxidation of organic micropollutants, hereby shown for the abatement of 7 type of endocrine disruptors and pesticides. We discovered the effectiveness of the thiolated Au nanoclusters in catalyzing the oxidation of more than 10 type of endocrine disruptors and pesticides under visible light (Output 8.1). To spatially separate the photocharges, the Au nanoclusters had to be supported on TiO2, as a visible light-inactive electron acceptor as well as the cocatalyst for the one-electron reduction of O2 (O2 + e- -> O2•-). We demonstrated the high durability of the Au nanocluster/TiO2 photocatalyst over at least 5 recycling runs (25 h irradiation). We reported a new mechanism for the reduction of hexavalent chromium. The formation of chromate ester from the reaction between the toxic hexavalent chromium and alcohol, was found to undergo homogeneous photodecomposition to the benign trivalent chromium when surface-coordinated on the metal oxide photocatalyst (Output 8.2). The combined mechanisms of homogeneous and heterogeneous reduction gave rise to the enhanced activity under visible light. Additional efforts were made to develop visible light photocatalysts, i.e., Mn2+-CdS/TiO2, Sn4+/FeOx and RGO/red P that treat micropollutants in wastewater and at the same time produces gaseous hydrogen. Systematic relationships on the size and types of organics and their hydrogen evolution rates were established (Output 8.6, 8.7, 9.1-9.7). We reported the first ever direct evidence of the current doubling effects. We found that atomically-dispersed Mn2+, Sn4+ and Cu2+ cocatalysts (Output 8.5, 8.6, 8.9-8.11) were beneficial in promoting the oxidation of micropollutant, both aqueous and airborne.

11337116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11337116.value: Through the project, we developed a plethora of spatially-decorated photocatalysts for the abatement of micropollutants under visible light (Output 8.1-8.7, 8.13). In particular, we carried out our studies based on the pollutants that are relevant to Hong Kong and the Greater China, including those of endocrine disruptors, pesticides, heavy metals, and gaseous pollutants (Output 8.4). We have laid the foundations on the variation of cocatalysts (i.e., metal nanoparticles, metal clusters, atomically-dispersed metal ions) to target specific redox reactions in the abatement of micropollutants, and how they can be paired with the visible light-active photocatalysts to achieve optimum efficiencies (Output 8.1-8.13). These are the underlying fundamentals that paves the way for the development of more efficient photocatalysts in the near future. The same technology will be extended to the treatment of antibiotics and pathogens found in the open environment. Perhaps interestingly, we also extended the knowledge to the simultaneous treatment of micropollutants in wastewater and the enhanced production of solar hydrogen. The technology is in line with the Hydrogen Economy 2.0 and has attracted the interests of the Drainage Services Department of Hong Kong (Output 8.6). In fact, we have shown the ability to continuously produce solar hydrogen from wastewater (collected from various domestic Wastewater Treatment Plants) under solar irradiation (Output 9.1-9.7). Efforts are underway for potential scale up applications.

11337116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11337116.value: New photocatalysts that can be activated under visible light (the largest component of solar spectrum) were designed specifically for the abatement of environmental micropollutants. These photocatalysts consisted of spatially-decorated cocatalysts that helped to enhance the overall redox reactions, thus allowing the efficient remediation endocrine disruptors, pesticides, heavy metals, industrial and even gaseous pollutants. This is a significant effort towards improving the advent of environmental technologies relevant to the Hong Kong and the Greater China. In fact, the technology was even extended to couple with clean energy production, where the capacity for solar hydrogen production was enhanced while treating the target pollutants in wastewater. This is in line with the wider effort in securing clean and sustainable energy technologies in the region. In terms of local workforce development, the project has contributed to the training of 2 PhD and 5 undergraduate students.

11337216.value: 静态或涨落约束下的最优过渡路径

11337216.label: Project Objectives
11337216.value: Develop action functional and efficient algorithms for constrained Minimum Action Method: We derive the correct variational problem in the large deviation theory for the constrained stochastic differential equation on a static and smooth manifold. The non-trivial algorithms of the constrained minimum action method for this problem will be pursued to efficiently account for the constraints and the state-dependent diffusion tensor. Formulate the large deviation result for fast-slow system when the manifold for constraints is subject to rapid random motion: To handle the coupled multi-scale stochastic systems for both the diffusion particle and the fluctuating manifold, we use the path integral formulation of Martin-Siggia-Rose and Doi-Peliti approach of second quantization to derive the large deviation results. Algorithmic development of the minimum action method to calculate the transition path in the slow-fast stochastic dynamics: Design and develop the minimum action method, based on the rate function derived above, for the slow-fast stochastic dynamics by the techniques from multi-scale method and stochastic programming. The exploration of saddle points on the averaged systems will also be investigated based on previous work.

Formulate the large deviation result for fast-slow system when the manifold for constraints is subject to rapid random motion: To handle the coupled multi-scale stochastic systems for both the diffusion particle and the fluctuating manifold, we use the path integral formulation of Martin-Siggia-Rose and Doi-Peliti approach of second quantization to derive the large deviation results.

Algorithmic development of the minimum action method to calculate the transition path in the slow-fast stochastic dynamics: Design and develop the minimum action method, based on the rate function derived above, for the slow-fast stochastic dynamics by the techniques from multi-scale method and stochastic programming. The exploration of saddle points on the averaged systems will also be investigated based on previous work.

11337216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11337216.value: 我们研究局限在欧几里得状态空间的一个给定的子流形上的随机动力系统的小噪音引起的过渡路径。这个问题源于某些受内在构形约束或局限在细胞膜上的扩散分子的稀有事件的研究。任何外部随机扰动必须尊重这些物理限制。约束不仅降低有效的自由度，而且也导致跟自由扩散显著不同的转移过渡的行为。甚至更有趣的情况是当与约束相关联的流形本身也在做随机移动。这种差异已经在膜的横向有效扩散系数的问题的研究上得到非常明确的确认和探讨。约束造成的独特的针对非平衡转移过渡行为的影响，将在此研究计划中通过大偏差理论和作用量最小化算法的新的发展进行研究。 我们考虑两种情况的约束流形：静态情况和波动情况。前一种情况对应于一组确定性和时间无关的限制，这密切联系经典的流形上的随机微分方程。而流形随机涨落的情况，在数学上更具挑战性，但实际上更重要。细胞生物膜通常是受到热涨落，使得膜的形状在时间上随机变化，但非常迅速。因此存在着分子慢运动和膜表面的快速波动的时间尺度特征。 本提案将在理论和发展数值方法来模拟并计算上述两种情况中的约束随机动力学流形上的最佳的过渡路径。对于静态情况下，基于在欧氏空间中Friedlin-Wentzell的大偏差理论传统的最小作用量方法将被推广到设计约束最小的操作方法。对于波动的情况下，我们应采用路径积分的框架追求的基本大原则来求得大的偏差率函数的平均形式。然后，我们将通过探索多尺度技术和从随机规划的随机梯度方法集中在对所获得的最小化问题的有效的数值算法。从这个研究项目的结果将是可能为生物物理学和材料科学更逼真的模型许多解决事件的问题提供帮助。

11337216.label: Realisation of objectives
11337216.value: For objective 1 on algorithmic development, we have the works on the constrained transition path method(constrained MAM). They can handle the static constraint manifold very well, including for applications from active matters. We also developed the constrained method even for transition state calculation. Objective 2 is achieved by the alternative traditional large deviation approach of Freidlin-Wentzell, not the proposal technical idea. The last objective is achieved by working on the various multi-scale problems and the rare events problems, including the applications to slow-fast coupled stochastic PDEs.

11337216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11337216.value: We complete this project quite completely by developing and exploring new numerical algorithms and applications to new types of rare events. Our method of simplified gentlest ascent dynamics appeared in Chaos, 2018. As one of the major applications, "Stochastic dynamics of an active particle escaping from a potential well" also appeared in Chaos, 2020 later. For the constraint shape of the limit cycle, our work appeared in Journal of Nonlinear Science 2019. There are some other minor works, e.g., the co-work with my Ph.D. student published in Commun. Comput. Phys., in 2018. Overall, the major funding in this project has contributed to this topic on handling constraints and rare events.

11337216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11337216.value: we find the constraint of mass/density conservation in fact has attracted many other researchers such as the transition in the probability space and the physical application of Bose-Einstein condensation, despite the simple constraint forms. More intrinsic modeling, instead of the ambient space with external constraints, might be quite natural and computation feasible for some problems like optimal transport in probability space.

11337216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11337216.value: Noise-induced transition events are ubiquitous in many areas of natural sciences with applications from large thermal fluctuations of molecules, configuration changes of polymers, emergent behaviours of interacting agents. In many practical applications, there exist many constraints, like the constant length of rigid molecules, the conservation of mass, and so on. By modelling these constraint by mathematical models like stochastic diffusion equations on a manifold, we investigate the rare events like how a random particle behaves on vibrating manifolds and develop various effective numerical methods to compute these rare events.

11337516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11337516.value: Ever since the importance of stereochemistry in carbon-containing compounds had been established, the making of enantiopure compounds became one of important goal of synthetic chemists and it is still one of the important goals of synthetic chemists today. To make enantiopure compounds, one of the most efficient ways is to use chiral catalyst. Traditionally, chiral catalyst can be formed with a ligand that has chiral carbon atom or atoms to coordinate with a metal ion. This approach has made great progress and there are a great number of catalysts that are made this way. Another approach is to use chiral catalyst based on chiral-at-metal complex. One can use chiral or achiral ligand in this case. Much less has been done using the chiral-at-metal approach and in this proposal, we propose to develop syntheses of chiral-at-metal complexes and use them as catalyst in organic transformations. Several different methods to synthesize new chiral-at metal complexes are detailed. 自從含碳化合物的立體化學的重要性被闡明之後，制備單一手性化合物就成為合成化學家的重要目標之一，至今仍是。採用手性催化劑是製備單一手性化合物最有效的方法之一。傳統意義上講，手性催化劑可以由含有手性碳原子的配體與金屬離子配位而得。這種方法已經取得了長足的發展，並且已經有大量的手性催化劑通過這種方法制備得到。另一種方法是利用那些手性中心在金屬上的配合物作為手性催化劑。這種情況下，手性或者非手性的配體都是可用的。採用這種手性中心位於金屬離子的方法進行的研究相比前述另一種方法少得多。在此，我們設計開發一種合成手性中心位於金屬的配合物，並且把它們用於有機物的轉化。在此，我們詳細闡述幾種不同的用於合成新的手性配合物的方法.

11337616.value: 2009年以來，薄膜的鈣鈦礦材料在太陽能發電領域的應用引起了社會各界極大關注，也吸引著潛心科研人員的濃厚興趣。目前太陽能電池的效率已高達20％。 膠體納米鈣鈦礦量子點（PQDs）是一個比較新的研究課題。 CH3NH3PbBr3 (MAPbBr3) PQDs由Perez-Prieto在2014年首次報導，利用中等碳鍊長度的配體穩定在有機溶劑中。這個材料具備高的光致發光量子產率和可調諧的發射波長，具有在發光器件（LED）、激光器、生物標記等不同領域的應用潛力。影響PQD的因素，包括尺寸、結構以及機理，在技術上是非常基礎和重要。儘管在這個領域有一些突破，但是對材料的合成仍然是一個挑戰。 目前，世界各地的研究人員發表20餘篇研究論文。已經報導方法具有若干缺點，例如所得到的材料的穩定性不足、形成機制有待充分探討等。 我們課題組最近發表的研究成果表明，在MAPbBr3 PQDs中存在量子限制效應，合成的材料在藍色/綠色光譜區的光致發光量子產率迄今為止最高，高達93％。這個研究計劃的最初階段將著重了解控制PQD的形成機制，進而獲得在整個可見光譜範圍內強發光而且穩定PQDs。通過使用不同的穩定劑，以及反應溫度為關鍵參數，實現對PQDs尺寸，形狀（球體，立方體，納米片和納米棒）的操控，並且對得到的PQDs進行表面保護。對形成機制的理解，可以為我們提供瞭如何進一步優化PQDs的光學性能提供方向。同時，我們也將對新型無鉛PQD，例如基於Sn或Ge的鈣鈦礦進行探索。 本項目的第二階段將著重於對已經合成的PQDs進行改性，從而提高它們的化學和光學穩定性。使用二氧化矽或聚合物對PQDs進行包覆，保護它們免受環境影響。 在本項目的第三階段，我們將之前獲得具有寬光譜覆蓋、可調發射光譜、高發光量子產率和穩定性良好的PQD用於發光器件（包括熒光轉換型白光LED和電致發光顏色可調的LED）。

11337616.label: Realisation of objectives
11337616.value: All the objectives of this project have been achieved. In relation to the objective 1, the following research activities have been performed: We have shown that the ligand-assisted reprecipitation (LARP) synthetic technique which was previously suggested by our group is a powerful method to synthesize bandgap-tunable CH3NH3PbBr3 NCs both at room temperature and at elevated temperature by using different concentrations of the precursors. The emission peaks of the synthesized NCs covered the range of 455–516 nm and high photoluminescence (PL) quantum yield (QY) reaching 70% for larger particles. We addressed in details the role of the two ligands (oleic acid and oleylamine) which are commonly used for the synthesis of CH3NH3PbBr3 NCs in terms of the coordination of the lead precursors and the NC surface. Chemical forms of the Pb precursor in the presence of these two capping ligands are affected upon imposing a pre-aging process and/or adjusting the ligand feeding sequence. Chemical forms of the metal-organic precursor are directly correlated with the effective supplying rate of the precursors when forming target nanoparticles, which consequently exhibits strong influences on the size-regulation ability. The growth mechanism of perovskite NCs has been elucidated by combining the experimental results with the principles of nucleation/growth models. The proposed formation mechanism of perovskite NCs will be helpful for further studies in this field and will be used as a guide to improve the synthetic methods. In another series of experiments, we addressed the key synthetic parameters (the sequence of solvent mixing, volume ratio of solvents, and the amount of ligands), which all determine the supersaturation driving the formation of CH3NH3PbBr3 colloidal particles in LARP synthesis. Single crystalline CH3NH3PbBr3 cubes (~500 nm) and rods (length 2-4.5μm, width ~100nm) were fabricated by varying these parameters, in particular the amount of ligands. XRD and HRTEM studies demonstrated that CH3NH3PbBr3 rods experience preferred growth orientation along the [100] crystallographic direction. Investigation of the nucleation and growth processes in the framework of the classical theory of crystal growth implied that the degree of supersaturation in the formation of perovskite cubes is higher than that in the formation of rods. The amount of octylamine introduced differently shaped nuclei, which eventually accounted for the anisotropic growth. We developed a top-down method for the fabrication of CH3NH3PbBr3 and CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite nanocrystals, employing a mixture of ligands oleic acid and oleylamine as coordinating solvents. Our approach avoids the use of any polar solvents, skips multiple reaction steps by employing a simple ultrasonic treatment of the perovskite precursors, and yields rather monodisperse blue, green, and red emitting methylammonium lead halide nanocrystals with a high (up to 72% for the green-emitting ones) photoluminescence quantum yield and remarkably improved stability. In relation to the objective 2, the following activities have been performed: Post-synthetic modifications of PQDs in order to improve their emission characteristics have been performed within the activities listed above under “Objective 1”. We have also conducted a literature search and provided a detailed literature analysis giving insights into two important issues inherent to lead halide perovskite nanocrystals, namely the advantages of defect-tolerance, and the ways how to improve their stability in environmental conditions. The defect-tolerance of lead halide perovskites offers an impetus to search for similar attributes in other related heavy metal-free compounds. We have found the origins of the significantly blue-shifted emission from CsPbBr3 nanocrystals, and the synthetic strategies towards fabrication of stable perovskite nanocrystal materials with emission in the red and infrared parts of the optical spectrum, which are related to fabrication of mixed cation compounds guided by Goldschmidt tolerance factor considerations. In relation to the objective 3, the following research activities have been performed: We conducted steady-state, time-resolved and excitation power dependent PL studies of CH3NH3PbBr3 cubes and rods, with the latter exhibiting higher PL QY and longer PL average lifetimes. Longer PL lifetime of the rods was attributed to the longer diffusion pathway in the axial direction for free electron-hole recombination. With the increase of the excitation power, both cubes and rods showed an emission threshold that correlated with the density of defect states, with the conclusion that the lower defect density of CH3NH3PbBr3 rods determined their high PL QY as compared to cubes. Optical phonon energies have been estimated from the broadness of the emission peaks of the both kinds perovskite particles. Our findings provide new insights into the shape dependent PL properties in colloidal CH3NH3PbBr3 systems. We synthesized hydrophobic-capped NCs of formamidinium lead bromide perovskite showing bright and stable fluorescence in solution and thin film states. When compared with isolated NCs in a solution, close-packed NCs in a thin film show extended fluorescence lifetime (ca 4.2 µs), which is due to hoping or migration of photo-generated excitons among NCs. Both fluorescence quantum efficiency and lifetime decreased in a NC thin film doped with C60, which is attributed to channeling of exciton migration in the NC film into electron transfer to fullerenes. On the other hand, quenching of fluorescence intensity of a NC solution was not accompanied by any change in fluorescence lifetime, indicating static electron transfer to C60 molecules adsorbed onto hydrophobic surface of individual perovskite NCs. Exciton migration among close-packed NCs and electron transfer to C60 places C60-doped perovskite NC thin films among cost-eﬀective antenna systems for solar cells. In collaboration with Prof. Lounis from University of Bordeaux (France), we have used magneto-photoluminescence spectroscopy of individual perovskite CsPbBr3 nanocrystals as a unique tool to determine their crystal structure, which imprints distinct signatures in the excitonic sublevels of charge complexes at low temperatures. At zero magnetic field, the identification of two classes of PL spectra, displaying either two or three sublevels in their exciton fine structure, showed evidence for the existence of two crystalline structures, namely tetragonal D4h and orthorhombic D2h phases. Magnetic field shifts, splitting and coupling of the sublevels provide a determination of the diamagnetic coefficient and valuable information on the exciton g-factor and its anisotropic character. Moreover, this spectroscopic study revealed the optical properties of charged excitons which allows the extraction of the electron and hole g-factors for perovskite systems. In relation to the objective 4, the following research activities have been performed: We have used perovskite NCs synthesized by top-down approach to produce white LEDs, which have been fabricated by combining the green-emitting CH3NH3PbBr3 NC@POSS powder with a red-emitting K2SiF6:Mn4+ phosphor, followed by their dispersion in a silicone resin and deposition onto a commercially available blue-emitting InGaN LED chip. Emission spectrum of the resulting WLED was a combination of three emission peaks: green one from perovskite NCs, red one from the K2SiF6:Mn4+ phosphor, and blue one from the InGaN chip. The position of the emission maximum for CH3NH3PbBr3 NC@POSS was in a good correlation with the solid-state PL peak of the CH3NH3PbBr3 NCs powder. The CIE chromaticity coordinate of this WLED was (0.30, 0.33), which is very close to the optimal white light positioning. The luminous efficiency was 38 lmW-1, two times stronger than that for the incandescent lamp (17 lmW-1). The spectral profiles of such WLEDs were preserved for a broad range of operation currents (20-120 mA). Moreover, we have fabricated several types of charge-injection perovskite LEDs, which went beyond the original plans of this project to demonstrate some prototypes of down-conversion LEDs, only. We will elaborate on this point under section 6.2 below.

11337616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11337616.value: This project was very successful, and has generated 19 original research papers and 3 review articles in high-impact research journals, including Nature Communication, NanoLetters, ACS Energy, and Materials Today. I allow me to stress that this has been one of the most successful outcome of any of my research projects completed in Hong Kong, so far. All the objectives of this project has been successfully achieved, as outlined in the section 5.3 above. This includes the development of novel synthetic routes towards perovskite nanocrystals of different sizes and shapes with a strong emission all over the visible spectral range; also different shapes of those nanocrystals (nanocubes, nanowires, etc) have been demonstrated. Perovskite nanocrystals have been fabricated using mostly the so-called "bottom up" (chemical synthesis in solution), but also the "top-down" fragmentation synthetic approaches. Growth mechanism of both nucleation and growth of perovskite nanoparticles have been elucidated in detail, which resulted in publication in Nature Communication in 2017. The stability of perovskite nanocrystals has been improved by applying a proper surface engineering strategy, and by fabricating heterostructured nanocrystals combined with a PbSe component; these materials have been used for device fabrication (photodetectors and sloar cells). The reasons behind emission quenching and recovery of illuminated perovskite nanocrystals have been revealed, and ascribed to consequences of halide ion migration. Exciton and biexciton dynamics has been studied on single perovskite nanocrystals without and under applying magnetic fields, which allowed for insightful details into the photopysical processes. The relation of exciton features of perovskite nanocrystals of different sizes to Mie resonances have been studies both theoretically and in experiment. A variety of not only down-conversion (excitation by light) but also more sophisticated charge-injection LEDs based on perovskite nanocrystals has been fabricated and studied, offering important insights into engineering of these devices. High external conversion efficiencies in the range of 10-15% have been achieved.

11337616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11337616.value: This project provided a solid foundation for the further development of research on light-emitting perovskite nanocrystals. Not only it has delivered perovskite materials with a strong, size- and shape-dependent emission, and allowed to established post-preparative procedures aimed on significant enhancement of their stability. It has also resulted in series of LEDs with record performance characteristics, such as those based on red-emitting iodide perovskite nanocrystals whose emission was improved by simultaneous silver doping and surface passivation, or strontium doping and chlorine surface passivation. Bright emission from lead-free 2D perovskites and from Zn-alloyed iodide based perovskite nanocrystals has been demonstrated, as well. In the course of further action, we will focus on further improvements of both performance and stability of such LEDs, and on making perovskite LEDs with polarised emission for use in displays.

11337616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11337616.value: Due to the high photoluminescence quantum yield and tunable emission, perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) have potential applications in different areas such as light emitting devices (LEDs). Development of the understanding of general synthetic principles regarding size, structure and mechanisms behind PQD formation is of immense fundamental and technological importance. This proposal has focused on elucidation and control of the PQD formation mechanism, and development of the synthesis of stable PQDs that are strongly emitting over the whole visible spectral range. This has been achieved through the use of different stabilizers, as well as reaction temperature as key parameters to manipulate the size, shape, and surface protection of the PQDs. Understanding of the formation mechanism provided us with clues on how to optimize the optical performance of PQDs. The resulting broad range of PQD emitters with emission tunability, high emission quantum yield, and good environmental stability has been used in the final stage of the project to produce phosphor-converter type white LEDs, and electroluminescent color tunable LEDs.

11337716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11337716.value: “Click Chemistry” refers to the establishment of versatile chemical linkages between molecular units via a series of “spring-loaded” chemical reactions under mild conditions. Amongst a variety of “click” reactions, some require photo-activation to react. These photo-triggered “click” processes enable precise spatial and temporal control of the molecular conjugation events and are much welcomed in the fields of synthetic chemistry, materials sciences and chemical biology. However, other than a few examples, most of the “photo-click” processes demand relative high photo-activation energy (excitation wavelength < 400 nm) to initiate and are, therefore, not very compatible to biomedical applications as high-energy photo-excitation may induce photo-toxicity in in vitro and in vivo systems. Our research team has developed an arenylmethyl phosphonium-based photo-triggered traceless Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation system that can “photo-click” molecular units with peptide bonds. At the moment, the optimal excitation wavelength of the system is 376 nm. Preliminary theoretical energy-level calculation suggests that this may be altered by perturbing the electronic properties of the arenyl and phenyl moieties of the phoshonium salts. In this project, we will investigate the mechanism of the photolysis of the arenylmethyl phosphonium system, and the related benzhydryl phosphonium system, by laser flash photolysis. A series of new phosphonium salts with various electron-donating and withdrawing substituents to their arenyl/benzhydryl and phenyl components will be synthesized to evaluate their photo-induced Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation reactivity. With a better understanding of the mechanism of the photo-triggering Staudinger-Bertozzi ligation process, reagents responsive to different excitation wavelengths can be developed. Selective and sequential “photo-click” processes can then be realized for bioconjugation, materials fabrication & functional surface modification. “點擊化學”乃指一系列可在溫和條件下將分子單元連結的化學反應 。若這樣的 “點擊”反應能受光線控制，將可大大提升它們在合成化學，材料科學和化學生物學領域中的工用。 然而，除了個別例子之外，大多數光控“點擊” 反應匀需要紫外光 （波長<400nm）來引發。這樣的高能光線，不能應用於生物醫學之上。我們的研究團隊早前開發了一種基於甲基鏻的光觸發無痕Staudinger-Bertozzi反應，乃一種全新的光控點擊化學反應。當時的最佳激發波長為376nm，仍然屬紫外光波段。我們現在掌握初步的理論能級計算數據，推斷可通過改變磷鎓鹽的芳烴基和苯基部分的電子性質而將激發波長推至可見光波段。在這個項目中，我們將研究苯甲基甲基鏻體系和相關的二苯甲基鏻體系的光解作用的機理。並通過激光閃光光解以及在其芳基/二苯甲基上引入一系列不同電子特性的功能團，改變我們的光觸發無痕Staudinger-Bertozzi反應的最佳激發波長。我們希望可開發出能響應不同激發波長的點擊化學連結劑，實現在生物共軛及材料科學上達到高選擇性和可編程的點擊連結作業。

11338016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11338016.value: Silicon (Si) and metal oxides are promising candidates for the next-generation Li-ion battery anode materials as substitute for existing commercial graphite anodes because of their high theoretical specific capacities, abundance, easy preparation, and low cost. These candidates have many advantages, but their poor electrical conductivity and slow Li-ions diffusion in solid bulk materials greatly limit the rate capabilities for fast charge/discharge. In addition, the dramatic volume change in these elements during charge/discharge results in pulverization and exfoliation from the current collector, leading to poor cycling performance and rapid capacity decay. Thus, the practical applications of Si and metal oxides are greatly challenged until today given their poor rate and cycling capability. This project aims to synthesize a versatile 3D hierarchical graphene networks@mesoporous carbon (3D-HGN@MPC) core-shell nanostructure and incorporate it with Si and metal oxides to obtain high-performance anode materials. This project is the first synthesis of a hierarchical carbon structure with a 3D graphene network core and a mesoporous carbon shell, whose thickness and pore size are tunable. The synthesis is based on a layer-by-layer assembly and a soft template method for mesoporous carbon through template removal, graphene oxide reduction, heat-induced assembly, and polymer carbonization. 3D-HGN@MPC is first integrated with nano Si (and metal oxides), and the hierarchical 3D graphene layer then fills the void space between the Si (and metal oxides) core and the outer carbon shell. Filling the void space can further improve electronic conductivity compared with the electrodes with a common yolk-shell structure. In addition, this unique 3D-HGN@MPC carbon material with 3D hierarchical interconnected pores facilitates the infiltration of electrolyte to ensure the efficient interfacial contact among electrolyte ions, electroactive materials, and mesoporous carbon shell. These features lead to excellent rate performance of the electrode and provide great potential for fast charge and discharge in practical applications. The dual protection provided by the 3D graphene layer and the mesoporous carbon shell can effectively buffer and restrict the volume change of the electroactive materials and thus increase cycle stability. This project will deliver important theoretical and experimental bases for designing exceptional anode materials with high capacity, high rate, and long cycle life. 硅及金属氧化物由于其高比容量被认为是目前最有希望替代商业石墨的锂离子电池负极材料，然而充放电过程中巨大的体积变化导致循环性能欠佳的缺点限制了其商业化。本项目拟将作为电活性物质的纳米硅和金属氧化物分别与新颖的三维分级石墨烯网络@介孔碳(3D-HGN@MPC)核壳结构的碳材料复合，以获得高性能的负极材料。将首次以逐层自组装结合软模板制备介孔碳的方法为基础，经过模板移除、氧化石墨烯还原、高温诱导下自组装、以及聚合物碳化等步骤得到内部为三维石墨烯网络，外壳为厚度和孔径可调的介孔碳的新颖分级碳材料。这种3D-HGN@MPC核壳结构的碳材料具有相互连通的三维分级多孔结构，能确保电解液、活性物质以及碳外壳三者间更有效地接触；同时三维石墨烯层与介孔碳外壳的双重保护能有效地限制活性物质体积的变化，提高循环稳定性和倍率性能。本项目研究将为设计高容量、高倍率以及长寿命的锂离子电池负极材料提供有效方法和科学依据。

11338016.label: Realisation of objectives
11338016.value: (1) This project developed nitrogen-doped hierarchical porous carbon and carbon nanotube hybrids (N-HPC-CNTs) by simple pyrolysis of the N-rich raw material melamine-formaldehyde (MF) resin in the presence of nano-CaCO3 template to create a hierarchical porous structure and bimetallic combination of Fe–Co catalyst for CNTs growth. During carbonization, the MF resin is converted into hierarchical porous carbon and the N atoms originated from MF resin are in-situ doped into the carbon matrix simultaneously. Such N-doped carbon with micro/mesopores can effectively prompt the physical and chemical adsorption of polysulfides. Meanwhile, the thermal decomposition of MF resin and released volatile gases could serve as carbon and nitrogen sources to grow nitrogen doped CNTs on HPC. The growth mechanism is the same as that for conventional CVD growth of CNTs on the metal catalysts, but the technological requirements are obviously not as harsh as those for CVD method. Low-cost raw materials and simple equipment are sufficient for the growth. Furthermore, the porosity of HPC, the density and length of the CNTs are tunable, which can be simply adjusted via applying different amounts of Fe–Co catalysts. Such a hybrid structure not only possesses a large surface area and pore volume for sulfur impregnation, but also ensures a fast electron transfer because of the incorporation of CNTs, which provides sufficient conducting pathways and effective connections between the CNTs and HPC. Furthermore, CNTs grown on HPC can act as physical barriers to block the large pores on HPC, thereby reducing the polysulfides loss. Benefiting from the aforementioned advantages of the N-HPC-CNTs, the N-HPC-CNTs/S cathode with 62.5 wt% sulfur exhibits a high initial discharge capacity of 1181 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C (1 C = 1675 mA g−1, based on sulfur weight) and a high rate capability of 624 mAh g-1 at 1 C, as well as excellent long-term cycling stability at a current rate of 1 C with only 0.066% capacity decay per cycle for over 600 cycles. The N-HPC-CNTs hybrids are desirable host prospect for Li-S batteries. (2) This project obtained a Cu-CuO-Ni sandwich structure with high surface area and low Li nucleation over-potential. The CuO exhibited much lower Li nucleation over-potential compared with that of Cu when electrochemical plating Li, and thus induced a uniform Li nucleation. In addition, the in-situ formed Cu layer on the surface acted as a protecting layer inhibiting structure collapse during the prolonging cyclic process. Furthermore, the Cu nanowire arrays made the electric field and Li+ ion flux evenly distributed due to the decreased local current density. Based on these synergetic effects, the Cu-CuO-Ni sandwich structure exhibited low nucleation over-potential and thus maintained a high Coulombic efficiency above 95% for more than 250 cycles of repeated Li plating and stripping at a current density of 1 mA cm-2 when used as a current collector. Meanwhile, it was stable for 580 h repeated Li plating and stripping in a symmetric cell. This strategy emphasizes the importance of micro-structure and interface design of the current collector, and is instructional to explore other transition metal oxides with low Li nucleation over-potential to achieve stable Li metal anodes. (3) This project achieved sulfur encapsulated inside the N-doped hollow carbon sphere and 3D interconnected graphene framework through the self-conversion template and the self-assembly route. We demonstrated that N-doped hollow carbon spheres played multiple roles in the fabrication of such an architecture and significantly suppressed the shuttling effect. On the one hand, hollow carbon spheres can act as scaffolds for the self-assembly of the 3D interconnected graphene framework. The carbon shell can provide physical confinement in the conversion reaction of ZnS into sulfur to avoid the large aggregation of sulfur and graphene. On the other hand, the hollow carbon shell can serve as an electrolyte reservoir and physical barrier to block the soluble polysulfides from directly diffusing into the bulk electrolyte. Moreover, the simultaneous introduction of nitrogen into the carbon matrix induced a strong chemical adsorption ability to trap polysulfide. The introduction of graphene in constructing a 3D conductive network that is interconnected with different S@NHC spheres under plane-to-point mode can facilitate continuous electron transfer in different dimensions, thereby increasing the conductivity of the whole electrode. Consequently, the obtained S@NHC-G cathode exhibited a considerably high capacity, an excellent rate performance, and a long-term cycling stability. These attributes suggested that S@NHC-GFW can be a promising design for Li-S batteries. (4) Many interesting results have been achieved (please refer to the publications in item 8 of Part C: Research Output), which are considered as the by-products of this project.

11338016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11338016.value: Although much progress has been made in this project, further development could be performed. First, the graphene content needs to be better controlled. If the graphene content exceeds a certain limit, it might lead to poor packing density hence poor volumetric energy density of the lithium ion battery. Second, the scheme for synthesis of silicon and metal oxide nanoparticles hybridized with 3D-HGN@MPC can be further improved. Third, more work can be carried out to further establish the relationship among the composition, structure, and electrochemical performance of 3D-HGN@MPC integrated with nano silicon and metal oxides. Fourth, the investigation on the transfer mechanism of electron and electrolyte ions clearly demonstrates that the challenges faced by lithium ion battery can be addressed by achieving innovation in the design and optimization of new electrode materials; consequently, more effort can be put for developing innovative electrode materials.

11338216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11338216.value: 近年由於人類對包括抗生素在內的藥物的廣泛使用與排放，環境中該類物質的分佈與風險已成為全球關注的問題。這類化學品由於對非目標生物體的潛在毒性，已被視為重要的環境污染物。由於市政，醫院、農業和工業廢水廣泛而持續的排放，此類化學品廣泛分佈於沿岸的表層海水、河岸地區，湖泊甚至在飲用水中，使得它們成為環境中的“偽持久性”污染物。另外一個藥物的重要污染源是水產養殖。為了應對快速增長的人口，水產養殖產量在過去的20年間顯著增長。越來越多的證據顯示，大量不同類型的獸藥尤其是抗生素，被廣泛應用於水產養殖點以控制水產疾病及促進生長。這導致了水產養殖產品及養殖設施附近環境的藥物殘留問題。可以想像的是，這些化學品可對水生生態系統產生不利影響，最終將對公眾和環境健康構成風險。 目前常用的藥物中，有超過一半是手性化合物。手性藥物能以對映異構體（enantiomers）的形式存在，這些對映異構體具有相似的理化特性，但能產生不同的生物作用。換句話說，這些藥物的效力和毒性是與其手性特質相關的。例如，S(-)-thalidomide可導致胚胎的嚴重畸形發展，而R(+)-thalidomide卻是一種有效的鎮靜劑。據報導，手性藥物及它們的對映異構體的相對組成可通過生物轉化，如人類或動物代謝，污水處理中的微生物過程改變。最近的監測研究結果表明在香港及珠江口的沿海地區普遍存在藥物殘留的問題。初步研究結果進一步表明，本地監測到的藥物有高達20%為手性藥物。如果環境條件有利毒性較高的對映異構體富集，當前與藥物相關的風險便有可能被嚴重低估。 雖然手性藥物可能對水生生態系統和人類健康具有潛在威脅，環境中手性藥物的對映選擇性歸趨的研究目前仍然非常有限。本研究將針對目標環境樣品，開發多種非手性及手性的人藥與獸藥的定性定量分析方法，以揭示水生環境中手性藥物及它們的對映異構體的相對組成，並研究其分佈、歸趨及潛在毒性。

11338216.label: Realisation of objectives
11338216.value: Objective 1: To determine the enantiomeric distribution of pharmaceutical compounds commonly used in Hong Kong (HK) by developing methods for multi-class quantification of achiral and chiral human and veterinary pharmaceuticals belonging to 17 therapeutic classes in sewage, surface water, sediments and fish In the first year, based on our prior experience working with brominated flame retardants (BFRs), we developed analytical methods for chiral compounds using two representative chiral BFRs, 1,2,5,6,9,10-hexabromocyclododecane (HBCD) and 1,2-dibromo-4-(1,2-dibromoethyl) cyclohexane (TBECH). Essentially, determination of HBCD stereoisomers was performed using high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-MS/MS consisting of an Agilent (Palo Alto, CA, USA) 1290 Infinity LC coupled to an AB SCIEX (Woodlands, Singapore) QTRAP 3200 MS/MS system with an electrospray ionization (ESI) interface in negative multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode. Determination of TBECH enantiomers was performed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) comprising an Agilent (Shanghai, China) 7890A GC coupled to an Agilent (Santa Clara, CA, USA) 5975C inert XL MSD with triple axis detector in negative chemical ionization (CI) mode. These analytical procedures for the identification and quantification of a total of sixteen stereoisomers of HBCD and TBECH were successfully applied to surface sediments, mollusks, crustaceans, fishes, and blubber of marine mammals, which constitute the key components of an important marine food web in Hong Kong waters. Trophic magnification potentials of (−)-α- and (+)-α-HBCD were observed in the food web, and the enantioselective bioaccumulation of the first eluting enantiomer of δ-TBECH in animals at higher trophic levels was consistently detected across samples (Details are given in Publications 1 and 2). During the second and third year, on the basis of the work on HBCD and TBECH, we successfully developed robust and sensitive analytical methods for the identification and quantification of a range of achiral and chiral human and veterinary pharmaceuticals in water, sludge, mollusks, crustaceans, and fishes. For this part of the project, special focus was placed on four commonly used pharmaceuticals in Hong Kong which are of high environmental concern. They were atenolol, metoprolol, venlafaxine, and chloramphenicol. Basic compounds, namely atenolol, metoprolol, and venlafaxine, were determined in positive MRM mode, while chloramphenicol, an acidic compound, was determined in negative MRM mode via gradient elution. We have successfully applied these analytical methods for achiral and chiral human and veterinary pharmaceuticals in water and sludge samples. Objective 2: To investigate and identify the factors determining the changes of enantiomeric fraction of chiral pharmaceuticals in the aquatic environments of HK The potential sources as well as factors influencing the transformation of chiral BFRs and chiral human and veterinary pharmaceuticals were studied using enantioselective analysis. Sewage and sludge samples were collected from four sewage treatment plants (STPs), employing two types of treatment processes, namely chemically-enhanced primary treatment (CEPT) and secondary (biological) treatment with traditional activated sludge (TAS), in Hong Kong. Four sampling campaigns were conducted over a period of two years. The occurrence, pollutant load, removal efficiencies, temporal dynamics, and enantiomeric distribution characteristics were investigated. Our data showed that α-HBCD predominated all samples, and its proportions increased in the effluent as compared to influent and sludge. α- and β-TBECH were the predominant TBECH diastereomers, with a proportional shift from the latter to the former diastereomer commonly observed after treatment. This research provided the first report on the enantiomer-specific behavior of chiral BFRs under various wastewater treatment processes (Details are given in Publication 3). Follow on from this, the stereoselective fate and distribution of chiral pharmaceuticals released from municipal discharges, sewage from tanks of sequential treatment processes among the four STPs were examined seasonally for four selected chiral pharmaceuticals, namely atenolol, metoprolol, venlafaxine, and chloramphenicol. Initial influent, degritted/settled sewage, non-disinfected effluent, and final effluent were analyzed. We observed high levels (> 1,000 ng/L) of Σatenolol (the sum of stereoisomers) in influent during the whole sampling period, whereas Σmetoprolol exhibited substantial concentrations (> 200 ng/L) throughout from influent to effluent. This indicates the large quantities of these two beta-blockers being constantly dispensed in Hong Kong’s sewage. Σvenlafaxine and Σchloramphenicol were detected at relatively low levels with higher loading amounts observed in the dry season ranging from 43 to 356 ng/L. Atenolol, metoprolol and venlafaxine, commonly marketed as racemates, exhibited variations in enantiomeric fractions (EFs) among samples. On the whole, the distomers of atenolol and venlafaxine were the predominant species, while a racemic pattern was generally observed with regard to metoprolol enantiomers. Sold as a single eutomer [(‒)-threo-chloramphenicol], chloramphenicol might undergo a possible preferential elimination in freshwater sewage during sewage treatment. Compared to TAS, the removal efficiencies of CEPT were found to be insufficient (< 50%) for the monitored pharmaceuticals. As well, the selected pharmaceuticals were consistently detected in all dewatered sludge samples. The estimated emissions calculated based on the concentration in efﬂuents and volume of dewatered sludge produced indicate that these pharmaceuticals were released predominantly in the aqueous fractions. The removal through sorption to sludge was found to be minimal (mostly < 5% of initial mass), which suggests that biodegradation and/or chemical transformation can be the dominant mechanism of removal for these drugs. Overall, results of this project revealed that larger quantities of the studied pharmaceuticals were released during the dry seasons; and biodegradation was the primary removal mechanism for atenolol and chloramphenicol. Marketed as an enantiopure pharmaceutical in R,R-para-form, chloramphenicol was preferentially eliminated after biological processes. Again, this research provided the first report on the occurrence of chloramphenicol enantiomers in the aquatic environment ( Details are given in Publication 4). Objective 3: To assess the potential ecological risks of target pharmaceuticals to the coastal ecosystem in HK Analytical methods for chiral pharmaceuticals in biological samples were successfully developed and validated using eel muscles as reference samples. Aquatic biota samples comprising key components of a local marine food web including mollusks, crustaceans, and fish, were analyzed to elucidate the contamination status of chiral pharmaceuticals in Hong Kong waters. This information was used for ecological risk assessments. To assess the risks of chiral pharmaceuticals to local marine ecosystems, tissue samples of 24 aquatic wildlife species were collected and analyzed for these drugs. The investigation involved four mollusk species, five crustacean species, and fifteen fish species, which allowed an evaluation of the enantiospecific trophic transfer potential of the studied chiral pharmaceuticals. Our data suggested that marine animals from the western waters were more contaminated by the studied pharmaceuticals than those from southern and eastern waters of Hong Kong. Interestingly, trophic dilution was observed for atenolol and chloramphenicol. R-(+)-atenolol, S-(−)-metoprolol, and R-(−)-venlafaxine were selectively accumulated in fishes, and stereoisomeric impurities of chloramphenicol, i.e., enantiomers apart from the R,R-para-form, were found widespread in the marine species analyzed. Our ecological risk assessment results indicate that atenolol and metoprolol might cause harmful effects to local fishes, especially those inhabiting the western waters and Victoria Harbor of Hong Kong (Details are given in Publication 5). These findings have enhanced our understanding on the enantiospecific toxicological effects of chiral pharmaceuticals on non-target aquatic organisms. In summary, all the tasks set out in the original proposal have practically been completed. Notwithstanding, as our study covers a large number of stereoisomers of chiral pharmaceuticals, the investigation of seventeen therapeutic classes turned out to be more challenging and time-consuming than anticipated. This work is still on-going.

11338216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11338216.value: Stereoisomeric compositions of 1,2,5,6,9,10-hexabromocyclododecane (HBCD) and 1,2-dibromo-4-(1,2-dibromoethyl)cyclohexane (TBECH) were investigated in the blubber of local finless porpoises (Neophocaena phocaenoides) and Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins (Sousa chinensis), from the South China Sea between 2005 and 2015. There is very little information on the environmental occurrence of TBECH and HBCD meso-isomers in marine organisms in the world. Our data showed an increasing trend of HBCD in dolphin blubber over the past decade, and there was a negative correlation between the enantiomer fractions of α-HBCD and the body lengths of porpoises. Dietary items of local marine mammals (e.g., fishes, crustaceans, and mollusks) were collected and analyzed for chiral BFRs (e.g., HBCD and TBECH) and chiral pharmaceuticals (e.g., atenolol, metoprolol, venlafaxine, and chloramphenicol). The trophic transfer of these chiral pollutants was tracked through marine food web studies. Biomagnification of each HBCD and TBECH diastereomer from individual prey species to marine mammals was observed. Trophic dilution was found for atenolol and chloramphenicol; and fishes selectively accumulated R-(+)-atenolol, S-(−)-metoprolol, and R-(−)-venlafaxine. These studies report, for the first time, the biomagnification of TBECH and the enantioselectivity of chiral pharmaceuticals in a food web. Sewage and sludge generated from diverse treatment processes were collected in four sewage treatment plants in Hong Kong over a period of two years for the analyses of selected chiral BFRs and chiral pharmaceuticals. Our results indicate that more effective HBCD removal was achieved via biodegradation as compared to sludge sorption, while both chemically enhanced primary and secondary treatment yielded high TBECH elimination. Biodegradation was the primary removal mechanism for atenolol and chloramphenicol, while the removal via primary sedimentation and disinfection was insignificant. A preferential elimination of (+)-α- and (+)-γ-HBCD and E2-β-TBECH took place consistently after biological treatment. Selectivity toward R-(+)-atenolol, S-(−)-metoprolol, and R-(−)-venlafaxine was commonly observed in secondary-treated effluent, and microbial activity mainly accounted for the preferential depletion of R,R-chloramphenicol. These studies underscore the importance of conducting enantiospecific analysis for chiral pollutants in wastewater treatment research.

11338216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11338216.value: The work undertaken in the current research project can be extended to psychiatric pharmaceuticals. Recently, psychiatric pharmaceuticals have received special attention because of their rising consumption, frequent environmental occurrence, bioaccumulation potential, and ecotoxicity. As over 50% of the marketed pharmaceuticals are chiral, it would be instructive to assess the environmental and ecological risk posed by different enantiomers of these pharmaceuticals. A more refined risk assessment on more than ten psychiatric pharmaceuticals, many of which exhibit chirality, is being planned. Chemical analyses will be performed on water and sediment samples collected in Hong Kong and the nearby South China area to determine the status and trends of different enantiomers of psychiatric pharmaceuticals commonly found in our coastal waters. Furthermore, laboratory-based investigations will be undertaken to examine the toxicological effects of these chiral pharmaceuticals on key marine organisms that are important in maintaining the structure and function our marine ecosystems.

11338216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11338216.value: More than 50% of marketed pharmaceuticals are chiral, and different enantiomers can have different toxicological effects on non-target organisms. Enormous quantities of pharmaceutical-containing wastewater discharged from Hong Kong end up in the South China Sea and can cause adverse impacts on the environment. Information on the enantiomeric profile of pharmaceuticals in marine environmental matrices is limited. This study focused on four commonly used pharmaceuticals, which are of environmental concern. They include two antihypertensives (atenolol and metoprolol, classified as β-blockers), one psychoactive (venlafaxine, classified as an antidepressant), and one antibiotic (chloramphenicol). Our results revealed that, during wastewater treatment, biological processes generally removed these chiral pharmaceuticals more efficiently than chemically enhanced primary treatment, and disinfection treatments seemed to have little effect on pharmaceutical elimination. Furthermore, atenolol and metoprolol in effluent-receiving waters in Hong Kong may pose risks to marine fishes. The bioaccumulation and spatial distribution of the studied chiral pharmaceuticals were investigated in local marine food webs. Fish, crustacean, and mollusk samples were analyzed. Organisms from Hong Kong western waters were more contaminated by the studied chiral pharmaceuticals than those from southern and eastern waters. Enantioselective bioaccumulation was widespread. Overall, results of the present study raise environmental concerns about chiral pharmaceuticals.

11338516.label: Project Objectives
11338516.value: To develop a methodology for the controlled synthesis of group-VI element-doped CNPs by solvothermal methods. The impacts of doping elements, carbon sources, solvent, and the reaction conditions such as reaction time and temperature on the doping efficiency, size, microstructure, and surface states of CNPs will be studied systematically. To study the optical properties of the doped CNPs, particularly with the focuses on the absorption and emission properties of CNPs; other characteristics of CNPs, such as the water dispersibility, and photo and chemical stabilities, will also be investigated. To explore the effects of doping on the photophysical and photochemical properties of CNPs, especially the photochemical conversion mechanism (including the capability in ROS generation or photothermal conversion) with the aid of theoretical modeling. The nanotoxicology, biodistribution, and performance in photodynamic therapy/photothermal therapy of CNPs will be evaluated through in vitro and in vivo experiments.
