11338516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11338516.value: As an emerging cancer therapy method, phototherapy (PT), including photodynamic therapy and photothermal therapy, have the advantages such as fewer side effects, negligible drug resistance, low systemic toxicity, and noninvasive nature. Phototherapeutic agents (PTAs) play a predominant role in determining the efficacy of PT. Nevertheless, the current organic PTAs have in general complicated synthesis procedures, poor photostability and water dispersibility, and low extinction coefficient at the PT window. On the other hand, inorganic PTAs have usually high cytotoxicity, poor biodegradability and stability which hamper their clinical applications. The carbon nanoparticles (CNPs) exhibit a unique combination of outstanding properties, e.g., broad absorption from visible to near infrared (NIR), good water dispersibility, high photostability, and excellent biocompatibility. Our recent report in Nat. Commun. (2014, 5:4596) illustrates that doping of CNPs with sulphur can tune the optical properties of CNPs, and lead to high-yield singlet oxygen generation and highly efficient PT of cancer. Moreover, our preliminary results also show that the S- and Se-doped CNPs have interesting photothermal effect. Although the heavy atom effect of sulphur and selenium (e.g., enhancing intersystem crossing rate constant and triplet states quantum yield) is believed to be a key in resulting in these prominent characteristics, the mechanism has not been fully understood. The relation between reactive oxide species (ROS) generation/photothermal conversion and doping effects of CNPs need to be further explored for the design and preparation of new CNPs-based PTAs. This project will focus on the synthesis and property studies of group-VI element-doped CNPs. S-, Se-, and Te-containing polymers will be synthesized and used as precursors to prepare CNPs by solvothermal methods. Doping of the different elements from the same group may facilitate our understanding on how they affect the energy conversion efficiency from light to heat or ROS generation. The impacts of carbon sources, solvent, and the reaction conditions on the doping level, size, microstructure, and surface states of CNPs will be studied systematically. The corresponding optical characteristics of CNPs, such as absorption, emission, and photostability will be revealed; the photophysical and photochemical properties of CNPs, including the capability in ROS generation and photothermal conversion will be investigated experimentally and theoretically. The nanotoxicology, biodistribution, and phototherapy performance of CNPs will be evaluated through in vitro and in vivo experiments. and the results will provide a guideline for the preparation of new carbon-based PTAs for cancer treatment. 光療，包括光動力治療和光熱治療，是一種新型的臨床治療方法，具有精准定位和光控治療的優點，為癌症等病症的精確診斷和高效治療提供了有效的手段。與傳統的癌症治療方法（如：手術，化學療法和輻射療法）相比，光療具有以下優點：i）能夠高選擇性地消滅腫瘤組織；ii）毒副作用低；iii）用藥量少，幾乎沒有抗藥性；iv）非侵入性；v） 可以和其他治療手段相結合。 光療技術中光敏劑的性能對癌症的治療效果有關鍵的作用。然而，目前臨床上使用的有機光敏劑光穩定性較差，水溶性不好， 同時在光療視窗（600-1000 nm）的摩爾吸光係數也比較低。而無機光敏劑（如半導體量子點和貴金屬的納米材料）的非生物降解性和高毒性限制了它們在臨床上的應用。 碳納米顆粒（CNPs）具有良好的生物相容性、寬的吸收光譜、發射光譜可調（從藍色到深紅色螢光）、光穩定性和化學穩定性好等優點，近年來被廣泛應用於生物醫學領域。同時，由於CNPs表面具有豐富的官能團如氨基、羧基等，很容易通過表面化學修飾以改善其物理化學性質並增加對腫瘤組織的選擇性。我們最近的研究工作（Nat. Commun. 2014, 5, 4596）發現，硫摻雜不僅可以調控CNPs的發光性質，還可以使得CNPs具有高的單線態氧量子產率，光照下可以有效地殺死腫瘤組織。另外，我們還發現，硫和硒摻雜的CNPs也具有較好的光熱效應。我們相信硫和硒的重原子效應（如對系間竄越速率和三重態的量子產率的影響）對CNPs的光化學、光物理性質有關鍵作用，但是具體的作用機理還需要進一步研究。特別是活性氧自由基產率/光熱轉換效率與CNPs摻雜效應之間的關係需要進一步的探討，並為製備新型可用於光療的CNPs提供理論依據。 本課題將對六族元素摻雜的CNPs的製備及其性質進行深入研究。我們將首先合成含有硫、硒或碲等雜原子的聚合物，並用它們作為前驅體通過溶劑法製備CNPs。通過同族不同元素的摻雜，可以使我們更好地理解摻雜對CNPs的光化學能量轉換途徑和效率的影響。本專案中，我們將系統地研究碳源和反應條件，包括溶劑，反應時間，溫度等對CNPs的摻雜量、尺寸大小、微結構和表面態的影響， 及它們和CNPs的光化學光物理性質（包括吸收，發射和光穩定性，產生活性氧自由基的效率和光熱轉換效率）之間的聯繫。我們將通過體外細胞和荷瘤小鼠模型實驗來評價CNPs的光療效果，本項目的研究結果對製備新型的光療用碳基光敏劑提供理論及實驗基礎。

11338516.label: Realisation of objectives
11338516.value: Objective 1: We have prepared a series of group-VI element-doped CNPs by solvothermal method using different carbon sources and solvents. We found that the carbon source, solvent, reaction temperature and time have great impacts on the morphology, size, microstructure, and doping level of the obtained CNPs. For example, by using poly-3-thiopheneacetic acid (PTA) as the carbon source, S-doped CNPs (S-CNPs) with different sizes and surface chemical compositions were prepared through adjusting the concentration of NaOH in an aqueous solution (sample named as CNPs-n with n indicating the NaOH concentration in the unit of mM). These S-CNPs exhibit spherical configuration except CNPs-1000 which have an irregular morphology. It is verified that CNPs-2.5, CNPs-5, CNPs-10 and CNPs-20 have crystalline structure, while CNPs-100 and CNPs-1000 are in amorphous state. Moreover, the average diameters of these CNPs increase with the increase of NaOH concentration, i.e., from 2.2 nm for CNPs-2.5 to 23.0 nm for CNPs-100. However, as the NaOH concentration is increased to 1000 mM, only bulky carbon grains with their sizes over 100 nm are obtained. It is also demonstrated that more negatively-charged groups could be formed on the surface of CNPs prepared with higher NaOH concentration, indicating NaOH plays a critical role in controlling the morphology, microstructure and surface states of CNPs. Se-doped CNPs were prepared by using PSe1 as the carbon source, and S and Se codoped CNPs (S,Se-CNPs) were prepared by hydrothermal treatments of PT2 and dipheneyl diselenide in alkaline solution. The concentration ratio of PT2 to dipheneyl diselenide is revealed to have only little influence on the S/Se ratio and optical properties of CNPs. The S,Se-CNPs show a crystalline structure with a mean diameter of ~20 nm, and in contrast to the S-CNPs, S,Se-CNPs have a platelet morphology with a height of ~4 nm. Moreover, by using 1,3,6-trinitropyrene as the carbon source, N,S-codoped and N-doped CNPs are also prepared in the presence and absence of Na2SO3, respectively. The surfaces of N,S-CNPs and N-CNPs are illustrated to be rich in oxygen-containing groups, such as carboxyl and carbonyl. Objective 2: We have systematically studied the optical properties of CNPs doped with different impurities, including the absorption and emission properties, and investigated their dependence on the microstructures, surface states, and defects of CNPs. 1) S-CNPs with different doping levels show the same absorption peak at ~ 250 nm, which is attributed to π–π* transition of C=C. However, as the concentration of NaOH is higher than 10 mM, the shoulder peak at ~ 360 nm originated from n–π* transition of C=O is enhanced. The fluorescence spectra of S-CNPs present an excitation wavelength-dependent characteristic, and the emission of S-CNPs depends strongly on the carbon precursors and solvents used in hydrothermal treatment. It is demonstrated that the higher surface oxidation degree of CNPs would cause more surface defects on CNPs, and as a result lead to smaller energy level separation and red-shift of fluorescence. 2) The N-doped CNPs show an absorption band from the visible region to over 800 nm. The N-CNPs aqueous solution emits yellow ﬂuorescence under the 365 nm light irradiation, with a ﬂuorescence quantum yield of 4.9%. A ﬂuorescence emission peak centered at ~570 nm is obtained under 500 nm excitation, and the ﬂuorescence spectra present excitation wavelength-independent characteristic. The N-CNPs could simultaneously generate singlet oxygen, hydroxyl radical, and heat under a 635 nm laser irradiation, with a singlet oxygen generation quantum yield of 5.7% and photothermal conversion efficiency of 73.5%. In contrast, the N,S-CNPs have a broader absorption spectrum from 250 to 1100 nm. The N,S-CNPs exhibit slight excitation wavelength-dependent fluorescence emission, and the strongest fluorescence with the peak at ~490 nm is acquired by 400 nm excitation. The yellow-colored N,S-CNPs aqueous solution delivers strong cyan fluorescence under 365 nm UV light irradiation with a fluorescence quantum yield of 49%. Significantly, the N,S-CNPs could simultaneously present strong fluorescence and generate singlet oxygen through two-photon excitation mechanism, and they also show outstanding photothermal conversion capability under irradiation by an 800 nm femtosecond pulsed laser. 3) For the Se-doped CNPs, absorption from 350 to 750 nm and weak fluorescence are observed. The fluorescence spectra exhibit excitation wavelength dependent behavior. Importantly, the Se-doped CNPs show singlet oxygen generation and photothermal conversion capabilities under white light. As the CNPs are co-doped with S and Se, they present an absorption band similar to that of Se-doped CNPs, and two emission peaks at 731 nm and 820 nm are obtained. Different from the Se-doped CNPs, the S,Se-CNPs cannot produce singlet oxygen under laser irradiation. However, they exhibit a high photothermal conversion efficiency of ~58.2%. In addition, the S,Se-CNPs are featured with a large two-photon absorption cross section, which enables them to have near infrared emission and photothermal conversion through two photon excitation mechanism. The CNPs are also illustrated to have excellent photostability and photochemical stability. Objective 3: In this project, based on the photophysical and photochemical properties of doped CNPs, the biomedical applications of the CNPs, including their performance in photodynamic therapy/photothermal therapy, were evaluated in vitro and in vivo. The S-CNPs cannot generate singlet oxygen and heat under light irradiation. However, it is revealed these CNPs present obvious fluorescence spectral response toward copper ions (Cu2+), through static quenching caused synergistically by electron transfer and inner filter effect. The O- and S-containing groups on the surface of S-CNPs are demonstrated to be responsible for their outstanding sensing performance. Based on that, a CNPs-based ratiometric fluorescent probe for Cu2+ with a high fluorescence quenching rate constant and a short response time is developed. Their practical applications in detecting Cu2+ in pond water and living cells are also demonstrated. In contrast, the N,S-CNPs and N-CNPs can generate singlet oxygen under 800 nm laser irradiation and concert light to heat. Moreover, the broad absorption spectrum of these CNPs also enables them to be used as an agent for photoacoustic imaging. The in vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that these CNPs have good biocompatibility and can serve as multifunctional phototheranostic agents for photoacoustic/fluorescence imaging, and photodynamic/photothermal synergistic cancer therapy using a single near-infrared laser. For the Se-doped CNPs, the in vitro experiments reveal that the CNPs could penetrate the cell membrane of HeLa cells and locate in the cytoplasm. The MTT experiments demonstrate that the CNPs had good biocompatibility. When the cell incubated with CNPs exposed to white light irradiation, obvious cell viability decrease is observed, revealing the phototherapeutic capability of the CNPs. The S,Se-CNPs also show outstanding biocompatibility in the in vivo experiments. Significantly, due to the near infrared fluorescence and the high photothermal conversion efficiency, the S,Se-CNPs could be used as an agent for fluorescence imaging and phototherapy. Strong red fluorescence is observed at the tumor site after injecting S,Se-CNPs aqueous solution. Under 880 nm laser irradiation, the temperature of the tumor site is increased to ~52 oC, which can effectively kill cancer cells. In contrast, a substantially smaller temperature change is detected for the control group without the injection of S,Se-CNPs. As a result, the tumor growth in the photothermal therapy group is inhibited. The in vivo experiments demonstrate that S,Se-CNPs could be used as a nanoplatform for the simultaneous fluorescence imaging and highly efficient photothermal therapy of cancer.

11338516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11338516.value: We have prepared a series of CNPs doped with different heteroatoms, including N, S, and Se. It is revealed that the doping elements, carbon sources, solvent, and the reaction conditions have great impacts on the morphology, size, crystalline structure, surface states, and defects of the CNPs, which in turn determine the properties of CNPs, such as biocompatibility, stability, and photophysical and photochemical properties. For example, by using poly-3-thiopheneacetic acid as the carbon source, CNPs with different sizes and surface chemical compositions were prepared through adjusting the concentration of NaOH in the hydrothermal process. The surface oxidation degree of S-CNPs increased with the increase of the NaOH concentration in the synthesis process. The excitation-dependent fluorescence of these S-CNPs were dominantly affected by the surface states, and the longer emission wavelength of the S-CNPs was demonstrated to be originated from their higher surface oxidation degree. Using organic molecule with large π conjugated 1,3,6-trinitropyrene as the carbon source, we have prepared N-CNPs and N,S-CNPs which can generate heat and reactive oxygen species under near infrared laser irradiation. It is revealed that the exited energy states in the CNPs can be manipulated through doping heteroatoms, e.g., S and Se co-doped CNPs present high photothermal conversion efficiency, but they are unable to generate singlet oxygen under light irradiation. For the large π–π conjugated structure, the energy gap between the excited singlet state (S1) and the triplet state (T1) is larger than 0.84 eV. The S1 energy of the S,Se-CNPs is calculated to be ~1.51 eV, and the T1 energy is accordingly estimated to be <0.67 eV, which is smaller than the energy required for sensitizing ground-state O2 (0.95 eV). Thus, under light irradiation, no singlet oxygen is generated by the S, Se-CNPs, and the absorbed light energy is mainly converted into heat. Moreover, the S,Se-CNPs have near infrared fluorescence, and thus the S,Se-CNPs can be used as a near infrared emissive phototheranostic agent. Doping has been illustrated to be an effective way to tune the photophysical and photochemical properties of CNPs, which enables the CNPs to be used as a potential multifunctional phototheranostic agents for cancer therapy.

11338516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11338516.value: The microstructure of CNPs is similar to that of organic molecules with large π-conjugated system. Their characteristics and functions are determined by the π-conjugated system of the carbon core and the chemical composition of the surface. The future research will be focused on how to realize the precise control of the π - conjugated structure and surface chemical composition of the CNPs, establish the relevant molecular structure model, and understand the influence of the microstructure of CNPs on their photophysical and photochemical properties. Moreover, targeting probes could be further modified on the CNP surfaces, enabling the CNPs to specifically identify and kill cancer cells. The biological toxicological properties of the modified CNPs, especially the long-term biological safety and metabolic behavior, should also be studied to promote the clinical transformation of CNPs in the field of cancer treatment.

11338516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11338516.value: Carbon is intrinsically a biocompatible material; the outstanding photo and chemical stability of carbon nanoparticles (CNPs) together with their excellent biocompatibility make them a promising candidate with the overall performance superior to that of traditional phototheranostic agents in in vitro and in vivo biomedical applications. Moreover, the surfaces of CNPs can be modified with other targeting and therapeutic agents, which allow them to selectively access the cancer cells and kill them by combining phototherapy and other therapeutic mechanisms. In this project, we have developed techniques and established methodologies for the synthesis of group-VI element-doped CNPs. We studied that the dependence of CNPs’ photophysical and photochemical properties on the doping elements, size, microstructure, and surface states. We prepared several CNPs which have high generation yield of reactive oxygen species and/or high photothermal conversion efficiency, and evaluated their phototherapeutic abilities through in vitro and in vivo experiments, and results demonstrated that these CNPs could be used as multifunctional phototheranostics agents for cancer therapy.

11338616.label: Project Objectives
11338616.value: Analysis of distributed learning with kernel-based regularization schemes. For the classical least squares regularization scheme in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, we plan to introduce a second order decomposition for differences of inverse operators and expect to derive optimal error bounds and minimax rates of convergence under a general noise condition. For distributed learning with the least squares regularization scheme, we propose to conduct rigorous error analysis without any assumption on bounds for the eigenfunctions of the integral operators. Error analysis for distributed learning with general kernel-based regularization schemes are expected by higher order decompositions for differences of inverse operators. Analysis of some partially online learning schemes. We plan to analyze a gradient descent algorithm for the minimum error entropy principle in a linear regression framework and get learning rates for the mean squared error by the approximation of covariance vectors and covariance matrices. For the general gradient descent algorithm in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, we expect to use regularization and study consistency when the scaling parameter is large. For the case of a small or fixed scaling parameter, we propose to restrict to homoskedastic models for the consistency analysis. 11338616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11338616.value: In [1] we consider online mirror descent (OMD), a class of scalable online learning algorithms exploiting data geometric structures through mirror maps. Necessary and sufficient conditions are presented in terms of the step size sequence for the convergence of OMD with respect to the expected Bregman distance induced by the mirror map. We establish tight error bounds under mild conditions on the mirror map, the loss function, and the regularizer. In [2] we provide analysis for convergence of the singular value thresholding algorithm for solving matrix completion and affine rank minimization problems arising from compressive sensing, signal processing, machine learning, and related topics. Concrete convergence rates in terms of Bregman distances and Frobenius norms of matrices are presented, by giving an identity for the Bregman distance as the excess gradient descent objective function values and an error decomposition. In [3], we introduce a distributed kernel gradient descent algorithm for the minimum error entropy principle and analyze its convergence. We show that the L2 error decays at a minimax optimal rate under some mild conditions. As a tool we establish some concentration inequalities for U-statistics which play pivotal roles in our error analysis. In [4] we study a learning algorithm for distribution regression with regularized least squares. To extract information from samples, we embed distributions to a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) and use a second stage sample to form the regressor by a tool of mean embedding. We show error bounds in the L2-norm and prove that the regressor is a good approximation to the regression function. We derive a learning rate which is optimal in the setting of standard least squares regression and improve the existing work, achieved by using a novel second order decomposition to bound operator norms. In [5] we consider stochastic composite mirror descent (SCMD) to capture both geometric and composite structures of optimization problems in machine learning. We propose a theoretically sound strategy to select an individual iterate of the vanilla SCMD, which is able to achieve optimal rates for both convex and strongly convex problems in a non-smooth learning setting. This strategy of outputting an individual iterate can preserve the sparsity of solutions which is crucial for a proper interpretation in sparse learning problems.

11338616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11338616.value: Distributed representations in distributed learning and stochastic gradient descent in online learning are the fundamental operations in deep learning methods and algorithms. Research results produced and methods arising from this project lead to potential applications in theoretical understanding of deep learning methods. We will use these findings to investigate the theory of deep learning in our further study.

11338616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11338616.value: This project is along the research direction of analyzing and processing big data from various fields of science and technology. It aims at theoretical study of two learning theory topics: distributed learning and online learning. For the two families of learning algorithms dealing with big data, we provide approximation theory viewpoints and quantitative estimates including explicit error bounds and optimal learning rates. For distributed learning with various regularization schemes in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, we derive error bounds and optimal learning rates by novel second order decompositions for differences of inverse operators. Rigorous error analysis is conducted for some online learning schemes and gradient descent methods for a minimum error entropy principle.

11500216.label: Project Objectives
11500216.value: Build a unified theoretical framework to analyze the impact of monetary incentive on user contribution. Identify conditions under which monetary incentive may positively or negatively affect the quantity and quality of user contribution. Understand the different impact of monetary incentive on different types of contributors. Study how these contributors react to an increase in the monetary incentive and what the resulting market outcomes are: who enters the market and who leaves; how the contribution quantity and quality levels are affected, etc. Examine the impact of different types of monetary incentives. Some mechanisms focus on the quantity while otheres focus more on the quality aspect. For example, Youtube.com adopts a revenue sharing program that shares revenue with the contributors based on the volume of content contributed (number of view). Such mechanism can be easily adjusted to share revenue based on the quality of content contributed, such as number of “likes”. Varying the mechanisms has different implication on the behavior of content providers. Understanding the impact of different types of monetary incentive mechanisms helps the policy maker to design proper incentives to achieve an ideal outcome. Study the impact of commercialization of content generation/contribution. Once the monetary incentive is paid high enough, the UGC contribution becomes a business, i.e., commercialized. The process of production-efficient contributors crowding out non-production-efficient contributors can be recognized as a transformation from UGC to PGC (professionally generated content). After purchased by Google in 2006 and introduceing the ad-revenue-sharing program in 2007, the traditional network and cable broadcasters (such as ABC, NBC and CBS) noticed the commercial value of YouTube, thus they (corresponding to the I ̅P contributors in our model) enter the market and contribute PGC to attract audience. It is not always good to be “commercialized”, especially for the knowledge contributing UGC platforms. This perhaps is the reason why the Wikipedia maintain a nonprofit UGC platform. We hope to study the impact of such commercialization as well as offer guideline for such commercialization. Collect real data and conduct empirical studies to verify, or test our theoretical results. Offer guidelines on whether to introduce monetary incentive, and if so, how to design the monetary incentive schemes to achieve an ideal outcome in terms of contribution volume, quality or marke composition. Promoting and propoer use of content contribution is an important issue in policy making. We hope this study shed lights on the public policy making related to public opinion gathering and analysis.

11500216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500216.value: User-generated content becomes more and more essential in people’s daily life, or for knowledge sharing/management in a business organization. To encourage content contribution, monetary incentives are often introduced. It is also found, however, that introducing monetary incentive may discourage contribution in some scenarios, for example, blood donation. How does monetary incentive impact the user-generated content contribution, then? We build a theoretical model studying user-generated content (UGC) contribution, where four types of contributors (classified by whether they are intrinsically-motivated and whether they produce content efficiently) compete for audience attention. Based on whether the monetary incentive positively or negatively modifies each type of contributor’s intrinsic motivation, as well as amount of the monetary incentive, we find that the introduction of monetary incentive creates different levels of competition among the contributors, and may either attract in or drive out certain contributors. For example, it may drive out contributors who view monetary incentives as a damage to his/her personal image (motivation crowding out). While it may attract contributors who are interested in the monetary payment, this increased competition also reduces attention received by other contributors who are not interested in monetary incentives (competition crowding out.) Accordingly, it can either reduce or increase the total contribution in the market. We also discuss how the quality and quantity of content contribution are affected differently by monetary incentives. Understanding this, we offer guidelines for the market maker to design better monetary incentive schemes. Depending on the desired quality or quantity of the content level, the market maker needs to offer appropriate level of monetary incentives to encourage content contribution. 在许多UGC平台上，货币激励经常被用来鼓励用户贡献内容（UGC）。但是，现存的实证研究对于货币激励的效果却有相互矛盾的结果。我们建立了一个理论模型研究货币激励对UGC的贡献，并假设引入货币激励以后，贡献者的内在动力有可能会增强或者削弱。我们发现，在特定条件下，货币激励的效果对贡献者贡献内容的质量和数量的影响是非单调的影响。我们的研究结果对于设计不同的货币激励机制来实现不同的市场结果有指导意义。

11500216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500216.value: We identify two types of crowding out effects associated with monetary incentives, specifically, (1) the “motivation crowding out” effect and (2) the “competition crowding out” effect. Under the “motivation crowding out” effect, the introduction of a monetary incentive may undermine contributors’ non-monetary motivations, because the monetary incentive may dilute the signaling effect of contribution behavior on prosocial preferences and increase that on greediness (Ariely et al. 2009; Bénabou and Tirole 2006); thus, the non-money-driven contributors may reduce their contributions or even stop contributing. Under the “competition crowding out” effect, when the monetary incentive increases, the competition for the scarce audience resource among the contributors is intensified; thus, the low-effectiveness contributors may reduce their contributions or even stop contributing. This “competition crowding out” effect is unique to UGC contribution but has received little academic attention. Under the influence of these two crowding out effects, the impact of monetary incentives is non-monotonic on contributor participation, as well as on the total content volume. Consequently, different equilibria emerge, depending on parameters such as the difference in contributors’ effectiveness in attracting the audience and how non-money-driven contributors’ rewards from contributions are affected by the monetary incentive. We also extend our model to have different number of contributors within each type. We identify more complicated crowding-out phenomena. For example, as the monetary incentive increases, contributors either continue contributing, or are crowded out, or restart contributing, depending on the magnitude of the monetary incentive. To the best of our knowledge, this study makes the first attempt to model the impact of monetary incentives on UGC contributions by incorporating competition among different types of contributors. It enriches our understanding of the “crowding out” phenomenon. Specifically, crowding out can occur for different reasons: (1) when the monetary incentive is low, the non-money-driven contributors are negatively affected by the introduction of monetary incentive, thus they reduce contribution or stop contributing (the “motivation crowding out;”) (2) when the monetary incentive increases, the high-effectiveness contributors start contributing and crowd out the low-effectiveness contributors (the “competition crowding out.”) Our study is the first to identify the “competition crowding out” effect, and finds that both contributor participation and total content volume can drop with an increase in the monetary incentive. We also provide guidelines to practitioners for designing appropriate monetary incentive mechanisms.

11500216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500216.value: This project has great potential for empirical verification. The completed project has derived a rich set of results, predicting different equilibrium outcomes under different conditions. It will be valuable to test empirically whether these predictions can be verified in reality. We have already collected data from different channels. It will be an exciting research direction.

11500216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11500216.value: Many platforms use monetary incentives to encourage user-generated content (UGC) contributions. However, empirical studies report contradictory findings: monetary incentives may either increase or decrease contribution. To understand the underlying mechanisms, we build a theoretical model where four types of contributors (classified by whether they contribute without monetary incentive and whether they are effective in attracting audience) compete for the audience. We identify two crowding out effects: (1) “motivation crowding out,” where the introduction of a monetary incentive reduces the non-money-driven contributors’ motivation to contribute (e.g., contributors may worry that they would be viewed as “greedy”), so they reduce their effort or even stop contributing; and (2) “competition crowding out,” where the low-effectiveness contributors reduce their effort or even stop contributing due to intensified competition when the monetary incentive increases. Under the influence of these two crowding-out effects, the impact of a monetary incentive on the contributors’ participation, as well as on their total content volume, is not monotonic. As a result, different equilibrium outcomes emerge as the monetary incentive increases. We also extend our model to the case where the number of contributors in each type could be different and identify more complicated crowding-out phenomena. Our findings offer guidelines for designing monetary incentive schemes for online UGC platforms.

11502016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11502016.value: 商务专业人士如何适应不完备信息系统

11502016.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11502016.value: Prof Alter, Steven Dr Ou, Carol XJ

11502016.label: Project Objectives
11502016.value: 1. The principle objective of this research is to investigate the following three research questions: (a) What are the social and organisational factors that contribute towards the inadequate IS provision that some employees encounter in the workplace? (b) How do organisational employees in Hong Kong and other locations behave when facing a working situation characterised by the provision of inadequate IS; (c) What types of changes to IS policy and planning would ensure that systems provide adequate functionality to employees? 2. Addressing the three research questions requires research falling broadly into the domain of ‘work systems’, i.e. the interaction of people, technology, processes and information in a working context. Much prior work on IT adoption has assumed that IT always has beneficial effects, though this is clearly not always the case. The provision of inadequate IS may be associated with individual IT applications being badly designed or at least not fit for purpose. A second cause of inadequacy in IS provision may be traced to a deliberate managerial decision to provide a set of IT applications that simply does not meet employee needs. 3. The three research questions call for recognizing the variety of conditions that may create perceptions that the available IS is inadequate. While some employees may comply with the expectation that they structure their work to fit the affordances of the system provided, others are likely to resist complying in a variety of different ways. Some may seek to subvert organisational authority and deliberately damage the extant system; others may create more effective working practices, working around the inconveniences of a system that they see foisted on them with little regard for their actual needs. We recognize that systems in organizations are more than just the technology that is used, and also include work processes, information available, and interactions with colleagues. 4. Our approach to addressing the three research questions involves a three-pronged strategy. In order to understand the antecedents to the provision of inadequate IS, the behavioural response of employees (whether as compliance or resistance), and the later consequences, we plan to (a) undertake intensive case studies in organizations; (b) develop and test a research model that captures the key elements associated with the phenomenon; (c) attempt to improve the situation by engaging in an action research project that protects the interests of both employees and the organisation.

11502016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502016.value: The organisational deployment of information systems (IS) is usually marked by a corporate interest in achieving such outcomes as competitiveness, effectiveness and efficiency. While the devising of IS policy is the prerogative of corporate management, the impacts of that policy are experienced by employees throughout the organisation. However, a disappointing percentage of IS deployments do not bring beneficial impacts to stakeholders. Consequently, employees are often dissatisfied with the IS with which they are provided. Some employees comply with a corporate expectation that they use the inadequate systems provided, doing the best they can in the circumstances; others resist compliance and seek better ways of achieving the outcomes that they desire, working around the inadequate systems. Unfortunately, existing models of IS adoption and improvement fail to consider the experience of stakeholders with respect to system inadequacies, and even fewer try to remedy those situations. We expect that a variety of conditions may contribute to the employee experience. For instance, an IS may be inappropriately designed for the task because management may inadequately understand employees’ needs, or simply ignore the socio-organisational context in which the IS is embedded. We also expect to see moderating effects from social, cultural and managerial sources that will mitigate or exacerbate the impact of circumstances on employee behaviour. We propose a three-pronged approach to investigate employee behaviour in situations characterised by inadequate IS provision. Firstly, we will engage in an intensive case study exploration of specific organisations, extending findings reached in earlier research and seeking to identify employee perceptions of and responses to inadequate provisioning with IS/IT resources. Secondly, we will develop a theoretical model that explains the influence of the various antecedent conditions and moderating factors on employees’ behaviour in the context of inadequate systems provision. We will test this model with data collected through a large-scale survey of organisational employees in multiple geo-cultural contexts so as to ground our theoretical contribution in the working experiences of employees as widely as possible. Finally, we will conduct a further test of the theoretical model in an Action Research investigation in one organisation. Drawing on the cause and effect linkages from the theoretical model, we will seek to enhance the adequacy of the IS for employees, at the same time protecting the legitimate interests of the firm. 公司通常为达到竞争力、效益和效率等方面的成果而部署信息系统，公司管理层拥有制定信息系统政策的特权，信息系统政策却影响着公司全体员工，可是大多数信息系统部署都没有给利益攸关者带来有利的影响，因此员工们往往会对公司所提供的信息系统感到不满，部分员工会遵从公司的期望，使用公司提供的不完备系统，尽他们所能将工作做到最好；而其他员工则拒绝顺从，避免使用不完备系统，并且寻找更好的变通方法从而满足他们工作的需要。 遗憾的是，现存各种有关信息系统采纳和改进的理论模型都没有考虑到利益攸关者在系统不完备的情况下的体验，甚至更少有试图改善这些处境。我们预计会有的各种状况引致员工在不完备信息系统情况下的体验，例如，可能由于管理层未能充分了解员工的需求，或者忽略了该信息系统嵌入的社会组织环境，结果导致了信息系统设计不当。我们也预计社会、文化和管理资源具有调节作用，会缓解或加剧不完备信息系统对员工行为的影响 。 在此我们提出了一个三管齐下的方法去研究在不完备信息系统条件下的员工行为。首先，我们计划对一个特定组织进行深入的案例分析，对之前的研究结果进行延伸，并且试图去鉴定员工对信息系统/信息技术资源供应不完备的感知及反应。其次，我们将建立一个理论模型来解释在不完备系统的情境下，各种不同的先行条件和调节因素对员工行为的影响。我们将进行的一个大规模调查，尽可能广泛地向不同地区文化和不同工作经验的公司员工收集数据测试我们的理论模型。最后，我们将采用行动研究法在一个组织中对我们的理论模型进行更进一步的测试。我们期望利用这个理论模型的因果关系，为员工提高信息系统的完备性，同时保护公司的合法利益。

11502016.label: Realisation of objectives
11502016.value: 1a. We have explored the social and organisational factors associated with inadequate IS provision in the workplace in the context of specific organisations. We find that the primary factors are those associated with poor understanding of the nature of work undertaken by employees. This poor understanding may be at a local level or a global level. Sometimes, the poor understanding is reflected in policies that block employees from accessing the IS resources they need. Social factors relate to aspects of the employees behaviour in the environment where the technology is used. Organisational factors relate to the way organisational policies are constructed and the restrictions that they impose on employee behaviour. 1b. Some employees do the best they can in the circumstances even though this means that their work may be imperfectly undertaken. Others (to a greater or lesser extent) ignore the policies and create their own IS-based workarounds to ensure that they can complete work effectively. These workarounds may be unique to one individual employee or they may be created by a team of employees and indeed shared with other employees. Employees may document these workarounds to ensure that new employees understand how they work. Some workarounds are hidden from management, others are in full view. 1c) IS planners need to be cognizant of the work that is done by employees, especially if this work follows non-standard practices that themselves result from idiosyncracies in the local working context. This is particularly sensitive in global organisations that may place great value on standardisation of procedures, yet where local practices cannot be standardised. 2. We have taken a work systems approach to explore the way employees use IS resources (whether officially approved or not) in the workplace. This has enabled us to map out the IS-based work processes in detail. We find that while approved IS applications may be beneficial, the opposite is also true. 3. In some cases reflective non-conmpliance with corporate IS policies may be necessary for employees to complete their work satisfactorily. This non-compliance may, paradoxically, be beneficial for the organisation and its clients/customers. We term this ‘beneficial non-compliance’. At the same time, unreflective compliance may be detrimental. 4a). We have undertaken intensive case studies. 4b) We have developed a research model as planned. The instrumentation for this model is complete and we have collected initial data. Data collection has been severely affected by events in Hong Kong in the last year and will have to be delayed beyond the time frame of this project. 4c) We have not been able to undertaken the action research project designed to protect the interests of both employees and organisation due to the social and health-related circumstances currently prevailing. We do have an organisation that is interested to proceed with the action research, but they are unable to commit to undertaking the work until the social situation and public health situation stabilises.

The principle objective of this research is to investigate the following three research questions: (a) What are the social and organisational factors that contribute towards the inadequate IS provision that some employees encounter in the workplace? (b) How do organisational employees in Hong Kong and other locations behave when facing a working situation characterised by the provision of inadequate IS; (c) What types of changes to IS policy and planning would ensure that systems provide adequate functionality to employees?

2. Addressing the three research questions requires research falling broadly into the domain of ‘work systems’, i.e. the interaction of people, technology, processes and information in a working context. Much prior work on IT adoption has assumed that IT always has beneficial effects, though this is clearly not always the case. The provision of inadequate IS may be associated with individual IT applications being badly designed or at least not fit for purpose. A second cause of inadequacy in IS provision may be traced to a deliberate managerial decision to provide a set of IT applications that simply does not meet employee needs.

3. The three research questions call for recognizing the variety of conditions that may create perceptions that the available IS is inadequate. While some employees may comply with the expectation that they structure their work to fit the affordances of the system provided, others are likely to resist complying in a variety of different ways. Some may seek to subvert organisational authority and deliberately damage the extant system; others may create more effective working practices, working around the inconveniences of a system that they see foisted on them with little regard for their actual needs. We recognize that systems in organizations are more than just the technology that is used, and also include work processes, information available, and interactions with colleagues.

4. Our approach to addressing the three research questions involves a three-pronged strategy. In order to understand the antecedents to the provision of inadequate IS, the behavioural response of employees (whether as compliance or resistance), and the later consequences, we plan to (a) undertake intensive case studies in organizations; (b) develop and test a research model that captures the key elements associated with the phenomenon; (c) attempt to improve the situation by engaging in an action research project that protects the interests of both employees and the organisation.

11502016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11502016.value: We document above the extent to which we have completed our objectives. The major findings that go beyond previously undertaken research (as published in the literature) relate to the detailed experience of the employees regarding inadequate provision of IS, the way employees deliberately engage in non-compliant working practices in order to ensure that they can complete work satisfactorily, and indeed share these non-compliant working practices openly. The theoretical model that we have developed and are now in the process of testing will help to validate the relative significance of these ideas. In our primary case organisation, we were able to complete a thorough investigation of how employees are affected by a software environment that was imposed on them without consultation. The situation is interesting because the new software was implemented about a year before our research commenced. The previous software was customised to the local situation and was generally liked by employees. When global headquarters decided to standardise the software used in all offices globally, radical changes to the way work was undertaken were expected. The HK office pointed out that the new software would not fit the working practices, but this advice was apparently disregarded. As a result, all the employees we interviewed indicated that to a greater or lesser extent, their work was affected negatively by the new software. Further, they all engaged in non-compliant workaround behaviour. Previous literature classifies this kind of work as “Shadow Systems”, in the sense that these workarounds are in the shadows, hidden from view. In our case company, we found that the workarounds were very much in public view. They were co-created, shared, enhanced, and then documented in a Standard Operating Procedures document. We drew on this intensive case investigation, as well as the literature, to create a theoretical model that we are in the process of testing. Although the initial case work was done in Hong Kong, we see no reason why the employee experience of inadequate IS should be limited to Hong Kong. Therefore we are in the process of collecting survey data in other countries: China, Thailand, Indonesia, Germany, Romania. Multiple language versions have been created and checked for these different contexts. A paper that draws on data collected in Romania is currently under review.

11502016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502016.value: The testing of the theoretical model will continue. At the time of writing, this is complicated by the Covid-19 situation. We are currently negotiating with a multinational German firm that is interested in helping us to collect data – because they are curious about the nature of inadequate IS provisions in their own organisational context. We expect that they will provide access for us to collect data in multiple locations around the world, including Canada, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Taiwan, USA. The action research that we planned to undertaken will take place, but we cannot predict when as it is dependent on a more stable public health environment. The focus company has operations globally, but our negotiations have been with offices in Hong Kong and China (Shanghai). Prior to this GRF project, we completed work with their offices in Guangzhou (2014-2016) and we hope to undertake the action research in either the Shanghai or Beijing office locations once the situation is suitable.

11502016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502016.value: Organisational environments are increasingly dependent on information systems for all aspects of the work that employees do. Global organisations in particular often standardise information systems on a global basis. In an ideal world, these information systems will be designed precisely so as to support the employees; the employees in turn will find that their legitimate working needs are met. However, there are situations where this is not the case. Employees are not always adequately served by the information systems provided by the organisation. As a result, completing their daily work can be problematic. Some employees accept the situation and do the best they can. Others take steps to work around the inadequate technology. By investigating this phenomenon, we find out how serious it is, document the nature of the workarounds that employees create, and suggest policy-level changes that may be needed. Initial work was done in Hong Kong. We are now validating our ideas globally with data collection in multiple other countries. We believe that organisations will benefit from this research because they will appreciate the need to ensure that local working practices are accommodated by global information systems. The value of non-compliant employee behaviour may also be appreciated.

11502116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11502116.value: 淘宝、易趣等电子交易平台通过更好的连接买家和卖家已经成为电子商务时代最重要的交易手段。2013年，中国60%以上的网上零售业务是通过电子交易平台完成的，这意味着电子交易平台辅助创造了近1800亿美元的商业价值。市场的增长与扩大带来了交易平台上卖家之间日益激烈的竞争。截至2013年底，中国的主导电子交易平台淘宝已拥有超过900万的卖家，较2011年增长了近50%。因此，如何在日益“拥挤”的电子交易平台上尽可能的扩大销量成为平台上每一个卖家的挑战。 电子交易平台大多通过平台上嵌入的在线功能（以下简称为平台功能）来吸引并留住用户。如淘宝、易趣等电子交易平台通常在店铺页面上提供丰富多样的功能来吸引更多的来访客户。这些可选功能一般涵盖价格（如限时折扣等）、营销（如奢侈品店铺链接等）、客户服务（如七天无理由退款等）等。虽然这些功能可以使卖家更有效的吸引客户，但也很容易被竞争对手观察并快速复制，无法提供卖家持久的竞争优势。因此，卖家越来越重视通过组合平台功能更好的吸引买家，并提高其销售业绩。本研究的首要研究问题是电子交易平台这一情景下，卖家如何通过组合平台功能更好的提高自身销售业绩。 通过对以往电子商务文献的研究，对于卖家如何组合电子商务平台功能增加其销售量的研究还存在不足，以往的研究也没有覆盖本研究提出的研究问题。因此，我们基于竞争行为类目理论[2-4]这一电子商务领域新理论为基础。该理论扎根于战略领域，揭示了竞争行为组合的特定结构特点，如数量、复杂性、异质性等对公司绩效的影响。通过扩展这一理论，本研究示电子交易平台上卖家对于不同平台功能的使用与组合为卖家的竞争行为类目，并研究其结构特点对绩效的影响。 本研究的第二个研究问题是基于竞争行为类目理论在电子交易平台上的应用，考虑权变因素在竞争行为类目与绩效关系间影响的作用。这一研究问题的提出主要是通过对竞争行为类目理论的研究。电子交易平台作为一个独特的情景因素使我们不得不注意一个重要因素：卖家信誉。在竞争激烈的电子交易平台上，卖家的信誉通常通过很直观的买家客户评级来决定。先前的研究已经论证了信誉对销量的直接影响[6-8]，但对卖家竞争行为类目的影响机制我们还知之甚少。因此，本研究将通过结合竞争行为类目理论与信号理论，进一步探索卖家信誉对其竞争行为类比和其销量件影响的作用。 本研究贡献点有如下几点：一、本研究通过结合竞争行为类别理论与信号理论，更好的理解电子交易平台上，买家评价不同的卖家如何组合平台功能这一竞争行为类目的结构特点对其销量的影响。这一研究问题在学术界还少有研究。二、本研究将卖家信誉作为竞争行为类目理论的边界条件，从而更好的审视竞争行为类目的结构特征与销量之间的关系[10-14]。三、本研究通过揭示在电子交易平台这一情景下，信誉对卖家竞争行为类目及销量间关系的影响，拓展了现有电子商务[5,15-18]及战略研究[19-21]中关于信誉对销量作用的理解。本研究将基于淘宝卖家的面板数据，如平台功能使用数据以及客观的销量数据等，对研究结论进行验证。

11502116.label: Realisation of objectives
11502116.value: (1) Finalize the MISQ submission of competitive repertoire in e-marketplace sellers’ performance. It was published in MISQ Mar 2019. As stated in the last progress report, we have made major progress on our research objective and addressed the comments and suggestions of the review panel and finally got our paper published in MIS Quarterly in 2019. In specific, we first further enhanced the theorizing on how competitive repertoire (e.g. volume, complexity, and heterogeneity) of platform-based functions will influence sellers’ sales performance based on previous competitive action literature and contextualization in e-marketplace context. Second, we incorporate the moderation role of sellers’ reputation during this process and suggest how platform-based functions will result in different effects at different levels of sellers’ reputation, in general is that seller reputation will work as a trust mechanism in affect consumers’ purchase decision when associated with different competitive repertoire. Third, we empirically test our research model, incorporate the new data set to ensure our robustness of the results, and discuss the results with existing findings. Theoretical contribution, practical implication, limitations, and future research are further suggested. Lastly, we further addressed the review panel’s comments on justifying the selection of sellers in e-marketplace, clarifying consumers' ability to recognize sellers’ competitive repertoire and discuss the generalizability of our findings. In doing so, the major research objectives of the project are achieved. (2) Further completed the paper of dynamic relationship between platform-based function repertoire, strategy group and performance of e-market place sellers, and currently under review at MISQ. Drawing upon the competitive repertoire theory and strategic group theory, we further developed a latent growth model to uncover the dynamic relationship between platform-based function repertoire. As mentioned in the last progress report, there exist five steps in analysis our longitudinal data set with latent growth model, we further finished the rest two steps (i.e. (d) examine the differences in the sales performance for each class; and (e) examine the interactions between the growth patterns of the three structural characteristics of competitive repertoires and that of strategic group membership when predicting sales performance) and complete our empirical data analysis. Our results further suggest that (1) the initial status of platform-based repertoire will positive affect the sales performance but will turns to negative effect over time; (2) positive and negative effect of the rate of increase of platform-based repertoire volume and heterogeneity on rate of increase of sales performance over time; (3) different growth patterns of four strategic group; (4) contingent role of strategic group memberships in shaping the dynamic relationship. Our paper further makes four sound contributions to existing literature including the extending competitive repertoire in dynamic and longitudinal way, extending strategic group theory into e-marketplace context, bridging the micro-action and macro-strategy perspective on the competitive dynamics in e-marketplace, and enriching the approaches to identify strategic group by incorporating the latent class modeling. Currently, this paper is under review at the top journal of the IS field, the MIS Quarterly, we will further address the review panel’s comments and suggestions to promote the publication process. (3) Examines performance impact of sellers’ competitive action repertoires sequence. We further finalize the theorizing process on how Gestalt properties (i.e., sequence simplicity, sequence predictability, sequence grouping and sequence motif) will influence sellers with information processing literature, which provide insights on how characteristics of sequence stimulus will influence audiences’ evaluation and decisions. Our analyses mainly suggest that the sellers’ competitive action sequence will influence consumers’ perception and evaluation and then further influence the sellers’ sales outcome. After operationalizing the Gestalt properties with our empirical longitudinal data set, we conducted a preliminary data analysis and obtained preliminary results. Our paper has been published in the Pacific Asia Conference on Information Systems (PACIS), Dubai, UAE, in 2020. We will further finalize the data analysis and get final empirical results, so as to get this paper to publish in a major IS journal. (4) Further examines the performance outcome of combinations of platform-based functions from a configurational perspective. Previous research mainly examines the performance outcome of platform-based function individually and moderators of this relationship but resulted in inconclusive findings. Given that sellers normally take multiple functions to gain competitive advantages and complex interaction among functions are hinted by previous studies, we take two theoretical approaches to examine the performance impact of combinations of platform-based functions and conduct empirical analysis with fsQCA on the data set of 3333 sellers in Taobao apparel industry. Firstly, we theorizing sellers’ usage of platform-based function as signals as these function fulfill the criteria as signals and further hypothesized the “collective signals” in which a combinations of credibility signals and visibility signals, findings and contributions are further discussed based on the empirical resulted, this paper got published in the Pacific Asia Conference on Information Systems (PACIS), Dubai, UAE, in 2020. Secondly, the sellers’ usage of platform-based functions can be treated as competitive actions to help gain competitive advantages. We further identify four configurations for sellers to achieve high sales performance, and label these four configuration as low cost, market-differentiation, reputation differentiation, and cost-benefit focus, with insights porters’ three generic strategic, given the close relationship among competitive actions and competitive strategy. Theoretical contributions for competitive action literature, online reputation literature, performance impact of platform-based function literature, and e-commerce study in general are suggested, practical implications for sellers are also discussed. This paper is currently under review at one of the top journals in the information system, the Information System Research.

11502116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11502116.value: There exist three sound opportunities for further research. First, dynamic relationships between competitive action sequence and competitive performance are worthy of further investigation, including the underlying mechanism for how these sequences are observable for consumers or rivals, and how it will further influence the competitive performance. Second, further examinations of the generalizability to other e-marketplace contexts (e.g. E-Bay, Amazon) and a wide array of industries are needed. We could collect new data sets in other platforms and multiple industries. Finally, we can further examine configurations of competitive actions for other important dimensions of sellers’ performance, such as consumer satisfaction, product return rate, and repeated purchase, and further examine whether configurations of causal relationships are sustainable over time by incorporating the Temporal Qualitative Comparative (TQCA) method, which enable identifying time-evolving configurations.

11502116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11502116.value: This project takes a holistic viewpoint in examining how the structure characteristics (i.e. volume, complexity, heterogeneity) of sellers’ usage of platform-based functions will further influence their sales performance, and the moderation role of sellers’ reputations. We further extend the competitive repertoire theory into e-marketplace context and integrate it with reputation literature, theoretical hypotheses are further tested with a longitudinal dataset of 43,992 seller-week observations from Taobao, one of the largest e-marketplaces in the world. The results suggest that volume and complexity of sellers’ platform-based functions will have positive effect on sales performance, while heterogeneity will have negative effect, also the sellers’ reputation will work as boundary conditions. Our project makes sound theoretical contributions for competitive repertoire literatures and e-marketplace literature by extending the competitive repertoire into e-marketplace context. Valuable implications for sellers on how to leverage platform-based functions to gain competitive advantages, and for platform governors on how to design and implement these functions are suggested. Furthermore, related dynamic relationships between competitive repertoire, strategic group and performance are examined; the salient role of characteristics of competitive action sequence; and the configurations of sellers platform-based functions for achieving high sales performance are identified, which collectively further strengthen the value and contributions in the broad field.

11504316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504316.value: 網絡贊助是搜索引擎常用的推廣方式（例如，推廣贊助商的產品或網站），它給搜索引擎提供了必要的收入。然而，用戶通常規避“贊助搜索結果”。這種規避會降低贊助搜索結果點擊率從而給付費搜索業務帶來了負面效應。 這個項目的目的是理論化和測試社會影響線索在減少用戶對贊助搜索結果的規避中的效用。我們計劃在消費者對消費者（C2C）的電子商務環境下進行，即用戶在網站上搜索產品和賣家，然後網站返回一個相關的產品和賣家的搜索結果頁面（包括贊助搜索結果和自然搜索結果）。這個項目的重點是探討兩種類型的社會影響線索。一種為信息性影響線索（例如，之前的用戶對贊助產品的質量評分和贊助產品的銷售量），另一種是規範性影響線索（例如，社交網絡上的朋友“查看”了該贊助產品）。 這個項目包括三個子項目。第一個子項目的重點是探討特定的信息性影響線索對降低用戶的贊助搜索結果規避。贊助搜索結果規避是由用戶心中對贊助產品的各種內隱理論驅動的（例如，贊助產品是不受歡迎的或低質量的）。我們提出了信息性影響線索對降低贊助搜索結果規避的匹配效應。具體地說，就是當信息性影響線索（例如，之前的用戶對贊助產品質量的正面評價）直接對應用戶心中的內隱理論（例如，贊助產品質量低而並非不受歡迎），那麽這個線索就能降低用戶對贊助搜索結果的規避。第二個子項目的重點是探索規範性影響線索的作用。根據規範性影響線索能影響用戶心中的內隱理論和伯恩斯坦的選擇轉移理論，我們提出規範性影響線索也能降低贊助搜索結果規避。 這兩個子項目的重點是贊助搜索結果與用戶的搜索關鍵詞相關。而第三個子項目將探討當贊助搜索結果偏離了用戶的搜索關鍵詞，這些線索是否還能降低贊助搜索結果規避。我們將進行一系列的實驗來驗證我們的猜想。這個項目結合了內隱理論，品牌偏好和社會影響，率先探討了用戶對贊助搜索結果的規避機制。另外，該項目也能促進贊助搜索模式的發展。

11504316.label: Realisation of objectives
11504316.value: All three research objectives have been achieved. First, we have identified a set of social influence cues in the context of online search results and investigated the effects of these cues on users’ avoidance of encountered sponsored search results (SSR) when the SSR matches their search queries (i.e., Objectives 1 and 2). We have conducted a series of laboratory experiments to empirically test the effects of these cues. We have revealed various theoretical mechanisms to explain the effects of social influence cues, which has advanced the social influence literature. Second, we have also examined the effects of social influence cues when the SSR deviates from users' brand preferences (i.e., Objective 3). We have conducted a series of laboratory experiments to empirically test the effects of social cues in this context. In addition to the above three objectives, our research work synthesized the avoidance literature and identified three forms of SSR avoidance, namely, cognitive, behavioral, and affective avoidance. We applied users’ implicit concerns on SSRs to explain users’ avoidance of an encountered SSR. We examined how and under what conditions the three forms of SSR avoidance can be reduced by various positive online social cues. The findings of this project uncover the theoretical mechanisms of social influence on reducing SSR avoidance in online settings. We also offer practical implications for online search service providers to help online users’ decision-making in their search process.

11504316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11504316.value: The results from a series of laboratory experiments reveal the effects of various social cues on users’ avoidance of spsonsored search results (SSR). We also identify three forms of SSR avoidance, namely, cognitive, behavioral, and affective avoidance, and reveal how and under what conditions the three forms of SSR avoidance can be reduced by various positive online social cues. The major findings are reported in the following forthcoming paper in a top-tier journal in the field of Information Systems, MIS Quarterly: DENG, Honglin; WANG, Weiquan; LI, Siyuan; LIM, Kai H., “Can Positive Online Social Cues Always Reduce User Avoidance of Sponsored Search Results?” forthcoming, MIS Quarterly, accepted on Jan. 11, 2021. This project also produced some other research findings that are not essential to the three research objectives. These findings are reported in (1) the following paper published in a top-tier journal in the fields of management and business, Management Science: Wang, W., Xu, J. D., and Wang, M. 2018. Distrust in Online Recommendation Agents: Moderating Role of Explanations for Organic Recommendations," Management Science (64:11), pp. 5198-5219. and (2) the following conference paper: XIONG, B., FU, M., and Weiquan. 2019. "How Story Works in Mobile App Stores? Exploring the Same-Side Effect from the Storytelling Perspective," Fortieth International Conference on Information Systems, Munich.

11504316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11504316.value: The research has great potential for further development, including the following potential areas: (1) we activated only one implicit concern during users’ decision-making to examine our posited effects of social cues. Different implicit concerns may co-exist especially when users make decisions that require much time and effort. Future studies can extend our work by examining the contexts where users apply multiple implicit concerns simultaneously and whether a specific social cue or multiple cues are needed to reduce users’ avoidance of encountered SSRs. (2) avoidance is opposite to the concept of approach, which refers to users’ intentional seeking of certain contents or objects. Future studies may extend our work by investigating potential strategies to increase users’ approach to advertised content in online settings. (3) we conducted laboratory experiments in this project, to increase realism and generalizability, future studies are encouraged to validate our findings in field settings.

11504316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11504316.value: Online social cues that utilize user-generated data, such as user reviews and product ratings, have become one of the key factors influencing online user behavior and decisions. This project focuses on sponsored search results (SSRs), a type of unsolicited information that matches users’ search queries and receives high evaluations from prior consumers. We investigate the effects of positive social cues on alleviating users’ avoidance responses toward an encountered SSR when searching for a product in a C2C e-commerce context. We synthesize the avoidance literature and identify three forms of SSR avoidance, namely, cognitive, behavioral, and affective avoidance. We examine how and reveal conditions the three forms of SSR avoidance can be reduced by various positive online social cues. This study is among the first to examine how and under what conditions various positive online social cues can influence users’ decisions and behavior and, particularly, their avoidance of SSRs when searching a product online. It offers many practical implications for online search service providers to choose and present influential social cues alongside SSRs to facilitate online users’ decision-making in their product search process.

11505016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505016.value: 這個研究計畫的主體是應用丹齊克-沃爾夫 (DW) 分解演算法來開發一類新的近似方法， 並將其用於求解大規模經濟均衡模型的變分不等式問題(VI)和混合互補問題 (MCP)。 例如，多商品經濟均衡模型可由一個成本最小化的線性規劃模型來刻畫，該模型由供應方和給需求作為價格等於邊際成本的供應需求函數的向量值函數組成。另一個例子是VI型式的運輸模型。 使用分解演算法的動機是通過連結單獨開發的子模型來求得一個全球解，以減輕模型開發和維護的難度。其他可能的好處包括使用多台電腦做平行計算，以解決在單台電腦上工作量太大的問題。我們用近似方法的目的是提高分解演算法的靈活性和性能。 具體的說，分解方法作為一個整合工具，也作為現有的用於VI 的DW分解原理的延伸，將原來的VI分成兩個子問題。分解後的VI模型由一個主問題（主-VI）和一個子問題（子VI）組成，這兩個問題都是平衡模型。如果子問題（子VI）具有特殊的結構，比如對角塊型約束，那麼它可以被進一步分解以利用平行計算的優點來縮短求解的時間。 求解上述分解VI模型計算序列可分為內外兩層。外層是分解的計算過程，其中，所述主VI和子VI以反覆運算的方式得到解決。在分解方法的每次反覆運算中，內層有兩個計算序列分別用於主VI和子VI。簡而言之，對分解方法我們有一個外層的計算順序和兩個內層計算序列，這兩個內層計算序列用於解決每次反覆運算分解出的兩個VI問題。 顯然，理想的結果是主VI和子問題-VI的近似解能使我們找到原來的VI解。從文獻中我們找到了主VI和子-VI問題逼近方法。然而，由於DW演算法和VI的解決方法的不同的收斂性，還沒有將這兩種近似方法進行整合的研究工作。在我們所提出的研究工作中，為VI所開發的一般近似-DW方法將通過結合DW分解法和現有的VI方法來得到。我們也將研究新方法的收斂特性和實證檢驗。

11505016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505016.value: In this research project, we derive an approximate Dantzig-Wolfe (DW) decomposition method for variational inequalities (VIs). The decomposed VIs consist of one approximate subproblem, which is nonlinear programming (NLP) and one approximate master program, which is also an NLP. If the VI mapping in the approximate master program is equal to that in the iterative methods for solving VI, then the approximate DW-VI simply consists of the computational sequence of solving NLP subproblem and NLP master problem in an iterative manner. The iterative methods for VI and the DW decomposition method are combined into a single iterative solution. The major findings are the proof of the convergence of the approximate DW-VI under reasonable assumptions that the VI mapping is continuous, and the development of the monotone-descent safeguard to solve the approximate master-VI only once per loop (like a big M method in solving linear programming problems). The resulting algorithm becomes more flexible to adopt other solution methods of VI problems to solve the approximate master-VI. Beside we used a time-of-use pricing model of Ontario electricity market to illustrate the application of the approximate DW-VI, we also developed another set of numerical result, based on a simple electricity market, illustrates that the approximate DW-VI can be faster than the PATH solver when solving large-scale problems. The PATH solver is the most popular solver to solve VI problems. All the above results were reported in Chung (2018, 2019).

11505016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505016.value: While some variants of the Newton’s method can be used to solve non-monotone VI problems, which is not the class of the VI problems in the current research work. Further development of the research is to combine some variants of the Newton’s method in solving the approximate master-VI. The resulting approximate DW-VI consists of the properties of the corresponding Newton’s methods, like solving non-monotone VI problems.

11505016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505016.value: While the large-scale economic equilibrium models (VIs) have been employed in the service provisioning problem in multi-cloud systems and stochastic variational inequalities with large-scale scenario analysis. The existing solver (like the most popular PATH) may be terminated because of lack of memory. Hence, decomposition methods can resolve this shortcoming. It is because the decomposed problems become much small subproblems which can be solved in an efficient way by simply and well-established optimization solution methods. In short, the significance of this research project is to remove the computational hurdle of developing very-large scale equilibrium models in this big-data era.

11505716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11505716.value: 軟件創新是如何影響IT公司市場表現及行業結構

11505716.label: Project Objectives
11505716.value: How does the rise of software-based innovation affect firm performance and the structure of the industry and industry boundaries? What are possible underlying mechanisms driving the impact of the software-based innovation on firm and industry?
rows: How does the rise of software-based innovation affect firm performance and the structure of the industry and industry boundaries?
What are possible underlying mechanisms driving the impact of the software-based innovation on firm and industry?

11505716.label: Realisation of objectives
11505716.value: This project has been going successfully so far. I'm going to explain what I have done to achieve the two objectives. The first objective is to examine how the rise of software-based innovation affects firm performance and the structure of the industry and industry boundaries. For this, I have done several things. I first collected the patent data and identified software patents to measure software-based innovation. I further used the topic modeling technique to classify software patents into pure software and software embedded with hardware. This allows us to examine what kinds of software patents affect firm performance most. We found that the greater software-based innovation within the firm is associated with less competition in product markets: increases in software intensity correlate with significant reductions in the similarity of product offering relative to that of rivals and the number of effective competitors in the market. This differentiation effect appears more strongly associated with software patents that are embedded within hardware products or devices, so as to reinforce their functionality. Moreover, software-enabled differentiation significantly mediates the relationship between software intensity and firm market value. In the process, we made an effort to provide more robust findings, for example by constructing an instrument for software innovation by exploiting annual variation in software workers across states. Our second objective is to examine possible underlying mechanisms. We now show that software-enabled differentiation significantly mediates the relationship between software innovation and firm market value. We conducted a formal mediation test for showing this. The results are robust to accounting for the potential endogeneity in the degree of software intensity.

11505716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505716.value: We find that the greater software-based innovation within the firm is associated with less competition in product markets: increases in software intensity correlate with significant reductions in the similarity of product offering relative to that of rivals and the number of effective competitors in the market. This differentiation effect appears more strongly associated with software patents that are embedded within hardware products or devices, so as to reinforce their functionality. Moreover, software-enabled differentiation significantly mediates the relationship between software intensity and firm market value. Our research contributes to the emerging literature on software-based innovation and the pathways by which software continues to transform other industry sectors, specifically through product differentiation.

11505716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505716.value: There are some limitations to our work that need addressing. First, we identify software patents using heuristics that are consistent with prior research; however, the general notion that software cannot be patented remains a significant limitation in this context. Most likely, this renders our measure of software intensity and software patenting an underestimate of the extent to which firms are truly investing in software innovation. But in the absence of clearer measures of software-based innovation, we use the best possible alternative measures. Second, recognizing that software-based innovation is endogenous, we develop models using instrumental variable regression; the results are fully consistent but we acknowledge that it is not possible to entirely rule out the effects of endogeneity bias. Third, we use the TNIC to measure product differentiation and competition but are still relatively new compared to more standard SIC-based measures of competition. Finally, we postulate and test for one possible mechanism through which software-based innovation can affect firm value – product differentiation leading to less product market competition. This does not imply that other possible mechanisms do not exist. We believe more work is needed to test other potential pathways as well.

11505716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505716.value: We test the empirical reality behind the aphorism that ‘software is eating the world.’ Indeed, the success of the current platform giants (Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, Google) also referred to as FANG, speak to the power of software-enabled innovation in upending existing market structure. In 2017 only, these four firms together added more than $600 billion to total market cap, representing 13.8% of the total increase in the U.S. market cap. Given the trends associated with the dominance of software, it is imperative for firms and managers to figure out ways to use software-based innovation to their favor. By using the patent data from 1996 to 2006, we show that software-based innovation, especially by embedded software, increases firm performance. This is partly because investing in software R&D allows firms to differentiate their products from competitors'.

11511816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11511816.value: 合同与信任：关系周期过程中之功能解析

11511816.label: Project Objectives
11511816.value: This study conceptually explicates how relational concerns vary during the relationship lifecycle, and how such concerns affect governance strategy choices. We disentangle the safeguarding and coordination functions of contracts in line with the firm's relational concerns in evolving relationship phases. Through discerning the main function of contracts in each relationship phase, we clarify when and how contracts and trust substitute and/or complement each other over the course of the relationship lifecycle. We thus advance our relationship-lifecycle theory of contracts-trust nexus, which sheds fresh light on the long-standing controversy of complements-substitues dichotomy. We aim to publish our research findings in Academy of Management Journal or Journal of Marketing.

11511816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11511816.value: The nature of the relationship between contracts and trust as modes of governance remains equivocal. A long-standing controversy has revolved around a simplistic complements-substitutes dichotomy. This study disentangles the safeguarding and the coordination functions of contracts, and theorizes that the contract-trust nexus is contingent upon the relationship phase throughout the relationship lifecycle. Specifically, we argue that contracts substitute trust in the exploratory phase in which firms are mainly concerned about the equity of cooperation, and complement trust in the expansion phase where the major relational concern becomes efficiency. In the mature phase in which the major relational concern is the maintenance of the relationship, the safeguarding function of contracts is replaced by trust, while the coordination function remains, complementing trust. Overall, we provide new insights into when and how contracts complement or substitute trust throughout the relationship lifecycle. 合同与信任作为两种企业管制机制，其功能是相互替代还是互补，迄今在学术界尚无定论。导致争论悬而未决的一个重要原因，在于学者们均沿用了一个静态的视角，即假定企业间关系在合作过程中保持不变。本研究基于企业关系生命周期理论，试图界定合同与信任两种管制机制在企业关系周期演进中的动态关系。具体而言，我们假定，企业在其合作关系的每一阶段，其关系焦虑是不同的，其决定企业管制机制功能的选择。在企业关系起始阶段，企业最主要的关系焦虑是合作的公平性，即对机会主义的疑虑。因此，在信任尚未建立的条件下，合同作为主要的管制机制，担任了企业关系监控的功能。在企业关系的发展阶段，企业最主要的关系焦虑是合作的效率性，合同的功能主要体现在资源的协调，其与逐渐发展的新任信任，相辅相成的推动企业合作的深度发展，保证合作效率。在企业关系的成熟阶段，企业的主要关系焦虑表现在良好关系的维持，因此，信任替代合同成为企业关系的管制机制。

11511816.label: Realisation of objectives
11511816.value: We set four major goals for this research project: we aimed to look at how the main relational concern during each developmental phase in the relationship lifecycle influences firm governance choice; we distinguished between the safeguarding and the coordination functions of contracts and attempted to disentangle their governance functions in line with the firm's main relational concerns in evolving relationship phases; we then tried to explain in a dynamical fashion when and how contracts and trust substitute and/or complement each other over the course of the relationship lifecycle. We thus advance our relationship-lifecycle theory of contracts-trust nexus, which sheds fresh light on the long-standing controversy of complements-substitues dichotomy; we aimed to publish our research finding bin top marketing/management journals. We believe we have fulfilled our goal satisfactorily. We have published two papers in leading marketing journals: Industrial Marketing Management (IMM) and Journal of Business Research (JBR). In the IMM, we aimed to empirically test our main hypotheses set in our GRF proposal to observe how evolving firm relational concerns affect firm governance choice and the choice patterns (i.e., complementary or substitutive in terms of contract and/or trust). In the JBR paper, we proposed and confirmed that trust could emerge in the contract negotiation phase, thus further extending the relationship lifecycle to a five-phase structure: pre-formation of relationship phase, initial phase, development phase, mature phase, and dissolving phase.
