11511816.label: Major findings and research outcome
11511816.value: We have published the research findings in two leading marketing journals: Industrial Marketing Management (Impact Factor: 4.779) and Journal of Business Research (Impact Factor: 4.028). In the IMM paper, we found that firm choice of governance strategy is the function of firm relationship lifecycle, with different main relational concerns determining firm governance strategies in different relationship phases. Thus, we shed fresh light on the long-standing controversy as to whether the contract and trust are complementary or substitutive to each other. In the JBR paper we found that interfirm trust can emerge during the contract negotiation phase that precedes the initial phase of the relationship lifecycle. Specifically, we discovered that firm contract design capability functions as the main driving factor of trust production during such a pre-formation phase of interfirm relationship.

11511816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11511816.value: Future research can draw upon this newly found five-phase relationship lifecycle to further investigate how firm relational concerns emerge and evolve and how firms make strategic governance decisions through the whole relationship lifecycle. Prior research typically take a dyadic perspective; future research could look at firm governance choice from a triadic or network perspective. Institutional factors can also be considered to affect firm governance decisions.

11511816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11511816.value: Firms need to establish a long-term cooperative relationship with their partners. Such cooperative relationship is not static but dynamic, namely it will change from an initial phase, through developing and mature phases, to a dissolving phase. During each phase, firms will have different relational concerns about their cooperative relationship with the partner, either equity or efficiency. In order to ensure the cooperation will proceed well, that is, the cooperation is efficient and/or each part will receive a fair share of the cooperation outcome, firms will choose different methods to manage the cooperative relationship according to their main relational concerns in different relationship phases. In other words, a firm's governance strategy (i.e., the use of contracts or trust) will be determined by the changing relational concerns arising from each relationship phase during the cooperation.

11518016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11518016.value: 商业秘密保护与研发工程的叙述性披露

11518016.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11518016.value: Dr Li, Yinghua Dr LIN, Yupeng

11518016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11518016.value: Corporate disclosure reduces information asymmetry between managers and shareholders, thereby increasing a firm’s stock liquidity and decreasing its cost of capital. Thus, absent any costs, value-maximizing managers have incentives to fully disclose their private information. Full disclosure, however, is rarely observed in the capital market. One of the most important constraints to full disclosure is that some disclosures may damage a firm’s competitive position in its product market. Verrecchia (1983) shows analytically that in the presence of proprietary costs, partial disclosure can be optimal, with the level of disclosure decreasing in the proprietary costs of disclosure. In this proposed research, we will examine the proprietary cost hypothesis using a trade secrets law setting that allows us to draw important causal inferences that are absent from prior empirical studies of the proprietary costs hypothesis. Specifically, we will exploit the staggered adoption of the inevitable disclosure doctrine (IDD) by U.S. state courts as an exogenous shock to the proprietary cost of disclosure. We predict that firms respond to IDD adoption by reducing the quantity and quality of narrative disclosures regarding their R&D activities. In addition, we expect that the main result is stronger for firms in more competitive industries, but weaker for firms facing more capital demand for financial information. The main contribution of this proposed research is that it has the potential to generate one of the first pieces of causal evidence on the proprietary cost hypothesis of corporate disclosure. This research also extends the literature on how laws impact financial reporting and disclosure. Previous research along this line has generally focused on laws pertaining to the capital markets, such as company laws and disclosure rules. In contrast, this research studies legal protections for trade secrets, which pertains to the laws of the product markets. The research potentially implies that product market laws can have spillover effects on capital market disclosures. 本研究计划利用美国州法院交错采纳不可避免披露原则对信息披露专有成本的外生冲击来检测会计理论里的专有成本假设。我们预测公司通过减少对研发活动的叙述性信息披露的数量和质量来回应升高的专有信息成本。此外，我们预期这个现象对外部资本市场依赖较少的公司和处在强竞争行业的公司比较明显。本研究的主要贡献在于它有可能为公司信息披露的专有成本假说首次提供因果证据。这项研究还扩展了对法律如何影响财务报告和信息披露的文献。之前的研究一般集中在有关资本市场的法律，如公司法和信息披露规则。本研究聚焦于产品和劳务市场的法律的法律保护。这项研究的一个可能的启示是产品和劳务市场的法律对资本市场披露有一定溢出效应。

11520816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11520816.value: 信息资产安全是一个组织广泛关注，需要越来越多的资源，因为这些资产的核心是实现战略优势，因为这些资产的安全威胁已经长大。不幸的是，企业最大的安全威胁之一是机构内部人士 - 的人，甚至是那些在组织外部（如股东），谁拥有专利的组织知识。事实上，内幕安全漏洞现在被认为是比外部泄露更具破坏性。例如有关香港的金融业包括流氓交易，欺诈，内幕交易，身份盗窃，泄露机密，敏感数据在U盘存储和引进的病毒进入企业网络。 传统的IT安全工作主要侧重于技术的保护，但这些方法只能提供部分保护。主要研究人员越来越多地认识到，安全的努力，更有效，还必须考虑个人和组织的影响。该帐户的内幕行为安全的努力具有防止违规和鼓励保护行为的可能性最大。 有几个有前途的方法，鼓励业内人士参与的安全行为和坚持以信息安全（ISEC）的政策已经制定。这些都用于保护激励理论，威慑理论，理性选择理论或计划行为的理论。一些研究还表明，暴露内部人士向安全，教育，培训和意识（SETA）计划的重要性。 不幸的是，许多结果相互矛盾或只有一次研究，不是普遍意义更广泛的研究或实践的支持。四大问题仍然存在：（1）没有研究充分测试的ISEC竞争理论; （2）ISEC的理论是'水平'从其他领域借用，并没有系统地contextualised; （3）大多数研究侧重于单一的行为，不涉及更广泛的实践; （4）大多数研究只关注一个文化背景下的经验数据收集（例如数据采集只能在西方或亚洲文化背景），即使ISEC强烈地受到文化的影响。 因此，我们计划进行ISEC文学的第一个广泛的荟萃分析。采用最新的荟萃分析技术，我们将（1）确定的理论提供了系统或安全合规内幕保护最强的解释和预测;（2）检查到的理论解释已妥善contextualised程度，（3）确定是否有根据所涉及（如强密码与病毒保护）行为的预测的差异，以及（4）检查到重点文化差异（如集体主义和个人主义）在文献中影响结果的程度。

11525716.label: Realisation of objectives
11525716.value: Objective 1 (100% Completed): We have conducted a thorough review on existing big data analytics technologies for online credit scoring (Pramanik et al. 2017a; Pramanik et al. 2017b; Pramanik et al. 2020). Then, we designed a new Spark-based parallel and distributed data stream-based system architecture for big data analytics (Yuan et al. 2018a; Lau et al. 2018). Moreover, a parallel Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model and parallel HDP model have been designed to mine the latent traces left by individuals on online social media to improve the accuracy of credit scoring (Yuan et al. 2018b; Lau et al. 2018). A social emotion mining method has also been examined, and it may have the potential to extract additional individual feature for advanced credit scoring (Li et al. 2017). All planned tasks related to Objective 1 have been completed. Objective 2 (100% Completed): A user behavioral feature mining model has been designed to mine the latent behavioral traces left by individuals on online social media to improve the accuracy of credit scoring (Yuan et al. 2018a). We also examined using deep neural network for extracting useful features from images (Yang et al. 2018; Yang et al. 2020). The imaged-based features (e.g., big spenders) can further improve the classification performance in online credit scoring. In addition, a utility-based feature selection method (Wang et al. 2019a) and an entropy-based term weighting method (Yang et al. 2019) have been developed for extracting and selecting textual features from online texts. All planned tasks related to Objective 2 have been completed. Objective 3 (100% Completed): We have successfully designed a community mining algorithm (Yuan et al. 2018b) and an anchor link-based method (Wang et al. 2019) for extracting an individual’s behavioral features from large social graphs to enhance the effectiveness of online credit scoring (Lau et al. 2021). Objective 4 (100% Completed): We have empirically evaluated the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed parallel LDA (Yuan et al. 2018a) and parallel HDP models (Lau et al. 2018), and behavioral feature classification model for online credit scoring. The aforementioned methods have been tested based on the individuals’ personal financial data and the corresponding social media data (e.g., Weibo) provided by our industrial collaborator (Yuan et al. 2018a; Yuan et al. 2018b). All planned tasks related to Objective 4 have been completed. Objective 5 (100% Completed): Based on the Constructivist Grounded Theory approach, we have collected and analyzed initial project data related to both the design process and the designed artifacts of big data analytics for online credit scoring (Lau et al. 2021). By synthesizing and analyzing these data, we are able to uncover preliminary principles for the design of a class of big social media analytics services for financial applications (Wang et al. 2019b). 11525716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11525716.value: “Internet Finance” is one of the essential components of the Internet Plus strategy which will drive the economic growth of the whole nation in coming years. Accordingly, our proposed GRF project is a direct response to these calls for strategic FinTech development in Hong Kong and the Greater China area. More specifically, the proposed research aims to design a novel online credit scoring framework which leverages big social media data to assess the potential credit risks of individuals. Online credit scoring is a supplement rather than a replacement of the traditional credit assessment method, and it lays the solid foundation to support an array of Internet Finance services such as online peer-to-peer (P2P) lending, online micro loans, personal wealth management, etc. Although some prior studies about online credit scoring have been reported in literature, none of them examines the challenging problem of extracting and analyzing credit intelligence from big data. Moreover, very few studies have explored the problem of analyzing individuals’ behavioral footprints left on online social media for the prediction of their credit risks. From a technological perspective, traditional computational methods cannot effectively resolve the volume, velocity, variety, and veracity issues of big social media data. Guided by the Design Science research methodology and the theoretical underpinning of Social Capital, the goal of the proposed research project is to fill the aforementioned research gaps by designing a novel framework which can leverage big social media data to enhance online credit scoring.

11525916.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11525916.value: 這對我有什麼好處呢？電商平台上的打假之戰

11525916.label: Project Objectives
11525916.value: To investigate whether different revenue models used on the platforms will result in different anti-counterfeit and pricing levels. To empirically verify whether pricing and anti-counterfeit levels are different for different platforms adopting different revenue models. To provide strategic and policy-related suggestions for all stakeholders in curbing counterfeit sales.
rows: To investigate whether different revenue models used on the platforms will result in different anti-counterfeit and pricing levels.
To empirically verify whether pricing and anti-counterfeit levels are different for different platforms adopting different revenue models.
To provide strategic and policy-related suggestions for all stakeholders in curbing counterfeit sales.

11525916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11525916.value: The continued digitization of society has given rise to a flourishing trend in online transactions. Online intermediary platforms (such as Taobao, Ebay) connect millions of merchants with consumers for product sales. However, many counterfeit products are being traded in those platforms, resulting in billions of dollars in losses for brand owners. Major e-commerce players such as Alibaba, Ebay, and Amazon all are caught up in lawsuits because of counterfeit sales on their platforms. As online commerce continues to grow, online intermediary platforms are increasingly being scrutinized for their effort in curbing counterfeits passing through their platforms. In this study, we examine the economic incentives of various stakeholders impinging on the online counterfeit sales problem. The major stakeholders are classified as authentic product merchants, counterfeit merchants and platforms for the intermediaries. Specifically, we focus on understanding how different revenue models affect the intermediaries’ incentives for fighting counterfeits. The two main revenue models – the advertising model and the brokerage model, are examined for their impact on intermediaries’ anti-counterfeit effort, and on the pricing decisions of the merchants operating on the platform. We construct a stylized model to demonstrate the intricate interrelationships of the three players in the problem of counterfeits. Data will be collected on a number of products from online platforms to verify our models. We will then apply text and data mining approach to determine the proportion of merchants selling counterfeit versions of the product across different platforms. This should enable us to empirically determine whether there is indeed a difference in pricing by the merchants as well as anti-counterfeit levels across the different intermediary platforms under different revenue schemes. This project seeks to enhance our understanding of how to align the incentives in curbing counterfeit sales. The study aims to provide insights on whether intermediaries are not “motivated” enough to address the counterfeit sales problem, or under certain occasions, are even beneficial. The findings should inform us whether online counterfeit sales have become a persistent problem due to misalignment of incentives. It also provides direct policy implications on curbing online counterfeit sales.

11525916.label: Realisation of objectives
11525916.value: The sale of counterfeit products is a common problem in the online platform. In recent years, there have been major discussions about how to fight against online counterfeit products. This study aims to show that the revenue models adopted by the platform reveal the incentive of the platform in fighting the sale of counterfeit products at the platform. 1. To investigate whether different revenue models used on the platforms will result in different anti-counterfeit and pricing levels. For the first research question, we built an analytical model to analyze the platform’s anti-counterfeit actions under two main types of revenue models: brokerage, promotion and advertising models. The real-world examples of these models are: Taobao, JuHuaSuan (JHS) and Tmall. In the platform, there are two types of sellers: authentical product seller and counterfeit product seller, competing against each other. Our results show the anti-counterfeit effect is lower in the advertising model, followed by the promotion model and brokerage model. This is because the advertising model relies on the advertising fees from both firms to derive profit. Note that such fees are collected independently of the transactions, which could be subject to complaint cost if counterfeits were sold. Hence, setting stricter anti-counterfeit measures could suppress counterfeit selling and decrease advertising revenue. Hence, for research question 1, we have accomplished the research objective. 2. To empirically verify whether pricing and anti-counterfeit levels are different for different platforms adopting different revenue models. For the second research question, we collected from two popular e-commerce websites: Taobao and Tmall. Both are e-commerce sites where sellers (merchants or stores) sell products to individual customers. Some sellers are brand-owner sellers, while others are third-party sellers. Given that it is impossible to gather all the data from Taobao and Tmall, we choose four representative categories of products: (1) shoes, (2) cosmetics, (3) electronic appliances and (4) clothing, commonly used products known to be susceptible to counterfeiting. For each product category, we choose multiple keywords to search for representative products. In total, we choose 35 keywords for the four product categories. Because we cannot observe the platform’s anti-counterfeit effort, we use a composite quality index to proxy the likelihood that the seller is a counterfeit seller. The results suggest that sellers in Tmall have relatively higher quality while the quality of sellers who joined JHS is not significantly different from sellers in Taobao. However, it could also be that Tmall sellers offer consumers better general and logistic services, which we further rule out in our robustness check. 3. To provide strategic and policy-related suggestions for all stakeholders in curbing counterfeit sales. Our results show that the phenomenon of counterfeiting selling may be tied to the platform’s revenue model. It also demonstrates that current discussions focusing on encouraging platforms to use stronger anti-counterfeit measures are perhaps missing the key point: the platform’s underlying incentive to fight counterfeit selling. From the policymaker’s perspective, it is important to recognize that different platforms have different incentives to address the counterfeit problem based on their economic interests, as reflected by the adopted revenue models. Hence, the proposal to have platforms self-regulate the counterfeit problem may work better for some platforms. Ultimately, as in the case of the advertising and promotion model in our analysis, fundamental tensions are likely to undermine the effectiveness of self-regulation.

Brand-conscious consumers will never buy counterfeit products. On the other hand, value-conscious and would compare the net values of buying counterfeit or authentic products. The results of the setting can serve as a robustness check of our original model.

11527216.label: Project Objectives
11527216.value: Understand the difficulty and solve the robust price-setting newsvendor problem. Develop a model that can help retailers to make effective price and inventory decisions under the condition of limited demand information. Provide a practically favorable solution to retailers who want to minimize the maximum regret due to the lack of complete demand information.
rows: Understand the difficulty and solve the robust price-setting newsvendor problem.
Develop a model that can help retailers to make effective price and inventory decisions under the condition of limited demand information.
Provide a practically favorable solution to retailers who want to minimize the maximum regret due to the lack of complete demand information.

11527216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11527216.value: The price-setting newsvendor problem has been well studied in the literature. However, it is commonly assumed that retailers have complete demand information modeled as a function of price and other random noises. In reality, a retailer may have very limited information on a demand model, because a retailer who has exercised only a few prices will not have sufficient information to accurately estimate a demand model. This creates a gap between academic research and practical applications. In this project, we consider the price-setting newsvendor problem with incomplete demand information. A retailer makes price and inventory decisions to minimize the maximum regret, defined as the difference between the expected profit based on limited demand information and the expected profit based on complete demand information. We try to derive a closed-form expression of the optimal price and inventory decisions for this problem, which makes our model easy to implement and hence practically favorable. To show its applicability, we will test our model on a real data set. 报童定价问题已经被大量的文献研究过。但是，这些文献都假定 需求作为价格的函数是已知的。然而，在实际中，零售商们往往 只在几个价格点上定过价。这些信息不足以准确的估计在所有价 格上的需求。这一点，使得理论研究无法应用到实践中。在这个 项目里面我们解决这个问题。我们研究没有完整需求信息下的报 童定价问题。零售商做价格和库存决策来最小化最大的遗憾，也 就是在完整需求信息和不完整需求信息下的利润差。我们将把最 优决策的形式尽量刻画出来，这会使得我们的方法能很容易的应 用在实践中。我们将用真是的数据来测试我们的模型。

11527216.value: The objectives have been completely achieved. We model it as a robust optimization problem with several layers of optimization. We successfully solved the problem by reducing it to a one-dimensional optimization problem such that it can be easily implemented in practice.

Develop a model that can help retailers to make effective price and inventory decisions under the condition of limited demand information.

11527216.label: Major findings and research outcome
11527216.value: We consider the price-setting newsvendor problem in which the retailer knows the expected demand on a few exercised price points and the distribution of the random noise. Both additive and multiplicative demand models are studied. The retailer makes price and inventory decisions to minimize the maximum regret, which is defined as the difference between the expected profit based on limited demand information and that based on complete demand information. We show that this robust optimization problem can be reduced to a one-dimensional optimization problem, and we derive the optimal price and inventory decisions. We also provide a demand learning policy that can reduce the minmax regret to any delta within O(1/delta) steps. We also study the problem in which the retailer maximizes the worst-case profit, and we obtain similar results. Extensive numerical studies show that our method has a great performance that dominates that of the regression method.

11527216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11527216.value: For future research, we may consider to remove the assumption of additive demand model or multiplicative demand model.

11527216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11527216.value: By relaxing the assumption on knowing complete demand information, this research moves a big step to push the pricing-setting newsvendor model to practical implementation.

11527316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11527316.value: 社交网络对零售业供应链管理的影响

11527316.label: Project Objectives
11527316.value: Characterize the tradeoff of endogenous social learning under different social network structures. Analyze the role of social learning in consumer panic buying, when facing supply disruption risks. Study the optimal dynamic pricing policy under social network structure in multi-period problems.
rows: Characterize the tradeoff of endogenous social learning under different social network structures.
Analyze the role of social learning in consumer panic buying, when facing supply disruption risks.
Study the optimal dynamic pricing policy under social network structure in multi-period problems.

11527316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11527316.value: 本项目的目标是建立一个研究社交网络对零售业供应链管理的影响的分析框架。 我们将集中考虑两种社交网络效应（社会学习和网络外部性），并研究它们是如何影响消费者的购买行为和零售商的定价和库存管理的决策，尤其是在新产品推出和面临供应中断的风险时。 当下，全球有超过二十亿人活跃使用社交媒体。在零售供应链管理的背景下，社交网络已经表现出对消费者购买决策显著的影响，尤其是当它涉及到新产品的采购或面临供应中断这样的异常事件 。例如，研究发现在20％-50％ 的购买决定里，朋友的建议和消费决策是最主要的影响因素，而这种影响在消费者购买首次的产品或服务时影响尤其显著（ Bughin，Doogan & Vetvik，2010）。 了解社交网络的影响对顾客的决策影响，并在新的社交网络时代优化运营决策（如定价和库存管理）对零售商越来越重要。在本项目中，我们计划解决以下关键问题：（1）根据不同的社交网络结构特征的内源性和社会学习的权衡， 如何优化社会学习管理和零售定价； （2）当出现供应中断的风险，如何应对社会学习对消费者的抢购行为和零售商的运营决策的影响； （3）在多阶段问题中， 如何优化社会网络效应下的动态定价和库存决策。 本项目负责人在建议的研究领域有丰富的研究经验，并已在相关研究方面取得了令人鼓舞的初步结果。建议研究的结果会使管理人员对在社交网络时代零售供应链的挑战和对策有更深的认识。

11527316.label: Realisation of objectives
11527316.value: There are three objectives. In the following, we show how each objective has been fully achieved: 1. We have fully achieved the first goal of characterizing the trade-off of endogenous social learning. We consider a two-period monopoly setting. Consumers can purchase in the first period based on their prior product value or in the second period based on their prior value and friends' purchasing information, which is acquired exogenously without cost or endogenously with a cost. We show how the cost of consumer learning affects the firm's dynamic pricing policy, consumer information acquisition decision, and social welfare. 2. We have fully achieved the second goal of analyzing the role of social learning in consumer panic buying, when facing supply disruption risks. Supply disruption refers to the interruption of the normal production or distribution of products within supply chains. Despite the extensive attention on supply disruptions from industry and academia, few studies have examined consumers’ behaviors and their impact on the retailer’s operational strategies when there is supply disruption risk. We develop a model in which the first batch of consumers evaluates the potential supply disruption risk and decides whether to stockpile extra units for future consumption (i.e., panic buying). Their purchase decisions influence the second batch of consumers via social learning. We derive the optimal inventory ordering policy for the retailer and evaluate the retailer’s loss of profit if the impact of social learning is not taken into consideration. 3. We have fully achieved the third goal of studying the optimal dynamic pricing policy under social network effects. First, we analyze a monopolistic seller’s optimal differential pricing problem with strategic consumers connected in social networks. The consumers who purchase in the later period can get positive externality from her friends who have purchased in the early period but have to bear a utility discount for the delayed consumption. We consider networks with general structures, which means that the influences (connections) between consumers can be different and asymmetric. We characterize how social networks influence consumers’ strategic purchasing decisions; how the sellers design the optimal differential pricing strategy; and how much the sellers can gain from using network-dependent differential pricing, compared to using uniform pricing. Second, we also study the optimal pricing policy for the novel POI-based collaboration model between online apps and offline venues (e.g., Pokemon Go and restaurants), when there are both social network effects and congestion effects. Finally, we consider users’ participation-dependent social learning, i.e., learning of the Quality of Service (QoS) through users’ online reviews. The key difference from the traditional social learning mechanism is that QoS, the social learning object, is not a fixed value, instead, it depends on the number of review participants. We study how such a new learning process affects the dynamic pricing strategy of the online service provider in both a monopoly market and a duopoly market.

11527316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11527316.value: 1. Based on our analysis of how the cost of consumer learning affects the firm's dynamic pricing policy, consumer information acquisition decision, and social welfare, we find that when consumer learning is costless, the firm's profit is a convex function of learning intensity; while when consumer learning has a cost, the firm's profit non-decreases in learning intensity and decreases in learning cost. Consumer learning is beneficial to consumers and social welfare, but learning without a cost is not always better for the firm, consumers and social welfare. For the details, please refer to paper 5 in Part C. 2. Based on our analysis of social learning effect in consumer panic buying under supply disruption risks, we show that when the portion of panic buying consumers among the first batch (which we define as the initial panic intensity) is at a moderate level, consumer panic buying and SL behaviors can be beneficial for the retailer and the social welfare. In contrast, if the initial panic intensity is very low or very high, SL can hurt the retailer’s profit and total social welfare. For the details, please refer to paper 1 in Part C. 3. Based on our analysis of dynamic pricing policy with strategic consumers connected in social networks, we find that when the influence between the consumers is symmetric and the intensity of the network externality effect is lower than a threshold, it’s optimal for the seller to conduct an increasing-pricing strategy. However, when the influence between the consumers is asymmetric and the network externality effect is very substantial, the seller may use decreasing-pricing strategy for some consumers. Second, we show that ignoring consumer network structure can cause substantial profit loss under certain conditions, which implies the high value of network information in such cases. Finally, the comparison between the differential and uniform pricing policies shows that the influence asymmetry among the consumers is beneficial for the seller in the former case but harmful in the latter case. For the details, please refer to paper 4 in Part C. 4. Base on our analysis of the novel POI-based collaboration model between online apps and offline venues, we develop an optimal two-part tariff scheme, which charges the venue for becoming a POI, and subsidizes the venue every time a user interacts with the POI. The subsidy design efficiently incentivizes the venue’s infrastructure investment, and we prove that our tariff achieves the highest app’s revenue among a general class of tariffs. For the details, please refer to paper 3 in Part C. 5. Based on our analysis of how the participant-dependent social learning process affects the dynamic pricing strategy of the online service provider, we show that (1) in a monopoly market, when the capacity is small or the users’ prior QoS belief is high, the provider will choose a higher introductory price in the first period than the price in the second period. This is in sharp contrast with the common practice of setting a lower introductory price to attract users when congestion is not an issue. (2) In a duopoly market, we model two providers’ competition in an infinite time horizon as a stochastic competition game and show that there exists at least one stationary Markov perfect equilibrium (SMPE). We then use a model-free reinforcement learning approach (i.e., the Nash Q-learning algorithm) to calculate the SMPE. We show that the time evolution process of the equilibrium prices will converge to steady states, where the equilibrium price strategy is dependent on the two providers’ capacities, but independent of the users’ prior QoS beliefs. For the details, please refer to paper 2 in Part C.

11527316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11527316.value: Further development of the research includes both further analytical studies and empirical studies on social network effect in the retail supply chain management. For example, in addition to pricing and inventory policies considered in this project, one may also consider other operational strategies such as surprise bonus strategies, in the presence of consumers’ social learning. In our working paper (paper 6 in Part C), we explore such aspects. One may also conduct empirical studies to verify these analytical findings.

11527316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11527316.value: There are over 2 billion people actively using social media worldwide. In the context of retail supply chain management, social networks have shown significant influence on consumer purchasing decisions, especially when it comes to new product purchasing or facing unusual events such as when supply disruption happens. It becomes critical for retailers to understand the effects of social networks on customers’ behaviors, and optimize their operational decisions (such as pricing and inventory management) in the new social network era. The aim of this project is to build an analytical framework to understand the impact of social networks on retail supply chain management. In particular, we address the following key questions: (1) How to characterize the tradeoff of endogenous social learning and jointly optimize social learning induction and retail pricing? (2) How does social learning influence consumers’ panic buying behavior and retailers’ operational decisions, when there are supply disruption risks? (3) How to optimize dynamic pricing and capacity decisions, when social learning is participant-dependent?

11529116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11529116.value: 實驗勞動力市場的禮物交換和不道德互惠

11529116.label: Project Objectives
11529116.value: To provide new theoretical perspectives to extend the research on gift exchange in experimental labor markets. To theoretically and empirically investigate unethical reciprocity in gift-exchange relationships in experimental labor markets. To empirically investigate how generous compensation may motivate employees to engage in unethical reciprocity to benefit their employers or managers.
rows: To provide new theoretical perspectives to extend the research on gift exchange in experimental labor markets.
To theoretically and empirically investigate unethical reciprocity in gift-exchange relationships in experimental labor markets.
To empirically investigate how generous compensation may motivate employees to engage in unethical reciprocity to benefit their employers or managers.

11529116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11529116.value: This proposal extends the research on gift exchange in experimental labor markets. Drawing on insights from both sociology and social psychology, the gift exchange model in economics suggests that employees are often motivated to reciprocate their employer’s generous compensation by working harder (Akerlof & Yellen, 1988; 1990, Fehr et al., 1993; Fehr & Gächter, 2000, for reviews). Positive reciprocity in the workplace, however, does not always lead to good-natured outcomes. For example, positive reciprocity between bribers and bribes can result in corruption. Thus, our proposal extends our common understanding about positive reciprocity in employment relationships to investigate unethical reciprocity in the workplace. Specifically, we investigate how and why generous compensation can motivate employees to engage in unethical reciprocity to benefit their employers at the expense of others. We suggest that because employees often view employers’ generous compensation as strategic investments instead of mere generosity, they are likely to feel obligated to positively reciprocate by actively promoting their employers’ economic outcomes. Thus, they may be biased in their ethical judgments and decision-making, resulting in unfair or unethical action to benefit their employers or managers even when doing so harms others. In particular, they may be more motivated to engage in such unfair or unethical actions when they do not have the opportunity or they don’t feel that they have adequately reciprocated the favorable treatment they have received from their employer. At the same time, we also expect that employers’ characteristics will considerably influence employees’ ethical choices. Employees often learn about their employers’ or managers’ expectations through their observations of their behaviors (Simons, 2002). Thus, we expect that observing their manager’s or employer’s lying in a different context will increase employees’ likelihood of engaging in unethical reciprocity because they can interpret their manager or employer as more willing to accept and support unethical action. In addition, we also expect that different kinds of lies (e.g., selfish black vs. altruistic white lies) from managers or employers will have different effects on the likelihood of employees engaging in different kinds of unethical reciprocity. In particular, observing managers’ or employers’ self-serving lies may make employees more likely to lie or cheat to benefit both themselves and their managers or employers. We plan to conduct three controlled behavioral experiments using modified gift exchange games (Charness, 2004; Fehr, et al., 1993; Fehr, et al., 1998) to test our hypotheses in experimental labor markets. 該研究提案延伸實驗勞力市場禮物交換方面的研究。 吸取了來自社會學和社會心理學的見解，經濟學的禮物交換模式認為，員工通常通過更加努力工作來積極地回報他們的雇主。但是，工作​​場所積極的互惠並不總是導致有益的結果。例如，行賄者和受賄者之間的積極互惠可能會導致腐敗。因此，我們的研究通過擴大了我們關於僱傭關係正互惠的共識來調查工作場所中不道德的互惠。 具體而言，我們研究為什麼優厚的薪酬可以激勵員工從事不道德的互惠來受益於雇主，但是對他人利益造成損害。我們認為，由於員工通常將雇主慷慨的待遇看作戰略性的投資，而不是單純的慷慨，他們很可能會覺得自身有義務來積極幫助雇主產生經濟方面的正回報。因此他們可能會在他們的倫理判斷和決策有所偏差，從而導致不公平或不道德的互惠行為來通過損害他人的方式來受益他們的雇主或經理。特別是，當他們感覺自己不能夠足夠回報顧主或經理的優厚的待遇的時候，他們可能會更積極地參與不公平或不道德的互惠。與此同時，我們也提出雇主本身的性格也將影響員工的道德選擇。員工經常通過雇主或經理人的行為來見了解和推斷他們​​的道德期望，因此觀察經理或雇主在不同的環境的不道德言行會增加員工從事不道德從事互惠的可能性。 此外，我們也希望研究雇主或經理在工作中善意和惡意的謊言會對員工不道德的互惠行為產生怎樣的影響。我們計劃開展三組不同的試驗來檢驗我們關於實驗勞動力市場中不道德互惠行為的假設。

11529116.label: Realisation of objectives
11529116.value: We have achieved most of the objectives that we originally planned. Specifically, our research takes a new theoretical perspective to investigate how pay variations may affect employees’ ethical behavior beyond the wage-effort exchange. Employer-employee exchange models from different disciplines suggest that an effective solution to workplace deviance is to provide market or even above-market compensation to increase employee contribution (e.g., Fehr & Gächter, 2000; Fehr, Kirchsteiger, & Riedl, 1993; 1998; Shaw, Dineen, Fang, & Vellella, 2009; Tsui, Pearce, Porter, & Tripoli, 1997). For example, both gift-exchange models in economics and research on human resource management practices suggest that relatively high overall compensation is important for high organizational performance (Akerlof & Yellen, 1988; 1990; Fehr, Kirchsteiger, & Riedl, 1998; Yellen, 1995; Youndt et al., 1996). In particular, ceteris paribus, highly paid employees are supposed to display stronger motivation and work ethics and be less likely to engage in sabotaging behavior than underpaid employees because they will reciprocate the above-market compensation with harder work. Although high compensation can reduce workplace deviance, we suggest that it may also inadvertently create a new ethical problem. In particular, different from previous research, we suggest that highly paid employees often feel obligated to actively promote their employers’ economic outcomes above and beyond their normal duties. As a result, they may be biased in their ethical judgments and decision-making, making them more likely to engage in unethical reciprocity that benefits their employers and managers but harms innocent others. Thus, our research investigates the inadvertent ethical consequences of high, above-market wages by integrating efficiency-wage theories (Akerlof, 1982; Akerlof & Yellen, 1988; 1990) and employer-employee exchange models from economics, social psychology, sociology, and management (e.g., Blau, 1955; Fehr & Gächter, 2000, Thibaut & Kelley, 1959). We have conducted several empirical studies to test our predictions. The results of these studies consistently show that generous compensation can motivate employees to engage in unethical reciprocity to benefit their employers/managers at the expense of others. Our research contributes to the research on compensation, employment relationships, and ethical behavior by integrating cross-disciplinary conceptual frameworks to investigate how both below- and above-market-wages can stimulate different kinds of unethical behaviors. In particular, it will advance our understanding of employees’ unethical reciprocity, a phenomenon that extant employer-employee exchange models have rarely investigated.

11529116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11529116.value: In the first paper, we conducted four empirical studies to test our prediction about the effects of high compensation on employees' unethical reciprocity. The first three complementary studies used behavioral economics games to tightly control for noise and exogenous variables and to precisely assess employees’ unethical reciprocity and reciprocal deviance in the lab (e.g., Camerer, 2003; Falk & Heckman, 2009; Murnighan & Wang, 2016). Specifically, Study 1 used a modified Gift-exchange game (Charness, 2004; Fehr et al., 1993) and a three-party Dictator Game (Hamman, Loewenstein, & Weber, 2010) to investigate employees’ favoritism and reciprocal deviance. Its results showed that high, above-market wages led employees to engage in unethical reciprocity to unfairly benefit their managers at the expense of a third party. In addition, when managers had the possibility to reward employees’ unethical reciprocity, employees demonstrated more favoritism, especially when they were paid below- rather than above-market-wages. Studies 2 and 3 used a similar modified Gift-exchange game and a Delegation Game (Erat, 2013; Gneezy, Rockenbach, & Serra-Garcia, 2013; Wang & Murnighan, 2016) to investigate employees’ unethical reciprocity and reciprocal deviance in terms of lying and deception. Their results showed that highly paid employees were more likely to act dishonestly to advance their manager’s interest. Finally, Study 4 complemented the first two experimental studies with some initial field evidence by testing whether highly paid police officers would be more likely to conduct illegal searches and seizures and make false arrests to help their department and/or supervisor. In the second paper, we investigated the possible mechanisms and how to remedy the effect of high compensation on unethical reciprocity. Specifically, in one study, we found that employees’ gratitude mediated the relationship between managers’ high compensation and employees’ unethical reciprocity. In another study, we found that offering contingent pay with high work effort requirements helped reduce the unintended effects of above-market wages on unethical reciprocity. We also extend some effects in another study to different cultural contexts.

11529116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11529116.value: Our studies fell short of testing how compensation might interact with other contextual factors to influence employees’ unethical reciprocity. In particular, because we solely focused on employees, we tightly controlled managers’ choices in our experiments. The drawback, however, is that when employees engaged in unethical reciprocity to help their managers, they simply assumed that their managers would approve or support their unethical favors. Models of interdependent preferences (Kelley & Thibaut, 1978; Fehr & Schmidt, 2006), however, suggest that people often adjust their own behavior according to the characteristics of their counterparts. Thus, employees are very likely to adjust their own behavior according to their knowledge or observation of their managers. For example, employees might be less inclined to engage in unethical reciprocity if they believe that their generous manager is also scrupulous and fair-minded. Thus, future research might investigate how information or social cues about a manager’s moral character would affect employees’ choice of unethical reciprocity.

11529116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11529116.value: This research extends exchange theory by investigating unethical reciprocity induced by high compensation in employee-manager exchange relationships. Results from three experimental studies based on behavioral economics games showed that after employees had reciprocated their managers’ wage offers with commensurate work efforts, managers’ previous compensation decisions still had potent effects on employees’ subsequent ethical behaviors. Specifically, Study 1 showed that high, above-market wages led employees to engage in unethical reciprocity to unfairly benefit their managers at the expense of a third party. In addition, when managers had the possibility to reward employees’ unethical reciprocity, employees demonstrated more favoritism, especially when they were paid below- rather than above-market-wages. Studies 2 and 3 replicated Study 1’s results using different games and designs. Their results showed that highly paid employees were more likely to act dishonestly to advance their manager’s interest. Finally, Study 3 complemented our experimental results with some initial field evidence, suggesting that highly paid police officers were more likely than their peers to engage in unethical and illegal actions to help their organization and/or supervisor. We discuss our results by applying cross-disciplinary insights about exchange models and compensation to organizational studies.

11530616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11530616.value: 稀缺效果下的庫存管理

11530616.label: Project Objectives
11530616.value: To study the optimal inventory decisions of a firm in the existence of scarcity effect and lost-sales. To examine the importance of availability decisions in the existence of scarcity effect. To analyze the impact of scarcity effect on inventory and availability decisions.
rows: To study the optimal inventory decisions of a firm in the existence of scarcity effect and lost-sales.
To examine the importance of availability decisions in the existence of scarcity effect.
To analyze the impact of scarcity effect on inventory and availability decisions.

11530616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11530616.value: The idea behind the proposed project has arisen from recent discussions with a local retail chain. Traditionally, inventory management aims at balancing the trade-off between risk of shortage and risk of excess inventory. However, practitioners may not necessarily see shortages as a curse anymore. In particular, shortage will create the illusion of scarcity among consumers, which may help increase future demand. Firms need to take into account this kind of scarcity effect when managing inventory. We will consider a single-item multi-period periodic-review inventory system in which the firm makes not only inventory decisions but also availability decisions. In other words, the firm does not need to make all inventory available. By withholding inventory, there is a higher chance of shortage, which has a positive impact on future demand. The goal is to study how to make inventory and availability decisions to maximize the firm’s expected total discounted profit. In the extensive literature on inventory management, there are only a few reported results for problems with scarcity effects. These reported results come from studies that focus on the case of backorder, i.e., outstanding customer demand will be fulfilled in the future if there is a shortage. While the backorder assumption is applicable in some industries, there are many industries where customer demand is lost whenever there is a shortage. There is significant differences between the backorder case and the lost-sales case in availability management: Outstanding demand can still be used to clear with-held inventory (that is not made available) as the outstanding demand will be fulfilled in future. In the lost-sales case, however, the firm has to bet on future demand to clear with-held inventory. While the optimal policy structure for the backorder case has been identified recently, there is little known about the lost-sales case. The proposed project will aim to fill the gap. 擬建項目背後的想法已經從近期與當地的零售連鎖店的討論出現。庫存管理背後的想法是平衡短缺的危險和過剩庫存的風險之間的折衷。然而，醫生不一定看到短缺的詛咒了。特別是，短缺將創造稀缺性在消費者中的錯覺，這可能有助於增加未來的需求。企業需要管理庫存時，考慮到稀缺性的影響這種。我們會考慮一個單一的項目多期定期審查的庫​​存系統中，該公司不僅使庫存決策，而且決策的可用性。換句話說，該公司並不需要讓所有廣告資源的情況。通過扣壓庫存，有較高的機會短缺，這對未來需求產生積極的影響。我們的目標是研究如何使庫存和供應情況決定最大化企業的期望總貼現的利潤。在對庫存管理的大量文獻中，只有少數報告具有稀缺效應問題的結果。這些報告的結果來自於研究，專注於缺貨，即卓越的客戶需求將在未來得到滿足的情況下，如果有短缺。雖然缺貨假設是適用於某些行業，有很多的行業，只要有不足的客戶需求都將丟失。還有就是缺貨的情況下和失去的銷售情況可用性管理之間的差異顯著：傑出的需求仍然可以用於清除庫存扣留（未提供）作為傑出的需求將在未來實現。在失去了銷售情況，但是，該公司已經將賭注押在未來的需求，以明確與持有的庫存。而對於缺貨情況下的最優政策結構已經最近發現，很少有知道關於遺失的銷售情況。擬議的項目旨在填補了國內空白。

11530616.label: Realisation of objectives
11530616.value: To study the optimal inventory decisions of a firm in the existence of scarcity effect and lost-sales, we formulate a novel model in which the firm makes availability and pricing decisions for successive generations provided both direct and relative scarcity effects. Specifically, the firm sells a new generation of some product period by period, where each generation goes through two phases in each period. In Phase 1, a new generation is launched, and customers have uncertainties in the valuation of the new generation due to its new functionality or new features that the market is not familiar with. However, scarcity in this phase may increase the utility of getting the product. As time goes by, in Phase 2, customers have more knowledge about this generation and hence their valuations are realized. Customers who arrive in Phase 1 are strategic and decide whether to attempt to purchase immediately or wait until Phase 2. The firm decides the price and availability for the generation in Phase 1, and dynamically decides the price for Phase 2. As scalpers are also an important player in the presence of scarcity, we moved on to study another model in the presence of a scalper. In particular, there are a monopolist firm, conspicuous consumers and a scalper in the market. Conspicuous customers decide from whom to purchase when the rm may use a rationing policy and a scalper may exist to compete with the rm. We first study the optimal rationing and pricing policy of the firm when there is no scalper due to laws or regulations. Then, we analyze the scenario when a scalper is allowed in the market. Finally, we compare the two scenarios. For both models, we analyze the availability decisions both in the presence and in the absence of scarcity effect. The results suggest that availability decisions are important in the existence of scarcity effect, and demonstract the impact of scarcity effect on inventory and availability decisions.

11530616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11530616.value: For the first model, we find that in the absence of scarcity effects, firm-induced scarcity is never optimal. The firm should either satisfy all demand in Phase 1 or not sell in this phase at all, where the choice between the two options depends on the inter-temporal difference in margin. When customers are affected by scarcity effects, however, such options remain to be optimal only if the market size in Phase 1 is small; otherwise, it is possible for the rm to induce significant scarcity and at the same time sell to a large number of customers. In this case, the optimal policy depends on how customers evaluate the relative scarcity effect. Due to the relative scarcity effect, there is an increase in utility when the current availability is lower than the past availability, and a decrease in utility vice versa. Customers are known as gain-seeking when the increase in the former case is larger than the decrease in the latter case and customers are known as loss-averse otherwise. Our results suggest that in the long run, the firm should adopt a constant availability policy if customers are loss-averse, and a varying availability policy if customers are gain-seeking. For the second model, we obtain three main results. First, in a deterministic situation, we demonstrate the scalper will join the market whenever the rm begins to ration a product. The reason is that conspicuous consumers have a higher purchase willingness when products are more difficult or expensive to buy. Accordingly, as long as the rm engages in rationing, it attracts scalpers to join in and in turn increase scarcity, and then, both rm and scalper can achieve excess profits. Our second main result is that due to customers' conspicuous consumption, the firm will introduce scarcity. Meanwhile, the rm is more likely to create scarcity in the market with the scalper. Furthermore, the fill rate adopted by the firm in a scalping market is always lower than that in the no-scalping market under the same consumers' level of conspicuousness. Finally, we find that the optimal price and associated prot of the rm in the scalping market are always higher than or equal to those in the no-scalping market. The reason is that the presence of the scalper helps the rm make the degree of scarcity higher but without losing consumers; thus, the firm's optimal price is higher and fill rate is lower in the scalping than in the no-scalping market.

11530616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11530616.value: This research project suggests that availability policy is important and it depends on customers' sensitivity to scarcity. As such, future research in several directions would be important. Empirically, it is important to measure customers' sensitivity to scarcity. Only with this sensitivity can firms accurately accurately find out the optimal pricing and availability decisions. Second, our paper assume that customers have homogenous sensitivity towards scarcity. Empirically, it is important to test how true this assumption is. In case customers are heterogenous in their sensitivities towards scarcity, how hetereogenous are they? Analytically, it would also be worthwhile to extend our research to the case when customers exhibit hetereogenous sensitivity towards scarcity. In particular, does the firm's optimal differ from the case when customers are homogenous? How much do we lose by assuming that customers are homogenous?

11530616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11530616.value: In this research project, we consider the effect that customers are more satisfied with getting a product when there is a shortage for the product, and we call it the scarcity effect. We study the firm's optimal pricing and availability decisions when customers are affected by scarcity effect. Without scarcity effect, a firm should never intentionally create a shortage for the product. With scarcity effect, however, it may be more profitable for the firm to create a shortage. However, the customers lose some customers by creating a shortage. In this aspect, a scalper may be able to help the firm to serve more customers and charge a high price at the same time. Our work suggests that scarcity effect has an impact on the firm's optimal pricing and availability policy. We suggest that more work should be done along this direction to guide firm's decisions in the existence of different customer behavior.

11531016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11531016.value: Gamification in the workplace is burgeoning. However, organizations frequently have difficulty sustaining user engagement with a gamified information system (IS). The project has focused on how a gamified IS in the workplace engages users and encourages them to continue system use. By proposing the concepts of flow experience (FE) and aesthetic experience (AE) as different ways to provide deep and meaningful user engagement, this study developed a model and explored the antecedents of FE and AE and their roles in explaining an individual’s continuance intention to use of a gamified IS. The model was tested utilizing data collected from 178 users of a gamified IS in a global consulting company. The results demonstrated that although FE and AE are complementary forces, AE was more salient than FE for explaining continuance intention. The research proposes AE as a parsimonious yet powerful construct that extends the research on user engagement. The findings contribute to research on gamification by shifting scholarly attention from deep engagement characterized by FE to meaningful engagement characterized by AE. The project has conceptualized gamification affordances and verified the utility of the constructs and explored how and why gamified IS often failed to engage users. The research project has generated scholarly outcomes, including four articles published in major IS journals (SSCI indexed) and one article in a premier international conference.

11531016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11531016.value: Gamification is increasingly adopted in many fields, including business, entertainment, and healthcare. The question of how to design more engaging technology (or applications) is attracting researchers and practitioners. The research project has potential to create academic and practical implications for those who seek to find a novel way to engage users via using game elements in non-game contexts. Although the PI believes that the study contributes to a better understanding of user engagement by validating AE as a construct to predict continuance intention, the magnitude of AE’s effect may vary depending on the purposes of gamified ISs. The PI calls on researchers to examine the model we proposed and tested in the current study in different gamification contexts in order to ensure the generalizability of the proposed model. The PI believes that further research may benefit from examining the role of AE in different types of IS use.

11531016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11531016.value: Many business organizations have introduced gamification in the ISs of existing business activities. Despite widespread belief in the benefits of gamification, empirical evidence shows that many gamified ISs fail to deliver on their objectives because the perceived beneficial effects of the game elements on user engagement are often short-lived. Given that the success of a gamified IS depends largely on continued user engagement, an understanding of how to sustain user engagement with a gamified IS is crucial. The project aimed to answer the question of how gamification works in sustaining user engagement with an enterprise IS in the workplace. To answer this question, drawing on the framework of situated motivational affordances and self-determination theory, the study developed and tested a theoretical model explaining the effects of motivational affordances on user engagement with an IS in the workplace. For academia, this peojct extended the theory of affordance by conceptualizing new affordances enabled by gamification technologies that have not been examined in previous IS literature. For industry, the project informed future designs and identified effective techniques and game mechanisms that ensure the successful gamification at work.

11531516.label: Project Objectives
11531516.value: To quantify the effect of monetary incentives on the quantity of content contribution in social media and online communities. To quantify the effect of monetary incentives on the quality of content contribution in social media and online communities. To investigate the determinants of online contributor coverage on stocks in the financial market context and examine how the effects of monetary incentives on crowd-sourced contributors’ content contribution vary based on the characteristics of stocks covered.

11531516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11531516.value: Few empirical studies have directly assessed the economic consequences of providing monetary incentives to content contributors in online communities. The lack of research on monetary incentives may be partly due to the unavailability of data on who receives money and how receivers behave before and after being exposed to the monetary incentive, as well as the absence of an objective measure on the quality of content in social media. Using data from Seeking Alpha (SA), one of the largest online crowd sourced equity research communities for investors, we overcome the hurdles mentioned above. The results of this proposed study could reveal how monetary incentives affect the quantity and quality of online content contribution. This study directly informs the decision making of online communities in terms of whether monetary incentives should be used to encourage content contribution and how to better allocate a limited budget to achieve diversity in content and maximize the benefits of monetary incentives. 很少有實證研究直接評估為在線社區的內容提供者提供金錢激勵所帶來的經濟後果。缺乏這方面研究的原因可能部分是由於缺少哪些人得到金錢激勵和他們在得到激勵前後的行為變化等方面的數據，以及內容貢獻的質量缺乏一個客觀的衡量標準 。這項研究利用美國最大的眾包證券研究在線社區之一SeekingAlpha（SA）所提供的數據克服了上述障礙。研究的結果可以揭示金錢激勵機制如何影響在線內容貢獻者提供的內容數量和質量。這項研究直接為網絡社區運營者提供決策支持，解答金錢激勵是否應該被用來鼓勵內容提供，以及如何更好地分配有限的預算來實現內容的多樣性和最大限度地發揮金錢激勵的效益等問題。

11531516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11531516.value: The research project examines the performance consequences of providing monetary incentive to both existing and new amateur analysts on social media and its implications for online investor communities. I find that monetary incentive is effective in increasing the amount of content output and generating more interest from the community, but it leads to neither better nor worse stock recommendations. Additional analysis suggests that monetary incentive results in wider stock and industry coverage, a sign of increased content diversity.

11531516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11531516.value: The monetary compensation examined in this research project is relatively small, especially compared with the high salary received by professional security analysts. It is possible that the effect of monetary incentive on amateur analysts may depend on the amount of monetary gain. Future research can further answer this question.

11531516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11531516.value: Social media is playing an increasingly important role in financial markets. It not only is the new and additional channel to obtain market information besides traditional media outlets (e.g., newspapers and TV) but also becomes the venue for investors to share and exchange investment ideas. How to encourage investors to contribute more contents of higher quality to social media discussion was not well studied. This research project contributes to the understanding of the role of monetary incentive in stimulating the sharing of value-relevant information by investors in social media communities and provides empirical evidence on how monetary incentive affects the quantity and quality of content outputs by amateur analysts on social media. We find that monetary incentive increases content contribution and diversity but does not lead to improved quality of stock recommendations.

11531716.label: Project Objectives
11531716.value: Construct a political economy model under uncertainty for environmental policy. Provide an interdisciplinary approach of environmental policy. Design a “second- best but implementable” environmental policy. Provide a new ranking –in terms of efficiency- of some usual environmental policy instruments. Provide a general framework that can be used for practical environmental policy. The general theory could be applied to the specific case of Hong-Kong.

11531716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11531716.value: 在這個項目中，我們的目標是分析效率和政治接受能力的平衡，最終目標為促使設計出真正可行的環境政策。因此，我們會考慮政策制定者的自身目標和大眾利益的分歧。我們已經知道一些常用工具的相對效率（例如指令和控制、稅收）會因不明朗的因素而發生急劇的變化。但是，我們希望把環境經濟學的相關特性添加成為整體考慮的一環，在排放容許的限制下考慮各種因素 。首先，環境政策通常發生在一個非常不穩定的環境。其次，投資在推動減排的環保政策基本上是不可逆轉的，而且需要時間來設置。因此，我們想建立一個政治經濟學理論來分辨最佳的政策工具，符合（一）政策的限制和（二）環境政策相關的經濟特質。

11531716.label: Realisation of objectives
11531716.value: The PI and co-Is have completed the project with success. In particular, we have achieved the objectives: 1. Construct a political economy model under uncertainty for environmental policy. 2. Provide an interdisciplinary approach of environmental policy. 3. Study the environmental policies that currently implemented in China, and design a “second- best but implementable” environmental policy. 4. Provide a new ranking –in terms of efficiency- of some usual environmental policy instruments. 5. Provide a general framework that can be used for practical environmental policy. The general theory could be applied to the specific case of Hong-Kong. We have successfully demonstrated objective 1 and 2 by constructing an economic model with political lobbying. We develop a model that will help us identify the best applicable option by appraising which policy maximizing the welfare of the local policymaker brings the economy to a situation that is the closest to the social optimum. The model will account for both the effect of interest groups and that of the relationships between local and national governments. Specifically, we allow for different level of government (federal and local) when the environmental policy is ultimately implemented at the local level, where many special interest groups can compete to lobby the decision maker. We continue to compare two environmental policy instruments taxes and tradable permits by introducing informational lobbying in a dynamic framework (objective 2 and 4). The contrast between the two instruments is as follows. Under a tax, everybody learns the quantity of abatement (and the polluter learns its cost). Under tradable permit, everybody learns the marginal cost. We also introduce natural catastrophe into our economic model (objective 1 and 2). In the paper draft “Environmental policy with natural catastrophe: A theoretical political economy framework”, we construct a political economy model to describe the determination of an environmental policy when the policy maker’s own objective interferes with the general interest. Specifically, we focus on the choice of the level of emission (abatement) when it both contributes to the economy and affects the severity of a risky natural catastrophe. We suppose that the policy maker is subject to an ex post performance pressure that does not appreciate the reduction of emission if no catastrophe has happened. As a result, it is likely that the socially optimal level of emission will not be reached, unless the benchmark for the policy maker’s performance evaluation is already set at the first best level. To achieve objective 3, we further study how the policy maker’s personal objective may affect the realization of a socially optimal environmental policy, especially when uncertainty associates with the ex post observable effectiveness of the policy. A policy maker may have multiple personal objectives, such as to gain the voters’ support or to reach a high score in a political tournament. The angel that we choose captures two features that may be especially relevant when a policy maker decides an environmental policy. The first feature is that a natural catastrophe is a risky event. We suppose that abatements reduce the severity of a catastrophe. In this case, the effect of abatements is hidden if catastrophe does not happen. The second feature corresponds to the observation that, although ex ante people understands the necessity of a preventive investment against a risky event, ex post they tend to downplay the investment when the risky event does not happen. For example, governmental agencies that have bought expensive catastrophe insurances complain about the insurance does not “pay off” to the end of a good year. On the other hand, a recently happened catastrophe may ease the political acceptability of abatement. The results are included in the manuscript “Pollution and bribery: a theoretical approach”. We also achieved objective 3 by constructing an empirical framework to estimate the government capacity in pollution mitigation and effectiveness of practical environmental policy. In the paper “The government capacity on industrial pollution management in Shanxi province: A response impulse analysis”, we employ Vector Auto-regression model with Generalized Response Impulse Function to analyse the dynamic nexus between economic growth and the industrial environmental pollution intensity for six specific pollutants in Shanxi province of China from 1995 to 2015. In our framework, we then compare three types of instruments (objective 4): the ones that are the most commonly used or debated for environmental policy, namely command and control (C&C thereafter), tax and tradable emission permits (TEPs thereafter). Even if the tax is decided at a local level, we assume that proceeds of the tax are collected by the federal government. Moreover, we assume that there is a free allocation of TEPs. As learned from the literature, economic instruments, i.e. tax and TEPs are cost efficient while C&C is not. Our objective is to derive the conditions and understand the mechanisms that make one of these instruments better, in the sense that it is closer to the optimum. All these form the first paper draft “Choosing the environmental instruments under decentralized policy and lobbying”. Finally, objective 5 has been achieved through the policy discussions in all the above-mentioned publications and manuscripts. Some of policy measures are implementable in Hong Kong. In addition, we explore the role of political connection on the overinvestment of Chinese energy firms. We argue that political connection can act as a “helping hand” that enables energy firms to obtain more government support to invest and a “grabbing hand” that forces politically connected energy firms to heavily overinvest for the promotion benefit of local politicians. Our analysis shows that overinvestment of an energy firm is positively affected by its political connection. In terms of the “helping hand” effects, we find that politically connected energy firms are more likely overinvest when they receive more government subsidy. In terms of the “grabbing hand” effects, we show that local politician is more likely to force energy firms to overinvest if the politician is approaching the 65-year-old promotion line. Although firms are less likely to overinvest during the economic downturn, local politician shapes the investment decision of energy firms through the “grabbing hand” effects.

11531716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11531716.value: We have constructed a model that accounts for features of the cities/regions that are determinant for the choice of the environmental policy. In addition, we considered the weight of the social welfare that of the city welfare and the one of the polluters lobby in the objective function of the city government. Finally, we accounted for the difficulty of environmental policy implementation at the local level through penalties the central government could impose to the city in case of large divergence between the socially optimal pollution level and the one exiting at the city level. In such a framework, a command and control policy would always be dominated by an ETS due to the cost inefficiencies generated by the command and control and the absence of any advantages relative to “lobby management” compared to the other instruments. A city/region with a large misalignment between local and central welfare should favour a tax, while a city with a low control of the central government over local implementation should favour permits (as it may even be impossible to set a tax accepted by the lobby). We further study the relationship between bribery and pollution. There may exist a particular level of pollution triggering a reduction in bribery. This level is not perfectly known ex-ante, leading only to a chance that bribery is reduced for higher levels of pollution. We construct a theoretical model to show the consequences of an uncertain pollution threshold on the lobbying effect. We find that policy makers face a trade-off: maintaining high levels of consumption and emissions enhances immediate benefits. But, at the same time, it increases the probability to reach the irreversibility threshold and to switch regime. Empirically, by analysing the dynamic nexus between economic growth and the industrial environmental pollution intensity, we find the Shanxi government shows significant capacity in the management of industrial solid waste and waste gas. Our results verify the existence of Environmental Kuznets Curve through dynamic interactions between industrial pollution intensity and economic growth impulse. By exploring the role of political connection on the overinvestment of Chinese energy firms, we find that political connection can act as a “helping hand” that enables energy firms to obtain more government support to invest and a “grabbing hand” that forces politically connected energy firms to heavily overinvest for the promotion benefit of local politicians.

11531716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11531716.value: As we have illustrated that when pollution really become a problem (like preventing people from working or kids to go to school), the politician may not be willing to accept pollution in exchange of bribery anymore. Therefore, it would be of interest to identify specifically the threshold level of pollution by using statistical data, and to estimate the related change to social welfare and economic development. Moreover, it will be more important to investigate the driving factors that determine the preferences of the politicians when making policy decisions. We highlight that there is a need to break the informal relationship between firms and local politicians. When promoting certain investment policies, the government can evaluate the long-term impacts of the policy in the presence of principal-bureaucratic agent problem. Strengthening the supervision on the government subsidy and various forms of supports to largely mitigate the rent-seeking incentives of energy firms and overinvestment is also important. Besides, the local government could also pay more attention to monitoring the performance appraisal of political connected CEOs, which can largely avoid the potential overinvestment issue caused by agency problem.

11531716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11531716.value: We study how to implement an environmental policy when there exists of lobbying, and take into account the difficulty of environmental policy implementation at the local level through potential penalties imposed by the central government. We find a city/region with a large misalignment between local and central welfare should favour a tax, while a city with a low control of the central government over local implementation should favour permits. We also study the consequences of an uncertain pollution threshold on the lobbying effect. We find that policy makers face a trade-off: maintaining high levels of consumption and emissions enhances immediate benefits. But, at the same time, it increases the probability to reach the irreversibility threshold and to switch regime. By using data, we find that provincial government shows significant capacity in the management of industrial solid waste and waste gas. By exploring the role of political connection on the overinvestment of Chinese energy firms, we find that political connection can act as a “helping hand” that enables energy firms to obtain more government support to invest and a “grabbing hand” that forces politically connected energy firms to heavily overinvest for the promotion benefit of local politicians.
