11532416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11532416.value: Joint chance constrained programs (CCPs) are a class of challenging optimization problems. In this project, we study solution methods for joint CCPs that rely on Monte Carlo simulation, and focus on the sample average approximation approach to joint CCPs. Motivated by the recent advances on sensitivity estimation of expectations with discontinuous integrands in the simulation society, we introduce simulation methods for estimating gradients of the joint chance constraints, including a kernel smoothing method, and a conditional Monte Carlo (CMC) method. The kernel smoothing method handles joint chance constraints by extending the existing result on a single discontinuity point to multiple discontinuity points. The CMC method is generalized from a change-of-variables viewpoint that leads to new gradient estimators for joint chance constraints. We propose to incorporate the gradient estimators into gradient-based optimization algorithms to solve joint CCPs, which is an underdeveloped research area to our best knowledge. We plan to study the theoretical foundations, algorithm design, and implementation issues of such gradient-based optimization algorithms. It is expected that the outcomes of this project may contribute to the simulation and optimization societies by adding efficient computational tools for solving joint CCPs. 聯合機會約束優化問題（joint chance constrained programs, JCCPs）是一類複雜並具挑戰性的優化問題。在這個項目中，我們研究基於隨機模擬和樣本平均逼近的JCCP的解決方法。受近幾年隨機模擬領域在非連續隨機變量的敏感度分析問題的突破所啓發，我們提出估計JCCP的梯度的隨機模擬方法，包括核估計方法以及條件蒙特卡洛（conditional Monte Carlo, CMC）方法。核估計方法通過擴展現有的對於單點非連續函數敏感度分析至多點非連續函數，從而有效用於JCCP的梯度估計。CMC方法是最近提出的變量替換方法的延伸，最終得到JCCP梯度的新估計手段。 我們建議把以上的梯度估計方法嵌入現有的梯度優化方法中去解決JCCP。我們將研究這種方法的理論支撐，算法設計，以及實際應用。我們期望本項目的研究成果將為隨機模擬和優化領域解決JCCP提供新的計算方法。

11532416.label: Realisation of objectives
11532416.value: Overall, the project objectives have been successfully realized. The details are summarized as follows. We have established a systematic way on developing kernel smoothing gradient estimators for joint CCPs. The key idea is based on a conditional expectation representation of the joint chance constraint, which is an extension of the sequence of work of the PI on kernel smoothing methods. The challenge due to the existence of multiple chance constraints is circumvented by applying a generalized chain rule on differentiation of the product of multiple indicator functions. Numerical experiments have been conducted for solving joint CCPs using gradient-based algorithms with the kernel smoothing gradient estimators, showing that the kernel smoothing estimators turn out to be promising. However, we observe that the quality of the solution depends on the bandwidth selection. With the typical rule of thumb method for selection bandwidth in statistics literature, it is observed that the numerical results are good in most of cases. Overall we observe that although kernel smoothing suffers from the well-known curse of dimensionality, its use in solving joint CCPs may lead to good solutions, mainly because the gradient of the joint chance constraint can be estimated by kernel smoothing approach with low dimensions. Compared to the investigation on the kernel smoothing estimator, we have developed theoretical support for the CMC gradient estimator, which has been the focus of our major effort. Part of our effort has been put on refinement of the theory for CMC estimators for conditional expectations in a general context. In this part, the focus is concentrated on the use of geometric measure theory to prove CMC representations for conditional expectations and sufficient conditions under which this result holds, especially in the context of CCPs. It turns out the CMC gradient estimator is not directly applicable to the joint CCPs, mainly because the existence of joint chance constraints violates the conditions for applying CMC. We have resolved this issue by looking into the structure of joint linear CCPs, which find a wide range of applications in practice. The current framework for joint linear CCPs is to decompose the gradient of the joint chance constraint into a sequence of components and then estimate each component using the CMC approach. This idea leads to multiple versions of gradient estimators for the joint chance constraint. The CMC gradient estimator has been incorporated into joint linear CCPs, and numerical experiments show that it work well in general. We have also observed that when the probability constraints are rare events, directly applying the CMC gradient estimator may not perform well, especially when the probability level of the joint chance constraint is closed to 1. In this setting, we look into the structure of the constraints and conduct transformations, which lead to equivalent formulation of the original joint linear CCPs and suitable for applying the CMC gradient estimator.

11532416.label: Major findings and research outcome
11532416.value: The major contribution of this project is to investigate the use of kernel smoothing and CMC gradient estimators for joint chance constrained problems (CCPs). When applying kernel smoothing, the chance constraints are allowed to be nonlinear. An important observation is that the traditional curse of dimensionality is not a problem for CCPs, mainly because estimation of the gradient can be decomposed into the estimation of conditional expectations that is equivalent to applying kernel smoothing to a one-dimensional problem. The kernel smoothing gradient estimator can thus accommodate more general constraints. However, the downside is that performance of kernel smoothing may depend on the selection of bandwidth parameters, which is problem dependent. While the typical rule of thumb for selection bandwidth may lead to reasonably good estimates, it might not perform very well in extreme cases. When applying the CMC gradient estimator, we consider an important class of CCPs where the joint chance constraints are linear. Under this setting, we develop efficient CMC gradient estimators that can be easily incorporated into gradient-based solution method for joint CCPs. We study in detail various settings, including the rare-event setting when the probability level of the joint chance constraint is close to 1, and propose various transformations that lead to a robust application of the CMC gradient estimator. Research outcomes have been summarized in two papers. Refinement results on CMC gradient estimator have been incorporated as part of the results in the paper titled "Conditional Monte Carlo: A Change-of-Variables Approach". The results on developing CMC gradient-based solution methods for joint CCPs have been summarized in a working paper titled "Probability based decision making via Monte Carlo", which shall be submitted soon.

11532416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11532416.value: So far the the development of CMC gradient estimator only works for joint linear CCPs. When there are nonlinear chance constraints, the derivation of analytical expression of the chance constraints is still a challenging topic. We plan to look into this issue and study potential solution methods for such cases.

11532416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11532416.value: We have studied the joint chance constrained problem (CCPs) from a gradient perspective. In particular, we study two different methods for estimating the gradients of the joint CCPs, including the kernel smoothing method and the conditional Monte Carlo (CMC) method. Performances of both methods in this context have been carefully examined, from both theoretical and practical standpoints. It is found that the kernel smoothing method may lead to good solutions for joint CCPs in most setting, and its application domain is broader compared to the CMC method. However, when applying to joint linear CCPs, the CMC method may perform much better if combined with transformation technique that serves as performance enhancement techniques when the probability constraints are rare events.

11534016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11534016.value: The emergence of Internet-based business-to-business (B2B) platforms substantially facilitates the firms’ supplier selection process. Online rating is an extensive practice on online platform to facilitate decisions on online transactions. However, little is known about the manner in which firms can strategically utilize online firm rating for supplier selection in the B2B setting. First, prior literature is primarily conducted in the business-to-consumer or consumer-to-consumer context, which does not fully manifest complex B2B decision making. Second, rating is often conceptualized as overall rating valence (i.e., an average value of a seller’s/product’s rating scores over time). The commercial consequences of online rating based on this conceptualization are somewhat inconclusive. Evidence implies that the rating is a more encompassing indicator. In this proposal, we aim to scrutinize the impact of firm rating on online B2B transactions through three steps. First, we identify two challenges that are salient in this context, namely, adverse selection in the online market (platform challenge), and reputation–bargaining power dilemma (B2B context challenge). Second, we explore how multiple firm rating-related cues (i.e., temporal horizon, rating valence, and rating consensus) can help address these two challenges for supplier selection on an online B2B platform. Third, we propose a plan to collect interview, survey and archival data to test the hypotheses. In this manner, this project will add to the accumulative research on online rating and supplier selection by advocating the multifaceted nature of firm rating and examining how it aids in supplier selection on online B2B platform. An in-depth understanding of the effectiveness of online rating can also provide firms with a set of best practices for detecting “lemons” and negotiating with good suppliers on an online B2B platform. B2B platform operators and policy makers can also obtain a useful understanding of the challenges confronted by firms and subsequently provide enhanced support. 基於互聯網的企業對企業（B2B）平台的出現，大大方便了企業對供應商的選擇。在線平台上廣泛的采用在線評級以方便买家網上交易的決定。然而，鮮為人知的是，企業怎样可以戰略性地利用公司在B2B平台上的在線評級来選擇合适的供應商。首先，以前的文献主要從企業對消費者或消費者對消費者的情景出发，並沒有充分體現複雜的B2B決策。其次，評級往往被概念化為總評價（即賣方/產品的評級分數在所有時間的平均值）。此种在線等級的算法所导致的商業後果是有些不確定的。有證據表明評級应该是一個更具包容性的指標。在本项目中，我們的目標是通過三個步驟來審視公司在線評級對于網上B2B交易的影響。首先，我們提出了兩個在此情景下的重要挑戰，即在網上市場逆向選擇（平台挑戰），和信譽-議價能力的困境（B2B方面的挑戰）。其次，我們将探索利用公司評級的多重線索（即时间，評價和評級共識）来幫助解決在線B2B平台上供應商選擇的這兩個挑戰。第三，我們提出了一個以訪談，問捲和歸檔數據來檢驗假設的計劃。該項目倡導公司等級的多面性，並研究它如何有助於網上B2B平台對供應商的選擇，因此對網上的評價和選擇供應商的研究做出贡献。對于網上評價的有效性的深入了解還可以用於檢測“檸檬”效应，並可以帮助在線B2B平台上的供應商进行談判。B2B平台運營商和政策制定者也能因此對企業面臨的挑戰有一個深刻的理解，並隨後提供相應的支持。

11534016.label: Realisation of objectives
11534016.value: The project objectives have been largely achieved. Objective 1. To understand the unique challenges of transactions (i.e., supplier selection) in the online B2B market. During the project, the project team has conducted comprehensive review of the relevant literature to identify the unique characteristics of online B2B market. Compared with B2C buyers, B2B buyers deliberate more extensively by assessing sellers’ quality from multiple perspectives and engaging in negotiation to bargain for acceptable deals. The electronic B2B marketplace changes the manner in which B2B buyers identify sellers, going beyond the mere benefits produced by the digitalization of services. This marketplace enables visitors to widen their seller choice and be less constrained by the geographical proximity of sellers. An inherited drawback of the B2B transactions is the information asymmetry, which sellers can hide negative information about seller’ quality to buyers. Objective 2. To explore how multifaceted online firm rating can address the identified challenges. We have collected and analyzed the secondary data from the B2B platform. Based on signaling theory, we propose three rating-related signals to assess sellers’ quality, namely, (i) rating valence, (ii) rating horizon and (iii) rating consensus. Rating valence represents how the average consumers view the seller. Rating horizon is a contingent signal to reveal how temporally far an independent signal (e.g., rating valence) is computed. A seller who has been in the business for two years could have two rating valences: near-past rating valence (rating valance based on transacted buyers’ assessment in the last one week) and entire-past rating valence (rating valence computed based on transacted buyers’ assessment for the last two years). These two rating valence values (i.e., of different rating horizon) would signify slight differences in the meaning of seller quality (i.e., recent performance and all past performance). Rating consensus is an independent signal to show the spread of individual ratings provided by transacted buyers (e.g., number of rating with grading of 1, 2, 3 and so on). Objective 3. To validate the proposed relationships in objective 2 using a multi-method approach. In this project, we have conducted multiple methods including secondary data analysis, interviews, and survey to validate the proposed relationships in objective 2. The secondary data analysis involves 5,018 clothing sellers (online wholesalers) in a pivotal seller-congregated electronic B2B marketplace, with sales change rate as the commercial consequence. The interviews include 23 B2B buyers to gain further situational insights of B2B transaction process in the electronic marketplace. The interviews are meant to serve as additional informational insights to our observations based on the empirical data. The survey data including 152 firms to understanding the firm collaboration. Objective 4. To offer concrete recommendations to firm managers, B2B platform operators, and policy makers. This study provides useful suggestions for the electronic B2B marketplace operators to better facilitate the prospective buyers in selecting sellers. First, for those B2B marketplaces typically only displaying the entire-past rating valence, findings of this study provide further suggestion on having enhanced, targeted support to the B2B buyers. For example, along with displaying the aggregated number of rating, the distribution of seller rating can be incorporated into the platform to allow buyers to assess the rating consensus of prospective sellers. Besides, rating can be computed based on different temporal horizons to help online buyers make wise transaction decisions by providing them with informational support. Second, should the sellers have access to the findings of this research, there might be a possibility for them to learn and engage in certain opportunistic behavior. For instance, to the extent that low rating consensus could signal a room for negotiation to buyers, sellers might strategically and deliberately not fulfill some of their orders to achieve a lower rating consensus. This type of opportunistic behavior is beyond the research on identifying faked sellers and electronic B2B marketplace operators need to design responding policy to detect and alert buyers on the probable sellers with opportunistic behaviors. Third, marketplace operators could further improve decision support to the buyers by identifying sellers with whom buyers might be interested in shortlisting for subsequent deal negotiation. Specifically, operators could incorporate rating horizon and rating consensus in addition to the rating valence when making recommendations. For instance, the marketplace operators can recommend sellers with high near-past rating valence with lower rating consensus than those with higher rating consensus.

11534016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11534016.value: This project considers the intricacy of seller rating and its relationship with electronic B2B sales change rate as manifested by the rating valence, rating consensus, temporal horizon. The results show that rating valence does not have a significant relationship with the sales change rate. To this end, we also observed from our data that sellers tend to have high rating valence (e.g., ranging from 4.1 to 4.4), which also reported on Amazon.com and bn.com. This genuine informational problem demands that subsequent research works should not merely consider rating valence as the sole operationalization of rating. B2B visitors (and buyers in general) may find the incremental improvement on the relatively high rating valence as less substantial to warrant a buying decision. Hence, they are compelled to seek additional keystone information cues, such as focal rating consensus, to aid their judgment. The results also reveal that the impact of rating valence is contingent on the rating horizon and consensus. The positive relationship between near-past rating valence and sales change rate is significant when the entire-past rating valence is high. When the signal, in the form of rating valence, is sent over time (i.e., near-past and entire-past), the consistent information boosts B2B buyers’ confidence in the seller’s quality. Hence, more potential corporate buyers are likely to be attracted and converted into actual buyers. However, when the rating horizon is near-past, the relationship between the rating valence and sales change rate is positive when consensus is low, but such moderating effect is not observed in the entire-past. Recent online rating literature recognizes the commercial value of the spread of rating scores in the consumer market. However, our results suggest that the role of rating consensus is limited in the online B2B setting over different temporal horizon. In our theorization, we propose that a dilemma occurs to a corporate buyer on whether to select a highly rated seller or maintain high bargaining power and rating consensus could help resolve this dilemma. To gain further insights deduced from the results of the hypothesis testing and the process/considerations of conducting transactions in the electronic B2B marketplace, we conducted post-hoc interviews with clothing B2B buyers. 11534016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11534016.value: There are several directions to further development this stream of research. First, this study utilizes valuable archival data to test the hypotheses. Future research can complement this study by using surveys, field experiments or more in-depth interviews. Second, there could be alternatives to the conceptualization and operationalization of the key terms. For instance, there could be different ways to conceptualize near-past horizon such as defining near-past as being proportional the entire temporal horizon of past ratings. Moreover, given that we focus on a single B2B marketplace, the operationalization of rating consensus can differ from some of the other works. Future works can seek to reconcile these alternatives by conducting more empirical assessments. Third, we do not have sellers’ offline reputation data in our dataset, which could be an important factor to influence seller’ performance. While we use fixed effect model to alleviate this issue, future research can incorporate this factor when feasible.

11534016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11534016.value: With an interest in electronic business-to-business (B2B) dealings, this research project addresses the mixed findings on the commercial consequences of seller rating. Seller rating denotes buyers’ quality assessment of a seller and is often shown through rating valence, i.e., average rating information. This study proposes that studying B2B seller rating should consider beyond the conventional manifestation of rating valence to include, for example, rating consensus (spread of rating information), and that rating information can be contingently time-based (near-past vs. entire-past). The findings through a multi-method approach support our argument by suggesting that simply considering the rating valence is inconclusive in determining B2B sales change rate, but taking into account the consistency of rating valence delivered in the near-past and entire-past does. Interestingly, the complementary role of rating consensus on rating valence works in the near-past but not in the entire-past. This research thus cautions the oversimplification of rating valence as the connotation of seller rating and demonstrates the intricacy of seller rating, which encompasses the interplay between multiple independent and contingent rating signals. The salient values of rating horizon and consensus offer insights to further improve the online rating system.

11601016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11601016.value: Cross-border migrants from mainland China to Hong Kong accounted for more than one-third of the city's total population in the past 50 years. While the majority was authorized mainlanders via the one-way quota system for family reunion, unauthorized immigrants escaping from wars, famine, and social turmoil formed a significant portion of the immigration population before the 1980s. Although there is a large body of literature focusing on Chinese immigrants’ adaptation in Hong Kong, few researchers have paid attention to the well-being of unauthorized migrants, most of whom are well into old age now, and even fewer to a comparison between unauthorized and authorized migrants. A comparison between the two subgroups will address the issue of migration selectivity, as the unauthorized migrants were assumed to be positively selected with the ability to successfully move across the border while the authorized migrants were assumed to be negatively selected with most being Hong Kong residents’ spouses and qualified children under age 14. The influx of migrant children, especially via the one-way quota system, caused public concerns about over-occupancy of educational resources and burdens to government welfare expenditure. Little research, however, has been done with population-based survey data to examine the impact of age at arrival for Chinese immigrants in Hong Kong, although the importance of age at arrival is widely acknowledged in migration literature. This project aims to fill in the gaps by examining the well-being (i.e., employment, occupation, earnings, health, and subjective well-being) of cross-border immigrants in Hong Kong, focusing on the impacts of mode and timing of immigration (i.e.,unauthorized/authorized, and arriving at 14-/15+). While previous researchers mainly examine post-immigration adaptation by comparing migrants with their counterparts in the destination country, the distinct feature of this project is its origin-destination approach to compare Chinese immigrants to both native Hong Kong residents and stayers in the mainland, using comparable data from the Hong Kong Panel Study of Social Dynamics (HKPSSD) and the China Family Panel Study (CFPS). HKPSSD include 4,109 Hong Kong natives and 2,843 immigrants from mainland. Among the immigrants 550 were unauthorized smugglers and 727 arrived at age under 14. Information on immigrants’ origin place in HKPSSD will be used to match their origin counterparts in CFPS (Guangdong sample) for origin-destination comparison. Both data sets include comparable measures on well-being. The study will also investigate the short-term and long-term effects of cross-border migration using Hong Kong censuses and China censuses data since 1990. 在過去五十年里，來自中國大陸的跨境移民構成了香港人口的三分之一。其中大多數是通過單程證抵港以實現家庭團聚的合法移民，而在1980年代之前，還有一個重要的移民群體：因戰爭、饑荒和社會動蕩而逃到香港的非法移民。 雖然有為數眾多的文獻關注大陸移民在港的適應狀況，卻很少有研究者關注現已大多步入老齡的非法移民的情況，將他們與合法移民做對比的研究則更少。由於非法移民有能力成功跨越邊界，一般被認為是正向選擇的移民；而合法移民則由於大多數是香港居民的妻子和14歲以下的孩子，一般被認為是負向選擇的移民。故此，這兩個群體之間的對比將有助於探討移民的選擇性問題。 移民孩子的湧入，尤其是通過單程證而來港的，引起了公眾的關注，擔憂他們會過度佔用教育資源以及成為政府福利開支的負擔。但目前為止，很少有研究基於代表性調查數據分析抵港年齡對大陸移民的社會融入的影響，雖然在移民研究的文獻中，遷移年齡的重要性已經得到廣泛的關注。 這項研究旨在通過檢驗來港跨境移民的康福狀態（包括就業、職業、收入、健康、和主觀幸福感）來填補以往研究的不足，并重點關注抵港年齡的影響以及非法移民與合法移民的比較。與以往關於移民融入的研究相比，這項研究的獨特之處在於結合了遷入地和遷出地的數據，即香港社會動態追蹤調查(the Hong Kong Panel Study of Social Dynamics , HKPSSD)和中國家庭追蹤調查(the China Family Panel Study , CFPS)，同時比較大陸移民、香港本地人、以及留在大陸的人。 HKPSSD訪問了4,109位香港本地人以及2,843位來自大陸的移民。在這2,843位移民當中，550位是非法移民，727位抵港時年齡小於14歲。這項研究將會用HKPSSD中包含的移民來源地信息將抵港移民與CFPS廣東樣本中的留在廣東的人進行比較。HKPSSD和CFPS包含相似的變量。此外，這項研究將運用自1990年以來的香港普查和中國普查數據，分析跨境遷移的短期和長期影響。

11601016.label: Realisation of objectives
11601016.value: The project objectives have been achieved. In total, we have published two papers out of this project, and we have two manuscripts under reivew now, and we have also completed a working paper to be refined and submitted to a peer-review journal. Corresponding to the project objectives, our summary is listed as below. 1. we adopted an origin-destination approach to simultaneously comparing (a) cross-border immigrants to (b) stayers in the mainland and (c) natives in Hong Kong, using data from two comparable representative surveys in the mainland and Hong Kong, namely the China Family Panel Study and the Hong Kong Panel Studies of Social Dynamics. 2. We used this origin-destination approach to study labor market outcomes, BMI, and self-rated health of immigrants in Hong Kong and Guangdong stayers in mainland China. And we published two papers using this origin-destination approach, one in Chinese Sociologicl Review and the other in Biodemography and Social Biology. 3. We further differentiated immigrant children (also referred to as 1.5-generation immigrants who arrived at age 14 or below) from adult Chinese immigrants (also referred to as first-generation immigrants who arrived at age above 15) in Hong Kong, and further compare them to their origin and destination counterparts to examine the effect of timing of immigration on labor market outcomes. 4. We further differentiated between unauthorized immigrants (who have successfully overcome the difficulties of illegally crossing the border) and authorized immigrants (most of whom immigrated under the family-reunion immigrant policy) to examine the impact of mode of immigration and to address the issue of positive/negative selectivity. 5. We also investigated the effects of cross-border migration on employment and occupation, and we found that mode of migration and age at arrival both play a significant role in labor market outcomes. Please refer to Zhang and Ye 2018. We are working on a topic comparing immigrants of different cohorts (who arrived in Hong Kong during a certain period) using data from the China censuses and Hong Kong censuses conducted since the 1990s, and the preliminary results are presented at a online meeting with colleagues from Shanghai University. 6. We extend our project to further study other outcomes such as political stance and identity by comparing migrants with different mode of migration and age of arrival to Hong Kong natives. The manuscript is now under review in Chinese Sociological Review. 7. We extend our project to further study whether and to what extent, place of birth as well as socio-economic status determine Hong Kong people's political values, attitudes toward mainlanders, and etc. The manuscript is now under review in the China Quarterly. 8. We extend our project to further examine the role of place of education in creating earnings disparities between Chinese immigrants and natives in Hong Kong. The manuscript has been completed and yet to be submitted to academic journal.

11601016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11601016.value: 1. Chinese immigrants have significantly lower ISEI than their counterparts in both the origin and the destination, suggesting that they moved out but not up. Please refer to Zhang and Ye 2018. 2. Documented immigrants have significantly lower ISEI than both GD stayers and HK natives, but no significant difference is found for undocumented immigrants. ISEI is lower for the immigrants who arrived at age 13 or older compared to either GD stayers or HK natives, whereas for those who arrived at younger ages the differences are positive and insignificant. 3. Further analyses with combined information on mode of migration and age at arrival show that among documented immigrants there is a disadvantage for those who arrived at age 13 or older, but not for those who arrived younger than 13. 4. Using the origin-destination approach, we also examined the health outcomes of immigrants, Hong Kong natives, and Guangdong stayers who experienced the China famine. We found that the stayers who experienced the famine have a lower BMI than the emigrants, and they are likely to have a poor SRH. Please refer to Zhang, Song and Wu 2017. 5. The earnings disadvantage of Chinese immigrants can be attributed to the lower value of education attained from mainland China. Chinese immigrants who attained highest education in Hong Kong do not differ from the natives in earnings whereas those who attained highest education in the mainland earn significantly less than both the natives and the Hong-Kong-educated immigrants. Please refer to Ye zhang Zhang (under preparation). 6. When we compared adult undocumented immigrants, adult documented immigrants, child documented immigrants, and Hong Kong natives, to investigate the effects of refugee experience, political socialization, and place of birth, we found that negative effects of refugee experience on support for pro-Beijing parties and Chinese identity, and a positive effect of political socialization in the mainland on support for pro-Beijing parties. Compared with adult documented immigrants, adult undocumented immigrants show significantly lower support for pro-Beijing parties, and their Chinese identity is weaker. Please refer to Zhang and Zhang (under reivew).

11601016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11601016.value: We are now working on several papers that are developed from this project. The innovation origin-destination comparative approach inpires the reserach team to explore the comparable data from the China Family Panel Study and the Hong Kong Panel Studies of Social Dynamics to study a couple of other topics such as intragenerational mobility of migrants in labor market and intergenerational mobility of migrants, stayers, and Hong Kong natives. This comparative approach is also likely to motivate future studies on other immigrant societies such as Singapore and Taiwai.

11601016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11601016.value: In this project, we used an innovative origin-destination approach to study migration and its consequences, with comparable survey data from the China Family Panel Study and the Hong Kong Panel Studies of Social Dynamics. We found that Chinese immigrants have significantly lower occupational attainment, measured by International Socioeconomic Index (ISEI), than their counterparts in both the origin (Guangdong) and the destination (Hong Kong). Disadvantages exist for documented immigrants and those who arrived in Hong Kong at age 13 or older, whereas undocumented immigrants and those who arrived younger than 13 do not differ significantly from either Guangdong stayers or Hong Kong natives. The origin–destination comparisons in this paper suggest that mode of migration and age at arrival should be simultaneously considered to examine the internal variations of Chinese immigrants. In response to public worries about child immigrants’ over-occupancy of public resources and burden on Hong Kong government welfare expenditure, the empirical results of this project suggest an optimistic prediction of child immigrants’ socioeconomic achievement: the younger the age at arrival, the better the integration of Chinese immigrants in the local labor market, even under the family-reunion one-way permit scheme.

11607916.label: Project Objectives

考察文白異讀構詞個體差異的成因及其背後隱含的語言規律；

11607916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11607916.value: Wénbái yìdú is the phenomenon where a single Chinese character contains two or more readings: a ‘colloquial reading’ commonly used in vernacular speech and a ‘literary reading’ commonly used in literary or formal registers. Many studies have so far been conducted on wénbái yìdú from phonological and lexical perspectives. This project, however, argues that an innovative morphological perspective on wénbái yìdú will offer great insights into word formation and morphological stratification, and open a new and important avenue for examining the historical development in Chinese dialects. We will collect samples of wénbái yìdú in Southern Mǐn through fieldwork in Xiàmén and Shàntóu. Southern Mǐn is chosen because the dialect offers a rich dataset for examining morphological stratification. There is an estimated 1,500 characters with wénbái yìdú. For example, 老 ‘old’ in Southern Mǐn has a colloquial reading lau7, a semi-literary reading lau2, and a literary reading lo2. Socio-linguistic methods will be employed to elicit data from 120 native speakers (60 from each location). The analysis will focus on synchronic variations in compound word formation between the two Southern Mǐn varieties with the aim of discovering any irregularities in morphological stratification across the dialect group, which will bring new perspectives on language change. Finally, this project will also address the role of Chinese characters in morphological stratification.

11607916.label: Realisation of objectives
11607916.value: Objective 1: To account for the formation of synchronic variations of morphological strata from a sociolinguistic perspective and the rules underlying such features. 1a. Compilation of the word lists: In order to elicit data from Xiamen and Shantou effectively, two sets of word lists were compiled before the field trips. The lists have made reference to published materials such as The Grand Dictionary of the Southern Min Dialects edited by Changji Zhou (2006), covering more than 900 morphemes with baidu 白讀/wendu 文讀 distinction in either dialect. For each item I list out all readings of the morphemes and several possible compound words (including colloquial and literary) made up of the morphemes in question. 1b. Field trips: During the project period, we conducted two field trips to Xiamen and two to Shantou, with a total of 59 subjects interviewed. The first two trips, which can be understood as pilot surveys, were made in December 2017 (Shantou) and April 2018 (Xiamen) respectively. During the surveys we limited our interview to just two, but very reliable, informants. The informants were asked to read out the compound words in our lists, and the forms (baidu or wentu) they chose for the ‘target’ morpheme have been recorded. We also pay special attention to the compound words which have wen/bai variations, e.g. /hun1 tshiu3/ ~ /pun1 tshiu3/ 分手 ‘break up’ in Xiamen, where /hun1/ is the wendu form of 分 ‘to separate’, and /pun1/ the baidu form. On the basis of the results obtained in the pilot surveys, we have designed two sets of new word lists which have been utilized in the following investigations. The one used in the Shantou survey, for instance, contains around 80 compound words with at least one morphemes having wen/bai variation in our main informant’s speech. It is unfortunate that Mrs. Zhong, our main informant of the Shantou Southern Min who also helps us contact other subjects in Shantou, was seriously injured in a traffic accident in summer 2018. Given this situation, our third and fourth trips could only be held in February 2019 (Shantou) and August 2019 (Xiamen) respectively, slightly later than the dates originally proposed. These two trips are sociolinguistic surveys in essence. Among the 59 subjects, 30 were natives of Shantou and the others Xiamen. The informants were divided into three groups according to their ages: Group (i) 60 or above; Group (ii) 35-59; and Group (iii) 34 or below. Their genders and education levels are also taken into consideration. All the data have been digitized subsequently. 1c. Data analyses: Firstly, we have summarized the social factors affecting the subjects of using the baidu and wendu forms in literary compound formation in the two dialects. One of the most striking tendencies is that the younger the subject is, the higher the chance s/he picks the baidu form. For example, in Shantou, the morpheme 流 ‘to flow’ has two readings, with /lau2/ as the baidu form, and /liu2/ the wendu form. When forming the literary compound word 流失 ‘to run off; to wash away’, 20% of the Group (i) members (2/10) use /lau2/. This form, however, is used by 60% of the members of Group (iii). The same is also true for the compound words like 留意 ‘to note’, 放棄 ‘to give up’, 平面 ‘a flat surface’, etc, where wen/bai distinctions exist in the first morphemes. This tendency generally agrees with what Cheng (1997) observed in Taiwanese Southern Min. For the Xiamen data, we have also figured out some tendency in respect to the subjects’ ages and other social factors. Secondly, we compare the Shantou data against the Xiamen data. While the behaviors of the two dialects do share some common tendencies, they also show their own characteristics. We found that, for example, the wendu forms in the Xiamen dialect are much more active and versatile than those of the Shantou dialect, surviving in a number of compound words which have no direct correspondences in Shantou. Our findings on this issue will be submitted to the Bulletin of Chinese in early January 2021. Objective 2: To achieve a comprehensive and comparative study of the morphological strata of Xiàmén and Shàntóu Southern Mǐn 2a. Using Proto-Southern Min to identify the stratal affiliation of the morpheme in question: When talking about morphological strata, we have to decide the stratal affiliations of multiple readings of a given morpheme. While it is not a difficult task for most cases, the boundaries of wendu and baidu have become blurred to some extent after prolonged interactions between the two strata. In this connection, we proposed the Proto-Southern Min phonological system which provides a reliable and effective framework for stratifying multiple readings of a given morpheme in Southern Min. We are able to confirm the affiliations of a number of morphemes which were previously viewed as members of an incorrect stratum, e.g. the morpheme /tso4/ 坐 ‘to sit’ in Shantou Southern Min was formerly regarded as a wentu form by Zhong (2016). Our study (Kwok 2018), however, considers it to be a member of the baidu stratum. 2b. Identifying factors that decide the results of morphological stratification: Previous studies such as Wang (1986/2007) have identified the ‘stylist-register factor’ in the development of morphological stratification in Chinese dialects. In Southern Min, the situation is more complicated: the baidu forms can occur as a part of literary compound words; on the contrary, wendu morphemes can also make up colloquial compound words (Yang 1991). After studying a sizable number of Southern Min examples collected from the field, we came to the conclusion that there are at least two factors interacting with each other. On top of the ‘stylist-register factor’, one should also consider the ‘semantic factor’ which suggests that the baidu form of a given morpheme usually has a clear border of sememe, and may extend to the literary stratum at compound formation level. If these factors collide with each other, the morphemes in question, mostly in literary compound words, may demonstrate wen/bai variations. Objective 3: To examine the role of Chinese characters in the interactions among different morphological strata 3a. Interactions between the ‘semantic loan characters’ 訓讀字 and the morpheme represented by the original character: Unlike the wendu form and the baidu form of a given morpheme which are etymologically related, ‘semantic loan character’ and the morpheme represented by the character are related only semantically. Yet, in some cases, they behave very similarly to what we observe for the real wendu and baidu forms when forming compound words. We assume that most literary compound words in Southern Min were formed by educated speakers who converted the Standard Chinese forms into their own ones by putting together corresponding character readings. 3b. A preliminary comparison of morphological stratification among Southern Min, Cantonese and Sino-Japanese: It is found that these three languages have some common points regarding morphological stratification such as the division of labor in the wendu and baidu forms in compound formation of a given morpheme. The use of Chinese characters (or kanji in Japanese) is a key factor which led to the formation of those features. Overall speaking, the three objectives stated in the research proposal have been fully achieved.

11607916.label: Major findings and research outcome
11607916.value: Major findings of this project include the followings: (1) A full reconstruction of the Proto-Southern Min (the putative ancestral language of all modern Southern Min dialects) phonological system [Part C, 8, No.2-5; 9, No.1-4, 7]: This reconstruction has been taken as the main criterion for classifying the baidu and wendu forms in our target dialects. I also discusses several cases of morphological stratification in Southern Min in my monograph [Part C, 8, No.3]; (2) Identification of two major factors deciding the directions of morphological stratification in the two Southern Min varieties [Part C, 8, No.1, 5-6; 9, Nos. 8-10]: These two factors are (a) the semantic factor, which considers that the baidu form of a given morpheme usually has a clear border of sememe, and may extend to the literary stratum at compound formation (‘CF’) level, and (b) the stylistic-register factor, which stresses the strong tendency of picking the wendu form in the formation of literary compounds, especially those which have direct correspondences in Standard Chinese. When these two factors do not interact with each other, the baidu and wendu forms of a given morpheme will form a division of labor in CF both semantically and stylistically. The collision of these two factors, however, will lead to wen/bai variation at the CF level, e.g. in Xiamen, the morphemes 分, 林, 高 allow wen/bai variations in the compounds 分手 ‘break up’, 樹林 ‘forest’ and 高度 ‘height’ respectively. We found that almost all such cases are literary compounds where the two factors are in competition. (3) Investigation into morphological variation from a socio-linguistic perspective [Part C, 8, No.7]: Our preliminary study reveals that age and education level of informants are decisive in how they pick the baidu or wendu of a given morpheme in CF, e.g. in Shantou, the younger the informant is, the high the chance s/he chooses the baidu form in CF. (4) Clarification of the indispensable role of Chinese characters in the formation of morphological stratification [Part C, 8, No.1]: Firstly, the superposition of the wendu and baidu forms within a given morpheme is unlikely without the introduction of Chinese characters; secondly, educated speakers of a dialect can easily convert the Standard Chinese compounds into their own forms by just putting together corresponding character readings. For Southern Min speakers, the questions is how they make the choice between baidu and wendu for the same character in CF.

11607916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11607916.value: Potential development of this research is of twofold: (1) Comparison between Southern Min and other Chinese dialects in terms of morphological stratification: While morphological stratification has been widely attested across Chinese dialects (see, for example, Wang 1986/2007 for Wenxi Mandarin in Shanxi; Lau 2001 for Hong Kong Cantonese), there is a strong lack of cross-dialectal comparison. This lack has hampered us to look into the peculiarity of the Southern Min cases. Our preliminary observation is that the 'semantic factor' (see Section 6.1) plays an important role in the stratification of Southern Min, where the baidu forms can easily penetrate into the literary stratum at the CF level. In other dialects, however, the the 'semantic factor' seems to be less effective than what is observed in the Southern Min. (2) Application of the lexical diffusion theory into morphological stratification: The theory of lexical diffusion has been applied to cases of sound change (Cheng & Wang 1973; Wang & Lien 1993, etc.) and syntactic change (Yue-Hashimoto 1993, Zhang 2000, etc.) in Chinese dialects. The nature of our case studies seem to conform to what Wang & Lien (1993) called 'bi-directional diffusion'. These issues will be explored in our future studies.

11607916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11607916.value: This project aims at exploring the rules of compound formation regarding to wendu (literary form) and baidu (colloquial form) in two Southern Min (‘SM’) dialects, namely, Xiamen and Shantou. SM is known for its preservation of a sizable number of wen/bai distinction in character readings, whose role in compound formation remains unclear. The data utilized in this project were elicited directly from four field trips conducted between 2017 and 2019, with 59 subjects interviewed. After studying the data, we are able to conclude there are at least two factors affecting the choice of using the baidu form or wendu form in compound formation: (a) the semantic factor, and (b) the stylistic-register factor. It is possible to observe wen/bai variation in the morpheme in question when these two factors collide with each other, mostly in literary compounds shared with Standard Chinese. The sociolinguistic surveys reveal that ages and education backgrounds of the subjects may impact their behaviors in compound formation. On top of these findings, this project also sheds new light on the importance of Chinese characters in compound formation with regard to wen/bai distinction. In connection with this argument, our cases are taken to compared with Cantonese and Sino-Japanese.

11610016.value: 構建數據洩漏通知框架以加強企業及組織資料的保密措施

11610016.label: Co - Investigator(s)

11610016.label: Project Objectives
11610016.value: To conduct an empirical study on the data breach problem in Hong Kong; To investigate the effectiveness of Hong Kong’s existing reporting system and whether it could lead to the development of a new data breach reporting scheme; To conduct comparative and doctrinal analysis of the key elements and issues of different US and the EU data reporting models; To examine how and the extent to which different US and the EU reporting models could enhance Hong Kong’s legal and corporate environment by (a) evaluating whether data breaches should be reported (b) what type of data should be reported (c) how data breaches should be reported and (d) to whom the breaches should be reported to; and To design an appropriate data breach reporting framework for Hong Kong.

To investigate the effectiveness of Hong Kong’s existing reporting system and whether it could lead to the development of a new data breach reporting scheme;
To conduct comparative and doctrinal analysis of the key elements and issues of different US and the EU data reporting models;

To examine how and the extent to which different US and the EU reporting models could enhance Hong Kong’s legal and corporate environment by (a) evaluating whether data breaches should be reported (b) what type of data should be reported (c) how data breaches should be reported and (d) to whom the breaches should be reported to; and

11610016.label: Realisation of objectives
11610016.value: Save for objective 1 where only approximately 88% of the objectives were achieved, the project had achieved its objectives. The investigators would have preferred to have a greater sample of participants for the semi-structured interviewed that was conducted to record the views of stakeholders about their understanding and perception of the data breach problem in Hong Kong and data breach notification. Due to the social conditions existing during the period, many participants who had previously agreed to participate were reluctant to do so. Given the situation, the research team had requested an extension of time for the project to complete in order to secure more participants. Eventually, twenty-four participants from the private industry (four from global companies, two regional and the remaining local companies) from the commercial, banking, insurance, legal and medical were recruited. Numerous attempts were made to solicit the participation from the public sector including but not limited to the Immigration Department, the OGCIO, the HK Police Force, the Inland Revenue - the invitations were declined. Invitations were also extended to four civil society organizations with only one organization accepting the invitation. Notwithstanding, the interview with participants were conducted smoothly, the findings of which were published in an internationally refereed journal, Computer Law & Security Review Vol. 42 September 2021. The journal is an A ranked journal. The paper is entitled, "Hong Kong's data breach notification scheme: From the stakeholders' perspectives".

11610016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11610016.value: The findings of the study showed the flaws and weaknesses inherent in the existing legal framework for data breaches. These can be narrowed down to two - (1) the current voluntary mechanism of breach notification which left the decision to report a data breach incident to the discretion of the breached organization and (2) the Privacy Commissioner Office (PCO) 's weak enforcement powers. The recommendation is for a mandatory as opposed to a voluntary approach be adopted to advance the objectives of deterrence, mitigation, transparency through information and public confidence. This may be achieved through purposely drafted laws and to ensure that such laws are properly enforced. A two-pronged approach is suggested to strike a balance between individuals' right to be notified of the data breach and maintaining support of a business-oriented environment. The first prong requires the PCO and the Hong Kong Police to be notified promptly and in any event no later than 72 hours when an unlawful loss, destruction and/or unauthorized access to, or disclosure of personal data has been detected. The second prong entails notifying individuals when ‘there is a likelihood that the breach will lead to a mis-use of the leaked personal data resulting in significant harm’. Given the lower trigger threshold in the first prong, the first prong's role is to provide an early warning allowing relevant authorities (specifically the PCO) to assess the effectiveness of the breached organization’s response plan and remedial measures. The second prong provides a higher notification trigger so that consumers are not unnecessarily notified. Under the mandatory mechanism, Breached organizations must submit an investigation report into the breach incident and the measures undertaken to rectify any harm that resulted from the breach to the PCO. This is regardless of whether affected consumers are notified. The PCO reserves the power to further investigate the breach incident and to recommend additional and further measures such as imposing fines where it deems appropriate. The PCO should also be empowered to override the breached organization’s decision not to notify affected consumers. Given that the PCO will be the entity to be mandatorily notified of all data breaches in HK, their role should be strengthened, their resources increased and the enforcement powers (including investigative and prosecution powers) increased.

11610016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11610016.value: Unlike Australia nd the US, Hong Kong does not have separate ‘specialized’ regulations for healthcare facilities in relation to health consumers’ personal health information. There is a need to consider whether medical health information should be classified as sensitive data requiring additional safeguards and whether a lower threshold for notification be required in event of a data leak of health information. A grant has been awarded which in part will study the above issue.

11610016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11610016.value: The research examines with data breach notification mechanisms, its usefulness and whether Hong Kong should retain its voluntary data breach notification mechanism. Given the increasing number of compromised data security incidents globally, it has become increasing important for governments to considered whether it should be mandated that an organization that has suffered a data breach involving personal identifiable information notify affected individuals and regulators. The purpose behind such laws is to ensure individuals are appropriately informed when their personal identifiable information has been compromised. This enables affected individuals (victims of data breaches) to mitigate any harm arising from the data breach. The research is significant because it advocates for Hong Kong to maintain its rightful place across international norms, as a modern, legally and commercially trustworthy and reliable jurisdiction, and at the same time continues to assure its citizens that the confidentiality of their personal identifiable information is secure, a mandatory approach to data breach notification needs to be implemented.

11611516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11611516.value: Public management research draws on the full methodological repertoire of the social sciences in the search for valid and reliable evidence. In the pursuit of ‘realistic evidence’ there has been a recent turn towards the use of experimental methods (Margetts 2011). This project will build upon this shift to examine the validity of social scientific knowledge by replicating and extending experimental studies on key questions of organizational design. The growth in public management studies employing experimental methods has not been matched by replication studies: to date none have been published. While challenges exist in publishing replications, there are growing examples in the social sciences (e.g. Nosek and Lakens 2014). Replications are not identical copies, rather they seek to test the theories employed in prior studies. In this project replications will be ‘empirical generalizations’ and ‘generalization and extension’ (Tsang and Kwan 1999): * Empirical generalizations draw on the same designs but uses different populations and settings. This leads to the proposition that the different context for the replications—Hong Kong as again Europe/USA—will result in findings in the same direction but with weaker results. It is theorized that this will arise from the more collective culture and Confucianism in Hong Kong. * Generalization and extension will see two extensions undertaken. The first addresses concerns in the discipline about practical relevance of findings on studies using students, thus experiments will be extended to include managers. Second, the impact of incentives on intrinsic and extrinsic motivation will be examined. The majority of experimental studies in public management have examined organizational design. We take this cue to inform the selection of the five replications that will be conducted in this study and examine performance management (Weibel et al. 2010), work motivation (Brewer and Brewer 2011), decision-making (Nutt 2005), and rules and red tape (Kaufman and Feeney 2014; Scott and Pandey 2000). The study, therefore, seeks to contribute towards better organizational designs that produce improved outcomes for public agencies by better understanding the generalizability public management knowledge. The project will be hosted in the Laboratory for Public Management and Policy, which provides the resources and facilities to undertake survey, vignettes, simulations and computer-based lab experiments. The study team, in keeping with best practice on replication and extensions, draws authors as Co-Is from the original studies giving access to research materials, commentary on research design and interpretation of results. 公共管理研究依賴有效及可靠的社會科學證據。為了實現 「逼真證據 (realistic evidence)」，公共行政研究的實驗方法開始有了改變(Margetts 2011)。這個項目會根據以上的趨勢，運用以上的方法來應用於組織架構設計，以便驗證以上實驗方法對社會科學知識是否有效。 越來越多公共管理研究的實驗方法並未曾滿足 「複製研究(replication studies) 」，故此至今未曾發表。雖然發表複製正的研究存在困難，但在社會科學中的案例也不斷增加(e.g. Nosek and Lakens 2014)。「複製(replication)」一詞在社會科學中並不等同完全相同的副本，而是套用並測試先前研究的理論。在這個項目中「複製」代表經驗性歸納化(Empirical generalizations」及「歸納化及延展(Generalization and extension」 (Tsang and Kwan 1999)。 「經驗性歸納化(Empirical generalizations」使用相同設計但應用在不同人口及變數。通常在不同的文化或環境複製, 舉例如下, 在香港進行研究並在歐美國家對照下會發現結果方向相同但得出較弱對比的結果。這是因為香港有比較較集中的文化及傳統儒家思想。 「歸納化及延展(Generalization and extension」將進行兩個階段。第一個階段解釋在不同使用學生所進行的研究當中不出結果的關聯性, 因此實驗張延展道包括經理 。第二個階段試探究愛在給內在動機的影響力。 大部分的公共管理研究已探究組織架構設計。我們運用這個事實，在本研究選擇進行五個「複製 」，以便調查其效能管理(Weibel et al. 2010)、工作動機(Brewer and Brewer 2011)、決策(Nutt 2005)以及規則及繁文縟節(Kaufman and Feeney 2014; Scott and Pandey 2000)。因此這個研究希望貢獻更好的組織架構設計讓公共代理更全面明白公共行政管理的通則性。 這個項目將在公共行政及管理實驗室進行, 實驗室將提供資源及設施以便進行問卷、模擬、花絮及電腦系統實驗。研究團隊將以最佳的方法來複製及延展，參考過的物料及設計將會以共同作者方式列入編者。

11611516.label: Realisation of objectives
11611516.value: The project has contributed to theoretical debates about replication in public management research and undertaken the first largescale set of replications in the field (objectives 1 and 3), including publication of 8 replications in a special issue of Public Management Review co-edited by the project PI. The primary contribution was to develop best practice recommendations for replicating experiments in public management. This project has shown that replication is a critical tool in the interdisciplinary field of public administration to test and retest theory and empirical evidence in different contexts to establish generalization, and thereby develop mid-range theories. This is significant in public administration because much theory, and indeed evidence, is derived from the West. In developing best practice recommendation for replicating experimental studies the project has offered a clear definition of replication types and provided a step-by-step guide to the conduct of replication. Conceptual and methodological questions have been raised, and a road map to navigate these has been suggested. Methodologically the findings of the project have challenged scholars to understand and improve experimental research designs. Conceptually, we have drawn attention to questions about the critical test case and questions of boundary conditions to develop contextualized hypotheses. Attention has also been brought to the presentation of findings, highlighting that replication findings that differ from the original study do not mean failure as has been the case in say social psychology, particularly when boundary conditions have been clearly articulated. The validity of the replication framework is demonstrated with further funding on this topic from the National Science Foundation China, Research Grants Council (GRF) and the Public Policy Research Fund (see 6.2). A number of challenges were faced in implementing the replications (objective 2). Building a panel of subjects proved troublesome. A subject panel called My Citizens Panel was launched, initially built from CityU students and alumni. Extensive advertising (social media, Google ads etc.) did not result in high levels of subject sign-up. Engaging with public managers was particularly difficult, which affected the ability to extend the replications to public managers. Thus, alternatives were pursued (discussed below). Future research building on the experiences of this GRF uses samples from survey companies such as Dynata and YouGov (see 6.2) to overcome these problems. Given the above, the replications (described below) varied in their success. They did, however, offer valuable experience to build sound knowledge and methodological insights into the conduct of replications in organizational design. Knowledge developed from the project directly contributed to the best practice replication framework and underscored the importance of replication as a method to develop mid-range theory in public administration. Findings also under public-private differences in intrinsic and extrinsic motivation. Brewer and Brewer (2011). Given the challenges in building a subject panel it was not possible identify public servants for this replication. Furthermore, the lab was located off the campus at the time of the replication and not easily accessible by public transport. The replication was conducted on undergraduate students and assessed intrinsic and extrinsic motivation. The study examined whether work effort differs between public and private settings, and by testing the ways that sector-specific incentives can address such differences. A psychomotor vigilance task that examined multi-dimensional performance (speed and accuracy) in a laboratory experiment was developed. The subjects were recruited into public and private settings on the basis of the majors they have chosen to study, and the types of compensation they receive. Using a two-by-two factorial design of the monetary-motivated (private) and the non-monetary-motivated (public) settings, with and without incentives, findings indicated that public and private settings differ in performance and response to incentives. The replication provides substantial new evidence on the lesser effectiveness of incentives in public sector settings, which underscores the relevance of research on public sector values and on motivation. Methodologically, the study showed how the choices that experimental subjects make can be exploited for modeling sectoral differences in a more naturalistic way than with a short-term prime, while preserving the advantages of a controlled laboratory experiment. This replication provided important insights into methods to extend an original study. Status: R&R at International Public Management Journal. Kaufman and Feeney (2014). The replication conducted with students discussed how boundary conditions and construct validity lead to different understanding of red tape from the original study. We drew attention to the Hong Kong context and how translation of the term red tape into Chinese could lead to subject’s different interpretation. As anticipated, the findings in the Hong Kong context are weaker than the original study (null findings) as there is a higher toleration of red tape. We sought to recruit public servants as subject and used administrators at City University of Hong Kong as subjects. The response rate was disappointing and results did not offer sufficient statistical power to merit analysis. Status: CUP book chapter. Nutt (2006). As previously reported, it was not feasible replicate this study because we could not access all the original materials. A new many labs replication of Hvidman and Andersen (2015) study of public-private differences on characteristics of organizational design was developed as an alternative. Nine replications were implemented in Asia and the West. Data were successfully collected from around 8,000 citizen subjects. However, it was not possible to establish construct validity: equivalence analysis indicated that the findings were not equivalent and were not suitable for publication. This study provided important insights into measurement equivalence and boundary conditions for the replication framework. Scott and Pandey (2000). The original study was a laboratory experiment which simulated the effect of red tape on the level of social welfare offered to clients. The Hong Kong context required extensive revision to the treatment materials which raised important questions about the feasibility of conducting the replication. A higher level of administrative burden in Hong Kong suggested that the findings would differ from the original study where low red tape was associated higher levels of social welfare benefit, which was upheld in our sample of 158 undergraduate students. Status: a draft manuscript is in preparation for submission to Public Performance and Management Review. Weibel et al (2009). The original study was conducted with MBA students in a private sector setting. Boundary conditions led to research design adaptation to the Hong Kong context by making the performance incentives suitable to the Hong Kong context. This this study we sought to directly survey civil servants, and scrapped email addresses from the Hong Kong government website resulting in a sample of 38,884. While response rate from the survey was low (1587, of which 189 were fully completed - most subject appeared to drop out because of the length of the survey) the within-subject design offered a sufficient sample for analysis. Findings are in keeping with our hypotheses and the Brewer and Brewer replication: intrinsic rewards are valued by public sector managers. Status: the manuscript will shortly be submitted to Review of Public Personnel Administration. Two graduate students have been trained in experimental research designs as part of the project, neither has yet graduated (objective 4).

11611516.label: Major findings and research outcome
11611516.value: The issue of replication has been examined in many disciplines in the social sciences for a number of years, particularly since the advent of the ‘replication crisis’ in economics and social psychology. However, it not been on the agenda of scholars in public administration. This project has visibly brought the issue of replication to the fore of public administration research. Project findings have shown how boundary conditions influence understanding of organizational rules (red tape) and that intrinsic incentives are move valued than extrinsic incentives in public sector settings. The project has defined replication in the applied interdisciplinary field of public administration, making an important distinction from reproduction. The project, and its associated publications, has also demonstrated the value of replication to advance knowledge in public administration. The Public Management Review (PMR) article presented a replication protocol. This protocol was developed into best practice recommendations for the replication of experiments in the Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory (JPART) article, drawing on the knowledge and experience gained by conducting replications. The project has substantially contributed to the publication of experimental replications on questions of organizational design in the field. Prior to the publication of the eight experimental replications in the special issue of PMR there no published replications. These publications, together with other project publications (of which some are under-review and or in preparation) and the various conference presentations, have shown that replication is a valuable tool to develop mid-range theory. A book edited by Brewer, James and Walker titled "The Replication of Social Science Research: Knowledge from Public Administration" will be published in January 2021 by Routledge (and will acknowledge RGC funding). The recognition of the research conducted and published can be seen by citation to the project research outputs. The articles published have good citation rates, all above the median for the respective journals (which stood at 2 in the 2018 Web of Science SSCI JCR). The JPART article has been cited 6 times and the PMR essay 7 times. The 9 articles published in the PMR special issue have been cited on at least 2 occasions (max 22), with an average citation of 9.2. These citations suggest that scholars have taken interest in the topic of replication. Alongside the conference presentations, the PI made presentations on this project at: Indiana University, Bloomington, Rutgers University, Newark, Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Yonsei University.

11611516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11611516.value: The project has laid a strong foundation for further development in public administration by demonstrating that through careful experimental research design theories developed and empirically tested (largely) in the West can be examined in other contexts to develop robust mid-range theories. The project thus opens up new courses of action and the development of new research agendas. Extensions of this project can be geographical, particularly in other Asian societies given the extensive use of Western theories of public administration, and also in other topics including the expectancy-disconfirmation model, strategic management, further aspects of decision-making and representative bureaucracy. Tangibly, and based on the achievements of this project, the PI has successfully had further replication projects funded: 1. National Science Foundation China: ‘Public Services, Performance and Citizen Satisfaction: Expanding Experimental Methods in China’ (2020-2023) will replicate studies of citizen satisfaction and performance information use. 2. Public Policy Research Fund: ‘Knowledge Illusion, Community of Knowledge and Citizens’ Extreme Attitudes in Politics and Public Policy’ (2020) replicates studies of knowledge illusion and political extremism and extends this study to include community of knowledge. 3. GRF: 'Publicness and Citizen’s Attribution of Blame and Success to Politicians in Public Service Delivery: A Comparative Replication Study' (2021-2023).

11611516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11611516.value: Scientific knowledge is accumulated through the replication of theory and findings. Replication permits knowledge to be tested in different contexts, and provides information about the ability to generalize research findings. In social science disciplines including economics and social psychology the inability to replicate studies has led to a ‘replication crisis’. This project developed best practice recommendations for replication experiments in the applied interdisciplinary field of public administration. To ensure that a replication crisis does not occur in public administration, and to ensure that better theory and practice can be achieved, scholars conducting replication studies are encourage to: 1. Clearly define the type of replication to be conducted, 2. Plan the replication asking if it is feasible to replication the original study, to assess the validity of the study, and make choices about statistical power, 3. Implement the replication by choosing the critical test case, establishing boundary conditions, and content validity, and 4. Ensure a fair comparison of findings. Findings from the project indicates how adopting these steps allows for the better understand of organizational rules (red tape) and incentive structures and work motivation in the public and private sectors in Hong Kong based on the replication of Western theory.

11612016.label: Project Objectives
11612016.value: To determine whether the institutional co-optation of former activists as municipal representatives contributes to fulfilling the goals of four urban movements (housing, gardening, health and education) in a particular context (six Spanish cities from 2011 to 2017). To explain why local government performance and municipal-level governance arrangements help urban movements to reach their goals. To determine the types and scope of effective movement outcomes produced from May 2011 to May 2017. To examine the similarities and differences between the observed cities and movements and test competing explanations for the movement outcomes.
