11665016.value: 摘要： 現今的全球金融市場是由過去持續的經濟活動，還是自2007－2008年全球金融危機所帶來的顯著金融市場破裂過程所塑造而成? 近年, 全球金融的其中一個主要特點是個體或公司利用避税天堂，以最低成本 (有時候甚至零關税) 跨越國界地轉移資金，因此離岸經濟是一個重要的測試個案。是項研究將會調查中國和印度兩個主要的新興市場在離岸金融體系的參與，從而判斷兩個經濟體與境外聯繫正在持續擴充、保持原狀抑或没落的狀態。研究將會特別關注中國和印度的決策者怎樣從事在毛里求斯的離岸經濟活動。研究將會呈現有關印度和中國公司（尤其是國企）以及中國和印度政府部門的動機和參與情況的新的資料。 是項研究假設受惠國會考慮到本地赤字問題而特別接納新興市場的境外資金，並認為此選擇是可以吸引外國資金的流入。與此同時，儘管非政府組織作出努力，受惠國在全球金融中的角色相對較為低調。是項研究也假設中國和印度的對外資金運作是根據已建構的離岸模式。此模式使中國和印度的公司在離岸結構下獲得成本、速度和法律上的優勢。相反,其他的南南投資卻暫時未能為受惠國提供另類的資金來源。 如果上述的假設能夠成立，是項研究將會因著不同的動力而產生意想不到的結果: 過去的研究廣泛地應為「中國模式」和「南南關係」是全球化下兩個不同的概念，但因著全球金融危機的沈重壓力底下驅使金融監管改革。此外,税收是新興市場的一個愈來愈大的社會問題，但該國家的政府會為了吸納離岸投資而放棄税收收入。 是項研究將會使用混合研究方法來取得有關材料，包括宏觀數據和趨勢、專家訪談以及個案分析。由於香港聚集了大批從事離岸經濟的專家，尤其是會計師和律師，因此香港是一個非常理想的地方收集有關數據。除此之外，研究者將會前往北京、新德里、毛里求斯和孟買進行實地考察。在資金全球化下,毛里求斯有著一個重要的地位，該國成為新興市場離岸網絡的一個重要節點。2014年的初步研究顯示毛里求斯對中國、印度甚至非洲的重要性。透過整合一套有關新興市場離岸聯繫的廣泛數據，此項目將會捕捉中國和印度在離岸經濟的融合。研究結果會對國際政治經濟學有以下的貢獻: 提供一幅更清晰的圖畫去解釋新參與者的動機，並且提供機會去反思全球金融的延續性和變化、南南關係以及國家資本主義與離岸活動的相容性。

11665016.label: Realisation of objectives
11665016.value: This project has offered a theoretical and empirical analysis of emerging markets and the offshore economic system. It has contributed to the scholarly discussion on continuity versus change, one of the most important questions in the study of International Political Economy (IPE). As the global offshore network has deepened in recent decades, most research has focused on Caribbean islands and the surprisingly large number of European offshore financial centers (OFCs)—by my count, 12 jurisdictions in Europe qualify as OFCs. These analyses lack sufficient consideration of non-East Asian emerging markets, since actors in these countries are also engaged with the low-tax offshore economy, especially in terms of easing the entry of foreign capital into their economies. The small island state of Mauritius is an underappreciated part of this story. While European OFCs overwhelmingly intermediate capital flows originating from Western countries, Mauritius is a key node in linking emerging markets to the global offshore economy. Few analysts are aware that corporate structures formed in Mauritius hold over $700 billion in assets in the global economy. Africa and India have had particularly close links with Mauritius as an OFC and these represent critical case studies in determining the trajectory of the global offshore economy. I developed several theoretical concepts during the research process, chief among them: “Consolidated survivor OFCs” The global financial crisis (GFC) has spurred consolidation into fewer OFCs. Many smaller OFCs of the periphery have fallen by the wayside, while core OFCs have stabilized. Consolidated survivor OFCs, namely the Cayman Islands, Mauritius and Switzerland, are largely compliant with international standards yet still carry significant tax advantages. “Network power of USD clearing banks” USD clearing banks set standards and control access to a global financial network that remains central to the functioning of global capitalism. Building on Castells, this network is shown to have switching power and the ability to switch off constituent parts, as seen among smaller OFCs. Semi-peripheral countries have found themselves in a dilemma between continuing to offer incentives in order to accommodate offshore capital, and curtailing problematic offshore activities, whether unilaterally through national legislation, or multilaterally by supporting, pushing for, or even driving global regulatory initiatives. The creation of a new global regulatory framework is felt differently across the global economy, with core and more developed semi-peripheral countries able to make more effective use out of it than less developed semi-peripheral and peripheral countries, the governments of which believe that they are critically dependent on the global offshore sector. The project confirmed the need to shine a light on India’s relationship with Mauritius and the broader offshore economy. India has convincingly exhibited its commitment to the new tax agenda having taken strong steps and implemented strict rules on how investors can utilize Mauritius for business transactions. The analysis combines a critical political economy framework with an understanding of India as a middle power that has learned to articulate global norms. Mauritius-India and Mauritius-Africa are indicative test cases in considering the depth of taxation reform in the post-GFC world. China represents another significant case study of the offshore world and the growing backlash against it, but as among large emerging markets, India has been the more interesting player. The data on Mauritius also led me to developments in Africa and away from China. I still managed to produce some significant findings on China in the context of the BVI case, as well as part of a future research agenda set out in the Routledge book. The China-focused journal article established the defining conflict as the tension between national/global regulations and an Asian-headquartered network that coordinates offshore financial flows globally, including to the Caribbean. The BVI-China relationship, after deep financial interconnections, is on a downward trajectory because of the global network’s shift to consolidated survivor OFCs and narrowing routes for Chinese capital exit. I expanded the research to include the case study of the Seychelles, as earlier raised by one of the GRF referees. Over the last two decades, the Seychelles quietly rose into the top echelon of the global offshore industry and then it experienced a sharp decline. Two different global networks contributed to this outcome. A global advisory network welcomed the Seychelles into its fold before a global banking network that controls access to US dollar transactions constricted its ties with the country. The larger significance is three-fold. First, attention must be paid to global networks as both facilitating neoliberal globalization and as partially recoiling from it. Second, networks oriented around US dollar clearing banks and offshore advisors should be studied closely given the power that comes from their gatekeeper roles. Third, a development strategy founded on offshore business can run aground when faced with tightening global networks and wavering domestic commitment. The result of these developments is a two-track offshore economy with a downward path in some jurisdictions but greater continuity in other parts of the offshore system. I prepared a 35,000 word manuscript for the Routledge Focus series and I was pleased that the referees felt the analysis: • fills a gap in the literature on the global offshore economy; • represents the “most definitive history of the India-Mauritius tax relationship”; • carries academic and societal relevance; • introduces an important new concept, the term “consolidated survivor OFCs”; and • is well-researched with particularly convincing evidence from elites interviews. The referees helpfully pointed out some avenues that could be pursued to further strengthen the manuscript. As a result, I decided that a logical way forward would be to partner with my former RA, Michael Tyrala (now a post-doctorial fellow at HKUST) and co-author a full-length 80,000 word manuscript. Dr. Tyrala brings particular expertise on the OECD and G20. A full-length book gives us room to provide the theoretical rationale and empirical grounding for the argument that an uneven global offshore economy is materializing with closer attention to the African case material. The referees think the concept of consolidated survivor OFCs is original and important. In the full-length book, this concept will be further fleshed out with a discussion of the key characteristics of consolidated survivor OFCs. The findings support the literature more broadly that the global financial crisis (GFC) engendered only incremental change in the global political economy. Mauritius continues to hold advantages in the global offshore economy and is likely to remain a reasonably important OFC. It qualifies as a consolidated survivor OFC. The massive capital flows that entered India via Mauritius in the last two decades, however, represent a unique moment in the history of the global offshore economy and an unrealizable future for the Africa-Mauritius relationship. Africa is not a panacea for Mauritius’ financial sector in the wake of India’s tougher stance on offshore finance. Global regulatory momentum is ongoing and there are reasons to adopt a cautiously optimistic medium-term outlook. One of the reasons is that India has emerged as a global tax leader whose advocacy will shape the potential of change in the future for other emerging markets. There are also emerging forces in the African region that portend a shift in taxation in the future. Two forces are noteworthy: African reporters who are engaged in the global investigative journalism network and better trained tax negotiators. These themes are being developed in the book manuscript.

11665016.label: Major findings and research outcome
11665016.value: This project sought to understand how the tension between globalizing finance and newfound points of resistance are playing out in emerging market cases. Looking back at the recent global project to better regulate taxation, it must be seen ultimately as having let down optimistic readings of an extensive overhaul of the offshore system. The attempts to establish global financial regulation appear to have, for the time being, reinforced many existing power hierarchies. There are more differentiated offshore outcomes in the post-GFC period than there were before. As one key example, the India-Mauritius pairing has undergone a more substantial transformation than the Africa-Mauritius pairing. Structural and ideological factors are critical. Many emerging markets in Africa are heavy recipients of foreign capital and are likely to continue accommodating offshore capital because their elites believe that such a position is necessary to attract foreign capital, particularly in light of domestic capital deficits. The longstanding relationship between India and Mauritius ruptured due to shifting domestic structural economic conditions, revised international norms, and a new configuration of domestic elites in both countries. The sharp policy break in the India-Mauritius offshore relationship stands out in comparison to African countries, which have mainly been following in the earlier footsteps of India in seeking to attract investment flows by means of advantageous tax terms with Mauritius. The conditions found in India are, to a significant extent, missing in other lower-middle countries, meaning that these countries may be unable or unwilling to follow India’s lead at this point. The comparative differences uncovered by this research project underscore the need for more national-level analyses that also incorporate regional and global influences. Any analysis would be incomplete if it focused only on global capital and/or international agreements. OECD action plans still leave individual countries to decide how faithfully they will implement minimum standards and whether they will move beyond those standards. OECD processes are fashioning norms, but they are not yet transformative in practice. The national level holds significant explanatory power concerning: • the ability to protect more established OFCs (Mauritius falls in this camp); • the inability to protect smaller OFCs (seen in the downfall of lowest common denominator OFCs such as the Seychelles); • the limited implementation of new rules by recipient countries of offshore finance (especially among African countries); and • forceful implementation of new rules by a small number of countries (especially India).

11665016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11665016.value: Contestation over the offshore world has generated an uneven landscape. IPE students should be paying close attention as civil society builds on the renewed attention on the offshore system and devote further resources to hold offshore actors to account. A key question is whether China will join India or not in adopting a tougher stance on the use of offshore mechanisms. There are parallels between China and India in their approach to the offshore world. Both have voice and leverage in the global economy, and China, like India, has been attempting to close down at least certain aspects of offshore routes. Still, China has been a more passive player, pursuing a more interest-based approach to the taxation of Chinese firms, and although it has been nominally supportive of reshaping global norms and practices in the area of international taxation, India has been the clear leader of such initiatives. For now, China has opted for a strategy of accommodation when it comes to Western-led institutions like the OECD, their norms, and their reform ideas, although recent geopolitical shifts and China’s considerably more assertive stance in international affairs may drastically alter its calculations vis-à-vis global tax rules.

11665016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11665016.value: The major output of this project is a book entitled “The Uneven Offshore World” because, despite the strong recent pushback against offshore transactions: • the OECD regime still grants the national level some autonomy and only a small number of minimum standards have been agreed to so far; • developing/emerging markets still have more degree of space than advanced economies; • there is varying civil society pressure; and • offshore financial centres have consolidated and as part of this trend, Mauritius remains a key node in global finance. The global offshore economy is a resilient system that is ongoing, although uneven. Pessimism about the degree of change is warranted because of the deep-rooted commitment to prioritizing foreign investment and because new civil society formations are nascent and unable to threaten power structures at present. Moreover, India is an exceptional case. The country is uniquely qualified to execute a new taxation approach given its economic power and lengthy multilateral track record. African economies, in contrast, are less likely to break from tax orthodoxy in the near future.

11665216.label: Project Objectives
11665216.value: Cultural Understanding: To investigate Hong Kong’s history as a manufacturing and materials innovator and reveal possibilities of reactive materials for innovation in art and design. This will be achieved through background research, a literature review and interviews with local manufacturers. Creative Opportunity: To catalogue the various material reactions and their potential use in the creative industries. The findings will be documented using SCM facilities and lead to a database and catalogue to be shared with Hong Kong’s art and design community. Creative Strategy: To establish new design procedures in which material potentiality is at the center of the creative process. This will be achieved through a series of smaller prototypes using the established material catalogue. Interdisciplinary Research: To determine interdisciplinary methods and application strategies (creative, cultural, social) through a cyclical influence of a multi-disciplinary panel. This will be achieved through several recorded colloquies that are edited in a series of journal articles, culminating in the publishing of a book. Behavior Mediation: To apply found material behaviors with the inherent possibilities of narrative, information and aesthetic as a mediation. This will be achieved through the design and fabrication of a high fidelity prototypical display. Sustainable Solutions: To explore smart materials as a low/zero energy medium in larger urban context as a way to reduce energy consumption and method to engage the population with creative solutions to environmental concerns. This will be achieved through an exhibiting of the prototypes as well as a public symposium..

11665216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11665216.value: The number of screens now manufactured has surpassed the number of humans on the planet. Mediated environments today have become so pervasive, it is difficult to think of a moving image that is not electronic; we rarely say ‘digital’ display anymore as the assumption is so ingrained in our culture. Electronic screens are always attached yet rarely integrated, usually added on after the fact. Hence most media understanding does not consider the relationship between the screen and its placement. Media is a skin that does not reach to the bones, the structure of our environment. Smart materials are designed to react to changes in the environment. Even subtle shifts in light, temperature, noise, moisture, pollutants, and more can cause dramatic changes in color, form or structure. These emerging material behaviors allow a rethinking of the relationship between “skin and bone” and ultimately between media and environment. Furthermore, through the ability to transform energy from an environmental input into a visual language, smart materials and their reactions can become a new form of reactive display design. This emerging media will shift from the independent to the integrated and yield opportunity for a new media art, free from the screen, yet still able to convey information, narrative and aesthetics. By bringing scientific, historical, cultural, technical and artistic considerations together into a single project to explore the potential for reactive materials, this proposal suggests a new design process. Instead of materials being selected at the moment of fabrication, we are articulating design through iterative material experiments and documentation. This new media results from environmental and material properties. We propose a two-folded approach to our research and dissemination. First, with support from previous industry relations, we will establish a catalogue of reactions. This initial research will be followed by a series of iterative design explorations, using the identified reagents to form new prototypical displays responding to the environmental changes. Due to the interdisciplinary complexity, we will collaborate with experts Dr. Vincent Ko, a top researcher in Applied Chemistry, Dr. Sarah Kenderdine, a seminal figure in the design of large scale displays, Mr. Louis Lai, a local automotive industry leader and President of SAR Motorsport and Mr. Tobias Klein, an architect and researcher in 3D printing. We will conduct periodical meetings and symposia-like structures that will be recorded and edited in the form of journal articles, an exhibition of the prototypes and a book format. 研究摘要 如今生產的屏幕已經超出了整個地球上人類的數量。如今數碼顯示裝置隨處可見，以至於你很難想象一個非數碼顯示技術所驅動的動畫該是什麼樣的；我們現在已經很少說“數碼顯示屏”，因為“顯示屏”已在我們的文化中默認成為“數碼顯示屏”的代稱。 電子屏幕極少機會是嵌入式製造，一般是在作品完成之後添加連接上的。因此大多數媒體的理解中從未考慮屏幕與它的位置之間的關係。顯示屏幕僅僅只是像“表皮”一样附着于表面，並沒有深入我们身边环境的“骨髓”——根本結構之中。 智能材料的設計旨在對環境的變化作出反應。光、溫度、噪聲、濕度、污染物和更多因素的任何一點微小變化都會引發智能材料在顏色、形狀或是結構上的劇烈變化。這些新的材料變化讓我們可以重新思考“皮與骨”之間的關係，並最終重新思考媒體和環境之間的關係。 此外，通過把周邊環境中輸入的能量轉換成視覺語言的能力，智能材料和它們的環境反應能力可以被用來創造反應式顯示裝置。這種新興的媒介將從仅仅附着在表面的獨立裝置轉而成為一個與周围环境集成化的整體，從而創造出一種新的媒體藝術形式，不依賴屏幕卻又能承載信息、闡述故事和傳達美學。 通過將科學，歷史，文化，技術和藝術整合到一個單一的項目一起探討智能反應材料的潛力，我們在此提案中建議使用一種新的設計過程。與常規的製造設計不同，我們不是在製造時按需選擇現有材料，反而是在多次實驗中歸納總結，以此進行設計。這種新的媒介是環境和材料共同作用的產物。 針對我們的研究和傳播，我們提議使用一個兩重步驟的做法進行研究和傳播。首先，利用我們在工業領域的關係，我們將獲取并建立一個反應材料的總目錄。之後，將通過對以上材料的反復迭代設計和探索，利用確定的材料創造出新的、響應環境變化的顯示器原型。 由於此研究的跨學科複雜性，我們將與應用化學的頂級專家Vincent Ko博士，在大型顯示器設計的開創性人物，Sarah Kenderdine博士合作，本地汽車行業的領導者和SAR賽車總裁Louis Lai先生，以及建築師、3D打印科學研究員Tobias Klein先生。我們會進行定期會議和以座談會形式的學術交流，會議內容將會記錄并整理為期刊形式，製造出的原型將會整理留檔發印成書及進行展覽。

Cultural Understanding: The objective to investigate Hong Kong’s history as a manufacturing and materials innovator and reveal possibilities of reactive materials for innovation in art and design is being achieved through background research, a literature review and interviews. The results have appeared in three published conference proceedings, and one pending journal publication. 2. Creative Opportunity: The objective to catalogue the various material reactions and their potential use in the creative industries has been achieved through an interactive website and online database of material behaviors. Behavior Mediation: The objective to apply found material behaviors with the inherent possibilities of narrative, information and aesthetic as a mediation was highly successful. Both low and high fidelity prototypes were developed and presented. 6. Sustainable Solutions: The objective to explore smart materials as a low/zero energy medium in larger urban context as a way to reduce energy consumption and method to engage the population with creative solutions to environmental concerns is core to the prototype designs and will be the uniting thread in the professional/industry interviews. 11665216.value: • A top tier peer-reviewed Conference Paper (Hessels/Klein) published our findings of the methodologies of working with smart materials in a larger teaching environment at SIGGRAPH Asia 2016. • A top tier peer-reviewed Conference Panel Paper (Hessels) on the use of smart materials as media display was presented at ISEA 2016. • An exhibition of sample prototype art and design projects was presented at ISEA 2016. • An interactive website has been created that includes video documentation of staged reactive material behaviors. A type of ‘how-to’ cookbook, all the steps in the process of making the reactions are documented and demonstrated. • An online database of international contemporary art and design practices and innovative directions for smart materials has been collected and organized. The database will be used for art and design classes and other researchers to build upon and explore further. • Concept designs have been created as 3D models for demonstration prototypes of sustainable applications. The designs have been submitted to competitions and exhibitions. • A discussion group and interview of professionals that work with material flux has been organized for June 2019 that will offer an opportunity to interview and understand practices that range from chemical to bacterial to organism to human to ecosystem, representing the full strata of possibility. • A new core course (6-credit) has been developed and accepted in the newly developed BAS program of the School of Creative Media that uses the strategies from this grant. • Student interaction in the course and research has totalled 117. The two courses are very popular with high TLQ results and high quality output that was shown internationally at the Symposium for electronic Arts (ISEA 2016) and internally at the City University annual Discovery Festival as exemplary results of innovation and discovery in the curriculum of SCM. • A GRF Grant was awarded to Hessels that selects and investigates further one of the potential materials that has been revealed in this research. • A TDG Grant has been received that provides further funding and materials for the course and the direction instigated by this research. • A top tier peer-reviewed Conference Paper (Hessels) published the high-fidelity prototype concept, programming, design and exhibited the documentation of the artwork in ISEA 2019, Korea. • Interviews were conducted with leading practitioners in the field of smart materials and compiled for a paper for journal publication. • An Academic Journal Paper (Hessels, Stoyanova) has been completed and is currently being submitted to top publishers.

11665216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11665216.value: Hessels has secured funding through the GRF to continue this research with regards to one material that proved most promising in terms of low-energy, sustainable urban contexts. The next phase is an in-depth study and construction of a high-fidelity prototype that will effectively lower both pollutants and energy usage in city signature. The prototype engineering plans have been developed and the PI is waiting for social distancing measures to lighten before hiring a team to begin fabrication. “Creative Applications for Smart Glass” began on January, 2020 but has been delayed due to CoronaVirus and the PI’s medical leave. It will resume in January, 2021.

11665216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11665216.value: The GRF grant and a supporting TDG grant became a highly regarded research initiative as well as a successful education experiment. The PI and Co-I created a course that merged new manufacturing strategies with emerging smart and reactive materials. The student work from the lab became acclaimed and the course itself was recognized internationally for its approach to new practices from new materials—it became part of the core curriculum at the School of Creative Media. The PI continued to explore materials that could be ‘mediated’—controlled through programming and adapted to low energy solutions for signage, wayfinding, warning systems, etc. A high-fidelity prototype of a working system used thermochromic pigments and a new type of heating system to create a display that changed its message with no electronics visible. This prototype was presented to enthusiastic response at a top-tier conference and triggered the larger discussion with others in the field. Their compiled explorations in this area were the foundation of a journal paper that will be one of the first to truly outline the advances being made in smart materials beyond their assumed singular role as environmental surfaces and towards their larger potential as media.

11666716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11666716.value: 得 到足够的身体活动 （physical activity）对儿童和青少年很重要。身体活动可以有效提高健康，如降低心血管风险因素、增强骨密度、改善心理健康。世界卫生组织建议，儿童和青少年每天至少保持60分钟的中等或剧烈体力活动。但是约80%的香港的儿童和青少年未达标。因此，当前香港政府的健康和疾病预防的策略包含促进儿童和青少年的身体活动。家和学校之间的交通，作为潜在的身体活动来源，获得越来越多的研究和社会关注。步行或骑自行车往返学校可以显著促进日常身体活动和发展积极的生活方式。然而，在过去的十年中，香港儿童和青少年步行或骑自行车上学的比例从40%稳步下降到29%。 城市建成环境被认为是影响的选择学校交通模式一个重要因素。大量研究发现，在某些环境特征的社区中，儿童和青少年更愿意步行或骑自行车去学校。这些特征包括居住密度高、靠近学校、比较安全。然而，大多数以前的研究已经使用自我报告方法收集交通模式和交通路线，可能受记忆力的影响。 另一方面，大多数研究都是在美国或欧洲进行的，其城市布局和上学交通模式与香港大相径庭。 我们提供了结合GPS和加速度计数据的解决方案。它可以客观量化的儿童的上学的交通方式、交通距离、实际路线和身体活动。本研究将在24所香港公立中学中调研600个14至15岁的学生。于社会生态学模 型的指导下，我们采用全面的数据收集方法来测量：(1)学校，社区，交通路线的建成环境特征；(2) 个人、家庭的因素和学校政策；(3) 身体活动数据。逻辑回归模型将用于调查建成环境特征与不同交通模式的关系。 这 项研究也有重要社会和科学上的意义。理论上，GPS方法将解决先前的研究中的依据记忆的局限性。研究也将识别支持步行或骑自行车上学的环境因素。在政策上，这项研究的结果将帮助香港政府优化建成环境以促进儿童和青少年的身体活动。实际上，这项工作将 有助于城市规划者和设计者创建一个改善儿童和青少健康的城市环境。这项工作也会促进孩子的身体活动和生活质量，从而减少潜在的社会医 疗成本。

11666716.label: Realisation of objectives
11666716.value: # 1 We have obtained a GIS database from Hong Kong government, comprising street centerlines, building footprint, and land use information. Consequently, the built environment features of more 391 public secondary schools has been assessed by: population density, land-use mix, and intersection density in the neighborhood. We developed a GIS database that includes the school walkability index, residential density, land use mix, intersection density, size of the 1-km pedestrian network area, and the average family income for the area around each secondary school in Hong Kong. # 2 Using the GIS database developed in task 1, 40 public secondary schools were selected on the basis of school walkability and average family income. The secondary schools were divided into deciles according to the walkability index scores. Secondary schools within the second, third, and fourth deciles were considered less walkable schools, and those within the seventh, eighth, and ninth deciles were considered highly walkable schools. The secondary schools were also be divided into deciles according to income level. The second, third, and fourth deciles represent low-income secondary schools, and the seventh, eighth, and ninth deciles represent high-income secondary schools. # 3 We conducted a face-to-face survey in March 2018 with 1,148 Hong Kong primary school students, comprised of 559 girls and 589 boys from the fifth and sixth grades of 40 primary schools in Hong Kong, of which 11 were located in Kowloon, 13 in Hong Kong Island, and the other 16 in New Territories. The 40 primary schools were selected by stratified random sampling, aimed at selecting schools in neighborhoods with different socio-economic and built environment contexts. # 4 Interviews were conducted by trained interviewers to collect data about participants’ demographic information, household information, and active school transport record. Participants were asked about “how many days did you walk or bike to/from school during the last 7 days?”. Hence, we identified participants who had done active school transport and those who had not done any active school transport. The participants and their parents were also required to provide a dwelling address, which was used to assess the built environment factors. Besides, participants were required to provide their body weight and height, which were then used to calculate body mass index (BMI), namely, the ratio between the weight in kilograms to the square of height in meters. # 5 In this study, urban greenery was measured using three objective methods: the number of parks, the NDVI, and street greenness. The number of parks was defined as the total number of parks within two buffer zones of a participant’s dwelling and school address. The data on the urban parks were obtained from the Land Department of Hong Kong SAR. Two buffer zones commonly used in walking/cycling built environment studies were adopted in this study: 400 m and 800 m. The NDVI was used to assess the gross urban greenness of a whole area from a multispectral imagery dataset, based on the contrast between two bands: the chlorophyll pigment absorptions of plants in the red band (Red) and the high reflectivity in the near-infrared band (NIR). The NDVI equation is expressed as NDVI = (NIR−Red) / (NIR+Red). NDVI values range between −1.0 and 1.0, with higher values representing higher levels of vegetation. The average NDVI value within a buffer zone for a dwelling and school location was used to measure the overall urban greenness. The street greenness extracted from GSV images was used to estimate the level of greenness perceived by students on streets. GSV-generating points were created along all streets at a spacing of 50 m. The coordinates of the GSV-generating points were input into a Python script, and four GSV images were downloaded for each point, with a 90° field of view and headings of north, east, south, and west. A separate script was developed to determine the level of greenness in each GSV image using an automated machine-learning vegetation extraction method (Houston, 2014). The ratio of greenery pixels to total pixels in four images from a GSV-generating point was used to assess the level of street greenness for the point. # 6 A two-step analysis strategy was implemented corresponding to the data we collected from participants: 1) logistic regression to examine the association between urban greenness and the odds of engaging in AST; 2) linear regression to examine the association between urban greenness and BMI. Multilevel modeling was used for the analysis after controlling for other built environment and individual confounding variables. Individual participants were clustered within street blocks, which are census defined and aggregated in Hong Kong as urban planning units. Models 1 and 2 were used for the 400-m and 800-m buffers, respectively. All of the analyses were performed using the statistical software STATA 13.0 (StataCorp LLC). Our results show that children attending schools with greener surrounding areas are more likely to engage in AST and have a lower body mass index (BMI). In addition, AST partially mediates the impact of urban greenery on BMI. The findings of our study demonstrate the importance of greenery around schools for children’s body weight status. They also offer public health and planning guidance on how to address overweight and obesity problems among children.

11666716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11666716.value: Children who are overweight or obese are at a higher risk of several diseases and are more likely to be overweight or obese in adulthood. Physical inactivity among children and adolescents is one of the major causes of the prevalence of overweight and obesity problems, and hence promoting physical activity, especially active school transport (AST), is a public health priority. Previous studies have provided some evidence that urban greenery may promote physical activity and improve body weight outcomes among children. However, the relationships reported between these factors are inconsistent, partly due to the use of different measures of urban greenery. In the present study, we assessed different dimensions of urban greenery using three measures: number of parks; the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) based on satellite imagery; and street greenness based on Google Street View images. Multilevel regression analysis and structural equation modeling were conducted to investigate the complex relationships among urban greenery, AST, and body weight for 1,148 primary school students in Hong Kong. Our results show that children attending schools with greener surrounding areas are more likely to engage in AST and have a lower body mass index (BMI). In addition, AST partially mediates the impact of urban greenery on BMI. The findings of our study demonstrate the importance of greenery around schools for children’s body weight status. They also offer public health and planning guidance on how to address overweight and obesity problems among children.

11666716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11666716.value: The findings of our study demonstrate the importance of urban greenery, especially around schools, in promoting children’s AST behavior and improving their body weight status. These findings have important implications for policymakers, architects, health promoters, and urban planners and designers. Government agencies should consider establishing targeted policy plans to promote children’s health by creating new greenspaces or improving existing greenspaces around schools. More specifically, future planning and design of urban greenspaces should shift from an exclusive focus on the size or the number of greenspaces to the practice considering the accessibility and visibility of those greenspaces, so they can be easily perceived by children in their daily lives. This is particularly critical for high-density cities, such as Hong Kong, where land supply is limited and greenspaces in built-up areas are scarce. Future studies could use natural experiments to deliver more robust scientific evidence. We also used questionnaires to assess AST, which may be subject to recall bias or social desirability bias. In future studies, school travel behaviors could be collected by portable GPS and/or accelerometer equipment for more objective measures.

11666716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11666716.value: project, in no more than 200 words) Using three urban greenery measures (number of parks, NDVI, and street greenery with GSV images), we found that street greenery in the area surrounding a school was significantly associated with children’s AST behaviors and body weight status. AST was also found to play a mediating role in the relationship between urban greenery and the body weight status of children. The findings of this study join others in highlighting the importance of greenery exposure around schools in promoting AST and improving body weight status among children. Future planning and design practice should consider the visibility of greenspaces as well as more traditional planning parameters such as the size or number of greenspaces.

11668916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11668916.value: 中国地方政府是如何应对气候变化的？研究中央政府如何制定气候政策的文献已汗牛充栋，但对宏观政策制定背景下的地方气候治理却研究甚少—此类研究必须考量央地关系在政策领域的主导地位（意指“政治中央化”和“经济地方化”下之政治/经济不对称对中央-地方关系的影响）。事实上，中央政府的气候政策能否成功在很大程度上取决于地方政府的实践。当下亟需对这一方面的实证研究。 “多层级治理”和“科层制实践”的理论有助于我们理解地方实践及其引发的制度变化，然而这些理论在气候治理方面的相关性和重要性却尚未得到验证。通过探究长江三角洲（包括上海、江苏、浙江，中国经济重心之所在—亦面临严重气候脆弱性）地方政府的气候创新政策及实践，本研究旨在回应下列问题： --地方政府在制度气候变化政策时，是如何在科层制结构的影响下进行前瞻性考量的？ --长三角单个地方政府的政策突破或制度创新是出于回应中央政府信号压力的需求，还是地方气候治理主体（包括气候变化专家及鼓吹者）的主动诉求？ --如果地方政府的政策动向依然严重受控于中央政府，那么实验性的气候交易制度和气候立法是如何影响超越省际范围的制度和政策调整的？ --当经济领域的省际合作并不鲜见时，为何省际气候政策的合作却极为罕见？ 本研究旨在探讨长三角省级政府制定的极其多样化的气候变化政策及实践结果，藉此验证“多层级治理”理论在气候变化领域的相关性—地方政府是否通过采取强有力的气候变化政策及行动，成为中央政府的政策代理者、和其他省级政府一起行动并融合非政府成员。我们也将分析“科层制实践”是如何影响地方政府制定并实施气候政策。通过解释为何省际层面的气候政策合作的缺失，本研究将丰富对中国情景下地方气候治理中的央/地关系的理解。

11669116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11669116.value: As the baby boomers (born between 1946 and 1964) are being joined by growing numbers of workers from Generation Me cohort (born between 1982 and 1999), today’s employees are increasingly likely to work and interact with coworkers from other age groups. However, because younger and older workers tend to have different work values and attitudes (Twegen et al., 2010), intergenerational conflicts are becoming more common in the workplace. Research also suggests that reactions to workplace conflict can vary according to the age of the employee and the age group of the opposing party (Birditt et al., 2005; Fingerman et al., 2008; Yeung et al., under review). In this project, we will extend our previous research by investigating the underlying mechanism of age-related differences in emotional and behavioral reactions to intergenerational conflict in the workplace. A large body of research on lifespan development suggests that older adults show a greater looking preference toward positive information and away from negative information than their younger counterparts (Isaacowitz, 2012). Drawing on the modal model of emotion (Gross, 2007), which posits that an individual’s attention precedes his/her appraisal of an event, we speculate that differences in older and younger workers’ visual attention affects their emotional and behavioral reactions to intergenerational conflict. In this project, we propose to conduct two eye-tracking experiments to objectively assess the looking patterns of younger and older workers when experiencing hypothetical workplace conflict. Study 1 will record the natural looking patterns of younger and older workers in response to video vignettes of hypothetical intergenerational and non-intergenerational workplace conflicts. This study aims to demonstrate whether there are any age differences in visual attention when experiencing conflicts with coworkers from different age groups. It will also examine the relationships among looking patterns, emotional and behavioural reactions, and work-related outcomes. Study 2 will make use of experimental manipulation to shape the looking patterns of younger and older workers when encountering workplace conflicts. The aim will be to test whether looking patterns account for the age-related differences in the emotional and behavioural reactions to intergenerational conflict. The findings of the proposed project will have both theoretical and practical implications. Specifically, it will advance the literature by unveiling the attentional underpinning of conflict management. It will also provide insights to human resources personnel for designing an age-sensitive training and development programs to meet the needs and preferences of older and younger workers when handling workplace relations. 現在職場的僱員普遍包括嬰兒潮一代（於1946至1964年間出生的 人）及千禧年一代（於1982至1999年間出生的人），令這兩代的 僱員有更多合作的機會。由於年輕及年長僱員有不同的工作價值 觀及態度，跨代衝突變得越來越普遍。過去的研究顯示工作衝突 的反應會受僱員的年齡及衝突伙伴的年齡組別而有所不同。本研 究將會延續過去的研究以探討導致跨代衝突反應之年齡差異的根 本原因。 過去的研究顯示與年輕僱員比較，年長僱員傾向觀看正面的資訊 ，並避免觀看負面的資訊(Isaacowitz, 2012)。根據Gross(2007)情緒 理論，此研究預測跨代工作衝突的反應會存在年齡差異。此研究 將進行兩個眼動追踪的實驗，以容觀地量度年輕及年長僱員在經 歷假設的工作衝突時所涉及的視覺觀看模式。第一個研究會記錄 年輕及年長僱員在經歷假設的跨代及非跨代的工作衝突時所涉及 的自然視覺觀看模式，並比較有沒有年齡差異。此外，這研究亦 會探討視覺觀看模式、情緒及行為反應和工作成果的關係。第二 個研究會利用實驗操作方法以影響年輕及年長僱員的視覺觀看模 式，用以了解視覺觀看模式是否導致跨代工作衝突的情緒及行為 反應所存在的年齡差異。 本研究的結果將有理論及實際的啟發，包括視覺注視模式在衝突 處理的角色，及有助人事顧問設計符合年齡組別的訓練課程，以 配合年輕及年長僱員的需要及喜好。

11669616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11669616.value: 過去十年間，廣告已經成為網站和應用程式的主要收入來源。但同時，它亦成為了監視用戶的主要手段，廣告商更收集和存儲大量用戶個人數據以用於定向營銷。雖然政府機構如美國國家安全局或英國GCHQ的監控手法已備受媒體關注，廣告商的監控手段可說是更令人擔憂。除了大規模監控引致已知的一般傷害，研究證明廣告監控也是散佈惡意軟件的平台，有不法之徒通過廣告機制注入惡意軟件，使用戶進一步受到威脅。廣告監控同時可顯著降低網絡瀏覽器的功能，因大量的第三方資源在用戶不知情或不同意情況之下被加載了。早前有的嘗試去規範這種做法大都無效，當中以「Do-No-Track (不要追蹤) 倡議」成為了最公開的失敗。 如果廣告監控的現狀持續下去，我們預見兩種趨勢將會繼續。首先，隨著廣告監控增加，隱私的威脅、惡意軟件的危害和降級的用戶體驗可能使一般低技術用戶限制自己的網上時間。第二個趨勢是越來越多用戶採用廣告攔截軟件，威脅到網絡內容的現行經濟模式。 廣告攔截軟件在近幾年日益普遍，蘋果電腦公司已於其新IOS（流動作業系統）引入了廣告攔截功能。同樣，Mozilla似乎準備為火狐瀏覽器中的可選功能實施「反跟踪保護」。這些趨勢結合起來將對非技術用戶和只有較慢連接的用戶有著極大影響，同時，規模較小的內容提供者將受到威脅和/或被迫採用訂閱模式，再次孤立了貧困和邊緣化的用戶。在這兩種情況下，我們看到一個非常不同的網絡發展前景：網絡由大型企業支配、監控和惡意軟件變得更為猖獗，而獨立製作的內容越見稀疏。 改變這種狀況需要兩件事：首先，用戶需要一種工具讓他們能更理解複雜的廣告生態系統。目前，普通用戶一就是不斷受到可見的廣告和隱藏的跟踪器轟炸，或且是安裝了廣告攔截軟件，讓他們什麼都看不到，而以上兩者都不能幫助用戶提高對廣告商操作的理解。其次，廣告監控的危害變得明顯之際，用戶需要一種方法來表達自己的不滿。雖然現行一些工具已嘗試解決這個問題的不同方面，到目前為止還沒有平台類近我們提出的AdNauseam，既可幫助用戶得到對問題的更深入了解，也能讓他們主動作出抗議。 AdNauseam能達到以上兩事的方法如下：AdNauseam利用廣告攔截軟件阻止廣告和跟踪器，並同時在背後捕捉每個廣告，使用戶可以透過互動的視化功能觀看自己默默被轟的廣告（見圖1）。及後，AdNauseam還以廣告商聽懂的方式，即通過經濟語言，讓用戶表示不滿。具體而言，軟件會在背後把每一個廣告都點擊，使用戶的個人數據污染了，同時也在廣告商和他們付費的點擊網絡之間產生不信任。 此提案說明我們如何將簡單的AdNauseam原型開發成為正式瀏覽器軟件插件，包括詳細的功能細節和評價方法。這項工作的成果將以附帶文檔的免費開源軟件於網上發行，並在國際會議及著名學術期刊發表。

11669616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11669616.value: We have designed, specified, and implemented a fully-functional, production-quality version of AdNauseam, including interactive visualisations with aggregate and detail views; ad-filtering via criteria such as network, content-topic, domain, date, etc.; an intuitive UI for managing block and white-lists, and configuring options (e.g., visitation frequency, etc.) The work has been described in the peer-reviewed Journal on Privacy Engineering (IEEE) and has been presented at a number of international conferences including in the USA, Holland, Norway, and Hong Kong. Over the course of the project we have successfully addressed a number of core research questions, including how users understand the advertising ecosystem, the relationship between targeted advertising and privacy, and the larger context of software for social change. Though the grant has concluded we continue to work on documentation, distribution, and improvements for AdNauseam, and explore further high-profile venues for publications and conference presentations.

11669616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11669616.value: There is high potential for further development of this agenda research via additional grants. One such proposal has already been submitted to the RGC for funding (see #11613419: Obfuscation-as-a-Service: Privacy via the Cloud). We are likely to re submit and/or submit this grant to other agencies in the future.

11669616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11669616.value: The AdNauseam project represents a highly impactful integration of research and tool-making with over 300,000 downloads of the software and scores of media reports including radio segments on CBC news radio and TVB news television. All told there have been more than 40 international articles, in at least 10 languages, on the software developed in this research (for full list see https://adnauseam.io/press.html). When the production version of AdNauseam was released in 2017, its impact led to Google banning AdNauseam from its Chrome Web Store, in a clear demonstration of the effectiveness of the strategy on unscrupulous data collectors. It has since been selected as a "Featured Extension" by Mozilla for their Firefox browser. Additionally it has resulted in peer-reviewed and popular articles, as well as a number of high profile international conference presentations. The overarching topic of 'privacy via obfuscation' (initiated in the PI's early project entitled TrackMeNot) has grown into an active subfield of computer science and privacy engineering research.

11670216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11670216.value: 儒家美德政治的演化: 从孟子到荀子

11670216.label: Project Objectives
11670216.value: Systemically reconstruct the political theories of Mencius and Xunzi against the political backdrop of the Warring States period. Deepen our understanding of the different ways in which Mencius and Xunzi built the characteristically Confucian nexus between the political and the ethical, which created the political tradition of Confucian virtue politics. Articulate how Xunzi transformed Confucian virtue political theory into a more philosophically robust political theory by critically engaging with Mencius’s moral and political ideas. Illuminate the distinctive features of Mencius and Xunzi’s political theories compared with the work of Western thinkers such as Nietzsche, Freud, Hobbes, and Hume.

11670216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11670216.value: One of the distinctive features in the recent development of Confucian political theory is the creative dialogue between classical Confucian political thought and normative political theory. The aim is to develop Confucianism in ways that are compatible with democracy, human rights, pluralism, and modern constitutionalism. However, although the normative orientations among contemporary Confucian theorists are attributed to their differing interpretations of classical Confucian political theory, they rarely offer detailed or systemic accounts of those interpretations, on which their normative arguments are predicated. Even when theorists do provide an explanation, their discussions do not address or account for the internal dynamics within classical Confucian political theory. Specifically, little effort has been made to capture the distinctive features of Mencius and Xunzi’s Confucian political theories in a philosophically systematic way. No one has identified what their otherwise distinctive political theories have in common as “Confucian” theories, how the theories differ from each other despite their shared Confucian roots, and what contributes to such differences. In this book project, I will shed new light on classical Confucian political theory by presenting Mencius and Xunzi’s political theories from a “philosophical evolution” perspective. I will show that Xunzi’s more intricate Confucian political theory of virtue politics, which significantly improved Mencius’ theory, was achieved through creative engagement in his predecessors’ (including Mencius’) ideas under the dramatically altered political situation during the “Warring States” period. Objecting to both the widely held view that reduces these thinkers’ virtue-oriented political theories to virtue ethics, and the recent revisionist view that completely decouples their “political” theories from their profound concern with virtue, I argue that Mencius and Xunzi each developed a unique mode of political theory in which morals and politics were inextricably intertwined. There are two important differences between Mencius and Xunzi. The first is the way they entwine morals and politics. The second is the way they extend the originally global, normative vision of Confucian virtue politics to emerging interstate relations during the late Warring States period. By investigating and comparing Mencius and Xunzi’s ideas on the origin of morality, moral standing of interest (li 利), relation between virtue and ritual, royal succession, good and evil government, and interstate relations and just war, this project aims to present an interesting development of political theory from Mencius to Xunzi. 近年儒家政治理论发展中最显著的特征之一，是经典儒家政治思想与规范政治理论之间，旨在令儒家与民主、人权、多元主义以及现代宪政主义相容的创造性对话。尽管当代儒学理论家之间不同规范取向的很重要一点来源是他们对经典儒家政治理论的不同阐释，但是儒学理论家极少提出对经典儒学的系统性解读，以便支撑各自的规范论述。即便当他们这样做时，其讨论也远远未能把握住经典儒家政治理论的内部动态——这种内部动态很大程度上由孟子与荀子奠定，二者均通过对前人的批判性考察，就孔子的政治思想进行了根本的革新，将其打造为孔子所设定的总体政治框架之下截然不同却又各自融贯的政治理论。换言之，从系统性的哲学角度把握孟子与荀子儒家政治理论各自特色的努力，实在少得令人惊讶。几乎没有人研究究竟是什么令二者相差甚大的政治理论构成共同的“儒家”理论，这两种理论如何在共享儒家根源的同时与对方相互区别，以及究竟什么导致了这种区别。 在这本书中，我从“哲学演化”的角度阐释孟子与荀子之间本来相互竞争的政治理论，进而以全新的视角来看待经典儒家政治理论。我将荀子较为精致的关于美德政治的儒家政治理论，理解为对孟子理论的重大改良，这种改良来自于他对前人（包括孟子）想法的有创造力的采纳，令其适应于战国时期截然不同的政治环境。我既反对主流那种将这些思想家以美德为导向的政治理论化约为其美德伦理、从而无法理解他们（不同的）儒家美德政治观的独特政治维度的做法，又反对最近一些将他们的“政治”理论与其对美德的深刻关切完全剥离的修正论调；相反我将论证，孟子与荀子各自发展出了一种独特的政治理论模式，其中道德与政治相互缠绕、无可解脱。我的论证核心是，孟子与荀子在两个方面存在重大区别，一是他们将道德与政治相缠绕的方式，二是他们如何将原本作为全局性规范愿景的儒家美德政治，拓展到晚期战国初生的国与国关系之中。

11671116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11671116.value: 韌性是指一個人成功適應逆境的能力。生態韌性風險模型強調來自個人、家庭和社會層面的風險和保護因素。這些因素對韌性的影響程度仍未清晰。此外，社會傳染理論，解釋心理特徵如何在跨網絡「傳播」，為探討母子二人跨代韌性傳遞提供了框架。家庭系統理論也假定，重要壓力影響整個家庭，而家庭成員間具有相互依存的關係。母親傳遞韌性至子女，是促進兒童韌性的其中一個機制。同時，兒童的韌性可促進母親的韌性以適應挑戰。除了在移民框架中探討韌性的風險因素和保護因素，是次研究集中在母子二人韌性的相互依存關係，探討（一）韌性在二人的傳遞程度和（二）抑鬱症狀和其他潛在調節變量，影響母子之間韌性一致性的程度。 本研究將招募300對從中國內地來港的母子組合（兒童年紀介乎11至15歲），並使用兩波的縱向設計。完成這些研究目標而獲得的資訊將對文獻有所貢獻：（一）以前移民研究中的傳統模型，集中在新移民的適應不良和心理問題；轉至集中在有效運作和正面成果的優勢模型；（二）提供有關有助韌性縱向變化的動態過程的資訊（即應對生活過渡壓力的韌性上升或下降）；（三）註明以前個人為本模型的限制（集中於兒童自己的素質和適應因素），突出母親在跨代傳遞韌性至兒童的角色，並使用雙向方法探討兒童在促進母親韌性的角色；（四）進一步探討潛在調節變量，以了解母子二人韌性傳遞的機制。 通過在新來港母子二人中使用主角-伴侶相互依存模型，本研究以新的角度審視家庭為本文化中的韌性。最終，研究結果將帶來適合中國文化的、為新來港家庭量身訂造的韌性干預方案。

11671116.label: Realisation of objectives
11671116.value: In the present study, 200 pairs of immigrant mothers and their children participated in two waves of the two-year longitudinal survey. Mothers reported low socioeconomic status (tertiary education or above, 48%; household monthly income lower than 20,000HKD, 62%) and stayed in Hong Kong less than 7 years. Children aged 7 to 18 years. We have achieved our first objective to examine risk and protective factors for resilience in immigrants. Our findings identified fluid mindset (the belief that an individual’s attributes such as intelligence are fluid and malleable) as cognitive resources to facilitate resilience (r = .44, p < .01, mothers; r = .32, p < .01, children). Individuals with fluid mindset view the adversities as opportunities for learning and exploration, and they build a repertoire of coping skills for positive adjustment (See our publication on Family Process). Moreover, perceived discrimination functioned as a risk factor for adjustment of immigrants, as this risk factor was associated with psychological distress (prevalent among individuals with low level of resilience) in both mothers (r = .57, p < .01) and children (r = .59, p < .01; see our publication on Applied Psychology). We have achieved our second objective on the congruence in resilience among mothers and children. Concurrently, there was positive association (r = .31, p < .01) between mothers’ and children’s resilience at baseline, indicating moderate level of congruence in the mother-child dyad (see our findings published on Family Process). Over time, the congruence between mothers’ and children’s resilience remained significant (r = .32, p < .01, for T1 child resilience and T2 mother resilience; r = .28, p < .01, for T1 mother resilience and T2 child resilience; manuscript under preparation). By achieving the third objective, our further analyses showed that the congruence between mothers’ and children’s resilience was moderated by depressive symptoms of mothers, such that for mothers reporting lower levels of depressive symptoms, the association between mothers’ resilience and children’s resilience was stronger. Children’s depressive symptoms did not significantly moderate the association between mothers’ and children’s resilience (manuscript under review). These findings highlight the importance of mothers’ depressive symptoms in the intergenerational transmission of resilience.

11671116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11671116.value: Immigration research has recently investigated positive adaptation outcomes such as psychological growth, however, it is unknown whether resilience works as the mediating mechanism to transmit the positive effect. Among 200 migrant mother-child dyads from Mainland China to Hong Kong, we examined the actor and partner effects between fluid mindset and psychological growth based on the actor-partner interdependence model, hypothesizing resilience as the mediator. The results showed that mothers’ fluid mindset had significant actor and partner effects on their own and their children’s psychological growth, whereas children’s fluid mindset showed an actor effect. Fluid mindset had significant actor indirect effects on psychological growth via resilience in both mothers and children. Mothers’ fluid mindset had a significant partner indirect effect on children’s psychological growth via children’s resilience. Our findings highlight the mediating role of resilience to transmit the positive effect of fluid mindset on psychological growth. Future resilience-based intervention programs on wellbeing enhancement are recommended to treat immigrant mothers and children as a whole and consider their interdependence. Guided by the family systems theory, we investigated the effects of congruence and discrepancies of perceived discrimination levels perceived by migrant children and mothers on their psychological distress. The results showed that when children’s and mothers’ reports of perceived discrimination were consistent, higher levels of perceived discrimination were positively associated with psychological distress in both mothers and children. In addition, when children’s and mothers’ reports of perceived discrimination were discrepant, higher perceived discrimination among children compared to mothers was associated with increased psychological distress for children, and higher perceived discrimination among mothers compared to children was associated with increased psychological distress for mothers. Our findings contribute to the understanding of the degree to which child-mother congruence and the direction of discrepancies in perceived discrimination predicts children’s and mothers’ psychological distress. Future psychological distress-reduction intervention programs among migrants need to consider the family context involving child-mother pairs, based on their levels of consistency in the perception of discrimination. Further to the research question of the congruence on resilience among mothers and children, it is possible for emotional symptoms such as depression to block the intergenerational transmission of resilience from mothers to children. Our findings showed that mothers’ resilience was significantly associated with children’s resilience only for mothers reported low levels of depressive symptoms; the association was not significant for mothers reported high levels of depressive symptoms. Interestingly, children’s depressive symptoms did not significantly moderate the association between mothers’ and children’s resilience. These findings advance the existing understanding about resilience transmission in the mother-child dyad, and highlight the interfering role of depressive symptoms. There are strong implications for future family-focused resilience intervention programs targeting children to alleviate mothers’ depressive symptoms.

11671116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11671116.value: Our findings highlight the importance of treating immigrant mother-child dyad as a whole in resilience research. There are five directions for further development: (1) Advanced theoretical frameworks on interdependence are needed to guide dyadic studies (e.g., the mother-child dyad, husband-wife dyad, patient-caregiver dyad). The existing theories (e.g., the actor-partner interdependence model, common fate model, mutual influence model) need more empirical support and supplement which will result in theoretical refinement to address their limitations. (2) The interdependence nature of mother-child dyad in various contexts (e.g., cultures, family structures, relationship stability, health conditions) deserve further investigations. Contextual consideration in different settings will inform specific needs of particular members and the family. (3) Using mixed methods integrating both qualitative research and quantitative research to elaborate how mothers and children execute mutual influences in the family context. (4) Investigations on the potential mediating and moderating factors (e.g., emotional responsiveness, dyadic coping, communication, relationship dynamics) underlying the mutual influences between mothers and children will contribute new knowledge to the field. (5) Treating the mother-child dyad as an intervention unit matches with the essence of the family-oriented intervention programs. Practical endeavors to design interventions based on the dyadic perspective will benefit both members and their families.

11671116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11671116.value: By targeting immigrant mother-child dyads, this project examined how the dyadic members exhibit mutual influences and the moderating mechanism to explain the strength of interdependence. Using the actor-partner interdependence model, we found that fluid mindset, functioning as cognitive resources, contributed to resilience, and further impacting on the outcome of psychological growth, for both mothers and children. Mothers’ fluid mindset also had significant partner indirect effect on children’s psychological growth via children’s resilience. We also examined the resilience congruence in intergenerational dynamics. The results showed that mothers’ depressive symptoms, rather than children’s depressive symptoms, reduced the strength of association between mothers’ and children’s resilience. These findings contribute to our understanding regarding the interdependence of the mother-child dyad in positive adjustment. There are strong implications to inform the treatment of the mother-child dyad as an intervention unit for wellbeing enhancement.

11671416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11671416.value: Different martial art styles and schools have influenced Chinese culture, philosophy, folklore but also medicine and sports. Especially Hong Kong has a long tradition in martial arts with its diverse and rich kung fu styles. With the traditional methods of documentation by photos, drawings or video, the different models of body mechanics are insufficiently recorded. This is why the International Guoshu Association and the School of Creative Media of City University are cooperating in the project 'The Hong Kong Martial Arts Archive' since 2013. Meanwhile 20 Kung Fu styles and over 120 weapon sets in form of motion data (MOCAP) but also HD Video interviews with contemporary witnesses have been recorded. The next step will be the planning of the structure of the archive and a model for the digital preservation based on international museum standards for documentation and preservation. In 2014 the Documentation Committee (CIDOC) of the International Council of Museums (ICOM) had established the CIDOC Intangible Cultural Heritage Working Group because the existing data field catalogues used in museums and archives lag often behind the demands made by intangible heritage. At the moment there is no existing model or data field catalogue based on museum documentation standards for the archiving of martial arts. This proposed research is perfectly suited to remedy this gap. In this study we will examine the way how martial arts related forms of intangible cultural heritage like performance art and performing arts like dance get documented and how their digital data can get prepared for long-term preservation. We are applying for a GRF to develop a data field catalogue based on international museum documentation standards to create a digital archive for martial arts in Hong Kong which can be used as a model for the further documentation of intangible heritage. By analyzing these standards as well as discussing several case studies, the needs for this archive will get defined. In this research project leading experts in the field of the documentation of performance art, performing arts and martial arts will meet at a Workshop in Hong Kong to share their experiences and their knowledge to define criteria for the archiving of ephemeral knowledge. The results will have a high impact on martial arts as Hong Kong’s renown cultural heritage, on documentation of intangible cultural heritage as well as on long-term preservation of digital museum data and therefore support the work of ICOM/CIDOC and UNESCO.

11671416.label: Realisation of objectives
11671416.value: A revision of the objectives became necessary after the RGC cut back on the funds provided. Objective 1: Existing data field catalogues for museum documentation have been analysed and evaluated. New data fields have been defined and presented on several conferences and workshops. For the publication see Objective 2. Objective 2: The definition of the guidelines was made. However, the implementation and publication of the guidelines and as part of this of the data fields have been delayed because the responsible working groups Documentation Standards, Intangible Cultural Heritage, and Digital Preservation of ICOM/CIDOC ICOM only meets once a year and therefore no decisions could be made in 2019 with regard to the planned guidelines. Objective 3: The exchange of knowledge and experience with registrars and the dialogue with the creative industries has taken place on several occasions such as conferences and workshops. Objective 4: The work of UNESCO and ICOM/CIDOC Working Group: Documentation Standards, Intangible Cultural Heritage, Digital Preservation has been supported. CIDOC Lausanne Objective 5 and 6: Despite several discussions with the Co-Is, the establishment of an archive for the documentation of martial arts could not be realised. On the part of the Co-Is, a Museum for Martial Arts in Hong Kong is being planned. The planned archive will then become part of this museum at a later date. Objective 7: The Co-Is realized several exhibitions and thus made Martial Arts visible as an important factor of the Cultural Heritage in Hong Kong. The PI was involved in these exhibitions as consultant and expert.

11671416.label: Major findings and research outcome
11671416.value: During the research project numerous projects and initiatives have been researched and analyzed for their strategies of the documentation of intangible heritage. For Archiving and Documentation in general: 22, for Performing Arts: 16, for Performance Arts: 8, for Martial Arts: 25. Information about these projects will be part of the coming publication. The analysis and evaluation of recent Museum Documentation data field catalogues like CIDOC Information Categories, SPECTRUM, CDWA Lite, CIDOC CRM, MuseumDat, LIDO, Dublin Core Metadata have brought an overview and shown that the existing data fields for Performance Arts and Perforing Arts are incomplete to document the needs of Martial Arts. Often the requirements are identical, but the terminology used is in urgent need of discussion to clarify the terms. An important event had been the workshop "Archiving Ephemeral Knowledge and Intangible Cultural Heritage – a Workshop for the Archiving of Performing Arts, Performance Arts and Martial Arts", held in 2017 at School of Creative Media at City University. During the workshop the renown Collection and Museum Management System specialist Norbert Kanter as well as formerly CIDOC Chairman and specialist for UNESCO Intangible Heritage Dr. Nicholas Crofts gave an analysis of the Museum Documentation data field catalogues related to the topic of intangible heritage and an overview of International Standards. Following their recommendations we have concentrated on the following standards and data field catalogues: - The UK Museum Documentation Standard SPECTRUM provides a format for exchanging object records between different collections management systems and aggregating data. - CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model (ISO 21127) (CIDOC CRM) is intended to promote a shared understanding of cultural heritage information by providing a common and extensible semantic framework that any cultural heritage information can be mapped to. - Museumdat is a harvesting format optimised for retrieval and publication, meant to deliver automatically core data to museum portals. It builds largely upon the data format CDWA Lite and is compatible with CIDOC-CRM. - Lightweight Information Describing Objects (LIDO) is an XML harvesting schema which is intended for delivering metadata. LIDO supports the full range of descriptive information about museum objects. From this the data fields were extracted and analyzed. In order to be able to do this in a practical way, the application of the preliminary data field catalogue was implemented using case studies. Some of these case studies were then presented and discussed at later meetings in Zurich, Lausanne. Currently, the data field catalogue is being discussed and evaluated by experts of CIDOC/ICOM.

11671416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11671416.value: After the evaluation by CIDOC/ICOM, the data field catalogue will be tested in a practical field of application in everyday museum life. This will show to what extent the given data fields meet the practical needs and where there are still open problems to be solved. From this, further questions can then be developed, which, for example, are dedicated to the documentation of performative works of digital art. Routledge has shown a strong interest in publishing the results of this research.

11671416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11671416.value: Performing Arts, Performance Art and Martial Arts have the same conditions to take place: they happen at a certain place and require a certain time in which they are realized. With the traditional methods of documentation by photos, drawings or video, the different models of body mechanics are insufficiently recorded. In 2014 the International Documentation Committee (CIDOC) of the International Council of Museums (ICOM) had established the Intangible Cultural Heritage Working Group because the existing data field catalogues lag often behind the demands made by intangible heritage. The task and aim of this research project was to work out the differences in the various forms of documentation, to compare them with each other and to develop a data field catalogue. In this research project we have examined the way how Martial Arts related forms of intangible cultural heritage like performance art, performing arts get recorded, documented and archived. The results of this research will have an impact on the guidelines on documentation of intangible heritage as well as for the long-term preservation of digital museum data and therefore support the work of ICOM/CIDOC.

11672416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11672416.value: This project intends to examine a unique genre of Western paintings produced in Canton (Guangzhou) from the late eighteenth through the mid-nineteenth century. It is, namely, the botanical and zoological illustrations conducted by a few Chinese craftsmen under the direction of a number of British traders and captains who were amateur naturalists. Natural history drawings combine interests in art and nature and create unique aesthetic experiences. On the one hand, they require accuracy and realism which are theoretically universal, on the other they are done by craftsmen or artists who have their own artistic tradition and training. The seventeenth and eighteenth centuries witnessed a boom in the development of natural science in Europe. In the Age of Enlightenment, familiarity with both literary classics and natural sciences was a hallmark of an educated person. Practicing natural history drawings allowed European literary men to combine the two interests together. It is under such circumstances that the British East India Company traders and captains who conducted China trade in Canton, the only port at which Sino-foreign trade was sanctioned between 1757 and 1842, used their spare time to study native plants and animals during their stay in Macau and the suburban area of Canton. As a supplement to their amateur scientific studies, they employed local craftsmen to produce natural history illustrations. This is how thousands of outstanding natural history drawings done by Chinese craftsmen came to form part of the collection of the Natural History Museum, the Kew Garden, the Horticultural Society in London, and some other public and private hands in the nineteenth and the twentieth centuries. They are important materials for studying how Western science and Chinese art could have been blended in the hands of ordinary craftsmen. These craftsmen were most likely also involved in the production of other types of export arts. They are almost unknown in Chinese art history, and yet they might have left a long-lasting impact on practical art and design which extended to the post-Opium War days. These collections are hitherto largely overlooked. A systematic analysis of these pictures substantiated with both Western and Chinese textual materials will be beneficial not only to appreciating this particular genre of art, but also to further understanding Sino-foreign cultural exchanges among ordinary people before the mid-nineteenth century, allowing us to re-examine the late imperial history of China against a wider global backdrop in a new light.

11672416.label: Realisation of objectives
11672416.value: About 80% of the samples among the Chinese botanical and zoological illustrations the PI collected at the Natural History Museum, the Royal Horticultural Society, and the Royal Botanical Garden (Kew) in London, have been identified. Between 2017 and 2019, she looked a number of archives and collections, namely, the William Farquhar Collection at the National Museum of Singapore, the John Bradby Blake (an East India Company’s captain)’s collection at the Oak Spring Garden Foundation (Virginia, US), the Chinese botanical drawings collected at Arnold Arboretum and Botany Library at Harvard University. [Objective 1] The PI has studied most of the related textual materials including private correspondences, scientific journals, travelogues, and magazines, especially the newly opened papers of John Bradby Blake collected at the Oak Spring Garden Foundation, on which she has conducted in-depth analysis. Likewise, with the assistance of part-time Ras, the PI has searched various databases of eighteenth- and nineteenth-century English and Chinese literature for further contextual information, and has conducted a literature review of studies on similar pictures produced in Southeast Asia in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. [Objectives 2-4] The PI has analyzed the images together with the primary and secondary sources. The John Bradby Blake’s papers have given her much hints about how the Cantonese craftsmen learnt the techniques required for conducting natural history drawings. Visits of museums’ collections show that most drawings were drawn on European paper with watercolours, although Chinese pigments and brushes might also be applied. Most of the paintings, especially the John Bradby Blake’s and John Reeves’ collections, were drawn from nature, although a comparison with the Southeast Asian collections show that copies from existing drawings and prints did exist. [Objective 5] The PI has published four journal articles and one book with the support of the grant. One English article discusses the English-Chinese environment against which the Chinese in Canton made a living by being in-between persons on a daily basis. One Chinese article (and its English version, co-authored with a RA) discusses the application of lithography in late 19th and early 20th century China. This is an extension of her previous findings about how lithography was applied on reproducing botanical drawings in the late Qing. Another Chinese article examines how “grana” (cochineal from South America) was applied on dyeing Chinese silk in Canton and how the term was transliterated into Cantonese against the backdrop of interregional trade. Her recently published book contains a long chapter in which John Bradby Blake’s papers are more thoroughly examined. [Objective 6] With the materials she has collected, the PI is drafting a manuscript for an illustrated monograph she is planning to publish. [Objective 7]

11672416.label: Major findings and research outcome
11672416.value: Major Findings include the followings: (1) The Blake’s papers are especially helpful in providing useful textual evidences for understanding the production of botanical drawings. The PI now has a better idea about what instructions English naturalists might have given to Chinese artists, how dissections of plants were made; and what Chinese references Chinese assistants might have used. Moreover, the Blake’s paper is hitherto the only source materials read by the PI in which the full name of a Chinese artist commissioned by English naturalists is found. (2) Literature review and two visits to the National Museum of Singapore also strengthened the PI’s assumption that an exchange of botanical drawing knowledge existed among the Chinese artists working in Canton and Southeast Asia. In other words, copies upon copies existed in the circulation of botanical illustration knowledge in a wider region of the South Sea due to exchanges among EIC personnel. (3) Markings found on some of the pictures seen at the Botany Library at Harvard University demonstrates what instructions and comments the commissioners might have made. The average quality of this collection also hints the possible existence of the presence of a stock picture market side by side with the more high-quality commissioned products. Moreover, studies on “grana” helps explain meaning of the Cantonese-transliterated term “Nga-lan” written on the back of some of the paintings the PI saw in Harvard. (4) All these findings are helpful for the PI to reconsider the overall theme of her project. She realizes that different forms of “copy” existed, deriving from both Chinese and Western traditions, in the process of producing botanical drawings in 18th and 19th century. This is how the tentative title of the monography – “Copying Nature, Copying Cultures” comes about. Research outcomes: The PI has published four journal articles and one book with the support of the grant. One English article discusses the English-Chinese environment against which the Chinese in Canton made a living by being in-between. One Chinese article (and its English version) discusses the application of lithography in late 19th and early 20th century China. This is an extension of her previous findings about how lithography was applied on reproducing botanical drawings in the late Qing. Another Chinese article examines how “grana” (cochineal from South America) was applied on dyeing Chinese silk in Canton. Her recently published book contains a long chapter in which John Bradby Blake’s papers are thoroughly examined.

11672416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11672416.value: The PI is writing a monograph with the materials she has collected. Tentatively titled “Copying Nature, Copying Cultures”, the monograph will be composed of six chapters discussing early Chinese botanical drawings commissioned by EIC in Amoy and later in Canton; the templates, paper, pens and pigments applied; how copies were copied by Chinese artists; how lithography was applied in the late 19th century on reproducing copies of botanical drawings. The concluding chapter will discuss how this particular genre of botanical drawings might have left an impact on South China school of painting. It has to be noted that despite the fact that the PI has identified the right samples for publication purposes, she is not able to apply for reproduction and copy-right clearance in 2020, the last year of her project, as most museums, especially the reproduction units, were closed due to the pandemic last year. As a result, the part of the funding particularly retained for this purpose is left unused. The PI has to look for other sources of funding to serve this purpose in the future.

11672416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11672416.value: Examining the botanical and zoological illustrations conducted by Chinese craftsmen under the direction of British traders from the late eighteenth through the mid-nineteenth century, this project contributes to the fields of China studies by developing new methodologies for studying Sino-Western exchanges through a blended examination of material cultures and textual archives. The significance of the project lies in the uses of newly found archives which helped the PI answer a series of questions critical to the understanding of the productions of this unique genre of paintings. John Bradby Blake’s papers collected at the Oak Spring Garden Foundation reveals what instructions British naturalists might have given to the Chinese artists early in the 18th century. A comparative perspective applied onto the Southeast Asian collection reveals that copies and templates were applied, suggesting a circulation of knowledge and techniques existed not only between Chinese and Westerners but also among the Chinese craftsmen who moved around in a wider area. The project has also delivered an in-depth study of the Chinese assistants hired by John Bradby Blake in Canton, presenting a more vivid picture of Sino-Western exchanges in the pre-Opium War days and offering a possibly alternative view of Modern Chinese history.

11672616.label: Project Objectives
11672616.value: To survey defamation litigation involving news media in China from 1985 to 2013. We will collect available DADs on the media-related defamation cases and analyze how the remedies, or lack of remedies, of reputation change over time and vary across regions, issues and courts. To examine what factors affect court decisions on the worthiness of reputation. We pay attention to how the court defines reputation in relation to a specific community. We will identify key features of communities, and we will analyze how the prices of reputation vary by different types of communities. To investigate the relations between the media and the court in China and to discuss how such relations affect the institutional process of constructing, or deconstructing, social justice in a transitional society. We will articulate its implications on the overall social transition in China.
