11672616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11672616.value: 摘 要 随着商业媒体和互联网的发展，中国名誉侵权案件数量激增，特别是针对媒体的诽谤诉讼。尽管这类社会学的诉讼揭示了社会对名誉的理解，却鲜有解读名誉侵权案件的实证研究。诽谤法的制定是为了实现社会对于防止和补救名誉侵害的需求（Post 1986）。与性格—— 一个人拥有的 真正的个人本质——不同，名誉体现了一个人的社会形象（Veeder 1904）。如同个人是个体在社会中的投射一样，名誉的本质具有社会属性：它反映了特定社会中人与人之间的关系（ Anderson 1984; Bellah 1986; Skolnick 1986）。作为对关系利益的损害，名誉侵权需要结合个人在他/她的社群中所形成的名声进行判断。正是名誉这一社会属性，使得确定损害大小和对此损害的公平赔偿显得异常困难。法庭不得不面对一个棘手的问题：如何为无价的名誉定价。 此外，确定一个人名誉的赔偿的困难还根植于这样一个事实： 即诽谤案件不仅仅牵涉名誉而已。正如纽约时报诉苏利文案件（New York Times vs. Sullivan）中所显示，在这类诉讼中言论自由受到威胁。在现代民主社会，法学家和记者使用“寒蝉效应”这一修辞来显示法院判决对媒体的影响（Barendt, Lustgarten, Norrie & Stephenson 1997; Bezanson, Cranberg & Soloski 1987; Dent & Kenyon 2004; Franklin 1986; Schauer 1978; Tushnet 2014）。如何寻求个人名誉与言论自由这一宪法权利之间的平衡，决定了法院和媒体的角色。这一情形在专制和过渡时期的国家变得更为复杂，因为这些政权试图通过诽谤诉讼来压制言论自由和控制媒体（Chen 2004; Goodroad 1998; Hao & Zhang 1996; Liebman 2006; Stockmann 2013; Stockmann & Gallagher 2011; Xu 2009; Zahralddin-Aravena 1998）。从这个意义上说，媒体与法院的关系为一个特定社会中个人名誉的价值设置了参考标准 。 不幸的是，大多数已有的针对诽谤的研究没有提及名誉赔偿的数额。很少有研究揭示了什么因素会影响法院作出个人名誉侵权赔偿的判决，以及如何进行赔偿。法院是如何界定个人名誉所存在社群的边界范围？社群的边界范围又在多大程度上会影响个人或组织的名誉赔偿？法院的决定是否会随着时间、事件、地区、法院界别的改变而变化？这些数据又如何揭示特定社会中的社会关系的本质？ 为了回答这些问题，本研究旨在分析法院针对媒体相关诽谤案件的裁判文书。最近几年，中国的很多法院都开始把它们的裁判文书公布出来，相伴而生的是提供关键词搜索功能的法律数据库。一份典型的裁判文书内容包括：诉讼当事人、代表或代表律师、个人诉讼当事人所述机构、争议事件和诉讼结果。因此，裁判文书能够很好的显示法院判决的内在逻辑。通过搜集和分析从1985年至2013年发生在中国的控告媒体的名誉侵权案件，我们将探究名誉和社群在中国社会的定义，进而研究什么因素会影响法院对名誉赔偿的判决。我们的研究将对于名誉的社会本质提供细致入微的洞见，并且揭示在专制体制中名誉与社群的关系。即便我们的研究聚焦中国，但是我们相信这一研究将为针对其他国家名誉侵权的比较研究提供可靠的依据。

11673316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11673316.value: 此研究針對廣東話產生中對語音的提取及加工過程。廣東話是華南的主要方言。此研究包括三個採用圖詞干擾命名範式的實驗，以研究音段(次音節與音節單位)與超音段(聲調)訊息在廣東話單字詞產生中的加工過程。廣東話被試需要對每幅單獨呈現的圖片作出即時命名並要忽略伴隨圖片的干擾字詞。圖片與干擾字詞會同時呈現。圖片與干擾字詞之間的語音關係會是此研究的一個重要變項，而此變項已被證實與語音加工步驟息息相關。更重要的是，此研究會同時記錄被試在作業期間的腦電信息。此研究的結果有兩個重要的理論貢獻，一者關於現時主要從非聲調語發展出的語言產生理論的普世性，二者關於使用聲調語中的特殊性。應用方面，此研究的結果將對改善聲調語使用者的發音，以及對聲調語的教學提供重要啟示。此外，基於其高時間分辨率，腦電信息將能提供有關音段與超音段訊息在廣東話產生中更清晰的時程變化資料，對了解聲調語言產生中的神經機制有著重要的啟示。

11673316.label: Realisation of objectives
11673316.value: The four project objectives listed above have been achieved with the support received and under the time frame proposed. Three experiments were carried out to investigate how segmental and tonal information are processed in Cantonese speech production using the picture-word interference task together with concurrent recording of event-related brain potentials. Findings from this project have also stimulated follow up research work on closely related issues under the same topic. Details are listed below. Objective 1: Participants’ picture naming responses were faster when the target and distractor shared the same syllable (with or without the same tone) relative to an unrelated control. A weaker priming effect was found when the target and distractor shared the same sub-syllabic components (e.g., syllable body and rhyme) only. In addition, both behavioural and electrophysiological data from this project indicate that the effect of syllable priming appeared earlier in time than that of sub-syllabic priming. These results suggest that both syllabic (i.e., segmental/atonal syllable) and sub-syllabic units are important in Cantonese phonological encoding and that syllable retrieval precedes sub-syllabic encoding in Cantonese spoken word production. Objective 2: Null effects on participants’ picture naming latencies were found when the target and distractor shared the same lexical tone only relative to an unrelated control. A similar null effect was evident in the EEG data in the tone alone overlap condition. However, the effect of tone was shown upon segmental overlap. The priming effect observed in the segmental syllable + tone overlap condition was significantly larger than that in the segmental syllable alone overlap condition. A similar non-additive pattern of results was observed in the EEG data prior to the articulatory response. These results indicate that tone has a unique role to play in Cantonese speech production and its realization depends on the availability of segmental contents. Objective 3: Significant effects on the EEG data were found when the target and distractor shared the same segmental syllable, relative to an unrelated control, starting from the time window of 190-250 ms post-stimulus onset. Similar effects on the EEG data were observed in a sub-syllabic overlap condition in the later time windows starting from 250-370 ms post-stimulus onset, indicating that syllable retrieval precedes sub-syllabic encoding in Cantonese phonological encoding with about 60 to 120 ms. Furthermore, as shown by our EEG data, a significantly larger priming effect was found in the syllable + tone related condition relative to the syllable alone related condition, but this difference was observed in the late time windows, suggesting a late locus (e.g., phonetic encoding stage) of tonal processing in Cantonese speech production. Objective 4: Two approaches have been adopted to analyze the EEG data obtained, namely stimulus-locked analysis and response-locked analysis. The former analyzes the EEG data time-locked to the stimulus onset (which is sensitive to the early stage of processing) and the latter analyzes the EEG data time-locked to the participant’s naming response (which is sensitive to the late stage of processing). Electrophysiological correlates associated with syllable/ segmental encoding were shown by using the stimulus-locked analysis whereas those associated with tonal encoding were found by using the response-locked analysis.

11673316.label: Major findings and research outcome
11673316.value: 1) Both segmental syllable and sub-syllabic units have their own representations and are legitimate processing units in Cantonese phonological encoding, consistent with our previous findings (Wong & Chen, 2008; 2009; 2015). Furthermore, both behavioural and EEG data of the current project show that tone has a unique role to play and its realization depends on the availability of segmental contents in Cantonese spoken word production (Wong et al., 2019; in preparation). 2) In terms of the time course of processing, the present EEG data show that syllable retrieval precedes sub-syllabic encoding with around 60 to 120 ms in Cantonese phonological encoding, indicating that the first selectable phonological unit (i.e., primary phonological unit) in Chinese speech production is not individual phoneme but the entire segmental syllable (findings reported in Wong et al., 2019; and see also Wang, Wong et al., 2017, as listed in Part C, for convergent findings). These results suggest that the primary phonological unit is language-specific which may vary across languages with different phonological systems. This is a novel finding challenges the existing prominent models of language production which generally assume that phonemes are the primary phonological units in phonological planning. 3) Furthermore, two data-analysis approaches (i.e., stimulus-locked and response-locked) were used to track the time course of segmental and tonal encoding in Cantonese speech production. Effects associated with segmental processing were shown by using the stimulus-locked analysis whereas the effects associated with tonal encoding were only shown by using the response-locked analysis (i.e., 300 ms prior to the naming response). These results suggest a relatively late locus of tonal encoding (which probably overlaps with phonetic encoding) in Cantonese speech production (Wong et al., in preparation). 4) In addition, by using the conventional picture-word interference task with concurrent recording of EEG signals, the relative time course of semantic and phonological processing in Chinese speech production was examined. Our EEG data indicate an early and robust semantic effect and a relatively late phonological effect in Chinese spoken word production (Wong et al., 2017). These results are consistent with the general assumption that semantic processing precedes phonological encoding in language production.

11673316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11673316.value: Findings of this project have provided important insights for the future development of research on language production. This project has offered evidence (with tangible research outputs) showing that this can be a promising approach by combining a conventional speech production task with concurrent recording of EEG signals to reveal the fine-grained temporal dynamics of the cognitive processes prior to overt speech production. Furthermore, this line of research and the newly developed methodology can potentially be applied to bilingual or even multilingual speech production. It is still largely unknown regarding how the different languages possessed by bilingual or multilingual speakers would interact with each other over the course of L1 or L2 speech production. For the proposed course of action, this research idea has been developed into a GRF research proposal and was awarded in the 2018-19 exercise (on-going).

11673316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11673316.value: This project was conducted to investigate how phonological information (e.g., syllables, sub-syllabic units, and tones) is retrieved and processed in Cantonese spoken word production by using the picture-word interference task with concurrent recording of the event-related brain potential (i.e., ERP, which reflects the speaker’s temporal brain activities). Our findings suggest that in Cantonese speech production, the entire segmental syllable is retrieved first prior to sub-syllabic encoding. Furthermore, our electrophysiological data suggest that tone is processed at a late stage of Cantonese phonological encoding. These findings refute the assumption postulated in many existing models of language production that phonemes are the first selectable (or primary) phonological units in speech planning. Conversely, our findings suggest that the primary phonological units in language production are language-specific. In addition, this study provides novel evidence showing the time course of tonal encoding and how tone is processed together with segmental information in tonal language production, issues that were largely unknown before. In terms of methodology advancement, this project shows that it is effective to investigate the cognitive mechanisms underlying language production by combining a conventional speech production task with concurrent ERP recording.

11673616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11673616.value: This project traces the formation and development of Cantonese film culture from Chinese cinema’s transition to sound filmmaking during the 1930s to the golden age of Cantonese cinema in the early 1960s. Tracking sound and the Cantonese dialect as salient factors in vernacular Chinese film culture, it studies critically the political and artistic articulations of Cantonese talkies in their negotiations with regional identity and nationhood, entertainment and politics, film art and audience reception. The study coins the notion of ‘Cantophone cinema’ as an alternative to the conventional understanding of Cantonese cinema as narrow, indigenous, and Hong Kong-based. It encourages thinking of Cantophone cultures and identities as plural and dynamic by mapping the changing production and reception contexts of this cinema in Hong Kong, Guangzhou, and Shanghai, and in the overseas Chinese communities of Southeast Asia and North America. The politics of soundscapes and dialectal variation in film provides a lens with which to explore the production, circulation, and consumption of Cantonese cinema in its Guangdong–South China and Southeast Asian contexts within the multi-dialectal environment of filmmaking in mid-century Hong Kong cinema. The early history of Cantonese film has been little explored. The politics of sound and dialects provide a focus through which to examine its audiovisual dynamics and sociopolitical meanings. First, what does a transregional inquiry into the variant production and reception contexts of Cantonese-language films tell us about the histories and meanings of Cantophone cinema within the diasporic Chinese communities? Second, what is at stake when engaged filmmakers align their commercial cinema with the call for national progress and political idealism? Finally, how did the politics of sound—dialectal utterance, phonic accent, music, and opera singing—create the intergeneric qualities of Cantophone cinema and so its aesthetic appreciation? The PI and Co-I’s will conduct archival research, biographical studies, and textual reading of representative film texts and literature, mining visual and historical materials in Hong Kong, Guangzhou, Singapore, and North America to map out the distribution and reception of Cantonese-language films in various reception contexts and communities and to analyze its politics and art over time and across place. The project will culminate in a conference that invites international scholars to study the art and politics of Cantonese cinema in the context of sound filmmaking and in a number of academic articles and an edited conference volume as an outcome of the research and the conference. 本計劃研究粵語電影文化，追溯從20世紀30年代的有聲粵語電影以至60年代初的發展，涉及方言和聲音對中國電影文化的影響，並研究其地方性的特徵和民族性，大眾娛樂，政治，電影藝術等的闢係。這項研究的嘗試以’Cantophone’電影概念作為一種更廣義的”粵語電影” 觀念，鼓勵多元文化和身份的思考，詳細考評粵語電影文化在香港，廣州和上海的複雜生產網絡，以及東南亞和北美的海外中國華人社群對粵語的電影認受。

11673616.label: Realisation of objectives
11673616.value: 1. Reconstructing the transnational connections of early Cantonese-language films and their receptions and meanings for different Chinese communities a) The PI successfully hired a full-time researcher (Sabrina Yunzhu TAO) to conduct systematic research work both in Hong Kong and in the Guangzhou provincial archive. Tao fulfilled her research duties by looking into historical materials about developments of and debates on Cantonese cinema, esp. during 1940s and 50s. These materials were collected from libraries and archives and online databases. Tao also went up to Guangzhou to look at the municipal archive, and she managed to collect some important sources about early Cantonese films. (b) In March-April 2019, the PI visited the New York State Archive that has a fairly comprehensive license records and scripts of imported Chinese-language films between 1927 and 1965 (because of the US government’s censorship policy on all foreign films shown in the country). The PI successfully discovered a wealth of US records of Chinese-language and Cantonese cinemas about their projections and receptions in North America. During the trip the PI also visited US National Archives II in Maryland/D.C. to uncover historical materials Hong Kong and China. These research activities has prepared for a solid ground for a transregional inquiry into the variant production and reception contexts of Cantonese-language films for us to understand the histories and meanings of Cantophone cinema to the diasporic Chinese communities. 2. Examining how national politics and marketism affected the ethics and aesthetics of Cantonese filmmaking and individual filmmakers and groups The PI and his student helpers have studied film columns in old newspapers and film journals available in databases and some hard copies at the Hong Kong Film Archive. Combining with the study of individual films, historical events, and filmmakers, the PI could write research papers to elaborate the matrix of national politics, regionalism, and the aesthetic performance of the Cantonese cinema. 3. Elaborating the art of film sound, genres, and adaptations, and the fusion of theater and screen in constituting the distinctive style and identity of Cantophone cinema The PI has published quite a number of research articles and conference papers to elaborate the above artistic performance of Cantophone cinema. More, a Chinese book manuscript is done and it is set to be reviewed and go to print by the Chunghwa Bookstore in Hong Kong. Inadequacy: Due to the pandemic and the previous social unrest, the bookstore has delayed the publication plan. But it will go to print in mid-2021 as the publisher promised.

11673616.label: Major findings and research outcome
11673616.value: Referring to the publication records in Part C, I have successfully produced quite a number of English and Chinese articles at various venues of Europe, Asia, and mainland China. These works cover the topics of censorship, cultural expression and repression in ghost narratives, reception of Shanghai cinema in postwar Hong Kong, early Cantonese cinema in the 1930s, regionalism and nationalism in Cantophone cinema. Some major findings were done at the New York State Archive where the PI successfully discovered a wealth of US records of Chinese-language and Cantonese cinemas about their projections and receptions in North America. The PI will be presenting these materials in an upcoming conference in January 2021 held by the Hong Kong Film Archive on the early histories of Cantonese / Hong Kong cinema during the 1930s and 40s.

11673616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11673616.value: a) The PI will use the materials in the New York State Archive to present a paper on early Cantonese cinema in US reception in a conference held by the Hong Kong Film Archive (「從無聲到有聲——三、四十年代香港電影研討會」) in January 9–10, 2021. b) The PI is submitting in the coming GRF application which will extend the study of transnational reception of Chinese-language cinemas in Southeast Asia. c) The PI will consider in the future the Lord Wilson Heritage Trust to turn these Cantonese film materials into documentation. d) My Chinese monograph on the development of Chinese-language cinema will be published by the Chunghwa Bookstore in Hong Kong in 2021.

11673616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11673616.value: This project examines Cantonese cinema and its historical evolution since the advent of sound cinema in the 1930s. Taking sound, music, and dialect as the important but often undervalued factors of Cantonese film culture, I am concerned about how Cantonese cinema, as the most sustainable tradition of dialect cinemas, engaged historically in negotiations with Chinese national politics and Cantonese regional identities. There was a strong Chinese national interest in censoring the growth of Cantonese film and denouncing the vibrant dialect film as culturally inferior. The project has enlightened us to look at the aesthetics of sound—dialectal utterance, phonic accent, music, and opera singing. I ponder how soundscapes, technologies, and dialectal variations in film provide a lens to look at entertainment and politics, film art and audience reception. On the basis of the project, the PI and researchers in the future can present the histories, culture, and art of the Cantonese cinema to the public as valuable forms of cultural heritage.

11674116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11674116.value: This project aims to shed light on the dynamics of online opinion leadership by comparing user influence on social media (i.e., Twitter and Sina Weibo) with well-validated survey-based measures of social influence. The aim is to assess whether the analysis of social media data—specifically, network analysis and content-based analysis, could provide feasible alternatives to the traditional survey-based measures. Our aim is also to understand any potential differences between real-world opinion leadership and that exercised on social media. The findings generated by this project will have a significant impact in the fields of communication, political science, psychology, and marketing as they will bring fresh, methodologically robust insights about opinion leadership within social media ecosystems in China and the United States, two of the World's largest economies. 這個研究項目旨在利用經驗證之媒體影響力調查測量方法比較社交媒體 - Twitter和新浪微博用戶之影響力, 從而闡明線上意見領袖之動態分析。 目的是評估社交媒體數據分析(即網路分析及內容分析)是否能夠有效替代以調查為基礎的傳統研究方案。 研究目的是探討意見領袖的影響力在現實環境與社交媒體中之潛在差別。 有關研究發現將就全球兩個最大經濟體- 中國和美國的社交媒體生態中的意見領袖分析帶來新穎和方法學上有力的見解, 從而在傳媒、政治科學、心理學和市場範疇帶來顯著 的影響。

11674116.label: Realisation of objectives
11674116.value: The originally proposed objectives of the study were not fully achieved, due to the problems encountered with the social media data collection part of the study. Still, the project has generated two significant journal publications and four conference papers. The PI has shifted the focus of the project to a study of opinion leadership in general, and re-focused some efforts on its relationship with environment engagement in China. A paper focused on the original objectives has been presented in 2019 and is currently under preparation for submission to a journal, so that the expected valorization of the project would be 3 journal publications. Regarding the problems encountered, the main issue was a significant change in the public availability of social media data that happened in the middle of the project (2018). In light of the changes in the technical and legal regimes governing the collection of social media data in both the United States and China, we were unable to collect all the data as planned and the collection process took far longer than originally estimated. Specifically, in the United States, following the scandal surrounding Cambridge Analytica’s unethical use of social media data in 2018, the service providers were unwilling to collect both survey and social media data (or any other personally identifiable data) due to privacy concerns. Furthermore, most of the survey respondents we recruited were also not willing to provide their social media account information (around 90% did not provide their Twitter profile). In China, the respondents recruited were mainly willing to provide their social media account information (i.e Weibo profile), but a range of unannounced changes to the application programming interface (API) severaly limited the data collection process. More specifically, data from the Weibo users with more than 200 followers could not be collected and the process of data collection was very slow and labor intensive. Still, the team managed to collect both survey and social media data for almost 90% of initial respondents. Although this allowed us to conduct a study of Chinese users, the comparison with the U.S. dataset would not be feasible given a huge difference in the social media data availability between the two research locales. The PI was still able to achieve good valorization by using the resources and the data collected for the project. More specifically, as a part of the literature review, we meta-analyzed a large number of studies focusing on social media predictions and published this as a paper in a reputable journal. Furthermore, a study examining opinion leadership and citizen engagement in China based on the survey data was also conducted in published in a journal in 2019, while another one, focused on the U.S. is currently in preparation for submission after being presented at a conference as a poster.

11674116.label: Major findings and research outcome
11674116.value: In our study of Chinese social media users, we analyzed the relationship between self-reported opinion leadership and the measures of network centrality derived from Weibo users’ digital trace data. The analyses show that. while in general the Weibo users have substantially correlated in-degree and out-degree centralities, the positive relationship is particularly high among those scoring high on self-reported opinion leadership scale. It suggests that on the Chinese microblog, people who perceive themselves to be influential tend to be hubs in their local networks as well. Furthermore, betweenness centrality has a more pronounced positive relationship with self-reported opinion leadership in less dense networks than in the more dense ones. It indicates influence on Weibo may be perceived as the ability to transmit information in the form of simple contagion. In initial findings based on the United States data suggests that in our ego-network data, the in-degree centrality (number of followers) and the out-degree centrality (number of following friends) were highly correlated. Furthermore, the eigenvector centrality, indicating the influence of a node in the network, was significantly correlated with the density of the network for the MTurk participants—an increased network size acting to decrease the influence of the egos in the network. However, in line with recent studies, we found that user’s eigenvector centrality had a weak, non-significant relationship with self-reported measures of leadership, and that the number of followers and followees on Twitter were similarly not significantly associated with the self-reported opinion leadership. Our study based on survey data collected in China, examined predictors of environmental engagement among Chinese citizens, paying particular attention to their leadership qualities and their news and social media use. We find that self-perceived opinion leadership, news media use, and Weibo use are all significant predictors of environmental engagement, partially mediated by environmental knowledge. We also explore interactions between opinion leadership and media use, showing differential impacts of news and social media use on environmental knowledge and engagement in China. More specifically, we find that the use of social media benefits people with higher levels of opinion leadership, widening the knowledge and participation gap between them and those who are lower in leadership qualities. In contrast, the use of news media narrows the gap in environmental knowledge and engagement, allowing citizens who do not perceive themselves to be opinion leaders to catch up with those who do. We also conducted a similar study using the U.S. survey data, finding a significant effect of opinion leadership on environmental engagement, mediated by Twitter use and psychological variables, such as environmental knowledge and environmental interest. Finally, we report the findings from a meta-analysis examining the predictive power of social media data by focusing on various sources of data and different methods of prediction: (1) sentiment analysis, and (2) analysis of structural features. Our results, based on the data from 74 published studies, show significant variance in the accuracy of predictions, which were on average behind the established benchmarks in traditional survey research. In terms of the approaches used, the study shows that machine learning-based estimates are generally superior to those derived from pre-existing lexica, and that a combination of structural features and sentiment analyses provides the most accurate predictions. Furthermore, our study shows some differences in the predictive power of social media data across different levels of political democracy and different electoral systems.

11674116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11674116.value: The project has initiated a new stream of research that looking into the role of opinion leadership (online and offline) and environmental engagement in the United States and China, which resulted in one SSCI journal publication and one conference poster at a renowned international conference (in preparation for the submission to a journal). A related project was funded in 2019 by the Environmental and Conservation Fund (ECF Project 114/2018) and is expected to generate direct input for the policy-makers and other stakeholders.

11674116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11674116.value: Our study shows that self-reported measures of opinion leadership (i.e. survey-based) are not directly related the key measures of online influence, i.e. the centrality of these individuals in the online spheres such as Weibo. This is in line with the previous research showing that self-designated opinion leaders are not necessarily those with the highest number of connections (e.g. followers) or those with the most central positions in the online networks. Self-perceived opinion leadership is thus indicative of hub-like diffusion behaviors and ability to connect the less well-connected parts of the social media networks in China, which suggests that it may play an important role in civic connectedness. More specifically, we find that the use of social media benefits people with higher levels of opinion leadership, widening the knowledge and participation gap between them and those who are lower in leadership qualities. In contrast, the use of traditional news media narrows the gap in knowledge and engagement, allowing citizens who do not perceive themselves to be opinion leaders to catch up with those who do. The findings have important implications for understanding the concept of opinion leadership in the era of social media and how it affects the participatory potential of ordinary citizens.

11674316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11674316.value: Assessing non-pecuniary damages in a consistent and predictable way is of central interest to tort law research and reform. Mental suffering damages, the equivalent term in Chinese tort law to non-pecuniary damages, are prevalently claimed in medical negligence litigation. Three categories of mental suffering damages may be awarded for medical negligence in China: mental suffering awards to an injured patient for his “pain and suffering” and “loss of amenities”; mental suffering awards to the close relatives of a deceased patient for their “loss of consortium”; and mental suffering awards to a patient whose right to informed consent was infringed but suffered no injury as a consequence. Although the Supreme People’s Court has required lower courts to consider six factors in assessing mental suffering damages, whether and how they consider and weigh these factors in medical negligence cases remains a mystery. The conflicting local rules on mental suffering damages further diminish the consistency and predictability of the law. Given little literature investigating Chinese judicial practice of awarding mental suffering damages in medical negligence cases, this project will fill the gap through a multi-dimensional research. Specifically, the first part of this project will present a doctrinal dimension through doctrinal research on the inconsistent local rules on mental suffering damages for medical negligence. The second part will supply an empirical dimension through large-scale empirical research to investigate the determinants of the three categories of mental suffering damages by drawing on three datasets to be constructed on judicial decisions of medical negligence cases involving the three categories of mental suffering damages. The third party will explore a legislative dimension through comparative and socio-legal research to offer reform proposals on assessing mental suffering damages for medical negligence so as to promote the consistency and predictability of the law. This project will generate unprecedented empirical findings on Chinese judicial practicing of assessing mental suffering damages for medical negligence and provide socio-legal analysis of the empirical findings. It will present reform proposals on damages assessment to improve Chinese law on mental suffering damages for medical negligence. This project will also, through the case of mental suffering awards, shed light on the exercise of judicial discretion of Chinese courts. 醫療過失案件的原告通常會請求精神損害賠償。依照中國法，醫療過失案件涉及的精神損害可分為三種類別：患者主張的因身体傷害所引發的精神損害；因醫療過失致死患者之近親屬所主張的死亡撫慰金；以及患者基於其知情同意權受侵害而主張的精神損害。儘管最高人民法院要求法官在確定精神損害賠償時須考慮六項因素，但实务中法官是否考慮以及如何在醫療過失案件中衡量這些因素並不明朗；相關的精神損害賠償之地方規則並不協調，亦影響法律的一致性與可預見性。本項目從三個角度研究中國醫療過失案件中的精神損害賠償問題：醫療過失之精神損害賠償的各項地方規則；認定醫療過失三種類別精神損害賠償的司法實務；改善醫療過失之精神損害賠償制度的建議。本項目的研究就醫療過失案件中精神損害賠償提供實證依據與分析以及立法建議，亦有助於深入了解法官在行使司法裁量權的現狀與問題。

11674416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11674416.value: Spatial Augmented Reality (SAR) is the use of projected light to alter the appearance of physical objects. In the last twenty years, SAR has been explored in multiple form factors, and uses. (Bimber and Raskar, 1998) Lately, its simplified commercial form, known as Projection Mapping, has become very popular. (Benko et al., 2014) Interactive SAR has also been explored, and different techniques offering single and multiuser interaction have been proposed. (Benko et al., 2014) However, these projects usually attempt to re-create existing forms of human-computer interaction in a SAR environment, not being able of taking advantage of the complexity and expressiveness of the new medium (Steimle et al., 2013). Existing proposals usually assume that the augmented objects are static, while being able to physically alter the projected surfaces can drastically expand the design possibilities. Arts-inflected research has proved being very successful in creating design alternatives, with artists contributing at keeping things culturally relevant while offering original cognitive approaches. (Brand, 1993) The project proposes using art-infused research to explore new SAR systems that incorporate mutable and unfixed geometry. These systems will be based on flexible and on unfixed screens (starting with elastic screens and screens mounted on drones), and will explore alternative data visualization and interaction designs. Spatial Augmented Reality systems are capable of radically affecting its users’ environment. What are the design strategies that permit a better understanding of the possibilities of augmented environments? What are their aesthetic possibilities and constrains? Adopting a user-centred design (UCD) approach we will examine existing SAR designs identifying their strengths. Selected strategies will be expanded by incorporating mutable geometry, and the results will be tested with small groups of representative users. UCD will allow us to involve users in the design and research processes and to iterate on the proposed interaction designs, ensuring the reliability and reproducibility of the project’s findings. The results will help significantly in the creation of new systems that fully integrate augmented space as a fundamental component. We expect the project to contribute to the current debate about interaction, augmented reality, and new media art, as well as to impact on the industry, specifically on the design of immersive spaces and novel human-computer interaction techniques. The published results, artworks, and videos will be published in the leading international conferences (such as SIGGRAPH, TEI, ISEA), and journals (such as Leonardo, TOCHI, IJMMS).

11674416.label: Realisation of objectives
11674416.value: All the objectives were satisfied. The project explored, implemented, and tested different implementations of Spatial Augmented Reality (SAR) - the use of projected light to alter the appearance of physical objects. Our project focused on exploring new implementations of SAR, focusing on the aesthetic, interactive, and design opportunities if brings. In this context, the appropriation of spatiality, together to SAR’s possible making explicit of some roles that the space can play, becomes a core component of a new interaction and expression medium. Analysing this new medium requires re-thinking the aesthetics and semiotics not only of digital interaction but also of the construction of inhabitable spaces. To further explore the possibilities of SAR, we created different prototypes able to change their properties, to reflect the projected light -thus modifying its environment-, and to respond in real-time to users (interactive SAR). We also investigated how SAR can interact and leverage other digital technologies, in particular we explored which roles can SAR play within Milgram’s “Reality-Virtual Reality continuum, situating our research under the umbrella term of Extended Reality (XR). In this sense we explored mixed setups where SAR and Virtual Reality Collaborated in the creation of richer and more expressive environments. Finally, we focused the use of SAR together with new machine learning powered interactive devices, exploring how SAR can collaborate to their understanding and benefit from intelligent interaction schemas. As planned, we adopted a hybrid approach, including artistic research into the creation of new interaction designs. Knowing that art–infused research helps providing a critique and commentary of otherwise hard to see cultural, social, and technological aspects of technology and design, while helping in keeping the results culturally innovative and relevant, we created and exhibited a series of artworks that allowed us not only to explore aesthetic and design alternatives but also operated as technological prototypes, proof-of-concept, and, more importantly, as testing devices that provided tangible information about the levels of success of the SAR designs. Below we describe the specific results with respect to each of the original objectives: 1 To propose alternative SAR designs that include actuating on the geometry being projected. Different prototypes of flexible and mutable, original, and flexible geometry where developed. Several artworks were created that explored different uses of projection and their combination with other technologies. In particular, the pieces Homs, Memoirs of the Blind and Smile (Exhibited in Korea, Spain, and Japan) have shown alternative interactive possibilities of SAR. 2 To design, develop, and test novel SAR techniques on flexible surfaces, integrating the deformation of the surface. We have explored the aesthetic and interactive properties of flexible screens. After several prototypes, we created and exhibited the artwork Ekphrasis (exhibited in TEI2019 and presented in Artech 2017, and published about in Technarte, TEI, and ISEA) implements a flexible screen that emulates a human body screen. This screen actuated using stepper motors exemplifies the aesthetic and interaction design possibilities that our project discovered. A larger piece with a moving flexible screen has been accepted for exhibition at an art fair in Hong Kong (we are not including this fair in the report as it depends on the covid-19 crisis). The project shows how centrally-controlled deformable allows for a novel exploration of technologically mediated perception as objectification. 3 To design, develop, and test novel SAR techniques on floating or unfixed surfaces, integrating projection screens and unmanned aerial devices. Several prototypes of floating and unfixed surfaces where developed using Parrot Drones and handheld projector. While the designs where successful and opened new doors for interactive moving screens, after several experiments run at the School of Creative Media, we decided to focus on non drone-based setups to reflect the security problems that we identified. The prototypes, however, provided with the technical base (in electronics, control, and projection mapping) that were integrated in the subsequent designs. 4 To explore the semiotics and aesthetics of SAR data visualization and interaction through the creation of interactive artworks. The project produced twenty-two artistic exhibitions, together with numerous internal tests, shows, and prototypes. Several of the pieces explore data visualisation within SAR, researching on the semiotic, politic, ethic, and artistic axes of data representation and ownership. 5 To disseminate results of the research in journal articles and conference presentations, as well as on a website for participants and general public. In addition to the exhibitions, publications, and presentations described in part c, we created public webpages for the projects Door, Box, Smile, Memoirs of the Blind, Awkward Consequence, Homs, Ekphrasis, Extraordinary Accident. 11674416.label: Major findings and research outcome
11674416.value: The project was successful in opening uncharted territory in the incorporation of SAR technologies in artistic production, as well as on the creation of novel interaction designs that incorporate SAR as a core component. As listed in Part C, the project yielded one journal publication, ten conference proceedings publications, and twenty-two artistic exhibitions. The project was able to explore the potential long-term impact of a successful application of Spatial Augmented Reality, in particular, it showed it has the ability of affecting the users’ environment, while contextualizing computational applications. A particularly relevant finding of the project is the suitability of Spatial Augmented Reality to leverage other interactive technologies providing a fruitful environment for digital interaction and artistic expression. The project was able to successfully integrate our SAR system with virtual reality applications, EEG-based brain-computer interfaces, and, perhaps most importantly, machine learning backed systems. The artworks and prototypes developed allowed the researchers to explore the social and technological implications of the adoption of SAR and AI technologies, using SAR we were able to explore contemporary relevant topics such as data ownership, privacy, and surveillance. In addition, as planned, we explored alternative data visualisation techniques, focusing on the aesthetic and semiotic components, and successfully translating these explorations into exhibited artworks. Finally, we explored the social, political, and ethical impact of this technology, as well as investigating how it can be integrated with other relevant technologies, namely Virtual Reality and Machine Learning. The project’s exhibited artworks effectively constitute a group of prototypes that showcase new applications of SAR, among these we would like to highlight: - Some of the first brain-controlled VR systems that provided a bio-feedback loop that, in turn, affected the projections. ´ - Flexible, centrally controlled surfaces that provided an orthogonal axis of data expression, augmenting and reconverting the semiotics of the screen. - Machine learning backed interactive systems that explored non-verbal communication, as well as the political significance of these new technologies. These, together with the rest of the project’s production constitute a significant body of work that effectively paves the road for future research.

11674416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11674416.value: The project can be further developed in several directions. We propose to focus on the addition of artificial intelligence to the augmented objects. This would allow for the creation of highly interactive, responsive, and flexible SAR setups that would benefit from the accelerated pace of innovation in AI. In effect, machine learning algorithms find complex relationships in data, recognising patterns that humans may not be able to identify, or not know how to formally express for explicit rule–based programming. This allows to create machine learning systems with unpredictable, yet somehow controllable behaviour using training datasets. While artistic uses of machine learning and SAR have been explored, the incorporation of machine learning into a semi-automated augmentation process remains unexplored and offers extraordinary potentialities.

11674416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11674416.value: Augmented Reality (AR) is a popular research topic, with potential direct impact in all aspects of human life. However, there has never really been a widely accepted “killer application” for AR, on the contrary, AR technologies and systems remain in artificial settings. In this project we designed and implemented new setups of Spatial Augmented Reality (SAR, the use of projected light to modify existing objects) which allowed us to develop highly original artworks, data visualization processes, and interaction designs. Our SAR designs included augmented objects that were also controllable by the system, blurring the frontier between physical and digital. With the inclusion of deformable and movable projection surfaces, the project took an important step in the creation of a new interaction language, liberating SAR from the constraints of static geometry. In addition, the project strongly contributed on the discussion of the role that SAR systems may play in future society, providing tangible prototypes of SAR systems that impacted both in terms of interaction design and in the exploration of its aesthetics. Finally, the project developed both prototypes and artworks that explored how SAR may exist in the future when integrated with other relevant technologies, namely Virtual Reality and Machine Learning.

11674716.label: Realisation of objectives
11674716.value: All objectives have been achieved. A large number of important ecological art projects in China since 1989 were identified and documented. An open online database (ecoartasia.net) has been built to host audiovisual materials of these projects. The database is organized by artists/ collectives. They are Liang Shaoji (梁绍基), Xu Tan (徐坦), Sazi (萨子), Shen Piji (沈丕基), Mao Chenyu (毛晨雨), Cheng Xinhao (程新皓), Gao Ling (高灵), Jin Lipeng (靳立鹏), Ren Ri (任日), Chen Youtong (陈友桐), Brother Nut (坚果兄弟), Cao Minghao and Chen Jianjun (曹明浩和陈建军), Lijiang Studio (丽江工作室), and Mind Fiber (心丝组合). These artists work in Beijing, Zhejiang, Hunan, Guangdong, Sichuan, and Yunnan. They use a wide range of artistic media, including photography, film, installation, sound, performance, and social practice. Their artworks address topics such as water, land, agriculture, pollution, animals (silkworms and bees), plants, and microbes. Narrative essays have been written on each artist / collective. A book-length, bilingual manuscript based on the narrative essays has been prepared and will be submitted to an academic publisher for review.

11674716.label: Major findings and research outcome
11674716.value: Major findings: The ecological art projects documented in this research project occurred in different parts of China and took many different forms, but they shared a common set of concerns: they all addressed real and pressing ecological issues and aimed to effect change. They all emphasized the importance to consider humans as part of nature, not outside and above nature. The main issues addressed by these ecological art projects include air pollution, land and water use, and affective relations with many forms of life. Many artists took an interdisciplinary approach, collaborating with biologists and geologists. They also worked with shamanic and indigenous traditions, reactivating festivals and rituals that invoke more-than-human sentiments. In addition to creating object-based works, several artists adopted social practice techniques to raise public awareness on environmental degradation. Many artists worked intensively with nonhumans: Liang Shaoji with silkworms, Shen Piji with frogs, Ren Ri with bees, and Chen Youtong with microbes. Their practices demonstrate interspecies dependency and care, and envision an alternative future where humans and nonhumans create art together. Research outcome: An open online database (ecoartasia.net) of key contemporary ecological art projects by Chinese artists has been built. It contains over 1,000 high-resolution images. A book-length, bilingual manuscript based on fourteen narrative essays has been prepared and will be submitted to an academic publisher for review.

11674716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11674716.value: Ecological art practices continue to develop in China. I will continue to follow this field and conduct further research in a few years.

11674716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11674716.value: This research project documents key ecological art practices in Mainland China from 1989 to 2019. It articulates the strategies that Chinese artists have developed to address pressing ecological issues ranging from pollution to intraspecies collaboration. It presents a comprehensive study of an important field of Chinese contemporary art.

11675716.value: To develop a process model to better understand important factors and mechanisms underlying social enterprises’ performance. 11675716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11675716.value: Launched in the late 1970s, the political agenda to “roll back the state”, or the New Public Management (NPM; Hood, 1991) reform movement, saw a reduced role for government (Pollitt and Bouckaert 2004) and increased importance of the non-profit sector. The failure of nonprofit sector (Salamon, 1987) in alleviating social problems effectively, however, suggests an increased need for social enterprises (Eikenberry & Kluver, 2004; Terjesen et al., 2015) as an extension of the government’s arm to provide public services that the state could not otherwise deliver “efficiently” (Defourny et al., 2014). Unfortunately, past research on social enterprises often lacks an empirical angle (Ho & Chan, 2010; Millar & Hall, 2013; Teasdale, 2012; Waddock & Post, 1991) or is still dominated by small Ns and qualitative studies (Defourny & Nyssens, 2010; Millar & Hall, 2013; Galera & Borzaga, 2009; Teasdale, 2012). In contrast, the burgeoning interest in social enterprise (SE) research (Terjesen et al., 2015) suggests that social enterprise research need to go beyond social entrepreneurs’ motivations (Miller et al., 2012), identities (Wry & York, 2015), and the institutional (Pache & Santos, 2013) environments of their organizations. In particular, much research is needed to understand social enterprises’ performance and social impact as well as their implications on public policies and administration. Given the importance of social enterprises as a third-party government (Jung et al., 2015; Salamon, 1987), it is valuable to investigate the impact of both organizational and personal factors on social enterprises’ performance. Thus, this proposal seeks to examine how social entrepreneurs’ passion and compassion will interact with their dominant identity to jointly affect the resources they can obtain, others’ trust on them, and the creativity of their organizations. We propose two complementary studies to test the relationships among these important factors, especially their joint impacts on social enterprises’ performance and social impact. Specifically, the first study will be based on semi-structured exploratory interviews to explore the factors we identify above. The second study will quantitatively test how these factors jointly affect social enterprises’ performance using samples from Hong Kong, Singapore and the UK. Our research will contribute to our understanding of important factors and mechanisms for successful social enterprises. The findings will help public managers to devise appropriate policies to support organizational practices to improve social enterprises’ performance.

12114416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12114416.value: 在骨局部微環境中，行使骨吸收功能的破骨細胞及行使骨形成功能的成骨細胞相互調控並協同工作，從而維繫骨內穩態。其中，成骨細胞對破骨細胞及其骨吸收功能的調控機制已比較明確，多項研究亦顯示破骨細胞可借助雙向信號系統或者自身的跨膜蛋白與成骨細胞進行直接溝通。此外，骨吸收過程中骨基質內釋放的的生長因子亦可促進成骨細胞分化並調控骨形成。儘管如此，目前我們尚不清楚破骨細胞是否可通過“旁分泌”等更高效的調控方式来影響成骨細胞。最新的研究證實，微小核糖核酸可以細胞外泌體包裹的形式從供體細胞分泌出來並在血循環中穩定存在從而介導細胞間的信號傳遞。然而目前尚無研究證實微小核糖核酸亦參與了破骨細胞對成骨細胞及骨形成的調控。 在前期工作中，我們發現成骨細胞內的微小核糖核酸214（miR-214）可抑制骨形成（Wang et al., Nat Med 2013）。我們近期獲得的臨床樣本數據顯示在老齡骨折病人中血清外泌體miR-214水平與骨標本內的骨形成標誌基因(BGLAP)的信使RNA水平呈負相關。在老齡骨質疏鬆小鼠模型中，我們進一步發現在增齡過程中血清外泌體miR-214水平不僅與破骨細胞內的miR-214水平正相關，而且與骨形成能力負相關。我們還發現體外培養的破骨細胞及其培養基上清液內外泌體的miR-214水平遠高於成骨細胞及其培養基上清液內外泌體的miR-214水平。另外，體外研究顯示miR-214可促進破骨細胞的活性，破骨細胞來源的外泌體miR-214可抑制成骨細胞功能 （Li et al., ASBMR Annual Meeting 2014）。我們還成功構建了破骨細胞特異性miR-214過表達（Ctsk／miR-214）小鼠,並開發了一種可靶向破骨細胞的小核酸遞送系統（Liu et al., Biomaterials, 2015，Zhang et al., Nat Med 2012）。此外，我們建立了提取破骨細胞囊泡的穩定方法（Li et al., ASBMR Annual Meeting 2015）。因此，我們假設破骨細胞來源的外泌體miR-214可抑制成骨細胞及骨形成。 我們將從以下四個方面驗證上述假設：（1）運用骨形態計量學及顯微CT檢測Ctsk／miR-214小鼠的骨形成能力及骨結構。（2）運用骨形態計量學、顯微CT及實時螢光定量PCR技術評估破骨細胞靶向遞送miR-214抑制劑對Ctsk／miR-214小鼠的骨形成能力及骨結構的影響。（3）運用骨形態計量學及顯微CT評估Ctsk／miR-214小鼠來源的破骨細胞外泌體對成年小鼠的骨形成能力及骨結構的影響。（4）運用骨形態計量學、顯微CT檢測及實時螢光定量PCR技術評估破骨細胞靶向遞送miR-214抑制劑對老齡小鼠的血清外泌體miR-214水平、骨形成能力及骨結構的影響。 本項目將有助於闡明一種由微小核糖核酸介導的破骨細胞對成骨細胞的全新調控方式。該研究還將為治療成骨能力下降的骨科疾病提供新的靶點。

12114416.label: Realisation of objectives
12114416.value: In the Midterm Progress Report for the period ending 31/03/2018, we reported the realisation of Aim1 and Aim2. We found that the elevated miR- 214- 3p in osteoclasts by genetic approach could result in reduced bone formation, as evidenced by the poorer bone micro structure and lower bone formation rate in Ctsk/miR-214 mice as compared to WT controls. We also found that the reduced bone formation in Ctsk/miR-214mice could be rescued by therapeutic inhibition of miR-214-3p in osteoclasts, as evidenced by the improved bone micro structure and higher lower bone formation rate in Ctsk/miR-214 mice treated with AMO (antagomir-214) as compared to those Ctsk/miR-214 mice without AMO treatment. In the Annual Progress Report for the period ending 31/09/2019, we reported the realisation of Aim3. We found that the exosomal miR-214-3p derived from osteoclasts could inhibit bone formation in vivo, as evidenced by detection of osteoclast-derived exosomes and the elevated miR-214-3p levels in osteoblastic cells in vivo after injection of osteoclast-derived exosomes from Ctsk/miR-214 mice, as well as the poorer bone micro structure and lower bone formation rate in mice treated with osteoclast-derived exosomes from Ctsk/miR-214 mice as compared to those mice treated with osteoclast-derived exosomes from WT mice. In this report, we have realised the Aim4, we found that osteoclast-targeted inhibition of miR-214-3p could promote bone formation to mitigate the aging-related osteoporosis in aged mice, as evidenced by the improved bone micro structure and higher bone formation rate in the AMO-treated aged mice as compared to those mice without AMO treatment.

12114416.label: Major findings and research outcome
12114416.value: In this project, we demonstrated that the osteoclast-derived exosomal miR-214-3p could inhibit bone formation, which suggests that targeting the osteoclastic miR-214-3p could be an anabolic strategy for combating aging-related bone formation reduction in senile osteoporotic individuals. Some of the findings of this project has been published in Nature Communications (Li et al., Nature Communications 2016) after we submitted the proposal of this project. In addition, basing on these findings, we have further developed a loop-Based and AGO-incorporated virtual screening model for targeting AGO-mediated miRNA–mRNA interactions for drug discovery to rescue bone phenotype in the Ctsk/miR-214 mice (Zhuo et al., Advanced Science 2020). The Ctsk/miR-214 mice in this project also facilitate another finding on the contribution of osteoclast-derived exosomal miRNAs in osteoarthritis (Liu et al., ASBMR 2019 Annual Meeting). Another research depicting the role osteoblast in regulating joint inflammation (He et al., EBioMedicine 2019) in rheumatoid arthritis was also partly supported by this project.

12114416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12114416.value: The findings of this project has showcased a previously unknown mechanism of osteoclast-osteoblast crosstalk and the contribution of osteoclast-derived exosomal microRNAs in reduced bone formation during aging. This research also encourage us to focus on the role osteoclast-derived exosomal microRNAs in mediating the bone-cartilage crosstalk in osteoarthritis. Ultimately, it would facilitate the development of novel therapeutic strategy for targeting the osteoclast-derived exosomes for the treatment of bone and joint diseases.

12114416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12114416.value: The current project demonstrated that the exosomal transfer of miR-214-3p from osteoclast to osteoblast could inhibit bone formation, which represents a previously unknown mechanism of osteoclast-osteoblast crosstalk that contribute to the reduced bone formation during aging. It also indicates that targeting osteoclastic miR-214-3p could be a potential anabolic strategy for senile osteoporosis.

12122516.label: Major findings and research outcome
12122516.value: Major findings: During previous research period, we have found that arthritis scores were continuously increased in (DSS)6-liposome-non sense siRNA (hereafter NS) and PBS-treated monkeys, whereas arthritis scores in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys maintained at a low level during 5-week treatment except Monkey 8. For the radiographic examination, we have found CKIP-1 siRNA treatment could alleviate the continuous increase of the PIP radiological score. For the microCT analysis, we have found better organized bony and joint structure in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys compared to NS and PBS-treated monkeys after treatment. The values of bone mineral density (BMD) and relative bone volume (BV/TV) were significantly increased in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys after treatment, whereas such changes were not observed in monkeys treated with NS and PBS (Please refer to 2017 annual report). Further, we have found that the joint inflammation and bone destruction in siRNA-treated monkeys was significantly attenuated than that of NS and PBS-treated monkeys after treatment. The histological score was significantly lower in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys compared to NS and PBS-treated monkeys after treatment. For the bone histomorphometry analysis, we have found a larger width between the two labeling bands in the CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys compared to NS and PBS-treated monkeys after treatment. The values of bone formation parameters mineral apposition rate (MAR) and bone formation rate/bone surface (BFR/BS) were also significantly higher in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys compared to NS and PBS-treated monkeys after treatment (Please refer to 2018 annual report). During this research period, we have found that the level of CKIP-1 mRNA was significantly downregulated in Ocn+ cells of CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys after treatment when compared with NS and PBS-treated monkeys. We have also found that the level of CKIP-1 protein was significantly downregulated in the articular bone from the PIP of CKIP-1 siRNA-treated monkeys after treatment when compared with NS and PBS-treated monkeys. This study further validates the role of CKIP-1 in failure of osteoblast-mediated repair for articular bone erosion in RA and facilitates clinical translation of RNA interference-based therapeutic strategy in RA. 12123716.label: Project Objectives
12123716.value: We will systematically map the HI loci in F1 hybrids by crossing the introgression lines that carry a C. briggsae genomic fragment in an otherwise C. nigoni background we produced previously. We will focus on the introgressions that are inviable as a homozygote or male sterile as a hemizygote. We will develop a total of 50 independent single-copy insertions of transgene expressing a GFP marker in C. nigoni pharynx. The transgene consisting of a fusion between a cbr-myo-2 promoter and GFP will be integrated into C. nigoni chromosome by either miniMos or CRISPR/Cas9 mediated knock-in using Cni-dpy-5 as an injection marker. The GFP reporter will serve as a visible and dominant marker to facilitate the site-directed backcrossing and mapping of HI loci. We will map the transgene insertion site within the above strains to the defined genomic region using single-worm inverse PCR followed by Sanger sequencing, which will lead to a C. nigoni genetic map consisting of the GFP markers with approximately one GFP marker per 3 to 4 million bps. We will cross the GFP-linked C. nigoni genomic fragments into C. briggsae background by repeated backcrossing for at least 15 generations, a process called introgression. We will render the GFP markers homozygous in C. briggsae background whenever possible. We will map the introgression breaking points by single-worm PCR with species-specific primers and confirm the mapping results for all homozygous introgressions and a subset of 10 heterozygous introgressions using Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS). We will systematically characterize the hybrid incompatibilities produced by the GFP-linked C. nigoni genomic fragments in C. briggsae background by scoring the phenotypes of embryonic lethality, larval arrest, fertility and sterility. We will contrast the HI results in mutual directions to identify the asymmetric HI loci between the two species.

12123716.label: Major findings and research outcome
12123716.value: Hybrid male progeny from interspecies crosses are more prone to sterility or inviability than hybrid female progeny, and the male sterility and inviability often demonstrate parent-of-origin asymmetry. However, the underlying genetic mechanism of asymmetric sterility or inviability remains elusive. We previously established a genome-wide hybrid incompatibility (HI) landscape between Caenorhabditis briggsae and C. nigoni by phenotyping a large collection of C. nigoni strains each carrying a C. briggsae introgression. In this study, we systematically dissect the genetic mechanism of asymmetric sterility and inviability in both hybrid male and female progeny between the two species. Specifically, we performed reciprocal crosses between C. briggsae and different C. nigoni strains that each carry a GFP-labeled C. briggsae genomic fragment referred to as introgression, and scored the HI phenotypes in the F1progeny. The aggregated introgressions cover 94.6% of the C. briggsae genome, including 100% of the X chromosome. Surprisingly, we observed that two C. briggsae X fragments that produce C. nigoni male sterility as an introgression rescued hybrid F1 sterility in males fathered by C. briggsae. Subsequent backcrossing analyses indicated that a specific interaction between the X-linked interaction and one autosome introgression is required to rescue the hybrid male sterility. In addition, we identified another two C. briggsae genomic intervals on chromosomes II and IV that can rescue the inviability, but not the sterility, of hybrid F1 males fathered by C. nigoni, suggesting the involvement of differential epistatic interactions in the asymmetric hybrid male fertility and inviability. Importantly, backcrossing of the rescued sterile males with C. nigoni led to the isolation of a 1.1-Mb genomic interval that specifically interacts with an X-linked introgression, which is essential for hybrid male fertility. We further identified three C. briggsae genomic intervals on chromosome I, II, and III that produced inviability in all F1 progeny, dependent on or independent of the parent-of-origin. Taken together, we identified multiple independent interacting loci that are responsible for asymmetric hybrid male and female sterility, and inviability, which lays a foundation for their molecular characterization. The results were published in DNA Research (2018), Nucleic Acids Research (2019), Genetics (2019) and Genome Research (2020). In addition, the project supported three PhD students and six conference abstracts (please see details in Part C). This project

12125116.value: 黑色素瘤是皮膚癌的主要死亡原因。研究表明，黑色素瘤中STAT3（信號轉導子與轉錄激活子3）和TLR4（Toll樣受體4）信號通路的激活，均能促進黑色素瘤的生長、血管生成及轉移。抑制TLR4或STAT3信號通路已被認為是治療黑色素瘤的新策略。白朮為補氣藥，廣泛應用於治療黑色素瘤的中藥複方中。我們的研究表明，從白朮中分離出的白朮內酯II（AT-II）可誘導體外培養的黑色素瘤細胞凋亡，並抑制其增殖和遷移。在無毒的劑量下，AT-II能夠顯著抑制荷瘤小鼠的黑色素瘤生長和轉移。此外，AT-II能抑制小鼠腫瘤及培養的黑色素瘤細胞中STAT3的活性，並在體外抑制細菌脂多糖（LPS, TLR4的特異性配體）誘導的STAT3激活。分子對接實驗提示AT-II可與TLR4/MD-2受體複合物結合。細胞實驗表明，AT-II減少了LPS與TLR4的結合，並且用MPLAs（合成的單磷酰脂質A，TLR4的激動劑）刺激細胞或過表達STAT3C（STAT3的顯著激活形式）可降低AT-II對抗黑色素瘤細胞增殖和侵襲的能力。因此，我們推測抑制TLR4/STAT3信號通路在AT-II抗黑色素瘤中發揮了重要的作用。為了證明這一假設，我們設計以下實驗：1）在黑色素瘤細胞中建立TLR4/STAT3通路；2）探討AT-II是如何抑制黑色素瘤細胞中的TLR4/STAT3信號通路的；3）探討抑制TLR4/STAT3信號通路對AT-II抗黑色素瘤作用的貢獻。本研究結果有助於我們進一步了解AT-II抗黑色素瘤的作用機制，為臨床上用白朮治療黑色素瘤提供化學和藥理學依據，並有助於推動AT-II作為新的抗黑色素瘤藥物的臨床試驗。

12125116.label: Realisation of objectives
12125116.value: The three objectives have been fully achieved. 1. We have established the TLR4/MYD88/STAT3 and TLR4/TRIF/STAT3 pathways and demonstrated their pathogenic roles in melanoma. The obtained results are as follows: 1) TLR4 expression and STAT3 phosphorylation are positively correlated in human melanoma samples (208 samples; provided by Servicebio, Inc., Hubei, China), especially in early-stage (T1N0M0) melanomas. 2) TLR4 ligands activate STAT3 through MYD88 and TRIF in melanoma cells. We found that LPS and MPLAs, two TLR4 ligands, increased the phosphorylation of STAT3 in multiple melanoma cell lines. Knockdown of TLR4, MYD88 or TRIF completely abolished LPS- and MPLAs-enhanced STAT3 phosphorylation. These data indicated that the LPS- and MPLAs-induced STAT3 activation is through TLR4, MYD88 and TRIF in melanoma. 3) TLR4 ligands promote STAT3-mediated cellular events in melanoma progression. We found that MPLAs and LPS, in a similar manner, promoted proliferation and invasion of melanoma cells. We also found that TLR4 signaling in melanoma cells increases the secretion of immunosuppressive cytokines that can be upregulated by STAT3. To examine whether activation of STAT3 is required for the cellular events in TLR4 signaling-mediated melanoma progression, we established a pair of stable cell lines, B16-STAT3β (a line overexpressing a dominant negative STAT3) and B16-NC (the negative control cell line harbouring the empty vector). We found that both LPS and MPLAs significantly increased cell proliferation and invasion in B16-NC cells but not in B16-STAT3β cells, suggesting a critical role of STAT3 activation in TLR4 signaling-caused melanoma progression. 4) Constitutive TLR4 signaling enhances STAT3 activation and promotes melanoma progression in mice. We established a pair of stable cell lines, A375-CA-TLR4 (harbouring a constitutively active variant of TLR4) and A375-NC (the negative control cell line harbouring the empty vector). It was found that protein level of phosphorylated STAT3 and transcriptional activity of STAT3 were higher in A375-CA-TLR4 cells than in A375-NC cells, indicating that constitutive activation of TLR4 enhances STAT3 activation in melanoma cells. EMT-like morphological features, such as losing cell-cell interaction and a spindle-shaped phenotype, were observed in A375-CA-TLR4 cells, suggesting that TLR4 activation promotes EMT in melanoma. In A375-CA-TLR4 and A375-NC xenografts-bearing mouse models, weights of A375-CA-TLR4 xenografts were heavier than those of A375-NC xenografts. Protein levels of total and phosphorylated STAT3 were upregulated in A375-CA-TLR4 tumors. IHC staining of tumor tissues showed that protein levels of Ki-67 (a cell proliferation marker), CD31 (an angiogenic marker), N-cadherin and vimentin (two mesenchymal markers) were increased and E-cadherin (an epithelial marker) was decreased in A375-CA-TLR4 tumors compared to A375-NC tumors. Together, these data indicate that activation of TLR4 enhances STAT3 activation in melanoma tissues and promotes tumor growth, angiogenesis and EMT in mice. 5) Activation of STAT3 is required for TLR4 signaling-mediated melanoma progression in mice. We found that LPS promoted tumor growth and STAT3 activation in B16-NC tumors, but had less effect in B16-STAT3β tumors, indicating that STAT3 activation plays a positive role in TLR4 signaling-mediated melanoma growth. IHC staining of tumor tissues showed that expression levels of Ki-67, CD31, N-cadherin and veminitin were increased, while the expression of E-cadherin was decreased in LPS-stimulated B16-NC tumors, compared to that in B16-NC tumors without LPS stimulation. No significant differences were observed in Ki-67, CD31, E-cadherin, N-cadherin and veminitin expression in B16-STAT3β tumors with and without LPS stimulation. The results of IHC staining imply an important role of STAT3 activation in TLR4 signaling-mediated melanoma growth, angiogenesis and EMT. We also found that LPS stimulation increased the percentage of splenic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in B16-NC tumor-bearing mice but not in B16-STAT3β tumor-bearing mice. Percentages of splenic CD8 T cells were significantly decreased in B16-NC tumor-bearing mice upon LPS stimulation. In B16-STAT3β tumor-bearing mice, LPS had a less potent decreasing effect on the number of splenic CD8 T cells than in B16-NC tumor-bearing mice, suggesting a role of STAT3 activation in LPS-induced splenic CD8 T cell reduction. Like CD8 T cells, natural killer (NK) cells directly kill cancer cells. Flow cytometric analyses showed that the number of NK cells was obviously decreased in LPS-stimulated B16-NC tumors, but not in B16-NC tumors without LPS stimulation. Blocking STAT3 activation by expressing STAT3β in the tumors increased tumor-infiltrating NK cells and attenuated LPS-induced NK cell reduction. The changes of immune cell profiles imply that activation of STAT3 contributes to TLR4 signaling-mediated immunosuppression in melanoma microenvironment. 2. We have examined how the TLR4 /STAT3 pathway is inhibited by AT-II in melanoma cells. The obtained results are as follows: AT-II competed with LPS in binding to TLR4. To determine if AT-II can bind to TLR4, molecular docking was performed. Docking simulation of AT-II (CID: 14448070) was carried out using the AutoDock4 program. The protein 3D structure of human TLR4/MD-2 (3FXI) was from the Protein Data Bank. AT-II could fit into the hydrophobic pocket of TLR4/MD-2 complex, with a high free binding energy of -7.11 (kcal/mol) and a predicted inhibition constant (Ki) of 10.08 μM. These data suggest a high binding affinity of AT-II toward TLR4/MD-2 receptor complex. LPS binding assay was conducted to determine if AT-II competes with LPS in binding to TLR4 in A375 cells. Result showed that AT-II dose-dependently blocked the LPS binding to TLR4 in A375 cells, suggesting that AT-II might be an antagonist of TLR4 in melanoma cells. 3. We have determined the contribution of inhibiting TLR4/STAT3 signaling in the anti-melanoma effects of AT-II in cell and mouse models. The obtained results are as follows: 1) Constitutive activation of TLR4 diminished the effect of AT-II in inhibiting STAT3 activation, reducing cell viability and inducing cell apoptosis in melanoma cells. We found that STAT3 is higher activation in A375-CA-TLR4 cells than in A375-NC cells. AT-II significantly inhibited STAT3 activation, reduced cell viability and induced cell apoptosis in A375-NC cells. But the effects of AT-II were less potent in A375-CA-TLR4 cells. These results suggest that inhibiting TLR4/STAT3 signaling contributes to the anti-melanoma effects of AT-II in melanoma cells. 2) Constitutive activation of TLR4 diminished the inhibitory effects of AT-II on tumor growth and angiogenesis in mice. Results showed that constitutive activating TLR4 in A375 cells promoted tumor growth in mice. AT-II oral administration potently inhibited the A375-NC melanoma growth in mice. The inhibitory effect of AT-II on tumor growth was less potent in A375-CA-TLR4-bearing mice than in A375-NC-baring mice. We also examined the inhibitory effects of AT-II on angiogenesis using IHC staining of CD31 in A375-CA-TLR4 and A375-NC xenografts. Results showed that AT-II significantly inhibited the expression of the angiogenesis marker CD31 in A375-NC xenografts. The protein level of CD31 was higher and the inhibitory effect of AT-II on CD31 expression is less potent in A375-CA-TLR4 xenografts than in A375-NC xenografts. These results suggest that inhibiting TLR4/STAT3 signaling contributes to the anti-melanoma effects of AT-II in mice.

12125116.label: Major findings and research outcome
12125116.value: The TLR4/MYD88/STAT3 and TLR4/TRIF/STAT3 pathways were established in melanoma. AT-II competed with LPS in binding to TLR4. Inhibiting TLR4/STAT3 signaling contributes to the anti-melanoma effects of AT-II in vitro and in vivo. A manuscript namely “Activation of STAT3 is a key event in TLR4 signaling-mediated melanoma progression” has been submitted to Cell Death & Disease (IF 5.96) and is under revision. A manuscript namely “Inhibiting TLR4/STAT3 signaling contributes to the anti-melanoma effects of atractylenolide II” is being drafted and to be submitted to Cancer letters (IF 6.51). Funded by this grant, 13 peer-reviewed journal papers have been published; and 4 conference abstracts have been published.

12125116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12125116.value: We have found that activation of TLR4/STAT3 signaling produces an immunosuppressive microenvironment in melanoma. AT-II inhibits TLR4/STAT3 signaling in melanoma. We are interested to examine if AT-II can reprogram melanoma microenvironment. We have established TLR4/STAT3 signaling as a new target for anti-melanoma drug discovery. We are going to identify more agents that can target TLR4/STAT3 signaling for treating melanoma. STAT3 activation has been linked to the development of resistance to BRAF(V600E)-targeted therapy in patients with BRAF(V600E)-mutant melanomas. AT-II inhibits STAT3 activation in melanoma. We can study if AT-II can overcome BRAF(V600E) inhibitor resistance in melanoma. AT-II shows good oral bioavailability and anti-melanoma properties. We are interested to develop AT-II into a drug for melanoma treatment/prevention.

12125116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12125116.value: In this study, the TLR4/MYD88/STAT3 and TLR4/TRIF/STAT3 pathways are established in melanoma, sheding novel insights into the pathophysiology of melanoma and suggesting new, potentially more effective, targets for treating melanoma. This study also provides evidence for the TLR4/STAT3 signaling-related mechanism of action of atractylenolide II (AT-II), a sesquiterpene compound from a Chinese medicinal herb Baizhu, in melanoma. This result provides chemical and pharmacological justifications for the clinical use of Baizhu in treating melanoma, and lay the groundwork for developing AT-II as an effective and safe agent in melanoma management.

12136616.label: Realisation of objectives
12136616.value: To realise Aim 1, we examined the effects of mmu-miR-206 transfection in soleus on miR-206 level in osteoblasts, bone formation, bone mass and bone structure in miR-206 KO mice following 28-day hind limb suspension (HLS). We found that the miR-206 levels within osteoblasts at the proximal tibia were markedly upregulated in the miR-206 KO mice after mmu-miR-206 transfection in soleus. We further documented the lower bone mass and poorer bone structure, as well as decreased bone formation rate at the metaphysis of distal femur in the miR-206 KO mice with mmu-miR-206 transfection in soleus following 28-day HLS when compared to those with miR-nonsense-control transfection in soleus. To realise Aim 2, The miR-206 KO mice were transfected with mmu-miR-206-eGFP in soleus, and intraperitoneally injected with (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome-encapsulated-antagomir-206 or (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome- encapsulated-antagomir-NC before they were subjected for 28-day HLS. The Runx2-positive osteoblasts isolated from the proximal tibia by laser-captured microdissection (LCM) were harvested and subjected to examine the miR-206 levels by QPCR. The distal femurs were collected for microCT followed by bone histomorphometry analysis. QPCR analysis showed that the miR-206 levels were dramatically lower in the osteoblasts from the antagomir-206-treated mice when compared to the antagomir-NC-treated controls. MicroCT analysis showed higher bone mass as well as improved bone structure in the antagomir-206-treated mice when compared to the antagomir-NC-treated controls. Bone histomorphometry analysis showed higher mineral apposition rate (MAR) and bone formation rate (BFR) in the antagomir-206-treated mice when compared to the antagomir-NC-treated controls. All these findings suggest that the (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome-encapsulated-antagomir-206 pre-treatment could promote bone formation in miR-206 KO mice transfected with mmu-miR- 206-eGFP following 28-day HLS. To realise Aim 3, The male SD rats were intraperitoneally injected with (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome-encapsulated-antagomir-206 or (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome-encapsulated-antagomir-NC before they were subjected for 28-day HLS. However, we found no significantly difference in the bone microarchitecture and microCT parameters between the antagomir-206-treated rats and antagomir-NC-treated rats. Interestingly, we found that the intraosseous miR-206 levels were not significantly upregulated in rats with HLS as compared to the control rats without HLS, which was inconsistent with our preliminary findings in murine HLS model. Theses inconsistency could be attributed to the different response of myomiR expression between mouse and rat. Therefore, we test the effect of (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome-encapsulated-antagomir-206 on C57BL/6 mice with HLS. As expected, we found that the antagomir-206 treatment markedly downregulated the intraosseous miR-206 expression in HLS mice. More importantly, the antagomir-206 treatment also resulted in the improvement of distal femur bone microarchitecture as well as the increased bone formation rate in HLS mice as compared to the HLS mice with antagomir-NC treatment. Taken together, these findings suggested that targeting inhibition of myomiR, i.e. miR-206 in osteoblast could promote bone formation in mice with HLS.

12136616.label: Major findings and research outcome
12136616.value: In this study, we provided the first preclinical evidence to show that the muscle-derived miRNA, i.e. miR-206, could contribute to the decreased bone formation during muscle atrophy. More importantly, we showed that osteoblast-targeted inhibition of miR-206 could be a potential anabolic strategy for muscle atrophy-related bone loss. With the support from this project, we have published two review papers: (1) Liu J et al. MicroRNA‐mediated regulation of bone remodeling: A brief review[J]. JBMR plus, 2019, 3(9): e10213.), (2) Dai R et al. Cathepsin K: The action in and beyond bone[J]. Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology, 2020, 8: 433. Moreover, one research article was recently accepted by Theranostics, while anther research article was conditionally accepted after minor revision by Nature Aging.

12136616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12136616.value: The findings of the current GRF project has also facilitate the initiation of another cluster research project supported by the research council of Hong Kong Baptist University (RC-IRCs-17-18). In this project, we aim to investigate the role of skeletal muscle-derived exosomal miRNAs on unloading-induced muscle atrophy by employing the skeletal muscle-specific microRNA loss-of-function models, i.e. ATCA-1 Cre; Dicer fl/fl mouse, in which most of the myomiRs are conditionally knocked down by genetic approach. This newly funded project is expected to extend the findings of the current GRF project to unravel the contribution of skeletal muscle-derived exosomal myomRs on the reduced bone formation during unloading-induced muscle atrophy.
