12141516.label: Realisation of objectives
12141516.value: In this project, a systematic investigation was carried out to define the relationship between plant secondary metabolite and different growing regions in order to elucidate the specific bioactive chemical profiles of superior germplasm resources. Xihuangcao derived from Isodon lophanthoides (Buch.-Ham. ex D. Don) H. Hara (IL), I. lophanthoides var. graciliflorus (Benth.) H. Hara (ILG) and I. serra (Maxim.) Kudô (IS) (family Lamiaceae), which have subtle phylogenetic relationships has been studied. ILG has a very close relationship with IL as they are both of the same species (ILG is a variety of IL), and IS is slightly alienated as a different species. Our studies have indicated the three taxa have distinct chemical profiles. IL and ILG mainly contain abietane and tricyclic type diterpenoids, while IS mainly contains ent-kaurane type diterpenoids. Through the present study, the variation of lipid compositions of the three Isodon taxa has been revealed, which may elucidate the potential role of plant lipids responsible for their different chemical profiles. Nine classes of lipids from three categories has been selected for analysis, namely, glycerophosphocholines (PC), glycerophosphoethanolamines (PE) and glycerophosphoglycerols (PG), glycerophosphoinositols (PI), monogalactosyldiacylglycerol (MGDG), digalactosyldiacylglycerol (DGDG), sulfoquinovosyldiacylglycerols (SQDG), ceramides (Cer) and glucosylceramide (GlcCer). By ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with electrospray ionization quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-ESI-QTOF-MS/MS), full spectra of lipid data has been acquired, and target lipids has been identified by extracting class-specific tandem mass fragments. With the addition of internal standards, relative quantitation of each lipid has been done. The MS data was further analysed by chemometrics software to compare the three Isodon taxa. Based on these data, a general way to describe CMM biochemically (in terms of a lipid or secondary metabolite profile) has been developed. This approach has been used with other CMMs, for example, Poria cocos (Schw.) Wolf. An ultra-performance liquid chromatography combined with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UHPLC-QTOF-MS/MS) approach was developed to describe CMM biochemically in terms of secondary metabolite profile, and an ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (UHPLC-QqQ-MS/MS) method was established to quantitatively characterize secondary metabolites and carbohydrates. These approaches were applied to characterize secondary metabolite and carbohydrate profiles of Poria cocos (Schw.) Wolf. Specifically, the established UHPLC-QTOF-MS/MS and UHPLC-QqQ-MS/MS methods were used to investigate whether and how the quality of Poria cocos correlates with its collection location by characterizing secondary metabolites in different samples from multiple geographical regions. The developed UHPLC-QTOF-MS/MS and UHPLC-QqQ-MS/MS approaches were also applied to explore how the form of Poria cocos decoction pieces affects its chemistry. In addition, the UHPLC-QqQ-MS/MS approach was used to characterize the carbohydrates (polysaccharides, oligosaccharides and monosaccharides) in three parts (epidermis, middle and inner part) of Poria cocos. These results will reveal the superior germplasm resources of CMM, which is helpful for its authentication and the selection of plantation cite. More importantly, the research work will provide a new tool for studying the germplasm resources of other CMMs.

12141516.label: Major findings and research outcome
12141516.value: Major findings are as follows: 1. Twenty-seven characteristic peaks were chosen to distinguish the three taxa. Establishment of the chemical profiles of the three taxa of Xihuangcao has been studied in this project. 2. Ten compounds were screened out as potential markers to distinguish the quality of Poria cocos samples from different geographical regions. This strategy clearly expounded the correlation between quality and geographical origins of Poria cocos. 3. The relationship between plant lipids and different species or growing regions has been established. From this, a way to define the influence of different environments on the growth of the herb can be developed. 4. These results could be significant for cultivation, not only for the selection of plantation site of CMM but also for attempts to grow CMM in other areas, which benefit by expanding the region of quality production . A correlation between plant lipids and the production of bioactive chemicals could be defined. In particular, the role of plant lipids in the production of bioactive chemicals may be advanced. 5. The application of plant lipidomics in the proposed study is expected to demonstrate that lipidomics can provide powerful insights into and useful information about the essence of superior germplasm resources of a CMM.

12141516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12141516.value: The lipid profiles of the three Isodon species were found to be different. As plant lipids play an important role in producing secondary metabolites, comparing the lipid profiles of different plant species may reveal the role of plant lipids in their distinct secondary metabolite profiles. Further studies on elucidating the role of plant lipids in the production of bioactive chemicals were proposed.

12141516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12141516.value: In recent ten years, the germplasm resources of Chinese medicinal materials (CMMs) have been endangered due to widespread environmental damage and ecosystem. Supplies of many CMMs are decreasing. As wild species and varieties disappear, germplasm is lost. This germplasm could be valuable for improving pharmaceutical efficacy of the plants and for ensuring the plant’s survival as climate changes. Thus, it is necessary to evaluate the germplasm resources of Chinese medicinal materials. In this study, a systematic investigation will be carried out to reveal the relationship between plant secondary metabolite and different growing regions in order to elucidate the specific bioactive chemical profiles of superior germplasm resources. Through this study, the relationship between plant lipids and different species or growing regions has been established. These results could be significant for cultivation, not only for the selection of plantation site of CMM but also for attempts to grow CMM in other areas. A correlation between plant lipids and the production of bioactive chemicals could be defined. The role of plant lipids in the production of bioactive chemicals may be advanced. The application of plant lipidomics could provide powerful insights into useful information about the essence of superior germplasm resources of a CMM.

12142016.label: Realisation of objectives
12142016.value: A.1. Synthesis and Bioactivity Evaluation of Mavacyocine Analogs (to fulfill Objective 1: b.1.2 and b.1.3 and Objective 3: b.3.2) We developed efficient synthetic routes to obtain the mavacyocine peptides [Jounal of American Chemical Society paper (JACS): Schemes 1, S1 and S2; Patent: Schemes 1-4), which had been used synthesize the structurally similar mavacyocine (MV) analogs of MVA (i.e. mavacyocine A). By replacing the amino acids of D- and L-DMCPGly of MVA with corresponding different D- and L-amino acids, MVD, MVC, MVC1 and MVE were synthesized. The cytotoxicity of MVA was evaluated against a panel of 11 cancer cell lines (IC50 = 0.25-1.85 nM) and one normal colorectal cell line (IC50 = 38.4 nM) (Figure 3 in JACS). The compound was further evaluated in the cancer cell line panel of Bayer Pharma AG pharmaceutical company with IC50 values ranging 0.084-1.2 nM. MVC demonstrates cell killing activity with IC50 values ranging from 20-100 nM, but MVD and MVE demonstrates no inhibition activity against the cancer cells at 10 M (JACS: Table 1).. By analyzing the SAR of the isolated and synthetic mavacyocines, we concluded that the novel amino acid residues D-DMCPGly and L-DMCPGly residues have played key roles in the activity potency of the cyclopeptides. For instance, MVD was synthesized to closely resemble the structure of MVA with no methyl groups substituted at the cyclopropyl groups in MVD. However, by comparing the in vitro assay data obtained from HCT116 cells, MVA showed remarkably 40,000 times more active than MVD in terms of the cancer cell killing activity. MVA was selected for the subsequent mechanism of action and antitumor efficacy studies delineated in Objectives 2 and 3 in the proposed application. HCT116 cell line was used in all these studies due to its stable cell proliferation and tumorgenesis. A.2. Characterization of Transforming Phenotypes of MVA Treated Cancer Cells (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.2) To investigate the impact of MVA on cell transformation, division and migration, we examined if MVA might be effective against reproductive integrity, tumorigenicity and metastasis of HCT116 cancer cells, and further determined their cell cycle, apoptosis and senescence effects. The colony formation, scratch wound and transwell migration assays determined that nM treatment of MVA decreases colony formation (JACS: Figure S3) and prevents cell migration (JACS: Figures S8 and S9) of HCT116 cells. However, no obious apoptotic induction effect was observed for MVA at its IC50 value concentrations up to 3.35 nM (JACS: Figure S4). Our flow cytometer data revealed that MVA increased G1 phase cells accompanied by a delay to enter S phase (JACS: Figure S5A&5B), and the Western blot analysis revealed that MVA treatment reduced the protein expressions of cyclin D1, CDK2, and CDK4 (JACS: Figure S5C&D). We further examined the cellular senescence effect of MVA on HCT116 cells by observing its notable increasing effects on the SA-β-gal-positive signals (JACS: Figure 6). We thus determined that the anti-proliferation effect of MVA is primarily derived from a non-apoptotic mechanism and it is a potential cellular senescence inducer. A.3. MVA Targeted Signaling Pathways Identified (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.3) A.3.1. MVA targets the p16/pRb signaling pathway We then examined the expression levels of a panel of senescence-related genes by means of RT2 profiler qPCR array (JACS: Figure 7A and Table S3) and further confirmed MVA significantly regulated genes using Western Blotting (JACS: Figure 7B&C), which determined that the mechanism of action of MVA in HCT116 cells was highly associated with the activation of the p16/RB axis, rather than the p53 nor p21 signaling pathway. A.3.2. MVA inhibits colon cancer cell proliferation via inhibiting the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway A phospho-specific protein microarray analysis containing 1318 phosphoprotein antibodies and the subsequent KEGG analysis revealed that 27 sites are highly associated the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway (JACS: Figure S6; Table S4; Figure S7 and Table S5), which was further assessed by the RT2 profiler qPCR array with a panel of focused PI3K-AKT-related genes (JACS: Figure 8A). The qPCR results demonstrated that MVA only regulates the protein phosphorylation process of the PI3K-AKT pathway, which were validated by our Western blotting results (JACS: Figures 8B&C-10; Table S6). A.3.3. MVA Suppresses Cell Migration via EMT Pathway We further examined whether the compound affects cellular mobilization and migration and the EMT regulators (N-cadherin, β-catenin, vimentin, MMP9 and MMP2) in colorectal cancer cells (JACS: Figures 11 and 12), which suggested MVA serve as an anti-metastatic agent. Our results thus revealed that MVA inhibited the proliferation of HCT116 cells through p16/Rb induced senescence by attenuating PI3K-AKT signaling pathway (JACS: Figure S10). A.4. Elucidation of the Anticancer Molecular Targets of MVA (to fulfill Objective 2: b.2.4) DARTS (Drug affinity responsive target stability) was introduced to elucidate the anticancer targets of MVA. After several rounds of optimized DARTS experiments (PhD thesis: Figures 5.2-5.8, p174-176), the bands specific to MVA were detected from SDS-PAGE (PhD thesis: Figure 5.9, p178). They are identified as the proteins Hsp90, calnexin, EF2, 14-3-3 and annexin A1 by mapping with protein databases (PhD thesis: Table 5.1, p179). Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) could be the potential binding target of MVA, and it is associated with PI3K-AKT pathway. Hsp90 is an essential partner for cancer cell growth and proliferation. An increased expression of Hsp90 has been found in many cancers. A.5. Assessment of Antitumor Activity of Mavacyocines In Vivo (to fulfill Objective 3: b.3.3) The in vivo efficacies of MVA were subsequently validated in the tumor xenograft-bearing mice against several types of cancer cells. Our previous data showed that MVA could significantly restricted the tumor growth against HCT116 and MCF7 cancer cells (Patent: Figures 21 and 22). MVA was further evaluated against A549 (lung), PC-3 (prostate) and A375 (melanoma) cancer cells. In all these studies, treatment of MVA at the doses of 0.5 and 1.0 mg/kg showed better tumor inhibitory effects (tumor suppression rates by 52-82 %) than the clinically used drug paclitaxel at the dose of 5 mg/kg (tumor suppression rates by 38-63 %) (JACS: Figure 5). Taken together, MVA appears a unique antitumor agent showing superior tumor restriciton profiles at much lower doses when compared to paclitaxel. A.6. Pharmacokinetic (PK) Analysis of MVA in Rats (to fulfill Objective 3: b.3.4) As we consider that the mavacyocines are more stable than their linear peptide counterparts, we have investigated the potential of both i.p. and p.o. routes of administration of MVA in rats in comparison with its i.v. route adminstration at 0.5 mg/kg. The main PK parameters were obtained as the following: 1) i.v.: AUC(0-t) (µg/mL/h) 1.13, AUC(0-∞) (µg/mL/h) 1.14, MRT (h) 4.22, t1/2 (h) 3.32, tmax (h) 0.083, CL (mg/(µg/mL)/h) 0.44, Cmax (µg/mL) 0.31; 2) i.p.: AUC(0-t) (µg/mL/h) 0.58, AUC(0-∞) (µg/mL/h) 0.58, MRT (h) 4.56, t1/2 (h) 3.51, tmax (h) 0.25, CL (mg/(µg/mL)/h) 0.86, Cmax (µg/mL) 0.17; 3) i.g.: AUC(0-t) (µg/mL/h) 0.55, AUC(0-∞) (µg/mL/h) 0.57, MRT (h) 6.60, t1/2 (h) 4.69, tmax (h) 0.75, CL (mg/(µg/mL)/h) 0.0.88, Cmax (µg/mL) 0.085. Based on these data, the bioavailabilities were determined as 50.9 % and 49.1 % for the i.p. and oral administrations of MVA, respectively. Our PK data determined that MVA could be orally administered as the oral administration showed similar bioavailability to the i.p. administration.

12142016.value: 1) We developed efficient synthetic routes to synthesize the mavacyocine peptides. (JACS, 2021; Patent, 2018). 2) We synthesized several structurally similar mavacyocine A (MVA) analogues, and further synthesized MVA. (JACS, 2021; Patent, 2018). 3) The isolated and synthetic mavacyocines were evaluated for their cell killing activity in vitro against a panel of cancer cell lines including colorectal, lung, prostate, cervical, leukemia, melanoma and breast cancer cells. None of the synthesized MVA analogs showed cytotoxic activities at 10 µg/mL. The over 10,000 times bioactivity difference between MVA and its analogs determined the remarkable importance of the novel D- and L-DMCPGly residues contained in MVA (JACS, 2021). Because of the high anticancer potency of MVA, the compound was selected to be evaluated in the cancer cell line panel of Bayer Pharma AG pharmaceutical company. 4) We then investigateed the impact of MVA on cell transformation, cell division and cell migration, and found that MVA is a potential cellular senescence inducer and could prevent migration of cancer cells (JACS, 2021). 5) Using several techniques such as qPCR array filing, phospho-specific protein microarray filing and immunoblotting assays, we determined that the anti-proliferative effect of MVA is conceivably derived from p16/Rb induced senescence by attenuating PI3K-AKT signaling pathway and its preventing cell migration and invasion is due to regulation of the mesenchymal cell markers (JACS, 2021). By using DARDS analysis, the PI3K-AKT pathway associated heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) was found to be the potential binding target of MVA (PhD thesis). 6) The antitumor efficacy of MVA was validated in the tumor-bearing mice against HCT116 (colorectal), MCF7 (breast), A549 (lung), PC-3 (prostate) and A375 (melanoma) carcinomas. In these in vivo studies, MVA with the administration doses of 0.5 and 1.0 mg/kg was demonstrated with superior antitumor efficacy than the clinically used drug paclitaxel at 5 mg/kg. We thus consider MVA with high potential for further development as a potent antitumor drug agent (JACS, 2021). Our PK study also found that MVA could be orally administered as it showed equivalent bioavailability to the i.p. administration. 7) Three research papers have been published (Zhang et al., 2016; Tsang et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2021), and one is submitted to the Jounral of American Chemical Society (JACS) (Xia et al., 2021). 8) One US patent was granted. 9) The study results have been presented in 3 conferences. 10) One PhD student has graduated, and another student is under PhD study.

12142016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12142016.value: In the present study, we have determined mavacyocine A (MVA) as a highly potent novel therapeutic lead for cancer. MVA was demonstrated with much higher anticancer potency than the clinically used drug paclitaxel both in vitro and in vivo. In addition, unlike many mainstay anticancer drugs, which cause cancer cell death through apoptotic induction, the anti-proliferative effect of MVA is positively correclated with induction of senescence. As senescence has been suggested as a tumor suppressive mechanism alternative to apoptosis, to develop mavacyocines as senescence-inducing drug candidates appears beneficial and complementary to the clinical management of cancer malignancies. To achieve this goal, we will seek different synthetic approaches in order to prepare MVA in large scale, which will relieve our burden to depend on the natural sources. At the same time, we will explore the potential of MVA as an ADC (antibody-drug conjugate) drug candidate, which can deliver this potent anticancer molecule to specifically target cancer cells with minimum side effects. On the other hand, we will seek collaborabion from pharmaceutical companies to carry out the safety and PK preclinical studies of MVA in order to advance the compound to clinical trials.

12142016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12142016.value: Cancer has become the leading cause of death in the world, accounting for about 15% of all human deaths. The current available cancer chemotherapeutics often have narrow therapeutic indices and severe side effects. In addition, cancers can develop resistance to these drugs. New anticancer drugs are thus very much needed. In the present studies, we have obtained a potent anticancer cyclopeptide molecule via isolation and total systhesis, and further evaluated its anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. The compound as found to potently inhibit tumor growth in animal studies against colorectal, lung, breast, cervical and melanoma cancer cells. The antitumor potencies displayed by administration of the cyclopeptide compound at a much lower dose was superior to the mainstay drug paclitaxel at a much higher dose. Our further mechanism of action studies determined the antitumor activities of the compound are highly associated with the p16/Rb induced senescence by attenuating PI3K-AKT signaling pathway. The results of our extensive studies suggest the novel cyclopeptide is a new class of anti-proliferative and antimetastatic remedy alternative to the mainstay apoptotic inducing agents, which is deemed to be a potential antitumor candidate for further development as clinical therapeutic in the management of cancerous pathologies.

12143316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12143316.value: 飢餓狀態下USF甲基化和表觀遺傳修飾對抑制脂肪生成基因的作用

12143316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12143316.value: 背景: 哺乳動物採用複雜的和精確的內分泌控制以維持代謝能量的穩定供應。編碼參與脂肪酸和三酰基甘油合成的酶基因的轉錄在脂肪生成組織肝臟和脂肪組織通過禁食/饋送和胰高血糖素/胰島素治療協同調控。脂肪生成的失調經常有助於代謝性疾病如肥胖症，脂肪肝，糖尿病和心血管疾病。轉錄因子，共調節因子和參與生脂組織脂肪生成轉錄調控信號分子代表了代謝性疾病的治療有吸引力的目標。在禁食/餵養和飢餓/胰島素，USF-1作為一個分子開關招收蛋白質的四個不同家庭的脂肪生成和糖酵解促進脂肪生成的轉錄調控：1），共調節因子，包括P / CAF和HDAC9，2）DNA斷裂/修理機械，包括，3）信號分子，包括PP1和DNA-PK，和4）染色質重塑複合物lipoBAF。期間餵食/胰島素，USF-1在S262通過DNA-PK，這是第一個去磷酸化/由PP1活性磷酸化。 USF-1的磷酸化允許的招募和乙酰化由P / CAF，從而在脂肪生成活化。在這方面，DNA-PK缺陷小鼠SCID小鼠也具有較低的脂肪組織的質量和體重，表示一個長期缺陷在餵養誘導脂肪生成。在平行於DNA-PK胰島素信號傳導，我們的研究鏈接BAF60c到aPKC的胰島素信號。響應於胰島素，BAF60c由aPKC的，這會導致BAF60c易位至細胞核，並允許與乙酰USF-1 BAF60c的直接相互作用磷酸化。因此，BAF60c被招募到形成lipoBAF複雜重塑染色質結構並激活脂肪生成基因。因此，BAF60c促進體內脂肪生成和增加甘油三酯的水平。我們，對於第一次，表明USF在介導脂質代謝的轉錄調節響應於禁食/饋送和飢餓/胰島素和會聚兩個胰島素信號，DNA-PK和aPKC的關鍵作用。 理: 到目前為止，我們已經表明，USF在胰島素作用，脂質和糖代謝和USF和其相互作用的蛋白質，包括P / CAF，HDAC9，SREBP-1c和BAF60c之間的相互作用依賴於USF翻譯後不可缺少的作用修改（磷酸化和乙酰化），通過DNA-PK和aPKC的小說由胰島素信號介導的。這些經驗教訓指向我們，USF的修改是在搜索的代謝狀態特定共調節因子的關鍵。 方法和目標: 在該提案中，1），我們將首先驗證PRMT5-MEP50複雜和改性的USF之間的相互作用。 PRMT5和MEP50會檢查自己的能力結合脂肪生成和糖酵解基因啟動子。 PRMT5-MEP50和修改的USF之間的直接互動將與輔助調節因子對轉錄抑制的功能意義一起進行調查。 2）USF甲基將在不同的代謝狀態，並與USF激活甲基化的功能意義沿胰島素治療條件進行審查。具體組蛋白甲基化事件將在啟動子以及染色質無障礙進行檢查。 3）通過過表達和沉默的動物和PRMT5 MEP50，我們將研究對糖和脂質代謝共調節因子在體內的後果。 USF甲基的體內意義將通過表達甲基突變體解剖。經鑑定PRMT5，MEP50和USF網站甲基化特異性是代謝性疾病治療所有潛在的藥物靶點。

12159916.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12159916.value: 擬南芥兩個E3 泛素連接酶（PUB2與 PUB4）和EXTRA LARGE G PROTEIN的功能研究

12159916.label: Project Objectives
12159916.value: Several putative substrates of PUB4/PUB2 have been identified, including the XLGs. We will determine whether PUB4/PUB2 regulate their activity/function by modifying them through mono-ubiquitination. We will define the role of PUB2/4-XLG interactions in related physiological and developmental processes. We have isolated four suppressor mutants of pub4 and identified a candidate suppressor locus. We will continue to characterize these mutants, isolate corresponding genes, and investigate their functional relationships with PUB4 and XLGs. Through transcriptome analysis and other methods, we will identify genes whose expression is altered by the pub2/4 and the xlg triple mutations. This will help to reveal pathways mediated by PUB2/4 and XLGs, including the response to cytokinin.

12159916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12159916.value: As sessile organisms, plants need to adjust their growth and development according to ever-changing environments. Environmental cues and endogenous signals are perceived by receptor or sensor proteins and transduced through sophisticated signaling pathways into appropriate cellular responses. Various G proteins and protein kinases are among the most common signal transduction components, and protein ubiquitination is also a prominent mechanism that regulates protein function and cell signaling. The signaling pathways often lead to transcriptional reprogramming that facilitates physiological and developmental response. We initially identified Arabidopsis EXTRA LARGE G PROTEIN 2 (XLG2) and XLG3 as positive regulators of immunity, which are now known to form heterotrimeric G protein complexes. Later, we identified two E3 ubiquitin ligases, PUB2 (PLANT U-BOX PROTEIN 2) and PUB4, as XLG-interacting proteins. The xlg and pub mutants, including their double and triple mutants, share similar pleiotropic phenotypes, such as defects in cell expansion, proliferation, and programmed cell death as well as in hormone response. The findings from our study and by other groups have indicated that these PUB and XLG proteins are newly discovered players in multiple important developmental and physiological pathways. The main goal of this proposal is to define the functions of the PUB and XLG proteins and their modes of action in mediating those cellular processes. Through genetic and molecular approaches, we have identified additional genes/proteins that physically and/or functionally interact with PUB4 and their roles in the PUB/XLG-mediated processes will be affirmed and further defined. We will determine whether PUB2/PUB4 regulate functions of their candidate substrates (including XLGs) by mono-ubiquitination. The molecular function of PUB4 in NITRILASE1-catalyzed auxin biosynthesis will be elucidated. The effects of the pub and xlg mutations on the cytokinin response will be investigated. By understanding the mechanisms by which these PUB and XLG proteins function, the proposed study will offer novel insights into the roles of protein ubiquitination and G proteins in regulating important cellular processes.

12159916.label: Realisation of objectives
12159916.value: 1. Identification of proteins that interact with PUB2/4 and XLGs and characterization of their interactions. We used yeast two hybrid, bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC), split luciferase complementation (LCA), and co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays to identify proteins that interact with PUB2/PUB4 and XLGs and to further characterize their interactions. XLG2, PUB2, or PUB4 was initially used as a bait in yeast two hybrid screens, leading to the findings that both PUB2 and PUB4 interact with all three XLGs. Their interactions in-planta were confirmed by BiFc and co-IP assays. BiFc detected their interactions on plasma membrane, and some of the interactions were displayed in the nucleus. These findings were included in the publication in Plant Physiol (Wang et al, 2017). The pub2/4 mutant was later found to be defective in the PAMP-trigged immune (PTI) responses and resistance to pathogenic and non-pathogenic strains of Pseudomonas syringae. Further analysis revealed that the E3 ligase domain of PUB4 is disposable but the C-terminal region, consisting of the ARM repeats, is essential and sufficient for its function in the immune response. The finding raised a possibility that PUB2 and PUB4 might use their ARM repeats as scaffolds to connect PTI signaling components. Various PTI signaling components were tested for their interactions with PUB2 and PUB4. Both PUB2 and PUB4 were found to interact with receptor/coreceptors of PAMPs and many downstream signaling components of the PTI response. Besides, PUB2 and PUB4 can form homo- and hetero-mers. Interactions between PUB2/4 and those proteins are dynamically regulated in response to PAMP treatments. These results indicate that PUB2/4 form scaffolds by using the ARM repeats as modular protein-binding interfaces to mediate interactions of the immune signaling components. These findings are included in a manuscript submitted to Plant Cell (Wang et al, under review). XLG2 was previously reported by Jianmin Zhou group to interact with BIK1, and RbohD. We found that XLG2 and XLG3 also interact with LYK5, PBL27, and MAPKKK5. The findings also raise a possibility that XLG2/3 might act as scaffolds or as anchors. The role of the E3 ligase domain of PUB2 and PUB4 remains to be defined. Likely their E3 ligase activity is involved in mediating other pathways they are involved. We previously hypothesized that XLGs could be the substrates of PUB2 and PUB4 for ubiquitination; however, such a hypothesis has not been proved and is most likely not valid. NIT1 was initially found to interact with PUB4 in a pulldown assay. However, this interaction could not be further confirmed and was likely a false positive. 2. Characterization of biological functions of PUB2/4 and XLG1/2/3 The xlg triple mutation and pub2/4 mutation share some common developmental and growth defects. Although we previously found that XLG2/3 function in disease resistance, the role of PUB2/4 in defense was not clear. We generated the transcripome profiles of the xlg/1/2/3 and pub2/4 and compared them with transcriptomes of wildtype. Among the genes down-regulated in pub2/4 compared with wildtype, the most prominent functional category is defense-related genes, indicating that PUB2/4 also function in disease resistance. Detailed analysis of disease resistance phenotypes was carried out. We found that the pub2/4 mutant displayed strikingly compromised resistance to not only the pathogenic strain of P. syringae but also to a normally non-pathogen strain (defective in type III secretion system). Besides, pub2/4 is defective in defense priming by pretreatment with flg22. We then analyzed some key physiological responses triggered by PTI. Both pub2/4 and xlg1/2/3 abolished the oxidative burst triggered by PAMPs. Besides, MAPK3/6 activation was severely compromised by these mutations. These findings indicate that PUB2/3 and XLG1/2/3 play critical roles in the PTI response. XLGs and PUB2/4 are also involved in many other biological processes, perhaps also through their roles as scaffolds. Further study is being carried out by using proximity ligation assays (in situ protein-protein interaction) to learn additional proteins that interact with PUB2/4 and XLGs and dynamic regulation of protein interactions in multiple pathways mediated by these proteins. 3. Genetic analysis to identify genes involved in the PUB4 and XLGs. Through genetic screening to find suppressor mutations that reverse the pub4’s morphological phenotype, we obtained a few putative suppressor mutants. Genetic mapping and genome sequencing were used to identify putative suppressor mutations. Some of the suppressor mutations have not been confirmed. One of the suppressors was apparently caused by a mutation in a gene encoding a receptor-like kinase SCRAMBLED (SCM)/ STRUBBELIG (SUB) which is known to be involved in regulating cell division and organogenesis. SCM also forms a complex with ANGUSTIFOLIA/DETORQUEO(AN/DOQ). Indeed, another pub4 suppressor mutation is likely due to a mutation in the AN/DOQ gene, which, however, remains to be confirmed. 4. Using transcriptome analysis and other methods to identify genes whose expression is altered by the pub2/4 and the xlg triple mutations to reveal pathways mediated by PUB2/4 and XLGs As mentioned earlier, RNA-seq was used to generate and compare the transcriptome profiles of wt, pub2/4, and xlg1/2/3. The transcriptome profiling helped us to learn that PUB2/4 play an important role in plant immunity, leading to further findings on the role of PUB2/4 in immunity. We previously reported that XLG2 and XLG3 are positive regulators of immunity. The transcriptome profile of the xlg triple mutant also showed that xlg1/2/3, like pub2/4, leads to down-regulation of many defense-related genes. Beside defense pathways, these mutants also shared similarity in expression patterns of cytokinin response genes. Expression of many Type-A ARR genes were decreased in the pub2/4 and xlg1/2/3 mutants. These results could at least partially explain the similar cytokinin response phenotypes caused by the xlg and pub mutants as we recently reported.

12159916.label: Major findings and research outcome
12159916.value: 1. PUB2 and PUB4 are critical components in pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) Transcriptome analysis indicated that the pub2/4 mutation results in downregulation of many defense-related genes. Detailed phenotypic analysis showed that the pub2/4 mutation leads to a severe compromise in resistance to virulent and normally non-pathogenic strains of P. syringae. Pretreatment with flg22 can normally protect plants from subsequent infection by P. syringae; however, flg22 treatment of the pub2/4 could not provide such protection. The pub2/pub4 mutation abolishes the oxidative burst and greatly reduces MAPK activation triggered by PAMP treatments. Similarly, the xlg1/2/3 mutation was also found to abolish the oxidative burst and reduce MAPK action. XLG2 and XLG3 were previously known to be positive regulators of immunity. 2. PUB2 and PUB4 function as scaffolds to connect signaling components of PTI. XLGs might have similar roles The U-box domain was found disposable but the ARM repeats of PUB4 is essential and sufficient for its function in immunity. The ARM repeats are known to mediate protein-protein interactions. PUB2 and PUB4 were found to interact with all three XLGs on plasma membrane and/or in the nucleus. PUB2 and PUB4 themselves can form homo- and hetero-dimers. PUB2 and PUB4 were found to interact with receptor/coreceptors and downstream signaling components of the PTI response, PUB2 and PUB4 interact with FLS2, BIK1, and PBL27. PUB4, but not PUB2, was found to interact with CERK1. PUB2 and PUB4 interact with RbohD and multiple MAPKKK3/5-MKK4/5-MPK3/6 cascade proteins. After PAMP treatments, PUB2/4 and those proteins dissociated, likely to attenuate the PTI response. These results indicate that PUB2/4 form scaffolds by using the ARM repeats as modular protein-binding interfaces to mediate interactions of the immune signaling components. In addition to the previous report that XLG2 interact with FLS2, BIK1, and RbohD, we found that XLG2 and XLG3 interact with LYK5, PBL27, and MAPKKK5. The findings also raise a possibility that XLG2/3 might act as scaffolds or as anchors. 3. PUB2/4 and XLGs function in many biological pathways PUB2/4 and XLGs have been found to be involved in not only the immune response but also in many other pathways, including growth, cell division, cell death, development, and tolerance to abiotic stresses. Genetic suppressor screen indicated that PUB4 might also be a component in cell division and organogenesis mediated by the receptor-like kinase SCM/ SUB and AN/DOQ. Many of the signaling components that interact with PUB2/4 and XLGs, such as RbohD and MAPK cascade components, are known to be involved in many developmental and physiological pathways. PUB2/4 and XLGs can assemble a large number of distinct protein complexes in a combinatorial way to mediate many biological processes in plants. Some of our findings have been included in a publication (Wang et al, Plant Physiology, 2017) and in a manuscript that is under review by Plant Cell (Wang et al, submitted).

12159916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12159916.value: Our study reveals that the ARM repeats of PUB2/4 function as scaffolds to mediate interactions between signaling components of the immune response. XLGs could also have a similar function. PUB2/4 and XLGs have a potential to form a large number of distinct protein complexes in a combinatorial way to mediate many biological processes in plants. Some of the proteins assembled by PUB2/4 and XLGs, such as RbohD and MAPK cascade components, also function in many other pathways. By connecting the common signaling components with other receptors or sensing proteins, such scaffolds could offer a simple and flexible mechanism for selectively activating or shaping new responses according to perceived internal and external signals. In addition to PUB2/4, there are other 39 U-box-ARM PUB proteins in Arabidopsis. Many of them could have similar modes of molecular functions in their roles in regulating a wide range of plant developmental and physiological pathways. Future study on the pathways that regulate upstream signaling events responsible for organizing these scaffolds could shed light on how plants use scaffolds to modulate protein interactions to tailor specific biological functions.

12159916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12159916.value: Living organisms use signaling pathways to convert external and internal signals into physiological responses. Signaling pathways are mediated by proteins and other signaling molecules. Information flow from signal-perceiving receptors to downstream signaling components are precisely controlled to mediate appropriate responses. In the plant immune response, receptors/coreceptors recognize invading pathogens and then activate downstream signaling components, leading to activation of defense mechanisms. We found that the Arabidopsis proteins PUB2, PUB4, and three XLGs play important role in plant disease resistance. They are involved in control of plant immunity by function as scaffold proteins to connect receptors/co-receptors and down-stream signaling proteins in the immune response. Our study provides novel insights into how the signaling pathway that leads to the immune response might be organized by using these scaffolds.

12162016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12162016.value: Homeostatic regulation of fluid and electrolyte balance is a vital process for guiding many cellular functions. It is crucial for upholding osmotic stabilization of living cells. Perturbations of body-fluid tonicity can cause distress in biological activities of macromolecules, the functions of cells and organs and putting threats to the health of animals. This may lead to a diverse group of pathological consequences, from renal failure, mild neurological symptoms to death. In the past decades, molecular and physiological factors related to osmotic homeostasis have been thoroughly studied. However our understanding on the molecular mechanisms that is involved in the progress of osmolar disorders, and the identification of therapeutic targets to the related diseases has yet to be fully elucidated. Nonetheless recent advances in the understanding of small non-coding RNAs (microRNAs) on regulatory circuit in physiological and pathophysiological functions shed light on a novel concept of disease cure. Given the emerging roles of microRNAs in osmotic stress responses, it warrants deeper investigations into how tonicity-inducible microRNAs modulate membrane transport in native tissues under anisosmotic conditions. The catadromous fish Japanese eels actively engage physiological responses to oppose osmotic perturbations to stabilize body osmolarity. Gills of these fishes possess great physiological and structural plasticity to adapt to large changes in external osmolality and to participate in ion uptake/excretion, which is critical for the re-establishment of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis. Therefore their fish gills provide an excellent model to study the role of microRNAs in direct osmotic stress responses. In the past 20 years, our laboratory has established both animal and primary gill cell culture models to investigate the interactions of hormones, tissue remodeling and molecular pathways in relation to osmoregulation of Japanese eels. Major knowledge gap exists in our understanding on how microRNAs are involved in osmotic perturbations and their functional roles to define cell specific functions in transepithelial transport. The study described here signifies a revolutionary step in the field as it aims to explore the importance of this fundamental and evolutionary conserved regulation. We target to identify tonicity-sensitive microRNAs and to define their expression and functions in the two specialized gill ion-transporting cells, pavement and mitochondria-rich cells. The results will open up a new approach for the investigation of fish osmoregulation and reveal how this fundamental process evolves in animals. 12162016.label: Major findings and research outcome
12162016.value: (1) We characterized the ex-vivo gill filament culture model with regard to its responses to hyper-osmotic stress. The purpose is to establish a culture model, which retains the three-dimensional organization (primary and secondary lamellae) and takes into account all the cell types [pavement cells (PVCs), chloride cells (CCs), mucous cells, and undifferentiated cells] in experiments. Our data demonstrated that the ex-vivo gill filament culture exhibited distinctive responses to hyperosmotic acclimation. It would be a useful model to investigate underlying mechanisms of osmotic responses in fish gills. In addition, we studied the expression of four major factors involved in miR biogenesis. The mRNA expression levels of drosha, xpo5, and dicer1 were dysregulated under hyperosmotic treatment, indicating that the treatment modulated miR-biogenesis in gill cells. (2) Micro-RNA sequencing was conducted using the gill filaments in both in vivo fish transfer and ex vivo gill culture experiments. Bioinformatics analysis of the dysregulated miRs at high stringency of filtering (p < 0.001) shortlisted two miR candidates, miR-29b-3p and miR-200b-3p. The family of miR-29 was known to respond to environmental stress and cellular repairing processes. While miR-200 was involved in epithelial ion transport to inhibit the expression of nherf1 in CCs. Integration of the transcriptome and miRNA data in the time-course hyperosmotic treatment, together with the miRanda algorithm analysis, we were able to determine the miR-mRNA binding. Klf4 and slc17a5 were identified to be the target genes of miR-29b-3p and miR-200b-3p, respectively. The role of Klf4 is in the maintenance of CC's progenitor’s population, while slc17a5 belongs to the solute carrier family of transporters to transport amino acids, which can serve as organic osmolytes to regulate cellular osmolality, against hyperosmotic stress. This is the first study to characterize the hypo-osmotic responses and the dysregulation of miR-biogenesis factors/miRs in ex-vivo gill filament culture under hyperosmotic challenge.

This analysis would help to identify evolutionary conserved miRs that regulate fluid and electrolytes balance. Moreover, there are many other tonicity-responsive miRs and genes were identified in this study. The data support further analysis of other miRs and transcripts to elucidate their regulatory roles in osmotic responses.

12218416.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12218416.value: Prof Chao, Christopher Yu Hang Dr Guan, Daogang Prof Ip, Margaret

12218416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12218416.value: Over the past 70 years, studies have attempted to determine the survival of airborne bacteria and the associated effects of environmental parameters in order to predict the risk of airborne disease transmission (through droplets or droplet nuclei) and design infection control strategy. We know something about airborne bacteria through these studies, but the underlying biological mechanisms affecting the bacterial performance and so these experimental results are still poorly understood. This is problematic because without understanding the mechanisms, we may misinterpret and misuse the results and could not identify a target to control the bacteria. Many people in Hong Kong spend over 90% of their time in indoor environments, most of which are controlled to different levels of temperature and sometimes RH for ventilation, energy savings and comfort. Little is known about the effects of the indoor climate on bioaerosol survival. This issue is of paramount importance in healthcare settings. Some interesting findings have been reported from bioaerosol studies and animal exposure models; for instance, a temperature of > 24oC has been shown to universally decrease bacterial survival, and some studies have reported a U-shaped decay curve with RH. Why do bacteria behave in such a manner? Scant research has addressed the fundamental question of the stress resistance of bacteria during aerosolisation. Our data demonstrated that rpoS mutants had almost completely died in aerosolisation. RpoS regulates various stress resistance genes in some bacteria. Missing this gene means missing a defence mechanism. This result prompts to a new idea that if we can identify the critical stress resistance genes, and the stress they respond to as well as the aerosol and environmental condition interacting with them, we may be able to use these genes as new engineering targets for environmental control of airborne bacteria. For instance, if RpoS-mediated stress resistance is important for bacterial survival, finding ways to suppress it can help to effectively inactivate airborne bacteria. Moreover, since the environmental factors that actually kill or preserve bacteria and the gene response to them will now be better known, we could select and optimise disinfection and control measures to reduce disease transmission e.g. to avoid stimulating or to increase the stress loading on a particular gene through changing the environment. We hypothesise that stress resistance genes are crucial in the defence against aerosolisation stress and this new knowledge could help to predict and reduce transmission risks of airborne bacteria. 過去70年，不同的研究嘗試找出環境因素對細菌在空氣中生存的影響，藉此有助對經空氣傳播的疾病(特別是經飛沫傳播)的風險評估，從而制定和改善控制傳染病的措施。雖然過去的研究為細菌在空氣中的生存帶來不少信息，但我們對細菌在空氣中生存的基理還是十分缺乏，因而令制定減低細菌在空氣中生存的方案甚為困難。一般香港人有九成時間在室內，但是一般室內各種條件(例如溫度和濕度)的調控，都是以舒適或者省電為本，並未以減低細菌在空氣中存活為目標而制定。其實此前已有一些關於環境條件影響細菌在空氣中生存的研究，比如一般細菌在攝氏24度以上都較易在空氣中失活，另外亦有研究指出在極高和極低的濕度下細菌在空氣中會較易失活。為何空氣中的細菌在不同的條件有如此的表現呢?這有可能是細菌的抗逆性基因在空氣中有不同的表達。我們的初步研究顯示，大腸桿菌中的rpoS基因對其在空氣中的生存十分重要，缺乏rpoS的突變體在氣化過程中差不多全部失活，由於rpoS是調控細菌不同境逆基因，以助其在不利的環境下得以繼續生存，故此我們的研究帶來一個新的研究方向 –針對抗逆性基因控制細菌在空氣中的存活。藉此作為基礎，以助在工程時制定不同的目標，去調控各種室內環境因素，而達致減低細菌在空氣中的存活。此外，了解各種環境因素對細菌在空氣中存活的影響，亦有助制定殺菌的條件和改善措施去減低空氣傳播疾病的風險，例如調制環境的因素去減少對某些基因的刺激。我們相信逆境性基因對細菌在空氣中的存活至為重要，而本研究將有助空氣傳播疾病的風險評估和減低空氣傳播疾病的風險。

12232716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12232716.value: 圖數據近年被廣泛應用，如社交網絡、信息網絡、組合購買網絡與生物化學數據庫。近年來這些真實的應用引發了在圖數據領域的研究。然而，圖數據的擁有者不一定有足夠的技術背景來提供面向大規模圖數據的查詢服務。另一方面，服務提供者能提供可擴展、靈活以及高效的服務，因此數據擁有者傾向於將數據或者查詢外包給第三方服務提供者。在化學藥劑領域裡，已有的公司在提供圖結構查詢時採納了這個方案。 第三方服務提供者不一定可信。安全性，如數據和查詢的隱私，是一項重要的服務質量指標。這直接影響數據擁有者和查詢用戶是否願意採用該服務。隱私保護的研究主要是在安全性和可用性（針對這個項目而言指的是性能）中尋求平衡。我們就隱私保護的前期工作提出了一些方案，但這些方案都是針對特殊的查詢，不具備通用性。而在基本的圖算法中，有一系列源於線性代數的通用方法。這項目提出了一個創新的、統一的線性代數隱私保護框架，能通用於實現圖查詢算法。 具體展開，我們將研究隱私的交集、並集、向量積與矩陣相加相乘等等。據我們所知，這樣的框架並沒有被研究過。研究方案如下： 1. 找出圖結構的編碼（如矩陣），圖屬性的編碼（如向量）。 2. 用矩陣和向量的相乘或者相加來重寫圖查詢算法。 3. 研究高性能加密方案。 4. 研究在不同攻擊模式下的安全保証。 通常而言，線性代數的方法在性能的方面存在優化的空間。我們利用我們在數據庫方面的經驗來優化上述方案。

12232716.label: Realisation of objectives
12232716.value: Objective 1. The main results of the proposal are reported in [ICDE 2021]. In the privacy-preserving graph query paradigm, we first propose to match queries with a notion of balls. A ball is the subgraph determined by a ball center node and the subgraph reachable from the center within the query diameter. (Matching queries with balls are often practical as the users do not need patterns far away in a large data graph.) Our techniques can be summarized as follows. The ball and the query are encoded by matrices. Then, the core of the existing query algorithm is transformed into a series of data-oblivious operations, which consist of additions and multiplications on matrices. We focused on additions and multiplications because we have found that encryption schemes (fully homomorphic and partially homomorphic encryptions) support additions and/or multiplications only. For instance, the privacy-preserving set intersections are not compatible with other encryption schemes. To propose a secure version of the algorithm, the matrices are encrypted, and the matrix operations are performed in the encrypted domain. The encryption used in this investigation is partially homomorphic encryption (PHE), called cyclic group based encryption (CGBE). Objective 2. To apply privacy-preserving optimizations for the specific algebra operations Since data-oblivious operations are generally inefficient. Also, in the case of CGBE, CGBE is correct only when the computed ciphertext corresponds to a plaintext that does not exceed a predeﬁned limit. Hence, we propose a series of pruning techniques as optimizations (such as neighbor-label pruning and path pruning) so that some data-oblivious operations can be skipped. As a result, the additions and multiplications are performed the balls that are relevant to the answer. These optimizations allow processing more balls in a privacy-preserving manner and reach the predefined limit of CGBE less often. The pruning techniques use some encrypted query structures such as neighbor labels and paths, whose plaintext is sensitive. Even the pruning techniques are done in the encrypted domain, the prunings of balls leak some information. Hence, we conducted a security analysis and quantified the loss of privacy. We conducted extensive experiments on massive networks to show that in practice, the pruning techniques are effective. Objective 3. 12232716.value: 1. In Section 5.3, realization of objective, we have detailed the findings of the project published in [ICDE2021]. 2. In addition, in many applications (e.g., social networks), the sensitive information can be different from [ICDE2021]. Users may prefer to hide parts or all of her/his data graphs (e.g., private friendships) from the public. This leads to a recent graph model, namely the public-private network model, in which each user has his/her own network. Such a model has been emerging during the course of the project. We use the keyword search on graphs as an example query of this study. The challenge is that the query answers on private networks and on a combination of private and public networks can be different. In [ICDE2020], our major result is a new efficient keyword search framework for massive networks, called public-private keyword search (PPKWS). PPKWS is a framework that consists of three major steps: partial evaluation, answer reﬁnement, and answer completion. PPKWS is a unified framework in the sense that existing semantics of keyword search patterns can be readily implemented on PPKWS. We propose indexes and optimizations for PPKWS. 3. 12232716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12232716.value: In this investigation, we have employed a partially homomorphic encryption (PHE) scheme, called CGBE, supporting both additions and multiplications. The CGBE scheme is relatively efficient when compared to other PHE schemes. However, the scheme is correct only when the computed ciphertext corresponds to a plaintext that does not exceed a predeﬁned limit. That is, the additions and multiplications on the plaintext must yield a plaintext small than the limit. Graph queries however need many additions and multiplications. It seems the approach of using such operations for graph queries has reached its limit. Hence, it is necessary to employ additional technologies to support more efficient and scalable privacy-preserving graph query processing. Further development is to exploit the recent secure co-processor to do a small part of computations that are either costly or impossible to do in the encrypted domain, such as pruning using sensitive information of a query.

12232716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12232716.value: In this project, we studied privacy preserving query services for strong simulation queries in the database outsourcing paradigm. In such a paradigm, clients send their queries to a third-party service provider (SP), who has the outsourced large graph data, and the SP computes the query answers. However, as SP may not always be trusted, the sensitive information of the clients’ queries. Importantly, the query structures, should be protected. This project proposed the three main steps of query processing in this paradigm. First, under this paradigm, we proposed to match queries with localized subgraphs called balls. Matching queries with balls are often practical as the users do not need patterns that are far away in a data graph. Second, the core of the existing query algorithm is transformed into a series of data-oblivious operations, which consist of additions and multiplications on matrices. To obtain a secure version of the algorithm, the matrices are encoded and encrypted, and the matrix operations are performed in an encrypted domain. Third, we proposed a series of pruning techniques. We quantified the loss of privacy. We conducted extensive experiments on massive networks to show that in practice, the pruning techniques are effective.

12244916.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12244916.value: 面向集值數據的分析查詢驗證服務

12244916.label: Project Objectives
12244916.value: Identify and formulate the authentication problem for analytical queries on set-valued data; Design privacy-preserving authentication protocols for various set operations that support application-level analytical queries; Develop authentication algorithms for various analytical queries and extend them to data integration settings; Perform security analysis and performance evaluation to demonstrate the robustness and efficiency of the proposed query authentication protocols and algorithms.

12244916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12244916.value: 隨著近來數據即服務（DaaS）及雲端計算的發展，基於雲的數據分析查詢服務得到了廣泛的應用。例如，在個人基因組分析應用中的聚合查詢用以確定與某些遺傳性疾病相關聯的常見基因類型；在市場購物籃分析應用中的關聯規則查詢力求找到客戶購買之間的關聯。然而，由於雲服務提供商一般是第三方，並非完全可信，其查詢結果的完整性必須加以驗證。目前大部分的查詢驗證技術僅局限於關係/空間/文本數據，尚不支持常見的集值數據上的分析查詢。在本項目中，我們將針對集值數據進行查詢驗證問題的研究，主要面臨三個挑戰。首先，由於數據和查詢請求的動態性，不可能預先計算查詢結果並加以認證。第二，集值數據分析查詢主要由大量的集合運算構成，這使得現有應用於選擇和連接查詢的驗證技術不可適用。第三，在許多應用領域，如商業和醫療保健，原始數據通常包含敏感的個人信息。因此，只有分析查詢結果可以被報告到查詢的客戶端，而敏感源數據不能在查詢驗證的過程中被洩露。為了應對這些挑戰，我們將開發新的查詢驗證協議和算法，以確保分析查詢結果的完整性，同時保護敏感源數據的私密性。本項目的研究議程包括：1）面向各類集合操作的驗證協議設計; 2）針對聚合查詢的隱私保護驗證算法開發與優化; 3）針對高級分析查詢的隱私保護驗證算法開發與優化； 4）所提技術在數據集成環境的擴展; 5）查詢驗證協議和算法的安全分析和性能評估。

12244916.label: Realisation of objectives
12244916.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. We have identified and formulated the problem of authenticated analytical queries on set-valued data. We have developed a family of privacy-preserving authentication protocols for primitive multiset operations. Using these protocols as building blocks, we have designed a novel privacy-preserving authentication framework for various analytical queries and further optimized their authentication performance [Conference/1, Journal/1]. We have also studied the problem of authenticating relational queries with fine-grained access control [Conference/2, Conference/5]. In addition, we have investigated query authentication techniques for large-scale image retrieval [Conference/4] and extended them to spatio-temporal integrity assurance in mobile environments [Journal/2] and range query processing in blockchain environments [Conference/3]. In all the above studies, we have performed security analysis and performance evaluation to validate the robustness and efficiency of the proposed query authentication protocols and algorithms. The research findings have been published in the top-tier conferences and journals including ACM SIGMOD, IEEE ICDE, IEEE TKDE, and IEEE TMC.

12244916.label: Major findings and research outcome
12244916.value: Aggregate query services over set-valued data are becoming widely available for business intelligence that drives decision making. However, as the service provider is often a third-party delegate of the data owner, the integrity of the query results cannot be guaranteed and is thus imperative to be authenticated. Unfortunately, existing query authentication techniques either do not work for set-valued data or they lack data confidentiality. To address this issue, in this project we have proposed authenticated aggregate queries over set-valued data that not only ensure the integrity of query results but also preserve the confidentiality of source data. As many aggregate queries are composed of multiset operations such as set union and subset, we have proposed a privacy-preserving authentication framework for aggregate queries [Conference/1]. It consists of an authenticated index Merkle Grid tree (MG-tree), a family of privacy-preserving authentication protocols for primitive multiset operations, and a series of aggregate query processing algorithms. We have further proposed several optimizations to reduce the computation and communication overheads for both the server and the query client [Journal/1]. Security analysis and empirical evaluation show that our proposed privacy-preserving authentication techniques are feasible and robust under a wide range of system workloads. We have also studied the problem of authenticating relational queries with fine-grained access control. The key challenge is how to protect information confidentiality during query authentication, which is essential to many critical applications. To address this challenge, we have proposed a novel access-policy-preserving (APP) signature as the primitive authenticated data structure [Conference/2]. A useful property of the APP signature is that it can be used to derive customized signatures for unauthorized users to prove the inaccessibility while achieving the zero-knowledge confidentiality. On top of this, we have proposed a grid-index-based tree structure that can aggregate APP signatures for efficient range and join query authentication. Besides, a number of optimization techniques have been proposed to further improve the authentication performance. A system called vABS has been developed to demonstrate the performance of the proposed techniques for verifying attribute-based search over shared data [Conference/5]. In addition, we have investigated the problem of query authentication for large-scale image retrieval [Conference/4]. Due to the large size of image files, the main challenges are to (i) design efficient authenticated data structures (ADSs) and (ii) balance search, communication, and verification complexities. To deal with these challenges, we have proposed two novel ADSs, the Merkle randomized k-d tree and the Merkle inverted index with cuckoo filters, to ensure the integrity of query results in each step of image retrieval. For each ADS, we developed corresponding search and verification algorithms on the basis of a series of systemic design strategies. Then, we put together the ADSs and designed an authentication scheme called ImageProof for verifiable image retrieval. Furthermore, we have proposed several optimization techniques to improve the performance of the proposed ImageProof scheme. Additionally, we have extended the authentication techniques to spatio-temporal integrity assurance in mobile environments [Journal/2] and range query processing in blockchain environments [Conference/3].

12244916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12244916.value: For further development, we plan to extend the proposed analytical query authentication techniques to federated data analytics systems. In federated data analytics, collaborative queries are performed over joint data distributed among multiple organizations. For example, a genome dataset might be maintained by multiple hospitals and institutions. The challenge is how to combine the authenticated data structures from individual data sources faithfully so as to support query authentication over aggregated data. We also plan to study more query authentication problems in blockchain systems. A key research issue here is how to efficiently maintain authenticated data structures with smart contracts, as the costs incurred by different smart contract operations differ dramatically (e.g., a smart contract write is two orders of magnitude more expensive than a smart contract read). Thus, it would be interesting to investigate update-efficient authentication techniques for various queries in the unique blockchain setting.

12244916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12244916.value: With recent advances in data-as-a-service (DaaS) and cloud computing, cloud-based analytical query services have become widely available. For example, an aggregate query in personal genomics analysis aims to identify frequent gene patterns associated with some genetic diseases; an association rule query in market basket analysis seeks to find associations between customer purchases. Analytical query results can be used to inform critical decision making and derive valuable business intelligence. However, as the cloud service provider, which is often a third party, might not be fully trustworthy, it is imperative to authenticate the integrity of query results. Unfortunately, most of the existing query authentication techniques have been confined to relational/spatial/text data and do not support analytical queries on set-valued data, which are commonly found in data analytics applications. In this project, we have investigated issues arising in query authentication on set-valued data, and developed novel privacy-preserving authentication techniques to ensure the integrity of analytical query results while protecting the privacy of sensitive source data.

12254316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12254316.value: 長時間視覺跟蹤的兩個研究問題：目標重檢測和魯棒性

12254316.label: Project Objectives
12254316.value: To estimate positive and negative conditional distributions from video frames after the object is lost as additional information to learn a re-detector; To investigate and develop a new method to model the commonality and diversity of multiple features and a new dynamic online feature-selection method for robust multi-feature tracking; To study and develop a new probabilistic framework for multi-feature model updating; and To create a new long-term video dataset containing different degrees of challenging videos for experimentation.
rows: To estimate positive and negative conditional distributions from video frames after the object is lost as additional information to learn a re-detector;
To investigate and develop a new method to model the commonality and diversity of multiple features and a new dynamic online feature-selection method for robust multi-feature tracking;
To study and develop a new probabilistic framework for multi-feature model updating; and
To create a new long-term video dataset containing different degrees of challenging videos for experimentation.

12254316.label: Realisation of objectives
12254316.value: The four listed objectives have been realized satisfactorily. Details are discussed as follows. The references [J#] and [C#] refer to the journal paper number and conference paper number in Sections 8 and 9 of Part C, respectively. Objective 1: We have developed a spatial-temporal regularized correlation filter-based object re-detector. We approach the re-detection problem from the perspective of the online generic object tracking process, in which some important information such as category, appearance, motion patterns of the object are unknown before the tracking is performed. Therefore, it would be intractable to utilize some offline data to explicitly train some parametric models for capturing the positive and negative conditional distributions. Instead, we have proposed a novel correlation filter-based re-detection framework. Based on the proposed framework, we implicitly estimate and model the positive and negative conditional distributions in an online manner by training and updating a correlation filters with adaptively selection of reliable samples. To ensure that the modeled positive and negative conditional distributions have large discrepancy which can guarantee strong discriminability of the tracking model, we have proposed to enforce the regression target of the correlation filter-based detector has distinguished responses on positive samples compared with negative samples. Besides, we exploit the dense sampling by using circulant shift operator of the base tracking sample to provide more virtual negative samples for negative conditional distribution modeling. A spatial-temporal regularizer is further imposed into the detector in which the spatial regularization can help to suppress effect from the cluttered background while the temporal regularization enables the adaptive incorporation of historical appearance cues to deal with appearance changes. To ensure that the object re-detector can handle data from multiple sensor sources, we extend the model to multi-modality version, and proposed an adaptive modality reliability estimation scheme to adaptively fuse reliable modalities. Experimental results on challenging videos demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. This work has been accepted by the ACM Transactions [J4]. Objective 2: To address the robustness issue and realize the objective 2, we have proposed a series of mathematical models which consider the commonality (consistency) and specificity in feature learning and fusion from two aspects: (i) commonality and diversity of different features, and (ii) consistency between the feature distance metric and feature variations. To model the commonality and diversity of multiple features, we have developed a novel multiple sparse representation model for appearance modeling [J1]. Our proposed method is developed based on two observations: (i) commonality is closely related to the concepts of agreement or consensus while diversity is related to feature-specific properties which provides complementarity for appearance modeling, and (ii) proximity information should be incorporated for more close matching between object and templates. As such, the proposed multiple sparse representation model decomposes the sparse representation with multiple features of the target into two components under an adaptive proximity constraint, which explicitly models the common and feature specific properties of different features and exploits the appearance proximity between the tracked target and the template for more accurate object representation. To adaptively update the proximity constraint for handling appearance changes, we have developed an online LogDet Regularized Multiple Metric Learning Algorithm [J1]. The proposed algorithm can automatically preserve the positive definiteness of the metric without an inefficient projection onto semi-definite cone, which is suitable for efficient online visual tracking. The theoretical mistake bound is also provided and proved in [J1]. We have derived an efficient learning algorithm to guarantee the optimality of the model parameters. We have performed extensive experiments to evaluate the proposed tracker. Experimental results show that the proposed tracker outperforms other state-of-the-art trackers on the visual tracking benchmark dataset. We have further extended the commonality (consistency) and diversity (specificity) modeling into object tracking problem with data of multiple modalities. To achieve robust multi-modality feature learning and fusion, we proposed to extract informative feature templates and exploit the modality consistency in representation ability for modality fusion-based appearance modeling. This work has been published in [J3]. We have also developed a collaborative discriminative feature learning model which consider modality consistency in terms of discriminability. This model further performs feature decontamination to enhance the robustness to large appearance changes. This work has been published in [C2]. We have proposed to integrate the point-to-set distance metric learning (DML) into visual tracking tasks to ensure that the distance metric is able to achieve the close and consistent matching between the tracked target and different training sample with different appearance changes. The metric learning model takes full advantage of all the training samples when determining the best target candidate [J2]. While most existing discriminative object tracking methods usually train a binary classifier via some binary classification scheme for target/background separation. The point-to-set DML is conducted on convolutional neural network features of the training data extracted from the starting frames. When a new frame comes, target candidates are first projected to the common subspace using the learned mapping functions, and then the candidate having the minimal distance to the target template sets is selected as the tracking result. Experiments are performed on several challenging videos, and the results show the proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art trackers. This work has been published in [J2]. Objective 3: To address the issues of label ambiguity and sample corruption in visual tracking, we have proposed a MIL-based Feature Template Learning Algorithm for object tracking model updating [C1]. This model takes the advantages of and integrates the robustness of spares representation and the flexibility of multiple instance learning into a probabilistic learning framework, which enables the tracker to separate out the corrupted samples and resolving label ambiguity caused by misaligned samples. In specific, we exploit the Laplacian distribution to model the outliers and derive the instance probability to be the positive sample (i.e. target sample) and the bag probability to be the positive bag, and then learn the feature template by maximizing bag-level-based posterior with logarithm operator under the framework of multiple instance learning. we have derived a learning algorithm to estimate the model parameters [J2]. Since the l_1 penalty function is non-differential, we first approximate the penalty function by a smooth function for tractable optimization, and then exploit the accelerated proximal gradient method to solve the problems. We have conducted extensive experiments on some challenging video sequences to validate the effectiveness of the proposed tracker. We find that the proposed tracker runs stably without drifting in most cases. Objective 4: We have developed a new long-term tracking dataset for the research community. With the success of tracking research in the past three decades, a number of algorithms with excellent performance for short sequence videos have been reported. However, in long-video sequence, these trackers may lose track of the target. Our developed HKBU LOng-term TRAcking Database (HKBU LOTRA) is a long-sequence video database with ground truth annotations, covering different variations in real-world scenarios. It contains 50 videos, each of which contains around 600 to 1200 frames. It covers different large appearance variations and background changes, which includes occlusion, illumination, cluttered background, pose variations. We also set up the webpage to enable the dataset publicly available. The link to the webpage is http://rds.comp.hkbu.edu.hk/lotra/.

12254316.label: Major findings and research outcome
12254316.value: In this project, we addressed the issues of robustness and re-detection in long-term tracking from several aspects. The major findings and research outcome are listed as follows. The references [J#] and [C#] refer to the journal paper number and conference paper number in Sections 8 and 9 of Part C, respectively. 1. We developed a spatial-temporal regularized correlation filter-based object re-detector [J4]. We implicitly estimate and model the positive and negative conditional distributions in an online manner by training and updating a correlation filters with adaptively selected reliable samples. We found that the clustered background can cause tracking drift problem, and tracking model updating with contaminated samples collected will degrade the tracking performance. Therefore, we incorporated the spatial-temporal regularization into the detector framework, in which the spatial regularization can help to suppress negative effect from the cluttered background while the temporal regularization enables the adaptive incorporation of reliable historical appearance cues to deal with appearance changes. 2. To achieve robust appearance modeling, we have developed a feature learning and fusion model based on multiple sparse representations which jointly considers the commonality and specificity of different visual cues (features) [J3]. We also found that incorporating the proximity information into the multiple sparse representation is beneficial, which can ensure the close matched feature template are utilized for target representation. Therefore, a novel proximity constraint is incorporated into the representation model for which we further develop an online LogDet Regularized Multiple Metric Learning Algorithm to learn the proximity metric. The algorithm can automatically preserve the positive definiteness of the metric without an inefficient projection onto semi-definite cone, which is suitable for efficient online visual tracking. We also derive the theoretical mistake bound and proved it in [J3]. We further extended the commonality (consistency) and diversity (specificity) modeling into object tracking problem with data of multiple modalities, by which we have developed a modality consistency feature template learning model [J3] and a collaborative discriminative learning model [C2] to enhance the robustness of multi-modality tracking in terms of representation ability and discriminability. We also found that close and consistent matching between the tracked target and different training samples with different appearance changes should be maintained under a proper distance metric during tracking. As such, we proposed a point-to-set metric learning algorithm to achieve this objective [J2]. We also found that dynamic model update [J1] could also improve the tracker’s robustness. 3. To address the issues of label ambiguity and sample corruption during model updating in tracking, we have proposed a MIL-based Feature Template Learning Algorithm for tracking model updating [C1]. We found that tracker updating model can be formulated into a probabilistic model. In this model, the outliers can be captured by Laplacian distribution, from which we can derive the instance probability to be the positive sample (i.e. target sample) and the bag probability to be the positive bag, and then learn the feature template by maximizing bag-level-based posterior with logarithm operator under the framework of multiple instance learning. All the above proposed algorithms and mathematical models are extensively validated in large-scale challenging dataset, which shows the effectiveness of the model.

12254316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12254316.value: This project addresses the robustness of long-term visual object tracking, which has a high commercial value. In this project, we have developed new algorithms to improve the robustness and the tracking accuracy on publicly available databases are encouraging. In order to further promote and translate the research results into practical applications, we will explore the collaboration with industry, in particular those companies working on computer vision. Along this line, we could further evaluate and fine-tune the proposed methods. It is hope that a prototype could be developed so that an impressive demonstration could be developed. Whenever possible, we will try to join the exhibition and present our research demonstration.

12254316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12254316.value: Visual object detection and tracking is the first step for many computer vision and pattern recognition applications, e.g. object recognition from videos captured by drone (unmanned aerial vehicle). While many research works have been done for object tracking, most of these work focuses on relatively short videos (less than one minute). In order to put the algorithms in practice, we have to perform long-term tracking. When the tracking process is longer, tracker’s robustness becomes an issue. This is what was researched in this project. Some new algorithms have been developed and proposed in this project to overcome these challenges.
