12258116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12258116.value: The graph model has been widely used to model complex relationships among entities. Examples include DBLP (citation relationships), Facebook (friend relationships) and the whole internet (link relationships). Many algorithms and systems are designed to work with these graphs. However, these graphs are growing more rapidly than the capacity of machines. For example, according to the statistics, in 2014, Facebook had more than 1 billion active users and more than 130 billion friendship edges. Just keeping all the edges of such a graph in memory would require hundreds of gigabytes. Moreover, the rate of increase of active users from 2014 to 2015 was 12%. Such a rate of growth makes it harder to work on these graphs as the main memory cannot hold the whole graphs and without careful design, a graph algorithm usually suffers from high latency when the graph has to be kept on disk. On the other hand, distributed systems are usually inefficient when dealing with many graph operations due to large communication costs. In this project, we focus on I/O efficient graph algorithms in which the size of the graph exceeds the size of the main memory and therefore the graph has to be kept on disk. The key issues we will investigate include graph storage, I/O efficient graph algorithms and system design. We aim to deal with operations on massive graphs by accessing only a small part of the whole. Previous studies usually consider subgraphs of the original graph iteratively with heuristic optimizations. Different from that, our methodologies focus on dividing and contracting these graphs to obtain a set of contracted graphs that can be used as the input to graph algorithms to reduce the cost. The contracted graphs are not certain to be the subgraphs of the original, but capture more structural properties. Under such a framework, we will design graph algorithms for different fundamental graph operations. In addition, we will integrate multiple graph operations to build a unified graph processing system. The importance of this project is in its exploration of a new framework for I/O efficient graph processing. We will concentrate on how to contract graphs, how to make the graph algorithms work with these graphs and how to design an effective indexing scheme to reduce the graph size. We will conduct extensive performance studies using real-world data in our prototype system to demonstrate the strength of our approach.

12258116.label: Realisation of objectives
12258116.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. To address the issues related to effective and efficient algorithms for massive graphs, we have proposed graph contraction & expansion framework, to reduce the graph size to be considered for various tasks. Objective 1 has been investigated in various forms in [1, 3, 4]. The graph contraction framework has found to be effective in many problems, including subgraph matching, graph traversal, etc. More specifically, graph contraction aims to reduce the graph size that needs to be concerned, and apply local searching in the contracted graph. After local searching, many redundant vertices and edges can be pruned. Our approaches are different from many existing works as many works focus on the graph partition problem, and our contracted graph may not be a subgraph of the original one. In [1], we propose to contract graph based on the neighbors of vertices. After contracting, the graph will contain only the candidates for the subgraph matching, and it transfers the access pattern on disk from random access to sequential access, which reduces the IO cost significantly. Regarding objective 2, we design the node centric operations and propose the library for graph analysis and query autocompletion tasks, and have been reported in [4, 5]. For analysis task, we analyze the access patterns and propose a lightweight library in [4]. In [5], we contract and maintain the query related patterns in the graph database. Regarding objective 3, we have developed many applications in [2, 6, 7]. In [2], the contracted graph is used to model the travel behavior of the users. Then we recommend alternative routes after expanding the graph. In [7], we further apply the ideas to divide the graph into private graphs and public graphs. The private one can be modeled as a contracted version of the original graph, and it satisfies the private concerns of the users. We further divide the graph into public and private graphs, so that they can be contracted in a different manner. The private graph depends on personal data and should be contracted locally, while public graph is open and the contracted version can also be published. Regarding objective 4, we have developed the system, and run many experiments on that. The results show that the contract & expand framework is efficient for various tasks, including cohesive subgraph exploration, graph traversal, route recommendation, subgraph matching etc. References: [1] Zhiwei Zhang, Hao Wei, Jianliang Xu, Byron Choi: GScan: Exploiting Sequential Scans for Subgraph Matching. 12258116.label: Major findings and research outcome
12258116.value: This proposal investigates a wide range of graph algorithms and applications. In [1, 4], we propose the basic node-centric algorithms based on the contraction & expansion frameworks. These algorithms are the basic operations for many graph applications, and we have released the code library of them. We found that, among all the massive real graphs, they have the power law property, and this property can affect the algorithm efficiency significantly. When the graph is too large to fit into the main memory, the degree-based contraction approaches can result in a much smaller graph whose size is less than 5GB in most cases. We have experimentally evaluated the techniques. The results show that by contracting graph and expanding the intermediate results, for the tasks including subgraph matching, graph traversal can save up to 50% of the time cost. We further construct several applications in [2, 6, 7]. The effectiveness and efficiency have been proved. * References are listed in Section 5.3.

12258116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12258116.value: Graphs are a powerful tool for a wide range of applications, including social networks, chemical databases, citation networks, knowledge graphs, etc. As the graph size is quite large and growing fast, there is an evident and pressing need to design efficient algorithms for these big graphs. Many existing works cannot be applied to massive graphs because they can generate a large number of I/O accesses if the graph is too large to fit into the memory. To overcome this, This proposal investigates a framework for basic graph algorithms, and these algorithms can help to improve many applications of graphs. We have developed contraction & expansion framework that proved to be effective for many basic operations like subgraph matching, graph traversal, etc. We have also designed a number of efficient algorithms for graph applications.

12305116.label: Project Objectives

12305116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12305116.value: In many countries, poor farmers farm marginal land that is not very fertile and prone to erosion. Farming such land has considerable negative environmental impacts (locally and downstream), and generates low incomes to the farmers. The country would benefit if such land was reforested, yet most countries do not have the financial resources to compensate farmers for the loss of agricultural income, and to finance reforestation. In this research we propose 1) to assess whether the value of the carbon sequestered by the trees can be used to finance reforestation and compensate farmers for their loss of agricultural incomes; 2) to determine the optimal rotation period of the trees, taking into consideration a) the value of the timber and related non-timber products, b) the value of the carbon and c) the opportunity cost of the land. The financial support for reforestation could come from carbon trading mechanisms (through Certified Emission Reductions [CER] and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation [REDD/REDD+]), which are being developed by the international community to help finance reforestation/afforestation. Fieldwork for this research will be carried out in Chongqing municipality in China, among farmers who joined the Grain for Green (GfG) programme. The GfG is the largest reforestation and rural development programme in the world, involving 32 million households, and costs over Yuan 400 billion. With the GfG programme, poor farmers are paid to reforest their marginal (mostly slope) land. The programme is presently being funded by the Chinese government, but the financial support is set to end. On the other hand, the Chinese government is planning to introduce a nation-wide carbon market by 2017. Our research will help the Chinese government assess the extent to which reforestation can be paid through carbon credits. Fieldwork will involve the collection and analysis of soil samples and surveys of the vegetation of reforested and not-reforested land, to determine the amount of carbon sequestered through reforestation since the program was first implemented, as well as socio-economic surveys of households, to assess the attitudes towards reforestation. Chongqing municipality has considerable environmental and socioeconomic diversity. Such diversity will allow the team to extrapolate the findings to the rest of China, as well as to other countries where farmers are farming degraded, marginal land. 很多国家里存在贫穷的农民在一些不太肥沃而且易于受到侵蚀的边际土地耕种的现象。耕种这样的土地不仅会对当地以及下游的环境产生相当大的负面影响，并且会降低农民收入。如果这些土地被用来重新造林，则会使国家受益。然而大部分国家没有财政资源来补贴给这些失去农业收入的农民和资助造林所需费用。这项研究包括两个方面：1.分析这些人工造林所产生的碳回收价值是否能被用来资助重新造林和补贴农民收入；2.确定这些树木的最佳轮伐期，从以下三点入手a.这些木材和相关的非木制产品的价值，b.碳回收的价值，c.土地的机会成本。重新造林的财政资助可以来源于国际社会认可的碳交易机制（核证减排量CER和从伐木和森林退化中减排REDD/REDD+） 这项研究的实地考察在中国的重庆直辖市进行，以参加“退耕还林”项目的农民为考察对象。“退耕还林”涉及了3200万户家庭，投入了4000亿元人民币，是世界上最大的重新造林和农村发展项目。这个项目通过付款给农民，让他们在边际土地（主要是坡地）上重新造林。项目所需资金目前由中国政府资助，但这项财政支持即将结束。另外，中国政府计划在2017年前在全国范围内引进碳交易市场。我们的研究将帮助中国政府评估从某种程度上再造林工程所需资金可以由碳交易来支付。实地考察将会收集并分析土壤样本，调查再造林地区和非再造林地区的植被，以此来确定这项首次实施的再造林工程的碳回收量。实地考察还会对住户的社会经济情况进行调查，来分析他们对重新造林的态度。重庆直辖市有着很高的环境多样性和社会经济多样性，如此的多样性也会有利于团队将此次研究成果推向中国其他地方，同时推向其他有农民在退化的边际土地上耕种的国家。

12305116.label: Realisation of objectives
12305116.value: All objectives of this research have been fully achieved. The fieldwork/data collection and analysis consisted of three different aspects: 1. Collection of soil samples Field data was collected for this study through physical measurement, field observation and laboratory analysis. We sampled 150 field plots across three subtropical zones (North subtropical zone, Middle subtropical zone and South subtropical zone). The sampling sites were in 6 provinces and 1 municipality, namely Anhui Province, Hubei Province, Hunan Province, Guizhou Province, Yunnan Province, Jiangxi Province and Chongqing Municipality. To estimate biomass carbon, at each site, at least three 10*10 m2 plots were sampled for tree measurement, identification and mapping. All stems in the tree layer were measured throughout the plot. We measured Diameter at Breast Height (DBH), then calculated height with a measuring tape and Clinometer. At each plot, undergrowth plants including shrubs and herbaceous plants were investigated. In addition, one subplot (1*1 m2) was randomly established in each subplot to measure litterfall biomass. For soil sample collection, three subplots (1*1m) in each sampling site were collected to measure organic carbon and bulk density at depth intervals of 0–20, 20–40 and 40-60 cm, using a soil auger. The samples were then transported in sealed aluminum foil to the laboratory for analysis. Soil samples were air-dried, hand-picked (to remove woody debris and charcoal, visible soil organisms, and stones), and weighed. Then the air-dried soil samples were sieved through a screen with 2 mm openings, and gravels (> 2 mm) were weighed. The carbon content of soils were measured using both a CN analyzer (PE- 2400 II; Perkin-Elmer) and the Walkley-Black wet digestion method. 2. Review of literature We supplemented the samples with a meta-analysis, with data from articles retrieved by searching Google Scholar and the Web of Science. This meta-analysis includes refereed articles which fulfil the following conditions. First, the studies had to either report the SOC value from soil depths of 0–20 cm, 20–40 cm or 40–60 cm, or at least three SOC stock data at different depths, so that we can extrapolate the missing values. Second, the study had to include a description of the land use history and provide the initial SOC stocks before afforestation or the SOC stocks of nearby non-forested sites. Third, the papers had to identify the planted tree species, plantation age and sampling depth. We reviewed over 300 studies and the final dataset comes from 90 peer-reviewed academic articles, and consists of 261 sites, including 261 topsoils (0–20 cm) and a large number of subsoils (168 from 20– 40 cm and 115 from 40–60 cm). Apart from SOC data, tree species, plantation age, soil sampling depth and soil bulk density, for each site, we recorded all geographical and climatic information, namely latitude, longitude, mean annual temperature and precipitation. 3. Socio-economic data Socio-economic data were collected through interviews with landowners in different regions from July to August 2018 and April to May 2019. To conduct the interviews, we firstly selected a region in terms of (i) abundance of the tree species we had selected, and (ii) physical accessibility. The landowners selected had to have plantations that fulfilled the following requirements: (i) monocultures, (ii) managed to ensure a survival rate of at least 70%, and (iii) no large-scale cutting. If these criteria were satisfied, farmers were interviewed using a questionnaire about the costs and benefits they experienced when planting and managing their plantation. Since labor costs varied substantially among different regions, we used the local labor costs in each region. This research has two components. First the carbon-sequestration by trees, and second the economic aspect of financing reforestation through carbon sequestration. We addressed the first component through fieldwork and a meta-analysis of the literature. Some of our conclusions are that: 1. Afforestation not only contributes to soil and water conservation on sloping land but also increases the SOC input from tree litterfall and root biomass, and therefore is an effective method of increasing SOC sequestration and retention. The present study shows afforesting steeply sloping land can sequester more SOC than afforesting slightly sloping land and there is a significant decrease in SOC stock after afforestation on gentle slopes (gradient lower than 10%). In the topsoil layer, slope gradient has a significant effect on the changes in SOC stock, while the effect is not significant in soil 40–60 cm deep. 2. Afforestation on sloping cropland results in an increase in SOC stock, especially in the upper soil. However, afforestation on grassland results in an increase in SOC stocks only on very steep slopes (gradient >60%). This indicates that the afforestation of sloping cropland is likely to result in greater SOC sequestration than the afforestation of sloping grassland, and it is suggested that only grassland on very steep slopes should be afforested. 3. Tree type has a limited effect on changes in SOC after afforestation on sloping land. Conifers show a greater SOC sequestration potential in deeper soils and on steep slopes with a gradient higher than 60%, while broadleaf trees sequester more SOC in the topsoil and on slopes with a gradient of 30–60%. The present study suggests that to increase SOC sequestration, the greatest benefit would result from the afforestation of cropland with conifer trees on steep slopes. The second component of this project provides a comprehensive economic valuation of carbon sequestration by afforestation projects in China considering ecological trees, economic trees and bamboo. Some of our conclusions are as follows: 1. Economic trees sequester less carbon than ecological trees and bamboo. Among economic trees, nut trees sequester more carbon than fruit trees. The regional context significantly influences the carbon sequestration potential with more carbon sequestered in southern and eastern regions than in northern parts. Bamboo also shows a remarkable carbon sequestration potential, which is even higher than Chinese fir and poplar in northern regions. 2. Generally, it is less attractive to afforest highly productive cropland because of the high opportunity costs. 3. Tree product revenues differ depending on the tree species, which results in a significant variation of economic net benefits. However, our results also show that no compensation is needed to convert most cropland to forest, unless the forest replaces cropland with relatively high revenues. 4. For ecological trees, afforestation is profitable if farmers harvest the timber after the normal rotation period of each tree species. Furthermore, with the recent increase of timber demand in China, the timber price has increased substantially, which makes afforestation projects even more attractive. 5. For economic trees, the amount of carbon sequestered is low, but selling fruits and nuts is quite profitable. Therefore, in most cases, there is no compensation needed for afforestation efforts. Further, our study suggests that bamboo afforestation can become economically more attractive, when carbon revenues are included. The same holds for other afforestation alternatives which require compensations. 6. If the carbon credits generated would be traded, e.g., in a Chinese carbon market, the opportunity costs of alternative land uses could be fully compensated, except for afforestation on highly attractive cropland. However, considering the uncertain development of future China’s carbon credit demand and supply, it could be advantageous to trade Certified Emission Reductions (CERs) generated by China’s afforestation projects in an international emission trading system.

12305116.label: Major findings and research outcome
12305116.value: 1. Forests have huge potential of both generating timber and storing carbon in a joint production process. Thus, countries can adopt afforestation projects as a means to achieve poverty alleviation and environmental protection goals, particularly in reducing atmospheric carbon dioxide. 2. Applying a modified Hartman rotation model, our results show that the optimal rotation period increases for all species when considering the joint production of timber and carbon sequestration. 3. The carbon accounting regime has a significant impact on the optimum rotation. For Eucalyptus, using Long-term CER (lCER) accounting lengthens the rotation period by 60% compared to only 20% using temporary CER (tCER) accounting. In contrast, for Chinese fir, using tCER accounting increases the rotation period by three years more than using lCER accounting. Further, the carbon value has a minimal impact on the optimal rotation period of Poplar plantations. 4. The present value of lCER revenues is three to four times higher than those generated by tCER for the same plantation in the initial 5 to 10 years. In contrast, when the project period extends to 30 years, the present value of lCER revenues is at least two times lower than the present value of tCERs. Therefore, forest managers have an incentive to apply tCER accounting to finance slow-growing plantations and lCER for fast-growing trees. 5. Our results further illustrate that the optimal rotation decision is sensitive to changes in both carbon prices and discount rates but with different sensitivity among plantation species and between carbon accounting regimes. The optimal decision of slow-growing species is highly sensitive to the changes of carbon price or discount rate under tCER accounting. However, the optimal decision for fast growing species is more sensitive under lCER accounting. For example, the optimal rotation period of Eucalyptus increases from 5 years to 12 years when the price of carbon increases from USD 0 to USD 30, and it experiences only a one-year extension of the optimal rotation period when the discount rate is reduced from 6% to 2%. Although the results show that lCER accounting is beneficial with respect to the economic and ecological impact of the fast-growing plantations, the lower flexibility of the lCER regime may reduce its feasibility in practice. Our research can contribute to the design of carbon sequestration projects in China. The methodology and results can be adapted and transferred to other regions in the developing world.

12305116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12305116.value: We have identified a number of research gaps, which we aim to address in a future research: a) In our research we only looked at incomes per unit of land (hectares). However, equally important are incomes per unit of labour (labour day), since widespread migration has resulted in labour, not land, becoming the scarcest resource. b) We did not set out to specifically look at particular factors which affect Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) sequestration rates. Our meta-analysis let us to conclude that these factors were also ignored by many other researchers. These include (i) Slope gradient, position and aspect: usually slope land is less productive and its reforestation has greater environmental benefits, so most reforestation takes place on slope land. Yet less research is done on change in SOC stock following reforestation. (ii) Fertilisers and pesticides: they are usually applied during crop cultivation and the first years of tree cultivation, but are usually ignored in analyses of SOC stock. c) While our research generally concluded that a market for carbon would help reforestation and poverty alleviation, creating such a market, and linking it to the nationwide carbon market that is being planned in China, would be a new endeavour.

12305116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12305116.value: In many countries, poor farmers farm marginal land that is not very fertile and prone to erosion. Farming such land has considerable negative environmental impacts, and generates low incomes to the farmers. The country would benefit if such land was reforested, yet most countries do not have the financial resources to compensate farmers for the loss of agricultural income, and to finance reforestation. In this research we 1) assessed whether the value of the carbon sequestered by the trees can be used to finance reforestation and compensate farmers for their loss of agricultural incomes; 2) determined the optimal rotation period of the trees, taking into consideration a) the value of the timber and related non-timber products, b) the value of the carbon and c) the opportunity cost of the land. The financial support for reforestation could come from carbon trading mechanisms (through Certified Emission Reductions [CER] and Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation [REDD/REDD+]), which are being developed by the international community to help finance reforestation/afforestation. Fieldwork involved the collection and analysis of soil samples in 150 field plots, and socio-economic data of farmers, across six provinces and one municipality in China.

12306616.label: Project Objectives

12306616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12306616.value: One of the core and important research problems in information retrieval is to evaluate importance or popularity of objects that can assist to handle many data mining tasks. For instance, we employ ranking for input query in a search engine or extract relevant communities in a social network. PageRank algorithm is well-known and useful to determine the importance of nodes in a directed graph which represents WWW of hyperlinks among webpages. PageRank algorithm is used to compute a stationary probability distribution of a modified first-order Markov Chain arising from the directed graph. Higher-order Markov chains are successfully used to study successive links among nodes for important data link analysis, e.g., successive citations of researchers in publication network and successive links of webpages in web network. The main challenge is to solve a very large matrix system especially when the number of nodes and/or the order is large. For example, when the order is two and the number of nodes is 10000, the matrix size would be of hundred million by hundred million. Many such large-scale applications can be found in web analysis, publication networks, social networks and bioinformatics. The most important and distinguished feature of higher-order Markov chains is that their transition probability matrices are sparse. The main aims of this project are to formulate sparse multilinear PageRank problems, and develop efficient algorithms for computing higher-order stationary probabilities. Our idea is to study the sparsity nature of the solution. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first attempt to address sparse solutions for sparse Markov chains. By making use of sparse approximation to solution, we can determine the approximation by formulating and solving a sparse optimization problem. Both computational and storage cost can be significantly reduced. Theoretically, we analyze the error bound of the approximation to solution. For sparse optimization problems, we develop an alternating minimization algorithm to solve it. The convergence analysis will be studied and analyzed. We also will use real data sets to demonstrate the effectiveness and usefulness of the proposed algorithm. We extend our idea to study sparse approximation to ranking scores of node-to-node and node-to-relation in coupled Markov chains arising from multi-relational data. We will analyze the error bound of the proposed sparse approximation. A sparse optimization problem can be formulated and iterative algorithm can be designed. The information retrieval data will be tested to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed formulation and algorithm. 信息檢索的核心和重要研究之一問題是評估重要性或受歡迎,可以幫助處理許多數據挖掘任務的對象。舉例來說, 我們採用了搜索引擎排名進行輸入查詢或提取相關社交網絡。網頁排名是有用的算法, 確定有向圖表示的WWW節點的重要性取決於網頁中的超鏈接。 網頁排名算法其實是用來計算一階馬爾可夫鏈的概率分佈。 高階馬爾可夫鏈被成功用於研究中連續鏈接為重要的數據鏈路的分析,例如在研究人員的連續引文節點網絡出版和網絡的網頁鏈接續。主要的挑戰是解決一個非常大的矩陣系統特別是當節點的數目和/或順序是非常大的。例如，當節點的數量是一萬, 矩陣尺寸是一億。許多這樣的大規模應用可以在網絡分析,發布網絡,社交網絡和生物信息學。 高階馬爾可夫鏈的最重要和最顯著特徵是,他們的轉移概率矩陣是稀疏。項目的主要目的是制定稀疏的多線性網頁排名的問題，並制定有效的算法計算高階平穩概率。我們的想法是研究稀疏的多線性網頁排名,通過利用稀疏逼近來解決高階馬爾可夫鏈,據我們所知,這是第一次嘗試解決稀疏馬爾可夫鏈方案。計算和存儲成本可以顯著降低。從理論上講,我們分析結合的近似解決方案。對於稀疏優化的問題，我們開發的交替最小化算法來解決它。項目進行收斂分析研究。我們也將使用真實數據集來演示有效性和算法的有效性。 我們進行稀疏逼近學習到的節點到節點的得分排名和節點到關係在從多關係數據而產生的耦合馬爾可夫鏈。 我們將分析結合所提出的稀疏逼近的誤差。稀疏優化問題可以配製和迭代算法可設計。信息檢索數據將被測試驗證效率和算法。

12306616.label: Realisation of objectives
12306616.value: In this project, we developed a fast algorithm for ﬁnding stationary joint probability distributions of sparse Markov chains or multilinear PageRank vectors which arise from data mining applications. In these applications, the main computational problem is to calculate and store solutions of many unknowns in joint probability distributions of sparse Markov chains. We have developed an algorithm to determine solutions by formulating and solving sparse and rank-one optimization problems via closed form solutions. The convergence of the truncated power method was established. Numerical examples of multilinear PageRank vector calculation and second-order web-linkage analysis were presented to show the efficiency of our proposed method. It is shown that both computation and storage are signiﬁcantly reduced by comparing with the traditional power method. Moreover, we analyzed relations ranking and object classiﬁcation for multi-relational data where objects are interconnected by multiple relations. We developed an algorithm, which is able to determine the ranking of relations and the labels of objects simultaneously. A set of tensor equations was required to obtain the stationary distribution of relations and objects via our proposed algorithm. We compared our algorithm with current collective classiﬁcation algorithms on two real-world data sets and the experimental results show the superiority of our method. Furthermore, the coupled scheme was studied under multi-domain or multi-view network association by using multiple graph clustering. We analyzed block Laplacian matrices and their eigenvalues and eigenvectors for different data mining and machine learning applications. The graph was introduced in manifold regularization on mapping to capture the intrinsic structure among data, which provides a good way to reduce the required labelled data with improving the classiﬁcation performance in many machine learning applications

12306616.label: Major findings and research outcome
12306616.value: In this project, we have published seven papers (six journal papers and one conference paper). In Research Output [1], We have studied a fast algorithm for finding stationary joint probability distributions of sparse Markov chains or multilinear PageRank vectors which arise from data mining applications. We have formulated the problem by approximating large-scale solutions of such sparse Markov chains by two components: the sparsity component and the rank-one component. In Research Output [4], we have shown the uniqueness multilinear PageRank vectors and demonstrated the required conditions. In Research Output [6,7], several applications in real data have been tested to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. In Research Output [2,3], we have studied and analyzed alternating minimization algorithms for solving sparse optimization problems arising from multilinear PageRank problems in machine learning and computer vision. In Research Output [2,5,7], we have studied and analyzed sparse coupled Markov chains and formulate optimization problems for co-ranking scheme from multi-relational data via multiple graph clustering.

12306616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12306616.value: Graph Convolutional Networks are extensively studied in recent years. Most of existing approaches are designed for the homogenous graphs with a single type of relation. However, heterogeneous graphs of multiple types of relations are also ubiquitous and there is a lack of methodologies to tackle such graphs. Some previous studies address the issue by performing conventional Graph Convolutional Networks on each single relation and then blending their results. However, as the convolutional kernels neglect the correlations across relations, the strategy is sub-optimal. In the future research, we plan to study the Multi-Relational Graph Convolutional Network framework by developing a novel higher Markov chain operator on multi-relational graphs. In particular, our high dimension Markov chain operator extends the graph spectral analysis into the eigen-decomposition of a Laplacian tensor. And the eigen-decomposition is formulated with a generalized tensor product, which can correspond to any mathematical transformation for analysis.

12306616.value: One of the core and important research problems in information retrieval is to evaluate importance or popularity of objects that can assist to handle many data mining tasks. PageRank algorithm developed by Google is well-known and useful to determine the importance of nodes in a directed graph. PageRank algorithm is used to compute a stationary probability distribution of a modified first-order Markov Chain arising from the directed graph. Recently, higher-order Markov chains are successfully used to study successive links among nodes for important data link analysis. The most important and distinguished feature of these higher-order Markov chains is that their transition probability matrices are sparse. Our research results are to employ sparse multilinear PageRank to deal with large-scale applications in web analysis, publication networks, social networks and bioinformatics. We have successfully developed sparse optimization algorithms for multilinear PageRank to compute high-order stationary probabilities for sparse multilinear PageRank problems, and conducted numerical comparison to demonstrate our proposed method can be useful in many data mining and machine learning applications.

12308416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12308416.value: There is a growing body of evidence showing that extracellular vesicles (EVs) play a critical role on pathological and physiological processes including inflammation, tumor growth and immune responses. Intensified research interest has been drawn to explore the potential medical applications of EVs, for instances as biomarkers for early disease diagnosis and monitoring since they contain ample disease related nucleic acids and proteins. EVs can be easily accessible from body fluids, such as blood, cerebral spinal fluid, saliva and urine; Among the EVs, exosomes (40-200 nm in size) are secreted after mutivesicular and subsequent membrane fusion. These small vesicles carry rich information of the biological functions including cell-cell communication, signaling, inflammation, tumor metastasis etc. However the understandings on exosome signal proteins and nucleic acids (in particular mRNA and microRNA) are still very limited due to the lack of accurate and fast isolation and purification of the exosomes of interest. Existing isolation and detection methods of exosomes are mainly based differential centrifugation, flow cytometry, dynamic light scattering, immunoblotting, and ELISA techniques. However, detection of EVs with high sensitivity still remains a great challenge. Highly sensitive, reliable and simple assays for exosome quantification and analysis will surely facilitate the mechanism studies of disease development. Based on our rich experiences on developing sensors for biomarkers quantification, here we propose to develop a highly promising platform for direct, high-throughput expression profiling of circulating cancer-derived exosomes in body fluids. The detection is based on the specific immuno-interaction between the antibody probe and the surface proteins on the target disease-derived exosomes. The captured exosomes will be collected for further analysis including surface proteins profiling and miRNAs profiling for disease diagnosis; as well as drug responses for the therapeutics screening and development. Neither offline sample enrichment nor purification is required for such a sensitive and selective detection and analysis. As a proof-of-concept, urine samples and serum of prostate cancer (PCa) associated exosomes will be our focus. We anticipate the proposed assay will be rapid, simple, highly specific and sensitive. The assay will not only be useful for the isolation and detection of exosomes, but also readily feasible for analysis of other EVs, including microvesicles and apoptotic bodies. The success of the project would provide a tool for exosome extraction and novel insight for EV based molecular diagnosis, cancer signaling pathways and therapeutic opportunities of EVs. 越來越多的證據顯示，胞外囊泡（EVs）在炎症，腫瘤的生長和免疫反應等病理和生理過程中扮演著的關鍵角色。許多研究致力於探索胞外囊泡（EVs）潛在的醫學應用前景，例如由於其含有充足與疾病相關的核酸和蛋白質，胞外囊泡（EVs）可以作為生物標誌物用於早期疾病診斷和監測。胞外囊泡（EVs）很容易從如血液，腦脊髓液，唾液和尿液等體液中獲得；作為胞外囊泡的一種，外泌體（大小為40-200 nm）是由多泡分泌後膜融合而成。這些微小的囊泡攜帶了大量的生物學功能信息，例如細胞與細胞間的通信，信號傳遞信息，炎症，腫瘤轉移等。然而，由於缺乏對目標外泌體準確、快速的分離及純化技術，我們對外泌體信號蛋白質和核酸（特別是mRNA和microRNA）的認知仍然非常有限。現有的外泌體分離和檢測方法主要基於梯度離心、流式細胞數、光動態散射、免疫印跡和酶聯免疫吸附測定（ELISA）技術。然而，發展具有靈敏度的胞外囊泡（EVs）檢測技術仍然是一個很大的挑戰。發展針對外泌體的高靈敏性，可靠性和簡易分析方法必將促進疾病的發展機制研究。基於我們已有的發展定量生物標誌物傳感器的豐富經驗，在此我們提出建立了一個非常有應用前景的平台，用於體液中直接、高通量表達分析循環腫瘤細胞分泌的外泌體。該方法的檢測原理是基於抗體探針和目標疾病產生的外泌體表面蛋白之間的特異性免疫相互作用。捕獲的外泌體將被收集用於進一步分析，這其中包括用於疾病診斷的表面蛋白分析和miRNA分析以及用於治療劑篩选和開發的藥物響應性分析。在這個靈敏的，選擇性的檢測和分析過程中，不需要離線的樣品分離和純化。為了進行該方法的概念驗證，我們選取前列腺癌（PCA）患者尿樣和血樣中的相關外泌體作為目標分析物。我們預計該方法具有快速，簡單，高特異性和靈敏性。該方法不僅可用於外泌體的分離和檢測，也可用於微泡和凋亡小體等其它胞外囊泡（EVs）的分析。該項目的成功將會提供一種外泌體的提取工具，並為基於胞外囊泡（EVs）的分子診斷，癌症信號通路和胞外囊泡（EVs）治療機會提供了新穎的見解。

12308416.label: Realisation of objectives
12308416.value: All three objectives were satisfactorily realized. Objective 1 has been fully achieved and reported in the mid-term report. For objective 2 and 3, we have the following results supporting the achievement of the objectives. We have demonstrated an ultrasensitive single vesicle imaging and detection platform with TIRF microscopy for quantitative analysis of target tumor Exos by building molecular-recognition-based ﬂuorescent DNA nanodevices in situ on target Exo surfaces. This TIRF assay is able to directly visualize and quantify circulating PTK7-Exo in plasma without any isolation and puriﬁcation steps and oﬀers multiple advantages (such as high sensitivity, a broad dynamic range, high throughput, little sample consumption, and low reagent cost) over a conventional ELISA. The TIRF assay for plasma PTK7-Exos is also informative in staging tumor progression and in monitoring early responses to treatment. In addition, with the ability to directly determine the quantiﬁcation and stoichiometry of target Exos in plasma at the single-vesicle level, the developed TIRF imaging platform opens the door to better understanding the roles of Exos in cell−cell communication in oncogenesis and tumor heterogeneity, oﬀering the possibility for early diagnosis of diseases including but not restricted to cancers and for designing personalized treatment regimens. Details were reported in Analytical Chemistry (2019), 91(4), 2768-2775. We developed a TIRF imaging platform that successfully achieves in situ quantification and accurate stoichiometry determination of the miRNA contents of nanosized EXs at the single-vesicle level by applying recent advancements in DNA nanotechnology. The rationally designed DNA probes can easily enter nanosized EXs mediated by SLO and selectively bind with exosomal target miRNAs to produce a readable fluorescence signal for the TIRF imaging analysis of individual EXs. Moreover, AuNPs-CD63apt nanocomposite probes were constructed to quantify the total EXs for the stoichiometric analysis of miRNAs associated with EXs. Compared with other methods such as qRT-PCR and flow cytometry, the TIRF assay is a single-vesicle in situ exosomal miRNA detection strategy with low serum consumption, simple procedure, short analysis time and low reagent cost. Moreover, the developed TIRF assay can directly determine the stoichiometry and composition of EXs in complex clinical serum samples to obtain insightful information about EX-mediated cell-cell communication. Based on these advantages, the TIRF assay is superior to conventional qRT-PCR for the detection of circulating exosomal miRNAs. The TIRF imaging assay can be easily refined for clinical use and readily adapted for the diagnosis and monitoring of other disease-specific miRNAs associated with EXs. Further studies demonstrated that the TIRF imaging assay for miR-21-EXs can discriminate cancer patients (melanoma, breast cancer and cervical cancer) from healthy subjects. The miR-21-EX level was also informative for detecting tumor progression and treatment responses. We thus propose that a TIRF miR-21-EX serum assay may have significant value as a cancer screening test because a rapid, accurate, noninvasive and inexpensive serum test for early cancer diagnosis could improve early detection rates and thereby patient outcomes. Therefore, our results indicate that the TIRF imaging assay, in addition to being a novel liquid biopsy platform for the detection of tumor-specific miRNA biomarkers in circulating EXs, may aid the diagnosis of a variety of diseases and the monitoring of early responses to treatment, which are important for new drug development and personalized treatment. (reported in Theranostics (2019), 9(15), 4494-4507.)

12308416.label: Major findings and research outcome
12308416.value: We developed and reported an ultrasensitive assay that can directly visualize and quantify tumor exosomes (Exo) in plasma microsamples (1 μL) at the single-vesicle level. The assay uses the specific binding of activatable aptamer probes (AAP) to target Exo captured by Exo-specific antibodies on the surface of flow cell to produce an activated fluorescence. Furthermore, the bound AAP triggers in situ assembly of DNA nanodevice with an enhanced fluorescence that improves the Exo detection sensitivity. By identifying tyrosine-protein kinase-like 7 (PTK7), total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) assay for PTK7-Exo distinguishes target tumors from control subjects. This assay is also informative in monitoring tumor progression and early responses to therapy. The developed assay can be readily adapted for diagnosis and monitoring of other disease-associated Exo biomarkers. Results were reported in Analytical Chemistry (2019), 91(4), 2768-2775.) In additions, a TIRF-based single-vesicle imaging assay was developed for direct visualization and quantification of the single-vesicles of EXs and their miRNA contents in serum microsamples. The assay uses co-delivery of inactive split DNAzymes and fluorescence-quenched substrates into nanosized EXs treated with streptolysin O to produce a target miRNA-activated catalytic cleavage reaction that amplifies the readout of fluorescence signal. We perform the in situ quantitative and stoichiometric analysis of serum exosomal hsa-miRNA-21 (miR-21), a common cancer biomarker, by using the developed TIRF imaging assay. The TIRF imaging assay for serum exosomal miR-21 can distinguish cancer patients from healthy subjects with better performance than conventional real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assay. The exosomal miR-21 level in serum is also informative for monitoring tumor progression and responses to treatment. Moreover, the TIRF assays can readily determine the precise stoichiometry of target exosomal miRNA contents in situ by delivering molecular beacon (MB) probes into EXs. (reported in Theranostics (2019), 9(15), 4494-4507. Analyst, 2018, 143, 813 - 816. ) The created TIRF imaging platform shows high applicability to serve as a universal and useful tool for the single-vesicle in situ quantitative and stoichiometric analysis of other disease-associated exosomal miRNAs markers and protein biomarkers; and is highly applicable to the treatment evaluation.

12309516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12309516.value: Despite the clinical success of several anti-cancer prodrugs (pharmacologically inactive forms of drugs that can be subsequently activated through normal metabolic processes) with improved cancer selectivity, water solubility and cell permeability, there is an unmet need to achieve the desired pharmacokinetics with minimal adverse side effects, coupled with the ability to monitor in-vitro/in-vivo. Most anti-cancer pro-drugs are distributed non-specifically throughout the body and their most effective dosage is questionable. Given the recent development of theranostic technology, where therapeutics and diagnostics are combined, we envision that developing theranostic prodrugs with responsive signals in-vitro/in-vivo can afford a promising solution to address this issue. Recently, we reported a ‘proof-of-concept’, two-photon-induced cleavable platinum–europium complex (PtEuL) which holds great promises as a controlled delivery vehicle for the drug, cisplatin. It offers real-time monitoring of the therapeutic process and the long-lived lanthanide emission allows time-resolved imaging, free from autofluorescence. We will use our experience and knowledge in peptide chemistry to trace the integrin avβ3 isoform in bladder cancer, thereby developing a route to bladder cancer-specific prodrug agents. Photo-triggered therapy coupled to optical imaging is most suitable for cancer cells located close to the skin surface/on exposed organs. Our design of multimodal theranostic prodrugs against bladder cancer encompasses three different synthetic approaches. It combines cancer specificity and permeability, with sufficient ‘dark stability’ and harnesses the two-photon-induced dissociation of the cisplatin coupled to responsive europium emission that permits imaging studies to enable quantitative evaluation of the time-dependent fate of the prodrug. Four key ‘proof-of-concept’ experiments have been undertaken done in support of this proposal: (i) two new europium complexes have been synthesized (peptide ligated in cis – N1 and trans-N7, N1-Pt-Eu-L1-P1 and N7-Pt-Eu-L1-P1) for evaluating the binding with the integrin avβ3; (ii) the design of each complex has been optimised following molecular docking simulations; (iii) binding between the designed prodrug and the integrin avβ3 isoform has been estimated via Western blots methods and selectivity towards bladder cancer confirmed by MTT assays/preliminary imaging studies; (iv) two photon-induced quantitative delivery assays have been carried out with the comparison of the light dosed-emission intensity-N1-Pt content, establishing the linearity of this relationship. Our goal is to develop a library of compounds with photo-dissociable prodrugs and target specificity by the use of different vectors for clinical application. We intend to translate our knowledge in chemical syntheses-biochemistry-lanthanide chemistry into practical and responsive biomedical probes, serving as a drug-delivery vehicle capable of being monitored in real-time. 儘管市面上已經有幾種具有治療癌症的臨床抗癌前體藥物（前體藥物本身沒有藥理活性，但可以通過正常的代謝過程活化產生具有藥理活性的藥），並且這類前體藥物的癌症選擇性、水溶性和細胞通透性都經過改良，然而它們仍然有不可忽略的毒副作用，而且它們在生物體內的分佈以及藥代動力學不能夠實施地追蹤與監控。這類前體藥物對腫瘤組織沒有選擇性，它們往往非特異性地分佈在整個身體中，其最有效的劑量是為人所質疑的。 考慮到診療技術(將治療和診斷合併於一體的技術)的最近發展，我們團隊致力開發具有在體外/體內回應信號的前體藥物，希望為上述問題提供一個解決方案。最近，我們報導了一項初步的“概念驗證”的研究工作，在這項工作中我們利用雙光子誘導的可裂解的銪-鉑配合物（PtEuL）作為順鉑釋放的前體藥物。我們設計的前體藥物在光至裂解之後釋放順鉑的同時生成可產生光至螢光信號的新的銪配合物（EuL）。EuL產生螢光信號可用於順鉑釋放以及治療過程的即時監控，同時長壽命的銪發光信號可以結合時間分辨成像技術有效過濾掉生物自體螢光對成像的干擾。 我們將利用多年來我們在多肽化學中的知識與經驗來設計可以靶向追蹤膀胱癌細胞過度表達的整合素avβ3蛋白，從而開發出一種到膀胱癌特異性前體藥物。這一設計非常符合光誘導療法與光學影像診斷最適於靠近皮膚表面的腫瘤組織的研究與治療這一特點。我們的設計的多模式的前體診療藥物能以簡便合成方法獲取。同時它結合了膀胱癌的選擇特異性、良好的腫瘤細胞通透性、較強的暗穩定性、雙光子誘導釋放順鉑的敏感性以及釋放過程中可以產生的稀土金屬銪的回應發光信號等特點。其中最大的優點是前體藥物釋放過程中銪的回應發光信號用於順鉑釋放的定量監控與分析。 我們的團隊已經進行了四個關鍵的“概念驗證”實驗來支持此專案計畫書： （1）我們設計合成了兩個新的銪-鉑配合物來評估其與整合素avβ3蛋白的結合能力。 （2）利用分子對接以優化對前體藥物配合物的設計。 （3）設計合成的前體藥物與整合素avβ3蛋白的結合能力通過螢光滴定、MTT毒性測試以及初步的成像分析得以評估。 （4）光誘導的順鉑定量釋放實驗研究了誘導光劑量與銪發光強度的線性關係。 我們的目標是開發一種腫瘤靶向性的光誘導釋放前體藥物的分字形檔以用於臨床的應用。我們致力於將我們在化學合成、生物化學以及稀土化學方面的知識轉化成切實可用的生物醫藥回應探針，用於一種可以即時監控其藥物釋放的前體藥物或藥物載體。

12309516.label: Realisation of objectives
12309516.value: Objective 1. To design and synthesize a series of biocompatible lanthanide complexes/materials which can selectively differentiate cancer cells; Three series of lanthanide complexes (total 15 lanthanide complexes) are synthesized for bladder cancer therapy. First series – Porphyrin-containing compounds have been representative examples of PDT drugs for decades. In this project, we prepared three porphyrinato-gadolinium complexes Gd-PEG-Rn (n = 1–3). They belong to a family of porphyrinato Gd(III) complexes based on R1, where a protective Kläui’s ligand is connected to alpha-v-beta3 integrin-targeting peptide (cQDGRMGFc) via a polyethylene glycol (PEG) and N-heterocyclic linker. R3 is based on R2 with improved water solubility through the conjugation with an extra RrRK amino acid sequence. (Adv. Therapeutics, 2019, 1900068) Second Series – We designed and prepared 12 cyclen-based lanthanide complexes and conjugated them to a ruthenium(II) or platinum(II) complex to yield prodrugs for cancer therapy with imaging capabilities (optical or magnetic resonance imaging depending on the lanthanide center of choice). These dual-functional complexes can be traced quantitatively in real time through imaging and have a low dark toxicity, which is ideal as prodrugs as the therapeutic effect only begins upon controlled photoactivation when they reach the designated regions of interest. (J. Med. Chem., 2017, 8923; Nanotheranostics, 2017, 186) Third Series – We prepared a micelle using amphiphilic molecular lanthanide-cyclen complexes through self-assembly. By using Yb and Gd complexes for micelle formation, the nanoplatform could achieve near-infrared (NIR) and magnetic resonance (MR) imaging capabilities. Optimization of the dual-imaging properties is done by precise control of the Ln ratio. To include anti-cancer properties, the lanthanide-cyclen complexes were conjugated to camptothecin (CPT), a well-known anti-cancer drug via a disulfide bond; the release CPT encapsulated in the micelle can be triggered by the cleavage of the disulfide bond under redox reactions. (ACS Applied Nano Materials, 2020, accepted). Objective 2. To develop complexes whose delivery can be visualized using a non-toxic excitation wavelength in which release of the cytotoxic cisplatin is triggered selectively upon reaching the overexpressed bladder cancer specific membrane receptor- alpha-v-beta3 isoform; First series – For the first series of complexes, we investigated their photodynamic therapy (PTT) inhibition efficacy on various cell lines, namely HeLa (cervical cancer), T24 (bladder cancer) and MRC-5 (normal lung cells). As expected for light-activated PTT, the dark toxicities of the complexes in all cell lines are quite low. However, upon light irradiation, the complexes became highly cytotoxic towards T24 cells, as demonstrated by their low IC50 value. This can be attributed by the selectivity of our complexes towards bladder cancer cells. Furthermore, R3 complex was shown to be the most effective of all and we believe its due to the RrRK sequence which improved its water solubility. Second Series – The prodrugs developed in Objective 1 also has imaging capabilities. By using 350 nm (or 700 nm if two-photon excitation is used) excitation, Eu(III) emission with long emission lifetimes can be observed and used for monitoring the drug release which is triggered using a 488 nm excitation. A quantitative evaluation of the drug delivery process was established through the linear relationship obtained between the concentration of the released anti-cancer drug and the Eu(III) luminescence or structural information from ESI-MS. Third Series – Following the positive results from in vitro drug release studies, we subsequently confirmed the localization of the CPT released from our nanoplatforms by co-staining experiments. Results revealed that the overlapping of the red and blue emissions in HeLa cells represented that both the lanthanide complex and the released CPT were located in the mitochondrion whereas in MRC-5 cells, the MitoTracker Red’s emission did not overlap with the blue emission from CPT, thus proving the cancer selectivity of CPT. Objective 3. To run comprehensive NIR imaging and real-time analysis (emission) of cisplatin released in-vitro; First series – Upon excitation, the porphyrinato chromophore gave red emission inside T24 cells, but no fluorescence was observed in HeLa and MRC-5 cells, demonstrating their in vitro selectivity brought about by the targeting peptide to alpha-v-beta3 integrin. The peptide was also responsible for the more intense fluorescence from Gd-PEG-R3 as it imparted higher water-solubility and biocompatibility. The intracellular localization profiles of the complexes were studied by co-staining experiments with LysoTracker. Overlapping of the green fluorescence from LysoTracker and the red fluorescence from our R2 and R3 complexes confirms localization in lysosomes, with Pearson’s coefficients of 0.394 and 0.279 respectively. Second series – The light-induced cytotoxicity of 12 PtEuL and RuEuL dual functional luminescent prodrug complexes were assessed under identical experimental conditions: 30 min of 488 nm laser irradiation (7 mW) in pure water. The observation of red Eu(III) luminescence in RuEuL solutions after 15 min indicated possible structural dissociation whereas none was observed in PtEuL. The same was observed in culture studies with HeLa cells. It was found that the intensity of Eu(III) luminescence was linearly related to the time of irradiation, suggesting increased Ru(II) dissociation against time. With the Ru(II) drug released after 15 mins of irradiation, cell lysis was detected suggesting severe cell damage. On the other hand, neither cell damage nor Eu(III) luminescence was observed for the PtEuL series, indicating that at 488 nm, cisplatin could not be released from PtEuL. Third series – The cellular uptake properties of the micellar nanoplatform was examined by confocal imaging. After incubation in HeLa cells for 24 hours, the emissions from CPT (visible light) and Yb complex (NIR) were both observed, implying efficient uptake and release in the tumor environment. Time-dependent confocal imaging was also carried out to assess the release profile of CPT against time. Objective 4. To evaluate the performance of our new delivery systems in-vitro/in-vivo. First series –The biodistribution studies of the three complexes were also performed with the same concentration injected into the caudal vein of the BALB/c nude mice. After 2 days, tissues and the tumor was collected and complexes were shown to localize in the tumor significantly more favorably than other tissues, thanks to our targeting peptide. Second series – Groups of two BALB/c nude mice carrying SW480 xenografts were injected 40 mirco-gram of RuEuL or RuEuL pre-activated by 488 nm radiation via intratumor injection and their body weight of the mice and size of tumor were monitors 3 times a week in 21 days. Results showed that the size of the tumor exhibited a 26.8% and 77.3% decrease for the groups of mice treated with RuEuL and pre-activated RuEuL respectively. In other words, tumor growth was inhibited by RuEuL treatment and the inhibitory effect was more significant when RuEuL was pre-activated to trigger drug release. Third series – By mixing the amphiphilic cycYb-ss-CPT and cycGd-ss-CPT, used for NIR and MR imaging respectively, in the self-assembly process, we were able to synthesize a dual-modality imaging nanocomposite system and optimize it by carefully controlling the ratio of the two complexes. The nanocomposites are highly dispersed in water and is extremely stable even at ultra-low concentrations (0.1 nM) over a prolonged period of time (17 days)in solution and ex vivo. Our nanocomposite system realizes the possibility of functional nanomedicine by offering real-time monitoring of drug delivery progress (MRI) and responsive tracking of drug release (NIR imaging) in cancer cells within a molecular hybrid self-assembled nanocomposite derived from amphiphilic cyclen-based lanthanide complexes.

12309516.label: Major findings and research outcome
12309516.value: In this project, we designed and developed a porphyrinato-gadolinium complex to serve as a dual-functional theranostic agent that could be used for PDT and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) simultaneously. We also conjugated a target-specific vector peptide to impart selectivity towards bladder cancer, tackling one of the major issues restricting the practicality of PDT agents: inability to discriminate between healthy and cancer cells. Exhaustive and successful fundamental studies in the first phase have allowed us to further investigate the performance of our gadolinium complexes in vivo. We found that our complex was able to accumulate in T24 bladder cancer cells but not HeLa or MRC-5 cell lines by monitoring the red emission from the porphyrinato chromophore. Specific interaction with the T24 cells was also indicated from a responsive, 17-times increase in T1 relaxivity in its MRI evaluation. The complexes’ PDT efficacy was determined by the photodynamic therapeutic index (PTI), which is 20-fold higher in T24 cells than the commercially available 5-aminolevulinic acid. Interestingly, though, there was no photodynamic inhibitory effect observed in HeLa cells, showing outstanding selectivity. These results have demonstrated huge potential for our complex Gd-PEG-R3 to become a new generation of dual functional anticancer PDT agent. We will try to extend our testing into pre-clinical and clinical practices. (Adv. Therapeutics, 2019, 1900068) In the second part of this project, we designed a ruthenium-europium complex (RuEuL) that can act as a prodrug with a low dark cytotoxicity. One of the major characteristic of RuEuL is that it can perform different actions by controlling the excitation light. Upon light irradiation at 488 nm, RuEuL is able to release an anticancer drug, thereby achieving light-triggered cytotoxicity. On the other hand, excitation at 350 nm (single-photon) or 700 nm (two-photon) will yield red and long-lived europium luminescence for real-time monitoring of the location of RuEuL and drug release quantitatively. The two-photon excitation property has allowed us to tackle the problem of poor tissue penetration of excitation light in the visible light spectrum. We believe with the use of a femtosecond laser and an animal imaging apparatus, in vivo real-time imaging could be easily achieved with RuEuL. RuEuL has demonstrated outstanding anticancer and imaging capabilities and has vast potential to become a quantiative theranostic agent for anticancer treatments. (J. Med. Chem., 2017, 8923; Nanotheranostics, 2017, 186)

12309516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12309516.value: In the near future, we envisage incorporating the bespoken theranostic agent developed from this project into various vectors to test its use in clinical practice. Furthermore, self-Assembled redox-sensitive nanoparticles for bladder cancer therapy and multi-modal Imaging and a modified amphiphilic prodrug will be synthesized by conjugating the cyclen lanthanide core and camptothecin (CPT) through a redox-sensitive disulfide bond. Hydrophobic CPT is encapsulated in aqueous solution to improve its water solubility and reduce the damage to normal cells by the formation of self-assembled nanoparticles (NPs). Its anticancer efficacy and selectivity can be enhanced by the cleavage of the disulfide linkage to release the drug in cancer cells after internalization of the self-assembled NPs into the tumor microenvironment since free CPT can lose their therapy efficacy easily due to structural degradation in blood circulation. Meanwhile, high contrast MR/optical images can be acquired at first few hours’ post-injection of NPs which can benefit real-time monitoring of the anticancer treatment. The pharmacokinetics, bio-distribution and therapeutic effectiveness of these agents and their bioconjugates in vivo on mice models for cancers will be worked out.`

12309516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12309516.value: In this project, we contributed a new method to combat bladder cancer through the design of a truly dual functional (anti-bladder cancer and imaging) probe which specifically targets bladder cancer cells. In this design, the photo-induced anticancer drug can be localized specifically on the bladder cancer cell membrane via known cancer receptors and its laser-excited photoemission signal can be monitored without triggering the phototoxic generation of reactive oxygen species/anti-cancer agents to the tissues. This treatment modality opens up a new direction in the development of “precision medicine”. Four papers have been published in international leading scientific journals. In the long term, we envision the use of these synthesized “2 in 1” in vitro imaging and photo-induced drugs incorporated with different vectors to enhance their target specificity in clinical practice. One US Non-Provisional Patent is filed (Application No. 15/709,942 of 20 September 2017; Title: A lanthanide toolbox for multi-modal, non-invasive tumor specific theranostic prodrugs). The pre-clinical trial of the complexes from this project will be carried on in the near future.

12313516.label: Project Objectives
12313516.value: Develop block-wise versions of a series of benchmark splitting methods for convex programming problems including the alternating direction method of multiplies, the strictly contractive Peaceman-Rachford splitting method, the customized proximal point algorithm, and their important variants. Conduct convergence analysis of the new block-wise splitting methods, including establishing the global convergence and estimating their worst-case convergence rates measured by the iteration complexity in both ergodic and nonergodic senses. Apply the new block-wise splitting methods to concrete applications in several areas.
rows: Develop block-wise versions of a series of benchmark splitting methods for convex programming problems including the alternating direction method of multiplies, the strictly contractive Peaceman-Rachford splitting method, the customized proximal point algorithm, and their important variants.

Conduct convergence analysis of the new block-wise splitting methods, including establishing the global convergence and estimating their worst-case convergence rates measured by the iteration complexity in both ergodic and nonergodic senses.
Apply the new block-wise splitting methods to concrete applications in several areas.

12313516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12313516.value: Many mathematical models in a variety of application domains are convex minimization problems with linear constraints and separable objective functions. Splitting methods are the most common approach to solving these models, because they can decompose a model with sophisticated structures (maybe from a multi-dimensional or multi-physical scenario) into simpler subproblems for highly effective and efficient computations. A common feature of splitting methods is that the uncoupled functions in the objective of a separable model are treated individually, and thus their properties can be fully exploited in algorithmic design. In this project, we focus on the case where there may be a large number of functions in the objective of the model; such cases have applications in big-data scenarios. In such cases, straightforward applications of existing splitting methods require too much splitting and thus usually fail to approximate a solution of the original model accurately. We propose combining splitting techniques with the block-wise grouping idea in algorithmic design, and thus developing block-wise versions for a series of important algorithms for separable convex programming problems. The key advantage of using the block-wise idea is that the large number of functions in the objective can be first categorized into a much smaller number of groups by data-preprocessing processes, e.g., a learning process. The functions of each group will reflect some common features or properties of an application. Splitting techniques are applied to different function groups outside to generate easier subproblems; functions within the same group are treated equally and their common features are remained. The algorithmic design should meticulously integrate the splitting and block-wise features, with an appropriate balance between the splitting outside and grouping inside, to guarantee both convergence and easy implementablility. For each proposed block-wise splitting algorithm, we shall rigorously analyze its theoretical convergence and exploit its applications in several areas. This is a timely discussion of bridging advanced splitting techniques with increasingly demanding convex programming models in high dimensionality. We promote a novel algorithmic design philosophy that can strengthen the current research on splitting methods and enhance the applicability of splitting methods in various areas. 很多不同應用領域里產生的數學模型都可以歸結為帶有線性約束和可分離目標函數的凸的極小化問題。求解這些數學模型的最常見的方法是分裂方法，因為分裂方法可以把一個帶有複雜結構的數學模型（複雜的原因可能是由於高維情形或者多種物理現象的復合）分解成一些更簡單的子問題，從而可以有效地計算。分裂方法的一個共同特點是它們都是單獨處理可分離目標函數中的各個函數，從而在算法設計中盡可能利用這些函數的固有性質。 本項目集中研究可分離的目標函數是由很多個函數組成的情形；這樣的情形通常在處理大數據的時候會出現。對於這樣的情形，如果我們直接使用已有的分裂方法，那麼通常會造成分裂次數過多從而不能有效地逼近原模型的困難。我們建議在算法設計中，結合現有的分裂方法技術和分塊處理模型的想法，提出一些求解可分離凸優化模型的重要算法的塊狀版本。分塊處理模型的主要優點是目標函數中的眾多函數可以先通過一些諸如學習技術的數據處理過程分成很少的幾類；同一類中的函數可以反映一個具體應用問題的某個共同特征或者性質。之後，我們用分裂方法處理已經分好的函數類；并同等地處理屬於同一類別的函數從而保留它們的共同屬性。算法設計要謹慎地結合分裂和分塊這兩個想法，達到針對不同函數類的外部分裂和相同函數類的內部分塊這兩者的良好平衡， 從而既保證算法的收斂性又使得算法容易實現。對於新設計的塊狀分裂方法，我們將在理論上嚴格證明它們的收斂性并檢驗它們在一些應用領域里的應用效果。

12316116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12316116.value: EM算法和Boosting算法有各自不同的源头：EM用于处理数据缺失和隐变量问题，而Boosting用于集成多个弱分类器而生成强分类器。目前为止，EM与Boosting的结合且用于实际问题还十分少见。 在目前的许多实际应用中，仅仅运用直接的信息往往还不足以到达令人满意的效果。由于大数据时代的到来，许多间接的信息正在大量地累计。在集成直接信息与间接信息时，隐变量模型起到了关键的作用，而EM算法常常用于这里的参数估计。但是，处理高维的间接信息的方法中涉及到计算与统计学的困难。 这个研究中，我们提出EM与Boosting相结合的方式尝试解决上述难点。在我们的前期研究中，我们发现这样的方法比经典的方法要更加高效，并且观察到算法能够以几何速率收敛到统计学精度。因此，在本研究中，我们尝试着建立该方法的理论性质并致力应用到更多的实际问题中。

12316116.label: Realisation of objectives
12316116.value: 1 Develop computationally efficient algorithms to handle large-scale problems in latent variable models. Yes, we have developed several computationally efficient algorithms to handle high-dimensional latent variables, including LLR [1], IGESS [2], PAMIR[3], LSMM [5], BIVAS [6], HIRE [7], VIMCO [8] and VGrow [9]. The successful design of these algorithms can be attributed to the following factors. First, Expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm and its generalized version, such as variational EM algorithm, are very effective to handle high dimensional latent variable problems. Second, the Boosting algorithm can be viewed as a gradient-based algorithm and can be further generalized as a functional gradient and stochastic gradient methods, such that the computation can be done in an efficient manner. These methods have been published on a number of top journals and conferences, as given in the research outcome part. 2 Investigate the theoretical properties of the proposed method. Yes, we have investigated the theoretical properties of the proposed methods. First, we have established the theoretical properties of the generative adversarial network (GAN) from the perspective of the functional gradient (boosting). Specifically, we have proposed a general framework by combining the strengths of variational gradient flow (VGrow) [9] on probability measure spaces, particle optimization, and deep neural networks. We have established a unified framework to understand GAN. We consider a variational gradient flow (VGrow) in probability measure spaces associated with the f-divergence loss which includes several commonly used divergences in statistics and machine learning. The gradient flow is governed by a velocity field that is the negative gradient of the first variation of the f-divergence between the evolving distribution and the target distribution. At the population level, we show that the evolving distribution converges to the target distribution sublinearly without any assumption. For a special case of the KL divergence, the convergence rate is linear under the assumption of Log-Sobolev inequality. Second, we have established the Convergence Rate of the (stochastic) EM Algorithm at both population and sample levels, and prove its optimality, stochasticity, and consistency [5]. In this project, we prove that: (i) the convergence rate of the population EM algorithm is optimal with respect to a ball of population contraction; (ii) the sample level convergence rate of the EM algorithm is a derived random variable of the data generating distribution, which adaptively yields the convergence rate of the algorithm on each finite set of samples from the population distribution; (iii) the sample level convergence rate satisfies a non-asymptotic concentration bound, and it is an asymptotically consistent estimator the population-level convergence rate. Our theory quantifies the optimality, stochasticity, and consistency of the convergence rate of the EM algorithm, and by giving a theoretical explanation to the surprising phenomenon in applications of the EM algorithm, i.e., the sample EM sequence sometimes converges even faster than the population EM sequence, it provides a better understanding of the convergence behavior of optimization algorithms under statistical settings. We apply our theory to the EM algorithm on three canonical models and obtain specific forms of the convergence theorem for each model. 3 Apply the proposed methods in real data analysis. Yes, the developed methods have been applied to genetic data [1,2,5,6], microbiome sequencing data [3], epigenomic data [7], transcriptome data [8] and image data [9]. For genetic data analysis, latent variable models are developed to account for the polygenic and pleiotropic genetic architectures of complex diseases. To accelerate the computational efficiency, Expectation-maximization (EM) algorithms and variational EM algorithms are designed to optimize the model, where the M-step often adopts the stochastic gradient as motived by the boosting algorithm. For microbiome sequencing data, we introduced a latent variable model to handle the compositional data. The challenge is that the data are often very sparse and the samples have different library sizes. We proposed an inverse regression method (PAMIR), to analyze microbiome sequencing data. Within this framework, an inverse regression model is developed for over-dispersed microbiota counts given the trait, and then a prediction rule is constructed by taking advantage of the dimension‐reduction structure in the model. An efficient Monte Carlo expectation‐maximization algorithm is proposed for maximum likelihood estimation. For epigenomic data, we propose a method, HIRE [7], to identify the cell-type-specific association in epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS): detecting whether a CpG site has any associations with the phenotypes in each cell type. To ensure that HIRE can estimate all those parameters well, we have shown mathematically that the HIRE model is identifiable under mild conditions that are easily met in reality. For transcriptome data, the latent variable model is designed to borrow information from multiple cell-types and multiple-phenotypes. For image data, we applied VGrow to the benchmark datasets (i.e., MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA, and LSUN) and a new Portrait dataset collected by our own, we show that VGrow is stable and outperforms state-of-the-art GANs. 4 Develop a user-friendly software to disseminate the results from this research. Yes, we have made the developed software publicly available. 12316116.label: Major findings and research outcome
12316116.value: The major findings and research outcome can be summarized from the following three perspectives: Theoretical analysis, methods for real data analysis, and software development. First, we have established new theoretical results [5] for the EM algorithm and its stochastic version, which is very helpful to explain why the EM algorithms can be so successfully applied in high dimensional latent variable models. Specifically, we established theoretical results for the convergence rate of EM algorithms and their stochastic version at both population and sample level. For example, we have shown that, under some mild conditions, the convergence rate of the stochastic EM algorithm can be linear, where the M-step can be characterized as the stochastic version of the gradient boosting algorithm. Besides the characterization of convergence of EM algorithm, we have also established statistical theory to explain the success of Generative adversarial networks (GAN). In our VGrow framework [9], GAN can be viewed as a latent variable model that aims to map the distribution of low-dimensional latent variables to the target distribution of high-dimensional observed objects. In this project, we show that the distribution of the latent variable can be driven to the target distribution through variational gradient flow, which is exactly characterized by the function gradient of the f-divergence of the evolving distribution and the target distribution. The convergence rate and estimation accuracy of VGrow have been guaranteed statistically. Second, we have developed latent variable models and applied them to real data analysis, including genetic data [1,2,5,6], microbiome sequencing data [3], epigenomic data [7], transcriptome data [8] and image data [9]. There two major reasons for the success of the developed latent variable models in real application. On one hand, latent variable models are very good at combining indirect evidence with direct evidence (observed data). On the other hand, computational efficiency is also a key ingredient for our methods in real applications because millions of latent variables need to be inferred. The developed algorithms are stable and scalable to large-scale data analysis. Third, we have made the software developed in our project publicly available for dissemination of the research outcome. In this project, the proposed algorithm can be implemented in R, Python, or C++. To enhance the computational efficiency, some implementations have been highly paralleled using openMP, such as LSMM [5], BIVAS[6] and HIRE [7], making these methods and tools useful in practice.

12316116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12316116.value: The developed methods in this project and their success in real applications have drawn much attention from the industry. In particular, the development here can be widely applied to genomic data analysis, motivating a deep collaboration between the PI and the WeGene company through the Innovation and Technology Fund (PRP/029/19FX, started June 1, 2020). In the ITF project, we aim to develop statistical and machine learning methods for human genomic big data analysis, such as regression models for genetic risk prediction and latent variable models for human facial recognition. The application of the techniques developed in this project not only facilitate health management (risk prediction for complex diseases) but also provide new tools to connect genomic data with imaging data.

12316116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12316116.value: The expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm and the Boosting algorithm have very different origins. On one hand, the EM algorithm was designed to handle incomplete data problems (i.e., data problems with missing values and latent variables), where the maximum likelihood estimate (MLE) based on incomplete data log-likelihood is often difficult to compute. With the growth of computational power, the EM algorithm has been widely applied to incomplete data problems. On the other hand, the Boosting algorithm was devised to combine multiple weak learners into a powerful committee. Despite their great successes in their own fields (i.e., incomplete data problems and supervised learning problems), the marriage of EM and Boosting has not been explored. In this project, we have established theoretical results for the “EM+Boosting” strategy, guaranteeing its convergence and accuracy. We have also shown that this strategy is widely applicable to real applications, where combining indirect evidence with direct evidence is the key to success. We have further made the developed software publicly available for better dissemination of our research outcome.
