12317216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12317216.value: With the ever-increasing data storage demands and the miniaturization of optoelectronic devices in the digital age of the 21st century, media of high reliability, small size, high-density and high-speed data storage are needed. As the areal density of commercial hard disk drives (HDD) is approaching the terabit per inch square(Tb/in2) milestone, the strong demand in developing new functional materials or fabrication technologies to reach multi-Tb/in2 level has drawn much attention. Traditional magnetic data storage is widely used today and the data storage density has increased rapidly. However, this still cannot fulfill the increasing need of information storage capacity and critically, the HDD industry is facing technical challenge for the areal density of magnetic grains to be further increased. In order to scale down the size of microscopic magnetic grains in increasing the storage capacity, the limitation imposed by their thermal stability(i.e. superparamagnetic effect) must be overcome. One of the promising technologies to relieve this problem is by using bit-patterned media(BPM), in which magnetic nanoarrays are fabricated and each “island” in the array forms a separate recording magnetic bit. To achieve the targeted areal density of 1Tb/in2 and beyond, the patterned media requires highly well-ordered nanoarrays with dimensions less than 12.5nm, which challenges the state-of-the-art lithographic technologies nowadays. Block copolymer(BCP) self-assembly represents a very promising bottom-up tool to access well-ordered nanostructures, which can outperform many top-down patterning techniques in terms of feature size and periodic length scale. Herein, we propose to design and develop a new suite of metal-containing BCPs coupled with the usage of directed self-assembly fabrication approach to create highly dense and ordered magnetic single domain patterns for BPM applications. As high magnetocrystalline anisotropy(Ku) and coercivity of magnetic materials are crucial for long-term stability of data storage to prevent demagnetization, metal alloy FePt-blocks will be pursued in the synthesis of BCPs. The connectivity constraints and the incompatibility between organic and metallic blocks in BCPs would induce spontaneous self-assembly into ordered-patterns in thin film. Therefore, the position of metal alloy NPs is fixed and patterned to the molecular level after the selective etching and pyrolysis processes of the BCPs film. Metallic BCPs undergo microseparation into metal alloy rich nanodomains which ensure ultra-high density magnetic NPs in a single-bit. This project offers versatile and cost-effective technologies and fabrication schemes to create higher areal density, greater uniformity and smaller-sized magnetic grains for the manufacture of magnetic BPM for future data storage devices. 在數字化21世紀時代，數據存儲需求不斷增長，光電器件逐漸微型化，有必要開發小型、高密度、存儲速度快的可靠存儲媒介。商用硬盤驅動器跨越了每英寸兆兆位的里程碑，開發新型功能材料和製備技術取得兆位層次的存儲密度顯得尤為重要。傳統的磁性數據存儲是當前應用最為廣泛的，其存儲密度也在不斷快速增長。但是，這仍然不能滿足日益增長的對信息存儲容量的需求，硬盤驅動器行業在進一步增加磁疇面密度上也面臨著巨大的技術挑戰。為了進一步降低微型磁疇的尺寸而增加存儲容量，必須打破熱穩定性帶來的局限。其中一個最具潛力的技術是位元介質規則，主體結構由規則的磁性陣列構成，每一個陣點形成一個獨立的磁存儲位元。但是，晶格介質往往需要高度有序的小於12.5nm 的陣列來實現1 Tb/in2及以上的面密度，迄今仍制約著先進的平板印刷技術。嵌段共聚物自組裝是一種很有潛力的自下而上製備有序納米結構的方法，比自上而下的製備納米圖案技術更容易得到大面積的高密度納米陣列。我們將設計並開發一系列含金屬的嵌段共聚物，並藉助其自組裝性能製備高密度的有序磁疇納米圖案用於位元介質規則技術。由於磁性材料的磁性各向異性和矯頑力對數據存儲器件的長期穩定及防止退磁非常關鍵，我們特意在聚合物中引入了含有鐵鉑的金屬嵌段。在金屬嵌段聚合物中，有機嵌段和金屬嵌段的性質差異及不匹配性能使其在薄膜中自組裝成有序的納米圖案，經選擇性刻蝕和高溫熱處理，金屬合金納米粒子在分子水平上固定在納米圖案中。金屬嵌段共聚物經顯微分離得到金屬合金納米疇以確保高密度的磁性納米粒子在單個位元中。本項目提供了通用且廉價的技術來製備具有更高存儲密度、更有序、磁疇更小的位元介質規則,並應用於數據存儲器件。

12317216.label: Realisation of objectives
12317216.value: Study 1 (Completed): One-pot synthesis of ferromagnetic FePd nanoparticles from single source organometallic precursors and size effect of metal fraction in polymer chain In this work, ferrocene-substituted terpyridine ligand 4’-(ferrocenyl)- [2,2’:6’,2’’]terpyridine was first synthesized. This ligand was further reacted with Pd(OAc)2 in dry MeCN to obtain [4’-ferrocenyl-(N^N^N)Pd(NCCH3)](BF4)2 TPy-FePd-1 in quantitative yield. On the other hand, the random block copolymer PS-P4VP was synthesized by the free radical polymerization, and further treated with TPy-FePd-1, in which the pyridyl group could be easily coordinated to the Pd complex to obtain a new metallopolymer. The metal fraction in polymer was able to be tuned, and hence, P1, P2 and P3 with 5 wt%, 10 wt% and 20 wt% of metal fractions, respectively, were prepared (Objective 1). All the polymers were characterized by 1H NMR spectroscopy (Objective 2) to find out their structural compositions. Self-assembly of polymers on thin film was carried out by directed self-assembly approach (Objective 3), but unfortunately, no regular patterning of polymers can be observed. The bimetallic complex TPy-FePd-1 was first used as a single-source precursor to synthesize ferromagnetic FePd nanoparticles (NPs) by one-pot pyrolysis. The resultant FePd NPs (FePd-1) have a mean particle size of 19.8 nm and show a coercivity of 1.02 kOe as measured from by vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM). The polymers P1, P2 and P3 were also pyrolyzed to prepare FePd NPs named as FePd-2, FePd-3 and FePd-4, respectively (Objective 4). The resultant NPs were characterized by TEM. The low resolution images demonstrated the morphology of the as synthesized FePd NPs. The particles were evenly embedded in the carboneous matrix to maintain the stability, which was consistent with FePd-1 NPs. The size of the particles was statistically analyzed from the TEM images. The mean size corresponding to FePd-2, FePd-3 and FePd-4 NPs was 10.5 nm, 14.4 nm and 17.5 nm, respectively. These average sizes are smaller than that of the FePd-1 NPs, and the particle was grown with larger size as the metal fraction in polymer increased. The difference in size can be assigned to the different steric structure of the organometallic polymer precursors. The ferromagnetic properties of FePd-2, FePd-3 and FePd-4 NPs were investigated at room temperature by VSM. The hysteresis loops reveal that the resultant NPs have chemically ordered fct phase, which are consistent with the XRD results. The coercivity values of FePd-2, FePd-3 and FePd-4 NPs were 0.95, 1.87 and 1.41 kOe (Objective 4), and the variation may be ascribed to the size effect of FePd NPs, because the sample size can induce the change between the multivariant mode and the single variant mode. Study 2 (Completed): One-step synthesis of platinum nanoparticles by pyrolysis of a polyplatinyne polymer In this study, a new bis(pyridyl)-coordinated platinum(II)-containing metallopolyyne polymer P1 was synthesized according to the following steps. Dialkylation of 2,7-dibromofluorene gave 2,7-dibromo-9,9-dihexadecylfluorene, which was crystallized out from ethanol as a white solid in good yield. Pd-catalyzed trimethylsilylethynylation was carried out on 2,7-dibromo-9,9-dihexadecylfluorene to afford the corresponding trimethylsilyl-protected ligand in satisfactory yield. This trimethylsilyl compound was then deprotonated to afford the terminal acetylene ligand (L1). This ligand was then coupled with the Pt(II) dichloride precursor (PtCl2L2, L = 4-tert-butylpyridine) to generate P1 in good yield (Objective 1). P1 shows very limited solubility in dichloromethane and tetrahydrofuran, which precluded characterization of molecular weights by gel permeation chromatography (GPC). P1 was characterized by NMR and Infrared spectroscopy (Objective 2). The thermal stability of P1 was evaluated by thermal gravimetric analysis (TGA) under a nitrogen atmosphere. P1 showed a good thermal stability with onset decomposition temperature of 310 oC. Bulk pyrolysis of the metallopolymer P1 has been carried out under a N2 atmosphere for 5 h (Objective 4) and fine powdery material was formed. The decomposition residue took the shape of the initial polymer precursor and was dark-silver in color. A simple test of the magnetic property was carried out using a bar magnet. The resultant composite material from Pt-containing P1 was not attracted at all, while other FePt-containing polymers from our previous studies could be attracted quite strongly to the magnet, hence indicating the absence of magnetic property (Objective 4). The nanoparticles were nearly monodisperse as indicated from the TEM analysis. Particle size analysis of the TEM image indicates that the average size of the particles was 13 ± 2 nm. EDXA elemental analysis was used to study the chemical composition of the nanoparticles. Only single Pt phases were observed as has been confirmed by the EDXA spectrum. Carbon phases have also been found due to the presence of the carbonaceous matrix which is associated with the Pt nanoparticles. Also, the absence of N phases indicates that the pyridyl ancillary co-ligands have completely dissociated from the metal center. In addition, the PXRD pattern for the nanoparticles from P1 provide information about the crystalline structure of the nanoparticles, which corresponding to a face-center cubic (fcc) structure. All the results suggest that the use of platinum(II)-containing polyyne polymer as nanoparticle precursor could be a promising route for the preparation of monodisperse Pt nanoparticles with defined morphology. This work may be extended to allow fabrication of patterned nanoparticles using various lithographic methods and look for potential applications in catalysis. Study 3 (undertaken): Nanostructured bimetallic block copolymers as precursors to magnetic FePt nanoparticles by directed self-assembly approach (Objective 3) A series of bimetallic BCPs has been synthesized by incorporating a complex containing Fe and Pt centers into the coordinating block of four different poly(styrene-b-4-vinylpyridine)s (PS-b-P4VPs, P1−P4). To facilitate phase separation for the resulting metalated BCPs (PM1−PM4), a loading of the FePt-bimetallic complex corresponding to ca. 20% was used (Objective 1). Complexation of the metallic complex to P4VP was confirmed by NMR, FT-IR, TGA, and TEM (Objective 2). The bulk and thin-film self-assembly of these BCPs was studied by TEM and atomic force microscopy, respectively. The spherical and cylindrical morphologies observed for the metalated BCPs corresponded to those observed for the metal-free BCPs in the preliminary studies (Objective 3). The products from the pyrolysis of the BCPs in bulk were also characterized by TEM, powder X-ray diffraction, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, which indicated that the FePt NPs formed exist in an fct phase with average particle sizes of ca. 4−8 nm within a carbonaceous matrix (Objective 4). A comparison of the pyrolysis behavior of the metalated BCP (PM3), the metalated P4VP homopolymer (PM5), and the molecular model organometallic complex revealed the importance of using a nanostructured BCP approach for the synthesis of ferromagnetic FePt NPs with a smaller average NP size and a close to 1:1 Fe/Pt stoichiometric ratio. From the above results, metallo-BCP lithography by self-assembly is proved to be an effective and coalescence-free approach to convert a single bimetallic source into FePt NPs without the need of surfactants of weak binding strength or a complicated addition sequence of monometallic salts. Refinement of materials and optimization of their self-assembly physics is undertaken and remains the necessity of further exploration in the future.

12317216.label: Major findings and research outcome
12317216.value: (1) A bimetallic FePd complex (TPy-FePd-1) was prepared and used as a single-source precursor to synthesize ferromagnetic FePd nanoparticles (NPs) by one-pot pyrolysis (Research Output 1). The resultant FePd NPs have a mean particle size of 19.8 nm and show a coercivity of 1.02 kOe. In addition, the labile ligand NCMe in TPy-FePd-1 was easily substituted by a pyridyl group. A random copolymer PS-P4VP was used to coordinate with TPy-FePd-1, and the as-synthesized metallopolymer made the metal fraction disperse evenly along the flexible chain. Investigation of FePd NPs from the bimetallic polymers with different metal fractions was also made, and the size of the resultant nanoparticles could be easily controlled by tuning the metal fraction in the polymer. (2) The synthesis and characterization of a new bis(pyridyl)-coordinated platinum(II)-containing metallopolyyne polymer was reported (Research Output 2). It was found that this metallopolymer can act as a precursor towards the synthesis of Pt nanoparticles upon pyrolysis (600 oC, 5 h). The resultant nanoparticles were characterized by transmission electron microscope, energy-dispersive X-ray analysis and powder X-ray diffraction. The results verify that monodisperse Pt nanoparticles with defined morphology can be obtained. This pilot study reveals the potential of fabricating patterned Pt nanoparticles by using various lithographic methods in the future. (3) A review article (Research Output 5) and a book chapter (Research Output 3) have been published to highlight the use of metallopolymer precursors for the synthesis of magnetic metal/metal alloy NPs and their nanostructures and the related applications. The contents include: (1) Classification and general synthetic procedures of metallopolymer precursors for the synthesis of magnetic metal/metal alloy nanoparticles (NPs); (2) Fabrication techniques of magnetic nanopatterned arrays; (3) Applications of the as-synthesized magnetic metal/metal alloy NPs; (4) Key challenges and opportunities of functional nanomaterials from metallopolymer precursors. (4) Arrays of FePt NPs were prepared from metalloBCP templating. To achieve this goal, bimetallic FePt complex was designed to facilitate the coordination linkage to the pyridine unit in PS-b-P4VP, so as to create phase-separated cylindrical or spherical FePt-containing nanodomains. Thin film self-assembly studies of metalloBCP were conducted to illustrate the capability of these polymers as precursors to form well-ordered spatially isolated FePt NPs. The corresponding morphology found in the bulk state was found to be reproducible in the thin films. The features were retained during pyrolysis for these metalloBCPs, but they did not show a high order. The size of the FePt-containing domains was similar to that before pyrolysis, which showed no or little coalescence after pyrolysis. UV-irradiation is required in the future study to allow better shape retention during pyrolysis to optimize the pyrolysis condition in our BCP system.

12317216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12317216.value: The patterned functional metallopolymer precursors and patterned arrays of magnetic nanocomposites hold great promise for applications in high-density data storage media devices. However, there are still some limitations and challenges remaining unresolved in this research area. For example, the controlled synthesis of heterobimetallic polymers with desirable solubility is still difficult and needs to be further addressed. In situ generation of ferromagnetic alloy NPs through self-assembly of metalloblock copolymers is also not easily achieved, because both the precise control of phase-separation and introduction of specific metal elements in each block are very challenging. Moreover, the relationship of the particle size, composition and shape of NPs with the metal center environment in the polymer backbone, as well as the nucleation mechanism of metal-based NPs are also not yet clear and need to be addressed in the future. The effects of pyrolysis parameters (such as temperature, heating ramp, heating duration, atmosphere, etc.) on the magnetic properties of as-generated NPs also need to be scrutinized and certified. Finally, the creation of ultra-high-density data storage devices based on patterned arrays of magnetic NPs is still not yet explored.

12317216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12317216.value: Development of using metallopolymers as precursors to generate functional magnetic metal/metal alloy NPs and different nanostructures by controlled pyrolysis has been demonstrated. Through rational molecular design and appropriate polymerization methods, heterobimetallic polymers with metallic elements on the side and/or main chain were generated smoothly. The structure of the metallopolymer and the pyrolyzing conditions can significantly influence the size, composition and properties of the resultant magnetic ceramic NPs. By comparison to the traditional synthetic approach, preparation of ferromagnetic alloy NPs (e.g. L10 FePt) from metallopolymer precursors is very attractive because it can avoid the step of post-annealing treatment. Moreover, some of the metallopolymers can act as the negative tone resist for the fabrication of the nanopatterned magnetic metal alloy NPs through lithographic techniques. Self-assembly followed by pyrolysis or solvent annealing of the metalloblock copolymers can form nanopatterns in situ with periodicity down to dozens of nanometers. The patterned functional metallopolymer precursors and patterned arrays of magnetic nanocomposites hold great promise for applications in high-density data storage media devices.

12317616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12317616.value: This project focuses on three directions for multivariate spatial point processes. The first direction is to develop model-free tests. There are several questions that one may have to answer before fitting any model to the data. Consider a forest with different tree species. Are the patterns of locations of individual species independent and do they have the same distribution? For the latter, some tests have been developed recently, under the assumption that the patterns are independent, which is natural when comparing patterns on, say, a cancer and a healthy tissue. However, for patterns of two different cells on the same tissue, the independence assumption may be violated. The proposal suggests a solution by using some newly proposed higher-order cross summary characteristics; the idea is to estimate the null distributions of test statistics constructed from these new characteristics by generating bootstrap samples obtained by simulating an auxiliary independent point process or an auxiliary random variable. Asymptotic approaches, based on nonparametric estimation of the variances of the test statistics, will also be developed. The second direction is to study random graphs that are constructed from multivariate point processes. Random graphs, either topological or constructed from univariate point processes so that vertex locations and edge physical lengths are relevant, have been well studied. The project suggests to construct random graphs for multivariate point processes so that points are connected if they meet some geometrical conditions and some conditions on their types. For example, the so-called six degrees of separation, stating that any two persons in the world are connected by a path of at most six persons knowing each other, as an example of the small-word phenomenon, will be revisited to study how long the path is if the persons have to be of different nationalities. Technically, this project attempts to establish the degree distribution of the typical vertex, characterise the spread by the asymptotic length of the shortest path between a randomly chosen pair of connected vertices, and find the limit of the mean clustering coefficient and the percolation threshold for the existence of a giant component in such a graph. The third direction is to study multivariate marked point processes, e.g. a forest with different tree species marked by their diameters. Existing summary characteristics for marked point processes do not take the inter-type mark correlation into consideration. This project proposes several new summary characteristics and studies the properties of their estimators. 這項多元（或稱多品種）空間點過程的研究將會集中在三方面。 第一是發展出不須假設仼何模型的統計檢定。在實際應用中，研究員往往需要在擬合模型之前先要作一些探索性的分析，例如在同一森林中不同品種的樹各自構成的點圖案的數據（統稱為空間點格局）是否獨立生成或是否有相同的統計分佈，便需要在擬合前先行解答。在假設點格局爲獨立生成的設定中，近年已經有研究員提出不同的統計檢定方法，並應用到例如癌組織與正常組織的比較之中。但例如在同一組織上不同細胞的分佈卻可能違反了獨立生成這個設定，因而不能將這些檢定方法應用於它們所構成的點格局的比較之上。這個研究計劃將會嘗試用高階交差概要統計量來解決這個問題。其基本構思如下：利用高階交差概要所構成的檢定統計量，在虛無假設之下，其分佈將由自助法所生成的樣本中的經驗分佈所近似，而當中自助法則需要模擬一輔助性的獨立點過程或隨機變數來生成樣本。另外，借助檢定統計量的方差的非參數估計，大樣本的漸近法亦將會在這研究中發展出來。 第二是研習由多元點過程所構作出的隨機圖。無論是拓撲的、還是由一元點過程所構作出因而點的位置及線的長度皆有物理意義的隨機圖，在文獻中已經有相當的探討，而今次的研究將會提出由連接多元點過程中符合某些特定幾何及品種條件的點所構成的隨機圖，這種由一元推廣到多元的例子可由小世界現象中的六度分隔所展現。所謂六度分隔，是指世上任意選出的兩人皆可由不多於六個中間人而聯繫上，而多元的版本則可要求例如中間人須爲不同國籍。用技術術語來說，這項研究將嘗試建立一個典型點的度數分佈、用隨意選取的一對有聯繫的點的最短路徑的漸近長度來表示圖的伸展度、及找出平均聚類係數的極限分佈與最大連通子圖的存在性的滲濾閾值。 第三是考究多元標值點過程，例如由森林中不同品種的樹而樹的胸徑爲其標值所構成的標值點格局便可被視為由多元標值點過程所生成的樣本。因現有的概要統計量並不考慮跨品種之標值的相關系數函數，所以這項研究將提出多款新的概要統計量及探討其估計量的特性。

12317616.label: Realisation of objectives
12317616.value: The objectives are about 80% instead of 100% fully achieved because the PI has been suffering from lymphoma and has been receiving chemotherapy and targeted therapy, which is still on-going. This also resulted in some deviation of the research work from the original proposal. The project addressed the statistical analysis of multivariate spatial point patterns in multispecies ecosystem of plants or animals. A commonly asked question in the analysis of such ecosystems is whether different species are living independently. In the literature, one of the three most common assertions (implicit or explicit) in existing unified theories in biodiversity is that individuals of one species are placed independently of individuals of other species. Therefore, it is of interest to know whether there is any spatial relationship between the locations (representing e.g. the nests) of the different species, i.e. to test the hypothesis of the so-called population independence in ecological context. The project successfully developed a small-sample test for testing independence of two species observed in a non-rectangular window without making any assumptions on the distribution of the underlying model. Simulation studies show that the new approach is more powerful than the existing approach that would require a rectangular sampling window. The project also successfully developed an asymptotic chi-squared test to test the equal distribution hypothesis for two given independent species (which is a generic term representing a type of points in a multivariate point pattern), assuming data of each species came from a model of stationary point process. This problem was motivated by the medical application that the patterns of midpoints of capillary profiles in healthy and cancerous tissues have to be compared under the constraint that there is only one realisation from each species. The PI established the asymptotic normality for the empirical second-order product density of a given point pattern at a pre-chosen lag vector, and consequently developed an asymptotic chi-squared statistic to measure the discrepancy between the empirical product densities of two given point patterns at several pre-chosen lag vectors. Simulation studies were carried out, which showed that, when comparing the same class of point processes with different parameters, the newly proposed asymptotic test was more powerful than the permutation test. Estimation methods in such multispecies ecosystem were also considered. A classical example of such a system of plants is Fisher's Iris flower data set, which consists of 150 observations of three species of Iris, where four measurements from each observation were recorded. Using a finite mixture of skew normal distributions to model the marginal distributions, we proposed a constrained maximum likelihood approach that outperforms the ordinary maximum likelihood estimation, which suffers from both degeneracy and divergence of the scale and skewness parameters. We established mathematically that the existence, strong consistency, asymptotic normality, and efficiency of the constrained MLE of the parameters over the restricted parameter space. Simulation studies provided empirical support to our findings. We then considered spatial point patterns in which each point has a real-value response. This is related to classical curve estimation problems. However, the inefficiency in nonparametric estimation of the curve without any dimension reduction of the spatial point pattern would make any local smoothing tests powerless. We developed a projection-based statistic which also enjoys the advantages of global smoothing, because the bandwidth of the Gaussian kernel for smoothing does not play a role in the proposed statistic, which relies on the inter-point Euclidean distances. Asymptotic properties of the proposed statistic were established. Simulation studies were carried out and showed empirically that the proposed statistic possessed the advantages of both local and global smoothing tests. However, not in all applications we could make the smoothing parameter unimportant, and the choice of its value becomes crucial for the success of the applications. We proposed data-driven approaches to choose spatially varying smoothing parameters for Gaussian kernels centred at points of a point pattern. We proved that the interpolation matrix in nonparametric curve estimation is almost surely invertible, when the smoothing parameter is an absolutely continuous random variable independent of the point pattern of the kernel centres, whose inter-centre distances are all distinct. Another approach is to introduce an extra dimension in addition to the dimensions (say d) of the point locations, so that we generate quasi-random point patterns in d+1 dimensions for the d-dimensional locations and the real-valued bandwidths of the kernels, so that nearby kernels are of distinctive shape. We applied this approach to solve PDEs, and numerical examples showed that our proposed approach yielded an efficient (small number of iterations with predictable run-time) solver that could produce cheap but accurate approximations, and it was also robust in the sense that the mean errors were small with small standard deviations among different functions and without bad runs. In spatial point pattern analysis, when asymptotic null distributions are not tractable, the p-values are often approximately by resampling. We formulated the bootstrap p-value as a Monte Carlo approximation of an integral by taking the average of the integrand values evaluated at the points of a stationary Poisson process in the unit hypercube. When the number of points are fixed, the conditional distribution of the Poisson points is independent uniform. However, the purpose of generating pseudo-random numbers is to simulate randomness, while for the numerical approximation of the integral, what is more important is whether the unit hypercube can be filled uniformly by the point set used to evaluate the integrand values. Using quasi-random methods can achieve this uniformity in space-filling better than using sets of independent pseudo-random points following the uniform distribution can. A quasi-random sequence is deterministic, but we could introduce randomness by e.g. scrambling. Randomisation can lead to improvement of the quality of the resultant point set. Moreover, for numerical examples, randomisation allows replicates so that we can get the bias and mean squared error. Our simulation study suggested empirically that the randomised quasi-Monte Carlo test often results in smaller approximation error in the estimation of the p-value and smaller deviation from the nominal level than the Monte Carlo test.

12317616.label: Major findings and research outcome
12317616.value: Seven journal articles were resulted from this project. [2] and [3] proposed tests for multivariate spatial point processes for modeling multispecies systems. [2] considered testing the independence between species observed in a small window. The new method outperformed the existing method such that unlike the existing ones, the new method does not require the sampling window to be rectangular; it can utilise the information everywhere in the window, not only in the maximal inscribing rectangle. [3] considered testing whether two given independent species are realisations of the same point process model. A new asymptotic chi-squared test was shown to be more able than the existing permutation test to detect the difference in the underlying models when the two patterns came from the same class of models with different parameters. [1] developed a constrained MLE method for multispecies systems with a new constrained EM algorithm for its execution. The new approach does not suffer from degeneracy and divergence of the scale and skewness parameters, while the ordinary MLE may. Moreover, the strong consistency, asymptotic normality, and efficiency were established mathematically and supported by simulation. [4] and [7] considered spatially varying smoothing parameters for kernels centred at points of a point pattern for nonparametric curve estimation. A constant smoothing parameter is often good enough for the estimation of smoothed curves, but variable smoothing parameters will do a better job when the curves to be estimated have complicated structures. [7] proposed adding an extra dimension in addition to the dimensions of the point locations and proposed to generate a quasi-random point pattern in the higher dimensional space to produce spatially varying smoothing parameters; numerical examples show that this approach has higher efficiency and accuracy. [4] proved the almost sure invertibility of the interpolation matrix for any point pattern for the kernel centres in nonparametric curve estimation. [6] proposed an approach to bridge the local smoothing and the global smoothing tests so that the proposed kernel estimation based approach can enjoy the advantages of both the local and global tests. [2] and many other tests in spatial point pattern analysis rely on bootstrap procedures. [5] uses quasi-random points to approximate the bootstrap p-value by formulating the bootstrap p-value as a numerical approximation of an integral over the unit hypercube and using a quasi-random point pattern in the hypercube to evaluate the integrand to yield an approximate for the true p-value by spatial averaging.

12317616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12317616.value: Using multivariate spatial point processes to model multispecies ecosystems has a limitation that points are dimensionless, representing solely the locations of something static, e.g. plants or animal nests at a particular time point, but they may not be appropriate for modelling territories of animals. The approaches involving the use of kernels developed in this project inspired the PI to consider the use of kernels to model territories. The existing spatial tessellation approach, such as using the Voronoi diagram, would have the restriction that animal territories have to be non-overlapping, because by definition a tessellation is formed by non-overlapping cells. The existing random set approach, such as using the Boolean model, would assume that the activity level within a territory is a constant. However, the advantage of using kernels is that kernels can overlap and kernels, unless restricting to rectangular kernels, have variable values. When in the future the health of the PI allows, a GRF proposal will be prepared to give a more precise formulation of the ideas of using spatially varying kernels to model species territories in a multispecies ecosystem.

12317616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12317616.value: The project was successfully completed and resulted in seven research articles. Multispecies ecosystems are often modeled by multivariate spatial point processes. This project proposed new methods for statistical inference, such as testing the independence of individual species and testing equal distribution of independent species. Small-sample and large-sample methods were developed. Computationally feasible estimation by using constrained maximum likelihood was suggested to overcome some technical issues in the traditional maximum likelihood estimation. The project also successfully developed a model-checking statistic that has the advantages of local and global smoothing, a fully adaptive approach for choosing spatially varying smoothing parameters, an almost sure invertibility theorem for the interpolation matrix with random smoothing parameters, and a quasi-Monte Carlo approximation of the bootstrap p-value. The practicality of all these developments was illustrated by empirical studies of simulated and real data.

12319716.label: Realisation of objectives
12319716.value: 1. Quantification of bisphenol A (BPA) in urine samples of pregnant women A liquid chromatography (LC) coupled to triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (QQQ MS) method was established for simultaneous measurement of BPA and other endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) in urine samples. Mass spectrometric analysis was performed in heated-electrospray ionization (H-ESI) negative ion mode. The MS conditions including sheath gas flowrate, aux flow rate, sweep gas flow rate, spray current, and capillary temperate were optimized. Multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode was used and the MS/MS parameters were optimized individually for each compound by continuous infusion of standard solution into the mass spectrometer. The parent ion and product ions of BPA was set as 227.1 and 212.2, respectively Biological sample preparation procedures and method analytical performance (e.g., sensitivity, linearity, precision, accuracy and matrix effect) were established and validated. Quality control (QC) samples were made by pooling the same volume of each re-dissolved urine sample. The QC samples were also analyzed randomly throughout the experiment to monitor instrument stability in terms retention time and peak intensity. A blank sample (solvent) was injected every three sample injections to minimize the carry-over throughout the sequence analysis. The method was applied to determine the BPA (and other EDCs) in urine samples collected from pregnant women in Wuhan, China. BPA was detected in more than 50% urine samples. 2. Establishment of MS-based metabolomics method for urine sample analysis A LC-Orbitrap MS-based platform was developed for supporting the metabolomics study. The method enabled metabolic profiling of endogenous metabolites in urine samples. Metabolomics analysis was carried out by analyzing the collected urine samples with the known BPA levels. The obtained LC-MS data were transferred to the built-in metabolomics software for data analysis, in which principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares-discriminate analysis (PLS-DA) were used to discriminate the metabolic differentness between groups of various BPA exposure levels vs controls. The details of the method has been described as follows: (1) Urine sample preparation Urine samples (1 mL) was placed into a tube; then incubated with 200 mL ammonium acetate (pH 5.0) and 10 μL β-glucuronidase, in a water bath at 37 °C overnight. The mixture was extracted for 3 times by adding 3 mL of solvent (methyl tert-butyl ether/ethyl acetate (5/1, v/v)) each time. The supernatants were combined into a glass vial and dried under a gentle nitrogen stream. The residue was re-dissolved with 200 mL of acetonitrile/water (6/4, v/v) and centrifuged at 13000 rpm for 10 min at 4 oC. The supernatant was stored at 20 oC until LC-MS/MS analysis. (2) LC-MS analysis Metabolomics analysis was performed by Q Exactive focus Orbitrap LC-MS/MS system. The ACQUITY UPLC HSS T3 column (2.1 mm × 100 mm, 1.8 μm) was used for chromatography separation. The UHPLC mobile phase A contained water with 0.1% formic acid. The mobile phage B contained acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid. The mobile phase gradient was as follow: 0.0–1.0 min at 2% B, 1.0–20.0 min from 2% B to 100% B and kept for 2.0 min, 22.0–22.1 min to 2% B and 22.1–25.0 min at 2% B. The column temperature was remained at 30 °C, the flow rate was 0.3 mL/min. The injected sample amount was 5.0 μL each time. The parameters of MS in both positive and negative ionization mode was applied: cone voltage to 35 V; cone gas flow to 35 L/h; source temperature to 120 °C; capillary voltage to 3000 V and 2600 V in the positive and negative ionization mode, respectively; mass range of full scan mode to m/z 133–1500; desolvation gas temperature to 320 °C; collision energy to 5 eV. (3) Biomarker identification Metabolite identification was based on comparing the MS/MS fragments and retention time with online database and literature reports and confirmed by using authentic standards. Human metabolome database (http://www.hmdb.ca/) (briefly HMDB) and Metlin metabolite database (http://metlin.scripps.edu/) were used for metabolite identification. Data of accurate masses for both parent and product ions were acquired with the utility of Orbitrap MS. MS/MS analysis with the accurate mass measurement, which is available on the Orbitrap MS instrument, was used for identification of potential metabolites in the study. (4) Biological interpretation Biological interpretation was performed based on spectral similarity, literature reports on reproductive disorder and public databases to experimentally identified metabolites by either structural elucidation from experimental approaches (e.g. HRMS, MS/MS) and/or statistical (e.g. statistical total correlation spectroscopy). The disturbed metabolic networks induced by BPA were described based on online databases. Human metabolome database (http://www.hmdb.ca/) (briefly HMDB), the metlin database (http://metlin.scripps.edu/) and mzcloud (https://www.mzcloud.org/), KEGG database (http://www.genome.jp/kegg/atlas/) and massbank (http://www.massbank.jp) were used for metabolite mapping. Moreover, public pathway resources, such as KEGG (http://www.genome.jp/kegg/pathway/html) and PathVisio, were used to explore the linkages between identified metabolites and functional and regulatory processes within known metabolic pathways. Specific attention was given to biological interpretation and potential biomarker related to BPA associated endocrine disruption. 3. Relationship between potential biomarker, endocrine disruption effect and BPA embryonic exposure level Correlation analysis among the identified potential biomarker, maternal BPA levels and endocrine disruption effects such as low birth weight was investigated. The potential biomarkers as well as their up- and down-regulation was determined for their relationship with reported results. In addition, we investigated the influences of developmental programming of endocrine disruption effect or disease induced by BPA exposure. To provide a specific example for examination on correlation with low birth weight, the identified potential biomarkers were evaluated with the possible metabolic pathways that were associated with the low birth weight cases along with the known BPA urinary levels. In this study, low birth weight is defined as a birth weight of a live born infant of less than 2500 g. Upon the successful completion of targeted metabolomics analysis, the correlation between the concentrations of potential biomarker was assessed. The metabolome view analysis was performed by using MetaboAnalyst 3.0, in which the adjusted odd ratios for low birth weight risk were calculated. In addition to the correlation analysis, the distributions of potential biomarker concentrations were elevated using Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test. The Wilcoxon matched pairs signed rank test was used to compare the difference of potential biomarker levels between the low birth weight and control groups. Conditional logistic regression analyses were then performed to assess the association between potential biomarker levels and birth weight by calculating crude and adjusted matched odds ratios and their 95% confidence intervals. In addition, we utilized regression models to analyze the potential biomarker levels as categorical variables. The linear trends of the risk of low birth weight and potential biomarker concentrations were evaluated by modeling the median values of potential biomarkers as a continuous variable, and the statistical significance of this predictor was calculated by the Wald test. In summary, we developed different MS-based methods for analyzing maternal urine samples. The levels of BPA and EDCs were measured with the utility of LC-QQQ MS. Metabolomics analysis of the urine samples was then performed by using LC-Orbitrap MS. Furthermore, the relationships between potential biomarker, endocrine disruption effect and BPA embryonic exposure level were investigated. The results of this project provided evidence regarding endocrine disruption effects induced by embryonic exposure to BPA.

12319716.label: Major findings and research outcome
12319716.value: In order to investigate the influence of BPA exposure in the developmental programming of diseases or disorder associated with endocrine disruption, we performed metabolomics analysis on the maternal urine samples collected from pregnant women in Wuhan, China. Endogenous metabolites that were able to discriminate among different BPA exposure levels vs controls were determined. In addition, the difference among groups with various BPA exposure levels, and groups of low birth weight vs controls was investigated. The results of this study elaborated the relationship of the BPA exposure levels on different pregnancy period (early, middle, and later) and provided evidence for the influences of developmental programming of endocrine disruption induced by embryonic exposure to BPA. Notably, the outcome of the study provided a linkage for investigation of the influence xenobiotic exposure on endogenous metabolites of pregnant women, which thus provided deep understanding on the developmental programming of endocrine disruption induced by embryonic exposure to BPA.

12319716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12319716.value: The protocols and developed methods in this study have been extended to the investigations on BPA-derivatives, such as bisphenol S (BPS) and bisphenol F (BPF), which are the major alternatives to BPA. As an important application for further development of the research, we aim to investigate the exposure levels and evaluate the potential health risks of these alternatives in Chinese women during pregnancy. The hazard ratio and toxicological mechanism of BPA and its derivatives will be investigated and compared. A list of potential metabolites and the suggested cut-off levels in the biological samples will be obtained. Additionally, more participants with detailed survey to record their socioeconomic characteristics and lifestyle habits will be recruited in this study. This action allows conducting large cohort studies and providing more robust results regarding the endocrine disruption effects of BPA and its derivatives on pregnant women. Because plasticizer exposure (e.g., BPA and derivatives) is often a long-term and chronic process, we hope to bring the issue of the pollution of these chemicals to a more extensive public attention through this study.

12319716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12319716.value: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a key industrial chemical used in the manufacture of polycarbonate plastics and other products, which has been defined as one of the major endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs). Nowadays, BPA exposure in humans has been implicated in a variety of reproductive disorder and diseases. However, there is a paucity of research on the metabolomics analysis of maternal urines induced by BPA exposure. In the present study, we utilized mass spectrometry-based metabolomics methods to investigate the endocrine disruption effect of BPA exposure in urine samples of pregnant woman. In achieving this, we first determined the levels of BPA and other EDCs in maternal urines and then performed metabolomics analysis to explore the altered metabolites among different BPA exposure levels vs controls. After that, correlation analysis was conducted to investigate the relationship between endogenous metabolites, endocrine disruption effect and BPA embryonic exposure level in the urine samples. The obtained results provided solid evidence to understand the endocrine disruption effects by embryonic exposure to BPA. In addition, the streamlined workflow used in the study has great potential for investigation of the toxicological mechanism of other environmental xenobiotics related to reproductive disorder and diseases.

12319816.value: 求解帶線性約束凸規劃的神經動態方法

12319816.label: Project Objectives
12319816.value: Investigate the theoretical properties including strong convergence for the trajectories of affine scaling family and central path family. Develop some efficient solution schemes for the ODE systems established in (1) above. Conduct extensive numerical experiments for all of our neurodynamical models for linearly constrained convex programming.

Develop some efficient solution schemes for the ODE systems established in (1) above.
Conduct extensive numerical experiments for all of our neurodynamical models for linearly constrained convex programming.

12319816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12319816.value: Convex programming problems arise in many fields of science, engineering, finance, business and management. Hong Kong, as one of the world centers of finance and logistics, has a very strong need for the cutting edge technology in convex programming. For instance, the portfolio optimization in finance and supply chain management in logistics often require fast and efficient solvers for convex programming. There are many research results on convex programming. In the literature, the following two groups of methods are very successful for linearly constrained convex programming. (a) Interior point methods: The success of interior point methods lies in the strong theoretical results and promising numerical performance. The continuous trajectory of the central path has been well studied in the literature. But the study of continuous trajectories for other related interior point methods is still missing. (b) Neural network methods: Besides the attractive hardware implementation, the success of neural network methods is also recognized by the introduction of a potential function, which is normally a Lyapunov function. In the neural network approach, the intermediate solutions may not always stay in the interior of the feasible region, which could cause degeneracy issues in some cases. Based on the success of the interior point approach and neural network approach for linearly constrained convex programming, a main goal of this research project is to combine the advantages of the two approaches. Specifically, in this project we propose a neurodynamical approach for convex programming with linear constraints. In the proposed neurodynamical approach, every neurodynamical model is established for one optimization problem and each model consists of two components: (i) a dynamical system or an ordinary differential equation (ODE) whose solution trajectory always stays in the interior of the feasible region and whose equilibrium point normally corresponds to an optimal solution of the underlying optimization problem; and (ii) a group of special functions, which will be used in proving the convergence of the solution of the above ODE system. The solution of each ODE system forms a continuous trajectory from an initial point to a limit point. Our study in this proposal will focus on the following aspects: (a) to investigate the theoretical properties including strong convergence for the trajectories of affine scaling family and central path family; (b) to develop some efficient solution schemes for the ODE systems discussed in (a); and (c) to conduct extensive numerical experiments for all of our neurodynamical models for linearly constrained convex programming.

12319816.label: Realisation of objectives
12319816.value: The three objectives have been fully achieved. For 1), the theoretical properties for the affine scaling and central path families have been fully investigated. Several research papers have been published. For 2), some efficient solution schemes have been developed. These solution schemes have been published in our research papers. For 3), numerical experiments for our neurodynamical models have been conducted. These numerical results have been published in our research papers.

12319816.label: Major findings and research outcome
12319816.value: (i) Some novel continuous trajectories for linearly constrained convex programming have been proposed. Their strong convergence has been also proved. Some solution schemes following these continuous trajectories have been developed in our current study. (ii) Generalized central paths have been proposed for linearly constrained convex programming. Strong convergence has been proved for these generalized central paths. It should be mentioned that the standard central path will not converge for some linearly constrained convex programming problems. (iii) Following a continuous affine scaling trajectory for semi-definite convex programming (a special class of linearly constrained convex programming), a solution scheme is proposed. The new scheme ensures the weak convergence while the original affine scaling scheme may not converge to some optimal solution.

12319816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12319816.value: (a) Following the work in 6.1 (i), a new solution scheme has been developed for linearly constrained convex programming. The work is nearly finished. (b) Following the work in 6.1 (ii), a new solution scheme has been developed. Very attractive numerical results have been achieved. We are working on the theoretical issues for this new solution scheme. (c) Following the work in 6.1 (ii), a matrix-free augmented Lagrange scheme has been developed. We are working on the final touch.

12319816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12319816.value: This research project has been fully completed. Several novel continuous trajectories for linearly constrained convex programming have been proposed. Numerical results have also confirmed the attractiveness of our new findings. Our new research results have strengthened and consolidated the state-of-art research for linearly constrained convex programming.

12324716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12324716.value: 擴展細胞群順序斑圖的普適形成機制

12324716.label: Project Objectives
12324716.value: Develop and implement methods to investigate the stability and bifurcation of a steadily propagating front. Perform linear stability analysis and identify conditions for the Hopf bifurcation driven by a single mode localized at the front. Discuss characteristic features of the unstable mode from the point of view of both linear and nonlinear analysis. Investigate the interplay between diffusion and reaction in the interfacial region through the construction of simplified representations of system dynamics. Discuss how the underlying processes of growth, diffusion and advection each and together contribute to the instability and its subsequent development. Using the results of the study, propose generic mechanisms of sequential pattern formation with reference to specific biological systems and processes.

Discuss characteristic features of the unstable mode from the point of view of both linear and nonlinear analysis.

Investigate the interplay between diffusion and reaction in the interfacial region through the construction of simplified representations of system dynamics. 12324716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12324716.value: In contrast to Turing's original proposal, developmental patterns are often formed sequentially in the biological world. In somitogenesis, for example, somites emerge one by one following an oscillating process localized at the posterior end of the elongating body axis. An adaptation of the morphogen gradient theory to such a situation was made by Cooke and Zeeman in the ``clock and wavefront’’ model, where the presomitic cells undergo rhythmic oscillations before committing to a specific differentiation path triggered by a moving determination front. Pattern formation generated by an oscillating front has also been demonstrated recently in a bacterial system where the motility of individual cells is controlled by a synthetic circuit (Liu et al., Science 334, 238 (2011)). In tumor growth, the expansion velocity of a solid tumor may show oscillatory behavior under suitable conditions. The mathematics to analyze sequential pattern formation is under-developed as the procedure to reduce the full nonlinear dynamics of a spatially extended system onto one or a few dominant unstable modes is cumbersome and usually not analytically tractable. In this respect, a lot can be gained by developing phenomenological theories of genotype (cellular-level behavior) to phenotype (population dynamics) mapping that focus on physical mechanisms of instability in the frontal region. In this project, we will examine in detail two extreme scenarios for a pulsating front: oscillations arising from a reaction cycle localized at the front, and (quasi) spatial separation of fast and slowly diffusing groups. Reduction of the full dynamics to a set of ODEs for the localized unstable mode will be carried out both numerically and analytically under physically motivated approximations. The resulting ``amplitude equations’’ will be investigated. Different types of transitions afforded by the amplitude equations, i.e., first order or continuous, will be examined. With a more complete understanding of the mathematical structure behind the dynamical instability, systematic comparisons between the model behavior and experimental observations can be carried out, and the role of various molecular components and their interactions (with relevant rate constants) in the patterning process quantified. We aim at generic descriptions of pulsating fronts in these systems. Lessons learned may very well be used to guide future design of synthetic molecular circuits to achieve patterns with desired features. 昆蟲、動物等的器官和體型的發育常常是按照某種順序進行的，這與英國科學家圖靈最初的想法不一樣。 例如，在脊椎動物體節的發育中，不斷延伸的胚胎體軸的末端形成振盪，每個週期生成新的一節。 庫克和塞曼對形態因數梯度理論進行修改，提出了「時鐘和波前」模型，已形成的體節末端觸發未分化細胞內部產生震盪，最終分化為新的體節。 由振盪的波前生成斑圖的現象最近也在菌落擴展實驗中觀察到了，方法是用一個人工合成的基因回路來控制單個細菌的運動。 在腫瘤生長的過程中，擴張速度在適宜條件下也可呈現振盪行為。 目前，描述上述現象的數學方法還很不令人滿意。 振盪的出現是一種低維失穩現象，但系統的動力學是由偏微分方程來描述的，如何將問題約化到幾個關鍵的自由度是一個非常繁瑣的操作。 在這方面，可以通過發展基因線路（細胞內部過程）到表像（群體行為）的唯像理論來研究波前失穩的物理機制。 本專案裡，我們將詳細研究振盪波前形成的兩種極端情況︰由局域在波前的反應環路產生的振盪，和由（准） 空間分離的快、慢擴散組合產生的振盪。 我們將基於物理的考慮將系統的動力學化簡為由常微分方程組定義的失穩問題，並對得到的「振幅方程」開展數值分析和討論。 我們將研究振幅方程所描述的一階或連續相變。 在對動力不穩定性的數學結構獲得較完整的理解後，我們將對模型和實驗觀測結果進行系統的比較，從而量化各種分子元件和它們交互作用在振盪形成過程中的角色。 我們的目標是建立形成脈動波前一般性理論。 研究所獲得的經驗可用於指導合成分子電路的設計，實現符合特定要求的斑圖。

12324716.label: Major findings and research outcome
12324716.value: We have carried out extensive numerical and analytical studies of a two-state model of cell motility which respond to the local cell density. Main findings are summarized in the accompanying manuscript "Traveling front instability in a two-state model of density dependent motility". The manuscript is in its final stage of preparation before submission. Completion of the work was delayed partly due to an ongoing research on COVID-19 epidemic modelling which the postdoctoral fellow on the project, Dr. QI Fei, also participated. The COVID-19 manuscript is in its final round of review at Nature Communications. Below is a brief summary of results achieved. The model proposed in the original work (Liu et al., Science 334: 238 (2011); Fu et al., PRL 108: 198102 (2012)) was directly motivated by experiments but is hard to analyze due to a variable diffusion constant. The PI has looked into the possibility of building more micro-structure into the model so that the density dependent motility arise as an average over subpopulations of fast and slow movers. This would overcome an artefact in the previous model where cell motility changes abruptly with the environment. Through discussions with my final year UG student ZHANG Xinyu at the start of this project, we came up with the idea of assigning internal states to a given cell. The student then joined Prof. Mitarai's group at NBI and continued the work. While they focused on the study of the stability of a spatially homogeneous system without cell proliferation, we continued our work on the stability of the front of an expanding bacterial colony as in the original experiments. Under the two-state model, the key dimensionless parameters are the overall switching rate between the two states (measured against the cell proliferation rate), and the Hill coefficient n that specifies the width of the zone between the front end where low motility cells convert to high motility ones, and the back end when the opposite happens. The extensive simulation work carried out during the project gave a clear picture how the two parameters work together to determine the stability line of the steadily propagating front. Among the interesting findings is an inverse power-law relation between the two parameters at the transition, with an exponent 3/2. The data also established clearly that the instability is driven by a mode localized at the front in the form of a Hopf bifurcation.

12324716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12324716.value: The extensive numerical results presented in the attached manuscript provided ample detail of the transition which will help completing the remaining tasks on the analytic side as stated in the original proposal. We derived the equations to perform the linear stability analysis as presented in the mid-term report but have not been able to make much progress further due to lack of insight. With a better understanding of the traveling wave solution and the shape of the localized mode that goes unstable at the transition, we will focus more on the region near rho = 1 where the fast component start to be converted into the slow one at significant rate. This produces a depression of the overall density profile in the co-moving frame which eventually led to the instability. We hope to finish the work in the next six months and submit updates of our progress to RGC. We have been looking into the effect of chemotaxis from nutrient gradient in pattern formation. It has been shown recently that, in the experimental system, the nutrient gradient is self-generated by bacterial consumption. This leads to a push front with novel behavior under investigation.

12324716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12324716.value: The emergence of patterns in motile cell populations is a fascinating topic in biology. As a “schema” for self-generation of life forms, Alan Turing in 1952 made the association of pattern formation with dynamic instabilities in reaction-diffusion systems. Other natural and synthetic systems undergo pattern formation sequentially with the help of an oscillating front. Focusing on a particular set of experiments with density-controlled cell motility, we study a model where individual bacterium switches between modes of fast and slow diffusion at rates that follow a Hill function of the local cell density. As parameters of the model are tuned, a second order phase transition from the steadily propagating to an oscillatory front is observed. The transition is of the Hopf bifurcation type associated with a mode localized in the frontal region. Interestingly, the instability line is well-described by an inverse power-law relation between the switching rate and the Hill coefficient, with an exponent 3/2. We further observe that, when oscillations are sufficiently developed, peaks and troughs of density oscillations are stationary in the lab frame, in agreement with experiments. The model study can help biologists to better understand and control the pattern-forming process by interfering or designing intracellular molecular circuits.

12327916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12327916.value: 海洋無脊椎動物不僅是具有價值的食物和經濟資源，牠們對於維持生態系統功能（例如維護棲息地、營養動力學、能量通量、生物地質化學循環及養分循環等）亦十分重要。磷酸三（1,3-二氯-2-丙基）酯（TDCPP）在過去十年間，已取代了五溴二苯醚（pentaBDE）成為全世界各式各樣的消費品之主要阻燃劑，使其廣泛存在於空氣、土壤、沉積物、以及動物和人體組織和排泄物之中。高速的工業化發展導致中國珠江三角洲的水域、沉積物和魚類組織中均含有高濃度的 TDCPP。體內外研究更發現 TDCPP對人類、嚙齒類、鳥類和魚類為致癌物，並具神經毒性和肝毒性。此外，TDCPP 可在魚類和哺乳類動物（包括人類）引致內分泌干擾及發展和生殖障礙。 海洋無脊椎動物雖然對經濟和生態十分重要，但 TDCPP 會否和會以甚麼方式影響海洋無脊椎動物仍是完全未知。廣泛分佈於太平洋的藤壺 Balanus amphitrite 和腹足綱 Crepidula onyx 對營養動力學、海底和水層耦合、以至調節海洋生態系統結構和功能都有關鍵作用。因此我們建議以這兩個物種作為研究模型，驗證 TDCPP 能夠影響海洋無脊椎動物的適應度，包括生長、發展、進食、繁殖、以及幼蟲附著行為的假設。我們將進一步進行實驗以驗證親代（F0）存活於含有 TDCPP 的環境會影響其後代（F1）的適應度之假設。這項全新的研究結果將提供重要資訊，以評估 TDCPP 對海洋無脊椎動物的適應度和可持續性，及對其生態系統功能構成的風險。研究結果亦能幫助識別可能受 TDCPP 影響的重要生態終點及敏感的生命階段，並引導未來有關 TDCPP 在海洋無脊椎動物中的毒性之機制研究。

12328216.label: Realisation of objectives
12328216.value: 1. We have measured the oxidative potential (OP) of 65 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong during a one-year-long period using an acellular DTT assay. Since we combined both water-soluble and lipid-soluble fractions of PM2.5 in DTT assay and many other studies only used the water-soluble fraction, a more inclusive evaluation of the DTT-ROS generation ability of PM2.5 was obtained here. The annual concentration of DTTV of PM2.5 was 0.48 ± 0.12 nmol min-1 m-3, which is much lower than other cities in China, such as Sichuan and Inner Mongolia, indicating that a lower inhalation risk for PM2.5 in Hong Kong in terms of DTT oxidative potential. We used two in vitro cell models, namely the murine macrophage cell line RAW 264.7 and murine hepatocyte cell line AML-12, to investigate the directly- and indirectly-induced toxicological responses by 65 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong during a one-year-long period. We exposed the total extracts (water-soluble + lipid-soluble fractions) of PM2.5 samples to RAW 264.7 cells and quantified the inflammation responses (i.e., TNF-α secretion and IL-6). We then treated the AML-12 cells using the supernatant of exposed RAW 264.7 cells, and the response of phosphorylation of IRS-1 on serine-307 was monitored. The cell expression of TNF-α for the 65 PM2.5 samples ranged from undetectable (3 out of 65 samples) to 437.9 pg mL-1, with the annual average value of 235.2 pg mL-1. When normalized TNF-α level by air volume, the median concentration is 37.6 pg TNF-α m-3 (range: undetectable – 70.1 pg TNF-α m-3). As for IL-6, its levels were close to or under the detection limit in most samples. Therefore, we did not report it in the manuscript. A clear upregulating of IRS-1 protein was observed in PM2.5 extracts treated AML-12 cells. On average, it increased by 2.7 times, with the ratio of IRS-1 level in treated and control samples varying from 0.57 to 12.46. No clear associations among DTT-ROS activity, TNF-α and IRS-1 response were observed. Results of this part are presented in Ma et al. (2022) and Hu et al. (2022). (Objective 1) 2. We have performed a comprehensive chemical analysis of major PM2.5 components in the 65 PM2.5 samples. More than 100 chemical species were identified and quantified, including organic carbon (OC), EC, WSOC, water-soluble total nitrogen (WSTN), eight major water-soluble ions (S2O42-, NO3-, C2O42-, NH4+, K+, Ca2+, Na+, Mg2+), 12 metals (Iron (Fe), Magnesium (Mn), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Vanadium (V), Nickle (Ni), Lead (Pb), Chromium (Cr), Cadmium (Cd), Arsenic (As), Silver (Ag), and Barium (Ba) ), 14 tracers of secondary organic aerosol, 12 saccharides, 11 di- and tri-carboxylic acids, 37 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and the derivatives, 29 alkanes, 18 hopanes, and eight steranes. Details on the chemical analysis procedures and concentrations of species included in PMF analysis were provided in Ma et al., 2022. (Objective 2) 3. We applied PMF to identify and apportion the relative contributions of primary and secondary sources to PM2.5 and PM2.5-induced OP. Five primary sources (i.e., marine vessels, Cu-related source, Fe-Mn-Zn-related source, vehicle emissions, biomass burning) and one secondary source were resolved for both PM2.5 mass concentration and DTT activity. Cu-related source, secondary formation, and marine vessels were the top three contributors to both PM2.5 mass concentration and its induced DTT activity, with secondary formation as the leading source for PM2.5 mass concentration (30.3%) and the Cu-related source as the predominant contributor (39.1%) responsible for the DTT consumption of PM2.5. As for the intrinsic oxidative potential of PM2.5 from different sources, PM2.5 emitted from marine vessels, and Cu-related source showed the highest values, indicating more toxic features of PM2.5 derived from these two sources regarding DTT activity. To identify the PM2.5 sources that related to the measured increase of IRS-1 and TNF-α, we applied multivariate linear regression (MLR) analysis for IRS-1 response and TNF-α (dependent variable) and PM2.5 mass apportioned to each source (independent variables). However, only PM2.5 from the Cu-related source was found as a significant factor for IRS-1, but with negative regression coefficients. Similarly, none of the PM2.5 sources was found to be the significant variable for TNF-α. We then did the MLR analysis by air mass categories, and PM2.5 from marine vessels and Cu-related sources showed statistically significant positive linear relationships (P ≤ 0.01) with TNF-α on long regional transport (LRT) days, and the regression coefficients were 0.444 and 0.429, respectively. For IRS-1, only Cu-related source was found to have a statistically significant negative relationship with it. We’ve also conducted genome-wide transcriptional analysis of exposed AML-12 cells. It was found that cellular processes, biological regulation, and response to stimulus were the most represented biological processes affected by PM2.5 exposure. TNF signaling pathway, NF-κB signaling pathway, hepatitis C, and those involved in response to chemokine signaling pathway were among the top 10 influenced pathways in PM2.5 treated AML-12 cells. Results of this part are presented in Ma et al. (2022) and Hu et al. (2022). (Objective 3) 4. Higher levels of DTTV activity were found on days mainly influenced by regional pollution sources (regional days, median: 0.52, range: 0.30 – 0.75 nmol min-1 m-3), followed by local days (median: 0.47, range: 0.22 – 0.69 nmol min-1 m-3), and then LRT days (median: 0.45, range: 0.21 – 0.67 nmol min-1 m-3). Higher levels of TNF-α secretion were found on days mainly influenced by local emissions (local days), which is opposite to the trends of the PM2.5 mass concentrations and DTT-ROS activity. On the other hand, the increase of IRS-1 response was more significant on days mainly influenced by regional pollution sources. Pearson’s correlation analysis between TNF-α, IRS-1 response, DTTV, and chemical components of PM2.5 (including EC, OC, WSOC, and markers of various primary and secondary PM2.5 sources) was conducted. TNF-α was found only statistically significantly correlated with WSOC and oxalate ion (p<0.01), but negatively. In fact, it showed negative correlations with almost all species, except for vanadium (V) and copper (Cu). IRS-1 presented strong positive correlations between hopanes and several transition metals (e.g., Fe, Mn, and Zn), indicating that vehicle emissions and metal-related industrial sources might be related to the PM2.5-induced IRS-1 response. (Objective 4)

12328216.label: Major findings and research outcome
12328216.value: In this study, 65 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong during a one-year period were analyzed, including carbonaceous components, major ions, metals, and a number of primary and secondary source markers. The oxidative potential of total extracts of PM2.5 (water-soluble + lipid-soluble fractions) were measured using an acellular dithiothreitol (DTT) assay. DTT activity, PM2.5 mass concentration, and its major chemical fractions all showed higher levels on days under regional pollution than on days under influences of long range transport (LRT) pollution and local emissions. We then conducted source apportionment using positive matrix factorization model. Marine vessels, Cu-related source, Fe-Mn-Zn-related source, vehicle emissions, biomass burning, and secondary formation sources were resolved for both PM2.5 mass concentration and DTT activity. Cu-related source, secondary formation, and marine vessels were the top three contributors to both PM2.5 mass concentration and its induced DTT activity, with secondary formation as the leading source for PM2.5 mass concentration (30.3%) and the Cu-related source as the predominant contributor (39.1%) responsible for the DTT consumption of PM2.5. As for the intrinsic oxidative potential of PM2.5 from different sources, PM2.5 emitted from marine vessels and Cu-related source showed the highest values, indicating more toxic feature of PM2.5 derived from these two sources regarding DTT activity. We exposed the total extracts of PM2.5 samples to the murine macrophage cell line RAW 264.7 cells and quantified the TNF-α secretion. We then treated the murine hepatocyte cell line AML-12 cells using the supernatant of exposed RAW 264.7 cells, and the response of phosphorylation of IRS-1 on serine-307 was monitored. Higher levels of TNF-α secretion were found on local days, which is opposite to the trends of the PM2.5 mass concentrations and its ROS activity. A clear upregulating of IRS-1 protein was observed in PM2.5 extracts treated AML-12 cells, and the increase of IRS-1 response was more significant on regional days. IRS-1 presented strong positive correlations with hopanes and several transition metals (e.g., Fe, Mn, and Zn), indicating that vehicle emissions and metal-related industrial sources might be related to the PM2.5-induced IRS-1 response. Genome-wide transcriptional analysis of exposed AML-12 cells revealed that cellular processes, biological regulation, and response to stimulus were the most represented biological processes affected by PM2.5 exposures. TNF signaling pathway, NF-κB signaling pathway, hepatitis C, and those involved in response to chemokine signaling pathway were among the top 10 influenced pathways in PM2.5 treated AML-12 cells.

12328216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12328216.value: Future studies will be carried out to explore more on the involved pathways of PM2.5-induced IRS-1 response. Other biological endpoints could be monitored to help explain the association between PM2.5 exposure and susceptibility to T2DM.

12328416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12328416.value: 切觸流形上次橢圓算子的指標定理--熱核方法

12328416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12328416.value: Atiyah--Singer 所建立的指標定理是數學上最傑出的結果之一，該定理將橢圓算子的解析指標與流形的拓撲指標聯繫起來。Atiyah--Singer 的指標公式包含了之前許多著名的定理，比如 Gauss--Bonnet--Chern 定理、Riemann--Roch--Hizenbruch 定理等都是其特例。最近，van Erp 與 Baum氏將 Atiyah--Singer 指標定理推廣到了切觸流形上的次橢圓算子的情形，他們的方法是利用K-理論與非交換拓撲學來定義一類合適的上同調類。 關於指標定理的證明，除了Atiyah 與 Singer 原本的 K-理論方法，Patodi 提出了另外一種基於熱核漸近展開的方法。Patodi 證明的思想是計算熱核之跡的漸近展開的係數，其中第 (n/2) 項的係數依賴於我們所關注的指標，在這裡 n 代表流形的拓撲維數。因而， Patodi 以及 Atiyah--Bott--Patodi 的證明方法需要大量的計算。後來，Getzler 氏提出了一種變量變換的方法使得指標定理的熱核證明得到極大的簡化。 本研究計劃的目標是利用熱核方法來證明切觸流形上次橢圓算子的指標定理。我們將利用擬微分算子的技巧來計算熱核漸近展開式。基於切觸結構，我們將 Greiner 的計算方法與 Heisenberg 分析法相結合，並且 Getzler 的方法也會用來簡化指標公式的計算。算子指標會包含很多幾何量，比如曲率及其協變導數，這些都依賴於次黎曼型的幾何結構。

12328516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12328516.value: Inverse scattering problems are concerned with recovering the physical properties of objects, such as their location, shape and medium inhomogeneity through the measurement of acoustic, elastic or electromagnetic waves. They play fundamental roles in a broad range of applications, including radar and sonar, geophysical exploration, non-destructive testing, medical imaging and near-field optics. A major challenge in inverse scattering problems is to break the diffraction limit, which asserts the highest resolution of the details for the recovered objects is limited by one half of the wavelength. Super-resolution imaging refers to the solution methods for which the diffraction limit is broken and the finest details of the reconstructed image is beyond one half of the wavelength. This project aims to build effective mathematical models and develop efficient numerical methods for super-resolution imaging associated with a few important inverse scattering problems. In the first part of the project we propose a novel model and method for the imaging of infinite or closed rough surfaces. Instead of measuring the near-field data directly as in traditional techniques, we place a prism of negative-index metamaterial above the surface and measure the field on the farther end of the prism. Using a method recently developed by the PI and his collaborators, we found an infinite resolution is obtained with some ideal parameter values for the imaging of infinite rough surfaces. We shall continue investigating this promising model in more detail, in particular the effect on the resolution if the parameters are perturbed from the ideal values. We shall also generalize the method to more practical 3D problems and to closed surfaces such as bounded obstacles or cavities. In the second part of the project we consider super-resolution imaging of obstacles by elastic waves, an important research area with limited results. We shall investigate both the direct scattering and the inverse scattering problems. For the direct scattering problem, we shall establish the existence and uniqueness by investigating both the original boundary value problem for the total displacement field and the coupled boundary value problem for the pressure and shear wave components. For the inverse scattering problem, we shall study the domain derivative of of the direct scattering operator and apply iterative optimization methods. We will also generalize the continuation method recently developed for inverse acoustic and electromagnetic scattering problems with multiple frequency data and adapt it to inverse elastic scattering problems. 逆散射問題研究的是如何通過測量聲波，彈性波或電磁波來重構物體的未知信息，例如位置，形狀和材料組成。這類問題有廣泛的應用背景，包括雷達和聲吶，地質勘探，無損檢測，醫學影像和近場光學。逆散射問題中的一個主要挑戰是打破衍射極限，即最高分辨率無法超過波長的一半。能夠打破衍射極限從而取得小於二分之一波長的分辨率的现象或方法稱為超分辨率。本项目旨在针对某些重要的逆散射问题中的超分辨率现象或方法构建有效的数学模型并开发高效的数值方法。 在項目的第一部分我們針對無限和封閉曲面的成像問題提出一個創新的模型和方法。傳統方法是直接測量曲面散射的近場數據，而新方法是在曲面上方放置一塊具有負折射率的超材料組成的棱鏡，然後在棱鏡的頂端測量場的數據。對於二維無限曲面問題，我們採用PI和他的合作者最近開發的方法發現在某些理想參數設置下可以得到無窮分辨率。接下來我們將更加深入和透徹地研究本模型，特別是當參數偏離理想數值時對系統分辨率的影響。我們還將考慮把此方法推廣至更加具有實際應用價值的三維問題和封閉曲面，包括障礙物和封閉空腔。 在項目的第二部分我們將考慮彈性波散射問題里的超分辨率現象。彈性波散射問題是一個重要的研究領域，但是結果卻相對有限。我們將同時考慮正散射和逆散射問題。對于正問題，我們將通過研究原位移場所對應的邊值問題和壓縮波﹣剪力波所對應的耦合邊值問題來證明正問題解得存在性和唯一性。對于逆問題我們將研究區域導數和迭代優化的方法。我們還將推廣最近在聲波和電磁波逆散射問題中得到發展的多頻延續法至彈性波的逆散射問題。

12328516.label: Realisation of objectives
12328516.value: OBJECTIVE 1 A mathematical model has been built for super-resolution imaging of infinite rough surfaces with prism of negative-index material. The infinite rough surface is modeled as a smooth periodic surface with small amplitude and the perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary condition. A horizontal prism of double negative (DNG) metamaterial is placed above the rough surface and an plane wave is incident upon the structure from above and scattered by the prism and rough surface. Thus the mathematical model for the scattering problem is a boundary value problem (BVP) consisting of the Helmholtz equation in a half space with the PEC boundary condition on the lower boundary and an radiating condition in the upper direction. Given the rough surface, the prism, and the incident field, the direct scattering problem is to find the scattered field. Given the prism and the incident field, the inverse scattering problem is to determine the rough surface from the measurement data of the scattered field. OBJECTIVE 2 The mathematical model has been analyzed using the approach of transformed field expansion (TFE) for periodic surface in one dimension. The method is an improvement from the ones of the PI’s previous work and a simpler reconstruction formula is obtained without using convolution. Because of the simpler formula, we are able to conduct the analysis of the error and resolution enhancement. Consider the scattering of a time-harmonic plane wave by a rigid obstacle which is embedded in an open space filled with a homogeneous and isotropic elastic medium.The synthetic measurement data is obtained by the standard finite element method (FEM) combined with the perfectly matched layer (PML) technique in the upper direction of the domain. Because of the sign-changing coefficients in the PDE, the well-posedness of the direct scattering problem is not known at this time. Thus the reliability of the measurement data is not guaranteed. The model and method can be readily extended to the cases of infinite rough surface (non-periodic) and doubly-periodic or infinite rough surfaces in 3D. Similar model and method can be obtained for the imaging of rough surface of a bounded domain (obstacle scatterer), where the prism is an annulus surrounding the domain. OBJECTIVES 3 and 4 We considered the scattering of a time-harmonic plane wave by an elastically rigid obstacle which is embedded in an open space filled with a homogeneous and isotropic elastic medium. Given the incident field, the direct problem is to determine the displacement of the wave field from the known obstacle; the inverse problem is to determine the obstacle’s surface from the measurement of the displacement on an artificial boundary enclosing the obstacle. We considered both the direct and inverse problems. For the direct problem, we modeled it as a BVP with Dirichlet and transparent boundary conditions and investigated its well-posedness using the variational formulation. The inverse problem is investigated by an iterative method based on the domain derivative and a frequency-continuation approach for multi-frequency data. Numerical experiments have been done to illustrate the effectiveness of the method.
