12328516.label: Major findings and research outcome
12328516.value: IMAGING USING DNG PRISM We solved the inverse scattering problem using the transformed field expansion (TFE) and obtained a reconstruction formula that is a one-to-one correspondence of the Fourier coefficients of the measurement data and those of the imaged surface. That is a great improvement from the convolution type formula in the PI’s previous work. From the reconstruction formula, we obtained the following major findings. Case 1: the permittivity and permeability are both equal to -1 in the prism. All the Fourier coefficients of the surface can be reconstructed stably. That is, the resolution of the reconstruction is unlimited in this case. Case 2: the permittivity and permeability are small deviations from the value -1. The resolution of the reconstruction increases as magnitude of the deviations decreases and there is a clear cut-off frequency for stable reconstructions. Numerical experiments confirmed the analytical results in case 2. However, the synthetic measurement data cannot be obtained reliably in case 1 because of the (potentially) ill-posedness of the direct problem. A draft paper has been written for the above findings. Since the well-posedness of the direct problem has not been established theoretically, we are not submitting the draft for publication yet for the sake of mathematical rigor. DIRECT AND INVERSE ELASTIC SCATTERING ( publication 1) We considered the direct and inverse obstacle scattering by elastic waves. The infinite domain is truncated using a circle enclosing the obstacle and a transparent boundary condition is derived on the circle. We then derived a variational formulation for the direct scattering problem and established the well-posedness (existence and uniqueness of the solution). For the inverse scattering problem, we derived the domain derivative for the forward mapping and proposed a continuation method by using multiple frequency measurement data on the enclosing circle. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the method. A NOVEL METHOD FOR OBSTACLE SCATTERING (publication 2) A novel numerical method is proposed for the inverse obstacle scattering for acoustic or electromagnetic waves. The method is based on the fact the Dirichlet eigenfunctions vanish on the boundary and eigenfunctions (together with eigenvalues) can be approximately found from the scattered wave in a given frequency band. The numerical experiments show that the super-resolution can be achieved using a single or multiple eigenmodes.

12328516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12328516.value: The well-posedness of the direct scattering problem involving DNG material is a new challenge rising in the study of the corresponding inverse problem. Two potential approaches may be utilized to solve this problem, namely the so called T-coercivity framework and the limit absorption principle. The existing literature has not covered the model considered in this project and our numerical experiments indicate the sign of both coefficients may affect the well-posedness of the problem. If the imaged surface is not a small perturbation of the plane, then we can’t use the TFE approach. In that case, we can solve the problem by an iterative method based on the domain derivative. It would be interesting to investigate the differences in the property of this method for general inverse scattering involving DNG materials. The research can be further developed in many other directions, including biperiodic surfaces, obstacle/cavity model and elastic/electromagnetic waves.

12328516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12328516.value: The advancement of modern science and technology demands the ability to observe/image increasingly small objects with high accuracy. The physical principle behind the imaging technology is the interaction between the object and the measuring wave, such as light or sound wave. The smallest detail that can be resolved in wave imaging is called the resolution, and it is limited by the wavelength of the wave. Since the smallest wavelength that can be used in practice is restricted, it is desirable to achieve resolution beyond the limit (so called super-resolution). This project is mainly concerned with the mathematical modeling, analysis and computational methods for wave imaging with super-resolution. As one part of the project, we proposed a novel imaging scheme using double negative index metamaterials, a type of artificial material that is non-existent in nature. Our analysis and numerical experiments showed that the resolution can be greatly enhanced under given conditions. Another part of the project is concerned with imaging with elastic waves, a relatively new area of research demanding more complicated analysis and techniques. We studied the mathematical properties of one such model problem and proposed a numerical method that can use utilize multiple frequency data.

12328916.label: Project Objectives
12328916.value: Because of the use of nonparametric estimation in the nonparametric generalized likelihood ratio test, there is a bias term in the limiting null distribution, which tends to infinity and the significance level is hard to maintain. We then propose a bias corrected NGLRT to improve the performance. A more serious problem caused by the use of nonparametric estimation is the very slow nonparametric convergence rate of the test statistics to their limits under the null hypothesis. Therefore, the significance level is hard to maintain, and the power cannot be high. We will suggest a general approach that uses the dimension reduction structure such that the tests behave like the ones with the dimension under the null hypothesis. The tests can also adapt to the structure under the alternative hypothesis such that the tests can still be omnibus. To maintain the dimension reduction structure, we will construct a test that is based on a martingale transformation such that the test is asymptotically distribution-free and can still detect general alternative hypothesis. To achieve this goal, we will see that an adaptive estimation for the number of linear combinations of predictors under both the null and alternative hypothesis plays a vital role. We will suggest some method to estimate it. This approach is applied to the NGLRT, the bias-corrected NGLRT and the NSST. The simulations and real data analysis will be conducted to examine their performance in finite sample scenarios. We also study how to apply this method to other testing problems such as the cases with error-in-variables.

12328916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12328916.value: 回归模型的假设检验是统计分析中的一个必要的步骤。当预测变量个数较小时，现有的方法已被证明是有效的，例如，参数型单指数模型的非参数的广义似然比试验 (NGLRT) 和非参数模型的重要预测变量的基于局部平滑的显著性检验(LSST)。然而，维数问题对该领域的研究造成很大的挑战。 现有模型检验方法通常使用给定所有预测因子下，残差的条件期望去构造检验统计量。即便在假设模型具有降维结构的情况下，这种战略也涉及所有预测变量，因而有以下缺点。基于局部平滑的检验的抽样零分布收敛到极限零分布的速度较慢，因而，当极限零分布用于确定临界值，显著性水平难以保持。而重抽样近似是计算量较大。此外，这些检验对于局部备择模型不够敏感，这样只能检测以较慢速度靠近零假设的备择模型假设。 NLGRT 和TSSL就是这类方法的典型例子。 在这个项目中，对NLGRT，我们提出一个纠偏方法，使得其为渐近无偏的。更重要的是，我们将自适应到模型的构建方式应用到纠偏NLGRT和LSST上，以便充分利用在零假设下的降维结构，使构造出来的检验表现得像只有很少预测变量情况下的NLGRT和LSST。这样就可以大大降低维数祸根问题。该方法也可以应用到其他模型检验问题。 显然，这一项目研究统计推断领域中的若干重要的高维问题。期望新的方法和理论发展的过程中，对统计科学产生持久的影响。

12328916.label: Major findings and research outcome
12328916.value: For this proposal, we eventually published 5 academic articles that have achieved the objectives designed in the proposal. Specifically, To alleviate the curse of dimensionality in hypothesistesting problems for regressions and used nonparametric estimation in local smoothing tests, we have proposed two novel methodologies to construct adaptive-to-model tests for various problems including bias corrected nonparametric generalized likelihood ratio test, the tests for the models with measurement errors in covariates and a martingale transformation-based test even when the number of covariates is divergent. The model adaptation property helps enhance the power performance of tests and keeps the dimension reduction structure under the null hypothesis even when the alternative models do not have such a structure. The numerical studies show their usefulness.

12328916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12328916.value: High dimensionality is a key issue in complex data structure we frequenctly encounter with advanced technology development, and thus dimension reduction is a necessary technique we need. For this purpose, hypothesis testing needs a good way to keep the simple model structure usually in the test statistic under the null hypothesis and adapt to alternative hypothesis such that the tests would not lose power too much. Therefore, the methodology we develop, particularly when the number of covariates is divergent, may be applied to other problems beyond regression analysis. We are also considering whether this idea can be applied to causal inference.

12328916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12328916.value: As parametric regression models are often used for modelling, hypotyhsis testing is a necessary step to prevent possible misleading conclusion in any further analysis. To construct omnibus tests against general alternative models, we propose bias correction for nonparametric likelihood ratio test and partingale transformation-based test, and apply the relevant methods to the problems with measurement error in covariates. The model adaptation property is derived and thus the curse of dimensionality is largely avoided. The performances of these tests are also examined by numerical studies.

12331316.label: Project Objectives
12331316.value: To elucidate the degradation behaviors of the persistent micropollutant – the artificial sweetener acesulfame – in disinfected drinking water. This will mean first identifying the formation of chloramination byproducts, and second, determining how they are formed by comprehensive instrumental characterizations by using ultra performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS), gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR); To investigate the influence of natural organic matter and bromide ion in the transformation chemistry of acesulfame under chloramination; To provide information on the terminal fate of acesulfame from the aspect of drinking water safety and by this to evaluate the role of acesulfame as a nitrogenous DBP (N-DBP) precursor and contributor to the perceived health risks in disinfected water; To provide knowledge of the disinfection chemistry of acesulfame necessary to engineers in designing treatment processes and to governments in controlling wastewater treatment to ensure safe drinking water now and for the long-term.

12331316.value: 人工代糖安賽蜜廣泛而大量地應用於各種食品添加劑以及日常用品中；其化學結構十分穩定，一般生活污水處理過程對安賽蜜不能起到理想的去除效果，最終其直接排放到環境中。與其他人工代糖相比，全球環境領域中安賽蜜的檢出率最高，已引起高度關注。有報導指出，高強度的化學消毒處理手段如臭氧化、氯化和氯胺可有效降解安賽蜜；其中，氯胺消毒法已受到國際的廣泛認可與應用，如美國、中國、澳洲和英國。然而，與安賽蜜相比，其氯胺消毒處理可能會產生毒性更高的副產物。到目前為止，安賽蜜氯胺消毒降解產物的環境行為以及由此而引發的生態影響仍處於空白。我們的初步實驗結果表明，安賽蜜氯胺處理後其分子結構發生漸進式改變，產生了一系列的氯胺取代副產物；哺乳動物細胞毒理實驗顯示，安賽蜜氯胺副產物具有顯著的致突變毒性。因此，進一步深入探討安賽蜜氯胺化的化學機制以及毒性評價對保證消毒處理後飲用水的安全性和有效性具有深遠的意義。 本專案的主要目標是追蹤安賽蜜氯胺處理過程中的化學降解途徑。首先，利用先進化學分析儀器鑒定安賽蜜氯胺副產物/含氮氯胺副產物的化學結構，為闡述氯胺降解機制提供必要的基本資料；其次，以哺乳動物細胞為模型，通過測定細胞急性毒性和去氧核糖核苷酸損傷，全面開展安賽蜜氯胺降解產物的生物測試，進一步評價安賽蜜氯胺處理的水安全隱患，確保人體健康；最後，與實踐相結合，監測污水廠水處理過程以及居民飲用水中安賽蜜氯胺降解產物是否真實存在，進一步驗證本課題的必要性和緊迫性。因此，本專案將化學與毒理學相結合，進一步完善現有生態環境資料，不僅為安賽蜜的全面環境影響評價奠定堅實的科學基礎，而且為“水”-這一重要資源的可持續發展和水消毒處理過程提供有價值的化學設計方案和方法。 本專案通過開展實驗室模擬氯胺水消毒處理過程，著手探討安賽蜜的降解過程。利用全面的儀器分析與表徵手段，鑒定氯胺產物的分子結構、闡述反應機理與降解路徑；體外實驗利用中國倉鼠卵巢細胞CHO-K1進一步探討與人體健康相關的慢性和基因毒性指標；收集污水廠水處理過程以及居民飲用水樣品，監測安賽蜜氯胺降解產物的存在和濃度水平，準確評價安賽蜜水消毒產物造成的潛在實際環境風險。

12331316.label: Realisation of objectives
12331316.value: The stated project objectives have been completely and satisfactorily achieved. The degradation behaviors of acesulfame (ACE) under different disinfection conditions (i.e., chloramination, UV photolysis and UV/chloramine (UV/NH2Cl)) were investigated. The UV/chloramine process is more effective in degrading acesulfame than UV photolysis and solely chloramination. For chloramination alone, a significantly higher concentration of NH2Cl is required to enable ACE degradation, as compared to UV/Chloramine process. Furthermore, the transformation products (TPs) of ACE in the three scenarios were also identified and structurally elucidated. In total, 28 TPs and 3 disinfection byproducts were identified. In particular, treatment of ACE under the UV/chloramine process led to the generation of ten new TPs, which are all chlorinated-TPs. The inclusion of chlorine atom in the TPs structure are proposed to be generated through Cl-substitution. Through structural elucidation and the purported transformation pathways of these TPs, a significant contribution of reactive chlorine species in the UV/NH2Cl transformation process is proposed. (Objective #1) The influence of natural organic matter, inorganic anions and pH to ACE under UV/NH2Cl process were investigated. Inhibition of ACE degradation was observed in the presence of 5 mg L-1 humic acid. For inorganic anions, bromide and chloride have no observable effect on ACE degradation, while bicarbonate was observed to the suppression of ACE degradation under UV/NH2Cl process. (Objective #2) To determine the safety of UV/NH2Cl treatment for waters containing acesulfame, the potential acute toxicity was compared with that by UV photolysis using Vibrio fischeri bioluminescence inhibition assay. The results revealed a higher toxicity of the suite of TPs derived from UV/NH2Cl than UV photolysis. Through further in silico quantitative structural activity relationships analysis using the Ecological Structure Activity Relationships (ECOSAR) Class Program, the increased toxicity was found to be attributed to most of the generated chlorinated-TPs, in particular those TPs resembling the chemical structure of halo-alcohols. These halo-alcohol TPs are predicted to be more toxic than their non-chlorinated analogues, and the other chlorinated-TPs. The combination of the in vitro V. fischeri bioluminescence inhibition assay, together with the ECOSAR prediction, allowed a more comprehensive evaluation of the toxicity impact of the UV/NH2Cl process. (Objective #3) It can be demonstrated that under disinfection scenarios, based on the findings in objectives #1, 2 and 3, ACE will be transformed to different TPs and DBPs, with a potential increase in toxicity as compared with the parent compound, considering both the TPs’ mixture toxicity and individual TP’s toxicity. In particular, attention should be paid to the generation of Cl-TPs which are even more toxic than their non-chlorinated analogues, as well as the production of halo-alcohol TPs. Considering the fact that both chloramination and UV photolysis are nowadays applied for water disinfection, their potential combined use (in particular in the form of UV/NH2Cl process) should be carefully evaluated, in order to strike a balance between micropollutant abatement and the post-treatment toxicity change. (Objective #4)

12331316.label: Major findings and research outcome
12331316.value: In the present study, the impact of chloramination on ACE transformation was studied in order to assess the potential risk of ACE chloramination to both human health and the environment. Laboratory simulation experiments revealed that ACE are degraded and transformed to different transformation products (TPs) in different disinfection scenarios (i.e., chloramination, UV photolysis, UV/chloramine process). Using UHPLC-QTOF-MS, TPs and DBPs of ACE in the above-mentioned scenarios were isolated and analyzed. Among the twenty-eight TPs identified, ten of them were firstly reported. The TPs’ molecular structures and transformation pathways were proposed for different disinfection scenarios. Further Vibrio fischeri bioluminescence inhibition assay revealed that the suite of TPs generated by UV/chloramine process were more toxic than the parent compound and the TPs generated from UV/photolysis, suggesting that those Cl-TPs could cause an enhancement in toxicity. In silico quantitative structural activity relationships analysis using the Ecological Structure Activity Relationships (ECOSAR) Class Program, revealed that the increased toxicity could be attributed to most of the generated chlorinated-TPs, in particular the halo-alcohols. Combining the elucidated transformation pathways of ACE under chloramination, UV photolysis and UV/chloramination, together with the post-treatment toxicity change, these results indicated that the accumulation and contamination of ACE in our precious water resources urgently needed a solution. A research article addressing the above findings was published in Journal of Hazardous Materials, 2021, 403, 123935. With the successful development of UHPLC-MS/MS and UHPLC-QTOF-MS analysis platform, the application was further extended to the determination of micropollutants in extreme trace levels. An additional publication using this platform for analysis was published in Water Research 187 (2020) 116419.

12331316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12331316.value: The present study provided critical knowledge on the transformation fate of ACE upon chloramination-based drinking water treatments. As observed, generated TPs were found to elicit higher toxicity than the parent artificial sweetener, and also the non-chlorinated TPs. Further studies on the environmental impact of these Cl-TPs must be conducted in order to comprehensively assess the potential hazards of these chemicals to the environment. A systematic evaluation of different sequence of UV photolysis and chloramination that may affect the transformation fate and toxicity of micropollutants has been planned - which allowed the comprehensive elucidation on the role of chloramine and UV irradiation in different sequence of treatment scenarios for micropollutants abatement. The ultimate goal of these studies will serve as important basis for developing new water treatment technique that can safely remove micropollutants and their corresponding toxic TPs.

12331316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12331316.value: ACE is one of the mostly occurred micropollutants in the environment worldwide due to continuous domestic input. The high levels of ACE has caught attention to a potential global problem of contaminating our precious water resources. From our present research findings, it is revealed that ACE will be transformed in the presence of disinfectants such as chloramine. During these disinfection processes, ACE will be transformed into a suite of chemical byproducts, in which the transformation route depends on the disinfection technique(s) used. Alarmingly, according to results of toxicity studies, the generated suite of chemical byproducts are more toxic than the original micropollutant. These findings suggested that various disinfection techniques adopted nowadays in water treatment facilities, which supposed to remove micropollutants and safeguard human health through disinfection, may generate even more problems. The success of present research project will provide guideline for future comprehensive risk assessment of similar types of micropollutants; and in the development of suitable water treatment techniques to safeguard both our environment and human health.

12338416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12338416.value: Due to their capability of converting heat into electricity (and vice versa), thermoelectric (TE) devices are expected to play an important role in addressing today’s global energy issues and solving the related environmental concerns. At present, research in this area mainly focuses on developing high-performance TE materials. Among these, inorganic semiconductors are currently the most commonly studied TE materials due to their intrinsically high mobility, tunable electrical conductivity through doping, and generally high Seebeck coefficient (S). However, the relatively high cost for production, scarcity of certain components, and toxicity of these materials tend to limit their large-scale deployment for TE devices. Carbon-based π-conjugated materials such as conducting polymers, carbon nanotubes and graphenes, and their hybrids offer new opportunities for TE applications because of their low thermal conductivity, large S, and tunable high electrical conductivity. Organic TE devices can be fabricated from solution-cast films, which will allow large-scale device fabrication from low-cost techniques. The current record TE figure of merit (ZT) values for inorganic and organic materials are 2.6 at 923 K and 0.42 at room temperature, respectively. While increasing effort has been put into the development of TE devices based on conjugated organic polymers recently, the exploitation of soluble metal-containing polymers in TE applications is still in its infancy. Examples of metallated polymers as active organic TE materials are very scarce indeed, despite their advantages. The most well-known examples to date are the poly(metal 1,1,2,2-ethenetetrathiolate)s with the best ZT of 0.20. However, all the conjugated polymers developed so far failed to compete with the inorganic semiconductors. To address this issue, we initiate a program of developing new series of electrically conducting metallopolymers for high-performance TE applications. Metal-containing polymers are good candidates owing to the immense structural diversity, range of properties and intermolecular/supramolecular interactions made possible by adding the metallic elements. The incorporation of transition-metal centers would be expected to facilitate intrachain charge transport and intermolecular stacking interactions. With our strengths in synthetic, polymer and coordination chemistry, the properties and performance of TE devices can be fine-tuned through chemical modifications of the metal-organic chromophore, which can give either p-type or n-type TE materials. The present work will certainly fill in a relatively under-explored area of organic TE research and would provide a new impetus to the creation of some technologically useful TE materials with higher stability and ZT.

12338416.label: Realisation of objectives
12338416.value: The PI has recruited two Ph.D. students to work on the project and one of them has graduated while the other one is writing up her thesis. So far, the PI has secured 13 publications from this project (including 1 paper in Nat. Commun., 1 paper in Chem. Eng. J., 2 papers in Coord. Chem. Rev., 1 paper in Polym. Chem. and 1 paper in Chem. Asian J., etc.). The PI has attended and given plenary/invited lectures in four national and international conferences. Both graduate students have received good training in several areas of modern science and technology in Hong Kong. A series of new metallopolymers (e.g. Pt metallopolyynes, metal-bis(terpyridine) coordination polymers, metal Schiff-base polymers, etc.) and their precursor complexes were synthesized via different approaches and characterized by spectroscopic, photophysical, thermal, structural and electrochemical methods. The structure-property-function relationships of these polymers were examined, which can form a good basis for the future design of new thermoelectric materials. Some polymers can be used to develop new thermoelectric materials with decent performance. As far as the GRF is concerned, the PI considers that he has addressed in full all the issues relevant to the objectives concerned.

12338416.label: Major findings and research outcome
12338416.value: A series of (metallo)polymers have been synthesized (papers 1-13) which represent a new family of organic thermoelectric (TE) materials. The spectroscopic and other physical properties of these new polymers were examined in detail. Among these, various platinum-acetylide polymers were developed (papers 7-10). A planar moiety of platinum acetylide in the π-conjugated system is introduced to enhance the intermolecular interaction with the SWCNTs via π-π and d-π interactions, which is crucial in regulating their TE performances. SWCNT composites based on the platinum acetylides-embedded polymers displayed a higher power factor at ambient temperature than those without platinum acetylides under the same conditions. Moreover, the strong interactions between the platinum acetylide-based polymers and the SWCNTs are demonstrated. Besides. some π-conjugated polymers with or without the incorporation of platinum acetylides are designed. Remarkably, the embedded heavy metal atoms can effectively sharpen their density of states nearby the Fermi levels as well as strengthening their through-bond coupling among the metal d-orbitals and the neighboring π-orbitals synchronously. Meanwhile, a simple interfacial modification by using trifluoromethanesulfonic acid is introduced to offer them dual electronic-ionic transport feature. Therefore, a remarkably high thermopower and an enhanced conductivity can be achieved, which is significantly superior to the polymer without platinum-acetylides. In addition, all these platinum-acetylides exhibit low thermal conductivity values. A series of new metallopolymers based on metal-bis(terpyridine) fragment and 3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene spacer were also synthesized and the metal centres played an important role in affecting the morphology of the metallopolymer-SWCNT composite thin films, which was a key factor that determined their TE performances. Additionally, the energy levels of the metallopolymers were feasibly tuned by selecting different metal centres (paper 11). Two series of poly(Schiff base)s with either C=C or C≡C linker and their metallopolymers were synthesized and doped with SWCNT to evaluate how the linking groups affected the TE properties of the resulting composites. Experimental results suggested that the linkers played a key role in determining the band gaps, preferred molecular conformation and extent of conjugation of the polymers, which became key factors that influenced the TE properties of the materials (papers 2 and 12). Some organic precursor molecules and polymers were also made which can be further derivatized to other organometallic systems in the future studies (papers 1, 5, 6). The PI was also invited to contribute related review articles on multifunctional metal-containing polymers and complexes in Coord. Chem. Rev. (papers 3-4) and Macromol. Chem. Phys. (paper 13).

12338416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12338416.value: The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future: (1) Extension of the work to other metal and ligand chromophores which can be expected to show improved thermoelectric properties. (2) Enhancement of the performance of the thermoelectric devices.

12338416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12338416.value: A series of metal-containing polymers have been prepared which represent a new class of thermoelectric organic materials. The spectroscopic, photophysical, thermal, structural and redox properties of these new organometallic and coordination polymers were investigated in detail. Furthermore, these metallopolymers were shown to exhibit thermoelectric effect useful for the conversion of heat to electrical energy. The present work fills in a relatively under-investigated area of organometallic thermoelectrics and would provide a new impetus to the creation of some technologically useful materials and systems for utilizing the wasted heat energy.

12505116.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12505116.value: Prof Hwang, Chuan Yang Prof Wong, Kit Pong

12505116.label: Project Objectives
12505116.value: Explaining why high dispersion stocks earn lower returns by disentangling the difference-in-opinion explanation from the self-censoring explanation. Examining the dispersion-bias relationship in greater details. Providing regulatory implications regarding the incentive structure of financial analysts.
rows: Explaining why high dispersion stocks earn lower returns by disentangling the difference-in-opinion explanation from the self-censoring explanation.
Examining the dispersion-bias relationship in greater details.
Providing regulatory implications regarding the incentive structure of financial analysts.

12505116.label: Realisation of objectives
12505116.value: We have successfully achieved all three goals set in the proposal. Details are as follows: Goal 1. Explaining why high dispersion stocks earn lower returns by disentangling the difference-in-opinion explanation from the self-censoring explanation. We focus on two plausible explanations to account for the dispersion effect that stocks with higher dispersion in analyst forecasts earn lower returns: (i) the difference-in-opinion explanation, and (ii) the self-censoring explanation. The first explanation postulates that forecast dispersion is a proxy for different opinions among investors. Short-sale constraints prohibit pessimistic investors from trading, so stock prices reflect only the optimistic views. This induces a greater upward bias in the prices of stocks with higher forecast dispersion, which in turn results in lower future returns. The second explanation postulates that the incentive structure of analysts induces them to self-censor unfavorable earnings forecasts to please managers. When analysts’ forecasts are more dispersed, there are more pessimistic forecasts to self-censor. Thus, there is a greater upward bias in the consensus earnings forecasts of stocks with higher dispersion in analysts’ forecasts. If investors do not take the upward bias into account when making their investment decisions, they tend to overvalue stocks with higher forecast dispersion, which, in turn, leads to lower future returns for these stocks. We utilize the different predictions regarding dispersion effect in stocks with respect to high institutional ownership between the two explanations. Institutional ownership is commonly used as a proxy for short-sale constraints in the literature. Stocks with high institutional ownership are less subject to short-sale constraints, as institutional investors are important suppliers of shares for short selling. Thus, stocks with higher institutional ownership will exhibit a weaker dispersion effect if the underlying reason for the dispersion effect is difference-in-opinion. On the other hand, institutional ownership is used as a proxy for demand for analysts’ services, which affects analysts’ incentives to self-censor. When analysts receive unfavorable signals about a firm’s upcoming earnings, the incentive structure of analysts induces them either to adjust their forecasts upward at a cost of losing reputation, or to issue no forecasts (i.e., self-censor). When analysts face greater demand for their services, they find the reputational cost of adding an optimistic bias to be higher, which makes them more likely to self-censor unfavorable forecasts. As self-censoring induces a greater upward bias to the consensus forecast than adding an optimistic bias does, stocks with greater demand for analysts’ services will have a stronger dispersion effect. Since the demand for analysts’ services increases with institutional ownership, stocks with higher institutional ownership will exhibit a stronger dispersion effect if analyst self-censoring explains the dispersion effect. The potentially endogenous nature of institutional ownership can bias the test inference. Using a sample in which stocks’ institutional ownership is exogenously determined we find a significant dispersion effect for stocks with higher institutional ownership, but no dispersion effect for stocks with lower institutional ownership. These results suggest that after we address the potential inference problem caused by the endogenous nature of institutional ownership, the dispersion effect is stronger for stocks with higher institutional ownership. These findings clearly refute the difference-in-opinion and are in favor of the analyst self-censoring story for the explanation of the dispersion effect. Goal 2. Examining the dispersion-bias relationship in greater details. Since the underlying source of the dispersion effect under the self-censoring explanation is the greater bias in analysts’ forecasts associated with high dispersion firms (positive dispersion-bias relationship), our results imply that the positive dispersion-bias relationship will be stronger in stocks with higher institutional ownership. Again, the potentially endogenous nature of institutional ownership can bias the test inference. The information advantage of institutional investors makes them less likely to hold stocks with unfavorable prospects, thus stocks with low institutional ownership are more likely to have unfavorable prospects, especially for high dispersion stocks (i.e., stocks with high information asymmetry). This – combined with analysts’ incentive to self-censor only unfavorable forecasts – should lead us to find the dispersion-bias relationship to be stronger among stocks with low institutional ownership. This is indeed the case. In a sample in which institutional ownership may be endogenous, we find a stronger dispersion-bias relationship among stocks with low institutional ownership that might have led us to reject the self-censoring explanation. However, once we avoid the potential endogeneity problem of institutional ownership, we find the opposite. These results provide further support to the self-censoring explanation, since a stronger dispersion-bias relationship among firms with high institutional ownership is a prediction unique to the self-censoring explanation; the difference-in-opinion explanation has no such prediction on dispersion-bias relationship. Goal 3. Providing regulatory implications regarding the incentive structure of financial analysts. We show that the incentive structure of analysts is significant enough to distort information production in financial markets. Also, in contrast to the moderating effect of institutional ownership documented in the literature, we find that analysts’ incentives can be exacerbated by institutional ownership. Ours provide additional evidence for regulatory action to better align the best interests between investors and financial analysts.

12505116.label: Major findings and research outcome
12505116.value: The project disentangles the two plausible explanations that account for the dispersion effect (that stocks with high dispersion in analyst forecasts earn lower future returns): (i) the difference-in-opinion explanation, and (ii) the self-censoring explanation. The first explanation postulates that forecast dispersion is a proxy for different opinions among investors. Short-sale constraints prohibit pessimistic investors from trading, so stock prices reflect only the optimistic. This induces a greater upward bias in the prices of stocks with higher forecast dispersion, which in turn results in lower future returns. The second explanation postulates that the incentive structure of analysts induces them to self-censor unfavorable earnings forecasts to please managers. When analysts’ forecasts are more dispersed, there are more pessimistic forecasts to self-censor. Thus, there is a greater upward bias in the consensus earnings forecasts of stocks with higher dispersion in analysts’ forecasts. If investors do not take the upward bias into account when making their investment decisions, they tend to overvalue stocks with higher forecast dispersion, which, in turn, leads to lower future returns for these stocks. We attempt to disentangle two plausible explanations by constructing two mutually exclusive hypotheses regarding the effect of institutional ownership on the strength of the dispersion effect. The difference-in-opinion explanation predicts a stronger dispersion effect among stocks with lower institutional ownership. The self-censoring explanation predicts the exact opposite. Although our initial results confirm the findings in the literature that the dispersion effect is stronger among stocks with lower institutional ownership and seem to support the difference-in-opinion explanation, we raise the concern that this conclusion can be tainted by the possible endogeneity of institutional ownership. Using a sample in which the variation of institutional ownership is exogenously induced, we find the opposite results. We find parallel results when we focus on the relationship between dispersion and bias. These findings suggest that the self-censoring story may be more plausible than the popular difference-in-opinion story as an explanation of the dispersion effect, and it deserves more attention in the literature. Our paper highlights the importance of controlling for the endogeneity of institutional ownership when institutional ownership is part of the hypothesis for the explanation of characteristics-sorted return effects, if the characteristics also proxy for the degree of the institutional investors’ information advantage.

12505116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12505116.value: Ours highlights the incentive problems of financial analysts. The incentive structure of financial analysts makes it hard for these analysts to report unfavorable news of companies they cover. Financial analysts, however, are important information producers in the financial markets. It is, therefore, important to design mechanisms/contracts such that their best interests are aligned well with investors at large. We believe the next line of research is i) to provide more evidences regarding the conflict of interests of financial analysts; ii) to design regulations such that investors’ best interests are protected.

12505116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12505116.value: We attempt to explain the phenomenon that the more financial analysts’ opinions differ with respect to a stock’s earnings, the lower future return the stock will earn. While many people argue that the opinion difference among analysts is the result of difference in opinion among all investors at large. Given it is very difficult for investors to sell a stock without owing one in the first place, only investors favor the stock will buy and push up the price. As a result, stock price is over-valued. We, however, argue that it is not the case and provide evidences showing that the underlying reason for these stocks earning lower future returns is due to analysts. We argue because of the trade-off between the concern of their own reputation and of their relationship with firms they cover, analysts will stop covering firms if they receive unfavorable news about these stocks. And stronger difference in opinion among analysts is a manifest of more of them have stopped covering firms, leading to negative information not reflected in stock prices and therefore the lower future return. Our project highlights the important incentive problems of financial analysts when it comes to unfavorable news.

12511016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12511016.value: 現代的科技發展顯著地改變了青少年現有的生活模式，將青少年的日常社交擴展到網上媒體。社交網雖然促進了青少年間的互動，但卻同時衍生出各種不良的現象，如網絡欺凌。近年來社交網絡欺凌的報導屢見不鮮，有更多的證據顯示社交網絡欺凌不再侷限於施暴者與受害者的相互關係，旁觀者在社交網絡欺凌的影響亦是十分關鍵 ，擔當著附和或煽動的角色。 在回顧文獻時，我們發現迄今的研究多側重於描述旁觀者的特點， 心理以及人格變量對他們行為的影響，以理論主導的旁觀者研究仍有待發展。網絡欺凌是一種透過信息通信技術作為媒介的欺凌行為，所以網絡媒體的特性對旁觀者的行為起了決定性的影響。唯這課題仍未獲得資管理訊系統學者深切的關注，故相關的記載仍然有限。 因此，我們借鑒道德脫離的理論來解釋旁觀者參與社交網絡欺凌行為的成因。具體來說，我們探討社交網站特性如何誘發旁觀者的基本道德脫離機制，引致他們參與社交網絡欺凌。這項研究將以活躍於社交網站的大學生為研究對象。 我們預期這項研究會對理論和實踐兩方面作出重大的貢獻。在理論方面，本研究從一個嶄新的角度探討旁觀者參與社交網絡欺凌行為的誘因和機制，豐富了網絡欺凌以及管理資訊科技相關的文獻。此外，本研究亦嚮應了學術界的呼籲，探索了使用資訊技術衍生的社會挑戰，這項研究的成果將揭示更多在使用資訊技術上的利與弊 。在實踐方面，本研究的結果將提供有效的干預方案（如：社交網站的界面設計指引 ），以遏止旁觀者參與社交網絡欺凌。

12512216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12512216.value: 本研究旨在測試心理模擬事件發生的過程和結果分別對消費者其後調節行為的影響。 消費者往往被鼓勵去模擬想像一下他們即將到來的消費體驗。有許多研究支持這個做法；這些研究區分出兩種不同類型的心理模擬：過程模擬 (process simulation) 和結果模擬 (outcome simulation) (Pham and Taylor 1999) ，並普遍建議前者比後者更有利於達到成果 (Escalas and Luce 2003; Pham and Taylor 1999; Taylor et al. 1998) 。然而，這些研究都有一些局限。第一，現時的研究大都集中於心理模擬中產生的想法有何影響，卻忽略了心理模擬過程中的主觀體驗。事實上，最近Thompson et al. (2009)在一項研究中考慮到心理模擬所產生的主觀體驗 (即信息處理的難度) ，並發現過程模擬在某些情況下可增加消費者的決策難度和降低他們及後的工作表現。因此，過程模擬不一定是有利的；當心理模擬時產生的主觀感受加入考量時，或許會對心理模擬的影響有新發現。第二，現有的研究均集中於心理模擬一件事情如何影響現實中對該事情的反應。對於心理模擬能否影響與模擬結果無關的行為仍不甚了解。 本研究測試過程和結果模擬分別產生的主觀感受如何影響及後在不相關情況下的調節行為。我們以資源調節的角度分析，並提出過程模擬會消耗資源，而結果模擬相反能提供更多資源。過程模擬中，消費者想像要通過什麼步驟才取得有利結果 (Pham and Taylor 1999) 。這種思考方式需要消費者想像如何調節其情緒和行為方能達到結果，故此會消耗他們有限的調節資源，令他們在及後不相關的情況下不能作出有效調節。相反，在結果模擬中，消費者想像達到結果的好處和快感，令他們自信有能力和充滿活力(Ryan and Deci 2000)。這種感覺延續至及後不相關的情況，令消費者自覺有足夠的調節資源來調節其行為。 我們亦提出過程模擬會否導致調節失效，取決於消費者對於想像的過程是否只有外在原動力 (即只視過程為達到結果的手段) ；而結果模擬會否有利於調節，則視乎獲得想像中的結果能否反映消費者的能力。這些規範條件顯示了模擬想像的效果是建基於它能提升或消耗調節資源。在本建議書中，我們還展示了一些支持我們理論的初步調查結果。 這項研究對心理模擬文獻作出兩方面的貢獻。第一，以往的研究主要集中於心理模擬在認知層面的影響，而本研究則調查消費者在模擬想像裡的主觀體驗 (即感到精力充沛還是精力耗盡) ，並測試這種感覺如何影響及後的調節行為。以資源調節角度為基礎，我們作出與認知角度研究不同的預測。第二，這項研究擴展了心理模擬的作用至與想像內容不相關 的情況(thought-content-independent contexts)，為我們對心理模擬效果提供更全面的理解。

12522916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12522916.value: Online crowdfunding has recently received a great deal of attention as an alternative and appealing financing channel. According to the “2015CF” Crowdfunding Industry Report (Crowdfundingsourcing.org 2015), global crowdfunding experienced accelerated growth in 2014, expanding by 167 percent to reach $16.2 billion raised, up from $6.1 billion in 2013. In 2015, the industry is set to again more than double, on its way to raising $34.4 billion. In any crowdfunding campaign, the fundraiser is the person who raises the funding request, and those who decide to contribute to the project are funders or contributors. Crowdfunding projects can be categorized into reward-based or donation-based, depending on whether or not the funders get rewards (either monetary or non-monetary) from funding the project. According to a random search on three leading crowdfunding websites (Kickstarter, GoFundMe, and Pozible), the two most frequently used words in crowdfunding project descriptions are “want” and “need”. Nearly 48% of projects posted on these websites use either “want” or “need” in their project description, with 147,066 projects using “want” and 278,634 using “need”. If a person is going to post a crowdfunding campaign on online platforms, will the subtle differences between “I want your help” and “I need your help” in his or her post influence the intention and behavior of potential funders? Though the words “want” and “need” are used somewhat interchangeably in many contexts, we propose that they can profoundly influence the perception of crowdfunding projects. By examining the fundamental difference between the two words from a linguistic perspective, we speculate that a “want” (versus “need”) claim helps to provide a competent image of the fundraiser, and thus increases the motivation and behavior of investors to fund their project when the crowdfunding campaign is reward-based. Conversely, when the crowdfunding campaign is donation-based, a “need” (versus “want”) claim increases the intention and behavior of investors to fund the project, due to the greater perceived criticality of the request activated by the “need” (versus “want”) claim. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate linguistic elements in the crowdfunding industry, which is an emerging marketing phenomenon increasing in popularity worldwide. Four studies are proposed to support our arguments, including an initial investigation on real market data and laboratory experiments. 網上群眾募資，作為另類的經濟集資手段，最近得到了大眾的關注。根據2015年的群眾募資行業研究報告，全球群眾募資在2014年得到了很大的增長。由2013年的61億元增長了167% 至162億元。在2015年，這行業甚至增長了一倍至344億元。在集資活動，募資者是提出集資計畫的申請人, 而資助者是為計畫提供資金的人。集資活動分為兩種，分別是有回報及沒有回報的，當中包括金錢上的回報或是非金錢上的回報。 根據三個最出名群眾募資網站 (Kickstarter的，GoFundMe和Pozible) 的隨機搜索，在群眾募資項目中，最常用的兩個字是“想要”和“需要”。在這些網站上的項目，有大概48％的人在自己的項目介紹上使用“想要”或“需要”這二字(分別有147,066個項目使用了“想要”和278,634個項目使用了“需要”)。但在一個募資者在網上平台的集資活動上，寫上“我想要你的幫助”或“我需要你的幫助”，這細小的差距會否影響潛在的資助者的意圖和行為？” 雖然“想要”和“需要”在許多情況下可以交替使用，但我們推測這兩個詞語的使用能深刻影響資助者對集資項目的看法。從語言學的角度來看，我們推測當集資項目是有實際回報時，使用“想要”有助提升募捐活動的形像，從而增加了投資者的投資動機和投資行為。相反，當集資活動是沒有回報的時候，使用“需要”會增加資助者的資助意圖和資助該項目。這是由於“需要”會令資助者覺得該項目更為緊急。集資行業的是一個新興的市場現象，而且在世界越來越普及。據我們所知，這研究是第一個調查這行業的。這份報告提出了四項研究去支持我們的論點，包括真實的市場數據和實驗性質的調查。

12522916.label: Realisation of objectives
12522916.value: Imagine that someone asks you for financial help. Will your response change depending on whether the request is framed as “I want your help” versus “I need your help”? This paper posits that such will indeed be the case, arguing that even though the terms “want” and “need” are often used interchangeably, the two can invoke very different inferences. This premise lies at the heart of a theoretical framework developed and tested in this research, which systematically predicts when and why a “want” frame is superior to a “need” frame in terms of inducing compliance, and when the reverse is true. We examine our ideas in the context of a type of financial appeal that is of particular relevance given the current prevalence of digital media: crowdfunding. Referring to the use of online platforms to raise money, global crowdfunding experienced accelerated growth and reached $34.4 billion in 2015 (Crowdsourcing.org 2015); further, it is forecast to continue growing at a compound annual rate of 26.87% between 2016 to 2020 (Crowdfundbeat.com 2016). This is a phenomenon that is important to understand, therefore. In addition, the crowdfunding context is of theoretical interest because the two different types of appeals that are primarily used in this context can evoke very different psychological processes: reward-based appeals in which funders contribute in exchange for rewards promised by the fundraisers (e.g., finished products, shares, monetary rewards), and donation-based appeals in which no reward is promised; rather, fundraisers primarily rely on contributors’ generosity (Belleflamme and Lambert 2014; García and Estellés-Arolas 2015). Despite offering applied and theoretical value, crowdfunding as a subject of exploration has been neglected by consumer psychologists. The current work addresses this gap, examining how the two different message frames discussed above – a want vs. a need frame – may prove differentially efficacious for reward-based vs. donation-based appeals. Our conceptualization integrates insights from the literature on semantic framing (Cheema and Patrick 2008; Patrick and Hagtvedt 2012) with that on relationship types – in particular, the norms guiding exchange vs. communal relationships (Aggarwal 2004; Aggarwal and Zhang 2006). We propose that for reward-based appeals, it is more effective to frame the request for funds as a “want” rather than a “need”, because doing so increases perceptions of the requester’s competence – which is influential under exchange norms. In contrast, for donation-based appeals, framing the request in terms of a “need” rather than a “want” is more effective, because the former enhances perceptions of the request’s criticality – which is influential under communal norms. This research advances knowledge in several directions. First, and most fundamentally, it contributes to the semantic framing literature by showing how and why two commonly used words – “want” and “need” – can have very different connotations, with consequential implications in an appeal context. Second, this paper is one of the first to introduce a consumer psychology perspective to the increasingly important domain of crowdfunding. Notably, our framework is able to offer integrated insights into both major types of crowdfunding: reward-based vs. donation-based campaigns. Third and relatedly, the obtained findings carry straightforward applied implications for those using crowdfunding to raise money; we show how a subtle difference in messaging can increase the effectiveness of either reward-based or donation-based appeals. In so doing, we also contribute to the broader literature on financial appeals (e.g., Duclos and Barasch 2014; Kristofferson, White, and Peloza 2014) by examining how a hitherto-unstudied factor – message frame – can influence appeal compliance. Finally, in grounding our theoretical conceptualization in the research on exchange vs. communal relationships, this investigation builds a conceptual bridge between two important literatures that had hitherto been mutually isolated: semantic framing and relationship norms.

12522916.label: Major findings and research outcome
12522916.value: This research uses a crowdfunding context to examine whether a simple difference in frame – using “want” vs. “need” in the request – can affect funders’ compliance with an appeal, and why exactly such a difference might be obtained. Our conceptualization integrates insights from two different literatures – semantic framing, and relationship norms – to propose that frame type will exert diametrically opposing effects for the two major forms of crowdfunding appeals: wants will elicit greater funder compliance than needs for a reward-based project, while needs will be more effective than wants for a donation-based project. Results from a field-based pilot study and four controlled experiments provide support for these effects, across both an organizational-based cause (funds being sought for a new technical product) and a personal cause (funds being sought to get into culinary school). Furthermore, findings across our studies provide insight into the process underlying these findings. In particular, both a mediator-based approach (study 2) and a moderator-based approach (study 3) obtained evidence convergent with the posited mechanism: for a reward-based appeal, the use of a want (vs. need) frame enhances perceptions of the fundraiser’s competence, and this increase in perceived competence drives contributors’ funding behavior. Conversely, for a donation-based appeal, the use of a need (vs. want) frame enhances perceptions of the request’s criticality, and perceived criticality then drives contributors’ funding behavior. Finally, study 4 takes a step back to examine the key underlying distinction between reward vs. donation appeals that yields these different effects. Results from this study were consistent with the premise that the relevant distinction has to do with reward (donation) appeals being rooted in the norms of an exchange (communal) relationship. Collectively, our findings offer novel insights into how and why the subtle linguistic elements of “want” versus “need” claims influence compliance with funding requests.

12522916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12522916.value: A promising line of inquiry would be to delve deeper into the two key mediators of funding behavior described here: perceived competence of the requester and perceived criticality of the request. For example, our proposition that perceived competence drives funding of reward-based appeals is particularly intuitive when the reward is contingent on the successful completion of the project for which funds are being requested – as was the case in all of the reward-based appeals studied here, and is indeed very often the case in reward-based crowdfunding (Giudici et al. 2012). Yet the implications of perceived competence might be even more far-reaching. Even when the reward promised in a crowdfunding project has nothing to do with project completion (e.g., one of the rewards promised in a Kickstarter project for a documentary movie was: “for every pledge of 250 USD or more, swag bag with south India cookbook”) perceived competence is likely to be important, for the simple reason that any form of reward requires the fundraiser to possess resources, and the possession of material/financial resources is itself used as a common heuristic for competence (Cuddy et al. 2007).

12605316.label: Project Objectives
12605316.value: To provide empirical instances to reveal how different groups of urban residents conceive, articulate and work for rights to urban space that they believe, or claim, they or other have, and to reveal the consequences for social justice. 12605316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12605316.value: This research will seek to advance the investigation of ‘right to the city’ in urban China. There is a growing interest to engage Lefebvre’s (1996) idea of ‘right to the city’ in urban China but existing works are concentrated on the identification of ‘whose’ right needs to be protected. A deep engagement which including discussions on the nature of rights and justice in Chinese cities and its relationship with urban politics has yet to be found. Nevertheless, given the sharp differences between China and liberal democratic societies and the profound meaning of the idea, adapting the idea to China needs to be done with care. It is the objective of this research to develop a Chinese version of rights to the city. Focusing on the everyday lives of urban residents, this research aims to provide on-the-ground evidence to demonstrate: (a) the various ways in which urban residents conceive their rights; (b) how their conception is translated into real actions; and (c) the spatial dimension of their conception and actions. Through these issues, at the theoretical level, this research seeks to address how is Lefebvre’s ‘right to the city’ relevant to China. The investigation of how different social groups conceive their rights to the city will take place in Guangzhou city. Different neighbourhoods inhabited by native villagers, migrant workers, professional migrants and local urban residents (both as homeowners and tenants) and involved in any form of space contest will be investigated. These target groups will be the primary unit for analysis and their neighbourhoods, including villages-in-the-city, urban quarters and gated communities, will constitute the major research sites. A case study approach will be used to examine the way that different target groups conceive right in contested urban spaces. Key platers involved in the contest of spaces will be identified and their relationships and negotiations with the target groups will be examined. Ethnographic methods, such as participant observation and semi-structured interviews will be employed to collect detailed first-hand information. 這個研究的目的是促進城市權(rights to the city)這個概念在中國的 討論。由Lefebvre所提出的城市研究框架和相關的概念在過去的二 十年掀起了廣泛的討論。他對城市權的論述，分析和主張亦引起 了不少西方與非西方城市研究學者的討論和興趣。然而現有的研究 大多集中於去介定誰人/社群的權利需要受到保護，對於城市權的 本質及其在不同地方的意義，以至與城市政治的關係則較少論及。 就城市權在中國的討論來說，城市權所包含的政治含意以及西方 自由社會與中國社會的區別，使學者們在應用此概念去討論城市 問題時需要特別小心。這個研究的目的就是要建構一個合乎中 國情況的城市權的討論。本研究聚焦於城市居民的日常生活， 目標是收集實際證據去展示： 1 城市居民如何理解及建構他們認為是合理的城市權利； 2 他們如何把上述的認知轉化為行動；以及 3 上述理解認知和行動的空間性。 透過以上問題，本研究除了在理論層面上探討Lefebvre的城市權 在中國的相關性外，更會嘗試建構一套符合中國情況的城市權討 論。

12605316.label: Realisation of objectives
12605316.value: The project has completed, with most of the objectives being met. In fact, this research has encountered a few unexpected problems during the long process of field investigation. This was because local authorities in the selected fieldsites appeared strengthening their control over the social space. As some of the inquiries were related to redevelopment, displacement, compensation and pursuing of rights, people were reluctant to disclose sensitive information, their actions and to discuss their views with the researcher. Among the three lines of inquiry that set up in this research, the first line was largely achieved. About 70 percent of the planned field study and interview were completed. Three different neighbourhoods were picked for a detailed investigation. They included two villages-in-the-city and one urban neighbourhood commonly known as ‘gate community’. Fifty-seven in-depth interviews were conducted. Among the 50 interviews conducted in two villages-in-the-city, I was able to talk to two ‘nail households’ (ding zi hu) and listen to their views on neighbourhood redevelopment, the reason for their resistance, their strategy for negotiation and their actions. This information is useful to interpret their perception on rights to the city. A major fault of the empirical research was the leaving of a co-investigator. As a result, the plan to investigate migrant workers’ perception on rights and social justice was interrupted and hence underachieved. Although efforts were spent to compensate, they were not successful at all. Finally, only two interviews were conducted. This is the biggest defect in this research; and led to the under-achievement of the first objective. Despite the under-achievement of empirical research, information collected from the field is able to help the researchers to achieve the second research objective. Many efforts have been spent on analysing and interpreting the views and narratives of interviewees. While the empirical findings show a picture varied from those portraited in existing literature, extra efforts have to be spent to understand the significance of such result in both empirical and theoretical terms. The contrasting views collected through interviewing different groups of dweller in Chinese cities are indeed inspiring. They have provided rich materials to help the research team to compare and to reflect on Lefebvre’s notion of right to the city. Regarding literature on Lefebvre's urban vision, this project allows the PI to update the on-going discussions on Lefebvre’s scholarship on the 'production of space', 'right to the city' and 'everyday life'. While more and more of his works are published and debated in the English-speaking world, such an update is crucial to attain the third research objective – to investigate the relevancy of Lefebvre’s ‘right to the city’ to China.

12605316.label: Major findings and research outcome
12605316.value: Major findings of this research include: Urban redevelopment in general and villages-in-the-city redevelopment in particular is not considered as a pernicious process as the critical scholarship has suggested. In fact, many affected resident perceived villages-in-the-city redevelopment as an excellent opportunity to improve their livelihood and social status and to have better future in an urban economy. As a result, their views on what they believe is rights and how they work for it are very different from those presented by the narratives provided by the critical scholarship. For residents in villages-in-the-city, rights of urban space means maintaining their status quo. This includes living in their existing neighbourhood, entitlement of collective-owned space for rental activities and enjoying rental income. This status quo is good enough to make them a de facto property class in cities with a decent, middle class level, income. To some young residents, rights of urban space means their right to benefit from neighbourhood redevelopment. They employ different strategies to negotiate with the authority for better terms of compensation. They strongly believe their loss (of houses) should be compensated probably. The way that they perceive rights has demonstrated a strong sense of redistributive justice. For migrant workers in Guangzhou, rights of urban space means job opportunities in cities more than affordable housing. They do concern about displacement, raise of rent and loss of cheap accommodations but these are not the most pressing issue for them. They are optimistic about the opportunities that they have in cities and they do not have resentment towards diverging income and lifestyle in cities. The way that urban dwellers perceive as rights in Chinese cities suggest a noncritical view on social justice. This form of thought is socially produced in the context of China’s progressive, state-led, economic growth. Social justice, therefore, requires a contextual interpretation. This variation does not suggest that Lefebvre’s vision of ‘right to the city’ are not relevant to China. If Lefebvre’s vision is to inspire people to think about the future of their city, questioning the status quo of the existing urban, then his challenges are relevant, not only to China, but also to all urban residents in different cities around the world. It is an envisioning process, allowing people to discuss and explore ways to change where they live.

12605316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12605316.value: This research has spanned across geography, sociology and political science. Such a scope shows potential for interdisciplinary collaborations with sociologists, political scientists and researchers who are interested in China’s societal changes. The missing of migrant workers in this research has left a gap for further investigation. Indeed, the investigation of migrant workers’ rights to the city has great potential to develop into an stand-alone research project. Another area for potential elaboration is the empirical investigation on right to the city. This point echoes the argument on ‘contextual interpretation’ of social justice in different places. The spatial variation would provide useful insight to explore the relevancy of Lefebvre’s vision on urban change in localities with different cultural background and different level of economic development. This would further shed light on the discussion of spatial justice.

12605316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12605316.value: This research has moved beyond convention discussions on justice, which based on normative principles and justice norms, and investigates ‘right to the city’ and social justice from a bottom-up manner. It investigates rights in Chinese cities on the ground through exploring different groups of urban dweller's form of thought and practices in the context of the country’s state-led redevelopment. Through this approach, this research has revealed different group of urban dwellers’ view on (a) what is perceived as rights and (b) how did they pursue these rights. This research reveals that urban dwellers possess a noncritical view on social justice. They aware urban inequality, displacement and lack of cheap housing in the city but they are not their prime concern. Their positive view is demonstrated by what they consider as rights. This includes rights to maintain their status quo, rights benefits from redevelopment and rights to urban job opportunities. Such perceptions vary from Lefebvre’s vision on ‘right to the city’ and the argument that presented by critical scholarship on social justice. This variation suggests (a) in theoretical sense, right to the city and social justice requires a contextual interpretation; (b) Lefebvre’s vision of ‘right to the city’ are not irrelevant to China. If Lefebvre’s vision is to inspire people to think about the future of their city, questioning the status quo of the existing urban, then his challenges are relevant, not only to China, but also to all urban residents in different cities around the world.

12620916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12620916.value: In tackling the issues arising from ageing population, the Hong Kong Government initiates age-friendly environment to promote active ageing. Older adults, however, is inactive in HK. Among different types of physical activity (PA), walking is easier to promote in older adults because it is safe, accessible, and easy to incorporate with daily routine (Yang, Sahlqvist, McMinn, Griffin, & Ogilvie, 2010). A substantial literature has been developed on the linkage between physical environment and walking (Cerin et al., 2013). However, research that links social environment to PA orwalking is sparse. Increasing but still few studies suggest that social environment is critical to disentangle the causal mechanism between physical/social environment and walking. Limitations were identified in the existing studies (Clark & Scott, 2013; Van Cauwenberg et al., 2011). They were i) conducted in low-density urbanized western countries; ii) relied on solely objective or subjective measurements of physical environment and walking; iii) moderators or mediators were seldom studied; iv) few research was done in older population; and v) small sample size of studies in social environment – PA associations. In 2015, the investigators of this proposal received funding from Public Policy Research (PPR) Fund on a project “Impacts of the Residential Physical and Social Environment on Daily Walking Behavior of Older Adults in Hong Kong” (See Appendix 2). This PPR project is a multilevel study with aims to examine a) the associations between walking, and physical and social environments among older adults in Hong Kong; and b) how genders moderate these environment-walking associations. Owing to the funding nature, this PPR project is a one-year cross-sectional study, which does not support for causality of results. Hence, the research team proposes this GRF project to extend the work of PPR project with aims to examine 1) the change of associations between physical environment, social environment and walking among older adults in a 3-year time period; and 2) the change of associations in relation to different socioeconomic statuses. Such longitudinal study could further demonstrate cause-effect relationships and lay the groundwork for developing future intervention. The data of the existing PPR project (2015-2016) will be used as baseline data for this proposed GRF project (2016-2018). The older adults recruited in the PPR project will be used for the 2nd/ 3rd measures in this GRF project. Multilevel longitudinal structural equation modeling (SEM) and multiple-group SEM will be conducted to answer questions 1 and 2 as mentioned above, respectively. 為了解決人口老化帶來的問題，香港政府開創高齡友善的環境去推動積極樂頤年的觀念。但是，香港的長者不活躍。在各種不同的體能活動中，步行是較容易向長者推廣的運動，因為步行相對較安全、方便以及較容易融入日常生活 (Yang, Sahlqvist, McMinn, Griffin, & Ogilvie, 2010)。 雖然現時有大量文獻記載着建成環境和步行之間的關係 (Cerin et al., 2013)，但將社會環境聯繫到體能活動或步行的研究不多。能夠指出社會環境是解開建成/社會環境與步行之間的因果機制重要一環的研究雖然有所增加，但依然只屬少數，再者我們發現現有的文獻當中有以下不足之處 (Clark & Scott, 2013; Van Cauwenberg et al., 2011)：1）研究是在一些低密度城市化的西方國家進行; 2）研究純粹依靠客觀或主觀的建成環境或步行測量方法; 3）很少着眼研究有關的中介/調節變數; 4）較少利用長者作為研究對像; 5）研究社會環境與體能活動關係的樣本數量少。在2015年，我們得到公眾政策研究基金的資助，题為「居住的建成和社會環境對香港長者日常步行表現的影響」(見附件2)，該資助項目是一個多層次的研究，目的在考究建成及社交環境跟香港長者步行的關係，亦查考性別如何調節以上關係。 基於資助的性質，這個公眾政策研究項目是一個為期一年、橫斷面的研究，並不能反映結果的因果性。因此，我們提交GRF提案去延續這個公眾政策研究的項目，目的在於：一）考究建成及社交環境跟香港長者步行在三年期間的關係；及二) 其與不同的社會經濟狀況之間關係的改變。這縱向性研究有助證明其因果關係，並為未來的干預計劃建立基礎。公眾政策研究項目（2015-2016）現有的數據將會用作GRF提案（2016-2018）的基本資料。參與公眾政策研究的長者將再次被邀請參與這GRF項目的第二及第三階段評估。多層次的縱向的結構方程模型和多組結構方程模型將用以解答上述提及的問題一/二。

12620916.label: Realisation of objectives
12620916.value: Objective 1 was achieved. The change of associations between physical environment, social environment and walking among older adults in HK in a 3-year time period (Time1 (2016), Time 2 (2017), and Time 3 (2018)) was examined among 1067 older adults using multilevel structural equation modeling (in individual level and neighborhood level). After data management, there were 483 and 796 adults of objective walking (Step per day) and subjective walking (total walking time in a week), respectively, as outcome variables included in the final data analysis. In neighborhood level, longitudinal structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to assess the associations among the dependent variables (i.e., step per day and total walking time in a week) and associated constructs [i.e. Social environment (i.e., perceived social cohesion) and objective environment from Geographical Information System (i.e., connectivity, density and land use mix)] in a 3-year time period. Results showed that there was no evidence to support directional pathway leading from social environment (i.e., perceived social cohesion) and objective environments (i.e., connectivity, density and land use mix) to older adult’s total walking time in a week (subjective walking) in Time 2 or Time 3. On the contrary, social environment (i.e., perceived social cohesion) and objective environment significantly predicted step per day (objective walking) among older adults in Time 2 and Time3. In individual level, same data analysis was used to assess the associations among the same dependent variables and another set of associated constructs [i.e. Social environment (i.e., Companionship, Encouragement, and Role model) and subjective environment (i.e., physical environment facilitators and physical environment barriers)] in a 3-year time period. Social environment (i.e., Companionship, Encouragement, and Role model) and physical environment barriers predicted older adult’s total walking time in a week (subjective walking) in Time 2 or Time 3. In objective walking measurement (i.e., step per day), all of studied constructs, social environment (i.e., Companionship, Encouragement, and Role model) and subjective environment (i.e., physical environment facilitators and physical environment barriers) were significant predictors of step per day among older adults in Time 2 and Time 3. The significant predictors to walking found in this study is similar to results of previous cross-sectional studies, such as objective environment including connectivity, density and land use mix (Barnett, Barnett, Nathan, Van Cauwenberg, & Cerin, 2017), social environment (Ory, Towne, Won, Forjuoh, & Lee, 2016) and physical environment facilitators (Leung, Chung, Wang, & Liu, 2018). Importantly, a causality of these predictors in 3-year time was established through this longitudinal study. In fact, our findings are similar to that of Kikuchi et al. (2018), which is one of the few longitudinal studies conducted in this area. Kikuchi and colleagues found that objective environment mitigated the 5-year reduction of walking among Japanese older adults. It is worth to note that in individual level, physical environment barriers were positively associated with subjective and objective walking in Time 2 and Time 3. In fact, previous studies on such association were in mixed results. Dawson, Hillsdon, Boller and Foster (2007) found that older adults who cited at least one environmental barrier to walking exhibited significantly less walking in the preceding week than those who cited none. Cerin and colleagues (2013) conducted study in Hong Kong and found no significant associations between physical environment barriers (i.e., crowdedness, traffic hazards, speed, social disorder, and crime) and walking in older adults. In a meta-analysis, Cerin and colleagues (2017) revealed that non-associations with active travel was found for most variables measuring neighbourhood cleanliness/order, traffic and crime. Physical environment barriers such as littering, vandalism, and decay were weakly and negatively associated while “human or motorized traffic volume” was positively associated with older adult’s total walking. Possible reason of our findings may be related to participants’ characteristics. Since most of the participants are from lower family income group, they then to have less option to travel with no or low cost that walking is necessary for all purposes, no matter the presence of physical environment barriers. Specifically, Hong Kong is a high density city; older adults seem to have difficulty to walking in such crowded and high traffic volume environment. Additionally, this finding was in line with the aforementioned meta-analysis study (Cerin et al., 2017) that higher human and motorized traffic volumes such traffic hazards, crowdedness and speed enhanced walking due to destination-rich, walkable areas that attracted by a large number of people. Also, surprisingly, contrary to previous cross-sectional findings (Cerin et al., 2017), we found that older adults who perceived higher neighborhood social cohesion were less likely to report higher objective walking at the follow-up assessment. A recently longitudinal study (Mertens et al., 2019) also found this contradictory result. From which the researchers explained that neighborhoods with high social cohesion were more likely to be areas located further away from the city center, making destinations too far to walk to. Objective 2 was achieved. In order to examine the change of associations in relation to different socioeconomic statuses (i.e., education, income, and types of housing), multiple group structural equation modeling was used. Results found that all of our proposed moderators [i.e., education (higher and lower education), income (higher and lower family income), and types of housing (own or rent)] were not significant moderators in the change of associations between physical environment, social environment and walking among the older adults in a 3-year time period, regardless of neighborhood and individual level of our study. In fact, regarding the insignificant income group differences, there might be due to the uneven distribution of income groups in our sample. About 80% of our sample had monthly family income HK$9999 or below. Other than sample characteristics, the insignificant results of our multiple group SEM might also relate to our outcome variables, “step per day” and “total walking time in a week”. Both of these outcome variables assessed total walking, regardless their walking purposes (e.g., transportation or recreation). Two studies (Inoue et al., 2011; Van Cauwenberg et al., 2012) found moderators on the association of physical environment in specific walking behaviors such as walking for transportation and recreation in the older adults. Perhaps in our study, moderator differences on the associations might be identified if more specific walking behaviors (i.e., for transportation and recreation) could be used for the analysis. Practically, these findings inform government that environment enhancement in walking can be conducted in regardless of the differences in education, income and type of housing of the older adults. Similarly, related practitioners may develop universal walking intervention to older adults in different socioeconomic statuses in Hong Kong.

12620916.label: Major findings and research outcome
12620916.value: In neighborhood level, there was no evidence to support directional pathway leading from social environment (i.e., perceived social cohesion) and objective environments (i.e., connectivity, density and land use mix) to older adult’s total walking time in a week (subjective walking) in Time 2 or Time 3. On the contrary, social environment (i.e., perceived social cohesion) and objective environments significantly predicted step per day (objective walking) among older adults in Time 2 and Time3. Specifically, older adults who lower neighborhood social cohesion were more likely to report higher objective walking (i.e., step per day) at Time 3 but not Time 2. Next, older adults perceiving more walkable objective physical environments (i.e., higher residential density, Land use mixed, and street connectivity) were more likely to report higher objective walking (i.e., step per day) at all the follow-up assessments (Time 2 and Time 3). In individual level, social environment (i.e., companionship, encouragement, and role model) and physical environment barriers predicted older adult’s total walking time in a week (subjective walking) in Time 2 and Time 3.Older adults who perceived better social environments (i.e., higher perceived companionship, encouragement, and role model) and reported higher perceived physical environment barriers (i.e., Crowdedness, Traffic hazards, speed, social disorder, and crime) tended to reported higher objective walking (i.e., step per day) at all the follow-up assessments. In our objective walking measurement (i.e., step per day), all of our studied constructs, social environment (i.e., companionship, encouragement, and role model) and subjective environment (i.e., physical environment facilitators and physical environment barriers) were significant predictors of step per day among older adults from Time 1 and Time 2, from Time 1 to Time 3, and from Time 2 to Time 3. In general, older adults who perceived higher social environments (i.e., higher perceived companionship, encouragement, and role model), perceived higher physical environment facilitators (i.e., higher perceived land use mix, higher accessibility to services, higher street connectivity, more walking infrastructure, more indoor facilities for walking, felt safer, easier access of residential entrance), and reported more physical environment barriers (i.e., more crowdedness, more traffic hazards, higher traffic speed, higher social disorder, and more crime) were more likely to report higher objective walking (i.e., step per day) at all the follow-up assessments. At last, education, income and type of housing did not moderate the above associations in this study.

12620916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12620916.value: To extend our existing work, future studies may consider: 1. Examine the change of associations between physical environment, social environment and walking in different purposes (such as recreation or transportation); 2. Study the moderators that may alter the agreement of perceived and objective physical environment. The possible moderators include older adult’s mobility, familiarity of destinations and routes, length of residency or other demographic characteristics; 3. Study the mediation effect of perceived environments between objective environments and walking among older adults; 4. Conduct qualitative study to examine the facilitators and barriers of walking among older adults in Hong Kong. A more in-depth experience shared by the older adults may help develop intervention strategies and programs for promotions of walking and active ageing. 5. Include self-selection, the process by which households choose their residential location based on their desired and expected travel behavior (Cao, 2015) into future study.

12620916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12620916.value: Hong Kong Government initiates age-friendly environment to promote active ageing such as walking. Based on the results, we found that in neighborhood level, no association between social environment and objective environments and the older adult’s total walking time in a week (subjective walking) in all follow-up measurements. On the contrary, perceived social cohesion and objective environments (i.e., residential density, land use mixed, and street connectivity) significantly predicted step per day (objective walking) among older adults. In individual level, social environment (i.e., companionship, encouragement, and role model) and physical environment barriers predicted older adult’s total walking time in a week (subjective walking) in Time 2 (2017) or Time 3 (2018). In our objective walking measurement (i.e., step per day), all of our studied constructs, social environment (i.e., companionship, encouragement, and role model) and subjective environment (i.e., physical environment facilitators and physical environment barriers) were significant predictors of step per day among older adults in Time 2 and Time 3. Additionally, education, income and type of housing did not moderate the above associations in this study. In future, walking intervention programs and environmental enhancement strategies could be developed to promote active ageing in Hong Kong.
