14107216.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107216.value: Objective 1. Identify subjects with NPC from our NPC screening population who are at risk of disease because of persistently elevated plasma EBV DNA, but do not have a diagnosis of NPC after the initial investigations and use this data to determine whether follow-up MRI has a role in the management of this group of subjects. 1. Subjects with persistently raised plasma EBV-DNA on at least three occasions and an MRI graded as intermediate index of suspicion (grade 3) or high index of suspicion (grade 4) are at risk of harbouring an undiagnosed NPC. 2. These early-stage NPCs are slow growing tumours and may take up to three years before they are visible endoscopically. 3. Follow-up MRI also detects other head and neck cancers which are outside the nasopharynx. These findings are published in Annals of Oncology (King AD et al. Annals of Oncology, 2019). Objective 2. Improve the diagnostic performance of MRI for distinguishing inflammation/hypertrophy from small NPCs. 1. Using the functional MRI sequence DWI, compared to benign hyperplasia, NPC showed significantly lower D (pure diffusion coefficient) and ADC (apparent diffusion coefficient) and significantly higher D* (pseudo-diffusion coefficient). 2. D showed the highest area under the curve (0.985) with a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 93.3% and accuracy of 96.9% for discriminating these two entities. These findings are published in European Radiology (Ai QY et al. European Radiology, 2019). Objective 3. Provide preliminary data for determining whether there is any potential link between EBV infection and patterns of inflammation/hypertrophy in the nasopharynx on MRI. 1. Positive plasma EBV-DNA and smoking were independent predictors of the presence of benign hyperplasia on MRI. 2. Younger age and smoking, but not plasma EBV-DNA level, were associated with the larger volume of benign hyperplasia. 3. After two years, subjects with static or progressive benign hyperplasia were more likely to have a plasma EBV-DNA that remained positive while those with resolution or regression of benign hyperplasia were more likely to have an EBV-DNA that became negative. Summary of research outcome 1. Subjects with elevated plasma EBV-DNA on at least three occasions without a biopsy-proven diagnosis of NPC after the initial set of investigations are still at risk of harbouring NPC or other head and neck cancers. Follow-up of at least three years is required for small early-stage NPCs to become endoscopically visible. Surveillance MRI (plain scan) should be performed in subjects with a grade 4 MRI if the abnormality is not accessible to biopsy and considered for those with a grade 3 MRI. 2. Diffusion weighted imaging (DWI) has the potential to improve the discrimination of benign hyperplasia and early-stage NPC. This functional MRI sequence has the advantage that it does not require an intravenous injection of contrast, which would be valuable when using MRI in screening programs. 3. The cause of inflammation/hyperplasia in the nasopharynx is likely to be multifactorial, but these preliminary results suggest that infection with the EBV could be a contributing factor. Our observation that subjects with long-term persistence of benign hyperplasia on MRI are more likely to have a persistently positive plasma EBV-DNA is an interesting area for future MRI research, which could lead to identification of MRI markers to predict risk and identify precursors of NPC.

14107216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107216.value: 1. MRI guidelines for early detection of NPC We are undertaking a study to improve the diagnostic performance of MRI in a plasma EBV-DNA screening setting by modifying the MRI grading system to improve the discrimination of benign hyperplasia and early-stage NPC. We also will propose a second grading system for use with a screening MRI that does not require intravenous contrast. 2. IVIM to discriminate between benign and malignant nodes from NPC Retropharyngeal nodes were also covered on our IVIM sequence of the primary tumour. Therefore we plan to perform the study which compares IVIM of benign and malignant nodes. 3. Long-term follow-up for the subjects in this study with persistently elevated EBV-DNA We have identified subjects with a persistently raised plasma EBV-DNA who harbored undiagnosed early cancer at the time of the initial investigations. However, we believe that persistently raised levels of plasma EBV DNA could be an indicator of risk of developing NPC in the future so we plan to continue MRI surveillance and perform follow-up study at a minimum of 5 years.

14107216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107216.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) often presents only after invading the skull base, brain or neck. This study continues our previous research using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to detect cancers at an earlier stage. We performed follow-up MRI after two years in subjects from an NPC population screening program who had raised plasma markers for NPC (EBV-DNA) on at least three occasions but no diagnosis of NPC. Head and neck cancers were identified in 5% of subjects at follow-up, four NPCs and two cancers outside the nasopharynx. Nasopharyngeal MRI of the four NPCs were graded as intermediate/high risk on the initial MRI and we observed these slow-growing early-stage cancers took up to three years to become endoscopically visible. Therefore, in selected cases follow-up MRI has a role in detection of early-stage NPC. We found DWI could discriminate benign inflammation/hyperplasia from early-stage NPC and so this MRI sequence, that does not require an intravenous injection, could be valuable in future screening programs. The cause of nasopharyngeal inflammation/hyperplasia on MRI is likely to be multifactorial, but our observations suggest EBV infection could be a contributing factor. This is an area for future research into MRI markers that predict risk or identify precursors of NPC.

14107516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107516.value: Glaucoma, a major cause of irreversible blindness in the world, is a progressive optic neuropathy characterized by gradual degeneration of retinal ganglion cells. Normal tension glaucoma (NTG) is a major subtype of glaucoma in Asian populations. Yet, the underlying pathogenic mechanisms of NTG are not well understood. At present, intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction remains the only proven treatment to stop or slow disease progression in NTG. However, a proportion of NTG patients continue to deteriorate even after maximum IOP reduction. Circulatory insufficiency is proposed to be one of the key non-IOP-dependent mechanisms leading to glaucomatous progression, and is likely to play a more important role in NTG where high IOP is absent. In this study, we propose to conduct a prospective cohort study on 500 NTG patients and 100 age-matched normal controls to identify new retinal vascular imaging markers that are associated with NTG and NTG progression. Digital retinal photography and optical coherence tomography-angiography (OCT-A) are now available to allow quantitative evaluation of the retinal vasculature. Changes in retinal vasculature (e.g. retinal arteriolar narrowing, decreased retinal vascular fractal dimension) and capillary network (e.g. capillary dropout, decreased vessel density) can be quantified to characterize the integrity of the microvasculature and circulatory insufficiency in retina. This study has 3 specific objectives: (1) To determine the associations of quantitative retinal vascular parameters from fundus photography and OCT-angiography with NTG by a cross-sectional study in an NTG cohort and normal controls; (2) To examine the relationship of these retinal vascular parameters with different disease severity in NTG patients; and (3) To examine prospectively the associations of baseline retinal vascular parameters with disease progression in NTG over 3 years. In this study, we will perform retinal vascular imaging on all recruited NTG patients and normal controls at recruitment, and then 6-monthly retinal vascular imaging, visual field testing, and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness measurements in NTG patients longitudinally for 2 years. The identification of anatomical vascular risk factors for NTG will lead to a better understanding of NTG pathogenesis, and will have important prognostic value and implications for treatment. Changes in retinal vasculature shown to be associated with NTG and NTG progression in this study will allow us to identify those patients who may benefit from more aggressive treatments. Future NTG treatments should target retinal vascular changes and ischaemic processes identified by this study, in addition to the current IOP-lowering approach. 青光眼是當今世界上導致不可逆的失明的主要原因之一。它是一種逐漸惡化的視神經病變，以視網膜神經節細胞退化為主要特征。其中，正常眼壓青光眼（Normal Tension Glaucoma）是亞洲人群青光眼的主要亞型。正常眼壓青光眼的基本致病機制尚未清楚，降低眼內壓以阻止或延緩疾病的進展仍然是唯一有效的治療方法。然而,在部分正常眼壓青光眼患者中，最大限度降低眼內壓並不能阻止該疾病的惡化。研究顯示血管循環功能是導致青光眼逐漸惡化的其中一個非眼壓依賴關鍵機制之一，並且很可能在正常眼壓青光眼中起到更加重要的作用。 在這項研究中，我們將募集500名正常眼壓青光眼患者和100名沒有正常眼壓青光眼並年齡匹配的志願者(對照群組）進行前瞻性研究，以鑒定正常眼壓青光眼和正常眼壓青光眼發展相關的新視網膜血管影像標記。現在，數碼眼底照相和光學相干斷層掃描血管造影術可以對視網膜血管進行定量評估。視網膜血管變化（例如，視網膜小動脈狹窄，視網膜血管分形維數減少）和毛細血管網絡改變（例如毛細管損壞，血管密度減少）的量化可以表徵視網膜微血管循環功能的完整性。 這項研究有3個具體目標： (1) 通過在正常眼壓青光眼患者組和正常對照群組之間作橫斷面分析，確定由眼底照與光學相干斷層掃描血管造影獲取的定量視網膜血管參數與正常眼壓青光眼之間的關聯; (2) 探究上述視網膜血管參數與正常眼壓青光眼嚴重程度的關係。 (3) 研究視網膜血管參數與正常眼壓青光眼在3年病情進展程度的前瞻性關聯。 在這項研究中，我們將對所有招募的正常眼壓青光眼患者和正常對照行視網膜血管成像造影，然後每6個月對正常眼壓青光眼患者行視網膜血管成像造影，視野檢查和視網膜神經纖維層厚度測量，為期2年。 正常眼壓青光眼解剖學血管危險因素的識別能更好地闡明正常眼壓青光眼的發病機制，並且對疾病的治療和預後有著重要價值。本研究揭示的視網膜血管改變與正常眼壓青光眼及其進展的關聯將使我們能夠確定積極治療的獲益者。未來正常眼壓青光眼的治療，除降低眼壓外，更應針對本研究所發現的視網膜血管的結構性與功能性改變。

14107516.label: Realisation of objectives
14107516.value: We have successfully achieved the project objectives with the support from GRF. 1. Objective #1 and Objective #2: To determine the associations of quantitative anatomical retinal vascular parameters from fundus photography and OCT-angiography, and to examine the cross-sectional relationship of retinal vascular parameters from fundus photography and OCT-angiography with different disease severity in NTG patients Under these two objectives, we aimed to offer a comprehensive global assessment of microvascular changes (arteriolar, venular and capillary) in NTG, and the associations between such vascular changes with disease severity (i.e. glaucoma-related structural and functional changes) in NTG. Furthermore, we aimed to compare the relative associations of arteriolar and venular changes with capillary changes in NTG eyes with the underlying structural and functional changes. Our results revealed generalized attenuations in both photographic arteriolar and venular metrics (straighter arterioles and venules) and OCT-A capillary metrics (decreased vessel density and fractal dimension) were associated with NTG and the structural (average retinal nerve fibre layer (RNFL) thickness) and functional (standard automated perimetry (SAP)) glaucomatous measurements. We further demonstrated that OCT-A capillary metrics have stronger associations with NTG than that of photographic metrics. Although current evidence is insufficient to indicate a direct causal relationship between capillary vasculature atrophy and RGC degeneration, degeneration in capillary vasculature is theoretically an ideal surrogate marker of vascular dysfunction, RGC degeneration and glaucoma. Our findings in this study with NTG patients lend support to such hypothesis by demonstrating the strong and consistent associations of NTG and the underlying glaucomatous changes with OCT-A capillary metrics. OCT-A capillary metrics may therefore be of utility in future studies of NTG vasculature and can potentially be assimilated into the standard of care to aid diagnosis and monitoring of NTG progression given their strong associations. 2. Objective #3: To examine prospectively the associations of baseline retinal vascular parameters from fundus photography and OCT-angiography with disease progression in NTG over 2 years Three hundred and ninety eyes of 197 NTG patients were followed up for at least 24 months. We found that baseline lower temporal circumpapillary vessel density (cpVD) and superotemporal cpVD were associated with visual field (VF) deterioration after adjusting for age, gender, blood pressure, untreated intraocular pressure, VF mean deviation, retinal nerve fiber layer thickness, axial length, and OCTA image quality score. We also found that narrower baseline photographic retinal arteriolar caliber and retinal venular caliber were associated with progressive RNFL thinning, and narrower baseline retinal arteriolar caliber was associated with VF deterioration, after controlling for age, gender, mean ocular perfusion pressure, axial length, standard automated perimetry mean deviation and baseline RNFL thickness. These findings revealed that baseline assessment of retinal vascular parameters from OCT-angiography fundus photography provides significant prognostic information to the evaluation of the risk of NTG progression. In the past, studies on retinal vasculature and glaucoma were of largely cross-sectional design, hence unable to ascertain the temporal and causal relationships between degeneration in retinal vasculature and glaucoma development. Findings from our longitudinal study provided novel and additional evidence on the elucidation of the vascular theory in glaucoma development by demonstrating that alternations in retinal vasculature herald the advent of glaucoma progression in NTG. Ischaemia in the eye can deprive RGC of growth factors and liberate a multitude of molecules including oxygen free radicals, nitric oxide, glutamate and intracellular calcium which serve as initiating signals of apoptosis to result in RGC loss. Narrowed retinal vessels and lower vessel density likely reflect a chronic state of optic nerve hypoperfusion and ischaemia, which potentially results in the terminal events of RGC death and glaucoma progression in NTG in the apparent absence of elevated IOP as postulated in the vascular theory. These findings may provide new insights about the vascular theory of glaucoma and support a prognostic role of retinal vasculature analysis in the clinical assessment of the risk of progression in NTG.

14107516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107516.value: Glaucoma, a major cause of irreversible blindness in the world, is a progressive optic neuropathy characterized by gradual degeneration of retinal ganglion cells. Normal tension glaucoma (NTG) is a major subtype of glaucoma in Asian populations. Yet, the exact underlying pathogenic mechanisms of NTG have not been well defined. Circulatory insufficiency is proposed to be one of the key non intraocular pressure (IOP) dependent mechanisms leading to disease progression. In this project, we used state-of-the-art retinal imaging techniques to assess retinal capillary network and retinal vasculature in a cohort of NTG. Specifically, radial peripapillary capillary network was imaged with optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) and quantitative capillary metrics (circumpapillary vessel density (cpVD) and circumpapillary fractal dimension (cpFD)) were measured with a customized MATLAB program. Moreover, quantitative retinal arteriolar and venular metrics were measured from retinal photographs using a computer-assisted program (SIVA program). In the cross-sectional analysis, we found that NTG was associated with decreased arteriolar and venular tortuosity, arteriolar branching angle, cpVD and cpFD. Decreased venular caliber, arteriolar and venular branching angles, cpVD and cpFD were associated with thinner average retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness. Decreased arteriolar and venular branching angles, cpVD and cpFD were also associated with worse standard automated perimetry measurements (mean deviation and visual field index). Compared with retinal arteriolar and venular metrics, regression models based on OCT-A capillary metrics consistently showed stronger associations with NTG and structural and functional measurements in NTG. We concluded that NTG eyes showed generalized microvascular attenuations, in which OCT-A capillary metrics attenuations were more prominent and strongly associated with NTG. In the longitudinal analysis, we found that lower temporal cpVD (hazard ratio [HR] per SD decrease, 1.481 95% CI 1.023 - 2.143) and superotemporal cpVD (HR per SD decrease, 1.616, 95% CI 1.106 - 2.359) measured from OCT-A were associated with VF deterioration after adjusting for age, gender, blood pressure, untreated IOP, VF mean deviation, RNFL thickness, axial length, and OCTA image quality score. We also found that narrower retinal arteriolar caliber (HR 1.36 [95% CI 1.05, 1.76]) and retinal venular caliber (HR 1.38 [1.03, 1.84]) measured from retinal photographs at baseline were independently associated with NTG progression in the multivariable model adjusted for baseline age, gender, mean ocular perfusion pressure, axial length, visual field mean deviation and RNFL thickness.

14107516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107516.value: Vascular insufficiency has been suggested to be of pathogenic role in NTG. We found that baseline attenuation of retinal capillary network and retinal vasculature conferred an increased risk of NTG progression, and these imaging based metrics improved predictive discrimination of NTG progression. Our findings offer new insights into the imaging-based metrics as a prognostic factor to be evaluated in risk assessment of NTG progression and the role of vascular factors in NTG pathogenesis.

14107516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107516.value: At present, intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction is the only proven treatment to stop or slow the progression of visual field defect in normal tension glaucoma (NTG), but a significant proportion of NTG patients continue to deteriorate even after maximum IOP reduction. In this study, we demonstrated that a series of imaging-based metrics, reflecting circulatory insufficiency, could be useful to identify who are at high risk for disease progression. The imaging-based metrics will also lead to a better understanding of NTG pathogenesis, and may have prognostic value and implications for treatment. Future NTG treatments may target retinal vascular changes and ischaemic processes, in addition to the current IOP-lowering approach.

14107616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107616.value: Parkinson’s disease is the second most common neurodegenerative diseases affecting millions of people worldwide and has been predicted to pose increasingly heavy burden on healthcare system in many regions. Loss of dopaminergic neurons in midbrain substantia nigra is believed to be the cause of motor disability in Parkinson’s disease. Currently there is no cure for Parkinson’s disease and only symptomatic treatments are available. Therefore, there is an urgent need to uncover the key pathogenic processes in Parkinson’s disease and develop disease-modifying treatment strategies that can slow down, stop or even reverse pathological progression of Parkinson’s disease. Iron accumulation is a hallmark in Parkinson’s disease, and believed to play a crucial role in the pathogenic process that leads to selective dopaminergic neuron degeneration. Iron-targeting treatment strategy, including iron chelation, by the iron-suppressing drugs that are currently available has been found beneficial in various Parkinson’s disease models but remain difficult for clinical application due to poor membrane permeability and lack of cell-type specificity. In a recent drug screening, we identified GSK-J4, previously regarded as a histone demethylase inhibitor, as the most potent cell-permeable drug that could suppress iron content at low dose and selectively in brain-related cells, providing hope to revolutionize iron-targeting treatment strategy. Together with our preliminary observation that GSK-J4 could reverse iron accumulation in Parkinson’s disease cell model, we therefore hypothesize that GSK-J4 is beneficial in Parkinson’s disease, possibly via epigenetic modification-induced iron suppression. In this proposal, based on the well-established mouse model of PD and the use of various transgenic mice, experiments are designed to investigate if GSK-J4 pre- and post-treatment is beneficial in models of Parkinson’s disease and to elucidate the detailed underlying mechanisms. 14107616.label: Realisation of objectives
14107616.value: The objectives of the present proposal have been fully realised. The major results have been published in a full article in an international peer-reviewed journal Cell Death & Disease (CDD), and some related results concerning the key role of iron regulation in manifestation and treatment of Parkinson's disease are reported in a paper in iScience, both are attached to this report. Objective 1. To confirm and characterize the therapeutic effect of GSK-J4 in experimental Parkinsonism We have conducted comprehensive experiments to confirm and characterise the therapeutic effect of GSK-J4 in experimental Parkinsonism, utilising both cell and animal models. The results have been fully described in the paper published in CDD and outlined in Section 6.1 Objective 2. To investigate if the beneficial effects of GSK-J4 are mediated by iron suppression and related mechanisms. We have investigated the mechanism underlying the beneficial effects of GSK-J4 in Parkinsonism, focusing on iron suppression. First, the role of iron accumulation and the effect of its manipulation had been studied and published in a paper in iScience, which is attached. Second, with respect to GSK-J4's action, we discovered that it's action is mainly mediated by inducing an increase in the expression of the iron exporter ferroportin-1, and accompanied by reduction of oxidative stress. Most importantly, GSK-J4 rescued the abnormal changes of histone methylation, H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 during 6-OHDA treatment. These results suggest that GSK-J4 upregulates H3K4me3-mediated ferroportin-1 expression. Therefore, a full and new mechanism is uncovered under this objective. The full results are reported in the CDD paper and outlined in Section 6.1

14107616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107616.value: In this project, we have completed the objectives of the proposal, namely to confirm and characterize the therapeutic effect of GSK-J4 in experimental Parkinsonism, to confirm that the beneficial effects of GSK-J4 are mediated by iron suppression and to elucidate related mechanisms. Our main results include: 1) we identified the histone demethylase inhibitor GSK-J4 with the ability to cross blood brain barrier as a potent iron suppressor. Only a trace amount of GSK-J4 significantly and selectively reduced intracellular labile iron in dopaminergic neurons; 2) GSK-J4 suppressed H2O2 and 6-OHDA-induced cell death in vitro. 3) The iron-suppressive effect of GSK-J4 was mainly mediated by inducing an increase in the expression of the iron exporter ferroportin-1. 4) In parallel, GSK-J4 rescued dopaminergic neuron loss and motor defects in 6-OHDA-induced PD rats; 5) This effect was accompanied by reduction of oxidative stress. 6) Importantly, GSK-J4 rescued the abnormal changes of histone methylation, H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 during 6-OHDA treatment although the iron-suppressive and neuroprotective effects were sensitive to H3K4me3 inhibition only. 7) Upregulating H3K4me3 increased ferroportin-1 expression and neuroprotection. Taken all the findings together, we demonstrated a previously unappreciated action of GSK-J4 on cell-specific iron suppression and neuroprotection via epigenetic mechanism.

14107616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107616.value: Compared with conventional iron chelators, GSK-J4 has a higher therapeutic potential for treating Parkinson's disease. Therefore, future work could focus on the translational potential of the present findings to clinical practice. Grant proposal on this aspect could be submitted to clinically oriented funding schemes such as the Health & Medical Research Fund.

14107616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107616.value: Parkinson’s disease is the second most common neurodegenerative diseases affecting millions of people worldwide. Currently there is no cure for Parkinson’s disease and only symptomatic treatments are available. Therefore, there is an urgent need to uncover the key pathogenic processes in Parkinson’s disease and develop disease-modifying treatment strategies that can slow down, stop or even reverse pathological progression of Parkinson’s disease. Our findings of the present project revealed that a small molecule GSK-J4 could ameliorate symptoms in Parkinson’s disease animal model. The detailed mechanisms underlying such beneficial effect were also elucidated, highlighting the role of epigenetic modification-induced iron suppression. Our results not only signify a new era for development of disease-modifying treatment against Parkinson’s disease through a novel brain cell-specific iron suppression but also provide insights into previously unknown pathogenic mechanism of this disorder. The results have potential to be translated to clinical practice in the future.

14108816.label: Realisation of objectives
14108816.value: Three specific aims have been all accomplished. For Specific Aim 1, both genders of Osx;Plekho1fl/fl (CKO) mice and wildtype control Plekho1fl/fl mice were recruited (n=36 in each strain, male:female=1:1). For Specific Aim 2, both genders of Osx/Plekho1-Smad1 mice, Osx/Plekho1 and Osx/Smad1 mice were recruited (n=36 in each strain, male:female=1:1). For above two aims, all the female mice were ovariectomized at 4 months old. Nine mice of each gender in each group will be sacrificed at 9-month old as baseline. The remaining mice of both genders were sacrificed at 19-month old. Ten days and two days before sacrifice, calcein green (10mg/kg) and xylenol orange (30mg/kg) were intraperitoneally injected to all the mice, respectively, to label bone formation surface. After sacrifice, the bilateral tibiae and femurs were collected. The left tibia was subjected to micro-CT measurement and subsequent bone histomorphometric analysis. The right tibia was subjected to real-time PCR analysis of Plekho1 mRNA expression in osteoblasts isolated by laser-captured micro-dissection (LCM). The bilateral femurs were pooled together for sorting the ALP+ cells (osteoblasts) using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) and subsequently subjected to western blot analysis for the protein expression of PLEKHO1, Smad1 and p-Smad1 as well as the ubiquitination level of endogenous Smad1. In Specific Aim 1, micro-CT analysis at the proximal tibiae showed that, the bone mineral density (BMD), Bone volume density (BV/TV) and trabecular number (Tb.N) were significantly less decreased during aging in CKO mice as compared to WT mice in both genders. Consistently, the CKO mice exhibited higher bone mass and more trabeculae as compared to WT mice at each time point, wherein the trabeculae structure was better preserved in CKO mice during aging in both genders. The bone histomorphometric analysis showed that the age-related decreases in mineral apposition rate (MAR), bone formation rate (BFR/BS), and osteoblast surface (Ob.S/BS) were rapid in WT mice but mild in CKO mice in both genders. Moreover, we found that the intraosseous mRNA level of Plekho1 was low in CKO mice and slightly elevated during aging, while it was much higher in WT mice and increased dramatically during aging. The intraosseous protein level of PLEKHO1 showed the similar trend with the Plekho1 mRNA. We also found that the protein levels of total Smad1 and p-Smad1 were higher in CKO mice when compared to WT mice at each time points, which decreased in bone specimens of WT mice during aging, whereas no obvious changes were found in CKO mice. The levels of ubiquitination Smad1 were lower in CKO mice compared to WT mice, which increased in bone specimens of WT mice during aging, while no significant change observed in CKO mice. Similar data were observed in both genders. Collectively, it is suggested that targeted depletion of Plekho1 gene in osteoblasts could attenuate the age-related reduction in Smad-dependent BMP signaling and bone formation. In Specific Aim 2, micro‐CT analysis showed that the decrease in BMD and BV/TV was both significantly attenuated in Osx/Smad1 mice than Osx-Cre mice during aging. In addition, bone histomorphometric analysis of the proximal tibiae revealed that the percentage of decrease in MAR and BFR/BS in Osx/Smad1 mice was also significantly lower than those in Osx-Cre mice. Furthermore, IHC analysis revealed more instances of co‐localization of pSmad1/5+ with ALP+ cells at proximal tibiae from Osx/Smad1 mice when compared to those from control littermates at each time point. Collectively, these results suggest that overexpression of Smad1 could attenuate the age‐related reduction in bone formation. However, the attenuation of bone loss during aging Smad1 overexpression would be abolished by Plekho1 overexpression, evidenced by significantly lower BMD and BV/TV determined by micro-CT analysis and lower MAR and BFR/BS assessed by bone histomorphometric analysis in Osx/Smad1‐Plekho1 mice than those in Osx/Smad1 mice during aging. For Specific Aim 3, Male and female Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were recruited. All the female rats were ovariectomized at 4 months old. Ten rats of each gender will be sacrificed at 13 months old as baseline before treatment. Thereafter, the remaining rats of both genders will be divided into siRNA treatment group, Non-sense siRNA group, vehicle control group and age-matched control group (n=10 for each group). The rats in the above groups were given weekly injections of aptamer (CH6)-conjugated Plekho1 siRNA (1 mg/kg), aptamer (CH6)-conjugated non-sense siRNA (1 mg/kg), free aptamer (CH6) and PBS for consecutive six weeks (short-term) and six months (long-term), respectively. All the rats were sacrificed after treatment. Ten days and two days before sacrifice, calcein green (10mg/kg) and xylenol orange (30mg/kg) will be intraperitoneally injected to the rats, respectively, to label bone formation surface. After sacrifice, the bilateral tibiae and femurs were collected. The left tibia was subjected to micro-CT measurement and subsequent bone histomorphometric analysis. The right tibia was subjected to real-time PCR analysis of Plekho1 mRNA expression in osteoblasts isolated by laser-captured micro-dissection (LCM). The bilateral femurs were pooled together for sorting the ALP+ cells (osteoblasts) using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) and subsequently subjected to western blot analysis for the protein expression of PLEKHO1, Smad1 and p-Smad1 as well as the ubiquitination level of endogenous Smad1. The intraosseous PLEKHO1 protein expression levels in siRNA group were remarkably lower, whereas the intraosseous p-Smad1/5 protein level in siRNA group was higher than those in non-sense siRNA, vehicle and control group. The micro-CT analysis and the bone histomorphometric analysis showed a better organized trabecular micro-architecture, a higher bone mass and a faster bone formation rate in siRNA groups as compared to the rats in non-sense siRNA, vehicle and control group. Moreover, the level of Smad1 ubiquitination was significantly lower in siRNA group compared to that in non-sense siRNA, vehicle and control group. For long-term treatment study, the animals with the treatment showed enhanced Smad-dependent BMP signaling, promoted bone formation, and elevated bone mass compared to the control group. Moreover, the treatment group didn’t show any sign of side effects. Taken together, intraosteoblast Plekho1 inhibition by Plekho1 siRNA could be a promising and safe therapeutic strategy osteoporosis. The study established the critical role of intraosteoblast Plekho1during age-related bone formation reduction and provide a novel therapeutic strategy targeting intraosteoblast Plekho1 for osteoporosis. The research work of the project has been reported in international conferences. Meanwhile, the researcher supported by the grant was also contributed to other musculoskeletal researches, which the granted was acknowledged in other 3 publications. 14108816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108816.value: The current project established the critical role of intraosteoblast Plekho1 in bone formation reduction during age-related. It also provided a promising and safe therapeutic strategy targeting the intraosteoblast Plekho1 for osteoporosis. For further development of the research, a nucleic acid aptamer-based drug targeting Plekho1 will be screened and developed. Nucleic acid aptamers are short, single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) molecules that are selected for bind¬ing to a specific target. They offer several advantages compared antibodies, including their relatively small physical size, flexible structure, quick chemical production, versatile chemical modification, high stability and lack of immunogenicity. Aptamers are promising drug candidates for intraosteoblast Plekho1-targeted therapeutic strategy for counteracting osteoporosis.

14108816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108816.value: Osteoporosis is a serious public health concern due to its high prevalence among the elderly population. However, the only FDA-approved agent stimulating new bone formation, parathyroid hormone (PTH), has the great concern of potential risk of osteosarcoma after long-term administration. Smad-dependent BMP signaling is responsible for bone formation. Pleckstrin homology domain-containing family O member 1 (PLEKHO1) specifically targets Smad ubiquitination regulatory factor 1 (Smurf1) to promote the poly-ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation of Smad1/5. The osteoblast-specific Plekho1 knockout mice demonstrated higher Smad-dependent BMP signaling and bone formation compared to wildtype mice during aging in both genders. Osteoblast-specific Smad1 overexpression attenuated the age-related bone formation reduction, while overexpression of Plekho1 in osteoblasts counteracted the above beneficial effect. Treating aging rats with weekly intravenous injection of Plekho1 siRNA conjugated with an osteoblast delivery system for six weeks significantly enhanced Smad-dependent BMP signaling and promoted bone formation in both genders. Meanwhile, long-term treatment showed consistently beneficial effects on bone formation and no significant sign of side effects was observed in aging rats of both genders. Taken together, the study established the critical role of intraosteoblast Plekho1 during age-related bone formation reduction. Targeting Plekho1 in osteoblasts may be a potential bone anabolic strategy to reverse osteoporosis.

14108916.label: Realisation of objectives
14108916.value: This project was completed according to schedule and fulfilled the three objectives. The data are based on 611 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus who had undergone serial transient elastography examinations and other clinical assessments at an interval of 3 years. Objective 1. To study the incidence of advanced fibrosis at 3 years in patients with type 2 diabetes and pre-existing NAFLD Among 487 patients with liver stiffness <10 kPa at baseline, 21 (4.3%) had follow-up liver stiffness ≥10 kPa. Independent factors associated with an increase of liver stiffness from <10 to ≥10 kPa included baseline body mass index, baseline alanine aminotransferase (ALT) level and an increase in ALT during follow-up. In the entire cohort of 611 patients, 73 (11.9%) had a ≥30% relative increase in liver stiffness. Similar to the first analysis, an increase in ALT during follow-up was the only factor associated with a ≥30% relative increase in liver stiffness. Objective 2. To study the incidence of NAFLD at 3 years in patients with type 2 diabetes but no NAFLD at baseline Among 198 patients with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) <248 dB/m at baseline, 103 (52.0%) had follow-up CAP ≥248 dB/m, of whom 55 had CAP ≥280 dB/m suggestive of severe hepatic steatosis. The only factor associated with an increase in CAP was high ALT level at baseline. Objective 3. To study clinical and genetic factors associated with incident NAFLD and advanced liver fibrosis in patients with type 2 diabetes The clinical factors associated with changes in liver stiffness and CAP are listed under Objectives 1 and 2. We also examined the following single nucleotide polymorphisms: patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 3 (PNPLA3, rs738409), apoplipoprotein C3 (APOC3, rs2854116 and rs2854117), glucokinase regulatory gene (GCKR, rs780094 and rs1260326), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors-gamma (PPAR-γ, rs3856806), adiponectin (rs1501299 and rs2241766) and leptin receptor (LEPR, rs1137100 and rs1137101). Both LEPR rs1137100 and 1137101 were associated with progression to advanced liver fibrosis (P=0.0074 and 0.024, respectively). In particular, the association with LEPR rs1137100 remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, duration of diabetes, body mass index and haemoglobin A1c. In contrast, adiponectin rs2241766 was associated with a lower risk of fatty liver (P=0.0184 after adjustment for the above factors).

14108916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108916.value: Type 2 diabetes is an important risk factor for nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and advanced fibrosis. Current international guidelines recommend the use of non-invasive tests as initial assessments for NAFLD, but the role of non-invasive tests as monitoring tools has not been established. We aimed to study the role of transient elastography as a monitoring tool in patients with type 2 diabetes. We recruited patients with type 2 diabetes without viral hepatitis or excessive alcohol intake from a complication screening facility in Hong Kong in 2013-2014 and repeated the assessments in 2016-2018. The primary endpoint was an increase of liver stiffness measurement (LSM) to ≥10 kPa. The secondary endpoint was the change in controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). 611 patients with type 2 diabetes and valid LSM (mean age 57.7±10.9 years; 342 males [56.0%]) were included in this study (568 also had valid CAP). Overall, there was moderate correlation between baseline and follow-up LSM (r=0.689, P<0.001). Among 487 patients with baseline LSM <10 kPa, 21 (4.3%) had follow-up LSM ≥10 kPa. Baseline body mass index, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and ∆ALT were independent factors associated with LSM increase. Among 124 patients with baseline LSM ≥10 kPa, 70 (56.5%) had follow-up LSM <10 kPa. Among 198 patients with CAP <248 dB/m at baseline, 103 (52.0%) had CAP increased to ≥248 dB/m. In conclusion, the prevalence and incidence of NAFLD in patients with type 2 diabetes are high. Although advanced fibrosis is common in this population, few patients progress to advanced fibrosis in 3 years. Future studies should define the optimal surveillance interval in diabetic patients.

14108916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108916.value: Because NAFLD and advanced liver fibrosis are common in patients with type 2 diabetes, we believe this is a high-risk group worthy of liver assessment. This notion has recently been endorsed by the latest guidelines of the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (Eslam et al. Hepatol Int. 2020 Oct 1. doi: 10.1007/s12072-020-10094-2. Online ahead of print). Looking ahead, as transient elastography may not be easily accessible outside hepatology practices, we are now conducting a randomised controlled trial to test the use of simple fibrosis scores coupled with automated electronic reminder messages to increase identification of advanced liver disease among patients with type 2 diabetes in general medical and diabetes clinics (NCT04241575). If it works, we will liaise with diabetes centres throughout Hong Kong to include liver fibrosis assessment as part of the comprehensive diabetic complications screening. Ultimately, we will promote this internationally as a standard of practice.

14108916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108916.value: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is currently the most common chronic liver disease worldwide and is a leading cause of liver cancer and cirrhosis in Western countries. In this study using serial transient elastography examinations, we show that NAFLD was present in 70% of patients with type 2 diabetes. Another half of patients without NAFLD also developed NAFLD in 3 years. Around 4% of patients with type 2 diabetes and NAFLD progressed to advanced liver fibrosis in 3 years. Factors associated with disease progression included obesity and high liver enzymes. Based on these data, we advocate liver assessment in patients with type 2 diabetes, especially for those who are obese or have increased liver enzymes.

14109516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109516.value: Hepatic cancer stem cells (HCSCs) is a small population of cancer cells but they are critical for cancer growth and recurrence, contributing to resistance to chemotherapy and radiation treatments in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). ZBP-89, a zinc finger transcription factor, regulates a number of genes related to cell proliferation, growth and apoptosis. In HCC, ZBP-89 has been shown to induce apoptosis of HCC cells via binding/interacting with p53, enhancing pro-apoptotic Bak, and stimulating caspase-6. Our recent results show that ZBP-89 is able to inhibit the expression of biomarkers related to HCSCs, including CD133, EpCAM and HIF-1a. Furthermore, we have found that in the promoter regions of human CD133, EpCAM, HIF-1 and PU.1 contain Sp1 sites. Binding of Sp1 to these sites appears to enhance their expression. ZBP-89 is known to compete with Sp1 to bind Sp1 sites, leading to inhibition of Sp1 function. We have also identified ZBP-89-binding sites in the other CSC-related transcription factor, GATA1. Inhibition of GATA1 can lead to reduction of cancer stem cells (CSCs). We therefore hypothesize that ZBP-89 can interact with Sp1 sites in the promoters of CD133, EpCAM, HIF-1 and PU.1, resulting in the reduction of their expression, and that ZBP-89 stimulates the expression of GATA1 via binding to the ZBP-89 sites in the GATA1 promoter. We believe, these interactions between ZBP-89 and the above molecules lead to the inhibition of HCSCs. This proposal is to test the above hypothesis by exploring whether the inhibitory effect of ZBP-89 on HCSCs is due to its ability to interact with the promoters of CD133, EpCAM, HIF-1a, PU.1 and GATA1 genes.

14109716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109716.value: When estrogen binds to estrogen receptor alpha (ERα66) it stimulates the proliferation and growth of human papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) cells. Inhibiting ERα66 sensitizes PTC cells to death stimuli and thus facilitates the treatment of thyroid cancer with chemotherapy. We have shown previously that thyroid cancer cells with elevated levels of heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) are resistant to cell death stimuli, and recently that activation of ERα66 induces autophagy. Autophagy is a cellular process that delivers energy at critical times of proliferation and so sustains cellular metabolism and promotes PTC cell survival and growth. ERα66-induced autophagy is associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) as well as activated phospho-p44/42 mitogen-activated protein kinase (Erk1/2) and autophagy-related protein 7 (ATG7). Activated ATG7 stimulates nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 2 (Nrf2) which is an inducer of HO-1. HO-1 is a key antioxidant enzyme that protects cells from oxidation-mediated damage and death by scavenging ROS. Therefore an increase in HO-1 should function to control the level of ROS in the pathway of ERα66-ROS-Erk1/2-ATG7-HO-1, possibly by a negative feedback loop. The feedback pathway that controls ROS is believed to function in tandem with ERα66 to maintain ROS at a level that stimulates tumor growth but without fatally damaging cells. If this feedback pathway was disrupted or key steps (such as Erk1/2 or ATG7) inhibited in ERα66-mediated autophagy, it might be reasonable to expect a rise in levels of ROS which in turn would damage cells and makes them vulnerable to chemotherapy. We thus hypothesize that (i) activated ERα66 stimulates the production of ROS and enhances Erk1/2, both of which induce autophagy, and (ii) that autophagy in turn results in the upregulation of HO-1 following the inhibition of Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1) and the activation of Nrf2, and (iii) that increased HO-1 is able to control ROS via a feedback pathway to maintain PTC cell growth and survival. Disrupting autophagy and/or inhibiting HO-1 should result in the over-production of ROS which sensitizes cells to damage and have a dramatic impact on the effectiveness of chemotherapy in patients with PTC. This would establish autophagy as a therapeutic target that may prove to be effectively inhibited by hydroxychloroquine for example, currently the only FDA approved autophagy inhibitor drug. Targeting autophagy will provide new opportunities for developing potent and specific autophagy inhibitors for patients with PTC where a breakthrough in their management is needed.

14109716.label: Realisation of objectives
14109716.value: 1. To confirm the induction of autophagy and HO-1 by ERα66 in PTC. 2. To explore whether there is an Erk1/2-mediated feedback loop to activate ERα66. 3. To study the role of ATG7 in ERα66-mediated HO-1 expression. 4. To determine whether HO-1 can control ROS via a negative feedback pathway in PTC. 5. To target autophagy or/and HO-1 to sensitize PTC cells to doxorubicin and other anti-tumor agents. 6. To use a mouse PTC model to verify the result. For Aims 1 and 5 (1.To confirm the induction of autophagy and HO-1 by ERa66 in PTC. 5.To target autophagy or/and HO-1 to sensitize PTC cells to doxorubicin and other anti-tumor agents), a series of experiments were performed in BCPAP (ERa-deficient PTC cells) and BCPAP-ERa (ERa-overexpressing PTC cells). The base level of autophagy in BCPAP cells was minimal or barely detectable but much higher in BCPAP-ERa cells. The ERa antagonist tamoxifen decreased the autophagy in BCPAP-ERa cells in a dose-dependent manner, but had little effect on autophagy in BCPAP cells. Similarly, the knockdown of ERa by siRNA significantly attenuated the autophagy in BCPAP-ERa cells. Therefore, these results suggest that ERa has a positive effect on the induction of autophagy in PTC cells. ERa is known to inhibit activity of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARg) and the level of PPARg ligands was significantly reduced in PTC as shown in this study. Since PPARg may act to counteract HO-1 (Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2008;177(11):1223-32), PPARg may functionally connect ERa and HO-1. We found that the expression of HO-1 protein was much higher in BCPAP-ERa than BCPAP, suggesting that ERa can upregulate the level of HO-1 in PTC cells. We further assayed the impact of HO-1 on the proliferation of PTC cells treated with doxorubicin (DOX), a chemotherapeutic agent that is frequently used in the treatment of thyroid cancer. The result showed that the cell proliferation was significantly reduced in BCPAP cells, compared with BCPAP-ERa cells. This finding suggest that the ERa may protect PTC cells from DOX-mediated inhibition via enhancing HO-1. The survival role of HO-1 in ERa-mediated PTC growth was confirmed by HO-1 inhibitory experiments as the inhibition of HO-1 could significantly reduce the growth of PTC. The above data were detailed in Figs 2 & 3 (2017 report) and some results were presented at meetings listed in Part C. For Aims 2,3,4 & 6 (2.To explore whether there is an Erk1/2-mediated feedback loop to activate ERa66; 3.To study the role of ATG7 in ERa66-mediated HO-1 expression; 4. To determine whether HO-1 can control ROS via a negative feedback pathway in PTC; and 6. To use a mouse PTC model to verify the result). We used the oxidation-sensitive probe DCFH-DA to measure the intracellular ROS levels by flow cytometry and our results showed that E2-stimulated autophagy was related to the induction of ROS in BCPAP-ERa cells (not in BCPAP cells). The inhibition of ROS with the free radical scavenger NAC could robustly attenuated E2/ERa-induced autophagy in PTC cells, further confirming the positive role of ROS in E2/ERa-induced autophagy. We noted that the high levels of ROS induced by E2/ERa were much earlier than the occurrence of autophagy and the elevation of HO-1 (3h vs 24h). This result has clearly indicated that the ERa-mediated increase of ROS predates the elevation of HO-1, supporting that ERa induces autophagy and HO-1 via stimulating ROS. Using the MEK/ERK inhibitor U0126 and the PI3K/Akt pathway inhibitor LY294002, we demonstrated that in contrast to the PI3K/Akt pathway which inhibits autophagy in PTC cells, the MEK/ERK pathway played a significant and positive role in the induction of autophagy in PTC cells. Moreover, E2-triggered activation of the MAPK pathway in BCPAP-ERa cells was attenuated by inhibiting ROS production with NAC, but not affected by the autophagy inhibitor CQ. E2-induced ROS production in BCPAP-ERa cells was not affected by inhibiting MEK activity with U0126. Using the xenograft mouse tumor model, we have verified some of the above key findings in vivo. Therefore, our data have demonstrated that E2-induced autophagy in ERa positive PTC cells is associated with generation of ROS and activation of MAPK pathway. And the induction of intracellular ROS can contribute to the activation of MAPK pathway, indicating that there is a crosstalk/feedback control between them. The above data were detailed in Figs 1-7 (2019 report) and some results were/will be presented at meetings listed in Part C.

To test the small molecules that can selectively inhibit ERa and to check whether these inhibitors can enhance current ant-tumor treatments for PTC. 2). 14109716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109716.value: An increasing number of publications have indicated that estrogen receptor alpha (ERa) contributes to the growth of papillary thyroid cancer (PTC). However, the mechanism responsible remains largely unknown. Autophagy is a catabolic process by which cells degrade their own components by targeting them for lysosomal degradation. In this study, we determined the connections between ERa and autophagy in PTC. We have demonstrated that ERa could induce autophagy in PTC and that the upregulation of ERK1/2 and reactive oxygen species (ROS) predated the occurrence of autophagy. The level of heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) was increased in the ERa-mediated autophagy cells. The enhancement of HO-1 could limit the levels of ROS as well as the autophagy, sensitizing PTC cells to chemotherapeutic agents. But, the downregulation of HO-1 could lead to the opposite results. In the mouse tumor model, tumors formed by PTC cells with ERa overexpression grew significantly larger, with enhanced autophagy. The application of ERa antagonist could reduce the growth of the tumor with decreasing autophagy. Therefore, our results have confirmed that ERa-induced autophagy is a survival factor for PTC. These data suggest that there are potential therapeutic targets to arrest the growth of PTC, including ERa, HO-1 and ROS.

14110016.label: Realisation of objectives
14110016.value: Under the supporting this GRF, we made great progress in dissecting the oncogenic properties of Slit-Robo GTPase-activating protein 1 (SRGAP1) mediated signaling and characterizing its molecular crosstalks in gastric cancer (GC). We confirmed that overexpression of SRGAP1 leads to dysregulation of multiple cellular pathways via upregulation of downstream oncogenic factors. The oncogenic regulatory network contributes a promoting role in gastric tumorigenesis. The mechanism responsible for SRGAP1 protein upregulation has been extensively revealed, such as post-transcriptional regulation by microRNAs (miRNAs). The findings lead to the identification of useful tumor biomarkers in GC and establishment of targeted interventions based on the recognized regulatory pathways. This has been illustrated in the following studies. In the first part, we reported the upregulation of SRGPA1 in GC cell lines and primary samples. It overexpression is correlated with poor outcomes in GC patients. In the second part, we aim to reveal the regulatory mechanisms of SRGAP1 in GC. Apart from genetic and epigenetic regulation, post-transcriptional modulation is known as another significant mechanism, such as miRNA regulation. In this study, we for the first time reported the tumor-suppressive miRNAs, miR-340 and miR-124, are the main regulators of SRGAP1 by bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation. In the third part, we focused on deciphering how SRGAP1 drives gastric carcinogenesis. By knocking down SRGAP1 in GC cells, we observed obvious morphological changes and inactivation status of β-catenin. The results implied that β-catenin was activated by SRGAP1. Moreover, the EMT (epithelial to mesenchymal transition) and metastasis related biomarkers was upregulated in the SRGAP1 overexpressed cells. Meanwhile, we found SRGAP1 knockdown induces accumulation of GTP-RhoA and GTP-Cdc42, while the EMT and cell migration were significantly inhibited. In summary, we provide evidence the Slit-ROBO-SRGAP1-β-catenin oncogenic signaling promotes gastric carcinogenesis and serves as a therapeutic target. The main findings of this project were published on Oncogene (Huang T et al, Oncogene, 2018). Supported by the grant, we also put much emphasis on the other oncogenic signalings, such as Hippo-YAP1, NOTCH, FGF-FGFR signaling (Huang T et al, Molecular Cancer, 2016; Zhang J et al, Cells, 2019; Zhang J et al, Oncogene, 2019). The interaction between secreted proteins and receptors are mainly responsible for transducing oncogenic signals into intracellular molecular mechanisms. Extracellular microenvironment plays a crucial role in triggering the tumorigenic progression in gastric carcinogenesis. Among the signaling pathway, we highlighted the Hippo-YAP1 signaling as a significant driver in gastric carcinogenesis by linking the immune reaction and GC cell responses (Zhou Y et al, Journal of Thoracic Disease, 2017; Zhou Y et al, Cancer Letters, 2018). Hippo-YAP1 signaling pathway conveys the effective signals to the downstream and controlling the cellular proliferative mechanism. Turning off Hippo cascade dramatically enlarges the size of tissues or organs, resulting in tumorigenesis. YAP1 localizes in the central position of the Hippo signaling. We previously reported that the disrupted upstream of Hippo pathway in malignancies including GC (Kang W et al, Clinical Cancer Research, 2011). In addition, the expression YAP1 is regulated by Motin members (Huang T et al, Journal of Translational Medicine, 2018). As a robust mediator of the extracellular matrix on tumorigenesis, YAP1 was also sensitive to mechanical stimulus. This was transducted by cytoskeletal remodeling in a mechanotransduction mechanism (Zhang J et al, Molecular Carcinogenesis, 2018; Zhang J et al, International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2019). These studies constitute a picture of the interaction between extracellular microenvironment and GC cells. LncRNA (long non-coding RNA) and miRNA are also our one research area. Supported by this GRF, we did lots of related studies. We summarized the functional role lncRNA-H19 in gastrointestinal cancers by interplaying with multiple miRNAs and binding partners (Zhang L et al, International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2017). Deregulation of miRNAs is associated with tumor initiation, maintainance and metastasis. In the miRNA studies, we investigated the aberrantly expressed miRNAs in GC cells and EBV-encoded miRNAs. EBV-encoded miRNAs specifically target multiple tumor suppressors and promotes EBVaGC (EBV associated GC) progression (Zhang J et al, Journal of Cellular and Molecular Medicine, 2017). In GC cells, many miRNAs were downregulated due to epigenetic regulation such as promoter methylation. miR-34a targeting IGF2BP3 and miR-590-5p targeting FGF18 have been firstly reported by our group (Zhou Y et al, Molecular Cancer, 2017; Zhang J et al, Oncogene, 2019). The deregulated miRNAs targeting Hippo-YAP1 related proteins was also comprehensively investigated. For example, miR-375 suppressed the expression YAP1/TEAD4/CTGF cascade and was involved in Hippo pathway (Kang W et al, Cell Death and Disease, 2018). The decreased miR-4269 was partly responsible for the activation of TEAD1 and TEAD4 in gastric carcinogenesis (Zhou J et al, Oncogene, 2017). Besides the above, we summarized a miR-630/YAP1/ERK feedback loop serving as a potent mechanism for drug resistance in EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinomas (Zhang J et al, Journal of Thoracic Disease, 2018). All the findings broaden our horizon on the molecular mechanism from extracellular stimulation to downstream effectors in gastric carcinogenesis. Identification of novel biomarkers enriches the prognostic biomarker pool and provides clinical translational implications in GC.

14110016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14110016.value: Our research focus mainly on the SRGAP1 mediated signaling crosstalk in gastric carcinogenesis. The involvement of Slit-ROBO, the upstream of SRGAP1, has been revealed to play a promoting role in gastric carcinogenesis. However, how Slit-ROBO drives GC progression has not been fully elucidated. SRGAP1, the direct Slit-ROBO effector, links Slit-ROBO with the downstream intracellular processes. To reveal the molecular mechanisms of SRGAP1 in GC, we performed a series of studies accordingly. Our findings include three major aspects. Firstly, we identified the abundance of SRGAP1 was associated with poor clinical outcomes in primary GC. Secondly, two well-known tumor suppressor miRNAs, miR-340 and miR-124, negatively regulate SRGAP1 expression and exerts inhibitory function. The upregulation of SRGAP1 in GC is partly due to the silence of miR-340 and miR-124. Thirdly, we unraveled that SRGAP1 promotes epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) and metastasis in GC by activating β-catenin pathway and GTP-Rac1-mediated cytoskeleton remodeling. The main findings were published on Oncogene (Huang T et al, Oncogene, 2018). Apart from miR340/124-SRGAP1-β-catenin cascade, we also performed other GC related experiments supported by this GRF grant. We have comprehensively delineated that multiple oncogenic proteins, such as IGF2BP3, FGF18, YAP1, and TEAD1/4, in driving gastric carcinogenesis and negatively regulated by miR-34a (Zhou Y et al, Molecular Cancer), miR-590-5p (Zhang J et al, Oncogene, 2019), miR-375 (Cell Death and Disease, 2018), and miR-4269 respectively (Zhou Y et al, Oncogene, 2017). The regulation of YAP1 by miR-630 is another potential mechanism contributing to drug resistance acquisition in EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma (Zhang J et al, Journal of Thoracic Disease, 2018). Meanwhile, we encouraged the postgraduate students and postdoctoral fellows to draft Review Articles on GC topic, thus to summarize the related findings and direct our future work. Supported by this GRF, we totally published 6 Review Articles on peer-reviewed journal such as Molecular Cancer, Cancer Letters, IJMS, JCMM, BMC Cancer, and Cells. In summary, our work not only provides a comprehensive picture about SRGAP1-mediated signaling network in gastric carcinogenesis, but also sheds light on the prognostic significance of the biomarkers and provides translational potential.

14110016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110016.value: We have delineated the molecular mechanisms of SRGAP1-mediated oncogenic signaling in gastric carcinogenesis, as well as its regulation by miRNAs. Our findings not only broadened our understanding of the SRGAP1 signaling, cytoskeleton remodeling, and deregulated miRNA network in GC progression, but also lead to the identification of multiple prognostic biomarkers for GC. In the future study, we need to develop applicable and effective anti-cancer strategies based on the current findings. Realizing the clinical translational potential comes to be our main research aim in the project. Firstly, the miRNA mimics (miR-340 and miR-124) will be employed to inhibit tumor growth in animal models. Secondly, targeting SRGAP1 related signaling is another issue. We are planning to reveal the crosstalks between SRGAP1 and other signaling pathways, such as Hippo-YAP1 signaling and tyrosine receptor kinases (TRKs). Thirdly, before forming the malignancy by single cancer cell, tumorigenesis is always along with an aberrant tumor microenvironment. Thus we will also delineate the tumor microenvironment in SRGAP1-positive cases. We hope our future studies will not only shed light on the prospective therapeutic direction in GC but also promote our academic research to a higher level.

14110016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110016.value: Gastric cancer (GC) is the one of the most common fatal malignancies worldwide. It is particularly prevalent in China including Hong Kong. The mortality rate remains relatively unchanged over the past 30 years with only 10-20% overall 5-years survival rate. Abnormal cellular signal transduction leads to carcinogenesis. The activation of oncogenic signalings has been defined as driver event for gastric carcinogenesis, such as receptor protein overexpression on the cell surface, activation of the downstream effectors, and enhancing the cell viability and mobility. Our studies mainly focus on the elucidation of the molecular crosstalks during gastric tumorigenesis. In this study, we clearly demonstrated that SRGAP1 plays oncogenic role in gastric carcinogenesis and serves as prognostic biomarker in GC patients. SRGAP1 promotes cytoskeletal protein rearrangement by directly regulating the Rho family thus to drive gastric initiation and progression. SRGAP1 upregulation in GC is partly due to the silence of two tumor suppressive miRNAs, namely miR-340 and miR-124. These two miRNAs exerts tumor suppressor function by targeting SRGAP1 and their expression shows negative correlation in primary GC samples. Our findings provide the first evidence that SRGAP1, a crucial SRGAP member, activates the oncogenic signaling transduction by promoting cell invasion and migration. Targeting SRGAP1 by small molecules or related miRNAs might serve a novel strategy for clinical intervention.

14111216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111216.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer worldwide. Both the incidence and death rate from CRC are increasing rapidly in Asian region, including Hong Kong. The mechanisms underlying CRC initiation and development however remain elusive. We have recently performed genome-wide DNA methylation sequencing and gene expression analyses of human CRC samples. Notably, tripartite motif 67 (TRIM67), a member of TRIM family genes, is frequently silenced in CRC tumor tissues due to its promoter methylation. Several TRIM family members have been found to play important roles in cancer development either as oncogene or tumour suppressor gene, whilst the functional significance and clinical implication of TRIM67 in human cancer are unclear. In this proposal, we provide strong evidences that TRIM67 plays a key tumor suppressor role in CRC tumorigenesis. We found TRIM67 exhibited distinct silencing or downregulation in CRC tumor tissues compared with their adjacent non-tumor tissues and in colon cancer cell lines. Our preliminary in vitro and in vivo functional studies supported a strong tumor inhibitory role of TRIM67 in CRC development, possibly through inducing the p53 pathway via directly interacting with endogenous p53 by its coiled coil domain, which increased the p53 stability. Moreover, we showed a positive feedback loop between TRIM67 and p53. Collectively, we propose to investigate the tumor suppressive role of TRIM67 for its novel function which cross talks with p53 pathway in the malignant progression of colon cancer. In this application, we propose three specific objectives: 1) to characterize the anti-tumor function of TRIM67 in colon cancer using a unique TRIM67 conditional colon-specific knock-out mouse model; 2) to investigate the mechanisms underlying the tumor-suppressive role of TRIM67 through interaction with p53 pathway; 3) to study the clinical significance of TRIM67 in CRC patients. These research objectives will be tackled with a multidisciplinary approach combining biochemistry, genomics, molecular and cell biology, signaling pathway, protein-protein interaction analysis and transgenic animal models. The new knowledge gained will provide insight into the role of TRIM67 in CRC initiation and progression, advance our understanding of CRC molecular pathogenesis and facilitate early diagnosis and more effective therapeutic strategy for CRC patients. 在全球範圍內，結直腸癌是第三大常見癌症。在亞洲地區，包括香港，其患病率和死亡率均呈現快速升高的趨勢。然而，結直腸癌的發生和發展機制仍然很不清楚。通過深度分析結直腸癌全基因組DNA甲基化測序和基因表達譜資料庫，我們最新發現一個TRIM家族的基因－tripartite motif 67 (TRIM67)—在結直腸癌組織中常常因為啟動子區域甲基化而發生沉默。已發現幾個TRIM家族的成員在腫瘤發展中可作為原癌基因亦或是抑癌基因而發揮重要作用，但是尚不清楚TRIM67在腫瘤中的功能。在本研究中，我們提供了強有力的證據證明TRIM67在結直腸癌的發生發展中作為腫瘤抑制因數發揮關鍵作用。 我們首先發現，相比相鄰的非腫瘤組織，TRIM67在結直腸癌腫瘤組織中顯著地沉默或者表達下調，在結腸癌細胞系中亦如此。我們初步的體外、體內功能研究顯示，TRIM67具有顯著的抑制結直腸癌發展的功能，這一功能可能通過其自身的coiled coil蛋白結構域與內源p53蛋白發生直接相互作用，增強p53穩定性，從而誘導p53信號通路的活化。同時，我們還發現在TRIM67和p53之間存在正回饋調節作用。 綜上所述，我們計畫對TRIM67這一通過與p53相互作用而產生的抗結直腸癌作用進行研究。在本專案計畫中，我們提出3項研究標的：1）利用獨特的條件性、結腸組織特異性TRIM67敲除小鼠模型，研究TRIM67抑制腫瘤的功能特點；2）研究TRIM67通過與p53信號通路相互作用發揮抗腫瘤作用的分子機制；3）研究TRIM67在結直腸癌患者中的臨床意義。這些研究標的將通過有機地結合多學科研究方法得以實施，包括生物化學，基因組學，分子和細胞生物學，信號通路，蛋白－蛋白相互作用分析和轉基因動物模型等。從本項研究所獲得的新知識可以使我們更加深刻地瞭解TRIM67在結直腸癌發生和發展中的作用，促進我們對結直腸癌分子病理機制的認識，並可能運用於結直腸癌患者的早期症斷和更高效治療方案的開發。

14111216.label: Realisation of objectives
14111216.value: Objective 1: To characterize the tumor–suppressing role of TRIM67 in colon cancer a) The tumor suppressive functions of TRIM67 were examined in colon cancer cell line models: TRIM67 overexpression assays were performed in CRC cells expressing wild-type p53 (HCT116, RKO and LoVo cells) and CRC cells expressing mutant p53 (HT-29, SW480 and DLD-1). TRIM67 knockdown assays were performed in normal colon epithelial cell line NCM460 and normal gastric epithelium cell line GES1. The cellular effects on cell growth, apoptosis and cell cycle were examined. b) study the role of TRIM67 in colon cancer progression in TRIM67 colon-specific conditional knockout mouse model: We generated constitutive Trim67 knockout mice and then crossed them to ApcMin/+ mice to determine the role of Trim67 deficiency in the ApcMin/+ mouse model of intestinal tumorigenesis. ApcMin/+, Trim67-/+, Trim67-/-, Trim67-/+ApcMin/+ and Trim67-/-ApcMin/+ mice were sacrificed at 3 months. Body weight, intestinal tumor and histology and Trim67 mRNA expression were examined. We also investigated the effect of colon-specific Trim67 deletion in a chemically (AOM)-induced model of colorectal carcinogenesis. Colon-specific, conditional Trim67 knockout mice were generated by crossing Trim67fl/fl mice to Cdx2-CreERT2 mice. Trim67 was deleted specifically in the colon after exposure to tamoxifen at 2 months of age, and colorectal tumorigenesis was subsequently induced by AOM injection. Body weight, intestinal tumor and histology and Trim67 mRNA expression were examined. Objective 2: To investigate the mechanisms underlying the tumor suppressive role of TRIM67 in activating P53 signaling pathway a) determine the direct interaction of TRIM67 and p53 proteins and explore the binding domains: To verify the direct interaction between TRIM67, p53 and MDM2 in cell free conditions, we performed in vitro protein binding assays using purified recombinant GST-tagged p53, GST-tagged MDM2 and Flag-tagged TRIM67 proteins. GST-p53, GST-MDM2 and GST proteins were expressed in BL21(DE3) E. coli and purified by Glutathione Sepharose 4B resin. Flag-TRIM67 protein was purified by ANTI-FLAG® M2 Magnetic Beads using cell lysates from HEK293T transfected with pcDNA3.1-Flag-TRIM67 plasmid. Purified TRIM67 interacted with p53 but not MDM2. We identified p53 domain(s) responsible for binding to TRIM67. p53 possesses a N-terminal transcriptional activation region (TAD domain), followed by a polyproline region (PPR), a central DNA-binding domain (DBD) and a C-terminal domain. We generated three p53 deletion mutants lacking TAD-PPR (N-D2), C-terminal (C-D3) or TAD plus C-terminal (N-D3) domains and tested their interaction with TRIM67 by co-IP. We determined which functional domain(s) in TRIM67 are responsible for its effect on p53 activation. TRIM67 possesses four major domains: a RING finger domain, a coiled coil domain (CC), a COS domain and a SPRY domain. We constructed eight TRIM67 deletion mutants. COS-SPRY deletion completely abolished nuclear translocation of RING-CC mutant; while other mutants are expressed in both cytosol and nucleus. As the nuclear localization of TRIM67 is essential for its capacity to protect p53, we fused RING-CC to a nuclear localization signal (NLS) to promote nuclear localization. We next tested effect of TRIM67 deletion mutants on expression of p53 downstream targets, p53 protein expression and cleavage of MDM2 to determine whether TRIM67 deletion mutants retained the ability of full-length TRIM67. b) elucidate the structure of TRIM67-p53-MDM2 complex: Our plan is to investigate three-dimensional structure of the protein-protein interaction complex (TRIM67-p53 or TRIM67-p53-MDM2) by single particle cryo-electron microscopy with the support from Dr. Ye XIANG (PI’s collaborator) from Basic Medical Sciences, Tsinghua University. However, this part failed due to the following reasons: 1) p53 protein is very unstable. The structure of full-length p53 protein has not been reported yet. 2) Co-crystallization of two proteins needs a very strong interaction between them. We have tried several times, but co-crystallization failed. The interaction between TRIM67 and p53 might not be strong enough for co-crystallization. Or the interaction needs post-transcriptional protein modification in eukaryotic cells. c) investigate the positive feedback loop between TRIM67 and p53: We confirmed that DNA damaging chemotherapeutic drugs doxorubicin (Dox) and actinomycin D (AcD) and ectopic p53 expression induced TRIM67 expression in NCM460 and GES1 cells. Two potential p53 half-sites in TRIM67 promoter were predicted. We examined the occupancy of p53 on TRIM67 promoter in NCM460 cells exposed to Dox by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-PCR using six pairs of primers spanning TRIM67 promoter region. Induction of TRIM67 mRNA expression by Dox was further confirmed by p53 knockdown assay. Moreover, we generated luciferase reporters containing TRIM67 promoter region ranging from -1200 to +100 and examined whether mutation of the potential site would affect the induction of TRIM67 luciferase reporter activity by p53. To examine whether the induction of TRIM67 by p53 is abrogated due to promoter hypermethylation in CRC cells, we checked TRIM67 expression upon ectopic p53 expression in HCT116 and RKO cells, in which TRIM67 promoter was densely methylated. We proposed that TRIM67 is engaged in a positive regulatory loop to trigger p53 induced proliferative arrest and apoptosis induction in response to cellular stress, such as DNA damage. We treated NCM460 and GES1 cells with Dox with or without knockdown of TRIM67. The effects on cell proliferation, apoptosis, cell cycle, p53 and DNA damage checkpoint proteins, and p53 downstream target genes were examined. Objective 3: To study the clinical significance of TRIM67 in colon cancer a) determine the association between TRIM67 methylation level and clinical status: We found that not enough DNA was left for most CRC tissues samples with clinical information. Therefore, we evaluated the protein expression of TRIM67 by IHC in tissue microarrays (TMA) consisting of 141 CRC patients for survival analysis. b) investigate plasma methylated TRIM67 DNA as potential biomarker in CRC patients: Genomic DNA was extracted from the plasma of CRC and control subject. The methylated TRIM67 DNA in plasma was assessed by BGS. However, due to the sequence characteristics of TRIM67 promoter, the PCR amplification efficiency was not good enough to amplify PCR product in the plasma DNA from most patients. Therefore, it is not optimal method for diagnosis.

14111216.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111216.value: Objective 1: To characterize the tumor–suppressing role of TRIM67 in colon cancer a) In vitro functional studies showed that TRIM67 possesses a tumor suppressive function in colorectal cancer. Ectopic expression of TRIM67 suppressed cell proliferation, as evidenced by cell viability assay and colony formation assay in HCT116, RKO, and LoVo cells. Conversely, knockdown of TRIM67 in normal human colon epithelial cell line NCM460 led to an increased ability to proliferate as compared with control cells. b) Using mutant Apc and AOM-induced colorectal cancer models, we demonstrated that either heterozygous or homozygous deletion of Trim67-predisposed mice to colorectal tumorigenesis. In particular, the loss of both Trim67 alleles greatly accelerated tumorigenesis, both in terms of tumor multiplicity and burden. Our findings provide evidence that TRIM67 functions as a tumor suppressor in colorectal cancer in vivo. Objective 2: To investigate the mechanisms underlying the tumor suppressive role of TRIM67 in activating P53 signaling pathway a) RNA-seq and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEG) revealed that DEGs upregulated by TRIM67 were most significantly enriched in the p53 signaling pathway. We found that TRIM67 overexpression led to accumulation of stabilized p53 in the nucleus, thereby activating its downstream signaling. b) Co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) was used to confirm the interaction between TRIM67 and endogenous p53 and MDM2 in colorectal cancer cells, as well as in cell-free systems with purified recombinant proteins. The TRIM67-p53 interaction protected it from MDM2-mediated ubiquitination. MDM2 is the major E3 ligase of p53. Domain deletion analyses showed that TRIM67 inhibits MDM2 action by occupying C terminus of p53, which destabilizes p53–MDM2 complex and blocks MDM2-mediated p53 ubiquitination and proteasome degradation. c) We also identified TRIM67 as a pivotal component of a positive feedback loop that amplifies p53 signaling under stress conditions. p53 directly regulates TRIM67 by binding to TRIM67 promoter. Treatment with DNA-damaging drugs dramatically upregulated p53-induced expression of TRIM67, which in turn, stabilized p53 and promoted p53-mediated downstream gene expression. Objective 3: To study the clinical significance of TRIM67 in colon cancer a) We evaluated protein expression of TRIM67 by immunohistochemistry in tissue microarrays (TMA) consisting of 141 patients with colorectal cancer. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis demonstrated that patients with low TRIM67 protein expression had significantly shorter survival. Multivariate Cox regression analysis showed that low TRIM67 expression was an independent predictor of poor survival of patients with colorectal cancer.

14111216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111216.value: Our results suggest that loss of TRIM67 expression in colorectal cancer leads to comprised p53 activation and chemotherapy response in cancers with wild-type p53. We have demonstrated that TRIM67 down-regulation is through heavy DNA promoter methylation. Thus, to increase the sensitivity of chemotherapy treatment, p53 reactivation through epigenetic restoration of TRIM67 may be an important therapeutic method in p53 wild-type CRC patients with low TRIM67 expression. Three DNA methyltransferase inhibitors 5-azacytidine (Vidaza®), DAC (decitabine or Dacogen®) and SGI-110 are clinically available or in clinical trials for various malignancy types. DAC has been shown to be able to reactivate TRIM67 expression in all silenced colon cancer cell lines. Further optimization of combining these drugs holds promise for the development of a new clinical chemotherapy instruction. On the other hand, TRIM67 expression and/or methylation in tumors serves a promising standard to distinguish the effectiveness of chemotherapy response. In our discovery cohort of 141 CRC patients, low TRIM67 protein level predicted poor survival in CRC patients. In the future, we plan to further validate our findings in large, independent cohorts of CRC patients.

14111216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111216.value: Inactivation of p53 is a key event driving colorectal tumorigenesis and resistance to DNA damaging chemotherapy. Apart from genetic mutations, p53 is frequently downregulated by post-transcriptional mechanisms in CRC. Here, our work in CRC cells and transgenic mice unveil that TRIM67 stabilizes p53 by preventing MDM2-mediated degradation. We also demonstrate that TRIM67 forms a positive circuitry with p53 to synergistically induce p53 signaling cascade, particularly in response to DNA damaging chemotherapy. Importantly, TRIM67 reconstitution significantly sensitizes CRC cells to DNA damaging chemotherapy. TRIM67 loss is also identified as an independent marker for disease prognosis in CRC. TRIM67/p53 axis represents a novel therapeutic target that could be harnessed to improve chemotherapy efficacy in CRC expressing wildtype p53 but with repressed p53 signaling.
