14111816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111816.value: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is one of the leading causes of acute liver failure. Unlike well-recognized DILI caused by conventional drugs, herb/natural product-induced hepatotoxicity has less public awareness and is an unresolved threatening problem worldwide. Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are probably one of the most common phytotoxins causing hepatotoxicity, and PA-induced liver injury (PA-ILI) contributes significantly to herbal hepatotoxicity. PA-containing plants widely distribute in ~3% of world's flowering plants. More than half of naturally occurring PAs have been reported hepatotoxic. PA contamination in the food chain is also common and becomes significant sources contributing to PA-ILI. Numerous PA poisoning cases have been reported yearly due to the unaware consumption of PA-containing plants used as herbal medicines, teas, and dietary supplements, and PA-contaminated foodstuffs, including green crop, honey, and milk. PAs can induce acute hepatotoxicity, known as hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (HSOS) with typical manifestations of hepatomegaly, jaundice and ascites. Chronic exposure to small amounts of PAs may imperceptibly induce chronic liver diseases such as liver fibrosis and cirrhosis that may not show overt symptoms in the early stage during disease progression, but eventually lead to liver failure. Although there is no any systematic survey, several observational reports revealed that PA-induced chronic illness, especially liver fibrosis, are common in the survivors who suffered from acute PA-induced HSOS. Our recent observation on 13 PA-ILI patients also indicated a high incidence (~62%, 8/13) of the development of liver fibrosis. Currently, clinical treatment of PA-ILI is usually supportive and symptomatic for the acute HSOS. While therapies targeting chronic diseases including liver fibrosis are largely unexplored. Moreover, the current knowledge on the disease progression and underlying mechanism of PA-induced liver fibrosis is very limited, which certainly hampered the exploration of potential therapeutic intervention against PA-induced liver fibrosis. Therefore, it is significant and timely to study PA-induced liver fibrosis and also investigate potential therapies. The present project aims to 1) develop an animal model of PA-induced liver fibrosis to study disease progression and mechanism of PA-induced liver fibrosis; and 2) investigate the potential therapeutic intervention against PA-induced liver fibrosis. The results obtained will facilitate the better understanding of the disease progression and mechanisms of PA-ILI from acute HSOS to chronic liver fibrosis, and also provide scientific evidences supporting further development of clinical management of PA-ILI especially for PA-induced liver fibrosis. 藥物性肝損傷是引起急性肝衰竭的主要原因之一。不同於已有廣泛認知的西藥引起之肝損傷，草藥或天然產物引起的肝損傷通常缺乏公眾認知，並已成為威脅人類健康的重大隱患。吡咯裡西啶類生物鹼（PA）是最為普遍的植物類毒素之一，占據草藥引發肝損傷的重要位置。含PA的植物廣泛分布於全世界約3%的有花植物中。迄今，在已發現的PA中，有超過半數已報道有毒。此外，PA對食物鏈的污染也很常見，並為PA引起肝損傷的重要途徑。由於無意中服用含有PA的植物，包括草藥、茶和膳食補充劑等，和PA污染的食物，如農作物、蜂蜜和牛奶等，每年都有數目眾多的PA中毒案例報道。 PA可引起急性肝損傷，主要為肝竇閉塞綜合征（HSOS），其典型症狀為肝腫大、黃疸及腹水。而長期攝入小劑量PA可能引致慢性肝病，如肝纖維化和肝硬化，此類病變通常在發病前期並無明顯症狀，但最終將導致肝衰竭。盡管沒有系統的統計調查，數篇觀察性報道揭示：在PA引起急性HSOS的存活病人中，PA所致慢性肝病的發生也非常普遍，尤其是肝纖維化。近期，我們對13個PA引起肝損傷病人的觀察研究中也發現較高的肝纖維化發生率（~62%）。 目前，針對PA引起急性HSOS的臨床治療方式主要包括保肝及對症療法。然而，針對PA引起的慢性疾病，如肝纖維化的治療手段卻幾乎空白。此外，目前對PA引起的肝纖維化的發病進程及其機制的了解也非常有限，這也限制了對其治療方式的研發。 因此，對PA引起的肝纖維化的機制及治療方法的研究迫切重要。此項目旨在1）建立PA引起肝纖維化的動物模型，並以此模型研究闡釋PA引起肝纖維化的發病過程及機制；2）研究PA引起肝纖維化的治療方法。 預期的研究結果將有利於我們更好的了解PA引起的肝損傷，包括急性HSOS到慢性肝纖維化的發病過程及相關機制。同時，研究結果也將為未來臨床診治PA引起的肝損傷，尤其是PA引起的肝纖維化，提供科學依據。

14111816.label: Realisation of objectives
14111816.value: Both objectives have been well accomplished. Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are probably one of the most common phytotoxins causing hepatotoxicity, and PA-induced liver injury (PA-ILI) contributes significantly to herbal hepatotoxicity. PA-containing plants widely distribute in ~3% of world's flowering plants. PAs can induce acute hepatotoxicity, known as hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (HSOS) with typical manifestations of hepatomegaly, jaundice and ascites. HSOS can be classified according to disease severity with a varied mortality of 30%-67%. In mild HSOS cases, 70-85% of patients recover spontaneously, and with some supportive treatment, the majority has satisfactory outcomes. However, moderate, and severe HSOS cases have higher mortality and are associated with chronic liver failure and chronic liver lesions such as liver fibrosis and cirrhosis at the late stage. Therefore, it is significant and timely to study the disease progression from PA-induced acute HSOS to PA-induced liver fibrosis, and the underlying mechanisms, which will certainly facilitate the further exploration of potential therapeutic intervention against PA-ILI. Objective 1: We have established rat models of acute resolving liver injury and chronic progressive liver fibrosis induced by retrorsine (RTS), a well-known hepatotoxic PA, via two dosage regimens, i.e. a single dose of 40 mg/kg RTS and two doses of 40 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg RTS on day 0 and day 7, respectively. Both dosage regimens caused acute liver injury on day 2 manifested as HSOS, characterized by sinusoidal dilation, endothelial cell damage, and elevated serum alanine aminotransferase activity and bilirubin levels. In single dose model, mild liver fibrosis developed at sinusoids and perisinusoidal space surrounding the central veins at week 1 and 2, and thereafter, all liver injury resolved gradually. In twice dose model, liver fibrosis progressed within the 16-week observation period. These models resemble clinical and pathological manifestations of different subpopulations of PA-ILI patients. For instance, after treatment of acute PA-HSOS, some patients were fully recovered and discharged from hospital, while others gradually developed to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and eventually liver failure. Our developed animal models can also sever as powerful tools for further mechanistic studies, and research and development of differential therapeutic strategies for both acute and chronic progressive PA-ILI (Paper 9; Abstract 1 in Part C). Using our established rat models, we investigated dynamic changes in hepatic gene/protein expression that may underpin mechanisms of PA-ILI and following regressive and progressive liver fibrosis. Compared with the control groups, RTS induced myofibroblastic activation, transforming growth factor (TGF)-1 signaling, and changes in expression of matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP-9) and tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 1 (TIMP-1). These dynamic changes differed in RTS single and twice dose groups and corresponded with the regression and progression of liver fibrosis, respectively, in two rat models. The results suggest that these fibrogenic factors and/or signalling pathways involved in the regression and progression of PA-induced liver fibrosis are potential therapeutic targets of PA-ILI (Papers 8-9; Abstract 1 in Part C). PAs are pro-toxins and undergo hepatic CYP-mediated metabolic activation to generate reactive metabolites (dehydro-PAs), which rapidly bind with cellular proteins to form pyrrole-protein adducts leading to hepatotoxicity. We delineated that both PAs and their N-oxides, which commonly co-exist with PAs in plants, undergo similar metabolic activation leading to hepatoxicity. Based on the metabolism-mediated toxicity, we have developed novel, sensitive, and specific mechanism-based biomarkers, pyrrole-protein adducts, for assessing and monitoring PA-ILI (Papers 2, 4-8; Abstracts 2, 4 in Part C), and for the first time identified pyrrole-haemoglobin adducts, which possess higher level and longer persistence in blood, as a more suitable biomarker (Papers 5, 7; Abstract 2 in Part C). We also demonstrated that ATP synthase subunit beta (ATP5B) was one of the proteins bound to dehydro-PAs and the formation of pyrrole-ATP5B adduct caused liver damages leading to PA-ILI (Papers 1, 3 in Part C). To date, the most part of the results of Objective 1 has been published (Papers 1-9 in Part C) and reported in conferences (Abstracts 1-2, 4 in Part C). Objective 2: Currently, supportive and symptomatic treatments are the mainstay in clinical management of PA-ILI. However, it has been reported that after receiving such treatments, over half of patients died or developed chronic liver diseases, and progressive liver fibrosis is a severe health problem with no effective treatment. In the early stage of liver fibrosis, there are often no apparent symptoms, while, under further development of fibrosis, signs and symptoms become apparent. Without treatment, liver fibrosis may further develop into cirrhosis, liver failure and/or cancer. Therefore, therapeutic strategies targeting PA-ILI, especially PA-induced liver fibrosis, are urgently required. Herbal medicines and their derived bioactive components have been widely embraced in the treatment of liver fibrosis. Based on our developed PA-induced progressive liver fibrosis rat model, anti-fibrotic effects of Fuzheng Huayu capsule (FZHY), a TCM proprietary product, with one dosage regimen (202.5 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks), salvianolic acid B (SalB) from Danshen with two dosage regiments (20 mg/kg/day or 20 mg/kg twice a day for 2 weeks), and baicalein (BAI) from Huangqin with two dosage regiments (40 mg/kg/day or 40 mg/kg twice a day for 2 weeks) treating from day 15 after the second dose of RTS, have been evaluated. They all inhibited the development of RTS-induced liver fibrosis, evidenced by the significant reduction of collagen area in liver sections and hepatic hydroxyproline content (the two well-established fibrotic biomarkers) in the treated rats. FZHY showed better anti-fibrotic effect than other two agents, and SalB twice-daily dosage regimen exerted a stronger anti-fibrotic effect than its once-daily dosage regimen. Further mechanistic studies indicated that FZHY and BAI but not SalB alleviated RTS-induced liver fibrosis via reduction of protein expression of TGF-β1 and inhibition of activation of hepatic stellate cells. In addition, BAI down-regulated TIMP-1 expression, leading to the decrease in ECM synthesis and alleviation of RTS-induced liver fibrosis. In addition, all three agents significantly reduced protein expression of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, an inhibitor of fibrinolysis, in the liver of the model rats, indicating that the fibrinolytic activity contributed to their anti-fibrotic effects. Furthermore, using HPLC-MS analysis under positive ionization mode, a metabolomic approach has also been applied to explore the potential mechanisms of FZHY, BAI and SalB against RTS-induced liver fibrosis. Collectively, the results showed a clear separation in the score plot of principal component analysis (PCA) among control, model and FZHY treated groups. The significant elevation of phosphatidylcholines (PC) content in the model group was observed, suggesting that glycerophospholipid metabolism might be the most relevant pathway involved in RTS-induced liver fibrosis. Interestingly, the PC content was significantly reduced back to the normal level after FZHY treatment, illustrating that FZHY exerted its anti-fibrotic effect via balancing the disorder of glycerophospholipid metabolism. On the other hand, although BAI and SalB showed significant therapeutic effects against RTS-induced liver fibrosis, no clear separation was found between BAI/SalB treated and the model group in PCA analysis. Collectively, the metabolomic study provided the novel insights into the mechanisms of RTS-induced liver fibrosis and particularly elucidated the potential therapeutic basis of FZHY. The present findings highlighted the possibility of using FZHY, BAI and SalB as effective drugs for the treatment of RTS-induced liver fibrosis. Parts of the results have been reported in conferences (Abstracts 1, 3 in Part C), and two papers reporting these findings are currently under preparation.

14111816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111816.value: Our findings for the first time provided a comprehensive information on the disease progression from PA-induced acute liver injury to PA-induced liver fibrosis. We have established rat models of acute resolving liver injury and chronic progressive liver fibrosis induced by RTS, a well-known hepatotoxic PA, and also explored changes in cellular and molecular biomarkers that may shed a light to underlying the mechanisms, including myofibroblast activation, TGF-1/Smad3 and Akt signaling, and changes in MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio in the liver (Paper 9; Abstract 1 in Part C). We have developed pyrrole-protein adducts, especially pyrrole-hemoglobin adducts, as novel, sensitive and specific exposing causal biomarkers for identifying and assessing liver injury induced by both PAs and PA N-oxides (Papers 2, 4-8; Abstracts 2, 4 in Part C). We also for the first time identified pyrrole-ATP5B adduct in RTS treated animal and cell models and revealed its important impact on PA-ILI (Papers 1, 3 in Part C). We investigated the anti-fibrotic effects of FZHY (Fuzheng Huayu capsule, a TCM proprietary product commonly used in China), BAI (salvianolic acid B Danshen) and SalB (baicalein from Huangqin) on RTS-induced liver fibrosis, and delineated their underlying mechanism (Abstracts 1, 3 in Part C). The obtained results demonstrated that FZHY and BAI exerted their anti-fibrotic effects via inhibiting TGF-β1 and α-SMA expression. BAI down-regulated the TIMP-1 expression, leading to the decrease in ECM synthesis and the alleviation of RTS-induced liver fibrosis. Moreover, FZHY, BAI and SalB reduced the expression of PAI-1, which could promote fibrinolysis, contributing to their anti-fibrotic effects. In addition, the metabolomic study suggested that glycerophospholipid metabolism also played an important role in the inhibitory effect of FZHY on RTS-induced liver fibrosis. The results demonstrated the therapeutic potential of these herbal medicines and/or their derived components for PA-induced liver fibrosis.

14111816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111816.value: Despite the evidence obtained from the present project shows that myofibroblastic activation, TGF-1/Smad3 and Akt signalling, and changes in MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio in the liver are all induced by RTS treatment, they are likely indirect targets of RTS. It remains elusive with what are the primary molecular targets in the liver that directly mediate RTS-induced toxicity, how cellular damage, inflammation, and fibrosis are subsequently caused, and how they can be effectively prevented. In addition, in the present project, we only used RTS as a representative PA, whether other types of PAs/PA N-oxides or mixed PAs/PA N-oxides, such as PA/PA N-oxides-containing herbal medicines, also shared similar pathological manifestations and toxic mechanisms still requires further investigation. Our metabolomics results indicate that there is no clear separation between BAI-/SalB-treated and model groups in PCA analysis. This might be due to that the present metabolomic study was only conducted under positive ionization mode using rat plasma samples. Therefore, other biological specimens such as rat urine samples and positive/negative ionization mode should be considered for further metabolomic studies to provide more information to discriminate different groups and further explore the detailed mechanisms underlying PA-induced liver fibrosis and the therapeutic effects of tested anti-fibrotic agents.

14111816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111816.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are natural toxins widely present in ~3% flowering plants. Humans are readily exposed to PAs by ingestion of PA-containing herbal products, i.e. herbal remedies, or PA-contaminated foodstuffs, such as wheat, honey, etc. Acute and subacute PA intoxication is known as hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (HSOS) with typical symptoms of hepatomegaly, jaundice, and ascites. With supportive and symptomatic treatment, PA-induced HSOS may further progress to chronic liver diseases, such as liver fibrosis. However, the current knowledge on the disease progression of PA-induced liver fibrosis and potential therapeutic treatment is very limited. We established rat models of acute resolving liver injury and chronic progressive liver fibrosis induced by retrorsine, a representative hepatotoxic PA. These models resemble the pathological manifestations observed in patients with PA-induced liver injury. We studied mechanisms underlying PA-induced regressive or progressive liver fibrosis and found the involvement of myofibroblast activation, TGF-1/Smad3 and Akt signaling, and changes in MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio in the liver. Fuzheng Huayu capsule, salvianolic acid B, and baicalein have been demonstrated effective for the treatment of PA-induced liver fibrosis via several pathways, including inhibiting TGF-β1 and α-SMA expression and promoting fibrinolysis. The results obtained will facilitate better clinical management of PA-induced liver injury.

14111916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111916.value: Congenial heart disease (CHD) is one of the leading causes of infant mortality. Importantly, maternal diabetes is a significant risk factor for CHD as infants of diabetic mothers have a fivefold increase in risk of malformation and dysfunction of the heart compared to that of the normoglycemic mothers. To date, pre/postnatal analysis of congenital heart anomalies is mainly restricted to major cardiac structures. Recent studies in chick and mouse embryos reveal that maternal hyperglycemia leads to reduced blood vessel formation during early heart development. Therefore, in this proposal, we will investigate whether hyperglycemia affects development of the early heart progenitors in humans. Our preliminary data by genome-wide RNA-sequencing of human fetal heart samples demonstrate that hyperglycemia reduced expression of genes specific for the Isl1+ heart progenitors, cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle and endothelial cells at gestation week 11, suggesting an overall disturbance in cardiogenesis. In addition, high glucose condition also reduced %Isl1 derivatives following direct differentiation in vitro as well as following transplantation of the lineage-tracing Isl1-Cre human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) into the hyperglycemic db/db mice compared to that of the normoglycemic db/m+ mice. Furthermore, we also observed a global reduction, irrespective of specific promoters, in both repressive and active histone marks in the human multipotent Isl1+ heart progenitors under hyperglycemic condition. We, therefore, hypothesize that hyperglycemia reduced the availability and possibly cell fate commitment of the Isl1+ heart progenitors during early human heart development. In this proposal, we plan to test our hypothesis using both human fetal heart and hESC models: we will first examine if hyperglycemia reduces survival (Aim 1) and differentiation (Aim 2) of the human Isl1+ heart progenitors. We will then examine the underlying molecular mechanisms by which hyperglycemia disturbs survival and differentiation of the Isl1+ progenitors (Aim 3). 14112916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14112916.value: Background Intracranial arterial stenosis (ICAS) is a major cause of ischemic stroke and carries a high risk of recurrence. ICAS is considered as a dynamic disease that may progress or regress, and its progression is associated with increased cerebrovascular risk. To understand factors that may affect evolution of ICAS may help delineate secondary stroke prevention strategies. Recently, the Ring Finger protein 213 gene polymorphism (RNF213 c.14576G>A), a susceptibility locus for moyamoya disease (MMD) in East Asians, was found to be present in 22-24% of non-MMD intracranial stenosis, indicating it may be a robust genetic risk factor for ICAS. Besides, high resolution Magnetic Resonance Imaging (HRMRI) has emerged as a promising technique to reliably visualize intracranial vessel wall pathologies, making it possible to quantify the plaque components which may be important markers in defining plaque vulnerability. However, the prospective data of HRMRI on intracranial atherosclerotic plaque progression and clinical correlation is lacking. Therefore, we hypothesized that intracranial arterial stenosis in patients carrying RNF213 c.14576G>A polymorphism will more likely to progress on HRMRI than patients without RNF213 c.14576G>A polymorphism, while on active medical treatment. Objective To evaluate the evolution of ICAS by serial HR-MRI vessel wall imaging and MR angiogram (MRA) in stroke patients with and without RNF213 genetic variant(s). Methods This is a prospective, academic-initiated study. A total of 120 consecutive patients due to acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) events within 2 weeks of symptom onset, with ≥50% MCA (M1-M2 segment) stenosis identified on MRA, will be recruited. Patients will receive 2 HR MRI+MRA scans at baseline and at 12 months, respectively. Temporal changes of atherosclerotic plaque area will be evaluated and stratified into 1) Progressive (plaque burden increase >5%); 2) Quiescent (plaque burden ±5%); and 3) Regressive (plaque burden reduce <5%). Other imaging outcomes such as progression of stenosis on MRA and clinical outcomes will also be recorded during 1-year follow up. Effect of RNF213 gene variants including c.14576G>A variant on the evolution of ICAS will be analyzed. Significance (1) Provide prospective data on the effect of RNF213 c.14576G>A polymorphism on the progression on vessel and luminal stenosis. (2) Document the natural history of progression of HRMRI in ICAS patient while on active medical treatment. (3) Explore any correlation between clinical event and progression of HRMRI. (4) Establish a new biomarker to identify high-risk stroke patient subset, which may help delineate secondary stroke prevention strategies. 研究背景及目的 在中國，顱內大動脈粥樣硬化性狹窄是缺血性腦中風及短暫性腦缺血（小中風）的主要病因。有顱內大動脈狹窄的病人再次發生心腦血管事件的風險增高。研究表明，顱內大血管狹窄為一項動態變化的損害，體現為進展，穩定或逆轉，其中進展的動脈狹窄則與腦血管事件的風險上升密切相關。此外，煙霧病的易感基因－RNF213基因突變，近來研究發現其也存在於22-24%的非煙霧病所致顱內大動脈狹窄中，提示其可能為顱內大動脈狹窄的一項基因學風險指標。高分辨率磁力共振成像技術是一種創新的同步化成像序列，可以同時評價顱內大動脈粥樣硬化性的狹窄程度和斑塊型態；磁力共振血管成像是一種無需使用顯影劑的無創傷的血管檢查，臨床上經常用於檢查中風患者的腦動脈情況，其檢查結果可用於患者的風險評估、治療選擇以及臨床結果的預測。基於以上研究背景，我們旨在運用高分辨率磁力共振成像及磁力共振血管成像技術動態觀察顱內大動脈狹窄在有或無RNF213基因突變的腦中風病人的演化情況，以確立一項新的篩查高風險腦中風人群的生物學指標。 研究方法 我們將誠邀約120位18歲或以上、發生缺血性腦中風或短暫性腦缺血發作的7天內、且已由腦部磁力共振成像掃描確定顱內動脈狹窄的患者參加研究。患者將在入組後兩週內及1年隨訪時接受兩次磁力共振掃描，並在入組後抽取靜脈血以作RNF213基因檢測。我們將分析在有或無RNF213基因突變的患者中，其顱內大動脈狹窄演化情況的差異，用以確立一項新的篩查高風險腦中風人群的生物學指標。

14113316.value: 此研究計劃的目標是探討血小板與腦神經糖脂的相互作用之分子機制，以及這個相互作用在創傷性腦損傷 (TBI) 和阿茲海默症(AD) 中的神經炎症和神經保護之角色。 神經炎症是在中樞神經系統 (CNS) 中，伴隨許多類型的神經系統疾病的一個多病理過程。神經炎症被認為是促成TBI和AD的原因；然而，科學界還未清楚知道在沒有感染的情況下，CNS炎症是如何被啟動的。據認為，CNS炎症是由免疫細胞（例如微膠細胞）導致神經元損害而引發，但尚未有研究解釋當中的機制。 神經細胞與腦毛細血管的內皮細胞互連，形成一個神經血管單位。當血腦屏障被破壞時，不同類型的血細胞會直接與神經細胞產生作用，從而發展出CNS炎症。血小板是數量極多的血細胞，比白血球數量多出100倍。血小板能夠立即對血管損傷作出反應，但我們還不知道它在神經退化性疾病中之角色。被活化的血小板能夠分泌許多物質(例如血小板活化因子(PAF) 和血清素)，這些物質可能擁有潛在促進炎症和提高神經元的存活的能力。 早前我們從研究中發現，神經抗去垢劑膜(脂筏)中的神經糖脂能夠引起大規模的血小板活化或脫顆粒作用。血小板可以在CNS炎症中辨認出腦神經節苷脂GT1b和GQ。因此，我們用了正常老鼠與缺乏ST3-Gal V (ST3KO) 老鼠來比較兩者之CNS發炎反應 (ST3-Gal V是腦部中主要的神經節苷脂)。結果發現，在TBI後的ST3KO 老鼠，比TBI後的正常老鼠體內的微膠細胞的活化程度，以及CNS 白血球滲入水平為低。而在損傷的區域中，ST3KO 老鼠比正常老鼠失去更多神經元。另一方面，我們發現不論在正常老鼠或ST3KO 老鼠體內，PAF受體拮抗劑均能夠降低外圍巨噬細胞滲入和微膠細胞的活化程度。這表示在 TBI期間，血小板衍生的PAF可引致CNS炎症。最後，與血小板共培養的神經元有更強的存活能力和有更多的軸突生長。 此專題研究能進一步調查血小板在神經元損傷後所誘發的急性炎症，還有促進神經細胞存活的角色。而血小板與脂筏的相互作用，對於治療TBI和AD，也有著長遠的潛在影響。

14113316.label: Realisation of objectives
14113316.value: The purpose of this project is the investigation of molecular mechanisms during the early events of the initiation of neuroinflammation during traumatic brain injury (TBI), epilepsy, and Alzheimer’s diseases (AD). The project is based on our previous discovery that platelets promote neuroinflammation by directly recognizing the brain-specific glycolipids that are expressed on the surface of neuronal cells. We found that several neuron-specific glycolipids (gangliosides GT1b and GQ1b) that were integrated into dense detergent-resistant membrane domains (also referred to as lipid rafts) were directly recognized by platelets. The interaction of platelets with these neuronal lipid rafts (NLRs) resulted in platelet degranulation and the instant release of several proinflammatory mediators (e.g. platelet-activating factor, PAF) and neurotransmitters (e.g. serotonin). In this proposal, we investigated interactions of NLR-activated platelets with microglia/macrophages and neurons in mouse models of TBI, epilepsy (pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced seizures), and AD (5XFAD mice). We also used st3gal5 (ST3) – deficient mice that lack major brain-specific gangliosides. In addition to the regulation of neuroinflammation when platelets interact with microglia/macrophages and cause activation of these cells in the CNS, platelets can directly interact with neuronal cells in the CNS and modulate their functions, gene expression profile, and electric activity, which was investigated in details using the models of TBI and PTZ-induced seizures. The main hypothesis of the study remained the same during the whole period (36 months) of the project: the interaction of platelets with brain-specific glycolipids localized within neuronal lipid rafts results in the release of several platelet-derived inflammatory mediators (e.g., PAF) and neurotransmitters (e.g., serotonin) that initiate neuroinflammation, decrease hemorrhage, modulate neuronal functions and promote neuronal repair. This hypothesis was investigated through three specific aims: 1) how interactions of platelets with NLR affect neuroinflammation in TBI; 2) how interactions of platelets with NLR affect neuronal functions; 3) how interactions of platelets with NLR regulate neuroinflammation and neuronal functions during AD. We received a substantial amount of new data and fully accomplished Aim 1, Aim2, and Aim 3 to 100%. In Aim 1, we established that during TBI platelet-derived serotonin modulate neuronal synaptic plasticity while platelet-activating factor (PAF) mediate neuroinflammation. Specifically, we found that PAF mediated neuroinflammation, while 5HT – neuronal plasticity and repair. The results were published in Brain Behavior and Immunity (IF=6.3, Research Output#1). In Aim 2, we found that upon the interaction of platelets with neuronal lipid rafts, platelet-derived serotonin and other mediators directly stimulated neuronal electric and synaptic activity and oxidative stress. This was critical for the development of PTZ-induced and post-traumatic epileptic seizures. The results were published in Progress in Neurobiology (IF=10.7, Research Output#5). Besides, we found that ST3-deficient mice have many psychoneuroimmunological and behavior problems and showed signs of demyelination, which was described in our recently submitted original research article (see Research Output#7). In Aim 3, we crossed ST3-deficient mice with 5XFAD transgenic mice (a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease) and found that ST3-deficient 5XFAD mice have a reduced level of amyloid depositions, normal expression of synaptic markers, no neuronal loss and brain atrophy, and decreased level of neuroinflammation. Moreover, treatment of WT 5XFAD mice with sialic acid-specific lectin Lymus Flavis agglutinin (LFA) improved AD pathology. Thus, we found that neuronal lipid rafts play an important role in the binding of amyloid fragments and the development of AD. The results were published in Neurobiology of Aging (IF=4.5, Research Output#3; we also filed US patent to use Lymus Flavis agglutinin (LFA) for AD treatment, see Research Output section). We also created PF4-APP transgenic mice with expression of human APP in platelets, but we did not find a stable expression of short platelet-derived APP fragments, indicating a different type of processing of amyloid in the platelets. This will require future investigation, which will be reflected in our further grant research proposal.

14113316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113316.value: As a result of the realization of this project, we published three original research articles in top academic journals in the field: Brain Behavior and Immunity (IF=6.3, Research Output#1, Part C.8. Major findings: 1) Glycolipid-deficient mice exhibit deficits in neuronal function after injury. 2) Brain glycolipids induce platelet activation after traumatic brain injury. 3) Platelet-derived serotonin and platelet-activating factor modulate neuroinflammation after injury. 4) Platelets contribute to neuronal rewiring and repair after injury), Progress in Neurobiology (IF=10.7, Research Output#5, Part C.8. Major findings: 1) Platelets substantially contribute to the severity of epileptic seizures. 2) During epileptic seizures, platelets enter CNS and secrete serotonin. 3) Platelet-derived serotonin enhances neuronal electric activity during seizures. 4) Platelets stimulate neuronal synaptic activity and contribute to neuroinflammation. 5) Platelets induce oxidative stress in neurons during epileptic seizures), and Neurobiology of Aging (IF=4.5, Research Output#3, Part C.8. Major findings: 1) Brain ganglioside-deficient ST3−/− 5XFAD mice do not have CNS amyloid depositions. 2) ST3−/− 5XFAD mice do not have Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related neuroinflammation. 3) ST3−/− 5XFAD mice do not have brain atrophy, neuronal loss, or synaptic dysfunctions. 4) ST3−/− 5XFAD mice perform normally in a cognitive test. 5) Treatment of WT 5XFAD mice with sialic acid-specific lectin improved AD pathology). Also, we published two peer-reviewed review papers in Frontiers in Immunology (IF=6.4, Research Output#2, Part C.8) and in Frontiers of Cellular Neuroscience (IF=4.6, Research Output#4, Part C.8). We also published one methodological book chapter (Indexed in Pubmed and WoS databases, Research Output# 6, Part C.8). Finally, one original research paper was submitted in the Journal of Affective Disorders (IF=4.5, Research Output#7, see the attached manuscript in Part C.8. Major findings: 1) Both sexes of ST3−/− mice show motor and cognitive deficits, anxiogenic changes. 2) Male ST3−/− mice display aggressiveness, hyperactivity, and signs of impulsivity. 3) ST3−/− mice show downregulation of myelin marker PLP-1 and altered insulin receptors (IRA and IRB) expression. 4) Interleukin-1β is over-expressed in brain and spleen in both sexes of ST3−/− mice. 5) LPS induces in mutants sex-related abnormalities in social behavior and inflammation). The results from the grant were presented in 13 recognized international research conferences over in the period from 2017 till 2020 (see Part C.9). Two international postgraduate students accomplished their Ph.D. programs (see Part C.10), two important international collaborations were established with Netherland and Germany, and one US patent was filed (see Part C.11).

14113316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113316.value: The most important continuation of this project that would have a high impact is the role of platelets in the pathology of Alzheimer's disease (AD). In our current project, we found that AD pathology (e.g. amyloid deposition) was substantially reduced in the brain of ST3-deficient mice. However, it is not clear was it because ST3-deficient mice have decreased level of neuronal lipid rafts that serves as an anchor point for amyloid depositions, or due to decreased level of platelet activation with neuronal lipid rafts (NLR). Indeed, we found that platelets from 5XFAD mice and AD patients exhibit activated phenotype (unpublished), but the exact role of this activation is not well understood. The role of platelet-derived amyloid for AD pathology will be further investigated making a new generation of transgenic mice where platelets will overexpress human mutated amyloid under platelet-specific PF4 promoter. We will also investigate the role of platelet-derived factors serotonin and platelet-activating factor (PAF) in AD pathology. Finally, it will be very interesting to know whether platelets could induce neuronal oxidative stress and enhance electric activity as we observed for the pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced seizure model. All these questions will be addressed in the new grant research proposal.

14113316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113316.value: The purpose of this project is the investigation of human diseases traumatic brain injury (TBI), epilepsy, and Alzheimer’s diseases (AD) using animal models. We found that blood cells called thrombocytes (also known as platelets) could recognize specific lipids in the area around brain blood vessels. During traumatic brain injury blood vessels become damaged and platelets become directly activated by these brain lipids. This activation results in the secretion of specific molecules by thrombocytes that induce inflammation, restrict the area of brain damage and promote neuronal repair near the trauma site. Platelets also stimulated neuronal activity and contributed to the development of trauma-associated epileptic seizures. Finally, we found that brain lipids were critical for the accumulation of aggregated proteins during AD pathology. Thus, the results from this proposal could be used for understanding the basic mechanisms of the pathology of neurological diseases and the development of future therapies of TBI, AD, and epilepsy.

14116916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116916.value: Our long-term goal is to elucidate the regulatory process of the enzymatic degradation of different lignocellulosic substrates by the model mushroom Coprinopsis cinerea . The specific aims are to (1) identify RNA editing sites involved in lignin degradation regulation on different substrates or inducers in Coprinopsis cinerea by in silico analyses, (2) confirm the RNA editing sites of transcription factors by RT-PCR and link transcription factors with CAZymes expressions and (3) confirm the regulatory relationship between selected transcription factors and CAZymes by knocking out these transcrtiption factor genes and test the changes of CAZymes expression under control. C. cinerea is a model organism in studies of homobasidiomycetes biology for its short life cycle under laboratory conditions. This fungus has been a target to study carbohydrate active enzymes (CAZymes) that take part in lignocellulose degradation, an important step in biomass to biofuel process. We know little about the regulation of CAZymes production and signal transduction pathways in fungi growing on different lignocellulosic substrates. Supported by next generation sequencing, there are many studies on the transcriptome studies of mushroom forming fungi. Our laboratory has studied the biology of fungi for more than 15 years. We have recently obtained RNA-seq gene expression profiles of 46 single spore isolates of C. cinerea and conducted eQTL analysis. Unlike general belief that gene expression varies with different genotypes of the transcription factors, we could not observe SNPs in transcription factors that associate with CAZymes expression . On the other hand, we found that gene expression is associated with the RNA editing sites on several transcription factors. Based on this observation, we propose to (a) screen TFs in silico to identify the transcription factors involved in C. cinerea CAZymes expression, (b) grow C. cinerea on different substrates to see if transcription factor RNA editing varies with different substrates, and (c) compare the RNA editing levels with CAZyme gene expression profiles. RNA editing sites in transcription factor genes and other regions important in substrate detection and CAZymes production will be revealed. To our knowledge, this would be the first functional study on RNA editing sites for roles in CAZymes production in mushroom forming fungi. Identification and functional characterization of regulators in CAZymes production will contribute to our understanding of the fungal lignocellulose degradation with potentials to benefit enzyme production industry. 我們的長期目標是通過模型蘑菇Coprinopsis cinerea 闡明不同木質基材的酶降解的監管過程。具體目標是：（1）識別由電腦分析涉及對Coprinopsis灰黴病不同基質，或誘導木質素降解調節的RNA編輯位點，（2）通過RT-PCR確認轉錄因子的RNA編輯位點及鏈接轉錄因子與CAZymes表達模式（3）通過敲除選出的轉錄因子以確定這些轉錄因子和CAZymes之間的關係及其監管和控制測試CAZymes表達的變化。 在實驗室條件下，C. cinerea的生命週期短，是homobasidiomycetes生物學研究模式。這種真菌已經是目標，研究碳水化合物活性酶的參與降解木質纖維素（CAZymes），生物質的重要一步生物燃料的過程。我們不太清楚CAZymes生產和信號轉導通路對真菌在不同的木質纖維襯底上生長的調節。通過新一代測序，蘑菇形成真菌的轉錄組有很多研究。我們的實驗室已經研究真菌生物學超過15年。我們最近獲得的RNA-SEQ基因表達譜用於C. cinerea 的46個單孢子及eQTL分析。有別於一般認為基因表達的轉錄因子根據不同基因型各不相同，我們並未發現與CAZymes關聯表達的轉錄因子SNP。另一方面，我們發現基因表達與幾種轉錄因子的RNA編輯位點相關聯。基於這種觀察，我們建議（a）用電腦鍳定參與C. cinerea CAZymes表達的轉錄因子，(b)利用生長在不同基質的C. cinerea鑒定轉錄因子的RNA編輯因應不同基質而變化，和（c）比較CAZyme基因表達譜與RNA編輯的水平。轉錄因子基因及其隣近序列對CAZymes生產重要的RNA編輯位點便可測知。據我們了解，這將是在蘑菇形成真菌CAZymes生產表達控制因子的RNA編輯作用的第一個功能性研究。鑑定與CAZymes生產的功能研究將有助於我們了解真菌降解木質纖維素酶，並且可以幫助酶生產工業。

14116916.label: Realisation of objectives
14116916.value: 1. To identify RNA editing sites involved in lignin degradation regulation on different substrates or inducers in Coprinopsis cinerea by in silico analyses We have performed experiments with CAZyme inducer, ABTS [2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid)] and low temperature. Both ABTS and low environmental temperature could increase the laccase activity in Coprinopsis cinerea. More importantly, these two inducers represent two categories, chemical and physical inducers, separately. We cultured the Coprinopsis cinerea mycelium in 3 groups: control group, ABTS group (ABTS was added in the agar medium) and LT group (under low temperature condition). We extracted crude laccases from the freshly collected mycelium The activity of laccase was assayed spectrophotometrically by monitoring the absorbance increase from oxidation of ABTS at 420 nm. Normalized by dry weight, the laccase activity of ABTS-treated group is about 7.6 times higher than the control group, while the low-temperature-treated group is about 1.4 times higher than the control group. We then performed the whole mRNA sequencing by illumina Hi-seq for the two laccase-induced groups and the control group, 3 samples in each group. We developed the RNA editing sites prediction pipeline, and trained this pipeline with three sets of published data. RNA editing candidates were called using the python script REDItoolBlatCorrection.py and REDItoolDnaRna.py in REDItools v1.0.4 (Picardi and Pesole, 2013) with the following cut-off: (i) to minimise the false discovery caused by sequencing and mapping error, the minimum reads quality and mapping quality of are set to 25 in both DNA and RNA, and multi hit reads are excluded; (ii) to ensure the significance of occurrence of editing events, at least 3 reads should support the variant, with the minimum frequency of 3% and minimum coverage of 10 reads; (iii) exclude positions with changes in DNA-seq to avoid false positive events resulted from genome variants; (iv) exclude positions near splice site within 4 bases to avoid the mismatch caused by misalignment of RNA; (v) to further minimise the false discovery rate, editing events should present in at least 2 biological samples of all samples of each dataset. In this study, “RNA editing site” refers to the location of RNA editing, while “RNA editing event” indicates the occurrence of RNA editing in biological samples. A total of 124 RNA editing sites and 1107 RNA editing events were identified in four developmental paths. The RNA editome in mycelium of C. cinerea was very different from those Ascomycetes fungi. The majority of RNA editing events had editing levels < 20 %, and the editing level remained constant and relatively low. T-to-C substitution took up over 55 % of the editing events. 2. To confirm the RNA editing sites of transcription factors by RT-PCR and link transcription factors with CAZymes expressions cDNA was synthesised from the total RNA with anchored-oligo(dT)18 primer and random hexamer primer using Transcriptor First Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit (Roche, Germany). The template-primer mix was denaturised at 65 °C, and the RT reaction was incubated as follows: 10 min at 25 °C, 30 min at 55 °C and 5 min at 85 °C. 1 µg of RNA was input into each 20 µl reverse transcription reaction. PCR amplification of RNA editing containing sequence were performed by using cDNA and gDNA as templates with KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix PCR kit (Roche, Germany) and the following program: 95 °C for 3 min, followed by 30 cycles 98 °C for 20 sec, 65 °C for 20 sec, and 72 °C for 15 sec, and 72 °C for 1 min. PCR products were detected on 1.5 % agarose gel and purified with MEGA quick-spin Plus Fragment DNA Purification Kit (MEGA, Korea). Sanger sequencing on PCR products of DNA and cDNA were performed by BGI. We have performed RT-PCR and sanger sequencing for more than 60 sites. But due to the sensitivity limitation of sanger sequencing technology, all the tested sites cannot be validated with high confidence. In order to test the efficacy of our methodology, we performed the above prediction and validation procedures with another dataset, which included biological triplicates of 4 developmental stages with 12 transcriptomes in total. 254 RNA editing candidate sites and 324 candidate events were called for this dataset. After RT-PCR and sanger sequencing for more than 60 sites, we finally confirmed that 2 RNA editing sites. Although the validation rate is low, the sanger sequencing is the Gold-standard for testing the existence of RNA editing events. Since we have successfully validated 2 RNA editing sites in at least more than 3 samples, we cannot exclude the existence of non-A-to-I RNA editing events. This is a very important finding in fungal biology, and we will further validate more RNA editing sites, to convince the reviewers with more data. 3. To confirm the regulatory relationship between selected transcription factors and CAZymes by knocking out these transcription factor genes and test the changes of CAZymes expression under control Since we could not validated any RNA editing sites in transcription factors, we moved on to elucidate the regulatory relationship between laccases and differentially expressed TFs and kinases. First, we found that both ABTS and low temperature could promote laccase activity, but they induced different sets of laccases. ABTS treatment increased the expression level of laccase 3_1 (CC1G_02449) by 23.89 times, laccase 1 (CC1G_09614) by 4.29 times, and laccase 5_2 (CC1G_06019) by 2.46 times. On the other hand, laccase 7_1(CC1G_09611), laccase 7_2(CC1G_09609), laccase 4 (CC1G_05972), laccase 3_2 (CC1G_03940) were down regulated by 2.21 to 7.68 times lower than control group. In the low-temperature group, laccase 8 (CC1G_05965) and laccase 5_1 (CC1G_00690) were increasingly expressed by 2.20 and 2.15 times, respectively. CC1G_06686 is a transcription factor (TF)with Fungal Zn(2)-Cys(6) binuclear cluster domain. Its expression was down-regulated by 148.11 times in ABTS group, but up-regulated by 2.02 times in LT group. There were another 3 TFs with reverse expression level under chemical and physical stimulations, they are CC1G_00225, CC1G_04998, CC1G_13750. There were no commonly up-regulated TFs under the two conditions, while there were 3 commonly down-regulated TFs. On the contrary, there are 19 TFs, 23 kinases specifically differentially expressed in ABTS group, and 10 TFs, 18 kinases in LT group. Most DEG from other functional groups were also uniquely regulated under the two conditions. It implied that different sets of signal transduction pathways were used to regulate different sets of laccases. Funk1 group of kinases were enriched (28 out of 52 kinases) in the DEG, and the expression changes were very significant. Funk1 are kinases only found in fungi, their functions were poorly characterized previously. The enrichment of Funk1 implied that they took important role in regulating secreted enzymes under different environmental conditions.

14116916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116916.value: The project explored the mechanism of laccase induction in Coprinopsis cinerea. The major finding is that chemical and physical stimulations affected different sets of genes and laccases. In terms of differentially-expressed-genes, we have identified 519 up-regulated and 1101 down-regulated genes, under ABTS treatment; while 603 up-regulated and 780 down-regulated genes, under low-temperature treatment. Most of the DEG are uniquely regulated under the two conditions. It implied that different sets of regulators were used to control different sets of laccases. Funk1 group of kinases were enriched (28 out of 52 kinases) in the DEG. Funk1 are kinases identified in fungi, their functions were poorly characterized previously. The enrichment of Funk1 during laccase induction implied that Funk1 took important role in regulating secreted enzymes under different environmental conditions. The pipeline developed to identify and validate the RNA editing sites by this project succeed in other transcriptome studies. We have successfully predicted and confirmed the existence of non-A-to-I RNA editing sites in another set of samples of the same strain. The transcriptomic analysis pipeline developed by this project was also applied in analysing another dataset, which focuses on transcriptomic changes during developmental path differentiation in Coprinopsis cinerea. The manuscript is submitted and under review.

14116916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116916.value: We have successfully predicted and confirmed the existence of non-A-to-I RNA editing sites using the method developed by this project. The discovery of the two RNA editing sites is a very important finding, since the non-A-to-I RNA editing events are rarely reported and always filtered away as noise. However, the low discovery rate suggests that RNA editing outcomes are highly efficient, and editing level up to 20% is already enough to make impacts. We should investigate its induction mechanism in greater details. When and where can we find RNA editing events? To answer this question, more experiments and more samples must be collected, and technology with higher resolution and higher sensitivity, e.g. single-cell sequencing and dd-PCR should be used. From our unsuccessful experiences, it seems that RNA editing events exist in a short time, and not in all cells. Research in this direction may lead us to identify a high-efficiency regulating mechanism to regulate the protein translation at RNA level. The importance of RNA editing mechanisms of fungi may be equivalent to nervous systems of animals

14116916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116916.value: The project explored the mechanism of laccase induction in mushroom forming fungi. We found that both chemical and physical stimulations could increase laccases activity in mycelium. We further investigated which laccases increased and how they were regulated. Surprisingly, the laccases induced by the two types of stimulations were totally different. Besides, most of the differentially expressed genes are also uniquely regulated under the two conditions. It implied that different sets of signal transduction pathways were recruited to regulate different sets of laccases. Funk1 group of kinases were enriched (28 out of 52 kinases) in the DEG. Funk1 are kinases found only in fungi. Their functions have been poorly characterized. The enrichment of Funk1 implied that they play important roles in regulating secreted enzymes under different environmental conditions. We confirmed the existence of 2 non-A-to-I RNA editing sites, and will test more predicted editing sites in the future.

14117316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117316.value: 鼻咽癌（NPC）與EB病毒感染密切相關。由EBV病毒編碼的LMP1具有調節多種信號通路和下遊靶蛋白表達的能力，在鼻咽癌發生發展中發揮重要的作用。我們的團隊長期致力於研究LMP1在鼻咽癌發生發展中的功能。目前，我們已確定LMP1的多種致癌特性，包括促進細胞增長、轉化、遷移、侵襲、有氧糖酵解和代謝的再編程。我們的初步研究成果表明，LMP1可促進脂肪酸合成。SREBP是脂肪生成的主要調節因子。LMP1可誘導表達和激活SREBP及其下遊蛋白：脂肪酸合酶（FASN）和ATP檸檬酸裂解酶（ACLY）。我們還觀察到在表達LMP1的上皮細胞中，細胞內脂肪酸和脂滴的濃度增加。有趣的是，在表達LMP1的上皮細胞中，SREBP1抑製劑（樺木醇）能顯著降低細胞增殖速度。我們同時發現，EB病毒感染的鼻咽癌細胞系和異種移植物高表達SREBP1和FASN。在鼻咽癌組織標本中，我們發現成熟SREBP1的表達，同時FASN與LMP1的表達顯著正相關。此外，在EB病毒感染的細胞中，siRNA介導的LMP1下調導致SREBP1活性降低。我們推測LMP1激活SREBP1，誘導脂肪生成，從而促進腫瘤細胞的生長。 雖然脂肪合成功能增強是公認的癌癥標誌，但其調節及其重要性在癌癥的發展還沒有被充分認識。我們的研究首次證實病毒蛋白在SREBP1活化中發揮重要作用，並闡明LMP1誘導脂肪合成，這些結果有助於揭示分子間的相互作用和癌癥發展機制。由於異常的脂肪合成在正常細胞中並不常見，因此本研究擬針對脂肪合成可以提供一種新的鼻咽癌治療方法。 在本項研究中，我們將深入研究LMP1，SREBP1和FASN在鼻咽癌標本中的表達以及與臨床相關參數可能存在的關聯，並確認SREBP1介導的脂肪合成在鼻咽癌發展中發揮重要功能。此外，我們將全面研究由LMP1調節脂肪生成並促進細胞轉化的機制。為了進一步改良鼻咽癌治療方案，我們將評估脂肪合成抑製劑對鼻咽癌細胞的毒性和治療的增效作用。這項研究結果將促進我們對脂肪合成在癌癥發展中的的認識，同時有助於開發新型鼻咽癌療法，尤其是在EB病毒相關的癌癥中，可針對脂肪合成進行靶向治療。

14117316.label: Realisation of objectives
14117316.value: Persistent EBV latent infection plays a driver role in activating multiple cancer hallmarks during transformation and progression of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. As summarized in our recent review articles, modulating the activity of metabolic regulators and manipulating metabolic pathways by the latent protein LMP1 are importance in EBV carcinogenesis (Lo et al., Int J Cancer, 2017; Tsao et al., Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci. 2017). LMP1 has been found to negatively regulate AMPK activity by inhibiting DNA dependent protein kinase (DNA‐PK) phosphorylation and activity, thereby facilitating LMP1‐mediated glycolysis. In nasopharyngeal epithelial cells, we have previously found that LMP1 also promote aerobic glycolysis by promoting GLUT1 translocation to the plasma membrane, increasing the cellular uptake of glucose and glutamine, enhancing LDHA activity and lactate production, but reducing PK activity and the intracellular levels of pyruvate. Furthermore, we have further revealed activation of FGF2/FGFR1 signaling by LMP1 contributes to aerobic glycolysis and cellular transformation. In our recent whole-exome and whole genome studies on 111 and 70 NPC tumors respectively, we have consistently demonstrated the high expression of LMP1 in 25.7 to 32.8% of the cases by immunohistochemistry and RNA in-situ hybridization. Notably, overexpression of LMP1 is mutually exclusive with somatic alterations in NF-kappaB signaling pathways in both studies (Tsang et al., Semin Cancer Biol. 2020; Bruce et al., 2020). Interestingly, we have previously shown that LMP1 activates aerobic glycolysis and upregulates glucose transporter 1 (Glut-1) via the NF-kappaB signaling pathways. While the acquired mutations associated with PI3K/AKT/mTORC pathways, FGF/FGFR signaling and lipogenesis (e.g. SREBP1, FASN) are not common, the genomic findings may indicate LMP1 and dysregulation of NF-kappaB signaling play critical roles in aerobic glycolysis and metabolic reprogramming in NPC. In this project, we firstly explored the role of LMP1 in modulating the fatty acid synthetic pathway and inducing de novo lipogenesis, which is essential for cancer cell growth. As shown in our recent report (Lo et al, J Pathol, 2018), LMP1 increases SREBP1 expression and activity in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. By Luciferase promoter reporter assays and RT‐qPCR analysis, we proved that LMP1 upregulates SREBP1 at the transcriptional level. Furthermore, LMP1 also promotes SREBP1 maturation and activates the transcription of multiple SREBP1 target genes that are involved in lipogenesis, including FASN. In addition to proven the LMP1-induced FASN expression by qRT-PCR, Western blotting and imminuofluorescence staining, we also demonstrated the effect of LMP1 on phosphorylation of ACLY, enhancing its activity to produce acetyl-CoA for fatty acid synthesis. Using a [14C]acetate incorporation assay, we have demonstrated the ability of LMP1 to promote lipogenesis. Notably, silencing LMP1 in EBV‐infected NPC cells resulted in a reduction in FASN expression and lipogenesis. The high level of the precursor and mature forms of SREBP1 and FASN expression was demonstrated in the LMP-1 positive NPC cells and PDXs. The signification correlation of LMP1 and FASN expression (p=0.0003) in a cohort of NPC primary tumors was determined by immunohistochemistry. In two independent cohorts of NPC primary tumors, overexpression of FASN and LMP1 were shown to be significantly associated with poor overall and disease-free survival of the NPC patients (Lo et al. J. Pathol, 2018; Li et al, Nat Commun. 2017). Our functional study has revealed that LMP1‐induced lipogenesis was dependent on mTOR signaling. In the NPC cells treated with mTOR inhibitors (Torin1 and Torin2) and siRNAs targeting mTORC1 and mTORC2 signaling, significant reduction of SREBP1 maturation, FASN expression and lipogenesis were detected by Western blotting and [14C]Acetate incorporation assays. In addition to mTOR inhibition, we also demonstrated that suppression of PI3k/AKT signalling with inhibitor LY294002 in LMP-expressing NP cells leads to reduction of SREBP1 activity and FASN expression. The findings confirmed that Akt/mTOR signaling activated by LMP1 participates in SREBP1-mediated lipogenesis. In NPC cells, we have confirmed that LMP1 induced phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 and p70S6K, two established downstream targets of mTOR signaling. By using multiple LMP1 mutants and inhibitors for its downstream pathways, we revealed that C-terminal activating region 2 (CTAR2) of LMP1 was shown to be the key domain involved in mTORC1 activation, mainly through IKKβ-mediated phosphorylation of TSC2 (Lo et al, J Pathol, 2018, Zhang et al, J Virol., 2017). The findings indicate the involvement of activating NF-kappaB signals in LMP1-induced mTORC1 activation and SREBP1-mediated lipogenesis. Recently, we also we showed that LMP1 activates mTORC2 through an autocrine activation of IGF1R signaling. Blocking the IGF1-IGF1R signaling axis by neutralizing antibody or IGF1R inhibitor suppressed the activation of mTORC2/AKT signaling in NPC cells (Zhang et al. Oncogene, 2019). As PI3K-Akt, IGF1-IGF1R and NF-kappaB are major pathways engaged by LMP1, LMP1 induction of mTOR-SREBP-induced lipogenesis appears to be mediated through multiple downstream targets and/or signaling pathways. Since overexpression of LMP1 is found in ~30% of NPC, our genome sequencing studies suggest that the SREBP1-mediated lipogenesis is mainly induced by somatic alterations in NF-kappa pathways in the LMP1-negative cases (Tsang, Semin Cancer Biol. 2020; Bruce et al.,2020). The LMP1 induced de novo SREBP1‐mediated lipogenesis was shown to be essential for cancer growth. We found that treatment with SREBP1-specific inhibitors (luteolin and fatostatin) could effectively inhibit SREBP1 maturation and FASN expression and dampen lipogenesis in the LMP1-expressing NPC cells. Importantly, inhibition of fatty acid synthesis by luteolin or fatostatin significantly reduced the proliferation of these LMP1‐expressing cells. The in vivo effects of the inhibitors of lipogenesis were further investigated in the EBV-positive tumor cells in the nude mice models. In the mice implanted with NPC tumor cells, we observed a substantially lower tumor weights and smaller tumor sized after luteolin or fatostatin treatment compared with vehicle controls. The treatment also showed no noticeable weight loss or other side effects in the mice. By immunohistochemistry staining and histological investigations, we have found that blocking lipogenesis by the two SREBP inhibitors significantly inhibited cell proliferation, increased apoptosis and induced necrosis in NPC tumors. The findings implied that the inhibition of lipogenesis by luteolin and fatostatin causes cell apoptosis and necrosis, leading to tumor growth suppression. However, there are lack of SREBP1-specific inhibitors that are available for clinical trials in cancer patients. Interestingly, we have recently revealed that targeting PRMT5 in multiple in vivo and in vitro NPC models resulted in dramatic SREBP1 suppression (Bruce et. al. 2020). As multiple clinical trials for inhibitors targeting PRMT5 are ongoing in various types of human cancers, we then explored the antitumor effect of depletion of SREBP1 by PRMT5 inhibition in EBV-positive NPC cells. Our preliminary finding indicates that lipogenesis inhibition is a potential effective therapeutic strategy for patients with EBV-associated NPC. 14117316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117316.value: In our recent whole-exome/whole-genome sequencing studies, we have detected the overexpression of LMP1 and somatic alterations in NF-kappaB pathways in 25.7-32.8% and 40-66% of NPC respectively while the mutations associated with PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathways, FGF/FGFR signaling and lipogenesis (e.g. SREBP1, FASN) is not common (Tsang et al., Semin Cancer Biol.,2020; Bruce et al.,2020). The findings support that LMP1 and activated NF-kappaB signals contribute to modulate mTOR pathways, subsequently activating glucose metabolism and de novo lipogenesis (Zhang et al., Oncogene,2019; Lo et al., J Pathol.,2018; Lo et al., Int J Cancer,2017). Our functional studies have revealed that EBV-encoded LMP1 promotes de novo lipogenesis via inducing the expression, maturation and activation of a master regulator, sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1) and its downstream target fatty acid synthase (FASN). Furthermore, LMP1 activation of the mTOR pathway is required for SREBP1-mediated lipogenesis and FASN expression that enhances lipid droplet formation and cell proliferation in NPC. Through the collaborative studies, the precise mechanism for LMP1 activated mTOR1 and mTOR2 signaling have been unveiled (Zhang, et al.,Oncogene, 2019; Tsao et al., Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci. 2017). In addition, LMP1 increases the phosphorylation of ACLY, enhancing its activity to produce acetyl-CoA for fatty acid synthesis. The essential roles of LMP1 induced lipid synthesis were proven in various representative nasopharyngeal epithelial cell models. We have revealed high levels of the precursor and mature forms of SREBP1 and FASN in the EBV-positive tumor lines when compared with EBV-negative NPC and normal NP cells. Through investigating the status of LMP1 and FASN in the clinical tumor samples, we have also revealed that the expression of FASN correlated with LMP1 expression. Both LMP1 and FASN expression were proven to be poor prognostic biomarkers for NPC patients (Li, Nat commun.2017; Lo et al., J Pathol.2018). To elucidate the effect of targeting lipogenesis on NPC cell growth, we have treated the LMP-1 expressing NPC cells and parental cell lines with SREBP inhibitors, luteolin or fatostatin. The LMP-1 expressing NPC cells were more susceptible for the growth inhibition by luteolin or fatostatin. Importantly, we have also demonstrated that blocking lipogenesis by the two SREBP inhibitors significantly inhibited cell proliferation and increased apoptosis in both in vitro and in vivo EBV-positive NPC models (Lo et al., J Pathol.2018). Our findings imply that the SREBP inhibitors are efficient therapeutic agents for clinical study in NPC patients.

14117316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117316.value: Our findings indicate that LMP1, SREBP1 and FASN are potential biomarkers for predicating patients’ outcome and important molecular targets for development of effective treatment for NPC patients. For the LMP1-driven NPC tumors, novel therapeutic approaches including LMP1-specifc aptamers, nanoparticles with LMP1-targeting peptides and siRNA have been developed for in vitro and in vivo preclinical studies in various EBV-positive NPC models in our recent collaborative studies that focus on targeting EBV latency. The promising effects of the SREBP1 inhibitors in suppressing NPC tumor growth with low‐level toxicity suggest possible clinical utility for the treatment of NPC. However, there are lack of SREBP inhibitors that are available for clinical trials in cancer patients. Recent studies revealed the critical role of protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) in promoting SREBP1 activity. While multiple clinical trials of PRMT5 inhibitors in cancer patients are ongoing, we will further elucidate whether PRMT5 inhibition will deplete SREBP1 lipogenesis in EBV-positive NPC cells. In addition to these new class of therapeutic agents (e.g. GSK3326595, JNJ-64619178), the potential antitumor effects of FASN inhibitor (TVB-2640) will be evaluated in NPC. Furthermore, the consequences of SREBP1 and FASN inhibition on EBV lytic reactivation will be explored.

14117316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117316.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-induced metabolic reprogramming is a unique cancer hallmark in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), a distinct viral associated head and neck cancers. The EBV-encoded oncoprotein, latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1) contributes to tumor transformation through activating multiple signaling pathways, promoting aerobic glycolysis and de novo lipogenesis. In this study, we uncovered the precise mechanisms that LMP1 induces SREBP1-mediated lipogenesis and FASN expression. The critical roles of activated NF-kappaB and mTOR signaling pathways in LMP1 induced lipid synthesis were identified. In the clinical NPC tumors, we revealed that the overexpression of LMP1 and FASN was significantly associated with the poor treatment outcomes, suggesting the potential applications in management of NPC patients. The promising antitumor effect of targeting lipogenesis on NPC cell growth were proven in both in vitro and in vivo NPC models by two SREBP1 inhibitor, luteolin and fatostatin. In addition to uncover the critical role of lipid synthesis in EBV carcinogenesis, our work provides important information for the development of potential prognostic biomarkers and effective targeted therapies in NPC patients.

14118316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118316.value: In utero exposure to either overnutrition (in calories) or undernutrition (in micronutrients) can result in the disturbance of neuroendocrine control, homeostasis and epigenetic programming of a developing fetus, contributing to their future risks of non-communicable diseases (NCD). Our recent studies on the long-term follow-up of offspring from mothers with gestational diabetes (GDM) and cohorts from HAPO study demonstrated two important observations: 1) maternal hyperglycaemia during pregnancy significantly increases the offspring’s risk of abnormal glucose tolerance, lower beta cell function, overweight, higher BP and greater arterial stiffness, in early childhood independent of various confounders; 2) maternal GDM differentially altered the offspring's methylation on several regions linked to insulin resistance, beta cell functions and metabolic traits through genome-wide methylation analyses. Vitamin D is an important micronutrient and its deficiency in pregnancy has been linked to GDM and offspring’s future metabolic risk. Furthermore, vitamin D deficiency is now a worldwide problem and is found to be more prevalent in the South Asian population. We, therefore, propose to use the HAPO study cohort - a unique population that about 15% of mothers fulfilled the diagnosis of GDM (WHO 2013) but received no antenatal intervention and remained blinded on the diagnosis – to investigate 1) whether maternal vitamin D deficiency at pregnancy will further increase offspring’s cardiometabolic risk in addition to maternal hyperglycaemia in pregnancy; and 2) whether maternal vitamin D deficiency at pregnancy influence children’s future glucose metabolism, namely insulin resistance and beta cell functions, through an epigenetic effect occurring in utero. This study will make use of both the serum and DNA samples of mothers collected at pregnancy, umbilical cord blood at delivery and children at 7 years of age to address our hypotheses. As the follow-up study on this unique cohort is still ongoing locally and internationally, any of our research findings can be further validated in multi-ethnics population. As there is a paucity of research addressing the importance of this micronutrient at pregnancy to the children’s future cardiometabolic risk and NCD at their adulthood, the proposed study will provide answers to this area. 在懷孕期間，不論孕婦營養過剩或營養不良均有可能會影響胎兒的神經內分泌、動態平衡和表觀遺傳編程，以致干擾他們未來對抗非傳染性疾病的風險。我們最近從數個有關妊娠糖尿病婦女所生子女之隨訪研究(例如: HAPO研究) 發現了兩個重要的現象：1）婦女在懷孕期間處於高血糖水平會顯著增加其子女的糖耐量異常風險、β細胞功能下降、超重、血壓和動脈僵硬度增高。 2）妊娠糖尿病會透過基因甲基化，改變子女的胰島素抗性、β細胞功能和代謝特徵的幾個基因區域。 維生素D是一種重要的微量營養素。在妊娠期間缺乏維生素D跟孕婦患上妊娠糖尿病和其子女未來的代謝風險有關連。現在缺乏維生素D是一個世界性的難題，這種情況在南亞人口裡越來越普遍。由於參加HAPO研究的婦女沒有受到任何相關的產前干預，因此，我們建議透過此組研究對象去探討: 1）妊娠期婦女缺乏維生素D是否會進一步增加其子女的心血管代謝風險。 2）孕婦缺乏維生素D是否會影響其子女未來的糖代謝功能, 如胰島素抗性和β細胞功能。 這項研究將利用母親懷孕時期所收集的血液､臍帶血和其子女在7歲時收集的DNA血清樣本。由於HAPO隨訪研究仍在本地及國際進行中，我們的任何研究成果將可再進一步在不同種族的人口裡驗證。另外，由於缺乏有關於維生素D在懷孕期間到子女的未來心血管代謝風險和非傳染性疾病之重要性的研究，本研究將更有助了解這個範疇。

14118516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118516.value: TM9SF4是一種在進化中保守的跨膜蛋白。它在單細胞生物，植物與動物中都有表達。在功能方面，TM9SF4參與細胞的吞噬活動。我們的初步研究發現： 1）把TM9SF4過表達於HEK293細胞及CHO細胞後，細胞會產生一種K+通透性電流。TM9SF4的蛋白質序列中上有一個K+通透性的專一蛋白序列。我們在這專一蛋白序列進行點突變。突變後TM9SF4的K+通透性會缺失。 2）TM9SF4蛋白在大鼠和小鼠的腎小管上皮細胞中有大量表達。我們利用營養飢餓在HEK293細胞中刺激自噬。在TM9SF4敲除的細胞中，營養飢餓對自噬的作用明顯減小。這些數據提示，TM9SF4是一種新型的K +選擇性離子通道。它在腎臟細胞中促進吞噬作用。在此項研究中，我們打算對TM9SF4離子通道進行系統的電生理和藥理方面的研究，並對TM9SF4在腎臟細胞自噬的作用機制進行研究。本研究有以下預期目標： 1）本研究會揭示TM9SF4 K +通道的電生理特性。 2）眾所周知，自噬可以保護腎髒及減少缺血性腎損傷。本研究會探討可否能對TM9SF4作為治療腎臟疾病的分子靶點。

14118516.label: Realisation of objectives
14118516.value: 1). Objective #1 is to characterize electrophysiological and pharmacological properties of TM9SF4. Regarding this objective, we have overexpressed TM9SF4 in HEK293 and CHO cells. In these overexpression systems, with the use of patch clamp, we have identified TM9SF4 as a novel potassium channel. The activity of the channels is blocked by Ba2+ and Cs+. Ion replacement studies confirmed that the channels mediate K+ current. Consensus sequence search found a putative ion permeation pore in TM9SF4 proteins. Mutation of the ion permeation pore abolished the K+ current, further confirming TM9SF4 as an ion channel by itself. The experimental part is finished. A manuscript is under preparation. 2). Objective #2 is to explore the functional role of TM9SF4 in renal proximal tubule cells. Along this line, we have explored the autophagy of human embryonic kidney cell line HEK293 cells and mouse kidney tissue in vivo. Several autophagic indexes were examined, which include LC3-II accumulation, LC3-II puncta formation, and formation of autophagosome and autolysosome. We also compared autophagic flux between wild-type mice and TM9SF4 knockout mice. Our results show that TM9SF4 promotes autophagy under amino acid starvation. This happens in HEK293 cells and mouse renal cells in vivo. Overall, we identified TM9SF4 as a novel protein that promotes autophagic flux under amino acid starvation condition. 3). The objective #3 is to explore the mechanism of TM9SF4 involvement in starvation-induced autophagy. Here, we have dissected out the signaling pathway of TM9SF4 involvement in starvation-induced autophagy. We found that under starvation, TM9SF4 functions to inactivate mTOR, consequently promoting autophagy. Furthermore, we identified the physical interaction of TM9SF4 with mTOR. In addition, we explored the mechanism of how TM9SF4 as a K+-permeable channel can affect autophagy process. We found TM9SF4 can enhance the thapsigargin- and ATP-induced Ca2+ release from endoplasmic reticulum (ER). This is a novel mechanism of keeping ER Ca2+ homeostasis and reducing ER stress in renal cells and cancer cells.

14118516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14118516.value: Through this study, we have identified critical role of TM9SF4 in autophagy and ER stress mostly in renal system and cancer. Due to vital importance of autophagy and ER stress in cancer, we plan to further our study in the cancer. Targeting TM9SF4 and/or its signalling pathway could be a novel strategy for future cancer treatment option.

14118516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14118516.value: In the present study, we identified TM9SF4 proteins as a novel potassium channels. For the first time, we found that this protein can promote autophagy and reduce the ER stress in kidney as a protective mechanism to maintain kidney to be healthy. We also found that TM9SF4 has important role in cancer chemoresistance. Targeting TM9SF4 could be a novel strategy for future cancer treatment option,

14118616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14118616.value: Caesarean section is the most commonly performed surgery globally, with the majority of cases performed under spinal anaesthesia. However, this type of anaesthesia has known complications, the most common of which is hypotension. Therefore, the management of hypotension during spinal anaesthesia for caesarean section has become a focus of international research to which we have been leading international contributors. A major recent advance has been the widespread adoption of phenylephrine administration as an effective method for preventing and treating hypotension. However, phenylephrine has a number of potential disadvantages including non-availability in some countries, cost, and a propensity to cause reflexive decreases in heart rate and cardiac output. Investigation of potential alternatives is therefore justified. One promising alternative is norepinephrine. Like phenylephrine, norepinephrine is a potent alpha agonist and effective vasoconstrictor, but it has the additional advantage of mild beta agonist activity. Furthermore, it is available in many countries where phenylephrine is not licensed or unavailable, and it is significantly cheaper (approximately one-third after adjustment for potency) than phenylephrine. In a recent GRF-funded research project (2012/13 no.472112) we completed the first comparison of norepinephrine versus phenylephrine, given by computer-controlled infusion during spinal anaesthesia for elective caesarean delivery. Our findings, published in the top-ranked journal Anesthesiology, showed that norepinephrine has similar efficacy for maintaining blood pressure but with the advantages of better maintenance of heart rate and higher cardiac output compared with phenylephrine. The latter properties are desirable for optimal maternal and fetal outcome. An editorial accompanying our paper discussed these advantages but highlighted the need for confirmatory studies using more equipotent concentrations, given using everyday methods of delivery. Importantly, confirmation of fetal safety is required before norepinephrine can be introduced to routine clinical care. To address these issues, the current proposal will compare equipotent solutions of norepinephrine and phenylephrine under a range of ordinary clinical conditions in a double-blinded, pragmatic, non-inferiority clinical trial. We hypothesize that norepinephrine will be associated with neonatal outcome, assessed by umbilical arterial blood pH, that is at least as good (non-inferior) compared with phenylephrine whilst having similar efficacy for maintaining maternal BP. Because norepinephrine is cheaper, globally more widely available, and has an improved haemodynamic profile versus phenylephrine it has potential to be routinely used in obstetric anaesthesia. If the results of this study show that neonatal outcome is at least as good (non-inferior) compared with phenylephrine this will inform and potentially change clinical practice. 剖腹生產是全球最常見的手術，這類手術大部分用脊髓麻醉進行。然而，脊髓麻醉會出現已知的併發症，最常見是低血壓。因此，脊髓麻醉剖腹生產過程中低血壓的管理成為國際研究焦點，我們在這方面一直引領方向。被廣泛採納有效的預防和治療低血壓的最新進展是使用去氧腎上腺素(phenylephrine) 。然而，去氧腎上腺素具有許多潛在的缺點，包括某些國家未能獲得，價錢的考慮以及它容易引起反射性減低心跳率和心臟輸出量。這些因素成為調查潛在替代品的理由。一個可供替代的是去甲腎上腺素(norepinephrine)。去甲腎上腺素就像去氧腎上腺素一樣是強效的α激動劑和有效的血管收縮劑，而且它還具有輕微的β激動劑特性，此外，在許多未經許可或没有去氧腎上腺素的國家也能獲取，它經過藥效計算後的調整價錢比去氧腎上腺素便宜約三分之一。最近我們完成了優配研究金(GRF)資助的研究項目（2012/13 no.4721132）脊髓麻醉擇期剖腹生產過程中用電腦控制輸注去甲腎上腺素或去氧腎上腺素的第一次比較。研究結果發表在位列世界第一的期刊Anesthesiology，結果指出去甲腎上腺素和去氧腎上腺素有相同維持血壓的療效，而去甲腎上腺素的優點是有更佳的心跳率和更高的心臟輸出量，它的藥性對產婦和胎兒的療效令人滿意。期刊評論了這些優點，但強調需要用等效濃度的研究藥採用在一般生產環境下的確證研究。目的是為了讓去甲腎上腺素引入日常臨床治療前確保對胎兒是安全的。目前的方案設計是回應這些建議，這個臨床研究以雙盲法，務實性，研究藥物的療效指標相似性的方法在一般臨床環境下比較有相同藥療的去甲腎上腺素和去氧腎上腺素。研究的假設是去甲腎上腺素和去氧腎上腺素同樣具有維持產婦血壓的療效，去甲腎上腺素對初生兒的影響以臍帶動脈血液pH值評估， 兩種研究藥的結果要至少一樣好（非劣於）。因為去甲腎上腺素比較便宜，在全球更容易獲取，也能改善血液動力學數據，因此有可能成為婦產麻醉科的常規藥。如果這項研究的結果發現去甲腎上腺素比去氧腎上腺素對初生兒的評估至少為相同的良好（非劣於），這將會改變臨床上的治療。
