14127316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14127316.value: Male fertility is sustained by the self-renewal and differentiation of a group of stem cells in the testis, known as the spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs). Retinoic acid (RA) is a metabolite of vitamin A that acts as a physiological inducer of SSC differentiation. However, how RA induces SSC differentiation remains elusive. Male infertility is one of the hallmarks of cystic fibrosis, a genetic disease caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene (CFTR). Our previous study has demonstrated spermatogenic defects in CFTR knockout mice. However, the exact role of CFTR in germ cell differentiation remains unclear. In our preliminary study, we showed that CFTR was expressed in SSCs and its expression was significantly up-regulated in response to RA treatment. Bioinformatics revealed two RA receptor binding sites at the promoter region of CFTR. Knockdown of CFTR in the spermatogonial cell line C18-4 perturbs differentiation. Moreover, genetic manipulation of CFTR led to the alteration of Wnt/β-catenin pathway, an important signalling pathway known to be involved in SSC self-renewal/differentiation. These observations prompt us to hypothesize that CFTR may be regulated by RA and involved in mediating the RA-induced SSC differentiation through modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signalling pathway. To test this hypothesis, we propose to 1) examine the effect of RA on the expression of CFTR and its underlying regulatory mechanism in SSCs; 2) examine the involvement of CFTR in mediating RA-induced SSC differentiation in vitro; 3) examine the effect of germ cell-specific CFTR knockout on SSC differentiation in vivo; and 4) elucidate the mechanism underlying the effect of CFTR on RA-induced SSC differentiation. The proposed study will provide novel insight into the regulation of SSC differentiation mediated by CFTR and the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, which may shed light on new diagnostic methods and therapeutic regimens for CFTR-associated male infertility.

14127316.label: Realisation of objectives
14127316.value: Our study aims to examine the involvement of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) in spermatogonial differentiation and the underlying mechanism. We sought to achieve the goal with three specific aims: 1) to examine the effect of retinoic acid (RA) on the expression of CFTR and its underlying regulatory mechanism in spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs); 2) to examine the involvement of CFTR in mediating RA-induced SSC differentiation in vitro; 3) to elucidate the mechanism underlying the regulation of RA-induced SSC differentiation by CFTR. In Aim 1, we have first examined the protein expression of CFTR in the testis of neonatal mice at 2, 4, 7, and 14 days postpartum and observed an increased expression of CFTR in both germ cells and Sertoli cells as distinguished by the germ cell marker TRA98 (Fig 1). Using a type A spermatogonial cell line C18-4 and the primary spermatogonial culture, we showed that RA induces spermatogonial differentiation as marked by the expression of differentiating spermatogonia marker Stra8. Of note, the expression of Cftr was significantly induced by RA (Fig 2). Spermatogonia express two RA receptors RARα and RARγ. Interestingly, the expression of RARα was induced by RA, while RARγ was constitutively expressed (Fig 2). In line with this finding, RARα agonist treatment and overexpression of RARα induced the expression of Cftr while knockdown of RARα by siRNA blunted the RA-induced Cftr expression (Fig 3). To determine how RA and RARα activate Cftr expression, we studied the promoter of the mouse Cftr gene. Luciferase reporter assay demonstrated that the promoter of Cftr contains two RA-responsive elements (RAREs). Mutation in either one of the RARE significantly inhibited the RA-induced Cftr promoter activity while mutations in both RAREs completely abolished the RA induction (Fig 4). Chromatin immunoprecipitation assay confirmed the binding of RARα to the two RAREs of the Cftr promoter in C18-4 cells and primary spermatogonia culture (Fig 5). Our results showed that RARα transcriptionally activates Cftr expression in response to RA in spermatogonia. In Aim 2, we have investigated the involvement of CFTR in mediating RA-induced spermatogonial differentiation. We examined the expression of spermatogonial differentiation markers Stra8 and c-Kit in Cftr knockout mice and in Cftr-knockdown C18-4 cells with or without RA treatment. Real-time PCR results showed a significant decrease in the expression of both genes in the knockout mouse testis (Fig 6). Moreover, knockdown of Cftr significantly decreased the expression of both genes in the absence of RA and blunted their upregulation induced by RA (Fig 6). In line with the loss-of-function models, overexpression of CFTR in C18-4 cells induced spermatogonial differentiation as evidenced by the upregulation of Stra8 and c-Kit, with expression levels comparable to that induced by RA (Fig 6). These results suggest that CFTR plays an essential role in the RA-induced spermatogonial differentiation. In Aim 3, we investigated the mechanism underlying the regulation of spermatogonial differentiation by CFTR. Previous studies by our group and others have shown that CFTR modulates Wnt/β-Catenin signalling that regulates stem cell self-renewal and differentiation. To test the involvement of Wnt/β-Catenin signalling in CFTR-mediated spermatogonial differentiation, we examined the activity of β-catenin and the expression of Axin 2, the readout of the Wnt/β-Catenin signalling pathway. The results showed that the RA-induced CFTR upregulation was associated with elevated levels of active β-catenin and Axin2, both of which were blunted by knockdown of CFTR (Fig 7). We further tested whether pharmacological activation of the β-catenin pathway can rescue the effect of CFTR knockdown on the RA-induced differentiation of C18-4 cells. The results showed that CHIR treatment restored the RA-induced expression of Stra8 and c-Kit in CFTR knockdown cells (Fig 7). These results suggest that the β-catenin pathway acts downstream of CFTR in mediating the RA-induced spermatogonial differentiation. We next asked what is the biological importance of CFTR in spermatogonial differentiation? Recent single-cell analyses of spermatogonial differentiation have revealed the up-regulation of genes involved in epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) during spermatogonial differentiation. Intriguingly, our previous studies have shown that CFTR modulates EMT in cancer metastasis. These results prompt us to reason that CFTR is involved in EMT during spermatogonial differentiation. Since there is no report on the involvement of the EMT process during spermatogonial differentiation, we extended our study to investigate the cell migration properties during spermatogonial differentiation. Our studies showed that the expression of connective tissue growth factor (Ctgf) and TGFβ2 (Tgfb2), both were known to be regulated by CFTR, were significantly upregulated upon RA-induced differentiation (Fig 8). RA treatment increased the migration of primary cultured spermatogonia in a dose-dependent manner. The induction of Ctgf by RA was observed in spermatogonial progenitor cells but not the stem cell compartment. Importantly, recombinant CTGF treatment increased the migration of C18-4 and primary spermatogonia. These results suggest that spermatogonial differentiation is associated with the EMT process regulated by the CFTR-CTGF axis. Taken together, the present findings reveal a pivotal role of CFTR in spermatogonial differentiation via regulating the Wnt/β-Catenin signalling pathway and the EMT process.

14127316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14127316.value: Our study has revealed the involvement of CFTR in spermatogonial differentiation. We have shown that retinoic acid transcriptionally activates CFTR via RARα. In turn, CFTR plays an essential role in spermatogonial differentiation by activation of the Wnt/β-Catenin signalling pathway. Knockout of Cftr perturbs spermatogonial differentiation and thus spermatogenesis, leading to subfertility or infertility outcome. This part of the results has been published in Biochimica et Biophysica Acta - Molecular Cell Research (2018). In the follow-up study, we have revealed for the first time that spermatogonial differentiation is associated with increased epithelial-mesenchymal transition and cell migration that may be regulated by CFTR. Notably, we have uncovered the involvement of a cytokine connective-tissue growth factor (CTGF) in mediating the spermatogonial migration associated with differentiation. This part of the results has also been published in Biochimica et Biophysica Acta - Molecular Cell Research (2020). Together, our study has revealed a pivotal role of CFTR in spermatogonial differentiation via regulating the Wnt/β-Catenin signalling pathway and the EMT process. Our study may shed light on the diagnosis of spermatogenic defects that underlie male infertility. Further investigation along this line may develop tools to enhance the spermatogonial stem cell transplantation efficiency.

14127316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14127316.value: The presently demonstrated role of CFTR in spermatogonial differentiation has an important impact on the biology and application of spermatogonial stem cells. Disrupting the homeostasis of spermatogonial stem cells causes spermatogenic arrest and male infertility. Previous studies have raised the necessity for CFTR mutation screening in azoospermia patients. The results of the present study have provided further mechanistic insight on the defective spermatogonia differentiation stemmed from the loss of functional CFTR. This provides sets of biological markers that aid the diagnosis of male infertility. On the other hand, our results suggest that the use of β-catenin activator and CTGF may rescue defective spermatogonial differentiation in male infertile patients with CFTR mutations. Currently, the transplantation of spermatogonial stem cells has been proposed to be a feasible approach in preserving and restoring fertility. However, the poor homing efficiency of spermatogonial stem cells after transplantation remains the major hurdle. The presently demonstrated ability of recombinant CTGF in promoting the migration of spermatogonia may increase the homing efficiency without disrupting the balance between self-renewal and differentiation of spermatogonial stem cells. Further investigation is required to test this potential application.

14127316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14127316.value: Male fertility is sustained by the self-renewal and differentiation of a group of stem cells in the testis, known as the spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs). Retinoic acid (RA) is a metabolite of vitamin A that acts as a physiological inducer of SSC differentiation. However, how RA induces SSC differentiation remains elusive. In this study, we showed that the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR), a gene involved in cystic fibrosis and male infertility, is involved in spermatogonial differentiation. RA induces the gene expression of CFTR through its receptor RARα. Loss of CFTR abolishes RA-induced spermatogonial differentiation. CFTR mediates spermatogonial differentiation by activating the Wnt/β-Catenin signalling pathway, a molecular pathway pivotal for stem cell maintenance and differentiation. We further showed that spermatogonial differentiation is associated with increased cell migration that may also be attributed to the regulation by CFTR. Together, our study has deciphered a molecular mechanism underlying spermatogonial differentiation. Our study may shed light on the diagnosis of spermatogenic defects that underlie male infertility.

14128016.value: 視覺特徵：FVS空間的系統發展

14128016.label: Project Objectives
14128016.value: Stimulus dimensions that affect featural and visual strengths Huang (2015c) showed that bar orientations can be weakened in two independent ways: low-contrast bars are reduced on visual strength, but not on featural strength, whereas the chubby bars are reduced on featural strength, but not on visual strength. I plan to explore similar conceptual distinctions in several other features. First, I will measure how the featural and visual strengths of Gabor orientations will be affected by spatial frequencies of the items. Second, I will test how featural and visual strengths of low-contrast colors are affected by perceived translucency. Third, I will test whether there is a systematic difference between the featural and visual strengths of hue and luminance. Generality of FVS space across stimulus types I plan to extend Huang (2015c)’s coverage of the stimulus types in two ways. First, Huang (2015c) has only tested artificial stimuli. Therefore, it is important to extend the FVS space to real-world stimulus types. Second, Huang (2015c) has generally tried the canonical, and strong features, so it is important to extend the FVS space to noncanonical features and stimulus types that are weaker but conceptually important (e.g., geometrical shapes). Generality of FVS space across groups The current measures of FVS space and weights of tasks have only been established in a fairly special group: young Asian. Therefore, it is important to find out whether FVS space can be applied to other groups, including the older adults, and westerners. Generality of FVS space across methods In Huang (2015c), the FVS space was based on a specific set of methodological parameters. Therefore, to become a more general framework for visual features, it needs to be extended in various ways, including display set size, spatial arrangements of items, and the range of contrasts. Determining the reason for the unexplained variance in grouping In Huang (2015c), the FVS space’s explaining power is lower on grouping (i.e., 89.7% of the variances) than for the seven other tasks. I will test the hypothesis that this happens because the observers sometimes used the artificial strategy of looking for “virtual lines” connecting top and bottom items.

14128016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14128016.value: 關於人類視覺系統的一項重要發現是一組基本特徵的提取，如顏色，朝向，形狀，尺寸等。一項最近的研究(Huang, 2015) 試圖確定是哪些因素決定了這些特徵在各種任務中的分數。 該研究中使用一種新的個體項差異分析：一組刺激類型在一個任務中的分數與另一個任務中的分數有怎樣的關係。本研究採用16種刺激和8種任務，並確保所有任務的可靠性為0.975或更高。結果表明有三個正交因素：特徵強度描述了刺激的接近基本特徵的程度，視覺強度描述了刺激本身的視覺品質，空間強度描述了刺激可以被表示為空間結構的程度。 特徵強度對幾乎所有任務都有普遍的提升，但對於知覺區分任務提升較少。視覺強度大幅提升低級任務，但對高級任務基本無提升。空間強度提升變化檢測任務，但損害集體匹配和視覺搜索任務。這三個因素合稱FVS空間，幾乎解釋了這16刺激類型在這8個任務中扮演的所有（96.4％）角色。 在該研究計畫中，我力求系統地發展FVS空間。這個項目有幾個重要的影響。首先，FVS空間是關於視覺特徵的因素唯一的現有框架，這個框架的系統發展將極大地豐富我們在這個方向的知識。其次，它會更系統的解答一些基本的研究問題，如現實世界刺激的注意力處理過程，以及注意力處理過程的文化因素。第三，系統的探討影響特徵和視覺強度的刺激維度，將揭示關於視覺特徵底層表徵的重要資訊。 關於FVS空間的研究將在以下的方向上開展（1）探討影響特徵強度和視覺強度的刺激維度。具體地講，我將測量伽柏朝向的特徵強度和視覺強度怎樣隨空間頻率改變，測量低對比度的顏色的特徵強度和視覺強度怎樣被透明感知影響，以及對色調和亮度的特徵強度和視覺強度之間進行比較。（2）擴大刺激類型的覆蓋面，從人工刺激到真實世界刺激類型，從規範的強的特徵到非規範的弱的特徵。 （3）測試FVS空間對不同的人群的普遍性，從年輕人到老年人，從東亞到西方人。 （4）測試在各種方法細節方面FVS空間的普遍性，包括顯示內容的大小，物體的空間分佈，以及對比度的範圍; （五）確定在分組任務中不能解釋的機制的原因。

Third, I have tested whether there is a systematic difference between the featural and visual strengths of hue and luminance, the results turn out to be negative, so no further action is taken. The objective 2 was the generality of FVS space across stimulus types. I have extended Huang (2015c)’s coverage of the stimulus types in two ways. First, Huang (2015c) has only tested artificial stimuli. Therefore, it is important to extend the FVS space to real-world stimulus types. I have tried this out and no meaningful difference between artificial and real-world stimuli has been identified, so no further action is taken. Second, Huang (2015c) has generally tried the canonical, and strong features, so it is important to extend the FVS space to noncanonical features and stimulus types that are weaker but conceptually important (e.g., geometrical shapes), the results turn out to be quite messy and inconsistent across the several categories of stimuli (color, shape, orientation) I have tried, so no further action is taken. The objective 3 was the generality of FVS space across groups. The current measures of FVS space and weights of tasks have only been established in a fairly special group: young Asian. Therefore, it is important to find out whether FVS space can be applied to other groups, including older adults, and westerners. I have tried both out, the data on older adults look messy. The featural, visual, and spatial strengths are generally reduced for older adults, but the relative importance is inconsistent across the different categories of stimuli (color, shape, orientation) I have tried, it may be worth pursuing this again sometime in the future, but for now, no conclusion can be drawn. The data on comparison between westerners (collected in UC San Diego) and Asians used Chinese characters as the stimuli revealed important knowledge about the ways how reading affects visual processing, this result has been summarized in a manuscript (New Preattentive Feature Can Hardly be Learned). The objective 4 was the Generality of FVS space across methods. I have extended the coverage of the FVS framework substantially from 8 tasks to 26 tasks (total sample size = 1744). This is the main breakthrough in this project. This result has substantial theoretical values and has been summarized in a manuscript (FVS 2.0: a Unifying Framework for Understanding the Factors of Visual Processing) and is currently being considered by Psychological Review. Besides, some of the side experiments made interesting findings that are not closely related to the main points of the FVS framework and they have been published in a separate paper (Distinguishing target biases and strategic guesses in visual working memory). The objective 5 was determining the reason for the unexplained variance in grouping. In Huang (2015c), the FVS space’s explaining power is lower on grouping (i.e., 89.7% of the variances) than for the seven other tasks. I tested the hypothesis that this happens because the observers sometimes used the artificial strategy of looking for “virtual lines” connecting the top and bottom items. The results are unclear because it only explains a minor portion of unexplained mechanisms, so no further action is taken.

14128016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14128016.value: The major finding of this project is summarized in the paper “FVS 2.0: a Unifying Framework for Understanding the Factors of Visual Processing” which is now being considered by Psychological Review. Across a broad range of stimulus types and tasks (16 stimulus types × 26 tasks, total sample size = 1744), the present study employed an individual-item differences analysis to extract the factors of visual Processing. Three orthogonal factors were identified and they can be summarized as an FVS 2.0 framework: featural, visual, and spatial strengths. Apart from one exception (low-level motion), the FVS 2.0 framework accounts for the vast majority (95.4%) of the variances in the 25 tasks. These results have two important implications. First, the three straightforward factors provide a unifying framework for understanding the relationship between stimulus types as well as those between tasks. Second, the role of preattentive features is rather different from the traditional view: visual features are general-purpose, exclusive, innate, constancy-based, and keyword-like. A GEICK conjecture is proposed which suggests that the features are conscious-level keywords generated by the specific brain area of V4 and/or IT and then used by all other brain areas. This study also has other implications on the nature of visual and spatial strength, as well as various other issues. Unfortunately, the publication of this study is delayed from my initial plan. The major reason is that the theoretical scope of this framework goes much beyond my original plan, so a lot of rethinking and literature search was needed. This is ultimately a great opportunity for me. But the completion of this theoretical paper was delayed for half a year (from the middle of 2019 to the end of 2019). Besides, the reviewing process is longer than expected. I have submitted this paper to Psychological Review at the beginning of 2020, but no final decision has been reached up to now. As for the other manuscripts, I have been holding them up for now until the theoretical framework is formally published. Despite the delay, I am very confident that these will ultimately turn out to be important papers and among the best of mine.

14128016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14128016.value: Of course, the first thing I will do next is to try to publish the four above-mentioned manuscripts. After they have been successfully published, I will try to develop this further by developing image-based formal algorithms to determine the meaning of featural, visual, and spatial strengths.

14128016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14128016.value: In the visual world, we can face various types of stimuli and can conduct various types of tasks. The interaction between stimulus types and tasks can reveal important information about the mental processing of visual stimuli. The present large set of experimental results has identified many counter-intuitive findings. For example, human observers are especially good at looking for some categories of stimuli (e.g., colors) but are especially bad at remembering them. For another example, human observers are especially good at looking for something (e.g., basic shapes, compared to complex shapes) even if they are no better at visually processing them as individual items. These and many other findings are explained in a unified FVS framework: all the variations of visual processing boils down to three factors: their featural, visual, and spatial strengths.

14130216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14130216.value: This 6-year longitudinal cohort study aims to investigate whether improvement in bone mineral density (BMD), bone quality and prevention of scoliosis curve progression induced by calcium and vitamin-D (Vit-D) supplementation (600mg calcium + 400/800 IU Vit-D3/day) persist after supplement discontinuation for girls with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) and low bone mass. The changes of the group without supplementation will also provide useful longitudinal data that is rarely available in adolescents. The study also aims to correlate the changes with serum and image-based bone turnover parameters. AIS is a complex three-dimensional spinal deformity mostly affecting girls during the peri-pubertal period. In severe cases, serious morbidities including cardiopulmonary compromise and early back degeneration can occur. 30-38% of AIS girls had osteopenia (BMD Z-score < -1) which could persist into adulthood and has been reported to be a significant and independent prognostic factor for curve progression in AIS. Vit-D regulates calcium absorption and plays an important role in skeletal growth and bone mineralization for achieving normal peak bone mass. Studies have revealed that AIS girls have low dietary calcium intake and high prevalence of Vit-D insufficiency. In light of these findings, our group has performed the first 2-year randomized double-blinded placebo-controlled trial with calcium and Vit-D supplementation to AIS girls with low bone mass (the Cal study). The study showed strong evidences of positive bone accretion effects and therapeutic control of curve progression in the group with supplementation. This proposed study is an extension of the Cal study investigating the changes in BMD, bone quality, bone strength, image-based and serum bone turnover parameters, and curve severity 4 years after discontinuation of calcium and Vit-D supplementation. The data will be analyzed together with the data generated from the Cal study thus constituting a total of 6-years follow-up. This project will provide scientific data on the long term effect of and after withdrawal of calcium and Vit-D supplements, thus justifying the need of lifestyle modification, and duration and dose of supplementation for better bone health and curve control in adolescents with AIS. The placebo control group will provide the longitudinal data on changes of bone density, bone quality and curve severity for those without supplementation. Altogether, this study will yield important information on bone quality, curve severity and the importance of calcium and Vit-D in achieving good bone health and preventing curve progression for adolescents with AIS. 這6年的縱向隊列研究方案旨在探討低骨量之青少年特發性脊柱側凸女性病患者從鈣和維生素-D補充治療（每天600毫克鈣+400/800 IU維生素-D3）導致骨密度，骨質量之改善和預防脊柱側凸惡化之療効能否在停止補充治療後持績。沒有補充治療之安慰劑組的變化亦提供罕有青少年的縱向數據。是項研究目的亦包括上述骨及脊柱側凸變化與血清和影像骨轉換參數變化之關聯分析。 脊柱側凸是複雜之三維脊柱畸形,主要影響青春期之女孩。嚴重脊柱側凸可引致心肺功能受損和早期脊柱退化等拼發症。30-38％脊柱側凸女病患者同時患有骨質偏低（骨密度 Z-指數<-1），骨質偏低可持續到成年，亦是脊柱側凸惡化與否的預後因子。 維生素-D調節鈣的吸收並對骨骼生長和骨礦化至正常峰值骨量具重要作用。研究顯示，脊柱側凸女孩膳食鈣攝入量和維生素-D水平偏低。本科研團隊已進行首次2年隨機鈣和維生素-D補充治療對特發性脊柱側凸並有低骨量之女性病患者之雙盲安慰劑對照臨床研究(簡稱”Cal研究”)。研究顯示鈣和維生素-D補充治療對骨增生和預防脊柱側凸惡化有顯著療効。 本研究方案是”Cal研究”之延績, 旨在調查鈣和維生素-D補充治療停藥4年後骨密度,，骨質量，骨強度，圖像和血清骨轉換參數，和脊柱側凸之變化。資料將連同”Cal研究” 所得之數據一併分析, 從而構建共6年之隨訪研究報告。 本研究方案將對鈣和維生素-D補充治療之長期與停藥後之效用提供科學數據，為特發性脊柱側凸女性病患者改善骨骼健康和預防脊柱側凸惡化而設定之生活方式建議和鈣和維生素-D補充治療提供客觀科研證據。沒有補充治療之安慰劑組的變化亦提供青少年骨密度，骨質量和脊柱側凸變化之縱向數據。換言之,本研究將對特發性脊柱側凸女性病患者之骨密度，骨質量和脊柱側凸變化及相關之鈣和維生素-D補充治療提供重要科學數據。

14130216.label: Realisation of objectives
14130216.value: As mentioned in our last request for extension of deadline for submitting the Final Report, the COVID-19 pandemic was expected to remain unstable for the first to second half of 2021. Unfortunately what followed shortly was the rampant fifth wave that began in Jan-2022 during which research staff was not allowed access to clinical areas where all the source documents and clinical data are located for this 6-year clinical study. Considering the potential impact of the current study, we insist data authenticity is of top priority. While inevitably this has led to delay in preparing the complete report for journal submission, very useful scientific information can be generated in a collateral manner resulting in publication of 4 papers to which this project has significant and direct contribution. As for the complete report of this 6-year longitudinal study, we are able to carefully capture all the required information without compromise of authenticity, and compile an accurate dataset followed by analysis to acheive both study objectives as detailed below. Despite the highly unfavourable pandemic environment, the manuscript reporting the main results of this study is now ready for journal submission as Item 5 in “Part C: Research Output, Session 8 on [Peer-reviewed publication]”. In brief, this novel 6-year longitudinal study provides strong evidences on the therapeutic effect of Calcium + Vit-D on improving bone health and controlling curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Improvement in bone health occurs readily upon completion of treatment but improvement in curve outcome probably lags behind with a gap of 1.5 to 3 years. Discontinuation of treatment will result in dissipation of treatment effect both on bone health and curve outcome. As for Revised Objective 1: The initial 2-year randomized trial using Calcium and Vit-D supplementation for AIS (ie the Cal study) has not been reported in the literature because we intend to include both the Cal study and this 6-year longitudinal study for publication on its entirety. Results of the complete study from baseline to 6-year follow-up including those corresponding to “Objective 1” and “Objective 2” have been depicted in details in the manuscript corresponding to Item 5 in “Part C: Research Output, Session 8 on [Peer-reviewed publication]”. Since interpretation of this current 6-year follow-up study is best done together with the results from the initial Cal study, the key findings for both the Cal study and the current study are bundled together and reiterated as follows (please refer to Item 5 for details, in particular for Figure 1 and various Tables mentioned below): A total of 1037 consecutive AIS subjects noted to be eligible at initial screening were evaluated and finally, 330 suitable subjects were randomised. Details of patient flow are depicted in Figure 1 of Item 5. The baseline characteristics of maturity, anthropometric, lifestyle, biochemical, DXA and HR-pQCT parameters are shown in Table 1 of Item 5. No significant difference was noted between Group 1, 2 and 3 (all with p>0.05) except serum P1NP. 270 (81.8%) subjects completed the 2-year treatment (Figure 1). The overall treatment compliance was very satisfactory, namely 83.3±12.9% (Group 1: 84.5±11.8%, Group 2: 82.5±14.0%, and Group 3: 82.8±12.8%, p= 0.519). At 6-year from baseline, very satisfactory follow-up rate was achieved. 237 subjects (87.8% of those who completed the 2-year treatment, or 71.8% of the initial cohort) were available for study at a mean age of 19.2 years old. In line with Objective 1 of investigating changes in bone parameters at 6 years follow up in AIS girls, it was first noted at the 2-year time-point, the gain in serum 25(OH)Vit-D in both Treatment Group 2 and 3, and the gain in left femoral neck aBMD in Treatment Group 3 were significantly greater than the Placebo Group 1 (all with p<0.05, Table 2 of Item 5). Changes in Trabecular vBMD, Trabecular Bone Volume to Tissue Volume Ratio and Trabecular Number were different between groups demonstrating therapeutic enhancement of bone health with Ca+Vit-D supplementation in the Treatment Group 2 and 3 as compared with the Placebo Group 1 (all with p<0.05, Table 2 of Item 5). In contrast, the increase in Trabecular Separation was significantly greater in the Placebo Group 1 than Treatment Group 2 and 3. At 6-year follow up after 4-year supplement discontinuation, and in contrast to the 2-year time-point, no difference was noted in all DXA and HR-pQCT bone density and bone quality parameters except increase in Cortical Thickness being greater only in Treatment Group 3 than in Placebo Group 1 (Table 3 of Item 5) What is more clinically important is the curve outcome. Curve outcome was evaluated according to curve progression defined as Cobb increase of 6 degrees or more from baseline at 3.5-year, 4.5-year and 6-year after the start of treatment respectively. As shown in Table 5A of Item 5, better curve control in Ca+Vit-D treatment group was numerically seen at the 3.5-year time-point (p=0.137) and reaching statistical significance at the 4.5-year time-point (p=0.003). In contrast, there was no difference in rate of curve progression at the 6-year time-point (p=0.200, chi-square). When considering the subgroup with Vit-D insufficiency (defined as serum 25(OH)VitD ≤ 50 nmol/L) at baseline, the treatment effect on curve progression was more apparently seen especially for Group 3 (Table 5B of Item 5). For Revised Objective 2: At baseline, no significant difference was noted between study groups for biochemical parameters except serum P1NP. There was no significant difference in changes of serum CTx and P1NP between study groups after 2-year treatment with Calcium and Vit-D. Interestingly, correlation between changes in bone parameters and changes in serum bone turnover biomarkers at 2-year time-point and at 6-year time-point are noted as shown in Table 6 and Table 7 of Item 5 respectively. It is noted that changes in serum CTx and P1NP are significantly correlated with majority of bone parameters including DXA-derived aBMD, various gross morphometry, volumetric bone mineral densities and bone micro-architecture parameters.

14130216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14130216.value: Based on the promising results from this novel 6-year longitudinal study, further studies are warranted: 1. A RCT on patients with early scoliosis with Cobb angle between 10 to 20° to investigate if Calcium + Vit-D can control curve from progression to bracing and surgical thresholds right at the early phase of the disease. 2. A RCT recruiting male subjects should be carried out to investigate if Calcium + Vit-D have therapeutic effect similar to that for female subjects If these studies do show Calcium + Vit-D is useful to control early cases of scoliosis from progression, it will be worthwhile to consider further large-scale studies investigating if adequate calcium and Vit-D intake either in form of supplementation or through lifestyle enhancement can prevent scoliosis from occurrence among schoolchildren in the general population.

14130216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14130216.value: This study aims at evaluating the therapeutic effect of oral Calcium + Vitamin D in improving bone health and controlling disease progression in children suffering from spinal deformity called scoliosis. This 6-year longitudinal study provides strong evidences on the therapeutic effect of Calcium + Vit-D on improving bone health and controlling curve progression in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Improvement in bone health occurs readily upon completion of treatment but improvement in disease outcome probably lags behind with a gap of 1.5 to 3 years. Discontinuation of treatment will result in dissipation of treatment effect both on bone health and curve outcome. Based on this study, more formal studies should be carried out to investigate if Calcium + Vitamin D supplementation can prevent scoliosis from deterioration to bracing or surgical thresholds.

14130716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14130716.value: Membrane trafficking is essential for plant growth and responses to external signals. The plant endomembrane system consists of several functionally distinct membrane-bound organelles, including the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi apparatus, trans-Golgi network (TGN) or early endosome, prevacuolar compartment (PVC) or multivesicular bodies (MVBs) and vacuole. Membrane proteins destined for degradation are usually ubiquitinated and sorted into the intraluminal vesicles (ILVs) of PVCs/MVBs for subsequent degradation in vacuole/lysosome upon MVB-vacuole fusion. This process is facilitated by the endosomal sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) machinery in eukaryotic cells. We have recently identified and characterized a plant unique ESCRT component called FYVE domain protein required for endosomal sorting 1 (FREE1). We have demonstrated that FREE1 plays multiple functional roles in regulating protein trafficking and organelle biogenesis in plants, including formation of ILVs of MVB, vacuolar protein transport, and vacuole biogenesis. Arabidopsis free1 loss-of-function mutant is seedling lethal and defective in the formation of ILVs in MVBs, in vacuolar protein sorting and vacuole biogenesis. To further illustrate the underlying mechanisms of FREE1 function in plants, we performed a forward genetic screen for mutants that suppressed the seedling lethal phenotype of FREE1-RNAi transgenic plants and the obtained mutants are termed as suppressors of free1 (sof). Barely detecting of FREE1 protein with normal vacuole morphology in M3 plants of putative sof mutants further identified 84 FREE1-related suppressors. Through next-generation sequencing (NGS) of bulked DNA from F2 mapping population of the first ten FREE1-related sof mutants, we have identified one interesting gene: SOF100 and SOF524. The causal locus in the four sof lines (sof100, sof220, sof452, and sof453) was mapped to the same gene RST1 (At3g27670), and all of them have premature stop codons, indicating that SOF100/RST1 is a true suppressor of free1. As expected, sof100 seedlings exhibited reduced FREE1 protein level and normal vacuole morphology. Our preliminary results indicated that SOF100/RST1 was localized to plasma membrane (PM) and Post-Golgi puncta in Arabidopsis cells. We thus hypothesize that sof100 is a true FREE1-related suppressor of free1, and that SOF100/RST1 may function as a suppressor of FREE1 in the secretory pathway in Arabidopsis. Therefore, the central goal of this research proposal is to characterize SOF100/RST1 as a FREE1 suppressor in the secretory pathway as well as to identify and characterize the distinct FREE1 protein complex in plants. Our long-term goal is to illustrate the underlying mechanisms of FREE1 function in intracellular trafficking and organelle biogenesis in plants. 細胞內膜介導的物質運輸是對於植物生長和應對外部信號至關重要。植物內膜系統由若干個功能不同的含有膜結構的細胞器，包括內質網（ER），高爾基體，反式高爾基網絡（TGN）或早期內涵體（EE），液泡前體（PVC）或多囊泡體（MVBs）和液泡。膜蛋白的降解通常需要經過泛素化標記，然後分選到多囊泡體的腔內小泡（ILV）中，隨後經過多囊泡體和液泡的融合而進入液泡降解。此過程是由一系列稱為ESCRT的蛋白複合體精細調控的。最近我們分離鑑定到含有FYVE結構域的擬南芥FREE1蛋白是植物特有的ESCRT組成部分。我們已經證明，FREE1在調節植物蛋白質運輸和細胞器的生物合成，包括形成MVB，液泡蛋白運輸，和液泡生物發生多個方面起作用。擬南芥free1功能缺失突變體幼苗期死亡，MVB不能形成腔內小泡（ILV），並在液泡蛋白分選運輸和液泡生成中有缺陷。為了進一步探究植物FREE1功能的分子機制，我們進行了正向遺傳篩選。我們以FREE1-RNAi的轉基因植物的幼苗致死表型為篩選背景， 篩選可以抑制FREE1-RNAi 幼苗致死表型的突變體，將得到的突變體稱為free1抑制子突變體，簡稱SOF（suppressor ​​of free1 ）。進一步FREE1蛋白檢測確定了84個和 FREE1相關的抑制子SOF突變體，這些突變體的M3植株有正常的液泡形態，並且幾乎檢測不到FREE1蛋白質。通過對前十個FREE1-相關SOF突變體的雜交F2圖位克隆群體DNA的進行新一代測序分析，我們發現一個有趣的基因：SOF100 。在四個SOF株系（sof100，sof220，sf452和sof453）的突變基因都定位到了相同的基因RST1，且都是提前終止突變，這表明SOF100 / RST1是free1的真正抑制子。正如預期的那樣，sof100的苗表現​​出降低的FREE1蛋白水平和正常形態的液泡。因此，我們假設，sof100是free1的抑制子，並且SOF100 / RST1和FREE1在擬南芥細胞分泌途徑中共同起作用。因此，本研究的中心目標是分析SOF100 / RST1在分泌途徑中的作用， 以及分離鑑定植物中不的FREE1蛋白複合體。我們的長期目標是要探明FREE1在細胞分泌途徑及細胞器行程過程中的分子機制。

14130716.label: Realisation of objectives
14130716.value: Objective 1: Our previous studies have demonstrated the important functions of FREE1 as a component of ESCRT (endosomal sorting complexes required for transport) in regulating MVB (multivesicular body) biogenesis and MVB-mediated endosomal sorting. In this project, we further uncovered a previously unappreciated function of FREE1 in the nucleus as a negative regulator to attenuate ABA (Abscisic acid) signaling. We obtained several lines of cellular, biochemical and genetic evidence that strongly support our hypothesis: (1) a portion of the FREE1 protein translocate into the nucleus in response to ABA treatment; (2) SnRK2.2 and SnRK2.3 mediate FREE1 phosphorylation, a prerequisite step for FREE1 nuclear import; (3) phosphorylated FREE1 interacts with ABF4 and ABI5 in the nucleus to inhibit their transcriptional activation activities; (4) the free1-ct mutant with defects in nuclear import of FREE1 in response to ABA shows normal growth and vacuolar sorting route, but displays hypersensitivity to ABA treatment; and (5) the abf4 and abi5 mutants are epistatic to the free1-ctmut in ABA sensitivity. Based on these findings and the previous report about FREE1 function in ABA signaling, we proposed a ‘double-brake’ working model for FREE1 function in attenuation of ABA signaling, in which FREE1 (1) can function in the cytoplasm to negatively regulate the cellular protein level of ABA receptors by mediating their vacuolar degradation in an ESCRT-dependent pathway; and (2) translocate into the nucleus to repress the transcription factors ABF4 and ABI5. These new findings have been published in Nature Plants in 2019. Thus, we have achieved the original objective 1 fully. Objective 2: We have finished the characterization of RST1 (RESURRECTION1) as a suppressor of free1 that, when mutated as a null mutant, restores the normal MVB and vacuole formation of a FREE1-RNAi knockdown line and consequently allows survival. RST1 encodes an evolutionarily conserved multicellular organism-specific protein, which contains two DUF3730 (Domain of Unknown Function 3730) domains, showing no similarity to known proteins, and predominantly localizes in the cytosol. The depletion of FREE1 causes substantial accumulation of RST1, and transgenic Arabidopsis plants over-expressing RST1 display retarded seedling growth with dilated MVBs, and inhibition of endocytosed FM4-64 dye to the tonoplast, suggesting that RST1 has a negative role in vacuolar transport. Consistently, enhanced endocytic degradation of membrane vacuolar cargoes occurs in the rst1 mutant. Further transcriptomic comparison of rst1 with free1 revealed a negative association between gene expression profiles, demonstrating that FREE1 and RST1 have antagonistic functions. Thus, RST1 is a negative regulator controlling membrane protein homeostasis and FREE1-mediated functions in plants. These results have been published in Plant Cell in 2019. Thus, we have achieved the original objective two fully. In conclusion, all the original two objectives in the research project have been successfully achieved, which is demonstrated by the publication as well as the research findings summarized in this completion report. This RGC-funded project sheds light into the research about FREE1 function and RST1 involvement in regulation of endomembrane trafficking pathways. Moreover, this project has also nurtured several graduate students, and resulted in publications in prestigious international journals.

14130716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14130716.value: 1. We have identified a plant-specific Bro1-domain protein BRAF, which regulates FREE1 recruitment to the MVB/PVC membrane by competitively binding to the ESCRT-I component Vps23. The data was published in journal Nature Communications in 2018. 2. We have characterized RST1 protein as a negative regulator in vacuolar trafficking pathway. The data was published in journal Plant Cell in 2019. 3. We have uncovered an unconventional role of FREE1 in nuclear transcription regulation. The data was published in journal Nature Plants in 2019. 4. With partially support from this project, we have also trained several excellent postgraduate students with outstanding research outputs as demonstrated by publications of their thesis work in a number of international journals. 5. The project has resulted in a list of outstanding publications in international journals including Plant Cell, Nature Communications, Nature Plants, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, Plant Physiology, and Trends in Plant Science.

14130716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14130716.value: Our studies on the Molecular mechanisms of FREE1 functions in Arabidopsis thaliana have shed lights on our discovery of novel regulators RST1 and BRAF as well as new function of FREE1. At the end, these new mechanisms expanded our understanding towards the complexity and plasticity of protein trafficking pathways in plants. Nevertheless, we shall further expand our understanding on the molecular mechanisms of novel players of these pathways via interactome identification with proteomics techniques on affinity-purified proteins, which could give further information on the functions of these novel regulators. Further research could be done to investigate the possible molecular mechanisms of RST1 as well as their functional relationship with BRAF in plants. Structural determination of RST1 via cryo-EM could also be an interesting future study.

14130716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14130716.value: This RGC-funded project aims to investigate the Molecular mechanisms of FREE1 functions in Arabidopsis thaliana through combined methods including genetic screening, biochemically identification and cell biology analysis. Results derived from this study have provided new insights about the molecular machinery of FREE1 function and FREE1-related new player BRAF AND RST1, as well as their functional implications in plants, with potential implications in future study of trafficking mechanisms of vacuolar transport in plants.

14130816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14130816.value: The mechanisms that instigate human parturition have not been completely understood, though hypotheses such as ‘functional progesterone withdrawal’ and inflammatory signaling have been proposed. Researchers including our group have previously identified panels of genes which were differentially expressed between placentas obtained after spontaneous birth and those after elective cesarean delivery. However, such findings obtained after birth could only reflects the late changes in parturition. To gain insights into the factors leading to the onset of parturition, research must focus at the changes before and around the latent phase of labor. However, there are a number of difficulties encountered: (1) sampling from the human placenta/myometrium at this stage requires invasive procedures which are not feasible or ethical; (2) prospective identification of women at the latent phase of labor who would then establish active labor subsequently is so unreliable that extensive work and costs are needed; (3) human parturition is distinguished from other species, making animal experiments unsuitable. To overcome these problems, we propose a two-phase project: Phase 1: We will focus on a small but well-defined group of women at 40 weeks of gestation without any signs of labor. We will collect their peripheral blood every alternative day until labor is established. The paired blood samples taken just before and just after labor onset (at latent phase) will be retrieved for whole-transcriptome study. We hypothesize that there are significant changes in the RNA levels of certain genes pre- and post-labor onset. These changes are implicated in the initiation of labor. We have preliminarily investigated 3 subjects who required induction of labor at term with gene expression microarrays, and identified 42 genes that were differentially expressed after induction (>2-fold and p<0.05 and q<0.05 after multiple testing adjustment by the False Discovery Rate method). Hence similar changes may occur in subjects undergoing spontaneous labor. We will use RNA-Sequencing to more comprehensively compare the whole-transcriptomes. Phase 2: We will validate the differential expression of genes identified in Phase 1 using reverse-transcriptase quantitative PCR. We will collect serial blood samples as before but from an independent cohort of non-laboring pregnant women. We reason that our two-phase project will pin down a panel of genes implicated in the early events of human parturition. Our data will bring insights into the mechanism triggering labor onset, and make early prediction of term or even preterm delivery more accurate. Effective intervention against preterm delivery may then be possible.

14133016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14133016.value: 特異性組織的形成和分化對多細胞生物來講是至關重要的。在這一過程中有著相同遺傳物質的細胞需要對特定的發育和環境刺激進行特定反應以產生不同組織需要的基因表達。最近新發現的超級增強子被證明對調控細胞內的特異性基因表達起著至關重要的作用。更有發現顯示這些超級增強子本身可以被轉錄而產生seRNA，但是這些seRNA有沒有作用及其如何作用尚未人所知。因此在本項目中我們決定利用骨骼肌成肌細胞形成肌纖維這一分化過程為模式系統探索seRNA的作用機制。通過一系列前期試驗獲得的結果我們認為seRNA不僅有功能而且它們對超級增強子本身的基因調控功能非常重要，因此我們在本項目中提出三個具體目標來進一步探索這其中的分子作用機制。通過這一課題，我們將推進整個seRNA及其增強子研究領域的進步，揭示新的基因調控機制，最終為深入理解細胞組織的生長分化添加新的認知.

14133016.label: Realisation of objectives
14133016.value: In the original proposal we hypothesized that seRNAs regulate gene expression through interacting with hnRNPL protein thus play a central role in SE functionality. To test this hypothesis 3 specific aims/objectives are proposed: We are pleased to report that all 3 aims have been successfully implemented with favorable outcomes. AIM 1: To explore the hnRNPL mediated mechanism underlying seRNA function. To this end, our RNA pull down and RIP assays have provided initial evidences for the interaction between seRNAs and hnRNPL. The above results triggered us to believe hnRNPL is a bona fide protein partner of seRNAs. To further solidify their binding nature, next, we used a series of truncated fragments of seRNA-1 or seRNA-2 to map hnRNPL-interacting regions. Our results suggested a 300 nt region at the 5’ of seRNA-1 (1 - 300 nt) and a 484 nt region at the 3’ of seRNA-2 (901 - 1,384 nt) are essential in mediating the interaction with hnRNPL; of note, the interaction of hnRNPL with 5’ seRNA-1 is comparable or stronger than the full length. Consistently, these domains exhibit high thermostability predicted by RNAfold. HnRNPL protein consists of four RNA recognition motifs. We next sought to dissect the functional relevance of the interaction between seRNAs and hnRNPL. When hnRNPL was knocked down, seRNA-1 target genes, Mb and Apol6, were evidently reduced while seRNA-1 itself was up-regulated, suggesting a functional synergism of hnRNPL with seRNA-1 in activating target gene expression. However, target genes associated with seRNA-2, Atp1a1 and Igsf3, were unaffected upon hnRNPL loss, indicating hnRNPL/seRNA co-action may not apply to this seRNA. This was further strengthened by nuclear run-on assay, which demonstrated that reduced hnRNPL dampened the transcription of Mb, but not Atp1a1. We thus concentrated our efforts on seRNA-1/hnRNPL henceforth. HnRNPL is known to bind to CA-rich motifs in mRNAs. An 8 tandem-repeats of CAAA tract was indeed identified in the 5’ domain of seRNA-1. To test whether this CAAA stretch mediates the interaction between seRNA-1 and hnRNPL, CAAA tract was removed from the FL or the 5’ fragment and used for in vitro RNA pull-down experiments. Expectedly, the deletion completely abolished the strong interaction between FL or the 5’ fragment with hnRNPL. We then tested whether hnRNPL-eRNA binding is associated with the expression of target genes. Through integrating hnRNPL CLIP-seq and RNA-seq in MT, we noticed the increase in expression of neighboring mRNA genes is positively correlated with the number of hnRNPL clusters at the corresponding eRNAs, suggesting a potential activating role of hnRNPL-eRNA binding in the expression of neighboring genes transcriptome-wide. To test this, we performed RNA-seq in hnRNPL knockdown cells. Compared to si-Control, hnRNPL depletion resulted in 153 genes up-regulated and 103 down-regulated, respectively. Importantly, expression of genes associated with hnRNPL-bound eRNAs tend to be altered upon hnRNPL knockdown relative to those associated with non-hnRNPL binding eRNAs. Moreover, these neighboring genes themselves are not enriched for hnRNPL CLIP binding, ruling out these mRNAs are regulated through direct interaction with hnRNPL. Overall, our results further support the notion that hnRNPL-eRNA interaction is critical in regulating target genes expression. Lastly, in mESC cells where seRNAs were identified by GRO-seq, we were able to experimentally confirm hnRNPL binding to several seRNAs. Taken together, these data demonstrate that hnRNPL interaction with eRNAs may be a general phenomenon in cells. AIM 2: To study MyoD/FoxO3 regulation of seRNA transcription To study MyoD regulation of seRNA transcription, GRO-seq was performed in MyoD knockout (MyoD-/-) cells that we recently generated by CRISPR-Cas9. In response to MyoD loss, the expression of MT eRNAs was dramatically diminished, but modestly enhanced for MB eRNAs. As illustrated on seRNA-1, -2 and -5, MyoD depletion almost blocked the dramatic induction of their transcription during differentiation. We also applied knock-down strategy using siRNAs against MyoD. We found that knockdown of MyoD also decreased MT seRNAs, again supporting the activating role of MyoD in seRNAs induction during differentiation. Finally, when MyoD was overexpressed in mouse embryonic 10T1/2 fibroblast cells to trigger myogenic trans-differentiation, we noted induction or increase in seRNAs expression. To further elaborate the direct regulation of MyoD, we confirmed the MyoD binding identified by ChIP-seq on seRNA-1 and -2 loci by ChIP-PCR. In addition, we cloned the TSS regions of these seRNA-1 and -2 harboring MyoD binding sites into a reporter construct. Expectedly, reporter activity was significantly increased during differentiation but markedly reduced upon MyoD repression. Promoter reporters also displayed concomitantly increased activity upon MyoD overexpression in 10T1/2 cells. Moreover, direct binding of MyoD was detected on these promoters during trans-differentiation, indicating MyoD induction of seRNAs is a prominent phenomenon during MyoD directed cell reprogramming. Together, these data solidified the key role of MyoD in inducing eRNA production during myoblast differentiation. AIM 3: To dissect regulatory defects in the CRISPR-Cas9 generated seRNA KO cells. To this aim, we employed CRISPR-Cas9 approach to introduce a small deletion in seRNA-1 locus encompassing the CAAA repeats in C2C12 cells, generating two knockout (KO) clones. RIP assay in the KO cells with hnRNPL antibody failed to retrieve seRNA-1 transcripts as compared to WT cells, suggesting the essential role of this CAAA tract in mediating seRNA-1/hnRNPL interaction. Nevertheless, the expression of hnRNPL was unaltered by the CAAA deletion, ruling out the possibility that the loss of interaction is due to reduction in hnRNPL level. Knowing RNA alternative splicing is a major function of hnRNPL-RNA interaction, we examined whether seRNA-1 was alternatively spliced in the KO cells and found loss of CAAA tract did not affect its splicing, leaving junction sites intact. Nevertheless, removal of CAAA tract appeared to have altered the secondary structure of seRNA-1. To test the functional importance of CAAA tract, we found Mb and Apol6 expression was largely attenuated in the KO cells, underscoring the importance of the interaction between CAAA tract and hnRNPL. Surprisingly, seRNA-1 itself was markedly increased in KO cells. We reason this may be due to altered TF binding in the deletion region; indeed in-silico TF prediction revealed multiple TFs including ETS2, FoxO4 and FoxP1 may lose their binding when CAAA tract is removed. To expand the above findings, we next determined the significance of CAAA tract in regulating seRNA-1 neighboring genes in vivo. To this end, we deleted the CAAA tract taking advantage of CRISPR/Cas9 mediated in vivo genome editing. Compared to AAV9-sgControl group, we observed an expected 86 bp deletion across the genomic locus in mice injected with AAV-sgseRNA-1. In addition, RNA analysis showed a fraction of transcripts with CAAA deletion, confirming the success of in vivo editing. Importantly, consistent with in vitro results from using KO cells, loss of CAAA tract significantly decreased the expression of Mb and Apol6, but strongly induced seRNA-1 level, suggesting the existence of regulatory axis involving CAAA tract-hnRNPL interaction in vivo. Altogether the above results indicate that seRNA-1 interacts with hnRNPL via a CAAA tract in its 5’ - 300 nt region and this motif is critical for hnRNPL binding and activation of neighboring genes both in vitro and in vivo.

14133016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14133016.value: Emerging evidence supports roles of enhancer RNAs (eRNAs) in regulating target gene. Here, we study eRNA regulation and function during skeletal myoblast differentiation. We provide a panoramic view of enhancer transcription and categorization of eRNAs. Master transcription factor MyoD is crucial in activating eRNA production. Super enhancer (se) generated seRNA-1 and -2 promote myogenic differentiation in vitro and in vivo. seRNA-1 regulates expression levels of two nearby genes, myoglobin (Mb) and apolipoprotein L6 (Apol6), by binding to heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein L (hnRNPL). A CAAA tract on seRNA-1 is essential in mediating seRNA-1/hnRNPL binding and function. Disruption of seRNA-1-hnRNPL interaction attenuates Pol II and H3K36me3 deposition at the Mb locus, in coincidence with the reduction of its transcription. Furthermore, analyses of hnRNPL binding transcriptome-wide reveal its association with eRNAs is a general phenomenon in multiple cells. Collectively, we propose that eRNA-hnRNPL interaction represents a mechanism contributing to target mRNA activation. All findings have now been published in Zhao Y. et. al. Nature Communications (2019;10(1):5787).

14133016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14133016.value: Research from our study not only increases our knowledge in the field of transcriptional regulation but also enhances our understanding of molecular regulation in skeletal muscle stem cell behavior and skeletal muscle development. This may eventually lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets for muscle relevant disease such as muscular dystrophy and sarcopenia. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of RNA binding proteins (RBPs) in regulating gene transcription. Based on our current study of hnRNPL in gene regulation, we believe many RBPs possess non-conventional gene regulatory functions We will thus continue to examine their functional mechanisms in the next chapter of the study.

14133016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14133016.value: Skeletal muscle is a form of striated muscle tissue which permits basic functions such as breathing and movement, accounting for ~40% of adult human body weight. Failure of skeletal muscle to develop prenatally leads to embryonic lethality, while the inability to repair or maintain skeletal muscle postnatally leads to a diminished quality of life and sometimes even death. Muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia are examples of deleterious muscle wasting conditions that are prevent in our society. Thus, the ability to regenerate diseased muscle has important medical implications. The cell responsible for muscle regeneration is the satellite cells (SC). The molecular mechanisms that integrate various extracellular signals and intrinsic control to establish the character of SCs during the regeneration are a matter of intense research. Here we have studied and for the first time revealed the function of seRNAs in promoting the regenerative capacity of SCs; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the regulatory mechanisms underlying muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases.

14133316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14133316.value: Background: Osteoporosis and cerebrovascular disease are two common debilitating diseases of old age leading to physical and cognitive impairment respectively. A clinical link between osteoporosis and cerebrovascular disease has been established. It is only recently, however, that osteoporosis has been shown to be strongly associated with impaired bone perfusion. Impaired tissue perfusion is not likely to be organ specific and is very likely to affect several organs simultaneous. That said, neither cerebrovascular disease nor impaired bone perfusion in osteoporosis are not necessarily accompanied by a generalised circulatory impairment. Both osteoporosis and cerebrovascular diseases are clinically silent diseases, with awareness of their existence only becoming manifest when complications such as osteoporotic fracture or stroke occur. This is clearly not ideal. The emphasis should be on detecting these progressive diseases at a much earlier age before they become clinically manifest and when they are likely to be more responsive to therapeutic intervention. MR imaging can detect clinically occult impaired cerebral perfusion and bone perfusion. Protocol: We will study 200 healthy females subjects aged between 60-70 years. These will be recruited from the Jockey Club Centre for Osteoporosis Care and Control (JOCOC). Subjects will be assessed with a clinical questionnaire and a cognitive function test. Dual energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) of the lumbar spine and hip will provide a measure of bone mineral density. High resolution ultrasound of the carotid arteries with measurement of intima media thickness and plaque will provide a quantifiable measure of cerebral large vessel disease which will also be assessed by MR angiography of the intracerebral vessels. Brain perfusion will be further quantified by arterial spin–labeling while the effect of impaired brain perfusion will be analyzed by quantitative grading of white matter changes and silent infarcts, both of which are a good indirect measure of impaired of brain perfusion. Sagittal MR screening of the whole spine will enable identification and reliable semi-quantitative grading of vertebral fracture. Bone perfusion will be assessed by dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI of the L3 lumbar vertebra with quantitative analysis of the time-intensity curve. Significance and value: Establishing a link between impaired bone perfusion in osteoporosis and impaired cerebral perfusion (i.e. cerebrovascular disease) would be a significant step in (a) understanding the pathophysiology of both these common diseases and (b) the development of a single therapy to help both conditions. 背景：骨質疏鬆症和腦血管疾病是兩種常見的老年退行性疾病，分別導致身體和認知功能障礙。臨床工作中已經建立了骨質疏鬆症和腦血管疾病之間的聯繫。然而，最近研究發現，骨質疏鬆症和受損的骨灌注之間有緊密相關。受損組織灌注不太可能具有器官特異性（即某一特定器官），很可能影響到多個器官同時發生。這就是說，無論是腦血管病，或骨質疏鬆症中骨髓缺損灌注都不一定伴發全身血液循環障礙。 骨質疏鬆症和腦血管疾病在初期均無明顯的臨床症狀，直到出現併發症，如骨質疏鬆性骨折或中風發生，才能發現這些疾病的存在。這樣顯然是不理想的。需要加強的是對於這些進展中的疾病，應該做到早期發現，進行臨床治療，或許會取得更好的效果。磁共振成像可以檢測臨床症狀不明顯的受損腦灌注和骨灌注。 研究計劃：我們會通過賽馬會骨質疏鬆症護理和控制中心（JOCOC）選擇200名健康女性，年齡在60-70歲之間參加這次研究。并將對受試者進行臨床調查問卷和認知功能評估測試。此外還需進行腰椎及髖部的雙能X線骨密度（DXA）檢查，頸動脈的高分辨率超聲檢查用來檢測內膜中層厚度及斑塊的測量，磁共振血管造影檢查用來評估腦部大血管疾病。動脈自旋標記可用於量化腦灌注，受損腦灌注的影響將通過白質的變化和無臨床表現的梗塞分級進行量化分析。 這兩種方法都能很好的間接測量受損腦灌注。全脊柱矢狀MR成像用來發現脊椎骨折并提供可靠的半定量分級。骨灌注將通過對第三腰椎的時間-強度曲線進行定量分析。 意義和價值：建立骨質疏鬆症中受損骨灌注和受損腦灌注（即腦血管病）之間的聯繫，意義：（a）了解這兩種常見疾病的病理生理學過程 （b）創造一種療法可以同時用來控制并治療這兩種疾病。

14133316.label: Realisation of objectives
14133316.value: The objective of this study were: a. To establish the link between impaired bone perfusion and impaired cerebral perfusion. b. To determine whether impaired bone perfusion is linked primarily to cerebral large vessel or small vessel disease The rationale behind this study was based on previous studies which have shown how: 1. Reduced bone mineral density was associated with reduced bone perfusion and increased marrow fat 2. Reduced bone density is associated with impaired cognitive function. 3. Impaired cognitive function is associated with reduced brain perfusion. We wish to determine if there was a relationship between (a) bone perfusion and brain perfusion and (b) whether impaired brain perfusion is linked primarily to cerebral large vessel or small vessel disease osteoporosis and cognitive impairment. Uncovering a common aetiological pathway between compromised bone perfusion, osteoporosis, and compromised brain parameters, could strength the possibility of treating both diseases with a similar medication. To this end, we completed all of the following examinations in 99 female subjects (mean age 65 years, range 54-75 years). • Cognitive testing (undertaken by research assistant when patient attended for MRI examination). • Serological examination (hemoglobin, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c levels). • Ultrasound examination common carotid arteries (undertaken by principal investigator) • MRI examination lumbar spine to assess bone perfusion and marrow fat content (performed in PWH MRI centre) • MRI examination brain to assess brain ischemia as assessed by brain volume, hippocampal volume, white matter score, infarct score, and cerebral / cerebrellar volume (performed in PWH MRI centre) Some unavoidable delays were encountered in completing this study. As the participants were research subjects i.e. there was no clinical requirement for them to undergo the necessary DXA and MRI examinations, there was a delay in recruitment as research subjects were forbidden in attending the hospital for much of the last year (2020 and this year 2021) due to COVID 19 restrictions. We also had some delay in data analysis as research staff were working intermittently from home as per COVID restrictions on working within the hospital environment and had returned to mainland China. Data analysis needed to be undertaken within the hospital setting where the necessary workstations are located and could not be performed off site. Nevertheless, despite these delays, we have fully realized the objective of this study, completed required data acquisition and analysis.

14133316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14133316.value: The major new finding of this study was that: (a) Bone perfusion and marrow fat parameters did correlate weakly (r = 0.228-0.293) with brain volume parameters (brain parenchymal fractional volume, hippocampal fractional volume and white matter fractional volume) which are an indirect feature of impaired brain perfusion. (b) Overall impaired bone perfusion is likely to correlate with impaired brain perfusion. This impaired brain perfusion is more likely to be driven by small vessel disease rather than large vessel disease as evidenced by no relationship being found between large vessel disease parameters (common carotid intima media thickness and MR angiography score) (c) There was also a weak correlation between serological parameters (fasting blood glucose, HBA1c, r = 0.269-0.480) with brain volume parameters (brain parenchymal volume, hippocampal volume and white matter volume and cerebellar blood flow). (d) That said, bone perfusion did not correlate with any direct indices of brain perfusion/blood flow (such as white matter hyperintensity score, infarct score, MR angiography score, or arterial spin labelling blood flow scores). We are currently preparing a manuscript detailing our research findings which will be submitted for publication with 4 weeks.

14133316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14133316.value: Although the relationship we found between bone perfusion and brain parameters is weak, we believe this association can be stretched by analyzing this greater depth the MR brain data. In particular, we are looking at ways to separate the arterial spin labeling parameters between central (i.e. larger) and terminal (i.e. (smaller) branches as all of the evidence uncovered by this study to date, suggests that the bone: brain relationship is through small vessel disease rather than large vessel disease. One of the problems with the study design, which we anticipated, is the while direct perfusion imaging could be performed on the bone, direct perfusion imaging could not be performed on the brain as perfusion imaging can only be performed on one site at any one time. Therefor arterial spin labelling which is an indirect measure of bone blood flow was performed on the brain. This is a good measure of brain blood flow though not as good as direct brain perfusion. This may have compromised the result. This could be overcome by asking subjects to return twice for MRI examination, once for MR perfusion imaging of the spine and one week later for perfusion imaging of the brain.

14133316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14133316.value: The study set out to establish a relationship between bone perfusion and brain perfusion. The rationale for the study was an already established relationship between (i) bone perfusion and osteoporosis and (ii) osteoporosis and cognitive impairment. Uncovering a common aetiological pathway between compromised bone perfusion, osteoporosis, and compromised brain parameters, could strength the possibility of treating both diseases with a similar medication. We studied 99 female postmenopausal patients with and without mild cognitive impairment clinically. This study found that there is a weak association between bone perfusion and deteriorating brain parameters. Reduced bone perfusion was associated with reduced brain parenchymal, hippocampal and white matter fractional volumes. Both hippocampal and white matter fractional volume reflect small vessel arterial disease. There was no association between impaired bone perfusion and large vessel disease parameters. Correlation between bone perfusion and brain parameters was similar to that between other risk factors such as fasting blood glucose and increased glycosylated haemoglobin (Hb A1c). We plan to analyse the brain perfusion data to uncover ways of separating the central and terminal elements of the brain blood flow data which we believe will strengthen the association between bone perfusion and brain perfusion.

14134916.label: Realisation of objectives
14134916.value: All the stated objectives have been completed (100%). The following describes how the objectives have been achieved: Study Setting This project was a collaborative, multicentre study involving 13 Asia Pacific countries/regions. The study sites included Mainland China, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, Brunei, Pakistan and Hong Kong. The participating centres included members of the Asia Pacific Working Group (APWG) on Colorectal Cancer (CRC) Screening, which have previously collaborated in large-scale research projects. Participants The inclusion criteria were consistently adopted in all the study sites, which include: (i) Age between 50 to 75 years; (ii) The absence of current or previous symptoms suggestive of CRC, and (iii) Not having received any CRC screening tests in the past 5 years. Exclusion criteria included: (i). A personal history of CRC, colonic adenoma, diverticular disease, inflammatory bowel disease, prosthetic heart valve or vascular graft surgery, (ii) family history of familial CRC syndromes and (iii). Medical conditions which were contraindications for colonoscopy. Each eligible participant completed a self-administered survey on their age, gender, family history of CRC, smoking status, drinking habits, past medical history, and chronic use of medications. The derivation and validation cohort We recruited 7,954 asymptomatic subjects who received screening colonoscopy in more than 13 study sites in the Asia Pacific region. We conducted a simple random sampling to allocate two-third of these subjects (5,303 participants) to the derivation cohort and evaluated the independent risk factors for APN. The other 2,651 screening participants formed an independent validation cohort. In the derivation cohort, the association between the detection of APN and each risk factor was examined by the Chi-square tests. The factors examined included the recognized risk factors for colorectal neoplasia, including age, sex, family history of CRC (in first-degree relatives [FDR]), smoking, drinking, body mass index, self-reported medical conditions, and use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents or aspirin and the most advanced finding of the distal lesions. All variables with initial p <0.05 in univariate analysis were included in a binary logistic regression model with APN as the outcome. Development of the risk scores A weighting was assigned to each independent variable in the risk score, applying the corresponding adjusted odds ratio (AOR) halved and rounded to the nearest integer. The risk score for each subject is the sum of all the risk factors. We used the following categories to classify the most advanced distal findings: “no polyps”; “hyperplasia”; “tubular adenoma<10cm”; and “advanced lesion”, since the histological feature of the distal lesions has been recognized as a determining factor for the prevalence of APN. Advanced lesion is defined as CRC, or any colorectal adenoma ≥ 10 mm in diameter; lesions with high grade dysplasia, villous or tubulovillous histologic characteristics; or any combination thereof. Statistical analysis The proportion of APN was evaluated according to each score in the derivation cohort. The score with a magnitude closest to and below the overall proportion of APN was allocated to the category “average risk”, whilst scores above were assigned as “high risk”. An additional binary logistic regression model was constructed by entering all the significant variables identified by the derivation cohort analysis, and the AORs were evaluated in the validation cohort. The Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit statistic was adopted to assess the reliability of the final model, where p>0.05 indicates a good match of predicted risk over observed risk. To evaluate the predictive ability of the scoring system, a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was constructed and the concordance (c)-statistics was used to reflect the discriminative ability of the prediction tool. The Cochran-Armitage test of trend was used to compare the prevalence of APN according to each score. The resources required to detect APN was estimated by the Number Needed to Screen (NNS) and the Number Needed to Refer (NNR) for colonoscopy to detect one APN. Achievements: Characteristics of participants The mean age was 58.19 years (SD ±6.57 years); 48.5% were male; 14.8% were smokers; and 15.3% had a family history of CRC in a first-degree relative. The characteristics of the validation cohort were similar to the derivation set in all variables investigated (p>0.05). The prevalence of APN in the derivation and validation cohort was 3.2% and 3.4% (p=0.688), respectively. Predictors in the derivation cohort According to multivariate analysis, age (≥71 vs. ≤ 50: AOR=4.25, 95% CI=1.54-11.73, p<0.001); family history (AOR=1.51, 95% CI=1.03-2.23, p=0.035), smoking (AOR=2.11, 95% CI=1.46-3.04, p<0.001) and distal finding (advanced neoplasia: AOR=7.17, 95% CI=4.74-10.87, p<0.001; non-advanced adenoma 5-10 mm: AOR=2.27, 95% CI=1.04-3.69, p=0.001) were found to have positive association with APN. Development and validation of risk score with distal findings A risk stratification system to predict APN was developed by incorporating distal findings. Points were assigned to the below risk factors for APN: age (≤ 60=0, 61-70=3, ≥71=4); family history of CRC present for a first-degree relative (absent=0, present=2); past or current smoker (no=0, yes=2) and distal findings (normal=0, hyperplastic polyps=0, non-advanced adenoma<4mm=0, Non-advanced adenoma 5-9 mm=2, advanced neoplasia=7). The scoring system ranged from 0 to 15 points and was divided into two tiers as: 0-3 “average risk” (AR) and ≥ 4 “high risk” (HR). Each screening participant received a score equivalent to the sum of their risk factors. In the derivation cohort, 81.0% (4,295) and 19.0% (1,008) of subjects were classified as “average risk” and “high risk”, respectively, in the derivation cohort. The prevalence of colorectal neoplasia in the two tiers (AR and HR) was 23.8% (95% CI=22.6 to 25.1), and 64.1% (95% CI=61.1 to 67.0), respectively. The corresponding prevalence of APN was 2.0% (95% CI=1.6 to 2.4) and 8.5% (95% CI=6.9 to 10.4). Among the validation cohort, the prevalence of colorectal neoplasia in the two tiers (AR and HR) was 23.0% (95% CI=21.2 to 24.8), and 63.5% (95% CI=59.4 to 67.5), respectively. Their corresponding prevalence rates of APN were 1.9% (95% CI=1.3 to 2.5) and 9.4% (95% CI=7.2 to 12.1). Subjects in the HR group had 5.08-fold (95% CI=3.38 to 7.62, p<0.001) increased prevalence of APN than that in the AR group. The c-statistics of the scoring algorithm was 0.74 (95% CI=0.68-0.79). The Hosemer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit statistic evaluating the reliability of the validation set had a p value >0.05. The respective NNR and NNS was 11 (95% C.I. 10-13) and 15 (95% CI=12-17). The above analysis was repeated excluding the variable “distal findings” (i.e. including sociodemographic and clinical variables only). The scoring system ranged from 0 to 10 points and is divided into two tiers as: 0-3 “average risk” (AR) and ≥ 4 “high risk” (HR). Points were assigned to the below risk factors for APN: age (≤ 50=0, 51-55=2, 56-65=3, 66-70=4, >70=5); family history of CRC in a FDR (absent=0, present=2); and past or current smoking (no=0, yes=3). Subjects in the HR group had 3.40-fold (95% CI=2.22 to 5.22, p<0.001) increased prevalence of APN than that in the AR group. Also, the HR group had 1.56-fold (95% CI=1.39 to 1.74, p<0.001) increased prevalence of colorectal neoplasia. The c-statistics of the scoring algorithm was 0.67 (95% CI=0.61-0.73), implying good discriminatory capability. The Hosemer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit statistic evaluating the reliability of the validation set had a p value >0.05, implying a close match between predicted risk and real risk. The NNR and NNS were 18 (95% CI=15-21) and 29 (95% CI=25-33), respectively.
