14134916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14134916.value: In this study, we have recruited 7,954 asymptomatic subjects in 13 Asia Pacific regions. The prevalence of advanced proximal neoplasia (APN) in the derivation and validation cohorts was 3.2% and 3.4%, respectively. Age, smoking status, family history of CRC in a first degree relative, and distal findings were found to be significant predictors. Utilizing the scoring system, 79.5% and 20.5% in the validation cohort was classified as “Average Risk” (AR) and “High Risk” (HR), respectively. The prevalence of APN in the AR and HR groups was 1.9% and 9.4%, respectively; subjects in the HR group had 5.08-fold (95% CI 3.38 to 7.62, p<0.001) increased prevalence of APN than the AR group. Also, the HR group had 2.77-fold (95% CI 2.50 to 3.06) increased prevalence of colorectal neoplasia. The c-statistics of the scoring algorithm was 0.74 (95% C.I. 0.68-0.79), implying good discriminatory capability. The Hosemer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit statistic evaluating the reliability of the validation set had a p value >0.05, implying a close match between predicted risk and real risk. Research outcome: The present study devised a risk score for prediction of APN based on four elementary variables, namely age, family history of CRC present for a first-degree relative, past or current smoker and distal findings. The risk algorithm was found to have a good predictive capability with a concordance statistic of 0.74 and a satisfactory goodness-of-fit. In addition, subjects in the high-risk group were found to have a 5.08-fold increased risk of APN when compared with those in the average risk group. It is recommended that subjects who receive FS screening and score ≥ 4 points should be referred for colonoscopy workup (Refer to Table 4 of "Validation of a scoring system to predict the risk of advanced proximal neoplasia for 2 colorectal cancer screening: a multi-centre study in Asia Pacific regions"). The study findings are particular relevant to be used in Asia Pacific countries or regions where FS is used as a primary screening tool.

14134916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14134916.value: This study developed and validated clinical scoring systems from a prospective, multi-centre colonoscopy trial that could inform individualization of screening strategies for detection of APN. The strength of the individualized approach to CRC screening is that use of an APN risk score allows detection of more APNs, as compared with a conventional strategy in which supplementary colonoscopy after FS is based entirely on distal colon ﬁndings. The scoring system based on age, smoking status, family history, and distal findings is useful in predicting the risk of APN. The scoring algorithm based on elementary patient information is simple to use, and thus could be adopted in primary care settings for risk stratification. The findings inform the need for subsequent arrangement of colonoscopy appointments. In addition, utilizing the scoring system requires low levels of colonoscopic resources, as reflected by the low NNS (11 [95% C.I. 10-13]) and NNR (15 [95% CI=12-17]). It is recommended that participants who receive FS screening and score ≥ 4 points should be referred for colonoscopy. This scoring system should be externally validated in other population groups. Also, the effectiveness of various strategies that aims to enhance its implementation in screening practices should be further explored.

14134916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14134916.value: This is a predictive study on an outcome (namely advanced proximal neoplasia [APN]), which could be detected by screening colonoscopy but not by flexible sigmoidoscopy (both are acceptable primary screening tests according to guidelines). We aimed to classify an individual as average risk (AR) or high risk (HR) according to their own characteristics. We recruited 7,954 asymptomatic subjects who received screening colonoscopy in 13 study sites in the Asia Pacific region, and developed a scoring system ranging from 0-15 divided into AR and HR based on the scores (0-3 vs. ≥ 4). The performance of the scoring system for predicting APN was examined. We devised a scoring algorithm based on four elementary variables, namely age, family history of CRC in a first-degree relative, past or current smoker, and distal findings to estimate the risk of APN; subjects in the HR group had 5.08-fold increased prevalence of APN than the AR group. The risk score had a good discriminatory capability with good match between predicted and real risk. This scoring system can be used by primary care practitioners to estimate the risk of APN after a screening participant has received flexible sigmoidoscopy to determine if subsequent colonoscopy workup is required.

14135016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14135016.value: The aim of this proposed project is to study the link between body lean muscle mass, muscle strength together with myokines and LBX1 expression in serum and muscle tissue with bone mineral density and bone quality in girls with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients (AIS) of different curve severity. AIS is a complex three-dimensional spinal deformity mostly occurring during puberty with reported prevalence of 2–4% worldwide. Despite the high prevalence and the associated with morbidities in severe cases, the current main treatment modality with bracing and corrective surgery remain unsatisfactory. Studies by our group and others have shown significantly lower bone mineral density (BMD) at various skeletal regions in over 30% of AIS. The osteopenia could persist into adulthood thus predisposing to osteoporosis and other related complications in later life. Our group has further shown that in addition to osteopenia, abnormal bone morphology, microarchitecture and volumetric bone density are all important prognostic factor for curve progression in AIS. During pubertal growth, bone adapts its structure and strength to withstand mechanical loads through the functional muscle-bone units. From our recent large-scale GWAS study, muscle-related genes (e.g. LBX1) were found to be associated with the susceptibility of having AIS. Other studies also suggested possible functional role of paravertebral muscles in the development and progression of scoliosis in AIS. The mechanism and whether this is a systemic muscle functional abnormality remains poorly understood. We hypothesize that muscle tissue might not only regulate bone mass through direct mechano-transduction effect, but also via paracrine and endocrine signaling pathways in the form of soluble factors (myokines) that can significantly influence systemic bone homeostasis, thus affecting the bone mass, microstructure and mechanical bone strength that could contribute to the initiation and/or progression in AIS. We therefore proposed to carry out a clinical and tissue level molecular study using well-established protocols, to elucidate the type of myokines, LBX1 expression in serum and muscle tissue - and its relations to bone metabolism, microstructure in AIS Vs control subjects. This study will be complementary to our on-going GRF funded study (Project Number 14116415 2015/16). The findings from this proposed study will help to advance our understanding on the link and cross-talk between muscle and BMD and bone quality- their possible contribution to the etiopathogenesis of AIS which might inform potential therapeutic strategies targeting at the functional muscle-bone unit locally and systemically. 本項目旨在研究青少年特發性脊柱側彎（adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, AIS）不同彎度女性患者的肌肉量、肌肉強度及肌肉激素與LBX1在血清和肌肉組織中的表達，同骨密度、骨質量間的聯繫。 AIS是一種多發于青春期的複雜三維脊柱畸形，發病率為2％﹣4％。儘管該病具有高發病率，作為目前主要的治療方式，支架佩戴和矯形手術通常仍難以達到滿意的效果。我們團隊與外界的研究已經表明超過30％的AIS患者在多個骨區域存在較低的骨密度。AIS患者的骨質缺乏可持續到成年期，因此易在晚年出現骨質疏鬆及其他相關並發症。我們團隊還發現，除了骨質缺乏之外，骨形態、骨微結構及體積骨密度異常均是AIS彎度進展的預後因素。 在青春期發育時，骨骼通過功能性肌肉﹣骨骼單位來調整其結構與強度以適應力學負荷。我們最近的大樣本GWAS研究表明，肌肉相關基因（如LBX1）與AIS的易感性相關。其他研究也發現了椎旁肌在AIS發生、發展中潛在的功能性作用。但其機制及是否為系統性肌肉功能異常仍不清楚。我們推測肌肉組織對骨量的調功可能不僅通過直接的力學傳導作用，而且以可溶性因子（肌肉激素，可顯著影響系統性骨代謝平衡）的形式通過旁分泌與內分泌信號通路發揮作用，從而調控影響AIS發生、發展的骨量、骨微結構及骨強度。 本研究將是我們在研的GRF項目（項目編號：14116415 2015/16）的補充。本研究的發現將有助於進一步探索肌肉、骨密度及骨質量在AIS發病機制中的作用，並可能為AIS在功能性肌肉﹣骨單位的水平提供局部性或系統性的治療策略。

14135416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14135416.value: Approximately, one in six couples suffers from infertility. Transfer of good-quality in vitro fertilized (IVF) embryos does not always result in successful implantation and viable pregnancy. It has long been thought that endometrial factors contribute to about 50% of implantation failure. Chronic endometritis (CE) is commonly diagnosed in women with unexplained infertility. Antibiotic treatment has been shown to improve reproductive outcomes in certain women with CE. Microbial colonization of the endometrium may have functional significance on reproductive failure, but has never been studied systematically. In our pilot study, using broad-range PCR targeting all bacterial species, we have shown that bacteria were readily detectable in the endometrial fluid samples of women with recurrent miscarriage (RM) or repeated implantation failure (RIF) after IVF treatment. Leveraging on our experience in studying the cervical microbiome, the comprehensive quantitative profile of all bacterial taxa in the cervix, we propose to study the endometrial microbiome and infertility. In Module #1, we hypothesize that the endometrial microbiomes in (i) the women in whom embryo transfer (ET) resulted in a successful outcome (i.e. a clinical pregnancy) are significantly different from (ii) the women in whom ET resulted in a failure. To test this, we will determine the abundances of >9,600 bacteria in the endometrial fluid samples of women immediately before ET. We will test if any bacteria are differentially abundant between groups (i) and (ii). We will establish if their abundances have any impact on the rates of implantation, pregnancy and miscarriage. In Module #2, we hypothesize that the endometrial microbiomes in women with RM, or women with RIF are different from those in fertile women (FW). To test this, we will profile and compare the RM, RIF and FW endometrial microbiomes. We expect to identify bacteria that are differentially abundant in the endometrium of women with RM or RIF, compared with that of FW. In Module #3, to gain insights into the distribution of the differentially abundant bacteria identified in Modules #1 and #2 in anatomical sites proximal to the uterus, we will compare their abundances in endometrial fluid, cervical canal, and ecto-cervix of the same woman. Our proposed work will be the first systematic investigation into the endometrial microbiome and establish its functional significance, if any, in reproductive failure. Our work should help planning of future work to verify if specific antibiotic treatment may help to improve outcome in this group of infertile women.

14135416.label: Realisation of objectives
14135416.value: BACKGROUND: Approximately, one in six couples suffers from infertility. Transfer of good-quality in vitro fertilized (IVF) embryos does not always result in successful implantation and viable pregnancy. It has long been thought that endometrial factors contribute to about 50% of implantation failure. Chronic endometritis (CE) is commonly diagnosed in women with unexplained infertility. Despite antibiotic treatment has been shown to improve reproductive outcomes in certain women with CE, the screening for CE in infertile women is not popular in routine practice because of several reasons. First, the detection of CE requires hysteroscopy and/or endometrial sampling for histological (presence of plasma cells in the endometrial stroma) or microbiological investigations (Gram-negative staining and culture), which involve additional time, labor and expertise. Second, these histology- or culture-based methods are only moderately sensitive, and may not detect bacteria that do not stain prominently in microscopy or grow well in culture. Most importantly, it is unknown whether those detected microbes are benign commensals or harmful pathogens. To-date, our knowledge on the entire collection of bacteria colonizing the endometrium (the endometrial microbiome) is still limited. HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesize that the certain bacteria colonizing the endometrium may have functional significance on reproductive failure. SUMMARY: To test the hypothesis, we have systematically measured the endometrial abundances of all bacteria of infertile women in three modules, which correspond to Objectives #1 to #3 (Section 5.2). Using a culture-independent approach (sequencing of the bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA gene), we investigated the endometrial microbiotas of women with unsuccessful outcome for in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer, recurrent miscarriage, or repeated implantation failure. Our results illustrated that, compared with fertile women, these three groups of infertile women had endometrial samples with significantly different abundances of certain bacteria (pg. 40-45 of this PDF, Part C, Conference #2, ASPIRE 2021, Figs. 1-3, titles highlighted in blue). Our data suggest that reproductive failure is associated with an altered endometrial microbiome. Notably, the ectocervical, endocervical and endometrial levels of the above-identified bacteria in the same woman were different (Figs. 4-5). Thus, ectocervical or endocervical microbiome may not fully reflect the endometrial microbiota. Further work is warranted to explore the potential of endometrial microbiome in subtyping the infertile women or predicting their reproductive outcomes. MODULE/OBJECTIVE #1: Endometrial samples were collected precisely 7 days after the luteinizing hormone surge in a natural cycle from 64 women (>55, the required sample size) before they underwent IVF-ET. The collection of endometrial fluid was performed via a double-sheathed catheter to minimize contamination by cervical and vaginal microbiota. Of these, 25 women ended in live birth (successful outcome) and 39 were not pregnant (unsuccessful outcome). Twelve bacteria with increased abundances and 4 bacteria with decreased abundances in the endometrial samples of women with unsuccessful outcome for IVF-ET, compare with those from women with a successful outcome for IVF-ET (pg. 40-45, Conference ASPIRE 2021, Fig. 1A). To summarize the above-identified bacteria in each woman, a differentially abundant microbiota score was devised. The score was calculated by dividing the total abundances of the 12 bacteria with increased abundances in women with unsuccessful outcomes by the total abundances of the 4 bacteria with decreased abundances in women with unsuccessful outcomes. This score was higher in the women with unsuccessful outcomes than those with successful outcomes (Mann-Whitney, p =1.1 ×10^-6, Fig. 1B). Using the 75th percentile of the successful group as a threshold for calling a positive test, 35 of the 39 women with unsuccessful outcome (true positives, 89.7%) and 6 of the 25 women with successful outcome (false positives, 24%) were identified. To explore whether the differentially abundant bacteria in endometrial samples may predict unsuccessful outcome for IVF-ET in a more realistic clinical setting, we performed five-fold cross validation. Area-under-ROC-curve (AUROC), optimal sensitivity and specificity were 0.580, 0.673 and 0.592, respectively. MODULE/OBJECTIVE #2: In total, endometrial samples from 89 women (>69, the required sample size) were sequenced. First, of these, microbiotas from 52 women with recurrent miscarriage (RM, a history of ≥3 miscarriages <20 weeks of gestation) and 19 fertile women (FW) were compared. FW had live birth resulted from a pregnancy before or 1 year after collection of the study sample. Fifteen bacteria with increased abundances and 25 bacteria with decreased abundances in the endometrial samples of women with RM, compare with those from FW (pg. 40-45, Conference ASPIRE 2021, Fig. 2A). To summarize, the differentially abundant microbiota score was calculated by dividing the total abundances of the 15 bacteria with increased abundances in women with RM by the total abundances of the 25 bacteria with decreased abundances. This score was higher in the women with RM than the FW (Mann-Whitney, p =1.8 ×10^-5, Fig. 2B). Using the 75th percentile of the FW as a threshold for calling a positive test, 36 of the 52 women with RM (true positives, 69%) and 5 of the 19 FW (false positives, 26%) were identified. To explore whether the differentially abundant bacteria in endometrial samples may predict RM, we performed five-fold cross validation. AUROC, sensitivity and specificity were 0.688, 0.703 and 0.783, respectively. Second, microbiotas from 18 women with repeated implantation failure (RIF) and the above 19 FW were also compared. RIF is defined as failure to achieve a clinical pregnancy after transfer of ≥4 good quality embryos in ≥3 IVF treatment cycles in a woman aged < 40 years. Forty-eight bacteria with increased abundances and 19 bacteria with decreased abundances in the endometrial samples of women with RIF, compared with those from FW (Fig. 3A). To summarize, the differentially abundant microbiota score was calculated by dividing the total abundances of the 48 bacteria with increased abundances in women with RIF by the total abundances of the 19 bacteria with decreased abundances. This score was higher in the women with RIF than the FW (Mann-Whitney, p =1.4 ×10^-7, Fig. 3B). Using the 75th percentile of the FW as a threshold for calling a positive test, all 18 women with RIF (true positives, 100%) and 5 of the 19 FW (false positives, 26%) were identified. To explore whether the differentially abundant bacteria in endometrial samples may predict RIF, we performed five-fold cross validation. AUROC, sensitivity and specificity were 0.718, 0.880 and 0.667, respectively. MODULE/OBJECTIVE #3: Lastly, we explore whether sampling microbiota from the endometrium may be replaced by sampling from the ecto- or endo-cervix which are more accessible. To address that, the abundances of the 123 differentially abundant bacteria (107 unique bacteria) in Objectives #1 and #2 were compared across the endometrial samples, endo-cervical and ecto-cervical samples of the same woman. This was performed on 105 women (>39, the required sample size), including women with successful or unsuccessful outcome for IVF-ET, women with RM, RIF as well as FW. Of the tested bacteria, 33 unique bacteria were shown to have significantly different abundances across the three anatomical sites (Friedman p <.05, pg. 40-45, Conference ASPIRE 2021, Figs. 4 & 5). To identify the pairwise comparison for which the abundances were different, the posthoc Dunn’s test was performed. The abundances of 29 bacteria (27% of 107) were observed to be different between the endometrial and the endocervical or the ectocervical samples (Dunn’s test, p<.05, Figs. 4 & 5).

14135416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14135416.value: Chronic endometritis (CE) is commonly diagnosed in women with unexplained infertility, but screening for CE by histology- or culture-based methods are only moderately sensitive. Most importantly, it is unknown whether those detected microbes are benign commensals or harmful pathogens. Hence, using the culture-independent method, namely amplicon sequencing of the bacterial 16S rRNA gene, we have embarked in this project to systematically measure the abundance of the entire collection of bacteria colonizing the endometrium (endometrial microbiome) of 3 well-defined groups of infertile women. We hypothesized that the certain bacteria colonizing the endometrium may have functional significance on reproductive failure. To test this hypothesis, we investigated the endometrial microbiotas of women with (i) an unsuccessful outcome for IVF-ET, (ii) RM, and (iii) RIF. Compared with women with a successful outcome for IVF-ET or fertile women (FW), these three groups of infertile women had endometrial samples with significantly different abundances of 16, 40 and 67 bacteria, respectively (pg.40-45 of this PDF, Part C, Conference #2, ASPIRE 2021, Figs. 1A, 2A and 3A, titles highlighted in blue). To summarize the ratio of endometrial abundances of bacteria identified to be increased in the respective adverse condition and those bacteria identified to be decreased, we calculated a differentially abundant microbiota score for each woman (see section 5.3). Using the 75th percentile score of the successful or fertile group as the threshold to call a positive test, 89.7% of women with an unsuccessful outcome for the subsequent IVF-ET, 69% of women with RM, and 100% women with RIF could be identified (Part C, Conference #2, ASPIRE 2021, Figs. 1B, 2B and 3B). To minimize data overfitting and to explore the predictive performance of differentially abundant bacteria in the endometrium in a larger and more realistic population as can be seen in a clinical setting, we performed the well-accepted technique of cross-validation. In essence, the dataset was first partitioned into the training and validation sets with approximately equal ratio of subjects with or without the adverse condition. Then, differentially abundant bacteria, differentially abundant microbiota score and a threshold were determined from the training set to form a model. Finally, AUROC, sensitivity and specificity of the model in predicting the adverse condition were assessed in the validation set, which comprise only samples not involved in building the model. The cross-validated AUROC of the models are 0.580, 0.688 and 0.718 for predicting unsuccessful outcome for IVF-ET, RM and RIF, respectively.

14135416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14135416.value: Our data suggest that the panels of differentially abundant bacteria identified in this study (Objectives #1 and #2) possess moderate potential in subtyping the infertile women or predicting their reproductive outcomes. To pave the way for further development, we also explored whether sampling from cervix, which is more accessible, may replace endometrial sampling. However, our data showed that the ectocervical, endocervical and endometrial levels of nearly one-third of the above-identified bacteria in the same woman were different (pg.40-45 of this PDF, Part C, ASPIRE2021, Figs. 4-5). Based on this, we propose that endometrial sampling is cannot be replaced by cervical sampling. Further, to save the time and cost of sequencing, quantitative PCR assays targeting the identified bacteria may be developed. However, the performance of such qPCR-based assays must be validated again. Lastly, since the effect of ethnic background on endometrial microbiome is not known, the results from our study must also be replicated in ethnic groups other than Chinese. That being said, we presented results to illustrate that endometrial microbiota is indeed associated with reproductive failure. In the longer term, it is hope that a more specific and hence effective antibiotic treatment will be developed for this group of women.

14135416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14135416.value: Approximately, one in six couples suffers from infertility. Transfer of good-quality in vitro fertilized (IVF) embryos does not always result in a viable pregnancy. Chronic endometritis (CE), a subtle but persistent inflammation of the inner lining of the uterine cavity, is commonly diagnosed in women with unexplained infertility. Antibiotic treatment has been shown to improve reproductive outcomes in certain women with CE. However, it is unknown whether those detected/targeted microbes are benign or harmful, since our knowledge on the entire collection of bacteria colonizing the endometrium (the endometrial microbiome) is limited. In this research project, we sequenced the endometrial microbiome of infertile and fertile women. Our data have shown that the levels of certain bacteria were significantly higher in women with an unsuccessful IVF outcome (not pregnant), compared with those with a successful IVF outcome (resulting in a live birth baby). Similarly, the levels of certain bacteria were higher in women with recurrent miscarriage (a history of ≥3 miscarriages) or repeated implantation failure (≥4 good quality embryos in ≥3 IVF treatment cycles), compared with fertile women. In a longer run, we reason that antibiotic treatment targeting for curing the identified bacteria may improve reproductive outcomes in women with unexplained infertility.

14136416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14136416.value: Our aim is to identify and functionally characterize novel long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) epigenetically suppressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). HCC is one of the most lethal cancers and has high incidence rate worldwide. Aberrant epigenetic regulations such as DNA methylation and histone modification are involved in the deregulation of critical genes in HCC. Recently, a new class of RNA called long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) is shown to have important roles in HCC. However, study on lncRNAs with tumor suppressor functions was limited and mechanisms underlying lncRNAs dysregulation in cancer were largely unexplored. Our genome-wide lncRNA expression microarray showed that two lncRNAs named TCAM1P and RP11-598D14.1 (arbitrarily named DN2 and DN5 respectively) were significantly upregulated in HCC cells upon either DZnep or 5-azacytidine treatments, which inhibited H3K27 trimethylation and DNA methylation respectively. Inhibition of Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 (EZH2) by shRNAs upregulated DN2 and DN5 expression in HCC cells, whereas overexpression of EZH2 in non-tumor hepatocyte MIHA cells downregulated their expression. Chromatin immunoprecipitation showed that enrichment of EZH2, polycomb repressive complex 2 core members EED and SUZ12, and H3K27me3 were higher at both DN2 and DN5 promoters in HCC cells, while inhibition of EZH2 significantly reduced their occupancies. The levels of both lncRNAs were dramatically reduced in HCC cell lines and human HCC tissues. Moreover, inhibition of either DN2 or DN5 promoted cell proliferation, colony formation and cell transformation. Our gene expression microarray showed that loss of either DN2 or DN5 expression induced alteration of important cancer-associated pathways. RNA pull down assay and mass spectrometer identified proteins with potential interaction with DN2 and DN5. Western blotting showed that IGF2BP1 and HIST1H1C had interactions with DN2, while STAU1 had interactions with DN5. RNA immunoprecipitation showed that the RNA-protein interactions were observed intracellularly, which suggested that DN2 and DN5 potentially exhibited their functions through the interaction with the proteins. Our preliminary results showed that epigenetically silencing of DN2 and DN5 possessed critical functions in HCC development. Here, we intended to 1) unravel the mechanisms underlying the silencing of DN2 and DN5; 2) further characterize the function of DN2 and DN5; 3) delineate the regulating mechanisms of DN2 and DN5; 4) identify the targets regulated by DN2 and DN5 that contributed to HCC development; 5) study the clinical relevance of both lncRNAs. Knowledge gained from this project will advance the understanding of the biological roles of lncRNAs in HCC. 本課題的目的是鑒別在肝癌中表達沉默的新的長鏈非編碼RNA (lncRNA)並對其進行功能分析。 肝癌的發病率高而預後差。表型遺傳學機制如DNA甲基化及組蛋白修飾對肝癌中關鍵基因的表達失調起了重要作用。最近的研究表明長鏈非編碼RNA在肝癌發生發展中具有重要作用。 然而，對具有抑癌活性的lncRNA的研究非常有限，lncRNA在腫瘤中表達失調的機制目前仍不清楚。我們前期的lncRNA表達晶片結果表明兩種名為DN2及DN5的lncRNA在肝癌中受DNA甲基化及組蛋白H3K27甲基化的調控： 抑制組蛋白H3K27甲基化酶EZH2顯著上調DN2及DN5的表達；過表達EZH2則顯著下調DN2及DN5的表達。 DN2及DN5在肝癌細胞及組織中表達顯著下調； 抑制DN2或DN5表達促進細胞增殖，集落形成及細胞轉化。基因表達晶片結果表明抑制DN2或DN5表達誘導癌症相關基因的改變。 RNA下拉實驗及質譜分析表明IGF2BP1及HIST1H1C是DN2及DN5的作用蛋白質。 在本課題，我們將1）：解析DN2及DN5表達沉默的機制；2）：進一步研究DN2及DN5的功能；3）闡明DN2及DN5的調控機制；4）鑒別受DN2及DN5調控的靶分子；5）研究DN2及DN5的臨床意義。 本課題的研究結果將有助於加深對肝癌中lncRNA生物學功能的認識。

14136816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14136816.value: Background EUS – guided choledocho-duodenostomy (ECDS) is an established option for bile duct drainage in unresectable malignant distal common bile duct (CBD) strictures when endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) fails. However, how primary ECDS compares with ERCP with covered self-expanding metallic stents (CSEMS) in unresectable malignant distal CBD strictures is uncertain. Aims and hypothesis The aim of the current study is to compare primary ECDS versus ERCP with CSEMS in unresectable malignant distal CBD strictures. We hypothesis that ECDS is associated with a higher 1-year stent patency rate. Methods This would be an international multi-center randomised controlled study conducted amongst 6 to 8 high-volume international institutions. Consecutive patients admitted for obstructive jaundice due to unresectable primary malignant distal CBD strictures would be recruited. The patients would be randomized to receive either ECDS or ERCP with CSEMS. The primary outcome is the 1-year stent patency rate. Secondary outcomes include technical success, clinical success, adverse events, re-intervention rates and mortality. Sample size calculation Assuming a 20% difference in 1-year stent patency betwenen ECDS and ERCP with CSEMS (87% vs 67%), with a 2-sided P value of 0.05 and a power of 80%, 69 patients would be required in each group. Taking into account a 20% dropout rate, 83 patients would be required in each group. Timeline and feasibility Patient recruitment would be conducted over a 2-year period. Each institution is required to recruit around 10 to 12 patients each year and they are followed-up to 1 year or until death. The annual volume of ERCP in The Prince of Wales Hospital is around 800 cases. Around 30 patients receive ERCP + CSEMS each year for malignant distal CBD obstruction. Thus, the recruitment schedule is highly feasible. Future study The findings of this could further establish the role of ECDS in management of malignant distal CBD stricture. Long-term patency data of ECDS versus ERCP with CSEMS could be obtained. In addition, the findings of this study could help form the basis for future comparisons of the procedure to surgical biliary bypass.

14136816.label: Realisation of objectives
14136816.value: Malignant biliary obstruction is a common sequel of pancreatic cancers or distal bile duct cancers, and its development can hinder the use of chemotherapy, decrease patient quality of life and decrease survival. Malignant biliary obstruction is traditionally palliated with ERCP and metallic stent insertion. However, these stents are prone to obstruction due to tumor ingrowth. In addition, ERCP may not always be possible due to tumor obstruction and percutaneous biliary drainage may be required. Recently, ECDS has been described as an alternative to percutaneous biliary drainage in patients with failed ERCP. The procedure is also associated with several potential advantages as compared to conventional ERCP. In particular, the risk of tumor ingrowth into the stent placed after ECDS is low and stent patency rates may be better than ERCP. Thus, the aim of the current study is to compare primary ECDS versus ERCP with CSEMS in unresectable malignant distal CBD strictures. We hypothesize that ECDS is associated with a higher 1-year stent patency rate. The secondary outcomes include technical success, clinical success, adverse events, time to stent dysfunction, re-intervention rates and mortality. The planned sample size was 164 patients by assuming a 20% difference in 1-year stent patency between ECDS and ERCP with CSEMS (87% vs 67%), at a 5% significance level and with a power of 80% and taking into account a 10% dropout rate. The study began in January 2017, there were some initial delays in patient recruitment as IRB approval was only available in 2 institutions by January 2018 (Prince of Wales Hospital and Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark) and 21 patients were recruited at that time. IRB approval was eventually obtained from all hospitals between 2018 to 2019 and all centers began patient recruitment. However, by March 2019, the COVID-19 pandemic began and all the international centers that joined this study were severe affected. As a result, patient recruitment was once again slowed down. By January 2020, 104 patients were recruited in the study (37 in Prince of Wales Hospital, 12 in Aarhus University Hospital, 4 in Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, 6 in Chulalongkorn University, 9 in The University of Leuven in Belgium, 22 in Hospital Jean Mermoz in France, 6 in Limoge University Hospital, 8 in Rajavithi Hospital in Thailand) and a request for a 6-month extension of the study was granted. Initially, we were expecting to be able to finish recruitment by July 2020, however due to COVID-19, many international centres had stopped recruitment completely including our hospital at some point. Although, we continued to urge our partners to continue with recruitment, conduction of this study was less of a priority than battling COVID-19 in many countries. Nevertheless, we were still able to recruit some patients during the pandemic. By July 2020, we have included 145 patients and another request for a 6 month extension was granted. Finally, recruitment was completed by January 2021 amidst all the difficulties during the pandemic. Regarding realisation of the objectives, all 4 objectives were completed. For the 1st objective, we were not able to show that ECDS was associated with a higher stent patency rate. The 1-year stent patency rate of both arms were 91.1%. There are several potential reasons for this. Firstly, some of the patients have not completed the 1 year follow-up, hence the final patency rate of the ERCP arm may be lower than our current number. Furthermore, on examining the causes of stent dysfunction in both arms, 6 patients in the ERCP group had tumour ingrowth as compared to 2 patients in the ECDS group, whilst in the ECDS, other causes of stent dysfunction were present including stent migration, food impaction and impingement of the stent. Resulting in a similar the final stent patency rates. Regarding the secondary outcomes, the ECDS group had better technical success rates (94.9% vs 78.5%, P = 0.004) and shorter procedural time [15.57 (15.91) vs 28.67 (18.89) minutes, P < 0.001] whilst no difference in other parameters were observed. The reason for better technical success rates were because technical failures in the ERCP group resulted from either failed cannulations or duodenal obstructions preventing successful ERCP. With a better technical success and shorter procedural time, it may also signify that ECDS is an easier procedure in these types of patients. Finally, with the above findings, we concluded that ECDS is associated with some advantages over ERCP in drainage of unresecetable malignant distal CBD obstruction. The procedure should be considered an option as the primary drainage procedure for these patients. On whether the procedure can be compared to surgical bypass will require more studies to establish.

14136816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14136816.value: Between January 2017 to January 2021, 166 patients were recruited in to the study (83 ECDS and 83 ERCP). There were no differences in background demographics. The majority of patients suffered from unresectable locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcninoma. ECDS was associated with significantly higher technical success (94.9% vs 78.5%, P = 0.004) whilst clinical success as per intention to treat were similar. The mean (S.D.) procedural time was also significantly faster in the ECDS arm [15.57 (15.91) vs 28.67 (18.89) minutes, P < 0.001]. Whilst no difference in hospital stay (6 IQR (2-10) vs 4.5 (IQR 1 – 10) days, P = 0.272), 30-day adverse events rates (19.2% vs 17.6%, P = 0.812), 30-day mortality rates (5.1% vs 6.5%, P = 0.744) and 1-year stent dysfunction rates (8.9% vs 8.9%, P = 1) were observed. However, since the last patient was recruited in January 2021, hence not all patients have completed 1 year follow-up. In patients that suffered from stent dysfunction, the cause was tumour ingrowth in 6 patients in the ERCP group whilst only 2 patients had tumour ingrowth in the ECDS arm. Conclusion ECDS is associated with some advantages over ERCP in drainage of unresecetable malignant distal CBD obstruction. The procedure should be considered an option as the primary drainage procedure for these patients. The abstract of the project was presented as an oral plenary abstract in the 2021 Digestive Disease Week in May. The full paper is currently being prepared for submission.

14136816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14136816.value: ECDS has been shown by multiple meta-analysis to be more advantageous then percutaneous drainage. The current study addressed how the procedure compared with ERCP and demonstrated that ECDS was associated with some advantages over ERCP when offered to patients with malignant distal biliary obstruction. To further assess whether ECDS is more advantageous to ERCP, we can perform a cost effective analysis using the current data to compare the 2 approaches. Furthermore, in patients with hilar obstruction, a similar randomised study comparing ERCP with EUS-guided hepatico-gastrostomy can be performed to assess if the EUS approach is associated with benefits on the 1-year stent potency rate, technical success, clinical success, adverse events, re-intervention rates and mortality.

The aim of the current study is to compare primary ECDS versus ERCP in patients suffering from unresectable malignant distal CBD strictures. 14138016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14138016.value: 鼻咽癌（Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, NPC）是一種惡性的上皮惡性腫瘤，其在香港和中國南部的發病率較高，並與EB病毒（Epstein-Barrvirus, EBV）感染有關。我們研究組的前期研究工作顯示EB病毒編碼的由BART產生的微小RNA（miR-BARTs）在鼻咽癌中表達較高。我們研究發現EB病毒微小RNA通過調節LMP-1, LMP-2A和PUMA等基因在鼻咽癌細胞中的表達在調控凋亡和宿主免疫反應方面起到重要作用。我們近期嘗試用電腦模擬的方法預測miR-BARTs在細胞中的靶標，並在一個重要的DNA雙鏈斷裂修復基因ATM的3’UTR發現多個miR-BART結合位點。在鼻咽癌臨床樣本中ATM的mRNA和蛋白表達均降低。初步結果顯示至少3個EB病毒編碼微小RNA（BART5-5p, BART9-3p 和 BART14-3p）參與了鼻咽癌中ATM的表達抑制。實驗表明他們可以個別地或聯合地調控ATM表達。過表達這3個微小RNA能夠在EB病毒陰性細胞NP69和HeLa中抑制由γ輻射誘導的ATM活性。報導顯示缺失ATM的細胞不能夠修復PARP抑製劑誘導的DNA雙鏈斷裂因而對PARP抑製劑較敏感。相反地，正常細胞能夠有效地修復這些DNA雙鏈斷裂從而保持基因穩定性。這種ATM缺失的鼻咽癌細胞與正常鼻咽上皮細胞在DNA修復能力上的差異為開發治療鼻咽癌的有效藥物提供了新的途徑。我們因此提出以下假設：EB病毒通過miR-BARTs抑制ATM介導的DNA損傷修復。這種DNA損傷修復的缺失不僅參與了鼻咽癌的發生髮展，也使得PARP抑製劑成為癌症治療的可行手段。本研究旨在闡明BART5-5p, BART9-3p及 BART14-3p與ATM的相互作用，通過體內體外實驗研究鼻咽癌miR-BARTs在ATM介導的DNA損傷修復中的作用。我們的最終目標是為PARP抑製劑與放化療結合在鼻咽癌中的臨床應用提供更多理論基礎。所得出的結果不僅能夠增強對EB病毒在鼻咽癌發展中作用的理解，而且為開發對抗鼻咽癌的新的治療手段做出重大貢獻。

14138016.label: Realisation of objectives
14138016.value: In Objective 1: We first used small RNA-sequencing to re-analyze the miRNA expression pattern in six well-known EBV-positive NPC samples, including 5 patient-derived xenografts and a EBV-positive NPC cell line (C666-1). In the experiment, we obtained 25-40% of the EBV-encoded miRNAs (miR-BARTs) from the total miRNAs in each sample and confirmed that the miR-BARTs expression patterns were vastly similar across the sample. By using the public available miRNA target prediction programs, miRnada and RNAhybrid, the putative miRNA binding sites of miR-BART5-5p, BART7-3p, BART9-3p and BART14-3p on the ATM 3’-UTR were suggested. The high expression levels of these miR-BARTs in NPCs were corroborated by RT-qPCR in primary NPC samples (16 NP and 45 NPC cases). On the other hand, downregulation of ATM in EBV-positive NPC cell line, xenografts and primary samples were validated by western blot and immunohistochemical (IHC) staining (35 NP and 46 NPC cases). The expression level of the ATM transcript in clinical NPC tumors (n = 45) were determined as compared to the non-cancerous NP tissues (n = 16) by RT-qPCR. The direct interaction of miR-BARTs with ATM-3’UTR was validated by performing a series of luciferase reporter assays with co-transfection of different combinations of miR-BART mimics and reporter plasmids in 293FT cells. The luciferase activity of the reporter plasmids containing a predicted ATM-3’UTR recognition site was strongly repressed by individual miR-BART (p < 0.01 in all combinations). However, the inhibitory effect was eliminated if the complementarities of the seed region on the binding site were either mutated or deleted. The suppressive effect was also canceled if the corresponding miR-BART inhibitor was co-transfected simultaneously. To examine the regulatory effect of miR-BARTs on ATM, we introduced the C666-1-BART-Cluster 1, C666-1-BART-Cluster 2 expression vector or a mimic of individual miR-BART into two EBV- negative, ATM-expressing epithelial cells, NP69 and HeLa. The ATM expression level was analyzed by western blot analysis 24 hours after transfection. The results illustrated that the expression of either individual C666-1-BART-Cluster or miRNA mimic could repress endogenous ATM expression. The synergistic suppressive effects on ATM was also observed when the cells were simultaneously transfected with either both miR-BART expression vectors or the mimics of all four miR-BARTs. In the rescue experiments, the ATM expression was restored in BART-Cluster 1 and BART-Cluster 2 expressing NP69 and HeLa cells when the cells co-transfected with BART5-5p, BART7-3p, BART9-3p or BART14-3p inhibitors. Likewise, ATM was re-expressed in C666-1 by inhibiting endogenous BART7-3p, BART9-3p, and BART14-3p activity, individually or together. The reason for the inability of the BART5-5p inhibitor to restore ATM expression is not clear. We have previously demonstrated that endogenous BART5-5p can regulate the effect on PUMA in C666-1 cells. Besides, low expression of cellular miR-18a/b, which have significant seed homology with BART5-5p, and no sequence variation on the putative binding site were identified in the cells, indicating that the putative BART5-binding site on the ATM is probably available in the cells. However, the involvement of the cell-specific mechanisms to shield the BART5-5p recognition site on ATM cannot be ruled out. In Objective 2, we postulated that suppressing ATM expression with miR-BARTs may enhance the radio-sensitivity of NPC cells. To prove this hypothesis, we transfected the NP69 and HeLa cells with either ATM-specific siRNA or individual miR-BART mimic and subsequently exposed the cells to γ-irradiation (IR). The IR-induced ATM activity, as indicated by the phosphorylation of both ATM and its downstream targets (γ-H2AX and p-CHK2), was observed in the control transfected cells. However, the magnitude of the IR-induced ATM activity was dramatically reduced in the cells where ATM expression was suppressed by siRNA or miR-BARTs, individually or together. The post-IR recovery ability of the transfected cells was analyzed with the γ-H2AX nuclear foci formation and the comet assays. After exposure to 3 Gy of IR, the number of positive γ-H2AX nuclear foci in all miR-BART transfected cells was significantly reduced (p <0.01 in all cases), indicating that the recovery ability of the cells from the IR-induced DNA damage was impaired by the miR-BART activity. Similarly, the DNA repair capacity of the miR-BART transfected cells was also obviously repressed in the comet assay (p < 0.05). More importantly, the long-term clonogenic survival of the miR-BART transfected HeLa cells was significantly reduced after IR treatment. After exposure to 1 Gy of IR, approximately 50% of the untransfected cells were survived. In contrast, nearly 88% of the BART5-5p (p = 0.008), 80% of BART7-3p (p = 0.009), 75% of BART9-3p (p = 0.018) and 60% of BART14-3p (p = 0.048) transfected cells were killed. In Objective 3: It has previously been reported that ATM-null cells exhibit sensitivity to PARP inhibitor. Since ATM is downregulated in C666-1, we initially planned to use this cell line as an in vitro model to evaluate the efficacy of olaparib, an FDA approved PARP inhibitor, in NPC treatment. However, we revealed that C666-1 is highly resistant to IR treatment. In the experiment to expose the cells with 10 Gy of IR, only 25% of the cells were killed at 72 hours in CCK8 assay and more than 60% of the cells finally survived in the long-term clonogenic survival assay. Increasing the IR to 20 Gy did not further suppress the long-term survival of the cells. On the other hand, C666-1 is also insensitive to olaparib. We first confirmed the efficacy of olaparib in three control cell-lines, including A549 (IC50 = 13.4µM), HeLa (IC50 = 51.4µM) and SW620 (IC50 = 25.4µM). The SW620 cells do not have any homologous DNA Double-strand Break Repair (DSBR) defect and is expected to have poor response to olaparib. However, increasing the dose olaparib to 300µM could only kill less than 25% of the C666-1 cells in 3 days. We realized that the C666-1 cells have high expression of endogenous BRCA1, another key DSBR gene, which might minimize the olaparib effect. Nevertheless, the olaparib effect did not showed significantly difference in the C666-1 where BRCA1 expression was knocked down by specific siRNAs. We further examined the effect of olaparib on two newly established EBV-positive (NPC-43T and C17-C) and a EBV-negative NPC (NPC-53T) cell lines. Unfortunately, all of these 3 NPC cell lines are highly resistant to olaparib treatment, albeit the endogenous ATM expression level is weak in all the cells. Finally, we demonstrated that C666-1 cells are sensitive to cisplatin (IC50 = 16µM) and doxorubicin (IC50 = 1.25µM). Although ectopic ATM expression in C666-1 cells did not apparently suppress the killing effect of these two chemotherapeutic agents, manipulating the expression of endogenous BRCA1, the downstream target of ATM, can modulated the cell sensitivity to both cisplatin and doxorubicin. In the cells with cisplatin (16µM) treatment, the clonogenic survival rate of BRCA1-siRNA-treated cells (26.9%) was significantly lower than the control (67%) (p = 0.011). Similarly, in the doxorubicin (1.25µM) treatment, the long-term survival rate of BRCA1-siRNA-treated (32.1%) was lower than the control (46%) (p = 0.008). Conversely, overexpressing BRCA1 in C666-1 cells could protect the cells from the cisplatin and doxorubicin treatment. To compared with the control, the survival rate of BRCA1-expressing C666-1 cells could increase from 34% to 78% in cisplatin treatment (p = 0.012), and from 10% to 29.3% in doxorubicin treatment (p = 0.031).

14138016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14138016.value: In the study, we have established a comprehensive transcriptional profile of both cellular and viral miRNAs in five NPC patient-derived xenografts and an EBV-infected NPC cell line. We confirmed that miR-BARTs are abundantly expressed (about 25-40% of the total miRNAs) in NPCs and their expression pattern is vastly consistence. Remarkably, we uncovered the role of miR-BART5-5p, miR-BART7-3p, miR-BART9-3p and miR-BART14-3p in modulating the expression of ATM. These four miRNAs occupied about 11% of the total viral miRNAs in NPC and suppressed ATM expression by directly binding to multiple sites on its 3’-UTR. In addition, downregulation of ATM was observed in primary NPC tissues in both q RT-PCR and IHC staining. The strong inverse association between ATM mRNA and miR-BART5-5p, BART7-3p, BART9-3p and BART14-3p expression in primary NPC tissues was also demonstrated. Since all the previous reported cellular miRNAs which responsible for modulating ATM expression are rarely expressed in NPC, viral miRNA may be the key ATM negative regulator in this EBV-associated epithelial cancer. More importantly, we revealed that miR-BARTs can work co-operatively to retard the ionizing irradiation-induced ATM kinase activity and eventually promote cell death. This observation may partly explain the exceptionally high radio-sensitivity of NPC. Our laboratory previously reported that overexpression of EBV-immediate-early lytic protein, BZLF1, in C666-1 cells can elevate the ATM kinase activity and finally provoke the viral lytic cycle. In the present study, we further demonstrated that suppressing endogenous BART6-3p, BART9-3p or BART14-3p activity in the BZLF1-expressing C666-1 cells can activate the ATM activity and accompanied by increasing the expression of the BMRF1 protein, an early viral lytic gene. Therefore, miR-BARTs may have important role to maintain viral latency by suppressing ATM activity, which in turn inhibits BZLF1 activity during viral lytic reactivation. Intriguingly, other research team demonstrated that miRNAs in BART Cluster 1 region can also directly target BZLF1 expression. Thus, the activity of BZLF1 is tightly controlled by miR-BARTs via different mechanisms. We found that all NPC cell lines available in our laboratory are insensitive to olaparib. However, they are sensitive to cisplatin and doxorubicin. Interestingly, manipulating the endogenous BRCA1 expression in C666-1 cells can modulate the sensitivity of the cells to both cisplatin and doxorubicin.

14138016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14138016.value: Although ATM is consistently downregulated in all of our laboratory available EBV-positive NPC cells (C666-1, NPC-43T and C17-C), they are resistant to olaparib in the in vitro experiment. However, our fresh exome-sequencing data in primary NPCs revealed that patients with mutations in critical DNA damage response genes had significantly shorter survival than those with null mutation (KWL unpublished data). Thus, it is worth to continue study the interaction between the DSBR gene expression and the DNA damaging agents in NPC. We propose to evaluate the cytotoxicity of olaparib directly in the NPC patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) (xeno-666, xeno-1915, C15 and C17), in which both ATM and BRCA1 expressions are relatively low. Recently, we identified that BRCA1, the downstream target of ATM, is also downregulated in EBV-positive NPC samples, except C666-1. However, suppressing BRCA1 activity by siRNAs can reduce the long-term survival rate of cisplatin treated C666-1 cells (KFT, unpublished data). Hence, we will study the regulation of BRCA1 expression in EBV-positive NPC and further explore the roles of BRCA1, alone or together with ATM, in the response to ionizing radiation/DNA damaging agents.

14138016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14138016.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common EBV-associated cancer and is particular prevalent in southern China. In NPC, viral-encoded miRNAs, miR-BARTs are abundantly expressed and can function as the key negative regulators in augmenting NPC tumorigenesis. It had previously been reported that ATM, an essential molecule of DNA repair system, is consistently downregulated in EBV-positive primary NPC with unknown mechanism. With the RGC grant support, we have established a comprehensive profile of miR-BARTs in five well-known EBV-positive NPC patient-derived xenografts and one NPC cell line. We confirmed the high expression level of 22 miR-BARTs in these tissues. And their expression patterns were significantly similar in each of the tested sample. Among the abundantly expressed miR-BARTs, we revealed the novel suppressive effect of BART5-5p, BART7-3p, BART9-3p, and BART14-3p in modulating the ATM signaling pathway. Besides, we clearly demonstrated that the expression of these four miR-BARTs significantly enhance the ionizing radio-sensitivity of epithelial cells and contribute to the maintenance of viral latency in EBV positive NPC cell lines. The finding of the project may provide important information for the development of effective therapies in NPC patients.

14138416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14138416.value: 研究背景：顱內動脈粥樣硬化性病變（ICAD）是導致缺血性中風的一個重要病因；相關患者有很高的中風復發風險。理解嚴重狹窄且不穩定的ICAD斑塊在藥物治療下如何進展或演變為穩定狀態可以為這類患者的中風二級預防提供相關信息與證據。 研究目的：使用三維旋轉血管造影（3DRA）的方法明確不穩定的ICAD斑塊的形態學特征，并揭示ICAD斑塊的進展和重構過程。 研究對象和程序：我們計劃入選70名由重度(≥60%)顱內動脈粥樣硬化性狹窄導致急性缺血性中風的患者。符合條件的患者會在中風發病后4周內納入研究。經磁力共振血管成像檢查提示頸內動脈顱內段或大腦中動脈存在局部血管信號缺失的患者會在基線時接受3DRA檢查，並在1年后再次進行3DRA檢查。所有納入的患者均接受短期（4周）阿司匹林（每天80mg）與氯吡格雷（每天75mg）聯合抗血小板治療，之後長期接受阿司匹林抗血小板治療。在1年的隨訪期間，所有患者血管危險因素的控制需要達到以下標準：1)低密度脂蛋白(LDL)≤70 mg/dL；2)糖化血紅蛋白(HbA1c) ≤6.5%；3)收縮壓≤140mmHg；4)戒煙。在基線以及1、3、6、12個月時，我們會對患者進行臨床評估（美國國立衛生院中風評分及改良的Rankin評分），并記錄患者的心血管危險因素指標， 包括HbA1c、空腹血糖、LDL、高密度脂蛋白和甘油三酯等。我們會分析患者ICAD斑塊從基線到1年的進展情況，包括血管管腔的狹窄程度以及其他的幾何學特征（表面形態、斑塊近端與血管壁的夾角、斑塊體積和分佈等）。另外，我們會分析上述形態學特征的變化與血管危險因素控制情況之間的關係。 主要的納入和排除標準：患者的磁力共振彌散灌注成像上必須存在動脈到動脈血栓栓塞相關的急性梗死病灶，並且存在相關的ICAD病變（狹窄程度≥60%）。若患者同時存在>50%的同側近端大動脈狹窄，或者此次中風的病因與ICAD無關，則不納入本研究。 研究時間：若每月納入5例患者，則患者入組會在14個月內完成。考慮到12個月的隨訪期和其他因素，本研究共需32個月完成。 關鍵詞：缺血性中風、顱內動脈粥樣硬化、血管重構

14139116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14139116.value: Stroke and coronary heart disease (CHD) are increasingly important public health care issues, with many risk equations having been developed in recent years to both evaluate and predict the risk of cardiovascular diseases especially stroke. These current risk methodologies are not specific enough on their own and therefore require extensive additional clinical and laboratory information which is inconvenient and expensive. Since the vessels (retinal) at the back of the eye are the only directly visible vessels in the whole body that share similar histological structure and pathological patterns with cerebral vessels, they can potentially provide an estimate of the risk of stroke and CHD. Most of the studies to date used only a limited number of vascular features such as narrowing of the small arteries, widening of the veins and/or the arteriole/venular ratio in an attempt to show the association with stroke. They are not fully automatic and technically difficult to apply in practice. In this proposed study, we will firstly investigate potential retinal vascular risk factors for CHD, and develop an automatic retinal image risk analysis method for CHD. A separate testing data set including both Hong Kong data and Wales UK data will be used to validate the model. The study team has already completed a number of methodological developments to identify important retinal characteristics associated with stroke risk in both general population and persons with type 2 diabetes. It is also important to realize that the stroke risk and CHD risk for type 2 diabetes patients may change in relation to the progression of the disease, especially for those who have already had a stroke and recovered. With the development of stroke risk and CHD risk assessment tools, we would therefore be able to evaluate the risk profiles of diabetes vascular complications and progression especially on stroke recurrence and CHD events.

14139116.label: Realisation of objectives
14139116.value: In this study, we have achieved all three objectives and have trained a PhD student. Our results show that retinal risk factors for stroke and coronary heart disease in patients with type 2 diabetes are primarily different but with minor overlap. We have evidence that this phenomenon is not only real in diabetes patients but also for other non-diabetic individuals. During the study, we have determined the risk factors specifically relevant to coronary heart disease (CHD) and separately for stroke. Still, we further discovered that the risk factors for ischemic stroke are different from that of hemorrhagic stroke. Unfortunately, all our hemorrhagic stroke cases were intracranial haemorrhage (ICH), and none of them was subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH). Otherwise, we would have been able to carry out the classification of hemorrhagic stroke subtype based on the retinal image. We have determined the retinal vascular risk factors that are significantly associated with CHD. Secondly, we have clarified that the retinal risk factors for stroke and the retinal risk factors for CHD have a small amount of overlap. However, there is a significant difference in risk factors among CHD and stroke subtypes. We have developed risk models that incorporate these characteristics to increase the sensitivity and specificity for CHD risk assessment using a similar methodology we developed for stroke risk assessment. The study on stroke subtypes and CHD risk profiles provide valuable information for us to understand the change of risk profiles of diabetic complications. For the whole study, a total of 2280 patients' data were obtained. Among them, 279 have coronary heart disease, and 311 have a stroke. To avoid bias due to the enormous imbalance effect on the determination of clinical and retinal risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD), we selected 197 CHD patients. We compared them with 128 controls for the development of the model. Among the 197 CHD patients, 167 (85%) of them have their retinal images done within 6 months of admission to the hospital. The patient characteristics significantly related to CHD include age, HbA1c, hypertension, and urea. We have selected 244 stroke patients, among them 154 (63%) have an ischemic stroke and 90 (37%) have a hemorrhagic stroke. The same 128 controls were used to develop the stroke risk models. For retinal characteristics significantly related to CHD, they include CRVE left and CRAE right, bifurcation coefficient for venule, asymmetry for both arterial and venule on the left eye, arterial occlusion, exudates, tortuosity. Significant clinical factors from the logistic model for coronary heart disease risk estimation with both clinical and retinal characteristics include hypertension, gender, age, diabetes, systolic blood pressure (SBP). Significant retinal characteristics include rNipping, rExudates, lAVR, colour component and structural component. The performance of the CHD models using both clinical and retinal variables have a sensitivity of 90.7%, and the specificity is 76.5%. The area under the ROC curve is 0.93, with a 95% CI of (0.90, 0.96). The testing data analysis also shows similar results with sensitivity and specificity of 88.2% and 75% respectively, for the clinical plus retinal characteristics. The 95% CI for the AUC for the model using clinical and retinal features is significantly better than the other two models. The ROC curves for CHD using logistics models on clinical characteristics alone, retinal characteristics alone, and both clinical characteristics and retinal characteristics have been determined. The results using clinical characteristics alone are significantly less effective than using retinal characteristics alone or both clinical and retinal characteristics.

14139116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14139116.value: For ischemic stroke risk estimation, the logistic regression model constructed using clinical characteristics alone had a sensitivity of 77.95%, a specificity of 76.16%, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.88. The model constructed using retinal characteristics alone had a sensitivity of 90.63%, a specificity of 91.56%, and an AUC of 0.98. The model that was constructed using both clinical and retinal characteristics had a sensitivity of 90.56%, a specificity of 92.21%, and an AUC of 0.99. For hemorrhagic stroke risk estimation, the logistic regression model constructed using clinical characteristics alone had a sensitivity of 76.85%, a specificity of 80.68%, and an AUC of 0.91. The model built using retinal characteristics alone had a sensitivity of 92.97%, a specificity of 85.56%, and an AUC of 0.98. The model constructed using both clinical and retinal characteristics had a sensitivity of 95.37%, a specificity of 89.77%, and an AUC of 1.00. We further investigated if we can separate hemorrhagic stroke patients from ischemic stroke patients, the logistic regression model using clinical characteristics alone had a sensitivity of 58.67%, a specificity of 71.05%, and an AUC of 0.71. The classification model constructed using retinal characteristics alone had a sensitivity of 89.47%, a specificity of 88.16%, and an AUC of 0.97. The classification model built using both clinical and retinal characteristics had a sensitivity of 88.16%, a specificity of 90.79%, and an AUC of 0.98. It is apparent that retinal characteristics are essential to provide the discriminatory power for the classification of the stroke subtypes. For CHD risk estimation, the logistic regression model constructed using clinical characteristics alone had a sensitivity of 67.18%, a specificity of 83.07%, and an AUC of 0.84. The logistic regression model constructed using only retinal characteristics had a sensitivity of 70.31%, a specificity of 86.80%, and an AUC of 0.90. Finally, the model built using both clinical and retinal characteristics had a sensitivity of 75.00%, a specificity of 88.21%, and an AUC of 0.93. Our results suggest that retinal vascular features afforded better risk estimates for CHD and stroke than traditional clinical characteristics; they can also help with stroke subtype classification. We further investigated the changes in both stroke risk and CHD risk. Observations have been summarized, and new hypotheses have been developed to study the development of various complications.

14139116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14139116.value: There are several potential research topics that were generated from this work. First, we have developed the tool to estimate the risk of stroke and CHD. Their changes during the cause of the disease can now be tracked. However, the complexity of various subgroups of patients by age, gender, occupation, smoking status, and other co-morbidities creates a lot of challenges to the analysis. We are working on a new study design to address this issue. Second, the risk profiles for patients before having an ischemic stroke, after diagnosis of ischemic stroke and their long-term follow-up for the development of CHD or hemorrhagic stroke is an entirely new area of study, and require a relatively large cohort of patients with retinal images. Third, we have determined that ischemic stroke and hemorrhagic stroke can be distinguished using the retinal image alone. However, all the hemorrhagic stroke cases are intracranial haemorrhage (ICH). We believe that we would be able to detect aneurysm from retinal images before the occurrence of subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) for the other types of hemorrhagic stroke cases. The future technological development for detection of the risk of haemorrhagic stroke subtypes would be a life-saving technology.

14139116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14139116.value: Our study is based on a novel technology, with patents already obtained by the Chinese University of Hong Kong, to monitor retinal vasculature and other characteristics to identify potential cardiovascular complication. The results of this study are especially relevant to patients with type 2 diabetes as stroke and CHD are common diabetic complications. We have successfully shown that retinal image analysis can detect coronary heart disease (CHD), and also stroke subtypes, including ischemic stroke and hemorrhagic stroke with high accuracy. Since all diabetic patients are recommended to have retinal images taken every year for diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening, these retinal images that contain plenty of information on the blood vessels will allow the additional assessment of other vascular-related complications such as stroke and coronary heart disease (CHD). Therefore, an automatic computer program that utilizes retinal images for cardiovascular risk assessment is highly efficient that incur a relatively small additional cost, but with a huge gain in terms of patient convenience and clinical management. Further research on hemorrhagic stroke subtypes may provide even more accurate risk assessment of unruptured intracranial aneurysms and subarachnoid haemorrhages for stroke prevention in practice.

14140816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14140816.value: 骨缺損常由日增的交通意外或地震等自然災害（中國地區高發）所致，是導致骨折延遲愈合或不愈合的常見骨科疾患。盡管聯合了先進的手術技術和各種固定器材，骨缺損仍是棘手而厄待解決的問題。基於道路安全的考慮，聯合國重新定義2011-2020年為下一個“骨關節十年”，也反映了這一問題的重要性。尋求高性價比的骨缺損治療策略是“骨關節十年”的首要任務。因此，研發可同時促進骨缺損的生物學愈合和功能性修復的新型治療手段是極具意義的。 近年來，由於具有可降解性、良好的生物相容性及接近皮質的骨力學性能，鎂及其合金吸引了廣大的關註。另外，體內60%的鎂儲存於骨組織內，是主要的礦物元素。本課題組和其他課題組已發現補充鎂離子可以促進幹細胞和內皮細胞的增殖，最終分別引起骨組織和血管增生，這兩方面對骨修復尤為重要。 我們的預實驗結果提示高純度鎂金屬制備而成的髓內釘植入到大鼠股骨髓腔之後可以明顯促進新骨形成。在該模型中，鎂促進了骨膜內的感覺神經末梢釋放降鈣素基因相關肽（一種已知的對成骨分化起重要作用的神經肽）。然而，由於降解過快，純鎂並不能保證在骨痂完成塑形之前的穩定骨折固定。因此，我們“揚長避短”地設計了一套載鎂髓內釘系統（把純鎂棒套到中空的不銹鋼髓內釘）。預實驗結果也提示了鎂離子可以顯著地促進骨髓間充質幹細胞的遷移。這一發現為載鎂髓內釘用於修復骨缺損提供了堅實的理論基礎。在此，我們可以大膽地假設載鎂髓內釘可通過以下三個方面發揮促進長骨骨缺損的修復：1）促進幹細胞募集和它們的成骨分化；2）促進血管形成；3）影響新生骨塑形過程中晶體礦化的程度。 在本項目中，我們將會測試這一新型載鎂髓內釘在大鼠股骨節段性骨缺損中的固定效果及其促進修復的療效。通過小動物計算機斷層掃描、生物力學測試、組織學和骨組織形態學分析，我們將既可以首次全面地評估載鎂髓內釘的療效，也可以闡明參與其中的分子機制。 總而言之，本項目以研發可有效促進骨缺損修復的新型載鎂髓內釘為目標。另外，我們也將尋求有力證據，以論證其“三效性”。本項目把載鎂髓內釘的作用充分利用起來，以解決骨缺損這一棘手的臨床問題為目標，是典型的“從實驗室到臨床”的研究。因此，從長遠看來，本項目將顯著地減輕社會和患者的經濟負擔。

14140816.label: Realisation of objectives
14140816.value: As described in 5.1. we have the following two main study objectives as stated in the original proposal that have been fully (100%) realized for our final report. To achieve the first objective (To establish an in vivo experimental model for investigating the efficiency of the released Mg ions from our innovative Mg-IM nail on bone defect healing in an established femoral segmental defect model in adult male rats and elucidating the role of Mg in bone defect repair ), we have established a 5-mm segmental bone defect model in rats. Mg-IM implantation increased almost 4 folds of new bone formation in the 5-mm rat femoral segmental defects at 12 weeks after surgery as indicated by the X-ray results (Figure 1). In line with the X-ray results, Micro-CT results showed that Mg-IM nail implantation augmented almost 4 folds of new bone formation and over 3 folds of new vessel formation in the 5-mm rat femoral segmental defects at 12 weeks surgery (Figure 2). In addition, Mg-IM nail accelerated bone formation and remodeling within the defect gap as revealed by the histology results (Figure 3). Meanwhile, immunohistochemistry showed higher expression of CD31, RUNX2, and osterix in bone defect region in Mg-IMN group than IMN group, indicating Mg-IM nail enhanced bone defect repair via the enhancement of angiogenesis and osteogenesis (Figure 4 A&B). Micro-CT based angiography showed Mg-IM nail implantation increased almost 3 folds of vessel volume formation compared IMN group. These results confirmed the efficiency of our innovative Mg-IM nail on bone defect healing. We also demonstrated that the beneficial effect of Mg-IM nail in bone defect healing was via enhancement of angiogenesis, osteogenesis, and bone remodeling. To achieve the second objective (To investigate mechanisms of the released Mg ion on tube formation of endothelial cells, the migration and osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs, and the mineral ratio of extracellular matrix), a series of experiments were performed. The results of Alizarin red staining (ARS) and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) staining showed Mg ions enhanced the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs (Figure 5 A&B). In vitro cell migration assay showed that Mg ions stimulate the migration of BMSCs (Figure 5 C). The western blotting assay showed that the Mg ions-enhanced osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs might though integrin β1-FAK signaling (Figure 5 D-G). Mg ions enhanced the migration of human endothelial cells as indicated by the in vitro scratch test results (Figure 6 A&B). In addition, Mg ions promoted the tube formation of endothelial cells as shown in the tube formation assay (Figure 6 C&D). We also found that Mg increased the mineral ratio of extracellular matrix (Figure 6 E). To extent the project objectives, we have also made breakthrough in the translational application of Mg-IM nail in accelerating distraction osteogenesis for critical size bone defect repair. We found that Mg-IM nail combined with distraction induced bone regeneration within 5-mm rat femoral segmental defects as demonstrated by the X-ray and the Micro-CT results (Figure 7). Mg nail accelerated bone formation and remodeling within the defect gap during distraction osteogenesis as demonstrated by the histology results (Figure 8). Mg-IM nail increased the Ca/P ratio and mechanical properties of the regenerate during distraction osteogenesis as indicated by the SEM/EDS and four-point bending test results (Figure 9). Moreover, we found out that the CGRP-FAK-VEGF signaling axis was responsible for Mg-enhanced critical size bone defect repair during distraction osteogenesis (Figure 10). Overall, as we stated above we have fully addressed the objectives.

14140816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14140816.value: In our study, we have proved the beneficial effect of Mg-IM nail for critical size bone defect repair in the 5-mm rat femoral segmental defects model. Moreover, we investigated the mechanism of Mg in enhancing angiogenesis, osteogenesis, and promoting bone remodeling. We further applied Mg-IM nail in accelerating distraction osteogenesis for critical size bone defect repair. Besides, we revealed, for the first time, the signaling pathway linking sensory nerves and endothelial cells. The major funding has been composed as a manuscript and will be submitted to the journal Science translational medicine. The Figures mentioned in 5.3 and the detailed information of the generated manuscript was submitted in Part C. In the project, we have established collaborations with other universities and/or professors in this field, such as Professor Jian LU from Material Engineering in the City University of Hong Kong and Professor Kathy LUI from Department of chemical pathology, Chinese University of Hong Kong, Professor Gang LI from Department of Orthopaedics and Trauma, Chinese University of Hong Kong, etc. Also, there are several publications raised directly from this funding. One of them has already been accepted by the Journal of Orthopaedic Translation. Two manuscripts are under preparation (One targeted to Science translational medicine, the other targeted to Biomaterials). For detailed information on the publications, please refer to Part C. Finally, two students (TAM, Siu Lai, MSc; Dr. LI, Ye, Ph.D.) have been trained under the support of this funding. For the details of the thesis, with the thesis under please refer to Part C.

14140816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14140816.value: Bone defect frequently occurs in trauma-induced fractures that require surgical reconstruction. There are around 4 million surgeries for treating bone defects annually in the USA, which are great burdens to the patients, their families, society, and health-care systems. With biomechanical strength close to cortical bone and degradable capacity, Mg and its alloys are currently recognized as a revolutionary bioactive metal with potential to develop to orthopaedic implants. Our current study provides solid evidence that the proposed innovative Mg-based nail for effective treatment of critical size bone defect, a foundation for further clinical applications.
