14143916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14143916.value: Soybean seeds are rich in secondary metabolites, particularly isoflavonoids such as genistein that can be manufactured into important nutraceuticals and pharmaceuticals. It is not clear how isoflavonoids accumulate at high levels in soybean seeds. One possible explanation is the presence of transporters that can translocate isoflavonoids or their precursors from pods to seeds. Wild soybeans generally contain higher levels of isoflavonoids in their seeds than their cultivated counterparts. Using a recombinant inbred population resulting from a cross between a wild and a cultivated soybean parent, we are able to identify quantitative trait loci (QTLs) that are associated with regulating the accumulation of anti-oxidants and phenolics, and flavonoids in particular, in soybean seeds. These QTLs overlap in the same genomic region which contains four putative multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporter genes. Phylogenetic analyses indicate that all four targeted MATE transporters are clustered with other plant MATE transporters that use flavonoids as their substrates and at least three out of the four MATE transporter genes are expressed in pods. We therefore hypothesize that these MATE transporter genes in the QTL regulating the accumulation of flavonoids (probably isoflavonoids) in soybean seeds are responsible for transporting these secondary metabolites or their precursors from pods to seeds. To test this hypothesis, several lines of experiments will be conducted to examine the possible roles of these MATE genes and their protein products, by way of gene expression patterns and subcellular localization. The transport functions of these MATE transporters will be tested in yeast cells, membrane vesicles, and in planta. Through these research activities, we will provide a better understanding of flavonoid transport from pods to seeds in soybean. This project is also a pioneer study on MATE transporters that may use isoflavonoids as their substrates. If any of the targeted MATE transporters are bona fide isoflavonoid transporters, they will provide a unique strategy for genetically engineering non-legumes to produce isoflavonoids by manipulating the sink-source relationship. 大豆種子富含次生代謝產物，特別是異黃酮。其中金雀異黃酮可以加工成重要的藥物和營養品。目前尚不清楚異黃酮如何在大豆種子中積累，一種可能的解釋是由於大豆中存在可以從豆莢運輸異黃酮或他們的前體到種子的轉運蛋白。野生大豆種子通常比栽培大豆含有更高水平的異黃酮。利用以野生大豆和栽培大豆為親本的重組自交系群體，我們找到了在種子中調節抗氧化活性，酚類和黃酮類積累的數量性狀基因位點（QTLs）。這些數量性狀基因位點部分重疊在基因組的一個相同區域，該區域含有四個擬定的大豆多藥及毒素排出轉運蛋白（MATE）基因。系統進化樹分析表明該四個大豆MATE轉運蛋白都與其他植物內以黃酮類為底物的MATE轉運蛋白聚類在一起，其中最少有三個基因能在豆莢中表達。因此我們推測該QTL中的MATE轉運蛋白基因是通過從豆莢中運輸次級代謝產物或其前體到種子的作用，參與調控種子中黃酮類（很可能是異黃酮）的積累。 我們將採用多種實驗證明這一推測，通過基因表達模式分析和亞細胞定位檢驗這些MATE基因及其蛋白可能參與的功能，並在酵母細胞，膜囊泡和植物體內鑒定這些MATE轉運蛋白的轉運能力。通過這些研究，我們將加深對大豆中黃酮類從豆莢到種子轉運過程的理解。這個項目同時也是MATE轉運蛋白以異黃酮為底物的先遣研究，如證實其中目的MATE轉運蛋白真是異黃酮轉運蛋白，這將會提供一個通過基因工程改造非豆類植物的源庫關係，從而生產異黃酮的全新的策略。

14143916.label: Realisation of objectives
14143916.value: Objective 1: To study the gene expression patterns of targeted MATE transporters during pod and seed development We made use of a recombinant inbred (RI) population derived from a high-content parent (W05) and a low-content parent (C08). We selected RI lines containing different alleles of the targeted MATE transporter genes and determined their phenolic compounds (TPCs) and total flavonoid contents TFCs. We collected different tissues for gene expression studies, including leaf, root, developing pods, and developing seeds (7, 14, 21, 28, 40, and 60 days after flowering). RI lines containing W05 or C08 allele of the targeted MATE transporter genes did not exhibit a clearly distinguishable expression pattern. We further demonstrated that the correlation between the total content of seed phenolic compounds and the expression of MATE genes in the seed pod, hulled seed, and seed coat, respectively, was not strong. We, therefore, followed up with the examination of the tissue-specific expression pattern of MATE genes. Using transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana as the model, we showed that the native promoter of W05 MATE1 (ProW05-MATE1) drives the expression of β-Glucuronidase in the funicle of the transgenic plants. A similar expression pattern was observed when A. thaliana was transformed to express β-Glucuronidase driven by the native promoter of C08 MATE1 (ProC08-MATE1). We extended the investigation of tissue-specific expression patterns using transgenic soybean plants. While seeds are considered as the sink for nutrients during senescence, the pod has been considered as the sink throughout plant development by pulling resources from surrounding tissues. Being able to produce seed assimilates, the pod is also able to transport nutrients into seeds. GUS stain results show that ProC08-MATE1 drives the expression of β-Glucuronidase preferentially in tissues near the sutures of pods. It is possible that tissues surrounding the phloem store and unload isoflavones to the phloem for transport to developing seeds. To further understand the regulation of the expression of MATE genes, we did a genome-wide survey of MATE antisense transcripts, which have been suggested to be the regulators of the sense transcripts. Using strand-specific RNA-seq data from public datasets, from various soybean tissues including developing pods, developing seeds, embryos, cotyledons and hypocotyls, roots, apical buds, stems, and flowers, we identified 35 antisense transcripts of MATEs from 28 gene loci with reference to a high-quality reference genome. The antisense transcripts showing differential expression patterns between developing seed and pod were selected for experimental validation. Several antisense transcripts were predicted to have a positive expression correlation with the respective sense transcripts. Using RT-qPCR, we were able to detect and validate the expression of the antisense transcripts and their corresponding sense transcripts. These antisense transcripts showed a positive expression correlation with the corresponding sense transcripts in developing seed and pod. From these results, we were able to identify and validate the antisense transcript of GmMATE4 and demonstrated its positive expression correlation with the sense transcript. Objective 2: To study the subcellular localization of targeted MATE transporters MATE1, MATE2 or MATE4 was fused with the cDNA of the yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) and expressed in Nicotiana tabacum bright yellow-2 (BY-2) cells to produce fusion proteins MATE1-YFP, MATE2-YFP or MATE4-YFP. BY-2 cells were stained with FMTM 4-64 to visualize membranes or ER-tracker to visualize endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The fluorescent signal (Ex:488nm; Em:509nm) from the fusion protein MATE1-YFP, MATE2-YFP or MATE4-YFP was overlaid with the signal from FM 4-64 or ER-Tracker. It was found that MATE1, MATE2 and MATE4 were localized on the vacuole membrane and ER. Objective 3: To perform functional analyses of targeted MATE transporters To perform a rapid functional assay of the targeted MATE transporters, we generated cMyc-fusion proteins. The recombinant constructs cMyc-MATE1, cMyc-MATE2, or cMyc-MATE4 driven by Alcohol dehydrogenase 1 (ADH1) promoter were ectopically expressed in yeast. The yeast culture was treated with isoflavone daidzein, daidzin, genistein, or genistin. Daidzein and genistein are major isoflavones in soybean seeds while daidzin and genistin are their respective glycoside forms. Since daidzein, daidzin, genistein, and genistin are antioxidants, the cellular ROS levels of the yeast cells were used to reflect the uptake of these compounds into the cells. After the treatment with the isoflavones, the yeast cells were stained with H2DCFDA to monitor the change in ROS levels. A decreased fluorescent signal at 520nm reflects the decreased cellular ROS levels and implies the uptake of the isoflavone. It was found that the expression of MATE transporters from W05 and C08 could facilitate the uptake of daidzein, daidzin, genistein, and genistin into yeast cells, however, with different efficiencies. We further investigated the isoflavone transport function of GmMATE1 (C08), GmMATE1 (W05), GmMATE2 (C08), and GmMATE2 (W05) and found that these MATE proteins mediate the uptake of aglycones, including genistein, daidzein, and glycitein into the yeast cells. We also investigated the isoflavone glycoside transport functions of these MATE transporters and found that these MATE transporters also mediate the uptake of isoflavone glycosides, including genistin, daidzin, and glycitin, into the yeast cells. For in planta experiments, we first attempted to use transgenic A. thaliana as a model to study the functions of the targeted MATE transporters in planta. However, we could not generate transgenic A. thaliana plants that produce isoflavones to a consistently measurable level. We then turned to construct soybean knock-out mutants. CRISPR/Cas9 system was employed to knock out GmMATE1 in cultivated soybean W82. The isoflavone contents in hulled developing seeds in the mutant mate1 and wild type were measured by UPLC. Results show that the genistin level is lower in mate1 compared to wild type. This result suggests the role of GmMATE1 in genistin accumulation in developing seeds. Further, using mature soybean seeds, we found that the mutation of GmMATE1 (C08) led to the reduction of the total isoflavone level in the seed. Besides, we also found that the overexpression of GmMATE1 (C08) in soybean led to the increase of total isoflavone level in the seed. The study on isoflavone uptake function was also done on GmMATE4. A poly-glutamate domain with seven glutamate residues was found in the protein sequence of GmMATE4. Transmembrane protein topology prediction indicated that the poly-glutamate domain is at the vacuolar side, where cations are transported to the cytoplasm in exchange for isoflavones to be stored in the vacuole. The negative charge of the glutamate residues possibly functions to attract cations to the transporter and thus regulate transport efficiency. A similar poly-glutamate domain was also found in the GmMATE4 homologs in other species including Medicago truncatula, Vigna ungiculata, Abrus precatorius, and Cajanus cajan with a varied number of glutamate residues. We, therefore, hypothesized that the number of glutamate residues may alter the transport efficiency of GmMATE4. We generated mutated GmMATE4 constructs, Gmmate4(E>A*3) in which three glutamate residues were substituted by three alanine residues and Gmmate4(E>A*7) in which all the seven glutamate residues were substituted by seven alanine residues. Using yeast as the model, we found that Gmmate4(E>A*3) and Gmmate4(E>A*7) had a weakened ability to mediate the uptake of glycitin, genistein, and daidzein into the yeast cells compared to GmMATE4. Together with the vacuolar localization property of these MATE transporters (Objective 2), we concluded that that GmMATE1, and possibly also GmMATE2 and GmMATE4, are bona fide isoflavone transporters that promote the accumulation of isoflavones in soybean seeds. Using GmMATE4 and the mutated constructs, we found the significance of poly-glutamate residues in regulating the transporter function.

14143916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14143916.value: (1) Consolidated Knowledge of Secondary Compounds in Relation to Domestication and the Functions of Multidrug and Toxic Compound Extrusion (MATE) Transporters Legumes such as soybeans are rich in micronutrients and secondary compounds, which could address the “hidden hunger” of global micronutrient malnutrition and provide good sources for bioactive secondary compounds (Outputs #1, #2, #8). Isoflavones, a group of important nutraceutical compounds, are uniquely found in several legumes and are of high contents in soybean seeds (Output #2). However, domestication may have a strong selection effect on the secondary metabolite composition in legumes (Output #3). Polyphenols such as isoflavones are possible substrates of MATE transporters in plants. The accumulation of these substrates is often associated with domestication-related traits (Output #6). Protons and cellular pH seem to play an important role in the transportation function of MATE transporters (Output #7). (2) Functions of Seed MATE Transporters in Transporting Isoflavones Soybean seeds have exceptional high contents isoflavones. We have identified the first group of seed MATE transporters that could transport isoflavone (Output #4). We have performed a detailed functional analysis of GmMATE1 and GmMATE2 which are very similar in structure and properties. These MATE transporters could transport isoflavones, mainly in the aglycone forms. Soybean mutants defective in GmMATE1 had significantly reduced total seed isoflavone contents, whereas the overexpression of GmMATE1 in transgenic soybean promoted the accumulation of seed isoflavones. Their encoding genes for both GmMATE1 and GmMATE2 are mainly expressed in the developing soybean pods. The subcellular locations of both MATE transporters were found to be on vacuolar membranes. These data suggest that GmMATE1 and possibly also GmMATE2, are bona fide isoflavone transporters that promote the accumulation of isoflavones in soybean seeds via compartmentalizing isoflavones in the vacuole. We also characterized the GmMATE4 transporter (see the result of Objective 3 above) which could also transport isoflavone. We also demonstrated the importance of a poly-glutamate domain (with seven glutamate residues) in GmMATE4 using a site-directed mutagenesis approach (Output #9). (3) Regulations of Seed-Specific MATE Genes Using GUS as the reporters, we showed the promoter of GmMATE1 could direct the expression of the GUS in siliques of transgenic A. thaliana and developing pods of transgenic soybean (Output #4). In addition, we also showed that the expression of GmMATE4 may be regulated by an antisense transcript of its own (Output #5). These regulations of gene expression could be related to the physiological functions of the corresponding MATE genes.

14143916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14143916.value: In this research, we have identified the first group of seed MATE transporters that could transport isoflavone. We also performed some functional domain dissection and gene regulation studies. To manipulate this group of MATE transporters to increase isoflavone contents in soybean seeds, we are currently working on a few aspects as following up: (1) to enhance the expression of the corresponding MATE genes; (2) to search for germplasm resources from the wild soybeans for strong alleles; and (3) to further dissect functional domains for a better understanding of the control of substrate specificity and transport efficiency. Another interesting observation is that overexpression of the seed MATE transporter genes from soybean, together with the soybean isoflavone synthase gene in A. thaliana did not elevate the level of isoflavones in Arabidopsis seeds to a consistently detectable level. Therefore, A. thaliana could be used as a null model to rebuild a pathway that leads to the accumulation of isoflavones in seeds.

14143916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14143916.value: Isoflavones are important nutraceuticals with high health value. Soybean seed is one of the major sources of isoflavones from the diet. Previously, little was known about the transporters that regulate the accumulation of isoflavones in soybean seeds. In the project, we have experimentally verified the substrate specificities of a group of Multidrug and Toxic Compound Extrusion (MATE) transporters. The genes encoding these MATE transporters express in seed pods and the transporters are located on the vacuolar membrane. Therefore, they could bona fide isoflavone transporters that promote the accumulation of isoflavones in soybean seeds via compartmentalizing isoflavones in the vacuole. We have therefore identified possible targets for future crop improvement to enhance the contents of isoflavones in soybean seeds.

14145916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14145916.value: 強化子是精確調控各種細胞和腺體中基因表達的重要因子。在人類的疾病中曾發現不正常的強化子活動增加或減少。這些不正常的強化子活動部份和表觀遺傳學的特徵改變有關，例如脫氧核榶核酸的甲基化和組蛋白的修飾。研究不正常的強化子與人類疾病的關係牽涉以下的任務：（一）找出在正常和疾病的情況下相關細胞和腺體內活躍的強化子；（二）找出這些強化子調控的基因；以及（三）預測這些基因的表達如何受這些強化子的表觀遺傳學的特徵改變所影響。 早期的強化子搜尋方法（任務一）採用與環境氛圍無關的特徵，例如序列中的基本圖形（motifs）和進化保守度。直至過去數年才出現探用取自特定環境氛圍的序列數據來預測這些氛圍中活躍的強化子的方法。對於強化子的調控對象（任務二），過往曾以基因組距離，活躍度相互關係和序列的同步進化保守度作預測，但這些方法都不能找出特定環境氛圍中強化子的調控對象。最後，強化子對目標基因的量化作用的詳細模型（任務三）一直以來都未曾有大規模地建立過，尤其當多個強化子的影響需要一同被考慮。這三個任務的其中一個共通困難，是以往只有少數的環境氛圍擁有充足的轉錄組和表觀基因組數據。 我們過往設計過不同方法預測強化子、強化子調控對象和表觀基因組特徵對基因表達的量化影響。在這些研究項目中，我們在Nature, Genome Research, Genome Biology和Bioinformatics發表過十篇以上的論文。 根據這些經驗，我們認為以上三項任務應該一同處理而非分別解決，因為如果一個統計模型可以準確地以強化子的基因組特徵來預測一個基因在不同的環境氛圍中表達的變化，那麼這個模型可以同時找出持定的環境氛圍中活躍的強化子、它們的對象基因、以及二者之間的量化關係。這種統合的模型需要以大量的數據來決定它適合的參數值。近日由ENCODE、FANTOM5和Roadmap Epigenomics團隊所發表，前所未有的大量轉錄組和表觀基因組數據正好為我們提供了數百種人類細胞和腺體中所需的數據。 在這個研究項目中，我們將利用這些數據和量化模型來建構這數百種人類細胞和腺體中的強化子調控對象網絡。具體而言，我們將會（一）利用上述的數據和機器學習方法來找出人類細胞和腺體中強化子和目標基因的多對一關係；（二）研究不同強化子間（例如同步活躍、互相排斥和各自獨立）和不同目標基因間的關係；（三）找尋最具成本效益（根據所需的實驗種類和數據量來衡量）的方法來找出特定環境氛圍中的活躍強化子；以及（四）找出在正常細胞和腺體中活躍而在相關癌症樣本中發生變異的強化子，以搜尋能夠透過我們的量化模型去解釋表達度有所變化的目標基因。

14145916.label: Realisation of objectives
14145916.value: Objective 1: We have developed a computational method, JEME, for predicting target genes of transcriptional enhancers. It contains two stages, namely a global stage that captures the general activity correlation between enhancers and genes, and a local stage that identifies the target genes of each enhancer in a specific context (cell/tissue type, for example). Both stages allow a gene to be regulated by multiple enhancers at the same time. This method was shown to be more accurate than both baseline methods and several state-of-the-art methods using external validation data from independent biological experiments. We have used JEME to infer the target genes of transcriptional enhancers in 935 human cell lines, primary cells and tissues. We have also compared the modeling power of enhancer, promoter and gene body features, and found that enhancer features, though not as informative as promoter and gene body features in indicating gene expression levels, are still sufficiently informative for the purpose of inferring enhancer targets. We have further compared different types of enhancer features, and found that combining multiple features provides the best modeling power. Objective 2: Based on our predicted enhancer-target pairs, we have studied various properties of the enhancers, target genes, and their interaction network. In particular, we have studied the average number of regulating enhancers per gene, number of target genes per enhancer, frequency for an enhancer to regulate the closest gene, and distance distribution between an enhancer and a target. We have also shown that enhancer-target pairs frequently co-occur within the same topologically associating domain (TAD) and CTCF/cohesin-mediated chromatin domain (CCD). Finally, we have shown that enhancer-target interactions can be used as cell/tissue signatures to cluster samples of the same cell/tissue origin. Objective 3: We have provided all our predictions for the 935 samples on our web site (http://yiplab.cse.cuhk.edu.hk/jeme/). We have provided the predictions produced by two different models. These files have been used by many studies according to citation counts and email inquiries received. Objective 4: We have shown that having only a few key histone modification features is sufficient for predicting enhancer targets in a context different from the one from which training data were obtained with reasonable accuracy. This is a big improvement as compared to previous methods. For example, another state-of-the-art method, TargetFinder, requires hundreds of features for constructing accurate models, which is hard to use in practice since acquiring such a large amount of features by performing the corresponding biological experiments is very costly. Objective 5: We have discovered several enhancers with DNA methylation changes between cancer samples of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and normal hepatocytes. We have experimentally tested the activity of these enhancers in liver cells using reporter assays, and proved the regulation of these enhancers of our predicted target genes through epigenetic modulation (treatment of 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine to demethylate the DNA) and genome editing (using CRISPR-Cas9 to delete the enhancer sequence).

14145916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14145916.value: 1. We have found that epigenetic features at transcriptional enhancers can be used to predict their target genes in a context-specific manner with a reasonable accuracy. 2. We have inferred the enhancer-target networks in 935 human cell lines, primary cells and tissues, and provided them as a free resource for the community. 3. We have used our predicted enhancer-target networks to study various properties of gene regulatory mechanisms involving enhancers. 4. We have discovered several enhancers with over-expression in hepatocellular carcinoma associated with hypomethylation of their predicted enhancers. We have further used this idea to study an enhancer of the CEBPB gene in great detail. Since this study was an extension of the project not covered in the original proposal, this GRF grant was not explicitly acknowledged but other relevant RGC funds were acknowledged. 5. We have discovered various limitations and ambiguities in the current definition of transcriptional enhancers, and discussed this aspect in detail. 6. This project has led to two direct journal publications (one in Nature Genetics [2018 ISI journal impact factor, IF: 25.455], one in Briefings in Bioinformatics [IF: 9.101]), one indirect journal publication (in Nature Communications [IF: 11.878]), and a manuscript in preparation for an extended sub-project. 7. The funding has provided support for two PhD students and training for two undergraduate students to perform academic research. 8. This project has helped establish a number of research collaborations. Some of the details are listed in Part C.

14145916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14145916.value: 1. The across-sample prediction accuracy is still not good enough as compared to cross-validation results within the same sample. Other types of features need to be incorporated such as those related to the three-dimensional genome architecture. 2. In order to incorporate very different types of features, a new data integration framework is needed for biological data. We have proposed to develop such a framework and received a new GRF for this research project [project ID: 14203119]. This framework is not only for studying transcriptional enhancers but all types of gene regulatory mechanisms in general. 3. The knowledge and experience obtained from this study can be applied to study dysregulated enhancers in other human diseases. In addition to hepatocellular carcinoma, we are also studying several other diseases including Hirschsprung's disease and nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

14145916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14145916.value: Imagine that in a skyscraper, rooms are numbered from 1 to 1000. Some rooms contain a television. You can turn on a television by pressing its on/off switch. Some rooms contain a remote-control that can adjust the volume of any nearby televisions of the same brand. Interestingly, rooms that are physically nearby may not have adjacent room numbers due to the architecture. Finally, some televisions and remote controls are locked in cabinets, making them inaccessible. Now, given the volume of all televisions, can we find out remote controls that are adjusting the volume of each television at this moment? This is actually a fundamental question in molecular biology, where each gene (television) is controlled by its promoter (switch) and enhancers (remote controls). With an unknown and changeable three-dimensional architecture of DNA (floor plan), dynamic chromatin states (cabinets) and expression profiles of the genes (volume) in different cell/tissue types (skyscrapers), the goal is to infer the enhancer-target gene networks in many cell/tissue types. In this GRF project, we have tackled this problem by integrating a huge amount of experimental data using a machine learning framework. Using the networks, they have also identified disrupted enhancers in control of important genes in liver cancer.

14148116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14148116.value: The aim of this project is to improve understanding of the functional properties of embryonic stem cells (ESCs)-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). ESCs are derived from the inner cell mass of blastocysts. ESCs are capable of self-renewal and are pluripotent, meaning that they can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in the body, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. For successful transplantation, transplanted cells must survive, integrate, and functionally couple with the native myocardium. The functional properties of these potential replacement cells must therefore be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. ESC-CMs are electrically active and generate spontaneous calcium transients and action potentials. Local calcium release and calcium transients are important determinants of the excitation-contraction coupling of cardiomyocytes. However, regulation of these calcium signals and action potentials in early differentiating cardiomyocytes is not fully elucidated. Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channels are non-selective cation channels that permeate calcium. Previous studies showed that TRPV1 channels are expressed in adult cardiomyocytes and their expression decreases during hypertrophy. However, the functional role of TRPV1 in normal cardiomyocytes is unexplored. Interestingly, preliminary data from our group showed that TRPV1 proteins are uniquely expressed on the sarcoplasmic reticulum of ESC-CMs. Importantly, TRPV1-specific inhibitors decrease both the amplitude and the frequency of calcium transients and decrease the action potential frequency of ESC-CMs. These results suggested that basal TRPV1 activity regulates the function of these cardiomyocytes. On the other hand, further opening of TRPV1 by TRPV1 activators also decrease the calcium transients and action potentials of ESC-CMs, suggesting that the precise level of TRPV1 activity is important for the normal function of these cardiomyocytes. However, the mechanisms underlying how basal activity of TRPV1 and over-stimulation of TRPV1 would lead to the observed effects are unknown. The overall objective of this proposal is to investigate how the TRPV1 located on sarcoplasmic reticulum regulates the local calcium release, calcium transients and action potentials of ESC-CMs. A combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiology and genetic manipulation techniques will be employed. This project will provide novel and important information on the role of TRPV1 in regulating the function of ESC-CMs. Altogether, the present study will be crucial for understanding the complex biology of ESC-CMs and will be pivotal for revealing the therapeutic potentials of ESC-CMs. 這個研究計劃的目的是認識胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞（ESC-CMs）在功能上的特性。 胚胎幹細胞來自囊胚的內細胞團，能夠自我更新和擁有萬能的特性，這意味著它們可以無限地被培養，並有能力分化為體內所有的細胞類型，包括心肌。因此胚胎幹細胞是科學研究和未來治療應用極好的心肌細胞來源。能夠達致成功移植，移植的細胞必須生存，並與心臟的天然心肌在結構上和功能上整合。應用ESC-CMs於細胞治療法之前，我們必須更好地理解這些細胞的功能特性。 ESC-CMs是電活性的，它會產生出自發性的鈣瞬變和動作電位。局部鈣釋放和鈣瞬變是決定心肌細胞激發與收縮的聯結的重要因素。然而，我們尚未完全理解早期分化的心肌細胞是如何調節鈣信號和動作電位。瞬時受體電位香草酸亞型1（TRPV1）通道是非選擇性滲透鈣的陽離子通道。以往的研究表明，TRPV1表達於成人的心肌細胞中，心肌肥大期間其表達會降低。然而，現時還沒有研究查明TRPV1在正常心肌細胞中的功能。有趣的是，我們研究團隊的初步數據顯示，TRPV1蛋白質獨特地表達於ESC-CMs的肌質網上。重要的是，TRPV1的抑製劑減少鈣瞬變的波幅和頻率，並減少動作電位的頻率。這些數據表明基礎水平的TRPV1活性能調節ESC-CMs的功能。另一方面，TRPV1活化劑也降低了ESC-CMs的鈣瞬變和動作電位，這表明精確的TRPV1活性水平對於ESC-CMs的正常功能是重要的。然而，基礎水平的TRPV1和過度激活的TRPV1的作用機制還是未知的。 這個研究計劃的總體目標是研究位於肌質網的TRPV1是如何調控ESC-CMs的局部鈣釋放，鈣瞬變和動作電位。我們會使用細胞生物學、分子生物學、電生理和遺傳操作技術以達致研究目標。這研究將對TRPV1在調控ESC-CMs的功能中的作用提供重要的信息。總括來說，本研究將對理解複雜的ESC-CMs的生物學和揭示ESC-CMs的治療潛力至關重要。

14148116.label: Realisation of objectives
14148116.value: Aim 1. To investigate if TRPV1 controls the calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. By immunocytochemistry and fractionation followed by Western blotting, TRPV1 was found to be located on the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). In addition, calcium imaging using pharmacological tools suggested that TRPV1 controls calcium release from SR of ESC-CMs. Adenoviruses Ad-EF1a-DN-TRPV1-EF1a-BFP [containing dominant negative of TRPV1 (DN-TRPV1)] for functional knockdown of TRPV1 and Ad-EF1a-MCS-EF1a-BFP (where ‘MCS’ stands for ‘multiple cloning sites’) as control were made and used to infect ESC-CMs. By calcium imaging, in the absence of external calcium, TRPV1 opener capsaicin caused an increase in intracellular calcium in control BFP virus-infected cells. DN-TRPV1 decreased capsaicin-induced increase in intracellular calcium, suggesting that calcium release from SR was specifically through the TRPV1 channel. Taken together, our results showed that TRPV1 controls the calcium release from the SR of ESC-CMs. Aim 2. To investigate if TRPV1 is involved in regulating the global calcium transients and/or the spontaneous action potential of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. By calcium transient (CaT) measurement, both TRPV1 blockers and TRPV1 openers decreased the amplitude and frequency, and increased the time-to-peak and decay time of CaTs in ESC-CMs. In addition, functional knockdown of TRPV1 by DN-TRPV1 decreased both the amplitude and frequency and increased the time-to-peak and decay time of CaTs. Moreover, TRPV1 opener capsaicin’s effect on CaT was attenuated by functional knockdown of TRPV1. By patch clamping under current clamp condition, blockade or opening of TRPV1 all led to a decrease in rate and diastolic depolarization (DD) slope without affecting maximum diastolic potential (MDP) and duration of action potential (AP). The results suggest that precise level of TRPV1 activity is important for regulating the APs in ESC-CMs. In addition, functional knockdown of TRPV1 decreased both the rate and DD slope without affecting MDP and duration of APs. Moreover, TRPV1 opener capsaicin’s effect on APs was attenuated by functional knockdown of TRPV1. Taken together, our results showed that TRPV1 is involved in regulating the global CaTs and spontaneous APs of ESC-CMs, and that the precise level of TRPV1 activity is important for regulating the automaticity of ESC-CMs. Aim 3. To elucidate the mechanism of how calcium release from TRPV1 would regulate the spontaneous action potential of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. SR calcium release has been known to be one of the calcium sources that trigger NCX. We hypothesized that calcium release via TRPV1 would affect NCX activity in ESC-CMs. NCX current was measured by patch clamping. TRPV1 blocker capsazepine reduced NCX current densities at both -100 mV and +50 mV. Similarly, DN-TRPV1 adenovirus-infected ESC-CMs also showed smaller NCX current densities at -100 mV and +50 mV when compared to control ESC-CMs. We concluded that TRPV1 inhibition decreased both the forward and reverse modes of NCX. The inhibitory effects of TRPV1 blockade on both modes of NCX led us to investigate the role of each mode in ESC-CMs. KB-R7943, a widely-used NCX blocker, could specifically inhibit the reverse mode of NCX at lower concentration (0.1 uM) while inhibit both the reverse and forward modes of NCX at higher concentration (1 uM) as previously reported. Interestingly, 0.1 uM KB-R7943 did not bring changes in the amplitude, frequency, time-to-peak or decay50 of global CaTs. However, decay90 was significantly decreased. Furthermore, 0.1 uM KB-R7943 did not affect the beating rate, DD slope, MDP, APD30 and APD50 of spontaneous APs. However, APD90 was prolonged. On the other hand, 1 uM KB-R7943, which inhibited both modes, dramatically decreased the amplitude and frequency and delayed time-to-peak and decay time of global CaTs. 1 uM KB-R7943 also decreased the frequency and DD slope, shortened APD of spontaneous APs. SEA0400, another NCX blocker, was also reported to inhibit both modes of NCX. Consistently, similar effects of SEA0400 treatment as 1 uM KB-R7943 was observed. Therefore, we concluded that both modes of NCX are functional in ESC-CMs. Forward mode regulates the frequency, DD slope and APD while reverse mode only contributes to the APD. To explore which mode of NCX is TRPV1 connected to, we pretreated the ESC-CMs with 3 uM SEA0400 (blocks both modes of NCX) or 0.1 uM KB-R7943 (blocks NCX reverse mode). Pretreatment of SEA0400 significantly attenuated the effect of capsazepine on the frequency and DD slope of spontaneous APs. Interestingly, pretreatment of KB-R7943 could not rescue capsazepine’s effects on the amplitude, frequency or time-to-peak of global CaTs; instead, upon KB-R7943 pretreatment, capsazepine further slowed down decay90, suggesting that TRPV1 is also connected to the reverse mode of NCX. Taken together, calcium release from the basal activity of TRPV1 regulates spontaneous APs of ESC-CMs through regulating the activity of both modes of NCX. Aim 4. To elucidate the mechanism of how overstimulation of TRPV1 would decrease the spontaneous action potential of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. By immunocytochemistry, the staining pattern of BKCa was found to partially overlap with that of alpha-actinin (a protein located at the Z-line), suggesting BKCa is located near to the Z-line. By calcium imaging, BKCa blocker IbTX was shown to attenuate the effect of TRPV1 activator capsaicin on CaTs of ESC-CMs, while IbTX alone did not affect CaTs. BKCa opener NS1619 decreased both the amplitude and frequency of CaTs, in a way similar to TRPV1 activator’s effects (see Aim 2). By patch clamping using current clamp, blockage of BKCa was found to attenuate effect of TRPV1 opening on APs, while BKCa blockage alone did not affect APs. BKCa opener decreased the frequency and DD slope of APs, in a way similar to TRPV1 activator’s effects (see Aim 2). These results suggest that overstimulation of TRPV1 decreases spontaneous APs via activating BKCa. To further confirm the presence of BKCa current in ESC-CMs, patch clamping using voltage ramp protocol was performed. A current sensitive to BKCa blocker was detected. BKCa opener could further increase the current. Importantly, capsaicin increased this current, and this increase can be attenuated by IbTX. Whole cell voltage-clamp recordings in DN-TRPV1 adenovirus-infected ESC-CMs were also conducted; capsaicin-sensitive BKCa current was almost abolished in these cells, confirming that TRPV1 opening can increase BKCa current. The interplay between TRPV1 and BKCa raises the possibility that TRPV1 may be located in the vicinity of BKCa. BAPTA chelates calcium at any distance while EGTA chelates calcium at a relatively longer distance. Processes that can be suppressed by BAPTA but not by EGTA suggests calcium source and calcium sensor are within nanodomain (~20nm). In contrast, processes with an equal BAPTA/EGTA sensitivity occur within microdomain (~20-200nm). Therefore, BAPTA and EGTA can be used to distinguish if an effect caused by calcium occurs within nanodomain or microdomain. Addition of BAPTA to the intracellular environment (note: in all other conditions, EGTA was included in intracellular solution) greatly attenuated capsaicin-induced enhancement of BKCa currents, suggesting that TRPV1 and BKCa form a functional complex and that calcium from TRPV1 activates BKCa within nanodomain. Next, whether TRPV1 and BKCa physically interact with each other in ESC-CMs was determined by co-immunoprecipitation. In the immunoprecipitants by the anti-BKCa antibody, TRPV1 could not be detected, indicating that TRPV1 and BKCa were not physically coupled. Taken together, overstimulation of TRPV1 decreased the spontaneous APs of ESC-CMs via activating BKCa. To conclude, all the objectives in this project were 100% achieved.

14148116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14148116.value: TRPV1 is expressed on the SR of ESC-CMs and controls calcium release from the SR. TRPV1 was found to be located on the SR but not on the plasma membrane of the ESC-CMs. TRPV1 controls calcium release from the SR. Precise level of TRPV1 activity is important for regulating the automaticity of ESC-CMs. Both decreasing or increasing the activity of TRPV1 was found to decrease the amplitude and frequency of CaTs in ESC-CMs. In addition, both decreasing or increasing the TRPV1 activity was found to decrease the rate and DD slope of APs. These results suggest that the precise level of TRPV1 activity is important for regulating the automaticity of ESC-CMs. Both the forward mode and the reverse mode of NCX are functional in ESC-CMs. Forward mode of NCX regulates the frequency, DD slope and APD of spontaneous APs in ESC-CMs, while reverse mode of NCX only contributes to the APD of spontaneous APs. Basal activity of TRPV1 regulates spontaneous APs by stimulating both modes of NCX. Blocking the basal activity of TRPV1 was found to decrease the frequency and DD slope of spontaneous APs. Calcium release from basal opening of TRPV1 was found to stimulate the forward mode of NCX and affect the frequency, DD slope and APD of spontaneous APs. On the other hand, calcium release from basal opening of TRPV1 was found to stimulate the reverse mode of NCX and affect the APD of spontaneous APs. BKCa is expressed in ESC-CMs. BKCa is expressed at both molecular level (as revealed by immunostaining) and functional level (as revealed by patch clamping) in ESC-CMs. BKCa was found to form a functional complex with TRPV1 without physically interacting with TRPV1. Overstimulation of TRPV1 regulates spontaneous APs by stimulating BKCa. Overstimulation of TRPV1 by TRPV1 opener was found to decrease the frequency and DD slope of spontaneous APs through increasing BKCa current. All results involving expression of TRPV1 on the SR and the role of basal activity level of TRPV1 in regulating the automaticity of ESC-CMs via stimulating NCX were published in form of conference abstracts and were packaged into a full-length research paper that is under revision (second revisions from the journal). The findings related to the overstimulation of TRPV1 in activating BKCa in ESC-CMs were published in form of conference abstracts; they are also packaged into another full-length research paper and the paper is under preparation.

14148116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14148116.value: In this study, TRPV1 was found to be located on the SR and control the calcium release in ESC-CMs. Whether TRPV1 would have the same location and function in other cell types are largely unknown. It is tempting to conduct further molecular and functional studies in different cell types to answer this. In addition, in this study, TRPV1 was found to be open at basal physiological level to regulate the function of ESC-CMs. While the existence of endogenous agonists such as endovanilloids, adenosine, ATP, and polyamines has previously been reported, it is unknown whether these agonists are present in cardiomyocytes, and if yes, whether their level would change in different physiological (e.g. mechanical stress) and/or pathological conditions (e.g. myocardial infarction, hypertrophy, atrial fibrillation). In addition, whether the activity and/or expression of TRPV1 would change upon different physiological and/or pathological conditions would need to be investigated. Further investigation would be conducted in these areas. Moreover, we aim to explore to develop new method [e.g. electrospray ionisation (ESI)-liquid chromatography (LC)-mass spectrometry (MS) (ESI-LC-MS)/MS method] for sensitive and reliable detection of the TRPV1 endogenous agonists.

14148116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14148116.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in the body, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. The functional properties of these potential replacement cells must be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. Calcium signals and electrical signals are important determinants of the functions of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). In this project, a combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiology and genetic manipulation techniques were employed. Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channels were identified to be a novel calcium release channel in ESC-CMs. Increasing or decreasing the activity of TRPV1 channels decreases both the calcium signals and electrical signals of ESC-CMs, suggesting that the precise activity level of TRPV1 channels is important for ESC-CM function. Detailed mechanisms of how TRPV1 channels exert their effect were also elucidated in this study. This project has generated novel and important information on the role of TRPV1 in regulating the functions of ESC-CMs. Altogether, this project is crucial for understanding the complex biology of ESC-CMs and is pivotal for revealing the therapeutic potentials of ESC-CMs.

14148916.label: Realisation of objectives
14148916.value: 1. Research achievements related to Objective 1: As described in the original project proposal, bzs433 was isolated from a T-DNA activation tagging mutant screen for bzr1-1D suppressor mutants (bzs) in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. bzr1-1D is a dominant gain-of-function mutant of BZR1, a master transcription factor in the brassinosteroid (BR) signaling pathway. This suppressor mutant screen was designed to identify novel gain-of-function mutations that can suppress bzr1-1D phenotypes. As expected for gain-of-function mutant screen, the bzs433 mutant showed a dominant inheritance pattern. bzs433 is a semi-dwarf with a small rosette size, upward-curling leaves, and pendent fluorescence stem in both Columbia (Col-0) and bzr1-1D background. These phenotypes are different from that of bzr1-1D, therefore it was chosen for further study. More interestingly, the mutant has clear defects in secondary cell wall (SCW) thickening, which might be the reason for the pendant inflorescence stem. Therefore, one objective of this project is to further characterize this mutant’s SCW phenotypes. (1) The deposition of major SCW components is greatly reduced in the bzs433 mutant In the original grant proposal, we have shown that the gain-of-function bzs433 mutation and the BZS433-overexpression significantly impair SCW thickening and integrity. To confirm this preliminary result, in this project we systematically characterized the SCW phenotypes of the bzs433 mutant and the BZS433-ox plants by using both histochemical and biochemical analyses. The histochemical staining of the three major SCW components (cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin) indicated that overexpression of the BZS433 gene resulted in significant reduction in the deposition of three major SCW components compared to the wild type plant (Col-0). In addition, consistent with the discontinued SCW phenotype at the interfascicular fibers (IFs), the three SCW components were almost undetectable in the IF regions. Next, we biochemically measured the contents of the three major SCW components in the bzs433 mutant and BZS433-ox plants, which also significantly decreased in these plants, compared to the levels in the wild type (Col-0) plants. (2) The bzs433 mutation does not affect the cell wall digestibility of the mutant plant Digestibility of Cell walls is an important parameter for biofuel industry. To determine whether misexpression of BZS433 affects the digestibility of plant cell walls, we then measured the abundance of the G and S monomers of lignin and calculated the G/S ratio in the bzs433 mutant and BZS433-ox plants. The results indicated that the G/S ratio SCW digestibility was not affected by either the bzs433 mutation or BZS433 overexpression, although the contents of the “G” and “S” monomers were both drastically reduced in these plants. (3) The bzs433 mutant is normal in brassinosteroid (BR) responses but BZS433-ox plants are less sensitive to BR This part of study is not the focus of this project but since the bzs433 mutant was identified from a genetic mutant screen for bzr-1-D suppressors in BR signaling, we want to know whether BZS433 is involved in plant responses to BR. Treatments with brassinolide (BL) and the BR biosynthesis inhibitor brassinazole (Brz) suggested that the bzs433 mutation does not affect the plant’s responses to both BR and Brz in a dark testing condition. However, the BZS433-ox plants showed much reduced responses to both BL and Brz, suggesting that BZS433 might be involved in BR regulation of plant development (e.g. SCW formation) and this will be further addressed in future studies. 2. Research achievements related to Objective 2: (1) Loss-of-function effects of BZS433 on SCW formation The reduced accumulation of major SCW components in the bzs433 mutant and BZS433-ox plants suggests that BZS433 is likely a negative regulator of plant SCW formation. To confirm this result, we generated the loss-of-function mutants of BS433 by RNAi and CRISPR-Cas9, respectively, and analysed the SCW phenotypes in these mutants by histochemical and biochemical approaches. The results indicated that the SCW phenotype and levels of major SCW components in these mutants are just as normal as the wild type plant, confirming that BZS433’s negative role in SCW formation. (2) BZS433 negatively regulates the expression of SCW biosynthesis genes To understand the molecular basis that BZS433 affects SCW formation, we performed a transcriptome profiling of BZS433-regulated genes in BZS433-ox plants by RNA-sequencing. Consistent with the phenotype, most genes related to cell wall, particularly SCW biosynthesis were significantly down-regulated in the BZS433-ox1 plants. These include 20 xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase (XTHs) genes, 7 laccase genes, 10 genes for lignin biosynthesis; 5 for cellulose biosynthesis genes; 3 for xylan (hemicellulose) biosynthesis, 9 MYB factor genes, and 7 NAC factor genes. To validate the RNA-seq results, the expression level of selected key biosynthetic genes of cellulose (IRX3, IRX5 and CES8), hemicellulose (xylan) (IRX10, FRA8), and lignin (IRX4, IRX12, 4CL1, AtCOMT1 and CcAOMT1) was analysed by qRT-PCR in seedlings of Col-0, bzs433(Col), BZS433-ox and BZS433-RNAi plants. As expected, the expression of all these genes was significantly down-regulated in the BZS433-ox and bzs433(Col) plants, but up-regulated in the bzs433(Col)-RNAi plants. (3) BZS433 forms a protein complex with MYB4 and MYB32 to negatively regulate SCW biosynthesis The synthesis of SCWs is regulated by a multi-layered transcription regulatory network that mainly consists of NAC- and MYB-type of transcription factors (TFs). The first layer of this transcription network is formed by the so-called ‘master regulators’ which are mostly NAC-type TFs (e.g. VND1-VND7, NST1/2) or homeobox HD-ZIP Class III (HD-ZIPIII) TFs. The second layer contains only two MYB TFs (MYB46 and MYB83), whereas the third layer include more than 10 MYBs that either positively or negatively regulate SCW formation. This third layer of TFs directly target the structural genes of SCW biopolymers. Our gene cloning indicated that BZS433 encodes a novel MYB-type TF. To determine its position and role in the transcription regulatory network of SCW biosynthesis, we tested the possible interactions between BZS433 and other known TFs from different layers of the network by yeast two-hybrid assays. The results unveiled that BZS433 only interacts with MYB4 and MYB32, two MYBs in the layer 3 that negatively regulate SCW formation, suggesting that the BZS433 likely forms a protein complex with MYB4 and MYB32 to negatively regulate SCW biosynthesis. The interactions between BZS433 and MYB4, MYB32 in planta have been confirmed by Bimolecular Fluorescence Complementation (BiFC) method. (4) Genetic study confirmed the role of BZS433 function in plant SCW formation Since our yeast two-hybrid assay suggested that BZS433 interacts with MYB4 and MYB32 in the third layer of the transcription network, we then attempted to test the genetic relationship between BZS433 and its upstream and downstream components. So far, we got two double transgenic plants between BZS433-ox and MYB46-ox, and SND1-ox, and phenotypic analyses of these plants indicated that both MYB46-ox and SND1-ox can completely or largely suppress the SCW defects in the bzs433-ox plants. SND1 belongs to the first layer and MYB46 belongs to the second layer of the transcription network. These results suggest that BZS433 may play a more important role in SCW formation, where it not only interacts with MYB4 and MYB32 to negatively regulate the expression of SCW biosynthetic genes but also modulate the activity of other TFs in the pathway including MYB46. The exact role of BZS433 in the network will be further determined in the future by using different approaches such as yeast one-hybrid assay, ChIP-seq and the ongoing genetic studies.

14148916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14148916.value: Secondary cell walls (SCWs) are important for plants to support their growth and adapt to changing environments. SCWs are composed mainly of three biopolymers, namely lignin, cellulose and hemicellulose. However, the molecular mechanisms by which regulate SCW formation and development have not been fully understood. From a T-DNA activation tagging-based genetic mutant screen in Arabidopsis, we identified a new mutant, bzs433, which has severe defects in SCW formation in stems, making the plant cannot stand erectly. Microscopy study indicated that the SCW of the mutant is very thin and the SCW deposition in interfascicular fibers is completely missing. SCW components assay showed that the level of the three SCW biopolymers (cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin) was significantly decreased in the mutant. BZS433 encodes a MYB-type transcription factor and overexpression of BZS433 led to similar SCW phenotypes as the bzs433 mutant. On the contrary, loss of BZS433 function resulted in normal SCW morphology, suggesting that BZS433 is a negative regulator of SCW biosynthesis. Furthermore, through a transcriptome profiling in the BZS433-overexpressing plants, we identified 61 BZS433-regulated genes involved in SCW development, which were mostly down-regulated by BZS433 overexpression. Finally, we demonstrated that BZS433 forms a protein complex with MYB4 and MYB32 to negatively regulate SCW formation. Taken together, our results suggest that we identified a novel negative transcription regulator for SCW biogenesis in plants.

14151416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14151416.value: In plant cells, sorting of soluble cargo proteins to the vacuoles are mediated by specific receptor-cargo interaction. Specific-sequence information, known as vacuolar sorting determinant (VSD), is recognized by sorting receptors such as vacuolar sorting receptor (VSR) and receptor-homology-transmembrane-RING-H2 (RMR) proteins. There are two types of VSD: (1) sequence-specific VSD (ssVSD), which is often found in hydrolytic enzymes that are targeted to lytic vacuoles; and (2) C-terminal VSD (ctVSD), which is often found at the C-terminus of storage proteins targeted to protein storage vacuoles. It is imperative that receptor-cargo interaction must be specific in order to avoid mis-sorting of proteins. However, how the sequence information of ctVSD is ‘read’ by the sorting receptors is currently unclear. It has been reported that both RMR and VSR are involved in recognizing ctVSD of plant storage proteins. One common feature of RMR and VSR is that they both contain a protease-associated (PA) domain in their N-terminal lumenal regions. The main theme of this proposal is to address how the PA domains of AtRMR1 and AtVSR1 recognize the ctVSD of cargo-proteins. First, we have identified structural features in the PA domain of AtRMR1 that may be important in recognition of ctVSD cargos. We will use site-directed mutagenesis to probe if mutations in these structural features will affect receptor-cargo interactions and result in mis-sorting of cargos in Arabidopsis protoplasts. Next, we will test the hypothesis if the PA domain of AtVSR1 (AtVSR1-PA) is involved in ctVSD cargo recognition. Finally, to provide the structural details of how ctVSD interacts with its sorting receptors, we propose to determine the crystal structures of ctVSD cargo in complex with the PA domain of AtRMR1 (AtRMR1-PA) and AtVSR1-PA. This proposal aims to understand the fundamental rules behind how sorting receptors recognize the sequence-specific information for correct trafficking of cargo proteins. A better understanding of such rules may help us to design specific proteins to be targeted to the protein storage vacuoles of genetically-engineered crops. 在植物細胞中，可溶性貨物蛋白的分揀排序是由特異性受體與貨物蛋白相互作用介導的。液泡分揀決定子（vacuolar sorting determinant，VSD）具有序列特異性，可以被VSR（Vacuolar sorting receptor）和RMR（Receptor-homology-transmembrane-RING-H2）這兩種分揀受體識別。有兩種類型的VSD：（1）序列特異性VSD（sequence-specific VSD，ssVSD），通常存在於裂解液泡的水解酶中；（2）C-末端VSD（C-terminal VSD，ctVSD），通常存在於蛋白質貯藏液泡中的貯藏蛋白的C-末端。至關重要的是，受體與貨物蛋白的相互作用必須是特異性的以避免出現蛋白質的錯誤分揀。然而，ctVSD的序列信息如何被分揀受體識別到目前還不清楚。 根據先前的研究，RMR和VSR都參與識別植物貯藏蛋白的ctVSD。RMR和VSR有一個共同的特點：在它們的N-端都包含有一個蛋白酶相關（protease-associated，PA）結構域。該提案的主要目標是解釋AtRMR1和AtVSR1的PA結構域是如何識別貨物蛋白中的ctVSD。首先，我們已經確定了AtRMR1的PA結構域的結構特征，其可能對於識別ctVSD具有重要作用。我們將會利用定點突變來檢測這些結構特征的突變是否會影響受體與貨物蛋白的相互作用，並導致貨物蛋白在擬南芥原生質體中的錯誤分揀。接下來，我們會論證AtVSR1的PA結構域參與ctVSD識別的猜測。最後，為了提供ctVSD如何同它的分揀受體相互作用的結構細節，我們將會解析ctVSD與AtRMR1-PA以及ctVSD與AtVSR1-PA這兩個復合物的晶體結構。這項提案的目的是了解分揀受體如何識別貨物蛋白中的特異性的序列信息，並將貨物蛋白正確轉運的機理。對此機理更加清楚的了解，可以幫助我們設計出特定的蛋白質，針對性的進入到基因工程作物的蛋白質貯藏液泡中。

14151416.label: Realisation of objectives
14151416.value: The main theme of this GRF is to understand how the C-terminal sorting determinant (ctVSD) is recognized by sorting receptors. In plants, there are two families of sorting receptors that can bind ctVSD, namely, vacuolar sorting receptor (VSR) and receptor-homology-transmembrane-RING-H2 (RMR) proteins. Since both VSR and RMR contain a protease-associated domain in the N-terminal lumenal region, we focus on understanding how the PA domain of VSR and RMR interacts with the ctVSD. 1. VSR1-PA interacts with the C-terminal sequence of cruciferin 1 We first tested if the PA domain of VSR1 (VSR1-PA) could interact with the C-terminal sequence of a storage protein, cruciferin 1 (CRU1), by in-vitro pull-down assay. Our results showed that VSR1-PA was associated with the NHS-resins coupled with the C-terminal peptide of CRU1, but not with the control resins coupled with glycine (Figure 1, Tsao et al.). Our results suggest that VSR1-PA can interact with the C-terminal sequence of CRU1. 2. Crystallographic analysis reveals how the C-terminal sequence of CRU1 is recognized by VSR1 To understand how the VSR1-PA recognizes the C-terminal sequence of CRU1, we have determined the crystal structures of the VSR1-PA in complex with the C-terminal pentapeptide (468-RVAAA-472) of CRU1. We expressed and purified recombinant VSR1-PA in E. coli as reported previously (Luo et al., 2014, Plant Cell, 26:3693). The structures of VSR1-PA in complex with ctVSD of CRU1 were determined to 2.35 Å and 2.45 Å at pH 6.5 and 9.0, respectively. The two structures determined are essentially identical with an average Cα displacement value of 0.18 Å. There are two major structural insights: (1) Arg95 is essential for recognizing the C-terminal carboxylate group of the ctVSD of CRU1; (2) the backbone conformation of CRU1 is important in forming a parallel β-sheet with the switch III residues of VSR1-PA and is maintained by a number of backbone-backbone hydrogen bonds (Figure 1, Tsao et al.). 3. Structural insights on receptor-cargo interactions were supported by mutagenesis Based on the structural insights, we argued that a R95M substitution of VSR1-PA and replacing the last 4 residues of ctVSD of CRU1 with proline residues should break the interaction between VSR1-PA and ctVSD of CRU1. We tested this hypothesis using in-vitro pull-down assay and thermal shift assay (Figure 2, Tsao et al.) and showed that both R95M and the PPPP substitutions disrupted the VSR1-PA/ctVSD interactions. Similar observations were found for VSR1-NT/ctVSD interactions, supporting the structural insights obtained in the crystal structures are essential for VSR/ctVSD interactions. 4. Specific interaction between VSR1/ctVSD is essential for vacuolar sorting of ctVSD-containing cargos. Next, we showed that the presence of the C-terminal decapeptide sequence of CRU1 (spRFP-Cru1) redirected the protein to the vacuoles in Arabidopsis protoplasts. In contrast, such vacuolar sorting was disrupted when the last four residues of the CRU1 sequence was replaced by proline in the spRFP-Cru1PPPP (SYGRPRPPPP) variant. The secretion assay further showed that the proline substitution promoted mis-sorting of spRFP-Cru1PPPP into the culture medium. We further showed that co-expression of R95M mutant of VSR1, but not wild-type VSR1, promoted mis-sorting of spRFP-Cru1 cargos to the culture medium (Figure 3, Tsao et al.). Taken together, our results suggest that specific interaction between VSR1/ctVSD is essential for vacuolar sorting. 5. Novel ctVSD of storage proteins recognized by VSR1 were identified and probed by mutagenesis studies In A. thaliana genome, there are four isoforms of cruciferin (CRU1, CRU2, CRU3, CRU4) and three isoforms of vicilin-like storage proteins (VL21, VL22, VL43). To explore if these proteins carry ctVSDs that are recognized by VSR1, we coupled the C-terminal decapeptide sequences of these proteins to the NHS-resins and test their interactions with Arabidopsis-expressed VSR1-NT in a pull-down assay (Figure, Tsao et al.) and showed that VSR1-NT interacted with the C-terminal sequences from cruciferin 4 (CRU4) and vicilin-like storage protein 22 (VL22). Mutagenesis studies support the structural insights obtained for VSR1/CRU1 interactions also held for VSR1/CRU4 and VSR1/VL22 interactions. We further showed that tagging the ctVSD of VL22, but not its proline-substituted variant (spRFP-VL22PPPP), redirected spRFP-VL22 to the vacuoles (Figure 4, Tsao et al.). The secretion assay showed that spRFP-VL22 was largely retained inside the protoplasts. In contrast, proline substitutions at the C-terminus resulted in a significant increase in secretion of spRFP-VL22PPPP. Co-expression of spGFP-VSR1-R95M increased secretion of spRFP-VL22 into the culture medium. Taken together, our results suggest that the ctVSD of VL22 is recognized by VSR1 in Arabidopsis protoplasts for its sorting to the vacuoles. 6. Sequence-specificity of RMR1, RMR2 and VSR1 are different We showed that in VSR1, the cargo-binding loop of the PA domain is involved in recognizing the ctVSD. As the cargo-binding loop contains a RGxCxF motif that is conserved in both VSR and RMR but the switch III residues are not conserved among the two families of sorting receptors (Figure S4, Tsao et al.), we hypothesized that the sequence-specificity of RMR and VSR may differ. We transiently expressed RMR1-NT and RMR2-NT in Arabidopsis protoplasts and their interactions with ctVSD from phaseolin, cruciferin 1-4, vicilin-like storage 21, 22 and 43. We showed that RMR1-NT interacted with the ctVSD, cruciferin 1 and 2, while RMR2-NT only interacted with cruciferin 2. These interactions were disrupted by replacing the conserved Arg residue in the RGxCxF motif (R89M in RMR1, R84M in RMR2) with a methionine. Similarly, proline substitutions of ctVSD also disturbed the interaction between RMR1/2 and their cognate ctVSDs. These mutagenesis results suggest RMR use the same cargo-binding site on the PA domain to recognize its cognate ctVSDs. Although we were not able to produce diffraction-quality crystals for structure determine of RMR, homology modeling of the RMR/ctVSD complex suggest variable residues in the switch III region may provide different local environment for sequence prefences in the ctVSD. 7. ctVSD of CRU2 is recognized by RMR2 for vacuolar sorting. To test if interaction between RMR2 and CRU2 is essential for its vacuolar sorting, we transiently co-expressed wild-type or R84M mutant of RMR2 with spRFP-Cru2 or its proline-substituted variant (spRFP-Cru2PPPP) in Arabidopsis protoplasts. Confocal imaging showed that Cru2-tagged spRFP was sorted to the vacuoles when co-expressed with wild-type RMR2. Vacuolar sorting of spRFP-Cru2 was prevented by R84M substitution of RMR2 or proline substitution in the ctVSD of CRU2, suggesting the ctVSD of CRU2 is recognized by RMR2 for vacuolar sorting. 8. The RING domain of RMR1 is an E3 ligase that is important for its trafficking In a side project, we determined the crystal structure of the RING domain of RMR1 and showed that it is an E3 ligase that undergoes self-ubiquitination at a unique Lys-288 residue (Figure 1 and 3, Chen et al.). Interestingly, mutations that inhibited self-ubiquitination resulted in retention of RMR1 in the Golgi, suggesting ubiquitination regulates proper trafficking of RMR (Figure 4. Chen et al.). In summary, we have combined structure determination, modelling, mutagenesis and functional studies to elucidate how ctVSD is recognized by the VSR and RMR and how such recognition is essential to vacuolar sorting of cargoes. In our opinion, we have achieved all the objectives.

14151416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14151416.value: We have determined the structure of VSR1-PA in complex with the ctVSD that provides a number of novel structural insights into how the PA domain recognizes the sequence-specific information on the cargo: 1. The C-terminal carboxylate group of ctVSD is recognized by Arg95 in the cargo-binding loop. In the crystal structure of VSR1-PA in complex with the CRU1 ctVSD, Arg95 form salt-bridges to the C-terminal carboxylate group of the bound cargo peptide. Replacing the positively charged Arg95 with a methionine residue disrupted the VSR/ctVSD interaction and led to increases in mis-sorting of the cargos to the medium in Arabidopsis protoplasts. 2. Proline is not favored at the last 4 residues of ctVSD Since proline residue lacks backbone amide group and has restricted backbone dihedral phi angle, it is not favored at the last 4 residues of the ctVSD. Consistent with the views that the backbone conformation of ctVSD is essential for VSR/ctVSD interaction, we showed that proline substitutions to the ctVSD sequences disrupted VSR/ctVSD interactions and led to mis-sorting of cargos in Arabidopsis protoplasts. 3. Tyr99 of the cargo-binding loop favors hydrophobic residues at the last two residues of ctVSD The complex crystal structure of VSR1-PA/ctVSD reveals that the last two residues of ctVSD could form hydrophobic interactions with Tyr99 of the cargo-binding loop of VSR1-PA, justifying the observation that ctVSD is often composed of mainly hydrophobic residues. 4. Local electrostatic environment favors basic, but disfavors acidic, residues in the ctVSD. In the cargo-binding site of VSR1-PA, there are two nearby negatively charged residues, Asp129 and Glu132. Modelling suggests that Arg602 in the ctVSD of β-conglycinin could form a salt-bridge with Asp129 of VSR1-PA. Charge-charge repulsion could also explain why VSR1 could not recognize the C-terminal sequences of CRU3, VL21 and VL43 that are rich in acidic residues. 5. We identified novel ctVSD in CRU2 and VL22. Through mutagenesis and confocal image analysis, we demonstrated VSR1-PA recognizes the C-terminal sequence of CRU1 and VL22, and RMR2-NT recognizes that of CRU2 for their vacuolar sorting. 6. We determined the crystal structure of the RING domain of RMR1 and showed that its E3 ligase activity is involved in its proper trafficking.

14151416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14151416.value: The structure of VSR1-PA in complex with the ctVSD of CRU1 provides for the first time how sequence information of ctVSD is ‘read’ by a sorting receptor at an atomic resolution. Given that the full sequence of ctVSD is accommodated in the cargo-binding site of VSR1-PA, it is tempting to speculate that the PA domain is sufficient for reading the ctVSD and sort the cargo to the vacuoles. One possible future development is to use the knowledge gain to engineering transgenic plants with designer sequences that sort proteins to the protein storage vacuoles in seeds. We can also use the rules of receptor-cargo interactions to predict which proteins in the genome is a potential cargo of VSR using bioinformatics techniques. On a side note, we are excited to find out that the E3 ligase activity of RMR is important in its trafficking. While the cargo-binding domain (i.e. the N-terminal PA domain) determines which cargo can get on the sorting receptor, it is the C-terminal cytoplasmic domain that determine the final destination of the receptor/cargo complex. It will be interesting to see if there are cross-talk between the two domains. (e.g. does cargo-binding regulates the E3 ligase activity of the RING domain?)

14151416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14151416.value: Seeds such as rice and wheat are staple foods that are consumed regularly in human diet. Storage proteins are transported by transporters known as vacuolar sorting receptors to a specialized location within seeds known as protein storage vacuoles. These sorting receptors recognizes sequence-specific information, or vacuolar sorting determinants (VSDs) on its cargo proteins. These VSDs are often located at the C-terminus of the cargo proteins so they are called C-terminal VSD (ctVSD). In this study, we use X-ray crystallography to elucidate the atomic structure of the protease-associated domain of a vacuolar sorting receptor bound with the ctVSD of a storage protein, cruciferin so that we can understand what are the rules that determine how VSRs recognize the sorting signals of storage proteins and target them to the vacuoles. Our work is complemented by mutagenesis and cellular experiments to demonstrate that the rules on receptor-cargo interactions gained from the structural studies are applicable in plant cells. A better understanding on how proteins are transported in seeds may help us in the future to apply our knowledge in target specific proteins (e.g. vaccine) to the protein storage vacuoles of engineered crops.

14160516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14160516.value: Hybrid rice can achieve higher yield by producing more spikelets per panicle than conventional cultivars. However, the yield potential of these hybrids is often not fully materialized due to poor grain filling in their late-flowering spikelets. Through our extensive investigations both in the field and in the laboratory, we have identified several factors that could influence grain filling, such as soil drying and N supply, hormones and their interactions, root activities and root-sourced compounds etc. Based on these findings, we have developed and promoted in large scale an alternative wetting and drying (AWD) water management scheme that could increase yield by 8-10% and reduce water usage by 25-30%. However, the key question regarding the molecular and genetic distinction between the early and late flowering spikelets remains largely unanswered. Indeed, few mutants or genes affecting grain filling have been reported so far. To address this problem from a genome perspective, we have generated preliminary RNA-Seq data for the early flowering (aka superior) spikelets that have higher grain filling rate and the late flowering (aka inferior) spikelets that have low grain filling rate. We have identified 10,110 differentially expressed genes and GO-term analysis has shown that besides the energy metabolism and transport genes, many genes involved in RNA processing are differentially expressed. In addition, we could identify unique alternative splicing events in superior and inferior spikelets, which raised an intriguing question as to whether alternative splicing could have important biological roles in regulating grain filling. It has been reported that DNA methylation changes are associated with endosperm-specific gene expression in rice and some key carbohydrate metabolism genes such as starch synthase III are targeted by demethylation. We have generated BS-Seq data to analyze DNA methylation in the superior and inferior grains. Together with the transcriptome data, we propose to: 1. Compare gene expression and alternative splicing events in both sink (superior and inferior spikelets) and source (straws) tissues in hybrid and conventional inbred rice cultivars. 2. Compare methylation status of the grain-filling-related differentially expressed genes in sink and source tissues in hybrid and conventional rice cultivars. 3. Select candidate genes for functional tests in order to examine their potential roles in regulating rice grain filling. This project could provide novel insights into the genetic mechanism regulating rice grain filling and identify crucial regulators for future crop improvement. 14160516.label: Realisation of objectives
14160516.value: Objective 1: Compare gene expression and alternative splicing events in both sink (superior and inferior spikelets) and source (straws) tissues in hybrid and conventional inbred rice cultivars. Moderate soil drying imposed at the post-anthesis stage has been known to significantly increase starch accumulation in inferior grains of rice. We applied moderate drying (MD) treatments to the soil at the post-anthesis stage and followed the dynamics of the conversion process of soluble sugars to starch in inferior grains using RNA-seq analysis. An elevated level of ABA induced by MD was consistently associated with down-regulation of ABA8ox2, suggesting that lower expression of this gene may be responsible for the higher ABA content, potentially resulting in better filling in inferior grains. In addition, MD treatments up-regulated genes encoding five key enzymes involved sucrose-to-starch conversion and increased the activities of enzymes responsible for soluble-sugar reduction and starch accumulation in inferior grains. Differentially expressed transcription factors, including NAC, GATA, WRKY, and M-type MADS, were predicted to interact with other proteins in mediating filling of inferior grains as a response to MD. Transient expression analysis showed that NAC activated WAXY expression by binding to its promoter, indicating that NAC played a key role in starch synthesis of inferior grains under MD treatment. Our results provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms that regulate grain filling in inferior grains of rice under moderate soil drying. These results have been mainly published in two papers by Wang et al. (2017, 2019) in Plant and Cell Physiology (doi: 10.1093/pcp/pcx072) and Journal of Experimental Botany (https://doi.org/10.1093/jxb/erz010). Objective 2: Compare methylation status of the grain-filling-related differentially expressed genes in sink and source tissues in hybrid and conventional rice cultivars. Stem of rice is a specific temporary source organ and contributes between 20-40% of the grain filling. Moderate soil drying (MD) enhanced carbon reserve flow from stems to increase grain yield. The dynamics and biological relevance of DNA methylation in carbon reserve remobilization during grain filling are clear. We generated whole-genome single-base resolution maps of the DNA methylome in the stem. During grain filling under MD, we observed an increase in DNA methylation of total cytosines, with more hypomethylated than hypermethylated regions. Genes responsible for DNA methylation and demethylation were up-regulated, suggesting that DNA methylation changes in the stem were regulated by antagonism between DNA methylation and demethylation activity. In addition, methylation in the CG and CHG contexts was negatively associated with gene expression, while that in the CHH context was positively associated with gene expression. A hypermethylated/up-regulated transcription factor of MYBS2 inhibited MYB30 expression and possibly enhanced b-Amylase5 expression, promoting subsequent starch degradation in rice stems under MD treatment. In addition, a hypermethylated/down-regulated transcription factor of ERF24 was predicted to interact with, and thereby decrease the expression of, abscisic acid 89-hydroxylase1, thus increasing abscisic acid concentration under MD treatment. We also compared the DNA methylome in indica and japonica rice stems. DNA methylation levels in indica were higher than in japonica and positively correlated with genome size. MD treatment had a weak impact on the changes in methylation levels in indica. Moreover, the number of differentially methylated regions (DMRs) was much lower in indica, indicating cultivar-specific methylation patterns in response to MD during grain filling. The hypomethylated beta-glucosidase 1 gene, involved in the starch degradation process, was up regulated in indica, resulting in improved starch to sucrose conversion under MD treatment. Additionally, increased expression of MYBS1 transactivated gene of AMYC2/OsAMY2A in both indica and japonica, leading to enhanced starch degradation under MD. In contrast, the downregulated MYB30 expression resulted in improved BMY5 expression in the two cultivars. Our findings decode the dynamics of DNA methylation in indica and japonica rice stems and propose candidate genes for improving carbon reserve remobilization. These results are published in two papers by Wang et al. (2020) in Plant Physiology (https://doi.org/10.1104/pp.20.00141) and Journal of Experimental Botany (https://doi.org/10.1093/jxb/eraa502). Objective 3: Select candidate genes for functional tests in order to examine their potential roles in regulating rice grain filling We applied moderate soil drying (MD) to rice at the post-anthesis stage, and then followed by dynamic proteomic and transcriptomic studies using SWATH-MS and RNA-seq analysis to identify key genes in grain filling. MD treatment upregulated the proteins alpha-glucosidase, beta-glucosidase and starch phosphorylase, which are responsible for starch degradation. Furthermore, MD treatment enhanced the expression of proteins involved in the sucrose synthesis pathway, including SPS8 and SPP1. In addition, various monosaccharide transporters (MSTs) and sucrose transporter 2 (SUT2), which are pivotal in carbon reserve remobilization, were also upregulated in straw by MD treatment. Differentially expressed transcription factors, including GRAS, TCP, trihelix, TALE, C3H, and NF-YC, were predicted to interact with other proteins to mediate carbon reserve remobilization in response to MD treatment. Further correlation analysis revealed that the abundances of most of the differentially expressed proteins were not correlated with the corresponding transcript levels, indicating that the carbon reserve remobilization process was probably regulated by posttranscriptional modification. Our results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of carbon reserve remobilization from straw to grain in rice under MD conditions. These results are mainly published in The Plant Journal (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.14565) by Wang et al. (2019).

14160516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14160516.value: In rice, better use of the carbon reserve pre-stored in rice stem and sheath contributes significantly to its yield. The initiation of whole-plant senescence is required to remobilize the carbon reserve to the grains. Controlled moderate soil-drying during the rice grain filling period has been shown to induce senescence, and hence, increase the remobilisation of non-structural carbohydrates from the stem to the grains. Nonetheless, the mechanism by which controlled moderate soil drying improves this carbon reserve remobilisation remains unclear. With the support of this research grant, we performed functional transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of rice stems and grains under moderate soil drying conditions and provided molecular and genetic evidences to explain the effects of moderate soil drying at the grain filling stage. The understanding of the remobilisation of non-structural carbohydrates in genome-wide and physiological levels has increased, and some links between molecular clues and physiological responses have been proposed.

14160516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14160516.value: This project has provided novel insights into the genetic mechanism regulating rice grain filling and identified crucial molecular regulators for future crop improvement. Information gathered should not only help explain why some agronomic practices such as controlled soil drying can enhance grain filling of inferior spikelets, but also crop improvement such as molecular breeding can benefit from the key genes and regulators we have found. We expect that we shall work with breeders for more useful genes and traits that can lead to better grain filling in terms of better use of pre-stored carbons.

14160516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14160516.value: We have been promoting for some time the controlled soil drying at grain filling stage as a way to increase rice yield and at the same time to save the irrigation used. This new irrigation practice, also called Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technique, has been well received by farmers and fundamentally changed the concept about irrigation management at the later stage of rice season. The results from this study proves that the AWD practice can initiate the molecular and genetic processes that controls the remobilization of the pre-stored carbon reserve during the grain filling period.
