14202016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202016.value: Imagine a world constructed of programmable matters and reconfigurable elements; an intelligent environment where objects can take on multiple forms based on localized desires and perform a myriad of tasks. The world would require to be conjoined with sensing, actuating and various human-inspired capabilities. Recent advances in additive manufacturing created four-dimensional (4D) printing technology as an emerging technology for creating dynamic devices that can change their shape and/or function on-demand and over time. This technique provides an effective means from idea to reality with performance-driven functionality built into structures. Recently, some researchers employed 3D printing combined with active materials to offer an innovative method for crafting custom-designed self-folding structures but it is still at the early stage. Moreover, the printable capability of active materials for self-unfolding still remains as a significant challenge. Self-folding/unfolding designs can have useful engineering applications such as robotic arms, to automate the folding and improve strength-to-weight ratio. They are also advantageous in situations where it is difficult to perform the manipulations needed to make the folding and unfolding movements. Often this is the case at small or large scales or in remote locations such as inside human-body, on the ocean floor or in outer space. This project is aimed to advance the 4D printing technology and employ it to design, fabrication and test of self-unfolding/unfolding structures/devices that assemble from flat sheets and then deploy on-demand automatically. Shape memory alloys (SMAs) and shape memory polymers (SMPs) are considered for transformation mechanisms printed in hinge forms. New aspects of metal- and polymer-based 4D printing processes are developed. The approach is based on a rigorous understanding of the complex thermo-mechanics of the SMA/SMP structures and experiments to determine the printed material properties, folding/unfolding motions of hinges in terms of relevant microstructural parameters as well as theory and simulation to describe the phenomena. The developed equipment and computational tools will be employed to digitally design and fabricate SMA/SMP adaptive structures that transform into a predetermined shape, changing property and function after fabrication and then recover their original shape. This project is expected to advance the state-of-the-art of SMA/SMP 4D printing, and provide pertinent formulations and results that will significantly contribute to a comprehensive understanding of thermo-mechanical behaviors of self-folding/unfolding structures and to be instrumental toward reliable fabrication and designs of these adaptive structures. 試想整個世界是由可編程的物體和可重組的元件組成的一個智能環境，根據環境的需要，物體可以呈現出多種形態來完成不同任務。這樣的世界需要有感知和驅動的能力。最近在增材製造領域的進展，創造出四維打印技術，它可以製造能隨時間變化按照人們需求而改變形狀或功能的動態設備。這項技術為環境自適應多功能結構的實現提供了有效的途徑。近來，一些學者運用三維打印技術結合智能材料，為製造特定的自動收縮結構提供了一個新穎的方法，但是這項技術才剛起步。用智能材料打印能自動變形的結構仍然是一個巨大挑戰。自動變形和恢復的設計有許多工程應用，比如能使其自動變形並提高強度重量比的機械臂。在難以執行需要變形和恢復操作的環境下，如在微小尺度，或在大範圍環境，亦或極端環境下；比如人體內部，海底深處，或是外太空，自動變形和恢復的設計十分有用。這項計劃的目的在於發展四維打印技術，同時將其應用於設計，製造和測試能自動變形的結構或設備，這些結構或設備能夠由平板直接組裝而成，然後按照需求自動變形展開。將形狀記憶合金和記憶複合材料作為變形機構打印成新的技術。這個方法是基於對形狀記憶合金/記憶複合材料結構複雜熱力學特性的深入理解；以及通過實驗來確定打印材料的屬性，連接處的自動變形/恢復運動和仿真來描述這樣的現象。用先進的設備和計算工具數字化地設計和製造形狀記憶合金/記憶複合材料自適應構，製造完成後能夠變形成預先設定的形狀，改變屬性和功能，之後又能恢復到最初的形狀。這項計劃能夠促進形狀記憶合金/記憶複合材料四維打印的發展，同時得到相關的方法和結果；這將極大地促進對能自動變形/恢復結構的熱機械特性的全面理解，從而有助於可靠地設計和製造這些自適應結構。

14202016.label: Realisation of objectives
14202016.value: One objective of this research is to create adaptive structures capable of self-expanding and self-shrinking by means of four-dimensional printing technology. An actuator unit was designed and fabricated directly by printing ﬁbers of shape memory polymers (SMPs) in ﬂexible beams with different arrangements. Experiments were conducted to determine thermo-mechanical material properties of the fabricated part revealing that the printing process introduced a strong anisotropy into the printed parts. The feasibility of the actuator unit with self-expanding and self-shrinking features was demonstrated experimentally. A phenomenological constitutive model together with analytical closed-form solutions were developed to replicate thermo-mechanical behaviors of SMPs. Numerical and experimental results revealed that the proposed planar lattice as meta-materials can be employed for plane actuators with self-expanding/shrinking features or as structural switches providing two different dynamic characteristics. A three-dimensional (3D) model was developed to simulate self-accommodation, anisotropic martensitic transformation/orientation, reorientation of martensite variants, asymmetry in tension-compression and phase-change-dependent elastic properties in shape memory alloys (SMAs) within a finite-stain regime. The model was developed based on a multiplicative decomposition of the deformation gradient into elastic and inelastic parts by satisfying the second law of thermodynamics in sense of Clausius-Duhem inequality. The mathematical equations were derived in terms of symmetric tensors simplifying the constitutive relations. The finite-strain model was linearized into the small-strain regime preserving the materially non-linear feature. A description of the time-discrete form of the proposed model and its associated solution algorithm was presented. Numerical simulations of the mechanical behaviors of highly-textured NiTi 3D printed parts, wires and helical springs subjected to simple and complex loadings were performed and compared with experiments. We explored large-deformation responses of hyper-elastic porous metamaterials made by 3D printing technology. They were designed as a repeating arrangement of unit-cells in parallelogram and hexagonal shapes. Fused deposition modeling was implemented to fabricate metamaterial structures from soft poly-lactic acid. 3D printed metamaterials were tested under in-plane tension-compression in axial and transverse directions. Experiments revealed that unit-cell shape, direction, type and magnitude of mechanical loading have signiﬁcant eﬀects on metamaterial anisotropic response and its instability characteristics. In addition, a simple and robust constitutive model was proposed to simulate mechanical behaviors of hyper-elastic materials under bi-axial normal-shear loadings in the finite strain regime. The Mooney-Rivlin strain energy function was adopted to develop a two-dimensional (2D) normal-shear constitutive model within the framework of continuum mechanics. A motion field was first proposed for combined normal and shear deformations. The deformation gradient of the proposed field was calculated and then substituted into right Cauchy-Green deformation tensor. Constitutive equations were then derived for normal and shear deformations. Fused deposition modelling technique as a 3D printing technology was implemented to fabricate hyper-elastic beam structures from soft poly-lactic acid filaments. The printed specimens were tested under tensile/compressive in-plane and compressive out-of-plane forces. A finite element formulation along with the Newton-Raphson and Riks techniques was also developed to trace non-linear equilibrium path of beam structures in large defamation regimes. It was shown that the model is capable of predicting non-linear equilibrium characteristics of hyper-elastic straight and curved beams. Fused decomposition modeling (FDM) as a 3D printing technology has been shown how we can engineer adaptive metamaterials with performance-driven functionality built directly into materials. The tactic was based on an understanding of thermo-mechanics of SMP and fabrication concept behind FDM as well as experiments to explore how FDM can program self-foldable metamaterials. A 4D printing method to program SMPs during fabrication process has been introduced. FDM as a ﬁlament based printing method was employed to program SMPs during depositing the material. This method has been implemented to fabricate complicated polymeric structures by self-bending features without need of any post-programming. Experiments were conducted to demonstrate feasibility of one-dimensional (1D)-to 2D and 2D-to-3D self-bending. We also introduced triple SMPs by 4D printing to shape adaptive structures for mechanical/bio-medical devices. The main approach was based on arranging hot–cold programming of SMPs with FDM technology to engineer adaptive structures with triple shape memory effect. Experiments were conducted to characterize elasto-plastic and hyper-elastic thermo-mechanical material properties of SMPs in low and high temperatures at large deformation regime. A phenomenological 3D constitutive model was developed for quantitative understanding of dual/triple SME of SMPs fabricated by 4D printing in the large deformation range. Governing equations of equilibrium were established for adaptive structures on the basis of the nonlinear Green–Lagrange strains. They were then solved by developing a finite element approach along with an elastic-predictor plastic-corrector return map procedure accomplished by the Newton–Raphson method. The computational tool can be applied to simulate dual/triple SMP structures enabled by 4D printing and explore hot–cold programming mechanisms behind material tailoring. It is shown that the 4D printed dual/triple SMPs have great potential in mechanical/bio-medical applications such as self-bending gripers/stents and self-shrinking/tightening staples.

14202016.value: Significant results (12 journal papers and 2 conference papers) have been obtained from this completed project. A journal paper received the Best Paper Award by American Society of Mechanical Engineers. The PI (Prof. WH Liao) also delivered a plenary talk about this research at 2019 SPIE Smart Structures/NDE, Denver, USA, on 6 March 2019. For the further development, multi-scale multi-material additive manufacturing for advanced mechatronic devices/systems should be conducted. This will add a new chapter to world-wide scientific efforts in research and development of smart materials, adaptive structures and intelligent systems.

14202016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202016.value: Imagine a world constructed of programmable matters and reconfigurable elements. The world would require to be conjoined with sensing, actuating and various human-inspired capabilities. Recent advances in additive manufacturing created four-dimensional (4D) printing technology for creating dynamic devices that can change their shape and/or function on-demand and over time. This technique provides an effective means from idea to reality with performance-driven functionality built into structures. In this project, we advanced the 4D printing technology and employed it to design, fabrication and test of self-unfolding/unfolding structures/devices that assemble from flat sheets and then deploy on-demand automatically. Shape memory polymers (SMPs) were considered for transformation mechanisms. Based on a rigorous understanding of the complex thermo-mechanics of the SMP structures, the printed material properties and folding/unfolding motions were investigated. The developed equipment and computational tools can be employed to digitally design and fabricate adaptive structures that transform into a predetermined shape, changing property and function after fabrication and then recover their original shape. This project has advanced the state-of-the-art of 4D printing, and provided pertinent formulations and results that significantly contribute to a comprehensive understanding of thermo-mechanical behaviors of self-folding/unfolding structures and to be instrumental toward reliable fabrication and designs of adaptive structures.

14203416.value: 製作聯鎖結構的計算：穩定性及穩健性的優化

14203416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203416.value: Interlocking is an intriguing condition about a 3D assembly structure, where the component parts tightly interlock with one another and immobilize one another, thus preventing the assembly structure from falling apart. This idea has been employed and practised in long-standing wooden architectural structures in China and Japan for connecting together columns and frames, as well as in challenging puzzle games such as the burr puzzle. Built upon the preliminary works done by the PI on interlocking computation, we aim to innovate in this project advanced computational methods to enhance and optimize the stability and steadiness of the 3D interlocking structures produced by our methods. Our ultimate goal is to generate interlocking assembly structures that are practically ready for physical construction. To achieve this goal, we will approach the problem with the following four research tasks: i) Iteratively analyze-and-optimize the structural steadiness and stability of the interlocking assembly according to the component connectivity and fabrication tolerance; ii) Optimize the joint geometry and assembly order of the component parts against various physical constraints, e.g., stability, construction procedure, etc.; iii) Develop non-orthogonal component connections to strengthen the interlocking; and iv) Explore applications for 3D printing and large-scale notched reciprocal frame structures. To summarize, we aim to innovate in this project novel computational methods to overcome assorted practical issues concerning 3D fabrication and the assembly construction process, as well as to produce stable and steady interlocking assembly structures that are practically ready for physical construction. In the end of this project, we target to develop and evaluate our results with 3D printing as well as with a potential industrial collaborator in Hong Kong. 聯鎖結構是一個非常有趣的三維組裝。在這三維組裝中，其部件相互緊密的連鎖、牽制並固定，從而防止組裝結構的瓦解。在中國和日本一些古老的木材建築中，這種組裝結構已被運用來連接建築中的支撐柱和骨架。除此之外，在一些富挑戰性的益智遊戲如魯班鎖，也應用了這種組裝結構。 基於之前首席研究員(PI)在聯鎖結構計算的初步工作，這項目的目標是創新出更先進的可計算方法去提升和優化三維聯鎖組裝的穩定性和穩健性。最終目的是產生一些幾乎可以直接應用在實際建設中的聯鎖結構。 為了實現這目標，我們將問題細化為如下的研究任務： 1. 根據組成部件的連接及製造間隔，反複分析及優化聯鎖結構的穩定性和穩健性 2. 考慮在物理約束下，如組合穩定性及建造流程，對部件連接部分的幾何結構和部件組裝順序進行優化 3. 開發一些非垂直連接的結構以加固聯鎖 4. 探索有關於三維打印技術和大規模自支撐架構的應用 總而言之，在這個項目中我們的目的是創造新的可計算的方法去解決有關於三維打印製造和裝配過程中的各種實際問題，同時生成穩定且穩健並幾乎可以直接應用在實際建造的聯鎖結構。在最後，我們會意圖應用三維打印技術並聯繫一些潛在的香港工業商，去印製及評估我們的研究結果。

14203416.label: Realisation of objectives
14203416.value: This project aims to facilitate the design and construction of 3D fabrication with interlocking assemblies. In short, we have developed various computational methods to facilitate the geometric construction of various 3D assembly forms and studied various methods for geometry analysis and computation. First, to construct 3D fabrication not only requires the computation of the 3D geometries but also needs to respect various 3D fabrication constraints related to the machine for fabrication, the assembly procedure, and fabrication efficiency. We conduct research for computing 3D assemblies and develop several methods for constructing multiple 3D object fabrication modalities. Here, we have to consider the 3D geometric constructions and also the associated fabrication constraints. (a) We designed a novel framework to support the construction of interlocking furniture assemblies that are reconfigurable, for which our method constructs a common set of parts that can be assembled into different forms for use in different situations; to achieve the 3D construction, we design a compatible decomposition of shapes with correspondence across forms and a planning process for well-matched joints to connect parts in each form; (b) We developed a computational design system to aid the design of wind-up toys, focusing on constructing a compact internal wind-up mechanism to realize user-requested part motions. Our key contributions include analytical modeling of a wide variety of elemental mechanisms found in common wind-up toys, including their geometry and kinematics, a conceptual design of wind-up mechanisms by computing motion transfer trees to realize the requested part motions, an automatic construction method of wind-up mechanisms by connecting multiple elemental mechanisms, and an optimization model on the part and joint geometry with an objective of compacting the mechanism, reducing its weight, and avoiding collision; (c) We designed a fully automatic method that finds a small number of machine-fabricable wires with minimal overlap to reproduce a wire sculpture design as a 3D shape abstraction; these non-planar wires can be fabricated by a wire bending machine, to enable efficient construction of complex 3D sculptures; (d) We developed a new computational solution for cost-efficient 3D fabrication using universal building blocks that are interlocking. These universal blocks can be massively prefabricated at a low cost, so we can quickly assemble and constitute a significant internal core of the target 3D object to be fabricated and 3D-print only the residual volume online. Further, we can improve the fabrication efficiency by decomposing the residual volume into a small number of printing-friendly pyramidal pieces. (e) Further, we extended the previously-developed methods in (a) to computationally design steady 3D dissection puzzles, in which we take two voxelized shapes as inputs and dissect them into a common set of parts, during which we allow slightly modification of the input shapes, preferably on their internal volumes, to preserve the external appearance. Particularly, we formulate a formal model of generalized interlocking for connecting pieces into a steady assembly using both their geometric arrangements and friction. (f) Lastly, we introduced a method to automatically compute LEGO Technic models from user input sketches, optionally with motion annotations, in which the generated models resemble the input sketches with coherently-connected bricks and simple layouts, while respecting the intended symmetry and mechanical properties expressed in the inputs. Our method is able to address the immense search space in this complex computational assembly problem and considers a rich brick set and connection mechanisms. Second, geometry analysis and computation are other key issues in this project to improve geometry construction. (a) We formulated a nonlocal low-rank normal filtering method for denoising 3D meshes, in which we explored the geometric similarity between local surface patches on 3D meshes in the form of normal fields and devised a low-rank recovery model that filters normal vectors by means of patch groups. First, our formulated guided normal patch covariance descriptor analyzes the similarity between patches. Second, we pack normal vectors on similar patches into the normal-field patch-group (NPG) matrix for rank analysis. Third, we formulate mesh denoising as a low-rank matrix recovery problem based on the prior that the rank of the NPG matrix is high for raw meshes with noise, but can be significantly reduced for denoised meshes, whose normal vectors across similar patches should be more strongly correlated. (b) We designed a new point cloud upsampling network, which is formulated based on a generative adversarial network (GAN), to learn a rich variety of point distributions from the latent space and upsample points over patches on object surfaces. To realize a working GAN network, we constructed an up-down-up expansion unit in the generator for upsampling point features with error feedback and self-correction and formulated a self-attention unit to enhance the feature integration. (c) We developed an encoder-decoder branch for predicting labels on 3D points by constructing an edge branch to hierarchically integrate point features and generate edge features. To incorporate point features in the edge branch, we establish a hierarchical graph framework, where the graph is initialized from a coarse layer and gradually enriched along the point decoding process. For each edge in the final graph, we predict a label to indicate the semantic consistency of the two connected points to enhance point prediction. At different layers, edge features are also fed into the corresponding point module to integrate contextual information for message passing enhancement in local regions. The two branches interact with each other and cooperate in segmentation.

14203416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203416.value: In summary, 7 journal papers and 9 conference papers relevant to this project have been generated, including five papers in ACM Transactions on Graphics (TOG) and two papers in Computer Graphics Forum (CGF). Note that these journals are related to top-tier conferences SIGGRAPH & SIGGRAPH Asia, and Eurographics, which publish accepted papers in TOG and CGF, respectively. First, we summarize major findings in 3D fabrication: - [J01]/[C01] proposes a novel framework to support the construction of interlocking furniture assemblies that are reconfigurable, i.e., a common set of parts can be assembled into different forms for use in different situations. - [J02]/[C02] developed analytical modeling of various elemental mechanisms in wind-up toys, an automatic construction method by connecting elemental mechanisms, and an optimization on part and joint geometry. - [J03]/[C03] presents a fully automatic method that can find a small number of machine-fabricable wires with minimal overlap to reproduce a wire sculpture design as a 3D shape abstraction. - [J04]/[C04] proposes a cost-efficient 3D fabrication approach using universal building blocks to assemble and constitute a significant internal core of the target 3D object to be fabricated, such that we only need to 3D-print the residual volume online. - [J06]/[C06] extends [J01]/[C01] to computationally design steady 3D dissection puzzles (which are interlocking), such that we can dissect two given voxelized shapes into a common set of parts, while allowing for slight modification of the input shapes to preserve the external appearance. - [J07]/[C09] introduces an automatic method to compute and design LEGO Technic models from user input sketches, optionally with motion annotations; the generated models not only resemble the input sketches with coherently-connected bricks and simple layouts, but also respect the intended symmetry and mechanical properties expressed in the inputs. Second, we summarize major findings in geometry analysis and computation: - [J05]/[C05] presents a nonlocal low-rank normal filtering model for 3D mesh denoising by exploring the geometric similarity between local surface patches on 3D meshes in the form of normal fields and devising a low-rank recovery model to filter normal vectors. - [C07] presents a new point cloud upsampling network, which is formulated based on a generative adversarial network to learn a rich variety of point distributions from the latent space and upsample points over patches on object surfaces. - [C08] presents an edge branch to predicting labels on 3D points by hierarchically integrating point features and generating edge features and enabling the feature interactions between the edge branch and point branch.

14203416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203416.value: In our future work, we shall develop a development platform that contains the designed algorithms, seek more collaborations, and transfer the algorithms for real applications. Our proposed course of actions includes the followings: - Collaborate with industries and architects to transfer the developed algorithms for real applications. - Apply research grants to further our research in computational design and 3D fabrication. - Integrate our technologies into an interactive environment for further adaptation.

14203416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203416.value: In this project, we developed various novel computational methods related to the design and construction of 3D fabrications. This includes a family of techniques, in which (i) we compute and construct a common set of component parts in reconfigurable interlocking assemblies, such that the part set can be assembled into different target forms for use in different situations; (ii) we formulated a cost-efficient method to fabricate 3D objects with universal building blocks, such that we can use the blocks to assemble and constitute a significant internal core of the target 3D object to be fabricated and need to 3D-print only the residual shell volume online; (iii) we designed a method to automatically find a small number of machine-fabricable wires with minimal overlap for fabricating wire sculpture designs as 3D shape abstractions; (iv) we developed an automatic method to compute and design LEGO Technic models from user input sketches, optionally with motion annotations; the generated models not only resemble the input sketches with coherently-connected bricks and simple layouts, but also respect the intended symmetry and mechanical properties expressed in the inputs; etc. On the other hand, we also developed novel methods on processing 3D meshes and point clouds.

14203616.label: Project Objectives
14203616.value: Application of network coded interference alignment in different systems We believe that network coded interference alignment can be applied to many systems with multiple simultaneous transmissions. Indeed, whenever interference alignment is applied, part of the aligned interference may be useful as network coded information to facilitate subsequent decoding and demodulation. Hence, we anticipate network coded interference alignment can be applied to many different systems. We would start with a few systems that are extensions of our preliminary work, and proceed to more general systems. Optimization of network coded interference alignment We would try to optimize different parts of the network coded interference alignment system, including the transmit beamformers and the receive beamformers. For a given system, there are usually multiple ways to perform network coding and interference alignment, which may give the same degrees of freedom, but potentially different signal-to-noise ratio performance. The suitable choice among these options would also be investigated. Network coded interference alignment with different modulations and error control codes Our preliminary study focused on binary data with simple antipodal signaling. Just like other physical-layer network coding schemes, non-binary data and high order modulations can be considered. In addition, error control coding would also be applied in most systems. Based on the literature, we would also expect significant challenges in dealing with the optimal decoding and demodulation of the data. Network coded interference alignment with imperfections In reality, we would need to deal with various imperfections. While imperfections in interference alignment and imperfections in network coding have been studied, in our case, we would need to tackle problems in both interference alignment and network coding together. For example, inaccurate channel parameters would lead to interference leakage as well as inexact network coding operations.

14203616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203616.value: Interference has always been one of the biggest problems in wireless communications. Recent results show that interference alignment could be the way to tackle interference in the wireless channel. The basic idea of interference alignment is to align interference observed by a receiver within a subspace while leaving another subspace for useful signals. Multiple users can transmit at the same frequency at the same time because of the differences of the wireless channels observed by different receivers. With a large number of simultaneously transmitting and receiving users, the data rate supported by the network can be tremendously improved. In most cases, the aligned interference would simply be discarded. However, we observe that the aligned interference, in some situations, can produce useful network coded information. Instead of simply discarding the aligned interference, we would like to extract the relevant network coded information to improve the performance of the wireless network. Our preliminary studies show that such an approach can have great potentials. In this project, we would like to perform a thorough investigation of network coded interference alignment. We would investigate different situations to use the network coded information in interference alignment systems. We expect our results would greatly enhance the application of interference alignment in wireless networks. 信號干擾是無線通訊需面對的重要問題之一。在近期的研究指出，干擾對齊能夠有效處理無線通訊的干擾信號。干擾對齊的主要概念是將干擾重疊在接收端的同一個信號空間，而期望信號則放在另一個信號空間。隨着同時傳輸的無線通訊設備增加，干擾對齊對數據速率提升有顯著的效果。 在大部分的情況下，這些已對齊的干擾信號都會被丟棄。可是，我們團隊發現它們在某些情況下能夠轉化為有價值的網絡編碼。與其丟棄已對齊的干擾信號，我們嘗試利用由它們轉化的網絡編碼去提升無線網絡的效能，初步研究發現這方向有非常大的潛力。 在這個項目，我們將會對網絡編碼干擾對齊進行全面的研究。我們會探索在不同情況下如何有效利用從干擾對齊獲得的網絡編碼，期望研究結果能夠有效加強干擾對齊在無線通訊的應用。

14203616.label: Realisation of objectives
14203616.value: The first objective is to apply network coded interference alignment in different systems. During our investigation, we have looked into many different systems, including multiuser relay networks [1], multicell multiple-input-single-output (MISO) systems [2], multicell (multiple-input-single-output) MIMO systems [3], the general MIMO X-channel [4], the cloud radio access networks (C-RANs) [5], the interference channel with limited feedback [6,7], and many more. Our investigation into these different systems is evident from our related publications. The second objective is to optimize different parts of the related systems. In every case, we try to optimize, if available, the coding strategies, the precoders, the transmit beamformers, the base station association, the power allocation, the relay processing matrices, the alignment strategies, the receiver beamformers, etc. For example, in [1], we try to optimize various parts of our system in order to achieve Pareto optimality. In [4], we provide an iterative algorithm to optimize the alignment of signals in the general MIMO X-channel. Indeed, in every publication, we have strive to optimize the various parts of our systems. The third objective is to look into different modulations and error control coding. We have investigated the pros and cons of different modulations and error control coding in our systems. Most of our proposed algorithms and systems can work with different modulations and error control coding. For example, in [7], instead of working with simple binary modulation, we have explicitly demonstrated that our system can work with, and benefit from, coded messages from the finite field GF(q). The last objective is to consider imperfections. In reality, we would need to deal with various imperfections in our systems, e.g., imperfect channel estimates. In our project, we have tested different cases of imperfections, especially in the simulations, in order to make sure that our proposed algorithms would work as expected, even with various imperfections. We believe that the original objectives have been fully achieved. [1] R. Hu and T. M. 14203616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203616.value: The project has resulted in seven international journal and conference papers, including five IEEE Transactions full papers. Four Ph.D. students are involved during the whole project. All of them have graduated with their Ph.D. degrees. In [4], we investigated interference alignment over finite signaling dimensions for a general multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) X-channel. The main challenge of the MIMO X-channel is that the two sets of conditions for interference alignment, namely the interference nulling conditions and the rank preservation conditions, get coupled. The usual interference alignment methods for the interference channel and the broadcasting channel cannot be applied anymore. We show that the rank preservation conditions can be replaced by a group of specific rank conditions. Then, based on our results, an iterative algorithm of interference alignment is designed for the MIMO X-channel with limited signaling dimensions. Simulation results show that our algorithm has good performances even under limited signal-to-noise ratio. In [5], we design an interference mitigation scheme, named signal-aligned network coding (SNC), for both uplink and downlink cloud radio access networks (C-RANs). The base stations are connected to a central processor via digital links with individual limited capacities. The users communicate with the central processor through the base stations. We focus on the situation that the digital links have moderate rate constraint so that the capacities of the digital links and the wireless links are of the same order of magnitude. Based on the concepts from interference alignment, we design a highly related signal alignment scheme to strategically aligns the signals. Then we decodes the aligned signals by physical-layer network coding (PNC). With proper designs of the transmitted network-coded messages and the alignment of signals, our SNC scheme significantly mitigates the inter-cell interference. No matter the size of the network, the SNC scheme achieves full degrees of freedom (DoF) asymptotically. For the finite signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) performances, simulation results show that our SNC scheme achieves superior sum-rate than the conventional compute-and-forward scheme in the two-user and the three-user cases, especially in the high SNR regime. These are just some examples of the results that we have obtained in our project. Due to word limits, we are unable to discuss most of our results. Please refer to our journal papers and conference papers in Part C.

14203616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203616.value: There are a few interesting directions for further research. For example, our signal-aligned network coding (SNC) scheme may be applicable to multi-user broadcast channels with simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). Unlike conventional interference mitigation schemes, our scheme does not minimize the interfering signals at the receivers. Our scheme cancels out the undesired messages over a finite field in the code domain. It preserves the interfering signals which can be beneficial energy sources for energy harvesting. This idea can be achieved by strategically designing the network-coded messages conveyed so that the interfering messages cancel with each other during demodulation. We expect such a scheme can achieve superior energy harvesting performance than the conventional interference mitigation schemes. More recently. we are also investigating into Internet of Things (IoT) networks. We find that our SNC scheme may also be applicable to IoT networks to enhance the Age of Information (AoI) performance. We are performing preliminary investigations into these directions. If the preliminary results are promising, we may apply for grants to support a relevant project.

14203616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203616.value: Recent results show that interference alignment could be the way to tackle interference in the wireless channel. The basic idea of interference alignment is to align interference observed by a receiver within a certain dimension while leaving another dimension for useful signals. In typical cases, the aligned interference would simply be discarded. However, we observe that the aligned interference, through careful design, can produce useful network coded information. Instead of simply discarding the aligned interference, we can extract the relevant network coded information to improve the performance of the wireless systems. In this project, we have performed a thorough investigation into network coded interference alignment. We have investigated many different communication systems, including multiuser relay networks, multicell multiple-input-single-output (MISO) systems, multicell (multiple-input-single-output) MIMO systems, the general MIMO X-channel, the cloud radio access networks (C-RANs), the interference channel with limited feedback, and many more. We have applied interference alignment and / or network coding implicitly or explicitly in our investigated systems. We have formulated different optimization problems in different scenarios in order to optimize various parts of our systems. We have also designed different practical algorithms so that our results can be readily implemented.

14204616.label: Project Objectives
14204616.value: To develop a synthetic methodology to produce perovskite polycrystalline thin films and single crystals. This objective comprises of: (i) to study the coordination, nucleation, transition state in the perovskite formation, degradation and recovery processes of hybrid perovskite and identifying important synthetic factors and conditions towards producing high-quality perovskite. (ii) to obtain highly crystalline, stable and size-controllable perovskite thin films as a light absorber for perovskite soar cells. (iii) to deliver high-performance and highly-stable PSCs. To establish a synthetic strategy as well as an optimized transfer process for conducting/semiconducting 2D layered materials, including graphene, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). To explore novel hybrid optoelectronic devices based on perovskites and 2D materials, both separately and in tandem. These include: (i) high performance photodetectors to be produced with graphene/TMD 2D materials and perovskite; (ii) efficient light emitting devices to be fabricated by utilizing the perovskite material in combination with MoS2, etc.; (iii) structural, optical, electrical and photoelectric properties to be evaluated in the optimization processes.

14204616.label: Realisation of objectives
14204616.value: Objective # 1. In this part, we interrogated various synthetic methods of perovskite thin films, including both directly spin-coating and sequential deposition, as well as single crystal preparation. We attained a much insightful understanding on the coordination, nucleation, and transition states in the perovskite formation. In one step directly spin-coating method, the coordination intermediate state is important for the crystallographic transformation from trigonal PbI2 to tetragonal perovskites. In perovskite precursors, the intermediate compounds exist as colloids and the coordination of central lead ion is vital to the film morphology and crystallinity. More can be found by Yan, et al., in JACS, 137 (13), 4460–4468 (2015) In sequential deposition process, the reaction of PbI2 and MAI undergoes an interfacial reaction of, then followed by a fine dissolution and re-deposition Ostwald ripening process. The interfacial reaction is fast and would leave many defects. Then during Ostwald ripening, the defects would be annihilated. More details can be found in Zhang, et al., Appl. Materials & Interfaces 8, 32366−32375 (2016) After having learned the coordination and nucleation mechanism, we developed several facile deposition methods to obtain highly crystalline, stable and size controllable perovskite thin films. First, the nonstoichiometric acid–base reaction (NABR) method, route optimization involves the reaction of PbI2 with excess HI to generate HPbI3, which subsequently undergoes reaction with excess CH3NH2 to deliver CH3NH3PbI3 thin films. High quality of intermediate HPbI3 and CH3NH2 abundance are two important factors to stabilize CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite. Excess volatile acid/base not only affords full conversion in nonstoichiometric acid–base reaction route but also permits its facile removal for stoichiometric purification. The most impressive result that NABR route provide is the synthetized perovskite thin film can sustain its high quality even after 2 months stored in 65% humidity. More details can be found by Long, et al., Nature Communications 7, 13503 (2016) On the basis of sequential deposition, we also developed a dual ion exchange (DIE) method to fabricate high quality mixed cation and mixed halide perovskite. The mixed perovskite (FAPbI3)1−x(MAPbBr3)x, prepared by directly mixing (DM) with different perovskite components, suffered from phase competition and a low-crystallinity characteristic, resulting in instability, despite the high efficiency. It was found that the threshold electrical field to initiate ion migration was greatly increased in DIE perovskite thin film because excess MABr on the surface can effectively heal structural defects located on grain boundaries during the ion exchange process. More can be found by #1 in Part C. Afterwards, we further optimized the NABR route, substituting the MA solution with MA gas and developed the gas-solid reaction, to build interpenetrating perovskite polycrystalline networks with less defects by utilizing cross crystal-linking to enhance the inter-crystal connectivity and thus facilitate charge transport and separation. A high crystalline perovskite MAPbI3 with texture structure prepared from HPbI3 reacted with low partial pressure (LPP) MA gas was synthesized using the home-built apparatus. More can be found by Long, et al., Nano Energy 33, 485-96 (2017). Objective #2 Transfer of large-scale 2D atomic layers onto desired targets is crucial for the integration toward practical applications. Conventional wet etching transfer of 2D materials grown on insulating substrates suffers from the degraded film quality caused by the prolonged exposure of radical chemicals. To establish a synthetic strategy as well as an optimized transfer process for conducting/semiconducting 2D layered materials, by adopting the water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol as a viscoelastic mediator and polymethyl-methacrylate as a protecting layer, we developed a green and robust transfer technique. This method is of high degree of freedom, which can realize both selective peel-off and aligned release. The transferred materials maintain their pristine qualities, promising a universal applicability for a diverse range of 2D materials and growth/target substrates, facilitating facile fabrication of 2D electronic devices with improved performance. See more in #3, Part C. Meanwhile a new growth method for 2D materials of telluride alloys was developed. See more in #14, Part C. Objective #3 Based on the high-quality perovskites and 2D materials, a few high performance photodetectors were prepared and interrogated. For example, two dimensional (2D) perovskite structure was investigated due to its improved stability for photovoltaic and light emitting devices. The introduction of spacer ligand would not produce pure 2D phase perovskite but yield multiple quantum well structure with 2D phases from n=1 to n=infinite (also called quasi-2D phase). Therefore, tailoring the phase and orientation of quasi-2D phases to boost efficiency has become the central topic of the 2D perovskite research. Our activities included on the following three aspects: Firstly, we systematically studied the energy transfer of excitons between the multiple 2D phases by time-resolved photoluminescence. Multiple component quasi-2D perovskite has shown excellent luminescent properties than its 3D counterparts. However, the lack of radiative recombination at room temperature was still not well understood. Our results found that the charge transfer process from high-energy 2D states to low-energy 2D states is gradually suppressed at elevated temperature owing to trap-mediated recombination. This may provide the bottleneck of efficient luminescence at room temperature in 2D perovskite, leading to large photovoltage loss in 2D perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Therefore, we proposed a novel bulk heterojunction (BHJ) structure to minimize the nonradiative recombination pathways. Secondly, we investigated the energy transfer between slices in layered perovskite using short ligand 1,4-butanediamine (BDA) and long-chain ligand n-butylamine (BA). Energy transfer behavior is significant in 2D perovskite materials, but how the energy transfer processes behave differently with varying insulating barrier width is still little known. We reported on a uniform distribution and exciton-coupling-induced efficient energy transfer in short ligand BDA samples, distinguished from graded composition and poor energy transfer in long ligand BA samples. The uniform distribution and strong exciton coupling effect together mitigated nonradiative recombination pathways and improves the open-circuit voltage to 1.15 V. Thirdly, we interrogated the property difference of D-J type perovskite based two isomers, i.e., trans-1,4-cyclohexanediamine (CHDA) and 1,6-diaminohexane (HDA). But how the structure of space impacts the perovskite crystallinity, orientation, phase distribution, and further structure stability is not fully reported. We reported on preferred orientation and improved crystallinity during annealing process in the CHDA samples, whereas the HDA sample showed severe phase competition with much poorer crystallinity. We further found a slantwise alignment structure in the CHDA sample, which differed from graded aligned perovskite composition commonly shown in the HDA sample. CHDA devices also provided better moisture stability, heat stability, and photostability than those of the HDA controlled devices, demonstrating excellent phase stability. Besides several high quality light emitting devices and 2D photodetector and graphene modulator were developed. More details can be found in #12 - #13, #15-#16, Part C. Trails for LED composed of perovskite and MoS2 were attempted without appreciable success. Nor were heterostructures consisting of 2D layered material and perovskite single crystal. More efforts are needed to further study the heterostructures.

14204616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204616.value: We have developed several synthetic ways to produce high quality organometal perovskite thin films via interface engineering and 2D/3D heterostructure for high-quality photovoltaic and light emitting devices. We have systematically investigated optoelectronic properties of the films and devices via various characterization techniques. (See more in #1, #6-13, Part C.) We have devised a graded band structure for efficient charge separation, and the conductivity of the 2D perovskite can be tuned by extrinsic FA incorporation, which provides effective conducting channels for holes, making the modified 2D perovskite layer a promising and stable HTL. Optimized solar cells based on 3D-2D PPPH showed a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 13.15% initially and 16.13% after thermal aging, and could maintain 71% output for 50 days under 65% humidity, and 74% for 30 days under 85 degrees C, without encapsulation. This work points to realize low cost and ambient compatible PPPH solar cells with high PCE and robust stability. By adopting the water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol as a viscoelastic mediator and polymethyl-methacrylate as a protecting layer, we developed a green and robust transfer technique for various grown 2D materials. This method is of high degree of freedom, which can realize both selective peel-off and aligned release. The transferred materials maintain their pristine qualities, as probed by various spectroscopic/microscopic characterizations. This technique promises a universal applicability for a diverse range of 2D materials and growth/target substrates, facilitating facile fabrication of 2D electronic devices with improved performance. Furthermore, by performing restacking steps, van der Waals heterostructures can be built. We realized a perovskite LED with a greatly improved stability. We introduced an alkyldiammonium 1,4-butanediamine (BDA) to be incorporated into perovskite emitting layer, which substantially optimized electrochemical stability and minimized interfacial deep traps under large external bias. The BDA-PeLED showed a record operational half-lifetime T-50 of 189.4 h at a high current density of 100 mA cm(-2) and 681 h under 50 mA cm(-2). Additionally, the device maintained its original performance upon 2500 cycles of voltage scan and withstands 10 000 times of ON-OFF under a pulsed voltage of 2.5 V. The degradation mechanism study revealed that the main origins of the instability property of PeLEDs without BDA were the generation of deep traps at the interfaces and the infiltration of anions into adjacent layers under long-term electric stress. Meanwhile high-quality photodetector and modulator composed of 2D and graphene were developed.

14205816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205816.value: Many financial asset prices experience large sudden movements in short time periods, as evidenced by observations from the latest global financial crisis and the stock market turmoil in Mainland China and Hong Kong in the summer of 2015. Jump processes are an essential tool to model such phenomena for option pricing and risk management in financial engineering. Popular financial models with jumps are often based on Levy processes, whose jumps are independent of the state. This can be quite unrealistic in some applications. The present proposal aims to study a large class of one-dimensional jump processes, known as subordinate diffusions, whose jumps are dependent on the state in general and hence have richer and more realistic behavior than the jumps of Levy processes. Subordinate diffusions are obtained by time changing a diffusion process with an independent Levy or additive random clock. The time change technique makes the diffusion process with continuous sample paths run on a randomly evolving clock with jumps in time, allowing jumps to be created in the subordinate diffusion. In fact, many popular Levy processes can be represented as a Brownian motion time changed with an independent Levy random clock. Thus one can view subordinate diffusions as a natural generalization of many Levy processes by time changing more general diffusions. A series of recent papers have already established the usefulness of subordinate diffusions for financial applications, but they only consider specifications that are analytically tractable for option pricing, which may fail to capture some important features. Fast and accurate numerical methods for option pricing that are applicable to general subordinate diffusion models are valuable in practice as they allow more realistic specifications to be used in a computationally efficient way for pricing. However, such methods are still lacking. Besides, the fundamental and practically important problems of hedging in subordinate diffusion models and their statistical inference have not been considered in the literature. This project aims to fill these gaps by developing (1) fast and accurate numerical methods for option pricing applicable to general subordinate diffusion models, (2) effective hedging strategies with consideration of transaction cost for a variety of option contracts in these models, as well as (3) computationally efficient inference methods with good accuracy to estimate these models from data. We will apply the developed methods to various financial applications and we expect impact to be found in financial engineering practice, research and education. 很多金融資產的價格都可能在短期内發生大的變化，正如人們在最近一次全球金融危機以及2015年夏天中國内地和香港股市的混亂中觀察到那樣。 跳躍過程是金融工程中用來刻畫這種現象用於期權定價和風險管理的基本工具。常用的帶跳躍的金融模型通常都是基於列維過程。這類過程的跳躍是獨立于當前狀態的。在一些應用中這可能不太現實。 本提案的目的是研究一大類稱爲次級擴散過程的一維跳躍過程。這類過程的跳躍一般取決于當前狀態，因此他們比列維過程擁有更豐富更真實的跳躍行爲。次級擴散過程是對擴散過程做隨機時間變換得到的。所用的隨機時間可以是一個列維或者可加的時間過程。隨機時間變換讓具有連續軌道的擴散過程在帶跳躍的隨機時間尺度上發展，這樣時間變換后得到的過程帶有跳躍。事實上，很多常用的列維過程可以對布朗運動做隨機時間變換得到，因此次級擴散過程可以看作是很多列維過程的推廣。最近一系列的研究證實了次級擴散過程在金融中的作用，但是它們只考慮了能夠得到期權定價解析解的情況。這些解析的模型可能不能夠刻畫市場中一些重要的特徵。對於一般次級擴散過程適用的又快又準的數值計算方法在實踐中有很大用處，因爲它能夠讓我們采用更加真實的模型又快又準的定價，但是這種方法還不存在。另外，對於次級擴散過程模型，基本且在現實中很重要的對衝以及統計估計問題在文獻中也還沒有考慮。 本項目將填補研究中的這些空缺。我們會開發（1）對於一般次級擴散過程適用的又快又準的數值計算方法， （2）在這類模型中對於各類期權考慮交易費用之後有效的對衝策略， 以及（3） 統計精度高且計算效率高的推斷方法把這類模型從實際數據中估計出來。我們將把開發出來的方法用到各類金融應用中。我們預期本項目的研究成果將會對金融工程的實踐，研究和教育產生影響。

14205816.label: Realisation of objectives
14205816.value: All four objectives have been fully achieved. For Objective 1, we have developed an efficient numerical method for pricing European, Bermudan and barrier options for general one-dimensional subordinate diffusions. The method is based on finite difference approximation and matrix eigendecomposition. The convergence of the method is proved and sharp estimates of the convergence rate for different payoff functions are obtained. We also show how to design the grid to achieve fast convergence. For Objective 2, we have developed an effective strategy for hedging options in subordinate diffusion models in a quadratic hedging framework based on the option pricing algorithm developed for Objective 1. For Objective 3, we have developed a method based on the theory of estimating functions and the algorithm we developed for Objective 1. The method is both statistically and computationally efficient and it can be applied to general one-dimensional subordinate diffusions. For Objective 4, we have applied our methods to applications including testing our option pricing method in various subordinate diffusion models for modeling different assets, hedging VIX options and estimating subordinate diffusion models from the VIX data and crude oil data.

14205816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205816.value: 1. We developed a computationally efficient method for pricing European options in one-dimensional subordinate diffusion models based on finite difference approximation of the diffusion generator and matrix eigendecomposition. These results were published in the paper "Option pricing in some non-Levy jump models" (SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 38(4), 2016). The paper was based on results declared in the grant proposal and it is not included as an output of the project because it was accepted before the project started. 2. The method was then extended to price barrier and Bermudan options in subordinate diffusion models. We tested our method on various models to establish its computational efficiency and accuracy. Comparison was also made with standard numerical methods to demonstrate the advantages of our method. The results are included in the PhD dissertation of my student ZHANG Gongqiu. 3. We proved the convergence of our method and obtained sharp estimates of its convergence rate for different types of payoff functions. We first obtained results in the uniform grid case, which were published Paper 2 in Part C. (The paper was submitted before the project start date. However, a major revision was done after the project started to make the paper acceptable by the journal.) We then generalized the analysis for general grids and proposed a class of grids to achieve fast convergence. The results were published in Paper 4 in Part C. These results were published together with some results from another RGC project in these two papers. 4. We developed an effective strategy for hedging options in subordinate diffusion models in a quadratic hedging framework based on the option pricing algorithm we developed. The strategy was used for hedging VIX options and it performed well. The results were published in Paper 1 in Part C together with results from an earlier RGC project. (The paper was submitted before the project start date. However, a major revision was done after the project started to make the paper acceptable by the journal.) 5. To estimate the parameters of subordinate diffusions, we developed a statistically and computationally efficient method based on the theory of estimating functions and the algorithm we developed for computing expectations of subordinate diffusions. We applied it to estimate subordinate diffusion models of VIX and crude oil prices and showed that our models could provide a better fit to data than some traditional models. The results were published in Paper 3 in Part C and were also included in the PhD dissertation of my student GUO Weiwei.

14205816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205816.value: 1. As many asset prices jump, subordinate diffusions are potentially useful for fitting the data of many assets. We can apply the estimation method we developed to these problems. 2. The project is focused on one-dimensional subordinate diffusion models. It is possible to extend our method to price multi-asset options in multivariate subordinate diffusion models.

14205816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205816.value: Jumps are often observed in financial markets. The stochastic processes known as subordinate diffusions studied in this project can produce realistic jump behavior and thus they are good candidates for modeling financial assets. In this project, we successfully developed a fast and accurate computational method for pricing and hedging options under these models as well as an efficient statistical method to estimate their parameters from market data. Our research results would equip financial practitioners with efficient computational and estimation tools to deal with jumps.

14206716.label: Realisation of objectives
14206716.value: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) patients with severe right-sided major thoracic curve who underwent posterior spinal fusion were prospectively recruited for standing low-dose biplanar X-ray device (EOS) imaging at preoperative, postoperative, and one-year follow-up stages. At both frontal and lateral view, EOS-based lung morphology was automatically measured to assess serial statistical changes in lung area, height, perimeter, width, equivalent diameter, extent, solidity, and aspect ratio, by leveraging in-house program. The measure-remeasure reliability for each lung geometric feature was also evaluated [J01]. To construct a 3D thoracic model bank, a lightweight pyramid attention quick refinement network (LPAQR-Net) was created for the first time to tackle with the challenging segmentation of deformed vertebra from EOS images. LPAQR-Net architecture consisted of three components: 1) a lightweight backbone network to prune network parameters and memory footprints to strike an optimal balance between speed and accuracy; (2) a range of global attention refinement (GAR) modules to selectively reuse low-level features to facilitate feature refinement; (3) an attention-based atrous spatial pyramid pooling (A-ASPP) module to extract weighted pyramid contexts to improve segmentation of blurred vertebrae. Additionally, multi-class training was leveraged to alleviate over-segmentation of adjacent vertebrae [J02, C04, P01]. A range of computational techniques for AIS were developed, which mainly included (1) an automated coronal plane Cobb angle measurement with EOS images [C12]; (2) affine registration to investigate normal range of transformation matrix (translation, rotation, scaling) [C16]; (3) automatic technique to quantify vertebral body dimension (anterior, middle, posterior) [C17]. Meanwhile, several 3D reconstruction experiments of spine and pelvic were performed using both prone computed tomography (CT) and upright EOS [J03, J04, C01, C03, C06, C08, C09, C11]. 1. Issues/Problems encountered Similar to our other research projects, the implementation of this GRF project has been substantially hindered by the global pandemic of COVID-19, which affects the normal operation of both institutions: the Hospital and the University. Firstly, on the Hospital side, in accordance with the stringent control measures against COVID-19 infection, the recruitment of both scoliosis patients and non-scoliosis controls in hospital had to be suspended during a long period. In the first year of COVID-19 pandemic, all non-urgent surgery including posterior spinal fusion for scoliosis have been cancelled. Recently, due to shortage of anaesthetists and nursing staff, despite resuming most operations in the hospital, the operation rooms are still not yet fully utilized. The above unprecedented circumstance has delayed our image acquisition considerably. Secondly, on the University side, we also faced an acute shortage of manpower throughout the whole period of project implementation, particularly during COVID-19 pandemic. PhD student and postdoctoral fellows who specialize in medical image processing and deep learning were unable to work in Hong Kong. Thirdly, even for successfully enrolled study subjects, their preferred timeframes/sessions had to be postponed or adjusted from time to time, interrupting initial imaging and follow-up schedules. Fourthly, COVID-19 inevitably caused inconvenience to the coordination of this GRF project which required conjoint efforts by multidisciplinary teams. The home-office period in the early stage of COVD-19 pandemic had a great negative impact on our research work efficiency. For above reasons, our planned study progress has been significantly delayed, which particularly affects our initial plan to establish 3D thoracic model bank of scoliosis patients with different Lenke curve types, as well as to validate the proposed method in a large cohort of post-operative scoliosis patients. As a result, we had to commence the technical tasks using very limited data/images from a much smaller cohort than what we have initially planned, in order to maintain the scheduled study progress as much as possible. Nevertheless, insufficient sample inevitably posed a formidable challenge to subsequent technical tasks, particularly to landmark identification using the deep convolutional neural network (CNN), for which the development and performance of the CNN framework heavily relies on sufficient learning and validation data size. 2. Attempts to overcome problems in various way. (1) To solve the problem arising from insufficient imaging data, we have attempted to use various remedial techniques that allow the learning with less annotation or other types of supervision, such as semi-supervised learning (SSL), transfer learning (TL), multiple instance (MIL). The task was performed by our PhD student majoring in mathematics. In the literature, the aforementioned techniques have been advocated as effective approaches to leverage limited labelled data and/or unlabelled data. However, the constructed models in our patient cohort were considered suboptimal, as reflected by poor performance metrics (e.g., area under the receiver operating characteristic curve-AUC, accuracy). (2) We then adopted other computational techniques and focused on solving the extremely complicated technical difficulties on image segmentation. The task was performed by another PhD student, who ultimately developed a new technique which had been awarded an US patent of deep learning technique. (3) To speed up the deep learning processing power in our department, we have upgraded and consolidated the facility and equipment dedicated to artificial intelligence, for instance, purchasing more advanced graphical processing units (GPUs) such as NVIDIA DGX™ A100. (4) We strived to seek for advice and comment from our overseas collaborators, technical experts/teams owning rich experience of deep learning and image processing, via proactive online communication. (5) To speed up the research project after the Hospital is back to almost full operation in year 2021, we spared no efforts to expand the research team. We have recruited an additional research assistant for the overall project coordination to facilitate more effective subject recruitment, image retrieval and data collection.

14206716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206716.value: EOS imaging demonstrated a distinctive pattern of lung morphology change in AIS patients underwent posterior spinal fusion. Left lung area significantly increased postoperatively but without continuous increase at one-year follow-up, while right lung area showed slight but insignificant interval improvement. Left lung height demonstrated a significant increase in both postoperative and follow-up stages, whereas right lung height did not significantly change postoperatively. The intra-observer reliability of lung geometric feature measurement was good-to-excellent at both frontal and lateral view. Results suggested that lung geometric change following surgery was likely due to the restoration of shape and symmetry of thoracic cage, which contributed to an improvement in expansibility, mobility, and kinematics of chest wall. This could ultimately lessen the mechanic restriction and increase the maximum amplitude for left lung motion during respiration, enabling a larger expansion of lung capacity. Our study is the first attempt to introduce EOS-derived automatic geometric feature quantification into assessment for serial change of lung morphology in AIS [J01]. To establish a 3D thoracic model bank, we first proposed a lightweight pyramid attention quick refinement network (LPAQR-Net), which was designed to overcome the extreme challenges deep learning-based vertebrae segmentation from EOS (e.g., low contrast, blended boundaries, and superimposition of many layers). LPAQR-Net was less prone to overfitting when addressing small datasets, and surpassed existing models in segmentation accuracy, speed, and GPU memory usage [J02, C04, P01]. We developed an automatic technique to measure Cobb angle from EOS, with high accuracy comparable to that from trained physicians[C12]. To set up a reference standard for vertebral geometric changes in AIS, in CT images, we employed affine registration to investigate normal range of transformation matrix between neighbouring vertebrae in healthy adults [C16], along with automatic quantification of vertebral body height of aging spine [C17]. We demonstrated that rib-vertebra angle difference (Mehta’s angle) was a representation of rotation and apical lordosis [C15]. Several 3D reconstruction experiments of spine and pelvic were performed using prone CT and upright EOS. Scoliotic curvatures could be largely represented by both imaging modalities, despite difference in body positioning [J04, C09]. Axial rotation at apical vertebra was distinguished as the most significant 3D parameter affected by scoliotic curve severity [C01]. Odontoid-hip axis angle was suggested as a complementary parameter for assessing global balance in AIS with thoracic hypokyphosis [J03, C03, C06, C08, C11]. All conference papers [C1-C17] arise from this project although acknowledgement has not been made.

14206716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206716.value: 1. The small sample size appears to be a common limitation in most of similar studies. Insufficient cohort is less likely to generate statistically significance, particularly for the latent lung geometric features slightly altered by surgery. Besides, potential selection bias was possibly introduced into single centre study. Thus, multi-centre study is advocated to enlarge sample size and eliminate the bias. 2. Novel deep learning frameworks/algorithms to overcome challenges arising from small dataset of lung images (EOS, CT or MRI) would be an interesting topic. Larger cohort may be achievable only by multiple-centre studies, which prioritize the active improvement of generalizability of computational AIS models. 3. The proposed vertebra segmentation technique can be further validated by external and internal datasets, especially in severe AIS datasets. Learning joint representations from frontal and lateral images is suggested to enhance segmentation performance. 4. Since our results were obtained shortly after the surgery within 12 months, prolonged duration of follow-up to represent ultimate outcome, is warranted to ascertain the improvement in lung morphology attained from EOS.

14206716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206716.value: The research project focuses on the lung morphology derived from EOS imaging in severe AIS patients, as well as on automatic computational segmentation of deformed structures/organs. We have observed a distinctive change pattern of lung morphology in response to spinal fusion surgery, characterized with a markedly improvement of left lung area. Results suggest that restoration of shape and symmetry of thoracic cage may improve expansibility and kinematics of chest wall, which lessen the mechanic restriction of left lung motion during respiration, enabling a larger expansion of lung capacity. Our findings indicate that EOS has potential to serve as a useful and cost-effectiveness surrogate imaging tool in AIS to assess lung morphology on top of scoliotic curvature within a single examination, with significantly lower radiation exposure. We have successfully constructed a novel deep learning framework to tackle with challenging segmentation of deformed vertebrae, which performance outperforms other existing models in accuracy and speed. This model may facilitate to make evidence-powered surgical plan and to boost AIS research efficiency. Its utilization could be extended to other forms of scoliosis. In summary, our morphology findings and computational techniques, after further verification and testing, may reinforce the usefulness of EOS in AIS imaging.

14208816.label: Project Objectives
14208816.value: Design and implement a network science analytic engine to handle large and time-varying graphs. Provide CPU and I/O-efficient algorithms to carry out many data analytics. For example, we propose to use the "canonical labeling" to pre-process the graph's data structures for the shortest distance computation. We also propose that the data structures can be vertical scaled for cluster computing paradigm or vertical scaled for single PC with efficient I/O support. Apply our network science analytic engine on some realistic applications, i.e., community/interest detection on the WeChat OSN so that one can do better personalized recommendation, and to discovery anomaly traffic in networking scenarios.

14208816.value: 近年來，有一種被稱為網絡科學的多學科研究。本研究的目的是為了開發高效的I / O保證數據的分析引擎。 這樣一方面可以嘗試各種網絡科學算法。 我們將用我們的分析引擎來解決一些新興的應用如個人推薦, 信息檢測突發. 這項研究認為，無論對於網絡科學分析算法的設計， 數學建模在在線社交網絡如信息最大化的應用，以及系統設計和實現一個數據分析系統。我們的研究結果可以幫助企業擴展他們的服務，而研究人員和工程師開展大規模網絡更有效的數據分析。

14208816.label: Realisation of objectives
14208816.value: We have designed and implemented a stand alone computing analytic system for online social networks and also for mobile traffic analysis. The analysis is based on the algorithms we proposed in this research. In designing the analytic system, we also carefully design some resource management schemes (e.g., CPU, memory, disk I/O scheduling) so that one can efficiently load the data from disks and perform data analysis in a pipeline manner. We want to emphasized that it was very labor intensive to do canonical labeling, and we spent many man-hours on doing this data labeling. We also like to note that our system design can be executed on a cluster machine. The porting to cluster machines took more time than we originally expected but the end resulting software system is more robust and extensible. To demonstrate the usefulness of our system, we demonstrated how to analyze online social networks as well as mobile traffic anomaly detection. We have also published number of conference and journal papers, and note that these research results were published in well-known venues. This showed that our research results are indeed up to the international standard.

Conference papers: 1,2,3, 6, 10. - Objective 2: Journal papers: 3. Conference papers: 1,6, 8, 9, 10. - Objective 3: Journal papers: 1, 2, 3, 4. Conference papers: 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. In addition, we have realized an analytic engine to analyze online social networks. The data we used were obtained from various sources, including public domain datasets for graphs, as well as data from Tencent's WeChat data sources (of course, we have to follow the confidentiality requirement as set by the company). We were able to efficiently analyze some of the dynamic data, we also performed numerous labelling tasks for the given data so that we can feed these data to our analytic engine for information discovery. Last but not least, we were able to carry out topics/interests detections for users in online social networks, and we also worked with networking companies, i.e., Huawei, so to detect anomaly traffics. Footnote: Please note that for journal #4, GRF acknowledgement was not shown because there was some miscommunication between the PI and the publisher. But we did intend to acknowledge GRF. Given that the number of publications and research results, we feel that we want to include this in our final completion report.

14208816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208816.value: One potential further development is to develop a multi-cluster distributed analytic engine. Currently, our system is a standalone computing system and if one wants to stress the system by feeding large scale online social networks (via streaming data format) it will take a long time for processing. Therefore, one possible extension is to extend our system design to a distributed/parallel system setting so to improve the performance as set by the application.

14208816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208816.value: In this project, we consider two important applications: online social networks and mobile traffic analysis. These two applications are important to our daily life. For example, many people are now interacting with their friends via online social networks, and many people are using mobile phones to communicate. For companies which operate the online social networks or mobile network, there is an urgent need for them to understand the underlying traffic so that the companies can provide proper resource provisioning, or if there is a mobile malware spreading the virus, companies need to understand their spreading dynamics. Using our analytic engine, companies which operate online social networks or mobile network can analyze their recorded data and to do further inference or analysis. This will help operators of these companies to better size their systems and to do better system management.
