14209416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209416.value: Healthcare associated infections (HAIs) are the disease that people acquire inside a healthcare setting such as hospital. This type of infections poses a serious threat to public health. For instance, there were about 722,000 cases of HAIs reported by U.S. hospitals in 2011. About 10% of HAI cases resulted in death (Magill et al. [1]). Another example was the 2003 SARS epidemic causing hundreds of deaths around the world. It was later traced back to an outbreak in a hospital in Hong Kong (Lee et al. [2] and Hung [3]). Among many control strategies against infectious diseases, targeted immunization is a common and effective approach for preventing infections among people. It requires identifying potential “super spreaders” and preventing them from being the sources that spread the diseases over human contact networks, with the goal of reducing the impact of epidemic outbreaks as far as possible. Except for direct protection for targeted individuals, targeted immunization also provides indirect protection for people who are in the same contact networks as the targeted individuals. These people may be infants and pregnant women who are not suitable for getting vaccinated themselves. Moreover, when vaccines are scarce, possibly due to limited budgets or shortages of supply, allocating resource optimally is essentially important for developing efficient intervention strategies. In this work, we plan to develop effective and efficient control strategies of target immunization against HAIs. This work leverages on the PI’s previous project on developing a hospital risk management system with indoor application of the RFID technology. This technology tracks the location and movement of human and medical equipment and monitors real-time ward events. We have conducted a four-month pilot study of our system in a public hospital in Hong Kong. Based on the data collected, we plan to conduct further investigation for developing network-based control strategies for minimizing HAI outbreaks. Specifically, several activities are involved to achieve this goal: •dynamic human contact network construction based on human tracking data in a hospital for characterizing person-to-person interaction in a healthcare setting, •concise formulation of targeted immunization as an outbreak minimization problem under network diffusion models, •investigation on the equivalence between the outbreak minimization problem and the influence maximization problem which is extensively studied in the field of social influence analysis, •solution to the outbreak minimization problem using optimization approaches, which is applicable to real-world scenarios, •experimental evaluations on real data and comparison to the existing methods to verify the performance and scalability.

14209416.label: Realisation of objectives
14209416.value: Three major research activities have been carried out to fulfill the research objectives: Activity 1: Development of Hospital Risk Management System (HRMS) for Traceability Study Activity 2: Traceability study based on HRMS for effective control Activity 3: Analysis of Outbreak Minimization and Influence Maximization using Optimization Activity 1: Development of Hospital Risk Management System (HRMS) for Traceability We attempt to understand how hospital acquired infections (HAI) spread out in a medical facility and hope that we can develop effective control strategies to stop the spreading in time. Our research hence focuses on the further development of a Hospital Risk Management System (HRMS) and makes use of HRMS to work on the control strategies. HRMS not only tracks the location and movement of patients and healthcare workers in the hospital, but also provides function modules for real-time event monitoring and human interaction analysis (Cheng and Kuo [2016]). The architecture of HRMS is shown in Figure 1. Figure 2 shows the devices used in the pilot study at the hospital. These devices were designed and developed by a group of researchers from Department of Electronic Engineering, CUHK. A real-time event monitoring system is designed with the capability to give real-time alerts of abnormal human and equipment situations for improving ward management. A human interaction analytics system traces person-to-person contact in the hospital and performs social network analysis. Tracking data of patients and healthcare workers collected in this project is used for our further research on HAIs. Activity 2: Traceability Study based on HRMS We define analytics requirements for visualizing and summarizing the traceability data obtained from the Hospital Risk Management System (HRMS), with specific focus on two modules – Traceability Analytics (TA) and Spatial-Temporal Co-occurrence Analysis (STCA). TA covers the front-end interactive visualization for analysts and managerial staff to learn about the insight of underlying object tracking data and object interactivities. STCA involves the back-end analytic processes for obtained various statistical at different levels of abstraction and for calculating contact occurrences based on time and location between pairs of tagged objects. All tag locations captured at a given time are shown in Figure 3. The entire movement path can be shown by connected all pairs of dots in time sequence (shown in Figure 4). For a specified time period, the contact relationships between all tagged patients and healthcare workers are shown in the connected network. This tool will allow users to interactively pick a particular object and follow its links to other objects that it has contacted with. The tracing processing can repeatedly be performed according to the needs. Activity 3: Outbreak Minimization vs. Influence Maximization As documented in Cheng et al. (2020), an effective approach to containing epidemic outbreaks is targeted immunization, which involves identifying "super spreaders" who play a key role in spreading disease over human contact networks. The ultimate goal of targeted immunization and other disease control strategies is to minimize the impact of outbreaks. It shares similarity with the famous influence maximization problem studied in the field of social network analysis, whose objective is to identify a group of in influential individuals to maximize the influence spread over social networks. This study aims to establish the equivalence of the two problems and develop an effective methodology for targeted immunization through the use of influence maximization. We present a concise formulation of the targeted immunization problem and show its equivalence to the influence maximization problem under the framework of the Linear Threshold diffusion model. Thus the influence maximization problem, as well as the targeted immunization problem, can be solved by an optimization approach. A Benders' decomposition algorithm is developed to solve the optimization problem for effective solutions. A comprehensive computational study is conducted to evaluate the performance and scalability of the optimization approach on real-world large-scale networks. Computational results show that our proposed approaches achieve more effective solutions compared to existing methods. 14209416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209416.value: We show the equivalence of the outbreak minimization and influence maximization problems and present a concise formulation for the influence maximization problem under the Linear Threshold diffusion model. A tradeoff between computational effectiveness and computational efficiency is illustrated. Our results suggest that the capability of determining the optimal group of individuals for immunization is particularly crucial for the containment of infectious disease outbreaks within a small network. Finally, our proposed methodology not only determines the optimal solutions for target immunization, but can also aid policymakers in determining the right level of immunization coverage.

14209516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209516.value: The aim of this project is to research original methods for power efficiency of analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) in high resolution and high speed arenas. Higher ADC power efficiency has been in great demand due to an exponential growth of battery-powered devices, like smart phones, wearable electronic devices, and devices connected to the internet-of-things. In all of these devices an ADC is an indispensable sub-system for acquisition of sound, video, radio, biomedical, environmental or other types of signals. After decades of evolution, the Delta-Sigma Modulator (DSM) and Successive Approximation Register (SAR), together with the pipelined type of ADCs, have dominated the ADC power efficiency chart. In this project, we will conduct two pieces of research in parallel for ADC power efficiency. Our first research will be on one type of DSMs known as Gm-C continuous-time DSM. Gm-C DSMs are the most power-efficient DSMs within the performance range that they can reach. However, a key issue of Gm-C DSMs is the nonlinearity of their Gm cells, which severely limits their dynamic range (DR) and thus their applications. We will investigate a new set of circuit and system techniques to overcome this problem of Gm-C DSMs so as to push their DR performance into uncharted territory. Two Gm-C DSMs in different applications will be developed in CMOS to demonstrate the techniques. The first DSM will be designed for the demanding GSM receivers which require an 80 dB DR over a 200 kHz bandwidth, a territory which the Gm-C DSM has never before reached. The second DSM will be designed for multi-mode wide-band (10 MHz or more) wireless receivers. Due to the use of the Gm-C circuit and the solution to its nonlinearity problem, both DSMs are expected to achieve power efficiency better than other types of DSMs with similar performances. Our second research will be into a brand new ADC architecture for power efficiency at a high conversion rate. It consists of an SAR sub-ADC and a time-to-digital converter capable of operating in a pipelined manner. A distinct feature of the proposed architecture is that it does not need an amplifier, thus getting rid of a major issue in existing pipelined SAR ADCs. The proposed ADC is also highly tolerant of circuit imperfections. To validate the method, we will design a 10-bit high-speed (100 MS/s) ADC suitable for applications in high-definition video signal acquisition and next generation (5G) wireless communication mobile receivers.

14209516.label: Realisation of objectives
14209516.value: We have successfully completed objective 1, which was to conduct a theoretical study on a new method to compensate for the major source of nonlinearity in a new Gm-C based DSM topology. To achieve this goal, we first proposed a DSM topology that employed a Gm-cell in the feedback path and a passive RC low-pass filter (LPF) at the input of this Gm-cell. The LPF suppresses the high-frequency components of quantization noise that exists in the feedback signal. This helps reduce the Gm cell’s input swing. With a reduced signal swing, the Gm cells’ linearity is improved. The LPF also avoids high-frequency quantization noise to fold into the signal band even if nonlinearity in the feedback Gm is present. With matched transfer characteristics, the input and feedback Gm circuits cancel each other’s nonlinearities. Second, we proposed a merged input-feedback Gm circuit with shared degeneration resistors. This merged Gm-cell has high trans-conductance and noise efficiencies and simultaneously allows the input and feedback signals to be large, which would cause nonlinearity in traditional Gm cells. These proposed techniques were analyzed theoretically and then validated by circuit simulations. Objective 2 is fully completed. Based on the theory laid in objective 1, we have designed and fabricated a Gm-C DSM prototype with a 100 kHz signal bandwidth in a 180nm CMOS technology. When two such DSMs are employed for I and Q channels in a receiver, the effective bandwidth becomes 200 kHz, as stated in the original objective. The prototype demonstrated that the proposed techniques could effectively cancel the nonlinearity of Gm cells. The Gm-C DSM prototype chip achieved a dynamic range of 80 dB over the 100 kHz bandwidth, meeting the stated goal. The chip consumed 222.5uW from a dual power supply of 1.5V and 1.8V. Its power efficiency, represented by Schreier’s figure-of-merit, was significantly better than prior Gm-C DSMs. Objective 3 is substantially completed. We designed a wideband Gm-C DSM in a 65nm CMOS process using a 1.5-bit quantizer, an FIR DAC and a merged input-feedback Gm. The bandwidth of the DSM is 70 MHz, which is wider than the planned value of 10 or 20MHz. The reasons for this were that we wanted to tackle a greater challenge and that the academic values and applications of a wider bandwidth Gm-C modulator would be greater and wider, respectively. The modulator was designed to have a 2.8GHz sampling frequency. It achieved a dynamic range of 71dB under a 37mW consumption from a 1.25V supply in post-layout simulations. The design was taped out for fabrication. Unfortunately, the measured dynamic range of the returned chip was far below the post-layout simulated results. We investigated the problems and re-ran post-layout simulations at different scenarios. However, the re-run simulation results were largely the same as before, and the exact source of the problems could not be identified. We suspected it was due to flaws in the fabrication. The design was not submitted for another round of fabrication as it could not be done before the end of the project. Objectives 4 and 5 are successfully completed. We conducted a theoretical study and system optimization on the SAR+TDC architecture for power-efficient and high-speed data conversion. We proposed a detect-and-skip (DAS) algorithm to break through the device limitations of switched-capacitor-based DACs in a coarse-fine SAR ADC architecture. The DAS algorithm reduces 55% of the energy and extends the valid bandwidth by seven times. Based on the theory, an ADC in the SAR+TDC architecture was designed and implemented in a 180 nm CMOS process. The ADC prototype achieved 10-bit resolution at a 10-MSps rate, and measured an energy efficiency of 57.8 fJ/conv.-step, which was among the highest at the time.

14209516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209516.value: First, a new Gm-C Delta-Sigma modulator topology and related new circuits were developed for improved power efficiency without sacrificing linearity. The new topology features a passive RC low-pass filter in its feedback. The passive circuit efficiently realizes a pole of the loop filter. It also suppresses high-frequency quantization noise at the output of the digital-to-analog converter (DAC), thereby minimizing the quantization noise folded to the signal band because of Gm nonlinearity. Associated with the new topology was a merged input-feedback Gm circuit. The new circuit technique frees the Gm circuit from the efficiency-harming source degeneration while maintaining high linearity for large input and feedback signals. A prototype Gm-C DSM with the proposed circuit and architecture was fabricated in a 180nm CMOS. It advanced the state of the arts of Gm-C DSMs in terms of power efficiency. These findings were published in outcome items 8.1 and 10.1 in Part C. Second, we found new power-efficient active-RC DSM architecture, which was rooted in the above Gm-C DSM topology. The key concept was to place a passive low-pass RC filter at the feedback path of an active-RC DSM. This technique significantly reduces the bandwidth, linearity and slew-rate requirements of the crucial first amplifier in the DSM, and hence can substantially reduce the power consumption of the modulator. Different variations of such an active-RC modulator topology were identified while we progressed in our research. They were reported in outcome items 8.2, 9.2, 9.3 and 9.4. It is noted that publication 9.2 was awarded a best conference paper award (item 11.1). Third, we proposed a new method to correct both static and dynamic DAC errors for wideband multi-bit DSMs. The work was published in item 9.1. Furthermore, we discovered an extremely linear multi-level DAC, which does not require any calibration, trimming, or dynamic element matching. The DAC could improve the power efficiency of a continuous-time DSM, while making it insensitive to clock jitter and inter-symbol interference. The work leads to the publication item 8.5. Fourth, for improving power efficiency, we developed a new SAR ADC switching scheme with MSB prediction, and a detect-and-skip algorithm for an ADC consisting of pipelined SAR and TDC. These works lead to publication items 8.3 and 8.4. Last, we proposed and demonstrated a temperature-compensation circuit technique for high-speed flash ADCs using power-efficient inverter-based comparators. The work leads to outcome item 8.6.

14209516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209516.value: There are plenty of opportunities to advance the power efficiency of ADCs towards the ultimate limit imposed by thermal noise. As demonstrated in this project, Gm-C DSMs have great potential for low-power ADCs as their linearity-efficiency conflict can be resolved. The Gm-C DSM architecture proposed in this project was the first attempt in this direction. It can be further optimized, for example, by incorporating the proposed extremely linear multi-level DAC, by eliminating some unnecessary Gm cells, by using a more aggressive excess delay loop compensation approach, and by using a SAR ADC as its quantizer. We plan to write a new RGC proposal for future development. A further action to expand the impact of this research is to develop other applications of the proposed extremely linear DAC, such as in discrete-time DSMs, pipeline ADCs and DSM-based DACs. On the other hand, the proposed DAC doubles the sampling rate to achieve its high linearity. Inherently highly linear DAC circuits without doubling the sampling rate present another further research opportunity. We will consider applying for an ITF grant to realize some industrial applications of the low-power ADC techniques developed in this project.

14209516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209516.value: The project investigated circuits and system techniques for advancing the power efficiency and performance of certain types of analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) with fruitful outcomes. First, we proposed a new system architecture and new circuits for Gm-C Delta-Sigma modulators (DSMs). These techniques fundamentally resolved the conflict between the linearity and power efficiency in this type of ADCs. A prototype Gm-C DSM fabricated in a CMOS technology demonstrated that Gm-C DSM is a great candidate for low-power ADCs. Second, we tackled a fundamental problem in a multi-bit DSM, that is, the linearity of its digital-to-analog converter (DAC) is limited by device mismatches. We discovered a multi-bit 2x sampling-rate DAC that can break the device mismatch limit. The proposed DAC is generic and can be used in other applications, such as discrete-time DSMs, pipeline ADCs, and DSM DACs for high linearity and low cost. Last, we developed new circuit techniques for improved power efficiency in SAR+TDC ADCs, and an automatic temperature compensation circuit for flash ADCs that use power-efficient inverter-based comparators. The proposed techniques were validated by prototype chips fabricated in CMOS processes. In summary, this project broadened our understanding of the above types of ADCs and contributed effective power-efficient ADC techniques.

14211316.label: Project Objectives
14211316.value: Provide analytical estimates of both ``Value-at-Risk" and ``Expected Shortfall" for static portfolios, under a wide range of elliptical multivariate distributions. There are two analytical challenges associated with the problem. First is to reduce the dimensionality of the problem due to its multivariate nature. Second is construct sensible asymptotic expansions when the method of saddlepoint approximation does not apply well. We plan to develop techniques to tackle these two. Analyze the diversification effect associated with portfolio tail risk. We plan to use results obtained in the first objective to examine the relationship between the amount of risk reduction and 1) the portfolio composition; 2) the parameters controlling asset tail behavior. With this analysis, we hope to shield some light on what are the key determinants of the diversification effect. Conduct empirical studies using real world financial data on representative asset classes, such as liquid stocks, government bonds, corporate debt, and mortgage-back securities. By fitting data to our targeted distributions and compare results between those from historical simulation with those from the first and second objects, we would like to evaluate the accuracies of our results.

14211316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14211316.value: Following the 2007-2008 financial crisis, both the United States and the European Union have enacted legislative proposals, according to which, existing risk management framework is considered imperfect. It is concerned that financial institutions may not have sufficient capital to weather catastrophic events if market risks are measured by the ``Value-at-Risk" metric. It is also concerned that aggregated counterparty risk, if not mitigated, is a threat to the stability of financial system. On the other hand, simply increasing capital requirements for banks and charging heavy margins at central counterparties may lead to liquidity problems as well as inefficient use of capital. At the center of this intricate trade off is the assessment and management of tail risk. This motivates us to conduct a technical investigation into the mathematical behavior of portfolio tail risk under the prevailing risk metrics. In particular, we plan to consider a rich parametric family of multivariate distribution and provide accurate analytical estimates of both portfolio value-at-risk (VaR) and portfolio expected shortfall (ES). We work with these distributions based on the consideration that they not only exhibit distinct behavior of tail heaviness and tail dependence, but also have the property that, under which, both VaR and ES are coherent risk measures. Our goal is to use these analytical results to examine the diversification effect associated with portfolio tail risk. By looking at the risk reduction amount which measures the dollar difference between the total risk of a static portfolio and the sum of that of individual positions, we intend to understand the role played by the following properties on tail risk diversification: the tail heaviness of individual asset, the pair-wise tail dependence, and the cross-asset heterogeneity. 2008年的全球金融危機讓監管當局深刻意識到現有的風控體制在面對系統性金融風險時存在嚴重不足。作為應對，歐美均積極通過立法，一方面要求銀行和金融機構大幅增加資本金防範於未然，另一方面要求各證券交易市場全面實行保證金交易制度。但無論是增加資本金還是保證金交易，如果不加分析的全面實施，對整個金融市場來說，都會增加不必要的資金需求，從而降低全市場的資金使用效率，使流動性承壓。其根本原因在於，合理的資本金額度和保證金額度因當因具體資產的虧損敞口不同而不同。因此這個兩難問題背後的核心之一是如何準確的度量一個資產組合的尾部風險（小概率的大額虧損風險） 以及對尾部風險的系統管理。本課題試圖從一族具有多元重尾特徵的資產價格分佈入手，通過運用漸進分析的方法，來分析並量化一個包含有限個資產的投資組合其巨額虧損是如何依賴於各個子資產價格分佈的重尾程度和以及各個子資產價格之間的極值相關性這兩個方面。在風險度量的選取方面，我們考慮 Value-at-Risk (VaR) 和 Expected Shortfall (ES) 這兩個當下最為重要的度量標準。在價格分佈的選取方面，我們假設組合中的各子資產價格滿足一族參數化的多元橢圓分佈。一方面，我們構造的這一族分佈能夠同時產生具有代表性的 Exponential-type 輕尾分佈和 Power-type 的重尾分佈。另一方面，這一族分佈也能產生寬範圍的極值相關係數以便我們研究資產間的相關性對整體風險的影響。於此同時，選取橢圓分佈的一個考慮是其對 VaR 和 ES 均滿足次可加性，便與我們能附帶研究尾部風險在一個組合中是如何分散降低的(Diversification benefits). 本課題的最終目的是理解並量化各個子資產價格的重尾度以及他們之間的相關性對整個投資組合的全局風險的影響。

14211316.label: Realisation of objectives
14211316.value: The three project objectives have been achieved satisfactorily with rich and comprehensive research output. The realization of each objective is described below. 1. We solved the two analytical challenges associated with the problem. The first one is solved through the specification of the elliptical distribution family where we used a geometric approach together with its intrinsic stochastic decomposition property. The second one is solved by constructing a general uniform expansion approach which works in cases where the method of saddlepoint approximation does not apply well. 2. We thoroughly analyzed the diversification effect associated with portfolio tail risk. This is possible due to the analytical methods we developed in meeting Objective 1. In particular, we used results obtained in the first objective to examine the relationship between the amount of risk reduction and the portfolio composition and the parameters controlling asset tail behavior. With this analysis, we have identified the key determinants of the diversification effect. 3. With the help of co-Is, we have conducted extensive empirical studies using real-world financial data on equities, government bonds, corporate debt, and mortgage-back securities. The empirical results are satisfactory up to the industrial standard at the risk management division of wall street banks.

14211316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14211316.value: The major findings are as follows: a) Tail heaviness dictates the absolute amount of initial margin charge when switching from VaR to ES; 2) Dependence structure dictates the relative magnitude of diversification benefits when merging multiple similar portfolios, irrespective of the risk metric; 3) Diversification does not reduce the tail event probability; it only mitigates the magnitude of damage. Research outcomes of this project are as follows: a) Journal paper: 1 paper submitted to the SIAM Journal of Financial Mathematics. It is currently under review. b) Conference talks: 6 presentations are accepted and delivered at all the major and most internationally recognized conferences in the area of Financial Engineering. These include the World Congress of the Bachelier Finance Society, the INFORMS Annual Meeting, the SIAM Conference on Financial Mathematics & Engineering, the European Conference on Operational Research, Federal Reserve Bank of New York Conference, and Asian Quantitative Finance Conference. 4 in North America, 1 in Europe and 1 in Asia. c) Industrial impact: Thanks to our co-I's collaboration, the models developed, together with their implementation and algorithms, are successfully tested and used at the risk management division of the New York-based Bank of Mellon.

14211316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14211316.value: The setup in the current study assumes homogeneous tail heaviness among asset returns. Future work should consider the heterogeneous case.

14211316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14211316.value: In the current environment of financial regulation, traceability is essential in day-to-day risk management, especially portfolio tail risks which are essential to the fast calculation of margin/capital requirements. This research develops a novel asymptotic expansion method that makes the portfolio tail risk tractable when the asset returns follow the multivariate elliptical distribution family. The models and the methods we developed are well received by the wall street banks through our collaborator. The models and methods are designed to suit the real-world production environment.

14212116.label: Realisation of objectives
14212116.value: The objective of this study was to determine the characteristics and cytotoxicities of organic aerosols (OA) in urban areas in Hong Kong. Quadrupole Aerosol Chemical Speciation Monitor (Q-ACSM), which can characterize the temporal variations of chemical components, including organic fractions, nitrate, sulfate, ammonium, and chloride, was used to determine the online nonrefractory submicron aerosol (NR-PM1) in this study. The chemical profile of organic species in PM1 was examined with twenty-four-hour integrated PM1 filter samples, and the concentration of criteria gaseous pollutants were monitored by various analyzers operated by the Hong Kong Environmental Protection Department (HKEPD) at the same location for reference. Two typical areas were chosen for sampling in this study: 1) Mong Kok (MK), an urban district in Hong Kong with dense buildings and traffic, suffered with heavy pollution; 2) Yuen Long (YL), which is located at a residential-commercial area with little industries. The combing of off-line and on-line PM investigation can provide more knowledge about the chemical characteristics, which is crucial for the toxicological analysis. In order to investigate the sources of organic compounds in NR-PM1, positive matrix factorization (PMF) was used. It is a bilinear model representing data entered as a linear combination of the factor’s time series. According to the different emission characteristics of air pollutants in MK and YL, varied pollution source were observed. In MK, three factors were resolved, namely primary oxygenated organic aerosol (POA), less-oxidized oxygenated OA (LO-OOA), and more-oxidized oxygenated OA (MO-OOA). In YL, three factors were also resolved, namely traffic OA (TOA), cooking OA (COA), and oxygenated OA (OOA). According to the source apportionment analysis, the major sources of organic aerosols in MK and YL were identified, and the contributions of each source has also been compared. Cell experiments were conducted with PM1 filter samples collected from two sites to determine their cytotoxicity. Human lung alveolar epithelial (A549) cells were used to investigate the toxicity induced by PM1. The A549 cells were exposed to PM1 for 24 h, and bioreactivity markers such as lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and interlukin-6 (IL-6) were examined. Inflammatory and oxidative responses were found after PM exposure, and the crucial organic compounds and organic sources for the cell responses were also identified. All of the targets have been accomplished on schedule. The outcomes were published in peer-reviewed journals. More results will be anticipated and expected for further articles submissions in due course.

14212116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14212116.value: Under ambient conditions, mass concentrations of particulate organics, sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, and chloride were determined by Q-ACSM, particulate organic (55.0%) was the most abundant in NR-PM1, followed by sulfate (21.0%), ammonium (13.0%), nitrate (10.0%) and chloride (1.0%) in MK. Three major organic sources were identified by positive matrix factorization, namely primary organic aerosol (POA, 40±19%), more-oxidized oxygenated OA (MO-OOA, 32±22%) and less-oxidized oxygenated OA (LO-OOA, 28±19%). In YL, the contributions of major chemical components in PM1 were similar as in MK. Particulate organic (summer: 45.9%, winter: 59.6%) were the most abundant in NR-PM1 in summer and winter, followed by sulfate (summer: 29.6%, winter: 17.6%), ammonium (summer: 16.3%, winter: 11.9%), nitrate (summer: 7.8%, winter: 10.2%) and chloride (summer: 0.4%, winter: 0.7%). But the sources of particulate organics were totally different from MK, traffic OA (TOA), cooking OA (COA), and oxygenated OA (OOA) were identified in YL. The contribution of OOA in summer (63.2%) was much higher than winter (48.4%) due to the higher temperature which promote photochemical reactions in the atmosphere; while in winter, TOA was the most abundant organic fractions to the total organics (37.7%). According to the abundances of organic markers, including alkanes (i.e., n- and iso-/antiiso-alkanes), hopanes, steranes, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), oxy-PAHs (OPAHs), and fatty acids, it demonstrated that traffic and cooking emissions were the dominant sources in MK. Cytotoxic effects of the PM1 on human lung alveolar epithelial (A549) cells were measured by means of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), reactive oxygen species (ROS), and interlukin-6 (IL-6). The increases LDH, ROS, and IL-6 levels after exposure indicated the occurrence of inflammatory and oxidative responses. In MK, POA was significantly associated with ROS and IL-6, which alkanes, hopanes, steranes, PAHs, and fatty acids presented medium to high correlations with LDH and IL-6, which demonstrated the importance of organic compounds (especially from primary emission) in cytotoxicity. In YL, elemental carbon (soot) was well correlated with ROS and IL-6 levels, indicated the crucial role of this carbon fraction. Moreover, COA was well correlated with IL-6, which indicated the contribution of cooking emission on inflammatory responses. These results indicated that organic aerosol/compounds emitted from traffic and cooking play a critical role in PM-induced oxidative stress and inflammation in urban areas of Hong Kong.

14212116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14212116.value: In this study, both online and offline sampling techniques were employed to determine the characteristics and cytotoxicities of organic aerosols (OA) in urban areas of Hong Kong. Except PM1, other size fractions of particle can also be investigated. In previous studies, the seasonal effects showed significant differences for coarse, fine and ultrafine PM in in terms of biological and cytological in vivo bioassay parameters. Moreover, organic sources were only identified in this study, the sources of PM1 were not resolved in details. Therefore, the sources of PM and their cytotoxicities can be further investigated. This is important to under the health effects of different emission sources for developing management strategies in Hong Kong. In addition, other human health effects could also be studied, such as cardiovascular and neurological diseases. PM can be inhaled into the trachea and easily deposited into the alveoli and even the bloodstream, resulting in an inflammatory response. It is assumed that this inflammation may not only be the cause of respiratory disorders but could also trigger the permanent damage of various organs. Therefore. this is important to perform more studies on the health effects of PM and their chemical compositions.

14212116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14212116.value: Long-term exposure to particulate matter (PM) has been well-recognized as a critical potential factor for cardiopulmonary system diseases. The size, composition, and source of PM and their interaction are responsible for PM’s adverse health effects. Organic matter has been regarded as a dominant driver of cytotoxic effects induced by PM. Hence, toxicological studies on organic aerosols (OA) are required to obtain more information on the roles of different OA components and their sources. A combination of online monitoring and offline OA analysis could provide knowledge on not only the characteristics of individual organic components but also the potential sources of OAs. Compared with PM2.5, PM1 has a higher toxic potential because of their greater concentrations and surface areas. PM1 can carry and deliver more redox-active organic compounds to the respiratory system than large particles, leading to adverse health effects. So it is important to study the characteristics of PM1 in different regions, and the cardiorespiratory health effects caused by PM1 are also important for future human health studies.

14212316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212316.value: 以腹腔鏡為代表的微創手術已經得到廣泛臨床應用，其主要優點在於失血少，住院短，術後疼痛少，傷口更為美觀。微創手術的成功很大程度上得益於手術器械的發展。現有微創手術用器械大多數為筷子一樣的硬質細桿，通過繞切口的擺動和伸縮來到達不同的手術部位。這樣的缺點在於：1）內部工作空間狹小；2）外部操作空間大；3）損傷切口；4）運動干涉。這是現有微創手術需要多個切口以及達芬奇手術機器人體積龐大的原因。柔性器械可以通過在體內的變形來到達不同部位，這大大減輕了上述局限。柔性器械的發展取決於柔性機構。現有手術器械用柔性機構可分為兩大類：線驅動柔性機構和同心管柔性機構。這兩種柔性機構都有各自的缺陷，限制了其在體內的工作空間和靈巧度。而這些正是影響微創手術的重要因素。 本項目旨在研究一種可在受限空間，如微創手術，實施靈巧操作的新型柔性機構。其原理在於通過對現有欠驅動柔性機構進行主動約束，從而擴大其工作空間和提高靈巧度。該機構取名為同心拉線機構。該機構的主要特點在於：1）更大工作空間；2）更高靈巧度；3）可變剛度；4）力傳感；5）小偏擺運動。工作空間的擴大可以幫助減少微創手術所需切口數量；靈巧度的提高有助於在體內進行更精細的操作並減少手術時間；可控的剛度有助於讓同一種手術器械完成不同負載下的操作而減少更換手術器械的次數；力傳感可以用來實現醫生的遠程觸覺；小偏擺運動有助於繞開關鍵組織結構從而提微創高手術的安全性。為了驗證同心拉線機構在微創手術中的有效性，我們計劃利用該機構研發一種柔性手術器械並集成到達芬奇手術機器人研究套件（DVRK）上。利用該柔性手術器械，我們計劃完成腹腔鏡手術系統（FLS）提出的五個基本手術任務。 我們的研究團隊在柔性機構設計以及柔性機器人方面擁有多年的研究經驗。研究工作受到國內外同行認可。我們期望這項研究有助於研發下一代靈巧型柔性手術機器人系統以及其它在受限空間內操作的柔性機器人系統，如災難救助機器人。

14212316.label: Realisation of objectives
14212316.value: This project aims to investigate a novel flexible mechanism for minimally invasive surgical robots. It contains two main objectives and they are fully achieved at the end of the project. The first objective is to design a hyper-dexterous flexible mechanism, named the concentric wire-driven flexible mechanism (CWM), and systematically study its performance from the following aspects: i) kinematics, workspace, dexterity and trajectory tracking at load free condition; ii) statics and payload ability distribution; iii) real-time shape estimation and reconstruction. We sought inspiration from the nature and designed the wire-driven mechanism, which contains a flexible backbone and a set of driving cables/wires. It is highly flexible and underactuated. By observing that the human finger’s flexion motion would change due to the external fixation of the proximal finger joint, we applied active constraints to wire-driven mechanism and lead to the constrained wire-driven mechanism. In the constrained wire-driven mechanism, the active constraint is a straight rod/tube that could move along the flexible backbone. It could help to expand the workspace of the wire-driven mechanism, however the constraint itself could not be bent. This motivated us to develop the CWM. In the CWM, there are two layers of wire-driven mechanism configured in a concentric manner. The inner layer is thinner and it could be serpentine wire-driven mechanism or the continuum wire-driven mechanism. The outer layer is in the form of a serpentine wire-driven mechanism. Both layers could be bent to two orthogonal directions and translated along the axis. In addition, the outer layer could be stiffened or slacked. When the outer layer is stiffened, it serves as the active constraint to the inner layer. When the outer layer is slacked, it could bend along with the inner layer. Since the outer layer could be bent and translated, it could constrain the backbone of the inner layer at any location within its workspace. The overall shape of the CWM is defined by the inner layer and the end effector position is at the tip of the inner layer. It is divided into two segments by the outer layer: the proximal segment that overlaps with the outer layer and the distal segment that is not covered by the outer layer. The kinematic model of the CWM is based on the piecewise constant curvature assumption. For each bending segment, it is assumed to be a circular arc when there is no load. By establishing the mapping between the wire length change and arc configuration and the mapping between the arc configuration and the tip location, the kinematic model of the CWM is established. Using this kinematic model, by traversing the parameters we could find the workspace of the CWM. Compared to the workspaces of a single segment wire-driven mechanism, a two-segment wire-driven mechanism and the constrained wire-driven mechanism, the workspace of the CWM is significantly expanded. It could reach any position in the volume bounded by the bending limit of the inner layer. The dexterity of the CWM is evaluated by the solid angle. By translating the base of the CWM, its workspace and dexterity are further improved. The static model is established by the Newton-Euler method. The external load is regarded as a lumped force and a bending moment at the tip. By using the static model, the bent shape of the flexible mechanism under external load could be predicted. The shape could be further measured by directly attaching optical markers to the flexible mechanism. A stereovision camera system is used to sense the spatial location of the markers and measure both the shape and twisting of the flexible mechanism. In addition, observing that the bending shape is smooth, we developed a shape estimation method using Bezier curve with the tip information. This method could well estimate the shape by using one electromagnetic sensor installed at the tip of the flexible mechanism. Furthermore, by combining the static model and the real-time shape estimation method, we developed the tip force estimation method. The second objective is to evaluate the efficacy of CWM in MIS instrumentation by: i) Develop a proof-of-concept surgical manipulator based on the CWM; ii) Evaluate the accessibility, dexterity, trajectory tracking and payload ability of the surgical manipulator experimentally. After the design and theoretical analysis of the CWM, we developed an experimental platform and a prototype. The flexible mechanism contains a pliant steel coil as the backbone. It is shared by both the inner layer and the outer layer. 3D printed spacing discs are fixed onto the coil and attached to four driving wires to form the continuum wire-driven mechanism. The outer layer is a serpentine wire-driven mechanism. It contains multiple 3D printed vertebrae with adjacent vertebrae forming a spherical joint. The vertebrae contain a central lumen that could fit the inner layer. Four wires are attached to the distal tip of the outer layer for controlling the bending motion and the stiffening/slacking. The prototype contains ten servo motors. Each of the bending layers was driven by five servo motors, with four controlling the two bending motions and one control the axial translation. The motor control was achieved using a STM32 micro processing unit. The Novint Falcon haptic device is used as the human interface. A miniature camera or biopsy forceps could be fit into the working channel of the CWM. To evaluate the performance of the CWM, a programmable channel was developed. It contains two bellows, with length, curvature and orientation adjustable. The CWM is controlled to enter the channel and follow the channel. The accessibility, dexterity and trajectory tracking capability were evaluated with the programmable channel. Last, the standard weights were added to the tip of the flexible manipulator to evaluate the payload ability. Besides these work, we also developed the flexible instruments and flexible endoscopes. Visual servo control was achieved for the flexible endoscope for tracking the instruments autonomously. A mockup cholecystectomy was performed by the visual guidance of the flexible endoscope. This further demonstrated the potential applications of the flexible mechanisms in the surgical setting.

14212316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14212316.value: In this project, we investigated a novel flexible mechanism (named as concentric wire-driven mechanism) that contains two layers of snake-like structures driven by cables. Both the inner layer and outer layer could be bent to two orthogonal directions and could be advanced axially. In addition, the outer layer could be stiffened or slacked. It served as an active constraint to the inner layer when it is stiffened. The kinematics, workspace, dexterity and trajectory tracking at load free condition were studied. Results show this mechanism could significantly expand the workspace and enhance the dexterity compared to a normal flexible mechanism with one or two segments. The bent shape of the flexible mechanism could be sensed in real time by either using the optical tracking with markers or the electromagnetic tracking using Bezier curve approximation. Statics model of the flexible mechanism was established and combined with the shape reconstruction method, tip force sensing was achieved. A proof-of-concept manipulator based on the proposed flexible mechanism was developed. Its accessibility, dexterity, trajectory tracking and payload ability was studied experimentally. It could be concluded that the concentric wire-driven mechanism is suitable for dexterous manipulations in confined spaces with small payload, such as endoscopy and thermal/electric ablation in minimally invasive surgery. The results were published in leading journals and conferences in both robotics and surgery, such as IEEE TNNLS, IEEE Access, IEEE Sensors, IEEE RA-L, ICRA, IROS, Surgical Endoscopy, etc. One PhD student and a number of undergraduate students were trained during the project.

14212316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14212316.value: The concentric wire-driven mechanism has its superiority in terms of workspace and dexterity. However, its payload remains small compared to the force requirement by surgical operations, such as organ retraction, dissection and stapling. The payload ability is majorly determined by the flexible backbone. In the current prototype, a steel coil is used which cannot well accommodate the bending and the payload requirements simultaneously. In the future, new designs on the flexible backbone could be investigated. In addition, the current size of the prototype is large for real surgical operations as the major components were 3D printed with plastic. In the future, machined parts could be used in developing the manipulator for reducing the size and improving the payload. At last, the CWM based manipulator is hyper redundant, its motion planning and human-robot-interaction are not well studied. To better control the manipulator and toward real applications, these should be investigated.

14212316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14212316.value: This project investigated a novel flexible mechanism that could work inside a confined environment, such as the surgical cavity in minimally invasive surgery. The proposed mechanism could access a wider area and is more dexterous compared to existing flexible mechanisms. We established the theoretical models for predicting the performance of the flexible mechanism, including the tip location, the accessible area, the trajectory it would cover and the load it could bear. In addition, methods of how to measure the shape of the flexible mechanism was proposed. A prototype was developed to experimentally evaluate the models and demonstrate the performance of the flexible mechanism. This research resulted in a new flexible mechanism and could be further developed into dexterous surgical manipulators that may allow surgeons accessing wider areas, avoiding critical organs, and performing surgeries with less trauma and less effort.

14212816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14212816.value: Optical interconnects are used in data centers and are proposed for use in future networks-on-chip because of the lower power consumption, higher bandwidth and increased reach they offer when compared with electrical interconnects. Data centers already make widespread use of active optical cables which employ directly modulated vertical cavity surface emitting lasers. Greater data transmission capacity can be obtained through the additional channels that are made possible by using either multiple fibers in parallel or by using dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) in a single fiber. Delivering higher data rates per optical fibers would help to reduce space requirements in data centers and avoid a proliferation of fiber cables that would increase the number of connectors in the system and reduce overall reliability. Hitherto, DWDM has been the main way of attaining higher data rates per fiber, but this results in more expensive wavelength selective architecture for the optical network because precise wavelength-control is required in the optical transmitters and wavelength-selective receivers. In the case of networks-on chip, the cost of the DWDM lasers is borne by a single end user, and thus DWDM in networks-on-chip has not yet become economically viable, in contrast to DWDM in telecommunications or data centers where the cost of DWDM is shared by many end users. Here we propose the development of an alternative approach based on single-wavelength 200 Gb/s 16-Quadrature Amplitude Modulators (16-QAM). Although 16-QAM modulators have been developed for optical telecommunications, the currently available 16-QAM modulators are expensive given the large chip area used to implement the dual cascaded travelling wave Mach-Zehnder Modulators (MZM) commonly employed in 16-QAM modulators. The proposed approach would use a more compact array of integrated electroabsorption modulators. The main advantages would be the substantially smaller chip area requirement (individual modulator lengths may be as short as 30 microns compared with the several millimeter lengths typically needed for travelling wave silicon MZM) and lower RF drive power requirements for the highly efficient electro-absorption modulators. The project would advance the state of the art in modulator technology for optical interconnects, reduce the underlying costs for optical interconnects and demonstrate a technology for high-speed and energy efficient optical interconnects for use in future networks-on-chip. 我們提出進一步發展基於集成電吸收調製器的十六位正交幅度調製（16-QAM），以應用於短距離光互聯。儘管16-QAM調製器已用於長距離光纖通信，但是現在常用的基於雙級聯行波馬赫－曾德調製器的16-QAM調製器佔用芯片面積大，導致價格昂貴。所提方案將採用更加緊湊的集成電吸收調製器陣列。該方案主要優勢在於明顯減小所需的芯片面積（與行波矽馬赫－曾德調製器數個毫米的長度相比，單個調製器長度可短至30微米）並且降低射頻驅動功率去驅動高效率的電吸收調製器。本項目將推進應用於光互聯調製器技術的發展水平，減少光互聯的基本成本並實現高速節能的光互聯技術，以應用到未來的片上網絡之中。

14212816.label: Realisation of objectives
14212816.value: We completed the first objective of this project: We designed silicon photonic integrated circuits (PICs) which used the germanium on silicon electroabsorption modulators (EAM) and had the PICs fabricated in the Multi-Project Wafer (MPW) shuttle run offered as a foundry service by IMEC. We designed dual parallel EAM circuits integrated with thermal phase shifters and waveguide grating couplers for generating 16-QAM signals by driving each EAM with a separate PAM-4 electrical modulation and introducing ninety degree optical phase shift between the two data streams. We also successfully demonstrated the use of the dual parallel EAM for other types of coherent modulation such as 4-QAM [1]. The key step in the successful generation of the 16 QAM coherent optical modulation with the EAMs was in programming the electrical modulation signal (generated by an arbitray waveform generator) to compensate for the nonlinear response of the EAM to drive voltage. By carefully mapping the precise modulation voltage for different transmission of the EAM, we were able to optimize the PAM-4 modulated signals and produce clearly open PAM-4 modulation in each EAM. 16-QAM signals were then produced in the photonic circuit by introducing exactly ninety degrees phase shift between the two branches of the parallel EAM driven to produce coherent optical 16QAM modulation. We further improved on this 16-QAM modulation scheme by adding a digital frequency shift to each of the EAM so that the complex conjugate lower frequency sidebands produced by the PAM-4 modulation in the quadrature arms complete the dual parallel EAM circuits for single sideband modulation, and this enabled the use of a single photodiode detector as a coherent optical receiver which could recover the amplitude and phase of the 16-QAM signals by use of the Kramers Kronig relationship and the Hilbert transform of the received signal [1]. The PICs we fabricated and funded by this project also included photonic circuits which were use to benchmark the performance of the EAM coherent modulators with dual parallel microring modulators for the IQ modulation instead of the EAM. Using the dual parallel microring modulators we were able to demonstrate 112Gb/s data transmission by combining 16QAM modulation with OFDM [2]. In comparison with the microring modulators, the EAM modulators had the advantage of having negative frequency chirp which could compensate for the fiber dispersion in short reach (~500m) optical interconnects and enabled a single PAM-4 driven EAMs to attain 112Gb/s data rates [3]. Both of these sets of results [3,4] were limited in data rates by the 25GHz bandwidth of the arbitrary waveform generator. In 2019 we had access to a 120Gs/s arbitrary waveform generator and were able to show that the MRM when used in a single ended configuration could reach datarates of 160Gb/s using PAM4 modulation [4]. The EAM also could attain 160Gb/s with the same drivers and by using an array of seven germanium EAMs and by driving these EAMs with the 160Gb/s PAM-4 modulation (using the same nonlinear mapping as developed for the 16QAM modulation), we were able to achieve an aggregate 1.12Tb/s data rage for transmission in a 7 core fiber [5]. The extensive testing and demonstrations, including advancing the state of art aggregate data rates per wavelength to 1.12Tb/s with the EAM reported above fully addressed the second objective of this project. In summary our experiments obtained the following key results: (i) the germanium EAM could produce negative frequency chirp during PAM4 modulation and this gave negative power penalty for the 112Gb/s data transmission because the frequency chirp introduced by the EAM compensated the optical dispersion in the 500m transmission fiber [3]. (ii) The data rates attained with the EAM were comparable with the use of the optimized microring modulators, and in our initial experiments it was limited by the bandwidth of the drive electronics. Our initial experiments demonstrated 80Gb/s 16 QAM optical modulation with the dual parallel EAM photonic integrated circuit [1] (iii) Later, when higher bandwidth drivers became available to us we were able to demonstrate 160Gb/s PAM-4 modulation in the EAM. However we did not have the 80Gbaud coherent optical receivers to test successfully the 320Gb/s 16QAM modulation with the dual parallel EAM photonic circuit. (iv) Nonetheless we were able to demonstrate a record breaking 1.12Tb/s single wavelength optical interconnect by using the integrated array of 7 EAM, each driven with digitally equalized PAM-4 signals, and transmitting the data over 7 core fiber for direct detection [5] We believe this result sets a new world record in the bandwidth density per wavelength of 1.38 Tbit/s per square mm of area of the silicon photonic transmitter. 14212816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14212816.value: The main results from this project include: (i) Germanium-on-silicon waveguide electroabsorption modulators (EAM) can be used for PAM-4 modulation, and produce negative frequency chirp which can compensate for the optical fiber dispersion in 500m of single mode fiber for 112Gb/s PAM 4 data modulation [3] (ii) Photonic integrated circuits with two EAMs in parallel and with an optical phase shift of ninety degrees between the two modulators can be used for 16-QAM optical modulation by driving each of the EAM with an independent PAM-4 data channel. [1] (iii) Single sideband modulation using the dual parallel EAM photonic circuit can be readily implemented by adding a frequency shift in the drive electronics so that the lower sideband of the PAM-4 signals from I and Q branches of the vector modulator are 180 degrees out of phase. We demonstrated that this approach can enable the dual parallel EAM to be used for coherent optical modulation with the optical carrier included in the transmitted signal satisfying the mimumum phase requirements of Kramers Kronig coherent optical receivers [1,2]. This will have a major advantage in enabling the use of direct detection photodiode (without any additional local oscillator laser) for measuring the amplitude and phase of the modulated signal, and thus reduce the cost of coherent optical receivers for their future use in data centers. (iv) Germanium on silicon waveguide EAMs are very small in size and enabled the demonstration of a silicon photonic transmitter with the highest bandwidth density of 1.38Tb/s per square mm of the transmitter chip in this project. Using seven EAMs in an array for modulating the 160Gb/s PAM-4 signals we attained an aggregate data rate of 1.12 Tb/s from the silicon transmitter with a single wavelength laser and transmitted the data over a short length of multicore optical fiber [5].

14212816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14212816.value: Our published results, advancing the datarates possible with EAMs integrated in photonic circuits bto beyond 1 terabit/s per wavelength have attracted interest from many groups and industry. We were invited to present our results at one of the major forums for industry in the International Solid State Circuits Conference 2021 (to be held online on 22 February 2021), and we have received inquiries from industry about the potential for developing this technology further for commercial products.

14212816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14212816.value: This project advanced the state of the art in the data transmission capacity and data density of silicon photonic transmitters by using the germanium on silicon waveguide electroabsorption modulators in photonic circuits. We demonstrated 160Gb/s with a single electroabsorption modulator, and by using an array of 7 EAM in a dense photonic circuit we attained an aggregate 1.12Tb/s data rate transmission per wavelength, with a world record bandwidth density of 1.38Tb/s per square mm of the photonic chip. The 1.12Tb/s data transmission was demonstrated experimentally on a single multicore optical fiber.

14213616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213616.value: Intelligent video analysis has a broad range of applications in video surveillance, multimedia and social networks, closely related to the public security and development of Hong Kong. The goal of this project is to develop new deep learning models to learn generic appearance and dynamic feature presentations from large-scale videos. Such generic feature representations can be effectively applied to various vision tasks related to video analysis and boost their performance substantially. Deep learning achieves great success in computer vision. An important discovery is that generic appearance representations can be learned by deep models from large-scale static image sets such as ImageNet and can be effectively applied to various vision tasks which only have small training data. They serve as powerful engines to drive the progress of many vision problems. However, there is still no effective way of learning both generic appearance and dynamic representations for video analysis yet. Existing approaches treat deep learning as a blackbox and apply CNN to 3D video volume in a straightforward way, while ignoring the fundamental difference between the temporal dimension and spatial dimensions. They either introduce many redundant connections between neurons, which increase model complexity and make training inefficient, or lose much dynamic information at the input layer. We propose new deep models which learn both generic appearance and dynamic feature representations for videos. The model design is inspired by understanding the spatial-temporal structures of video volume and the semantic meanings of neural responses. The model complexity is largely reduced by adding effective regularity which separates appearance and dynamic representations in the filter design and also keeps proper interactions between them at multiple layers. Specifically, the model design is based on the decomposition of 3D video volume and its 3D feature maps into 2D image and 2D temporal-slice representations. In the new model, 3D filters are approximated with a set of 2D image filters and 2D temporal-slice filters, which implicitly add regularity on filter learning and lead to sparse networks. When temporal-slice filters are applied to 3D feature maps generated by image filters at different layers, they extract dynamic representations of different semantic units, such as groups, objects, parts and distinctive patches. The outcome of this project will have substantial impact since learning generic appearance and dynamic representations from videos is a fundamental problem in computer vision and deep learning. 14213616.label: Realisation of objectives
14213616.value: All the objectives of this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have studied deep learning visual representations given temporal slices as inputs and investigate dynamic information captured by filters learned at different layers. Given each video, we first reshape and decompose the videos into a collection of different 2D xy-, xt-, and yt-temporal slices. The three different types of slices would be input into 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models to obtain feature cuboids to capture information in different dimensions. Recognition of video attribute is achieved by appending a classifier on the concatenated feature vector extracted from the feature maps of xy-, xt-, and yt-representations. (2) We have studied selectiveness of image filters on object, and investigate how the movements of different semantic units are encoded in the feature maps generated at different layers. Previous studies have shown that the spatial filters in 2D CNNs on image-related tasks possess strong selectiveness on patterns corresponding to object categories and object identities. Specifically, the feature map obtained by a spatial filter at one intermediate layer of a deep model records the spatial distribution of visual pattern of a specific object. We conducted human study to investigate the selectiveness of the spatio-temporal feature maps. Based on the observations, we actually exploit such feature cuboids to separately monitor the movements of different object categories, both spatially and temporally, while reducing the interference caused by the background clutter and irrelevant objects. (3) We have developed a deep learning model which approximates 3D filters with a set of 2D image filters and 2D temporal-slice filters. Deep learning models for 3D video analysis were created by using 2D image filters and 2D temporal slice filters to approximate the 3D filters. Our final model adopts three such 2D CNN branches to capture xy-, xt-, yt-features and concatenate them into joint feature representations for final video analysis and classification. (4) We have developed a deep learning model which applies temporal-slice filters to the 3D feature maps generated with image filters at different layers to extract dynamic representations of different semantic units. Previous studies typically learn dynamic features from raw video volumes or hand-crafted motion maps. However, much information is lost at the input layer since they compress the entire temporal range by subsampling frames or averaging spatial feature maps along the time dimension. Indeed, dynamic feature representations can also be described from 2D temporal slices that cut across 3D volume from another two orthogonal planes, as spatio-temporal slices. It is a general case that an xt- or yt-slice captured from a raw video volume contains motion patterns of multiple objects of different categories, which cannot be well separated since the features that identify these categories always refer to appearance but not motion. Motivated by this observation, we propose semantic temporal slice extracted from semantic feature cuboids, which are obtained from the xy convolutional layers. Such kind of slices can distinguish and purify the dynamic representation for a certain semantic pattern without the interference from other objects, instances or visual patterns inside one temporal slice. (5) We have applied the developed deep models and the obtained feature representations to tasks related to video analysis. The proposed 3D CNN model and the learned spatio-temporal feature representations can be used for video-related vision tasks. In (Part C.8 No. 1), we have applied learned video representations for conducting online multi-object tracking. The proposed Deep Continuous Conditional Random Field is built upon our learned spatio-temporal representations, which consists of unary and pairwise terms. The unary terms estimate tracked objects’ displacements across time based on visual appearance information. The asymmetric pairwise terms model inter-object relations in an asymmetric way. In (Part C.8 No. 2), we have used the video representations for object detection from videos. We propose a deep learning framework that incorporates temporal and contextual information from tubelets obtained in videos, which dramatically improves the baseline performance of existing still-image detection frameworks when they are applied to videos.

14213616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14213616.value: As research outcomes, 2 journal papers and 30 conference papers were published. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology is one of the top journals on video analysis and understanding. 30 papers were published on top conferences on computer vision and machine learning (CVPR, ICCV, and ECCV). Based on the learned temporal representations, we have proposed a series of research methods for various video-related applications. Object detection and tracking from videos. In (Part C.9 No. 4), we observe that previous methods have major limitations in generating high-quality tubelets for object detection from videos. Motion-based methods are able to obtain dense tubelets efficiently, but the lengths are generally only several frames. In this work, we propose a framework for object detection from videos, which consists of a novel tubelet proposal network to efficiently generate spatiotemporal proposals to incorporates temporal information from tubelet proposals for achieving high object detection accuracy in videos. In (Part C.8 No.2), we found that simply applying single object tracker for MOT will encounter the problem in computational efficiency and drifted results caused by occlusion. We propose a new framework that introduces spatial-temporal attention mechanism (STAM) to handle the drift caused by occlusion and interaction among targets. The visibility map of the target is learned and used for inferring the spatial attention map. The spatial attention map is then applied to weight the features. Besides, the occlusion status can be estimated from the visibility map, which controls the online updating process via weighted loss on training samples with different occlusion statuses in different frames. Spatio-temporal object re-identification. Object re-identification aims to identify the same object across different cameras. In (Part C.9 No. 11), we tackle the problem of spatio-temporal vehicle re-identification. we propose a two-stage framework that incorporates complex spatio-temporal information for effectively regularizing the re-identification results. Given a pair of vehicle images with their spatiotemporal information, a candidate visual-spatio-temporal path is first generated by a chain MRF model with a deeply learned potential function. A Siamese-CNN+PathLSTM model takes the candidate path as well as the pairwise queries to generate their similarity score. In (Part C.9 No. 14), we address the problem of video-based person re-identification. Our approach divides long sequences into multiple short video snippets and aggregates the top-ranked snippet similarities for sequence-similarity estimation. With this strategy, the intra-person variation of each sample could be minimized for similarity estimation, while the diverse appearance and temporal information are maintained.

14213616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14213616.value: In this project, we presented and studied novel temporal slicing techniques for video understanding, with only 2D filters. We show that the spatial (xy-) filters capture appearance information, while temporal-slice (xt- and yt-) filters capture dynamic cues like speed and acceleration in x- and y-directions respectively. We will further purse this research direction to investigate how to better purne the spatio-temporal filters according to their importance. We will further explore more strategies on feature cuboids selection in the future. More video related applications based on temporal slicing CNN will also be studied.

14213616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14213616.value: In this project, we propose new deep models that learn dynamic representations, and effectively combine them with appearance features for video analysis. We propose a novel spatio-temporal Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), based on the decomposition of 3D convolutions into 2D spatio- and 2D temporal-slices operations. The decomposition has distinct advantages: (1) the model is capable of capturing dynamics of general objects and persons in the scene, (2) it learns to disentangle appearance and dynamic representations while keeping the proper interactions between them, and (3) it utilizes the selectiveness of spatial filters to discard irrelevant background clutter to achieve more accurate video understanding and analysis. The learned video representations can be widely used for different video understanding tasks. The final results show improved video representations and performances on multiple public benchmarks.

14213716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14213716.value: Optimization theory and methodologies have demonstrated their prowess in virtually every industrial and managerial field, and the past five decades have witnessed countless success of their applications. Among various categories of optimization formulations and methodologies, except for linear programming, quadratic programming has found the widest spectra of applications, as it captures one inherent feature of the nature, nonlinearity, in its simplest possible form. The quadratically constrained quadratic programming (QCQP) problem formulation represents one of the most important subclasses of non-convex programming problems, and remains as a great challenge in front of the optimization community. This research project seeks to advance the state of the art of QCQP in both theoretical and methodological aspects. While the current literature reveals that the generalized trust region subproblem (GTRS) admits a semi-definite programming (SDP) reformulation in general, the relatively large computational complexity of SDP algorithms prevents them from scaling to large-scale problems. We aim to prove in our research a significant theoretical result: All GTRSs with a finite optimal solution admit a second-order-cone programming (SOCP) reformulation. Compared to the SDP representation of GTRS, the SOCP representation delivers a much faster solution algorithm, which could have profound impact for nonlinear programming algorithm design for large-scale problems. We also expect to extend this result to GTRSs with equality constraint or that with interval constraint. Identifying a global optimal solution of QCQP is generally NP-hard. While the current literature focuses on finding a high-quality convex relaxation with a small duality gap, the state-of-the-art methodology lacks valid inequalities for nonconvex quadratic constraints (other than direct linearization). Our goal in this project is to develop a novel and tight convex relaxation by extending the state-of-the-art of the SOC-RLT scheme to nonconvex constraints, thus enhancing the computability in solving nonconvex QCQP and generalizing the applicability of QCQP formulations. Chance constrained quadratic programming (CCQP) is a special class of mixed integer QCQP and finds its direct application in portfolio selection. Dealing directly with CCQP in branch-and-bound frameworks often does not yield good performance because the bound generated from its continuous relaxation could be very loose. Our challenging task in this project is to identify the best linearly constrained QP reformulation of CCQP whose continuous relaxation provides a tight bound and which can be effectively solved by standard MIQP solvers.
