14215416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14215416.value: Driven by the diminishing land-based resources, competition for undersea resource exploration and excavation has significantly intensified in recent years. High-speed underwater wireless communication systems are essential to enable environment-conscious exploration of marine resources and the monitoring of environmental conditions. Besides, the ever-growing traffic flow and the emerging self-driving cars also call for efficient wireless communication solutions to share real-time information of traffic and neighboring cars’ status and surrounding views. Visible light, in particular, blue/green light, exhibits smaller attenuation in water compared to other wavelengths, making it a favorable carrier for underwater data transmission. Furthermore, LEDs have been widely used as traffic lights, automobile’s head lights, and diver’s helmet lights. By reusing LEDs, visible light communication (VLC) enables ubiquitous and seamless network connectivity for underwater and intelligent transportation systems (ITS). In the literature, single-user static point-to-point VLC systems have been widely investigated. However, the study of VLC and networking in mobile environment is still in its infancy, thus requiring further extensive research. In this project, we will investigate high-speed mobile VLC systems for underwater and ITS applications, by leveraging the expertise gained through our previous works on advanced optical signal processing, burst-mode receivers (BMRs), optical physical layer networking and preliminary studies on VLC systems. We will systematically investigate VLC-based mobile underwater and ITS, from the modulation, coding, detection and networking schemes to the field-programmable gate array (FPGA) based real-time system implementation and optimization. The former focuses on modulation formats, coding, detection and networking schemes in the presence of terminal mobility and other environmental factors in the target applications (in particular artificial light, sunlight, water attenuation and turbulence), and aims to identify the optimal solution that can be adapted to these applications with minimized complexity to realize preferable system performance. The latter verifies and further optimizes system-level algorithms and designs at the register transfer level for FPGA designs and implements real-time testing. The project not only maintains a high-quality scientific program investigating novel designs, but also promotes early-stage transfer of innovation to industry to improve the competitiveness of the economy. This proposal is strategically important to Hong Kong, a coastal city with high population density and heavy traffic load, as it has natural advantages to establish sustainable marine resource exploration and intelligent transportation systems. The work will also enhance the research collaborations internally and with overseas institutes, Sharif University of Technology and Zhejiang University, for the development of underwater optical communication systems. 由於陸上資源的逐年減少，近年來對於海底資源的探測及開採的競爭愈演愈烈。而要實現可靠的水下資源探測及環境監測，高速的水下無線通信系統至關重要。此外，日漸擁堵的交通以及近來提出的無人駕駛均需要一種高速有效的無線通信技術來保證交通信息、鄰近車輛行駛狀態及視野等信息的實時共享。可見光，尤其是藍/錄光，相對其他波長的光而言，在水下傳輸的衰減較小，因而成為較佳的水下通信的傳輸媒介。而且，LED被廣泛地應用于交通燈，汽車尾燈及潛水員頭燈等。通過對LED發射燈光的調製，可見光通信可以實現水下及智能交通系統的無縫網絡連接。對於單用戶靜態可見光通信系統目前已有較多的研究，然而對於移動環境下可見光通信系統及網絡性能仍需要深入的研究。 基於課題組此前關於先進光信號處理、突發模式接收機、光網絡層編碼的研究經驗以及可見光通信的初步研究結果，本項目旨在系統地研究水下及智能交通應用中移動式高速可見光通信系統的性能，涵蓋（1）調製，編碼，接收及網絡技術、以及（2）基於FPGA的實時系統的實現和優化。前者主要研究在終端移動性以及人工光源、水下衰減及湍流等因素下，可見光通信的水下及智能交通通信系統的性能，旨在探究低複雜度的前提下，性能最佳的最優方案。後者則通過基於FPGA的實時通信系統的實現，驗證以及進一步優化系統層級的算法和寄存器層級的FPGA系統設計。本課題不僅是研究新型技術及系統設計的科研項目，同時也能夠促進新型技術向工業應用的轉化，進而提升經濟的競爭力。 本課題對於香港具有重要意義，因其作為港口城市，人口眾多、交通負荷高，擁有天然的優勢建立可持續的水下資源探測及智能交通系統。同時，本課題將提升與海外院校，即謝里夫理工大學和浙江大學，關於水下無線光通信系統方面的合作研究。

14215416.label: Realisation of objectives
14215416.value: [Realization of Objective 1] We have studied the channel characteristics with experimental investigations on single- and multi-user VLC systems with terminal mobility. We have also investigated the environmental effects on the optical link for the underwater scenario, such as air bubbles. • We first implemented a Monte-Carlo ray-tracing method to investigate the channel characteristics of a VLC channel. The results were incorporated for the channel modeling of the VLC-based underwater and intelligent transportation system (ITS) in our following works. Furthermore, we developed an Arduino-based platform, with which the moving distance and moving speed of a VLC transmitter/receiver, i.e., the time-varying channel characteristics, can be controlled. We investigated the channel characteristics in the form of the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of BER distributions with precisely controlled moving distance and moving speed of a VLC user [C8]. We showed that the optical channel condition degrades with the increase of the receiver’s moving speed in terms of the average and the variance of the received optical power. • We have simulated the effects of bubbles on the underwater light propagation with the Monte-Carlo simulation of a Gaussian beam. Experimental investigation on the bubble-induced performance degradation for UOWC with different bubble sizes and positions was studied in SISO and MIMO systems [J6]. The statistics of bubbles were analyzed (size and number distribution) using the developed image-based edge detection method. The communication link performance in terms of BERs under different bubble distribution and relative location with respect to the transmitter was investigated and analyzed in terms of the probability density function (PDF) of the BERs. [Realization of Objective 2] • In [C8], we investigated the use of spatial diversity to mitigate the receiver’s mobility-induced impairments in mobi-VLC and experimentally demonstrated enhanced robustness in different mobility scenarios. In [J6], it was also experimentally verified that spatial diversity could significantly reduce the BER fluctuation and increases the link stability for a UWOC system with the impairment of air bubbles. • We proposed and demonstrated a real-valued OCT precoding for optical FOFDM [C6]. While achieving CSI-free linear equalization, the proposed precoding exhibited a uniform signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) profile over subcarriers. Consequently, the high-frequency fading issue of fast-OFDM based VLC could be resolved, leading to significant BER performance improvement. Furthermore, by theoretical analysis and experimental verifications, it was found that the equalized SNR level approached the harmonic mean of the original SNRs over the subcarriers. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme was experimentally verified by 2-ary/4-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) optical fast-OFDM with different baud rates. Results showed that more than 35% capacity enhancement could be achieved for 4.2-Gbit/s transmission over 2-m length. • We also proposed the first adaptively-loaded DCT-based PAM-Fast OFDM [C5]. A simple yet effective signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) threshold-based adaptive bit and power loading algorithm for PAM-fast-OFDM was proposed, and its effectiveness was experimentally verified. It was demonstrated that similar to the adaptively-loaded QAM-OFDM, a ladder-like SNR profile could also be obtained for the PAM-fast-OFDM by using the proposed loading algorithm, resulting in significantly reduced BER. Experimental results showed that a data rate of 5.2-Gbit/s transmission could be achieved, with capacity enhancement of ~44%. • We proposed and experimentally demonstrated the first probabilistically-shaped CAP (PS-CAP) for a high-speed optical wireless communication system [C7]. For a 12.5-Gbit/s transmission, ~1-dB sensitivity improvement was achieved. The proposed PS-CAP enables the ability of capacity maximization for CAP-based systems. We further proposed a capacity-approaching scheme via joint probabilistic shaping (PS) and precoding in the OWC system [J3]. Different from the bit-and-power- and entropy-loading schemes, the proposed scheme only required one modulation format with one single-PS distribution while offering the ability to maximize the system’s throughput. Moreover, we showed that the proposed scheme also exhibited superior spectral efficiency (SE) and generalized mutual information (GMI) performances. As a result, the implementation complexity was significantly reduced without affecting the capacity-approaching capability. We showed that for a 36-Gbit/s OWC transmission, ∼5 dB improvement in the received optical power (ROP) sensitivity could be achieved by using the proposed scheme. • We proposed a low-complexity and effective joint transmitter-side digital signal processing (DSP) that includes geometric shaping, time-domain tone reservation (TR), and clipping [J8][C9] for a water-air communication system. We developed a real-time 2.2-Gb/s system, which was optimized for its shaping ratio and clipping ratio. With the help of the efficient DSPs, an 8-dB received optical power enhancement was realized under the bit-error-rate threshold of 3.8×10-3. We also successfully demonstrated a time-multiplexed four 4K video transmission in real-time using the proposed scheme over a 3.6-m underwater and 8-m free-space channel. The implementation details, as well as the analysis of system stability, resource utilization, and latency, were presented. The results validated the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed scheme and a 2.2-Gbit/s real-time OWC system was demonstrated for a water-air communication link. • We also extended our work on different peak-to-average ratio (PAPR) reduction schemes for the OFDM-based VLC system [J2], bit-loaded multi-band orthogonal circulant matrix transform (MB-OCT) precoding scheme [J4], a generalized Discrete-Circulant-Transform Spread OFDM scheme [J5], and an adaptive physical-layer network coding (APNC) for VLC-based two-way relay (TWR) networks [J7].

14215416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14215416.value: In this project, we systematically investigated VLC-based mobile systems and UOWC systems. We modeled and experimentally investigated the effects of mobility and environmental factors on channel characteristics. We proposed and experimentally demonstrated novel schemes to improve the robustness and overall throughputs for underwater and inter-vehicle applications. Some major findings are as follows. We investigated the channel distribution in a VLC system by developing an adaptive moving platform with programmable distance and user moving speed [C8]. This enables the first study of terminal mobility effects in the VLC system. We showed that the optical channel condition degrades with the increase of the receiver’s moving speed in terms of the average and the variance of the received optical power. We also showed that the use of different spatial diversity schemes could enhance robustness in different mobility scenarios. The space-time block code offers superior tolerance to the variation of the user’s moving speed. Submarine air bubbles can have a significant impact on the underwater light propagation and the corresponding optical communication links, but the effects have not been systematically investigated. We developed a simulation model for an optical link under the influences of air bubbles. The BER performances under different bubble distributions and the relative location were investigated and analyzed [J6]. It was experimentally verified that a MIMO system could significantly reduce the BER fluctuation and increases the link stability. We have developed novel signal processing schemes with low complexity, facilitating cost- and complexity-sensitive underwater/ITS applications. A real-valued orthogonal circulant matrix transform precoding scheme was proposed to provide data rate improvement with relatively low complexity [C6]. An adaptively-loaded DCT-based Fast OFDM scheme was proposed to boost the capacity [C5] further. We introduced a low-complexity and effective joint transmitter-side digital signal processing (DSP) for the underwater-air communication system [C9]. An 8-dB received optical power enhancement was realized, which can potentially increase the transmission distance. We also successfully demonstrated a time-multiplexed four 4K video transmissions in real-time using a proposed scheme that combined geometric shaping and tone reservation with clipping over a 3.6-m underwater and 8-m free-space channel, confirming the effectiveness for underwater-air scenarios. An adaptive physical-layer network coding scheme in a two-way relay network was proposed and experimentally demonstrated to solve the blocking issue for a mobile system [J7]. The research outputs were presented in conferences and journals. The investigations not only provide high-quality scientific researches but also support smooth transfers to practical applications.

14215416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14215416.value: For the mobile-VLC system, real-time investigations of the transmission performance can be conducted in the future. Moreover, a prototype can be developed using a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). The proposed adaptive network-coding scheme and spatial-diversity scheme can be implemented and validated in real-time systems. For underwater communication applications, it is desired to establish an optical network for the underwater and terrestrial platforms to accommodate multi-user scenarios. For an FSO-UOWC convergence system that exhibits a water-air link, the channel model of underwater turbulence combined with atmospheric turbulence should be studied, and novel modulation techniques are needed for the convergent system. The wave effect on the transmission can be modeled properly to help develop a suitable beam steering scheme. A properly designed light tracking system will be a possible solution to mitigate the issue. The change of the wavefront of the laser beam through waves can be compensated at the transmitter side using spatial light modulator and feedback signals. The study of VLC and networking in an FSO-UOWC convergence system with environment turbulence entails further research.

14215416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14215416.value: In recent years, there is an increasing demand for undersea resource exploration and excavation. High-speed underwater communication systems are vital for efficiently exploring marine resources and monitoring environmental conditions. Visible light communication has great potential for submarine applications due to its unique advantages of low transmission loss compared to that of the radio-frequency and acoustic communications. Moreover, the VLC-based system can also provide seamless connectivity for intelligent transportation systems by reusing the LEDs of the traffic lights and automobile’s headlights. The channel with turbulence effect and terminals’ mobility are the most challenging issues for these scenarios. We modeled and studied some of the environment-induced impairments, such as user mobility, turbulence, and air bubble effects. We have also proposed and investigated several novel schemes to mitigate these impairments. These include spatial diversity, adaptive bit/power loading, and physical-layer network coding. Meanwhile, low complexity was also taken into consideration to achieve a higher data rate for the low-cost and low-power-consumption VLC applications. Experimental results show that the proposed schemes are robust to the aforementioned environmental effects and can boost the throughput of the VLC system. This will greatly enhance the chance of successful deployment of future VLC underwater and ITS systems.

14216316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14216316.value: To maintain data availability against failures, today's data centers introduce redundancy to data storage via erasure coding, which emerges as a practical redundancy mechanism that provides higher fault tolerance with much less storage redundancy than traditional replication, thereby significantly saving the operational costs for data centers. Erasure coding has been widely studied in the literature in the context of storage systems. One special class of erasure coding is called regenerating codes, which minimize the amount of network traffic transferred for failure repair. However, the seamless deployment of regenerating codes in data centers remains complicated, mainly because data centers are inherently hierarchical by arranging storage nodes in groups of racks. We observe that existing regenerating codes, as well as most erasure codes in the literature, inevitably trigger substantial cross-rack network traffic in repair, while cross-rack bandwidth is an over-subscribed resource in data centers. In this research, we propose to adapt regenerating codes to address the hierarchical nature of data centers. Our preliminary study proposes double regenerating codes, whose idea is to perform encoding at both node and rack levels during repair. We show via theoretical analysis that double regenerating codes minimize the amount of cross-rack network traffic for both single-node and single-rack failure repairs, while minimizing the storage redundancy. Our findings on double regenerating codes open many important research directions, including the analysis of double regenerating codes for general scenarios, as well as real-world implementation and experimentation. The contributions of this research will enable enterprises to effectively manage the big data storage of data centers with the guarantees of fault tolerance, repair efficiency, and storage efficiency. 為了維持在故障發生時數據的可用性，現今的數據中心通過糾刪碼作為一種實用的冗餘機制，它不但提供了更高的容錯性，同時比傳統的複製存儲冗餘要少得多，因此顯著節省了數據中心的運營成本。 糾刪碼式的存儲系統在文獻中已被廣泛研究。再生碼為當中一類特別的糾刪碼，能證明其最小化傳輸故障修復的網絡流量。然而，在數據中心上再生碼的部署依然很複雜，主要是因為數據中心是以分層方法由機架組安排存儲節點。我們觀察到現有的再生碼，以及最新的糾刪碼，無可避免地在故障修復過程中引起明顯的交叉機架網絡流量，而跨架帶寬是數據中心裡的瓶頸資源。 在這項研究中，我們提出以再生碼為基礎，以解決分層數據中心的性質。我們的初步研究提出"雙再生碼"，其想法是透過兩個階段的修復，進行節點和機架級別編碼。我們通過理論分析雙再生碼能減少單節點修復和單機架修復的交叉機架網絡流量，同時達到最小化存儲冗餘。我們雙再生碼的發現開闢了許多重要的研究方向，包括一般情況下的雙再生碼的分析，以及真實環境的實踐和試驗。 這項研究將使企業能夠有效地管理大數據的數據存儲與容錯，維修效率，和存儲效率。

14216316.label: Realisation of objectives
14216316.value: (i) Objective 1 [General code constructions]: We have derived several code constructions for hierarchical data centers. We propose two families of Double Regenerating Codes (DRC) [TOS'17], which not only minimize the cross-rack repair traffic but also have several practical properties that improve state-of-the-art regenerating codes. The supported parameters cover a wide range of practical scenarios. Also, we characterize the optimal trade-off curve between storage redundancy and cross-rack repair bandwidth specifically for hierarchical data centers. We propose a general family of erasure codes called rack-aware regenerating codes (RRC) that achieve the optimal trade-off [TIT'19]. We identify two extreme points, the minimum-storage rack-aware regenerating (MSRR) point and the minimum-bandwidth rack-aware regenerating (MBRR) point. Our RRC constructions support a wide range of parameters and are shown to achieve less cross-rack repair bandwidth than the classical regenerating codes without rack awareness. Along this direction, we propose an exact-repair constructions for the MSRR codes that have better computational complexity with small sub-packetization [ISIT'20]. Furthermore, we propose repair-efficient techniques that work for general erasure codes (e.g., Reed-Solomon codes or any linear erasure codes), including fast predictive repair [DSN'19], cross-rack-aware recovery scheme [TDSC'20]. Besides repair operations, we also propose the cross-rack-aware update scheme that reduces the cross-rack update traffic in hierarchical data centers and works for general erasure codes [ICPP'18, TPDS'20]. (ii) Objective 2 [General bandwidth constraints]: We consider the heterogeneous environments where the link bandwidth varies across different links. We propose the repair pipelining technique [TOS'20] that finds an optimal path that minimizes the maximum link cost over a repair path. We show that repair pipelining significantly reduces the repair time. It also works for hierarchical data centers, such that it minimizes the cross-rack repair traffic and the overall repair time. (iii) Objective 3 [General failure patterns]: We consider general failure patterns aside fail-stop failures. We consider stragglers (i.e., nodes with slow performance). We propose POCache [MSST'19], a parity-only caching scheme that provides robust straggler tolerance without relying on timely and accurate straggler detection, while incurring limited redundancy overhead by caching only parity chunks. Furthermore, state-of-the-art repair-efficient schemes mostly focus on optimizing the single-failure repair performance. We extend our repair pipelining scheme [TOS'20] to address concurrent failures (i.e., multiple chunk failures in the same stripe), such that the repair time for the concurrent failures is reduced to almost the normal read time for the same number of blocks. (iv) Objective 4 [Reliability analysis]: We study via reliability analysis regarding the trade-off between minimizing the cross-rack repair bandwidth and the storage reliability under concurrent failures, in which we consider the case where a fraction of nodes are crashed simultaneously (e.g., due to power outages). Our reliability analysis shows that minimizing the cross-rack repair bandwidth actually improves the storage reliability provided that the fraction of failed nodes under concurrent failures is within a practical range [TOS'17]. We further build a discrete-event simulator, SimEDC, which can report reliability metrics for an erasure-coded data center deployed in general settings [SRDS'17, TPDS'19]. (v) Objective 5 [Implementation and experimentation in data centers]: We have built several prototypes that realize high repair performance for erasure-coded data centers. Such prototypes are also successfully integrated into Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS). They include: (i) DoubleR [TOS'17], which realizes Double Regenerating Codes, (ii) ECPipe [ATC'17, TOS'20], which realizes repair pipelining for erasure-coded data centers and has been evaluated extensively on Amazon EC2, (iii) OpenEC [FAST'19], which provides a unified framework for erasure coding deployment, (iv) POCache [MSST'19], which provides robust straggler tolerance, and (v) FastPR [DSN'19], which realizes fast predictive repair. In particular, our OpenEC prototype [FAST'19] can easily integrate Double Regenerating Codes (DRC) [TOS'17] and repair pipelining [ATC'17, TOS'20] into hierarchical data centers with limited code changes to HDFS. (vi) Additional objectives: We further study other fundamental aspects of deploying erasure codes and regenerating codes in data centers. In particular, we consider storage scaling, which refers to the conversion of coding parameters of erasure-coded storage. Our work includes optimal scaling via information flow graph analysis [INFOCOM'18, ISIT'18, INFOCOM'20] and I/O-efficient scaling [SRDS'20]. In particular, our analysis [INFOCOM'20] shows the fundamental trade-off between repair and scaling performance in hierarchical data centers. We also propose Elastic Reed-Solomon (ERS) codes [SRDS'20] that supports I/O-efficient scaling in erasure-coded key-value stores; the work received the best paper award at IEEE SRDS'20 (1 out of 131 submissions). Undergraduate student training: In this project, we hired one undergraduate student in 2017-18 to conduct research on deploying erasure coding technologies in distributed storage systems. The student is responsible for the following tasks: (1) analyzing the source code of the storage systems (all of them are open-sourced); (2) identifying the parts of the source code that should be revised to support efficient erasure coding technologies; (3) conducting preliminary testing on the performance of the storage systems when erasure coding is enabled. We believe that the student has received substantial training to conduct large-scale systems research. The student's findings on distributed storage systems also inspire us in future research.

14216316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14216316.value: We explore several areas of research to improve the current erasure coding deployment in hierarchical data centers, where the cross-rack bandwidth is limited. (I) Optimal erasure code constructions. We propose optimal erasure code constructions that minimize the cross-rack repair bandwidth subject to different constraints, including Double Regenerating Codes [TOS'17] and Rack-aware Regenerating Codes [TIT'19, ISIT'20]. In particular, we characterize the optimal trade-off curve between the storage redundancy and the cross-rack repair bandwidth, and show that the cross-rack repair bandwidth is often lower than the classical regenerating codes [TIT'19]. (II) Repair-efficient techniques. We propose various repair-efficient techniques that work for general erasure codes. They include repair pipelining [ATC'17, TOS'20], fast predictive repair [DSN'19], and cross-rack-aware recovery [TDSC'20]. We also study straggler tolerance, and propose parity-only caching that maintains access performance in the presence of stragglers while incurring limited redundancy overhead by caching only parity chunks. (III) Update-efficient techniques. We propose update-efficient techniques for hierarchical data centers [ICPP'18, TPDS'20], and show that we can reduce the cross-rack update traffic by carefully scheduling the update operations. (IV) Reliability analysis. We develop a simulator SimEDC that characterizes the storage reliability subject to the trade-off between minimizing the cross-rack repair traffic and reducing rack-level fault tolerance [SRDS'17, TPDS'19]. Our SimEDC simulator is designed to generally support different erasure coding parameters, topology configurations, as well as failure and repair patterns. (V) Implementation and prototyping. We have implemented several prototypes that realize erasure coding for hierarchical data centers [TOS'17, ATC'17, FAST'19, MSST'19, DSN'19, TOS'20]. Our OpenEC prototype [FAST'19] provides a unified configurable framework that can easily deploy erasure coding solutions into existing distributed storage systems, such as HDFS and QuantcastFS (QFS). All the prototypes are now open-sourced.

14216316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14216316.value: We believe that the erasure coding deployment in hierarchical data centers still has many open issues. In particular, non-volatile memory (NVM) architectures are increasingly deployed. How to properly deploy erasure coding in a hybrid architecture with hard-disk drives (HDDs) and NVM drives is an interesting direction. Also, we are currently looking into storage scaling on how to dynamically adapt the coding parameters based on the current workload and reliability characteristics. Our recent studies [INFOCOM'18, ISIT'18, INFOCOM'20, SRDS'20] provide preliminary results on storage scaling. Finally, we explore the integration of erasure coding with deduplication, which is a compression technique that has been widely used to reduce storage overhead. Combining erasure coding and deduplication can provide new opportunities to achieve high storage savings in the face of massive amounts of data in the wild.

14216316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14216316.value: To maintain data availability against failures, today's data centers deploy erasure coding as a practical low-cost redundancy mechanism for fault tolerance. However, the seamless deployment of erasure coding in data centers remains complicated, mainly because data centers are inherently hierarchical by arranging storage nodes in groups of racks. We observe that existing erasure coding schemes inevitably trigger substantial cross-rack network traffic in repair. In this research, we propose to adapt regenerating codes to address the hierarchical nature of data centers. We propose optimal erasure code constructions on minimizing cross-rack repair traffic, as well as design repair-efficient and update-efficient techniques that work for general erasure codes in hierarchical data centers. We also characterize the storage reliability when erasure coding is deployed in hierarchical data centers. Our findings are backed by rigorous theoretical analysis as well as empirical analysis real-world distributed storage systems. We have published a number of papers in prestigious conferences and journals on our findings; our prototypes have also been released as open-source software.

14217516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14217516.value: Due to the stylish, lively presentation of hand-drawn cel animation, traditional hand-drawn animation remains one major way to produce cartoons, regardless of the advancement of computer graphics. However, animators cannot draw stereo-frames by hand, making its stereoscopic version hard to produce. A recent technological advancement can automate the stereoscopic conversion of 2D hand-drawn animation, but heavily relies on the accuracy of region correspondence estimation among frames. However the region correspondence estimation remains an open research problem due to the non-existence of physical correctness, the lack of texture, and the large motion in hand-drawn cartoons. In this project, we propose a novel partial-shape matching descriptor that will raise the overall accuracy of region correspondence estimation in cartoon sequence. A major challenge is to overcome the partial occlusion/change that is unavoidable in cartoon sequences, and simultaneously handle the arbitrary camera motion (zoom-in/out, panning, or rotation). We propose to design a shape descriptor that has a local support and transform-invariant. Its locality overcomes the partial occlusion/change, and its transform invariance tackles the arbitrary camera motion. With the transform invariance, we can eliminate the shape matching in scale dimension, and achieve a fast shape similarity analysis. Our major challenge is that the local support property can hardly coexist with the transform invariance. This is why none of the existing shape descriptors are simultaneously locally supported and transform-invariant. Existing descriptors cannot effectively solve our region correspondence estimation. By identifying a suitable transform-invariant domain, we will design a locally supported shape descriptor in this domain for efficient and effective partial-shape matching. By solving these research challenges, we believe the outcome (the knowledge, publications, and algorithms) from the proposed project should motivate further study along the direction of partial-shape similarity analysis, which is currently scarce. Besides, the proposed shape descriptor shall also be directly applicable to many existing pattern recognition applications such as optical character recognition and road-sign detection. Via the technology transfer, the proposed method shall provide a technological niche to the animation and film industry in Hong Kong and mainland China. 儘管近年來計算圖形學飛速發展，但鑒於動畫風格突出、形象鮮明的表現手法，傳統的手繪動畫生產模式仍然在動畫產業中佔據主流。由於動畫藝術家無法以手繪的方式製作立體幀，這使得製作動畫的立體版本變得難以進行。最近出現的一種技術能將2D手繪動畫自動地轉為立體動畫，但這種技術極度依賴不同幀之間區域對應關係的準確性。然而，手繪動畫中普遍存在的作畫物理性錯誤、紋理缺乏和長距離移動使得區域對應關係成為了該領域研究中的一個公開難題。 在本項目中，我們提出一個全新的局部形狀匹配描述符，它可以提高動畫序列中區域對應關係的整體準確率。在區域對應關係的問題中，最主要的難點就在於克服動畫序列中的部分遮擋與改變，並同時處理好鏡頭變換問題（包括放大/縮小、平轉或轉動）。我們計劃設計出一個新的形狀描述符支持局部性的比較並且具有變換不變性。它的局部性可以克服遮擋與改變的問題，而變換不變性則可以很好地對應任意的鏡頭變換。與此同時，變換不變性可以對應不同大小的形狀匹配，以達到快速的形狀相似度分析。對我們來說最主要的挑戰是使得描述符的局部性支持與變換不變性共存。這也正是所有現存形狀描述符所不具備的特性，這使得僅依靠現有形狀描述符無法有效解決區域對應關係問題。通過尋找一個合適的變換不變性的域，我們將設計出一個具有局部支持性的形狀描述符以進行有效且效率的局部形狀匹配。 通過解決以上的研究難點，我們相信本項目的結果（包括知識、算法與出版物）將驅動目前稀缺的關於局部形狀相似性的研究。同時，提出的形狀描述符對於許多現存的模式識別應用比如光學字符識別，道路標誌檢測具有直接應用價值。通過該技術的傳播，我們提出的方法可一定程度上地填補香港和中國的動畫與電影產業之間的鴻溝。

14217516.label: Realisation of objectives
14217516.value: The ultimate goal of this project is to achieve reliable automatic stereoscopization of hand-drawn animation, as manually drawing stereo-frames are infeasible. However, one of the major challenges during the process is the region correspondence problem between consecutive frames, due to the lack of natural textures, and physical cues in cartoon drawing. Severe occlusion further complicates the problem. In this project, our goal is to reliably determine the correspondence without the interference of occlusion. Shape matching is a classical problem in pattern recognition. However, one major obstacle for shape matching is the partial occlusion. Many existing methods mainly assume the matching shapes are occlusion-free, which is an impractical assumption in real-world applications. Even the state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks based shape recognition methods have a very high successful rate for complete-shape matching, occlusion still strongly influence their correctness. To deal with the occlusion, partial-shape matching is the key. We proposed a partial-shape matching that is scale-invariant. Since the scale of regions may change over the frames, scale invariance is crucial to efficient evaluation. Otherwise, we have to evaluate the matching in multiple scales. We proposed the pyramid of arclength shape descriptor (PAD) which is scale-invariant and very simple to compute. Due to its local-support and scale-invariant natures, it can naturally be applied to partial-shape matching in a very efficient manner. This PAD is essentially a vector of arclengths. Each element of the vector is the arclength of an interval surrounding the current point of interest, and cumulates certain amount of absolute curvature. Therefore a 5D PAD vector describes the arclengths of 5 intervals that cumulate 5 different amount of absolute curvature. This descriptor is scale-invariant, rotation-invariant, and translation-invariant, and more importantly it has a local support. The matching comparison between two points of interest is very efficient, it is just a dot product between the two corresponding PAD vectors. To evaluate the robustness of PAD for real-world application, we tested its resistance to noise. Note that edge detection usually generates many noisy edge pixels and may lead to computational error and confusion. For example, broken edges or overly-wiggle edges may hurt the accuracy of partial shape matching. To evaluate the PAD, we first applied it to search the target shape in a noisy edge map with many broken edges and unwanted edge pixels. A statistical approach is developed to efficiently and accurately identify the target shapes even for a natural photograph. We have published the work in the journal Computational Visual Media [J01] and orally presented it in the international conference CVM 2018. However, there is one major disadvantage of using PAD. It requires the computation of curvature. In the early attempt, we first fit the edge pixels with cubic splines in order to evaluate the absolute curvature with the close-form equation. However, this is computational intensive. In a second attempt, we approximate the curvature using the discrete curvature computation. Experiments show that the matching quality of using the discrete curvature is comparable to that of curvature evaluated from close-form equation. This approximation makes the PAD even more practical for real-world partial shape matching. As our goal is to apply our scale-invariant partial shape descriptor to animation stereoscopization, we try to evaluate the effectiveness of this partial shape descriptor in the pipeline of stereoscopization of cel animation. Our stereoscopization heavily relies on the T-junction cue. In our early attempt, we determine the T-junction by tracing, which is error-prone and not very fast. To accurately identify all T-junctions accurately and efficiently, we propose a learning-based junction detection method using convolutional neural network. The accuracy is significantly improved and, more importantly, the detection is almost real-time, thanks to the parallel CNN computation driven by GPU. We also applied such junction detection to vectorization of structural lines of hand-drawing. The work is published in journal Computer Graphics Form [J03] and orally presented in Pacific Graphics 2019. During the development, we found that the rich pattern and texture in region of cel animation severely confuse the region matching. Because the tiny cells within a pattern may be incorrectly identified as regions for shape matching. This is problematic as many tiny cell regions are basically equal in shape. Unfortunately, we cannot naively assume the size of pattern cells to be small, as there is not constraint for cartoonists in creating their artwork. While human can differentiate texture pattern from the semantically meaningful regions, naïve computer algorithm may not. So we employed a learning based analysis to better understand the patterns. We trained a screentone variational autoencoder (screenVAE) dedicated for analyzing patterns. The goal is to digest the pattern of the local neighborhood surrounding a point of interest into a single point. With this screenVAE, we are able to represent the texture characteristics at a point with a screenVAE vector, instead of the spatial neighborhood. It can convert a region fully dressed with complex texture/pattern into a region of homogeneous screenVAE values. Hence, it allows us to easily identify the region boundary without being interfered by the fine pattern structure. At the time of preparation of this completion report, this finding is accepted for publication in ACM Transactions on Graphics [J04] and will be orally presented in ACM SIGGRAPH Asia 2020. Once the region correspondences are reliably determined, we can synthesize the stereo-frames by inferring a continuous depth value for each region. This explains why region correspondence is so crucial in correct generation of depth values and eventually the generation of stereo-frames. However, gaps (disoccluded region) appear when we move the region based on the synthesized depth. This effectively is an inpainting problem. We proposed a learning-based hinted colorization technique dedicated for handdrawing for better gap filling result. This work is published in ACM Transaction on Graphics [J02] and orally presented in ACM SIGGRAPH Asia 2018. To further evaluate the visual pleasantness of the stereoscopization which indirectly measures the effectiveness of our partial shape matching, we have conducted multiple experiments. We have manually prepared the groundtruth for comparison. A user study is also conducted to evaluate the visual quality achieved. The user statistics can also be used to fine tune the parameters in our system, including the level of PAD that best balances the computation and matching quality.

14217516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14217516.value: Please refer to the field “Title” in research output section for the reference ID like [J01][J02],... 1. Even the state-of-the-art CNN-based shape recognition methods have a high successful rate for complete-shape matching, occlusion still strongly influence their correctness. Scale-invariance is crucial to efficient evaluation as there is no need to evaluate the matching in multiple scales. We proposed the pyramid of arclength (PAD) descriptor which is scale-invariant and very simple to compute. Due to its local-support, it fits well for partial-shape matching. 2. Due to the noisiness of edge detection, our PAD may be confused by edge fragments. We proposed a statistical approach during the evaluation of partial-shape matching and the evaluation is very efficient. It is robust to noise contamination. The result is published in a journal Computational Visual Media [J01] and to be orally presented in the international conference CVM 2018. 3. A bottleneck of our PAD is its computation. Since it relies on the curvature integration, our early implementation performs an inefficient curve fitting over the edge pixels. So, we later approximate the curvature with the discrete curvature, and experiment its effectiveness in shape matching. Comparable matching quality can be obtained. 4. Our application of partial shape matching is for hand-drawn animation stereoscopization. Junction detection of structural lines is crucial step. Naïve tracing of junctions is unreliable. We proposed a learning-based junction detection that can accurately detect junctions in real-time. It is orally presented in Pacific Graphics 2019 and simultaneously published in journal Computer Graphics Forum [J03]. This paper receives the Best Student Presentation Award of Pacific Graphics 2019. 5. Texture/pattern within the cartoon regions interfere the region detection and hence the subsequent the region matching. Naïve region detection may incorrectly identify cells within the pattern as many tiny regions and confuse the partial shape matching. We propose a learning-based model, variational autoencoder (screenVAE), to convert a region dressed by texture/pattern to a region of homogenous screenVAE value. This drastically reduces the interference. The work is accepted for oral presentation in ACM SIGGRAPH Asia 2020 (at the time of preparation of this report), and will be published in ACM Transactions on Graphics [J04]. 6. Once regions are matched and the region ordering is determined, rendering of stereoscopic frames can be performed. Gap may be resulted. We proposed a learning-based model for hinted colorization for filling the gap. It was orally presented in ACM SIGGRAPH Asia 2018 and published in ACM Transactions on Graphics [J02].

14217516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14217516.value: Further development: In this project, we proposed a locally supported, scale-invariant, rotational-invariant and translational-invariant partial shape descriptor for partial shape matching. Since it relies on the curvature, the bottleneck is its computation. We found that that high accuracy of computed curvature may not be necessary. In other words, approximation to curvature may be sufficient for practical applications. We shall follow this direction to further speed up the computation of pyramid of arclength descriptor. Course of action: With the success of curvature approximation with discrete curvature, we plan to further utilize the convolutional neural networks to compute the pyramid of arclength descriptor along the edge pixels. With the real-time performance of testing phase of convolutional neural networks, it may be possible to return multiple pyramid of arclength descriptor in real time, given an input image.

14217516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14217516.value: With the low-cost stereoscopic display being widely available, there exists a lag of stereoscopic content, especially on handdrawn animation, due to the infeasibility of 3D frames drawing by hand. With the animation stereoscopicization, we can convert monocular cartoon to its stereoscopic counterpart automatically. However, a technical challenge lies on the accurate determination of the region correspondence between frames. This project serves as a step forward to solving the region correspondence, via proposing a novel partial shape descriptor. With the proposed technique, practical automatic conversion of monocular cartoon to stereoscopic one becomes feasible.

14217816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14217816.value: 物聯網中的設備安全配置與認證關鍵技術研究

14217816.label: Project Objectives
14217816.value: 1. New device authentication techniques and protocols based on hardware fingerprints of IoT equipments. Previous studies from our group and other researchers have demonstrated that it is possible to extract some unique fingerprint from hardware features of a device. In this project, we plan to extend our own work published on ACM CCS'2014 and propose to explore a new technology called "authentication based analog computing". The basic idea is to send a challenge to device for processing (e.g., asking a device to play a piece of specially crafted sound with its speaker), and by comparing features extracted from device response (e.g., recorded sound played by that speaker) with results from pre-built model, a system can tell true devices from illegal ones. 2. Exploration of new near distance communication channels based on various sensors installed on IoT devices as well as smartphones. Currently, most device management work are done remotely through wired or wireless network, which is insecure by nature. In this project, we propose to study some new sensor-based near distance communication channels that use smartphone to provide configuration interfaces and achieve security by distance bounding so that sensitive operations, like installing digital certificate, encryption keys, system upgrading, etc., can only be done within short distances. This is also an extension of our previous work. 3. Device authentication techniques/protocols based on shared environmental context. This also leverage distances to achieve system security, but here we proposes to ask an devices to calculating authentication proofs based on environmental properties, like sound, light, temperature, magnetic field, etc. Such an environmental context could be passive (i.e., existed as it is), or injected by master devices actively (e.g., beeping in a special pattern).

14217816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14217816.value: 目標 研究新型系統結構和協議，以支持物聯網系統的安全認證和配置 項目背景 物聯網(IoT)系統是有一組具備傳感器、嵌入式處理器、相應軟件以及通信能力的智能設備相互連接而成。物聯網有着廣泛的應用，而本項目將以智能家居系統爲背景。 物聯網的安全問題至關重要，因爲它不但涉及到用戶的隱私，而且可能導致嚴重的安全事故，例如意外開機具有潛在火災危險。 儘管如此，由於多方面的原因，物聯網系統目前尚未有一套公認的標準或者協議來確保其安全。一方面，對於系統開發商而言，系統的功能以及能否迅速上市、提高市場佔有率總是優先於安全方面的考慮。而另一方面，物聯網中的設備在功耗，處理能力，部署位置等方面存在各種約束條件，使得現有許多安全技術和協議並不能直接應用。 項目概述 本項目將針對智能家居物聯網系統研究新型系統結構和協議，能夠支持安全的設備配置和認證操作。在系統配置方面，將研究如何管理、初始化以及重新配置物聯網設備和系統。例如，如何將物聯網設備組織成一個安全、功能正常的系統，如何將一個新的物聯網設備加入到一個現有系統中，以及當用戶搬入新的住所時，如何對之前已經存在的物聯網系統進行重新配置，確保安全。在認證方面，我們將研究如下關鍵技術。首先是新型、基於傳感器的近場通信鏈路，其次是基於上下文的設備認證，包括各種環境因素，例如聲音，光，震動等等。 創新性 根據目前的調查，本項目是第一個提出使用一般的傳感器來建立新型近場通信鏈路，進而幫助物聯網設備認證的方法。 影響力 本項目的研究將幫助物聯網系統在應用中的安全性，保護用戶隱私和生命財產安全。所研究的相關技術也具有商業潛力，幫助香港本地信息技術產業的全球競爭力

14217816.label: Realisation of objectives
14217816.value: Object 1. Use device fingerprint for authentication. We have conducted studied towards this goal and have achieved a new device fingerprinting method and a new authentication protocol based on it. In the paper "Beware of Your Screen: Anonymous Fingerprinting of Device Screens for Off-line Payment Protection" (published on ACM Annual Computer Security Applications Conference 2018), we found that the brightness of each LCD screen is unique, even for screens from the same vendors manufactured within the same period of time. We developed algorithms to generate robust fingerprints and a new protocol that uses this fingerprint to secure authentication process. Object 2 Secure configuration with Near communication channel When working towards this object, we found some paper that had already realized a similar idea. For example, "Secured and Easy-to-Use NFC-Based Device Configuration for the Internet of Things". This paper was published on IEEE Journal of Radio Frequency Identification on March 2017, while our proposal was submitted in Oct 2016. So we switched to study the security of near field communication channels and we come up with another work on the security of mobile payment. Near field communication protocols are widely used in mobile payment, and our paper is the first one to systematically study the security of its underlying communication channel (including: NFC, audio, and QR code). The work was published on USENIX Security (one top tier conference in security area) in 2017. Object 3 Authentication based on Common Environment We have also done some work towards this goal but unfortunately were facing some challenging problem which is under studying. Our original plan is to fingerprint the environment where an IoT device is located, and if two devices could provide the same environmental fingerprints then we could conclude that they are located at the same place and can securely exchange data. However, we could not found a suitable algorithm that can generate a stable fingerprint. We tried to extend our research to construct a Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) based on the physical environment surrounding a given IoT device. With a successful construction of PUF, we would be able to establish a challenge-response protocol which can be used to perform IoT device authentication. Again, we failed to find a good method to generate an usable PUF candidate. However, we believe the common environment indeed contains some information that could be used for device authentication. We will keep this problem in mind and further study this problem in future.

14217816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14217816.value: 1. We have studied the security of near field communication channels (such as NFC, sound, light) used in mobile payment, and discovered several vulnerabilities. We have reported those problems to system vendors who had confirmed our discoveries and contributions. (refer to paper published on USENIX security paper in 2017) 2. We have proposed a new fuzz testing methods to discover IoT device authentication vulnerabilities. By leveraging the program analysis technique, we are able to extract useful information from the paired Android applications of IoT devices, then use the extracted information to guide the fuzzing process. Such method can significantly boost the fuzzing efficiency and is able to discover new vulnerabilities that were not found previously. 3. We have studied the code protection mechanisms related to the IoT devices and their paired Android Applications. For Android Apps, we studied the effectiveness of obfuscation, one of the major code protection method. For IoT firmware, we investigated the use of crypto tools and found several misuses. These works were published on SecureComm 2018 and RAID 2019 respectively. 4. We also studied the authentication protocols used in IoT devices, especially for the remote binding (during device initialization) and authorization among multiple service providers. We discovered a new type of vulnerabilities called "privilege leakage" where the authorized permissions may become a residual privilege even after that permission had been removed. These works were published on DSN 2019 and The Third Workshop on Security, Privacy and Trust in the Internet of Things respectively. 5. We have studied the accessibility mechanism provided by Android to facilitate the use of Android apps (including those apps paired with IoT devices), and found several security loopholes which could be exploited by attacks to install malicious Apps and steal personal information. This works was published on RAID in 2019.

14218516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14218516.value: 在該項目中，我們旨在研發一種新型並且簡易的磁性微型機器人體內實時追蹤成像技術，基於遊動微機器人生物模板的自發螢光和細胞內吞量子點現象。天然螺旋藻類和內吞量子點的螺旋藻類的螢光發光現象將被用於磁性微機器人的模板來實現該體內實時追蹤微型遊動機器人的目標。 首先，我們將在帶有量子點的培養液中培養藻類，并研究螺旋藻和量子點之間的相互作用。然後，生物模板法將被採用用於在螺旋藻的表面覆蓋一層超順磁性的四氧化三鐵納米顆粒用於磁場驅動微型機器人。該磁性層的微結構和厚度將被優化以達到最優化的體內螢光成像效果。接下來，我們也會研究該磁性螺旋狀微型機器人的細胞毒性。最後，我們將通過動物實驗來系統性研究基於內吞量子點和天然螺旋藻生物模板法製備的微型遊動機器人在實驗室小白鼠體內的螢光成像效果。我們的初步試驗結果顯示，表面包裹四氧化三鐵納米顆粒螺旋藻的自發螢光可以用於小白鼠體內某些特定組織的螢光成像。我們將會利用該三年課題進一步探索微機器人靶向藥物輸送過程中基於螢光技術的體內實時成像和可控性運動。

14218516.label: Realisation of objectives
14218516.value: Microrobots are considered as promising tools for minimally invasive medicine. However, the imaging modality and control of these tiny agents are highly challenging in order to be further applied on in vivo environments. The same view was also presented by Schmidt et al in Nature (Vol. 545, 406–408, 25 May 2017, doi:10.1038/545406a). In this GRF project, we aim to explore and develop an enabling technology for in vivo tracking of biohybrid magnetic microrobots using fluorescence and/or other bio-imaging tools, and to understand the motion control and tracking of these microagents in the complex fluidic environment. The achievement from this GRF project will pave the way for the advance of medical microrobots for biomedical applications. During the project period, we have successfully developed an approach to obtain mass-production of hybrid magnetic swimming microrobots using spirulina-templates via the interaction of spirulina and the magnetic nanoparticles (i.e. magnetite nanoparticles). Moreover, we have sorted out the optimized parameters for biohybrid magnetic swimming microrobots with a high drug loading capacities, and controlled drug release can be realized via degradation of the biohybrid microrobots. The magnetic actuation and in vivo swimming of spirulina-templated microrobots were conducted using lab mice as the animal study model. Two imaging modalities were investigated, i.e. fluorescence imaging and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In addition, the stability, imaging contrast and depth, the cytotoxicity and biodegradability of the helical biohybrid microrobots were investigated systematically, thanks to the collaboration with Prof. Kostarelos group, Nanomedicine Lab, at University of Manchester, and also the collaborators from CUHK medical school. One journal paper about multifunctional biohybrid microrobots was published in the prestigious AAAS journal, Science Robotics, in 2017. And the work was also highlighted in Science News (AAAS), entitled "This robot made of algae can swim through your body - thanks to magnets", and the RGC YouTube Channel, see https://youtu.be/l2NQfgW8tSQ. The drug loading and release using the biohybrid microrobots was published in the journal Applied Materials Today in 2019, in which the main advantages of using micro-algae as the biotemplate for molecular cargo delivery were highlighted, i.e. (i) reversible dehydration and rehydration processes of spirulina cells; (ii) Cellular loading of model macromolecules and small molecules. (iii) Controllable biodegradation-induced release of molecular cargos. (iv) Intact bioactivity of guest TGF-β1 and function on human mesenchymal stem cells. The study also validates that the biohybrid magnetic swimmers are able to navigate in complex biofluidic environments without fuel supply. Taking advantage of the natural dehydration and rehydration of their cellular microstructures, either biomacromolecules or small molecules can be encapsulated into the Spirulina cells. And the cargo loading causes minor adverse effects to the maneuverability of the host swimmers. The Spirulina-borne model molecules are released by two different mechanisms, both subject to degradation of the host swimmers. The bioactivity of guest molecules after release, taking TGF-β1 as an example, is proved intact through evaluation using a stem cell micromass system. Assembled together, these desirable characteristics suggest a novel cell-based magnetic microswimmer envisioned for potential molecular delivery in various applications confronted by minimally invasive medicine. The biotemplating approach has also been applied to prepare multifunctional biohybrid magnetic microrobots with decoration of carbon dots (i.e. quantum dots with a diameter less than 9 nm). In comparison to organic fluorophores and semiconductor quantum dots, the main advantage of the carbon dots are their excellent biocompatibility, robust chemical inertness, simple and inexpensive preparation, and abundance of raw material in nature. We have published one paper in Sensors and Actuators B, about the fluorescent carbon dots with multi-dopants for sensing. Another key publication reports the carbon dots functionalized biohybrid microrobots for pathogenic bacteria sensing in the GI tract. A rapid, direct, and low-cost method for detecting bacterial toxins associated with common gastrointestinal diseases remains a great challenge despite numerous studies and clinical assays. Motion-based detection through tracking the emerging micro- and nanorobots has shown great potential in chemo- and biosensing due to accelerated “chemistry on the move”. In this work, the PI, Co-I and the team described the use of fluorescent magnetic spore–based microrobots (FMSMs) as a highly efficient mobile sensing platform for the detection of toxins secreted by Clostridium difficile (C. diff) that were present in patients’ stool. These microrobots were synthesized rapidly and inexpensively by the direct deposition of magnetic nanoparticles and the subsequent encapsulation of sensing probes on the porous natural spores. Because of the cooperation effect of natural spore, magnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles, and functionalized carbon nanodots, selective fluorescence detection of the prepared FMSMs is demonstrated in C. diff bacterial supernatant and even in actual clinical stool samples from infectious patients within tens of minutes, suggesting rapid response and good selectivity and sensitivity of FMSMs toward C. diff toxins. Very recently, the PI’s team has also developed a fully automated microrobotic platform which can conduct the quick detection of patient’s stool sample. A media report on the microrobotic platform can be found in CUHK CPR news, please see https://www.cpr.cuhk.edu.hk/en/press/cuhk-develops-novel-microrobotic-diagnostic-system-to-accurately-diagnose-infectious-pathogens-with-full-automation-and-low-cost/ Overall, based on the funding support from RGC, we have successfully reach the five objectives of this GRF project, and published several key papers for the advance of microrobotics for biomedicine, including one Science Robotics, two Science Advances, and two Nature Communications. For details, please refer to the research outputs.

14218516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14218516.value: The major findings and research outcomes from this GRF project is very fruitful. The PI's group has published several key papers in top journals, including Science Robotics and Science Advances. 1. L. Zhang et al., Multifunctional biohybrid magnetite microrobots for imaging guided therapy, Science Robotics (AAAS), Vol. 2, eaaq1155, 2017. (Impact factor: 19.4, Ranked #1 in the category of “Robotics” in ISI Web of Science) Note: This work has been highlighted in Science News (https://www.sciencemag.org/news/2017/11/robotmade- algae-can-swim-through-your-body-thanks-magnets, by Hong Kong RGC YouTube Channel, https://youtu.be/l2NQfgW8tSQ.) The work is indexed as an ISI Highly Cited Paper. In this paper, a new type of multi-functional helical microrobots has been developed based on the new concept of biohybrid design. We report that the batch fabrication of helical microrobots can be realized using biotemplating approach with ease by using microalgae. Moreover, for the first time, the microrobotic agents are capable of in-vivo tracking using dual imaging modalities, i.e. fluorescent imaging and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and with controlled degradability. The results undoubtedly make an important step towards the use of wirelessly controlled microrobots for image-guided minimally invasive intervention. 2. The biotemplating approach has also been applied to prepare multifunctional biohybrid magnetic microrobots with decoration of carbon dots (i.e. quantum dots with a diameter less than 9 nm). In comparison to organic fluorophores and semiconductor quantum dots, the main advantage of the carbon dots are their excellent biocompatibility, robust chemical inertness, simple and inexpensive preparation, and abundance of raw material in nature. Another key publication from the team reports the carbon dots functionalized biohybrid microrobots for pathogenic bacteria sensing in the GI tract (Science Advances 2019). In this work, the PI and the team described the use of fluorescent magnetic spore–based microrobots (FMSMs) as a highly efficient mobile sensing platform for the detection of toxins secreted by Clostridium difficile (C. diff) that were present in patients’ stool. These microrobots were synthesized rapidly and inexpensively by the direct deposition of magnetic nanoparticles and the subsequent encapsulation of sensing probes on the porous natural spores. Because of the cooperation effect of natural spore, magnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles, and functionalized carbon nanodots, selective fluorescence detection of the prepared FMSMs is demonstrated in C. diff bacterial supernatant and even in actual clinical stool samples from infectious patients within tens of minutes, suggesting rapid response and good selectivity and sensitivity of FMSMs toward C. diff toxins.

14218516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14218516.value: The research team is currently working on translating the technology into different in vivo applications. These include targeted delivery of therapeutic drugs deep inside the body, which can minimise the side effect of drugs with high dosage circulating in the body. In terms of treating gastrointestinal diseases, biohybrid soft microrobots also have high potential in treating bile duct cancer, intrahepatic duct stones in narrow lumens, and so on. The next step for the team is to conduct animal trials to validate its safety and efficacy. Furthermore, the PI and his research group also engage in developing a swarm control strategy that allows the coordinated and synchronised navigation of multiple microrobots. Tens, hundreds or even more microrobots are gathered into a dynamic entity to traverse tiny and tortuous lumens through adaptive transformation, which not only increases the delivery efficiency, but also enhances the in vivo imaging contrast. Moreover, other kinds of microrobots with different functions (e.g., sensing and imaging) will be integrated to construct a heterogeneous swarm system. In this manner, the clinical tasks are envisioned to be completed via the cooperation between different specialized microrobots, making the system more intelligent, feasible and safer than before.

14218516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14218516.value: Remotely actuated microrobots have the potential for biomedical applications, such as minimally invasive medicine, due to their small sizes and accessibility to hard-to-reach regions inside human body. However, in a more practical scenario, the complex physiological environment, the challenges on real-time in vivo tracking, and the unclear therapeutic effects and the bio-safety issues shall be well addressed first. The aim of this GRF project is to explore and develop an enabling technology for in vivo tracking of biohybrid magnetic microrobots using fluorescence and/or other bio-imaging tools, and to understand the motion control and tracking of these microagents in the complex fluidic environment. The PI's lab has successfully demonstrated that a swarm of micro-algae-based helical microrobots can be tracked using MRI and fluorescence signals in vivo, which has high potential for image-guided therapy. Furthermore, the team has reported real-time tracking of fluorescent magnetic spore–based microrobots for remote detection of C. diff toxins. The key results were published in top journals, such as Science Robotics and Science Advances, and were highlighted in many international and local media.

14218716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14218716.value: This project aims to (1) understand the structure-property relations at the solid-liquid and solid-cell interfaces in organic bioelectronics using charge modulation spectroscopy and to (2) develop a combined spectroscopic/electrical sensing scheme based on the fundamental findings. Organic electronics has recently emerged as a powerful technology platform for bio-sensing applications. In many applications, the organic devices are operated in direct contact with an aqueous environment, thus resulting in strong coupling between charge transport in the organic solid and water dipoles, ions and cells in the liquid. These interactions, although dictate the sensing performance, are not well understood. In particular, how these interactions are influenced by the structural and morphological properties of the organic materials remains unknown. In terms of sensing mechanisms, many devices make use of only the electrical responses of organic semiconductors, while the optical signatures of these materials, which are very sensitive to their surroundings, have not been utilized. To addresses these limitations, we will develop a combined spectroscopic/electrical characterization protocol for interface studies of organic bioelectronics. Specifically, we will use charge modulation spectroscopy (CMS) to investigate a liquid-gated transistor structure. This method allows detection of the characteristic absorption features of charge carriers in the complex sensing environment. With CMS we will first investigate how the interface electronic and electrochemical processes are influenced and controlled by the molecular structure and film morphology of the organic semiconductor layer. The study will help us to identify the optimal material and device designs for stable and sensitive spectroscopic and electrical measurements. In the second stage of the project we will incorporate a cell layer into the transistors and investigate how the morphological variations of the cell layer modify the CMS and electrical responses of the devices. Through a comparative study on the spectroscopic and electrical signals we will establish a device model to describe the cell-regulated ionic and electronic conduction. Based on these findings we will demonstrate monitoring of barrier tissue integrity using the spectroscopic-electrical test model developed in this project. The proposed work represents the first attempt to spectroscopically probe charge transport at liquid-solid and cell-solid interfaces, and will complement previous electrical measurements to provide more precise device models to describe the concerted processes in a bio-sensing system. The research outcomes will not only elucidate the structural-property correlations in organic bioelectronics, generating new material design principles, but also enable new in vitro measurement methodologies for live-cell sensing. 該項目旨在: (1)利用電荷調製光譜技術來探究有機生物電子器件的固體-液體和固體-細胞界面的結構-性能關係； (2)發展結合光譜測量和電學測量的生物傳感機制。 近年來，有機電子器件逐漸發展成為了生物傳感等應用的強大技術平台。在許多實際應用中，有機電子器件都在與液體直接接觸的環境中工作，進而導致有機固體材料中的電荷傳輸與液體中的水偶極子，以及離子和細胞之間發生強耦合作用。儘管這些相互作用很大程度上決定了器件的傳感性能，卻沒有得到良好的理論理解。特別是有機材料的結構和形態性質對這些相互作用的影響仍亟待研究。在感測機制方面，許多設備僅利用了有機半導體的電響應，而對周圍環境非常敏感的光學特性卻沒有得到充分利用。 為了打破這些限制，我們將研發出結合光譜和電特性的表徵方法來研究有機生物電子器件的界面性質。具體地說，我們將使用電荷調製光譜（CMS）來研究液體柵極晶體管。此方法能夠在復雜的傳感環境中檢測電荷載體的特徵吸收。利用CMS測量，我們將首先研究有機半導體材料的分子結構和薄膜形態對其界面的電子和電化學過程的影響控制機制，從而幫助我們篩選能實現穩定、靈敏的光譜和電氣測量的最佳材料和器件設計。在該項目的第二階段，我們將結合細胞層和晶體管，進一步研究細胞形態變化將怎樣改變器件的CMS和電信號。通過對光譜和電信號的比較研究，我們將建立一個描述細胞調節離子和電子傳導的器件模型。基於這些發現，我們將利用此項目研發的光譜-電學測量模型來監測細胞組織的完整性。

14218716.label: Realisation of objectives
14218716.value: The objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1: We have developed several characterization protocols to combine charge accumulation spectroscopy (one type of charge modulation spectroscopy) with structural (grazing incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS)), morphological (AFM), chemical (Raman spectra and FTIR) and mass (electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance) analyses as well as electrical current-voltage measurements to investigate the interface structural-property relations in organic bioelectronic devices. Objective 2: Through the protocols established in Objective 1, we have established physical models to explain the effects of water dipoles and ions on the characteristic absorptions of polaronic charge carriers. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the water-ion-charge interactions can be modified by varying the molecular structure and film morphology of the organic semiconductors. Objective 3: We designed, modeled and fabricated a solid–liquid dual-gate organic transistor structure, where the threshold voltage of the cell-interfaced, liquid-gated conduction channel is controlled by an additional gate that is separated from the channel by a metal-oxide gate dielectric. With this design, the threshold voltage of the “sensing channel” can be linearly tuned in a voltage window exceeding 0.4 V. Objective 4: Based on the device structure developed in Objective 3, we have achieved a much more sensitive and rapid sensor response for monitoring detachment of human mesenchymal stem cells. Objective 5: Overall, by conducting studies towards Objectives 1-4, we have identified some key material parameters, such as molecular packing, rigidity and hydrophobicity of side chains and molecular interaction with ions, that can greatly affect the sensitivity and stability of an organic semiconductor in a physiological environment.

14218716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14218716.value: 1. We demonstrated a charge accumulation spectroscopy (CAS)-based protocol, exploiting water-gated organic field-effect transistor as the testing platform, to investigate the structure-dependent localization of polaronic charge carriers at the organic semiconductor–liquid interface. Our results reveal that the degree of charge delocalization is reduced drastically when the charge carriers are moved from the bulk semiconductor to the semiconductor–water interface, suggesting the existence of a highly disordered surface layer in contact with water. It is also found that the charge delocalization could be further reduced by intercalation of chloride ions (from salt water) in the semiconductor surface layer. This study suggests that the spectroscopic signatures of polaronic charge carriers could be a sensitive probe to detect the structure-dependent charge localization at organic solid–liquid interfaces. (Publication #2) 2. The cell-safe voltage constraint (typically 0.3 V or lower) often prevents the operation of the transistors at their maximum transconductance or most sensitive regime. Here, we exploit a solid–liquid dual-gate organic transistor structure, where the threshold voltage of the liquid-gated conduction channel is controlled by an additional gate that is separated from the channel by a metal-oxide gate dielectric. With this design, the threshold voltage of the “sensing channel” can be linearly tuned in a voltage window exceeding 0.4 V. We have demonstrated that the dual-gate structure enables a much better sensor response to the detachment of human mesenchymal stem cells. In general, the capability of tuning the optimal sensing bias will not only improve the device performance but also broaden the material selection for cell-based organic bioelectronics. (Publication #1) 3. We quantified the number of ion and water injection into the organic active layer and analyze the change of microscopic molecular packing of typical polymeric conducting materials by integrating electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (EQCM-D), CAS, and electrical current-voltage measurements. We demonstrate that the penetration of a large amount of ions and water molecules can lead to viscous and disordered microstructures in organic mixed conductors and that the water uptake property plays a more dominant role in morphological disruption, as compared with ion uptake. The study demonstrates the potential application of CAS in evaluating organic mixed conductors and highlights the importance of coordinately tuning the hydration, structural integrity and charge transport properties of the material systems in order to achieve high performance and stable devices. (Publication #4) 4. Through the course of this project, we also developed other general device strategies (e.g., electrode modification) to improve the stability of organic electronic devices. (Publication #3)

14218716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14218716.value: Our project clearly demonstrates that charge modulation spectroscopy, or more specifically, charge accumulation spectroscopy, is a powerful tool for studying the structure-dependent electronic properties at organic solid–liquid interfaces. Our studies also point out that new material designs are needed to better manipulate the water-molecule and ion-molecule interactions, as well as balancing the needs of sufficient hydration, good structural integrity and efficient charge transport. Towards this goal we aim to push forward the application of our spectroscopic tools by setting up collaborations with various material science and chemistry groups that are developing new organic molecules for bioelectronics, and we expect that the spectroscopic tool will become a facile screening tool for the chemists to examine their newly designed molecules. Also, although the current spectroscopic setup has no spatial resolution, it can be reconfigured and integrated with a scanning microscope system to enable mapping of cell functions. A preliminary study along this direction has already been initiated and a confocal microspectroscopy system with a resolution of 3 micron has been achieved.

14218716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14218716.value: Organic electronics has recently emerged as a powerful technology platform for bio-sensing applications. In many applications, the organic devices are operated in direct contact with an aqueous environment, thus resulting in strong coupling between charge transport in the organic solid and water dipoles, ions and cells in the liquid. These interactions, although dictate the sensing performance, are not well understood. In particular, how these interactions are influenced by the structural and morphological properties of the organic materials remains unknown. Through this project we have developed new characterization protocols based on charge accumulation spectroscopy (CAS) to study the electronic and electrochemical processes at the solid-liquid and solid-cell interfaces. We have identified the structural-property relations at the liquid-solid interface and the impact of ion diffusion and water swollen on charge transport and electrochemical doping/reaction processes, providing critical knowledge to bridge solid-state physics and electrochemistry. Furthermore, the project generates new material design principles and provides in vitro sensing platforms with multiple functionalities and improved accuracy. By identifying the molecular building blocks for high sensitivity and stability, our study sheds light on the R&D activities towards creating new material toolboxes for bioelectronic applications in physiological environments.

14219016.label: Project Objectives
14219016.value: Propose effective pricing and revenue sharing schemes for crowdsourcing user Wi-Fi access points, by encouraging desirable user membership selection and network access behaviors. Analyze users' bandwidth sharing and data quota trading behaviors, considering the user heterogeneity in terms of usage patterns, QoS requirements, price sensitivities, and risk and loss aversion levels. Design fair, effective, and distributed user resource collaboration schemes that have low complexity and are robust to network dynamics.

14219016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14219016.value: 本項目致力於提出一整套促進無線網絡運營商和用户之間有效合作的經濟激勵機制。由於智能手機的日益普及及其不斷增長的屏幕尺寸，分辨率和處理速度，消費者所需的無線數據服務正在迅速增長。按照思科的預測，全球移動數據流程量將在2014年到2019年達到61％的年增長率。考慮到蜂窩網絡容量的相對緩慢增長，這將對移動通信網絡的運營提出很大的挑戰。無線運營商都盡力獲得更多的頻譜資源和升級網絡基礎設施以跟上用戶快速增長的需求。然而，無線數據的隨機性使得運營商的很多資源在大部分時間沒法得到有效的利用。對於移動用戶來說，他們的服務質量依然會在網絡擁塞的時候受到影響。緩解這些問題的方法之一是鼓勵運營商之間和用戶之間進行有效的網絡資源共享，以降低成本和提高該服務質量。為了實現這一目標，我們需要設計有效的經濟機制，激勵運營商和用戶透露他們的私人信息和開展雙贏合作。在這個項目中，我們計劃將回答以下幾個關鍵問題。 （1）如何鼓勵運營商協作投資和共享網絡基礎設施？（2）如何運營商眾包網絡資源來提高網絡覆蓋和用戶的性能？ （3）運營商應該如何鼓勵用戶之間的帶寬共享和數據的交易？ （4）用戶之間如何分布式地交換網絡資源和協作？新的經濟機制將有助於解決網絡性能的瓶頸，以充分發揮無線網絡的潛力。

14219016.label: Realisation of objectives
14219016.value: All project objectives have been successfully completed. The detailed research outputs listed as follows. We proposed a behavioral economics model to understand the mobile data trading behavior for users in wireless networks. This is related to journal paper 1 and conference paper 3. We proposed effective incentive mechanisms to achieve efficient collaborative mobile video streaming among mobile users. This is related to journal papers 2, 17, 20, and conference paper 7. We proposed an effective mechanism for the integration of cellular and Wi-Fi networks, where users are assigned to different networks by considering the impact on network congestion and user QoS. This is related to journal paper 3. We analyzed the public Wi-Fi ecosystem, where venues, advertisers, and mobile users work together to improve the venue revenue while providing differentiated services to the users. This is related to journal paper 4. We designed an incentive framework for mobile data offloading considering the impact of price competition and energy consumptions. This is related to journal papers 6, 21, and 23. We proposed effective crowdsourcing mechanisms that take advantage of data reuse, data sharing, and user diversities. This is related to journal papers 6 and 7 and conference paper 5. We explored the design flexibility in terms of time, user, and location in terms of wireless data pricing. This is related to journal papers 8, 11, 12, 16, as well as conference papers 8, 10, 13, and 16. We designed an effective incentive mechanism to ensure fair benefit sharing in wireless power transfer. This is related to journal paper 9 and conference paper 11. We designed an efficient network sharing mechanism with asymmetric constraint information. This is related to journal paper 10 and conference paper 18. We proposed a collaboration mechanism for online application developers and offline venues to ensure effective utilization of wireless resources. This is related to journal paper 13 and conference paper 9. We modeled and analyzed users' bounded rational behaviors in mobile crowdsourcing based on the framework of cognitive hierarchy. This is related to journal paper 14 and conference paper 15. We analyzed the impact of user cooperation on the mobile operators and suggested optimal pricing strategies from the operators' side. This is related to journal paper 15 and conference paper 4. We analyzed the equilibrium system behavior on crowdsensing systems where the applications are delay-aware. This is related to journal paper 18. We proposed a general framework for users to share communications, computation, and caching resources in mobile networks. This is related to journal paper 19 and conference paper 6. We considered how to incentivize effective Wi-Fi network sharing through crowdsourcing. This is related to journal paper 22. We proposed a general taxation approach that can turn any noncooperative static game into a cooperation system achieving social efficiency. This is related to conference paper 1. We proposed an incentive mechanism that encourages users to share their data cooperatively while ensuring data privacy. This is related to conference papers 2, 12, and 14. We examined how live streaming platforms should set the incentive mechanism to maximize the platform's income. This is related to conference paper 17. We analyzed how to price the freshness of data to achieve the maximum profit for the data generator. This is related to conference paper 19. We analyzed the impact of selfish routing on networks. This is related to conference paper 20. We proposed an incentive mechanism for ensuring crowdsourced worked exerting efforts and telling the truth. This is related to conference paper 21.
