14219016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14219016.value: This project proposes and analyzes a family of economic mechanisms that facilitate effective collaborations in wireless networks to improve system efficiency. Due to the proliferation of smartphones with increasingly larger screens, higher resolutions, and faster processing speeds, consumer demands for wireless data services are growing rapidly. This is pushing the cellular networks to their performance limits, considering the relatively slow growth of cellular network capacity projected over the next few years. Wireless operators are under great pressure to obtain more spectrum and upgrade the network infrastructure, to keep up with the fast demand increase. However, stochastic mobile traffic makes it difficult for an operator to make its resources fully utilized most of the time. Mobile users not only experience frequent QoS degradation due to network congestions but also face the mismatch between the inflexible monthly data quotas and the random unpredictable demands. We design effective economic mechanisms to incentivize operators and users to reveal their private information and engage in win-win collaborations.

14219516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14219516.value: More and more complex engineering tasks are performed by coordinating the function of a group of individual systems called networked multi-agent systems. Typical tasks include the formation of mobile robots, multiple spacecraft attitude alignment, mobile sensor area coverage, and control of electric power grids. These applications have led to the emerging research topic: cooperative control of networked systems. A great challenge to deal with various control problems of networked systems is that the control law has to satisfy the time-varying or even switching communication constraints. Such a control law is called distributed control law. This project aims to develop a systematic framework for designing a distributed control law. This framework consists of three steps. The first step is to find a purely decentralized control law for networked systems under the assumption that the leader’s signal is available for the control of each follower. The second step is to design a so-called adaptive distributed observer for the leader system which is able to provide the estimation of both the leader's signal and the leader’s dynamics to each follower for feedback control without knowing the global information of the leader. Finally, we synthesize a distributed control law by replacing the leader’s signal in the purely decentralized control law with the estimated leader’s signal provided by the adaptive distributed observer. Such designed control law is called certainty equivalence distributed control law. If the certainty equivalence distributed control law can accomplish the same task as the purely decentralized control law, then we say this control law satisfies the certainty equivalent principle. The success of this design philosophy depends on two key issues: the existence of the adaptive distributed observer and the satisfaction of the certainty equivalence principle. However, so far the existence of this adaptive distributed observer is only ascertained for undirected switching networks, and the certainty equivalence principle has not been established for complex tasks and complex networked systems. Thus, this project has three specific objectives. First, we extend the adaptive distributed observer from undirected switching networks to directed switching networks. Second, we establish the certainty equivalence principle for several cooperative control problems for complex networked systems subject to directed switching networks such as the consensus problem for Euler-Lagrange systems, rigid-body systems, and the connectivity preservation problem for double-integrator systems and Euler-Lagrange systems. Finally, we apply the framework to some practical problems in robotics, flight control, and networked manufacturing. 越來越多的複雜工程任務需由網络化系統的協調控制來完成。 這樣的例子包擴移動機器人的編隊, 多個航天器的姿態控制, 移動傳感網络的區域覆蓋, 及電網的控制等。 這些工程應用催生了控制領域的一個熱門研究課題:網络系統的協作式控制。 網络系統有若干協作式控制問題, 它們面臨的一個共同難點是網络系統的控制律必須滿足時變的或切換的通訊約束。 這類控制律被稱之為分布式控制律。 本專案旨在開發一個設計分布式控制律的系統框架。 該框架由三個步驟構成。 第一步是在每個跟隨系統都可獲得領導系統狀態或輸出的假定下尋求一個網络系統的純分散的控制律。 第二步是為領導系統設計一個自适应分布式觀測器。 該觀測器能夠在不使用全域資訊的情況下向每個跟隨系統提供領導系統的狀態與動態特性。 第三步 是通過確定性等價原理將純分散的控制律與自适应分布式觀測器綜合為一個所謂的確定性等價分布式控制律。 如果這樣合成的控制律具有與純分散控制律相同的功能, 則稱這樣合成的控制律滿足確定性等價原理。 這一設計思路的成功取決於兩個關鍵因素:自适应分布式觀測器的存在與否與確定性等價原理是否成立。 然而,目前對於第一個問題,只有假定網络是雙向時才能證明自适应分布式觀測器的存在性。 而第二個問題也只對較簡單的網络系統及較初步的若干協作式控制問題得到驗證。 本專案有三個具體目標。 第一, 證明單向切換網络的自适应分布式觀測器的存在性。 第二, 對若干複雜的單向切換網络系統的協作式控制問題建立確定性等價原理包括歐拉系統及剛體系統的趨同問題, 二階積分系統或歐拉系統的連通性保持問題等。 第三, 將本框架應用於機器人群組,飛行器群或製造系統的分散式控制等問題中。

14219516.label: Realisation of objectives
14219516.value: The two objectives of the project are as follows: 1. Establish the adaptive distributed observer subject to directed switching networks. 2. Develop the certain equivalence control design framework for dealing with such problems as consensus/formation problem and cooperative output regulation problem of some classes of linear and nonlinear systems. Both objectives have been successfully achieved. The research has led to eight journal papers, and four conference papers including six papers in the two top journals of the control field, namely, IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control and Automatica. Six Phd students have been trained through conducting this project and two Phd students have got their PhD degree. The project has also led to collaboration with Prof. He Cai of South China University of Technology. Details are referred to Section 6 and Part C.

14219516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14219516.value: The main objective of this project is to develop a systematic framework to synthesize a distributed control law for complex systems such as rigid-body systems, Euler-Lagrange systems via the so-called certainty equivalence principle. The first objective of this project is to establish the adaptive distributed observer subject to directed switching networks. So far, we have successfully achieved this objective and the main findings are reported in Journal papers No. 1 and No. 5 and conference paper No. 4. In particular, Journal paper No. 1 established the adaptive distributed observer for rigid body systems subject to jointly connected switching networks. This observer in turn leads to a distributed control law for solving the leader-following attitude consensus problem of multiple rigid body systems over directed switching networks. . The second objective is to develop the certain equivalence control design framework for dealing with such problems as consensus/formation problem and cooperative output regulation problem of some classes of linear and nonlinear systems. We have also successfully accomplished this objective. The main findings can be found in Journal papers Nos. 4- 6. and conference paper No. 1. In particular, Journal paper No. 4 solved the consensus problem for multiple Euler-Lagrange systems, which can describe the motions of many practical systems such as robot manipulators, unmanned aerial vehicles. Journal paper No. 6 and conference paper No. 1 solved the consensus problem for multiple spacecraft systems, and Journal paper No. 5 established distributed observer for a class of nonlinear systems. Additionally, we have expanded the scope of the research along the following three directions: 1. Studied the cooperative control of discrete-time multi-agent systems. The main findings can be found in Journal paper No. 2. 2. Investigated the cooperative control of continuous-time networked systems by sampled data control and event-triggered control. The main findings can be found in Journal papers No. 7 and No. 8 and the conference paper No. 3. 3. Established distributed observer for unknown leader systems. The main findings can be found in Journal paper No. 3 and conference paper No. 1.

14219516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14219516.value: Two expansions of the project are summarized as follows: 1. This project has focused on the class of continuous-time multi-agent systems. The extension of this project to discrete-time or / and sampled-data multi-agent systems is on-going. 2. In this project, we have established a distributed observer for a known leader system. It is more interesting and more practical to establish a distributed observer for an unknown leader system. This generalization is under way.

14219516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14219516.value: Various cooperative control problems of networked multi-agent systems are motivated by such applications as the formation of mobile robots, multiple spacecraft attitude alignment, mobile sensor area coverage, control of electric power grids, biological cell sorting, and so on, and have been extensively studied since the early 2000s. What makes the cooperative control of multi-agent systems challenging is that the control law has to be distributed in order to satisfy communication constraints and to possess such advantages as simplicity, low cost and robustness against various uncertainties. The PI of this project had previously developed a distributed observer based control approach to handling general networked systems. However, a restriction associated with this distributed observer is that it is not purely distributed in the sense that each follower needs to know the system matrix of the leader system. In this project, the PI has further developed a so-called adaptive distributed observer to eliminate the assumption that each follower knows the system matrix of the leader system, thus leading to a purely distributed control law. The design method has been successfully applied to the consensus problem of the networked Euler-Lagrange systems and attitude synchronization of the multiple rigid-body systems in a more realistic setting.

14220716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14220716.value: Aim This study aims to develop a bioadhesive, growth factor-retentive, and fast-gelation hydrogel for biomedical applications. Background Osteoarthritis (OA) is characterized by the progressive degradation of the articular cartilage in articulating joints such as knee and hip joints. Early treatment of the cartilage lesions due to traumatic injuries helps reduce the incidence of OA. Cell-based cartilage tissue engineering is a promising approach for repairing cartilage lesions. However, direct administration of cells to the cartilage defects often results in limited efficacy due to significant cell death in the harsh environment of diseased joints. Therefore, there exists a huge demand for effective carrier biomaterials to provide a conducive environment to the delivered cells for better cartilage repair. Hydrogels are widely used as a biomaterial scaffold for cartilage tissue engineering. However, most of the conventional hydrogels lack the bioadhesiveness to bone and cartilage, especially in the presence of body fluids. This results in poor retention of the implanted hydrogels in the intended sites, thereby compromising the therapeutic outcome. Previous studies have shown that the catechol groups in the adhesive proteins from marine mussels are the key to the remarkable adhesiveness of these proteins under aqueous environment. Project Description Inspired by this finding, we propose to develop bioadhesive hydrogels based on our novel catechol conjugation technique using isothiocyanate instead of the conventional carbodiimide coupling. The obtained catechol-conjugated biopolymers form adhesive hydrogels at accelerated rate independent of pH. In this project, we will further investigate the gelation mechanism and optimize the gelation and physical properties of the hydrogels. Furthermore, we will evaluate these hydrogels as carrier materials for stem cell-based cartilage repair. The novelty of this work lies in four aspects. Firstly, the proposed conjugation of dopamine to biopolymer via isothiocyanate is novel and efficient without the undesirable side-reactions of the conventional protocols. Secondly, the unique reducing groups introduced by the isothiocyanate conjugation mimic the anti-oxidant components of natural adhesive proteins and therefore promote the adhesion of the hydrogels. Thirdly, the entirely different gelation mechanism of the obtained catechol-conjugated biopolymers exhibits unique features including being fast and pH-independent, and these features are desirable for cartilage repair. Lastly, few prior studies have investigated the efficacy of such bioadhesive hydrogels as carriers of stem cells and growth factors for cartilage repair. Significance The hydrogels developed in this study will be instrumental in developing stem cell therapies for repairing connective tissues including cartilage, ligaments, and meniscus. 目標 這項研究的目的是發展具有生物粘附性的並為生物醫學應用的快速凝膠水凝膠。 背景 骨關節炎（OA）特徵在於關節軟骨的逐漸退化。一項研究發現，約10％的50歲以上的香港居民從患有這種疾病。也有不少患者因軟骨損傷導致軟骨的全面退化。目前的治療軟骨退變的療法有許多局限性，如壽命有限，缺乏供體組織和疾病傳播的風險。使用治療細胞（包括幹細胞）的軟骨組織工程是一種用於軟骨修復的有前途的方法。但是，細胞在軟骨缺損部位的直接施用通常由於患病關節的惡劣環境導致大量細胞損失，因此療效有限。因此，臨床對能夠為細胞提供一個有利的環境並促進軟骨的癒合的載體生物材料存在著巨大的需求。因此，醫院存在的有效載體的生物材料的巨大臨床需求，用於承載幹細胞進行軟骨修復。水凝膠被廣泛用作用於軟骨組織工程的生物材料支架。然而，大多數現有的水凝膠的缺乏對骨及軟骨的粘附性，特別是在體液的存在的情況下。這導致在預期部位植入的水凝膠保留性差，從而損害的治療結果。先前的研究已經表明，在從貽貝粘合劑蛋白的兒茶酚基團的這些蛋白質具有顯著的粘合性的關鍵因素。 項目介紹 受此發現啟發，我們提出了一種基於異硫氰酸使用代替傳統的碳二亞胺偶聯我們新的鄰苯二酚結合的技術來開發生物粘合劑水凝膠。所得到的兒茶酚共軛生物聚合物形成以速率與pH無關，並加速粘合劑水凝膠的形成。在這個項目中，我們將進一步研究凝膠化機制，優化凝膠和水凝膠的物理性能。此外，我們將評估這些水凝膠的載體材料為基礎的細胞幹軟骨修復結果。這項工作的新穎之處在於四個方面。首先，多巴胺通過異硫氰酸生物聚合物的提議偶聯是新穎的和有效的，而不具有有害的副反應。其次，通過異硫氰酸酯共軛引入的唯一的還原基團模仿天然粘合劑的蛋白質的抗氧化劑組分，因此促進水凝膠的粘合性。第三，獲得的兒茶酚結合的生物聚合物的完全不同的凝膠化機制具有獨特的功能，包括快速且與pH值無關，而這些功能是理想的軟骨修復支架材料所需的。最後，很少有先前的研究調查了這樣的生物粘附凝膠作為幹細胞的載體和生長因子的軟骨修復的功效。 意義 在這項研究中開發的水凝膠將在促進幹細胞療法用於修復結締組織包括軟骨，韌帶和半月板治療的臨床轉化。

14220716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14220716.value: In summary, we developed a bio-inspired hydrogel based on thiourea-Cat coupling between the NCSN (thiourea) and Cat groups grafted to polymer backbone. The presence of the reducing NCSN groups helped reduce the excessive oxidization of Cat, thus preserving the adhesiveness of the hydrogels. Such hydrogels exhibited ultrafast gelation independent of pH, and simply spraying a low concentration of oxidant on top of the precursor achieved rapid in situ formation of stable and adhesive hydrogels. We have demonstrated the excellent adhesion strength of the hydrogel. We further showed that the hydrogel are excellent carrier material of hMSCs in vitro. The hydrogel could be applied to the GI lumen where the internal environment is relatively complex and challenging due to the secretion of digestive juice and constant gastric movements.

14220716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14220716.value: Our current data show that the developed bioadhesive hydrogels could be endoscopically delivered to the target ulcer site in the stomach of the pig and retained in situ for at least 48 hours. As a protective barrier formed at the ulcer surface to impede the infiltration of external catabolic factors and to accumulate growth factors around ulcer area, our hydrogels promote the ulcer healing process in both rodent and porcine models through suppression of inflammation and promotion of neovascularization and cellular proliferation. The therapeutic efficacy of our hydrogels is comparable to the drug treatment (sucralfate) group, suggesting that it is a promising alternative for the treatment of a number of clinical conditions including refractory ulcers in clinical scenarios.

14220716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14220716.value: In this project we have developed a bioadhesive hydrogel based on our novel catechol conjugation technique using isothiocyanate instead of the conventional carbodiimide coupling. The obtained catechol-conjugated biopolymers form adhesive hydrogels at accelerated rate independent of pH. In this project, we will further investigate the gelation mechanism and optimize the gelation and physical properties of the hydrogels.The novelty of this work lies in four aspects. Firstly, the proposed conjugation of dopamine to biopolymer via isothiocyanate is novel and efficient without the undesirable side-reactions of the conventional protocols. Secondly, the reducing groups introduced by the isothiocyanate conjugation better mimic the natural adhesive protein and therefore promote the adhesion of the hydrogels. Thirdly, the entirely different gelation mechanism of the obtained catechol-conjugated biopolymers exhibits unique features including being fast and pH-independent, and these features are desirable for cartilage repair. Lastly, few prior studies have investigated the efficacy of such bioadhesive hydrogels as carriers of stem cells and growth factors for disease treatment. The hydrogels developed in this study will be instrumental in developing stem cell therapies for a wide array of clinical conditions.

14221716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14221716.value: Graph has been widely used as a data structure to abstract complex relationships among entities in a form on which algorithms are designed and systems are developed to maintain information, understand the complex relationships, and discovery knowledge. There are many large graphs: online bibliographic networks, online social networks, Wikipedia, etc. In this project, we explore hidden global structures in a large graph for better analytical processing. This is motivated by the fact that there is a social hierarchy in a social network as studied in sociology and social network analysis. But it remains unknown how to find such social hierarchy by computing. In general, the issues are how much we understand a large graph from the viewpoint of its hidden backbone structure, which can be structured or even unstructured, how to find such hidden structures by computing efficiently, since such hidden global structures are believed to play an important role to determine what we can observe and what we can get from the entire graph. In this project, we focus on a directed graph. To identify a hidden structure, one way is to find a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph), which is cycle free. But, the number of DAGs for a directed graph is huge. It needs to find one that is representative and can be effectively used to conduct graph analytical processing tasks. In our preliminary study, the DAG found by eliminating the maximum Eulerian subgraph from the graph can serve the purpose. We plan to further explore the effectiveness and the efficiency. From a different viewpoint, a hidden structure may be unstructured as dimensions (or reference points). In theory, the first graph dimension was defined by Erdos, Harary, and Tutte in 1965, but in practice, the number of such graph dimensions is too large to be possibly handled for a large graph. We focus on finding new effective and efficient ways to conduct analytical processing over certain set of reference points for a large graph. Such a set of reference points needs to allow us to collect statistics on the occurrences of the structures in the large graph, and to enlarge/shrink in a drill-up/down manner to understand the statistics changes from different viewpoints. The academic significance of the project is of two folds. In addition to publications reporting the project finding, the methodology and techniques developed will be implemented to demonstrate the strength of our approach. 圖被廣泛的用作抽象實體間復雜關系的數據結構。現有很多大圖：比如文獻網絡，在線社交網絡，維基百科等。為維護信息，理解復雜結構，發現知識，圖算法和系統被設計研發。在這個項目中，我們探索大圖中隱藏的全局結構使其更好地用來分析處理大圖。而這正是受社會學與社交網絡分析所研究的一個事實啟發， 那就是在社交網絡中存在一個社會階層。但目前如何通過計算來找出這樣的社會階層仍然未知。我們的問題是通過隱藏的骨架結構，可能是結構化也可能非結構化的，理解一個大圖，並通過計算有效地找到這樣的隱藏結構，因為我們相信這樣一個隱藏的結構在幫助我們觀察分析整個圖等方面發揮著重要的作用。 在這個項目中，我們關注有向圖。為了找到這樣一個隱藏的結構，一種方法是找到一個DAG (有向無環圖)，一個不包括任何圈的結構。但是一個有向圖包含大量的DAG。我們需要找到一個具有代表性同時能夠有效地用來進行圖分析處理的DAG。在我們初步的研究中，通過刪除最大歐拉子圖得到的DAG可以達到這個目的。同時我們計劃進一步提高效率有有效性。從不同的觀點來看，一個隱藏的結構可能是非結構化的，比如多維的 (或參考點)。從理論上，第一個圖維度由Erdos, Harary和Tutte在1965年定義，但是在實際中，圖的維度往往太多以至於無法處理大圖。我們側重於尋找新的有效而高效方法，基於某組參考點對大圖進行分析處理。這樣一組參考點需要允許我們收集一些結構在圖上出現的統計數據，以及通過向上/向下鑽取以放大/縮小來從不同角度理解統計數據的變化。 這個項目的學術意義有兩個層面。除了發表論文報告項目發現，開發的方法與技術也將被實現用以展示我們方法的優勢

14221716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14221716.value: We summarize the main results below. First, we study clustering coefficient estimation in massive graphs. We propose a new sampling scheme to estimate the local clustering coefficient with error bounded, where global and binned degree-wise clustering coefficients can be considered as special cases. Based on our sampling scheme, we propose a new framework, and we further design an efficient MapReduce algorithm under this framework in DASFAA’17. Second, we study most influential community search over large social networks. Detecting the communities of high outer influence has particular interest in a wide range of applications. In ICDE’17, we propose a new community model, maximal kr-Clique community. Then, we design a novel tree-based index structure and develop four advanced index-based algorithms. In VLDBJ, we introduce a novel community model called k-influential community based on the concept of k-core to capture the influence of a community. Third, we study finding the maximum clique in massive graphs. In PVLDB’17, we devise a randomized algorithm for the maximum clique problem. Fourth, we study scalable simRank computation over large graphs. In ICDE’17, we design a Monte Carlo based method, UniWalk, to enable the fast top-k SimRank computation over large undirected graphs without indexing. Fifth, we study new network aligner for revealing large conserved functional components (e.g.. the alignment of protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks). Due to the computational intractability, global PPI network alignment remains challenging. We introduce a novel global network aligner based on graph matching method, called GMAlign in BIBM’17. Sixth, we study keyword search on RDF graphs in CIKM’17, and study natural language question/answering in CIKM’17. Seventh, we study DAG reduction for fast answering reachability queries over graphs in SIGMOD’17. Eighth, we study a fast order-based approach for core maintenance in ICDE’17. Ninth, we study how to support graph processing in RDBMSs in SIGMOD’17. Tenth, we explore triangle-free dense structures. We focus on K3,3 where there are two subsets of three vertices, a vertex in a subset has an edge connected to every vertex in another subset while it does not have an edge to any other vertex in the same subset. Such K3,3 implies a philosophy contradiction. However, we find such induced K3,3 does exist frequently, and they do not disappear over time over a real academic collaboration network. We report it in TKDE’18. Eleventh, we study skyline community search in multi-valued networks in SIGMOD’18. We model a network as a multi-valued network where each node has d numerical attributes (i.e., h-index, diversity, PageRank, similarity score, etc.). A skyline community is a maximal connected k-core that cannot be dominated by the other connected k-cores in the d-dimensional attribute space.

14221716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14221716.value: With the rapid growth of social networks and new applications, there are many possible hidden global structures still to be investigated. We will continue to work on these issues.

14221716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14221716.value: This project is to find hidden structures over a large graph to help graph analytical tasks, and find such structures efficiently. As a classic measure to characterize the connectivity of graphs, clustering coefficient and its variants are of particular interest in graph structural analysis. However, the largest of graphs may have nodes and edges in billion scale, which makes the simple task of computing clustering coefficients complicated and expensive. We investigate a new sampling scheme to estimate the local clustering coefficient with error bounded, where global and binned degree-wise clustering coefficient is a special case. Triadic closure is ubiquitous in social networks, which refers to the property among three individuals, A, B, and C, such that if there exist strong ties between A-B and A-C, then there must be a strong or weak tie between B-C. We explore triangle-free dense structures, K3,3, where there are two subsets of three vertices, a vertex in a subset has an edge connected to every vertex in another subset while it does not have an edge to any other vertex in the same subset. Such K3,3 implies a philosophy contradiction: (a) Any two individuals are friends if they have no common friends, and (b) Any two individuals are not friends if they have common friends. We find such induced K3,3 does exist frequently, and they do not disappear over time over a real academic collaboration network. Such K3,3 found helps to find new stars collaborated by well-known figures who themselves do not collaborate. Our findings are reported in major international journals and top international conferences.

14222816.value: 大規模圖計算的高性能系統的設計

14222816.label: Project Objectives
14222816.value: To study the performance limits of a distributed graph computing system. To build an efficient distributed system for large-scale graph analytics.

To build an efficient distributed system for large-scale graph analytics.

14222816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14222816.value: The project proposes to design and develop an efficient distributed system for large-scale graph analytics, for both small and big companies. Graph analytics is an important class of data analysis, thanks to the flexibility of using graphs to model and study objects and their relationships from a wide range of application domains. Many parallel graph computing systems have been proposed in recent years, but there are important issues that remain to be answered, including scalability with high performance (i.e., handling very large graphs efficiently with affordable hardware), the quest for the best computing model, and efficient fault tolerance. Above all, the question how fast a distributed graph computing system can be has largely been neglected as existing work mostly attempted to improve previous systems by identifying and addressing their limitations. We propose a more systematic approach by benchmarking the performance of distributed graph computing systems for running different algorithms on different graphs with different hardware. With the results of the benchmarks, we will then study different computing models in order to find the best model for different application scenarios. We also propose to achieve better scalability using compression techniques, and design more efficient fault tolerance mechanisms. Finally, we discuss how our proposed system will be useful to real-world applications. 本項目提議設計並開發一套用於大規模圖分析的高性能分佈式系統，從而滿足大小企業的日常需求。圖分析已經成為數據分析中非常重要的一部分，這歸功於圖模型能靈活地對現實生活中的實體以及它們之間的聯繫進行建模。近幾年湧現出許多並行的圖計算系統，但仍有一些重要問題亟待解決，其中包括兼具高性能的可擴展性（例如，在經濟可負擔得起的硬件上處理非常大的圖），最佳計算模型的追求，和高效的容錯能力。特別地，已有的工作大多數是嘗試發現現有系統的局限性，解決這些局限並提高性能，然而忽視了一個很重要的問題，即分佈式圖計算系統最快能有多快。我們提出一個更系統的測評方法，在不同的硬件資源上運行各類算法處理不同的圖數據，從而全面地衡量一個分佈式圖計算系統的性能。有了這些評測數據，我們將進一步研究不同的計算模型，從而為不同的應用場景找到最好的選擇。我們同時使用壓縮技術和設計更加高效的容錯機制，讓系統能被更好地擴展。最後，我們討論我們提出的系統對現實應用有怎樣的好處。

14224316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14224316.value: Human attributes are describable characteristics of face, body, and attire. For instance, a person can be described by ‘oval’ and ‘smiling’ face, with a ‘small’ mouth, and a ‘tall’ body ‘wearing casual suit’. Automated recognition on such fine-grained attributes is important for video-based business intelligence and security applications, e.g., person recognition and re-identification. In most surveillance scenarios, clear close-shots of face and body regions are hardly available. The absence of high-resolution target images not only adversely affects human inspection, but also reduces the performance of automated attribute recognition. The objective of this project is to devise a new method that can simultaneously perform attribute recognition and infer high-resolution image from low-resolution ones (a.k.a. hallucination or super-resolution). These two tasks are conventionally addressed as independent problems. We believe that attribute recognition and image hallucination can benefit each other. Specifically, accurate attribute recognition relies on detailed visual features from high-quality images to infer the semantics; image hallucination, on the other hand, infers high-resolution images through bottom-up approach but would benefit from top-down semantic supervision. The problem is non-trivial since we are facing with low-resolution images captured in the wild, with the presence of significant noise and blurring, as well as body/facial parts mis- alignment across images. The latter problem is especially detrimental to image hallucination. In addition, the joint learning of the two tasks is challenging due to their very different optimisation cost functions. The dimension to optimise in image hallucination is much higher compared to that in attribute prediction (thousands of pixels versus tens of attributes). The learning difficulty is further compounded by the sparse and imbalanced attribute data. We address the aforementioned problems through (i) a novel end-to-end global-local deep convolutional network (DCN), which is specially designed to work on low-resolution inputs, and to better capture the global context and local parts, (ii) multi-tasks learning to handle the different cost functions more effectively, which allows the two tasks to create synergy via joint optimisation in the training process, and (iii) a new DCN pre-training approach that comes with a novel quintuplet sampling and a large-margin triple-header hinge loss to cope with the imbalance issue. The experience we gain in this project will surely provide valuable insight to creating new tools for video surveillance applications, where the resolution of face and pedestrian images are typically low, yet the details of features are crucial for human inspection and machine-based attribute recognition. 行人屬性被定義為可通過臉部、身體和服裝等可描述的特徵。例如我們可以描述一個人有一張“橢圓形”和“微笑”的臉、“小嘴巴”、和一個“穿著休閒西裝”的“修長”身軀。這種細粒度的屬性自動識別在基於視頻分析的智能商業和安全應用中，例如行人識別和跟踪，有很高的價值。一般現有的監控系統難以拍到清晰的臉部和身體特寫。缺乏高分辨率目標圖像不但影響人工目測檢查，同時也降低了自動化屬性識別的性能。這個項目的目標是設計一個可以同時從低分辨率圖像執行屬性識別​​和高分辨率圖像重構（又名幻構或超分辨率）的新方法。這兩個任務通常被視為獨立的問題。我們相信，屬性識別和圖像幻構是可以相互受益的。具體來說，準確的屬性識別依賴於從高質量圖像裡得到的視覺特徵以推斷語義;另一方面，圖像幻構可受益於語義的高層次監督。解決這個問題的難度在於如何有效抵抗低分辨率圖像中的噪聲和模糊，及多張圖像裡的身體或面部對準問題。後者往往對圖像幻構帶來很大的困擾。除此之外，屬性識別​​和圖像幻構需要不同的優化目標。圖像幻構的千萬像素比幾十個屬性識別的優化維度高得多。如何有效地平衡兩個任務的優化是一個富挑戰性的問題。屬性數據的稀疏和正負樣本不平衡的問題進一步加劇學習的困難度。我們通過以下幾個方法解決以上的問題：（i）提出一種新穎的端至端全局加局部深度學習卷積網絡（DCN）。它可以有效地在低分辨率圖像上操作並且能更好地捕獲全局上下文和局部信息。 （ii）提出新的多任務學習方法以更有效地處理不同的優化函數，允許兩個任務在訓練過程中通過聯合優化協同合作，以及（iii）提出新的DCN訓練方法，以五重採樣和三頭鉸鏈損失函數以應付正負樣本不平衡的問題。我們相信在這個項目中累積的經驗和實驗結果可以為視頻監控應用提供有價值的解決方案。

14224316.label: Realisation of objectives
14224316.value: First objective ============= To address the image hallucination problem, we have formulated a new method for generating imagery textures through generative adversarial learning. Although the context we were addressing is fashion synthesis, the same technique can be extended to face easily. This work has been reported in the mid-term report. In another work, we include spatial-wise semantic information for image super-resolution. The method captures both local and global parts information effectively. In particular, we show that it is possible to recover textures faithful to semantic classes. In particular, we only need to modulate features of a few intermediate layers in a single network conditioned on semantic segmentation probability maps. This is made possible through a novel Spatial Feature Transform (SFT) layer that generates affine transformation parameters for spatial-wise feature modulation. SFT layers can be trained end-to-end together with the SR network using the same loss function. During testing, it accepts an input image of arbitrary size and generates a high-resolution image with just a single forward pass conditioned on the categorical priors. Our final results show that an SR network equipped with SFT can generate more realistic and visually pleasing textures in comparison to state-of-the-art Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) and EnhanceNet. We also carefully study the use of generative adversarial network for image hallucination. We found that adversarial training helps generating more realistic textures and it should help attribute recognition in turn. We carefully study the SRGAN, which is the state-of-the-art method for super-resolution. We found that the hallucinated details are often accompanied with unpleasant artifacts. To further enhance the visual quality, we thoroughly study three key components of SRGAN – network architecture, adversarial loss and perceptual loss, and improve each of them to derive an Enhanced SRGAN (ESRGAN). In particular, we introduce the Residual-in-Residual Dense Block (RRDB) without batch normalization as the basic network building unit. Moreover, we borrow the idea from relativistic GAN to let the discriminator predict relative realness instead of the absolute value. Finally, we improve the perceptual loss by using the features before activation, which could provide stronger supervision for brightness consistency and texture recovery. Benefiting from these improvements, the proposed ESRGAN achieves consistently better visual quality with more realistic and natural textures than SRGAN and won the first place in the PIRM2018-SR Challenge. With the aforementioned works, we fulfilled the first objective. Second objective ============= An important problem we need to solve in this project is face detection. We formulated a new method for multi-task attribute prediction and face detection. The paper has been published by IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence. We propose a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) for face detection leveraging on facial attributes based supervision. We observe a phenomenon that part detectors emerge within CNN trained to classify attributes from uncropped face images, without any explicit part supervision. The observation motivates a new method for finding faces through scoring facial parts responses by their spatial structure and arrangement. The scoring mechanism is data-driven, and carefully formulated considering challenging cases where faces are only partially visible. This consideration allows our network to detect faces under severe occlusion and unconstrained pose variations. Our method achieves promising performance on popular benchmarks including FDDB, PASCAL Faces, AFW, and WIDER FACE. The paper has now accumulated over 480 citations. This study helps us to achieve the second objective. One of the objectives of this project is to recognize facial attributes robustly. Facial age can be considered as a kind of facial attribute. We introduce a novel approach for annotating large quantity of in-the-wild facial images with high-quality posterior age distribution as labels. Each posterior provides a probability distribution of estimated ages for a face. Our approach is motivated by observations that it is easier to distinguish who is the older of two people than to determine the person’s actual age. Given a reference database with samples of known ages and a dataset to label, we can transfer reliable annotations from the former to the latter via human-in-the-loop comparisons. We show an effective way to transform such comparisons to posterior via fully-connected and SoftMax layers, so as to permit end-to-end training in a deep network. We then train a multi-task network that jointly performs ordinal hyperplane classification and posterior distribution learning. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on popular benchmarks such as MORPH2, Adience, and the newly proposed MegaAge. The study of this multi-task network helps us to achieve the second objective. In addition, this method will help to hallucinate faces of different ages, helping us to meet the first objective of this project too. With the aforementioned works, we fulfilled the second objective. Third objective ============= To address the third objective, we demonstrate that more discriminative deep representation can be learned by enforcing a deep network to maintain inter-cluster margins both within and between classes. This tight constraint effectively reduces the class imbalance inherent in the local data neighborhood, thus carving much more balanced class boundaries locally. We show that it is easy to deploy angular margins between the cluster distributions on a hypersphere manifold. Such learned Cluster-based Large Margin Local Embedding (CLMLE), when combined with a simple k-nearest cluster algorithm, shows significant improvements in accuracy over existing methods on both face recognition and face attribute prediction tasks that exhibit imbalanced class distribution. This paper is published in TPAMI, the top journal in computer vision. With the work aforementioned, we met the third objective of this project. Forth objective ============= In this project, we also collected a new large-scale face attribute dataset on facial age (called MegaAge). The dataset consists of 41,941 faces annotated with age posterior distributions. See http://mmlab.ie.cuhk.edu.hk/projects/MegaAge/ We also collected WIDER Attribute is a large-scale human attribute dataset. It contains 13789 images belonging to 30 scene categories, and 57524 human bounding boxes each annotated with 14 binary attributes. See http://mmlab.ie.cuhk.edu.hk/projects/WIDERAttribute.html With the two datasets, we met the fourth objective of this project.

14224316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14224316.value: As research outcome, 2 journal papers and 5 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI) is the best journal on computer vision and machine learning with an impact factor of 17.861. Five papers were published on the top conferences in computer vision (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and BMVC). In this project, we proposed novel methods for image super-resolution and hallucination. In particular, we discovered the importance of decomposing a complex generative process into multiple conditional stages (Part C.9 No. 1). This helps us to understand the better use of GANs in our subsequent face hallucination and super-resolution studies. We further developed a new approach known as Spatial Feature Transform (SFT) that is capable of altering the behavior of an super-resolution network through just transforming the features of some intermediate layers of the network (Part C.9 No. 3). We devised ESRGAN model that achieves consistently better perceptual quality than previous super-resolution methods. In particular, we have formulated a novel architecture containing several RDDB blocks without BN layers. We have also introduced the use of relativistic GAN as the discriminator, which learns to judge whether one image is more realistic than another, guiding the generator to recover more detailed textures (Part C.9 No. 4). In addition, we discovered a novel notion of interpolation in parameter space, and its application in low-level vision tasks (Part C.9 No. 5). In attribute recognition, we proposed new methods that can address the class imbalance issue, which is the main challenge in attribute recognition. We proposed a Cluster-based Large Margin Local Embedding method that works remarkably well when just combined with a simple k-nearest cluster classifier (Part C.8 No. 2) for class imbalance problem. In the process of our research, we found that face detection a pre-requisite for attribute recognition and thus we developed a new method for face detection based on facial part responses (Part C.8 No. 1).

14224316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14224316.value: In our study, we found that generative adversarial learning performs exceedingly well on the image super-resolution task. We will further pursue this research direction to develop more powerful GAN-based methods for the task. In particular, we believe that we should better employ the image prior captured in pre-trained GANs for better texture and details recovery.

14224316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14224316.value: The objective of this project is to devise new methods that can simultaneously perform attribute recognition and infer high-resolution image from low-resolution ones (a.k.a. hallucination or super-resolution). These two tasks are conventionally addressed as independent problems. We believe that attribute recognition and image hallucination can benefit each other. Specifically, accurate attribute recognition relies on detailed visual features from high-quality images to infer the semantics; image hallucination, on the other hand, infers high-resolution images through bottom-up approach but would benefit from top-down semantic supervision. In this project, we have developed effective approaches that can considerably improve the quality of low-resolution images and recognize attributes given highly imbalanced class distribution.

14225616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14225616.value: Conventional multitouch visualization systems mostly consider only 2D finger contacts on the touch surface to support the user interaction with the visualization. So far, rich contextual and dynamic information contained in user's hand and wrist above the touch surface remain silent and unexplored. With advances in user interaction technologies and commodity hardware devices, we aim to develop in this project cost-effective methods to enrich our interaction capability and performance in multitouch-based medical data visualization on tablet through joint interaction among tablets, smart watches and depth sensing. In summary, we will take a cost-effective approach to develop our solution with commodity hardware devices. Our key idea is to integrate partial hand geometry and motion information estimated from depth sensing (depth sensor) and motion sensing (smart watch), and then correlate these information temporally with finger contact information on tablet surface. By this, we can make use of the real-time hand and wrist dynamic information to enrich our 2D multitouch interaction in the medical data visualization. For example, we shall be able to effectively differentiate touches from different hands and from different fingers, support finger-tilt and pinch-tilt dynamics, authenticate user touches, etc. By this, we could directly create a clipping plane on the tablet visualization with bare hand, and interactively explore the visualization by simply tilting and moving our fingers and wrist above the tablet surface. Altogether, we will have five research tasks in this project: 1) Explore joint interaction between depth sensing and multitouch on tablets 2) Explore joint interaction between smart watches and multitouch on tablets 3) Develop GPU-based medical visualization methods on commodity tablets 4) Construct collaborative interaction model with different levels of authentication through motion correlation 5) Study the design space of interaction and develop user interaction methods for assorted medical visualization scenarios, e.g., volume visualization, medical image analysis, etc. To summarize, this project is built upon the expertise of the PI and Co-I who have done extensive research on medical visualization, medical image analysis, and user interaction methodologies. In particular, our ultimate goal in the project is to develop an efficient and low-cost medical visualization environment with commodity hardware devices, so that the interactive environment can enhance our interaction capability and performance with the medical data visualization while being easily adoptable for clinical and educational usage. 傳統的多點觸控可視化系統大多僅考慮通過觸屏上的二維手指接觸來支持用戶的可視化交互。到目前為止，位於觸屏上空的包含在手部與腕關節的豐富的上下文與動態信息仍未被利用。隨著用戶交互技術以及商業硬件設備的發展，在本項目中我們期望通過平板，智能手錶以及深度感知的聯合交互，開發低成本的方法來強化平板上基於多點觸控的醫學數據可視化的交互能力與表現。 整體而言，我們將採用一個高性價比的方法來開發我們在商業硬件設備上的解決方案。我們的關鍵思路是結合手部的局部幾何結構以及從深度感知（深度傳感器）和運動感知（智能手錶）中估計的運動信息，將這些信息與平板表面的手指觸控信息進行時間上的聯繫。基於此，我們即可利用實時的手部與腕關節動態信息來豐富我們在醫學數據可視化中的二維多點觸控交互。例如，我們應能夠高效區分來自於不同手不同手指的觸摸，支持單指傾斜與雙指傾斜操作，認證用戶觸控，等等。基於此，我們能夠通過裸手直接創建一個剪切面，並且通過簡單的傾斜和移動我們的手指和腕關節來交互式地探索可視化。 在這個項目裡我們將有五個研究目標： （1） 探索深度感知與平板上多點觸控的聯合交互 （2） 探索智能手錶與平板上多點觸控的聯合交互 （3） 開發運行於商業平板上，基於GPU的醫學可視化技術 （4） 通過動作關聯，搭建一個擁有不同級別認證的組合交互模型 （5） 研究交互的設計空間以及開發針對各種醫學可視化情景下的用戶交互手段，比如體素可視化，醫學圖像分析等等 我們在這個項目裡的最終目標是開發一個基於商業硬件設備的高效並低成本的醫學可視化環境，這樣的交互環境能夠提高醫學數據可視化的交互性能與表現，同時也易適用於臨床和教學的使用。

14225616.label: Realisation of objectives
14225616.value: This project aims to develop an efficient and low-cost medical visualization environment with commodity hardware devices so that the interactive environment can enhance our interaction capability and performance with the medical data visualization while being easily adaptable for clinical and educational usage. To achieve this goal, we perform various research studies that contain medical image analysis, medical image visualization, depth sensing, image processing, and human-computer interaction. First, medical image analysis is a fundamental and important research issue in this project. We conduct research and develop several methods for multiple medical modalities, including MRI, fundus, histology, and surgery videos, which will be further transferred into our system. (a)We present a novel deep network architecture, namely ψ-Net, for sub-cortical brain structure segmentation, aiming at selectively aggregating features and boosting the information propagation in a deep convolutional neural network. To achieve this, we first formulate a densely convolutional LSTM module (DC-LSTM) to selectively aggregate the convolutional features with the same spatial resolution at the same stage of a CNN and then stack multiple DC-LSTMs from the deepest stage to the shallowest stage to progressively enrich low-level feature maps with high-level context. (b) We present a novel patch-based Output Space Adversarial Learning framework to segment optic disc and cup from different fundus images. We first employ a lightweight and efficient network with the morphology-aware segmentation loss to generate accurate and smooth predictions and then exploit unsupervised domain adaptation model to improve the generalization of the segmentation network. (c) We present a novel uncertainty-aware semi-supervised framework for left atrium segmentation from 3D MR images. Our framework can effectively leverage the unlabeled data by encouraging consistent predictions of the same input under different perturbations. (d) We propose a novel Instance Relation Network (IRNet) for robust overlapping cell segmentation by exploring instance relation interaction. (e) We propose a novel framework to leverage instrument motion information, by incorporating a derived temporal prior to an attention pyramid network for accurate segmentation in minimally invasive surgery video. Second, human-centered computing and human-computer interaction are the key issues in this project to enrich our interaction capability and performance in multitouch-based medical data visualization. (a) We design the TwistIn, which is a simple gesture that takes a smartwatch as an authentication token for fast access and control of other smart devices. Our mechanism is particularly useful for devices such as smartphones, smart glasses, and small IoT objects. We implemented TwistIn, collected thousands of gesture samples, and conducted various experiments to evaluate our prototype system and show that it achieved over 95% detection accuracy. (b) We propose a novel approach to realize augmented virtual reality (AVR), which first analyzes the physical environment in the user’s egocentric view through depth sensing and deep learning, then acquire the layout and geometry of the surrounding objects, and further explore their affordances. Based on the above information, we create a visual guidance path and hybrid user interfaces to augment the AVR interaction. (c) We explore the concept of virtually-extended proprioception by appending virtual body parts mimicking real body parts to users’ avatars, to provide a spatial reference to virtual targets. Our studies suggest that our approach facilitates more efficient target selection in VR as compared to no reference or using an everyday object as reference. Besides, by cultivating users’ sense of ownership on the appended virtual body part, we can further enhance target selection performance. Third, medical data visualization is an important module in interactive visualization platform. We research several representative medical data, including point cloud, EEG singles, and mesh, which will be further transferred into our system. (a) Point cloud is a fundamental 3D representation produced by depth sensors. Learning and analyzing 3D point clouds with deep networks is challenging due to the sparseness and irregularity of the data. We present a point cloud upsampling network to improve the performance for point cloud up-sampling. (b) We propose a novel multiclass classifier for single-trial EEG data in matrix form, namely multiclass support matrix machine (MSMM), to improve the classification accuracy of multiclass EEG signals, and hence enhancing the performance of EEG-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) involving multiple mental activities. The proposed MSMM can leverage the structural information encoded in EEG matrices for more accurate multiclass classification, and hence improve the performance of BCI systems with multiple tasks. (c) We present a deep normal filtering network, called DNF-Net, for mesh denoising. To better capture local geometry, our network processes the mesh in terms of local patches extracted from the mesh. Overall, DNF-Net is an end-to-end network that takes patches of facet normals as inputs and directly outputs the corresponding denoised facet normals of the patches. In this way, we can reconstruct the geometry from the denoised normals with feature preservation. We present comprehensive experiments to evaluate our method and demonstrate its superiority over the state of the art on both synthetic and real-scanned meshes. Last, the techniques for medical image analysis are usually developed from computer vision and image processing. Hence, we research fundamental but challenging vision tasks, which include shadow detection, saliency detection, and texture smoothing. (a) We present a novel deep neural network design for shadow detection by analyzing the spatial image context in a direction-aware manner. To achieve this, we formulate the direction-aware attention mechanism in a spatial recurrent neural network (RNN) by introducing attention weights when aggregating spatial context features in the RNN. By learning these weights through training, we can recover the direction-aware spatial context (DSC) for detecting shadows. (b) Salient object detection aims to highlight the most visually distinctive objects or regions in an image. First, we develop a novel deep saliency network equipped with recurrently aggregated deep features (RADF) to more accurately detect salient objects from an image by fully exploiting the complementary saliency information captured in different layers. Then, we propose a novel recurrent residual refinement network (R3Net) equipped with residual refinement blocks (RRBs) to more accurately detect salient regions of an input image. (c) Texture smoothing aims to smooth out textures in images while retaining the prominent structures. We present a saliency-aware approach to the problem by first designing a deep saliency network with guided non-local blocks for learning long-range pixel dependencies and then formulating a joint optimization framework to take saliency information when iteratively separating textures from structures.

14225616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14225616.value: In our future work, we shall develop a flexible and user-friendly development toolkit that contains the designed algorithms on user interaction, medial image analysis, and medical data visualization in a user-friendly system, seek more collaborations, and transfer the algorithms for real applications. Our proposed course of actions include: - Collaborate with doctors to transfer the developed algorithms for real applications. - Provide software licensing for educational purposes and beta testing. - Apply research grants to further our research in medical visualization and multitouch interaction. - Integrate our medical data processing technologies into a tailored interface to build an interactive environment, which can be easily adoptable for clinical and educational usage.

14225616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14225616.value: Conventional multitouch visualization systems mostly consider only 2D finger contacts on the touch surface to support user interaction with the visualization. This project explores the rich contextual and dynamic information contained in the user's hand and wrist above the touch surface and develops cost-effective methods to enrich our interaction capability for medical data visualization. In this project, we have developed a series of deep-learning-based algorithms to analyze the medical data with multiple modalities, including MRI, fundus, histology, and surgery videos. The proposed algorithms achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple tasks, including brain segmentation, prostate segmentation, joint optic disc, and cup segmentation, 3D left atrium segmentation, cervical cell segmentation, and surgery video analysis. The deliverable of medical data analysis can be transferred into our system for visualization. Then, we have developed the systems for collaborative interaction, which helps to improve the immersion for users and enrich the multitouch interaction in the medical data visualization. Next, we have explored the geometry information estimated from depth sensing to perform point cloud up-sampling and mesh denoising. Finally, we have developed deep-learning-based methods for natural image processing and the developed algorithms enhance the feature representation capability of deep networks, thus improving the performance of medical data analysis.

14225916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14225916.value: In neoclassical finance, investors trade financial assets to maximize their utility of consumption and terminal wealth. Recent studies in behavioral finance, however, show that in addition to intermediate consumption and terminal wealth, investors are also sensitive to sale gains and losses. The utility experienced by the investors regarding sale gains and losses is referred to as realization utility. In this proposal, the PI first proposes a trading model that accounts for realization utility. In this model, the agent maximizes her terminal wealth utility and realization utility by switching her position between a stock and a risk-free asset. The stock price is assumed to be regime switching with unobservable regimes. The PI plans to solve this trading problem by the use of Wonham filter and dynamic programming. Finally, the PI plans to use this model to explain why investors trade too much, an empirical puzzle that cannot be explained by neoclassical finance. The PI then attempts to explain disposition effect, which is an empirical finding that investors tend to sell winners and hold losers. To this end, the PI plans to generalize the trading model with realization utility by allowing the agent to trade multiple stocks. The approach to this generalized problem is a combination of Wonham filter and dynamic programming. To test whether this multi-stock trading model can explain the disposition effect, the PI plans to compare the realized returns of the stock the agent sells at a gain and the stock the agent holds at a loss in a fixed subsequent period. A reference point determines the gain and loss experienced by an investor in her stock trading. Abundant empirical evidence reveals that when selling a stock, investors’ reference points adapt to the stock’s prior gain and loss and to the stock’s historical average price. The PI plans to propose a trading model to account for the reference point adaptation. The PI plans to study and compare the trading behavior of two types of investors: adaptive investors who realize prospectively their reference adaptation and naive investors who fail to do so. Finally, the PI plans to study a trading model with realization utility in which an investor can diversify between a stock and a risk-free asset. Consequently, in this model both portfolio rebalancing and realization utility motivate the investors to sell winners and hold losers, and the PI plans to study which of the two is the main motivation. 在新古典金融學的研究中，一個通常的假設是投資者以最大化他們的消費以及財富的期望效用為目的。近些年來，大量的研究表明除了消費以及財富，投資者還關心每個交易的盈利以及虧損，由此產生的效用被稱為實現效用。 在這個提案中，我們首先提出一個基於實現效用的交易模型。在這個模型中，投資者可以選擇投資一個股票或者無風險資產，他們的目標是最大化他們的財富效用以及實現效用。我們假設股票價格服從一個狀態轉化模型，暨股票價格取決於市場的狀態，譬如牛市或者熊市，而且市場的狀態是不能直接觀測到的。我們將會利用Wonham濾波以及動態規劃原理來解出這個交易問題。最后，我們計劃用這個交易模型來解釋一個市場上常見的，長久以來卻不能被新古典金融學解釋的現象，暨為什麼投資者過於頻繁的交易以致降低了投資收益。 我們接著嘗試解釋另一個市場上常見的，長久以來卻不能被新古典金融學解釋的現象，暨所謂的處置效應：投資者趨於過長時間地持有正在虧損的股票而過快地賣掉正在盈利的股票。為此，我們計劃擴展上述交易模型：投資者有多個股票可以選擇。同樣的，我們計劃用Wonham濾波以及動態規劃原理來解出這個交易問題。接著，在這個模型中，我們計劃比較投資者賣掉的，正在盈利的，以及投資者沒有賣掉的，正在虧損的股票的后繼收益，以此來檢驗這個模型是否能解釋處置效應。 接下來，我們來研究參照點，暨投資者用於和當前股票價格比較的一個值，從而在心裡上覺得他們是處於盈利還是虧損狀態。譬如，某個投資者的參照點可以是股票的買價的百分之十，那麼即使股價上漲了百分之五，該投資者在心理上仍然認為他處於虧損狀態。近些年來，大量的實驗結果表明當賣掉一隻股票的時候，投資者的參照點不僅依賴於買價，還依賴於當前股價以及歷史平均股價。我們計劃提出一個包含參照點變化的股票交易模型，繼而研究兩種投資者的交易行為：第一種投資者事先意識到他們將來的參照點依賴於當時和歷史平均股價，而第二種投資者沒有。 最后，我們計劃考慮一個允許投資者分散投資的，包含實現效用的交易模型。在這個模型中，由分散投資導致的投資組合調整以及實現效用都會促使投資者持有正在虧損的股票和賣掉正在盈利的股票，暨引起處置效應。我們希望研究哪種原因更為重要。

14225916.label: Realisation of objectives
14225916.value: Objective 1 has been completely achieved. The details are as follows: We first propose a model of optimal stock trading with realization utility in a geometric Brownian motion setting, where an investor buys and sells a stock sequentially to maximize her utility of realizing gains and losses at each sale and of her terminal wealth; see the research output He and Yang (2018, Mathematical Finance) in Part C-8-1. Second, we extend the above model by changing the stock dynamics from the geometric Brownian motion to a regime-switching process with two observable regimes, referred to as the bull and bear regimes, respectively. The stock has the same volatility but different mean return under these two regimes, and the transition of the two regimes is modeled by a two-state, observable Markov chain. See Chapter 2 of the research output Shao (2019, Phd Thesis) in Part C-10-1 for details. Third, we revise the setting of the second model by considering unobservable regimes, so the investor has to infer the regime from the historical stock price; see Chapter 3 of Shao (2019). The above three different models, which build on different stock price dynamics, allow us to study the effect of regime-switching on stock trading with realization utility. Moreover, the first two models can be used as benchmarks for the third model. Finally, we consider a stock trading model with diversification. In this model, unlikely the above three ones, the investor can diversify between the risk-free asset and the stock. The objective of the investor is again to maximize the realization utility and wealth utility. Assuming a geometric Brownian motion stock price, proportional transaction costs of trading the stock, and (piecewise) linear utility functions, we are able to formulate this stock trading model into a stochastic singular control problem. This formulation is more convenient than the stochastic impulse control formulation that is originally proposed. The final model is not included in Shao (2019) because it is completed by another PhD student. We have completed most analysis of the model and will finish writing up a paper soon. Moreover, the paper will be part of a thesis. Objective 2 has been completely achieved. The details are as follows: For the first model, we first derive a variational inequality heuristically. Then, we prove that the value function of the stock trading problem, namely, the optimal utility of selling and buying the stock, is the unique viscosity solution to the variational inequality. For details, see He and Yang (2018). For the second model, we consider the case in which the terminal wealth and gain-loss utility functions are linear. Because of regime switching, the value function depends not only on the investor’s prior gain or loss in the stock but also on the current market regime. We prove that the value function is the unique solution to a system of variational inequalities. Thanks to the linear utility functions, we are able to derive the solution to the variational inequalities in closed form. For details, see Chapter 2 of Shao (2019). For the third model, we apply Wonham filter to infer the probability that the market is in the bull regime given the historical stock price. Consequently, the value function and the investor’s decision depend not only on the investor’s prior gain or loss in the stock but also on the above probability. We prove that the value function is the unique viscosity solution to a variational inequality. Because of the unobservable regimes, we are not able to solve the value function in closed form. Instead, we use the penalty method to solve it numerically. For details, see Chapter 3 of Shao (2019). For the fourth model, we formulate the stock trading problem as a stochastic singular control problem. Compared to classical portfolio selection models with proportional transaction cost, in our model, we need an additional state variable---the investor’s prior gain and loss. We prove that the value function is the unique solution to an HJB equation. The HJB equation consists of three terms, which correspond to the actions of no trading, buying the stock, and selling the stock, respectively. Thanks to the (piecewise) linear utility functions, we show that the value function is homogeneous and thus we are able to reduce the dimension of the state space from three to two. Objective 3 has been completely achieved. See below for details: In the first model, we attempt to explain the disposition effect. To this end, we compute various statistics related to the disposition effect, such as average gain and loss at a sale, probability of selling at a gain, the fractions of time that the stock has an unrealized gain and loss, average stock holding time, percentage of gains realized, percentage of losses realized, and their ratio. Then, we compare these statistics from our model with the empirical counterparts in the literature. We find that we cannot match the empirical estimates with reasonable utility parameter values. This suggests that the first model cannot explain the disposition effect perfectly. For details, see He and Yang (2018). We also consider the possibility that the investor’s reference point adapts to prior gains and losses. Then, different types of investors may have different beliefs of how their reference points adapt: some investors may foresee the adaptation of their reference points, but others may not. We compare the trading strategies of these two types of investors, and find that the first type of investors sells the stock more frequently at a gain and less frequently at a loss than the second type of investors. The above result is not published because of the page limit when He and Yang (2018) is accepted for publication. In the second model, we focus on the expected duration of an investment episode, which is inversely related to the trading frequency, and the expected return. We find that the more the investor weighs the realization utility, the more frequently she trades and the lower the expected return is. This shows that our model can explain the excessive trading puzzle. See Chapter 2 of Shao (2019) for details. In the third model, we show that it can match the empirical estimates of a set of disposition-effect related statistics better than the first model. Moreover, we show that it can generate empirically observed V-shape pattern for stock selling: the frequency of selling at a gain is increasing with respect to the magnitude of the gain, and so is the frequency of selling at a loss. Thus, the third model can explain the disposition effect. See Chapter 3 of Shao (2019) for details. In the fourth model, we show that realization utility generates diversification. Moreover, this model generates some well-known follow-on purchase behavior documented in the empirical and experimental literature. We also investigate in the second and third models the impact of realization utility on the performance of the investor’s trading strategy, such as the expected return and tail risk. In this course, we find that there are two types of tail risk measures that are commonly used in the literature. To further understand which one is better to use, we compare these two

14225916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14225916.value: First, we develop a new methodology to prove the existence and uniqueness of the solution to certain variational inequalities. This methodology combines the classical viscosity solution theory for stochastic control problems with given boundary conditions with a fixed point argument. See He and Yang (2018) and Chapter 3 of Shao (2019) for details. Second, we find that realization utility with a geometric Brownian motion is able to partially explain the disposition effect in that it can match some, but not all, empirical statistics that are related to the disposition effect. Replacing the geometric Brownian motion by a regime switching model significantly improves the fit of the model to the empirical statistics. This implies that both realization utility and regime switching play a role in generating the disposition effect. See He and Yang (2018) and Chapter 3 of Shao (2019) for details. Third, we find that realization utility with regime switching stock dynamics can generate a V-shaped trading pattern: the frequency of selling at a gain is increasing with respect to the magnitude of the gain, and so is the frequency of selling at a loss. This pattern is consistent with the empirical findings. However, the V-shape in our model is not strong as empirically observed. See Chapter 3 of Shao (2019) for details. Fourth, we find that realization utility with regime switching stock dynamics can explain the excessive trading puzzle. More precisely, in this model, we find that the more the investor weighs realization utility, the more frequently she trades the stock and at the same time the lower the expected return of her trading strategy is. See Chapter 2 of Shao (2019). Fifth, in the stock trading model with diversification, we find that realization utility results in diversification even when the utility function is set to be linear. Moreover, this model also generates some empirically observed follow-on purchase behavior, such as purchasing additional shares of stocks that decreased rather than increased in value subsequent to a prior purchase. Sixth, in the comparison of value-at-risk and expected-shortfall, which is motivated by the study of the effect of realization utility on tail risk of trading strategies, we find that value-at-risk is completely characterized by a set of properties. This implies that value-at-risk is more suitable to measure tail risk in some settings. For details, see He and Peng (2018). The above findings can help us better understand investor behavior and guild investment.

14225916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14225916.value: First, we observe that in our third model, the probability of selling the stock at a loss is less than the empirically observed number. This motivates us to extend our model by adding another regime in which the stock is delisted. The presence of this regime induces the investor to sell the stock at a loss more likely. Second, we can consider trading with multiple stocks, which is a more realistic setting. This greatly increases the complexity of the problem, so we cannot solve the problem using classical numerical methods. We can use machine learning to solve the problem and then study the financial implications of the model. Third, we can combine realization utility with the extrapolation model in which the investor forms beliefs about future stock market returns by extrapolating past returns. In this model, on the one hand, the investor is reluctant to realize losses due to realization utility and on the other hand, she wants to sell at losses due to extrapolation. Fourth, we can extend our model of trading with diversification to the setting with nonlinear utility functions. As such, the investor is motivated to diversify due to both realization utility and nonlinear utility functions.

14225916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14225916.value: When the stock price has decreased since the purchase, will you sell it, and when the stock price has increased since the purchase, will you keep holding it? For most retailer investors, the answer is no, and this answer causes significant financial losses, a phenomenon known as disposition effect. Does the stock market swings between the bull and bear markets? For most retailer investors, the answer is yes. In other words, they believe that the stock price switches between the bull and bear regimes. In this project, we have mainly answered two questions: First, what drives the disposition effect? Second, how does the investor trade under market regime switching? We find that investors derive utility when they realize a gain or loss at each sale, and this realization utility generates the disposition effect because they want to realize gains as soon as possible and delay the realization of losses as much possible. Regime switching induces investors to sell after experiencing consecutive losses and to hold after consecutive gains. Our findings also provide useful trading suggestions: to avoid financial losses due to the disposition effect, investors can trade and monitor their trading accounts less frequently so as to experience less realization utility.

14226616.label: Project Objectives
14226616.value: To investigate and build prototypes of wireless jumbo message systems supporting large packet transmission on the order of hundreds of megabytes in wireless networks, by adopting techniques that are different from the IEEE 802.11ac frame aggregation. To devise techniques to ensure fairness so that jumbo messages can co-exist with delay-intolerant short packets (e.g., voice packets) in a harmonious manner without jeopardizing their quality-of-service requirement (e.g., introduction of interruption techniques to break off jumbo message transmission in deference to short packets). To devise techniques to ensure efficiency in jumbo message delivery while maintaining fairness dictated by objective 2 (e.g., use of rateless codes so that partial jumbo message delivery remains useful despite the aforementioned interruption techniques in objective 2).

14226616.value: 研究目的： 本項目旨在研究無線局域網（WLAN）中無線大數據包傳輸的可行性。 研究背景： 目前無線網絡（例如Wi-Fi）中傳輸的數據包主要是小數據包。傳統的小數據包模型通常會被人們帶入到新型無線系統的設計上。正如本申請書正文中將要詳細闡述的，使用小數據包的原因來自於從前的設計定式、過時的技術、和陳舊的應用需求。 許多先進無線技術（例如，強大的信號處理技術和接近香農極限的信道編碼技術）的相互融合使我們有機會直接傳輸大的甚至是“巨大”的數據包，而不是先它們分解成小數據包然後再分別傳輸。首先，在保證信號傳輸可靠性的前提下，采用大數據包的系統比采用小數據包的系統更加高效。其次，並且更重要的是，現在及未來的許多應用場景都有“大數據（Big Data）”的傳輸需求（例如，多個存儲服務器之間的數據交換必然涉及大數據）。 為了探討無線大數據包傳輸的可行性，我們開展了一些初期實驗。例如將在本項目主體部分進行闡述的，初期實驗結果表明：在無線局域網中，當傳輸可靠性接近100％時，數據包的長度可以達到128 KB（相比而言，WLAN通常采用1.5KB作為單個包長最大值，和64 KB作為幀聚合包長最大值（在IEEE 802.11ac協議下，幀聚合包長最大值為4.6MB））。然而，要設計出一套完整的無線大數據系統解決方案，許多重要的問題仍亟待解決。例如，我們相信可以進一步增大WLAN中數據包的長度並打破現有的長度限制，從而進一步提高傳輸效率。此外，在物理層實現大數據包傳輸的同時，無線網絡的接入層也需要重新設計，以確保大數據包和傳統的小數據包的和諧共存。本項目將針對上述挑戰進行相應的系統設計。 項目概述： 本項目側重於研究無線大數據系統的三個基本問題。首先，大於128KB長度的大數據包的傳輸時間可能會超過無線信道的相干時間。我們將研究如何處理數據包內信道變化對解碼器產生的各種影響。其次，大數據包長期占用信道可能導致小數據包（如：不需要高帶寬但需要快速傳輸的語音小數據包）的傳輸延遲增大。我們將設計一套機制，允許大數據包的傳輸被要求及時傳輸的小數據包所中斷。最後，大數據包，如果被上述小數據包中斷或被其它信號及噪聲干擾，將產生傳輸錯誤，重傳整個大數據包的代價是昂貴的。我們將研究如何采用無速率信道編碼來充分利用隱藏在錯誤（或中斷）數據包中的有用信息，從而使重發數據量最小化。 為了確保上述設計的實用性，我們的研究不僅包含理論設計部分，特別是我們還將在軟件無線電平台下開發原型機系統，從而確保該設計在實際環境中的魯棒性和可行性。 研究意義： 從長遠價值來看，該研究必然會為無線網絡中大數據的傳輸帶來新的發展。該研究如果得以順利實施，將進一步提升無線局域網的性能，特別是將提高無線大數據交換網絡的系統性能。

14226616.label: Realisation of objectives
14226616.value: The original PI of this grant was Prof. Lu Lu. Prof. Lu was a Research Assistant Professor (RAP) at CUHK when this grant was approved. In August 2017, Prof. Lu joined The ChineseAcademy of Sciences, Beijing; Prof. Liew (previously the Co-I) took over as the PI. Despite the transition, Prof. Liew has been able to carry out the project to achieve the three objectives as originally stated. In the midterm report, we mentioned that, to provide the context for jumbo messaging, we were focusing on two application scenarios: 1) UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) networks and 2) vehicular networks. We are happy to report both these applications scenarios have been investigated to fruition, resulting in the following publications: * Student in Prof. Liew’s group, ** RA/Postdoc in Prof. Liew’s group 1) H. Pan*, S. C. Liew, J. Liang*, Y. Shao*, L. Lu, “Network-Coded Multiple Access on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle,” IEEE J. on Selected Areas in Commun., vol. 36, no. 9, pp. 2071-2086, , Sep. 2018. 2) Y. Shao*, S. C. Liew, J. Liang*, “Sporadic Ultra-Time-Critical Messaging in V2X,” IEEE ICC, May 2018. 3) Y. Shao*, S. C. Liew, J. Liang*, “Sporadic Ultra-Time-Critical Crowd Messaging in V2X,” IEEE Trans. on Commun., IEEE Trans. on Commun., early access, DOI: 10.1109/TCOMM.2020/3037550, Nov. 2020. 4) S. Salamat Ullah*, G. Liva, S. C. Liew, “Physical-layer Network Coding: A Random Coding Error Exponent Perspective,” IEEE ITW, Nov. 2017. 5) S. S. Ullah*, S. C. Liew, G. Liva, T. Wang**, “Short-Packet Physical-Layer Network Coding,” IEEE Trans. on Commun., vol. 68, no. 2, pp. 737-751, DOI, Feb. 2020. 6) Y. Fang**, S. C. Liew, T. Wang**, “Design of Distributed Protograph LDPC Codes for Multi-Relay Coded-Cooperative Networks,” IEEE Trans. on Wireless Communications, vol. 16, no. 11, pp. 7235-7251, Nov. 2017. Research Activities and Main Outcomes Related to Objectives 1 and 3: We have built a software-defined radio (SDR) prototype for UAV networks in which a UAV serves as a base station sending information simultaneously to a group of ground stations. We have tested the UAV in flight communicating jumbo messages to ground. Rateless codes within the construct of Network-coded Multiple Access (NCMA) was used. UAV has a finite flight time due to limited battery lifetime. Thus, any idle time during which the UAV is flying but not transmitting information will be a waste of the battery energy (flying takes more energy than transmitting information). Jumbo messaging aims to eliminate the idle time to allow the UAV to keep transmitting information during its flight. We have devised a NOMA (non-orthogonal multiple access) scheme tailored especially for Jumbo message delivery by UAV. Our major findings are reported in publication 1) above. The dual of jumbo messages is short packets. Short packets are typically urgent packets that contain control commands, etc. When they arrive, jumbo messages have to give way to the transmission of short packets. In order that we could revert to the transmission of jumbo messages quickly, the transmissions of short packets must be efficient so that they can be concluded quickly. Publications 4) and 5) are related to the use of physical-layer network coding (PNC) to improve the efficiency of short-packet transmissions. Meanwhile, publication 6) explores the use of LDPC protograph codes for relay networks. This class of codes may have potential application for the UAV network above in the relay setting. Research Activities and Main Outcomes Related to Objectives 2 and 3: We have designed a vehicular network architecture for critical safety message delivery (safety messages that must be delivered reliably from vehicle to vehicle within 10 ms). Such critical messages arise only sporadically when there is an emergency (e.g., a vehicle losing control on a slippery road). Given the sporadic nature of critical safety messages, it will be wasteful to dedicate wireless spectrum exclusively for them; on the other hand, given the need for reliable delivery within an ultra-short time, it appears at first sight that exclusive wireless spectrum allocation is necessary. Our solution to avoid the inefficiency while satisfying the highly stringent QoS requirements is an “override” architecture. In this architecture, wireless spectrum is allocated for regular messages (non-critical messages) only. However, when a vehicular network has a critical safety message to send, it will first send an interrupt signal to other vehicles that are transmitting regular messages to pre-empt them; after that it will send its critical message on the wireless spectrum originally dedicated for regular messages. The interrupt mechanism is the similar to that required for Jumbo message. To prevent a Jumbo message from hogging the wireless spectrum indefinitely, we need an interrupt mechanism so that a node that has a short but urgent message can pre-empt the node transmitting the Jumbo message to acquire to the wireless resources. For the work described in the previous paragraph, we have designed an out-of-band interrupt mechanism that we have successfully demonstrated its effectiveness (detection time within 1ms). Publications 2) and 3) report our major findings.
