14226616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14226616.value: Overall, this project has resulted in six IEEE journal papers and three IEEE conference papers. In addition, a number of students have also been trained, and research collaborations struck up with Prof. Lu Lu of the Chinese Academy of Science, Beijing. As mentioned in Section 5.3, we focused on the use of Jumbo messages and the co-existence of Jumbo messages and regular short messages in the context of UAV communication and vehicular-network communication. We find that the use of rateless codes was essential for Jumbo messaging because of the large size of the message (i.e., we do not want to lose the whole message because a tiny fraction of it has errors). Thus, it is essential to construct the Jumbo message with small chunks using rateless codes. If a certain small chunk is in error, the other chunks may compensate for the errors. A second essential technology for Jumbo messaging is wireless interrupts. When the transmission of a Jumbo message is in progress, other short but urgent messages will not be able to use the wireless spectrum. Thus, it is essential to have a “wireless interrupt” mechanism to interrupt the transmission of the Jumbo messages to make way for the transmission of urgent short messages. This project has produced several feasible designs on both fronts – i.e., the incorporation of rateless coding and wireless interrupts into Jumbo messaging.

14226616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14226616.value: We believe the basic research on Jumbo messaging has been completed in this project. The various tradeoffs in the design are now well understood with the basic research results obtained. Going forward, it will be interesting to explore if the prototypes we built can be further developed for potential technology transfer to the real world. Currently UAVs serving as base stations for wireless networks are still speculative. Although the idea is interesting, their applications may not be in the immediate future. On the other hand, vehicular networks that make use of Jumbo messaging to transfer high-volume data efficiently while allowing life-critical short messages to interrupt the Jumbo message when necessary will be an application scenario to explore to see if the concept will find use in the near future. The PI will explore on the latter front, and if the idea is worthwhile, he will apply for an ITF grant to further carry out the R&D effort.

14226616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14226616.value: This project aimed to establish the feasibility of jumbo-message wireless communication. The data packets in today’s wireless networks (e.g., Wi-Fi) are typically small packets. This conventional paradigm has been carried over to many new wireless systems being designed. The confluence of many advanced wireless technologies (e.g., powerful signal processing techniques and Shannon-limit approaching channel codes) are now making it possible and desirable to directly transmit large or even “jumbo” messages rather than breaking them down into small packets. Large packet delivery is more efficient than small packet delivery if reliability can be guaranteed. Second, and perhaps more importantly, many of today’s applications are calling for the delivery of large volumes of data (e.g., big data applications involving data exchange between multiple data servers). This project has identified methods to use rateless coding to ensure reliable transmission of jumbo messages. Furthermore, it has resulted in the proposal of the concept of “wireless interrupts” whereby urgent small messages can interrupt the transmission of long messages – which can take a long time – so that the urgent small messages can take priority over the long messages. The two technologies have been applied to prototypes of Unmanned Aerial Vehicular communication and ground V2X vehicular networks.

14227216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14227216.value: Speech is the most natural and convenient way of communication between humans. Spoken language technologies (SLT) are developed in order to enable the use of speech as a modality of human-computer interaction. Conventionally the development of SLT requires abundant language-specific resources, including large amount of transcribed speech data, word pronunciation dictionary, and language rules of various levels. For many less popular languages, including numerous minority languages in China, such linguistics resources are unavailable and very difficult to acquire. The proposed research addresses the key problems in SLT development for low-resource or under-resourced languages. More specifically, given a few hours of speech recordings of unknown content in a language that is completely unknown to us, we need to find ways to discover the basic constituents and structure of the language. The research is divided into three tasks: (1) unsupervised acoustic modeling; (2) unsupervised language modeling; and (3) applications to low-resource languages. Unsupervised acoustic modeling is formulated as a bottom-up self-organizing process in which acoustic unit inventory and model parameters are estimated jointly or iteratively. For unsupervised language modeling, we focus on the problem of automatic word discovery. The intended applications include spoken keyword search, topic discovery of spoken documents, and technology-assisted linguistic study of minority languages. The research results will contribute to the development of language-independent technologies for multimedia multi-lingual information retrieval and the preservation of minority languages and culture. The project team is composed of experienced speech researchers and linguistic experts, who have carried out a wealth of relevant research works. We seek for a funding of HK$1.547 million to support the project for three years. 語音是人與人之間最方便和自然的溝通方式。基於信號處理和自然語言處理的電腦語音技術已經發展得相當成熟，基於語音的人機交互和資訊檢索系統日漸普及。傳統上，針對某特定語言的語音技術開發依賴於各種相關的語言資源，包括大量含標注的語音材料，發音字/詞表，語法語義規則等。大部分非主流語言，包括中國境內的一些地區方言和少數民族語言，並不能滿足以上的語言資源條件。本研究項目探討針對低資源或甚至零資源語言的語音技術開發問題。具體而言，假設我們對目標語言一無所知，如何從少量未知內容的音頻資料中，自動學習該語言的基本語音語言組成和結構。本研究包括三部分：(1) 非監督型聲學建模；（2）非監督型語言建模；（3）語音模型在低資源語言上的應用。非監督型聲學建模是一個由下而上的自組織過程，目的建立基本語音單元庫，同時對這些語音單元的聲學模型進行優化。在語言建模方面，研究重點在於從語音資料中自動發掘詞彙並生成語法規則。我們主要關注的應用包括關鍵字檢索，主題發掘及電腦輔助語言學研究。本項目的研究成果在多媒體多語種資訊檢索和少數民族語言資源保護等領域作出重大貢獻。項目團隊成員包括語音技術和語言學方面的專家，他們在相關的領域已經做了大量的工作。項目為期三年，申請研究經費一百五十四萬七千元港幣，獲批六十七萬五千元。

14227216.label: Realisation of objectives
14227216.value: All of the three objectives have been addressed and achieved. Toward Objective 1, extensive studies on a wide range of approaches to extracting robust representations for segment clustering were carried out. These representations include speech signal based features and learned embedding features. There were two main focuses of our work: (1) use of data from other resource-rich languages; (2) development of new unsupervised adaptation methods. Both parts aimed at addressing the problem of lacking transcribed speech data of low-resource languages. Initially an investigation was done on posterior features derived from multiple well-trained phone recognizers from other languages (Feng & Lee, INTERPSEECH 2017). We proposed a framework of unsupervised learning of multilingual bottleneck features. To facilitate unsupervised speaker adaptation with untranscribed speech, frame-level labels were hypothesized either by clustering or making use of out-of-domain ASR systems (Feng & Lee, INTERSPEECH 2018). Subsequently we seek to improve the goodness of hypothesized frame labels by disentangling linguistic content from speaker-dependent factors in speech (Feng & Lee, INTERSPEECH 2019), and applying adversarial training (Feng et al., INTERSPEECH 2019). With various types of unsupervisedly learned multilingual bottleneck features (BNFs), acoustic modeling of low-resource languages can be done (Feng & Lee, IEEE/ACM TransASLP 2019) We developed a series of robust methods for DNN acoustic model adaptation in automatic speech recognition. A recurrent neural network (RNN) based clustering scheme was proposed to learn both the standard latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) cluster labels and their temporal dependency (Xie et al., INTERSPEECH 2017). For robust learning of adaptation parameters for DNN, a significant amount of data are needed. With the well-established learning hidden unit contributions (LHUC) based DNN adaptation, the approach of Bayesian learning was developed and applied successfully to address the problem of poor generalization with limited adaptation data. A posterior distribution over the LHUC scaling vectors was used to model the uncertainty, and an efficient variational inference based approach was adopted to estimate the LHUC parameter distribution (Xie et al., ICASSP 2019). Furthermore, we proposed a new method of efficiently predicting LHUC scaling vectors directly from acoustic features using a time-delay DNN (TDNN) and an online averaging layer (Xie et al., INTERSPEECH 2019). Toward Objective 2, a complete system framework of automatically discovering spoken keywords from untranscribed audio archives has been developed and thoroughly evaluated. The system comprises two stages: (1) unsupervised acoustic modeling and decoding; (2) pattern mining in recognized unit sequences. Stage 1 essentially has the same goal as unsupervised subword modelling in Objective 1. The efficacy of modelling can be evaluated in two ways. We first analyse the linguistic relevance of learned subword units based on symmetric Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the learned units and ground-truth phonemes for a few resource-rich languages (Feng & Lee, INTERSPEECH 2017). In a truly unsupervised scenario, the ground-truth phoneme identities and time alignments are not available. A commonly used task of evaluation is known as the ABX discriminability test. We compared and demonstrated the performance of various types of posterior features and learned bottleneck features. It was found that combining different types of BNFs by vector concatenation leads to cross-speaker ABX error rate of 9.7%, which is comparable with the best submitted system in ZeroSpeech 2017 and better than other recently reported systems (Feng, CUHK PhD Thesis 2020). With the unsupervisedly learned subword units, a given audio archive is represented by a pseudo transcription, from which spoken keywords can be discovered by string mining algorithms. A bag of word candidates were first obtained by identifying repeated patterns in the pseudo transcriptions. Grouping of similar word candidates was carried out by the leader clustering algorithm. Each of the resulted clusters was hypothesized as a keyword. The proposed system was evaluated on a database of 180-hour lecture recordings from the publicly accessible MIT OpenCourseWare website. The performance was analysed in terms of the quality of clusters, i.e., whether they correspond to useful keywords, and the clusters' coverage on content of the lectures (Sung et al., APSIPA 2018). Toward Objective 3, the proposed feature representations, adaptation methods and pattern discovery algorithms can be applied straightforwardly to spoken term detection, topic discovery and text-to-speech without text. Since 2017, we have been participating the influential Zerospeech Challenges (https://zerospeech.com/), which comprise various applications related to unsupervised subword modeling (Feng et al., INTERSPEECH 2019). With the MIT OpenCourseWare lecture recordings, we analyzed the topic relevance of automatically discovered keywords, using the term-frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) metrics. It was clearly shown that the discovered keywords could effectively identify the topics of lectures and differentiate different lecture topics (Sung, CUHK MPhil Thesis 2019). Undergraduate students were involved in this research by carrying out summer research, Final-Year Projects and helping in manual annotation of speech data. The cost for providing the undergraduate research experience was covered by the department and faculty's funding. and thus this budget item of the project was not spent.

14227216.value: A complete framework of unsupervised learning of multilingual bottleneck features was developed and evaluated thoroughly. It was found that out-of-domain data resources and trained ASR systems could be exploited in the learning of speech feature representations. With the multi-genre nature of out-of-domain data, adaptation on speaker and environment variation is a critical process in feature learning. Acquiring high-quality frame-level label is also important in unsupervised adaptation and subword modeling. These findings and relevant experimental results were published in the journal paper (Feng & Lee, IEEE Trans. ASLP 2019) and presented in a number of conference papers (Feng & Lee, INTERSPEECH 2017; Feng & Lee, INTERSPEECH 2018; Feng & Lee, INTERSPEECH 2019). Adaptation of DNN acoustic models has not been studied as extensively as that of hidden Markov models. Our work showed that Bayesian learning could be effectively applied to address the problem of adapting huge number of DNN model parameters with limited amount of data. This was the first effort on using Bayesian learning for DNN speaker adaptation. It was presented in an award-winning conference paper (Xie et al., ICASSP 2019). We also showed that the adaptation parameters can be predicted on the fly without requiring the multiple decoding passes for test-time adaptation. The above methods can be applied to any identifiable variation of speech conditions, including episode, genre, accent, noise type, bandwidth and others. These results were presented in a few other conference papers (Xie et al., INTERSPEECH 2017; Xie et al., INTERSPEECH 2019) and reported in detail in a PhD thesis (Xurong Xie, 2020). On speech databases of different nature, automatically discovered subword-level and word-level speech units are found to have high linguistic relevance. The challenge is how to segment and determine the boundaries of meaningful unit sequences. It was found that longer unit sequences are more likely to represent distinctive keywords and shorter sequences tend to constitute common parts shared among different words. Despite the noisy results of word discovery, the proposed approach can be applied to realise fully automatic analysis of untranscribed speech from low-resource languages. This would greatly help improve the efficiency of analyzing huge amount of raw data. These findings were presented in the conference papers (Sung et al., APSIPA 2018; Feng & Lee, INTESPEECH 2017; Feng et al., INTERSPEECH 2019) and an MPhil thesis (M. L. Sung, 2019).

14227216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14227216.value: The efficiency of the proposed Bayesian adaptation methods could be improved further with a feature prediction network. Specifically, the estimated hidden layer scaling vectors or other model parameters can be compressed and predicted online. Another extension is to introduce attention mechanism in the adaptation process. In order to learn speaker-invariant and subword-discriminative feature representation, pair-wise learning can be investigated in a post-processing stage. Other robust algorithms of clustering could also be attempted. In this project we have developed a complete but very basic system for spoken word discovery. It opens up a wide range of down-stream problems, namely lexical modelling, language modelling, topic modelling, unsupervised ASR, speech summarization, for which exciting further investigations are anticipated.

14227216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14227216.value: This research tackles the challenging problem of "analyzing a spoken language without knowing the language". That is, we are given only a large amount of audio recording of speech in an unknown language, for which there is no way to obtain any information about its content. Can we apply signal processing and machine learning technologies to find out the structure and extract useful information from the speech ? Our proposed solution comprises two main elements. First, we maximally leverage the existing data resources of "known" languages. Second, we try to reduce the effect of factors that are not related to the speech content. We successfully developed a complete system that can automatically generate a set of "keywords" or "key phrases" from raw audio. These keywords can largely capture the core content and topic of the recordings being analyzed.

14231916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14231916.value: Interference channels model one of the most commonly occurring scenarios of resource contention in wireless networks, that of multiple point-to-point transmission schemes interfering with each other due to their sharing of a common medium for communication. Following Shannon's seminal work in forming a mathematical model for point-to-point digital communication, the interference channel also has a well-defined mathematical model that has been studied extensively since the seventies. Once a commonly accepted model had been developed, one of the central problems in the area of network information theory is to characterize the set of achievable data rates for this model, or more commonly referred to as the capacity region. For two-receiver interference channels, the achievable rate region proposed by Han and Kobayashi [hak81] represented the gold standard. Indeed, up until a few months ago, till the PI and his students showed that one can improve on the Han-Kobayashi rate region, it was not even clear whether Han-Kobayashi region matched the capacity region or not. It took the PI a few years of work, to develop the intuition and the mathematical ideas concerning extremal distributions, to show that for some channels one can indeed out-perform the Han-Kobayashi region. We now have a class of channels where it has been demonstrated that Han-Kobayashi region is strictly sub-optimal [nxy15]. The natural path forward is to devise new schemes that can improve the achievable rates, primarily exploiting the classes of channels and the ideas that were used to show that the Han-Kobayashi region was sub-optimal. This is the main focus of the proposal. Clearly, the main thrust of this proposal is quite theoretical; however, as with such problems that are deeply intertwined with fundamental communication problems, the insights and ideas should help practical code designers to achieve better data rates. 干擾信道是無線網絡中關於資源分配的最常見的模型之一，其中多對點對點通信由於共用傳輸媒介產生互相干擾。緊跟Shannon對於點對點通信中提出的開創性的數學模型，干擾信道同樣有一個定義清楚的數學模型，這個模型自從七十年代後被廣泛研究。當一個模型被廣泛接受後，網絡信息論的核心問題之一是刻畫對於此模型所有可達到的數據傳輸率， 也被稱為信道容量區域。 對於有兩對接收端的干擾信道，由Han和Kobayashi [HK81]提出的可達到的數據傳輸率曾經是黃金標準。事實上，學界一直都不清楚Han—Kobayashi傳輸率是否就是信道容量，直到幾個月前，PI和他的學生證明Han—Kobayashi傳輸率還能夠提高。PI用了幾年的工作得到了相關的極端概率分佈的直覺和數學想法用以提高Han—Kobayashi傳輸率。現在我們能夠證明，對於一些信道，人們可以提高Han—Kobayashi所能達到的數據傳輸率[NXY15]。 接下來很自然的工作是設計新的方案來提高傳輸率，首要的是利用那些用來證明Han—Kobayashi 非最優的信道和想法。這就是本提議的焦點。顯然，本提議的要旨很偏於理論，但這個問題深刻地與通信領域的其他基本問題相關聯，從中洞察出的見解和想法可以幫助實際中編碼設計者達到更高的數據傳輸率。

14231916.label: Realisation of objectives
14231916.value: Let me address Objectives 2 and 3 first. Since the capacity region of the interference channel and multi-user settings in general is a very basic collection of open problems in this field where progress has been marginal for several decades; the PI has recently focussed attention on studying the behaviour of the capacity regions near its "corner points". This is a rather new direction in the entire field. The only "corner point" question that had really got the attention of the community was that of the "Costa-corner-point" in the Gaussian Z-interference channel. Costa "established" the corner point to the capacity region in 1985 using several new ideas; however a gap in one of the lemmas was discovered by Sason in 2002. This was then fixed only in 2015 by Polyanskiy and Wu. In this fix, the outer bound that they had computed had a flat slope at the corner point; by this, point of the form $(C_1-eps, R_1^* + Theta(sqrt{epsilon})$ belonged to their outer bound. However this was drastically different from the inner bound that showed a linear tradeoff. The story was also similar to the particular example where the PI had found the counter example for the optimality of the Han-Kobayashi region for a discrete setting, the clean Z-interference channel. This led to the formulation of the Objectives 2 and 3.: Are the inner bounds so fundamentally off from the true capacity region that it presents a different picture or are the outer bounds off from the true behaviour? It was a rather ambitious objective given that even determining the corner point exactly took well over three decades. Towards resolving this, the first thing that needed to be computed was the real behaviour of the inner bound near the corner points. This was not easy since the inner bound evaluations reduce to non-trivial non-convex optimization problems. Nevertheless, the PI along with Costa and his PhD student David Ng, computed it for the Gaussian interference channel; and the PI along with this PhD student Mehdi Yazdanpanah addressed it for the Clan Z-interference channels. We showed that the inner bounds had a linear trade-off as suggested by the intuition and computed the critical slope of the corner point at the various corner points. For the discrete case, we turned out to be rather lucky. There was a little known outer bound due to Etkin and Ordentlich which really came to our rescue. It turns out that this outer bound is really suited for studying clean Z-interference channels (the authors had originally developed it for binary deterministic interference channels); and so we used this outer bound to show that even the capacity region has a linear trade-off at the corner point. The Gaussian case was, unsurprisingly, much harder. But our tremendous persistence did pay off at the end. Now we have two different outer bounds, using two different lines of attack, that both show a linear tradeoff at the Costa's corner point. The first one came from a very novel technique invented by the PI and his collaborator Amin Gohari, by making use of an auxiliary receiver, to develop outer bounds in multiterminal settings. This novel approach has taken a life of its own and have led to real breakthrough in some of the older problems. The second approach is really the only which came out of sheer persistence. By looking at the Fenchel-dual representation of the concave envelope and by formulating a conjecture, and finally proving the conjecture it was a sheer force of will that led to the second outer bound. This is why I claim that Objectives 2 and 3 were fully addressed. As for Objective 4, the PI and his student David Ng studied the multi-letter extensions of the Han-Kobayashi regions with Gaussian signaling. The main issue here is that the optimization problems were non-convex. There was a claim by researchers Merhav and his collaborator that such extensions would improve on the Han and Kobayashi region with Gaussian signaling, but they had thrown up their hands at computing the original region with Gaussian signaling due to its non-convexity. The PI and his student, refuted the above statement by showing that multi-letter extensions do not improve on the single letter scheme (result published in a very short time period in Trans IT) by invoking a couple of very novel arguments to the field to tackle the non-convex optimization problem. This exercise also gave a very insightful interpretation to waterfilling and other communication strategies as well as correlation across time. These three objectives took a real amount of focus that Objective 1 was done in a tangential manner. We investigated schemes that imporve the state of the art single letter schemes motivated by the counterexample of the optimality of H-K region as inspired by Objective 1's question. This then led the PI and his student Mehdi to solve yet another open problem in the book network information theory about the optimality of superposition coding region. He again block repetition and temporally correlated codes outperformed single letter codes. Further in this setting we exactly computed the two letter regions and come up with completely novel computable outer bounds to capacity region (in Mehdi's thesis and being prepared for journal submission). Since the objective was tweaked a bit and applied to slightly different setting, the PI marked its completion as 90%. However we believed that this was a much more worthwhile track to take up in the short term. Apologies: In one of the research publications in ITA, the author just specified support from RGC instead of specifying the precise GRF number (due to negligence) and in another one at the same venue the PI forgot to acknowledge the grant support. The ITA workshop is mainly focussing in presentations and hence the written proceedings version is mainly to documents the proofs. The PI should have included it nevertheless and apologise profusely for the oversight.

14231916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14231916.value: The study of the Han-Kobayashi region for the Gaussian and discrete interference channel has been responsible for half of my research focus during this period (the other half has been in broadcast channels though they share similar insights). Improvement over the single-letter scheme by using correlated messages (as in Objective 1) has been the main contributor for solving the open problem 8.2 in the book Network Information Theory by El Gamal and Kim. A main focus of the study has been in the behaviour of the capacity region around the corner points: towards this end, we calculated the exact slope of the Han-Kobayashi region at the Costa-Sato Corner point. We developed an out bound for the Gaussian interference channel that for the first time demonstrated that there was a slope discontinuity to the capacity region at the Costa-Polyanskiy-Wu corner point. This was all the more surprising given that when Polyanskiy and Wu fixed the gap in Costa's argument for the corner point, they also mentioned that getting a finite slope would involve arguments significantly different from their techniques of using Talagrands inequality, which was true. This research project resulted in the development of a lot of novel techniques and findings which are listed below: 1. Showing that multi-letter extensions of Han-Kobayashi region with Gaussian signalling could not improve on the single letter scheme (ITA '18, IT-Trans '19). This is contrary to the observation in https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05726 (please see the "comments" in this website as they withdrew the paper after we published ours). 2. Showing that multi-letter extension of superposition coding strictly improved the capacity region for a three receiver broadcast channel with degraded message sets (motivated by 1.) 3. The auxiliary receiver approach and developing a new method for obtaining outer bounds in network information theory. This was then used to find a finite slope to the capacity region at the Costa-Polyanskiy Wu corner point. 4. Development of the Fenchel duality as a way to establish the optimality of Gaussian Z interference channel, development of a precise mathematical conjecture, and finally the proof of the conjecture in certain regimes. 5. Use of Etkin-Ordentlich outer bound for studying the behaviour of capacity regions for Clean Z interference channels and using this to find finite slopes at corner points.

14231916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14231916.value: As good research should do, this research has opened up a whole avenue of new possibilities which already has had very significant consequences. 1. The auxiliary receiver paper has already has a follow up paper on the relay channel which has solved several long standing open problems. 2. The Fenchel dual conjecture has opened up new ways of proving optimality of Gaussian signaling with power control. 3. The Etkin-Ordentlich conjecture has made an improvement in the long-standing sandglass conjecture and prompts further research. Beyond the points mentioned above, there are also other avenues for research that are very promising that has genesis from this project.

14231916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14231916.value: This research has led to solving several "open" problems (some published as open) that are of fundamental interest in network information theory and in particular in the subject of interference channels. These are questions that seek to determine the fundamental limits of reliable communication in certain settings. Most of these problems are completely mathematical in nature, but is deeply related to engineering applications. As such progress in these questions necessitate new and fresh mathematical tools and ideas; which are significantly harder than using existing ideas and apply them to the settings of interest. hence the amount of creativity and luck required to make such findings are gargantuan and we have been very fortunate that some of our approaches have borne fruit. The results of this project and related projects have certainly made the information theory community take notice.

14232816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14232816.value: Due to the growing popularity of social networking, microblog is now a popular digital communication platform. However, large volume of microblog messages produced daily makes it difficult to understand the key information behind these messages. The goal of microblog summarization is to identify salient excerpts from the target microblog messages, digest them and represent them in a succinct form for easy reading. Traditional summarizers for natural language text rely heavily of text signal. They are, however, ineffective for microblog summarization due to the short and informal nature of microblog messages. To overcome this problem, existing research works mainly leverage on microblog users’ authority and/or message reposting count, etc. But, these features do not necessarily indicate salient messages. For example, an influential celebrity can post a popular message with no important content. This lays down the objective of our research: To investigate the use of discourse information for microblog summarization. Discourse information has been proven useful for single document summarization for natural language texts. We argue that it is also useful for microblog summarization. We propose to organize microblog messages as repost trees based on reposting relations and extract discourse information from a microblog repost tree by analyzing both the content and the structure of the tree. The discourse information will then be used to determine the saliency of each repost message, which will in turn be used for extractive summarization of the given tree. A prototype system will be developed based on this operational principle. The system is composed of two modules: (1) the discourse tagging module makes use of tree structured Conditional Random Fields (CRF) and the extended “Conversation+Topic” method to automatically model the discourse relations of the reposting messages; and (2) the summarization module utilizes a novel Continuous CRF method to analyze the detected discourse tags of each reposting message and identify salient and high quality messages by ranking. Both modules will be evaluated separately using real-world microblog corpus produced by this project. Also, we will use ROUGE metrics to evaluate our microblog summarization system against the state-of-the-art baselines. 由於社交網絡日益普及，微博現在已成為一個流行的溝通平台。然而，大量的微博條文使得我們難以理解這些條文背後的關鍵信息。「微博話語總結」是針對大量的微博條文而自動生成一個簡潔並方便閱讀的關鍵信息條文的硏究。已有的研究並不適用於微博，因每一條微博條文非常短而且簡潔。而且已有的研究會傾向於認為一個有名人發布的微博條文更為重要，但現實是，一個名人發布的微博條文可以只是流行用語而無重要內容。這奠定了我們的研究目的：探討微博總結運用「語篇信息」。「語篇信息」已被證實為單一文件總結非常有用。我們認為，這也對微博話語總結有用的。我們建議組織微博訊息作為根據，並以轉發關係樹，轉貼關係樹，和微博條文內容作為硏究始點。原型系統將基於這個工作原理來開發。該系統由兩個模塊組成：「話語標記模塊」和「聚合模塊」。這兩個模塊將分別使用由該項目產生的真實世界的微博語料庫進行評估。此外，我們將用 ROUGE 指標來評價我們的原型系統。

14232816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14232816.value: The primary objective of this project is to research and develop an effective model to summarize repost trees based on the discourse relations among the messages. In particular, our research will focus on Twitter-like Chinese microblog site Sina Weibo. We collected repost tree data using public microblog toolkit WeiboEvents. However, since there is no largescale public dataset for training and evaluation of our work, building annotated repost tree corpus for discourse labeling and summarization is another challenge of our project. To this end, one of our targets is to compile and make public the first large-scale repost tree corpus to support open discourse labeling and summarization research. We therefore constructed the first large scale annotated repost tree corpus with discourse tags and editorial summaries, and are detailed in our published papers. This corpus is useful for future research works on microblog discourse processing and summarization. We are the first to propose extracting discourse structures from microblog repost trees for summarization. We present methods based on tree structured CRF and “Conversation+Topic” extended model for effective extraction of discourse relations. And then we incorporate the discourse relations extracted from the repost trees into a supervised summarization model based on Continuous CRF to rank and identify salient messages. In this project, microblog messages are organized as repost trees based on reposting relations, where nodes represent microblog reposting messages, namely reposts, and edges denote the relations between reposts. We propose to utilize the hidden contextual information embedded in repost trees, i.e. discourse structures, to help summarize short messages. Discourse relations of repost trees, such as “statement”, “acknowledge”, “respond”, etc. can indicate how a message relates to each other semantically or pragmatically, and help summarizers identify salient messages. For example, a “statement” message is likely to be a strong summary candidate for repost tree compare to a “respond” or “acknowledge” message. For another example, our prior works have demonstrated that coarse-grained discourse relations, i.e., “leader-follower” relations, are strong indicators for repost tree summarization.

14232816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14232816.value: This project investigated the use of contextual information embedded in a repost tree to identify discourse relations in microblog posts for summarization purpose. Note that, in reality, influential authors may not always post salient messages. For example, a celebrity may post a message, which does not carry any important content. Also, their model required substantial amount of other external information to model author influence, such as the historical tweets, social networking information of the authors, etc. These can be a potential future direction to study.

14232816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14232816.value: The increasing popularity of microblog platforms, e.g. Twitter, Weibo, etc., results in huge volume of on-line data. This inevitably leads to information explosion, which can seriously affect the effectiveness of many on-line applications, e.g. digital marketing. Thus, there is an urgent need for effective summarization systems to avoid users from making wrong, and often risky, decisions due to superficial understanding of huge volume and unmanageable amount of social networking information. Automatic summarization is a conventional technique for identifying important contents and representing lengthy document(s) in a short and comprehensible form. While these techniques are effective for summarizing natural language texts, their effectiveness on microblog texts is questionable. This is because, unlike classical text, microblog consists of many short and informal messages linked together by their reposting sequence.

14233016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14233016.value: 目標 本項目旨在使用雙站雷達干涉測量及雷達影像分類技術考察高亞洲地區冰川動態 專案背景 冰川作為全球冰凍圈的重要組成部分，在氣候變化中扮演了重要角色，同時冰川退化也是全球變暖的指示器。高亞洲地區分佈有全球數量最多的低緯度高海拔的冰川，2003-2009年間導致海平面上升的冰川融水大約有10%由該地區貢獻，海平面影響著包括香港在內的所有沿海城市。高亞洲地區冰川同時也是亞洲主要大河的起源，養育有數十億民眾，對乾旱地區是重要的季節性及長期固態水庫。 鑒於其重要性，大量研究已著手于調查高亞洲地區冰川狀態比如冰川物質平衡及冰川物質平衡線變化等。由於嚴酷環境及高額實地考察費用，該地區僅有少於1%的冰川有過實地調查。考慮到極大的覆蓋範圍，遙感技術對區域尺度冰川狀態調查具有重大潛力。大多數的星基大地測量方法比如鐳射衛星測高及多期地形差分可以用於冰川物質平衡，但是在一些子區域得到了截然相反的結果。單極化雷達資料分類可以用於提取冰川物質平衡線，但新近發射的幾顆雙極化衛星資料並沒有針對性演算法研究。 項目簡介 本專案中，我們將使用多元遙感資料調查高亞洲地區多時間尺度的冰川狀態。雙站雷達干涉將用於構建冰川地區地形並與2000年獲取的太空梭地形任務地形對比獲取十年尺度冰川高程變化資訊。相似的星載感測器及相同的生成數字地形原理將有助於得到比立體攝影測量更好的結果。雷達影像分類將用於調查該地區年尺度冰川物質平衡線變化。我們將開發針對單極化及雙極化雷達影像資料的新的冰雪表面分類演算法。歐洲空間局哥白尼計畫將使用此資料至少六或12日覆蓋地球一次。 項目重要性 本項目的產出將有助於進一步瞭解當今高亞洲地區冰川動態，退化速度以及對海平面上升的貢獻；同時也將協助高亞洲地區水資源管理，特別是乾旱地區。

14233016.label: Realisation of objectives
14233016.value: Object 1, We’ve applied H-Alpha dual polarization decomposition to summer-end C-band Sentinel-1 A&B images at different sites at HMA, including Tien Shan, Pamir, Karakoram, different section of Himalaya, Inner Tibetan Plateau and Eastern Nyainqêntanglha. According to the H-Alpha dual polarization decomposition result shows that C-band dual polarization show with low entropy at ablation area except for valley glaciers at their lowest section where are rather rough, when at accumulation area, the entropy is high. Compare to only adopt backscattering coefficient of SAR image, using both backscattering coefficient and dual polarization decomposition information helps in increasing the precision in identify the accumulation and ablation zone. In addition, polarization ratio and C2 matrix also helps in identify the accumulation and ablation zone. We adopted long time supported C-band ERS 1&2, EnviSAT, and Sentinel-1 A&B and extracted summer end snow line altitude time series for several representative sites. The result shows that the summer end snow line altitude (can be regarded at equilibrium altitude) shows a high correlation to glacier mass balance rate. At Karakoram and West Kunlun, where shows balanced or even positive glacier mass balance show almost no increasing or decreasing of summer end snow line altitude. At western Nyainqentanglha, where we found glacier mass balance at around -0.28m w.e. /s, the summer end snow line has been increased above 6000m after 2012, which were claimed between 5600m and 5700m at first decade of 21st century. Eastern Nyainqentanglha is the area where shows quickest glacier mass lost rate among the entire High-mountains Asia, where also show most obvious summer end snow line arising. The glacier lost rates was at 2-3 folds of global average and its summer end snow line has been raised above 5300m in recent years considering its ELA was at 4600m around 2000. Object 2, we have developed bash script to automatically to drive Gamma software to derive glacier height change, and orbital error. We have developed Matlab codes to perform penetration depth correction between C- and X-band SAR images. It turns out that by joint use of bistatic SAR images with short and long perpendicular baseline will be more accurate for estimating the glacier height changes specifically for regions present with large glacier height changes. Due to the limitation of bistatic SAR images quotas, we only test at the Everest and Eastern Nyainqentanglha area, it found that bistatic SAR images with short perpendicular baseline helps to derive digital elevation model with relatively low precision robustly, and with long perpendicular baseline helps to increasing the precision. We developed Matlab code to mosaic the glacier height changes that derived separately from descending and ascending bistatic SAR acquisitions. We test this at the West Kunlun, Western Nyainqentanglha and the Everest region. Object 3, we have mapped decadal glacier mass (2000 - ~2012) balance in High mountains Asia by topography differencing based on bistatic SAR interferometry (TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X) and SRTM. Especially, we focus more on four sites, which are 1st, West Kunlun, Karakoram, Hindu Kush and Pamir, where ‘Karakoram anomaly ’ and/or ‘Karakoram-Pamir anomaly’ locates; 2nd, western Nyainqentanglha at Inner Tibetan Plateau and has strong interaction to inland plateau lakes; 3rd, Himalaya range, including the Everest, Shishapangma, Gangotri, and Naimona'nyi; 4th, Eastern Nyainqentanglha and Hengduan Mountain. Our results find consistence comparing to ICESat and/or ASTER derived result in terms of spatial pattern. Due to the principle of SAR interferometry, we provided more spatial details for further study. For glacierized area distributed with heavy debris covering, we compared glacier downwasting rates at clean ice area, with shallow debris cover, with heavy debris cover, and with both debris cover and supraglacial lake. Our result shows that shallow debris cover and supraglacial lake can accelerate the melting of the glacier when temperature rises while heavy debris can protects glacier from melting despite temperature raising. In terms of glacier flow rates, at most of our study sites, surge and stagnant glaciers can occupy great area, if not include those glaciers we noticed a strong correlation between annual precipitation and glacier flow rates.

14233016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14233016.value: We developed automatic processing strategy of employing bistatic SAR image to derive decadal scale glacier height changes and applied such method to all representative area among High Mountains Asia. Our major finding includes that 1, bistatic SAR images can effectively be applied to extract glacier height changes and mass balance; multi-baseline bistatic helps to increasing robustness and accuracy in estimating glacier mass balance; ascending and descending images help to increase the percentage of availability of observations in terms of glacier height changes. 2, In recent decades, High Mountains Asia experienced spatial heterogenous mass loss rate, East Nyainqentanglha experienced quickest glacier mass lost, Himalayan range’s rate was similar to global average, Inner Tibetan Plateau showed with slightly less losing rate than regional and/or global average, while western part of HMA including western Kunlun Shan, the Karakoram, Hindu Kush, and Pamir Plateau presented balanced or even positive glacier mass balance; 3, centre of the ‘Karakoram anomaly’ locates at western Kunlun Shan and glacier mass balance present with a decreasing gradient from edge of the Tarim to the Karakroam; 4, Thin debris and supraglacial lake accelerate glacier melting while thick debris prevents glacier from loss mass. 5, dual-polarized C-band SAR images helps to identify summer end snowline (glacier equilibrium line) and shows potential to derive long-term ELA (equilibrium line altitude) changes. There are three SCI papers published directly supported by this project. Two of them acknowledge RGC’s funding support. Supported by this project, we also participate three times of international conference including ESA-MOST cooperated Dragon Symposium in 2017, 2018, 2019 and ESA Living Planet Symposium 2019.

14233016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14233016.value: In terms of technique, our developed data process strategies can be applied to alpine glaciers that distribute at rest part of the world including Alaska in US, Alps at Europe, and Andes in South America. We found that bistatic SAR interferometry is powerful tool for deriving glacier height changes. For future study, it is necessary to develop algorithm to combine or fusion the results of bistatic SAR interferometry, photogrammetry, and Laser altimetry to achieve high temporal resolution of glacier mass balance observation. Both glacier mass balance and glacier equilibrium line altitude changes are results of accumulation and melting, it is necessary to make simultaneous observation to find correlation between these two features. In terms of scientific significant, our derived results of glacier mass balance are valuable of regional climate study, hydrology study and glaciology study. Since we have provided glacier mass balance over High mountains Asia, it is necessary to explorer the meteorological reason why such spatial heterogenous pattern of glacier mass balance occurred by performing regional climate model simulation. Besides, glacier melting has an impact on reginal hydrology including endorheic lake and outflow river. It is necessary to establish coupled glacial-hydrological model to explorer to multi-sphere interaction.

14233016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14233016.value: In this project we developed algorithm to separate accumulation and melting area of the glacier by using dual-polarized SAR image. We also developed automatic processing script to derive glacier height changes by using bistatic TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X SAR images. We derived decadal glacier height changes at all typical area across High-mountains Asia. We found that dual-polarized C-band SAR images are better than single-polarized C-band images in terms of glacier zone classification. Bistatic SAR interferometry plays essential role for deriving glacier height changes. We found that ‘Karakoram anomaly’ is centred at the edge of southwestern Tarim in China rather than Karakoram. The eastern Nyainqentanglha show the quickest glacier mass lost rate during 2000 and 2012. Everest and its surrounding show acceleration in losing glacier mass before and after ~2012. Debris cover mostly protect glacier from losing mass at warmer situation in most area. Our findings help the research in regional climate, regional hydrology study and glacier remote sensing study. The derived glacier mass balance is helpful to calibrate glacier energy and mass model which should be useful to predict future glacier fate.

14234116.label: Project Objectives
14234116.value: We will extend the shock tube for studying low-vapor-pressure liquid fuels using a custom-designed de Laval nozzle and improve the shock condition repeatability with a new diaphragm breaking mechanism. We will also revise the shock wave calculation method by accounting for droplet evaporation and additional thermodynamic/gasdynamic factors. We will develop laser absorption diagnostics for quantitative concentration time-history measurements of CO, CO2, C2H4, CH2O and fuel. New line-selection rules will be adopted to improve the detection accuracy of CO and CO2 by minimizing the detection uncertainty caused by temperature variation. We will implement a quantum cascade laser at 10.53 micron to achieve interference-free C2H4 detection using wavelength modulation spectroscopy or a differential absorption scheme. We will also develop new absorption sensors for CH2O and fuel diagnostics using interband cascade lasers between 3.3-3.6 micron. We will perform shock tube and kinetic modeling study of the pyrolysis of long-chain FAMEs, including methyl decanoate, methyl-5-decenoate, methyl palmitate and methyl oleate. We will conduct simultaneous measurements of the time-dependent species concentrations throughout the thermal decomposition process at different temperatures (1,000-1,600 K) and pressures (1-10 atm). We will particularly examine the influences of the C=C double bond and the length of aliphatic chain on fuel decomposition pathways, CO/CO2 formation, and eventually reactivity and pollutants. We will investigate and validate the rate coefficients of the key elementary reactions involved in the biodiesel kinetic mechanism. In particular, we will measure the rate coefficients of HOCO radical thermal decomposition reactions and address the aldehyde reactions from their appropriate precursors. We will construct a highly reliable and informative experimental database for the future interpretation of the key rate coefficients and validation of the detailed biofuel kinetic models.

14234116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14234116.value: This project aims to understand the pyrolysis chemical kinetics of biodiesel fuel and surrogates, the long-chain (C10-C18) methyl esters, through experimental research using an aerosol shock tube equipped with advanced laser diagnostics. Biofuels, as additives or alternatives to petroleum-based transportation fuels, are of growing interest in national strategic fuel planning due to their sustainability and lower exhaust emissions. Biodiesel is among the best candidates to replace the diesel fuels used in current engine systems. Most biodiesel fuels consist of mixtures of C16-C18 fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs), which can be derived from the transesterification process of renewable sources like vegetable oil or animal fat with methanol. In particular, Hong Kong has numerous restaurants annually generating 20,000 tons of used cooking oil and 170,000 tons of grease trap waste, which can be collected and converted into biodiesel instead of being simply poured into drains. Understanding the fuel combustion chemistry is of critical importance for optimizing the engine efficiency and minimizing pollutant emissions. In the combustion chamber, fuel molecules break down first prior to burning to form a large amount of intermediates and soot. This process is known as pyrolysis and one that is still poorly understood or completely unknown for biodiesel. We have previously investigated the pyrolysis kinetics of C1-C4 small alkyl esters to understand the impact of the ester function group on the fuel reactivity. However, it has recently become acknowledged that the selection of small esters as biodiesel surrogates is unsuitable because of their different combustion characteristics from actual biodiesels. There is thus a strong need to extend the biodiesel pyrolysis study to larger FAMEs or even the actual fuel components. In this project, we propose to use a shock tube study to address the pyrolysis of two C10 biodiesel surrogates, methyl decanoate and its unsaturated counterpart, methyl-5-decenoate, as well as two actual biodiesel components, methyl palmitate and methyl oleate. The experimental approach involves the use of a novel aerosol shock tube, which is equipped with advanced laser absorption diagnostics for quantitative and time-resolved species detection. In addition to exploring the pyrolysis chemistry of these molecules, the PI plans to measure the rate coefficients of the key elementary reactions involved in the detailed kinetic mechanisms. The potential outcome of the proposed study will significantly help to understand the first steps during the combustion of biodiesel fuels and lead to technology improvements in the area of renewable biofuels. 本項目旨在實驗研究生物柴油及其替代物（C10-C18長鏈脂肪酸甲酯）熱解的化學反應動力學機理。生物質能直接或間接地來源於綠色植物的光合作用，可替代傳統化石燃料，具有可再生、低汙染等特點。在眾多生物質能利用中，生物柴油作為含C16-C18的脂肪酸甲酯，可從多種生物原料中提取，具有低硫量、低芳烴含量、良好的潤滑性等特點，是一種優質的柴油引擎清潔燃料。需要特別提到的是，香港每年約產生 20,000 公噸廢食油以及170,000公噸隔油池廢物，這些地溝油經過簡單的工藝提取能成為制備生物柴油的原料，因此有關生物柴油燃燒特性的研究受到廣泛關註。在燃燒過程中，燃料分子的初步反應通常是分解生成大量的中間體和碳黑，該過程也被稱為熱解反應，然而生物柴油的熱解反應機理至今仍不清楚，長鏈甲酯的熱解研究無論在實驗還是理論上都存在很高的難度。我們計劃采用激波管技術，結合激光吸收光譜測量，實驗研究兩種癸酸甲酯類生物柴油替代物以及兩種生物柴油實際組分（棕櫚酸甲酯和油酸甲酯）的熱解，測量這些酯類燃料熱解過程中的重要基元反應速率常數，並創建更為合理的反應機理模型。本研究將為理解生物柴油熱解反應提供重要的實驗數據，有助於徹底理解生物柴油燃燒機理，降低燃燒過程中汙染物的生成。

14234116.label: Realisation of objectives
14234116.value: All the research objectives have been achieved in the project period. We have made significant progress in all respects of this project on experiment and modeling. Our research findings have resulted in eighteen papers published in the peer-reviewed journals such as Combustion and Flame, Proceedings of Combustion Institute, The Journal of Physical Chemistry, Physical Chemistry and Chemical Physics, and Angewandte Chemie. Here we summarize the key research results and findings. Objective 1: Development of an aerosol shock tube for studying low-vapor-pressure liquid fuels. We developed an aerosol shock tube with an inner diameter of 12 cm, a driver section of 3 m, and a driven section of 6.5 m; the facility provides a temperature of 800-2000 K and pressure of 0.1-6.0 MPa, and a test time of 10 ms. The fuel aerosol was generated using a Laval nozzle with a size distribution between 2-5 um. The uniform aerosol was then drawn into the driven section of the shock tube for high-temperature experiments. To generate a shock wave with well-controlled T5 and P5 conditions, a sharp plunger with a needle head was fabricated to rupture the diagram with the selected initial T1 and P1. A temperature variation of less than 0.3% was achieved using the current diaphragm breaking mechanism. Additionally, we systematically validated the AEROFROSH code in our facility by conducting temperature measurements using laser-based two-line thermometry. Objective 2: Development of laser-based combustion diagnostics for multi-species measurements. We developed laser-based sensors using the mid-infrared absorption lines for the sensitive and fast detection of CO, CO2, C2H4 and CH2O. Two quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) at 4.6 um and 10.5 um were exploited for CO and C2H4 detection, and two interband cascade lasers (ICLs) at 3.6 um and 4.3 um were used for CH2O and CO2 detection. A mid-infrared two-line thermometry based on H2O absorption was developed for in situ and sensitive temperature measurements, which has been reported in Combustion Science and Technology. Such an absorption sensor was also used for the improved study of the uniformity of laminar premixed flames. This work has been published in journals Energy & Fuels and Experimental Thermal and Fluid Science. In addition, we developed the first heterodyne phase-sensitive dispersion spectroscopy for the simultaneous temperature and species concentration measurements in combustion environments, which has been published in Applied Physics B. The injection current of each QCL was modulated at sub-GHz or GHz to generate the three-tone radiation and the dispersion signal was detected by the radio-frequency down-conversion heterodyning. We demonstrated that HPSDS was immune to optical power fluctuations by measuring the dispersion spectra at varied incident laser powers, which has been reported in Proceedings of the Combustion Institute. Objective 3: Chemical kinetic modeling and shock tube studies of fuel pyrolysis. For large molecules such as long-chain FAMEs, it was challenging to predict accurate thermodynamics and kinetics by theoretical calculations due to the very high computational cost for electronic structure calculations and the high complexity for anharmonicity treatment. Thus we developed a two-layer ONIOM-CCSD(T)/CBS method for bond dissociation energies of C6-C20 alkanes (published in Chemical Physics Letters), a cascaded group-additivity ONIOM method to approach the globally accurate electronic energies of C12-C16 hydrocarbons (published in Combustion and Flame), and a novel multi-structural 2-dimensional torsion method (MS-2DT) based on minimally coupled approximation to treat the low-frequency anharmonicity presented in large flexible hydrocarbons (published in Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics). After being validated against the experimental measurements, these methods opened up new opportunities of predicting the thermodynamics and kinetics of large hydrocarbon systems accurately and efficiently. In shock tube experiments, we measured multi-species (CO, CO2 and H2O) concentration time-histories during the pyrolysis and oxidation of ethyl formate at 1331−1615 K and 1.52−1.74 atm, which were compared with a detailed chemical kinetic mechanism over the entire temperature range. This work has been published in Journal of Physical Chemistry A. Additionally, we studied the chemical kinetics of nitromethane by measuring the NO time-histories during the pyrolysis of nitromethane at ∼3.5 atm and 1013 K–1418 K in the shock tube. All the NO time-histories measured over the entire temperature range were well-predicted by a recent kinetic model in terms of the initial NO formation rate and the final plateau level. This work has been published in Proceedings of the Combustion Institute. Objective 4: Investigation of the rate coefficients of key elementary reactions. The rate coefficients of several key reactions were studied in shock tube experiments using laser absorption measurements and by theoretical calculations. We studied the rate coefficients for H-abstractions of methyl formate and ethyl formate over a wide temperature range 900‒1300 K and varied pressures by monitoring the species time-history of hydroxyl radical using UV absorption. This work has been published in Journal of Physical Chemistry A. For the H-abstraction reactions of a larger ester, phenyl formate, we measured the OH concentration time-histories in a shock tube at 968‒1128 K and 1.16‒1.25 atm. The obtained rate coefficients were compared with the theoretical calculations using the composite method ROCBS-QB3//M06-2X/cc-pVTZ, showing a good agreement (within 15%) over the entire experimental conditions. Comparisons of site-specific H-abstractions with other esters and hydrocarbons were performed to understand the effects of different functional groups. This work has been reported in Physical Chemistry and Chemical Physics. Additionally, we conducted a high-accuracy quantum chemistry method and variational transition state theory to study the particular reaction involving methanol, hydroxyl and water vapor. Our study reveals that the catalytic effect of water vapor on the methanol and hydroxyl reaction is negligible in the atmosphere. This work has been reported in Angewandte Chemie and highlighted as the Very Important Paper (VIP).

We will also revise the shock wave calculation method by accounting for droplet evaporation and additional thermodynamic/gasdynamic factors.

We will develop laser absorption diagnostics for quantitative concentration time-history measurements of CO, CO2, C2H4, CH2O and fuel. New line-selection rules will be adopted to improve the detection accuracy of CO and CO2 by minimizing the detection uncertainty caused by temperature variation. We will implement a quantum cascade laser at 10.53 micron to achieve interference-free C2H4 detection using wavelength modulation spectroscopy or a differential absorption scheme. We will also develop new absorption sensors for CH2O and fuel diagnostics using interband cascade lasers between 3.3-3.6 micron.

We will perform shock tube and kinetic modeling study of the pyrolysis of long-chain FAMEs, including methyl decanoate, methyl-5-decenoate, methyl palmitate and methyl oleate. We will conduct simultaneous measurements of the time-dependent species concentrations throughout the thermal decomposition process at different temperatures (1,000-1,600 K) and pressures (1-10 atm). We will particularly examine the influences of the C=C double bond and the length of aliphatic chain on fuel decomposition pathways, CO/CO2 formation, and eventually reactivity and pollutants.

We will investigate and validate the rate coefficients of the key elementary reactions involved in the biodiesel kinetic mechanism. In particular, we will measure the rate coefficients of HOCO radical thermal decomposition reactions and address the aldehyde reactions from their appropriate precursors. We will construct a highly reliable and informative experimental database for the future interpretation of the key rate coefficients and validation of the detailed biofuel kinetic models.

14234116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14234116.value: In this project we have developed laser-based optical sensors for the sensitive and fast detection of CO, CO2, C2H4, CH2O and H2O. Two quantum cascade lasers (QCLs) at 4.6 um and 10.5 um were exploited for CO and C2H4 detection, and two interband cascade lasers (ICLs) at 3.6 um and 4.3 um were used for CH2O and CO2 detection. A mid-infrared two-line thermometry based on H2O absorption was developed for in situ temperature measurements [Combustion Science and Technology, 190; Energy & Fuels, 32; Experimental Thermal and Fluid Science, 112]. We also developed the first heterodyne phase-sensitive dispersion spectroscopy for the simultaneous temperature and species concentration measurements [Applied Physics B, 124], which demonstrated intrinsic immunity to optical power fluctuations [Proceedings of the Combustion Institute, 37]. For the theoretical study of large fuel molecules, we proposed a two-layer ONIOM-CCSD(T)/CBS method for determining bond dissociation energies [Chemical Physics Letters, 699], a cascaded group-additivity ONIOM method for approaching the accurate electronic energies [Combustion and Flame, 201], and a multi-structural 2-dimensional torsion method (MS-2DT) for low-frequency anharmonicity treatment [Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics, 21]. After being validated against the experimental measurements, these methods opened up new opportunities of predicting the thermodynamics and kinetics of large hydrocarbon systems accurately and efficiently. In shock tube experiments, we measured multi-species (CO, CO2 and H2O) concentration time-histories during the pyrolysis of methyl and ethyl esters, which were compared with detailed chemical kinetic mechanisms [Journal of Physical Chemistry A, 121(35); Proceedings of the Combustion Institute, 211]. The rate coefficients of key reactions such as the hydrogen abstraction reactions of ethyl formate [Journal of Physical Chemistry A, 121 (33)], phenyl formate [Physical Chemistry and Chemical Physics, 20], and methyl formate [Angewandte Chemie, 59] by hydroxyl radical were theoretically calculated and experimentally validated in this project. We expect that our research outcomes provide a versatile theoretical and experimental database for the thorough understanding of large-size fuel molecules such as biodiesel.

14234116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14234116.value: The progressive depletion of oil reserves and the negative environmental impact of fossil fuel use have made it critical to develop alternative liquid transportation fuels. A frontier in this area is to completely understand the combustion properties of fuel components, thereby leading to a validated and predictive combustion modelling capability to optimize the design of evolving fuels in advanced engines. It has been recently accepted that furans and tetrahydrofurans are the promising second generation biofuels, which can be used in internal combustion engines as pure fuels or fuel extenders. However, pyrolysis and oxidation properties of furan-based fuels are poorly understood or completely unknown. With the completion of this project, we have demonstrated the capability of studying large fuel molecules using ab initio calculations and shock tube experiments. We will further extend these methods and techniques to other new types of biofuels such as furans. We will seek the funding support from RGC to conduct a comprehensive study of different furan-based fuels and to identify the optimal fuel type for a higher combustion efficiency and lower emission. Our ultimate goal is to adopt the state-of-the-art experimental and modelling research to explore the next-generation biofuels.

14234116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14234116.value: It is important to understand the combustion performance of biofuels before they are directly used in engine systems. In this project we have developed laser-based sensors for the sensitive and fast detection of multi-species in combustion environments. We also developed the first heterodyne phase-sensitive dispersion spectroscopy for the simultaneous temperature and species concentration measurements, which demonstrated the intrinsic immunity to optical power fluctuations. For the theoretical study of large fuel molecules, we proposed a two-layer ONIOM-CCSD(T)/CBS method for determining bond dissociation energies, a cascaded group-additivity ONIOM method for approaching the accurate electronic energies, and a multi-structural 2-dimensional torsion method (MS-2DT) for low-frequency anharmonicity treatment. These methods opened up new opportunities of predicting the thermodynamics and kinetics of large hydrocarbon systems accurately and efficiently. In shock tube experiments, we measured multi-species (CO, CO2 and H2O) concentration time-histories during the pyrolysis of different methyl and ethyl esters, which could be used to understand the detailed chemical kinetic mechanisms. The rate coefficients of several key reactions such as the hydrogen abstraction reactions of fuel molecules were theoretically calculated and experimentally validated in this project. Our research outcomes provide a versatile theoretical and experimental database for the thorough understanding of large fuel molecules.

14234416.label: Project Objectives
14234416.value: Cost-Effective Logging Mechanism Design The effectiveness of log analysis is heavily dependent on the quality of logs collected, which are further based on the underlying logging. Logging is a non-trivial task. Logging too little may miss important information of interest, while logging too much will incur high cost, such as consuming additional system resources and causing non-negligible performance overhead. The objective of this task is to improve the quality of logging in software systems by designing and implementing a cost-effective logging mechanism. Log Collection and Parsing Large-scale distributed systems are presently generating tons of logs. To make use of such logs, usually, the first step is log collection that ensembles all the logs into a center node or a distributed file system such as HDFS. However, with the increasing scale of a software system, coupled with the wide geographical distribution of software components, log collection has become a highly challenging task. Besides, logs mostly contain free-text messages, which make it difficult for automated analysis. The objective here is to develop an efficient framework for log collection and online parsing so as to enable both offline and online log analyses. Log Analysis for System Troubleshooting Logs contain a wealth of information for reliability engineering tasks. Traditional approaches that rely heavily on manual inspection of logs have become inadequate, as they are labor-intensive, error-prone, and inefficient. The objective here is to advance the state-of-the-art techniques of log analysis for automated system troubleshooting. To be specific, we will investigate the following two phases: anomaly detection and system problem diagnosis.

14234416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14234416.value: Nowadays software services play an indispensible role in our daily life, providing a wide variety of functionalities including search engine, social networking, online chatting, and online shopping, etc. Unlike traditional shrink-wrapped software, most of these software services are designed as large-scale distributed systems operating on a 24x7 basis to serve millions of users globally. The success of such a software service is highly dependent on its reliability, which is one of the most important quality-of-service measures. Any service outage or degradation of service quality can lead to user dissatisfaction and cause significant revenue loss. The high cost of such service incidents reveals the critical need for reliability engineering involving engineering principles and techniques to maintain high reliability of a software system. With the increasing complexity and scale of distributed systems, coupled with the geo-distribution of different service components, maintaining high reliability of these systems becomes a notoriously challenging task. Data-driven reliability engineering is emerging as a new trend that makes use of data-driven approaches to gain actionable information and provide powerful insights for system troubleshooting. In practice, pervasive logs generated by large-scale distributed systems are often used as a principal tool for reliability engineering tasks. These include anomaly detection and failure diagnosis. But with the increasing volume of log data, traditional approaches that heavily rely on manual inspection of these logs have become inadequate. This is because they are often labor-intensive, error-prone, and inefficient. As a result, there is a high demand for powerful tools to automate the entire process, including instrumentation, collection, parsing, and analysis of logs. This project aims at advancing the state-of-the-art techniques of log monitoring and analysis for data-driven reliability engineering. To address the critical challenges posed by large-scale distributed systems and huge amounts of logs, we will explore topics across areas in data analytics and distributed systems, and investigate a novel use of data analytic techniques to develop tools that are efficient and intelligent enough for automated system troubleshooting. Specifically, four tasks are proposed: Task 1 will study the design of a cost-effective logging mechanism to balance the utility and overhead of system logging; Task 2 will explore the framework for efficient log collection and parsing; Task 3 will investigate automated analysis of logs for system troubleshooting, including anomaly detection and problem diagnosis; and finally, Task 4 will implement the proposed techniques into an open-source toolkit and publish a set of real-world log datasets. 軟件服務在我們今天的日常生活中扮演不可或缺的角色，提供了多種功能，包括搜索引擎，社交網絡，網上聊天，網上購物等，與傳統的套裝軟件。其中大部分軟件服務都設計為在大型分佈式系統上全天候運作，以便服務於全球數以百萬的機用戶。這樣的軟件服務的成敗，很大程度上取決於它的可靠性，這也是高質量服務的最重要的措施之一。任何服務中斷或服務質量的降低可能會導致用戶不滿，造成顯著經濟損失。高成本的服務事故，顯示了涉及工程原理和技術上迫切的需要，以維護軟件系統的高可靠性。隨著日益複雜規模的分佈式系統，再加上不同的服務組件的地理分佈，維護這些系統的高可靠性成為富有挑戰的任務。爲此，數據驅動的可靠性工程成為一種新的趨勢，即利用數據驅動的方法來獲取可操作的信息，並提供系統故障排除的功能。在實踐中，由大規模分佈式系統產生普遍的日誌，常被用作可靠性工程任務的主要工具；這些包括異常檢測和故障診斷。但隨著日誌數據量的不斷增加，人工檢查日誌的傳統方法，已經顯得不足。這是因為人工檢查往往勞動密集，容易出錯，並且效率低下。因此，我們對使整個過程自動化的步驟和工具，包括測量，收集，分析，和日誌的分析，有很大的需求。 本項目旨在推進日誌監測和分析的最先進的技術，從而建立數據驅動的可靠性工程。為了解決大規模分佈式系統和大量日誌所帶來的嚴峻挑戰，我們將探討在數據分析跨區域主題和分佈式系統，並研究利用數據分析技術，開發出高效與智能工具，達成自動化的系統故障排除。具體而言，我們提出四個任務：任務一是研究具有成本效益的記錄機制，以平衡實用程序和系統日誌的開銷;任務二是探索有效的日誌收集和分析框架;任務三是探討日誌系統故障排除技術，包括異常檢測和故障診斷的自動分析；最後，任務四是實現所提出的技術到一個開源工具包，並發布了一組真實世界的日誌數據集。

14234416.label: Realisation of objectives
14234416.value: All the objectives in this project have been either completely achieved or exceedingly achieved. We proposed to improve the reliability of various systems with a massive number of logs that capture abundant system runtime information. Our methods are generally applicable to a wide range of systems, including mobile systems, software systems and distributed systems, which can be employed to most applications and services nowadays. To achieve the first objective, we proposed to improve the logging mechanism by studying the logging statements with natural language processing. Regarding the second objective, we investigated the log parsing, which is very crucial to the down steaming tasks, log analysis, as described in the third objective. We thereby designed a novel and high-efficient log parsing approach and verified its effectiveness on various datasets. Since the log is free-form text, it can be analyzed with advanced natural language processing techniques. In the third objective, we suggested several novel natural language processing methods for text classification, topic modeling, etc. To achieve our project objectives, several machine learning and natural language processing techniques were also employed and designed, including emerging issue identification, learning to rank, multi-arm bandits, etc.

14234416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14234416.value: In total, 1 journal paper and 20 conference papers are published, covering the project’s objectives in various aspects. These publications all acknowledge the support of this grant. We describe the resulting outcomes as follows. (We use [C1] label to refer to conference publication [1], and [J1] label to refer to journal publication [1], etc.) The first objective is to design a cost-effective logging mechanism, we designed a “learning to rank” method [C5], which used localized geometric mean metrics and could be applied to rank the priority of potential logging places. Besides, we also designed a covariance matrix estimation method on compressed data [C9], which could guide the strategic logging method. In addition, we proposed an aggregated temporal tensor factorization model [J1] to recommend point-of-interests, which further supported the logging statement recommendation. In addition, we proposed to complete the source code with advanced neural networks, where logging statement can also be generated [C11]. We further studied the resilient bi-opaque rredicates against symbolic execution, which helped determine the logging statement position in the source code [C13]. Moreover, we proposed to improve the logging mechanism by investigating the logging statements with natural language processing (NLP) [C20]. In the second objective of log collection and log parsing, we have proposed an online log parsing method, namely Drain [C1]. Due to the great number of logs that might be generated in an online stream, an efficient and effective hashing method [C6] was proposed for disk space saving and the logging traffic should be predicted accurately with machine learning methods [C7] to better adopt the logging volume. To improve log analysis for system troubleshooting (the third objective), we suggested a reliability prediction method, namely CARP [C2], which could predict the reliability of black-box Web service with historical usage data. We also designed several approaches based on state-of-the-art NLP techniques and deep neural networks, which can be engaged to predict the anomaly or the problem type [C4, C16, C19]. An effective emerging issue identification method was proposed and verified on various datasets, which could be applied to the log-based issue identification [C10]. Furthermore proposed several machine learning based methods [C8, C12, C14, C15, C17, C18], which could provide some insights on the anomaly detection, problem identification, and more efficient data processing, etc., for log analysis. Finally, we have implemented the above-mentioned techniques and conducted comprehensive experiments accordingly. The source code and data were publicly released to promote related research.

14234416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14234416.value: In this project, we have investigated a framework for log monitoring and analysis for data-driven reliability engineering, including the logging statement, log collection and parsing, and anomaly detection. To this end, various machine learning and natural language processing techniques have been proposed and employed, including convolutional neural networks, topic modeling, text classification, and so on. For future research, we would consider the case of real-world deployment, where the labeled data is very limited. Given the limited labeled data, it is hard to incorporate a complex machine learning or deep learning model into the real use. Besides, we can collect more kinds of data source, e.g., CPU statistics, memory usage in a systematic and comprehensive way. We will attempt to improve the reliability of modern systems by observing these aspects jointly.

14234416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14234416.value: In this project, we investigated and improved system reliability based on a massive number of logs. The targets include mobile systems, software systems and distributed systems, which are employed to support most applications and services nowadays. We studied the logging statements with natural language processing techniques, which have shown their potential to improve the logging mechanism. As log parsing process is very crucial to the down steaming tasks such as log analysis, we improve the log parsing process with a novel and high-efficient approach, and verify its effectiveness on various datasets. In addition, we designed several novel machine learning and natural language processing techniques, including learning to rank, text classification, topic modeling, which can support the log-based analysis task. The research outcome can bring new insights and practical applications for systematic reliability engineering of modern systems.
