14236516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14236516.value: Recent years have witnessed unprecedented enthusiasm towards online photo sharing across the globe. The value of online images consists not only in the images themselves but also in the rich semantic information that they convey. Despite the remarkable progress in the past several years (thanks to the breakthrough in deep learning), attempts to extract and utilize such information using vision techniques, however, still meet with fundamental difficulties. It has been a long standing practice in computer vision to develop models based on closed training sets, where the data are carefully curated and the concepts to be recognized are well defined. This approach is obviously infeasible in a web-scale environment, where we are facing billions of highly diverse images with little annotation. Moreover, the Internet sees new images every day -- many of them may reflect new semantic concepts that the model has never seen. In response to such challenges, we move beyond conventional paradigms and propose a novel framework that combines two innovative techniques for web-scale image tagging. First, we propose a new formulation based on Discriminative bundles, where each bundle is a combination of a small group of samples and a small subset of tag classes. This leads to an efficient learning algorithm that allows new tags to be introduced on the fly and adaptive schemes where difficult cases would receive more attention. Second, we propose a contextually-supervised learning algorithm, which circumvents the huge cost of annotation by exploiting the contextual data, such as textual descriptions and similar samples. With a statistical context model, it can reason about possible tags of an unannotated image by associating it with the context, and estimate the confidence of the inferred tags. In this way, we are able to utilize the immense amount of data on the web in a reliable way without involving an expensive manual annotation process. Whereas we are focusing on a specific problem, namely image tagging, the impact of this work will reach far beyond this topic. The experience that we gain in this course will surely provide valuable insight to Big data analytics, and the methodologies thus developed can be adopted in a broad range of applications that face significant challenges in exploiting large-scale open data, such as consumer trend analysis in e-commerce and the Internet of Things. 近年來，全球範圍掀起了對在線圖像分享的前所未有的熱情。在線圖像的價值不僅僅存在于這些圖像本身更在於它們所蘊含的豐富語義信息。儘管由於深度學習的突破，圖像識別取得了顯著的進展，利用視覺技術從網絡圖像中獲取依然面臨著很大的困難。 在計算機視覺領域，模型通常實在封閉的數據集上訓練的。數據集中的圖像需要事先經過細緻的人工檢驗，分類的類型也是事先定義好的。這個方法在互聯網級別規模的數據（數以十億計算的高度多樣化的圖片）中是不適用的。更嚴重的困難在于，網絡上的圖片每天都在急遽增長。 為了應對日益增長的數據規模和多樣化的挑戰，我們需要打破原有圖像識別範式的限制。為此，我們提出兩個新型的技術。首先，我們提出可鑒別样本束的概念。這裡，每個樣本束是一小群樣本與一個標注類小子集的結合體。基於這個概念，我能可以獲得更為高效靈活的算法，它允許隨機引入的新標注類型並且允許學習過程自適應地調整關注點。另外，我們提出一種由語境監督的學習算法，它通過對語境信息（比如圖像描述或者其它帶標注的相似圖像）的充分利用來避免人工標注以及尤其來帶的巨大標注成本。這個算法通過一個統計語境模型對一個未標注圖像的可能標注進行推斷，並評估推斷得到的標注的置信度。這樣，我們就可以可靠地利用互聯網上海量的數據信息而不需要昂貴的大規模人工標注。 雖然這個項目專注于圖像標註應用，這個工作的影響將遠超這個應用本身。在研發這個框架的過程中，我們將獲得大數據分析與利用的寶貴經驗，而因此獲得的方法也將能廣泛運用於對大規模開放數據的分析，比如在電子商務以及物聯網中的消費趨勢分析。

14236516.label: Realisation of objectives
14236516.value: Overall, all project objectives have been completely achieved. The primary goal of this project is to develop a web image tagging system. The development of such a system requires a module for visual analytics that can effectively recognize the content in images and detect objects of interest, a module to discover and exploit the relationships between an image and its contextual text, as well as a module that can continuously learn from massive amount of new data, which allows a model to be improved progressively. Through a series of research works, the techniques behind these modules have been substantially improved and ready for large-scale practical use. Along with the development of these techniques, we constructed a large-scale dataset with 8M images associated with rich semantic information and description and built a prototype demo. The details of the developed techniques are presented below. Note that all the presented techniques have been published on major international conferences, namely CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS and AAAI. ### Object Detection It has been widely recognized by the computer vision community that object detection plays a central role in image understanding. Over the past several years, thanks to the wide adoption of deep learning technologies, we have seen remarkable advances in object detection. However, we still often find that object detection in the wild remains very challenging. To tackle the challenges in practical object detection, we carefully examined the pipeline of mainstream detection frameworks, and developed a series of methods to improve the overall accuracy and efficiency. 1) We revisited the stage of anchoring, a foundational stage for modern object detection frameworks, and developed a new anchoring method named Guided Anchoring, which leverages semantic features to predict the spatial distribution of anchors, thus resulting in much more effective anchor placement. 2) We also considered the feature upsampling operation. In particular, we proposed CARAFE, a feature upsampling operator that allows adaptive construction of feature pyramids, thus significantly boosting the detection performance. 3) We carefully examined the standard training practice of modern detectors, and proposed several balancing techniques to address the imbalance issues at the sample level, feature level, and object level, leading to a more effective design, named Libra R-CNN. 4) To pursue more accurate detection and instance segmentation, we developed Hybrid Task Cascade, a new framework that allows bounding box detection and mask prediction to interact with each other. This framework not only leads to more reliable localization but also more accurate differentiation between foreground and background. ### Person Recognition In many images, especially those on the web, persons are often the major entities. Hence, people recognition is a key component in a web image tagging system. It is noteworthy that “person recognition” is not equivalent to “facial recognition”. In addition to facial appearance, one may also resort to other cues, such as wearings and other contextual cues to infer a person’s identity. Along this direction, we developed a framework that leverages visual and social contexts for person recognition. This framework integrates facial appearance, clothes, as well as social relations when predicting the identity of a person, mitigating the difficulties caused by issues like profile views, unfavorable lighting, and occlusion, which often arise in practice. In a later work, we extended this framework, incorporating not only visual connections but also temporal links inherent in videos to propagate identify inference results, which significantly improves the reliability of person recognition in long videos and real-world visual collections. ### Joint Visual and Linguistic Analysis As an important goal of this project, we aim to move beyond the conventional paradigm where the tagging model is learned in a way that is similar to learning a classification model. In this project, we want to learn the tagging model by associating the visual domain and the linguistic domain. In this way, we can effectively leverage the tremendous amount of data on the web. In recent years, joint analytics of visual and linguistic data has emerged as an active research topic. The research on this topic generally fall in two categories: captioning and grounding. The progress on these tasks would lead to more expressive representations for both images and text. In this project, we carefully examined the current paradigm of image captioning and developed a contrastive learning algorithm that encourages distinctiveness while maintaining the overall quality of the generated descriptions. We found that this method often results in more expressive descriptions. We also revisited the latent representation and proposed a 2D representation to take the place of conventional 1D representation, which substantially improves the expressive power, allowing various parts of the description to be individually related to specific areas of the image. In a latest work, we drew on our advances in visual and linguistic representations, and developed a comprehensive framework to bridge the visual and the linguistic domains. This is a graph-based framework, which, by matching a scene graph in the visual domain and a semantic graph constructed from the textual description, can produce detailed matching between an image or a video and a long textual description. ### Large-scale Learning To obtain the models for visual understanding, learning is the key approach. Note that we are aiming at a model that can cover generic web-scale tagging. Therefore, the capability of learning from massive amount of data is crucial. In developing the learning method, we are facing two significant challenges arising from practice: 1) annotating a huge amount of data is prohibitively expensive, and 2) training a model on a large-scale dataset is also very costly. The efforts to tackle these two difficulties respectively lead to our works in unsupervised / semi-supervised learning and continual learning. We proposed an unsupervised feature learning method, which shows that good feature representation can be learned by discriminating between instances in a nonparametric manner. This work, since its publication, has already generated great impact on the area of unsupervised learning. Later, we took a deeper look into the visual structure, and developed a self-supervised learning method via conditional motion propagation, which leverages motion cues to learn a representation of the inherent visual structure. We also considered the setting of combining a small set of annotated data (as seeds) with a large quantity of unannotated data and developed a new method called Consensus-driven propagation that allows effective use of massive unlabeled data by using a learned modulator to control the propagation of identities. Recent works have shown that clustering unlabeled samples is also a promising approach. We explored a new approach that learns how to effectively cluster faces, which can yield much more accurate clustering results than conventional methods, thus leading to further boost of the recognition performance. Along the direction of continual learning, we developed a progressive learning method, which strikes a good balance between preservation and adaptation via a new scheme: adapting through knowledge distillation and preserving through an adaptive cache. Later, we improved this approach through a combination of rebalancing techniques, namely cosine normalization, less-forget constraint, and inter-class separation. These techniques effectively mitigate the issue of catastrophic forgetting, making continual learning a practical approach.

14236516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14236516.value: Overall, we found that effective image tagging at the web scale requires a combination of multiple techniques, including visual recognition techniques (especially object detection and person recognition), connection between visual and linguistic domains, and large-scale learning that can leverage unannotated data. 1. Effective object detection is the key to accurate image tagging. Current detection frameworks can be improved in various aspects: a) anchoring can be guided by content (CVPR’19); b) adaptive feature upsampling can lead to more expressive feature pyramids (ICCV’19); c) balance needs to be maintained at different levels of the detection pipeline (CVPR’19); d) detection and segmentation are mutually conducive and therefore it is beneficial to interleave these tasks in a hybrid cascade framework (CVPR’19); and e) the computation cost for object detection in videos can be greatly reduced by exploiting the temporal continuity (CVPR’18). 2. The performance of person recognition can be improved by leveraging contextual information. Specifically, we found that social context can provide complementary information (CVPR’18), and that visual and temporal links and be combined to help propagate person identities (ECCV’18). 3. The connections between the visual and linguistic domains are important. Effective utilization of such connections can help us to leverage the tremendous amount of data on the web. Specifically, we found: a) distinctiveness is a key quality to pursue when connecting these two domains and this can be accomplished by contrastive learning (NeurIPS’17); b) a two-dimensional latent representation is more effective than one-dimensional in connecting across domains; and c) a graph-based framework can take the vision-text association to a new level, where individual parts of a description can be effectively associated with specific visual regions (ICCV’19). 4. There exist effective methods to leverage unannotated data to learn visual recognition models, which is crucial for developing a web-scale tagging system. In particular, we found: a) nonparametric discrimination can learn features in an unsupervised manner (CVPR’18); and b) motion cues are beneficial for unsupervised feature learning (CVPR’19); and c) semi-supervised learning can be made more effective by learning how to propagate (ECCV’18) and how to cluster (CVPR’19). 5. A model can be learned in a progressive way without being re-trained from scratch when new data come in. Effective progressive learning requires a balance between preservation and adaptation (ECCV’18) and rebalancing techniques can help (CVPR’19).

14236516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14236516.value: This project poses several questions that deserve further development in future exploration. 1. The connections between visual and linguistic domains are important. We may explore effective representations to jointly model the entities in both domains. Recent advances in natural language processing, especially the development of powerful language models such as BERT and GPT-3 may open a door to move this research to a new level. 2. As short videos grow rapidly over the web, it is interesting to see how the methods developed in this project can be extended to accommodate video data. In particular, video data provide a new dimension, namely the temporal evolution, and thus new opportunities for future research. 3. To more effectively tag or interpret visual content, we may want to upgrade the current techniques for visual understanding from intermediate level (e.g. object, person identities, and action) to a higher level (e.g. stories). It is very challenging to attain this level of understanding. However, with more advanced techniques being developed, this is worthy of exploration.

14236516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14236516.value: This project is to develop a set of techniques to support web-scale image tagging, which is a task to automatically provide semantic tags, e.g. wedding, tiger, beautiful summer, to any given image. With such a tagging system, one can easily and efficiently retrieve and organize the tremendous amount of images shared on the web. Note that while image tagging techniques have existed for years. Previous methods fall short in accuracy, efficiency, and generality. Hence, it is difficult to apply such techniques for large-scale real-world application. The primary goal of this project is to overcome the key difficulties in such techniques, making automatic image tagging a viable technique for practical use. With the methods developed in this project, we significantly improved the expressive power of the visual and linguistic representation, and thus boosted the accuracy and generality of the tagging system. It is also noteworthy that the techniques for unsupervised, semi-supervised, and continual learning, which we develop in this project, can greatly reduce the data cost and computing cost for training a visual recognition model in large scale.

14237616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14237616.value: One central research problem in the field of financial engineering is to design and price derivative assets. Among the most important tools to manage risks, financial derivatives offer market participants flexible protections against the shock of adverse events. Stimulated the great need of using derivatives for the purpose of risk management, the global derivative markets have experienced remarkable growth over the past several decades, reaching a total size of US$630 trillion in terms of notational amounts outstanding as of Dec. 2014. How to accurately value derivatives in line with their risk profile is surely one key to maintain this tremendous market functioning well. Emerging in the recent literature, two broad families of stochastic models, Levy process-driven models and affine jump-diffusion models, attract enormous attention from both academia and industry because they provide sufficiently flexible modeling vehicles to capture some important empirical regularities of the price movements. Many researches corroborate that such kind of models can achieve superior performance in derivative pricing. However, the transition probability density functions of both the classes of models, one essential component for the pricing methods, are explicitly known only through the corresponding characteristic functions. This limited tractability significantly confines the application domains of the models. Except for some simple cases, how to use them to evaluate derivatives with complex payoff structures or dependent on a multiple of underlying assets, where quantitative methods are most needed to understand the risks, poses a great computational challenge. Motivated by this application in finance, the proposed research aims to develop a Monte Carlo approach to simulate and compute from characteristic functions. Based on a key relationship, known as the Parseval identity in Fourier analysis, we innovatively propose to transform a problem of simulating from the original probability space to a task of simulating in its frequency domain. This new approach will yield unbiased estimates for functions of random variable whose distributional laws are explicitly given by their characteristic functions. From it, we can build up efficient computational methods to resolve the difficulties that the conventional approaches encountered in pricing derivatives modeled by such new models as the above two. Our approach will also provide convenient tools for performing sensitivity analysis on pricing results. We can use them to quantify the impacts caused by changes of risk factors, which will contribute valuable insights into risk management on the derivatives. 金融工程領域的一大核心問題是如何設計及定價衍生產品。作爲重要的風險管理工具，金融衍生物為市場參與者提供了對沖市場反向衝擊的方便靈活的保護措施。正是因爲這種風險管理的需要，全球衍生品市場在過去的幾十年中得到了長足的發展。到2014年底，市場名義流通量達到了驚人的630万億美元。 如何準確的對衍生產品定價，使之能正確反映它們的風險程度，顯然是維護這個龐大市場正常運行的關鍵一步。近年來在文獻中出現的兩大類隨機模型，Levy過程驅動的隨機模型以及仿射跳躍擴散過程，因爲它們能產生出於實證觀察相吻合的現象，而受到學術界和工業界的廣泛關注。但是這兩類過程的轉移概率密度函數並不擁有顯式表達式，人們只能通過對其對應的特徵函數求逆來認識它們。這樣有限的解析性為我們對用這些模型建模的複雜金融產品定價帶來了計算上的困難。 應映這樣的挑戰，該項目建議發展一種基於特徵函數直接抽樣的蒙特卡洛模擬方法。從富立葉分析的Parseval等式出發，我們創造性地提出把在原概率空間上的模擬問題轉化成其頻域空間的模擬問題。利用已知的特徵函數，我們能夠構造針對定價的有效無偏估計，同時為定價的敏感度分析提供方便的計算工具。我們的研究可以用於對各種風險因子變化引起的價格變化進行定量分析，從而為衍生品的風險管理貢獻有價值的策略。

14237616.label: Realisation of objectives
14237616.value: 1. The principal investigator, together with his co-authors, developed an innovative delta expansion approach to deriving analytical approximation to the transition densities of multivariate diffusion processes. Our new approach represents the transition density as a conditional expectation of the Dirac delta function on the diffusion process and expands it into a sum of Hermite polynomial based terms by applying the celebrated Ito-Taylor expansion on it. The new method is universally applicable for a wide spectrum of processes with known or unknown characteristic functions. The PI apply it to both the maximum likelihood estimation for diffusion processes with discretely observed data and derivative pricing problems. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the method. Objectives 1 and 3 in the original application are thus successfully achieved. 2. The new approach is also useful in developing unbiased sensitivity estimators for derivative risk management. By performing the likelihood ratio method on the estimator stemmed from the above approach, the principal managed to construct accurate unbiased estimators for the purpose of estimating derivative sensitivities, a crucial input for the risk management of this important financial product. Objective 2 in the original application is successfully completed.

14237616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14237616.value: There are three major research outcomes related to this project. The principal published one paper (cf. Part C) in Journal of Econometrics, one leading journal in the area of theoretical and econometrics, based on the findings summarized in the research objectives. In that paper, we develop a new delta expansion approach to deriving analytical approximation to the transition densities of multivariate diffusions using the Ito-Taylor expansion of the conditional expectation of the Dirac delta function. Our approach yields an explicit recursive formulas for the expansion coefficients and is universally applicable for a wide spectrum of models, particularly the time-inhomogeneous non-affine irreducible multivariate diffusions. The main target of the project research, the processes the characteristic functions of whose transitional distributions are explicitly known, constitutes one of the most important model classes in which the new approach is applicable. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of our approach in statistical estimation on discretely observed financial data and in evaluating financial derivatives and their sensitivities. As by-products of the project, the other two research outcomes have been submitted to and under review of the journal of Operations Research, the flagship publication outlet of the area of financial engineering. The first one is about a duality-driven iterative algorithm to obtaining and improving confidence interval estimates for the true value of finite-horizon stochastic dynamic programming problems. The experiments show that we can effectively obtain policies with a superb performance guarantee for large-scaled control problem. The journal reviewer reports are generally positive (One minor revision, one major revision). The Editor indicated the possibility of acceptance conditional on satisfactorily addressing the issues raised by the reviewers. The second one is about risk quantification in a financial network. In it, the PI together with his co-authors proposed a simulation based robust optimization approach to obtain the worst-case default probabilities and associated capital requirements for a specific group of systematically important banks under the network information uncertainty. The paper is under the second round of review now. One student, Yiwei Wang, completed her PhD degree training partially supported by this project. Her thesis was about simulation based on characteristic functions.

14237616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14237616.value: The principal will continue the investigation stemmed out from this research project to investigate effective estimation and simulation of stochastic processes and the related topics. A particular near-term objective is to get the two papers mentioned in Sec 6.1 published. In addition, the PI will extend the Ito-Taylor expansion approach to study various statistical inference problems in the presence of both stock and option trading data.

14237616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14237616.value: This funded research develops a new statistical approach to extract information from financial asset price time series. The methodology derived from the investigation leads to accurate approximate estimators on the transitional probability of the price processes. From it, people can construct practical tools for building up both proper statistical models to describe the dynamics of financial asset prices and accurate simulation-based evaluation of derivative prices and their sensitivities. Results from this study contributes fundamentally to risk management of financial derivatives.

14238416.label: Realisation of objectives
14238416.value: We have fully accomplished the objectives of the proposal. - We have synthesized single crystalline CuPc nanoribbons by physical vapor deposition method in a horizontal three-zone tube furnace. The starting materials, copper(II) phthalocyanine (CuPc, >99.95%) powders, are purchased from Sigma-Aldrich and used as received. CuPc powders are placed at the high-temperature zone of the tube furnace and vaporized at 450°C for 1 hour. The vapor is carried by high-purity argon flowing from the high-temperature zone to the low-temperature zone at a rate of 200 sccm. Single crystalline CuPc nanoribbons were obtained on silicon substrates at the low-temperature zone (200-300°C). In this project, we have tried to tune the carrier concentration of individual nanoribbons through organic solvent, ion irradiation, and copper intercalation. - We have systematically characterized thermal and electrical transport properties of individual nanoribbons via a suspended thermal bridge method. A novel batch-fabricated micro-device was developed to characterize the carrier concentration of individual nanoribbons in a physical properties measurement system. We also experimentally investigated thermal transport through nanoscale van der Waals interface between two individual CuPc nanoribbons. An interface heat transfer model was developed to extract the interfacial thermal conductance. The ultralow thermal conductance between CuPc nanoribbons was explained by molecular dynamics simulations and contact mechanics analysis. - We further fabricated amorphous thermoelectric thin films with ultralow thermal conductivity and high thermoelectric figure of merit. Elemental powders of Fe (99.8%, 50-100 mesh, Alfa Aesar, UK), V (99.9%, 100-200 mesh, Aladdin, USA), and Sb (99.5 %, 100 mesh, Alfa Aesar, UK) with a ratio of 1:1:1 were weighed and mechanically mixed. The powder mixture was sintered in vacuum in a hot-pressing system under 20 MPa at 500°C for 2 hours. The sintered sample with a diameter of 6 cm and a thickness of 3 mm was used as the FeVSb target for magnetron sputtering. Non-doped <100> silicon wafers with a resistivity of more than 1 MΩ·cm were used as the substrates. The wafers were oxidized to obtain a 300 nm thick SiO2 layer. (FeVSb)1-xTix films were deposited on the substrate at room temperature by magnetron co-sputtering. FeVSb and Ti (6 cm in diameter, 99.99 at. %) targets were used and the power sources were direct current and radio frequency powers, respectively. The sputtering power on the FeVSb target was 120 W. The power on the Ti target was 0, 35, 54, 65, 80 or 92 W in order to obtain different Ti concentrations in as-deposited films. The base pressure in the sputtering chamber was below 3E-4 Pa, the deposition pressure was 2.0 Pa, and the argon gas flow rate was 20 sccm. - We have systematically investigated the microstructure, thermal stability, and thermoelectric properties of the developed amorphous thin films. The film thickness was measured with both a profilometer (Dektak XT, Bruker, Germany) and atomic force microscope (AFM, AR Cypher, Oxford, UK). The surface topography and roughness of thin films were studied by AFM. The microstructure of thin films at room temperature was characterized by X-ray diffractometry (XRD, D/max-2500, Rigaku, Japan) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM, JEOL 2100, JEM, Japan). Thermal stability of the films was analyzed by in situ high temperature XRD (D8 Advance, Bruker, Germany) and high resolution TEM (HRTEM). The film composition was determined by scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive spectrometry (SEM-EDS, LYRA3, Tescan, Czech). Electrical conductivity was measured using the van der Pauw method on a four-probe station with a temperature-controlled platform. Seebeck coefficient was measured via a customized setup. Carrier concentration and mobility were measured with a Hall measurement setup (mCFMS, Cryogenic Limited, UK). Thermal conductivity of the deposited thin films was measured by a suspended thermal bridge method. The thin film along with the substrate was soaked in 1 mol/L KOH solution at 80°C for 30 mins, peeled off from the substrate, and then transferred onto the testing microdevice for in-plane thermal conductivity measurement. Each sample was measured at three different suspended lengths in order to extract the intrinsic thermal conductivity. A planar thermoelectric generator with 4 thermocouples based on amorphous thin films is fabricated.

14238416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14238416.value: - We have advanced electrical and thermal measurement techniques for characterizing transport properties of individual nanoribbons and thin films. We developed an experimental system that is capable of measuring the Seebeck coefficient and the electrical resistivity of both bulk thermoelectric materials and thin films in a wide temperature range from 80 to 500 K, which can be further extended to even higher temperatures. On the other hand, we extended the micro-thermal-bridge method to high temperatures and demonstrated thermal conductivity measurement of boron nanoribbons up to 740 K. (A book chapter and two journal publications on Review of Scientific Instruments and Measurement Science and Technology) - We have experimentally investigated thermal transport through nanoscale van der Waals interface between two individual CuPc nanoribbons. An interface heat transfer model was developed to extract the interfacial thermal conductance. The interfacial thermal conductance is found to be on the order of 105 W/m^2/K at 300 K, which is over two orders of magnitude lower than the value predicted by molecular dynamics simulations for a perfectly smooth interface between two parallelly aligned CuPc nanoribbons. Further molecular dynamics simulations and contact mechanics analysis reveal that surface roughness can significantly reduce the adhesion energy and the effective contact area between CuPc nanoribbons, and thus result in an ultralow interfacial thermal conductance. In addition, the adhesion energy at the interface also depends on the stacking configuration of two CuPc nanoribbons, which also contributes to the observed ultralow thermal conductance. (Publication on Materials Today Physics) - We have developed amorphous thermoelectric thin films with ultralow thermal conductivity and high thermoelectric figure of merit. Amorphous FeVSb-based thin films doped with Ti are deposited by magnetron sputtering. The microstructure, thermal stability, and thermoelectric properties of the films are systematically investigated. The amorphous thin film with 6% Ti doping achieved an ultralow thermal conductivity of 0.93 W/m-K and a thermoelectric figure of merit of 0.23 at 300 K. A planar thermoelectric generator with 4 thermocouples based on the developed amorphous thin films is fabricated, which gives a maximum output power of 248 nW and an open-circuit voltage of 15.4 mV at a temperature difference of 59.4 K. (Publication on Journal of Materials Chemistry A)

14238416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14238416.value: The success of the project shows that low-dimensional materials such as nanoribbons and thin films with ultralow thermal conductivity are promising for thermoelectric applications. However, it is challenging to characterize and tune the doping level of individual nanoribbons for optimizing thermoelectric figure of merit. In this project, we have fabricated a batch-fabricated microdevice to characterize the carrier concentration of individual nanoribbons. Based on this technique, we will further investigate how to optimize the power factor of individual nanoribbons through tuning the size and doping level. It might lead to new design rule on how to optimize the thermoelectric properties of low-dimensional nanostructures.

14238416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14238416.value: In this project, we have significantly advanced thermal and electrical measurement techniques of individual nanoribbons and thin films. Based on the developed techniques, we have systematically investigated thermal transport through the interface between two CuPc nanoribbons. Our results revealed an ultralow interfacial thermal conductance between organic nanoribbons, which can be ascribed to the reduced adhesion energy and effective contact area induced by surface roughness and stacking configuration. This project provides a new approach for studying thermal transport through nanoscale van der Waals interfaces, and discloses the critical role of nanoscale surface roughness in reducing the interfacial thermal conductance. On the other hand, we developed Ti-doped amorphous thin films with ultralow thermal conductivity and high thermoelectric figure of merit. A planar thermoelectric generator was fabricated based on the developed amorphous thermoelectric thin films, which demonstrated a great potential for low-grade heat harvesting. Low-grade heat is distributed ubiquitously in the ambient environment. Thin-film-based thermoelectric generators are promising power sources for wearable electronic devices by converting low-grade heat into electricity.

14238716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14238716.value: 我們提議研究以下兩個關於有噪音的隨機線性模運算方程組的任務之間的關系：找到該系統被植入的解(難度)和把該系統與真正隨機的系統區分開(偽隨機)。我們考慮兩個隨機方程的模型(稀疏和密集) 以及兩種噪音(隨機和確定性)。 對於稀疏的有噪音二進制線性方程組，我們主要的目標是提高由Applebaum (SIAM J. Comp., 2013)提出的難度到偽隨機的規約所需方程數目複雜度。我們展示只要能為異或編碼在壹個沒有被研究過的慘數範圍內設計壹個更高效列表解碼算法，我們就可以獲得改進。 對於密集線性方程組，我們致力於取整噪音 (也就是方程組右邊的低位有效被抹去)。我們討論由Yao, Goldreich 和 Levin, 以及 Akavia, Goldwasser 和 Safra提出的把難度轉為偽隨機性的經典方法的在這個問題上的可應用性。 最後，我們計劃研究稀疏度對偽隨機性的影響。我們斷言如果m個稀疏度為k的隨機方程式是偽隨機的，那麼m²個稀疏度為k²的隨機方程也是偽隨機的。我們對這個斷言提供了壹些證據同時也建議了兩行攻擊。

14238716.label: Realisation of objectives
14238716.value: The theme of this project was to investigate a conjectured connection between two problems: Search versus distributional hardness of sparse noisy linear equations and approximately decoding k-XOR codes. This was realized in the paper "XOR Codes and Sparse Random Linear Equations with Noise". The main novelty is the development of a new list-decoding algorithm for such codes in the high-error regime, which gives rise to a new search-to-decision reduction for linear equations. Thus the first objective of the project has been fully realized. An ongoing work by my student King On Yung has largely addressed the third objective. He analyzed a natural algorithm for solving random linear equations (with or without noise) and showed that the algorithm works precisely for those instances for which the clause-to-variable ratio is low enough not to induce a core. This is a concrete, rigorous argument of algorithmic hardness up to the statistical threshold at which such instances start exhibiting non-trivial structure. Owing to the short duration of the project, the manuscript is still under preparation and will be published in the future. Regarding the second objective, we managed to generalize previous analyses to more general settings (larger class of rings) but failed to obtain quantitative improvements. This problem has recently received a lot of attention in the cryptographic community as several practical protocols for post-quantum cryptography are based on it, yet as a testament to its difficulty there has been no improvement in the analysis after my work with Guo, Masny, Richelson, and Rosen from 2016. Another work that arose partially from this project is the paper "Optimal Deterministic Extractors for Generalized Santha-Vazirani Sources", where we used related probabilistic and analytic methods to analyze a common randomness extractor.

14238716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14238716.value: The major findings are: 1. XOR codes are efficiently approximately list-decodable in the high-error regime. We give a novel algorithm for this and prove lower bonds on the list size. (from "XOR Codes and Sparse Random Linear Equations with Noise") 2. It is possible to convert algorithms for distinguishing noisy linear equations from random ones into ones for solving such equations with a much smaller blowup in the number of equations than previously known (but larger running time). (from "XOR Codes and Sparse Random Linear Equations with Noise") 3. The "phase transition" for the occurrence of a core in sparse linear equations occurs exactly at the point where a simple randomized algorithm (clean up the system then make a random choice) starts failing, giving concrete evidence of the hardness of this problem. (manuscript in preparation)

14238716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14238716.value: Our work on decoding XOR codes leaves open an exponential gap between the upper and lower bound on list size. Despite considerable effort we have not been able to close this gap; we believe that doing so will require novel methods. Our hardness-to-randomness reduction is exponential time where the exponent improves with density. It is an open question whether this is achievable in polynomial time.

14238716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14238716.value: This results of these projects provide novel additional evidence of certain hardness assumptions in cryptography and computational complexity theory. One concrete benefit is that they increase our confidence in the security of a myriad cryptographic schemes based on the hardness of such problems, some of which are likely to become widely deployed in a post-quantum world, which a large part of the physics and computer science community believe will happen within the next 10-15 years.

14238816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14238816.value: Over the past decade, fiber transmission capacity has grown rapidly by utilizing optical coherent communication signals in higher-order modulation formats. The price to pay is a larger optical signal-to-noise ratio to maintain a certain bit-error rate. Consequently, higher launched power is required, and the resulting inter-channel interactions mean that transmission capacity approaches the nonlinear Shannon limit. To further increase the capacity, it is necessary to mitigate the nonlinear impairments in transmission. One approach is to rely on electronic signal processing through digital backpropagation. However, as this requires intensive and time consuming computational processes, it is often performed offline. Also, given the limited bandwidth of coherent receivers, only intra-channel nonlinearities can be compensated. The second approach uses optical phase conjugation (OPC), either at the transmitter end, mid-span, or receiver to generate phase-conjugated twin waves or to perform spectral inversion that results in a time reversal of signal propagation. Recently, the use of OPC has been investigated by many major groups because of the scope for real-time processing, the transparency to modulation formats and date rates, as well as the potential for wideband multi-wavelength processing and reduced power consumption. Field deployment of mid-span OPC has also been demonstrated recently. Unfortunately, OPC is a nonlinear process that gives rise to undesirable nonlinear noise and distortion, particularly for signals in multi-carrier modulation format and/or multi-wavelength communications, where the inter-carrier or inter-channel nonlinear crosstalk becomes significant. This crosstalk limits the OPC performance. To minimize nonlinear noises, one can lower the input signal power. However, this implies a weaker conjugated output, unless a stronger parametric pump is used in the OPC. The parametric pump power is in turn limited by the occurrence of stimulated Brillouin scattering in the nonlinear fiber. Even though many sophisticated techniques have been employed to increase the Brillouin threshold, the OPC performance is still fundamentally limited by the exponentially decaying pump power along the fiber that results from photon annihilation and propagation loss. In this proposal, we address the elementary issue of rectifying the power profiles of the parametric pump(s), the input signal, and the conjugated idler along the fiber to minimize the undesirable nonlinear noises. Our scheme relies on distributed backward Raman amplification in the OPC together with appropriate parametric pump and Raman pump powers and wavelengths. Theoretical analysis, numerical simulations, and experimental investigation will be carried out to reveal both the potential and possible limitations of the proposed approach. 在過去的十年內，由於高階調製格式在相干通信中的廣泛應用，光纖通信的容量迅速增長。 然而為了維持某一特定誤碼率，這些高階調製格式往往需要更高的光信噪比。這也意味著光纖輸入端需要注入更高光強的信號。這些具有高光強度的信號在光纖中發生互相作用，使得傳輸的容量接近非線性香農極限。為了進一步增加信道容量，降低傳輸中的非線性損耗是非常重要的。其中一種方式是利用數字信號處理中的反向傳播算法。但是這種算法需要的計算過程強度高且耗費時間，所以只能對信號進行離線處理。同時，因為相干接收機的帶寬有限，這種方法只能補償單波長信號內的非線性噪聲。另外一種方法是全光相位共軛。這個系統模塊可以放置在傳輸鏈路的發射端，鏈路中段和接收端，使得信號在時域上進行反向的傳播。由於它可以實現信號實時處理，能處理各種信號調製格式和速率，以及高帶寬的多波長信號，這種方法在最近幾年受到世界上很多主要研究小組的廣泛關注。其中中間鏈接的光相位共軛已經在現場試驗中得到驗證。 然而，光相位共軛是一個非線性過程，因此過程中會造成非線性噪聲和信號失真。由于子載波或者波長間的非線性串擾，這種損耗對於多載波信號或者多波長信號尤為嚴重。這種串擾會限制光相位共軛系統的信號質量。減少輸入光信號的功率可以減少非線性噪聲。然而，除非提高參量泵浦的光強，這種方式會降低共軛信號的光強。而參量泵浦的光強往往會受到非線性光纖中受激布里淵散射的限制。雖然採用了很多複雜的方式去提高光纖的布里淵散射的閾值，光相位共軛的性能最終還是會受到光纖中不斷被損耗的泵浦光的影響。在我們提案中，我們主要通過改變參量泵浦，輸入信號和共軛閑頻光在光纖中的光強變化，從而減少不必要的非線性噪聲。這種方法主要利用了分佈式背向傳播的拉曼放大在光相位共軛中的相互作用，通過選擇恰當的參量和拉曼泵浦光的光強和波長，達到減少非線性噪聲的目的。我們將對這種方法進行理論分析，數值仿真和實驗驗證，研究這種方法的前景和可能的局限性。

14238816.label: Realisation of objectives
14238816.value: 1. To demonstrate experimentally the suppression of nonlinear noise and distortion in optical phase conjugation of multi-wavelength coherent communication signals under the influence of backward Raman amplification. We have designed experiments and conducted measurements to investigate how Raman amplification can be advantageously used to suppress the undesirable nonlinear noise and distortion. We demonstrate that Raman-assisted scheme significantly improves the performance of four-wave mixing based optical processing including optical phase conjugation [J5, J8], optical parametric amplification [C1], phase-sensitive amplification [J3, C4], multi-channel parametric sampling [J4, C2], and serial-to-parallel conversion via time lens processing [J1]. In particular, the multi-wavelength processing capability has been successfully demonstrated in the applications of optical phase conjugation [J5], optical sampling and time-lens processing. Polarization-insensitive Raman-assisted four-wave mixing has also been demonstrated [C3]. The application of four-wave mixing for polarization-division-multiplexed signals in coherent communication systems has also been investigated. [J2]. New methods for generating multi-wavelength optical signals using a coherent optical frequency comb has been demonstrated [J6], and carrier recovery of the WDM system at the optical receiver has been successfully realized [J7, C5]. 2. To investigate the influence of the residual distortion products in the Raman-enhanced OPC on the transmission performance A recirculating fiber loop has been set up to investigate the transmission performance of optically processed coherent communication signals. We have demonstrated effective four-wave mixing processing of polarization-division-multiplexed QPSK communication signals using a dual-orthogonal-pump configuration. The transmission performance of the processed outputs, which are phase-conjugated and wavelength converted, have been analyzed using a recirculating fiber loop consisting mainly of 80 km single-mode fiber, a fiber amplifier, and two acousto-optical modulators [J2]. Q-factors of the processed signal in both polarizations have been successfully measured as a function of the transmission distance up to 480 km. Next, the transmission performancea of signals in different modulation formats are measured and analyzed [J5, J7, C6]. With a Raman-enhanced OPC [J5], we observe that the optimum launched power is increased by 2 dB and the maximum Q factor is increased by 0.4 dB compared to direct transmission for a WDM OFDM system. Similar performances are observed across all the wavelengths, proving that our scheme of suppressing the nonlinear distortion works well with WDM transmission systems. 3. To analyze the Raman-enhanced OPC and to simulate the power profiles of the interacting light waves along the fiber and the improvement in Q-factor. We have analyzed the distributed Raman gain along the nonlinear fiber [J1]. The spectral dependence of the Raman gain has been evaluated. At a higher Raman pump power, not only the signal gain is higher, but also the spectral dependence of gain is stronger. The spectral asymmetry in saturated Raman-assisted parametric amplification has been investigated experimentally and numerically using a five-wave model [C1]. Our analysis is found to be more efficient than the split-step Fourier method (SSFM) in solving the nonlinear Schrodinger equation. Also, evolution of the pump and idler fields in four-wave mixing based optical phase conjugation has been investigated [J2]. The role of phase mismatch in influencing the efficiency of generating the conjugated idler has been theoretically analyzed. The Raman-enhanced OPC effectively mitigates the nonlinear impairment introduced by inter-subcarrier mixing via the OPC pump in the back-to-back module. As a result, the input signal power increases by 3 dB and the maximum Q factor increases by 2.4 dB compared to the conventional OPC system [J5]. The reduced nonlinear impairment by Raman amplification gives rise to a 2-dB enhancement in the launched power of the transmission system and a 0.4-dB Q factor improvement. In comparison, the nonlinear noise in the conventional OPC introduces 1.1 dB Q factor penalty.

14238816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14238816.value: Following the proposed plan, we have successfully developed effective optical phase conjugators to compensate for dispersion and nonlinearity impairments in different optical fiber links. In particular, we have demonstrated Raman-enhanced OPC for coherent orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals in a WDM transmission system [J5]. We have also realized mitigation of transmission impairments for single sideband signals in a Kramers–Kronig direct detection link [J8, C6]. In the coherent OFDM system, we investigate the performances of Raman-enhanced OPC in both back-to-back (BTB) and transmission systems with 3 × 25 Gbaud optical OFDM signals. In the BTB OPC system, Raman amplification boosts the tolerance to system nonlinearity, achieving a 3-dB improvement in the output power, a 2.4-dB improvement in the Q factor, and a 6-dB improvement in the input dynamic range. In the transmission system with Raman-enhanced OPC, the optimum launched power is increased by 2 dB and the maximum Q factor is increased by 0.4 dB compared to direct transmission. Similar performances are observed in all the wavelengths, indicating that our scheme works well with WDM transmission systems. In the Kramers-Kronig direct detection link, The single-sideband signal is modulated at 80-Gb/s 16-QAM with OFDM. In the 180-km transmission experiment, the OPC surpasses digital chromatic dispersion compensation in Q factor, optimum launched optical power (LOP) and optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) sensitivity. The improvement in Q factor, optimum LOP and OSNR sensitivity are 0.9 dB, 1.0 dB, and 1.7 dB respectively. The superiority of OPC over pure optical dispersion compensation is also analyzed by simulation. The results indicate that the OPC is an effective means to enhance the transmission performance of single-sideband signals. We have extended our investigation to related work including the generation of optical frequency comb for coherent WDM communications [J6], and carrier regeneration in a comb-based WDM system [J7, C5]. We also demonstrated other applications of Raman-enhanced four-wave mixing processing schemes such as serial-to-parallel data conversion [J1], phase-sensitive amplification [J3], and optical parametric sampling [J4, C2].

14238816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14238816.value: Our research results clearly demonstrated the effectiveness of applying Raman amplification in a fiber-based OPC to compensate for fiber transmission impairments in a WDM system. While fiber-based OPC provides the large optical bandwidth for dispersion and nonlinearity compensation, there are other platforms in realizing more compact OPCs, such as semiconductor optical amplifiers and silicon waveguides. However, the waveguide dimensions have to be properly tailored to control the waveguide and hence the total dispersion profile. Performance degradation caused by other undesirable mechanisms such as two-photon absorption, free-carrier absorption, cross-gain and cross-phase modulations need to be minimized. Another area worth investigating is the generation of optical frequency comb for multiwavelength communications. Instead of relying on a number of independent lasers with associated electronic control circuits, a frequency comb can be used to provide a bank of coherent optical carriers. It can serve as a versatile tool for research in WDM communication systems. A GRF proposal on the generation, characterization, and application of optical frequency combs has been submitted to RGC and was successfully funded.

14238816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14238816.value: The increasing traffic over the Internet prompts for the transmission of higher-bandwidth signals over a longer distance. This will give rise to increasing linear and nonlinear noises during the fiber transmission. A promising solution to solve the problem is to apply optical phase conjugation in the transmission link owing to its benefits in real-time and wide bandwidth operation. The principle is based on time reversal, which is a technique to invert the distortion of signals on the second half of the link. In this project, we have successfully investigated the system performances of transmission links with fiber-based conjugators for signals in different modulation formats, data rates, and communication systems. We further demonstrated the use of backward Raman amplification in the optical phase conjugator to reduce undesirable distortions and noises. Consequently, we have obtained improved system performance that can be translated into the support of higher bandwidth signals over a longer transmission distance.

14239416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14239416.value: 通過傅里葉分析研究量子和經典複雜性度量

14239416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14239416.value: 傅立葉分析是通過傅立葉基分解來研究函數的一種有效方法。在過去的三十年中，它已被證明是一個非常有用的工具來設計算法和分析的布爾函數這一理論計算機科學的基本構件的複雜性。傅里葉係數反映了函數的很多組合和功能的代數性質，也和很多重要的組合與代數性質密切相關，如靈敏度，決策樹複雜性，以及通信複雜性。在這個提案中，我們計劃通過傅立葉分析來研究這些以下兩個類別的函數複雜性度量。 第一類是那些有著小的傅立葉p範數的函數，這些函數早已因其與計算學習算法的緊密關係引起人們的注意。我們對這一類函數最近發現的一些​​有效的通信協議帶來對它們的結構的進一步研究的興趣。具體來說，如果我們能提高函數方嚮導數的傅立葉範數，那麼我們就能夠設計出更加有效的傳統和量子通信協議。我們在這個體案中的前兩個問題就是關於這些函數的。我們計劃使用量子草圖和奇偶決策樹作為研究的主要工具。另一個感興趣的問題是提高一個格林和桑德斯有關布爾函數的小傅立葉1-範數的經典定理。他們的結果通過把這些函數用子空間之和來表示，但是子空間的個數是雙指數的，雖然下界只有多項是。我們計劃通過提高我們最近奇偶決策樹算法效率，以及利用我們新推出的子空間查詢模型的方法，來減小這中間的間隙。 第二類是關於單調函數或接近於單調函數。所研究的度量是平均和最大靈敏度。這不僅在復雜性理論的基本概念，而且與學習算法，社會選擇理論等等密切相關。 1。對於單調函數，Servedio和Tan猜測平均靈敏度是漸近小於最大靈敏度。無論是一個肯定的答案或給出一個這兩種靈敏度的小的差別都會非常有趣。在前期工作中，我們已經發現比以前的記錄間隔小的函數，我們計劃繼續沿著這條思路去研究。 2。在復雜性理論中的一個長期懸而未決的問題是靈敏度是否到其他的複雜性度量多項式相關。我們計劃對接近於單調的函數研究這個頗有挑戰性的問題。這裡函數之間的距離是由一個交替數的概念來測量的，這類函數最近在復雜性，學習理論和密碼學中都備受關注。 傅里葉分析提供了一個不同的視角來研究函數，成為了複雜性理論的有力工具。該提案提出的都是一些根本問題，對這些問題的研究將大大加強我們的重要的函數類（如單調函數，傅立葉稀疏的函數，低靈敏度函數）的理解。在這些問題方面取得進展，有些能夠立即轉化為有效的算法和通信協​​議。該PI已在其中的一些問題有些部分進展，並希望通過進一步調查，取得更大的成就。

14239816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14239816.value: 基於深度神經網絡的人群場景動態建模

14239816.label: Project Objectives
14239816.value: Develop a multi-branch deep neural network for understanding crowd scene dynamics. Apply the learned crowd scene dynamics as priors to crowd-related applications, such as pedestrian tracking, walking path prediction, and abnormal event detection. Build a large-scale benchmark dataset for crowd analysis.
rows: Develop a multi-branch deep neural network for understanding crowd scene dynamics.
Apply the learned crowd scene dynamics as priors to crowd-related applications, such as pedestrian tracking, walking path prediction, and abnormal event detection.
Build a large-scale benchmark dataset for crowd analysis.

14239816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14239816.value: Hong Kong has the 4th highest population density in the world. Intelligent video surveillance technologies are valuable for increasing city management efficiency. The aim of this project is to develop deep neural networks for modeling crowd scene dynamics from surveillance videos. The proposed framework has many potential applications, such as pedestrian walking path prediction, crowd stationary time estimation, and travel time estimation. It would also provide important prior for other crowd-related applications such as pedestrian tracking, abnormal event detection, and traffic congestion localization. The key task of crowd scene understanding is to model how the global scene dynamics evolve, and how each individual react to the global scene dynamics and make their behaviour decisions. All existing methods were based on hand-crafted features and assumed that the dynamics of a scene are governed by models of pre-defined forms, e.g. Gaussian Mixture models. Such assumptions are likely to mismatch the underlying dynamics processes that are of more complex forms. Our proposed models jointly learn the spatio-temporal feature representations, the global scene dynamics, and the person-specific dynamics with a deep recurrent neural network. Because of the large representation capacity of deep neural networks, the complex scene dynamics can be learned as highly non-linear functions, which are optimized with training samples. To make full use of the available video data and avoid exhaustive manual labeling, our proposed deep neural network is trained in an unsupervised manner for learning global scene dynamics and in a semi-supervised manner for learning person-specific dynamics. The two parts share the same spatio-temporal feature representations by the bottom layers, and each part has its own branch on the topmost layers and different learning objectives. The proposed deep neural network is quite general and can be easily adapted to various applications by simply modifying the output layers and the learning objectives of the person-specific dynamics branch. The learned person-specific dynamics can also be directly used in other applications by serving as priors. To the best of our knowledge, this would be the first project that utilizes deep neural networks for comprehensively understanding crowd scene dynamics. We would also contribute a large-scale crowd scene dataset that is at least 5 times larger than any existing dataset. The output of this project would significantly benefit and advance the research of crowd scene modeling, and also the related applications. It would make fully automatic surveillance systems more practical. 香港有著全球第四高的人口密度。智能監控技術對於增強城市管理效率具有較高的價值，本項目的目標在於利用深度神經網絡對監控視頻中的人群動態進行建模，該深度學習框架有著很多富有潛力的應用，包括行人路徑預測、靜止人群時間規矩、行人行走時間估計等。它同時對於其他人群的相關應用，如行人跟蹤，異常行為檢測，和交通擁堵定位等，能夠提供重要的先驗知識。人群場景理解的關鍵任務在於如何對整體場景動態的變化進行建模，以及如何對單獨行人對整體場景動態作出反應并作出行為決定進行建模。已有的算法均使用人工設計的特征描述器，並且假設場景的動態是由一個已知形態的數學模型（如高斯混合模型）決定的。這種假設可能與真實場景中複雜的動態過程不相符合。我們提出的算法能夠使用深度循環神經網絡同時學習監控場景的時空間特征、整體場景動態、以及單獨個體行人動態。因為深度神經網絡一般具有較強的表達能力，神經網絡中的非線性函數能夠學習複雜的場景動態，並且使用訓練樣本進行優化。為了充分使用已有的視頻數據並且規避繁瑣的人工標註，我們提出的深度神經網絡使用非監督學習的方法學習整體場景動態，使用半監督學習的方法學習個體行人動態。這兩個部分共享由深度神經網絡底層網絡得到的相同時空間特征，但是每個部分又有其獨立的高層網絡層以及不同的訓練目標。我們提出的深度神經網絡具有較好的可適性，能夠通過簡單的改變深度神經網絡單獨行人動態的輸出層和訓練目標，從而處理不同的應用。我們學習得到的單獨行人動態也能夠作為先驗知識被用於其他應用。本項目是第一個使用深度神經網絡來完備的理解人群場景動態的項目。我們還會提出一個大規模的人群場景數據集，其是已有最大的數據集五倍以上。該項目的研究結果能夠推動及有益于擁擠場景建模和相關的應用，能夠使全自動監控系統具有更高的實用性。

14239816.label: Realisation of objectives
14239816.value: All the objectives of this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have developed deep neural networks for understanding and modeling crowd dynamics in surveillance videos. Modeling crowd movements and inter-person interactions is a fundamental problem in understanding crowd dynamics. We observed that, in previous crowd dynamic modeling and tracking methods, they mostly modeled individual persons’ movements separately. Inter-person relations on movements are manually designed and in a symmetric way, which we argue is not an optimal setting. Manually designed inter-person interaction models generally utilize Gaussian or other easy-to-define symmetric mathematical models, which might not well capture realistic person-to-person interactions. To tackle the issues, we propose a deep continuous conditional random field (DCCRF) model, which adopts deep neural networks to model individual and inter-person relations. The DCCRF consists of unary and pairwise terms. The unary term learns visual features for associating persons across time, while the pairwise term model inter-object relations in an asymmetric way, which encourages high-confidence tracklets to help correct errors of low-confidence person tracklets and not to be affected by low-confidence ones much. The DCCRF is trained in an end-to-end manner for better adapting the visual information as well as inter-person relations. The inter-person relation models are shown to be general and can be applied to other downstream applications. (2) Based on the learned crowd and person dynamics, we have developed novel algorithms for multi-person tracking and video object detection. The DCCRF model can directly be generalized to perform multi-person tracking. The asymmetric pairwise terms in DCCRF aim to tackle the mis-tracking problem caused by person-to-person occlusions, person mis-detections and global camera motion. For two neighboring tracked person trajectories, the interacting influences are different along each direction to let the high-confidence person trajectory assists the low-confidence one more. Our proposed DCCRF utilizes mean-field approximation for inference and is trained in an end-to-end manner to estimate the optimal displacement for each tracked person. Based on the learned dynamics model, we also proposed a deep learning framework T-CNN that incorporates temporal and contextual information from tubelets obtained in videos, which dramatically improves the performance of existing still-image detection frameworks when they are applied to videos. One major innovation is to improve the temporal consistency of detected objects via propagating detection results to neighbor frames with pre-trained dynamics models to reduce sudden changes of detection results. If an object exists in a certain frame, the adjacent frames are likely to contain the same object at desired locations with similar confidences. Such a strategy has been shown to significantly boost video object detection performance. (3) We built a large-scale benchmark dataset for crowd person modeling. Modeling dynamics usually requires associating the persons across frames accurately with discriminative person visual features. Although there are large-scale person re-identification datasets on learning person appearances, such as Market-1501, DukeMTMC, MSMT’17, etc. We argue that they only provide relatively weak annotations of person IDs for person visual feature learning. To create a large-scale dataset with strong visual annotations, we collect a large-scale person description dataset with detailed natural language annotations and person samples from various sources, termed as CUHK Person Description Dataset (CUHK-PEDES). We collected 40,206 images of 13,003 persons from existing person re-identification datasets. Each person image is described with two sentences by two independent workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). On the visual side, the person images pooled from various re-identification datasets are under different scenes, viewpoints and camera specifications, which increases the image content diversity. On the language side, the dataset has 80,412 sentence descriptions, containing abundant vocabularies, phrases, and sentence patterns and structures. The annotations have much freedom to use any word to describe the persons. We conducted a series of user studies to show the richness the annotated language descriptions. The proposed dataset has been shown to effectively boost the performance of learning visual features of persons.

14239816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14239816.value: As research outcomes, 2 journal papers on IEEE TCSVT and 13 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology is one of the top journals in video understanding and modeling. CVPR/ECCV/ICCV/NeurlPS are the top conferences on computer vision and machine learning. In this project, we propose DCCRF (Part C.8, No. 1) to model inter-person interactions and dynamics using deep neural networks, which can better capture the complex behaviors of pedestrians in crowded spaces with an end-to-end deep neural network. The resulting network does not only model the crowd dynamics but can be directly applied to boost the performance of multi-person tracking. The dynamic model can also assist the task of single object tracking and further improves multiple object tracking (Part C.9 No. 7). In addition, we show that the learned dynamic model can be used to improve the performance video object detection (Part C.8 No. 2). The dynamics model can guide the propagation of detection boxes to temporally neighboring frames so that temporal consistency of the detection results and the detection performance are improved. In (Part C.9 No. 2), we further propose a novel tubelet proposal network (TPN) to incorporate long-term temporal information for improving video object detection. The TPN can efficiently generate accurate spatiotemporal tubelet proposals with the learned dynamics models. To associate persons of different appearances across time to create training trajectories for crowd dynamics modeling, we have proposed a series of methods on learning persons’ visual features. In (Part C.9 No. 9), we propose to establish spatial correspondences between pairs of person images on-the-fly for learning better visual features. In (Part C.9 No. 11 & No. 14), we propose to exploit the inter-person similarities using Random Walk or Conditional Random Field models to refine pairwise similarities. (Part C.9 No. 12) further extends the pairwise relation modeling from hand-crafted random walk or CRF models to Graph Neural Networks. We also explore encoding persons' visual appearances in surveillance videos (Part C.9 No. 10). In (Part C.9 No. 10), the long person sequences are divided into multiple short video snippets and the top-ranked snippet similarities are aggregated for sequence-similarity estimation. We also propose novel algorithms (Part C.9 No. 1, No. 5, & No. 13) that use natural language descriptions to learn more discriminative visual features for person images.

14239816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14239816.value: In this project, we found that deep neural networks can learn crowd and video dynamics better than manually-designed mathematical models. We will further pursue the direction on learning stronger dynamics models with deep neural networks and applying the learned dynamics models to solve other downstream research problems. We also found natural language can act as strong supervisions for learning visual understanding and modeling, we will continue to work on this direction.

14239816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14239816.value: The aim of this project is to develop deep neural networks for modeling crowd scene dynamics from surveillance videos. The proposed framework has many potential applications, such as pedestrian tracking and detection, cross-camera person re-identification and travel time estimation. We have developed deep neural networks that can better model inter-person relations of behaviors and general scene dynamics. The learned dynamics models can be well generalized to multi-person tracking and video object detection. We also build a large-scale dataset on describing person appearances for learning better visual features to establish more accurate temporal correspondences so that they can be used to model more accurate scene dynamics.

14241716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14241716.value: Deep convolutional networks (DCNs) have been extensively applied on computer vision and image processing problems giving state-of-the-art results on recognition, detection, segmentation and retrieval. To achieve satisfactory performance with DCNs, in general, one requires to gather and annotate massive quantity of input-output pairs. For example, training the Facebook's DeepFace network for face verification requires millions of faces with labelled identity. Not many research groups can afford the annotation cost. Importantly, the training data requirement is often infeasible for many vision problems, such as facial expression recognition, of which annotation is difficult to obtain due to scarcity of data and ambiguity in labelling. The objective of this project is to explore novel techniques to overcome the data obstacle through exploiting the abundant unlabelled data. This is a non-trivial problem since it is well-known that DCNs are labelled data hungry, while unlabelled data lacks of the required supervisory signals for guiding the parameters learning. Nevertheless, unlabelled data is available in large quantity without cost. If we could unleash the power of unlabelled data, many existing computer vision problems can be better solved using DCNs. Another reason that motivates us is that human, by nature, is capable of learning a new visual concept or category without the need of extensive supervision. The abilities to generalise, identify linkages and patterns, spot correlations and connections between data without being told what to look for, are highly sought after by deep learning research community. In this project, we move beyond conventional paradigms and explore a new framework for learning DCNs in an unsupervised manner. The method takes imagery data as input and returns as output a compact list of attributes in the form of binary codes. It also provides discriminative deep feature representations, which can be used in place of hand-crafted features for many tasks. We investigate how to use the attributes and deep representation learned in this way for object proposal generation, image classification and retrieval. We further explore extensions to generalise the framework to perform semi-supervised learning when partially labelled data is available, and unsupervised learning of spatio-temporal attributes. 深層卷積網絡（DCN）已經被廣泛應用於計算機視覺和圖像處理，在物體識別、檢測、分割、和檢索的問題上都取得豐碩的成果。 DCN的性能一般取決於大量的標註數據。例如，訓練Facebook的DeepFace人臉比對網絡便需要數百萬標有身份的人臉圖片。高昂的數據標註成本往往讓很多研究小組卻步。更重要的是，在許多計算機視覺問題裡，獲取足夠的訓練數據是很難實現的。比如臉部表情識別，由於數據匱乏和標籤語義含糊，導致很難獲得精確的面部表情標註。這個項目的目標是探索新技術以利用豐富的未標記數據克服數據標註的障礙。眾所周知，DCN需要大量的標註數據訓練，但未標註的數據卻缺乏用於引導參數學習所需的監控信號。然而，未標註的數據可以大​​量無成本獲取。如果我們能發掘未標註的數據的能力，許多現有的計算機視覺問題便可以更好地使用DCN解決。另一個促使我們考慮未標註數據的原因是，人類在本質上能夠在不需要廣泛監督下學習新的視覺概念或範疇。深度學習的科學家正再努力探索讓計算機擁有概括的能力，並自動找出數據之間的聯繫和模式。在這個項目中，我們將探索新的框架以無監督的方式學習DCN。該方法以圖像數據作為輸入並返回以二進編碼的屬性標籤作為輸出。同時，它也提供了高質量的深度學習特徵，來取代現有常用的手工特徵。我們將研究如何在各方面如物體檢測、圖像分類、和檢索等應用使用這種特徵。我們也會進一步探討半監督學習框架和時空屬性的無監督學習。

14241716.label: Realisation of objectives
14241716.value: In the mid-term report, we explain several works that realized the objectives. These works include a ‘mix-and-match’ (M&M) tuning approach for self-supervision approaches, a face clustering approach based on inverse reinforcement learning, and a deep network that is capable of generating discriminative questions to help disambiguate visual instances. In the following we present new additional works that realized the objectives of this project. Objectives 1, 2, and 3 ==================== We met the three objective through a novel framework. We conducted our research on face recognition, which is a kind of image classification problem. Face recognition has witnessed great progress in recent years, mainly attributed to the high-capacity model designed and the abundant labeled data collected. However, it becomes more and more prohibitive to scale up the current million-level identity annotations. In this work, we show that unlabeled face data can be as effective as the labeled ones. Here, we consider a setting closely mimicking the real-world scenario, where the unlabeled data are collected from unconstrained environments and their identities are exclusive from the labeled ones. Our main insight is that although the class information is not available, we can still faithfully approximate these semantic relationships by constructing a relational graph in a bottom-up manner. We propose Consensus-Driven Propagation (CDP) to tackle this challenging problem with two modules, the “committee” and the “mediator”, which select positive face pairs robustly by carefully aggregating multi-view information. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of both modules to discard outliers and mine hard positives. With CDP, we achieve a compelling accuracy of 78.18% on MegaFace identification challenge by using only 9% of the labels, comparing to 61.78% when no unlabeled data are used and 78.52% when all labels are employed. Objectives 2, 4 ==================== Intelligent agent naturally learns from motion. Various self-supervised algorithms have leveraged motion cues to learn effective visual representations. The hurdle here is that motion is both ambiguous and complex, rendering previous works either suffer from degraded learning efficacy, or resort to strong assumptions on object motions. In this work, we design a new learning-from-motion paradigm to bridge these gaps. Instead of explicitly modeling the motion probabilities, we design the pretext task as a conditional motion propagation problem. Given an input image and several sparse flow guidance vectors on it, our framework seeks to recover the full-image motion. Compared to other alternatives, our framework has several appealing properties: (1) Using sparse flow guidance during training resolves the inherent motion ambiguity, and thus easing feature learning. (2) Solving the pretext task of conditional motion propagation encourages the emergence of kinematically-sound representations that possess greater expressive power. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework learns structural and coherent features; and achieves state-of-the-art self-supervision performance on several downstream tasks including semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and human parsing Objectives 2, 3 ==================== Face recognition sees remarkable progress in recent years, and its performance has reached a very high level. Taking it to a next level requires substantially larger data, which would involve prohibitive annotation cost. Hence, exploiting unlabeled data becomes an appealing alternative. How to effectively cluster, especially on a large-scale (i.e. million-level or above) dataset, remains an open question. A key challenge lies in the complex variations of cluster patterns, which make it difficult for conventional clustering methods to meet the needed accuracy. Our first work in this direction explores a novel approach, namely, learning to cluster instead of relying on hand-crafted criteria. Specifically, we propose a framework based on graph convolutional network, which combines a detection and a segmentation module to pinpoint face clusters. In our second work, we propose a fully learnable clustering framework without requiring a large number of overlapped subgraphs. Instead, we transform the clustering problem into two subproblems. Specifically, two graph convolutional networks, named GCN-V and GCN-E, are designed to estimate the confidence of vertices and the connectivity of edges, respectively. With the vertex confidence and edge connectivity, we can naturally organize more relevant vertices on the affinity graph and group them into clusters. Experiments show that our method yields very accurate face clusters, which, as a result, also lead to further performance gain in face recognition.

14241716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14241716.value: As research outcome, eight conference papers are published on the top conferences in computer vision and artificial intelligence (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and AAAI). In this project, we proposed novel techniques for self-supervised learning. This includes a ‘mix-and-match’ (M&M) tuning method that is readily applicable to many self-supervised learning methods (Part C.9 No. 1). It does not use more annotated samples than the original process. Yet, it is capable of boosting the performance of target image segmentation task to surpass fully-supervised pre-trained counterpart. We further proposed a new paradigm to better leverage motion in representation learning and achieve promising performance on various benchmarks (Part C.9 No. 4). Interestingly, our CMP model is capable of capturing kinematic properties of various objects without any manual annotations. We participated in 2019 Self-Supervised Learning Challenge organized by Facebook and we won the champions for all four tracks. We also developed new methods for semi-supervised clustering. In our first work, we formulate a novel face grouping framework based on imitation learning (IL) via inverse reinforcement learning (Part C.9 No. 3). This is the first attempt to address visual clustering via inverse reinforcement learning. Once learned, the policy can be well generalized to unseen photo albums with good performance. In our second work, we investigate the usage of massive unlabeled data (over 6M images) for large-scale face recognition. Our setting closely resembles real-world scenarios where the unlabeled data are collected from unconstrained environments and their identities are exclusive from the labeled ones. We propose consensus-driven propagation (CDP) to tackle this challenging problem (Part C.9 No. 7). We show that a wise usage of unlabeled data can complement scarce manual labels to achieve compelling results. In our third work, we proposed a framework for face clustering based on graph convolutional networks (Part C.9 No. 5). The proposed method significantly improves the clustering accuracy on large-scale face data, achieving a F-score at 85.66, which is superior to the best result obtained by unsupervised clustering methods (F-score 68.39). We make the first attempt to perform top-down face clustering in a supervised manner. It is the first work that formulates clustering as a detection and segmentation pipeline based on graph convolution networks. In the fourth work (Part C.9 No. 6), we further proposed a novel framework that formulates clustering as an estimation of confidence and connectivity, both based on learnable components. Our approach is an order of magnitude faster than existing learning-based methods. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both large-scale face clustering and fashion clustering.

14241716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14241716.value: We have seen the effectiveness of using unlabeled data for learning deep representation. We believe that more discriminative representation can be learned through better design of loss functions, e.g., contrastive learning, which carefully considers both inter- and intra-cluster relations in data. We also wish to explore knowledge distillation, i.e., transferring knowledge from a teacher model to a student model. It is another way of saving annotation costs by mining dark knowledge from the cumbersome teacher model. There is an inherent relation between knowledge distillation and self-supervised learning, which we shall explore in future work.
