14243616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14243616.value: This projects aims at realizing uniform high-aspect-ratio (HAR) metal-assisted chemical etching (MaCE) in nanoscale by fundamental understanding of the physicochemical processes that influence the uniformity of MaCE. 3D nanomanufacturing technology plays a pivotal role in fabricating the devices with revolutionized performance by utilizing the surface as well as the bulk volume inside Si substrate. Novel methods of producing structures with smaller lateral size in nanoscale, larger depth and high geometric uniformity, which are referred as HAR nanostructures, are the key to next-generation high-performance devices. Currently, HAR nanostructures on Si are primarily manufactured by the expensive and low throughput dry etching technologies in which Si substrates are etched by plasma, requiring multi-million-dollar instruments and high maintenance cost. On the other hand, HAR structures can be made by several wet etching methods with economic viability, such as the KOH etching and electrochemical etching. However, these available wet etching methods lack the capability in etching nanoscale features. Here, we propose the study of a novel low-cost, high-throughput wet etching method, named MaCE. By combining morphological and chemical analyses on a set of well-controlled etching systems, we will investigate both the microscopic processes and macroscopic processes during etching, with the microscopic processes (0.1-10 nm) covering the transport and chemical reactions in the catalyst-silicon interfacial region and the macroscopic processes (10 nm-500 μm) covering the transport of chemicals in the bulk etching solution and inside the HAR structures. Based on the analyses, a parametric study of HAR MaCE with varying the etching solution composition, etching time and etching temperature will be conducted. The etching results will be collected and the macroscopic processes will be inferred with assistance of mathematical modeling using diffusion-reaction equations. New etching protocols involving different substrates and metal catalysts will be proposed and experimented based on the fundamental study. Uniform MaCE of nanoscale structures with aspect ratio up to 800:1 will be achieved. The proposal research addresses several fundamental issues in nanoscale science, such as fluidic transport through nanoporous films and HAR structures and metal-semiconductor interface electrochemistry. The result of research will benefit a variety scientific fields such as microfluidics, catalysis, thin film technology and etc. The research will enable wet etching with revolutionized performance, thus may open a new era in high-volume nanomanufacturing. 本項目旨在通過對影響金屬輔助化學刻蝕（MaCE）均勻性的物理化學過程的基礎理論研究來實現均勻且具有高深寬比（HAR）的納米級刻蝕。 三維納米製造技術在製造具有革新性能的器件方面有舉足輕重的作用，它不僅能利用矽襯底的表面，還能深入到矽內部空間。尋求新方法來生產具有納米尺度上更小的橫向尺寸，更大的深度和較高的幾何均一度的結構，即所說的HAR納米結構，是製造下一代高性能設備的關鍵。目前，矽襯底上的HAR納米結構主要是依靠昂貴而低通量的​​干刻蝕技術，其中矽基是利用等離子體刻蝕，需要數百萬美元的昂貴儀器和高額的維護成本。另一方面，HAR結構可以通過經濟實用的濕刻法實現，例如氫氧化鉀刻蝕和電化學刻蝕。然而，這些可用的濕刻蝕方法仍缺乏刻蝕納米級特徵的能力。 這裡，我們提出一種新的低成本高通量的濕刻蝕法的研究，名為金屬輔助化學刻蝕。通過結合形貌和化學分析於一系列良好控制的刻蝕體系，我們將探究刻蝕中的微觀和宏觀過程，其中微觀過程（0.1到1納米）包括在催化劑和矽界面的傳輸和化學反應，而宏觀過程（10納米到500微米）覆蓋在本體刻蝕溶液和在HAR結構中的化學試劑的傳播。 基於分析，我們將通過改變刻蝕液組分，刻蝕時間和刻蝕溫度來對高深寬比的金屬輔助化學刻蝕進行參數研究。刻蝕的結果將被收集，宏觀的過程將通過數學建模用擴散反應方程來推論。通過基礎研究，新的刻蝕方案將被提出，包括使用不同的基底和金屬催化劑。同時縱橫比高達800:1的均勻金屬輔助化學刻蝕的納米結構將得以實現。本提案的研究解決了納米科學的幾個基本問題，例如納米多孔薄膜和HAR結構中的流體傳輸以及金屬半導體界面的電化學認識。該研究的結果將有助於各種科學領域，如微流體，催化，薄膜技術等，並將開創高通量納米製造的新時代。

14243616.label: Realisation of objectives
14243616.value: We have achieved most of the project objectives and developed multiple methods to achieve high-aspect-ratio nanostructures in both silicon and silicon carbide. Firstly, we have developed physical models to describe the charge transport and mass transport processes involved in metal-assisted chemical etching (MaCE). By combining band bending-induced charge generation at the metal catalyst-semiconductor interface with a diffusion-controlled model for mass transport at the etchant-semiconductor interface, we have established a theoretical base to understand how the etching environment and initial etching structure (e.g., etchant concentration and diffusion rate, junction built-in field and junction orientation, etc.) affect the microscopic removal processes of silicon atoms. Secondly, we have performed parametric etching experiments to validate the theoretical model and demonstrate macroscopically how different high aspect ratio nanostructures can be generated by varying the processing parameters, such as the etchant composition and concentration, external electric field applied to the semiconductor wafer, deposition direction of the metal catalyst, and so on. Through this project, we were able to generate a range of nanostructures, such as straight and zig-zag nanowires (NWs), nanopores, and micro-trenches with controllable slanting profiles, through MaCE. Notably, these structures all have practical applications in microelectronics and energy devices. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that the methodology can be extended from silicon to silicon carbide – a promising third-generation semiconductor material. In the following, we summarize the six fabrication protocols we have established through this project to achieve uniform etching of high aspect ratio (HAR) nanoscale structures: (1) A viscosity-tuned diffusion-reaction process to create silicon zigzag nanowires: A diffusion-controlled MaCE method has been developed to fabricate silicon zigzag NWs. By tailoring the composition of the etchant (i.e., a mixture of HF, H2O2, glycerol, and DI water), the etchant diffusivity, etching direction and etching time can be tuned, leading to controllable growth of various zigzag NWs. It has also been demonstrated that such zigzag NWs provide the silicon substrate with self-cleaning and antireflection properties. This method may provide a feasible and economical way to fabricate zigzag NWs and other related structures. (Done by the original project PI: Ching-Ping Wong). (2) Tilted-MACE (tMACE) for fabrication of micro-trenches with controllable slanting angles: Micrometer-scale 3D trench arrays have been achieved on a silicon substrate through tMACE. The tMACE system consists of a gold layer, a photoresist layer, and a silicon substrate. Firstly, an etchant containing HF, H2O2, and DI water is applied and the straight section of the trench was fabricated. Secondly, glycerol is added into the MACE etchant. Due to the higher viscosity of the glycerol, the diffusion properties of the reactants (HF and H2O2) are changed and unbalanced etching rates are established. Accordingly, the metal catalyst layer starts to tilt, and therefore the etching direction is altered. With the prolonged etching time, micro-trench arrays with controllable slanting angles (ranging from 0 to 63°) and lengths (ranging from 30 to 52 μm) are achieved. (Done by the original project PI: Ching-Ping Wong). (3) Non-close-packed polystyrene nanosphere-templated MaCE for HAR silicon NWs: We have developed a low frequency (40 kHz) plasma etching system to fabricate non-close-packed monolayer arrays of polystyrene (PS) nano-spheres with smooth surfaces. The size and spacing of the PS nano-spheres can be precisely controlled by either adjusting the etching time or power of the system. Through introducing oxygen as the assisting gas in the low frequency plasma etching system, we achieved a coalesced PS nano-sphere array and used it as a template for MaCE. This method can significantly improve the aspect ratio of the silicon nanowires to over 200 due to the improved flexure rigidity. (Done by the original project PI and new PI). (4) Anodic - MaCE hybrid fabrication method to create silicon carbide nanowires: a hybrid anodic and metal-assisted chemical etching (Anodic-MACE) method has been proposed to fabricate SiC NWs at room temperature and under atmospheric pressure. In this method the metal component acts as both a catalyst to produce hole carriers and a mini-electrode to introduce band bending at the SiC surface for hole accumulation. The combined Anodic - MACE method lowers the working potential (3.5 V for etching SiC and 7.5 V for creating SiC nanowires) of the fabrication process while enhancing the etching efficiency. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that by tuning the etching electrical bias and time, various nanostructures can be obtained and the diameters of the obtained pores and nanowires can range from tens to hundreds of nanometers. This facile method may provide a feasible and economical way to fabricate SiC nanostructures for a broad range of applications. (Done by the original project PI and new PI). (5) Backside ultraviolet illumination enhanced MaCE for HAR silicon microstructures: In order to address the limited diffusion of reactants and resultants in HAR structures, we developed a back-side ultraviolet (UV) illumination platform for MACE, where additional hole carriers are generated through photoexcitation. It was found that the photo-generated holes can diffuse through bulk silicon and accumulate at the etchant/silicon interface to participate the etching reaction. As such, the method significantly enhances the etching rate and enables creation of root-like silicon microstructures. (Done by the original project PI: Ching-Ping Wong). (6) Machine learning-guided MaCE for fabrication of sub-10 nm silicon nanopore array: Machine learning algorithms have been explored to facilitate the design of MaCE processes for fabrication of sub-10 nm nanopore arrays in silicon wafers. In particular, a model based on a support-vector machine algorithm has been established and experimentally verified to describe the relationship between the nanopore structures and the fabrication conditions, including the etching solution, etching time, dopant type, and concentration. Based on the model, we demonstrate prediction of processing parameter windows for generating nanopore arrays in silicon wafers with variable doping types and concentrations. The proposed machine-learning-assisted etching method will provide an economical way to reduce the optimization workload of MaCE as well as enhancing its reproducibility in creating high-resolution nanostructures. (Done by the original project PI and new PI). Finally, it is noted that in the original objectives we target to achieve > 800:1 aspect ratio. While our new MaCE method can in principle reach this target, we found that as the aspect ratio exceeds a few hundreds the flexure rigidity of the nanostructures (e.g. nanowires) deteriorate rapidly, leading to collapse of structures and impede further development of higher aspect ratios. It is worth noting that through this project we have already demonstrated record high aspect ratio for MaCE produced nanostructures and further study along this direction should include improved mechanical design of structures and chemistry development for improved etchant diffusion to deep complex nanostructures.

14243616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14243616.value: Firstly, a diffusion-controlled metal-assisted chemical etching method has been developed to fabricate silicon zigzag NWs. By tailoring the composition of the etchant to change its diffusivity, etching direction, and etching time, we demonstrate the fabrication of various zigzag NWs. On the fundamental side, our study highlights the importance of controlling the mass transport process in MaCE and reveals that the viscosity of etchant plays a critical role in defining the zigzag configuration through affecting the diffusion rate, etching direction, and etching time. The study has been published. (Publication #1) Secondly, we developed a tilted-MACE (tMACE) method to fabricate HAR microstructures with a slanting angle variation from 2 - 70. The study validated a fundamental hypothesis that under a uniform MaCE environment, the preferred etching direction is always along the normal of the thin film catalysts, regardless of the relative orientation of the catalyst to Si substrates or the crystalline orientation of the substrates. The method paves the way to HAR 3D microfabrication with arbitrary slanting profiles inside silicon. The study has been published. (Publication #2) Thirdly, we developed an oxygen-assisted low frequency plasma etching system to fabricate non-close-packed monolayer arrays of polystyrene (PS) nano-spheres with smooth surface and controllable geometry. Using the coalesced PS nano-sphere array as a template for MaCE, we demonstrate fabrication of silicon NWs with over 200 aspect ratio, representing the highest value achieved with wet etching method. The study has been published. (Publication #3) Fourthly, we developed an anodic-assisted MaCE method to fabricate SiC nanostructures at room temperature and under atmospheric pressure. SiC is one of the most important third-generation semiconductor materials; however, the chemical robustness of SiC makes it very difficult to process, and only very limited methods are available to fabricate nanostructures on SiC. By utilizing metal as both the anode and catalyst material, we achieved controllable fabrication of various nanostructures (e.g., nanopores and nanowires) with a diameter of tens to hundreds of nanometers. The study has been published. (Publication #4) Finally, we applied machine learning methods to improve the design of MaCE processes of HAR structures. A support-vector machine based model has been developed to predict processing parameter windows for generating silicon nanopore arrays through MaCE. The AI-assisted etching method will provide an economical way to reduce the optimization workload of MaCE as well as enhancing its reproducibility in creating high-resolution nanostructures. The study has been published. (Publication #5)

14243616.value: We note that the backside ultraviolet illumination-enhanced MaCE process may have a unique advantage in creating interlayer nanostructures in 3D IC chips. Recently we initiated an ITF-TCFS project based on this technology and target to develop fabrication systems and protocols for defining interconnect structures, such as straight and bended through-silicon via (TSV), in wafers with 3D IC configurations.

14243616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14243616.value: 3D nanomanufacturing technology plays the pivotal role in fabricating the devices with revolutionized performance by utilizing the surface as well as the bulk volume inside Si substrate. Novel methods of producing structures with smaller lateral size in nanoscale, larger depth and high geometric uniformity, which are referred as high-aspect-ratio (HAR) nanostructures, are the key to next-generation high-performance devices. Currently, HAR nanostructures on Si are primarily manufactured by the expensive and low throughput dry etching technologies in which Si substrates are etched by plasma, requiring multi-million-dollar instruments and high maintenance cost. In this project we developed several metal-assisted chemical etching (MaCE) methods to create HAR nanostructures in silicon and silicon carbide with low-cost and high-throughput. By combining morphological and chemical analyses on a set of well-controlled etching systems, we have developed physical models to describe the microscopic and macroscopic processes during MaCE. Based on the fundamental findings, we innovate the MaCE schemes by creating new etchant formula and new etching template, introducing electrical or optical modalities and applying AI to assist process design. Through these efforts, we successfully demonstrated fabrication of a variety of HAR nanostructures. The research output will empower wet etching with revolutionized performance.

14245316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14245316.value: Learning a knowledge representation from text is a fundamental problem in artificial intelligence. The problem is challenging as raw text is largely unstructured. We need to extract knowledge from the textual content into a representation that offers effectiveness and efficiency in processing and understanding. It is desirable for such a knowledge representation to be: (1) quantifiable to enable automatic computation for tasks such as search and comparison; (2) compact to enable efficient computation; (3) reflective of the semantics of the textual content; (4) structured to encode the different levels of semantic granularity; and (5) easily interpretable by humans. A knowledge representation with these properties will benefit a diversity of applications, e.g. Web search, document retrieval, information extraction, etc. Previous approaches such as vector-space models, latent semantic analysis, topic modeling and word embedding, etc., have not yet been able to learn a knowledge representation with all the above properties. We propose to develop a tensor-based framework to learn such a knowledge representation. A tensor is a multi-dimensional extension of a matrix and supports data representation and processing with multiple facets. We will learn the word and document representations simultaneously using a higher-order SVD (HOSVD) in the tensor-based framework, to capture both the structural and semantic information of textual documents. The learned representations are fully quantifiable and computable. We represent the document using the word co-occurrence matrix to incorporate the local context of words which enriches the semantics. We further propose using the polytopic tensor product model to enhance the interpretability of the document representations by transforming the topic modeling problem into a geometrical problem. We assume that all the documents from a corpus are points in a high-dimensional space, inside a convex polytope spanned by the vertices as the topics. A document can then be represented as convex combinations of topics where the coefficients are the topic proportions. Hence, learning the topic and document representations is equivalent to finding an adequate convex polytope under specific conditions. Mathematically, such a geometrical problem can be solved by the tensor product output of HOSVD using the convexity incorporation techniques in tensor product model transformation. Various convex polytopes can be generated based on different conditions. This method is more flexible and interpretable than the current approaches. The proposed approach is a first attempt to study the feasibility and advantages of tensor operations in learning a knowledge representation for words and documents.

14245316.label: Realisation of objectives
14245316.value: Objective 1: Develop a convex polytopic model to represent topics in a tensor-based framework We have developed a novel topic discovery approach that can embed textual information units (e.g. documents, sentences, etc.) in a low-dimensional affine subspace and generate a compact convex polytope to enclose all the embedded textual information units. We show that the vertices of the polytope can capture key content (or semantic patterns) that are representative and interpretable, more so than existing methods such as latent semantic analysis. This capability can be demonstrated even for short textual information units. The tensor-based framework is applied for high dimensionality. Our investigation on feasibility was first conducted on two small-scale corpora. The proposed model has several advantages. First, it offers transparency, as the process can be visualized and understood in terms of geometry. This enhances the interpretability of the model which is useful to justify the results. Second, it is robust as the approach can always generate a polytope that is unique (i.e. the NO-type polytope), which also avoids the selection of hyper-parameters. Third, the resulting topics are consistent with human expectation, not only in a corpus with clear information categorization among the textual information units, but also in a corpus where the textual information units contain multiple, overlapping information categories. This presents the advantage of enhanced interpretability. Objective 2: Investigate different convex polytopes types for improved interpretability As mentioned above, the distance of points in the subspace of textual information units (e.g. documents or sentences) measures the difference between the textual information units. Hence, we assume that the extremes of the point set have the least similarity and hence can represent the key semantic patterns for the corpus. Finding the extreme points is equivalent to finding the convex polytope with the minimum volume that encloses all the points, where the vertices are the extreme points. We define the vertices as the representative semantic patterns for the corpus. Note that all points can thus be represented by the convex combinations of the vertices, and the minimum volume enclosing convex polytope always exists and is unique under the permutation of vertex labels for a finite point set. We refer this type of polytope as the normal (NO)-type, where all the vertices are within the point set. The textual information units associated with the vertices are thus referred to as textual information units. Hence, the semantic patterns represented by the vertices are interpretable as the human can understand the text of the constituent textual information units directly. This is different from the existing semantics discovery approaches where the semantics are represented either by a vector or a distribution of words. There are several algorithms that can generate NO-type polytope, under the class of convex hull algorithms. For example, Quickhull is a popular divide-and-conquer-based convex hull algorithm. For the NO-type polytope, the number of vertices may be as large as the number of textual information units N. However, in some circumstances, we prefer to extract a fixed number of semantic patterns, denoted by K, which is less than N. The problem can thus be formulated as finding the K-vertex enclosing convex polytope with the minimum volume. This is equivalent to finding the minimum volume simplex (MVS) that contains the point set of the textual information units. We refer this as the MVStype polytope. Note that the vertices may no longer be in the point set. We define a special type of MVS-type polytope called close-to-normal (CNO)-type, where at least one of the vertices are in the point set. Those vertices can then be interpreted just like in the NO-type. Objective 3: Simultaneous word and document representation learning from word co-occurrence document tensors We experiment with a dialog corpus, where each textual information unit is a transcribed spoken utterance. The utterances in the dataset are projected to an affine space and enclosed by a polytope. The utterances with a mixture of multiple semantic patterns tend to be in the interior of the polytope. Second, the vertices (extreme points) of the polytope can capture distinct semantic patterns. Two geometric properties relate to interpretation of these patterns: (i) For each vertex, the top-k terms with k highest weights (i.e. coordinate values) are the most frequently observed terms in the corresponding pattern and hence can be used to interpret that semantic pattern. (ii) The k-nearest neighboring data points of each vertex are the utterances that carry the corresponding semantic pattern. Therefore, the semantic pattern of the vertex can be interpreted by observing the common patterns among these k-nearest utterances. Third, polytopes with a higher dimensionality can preserve more diversified distinct semantic patterns. The vertices containing mixed patterns in a lower dimensional space may be disentangled into different vertices in a higher dimensional space. Objective 4: Pilot experimentation based on word similarity and text classification tasks We verify the properties of the CPM for automatically extracting semantic patterns from the raw dialog corpus of the Air Travel Information System (ATIS-2 and ATIS-3) training sets with nearly 5,000 utterances. The corpora are from the air travel domain. After embedding the utterances of the corpus into the low-dimensional affine subspace via PCA, we generate the NO-type convex polytope and the MVS-type convex polytope. For the NO-type convex polytope, the utterances at the vertices of the polytope are all short and contain fewer semantic patterns. The complex utterances that are combinations of multiple patterns are mapped to the interior of the polytope. Utterances with similar semantic patterns (including multiple semantic patterns) tend to cluster together. For the MVS-type convex polytope, can also capture distinctive semantic patterns, the process of which are interpretable through analyzing the nearest utterances and top words. We also observe that the vertices with mixed patterns in the lower-dimension polytope may split into different vertices with dimensionality increased and in this way the semantic patterns are preserved, but there are also new semantic patterns that can emerge in higher dimensions. In general, the polytopes with a higher dimensionality preserve more distinct semantic patterns. Overall, we find that the CPM approach can identify semantic patterns in an unsupervised way from the utterances, and the patterns can be used to develop semantic frames and domain ontology for the purpose of natural language understanding in a dialog system.

14245316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14245316.value: We have developed a novel topic discovery approach that can embed textual information units (e.g. documents, sentences, etc.) in a low-dimensional affine subspace and generate a compact convex polytope to enclose all the embedded textual information units. The vertices of the polytope capture key content (or semantic patterns) that are representative and interpretable, more so than existing methods such as latent semantic analysis. This capability can be demonstrated even for short textual information units. The tensor-based framework is applied for high dimensionality. The investigation on feasibility was first conducted on two small-scale corpora. Results reflect the advantages of the convex polytopic model (CPM) in terms of model transparency and interpretability, robustness in generation and the generation of semantic patterns that are consistent with human expectation across distinctive and overlapping information categories. (This is reported mainly in the CogInfoComm 2018 paper) Further investigation shows that as the textual information units are embedded as points in a subspace, the key semantic patterns are located at the vertices of the convex polytope with minimum volume that encloses all the points. The minimum volume convex polytope always exists and is unique under the permutation of vertex labels for a finite point set. This is referred to as the normal (NO)-type, where all the vertices are within the point set and can be generated. If we specifically set the number of vertices and generate the minimum volume simplex (MVS) that enclose all the points – this is referred as the MVS-type polytope. We explored the use of these two types of polytopes in small corpora (CogInfoComm 2018 paper) to focus on feasibility, followed by the use of the ATIS (Air Travel Information System) corpora (ISCSLP 2019 paper) to focus on scalability. We show that our approach is viable in both papers. Finally, we furnish detailed analyses of the CPM approach applied to the ATIS corpora, in terms of semantic and geometric properties, compositional analyses, and word-word correlation analyses, as well as utilizing the semantic patterns extracted by the CPM approach to guide the learning of a neural model of a natural language understanding task. (This is reported in the submitted journal paper.)

14245316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14245316.value: We have proposed a novel, unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the Convex Polytopic Model (CPM) to discover key semantic patterns from transcribed dialog data. Experiments were conducted in the ATIS (Air Travel Information Domain). We show that the automatically extracted semantic patterns by the CPM approach from a given utterance are strongly related to the information and slot-value pairs in the corresponding semantic frame. Also, the compositional analyses and the discovered underlying structure of an utterance agree with human understanding. We have also elucidated the geometric properties of the extracted semantic patterns through detailed analyses. Experimental results also show that the semantic patterns extracted by the CPM method can boost the performance of state-of-the-art deep learning based approaches towards natural language understanding. Future work will be dedicated towards extending this approach for ease of transfer across information domains, as well as establish a semi-supervised learning framework for it.

14301316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301316.value: This project aims to investigate the recently available ultra-pure Sr2RuO4 single crystals under high pressures using a magnetic field to probe the suppression of superconductivity. In a superconductor, electrons form Cooper pairs that can condense into a coherent collective quantum state. An important parameter which characterizes different classes of superconductors is the symmetry of the energy gap and the closely related total spin angular momentum of the Cooper pair. Of all superconductors known to date, an overwhelming majority of them host Cooper pairs with zero total spin angular momentum (S=0), i.e. the electrons forming the pair have spin-up and spin-down, respectively – this is the spin singlet case. In contrast, the spin triplet case where the Cooper pairs have S=1 is very unusual. These different cases will react differently to the weakening of superconductivity when the magnetic field is applied. Sr2RuO4, the title compound of this project, is the leading candidate of a spin-triplet superconductor. Therefore, Sr2RuO4 has enjoyed a long-standing attention for more than two decades. Intriguingly, first-order superconducting transition was recently discovered at low temperatures in ultra-pure Sr2RuO4 single crystals. This cannot be easily reconciled with the known mechanisms for the destruction of the Cooper pair if the spin-triplet scenario must be upheld. To shed light on this issue, we will measure the upper critical fields of ultra-pure Sr2RuO4 under pressure for various magnetic field orientations to track the nature of the superconducting phase transition and to examine how superconductivity is weakened in the presence of the magnetic field. We believe we are in a unique position to carry out this project due to our well-established high pressure capability, the newly installed cryomagnetic facilities, and the availability of the purest single crystals. Despite decades of intensive research efforts, this project represents the first systematic high pressure investigation of the superconductivity in Sr2RuO4 with a pair breaking magnetic field, which promises to result in an extensive dataset spanning a wide phase space for a critical examination of the pairing symmetry in Sr2RuO4.

14302516.value: New notions of smoothness and differentiability are introduced and we have done variational analysis along a direction set in the general locally convex topological vector space setting and thereby generalized the classical Mazur Theorem and the Asplund theory in the broader context. 14302716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302716.value: In this project we aim at developing the Littlewood-Paley theory to study the well-posedness of the Cauchy problem on the Boltzmann equation and related collisional kinetic equations in the spatially inhomogeneous and close-to-equilibrium framework. Our main goal is to find out the Besov-type energy space with lower regularity in both space and velocity variables in which solutions with small amplitude exist globally in time and are unique. Our focus is to understand critical regularity of solutions through Besov spaces and also propagation of boundedness of solutions in higher order Sobolev norm as well as possible blow up criteria. We will carry out the mathematical analysis of the problem for different kinds of intermolecular interaction potentials under the Grad's angular cutoff assumption. Since Maxwell and Boltzmann established their fundamental equation in the kinetic theory of rarefied gases, the mathematical studies of the Boltzmann equation have been increasingly developing in many aspects. Among them, well-posedness should be one of the most important and hard issues. Particularly, so far it is still unknown whether the DiPerna-Lions' renormalised solution for large data is unique. On the other hand, the perturbation theory for close-to-equilibrium data has been extensively investigated due to Grad, Ukai, Guo and many others, and the existence of perturbative solutions even for angular non cutoff potentials also has been well understood in recent years. However, as far as only the Hilbert structure in the spatially inhomogeneous framework is concerned, initial data are generally required to be regular enough for a global-in-time existence result. Thus we expect to further study the well-posedness with critical regularity by borrowing techniques based on the Littlewood-Paley decomposition which actually has proved to be a very efficient analytical tool in the context of fluid dynamical equations. In the meantime, the research of this project is also expected to be our first step for understanding the link of the Boltzmann equation with the Navier-Stokes equations in Besov spaces with lower spatial regularity. 本項目旨在空間非齊次和近平衡態的框架下利用Littlewood-Paley理論來研究Boltzman方程和相關的帶碰撞的動力學方程柯西問題的適定性。我們的主要目標是尋求空間和速度變數都具有較低的正則性的Besov型能量空間，並在此空間研究小振幅解的整體時間存在性和唯一性。研究的重點是應用Besov空間理解臨界正則性和高階Sobolev範數有界性的傳播，以及可能的爆破準則。在Grad的角截斷假設下，我們將開展對不同類型的分子位元勢模型相應問題的數學分析。 自Maxwell和Boltzmann建立稀薄氣體動力學的基本方程起，Boltzmann方程的數學研究在諸多方面進展迅速。其中，適定性應該是最重要和最困難的問題之一，特別地，到目前為止仍不清楚DiPerna-Lions的大初值重整化解的唯一性。另一方面，關於近平衡態初值的擾動理論已被廣泛研究，這歸功於Grad、Ukai、Guo和許多其他人，甚至對角非截斷情形擾動解的存在性也在近幾年取得較好的理解。然而，在空間非齊次的框架下，如若我們僅考慮Hilbert結構並以此獲得解的整體適定性，那麼初值的正則性通常被要求足夠高。因此，我們希望進一步借用Littlewood-Paley分解研究具有臨界正則性的解的適定性，實際上，LP 分解已被證明在流體力學方程的研究背景中是一個非常有效的分析工具。 最後，我們期望本課題的研究能在具有較低的空間正則性的Besov空間中理解Boltzmann方程和Navier-Stokes方程之間的聯繫上提供一定的幫助。

14302716.label: Realisation of objectives
14302716.value: The first objective is to study well-posedness of the Boltzmann equation for soft potentials in a Besov space with critical regularity. We have fully achieved this objective in the research paper "Solution to the Boltzmann equation in velocity-weighted Chemin-Lerner type spaces" in collaboration with Shota Sakamoto. Specifically, in the aforementioned paper, we have studied the Boltzmann equation near global Maxwellians in the multi-dimensional whole space. A unique global-in-time mild solution to the Cauchy problem of the equation is established in a Chemin-Lerner type space with respect to the phase variable. Both hard and soft potentials with angular cutoff are considered. The new function space for global well-posedness is introduced to essentially treat the case of soft potentials, and the key point is that the velocity variable is taken in the weighted supremum norm, and the space variable is in the Besov space including the spatially critical regularity case. The proof is based on the time-decay properties of solutions to the linearized equation together with the bootstrap argument. Particularly, the linear analysis in case of hard potentials is due to the semigroup theory, where the extra time-decay plays a role in coping with initial data in the usual Hilbert space with respect to the space variable. In case of soft potentials, for the time-decay of linear equations we borrow the results based on the pure energy method and further extend them to those in the supremum-norm framework through an interplay technique developed by Guo. In contrast to hard potentials, an additional integrability in space variable for initial data is necessary in case of soft potentials so that one can obtain global solutions to the nonlinear Cauchy problem. Besides the consideration of constructing solutions with spatially critical regularity, we also have made an extensive study of low regularity solutions in another paper "Global mild solutions of the Landau and non-cutoff Boltzmann equations" in collaboration with Shuangqian Liu, Shota Sakamoto and Robert Strain. This paper proves the existence of small-amplitude global-in-time unique mild solutions to both the Landau equation including the Coulomb potential and the Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff. Since the well-known works on the construction of classical solutions in smooth Sobolev spaces which in particular are regular in the spatial variables, it still remains an open problem to obtain global solutions in an framework with the supremum norm in space and velocity variables, similar to that in the work by Guo, for the Boltzmann equation with cutoff in general bounded domains. One main difficulty arises from the interaction between the transport operator and the velocity-diffusion-type collision operator in the non-cutoff Boltzmann and Landau equations; another major difficulty is the potential formation of singularities for solutions to the boundary value problem. In the present work we introduce a new function space with low regularity in the spatial variable to treat the problem in cases when the spatial domain is either a torus, or a finite channel with boundary. For the latter case, either the inflow boundary condition or the specular reflection boundary condition is considered. An important property of the function space is that the distribution function is in the Wiener algebra in the spatial variables, namely, the Fourier transform is an absolutely convergent series. Besides the construction of global solutions in these function spaces, we additionally study the large-time behavior of solutions for both hard and soft potentials, and we further justify the property of propagation of regularity of solutions in the spatial variables. Surprisingly, all the obtained results are satisfied for all the range of molecular interaction potentials, either hard or soft. As mentioned before, one main difficulty in case of soft potentials usually occurs to the nonlinear estimates with velocity growth effect. In the previous works by the PI together with his collaborators, we have found out a time-velocity mixed exponential weight function whose time derivative induces an additional dissipation term. Such extra dissipation disappears in large time but it still can be used to overcome the difficulty for the nonlinear estimates whenever the solution a priori decays in time. Therefore, this approach fails if the explicit time decay rate is no longer available, for instance, in the framework of perturbations around some non-trivial profiles. In a recent research paper "Asymptotics toward viscous contact waves for solutions of the Landau equation" in collaboration with Dongcheng Yang and Hongjun Yu, we have found out a new weighted energy method that may not reply on the a priori time-decay of solutions. The main idea is to directly include the time integral of the energy dissipation rate functional as the time-dependent exponent coefficient of the exponential velocity weight function. In such way, the time derivative of the weight function leads to a quartic dissipation functionals accounting for the bound of the nonlinear terms in soft potentials. Although the current work is only restricted to the regular solutions, we believe that the method developed there can be so robust that it can be adopted to treat other situations with similar difficulties, in particular, even when the low regularity solutions are considered. The second objective of this project is to extend the corresponding results to the Boltzmann equation with self-consistent forces and further to the Vlasov-Poisson-Landau system with the Coulomb potential. We have almost fully achieved this objective in a recent work in progress "Low-regularity solutions for the Vlasov-Poisson-Landau/Boltzmann system" in collaboration with Dingqun Deng. In the paper, we are concerned with the nonlinear Cauchy problem on the Vlasov-Poisson-Landau system in torus or finite channel around global Maxwellians with the non-cutoff Boltzmann collision considered in a parallel way. We are able to establish the global existence and large time behavior of small amplitude solutions for a class of low regularity initial data by using the similar techniques in Duan-Liu-Sakamoto-Strain [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 74 (2021), no. 5, 932-1020]. The molecular interaction type is restricted to the case of hard potentials for two classical collision operators because of the effect of the self-consistent forces, so the case of soft potentials is still left open. The main difficulty occurs once again to the self-consistent force term containing the potential field. Such term is gone in the normal energy estimate process using the Sobolev space, while it still stands there when we take the Fourier transform in space variables and further try to make use of the low regularity function space to estimate the resultant equation. Therefore, we need to turn to the time-weighted energy method in terms of the time-decay of solutions mentioned before. In the meantime, the velocity diffusion regularity property of the non-cutoff Boltzmann operator and the Landau operator have to be essentially used.

14302716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302716.value: 1. We have studied the Boltzmann equation near global Maxwellians in the whole space. A unique global mild solution to the Cauchy problem is established in a Chemin-Lerner type space with respect to phase variables. Both hard and soft potentials with angular cutoff are considered. The new function space is introduced to essentially treat the case of soft potentials, and the key point is that the velocity variable is taken in the weighted supremum norm while the space variable is in a Besov space with the spatially critical regularity. See the research paper item No. 1 in Section 8, Part C. 2. We have introduced a new function space with low regularity in spatial variables to treat the well-posedness for the non-cutoff Boltzmann and Landau equations in cases when the spatial domain is either a torus, or a finite channel with boundary. An important property of the function space is that the the distribution function is in the Wiener algebra in spatial variables. In addition, we study the large-time behavior of solutions for both hard and soft potentials, and further justify the property of propagation of regularity of solutions in the spatial variables. See the research paper item No. 2 in Section 8, Part C. 3. We have studied the nonlinear Cauchy problem on the Vlasov-Poisson-Landau/Boltzmann system in torus or finite channel around global Maxwellians. The main goal is to establish the global existence and large time behavior of small amplitude solutions for a class of low regularity initial data. The result extends the previous one to the case of the VPL or VPB system. See the research paper item No. 3 in Section 8, Part C. 4. We have found an elaborate energy method to overcome the difficulty of estimating the nonlinear term due to the strong degenerate dissipation in case of soft potentials. The main finding is that the time derivative of the weight function we introduced is able to induce an extra quartic dissipation term. The time-decay of solutions is no longer required in contrast with the previous works. We believe that new weighted energy method is so robust that it can be applied to many problems in the similar situation. See the research paper item No. 4 in Section 8, Part C.

14302716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302716.value: 1. To study the fluid dynamic limit of the obtained global solutions with low regularity. The question is very interesting because the well-posedness for the fluid dynamical equation in those function spaces has been well understood. The low regularity feature would make it more difficult to analyze the problem than that for the regular solutions. 2. The current project is focused on the small-amplitude global solutions with low regularity. It would be interesting and challenging to treat the case of large amplitude but low regularity solutions, in particular, for the non-cutoff Boltzmann and Landau equations. In this direction, few are known except some small-amplitude results. In this regard, we expect to open a new research project to study the problem.

14302716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302716.value: Since Maxwell and Boltzmann established their fundamental equation in the kinetic theory of rarefied gases, the mathematical studies of the Boltzmann equation have been increasingly developing in many aspects. Among them, well-posedness should be one of the most important and hard issues. Particularly, so far it is still unknown whether the DiPerna-Lions' renormalised solution for large data is unique. On the other hand, the perturbation theory for close-to-equilibrium data has been extensively investigated due to Grad, Ukai, Guo and many others, and the existence of perturbative solutions even for angular non cutoff potentials also has been well understood in recent years. However, as far as only the Hilbert structure in the spatially inhomogeneous framework is concerned, initial data are generally required to be regular enough for a global-in-time existence result. In the project, we have attempted a study of the well-posedness for the Boltzmann and related kinetic equations with a class of initial data of low regularity in space variables.

14302916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302916.value: In vivo delivery of nanoparticles to the brain represents an enormous challenge, because they cannot easily penetrate through the "blood-brain barrier (BBB)", a layer of tightly packed endothelial cells that separates the brain from circulating blood. Selective delivery to neurons after BBB permeation remains to be desired. In this proposal, we will develop novel nanoparticles that can cross the BBB and then selectively enter neurons following a single intravenous injection. The nanoparticle will consist of two types of biocompatible polymers, poly(adenylic acid) (Poly(A)) and polydopamine (PDA). Specifically, the Poly(A) oligonucleotides will decorate the surface of the PDA nanoparticle core to form a PDA@Poly(A) core-shell nanostructure. We hypothesize that Poly(A) oligonucleotides, a linear polymer of adenosine (which is a native agonist of the adenosine receptors expressed by brain endothelial cells), will transiently relax the tight junctions to facilitate the permeation of nanoparticles through the BBB. We also envision that PDA, a cross-linked polymer of dopamine (which is a neurotransmitter and native ligand of the dopamine receptors expressed by neurons), can promote selective uptake by neurons after the nanoparticle crosses the BBB. We will first fabricate a library of PDA@Poly(A) nanoparticles with different physicochemical characteristics (e.g., size, dopamine content, adenosine content). Next, we will ascertain the ability of these nanoparticles to cross a monolayer of brain endothelial cells and subsequently enter neurons by using an in vitro BBB model. Based on these "structure-function relationship" data, we will identify the best-performing candidate nanoparticles and further explore their potential of delivering neuroprotective agents selectively to brain neurons in vivo. In particular, we plan to incorporate curcumin, a natural yet water-insoluble pigment with a promising role in preventing Alzheimer's disease, to the PDA@Poly(A) nanoparticles. After intravenously injecting the curcumin-loaded nanoparticles into mice, we will monitor their delivery to the brain by in vivo imaging and ex vivo microscopic analysis. Based on our published data (Choi CKK et al., JACS, 2015), we have developed the chemistry for immobilizing DNA oligonucleotides to the surface of PDA-coated nanoparticles. From our preliminary data, we have demonstrated that neurons can internalize PDA-coated nanoparticles more efficiently than brain endothelial cells and that Poly(A)-coated nanoparticles can transiently relax the tight junctions between brain endothelial cells in vitro. Results from our proposed research will guide the design of more effective nanoparticles to non-invasively treat and image brain-related medical conditions, such as dementia, stroke, and other neurodegenerative or psychiatric diseases. 要把納米粒子經體內傳送到大腦可謂一項十分艱辛的任務，因為它們通常難以穿越腦內由一層緊密連接的內皮細胞而組成的「血腦屏障」。更具挑戰性的是，納米粒子要能夠在通過血腦屏障後，選擇性地運入神經元內。 在此計劃書中，我們會研製一種能同時穿越血腦屏障以及選擇性地進入神經元的納米粒子。這嶄新的納米粒子含有兩項具有水溶性的高分子: 多聚腺苷酸(poly(adenylic acid))及聚多巴胺(polydopamine)。具體來說，我們會先用化學方法將多巴胺(一種廣為人知的神經遞質)聚合成為聚多巴胺納米粒子。然後，我們會將聚腺苷酸，一條由DNA之鹼基腺苷(adenosine)聚合而成的聚合物，修飾在聚多巴胺納米粒子之表面，從而形成核殼納米結構。由於在建構血腦屏障的腦內皮細胞之表面是有高表達的腺苷受體，我們預計在聚多巴胺納米粒子表面上的多聚腺苷酸能有效刺激於腦內皮細胞上的腺苷受體，使血腦屏障短暫打開，讓納米粒子穿越血腦屏障。此外，因為神經元表面有著大量的多巴胺受體，我們推論多聚腺苷酸披覆聚多巴胺納米粒子在穿越血腦屏障後，可以選擇性地進入神經元。 我們會先合成一系列帶有不同物理化學性質的多聚腺苷酸披覆聚多巴胺納米粒子。我們會針對納米粒子的大小和多聚腺苷酸的長短等性質作深入調查，利用體外血腦屏障模型去測試納米粒子穿越血腦屏障之能力。從體外細胞測試的數據，我們將找出最佳的合成設計來製備用於往後體內動物實驗之多聚腺苷酸披覆聚多巴胺納米粒子。在其後的動物實驗中，我們會嘗試把薑黃素，一種不易溶於水但對治療腦退化症有良好效用的食用色秦，組裝在我們所研製出來之多聚腺苷酸披覆聚多巴胺納米粒子中。經過靜脈注射到老鼠體內，我們會利用不同的體內及體外成像技術來觀察載有薑黃素之多聚腺苷酸披覆聚多巴胺納米粒子的腦內含量和分佈。較早前，我們發表了將DNA寡核苷酸固定在聚多巴胺披覆納米粒子上之化學方法(Choi CKK et al., JACS, 2015)。根據前期實驗數據，我們證實了神經元比腦內皮細胞更有效內吞聚多巴胺披覆的納米粒子，亦證明了多聚腺苷酸披覆的納米粒子能令體外血腦屏障短暫地變得鬆散。 此項研究計劃的成果將能夠指導納米粒子的設計，有助於更有效地治療和檢測與腦部相關的醫療狀況，如痴呆症、中風及其他腦退化或精神科疾病。

14302916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302916.value: The core component of our nanoscale delivery system consists of PDA-coated gold nanoparticles. The first major finding lies on the comprehensive understanding in the bio-nano interactions of PDA-coated nanoparticles. Before the publication of our work in 2018, the field had yet to understand how essential reaction parameters such as dopamine concentration and polymerization time impact the synthesis of PDA-coated nanoparticles, their protein adsorption profile, and cellular uptake properties. These results will support the reproducible synthesis of PDA-coated nanoparticles with defined sizes and shapes for biomedical applications (Sy et al., Langmuir, 2018). Moreover, such understanding leads us to discover an unprecedented method of preparing PDA-coated gold nanoworms by one-dimensional bottom-up assembly. As these plasmonic nanoworms enter mammalian cells abundantly and are resistant against intracellular degradation, they are attractive agents for intracellular dark-field imaging and photothermal therapy (Choi et al., ACS Nano, 2019). For our work on PDA-coated nanoworms, my PhD student and I have received the Best Paper on Materials 2019 (Postgraduate Group) by the HKIE Materials Division and a “Poster Presentation Award” at the 2019 GRC Plasmonically-Powered Processes. The intended application of the PDA-coated nanoparticle is for brain delivery. At the in vitro level, the major finding is that poly(A)-appended PDA-coated gold nanoparticles are effective in transiently opening up the tight junctions in a Transwell blood-brain barrier (BBB) model. For these results, my final-year project undergraduate student received an Innovation and Technology Project Competition Award from the Hong Kong Electronic Industries Association Limited. Also, I supported a related work on the use of targeted nanoparticles for crossing the BBB in vitro (Luo et al., ACS AMI, 2019). At the in vivo level, the major finding is that the route of administration significantly influences the delivery of PDA-coated nanoparticles to the brain. Upon an intracranial injection into the brain of Balb/c mice, PDA-coated nanoparticles primarily accumulate near the ventricular area (near the injection site) and diffuse to the striatum and cortex 24 h after injection. Upon an intravenous injection, the same nanoparticles primarily accumulate in the liver without appreciable accumulation in the brain or sites with profuse expression of the dopamine receptor. Motivated by these different pharmacological behaviors, we published an extensive review on nanomedicines for delivery to the brain (Lee et al., Mol. Pharm., 2020). We analyzed the design criteria of nanoparticles for brain delivery, animal models with brain diseases, merits of various methods of administration, and potential for translation.

14302916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302916.value: From our investigations in the bio-nano interactions of PDA-coated nanoparticles, we discovered that the PDA-coated plasmonic gold nanoworms are impressive agents for dark-field imaging and photothemal killing of cancer cells in vitro. We will study the potential of these nanoworms for photothermally ablating tumors in animal models. As these nanoworms do not pronouncedly accumulate in acidic organelles inside the cancer cell, we will study the efficiency of these nanoworms for delivering functional nucleic acids (e.g., oligonucleotides and plasmids) to the cytosol or nucleus to achieve improved gene regulation or gene expression, respectively. Furthermore, we will explore the delivery of functional nucleic acids to cancer cells in tumor-bearing animal models and verify if the nanoworms and/or nucleic acids will also accumulate in acid organelles in reduced amounts in vivo. Pending promising data, we may evaluate the anti-tumor efficacy of the nanoworms by gene regulation in mice that bear brain glioblastoma. Finally, we will engineer a more effective nanoparticle for penetrating the BBB upon an intravenous injection, because intracranial injection is too invasive. We are now investigating the effects of nanoparticle size and surface chemistry on the penetration of nanoparticles through the BBB in mice with Huntington's Disease, a neurodegenerative disease.

14302916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302916.value: The research project has expanded our understanding in how PDA-coated nanoparticles interact with brain cell types (e.g., neurons and brain endothelial cells) and other cell types. These are valuable data because PDA-coated nanoparticles are an important class of bionanomaterials with attractive properties for biomedical applications, such as biocompatibility and abundant entry to cells. On the materials front, we have learned how to prepare PDA-coated nanoparticles of defined sizes and shapes reproducibly (e.g., nanoclusters, individual nanospheres, and nanoworms) and reported the composition of serum proteins adhere to the surface of nanoparticles. On the biology front, we have learned that attachment of poly(A) oligonucleotides allows PDA-coated nanoparticles to cross the blood-brain barrier in vitro. For animal studies, we have shown that intracranial injection is a more effective method for delivering PDA-coated nanoparticles to the brain than intravenous injection; once entering the brain, the nanoparticles primarily accumulate near the injection site in the cortex and striatum, but without strong localization to the sites with profuse expression of dopamine receptors. These mechanistic insights will benefit the design of nanomedicines for delivery to the brain and treating diseases (e.g., glioblastoma and Huntington's Disease).

14303516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303516.value: The geometry of Calabi-Yau manifolds is a very rich subject and it has been studied extensively from many different perspectives, including differential geometry, algebraic geometry, symplectic geometry, as well as string theory in physics. For instance, mirror symmetry is a highly nontrivial duality between mirror Calabi-Yau manifolds. Geometry of Calabi-Yau threefolds also has a surprising relationship with knot theory. In this proposal, the PI plans to study several important aspects of the geometry of Calabi-Yau manifolds. These include Lagrangian foliations and their corresponding non-commutative geometry, moduli spaces of noncompact Lagrangian submanifolds and their relationships with geometric engineering and knot theory. These studies would have useful applications in mirror symmetry. 卡拉比丘流形的幾何是一門內容豐富的學問，也已經有大量從 不同角度的研究，包括微分幾何 ，代數幾何，辛幾何和物理中 的弦理論。鏡對稱是其​​中有關卡拉比丘流形極​​為複雜的對偶性。 同時三維卡拉比丘空間和結理論有着令人驚嘆的關係。​ 研​​究員在這研究計劃中準備硏​​究卡拉比丘幾​​何幾個重要的方向。 其​​中包括拉格朗日葉狀結構​​​​及它們對應的非交換幾何,非緊拉格 朗日子流形及它們與幾何工程和結理論的關係。這些硏究會對 鏡對稱有重要的應用。​​ ​

14303516.label: Realisation of objectives
14303516.value: Both objectives have been achieved successfully. The PI have extensively expanded our understanding of the symplectic geometry for Calabi-Yau manifolds. This includes new results in counting pseudo-holomorphic disks, constructions of Lagrangian torus fibrations, understanding the geometry of Maurer-Cartan equation near degenerate Calabi-Yau varieties and geometric relationship with scattering diagrams and their refined counterpart. For non-compact complex Lagranians, the PI explained the behavior under flops and relationships with Plucker formula and homological projective duality. Related new discoveries include obtaining an energy bound for Kapustin-Witten solutions in the model and equivariant deformation quantization and its relationship with coadjoint orbit method and representation theory of real reductive groups.

14303516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303516.value: Given a degenerate Calabi-Yau variety equipped with local deformation data, the PI have constructed an almost dgBV algebra, giving a singular version of the extended Kodaira-Spencer dgLa in the Calabi-Yau setting. Assuming Hodge-to-deRham degeneracy and a local condition that guarantees freeness of the Hodge bundle, we prove a unobstructedness theorem for the smoothing of singular Calabi-Yau varieties. We also demonstrate how our construction yields a logarithmic Frobenius manifold structure on a formal neighborhood in the extended moduli space. These results are given in the joint paper 'Geometry of the Maurer-Cartan equation near degenerate CY varieties'. We further develop the asymptotic analytic approach to the study of scattering diagrams by analyzing the asymptotic behavior of Maurer-Cartan elements of a dgLa constructed from a monoid-graded Lie algebra. We interpreted Maurer-Cartan elements, and therefore consistent scattering diagrams, in terms of the refined counting of tropical disks. We also describe theta functions in terms of distinguished flat section of the Maurer-Cartan deformed differential. These results are given in the joint paper 'Refined scattering diagrams and theta functions from aspmptotic analysis of Maurer-Cartan equations'. We construct pseudotoric structures on the two-step flag variety Fℓ1,n−1;n, and explain a general relation between pseudotoric structures and special Lagrangian torus fibrations, the latter of which are important in the study of SYZ mirror symmetry. As an application, we speculate how our constructions can explain the number of terms in the superpotential of Rietsch’s Landau–Ginzburg mirror. These results are given in the joint paper 'Pseudotoric structures and special Lagrangian torus fibrations on certain flag varieties'. We compute orbi-disk invariants of compact Gorenstein semi-Fano toric orbifolds by extending the method used for toric Calabi-Yau orbifolds. As a consequence the orbi-disc potential is analytic over complex numbers. These results are given in the joint paper 'A note on disk counting in toric orbifolds'. We generalize the fundamental theorem of HPD beyond linear sections by studying conormal complex Lagrangian in the cotangent bundle of projective spaces. These results are given in the joint paper 'Categorical Plucker formula and homological projective duality'. We show that for solutions of Kapustin–Witten equation with Nahm pole boundary condition on S3 × R+, there exists a universal constant bound on its Yang–Mills energy. These results are given in the joint paper 'Energy Bound for Kapustin–Witten Solutions on S3 × R+'. We apply deformation quantization to the study of the coadjoint orbit method in the case of real reductive groups. We first prove some general results on the existence of equivariant deformation quantization of vector bundles on closed Lagrangian subvarieties, which lie in smooth symplectic varieties with Hamiltonian group actions. Then we apply them to orbit method and construct nontrivial irreducible Harish-Chandra modules for certain coadjoint orbits. Our examples include new geometric construction of representations associated to certain orbits of real exceptional Lie groups. These results are given in the joint paper 'Equivariant deformation quantization and coadjoint orbit method'.

14303516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303516.value: New methods and tools obtained in the project, including constructing solution of Maurer-Cartan equation from scattering diagrams, would be very useful in further understanding of the moduli space of Calabi-Yau varieties near boundaries.

14303516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303516.value: Symplectic geometry is an important bridge between geometry and physics. The discoveries in this project advances our understanding of this highly mysterious subject.

14303816.label: Project Objectives
14303816.value: To develop viable synthetic routes to several curved PACs by embedding a non-planar TBTQ unit as the central core to a polycyclic aromatic system. To examine their structural, conformational and potential self-assembling properties by spectroscopic methods and X-ray crystallography.

To examine the electronic properties of these compounds and their potential applications as organic semiconductors in thin film transistors.

14303816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303816.value: Polycyclic aromatic compounds (PACs) that possess a curved π surface are a class of interesting molecules due to their novel structures and unusual properties. The non-planar nature of PACs can be generated by incorporating non-hexagonal rings in a nanographene sheet, or by inducing twisting of the aromatic rings in a nanographene sheet by steric crowding. As an alternative approach, this project seeks to design and synthesize a class of curved PACs by the introduction of several sp3 hybridized carbon centers into a flat polycyclic aromatic fused ring system using a tribenzotriquinacene (TBTQ) moiety. The effect of the curved surface on the structural, self-assembling, electronic and chemical reactivity properties of the TBTQ-modified PACs will then be examined. These compounds can also be considered as structural mimics of defective graphene, and hence the study of their properties can provide interesting insights into the many unusual chemical and physico-chemical features of such twisted π-systems. 非平面π體系的稠環芳香化合物( PACs )是一類有趣的分子， 因為它們具有新穎的結構和特殊的性質。非平面的稠環芳香 化合物可以通過在納米石墨烯結構嵌入非六元環或者引入由 於位阻效應導致扭曲的芳香環來獲得。作為一種可以替代的 方法，這個課題試圖引入具有幾個sp3雜化碳原子中心的三苯 三戊並烯( TBTQ )到平面稠環芳烴從而設計並合成一類非平面 稠環芳香化合物。有關彎曲表面對TBTQ修飾的稠環芳烴的結 構、自組裝、電子和化學反應活性等性質的影響將會被檢測。 這些化合物也可以被認為是缺陷石墨烯結構的類似物， 因此它們的性質研究可以為這類非平面π體系特殊的物理、 化學性質提供深刻的理解。

14303816.label: Realisation of objectives
14303816.value: 1. Objective 1: (a) First level peripheral π-extension on a tribenzotriquinacene (TBTQ) core: Our approach toward the synthesis of the target compounds in this proposal is to append the aromatic rings on the peripheral of a TBTQ core in a layer-by-layer manner. In this way we can exert better synthetic control of the product purity. Hence, a series of 1,4,8-triaryl-substituted TBTQ derivatives 1 bearing different electron donating substituents was first prepared using a synthesis route developed by us (see Appendix Figure 1). These compounds were then subjected to a threefold nonclassical Scholl type cycloheptatriene formation in the presence of dichlorodicyanobenzoquinone (DDQ)/triflic acid to form the wizard-hat type molecules 2. As it turned out, only strongly electron donating substituents such as dimethoxyphenyl and trimethoxyphenyl groups could promote the successful cyclization to form the target molecules (i.e. compounds 2a and 2b). It was also found that the key side reaction is the bridgehead hydroxylation. This work was published in Org. Chem. Front. and presented in the ACS Asia-Pacific International Chapter Conference in Nov 2017. (b) Second level peripheral π-extension: After the successful addition of the first rim of aromatic rings to furnish compound 2a, the peripheral C–H bonds were then functionalized via electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions in order to add the second rim of aromatic rings. When compound 2a was subjected to six-fold electrophilic aromatic bromination, the hexabromides 3 were produced as a mixture of regioisomers. Interestingly, due to steric congestion, it was found that only one bromine atom could be accommodated in each of the six bay-regions of 3. Without further purifications, all these isomers were used for the subsequent Suzuki-Miyaura coupling to give a regioisomeric mixture of hexaphenylated compounds. In the final Scholl cyclization reaction, all the isomers reacted convergently to produce the same π-extended nonplanar nanographene 4 in 38% yield. This work was published in J. Org. Chem.. (c) Third level peripheral π-extension on compound 4: Approaches to convert the hexamethoxy compounds 4 to other derivatives followed by third round of π-extension failed due to the poor solubility of the resulting system. Another attempt which tried to directly attach the second and third layers of aromatic rings simultaneously to the hexatriflate derivative of 2a via Suzuki coupling was also unsuccessful because of similar solubility problems. Alternatively, we also tried the Friedel-Craft cyclization method to construct the cycloheptane ring but this approach also failed to materialize. (d) Efforts were then switched to the preparation of other π-extension TBTQ derivatives with a porous architecture. After various experimentations, a trefoiled shaped nonplanar nanographene 6 bearing three pores was prepared via a threefold Scholl type macrocyclization approach from precursor 5 (see Appendix Figure 2). The overall yield of this synthesis was extremely high (41%) from readily available starting materials. This work was published in one of the top journals in Chemistry – Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. and presented as a contributed lecture at the 18th International Symposium on Novel Aromatic Compounds in Jul 2019. Further effort was also conducted in collaboration with Prof. Cao of Lanzhou University on another type of porous π-extension TBTQ cage compounds. A pair of enantiomerically pure cages 8 was prepared via intramolecular Hay-coupling of the triacetylene precursor 7 in 15% yield. This work was published in Org. Lett.. 2. Objective 2: (a) The structural, conformational and self-assembling properties of the synthesized compounds 2, 4, 6 and 8 were examined by a combination of spectroscopic and structural methods. Crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction analysis were obtained from compound 2a (see Appendix Figure 3). The result showed that 2a had a wizard-hat structure with a hat depth of 3.2 Å. π–π Stacking interaction was found between the molecules in the solid state, but molecular aggregation was not observed in the solution state. For compounds 4 and 6, we were unable to obtain good quality crystals for structural analysis. Nonetheless, their 1H NMR spectra showed significant signal broadening, indicating a higher degree of molecular association in the solution state. Fortunately, one of the derivatives of 6 was amendable to X-ray structural analysis, showing that it has a distorted wizard-hat structure with a hat depth of 4.9 Å, but only possesses weak π–π stacking interaction in the solid state. (b) The host-guest property of the TBTQ derivatives was also examined. One derivative of porous nanographene 6 was found to bind to chloride ion in a 1:1 stoichiometry with an association constant of 88 M–1. Based on DFT calculations, it was believed that the Csp2–H bonds were the ligating functionalities responsible for the anion binding. We also found out that the presence of quaternary ammonium salts of different cationic size could change the supramolecular architecture of the host-guest complexes involving the TBTQ host. The latter work was published in Cryst. Growth Des.. 3. Objective 3: The chemical reactivity of the peripheral C–H bonds was examined by performing electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions on compound 2a. With regard to the sixfold bromination reaction, conversion of the C–H bonds to the C–Br bonds was possible, albeit the regioselectivity was difficult to control and generally a mixture of regioisomers was obtained. Gratifyingly, we were able to make use of this reaction to prepare the second level π-extended compound 4, details of which had been described earlier in section 1(b). 4. Objective 4: (a) The electronic properties, such as UV and fluorescence properties were determined by spectroscopic methods. Generally speaking, further π-extension leads to a red-shift of UV absorption maximum. For example, the absorption edge of compound 2a is 347 nm, while that of the π-extended compound 4 is 490 nm. (b) The redox properties of the compounds were also examined by cyclic voltammetry. It was found that the more π-conjugated compound 4 gave reversible redox properties, while the less π-conjugated congener 2a produced irreversible redox waves. Based on the UV and cyclic voltammetry data, the HOMO-LUMO gap of compound 2a and 4 were determined to be 3.57 and 2.53 eV, respectively. Unfortunately, due to the poor stacking properties of the compounds in the solid state, they do not show any interesting semiconducting properties.

14303816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303816.value: 1. In this research work we developed several successful approaches to prepare π-extended derivatives on the TBTQ core. Four different classes of new compounds, 2, 4, 6 and 8 were obtained. For the synthesis of compound 2, a new non-classical Scholl cycloheptatriene formation reaction was developed. For the preparation of 4, a new regioconvergent synthesis based on a non-regioselective C–H bromination of compound 2 was identified. For the production of the porous nanographene 6, a novel threefold Scholl-type macrocyclization of precursor 5 was exemplified. For the synthesis of the TBTQ cage compound, a threefold Hay C–C bond coupling was realized. The research results demonstrated the TBTQ skeleton was amendable to a wide variety of synthetic manipulations to produce nonplanar nanographenes of various topologies. 2. The structural, conformational and supramolecular properties of the target compounds were examined by various spectroscopic methods. As revealed by X-ray crystallography, some of these compounds possess a wizard-hat topology. Unfortunately, the stacking properties of these compounds were not favorable in the solid state such that they do not exhibit useful semiconducting properties. On the other hand, the porous nanographene 4 and some of its derivatives were found to bind to chloride ion, which is the second literature report demonstrating the interesting anion binding property of this type of porous nanographene. 3. Based on the research results, five original research papers and one review article were published in international journals. In addition, two lectures were presented in international conferences. The six papers appeared in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (IF = 12.959), Org. Lett. (IF = 6.091), Org. Chem. Front. (IF = 5.155), J. Org. Chem. (IF = 4.335), Cryst. Growth Des. (IF = 4.089) and Chin. J. Org. Chem. (IF = 1.344). 4. One part of the research work was conducted in collaboration with Prof. Cao of Lanzhou University. 5. Two PhD students were trained on this project. One had already graduated and the other is writing up the thesis soon and he is expected to complete the work by the end of 2021.

14303816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303816.value: This research work develops new methods towards the synthesis of new types of nonplanar nanographene architectures. The most interesting compounds revealed here are the porous nanographene molecules 4 and the TBTQ cage derivatives such as 8. First, non-heteroatom-containing compounds that can bind to anions are rare. The finding of such property in the former compounds opens up the possibility of designing new anion sensors, with the potential to couple the sensing mechanism via photoelectronic transitions. For the latter compounds, this research work opens a potential to examine their encapsulation properties. The fact that the molecules themselves can be prepared in optically pure form also suggested that they may be used for enantioselective guest binding. We are pursuing these new directions within our group and in collaboration with Prof. Cao of Lanzhou University.

14303816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303816.value: In this research project we developed new methods for the preparation of several new class of curved, carbon-rich nanographene compounds that show interesting geometrical and structural properties. Although our initial goal of aiming to prepare organic semiconducting materials based on these compounds failed to materialize due to their poor packing property of the molecules in the solid state. It was found that these compounds possess other interesting properties such as interacting with anions and potential trapping of small molecules using their interior voids. This finding opens up the possibilities of using these compounds as sensors of molecular anions or as storage materials for small molecules.

14304616.label: Project Objectives
14304616.value: Survey cold-medium B-fields in face-on galaxies to test cloud formation scenarios (Fig. 1A): One can never achieve this by observing clouds within the Milky Way, from where all the cloud B-field data were taken before Li and Henning (2011); this is because the angular momentum and the turbulence stemming from galactic shear are not observable from an edge-on view of a galactic disc. We have started this strategy with M33 by using the SMA (Fig. 1B; Li & Henning, 2011), but M33 is the only spiral galaxy close enough for SMA to resolve molecular clouds. We will use ALMA to continue the survey. (same as original #1). Survey 10-kAU scale B-fields around protostellar discs to test disc formation scenarios (Fig. 2): Most simulations of protostellar disc formation show that cloud B-fields start to gradually turn into toroidal ones at the kAU scale (Fig. 2 e), irrespective of how the cloud fields are assumed to be. Interferometer observations usually focus on this kAU scale (e.g., Hull et al., 2013), and thus they cannot put constraint on competing simulations. We will use APol to study field morphologies from the 1 to 10 kAU scale in the vicinities of protostellar discs, where strong-/weak-field scenarios predict different field morphologies (Fig. 2 d). (same as original #2). Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations and radiation transfer: Our team includes experts on numerical MHD simulations to simulate the objectives in points 1, 2 and 3. Comparing simulations with observational results allows us to study the physics behind each objective. We realize that ALMA time is highly competitive. In case during any year the observation proposals are not successful (we can propose ALMA observations every year and ASTE observations twice a year), observers in the team can still perform simulated observations on the MHD simulations to predict future observational results. (same as original #4; original #3 is cancelled due to the limited funding)

14304616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304616.value: 星系盤會分裂成旋臂，從而進一步分裂成分子雲（〜10 parsec) -- 恆星的搖籃。在恆星誕生之前, 分子雲的一部分將凝結成“雲核”（〜10-1 parsec) 及恆星盤（<10-3 parsec)。雖然上述恆星形成過程已被廣泛地觀察，但其生成原理仍不明朗。其中最神秘的力量莫過於磁場。 我們最近觀察到的多尺度有序磁場強烈地建議磁場在分子雲碎裂的過程中扮演重要角色. 我們對河外星系的觀測則建議磁場對分子雲生成亦同等重要. 然而，受限於望遠鏡靈敏度, 以上實驗樣本規模都很小. 新望遠鏡”阿塔卡馬大型毫米波/亞毫米波列”（ALMA），提供了空前的靈敏度。通過新成立的中國 - 智利聯合天文學中心, 我們將出ALMA觀測計畫，以提高樣本大小。同時，我們正在建設的ASTE偏振儀（APol; GRF 14600915）則能夠調查磁場對恆星盤形成的作用。我們計劃派遣博士後和學生長駐智利以開展ASTE和ALMA觀測。

14304616.label: Realisation of objectives
14304616.value: Objectives 1 and 2 are not 100% achieved mainly due to the fact that ALMA polarimetry had not reached its full capability. We were indeed awarded ALMA time and acquired data from NGC 628 (for objective 1) in 2017 and NGC 2024 (for objective 2) in 2019, but no convincing polarization had been detected. Moreover, the 2020 ALMA operation and proposal submission were suspended due to the pandemic. This is only the first decade of the ALMA operation; we will keep on trying as ALMA approaching its optimization in the coming years. We can still achieve 90% of the goals of objectives 1 and 2 because of alternative methods. For objective 1, we collaborated with the Dept. of Statistics to redo the Bayesian analysis (Crutcher et al. 2010) that was generally considered against our M33 result (Li & Henning 2011, see objective 1). Our more careful analysis (Jiang, Li & Fan 2020) on the same set of data used by Crutcher et al. (2010) showing no controversy with Li & Henning (2011), i.e., the magnetic field is dynamically important with density up to several thousand hydrogen molecules per cubic cm. Crutcher et al. (2010) concluded with a much lower density due to an underestimate of the data uncertainty. We also identified other evidence in Law, Li & Leung (2019) and Law, Li, Cao & Ng (2020) For objective 2, we first observed the decoupling scale between turbulence eddies and magnetic fields (Tang, Li & Lee 2018) and then showed that turbulence below this scale is super-Alfvenic (Zhang, Guo, Wang & Li 2019). Both are critical for solving the "magnetic braking catastrophe" for protostellar disk formation, the motivation of objective 2. For objective 3, I would say that the achievement rate is 200%. Our numerical simulations are not only playing a major role in interpreting the observations in objectives 1 and 2 (which is the goal of objective 3), they also suggested new "observables" for future observations (Qu & Li; Cao, Li, Wang & Fan; Wang, Cao, Fan & Li; in preparation). All the leading authors in the 2018/2019/2020 publications mentioned above are my Ph.D./M.Phil students supported by this project.
