14313816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14313816.value: Focusing on investigating the seismogenesis and structures of the southern Mariana subduction zone using the near-field OBS observations, we have produced a series of research outcome, as listed in Part C. Major findings in the project include (1) We obtain the first-ever near-field OBS data and a precise local earthquake catalogue in the southernmost Mariana margin. (2) The maximum depth of slab-related earthquakes increases from ~100km to ~240km while the dip angle of the subducted plate increases from west to east towards Guam. However, the dip angle at shallow depth is much smaller than that at great depths. (3) The plate bending models show that the axial loading and stresses of old subducting plates vary significantly along the Mariana trench. Such along-strench variation of stress corresponds to non-uniform distribution of outer-rise earthquakes. (4) The tomographic results show low velocities within the upper ~30 km of the mantle near the trench, indicating extensive mantle hydration and a large amount of water input into the southern Mariana subduction zone.

14313816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14313816.value: Motivated by the findings in this project, we are presently working on two aspects to better delineate the shallow seismogenic zone and constrain outer-rise faultings. First, we are detecting more earthquakes using the state-of-art machine learning methods on the OBS dataset. Second, we are developing 3D bending models by incorporating curvatures of the trench and subducting plate. These efforts will extend and broaden the scope of the project and can leverage further research opportunities and funding supports.

14313816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14313816.value: The Mariana subduction zone with the deepest spot on Earth, the Challenger Deep (~10.9 km), remains mysterious in a number of scientific aspects and is regarded as the fourth pole of the Earth. Scientists have long wondered what accounts for that steep dive, and why massive earthquakes have not been recorded along the Mariana subduction zone. Motivated by the above multidisciplinary problems, a series of scientific expeditions are conducted across the southern Mariana subduction zone where we conducted the first-ever OBS experiments. Using the first near-field seismic dataset, we construct a precise local earthquake catalogue, model bending deformation of the subducting plate, and derive the velocity structures of the crust and upper mantle in the southernmost Mariana margin. Our results produce the first high-resolution earthquake catalogue in the southernmost Mariana subduction zone, which provides valuable constraints on the slab geometry and subduction zone dynamics. Furthermore, the lack of massive earthquakes in Marianas was likely due to the low plate locking and small seismogenic zone, which were inferred from our seismological results. Our findings in this project mark the first critical step to investigate the southernmost Mariana subduction zone, and have leveraged continuous efforts for further investigations.

14314216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14314216.value: The primary goal of this project is to design and carry out in-situ synchrotron characterization experiments for organic and inorganic halide perovskite thin films in order to understand the perovskite crystallization kinetics, process-structure-performance correlation, and in turn improve the device performance and reproducibility. Recently, organic and inorganic halide perovskite solar cell has become the new rising star in solar cell research due to their rapid surge of power conversion efficiency and appealing low-cost solution processability. Fine-tuning the device fabrication parameters is one of the feasible and promising routes to further push the power conversion efficiency, however, requiring huge amount of time and research efforts. Despite fruitful results on fabrication methodologies and device performance optimization, fundamental studies on perovskite crystal structure and morphology, crystal growth and film formation mechanism are still very limited. Careful explorations on these aspects are highly desired, in order to effectively guide future directions of device optimization. In addition, this will also shed light on understanding fundamental problems of perovskite solar cell devices, such as hysteresis and exciton diffusion within the perovskite film. Herein, we propose an in-situ synchrotron characterization scheme to systematically monitor the crystallization and film formation under various fabrication conditions. Synchrotron techniques, such as grazing incidence wide/small-angle X-ray scattering, near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure, X-ray/Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy will be employed to provide comprehensive structural, compositional and electronic information about the samples. A homemade sample chamber equipped with spin coater, annealing stage, UV lamp, and compatible with many synchrotron beamlines for different characterization purposes will be designed and constructed. The high-brilliance and time resolution of synchrotron light will offer superior data quality and save a great amount of time for in-situ characterizations. We believe that the proposed work will open up a new viewpoint to this area, provide more insights on device optimization, obtain a deep understanding of the process-structure-performance correlation and thereby contribute to the future widespread application of perovskite solar cells.

14314216.label: Realisation of objectives
14314216.value: To conduct in-situ characterizations of perovskite films, we have designed and constructed several in-situ chambers in order to mimic perovskite fabrication conditions (objective 1). Firstly, an air-tight chamber containing a heating stage was fabricated and utilized to monitor the annealing process of perovskite films. The temperature of the heating stage can be remotely controlled, and the chamber can be filled with N2 which is consistent with the perovskite fabrication environment in the glovebox. The chamber is compatible with the synchrotron beamline in Shanghai and we have successfully captured the phase transition from the intermediate phase to the perovskite phase during the annealing process of perovskite films. Secondly, we have designed and constructed a remote-controllable spin-coater for the purpose of investigating the perovskite crystallization kinetics during the spin-coating process. The spin-coater can be remotely controlled so that it is supposed to be used in the synchrotron beamline, but it is found that the spin-coater is too big to be integrated into the synchrotron beamline due to the size of the rotating motor. Fortunately, our collaborators in beamline 23A1, National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center (NSRRC), Taiwan, have an integrated spin-coater in the beamline. We have upgraded the spin-coater chamber and obtained many important findings that will be described in detail in the following. Thirdly, we further designed and made an air-tight chamber with Kapton windows that can let X-rays and simulated sunlight simultaneously pass through. As a result, the light-induced structural evolution of perovskites has been also successfully obtained. To improve the structure and morphology of perovskite films, we have explored and developed several fabrication procedures with the aid of ex-situ characterizations such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscope (SEM), ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) absorption spectroscopy, etc. (objective 2). One-step spin-coating method was first employed to deposit (FAPbI3)0.83(MAPbBr3)0.17 perovskite films, and anti-solvent such as chlorobenzene (CB) was adopted during the spinning in order to quickly wash off the perovskite solvent and form a uniform film rather than a dendritic morphology with many unwanted pinholes. In the meantime, the perovskite precursor stability was greatly improved by adding a small molecule ITIC-Th (Adv. Energy Mater. 2018, 8, 1703399). We also found that the as-cast FAMAPbX3 film should be annealed immediately with the end of the spin-coating process. Otherwise, the resulted perovskite film will contain secondary phases that are detrimental to device performance (Adv. Mater. 2019, 31, 1901284). The underlying mechanism of this interesting phenomenon was not disclosed until we employed in-situ characterizations, which will be illustrated in the following. One-step method was also employed to fabricate efficient all-inorganic CsPbI2Br perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with an efficiency of 14.34% (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2019, 7, 27640-27647). Then, we explored a two-step method to fabricate perovskite films, which consisted of sequential depositions of an inorganic PbI2 layer and organic salts. The two-step fabricated perovskite films exhibit better stability and higher light absorption ability with a thicker film. In addition, we developed a sequential A-site doping strategy to precisely control the perovskite crystallization kinetics, thus boosting power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of perovskite solar cells over 23% (Adv. Mater. 2020, 32, 2004630). Since both the one-step spin-coating process and two-step process can deliver high-efficiency PSCs (objective 3), we conducted in-situ grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) to capture the corresponding perovskite crystallization and film formation process. We successfully obtained frequent synchrotron beam time at 23A1 of TLS in Taiwan and BL19U2 of SSRF in Shanghai, and observed many interesting phase transition pathways for various perovskite systems under different fabrication processes. For the mixed perovskite (FAPbI3)0.83(MAPbBr3)0.17, three crystallization stages during spinning are identified: I) precursor solution state; II) hexagonal δ-phase (2H), and III) complex phases including hexagonal polytypes (4H, 6H), intermediate phase, and perovskite α-phase. In contrast, the perovskite with Cs+ doping only experienced two crystallization stages: I) precursor solution state, and II) hexagonal δ-phase (2H) and perovskite α-phase (Adv. Mater. 2019, 31, 1901284). In comparison, for the pure perovskite MAPbI3, only phase transition from precursor to the intermediate phase was recorded, and there is no perovskite phase formed during the spinning process (Joule, 2020, 4, 1-22). We also systematically investigated the crystallization processes of all-inorganic perovskite CsPbX3 (X=I, Br, Cl) during the one-step spinning procedure. The CsPbI3 perovskite can only form non-perovskite phases from the precursor during spinning, while the incorporation of GA+, Br- and Cl- can significantly promote the formation of the perovskite α-phase from the precursor state (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2019, 7, 27640-27647; Nano Energy, 2020, 75, 104933). Besides, we further studied the perovskite film formation process during the two-step fabrication procedure. The phase transition from the hexagonal PbI2 phase to the perovskite phase was unveiled through in-situ GIWAXS measurements, which is quite different from the one-step spinning process. Interestingly, the doping of Cs+ in the first step can induce the formation of δ-CsPbI3 phase, while the doping of GA+ in the second step can promote the phase transition from δ‐CsPbI3 to the perovskite α‐phase (Adv. Mater. 2020, 32, 2004630). In the light of fruitful in-situ GIWAXS results of perovskite films and abundant ex situ characterizations (objective 4), we have obtained an in-depth understanding of perovskite formation mechanisms and concluded the correlation between process, structure, and device performance. For the mixed perovskite (FAPbI3)0.83(MAPbBr3)0.17 deposited by the one-step spin-coating method, we found that it is important to avoid the formation of hexagonal polytypes (4H, 6H) in stage III during the crystallization process, which can be achieved by annealing the as-cast film immediately after the CB dripping during the second stage of the crystallization process. Otherwise, the device efficiency will drop from 19% to 14%. Remarkably, the incorporation of Cs+ can suppress the formation of hexagonal polytypes (4H, 6H) during the film formation process as well, thus improving the device efficiency as well as the device reproducibility (Adv. Mater. 2019, 31, 1901284). For the formation mechanisms of all-inorganic perovskite CsPbX3 (X=I, Br, Cl) during the one-step spinning process, it was found that an enhanced direct phase transition from precursor to the perovskite α-phase and suppression of the formation of yellow-phase are prerequisites to achieving high-efficiency devices. A-site cations such as GA+ and X-site anions such as Br- and Cl- can promote the formation of the perovskite α-phase and inhibit the appearance of yellow-phase, hence delivering a higher efficiency over 17% for all-inorganic PSCs (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2019, 7, 27640-27647; Nano Energy, 2020, 75, 104933). As for the two-step spinning process, we employed a sequential A-site doping procedure in the second step to precisely control the perovskite crystallization kinetics. As a result, the perovskite film has a larger crystal grain size of 1 um, higher crystallinity and reduced density. Consequently, efficient PSCs have been achieved. During the progressing of this project, we also established good collaborations with several teams in mainland China and obtained interesting results in terms of PSCs (Adv. Funct. Mater. 2019, 29, 1900092; Nano Energy, 2020, 75, 104933; Adv. Energy Mater. 2018, 8, 1702498), organic solar cells (Nat. Commun. 2019, 10, 2152; Adv. Mater. 2018, 30, 1706571), organic transistors (Adv. Mater. 2018, 30, 1705745; Chem. Mater. 2018, 30, 7988−8001), etc.

14314216.label: Major findings and research outcome
14314216.value: Through this project, we published 46 publications in peer-reviewed journals and presented our results 8 times in local and international conferences (part C). Overall, our results provided guidelines and insights for precisely controlling the perovskite crystallization kinetic toward high-efficiency perovskite solar cells. Major finding 1: We first reported and improved the long-term stability of the perovskite precursor solution by incorporating small molecule ITIC-Th, suggesting a new route toward future high-efﬁciency solar cells - incorporating organic non-fullerene acceptors and halide perovskite materials into the same active layer. Major finding 2: We revealed the detailed crystallization process of mixed perovskites (FAPbI3)0.83(MAPbBr3)0.17 during one-step spin-coating by in-situ GIWAXS measurements for the first time, while the Cs+ doping can bypass the formation of secondary phases, thereby significantly extending the annealing window and improving device efficiency. Major finding 3: We investigated the crystallization pathway of a benchmark FAxMA1-xPb(IxBr1-x)3 perovskite throughout the whole two-step spin-coating process through in-situ GIWAXS measurements, and the sequential A-site doping of Cs+ and GA+ can finely control the perovskite crystallization process. Our work demonstrated the feasibility of fine‐tuning the crystallization pathways using sequential A‐site doping in the two‐step fabrication to fabricate high-performance photovoltaic devices. Major finding 4: We systematically studied the crystallization processes of all-inorganic perovskite CsPbX3 (X=I, Br, Cl), and found that an enhanced direct phase transition from precursor to the perovskite α-phase and suppression of the formation of yellow-phase are prerequisites to achieving high-efficiency devices.

14314216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14314216.value: 1. Extending the in-situ characterization of perovskite films to in-operando characterization of perovskite devices. A proposal was just submitted in the 2021-22 GRF practice. 2. Extending perovskite crystallization research on lead-free perovskite systems such as the tin-based perovskite. A better understanding of the crystallization kinetic will enable us to further improve the device performance based on lead-free perovskites. We are working on the optimization of tin-based perovskite solar cells, and an efficiency > 6% has been achieved.

14314216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14314216.value: Perovskite solar cells are emerging as one of the most promising competitors to silicon solar cells with certified efficiencies over 25%. A decent device efficiency requires the formation of high-quality perovskite films, which largely depends on the crystallization kinetics of perovskite crystals. This project utilizes the state-of-the-art in-situ X-ray scattering techniques to systematically investigate the crystallization and film formation processes of various perovskite systems under different fabrication conditions. It reveals underlying reasons for the time-sensitive of fabricating mixed-perovskite devices, the roles of cations and halides on the crystallization kinetics of all-inorganic perovskites, and the precise control through sequential A-site doping during the two-step deposition process. The findings in this project provide insightful guidelines for manipulating the perovskite crystallization pathways toward higher device performance.

14314516.label: Project Objectives
14314516.value: Investigate the open mirror theorem and open crepant resolution conjecture for compact toric orbifolds. Relate bulk-deformed Lagrangian Floer theory and open Gromov-Witten invariants to closed mirror symmetry. Explore the relation between open mirror symmetry and homological mirror symmetry.
rows: Investigate the open mirror theorem and open crepant resolution conjecture for compact toric orbifolds.
Relate bulk-deformed Lagrangian Floer theory and open Gromov-Witten invariants to closed mirror symmetry.
Explore the relation between open mirror symmetry and homological mirror symmetry.

14314516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14314516.value: This project continues the PI's study of open Gromov-Witten theory and its application to mirror symmetry for toric varieties from the SYZ perspective. Mirror symmetry is a striking and mysterious duality between the algebraic geometry and symplectic geometry on two different Calabi-Yau (CY) manifolds. Since its discovery in the early 1990s, mathematicians have been striving extremely hard to crack the secret mechanism behind it. In 1996, Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed an elegant and convincing geometric explanation for mirror symmetry. They suggest that mirror CY manifolds should admit dual Lagrangian torus fibrations and mirror symmetry can be explained as a geometric Fourier-type transform. Since then, quantum corrections such as open and closed Gromov-Witten (GW) invariants have been playing a vital role in the study of this conjecture and mirror symmetry. This project is a continuation of a previous one, in which the PI aimed at a solid understanding of mirror symmetry for toric manifolds via an in-depth study of quantum corrections. The first goal of the current project is to extend our previous results to the orbifold setting, and apply it to establish an open-string version of the crepant transformation conjecture, which is a very important problem in Gromov-Witten theory. The PI also plans to extend the study of the relation between period integrals, quantum cohomology and open GW theory to the “big” case. To do this, we must study Fukaya, Oh, Ohta and Ono's bulk-deformed Lagrangian Floer theory and the corresponding open Gromov-Witten invariants with interior marked point insertions. The PI will develop new techniques to compute these invariants, and apply the results to understand the relation between them, period integrals and big quantum cohomology. On the other hand, building on his previous work on homological mirror symmetry (HMS) for toric CY manifolds, the PI would like to study the predicted equalities between the A- and B-model topological string amplitudes from a geometric viewpoint. The SYZ conjecture provides a way to canonically build a geometric functor realizing HMS. Together with the SYZ transform which exchanges the de Rham and Dolbeault complexes, this should lead to a better understanding of the mysterious and somewhat surprising equalities. 本項目將繼續PI在開格羅莫夫-威滕（Gromov-Witten）理論的研究，以及它在環簇的SYZ鏡對稱的應用。 鏡對稱是兩個不同的卡拉比-丘（Calabi-Yau）流形上的代數幾何與辛幾何的一個驚人而且神秘的對偶現象。自20世紀90年代早期發現後，數學家一直致力破解它背後的神秘機制。 1996年，Strominger，丘成桐和Zaslow提出了一個優雅而又令人信服的鏡像對稱的幾何解釋。他們認為，一對鏡對稱卡拉比-丘流形應該有對偶的拉格朗日圓環纖維結構，而且鏡對稱應理解為一種廣義的傅立葉變換。量子修正（例如開和閉的格羅莫夫-威滕不變量）一直在這個猜想和鏡對稱的研究中起著至關重要的作用。 本項目的PI的前一個項目的延續，因此PI將繼續通過對量子修正的深入研究去理解環簇的鏡對稱。本項目的第一個目標是將我們以前的結果推廣到orbifold的情形，並將其應用於開crepant變換猜想的證明，這是在格羅莫夫-威滕理論一個非常重要的問題。 本項目的PI還計劃將其對期間積分，量子上同調，以及開格羅莫夫-威滕理論之間的關係的研究推廣到“大”的情況。要做到這一點，我們必須進一步理解Fukaya，Oh，Ohta和Ono的拉格朗日弗洛爾的體積變形理論和相應的開格羅莫夫-威滕不變量。本項目的PI將研發新的技術來計算這些不變量，並將結果應用於理解他們跟期間積分和大量子上同調之間的關係。 另一方面，建立於本項目的PI之前在環卡拉比-丘流形的上同調鏡對稱的工作，我們希望從幾何觀點研究A-和B-模型上的拓撲弦振幅之間的等式。SYZ猜想提供了一個自然的辦法去建構一個幾何函子去實現HMS。加上SYZ變換以及它能交換的de Rham和Dolbeault複合鏈，這應能使我們對那些神秘而令人驚訝的等式有更深入的了解。

14314516.label: Realisation of objectives
14314516.value: The first objective of this project was to investigate the open mirror theorem and open crepant resolution conjecture for compact toric orbifolds. We have completely solved these problems in the Gorenstein case. In the PI’s previous project (RGC Ref No. 404412), we successfully applied the capping-off trick to certain partial compactifications of toric Calabi-Yau manifolds/orbifolds to prove some very powerful open-closed equalities for orbifold disk invariants (i.e., genus 0 open orbifold Gromov-Witten invariants), which enabled us to deduce an open-string version of the mirror theorem and hence a proof of the Gross-Siebert conjecture which in particular gives an enumerative meaning to the inverse mirror map. We were also able to establish an open-string version of Ruan's crepant resolution conjecture (CRC) for all toric Calabi-Yau orbifolds in any dimension. In another work, we related disk invariants (i.e., genus 0 open Gromov-Witten invariants) of a compact toric semi-Fano manifold to those of its Seidel spaces. This novel construction allows us to give an effective and complete computation of all the disk invariants for a general compact semi-Fano toric manifold of any dimension, which leads to various profound applications in mirror symmetry. In the current project, the PI and collaborators continued to apply the capping-off and partial compactification trick to compact Gorenstein semi-Fano toric orbifolds. The key new insight and also the main reason for the applicability of this trick is the discovery that computation of the orbifold disk invariants actually only depends on local contributions, as we have anticipated in the proposal of this project. This allows us to obtain generalizations of all the results in the previous project to the orbifold case. On the other hand, the PI has attempted to construct the SYZ mirror for a toric Calabi-Yau manifold using instanton corrections coming from Woodward’s quasimap Floer theory, instead of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono’s Lagrangian Floer theory. We found that the resulting SYZ mirror is precisely equal to the one predicted by physicists (Hori-Vafa, Hori-Iqbal-Vafa and others) and the mirror maps are completely trivial in this case. This is in line with the expectation, but no proof was given prior to our work. The second objective of this project was to relate bulk-deformed Lagrangian Floer theory and open Gromov-Witten invariants to closed mirror symmetry. The work we did in the current project has pointed to a precise conjecture, namely, the bulk-deformed Lagrangian Floer superpotential should give precisely the primitive form in the mirror Landau-Ginzburg theory. However, a proof of this conjecture still seems out of reach. We expect that the eventual proof requires a more detailed analysis of the moduli spaces of holomorphic disks, and more importantly, the relation between these moduli spaces. To understand such moduli spaces, we first attempted to investigate their tropical analogues, building on pioneering works of Floer, Fukaya-Oh and Mikhalkin. In a joint work with Ma, the PI combined techniques from a previous project (RGC Ref No. 14302015) with the tropical analogue of open Gromov-Witten theory for toric Fano surfaces to deduce a new interpretation of the so-called tropical vertex group. More precisely, we show how one can equip the tropical vertex group with a Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) structure, and then we apply techniques from asymptotic analysis to study the solutions of the Maurer-Cartan equation associated to the corresponding differential-graded BV algebra. Our main result says that semi-classical limits of Fourier modes of a specific class of Maurer-Cartan solutions naturally give rise to tropical disks in the toric surface with Maslov index 0 or 2, the latter of which produces a universal unfolding of the mirror superpotential. This explains various phenomena such as the wall-crossing formula for disk counting invariants, and gives new understanding of the bulk-deformed Lagrangian Floer superpotential. The third objective of this project was to explore the relation between open mirror symmetry and homological mirror symmetry. We have actually changed our perspective a bit and set an even more ambitious goal, namely, to obtain some geometric meanings of mirror symmetry which are beyond the reach of homological mirror symmetry. As a first testing case, we look at the A-model open string theory on the mirror of a toric variety (not the toric variety itself) and apply it to give a new solution of a well-known problem in geometric quantization, namely, whether the Hilbert space depends on the choice of a polarization. By applying SYZ transforms twice, we successfully prove that the invariance of polarization is actually a consequence of SYZ mirror symmetry. Along the way, we also discover that the limiting behavior of the Hilbert spaces associated to a family of complex polarizations which tend to a real polarization is precisely dictated by the Witten deformation on the base of the Lagrangian torus fibration (or the toric moment map). This builds a bridge linking mirror symmetry with quantization, and somehow forms the basis for one of the PI’s subsequent projects.

14314516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14314516.value: The first major finding is that the orbifold disk invariants (i.e., genus 0 open orbifold Gromov-Witten invariants) only depend on local contributions coming from Chern number zero rational curves (or sphere bubblings) connected to the relevant toric divisor. This discovery allows the extension of previous techniques such as the capping-off trick and partial compactification technique to the compact orbifold setting, thus enabling us to prove generalizations of the open mirror theorem and open-string crepant resolution conjecture for all Gorenstein compact semi-Fano toric orbifolds of any dimension. The second major finding is a relation between the so-called quasimap SYZ mirror, constructed using instanton corrections (i.e., open-string Gromov-Witten—type invariants defined by moduli spaces of open quasimaps) coming from Woodward's quasimap Floer theory and the usual SYZ mirror, constructed using genus 0 open Gromov-Witten invariants coming from Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono's Lagrangian Floer theory, in the case of a toric Calabi-Yau manifold. Such a relation can be regarded as an open-string analogue of Hori-Vafa’s work on a physical proof of mirror symmetry for toric varieties, and as such, gives a new perspective on the understanding of their work. The third major finding is a new link between tropical geometry and deformation theory. The PI and Ma applied the philosophy that asymptotic analysis of the Maurer-Cartan equation associated to a (sheaf of) differential graded Lie algebras over an integral affine manifold (with singularities) will in general give rise to tropical objects to the mirror symmetry between a toric surface and its mirror Landau-Ginzburg model. We proved that semi-classical limits of the Fourier modes of Maurer-Cartan solutions of the extended deformation theory of the Landau-Ginzburg model naturally give rise to tropical disks of Maslov indices 0 and 2 in the original toric surface. This has led to a new direction for further studies. Finally, the PI and his student applied SYZ transforms in the toric case to solve the invariance of polarization problem in geometric quantization for toric manifolds. This opens up an entirely new chapter on the relationship between mirror symmetry and quantization. We expect that this would lead to a lot of future research works.

14314516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14314516.value: To prove the conjecture that the bulk-deformed Lagrangian Floer superpotential of a toric manifold gives rise to precisely the primitive form in the mirror Landau-Ginzburg model, we need a very deep understanding of the relation between different moduli spaces of holomorphic disks. We shall further develop and make use of the link between tropical geometry and Gromov-Witten theory to help search for the correct relations. On the other hand, and perhaps more importantly, such an investigation would be crucial if we want a much deeper understanding of mirror symmetry. This is expected to yield new results even beyond the toric case as well. Certainly the most interesting case should be mirror symmetry for compact Calabi-Yau manifolds. Exploring further geometric meanings of mirror symmetry which are beyond the reach of homological mirror symmetry is another area of almost uncharted waters. It would be very interesting to see how SYZ mirror symmetry and related techniques can be applied to problems related to subjects like stability conditions and behavior of Calabi-Yau metrics. To remain in the realm of toric geometry, the next step could be studying hypertoric varieties – these have been studied intensively by both mathematicians and physicists in recent years.

14314516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14314516.value: Mirror symmetry is a highly nontrivial and mysterious duality between the symplectic geometry of a space and the complex geometry of a completely different space. It was discovered by string theorists in the early 1990s. It has led to numerous surprising and deep mathematical conjectures. Since its discovery, mathematicians have been working very hard to try to understand the mechanism of mirror symmetry. A breakthrough came in 1996 when Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed that mirror symmetry should be understood as a geometric Fourier transform. Lying at the heart of the SYZ conjecture is the role played by quantum corrections, which is the key to explain the miraculous power of mirror symmetry. In the toric setting, quantum corrections are exactly given by disk invariants. Our full computation of these invariants for a general Gorenstein compact semi-Fano toric orbifold of any dimension therefore plays a crucial role in the study of mirror symmetry. Our results provide important insight on how quantum corrections dictate the geometry of mirror symmetry and explain why it has been so powerful in making enumerative predictions.

14315616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14315616.value: Even though single and multicrystalline silicon solar cells have dominated the photovoltaic commercial market with a module efficiency of about 18% for years, Cu(InGa)Se2 (CIGS) solar cell is becoming more and more attractive since it can not only be produced in thin film form at low-cost but has also demonstrated the highest cell conversion efficiency of 21.7% among all thin film technologies, even higher than the record conversion efficiency of multicrystalline silicon solar cell (20.7%). Despite the success of photovoltaic devices, the solar cell efficiency level must be further raised in order to economically compete with the traditional energy using fossil fuels and hydropower. The limit of solar energy to electric energy conversion is mostly related to the spectral mismatch of incident solar photon energy to the band gap of a solar cell. Due to thermalization and recombination effect, almost all solar cells have a low response to the short wavelength light. For CIGS solar cell, this problem is particularly serious considering the strong useless absorption by the common CdS buffer layer to photons of energy larger than 2.4 eV, equivalently with wavelength shorter than 520 nm. The intensity of solar light with wavelength shorter than 520 nm is still high (`20%) and the use of this wasted energy is an attractive scientific issue. Luminescent down conversion materials, which can absorb short-wavelength light and re-emit it at longer wavelengths, can provide a promising way to circumvent the above problem. There are two ways to realize photon down conversion. The first is down shifting, which can shift one photon from high energy to lower energy and thus effectively reduce the surface recombination losses and the CdS buffer layer losses. The other is quantum cutting, which is more attractive since it can transfer one high energy photon to two useful near-infrared photons and thus can effectively outperform the Shockley-Queisser limit of 30% efficiency to as high as 39% according to theoretical calculation. In this project, rare earth doped quantum cutting materials and down shifting materials such as carbon dots will be prepared and their luminescent properties will be optimized to suit for down conversion application on CIGS solar cells. Furthermore, the influence of down conversion layer on the overall photovoltaic performance of CIGS solar cell will be optimized. Through our study, we expect to bring new understanding for down conversion effect and to provide guidance for further improvement of CIGS solar cell efficiency. 雖然單晶矽和多晶矽太陽能電池以18%的模組轉換效率主導商業光伏市場多年，但是銅銦鎵硒太陽能電池正受到越來越多的重視，作為薄膜太陽能電池的代表，不僅生產成本低，而且它的轉換效率也是所有薄膜技術裡最高的，達到了21.7%，甚至高於多晶矽太陽能電池的效率。雖然光伏技術已經在許多方面取得成功，但是為了提升太陽能電池相對于傳統化石能源和水力發電的市場競爭力，太陽能電池的效率水準仍亟待進一步提高。太陽能轉化為電能的主要限制因素在於入射太陽光譜與太陽能電池有效吸收光譜之間的失配。由於熱弛豫和複合的影響，幾乎所有的太陽能電池對短波長光的利用都較差。對於銅銦鎵硒太陽能電池，這個問題會顯得尤為嚴重，這是因為CdS緩衝層的帶隙約為2.4eV，會強烈吸收波長小於520nm的光子，而CdS的這部分吸收並不能轉化為電能，並且太陽光中波長小於520nm光子的能量還是相當可觀（約占總能量20%），如何有效利用這部分被浪費的能量仍是一個非常吸引人的學術課題。 下轉換發光材料，這種材料可以吸收短波長的光，再發射出長波長的的光，被很多人認為具有克服以上問題的潛力。實現下轉化有兩種方法：第一種是下轉移，就是把一個高能量的光子轉變成一個低能量的光子，這樣可以有效減少表面複合和CdS緩衝層吸收造成的損失。另一個是量子裁剪，這種方法更具有吸引力，因為這種方法可以把一個高能量的光子轉換成兩個有用的近紅外光子，根據理論計算可以有效突破Shockley-Queisser的30%的效率極限使理論效率極限達到39%。在該項目中，我們會用稀土摻雜的方式製備量子剪裁材料並製備碳量子點作為下轉移材料，再優化它們的發光性能使之適合作為銅銦鎵硒電池的下轉化層。此外，下轉換層如何影響銅銦鎵硒太陽能電池的光伏性能也會得到深入研究從而作出優化。通過這些研究，我們希望對於下轉換層在太陽能電池上的作用得到新的認識，並為銅銦鎵硒太陽能電池效率的進一步提高提供思路。

14315616.label: Realisation of objectives
14315616.value: Even though Cu(InGa)Se2 (CIGS) solar cell is becoming more and more attractive since it can not only be produced in thin film form at low-cost but has also demonstrated the highest cell conversion efficiency of 23.4% among all thin film technologies (2018) (perovskite solar cell has recently exceeded CIGS in terms of the highest cell conversion efficiency), even higher than the record conversion efficiency of multicrystalline silicon solar cell (23.2%). The limit of solar energy to electric energy conversion is mostly related to the spectral mismatch of incident solar photon energy to the band gap of a solar cell. Due to thermalization and surface recombination effects, almost all solar cells have a low response to the short wavelength light. For CIGS solar cell, this problem is particularly serious considering the strong useless absorption by the common CdS buffer layer to photons of energy larger than 2.4 eV, equivalently with wavelength shorter than 520 nm. Luminescent down conversion materials, which can absorb short-wavelength light and re-emit it at longer wavelengths, can provide a promising way to circumvent the above problem. There are two ways to realize photon down conversion. The first is down shifting, which can shift one photon from high energy to lower energy and thus effectively reduce the surface recombination losses and the CdS buffer layer losses. The other is quantum cutting, which is more attractive since it can transfer one high energy photon into two useful near-infrared photons and thus can effectively outperform the Shockley-Queisser limit of 30% efficiency to as high as 39% according to theoretical calculation. In this project, the objectives are the following 1. To design and synthesis down conversion materials such as CaSc2O4: Ce3+/ Yb3+, YAG: Ce3+/Yb3+ , and carbon dots 2. To optimize the photoluminescence quantum yields and the excitation and emission spectra to make it more suitable for application to CIGS solar cell 3. To optimize the effect of down conversion on the overall CIGS solar cell performance For down shifting, we have chosen Ce-doped Y3Al5O12 (Ce3+:YAG) ceramics which has a good spectral matching and high luminescent efficiency. By properly designing the optical structures to integrate the down-conversion material with the CIGS solar cell, the fluorescent photons are efficiently guided to the CIGS absorber layer in addition to eliminating the scattering and maintaining the antireflection (AR) for incident light, addressing objectives 1-3 all together for this material. The Y3Al5O12:Ce3+ ceramic down converter on CIGS solar cells can bring an enhancement of 0.53 mA/cm2 to the short-circuit current density solely from down conversion, which is responsible for the major increase in energy conversion efficiency from 18.5% to 19.0%. As shown in Publication #1, a positive down-conversion effect is demonstrated over AR layer-coated CIGS solar cells without misclaiming contributions from other accompanied effects or jeopardizing any other accompanying effects. For quantum cutting material, we have chosen Yb doped perovskite CsPbX3 quantum dots (PQDs) which are emerged as the most competitive luminescent material recently. Benefited from its size and composition dependent bandgap, the spectral conversion is controllable and convenient. Moreover, thanks to the introduction of Yb ions, the formed defect state is just twice of the Yb’s excitation energy, thus quantum cutting could be achieved in this energy transfer process. In our work, Yb doped mixed halides (Cl/Br) are synthesized to match the absorption bands, and over 130% Photoluminescence Quantum Yield (PLQY) has been achieved, indicating the efficient energy transfer process from the PQDs to RE ions. While this material is promising and should provide a positive effect for the solar cell, some optimizations in terms of the optimizations on optical properties and controlling of the film deposition process have not completed yet. Due to the Covid-19 pandemic, our continued work in Wuhan University has been severely delayed. Thus, only the preliminary results are written in the Thesis by Dr. Zhiyu Xiong. The above results were published in one paper in Solar RRL (publication #1) and the rest is in a working paper. We regard that all the objectives are well achieved for the spectral down shifting material and further work need to be done for the quantum cutting material. While there are quite a number of researchers have participated in this work, a Ph. D student was successfully trained.

14315616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14315616.value: There are plenty of reports on the study of down-conversion materials; however, more is said than done in this area and most of the previous works only demonstrate a theoretical potential rather than a device reality. In the rare-earth-doped phosphors we have chosen: Ce-doped Y3Al5O12, we indeed found its appropriate absorption of short-wavelength photons and efficient emission of long-wavelength photons with high fluorescence quantum efficiency. However, we discovered that the micrometer-sized particles form of this material, once applied on the top of a solar cell as a down-conversion layer, would strongly scatter light and significantly reduce the amount of light entering the absorber of the solar cell, and thus decrease the conversion efficiency. Even dispersing these particles in glass or plastic matrix with sizeable refractive index mismatch, the scattering effect remains strong and no improvement of conversion efficiency can be achieved at the device level. Therefore, we have to use YAG itself as the matrix to host the luminescent particles to reduce scattering and index matching fluid between down-converter and solar cell to transmit most of the luminescent light into the absorber. Such a device level design and understanding is crucial for down conversion to benefit improvement of solar cell conversion efficiency. These observations and findings were presented in publication #1 and conference presentation. . In publication #1, we have demonstrated for the first time that an overall enhancement of conversion efficiency can be achieved over AR-layer-coated CIGS solar cells with a clear and significant positive down-conversion contribution using a YAG:Ce3+ ceramic slide as the spectral down converter. The down- conversion effect has led to a short-circuit current density increase by 0.53 mA/cm2 , and a solar energy conversion efficiency increases from 18.5% to 19.0%. Using Yb doped CsPbX3 quantum dots as quantum cutting material, we have observed a quantum efficiency of emission ~130%, a good sign in use of down-converter for solar cells. At this stage, we are not able to make an overall positive effect in enhancing CIGS solar cell efficiency due to: i) strong absorption of light due to Yb ions at the emission wavelength which reduces the original external quantum efficiency at ~980nm. Stronger quantum cutting effect may help to reduce such drawbacks; ii) better optical design to make use of the luminescent light which emits in other directions away from the forward. The findings here were summarized in Dr. Xiong's Thesis.

14315616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14315616.value: Quantum cutting that can convert a high energy photon (short wavelength) into two low energy photons (long wavelength) is attractive for better use of solar radiation energy. Finding a suitable material that can absorb all the short wavelength light below a predesignated value and emit luminescent light in the region where the solar cell has a high external quantum efficiency is the first step. Managing most if not all the luminescent light to propagate into the light absorber material of the solar cell is the subsequent step. With our initial success in Yb doped perovskite CsPbX3 quantum dots (PQDs), we should pursue this direction by further increase the quantum cutting efficiency to close to ~200% from the present 130% level. Afterwards, we should deposit such PQDs in appropriate form on the solar cell and ensure the luminescent light to propagate forward into the light absorber layer of the solar cell. In the end, we could achieve an overall better energy conversion efficiency for the solar cells.

14315616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14315616.value: To make better use of the solar spectral radiation by a solar cell is always a key direction of solar cell research. Due to thermalization and surface recombination effects, almost all solar cells have a low response to the short wavelength light. For Cu(InGa)Se2 (CIGS) solar cell, this problem is particularly serious considering the strong useless absorption by the commonly used CdS buffer layer for photons of energy larger than 2.4 eV, equivalently of wavelength shorter than 520 nm. In this study, we used a down conversion concept to efficiently convert the short wavelength light in the solar spectrum to relatively long wavelength where the external quantum efficiency of the solar cells is high. Using Ce-doped Y3Al5O12 (Ce3+:YAG) as spectral down shifting material and Yb doped CsPbX3 quantum dots as quantum cutting material, both of which can convert short wavelength light into relatively long wavelength light with an overall high quantum efficiency, we have demonstrated that an increase of overall solar cell conversion efficiency can be achieved. To make the effect well used, a good design of the optical structure between the down-converter and the CIGS solar cell was shown necessary.

14315716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14315716.value: 這個擬議工作的目的是開發一類新的兩性離子有機催化劑作為有機合成中的有力工具。 在化學合成中，使用有機小分子作為催化劑是一個新興的研究領域。有機催化劑被認為是一個金屬催化劑的替代物，並且在綠色化學工業中具吸引力。在現代有機催化劑的設計中，雙功能體系是被普遍採用，因為它可以幫助使底物和反應中間體在較低的動力學屏障下接近。 在許多現有的雙官能有機催化劑系統中，氫鍵供體是經常存在的。比較之下，兩性離子有機催化劑，即在單個分子中具有一個正和一個負電荷，在一些情況下顯示出不尋常的反應性。但是，事實上它是一個鮮被利用但新穎的雙功能催化劑體系。 在我們的初步研究中，最近我們報導了採用基於硫化物的兩性離子作為高效催化劑並用於環狀有機化合物的合成（J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2012, 134, 16492)。然而，由於這催化劑穩定性低，使它在其他反應中不能被廣泛應用。儘管如此，在更近的未發表的作品，我們已經合成了一個結構穩定的兩性離子催化劑並將其應用在某些反應中。 基於此發現，在這個擬議的工作，我們計劃進一步發展，探索和應用這類新的兩性離子有機催化劑。預計這新的類催化劑可以在有機合成中成為一個功能強大的工具，可以在不同的反應中被利用。

14315716.label: Realisation of objectives
14315716.value: 1. Prepare a series of aminopyridine-based zwitterionic organocatalysts that are easily synthesized from aziridines. At the initial stage of the project, a series of amino-pyridine-based zwitterionic organocatalysts were prepared. Aziridines derived from cyclic alkenes (e.g., cyclopentene and cyclohexene) and aliphatic alkenes (e.g., styrene, stilbene) were used to prepared the zwitterionic catalysts. For the nucleophilic partners, a range of amines, pyridines, and imidazoles with different substituents were used. The reaction procedure started from aziridines, which were prepared from between alkenes and anhydrous chloroamine-T in the presence of catalytic amount of PTAB in acetonitrile. Alternatively, we also prepared the pyridinium-based zwitterionic organocatalysts from aziridines derived from epoxides. Aziridines were then opened by different nucleophilic partners to give the zwitterionic organocatalysts. By using a similar approach but changing the aziridines to isothiocyanates, a series of aminopyridine-based zwitterions were also prepared. 2. Study the stability of the newly prepared zwitterionic organocatalysts. The newly prepared zwitterions were tested in terms of their stability under different conditions. For instance, the catalysts were placed under ambient conditions. Also, the catalysts were also refluxed in various solvents and the catalysts were recovered. In addition, the compound was stable under basic or acidic condition. However, the zwitterionic organocatalysts that are derived from aliphatic backbones were found to be relatively structurally unstable. It appears that the zwitterions could cyclized back to the aziridine starting materials. We speculate that the release of high-ring strain in cyclic alkenes-derived aziridines due to the bicyclic systems could be the main driving force in the ring-opening of the structurally stable zwitterions. 3. Examine the catalytic ability of the catalysts in various organic transformations. The catalysts were utilized in a range of reactions. Their performance in the reactions were examined. Parameters such as reaction time, temperature, solvent, concentration, were evaluated. Two types of reactions were testified: activation of electrophiles and base-catalyzed reactions. Halogenation: Initially, the zwitterions were used in the electrophilic aromatic halogenation. To our delight, the halogenation of arenes containing electron-donating substituents such as alkoxy and benzyloxy proceeded smoothly to give the corresponding para-brominated products in excellent yields. In addition, 1,2-and 1,3-disubstituted and 1,3,5-trisubstituted substrates also gave the corresponding products with mono-bromination at the para position with respect to the alkoxyl substituent. Sterically hindered substrate was also compatible. For the 1,4-disubstituted substrate, the mono-bromination took place at the ortho position with respect to the methoxy group exclusively. Naphthyl substrates were found to work equally well. Other than the oxygen-substituted substrates, anilines were also found to be compatible with this catalytic protocol. Acetyl, benzyl, pivaloyl, and Boc anilines readily underwent the catalytic mono-bromination. Similar to the alkoxyarenes, the disubstituted phenyl system could be mono-brominated with excellent site selectivity. It was realized that aromatic bromination could be catalyzed smoothly with only very load catalyst loading (0.05 mol%). It is also notable that the bromination catalytic protocol could be easily scaled up and the catalyst loading could be further reduced. This advantage makes the present method more attractive for large-scale production in organic synthesis. In addition, the catalysts were applied to the amino-dibromination of nitroalkanes, which gave rise to a library of halo-nitroalkanes. Subsequent transformation of halo-nitroalkanes via oxidation furnished glycinamides, which are valuable motifs existing in pharmaceutically important peptides and natural products. Transesterification: Zwitterionic organocatalysts contain basic anions, which are potentially useful to activate alcohols for substitution reactions. Catalytic transesterification was then examined using the zwitterions. The catalytic performances of zwitterions in the transesterification of triglycerides to fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs, commonly known as biodiesel) were evaluated. The transesterification proceeded smoothly and the FAME was obtained in good yield at room temperature when zwitterions were used as the catalysts. The reaction efficiency was found to be highly dependent on the structurally rigidity and Bronsted basicity of the zwitterions. It was also found that the catalytic performance of the zwitterions was far superior to other existing catalytic systems. Since the zwitterions are aqueous soluble, FAME could be separated simply by aqueous washing to remove the glycerol and zwitterionic catalyst. In addition, the byproduct mixture containing glycerol (a glut byproduct from the production of biodiesel) and catalyst could undergo transesterification with ethyl acetate to give triacetin, which has various applications such as biodiesel additive, antiknock agent, food additive, and plasticizer. The zwitterionic catalyst could then be recycled and reused in the next round of FAME synthesis with similar performance. The catalytic protocol could also be applied to the transesterification of simple substrates. In general, the reaction worked well with various aliphatic alcohols bearing electron-donating or -withdrawing substituents. Functionalities including alkene, alkyne, and furan, which are sensitive to conventional acid-mediated transesterification conditions, were compatible with the zwitterion-catalyzed system to give the corresponding acetate products in good-to-excellent isolated yields. Acetylation of diols could also be achieved to yield diacetates smoothly. Interestingly, triacetylated sugar derivative was furnished in good isolated yield. It is worth mentioning that acetylation of alcohols, which is one of the most common protection methods, typically requires the use of acetyl chloride or acetic anhydride. In contrast, our approach can easily introduce the protecting group acetate into alcohols without acidic conditions. Interesting, the zwitterions could also catalyze the dehydrative esterification. A wide range of alcohols bearing electron-rich or electron-deficient substituents were found to be compatible and the corresponding diester products could be obtained in good isolated yields under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies such as DFT calculation were performed. It was found that the amide anion and the iminium cation activates the alcohol and the carbonyl group, respectively. The bifunctional catalyst activates the reaction partners simultaneously in a favorable interaction distance, leading to efficient transesterification without the use of strong base or acid. Halogenation with ammonium salts: During the study of zwitterionic catalysts, it was found that the electrostatic interaction between the cation of zwitterion and the substrate is crucial for the high catalytic performance. Later, it was unexpected to realize that simple ammonium cations could activate the electrophilic reagents and were able to effectively promote the ortho-selective electrophilic functionalization of phenols and anilines. The methodology is applicable to a wide range of substrates including BINOL. Selective ortho-functionalization of BINOL gives rise to many BINOL ligands, which are useful in various catalytic asymmetric reaction. In addition, the ammonium catalysts were found to be applicable to ortho-halogenate phenols in the synthesis of chiral bis-phenol ligands. 4. Publication of the results in world-class peer-reviewed international journals. Under this project, four high-impact publications (1 Org. Lett., 2 ACS Catal., 1 Chem) were generated. In addition, a manuscript has been submitted to Asian J. Org. Chem., which is under revision. The detail appears in Part C. Overall, all objectives have been fully realized and a summary of the major research outcomes is shown below.

14315716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14315716.value: 1. Zwitterion-catalyzed aromatic halogenation (Part C, output 1): A zwitterionic-salt-catalyzed electrophilic monobromination of arenes with high regioselectivity has been developed. Under mild reaction conditions, a wide range of monobrominated aromatic compounds can be obtained in excellent yields. The reaction can be operated using an extremely low catalyst loading (0.05 mol %) with the inexpensive brominating agent N-bromosuccinimide. The versatility of this catalytic protocol has been demonstrated by the scale-up reaction with a 0.01 mol % catalyst loading to provide the selectively halogenated compound in quantitative yield. 2. Zwitterion-catalyzed (trans)esterification reactions (Part C, output 3): A class of zwitterionic organocatalysts based on an amide anion/iminium cation charge pair has been developed. The zwitterions are easily prepared by reacting aziridines with aminopyridines. They are catalytically applicable to transesterifications and dehydrative esterifications. Mechanistic studies reveal that the amide anion and iminium cation work synergistically in activating the reaction partners. The reaction can be applied to large-scale synthesis of biodiesel under mild conditions. 3. Zwitterion-catalyzed amino-dibromination of nitroalkenes (Part C, output 5): Glycinamides are valuable building blocks of natural products and biological relevant molecules. Many existing methods for the synthesis of glycinamides rely on harsh conditions. In this work, a zwitterion-catalyzed aminobromination of nitroalkenes using N-bromosuccinimide as the Br source and the amide donor has been developed. The resulting aminobromide products are converted into glycinamides. 4. Ammonium salt catalysts electrophilic ortho-functionalization (Part C, output 2, 4): An ortho-selective ammonium chloride salt-catalyzed direct C−H monohalogenation of phenols and 1,1′-bi-2-naphthol (BINOL) with 1,3-dichloro-5,5-dimethylhydantoin as the chlorinating agent has been developed. The catalyst loading was low (down to 0.01 mol %) and the reaction conditions were very mild. A wide range of substrates including BINOLs were compatible with this catalytic protocol. Chlorinated BINOLs are useful synthons for the synthesis of a wide range of unsymmetrical 3-aryl BINOLs that are not easily accessible. In addition, the same catalytic system can facilitate the ortho-selective selenylation of phenols.

14315716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14315716.value: Transition metal catalyzed transformations are inevitably the major sector in catalysis. Ligands are crucial in dictating the catalytic performance including reactivity, efficiency and even selectivity. Zwitterions are an emerging class of organocatalysts that have been utilized in some reactions and exhibited unusual reactivity and selectivity (see section 6.1). Unlike many other bifunctional catalyst systems that rely on neutral functionalities, zwitterions involve site-isolation of the positively and negatively charged partners in the same molecules. Stronger cationic and anionic partners can be achieved if the charge pair is not in conjugation so that they can operate synergistically in the catalytic reactions without self-neutralization through charge delocalization. However, the use of zwitterions as ligands in transition metal catalysis is under-exploited. During the research activity, it was realized that the zwitterions can be used as ligands to coordinate to metal in organometallic catalysis. In future, we will further explore the application of zwitterions in organometallic catalysis.

14315716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14315716.value: Many chemical manufacturing processes are energy- and atom-inefficient, leading to the generation of significant amount of wastes and emissions. To meet the growing demand on energy for the global economy, it becomes more important than ever to look for green alternatives of energy-efficient processes. However, the current state of technology lags behind the schedule to meet the international targets. Small molecule catalysts are considered as nanoscale molecular machines that can provide control in various transformations at molecular level. Catalysis underpins many industries as over 90% of chemicals produced rely on the use of a catalyst to certain extent. It is obvious that catalytic processes play a key role in improving air and water quality, reduce energy consumption and emission, and offer solutions to long-term sustainable energy and environmental protection. In the current project, we have developed a number of industrially useful catalytic protocols based on zwitterions. Our work on the novel catalysis provides a very useful tool for various transformations. In addition, organocatalysis is mild and metal-free, which are attractive features to the manufacturing sectors. The research endeavor results in the synthesis of a wide range of useful building blocks for various medicinal and chemical applications.

14316516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14316516.value: The PI proposes to continue her study on the relation among Floer theories arising from gauge theory settings and sympletic geometry. The Seiberg-Witten Floer homology (HM), the Heegaard Floer homology (HF), the embedded contact homology (ECH)/(PFH) are three Floer homologies that form important tools in low-dimensional topology and symplectic/contact topology. Though arising from very different origins and each better suited for different purposes, they are formally parallel and in fact expected to be equivalent. In the case of closed 3-manifolds, (HF), (ECH), (PFH) are all shown to be equivalent to (different verions) of (HM). Among the three equivalence theorems, the first and the last are proved by the proposer and her coauthors cite{KLT}; cite{LT}, and the second by Taubes cite{T:ECH}. The relation of these theories has deep consequences. However, the Floer homology for closed 3-manifolds is only the first element in a big package of invariants, such as invariants for closed 4-manifolds, 4-dimensional cobordisms, invariant for contact structures on 3-manifolds, knots, and 3-manifolds with boundary with certain prescribed boundary data. (Not all above are completely developed in three theories). The theories acquire wider applications with this larger framework. In this project, the proposer intends to study the three theories' relations for 3-manifolds with boundary through the construction of certain filtered Floer homologies of sutured 3-manifolds. 本計畫將繼續探討 Seiberg-Witten Floer homology (HM), Heegaard Floer homology (HF), the embedded contact homology (ECH)/(PFH) 衍生的一些低維流型不變量之間的關係。這些不變量是當今低維拓撲研究和星幾何與contact topology的重要工具。 在之前的研究中，計劃主持人與他的合作者證明了前二者的 Floer homology for closed 3-manifolds 是等價的。在本計劃中我們希望能推廣這些結果到 3-manifolds with boundary.

The first, long paper addresses the technical foundation, and has wide applications beyond the scope of this project. It has been submitted to J. Diff. Geom. The second paper is currently under preparation. As mentioned in the proposal, the second object is unlikely to be achieved in the duration of the award. We are still working towards this goal. The progress has been slowed partly due to the following reasons: The PI was unable to fully concentrate on this project: she needed to finish the writing and revise papers generated from the previous project, on which this project depends. In the final year of this award, the PI started a new, ambitious collaborative project which is very far from this project. She had to spend much time on this new project in order to keep up with the progress of her collaborators. In addition, the PI had problems finding appropriate postdocs to help with her research. A postdoc had only been found four months before the end of this award. The political turmoil in Hong Kong and the Covid pandemic also impeded the progress.

To show that the aforementioned "tilde" version of sutured $HM$ Floer homology is equivalent to Juhasz's sutured Floer homology, and in the case of knot complements, the system is equivalent to the full system of Ozsvath-Szabo's Heegaard knot Floer homologies. (Note: this part will likely take longer than 3 years to complete and may form parts of future projects).

14316516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14316516.value: The PI continued her study on the relation among Floer theories arising from gauge theory settings and sympletic geometry. The Seiberg-Witten Floer homology (HM), the Heegaard Floer homology (HF), the embedded contact homology (ECH)/(PFH) are three Floer homologies that form important tools in low-dimensional topology and symplectic/contact topology. Though arising from very different origins and each better suited for different purposes, they are formally parallel and in fact, expected to be equivalent. In the case of closed 3-manifolds, (HF), (ECH), (PFH) are all shown to be equivalent to (different versions) of (HM). Among the three equivalence theorems, the first and the last are proved by the proposer and her coauthors cite{KLT}; cite{LT}, and the second by Taubes cite{T:ECH}. The relation of these theories has deep consequences. However, the Floer homology for closed 3-manifolds is only the first element in a big package of invariants, such as invariants for closed 4-manifolds, 4-dimensional cobordisms, invariant for contact structures on 3-manifolds, knots, and 3-manifolds with boundary with certain prescribed boundary data. (Not all above are completely developed in three theories). The theories acquire wider applications with this larger framework. In this project, the PI studied the three theories' relations for 3-manifolds with boundary through the construction of certain filtered Floer homologies of sutured 3-manifolds.

14316716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14316716.value: Na ion batteries (NIBs) are promising alternatives for Lithium ion batteries (LIBs) mainly due to the Na abundance and low cost. A big challenge in the development of NIB is to find suitable anode materials. Sn-P based composite appears as a most promising anode material system due to the high capacity of both Sn and P, and the synergistic effect between the two. However, the reversible capacity, rate performance and cycle life of Sn-P based NIB anode are limited by the low electronic conductivity of the binary Sn-P phases, the aggregation of Sn and the stress built up during charge-discharge cycles, as well as the chemical instability of the sodiated phosphorus containing phases. Our preliminary work on Sn-P composite shows that the anode cyclability can be largely improved by introducing metallic element(s) inert to sodiation (e.g. Co). Based on these findings, we propose in this RGC/GRF project, to introduce a third metallic element to the Sn-P phase to form ternary composites with controlled composition, size, and morphology. The electrically conductive, mechanically ductile metallic component can provide an effective matrix to bridge Sn-P phases (of low electronic conductivity), prevent Sn aggregation, accommodate stress induced by volume change, and stabilize the sodiated phosphorus containing phases. In addition, the presence of specific metallic elements may promote the glass formation (i.e. amorphization) of the Sn-based alloys, which can speeds up the Na+ kinetics and enhances the cyclability via release of structural stress associated with sodiation/desodiation. Moreover, morphology control of the ternary composites (e.g. porous structures) and their size reduction to appropriate range further enhance the anode kinetics (improving both electronic conductivity and Na+ diffusion) and accommodate the volume change during cycling. By combining research expertise in controlled nanostructure synthesis and ex situ/in Operando characterizations of battery materials from PI and collaborator’s teams, we will fabricate the ternary composite anode using both ball milling and wet chemistry methods, define the critical material parameters including composition, phase, size, and morphology of the composite anode, and investigate its electrochemical properties as functions of these parameters. Mechanistic study on the composite anode’s electrochemical behavior will be carried out by systematic structure/property investigation both ex-situ and in Operando, in order to optimize the anode performance. This proposed project will provide an in-depth understanding of the material system, and contribute to the development of Na ion battery anodes with highly reversible capacity, good rate performance, and long cycle life. 當前鈉電池領域的一個瓶頸問題就是其負極材料的選擇。 與鋰電不同，鈉離子相對大的離子半徑及其氧化還原電位使得石墨不再適用。 開發合適的鈉電負極材料是當務之急。在為數有限的可能選擇當中，錫磷合金脫穎而出。 錫和磷本身都是容量高的鈉電負極材料，但都存在緻命弱點。 它們的合金有效的保留了它們各自的性能優勢，同時其互補性在一定程度上由緩和了缺點和問題。但是，合金材料的導電性差，充放電過程中錫容易聚集，電極體積膨脹，應力增加，以及磷基材料的穩定性問題仍然有待解決。我們提出在錫磷合金中引入第三元素，並通過控製材料形貌和尺寸的方法，控製和解決上述問題，從而開發出新一代高能量密度高穩定性的鈉電負極材料。

14316716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14316716.value: We have developed both ball milling and wet chemistry based methods to synthesize Sn-P based compound for application of sodium ion battery anode. While fine controlling the size and morphology of the compound is difficult using ball milling, it is rather straight forward to introduce a third element/phase to the Sn4P3. Wet chemistry based methods have better control over the size and shape of the produced nanoparticles, however, introduction of a third element results in ternary compound or multiphase composite, as determining by the synthetic chemistry and the properties of the involved elements. The Sn4P3 compounds obtained from both methods show reasonable capacity and reasonably rate performance. However, both of them suffer from low cycle life. Ex-situ XRD results suggest that the Sn agglomeration and loss of P due to unstable SEI are the major causes for the poor cycling stability of the electrode. By introducing TiC phase to the ball milled Sn4P3 sample, the cycling life is largely improved, as the ultrafine TiC phases help to uniformly disperse the Sn4P3 phase and largely reduced the Sn agglomeration during cycling [Wang et al., Journal of Power Sources 364, 420-425, 2017]. By introducing Cu in the wet-chemistry synthesized Sn4P3 samples, a stable Cu4SnP10 phase is obtained with higher P content. The present Cu stabilize the Sn (completely eliminated the Sn aggregation). However, the cycling performance remains unsatisfactory, which is mainly ascribed to unstable SEI and P phases [Lan et al., NANO ENERGY, 39, 506-512, 2017 ]. We also attempted to introduce SnSb phase to the Sn4P3 sample, and Sn4P3/SbSn nanocomposites with a side-by-side configuration in individual nanoparticles have been obtained. In such a configuration, moderate improvement on the cyclic stability of the phase-pure Sn4P3 electrode is obtained without sacrificing its practical capacity [Lan and Li, ChemElectroChem 2018, 5, 1–5]. A few other Sn based materials have been synthesized to be compared with the Sn-P system and evaluate the evolution of Sn in the respective materials. By encapsulating nano-sized SnSb particles in porous 3D carbon matrix, we show that the architecture of nano-sized SnSb residing in porous structure constructed by 3D carbon effectively suppresses the particle pulverization and crack generation in the electrode upon repeated cycling, contributing to the improved electrochemical property [Wang et al., Journal of The Electrochemical Society, 165 (7) A1455-A1459 (2018)]. In the SnS system, we found both progressive Sn agglomeration and crystalline Na2S enrichment contribute to the capacity decay of the electrode upon repeated cycles. Introducing multi-wall carbon nanotubes as the additive, the cycle stability of the SnS electrode is largely improved, correlating to the suppression of both Sn agglomeration and Na2S enrichment at the end of desodiation cycles [Wang et al., Journal of Power Sources 377, 1-6, 2018 ].

14316716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14316716.value: Experimental results suggest that stabilization of both Sn and P in the local chemical environment without sacrificing its sodiation activity is critical to simultaneously achieving high capacity and long cycle life of the electrode. This stimulate use to manipulate the chemical environment of P by forming phosphorus-titania−carbon (P−TiO2−C) composite. A high-performance anode material is obtained with a reversible capacity of 1147 mA h g−1 at a current density of 100 mA g−1, , a high rate capacity retention of 81.5% for charging/discharging rate increasing from 100 to 1000 mA g−1, and a good cycle stability (540 mA h g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1 is maintained after 100 cycles) . The excellent electrochemical properties of the composite anode originate from the changed chemical states of both TiO2 and P, providing an effective strategy in designing high-performance sodium ion battery anode materials [Lan and Li, Applications ACS Appl. Energy Mater. 2019, 2, 661−667]. In the future, other strategies of manipulating the local chemistry of P/Sn can be investigated for the best performance of the Sn- or P-based anode materials. On the other hand, the detailed of mechanism of capacity decay in Sn-P based material remains arguable, and well planned ex situ characterizations at different stages of sodiation/desodiation is needed.

14316716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14316716.value: Sn4P3 is promising candidate for sodium ion battery anode with high capacity and relatively low redox potential. However the cycle performance of Sn-P based material is poor, limiting its practical application. In the present project, we took a few different approaches, trying to improve the cycle performance while simultaneously maintain its capacity. We have developed both ball milling and wet chemistry based methods to synthesize Sn-P based compound. Experimental results suggest that phase separation and aggregation of the Sn is one major contributor to the capacity decay. The stabilization of Sn can be realized by introducing either a third element forming ternary compound or a second phase to protect Sn from segregation. Lost of P is another problem leading to the poor cycle performance of the electrode. Stabilization of P can be partially realized by manipulating the local chemical environment without sacrificing its sodiation activity, leading to simultaneously achieved high capacity and long cycle life of the electrode.

14316816.label: Project Objectives
14316816.value: For a self-similar set $K$, we equip the coding space with a natural hyperbolic graph. We will study reversible random walks on such a graph. Under suitable conditions, we can identify the self-similar set with the Martin boundary and hyperbolic boundary some random walk. We will study the hitting distribution, Martin kernel, Naim kernel, and the induced (non-local) Dirichlet form with an explicit expression. Also, we will consider certain non-reversible random walks. In order to obtain the desired induced (local) Dirichlet forms, we will place our emphasis on the identification of the Martin boundary with the self-similar set. This will address ourselves to the question of existence of Laplacians on self-similar sets. In another direction, we will use the method of outer approximation to investigate the induced Laplacians, and more generally, the Dirichlet forms, and compare them with those obtained by using random walks. We will study the associated function spaces (Besov spaces), walk dimension, spectral dimension, eigen-problems, Green functions, and heat kernels that arise in the investigation.

14316816.value: 分形是一類不規則，複雜的集合或現象，它們具有自相似性質 及分數維數。分形在自然界及人類生活領域中經常出現，例如 海岸綫形狀，地層的組成，天體星雲的分布，DNA樣本，微血 管及肺的結構以及股票的上落數據曲綫。科學家及工程師們利 用分形作圖像壓縮，手機上天綫的設計，石油地質的探測。 醫學上，分形維數的計算，亦可用來顯示異常細胞的出現。 在這個建議書中，我們提出研究分形上的狄克雷型（或稱能量 型）。這套理論包括重要的拉普拉斯算子。我們知道，在經典 分析，熱傳導及波傳播以及許多在偏微分方程上的問題，都依 賴於拉氏算子。這類算子由微分定義，但分形是絶對非光滑的， 微分在上面沒有定義。因此所有經典上的概念及理論，都需要 有適當的調整。在分形上，拉氏算子的存在性，成為一個中心 的問題。在這個計劃上，我們將會利用分析及概率上的工具， 對這個問題作一個深入的研究。

14316816.label: Realisation of objectives
14316816.value: In a previous project ``Tree structure and boundary theories on fractals"(Project 1430221), we proved that on the tree of symbolic space of a self-similar set, we can add new edges to the tree according the neighboring cells to obtain an augmented tree; the augmented tree is hyperbolic, and the self-similar set is Holder equivalent to the hyperbolic boundary. The importance of this result is that if we run a reversible transient random walk on a hyperbolic graph, then the limits of the sample paths, called Martin boundary, is homeomorphic to the hyperbolic boundary, and hence also homeomorphic to the self-similar sets under consideration. It is well-known that in the study of Markov chains, there is a discrete potential theory to investigate the harmonic structure, Laplacian and energy of the system. We can therefore transfer this theory onto self-similar sets. In this regard, our first major achievement in this project [1] is to investigate a class of random walk on the augmented tree that have return ratio lambda, we call it lambda-natural random walk (NRW). The corresponding energy on the graph induces a non-local regular Dirichlet form on the self-similar set. Through the hyperbolic structure, we obtain an explicit expression of the kernel of the Dirichlet form, which is corresponding to a fractional Laplacian. The non-local Dirichlet forms arisen has the class of Besov spaces as its domain. The parameter beta in the expression of the Dirichlet form is interesting; it depends on the return ratio of the random walk, and the domain can be trivial when beta is large. The critical lambda is the largest value that the Besov space is non-trivial, it carries a lot of important information of the underlying set; in particular in the cases of the Sierpinski gasket and some other standard fractals, the critical exponent is where the local regular Dirichlet form is located. A local regular Dirichlet form associates with a Laplacian, and is of central importance in the study of analysis on fractal. We have considerable progress in in that aspect [2,4]. Recently, we discover that on a compact space of homogenous type, there is a refining net of partitions of the space, which gives a hyperbolic augmented tree, and our consideration of the boundary theories can be applied to those sets. The class of space of homogenous type is very broad, it covers the classical domains, Reimannian manifolds, and the fractal sets called d-sets, it is known for a long time, and has been studied extensively in harmonic analysis and Hp-space theory. We can extend the previous results to this much broader setting [3]. In a recent paper [5], we study the convergence properties of Besov norms on homogeneous p.c.f. self-similar sets near critical exponent sigma-star, and that of the associated Dirichlet forms. Our convergence result extends a celebrate theorem of Bourgain, Brezis and Mironescu on Euclidean space.

14316816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14316816.value: In [1] we investigate a class of random walk on the augmented tree that have return ratio lambda, we call it lambda-natural random walk (NRW). The corresponding energy on the graph induces a non-local regular Dirichlet form on the self-similar set. Through the hyperbolic structure, we obtain an explicit expression of the kernel of the Dirichlet form, which is corresponding to a fractional Laplacian. In [2], we study the partition systems and the tree structures for compact spaces of homogeneous type and establish the hyperbolicity of the augmented trees. We investigate the λ-NRW on the augmented trees; we identify the underlying set with the hyperbolic boundary and the Martin boundary. The estimations of the Martin kernel and the Naim kernel are stated. Finally, we study the induced Dirichlet forms and give a criterion of the critical exponents. In [4], we study Dirichlet forms and critical exponents of fractals and explore new situations that the underlying fractal sets admit inhomogeneous resistance scalings, which yield two types of critical exponents. We restrict our consideration on the p.c.f. (post critically finite) sets. We first develop a technique of quotient networks to study the general theory of these critical exponents. We then construct two asymmetric p.c.f. sets, and use them to illustrate the theory and examine the function properties of the associated Besov spaces at the critical exponents; the various Dirichlet forms on these fractals will also be studied.

14316816.value: To develop the theory of analysis (Dirichlet forms and Laplacians) for some non-p.c.f. fractals.

14316816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14316816.value: In this proposal, we study Dirichlet forms (equivalently, energy forms) on fractals. The theory includes the important Laplace operator. As is known, in classical analysis, the theories of heat diffusion, wave propagation and all considerations in partial differential equations depend on the Laplacian. The operator is differential in nature while fractals are highly non-smooth, and hence many classical perceptions need to be adjusted. Therefore defining the Laplacian on fractals and studying its properties are some central problems in the subject. In this project we obtained some new and interesting properties of the Dirichlet forms and Laplace operators on self-similar sets and compact spaces of homogeneous type. These works lead to better understanding of analysis on fractals.
