14317516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14317516.value: Transport processes in porous media cannot be separated from the flow. Indeed, the transport equation constitutes the material balance law for transported constituents. The transport equation is often convection-dominated and driven by a multiscale velocity field. Solving these multiscale transport equations can be very challenging computationally due to disparity of scales, high variations in the velocity field, and high Peclet number. Moreover, one also needs to resolve fine-scale features of the velocity field, which includes multiple scales and high contrast. Thus, developing reduced-order models, that are stable and accurate, is a challenging task in many applications including material sciences, filtration, membrane applications, groundwater hydrology, petroleum engineering, and so on. There are a number of traditional approaches, which include numerical homogenization, numerical upscaling, multiscale finite element method, and so on. These methods only use a few degrees of freedom to approximate the solutions and do not allow enrichments. As a result, they typically give a limited accuracy and stability for complex media without scale separation, high contrast, and high Peclet number. In this project, our focus is to develop accurate and stable reduced-order models for a coupled flow and transport in heterogeneous media. To achieve a desirable accuracy, we will design a systematic approach for computing multiscale basis functions for both flow and transport equations. This construction will be based on the analysis and will provide apriori error bounds. In multiscale problems, time and space adaptivity is essential as some regions may require a very few basis functions (as in numerical homogenization), while other regions may require more basis functions at certain time instants. For this, we will construct computable error indicators, to adaptively enhance the solutions in some localized regions. Due to high Peclet number, a multiscale stabilization is required. We will achieve it with a judicious construction of multiscale test functions. The proposed research provides a novel model reduction method for coupled flow and transport problems in "real-world" porous media with non-separable scales and high contrast. Our approaches can be used as a modeling tool to identify important parameters (in terms of basis functions) in a continuum coarse-scale modeling. Our novel techniques avoid idealized scale concepts, such as Darcy scale, and help us seamlessly without postulating any assumptions to transition from pore-scale to the continuum scales. We expect that our methodology will provide an accurate and efficient tool for many real applications involving flow and transport in porous media. 在多孔介質運輸的過程中流是不能分離的。輸運方程往往是對流為主，對流通過多尺度速度場驅動。由於尺度，在速度場高變化，和高Peclet數的差距，解決這些多尺度輸運方程是非常具有挑戰性的計算。此外，人們還需要解析速度場，其中包括多尺度和高對比度的精細尺度特徵。因此，顯影降階模型，是穩定的和精確的，但在許多應用中，包括材料科學，過濾，膜應用，地下水水文，石油工程，等一個具有挑戰性的任務。有許多的傳統方法，其中包括的數值均化，數值的升頻，多尺度有限元法，等等。這些方法只用幾個自由度來近似的解決方案和不允許富集。其結果是，它們通常給一個有限的精度和穩定性為複雜的媒體沒有標分離，高對比度和高Peclet數。 在這個項目中，我們的重點是制定對非均勻介質耦合流動和運輸的準確和穩定的降階模型。為了達到理想的準確性，我們將設計計算多尺度的基礎功能都流和輸運方程系統的方法。這種結構將被分析的基礎上，將提供先驗誤差界限。在多尺度的問題，時間和空間的適應性是必要的，因為一些地區可能需要很少的基本函數（如數值同質化） ，而其他地區可能需要在某一時刻的更多的基礎功能。為此，我們將建立可計算的誤差指標，自適應地增強一些局部區域的解決方案。由於高Peclet數，需要一個多尺度穩定化。我們將與多尺度測試功能明智建設實現它。 我們提出的研究提供了與非分離尺度和高對比度的耦合流動和運輸問題，在“現實世界”多孔介質一種新的降階方法。我們的方法可以作為一個建模工具，以確定重要的參數（在基函數）在一個連續粗尺度模型。我們的新技術避免理想化規模的概念，如Darcy模型，並幫助我們實現從孔隙尺度過渡到連續尺度。我們希望我們的方法將提供涉及多孔介質流動和運移許多實際應用的準確和有效的工具。

14317516.label: Realisation of objectives
14317516.value: All the objectives are achieved successfully. For the first objective, we have proposed new multiscale basis functions by solving suitable local problems with suitable boundary conditions. In order to obtain dominant modes, we design suitable local spectral problems. For the second objective, we have proposed new multiscale test functions. The idea uses a given set of trial basis functions. Then a local problem is solved to obtain a test function that can minimise the stability constant. For the third objective, we have designed an adaptive procedure. The idea here is to apply a local error estimator using the residual of the solution. In the 4th objective, we have applied some new mathematical tools to prove that the proposed method has a fast convergence. In order to achieve the final objective, we have applied our method to some realistic applications, and we observed very good results.

14317516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14317516.value: In this project, the PI successfully developed new multiscale methods for solving coupled flow and transport problems in heterogeneous porous media. There are several new ingredients. First of all, new multiscale basis functions are constructed for both flow and transport problems. These basis functions are able to capture the solutions using a low dimensional approximation. Next, a class of multiscale test functions is constructed. The proposed basis can be used to stabilise convection dominated diffusion problems. Third, an adaptive procedure is designed for the adaptive enrichment of basis functions. The proposed method is based on a new a-posteriori error analysis. The method allows one to enrich multiscale space adaptively. Moreover, full convergence of the method is given. Finally, the method has been successfully applied to applications.

14317516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14317516.value: The research has rooms for further research. One potential future work is to consider another more complex flow model, which can capture more fluid dynamics for various situations. In this case, we need to design new multiscale basis functions in order to capture the more complicated dynamics. Another possible work is to consider the nonlinear effects and design nonlinear multiscale basis functions.

14317516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14317516.value: The proposed research gives a multiscale model reduction technique for complicated flow and transport problems. It is known that computing the solution for these problems requires high computational cost and time, and is sometimes impossible due to the large scale of the applications. The proposed work gives a systematic procedure to obtain a reduced computational model for more efficient simulations. The proposed model is justified mathematically and is tested for many practical applications, and has shown its excellent performance. In addition, the proposed technique allows adaptively, which is desirable for many applications in which user defined error tolerance should be satisfied.

14317716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14317716.value: 本計劃目旨在研究分量迴歸(Quantile regression)應用於分析時間變數數據(Time-to-event data)。 傳統的迴歸分析(Regression analysis)主要透過建立數學模型以便觀察特定變數來預測研究者感興趣變量(Covariates)的均值，分量迴歸分析則著重對感興趣變數的各個份位數(Quantile)以至整個分佈（Distribution)與特定變數關係的建模。因其簡明但有效的模型表達式，分量迴歸一直都廣範被應用於經濟學（Economics)、衛生統計(Health Statistics)及其他不同學科作為常用的統計工具。與醫學及臨床試驗(Clinical trials)有密切關係的生存分析(Survival analysis)，在常用模型如Cox比例風險模型(Cox proportional hazards model)或加速失敗模型(Accelerated Failure Time Model, AFT)不足以描述相關數㨿的情況下，亦可從分量迴歸模型角度建模。 雖然文獻上已有不少論述分量迴歸在時間變數數據上如何作統計推論的著作，一些重要問題，如整體線性假設(Global linear assumption)、推論效率(Efficiency)和變量選擇(Variable selection)等題目依然缺乏討論。有見及此，本計劃透過理解分量迴歸與加速失敗模型的關係，從而針對以上幾方面問題尋找更佳的答案。此外，最近提出的擬似值(Pseudo-value method, PVM)亦可用於分量迴歸模型上作超高維(ultra high-dimensional)變量選擇。 分量迴歸一直得到廣範的應用和關注。本計劃目的是在回答上述數問題中為該範籌的研究作貢獻。

14317716.label: Realisation of objectives
14317716.value: The three objectives of the project have been achieved in this proposal for various projects. 1. One publication output entitled “Dynamic Transformed Censored Quantile Regression” (see Publication #2 in Part C) proposes a generic framework for inference problems of censored quantile regression. In the literature, one important and effective strategy for estimating model parameters of quantile regression based on censored observations is due to Peng and Huang (2008; JASA). Their formulation requires, however, a rather restrictive global linear assumption across all quantile levels in the sense that every quantile value of the failure time concerned has to be a linear function of the quantile-specific regression coefficient and the covariates considered. Since in real applications, it is rather difficult to check whether or not the said assumption is satisfied. Inspired by other previous works in the literature, we successfully incorporated the Box-Cox transform to individual quantile values (hence the concept “dynamic” in the title) so that only the transformed quantiles is required satisfy the global linear assumption. It is also, to the best of our knowledge, the first proposal that investigates the performance of modelling with the dynamic, quantile level-specific transformation parameter as a process. This paper first constructs a set of estimating equations for both the transformed parameter process and the regression parameter process. By utilising the cumsum statistic, given specific, optimised regression parameter (and the previous estimated parameters), one can determine consistent estimates of the transformation parameter process as well. The estimators proposed are also proved to be asymptotically unbiased and normally distributed upon the root-n standardisation. The first objective, is therefore, achieved for this work. Since solving our estimating equation directly may encounter numerical issues (the additional Box-Cox transformation parameters disturb the original, neat convexity of the Peng and Huang (2008) formulation), a careful grid-search procedure is discussed whose solutions can thus be more reliable. This enables our inference procedure can be more stably implemented and our second goal is also achieved. Finally, in terms of numerical accuracy and feasibility, this paper considers different types of violations of the global linear assumption and our results demonstrate very decent performance. The point estimates are virtually unbiased and the corresponding empirical coverage probabilities of the confidence interval constructed based on bootstrap are generally very close to the nominal values. One dataset is also analysed in this paper with conclusions that are consistent with previous findings. This further verifies the reliability of our proposed method as well as its versatility. The third objective of this project is also achieved. 2. Another manuscript prepared entitled “Efficient Estimation for Censored Quantile Regression” attempts to answer another question that has not yet been properly answered, in our humble opinion, is the study of estimation efficiency for censored quantile regression parameters. Since the corresponding likelihood is typically not tractable because of the error heterogeneity, conventional most efficient, maximum likelihood estimate (MLE)-type of results cannot be easily derived for quantile regression models. There have been research efforts made on analysing the most Z-measureable efficient weight for uncensored quantile regression problem (see Koenker, 2005), where Z denotes the covariates considered in the model, corresponding discussion for censored quantile regression model is, however, missing. In our submitted manuscript (see Publication #4), we attempt to answer this important question. Our model first of all proposes a modified estimating procedure based on the one proposed in Wang and Wang (2009). After justifying that our formulation results in asymptotically equivalent results as compared to Wang and Wang (2009)’s, we carefully analyse the resulting variance-covariance matrix of the resulting estimator upon which we conjecture the form of a possible weight function such that the the corresponding variance is minimised. With rigorous theoretical and numerical justifications, we have proved that the proposed weight function can lead to the minimum variance amongst all the Z-measureable weights. It also degenerates to the one proposed in Koneker (2005) when all the observations are uncensored. The first objective of the proposal is hence achieved for this project. Since the proposed weight function depends on the known density function of the failure time, we recommend a kernel based approach which gives accurate estimates and results in promising numerical results through which we achieve the second objective of the project. In the submitted manuscript, the data analysis provided produces the narrowest confidence intervals for the parameter estimates as compared to other existing methods. The third objective of the project outline is also achieved. It is unfortunate that, probably due to the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak, we have not yet received any feedback from the journal for our submitted manuscript despite the fact that it has been almost a year since we submitted it to the journal. We hope that we can hear positive feedback from the journal soon and our results can be published and contribute to the literature. 3. The three objectives are also achieved for another paper entitled "Value at Risk Simulation for High-dimensional Portfolios" (see Publication #7). In the field of risk management, value-at-risks (VaRs), the quantiles of the change in the value of the portfolio concerned over a pre specified investment period, have been frequently adopted as an effective tool for calculating risk capital reserve as required by international banking regulatory bodies including Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). With our experience in handling quantile estimation in the previous work, in this paper, we apply variable selection including LASSO to provide a more objective and accurate approach for VaR estimation. Under mild regularity conditions, we can establish the model consistency as well as convergence results of the VaR estimates. Two simulations and a real data analysis are also presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of this new proposal. Other projects, say Publications #3 and 6, also achieve the three objectives stated for network event time modelling and censored quantile regression with time-dependent variables under length-biased sampling scheme. All of these results are presented in regional/international conferences also. References: Koenker, R. (2005), Quantile Regression, Cambridge University Press. Koenker, R. and Bassett, G. 14317716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14317716.value: The main focus of this research project is to develop proper treatments for handling various issues related to censored quantile regression. Existing methods, although have been recognised as effective tools in modelling specific quantile level(s) of event time distribution given covariates, some of the technical issues remain unanswered. A novel and insightful idea in the literature reframes the conventional quantile regression check function framework (see Koenker and Bassett, 1978; Econometrica and Koenker, 2005) into a martingle-based, counting process formulation (see Peng and Huang, 2008; JASA). While this idea intricately and naturally makes use of the conventional techniques in survival analysis and apply it to adjust for the biasedness due to censored observations, it relies on an assumption that all the quantile values are linear functions of the covariates concerned, hence the so-called “global linear assumption”. To further generalise the model and relax the said assumption, we (see Publication #2) have developed a transformed censored quantile regression model in which a Box-Cox transform is applied to every single quantile level concerned, as a process, so that the linearity assumption is applied only on the transformed quantile levels after transformation. Another open question that we have attempted to answer is the possible improvement in the efficiency of existing censored quantile regression procedure. Unlike other statistical models which can be developed via more tractable quantities such as likelihood functions and/or estimating equations on homogeneous errors, quantile regression models’ efficiency is typically challenging to be investigated because of the potential heterogeneity involved. The censored observations further complicate the problem. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first attempt to analyse the covariance structure of the limiting distribution of our estimator inspired by Wang and Wang (2009; JASA) and propose a computable weight function which achieves the most efficient estimates under a very broad class of possible Z-measureable weight functions. The manuscript was finalized in Q4 2019 and was submitted to a journal for review. Unfortunately, possibly because of the COVID-19 pandemic, we have not yet received any feedback from the journal for almost one year. We hope that the manuscript can be published as soon as possible. (see Publication #4) Other publications including Publications #3,6 and 7 discuss other various issues related to censored observations under the network context and length-biased sampling schemes. They appear in reputable journals and/or book series. All the aforementioned results are also presented in various regional/international conferences.

14317716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14317716.value: Despite the desirable results that we have developed in this proposal, one of the limitations that many of the projects discussed share is its inability of handling time-dependent covariates under conditionally independent assumption between the failure time and the censoring time given covariates. In various medical studies, it is very often to encounter situations where subjects’ attributes vary as time proceeds. Typical examples include, for instance, blood pressure, body temperature, white blood cell counts, external air pollution levels. Amongst these time-dependent covariates, there is subtle difference between external/internal covariates. Recall that an internal time-dependent covariate is one where the change of the covariate over time is related to the behaviour of the individual and an external time-dependent covariate is one whose path is generated externally. It is interesting to extend or generalise the current settings so that time-dependent covariates can be incorporated in the model in which case the applicability of the models concerned will be much more expanded. Since there is no straightforward interpretation of the quantile estimates when there are internal covariates, it is a research direction with good potential. Some preliminary work including simulations and theoretical analysis have been carried out.

14317716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14317716.value: While traditionally means and medians are typical summary statistics to describe distributions concerned, it is more informative to model the quantiles concerned through quantile regression. Another benefit that quantile regression estimates enjoy is their robustness against outliers in the response measurements. All these desirable features make quantile regression valuable tools for modelling. In medical studies, censored observations are frequently observed, it is therefore useful to expand the current literature on censored quantile regression. Existing methods require rather restrictive assumptions, including global linear assumption, for instance, or do not discuss issues on improving estimation efficiency (accuracy). Through the extensions introduced in this project, censored quantile regression model can be an effective tool for more settings with better efficiency. It is expected that the methodologies developed can benefit various different end users who are interested in efficient, and accurate quantiles modelling for time-to-event data.

14318016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14318016.value: In July 4, 2012, the ATLAS and the CMS experimental collaborations at the European Organization for Nuclear Physics (CERN), announced the discovery of a particle compatible with the Standard Model Higgs boson in the analysis proton-proton collisions produced by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The discovery was recognized (among other awards) with the High Energy and Particle Physics Prize 2013 of the European Physical Society, awarded to the ATLAS and CMS collaborations, and the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded to Professors Peter Higgs and Francois Englert. After an extended shut-down period for maintenance and upgrades, the LHC has re-started operations with a collision energy of 13 TeV, which is significantly higher than the energy used to find the Higgs boson (up to 8 TeV), and will collect a much larger data sample. This new data-taking period, customarily called “Run II”, will allow detailed studies of the properties of the Higgs boson, and will make it possible to explore a range of energies previously inaccessible. Hong Kong institutions, building over the solid foundation provided by the success of the Daya Bay Reactor Experiment, have created the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong (JCFP). In June of 2014, the JCFP was accepted as a member of the ATLAS Experimental Collaboration. Hong Kong researchers and students are already actively involved in the analysis of data from Run II of the LHC. The JCFP collaborates with the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer Project, Higgs studies and Exotic Physics searches, and will undertake a number of responsibilities within the ATLAS collaboration. The goal of this project is to strengthen the participation of the JCFP in the ATLAS Experiment at CERN through work on the following areas: 1. Search for high-mass resonances in lepton-flavor violating decays to lepton pairs (e-mu, e-tau, mu-tau). 2. Study of the decay of the Higgs boson into pairs of tau leptons. 3. Tau-lepton identification and reconstruction algorithms. These areas are designed to avoid overlap with the objectives of the JCFP proposal and, to the maximum extent possible, to complement them to build a complete and solid physics program from Hong Kong institutions, with a significant impact and a long-term contribution to LHC Physics.

14318016.label: Realisation of objectives
14318016.value: All objectives were achieved. Details on each one are given below; research outputs mentioned in PART C are referred to as RO1, RO2. Objective 1. Search for high-mass resonances in lepton-flavor violating decays to lepton pairs (e-mu, e-tau, mu-tau) Before this project, our team had already participated in the ATLAS searches for high-mass resonances in lepton flavor violating decays to pairs of charged leptons using 3.2 fb-1 of proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, using the e-mu channel [LFV15], and adding later the tau channels (e-tau, mu-tau) [LFV16]. This project allowed us to become one of the main contributors to this research work in ATLAS. After the above publications, we led the subsequent studies to define selection criteria for the signal region, and the definition, validation and use of control regions for background estimation. We studied the background processes arising from jets mis-reconstructed as leptons (W+jets and multi-jet processes), which have a key role in the final states that include taus. We were also in charge of the preparation and maintenance of the analysis code used and had the roles of analysis contact and publication editor within the ATLAS Collaboration for the corresponding paper [RO1]. These new published results, based on 36.1 fb-1 of pp collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13TeV, were shown at the LHC Physics Conference in Bologna, Italy [OKU18]. No significant excess was found over the SM expectation, which allowed us to put 95% CL limits on the cross-section times branching ratio, as well as mass limits for three classes of new physics models; namely: a heavy neutral weak boson with an LFV coupling [Lang09], an R-parity violating scalar neutrino [Far78, Bar05] and quantum black hole production [Gin10]. Objective 2. Study of the decay of the Higgs boson into pairs of tau leptons. The Higgs boson, discovered in 2012 at CERN [ATL12, CMS12] is a cornerstone of the SM. Its coupling strengths were measured using the complete Run 1 LHC dataset by the ATLAS collaboration [ATLASCo14]; these measurements were later updated including additional decay channels [ATLASCo16]. Before this project, in close collaboration within the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong, we contributed to the preparation of the above Higgs results, which were later used for a joint ATLAS-CMS measurement of Higgs boson production and couplings [ACCo15]. We made strong contributions to the preparation of more recent results for the inclusive and differential cross sections in the four-lepton decay channel, based on 36.1 fb-1 of 13 TeV data [H4l17]. Our group has been involved in searches involving leptons since the beginning of our work with ATLAS. This has allowed us to develop the techniques and software tools for selection, study and analysis of final states resonances with high-momentum tau-leptons. We have also worked with the ATLAS Group in charge of identification and reconstruction of taus, to explore variations to the analysis used so far in the Higgs to tau pairs studies that will take advantage of the larger Run 2 dataset. We also studied methods to improve the sensitivity of CP violation studies in the ditau decays of the Higgs boson [Ber15]. Specifically, we focused on strategies for the reconstruction of the primary vertex, to reduce the bias due to the use of a beamspot constraint, which can potentially affect a CP-sensitive angle used in the analysis. We tested various approaches to reduce these biases to increase the discrimination between CP-even and CP-odd potential BSM components of the Higgs boson. The study of the CP invariance in the Higgs decays to tau leptons with the ATLAS detector using run 2 data was published in Phys. Lett. B [RO2]. Objective 3. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. One postdoctoral research associate, one PhD student (Kevin Kwok), one MPhil student (Yun Sang Chow) and two undergraduate students (Erfei Wang and Kyle Lau) have worked on the project. This has allowed them to benefit from the close interaction with colleagues from other ATLAS institutions (located both in Hong Kong and overseas), from learning several of the tools used for research in High Energy Physics, and from working with recent data and Monte Carlo simulation from the Large Hadron Collider, on searches and measurements at the energy frontier. 14318016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14318016.value: A search is performed for a heavy particle decaying into different-flavor, dilepton pairs (eμ, eτ or μτ), using 36.1/fb of proton-proton collision data at √s=13TeV collected in 2015–2016 by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. No excesses over the Standard Model predictions are observed. Bayesian lower limits at the 95% credibility level are placed on the mass of a Z′ boson, the mass of a supersymmetric τ-sneutrino, and on the threshold mass for quantum black-hole production. For the Z′ and sneutrino models, upper cross-section limits are converted to upper limits on couplings, which are compared with similar limits from low-energy experiments and which are more stringent for the eτ and μτ modes. A test of CP invariance in Higgs boson production via vector-boson fusion in the Higgs to di-tau decay channel was performed. Using 36/fb of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC. No sign of CP violation is observed.

14318016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14318016.value: There are several areas for potential refinements and improvements. For the search of high-mass lepton flavour violating decays, the use of novel machine learning techniques may yield a larger sensitivity, especially in the mass regions where the expected standard model backgrounds are much larger than the potential signals. We are currently exploring some of this possibilities. For the Higgs analysis, many developments are currently under way, both on the theory side and in terms of experimental techniques; one example is the use of machine learning to refine the identification and reconstruction of tau leptons, which is also being actively pursued by our group.

14318016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14318016.value: This research project contributes to our understanding of the fundamental processes of Nature on two fronts: (a) searching for phenomena that is not expected in our current theories, and (b) the characteristics of the Higgs boson. These objectives are pursued through the analysis of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland. There, protons travel almost at the speed of light; when they collide, they can transform into any particle allowed by the laws of Nature. Our current description of these laws (the “Standard Model”, or SM) provides very precise predictions for the possible outcomes of these collisions, but we know that the SM is incomplete, so we are making a systematic search for phenomena not contained in it. We aim specifically to (a) search for new high-mass particles that may be able to decay into two different kinds of leptons (which are charged elementary matter particles that do not feel the strong nuclear force), and (b) study the decay of the Higgs boson into the heaviest leptons, which will help us measure, among others, the symmetry properties of the Higgs boson.

14319016.label: Realisation of objectives
14319016.value: We have successfully addressed the objectives of this project, with a key achievement - a world-record spectral resolution (3.4 Hz) of the nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) of a single atom (namely, a carbon 13 nuclear spin in diamond lattice). This key result is published in Nature Communications (Part C 8, Item 3. see https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08544-z ) and we are invited to report this results in many prestigious conferences (including the Gordon Research Conference on Quantum Sensing and the Winter Colloquium on the Physics of Quantum Electronics). Below we describe the main results related to the objectives. 1. The most important challenges to quantum sensing is the noises from the environments and the errors in the control itself. We designed advanced dynamical decoupling schemes (e.g., the so-called concatenated KDD sequences) to suppresses the effects of environmental noises (including the couplings to nuclear spins in the backgrounds) and to improve the control fidelity of the sensors. This part of works addressed Objective 1. 2. We developed schemes of sequential quantum weak measurements and designed, demonstrated, and analyzed the output correlations of the sequential measurements. The weak measurement is realized by controlling the coupling between the sensor and the target and then by a project measurement on the sensor. Since the sensor and target are controlled to be weakly entangled, the projective measurement on the sensor constitutes only a weak measurement on the sensor (for it only weakly distinguishes the target states). The weak measurement has the advantages of weak quantum back-action to the sensor and hence small disturbance of the target spin resonance. This turns out is the key to high-spectral resolution under realistic measurement time. We analyzed different types of correlations in the outputs of the sequential measurement and related them to the correlations of the target spin. The analysis provides basis of applying the correlations of the sequential weak measurement to extracting the resonance and decoherence information about the target spin. We discovered the parameter regions where the spectral resolution is optimized and phase transitions between different regions of the measurement strength in which the target spin performs either coherent oscillating or being coherently trapped. These works address Objective 2. 3. We applied the dynamical decoupling schemes to the control of nitrogen-vacancy center spins in diamond under realistic conditions and the sequential weak measurement schemes to the NMR detection of a single carbon-13 spin. The analysis of the experimental data took into account important imperfections in experiments, such as the photon detection inefficiency, disturbance of the target spins due to quantum jumps of the nitrogen-vacancy center during the state preparation and measurement, and the instability of the magnetic fields. We therefore optimize the parameters for the experimental realization of high spectral resolution for single-atom NMR. With our experimental collaborators' great efforts, we eventually achieved the world record of spectral resolution of single atom NMR. (3.4 Hz, which is comparable to conventional liquid state NMR and has met the resolution requirements for molecular structure analysis using chemical shifts). This work addressed Objective 3.

14319016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14319016.value: In this project, we achieved the world-record spectral resolution in the nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) of a single atom - 3.4 Hz resolution of a carbon 13 nucleus in diamond. We used nitrogen-vacancy center spin as the sensor and designed advanced dynamical decoupling pulse sequences to control the coupling between the sensor spin and the C-13 nuclear spin so that the sequential weak measurement is realized. We further designed, measured, and analyzed the correlations among the outputs of the sequential weak measurement under the dynamical decoupling control. Therefore we extract the resonance signal of the C-13 nuclear spin. By decreasing the measurement strength, we minimize the quantum back-action of the detection to the C-13, which would otherwise disturb the nuclear spin and broaden its resonance. So that the ultra-high spectral resolution of single-atom NMR. Such a spectral resolution is even comparable to that of conventional liquid-state NMR and meets the requirements for measuring precisely the chemical shift of nuclei in single molecules. This is an important step forward for single-molecule NMR and atomic scale magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The result is published in Nature Communications (Part C 8, Item 3. see https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-08544-z ).

14319016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14319016.value: An important potential for further development is to use the higher-order correlations of sequential weak measurement (whose strength and measurement bases can be controlled by dynamical decoupling) for quantum sensing schemes that have no classical counterparts. For example, certain types higher-order correlations of a quantum system cannot be accessed by a classical probe and certain types of higher-order correlations do not exist in classical targets. Therefore, using such correlations, we are working toward the development of new quantum sensing approaches to quantum many-body physics and to classical-noise-free detection of quantum targets.

14319016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14319016.value: NMR and MRI are important analysis and imaging techniques, widely used in chemistry, materials science and engineering, mineralogy, biology, neuroscience, and medicine. However, the conventional liquid-state NMR needs many (from trillions of to millions of trillions of) molecules to be detected together for sufficient signal-to-noise ratio. Such low sensitivity limits the MRI resolution to millimetres. The grand challenge in the fields of NMR and MRI is to realize the single-molecule NMR and hence atomic scale MRI. This task is extremely challenging for at such a small scale the target and the sensor are both quantum and their states are fragile to even the weakest perturbation from realistic environments and to their mutual interaction. In this project, we first designed dynamical decoupling control to minimize the coupling between the sensor and the environments so that it quantum properties are well preserved. Furthermore we use the dynamical decoupling to control the interaction between the sensor and the target (a single nuclear spin) so that the disturbance of quantum back-action to the target spin is minimized. We applied the method to detect the NMR of a single carbon 13 nuclear spin in diamond lattice, using a nitrogen-vacancy center spin as a sensor (the quantum version of the pick-up coil in conventional liquid-state NMR). We achieved the world-record spectral resolution - 3.4 Hz for the single-nucleus NMR. This result constitutes an important step toward single-molecule NMR and atomic scale MRI.

14319416.label: Project Objectives
14319416.value: Study of controlling ZnS in the bulk of CZTS. We plan to replace Zn with Mg in CZTS. The first step will be a study of all the native defects of CMTS to fully understand their stability and electronic properties. We’ll calculate the formation energies of neutral and charged defects and their transition energies. The proposed defects include Mg_Cu, Cu_Mg, Cu_Sn, Sn_Cu, Mg_Sn, Sn_Mg, V_Cu, V_Mg, V_Sn, and V_S. Defect complex will also be studied to understand the interaction between different defects and search for the lowest energy configurations of the defect complex. With all the data calculated, we will compare the formation energies of these defects with those of the similar defects in CZTS. Study of controlling ZnS near the surface of CZTS using surfactant approaches. We plan to search for effective surfactant elements that may significantly reduce ZnS formation. We will also study the kinetics of Zn near the surface as well as the stability of ZnCu at the subsurface with and without Na. We will then test the surface adsorption of Zn with and without Na and further study the electronic properties when Na is incorporated. The Na surfactant effect on the bulk O will also be examined. Finally, we plan to search for other possible surfactant candidates, including Ca and transition metals with a valence of one or two. Based on the theoretical predictions, the co-I will carry out experiments to verify these strategies. 3 Study of controlling ZnS at the grain boundaries of CZTS. Based on our knowledge in the structural properties of various ∑3 (60°) grain boundaries, we'll investigate the electronic properties of the grain boundaries. Our results will be compared with observations from the co-I’s experiments. We will then study the adsorption and diffusion of Zn, Cu, Na on the grain boundaries. From these studies, elements that may effectively remove the gap states near the grain boundaries can be identified, and new strategies that may largely reduce the Zn concentration near the grain boundaries will be proposed.

14319416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14319416.value: The aim of this project is to control the secondary phase of ZnS in the bulk, on the surface, and on the grain boundaries of Cu2ZnSnS4 by density functional theory approach and collaborating with co-I in experiments. Cu2ZnSnS4 is a promising photo voltaic absorber material consisted with nontoxic and earth abundant elements. Unfortunately, several secondary phases may form during the growth, among which ZnS is detrimental because it may reduce the short circuit current, shrink the absorber volume, and limit the grain sizes. Large improvements in efficiency may be achieved if the formation of ZnS can be suppressed. However, it is difficult to reduce ZnS concentration due to its stable structure and the Cu poor and Zn rich growth condition. As a result, large amount of ZnS exists in the bulk, on the surface, or on the grain boundaries of Cu2ZnSnS4. The study of ZnS control is especially challenging because of the relative complex growth environment and the intrinsic difficulties of in situ observations of ZnS during growth. Therefore, few ZnS control strategies have been proposed. Density functional theory is a well-established technique that can accurately calculate doping and defects properties. By applying this approach, we have studied and proposed many novel strategies to control the defects concentrations and types in GaP, ZnO, Si, Cu2ZnSnS4, and Cu2ZnSnSe4. In this project, we plan to: (1) reduce ZnS in the bulk by replacing the Zn elements with Mg or other valence II elements; (2) reduce ZnS on the surface by incorporating Na as a surfactant, study the effect of Na on O near the surface, and search for the most effective surfactant in ZnS reduction; and (3) reduce ZnS near the grain boundaries by understanding the structure properties of grain boundaries, calculating the kinetic properties of elements on the grain boundaries, and searching for effective passivation schemes to remove gap states and reduce ZnS on the grain boundaries. The studies will also be extended to Cu2ZnSnSe4. Our findings will help improve the basic scientific understandings towards the electronic properties and the controlling schemes of ZnS in Cu2ZnSnS4. We expect that our results will effectively reduce ZnS concentration and improve the efficiency of Cu2ZnSnS4 based solar cells. These results will directly influence the field of photo voltaic devices, and the general secondary phase control strategy will also help improve other semiconductor alloy devices, which have played or will play important roles in our daily life. 這個研究項目的目的以密度泛函理論為基礎，結合實驗合作，來控制硫化鋅次生相在銅鋅錫硫塊材內部，表面上，以及晶界面上的分佈。 銅鋅錫硫是一種有前途的光伏吸收材料。它是由無毒和在地球上廣泛分佈的元素組成的。遺憾的是，在其生長過程中會出現多種次生相。次生相中的硫化鋅是有害的，因為它會降低短路電流，降低光子吸收，並限制晶粒尺寸。如果硫化鋅的形成被抑制，我們就有可能大大提高光伏器件的效率。然而，由於其穩定的結構以及少銅富鋅的生長環境，硫化鋅的形成很難被抑制。這導致了大量的硫化鋅會分佈在塊材內部，表面上，或者在晶界面上。另外，因為銅鋅錫硫相對複雜的生長環境，以及在其生長期間很難觀察到硫化鋅，所以硫化鋅的控制策略很少被研究者提出。 密度泛函理論是一個行之有效的計算技術。它可以精確預測摻雜和缺陷的結構和電子性質。通過這種方法，我們已研究和提出許多新的策略來控制磷化鎵，氧化鋅，矽，銅鋅錫硫等材料中缺陷濃度和類型。在這個研究項目中，我們計劃：（1） 用Mg或其它二價元素來替換鋅; （2）尋找和利用表面活性劑，來減少對硫化鋅在表面的形成（3）計算在晶界面附近元素的動力學性質， 尋找有效的鈍化方案來飽和晶界面附近的懸掛鍵，並降低硫化鋅在晶界面附近的形成。這些研究也將擴展到銅鋅錫硒。 我們的研究結果將有助於提高對銅鋅錫硫電子性質的基礎科學理解以獲得硫化鋅的控制方案。我們希望我們的結果將有效降低硫化鋅濃度，提高銅鋅錫硫太陽能電池效率。這些結果將直接促進光伏器件的領域的發展。另外，這些次生相控制策略也將有助於改善其他半導體合金器件，它們都會對我們的日常生活發揮重要作用。

14319416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14319416.value: In the whole project, we discovered the following interesting scientific results: The invasion behavior of Zn at Cu site on un-passivated surface of CZTS, the detrimental electronic properties of such invasion induced defects, and the protection of the Cu site with the help of surfactants. In addition, we discovered interesting Zn incorporation sites with Na as surfactants, carefully compared the diffusion of Zn and surfactant atoms on the surfaces, compared the efficiencies of different surfactants and developed a general guideline on surfactant enhanced growth of semiconductors. The results were published at Physical Review Materials Phys. Rev. Materials 1, 045403. The another paper was just accepted by Journal of Physical Chemistry C. We computed grain boundaries of CZTS and disovered new type of grain boundaries with a new algorithm, and investigated various passivation strategies to remove the detrimental effects and exchanged our findings with our experimental collaborators. The related results are published at JPCC. 2018 The Journal of Physical Chemistry C, J. Phys. Chem. C 2018, 122, 14, 7759–7770. We performed systematic point defect calculations of group I in CZTS and CMTS. The results are published at Journal of Applied Physics 124, 165701 (2018). In addition, we conducted theoretical investigations on interlayer coupling mechanism and published the results at PNAS, July 3, 2018 115 (27) 6928 Also, we developed thermodynamic stability analysis of compound semiconductor stability, and published the results at NANO SCALE, Issue 37. 17683. (2018). Also, a new algorithm of semipolar surface stability of compound semiconductors has been discovered and published at Phys. Review. Materials, Phys. Rev. Materials 2, 073401, 2018. With the support of this fund, we also conducted an interesting p-type and n-type defect separation study and published at National Science Review,Volume 6, Issue 3, May 2019, Pages 532

14319416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14319416.value: Along the direction, we further finished the results of defect investigations in CMTS and currently sent for review at Journal of Applied Physics. Another paper on surfactant design is under review at JPCC and was just accepted. In the future, we also plan to further investigate Sn incorporation mechanism on front contact, back contact modifications with 2D materials and to demonstrate our unique lead and insights in the defect and surface studies of energy materials.

14319416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14319416.value: This project demonstrates that combinations of surface kinetics, bulk defects, grain boundary passivations and surfactant design can be very powerful tools to enhance understanding and inspire new strategies to improve the device efficiency of CZTS solar cell. The surface kinetics of Zn invasion behavior was discovered and effective strategies to suppress the formation of detrimental defects were proposed. A lot of new physical insights are developed computationally and close collaborations are conducted efficiently with several experimental collaborators. In addition, new algorithms and new type of grain boundaries have been discovered. The interlayer coupling mechanism discovered in this project is also general. The overall practice shows that both fundamental physical discoveries and insights in device and crystal growth can be obtained at the same time.

14320616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14320616.value: Boron is the 5th element in the periodic table, right next to carbon, with four valence orbitals but only three valence electrons. Its trivalent compounds have been extensively studied and found wide applications as reagents in chemical transformations and as building blocks in materials science. In contrast, the chemistry of low-valent boron compounds, for example, borylenes analogous to carbenes, is much less developed. Only in recent years, several Lewis base stabilized borylenes in the form of (L2)BR (L = Lewis bases) have been isolated and structurally characterized. They have demonstrated a very rich chemistry. In general, to stabilize both electronically and sterically unsaturated borylenes, ligands featuring both strong σ-donating and π-accepting ability are preferred as they can not only fill the vacant orbitals of boron(I) centers, but also disperse some electron density by accepting lone pair electrons from boron centers. With this in mind, we have designed an iminocarboranyl ligand for the stabilization of boron(I) compounds. Preliminary results (Chem. Commun. 2015, 51, DOI: 10.1039/c5cc06818e) indicate that this is a very good ligand as the imino unit can not only occupy the vacant orbital of boron(I) center to decrease its Lewis acidity, but also act as π acceptor to diminish its Lewis basicity. In addition, sterically very bulky carboranyl moiety can protect the reactive boron(I) center from electrophilic attack. In this proposal, we plan to design a new class of carborane-based ligands appended with various Lewis base functionalities for the preparation of Lewis base stabilized boron(I) and boron(0) compounds, to understand their bonding properties, and to study their reaction chemistry. It is anticipated that this research would enhance our fundamental understanding of the bonding properties and reactivity of low-valent boron compounds. It is also fascinating to discover what lies beyond. 硼是元素周期表中的第五個元素，與碳相鄰。它有四個價軌道，却只擁有三個價電子。三價硼化合物已經得到了深入的研究，它不僅是化學轉化中廣泛使用的試劑，同時也是材料科學領域中常用的基礎構件。相比之下，諸如硼烯(卡賓的類似物)一類的低價態硼化合物的化學則發展的較慢。直到最近幾年，幾例結構確定的路易斯碱穩定的硼烯，L2BR (L爲路易斯碱)，才被分離得到。研究證實，這類化合物有著非常豐富的化學。通常，爲了穩定這類缺電子且配位不飽和的硼烯，那些同時具備强σ電子給體和π電子受體特質的配體會被優先選擇。因爲它們不僅可以填充一價硼中心的空軌道，也可以通過接受硼中心的孤電子對分散硼中心的電子雲密度。基于這種想法，我們設計了一個亞胺碳硼烷配體，幷用于穩定一價硼化合物。初步結果(Chem. Commun. 2015, 51, DOI: 10.1039/c5cc06818e)表明它是一個很好的配體，因爲亞胺不僅可以通過占據一價硼中心的空軌道來减少一價硼中心的路易斯酸性，還可以通過接受電子來降低一價硼中心的路易斯鹼性。同時，位阻很大的碳硼烷還可以阻止高反應活性的一價硼中心受到親電試劑進攻。在這份研究計劃中，我們計劃在碳硼烷骨架上搭載各種路易斯碱基團，設計合成一系列新的基于碳硼烷的配體，這些新的配體可以用來製備路易斯碱穩定的一價硼和零價硼化合物，進而理解這類低價態硼化合物的結構特徵，幷研究它們的反應性。我們希望這項研究可以提高我們對于低價態硼化合物結構特徵和反應性的理解。同時，也期待著意外的發現。

14320616.label: Realisation of objectives
14320616.value: Boron is the 5th element in the periodic table, right next to carbon, with four valence orbitals but only three valence electrons. Its trivalent compounds have been extensively studied and found wide applications as reagents in chemical transformations and as building blocks in materials science. In contrast, the chemistry of low-valent boron compounds, for example, borylenes analogous to carbenes, is much less developed. In general, to stabilize both electronically and sterically unsaturated borylenes, ligands featuring both strong σ-donating and π-accepting ability are preferred as they can not only fill the vacant orbitals of boron(I) centers, but also disperse some electron density by accepting lone pair electrons from boron centers. In view of sterically very bulky carboranyl moiety that can protect the reactive boron(I) center from electrophilic attack, we have designed a new class of carborane-based ligands appended with various Lewis base functionalities for the preparation of Lewis base stabilized boron(I) compounds, and to understand their bonding properties, and to study their reaction chemistry. According to the proposal, we have designed, prepared and characterized a new class of carborane-based ligands appended with various Lewis base functionalities including carborane-based imines, carboranyl supported germylenes, cyclic amino(carboranyl) silylenes, carborane-based silylenes, and carborane-based bissilylenes. With these new ligands in hand, we then prepared a series of stabilized borylenes and studied their reaction chemistry. A carbene-stabilized iminocarboranylboron(I) compound has been synthesized and structurally characterized. Single-crystal X-ray analyses and DFT calculations show that the π back donation of lone pair electrons on the boron(I) center onto π* orbital of imine unit is crucial for removing the electron density of the boron center and thereby stabilizes such species, in which the carbene serves solely as σ donor. This work also demonstrates that imines play a similar role to that of carbenes in the stabilization of low-valent boron compounds. This boron(I) compound can undergo a fully reversible photothermal isomerization, leading to the isolation and structural characterization of the first example of carborane-fused borirane. DFT calculations indicate that the azaborole is thermodynamically more stable than the borirane by 11.2 kcal/mol, and the energy barrier for the thermal conversion from azaborole to borirane is 35.5 kcal/mol. The reactivity studies show that the B-C(cage) bond in borirane can be broken in the reaction with CuCl, HCl or elemental sulfur. Using carborane-based bissilylenes as the ligand, the first example of bis(silylene)-stabilized borylene carbonyl cation has been prepared and structurally characterized via the reaction of bis(silylene)-stabilized bromoborylene with W(CO)6. This is a borylene cation coordinated by three neutral ligands, which can be viewed as a cationic form of a long-sought Lewis base stabilized zerovalent boron compound. To understand its electronic structure, DFT calculations have been performed. The HOMO consists of the lone pair orbital on the boron center having noticeable π back-donation interaction with the coordinated CO ligand. The B-C (CO) Wiberg bond index (1.48) is significant, confirming the above-mentioned π back-donation interaction. The B-Si Wiberg bond indices (1.00 for both bonds) in this cation suggest that the silylene units serve mainly as σ donors. This study demonstrates that silylenes can function as good supporting ligands for the isolation of silylene-stabilized borylenes. This work has been published as a cover paper in JACS. On the other hand, reaction of carborane-based bissilylenes with 2 equiv of BBr3 in toluene, followed by reduction with 3 equiv of KC8 in THF at room temperature, affords a bis(silylene)-stabilized bromoborylene. Its reduction with 2 equiv of sodium gives a new compound with a B-B single bond. This represents a new strategy to construct electron-precise B-B single bond via direct borylene insertion into B-H bond. Both experimental and DFT (density functional theory) results suggest that such an electron-precise B-B single bond is formed via in-situ generated borylene insertion into B-H bond. We then studied in detail the reaction chemistry of the aforementioned borylene cation, [bis(silylene)B(CO)]+. Diverse reactivity patterns of borylene-carbonyl including reduction, migration and complete cleavage of CO have been observed at a boron center, leading to the formation of new types of borylenes. In addition, this cation can split dihydrogen to give boron hydride. These reactions not only serve as new methodologies for the synthesis of various stable borylenes, but also demonstrate that main group element compounds can mimic the behavior of transition metal complexes. The associated reaction mechanisms have been studied by DFT calculations. This work has been published as a back cover paper in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. In summary, we have prepared and structurally characterized a series of new borylenes (monovalent boron compounds) using newly designed carborane-based Lewis base ligands. Their reaction chemistry has been studied and associated reaction mechanisms have been proposed on the basis of DFT calculations.

14320916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14320916.value: The aim of this proposal is to (i) synthesize submicrometer spherical dielectric particles with strong electric and magnetic resonances in the visible or near-infrared region; (ii) understand the electromagnetic resonance interactions in all-dielectric and dielectric-metal dimers as well as oligomers; and (iii) investigate the surface-enhanced fluorescence and Raman scattering performances of submicrometer dielectric particles and the aforementioned dimers. Nanomaterials supporting strong electromagnetic resonances possess absorption and scattering cross-sections much larger than their physical cross-sections; they can focus light to spatial regions that are much smaller than the wavelength of light; they can largely change the local density of photonic states. Such nanomaterials have been studied intensively for enhancing light-matter interaction at the nanoscale, as well as for functioning as basic building units in the construction of metasurfaces and metamaterials to achieve a variety of advanced optical phenomena and functions. Tremendous efforts have focused on metal nanoparticles and nanostructures, which exhibit strong plasmon resonances, i.e., collective oscillations of electrons. Although enormous progresses have been made, plasmonic metal nanoparticles generally suffer from two drawbacks: (i) energy loss through Joule heating, which can strongly damp electromagnetic resonances, reduce device performances and limit the scalability to macroscopic sizes; and (ii) the existence of only electric plasmon resonances with simple metal nanoparticles. To create magnetic plasmon resonances, metals are often designed into complex nanostructures. Submicrometer high-refractive-index dielectric particles have been known to support both electric and magnetic resonances in the visible to near-infrared region. Some studies have been made in recent several years on this topic, with rapid progresses appearing since 2014. So far, a majority of these works have focused on submicrometer Si particles and structures. While significant understanding and achievements have been obtained, submicrometer Si particles have limitations in three aspects. (i) They are difficult to be synthesized chemically. (ii) Owing to the refractive index function of Si, the electric and magnetic resonances are inherently separated spectrally, which prevents them from being strongly coupled together. (iii) Light absorption above the band gap of Si can cause energy loss in the visible region. Here we propose the synthesis of submicrometer spherical dielectric metal oxide particles and study of their electromagnetic resonance properties. The success of this proposal is expected to provide low-loss and cost-effective submicrometer metal oxide particles supporting strong electromagnetic resonances, enrich the toolkit for enhancing light-matter interaction at the nanoscale, and offer guidance in designing metasurfaces and metamaterials with dielectric nanomaterials. 本項目的主要目的包括：(1)合成在可見和近紅外波段具有強的電和磁共振的亞微米介質球；(2)掌握介質球和介質/金屬球二聚體及寡聚體中的電磁耦合規律；(3)研究亞微米介質球及二聚體對熒光和拉曼信號的增強效應。 具有強電磁共振的納米材料的吸收和散射截面積遠大於它們的物理截面積，它們可以把光場局域到遠小於入射光波長的空間，從而極大地改變局域光場態密度。因此，這類納米材料被廣泛地用來增加光在納米尺度和物質的相互作用。同時，該類納米材料也可以作為結構單元來構建具有一系列奇特光學特性和功能的超表面和超材料。目前，大量的研究集中在具有表面等離激元共振性質的金屬納米粒子和納米結構。儘管該方面的研究已經取得了很大的進展，但是表面等離激元共振金屬納米粒子具有兩個較為突出的缺點：(1)金屬中的焦耳熱效應會導致能量損耗，從而極大地削弱電磁共振和危害器件的性能；(2)簡單的金屬納米顆粒只能產生表面等離激元電共振，為了得到表面等離激元磁共振，金屬必須設計成複雜的納米結構。 具有高折射率的亞微米介電顆粒能夠同時在可見光到近紅外波段支持電共振和磁共振。近幾年，國內外科學家開始逐漸關注介質顆粒的電磁共振並在該領域開展研究。2014年至今，該領域迅速發展。目前為止，大部分研究主要集中在亞微米硅顆粒和結構。儘管已取得較深入的理解和顯著的進展，亞微米硅顆粒的研究仍有三個方面的局限性：(1)它們難以通過簡單的化學方法製備；(2)由於硅的折射率較高，硅顆粒的電共振和磁共振模式在頻域上相隔較大，不利於電模式和磁模式間的相互耦合；(3)硅的帶間躍遷會導致可見光頻域的能量損失。 在本項目中，我們計劃利用化學方法製備亞微米球形介質金屬氧化物顆粒，並研究它們的電磁共振特性。本項目的成功開展將實現低電磁損耗的金屬氧化物亞微米顆粒的低成本製備，豐富在亞微米尺度增強光與物質相互作用的材料庫，並為介電超表面和材料的設計提供指導。

14320916.label: Realisation of objectives
14320916.value: I will describe the realization of the objectives in a point-by-point manner. The first objective is the synthesis of submicrometer spherical dielectric particles, the study of their electric/magnetic resonances, and the understanding of their directional light scattering properties. This objective has been well accomplished. We have synthesized cuprous oxide, titania and zirconia submicrometer nanospheres. The cuprous oxide nanospheres are prepared by a wet-chemistry method. Their diameters can be varied in the range from ~100 nm to ~250 nm. The titania and zirconia nanospheres are prepared by an aerosol spray method. The produced oxide nanospheres span a broad size range from ~100 nm to a few micrometers in diameter, and their refractive index can be varied from ~2.0 to ~2.35 in the visible region by synthetically changing their crystalline structure. We have systematically investigated their diameter-dependent electromagnetic resonance modes by optical dark-field scattering imaging and spectroscopy together with Mie theory-based calculations and electromagnetic simulations. The Mie theory-based mode decomposition reveals the spectral overlap between the electric and magnetic dipole resonances of these oxide nanospheres with moderate refractive indexes. These dielectric nanospheres exhibit the forward light scattering behavior. The forward-to-backward scattering intensity ratio has been found to increase with diameter. The second objective is to study and understand the electric/magnetic resonance interactions in all-dielectric dimers and dielectric/metal dimers made of one dielectric nanoparticle and one plasmonic metal nanoparticle. This objective has been realized completely. The dimers are prepared by drop-casting the dispersion solutions of the dielectric nanospheres and the gold nanospheres. The formation of the dimers is caused by the capillary force of the solvent during its evaporation. Although the yield of the dimers is limited, it is sufficient for carrying out optical measurements at the single-particle level. We have found that the interactions between two dielectric nanospheres and between one dielectric nanosphere and one gold nanosphere are not as strong as that between two gold nanospheres. This result has been understood to result from the small electromagnetic field enhancement of dielectric nanoparticles and the confinement of the enhanced electromagnetic field within the dielectric nanoparticle. Moreover, we have also studied the substrate effect on the electromagnetic resonances of the cuprous nanospheres. The considered substrates include indium tin oxide-coated glass slides, silicon wafers and gold films. The cuprous nanospheres show rich colors when supported on indium tin oxide-coated glass slides and silicon wafers. The nanospheres on gold films show largely redshifted electromagnetic resonances, and a new magnetic resonance mode. The large redshifts and the appearance of a new magnetic resonance mode are ascribed to the strong interaction between the electromagnetic resonance modes in the nanospheres and their image modes in the gold film. The effects of the different substrates have been understood through theoretical calculations and numerical simulations. In one sense, dielectric nanoparticles supported on gold films can be treated as dimers made of two dielectric nanoparticles. The third objective is to study the surface-enhanced fluorescence and Raman scattering performances of submicrometer dielectric nanoparticles and the dimers mentioned above. This objective has been well accomplished. We have coated organic dye molecules on the colloidal cuprous oxide nanospheres and studied the fluorescence emission of the hybrid nanoparticles and the resonance coupling between the Mie resonances of the single-crystalline cuprous oxide nanospheres and the excitons of the dye aggregates. For the cuprous oxide nanospheres, the splitting of the scattering peak is observed upon the coating of rhodamine aggregates. The peak splitting results from the resonance coupling between the dipole Mie resonances in the oxide nanospheres and the excitons in the dye aggregates. A mode splitting of 0.30 eV is determined from the anticrossing branches of the hybridized modes. This work deepens our understanding on the coupling between Mie resonances, especially in moderate-refractive-index nanostructures, and molecular excitons. We have also evaluated the surface-enhanced Raman scattering of the dielectric oxide nanospheres deposited on different substrates. The Raman scattering measurements reveals that large electromagnetic field enhancements are produced in the gap region between the oxide nanosphere and the substrate. The average intensities of the Raman scattering peaks of the cuprous oxide nanospheres supported on the different substrates are in the order of gold films > silicon wafers > indium tin oxide-coated glass slides. Moreover, europium-doped submicrometer zirconia spheres are synthesized by aerosol spray. Their diameters range from ~100 nm to ~2000 nm. Single-particle scattering and fluorescence measurements show that the magnetic resonance modes dominate the electromagnetic resonances of the doped zirconia spheres. The magnetic dipole emission from the doped euporium ions is enhanced by the magnetic resonances of the spheres under the resonant conditions. Careful analysis reveals that the magnetic resonances supported by the spheres preferentially enhance the magnetic dipole emission of the doped europium ions. The experimental results are in good agreement with numerical simulations, where the Purcell factors of the electric and magnetic dipole emissions of the europium ions are determined as functions of diameter. Furthermore, the emission spectra measured from heterostructures made of gold nanospheres and the europium-doped spheres indicate that the interaction between the magnetic dipole emission and the plasmon resonance is much weaker than that between the electric dipole emissions and the plasmon resonance. This study opens a new route for fully using the magnetic resonances confined inside all-dielectric nanoresonators to control the magnetic dipole emissions from embedded quantum emitters. The fourth objective is to fabricate all-dielectric and dielectric/metal oligomers out of dielectric and plasmonic metal nanoparticles and study the electric/magnetic resonance interactions in these oligomers. This objective has been realized completely. Two major fabrication approaches have been tested. The first is based on the capillary force. In one route, the different nanoparticles are mixed together in solutions and then deposited on different substrates. In another route, the solution of one type of nanoparticles is deposited on the substrates. After the substrate is dried, the solution of another type of nanoparticles is deposited. In both routes, the solvent flow during the drying process on the substrate pulls the nanoparticles together. The yield of the oligomers is affected by the solvent drying speed and the particle concentration. The second approach is based on trenches fabricated by electron-beam lithography. A positive electron-resist is employed to fabricate trenches of different lateral sizes and depths on substrates through exposure to an electron beam. The nanoparticle dispersion solution is then deposited on the substrate with trenches. During the drying process, the nanoparticles are pulled into the trenches. The number and shape of the oligomers are determined by the lateral sizes and shape of the trenches. In addition, the nanoparticles can be assembled laterally or vertically. We have measured the forward and backward scattering spectra of the oligomers made by the first approach. The oligomers show intriguing scattering features and exhibit distinct forward and backward scattering spectra. Numerical simulations have been performed to understand the scattering spectra. However, we have not been able to obtain consistent understanding. The major reason is that our fabrication approach does not allow us to systematically change the geometrical and dimensional parameters of the oligomers. We have difficulty in measuring the scattering spectra of the oligomers fabricated by the second approach. The electron resist hinders the scattering measurements. The oligomers tend to be destroyed if the resist is removed.

14320916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14320916.value: The major findings and research outcome from this project are in three aspects: publications, PhD student training and research collaboration. A total of 6 publications have been produced from this project. In the beginning of the project, we spent time on studying the literature about dielectric nanoparticles and nanostructures, including their synthesis, coupling among dielectric nanoparticles, coupling of dielectric nanoparticles with substrates and plasmonic metal nanoparticles, and their applications. We summarized our understanding in a review article, which is published on Physics Reports 2017, 701, 1-50. Aerosol spray was employed to synthesize submicrometer titania and zirconia spheres. The crystalline structure of the spheres can be well controlled. Their scattering images and spectra were systematically investigated as functions of diameter. Their size-dependent electromagnetic resonances were well understood. These results were published in Advanced Optical Materials 2019, 7, 1900396. A wet-chemistry method was used to synthesize cuprous oxide nanospheres of different diameters. The effect of different substrates on the electromagnetic resonances of the cuprous oxide nanospheres was ascertained. The SERS performances of the cuprous oxide nanospheres on the substrates were evaluated. Moreover, the coupling between the electromagnetic resonances and the excitons of dye aggregates was examined by coating the dye molecules on the cuprous oxide nanospheres. A clear anticrossing behavior with a mode splitting of 0.30 eV was observed. These results were published on Particle & Particle Systems Characterization 2020, 37, 2000106 and ACS Photonics 2018, 5, 3838-3848. In addition, a closely related type of plasmonic nanostructure was prepared out of gold nanoplates and gold nanospheres, where the nanoplates were deposited on silicon substrates and the nanosphere was positioned on the top of the nanoplate. The gap region between the nanoplate and nanosphere was filled with different molecules, which were either conducting or non-conducting. Rich plasmon modes were observed on this type of nanostructure, including high-order charge transfer plasmon and Fano resonance. These results were published on ACS Nano 2018, 12, 12541-12550 and Nanoscale 2020, 12, 1975-1984. Two PhD students have been trained on this project. One is in materials science and engineering and worked on the cuprous nanospheres. The other is in physics and worked on the titania and zirconia nanospheres. Through this project, research collaboration between Professor Hai-Qing Lin from Beijing Computational Science and Research Center and my group has been greatly strengthened. Four of the above 6 publications are co-authored by Professor Lin and me.

14320916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14320916.value: Aerosol spray has been used by us to prepare transition metal oxide nanospheres. It is versatile for making various porous and nonporous metal oxide spheres. It can potentially be scaled up for continuous production. In particular, titania and zirconia spheres have been successfully prepared by this method. We have found that titania and zirconia spheres can be transformed to titanium nitride and zirconium nitride in an ammonia atmosphere at high temperatures. Titanium and zirconium nitrides exhibit strong plasmon resonance. Compared with traditional noble metal nanomaterials, nitrides possess general advantages of low cost, high chemical and thermal stability, corrosion resistance, and mechanical hardness. The study of plasmonic nitrides has remained in an early stage. Plasmonic metal nitride nanostructures have mostly been fabricated by physical methods, which are tedious, expensive, limited in shape control, and difficult to be scaled up. Physically fabricated nanostructures are also often attached to substrates, which makes it inconvenient to integrate them with other nanomaterials. Chemical synthesis of plasmonic metal nitride nanoparticles has remained challenging. We will combine aerosol spray together with ammonia treatment to synthesize metal nitride nanomaterials, study their plasmonic properties, and explore their plasmon-enabled applications. Proposals have been prepared and submitted based on this topic.

14320916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14320916.value: Nanoscale light-matter interactions are both fundamentally interesting from the physics point of view and will bring many unprecedented technological breakthroughs, such as ultrathin, high-performance lenses and all-optical ultrafast switching. To realize strong light-matter interactions at nanoscale, nanoresonators that can tightly focus light at controlled wavelengths are highly desired. There have been two general types of nanoresonators, which are based on plasmonic metals and dielectric materials. Plasmonic metals are powerful and versatile in light control. However, they suffer from inevitable resistive loss due to the movement of charge carriers. Dielectric nanomaterials exhibit small loss and offer an alternative to plasmonic metals, because their electromagnetic resonances are based on polarization charges and displacement current. In this project, we have developed chemical methods for the synthesis of different dielectric nanospheres. By combining together experiments, theoretical modeling and numerical simulations, we have achieved deep understanding of the electromagnetic resonances of dielectric nanospheres and their interactions with substrates and different quantum emitters. Our project demonstrates the feasibility of using all-dielectric nanoresonators to manipulate the optical properties of other species. In addition, our cost-effective and productive chemical synthesis method opens up many possibilities for the wide use of dielectric nanoresonators in the field of nanophotonics.

14321116.label: Realisation of objectives
14321116.value: All three objectives have been successfully realized. (1) RIα peptide dimer and RIAD peptide have been engineered to realize the covalent conjugation of enzyme complexes. Cysteine containing variants of RIα peptide and RIAD peptide were engineered, air oxidation leads to covalent protein complexes with different stoichiometry and shapes. (2) Multienzyme complexes of menaquinone biosynthetic enzymes and carotenoid biosynthetic enzymes were both constructed in vitro and in vivo, and their catalytic properties fully explored. (3) Orthogonal conjugation reactions have led to different enzyme complexes both in vitro and in vivo. The details are elaborated below. RIα-RIAD mediated assembly of multienzyme complexes. The RIα peptide forms a stable dimer and then binds with RIAD peptide with nM affinity. We then designed cysteine residues at selected positions of RIα and RIAD based on the crystal structure of the complex. The noncovalent peptide – peptide interaction will bring these two cysteine residues into proximity. Several oxidation conditions were explored, including DMSO oxidation and air oxidation. Eventually, we discovered that air oxidation gave the mildest condition to covalently crosslink the protein complexes. Therefore, we constructed the MenD-MenH complexes in 4:2, 4:8, and 4:16 ratios, and verified the complex structures by an electron microscope. Besides mediating multienzyme complexation in vitro, the RIα-RIAD interaction also directs the formation of enzyme complexes in vivo inside bacterial cells. By appending Idi and CrtE with RIα and RIAD peptide respectively, we successfully observed the assembly of these two enzymes in cells. Three lines of evidence have been acquired. First, immune-TEM reveals that Idi has relocated from the cytosol to the cell membrane where CrtE is located. Second, fluorescently labeled Idi and CrtE co-localized in the cells. Third, the FRET signal between fluorescently labeled Idi and CrtE showed that these two enzymes have been assembled inside the cells. Enzyme assembly increases the cascade biosynthesis efficiency. Multienzyme complexes are known to promote substrate and intermediate transfer between sequential reactions. We next measured the overall cascade catalytic rate of the MenD-MenH complexes and observed that higher order of enzyme assembly corresponds to increased catalytic rates. Specifically, the MenD-MenH complex of 4:16 showed the highest catalytic rates than the MenD-MenH complex of 4:2 or 4:8 ratios. In vivo activity measurement also showed that Idi-CrtE complexes showed significantly higher catalytic efficiency towards the biosynthesis of beta-carotenoids, such as astaxanthin and lycopene in E. coli cells. We brought these strains to fermenters and discovered at least a 7-fold increase in the production of the yield of total beta-carotenoids include astaxanthin, zeaxanthin, canthaxanthin, beta-cryptoxanthin, lycopene, and beta-carotene. The highest increase reached 70-fold. We also measured the concentrations of the intermediates and prove that assembly of Idi and CrtE streamlines the biosynthesis of carotenoids and significantly increase the metabolic flux. To prove the general applicability of this strategy, we also assembled Idi and CrtE in yeast cells, in S. cerevisiae and observed a significant increase of the product. Taken together, this result shows that assembling the key enzymes increases the metabolic flux in biosynthesis and leads to significant improvement of the catalytic rate and final outcome. Besides the RIα-RIAD interactions, other interactions that are orthogonal with this pair can also mediate multienzyme assembly. For example, we explored the use of covalent protein reaction pairs, SpyCatcher and SpyTag, and SnoopCatcher and SnoopTag to assemble three enzymes in the mevalonate biosynthetic pathway, ACAT, HMGS, and HMGR in E. coli cells. The three enzymes were covalently assembled together by site-specific isopeptide bonds to form 1:1:0, 1:0:1, 1:1:1, 1:2:2 complexes. We show that these complexes can be purified from cell lysates, and mass spectrometry provides compelling evidence that the covalently linked complexes indeed contains the three enzymes. Electron microscope revealed that these complexes are ellipsoidal nanostructures with hollow interior space and uniform thickness and shapes with diameters around 20-40 nm. The strains contain multienzyme complexes also showed significantly higher catalytic rates. Other groups of interactions are the docking domains (DDs), natural linkers in polyketide synthases. The docking domains (DDs) are 25-residue two-helix, pseudosymmetric peptides that bind speciﬁcally in pairs and mediate the self-assembly of the multimodular polyketide synthases. Each pair has a binding aﬃnity of 1−10 μM, and diﬀerent pairs have minimal cross interactions, making them ideal orthogonal pairs to assemble enzymes together. We utilized four diﬀerent pairs of docking domains, namely, BaeM/BaeN, MlnB/MlnC, MlnD/MlnE, and VirA/VirFG, from diﬀerent sources to assemble menaquinone biosynthetic enzymes MenD and MenH on a protein scaffold. We then demonstrated that the enzyme complexes showed a significantly higher catalytic rate than three enzymes without assembly. Taken together, all three objectives have been successfully fulfilled.

14321116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14321116.value: This project has led to several significant outcomes. We demonstrate that peptide – peptide interactions such as RIα-RIAD can be utilized to assemble sequential enzymes in biosynthetic pathways into multienzyme complexes, and elevate the catalytic efficiency of biosynthesis. Several systems have been showcased to prove this novel statement. Assembly of menaquinone biosynthetic enzymes in different ratios and stoichiometry gave complexes with different shapes and geometry, and lead to a significant increase of the catalytic rate. Assembly of beta-carotenoid biosynthetic enzymes Idi and CrtE results in novel bacterial strains that can produce beta-carotenoids with a record high yield. The same assembly strategy also gives yeast strains with much higher catalytic efficiency than without assembly. Taken together, the following conclusions were drawn: (1) We prove that multienzyme assembly is a powerful strategy to increase the catalytic rate of biosynthesis both in vitro and in vivo. (2) Assembly of Idi with downstream enzyme CrtE can direct the toxic intermediates IPP to the downstream pathway and alleviate its toxicity and promote cell growth. (3) Several bacterial and yeast strains that we produce have significant commercial values in the biosynthesis of carotenoids. Several papers have already been published to report the results above. The major findings are published in Nature Communications. This work was also reported in international conferences as invited talks. A total of four Ph.D. students received training under this project, with two have graduated with a Ph.D. degree during the period.
