14321116.value: This research paves the road towards the future development of multienzyme complexes for biosynthesis. Its significance lies in the potential application in synthetic biology and the biosynthesis of valuable products. One highlight of our work is that it is highly orthogonal with all the existing metabolic engineering strategies. Therefore, on top of all the optimizations of the metabolic pathway via the traditional methods, our enzyme assembly strategy can still significantly increase the product year by 5-10 folds. Based on these proof-of-principle results, we are developing more effective multienzyme assembly strategies and apply them to the biosynthesis of highly valuable natural products. These bacterial or yeast strains will high product titers will have marked commercial values. We will apply for grant supports to commercialize the use of these strains in large-scale fermentations, through collaboration with industrial partners. Eventually, these endeavors will significantly reduce the cost of production of key drug intermediates or other valuable chemicals.

14321116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14321116.value: Enzymes are naturally evolved catalysts that can convert low-value chemicals to high-value ones. By linking enzymes together, we form nanomachinery like little instruments that can generate products in highly efficient ways both in the test tube and in cells. Biosynthesis aims to replace the traditional chemical synthesis which uses compounds from fossil fuels to synthesize household chemicals. A significant reduction of solvents and chemical wastes makes biosynthesis a greener, environmentally more friendly, and more sustainable industry in the future.

14321416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14321416.value: 双自旋凝聚体里的量子相干和退相干

14321416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14321416.value: Quantum coherence is a fundamental feature to distinguish quantum systems from their classical counterparts. Quantum dynamics, such as the textbook example of a single spin precessing in a magnetic field, is a useful means to explore quantum coherence. Whereas quantum coherence and quantum dynamics of isolated non-interacting systems have been well understood, the decoherence introduced by interactions in many-body systems remains to be a crucial question for understanding how the quantum world in the microscopic level gradually evolves to the macroscopic classical one. In this project, we will theoretically study the quantum coherence and decoherence in the spin dynamics of a mixture of two species of spinful bosons, a new system that has been recently realised by an experimental group led by Professor Dajun Wang in my university. A unique feature of such a system is that, these two species of atoms, Rubidium (Rb) and Sodium (Na) with highly controllable microscopic parameters in experiments, have spin-exchange interaction so that novel inter-species spin dynamics may rise. Whereas the spin exchange between Na and Rb has been observed and a simple Rabi oscillation picture well captures the dynamics in the weakly interacting regime, the quantum coherence and decoherence in the strongly interacting regime have not been systematically explored. Using both analytical and numerical approaches, we will explore how the inter- and intra-species interaction influence the quantum spin dynamics of two condensates of Rb and Na in both the continuum and the lattice. We will formulate suitable theoretical frameworks in the strongly interacting regime, where the simple Rabi oscillation picture is no longer applicable. We will study a number of fundamental questions regarding the underlying mechanism of decoherence, schemes to restore the quantum spin coherence, the connection between the lost of coherence in each individual species and the establishment of the inter-species correlations, the applications of the decoherence in quantum phase transitions, and the dynamical growth of spatial spin-spin correlations across the lattice. This project will deliver useful theoretical results of quantum spin dynamics in a new system that has not been studied systematically before. The outcome will provide new insights for manipulating and utilising quantum coherence and decoherence in interacting many-body systems. Our results are directly relevant to experiments. Professor Dajun Wang's group will test our theoretical predictions. Our results are also useful for other experimental groups working on spin dynamics of ultracold atoms. N/A

14322316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14322316.value: In this project we propose to investigate the swimming behavior of flagellated bacteria confined in two-dimensional space. Motile behavior of bacteria is of great ecological and medical significance because it is essential for bacterial dispersal, chemotaxis, and pathogenesis. A large number of bacterial species use flagellar motility to propel their motion. Flagellar motility in bulk fluids has been studied extensively. By contrast, flagellar motility in confined space where the motion of cells is physically restricted to be two-dimensional (2D) is less well understood, despite the fact that 2D bacterial swimming in confined space is ubiquitous in natural environment and in clinical settings. In this project we propose to investigate 2D bacterial swimming behavior at the single-cell level. The research plan stems from our recent finding that bacteria in 2D confinement display several surprising features in their swimming patterns. In particular, we found that cells in 2D confinement tend to swim in a cooperative manner. Results from our computational model suggest that this cooperative swimming behavior promotes population spreading in 2D environments. Here we plan to further investigate the mechanism for the observed cooperative swimming behavior. We will also study the population spreading and chemotactic response of cells in 2D confinement. The project lies at the interface of biology and physics. 2D bacterial swimming behavior is relevant to bacterial colonization in unsaturated soils and bacterial spreading in interstitial fluids. Also the motion and interaction patterns of single cells in 2D confinement to be uncovered in the project will help to elucidate collective motion in bacterial colonies, which is a topic of increasing interest to microbiology and physics. Overall, results obtained in the project will provide essential information for understanding bacterial colonization, spreading, and collective dynamics in 2D environments. 此項目將研究細菌在受限的二維環境中的運動行為。 細菌的運動行為與細菌的擴散，趨化性以及致病性有密切關係，因此具有重要的生態學和醫學意義。許多種類的細菌利用鞭毛運動。旋轉的鞭毛可以產生推力，驅使細菌在液體環境中前進。人們對於在不受限（即三維）的液體環境中的鞭毛運動機制已經作了大量的研究，然而對於細菌在受限的二維環境中的運動行為仍然缺乏了解，儘管後者在自然界和臨床環境中相當普遍。 在此項目中我們計劃在單細胞層次研究細菌在受限的二維環境中的運動，相互作用模式和機制，以及趨化性。在前期工作中我們已經發現細菌在二維環境下會做協同運動。利用計算模型，我們推測這種協同運動有助於細菌群體在受限環境中的擴散。我們計劃用更加嚴格的實驗手段來探索這一協同運動行為的物理機制。 此項目涉及物理學和生物學的交叉領域，所得到的結果會增進人們對細菌在受限環境中的定殖、擴散和集體運動等行為的認識。

14322316.label: Realisation of objectives
14322316.value: With the funding from this grant, we have realized both objectives. We have investigated bacterial motion in confined two dimensional space, in fluid films of a thickness ~2 micron under well controlled physicochemical conditions (Objective 1). We discovered that motile cells of peritrichously flagellated bacteria in such confined 2D space can self-organize into two adjacent, counter-rotating rings that surround the entire colony. To understand the mechanism of motile ring formation, we first examined the motion pattern of individual cells at low densities. We found that cells colliding with the edge of such liquid drops tended to turn CW with respect to the contact point about an axis normal to the underlying substrate and subsequently move to the right along the edge. Working with our collaborators we have understood the mechanism of self-organization of the motile rings (Objective 2). We also revealed that motility heterogeneity can promote the spatial segregation of subpopulations via a dynamic motility selection process. The dynamic motility selection is enabled by speed-dependent persistence time bias of single-cell motion, which presumably arises from physical interaction between cells in a densely packed swarm. We further showed that the dynamic motility selection may contribute to collective drug tolerance of swarming colonies by segregating subpopulations with transient drug tolerance to the colony edge (Objective 2).

14322316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14322316.value: Two major research outputs arose from this project: 1. Haoran Xu, Justas Dauparas, Debasish Das, Eric Lauga, Yilin Wu (2019) Self-organization of swimmers drives long-range fluid transport in bacterial colonies. Nature Communications. 10, 1792. Bacteria commonly live in structured communities that affect human health and influence ecological systems. Heterogeneous populations, such as motile and non-motile populations, often coexist in bacteria communities. Motile subpopulations in microbial communities are believed to be important to dispersal, quest for food, and material transport. However, except in circumstances where motile cells drive colony expansion (e.g. bacterial swarming), the physiological functions of motile subpopulations in bacterial communities are largely unclear. Here we discovered that motile cells in sessile colonies of peritrichously flagellated bacteria can self-organize into two adjacent, centimeter-scale motile rings surrounding the entire colony. The motile rings arise from spontaneous phase separation of a homogeneous swimmer suspension; the process is mediated by cell-substrate hydrodynamic interaction and shear-induced depletion. As a result of this phase separation, cells drive fluid flows to circulate around the colony at a constant peak speed of ~30 µm/s, providing a stable and high-speed avenue for directed material transport at the macroscopic scale. These findings present a unique form of bacterial self-organization that influences population structure and material distribution in bacterial communities. 2. Wenlong Zuo & Yilin Wu (2020) Dynamic motility selection drives population segregation in a bacterial swarm. Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA. 117(9):4693-4700. Two dimensional Structured microbial communities provide model systems to study space competition during range expansion. Here we use bacterial swarms to investigate how single-cell motility contributes to space competition among heterogeneous bacterial populations during range expansion. Our results revealed that motility heterogeneity can promote the spatial segregation of subpopulations via a dynamic motility selection process. The dynamic motility selection is enabled by speed-dependent persistence time bias of single-cell motion, which presumably arises from physical interaction between cells in a densely packed swarm. We further showed that the dynamic motility selection may contribute to collective drug tolerance of swarming colonies by segregating subpopulations with transient drug tolerance to the colony edge. Our results illustrate that motility heterogeneity, or "motility fitness," can play a greater role than growth rate fitness in determining the short-term spatial structure of expanding populations.

14322316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14322316.value: The mechanism underlying motile-cell phase separation deserves further study in the context of flagellar hydrodynamics and active matter self-organization. Shear-induced depletion may account for the accumulation of cells that leads to the formation of inner motile ring, but it does not explain the nematic order of inner motile ring. The emergence of a dense nematic band out of the dilute phase of self-propelled polar objects (e.g. bacterial swimmers) is non-trivial. The unique mechanism of bacterial self-organization we uncovered here may be important to the physiology and stress response of bacterial communities in widespread environments. Phase separation of motile subpopulations apparently reshapes the population structure in bacterial communities, which could facilitate the initiation of dispersal or range expansion. In addition, the phase separation of swimmers generates highly directed fluid flows, providing a stable high-speed avenue for large-scale directed material transport in bacterial communities. The empirical relation between cell speed and motion bias we uncovered in 2D bacterial swarms offers a unique mechanism via which individual motility may contribute to space competition among heterogeneous microbial populations during range expansion. Like in other organisms, space competition in microbial communities is crucial to population survival and interaction. Our findings are therefore relevant to microbial stress response and ecology. The findings are also relevant to range expansion in other biological systems, such as tumor invasion and collective stress tolerance of cancer cells in densely packed environments.

14322316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14322316.value: More than a means of culturing bacteria, colony mode of bacterial growth is a model system to study structured microbial communities. Understanding the physiology of colonies may guide the treatment of chronic infections and provide useful information for industrial applications, such as food hygiene, bioremediation, and anti-biofouling. Here we sought to understand the physiological function of motile cell populations that often persist in bacterial colonies. We revealed that motile sub-populations are able to self-organize and drive directed fluid flows at the colony scale. Our results reveal a unique means of large-scale active transport of materials in bacterial colonies, and offer an intriguing example of active matter self-organization. Microbial communities offer unique systems to study how an individual’s motility contributes to space competition among heterogeneous microbial populations during range expansion. Here we show that motility heterogeneity can promote the spatial segregation of subpopulations in structured microbial communities via a dynamic motility selection mechanism. Our findings are relevant to microbial stress response and microbial ecology. The results may also provide new insight to range expansion in other biological systems, such as tumor invasion and collective stress tolerance of cancer cells in densely packed environments.

14322516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14322516.value: 求解非線性逆問題的直接採樣方法

14322516.label: Project Objectives
14322516.value: We propose and formulate a general framework for constructing direct sampling-type methods for nonlinear inverse problems of both stationary and time-dependent partial differential equations, based on two fundamental criteria. We apply and verify our new general framework to several challenging ill-posed inverse problems, including inverse acoustic and electromagnetic scattering, electric impedance tomography, diffusive optical tomography, elliptic and parabolic Robin inverse problems. Then we derive the explicit formulation of the direct sampling-type method corresponding to each of these inverse problems. We conduct a large number of numerical experiments for the direct sampling-type methods formulated in Objective 2 for our concerned nonlinear inverse problems, especially we shall test the effectiveness and robustness of the methods with real experimental data (see section 8(c) for Collaborations for more detail). We analyze different sets of two fundamental criteria that are satisfied by the direct sampling-type methods developed in Objective 2 for two most frequently used measurement surfaces, and find the most feasible and effective set of two fundamental criteria for each concerned nonlinear inverse problem. With the approximate solutions provided by the new direct sampling-type methods as the ideal initializations, we apply and improve some existing advanced nonlinear optimization approaches to achieve more accurate numerical reconstructions for our concerned nonlinear inverse problems, in the cases when highly accurate solutions are required.

14322516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14322516.value: 這個研究項目的主要目的是發展一些高效、穩定和計算量小的直接採樣方法，用於求解各類非線性的不適定反問題。求解微分方程的正問題通常是適定的，但反問題大部分都是不適定的，特別是反問題的解關於測量數據的變化是不穩定的。所以，反問題的求解比正問題要難很多。 現有的大部分求解反問題的數學方法都是基於非線性優化，加上適當的正則化。這些優化問題離散之后，一般是非線性的，非凸的，且規模大，所以數值求解非常困難。 我們將發展的直接採樣方法，不需求解任何微分方程正問題，計算量小，且非常穩定。最重要的優點是測量數據很少時也可應用。這類新方法將在求解非線性反問題中起到很重要的作用。

14322516.label: Realisation of objectives
14322516.value: We developed and studied a series of new and effective direct sampling methods (DSMs) in [1][2][3][4] for many important nonlinear inverse problems of recovering multiple stationary or moving physical inhomogeneous inclusions (including multiple inclusions of different physical nature), such as inverse acoustic or electromagnetic scattering, electric impedance tomography, diffusive optical tomography, etc. These DSMs proved to work effectively for those practically important applications when very limited measurement data is available. We showed these DSMs are able to locate multiple stationary or moving extended objects, and track moving objects stably and efficiently. This is the first robust DSMs in the literature for locating and tracking time-dependent moving inhomogeneous inclusions as well as multiple objects of different physical nature. The novel DSMs differ essentially from most existing DSMs for stationary or time-harmonic nonlinear inverse problems, and demonstrate three crucial features: very robust against the noise in the observation data, easy to implement and computationally inexpensive. Mathematical derivations and justifications of DSMs and the desired fundamental criteria are provided. The DSMs we developed in [1][2][3][4] can provide desired approximate solutions when very limited measurement data is available in many practical applications. When measurement data is sufficient, the DSMs may further serve as a satisfactory initial approximation for those expensive optimization approaches to achieve more accurate solutions. We developed in [5] two numerical optimization strategies for solving general elliptic and parabolic inverse Robin problems. Although nonlinear optimization approaches are most popular, they are known to be highly nonlinear, non-convex and unstable due to the severe ill-posedness of the inverse problems. To overcome these drawbacks, we proposed in [5] an improved and very efficient Levenberg-Marquardt (L-M) method to solve the nonlinear optimizations for inverse Robin problems. With this method, we need only to solve a convex optimization at each iteration, whose minimizer can be computed explicitly, in combination with the surrogate functional technique. We also established the quadratic rate of convergence of the L-M method for both elliptic and parabolic inverse Robin problems. This is the first time in the literature to demonstrate the quadratic convergence of the L-M method for nonlinear inverse problems, much more challenging than the convergence for the direct optimal control or nonlinear optimizations. In combination with traditional iterative methods, effective preconditioners have proved to be a powerful strategy for solving large-scale discrete systems arising from forward PDEs, which are the main computational efforts in most optimization approaches for nonlinear inverse problems. In this project, we made a series of very promising progresses in this direction in [8][9]. We proposed in [9] a novel edge element method for solving the optimal control of the stationary electromagnetic Maxwell's system. This new method does not require the usual saddle-point formulation and solves only positive definite systems, for which fast and optimal preconditioning solvers are available in the literature. We also established optimal error estimates and strong convergence for both edge element solutions and discrete Gauss' laws. Furthermore, we proposed and analyzed in [8] three block preconditioners for solving electromagnetic wave scattering problems. When the scattering systems are discretized by finite element methods, the resulting discrete systems are always large-scale, complex and indefinite, so are highly challenging to solve. We reformulated the systems into a real symmetric but indefinite saddle-point system. We presented two block triangular preconditioners that can preserve the symmetry of the systems, and were able to estimate both the lower and upper bounds of positive and negative eigenvalues of the preconditioned systems. Moreover, we managed to work out a spectral estimate of the preconditioned system for a very effective preconditioner that was recently developed by PI of this project. In the second part of [8], we derived and proposed two new preconditioners for the saddle-point systems arising from the edge element discretization of the time-harmonic electromagnetic Maxwell systems. With rigorous analyses, we demonstrated that the most desired preconditioned conjugate gradient method work effectively and stably for the saddle-point systems when wave numbers are not too large, while other popular methods like MINRES can apply when wave numbers are large. We established the explicit spectral estimates of the resulting preconditioned systems for these new preconditioners. Super-resolution is a very important physical phenomenon that was observed some years ago in imaging extended targets with high contrast. We investigated in [4] the super-resolution of a highly nonlinear inverse problem, namely the inverse acoustic scattering problem (also for electromagnetic wave in TE and TM modes) with high-contrast targets. We developed a general theory to analyze mathematically this physically observed very important phenomenon about super-resolution. Particularly, we derived and justified the super-resolution at a set of specific high contrast values based on a novel concept of scattering coefficients. This work provides the first rigorous mathematical theory to justify the super-resolution in the context of imaging high-contrast inclusions. Our findings may help develop resonant structures for resolution enhancement. Nonlinear inverse problems are mostly ill-posed. There are some fundamental mathematical issues that can help us better understand inverse problems and construct effective numerical solvers. The first fundamental issue is when an inverse problem is uniquely identifiable. Continued with a series of our earlier investigations on this topic, we successfully solved in a recent work [7] an open unique identifiability for some inverse acoustic and electromagnetic scattering problems. We demonstrated that for some typical and important acoustic or electromagnetic scattering problems, the electric far-field data from a single incoming wave is sufficient to determine a penetrable scatterer of rectangular type uniquely. We are extending this theory to penetrable scatterers of general polyhedral type. Another fundamental issue is how to regularize an inverse problem to reduce its ill-posedness through a series of regularized approximate solutions. Most existing analyses of regularizing operators and regularized solutions are qualitative and does not give explicit convergence rates of regularized solutions. We made an important effort in [6] to fill this gap, and proposed a systematic approach to study explicit convergence rates of regularized solutions for ill-posed backward evolution equations associated with general sectorial or half-strip operators, which cover a much more general class of PDEs than the existing self-adjoint or coercive ones. Moreover, we established in general Banach spaces the connection between the prior estimate of the exact initial data of the backward evolution equations and the explicit convergence rate of the regularized solutions. Inverse problems of fractional differential equations are known to be less ill-posed than integer equations. Therefore it appears to be a promising strategy to use fractional equations as the forward models in inverse problems. This needs some quantitative mathematical and numerical understanding of fractional differential equations. In our recent work [10], we made some significant progresses on this topic, and established the dissipativity, asymptotic stability and contractivity of fractional differential equations with algebraically contractive rate mathematically and numerically. Through this RGC project, we carried out a great number of numerical experiments to show the stability, effectiveness, efficiency, and other behaviors such as super-resolution, of all our numerical methods, especially the DSMs, for various inverse problems. The experiments demonstrated our new methods can provide novel alternative promising strategies for solving nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems of recovering multiple stationary or moving physical inhomogeneous inclusions. In addition, these numerical experiments helped us confirm our theoretical predictions and improve our numerical methods.

With the approximate solutions provided by the new direct sampling-type methods as the ideal initializations, we apply and improve some existing advanced nonlinear optimization approaches to achieve more accurate numerical reconstructions for our concerned nonlinear inverse problems, in the cases when highly accurate solutions are required.

14322516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14322516.value: We developed new and effective direct sampling methods (DSMs) in [1][2][3][4] for many important nonlinear inverse problems of recovering multiple stationary or moving physical inhomogeneous inclusions. These DSMs work effectively for those practically important applications when very limited measurement data is available, and demonstrate three crucial features. Mathematical derivations and justifications of DSMs and the fundamental criteria are provided. We developed in [5] two computationally very fast optimization strategies for solving general elliptic and parabolic inverse Robin problems, and established the quadratic convergence of the methods. We proposed in [9] a novel method for the optimal control in the stationary electromagnetic system, and established error estimates and strong convergence for edge element solutions and discrete Gauss' laws. We proposed and analyzed in [8] block preconditioners for solving electromagnetic wave scattering problems, and estimated the lower and upper bounds of eigenvalues of the preconditioned systems. We also gave a spectral estimate of the preconditioned system for an existing effective preconditioner. Furthermore, we derived and proposed two new preconditioners for the saddle-point systems arising from the time-harmonic electromagnetic systems, and demonstrated that the preconditioned conjugate gradient method work effectively for the saddle-point systems with small wave numbers, otherwise other popular methods can apply. We investigated in [4] the super-resolution of the highly nonlinear inverse acoustic or electromagnetic scattering problem with high-contrast targets. We developed a general theory to analyze the super-resolution mathematically, and justified the super-resolution at specific high contrast values. This provides the first rigorous theory to justify the super-resolution for imaging high-contrast inclusions. We solved in [7] an open unique identifiability for some typical inverse acoustic or electromagnetic scattering problems, and demonstrated that the electric far-field data from a single incoming wave is sufficient to determine a penetrable scatterer of rectangular type uniquely. We proposed in [6] a systematic approach to study explicit convergence rates of regularized solutions for ill-posed backward evolution equations associated with general sectorial or half-strip operators, established in Banach spaces the connection between the prior estimate of the exact initial data and the explicit convergence rate of the regularized solutions. In our recent work [10], we established the dissipativity, asymptotic stability and contractivity of fractional differential equations with algebraically contractive rate mathematically and numerically. We carried out a great number of numerical experiments to show the stability, effectiveness, efficiency and other behaviors of our numerical methods, especially the DSMs, for various inverse problems.

14322516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14322516.value: We developed effective direct sampling methods (DSMs) in [1][2][3][4] for many nonlinear inverse problems of recovering multiple stationary or moving physical inhomogeneous inclusions. These DSMs proved to work effectively even when very limited measurement data is available, and demonstrate three crucial features. It is very interesting and important to extend these DSMs for more nonlinear inverse problems from applications, and develop a general theory to study the mathematical and numerical stability and convergence of these DSMs. We developed in [5] very fast optimization strategies for solving general elliptic and parabolic inverse Robin problems, and established their quadratic convergence. It is very interesting and significant to establish similar numerical strategies and their quadratic convergence for other important nonlinear inverse problems. We proposed and studied in [8][9] several efficient solvers for Maxwell optimal control problems, and analyzed a couple of effective preconditioners for electromagnetic wave scattering problems. It is an important research topic to develop similar numerical solvers and effective preconditioners for other forward models of PDEs that are frequently used in nonlinear inverse problems. It is a physically and mathematically very interesting research direction to extend our theoretical findings in [4] about super-resolution to nonlinear and non-wave type inverse problems.

14322516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14322516.value: In this three-year RGC project, we have developed a series of efficient and robust sampling-type methods for solving several challenging nonlinear inverse problems from real applications. Most existing sampling-type methods in the literature work only for a special inverse problem each, their constructions and motivations are very different from each other, their derivations and justifications are mostly restricted to a set of special physical and mathematical conditions. These new sampling-type methods are constructed under a general framework with two fundamental criteria. These new numerical strategies and framework can help us greatly improve the performance of existing methods for various nonlinear inverse problems, and guide non-math experts to construct new and more efficient and robust sampling-type methods. This project and its achievements are of essential significance to numerical solutions of highly challenging nonlinear inverse problems from physical, engineering and medical applications. More importantly, the findings in this project can help us better understand general sampling-type numerical methods and their stability and convergence behaviors so that we may design more efficient and reliable new reconstruction methods.

14323116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14323116.value: The proposed research aims to investigate how agricultural emissions of nitrogen compounds into the atmosphere may influence air quality and climate through various physical, chemical and biological feedback mechanisms. Over the past century, increased food production for the growing world population has contributed to a cascade of environmental problems, with significant impacts on human health. Many of the impacts are attributable to the widespread application of chemical fertilizer, which has led to substantial release of reactive nitrogen gases into the atmosphere and contributed to particle air pollution and global warming. A realistic assessment of the environmental impacts of future food production is thus necessary for long-term sustainable planning concerning public health, food security and climate management. A major uncertainty is associated with the biogeochemical and vegetation feedbacks induced by excess nitrogen deposition. When nitrogen-containing particles in air are washed onto the land surface by rainfall, the reactive nitrogen may modify soil microbial processes and enhance vegetation growth, generating downstream effects that alter both soil emissions and plant-atmosphere interactions. This constitutes important feedbacks between agriculture, atmospheric composition and biogeochemical cycles, which are largely unexplored but potentially significant with ramifications for both air quality and climate. To address this gap of knowledge, we will implement a new set of schemes for the carbon-nitrogen cycle in the Community Earth System Model to simulate the immediate interactions and feedbacks involving nitrogen exchange between the atmosphere and terrestrial ecosystems in a fully coupled configuration. We will conduct a comprehensive suite of simulations to quantify the impacts of agricultural nitrogen emission on air quality and climate, including both the primary effects, and secondary effects through biogeochemical and vegetation feedbacks induced by nitrogen deposition. Simulations will be conducted with present-day conditions and under future (mid-21st century) scenarios of food production, land use and global warming. We will derive a more reliable set of future projections for concentrations of atmospheric pollutants and fluxes of long-lived greenhouse gases, which can then be used to evaluate the impacts on human health and long-term climate change. The anticipated findings are crucial for better policy formulation concerning air quality and agriculture, and will likely motivate the search for more sustainable farming strategies that can secure both food production and public health. The proposed full carbon-nitrogen coupling between the atmosphere and terrestrial ecosystems will also represent an important contribution to geoscientific model development. 該項目旨在研究農業排放的氮化合物如何通過各種物理、化學和生物反饋機制影響空氣質素和氣候。在過去的一個世紀中，世界糧食生產不斷提高以應付急劇的人口增長，但同時造成嚴峻的環境問題，對人類健康的影響尤其顯著。大部分的影響可歸因於化學肥料的廣泛應用，這導致活性含氮氣體大量釋放到大氣中，並促進了粒子空氣污染和全球暖化。故此，為未來糧食生產對環境的影響做出切實的評估是必要的，因其涉及公共衛生、糧食安全和氣候管理的長期發展與規劃。一個主要的不確定性是關於過量的氮沉降而引起的生物地球化學和植被反饋作用。當空氣中含氮粒子被雨水衝到地面，粒子中的活性氮可改變土壤中的微生物過程，亦可提高植被的生長，繼而產生一系列次生影響，改變土壤氣體排放和植物大氣間的相互作用。這構成了農業、大氣成分和生物地球化學循環之間的反饋，這為空氣質量和氣候都可能帶來顯著的影響。 我們將在一個地球系統模式內碳氮循環的部分實施一套新的模型方案，以在一個完全耦合的配置下，模擬與大氣和陸地生態系統之間的氮交流相關的直接相互作用和反饋。我們會進行各項模擬實驗來量化農業氮排放對空氣質素和氣候的影響，包括原生作用和通過氮沉降引起的生物地球化學和植被反饋而產生的此生作用。模擬將與當今的條件下和未來糧食生產、土地利用和全球暖化的預測情況下進行，由此我們可以對大氣污染物和溫室氣體的濃度作出一系列更可靠的預測，然後用於評估對人類健康和長期氣候變化的影響。預計研究結果對制定更有效的空氣質素和農業政策至關重要，並藉此促使決策者更積極找尋更多可持續的農業策略，以保衛未來糧食生產和公共健康。在模式內建立大氣和陸地生態系統之間的全面碳氮耦合，也將為地球科學模型發展作出重要貢獻。

14323116.label: Realisation of objectives
14323116.value: The research plan and activities set forth in the proposal have been followed closely and conducted accordingly, and the three objectives have been achieved to a highly satisfactory extent. Some aspects of the project have also been further expanded beyond the original objectives, leading to significant results. The findings of this project have led to five publications (three already published, one currently in press, and one currently under review). Objective #1 and Objective #2 have been successfully achieved by: 1) implementing into the CESM a new prognostic ammonia emission model and two-way exchange of nitrogen fluxes between the land and atmosphere components, and 2) performing model simulations to examine the impacts of current nitrogen emissions on atmospheric chemistry and strength of land-atmosphere feedbacks. The results have been presented in one published work and another publication currently under review: Zhao, Y., Zhang, L., Tai, A. P. K., Chen, Y., and Pan, Y.: Responses of surface ozone air quality to anthropogenic nitrogen deposition in the Northern Hemisphere. Objective #3 has also been achieved by making use of the same modeling framework, but utilizing a different coupling method (asynchronous instead of synchronous coupling), to examine the effects of future ammonia emissions following future food production trends on terrestrial vegetation and atmospheric feedbacks. The findings have been published here: Liu, X., Tai, A. P. K., and Fung, K. M.: Responses of surface ozone to future agricultural ammonia emissions and subsequent nitrogen deposition through terrestrial ecosystem changes, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics, 21, 17743–17758, https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-21-17743-2021, 2021. 14323116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14323116.value: With the rising food demands from the future world population, more intense agricultural activities are expected to cause substantial perturbations to the global nitrogen cycle, aggravating surface air pollution and imposing stress on terrestrial ecosystems. Here we first examined the responses of surface ozone air quality to terrestrial ecosystem changes caused by 2000–2050 changes in agricultural ammonia emissions and the subsequent nitrogen deposition by asynchronously coupling between the terrestrial and atmospheric models. We found that global gross primary production and leaf area index are both enhanced by the increase in global nitrogen deposition by year 2050. Such vegetation changes, together with rising soil NOx emissions following greater nitrogen deposition, could lead to surface ozone changes by up to 4–6 ppbv. We further examined how fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution may be alleviated by improving both farming methods and food consumption patterns. Excessive fertilizer use has led to large emissions of reactive nitrogen into the atmosphere, where they contribute to PM2.5 pollution. Intercropping has been considered as a sustainable, more environmentally friendly agricultural practice, but its potential benefits beyond the farm scale have rarely been examined. Here we developed an integrated modeling framework to quantify the benefits of nationwide adoption of maize–soybean systems in China in terms of gains in crop production gains and reductions in fertilizer use, ammonia emission, and PM2.5 concentration. We found that annual mean PM2.5 can be reduced by up to 1.5 μg m–3, saving a health cost of ~US$13 billion. In another work accepted by Nature Food, we examined how shifting towards more meat-intensive diets may have indirect health consequences through environmental degradation in China over 1980–2010. Changes in dietary composition alone, mainly by driving the rising demands for meat and animal feed, have enhanced ammonia emissions by 63% and increased annual PM2.5 by up to ~10 μg m–3 (~20% of total PM2.5 increase) over the period. Shifting the current diet towards a less meat-intensive recommended diet can decrease ammonia emission by ~17% and PM2.5 by 2–6 μg m–3, and avoid ~75,000 related annual premature deaths. Combined together, our work demonstrates novel linkages between food consumption, agriculture, air pollution and health, and provide strong scientific basis for policy consideration as governments and stakeholders explore more sustainable farming options and dietary recommendations to achieve multiple environmental, socioeconomic and public health goals.

14323116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14323116.value: Our work has demonstrated novel and important linkages between food consumption, agriculture, air pollution and health, and provide strong scientific basis for policy consideration. This becomes imperative to further examine how future changes in food consumption, production and trade may further influence air quality and health in China and beyond, and how targeting agricultural emissions may complement the efforts to reduce fossil fuel combustion in tackling air pollution. We therefore propose to integrate future projections of food consumption, production and trade patterns under different socioeconomic scenarios based on analysis by the Food and Agriculture Organization, further develop our modeling framework, and examine what combinations of dietary recommendations and sustainable farming methods may help alleviate the health impacts of air pollution on whole populations in China and beyond. This is indeed what we have proposed to do in our currently submitted proposal to the General Research Fund 2022–23 funding scheme.

14323116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14323116.value: Agriculture is one of the major sources of reactive nitrogen compounds to the atmosphere. These compounds are mostly from chemical fertilizer and animal wastes in livestock raising, leading to a cascade of environmental problems. The rapid rise in food production in recent decades has substantially increased reactive nitrogen emissions, driven mostly by population growth and a widespread dietary shift toward heavier meat consumption, contributing to air pollution with severe implications for human health. Such nitrogen compounds also influence natural vegetation and soil as they are deposited onto the land, and such terrestrial changes may further modify the atmosphere and affect air quality. Our work has demonstrated strong and novel linkages between food consumption, agriculture, air pollution, and human health. For the first time we showed that dietary changes in China have worsened not only nutritional health but also respiratory health via worsening air pollution. To reduce air pollution and its health impacts, more sustainable farming methods as well as a shift toward a more plant-based diet can tremendously help, providing complementary strategies to fossil fuel control. We also showed that agricultural changes can also influence natural ecosystems, and the corresponding feedback effects onto air quality can be substantial in the coming decades.

14323216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14323216.value: There has been growing interest in using enzymes to catalyze industrial reactions due to their high reactivities, excellent regio- and enantiospecificities, and low environmental toxicities. In order to enhance their catalytic and mechanical stability for use over multiple reaction cycles, biocatalysts are generally immobilized. There are many immobilization techniques, each with its limitations in terms of production, catalytic efficiency and/or stability. Herein, we propose an innovative approach to enzyme immobilization that is facile, robust, and can potentially overcome the constraints of traditional immobilization strategies. We plan to test this technique in the scope of lipase-mediated production of biodiesel, an environmentally safe alternative fuel. 近年來，由於酶的高反應性，優異的區域以及異構體特異性和低環境毒性，利用酶催化工業反應引起了廣泛的關注。為了提高生物催化劑在多個反應週期應用中的催化穩定性和機械穩定性，他們通常是被固定化的。現在有很多的固定化技術，但是它們在生產，催化效率和/或穩定性方面存在諸多限制。因此，我們提出了一個簡單有效的新方法來固定化酶催化劑，克服了傳統固定化策略的製約。脂肪酶能夠介導環境安全的替代燃料——生物柴油的生產。我們計劃利用這一反應來測試這一新的固定化技術。

14323216.label: Realisation of objectives
14323216.value: All of the objectives have been realized. (1) We showed that we produced immobilized lipases by genetically fusing them to Cry3Aa proteins and producing and directly isolating them from Bacillus thuringiensis. (2) We showed that Cry3Aa-lipA and Cry3Aa-PML fusion crystals were more thermostable and more resistant to denaturation from organic solvents. (3) Unexpectedly, we found that pre-evolved PML mutants with enhanced stability were less stable than wild-type PML when fused to Cry3Aa. (4) We subsequently evolved a distinct PML mutant with enhanced catalytic activity when fused to Cry3Aa. Interestingly, this mutant was less stable than wild-type PML as the free protein. Thus because of the stability imparted by fusion to Cry3Aa, we could identify a PML that was naturally less stable but more active.

14323216.label: Major findings and research outcome
14323216.value: The practical use of enzymes as industrial catalysts to drive chemical transformations requires strategies that can produce the enzyme cheaply, and in a form where the enzyme can be used for multiple catalytic cycles. This project demonstrated the use of Cry3Aa protein crystals as a platform to achieve these goals. We show that by producing Cry3Aa genetically-fused to the lipase lipA, we could produce Cry3Aa-lipA fusion crystals in a way that was both simple and cost effective. Characterization of the resulting crystals showed that fusion of lipA to Cry3Aa and its subsequent crystallize stabilized it against both temperature and organic solvent denaturation. The resulting crystals were then shown to be suitable for use in the conversion of canola oil to FAME biodiesel for multiple catalytic cycles. We subsequently explored the evolution of lipA as a Cry3Aa-lipA fusion crystal. We were able to identify a more active Cry3Aa-lipA and showed that it could be used as an improved catalyst for the canola oil to FAME biodiesel conversion. identified from the evolution screening assay. It was only as a fusion to lipA that this lipA was stable enough for use. The structure of the mutant lipA was determined and provides insights into the possible origins of the increased activity. Finally, this project provided preliminary data in support of entrapping lipases within Cry3Aa crystals which was continued and brought to fruition in a subsequently GRF grant.

14323216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14323216.value: A patent application on these lipase fusions has been submitted and is with the patent office. This work subsequently led to the identification of a strategy to entrap proteins within Cry3Aa protein crystals which has also been submitted for patent protection. An ITF for the scale up of these Cry3Aa lipase crystals has also been funded.

14323216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14323216.value: Global warming is a growing problem in the world because it leads to higher sea levels and more intense weather events. It is generally agreed that the major cause of global warming is the increased levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere resulting from the combustion of fossil fuels. One way to reduce carbon dioxide emissions is use biofuels produced from plant oils. Because the plants capture the carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, their subsequent combustion is carbon neutral. Thus developing efficient catalysts to promote this reaction is important. In this project, we demonstrate that we can use a novel Cry protein crystal to directly immobilize a lipase that can convert canola oil to biodiesel. The attractive features of this approach is cheaper than other standard methods, and can stabilize the lipase against degradation. We show that this catalyst to convert canola oil to biodiesel over multiple catalytic cycles. We are currently working to scale up these and related technologies to make them practical for larger scale reactions.

14323416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14323416.value: 摘要: 組成為NO3−(HNO3)m(H2O)n, HSO4−(H2SO4)m(H2O)n,与 HSO4−(NHO3)m(H2O)n的無机酸陰离子團簇是高層大气之中最為常見的陰离子。它們產生于泄露大气之中的微量化學品，是气溶膠的前体，對大气研究有重要的意義。气溶膠是大气的重要成份，影響人類的健康，空气能見度与質量，也影響气候。 這些陰离子團簇与其它离子團簇類似，可以在實驗室生成。通過質譜儀選出之后，可以進行譜學研究。多光子紅外解离譜（IRMPD）是其中最為重要的一种研究手段，可以在基態的勢能面上探索紅外振動，獲得許多分子層級的細節。 理論模擬是理解IRMPD的重要一環。我們最近的研究顯示，對氫鍵主導的离子團簇，動力學效應极為重要，因為其相應的勢能面相當平坦。由此造成的譜線位移与加寬提供團簇之中分子作用的細節，需要結合從頭算分子動力學（AIMD）与標准量化計算來解析。 我們計划以AIMD与量化計算來研究對大气化學之中重要的無机酸團簇离子進行研究，探索其中的結构板塊，能量，熵效應，振動譜与動力學效應，為理解气溶膠的形成及大气化學离子模型的建立提供基礎。

14323416.label: Realisation of objectives
14323416.value: We have systematically investigated the structures and landscape of the NO3-(HNO3)m(H2O)n cluster anions. There are a large number of isomers, for such clusters held together by hydrogen bonds. Our focus is on the HNO3(NO3-)(H2O)n system, which contains the basic model of the HNO3...NO3- core. Additional HNO3 molecules only add more HNO3...NO3- units to the system. The structural evolution of HNO3(NO3-)(H2O)n is the key to understand the structural and vibrational characteristics of these cluster anions. The fluctuations of hydrogen bonds are very important. While the HNO3...NO3- hydrogen bond is very strong, the H2O...NO3- and H2O-HNO3 hydrogen bonds are like typical strength and could shift extensively. Even along the strong HNO3...NO3- hydrogen bond, there is significant rotation and also change in the hydrogen bond distances. Ab initio molecular dynamic (AIMD) simulations are very helpful for understanding how the structures change, which are performed at a number of temperatures for each individual cluster anion. The energy gap between various isomer structures are found to be quite small, which is the reason for the extensive structural fluctuation. It also means that the entropy factor is quite important, which can be sampled by AIMD simulations. The most interesting finding is the unique structure identified for HNO3(NO3-)(H2O)2. It's a H5O2+ core held together by two NO3- anions. In contrast to the well-known Zundel structure in which two H2O share a proton, this H5O2+ is asymmetric, with a H3O+ solvated by another H2O. The vibrational spectra for these clusters are re-interpreted, in light of the importance of dynamic fluctuation and the entropy factors. We further make prediction about the frequency regions above 2000 cm-1, which is important for the identification of the signature of the asymmetric H5O2+ core. In collaboration with experimentalists at Dalian Institute of Chemical Physics, we also did AIMD simulation on the neutral clusters, TMA...H2O and TMA...HOMe, which are also important in atmspheric chemistry, characterized by a very strong hydrogen bond. The focus is on the comparison between the spectra when H2O is replaced by MeOH.

14323416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14323416.value: Two papers have been published. For HNO3(NO3−)(H2O)n (n = 0-2), the AIMD results indicate that the structure of the n = 0 cluster is very flexible, even though its hydrogen bond is quite strong. Significant rotations around the hydrogen bond and frequent transfers of proton from HNO3 to NO3− are observed in AIMD simulations. Dynamic changes are therefore an important factor in understanding the broadening of vibrational features. For n = 1, the extent of structural fluctuation increases further, as H2O could move around the anion while the HNO3(NO3−) core also goes through structural changes. Its vibrational spectrum can be understood as a mixture of many isomers visited during AIMD simulations. By n = 2, the structure is stabilized around one isomer, with the linker between the two nitrates being H5O2+, rather than H+. Due to strong hydrogen bonds between nitrates and water molecules, this H5O2+ takes the extraordinary structure with the H+ localized on one H2O, rather than being shared. While this novel structure is stable during AIMD simulations, the dynamic fluctuations in hydrogen bond distances still produce significant broadening in its vibrational profile. For TMA...H2O and TMA...HOMe, surprisingly broad progression of distinct OH stretching peaks over ~700 cm-1 is observed in the spectrum of trimethylamine-water, indicative of an anomalously large amplitude fluctuation in hydrogen bond distance and drastic internal rotation of H2O as verified by harmonic analysis and ab initio molecular dynamic simulations. The dramatic reduction of this progression in the trimethylamine-methanol spectrum provides direct evidence for dynamic couplings. State-of-the-art quantum mechanical calculations reveal that such dynamic couplings are originated from strong Fermi resonance between the stretches of hydrogen-bonded OH and several motions of the solvent water/methanol, such as translation, rocking, and bending. Since this new Fermi resonance coupling mechanism does not depend on the molecular specification of trimethylamine, the strong dynamic coupling we observed is an intrinsic property of hydrogen-bond fluctuations relevant to proton transport in atmosphere and biology such as new particle formation and fuel-cell membranes.

14323416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14323416.value: The OH stretching region of HNO3(NO3−)(H2O)n should be examined to identify the structures found in our studies. Discussion with experimentalists are ongoing.

14323416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14323416.value: Upper levels of atmosphere are populated by gas phases clusters which play an important role in cloud and areosol formation, with significant impact on the environment. By computer simulations, we are able to study the structural transformation of these clusters and interprete their spectral signatures. These data would be valuable to understand their stability and structural evolution and essential for the modeling in atmspheric chemistry.

14323516.value: 微分幾何中關於全像原理的整體問題

14323516.label: Project Objectives
14323516.value: Understand the effects of Ricci curvature and mean curvature on the topology and geometry of the underlying manifold Discover more examples of holographic principles in geometry and perhaps their associated physical counterpart Develop geometric and analytic tools to study non-local questions in Riemannian Geometry

Discover more examples of holographic principles in geometry and perhaps their associated physical counterpart

14323516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14323516.value: This project aims at exploring the holographic principles in differential geometry and their relationship with Einstein metrics and mathematical physics. The holographic principle, in simple terms, says that all the information in the interior should be encoded by its projections onto the boundary, which is of lower dimension. A famous example from physics is the AdS/CFT correspondence which establish a duality between conformal field theories on the boundary and the theories of quantum gravity in the bulk. Mathematically, it relates the conformal geometry of the boundary to the geometry of Einstein metrics in the interior. Since then it has led to great advance in conformal geometry, following in spirit a program initiated by Fefferman and Graham in 1985. This project investigates other geometric holographic principles on how the boundary geometry affects the interior geometry and vice versa, motivated by a boundary value problem for Einstein metrics. The PI proposes to initiate a systematic study of spaces with boundary satisfying certain convexity conditions, as a first step towards understanding the existence question of Einstein metrics to a natural elliptic boundary value problem. The project requires state-of-the-art techniques from geometry and analysis, including minimal surface theory, geometric flows and geometric partial differential equations, and would bring substantial developments in these fields. The objects under investigation also have close relationship with other physical theories like the concept of mass in mathematical general relativity. In the long run, the project may lead to discoveries of other holographic principles which are yet to be explored. On the other hand, our study on some non-local Poincare-Steklov type operators would also find applications, for example, in electrical resistivity tomography in geophysics. 此項目旨在探索微分幾何中的全像原理和它與愛因斯坦度量、數學物理的關係。 簡單來說，全像原理就是內裡的所有訊息都應該能通過某種投射被反映在它維度較低的邊界上。一個物理學裡有名的例子是AdS/CFT對應 ，亦即邊界上的共形場論和內裡的量子重力之間的對偶性。在數學的本質上，它等同於給出了邊界上的共形幾何和內裡愛因斯坦度量的幾何之間的關係。在1985年，Fefferman和Graham的工作已經提出類似的觀點，為共形幾何這個領域帶來重大發展。 為愛因斯坦度量的邊界值問題所啟發，此項目旨在研究幾何上的全像原理，例如邊界幾何跟內在幾何之間的關係。 此項目負責人將會有系統性的研究邊界滿足某種凸性的空間，藉以增加對“愛因斯坦度量的存在性作為橢圓邊界值問題”的初步了解。此項目需要運用幾何和分析中最前沿的概念與技巧，包括極小曲面理論、幾何流和幾何偏微分方程，同時將給這些領域帶來顯著的進展。這些被研究的對象也跟其他物理理論例如廣義相對論中的質量概念密切相關。此項目更為長遠的目標是發現更多其他領域中存在的全像原理。除此以外，此項目對非局部Poincare-Steklov類算子的研究也可以應用於其他領域，比如地球物理學裡的地電阻法的理論。

14323516.label: Realisation of objectives
14323516.value: Regarding Objective 1, we achieved a great advance in understanding the effects of Ricci curvature and mean curvature on the topology and geometry of the underlying manifold, via their influence on the qualitative and quantitative behaviour of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces. We discovered that the mean curvature of the boundary is related to the density of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces near the boundary. Moreover, we established in the free boundary setting optimal Morse index bounds for the multi-parameter Almgren-Pitts min-max theory. This is crucial to the general program of establishing an effective Morse theory for the area functional in order to understand the geometry and topology of the underlying space. These works (and other follow-up work in the literature) have provided an important tool of studying background geometry using free boundary minimal hypersurfaces, hence completing Objective 1. For Objective 2, the PI has successfully explored new directions in general relativity which exhibits holographic principles. Together with his collaborators, the PI proposed an entirely new 4+1 covariant formulation which covers radiative transfer in dynamical spacetimes. The approach overcomes several limitations of previous theoretical and numerical methods, especially when applied in the strong-field regime, by promoting the 3+1 numerical relativity decomposition via an embedding of a 4D spacetime into a 5D non-flat pseudo-Riemannian manifold. This provides a radically new way to study the null geodesics, hence the causal structures of spacetimes. Finally, we have developed new geometric and analytic tools in geometric flows with boundary to study non-local questions in Riemannian Geometry. We devised a novel non-local curve shortening flow which exhibits interesting non-local geometric behaviour. We have studied both the short time and long time existence of the flow and applied it to give a new analytic proof of the Lusternik-Schnirelmann theorem. Furthermore, we explored geometric flows with boundary with our initial focus on Mean Curvature Flow (MCF). Together with Sven Hirsch, the PI proved a fundamental convergence result for convex surfaces in the context of MCF with free boundary. One important discovery here is how the boundary geometry affects the evolution behaviour in the MCF setting, which reconciles with the theme of holographic principles in this project as the effects are surprisingly found to have a non-local nature. This last result provides an excellent example of unifying all three objectives in this project. In summary, all the objectives set out in this project has been achieved and many new directions have been opened up.

14323516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14323516.value: We have proposed (in Research Output 1) a novel non-local geometric flow which exhibits new geometric and analytic phenomena which is different from the classical geometric flows like Ricci Flow and Mean Curvature Flow. We used this new flow to simplify the ad-hoc proof of a classical result of Lusternik-Schnirelmann which is a central result in counting periodic orbits in dynamical systems. This work has appeared in Pacific Journal of Mathematics. In Research Output 2, we investigated further properties of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces produced using the multi-parameter min-max theory in the Almgren-Pitts setting. We obtained precise estimates of the instability of minimal hypersurfaces constructed and the density of minimal hypersurfaces for generic metrics subject to a mild condition on the boundary which settles a well-known conjecture of S.T. Yau in the boundary case. Our result also gave a simplified argument for part of the proof of A. Song on the Yau Conjecture in the closed case. Our work has expanded our current knowledge on the existence theory of minimal hypersurfaces with boundary and how the boundary geometry can play a role in the theory. This work has been published in the Mathematische Annalen and there have already been a few follow-up papers using our work. In Research Output 3, the PI has collaborated with physicists to apply geometric methods in problems arising from general relativity. We proposed a new level set approach using (conformal) isometric embeddedings and used it to recover the spacetime casual structure. Compared to the classical ray tracing method using in numerical relativity, our work has provided an entirely new point of view towards the study of null geodesics by more differential geometric techniques. Our project has led to a series of further works which will be culminated in several papers. Our first paper has been submitted to a top physics journal and is currently under review. Finally, in Research Output 4, we proved a fundamental convergence result for convex surfaces evolving under Mean Curvature Flow with free boundary. We proved that strong convexity of an initial surface will contract to a point under the flow. This is the first convergence result which works for non-umbilic barrier surfaces. Our work has already caught a lot of attention in the field and we have been invited to present our results in international conferences and prestigious research institutions. This work is currently under review in a reputed mathematics journal.

14323516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14323516.value: Our work has pointed out several new directions that are worth further investigations. We believed that the new phenomena discovered in this project exist in a much wider context in various mathematical and physical problems. We propose further future work on geometric flows with boundary, e.g. the Ricci flow and Yamabe flow. It would also be very interesting to see how the boundary behaviour plays a role in geometric problems arising in mathematical relativity.

14323516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14323516.value: This project expanded our understanding of how ambient geometry (e.g. curvatures) affect the qualitative aspects (e.g. instability) of geometric objects inside. There are many natural phenomena in mathematics and physics where the effect of both short-range and long-range interactions play a role. The project makes use of geometric and analytic methods to demonstrate some of these newly discovered phenomena in a wide range of research areas.

14323616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14323616.value: Symmetric spaces or Bruhat-Tits building associated to a semisimple group over a local field is of great importance in representation theory and automorphic forms. The case of the Bruhat-Tits building is particularly rich in its structure and applications. But its foundation theory is rather involved. We propose a conjectural simple construction of the Bruhat-Tits building. The idea comes from the celebrated Moy-Prasad theory and indeed the result, once established, would absorb a large part of Moy-Prasad theory into this simple construction. The idea can be applied equally well to a real group, yielding an equally interesting construction of the symmetric space. 對稱空間和 Bruhat-Tits 建築是附屬於局部緊域上的半單群的重要結構，在表示論和自守形式裡有很多應用。Bruhat-Tits 建築的結構和應用更是特別豐富，但是其基礎理論相當複雜。我們猜測了一個 Bruhat-Tits 的簡單建構，其想法來自於 Moy-Prasad 理論。如果能完全實現，也因此能把 Moy-Prasad 理論部份納入這個簡單的建構理論裡。同樣的想法也能適用於實李群，因此得到一個對稱空間的新描述。

14323816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14323816.value: 對分枝桿菌細胞外膜的計算機建模與分子動力學模擬

14323816.label: Project Objectives
14323816.value: Uncover atomic-level structural details of the mycomembrane. Due to the limited resolution of cryo-EM images, structural details of the mycomembrane remain largely missing. Combining existing force field parameters with QM/MM calculations, the PI will construct AA models for major mycomembrane components while the co-I will construct the corresponding CG models. Together, these models will be used to understand how the (presumably folded) mycolic acids are packed in the mycomembrane as well as how porins, such as MspA, are accommodated. Elucidate the mechanism of small molecule permeation in the mycomembrane. A bottleneck in antibiotic development is the paucity of compounds that can penetrate into bacterial cells. Based on our mycomembrane model, we plan to determine the permeability of selected nutrients and drugs through rigorous free energy and diffusivity calculations. Our calculations will shed light on the origin of the mycomembrane's exceptionally low permeability, and elucidate how different physico-chemical properties affect the permeability of a given small molecule.

14323816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14323816.value: Tuberculosis (TB), an infectious disease killing over one million people every year, is caused by the mycobacterium pathogen M. tuberculosis (M. tb). Unlike its Gram-positive bacterial counterparts, M. tb possesses an outer membrane which is highly impermeable to drug and nutrient molecules alike. This membrane, named the mycomembrane, contributes to M. tb's exceptional ability to withstand harsh environments as well as its natural resistance to many antibiotics. Given its function as an essential fortress protecting the bacterial cell, understanding the detailed structure of the mycomembrane is of considerable importance to tuberculosis research. However, direct visualization of the membrane via cryo-EM experiments only identified it as a morphologically symmetrical lipid bilayer. Due to the limited image resolution, the detailed structure of the membrane cannot be resolved, which leaves important questions regarding lipid packing, accommodation of membrane porins, as well as the uptake pathway and permeation barrier of small molecules largely open. Here, we propose to combine quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics calculations with the latest experimental data on its individual components to develop accurate models of the mycomembrane. Combining the strength of all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we plan to fully uncover lipid conformation and molecular packing in the mycomembrane, quantify its barriers against permeation of nutrient and drug molecules, and explore how a key M. tb enzyme locates and operates on its substrates. By constructing realistic models grounded in experimental data, we will reveal unprecedented structural details of the mycomembrane and elucidate the origin of its exceptionally low permeability. Our results will also lay the foundation for further studies, both computational and experimental, of the complex cell envelope of M. tb and provide guidance for the design of more efficient therapeutics against this important bacterial pathogen. 肺結核是由結核分枝桿菌引起的一種傳染性疾病，每年造成約一百萬人死亡。同其他革蘭式陽性菌不同，結核分枝桿菌有一層細胞外膜，對藥物等小分子的滲透性極低。由於採用冷凍電鏡等實驗技術得到的圖像無法提供足夠的分辨率，儘管這層外膜起著保護細菌的重要作用，我們對它的結構細節仍知之甚少。本項工作旨在採用計算機建模與分子動力學模擬的手段構建分枝桿菌細胞外膜的模型。我們將結合全原子與粗粒化模擬，研究脂類分子在該層外膜中的構象，並定量計算小分子穿過該層外膜的能壘和滲透系數。這一工作的結果將為進一步研究分枝桿菌複雜的細胞壁和研發針對結核桿菌的有效藥物提供基礎。

14323816.label: Realisation of objectives
14323816.value: Along the line of objective 1, the PI's group has performed both quantum mechanics and molecular mechanics calculations to parameterize all-atom models of the three proposed mycolic acids (MAs), namely, the alpha-, keto- and methoxy- MAs. An extensive set of monolayer simulations have been carried out to validate the resulting models. The number of folded vs. extended MA tails, as well as the surface tension of the monolayer were measured and compared with experimentally determined pressure-area isotherms. Altogether tens of microseconds simulations were performed, which produced reasonable agreement with experimental measurement. Apart from the all-atom models, a corresponding set of coarse-grained models of the above lipids have been developed by the co-I. We are currently planning a joint publication by the PI and the co-I groups that summarize the above findings. As proposed in objective 2, the PI's group has performed hundreds of nanoseconds' simulations of the key M. tb enzyme Ag85. Through these simulations, we investigated the enzyme's conformations and dynamics both in bulk water and at the interface of an MA leaflet. However, due to the structural complexity of the arabinogalactan polysaccharide, we are still exploring the spatial organization of this layer and how such organization is affecting the accessibility of Ag85 to its substrate. A major challenge has been the extensive sampling required to model the structurally complex polysaccharide. In an effort to address this challenge, we have employed a 'divide-and-conquer' strategy, where increasingly longer arabinogalactan chains with more complex branches are simulated in stages. Along with the recent availability of multiple graphical processing units in our group, which provides much improved computational speed, we are now expanding our modeling and simulations to larger arabinogalactan layers and examining their influence on Ag85. With regard to objective 3, the PI's group first evaluated computational protocols for membrane permeability estimation, namely, the adaptive biasing force (ABF) method and the Bayesian inference diffusivity calculation scheme. This was achieved through computing the permeability of three drug or drug-like molecules in pure POPC and POPC:cholesterol membranes. Additionally, we determined the permeability of a short-chain alcohol molecule in both pure lipid bilayers and a model mammalian membrane. Given the steep computational cost of these calculations, we also investigated an alternative approach, namely, replacing ABF by free energy perturbation (FEP) at selected locations along the membrane normal. For small drug or drug-like molecules, the latter method is found to render permeability calculations more efficient and affordable. These findings have been summarized in the first two publications listed in part C. Given the tremendous computational cost of these permeability calculations, we then investigated whether a simulation speed-up strategy, namely, the hydrogen mass repartitioning (HMR) method, can be applied reliably on membrane systems. Through extensive simulations and tests we showed that HMR, in combination with a properly chosen cutoff, can well reproduce membrane properties while allowing the timestep to be doubled, thereby, enhancing simulation efficiency by two fold. These results have been summarized in the third publication listed in part C. Following the above works, we proceeded to model a representative, first-line anti-tuberculosis drug, rifampicin, and determined its POPC permeability using both the ABF and FEP approaches. While the FEP approach did not perform as well due to the large size of the rifampicin molecule, extensive ABF simulations totaling several microseconds revealed detailed permeation mechanism and produced results that compared favorably with the experimental reference. A thorough analysis was also performed to shed light on the proper interpretation of experimental data obtained via fluorescence leakage assays. A publication summarizing these findings is being revised and will be submitted shortly. A major challenge in addressing objective 3 has been the parameterization of rifampicin. This drug molecule has an unusually large number of hydrogen bond partners and molecular weight, which rendered its parameterization particularly challenging. Through three rounds of refinement, we finally obtained a set of parameters that reproduced the molecule's experimentally measured octanol:water partition coefficient, which was subsequently used in the aforementioned ABF calculations. We are currently employing these established simulation protocols and the rifampicin model to examine the permeation of this representative anti-tuberculosis drug within the mycolic acids.

14323816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14323816.value: The PI's group developed all-atom models for three major mycolic acids (MAs) and validated the models through comparison with experimentally determined pressure-area isotherms of MA monolayers. Correspondingly, the co-I's group developed a set of coarse-grained models of the above lipids. Along with simulations of a key M. tb enzyme Ag85, our results shed valuable light onto the structure and dynamics of the mycobacterial outer membrane. To further examine the permeability of this membrane to drug molecules, we investigated a number of computational protocols, including the adaptive biasing force (ABF) and free energy perturbation (FEP) methods, the Bayesian inference diffusivity calculation scheme, as well as the hydrogen mass repartitioning (HMR) approach. Our studies not only established protocols for accurate permeability calculations, but also provided guidance to membrane simulations in general, including both pure lipid bilayer and membrane protein systems. We have also developed and validated all-atom parameters for the anti-tuberculosis drug rifampicin and determined its permeability within a model membrane. Three publications, as listed in part C, have resulted from the above works, with one additional publication planned and one working manuscript to be submitted shortly.

14323816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14323816.value: Reliable and efficient computation of the membrane permeability of relatively large drug molecules remains to be further investigated. As revealed by our works, while the relatively low-cost FEP approach can handle small or moderately sized molecules, the ABF approach, which often requires microsecond sampling, is still called for when handling large drug molecules such as rifampicin. The PI plans to continue to investigate protocols for these calculations, such as optimizing the number of windows, accumulation of statistics as well as pre-equilibration time. Furthermore, apart from continuing on the mycobacterial outer membrane, the PI aims to expand our modeling and simulation efforts into other bacterial membrane systems, examining, for instance, small molecule permeation as well as antimicrobial peptide interactions in these environments.

14323816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14323816.value: Membranes are fluid 'walls' separating the inner material of a cell from its outside environment. They present significant barriers against a large number of biomolecules and yet offer effective passage to selected species such as nutrients. Understanding the structure, dynamics and permeability of lipid membranes is therefore essential to gaining insight into the interactions and material exchange between a cell and its environment. In the case of bacteria, a quantitative description of their membrane permeability can guide the design of more efficient therapeutics against these pathogens. In this project, we modeled and simulated major lipid components of the mycobacterial outer membrane and established a set of protocols for accurate computation of membrane permeability. We also developed and validated parameters for a first-line anti-tuberculosis drug molecule and calculated its permeability within a model lipid bilayer. Our work lays the foundation for further investigation of the exceptionally 'tough' mycobacterial outer membrane. The protocols established here also provide a reference for future computational studies targeting a wide variety of membrane systems.

14323916.value: Experimental measurement of the permeability and strains of two porous limestones under confining and pore pressures in room temperature on saturated samples. Triaxial compression experiments on two samples of each limestone at relatively low and high confinements, with inelastic damage that is dilatant and compactant, respectively. 14323916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14323916.value: 地殼里的孔隙空間很可能是相互連通的，其包含的流體，在沉積、變質和構造過程中，對岩層形成普遍存在物理、化學作用，對地震構造、經濟地質、石油地質以及岩土工程均有重大影響。對這些過程的基本認識取決於孔隙壓力的力學特征、孔隙壓力與上覆岩層壓力、構造應力的相互作用、流體-岩石相互作用以及複雜的耦合過程的系統研究。 本實驗方案主要研究含孔隙石灰岩中流體的力學作用。岩層的形變主要受外部應力和孔隙壓力影響，關鍵是哪種力學作用對已知的物理特征起主導作用。人們發現這些物理特征與每個施加的應力成線性關係，因而使用“有效應力”的概念來描述這兩種應力場的共同作用。用“有效應力係數”來表明兩種應力場中各個應力場所做的貢獻大小。在大多數結晶岩和一些沉積岩中，滲透率有效應力係數和應變有效應力係數均小於1。然而，許多研究發現，含黏土的砂岩和鮞狀灰岩的滲透率有效應力係數均大於1，這表明在儲層或者斷層中孔隙壓力對流體運移的影響程度是不同的。 假設用雙孔介質模型來表征灰岩的孔隙結構，那麼有效應力變化特征應與幾何屬性有緊密的關係。在圍壓和孔壓的作用下，本實驗將對四塊灰岩進行研究，記錄滲透率、體積應變和孔隙應變。為了研究力學的影響，排除其他影響因素，將在氮氣飽和環境下進行實驗。通過三軸壓縮實驗獲得樣品的膨脹與壓縮損傷。這些帶有損傷樣品的有效應力特征也將被研究。初步實驗將對水飽和后的樣品進行研究，來分析潛在的化學影響。 利用X射線計算機層析成像技術，獲得灰岩樣品的孔隙空間結構。使用混合模擬方法（離散格子玻爾茲曼方法和有限元模擬）來擬合與圍壓和孔壓有關的形變函數與滲透率函數。總體目標是在雙孔介質的真實幾何結構基礎上，建立一個統一的與滲透率和應變有關的有效應力法則的孔彈性模型。

14323916.label: Realisation of objectives
14323916.value: 1. We have completed measurements of permeability, pore volume change and bulk strain of four limestones under hydrostatic loading. The comprehensive set of data was presented by Wang et al., JGR, 2018. 2. We have conducted triaxial compression experiments on two limestones, measured the permeability evolution, and effective stress behavior of the damaged samples. The data were presented by Meng et al., JGR, 2019. 3 & 4. Relevant microCT data of the undeformed and deformed samples of limestones have been acquired. The data were segmented and the research group of co-PI has conducted voxel-based simulation of the permeability and deformation. The detailed results are being written up, and will be presented in a future publication. Digital volume correlation (DVC) analysis was performed on the samples, which reveals the detailed development of failure and strain localization. 5. Synthesis of the laboratory data has motivated the development and refinement of models for interpretation of effective stress behavior in relation to microscopic heterogeneity of the pore space, as presented by Wang et al., 2018 and Meng et al., 2019. Integrating the DVC analysis of CT data and laboratory observations, Baud et al., JGR 2021 presented one of the most comprehensive analysis of brittle-ductile transition in porous limestones.
