14323916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14323916.value: We have conducted the first integrated investigation of the effective stress behaviors for both permeability and deformation in porous limestones. Our data underscore the fundamental difference between limestones with dual porosity and ones with simpler microstructure, which confirm prediction of models on the critical control of microstructural heterogeneity on rock physics properties (Wang et al., 2018). Extending from hydrostatic to triaxial comprssion, our experiments further highlight the control of deviatoric stresses on permeability evolution and effective stress behavior (Meng et al., 2019). Motivated by our limestone experiments, we revisited the behavior in clayey sandstones. We obtained the first set of data simultaneously on permeability and pore volume change, which underscores the inadequacy of existing models to provide a consistent interpretation of the effective stress behavior of these two related quantities. To resolve this dilemma, we develop a dual equivalent-channel model, which can satisfactorily explain our new data. Our investigation also clarifies the important role of microcracking on effective stress behavior. The data and analysis were recently presented by Meng et al. JGR 2020. A parallel study was also conducted on the effect of bedding anisotropy, which is presented by Meng et al., Rock Mech & Engin., 2020. Our systematic laboratory data and DVC analysis demonstrate that the brittle-ductile transition in several porous limestones with dual porosity is in agreement with theoretical prediction of bifurcation model associated with plasticity and the normality condition, with important implication on how to analyze failure and inelastic deformation of these reservoir rocks. (Baud et al., 2021) We have also initiated in situ measurement of failure using the ESRF synchrotron facilities in Grenoble, and successfully obtained the first 4D observation of multiscale failure and strain localization in a porous limestone, which has recently appeared in EPSL (Huang et al., 2019). Analysis of the synchrontron 4D data builds upon a systematic mechanical deformation study of the same limestone presented by Baud et al., JGR, 2017.

14323916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14323916.value: The 4D observation of multiscale failure and strain localization in a porous rock using the synchrontron represents a major technical advance, which we plan to pursue by further collaboration with our current collaborators in Granoble, Oslo and Strabourg.

14323916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14323916.value: Rocks in the upper crust of the Earth are embedded with pore space made up of numerous cavities with dimensions ranging over ten orders of magnitude. In most instances, these features in the pore space are interconnected, thus constituting a percolative structure for fluid flow. A fundamental understanding of the transport and failure properties of rock is of importance in many natural resources and environmental applications. This project builds upon scientific advances on two fronts: 3D imaging of pore space using X-ray microcomputed tomography, and advances in computation. There have been a paucity of systematic investigations of porous limestones that integrate experimental and digital rock physics research. In this project systematic measurements have highlighted the interplay of applied stresses and pore fluid pressure on controlling the mechanical and hydraulic properties. A pioneer effort to conduct 4D imaging of deformation and failure in a synchrotron facility was also pursued. These data have provided important insights into the failure and permeability evolutions in porous limestones.

14324116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14324116.value: Phthalocyanines were accidentally prepared during the industrial production of phthalimide from phthalic anhydride at a dye factory in Scotland in 1928 and characterized a few years later. Owing to their high thermal stability, intense color, inertness, and low solubility, these compounds were widely used as pigments in the textile, printing, and paint industries. Over the last few decades, along with the advances in the chemistry of this class of compounds, they have been demonstrated to possess a wide range of intriguing properties, rendering them to find practical applications in various disciplines, such as molecular electronics and photonics, photovoltaics, electrophotography, electrochromic displays, electrocatalysis, sensors, and photodynamic therapy. To extend the scope and optimize the performance of these materials in these applications, it is of paramount importance to have versatile synthetic methodologies to prepare and modify these macrocyclic compounds. Traditionally, phthalocyanines are prepared by cyclotetramerization of phthalonitriles or their derivatives, such as 1,3-diiminoisoindolines, phthalimides, and phthalic anhydrides. Whilst these methodologies can effectively produce a wide range of symmetrical phthalocyanines with four identical aza-linked isoindole units, the preparation of the unsymmetrical analogues by mixed condensation of two of these precursors inevitably gives a mixture of products which may not be separated readily. Mixed condensation with more than two of these precursors is not feasible to prepare phthalocyanines with an even lower symmetry. To circumvent this problem, a number of alternative synthetic pathways have been developed for low symmetry phthalocyanines. Unfortunately, they still suffer from various limitations which preclude their general use, and phthalocyanines with more than two different isoindole units remain extremely rare. As low symmetry phthalocyanines could exhibit unique properties that cannot be found in the symmetrical counterparts, further development of practical approaches to prepare these compounds is deemed necessary. In this proposal, we aim to develop a programmed synthetic strategy for novel low symmetry phthalocyanines that cannot be synthesized readily by conventional methods. The approach involves a pre-selection and conjugation of four phthalonitrile precursors followed by an intramolecular cyclization in the presence of a metal template. This controlled pathway allows tailor-made phthalocyanines to be synthesized. We will first optimize the reaction conditions and other parameters, and then prepare a series of these compounds, including the ABCD-type phthalocyanines, amphiphilic phthalocyanines, and push-pull phthalocyanines to demonstrate the versatility of this synthetic strategy. The unique features and intriguing properties of these compounds, such as their self-assembly and non-linear optical properties will also be investigated. 酞菁是1928年蘇格蘭一個染料工廠由鄰苯二甲酸酐工業製備鄰苯二甲酰亞胺時意外合成的，其結構在幾年後得到了表征。該類化合物的高熱穩定性，高顯色，惰性以及低溶解性使其作為染料廣泛應用於紡織、印刷和塗料工業。過去幾十年酞菁化學的進步證明了酞菁具有許多有趣的性質，使其在不同的方面具有實際應用前景，例如分子電子學與光子學、光伏發電、電子攝影術、電致變色顯示、電催化、傳感器和光動力學治療。為了擴展酞菁材料的應用及提升其性能，能夠有多種合成方法製備與修飾該類大環化合物變得極其重要。傳統上，酞菁是由鄰苯二甲腈或其衍生物，例如1,3-二亞氨基異吲哚啉、苯鄰二甲酰亞胺和鄰苯二甲酸酐四聚合環化所製備的。這些合成方法能夠有效地製備多種氮雜連四個相同異吲哚單元的對稱型酞菁，然而，利用兩種不同的前體混合縮合製備不對稱型酞菁則不可避免會生成多種產品的混合物並且難以分離。利用多於兩種的前體混合縮合去製備更低對稱性的酞菁並不可行。為了解決這些問題，多種用於製備低對稱型酞菁的合成方法被研發出來。遺憾的是，這些方法依然具有各種各樣的局限而不能夠通用，具有多於兩種不同異吲哚單元結構的酞菁依舊十分稀少。由於不對稱型酞菁的特殊性質是對稱型所不具備的，所以進一步探索該類化合物的製備方法十分必要。在此計劃，我們旨在發展一種傳統方法不易製備的不對稱型酞菁的程序化合成策略。該方法包含四個鄰苯二甲腈前體的預選擇和結合，之後在一個金屬模板下進行分子內環化。該類可控的方法可用於合成特製結構的酞菁。我們將首先優化反應條件與其他參數，然後製備一系列的化合物，其中包含ABCD型酞菁，兩親性酞菁，以及推拉酞菁以證明該法的多功能性。我們也將研究這些化合物的特殊性質，例如分子組裝和非線性光學性能。

14324116.label: Realisation of objectives
14324116.value: This project aims to develop efficient synthetic strategies for low-symmetry phthalocyanines using pre-linked phthalonitrile precursors and to study their unique features and intriguing properties. The first objective of this project is to optimize the intramolecular cyclization reactions of tetrakisphthalonitriles, including a study of the effects of the linkers and the cyclization conditions. We first employed bisphthalonitriles as model precursors that were connected by various linkers, including o-xylylene, benzaldehyde acetal, and disulfide moieties, and at different positions. A series of bisphthalonitriles were prepared, in which the linker could be cleaved afterward by conc. H2SO4, trifluoroacetic acid, and dithiothreitol, respectively, to free the hydroxyl or thiol groups that could be used for further functionalization. For some of the bisphthalonitriles, an additional substituent [tetraethylene glycol (TEG) or triisopropylsilylethynyl (TIPSE)] was introduced to enhance the solubility and lower the symmetry of the resulting phthalocyanines. By using the bulky TIPSE group, it could also impose steric hindrance to direct the cyclization. The linkage of two phthalonitrile units at different positions (alpha and beta’ respectively) could further reduce the symmetry of the phthalocyanines formed. These bisphthalonitriles were then self-cyclized or mixed condensed with phthalonitrile with two TEG chains at the alpha-positions in the presence of Zn(OAc)2 and 1,8 diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene (DBU) to give the corresponding zinc(II) phthalocyanines. The reaction conditions, including the solvent, concentration, base, and temperature were varied systematically and optimized to improve the reaction yield and simplify the purification process. Up to 17% yield could be obtained. The use of alpha, beta’-disubstituted bisphthalonitriles as precursors could lead to the formation of phthalocyanines with C1 symmetry. The presence of a bulky TIPSE substituent at the alpha-position of one of the phthalonitriles could control the self-cyclization to give the head-to-tail isomer as the sole product. In contrast, self-cyclization of the TEG analogue gave a mixture of head-to-tail and head-to-head isomers in equal amounts (7% each). All the phthalocyanines were characterized by various spectroscopic methods. The molecular structure of the alpha, alpha’-isomer with two TIPSE groups was also determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. Interestingly, while the electronic absorption spectrum of this compound in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) showed a typical sharp and intense Q band at 708 nm, the spectrum of the alpha, beta’-analogue gave four well-resolved Q bands, which is a typical feature of metal-free phthalocyanines and can be attributed to its reduced symmetry. The study was then extended to trisphthalonitriles. It was expected that the pre-connection of three phthalonitrile units could facilitate the mixed condensation with another phthalonitrile and reduce the side products. By using a trisphthalonitrile with two TEG chains at alpha-positions and a range of dicycano arenes, including phthalonitrile, 3-hydroxyphthalonitrile, diphenylmaleonitrile, 2,3-naphthalonitrile, and 2,3-dicyanobenzothiophene as precursors in the presence of Zn(OAc)2 and DBU, a series of zinc(II) phthalocyanines and their analogues were obtained. After optimization of the reaction conditions, the reaction yield could be up to 11%. In addition, mixed cyclization of a trisphthalonitrile with one TEG side chain and 4,5-bis(octylthio)phthalonitrile led to the formation of an ABCD-type phthalocyanine in which the four isoindole units are all substituted with different substituents. By using a trisphthalonitrile with two octylthio chains in the middle phthalonitrile unit and 4,5-bis(3,6,9-trioxadecylthio)phthalonitrile as precursors, an amphiphilic zinc(II) phthalocyanine was formed which could self-assemble to form nanoparticles in water with a hydrodynamic diameter of 220 nm as shown by dynamic light scattering. The spherical morphology was also confirmed by scanning electron microscopy. The results of the aforementioned studies will soon be submitted for publication. Most of these low-symmetry phthalocyanines have a unique substitution pattern that cannot be prepared by conventional mixed condensation. The “3+1” cross condensation approach was found to be a versatile synthetic methodology of low-symmetry phthalocyanines as different substituents can be introduced to the trisphthalonitriles and a wide range of dicyano arenes can be used as the other reaction component. In addition, this strategy can reduce the synthetic effort to pre-link the fourth phthalonitrile unit. Hence, we did not study the intramolecular cyclization of tetrakisphthalonitriles as originally planned. To extend the study further, some potential applications of low-symmetry phthalocyanines were examined. Two bisphthalonitriles linked with two sulfide or sulfone linkers were prepared which underwent self-cyclization in the presence of Co(OAc)2·4H2O and DBU to form the corresponding polymeric cobalt phthalocyanines that could be coated on various substrates (Adv. Funct. Mater. under revision). These materials could serve as electrocatalysts for water splitting and the activity depended on the electronic nature of the substituents. For the sulfide-linked analogue coated on Co3O4 nanosheets, it exerted a cooperative effect in promoting both the oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions. After phosphorization, the material could achieve an overpotential of 320 and 120 mV, respectively, at 10 mA cm-2. When engaged as a bifunctional electrocatalyst for the overall water splitting, this material required a low cell voltage of 1.672 V at 10 mA cm-2 and exhibited stable performance for 12 h, showing the characteristics of long-term durability and mechanical robustness. Apart from using pre-linked phthalonitrile precursors, we also used tailor-made phthalonitriles to control the cyclization process. By introducing two bulky permethylated beta-cyclodextrin moieties at the alpha-positions of phthalonitrile, it could prevent the self-condensation of this phthalonitrile. As a result, statistical condensation of this phthalonitrile and 2 equiv. of unsubstituted phthalonitrile in the presence of lithium and Zn(OAc)2 led to the formation of bis- and tetrakis-beta-cyclodextrin-substituted zinc(II) phthalocyanines in 9% and 6% yield, respectively (Chem. Commun. 2021, 57, 3567-3570). The latter is a crosswise-functionalized or ABAB-type phthalocyanine. Both compounds could be immobilized readily on the surface of adamantane-modified silica nanoparticles through host–guest interactions in water. These molecular and supramolecular systems could catalyze the photooxygenation of 1-naphthol and 2-furoic acid in organic and aqueous media with high conversion efficiency and reaction yield, and photodegradation of 2-chlorophenol in water. Having a higher photostability and recyclability, the supramolecular nanosystems were particularly promising for these photocatalytic applications. By using 2,9-diamino-1,10-phenanthroline as precursor, it could condense with 4,5-bis(4-tert-butyl-2,6-dimethylphenoxy)phthalonitrile in the presence of M(OAc)2 (M = Ni, Pd, Zn) to give the corresponding metal phenanthroline-fused phthalocyanine analogues with a 16 pi-electron skeleton (Org. Lett. submitted). They could be regarded as AABB-type phthalocyanine analogues. Based on their 1H NMR data and the nucleus-independent chemical shift (NICS) and anisotropy of the current-induced density (ACID) calculations, these compounds exhibited non-aromatic characteristics, while the unsynthesized metal-free derivative was inferred to be an anti-aromatic compound. While the arrangement of elements along the inner perimeter of these macrocycles is the same as that of the hitherto reported trivalent corroles that possess (4n+2)pi aromatic properties, they represent the first example of porphyrinoids possessing a monovalent corrole inner perimeter with 4npi non-aromatic properties. Finally, a series of low-symmetry phthalocyanines were also prepared through post-modification. A phthalaldehyde-substituted phthalocyanine was first synthesized through mixed condensation of two phthalonitriles followed by nucleophilic substitution of a bromo-substituted phthalaldehyde (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 7098-7102). This phthalocyanine could conjugate with a range of biomolecules, including peptides, monosaccharides, lipids, and DNAs, and be immobilized on the surface of bovine serum album nanoparticles and glass slides using the efficient phthalaldehyde-amine capture reactions. The latter two materials were photocytotoxic against cancer cells and bacteria, respectively, showing that they were highly efficient photosensitizing systems for photodynamic therapy. All the above results show that the originally set objectives of this project have been fully achieved.

14324116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14324116.value: We have prepared several series of low-symmetry phthalocyanines through different synthetic strategies and examined their properties and potential applications. The first strategy involves the pre-connection of two or three phthalonitrile units followed by self-cyclization or mixed condensation with other phthalonitriles or dicyano arene derivatives in the presence of Zn(OAc)2 and DBU (unpublished results). This approach can reduce the number of side products and facilitate the purification process. The introduction of a bulky substituent (e.g. TIPSE) to the bisphthalonitriles can exert an additional steric effect to control the cyclization process. After optimization of the reaction conditions, the target low-symmetry phthalocyanines can be obtained in up to 17% yield. By using cleavable linkers connecting two phthalonitrile units at different positions (alpha and beta’), phthalocyanines with a symmetry as low as C1 (or the so-called ABCD-type phthalocyanines) can be obtained and the functional groups (OH and SH) can be released after cleavage that can be used for further functionalization. An amphiphilic phthalocyanine has also been prepared which has two hydrophilic and two hydrophobic chains at opposite positions. It can self-assemble in water to form spherical nanoparticles as shown by dynamic light scattering and scanning electron microscopy. The spectral features of these compounds have also been examined. Some of them exhibit 4 well-resolved Q bands as metal-free analogues, which is in accordance with their reduced symmetry. With a unique substitution pattern, most of these low-symmetry phthalocyanines cannot be prepared by conventional intermolecular condensation methods. To explore the potential applications of low-symmetry phthalocyanines, we have performed self-cyclization of bisphthalonitriles in the presence of Co(OAc)2·4H2O on various substrates. The resulting polymeric cobalt phthalocyanines can serve as efficient electrocatalysts for water splitting with a low cell voltage of 1.672 V at 10 mA cm-2 and stable performance for 12 h (Adv. Funct. Mater. under revision). By using mixed cyclization of tailor-made phthalonitriles, we have also prepared an ABAB-type beta-cyclodextrin-conjugated phthalocyanine that can be used as a supramolecular and recyclable catalyst for photooxygenation reactions (Chem. Commun. 2021, 57, 3567-3570), and a phthalaldehyde-substituted phthalocyanine that can conjugate with various biomolecules and on various surface using the versatile and efficient phthalaldehyde-amine capture reactions (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 7098-7102). Mixed condensation of a phthalonitrile with 2,9-diamino-1,10-phenanthroline in the presence of M(OAc)2 (M = Ni, Pd, Zn) gives a series of novel phenanthroline-fused phthalocyanine analogues which possess an unprecedented monovalent corrole inner perimeter and 4npi non-aromatic properties (Org. Lett. submitted).

14324116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14324116.value: The “3+1” cross condensation approach using pre-linked trisphthalonitriles is particularly promising as different substituents can be introduced to the trisphthalonitriles and various dicyano alkenes and arenes can be used as the other reaction component. It can control the sequence of the four isoindole units in phthalocyanines by careful design and selection of the precursors. This versatile approach can be utilized further to synthesize a wide range of novel low-symmetry phthalocyanines and their analogues that cannot be prepared by conventional mixed condensation method. Emphasis could be put on those with special functionalities at specific positions for specific applications. The use of cleavable linkers can facilitate the cyclization and release of functional groups after subsequent cleavage of the linkers. The molecular design, optimization of the reaction conditions, and utilization of the tailor-made functionalized phthalocyanine derivatives in various disciplines could be a future direction. In addition, we have demonstrated that phthalonitriles can also condense with 2,9-diamino-1,10-phenanthroline to form novel phenanthroline-fused phthalocyanine analogues which exhibit unprecedented electronic properties. Other diamino aromatic systems can also be used for the cross condensation to prepare other exotic porphyrinoids, which remain as a research focus owing to their intriguing characteristics.

14324116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14324116.value: Phthalocyanines are highly conjugated macrocyclic compounds. Owing to their intriguing optical, electronic, and photophysical properties, these compounds have been extensively studied and found practical applications in various disciplines, such as molecular electronics and photonics, photovoltaics, electrophotography, electrochromic displays, electrocatalysis, and photodynamic therapy. To extend the scope and optimize the performance of these materials in these applications, it is of paramount importance to have versatile synthetic methodologies to prepare and modify these compounds, in particular the low-symmetry analogues which may exhibit unique properties that cannot be found in the symmetrical counterparts. In this proposal, we aim to develop efficient synthetic strategies for low-symmetry phthalocyanines that cannot be synthesized by conventional mixed condensation methods. We have prepared several series of these compounds through different approaches, including pre-connection of two or three phthalonitrile units followed by self-cyclization or mixed condensation with other phthalonitriles or dicyano akene and arene derivatives, the use of tailor-made phthalonitriles to control the cross condensation reactions, and post-modification using the highly efficient phthalaldehyde-amine capture reactions. The applications of these low-symmetry phthalocyanines as efficient and robust electrocatalysts for water splitting, recyclable supramolecular catalysts for photooxygenation reactions, and efficient photosensitizers for photo-eradication of cancer cells and bacteria have also been demonstrated.

14325216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14325216.value: 漸近非平穩時間序列的預測

14325216.label: Project Objectives
14325216.value: The main objective of the proposed study is to develop useful statistical methodologies for the analysis of non-stationary, heavy-tailed and/or long-memory time series, and to study the mean squared prediction errors of the underlying statistics. In particular, we propose a class of nearly non-stationary models, which unifies all the critical prediction phenomena that had to be dealt with in a case-by-case manner previously. The second and equally important goal is to study the mean squared errors resulting from the corresponding limiting results obtained in Objective 1. It is well known that the order of mean squared error prediction furnishes an important quantity to evaluate the performance of different model selection criteria such as AIC, BIC, and FPE for stationary time series. To further understand these criteria in a non-stationary setting, subtle asymptotic techniques are required to analyze the mean squared prediction errors so that both local and global behaviors can be assessed. As the asymptotic results involve evaluating the nonstandard limit distributions of stochastic integrals of generalized stochastic processes with random jumps and/or fractional Brownian motions, which is computationally challenging, we aim to develop efficient algorithms to compute these procedures in real time. Using the asymptotic results established in the proposed study, we will develop efficient numerical procedures that can be applied empirically. As finance is a rapidly developing discipline, it is crucial that pioneering research results be incorporated into the pedagogical front in a timely fashion. Because practitioners are faced with the challenge of handling operational risks that are non-stationary in nature, the successful completion of this project will lead to a deeper understanding of these statistical methods, which will enhance the applicability of non-stationary time series to risk management and other disciplines.

14325216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14325216.value: The recent surge of activity in risk management and financial econometrics has led to a huge demand for non-standard statistical procedures to be developed for the modeling of non-stationary and non-regular time series. In general, these types of time series belong to the area of critical phenomena, in which non-standard asymptotic are the rules rather than the exceptions. It is now generally accepted that the dynamic nature of diverse physical and financial phenomena requires one to take into account the ever-changing non-stationary, heavy-tailed and long-memory behavior. Throughout the past two decades, a cascade of theoretical research on the inference of non-stationary and heavy-tailed time series has been developed. In the course of these developments, it was found that many of the standard tools in asymptotic theory are not applicable and that there is a need to develop new ideas of weak convergence. In general, the weak convergence technique used in the finite variance case is very different from the infinite variance case, which in turn is drastically different from the long-memory case. With the concerted efforts of many scholars, it is now high time to assemble these results in order to prescribe a more comprehensive treatment of the asymptotic theory for critical phenomena from a prediction perspective. One major objective of the proposed study is to pursue a comprehensive treatment of these prediction results, from which we expect to derive new insights into these crucial phenomena. Establishing the asymptotic results of the relevant statistics constitutes only the first stage in the asymptotic inference. To understand the properties of the test statistics, one also needs to consider higher-order asymptotic of the corresponding prediction errors. Recently, Chan, Huang and Ing (2013) established a negative moment bound for the Fishers information matrix of a general time series, which provides the critical component for developing the higher order properties, including but not limited to prediction error analysis and model selection. The second objective of this study is to extend the idea of moment bounds to general non-stationary time series and to apply the moment bounds to prediction and model selection for non-stationary time series. Although many of these theoretical results are highly technical, it is expected that further understanding of the numerical underpinnings will be realized in this study, from which relevant practical implications can be derived.

14325216.label: Realisation of objectives
14325216.value: The main research objectives of this proposal have been realized. New statistical techniques for unifying non-stationary and/or long-memory processes and their related propoerties have been established. By virtue of the mean squared prediction error ideas, statistical methodolgies and their corresponding relationships with model selection criteria such as AIC, BIC and FPE for non-stationary time series are established. Consistency and asymptotic results have been obtained. The findings of this project cover a wide scope of statistical inference for non-stationary and/or long-memory time series. Together they cover objectives 1 and 2 to a large extent. In the course of these findings, new numerical procedures have to be developed and some of these methods have been reported in the relevant publications, which address objectives 3 and 4.

14325216.label: Major findings and research outcome
14325216.value: The major finding of this proposal is to employ mean squared prediction errors techniques to establish a unified statistical inference procedure for both non-stationary and long-memory time series models. In particular, by making use of the prediction criteria, consistency and related asymptotic properties of model selection criteria for non-stationary models are established. Further, numerical methods have also been developed in the course of this project to handle the convergence properties. The collected research outcomes not only offer an novel method to analyze non-staitonary time series, but also provide new avenues to evaluate model selection criteria for non-stationary and long-memory time series. Important research findings from this project were reported in major international conferences and published in premiere refereed journals, as stipulated in Part C: Tables 8 and 9.

14325216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14325216.value: As non-stationary models are widely used in different disciplines, the results obtained in this proposal can be used in many contexts. In particular, by introducing the idea of mean squared prediction errors, results from this project offer a novel way to analyze non-stationary and/or long-memory time series, which is of huge potential interest in financial risk management. The techniques developed in this project can be applied both to non-stationary and long-memory time series. In summary, with the established theoretical properties of the mean-squared prediction errors, the pursuit of a unified framework to analyze non-regular time series is greatly enhanced. Finally, in areas such as financial risk management and network engineering, where non-stationary and/or long-memory phenomena are rules rather than exceptions, results of this project offer a viable means to handle problems often occur in finance and economics.

14325216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14325216.value: All of the major objectives have been realized in this project. By virtue of the mean squared prediction error techniques, advances in model estimation and model selection can now be conducted in a unified manner. This project will bring significant impacts in modeling important non-stationary features not only for a single time series, but also for series exhibiting both non-stationary and long-memory behavors, where the joint effects from different sources have to be taken into account. In particular, the four objectives achieved in this proposal offer a platform and new direction that will lead to important advances in the pursuit of modeling non-stationary financial data. Finally, by publishing relevant papers in statistics as indicated in objective 4, important research developments can be disseminated to practitioners timely and effectively.

14500516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500516.value: 工作環境中基於參照點的自我控制研究：理論分析與經驗證據

14500516.label: Project Objectives
14500516.value: We test the effectiveness of various reference point candidates in workplace settings requiring workers’ self-control. We evaluate workers’ responsiveness to upward-revised versus downward-revised goals set by the employer. Comparing the influence of socially versus individually set goals, we evaluate the circumstances under which social-oriented comparison points, versus individual-oriented comparison points are more effective in motivating worker’s self-control. Then focusing on the social domain, we analyze whether being in a highly ranked position in a lower performing comparison pool of workers, or being a lower ranked worker in a high-performing pool of workers is more motivating for workers’ self-control. For each of the above hypotheses, we provide a psychologically plausible theoretical model which can explain behavior, and ultimately attempt to tie the collection of results across hypotheses together into a more generalized framework.

14500516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500516.value: Workers face many potential temptations in the workplace, such as working less diligently when not being monitored, delaying their work until the last minute while sacrificing quality, and engaging in detrimental but emotionally satisfying interactions with fellow workers and clients. Self-control is thus an important characteristic for workers’ successes. How can employers structure the workplace so that workers avoid succumbing to temptations, such that a constructive and productive workplace can be maintained? One strategy which is supported by several theories in behavioral economics, is that individuals can use benchmarks or “reference points” as self-control aids to reduce tendencies to give in to gratifying activities. Cultivation of reference points can assist in developing psychological rewards for achievement, psychological penalties for succumbing to undesirable activities, and mental preparedness for challenging situations, all of which can assist workers in self-control success, even in the absence of additional monetary or material rewards. Recent evidence establishes workers’ effective responses to existing reference points, as well as their willingness to voluntarily adopt reference points to motivate themselves. However, studies of what employers can do to develop and mold workers’ reference points are relatively sparse. In this project, we examine specific methods that employers can use to cultivate reference points as motivators for self-control in workplace environments, building upon research at the intersection of self-control and reference-dependence. We develop theory and collect empirical evidence which develops a more thorough understanding of individuals’ willingness to accept and adapt to various reference points to control their own efforts, including when goals can be beneficial and when they can be detrimental. Our studies focus on three themes on the effectiveness of reference points as self-control motivators: 1. the adjustment of the reference point over time in the upward or downward direction; 2. the relative influences of individual versus social reference points; and 3. the reference effect of a worker’s position in different local pools of co-workers. The results of our study will be of practical use to employers, providing insights on the behavioral benefits and drawbacks of various workplace structures which seek to cultivate reference points to motivate workers. We advance the academic literature at the intersection of reference-dependence, reference point selection, worker motivation and self-control, by providing insights on how workers respond to managers’ use of reference points. 雇員在工作中存在諸多傾向，例如當不受監督時有意降低努力程度、把工作拖延到最後一刻從而無法保證工作品質、為了滿足個人情感與同事進行不利於工作的互動，等等。因此，自我控制成為工人能保證工作品質的一項重要特徵。鑒於此，雇主應該如何創造有利的工作條件以使得雇員避免產生上述傾向，從而維持高效有益的工作環境？ 行為經濟學的多項理論為上述問題提供了一種可能的解決途徑：個體可以通過使用基準或“參照點”來輔助實現自我控制，以降低自身對具有誘惑性行為的傾向性。培養起參照點有助於建立對實現成就的精神層面獎勵、對不合意行為的心理層面懲罰、以及對具有挑戰性情境的心理預期，而這又有助於個體在缺乏貨幣或物質獎懲的條件下實現自我控制。近年來研究證明，雇員不僅會對已有的參照點做出有效的反應，也會為了實現自我激勵而自願選擇並建立參照點。然而，關於雇主如何影響雇員以建立有利於實現雇主自身目標的參照點方面的策略，已有研究涉及較少。 在本專案中，基於自我控制與參照依賴互動的研究，我們考察雇主在工作環境中可用來培養雇員參照點以幫助雇員實現自我控制的具體方法。通過理論建模和實證分析，我們試圖更加深刻而全面地理解個體如何接受並適應不同參照點來控制自身的努力程度，例如何時設定目標是有益的，而何時設定目標是有害的。我們的研究關注于參照點作為自我控制手段有效性的三個方面：1. 參照點隨時間推移的動態調整方向；2. 個體參照點與社會參照點的相對影響力；2. 個體雇員在不同雇員群體中所處位置的不同參照效應。 我們的研究結果將為各種不同的通過培養參照點以激勵員工的工作環境對員工行為所造成的利弊提供解釋和建議，這對企業的建設有直接的現實意義。我們通過考察雇員如何應對雇主設定的參照點，推進了學術文獻在參照依賴、參照點選擇、員工激勵、以及自我控制如何交叉互動這一領域的研究。

14500516.label: Realisation of objectives
14500516.value: Our project seeks an understanding of how workers respond to different types of reference points introduced by their employer, and thus contributes to knowledge of behaviorally effective reference-point policies that employers can use to effectively motivate workers. The objectives of the project have been achieved in a manner which is flexible to the dynamic process of discovery and design refinement. We believe that our originally stated objectives have been well-captured by the final outputs of this project. We describe briefly here what we have done, and the relevant outputs. We conducted two main types of experiments in this project, field experiment, and lab experiment and we produce one new manuscript for each type, respectively. The manuscripts (attached to this report) will be further refined and soon submitted to journals for publication. a. Mechanical Turk online experiments i. Individual effort tasks We utilized the online worker platform Mechanical Turk to implement our experiments in the field. The experiments took place between March 2019 and December 2020, and workers engaged in one of two possible tasks: a video word transcription task, designed to represent cognitive effort, and an online sliding bar task, designed to represent manual effort. From the video transcription tasks, which over 800 unique workers participated in, we found that workers’ performances were significantly influenced by our treatment interventions, which consisted of a 2x5 factorial design, with the two factors being: asking workers for an ex-ante non-incentivized self-estimation of how many words they would transcribe correctly, and the timing and level of external reference point (in the form of information about the performance of another worker). Both ex-ante self-estimation and exposing workers to a high reference point, on their own tended to increase performance, while there are nuances in terms of the details of the interactions between self-estimation, reference point level and timing. The margin for performance differences was primarily in terms of keeping workers from quitting or giving up on the task. We then implemented a series of different types of treatments with manual sliding of bars using a mouse as the main task. Over 2200 unique workers participated in these tasks altogether. Our individual task with the sliding bars was designed largely based on the treatments implemented in the video transcription task. Some adjustment was needed in finding the appropriate number of sliding bars to offer subjects appropriate piece rate payment per bar, and appropriate online page design to allow workers convenient stopping of the sliding bars if they would like to. These adjustments were made over 3 individual level sliding bar task experiments, which each also yielded useful information about the treatment effects. One of the striking findings was that, while introducing a high external reference point or asking for workers’ self-estimations still generally still enhanced performance, self-estimation sometimes induced negative performance effects, particularly among subjects who found the task more tedious. This raised a potential downside to self-estimation previously not apparent in the video transcription task: self-estimation can serve as a stopping cue, particularly when the external reference point introduced is a low one. On the other hand, we found that a low externally provided reference point by itself surprisingly has the potential to improve performance, perhaps through workers’ feeling of achievement. ii. Team Production We next implemented the sliding bar task, but in a more realistic setting, specifically team production. We informed workers that they would be matched with another MTurk worker, and both of them would be paid according to the average of the two workers’ performances. Thus, the team production setting is similar to a public goods game. In the first team production treatment, we utilized workers from the individual sliding bar task, and provided information about how they and their partner had previously performed in the individual task, thus effectively providing a social reference point. We found that surprisingly, there was hardly any free riding in this scenario. We also implemented the Team Production setting on brand new workers and found widespread shirking. We can deduce that prior experience completing a task successfully on an individual level prevents shirking under team production. iii. Social Distributions To examine the effect of payment inequality on worker motivation, we implemented an experiment in which each worker completes a simple and short task (10 sliding bars), and receives one of 5 random payments, where other workers in their group are assigned the other possible payments. We then compared workers’ willingness to incur risk based on their payment ranking, to their willingness to make a commitment to complete more work. We find that while the 4th ranked worker (second to last) is both most willing to take monetary risk, and most willing to commit to completing more work, the 1st ranked worker is also highly willing to commit to completing more work, while being relatively unwilling to accept monetary risks. b. Laboratory experiments on swagger and bragging We also implemented two main sets of experiments in the laboratory, using students from Tsinghua University and Beijing Foreign Studies University. The purpose of these experiments was to study specifically in more detail about self-declarations in the public and private domain, particularly with application to social media and social approval as a potential motivator. We conducted 4 treatments on swagger (ex-ante announcement about future action), and 4 treatments on bragging (ex-post announcement about past action). The treatments vary based on features of the level of social exposure and approval (ie. peers can anonymously provide “likes”), as well as subjects’ choice set in making the declarations. A total of 256 subjects participated in these laboratory experiments, which were run in April 2019 at Tsinghua, and in December 2019 at Beijing Foreign Studies University. While it is natural to think that the opportunity to self-declare about one’s accomplishments could serve as a substantial motivator, there are also some interesting counter-intuitive findings. Private goal-setting (swagger) and self-estimation (bragging), is generally less effective than public declarations in terms of improvement obtained, and in some instances, private evaluation performs worse than the control treatments. In the swagger treatments, the ability to choose one’s own goal is highly important in making an effective goal. Subjects were not so responsive to an externally set high goal, but they showed 100 percent compliance with their own endogenously chosen goals, and delivered the best performance improvements out of the treatments. We also find interesting dynamics regarding subjects’ allocation of “likes” among their peer groups. Subjects are generally not convinced by swagger, and only real results earn social approval. In addition, subjects tended to reward peers with median level self-declarations. However, when they can observe final performance, and can give “likes” twice, subjects tended to have sympathy both for those who consider themselves at the top and at the bottom. Summary: Thanks to this grant, we were able to implement at least 6 main sets of online and laboratory experiments that address the specific questions we set out to answer, as well as further examining closely related follow-up questions that arose during the research process. In addition, we have produced several publications that are related to the issues of individual motivation and social comparisons in different settings. These related projects all assisted and helped inspire our progress on this project, and we acknowledge the RGC accordingly in them.

14500516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500516.value: Online Experiments (select results): Insight 1: In the cognitive task, workers that self-estimated their performance have higher performance. Workers exposed to a high performance result by another worker also have higher performance. Insight 2: While all reference point treatment interventions produce significantly better aggregate performance than the control treatment in the cognitive task, the significant margin is in terms of worker retention. Insight 3: Asking workers for a self-estimation of their future performance significantly reduces their ex-post impressions of how they performed in the cognitive task. Insight 6: When workers are not informed about the total amount of possible work in a tedious task, the presence of externally provided reference points are influential in workers’ self-estimations and stopping points in their own performance. Insight 7: In a tedious task, the combination of introducing self-estimation and externally provided reference points as well as the timing of each, yields significant interaction effects. Insight 8: Among workers who have already performed a tedious task well at an individual-level, free-riding in the analogous team task setting is very rare compared to that of new workers. Insight 9: Workers at the bottom of the payment distribution take significantly more risk. However, workers near the bottom and the top of the payment distribution are most willing to make a commitment to additional work. Laboratory Experiments (select results): Result 1: In the swagger treatments, the privately set goal performs worse than the control treatment with no goal, while the treatment with public endogenous goal choice outperforms both the treatment with public exogenous goal choice and private goal. Result 2: Subjects in the public endogenously set goal successfully meet their goal, whereas the same is not true for either the privately or publicly exogenously set goal. Result 3: Publicity tends to alter subjects’ self-assessments away from the median. Result 4: In the bragging treatments, public self-assessment with one round of social approval and no verification tends to achieve the highest subsequent performance improvement. Result 5: Subjects in the private self-assessment treatment are more underconfident that subjects in the public self-assessment treatments. The public self-assessment with two rounds of social approval helps eliminate extreme over-confidence. Result 6: Self-assessment level is positively associated with subsequent performance. Over-confidence negatively predicts subsequent performance, while its influence wanes with the degree of public or social approval opportunity. Under-confidence positively predicts subsequent performance, while its influence strengthens with the degree of public or social approval opportunity. Further details are available in attached manuscripts.

14500516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500516.value: We have several plans for further development of this research. Firstly, we intend to more carefully analyze the survey data that we collected with the online experiments, which has not been incorporated into the current analysis yet, due to economists’ relative under emphasis on such data. However, we think that it could still yield interesting insights on how to better tailor reference point introduction to individual workers. Secondly, for the laboratory experiments, we intend to conduct further experiments and consider different types of social approval mechanisms to see if they effectively enhance performance.

14500516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500516.value: We conduct a series of experiments on how reference points from different sources potentially affect worker motivation in the absence of any material pay adjustment. In each experiment, whether online or in the laboratory, participants were invited to complete as many tasks as they preferred at a constant piece rate payment. Treatment interventions introduced one or more reference point suggestions or mechanisms as a potential ‘soft’ incentive. In the individual tasks, workers were asked to self-estimate their performance before-hand, and/or were informed about the performance of another worker, all of which have no direct implications on their payment earned. In additional treatments, workers were paid with each other in a team production setting, and informed of their partner’s prior performance. Follow-up treatments examined the effect of pay inequality on workers’ willingness to do more work. Laboratory experiments introduced a social media-like component with peer approval as a soft incentive. We find that reference-points in the non-monetary domain, whether through observation of peers, peers’ approval, or self-reflection, all have significant effects on workers’ performance, occasionally in counter-intuitive directions. The results should be informative to managers that would like to motivate employees without necessarily providing or imposing hard incentives.

14501616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501616.value: Liquidity plays a central role in the functioning of financial markets. Liquidity measures the ease with which market participants can transact, or the ability of markets to absorb large purchases or sales without much impact on prices. The importance of liquidity in financial markets is increased thought the recent innovation and structural changes in the financial system and is highlighted by the recent market turmoil, including the 1997 Asia financial crisis, the 2008 financial crisis, and the “flash crash” of May 2010. A greater diversity of financial institutions, which constitutes the market making industry, now plays an active role in the provision of liquidity. To guarantee liquidity supply, binding designated market making (DMM) contract is one of the widely used mechanisms in European security markets. Recently, exchanges in the US are also proposing to adopt this mechanism. However, the effect of this mechanism is yet to properly identify. In this project, we propose to exploit a discontinuity in the contractual obligations of Designated Market Maker (DMM) firms on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) to identify the causal effect of more binding DMM obligations on market quality. In particular, DMM firms on the NYSE are required to participate in the best bid and offer (BBO) quotes for a percentage of the trading day that depends on trading volume, with a discreet shift in the percentage above 1 million shares of average trading per day. A regression discontinuity research design focused on firms whose average trading volume passes through one million shares can reveal the causal effect of changing DMM quotation obligations on an array of market quality measures, including liquidity and price efficiency. In addition, we intent to use proprietary NYSE data to measure actual DMM trading activity as a function of DMM quotation obligations, and the attendant effects of DMM trading on market quality. 為了研究增加做市商需履行義務和市場運行質量變化的因果關係，我們找到了紐約證券交易所（NYSE）中指定做市商（DMM）公司做市義務變化的斷點事件。通常來講，紐約證券交易所的指定做市商公司必須為每交易日中一定百分比的交易提供最優詢／報價（NBBO），這個百分比是由交易量的多少確定的，根據每日平均交易大於一百萬股與否該百分比有兩個不同的規定值。因此對那些日均交易量在一百萬股上下的公司進行斷點回歸分析就可以揭示出做市商報價義務變化對於一系列市場運行質量指標變化的因果效應。我們發現增加做市商義務會提高市場流動性，價格有效性，和公司價值。

14501616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501616.value: We exploit a discontinuity in the New York Stock Exchange Designated Market Maker (DMM) contract to identify causal effects of DMM participation on equilibrium market outcomes. We document that contractual features that enhance DMM participation are associated with increased depth, narrower bid-ask spreads, and higher rates of price improvement, with most of the improvements attributable to increases in liquidity provision on markets other than the NYSE. These results cannot be attributed to the mechanical effects of the contractual changes and support the interpretation that market making is characterized by strategic complementarity. (JEL G10, G12, G19, G29) The paper has been accepted for publication in one of the top tier finance journal: The Review of Financial Studies.

14501616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501616.value: These results provide strong, if indirect, evidence that the knowledge that NYSE DMM contract is enhanced affects other traders’ order submission strategies and equilibrium in the market for liquidity. In particular, the results support the reasoning that market-making equilibrium is characterized by strategic complementarity in the sense of Bulow, Geanakoplos, and Klemperer (1985), where more aggressive play by one supplier (the DMM) results in decreased marginal costs for competitors. This result would arise if competitors are more certain that they can unwind unwanted inventory positions when the DMM obligation is more binding. The existence of strategic complementarity implies positive spillover effects in the business of liquidity supply. Such positive spillovers are important for theoreticians seeking to develop models of security market equilibrium, and also help to understand both the existence of illiquidity spirals and the fact that seemingly small DMM obligations can have substantive effects on equilibrium liquidity. Developing models that allow for such spillovers to gain an improved understanding of how the presence of contractually required DMM orders alters other traders’ behavior and equilibrium outcomes comprises an important challenge for future research.

14501616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501616.value: A key question facing those who design or regulate securities markets is whether the electronic limit order book can attract sufficient liquidity. A number of stock markets have voluntarily adopted DMMs for at least some securities, and recent MiFID II regulations require DMM contracts for algorithmic firms on European markets, while leaving the parameters of the contracts to the discretion of individual Exchanges. However, our collective understanding of economics of DMM contracts remains quite incomplete. We contribute to the understanding of these issues by studying DMMs on the New York Stock Exchange.

14501716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501716.value: 目標 本項目的目標是，分別從短期和中期來研究企業平均燃料消耗的市場均衡及福利效應。 項目背景 2012年,為了推動汽車製造商提高燃料節約技術水平,從而減少燃料消耗以及使用汽車產生的外部性,中國施行了《企業平均燃料消耗(CAFC) 標準》,要求每個企業以銷售額為權重的企業平均燃料消耗量(單位：升/ 100公里)必須低於一個因企業而異的目標值。 項目簡介 本項目將首次展開中國燃料節約法規的福利經濟學分析。根據Klier和Linn (2012),我們將構建和評估一個同時包括汽車市場需求和市場供給的均衡模型。特別地,我們將考慮汽車製造商短期的定價決策和中期產品特性的最佳選擇。然後，考慮到技術的可行性，我們將基於以上的估計進行政策模擬，來評估《CAFC標準》的福利效應。我們將進一步擴展Klier和Linn (2012)的模型，將汽車消費產生的外部性納入福利效應分析。這是政策評估中一個非常重要的問題，因為《CAFC標準》的主要目標就是減少這些外部性。 項目意義 本項目將擴充分析《CAFC標準》福利效應與成本效益的這部分文獻。這部分文獻普遍認為，同樣在美國施行《CAFC標準》，比直接徵收汽油稅的成本效益率更低，因為這些法案並不能促進汽車使用中汽油節約行為的產生。我們將提供《CAFC標準》福利效應的經驗證據，在這裡我們特地考慮了產品質量的內生選擇行為,因為這可能顯著降低《CAFC標準》的福利成本。此外,我們的研究將重點突出，燃料節約技術在所有權結構、來源國不同的公司以及遵守標準可行性不同的公司之間的異質性。然後，測試公司的決定是否符合《CAFC標準》這些政策背後的動機——推動合資企業使用他們的最佳技術以及推動本土企業迎頭趕上。最重要的是,我們將考察汽車使用的外部性,進而衡量《CAFC標準》的整體福利效應,而以往的研究都集中在考察《CAFC標準》的均衡效應。

14501716.label: Realisation of objectives
14501716.value: The project was completed and all objectives have been accomplished. In Xiao and Li (2018), we specify and estimate a market equilibrium model with both demand and supply sides. The demand side builds from a random utility model with consumer preference heterogeneity and this model leads to a random coefficients discrete choice model of vehicle demand. The supply side consists of multi-product firms that choose prices and vehicle attributes along the technology frontier which defines the tradeoffs between fuel economy and other vehicle attributes. Based on parameter estimates, we conduct counterfactual simulations to examine the impacts of the policy on product offering and market shares. We first conduct simulations for the short run where firms are only allowed to adjust prices but not other vehicle attributes as in traditional CAFE analysis (e.g., West, 2004; Jacobsen, 2013). In the medium-run, we allow adjustments in prices, vehicle weight and horsepower. We then measure the welfare effects of the policy taking into account consumer surplus, firm profits, externalities from gasoline consumption, and consumer undervaluation of fuel economy. The primary dataset includes: (1) detailed vehicle characteristics at the model level from 2008 to 2012 covering all vehicles sold in China; and (2) monthly national sales data by vehicle model from 2008 to 2012. We assess the effect of fuel tax (objective 5) in a sperate project. In Tan, Xiao and Zhou (2019), we investigate the market equilibrium and welfare effects of a fuel tax in China relative to an alternative policy instrument that rations the number of new automobile sales through auctioned quotas. Unlike those of previous studies, our modeling approach incorporates both household car purchase and utilization decisions, the latter of which have been ignored in previous studies on China's fuel tax. Ignoring this margin of choice will underestimate the fuel tax's ability to mitigate externalities. Using detailed household-level panel data and a fixed effects econometric specification, we estimate the fuel price elasticity of vehicle miles traveled is −0.59 on average. The results of the counterfactual analysis suggest that a 51% increase in tax-inclusive gasoline prices will reduce car sales by 24.9% but increase social welfare to a degree that depends on vehicles' lifetime. We find that compared to auctioned quotas, the fuel tax results in greater car sales but higher social welfare.

14501716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501716.value: The empirical findings of Xiao and Li (2018) suggest that in the short run, the market responses are very different across vehicle segment. The average prices of mini and small segments would decrease while sales increase for both cases of penalty levels. The pattern is opposite for the other five segments. In the short run, consumer welfare gain based on compensating variation is 2.66 billion Yuan per year and 3.98 billion Yuan under the low and high penalty cases, respectively. The medium run results are quite different from those in the short run. Vehicles prices drop quite significantly across all vehicle segments, especially for larger vehicles. The large price changes are likely driven by the fact that firms respond to the regulation by reducing vehicle horsepower and weight to increase fuel economy. Interestingly, vehicle sales only increase for mini, small and compact segments. The comparison between the short-run and medium-run results suggests that firms are able to respond to the fuel consumption regulation by changing vehicle attributes in the medium run in order to better comply with the regulation to avoid penalty. Overall, the impact on vehicle sales is dampened in the medium run relative to the short run because of the additional margins of adjustment. The empirical findings of Tan, Xiao and Zhou (2019) suggest that, on average, consumers will decrease their VMT by 0.59% in response to a 1% increase in fuel prices. We refer to this effect of the fuel tax on vehicle utilization as the VMT effect. A fuel tax leads to a welfare gain in all simulated scenarios with various assumptions on the lifetime of new vehicles, but the magnitude of welfare gains varies across scenarios. The VMT effect will not affect the overall welfare assessment when the fuel tax corrects only the externality, but it will affect the assessment of externality reduction: without considering the VMT effect, the effect of the fuel tax on externality reduction will be underestimated. Our main conclusions are not sensitive to various tax rates. These empirical results suggest a possible direction to extend the literature on the welfare analysis of vehicle-control policies in China (Li, 2018; Xiao et al., 2017), which has not considered the VMT effect. In contrast to the VQS in Shanghai, the fuel tax is less effective in vehicle control but more efficient in promoting social welfare.

14501716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501716.value: A potential extension of current research is to analyze a reform of the CAFC taking into account the role of electric vehicle in reducing the corporates' average fuel consumption. This is a very important topic as the market share of electric vehicle expands. Electric vehicle can dramatically reduce pollution and so enhance social welfare. Therefore, a reformed CAFC in favor of electric vehicle manufacturer should contribute to social welfare gain. A comprehensive welfare analysis of such a policy can provide rare empirical evidence to the literature.

14501716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501716.value: This study provides the first analysis on the welfare impacts of Corporate Average Fuel Consumption Standards first enacted in 2012 in China. Our analysis shows that the CAFC regulation leads to overall welfare gain in the short run but welfare loss in the medium run by changing the nature of competition. Consumers benefit from the regulation while firm profit decreases as the competition intensifies with the regulation effectively making product differentiation more costly.

14502416.label: Project Objectives
14502416.value: From a managerial marketing perspective, we will find and decompose the various effects that social communications among customers in mobile social networks have on firm performance. It is important that marketers learn to manage social communications among the members of mobile social networks, as these communications eventually generate profits to firms. This study will explore the different effects that network members’ social communications have on the stages of visitation, conversion and purchase amount. The results will help marketing managers to understand not only how social communications operate, but also how to plan and implement social network marketing campaigns for those stages of participation. From a theoretical perspective, we will provide a new concept of overlapping networks that is highly relevant in today’s online social networking environment. Despite the wealth of sociological theory in relation to social networks, our concept of studying network overlaps has not previously been proposed, even though it has some similarities with research on network embeddedness or overlapping cliques. This gap in research exists mainly because when the prevailing sociological theories on social networks were developed decades ago, online social network platforms did not exist as we have them today. Our study will make an important contribution by extending and updating social network theory in the field of sociology. From a methodological perspective, we will provide a generalized framework of empirical analysis on the various stages of users’ activities (visits, conversions and purchase amounts) across multiple online social networks. First, our model will find and decompose the net effects that social communications have on three stages of user participation in a single social network platform. Second, our generalized model will enable us to discover various sources of dependencies that induce customers to engage in multiple social network platforms. These sources of dependency include coincidence, correlated sensitivities and experience spillover. More importantly, our model will find whether and to what degree the spillover effects of social communications are asymmetric across networks.

14502416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14502416.value: This study will investigate various effects that social communications among customers in multiple mobile social network platforms have on service performance. First, we will develop an integrated model of visitation, conversion and purchase amount for customers in a mobile social network game. To do so, we will develop a new measure of social communication effects, integrating the whole network structure along with the quantity and quality of peer-to-peer interactions using the Markov random field (MRF). We will apply this model to the data from a mobile social network game service, which contain information on daily levels of usage, purchases and peer-to-peer communication activities. Our model will detect when and how social communications are effective for customers who enjoy mobile social network games. Such information can provide important managerial implications for the timing of social marketing campaigns. Furthermore, our MRF model will be able to discover the relationship among people in a whole network and the strength of its dyadic bonds. Second, we will study customer behavior across multiple social network platforms. To be specific, we are interested in one of the sources that create interdependency across networks, that is, social communications with overlapping friends across networks. To address this factor, we propose a joint model that accommodates communication activities across social networks. We will apply our model to the data from two mobile social network game services, wherein the users have considerable overlap among friends across games. The data also contain daily levels of activity (i.e., visits, purchases and peer-to-peer communication activities) at the individual level. Our second model will capture various sources of interdependencies across social networks, including coincidence (e.g., whether users accidentally play multiple social network games), correlated preference (e.g., whether users happen to be influenced by social communications in both or either of the networks) and experience spillover across networks (e.g., whether users’ play experience in one network platform may affect their play in the other network platform). Our model will also determine whether the spillover effects of social communications (i.e., information flows) are asymmetric across networks. We will conduct a simulation study that provides managerial implications for organizations attempting to target valuable customers and to allocate marketing resources across multiple social networking services. 這項研究將會考察在多個移動社交網絡平臺中用戶之間的社會溝通對用戶行爲和服務體驗的多種效應。 首先，我們會建立關於一個移動社交網絡遊戲的用戶瀏覽，轉化和購買行爲的綜合模型。基於這個模型，我們將會發展一個新方法去測量社會溝通效應。這個新方法會利用Markov Random Field（MRF），並同時考慮整體網絡結構以及其中點對點互動的品質和數量。 我們將應用這個綜合模型去擬合關於一個移動社交網絡遊戲服務的數據。該數據包括使用，購買以及點對點溝通行爲的每日信息。綜合模型將會檢測社會溝通在何種時機和何種狀態下對正在使用移動社交網絡遊戲服務的用戶是具有效用的。這方面內容具有非常重要的管理營銷意義，特別是針對社交網絡的營銷信息的推送時機方面。此外，MRF模型還能夠考量在整個網絡當中人與人的聯系和感情的強度是正面還是負面。 第二，我們將會研究用戶在多個移動社交網絡的跨平臺行爲。我們感興趣的是其中一種導致跨平臺相互聯系的原因，即是不同的社交網絡平臺中擁有重疊的用戶。爲了研究這個問題，我們提出一種聯合模型可以包含跨社交網絡平臺的溝通行爲。 我們將會應用這種聯合模型去擬合關於兩個移動社交網絡遊戲服務的數據，在這兩個移動社交網絡遊戲平臺當中用戶擁有相當大比例的重疊。該數據包括用戶瀏覽，購買以及點對點溝通行爲的每日信息。 在第二個模型擬合的分析當中，我們將會同時捕捉多種跨社交網絡平臺的相互依賴效應，包括偶然效應（例如，用戶是否巧合地同時參加多個社交網絡遊戲），相關偏好（例如，用戶是否受到雙方或一方網絡社會溝通的影響），外溢效應（例如，用戶在一個網絡平臺上的遊戲體驗是否會影響他們在其它網絡平臺上的體驗）。我們的模型也會檢視社會溝通的溢出效應在不同網絡平臺上是否對稱。此外，我們也會進行模型仿真分析，該分析將會對尋找潛在價值客戶以及在多個網絡平臺分配營銷資源提供指引。

14502416.label: Realisation of objectives
14502416.value: The original proposal was intended to tackle the issues of social communication effects on social network platforms from both academic and managerial perspectives, for example, how peer-to-peer communications operate in customers’ various decision making processes (e.g., usage, conversion, purchase volume) and it has spillover effects across multiple social network platforms. However, the reviewers from journals had raised a concern of endogeneity and identification of social communication and social influence. Thus, we measure the social communication through observational learning, instead of communications between peers (i.e., how many times a peer exchange text and non-text messages). Then, we use the social communication to identify homophily rather than to measure social influence. In addition, the previous version identify two types of friends such as overlapped and not overlapped between different social networking services. Going through review processes for journals, we further identify the types of friends. Specifically, we categorize friends of a user into four types based on network embeddedness within and across social network services as conceptualized in the previous section. The first type is a set of friends of a user embedded within a network and across two networks. These friends share mutual friends in network A and are friends to each other in both networks. The second type is a set of friends of a user embedded only across two networks. They are friends to each other in both networks, but they do not have mutual friends in a network. The third type is a set of friends of a user embedded only within a network. That is, they share mutual friends in a network with a user, but they are not friends with a user in both networks, as they do not belong to the other network. The fourth type is a set of friends of a user who are not embedded within or across networks By doing so, we found that friends exert different social effects depending on whether they are embedded within a network or across networks. Specifically, the social influence of embedded friends is stronger than that of friends not embedded. More importantly, friends embedded only across networks are more positively associated with users’ repeat visits to a focal network service, followed by friends embedded both within a network and across networks. Importantly, this offers an explanation on mixed findings for network embeddedness by previous literature. For practical and managerial purpose, we also demonstrated how practitioners can use our proposed approach by conducting an analysis in which the firm manages two social network services. For example, if firms do not analyze customers’ individual (ego-centric) networks across different services, they cannot identify pairs of users who are important to each other. Our study also makes theoretical contribution to studies on issues that arise when people engage and communicate with friends over multiple social network services, as neither empirical nor theoretic work has explained different social effects when friends are embedded across different network platforms. Drawing on social learning theory and information transfer theory, we can explain the differences. Friends embedded within as well as across networks may exert normative social influence. However, friends embedded across networks may not necessarily exert more normative influence than those embedded only within a network. In terms of informative social influence, we posit that friends within and across networks may play different roles in social networks. Friends embedded across different networks may exert more informative social influence than friends embedded in only one network. In addition, our study offers a new direction to investigate the contradictory findings (e.g., weak or strong) on the effects of network embeddedness compared to prior studies.

14502416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14502416.value: First, consistent with prior studies, we find that social influences account for increases in users’ repeated visitations to multiple social network services. Second, our empirical results show that friends embedded within a network and those embedded across network services are associated with users differently. Specifically, when friends are embedded only across networks, their social influence is the greatest, followed by the social influence from friends embedded both within and across networks. Friends embedded only within a network do not exert a great social influence. We also conduct analyses to determine how customer strategies depend on network embeddedness structures of users across the services. First, we provide a strategy of targeting customers by network embeddedness and social network strategies. We find that firms that do not analyze users’ friends embedded both within and across networks are not able to identify and target pairs of users (i.e., social groups) by accessing biased social influences. Interestingly, this finding also offers an explanation of mixed findings (e.g., positive or negative) on network embeddedness by previous studies. In addition, we also explore how the influences of variously embedded friends evolve over time. The influence of friends embedded across network services tends to decrease over time, while that of friends embedded only within a single network remains rather stable. Specifically, firms need to use network friends embedded across network services when users begin engaging in the service. However, friends embedded only within a network become more influential later on. This result shows the importance of “weak ties”; friends embedded only within a network represent weak ties, while friends embedded across networks represent strong ties in our context. We also offer a theoretic explanation for this based on social influence theory.

14502416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14502416.value: It would be a useful extension of our study to investigate how people’s social networks that have been structured in one platform affect their networking behaviors on other platforms (e.g., spillover, learning from the old platform). Different data and modeling approaches are required to determine how embedded friends contribute to the joint evolution of multiple social network services. In addition, we applied the models empirically to the data sets from two mobile social network games, each with its own networks. Thus, our managerial implications may be limited to the empirical context of social network gaming services. Further research is warranted to establish generalizability, as other social network services such as Facebook and Instagram may have different features. Other strategic implications, such as sharing content across social network services, may require additional analyses in disparate contexts. Last, our focus on the structures of two networks is limited to the measure of network embeddedness. This aspect could be extended in studies that explore the effects of network centrality properties, such as connectivity, betweenness, and closeness, on management phenomena. Developing new network centrality properties applicable to more than one network would provide new insights into network structures across multiple social networks. We leave these worthwhile directions to further research.

14502416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14502416.value: The findings of our study shed light on social marketing strategies and customer relationship management when firms manage or take part in more than one social network service (e.g., Facebook, Tencent, Zynga, EA). We found that friends exert different social effects depending on whether they are embedded within a network or across networks. Specifically, the social influence of embedded friends is stronger than that of friends not embedded. More importantly, friends embedded only across networks are more positively associated with users’ repeat visits to a focal network service, followed by friends embedded both within a network and across networks. However, although friends embedded only within a network represent weak ties, their social influence remains stable. By contrast, the social influence of friends embedded across networks decreases over time, which can be explained by their informative social influence. Last, we also demonstrated how practitioners can use our proposed approach by conducting an analysis in which the firm manages two social network services. For example, if firms do not analyze customers’ individual networks across different services, they cannot identify pairs of users who are important to each other.

14503416.label: Project Title(Chinese)

14503416.label: Project Objectives
14503416.value: This project will construct a unique spatiotemporal data set of the transportation system of China in 2000s and the firm level data with geo-referenced information. This data set can be the foundation for many other important topics such as how infrastructure reshapes industrial agglomeration, inter-regional trade, city growth, and pattern of migration. The project will conduct the first systematic analysis on the impact of the massive investment in infrastructure in China on firm performance. In particular, we will study how the transportation network in China helps domestic firms to export and import, and also improves firm productivity. We will explore the heterogeneous effect of transportation infrastructure on different types of firms. One particular question is which types firms benefit more from the improvement of transportation network. Our analysis will have important policy implications, particular for the government new initiative for globalization: “One Belt and One Road”. Our analysis can cast the light on the question how infrastructure improves market integration within China and thus helps firms go globally. This project also provides micro evidence for the government spending multiplier. Public investment in infrastructure is one of the important channels that fiscal stimulus could boost the economy. However, most of studies focus on macro level analysis and our study can provide micro-evidence for the effect of infrastructure investment on firms output and productivity.
