14519816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14519816.value: We build a dynamic model to link two empirical patterns: the negative failure probability-return relation (Campbell, Hilscher, and Szilagyi, 2008) and the positive distress risk premium-return relation (Friewald, Wagner, and Zechner, 2014). We show analytically and quantitatively that (i) equity-to-debt ratios and levered equity betas negatively covary with the market risk premium in distressed firms; (ii) negative covariance generates low stock returns and negative alphas among those firms; and (iii) firms with a lower distress risk premium endogenously choose higher leverage, so they are more likely to become distressed and earn negative returns. We provide empirical evidence to support our model predictions.

14519816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14519816.value: It would be interesting to extend the model and estimate the intangible, human capital cost of a manager via structural estimation, if the firm she has been managing goes bankrupt.

14519816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14519816.value: Distress risk plays a central role in corporate financing choices and asset prices. Even though distress risk deters debt taking, empirical evidence on the equity distress risk premium in asset prices is mixed. We expect high returns for high risk-taking. However, Campbell et al. (2008) document a negative relation between failure probabilities and stock returns. This is puzzling because it is against our intuition. In contrast, Friewald et al. (2014) find a positive relation between the distress risk premium (from credit default swaps) and stock returns, which differs from the finding by Campbell et al. Even more puzzling, firms with a high failure probability or a low distress risk premium have high equity betas but low stock returns on average. In this study, we develop a unified framework to explicitly link seemingly contradictory observations, i.e., the negative failure probability-return relation and the positive distress risk premium-return relation

14521316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14521316.value: 眾籌平台作為一個新的融資方式為創新者提供了一個在網絡上向大眾融資的機會。創新者（又稱為“項目創始人”）可以在眾籌平台上提交一個項目，並向大眾公開融資；而大眾（又稱“項目支持人”）可以在眾籌平台上給自己支持的項目投資。眾籌平台已經在全球迅速興起。目前已經融資162億美金。而北美和亞洲已經在2014年成為最大的兩個眾籌市場。隨著眾籌平台的興起，企業家和研究者都想知道是什麼因素影響了一個項目在眾籌平台上的成敗。 我們從兩個渠道收集了獨特的數據：眾籌平台和社交網絡。更重要的是，在我們的數據中，我們收集了眾籌平台使用者的社交網絡數據。因此，我們可以准確地知道項目創始人和支持者背後的社交網絡。隨後我們將這些數據和計量模型相結合，以便研究一個項目的成敗是如何受到項目創始人和支持者的社交網絡的影響。具體而言，我們聚焦三個問題：朋友的支持在什麼時候最重要，什麼類型的項目最需要朋友的支持，哪裡的朋友（本地的還是外地的）的支持更重要。 我們的研究對理論有三方面的貢獻。首先，眾籌平台和社交網絡數據的結合使項目創始人和支持者的社交網絡得以准確定位。因此我們可以准確地知道社交網絡對於眾籌平台的作用。第二，通過比較社交網絡對不同類型的項目在融資周期的各個階段的作用，我們可以幫助研究者更好地理解社交網絡對眾籌平台的動態影響，以及對各類項目影響的大小。第三，我們對於本地朋友和外地朋友的研究可以幫助研究者更好地理解眾籌平台是否不再受到地理位置的影響。 我們的研究還可以幫助創業者在眾籌平台上成功地融資。我們的研究將告訴創業者什麼樣的項目在什麼時候最應該仰仗朋友的幫忙，什麼樣的朋友（本地的還是外地的）的幫忙是最重要的。

14521316.label: Realisation of objectives
14521316.value: Overall we have successfully completed almost all objectives. Most importantly, our paper "The Small Predicts Large Effect in Crowdfunding" out of this project is forthcoming at Journal of Consumer Research (DOI 10.1093/jcr/ucaa013). Here are the details of our achievement of each objective. For the first objective, we have successfully achieved it by compiling a comprehensive dataset that combines the individual funders' contributions on one of the earliest crowdfunding platforms in China (DemoHour.com) with those funders' as well as project creators' online social networks from one of the largest online social networks in China (Weibo.com). With this unique dataset, we are able to identify whether a funder and a project creator are online friends on Weibo.com. For the second objective, we carefully investigated the impact of project creators' friends on the fundraising success of a crowdfunding project. We found that if a friend contributed a large amount of money at the early stage of a project's fundraising campaign, it can hurt the fundraising success of this project, even though the friendship is not observed on crowdfunding platform. But the small amount of contributions from friends can help the fundraising success of a project. We term this finding "Small Predicts Large Effect". With five online experiments (including a incentive compatible experiment), we showed the reason behind this seemingly counter-intuitive finding. We found that this Small Predicts Large effect is driven by people’s relationship inferences: when contributions made at the early stages of a crowdfunding campaign mainly comprise relatively large amounts, consumers tend to infer that those large contributions were made by the entrepreneur’s friends or relatives. Because of this relationship inference, prospective funders perceive larger contributions as being less diagnostic of others’ true opinions of the project, and this perception negatively affects their willingness to contribute. Furthermore, we showed that if a crowdfunding campaign provides sufficient justification for the early-stage large contributions, this Small Predicts Large effect will be eliminated. In addition, we showed that the Small Predicts Large effect has a time window, that is, the Small Predicts Large effect is significant in the first week of a crowdfunding campaign and is not significant afterwards. In fact, a Large Predicts Large effect begins to be observed after the 13th day of a crowdfunding campaign. In other words, we found that the Small Predicts Large effect is significant in the early stages of a crowdfunding campaign and becomes insignificant or even becomes opposite in the late stages. These findings highlight the crucial role of early-stage funders’ behavior in a project’s success, and help us reconcile the findings of our main analysis with prior research on herding behavior (Zhang and Liu 2012). Furthermore, we carefully examined the categories of projects which are most influenced by friends' contributions, as we put in the third objective. We found the Small Predicts Large effect is robust across different project categories, including charity vs. non-charity projects, large vs. small projects. In the experiments, we also used different types of projects and we found the Small Predicts Large effect in all those projects. For the fourth objective, we examined if friends' influence on the success of a project depends on their geographic locations. But we found the geographic locations do not significantly influence the success of a project. One potential reason is that most funders and project creators were from the large cities in China (e.g., Beijing, Shanghai) and therefore our data lack variation in geographic locations. But we believe it is an interesting research question for future studies.

14521316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14521316.value: Entrepreneurs are increasingly relying on online crowdfunding — the use of online platforms to raise money from a large number of people — to finance their ventures. This research explores the proposition that the amounts contributed by the majority of funders in the early stages of a crowdfunding campaign may have a counterintuitive influence on follow-up contributions and on the campaign’s fundraising success. Findings from an analysis of real-world large-scale crowdfunding data and five experiments show that potential funders are more (vs. less) likely to contribute to a newly launched project when early contributions consist mainly of relatively small (vs. large) amounts. The results further show that this Small Predicts Large effect is driven by people’s relationship inferences: when contributions made at the early stages of a crowdfunding campaign mainly comprise relatively large amounts, consumers tend to infer that those large contributions were made by the entrepreneur’s friends or relatives. Because of this relationship inference, prospective funders perceive larger contributions as being less diagnostic of others’ true opinions of the project, and this perception negatively affects their willingness to contribute. However, if a crowdfunding campaign provides sufficient justification for the early-stage large contributions, this Small Predicts Large effect will be eliminated.

14521316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14521316.value: Our research demonstrated that, in the early stages of a crowdfunding campaign, potential funders use individual funders’ contribution amounts as a basis for relationship inferences. Future research might investigate other potential relationship signals in crowdfunding contexts, such as fundraising pace or the comments funders leave for the entrepreneur on the crowdfunding platform. Research might also identify which information items potential funders tend to focus on at different stages of a crowdfunding campaign. Future research may also provide further insights into the interplay between individual differences and social relationship inferences in affecting people’s willingness to contribute to a crowdfunding campaign. For example, the need for uniqueness (Snyder and Fromkin 1977, 1980) and power perception (Rucker, Galinsky and Dubois 2012) may motivate consumers to manifest their differences relative to others, and therefore be less likely to follow the behavior of early funders. Finally, our research used online social network data to show that entrepreneurs’ online friends contributed more money and contributed earlier than strangers contribute. However, the data did not allow us to test the causality between online friendship and crowdfunding contributions. Therefore, future research might further examine the role of online friendship in motivating contributions to crowdfunding projects.

14521316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14521316.value: Online crowdfunding has emerged as a popular way for entrepreneurs to finance their ventures. Prior research has generally shown that entrepreneurs’ friends and relatives play a positive role in promoting campaign success. This research adopts the perspective of potential funders and finds that contributions from an entrepreneur’s friends and relatives may be counterproductive. Findings from an analysis of real-world large-scale crowdfunding data and five experiments show that people are more (vs. less) likely to contribute to a newly launched project when early contributions consist mainly of relatively small (vs. large) amounts. We suggest that this Small Predicts Large effect is driven by people’s relationship inferences: when contributions made at the early stages of a crowdfunding campaign mainly comprise relatively large amounts, people tend to infer that those large contributions were made by the entrepreneur’s friends or relatives. Because of this relationship inference, prospective funders perceive larger contributions as being less diagnostic of others’ true opinions of the project, and this perception negatively affects their willingness to contribute. Our research contributes to the literature on crowdfunding and herding. We also offer useful practical implications for entrepreneurs seeking to succeed in crowdfunding initiatives and for the design of crowdfunding platforms.

14521716.label: Project Objectives
14521716.value: 1. To develop a general approach to modeling consumer behavior within a network. In particular, two issues, the endogeneity of network formation and the effects of network structure will be specifically addressed. I will apply this new approach to study the adoption of the new smartphone within an individual’s telecommunication network. a. Set up the general model. The model will combine the classic spatial autoregressive model with a latent spatial model that deals with network formation. I will define the regulator conditions for the system, in particular, the restriction condition for estimation. b. Estimate the empirical model using the mobile dataset obtained from a major wireless carrier in China. I will use Bayesian MCMC to estimate the model. 2. To develop a procedure to define the boundaries of networks and calculate the measures of network structure. a. Use the modified T-CLAP algorithm (Godinho de Matos et al., 2014) to define the network boundaries of so as to minimize the overlap among networks. b. Calculate network structure measures at both the micro and macro level. Conduct factor analysis to identify the hidden factors in the measures so as to deal with the multicollinearity issue arising from high correlation among the structure measures. 3. To conduct policy simulation based on the model and parameter estimates, and offer insights into the network-based targeting strategy, which will allow companies to perform more effective targeting compared to the individual-based targeting strategy.

14521716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14521716.value: We propose a new modeling approach for individual behavior within a network, which considers the effects of the network structure through three channels: (1) the local network position of each individual; (2) the global network structure as a correlated effect; and (3) the effect of network structure on social influence. Network structure is measured by both ego and full network strategies according to three aspects of the network: centrality, transitivity, and diversity.The challenge of modeling the effects of network structure is the endogeneity of network formation, which we propose to overcome by using a general network formation model with controls for individual unobserved heterogeneity. Specifically, we study the new smartphone adoption behavior using the data collected from a telecommunications company. We find the transitivity measure of a network structure to have the largest effect - the more clustered the network is, the more adopters it will have. The alternative model specifications without network structure face an omitted bias problem. We also collected additional data five months after the initial sampling period, conducted out-of-sample predictions using the transitivity information of a two-layered snowball sample network for each individual, and then compared the prediction results of our model with a Probit model, both with and without network structure information. The results demonstrate a superior predictive validity of the proposed strategy and confirm that incorporating network structure information can improve individual adoption predictions and thus the effectiveness of targeting, especially for innovative products in the early stage. We name this new strategy ``network-based targeting.'' Research outcome: This research was published as Chapter 7 in the book "Mining Over Air: Wireless Communication Networks Analytics" (ISBN: 978-3-030-06403-7) by the renowned publisher Springer. The book has been translated into Chinese with the name "移动通信大数据分析——数据挖掘与机器学习实战 " (ISBN：9787302541240) by 清华大学出版社. Note: As both publications are books, the full versions are too big to be submitted to RGC. I have provided the book purchase links instead. The PI has also presented the result in several conferences and seminars with acknowledgement of RGC funding support: 1. Guest Speaker, China Telecom (Shang Hai), Big Data and Technology in Telecom Industry Workshop 2. Seminar, Network Based Targeting: The Effectiveness of Peer Influence within Social Networks, NUS 3. Guest speaker, Network based targeting, BIT's 5th Annual Global Congress of Knowledge, Qingdao, China, 09/2018

14521716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14521716.value: This research can be further developed along two dimensions. First, the technique of network analysis can be applied to other studies. PI is currently working on a project related to the market structure of the App industry. In that project, PI will use network analysis to depict the industry. Second, the proposed idea of Network Based Targeting can be used to solve real business problem. PI plan to work with telecom companies to implement this strategy.

14521716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14521716.value: The current targeting strategy used in marketing field tends to focus on individual demographic and immediate social network information . And when companies choose influencers in digital marketing campaigns, they only rely on a single indicator, which is how many followers the internet celebrity has. We proposed a new targeting strategy, which utilizes the information regarding the importance and characteristics of each individual within an entire social network, to achieve a better targeting effects. The new strategy can help companies choose the "super influencer" based on a comprehensive analysis of the social network to more effectively promote their products or services. This research demonstrates the value of big data as well as the cutting-edge analytical tools that combining the two can significantly broaden our understanding of human behavior and make big changes to the practices.

14522716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14522716.value: We define non-GAAP tax rate as the effective tax rate applied to non-GAAP earnings. When firms decide to exclude certain income and/or expense items from GAAP earnings, they have to adjust these exclusions net of tax to arrive at after-tax non-GAAP earnings. Thus, the non-GAAP tax rate has a direct effect on after-tax non-GAAP earnings, a metric focused on by managers and market participants. Depending on the types of exclusion items, some exclusions create a permanent difference between book and taxable income, whereas other exclusion items create a temporary difference or no book-tax difference. Hence, the non-GAAP tax rate is a function of the GAAP tax rate and the existence and magnitude of exclusion items that create permanent differences. We study non-GAAP tax rates for two reasons. First, despite the SEC’s guidelines on the disclosure of the tax adjustment on non-GAAP earnings, there is scant evidence as to how and to what extent firms comply with the guidelines in a large sample. Second, we expect that managers could use non-GAAP tax rates opportunistically when they report non-GAAP earnings. When the market has an expectation of what items are typically excluded, adding an exclusion item that was not previously excluded is likely to draw attention and be penalized by the market. Managers could instead adjust the tax rates applied to existing exclusions to affect the after-tax non-GAAP earnings. Moreover, manipulating the tax rates applied to exclusions does not require journal entries or justification with the auditor because non-GAAP numbers are not audited. Finally, manipulating non-GAAP tax rates will not affect the reported total or deferred tax expenses, so managers are less concerned about future reversals. In the non-GAAP reporting setting where the complexity of tax expense estimation is high and rigorous verification from external auditors is low, we hypothesize that managers have opportunities and incentives to manipulate the tax rates applied to exclusions to meet or beat earnings benchmarks. We test the hypothesis by exploiting a new disclosure requirement under the SEC’s Compliance and Disclosure Interpretation published in 2010. Our study contributes to the literature by providing new evidence on an alternative tool managers could use to manipulate reported non-GAAP earnings. Our initial evidence also suggests that the noncompliance of firms’ reporting of the tax effects of exclusions is pervasive, which potentially merits the attention of regulators. Finally, the evidence also has implications for market participants such as investors and financial analysts. 我們定義非公認會計準則稅率(Non-GAAP tax rate)為適用於非會計準則收益 (Non-GAAP earnings)之有效稅率。當公司決定排除某些收入和/或支出項目時，必須調整這些排除項目所得稅费用對收益之影響以計算出 Non-GAAP earnings。一些排除項目會造成帳務處理與稅務處理之永久性差異，而其他排除項目會造成暫時性差異或沒有差異。因此，Non-GAAP tax rate 對 Non-GAAP earnings 有直接的影響。 我們研究 Non-GAAP tax rate 動機如下。第一，儘管美國證交會對如何披露 Non-GAAP tax rate有其規範，現有文獻對公司披露是否符合規範沒有相關的記載。第二，我們推測經理人可用操縱 Non-GAAP tax rate 做為盈餘管理的手段之一。首先，經理人可以調整排除項目的適用稅率來影響Non-GAAP earnings。之外，操縱Non-GAAP tax rate 不需透過計帳分錄或審計師批准及審核。最後，操縱Non-GAAP tax rate不會影遞延稅項，所以經理人不需擔心未來應計項目迴轉。在市場重視 Non-GAAP earnings 及所得稅費用估計的複雜性高及外部審計師核實率低的情況下，我們推測經理人有機會操縱 Non-GAAP tax rate 來進行盈餘管理。 我們通過美國證交會於2010年頒布有關如何披露 Non-GAAP tax rate來測試假說。透過提供新的數據及實證結果對盈餘管理領域做出貢獻。初步證據顯示，企業所披露之 Non-GAAP tax rate 違規情況相當普遍。監管部門，投資者，分析師對其潛在問題值得關注。

14522716.label: Realisation of objectives
14522716.value: We have completed the project with the stated objectives. Overall, we have completed a working paper with solid results. We have presented this paper at various interactional conferences, including AAA Annual Meeting, EAA Annual Congress, and Hawaii Accounting Research Accounting Conference. In addition, we have presented our paper at workshop at various universities such as National Tsing Hua University, National Taipei University, and National Chengchi University. The paper has gone through the review process at JAR and The Accounting Review. The paper is currently under revision to be submitted at Review of Accounting Studies in May. We believe the objectives are fully completed as follows: Regarding the objective 1, to our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate income tax disclosure in non-GAAP reporting. Despite the SEC’s concern about firms not fully disclosing the tax effect of non-GAAP exclusions, there is a dearth of empirical evidence on how firms comply with the disclosure requirements outlined in the two C&DIs. Among non-financial S&P 1500 firms that report after-tax non-GAAP metrics in 2013, we find that a nontrivial percentage do not disclose or discuss the tax effect of non-GAAP adjustments. Given the complexity of accounting for income taxes and the amount of discretion that managers have in non-GAAP reporting, our study sheds light on whether regulators should mandate more detailed and standardized disclosure on the tax effect of non-GAAP exclusions. For the objective 2, our study identifies a specific tax channel through which mangers can use at their discretion in the meet or beat setting. McNichols (2003) argues that a specific accrual approach could have greater power to identify earnings management. We show that perception management via TREx is incremental to earnings management via GAAP-based accounts. Hence, our study adds to the literature that focuses on firms’ uses of specific accounts in perception management and aids our overall understanding of firms’ discretionary income tax reporting. We have also achieved Objective 3 and Objective 4. Our study has implications for users of non-GAAP numbers, including investors, analysts, and regulators. Our results should aid financial statement users in monitoring non-GAAP earnings disclosure, especially the GAAP to non-GAAP reconciliation. In particular, when TREx deviates from GAAP ETR or the statutory rate, and when such deviation increases after-tax non-GAAP earnings, it raises a red flag about the reported after-tax non-GAAP numbers. Given that tax effects take up about one-third of pretax numbers, users of non-GAAP numbers should pay closer attention to how TREx is determined. Our earnings and cash flow tests suggest that re-computing non-GAAP earnings using GAAP ETR or the statutory rate can improve one’s ability to forecast future GAAP earnings and cash flows.

14522716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14522716.value: In this study, we assemble a detailed hand-collected dataset of S&P 1500 firms to provide the first large-sample evidence on the reporting of the tax effects. We document three findings. First, echoing the SEC’s concern, a significant proportion of non-GAAP reporting firms do not comply with the C&DIs’ disclosure requirements (i.e., the tax effects of exclusions are not separately disclosed). Second, among firms that comply with the C&DIs and disclose the tax effects of exclusions, we find that managers opportunistically use the tax rate applied to non-GAAP exclusions (hereafter, TREx) to achieve after-tax earnings targets. Third, firm-reported non-GAAP earnings calculated using TREx are less persistent for future operating earnings and cash flows, as compared to non-GAAP earnings calculated using various benchmark tax rates. Overall, our study provides the first large-sample evidence on firms’ strategic use and reporting of TREx.

14522716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14522716.value: Our study provides the first large sample evidence on the use and reporting of TREx. Our study is of interest to the SEC, analysts, investors, and researchers. Our findings suggest that a discrepancy between TREx and GAAP ETR (or the statutory rate) may raise a red flag about managerial opportunism and the informativeness of the reported non-GAAP numbers. Given the updated SEC Compliance and Disclosure Interpretations issued in 2016, and the increasing volume of SEC comment letters that request firms to improve their disclosure of the tax effects of exclusions, future research can explore the time-series change in firms’reporting behavior in this area.

14522716.value: We define non-GAAP tax rate as the effective tax rate applied to non-GAAP earnings. When firms decide to exclude certain income and/or expense items from GAAP earnings, they have to adjust these exclusions net of tax to arrive at after-tax non-GAAP earnings. Thus, the non-GAAP tax rate has a direct effect on after-tax non-GAAP earnings, a metric focused on by managers and market participants. In the non-GAAP reporting setting where the complexity of tax expense estimation is high and rigorous verification from external auditors is low, we hypothesize that managers have opportunities and incentives to manipulate the tax rates applied to exclusions to meet or beat earnings benchmarks. We find evidence that is consistent with our hypothesis. Our evidence echoes the SEC's concern that current disclosure on non-GAAP disclosure might be insufficient.

14525116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14525116.value: This paper examines the effects of comprehensive double taxation agreements (CDTAs), also known as bilateral tax treaties (BTTs), signed between the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) and its trading partners. Regulators, accountants, and prior research suggest several potential benefits to CDTAs such as increased cross-border investment, reduced uncertainty for investors, and lower tax liabilities to companies. However, CDTAs are also associated with potential costs such as reduced tax revenues and increased financial reporting costs. This paper seeks to examine these benefits and costs, especially as they relate to the Hong Kong SAR. It is important to examine these questions because the Hong Kong government continues to negotiate CDTAs with its trading partners, but internationally, the effects of CDTAs are not well understood. This project seeks to provide a better understanding of the effects of CDTAs on firm performance, which in turn, has important implications for the Hong Kong economy more generally. 本課題將檢驗香港特別行政區和其貿易國所簽訂的全面性避免雙重課稅協定的作用。監管者，會計師和過去的研究表明全面性避免雙重課稅的協定可以增加跨境投資，消除股市不確定性，並且降低公司稅收負擔。同時，此協議也降低了公司稅收收入和增加了會計信息的披露成本。鑑於全面性避免雙重課稅協定對香港經濟的重要性，本課題將檢驗該協定帶來的成本和收益。本課題之所以重要是因為儘管香港政府繼續和貿易夥伴國協商雙重課稅協定，是國際上對協議的作用卻了解的不多。本課題將研究雙重課稅協定對公司績效的作用，這對香港經濟具有重要意義。

14525216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14525216.value: The ability to appropriate value is a significant strategic consideration for startup firms in the market for technologies when they form cooperative commercialization agreements with established incumbents that own complementary assets to develop and commercialize their innovations. This work builds on the ideas explicated in economics of incomplete contracts to investigate the impact of startup firms’ relative bargaining power on the ex-ante allocation of control rights for startup firm. We propose two distinct sources of bargaining power for the startup innovator associated with i) the prominence of startup firms’ founders and ii) experience of venture capitalists (VCs) backing the startup, and suggest that they have a positive effect on the control rights allocated to the startup firm. Specifically, we suggest that startup founders’ serial entrepreneurial credentials and investment experience of startups’ VC backing credibly enhance the bargaining position of startups and obtain them a greater share of the pie-splitting control rights in cooperative commercialization agreements. Further, we also suggest that the two sources of bargaining power for the startup will be more beneficial for startups when i) the startup’s technological innovations are of higher value and ii) the technological resources of the startup and established incumbent are related. 摘要：对于技术市场上的初创企业来说，当与一些拥有互补型资产从而得以实现创新商业化的老牌企业签订商业合作协议时，能够发挥一定的价值是基于战略层面的重要考虑。本研究立足于不完全契约经济学的有关观点，试图研究初创企业的相对谈判能力对于其事前控制权分配的重大影响。我们提出初创企业谈判能力的两个不同来源：i）创业者的突出能力 以及ii）风险投资人（风投）的融资经验。我们认为这两个因素对于初创企业的控制权分配均起到积极的作用，特别是创业者长期作为企业家的资历和风险投资人丰富的投资经验能够卓有成效的提升初创企业的谈判地位，并且使初创企业在商业合作协议中获得更多的利益。另外，我们还认为如果初创企业的技术革新具有很高的价值并且初创企业和老牌企业的技术资源是相关联的，那么影响初创企业谈判能力的两个因素将会发挥更大的作用。

14526216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14526216.value: Many governments seek partnerships from the private sector to offer some of the same services that are also delivered by government institutions. Such public-private partnerships have proliferated in the world as the governments expect that the market forces can help to slash waste and delivering much-needed public services without putting too much pressure on public financial resources. But how effective are these much-touted partnerships much depend on how well both public and private institutions understand the challenges in the management of the competition between public and private service systems due to conflict goals of two competing sectors: while public institutions are obligated to offer the largest social welfare, the private firms aim to maximize their own profits. Motivated by observations around the world and especially in Hong Kong (e.g., the competition between public and private underwater tunnels), we propose to study the competition between public and private service systems using a queue-based modeling framework. We will study two sets of problems. In the first set of problems, the public and private service systems compete through market mechanism (i.e., setting appropriate service prices) to attract potential customers. The second set of problems will incorporate various potential government policy mechanisms such as profit guarantee, tax or subsidy. One of the key features of this proposed study is that it casts a social planner’s decision in a game-theoretic setting taking into consideration of possible reactions of the private counterpart. Thus, the optimal decisions under competitive market equilibrium may be quite different from that of a monopolistic planner. We will investigate various market and policy mechanisms that have the potential to create win-win benefits for public-private partnerships. We expect that our proposed study will offer managerial insights on how a government can design appropriate mechanisms and policies to improve its services to the society. For private firms, we expect that our study will help them to gain insights on how to invest in their systems’ service capacity and quality for improved profitability. Our proposed research is also expected to make significant academic contributions as very few papers in the existing literature explicitly model the public vs private competition using queue models. 政府希望私營企業能夠和公共機構一道為社會大眾提供相關的 服務。這樣的公共-私營共存的現象在全球各地都很普遍。 其中很重要的一個原因是政府的財政預算有限，它希望借助 市場力量來提供高質量的且滿足公眾需求的服務。但是， 這樣的公共-私營系統是否能夠真正有效地為公眾提供服務呢？ 公共系統和私營企業有非常不同的目標：公共系統是從公眾 角度出發，希望最大化公眾利益；而私營企業則是希望最大 化自身利潤。不同的目標會引導出不同的決策。因此，如何 協調公共服務系統和私營企業之間的競爭是非常重要的， 也很具有挑戰性。 公共-私營現象在香港也是很普遍的。例如，香港的幾條海底 隧道就是分別由政府和私營企業管理。基於上述現象，我們 計劃建立一個排隊論模型來研究公共系統和私營企業之間的 競爭。我們將會研究兩大類問題。首先，在第一類問題中， 我們會研究公共系統和私營企業完全通過市場機制進行競爭： 即通過服務定價來競爭消費者。在第二類問題中，我們計劃 研究各種政府政策對市場競爭的影響，例如利潤保底政策， 稅收或補貼政策。此研究的一個特點是我們把社會決策者的 行為嵌入到博弈論模型中，同時考慮了私營企業自身的盈利 性行為。因此，公共-私營系統下的市場均衡可能會和社會決 策者的最優策略有很大不同。我們將研究在各種市場機制和 政府政策下公共系統和私營企業的決策。另外，我們希望能 夠得到一些政策，使得公共系統和私營企業同時受益。 我們期望我們的研究能夠為政府設計政策提高公眾服務水平 提供相關的管理啟示。對於私營企業，我們希望我們的研究 能夠為他們的決策行為提供建議，例如如何規劃運營能力和 服務質量來實現更大的利潤。之前，很少論文利用排隊論 模型來研究公共系統和私營企業的競爭。因此，此研究也將 會有很大的理論學術貢獻。

14526216.label: Major findings and research outcome
14526216.value: The two papers funded by this research projects have produced some interesting findings as follows: (1) In the first paper titled "On the Benefit of Privatization in a Mixed Duopoly Service System", we find that although the public service system's goal is welfare maximization, the whole system's (with one private and one public owned servers) welfare can be worse than that of the system with only profit-seeking private servicers. We further find that the system’s welfare can be maximized by partially privatizing the public server, that is, changing its goal to be a level between welfare and profit maximization. In some cases, such as when the service capacity of the public server is very small, full privatization of the public server generates the highest social welfare for the whole system. (2) In the second paper, we use a more stylized model to study the impact of public intervention under two commonly used pricing policies: fixed pricing and congestion pricing. We find that the availability of congestion pricing always intensifies the competition between the two servers (one public and one private) and improves the social welfare. The public intervention, however, may hurt the social welfare. The public intervention is able to better manage the traffic congestion level in the public server, but may enlarge the congestion imbalance between two servers, and thus hurt the overall social welfare when the two servers’ capacities are significantly differentiated. We also show that the competition between two private servers may lead to prison dilemma where both servers use congestion pricing to compete more aggressively in equilibrium, but their profits would be higher under fixed pricing strategy.

14526216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14526216.value: The two papers produced under the support of this research project have the potential for future research on how a social planner can reply on private investment to fulfill its obligation of providing benefits to the society.

14526216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14526216.value: The findings in the research produced through the support of this project provide a number of significant managerial insights for the public service providers (or social planners): First, it may not always better for the public institution to directly provide a service even if the intension of maximizing social welfare is well justified. In many situations, allowing private firms to offer the public services such as public transports etc., could produce the same or even higher overall social benefits; Second, there are economic benefits for the social planners to regulate on how to limit or incentivize private service providers in order to provide better social benefits. Direct intervention by providing a public server is one approach. Another approach is the pricing structure. For example, congestion pricing in many situations is beneficial for the society.

14600716.label: Project Objectives
14600716.value: To develop a matrix based on building envelope wall types of typical housing block types in Hong Kong in terms of sustainable design and construction performance parameters. To identify occupant interaction patterns with identified building envelope types through field data driven window opening behaviour models based on given site environmental conditions. To perform energy simulation studies to evaluate design parameters (i.e., thermal performance, daylighting potential and energy efficiency) and construction parameters (i.e., time, cost and project management methods) with occupant behaviour models described in Objective 2. To conduct design permutations to test passive design strategies on envelope wall types using energy simulation studies described in Objective 3 to assess energy performance and physical models to assess construction methods. To form a set of design guidelines for designers to use as a reference for site-responsive high performance building envelope design strategies utilising passive design, advanced project management and modelling techniques in high density housing.

14600716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600716.value: The research study proposes to investigate the performance of building envelope designs of Hong Kong public housing from the dual perspectives of design and construction, and then seek integrated methods for high performance building envelope design. The building industry is undergoing a global push to consider ways of making building design and process more efficient and this is evident by the increasing adoption of sustainable building design strategies, green building rating systems (HK Green Building Council, HKGBC), advanced project coordination and management. International building design standards, in the past two decades, have incorporated design criteria for building envelopes to control heat gain, airflow and daylighting potential. The building envelope separates interior and exterior, and affects building performance through design configurations to improve efficiency in environmental control, fabrication and construction: key factors of high performance building design. Hong Kong has issues of high public housing demand and undesirable compact living conditions with minimal daylighting and ventilation (Lau, 2011). The question arises as to why there is so little change in the design of housing building envelopes in respect of different orientations; smarter envelope designs need to be explored for climate site responsiveness while considering construction parameters of mass prefabrication, installation and cost. The proposed study will begin with the selection of 9 public housing buildings representing common envelope design typologies within comparative site conditions. Systematic research will be conducted with field observations and measurements, followed by building energy simulations modified to include field-data findings. This methodology of using adapted user behaviour models from field data, for more accurate investigations of building energy performance, leads to better understanding of building design, climate, occupant comfort and energy use (Rijal et al., 2012, Fabi et al., 2013). Envelope design permutation simulations driven by passive design and construction parameters, paired with physical model testing validations, will be performed using energy models developed in previous steps. A set of design guidelines will be developed based on the findings and design testing. The findings from the research will contribute to the understanding of holistic methods of approaching building envelope design given construction constraints for an integrated approach to high performance housing. In practice, the findings will lead designers towards better envelope designs and provide a valuable reference for passive design through the envelope design approach. Energy saving building envelope designs can benefit low-income residents who are economically sensitive to energy costs while maintaining thermal comfort. 本研究建議以設計和建設的雙重角度研究香港建設公屋圍護設計的性能，然後尋求高性能建築圍護結構設計的集成方法。 建築行業正在經歷一個全球性的推動去考慮建築設計更高效率的方式。可持續建築設計策略丶綠色建築評級系統（香港綠色建築委員會，HKGBC）丶先進的項目協調和管理都越來越多地這被採用 。在過去的二十年中，國際建築設計標準已納入設計標準為控制建築圍護結構的熱量吸收丶氣流和採光的潛力。建築圍護分隔內部和外部，通過設計影響建築性能，以改善環境控制丶製造和施工的效率：高性能建築設計的關鍵因素。香港有很高的公共房屋需求問題，並最小的採光和通風（劉，2011）過度緊湊的不良居住環境問題。 為什麼房屋建築圍護的設計沒有就不同方向變化改善？我們需要因應氣候丶考慮大量預製的施工參數丶安裝和成本去探索更智能的圍護設計 。 研究建議由九個有常見的建築圍護設計和相似環境條件的公營房屋樓宇開始。系統性研究將以實地觀察和測量進行，接著是包括現場數據的建築能耗模擬。利用現場數據得出的使用者反應模型能更準確的調查研究建築能源性能，也有助於更好地理解建築設計丶氣候丶居住舒適度和能源使用（的里賈爾等，2012年，法幣等。2013年）。建築圍護設計排列的模擬是由被動設計和施工參數驅動，以及以物理模型試驗來驗證。這將會使用前面的步驟發展得出能源模型進行。最後根據調查結果和測試設計開發一套設計指南。 研究結果將有助於在高性能住宅的施工約束上理解圍護設計給的綜合方法。在實踐中，結果能引導設計師設計更好的建築圍護，並通過圍護設計提供給被動設計一個具參考價值設計方案。總之，節能建築的圍護設計可以有利於對能源成本敏感的低收入居民是，同時保持熱舒適性。

14601116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601116.value: This project aims to study the motivational processes in which a relationship partner's instrumentality to an active goal leads to its objectification (i.e., being represented as a "tool" rather than a helpful human being). In particular, the project examines how broad motivations for promotion and prevention may drive this process. Objectification has been consistently found to be detrimental to the objectified person’s well-being and societal welfare. Previous research on objectification has mainly focused on sex-related goals. However, objectification can occur in the pursuit of other types of goals. Given the rise of research on interpersonal self-regulation, the project examines how (and when) goal instrumentality of a relationship can promote objectification. This project proposes one motivational mechanism: motivational concerns for promotion and prevention. It is hypothesized that concerns for growth (promotion) elevates the importance of personal independence and autonomy, and therefore promotes objection of instrumental helpers. On the contrary, concerns for security (prevention) elevates the importance of interdependence and social connection, and therefore reduces objectification. Six experiments are proposed to closely examine the influence of regulatory focus on different manifestations of objectification across three different stages (i.e., activation, execution, and completion) of goal pursuit. It is expected that promotion versus prevention focus (a) deemphasizes goal-irrelevant implications of warmth or kindness (e.g., potential to be friends) in the stage of goal activation (Studies 1a and 1b), (b) ignores the helper's cost of helping in the stage of goal execution (Studies 2a and 2b), and (c) downplays the importance of the helper's displayed prosocial intention in the stage of goal completion (Studies 3a and 3b). In sum, the proposal examines how broad motivations for promotion and prevention may influence objectification through its emphasis of relational considerations By testing this motivational account, the project identifies potential ways to help goal pursuers avoid objectifying their helpers and develop mutually fulfilling (work or close) relationships. By reducing objectification, the project also provides ways to promote a more harmonious society. 人們對可以利用其達成目標的人物加以物化，將其視為“工具”而不是一個能夠帶來幫助的人。本研究致力於探究這一現象背後的動機過程。本研究著重探究促進焦點(promotion focus)和預防焦點(prevention focus)的動機可以如何驅動這一過程。物化一再被證明對被物化者的安康和福利造成損害。以往關於物化的研究主要針對與性有關的目標。然而，物化也可以發生在追求其他類型的目標的過程中。 本研究將檢視人際關係對於目標追求的工具性如何（及何時）能夠促使物化的發生。本研究提出的動機機制是：以促進和預防為焦點的動機。本研究假設促進焦點會提升個人獨立自主的重要性，從而推動對於可利用的幫助者的物化。相反，預防焦點會提升互相依賴和社會關聯的重要性，從而削弱物化的傾向。本研究擬進行六項實驗來探究不同焦點在目標追求的三個階段（起始、執行和完成）中，調節焦點對物化的不同表現的物化所造成的影響。我們預期，促進焦點相對於預防焦點來說（一）在目標起始階段，弱化與目標無關的親切、友好態度的意義（例如與幫助者成為朋友的潛在可能）（實驗1a和1b），（二）在目標執行階段，忽視幫助者因提供幫助所付出的代價（實驗2a和2b），以及（三）在目標完成階段，低估幫助者所表現出的利他意圖（實驗3a和3b）。 總之，本研究將剖析促進焦點和預防焦點如何通過關注人際關係中的不同面向，從而影響物化。通過驗證基於這一動機機制的解釋，本研究會提出一些潛在的方法來幫助目標追求者避免 物化他們的幫助者，從而建立讓彼此都感到滿足的（工作或親密）關係。本研究所提出的減少物化的途徑亦有利於促進和諧社會的建立。

14601116.label: Realisation of objectives
14601116.value: We have run the six studies as planned and fully achieved all the following three project objectives. Below are the particulars: -------------------------------------------------------------- Objective 1: To examine, in a general sense, the motivational processes in which a relationship partner's instrumentality to an active goal leads to its objectification (i.e., being represented as a "tool" rather than a helpful human being) Answer: Based on the results, it is clear that promotion and prevention concerns are related to objectification. In the proposal, I predicted that promotion concerns should be more strongly related to objectification. However, the results showed that prevention concerns are actually more strongly linked to objectification (e.g., devaluation of the helper’s kindness). Although the literature suggested that prevention-focused individuals are more concerned for other’s well-being, such concerns may not apply to their interactions with strangers (as in our studies). To execute this proposal, I have also created a new manipulation of regulatory focus that is more effective in our Chinese student sample (Hui, Lui, Lai, Wong, & Wong, in press). I pilot-tested the manipulation and explored whether regulatory focus relates to objectification in romantic relationships. However, the results were inconclusive. -------------------------------------------------------------- Objective 2: To examine how promotion versus prevention concerns can increase objectification, by reducing responsiveness to the task helper's mental states or experiences, including interpersonal warmth (Studies 1a and 1b), psychological costs of helping (Studies 2a and 2b), and prosocial intentions to help (Studies 3a and 3b) Answer: I found that prevention concerns increase objectification, by reducing responsiveness to the task helper’s kindness and prosocial intentions. Apparently, prevention-focused individuals are less sensitive to the helper’s warmth when warmth is not instrumental to their goal outcomes. I have submitted a manuscript that summarizes these findings (Hui, under review). I also conducted follow-up studies testing whether prevention-focused individuals are less inclined to seek help from warm close friends, when the close friends are less instrumental than cold distant friends (Hui, Fung, Hui, & Ng, in press, Study 3a). However, I did not observe any regulatory focus effects, likely because participants in our studies were more concerned with whether the potential helpers were available rather than instrumental. My studies also showed that regulatory focus does not affect people’s attentiveness to the partner’s psychological costs of helping. Specifically, regulatory focus did not interact with the cost manipulation in predicting participants’ request of help from the helper. However, I found that social value orientation (SVO), initially measured as a control variable in the planned studies, interacted with cost manipulation in predicting participants’ help request. Specifically, prosocials were more likely to ask for less help from the helper if the task was more demanding. However, proselfs asked for similar amounts of help from the helper whether the task was demanding or not. I planned to submit the findings of these studies with an emphasis on this SVO x cost interaction (Hui, in preparation). -------------------------------------------------------------- Objective 3: To examine the influence of regulatory focus on objectification of a task helper across three different stages (i.e., activation, execution, and completion) of goal pursuit (in six studies) Answer: The results showed that regulatory focus only influences objectification of a task helper when the goal is activated and completed. Regulatory focus was not related to objectification when a goal is being executed. -------------------------------------------------------------- To summarize, I have addressed all the objectives with the planned studies. Based on the findings, prevention versus promotion concerns inspire stronger objectification, especially in the stages of goal activation and completion.

14601116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601116.value: When pursuing a personal goal, people often evaluate a social target based on his or her instrumentality to the goal or the extent to which the attributes of the target can facilitate goal attainment. This project showed that this tendency is stronger when individuals are concerned with safety and prevention (rather than growth and promotion). Indeed, prevention-focused people were more likely to show (a) indifference to warm and cold targets when warmth was not useful to their upcoming task and (b) similar levels of appreciations after working with a prosocial or proself partner. These results were summarized in a manuscript (Hui, 2020a). As an extension of these findings, I also examined whether heightened instrumentality concerns may motivate prevention-focused individuals to seek help from distant friends when the distant friends are colder and yet more helpful than the close friends. However, regulatory focus did not predict preferences for distant friends in such situations. Apparently, the instrumentality concerns were over-driven by other concerns (Hui, Fung, Hui, & Ng, 2020). Moreover, while individuals obtain help from another person, they often gain benefits by incurring certain costs on the helper. My studies showed that prevention- and promotion-focused individuals asked for similar levels of help. These results suggested that prevention concerns inspire more instrumentality-based evaluation, but not more exploitation behaviors. These studies also found an interesting effect of prosociality, which was included as a control variable. The results showed that prosocials sought less help from a helper when it costed the helper more. However, proselfs sought similar amounts of help, disregarding the costs on the helper. Based on these findings from the funded studies, the implications of prosocial concerns in support seeking will be discussed in another manuscript (Hui, 2020b).

14601116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601116.value: Two research directions will be pursued: 1. Sense of insecurity (e.g., from job insecurity and self-esteem threat) often leads to inconsiderate treatment of other individuals (e.g., abusive leadership and aggression). Given that sense of insecurity often trigger prevention motivations and that prevention motivations inspire objectification, I will further explore whether prevention motivations mediate the effects of different forms of insecurity on misbehaviors toward other individuals. 2. In these studies, I found that individuals high in prosocial concerns consider other people's psychological cost when deciding how much help they want from the other. However, individuals high in self-interested concerns do not have such tendencies. I am working with a clinical psychologist in the department to further examine how individual differences in empathy and psychopathological tendencies may shape the disregard of other's psychological costs in help seeking and other interpersonal behaviors.

14601116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601116.value: Sometimes, individuals may objectify another human being, mentally representing a helpful helper as a mindless tool rather than a mindful person. This project showed that this tendency is stronger when individuals are concerned with safety and prevention (rather than growth and promotion). Across studies, I found that participants, when concerned with safety, were more likely to ignore the helper’s kindness and prosocial intention. I also found that, when seeking help from the helper, prevention-focused participants did not ask for more help from helper than promotion-focused participants. It appears that, while prevention-focused individuals were more likely to evaluate a helper based on its instrumentality, they did not exploit the helper more to gain more benefits.

14602516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602516.value: The aim of this project is to examine the effects of physical education continuing professional development (PE-CPD) on teachers’ physical literacy and self-efficacy and students' learning outcomes. The levels of physical activity (PA) among young people in Hong Kong and in other developed nations are below the levels that are sufficient to promote health. The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) (2015) asserts that a quality physical education (QPE) is a core part of school curricula and QPE is a foundation of a lifelong engagement in PA and sport for young people. Therefore, to strengthen learning and teaching effectiveness, PE-CPD should be a key priority of any national QPE strategy. In connection with the above assertion, the research team has found that very little is known about the impact of physical literacy and self-efficacy of PE teachers on students’ learning outcomes in association with PE teachers’ experience of PE-CPD in the Hong Kong context. In this proposed project, a randomized controlled trial (RCT) method will be used to explore how PE-CPD influences teachers’ knowledge of physical literacy and self-efficacy and the extent to which student have achieved stated learning outcomes. Teacher participants will be randomly allocated into two groups (interventions and controls). A 50-hour PE-CPD program will be developed based on the Teacher Competencies Framework (COTAP, 2013) in an eight-month period followed by another eight-month period involving students’ intervention. Student participants will attend PE lessons taught by the teacher participants. A physical literacy inventory and teacher’s self-efficacy scale will be used to examine the changes of physical literacy and self-efficacy of PE teachers. PA levels, knowledge of physical literacy, motivation and PA enjoyment will be measured to examine students’ learning outcomes. Data will be collected at baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up. The study will be significant because physical literacy has great impact on an individual’s sense of self and self-confidence, communication with others, knowledge and understanding of PA, and motivation and accomplishments. PE teachers will better appreciate the importance of PE-CPD as a vehicle for improving their professional competence, and this will also benefit their students. This proposed study will provide a model by which the Hong Kong Education Bureau and the teacher education institutions can assist in supporting the implementation of PE-CPD. Teachers’ physical literacy and self-efficacy can be regarded as major determinants of effective teaching which in turn influences the students’ learning and achievements. 摘要 本研究專案之目的為探查體育持續專業進修對教師的體育素養與自我效能及學生學習成效之影響。香港與其他地區青少年的體力活動不足使其未能達致健康要求，聯合國教科文組織(UNESCO,2015)宣稱優質體育(QPE)是學校課程的核心及青少年終身參與體育運動的基石。因此，體育教師持續專業進修對鞏固優質體育(QPE)的學與教，乃為任何國家優先考慮的策略。 根據以上的主張，本研究團隊發現鮮有知識關於香港體育教師的體育持續專業進修對其體育素養和自我效能與學生學習成效的關係。 本研究專案將使用隨機對照試驗(RCT)探討體育持續專業進修如何影響教師的體育素養認知和自我效能，從而瞭解學生不同方面的學習成效。參與的教師將被隨機分配到實驗組或控制組，實驗組教師將被邀請參與為期8個月共50小時依照教師專業能力理念架構(COTAP, 2013)設計的體育持續專業進修課程，緊接著為期8個月實驗組教師的體育課介入以探查學生的學習成效。體育素養認知問卷及教師自我效能問卷用做檢測兩組教師的體育素養及教師自我效能的變化；體力活動水平、體育素養認知及體育愉快度用作評估學生的學習成效。數據收集將分為前期、後期和追蹤期三個階段。 本研究專案具重大意義是因為個人具備的體育素養認知，皆對其自身感和自信、與人溝通、體力活動的知識與領會、以及其動機和成就影響甚鉅。而且，體育教師會更意識到體育持續專業進修對其專業能力的重要性，而最終得益的是他們的學生。展望是次研究專案能提供範本予香港教育局及師資培訓機構以作貫徹執行體育持續專業進修，而教師的體育素養和自我效能可成為主要決定因素，影響學生的學習及成就。

14602516.label: Realisation of objectives
14602516.value: 1. To develop and evaluate a PE-CPD programme for school PE teachers The intervention program has been delivered to the participating teachers in the intervention group. The eight-month PE-CPD programme was held in the university and conducted by PE teacher educators and experienced PE teachers. This framework includes four domains related to the dimensions of physical literacy. The PE-CPD program was appropriate and practical because it commenced after teachers’ busy work during the first term and finished before summer break. Teacher participants have time to reflect on the PD intervention and learned materials over the summer break such that they can plan for implementation of the physical literacy programme for the following eight-month curriculum intervention period. Prior to the PE-CPD programme as an intervention of teacher participants, a small scale ‘Customised Continuing Professional Development Programme’ was developed to gain an in-depth understanding of PETs’ CPD experiences. Teacher participants (N=9) were asked to talk about their ideal topics for PE-CPD, to comment on programme effectiveness and their perspectives of an effective PE-CPD. 2. To examine the effectiveness of PE-CPD in terms of changes in teachers’ physical literacy and self-efficacy The baseline, post intervention and follow up surveys have been conducted, and analysis revealed the effect of the intervention program had on the PE teachers. As stated in the annual report, the research team did try various ways to collect the questionnaires from teacher participants. However, the deduction of the sample size from 62 to 46 teacher participants (phase one to phase two) due to many teacher participants were on contract base. After eight-month intervention which is the period between phase one and two, many of the teacher participants (EG & CG) changed to other schools. Therefore, teacher participants who participated in all three phases was forty-two [20(EG); 22(CG)] had completed the survey. From baseline findings, PET participants’ perceived physical literacy did show consistently high scores in the 3 domains of physical literacy across the whole sample. Results also indicated that there is a moderately weak negative correlation between teaching experience and two of the examined domains of physical literacy, namely ‘Knowledge and understanding’ and ‘Sense of self and self-confidence’. Regarding the relationship between perceived physical literacy and teaching efficacy of PET participants, results revealed that physical literacy has moderate positive correlations with all 7 factors of teaching efficacy in PET participants. To achieve this objective and overcome the problems, qualitative approach to examine the changes in teachers’ physical literacy and self-efficacy has been adopted. Findings revealed that PET participants had undergone a certain degree of immediate and intermediate changes in relation to their teaching efficacy and physical literacy after completing the PE-CPD programme. This qualitative study has been submitted and is under review in a targeted journal – UNSECO Prospects Journal (Refer to Part C: Research Output) 3. To examine the effectiveness of PE-CPD in terms of changes in students’ learning outcomes such as PA levels, physical literacy, motivation and PA enjoyment The baseline, post intervention and follow up surveys have been conducted. The research team used data from the students’ participants of the first stage to examine the association of perceived physical literacy, situational intrinsic motivation and physical activity enjoyment during PE classes. Data analysis revealed that situational intrinsic motivation increased as increase in age. Primary students scored higher than secondary students, whereas boys scored higher than girls especially secondary girls. Regarding PE class enjoyment, secondary students scored higher than primary students. Boys enjoyed PE classes more than girls. In particular, secondary girls scored the lowest in comparing with their counterparts. Secondary girls also had a lowest score on their perception of physical literacy. The result also revealed that perceived physical literacy is the best predictor for PE class enjoyment With regard to the changes in students’ learning outcomes, data analysis revealed that the correlation coefficient between teachers’ perceived physical literacy and teaching efficacy was quite high and significant correlated in teachers’ group. In student group, the correlation coefficient among students’ learning outcome (students’ perceived physical literacy, situational intrinsic motivation and physical activity enjoyment) were also high and significant correlated. However, there were no significant association between teacher behaviors and all their fellow students’ learning outcomes. All of the correlation coefficients are very low. Results of the above have been presented in various regional and international conferences (refer to Part C: Research Output) 4. To examine the influence of changes in teachers’ knowledge of physical literacy and self-efficacy on students’ motives in undertaking PA. All three stages of teachers’ and students’ data collection have been finished. To overcome the deduction of the sample size of PET participants, the research team further divided the PET participants of the experimental group into two groups in terms of their teacher’s attendance of continuing professional development programmes [high attendance teacher (HAR) (above 50% attendance rate) and low attendance teacher (LAR) (below 50% attendance rate)] which is to evaluate the change of interventions on the students’ perceived physical literacy, situational intrinsic motivation and enjoyment. Data analysis indicated that student participants of intervention group (HAR & LAR) reported significantly higher the control group (CG). HAR group scored the highest in three constructs (perceived physical literacy, situation intrinsic motivation and enjoyment) at three different time points which reflects that continuing professional development of PE teachers play crucial role on students learning outcomes. The findings of the above is under preparation and will be ready to submit to targeted journal – European Physical Education Review). Throughout the research process, objective 1 and 2 is accomplished with relatively less than expected sample from teacher participants’ data collected. However, qualitative data can be an alternative way to reflect on changes of PET’s teaching efficacy and physical literacy. The research team found that the data collection process was smoothly implemented in the beginning of the project. However, after the baseline and post intervention data collection, some teacher participants have changed their serving schools or PE classes. As such, the number of teacher participants and student participants had dropped both at the post-intervention and follow-up phases.

14602516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14602516.value: We found that the correlation coefficient between teachers’ perceived physical literacy (T-PPL) and teaching efficacy (TE) was quite high (r = 0.60) and significant correlated in teachers’ group. The results also showed that students’ perceived physical literacy, physical activity enjoyment and situational intrinsic motivation were significantly correlated. Regressions further revealed that students perceived physical literacy was the best predictor for physical activity enjoyment (b=.527). While physical activity enjoyment was used to predict perceived literacy, physical activity enjoyment was the best predictor for perceived physical literacy (b=.531). In addition, knowledge and understanding (subscale of perceived physical literacy) (b=.41), intrinsic motivation (b=.41) and amotivation (b=-.169) (subscales of situational intrinsic motivation) were significant for predicting physical activity enjoyment in PE classes. All three stages of teachers’ and students’ data collection have been finished. The research team further divided the teacher participants of the experimental group into two groups in terms of their attendance of continuing professional development programmes [high attendance teacher (HAR) (above 50% attendance rate) and low attendance teacher (LAR) (below 50% attendance rate)] which is to evaluate the change of interventions on the students’ perceived physical literacy, situational intrinsic motivation and enjoyment. Data analysis indicated that student participants of intervention group (HAR & LAR) reported significantly higher the control group (CG). HAR group scored the highest in three constructs (perceived physical literacy, situation intrinsic motivation and enjoyment) at three different time points which reflects that continuing professional development of PE teachers play crucial role on students learning outcomes.

14602516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14602516.value: This study was the first attempt to examine the effects of continuing professional development (CPD) on teachers’ physical literacy and self-efficacy and students' physical literacy and physical activity (PA) participation. Findings suggest that the proposed 8-month intervention was effective in increasing students’ learning outcomes. Future efforts should investigate feasibility of implementing CPD intervention in other settings, e.g. professional learning communities or community of practice, to maximize the coverage. Findings of the present study provided framework of interventions in promoting quality physical education (QPE) in Hong Kong primary and secondary schools. Promoting QPE with elements of physical literacy may be an effective means of ensuring students’ motivation, enjoyment and physical literacy development. Findings also provide a new perspective for teaching education institutions and professional development programmes by emphasizing the concept of physical literacy.

14602516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14602516.value: The purpose of this project is to examine the effects of continuing professional development (CPD) on teachers’ physical literacy and self-efficacy and students' learning outcomes. A 50-hours CPD was completed by teachers and they completed physical literacy and self-efficacy questionnaires prior to, and at the end of the CPD. Teacher participants had undergone a certain degree of changes in their teaching efficacy and physical literacy. CPD intervention teachers then delivered an 8-month curriculum focused on developing student physical literacy. Control group teachers received no intervention treatment. Prior to, and following the intervention students completed questionnaires on their physical literacy, motivation and enjoyment. After three stages of data collection, the research team further divided teacher participants of the experimental group into two groups in terms of their attendance of CPD [high attendance teacher (HAR) and low attendance teacher (LAR)] which is to evaluate the change on the students’ learning outcomes. Data analysis indicated that students of intervention group (HAR & LAR) reported significantly higher the control group (CG). HAR group scored the highest in three constructs at three different time points which reflects that continuing professional development of PE teachers play crucial role on students learning outcomes.

14603416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603416.value: The causal impact of maternal education on women’s reproductive behavior and their offspring’s health outcomes is well documented. However, little is known about the causal effects of parental schooling on very early life outcomes for children, such as birth weight. Economists and demographers have also long been interested in the impact of education on women’s reproductive decisions because these outcomes are correlated with child’s wellbeing, and more importantly, reproduction and childbirth outcomes are important mechanisms for intergenerational human capital transmission. It is difficult to isolate the effect of maternal education from other unobserved characteristics that affect these outcomes. In this proposed project, we will take advantage of two waves of compulsory education reforms in 1971 and 1978 in Hong Kong to study the causal effects of women’s education on a range of outcomes related to women’s reproductive health and children’s wellbeing. Using richly detailed administrative data on births and marriages in Hong Kong, we employ a regression discontinuity design and compare women who were born just months before and after the educational policy eligibility cutoff, analyzing their age at first marriage, age at first childbirth, total fertility, probability of assortative mating, offspring birth weight, and birth spacing. We will also explore the heterogeneous effects of maternal education across gender and socioeconomic background. Robustness checks will be conducted following standard regression discontinuity practices. Our study builds on existing literature and makes several novel contributions. We study the causal impact of women’s schooling on birth spacing, a subject that has not been widely discussed in the previous literature. Whilst existing studies offer mixed evidence about the effect of maternal education on child’s birth weight, our study will provide new evidence from Hong Kong. More importantly, by comparing the impact of two different compulsory education reforms with results from other regions, we will analyze the potential cultural, historical and political context that might drive differences in potential impact. These research questions will help scholars, policy makers, and stakeholders evaluate the utility of compulsory education and better understand its effects on children and families. Lastly, we show that Hong Kong’s dynamic and growing society has benefitted from the past policies. Education expansion policies have been found to increase individuals’ educational attainment as well as subsequent labor market earnings, especially among women. Our findings will show how the increased human capital of mothers might be transmitted to the next generation in Hong Kong. 母親受教育程度對女性的生育行為及其子女的健康結果的因果關 係是有據可查的。然而，極少研究父母教育程度對兒童早期生命 狀況（如出生體重）兩者之間的因果關係。經濟學者及人口統計 學者向來關注教育如何影響女性的生育決策，因為這些結果與孩 子的健康密切相關。更重要的是，繁殖和分娩的結果均是 人類資 本代際流動的重要機制。然而, 把母親教育從其他同樣會影響 這些結果的隱性特質區別開來相當困難。 在本研究項目中，我們採用香港1971年及1978年兩次強制義務教 育改革，來探究女性教育與一系列婦女生殖健康和兒童健康結果 的因果關係。 透過採用大量詳實的生育及婚姻數據，我們採用了斷點迴歸設 計，並比較在受到強制義務教育政策影響前後出生的女性， 分析她們的初婚年齡、首次分娩年齡、總和生育率、配偶選擇、 子女出生體重及生育間隔的概率。我們亦會探究母親教育在子女 不同性別及不同社經背景家庭的異質影響。我們亦會依據斷點迴 歸的標準進行穩健性檢驗。 本研究奠基於現有文獻，並提出嶄新的貢獻: 本研究探討一個在以往文獻中未得到廣泛討論的課題, 即女性教育和生育間隔的因果關係。雖然現有的研究提供了關於母親的教育對幼童出生體重的效果眾說紛紜，莫衷一是, ,本研究將利用香港的數據提供新的實證結果。更重要的是，通過比較與其他地區不同的兩次義務教育改革的影響，我們將探討，其潛在的文化、歷史及政治背景如何可能導致政策影響差異。這些研究問題將有助學者、政策制訂者及其他相關持份者去評估強制義務教育的效用，更好地了解其對兒童和家庭的影響。 最後，本研究也展現了香港的動態的持續增長的社會已從過往政策中獲益。教育擴展政策已被證實可提升個人 ，尤其是女性的教育造詣以及隨後的勞動力市場的收益。本研究計劃的發現將會顯示香港母親的人力資本增長將如何能被傳遞於下一代。

14603616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14603616.value: 廣東流行曲與文化現代化在戰後香港

14603616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603616.value: Using Cantonese siukuk as a case study, particularly those produced by Wong Yuet Sang in 1950s-1960s, this project examines how stylistic changes in music integrated Cantonese opera and popular culture in Hong Kong, and produced new aesthetic framework that characterised cultural modernity in post-war, colonial Hong Kong. Siukuk (廣東小曲, “Cantonese small tune”) are memorable tunes with relatively fixed melodies, which can be performed as instrumental music, or to which text are inserted and performed as songs. Historically linked to kunqu (Kun opera), sizhu (silk and bamboo instrumental ensemble), and used in Cantonese opera since the early 20th century, siukuk developed in its style and repertory with new compositions at least since the early 20th century to become an important music genre in Hong Kong. Compilations of siukuk appeared earlier, when it was also referred to as siudiu 小調 or daidiu 大調. Some well-known collections include Xiange Bidu (絃歌必讀, 1916) and Qinxue Xinbian (琴學新編, 1921) by Qiu He Chou 丘鶴儔 (1880-1942) and Xiange Zhongxi Hepu (絃歌中西合譜, 1928) by Shen Yun Sheng 沈允升. Since the 1950s, the musical development of siukuk under the intersection of local Cantonese cultural traditions, Western popular cultures, and Chinese cosmopolitan influences can be heard in numerous pieces by siukuk composers, including around 150 works by Wong Yuet Sang 王粵生 (1919-1989). Performance opportunities for Cantonese opera declined in post-war Hong Kong (Chung 2004). However, collaborations between Cantonese opera troupes and film companies in Hong Kong, such as Sun Luen Film Co., Union Film Enterprise, Kong Ngee Film Co., and Wa Kiu Film Co sustained the production of “new” Cantonese opera and drew forth Wong’s siukuk, which were based on a wide range of sources, including traditional operatic tunes, folksongs, instrumental pieces from local origins or other provinces, and Western popular songs, and were also newly composed. While the composition and adaptation in the music of siukuk were not widely recognized in the Cantonese opera circle and were much debated in 1950’s Hong Kong, Wong’s works created a catalyst for siukuk to be socially relevant and to prevail during a time of political repression of Chinese dialects, and by extension, traditional art forms (ibid.). In terms of cultural influence, Wong’s siukuk works not only reflect the influx of non-conventional melodies and instruments into the Cantonese opera tradition and their popularity in modern entertainment culture, but also effected new practices of music composition in Cantonese opera. 本計劃以王粵生在1950、1960年代所生產的廣東小曲作為案例研究，探討音樂風格的改變如何融合香港的粵劇與流行文化，進而影響香港戰後殖民時期文化現代性新美學架構的誕生。 廣東小曲是一種相對來說旋律較固定、可以記憶的歌謠。它可以作為器樂來演奏，也可以看情況加入文句以歌曲的形態演出。小曲從歷史角度來說，跟崑劇、絲竹音樂都有連結，並從二十世紀早期開始用於粵劇。這個時期由於在風格和曲目兩方面的發展，它一躍成為香港重要的樂種。小曲的集成更早已經出現，當時被稱作小調或大調。著名像是丘鶴儔（1880-1942）的《絃歌必讀》（1916）、《琴學新編》（1921），沈允升的《絃歌中西合譜》（1928）。1950以來，小曲音樂在廣東文化、西方流行文化和中國都會化交錯影響下的發展在許多小曲作曲者的作品中可以聽到，包括王粵生（1919-1989）大約150首的作品。 戰後中國戲曲的表演熱潮減退，但粵劇團和電影公司在香港的合作，像是新聯影業公司、中聯電影企業有限公司、光藝製片公司、華僑電影製片公司等，延續了新粵劇的生產並帶出了王粵生揉合傳統廣東音樂、民歌、各省器樂和同樣也是新創西方流行歌等多種元素的小曲。 1950年代的香港，粵劇圈尚未普遍承認小曲音樂的創作與改編，並且對此多有爭議。王粵生的作品保護了小曲在中國方言乃至傳統藝術形式受政治壓迫的當時，維持其社會聯繫和傳布機會。就文化影響而言，王粵生的小曲不但反映了非傳統旋律和樂器進入廣東戲曲傳統，以及它們在現代娛樂文化中受歡迎的情形，還進一步推助了粵劇中音樂創作的新實踐。

14603816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14603816.value: 漢娜.鄂蘭的政治理論和香港2014雨傘運動
