14603816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603816.value: Hong Kong’s 2014 Umbrella Movement began as a political movement to demand the “high degree of autonomy” promised to Hong Kong before the 1997 handover. But the movement, despite the tremendous amount of energies collected and released, made no impacts to, or even reinforced, the political impasse. It also seemed to have failed to realize the “genuine universal suffrage” it demanded. A major slogan of the movement, particularly in the latter period, is “not to forget our original intention” 無忘初衷. This slogan indirectly attested to the many directions the movement ended up going, and it seemed to have lost in its own realization. Shall we understand the value and the meanings of the movement based on the degree of success of achieving the original objectives? This research tries to reconstruct the predicaments and possibilities of the movement along Arendt’s political theories, and divert our attentions from the political agenda and effects of the movement to the event itself, as a staging of “appearances” and an experiment of “cohabitation.” It will also contextualize the movement within its own historical unfolding, and demonstrate how the event was both caught in its historicity and struggled to open up its own horizon. Arendt’s political theories are theoretical resources to conduct this research, while this study will also help us to re-read her theories. We will explore some of her blind spots, such as her ignorance to social conditions beyond the “west,” and we will also confront some of her most controversial ideas, such as her insistence on the public over the private. In the 2014 Hong Kong event, occupants and supporters struggled to articulate a common politics with their own personal emotions and private concerns, which do not necessarily fit in Arendt’s relatively idealistic picture of political participation formulated largely according to the Greek polis. The new social media platforms and the global environment also give the “public” new substances and new meanings, complicating Arendt’s idea of the political community and the common. But Arendt’s stubborn insistence on the public also sheds light on some of the problems this Hong Kong movement faced. This project asks whether her ideas can offer us new insights to understand the continual development of Hong Kong’s civil society and to reconstruct a more productive relationship with the PRC. 香港2014年的雨傘運動本是一場政治運動，訴求維持九七回歸前獲承諾的「高度自治」。然而，這場運動縱使聚眾甚多，迴嚮甚巨，卻沒有改變香港的政治困局，甚至更形嚴峻。運動訴求的「真普選」亦未見成真。運動發展至後期常常聽見人們高喊「無忘初衷」，這句口號於運動結束後的各種後續發展迂迴地得到體證，但口號本身所指的初衷，卻無法實現。究竟我們應否以訴求之得失成敗，論斷這場運動的價值和意義？本研究將援引漢娜·鄂蘭的政治理論，嘗試重構這場運動的困境和可能性，把思考的側重點從運動的策略和得失拉開，放置於運動這一事件本身——既是「顯現 （appearance）」的舞台，也是「共同生活（cohabitation）」的一次實驗。本研究將把雨傘運動置於其歷史語境，闡釋運動作為事件如何為其獨特的歷史處境所局限，又如何撐開其獨有的一片天地。 本研究援引鄂蘭的政治理論作理論資源的同時，也將以雨傘運動為資源，再讀鄂蘭的政治理論。例如，鄂蘭對「西方」以外的社會處境缺乏認識，我們就着她某些理論的盲點作探討。又，鄂蘭堅持把「公」置於「私」之上，此論點一直甚具爭議，我們將切進此爭議以展開相關的思考。香港2014年的佔領期間，佔領者和支持佔領的人們投注大量的情感和個人想法，努力勾述一種共同參與的政治。他們的嘗試並不一定跟鄂蘭那根據希臘城邦所構想、相對地理想化的政治參與圖像相符。新式社交媒體平台和全球化的社會環境，亦為「公共」賦予新的內容和意義，令鄂蘭的政治共同體和公共的概念更形複雜。而同時間，鄂蘭對公共的執持，亦為香港這場運動所面對的部份難題，帶來另類出路。這項研究所要探問的是，究竟鄂蘭的理論能否帶來新視野，幫助我們理解香港公民社會的持續發展？以及能否幫助我們重新建立一種更具建設性的中港關係？

14603816.label: Realisation of objectives
14603816.value: The research was scheduled to be finished in December of 2018. But it has to be ended now because the PI has submitted a new proposal (14608718) in the current exercise requesting relief teaching. The PI has been instructed by the RGC that this research must be ended by mid April in order to qualify her application for relief teaching in the upcoming grant application. Although she has to cut the research short, and there are still have a few tasks scheduled to be done in the next few months, the PI feels comfortable ending the project now. Most of the research objectives have been completed to a satisfying degree. Close to thirty Umbrella Movement participants have been interviewed. They are chosen among a much larger potential pool, to represent the diverse backgrounds, in terms of education, age, religious belief, political positions, etc. of the movement participants. Some of them were interviewed for more than one time. There are now more than 80 hours of interviews collected, mostly transcribed, and together they show how the movement is both political and social. These participants might have come for their different political demands, but during the occupy they also developed new social networks and human relationships, and they also came to new understanding of the city and the meanings of democracy. Originally the PI has planned to do some additional interviews, particularly follow-up interviews to understand how some of the interviewed subjects have, or not, gained new insights and transformed views several years after the movement. But these information is not essential to the final analysis of the current form of the research, and the PI would still like to continue keep in touch with the subjects on her own. In terms of theoretical framework, the PI has also read most of Arendt's writing as well as a lot of secondary commentaries on her works, and she is able to wield Arendt's central idea of appearance to gain new insights about the participatory politics engendered in this movement. But the PI also discovers that Arendt's framework is not able to help us to completely understand this movement, and Arendt's discussions of the private and public are particularly troublesome when placed in the Umbrella Movement. During the research the PI also tries to obtain help from other contemporary political theorists; through this wide reading process she is able to fathom and reflect on the uniqueness of the Umbrella Movement. As a result, the PI has altered her original theoretical framework a little bit and no longer focused only on the political theories of Hannah Arendt, so she does not need to completely exhaust all the secondary literature about her writing. Instead, she has decided to include the ideas of a few other major political theorists, including Wendy Brown, Bonnie Honig, Etienne Balibar, and William Connolly, to build an interpretive framework for the Umbrella Movement. Overall the PI has done much of what she needs to do, and a book manuscript has already been drafted and is now under consideration by a major university press. She is also writing a separate paper devoted to Arendt's political theories.

14603816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603816.value: The analysis and insights has now been written in a book manuscript, "The Appearing Demos: Hong Kong during and after the Umbrella Movement," which is currently under review by University of Michigan press. In this manuscript the PI provides an original and comprehensive analysis of the movement and the political struggles engendered in this postcolonial, neo-liberalist, global city, which echo with many predicaments people in other parts of the world are also experiencing. It also offers a two-way criticism to both PRC’s chauvinistic nationalism and the localism developing in Hong Kong against that chauvinism, both of which are equally problematic. Through the Umbrella Movement, the manuscript explores a way out of totalitarian politics on the one hand and essentialized identity politics on the other. Separately, she is also writing two related essays, one related to Hong Kong's current predicament as a legal community, and one related to Arendt's idea of cohabitation. They are both spin-offs of this project, and hopefully will be published in academic journals.

14603816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603816.value: The PI is expecting to receive reviewer reports, both positive and negative, from the University of Michigan press related to the book manuscript, and she looks forward to revising the manuscript accordingly. Whether the University of Michigan Press has decided to take it up or not, the PI will for sure publish the research as a monograph. She is also hoping to write a Chinese version, based largely on the English manuscript, but also specifically written for a Hong Kong readership. As mentioned earlier, she is also writing separate articles from this research.

14603816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603816.value: This project is devoted to both the Umbrella Movement as a political event and Hong Kong as a political city, and it studies how the protesting crowd in the Occupy and the Hong Kong people in general strive to develop a political community and express themselves through cultural productions. The research investigates how the political movement and the city's general political culture are intertwined, and the urgency for the city to continue to respect both the principle of plurality and the principle of equality. Although the Umbrella Movement ended without achieving anything concrete, the complex intellectual-emotive struggles involved echo in many ways the political struggles around the world. This research contributes to the current studies of contentious politics not only by providing a unique case study but also a city-based theoretical framework to disentangle the many current political problems arised from the nation-state system.

14605416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14605416.value: 社會兩難中的遊戲風驗模型的伸延

14605416.label: Project Objectives
14605416.value: To validate predictions from the extension of the game riskiness model that cooperation is determined by the interaction of game riskiness, expectation of cooperation and risk orientation; and that expectation of cooperation causes cooperation in prisoners' dilemmas involving risk; To resolve inconsistent findings in the effect of framing on cooperation by applying Prospect Theory to manipulate risk orientation through framing and by applying game riskiness model that differentiates games into more-risky and less-risky games; To extend the application of the game riskiness model from a two-person PD to an N-person PD; To demonstrate that predictions of the effects of risk on cooperation are valid in real-life situations beyond laboratory settings.

To resolve inconsistent findings in the effect of framing on cooperation by applying Prospect Theory to manipulate risk orientation through framing and by applying game riskiness model that differentiates games into more-risky and less-risky games;

14605416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605416.value: One pervasive aspect of social interaction is the conflict between the maximization of personal interests and the maximization of collective interests. It is rational to maximize self-interests (i.e., defection), but if all choose to do so, then all are worse off than if all choose to maximize group interests (i.e., cooperation). Such situations are known as social dilemmas. Individuals face a risk in their individual outcomes and group outcomes because outcomes in a social dilemma are jointly determined by all members. Au et al. (2012) proposed an index of game riskiness to formally operationalize the riskiness of cooperation relative to defection in a two-person prisoner’s dilemma (PD) that differentiates PD games into more-risky games versus less-risky games. They predicted and found that risk seeking individuals cooperated more in more-risky games whereas risk-averse individuals cooperated more in less-risky games. Ng and Au (in press) examined the relation between game riskiness, expectation of cooperation and cooperation and found that the positive effect of expectation of cooperation on cooperation was stronger among more risky games than among less risky games. The present project advances beyond previous work to examine risks in social dilemmas that integrates game riskiness, risk orientation and expectation of cooperation using expected utility analysis. Our core prediction is that the positive effect of expectation on cooperation will be the strongest for risk-averse individuals in more risky games and the weakest for risk-seeking individuals in less risky games. The first study examines the causal direction that expectation of cooperation causes cooperation in PDs involving risk. Expectation of cooperation will be manipulated in order to assure that it is expectation causing cooperation but not the other way round. The second study examines ecological validity by extending the game riskiness model that is originally developed for two-person PD to N-person PD that could address more real-life situations. The third study further examines the internal validity of game riskiness model predictions by incorporating the effect of framing. We will manipulate risk orientation using framing instead of measuring it as an individual differences variable. By applying the game riskiness model and Prospect Theory, we predict that people will cooperate more in a gain frame when playing less risky games and people will cooperate more in a loss frame when playing more risky games. The fourth study extends beyond laboratory settings by examining game riskiness model predictions in real-life situations in order to establish external validity. 社會兩難中的遊戲風驗模型的伸延 個人利益最大化與集體利益最大化之間的衝突是一個普遍的社會現象，在日常生活中非常常見。個人選擇最大化自己的利益（叛逃）是理性的，但如果所有人都選擇這樣做，結果會比所有人都選擇集體利益最大化（合作） 更糟。這種情況稱為社會兩難 (Social Dilemma) 。 不論個人選擇合作或背叛，都需要面對風險，因為社會兩難的結果取決於其他成員的決定，而他們的決定是不確定的。我們於早前的研究建立了一個遊戲風險模型 (Game Riskiness Model)，這個模型讓我們可清晰定義囚犯困境 (Prisoner’s Dilemma)中合作和背叛的風險，透過遊戲風險 (Game Riskiness) 指數，我們可更準確預測個人風險取向 (Risk Orientation)如何影響人們在囚犯困境中的合作率。我們在之後的研究也找出遊戲風險和合作預期度 (Expectation of Cooperation) 會產生相互作用影響合作率。當個人認為對方會選擇合作，自己也會有較大機會選擇合作，但這個效果於高風險囚犯困境比低風險囚犯困境更大。 這個研究計劃希望為遊戲風險模型作出伸延，利用預期效用假說 (Expected Utility Hypothesis)，把遊戲風險，個人風險取向和合作預期度一併放進模型內去預測合作率。我們最主要的預測是厭惡風險的人面對高風險囚犯困境時，合作預期度和合作率的正面關係最大；喜愛風險的人面對低風險囚犯困境時，合作預期度和合作率的正面關係最小。 我們將會進行四個實驗。於第一個實險，我們希望確立合作預期度影響合作率這個因果關係，嘗試排除合作與否這個決定會反之影響合作預期度這個可能性。 於第二個實驗，我們希望為遊戲風險模型作出伸延，令原本適用於二人囚犯困境的模型擴展至適用於多人囚犯困境。 於第三個實驗，我們會用框架效應 (Framing Effect)和展望理論 (Prospect Theory)去擴展遊戲風險模型，我們預測當囚犯困境以得益框架(Gain Frame)表示，低風險囚犯困境的合作率會較高；當囚犯困境以損失框架 (Loss Frame)表示，高風險囚犯困境的合作率會較高。 於第四個實驗，我們會把實驗室的結果擴展至現實生活，希望模型能於日常生活中應用。

14605416.label: Realisation of objectives
14605416.value: Regarding Objective 1, we investigated the expectation-of-cooperation by game riskiness interaction on cooperation rate using four studies, including three laboratory studies and one field study. Consistent with our hypothesis, across all the four studies, we found that the effect of expectation-of-cooperation on cooperation rate was moderated by game riskiness. The effect of expectation-of-cooperation on cooperation rate was larger in cooperation-more-risky prisoner’s dilemmas than in cooperation-less-risky counterparts. Furthermore, we examined the causal effect of expectation-of-cooperation on cooperation in one of the laboratory studies by manipulating expectation-of-cooperation in two different ways. Our results supported that expectation-of-cooperation did have a strong positive causal effect on cooperation, and such effect was moderated by game riskiness. Therefore, Objective 1 has been achieved. Regarding Objective 2, we investigated how risk orientation can moderate the effect of game riskiness on cooperation rate in four studies. In one of these four studies, we also attempted to manipulate risk orientation through framing. Nevertheless, we failed to find a consistent risk orientation x game riskiness interaction effect on cooperation rate. Among the four studies we have conducted, we can only find a significant risk orientation x game riskiness interaction effect in one of the risk orientation measures in one study. In order to overcome this issue, we have attempted to include several different risk orientation measures in each study in order to figure out when and why the risk orientation x game riskiness interaction effect would exist. However, we did not find a consistent pattern when such interaction effect would exist. Based on the low correlations between different risk orientation measures, we suspect that individuals may not have a stable risk orientation and that the risk orientation of individuals may vary depending on how it is elicited. Although we failed to find a robust risk orientation x game riskiness interaction effect, our results did provide insight to the research field of risk and uncertainty that humans may not have a stable risk orientation and that we should not treat risk orientation as a personality measure. Regarding Objective 3, we conducted a laboratory study to test whether the game riskiness model can be applied to prisoner’s dilemmas with group sizes of three to six. Consistent with our prediction, we found that the model can be applied to prisoner’s dilemmas with different group sizes, thus extending the applicability of the game riskiness model. Therefore, Objective 3 has been achieved. Regarding Objective 4, we carried out a field study to test whether the game riskiness model can be applied to real-life situations. Particularly, we recruited undergraduate students taking part in group projects to test our model because a group project represents an N-person prisoner’s dilemma in daily life. We asked them about their expectation of contribution towards other group members as well as their contribution intention. We then fitted their responses into the game riskiness model and found that the results can be replicated in group project settings. Therefore, Objective 4 has been achieved.

14605416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605416.value: We found across four studies that the effect of expectation-of-cooperation on cooperation rate was moderated by game riskiness. The effect of expectation-of-cooperation on cooperation rate was larger in cooperation-more-risky prisoner’s dilemmas than in cooperation-less-risky counterparts. This effect was observed in N-person prisoner’s dilemmas, prisoner’s dilemmas presented in both gain and loss frame, prisoner’s dilemmas where expectation-of-cooperation was manipulated instead of measured, and real-life situations. This effect is also robust for individuals with different social value orientations such that the effect held for both pro-socials and pro-selfs. We also found that game riskiness index was a significant predictor of cooperation rate over and above the index of cooperation. These findings depicted how risk can affect cooperation rate in social dilemmas. These findings were presented at the 17th International Conference on Social Dilemmas and the Society for Personality and Social Psychology Annual Convention in 2017 and 2018 respectively. A manuscript presenting these findings will also be submitted for publication very soon. In addition, in two of the abovementioned studies, we recorded the time needed for participants to make each decision in prisoner’s dilemmas and found that game riskiness moderated the effect of decision time on cooperation rate in prisoner’s dilemmas. Across two studies, participants cooperated more when they used less time to make decisions. This effect was stronger among cooperation-more-risky prisoner’s dilemmas than among cooperation-less-risky counterparts. Our results addressed when and why the intuitive-cooperative effect would exist. These findings were presented at the Society for Personality and Social Psychology Annual Convention in 2019. A manuscript presenting these findings will also be submitted for publication very soon.

14605416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605416.value: Although we identified game riskiness as a robust situational factor that moderates the effect of expectation-of-cooperation on cooperation rate, the underlying motivation of why individuals cooperate or defect remains to be explored. By mathematical derivation, we found that the game riskiness index is related to other established indices of prisoner’s dilemmas including the index of cooperation, the fear index, and the greed index. It is likely that fear and greed would be the two major motivations that drive different cooperation rate in prisoner’s dilemmas with different game riskiness index. We plan to conduct a follow-up study to examine explicitly why individuals cooperate or defect under different game riskiness. Furthermore, although we found that game riskiness moderated the effect of decision time on cooperation rate in prisoner’s dilemmas, the decision time was measured instead of manipulated so causal inference cannot be drawn. Given that there is a heated debate of whether intuition causes more cooperation, we plan to conduct a follow-up study by manipulating intuitive thinking vs. deliberative thinking in order to establish the causal inference.

14605416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605416.value: Social dilemmas are situations where decision-makers experience conflict between maximizing individual gains (i.e. defection) and maximizing collective benefits (i.e. cooperation). When considering whether to cooperate with others, people usually consider whether the others will cooperate. Therefore, not surprisingly, there is a positive relationship between expectation-of-cooperation and cooperation rate. In this project, we proposed that the riskiness of cooperation in social dilemmas will affect the strength of the relationship between expectation-of-cooperation and cooperation rate. We conducted three laboratory studies and one field study to test our hypotheses in different contexts. Consistent with our prediction, we found across four studies that the riskiness of cooperation affected the strength of relationship between expectation-of-cooperation and cooperation rate. While most previous studies focused on how personalities can affect the degree of cooperation, this project identified an important situational factor, the riskiness of cooperation, that can affect cooperation. This project also highlighted how subtle changes in the payoff structure can impact the degree of cooperation in social dilemmas. Lastly, this project illustrated that our theoretical prediction about the riskiness of cooperation can be applied to real-life contexts.

14606216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606216.value: This proposed project aims to address the grave issue of trust in post-colonial Hong Kong. With strong support from the World Values Survey Association (WVSA) -- the world's largest cross-national and time-series investigator of human beliefs and values -- this research will examine the nature, levels and determinants of trust in Hong Kong through conducting a territory-wide questionnaire survey, followed by in-depth interviews in the city. As Hong Kong is at a crossroads in the aftermath of the 2014 Occupy protests, it would be particularly opportune and important to include Hong Kong in the next wave of WVS, scheduled for 2017. By establishing an original set of comprehensive time-series and internationally comparable databank in accordance with WVS framework, this project envisions a rigorous longitudinal study of trust in Hong Kong, without which WVS’s time-series data on Hong Kong would be interrupted. Research findings of this project will be of significant practical value to policymakers by producing data as well as insights to assess the extent of social cohesion, evaluate a wide range of social and public policies, and formulate strategies for trust building and rebuilding. Trust contributes to social capital, and social capital is an essential base of social, political and economic well-being. Erosion of trust in modern societies is among top academic concerns. This issue is particularly in urgent need of attention and remedies in Hong Kong, given the intensified tensions between state and society, declining confidence in multilateral institutions, and widening cleavage across political spectrum, age and class in post-colonial period. The study will contribute to the longstanding theoretical discussion of trust and its connection with social capital. By studying the trend and determinants of trust in Hong Kong based on the earlier and upcoming waves of WVS, this research will situate the relevance of the city’s activism in the theoretical discussion on the causes and consequences of the recent trend of activism in hybrid regimes in different parts of the world. 本研究計劃旨在研究後殖民香港的一個重大課題: 信任。在全球最大的跨區域價值觀調查機構「世界價值觀調查協會」的大力支持下，本計劃將透過進行全港性的問卷調查及質性訪談，探討信任在香港社會的性質、程度和其決定因素。2014年佔領事件突顯香港社會的信任危機，因此參與在2017年舉行的第七波世界價值觀調查不但適時，且至為重要。本研究旨在建立全面、時間序列及具國際可比性的數據庫，以便對香港信任度作嚴謹的縱貫性研究，並令香港的世界價值觀數據免於中斷。研究結果將有助政策制訂者分析社會凝聚程度、檢視社會公共政策的成效及制訂信任修復的策略。 信任有助加強社會資本，而後者則是社會、政治和經濟發展的重要基石。現代社會中的信任下滑, 一直以來是學者最關注的研究課題之一。後殖民時期香港的「政府－社會」關係愈趨緊張、對眾多制度和組織的信心減低、世代和階級分歧日趨嚴重，正正說明信任下滑是香港社會迫切探討和解決的課題。 本研究將為信任及其與社會資本的關係的學術討論帶來貢獻。它運用歷屆及來屆的世界價值觀調查數據，探討信任在香港社會的趨勢及其決定因素，籍此理解香港的社會行動，並將之放置於近年世界各地的混合政體裡發生的社會行動的成因和後果的學術討論中作進一步探索。

14606216.label: Realisation of objectives
14606216.value: The research objectives in terms of data collection, analysis, and conceptual development have been achieved as planned. A number of research impact activities and outputs have also been disseminated in reputable academic and public venues. The details are as follows. Objectives 1 and 2: The research team has produced a set of original, large-scale and internationally comparable databank on well-being and social values through implementing the World Values Survey Wave 7 in Hong Kong. The WVS is one of the most reputable global surveys of well-being and trust. Six waves were conducted from 1981 to 2014, and Hong Kong has participated since Wave 5. It consists of nationally representative studies for different societies based on a standard questionnaire. The standard questionnaire measures "social values, attitudes, stereotypes, societal well-being, social capital, trust and membership, economic values, migration, security, postmaterialist index, science and technology, religiosity, ethnical values and norms, political interests and participation, political culture, political regime and governance". In this wave, new indicators concerning migration, conflicts and forms of political participation were added. We also incorporated a set of local questions covering identity, social media usage, participation in the Umbrella Movement, perceived injustices, and housing ownership. We adopted a mixed-methods approach that combined a face-to-face survey with a paper questionnaire and an online survey in the W7, which was conducted by the Centre for Communication and Public Opinion Survey of CUHK and Survey Sampling International, respectively. We also established a set of protocols such as Contact with selected prosperity agencies, GIS, speeder, open-end check, straight-liner, back-checking, weighting, and other procedures to increase the response rate and data validity. The total number of N was 1,031 for the face-to-face survey and 1,044 for online survey. The data were made publicly available on the archiving website of WVSA for the use of local and international communities. Objectives 3 and 4: The findings of the project have provided original and vibrant evidence to unpack the relationship between trust, social capital, and the rise of political activism in Hong Kong. The new mode of mobilization is characterized by horizontal organization, massive self-mobilization, and radicalized actions through social media and the active participation of the younger and educated populations. First, we found a general trend of declining social and political trust in the city, which is often mediated by critical event and age, and moderated by post-modernism, identity, social capital and perceived participatory outcomes. Second, we also found a further rise of the post-modelist values of the Hong Kong population in general and the youth in particular, which are comparable to Western Europe and in sharp contrast to East Asia. We also examined the interactive mechanisms between the socioeconomic and political values. For instance, individuals who are more dissatisfied with their lives are more likely to engage in "unconventional political participation" such as strikes and boycotts. This negative relationship is particularly strong among people with a post-materialist orientation, yet life satisfaction is not related to "conventional political participation", including voting and peaceful protests. Finally, we also unpacked the relationship between mobilization and countermobilization in Hong Kong through event anlysis and network analysis. While the rise of new regime repertoires in the post-Occupy ears have curtailed organized resistance during some periods, they have also eroded the regime's legitimacy, exposing it to the re-eruption of protests. The outputs differentiate interactive mechanisms between conventional and unconventional contentious actions and unpack the positive correlation between mobilization and countermobilization are timely. They help to situation the Hong Kong case to the broader and timely inquiry between governance and dissent and explain the background of the rise of the massive and resilient protest movement in 2019. Objective 5: The above new findings have distorted the institutional trust and weakened the role of traditional intermediate organizations. They also revealed a challenge to governance: how to manage the diverse values and rising expectations of the public and absorb and respond to the decline in social and political trust. A tentative list of policy recommendations for public opinion tracing, reform in consultation structure, strategic partnerships with trusted organizations, civic education programs, and community and digital engagements was derived. The trends and determinants of trust were found to be increasingly correlated with the indicators and platforms commonly associated with political polarisation and identity politics. It is therefore recommended that the government should first acknowledge the change in public values that is not only local but also global. It should also develop new mechanisms to increase citizens' political efficacy in policymaking and everyday life to resolve political polarization among the population. We have obtained a matching grant from the Policy and Innovation Coordination Office of the Hong Kong Government to increase the sampling size, questions, and validity of the survey. The data and a competition report has been submitted to the Office in March 2019 and made publicly available.

14606216.label: Major findings and research outcome
14606216.value: A number of outputs in reputable venues and include three conference papers, one edited volume, and six journal articles (two published, two under review, and two in preparation). All these outputs help to provide methodological insight, empirical findings and conceptual development in the fields of are studies, political institution and social movement studies. Three conference papers were presented. These included the annual meeting of Association for Asian Studies, the biannual meeting of the International Political Science Association, and a contentious politics symposium at the University of California Berkeley. The PI authored and published the China Journal deals with the repertoire of and the relationship between mobilization and counter-mobilization. He also co-authored another article in Island Studies Journal that argues that the contestation between autonomy and sovereign control cannot be read in purely constitutional terms but must be considered within the changing socioeconomic and legal context. His co-authored article to be published in International Political Science Review, treats life satisfaction as an independent variable and examines its interactive terms with post-modernist values, political trust, and forms of conventional and unconventional political participation. The PI also co-edited and published an edited volume that surveys the antecedent and contingent process of a critical event, the Umbrella Movement. The volume has been positively reviewed in China Quarterly, China Journal, China Perspectives, and Social Movement Studies as well as featured in internal Bookfairs in Europe and Asia. His co-authored under-review article in Social Indicators Research underscores the context of socialization in influencing both a postmaterialist orientation and intergenerational change occurring during a critical event, which sheds light on the relationship between value change and regime resilience.

14606216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14606216.value: The project has facilitated cross-national collaboration in the East Asian region. The PI have organized a panel on political trust and populism in East Asia at the 25th World Political Congress in Australia. The panelists include the PIs of WVS in East Asia as well as esteemed scholars in these subfields. They will further collaborate in developing regional indicators for the future waves of WVS and produced research outputs. The current project has also inspired new projects that touch upon social network analysis and contentious politics. The PI has received one ECS, one GRF, two PPRs that study everyday politics, popular contention, and state-diasporic relations in Hong Kong and the East and Southeast countries. The PI is writing up two manuscripts comparing the WVS survey data and other databases. The first paper with Prof. Stan Wong of Poly compares the findings from face-to-face and online surveys. The second paper with Prof. Eric Fong of HKU deals with sequence analysis of protest events.

14606216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14606216.value: Trust is a prerequisite for social integration, economic efficiency, and political stability. The prevalence of contention in Hong Kong indicates a lack of trust between the state and civil society, and even among members of the two realms. Through implementing the World Values Survey Wave 7, this project provides an internationally comparable database supplemented with local questions and experimental designs for the use of academic, public, and civil society sectors locally and globally. Methodologically, the project has established fieldwork protocols that will inform other researchers on the what and how to conduct face-to-face household surveys in gated communities and to identify the challenges and benefits of combing face-to-face and online methods. Empirically, our primary finding was that citizens’ social and political trust is dynamic, changes over time, and varies between sectors. We found a general trend of declining social and political trust in the city, which is often mediated by critical event and age, and moderated by post-modernism, identity, and perceived participatory outcomes. Theoretically, our research outputs differentiate conventional and unconventional contentious actions and unpack their interactive mechanisms at the individual level, which help to situation the Hong Kong case to the broader and timely inquiry between governance and dissent.

14607416.value: 功能組別與香港的產業干預

14607416.label: Project Objectives
14607416.value: Study the campaign issues and mobilization strategies of functional constituency elections in the 2016 Legislative Council elections, and compare the mobilization patterns and campaign issues in different types of functional constituencies and different candidates/parties. Study how the rise of new political groups in different professional sectors after the 2014 Umbrella Movement affect the salience of political issues (e.g. constitutional development) in the campaigns of their respective sectors. Compare the legislative performance of different types of functional constituency legislators with the popularly-elected legislators, in 2008-2016, and see if their policy demands had brought about a trend of sectoral intervention by the government in the period.

14607416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14607416.value: This project studies the election campaigns of the functional constituencies in the 2016 Legislative Council elections of Hong Kong, and its relations to the legislative performance of the functional constituency legislators. It will examine the impact of newly-formed political groups in various professional sectors, as a result of the Umbrella Movement in 2014, on the 2016 campaign. It will compare the legislative performance of different types of functional constituency legislators (representatives of corporate, professional, social sectors and the ‘Super District Council” sector) in the 2008-12 and 2012-16 Legislative Council. The focus will be on the relations between the campaign platforms, campaign issues, and actions and demands of legislators and policy outputs of the government. It will examine how the legislative actions of the FC legislators since 2008 affected government policy-making, especially the role of the government in the economy. In particular, it examines whether or not different functional legislators will drive the Hong Kong government towards more sectoral intervention. 本計劃研究2016年立法會選舉中的功能界別的選戰。研究焦點包括雨傘運動如何影響這次選戰，包括在佔領運動期間湧現的大量不同專業界別的政治組織，如何影響及參與這次選舉。 研究亦會比較不同類別的功能組別議員(包括超級區議會議席)在議會的表現，以及其與直選議員的表現的比較。 研究會集中功能界別選戰、各候選人政綱中提出的界別訴求或政策訴求、與議會表現及政府政策之關係，從而檢討功能界別議員的表現，是否有改變政府的政策和在經濟中的角色。

14607416.label: Realisation of objectives
14607416.value: (1) The campaign issues and mobilization strategies of candidates in selected functional constituencies in the 2016 Legislative Council election were studied, through interviewing of candidates, collection and analysis of campaign materials, observation of the campaign process, and studying election forums. The campaign issues and mobilization strategies of different FCs are compared, most notably between the professional FCs which adopt individual voting, and corporate FCs which adopt corporate voting. (2) It studied how the post-Umbrella professional groups made an impact in the 2016 Functional constituency elections, and in the 2016 subsectoral elections for the Election Committee that elected the 2017 Chief Executive. It also showed how these groups transformed and politicized these elections in 2016 and beyond. (3) We conduct a comprehensive collection and tallying of various indicators of legislative performance of all legislators from 2008 to 2016. The indicators include attendance figures, vote decisions, speeches and positions in major voting decisions and budget debates. The performance of different types of legislators will be compared. All the three research objectives have been achieved in full by the completion of the project.

14607416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14607416.value: 1. The Umbrella Movement gave rise to a new crop of professional groups which are politically-oriented, more intent to challenge the conservative establishment and promote democracy. Some of these groups played a more important role in their sectors in the 2016 Legco election (e,g. Architecture, Information Technology). 2. These groups played an important role in finding candidates for the 2016 Subsectoral election for the Election Committee that elects the Chief Executive. They played an important role in politizing the campaign and mobilizing for support, which makes the campaign issue of anti-CY Leung overwhelm the sectoral concerns of the sectoral elections. They also continue to take a more active role in the election of their respective professional bodies. 3. These new groups posed important "traces" of the Umbrella Movement, which stimulates political participation in respective professional sectors. This will have major impacts for years to come, not the least in the 2019 Anti-extradition Bill movement. 4. A preliminary analysis of the performance of the legislators, comparing the Functional Constituency and directly-elected members in 2008-2016, showed some similar patterns as those in 1998 to 2018. The functional constituency legislators put in a lot more sectoral demands. They are more in favor of asking the government for sectoral subsidies and policy help. The years 2008-2016 showed improved performance of functional legislators in terms of attendance, but the vote decisions are more party-aligned, with the functional legislators much more likely to vote for the government.

14607416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14607416.value: 1. The PI is going to write a book that comprehensively assesses the functional constituency experience, including the origins and development of the system, the evolution of campaign styles, and analysis of the legislative performance of those elected 20 years after 1997. By late 2019, the PI has half of the manuscript finished. 2. The theme of the impact of the Umbrella Movement on the political participation of Hong Kong people has been developed into a new project, which has got GRF funding in 2019/20 (Ref: 14606319). It studies the "traces" of the Umbrella Movement as how the 2014 movement experience shapes political participation of different people since 2014. The analysis will focus on their participation on electoral level, community level, and cultural level. 3. Following (1) and (2), the PI will continue to research and compare the 2020 functional constituency campaign with the previous ones, and how the politicization process of professionals affect the 2020 Legislative Council election. These will be written into parts of books, to be published by university presses, and articles in internationally refereed journals.

14607416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14607416.value: This research on the functional constituency elections studies the campaign process and electoral strategies of different sectors in the 2016 Legislative Council elections. It also analyzes and compares the performance of legislators who are elected by different methods, from 2008 to 2016. It shows that the functional elections usually focus on sector issues, and the functional legislators are more prone to put in sectoral demands, which led to more government intervention and subsidies. The project shows the impact of the Umbrella Movement on the political participation of various professional groups. Some of these groups had significant impact on some of the sectors in the 2016 Legco election. Many of these professional groups succeeded in politicizing the 2016 Subsectoral election for the Election Committee for the Chief Executive, which led to a landslide victory of the democrats. The politicization effect points to a generational change in various professions, with a younger cohort who are more politically active, more post-materialist, more anti-establishment, which can bring political changes in years to come.

14608416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14608416.value: In Hong Kong and China (Guangzhou/Suzhou), there are many classic Chinese gardens (CCG), open and green spaces which are considered as modern parks (MPs). Such spaces offer a variety of psychological, physical and social benefits promoting a stronger sense of community and allowing people to cope better with everyday stress. Such areas are designed to provide tranquillity for people and it is now an emerging area of policy in the promotion of quality of life. Previously, we have studied the elucidation of the tranquillity concept in Hong Kong. It is evident that there are discrepancies in the understanding of tranquillity and the places where it exists. The study concentrated on urban areas and country parks at the periphery of Hong Kong. It is, therefore, incumbent on scholars to seek to further understand the concept on a broader scale. Tranquillity is a natural asset. It reflects the degree to which human beings experience the environment unhindered by unwanted intrusiveness both audio and visual. Although they are vital, tranquil spaces are under threat especially in urban areas. It is, therefore, important to identify and understand such places so that they can be further planned and managed for continuing benefit. In Hong Kong and South China, many people visit CCGs and MPs with the intention of experiencing peace and quiet. This study will conceptualise the understanding of tranquillity and determine the extent to which a tranquil environment can be achieved. The study will identify if there are important features of CCGs that can be employed in MPs, or vice versa. As tranquillity is often associated with the absence of noise, the method will involve the assessment of traffic noise levels and measurement of the percentage of natural and contextual features. Analysis will be used by adopting a Tranquillity Rating Prediction Tool (TRAPT). This tool is useful in identifying valuable tranquil spaces and can be used by a range of stakeholders including administrators, planners and managers of CCGs and MPs. An important aspect of the study will involve the quantification of the effect of visitor numbers on the experience of tranquillity. The predicted tranquillity rating in eight contrasting environments (4 CCGs and 4 MPs) will be surveyed. The results and analysis will add to the growing body of knowledge in this discipline and help decision-makers, planners and managers of CCGs and MPs and may have possible application elsewhere. 在香港和中國內地（廣州/蘇州）有一些經典的中國花園（CCG），以及被認為是現代公園（MPs）的開放和綠色空間。 這些地方提供了多種多樣物質的、精神的和社會的益處來增強社區的認同感以及幫助人們更好地面對每天的壓力。這些地方的設計是為了提供給人們寧靜， 現在它已經成為制定提高人們生活品質政策的新興領域。 過去，我們已經了解到寧靜這個概念在香港的意義， 我們可以清楚地看到對寧靜這概念的理解和寧靜真實存在之間的差異。 此次研究著重於都市地區以及香港周邊的郊野公園。 因此，學者應當義不容辭地在更廣闊的範圍進一步理解寧靜這個概念。 寧靜是一種自然資產。 它能反映 人類不受聲音和視覺的干擾去感受自然的程度。儘管它們是重要的，但寧靜的空間正受到威脅，尤其在都市地區。 因此，辨析和了解這些地方顯得尤為重要，這樣能通過進一步的規劃和管理使這些地方持續獲益。 在香港和中國南方，一些人遊覽經典的中國花園（CCG）和現代公園（MPs）是為了體驗平和及安靜。 本次研究會使大家對寧靜的理解更概念化以及決定寧靜環境所能達到的程度。本次研究將會辨析典型中國花園的重要特徵能否應用到現代公園，反之亦然。寧靜經常與無噪音相聯繫，研究的方法將會涉及交通噪音程度測量以及自然與環境特徵的百分比評估。 分析將會使用寧靜評級預測工具（TRAPT）。 這種工具在辨析有價值的寧靜空間 時很有用，適用於廣泛的利益相關者，如經典的中國花園和現代公園的行政管理員、規劃者、管理人員。本次研究中涉及的一個重要方面是遊客數量對寧靜體驗的影響。 預測寧靜評估將會在8個不同的地方進行（4個經典的中國花園CCG 和 4個現代公園 MPs）。研究結果和分析將應用在這個學科中日益增長的知識體系，並且幫助經典的中國花園和現代公園的決策制定者、規劃者和管理者，甚至可能應用在其他地方。

14610516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14610516.value: The proposed project seeks to investigate the emergence and development of ‘Canton enamel’ or Guangdong falang 廣東琺瑯 in the Qing dynasty (1644-1911) with special attention to its production and distribution pattern. Major issues to be dealt with are: (1) the stylistic differences among imperial wares, export wares and those designated for national and local circulation; (2) the collection and distribution history of these wares in overseas markets; and (3) the artistic affiliation between Canton enamel metalwares and enamel porcelain wares or Guangcai 廣彩, another outstanding craft produced in Guangdong during the Qing Dynasty. ‘Canton enamels’ designate a specific type of enamel metalwares produced in the Guangdong region. They mainly consist of painted enamels and Basse-taille enamels. Inspired by painted enamelware imported from Europe, workshops in Guandong pioneered in the production of enamel metalware as early as in the Kangxi reign (1662-1722) and had in fact, provided technical and human resources support to zaobanchu造辦處, the Palace Workshop in Beijing, the Qing Capital. The emergence of Canton enamels, thus, was critical to the development of enamel works made from various materials in Qing China. The proposed project probes into the production, distribution, and trading mechanism of Canton enamels through the Qing Dynasty. Further, it examines how the artistic style of Canton enamels varied with different target consumers and through different periods. It also considers the connections between Canton enamel metalwares and Canton enamel porcelain wares, and the impact of the former on overseas art markets. Its aim is to unveil how Guangdong interacted with Beijing, other Chinese provinces and foreign countries in terms of art, culture and economy during the Qing Dynasty. The proposed project attempts to build a database of all extant Canton enamels and an archive of relevant historical accounts. A series of scholarly articles on the following topics will be produced: 1) The production and trading mechanism of Canton enamels in the Qing dynasty. 2) Stylistic variations of Canton enamels designated for imperial use, local and overseas markets across different periods of the Qing dynasty. 3) The artistic interactions between Canton enamel metalwares and enamel porcelain wares. 4) The distribution and collection of Canton enamels in Europe and America in Qing times. Moreover, an academic conference will be organized and a special exhibition on Canton enamels will be mounted so that the research findings can benefit the academic community and the public.

14610516.label: Realisation of objectives
14610516.value: Objective 1 1.1 An image database of extant Canton enamels has been completed. It contains more than 1500 images collected from over 40 public museums and private collections across Asia, Europe and America through field trips and publication. They are primarily images of 18th to 20th century Canton enamels. 1.2 A literary archive has been established. About 210 books and essays on Canton enamels have been collected. Since Canton enamel is rarely mentioned in local historical documents, effort was made to explore its records in Qing Palace Archives. A database extracting all records of enamelled copperwares (including Canton enamels) from the Furnishing Archive of Qing Palace清宮陳設檔案 was created, which offer much information for understanding the amount, type, and location of display and storage of Canton enamels in the Qing court from the Kangxi to the Daoguang periods (1662-1852). This database is open to public and can be access via this link: http://www.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/~fadept/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/Furnishing-Archive-of-Qing-Palace.pdf Objective 1 has been achieved. Objective 2 2.1 Based on the established image archive, together with data collected through 13 field trips to major cities, such as Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou in the Mainland China; New York, Boston, Chicago, Salem, Los Angeles in the U.S; Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Vietnam in Southeast Asia, together with Russia, United Kingdom and Portugal, the project team collected a huge amount of date, compared and analyzed Canton enamels for different markets from the 18th to the 20th centuries. 2.2 Rare information about Canton enamels only circulated among local collectors and published in Southeast Asia. It was collected during field trips to those countries. Besides, scholars, experts and collectors were invited to join two workshops organized by the project team in 2018 and 2019 respectively. Although the second workshop was finally cancelled due to social unrest in Hong Kong, conference papers from 9 scholars coming from Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Beijing and Sichuan of the Mainland, Taiwan, Vietnam, United Kingdom are gathered. A draft proceeding was produced. This offered valuable opportunity for us to get rare information and comments from scholars who had access to Canton enamel collections in other places. 2.3 The Co-I composed two papers, one focusing on Canton enamels for different markets and the other one dealing with the overall stylistic development throughout the Qing dynasty, for the two workshops. Both are published in academic refereed journals. Objective 2 has been achieved. Objective 3 3.1 The PI conducted a microscopic research on a decorative motif called “honeycomb” that was prevalent in 18th century Canton enamel metalware and porcelain. A macroscopic comparative study between the two types of wares made in Guangzhou was also conducted to see the extent to which their production technique and decorative style affected one and the other in the 18th century. 3.2 Apart from studying the image and literary achieve, the PI and Co-I also visited Master craftsmen (producer of Canton enamel copperware and porcelain) in Guangzhou to gain better understanding about the technical aspect of the research. Both the microscopic and macroscopic studies done by the PI are turned into refereed journal articles. Object 3 has been completed. Objective 4 4.1 To explore the organization of production and trading mechanism of Canton enamels, the PI and Co-I researched different local records and gazetteers of Guangdong and other provinces in China, as well as trading records of China and Europe. Unfortunately, since copper was forbidden from exporting to other countries during the Qing dynasty, very few written records about the trading of Canton enamels are found. Instead, we gathered more information about different Canton enamel workshops on objects as the designations of many workshops were inscribed on their products. Also, the trading pattern and transfer of technique from Guangzhou to other places are unfolded through our study of objects sold to overseas markets and their related local records. 4.2 Since the information on the production organization and trading mechanism is rather fragmented, no separate article about these aspects are written. The research result is integrated into the article on the overall development of Canton enamels through the ages prepared by the Co-I. Objective 4 is achieved. Objective 5 5.1 Based on the image and literary archive, especially the palace records of craftsmen and enamel copperwares extracting from the Furnishing Archive of Qing Palace, the interaction between the imperial and local workshop in Guangzhou and the Qing imperial court, especially their exchange of craftsmen, production technique and decorative methods, became clear. Our visits to the palace museums in Beijing and Taipei, and provincial museums in Guangzhou allowed us to compare objects produced for local and overseas markets and those especially for the imperial court. 5.2 The exchanges of decorative motifs and artistic styles across different media produced in different provinces, including porcelain made in Jingdezhen, porcelain and enamel copperwares made in Guangzhou, textiles made in Jiangnan for the imperial court, and imperial enamel copperware made in Beijing from the late 17th to the 18th century are thoroughly explored in one of the PI’s article. 5.3 Since there is hardly any solid evidence left for the production of enamel copperware in places other than Guangdong and Beijing in China, this area can hardly be explored further unless new evidence appears in the future. Objective 5 is, in the main, achieved.

14610516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14610516.value: 1. The project team identified 15 pieces/sets of Canton enamels, the production years of which are clear. They serve as standard objects for dating many extant pieces. They are presented in our first workshop (Part C, 9, no. 4) and the article composed by our former Research Assistant, Hu Tingting, has been published (Part C, 8, no. 3). 2. The overall development of Canton enamels was presented for the first time. The project team divides its development into three phases. In the first phase from late 17th to mid-18th century, Canton enamels were mainly for export and their production was closely related to enamel porcelain production in Guangzhou. In the second phase from mid to late 18th century, an imperial enamel workshop was set up in Guangzhou for making wares for the court. The style of these imperial wares became increasingly different from those made for local market. In the third phase from late 18th century to early 20th century, apart from those commissioned by nobles of Siam and Vietnam, most Canton enamels were sold as souvenirs or everyday utensils. This development of Canton enamels is presented in our second workshop (Part C, 9, no. 5) and the article is published (Part C, 8, no. 4). 3. Canton enamels for Siam, Islamic and Europe markets show distinctive features and they differed in object types and decorative styles. This topic is discussed in our first workshop (Part C, 9, no. 3), presented in a public lecture (Part C, 11, no. 3) and the paper is published (Part C, 8, no. 1). 4. Our research shows that enamel copperware and porcelain were initially produced in the same workshops in Guangzhou in early 18th century, but later separately manufactured after 1730s when the demand for enamel porcelain increased. This finding is presented in our second workshop (Part C, 9, no. 6) and published. (Part C, 8, no. 5) 5. Through discussing the honeycomb motif found on Canton enamel copperware and porcelain, the close interrelationship between different materials of the 18th century is unveiled. The impact of textile on other materials including Canton enamels was prominent. The argument is presented in an international conference (Part C, 9, no. 2) and published (Part C, 8, no. 2). The draft proceeding of the second workshop is produced for sharing among scholars in the field of Canton enamels (Part C, 11, no. 4).

14610516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14610516.value: 1. A more intensive study on the trade and production of Canton enamels for overseas markets, especially Southeast Asia and the Islamic world, will unfold the intricate trading network between China and Southeast Asia. Many private and local collections of Canton enamels in the Islamic world are yet to be explored. Besides, the impact of Canton enamels on the use and manufacture of enamel ceramics for Southeast Asia deserves further attention as this important aspect is little known. 2. The close relation between enamel workshops in Beijing and Canton deserves further exploration. Only a small number out of hundreds of enamel copperwares produced in Guangzhou now in the palace museums in Beijing and Taipei are published and known to us. If it is possible to have access to this large number of extant imperial pieces, it will become possible to further discuss how Canton craftsmen transformed conventional and western motifs into those matching the imperial taste and how the two workshops interacted and influenced each other in the 18th and 19th centuries.

14610516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14610516.value: The project aims to investigate the emergence and development of “Canton enamel” or Guangdong falang, a type of enamel metalware produced in Guangzhou, in the Qing dynasty (1644-1911). The project has achieved the followings: First, it established an image archive of all extant Canton enamels from public and private collections which made the study of this little documented subject possible. Second, it identified 15 pieces/sets standard objects for dating extant Canton enamels. Third, it established the chronological development of Canton enamels from the late 17th to early 20th century for the first time. While Canton enamel copperware and porcelain were closely related in the first phase between late 17th to mid 18th century, those produced in Guangzhou for the imperial court and oversea markets developed into two distinctively different styles in the second phase that ended in the late 18th century. By the early 20th century, Canton enamels were mostly made as souvenirs and everyday utensils. Specific vessels were commissioned for the markets of Siam and Vietnam. Canton enamel as a product for imperial consumption and overseas markets prove it to be a subject deserving further investigation in the future.

14613416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613416.value: Background Dementia is a large and growing health problem and since the majority of dementia patients live at home, caring responsibilities generally fall to family members. Caregivers are often inadequately supported by formal health services and can experience burden as a result of providing care over a long period of time. Caregivers are known to have poorer psychological health, physical health, social networks and also suffer from financial burden. Interventions for caregivers are diverse and multiple contextual factors may contribute to success or failure. Existing reviews tend to examine either qualitative or quantitative evidence, they may focus on just one type of intervention (e.g. mentoring) or one delivery method (e.g. internet support). Reviews typically strive to aggregate findings but for complex interventions this can be counter-productive because important contextual detail about why interventions were beneficial or not may be lost through these approaches. Objective Use high-quality trial data to determine which interventions for caregivers of people with dementia work, for whom and in what circumstances, to improve burden and depression in caregivers. Interpret intervention effectiveness in the context of existing health services and caregiver characteristics in included studies. Data collection and methods A mixed methods approach will be used to understand the complexity in interventions for caregivers. First, high-quality quantitative data from randomised trials will be sought through a systematic review. Included studies will be randomised interventions for caregivers of people with dementia and studies with comparison groups providing other interventions in caregivers or no interventions (control group). Caregiver outcomes such as burden or depression will be statistically combined (meta-analysis) where possible to assess intervention effectiveness. Subgroup analysis will be conducted to examine types of interventions and the effect on different outcomes. Network meta-analysis will also be used to directly compare interventions to find the most effective. Findings will be supplemented with qualitative information or process evaluations from each of the included studies. This information will be synthesized to contextualize and explain why interventions were successful in certain circumstances. Main outcomes Intervention effectiveness will be assessed in terms of caregiver outcomes for stress (burden) and mental health (depression, anxiety and general mental health outcomes). Secondary outcomes include physical health status, subjective well-being, self-efficacy or knowledge and positive aspects of caregiving. The effectiveness of different interventions on primary and secondary outcomes will be interpreted using qualitative evidence and process evaluation measures relating to intervention facilitators and barriers. 研究背景 因為癡呆患者通常居住在家中並由家庭成員照顧，癡呆正在成為一個日趨嚴重的公共衛生問題。由於提供照顧的周期長加之針對照顧者的衛生服務不足，癡呆照顧者通常承受著巨大的身心負擔。通常來說，癡呆照顧者的身心健康和社會網絡較差並且承受著沈重的經濟負擔。 針對癡呆照顧者的幹預措施多種多樣，幹預措施的成敗取決於多種情境因素。目前已有的定量和定性的綜述大多針對某一種幹預措施(例如心理輔導)或是某一種幹預實施方式(例如網絡支持)。這些綜述通常試圖簡單的合並研究結果，但是這種方法對復雜幹預措施是不合適的，因為我們可能會遺漏影響幹預成敗的重要情境因素。 研究目的 我們利用高質量的臨床試驗確定哪種復雜幹預措施對癡呆照顧者更為有效；對哪種照顧者，在何種情境下可以緩解照顧者的壓力和抑郁。我們還將解析復雜幹預措施在不同的衛生服務背景下，針對不同類型照顧者的效果。 數據收集和研究方法 我們將用混合研究方法解析多種復雜幹預措施對癡呆照顧者的效果。首先，我們將從相關系統綜述中搜尋符合入選標準的隨機對照臨床試驗。我們將納入在癡呆照顧者中比較復雜幹預措施和其他幹預措施或無幹預措施效果的隨機對照臨床試驗。在可能的情況下，我們將利用薈萃分析的方法合並諸如壓力或抑郁等評估幹預效果的研究結局。我們將利用亞組分析的方法比較不同幹預措施對不同研究結局的幹預效果。我們將利用網絡薈萃分析的方法尋找最為有效的幹預措施。我們還將從納入的研究中提取定性的或是過程分析的信息，以了解幹預措施在特定情境下起作用的機制。 研究結局 主要研究結局包括癡呆照顧者的壓力和精神健康情況（如抑郁，焦慮和其他精神問題）。次要研究結局包括癡呆照顧者的身體健康，主觀幸福感，對服務的信心、知識以及其他積極的態度。定性的或是過程分析的信息將用來解析不同幹預措施對主要和次要結局起作用的機制。

14613416.label: Realisation of objectives
14613416.value: We proposed four objectives in the original study. (1) Identify, appraise and thematically synthesize findings from high quality intervention studies for caregivers of people with dementia. (2) Undertake statistical synthesis of findings to compare the relative benefits of intervention components on outcomes or features of intervention, participant and contextual factors that contribute to intervention success.(3) Identify qualitative research or process evaluations for each included RCT and synthesise findings to enable comprehensive contextualisation of intervention success and outcomes.(4) Summarize which interventions are optimal, in what circumstances and determine implementation issues that are relevant for service planners to deliver appropriate and acceptable interventions. The first two objectives are the primary objective, and the third and fourth objectives are the secondary objectives.Based on the above four objectives, the project is carried out in two phases: the first phase is systematic literature review and meta-analysis of high quality intervention, and second phase is literature search to aid contextualization of RCT findings – a realist review. To achieve the above proposed objectives, we conducted an electronic literature search of Medline, Embase, PsychInfo and CINAHL Plus from their respective inception to Apr 2017, and a total of 7289 records were retrieved. After excluding duplicates and screening of titles and abstracts, 272 citations were left for full text screening. Among these 182 were excluded according to inclusion criteria, in total, 72 relevant studies were identified, included studies will be randomized interventions for caregivers of people with dementia and studies with comparison groups providing other interventions in caregivers or no interventions (control group). Main outcomes include burden and depression of caregiver, and secondary outcomes include quality of life, anxiety, self-efficacy, stress, distress, coping, mental health, and social support. A mixed methods approach will be used to understand the complexity in interventions for caregivers. First, high-quality quantitative data from randomized trials will be sought through a systematic review. Caregiver outcomes such as burden or depression will be statistically combined (meta-analysis) where possible to assess intervention effectiveness. Subgroup analysis will be conducted to examine types of interventions and the effect on different outcomes. Network metaanalysis will also be used to directly compare interventions to find the most effective.Findings will be supplemented with qualitative information or process evaluations from each of the included studies. This information will be synthesized to contextualize and explain why interventions were successful in certain circumstances. To achieve the primary objective, details from included studies will be extracted in duplicate, using standardised forms to ensure consistency and discrepancies will be confirmed through checking the original article. Information in the following key areas will be extracted from studies: citation details; intervention characteristics (components included, psychological frameworks employed in psychosocial interventions, mode of delivery etc.); participant characteristics (spouse, adult children, caregivers of people with mild or severe cognitive impairment); outcomes evaluated (which outcomes, scales or tools used to assess outcomes, whether scales/tools are validated; follow-up assessment details (number/frequency of assessments); losses to follow-up (number of drop outs). Cochrane Collaboration's tool for assessing risk of bias. Effectiveness of interventions will be examined by grouping interventions and outcomes by type. Individual study findings will be statistically combined using meta-analysis methods or be narratively synthesized if there are high between study heterogeneity. Network meta-analysis methods will be used to compare the effectiveness for different outcomes across different intervention types. This allows comparisons between interventions that have not directly been assessed in head-to-head studies and will thereby allow us to rank which interventions are most or least effective for improving different outcomes. A realist review will be used to assess secondary objectives. A realist review will be undertaken to help to untangle the complexity of intervention findings and set conclusions in context by identifying enabling factors, barriers and contexts with better intervention success. Identified literature will be scrutinised by two researchers to exclude low quality or irrelevant evidence.An inductive approach will be used to dictate narratively synthesis information using the themes that are identified in the evidence. Disseminate, implement and evaluate: The findings from the realist review in combination with the main review will be disseminated as simple recommendations for service providers to help identify which interventions are likely to work in which circumstances and for whom. Attempts to overcome problems Conducting a meta-analysis with such a scale (10 outcomes, 5 interventions) is very challenging. We encountered several major difficulties during project implementation, including: (1) Difficulty in depth extraction of data Since the project is aimed at high quality data assessment and qualitative circumstances analysis, there are high requirements for data extraction. The main difficulties are large amount of data, large amount of content extraction and time consuming. We extracted 233 data sources of 9 categories over 13 months. Two full-time investigators (HS, JZ) independently reviewed the full manuscripts of eligible studies and extracted information into an electronic database to ensure the smooth operation of the work. (2) Difficulties in the application of Network Meta-analysis and realist review Network meta-analysis is used to compare the effectiveness for different outcomes across different intervention types, and to find the most effective. This method has higher statistical requirements, and the selection of models, the application of software, and the interpretation of results analysis are all challenging, We implemented the analysis using softwares including R,STAT, and GeMTC, and used normal prior distributions to fit the model, yielding 150 000 iterations (50 000 per chain) to obtain the posterior distributions of model parameters. At the same time, realist principles should be applied to enhance the potential to inform intervention design given this complexity. Realist review analysis, as a qualitative analysis, is more subjective. In order to ensure the accuracy and consistency of the data. Two investigators (HS, JZ) respectively reviewed a large number of literatures and summarized their opinions when describing and analyzing the social background and context-mechanism-outcome (CMO) mechanism, and the inconsistent opinions were determined by Dr. Liang. Despite these, the whole team has done extremely hard work and eventually overcome all these challenges and successfully completed the project.

14613416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14613416.value: 72 randomized controlled trials were included. For the primary outcomes (burden and depression), network meta-analysis shows that respite care relief has a significant difference in caregiver burden at post-treatment compared with usual care (SMD,-10.04; 95%CI,-16.28 to -5.48, P<0.001). Although the protective effect of support compared with psycho-education was not statistically significant (SMD, 4.9; 95%CI,-3.2 to 13.0, P=0.42), support had the greatest probability (73.9%) for being the best intervention for caregiver burden at post-treatment. While none of the interventions clearly had high efficacy, multicomponent had the greatest probability (54.8%) for being the best intervention option on caregiver depression at post-treatment. For second outcomes, compared with usual care, psycho-education had a significant effect on the two domains of quality of life for caregivers in 6 month, including physical domain(SMD=0.49, 95%CI 0.11 to 0.86, P=0.01) and relationship domain (SMD=0.52, 95%CI 0.14 to 0.90, P=0.008); psychotherapy had a significant effect on caregiver stress in post-treatment (SMD=-0.62, 95%CI -0.98 to–0.26, P<0.001, P=0.35). In the systematic review of articles that cannot be analyzed by Dual-arm Meta, there is a considerable heterogeneity of the interventions for caregivers of people with dementia in intervention components, mode of delivery and length or intensity of intervention. Based on this, we conducted a realistic review, four categories of the topic are obtained by context-mechanism-outcome (CMO) relationships analysis: (1) congruence with local background; (2) congruence with local health care; (3) congruence with intervention background; (4) within-intervention feedback. Analysis indicatied that failure to align the intervention with contextual influences, including with local background and with the existing local health care pathway, frequently leads to implementation failure. Although the theory is fundamental to the implementation of the intervention, intervention design should incorporate theories operating at higher ecological levels (background and local health care).

14613416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14613416.value: Today worldwide over 44 million people are suffering from dementia with an expected increase to over 132 million by the year 2050. It’s known that caregivers of dementia patients mostly experience higher physical and mental burden than caregivers of non-demented relatives. Interventions addressing informal care dyads always have the potential to affect outcomes on side of both the caregiver and the care recipient. We have successfully established the Database of Dementia Caregiver Intervention and Effects (DCI&E), so that we can assess the effect of different interventions on both caregiver and care recipient outcomes. Building upon our previous work of the effects of interventions on caregiver outcome, we will apply for RGC and other funding to investigate the effect of different interventions on care recipient outcomes, particularly using the network meta analysis to determine the best available intervention on both caregiver and carge recipient outcomes first. In addition, besides measuring and reporting on programme effectiveness, we also propose to explain why the intervention worked or did not work when applied in different contexts or circumstances through realistic review method. Finally, we want to decide “What intervention works for Hongkongers, under what circumstances, how and why?”

14613416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14613416.value: This research project used high-quality trial data to determine which interventions for caregivers of people with dementia work, for whom and in what circumstances, to alleviate burden and depression in caregivers. We conducted an electronic literature search of Medline, Embase, PsychInfo and CINAHL Plus from their respective inception to Apr 2017. A mixed methods approach was be used, including dual arm and network meta-analysis, systematic review, and realist review. Finally, 72 articles were included in our project. The result suggests that respite care relief is a significant intervention in caregiver burden at post-treatment compared with usual care, and support had the greatest probability for being the best intervention of caregiver burden. While none of the interventions clearly had high efficacy, multicomponent had the greatest probability for being the best intervention option to relieve caregiver depression. There is a considerable heterogeneity in the interventions for caregivers in intervention components, mode of delivery and length or intensity of intervention. Realist review analysis indication that failure to align the intervention with contextual influences, including with local background and with the existing local health care pathway, frequently leads to implementation failure. These results are important in the formulation of intervention.

14613516.value: 一個關於心靈因果性的平行主義進路

14613516.label: Project Objectives
14613516.value: To offer an original and fruitful solution to the exclusion problem by developing a parallelist approach to mental causation. To address possible objections to the parallelist approach and to highlight the theoretical advantages of this approach. To develop a sophisticated counterfactual theory of causation that is suitable for an analysis of mental causation and supervenient causation in general. To distinguish between different versions of the causal completeness of physics and to argue that none of those versions is satisfactory for challenging non-reductive physicalism. To argue against some influential solutions to the exclusion problem, such as the token-identity solution and the overdetermination solution.

14613516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14613516.value: 心靈因果性是人類認知與行動的前提條件。心靈是否（以及如何）具有因果效力是心靈哲學的一個核心問題。根據一個普遍接受的觀點，心理屬性依賴於（但卻不同於）物理屬性。如果是這樣，那麼物理屬性似乎才是產生結果的真正原因——心理屬性的表面上的因果效力其實被它們所依附的物理屬性的因果效力「排除」了。這就是所謂的「排除性問題」——它是對非還原物理主義的一個最爲嚴峻的挑戰。 在這個研究計劃中，我試圖通過復興和發展「平行主義」的理論資源——這一傳統在今天的心靈哲學里消聲匿跡——來解決排除性問題。我提倡的平行主義和傳統的平行主義有兩個重要的區別。第一，我的版本預設了物理主義的框架，而不是反物理主義的立場（比如唯心主義、二元論和中立一元論）。 心物之間的「預定和諧」乃是基於心理-物理的隨附性，而非上帝的意志或任何物理主義不能接受的因素。 第二，傳統的平行主義主張，心理現象只能產生心理現象，而不能產生非心理的現象（比如行為）。但這種理論沒有充分尊重人類的能動性。與之不同，在我的平行主義框架內，心靈可以產生「高階屬性」（如心理屬性、行為屬性和社會屬性）。所以，我的理論能夠更為滿意地捍衛心靈因果性。 根據我的平行主義進路，雖然心理屬性不能是基礎物理屬性的原因，但心理屬性卻可以是高階屬性的原因。這一進路是否可行在很大程度上取決於我們應該如何理解因果關係。然而，關於心靈因果性的文獻卻很少討論是否平行主義能夠爲某些可信的因果理論所支持。我的研究計劃將會深入地討論幾種主要的因果理論，並同時提出一種精緻的反事實因果理論。首先，我的理論採用了一個「因果的雙條件概念」。根據這一概念，A是B的原因當且僅當（1）B的在場依賴于A的在場；以及（2）B的缺席依賴于A的缺席。其次，雖然傳統的反事實因果理論訴諸於「可能世界相似性」的標準，我的因果理論訴諸於「干預主義」的框架——這一框架能夠更好地處理隨附因果性的問題。我將表明，我所採納的因果理論對平行主義提供了一個有力的支持。 此外，我還會論證平行主義的解決方案優於其他解決方案（例如，「殊型同一論」的方案和「過度決定」的方案）。我的研究計劃凸顯了平行主義進路的兩個理論優勢。一方面，這一進路不需要假定一些有爭議的形上學命題，比如心理-物理的過度決定。另一方面，這一進路試圖建立心理「類型」（而非心理「殊型」）的因果效力，因此能夠對心靈因果性給予一個充足的辯護。

14613516.label: Realisation of objectives
14613516.value: The objectives have been completely realized. 1) In the article “Intervention, Fixation, and Supervenient Causation” (forthcoming in Journal of Philosophy, widely regarded as one of two best journals in philosophy), I develop a sophisticated counterfactual theory of supervenient causation. I argue that this theory is better than competing theories (such as Lewis’s counterfactual theory and Woodward’s interventionist theory) in defending mental causation. 2) In the article “Taking Emergentism Seriously” (published in Australasian Journal of Philosophy, widely regarded as a top-ten journal in philosophy) as well as the Journal of Philosophy article, I raise serious challenges to the overdetermination approach, a very influence solution to the exclusion problem. By appeal to the distinction between realization-sensitivity and realization-insensitivity, I argue that the overdetermination solution is too ad hoc to be plausible. 3) In the article “A Parallelist Approach to Mental Causation” (under review in Philosophical Quarterly, widely regarded as a top-ten journal in philosophy), I develop a promising parallelist solution to the exclusion problem and also address some well-known objections to the parallelist approach (such as the downward causation objection). Whereas traditional parallelism, which claims that mental states can only cause other mental states, is unsatisfactory for accommodating human agency, mental causation is better preserved in my parallelist framework, which argues that a mental state can cause higher-level (e.g. mental, behavioral, and social) states even if it fails to cause fundamental physical states. 4) In the article “Three Versions of Causal Closure” (under review in Ratio, widely regarded as a top-twenty journal in philosophy), I distinguish between different versions of the causal closure of physics: a narrow version, a moderate version, and a broad version. I then argue that none of those versions is satisfactory for challenging non-reductive physicalism.
