14634116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14634116.value: Aim: To formulate proposals on the regulatory adjustments necessary for Emissions Trading to be operated successfully in China. Project Background: In 2013 China established seven pilot Emissions Trading Schemes (ETS), with the goal of a national scheme in 2017 to reduce its carbon emissions. In developing its national scheme, China has been inspired by the world’s largest greenhouse gas (GHG) ETS – the European Union ETS. ETS is a market-based “cap and trade” approach to GHG emission reductions: the total amount of authorized emissions of industrial installations are capped and reduced over time, and installations can meet their carbon obligations by trading allowances. In theory, ETSs reduce emissions in a more cost-effective way than “command and control” measures. However, in practice, ETS has yet to demonstrate its effectiveness in stimulating low-carbon investments. Ten-years of emissions trading in the EU have highlighted investors’ reluctance to invest in low-carbon energy solely based on carbon prices – considered too low, volatile and unpredictable. The EU is currently engaged in a structural reform of its ETS to address these concerns. Despite the widespread perception that the EU ETS has failed, China is emulating this scheme. Project Description: This project will reflect critically on the “legal transplant” of the EU ETS “model” to China. Answering this question is essential for evaluating the potential effectiveness of China’s climate policy – particularly the success of its ETS in generating low-carbon investments. Two theoretical strands underpin this project. First, building on the “lesson-drawing” literature, it assesses the lessons to be learnt from the European experience. Second, building on the “legal transplant” literature, it examines whether the EU market-based ETS “model” can successfully be introduced into China, where energy and environmental regulation is still characterized by “command and control”, despite repeated announcements of market reforms. Significance of Project: As the largest single GHG emitter, it is critical to global climate policy that China adopts measures that are effective in reducing emissions. Market-based schemes have great theoretical potential to be both effective and economically efficient, but have disappointed in practice. This project will make recommendations that could enable China to realize the full potential of ETS, and thus contribute to global climate mitigation efforts. This analysis will be of relevance to Hong Kong taking into account opportunities for Hong Kong in the field of carbon finance, and the possible introduction of ETS in Hong Kong itself. 目标：对如何在中国成功得运行碳排放市场交易体系所需要做出的控规调整提出建议 项目背景：中国于2013年启动了七个碳排放交易试点，以期于2017年建立一个全国性的交易体系从而减少二氧化碳的排放量。欧盟碳排放交易体系是世界上规模最大的碳排放交易市场，对中国建立其自己的交易体系影响颇深。碳排放交易体系采用以市场为基准的“总量管制和交易”规则以达到对温室气体排放量的削减：对于工业生产设备的碳排放数量总额加以限制并逐步削减，在该机制下的工业生产部门可以通过对污染物排放许可配额的交易来完成各自的减排任务。理论上来说，碳排放市场交易体系相比“命令和控制”的方法在减排方面具有更高的成本效率。但是，从实践上来说，碳排放市场体系能否有效促进低碳投资仍然不得而知。从欧盟为期十年的碳排放交易经验中来看，由于碳价格的过低，不稳定和难以预估，投资者往往都不愿意对低碳能源进行投资。欧盟正在对碳排放交易体系进行结构性的改革，以期解决这些问题。尽管欧盟的碳排放交易体系的在很多人的眼中是失败的例子，中国仍然在对其进行模范。 项目介绍：该项目将对欧盟碳排放交易模式在中国的法律移植进行批判性的分析。解答该问题对于中国气候政策有效性的评估至关重要，尤其是如何在中国的碳排放交易体系成功开展低碳投资。对此有两种观点值得探究：第一，以一些“经验学习”的文献为基础，考察如何从欧洲实践当中学到经验。第二，从“法律移植”的文献中探究欧盟以市场为基础的碳排放交易体系能否为中国成功借鉴。尽管中国已经反复强调要对市场进行改革，但是目前其在能源和环境领域的管理仍然带有“命令和控制”的特色。 项目意义：作为世界上温室气体排放总量最高的国家，中国能否实施有效的减排措施对于全球气候政策都有至关重要的影响。以市场为基础的交易体系从理论上来说可以很大得发挥作用又兼具经济效率，但在实际应用中却往往不尽如人意。该项目将对如何确保中国在碳排放市场交易体系中发挥所有的潜能提出意见，从而对减缓全球气候变化做出贡献。本文就香港在碳融资领域中如何抓住机遇以及有可能引进的碳排放交易体系也会给出相关讨论。

14634116.label: Realisation of objectives
14634116.value: All objectives of the project have been achieved and, in many ways, overachieved. The interaction between ETS and electricity regulation in China and price stabilisation mechanisms in the Chinese ETS have been studied in detail. The findings of our research have been published in world-leading and high-impact environmental law and climate policy journals (including two papers in Climate Policy - Impact Factor 4.797 - and one paper in the Journal of Environmental Law). We have organised two international conferences that covered the topics of ETS-electricity interaction and price stabilization, and have presented our research at international conferences organised by leading institutions. These events enabled us to have impact by sharing our research with policy-makers in China and the region. 1. The project participants have developed a sophisticated analysis of the interactions of ETS and energy market regulation in China. The main conclusion is that the importance of traditional energy regulation does not mean that the ETS will not contribute to the decarbonisation of China’s energy supply, but the role of the ETS will be different from that in liberalised energy markets (e.g., the EU) where the market is supposed to be the main driver of emission reductions. In China, the role of the ETS will be limited to helping achieve the energy investment targets set under the government’s central planning policy. The analysis was published in a leading law journal - the Journal of Environmental Law (Oxford University Press) - and has already been cited in different academic publications and in reports by international organisations, such as the International Carbon Action Partnership. 2. The project participants proposed specific adjustments to the regulation of ETS in China, to address the constraints of energy market regulation.At the retail level, covering indirect emissions or imposing an additional charge that reflects the allowance price (for large consumers) under the ETS represents a design option that can allow an ETS to pass through the cost of carbon to end-consumers, despite retail price regulation. At the production level, competitive wholesale electricity markets ensure the allowance price is reflected in dispatch decisions, incentivizing investments in low-carbon technologies and closing high-carbon generators. Alternatives to the coordination and incentive role that markets play in delivering low-carbon electricity are limited and inevitably incur efficiency losses. Where an ETS is introduced within the context of a regulated wholesale electricity market, design options that look to ensure the carbon price signal reaches generation as well as consumption decisions are important. In particular, tariff authorities have a crucial role to play in determining the extent to which power producers can recover the cost of carbon through regulated wholesale prices. Tariff authorities will also play a key role in incentivizing low-carbon investments. With the cost-plus method, at least some of the additional cost of purchasing allowances must be kept out of the tariff basis to ensure electricity producers also have an incentive to reduce the carbon intensity of the electricity they supply. With the rate-of-return method, tariff regulators can incentivize power producers to prioritize low-carbon alternatives by including the capital invested in clean projects in the regulated tariff base of utilities. In contrast to the volatility of liberalized electricity markets, regulated price guarantees may provide significant stability to investors, and thereby provide a stable framework for low-carbon investments. Where electricity production is regulated, administrative dispatch could prioritize low-carbon parameters and thus deliver an analogous effect on dispatch that an ETS is designed to deliver. 3. The project participants analysed the stabilisation of carbon prices in China and critically reflected on these mechanisms, based on a comparative analysis with the EU ETS and with the Chinese pilot ETSs. This study has shown that China’s pilot ETSs have incorporated the price stabilization mechanisms examined in the environmental economics and financial market literature. The adoption of these mechanisms reflects the concern of local governments over the impact that exogenous economic developments may have on the carbon price trend and daily price volatility in China. China’s experience can serve as a reference for others in designing ETSs, as concerns about excessive price fluctuation increase together with growing economic uncertainty. Varying market performances help demonstrate the effectiveness of the different price stabilization mechanisms in stabilizing the intrinsic price trend and limiting daily price volatility. The price ceiling–floor and cap-update mechanisms have the most significant effects on intrinsic price trends, as ETS pilots that have properly designed these mechanisms show better performance. Trading risk management measures limit daily volatilities, but with little influence on price trends. Our research contributes to the understanding of the importance of regulatory intervention to manage carbon price instability and volatility. However, we remain cautious about the desirability of regulatory intervention with regard to ETS. Mechanisms that enhance supply flexibility can undermine investors’ expectations and, in some cases, jeopardize the environmental integrity of an ETS. As illustrated by the Chinese experience, without pre-determined rules or trigger conditions, policymakers can interfere with the market at their own discretion. To avoid excessive government intervention, the regulatory design of price stabilization mechanisms must integrate a sufficient degree of transparency and predictability. 4. The PI published two papers on the subject of ETS and energy market regulation in China in two world leading journals: First, “The Role of the Market and Traditional Regulation in Decarbonising China’s Energy Supply” (2018) 30(2) Journal of Environmental Law 261–284 [impact factor: 1.487] Second: "Emissions Trading in Regulated Power Markets" (2019) Climate Policy [impact factor: 4.797] https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/14693062.2019.1682491 5. The PI published two papers on the subject of price stabilisation in the Chinese ETS in world leading journals. First: “Fixing the Emissions Trading Scheme: Carbon Price Stability in the EU and China” (2019) 26 European Law Journal 333-347 [impact factor: 1.81] Second: "Price Stabilization in China's Pilot Emissions Trading Schemes" (2019) Climate Policy [impact factor: 4.797], https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/14693062.2019.1680338 6. 14634116.label: Major findings and research outcome
14634116.value: The introduction of an ETS to decarbonise the Chinese economy faces challenges relating to the tradition of heavy regulation that characterises the functioning of the most carbon-intensive sector – coal-fired electricity production. However, the importance of traditional regulation does not mean that the ETS will not contribute to the decarbonisation of China’s energy supply, but the role of the ETS will be different from that in liberalised energy markets (e.g., the EU) where the market is supposed to be the main driver of emission reductions. In China, the role of the ETS will be limited to helping achieve the energy investment targets set under the government’s central planning policy. Following the experience of high price instability and unpredictability in the European ETS, the management of carbon prices is a key concern for Chinese authorities. The objective is to avoid excessive price volatility in daily trading and stabilize the intrinsic price trend. Building on environmental economics and financial market theories, we reviewed the design of carbon price stabilization mechanisms in China’s seven pilot ETSs and assessed their performance. The pilot ETSs have incorporated most price stabilization mechanisms recommended in the literature, including price ceiling–floor, intensity-based allocation, ex-post adjustment of allowances, intertemporal flexibility, and daily trading risk management. By examining this wide range of mechanisms, our analysis helped understand the different design options available to stabilize carbon prices. Furthermore, by decomposing carbon price data in the different pilot ETSs, our analysis helped evaluate the effectiveness of these mechanisms. Price limits (ceiling–floor) and intertemporal flexibility (update of ETS cap) are the most effective mechanisms for stabilizing the intrinsic price trend. Daily trading risk management mechanisms help control price volatility but have little impact on the intrinsic price trend. However, we are cautious about the desirability of regulatory intervention for influencing carbon market prices. Depending on the institutional context and their design, price stabilization mechanisms can cause regulatory uncertainty.

14634116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14634116.value: To the extent that final end customers are shielded from the allowance (ETS) price through retail electricity price regulation, abatement opportunities in the residential sector will be lost. It is then an empirical question as to how much mitigation potential will be foregone that must be considered against the policy goals of retail price regulation. This is an area where further empirical investigation could be beneficial. With auctioning, pass-through will almost entirely depend on the regulatory decisions of the tariff authorities. With free allocation of allowances, covering indirect emissions or imposing an additional charge that reflects the allowance price (for large consumers) under the ETS represents a design option that can allow an ETS to pass through the cost of carbon to end-consumers, despite retail price regulation. Coverage of indirect emissions has been adopted under the Chinese pilots where electricity prices are subject to various forms of government control. That said there has been little assessment of this design option in terms of its effectiveness in circumnavigating electricity regulation. This is an area that demands attention.

14634116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14634116.value: Emissions Trading Schemes (ETS) are an increasingly common approach to addressing climate change. However, the use of ETS to decarbonise the Chinese economy faces challenges relating to the heavy regulation that characterises the Chinese electricity industry. We argued that, although economic agents are constrained in how they can respond to an ETS through various forms of electricity market regulation, the ETS can be adjusted to the electricity market reality. On this basis, we proposed regulatory alternatives to address the efficiency losses that may emerge from specific forms of power sector regulation. One of the main risks for investors in environmental markets is the high volatility of market prices, combined with the risk of government intervention in the market. We examined the stabilisation of carbon prices in the Chinese ETS and concluded that regulatory adjustments are necessary to address the risk of price instability in China, but more stringent government control over the market exacerbates the threat that price control measures represent to the integrity of the ETS.

14635916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14635916.value: Mangrove forests are ecosystems of considerable ecological, biological and socioeconomic significance as: 1) vital habitats for a wide variety of animal and plants species, 2) important sources of carbon for detritus-based food webs in adjacent coastal waters, 3) a means of reducing the erosion of shorelines, and 4) buffers against the impact of storm waves and floods. However, mangrove forests have been significantly eroded over the past century due to various human activities such as agriculture conversion, urbanization and tourism. Hong Kong benefits from a number of mangrove forests which continue to play important ecological and socioeconomic roles to local communities. Unfortunately, mangrove forests cover has rapidly decreased in the past few decades due to increasing agricultural exploitation and infrastructural development such as new highways and airport as well as associated construction. Given the importance of mangrove forests, timely and accurately monitoring at large scale is imperative for their conservation and restoration. Mangrove forests are usually located in inaccessible regions and often temporarily inundated, which makes it difficult to carry out large-scale and long-term monitoring with traditional field survey approaches. Therefore, satellite techniques have been widely employed for large scale monitoring. However, the coarse spatial and spectral resolution of early satellite imaging restricted the detail and accuracy of the results. With the latest high resolution satellite sensors, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data has been increasingly reported to be sensitive to biomass and structural attributes of vegetation and thus holds great potentials for mangroves monitoring. Nevertheless, the potentials of SAR for discriminating mangrove species are still underexplored, especially with fully polarimetric SAR data. The general aims of this research are to: 1) investigate the comprehensive potentials of multi-frequency polarimetric SAR data with single, dual, compact and full polarizations for improving the discrimination of mangrove species in Hong Kong, and 2) develop effective and efficient methods for synergizing polarimetric SAR data and high resolution optical data at both feature and decision levels. The outcomes of this proposed research will not only include a comprehensive method for investigating a diversity of polarimetric features by evaluating their effectiveness and responses to various mangrove species, but also a general framework for incorporating high resolution optical and multi-frequency polarimetric SAR features for mangrove species discrimination. The implementation of this project can serve as a general model to promote polarimetric SAR techniques for mangrove forests monitoring, and finally, to support the conservation and restoration of mangrove forests. 紅樹林生態系統具有重要的生態、生物和社會經濟意義：1）是多種動植物物種的重要栖息地，2）是周邊沿海水域碎屑食物鏈重要的碳來源，3）是一種减少海岸帶侵蝕的途徑，4）是對抗海嘯和洪水屏障。 然而，在過去的一個世紀裏，紅樹林由于農業轉型，城市化發展和旅游業發展等人類活動已經遭到嚴重侵蝕。香港受益于它至今仍然發揮著重要生態和社會經濟意義的數量可觀的紅樹林濕地。但不幸的是，在過去的幾十年裏，由于農業開墾活動和修建高速公路，機場和其他配套設施等的基礎設施發展活動的增加，紅樹林面積已經急速减少。 鑒于紅樹林的重要性，及時、準確、大範圍的監測對于保護與修復紅樹林而言意義重大。然而，紅樹林多生長于難以進入，會暫時性被淹沒的地區，這增加了實行大範圍和長期進行傳統野外調查監測的難度。幸運的是，衛星技術已經被廣泛地應用于大尺度監測問題上。然而，較早發射衛星較爲粗糙的空間和光譜分辨率限制了結果的細節性和準確度。有著最新的高分辨率傳感器，合成孔徑雷達數據已經被越來越多地表明對于植被生物量和結構特徵上有較高的敏感性，因此對于紅樹林監測應用上具有極大的潜力。然而，對于合成孔徑雷達，尤其是全極化合成孔徑雷達在紅樹林物種識別應用上的潜力還有待被開發。此項研究的目的主要包含全面地探討了多頻極化合成孔徑雷達與單極化、多極化、簡縮極化和全極化合成孔徑雷達在提高香港紅樹林分類精度方面的潜能；同時提出了一種在特徵層和决策層對極化合成孔徑雷達和高分辨光學影像進行融合的有效方法。此外，研究通過計算不同紅樹林樹種的極化特徵幷檢驗其有效性，從而展示了方法的普適性。 最後，研究將提出一個結合高分辨率光學影像的特徵和多頻率極化合成孔徑雷達特徵，幷應用于紅樹林分類的技術框架。該項研究主要用于提高極化合成孔徑雷達在紅樹林監測上應用，爲紅樹林的保護和修復提供支持。

14635916.label: Realisation of objectives
14635916.value: Over the two objectives of the project, all of the scheduled research has been completed. Details of the realisation of the two objectives in this project are as follows: 1) A comprehensive assessment and comparison of textures in the mangrove species discrimination in Mai Po was conducted using Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and Gaussian Markov Random Field (GMRF) to offer a better understanding of their roles in mangrove species discrimination using high-resolution optical satellite data. The experiments were designed to highlight two aspects of textural features - local pattern and textured region size - to assess their effect on mangrove species discrimination based on texture definition. The results indicated that adjusting the textured region size can easily improve texture extraction, and GMRF outperformed GLCM in texture representation of mangrove forest using the same parameters, with an increase in overall accuracy (1.54%, 6.47% and 10.66% on average at three different local pattern sizes). 2) Four dominant native mangrove species in Mai Po were investigated in this study according to the field surveys. Two machine learning methods, Random Forests and Support Vector Machines, were employed to classify mangrove species with Landsat 8, Simulated Hyperion and GF-5 data sets. The results showed that 97 more bands of GF-5 over Hyperion brought a higher over accuracy of 87.12%, in comparison with 86.82% from Hyperion and 73.89% from Landsat 8. The higher spectral resolution of 5 nm in GF-5 was identified as making the major contribution, especially for the mapping of Aegiceras corniculatum. Therefore, GF-5 is likely to improve the classification accuracy of mangrove species mapping via enhancing spectral resolution and thus has promising potential to improve mangrove monitoring at species level to support mangrove management. 3) Three different combinations of optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) datasets were designed fromWorldview-3 and Radarsat-2 data to classify four mangrove species in Mai Po, Kandelia obovate (KO), Avicennia marina (AM), Acanthus ilicifolius (AI) and Aegiceras corniculatum (AC). Then, the Rotation Forest (RoF) method was employed to classify the four mangrove species. Results indicated the benefits of dual polarimetric SAR data with an improvement of accuracy by 2–3%, which can be useful for more accurate large-scale mapping of mangrove species. Moreover, the difficulty of classifying different mangrove species, in order of increasing difficulty, was identified as KO < AM < AI < AC. Dual polarimetric SAR data are recognized to improve the classification of AI and AC species. Although this improvement is not remarkable, it is consistent for all three methods. The improvement can be particularly important for large-scale mapping of mangrove forest at the species level. These findings also provide useful guidance for future studies using multi-source satellite data for mangrove monitoring and conservation. 4) A polarimetric SAR feature was analyzed to discriminate among different mangrove species in Mai Po. This feature, which is related to the Wishart distance, maximizes the contrast among mangrove species optimizing the ratio between quadratic forms. The discrimination performance is assessed both against ground truth and by inter-comparing it with conventional model-based decomposition feature. Results, obtained by processing actual L- and C-band full-polarimetric (FP) SAR scenes collected by ALOS- PALSAR-2 and RADARSAT-2 missions, show that the proposed approach achieves accurate enough discrimination performance to differentiate two out of the four mangrove species. In addition, results suggest using multi-frequency SAR data in C- and L- bands to maximize discrimination performance among the four dominant species in Mai Po.

14635916.label: Major findings and research outcome
14635916.value: The research team has established conducted multiple research on the mangrove species discrimination in Mai Po Nature Reserve (MPNR) of Hong Kong, using various high resolution optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite images. The dominant mangrove species in MPNR have been analyzed in our studies. First, a comprehensive assessment and comparison of textures in the mangrove species discrimination in Mai Po was conducted using Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) and Gaussian Markov Random Field (GMRF) for high-resolution optical satellite data. The results indicated that adjusting the textured region size can easily improve texture extraction, and GMRF outperformed GLCM in texture representation of mangrove forest using the same parameters, with an increase in overall accuracy (Wan et al., 2018). The methods were further applied to investigate the time-series changes of mangroves in Mai Po and in the Philippines (Liu et al., 2018; Buitre et al., 2019). Second, two machine learning methods, Random Forests and Support Vector Machines, were employed to classify mangrove species with Landsat 8, simulated Hyperion and GF-5 data. The results showed that the higher spectral resolution of 5 nm in GF-5 was identified as making the major contribution, especially for the mapping of Aegiceras corniculatum. Therefore, GF-5 is likely to improve the classification accuracy of mangrove species mapping via enhancing spectral resolution and thus has promising potential to improve mangrove monitoring at species level to support mangrove management (Wan et al., 2020a). In addition, the deep learning network was further employed to identify both the native and exotic mangrove species in Mai Po (Wan et al., 2019; Wan et al., 2020b). Third, the Rotation Forest (RoF) method was employed to classify the four mangrove species. Results indicated the benefits of dual polarimetric SAR data with an improvement of accuracy by 2–3%. Moreover, the difficulty of classifying different mangrove species, in order of increasing difficulty, was identified as KO < AM < AI < AC. Dual polarimetric SAR data are recognized to improve the classification of AI and AC species. Although this improvement is not remarkable, it is consistent for all three methods. The improvement can be particularly important for large-scale mapping of mangrove forest at the species level. These findings also provide useful guidance for future studies using multi-source satellite data for mangrove monitoring and conservation (Zhang et al., 2018). Fourth, a polarimetric SAR feature was analyzed to discriminate among different mangrove species in Mai Po. Results, obtained by processing actual L- and C-band full-polarimetric (FP) SAR scenes collected by ALOS- PALSAR-2 and RADARSAT-2 missions, show that the proposed approach achieves accurate enough discrimination performance to differentiate two out of the four mangrove species. In addition, results suggest using multi-frequency SAR data in C- and L- bands to maximize discrimination performance among the four dominant species in Mai Po (Ferrentino et al., 2020).

14635916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14635916.value: The general aims of this research are to investigate the full potential of multi-polarimetric SAR data for improving mangrove species discrimination, with a study area in Mai Po Nature Reserve (MPNR), Hong Kong, and to develop effective methods for combing optical and polarimetric SAR data. Both the research objectives have been achieved during the past two and half years. Great potential for further development goes to the applications of the proposed methodology for monitoring the mangrove species beyond MPNR, from the local Hong Kong, to the whole China, and even to the mangrove in other tropical countries. Another great potential goes to the application of mangrove dynamics investigation at the species level for better understanding their ecological functions and services.

14635916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14635916.value: The research team has established conducted multiple research on the mangrove species discrimination in Mai Po Nature Reserve (MPNR) of Hong Kong, using various high resolution optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite images. Four dominant mangrove species, Kandelia obovate (KO), Avicennia marina (AM), Acanthus ilicifolius (AI) and Aegiceras corniculatum (AC), in MPNR have been analyzed in detail. We found that 1) adjusting the textured region size can easily improve texture extraction from high resolution optical images to obtain an increase in overall accuracy; 2) the high spectral resolution of 5 nm in the hyperspectral satellite GF-5 images was able to make a good contribution for mangrove species identification, especially for the species AC; 3) the difficulty of classifying different mangrove species, in order of increasing difficulty, was identified as KO < AM < AI < AC. Dual polarimetric SAR data (Radarsat 2) are recognized to improve the classification of AI and AC species; 4) multi-frequency SAR data in C- and L- bands was found to maximize discrimination performance among the four dominant species in MPNR.

14636616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14636616.value: Since 1757, all foreign trade in China was confined to one city, Canton (Guangzhou). The so-called Canton System, under which the Westerners could only trade with a small group of licensed Hong merchants, lasted for almost one century until the conclusion of the Treaty of Nanking in 1842 after the First Opium War. Foreign traders suffered from financial exploitations and at the same time were submitted to strict rules of conducts. To the British, the situation turned acute with the end of trade monopoly of the East India Company in China in 1834 because national honour was at stake when the Superintendent of Trade, representing the British government, was sent to China to handle all British nationals and trade matters. Historians generally agree that the Canton System was one of the contributing factors to the British declaration of war in 1840. Because of its importance, there are some significant studies on the Canton system, mostly as a political or commercial history topic. Unfortunately one important aspect of the system, communication between the foreign traders and the Chinese authorities, has largely been neglected. For a long time, serious language problems hindered effective communication. Translation and interpreting services were supplied by the linguists (tongshi 通事) from the Chinese side, who were linguistically incompetent and ethically unworthy. On the other hand, the British were not able to train up their own translators until the 1810s. But communication problems persisted because the Chinese authorities refused to deal directly with the British translators, whose proficiency in the Chinese language was often doubtful. As a result, a serious problem in the Canton System was communication, and we see in both English and Chinese records many complaints about poor translations. The present project studies the communication and translation problems in the Canton System before the Opium War. By collecting and digging into the huge volume of first hand materials, it examines the causes as well as the impact for the lack of effective communication. It will explain the backgrounds and constraints of the translators of both sides; analyze the mistakes, deliberately made or not, found in the translations of the exchanges; and determine the implications and consequence on subsequent historical developments of such mistakes. By working out the role of translation in the operation of the Canton System, we will be able to have a more accurate and comprehensive understanding of Sino-British relations in the pre-Opium war period. 本項目旨在研究18世紀中葉以後至19世紀鴉片戰爭前所謂廣州貿易體制下出現的翻譯現象及問題，重點探究當時中英交往過程中所面對的語言障礙、雙方的應對手法，以至由此而引起種種深遠的歷史影響。 有清一代自乾隆中葉以後規限所有外國貿易只可在廣州一口進行，並為有效管理，朝廷陸續頒下各種“制夷＂方案，對外國商人實施諸多限制，除規定只能與特定“行商＂進行買賣外，其他不少人身自由也受到約束，惹來嚴重不滿。1834年，東印東公司在華貿易壟斷權結束，英國政府首次派來駐華商務監督，問題變得更複雜，原來的商務問題跟英國的國家榮耀扯上關係。1840年，英國發動戰爭，他們所持一個主要理由就是英國國家利益及榮耀在廣州貿易體制下受到傷害。第一次鴉片戰爭後中英所簽署〈南京條約〉，開放五口通商，廣州貿易體制才告結束。 由於這維持長達差不多一百年的廣州貿易體制在近代中外交往史上佔有極其重要的位置，引起不少學者的關注，但長期忽略的是當中所涉及的翻譯問題。中英雙方要有效溝通，除政治體制及文化差異外，語言障礙毫無疑問是關鍵所在。但當時幾乎完全沒有精通中英雙語的人才。傳統以來，中國政府及官員輕視譯者，甚至視之為漢奸，不可能有優秀的翻譯人員，惟有依賴只懂略說“廣州式英語＂、但不能閱讀書寫英文的“通事＂；另一方面，儘管東印度公司曾嘗試培養中文人才，但由於種種限制，包括一般中國人不能向西方人教授中文，東印度公司要待到19世紀初新教傳教士馬禮遜獲聘為譯員，並開設中文班後，情況才有改善。然而，長期以來，語言及翻譯問題嚴重地影響了雙方的有效溝通，以致在商貿及政治上的矛盾越見深化。 本項目通過搜集、整理及分析第一手原始資料（主要為東印度公司、英國外交部檔案以及廣州十三行檔案等），深入探討在18至19世紀中葉鴉片戰爭前廣州貿易體制下出現的各種翻譯現象及問題，當中包括雙方所聘用的譯員背景、能力及行徑、重大歷史事件中的翻譯問題、兩國政府如何看待語言及翻譯問題、以至翻譯上的失誤如何影響歷史發展等，期望能對18-19世紀中英關係研究有所貢獻。

14636616.label: Realisation of objectives
14636616.value: Overall speaking, it was a very satisfying and rewarding experience in conducting the project. The PI has successfully mapped out the important roles played by translation in the daily operation of the Canton System. Most of the relevant materials were collected and studied, several case studies were completed, and some papers were published. For Objective 1, the collection of research materials, it is a pity that it cannot be described as 100 per cent accomplished. The PI is fully aware of the importance of historical materials for a historical project of this kind. Great efforts were made to exhaust all relevant materials, locally and outside Hong Kong. However, some unexpected and irresistible factors have hindered a smooth completion of the task. First, the social instability in Hong Kong in the second half of 2019 has caused some inconvenience in searching archival collections in local libraries. Then from February 2020, we have been badly hit by the COVID-19 pandemic. We (in particular my research assistant) had to work from home and there was no way for us to go to libraries. Most disappointingly, I had to cancel my trip to London and Cambridge for the important materials of the East India Company in the British Library and the Jardine-Matheson Archives at the Cambridge University Library. The original plan was to make a longer stay in the UK in the first half of 2020, when I had no teaching. It was for this reason that I applied for an extension of 6 months for the project. Unfortunately this plan could not be realized. Nevertheless, the negative impact was not as serious as expected. With the generous permission of Professor Paul Van Dyke of the Sun Yat-sen University, I was able to copy a large volume of archival documents of the East India Company Office Records (IOR) that had not been digitized by Adam Mathews (my original plan was to copy them from the British Library). Moreover, Professor Van Dyke has kindly allowed me to make use of the index of IOR that he compiled over a period of 20 years to search for entries in the Records related to translation. I used the names of the translators and several major events involving translation for keyword search. It saved me a lot of time and generated very fruitful results. I would like to register my sincerest thanks to Professor Van Dyke here. Less satisfactory is that I could not consult the Jardine-Matheson Archives of the Cambridge University, which has not been available electronically. As I could not make a trip to Cambridge, I had to count on the edited volume compiled by Alain Le Pichon, China and Trade and Empire: Jardine, Matheson & Co. and the Origins of British Rule in Hong Kong, 1827-1843 (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2006). It covers roughly the latter part of the project period; but its focus is not on the Canton System, not to say that only a small percentage of the entire collection is represented. For this reason, I could only say that for Objective 1, 90% has been achieved. I sincerely hope that when the pandemic is over and I can travel again, I will do a thorough search of the archive. Fortunately, I was able to make one trip to London on 12-22 August 2017, and another to Guangzhou on 24-26 March 2019. The trip to London was reported in the mid-term report, so I would just make a very brief recap here. During the ten day trip, I conducted research at the National Archives, British Library, and the archive of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland at London. For the Guangzhou trip, I visited the two key units in China that focus their research on the Canton System: the Key Research Base for the Treaty Port History of Guangzhou, Sun Yat-sen Uinversity中山大學廣州口岸史重點研究基地; and the Archival and Research Centre for the Hong Merchants, Guangzhou University廣州大學十三行研究中心. I consulted their library collections as well as some private collections of individual scholars, such as and in particular Professor Paul Van Dyke. Prof. Ye Aiyun of Guangzhou University was also very helpful. She shared with me some Chinese materials on Canton trade in the 17-19th centuries from the Foreign Office Records, UK. Both trips were very fruitful. While Objective 1, to collect relevant research materials, was important, the more demanding tasks were to study and analyse them in order to accomplish Objectives 2-4. Basically I can confidently say that I have been able to achieve the three objectives. The first thing done was to sort out and identify any relevant information on translation. This was not an easy task because the volume was huge, and all the materials were handwritten, and there were many very blurred images. It took great efforts and time to decipher them. In the Canton system, translation played a critical role in its daily operation, because the parties involved (the Western traders, the Chinese merchants, the Chinese officials) spoke different languages. By digging into firsthand materials, I worked on several representative cases. One particular case is the Macartney Mission. Almost all studies on this first official embassy sent by Britain to China pay attention to what happened at Beijing and Rehe, but in fact many of the issues first emerged in Guangzhou. An article I published for the present project is about the translation issues concerning the letter sent by the Director of the East India Company to the Viceroy of Guangdong announcing the dispatch of the embassy. It examines how the limited resources available to both the Chinese authorities and the British traders hindered effective communication. Another case is about Britain’s first Sinologist, George Thomas Staunton. Although he first started to learn Chinese during his trip from Britain to China in the Macartney mission, his proficiency in the language was greatly enhanced during his Guangzhou days as a writer of the East India Company. His appointment as the translator of the Company put him in the forefront in the negotiations, hence conflicts, with the Guangzhou authorities. These two cases, together with the ones on Li Yao and Thomas Manning, demonstrate most conspicuously translations and mistranslations made great impact in different ways on the development of historical events, big or small. As Guangzhou was the only Chinese port opened to foreign trade before the signing of the Treaty of Nanking in 1842, studying the translation issues in the Canton System will be fundamental in our understanding of the role played by translation in Sino-Western relations before the Opium War. It was with this conception that Objective 4 was drawn up. With the several case studies, I demonstrate that more studies on Sino-Western relations should be made from the perspective of translation history, a task that the PI will continue to work on.

14636616.label: Major findings and research outcome
14636616.value: Several case studies were done for the project with important findings. The first one, about the Macartney Mission, would hopefully make strong academic impact, because although there are some studies on the Mission, no research has paid serious attention to the role of translation. In 2009 and 2013, I published a few articles on some translation issues involving the Macartney Mission. With the new materials available from the present project, I revisited the project and wrote up a couple of new articles. By highlighting the distortions of meanings through mistranslating the originals, my papers explain more convincingly why the Mission failed. The paper on Li Yao is one of the very few studies on the tongshi (linguists/interpreters) of the Canton System. While it has generally been acknowledged that they were instrumental in the daily operation of the Canton System, the topic has been under-researched because very little information is available. I made use of the Foreign Office Records of the National Archives, mainly FO 1048, as well as the India Office Records, to study the case of Li Yao to expose how the linguists worked under insurmountable pressure from both the Chinese and the British. It lays the foundation for further research of this special group of people of the Canton System. On the other hand, the papers on George Thomas Staunton and Thomas Manning look at the interpreters of the British side. Expectedly, they tell different stories. One focus of my research is on the constraints for them to fight for the best interests of the British under the Imperial rule of China. Another very interesting angle is to find out how they acquired the Chinese language and culture, and determine how good their Chinese were. For the project, a total of six articles are published. A book manuscript on the translation issues of the Macartney Embassy, with a total of 350000 words, has recently been submitted to Chinese University Press for external review; and at least one and a half chapters are directly related to the Canton System.

14636616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14636616.value: While the present project has laid a solid foundation for the understanding of the role played by translation in the Canton System, more case studies on individual interpreters from both sides as well as on important historical events involving translation should be carried out. One valuable direction is to examine how the British trained their own interpreters and how these interpreters coped with the situation and met the demand for communication. Another group of people worthy of academic attention is the Chinese assistants employed full time or part time by the British to assist them for communication with the Chinese authorities. They are seriously under-researched because very limited relevant materials are available. While they were trusted and valued by the British, the Chinese authorities saw them as “traitors” (hanjian) as they were too close to the foreign barbarians. In fact, in those days, not only those employed by the British were seriously discriminated, even the linguists in general were often taken as hanjian. The “hanjian” issue in Chinese translation history is definitely another important question deserves in-depth research.

14636616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14636616.value: With several representative case studies, the project demonstrates the important role played by translation in the operation of the Canton System before the Opium War. The translation of the letter from the East India Company to the Chinese authorities in Guangzhou announcing the Macartney Mission exposed the serious problems of communication. Without qualified translators, plus the imbalanced power relationship between the translators and the officials, the message from the British was heavily distorted, depicting the embassy as a tributary mission from a far-away barbarian state. The case on the linguist (interpreter) Li Yao was also illuminating. Exiled to Xinjiang, his story confirms that any Chinese working too closely with the British was dangerous. Both cases demonstrate the complex and difficult situation for effective communication in the Canton System. The studies on George Thomas Stanton and Thomas Manning show how the British attempted to train up their own interpreters in Guangzhou. The project is significant because Guangzhou was the only Chinese port opened to foreign trade before the Treaty of Nanking in 1842. Studying the translation issues in the Canton System will be fundamental in our understanding of the role played by translation in Sino-Western relations.

14637516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14637516.value: 規劃中的環境語言：走向一種針對中國内陸城市的尺度化話語分析

14637516.label: Project Objectives
14637516.value: To discover the changing environmental discourses in China’s urban planning regime in general, and in inland cities in particular. To explore forces at multiple geographical scales, which shape the inclusion or exclusion of particular environmental discourses in planning; that is, to understand how political actors and their respective agents make sense of environmental phenomena rather than merely the urgency of those phenomena, and to review what political projects and initiatives they use in pursuit of their agendas. To discern how political actors acquire persuasive power by deploying scale to legitimize their political projects and initiatives and to frame how the world should be viewed. This objective, together with the one mentioned in Point 2, will contribute to our understanding of both material production and the epistemological construction of scale. To refine and advance the ‘scaled discourse analysis’ as a theoretical construct to ‘denaturalize’ the prevailing technically oriented view of environmental discourses and to acknowledge the social construction of both ‘scale and discourse’. To critically analyze and evaluate the discursive process of planning regarding environmental governance and to make recommendations on how urban planning can be improved to make it more environmentally friendly.

14637516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14637516.value: 本研究特別針對中國内陸城市規劃中的環境話語。 研究背景：中國環境問題正快速演變成一場危機。在經濟飛速發展的同時，各種環境問題惡化，政府官員難以應對。落後的内陸地區更是如此。這些地方在國家西部大開發的驅動下正全速制訂經濟趕超政策，對本已極度脆弱的生態系統帶來壓力。很多内陸城市面對一種真實的政策困境：提高收入的同時需治理環境損害。這種情況為城市規劃帶來巨大壓力，因爲城市規劃是調節不同城市空間需求的主要政策工具。 實際上，過去三十年，城市規劃中的環境話語呈爆炸式增長，有諸如氣候變化和全球暖化等世界上十分流行的術語，也有諸如生態城市和海綿城市等地方實踐性詞彙。雖然這種詞彙的增長也許顯示了政府對環境問題意識的覺醒，但絕不能説明中國城市規劃已經在生態保護方面起決定作用。發展生態城市、避開生態敏感區等理念與作爲推動經濟繁榮重要工具的規劃觀念之間常常充滿矛盾。學者們開始重視政策話語與實施差異的研究，他們提出過富有創見性的理論觀點。但是，現有研究有明顯的理論缺陷，這主要表現在三方面。其一，這些研究偏向技術方法，忽略話語的社會建構性。其二，它們缺乏尺度視角，忽略話語建構的多尺度動因。其三，它們常常以偏概全，用沿海地區的案例總結出全中國適用的理論。 研究簡介：本研究旨在填補這些學術方法的缺陷。理論方面，本研究將採用尺度化話語分析方法來解析那些用來技術性地描述地方環境問題或應對上級要求的話語。爲此，我將結合政治經濟學和后結構主義的觀點，提出一種更爲全面的研究方法，探討如何理解規劃中環境話語在尺度方面的實體建構和認識論建構。實證方面，本研究選取貴州省的三個城市作爲案例，分析城市總體規劃中環境話語的納入和排除過程。主要看兩個方面。第一個方面是話語制訂過程中所涉及的尺度建構，探究不同尺度主體如何應用政治手段和策略影響並控制規劃中環境治理的尺度關係。第二個方面是尺度的認識論建構，即不同主體如何策略性地應用尺度話語來合理化他們的社會實踐。 研究意義：研究成果將對政策制訂產生重要影響，有助於決定如何更好地將環境理念融入中國特別是内陸地區的規劃實踐中。

14637516.value: The COVID-19 outbreak has affected the research plan. Due to cross-border travel restrictions, the team was not able to conduct follow-up fieldwork proposed when applying for project extension. However, during the first three years after the project commenced, the team conducted six rounds of fieldtrip to Guizhou to collect a comprehensive dataset, covering over 60 in-depth interviews, 100 pages of notes, hundreds of photos, rich audio data, and numerous site visits. Thus, the team has been able to generally achieve the five stated objectives. First, the team has fully discovered the changing environmental discourses in China’s planning in general and in inland cities in particular. In a general sense, the first three decades of post-1949 China were under the influence of Mao Zedong’s oppositional thesis on the human–nature relationship. Environment was at the time treated primarily as a barrier to be conquered for socialist industrialisation. Urban planning was required to transform nature to provide right land plots for industrial projects in economic plans, while paying little attention to local environmental specificities and spatial coordination. In a more specific terms, the team has identified the following:  In the 1980s, urban environment was primarily defined as ‘problems’, which could be rectified within the basic framework of administrative structure. Therefore, state institutions and practices were considerably enlarged to eliminate environmental problems.  In the early 1990s, the environmental discourses in planning were destabilised because of the growing top-down environmental regulation and the strong local desire for expansion. The powerful economic imperative and the eagerness for land were deeply ingrained in the political reality of Chinese cities, resulting in a policy process that astutely assimilated environmental concerns. The environmental discourses were used as a political tool to rationalise planning decisions.  Since the mid-1990s, there has been a growing domestic environmental awareness. It was a period when China engrossed in an urgent backyard problem – dwindling domestic supply of natural resources. As resource shortages posed direct constraints to production expansion, an unprecedented eagerness to unify the economic and the environmental systems was garnered in Chinese leadership. ‘Circular economy’ was proposed by top central leaders, under which the conventional ‘takemake-waste’ production model is replaced with one emphasising waste recovery and resource efficiency. The emerging environmental discourses at the central scale were ‘ecology/ecological’, efficiency of [resource use]’, ‘water-saving’ and ‘energy-saving’;  In the 2000s, natural hazards such as the Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008 stimulate an escalating concern on environmental risks. Pressure is mounting for urban governments to seriously think of quality environment as a precursor of social stability and city security apart from as an apparatus of city growth. Terms such as climate risk and security were added to the league of prevailing environmental discourses.  Since 2012, we have witnessed an unprecedented effort to promote ecological civilization (EC). There has been an effort to moving EC beyond a theoretical cliché to codifying the term as China’s long-term development approach through injecting environmental awareness into almost every political and economic domain, with Chinese characteristics. Such effort reached a climax when President Xi announced in 2020 that China would strive to be ‘carbon neutral’ by 2060. The research shows that EC and carbon neutral have been predominate environmental discourses in China’s planning regime. Second, the research team has thoroughly explored how inland cities’ local political actors and their respective agents make sense of environmental phenomena. Like their coastal counterparts, inland cities have also strategically selected environmental discourses to be included in their planning documents. The inclusion of these discourses depends on how the local political regime makes sense of an environmental and/or economic phenomenon rather than simply the urgency of local environmental problems. This is exemplified by the three cities under investigation in Guizhou. The inclusion of particular environmental discourses in the three cities is a result of a strategic selection of local governments for various political agenda - local governments have (re)framed their environmental problems in particular ways to selectively privilege certain discourses to serve their specific needs. Third, the research team has systematically argued with ample evidence that scalar struggle is a constant within cities’ rapid changes in leadership, with scale being a versatile category which can be instrumentalised in a variety of discursive and material ways. The team has set apart different functional forms of scalar discourses as well as different ways to engage with material scales, thereby offering a more systematic account of the scalar leaps of cities under investigation. We argue that although the degree to which inherited scalar structures are subject to transformation through emergent social and political projects is an empirical question, it is necessary to generalise how scalar politics is played out to avoid our analytical accounts from simply replicating the empirical messiness of scales, whether as discursive instruments or material expressions of power. Fourth, the research team has successfully refined and advanced the ‘scaled discourse analysis’ as a theoretical construct. Echoing a growing rank of scholars, the team contends that studies of the political significance of scale should neither be limited to its material existence as institutionalised socio-spatial structures and practices attributing authority to some interests over others, nor its discursive role in casting different lights on how we should perceive and organise space and society, but draw attention to the dialectical relations of these two moments of scale. While existing works primarily addressed this dialectic at an abstract level, the team has elucidated a framework to analyse it in concrete-complex terms, paying attention to two material aspects of the deployment of scalar discourses. The first aspect is material scalar functions, i.e. the different ways scale is evoked to frame people’s actions in and explanations of reality. The second aspect is material scalar conditions, i.e. the different ways scalar discourses engage with existing scalar structures to exploit the opportunities such structures offer and circumvent the accompanying constraints. Finally, after critically analyzing and evaluating the discursive process of spatial planning regarding environmental governance, the research team has identified two policy implications. For local governments in inland cities, it is possible to achieve a win-win situation, i.e. meeting the central government’s environmental imperatives while guaranteeing local growth, by maneuvering the discursive forces of scale. One example is how Guiyang has skillfully rallied the ‘global’ as a powerful discursive vehicle to elevate its position in the global urban hierarchy, and give its emerging convention and exhibition economy and big data economy a boost. For the central government, it is important to note that the local pursue for ecological civilization has alterative agenda. When the spatial planning power is fragmented among line ministries which can make different spatial plans to safeguard their vested interests, local governments can easily exploit gaps between these plans to advance their projects. This is exemplified by case cities’ efforts to propose urban expansion by using ‘local’ as a scalar focus to take advantage of development trajectories outlined in local socioeconomic plans despite their limited land resources. This situation calls for a relatively centralized spatial planning system to insert environmental care into all domains of political and economic life. China’s spatial planning reform in 2018 to consolidate all planning powers to one central ministry is a direction aligning with the policy implication arising from this project.

14637516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14637516.value: The research has produced important findings. The existing literature has widely acknowledged that urban green governance is selective and rooted in the scalar reorganisation of state regulation. Much attention is on how the central government has downscaled state economic and environmental responsibilities, challenging local growth regimes to juggle their economic objectives with environmental imperatives. Much less attention is on the agency of local actors. This research has found that local governments are indeed very active in strategising, rather than taking for granted, the multi-scalar regulatory context in which they are situated to negotiate their economic and environmental priorities. Their ways to strategise the multi-scalar regulatory context take different forms, depending on their cities’ historical specificities and positions in multi-scalar economic landscapes. The research has also been situated in Guizhou’s emerging development issues. Recently, impressive local GDP growth has been fuelled by significant local government borrowing. Yet, the pressure for higher economic growth to finance the debt has not reversed the desire for urban greening. Cities in Guizhou have introduced a ‘smart green deal’ based on the emerging big data sector, involving the storage, processing and application of large and complex datasets. They promoted Guizhou as an environmentally ideal site for the sector. Such sustained effort to align local economy materially and discursively with the environment reflects the unprecedented significance of environmental issues in the institutional structure of the Chinese state under a central government aggressively reasserting its helm. More importantly, it testifies yet again the salience of scalar politics in today’s urban politics. In a numerical term, though the project has been completed in terms of RGC funding support, the team is still continuing relevant research activities. They have completed two English papers. One paper is published by a top-notch journal, and the other is under review by another top-notch journal. They are preparing and will prepare other papers to be sent out for review by top journals. The team has also presented research findings in six international conferences and other workshops and seminar series. Research findings have inspired the team to prepare two other GRF proposals and they have successfully secured the funding for both (see 6.2 for details). The PI has established collaboration with the Guizhou Normal University (GNU) in both research and teaching domains. For research, a GNU professor has involved in the two new GRF projects. For teaching, the PI’s department and GNU will jointly develop an undergraduate fieldtrip programme, based on data arising from this project.

14637516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14637516.value: With knowledge arising from this project, the research team has successfully secured other two GRF projects. One is entitled ‘More data, better governance? The central-local politics of environmental data in China’. With Guiyang as one case study site, this project examines the politics of environmental data (centred upon the environmental protection system of the Chinese state). The other is entitled ‘Big data for big land grab? A discursive–material nexus analysis of big data-themed land development in China’s inland Data Valley’. This is a project with a focus on Guizhou’s big data sector to investigate how big data-themed initiatives succeed in obtaining land through a combination of discursive and material endeavours. The three GRF projects including this one have provided essential funding for us to study inland Chinese cities, which are still systematically unexplored. In the future, we may propose to compare the development courses in coastal cities and inland cities for a more nuanced understanding of China’s urban development.

14637516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14637516.value: This research is to answer an intriguing question on urban development of China’s inland region with Guizhou as an example. Guizhou is a province of economic backwater with highly vulnerable eco-systems and limited land resources. Yet, its many cities have planned extravagant urban expansion. How can they succeed in doing this in a land-scarce context with a tight top-down environmental regulation? Answering this question requires us to assess how cities interpret environmental issues to satisfy both ecological imperatives and economic take-off. Our research finds that cities have taken advantage of ‘scale’ as a powerful tool to promote their goals in two ways. One is to invent political projects to advance their positions in the hierarchical (i.e. scaled) institutional structure. For instance, Guiyang has upscaled its eco-forum from a local fair to an international expo, giving the city more political leverage in bargaining for its big data industries. The other way is to deploy ‘scale’ as a discourse to justify their proposals. One example is the use of ‘regional scale’ by Guiyang to affirm the city’s role as a regional economic hub to legitimize its planned expansion. We can draw on these findings to recommend ways to improve China’s spatial planning.

14639016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14639016.value: Dementia has developed into a full-blown global epidemic. Support from family caregivers of persons with dementia (PWDs) is a crucial buffer for the associated disease burden on society. However, they are providing care at the cost of role stress, psychological burden and social isolation, and resulted in high prevalence of physical and mental morbidities. Family caregivers of PWDs are always referred to “the invisible second patients” whose jeopardized health could greatly affect the quality and sustainability of this important informal care. Recently, substantial research evidence has identified the positive relationships between sense of coherence and health status of family caregivers of PWD. Sense of coherence is an inner strength representing the extent one views a given life situation as structured, predictable and manageable. Effective coping was found to mediate such positive relationship. However, no study has attempted to enhance SOC and thereby health outcomes of family caregivers of PWDs. This study has adopted the Antonovsky’s theory of saluotogenesis to develop a strengths-based intervention for family caregivers of PWDs, and aims to i) identify the effects of this strengths-based intervention on caregiving burden, depression and HRQL of family caregivers of PWD, ii) examine whether the health-enhancing effects of strength-based intervention are mediated through an increase in SOC and effective coping and, iii) explore the family caregivers’ perception of the intervention. This sequential mixed-method study consists of a double-blind randomised controlled trial and a descriptive qualitative study. A group of 372 family caregivers, who co-reside with and provide care for PWDs for≥ 4 hrs/ day, will be recruited from eight elderly community centres. They will be randomly assigned to receive the strength-based intervention or basic education on dementia care. Outcome evaluation will be done at baseline, 14 weeks and 22 weeks with validated measures. Advanced statistics will be used to compare the changes in outcomes between the two study arms, and to test the mediators (i.e., SOC and coping) for the health-enhancing effect of the strengths-based intervention. A subsample of 30 caregivers from the strengths-based intervention group will be interviewed for their perceptions of the intervention. This study marks the first attempt to improve the health of family caregivers of PWDs by using a strength-based intervention. The findings may i) advance the understanding of the theory of saluotogenesis, ii) inform the health-benefits of strengths-based interventions to family caregivers of PWDs, and thus, iii) provide new strategic direction to support family caregiving.

14639016.label: Realisation of objectives
14639016.value: The three research objectives were fully achieved. Subject recruitment Subject recruitment took place from May 2017 to Aug 2019 from 24 elderly community centers operated by 12 NGO in Hong Kong. Of 433 invited eligible family caregivers, 350 consented to participate [mean age: 64.9 (SD=12.1)]. There was quite even distribution of spousal (47.7%) and child (47.6%) caregivers, but the sample was biased towards female (84.6%). The caregiving duration ranged from 1-8 years, and majority of the care recipients (67.7%) were in mild to moderate dementia. Randomization successfully balanced the demographic and outcome characteristics between the two study groups. Implementation of the strength-based intervention We have delivered the strength-based interventions to 29 groups of caregivers (n=5-6/ group) and the educative interventions to another 31 groups of similar group size. For both interventions, the program team has developed an implementation protocol, comprising detail session plan, training materials in form of PowerPoint slides, worksheets, and toolkits to enhance the intervention fidelity. For the strength-based intervention, a workbook was developed to enable the caregivers to build a personalized caregiving roadmap while engaging in the externalizing conversation. Specifically, they used the metaphor representing the more vulnerable current condition as the starting point and the metaphor for the most desirable situation, where the problems gone, as the destination. We assimilated the input from the Program as the fuel enabling the caregivers to get to the destination. The fuels consists of i) the strengths of the caregivers as identified through the analytic dialogue using re-authoring conversation, ii) the successful caregiving experience from the peers, and the iii) empowerment-based training. The workbook also enables an easy documentation of the goal-oriented action planning to guide the behavioral changes. The PI reviewed the audio-taped training content for a total of 12 group and no significant deviation from the protocol was noted. The reflective note prepared by the RAs after each training session also indicated the good acceptance of the interventions by the participants. Even though the overall strength-based intervention consisted of 14 in-hall group sessions, the attendance rate was a high as 90.2%, which was very comparable with the education group (89.3%). The family caregivers, in general, had very good participation in the sessions after the initial ice-breaking in the first few sessions. Echo with the qualitative data (please refer to the last paragraph), the observation indicated the caregivers had very strong needs to make the self-disclosure when facilitated by the narrative strategies. They were highly receptive to the empowerment-based training and had implemented the action plan. Even though the goal attainment in some cases was affected by unanticipated changes in the dementia manifestation, family caregivers were well engaged in the partnership relationship with the peers and interveners in overcoming the corresponding barriers. Data collection and analysis Data collection by face-to-face interview went smoothly. The attrition rate is about 22.3%, mainly due to the competing caregiving roles. To respond to this situation, the research team has solicited manpower resource to provide respite service when the caregivers were attending either the strength-based or education intervention. By generalized estimating equation, which better accommodates missing values in longitudinal evaluation, caregivers received the strengths-based intervention reported significantly greater improvement in sense of coherence, burden (Zarit Burden Inventory; ZBI), depression (Center of Epidemiology Depression Scale; CES-D), and mental well-being (Short-Form 36 Mental Component Summary; MCS) of the family caregivers than the education group over the three study endpoints. (Research objective #1). Path analysis using the three clusters of data at baseline (T0), 14th week (T1) and 22nd week (T2) after imposing the equality constraints from T0 to T1 and T1 to T2 support the theoretical postulations underpinning this study. In particular, the positive changes in depression and mental health are all mediated through the successive improvement of SOC over the 22-week evaluative period, with the results of path analysis showed data-model fit. (Research objective #2). We interviewed 30 family caregivers for their perception on the effects and acceptance of the strength-based intervention, with the interviews lasted for 45-93 minutes. The findings echoed very well with the quantitative findings, and the five categories which conveyed the effects of the strength-based program include: i) increased the comprehensibility and predictability of dementia caregiving, ii) increased perceived manageability of the caregiving situation, iii) reframe the caregiving journey in a new cognitive and attitudinal schemata, iv) improved role fulfillment, and v) improved emotional well-being and stress-related symptoms. The data also provided more in-depth explanation for such positive changes. In particular, the self-disclosure of caregiving experience to the peer caregivers with similar experience was very therapeutic to relieve their emotional burden. The self-disclosure allowed the caregivers to recognize their own efforts, strengths and resilience in role fulfillment, and they felt no regret for whatever outcomes. They had more confidence in themselves when they were directed to identify their successful caregiving experience. The corresponding situation analysis on such experience, together with the peer sharing and the empowerment-based training, offered the caregivers many insights on how to tackle the caregiving challenges. Indeed, they regarded the goal-setting approach as offering them clear direction on how to move forward, and they mentioned that they became more hopeful even though they may stuck on the process at some times in the future. The caregivers in each group developed very cohesive relationship, and this sense of social connectedness also played a part to explain their improved mood status. Another theme also emerged from the qualitative data which reflected the high acceptability of the strength-based intervention. Even though the 14-week program was very time-demanding, the caregivers mentioned that the program well addressed their needs for self-disclosure. In particular, they mentioned that the externalizing conversation has engaged them in thorough self-reflection by which they really made sense of the stressful encounter and be more able to see the outlet. They also felt more in control over the situation when goal-oriented approach with explicit action planning was set up to guide their coping (Research objective #3). Implementation challenges and resolution We encountered subject recruitment delay since mid-2018 for two reasons. After the first year of study implementation, the Dementia Community Support Scheme (DCSS) which provides service to persons with mild to moderate dementia for reducing the caregiver burden has extended to more non-government organization, and the model has become even more regularized in early 2019. In order to prevent bias, subjects engaged in the DCSS were excluded from the current study. As such, the recruitment rate has greatly slowed down, and we had played great effort to make connection with an additional 12 elderly community centers in six other NGO to catch up the progress. We eventually recruited 350 subjects up to Aug 2019 and still need 22 subjects to reach the proposed sample size. Despite we had finally invited two additional centers to participate, the growing social unrest and the subsequent pandemic had hindered the recruitment process. We finally decided to cease the study in June 2020. The research team is now catching up with the publication and the paper on the RCT was under the review of ISI journals. The PI did not apply for extension of the project before the project end-date as she was making the career move to the current administering institution by that time.

14639016.label: Major findings and research outcome
14639016.value: For objective #1, the within-group comparison indicates that the strengths-based intervention group, but not the education group, reported significant improvement on SOC, ZBI, CES-D, SCSQ, and MCS over theT0, T1 and T2 time points (Section C8(2): Table 2). The GEE results suggests the health benefits of the strength-based intervention as the caregivers reported significantly greater improvement in SOC, ZBI, CES-D and MCS than those received the educational intervention (Section C8(2): Table 3). For objective #2[Section C8(4)], path analysis showed acceptable data-model fit for the models which examined whether the positive effects of strength-based intervention on MCS (Χ2(45)=1031.64, p<0.001; CFI=0.993;RMSEA=0.043;SRMR=0.027) and CES-D (Χ2(45)=1204.882,p<0.001; CFI=0.992;RMSEA=0.052;SRMR=0.028) were mediated through SOC and coping after imposing equality constraints to the cluster of data from T0 to T1 and T1 to T2. For MCS, the intervention has significant effect on SOC at T1 (β=0.12, p=0.019), which further mediate its effect through SOC at T2 (β=0.84, p<0.001) to positively affect mental health (β=0.42, p-value<0.001), with the total indirect effect mediated through SOC as 0.045 (95%CI=0.002, 0.088, p = 0.038]. The mediating role of SOC for the intervention effects on CSE-D is similar, with the intervention effect on SOC at T1 as (β=-0.12, p=0.009), which, in turn, mediates its effect through a further improved SOC (β=.51, p<.001) at T2 to reduce depression (β=-.38, p-value<0.001), and the total indirect intervention effects mediated through SOC as -0.052 (95%CI=-0.094—0.001); p=0.016. For objective #3 [Section C8(5)], content analysis of the interviewing data identifies two major themes on high intervention acceptability and benefits over stress perception, caregiving role fulfillment and mental well-being. For intervention acceptance, the caregivers regarded narrative strategies as unique to facilitate self-disclosure and self-reflection on the complexity in the coping process so that they could make sense of the situation. They commented that the goal-setting process helped them to develop the roadmap to handle the caregiving difficulties. For treatment benefits, the caregivers noticed their own efforts, strengths and resilience in the role fulfillment when engaged in the analytic dialogues (narrative therapy), and this self-affirmation enable them to see the outlet in future difficulties. Besides, the peer sharing on successful experience form a repertoire of knowledge on almost the full course of dementia manifestation and management, and increased their comprehensibility on the situation. Indeed, the group dynamic over the 14 weeks also induced out a sense of social connectedness. All these changes were commented as reasons for the increased mood status.

14639016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14639016.value: The study findings affirmed the Antonovsky’s Theory of Salutogenesis that SOC is modifiable through remodeling one’s perception of the stressful encounter and roadmap for situation management. Together with its significant role in mediating the mental health benefit, the findings call for a paradigm shift in caregiver research. Instead of focusing on the caregivers’ deficit through the stress and coping paradigm, future research need to optimize the use of their strengths in the stressful encounters. As such, the PI has obtained a seeding fund (Ref: 1040005942) to examine the effects of engaging the caregivers as partners to provide exercise training for dementia person. She also submitted a proposal to extend the use of strengths-based approach to enhance the stress adaptation in a dyadic perspective (RGC/ref/17607021). To further advance the theory, the research team is also planning for a grounded theory study to investigate how inner strengths evolves in the caregiving journey. Besides, the study implementation has a territory-wide coverage (24 centers from 14 non-government organization) and we received very positive feedbacks from both the participants and service stakeholders. We are planning to apply for a knowledge translation fund to support the train-the-trainer, impact assessment and practice guideline development in 2021-2022.

14639016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14639016.value: From May 2017 to Aug 2019, 350 dementia family caregivers participated in this study, with 166 received the strengths-based intervention and the other for the education program. The attrition rate over the 22-week study period was 22.3%, with the competing caregiving duties as the major reason. No attrition bias was detected. For the competers, the attendance rate is as high as 90.2% and 89.3% for the strength-based and education intervention, respectively. Data analysis indicated that the strengths-based group reported significantly greater improvement in sense of coherence, mental well-being, perceived burden and depression over the three evaluative time points at baseline, 14th and 22nd week thereafter. Conforming to the theoretical postulation underlying this study, the improvement in mental well-being and depression over the evaluative period is partially mediated through a successive improvement in sense of coherence. We interviewed 30 family caregivers. They showed high acceptance to the analytic dialogues, peer sharing on successful experience and goal-setting process of the strengths-based intervention. They mentioned that they were more able to realize the overall dementia manifestation and their own efforts, strengths and resilience throughout the engagement, and perceive there must be an outlet for the future caregiving difficulties. 14639116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14639116.value: 過去十年，有關人格特質（亦稱為人格技巧，非認知特質/技巧）和健康不平等關係的研究已經成為社會科學中最令人興奮並且快速擴張的前沿領域。與家庭背景和認知能力不同，人格特質的可塑性強，能夠在生命週期中改變， 可以因為社會政策的干預改善。人格特質對於健康不平等的影響之所以廣受關注，一方面是由於近期人們對於此類研究的政策價值的認識，另一方面經濟學家試圖尋求有效的政策干預措施，以便於改善出身弱勢家庭孩子的勞動力質素及生活際遇。 令人驚訝的是，有關該領域的理論仍然缺乏：實證的發現很難與經典的經濟學和心理學理論相調和，而且在這領域有兩個缺口：(1) 社會學在該研究前沿已處於落後位置；(2) 因為該群體獨特文化和組織有可能會型塑人格特質對健康影響，合適數據的缺乏限制了將該研究前沿拓展到華人的嘗試。對於社會學者而言，現在正是時候尋找一條可行的道路去克服數據局限，為研究華人社會做出貢獻。 本研究計劃是第一個出自社會學家對該前沿領域進行拓展並著眼於一個主要的華人社會的研究。本研究使用的生物社會數據來自於一項大規模的全國性調查，被訪者是台灣的一個健康檢查項目的參加者。所有被訪者不僅參加了健康檢查，還填答了調查問卷。因而，我們的數據含有關於被訪者的青少年時人格特質，整體健康狀況，代謝官能症的生物標記、疾病用藥史以及社會經濟背景等方面的資訊。 本研究的分析目標之一是檢驗兩個文獻中的命題：(1)某些孩童或青少年時期人格特質是一種資本，能夠影響多年後的健康。(2)人格特質對健康的影響是有顯著的男女差異。本研究屬於一項探索研究，使用自2014年開始的數據。儘管如此，本研究的經驗分析是獨特的，因為它在一個主要華人社會中檢驗兩個命題，提供了大規模的生物標記證據，及它們對於健康不平等的意義，分析結果有利對於健康不平等認識的重新檢視。 第二個分析目標是評估使用回溯性人格特質的指標測量對於研究結果的影響，以便改進未來測量指標。使用已有的結構方程模型能夠糾正可能產生的回答偏誤。我們認為對於缺乏大規模全國性且長期追蹤的華人群體數據的問題，該策略提供了一個快速的及低成本的解決方案。

14641516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14641516.value: 城市暫停：開拓香港的殘餘城市空間。

14641516.label: Project Objectives
14641516.value: To survey the social/spatial characteristic of “Urban Pauses” in Hong Kong identifying a series of typical and prevalent conditions that characterize both the negative as well as the positive examples. To position Hong Kong’s Urban Pauses as a new typology of public space, unique to the city and distinct from other categories identified in existing academic studies. To implement four architectural prototypes that will focus and capture public imagination and also leverage support for improving and transforming Urban Pauses. To create a comprehensive knowledge framework regarding Urban Pauses in Hong Kong and to articulate a phased urban design strategy that capitalizes on three dimensional spaces, namely usable land, existing infrastructures and surfaces possibilities.

To implement four architectural prototypes that will focus and capture public imagination and also leverage support for improving and transforming Urban Pauses.
