14641516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14641516.value: The aim of this project is to devise a creative strategy to reclaim urban pauses within Hong Kong through specific design transformations, connecting the marginal, hidden and neglected urban spaces back into the fabric of the city. Due to Hong Kong’s extreme density, where 7.1 million inhabitants occupy a built up area of only 14% of its total surface, urban pauses can no longer be neglected or dismissed; they arguably encompass the biggest opportunity to impact on the existing tissue of the city, an untapped public asset, one which has the potential to strategically push forward ecological and technical infrastructures and redefine the spatial urban ecology of Hong Kong. Architects tend to project their desires onto vacant spaces, with the resulting interventions often acting as violent transformations that shatter the existing continuity both in time and space. Inspired by Solà-Morales’ paper “Terrain Vague” (1995), where he argues that abandoned and unproductive spaces represent the anonymous reality of the city that help to generate a sense of urban continuity, this research project seeks to unfold and differentiate Hong Kong’s vacant spaces to change their common negative perception and devise a strategic activation plan. We intend to survey the existing Urban Pause conditions of Hong Kong by identifying four categories that are the result of prior research into the field, namely: margins, infrastructure, artificial and traces. From these conditions, based on established research templates for this kind of study, we will generate a catalogue of typologies of the various Urban Pauses, and through a series of participatory workshops, soliciting input from the key players (public and private), we will aim to produce a series of micro prototypes in the form of temporary toolkit of interventions. Finally, working with such findings, we will attempt to formulate a macro strategy for how the city can engage with Urban Pauses to develop new design typologies that could be employed throughout the city. Although the issue of reclaiming urban residual spaces is rapidly becoming the zeitgeist of our epoch, with numerous urban and architectural projects underway around the world, Hong Kong paradoxically has, given its extremely urban characteristics, few critical studies on the matter. This project will address this deficiency, exploiting the way in which multi-layered urban pauses can accommodate overlapping programmes, and through creative design solutions, transform typically avoided public spaces that isolate and blight communities into alternative paradigms. 該項目的目標是制定通過具體的設計變革收回香港市區範圍內暫停創作策略，連接邊緣，隱藏的和被忽視的城市空間回城的結構。由於香港的極端密度，其中710萬人口僅佔其總面積14％的建成區，城市暫停不能再被忽視或辭退;它們包括可以說是對城市的現有組織影響最大的機會，一個尚未開發的公有資產，即有潛力的戰略推動生態和技術基礎設施，並重新定義香港的空間城市生態。 建築師往往會投射到空車位自己的慾望，與得到往往干預作用的破碎在時間和空間上現有的連續性劇烈變革。通過Solà酒店 - 莫拉萊斯的論文“在地形模糊的” （ 1995） ，他認為，被遺棄和非生產性空間代表的城市，幫助產生城市連續感的匿名現實的啟發，該研究項目旨在展現和分化香港的空置和空閒的空間，以改變他們共同的負面看法，並制定一項戰略行動計劃，以重新激活這些不存在的空間。 我們打算通過識別四類是以前的研究結果進入該領域，即調查香港現有的城市暫停的條件：邊距，基礎設施，人工和跟踪。從這些條件的基礎上，這種研究建立了研究的模板，我們將生成一個目錄的各種城市暫停，並通過一系列的參與式研討會類型學，從關鍵球員徵求意見（公立和私立） ，我們的目標是產生一系列微原型在暫時位點特異性的干預的形式。最後，這樣的調查結果的工作，我們力求制定怎樣的城市能夠與城市暫停搞開發，可以在城市中使用特定的網站設計類型學一個宏觀戰略。 雖然回收殘餘城市空間的問題正在迅速成為我們時期的時代精神，與世界各地的眾多正在進行的城市和建築項目，香港矛盾的是，由於其極端的溫文爾雅，對此事一點批評研究。該項目將解決這一不足，利用城市暫停如何多層重疊的適應方案，並通過創意設計方案，改造通常避免公共場所和疫病社區替代性範式，不僅將香港，但在其他新興城市受益中國和東南亞。

14641516.label: Realisation of objectives
14641516.value: Objective 1: SURVEY In order to get a balanced accurate cross-section of the urban residual spaces of Hong Kong, the survey was divided into three areas of study: Hong Kong Island, Kowloon and New Territories. Over 185 sites were surveyed (Report Section 1.1.1 -1.1.3) from which a Digital GPS map was created (Report Section 1.1.4). Each site was analyzed in terms of an urban condition (history, photography and digital modelling) resulting in a Residual Feasibility report (Report Section 1.2) that reads as a taxonomy of residual conditions of Hong Kong. In tandem ran several Elective Classes were hosted within the School of Architecture at CUHK (Report Section 1.3.1-1.3.3), where classes of 15 students would advance the research documentation. As a comparative exercise, we visited Tokyo to sample how urban residual environments differ in other Asian metropolitan cities, over 10 cases were examined (Report Section 1.4.1). While in Tokyo our research findings were presented at Chiba University, Department of Architecture (Report Section 1.4.2). Finally, a specialized Literature Review was produced for both Hong Kong’s Residual Urban Conditions and the topic generally (Report Section 1.5.1 – 1.5.2). Objective 2: TYPOLOGY By examining a large sample of residual sites (Objective 1), it was possible to compare conditions and discover underlying patterns. Six categories of urban residual spaces were identified: Work, Temple, Infrastructure, Commercial, Temporary and Dwelling. Three sites were then selected for an in-depth analysis considering: Historical and Cultural Development, Existing Infrastructure, Typologies of Programme. The area selected were: Shau Kei Wan, Mei Foo and Sham Shui Po, the common ground being that all three sites were built on reclaimed land and had a similar urban density rich in residual appropriated sites (Report Section 2.1.1 – 2.1.3). The findings underlined a relationship between urban historical vestiges and the new urban morphology, where existing rituals play a role in how residents inhabit these residual environments. The work developed was presented at the UIA (International Union of Architects) International Conference in Seoul (Report Section 2.2.1) as well as being the topic of my keynote speech at the 3rd International Conference of Urban Planning in Singapore (Report Section 2.2.2) and also at the IFOU International Conference in Hong Kong (Report Section 2.2.3). During this period, I ran a Design Workshop together with Prof. Margaret Crawford (UC Berkeley) titled “Urban-action” held at CUHK, looking at ways to revitalize residual conditions of the Mei Foo estate (Report Section 2.3.1) as well as participating at the 1st Seoul International Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism with an exhibition titled “By City/ By Product” where the Urban Pause research was presented to a wide international audience. Objective 3: PROTOTYPE The prototype is the core objective of this research project where the team engaged in Design, Public Consultation and Fabrication of various architectural prototypes. Most importantly the prototype allows first-hand knowledge to be developed throughout the implementation stages, from design to occupancy. Four different prototypes were designed (Report Section 3.1.1 -3.1.3), where one proposal was further developed (Book Tree - Mei Foo) into a fabricated pilot project. In order to have the prototype built and installed in-situ, a series of government consultations and formal applications processes had to be submitted (Report Section 3.2.1 -3.2.6), including Meetings with the local District Councilor, Public Consultation with the Mei Foo Community, Presentation to the Sham Shui Po LEGCO Councilor, Commissioning a Structural Feasibility Report, Submission of Applications to the Lands and Health a Safety Government Departments. Engaging into a full “temporary-use” application, gave the team insights into the various layers of bureaucracy required to implement the installation of a 1:1 physical structure within a public space in Hong Kong, revealing in the process the multi governance of these so-called “lost” urban spaces. The final “Book Tree” Prototype took three months to fabricate, funded by our team for a sum of 50,000 HKD and was entirely built using sustainable timber sourced from China. It was erected in 3 days by a team of research assistants and students from CUHK SOA and was in operation for 3 months from August -November 2018 under the Kwai Chung Road elevated highway. The main idea behind the structure was to create a public space for the exchange of books, through consultations with the community we found out that a large number of families were ready to donate used books, hence the Book Tree became a platform for the exchange (without financial transaction) of used books. This entirely open structure became an open bookshelf where the neighbourhood would come to meet and at the same time share books. During the life span of the structure, we carried out a series of Public Events, Interviews, Public Surveys and several local newspapers covered the event (Report Section 3.4.1 -3.4.4) and estimate over 10,000 people engaged with the prototype. The research was published as a book chapter in “Chasing the City: Models of Extra Urban Investigation” Routledge Press, 2018 (Report Section 3.5.1) as well as being presented at 3 International conferences (Report Section 3.6.1-3.6.3). I was invited to talk about the project at a Hong Kong TED Talk and University Library Festival (Report Section 3.7.1 – 3.7.2) as well as exhibiting the project at two International Exhibitions (Report Section 3.8.1 -3.8.2). Finally, as a result of the success and the “Book Tree” prototype, our research team was contacted by the Kowloon Junior School in Mong Kok to build another prototype for their school library (Report Section 3.1.4) which was designed and built as part of an Architectural Elective class and the new Mei Foo Council also asked us to design a continuation project called “Book Stage” (Report Section 3.1.3). Objective 4: STRATEGY For the last objective, we produced the Final Report compiling the findings assimilated over the project duration (Report Section 4.1.1 – 4.1.3) setting out the framework for further action and dissemination. Further consultations meetings were held with local government officials as well as exhibiting the findings at Design Inspire Hong Kong (Report Section 4.3.1). Having studied and worked on several sites within Hong Kong our final strategy concluded that: 1) Any activation of residual sites has to be implemented with the support and participation of the local community; 2) Political support is imperative to allow the project realistic chance of success; 3) Proposals at a micro-scale and of a temporary nature have greater chances of engaging the community and therefore of imparting social impact; 4) A network of exchange places allows multiple residual spaces to be activated simultaneously; 5) In tandem to the physical infrastructure of the prototype a soft infrastructure of maintenance and management is required; 6) The success of the inserted structure is related to its proposed social programme; 7) Educational institutional support for any project allows for better public support. Finally, we published our research findings in a local journal, Being Hong Kong, titled “Glances of perplexity: A Short Walking Manual to Hong Kong’s Hidden Conditions” revealing the hidden potential of residual spaces to the general Hong Kong audience (Report Section 4.2.1).

14641516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14641516.value: Residual Typologies Hong Kong has a multitude of residual urban conditions that arise from its geographical context, extreme density and complex history. Its territory is highly engineered, relying on an efficient infrastructural system that allows the city to operate efficiently. From this perspective, the notion of the residual is complex and multilayered. During the course of our research, we identified a series of residual typologies defined by the categories: Work, Temple, Infrastructure, Commercial, Temporary and Dwelling common to the whole territory. By carefully analyzing how every day lost spaces have been activated we were able to define a taxonomy of Hong Kong Residual Conditions. Public Engagement Prior to commencing the project, the ownership and regulatory side behind how various types of residual spaces worked in Hong Kong was unclear to us. Through the direct engagement of the Mei Foo “Book Tree” project, we were able to unravel the statutory regulations and procedural requirements. Specifically, there were two licenses granted by the Lands Department and Food and Hygiene Department that were crucial to allowing the installation of the structure. We were also fortunate to work with District Councilor Ambrose Cheung, who helped us arrange a series of community consultations and generally promoted the project to the residents of Mei Foo. Such practical knowledge could only have been assimilated through direct action, i.e. the realization of the prototype. Prototype The prototype, in its various iterations, has been the vehicle to generate knowledge about residual urban conditions. As a Design vehicle, it allowed the project to address realistic problems of better engaging the local community with potentially lost spaces. From the outset, the ambition of the project was to challenge the notion of design as an exclusively a high-end solution, the norm in Hong Kong, and employ design to address important social issues and critically generate a sense of civic identity that could impact the neighborhood for the better. Key to the success of the prototype was its temporary status; static architectural solutions are not ideal for these urban spaces that require flexibility. Temporary structures allow a dynamic solution that is both innovative and changeable. The materiality of the prototype, timber, was key in keeping fabrication costs low and the assemblage system straight forward. Finally, the educational component of the prototype, it was assembled by CUHK students, allowed students to engage directly in a “live” project and instill a sense of social agency.

14641516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14641516.value: The next stage of the project is to translate the findings of the prototype into a framework of “Book-Exchange” platforms that act as an urban network. In the final chapter of our submitted report (Section 4.4.1) we have started the design development of such a network, applying it as a case study to the Sham Shui Po neighbourhood of Hong Kong, that sits adjacent to Me Foo. For this next project to become reality, we aim to team up with a bigger multidisciplinary team including Educational Professionals, Psychology researchers, Local Libraries as well as government bodies. Sham Shui Po seems the right venue given social problems, the rich potential of residual urban spaces and our connections with Local government. It is important that the next step is not seen as a “token” architectural intervention, but rather understood as an integrated community-led experiment aiming at engaging children and adults with the joys of reading physical books. Design will simply be the agent that makes the idea possible.

14641516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14641516.value: This project first identified various types of residual urban spaces in Hong Kong. Subsequently, via a series of design prototypes attempted to find ways to activate these “lost” spaces and finally fabricated a 1:1 timber prototype below the Kwai Chung Road elevated highway within the Mei Foo housing estate. The key lessons learnt from the research related to Design and Public Participation, the Complex Nature of Governance behind such spaces, the required Statutory Protocols required to receive a temporary license and the potential social impact of temporary public structures. Besides the specific design solution of the Book Tree, a tectonic timber structure, the main innovation finding of the project relates to the idea of “exchange”, where via several community consultations we learnt that families are reluctant to through books away, that children seldomly visit their local library and there are few public spaces to engage with books. Exchange in this context became synonymous with meeting people, engaging in social acts of sharing and participation. The impact of the project relates to awakening the general public to the latent potential of these backgrounds, hidden and often forgotten spaces through design; ultimately to reconnect the profession with its social responsibilities.

14642816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14642816.value: Although boarding schools have existed in rural China since 1950s, they are now much larger and more numerous than they were in the past. In the late of 1990s, with decreasing numbers of children due to a declining birth rate and rural-to-urban migration, many primary schools have fewer children in rural China. Aiming to improve the quality of education, make use of economies of scale and relieve the burden of families with migrating parents, the Ministry of Education (MOE) launched an aggressive School Merger Policy, which closed down a large number of geographically scattered primary and secondary schools and merged their students into more centralized locations. As such, a great number of young students have to attend boarding schools at a distance from their home, or they have to walk a long way to attend schools. Nowadays the program to merge schools is almost complete. However, few studies have examined the influence of student’s boarding history and boarding status on their well-being, let alone whether the boarding experience has been beneficial to children who are left-behind. This proposed project will investigate three important questions in a context of school merging and massive parental out-migration in rural China. First, what is the impact of boarding experiences on child welfare academically, physically and psychologically when they are in secondary schools? Seconds, what are the mechanisms which intervene or moderate the process of boarding and children’s outcome? Third, how would the boarding at schools matters for children in the context of parental migration? In this proposed study we will collect a sample size of 2430 students from 27 schools (90 per school) in three provinces of Shannxi, Huanan and Anhui in rural China. In addition to the questionnaire survey, we will conduct focus group interviews to collect additional information via brain-storming sessions involving students and parents. We will also collect semi-structured questionnaire survey from class-leading teachers, school heads and local officials. Our survey will include detailed information on student’s welfare, boarding history, the measures to test the mechanisms between boarding and welfare as well as demographic and family socioeconomic status information. We will merge these data into a multi-level data set with hierarchical levels of individual, class and school. This proposed study will not only add to the broader literature on boarding school and adolescent well-being, but will also have important policy implications for narrowing the education gap between rural and urban students. 在中國農村，寄宿學校自上世紀50年代就開始存在，但今天已經具有相當的規模和數量。上世紀90年代，隨著出生率下降和農村到城市的遷移，農村學齡兒童大大減少。為了提高教學質量，充分利用規模經濟以及減輕在外打工家庭照料學齡子女的負擔，教育部發起了撤村並校的教育政策，此政策消減了大量地理位置上比較偏遠和人數比較少的中小學，以至於大量的小學生和初中生不得不去較遠而教育資源相對集中的地方去上學。作為中國歷史上最為重要的一次教育變革，學術界關於寄宿對孩子福祉的影響卻遠遠不夠，其中對父母遷移的小孩是否有更為特殊的影響更為缺少。此研究將主要集中在三個研究問題：第一，寄宿經歷對小孩的學業，身體和心理健康到底有什麼樣的影響？第二，如果有影響，那影響的機制到底是什麼？第三，寄宿對父母遷移和未遷移小孩的影響到底有何不同? 我們將在湖南，陝西和安徽三個省份收集青少年，學校以及家庭和村落的數據來進行此項研究。

14642816.label: Realisation of objectives
14642816.value: We have largely achieved all the research objectives for this funded project. Since the objectives are connected with each other, I will describe the realizations of the objectives together as below. The most important objective we would like to achieve is to examine the impact of boarding experiences on child well-being including academic, physical and emotional well-being as well as risky health behaviors in Chinese context, in particular in rural context. To achieve this goal, we have taken the following actions. First, we have used the existing national data set to examine the impact of boarding status on student outcome. We have used the Chinese Family Panel Studies (CFPS) and the China Education Panel Survey (CEPS) because these two data complement each other. The former is a household data collection effort, while the latter is the school level data. Using the CFPS data, we have written a paper titled as “Boarding at School and Students’ Well-Being under the Context of School Merging in Rural China”. This paper has been submitted to Comparative Education Review. The paper found that boarding at school is harmful to student mental health, but it is beneficial to students’ academic well-being. Some mechanisms have been examined, including study time and attachment to parents. Using the CEPS data, we have focused on boarding/school environment and student academic outcome. We developed two papers based from this data set. The first paper is about parental socioeconomic status and student academic performance: the disparity between migrant and non-migrant students. This paper has been published in the American Education Research Journal. It found that migrant children, in particular rural to urban migrant children benefit less from better-off school SES environment, and this is more salient when the class has discrimination atmosphere toward migrant children. Using CFPS data, we have developed a second paper. In this paper, we mainly examine the heterogeneity of boarding and academic outcome across different student groups by their Hukou and migration status. The paper is titled as “Who Benefit from Boarding Academically? The Disparity of Boarding and Academic Achievement across Students’ Migration and Hukou Status in China”, and this is a working paper with manuscript under preparation for journal publication. This paper found that the beneficial impact from boarding only exists in the rural schools, but not urban schools. The above two papers used the national level existing data sets, but both data have some limitation on the details of boarding. For instance, the boarding experience. Therefore, we have used part of GRF fund to collect more detailed boarding data from rural areas in three provinces in China, including Hunan, Shaanxi and Anhui. We collected over 2500 students in three counties from these three provinces. Based on the self-collected data set, we have developed three papers. The first paper is more about the gender gap on education outcome in rural China, and considering the boarding status. It is titled as “The Gender Academic Performance Gap of Youth in Rural China: The Role of Gender Egalitarian Values”. This paper examines the role of gender egalitarian values in closing gender academic gap, and we have examined whether there is a disparity between boarding and non-boarding students. This paper has been presented in the annual Meeting of Population Association of American in 2019, and has been submitted to American Education Research Journal in January 2021. The second paper based on this self-collected dataset examines the boarding experience and students’ academic preformation in the context of parental migration in China. We examine the heterogeneity of boarding for students with migrant and non-migrant parents. This paper has been presented in the Research Committee for Family Studies in the International Sociology of Association in 2019. The third paper based on this self-collected data set is title as “Boarding at School and Experience of Victimization in the Context of Parental Migration and School Merging Program in Rural China”. In this paper, we mainly examine how boarding is associated with students’ victimization experience. This paper has been presented in the Hong Kong Sociology Association Annual Meeting in 2019, and its further developed version has been accepted into Asia Population Association Meeting in 2020. Unfortunately, the meeting has been cancelled because of the pandemic. In addition to participation in the academic conferences, submitting papers to academic journals, we also published a layman article in two popular E-magazines (Wechat public accounts in China). One is 知识分子, and the other is 缪斯夫人. It is the same article which has been published in two accounts, and it has been read by more than 20, 000 readers and many discussions have been followed in that post.

14642816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14642816.value: The major findings can be summarized in two aspects. One is about boarding at school on student academic achievement and well-being. The other is about the factors contributing to the linkage between boarding at schools and student academic outcome and well-being. In terms of the boarding at schools and student outcome. We found that boarding at school is beneficial for students’ academics in both word recognition and numerical skills. However, boarding students are also more likely to be sick and have higher depression scores. We also found that boarding at school is associated with a higher level of victimization, and the experiences of boarding and the score of victimization exhibit a non-linear relationship. Moreover, earlier exposure to boarding such as boarding starting at the primary school level has a stronger positive association with experience of victimization than exposure at a later stage such as in secondary school, indicating the life stage importance in boarding outcome. We found that instead of a double disadvantage of de-attachment from parents and family environment, boarding at schools actually can reduce the level of victimization caused by father absence, but it is not the case for mothers’ absence. We also find that boys are more vulnerable to victimization when they are boarding, and it is particularly the case when their mothers are migrating. In terms of the linkage between boarding at school and students. First, we showed that the positive outcome of boarding on students’ academic skill is caused by their increased exposure to the learning environment. In contrast, detachment from the home environment and dormitory conditions might be the causes of more frequent sickness and higher levels of depression. We also found some heterogeneity about boarding on student outcome. For instance, for middle school students, boarding at school in both grades facilitate students learning. However, when students are not boarding in grade 7, but newly boarded in grade 8, boarding shows a significantly negative effect on academic scores. We also found that there is disparity across parental migration status. Scholars and policy makers argued that boarding at schools may be particularly beneficial to students in the case of parental migration because of the lack of parental figures at home for these children. Our studies show that the beneficial effect can be intensified when both parents are migrating, indicating that school boarding are more beneficial to students in the case of parental migration.

14642816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14642816.value: This project has opened new doors for my research interest in the sociology of education. I have become more and more interested in pursuing studies about rural education inequality in China. Inspired by this project, I have developed a research proposal to study peer influence on student academic outcome and well-being. One of my ongoing internal grants will make use the data sets I mentioned above to examine peer influence on children outcome from multiple perspective. I am also particularly interested in the gender disparity of rural education, which I plan to do some new data collection with experimental design. I also plan to conduct some international comparative studies about boarding, school context and student outcomes in East Asia countries.

14642816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14642816.value: Since 1990s, with decreasing numbers of children due to a declining birth rate and rural-to-urban migration, many schools in rural China have been merged. As such, a great number of young students have to attend boarding schools at a distance from their home, or they have to walk a long way to attend schools. In this project, we examine the impact of boarding experiences on child welfare academically, physically and psychologically as well as the mechanisms which intervene or moderate the process of boarding and children’s outcome. Using some national level data sets as well as self-collected school children data on boarding experiences and children outcome, our papers based on this project have been published, submitted or presented in academic journals or international conferences. We found that boarding has beneficial impact on children learning and their academic outcome in rural China, but it is at the cost of psychological well-being. Boarding experiences at different life stages exhibit different impact on student outcomes. Boarding at very young life stages have negative consequences for children. Boarding also has displayed different impact for children from migrant and non-migrant families. Our study suggests that boarding at school should be understood according to the context.

14643716.label: Realisation of objectives
14643716.value: 本研究計劃以清代避諱學研究的幾部著述為主要研究對像，並將重點集中在諸書所討論的歷代帝王名諱之上，在研讀古籍上取得一定的成效，解決了一些古籍校勘上的問題。避諱之俗，起於周，成於秦漢，盛於唐宋，延至清末。避諱學即專門研究避諱情況的學問，陳垣《史諱舉例》指出，「研究避諱而能應用之於校勘學及考古學者，謂之避諱學。」在先秦至明代，有關避諱的著述大多在於諱例的搜集，少有系統分析，談不上有學科建設的出現。一直到了清代，如本研究計劃所關注的數部避諱學典籍，才算是具有避諱學理論和應用的意識。其中周廣業《經史避名彙考》乃集大成之作，全書共有四十六卷，從不同方面探討和分析了前代避諱的情況。其他如周榘《廿二史諱略》、陸費墀《歷代帝王廟謚年諱譜》、劉錫信《歷代諱名考》、黃本驥《避諱錄》等四書，雖篇幅較短，資料沒有如《經史避名彙考》般充足，但仍極具參考價值。 本研究計劃利用清代避諱學著述所提出的前代避諱情況及其所歸納的理論，分析在古籍研讀上的各種狀況。舉例而言，拙作〈論避諱與兩漢典籍之傳鈔〉以出土文獻與傳世文獻為據，利用互見文獻對讀之法，輔之以避諱學研究理論，分析兩漢典籍傳鈔之情況，並討論避諱學在文獻研究上之作用。出土文獻或鈔本更能保持典籍在不同時代傳鈔時候之避諱情況。避諱理當只牽涉同朝帝王名諱，在改朝換代以後，自當不必迴避，可以回改。因此，出土文獻保存了不少避諱資料，更可藉此作為典籍傳鈔時代下限之佐證。此外，較諸刻本而言，鈔本亦能保存避諱之時代信息，對於考證典籍之傳鈔歷史，亦能起巨大之作用。 此外，本研究計劃以五部清代避諱學專書為基礎，按其成書年代先後排序應為周榘《廿二史諱略》、陸費墀《歷代帝王廟謚年諱譜》、劉錫信《歷代諱名考》、周廣業《經史避名彙考》、黃本驥《避諱錄》。諸書之中，周廣業《經史避名彙考》嘗批評《廿二史諱略》，云：「既自署廿二史，而于漢順、冲、靈、獻諸帝，東晉諸帝，宋武帝至明帝，齊、梁、陳三朝，及十六僭國皆云無考。」（卷三）批評《諱略》「無考」過多。《廿二史諱略》云：「宣帝初諱病己，後諱詢。凡詢皆改洵。」《經史避名彙考》卷七：「《諱略》謂『詢』皆改『洵』，尤謬。」又如史皇孫，《諱略》云：「宣帝父史皇孫諱進，宣帝即位後始避『進』，以『前』字代之。此避廟諱之始也。」《經史避名彙考》卷七：「《諱略》妄言以『前』字代之，為避廟諱之始，可怪也。」周廣業討論漢和帝劉肇名諱時，云：「《諱略》妄云兼避『兆』、『照』，改『兆民』為『萬民』，『照臨』為『燭臨』，謬甚。」（卷八）今考《諱略》每多陳列現象，而少作考證，與《經史避名彙考》之治學方法相異，故周廣業多所批評。相關資料已告整理，並在日後的學術會議上發表。

14643716.label: Major findings and research outcome
14643716.value: 主要分為兩類，第一類是以避諱學為重點的學術論著，第二類是利用避諱學以解決古籍校點上的問題。〈論古文獻避諱與異體字之關係──以前漢帝王名諱為例〉與〈論避諱與兩漢典籍之傳鈔〉即屬第一類。前者利用周廣業《經史避名彙考》有關宋代洪适《隸釋》的論述，以前漢帝王名諱為例，討論異體字的出現與避諱的關係。後者以出土文獻和古籍鈔本為例，指出這兩種狀態的本子較能保存前代避諱的痕跡。且在不同年代出現同一古籍的鈔本，更可呈現不同的諱字，進而能夠得見古籍在過去的流傳。〈《漢書》所見避諱資料研究〉、〈論顏師古《漢書注》與《急就篇注》釋義之異同〉、〈《群書治要》所載《文子》異文研究——兼補王利器《文子疏義》以《群書治要》校勘《文子》例〉等皆屬第二類。三篇論文分別討論了《漢書》、顏注《漢書》與《急就篇》，以及《文子》之避諱情況，其中如《急就篇》及《文子》之文，其重點雖非在避諱，然可以清代避諱學著述解決二書文字上之問題。

14643716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14643716.value: 本研究計劃以利用清代避諱學著述所提出的證據以解決古籍校勘上的問題，但就避諱學理論，以及避諱學諸書之間的關係，所論尚未充足。展望將來，可利用已經整理的清代避諱學諸書，詳加分析避諱學理論之發展和因由，以及比較研究清代避諱學諸書的承傳與批判的關係。此外，沒有清代避諱學的豐碩成果，亦不可能孕育近世以來的避諱學研究。因此，清代避諱學對後世避諱研究的影響，亦當加以探討。

14643716.value: 避諱是先秦以來已出現的現像，具體呈現是在不同時代的典籍上。避諱學是對避諱現像的分析，清代是避諱學集大成的時代。本研究計劃以清代避諱學典籍為中心，分析其中所提出的避諱理論與用例，並以此研讀若干古籍，解決了一些在古書傳鈔而引起的問題。此外，避諱學理論不可能平地而起，皆是前有所承，後有所繼，本計劃同時鑽研清代避諱學諸書之間的承傳關係，包括後作對前作的批評，以及後出轉精的優勝處。

14643816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14643816.value: Urban planners and governments need information to integrate urban climatic understanding when designing more livable cities. China’s Pearl River Delta (PRD) region is the most densely populated and urbanized region in the world, and its urban expansion and development will continue. The associated environmental pressures will exacerbate the already serious urban heat island (UHI) effects, worse heat stresses and cause high public health risks. These problems must not be under estimated. There is a need to better understanding the physical surface properties of the urban areas of the PRD region. It will help planners to quantify the UHI intensities of the city. This will lead to better informed planning to improve the urban thermal living conditions. The initial concept of the Local Climate Zone (LCZ) classification system was developed by Stewart and Oke (2012). It aims to characterize local urban surfaces with regard to their effect on local climate. Recent studies making use of the LCZ scheme have concentrated mostly on quantifying the air temperature differentials between the various LCZs (Stewart et al., 2014). There is a need to extend the study scope of the LCZ to its related thermal comfort studies, and to apply the more comprehensive understanding to develop methods to aid planners. The proposed project aims to contribute to this knowledge gap by: (a) applying the LCZ classifications into the cities in the PRD region by using WUDAPT method (See, Mills & Ching, 2015; Mills, et al., 2015) to develop an open-access database; (b) investigating the characteristics of outdoor thermal comfort of the different LCZ classes by using field measurement and ENVI-met model simulations; (c) integrating the findings of (a) and (b) to develop of thermal comfort threshold of selected LCZ classes for high-density subtropical urban areas; and (d), based on (c), establishing urban design guidelines of outdoor thermal comfort for different LCZ classes for planners in the PRD region . This project will contribute to the scholarly understanding of the outdoor thermal comfort conditions of LCZ classes. In practice, the developed dataset will provide planners in the PRD region with a quantitative understanding of the relationship between urban morphological characteristics, urban climate and urban thermal comfort based on a spatial information platform. The design guidelines will inform “The PRD Reform and Development Plan (2008-2020)” of the Chinese government. The findings will also be a useful reference for governments of other high-density cities in the sub-tropical regions. 城市規劃師和政府需要融合城市氣候理解和資訊以便設計出更宜居的城市。 中國珠江三角州以世界上人口密集和高城市化區域而聞名於世，其城市化擴張和發展還將繼續。隨之環境承受的壓力將加速已經嚴峻的城市熱島效應，加重熱負荷和導致公共健康的高風險。 這些問題不容忽視，迫切需要瞭解該區域的城市物理表面狀況。 這將有助於規劃師量化城市熱島效應的強度，從而形成有資料支撐的更好規劃方案。 利用加拿大Stewart博士創立的城市局地氣候區（LCZ）的方法，將相關的熱舒適度研究納入應用，以輔助規劃師的設計。 擬開展的研究專案的主要目標： a）利用WUDAPT方法將城市局地氣候區的分類方法應用於珠三角地區並建立開放資訊平臺；b）利用實地測量和ENVI-met模擬探索不同城市局地氣候區的室外熱舒適度的特徵；c）結合a）和b）的研究結果，建立針對高密度亞熱帶城市區域的熱舒適度閾值；d）基於c)的研究結果確立針對珠三角地區的不同城市局地氣候區的城市設計標準； 該研究將有助於理解不同城市局地氣候區的熱舒適度狀況。對於實際設計，開發的資料庫將為珠三角洲地區的規劃師提供適於城市形態、城市氣候和城市熱舒適度的量化理解和空間資訊平臺。 而設計導則將有助於《珠三角洲地區改革發展規劃綱要（2008-2020）》。同時研究結果也可供其他亞熱帶區域的高密度城市供參考。

14643816.label: Realisation of objectives
14643816.value: The local climate zone (LCZ)classifications to the cities of the PRD region by using The World UrbanDatabase and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT) method has been applied and developed. The multi-temporal land cover change and land surface temperature have been detected. The result was published in the journal of Urban Climate(Wang, et al. 2019). The results show that urbanization in this region comprises transformation from natural land covers to built types and conversion in the built-up, in particular densification and vertical enhancement of existing urban types. The land surface temperature (LST) in the region increased in general but the spatial pattern of LST increase is affected by the land cover change. LCZ 6 (open low-rise) and LCZ 8 (large low-rise) show the greatest increase in LST. LCZ 4 (open high-rise) and LCZ 8 are the two dominant CDs in high SUHI zone and LCZ 8 keeps growing as the most principal LCZ type. The characteristics of the outdoor thermal comfort of the different LCZ classes were investigated by using field measurement and the corresponding thermal comfort threshold of selected LCZclasses has been developed. The study results were published separately in the journal of Urban Climate (Shi, Lau, Ren & Ng, 2018) and the journal of building and Environment in 2019 (Lau, Chung & Ren, 2019) The first paper (Shi, Lau, Ren & Ng,2018) evaluated the LCZ mapping in such a unique urban context using in-situ air temperature data. The fine-scale spatial variation of the daytime and nighttime screen-level air temperatures was investigated via mobile measurements during the summertime of 2016. The measured data were collated in geographic Information System (GIS) based on the current LCZ maps. Statistically significant air temperature differences were observed between mostLCZ classes, which confirm the veracity of LCZ in high-density heterogeneous urban contexts. Higher uncertainties in the site-averaged air temperature and considerable intra-LCZ air temperature differences in LCZs 1 to 6 were observed. The second paper (Lau, Chung & Ren,2019) evaluated the microclimatic conditions and subjective perception of the thermal environment in eight LCZs in Hong Kong, using questionnaire surveys and field measurements. An ANOVA test showed that the microclimatic conditions were significantly different across eight LCZs, and this could be attributed to the urban morphology and the geometry of the outdoor urban spaces. This does not only affect the critical conditions but also the variations in the thermal environment. The highest maximum temperature (38.9 °C) was found in LCZ 1, and the lowest maximum temperature (29.9 °C) was observed in land cover LCZs. The subjective assessment showed that compact or high-rise settings were associated with warmer thermal sensations reported by the respondents. The relationship between the level of thermal stress and subjective thermal sensation changed across LCZs. This study demonstrated that the LCZ classification provides a characterization of both the physical and thermal environment. It is also one of the first attempts to examine the relationship between the thermal environment and subjective perceptions using the LCZ classification system. Further work is required to investigate how thermal comfort indicators can be used to represent the thermal comfort conditions in different LCZs. Based on the project findings of (Wang, et al. 2019), (Shi, Lau, Ren & Ng, 2018), and (Lau, Chung & Ren, 2019), itis found that urban greenery and wind corridor are the effective design measures to improve thermal comfort conditions in such sub-tropical high-density urban regions. Another two journal papers were published on design measures. Ouyang, Morakinyo, Ren, &Ng, E. (2020) investigated and discussed cooling efficiency by measuring the relationship between greenery coverage ratio and the cooling effects of greenery. Parametric studies were conducted in a validated ENVI-met model, with different combinations of urban densities (Low, Mid, and High) and tree coverage ratios (2–30% at 2% interval, and 56% for full area coverage other than building). Then the pattern of the cooling efficiency was explored under three urban densities scenarios and two selected temporal periods on a typical summer daytime. For a subtropical climate background, results showed anon-linear (logarithmic) pattern for tree coverage ratio (TCR) and cooling effects, irrespective of the urban density, temporal periods, and heat indicators. When TCR reached 20–30%, the optimal cooling efficiency of trees was achieved, irrespective of building densities and temporal periods. The optimal threshold for greenery coverage in this study can provide science-based suggestions to urban planners and designers for better microclimate and thermal comfort environments at the neighborhood scale. Another study (Ren, et al.,2018) introduced the method of urban ventilation corridor and demonstrate the implementation of such considerations in local planning exercises in Chinese cities. There are several barriers to the development of LCZ data for the PRD region. Since 80-90% of the time in the PRD region is cloudy or partially cloudy, the quality of satellite images is not very good and available satellite images are limited.

14643816.label: Major findings and research outcome
14643816.value: The PRD region, the study area is one of the largest mega-urban regions characterized by high population and high building density on earth. Based on the developed LCZ data, it is found that urbanization in the PRD region has change land surface and urban morphology. The transformation from natural land covers to the urban types and conversion within the built-up areas, in particular densification and vertical enhancement of existing built-up areas were observed (Wang, et al. 2019. The land surface temperature in the PRD region increased in general but its spatial pattern change has corresponded to the land cover change. Statistically significant air temperature differences were observed between most LCZ classes, which confirm the veracity of LCZ in high-density heterogeneous urban contexts (Shi, Lau, Ren & Ng, 2018). The relationship between the level of thermal stress and subjective thermal sensation changed across LCZs. This study demonstrated that the LCZ classification provides a characterization of both the physical and thermal environment (Lau, Chung & Ren, 2019). If we want to adopt urban greenery to improve the thermal comfort and urban heat island conditions in subtropical cities, our study results showed a non-linear (logarithmic) pattern for tree coverage ratio (TCR) and cooling effects, irrespective of the urban density, temporal periods, and heat indicators (Ouyang, Morakinyo, Ren, & Ng, 2020). For the method of urban ventilation corridor, it has been developed into a national technical guide of China now (Ren, et al., 2018). The Funded GRF study is a part of the global initiative project named ‘World Urban Database and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT)’. Part of the study results has been included and published in the below joint paper. The PI is one of the co-authors. The international academic journal “Urban Climate” recently announced “the most cited articles” published since 2017. It is one of the top 25 papers of Urban Climate. This shows the WUDAPT study is of great concern and reference value to global researchers. Bechtel, B., Alexander, P.J., Beck, C., Böhner, J., et al. (2019). 14643816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14643816.value: A new collaborative study on urban greenery and its health impact in China has been initiated. Based on the method we developed from the funded GRF project, the PI has further developed LCZ data of China. This new set of LCZ data includes detailed urban green space information, so the PI has been worked with researchers from East China Normal University and The City University of Hong Kong to investigate the relationship between urban greenery and adiposity among undergraduate students in China. The below joint paper is under review. Yang, H., He, D., Lu, Y., Ren, C., et al. (2020). Association between different types of urban green spaces and adiposity outcomes among undergraduate students in China. Landscape and Urban Planning. (under review)

14645416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14645416.value: ---Project Background--- Human multitasking can be defined as the practice of performing more than one task at the same time (dual-task), rapidly alternating between multiple tasks (task switching), or dealing with interruptions. With the advance of technology and changes in lifestyle, multitasking has become a common practice, with frequent undesirable consequences. For example, driving while using a cell phone is an important cause of traffic accidents, and computer usage in class interferes with learning. Research on the cognitive limitations involved in multitasking has been focusing on individual paradigms, with lots of insights obtained. However, there has been surprisingly little effort in integrating the understanding obtained across paradigms. It is therefore unclear how the multitasking costs measured with different paradigms relate to each other. Do they reflect common underlying limitations, and is there some degree of separability? ---Brief Project Description--- The objective of this project is to reveal the common and distinct limitations underlying the multitasking costs measured with different paradigms. An individual-difference approach will be used, with multitasking costs measured for different paradigms introduced to each participant. The paradigms include commonly used tasks from different types of multitasking (dual-task, task switching, interruption). Principle component analysis will be used to reveal the constructs behind the multitasking costs in different paradigms. Structural equation modeling will also be used to test models with different postulations concerning general and specific multitasking limitations as well as the relationship between multitasking limitations and intelligence and processing speed. ---Significance of Project--- This project is one of the first empirical attempts to bridge the research areas on dual-task performance, task switching, and interruption. Findings will help depict an overall picture of multitasking ability by identifying the cognitive limitations common to various multitasking situations and the limitations specific to individual paradigms. This will establish a basis for further investigating the cognitive and neural underpinnings of the common and specific limitations across multitasking situations. This will also help future studies illuminating the relationship between multitasking abilities and other laboratory measures like executive function and societally important skills like self-control. Furthermore, the findings will help resolve potential conflicting results between studies as a result of using different and/or impure paradigms to compare multitasking abilities between different populations. ---研究背景--- 人類多任務處理可定義為同一時間處理多於一個任務 (雙任務)， 或在多個任務之間快速轉換 (任務轉換)，又或處理任務中斷的情況。 隨著科技進步和生活模式的轉變，多任務處理日漸普遍，並常引致一些不良後果。例如駕駛時使用手提電話增加交通意外的機會，在課堂上使用電腦影響學習等。過往對多任務處理背後認知限制的研究大多集中於個別的範式。 雖然這些研究得到不少成果，但是鮮有嘗試將不同範式得出的結論綜合比較。因此，迄今為止不同範式當中所量度的多任務處理成本之間的關係仍未有一個清晰的答案。它們是共同反映了一個普遍的多任務處理限制因素還是分別反映不同的、個別範式特有的限制因素？ ---研究簡介--- 此研究旨於揭示不同的多任務處理範式背後的各種共通限制。本研究將邀請參與者參與不同的範式，然後採用個體差異方式對量度所得的各種多任務處理成本進行分析。相關範式將包含各類型多任務處理(雙任務、任務轉換及任務中斷)常使用的任務。主成分分析將用於提取不同多任務處理成本背後的共通限制。然後，本研究將建立不同的結構方程模型以描述各普遍、範式特有的限制因素及各因素與智能和處理速度之間的關係，並對各模型進行比較測試。 ---研究意義--- 本項目是首批嘗試結合雙任務、任務轉換及任務中斷三個領域的實證研究之一。研究成果將通過提取共通於不同多任務處理情況和個別範式特有的認知限制來描繪多任務處理能力的全貌。這將為未來探勘各多任務處理的共有和特有的限制背後的認知和神經基礎提供依据。這亦有助於將來的研究去闡明各多任務處理能力與其它實驗測量如管控功能和自我控制等社交技巧之間的關係。最後，此研究成果亦有助於對一些因使用了不同或不純正範式去比較不同群體之間的多任務處理能力所引致的矛盾結果進行解析。

14645416.label: Realisation of objectives
14645416.value: Concerning the first objective, eleven indicators of multitasking abilities were measured for participants completing multiple computer tasks at the same time or switching between different tasks in the laboratory. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) revealed not a general cognitive factor that explains multitasking performance across different contexts. Instead three different processing limitations were found, and they were associated with response selection, retrieval and maintenance of task information, and mental reconfiguration upon switching to a new task. It was also found that different tasks tend to involve all these processing limitations, albeit to a different extent. In other words, there is no a general bottleneck limiting multitasking performance in different paradigms. Instead multiple processing limitations are together responsible for determining how well one perform in different situations. Concerning the second objective, participants also performed other tasks measuring fluid intelligence, working memory capacity and processing speed, and reported their video game playing ability and experience in a questionnaire. It was found that these measures only correlated weakly with the multitasking factors. This suggests that one’s multitasking abilities cannot be fully explained by her/his intelligence or other well-studied cognitive abilities. During pilot testing for the work above, it was found that while the dual-task and task switching paradigms provide reliable measures of multitasking performance, interruption paradigms did not. That led to the exclusion of interruption paradigms in the first study. Subsequent effort has been given to the development of paradigms involving interruptions that also provide reliable performance measures, and to examine the individual differences in different constructs underlying multitasking. We in general replicated the separation of different aspects of multitasking, and found that female and male participants enjoy strengths in different aspects of multitasking.

14645416.label: Major findings and research outcome
14645416.value: It was found that there were multiple constructs behind multitasking costs measured in different paradigms. Limitations in different phases of processing involving response selection, retrieval of task demand, and reconfiguration of the cognitive system for a new task all play a role in accounting for one’s multitasking performance across different contexts. In addition, the constructs identified behind multitasking costs showed very weak correlations with measures of general intelligence, working memory, and processing speed. In other words, multitasking may require different abilities from those typically referred to as intelligence and executive function. A poster was presented at International Convention of Psychological Science in Vienna in 2017. A paper was published in Psychological Research in 2019. A second manuscript has been submitted to another academic journal for peer review.

14645416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14645416.value: Several questions can be asked following the findings of the study. For example, would additional processing limitations be revealed with multitasking paradigms that are more realistic than those typically used in the literature? Also, can individual difference in multitasking ability be explained by differences in previous experience in multitasking? Some pilot work is under way and proposals have been submitted to acquire internal and external grants for further investigation.

14645416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14645416.value: Human multitasking can be defined as the practice of performing more than one task at the same time or in rapid alternation. Research on the cognitive limitations involved in multitasking has been focusing on individual paradigms, with lots of insights obtained. However, there has been surprisingly little effort in integrating the understanding obtained across paradigms. This project aimed at revealing the common and distinct limitations underlying the multitasking costs measured with different paradigms. Multitasking costs were measured for different paradigms for a group of college participants, and multiple distinct limitations were identified that did not correlate with general intelligence and working memory. This suggests that multitasking is a multifaceted ability distinct from the well-known intelligence and executive function. This may explain why earlier studies produce conflicting results because of the use of different paradigms tapping on different aspects of multitasking. The findings also pave the way for further investigation of the cognitive and brain underpinnings of the common and specific limitations across multitasking situations.

14646916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14646916.value: As a consequence of climate change, extreme storm events are on the rise to increase flood risks around the world. Existing high-density cities are particularly vulnerable. The conventional approach to urban flood hazard mitigation, which focuses on flood control engineering, has shown its limitation to address the challenge. An alternative approach is urgently needed. This project investigates the potential effectiveness of an unconventional approach that aims to create “floodable spaces” in the high-density city of Taipei, Taiwan. In recent years a new flood mitigation concept, which calls for more space to accommodate floodwater, receives increasing attention. The concept has been implemented in some rural areas in the West. However, it is seldom carried out in urban areas, mainly because it is intuitively assumed that cities have little extra space for water because of the concentration of people and activities and that cities have no choice but continue counting on flood control infrastructure. Based on resilience theory the PI has challenged such conventional wisdom and argued that it is plausible to create spaces for out of the existing urban fabric through urban design (Liao 2012, 2014). To move towards flood resilience, instead of struggling for preventing the city from flooding, the city should create as many floodable spaces—land areas that can permanently or temporarily store, convey, and/or infiltrate water—as possible to make itself floodable, that is, being flooded without physical damage and socioeconomic disruption. There has not been any large-scale scheme to create floodable spaces in modern cities. This concept of a “floodable city” is still theoretical. To move beyond theory, the floodable-city approach needs to be tested against real-world conditions. This project investigates the potential effects of the alternative approach on pluvial and riverine flooding in the flood-prone city of Taipei. The city epitomizes the vulnerability and the built environment typically of many high-density Asian cities. The project focuses on two most flood-prone areas—Mucha and Shezidao—in Taipei to identify the open spaces that could potentially be re-designed as floodable spaces, to evaluate the potential effects of the floodable-city approach on flood hazard mitigation, and to understand the obstacles associated with public perceptions to the implementation of the floodable-city approach. Based on the research results, we will develop a set of urban design guidelines for Taipei—also expected to be useful for other similar high-density Asian cities—to move towards a resilient, floodable city. 14647516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14647516.value: In Qing China, hundreds of thousands of students fanatically practised writing “eight-legged essays” in a bid to succeed in the imperial civil examination. The gist was not about correct understanding (which was assumed) of Confucian classics but about beautiful literary craftsmanship: an essay that included an introduction, four pairs of couplet paragraphs (hence the name “eight-legged”), and a conclusion. To master the writing of “eight-legged essay”, students needed the help of supplementary materials such as collection of ready-made couplet sentences, model eight-legged essays, collection of exegetical works, etc.. Where there is demand, there is supply. A market was created for such supplementary materials, known as the commercialized commentaries on Confucian classics for the examination. Historians know well and agree that the civil examination system was the most powerful impetus to the commercial printing industry in late imperial China. This research project, however, does not stop here. Instead, this project argues that these commercially driven and examination-oriented commentaries on Confucian classics had become a cultural force in its own right. As students feverishly crammed these commentaries into their heads, the eight-legged essays they churned out bore two important characteristics. Firstly, these essays were largely homogenous as they were but variants of a set of model answers prepared by the commentaries. Secondly, Zhu Xi’s commentaries on the Four Books, in theory the most authoritative textbook for the examination, were in effect “usurped” by these commercially driven and examination-oriented commentaries. An example was found in the 1886 Metropolitan Examination. A random sample of fourteen essays reveals that eleven of them did not follow Zhu Xi’s commentaries! All these eleven essays established their main themes with reference to “sincerity誠[cheng]”, a keyword that Zhu Xi’s commentary did not mention at all. Why? Because, as this project shows, they all followed the teaching of Jin Cheng金澂’s Sishu weigenlu四書味根錄, one of the most popular examination-oriented commentaries at the time! Consequently, if the purpose of the eight-legged essay was to “speak for sages代聖人立言”, the purpose was no longer fulfilled by Zhu Xi, but by a cultural industry that was commercially driven and examination-oriented, one that endeavored to “print for profit”. This project investigates the industry of this commercialized commentaries and evaluates its impact. It sheds new light on a hitherto uncharted terrain of the study of the imperial civil examination. 明清科舉制度下，士子花大量精力練習寫作八股文，八股文的難度不在於內容而在於形式。有需求自有供應，一個服務於八股文寫作的文化產業應運而生，這個產業包括各種應試輔助教材，例如現成對仗句、範文、四書五經典故的匯集，歷屆考試題目及優秀試卷，等等。逐漸地，這類應試輔助教材主導了科舉考試，而朱熹《四書集註》這本朝廷欽定的科舉考試標準答案，反而不受士子重視。八股文是「代聖賢立言」，但教導士子「代聖賢立言」的，不再是朱熹《四書集註》，而是一個按商業模式經營、服務於科舉考試的文化產業。本計劃探討這個產業的細節，追蹤當時的熱門八股文參考書及其編纂者，力圖發掘科舉制度研究中迄今為止這一較少受到關注的領域。

14647516.label: Realisation of objectives
14647516.value: Objective 1 aims at publishing one book. The P.I. has more than accomplished the objective. (1.1) In April 2017, Zhengbian shiqi de bagu政變時期的八股, a book coauthored and coedited by the P.I., was published: Zhengbian shiqi de bagu: guangxu 24 nian wuxuke huishi shijuan fenxi政變時期的八股：光緒二十四年戊戌科會試試卷分析[Eight-legged essays in a time of coup d'état: an analysis of the papers for the 1898 Metropolitan Examination] (Hong Kong: Chung Hwa Books, 2017). 287 pp. ISBN 9789888463312. https://www.airitibooks.com/detail.aspx?PublicationID=P20180105401; https://www.worldcat.org/search?q=isbn%3A9789888463312. In this book, the P.I. shows that in the 1886 Metropolitan Examination, many students' answers bore significant similarity with commercially-driven and exam-oriented commentaries, whereas Zhu Xi朱熹' commentaries, the most official and authoritative one in theory, were largely ignored in practice. This is a very illuminating case of the vibrant existence and strong impact of a cultural industry fostered by the examination system in late imperial China. This output is derived from a course (HIST4920) the P.I. taught between September and December 2015. However, the P.I. kept revising the book manuscript and editing the proof until mid-March 2017, two months after the project start date and one month before the book was formally published. (1.2) In April 1st, 2020, the P.I. secured a book contract with Chung Hwa Books (Hong Kong). The book, entitled Keju yu mingqing shehui 科舉與明清社會 [The imperial civil examination and Ming-Qing society], contains approximately 90,000 Chinese characters as of now and will be expanded to 120,000 before being submitted on April 1st, 2021. The book, to be included into the renowned series Zhonghua Wenshi Congkan中華文史叢刊[Chinese Culture and History Series], studies various aspects of the imperial civil examination system in the Ming-Qing era and further explores the culture industry that served the examination. The book has been accepted for publication by Chung Hwa Books (Hong Kong), as can be proven by the publication agreement in the first page of the book manuscript. Objective 2 of this research project is to create for the public the first ever searchable digital database of Metropolitan Examination topics of the entire Qing dynasty. Accordingly, on March 23rd 2017, the P.I., with the help of his R.A., created such a database in the Knowledge Transfer and elearning page of his department website. The hyperlink is http://www.history.cuhk.edu.hk/proj/keju.html. This searchable digital database contains 19,208 words and Chinese characters, recording exam topics of 112 Metropolitan Examinations in the Qing dynasty, from 1646 to 1904. Objective 3 aims at publishing two journal articles. (3.1) One article has been submitted to the Journal of Chinese Studies中國文化研究所學報[http://www.cuhk.edu.hk/ics/journal/chi/journal.html] and is under review. This paper studies Wang Yirong's answers to the first question of the Third Session of the Imperial Civil Metropolitan Examination of 1880. This first question contained 11 sub-questions, and were all about philology. Both the design of the question and of Wang Yirong王懿榮's answer demonstrated the profound impact of Qian Daxin錢大昕's academic contribution in ancient philology. This serves as an interesting case of the close relationship between the Qing "Evidential Research School" and the Qing Imperial Civil Examination System. The P.I. will definitely update RGC about the progress of the paper submission process. (3.2) One article has been prepared and, upon further revision and expansion, will be submitted to 史林[http://shilin.goooc.net/]. This paper argues that it was exactly the imperial civil examination system that helped prevent regional cultural identity from developing into political separation. The southern part of Fujian, composed of Xinghua, Quanzhou and Zhangzhou, was widely noted and discussed in Ming archives as a region with very unique and strong local identity. However, such strong local identity in no way led to conflict with grander political and cultural narrative of China. The reason, argues this paper, is the imperial civil examination system that set a general ladder of success for candidates from all regions and promised them lucrative rewards. The P.I. will definitely update RGC about the progress of the paper submission process. In particular, Song reveals that Lao Naixuan's "eight-legged essay" has a unique style. As to Other Impact, the P.I. has three items to report. 14647516.label: Major findings and research outcome
14647516.value: Through this project, the P.I. has contributed to the research of the Chinese imperial civil examination system. The project highlights the formation, development and significance of a cultural industry that was commercially driven and exam-oriented, that made its strong presence felt in students' answers to the First Sessions. The orthodox commentaries on the Four Books by Zhu Xi was largely ignored. Through this project, the P.I. has (1) published one coauthored book in 2017; (2) scheduled to publish a scholarly monograph by 2021; (3) created a searchable digital database for topics of the First Sessions of various Metropolitan Examinations in the Qing dynasty; (4) submitted an article for an academic journal; and (5) scheduled to submit another article to an academic journal. In addition, the P.I. has delivered a paper for a conference and trained three B.A. students on the writing of their graduation theses. The P.I. has also delivered five public lectures on the Qing imperial civil examination and invited a scholar from Japan to visit CUHK to deliver two lectures. In the future, the P.I. will further explore the Third Sessions of the imperial civil examination system.

14647516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14647516.value: Contemporary studies of the mechanism of the imperial civil examination are mostly confined to the First Session, i.e., the session that required candidates to write three eight-legged essays and one poem. Comparatively speaking, the Third Session receives little attention. And here lies a historical gold mine that the P.I. thinks highly promising. The Third Session required candidates to answer five essay questions on Classics, historiography and contemporary affairs. With the answers of Wang Yirong as an example, the P.I. has done a preliminary research on the Third Session. The design of questions and answers in various Third Sessions reveal the influence of Qing academic thoughts in general and the impact of the Evidential Research School in particular. The P.I. is poised to (1) develop a searchable digital database of the topics of various Third Sessions, (2) and publish more papers on the study of the Third Sessions.

14647516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14647516.value: Under the Qing imperial civil examination system, students fanatically practiced writing "eight-legged essays" in a bid to succeed. The gist was not about correct understanding (which was assumed) of Confucian classics but about beautiful literary craft: an essay that included an introduction, four pairs of couplet paragraphs (hence the name "eight-legged"), and a conclusion. To master the "eight-legged essay", students needed the help of supplementary materials such as collection of ready-made couplet sentences, model essays, exegetical works, etc.. Where there is demand, there is supply. A market was created for such supplementary materials. Consequently, Zhu Xi's commentaries on the Four Books, in theory the most authoritative textbook for the examination, were in effect "usurped" by these commercially driven and examination-oriented commentaries. If the purpose of the eight-legged essay was to "speak for sages", the purpose was no longer fulfilled by Zhu Xi, but by a cultural industry that was commercially driven and examination-oriented, one that endeavored to "print for profit". This project investigates the industry of this commercialized commentaries and evaluates its impact. It sheds new light on a hitherto uncharted terrain of the study of the imperial civil examination.

14649316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14649316.value: Aim This project is an ethnographic study of volunteering and the ways it is related to the construction of urban culture and identities in Beijing, China today. It examines the formation of a new public culture related to giving and civic participation in the context of changing state and society relations. It focuses specifically on urban volunteering at museums, at NGOs and at residential communities. The project seeks to understand through volunteering the politics of culture – the emerging values and identities surrounding city, class, gender and generation in urban China. Project Background Numerous researches have studied volunteering in terms of personal developments or altruistic practices. Scholars have also turned to analyze the politics of volunteering and links the practice to the retreat of the welfare state and the growth of neoliberal policies in U.K. and U.S. In China, existing research has examined volunteering both in relation to the party-state mobilization campaigns and to the growth of civil society. Attention has yet paid to examine volunteering in relation to the production of new identities and urban public culture. This project focuses on three popular types of urban volunteering in Beijing: “museum volunteers” who deliver free guided tours, “NGO volunteers” who provide services for the needy, and “residential community volunteers” who promote neighborhood safety and public security. It examines how these three types of volunteering have attracted different groups and generations in the capital. It asks whether and how volunteering might give rise to new urban identities related to culture and history, to class and gender, and to the socialist legacy. It also asks how the state deploys these volunteers to manufacture a certain type of cultured, patriotic and caring citizen. Together these questions shall inform the making of urban citizens and public culture in China today. Significance of Project The project contributes to a nuanced ethnographic understanding of volunteering practices in Beijing. It hopes to help answer important questions concerning the growing role of volunteering in the social-cultural and urban identity transformations in China. This project shall contribute to the field of cultural anthropology, which concerns the local reworking of global discourse and practice of civic engagement. The study of volunteering in Beijing, offers a way into this discussion, in examining how the Chinese state, civil society, and urban citizens understand civic identity and giving practices in the context of a one party state regime. 本研究項目是一個當代北京志願者與城市文化和身份認同的田野調查研究。研究目的是關乎一個新的公民參的公共文化和國家社會關係。研究聚焦於博物館，社區和非政府組織的志願者和組織，以了解新的城市，階級，性別和代際的身份認同。 現行的研究大多講述志願者的利他動機和成長經驗。有學者也分析志願作為尤其在西方的新自由主義政策下的國家福利的倒退表現。在中國有分析指出志願是一種新型的共產黨動員策略和一種新的民間社會發展。暫時還沒有研究調查志願和新城市文化與身份的關係。 本項目聚焦三項具有普遍性的志願服務： 博物館志願者，非政府組織的志願者， 和社區的志願者。項目調查折三種服務如何吸引不一樣的年齡，性別和階級群體。研究問題包括志願服務如何形成新的城市身份和文化， 與社會主義時代的奉獻傳統關係如何。研究同時敲問國家如何利用志願作為一種培養愛國公民的手段。 研究項目將會讓大家了解當代中國北京的志願行為和文化。更重要的是，研究會讓我們了解當代中國的新的城市身份認同和城市文化。

14649316.label: Realisation of objectives
14649316.value: The first objective has been fully achieved. Extensive ethnographic fieldwork and interviews works have been conducted with volunteering initiatives at museums, NGOS, residential communities in Beijing. Moreover, the PI has conducted interviews with feminist volunteers in protests, which forms a contrasting case from the state/danwei organized volunteers. In all these examinations, the role of the state has been looked at closely in terms of mobilizing, deploying and suppressing these various volunteer initiatives. The second objective has been achieved. The ethnographic fieldwork has looked at the few types of volunteering in relation to the formation of urban identity, gender, class and generational subjectivities. My current writing is analyzing how the Chinese government and media are mobilizing gender, race, and class differences in shaping an ideal and compliant citizen in the neighborhood. Through these volunteers organizing, I found the Chinese state is actively shaping the nativist, gender, racial and class boundaries of active citizens. Women of lower class, and people of migrant and ethnic backgrounds are usually seen as target of surveillance by nativist residents in these volunteer narratives. In the case of neighborhood volunteering, I also put together interviewees’ narratives of self-fulfillment with the official narratives of anti-terrorism together. I also contrast my interviews with netizens’ understanding of volunteers in the form of online satire literature. The third objective has also been achieved. I have looked at volunteering as a complex process of citizen making in which not only the state actively engineers model "civilized citizens" but that various work units (danwei) are also experimenting with many other civic or social initiatives. This is especially true in the case of museum volunteers. Many educated, middle class background women and men joined such initiative also to learn culture, tradition and history. These museum volunteers could be highly reflective individuals whose personal views do not easily align with the official narratives of the nation. In the big wave of museum fever, where millions crowd into various exhibits, museum volunteers have found themselves torn in contesting narratives of personal growth, serve the people, cultural rejuvenation, and a class anxiety of lacking taste for culture. The last objective has also been achieved. My current writing is analyzing how these various initiatives are contributing to a new urban public culture under the slogan of the China Dream and a nationalist identity that is also based on civic and learned participation. The case of the feminist volunteer organizing is the most interesting one that is also contesting the official China Dream narrative that is sexist and male oriented.

14649316.label: Major findings and research outcome
14649316.value: This research has examine closed connections among active volunteer mobilization, citizen-making projects and gender media campaigns in the last decade of contemporary China. Through ethnographic research, the research has found that the state has been using massively powerful media strategies and volunteering campaigns to promote civic nationalist belongings and ideal citizenship in China. The research is teasing out the ways volunteering is related to gender images of desirable womanhood, class images of the cultivated citizens, and campaigns of urban security and surveillance control. Through the feminist volunteers, the research has also found that grassroot organizing is also fighting a battle to contests the official discourse of the China Dream that is male and state centered. The book contributes to the global discussion of nationalism, in which cultural identity, governance and civic responses have become newly configured in the last decade of neo-liberalizing economy and intense migration. The volunteering cases provides a special insight for the case of China, in which nationalism is simultaneously about party-state tightening control, civic volunteering initiatives, soft power as well as gender imaginations. Research outcome has come in many forms. Last year when the PI was doing a sabbatical leave in the United Kingdom, individual presentations based on this resarech as been shared at invited seminars at the Middle eastern and China Studies at University of Cambridge, at the Oxford China Center at University of Oxford, and Modern Languages and Cultural Studies at Westminster University.

14649316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14649316.value: The research can be further developed in the future by comparing the cases of civic nationalism and urban identities in China with that of other Asian countries. The PI is in the process of writing up a book manuscript. Currently the PI is in touch with editors of a few publishers: Cambridge University Press, UC Press of California, and Amsterdam University Press. The research has developed into several journal article writings. One is under peer-reviewed in the journal of Feminist Studies.

14649316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14649316.value: Currently, the mainstream media has provided a picture of Chinese nationalism, led by the communist party-state, featuring politically and economically aggressive projects such as the highspeed railway, the One Belt One Road, and very soon, the cultural and sport campaign of hosting the Winter Olympics. The research is significant in providing an understanding of nationalism from a bottom up perspective. It is an ethnographic exploration of citizen identity and national sentiments in contemporary China. Based on the cases of urban volunteering initiatives, the research examines how citizens in China understands their civic participations, their notions of citizenship rights, and their relations with the official discourse of the China Dream, in an economically growing yet politically authoritarian party-dictatorship context. Most importantly, it provides nuanced analysis on the ways the ideal citizen is understood and mediated in specific gender, class, racial images. This research will provide an important understanding of how civic nationalism is understood, engineered and contested in China, in the global context of anti-immigrant and pro-surveillance sentiments.

14649416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14649416.value: This project will provide an in-depth analysis of the current condition of the humanities disciplines in higher education in Hong Kong, including the issues and problems they face and the contributions they make. It aims to create an objective picture of the “value” and contributions of humanities degrees in relation to the needs and growth of Hong Kong. It will do so by using both quantitative survey data, and qualitative interview data. The former comprise labour data for humanities graduates’ job destinations, which will be compared with data of these same job fields for the Hong Kong economy as a whole (Kraeger 6) in order to provide a concrete picture of the contributions of humanities degrees to the economic needs and growth of Hong Kong in the past two decades. The latter comprise two sets of interviews. The first set is with humanities graduates from 15 to 20 years ago to explore more subjective constructions of the “value” of a humanities degree over an individual’s lifetime, although this may also take the form of social or economic contributions the individual has made. The second set is with senior humanities practitioners in Hong Kong asking for their assessment of the value of a humanities degree and indeed of the humanities themselves. Towards the end of the project, the results of this study will be published as a report. They will also be furthered and disseminated by holding a roundtable discussion with experts in the humanities from Hong Kong, including at the Academy of the Humanities in Hong Kong, and other countries. These will be collected and published in separate proceedings. The importance of the study lies in how it will, for the first time, give clear evidence of the important and often undocumented contribution of the humanities in Hong Kong. By using two different types of data (survey and interview data), the research will give a rounded picture of the value and contributions of a humanities degree which can speak to both insiders and outsiders to the field. The results of this study can concretely demonstrate what utility the individualist and interpretative approaches in humanities subjects, conventionally thought less directly useful to society, in fact have. Last but not least, the empirical research in this study can support informed decision-making on the allocation of funding and resources by the government in future. 本計畫將深入分析本港高等教育之人文專業的現況，包括人文專業所面對的情況、問題及貢獻。本計畫旨在客觀地評估人文學位對應香港的需要及發展的「價值」及貢獻。 本計畫將採用量性問卷及質性訪問兩種數據。前者比較人文學科畢業生的就業數據及相關行業在本港整體經濟發展的數據（Kraeger 6)，從而檢視人文學位在過去二十年對於香港的經濟需要及發展所發揮的實際績效。後者為兩組訪問。第一組訪問的對象是十五至二十年前的人文學科畢業生。訪問內容探討畢業生主觀地認為人文學位對其個人成長的「價值」，同時亦評估畢業生對社經發展的貢獻。第二組訪問的對象是在本港從事人文教育的資深工作者。訪問將邀請他們評價人文學位及人文學科本身的價值。 本計畫的末部將整合上述研究的結果並發佈報告。研究員將舉辦圓桌論壇，並在會上向本港及海外的人文學科專家，包括香港人文學院，派發報告及進行跟進討論。而研究員將收集並分冊發佈跟進討論的內容。 本計畫的價值在於首次清晰地申述本港重要卻鮮有實質紀錄的人文學科的貢獻。透過收集兩種不同性質的數據（問卷及訪問），本研究能令行內及行外人掌握人文學位之價值及貢獻的全面狀況 。本研究的結果能具體地證明人文學科中個人主義及詮譯模式的效用，反駁傳統上認為這些模式對社會發展只有較為間接的作用的看法。 最後，本計畫的實證研究將支持政府在未來有效地分配高等教育的基金及資源。

14650816.label: Project Objectives
14650816.value: Scholars in the past have paid particular attention to either the relationship between history and poetry in Wu’s poetry or the artistic value of his works. The proposed project, at once a literary and cultural history one, will open up a new horizon for the study of Wu Weiye. I created the “Three Contextualizations Method” (i.e., literary contextualization, biographical contextualization, historical contextualization) for the study of Ming-Qing literature, which colleagues in the field have found valuable. I will employ this method in my new book on Wu Weiye to further test its effectiveness. I will publish the results of my research in scholarly journals. After revision, they will appear in book form. I will attend academic conferences and accept speech invitations to share my ideas on Wu Weiye’s poetry, and to further promote literary and cultural studies of Qing literature. I will offer a class on Wu Weiye and other Qing poets through the Department of Chinese Language and Literature (CUHK) for the purpose of attracting and training more students to conduct research on Qing literature.
