15129116.label: Realisation of objectives
15129116.value: Objective 1: Ultrasound examinations of the parotid and submandibular glands of the subjects were carried out by the same operator at each time interval. The examination was carried out with a 12 to 5 MHz linear transducer. The echogenicity of the parotid and submandibular glands was assessed and subjectively classified into hypoechoic, isoechoic and hyperechoic when compared to the adjacent mylohyoid/masseter muscle. In the assessment of echogenicity, the gland was considered to be homogeneous when its parenchyma had a uniform echogenicity, whereas it was considered heterogeneous when it showed non-uniform parenchymal echogenicity. For assessing the haemodynamic condition of the glands, the blood flow velocity (peak systolic velocity PSV, end diastolic velocity EDV) and vascular resistance (resistive index RI, pulsatility index PI) were measured using the power. For each gland, the mean PSV, EDV, RI and PI calculated will be used for analysis. The MRI examination was conducted in the 1.5T MRI unit in the Department of Diagnostic Radiology, Li Ka Shing Faculty of Medicine, University of Hong Kong. The scanning volume covered from the base of skull to the hyoid bone. The scanning sequences included: T1 axial and sagittal, and T2 axial and sagittal scans with slice thickness of 3 mm and no inter-slice gap. Images generated from the scanner were transferred to the workstation equipped with MIM Maestro where the images were displayed and the delineation of the parotid and submandibular glands was conducted. The volume of the each gland was calculated by the system. The MRI results at each time interval was compared with the pre-RT MRI images, from which the percentage changes in gross morphology at each time interval was generated. Trend lines of the mean value of the measured parameters from pre-Rt to 48 months post-RT were plotted to display the pattern of changes with respect to time to illustrate the progression pattern. Objective 2: All subjects were required to complete a structured and validated xerostomia questionnaire adopted from Zimmerman et al (1997) at each time interval. The questionnaire consisted of five questions and was used to assess the condition of xerostomia by collecting the patients’ comments on the severity of xerostomia in terms of its impact on their daily life including (1) difficulty in swallowing and mastication, (2) difficulty in speech, (3) interruption of sleep, (4) discomfort of mouth and (5) dryness of mouth at the time of this study (Wu et al 2011). A continuous scale from 0-10 was used to assess the severity of individual conditions, with “0” implying the least severe condition and “10” the most severe condition. Apart from the individual question scores, an overall “impact factor” (IF), which was also calculated by taking the average scores of the five questions, was used to indicate the patient’s subjective xerostomia severity. In addition, each patient was also asked to give a subjective assessment on the percentage of salivary function at the time of assessment as compared to their salivary function before radiation treatment (residue percentage = RP). Trend lines of the mean value of the measured parameters from pre-Rt to 48 months post-RT were plotted to display the pattern of changes with respect to time to illustrate the progression pattern. Objective 3: To estimate the doses received by the parotid and submandibular glands, the subjects’ IMRT treatment plans were retrieved from the Eclipse treatment planning system. The doses (mean dose, V30) to each gland will be calculated by generating their respectively dose volume histogram. The correlations between doses and morphological changes at each time interval was investigated using Pearson correlation test.

15129116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15129116.value: The saliva flow rates of the parotid gland and submandibular gland showed significant decrease of over 80% at 6 months post-radiotherapy (RT) and stayed at similar low level thereafter. There was no significant correlation between post-RT saliva flow rate changes and mean doses received by the glands. The feelings of dryness and comfortability of mouth in patients deteriorated significantly at 6 months post-RT. Great impacts of xerostomia on sleeping, speaking, eating and wearing dentures were also observed at 6 months post-RT and they remained fairly constant afterward. The volume of the parotid and submandibular glands demonstrated a significant drop from pre-RT to 6 months post-RT. The parotid gland changed from hyperechoic before RT to either isoechoic or hypoechoic after treatment. The resistive index and pulsatility index decreased from pre-RT to 6 month post-RT, then started to increase at 12 month time interval. Both peak systolic velocity and end diastolic velocity increased after 6 months post-RT then followed a decreasing trend up to 24 months post-RT. There was mild correlation between post-RT gland dose and gland volume, but not with haemodynamic changes. The average mean doses to parotid and submandibular glands were around 35 Gy in IMRT of NPC patients, which significantly reduced the saliva flow rates of the parotid and submandibular glands. The impact was greatest at 6 months post-RT and was long lasting. Patients’ quality of life was affected by the severity of xerostomia and the effects showed similar pattern as the saliva flow rates. Radiation from IMRT caused shrinkage of parotid and submandibular glands in NPC patients. It also changed the echogenicity and vascular condition of the parotid gland. The most significant changes were observed at 6 months after radiotherapy.

15129116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15129116.value: Dry mouth is one of the common radiation-induced complications in NPC patients after radiotherapy. The cause of xerostomia is due to the damage of the parotid and submandibular glands. This longitudinal study investigated the radiation induced damage to the salivary glands by applying ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging on NPC patients before, during and after radiotherapy at 3-6 months intervals up to 24 months. Validated questionnaire about the severity of dry mouth was also completed by the patients during each assessment intervals. The results of this study demonstrated that there were significant impacts on the salivary glands due to radiation, which included effect of the gland volume, saliva flow rate and patient life quality. In addition, the pattern of changes in the parotid and submandibular glands during a course of radiotherapy and its relationship to the mean dose to these salivary gland were also studied. This project provides better understanding of the relationship of radiation dose and progression pattern of major salivary gland changes, which can help in better prediction of the complication and provision of better management of the condition for the patients.

15159416.label: Realisation of objectives
15159416.value: The research objectives are 100% achieved. The project resulted in a number of conference presentations and journal publications on the topic of dual-task walking in stroke patients. We studied more than 150 chronic stroke patients, and were able to thoroughly examine the effect of task choice and stroke characteristics on dual-task mobility performance. We were also able to design an innovative dual-task exercise training program that was shown to improve dual-task walking function in chronic stroke patients.

15159416.label: Major findings and research outcome
15159416.value: The findings revealed that the dual-task interference phenomenon during walking is a substantial problem among people with stroke. The degree of interference is highly dependent on the type and complexity of the mobility and cognitive tasks chosen in the dual-task testing paradigm. Poorer dual-task walking performance is significantly associated with more severe motor impairment in the affected lower extremity. The dual-task walking performance in cortical and subcortical stroke patients was largely similar. In addition, we found that an 8-week cognitive-motor dual-task exercise program was effective in reducing cognitive-motor interference during walking, and also decreasing the fall rate and fall-related injuries by 25% and 22% respectively. The treatment effect was well maintained for at least 8 weeks after the termination of the exercise program.

15159416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15159416.value: Further study should examine the activity in different brain regions during dual-task walking in stroke patients, and how the activation pattern varies with stroke severity and location of the brain lesion. Further research should also explore the neural mechanisms associated with the improvement in dual-task walking function after dual-task exercise training. A new GRF research grant application has been submitted based on these research concepts. The dual-exercise program, proven to be effective in this project, has potential for widespread implementation in daily clinical settings that offer stroke rehabilitation services. We have started a pilot scheme to implement the exercise program in one of the non-governmental organization that provides stroke rehabilitation services. We will evaluate the program after one year of implementing this program. A press conference aimed at promoting this exercise program is under preparation.

15159416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15159416.value: Community walking requires the individual to perform walking while engaging in another cognitive task simultaneously, such as talking on the phone while walking or attending to traffic signals while crossing the street. Stroke patients often have more deficits in dual-task walking relative their age-matched counterparts. The project has shed light into the factors that affect the dual-task walking function in stroke patients. More importantly, the project has resulted in an innovative and economical community-based dual-task exercise training program. After 8 weeks of training, stroke patients show significant improvement in dual-task walking ability and there was a substantial reduction of fall risk and fall-related injuries.

15164216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15164216.value: Neurogenesis, or production of new neurons, could be found in the hippocampus and olfactory system and it is suggested to take part in spatial memory formation, emotional regulation and olfactory discrimination. This particular type of neural plasticity attracted attentions since it serves as a potential treatment target in disorders related to memory formation, emotional regulation and social functioning. Neurogenesis is subjected to the regulation of different external stimulus, such as multiple sensory stimulations in enriched environment. However, apart from olfactory stimulation, it remains obscure whether neurogenesis could be stimulated by a single sensory modality. Recently it is reported that presentation of tactile stimulation promotes neurogenesis in the dorsal horn of spinal cord, and tickling increased neurogenesis in rats. These finding suggest that tactile stimulation may be a pro-neurogenic stimulus for hippocampal neurogenesis, and may consequently affect emotional and cognitive behaviors. Tactile stimulation is employed in rehabilitation to enhance recovery of cognitive functions and emotion. For instance, a brushing protocol which provides tactile and pressure sensation is used to treat children with anxiety and emotional liability. Repeated stimulation in the form of massage was also shown to reduce anxiety levels in burn injury patients. As tactile stimulation is non-invasive, inexpensive and simple to apply, it serves as an attractive rehabilitative option in different conditions. The therapeutic effect of tactile stimulation is hypothesized to rely on the promotion of neural plasticity, while the theoretical basis and exact mechanisms remains largely elusive. The lack of understanding discourages generalization of tactile stimulation in different conditions and the further development of related treatment methods. Based on the clinical usage of tactile stimulation and the neurogenic effect of tactile stimulation, we hypothesized that tactile stimulation promotes neurogenesis in the brain and affects emotional behaviors and neurogenesis is a mechanism underlying the therapeutic effect of tactile stimulation. We propose to examine the effect of tactile stimulation on an anxiety animal model induced by hypercortisolemia. The effect of tactile stimulation on affective behaviors, hippocampal neurogenesis and the molecular regulation of neurogenesis will be examined. The necessity of neurogenesis will be determined by blocking neurogenesis. Preliminary result shows that repeated tactile stimulation for two weeks reversed the anxiety and depression-like, which is accompanied with enhanced hippocampal neurogenesis and dendritic formation of new neurons. These results support our hypothesis, and the result would provide novel knowledge on the regulation of hippocampal neurogenesis and mechanism of treatment related to tactile stimulation. 神經元新生(Neurogenesis)，即新神經元的產生，可在海馬和嗅覺系統中發現。神經元新生參與空間記憶的形成、情緒控制和嗅覺辨識。作為一種特定類型的神經可塑性，神經元新生吸引了廣泛的關注，因為它能影響記憶相關疾病的發展、情緒的調節和社交功能，故擁有充當潛在治療目標的可能性。不同的外部刺激(例如在充滿豐富感官刺激的環境中)均有可能激發神經元新生。然而，除了嗅覺刺激以外，現時仍不清楚神經元新生是否可以通過其他單一的感官模式來激發。最近的研究表明，提供觸覺刺激可以激發脊髓的神經元新生；另外，呵癢亦能激發大鼠的神經元新生。這些發現提示了觸覺刺激可以激發海馬的神經元新生，從而影響情緒與認知行為。 觸覺刺激被廣泛應用於康復治療中，增強認知功能和情感的恢復。例如，一種可同時提供觸覺與壓力刺激的梳刷方法，被用於治療焦慮和有情感障礙的兒童，而重覆性的按摩刺激能夠減低燒傷病人的焦慮程度。由於觸覺刺激具有非侵入性、廉價及容易實施的優點，故是一項具有吸引力的治療選項。觸覺刺激的治療效果可能建基於促進神經可塑性，但理論及實際的機制仍然未解，缺乏對此治療的了解限制了這治療方法的普及性與進一步發展。 基於觸覺刺激的臨床使用和對脊髓的神經元新生有激發作用，我們假設；一. 觸覺刺激會激發腦內的神經元新生和影響情感行為；二. 神經元新生是帶來觸覺刺激治療效果的根本機制。我們建議研究觸覺刺激在焦慮性動物模型上的治療效果，情感行為、海馬神經元新生及其份子機制均會被檢測。神經元新生的必要性將通過壓抑細胞增生証明。初步結果表明，兩星期的重複觸覺刺激可以避免皮質酮導致的焦慮、抑鬱及神經元新生的壓抑。這些結果支持了我們的假說，亦對觸覺刺激治療的理解提供新的知識和方法。

15164216.label: Realisation of objectives
15164216.value: The project aims to examine the effect of tactile stimulation on adult hippocampal neurogenesis and affective behaviors. To investigate the potential therapeutic effect of tactile stimulation (Objective 1), we applied tactile stimulation on the whole body of animal subjects with reference to a brushing protocol used in rehabilitation (Wilberger’s protocol). To simulate the affective disturbances, we used a hypercortisolemia animal model to induce depression- and anxiety-like behaviors in animal subjects. To determine whether repeated tactile stimulation increases hippocampal neurogenesis and affect emotional behaviors in healthy animals, animal experiment which divided the subjects into two experimental groups (Control and brush groups) was carried out. The brush groups received brushing treatment daily while control group received similar handling but no brushing treatment. The administration of brush treatment was applied on different body regions including dorsal trunk and lumbar region, whisker pad (an area with rich supply of tactile sensory receptors), forelimbs and hindlimbs of the animals by using the head of a conventional toothbrush which is attached to an analog push force gauge to monitor the force applied continuously. In order to differentiate the effect of acute, subchronic and chronic treatment, the treatment periods were divided into acute (2 hours), subchronic (14 days) and chronic (28 days). To assess neurogenesis in the hippocampus, bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU, 50mg/kg) was intraperitoneally injected at the end of treatment periods, which labels the newly proliferative cells. Brain sections which contain hippocampus were immunostained with anti-BrdU antibody in 1-in-12 series, and immunoreactive cells were quantified by unbiased stereology. After provision of acute brush treatment, cell proliferation and neuronal differentiation of neuronal progenitor cells were found to be not affected by the treatment. However, the dendritic complexity of immature new neurons, as indicated by sholl analysis of doublecortin-immunoreactive cells in the hippocampus, was shown to be improved in the brushing group. We speculate that the alteration in dendritic complexity but not in cell proliferation/differentiation is due to the fact that dendritic formation in immature neurons are more dynamic. Depression-like behavior, assessed by forced swimming test, was found to be significantly increased in the tactile stimulation group. This is in contrast to the original expectation that tactile stimulation would reduce depression-like behavior. Animals received brushing showed a tendency to have reduced anxiety-like behavior but the experimental results are not statistically significant. From the result of subchronic and chronic treatment, affective behaviors were found to be different from the acute experiment: depression-like behavior was not induced in the brushing group, while anxiety-like behavior was significantly reduced in the treated animals after 28 days’ treatment. Social anxiety was not affected by the treatment. From these results it is possible that the treatment may need to be applied for a sustained period in order to exert its effect. In terms of cell proliferation, no significant difference can be found between the control and brush group with subchronic and chronic treatment period. However, being similar to the acute experiment, the dendritic complexity of the brush groups was found to be significantly higher than the control group. To examine whether the Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis (which regulate the fight/flight response) is affected by tactile stimulation, the weight of adrenal gland was also assessed, and no significant difference in weight was observed between the treatment and control groups. Thus in healthy animals it is likely that brushing alone may only induce minimal effect on morphological and affective aspects, while the effect may change and will be dependent on the length of treatment received. In summary, the objective 1 is achieved. To determine whether tactile stimulation shows beneficial effect on affective behavioral disturbances in disease model of depression (Objective 2 and 3), an animal experiment which adopts the hypercortisolemia animal model was used. Animals were divided into 4 groups: 1) Control group with daily handling and vehicle injection; 2) Cort group with daily high dose corticosterone treatment (40 mg/kg, subcutaneous injection); 3) Brush group with daily tactile stimulation alone and 4) Brush+cort group with corticosterone treatment and brushing. The duration of treatment was decided to last for 14 days, as both subchronic and chronic treatment showed similar effect in experiments abovementioned. Disturbance in affective behavior and neurogenesis suppression were induced by high dose corticosterone treatment and the potential therapeutic effect of brushing was determined. After treatment for 14 days, animals were subjected to behavioral tests, followed by sacrifice at day 16. Three cohorts of animals were involved in this experiment to examine (1) cell proliferation, (2) cell survival and (3) plasma hormonal level. To assess cell proliferation, animals received BrdU injection at day 14. For cell survival, animals were injected with BrdU at day 1, before the start of treatment. For cohorts (1) and (2), animals were sacrificed by transcardial perfusion. In terms of general health, hypercortisolemia treatment significantly suppressed the weight gain of the animals. Interestingly, brushing can promote the weight gain significantly in both corticosterone treated and non-treated groups. As similar to the result in subacute experiment abovementioned, brushing reduced anxiety-like behavior in corticosterone-treated rats in the result of open field test. Corticosterone slightly increased anxiety-like behavior while brush treatment reversed the condition. Rats received co-treatment showed a similar anxiety-like level as Ctrl group. Social anxiety was assessed by social interaction test. Corticosterone treatment has lower number of social interaction than control group (Ctrl vs. Cort) but co-treatment with brushing increase the interactions significantly (Cort vs. Brush+Cort). Rats received co-treatment showed a similar number of positive social interactions as Ctrl group. For depression-like behavior, brushing reduced corticosterone-induced depression-like behavior as indicated by the duration of immobility during the FST. One-way ANOVA and Post-hoc analysis showed that 14 days corticosterone treatment significantly induced depression-like behavior (Ctrl vs. Cort), while the brush treatment reduced the level of depression-like behavior in corticosterone-treated rats (Cort vs. Brush+Cort). Rats received co-treatment showed a similar level of depression-like behavior as Ctrl group. However, brush treatment slightly increased depression-like behavior in control rats (Ctrl vs. Brush), which is similar to result in the acute experiment of brushing alone. At morphological level, brushing reverted corticosterone-suppressed hippocampal neurogenesis by enhancing neuronal differentiation. The quantification of doublecortin-immunoreactive cells indicates the effect of corticosterone and brushing on neuronal differentiation. Corticosterone treatment significantly suppressed neuronal differentiation (Ctrl vs. Cort) while brush treatment reverted the suppressive effect (Cort vs. Brush+Cort). In summary, objective 2 is achieved. To evaluate neuronal differentiation, co-labeling of DCX/BrdU+ cells were carried out. Brush treatment increased the number of co-labeled cells (Ctrl vs. Brush and Cort vs. Brush+Cort), however, the results are not in statistical significance (NS). For the assessment of plasma level of brain-derived neurotrophin factor (BDNF) level (Objective 4), it was shown that corticosterone treated group didn’t show the expected down regulation of BDNF. While after the suppression of neurogenesis by anticancer drug, the effect of brushing was still present. These implies that neurogenesis may be an associated but not essential factor underlying the beneficial effects. In summary, objectives 2-4 are achieved.

15164216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15164216.value: The results and conclusions generated from the current project resulted in 3 published peer-reviewed papers, two manuscripts under review and one conference presentation. In one of the publication (Liao), the potential of targeting neurogenesis and endogenous neural precursor cells as a means for CNS-related disorder was discussed. On top of tactile stimulation, we also extended the study to another sensory stimulation (olfaction), and it was found that the depression-like behavior induced by corticosterone can also be reversed by odor, with the association of neurogenesis (Sanchez-Vidana). Two other publications with the results generated from the current study were under review.

15164216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15164216.value: The results from the current study provides evidence to support the clinical practice of applying tactile stimulation and brushing to tackle emotional disturbances in rehabilitation treatment. The treatment may be effective to alleviate affective disturbances including depression and anxiety, and may act as a potential adjunct therapy for depression and anxiety disorders. The mechanisms underlying the beneficial effect of brushing is worth further exploration, which may beyond neurogenesis.

15164216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15164216.value: Tactile stimulation is known as a commonly used method to relieve anxiety and pressure, and it was adopted in rehabilitation to alleviate symptoms related to stress. The result from this study has shown that with animal experiments, tactile stimulation shows effect in alleviation of depression and anxiety, and this is associated with the change of endogenous stem cells in the hippocampus, a brain region related to emotional regulation. With tactile stimulation, the endogenous neural stem cells showed increase in number, and the dendritic outgrowth of the new neurons are found to be improved by tactile stimulation. The effect of tactile stimulation is proven in this study, and the benefit may be due to regulation of stem cells in the central nervous system.

15200616.label: Project Objectives
15200616.value: How to acquire/incorporate an ontology sufficient to help with inference between concepts in the generalization hierarchy: Firstly, we need to investigate the appropriate schemes to split the commonsense knowledge into two components with appropriate knowledge representation power and efficiency. Secondly, we need to select from appropriate English and Chinese resources to build ontology for word to concept mapping. We also need to develop inference mechanism for concept generalization to help instantiate new knowledge for emotion analysis. How to acquire an affect-linked commonsense knowledgebase: We need to select from appropriate English and Chinese resources to set up the initial commonsense knowledgebase and develop methods to link the commonsense knowledgebase to emotions. How to make use of resources in other languages such as English to jump start the acquisition process and to facilitate the gradual build-up of the Chinese knowledgebase and other resources: We need to consolidate the resources to bootstrap the construction of emotion-linked Chinese commonsense knowledge base and ontology through cross-lingual knowledge acquisition, and develop methods to extend the Chinese commonsense knowledgebase using available Chinese running text.

How to make use of resources in other languages such as English to jump start the acquisition process and to facilitate the gradual build-up of the Chinese knowledgebase and other resources: We need to consolidate the resources to bootstrap the construction of emotion-linked Chinese commonsense knowledge base and ontology through cross-lingual knowledge acquisition, and develop methods to extend the Chinese commonsense knowledgebase using available Chinese running text.

15200616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200616.value: Emotion analysis is attracting much research interests in recent years as social media has become a common platform for expression of opinions and emotional support in online communities. Current emotional analysis methods for the Chinese language mostly focus on lexical words that are explicitly linked to emotions defined in some affect lexicon. Other studies extend it to lexical affinity with emotions. However, there are only limited means to analyze emotions triggered by text without explicit affective words. For example, in the sentence “I went swimming, but it was closed due to public holiday.”, the disappointment is only expressed implicitly. Understanding the emotion expressed in such text requires commonsense knowledge at the conceptual level beyond the surface form of text. The goal of this proposal is to investigate appropriate methods to build Chinese commonsense knowledgebase for emotion analysis. The main challenge is to address the scalability issue as knowledge inference can be intractable when the system grows to certain size. The second challenge is to acquire affect-linked commonsense knowledge for Chinese — a resource poor language. Our proposed method is to divide commonsense knowledge into two parts. The first is an affect-linked Chinese commonsense knowledgebase; the second is an ontology containing a set of common concepts with relations to other concepts for generalization. The ontology provides background knowledge for inference with reduced search space. The linking of an affect-linked commonsense knowledgebase to a concept based ontology makes conceptual inference more efficient, as the knowledge can be kept at a more manageable size. The proposed work needs to address three main issues: 1) How to acquire/incorporate an ontology sufficient to help with inference between concepts in the generalization hierarchy; 2) how to acquire an affect-linked commonsense knowledgebase; 3) how to make use of resources in other languages such as English to jump start the acquisition process and to facilitate the gradual build-up of the Chinese knowledgebase and other resources. The ability to feel emotions is an intrinsic property of human beings and our affect-linked commonsense knowledge captures this information for emotion analysis. This work will bring the current study on emotion analysis to a more comprehensive level. It can also empower computer applications to understand human emotions and even to express emotions like human beings. The methodology developed for knowledge acquisition can also be applicable to other fields, such as information retrieval, machine translation, and text summarization. 近年來社交媒體已經成為人們表達觀點和尋求感情共鳴的平臺。情感分析也因此受到很大的關注。目前中文的情感分析方法主要集中在抽取情感詞或者情感關聯詞的文本分析。然而，即使文本中沒有直接的情感描述也可以表達某種情感。在例句“昨天我去游泳，由於是公共假日，游泳館關門了” 中，表達了失望的情緒，但文本中沒有直接和失望相關的詞語。對這種文本中情感的理解需要文本形式之外的常識知識。 本項目旨在研究如何建立有助情感分析的常識知識庫。其中最大的挑戰是常識知識庫的可擴展性因為知識的推理在資料增長到一定程度後會面臨不可處理性。另外，電腦處理技術中所需的中文語言資源相對貧乏，因此我們還需直面如何獲取與情感相關聯的中文常識知識。 我們提出的方法是將常識知識分成兩部分，第一部分是建立一個和情感相關聯的中文常識知識庫。第二部分是建立一個概念知識的本體，用來做知識的抽象和整合。本體提供推理需要的背景知識，並減小搜索空間。因此提高情感分析中常識推理的效益。此項目的工作需解決三個主要問題: 第一，如何獲取一個有助概念框架下推理的本體；第二，如何獲取與中文情感有關聯的常識知識庫；第三，如何利用其它語言的資源來有效啟動中文常識知識獲取的過程，並建立中文所需的相關資源。 表達和體會情感是人類固有的能力，而我們所建立的與情感關聯的常識知識庫就是為了獲取這樣的信息用以輔助中文文本的情感分析。該工作有助更全面的進行情感分析。其結果可以幫助現有的應用理解情感表現形式並提高電腦應用中情感表達的多樣性和真實度。研究結果中的知識獲取方法也可以使用在如信息檢索、機器翻譯及文本摘要等其他領域的知識獲取中。

15200616.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200616.value: In this Project, we focused on the use of deep learning based methods to acquire common sense knowledge linked to emotions and improve performance using these acquired knowledge. The first major effort is to acquire affective knowledge. We explored the use of lexical knowledge as well as projected affected information from deep learning models to improve performance in affective tasks. With deep learning models, some of the traditional background knowledge, which we refer to as common sense knowledge, are implicitly given in data representation as context learnt becomes a part of common sense knowledge. The main issue is how to make these implicit knowledge explicit. We explored two approaches. The first is to make use of available sentiment/affective lexicon as explicit knowledge and make good use of in deep learning models for affective analysis. A number of journal publications were produced including ( J3, C1, C4). The second one is acquire explicit knowledge using deep learning models to obtain affective lexicons using different affective models including the use of affective control theory to acquire affective knowledge using EPA model and VAD models as well as eye tracking data with very good result( J1, J4, C4, C6). Our proposed affect driven approaches to incorporate affective knowledge into LSTM learning models have obtained improvement in three large benchmark datasets for emotion prediction. As for the use of ontological information, we working on incorporating domain specific knowledge to improve multi-labeled emotion classification with good improvement (C5). The use of hypernym for lexical augmentation as ontological information is also proven to be effective (C6). As much as we have success in using English resources and data, the acquisition of Chinese common sense knowledge is still lacks sufficient resources. This is particularly lacking for web text in social media. So, one of the attempt by use is to look at other cues in Chinese social media text. Our exploration include the use of code switch information, tags, as well as link information (J2, J5, C2 ). In order to prove the acquired knowledge is useful, we focused on Chinese irony detection as a downstream task directly related to affective analysis. We build an annotated corpus for irony detection, as well as on irony evaluation (C3, C7). Two PhD students were supported by this project, one graduated and is working in Huawei. The other student is also scheduled to graduate in the first half of 2021.

15200616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200616.value: There are two main directions: 1. Since Chinese sentiment knowledge resources are relatively scarce, we plan to use machine learning models to generate Chinese sentiment knowledge resources from other sentiment resources language, e.g. English. The form of these knowledge resources include but limit to sentiment lexicon with polarity, EPA vectors, VAD vectors, sentiment related knowledge graph. The translation system and multi-lingual embeddings are initially proposed to use. 2. Knowledge graph can provide structured and relations of higher dimensions. We plan to set up schema to incorporate current knowledgebase that organize the conceptual entities in different format or symbolic methods. Then, integrating these knowledge terms into natural language processing tasks can be further investigated.

15200616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200616.value: The project investigate how background information can be used to help with affective analysis especially for words in text that have no explicit affective knowledge. Our findings include using existing affective resources such as affective lexicons in deep learning models so that such information can be effectively being used in deep learning models to improve performance of sentiment analysis as well as emotion classification. We are particularly interested in acquire common sense knowledge currently provided by deep learning based representation models implicitly based on learnt context information. By using some available lexicons, we are able to just start and extend affective lexicons as explicit affect knowledge. Even if many words do not have explicit affective knowledge linked to them, we can still obtain them using regression analysis and augmentation techniques. This work proves that affective knowledge can be learnt through deep learning based representations models even though such information was implicitly contained. An application task of Chinese irony detection was also studied in this work leveraging on English, hypertext, coding switching detection using machine learning methods.

15201416.label: Realisation of objectives
15201416.value: In this project, four objectives have been proposed, and all of them have been fully accomplished by end of this project. The past decade has witnessed the prosperity in R&D of enabling technologies to facilitate human exploration of outer space. Of particular interest are technologies that can enhance the integrity, durability and airworthiness of spacecraft, as typified by burgeoning structural health monitoring (SHM). In such a backdrop, this research project was proposed based on the recognition that the uniqueness of space applications makes the deployment of SHM on space structures significantly distinct from that in other ordinary engineering realms. In particular, the damage committed to spacecraft by the debris clouds, as a consequence of hypervelocity impact (HVI), features hundreds of craters and micro-cracks chaotically scattered, and evaluation of such highly specific damage is far beyond the detectability of conventional SHM methods. With this motivation, a probabilistic SHM strategy, allying ameliorated passive acoustic emission with active nonlinear ultrasonic-based characterization, has been well developed via this GRF project. It main includes the following aspects: 1. Dedicated modeling and simulation based on 3D smooth-particle hydrodynamics have been conducted, to advance the insight into debris cloud-caused damage and HVI-induced waves; 2. With a novel sensing philosophy to accommodate space applications, a nano-engineered in-situ sensing network coating has been developed, and deposited on structures, to passively perceive HVI-induced waves; 3. Acousto-ultrasonic waves (AUWs) were actively excited and acquired using the sensing coating, from which the cumulative energy transfer from linear to nonlinear AUW modes was ascertained, to formulate a damage index. With the index, in conjunction with a probabilistic model, the highly specific damage induced by HVI debris clouds were evaluated quantitatively and precisely; 4. This proposed strategy has been validated experimentally using HVI facilitates and a mock-up spacecraft structure (comprising a shielding layer and inner structure). In order to achieve all these objectives, fundamental investigations were first carried out. From fundamental research to application-oriented implementation, this proposed research has reached its expectation, ending up with an innovative SHM framework for in-service space structures. In conclusion, all the proposed research objectives have been successfully and fully accomplished. The research outputs are expected to enhance the survivability of spacecraft after HVI via accurate damage evaluation.

15201416.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201416.value: Upon completion of this GRF project, an innovative structural health monitoring (SHM) framework for in-service space structures has been fully developed and functional. The research outputs are expected to enhance the survivability of spacecraft after hypervelocity impact (HVI) via accurate damage evaluation. Benefiting from in-depth fundamental interrogation and intensive experiment, this proposed research has reached some very important conclusions and achieved significant findings and outcomes which can benefit relevant students in future. This new SHM strategy, allying ameliorated passive acoustic emission with active nonlinear ultrasonic-based characterization, is able to evaluate highly specific damage caused by the debris cloud under HVI (>4 km/s) quantitatively, promptly, and precisely – a task difficult to achieve using currently available methods. For scientific research, the research outcome can facilitate to circumvent the key technical bottlenecks that current SHM methods may confront when extended to space-related applications; for troubleshooting of a practical engineering problem, this research can enhance the survivability of spacecraft after HVI via accurate damage evaluation. A number of high-level publications have been arising from this research project, including 25 papers in top-tier SCI journals, along with another 11 papers in the international conference proceedings (see Part C).

15201416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201416.value: Although all the proposed objectives have been well achieved, the team has also identified some potential directions along which deeper and broader research could be expanded. In particular, this research targets at innovative structural health monitoring (SHM) framework for in-service space structures, to enhance the survivability of spacecraft after hypervelocity impact (HVI) via accurate damage evaluation. All work has been done in the laboratory, with mock-up structures. The team is now proactively coordinating with research partners in China Academy of Space Technology, to seek opportunity to validate this technique in real space environment.

15201416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201416.value: The recent quantum leap in space technology has intensified innovative quests by humans to penetrate outer space. As a consequence, near-Earth space is now cluttered with orbiting spacecraft (e.g., satellites, space stations), as well as countless micrometeoroids and man-made orbital debris (MMOD). Though small in size, MMOD travel at such high speeds that even a small object can severely impact spacecraft. This sort of impact is commonly referred to as “hypervelocity impact” (HVI) – a scenario typically involving an impacting velocity in excess of 1 km/s. HVI is ubiquitous in space, as evidenced by the hundreds of impact lesions seen on spacecraft after every flight mission. The figure “33%” is the minimal probability for a space station to be impacted by MMOD at least once every ten years. However, the uniqueness of space applications makes the deployment of SHM on space structures significantly distinct from that in other ordinary engineering realms. In particular, the damage committed to spacecraft by the debris clouds, as a consequence of hypervelocity impact (HVI), features hundreds of craters and micro-cracks chaotically scattered, and evaluation of such highly specific damage is far beyond the detectability of conventional structural health monitoring (SHM) methods. With this motivation, a probabilistic SHM strategy, allying ameliorated passive acoustic emission with active nonlinear ultrasonic-based characterization, has been developed via this GRF project. An innovative SHM framework for in-service space structures has been fully developed and functional, to enhance the survivability of spacecraft after HVI.

15204016.label: Project Objectives
15204016.value: The effect of the haptic feedback on brain activities will be investigated in the contexts of vibrotactile stimulation and 3 degrees-of-freedom haptic forces. A rehabilitation related prototype with audio, visual and haptic feedback will be built to acquire and analyse the brain signals. Novel algorithms will be developed to enable the construction of classification models for identifying the cognitive load of people by transfer learning technology.

15204016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204016.value: 腦機接口為癱瘓人士提供了一個與世界互動的機會。癱瘓者可以利用腦電波、通過腦機接口來控制外界的物體。這項技術在近年來取得了較大進展，但實際的使用仍然是一個挑戰。大多數的腦機接口系統依靠視覺和聽覺作爲反饋，並沒有充份利用觸覺。另一方面，系統的性能取決於腦電信號分類算法的準確度。開發這些算法需要大量的數據，而漫長的數據採集過程會對癱瘓人士構成一定的風險。針對以上兩點，本項目首先研究觸覺在腦機接口系統中的所擔當的角色，並分析由觸覺而產生的腦電波。接下來，利用遷移學習技術來開發一些新的腦電波分類算法，採用較容易獲得的健全人士的腦電信號來對殘疾者的腦電波進行分類。最後，開發一個基於腦機接口、並包含觸覺，聽覺和視覺的多感官虛擬實境康復系統，為殘疾者提供康復培訓。

15204016.label: Realisation of objectives
15204016.value: The objectives of the project have been realized. 1. The effect of haptic force feedback on brain activities was investigated by studying the electroencephalography (EEG) signals generated with vibration serving as haptic stimulation or feedback, using the paradigms of event related potential (P300 odd ball paradigm), steady state somatosensory evoked potential (SSSEP) and motor imagery (MI). Furthermore, a hand rehabilitation prototype system was developed by monitoring EEG signals of users when they were performing virtual handwriting tasks using a 6 degrees-of-freedom (dof) haptic device. The signals were analyzed in real time to identify user’s cognitive workload during the process. Force guidance was activated when the signals indicated high cognitive workload, and vice versa. 2. Computational algorithms were used to analyze and recognize EEG signals. Novel techniques were developed by using transfer learning technology, particularly on fuzzy system framework, and the contemporary multi-view and deep learning approaches.

15204016.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204016.value: (N.B. In the following, the references inside the square bracket [] correspond to the research output in Part C, with J stands for journal paper and C for conference paper) Vibrotactile forces applied to extremities were an effective means to provide haptic stimulation in the “odd ball paradigm” to evoke P300 EEG signals [C1]. The data collected could be classified using machine learning algorithms [C4]. In SSSEP, continuous vibrotactile forces applied to extremities achieved similar results [C1], while users reflected that continuous vibration at non-target limbs were somewhat distracting. In MI, vibration served as haptic feedback to inform user that the imagery of targeted motor tasks (e.g. moving a specific limb) had been achieved and successfully identified with algorithms [C2]. The idea was extended to walking imagery (a form of MI) for detecting brain activities of lower limbs [J7, C2]. Virtual-reality-based systems were developed to investigative EEG signals of users performing different cognitive tasks, in the contexts of fixation plate placement [J2] and handwriting [C3]. For the latter, passive EEG signals were acquired on the fly during the process to identify user’s state of mind, thereby triggering force guidance on demand through the force output (3 dof) of a haptic device [C3]. Other than common algorithms in BCI research, such as LDA and SVM [C4], advanced algorithms were developed to process EEG signals based on transfer learning technology [J3, J4, J5], with a focus on its application to fuzzy systems [J1, J4, J5], which had been evaluated favorably with EEG datasets. Furthermore, deep learning and multi-veiw approaches were also investigated [J6, J7], and applied to a study on walking imagery in virtual environment [J7] with 9 healthy subjects and 1 paralyzed patient. The results of the project have generated new ideas on the use of haptic feedback for BCI-based lower limb rehabilitation, which contributed to successful bidding in the recent GRF 2019/20 application.

15204016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204016.value: The study demonstrated that the sense of touch, i.e., haptic stimulation and feedback, is a useful perception channel through which BCI performance can be enhanced, in addition to the vastly exploited visual channel. The flexibility of virtual reality for BCI applications was manifested in the project, which provides a platform for testing, evaluation and improvement before real-world experiments. Haptic-based event related P300 potential was shown to be promising for BCI development, which is worthwhile further investigation to enhance and realize practical BCI applications. As mentioned in Section 6.1 above, inspired by this project, haptic feedback will be exploited for BCI-based lower-limb rehabilitation, where virtual reality will also be leveraged to facilitate rehabilitative training. The novel algorithms developed in the project has demonstrated potential for accurate classification of EEG signals. Performance evaluation of EEG-based applications in domains other than BCI, e.g. neuroscience, can also be carried out. In particular, advanced methods for classifying mental states using EEG signals will be developed based on the new algorithms proposed in the project.

15204016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204016.value: Brain-computer interface (BCI) provides a means for paralyzed patients to communicate with external world by the electrical brain signals, which can be acquired non-invasively from the scalp to recognize user intentions and carry out the corresponding actions through external devices. However, brain signals are weak and noisy. Users need to generate characteristic signals to facilitate the recognition of their intentions, which usually relies on the provision of visual stimuli or feedback, rendered through simple computer graphics or virtual reality. In the project, the sense of touch (i.e., haptics) is exploited to enhance the performance of vision-based BCI, which can reduce fatigue caused by prolonged visual attention in the same time. Besides, novel machine learning techniques are investigated to accurately classify brain signals generated under different situations. A focus of the project is to investigate a specific school of techniques called transfer learning, by which data of healthy subjects can be used to compensate the lack of patient data. The outputs of the project on haptic-assisted BCI are instrumental to promote the development of practical systems for rehabilitation. The algorithms developed can be extended to other applications, such as recognition of mental states.

15204116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15204116.value: 內存分析數據庫中佈局感知的查詢處理

15204116.label: Project Objectives
15204116.value: Design a holistic in-memory data layout that can benefit key column-store operators: FILTER-SCAN, RECONSTRUCT, PARTITION, and SORT. These operators are the building blocks for major relational operators: SELECTION, PROJECTION/AGGREGATION, JOIN, and GROUP-BY, respectively. Design a layout-aware algorithm for each column-store operator and analyze the efficiency of each algorithm. Evaluate running time improvement at both operator-level and query-level.

Design a layout-aware algorithm for each column-store operator and analyze the efficiency of each algorithm.
Evaluate running time improvement at both operator-level and query-level.

15204116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204116.value: In modern main-memory analytic databases, data is memory-resident and stored column-by-column (instead of row-by-row), queries are read-mostly, and the performance goal is to support real-time analytic. When the performance is not disk-bound, the performance goal of various data processing operators is to process the data at (or near) the speed of CPU. Recently, research in this emerging area has shown that storing the data in memory using a specific data layout (e.g., storing the i-th bit of values from the same attribute/column in consecutive memory region) can substantially accelerate the SELECTION operator. Although powerful, that line of research has actually ignored the fact that analytical queries are usually composed of multiple operators, including not only SELECTION, but also JOIN, GROUP-BY, etc. In our preliminary study, we found that while existing specialized data layouts can really accelerate SELECTION, they might hurt the performance of other operators and thus hurt the overall query execution time. In this project, we aim to fill that technology gap. In the first phase of the project, we will design a data layout that could holistically accelerate all key operators in a main-memory analytic database. Coming up with such a layout is challenging because a good layout should embrace the characteristics of many operators together. In the second phase, we will develop the corresponding execution algorithm for each operator. This is also challenging because the algorithms have to be designed to gain maximum benefit from the data layout and at the same time be aware of various concerns in modern CPU architecture (e.g., be cache-conscious, exploit CPU’s SIMD (Single-Instruction-Multiple-Data) instructions). In the last phase, we will prototype our research results into MonetDB and evaluate both individual operator performance and overall query performance. This project will pioneer the area's first holistic in-memory data layout and the corresponding set of layout-aware query processing algorithms. By integrating our results into MonetDB, a popular open-source main-memory analytic database that has an increasing number of industry and academic users, the project will yield not only significant scientific merit, but also high practical value. 在現代內存分析數據庫中，數據駐留在內存中並以逐列存儲（而不是逐行存儲）， 查詢以讀為主，而且性能目標是支持實時分析。當性能瓶頸不再是磁盤讀寫時，性能目標是通過優化數據處理操作符從而達到接近CPU的數據處理速度。近日，這一新興領域的研究表明，在內存中使用特定的佈局存儲數據（例如，存儲来自相同屬性/列的值的第i位在連續的內存區）可以顯著加快SELECTION操作符。但是，這些研究實際上忽略了一個事實，即分析查詢通常是由多個操作符組成，不僅包括SELECTION，也包括JOIN，GROUP-BY等。在我們的初步研究中，我們發現，儘管現有的數據佈局確實可以加速SELECTION，它也會降低其他操作符的性能，從而增加了整體查詢執行時間。 在這個項目中，我們的目標是填補这个技術缺口。在項目的第一階段，我們將設計一個數據佈局，它可以從整體上加速內存分析數據庫中所有主要操作符。想出這樣的佈局是具有挑戰性的，因為一個良好的佈局應該權衡很多操作符的特點。在第二階段，我們將為每個操作符開發相應的算法。這也是具有挑戰性的，因為算法設計既要盡可能獲得最大的性能提升，同時要考慮現代CPU架構的特點（例如，緩存感知，充分利用CPU的SIMD（單指令多數據）指令）。在最後階段，我們將評估單個操作符和整體查詢的性能提升。

15204116.label: Realisation of objectives
15204116.value: 1) Design a holistic in-memory data layout that can benefit key column-store operators: FILTER-SCAN, RECONSTRUCT, PARTITION, and SORT. These operators are the building blocks for major relational operators: SELECTION, PROJECTION/AGGREGATION, JOIN, and GROUP-BY, respectively. [100% achieved] We have developed a holistic in-memory layout for FILTER-SCAN, RECONSTRUCT, PARTITION, and SORT. The layout can facilitate parallelism for those operations and achieve excellent cache and TLB re-use. 2) Design a layout-aware algorithm for each column-store operator and analyze the efficiency of each algorithm. [100% achieved] For each algorithm, we have used AVX256 SIMD to accelerate the processing speed. We have also used multiple-core to parallelize the processing. When using multiple-cores, we are able to reach a memory-bound (maximum) performance. 3) Evaluate running time improvement at both operator-level and query-level. [100% achieved] The runtime improvement is evaluated using different operators as well as benchmark such as TPC-H. The undergraduate funded under this project participated in objectives 2 and 3.

15204116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204116.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a holistic in-memory data layout and efficient algorithms for each analytics operators on top. For each algorithm, we have fully unleashed the power of the latest hardware to maximize performance. We have implemented and tested our algorithms on real data sets and TPC-H datasets (Part C, Papers #8.1, #9.1, #9.4). We have also extended our techniques to sequence data (Part C, Paper #8.2), and some machine learning operations (Part C, Papers #9.2,#9.3). Also, we are building a prototype system that puts everything together (Part C, Paper #8.3). Research Outcomes: 2 journal papers (+1 under submission), 4 conference papers, 2 PhD students.

15204116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204116.value: One potential further development is to extend the layouts and algorithms to deal with more machine learning operations.

15204116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204116.value: In modern main-memory analytic databases, data is memory-resident and queries are read-mostly, and the performance goal is to support real-time analytic. When the performance is not disk-bound, the performance goal of various data processing operators is to process the data at (or near) the speed of CPU. Recently, research in this emerging area has shown that storing the data in memory using specific layouts and algorithms can improve performance. In this project, we have successfully developed efficient layouts and algorithms that can work on a variety of data and hardware. The project has successfully completed. In addition to academic publications, we have also open-sourced the codes such that others can test and integrate them into their systems.

15204216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15204216.value: 具有棘手資產的投資模型

15204216.label: Project Objectives
15204216.value: In financial investment problems, there is an important type of model uncertainties -- which we call intractable claims -- that are neither predictable nor hedgeable based on the underlying market. There has been little study on investment models involving intractable claims, especially in the continuous time setting. This project aims to fill out this gap and proposes to study several investment problems with intractable claims. The first problem is the mean-variance model with an intractable claim. The problem is typically time-inconsistent which leads to a mean-field type of stochastic control problem. We plan to apply the recent mean-field control theory to study it. The second problem is the expected utility (EU) model and the goal-reaching model with an intractable claim. We plan to extend the Hardy-Littlewood theorem to non-linear case and adopt the quantile formulation to solve the problems. The third problem is the rank-dependent utility (RDU) model with an intractable claim. This problem promises to be very hard, with the main difficulty arising from the presence of the probability weighting function. Our plan is to attack this problem by exploring the properties of monotonicity and convex order of the objection functional.
rows: In financial investment problems, there is an important type of model uncertainties -- which we call intractable claims -- that are neither predictable nor hedgeable based on the underlying market. There has been little study on investment models involving intractable claims, especially in the continuous time setting. This project aims to fill out this gap and proposes to study several investment problems with intractable claims.

The first problem is the mean-variance model with an intractable claim. The problem is typically time-inconsistent which leads to a mean-field type of stochastic control problem. We plan to apply the recent mean-field control theory to study it.

The second problem is the expected utility (EU) model and the goal-reaching model with an intractable claim. We plan to extend the Hardy-Littlewood theorem to non-linear case and adopt the quantile formulation to solve the problems.

The third problem is the rank-dependent utility (RDU) model with an intractable claim. This problem promises to be very hard, with the main difficulty arising from the presence of the probability weighting function. Our plan is to attack this problem by exploring the properties of monotonicity and convex order of the objection functional.

15204216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204216.value: In studying financial investment models, it is important to take environmental uncertainties into consideration. Problems when the uncertainties are determined by the underlying market states have been widely investigated. The proposed project focuses on investment problems where the uncertainties (called intractable claims) have little or no relevance with the market states. We plan to investigate the following three inter-related problems: (I) the Markowitz mean-variance model; (II) the expected utility model and the goal-reaching model; and (III) the rank-dependent utility model, all with an intractable claim in a dynamic setting. As these models are fundamentally different from the classical robust models under ambiguity and hard to be tackled by the conventional stochastic control or duality approaches, new methodologies are called for in order to analyze and solve them. Research in the project represents a largely unexplored and challenging area. We anticipate that the results obtained from this project will help people have a better understanding of financial markets, and open up a new avenue of research on uncertainties and risks.

15204216.label: Realisation of objectives
15204216.value: This project has planned to study some problems with model uncertainties under both classical and behavioral settings. It has aimed to study the effects of the intractable claims on trading strategies. These problems are extremely challenging due to their time inconsistent nature. They belong to an important but unexplored research field. To accomplish our targets, we developed some new methods to tackle the proposed problems and many useful results both from theory and practice points of view were obtained. All the proposed targets were addressed in our work, which can seen from the published works in the report. Both the new quantile formulation method and the classical tools in stochastic control and optimization were widely used to study the proposed models. Because this is an unexplored research field, we plan to continue the study of this direction in some new project in the future.

15204216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204216.value: We have got many important findings and outcomes from the present project. For instance, we introduced the quantile formulation method in the past works to study behavioral finance problems; in the present project, we further extended this method so as to tackle the proposed problems. In the past works, the optimal solutions were obtain by solo quantile formulation method and they are usually expressed through concave envelope of some functions. But the newly proposed problems can not be studied by this approach and the optimal solutions turns out to have no such expressions any more. When we studied the problems in the paper titled "Optimal Insurance under Rank-Dependent Utility and Incentive Compatibility'', we found that these problems can not be tackled by a single tool, instead must be tackled by combining the standard tools for solving classical problems and the new developed tools for solving behavioral finance problems. We used dedicated analytical tools such as calculus of variations and quantile formulation method to study the problem. And eventually we completely solved the problems and obtained explicit optimal solutions by this new approach. This paper has been published in the top-tier journal "Mathematical Finance'' in the filed. We believe this is one of the most import outcomes of this project. We have also made many other contributions from this project. Most of these works are published in the highly respected journals in the fields, such as "Mathematics of Operations Research'', "SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics'' and "Insurance: Mathematics and Economics''. These published papers are listed in the final report. Meanwhile, we have been invited to delivery talks in several important world leading international conferences such as the "10th World Congress of the Bachelier Finance Society'', "SIAM Conference on Control and Its Applications'' and the "12th AIMS Conference on Dynamical Systems, Differential Equations and Applications''. Our results have attracted many attentions from the audience. In particular, I was awarded the Distinguished Keynote Speaker in the "Sixth Asian Quantitative Finance Conference" in Nov. 2018. Moreover, one PhD candidate has joined the project and accomplished parts of the work. He will continue the research along the research direction proposed by the present project.

15204216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204216.value: As intractable claims have barely been studied in the past, so there are many potentials for further development of our research project. We can take this new ingredient into consideration into the classical expected utility models or behavioral models such as Yaari’s dual model and Lopes’ SP/A model. These problems must be extremely challenging because nonlinear expectations will appear in them and classical method may largely fail. As mentioned in the major findings and research outcome, we have one PhD candidate to continue the study. We also hope the the RGC will support a following project along this research direction.

15204216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204216.value: People are often facing uncertainties when making decisions. This project studied how to choose the best investment strategies when facing one particular uncertainty, named intractable claims. We derived the optimal trading strategies for the proposed models. The findings of this research project will help people have a better understanding of financial investment when facing this situation.

15204416.value: To engineer body temperature sensitive stress memory polymeric filaments through optimizing the composition of semi-crystalline MPs and fiber spinning conditions for smart compression stockings with thermal dynamic massage functions. To fabricate tubular fabrics as compression stockings through structural design and manufacturing conditions for achieving desirable cyclic memory stresses. To characterize the memory stress in MPs, filaments, fabrics and compression stocking for investigating its relationship with structures, thermal, and mechanical conditions at micro and macro scales. To establish theoretical models for describing and predicting pure memory stress/pressure in fibers, fabrics and compression stocking on hard and soft surfaces.

15204416.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204416.value: As in the proposal, we firstly successfully applied stress-memory polymeric filaments to compression stocking for thermal sensitive therapy as expected. Furthermore the most significant outcome of this work is the generalization of stress memory principle : namely, enthalpy-controlled. This generalization was later proved by other materials based on this principle from nature and synthetics. Thus, we applied enthalpy controlled stress-memory materials to artificial muscles with dual contractive modes.

15204416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204416.value: We are going to make commercial compression stocking after the fibers can be massively manufactured, which is underway by a company in Mainland China. Other further development is the artificial muscles. Our students can continue to optimize the materials design with textile structure for specific applications. If funding allows, we will establish models for predicting the effect of twist structures of shape memory yarns on artificial muscles.

15204416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204416.value: The main research objective of this project was to study and apply the “stress memory” concept in developing a smart integrative multifunctional compression stocking for the management of chronic deceases. For this purpose, we successfully designed a polymer for filament yarns which then are applied for compression stocking. We also established a model and generalized a theory for how to control a stress memory of a material, namely, in the switch element there is enthalpy change. Due to this new discovery, we further installed enthalpy in a materials so that it can be applied for artificial muscle with novel dual contractive behavior.

15205216.value: 近十年來，人們意識到主要由於液化石油氣的使用，空氣中的丙烷和正/異丁烷濃度正在逐年升高。 2013年10月1日以來，香港政府陸續向燃燒液化石油氣的出租車和輕型客車的車主們提供更換汽車催化轉化器及相應部分的一次性補貼，稱為“液化石油氣催化轉換器替換程序”。 此項研究會大量的減少液化石油氣車輛的尾氣中揮發性有機化合物（VOCs），即丙烷和正/異丁烷，還有氮氧化物（NOx）的排放，同時有效減少光化學臭氧的形成。 一方面，因為城市臭氧的形成很大程度上會受VOCs的限制，所以丙烷和正/異丁烷濃度的降低可以很明顯的限製香港地區近地面臭氧的形成。 另一方面，作為前體碳氫化合物，丙烷和正/異丁烷與NOx反應時會生成烷基硝酸鹽。烷基硝酸鹽的出現會抵消掉VOC對臭氧生成的控制能力；另外，在高強度的光化學反應活性及高濃度的VOC含量下，突然移除VOC會改變烷基硝酸鹽的有效分支比，從而會潛在的促進臭氧的生成。 此外，在此項目中NOx的削減會降低臭氧的一氧化氮滴定，進一步引起臭氧濃度的升高。 因此，本項目的研究將會：i) 通過實地測量調查、台架試驗和污染源分析，來判斷燃燒液化石油氣的車輛的主要排放物的變化趨勢，從而評估替換其催化轉化器後兩年來對於空氣質量影響的效果。 ii）第一次嘗試下，該研究應用了自主研發的光化學盒模型（PBM）及經過化學輸送模式（CTM）、天氣研究與預測模式（WRF）和區域環境質量模式（CMAQ）驗證的化學反應主導模型（MCM），來輔助研究空氣中丙烷、丁烷和NOx的濃度是否有下降；並且通過改變VOC與NOx的比例來影響其之間的反應，最終影響光化學反應臭氧的形成。 在液化石油氣轉換器的替換項目或者任何其他的控制措施的實施中，可以觀察到臭氧濃度跟隨不同的VOC和NOx濃度而變化，於是相應的O3-VOCs-NOx相關性方程即可得出。 此項目將有助於系統地制定最佳的臭氧控制方案，並合理評估其在香港或其他人口稠密的城市的實行效果。此項研究也將論證一個有效的結合系統化的實地測量和可靠的數值模擬方式的方法，此方法將極有可能實現對二次污染物的高效控制。

15205216.label: Realisation of objectives
15205216.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The achievements are shown as follows. * Data of ambient volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and other trace gases continuously monitored from 2005 to 2013 at a suburban site and from September 2012 to April 2017 at a roadside site were used to evaluate the continuous effectiveness of the replaced catalytic converters on the reduction of air pollutants. * The contributions of diesel commercial vehicles (DCV), solvent usage and gasoline/LPG vehicles to ambient VOCs before the LPG catalytical converter replacement program were apportioned. * The proportional contributions of LPG-fueled vehicles to ambient VOCs and NOx before, during and after the LPG catalytic converter replacement program were quantified with receptor model PMF. * The long-term impact of control measures of DCV and solvent usage, and uncontrolled gasoline/LPG vehicle emissions on ozone production before the LPG program was evaluated using our own-developed PBM-MCM model. * The detailed photochemistry of VOCs particularly LPG tracers propane and n/i-butanes before and after the LPG program was explored using the PBM-MCM model. * By combining the measurement data with receptor model and photochemical box model, an effective new methodology for secondary pollution control was established. The method will help policy-makers formulate future control strategies on anthropogenic source emissions in Hong Kong and even in the greater Pearl River Delta region.

15205216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205216.value: * Before the LPG program, the sum of toluene, ethylbenzene and xylene isomers from solvent usage decreased continuously with an average rate of -99.1 ± 6.9 pptv/year, whereas the sum of ethene and propene increased by 48.2 ± 2.0 pptv/year from before to during the DCV program. * LPG-related VOCs (propane and n/i-butanes) and several trace gases (CO, NO and NO2) decreased significantly from before to after the program (p < 0.01). The reduction rates of propane and n/i-butanes remained high and constant after the program 1-3 years. * source apportionment results showed that prior to the LPG program, VOCs emitted from diesel exhaust decreased at a rate of -304.5 ± 17.7 pptv/year, while solvent related VOCs decreased at a rate of -204.7 ± 39.7 pptv/year. The gasoline and LPG vehicle emissions elevated by 1086 ± 34 pptv/year, and were responsible for the increases of ethene and propene. * Source apportionment analysis indicated that LPG-fueled vehicular emissions were the top contributor to ambient VOCs in the roadside environment while the VOCs emitted from LPG-fueled vehicles decreased at a rate of 4.21 ±2.38 ppbv/year. * PBM-MCM simulations found that before the LPG program, the simulated O3 rate of increase was lowered from 0.39 ± 0.03 to 0.16 ± 0.05 ppbv/year by the solvent and DCV programs, because O3 produced by solvent usage and diesel exhaust related VOCs decreased (p < 0.05) by 0.16 ± 0.01 and 0.05 ± 0.01 ppbv/year between 2005 and 2013, respectively. However, enhanced VOC emissions from gasoline and LPG vehicles accounted for most of the O3 increment (0.09 ± 0.01 out of 0.16 ± 0.05 ppbv/year) in these years. * PBM-MCM simulations revealed that the net negative contribution of VOCs and NOx emitted from LPG-fueled vehicles to O3 production strengthened at a rate of 1.9 × 10−2 pptv/day from before to after the LPG program (p < 0.01).

15205216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205216.value: Since air pollution control is a long-term task, it is essential to ensure the lasting effectiveness of existing and future control measures. As such, it is strongly suggested that the continuous effectiveness of the existing control measures be regularly assessed every several years so that appropriate adjustment and supplement can be made in time. In addition, the proposed methodology in this study will be helpful for policy-makers to develop new control measures. Furthermore, continuous monitoring of air pollutants including VOCs and other trace gases is the base for effective assessment of the control measures using the proposed methodology in this study. To more accurately simulate the impact of control measures on in-situ photochemical ozone formation, the interval between each input of the measured data injected into the PBM-MCM model can be shortened from one hour to 200 seconds.

15205216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205216.value: Recognizing the increased levels of ambient propane and i/n-butanes, the main component of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), in the past decade, the Hong Kong government has offered one-off subsidy to help vehicle owners to replace the catalytic converters and associated components of their LPG taxis and light buses to meet the corrected emission limits since 1 October 2013, i.e., the LPG catalytic converters replacement program. The measurement data showed that LPG-related VOCs and several trace gases (CO, NO and NO2) decreased significantly from before to after the program. Source apportionment analysis indicated that LPG-fueled vehicular emissions were the top contributor to ambient VOCs while the VOCs emitted from LPG-fueled vehicles decreased at a rate of 4.21 ±2.38 ppbv/year from before to after the LPG program. Furthermore, the photochemical box model simulations revealed that the net negative contribution of VOCs and NOx emitted from LPG-fueled vehicles to O3 production strengthened at a rate of 1.9 × 10−2 pptv/day from before to after the LPG program. The findings proved the continuous effectiveness of the intervention program, and are of help to future control strategies in Hong Kong.

15205616.label: Project Objectives
15205616.value: to construct 3D conformal porous microstructures on the nonplanar surface of textile fabric substrates by breath figure (BF) technique; to develop a new modified BF apparatus for efficient incorporation of conformal porous microstructures on textile substrates; to investigate the influence of different processing parameters on the formed porous microstructures; to characterize, evaluate and optimize the obtained 3D conformal porous microstructured textiles (3D CPMTs); to incorporate functional materials into the 3D CPMTs for further applications.

15205616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205616.value: 3D conformal porous microstructures are nonconventional micro-porous structures that are conformal or contouring to the profile of non-planar and uneven surface of their substrates. When properly designed and incorporated into textiles, this kind of structure can be exploited for generating a new kind of textile composites, 3D conformal porous microstructured textiles (3D CPMTs), with enhanced physicochemical properties. The most crucial point to achieve 3D CPMTs is the proper design of their structures and fabrication methods. A survey of the literature has shown that little work has been done in this area. Therefore, there is a need to carry out a study for a basic understanding of their structures and properties. More specifically, the project will address fundamental issues of the fabrication, structure and performance of the 3D CPMTs. Based on previous work done by the applicant, a special strategy and apparatus will be developed to produce this kind of new 3D CPMTs. A series of 3D CPMT samples will be produced by adjusting the surface structures and properties of textile substrates, film-forming materials, polymer solutions and processing conditions. Systematic studies will be carried out to analyze various influential factors in order for the improvement and optimization of constructed 3D CPMTs. Moreover 3D CPMTs with incorporation of functional materials will also be prepared and evaluated for further applications. 三維多孔微結構是一種非傳統的和能夠帖服於非平面基體不均勻表面的維孔結構。如果能夠合理地設計和應用於紡織領域，這種結構可以被利用來開發一種新型的和具有增強物理化學性能的三維微孔復合紡織材料結構。為了獲得這種復合紡織材料，對其結構和加工方法的正確合理設計是技術關鍵。經文獻檢索，目前還沒有相關的技術報道。因此，有需要對這種復合材料的結構和性能進行系統的研究。為此，本項目將開展對這種材料在加工，結構和性能上的基礎研究。在申請人相關工作的基礎上，本項目將研發一種特殊的制備工藝和設備來加工這種三維微孔復合紡織結構。並通過調整一系列工藝參數，例如表面結構和性能，制膜材料，聚合物溶液和加工條件，來加工一系列的三維微孔復合紡織結構。並通過對其影響因素的系統研究，來提高和優化這種新型的復合紡織材料結構。另外，本項目也會嘗試在這種復合結構中添加功能性材料，並評估和研究添加復合後的材料性能。

15205616.label: Realisation of objectives
15205616.value: All the objectives of this project have been fully achieved. For the first research objective, a new nature-inspired approach [1-5] has been designed and developed for constructing 3D conformal porous microstructures on the nonplanar surface of textile fabric substrates via breath figure (BF) technique, forming a new kind of textile composites, i.e. 3D conformal porous microstructured textiles (3D CPMTs). The obtained 3D CPMTs not only possess customized functionality of introduced brick materials at micro-scale, but also maintain the unique macro-scale texture features (such as woven pattern) and excellent inherent advantages (such as flexibility, air permeability and water vapor permeability) of textile fabrics. Moreover, it allowed one-step functionalization of 3DCPMTs by incorporation of functional nanomaterials (such as TiO2 NPs) into the porous microstructures for functional applications [1]. For the second research objective, a new BF apparatus [4] has been developed for efficient construction of conformal porous microstructures on textile fabric substrates. The apparatus mainly included humidifier, heating platform and BF chamber. Environmental humidity and temperature could be controlled in the chamber for providing a desired moist environment for efficient fabrication of 3D CPMTs. For the third research objective, a systematic study [3] was carried out to investigate the influence of different processing parameters on the formed porous microstructures. In this study, a series of 3D CPMT samples were design and developed by adjusting various processing parameters of 3D CPMT including solution concentration, temperature, humidity, brick materials and textile substrates. The obtained 3D CPMTs were then characterized and evaluated for investigating the influence of these processing parameters on the formation and morphology of porous microstructures. For the fourth research objective, studies [3,1,2] have been carried out to characterize, evaluate and optimize the obtained 3D CPMTs. Different structural parameters of 3D CPMTs such as pore shape and pore size [3,1] and various physical properties of 3D CPMTs such as surface wettability, tensile behavior, ventilation resistivity, water vapor permeability and thermal conductivity were characterized and evaluated [3,2]. The results were also compared with control samples without conformal porous microstructures. With the disclosure of their influences on the porous microstructures, the desired and optimal processing parameters were also obtained for the 3D CPMTs. For the last research objective, the potential applications of the new 3D CPMTs were well explored and their promising applications in various fields have been successfully demonstrated, including photocatalytic degradation of pollutants [1,5], oil/water separation [3], wearable sensing [3] and personal thermal management [2,5]. First, functional material such as titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO2 NPs) was incorporated into the porous microstructures of 3D CPMTs during the BF process for the promising application of photocatalytic degradation of pollutants [1]. Comparing to the sample without porous microstructures, the resultant TiO2 NPs-incorporated 3D CPMTs showed an encouragingly enhanced performance on photocatalytic degradation of pollutants under the same ultraviolet irradiation conditions. Secondly, with its unique microporous structure and hydrophobic characteristics, 3D CPMT was successfully explored to serve as a brand-new absorbent material to selectively separate oil from water [3], demonstrating its promising potential in the applications of oil/water separation. Besides photocatalytic degradation and oil−water separation, the most promising applications of 3CPMTs are in the development of a kind of truly wearable devices based on the introduced functions of brick materials and their well-maintained textile advantages. As a demonstration, 3D CPMT was successfully explored for assembling a kind of self-powered pressure sensor devices [3] with textile comfort and breathability which are suitable for detecting human motions. As another demonstration, 3D CPMTs was successfully explored for assembling a kind of electrothermal textile (ET) devices [2] with both good wearable comfort and enhanced personal thermal management. Compared to the sample devices without porous microstructures, the 3D CPMT-based ET devices can obtain higher temperatures under the same input power to provide thermal comfort for human beings, while saving more electric power to achieve the same thermal equilibrium temperature.
