15205616.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205616.value: In this project, a unique strategy for direct introduction of desired brick materials onto nonplanar fabric surfaces with three-dimensionally conformal porous microstructures was designed and developed, which brings a brand-new kind of three-dimensionally conformal porous microstructured textiles (3DCPMTs). The approach was robust and versatile for customized preparation of 3DCPMTs based on different fabrics (e.g. natural cotton-fabric, synthetic polyester-fabric, conductive copper/nickel coated-fabric) with common polymers (e.g. PS, SBS, PDMS-g-PAs). Moreover, it allowed one-step functionalization of 3DCPMTs by incorporation of functional materials (such as TiO2 NPs) into the porous microstructures for functional applications. The systematic study on the influential processing parameters showed that solution concentration played an important role in formation and morphology of porous microstructures. Both very high (e.g. >250 mg/mL) and low concentration (e.g. <0.5 mg/mL) would not lead to formation of regular and continuous porous microstructures. The optimal value would range 15-200 mg/mL, depending on textile substrates and brick materials employed. In addition, high relative humidity (e.g. >99%) and room temperature (e.g. 20 degrees Celsius) would be preferred for formation of porous microstructures. Comparative study showed that, compared with control samples without porous microstructures, 3DCPMTs not only showed remarkable hydrophobic wetting performance, improved strength, and higher thermal insulation properties but also maintained excellent inherent properties of fabric such as flexibility, moisture permeability and unique texture features. With its unique microporous structures, introduced functions of brick materials and well-maintained textile advantages, 3DCPMTs have demonstrated promising applications in various fields including photocatalytic degradation of pollutants, oil/water separation, wearable sensing, and personal thermal management. Experimental results showed that photocatalytic efficiency of 3DCPMTs-based sample was generally 1 time higher than that of control sample without porous microstructures in degradation of pollutants under the same conditions. For oil/water separation, 3DCPMTs-based samples could selectively absorb oil from water surface and effectively separate oil−water emulsions (e.g. corn oil/water, Krytox GPL103 oil/water), demonstrating promising applications for organic contaminant removal, environmental protection, resource recovery and sustainable development. For wearable sensing, a new kind of all-textile-structured pressure sensor based on 3DCPMTs was developed. The results showed that the sensor would be suitable for detecting human motions. For personal thermal management, investigation results showed that electrothermal textile (ET) devices based on 3DCPMTs exhibited better eletrothermal performance and energy-saving properties than control-based ETs under the same conditions. Based on the research work of this project, we have published 3 SCI journal articles, and also presented our research in 2 international conferences.

15205616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205616.value: In this project, a brand-new kind of textile composites, three-dimensionally conformal porous microstructured textiles (3DCPMTs), were innovatively designed and developed. The new textile composites exhibited a unique combined feature of functionality of brick materials and comfort properties of fabrics. Results showed that they are promising in various applications such as photocatalytic degradation of pollutants, oil/water separation, wearable sensing, and personal thermal management. Based on the fundamental studies of this project, potential further work can be a deep study on how to apply this new composites/approach for practical applications with high value and significance. It may involve exploration and selection of specific applied field, deep investigation and comparison of other methods/products with similar functions, refinement of the developed method, composite materials and structures optimization, quality accreditation, and prototype development, etc. Collaboration with interested companies may be explored for supporting these potential further works.

15205616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205616.value: 3D conformal porous microstructures are nonconventional micro-porous structures that are conformal to the profile of non-planar and uneven surface of their substrates. When properly designed and incorporated into textile fabrics, this kind of structure can be exploited for generating a new kind of textile composites, 3D conformal porous microstructured textiles (3D CPMTs), with enhanced physicochemical properties. The most crucial point to achieve 3D CPMTs is the proper design of their structures and fabrication methods. A survey of the literature has shown that little work has been done in this area. Therefore, there is a high need to carry out a study for a basic understanding of their structures and properties. More specifically, the project addresses fundamental issues of the design, fabrication, structure, performance and application of the 3D CPMTs. Studies were also carried out to analyze various influential factors of materials and processing parameters. The significance of this project is to provide a feasible way for direct creation of conformal porous microstructures on nonplanar and flexible surface. This study also paves the way to develop a new kind of 3D CPMTs with enhanced features that combine inherent properties of textile substrates and the well-defined properties of conformably formed porous microstructures.

15207016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15207016.value: 基于三阶非线性剪切波并用于微损伤识别的给构健康监测方法

15207016.label: Project Objectives
15207016.value: To establish a theoretical model to investigate the adhesive nonlinearity for guiding practical design of SHM systems. To understand the relationship among the damage and measured nonlinear parameters for demonstrating the high-sensitivity of the third-harmonic SH waves with damage. To propose a SHM methodology based on third-harmonic SH waves for diagnosis of incipient damages and to experimentally demonstrate its feasibility.
rows: To establish a theoretical model to investigate the adhesive nonlinearity for guiding practical design of SHM systems.
To understand the relationship among the damage and measured nonlinear parameters for demonstrating the high-sensitivity of the third-harmonic SH waves with damage.
To propose a SHM methodology based on third-harmonic SH waves for diagnosis of incipient damages and to experimentally demonstrate its feasibility.

15207016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207016.value: Structural health monitoring (SHM) is an emerging technology aiming at the on-line diagnosis of damages inside structures during their operation. Successful implementation of SHM allows enhancing the safety and evaluating residual lifetime of structures in service, thus avoiding exorbitant maintenance costs. Very recent work indicates that nonlinear third-harmonic shear horizontal (SH) waves may be sensitive to micro and incipient defects, pointing at the possibility of using SH waves for achieving early detection of damage or even its precursor. The underlying physics behind the phenomenon is yet not well understood, and its possible use for SHM has not been explored up to now. Based on our preliminary work, this proposed project attempts to address a few bottlenecking problems related to the nonlinear third-harmonic SH waves, of both fundamental and applied nature. The study is expected to deepen the understanding of the underlying physics on one hand, and to explore the feasibility of using nonlinear SH waves for SHM applications on the other hand. As a key contributing and undesirable nonlinear factor, the adhesive nonlinearity of the bonding layer between the transducers and the structure under inspection is investigated. Fundamental mechanism of the interaction between measured nonlinear parameters and the material plasticity are also to be revealed, providing guidelines for SHM applications. A SHM strategy based on the nonlinear third-harmonic SH waves is finally proposed and assessed by experiments. The significance of the project lies in its direct applicability to a wide range of SHM problems which are of direct benefit to both Hong Kong and beyond. In a broader sense, the problem to be investigated is fundamental and generic in nature, which has significant scientific and practical value for advancing the state-of-the-art of SHM technologies. 结构健康监测（SHM）是一种新兴的技术，用于对工作期间结构健康进行在线诊断。成功实施SHM可增强机构的安全性和评价其剩余寿命，并在很大程度上避免过高的维护成本。最近的工作表明，非线性三次剪切波对微型和初期缺陷敏感，因而对实现早期检测提供了可能性。根据我们的前期工作，该项目试图解决存在于非线性三次谐波SH波的几个瓶颈问题并探讨其在SHM上的应用性。 为此对粘合剂引起的非线性需进行研究，并对所测量的非线性参数和材料塑性及损伤之间的相互作用的基本机制进行揭示，对于SHM应用提供理论指导。最后对基于非线性三次谐波SH波所提出的SHM方法的可行性和最后的实施方案进行评估。

15207016.label: Realisation of objectives
15207016.value: All objectives of the projects have been systematically addressed and realized. Research activities carried out, in relation to the research objectives are summarized as follows: 1). To establish a theoretical model to investigate the adhesive nonlinearity for guiding practical design of SHM systems. Both SH waves and Lamb waves propagating inside typical structures are considered. In particular, a theoretical model for the shear horizontal (SH) wave generation is established based on continuum mechanics theory, in which the full dynamic coupling between the PZT actuator and a metal plate is considered. The inevitable imperfect bonding between the actuator and the plate is taken into account through a spring model, i.e., the stress is continuous and the tangential displacement is allowed to be different from both sides of the interface. The solutions, which can simultaneously satisfy the governing dynamic equations and boundary conditions, are obtained in a closed form using trigonometric series and modal superposition method. The convergence of the series is demonstrated and the model is numerically validated with the aid of FEM results using a PZT-5H wafer bonded on the surface of a thin aluminum plate. Meanwhile, a critical truncation of the series, related to the size of actuator and the wavelength of SH0 wave, is proposed. Based on the dynamic model, a systematic numerical simulation is carried out, which furthermore reveals that the dynamic coupling between the PZT and the metal plate has a significant influence on the SH0 wave generation. The importance of considering this coupling in the design as well as explanations to some experimentally observed phenomena are demonstrated. The proposed theoretical model is expected to provide a useful tool for physical mechanism exploration, structural design and eventually system optimization for SH0 wave generation in SHM applications. Details can be found in the published papers listed in this report. Meanwhile, various models which consider Lamb waves in conjunction with the consideration of adhesive and incipient damage have also been investigated with results published in several papers. 2). To understand the relationship among the damage and measured nonlinear parameters for demonstrating the high-sensitivity of the third-harmonic SH waves with damage. More specifically, a nonlinear theoretical framework is developed, covering the process of wave generation, propagation and sensing, with the aim of investigating the mechanism and characteristics of Adhesive Nonlinearity-induced Lamb waves in plates, which potentially allows for further system optimization to minimize the influence of AN. Meanwhile, the SHM promising second harmonic Lamb waves in nonplanar 2D wave propagating cases are investigated in the perspective of their characterizations and quantifications. Under the assumption of the weak material damping in metallic plates, both the primary and the second harmonic undergo attenuations, dominated by the wave divergence. Theoretical analyses first show the deficiency of the widely-used traditional nonlinear parameter (TNP) to characterize the cumulative features of the second harmonic Lamb waves with changing measuring distances. As an alternative, a so-called refined nonlinear parameter (RNP) is proposed. The new parameter considers the wave propagating characteristics in a practical 2D configuration, aiming at a better characterization and differentiation of the localized and distributed nonlinear sources. In parallel, the high-order waveguide modal theory, usually used in electromagnetics and acoustics, is adopted to investigate the propagation properties of shear horizontal waves in a periodic stubbed plate. Beyond the sub-wavelength regime, higher-order modes are included to calculate the exact band structures caused by the stubs. Theoretical solutions are obtained in a closed form, in which both the dynamic governing equations and the boundary conditions are strictly satisfied. As a last part of the generalization of the work, thick-walled structures with varying geometry are investigated. These problems are challenging for guided wave inspection due to the multi-modal behavior and the complex scattering of the wave modes. The influence of the geometrical transitions on the propagation of the elastic waves in thick-walled cylindrical structures is thoroughly investigated and a structural evaluation technique based on the identified wave phenomena is proposed. Details can be found in the published papers listed in this report. Meanwhile, the superior sensitivity of the SH waves, over conventional Lamb waves, has been demonstrated both numerically and experimentally. This, along with the discovery of different mode-mixing phenomena, greatly enriched the existing detection capability of incipient structural damage and thermos-induced ageing of materials.

15207016.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207016.value: 1). Nonlinear effects of the bonding layers in a typical PZT-actuated SHM system are non-negligible. The frequency tuning characteristics of S0 mode nonlinear Lamb waves from the theoretical and experimental results agree with each other. AAN acts as a much stronger nonlinear source influencing on the nonlinear SHM system when compared with the SAN. 2). A near-field wave enhancement effect caused by the crack-wave interaction is explored. Longitudinal ‘quasi-surface’ waves results in the wave enhancement phenomenon. 3). A high-order waveguide modal theory is developed for SH wave propagation in a plate with periodic stubs. The approach guaranties fast convergence and computation accuracy by using a small number of series terms. 4). Through compensations for the wave attenuation associated with the wave divergence, the new parameter entails a better characterization and differentiation of the cumulative MNP and other noncumulative localized nonlinear sources. 5). Optimized nonlinear Lamb wave-based SHM systems can be designed with the mitigated influence of the undesired AN on the system. 6). Apart from the third harmonic generation caused by the cubic self-interaction of the 1st SH waves, another important path is discovered, through which mixed third harmonic SH waves are generated. This can be taken advantages of for SHM applications. 7). A nonlinear ultrasonic method is proposed based on a group of newly discovered wave triplets where two primary co-directional shear-horizontal SH0 waves mix in a weakly nonlinear plate and generate a cumulative S0 Lamb wave at the sum frequency. 8). A theoretical model on the shear horizontal (SH) wave generation is established based on the continuum mechanics theory. The dynamic coupling between the PZT and the plate is considered in the design of PZT-activated SH0 wave generation. 9). A special type of second harmonic A0 mode Lamb wave is discovered, which is generated through the mixing of primary S0 and A0 mode Lamb waves in a PZT-activated weakly nonlinear plate, applicable to SHM. 10). Third harmonic shear horizontal waves are experimentally shown to exhibit high sensitivity to microstructural changes. A third harmonic SH wave–based system allows for effective characterization of thermal aging–induced microstructural changes. 11). The shear-lag model is combined with the normal mode expansion method, through coupling an MsT with a host plate via a bonding layer. 12). A two-dimensional incipient damage localization method is proposed based on a newly discovered wave mixing phenomenon. A dedicated localization algorithm is proposed and evaluated experimentally.

15207016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207016.value: Through four years of research on SH-based SHM research, our group is now regarded as one of the most active research groups in the SHM area. Apart from the academic reputation gained out of this effort, we have successfully attracted strong interest from a number of companies, who decided to support our research through collaborative/consulting projects, which shows the huge application potentials of the technology. This include our on-going collaborations with Chines space agency (CAST) on the monitoring of satellite modules. This will obviously be continued in the future. In addition, we engage going into more proactive R&D with other industries to promote the present research. Academic-wise, further effort is still needed to solve two problems: 1). Improve the feasibility of the proposed SHM technology in more realistic industrial environment; and 2): embracing more advance technology such as big data, machine learning and information processing techniques to further improve the applicability of the SHM technology. We are now looking at these issues, with the great support from various industrial partners. Hopefully, a few realistic industrial applications will be materialized in the near future.

15209616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15209616.value: 用於增強運動服飾可變形性和舒適性的拉脹織物

15209616.label: Project Objectives
15209616.value: To design a new type of auxetic fabric structures for sportswear with enhanced deformation ability and comfort based on a basic understanding of the relationships between fabric geometrical structures and auxetic behavior; To fabricate auxetic fabrics according to the above designed fabric structures using warp knitting technology and laying-in technique; To conduct experimental studies on the deformation behavior and other physical and mechanical properties of the above fabricated auxetic fabrics for sportswear; To conduct theoretical studies on the deformation behavior and other physical mechanical properties of the auxetic fabrics, and compare with experimental results.

To fabricate auxetic fabrics according to the above designed fabric structures using warp knitting technology and laying-in technique;
To conduct experimental studies on the deformation behavior and other physical and mechanical properties of the above fabricated auxetic fabrics for sportswear;
To conduct theoretical studies on the deformation behavior and other physical mechanical properties of the auxetic fabrics, and compare with experimental results.

15209616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209616.value: Auxetic fabrics are nonconventional fabrics having negative values of Poisson’s ratio. In contrast to most conventional fabrics, auxetic fabrics expand when stretched. This unusual behavior makes them very attractive for sportswear application with enhance deformation ability and comfort. The most important point to the realization of auxetic fabrics for sportswear is the proper design of their structure and manufacturing process. A survey of the literature has shown that auxetic fabrics so far developed are not suitable for sportswear application due to some limitations such as high fabric thickness, low structural stability and elastic recovery, or low extensibility and comfort. Therefore, there is a need to conduct a systematic study on auxetic fabrics for sportswear to get a basic understanding of their structure design, manufacturing process, deformation behavior, physical and mechanical properties. More specifically, the project will deal with fundamental issues of warp-knitted auxetic fabrics for sportswear and their deformation behavior, physical and mechanical properties. A special warp knitting process will be specially developed to fabricate this type of nonconventional fabrics by using yarn laying-in technique, based on a new concept in which auxetic geometries are introduced into a ground fabric structure having high extensibility and good elastic recovery. Various auxetic fabrics for sportswear will be produced using different types of yarns and structural parameters. Both theoretical and experimental studies will be conducted to investigate their deformation behavior, physical and mechanical properties. A wearing performance study of auxetic fabrics produced with optimized structural parameters will also be carried out based on the measurement of fabric pressure on the skin under simulated movement conditions of muscles and joints. 拉脹織物是一種泊松比為負值的特殊織物。與大多數普通的織物不同，拉賬織物在被縱向拉伸時其橫向膨脹。這種不同尋常的特性使得拉脹織物非常適合應用在具有更好可變性性和舒適性的運動服飾上。而得到這種在運動服飾上應用的拉脹織物的最好的辦法是採用合適的結構設計和製造工序。對於文獻的研究表明，由於其織物厚度厚，結構穩定性和拉伸回復性差，亦或者是不好的延展性和舒適性，拉脹織物至今為止仍不適合應用在運動服飾領域。因此，有必要對應用於運動服飾上的拉脹織物開展一項系統性的研究，以便對其變形性能和物理機械性能，以及在結構設計和製造工序上的要求有一個基本的了解。 更具體地來說，該項目將涉及到有關運動服飾用的經編拉脹織物的根本問題以及對經編拉脹織物的變形特性和物理機械性能的研究。同時，基於將負泊松比幾何結構引入到地組織中從而獲得高延展性和好的拉伸回復性的新理念，一種特殊的機織工序將被開發，并結合衬垫技術織造得到這種特殊的織物。在此期間，將會織造得到各種由不同種類紗線和結構參數形成的運動服飾用的拉脹機織物，並開展相應理論和實驗上的研究來探討其變形特性和物理機械性能。另外，在模擬移動的條件下，通過對織物在肌肉和關節皮膚上產生的壓力的測量，一項有關於優化設計后得到的拉脹機織物的穿著性能研究將被開展。

15209616.label: Realisation of objectives
15209616.value: Objective 1: This objective was successfully achieved. A new type of warp knitted auxetic fabric structure for application in sportswear was first designed. In the initial design, we suggested to insert the straight laid-in yarns into a warp knitted ground structure to produce the auxetic geometries. However, after a series of preliminary tests, we found that the use of laid-in yarns to realize auxetic geometries makes the knitting process very difficult as a large variation in laid-in yarn length is required. Besides, as the deformation behavior of the fabric structure is mainly controlled by ground warp knitted structure, the auxetic effect was very difficult to be achieved. Instead of using laid-in yarns, we used elastic yarns to change a conventional non-auxetic warp knitted fabric net structure to an auxetic structure after the fabric was taken from the knitting machine. Compared to the initially proposed design, the new design is easier realized with warp knitting process to produce the warp knitted fabric structure with expected auxetic behavior. In addition, we also successfully designed another type of auxetic fabric structure for sportswear using weaving method. Objective 2: This objective was successfully achieved. A series of warp knitted auxetic fabrics were first produced on a Tricot warp knitting machine by using both elastic and non-elastic yarns based on a warp knitting process specially developed. A Chinese invention patent “A warp knitted auxetic fabric structure and relevant fabrication method” was granted. In addition to warp knitted auxetic fabrics, a series of bi-stretch woven auxetic fabrics in the purpose of application for sportswear were also produced on a Dobby weaving machine using both elastic and non-elastic yarns based on folded and re-entrant hexagonal geometries. The main problem encountered during fabrication process was difficult to control yarn tension of elastic yarns to produce very uniform auxetic fabrics as a large number of elastic yarns were used. This problem was resolved by adopting separate beams for elastic yarns and non-elastic yarns. Besides, sizing process was also developed for sizing elastic yarns for weaving process. Objective 3: This objective was successfully achieved. The deformation behaviors and mechanical properties of both the knitted and woven auxetic fabrics for sportswear in different tensile directions were systematically studied via experiments under single and repeating tension conditions. Based on testing results, the relationships between the Poisson’s ratio and tensile strain, the tensile stress and tensile strain for the fabrics made with different yarn materials and different structural parameters were generated. In addition to the tensile tests, other type of tests such as air permeability and moisture transmission were also conducted. Objective 4: This objective was successfully achieved. The theoretical analyses of both knitted and woven auxetic fabrics developed were conducted in detail. Based on these analyses, the geometrical and finite element models which can be used to predict the deformation behavior of the auxetic fabric structures for sportswear were successfully established and compared with experiments.

15209616.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209616.value: 1. New fabric structures and manufacturing processes developed to produce both the knitted and woven auxetic fabrics for sportswear by non-auxetic yarns. It is found that auxetic behavior can be achieved into a knitted structure by modifying a non-auxetic net structure to an auxetic structure with the use of elastic yarns or a woven structure by combining different tight weave and loose weave with the use of elastic and non-elastic yarns to create different auxetic geometries. The study has provided a new approach to produce auxetic fabrics for sportswear with low costs by using conventional knitting and weaving machinery. (Please refer to the publications 1-4 as attached in Part C). 2. Dependency of the auxetic behavior on tensile strain, tensile directions and tensile cycles. All the experimental studies have confirmed that the auxetic behavior of auxetic fabrics first increases and then decreases with increase of the tensile strain in all tensile directions. It is also found that all the auxetic fabrics have better auxetic behavior in the principal directions and auxetic effect decrease with the increase of tensile cycles. (Please refer to publications 2-5 attached in Part C). 3. The geometrical models developed to theoretically calculate the Poisson’s ratio values of the auextic fabrics structure based on reentrant hexagons and foldable geometry. It is found that semi-empirical relationships between the Poisson’s ratio and tensile strain can be established based on the observation of deformation process of auxetic fabrics and can be used to guide the design and fabrication of auxetic fabrics with desired auxetic behavior using the same type of materials and fabric structure. (Please refer to publications 6 and 8 attached in Part C). 4. Finite element model developed to simulate the deformation behavior of the warp knitted fabric structure based on a real fabric geometry. It is found that the modified reentrant structure from rectangular geometry by using yarns with different moduli can achieve auxetic behavior and its Poisson’s ratio are strongly dependent on their initial micro-geometric parameters. (Please refer to publication 7 attached in Part C). 5. 8 refereed journal papers, 4 oral presentations at international conferences and one granted patent.

15209616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209616.value: The proposed project is concerned with a systematic study of auxetic fabrics for sportswear with enhanced deformation ability and comfort. The warp knitted and woven auxetic fabrics are first designed and fabricated using elastic and non-elastic yarns based on different auxetic geometries. Then, the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of the auxetic fabrics under single and repeating tensile loading conditions are experimentally and theoretically studied. Geometrical and finite element models are finally developed to predict the deformation behavior of these special fabric structures. The significance and value of the project is to provide a basic understanding on the structure characteristics, formation principle, fabricating method, deformation behavior and mechanical properties of auxetic fabrics. The study will provide direct insights into the design and fabrication of auxetic fabrics with nonconventional behavior using both knitting and weaving technologies. Due to the unusual properties, the newly developed auxetic fabrics cannot only be used for sportswear, they can also be very attractive for many other applications such as underwear, functional garments, smart bandages, etc. The study will promote the new development of textile products using the latest concept and technologies to increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile and fashion industry.

15210116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210116.value: One of the most common types of 3-dimensional spinal deformities with unknown etiology in youths is adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). The spinal curvature increases as puberty progresses. Generally, rigid orthotic bracewear is prescribed as non-invasive treatment for moderate AIS if treatment begins early and the orthosis is worn with compliance. Obviously, teenage patients are reluctant to accept a rigid orthosis due to aesthetics and the physical constraint. Therefore, semi-rigid and flexible orthoses have been developed, but their efficacy is still controversial and there are other issues, such as high pain scores. There is clearly room for improvement. Therefore, a garment-type of bracewear will be designed and developed to correct spinal deformity, reduce the possibility of spinal curve progression, and satisfy the needs of the patients as well as take their psychological concerns into consideration. A multi-disciplinary collaborative approach is adopted for this project. The design of the anisotropic textile braces will provide different mechanisms with rigid, semi-rigid and flexible materials: a) axial elongation through a close fit of the brace supported with textile composites on the lateral sides of the trunk, b) 3-point pressure with push and counter-pushes through semi-rigid pads inserted inside the pocket lining, c) pulling or compression to correct kyphosis or lordosis in the sagittal plane with elastic bands, d) derotation between the pelvis and shoulders with uneven straps, and e) an active mechanism with sensors added to the brace to maintain correct posture. The biomechanical efficiency of the braces will be evaluated with finite element (FE) modeling of the spine of AIS patients. The effects of the design components of the anisotropic textile braces, such as stiffness of the textile composite and loadings on different body parts, will be examined by the established FE model. The main and two-way interaction effects of the tested design components on the 3D corrections generated by the textile brace can be evaluated. Clinical trials and a non-invasive method for evaluation and periodically monitoring will also be carried out. The activity profiles and postures of the subjects during the wear trial period will be logged on their smart phones. Researchers or doctors can access the data to check user compliance and provide comments. Psychological and physiological changes after wearing the brace will be recorded. The brace will also be examined for dimensional changes and deformities. The effectiveness of the anisotropic textile braces will be evaluated through X-ray radiography at pre- and post- treatment. 青少年原發性脊柱側彎 (AIS) 是三維脊柱變形中最常見的一種，病因至今仍然不明。在青春期間，脊柱側彎變形的情況會越見惡化，因此建議患者盡早配合治療。配戴硬支架矯正器為非侵入性治療，一般可用作治療中度脊柱側彎患者，但基於美觀和活動限制因素，大部分青少年病患均感到抗拒。隨後，半軟硬脊柱矯正器的研發正正能改善其靈活性，卻衍生了痛楚問題，而其矯正功效亦備受爭議。 有鑒於此，本項目將會設計研發一件非等向性紡織矯正衣 ，用以改善脊柱變形、減低脊柱側彎弧度遞增的風險及將患者的心理顧慮列入考慮因素，以滿足病患者需要。 是次非等向性紡織矯正衣研究項目採取多學科協作模式，集硬、半軟硬和柔軟物料於一身，以提供有別於以往硬支架矯正器的機能構造：1) 利用矯正衣的緊身性質配合放置在身驅兩側的紡織合成物從而達至軸向延長效果，2) 透過放置多塊呈半軟硬的墊於不同位置的內置口袋以形成三點推及反推之壓力, 3) 運用鬆緊帶在縱切面的拉和施壓去改正脊椎前凸或後凸的狀況，4) 不規側的帶在盤骨和肩膊間有反旋的作用，及5) 附加在矯正衣的感應器能發揮活性機械作用， 用以保持正確的姿態。 矯正衣針對AIS 患者脊柱的生物力學效率將會以有限元模型的方式作評估，當中包括布料的堅硬度、施加於身體各部位的負荷等設計元素，從而推計對三維脊柱較正的主要和相互影響。 監察和評估將以臨床測試及非侵入性方式定期進行。穿戴矯正衣時的姿勢和活動分析將記錄在患者的智能電話，以便研究員和脊柱外科醫生就觀察用者的配合性作出相應的建議。穿戴後的生心理變化 ，矯正衣的尺寸變化和變形程度，以及治療前後的 X-光攝片則會用作評估矯正衣的效用。

15210116.label: Realisation of objectives
15210116.value: The research methodology includes the design and development of a new anisotropic textile brace for patients with AIS, finite element modelling for design optimization and clinical trial of the proposed brace design. In response to the first objective, an anisotropic textile braces for AIS was developed. The anisotropic textile braces comprised a bra top, pants, a pelvis belt, as well as an artificial back bone with hinges that were cushioned with padding and corrective components that aim to maximise the corrective effect of the flexible bracing and minimise the negative impacts of rigid bracing such as mobility restriction and discomfort. The corrective component with a semi-rigid silicone pad is the key to providing direct corrective forces that push against the convex part of the body for spinal correction. The open design of the concave part of the brace allows for expansion of the body to promote the corrective performance. The textile materials for the anisotropic textile brace are also selected based on the fabric testing results and the criteria required of the individual components. Elastic band R153132_166 was selected for the corrective component due to its high modulus and low force decay with time and repeated exercise movement. Fabric DN64013S was selected for the main fabric due to its outstanding tensile behaviour, excellent thermal comfort, moderate sensorial comfort, and good dimensional stability during laundering. Elastic Strap 4443_25 was selected as the elastic webbing of the bra top and pants due to its outstanding modulus, excellent recoverability and good dimensional stability during laundering. As for the development of the garment pattern, 21 AIS subjects were recruited to undergo 3D body scanning to obtain their measurements. Their upper breast, under breast, under band, pelvis, hip circumferences, leg hold, waist to gusset, under band to pelvis, upper breast to pelvis and shoulder strap lengths were measured. In order to achieve a better fit through mass production of the prototype, two prototype sizes were developed - small and medium, according to the BMI results. In total, 35 pieces were used to construct the proposed functional intimate apparel for AIS including one thoracic and one lumbar corrective component. In response to the second objective, a numerical finite element model (FEM) was developed to simulate the effectiveness of in-brace spinal correction of the anisotropic textile brace. Few studies that have investigated the effectiveness of flexible braces for treating scoliosis by using a biomechanical model. This study, therefore, develops 3D skeletal, torso, and brace models for FE analysis. A scoliotic female subject was recruited for the development of the FEM and her parents provided consent for her participation. The subject was invited to undergo a radiographic examination, and then 3D body scanning to extract the geometry of her skeletal frame and torso. The simulation model mainly consists of three parts: the torso body, skeleton and FIA. To build the FEM, first, the geometry models of the torso body, skeleton and FIA were created. Secondly, the material properties and element type were defined. After meshing, the numerical processing of wearing the FIA on the torso was conducted by defining the initial and boundary conditions, displacement condition of the FIA and the loading condition of the torso surface to obtain the numerical solution. To validate this FE model, a scoliotic patient was recruited and an in-brace radiographic examination was conducted. The measured and simulated spinal curves showed a similar trend. The correlation coefficient of the vertebral body displacement was 0.74 which was comparable to the results obtained experimentally. To further investigate the biomechanics of the brace and optimise the design of the brace, the effect of loading which was applied on the torso surface on the vertebrae was studied. Fifteen models with thoracic and lumbar loading which increased from 20% to 140% and decreased from 20% to 80% were created to investigate the effect of the spinal curve on the magnitude of loading. To response to the third objective, a clinical trial has been conducted. The aim of this trial is to assess the effectiveness of proposed anisotropic textile brace. The clinical study involves two phases which are the 2-hour clinical study and 3-month clinical study. The subject selection criteria were females diagnosed with AIS who have a Cobb’s angle between 20 to 30 degrees, between 10 and 13 years old, at a high risk of further progression in their spinal curve, and a Risser grade ≤ 2. The exclusion criteria were patients with contraindications of x-ray exposure, diagnosis of other musculoskeletal or developmental illness that might be responsible for the spinal curvature, contraindications for pulmonary or exercise tests, and psychiatric disorders. The 2-hour clinical study investigated the initial performance of the functional intimate apparel, including variables such as the initial in-brace performance, initial changes in the body contours, psychological and physiological comfort on the wearers and effect of the biomechanics of the brace on the interface pressure. After the initial 2-hour clinical study, the subject who showed an in-brace reduction of the spinal curvature of 80% was invited to participate in the 3-month clinical study. During the 3-month clinical study, she wore the functional intimate apparel for at least 8 hours every day for three months. Subsequently, she underwent an ultrasound assessment and 3D body scanning, answered questions to determine her health-related quality of life (HRQL) and participated in a short interview to provide feedback.

15210116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210116.value: A simulation model was constructed which simulated the loading of the anisotropic textile brace onto the body, showed the biomechanics of the brace and predicted spinal movement after using the brace. Fifteen FE models with different thoracic and lumbar loadings were created to further optimise the loading of the pads. The results show that managing lumbar loading was essential since it was a counter force to the thoracic loading and influenced the movement of the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae. The models in this study showed that a 140% increase in lumbar loading provided the optimum amount of spinal correction. From the results of clinical study, 3 of the 5 subjects showed an in-brace reduction of more than 5˚ in their spinal curvature, 1 about 5˚ and 1 showed an in-brace increase in curvature of about 5˚. The initial rate of the in-brace reduction of the spinal curvature ranged between 9.7% and 88.7%. The result of this preliminary study might be potentially comparable with those of some of the rigid braces in the literature. Regarding the changes in the initial asymmetry of the contours, 4 of the 5 subjects showed a reduction in body asymmetry and the in-brace rate of reduction of POTSI ranged between 13.1% and 43.2%. Regarding the wear comfort, the average BSSQ-Brace score was 14.0 ± 3.3 which meant that the subjects experienced a moderate level of stress when they wore the garment. Also, the BrQ score showed that the proposed brace almost never caused negative impacts or problems in terms of their perceived general health, physical functioning, body pain and social functioning. Regarding biomechanics, the interface pressure of the thoracic corrective pad and lumbar/thoracolumbar corrective pad ranged between 6.0 kPa-24.4 kPa and 6.1 kPa-9.7 kPa respectively which is similar to that of the rigid braces. This implied that textile materials might be possible to exert a similar amount of corrective force as rigid braces. One of the subjects consented to participation in a three-month clinical study. After wearing the brace for 3 months, her Cobb’s angle was reduced by 52.7%, shoulder rotation was reduced by 29.8% and POTSI was increased by 13.1%. However, her shoulder obliquity increased by 1.3˚.In terms of changes in quality of life, her SRS-22 Questionnaire score at pre-intervention and after 3 months of brace wear was similar, which implied that her quality of life was not substantially affected after wearing the proposed brace.

15210116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210116.value: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using anisotropic textile materials which exert direct corrective force for spinal correction. The finite element model enables to simulate the biomechanics of the proposed brace for design optimisation. By changing the material properties of the model, an ideal condition for achieving the optimum spinal correction could hence be predicted in the future. More importantly, the current clinical results show that the proposed anisotropic textile brace provides adequate corrective pressure and obtains certain in-brace correction. Nevertheless, the sample size was too small. A larger sample size with randomised control trial is highly recommended for further investigate the effectiveness pf proposed brace. Moreover, a comparison of rigid brace is also suggested for further evaluation. To ensure the validity of results, a 2-year randomised control trial with 90 sample size is recommended. Subjects are randomly assigned into one of three groups of proposed brace, rigid brace, and observation group as a control and undergo at least 2 year follow up in which the spinal deformity, contour asymmetry and quality of life are examined.

15210116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210116.value: About 2-3% of teenagers had a condition of spinal deformity with unknown reasons, also known as adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Scoliosis not causes asymmetry in body contour, but also might lead to back pain and even respiratory diseases. To slow or arrest the progression of scoliosis, bracing is a universal conservative treatment option. There are two kinds of scoliosis braces, namely, rigid brace and flexible brace. Rigid bracing is a traditional effective treatment. However, mobility restriction and discomfort are usually the shortcoming of rigid brace. Therefore, flexible brace is an alternative option; however, its effectiveness is still controversial. In this study, a scientific approach is adopted to design and develop an anisotropic textile brace as a treatment option for adolescents with moderate scoliosis. Finite element model was developed for investigating the biomechanics of the spinal correction process. An anisotropic textile brace was developed to enhance the correction effect and maximise wear comfort as well as wearers’ mobility. The artificial hinge is the key component to stabilise the asymmetric corrective straps for the effective corrective forces. The clinical study shows that the proposed brace provided about 39% in-brace correction.

Demonstrate high power output >1 Watt of the mode locking and Q-switching laser operating at near and mid infrared region, e.g. 1 micron, 1.5 micron by using these novel 2D materials based saturable absorbers, as well as charactering the long term stability of output pulses.

15210916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210916.value: 層狀結構二維材料作為下一代光電器件的核心模塊，已逐漸引起基礎科學和技術應用領域的极大關注。各個層內通過化學鍵牢固連接，層間以範德華力吸引結合，並顯示出量子限域特性, 這些優越的物化性能使得二維材料在製備高性能柔性精密光電子器件中備受矚目。石墨烯帶隙窄、層間結合力小，導至較弱的光學調製特效，在非綫性光電應用中受到限制。目前，研究熱點現已轉到具有可調控能帶結構特性的二維材料。 新型能帶可調的二維材料主要有黑磷及過渡金屬硫化物（如能帶可調的二硫化鎢），光譜響應範圍介于可見光到中紅外綫，幾乎可使用于所有商用激光及光電子設備係統。因此，調控新型二維材料的光學飽和吸收性能有著巨大的基礎研究意義和實用價值。然而，到目前為止，通過能帶調控優化的二維材料應用在高性能激光器件研究很少。 本課題的研究重點在于研究上述材料的光學飽和吸收性能與其在激光器件上的應用，我們已證實了二硫化鎢二維材料的非綫性光限幅特性，該工作已發表。在該研究基礎上，通過進一步調整二維材料帶隙，優化光學性能，可實現光限幅特性的不斷提高。 最新研究表明，一些多層二維材料在空氣或者液體裏不穩定，尤其是在激光激發狀態下。因此通過一些方法或技術來封裝這些二維材料至關重要。本課題提出解決這一問題的方法，例如通過將材料納入玻璃基質或者埰用其他封裝技術。從該研究中我們將了解到製備具有高光學損傷閾值的飽和吸收體，在不同波長下操作的高功率脈沖激光器和鎖模激光係統來表徵所製備的飽和吸收體的性能。 光學飽和吸收作為自然界一種重要的物理現象，有著許多重要的應用，包括脈沖激光、生物成像、光開關、光學計算機和數據存儲。這些二維材料在太陽能電池、晶體管、光限幅、葯物傳輸和可再生能源發電等領域也有廣泛的應用。因此，開發這些材料的飽和吸收性能和封裝技術對脈沖激光及其他不同領域的研究也有著長遠的影響。

15210916.label: Realisation of objectives
15210916.value: It is my second GRF since I came back Hong Kong in 2009. I have used the money very carefully. This project has been carrying out successfully and producing many high quality publications 27 SCI journals in total and 1 new journal. All objectives are achieved. * From the mid-term report comments, I can see the assessor have some concerns regarding the first author of the publications, whether they are research students under my supervision or not. Therefore, I have checked and found that my PhD students are first author for 17 papers and my research associate is first author for 2 papers. These publications, demonstrating the research output, include 1 × IF, Impact Factor = 12.1 Advanced Functional Materials, “frontispiece”, 1 × IF = 9.2 NPG Asia Materials, 10 × (IF > 5), e.g. ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces, Nano Research, J Material Chemistry C, 13 × (IF > 3) e.g. Photonic Research, Optic Letters, Optics Express, IEEE J. of Lightwave Technology, RSC Advances, etc. (3 × cover pages and 1 × frontispiece articles are also included.) The saturable absorption properties of the WS2 nanofilms were investigated systematically under the excitation by laser pulses with various durations in the fs, ps and ns. A pulse width-dependent theoretical model of saturable absorption that considers the effects of interband exciton recombination has been proposed for the first time. This work has been accepted by The JMCC as cover page article [1]. Moreover, the optical limiting properties of the MoS2/PMMA films were studiedand published as cover page article [13]. We have tried various fabrication technique, e.g. melt quenching, sputtering etc. for fabricating various 2D materials based saturable absorbers. This research focus on exploring the novel 2D material’s nonlinear optical properties and used for Q-switching and mode locking operations with producing operational wavelengths mainly 1 micron or 1.5 micron. The long terms stability are tested and reported for various 2D materials based absorbers. In correspondence to that, the WS2 saturable absorber was fabricated and characterized. The absorber was used to generate Q-swicthed pulses [2]. However, recently the research on group 10, 2D materials has become very important and popular due to its exceptional electronic and optoelectronic properties. Therefore, the novel PtS2, PtSe2 and PtTe2 film have been fabricated and characterized for this research project. Moreover, luminescent PtS2 quantum dots were fabricated and investigated [18]. However, we have found that it has broadband saturable absorption features and excellent optoelectronic properties. It exhibits excellent properties for saturable absorbers applications. Therefore, we have used PtS2 microflakes saturable absorber for generating Q-switching pulses [3] and ultrafast mode locking [20], vertically standing PtSe2 absorber to generate mode locking laser pulses [4] and PtTe2 absorber for Q-switching applications [23]. The laser output power and stability were also characterized. Size –dependent NLO properties of the atomically thin PtS2 nanosheet are also studied [25]. Furthermore, it was demonstrated that PdS2, a new member of 2D materials based saturable absorber, can be used to produce Q-switched and mode-locked laser pulses [24]. In2Se3 2D layered nanosheets were also successfully used for femtosecond laser pulses generation [22]. Another novel ultrasmall 2D GaTe [15] and NbSe2 [27] quantum dots were used for ultrafast laser pulse generation with duration of 115 fs [15] and 380 ps [27]. The GaTe research is highlighted as cover page [15]. Additionally, we have also found that some of these 2D layered materials exhibit favorable optoelectronic properties for photodetector applications. Therefore, the materials fabricated in our Lab has also been used to fabricate some high performance heterojunction photodetectors. The layered PtSe2 combined with GaAs to produce heterojunction. Our research findings related to this PtSe2/GaAs heterojunction photodetector was published in Advanced Functional Materials (IF~12.12) and this paper was selected as frontispiece article [5]. Ultrafast and sensitive photodetector based on a PtSe2/Silicon nanowire array heterojunction are fabricated and it exhibits multiband spectral response from 200 to 1550 nm [12]. PtSe2/GaN heterojunction for self-powered deep ultraviolet photodetector was fabricated and characterized [21]. Additionally, the fabricated MoS2 material has been used to fabricate high quality photodetectors as well [6] and [7]. 2D Layered PtSe2/CdTe heterojunction was produced for the high-performance, room-temperature, broadband, infrared photodetector [28]. This project is also partly support some other works related to novel materials used for renewable energy generation [8] [9] [21], solar cells related theory and technology development [11] [16] [17] [26], ultrahigh adsorption 2D materials for water pollutants removal [14] and a novel sensor for real time health monitoring [10]. 15210916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210916.value: We are the pioneer research group working in the novel group 10 2D materials used for pulsed lasers and photodetectors. These novel 2D materials exhibit strong optical and electronic properties, and importantly it is very stable under ambient conditions. We have demonstrated the potential and possible of these novel materials to be used for high performance broadband light detection or as saturable absorbers used for pulsed laser generation. Due to the favorable features of the materials, it allows high performance and strong operational stability compared with other 2D materials. Therefore, these publications achieved a high level of citation within a short period of time. Additionally, this project also allow us to explore some common package waste used for solar energy conversion for fresh water generation. This work is later awarded silver Medal in the Asia Exhibition of Innovation, Hong Kong. It is hosted in Hong Kong, organized by The Hong Kong Exporters’ Association (HKEA) and the International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva. Our group is also predominantly working on the optics of perovskite solar cells. Perovskites are one of the most exciting material systems in the photovoltaic research community that includes extraordinary optical and electrical properties. The energy conversion efficiency has been increased from 3.8% to over 25%. We systematically investigate the optics of perovskite solar cells, and it is found that the front contact of the perovskite solar cells has a major impact on the optics of perovskite solar cells. We carried out simulations to apprehend the optics and optimization of the device design. Furthermore, we experimentally fabricated an optimized design for the front contact of perovskite solar cells, which allows proving efficient photon management through improved light incoupling and light trapping. Hence, the short-circuit current density and energy conversion efficiency are significantly enhanced.

15210916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210916.value: The 2D layered materials based laser photonic devices is expected to bring some revolutionary changes into the field. Therefore, it attracts a great deal of attention from the research community globally. Further research on properties of other new and unexplored 2D materials will continue to be a hot research area. Another direction is further enhanced the laser photonic device performance by enhancing the 2D materials intrinsic properties through materials engineering. Some of our preliminary study shows further reduce 2D materials layer into quantum dot could greatly enhance the nonlinear optical properties. We can further explore the device performance and production methods regarding the novel 2D quantum dots. Additionally, the device performance changes for further minimization of the device in the micro scale is no yet been fully explored and studied.

15210916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210916.value: The project allows us to explore some novel two dimensional materials (graphene like structure), e.g. GaTe, MoS2, WS2, PtS2, PdS2, NbSe2 based 2D materials. These new atomic thick materials have many attractive features e.g. wide bandgap, strong light response, high conductivity, high stability so that devices made up of these materials could have some attractive properties e.g. broad operational wavelength range and strong optoelectronic properties, compactness etc. Devices made up of these novel materials offer revolutionary changes in performance and function. We have successfully demonstrated some low cost method to engineer the intrinsic nonlinear optical properties of PtS2. By using these newly developed materials, we have first demonstrate some practical applications e.g. ultrafast laser pulses generation (with pulse duration ~115 fs) and high performance broadband (ultraviolet to infrared) photo-detection. Additionally, the funding also supports some completed research works for solar thermal energy conversion for fresh water generation, solar cells development, sensors for health monitoring. These project have open new research directions and opportunities for these novel materials.

15211016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211016.value: Wearable textile devices that harvest mechanical energy from ambient or human motion are attractive because the renewable energy source can be carried by people to anywhere without restriction of fixed recharging stations. However, up-to-date, among various approaches, that is, piezoelectric, triboelectric and electromagnetic ones as well as their hybrids, there has not yet been single one that reaches the required level of energy. Among them, triboelectric generators are light, low cost and show great promises to meet the challenge. In principle, triboelectric generators are based upon triboelectric effect and electrostatic induction. Previously, the electrostatic induction has been treated theoretically by others with success. However, the charge generation by triboelectric effect at molecular level has been regarded as a complex and small-probability event poorly understood in general. The effects of secondary structures of polymers, e.g. crystallinity, localized polarization and doping of fibers, as well as textile structures remain elusive. This project is, therefore, attempted to address these critical issues. First, triboelectric properties of a range of textile materials will be measured in terms of areal density, affinity, half decay time of the charges by using a newly developed characterization platform. Their relationships with fiber materials, textile architectural parameters, friction and surface morphology will be established experimentally for the first time. Secondly, an extended triboelectric table will be formed by including new fiber materials and textile structures that are missing in the existing triboelectric tables. The new table will provide a very useful guidance for design and selection of textile materials . Thirdly, the project attempts to develop a theoretical model for the triboelectricity of textiles. The ab initio method will be employed to determine the intrinsic polarity and saturated areal density of charges based on the molecular structures of fiber materials given in the new triboelectric table. The effects of secondary structures in polymers, doping and structural parameters of textile surfaces will also be considered as correction factors for the prediction model verified by experiments. Finally, novel demonstration prototypes of textile triboelectric generators will be designed under the guidance of the newly developed theoretical model and triboelectric table, fabricated and tested. Their performance will be benchmarked against those reported in the literature and our previous work.

15211016.label: Realisation of objectives
15211016.value: All objectives have been achieved fully. Our lab-made characterization platform for fabric triboelectricity has been used to determine the effects of pressure, speed, length of frictional contact of a range of textile fabrics made from existing and new fibers. The investigations included yarn parameters like counts and twist or intermingling frequency and knitted fabric parameters like structures, density, and surface finishing. All the planned measurements were completed and data collected. The relationships between the measured triboelectric properties and materials, textile architecture, and surface properties have been derived by analyzing the experimental data. A new list of triboelectricity of the studied fabrics was developed and compared with previously published ones. We have developed and demonstrated a few prototypes of textile triboelectric generators in both contact mode and sliding mode, benchmarking their performance with literature.

15211016.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211016.value: We have used a previously developed characterization platform of fabric triboelectricity, experimentally determined the effects of pressure, speed, length of frictional contact on triboelectric properties of textile materials, and established testing protocols by optimizing the operational parameters. Then we conducted a systematic experimental study of a range of textile materials with selected fibers, designed structural architectures of fiber, yarn and fabric. An extended triboelectricity table of fabrics (areal density and polarity of electric charges) was constructed including new polymers fibers. We investigated the theoretical upper limit of output from a contact TENG by introducing the field-induced charges. We also designed and fabricated prototypes of textile triboelectric generators using the selected fibers, yarn and fabric structures, tested the prototypes and compared their energy harvesting efficiency with those reported in the literature and our previous work.

15211016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211016.value: Our theoretical analysis indicated that the current triboelectric materials and charge-induced electric breakdown may limit the resultant contact-separation mode triboelectric generators in driving existing wearable systems. We need to explore new mechanisms to increase charge density and increase the energy output of harvesters.

15211016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211016.value: We have studied the triboelectric properties, related surface and porous structures of a range of polymeric textile fabrics. We developed a new extended triboeletricity table of areal charge density of a range of textile fabrics made from polymer fibers. We discovered that the bio-based fibers like PLA, PGA, PHB or PHBV from the linear aliphatic polyester family have the highest positive charge density. The pressure has a significant effect on charge transfer. We also discovered that field-induced breakdown limits the output energy from a contact-separate mode triboelectric generator. We established the theoretical upper limits for these generators, which will shed light on the directions of future research endeavor.

15213516.label: Project Objectives
15213516.value: To develop a generalized self-paced learning (GSPL) approach for automatic annotation and uncertainty modeling – By exploring the intrinsic structure of the given data, we will develop a GSPL model to iteratively assign an uncertainty degree and a pseudo label for each unlabeled sample. Elaborate self-paced functions will be designed to guide the learning of uncertainty measure, while appropriate loss functions and regularizers will be defined to guarantee the robustness of GSPL against outliers. The GSPL will reduce significantly the burden of manual annotation. To develop an uncertainty-guided sample selection approach for minimal manual annotation – With the proposed GSPL, there still remain a substantial amount of unlabeled samples with high uncertainty. We will develop an uncertainty-guided structured sparse representation (USSR) model to select a minimal amount of most representative and informative samples for manual annotation. To develop a robust learning approach for classification – Since outliers and incorrectly labeled data are inevitable for large-scale datasets, we will develop robust learning models and algorithms to assure the robustness of classifier by considering both margin-based loss and distribution-based loss. To design new performance evaluation measures for large-scale visual recognition – The existing evaluation measures for visual recognition mostly focus on the overall classification accuracy, without considering the labeling cost and model robustness, which are crucial factors for large-scale visual recognition. In this project, new measures will be proposed to more comprehensively assess the performance of large-scale visual recognition methods.

15213516.label: Realisation of objectives
15213516.value: Objectives 1 and 2: Self-paced learning for automatic annotation and uncertainty-guided sample selection Learning from large-scale unlabeled or partially labeled data is of fundamental importance. Many active learning (AL) methods have been proposed to retrieve representative minority samples according to predefined confidence or uncertainty thresholds. However, these AL methods ignore the remaining majority samples (i.e., those with low uncertainty or high prediction confidence). Under the applications of object detection and video summarization, we investigated the problem of learning with minimal annotation as follows. First, we developed a principled self-supervised sample mining (SSM) method for the real challenges in object detection. Specifically, our SSM concentrates on automatically discovering and pseudo-labeling reliable region proposals for enhancing the object detector, i.e., pasting these proposals into different labeled images to measure their values under different image contexts. By resorting to the SSM process, we proposed a framework for gradually incorporating unlabeled or partially labeled data into the model learning while minimizing the annotating effort of users. This work is published in CVPR'2018 [C1]. Second, we developed an active sample mining (ASM) framework. We demonstrated that cost-effectively mining samples from the unlabeled majority data is the key to train more powerful object detectors while minimizing user annotation. Specifically, our ASM framework involves a switchable sample selection mechanism for determining whether an unlabeled sample should be manually annotated or automatically pseudo-labeled via a novel self-learning process. In this process, the detector is first applied to the unlabeled samples (i.e., object proposals) to estimate their labels and output the corresponding prediction confidences. Then, we select a number of samples and assign pseudo-labels to them. Then, these temporarily labeled samples are employed for network fine-tuning. Our method is suitable for object categories that are not seen in the unlabeled data during the learning process. Our ASM framework can achieve performance comparable to competing methods but with significantly fewer annotations. This work is published in TNNLS'19 [J1]. Third, the anchor refinement module (ARM) has been proposed to adjust the initialization of default anchors. However, this module brings another problem: all pixels at a feature map have the same receptive field while the anchors associated with each pixel have different positions and sizes. This discordance may lead to a less effective detector. We developed a dynamic feature selection operation to select new pixels in a feature map for each refined anchor received from the ARM. Furthermore, to enhance the representation ability of selected feature pixels, we design a bidirectional feature fusion module by combining features from early and deep layers. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC and COCO demonstrated the effectiveness of our dynamic anchor feature selection (DAFS) operation. This work is published in ICCV'19 [C5]. Fourth, unsupervised domain adaption (UDA) is a promising solution to enhance the generalization ability of a model from a source domain to a target domain without manually annotating labels for the target data. Recent works in cross-domain object detection mostly resort to adversarial feature adaptation to match the marginal distributions of two domains. However, perfect feature alignment is hard to achieve and is likely to cause negative transfer due to the high complexity of object detection. We proposed a different approach to reduce the domain gap by a self-training paradigm, which regards the pseudo-labels as ground truth to fully exploit the unlabeled target data. In order to generate more informative pseudo labels, we proposed a category dictionary guided (CDG) UDA model for cross-domain object detection. Compared with decision boundary based classifiers such as softmax, the proposed CDG scheme can select more informative and reliable pseudo-boxes. Experiments show that the proposed CDG significantly exceeds the state-of-the-arts in cross-domain object detection. This work is published in AAAI'21 [C6]. At last, Video summarization is a challenging under-constrained problem because the underlying summary of a single video strongly depends on users’ subjective understandings, while it is extremely expensive to acquire the temporal annotations of a large-scale video dataset. To leverage the plentiful web-crawled videos to improve the performance of video summarization, we developed a generative modelling framework to learn the latent semantic video representations to bridge the benchmark data and web data. A loss term to learn the semantic matching between the generated summaries and web videos is presented, and the overall framework is further formulated into a unified conditional variational encoder-decoder. Experiments on the CoSum and TVSum datasets demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed weakly supervised method to existing state-of-the-art methods. This work is published in ECCV'18 [C3]. Objective 3. Robust learning approach for visual classification In this project, we proposed two robust learning approaches for visual classification. First, fine-grained visual categorization (FGVC) extremely relies on the modeling of appearance and interactions of various semantic parts. To address this issue, we propose an end-to-end framework based on higher-order integration of hierarchical convolutional activations for FGVC. A polynomial kernel based predictor is proposed to capture higher-order statistics of convolutional activations for modeling part interaction. To model inter-layer part interactions, we extend polynomial predictor to integrate hierarchical activations via kernel fusion. Our approach exploits higher-order intra-layer and inter-layer relations for better integration of hierarchical convolutional features. The proposed framework yields more robust discriminative representation and achieves competitive results on the widely used FGVC datasets. This work is published in ICCV'17 [C2]. Second, 2nd order pooling has proved to be more effective than its first-order counterpart in visual classification tasks. However, second-order pooling suffers from the high computational cost. We developed a novel architecture, namely detachable second-order pooling network, to leverage the advantage of second-order pooling by first-order networks while keeping the model complexity unchanged during inference. During the training stage, the auxiliary second order pooling networks assist the backbone first-order network to learn more discriminative feature representations. When training is completed, all auxiliary branches can be removed and only the backbone first-order network is used for inference. Experiments conducted on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet datasets demonstrated the leading performance of our network. This work is published in TNNLS'21 [J2]. Objective 4. Performance evaluation measures for visual understanding We investigated the problem of new performance evaluation measures in the application of image cropping, which aims to improve the composition as well as aesthetic quality of an image by removing extraneous content from it. Existing image cropping databases provide only one or several human-annotated bounding boxes as the groundtruth, which cannot reflect the non-uniqueness and flexibility of image cropping in practice. The existing evaluation metrics such as intersection-over-union cannot reliably reflect the real performance of cropping models, either. We revisited the problem of image cropping, and presents a grid anchor based formulation by considering the special properties and requirements (e.g., local redundancy, content preservation, aspect ratio) of image cropping. Our formulation reduces the annotation space of candidate crops from millions to less than one hundred. Consequently, a grid anchor based cropping benchmark is constructed, and more reliable evaluation metrics are defined. Our model can stably output visually pleasing crops and our measure can better reflect the cropping quality. This work is published in CVPR'19 [C4].

15213516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213516.value: 1) A principled self-supervised sample mining (SSM) is proposed, which automatically discovers and pseudo-labels reliable region proposals to enhance the object detector. By using SSM, a framework is developed to gradually incorporate unlabeled or partially labeled data into the model learning while minimizing the annotating effort of users. [C1] 2) An active sample mining (ASM) framework is developed to cost-effectively mine samples from the unlabeled majority data to train more powerful object detectors while minimizing user annotation. ASM is well suitable for object categories that are not seen in the unlabeled data during the learning process. It achieves competing performance with SOTA but with significantly fewer annotations. [J1] 3) A dynamic anchor feature selection (DAFS) method is proposed to enhance the representation ability of selected feature pixels for single-stage object detector. A bidirectional feature fusion module is designed by combining features from early and deep layers. [C5] 4) We propose a novel approach to reduce the domain gap in cross-domain object detection by a self-training paradigm, which regards the pseudo-labels as ground truth to fully exploit the unlabeled target data. The proposed method significantly exceeds state-of-the-arts in cross-domain object detection. [C6] 5) We propose an end-to-end framework based on higher-order integration of hierarchical convolutional activations for fine-grained visual categorization. Our approach exploits higher-order intra-layer and inter-layer relations to yield more robust discriminative representation and achieves competitive results. [C2] 6) We developed a novel architecture, namely detachable second-order pooling network, to leverage the advantage of second-order pooling by first-order networks while keeping the model complexity unchanged during inference. [J2] 7) We revisit the problem of image cropping, and presents a grid anchor based formulation by considering the special properties and requirements of it. Our formulation reduces the annotation space of candidate crops from millions to less than one hundred. A grid anchor based cropping benchmark is constructed, and more reliable performance evaluation metrics are defined. [C4]

15213516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213516.value: With the rapid development of deep learning techniques and their applications in recent years, the amount of available training data is significantly increased. However, the labeling of huge amount data is still expensive or prohibitive. Semi-supervised and even unsupervised learning become more important. In this project, we developed several self-supervised and weakly-supervised learning methods, as well as some new feature learning algorithms, to address the problem of robust learning with minimal annotation. In the future, we will further investigate the following two problems: 1. Cross-domain visual adaption. We may have enough labeled data in domain A to train a good model, but very few labeled data of the same objects in domain B. So how can train robust model in domain B without much labeling cost deserves to be further studied. 2. Data augmentation and generation. The generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown great potentials to synthesize realistic images. If we can train GANs to generate virtual samples with labels, this will be a very cost-effective way for data augmentation.

15213516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213516.value: The success of visual recognition relies heavily on labeled training data. However, annotating a massive amount of samples is expensive. In this project, we developed several cost-effective and robust learning methods for visual recognition and understanding with minimal manual annotation. First, we proposed a self-supervised sample mining and an active sample mining methods to automatically discover and pseudo-label reliable region proposals to train powerful object detectors while minimizing user annotation. A dynamic anchor feature selection method was also proposed to enhance the representation ability of selected features. Second, we proposed a novel approach to reduce the domain gap in cross-domain object detection to fully exploit the unlabeled target data. Third, we proposed a higher-order feature learning framework to learn more robust representation for fine-grained visual classification, and developed a detachable second-order pooling network to leverage the representation power of second-order pooling while keeping low model complexity. At last, we reformulated the problem of image cropping, which reduces the annotation space of candidate crops from millions to less than one hundred. A new benchmark and more reliable performance evaluation metrics were also defined. Our outputs provide practical solutions to train low-cost models for large scale visual learning problems.

15214916.label: Project Objectives
15214916.value: The goal of this research is to develop a novel method to calibrate satellite remote sensing water vapor measurements using ground-based multi-station, multi-sensor water vapor observations, with the aim to improve the accuracy of water vapor data retrieved from remote sensing satellite. More specifically, this project will achieve the following objectives: (1) Develop a new approach for satellite remote sensing water vapor retrieval that numerically models the relationship between solar radiation transmittance and accurate real-world ground-based, multi-station, multi-sensor PWV observations. The innovation of this model is that it is based on accurate real-world observations and that it can be frequently updated using frequently observed ground-based PWV. This is an improvement over the traditional Look-Up-Table method used in satellite remote sensing PWV retrieval, which is generated based on radiative transfer models (they are empirical models). (2) Investigate two new strategies to enhance the accuracy of water vapor retrieval from ground-based GNSS observations, which will provide the most important source data for both model construction and model validation. (3) Investigate three new strategies to heighten the accuracy of satellite remote sensing PWV by considering different types of land cover specifics and multiple new mapping functions. The innovation of this work is to develop land-cover-specific satellite remote sensing PWV calibration model by considering the type of land cover, by identifying the most accurate PWV mapping function.
