15214916.label: Realisation of objectives
15214916.value: A novel retrieval method has been developed for the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectro-radiometer (MODIS) onboard the Terra and Aqua satellites based on ensemble-based empirical regression analysis. This new approach provides an effective way to retrieve water vapor without pre-obtained atmospheric information. Water vapor data observed during 2003 ~ 2017 from 464 GPS stations located in western North America and their spatial-temporal collocated MODIS level 1 reflectance data were employed as training data for model development. The training data were resampled into 10 subsets using the bootstrap method. The regression functions trained by these independent subsets reduced the uncertainty in the model training and minimized the sensitivity of possible channel drifting. Verifications in North America show that the root mean square error (RMSE) for water vapor calculated from MODIS/Terra reduces 48.12% to 2.362 mm when using two-channel ratio transmittance and 50.74% to 2.243 mm when using three-channel ratio transmittance. The RMSE for water vapor calculated from MODIS/Aqua reduces 42.54% to 2.562 mm and 42.99% to 2.541 mm when using two-channel and three-channel ratio transmittance, respectively. Validations over five additional stations also show that the overall RMSE for MODIS/Terra data reduces 22.80% to 5.946 mm when using two-channel ratio transmittance, and 21.69% to 6.006 mm when using three-channel ratio transmittance. For MODIS/Aqua data, the reductions are 16.42% to 6.010 mm when using two-channel ratio transmittance and 15.26% to 6.094 mm when using three-channel ratio transmittance. The retrieval algorithm has been validated in Australia and its neighbouring area for the first time. The observation results over the years of 2017 ~ 2019 have clearly shown that our new ensemble-based empirical regression model, which was developed using data from the North Hemisphere, is still valid in the South Hemisphere. For the data obtained from MODIS/Terra, the RMSE has reduced by 58.53% from 5.712 mm to 2.369 mm when using 2-channel ratio transmittance and has reduced by 56.14% to 2.505 mm using 3-channel ratio transmittance. For the data obtained from MODIS/Aqua, the RMSE has reduced by 49.17% from 5.170 mm to 2.628 mm using 2-channel ratio transmittance and has reduced by 46.60% to 2.761 mm using 3-channel ratio transmittance. The results further prove that the newly proposed retrieval model has very good property of having no temporal or spatial dependency over a large observation area. The model’s coefficients can be easily applied to areas of interest without pre-calculated input parameters of atmospheric profiles. It thus can be concluded that this algorithm provides an effective way to retrieve water vapor globally under cloud-free condition. On the other hand, regression functions trained for different land cover types adapted from MCD12Q1 IGBP legend are discussed. After land cover type classification, validations in North America show that for data calculated from MODIS/Terra, the overall RMSE has been reduced 50.78% to 2.229 mm for data using two-channel ratio transmittance and 53.06% to 2.126 mm for data using three-channel ratio transmittance. For data obtained from MODIS/Aqua, the overall RMSE has been reduced 45.54% to 2.423 mm when using two-channel ratio transmittance and 45.34% to 2.432 mm when using three-channel ratio transmittance. The validation also show that new algorithm has improved accuracy for all types of land surface. For MODIS/Terra data, the RMSE is between 1.971 mm and 3.295 mm using two- channel ratio transmittance, and is between 1.935 mm and 3.748 mm using three-channel ratio transmittance. For MODIS/Aqua data, the RMSE is between 2.197 mm and 3.485 mm using two-channel ratio transmittance, and is between 2.243 mm and 4.021 mm using three-channel ratio transmittance. The retrieval over shrubland has the best accuracy among all surface types using the new algorithm. For MODIS/Terra data, the RMSE has been reduced to 1.971 mm and 1.935 mm using two-channel and three-channel ratio transmittance method, respectively. For MODIS/Aqua, the RMSE has been reduced to 2.197 mm and 2.243 mm using two-channel and three-channel ratio transmittance method, respectively. The retrieval over barren has the largest RMSE reduction rate for both MODIS/Terra and MODIS/Aqua satellites. For MODIS/Terra data, the RMSE has been reduced by 64.13% (from 5.843 mm to 2.096 mm) and 63.37% (from 5.843 mm to 2.140 mm) using two-channel and three-channel ratio transmittance, respectively. For MODIS/Aqua data, the RMSE has been reduced by 61.55% (from 5.904 mm to 2.270 mm) and 59.55% (from 5.904 mm to 2.388 mm) using two-channel and three-channel ratio transmittance, respectively. It is also worth mentioning that the performance of water vapor retrieval over water bodies remain problematic. Only limited RMSE reduction is observed using the two-channel ratio transmittance method. When using the three-channel ratio method, the RMSE values are even getting larger. This is probably because the water bodies sometimes act as black surfaces that affect the signal of absorption channels. The empirical regression method is also implemented for water vapor observation from Medium Resolution Spectral Imager (MERSI) onboard the Chinese Fengyun 3B satellite’s NIR channels. The collocated MERSI L1b reflectance data in the NIR channels are used for water vapor retrieval. Precipitable water vapor (PWV) data observed from 256 ground-based GPS stations located in the western North America in 2016 are used as reference data for model development. Then, validation is performed with data obtained during 2017 ~ 2019 from both the western North America and Australia to assess the performance of the proposed algorithm. The results indicate that the new PWV results agree very well with ground based PWV reference data. The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for ensemble median PWV is 16.72% ~ 36.74% in western North America and is 15.47% ~ 32.31% in Australia. The RMSE is 4.635 mm ~ 8.156 mm in western North America and is 5.383 mm ~ 8.900 mm in Australia. The weighted mean value using three-channel ratio transmittance has the best retrieval accuracy, with RMSE of 4.635 mm in western North America and 5.383 mm in Australia. With this method, more accurate water vapor data from MERSI instruments onboard Chinese FY satellite series can be obtained, which will contribute to global weather, climate and environmental research.

15214916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214916.value: The new ensemble-based regression model developed under this project provides an efficient way to estimate total column water vapor from MODIS NIR channels with high precision. A comprehensive validation against the GPS reference water vapour dataset reveals that the overall accuracy of the calibrated water vapour records has been greatly improved compared to the operational product. The weighted mean water vapour data has reduced the RMSE by 42.54% ~ 58.53% when compared to the operational products from MODIS. The coefficients obtained can be easily applied to areas of interest without pre-calculated input parameters of atmospheric profiles. It can be concluded that this algorithm provides an effective way to retrieve water vapour globally under cloud-free condition. The water vapor retrieval algorithm is very robust spatially, temporally, and under different land surface types. This model built using data from North American (North Hemisphere) can be directly applied to the data observed in Australian (South Hemisphere) in different years and still significantly improve the accuracy of satellites’ water vapor products. This shows that the method is robust in space and in time. It is independent of the space and time of the satellite water vapor data. Our test also shows that the method is very robust with the land surface types. Under different land surface types, the method can improve the accuracy of satellite water vapor data almost at the same level of effectiveness. The regression method can be applied to process satellite data to retrieve water vapor directly. We applied our method to the Chinese FY-3B satellite data and successfully retrieve water vapor data from FY-3B satellite, though no water vapor data from FY-3B are publicly available on the internet. Validation of FY-3B water vapor data shows that the mean absolute percentage error for ensemble median PWV is 16.72% ~ 36.74% in western North America and is 15.47% ~ 32.31% in Australia. The RMSE is 4.635 mm ~ 8.156 mm in western North America and is 5.383 mm ~ 8.900 mm in Australia. The weighted mean value using three-channel ratio transmittance has the best retrieval accuracy, with RMSE of 4.635 mm in western North America and 5.383 mm in Australia.

15214916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214916.value: The GPS stations over the globe should be included in the training and testing procedures. Especially for stations over the extreme wet areas (e.g., the Amazon Rain Forest, the Philippines) and extreme dry area (e.g., central Australia, the southwest Africa) should be discussed in detail. Observations from more diversed surface types should be included in the model development to further increase the robustness of the model. Ancillary data, such as atmospheric temperature, elevations, and aerosol concentrations, should be used to restrain the training dataset to ensure a meteorologically meaningful result. Other approaches in the procedure of developing the radiative transfer equations can also be discussed, such as the neural network analysis, the advanced radiative transfer model. It may further improve the retrieval accuracy.

15214916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214916.value: Water vapor is the most abundant greenhouse gas. The water vapor plays a very important role in weather, climate, and environmental research. There are many different tools and techniques to observe water vapor, among which satellites are the most efficient tool because of their large geographical coverage and reasonably good temporal resolution. However, the water vapor observations from satellites have a relatively low accuracy compared to other techniques. This project develops a new algorithm to process the satellite data, which can improve the accuracy of satellite water vapor data by up to 50%. We have tested this method with multiple years of data in both North Hemisphere (North America in our study) and South Hemisphere (Australia in our study). It shows that this method is very robust in both time and space domain. The model developed in the North Hemisphere can be directly applied in the South Hemisphere and the results are still very accurate. The development of this method will help us to make more accurate observation of atmospheric water vapor at a regional or even global scale, the most abundant greenhouse gas and one of the most important elements in weather forecasting and climate studies.

15215116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215116.value: The researches on the liquid droplet breakup after impinged by a shock wave have been continued over 60 years in the aerospace and nuclear engineering communities, due to their importance in the industry applications, such as better ablation management of space vehicles caused by rain droplet impingement during an atmosphere reentry, higher efficiency for combustion in multiphase mixtures, more complete damage evaluation and evacuation plan if a nuclear plant explodes, etc. Due to numerous emerging applications, such as the national security measures for the terrorist attack of an airborne bio/chemical weapon explosion, it receives significant attention again in recent years. Despite numerous findings from the earlier theoretical and experimental researches, the detailed breakup mechanisms and flow features are still not fully understood. Theoretical analyses can only describe the onsets and growths of the initial instabilities. Experimental approaches are limited by insufficient spatial/temporal resolutions of the conventional shadowgraphy and the high cost of the advanced high-speed laser induced fluorescence technique. Therefore, computer simulations provide the ideal means to depict the rich flow patterns and the associated flow physics. This project has three objectives--(1) develop a reliable numerical platform for compressible multi-fluid simulations and a budget shadowgraph system in the shock tube for experiments, (2) determine various flow regimes and associated timings in deformation and breakup of a liquid droplet, after being impacted by a shock wave, and (3) investigate thoroughly the corresponding physics of deformation, interfacial instability and breakup in different flow regimes. Our in-house inviscid characteristic space-time conservation element and solution element (CE/SE) method will be further extended to include the sharp interface treatment method (LevelSet) and surface tention and viscosity effects for the study of this multiphase problem. The present inviscid CE/SE code shows good performance in capturing shock waves and contact discontinuities. By coupling with the five-equation multi-fluid model, the current CE/SE code has successfully simulated a few compressible multi-fluid problems. Simultaneously, a newly-built shock tube with a budget shadowgraph visualization system will be used to validate the numerical simulations. The experiments and simulations will be mutually validated by using a novel numerical visualization technique which is developed according to the fundamental principle of the shadowgraphy. Extensive computer simulations will be conducted to understand the underlying physics, thereafter. It is envisaged that the knowledge gained from this project will help to complement the earlier research results and to further understand the fundamental physics embedded in this problem. 在航空航太和核能工程領域，研究者們針對液態微滴受激波衝擊後破碎現象的研究已經持續開展了60多年。俱因這一現象廣泛存于工程應用中，典型如為航太器重返大氣層時抵禦雨滴碰撞侵蝕提供更優的防護；提升多相混合類發動機的燃燒效率；更完善的核武器爆炸風險評估及疏散策略等。随着一些新興應用的興起，此項研究近年又引起了重要關注。例如針對使用經空氣傳播的生物/化學武器爆炸攻擊的恐怖襲擊，此項研究有助於規劃國家安全措施。儘管至今已在理論及實驗研究中有眾多進展，但完善的液滴破碎原理及流動特性仍未被完全解析。理論分析只能描述破碎初期液滴表面的介面不穩定性變化。而實驗方法則受制於陰影法等流場觀測方法的時間/空間局限性，並且先進的高速激光誘導螢光技術的成本過高。因此，數值模擬為分析液滴的破碎模式及複雜流動特性提供了最佳研究手段。此項研究有三個具體目標:（1）建立一個可信的可壓縮多介質流體分析數值模擬平臺；（2）確定受激波衝擊後液滴的多種破碎模式及液滴變形和破碎的時間規律；（3）全面分析在各種液滴破碎模式下的液滴變形現象、介面不穩定性及破碎原理。我們自主開發的時空守恆元/解元(CE/SE)數值模擬平臺未來會集成間斷介面處理方法(LevelSet)、表面張力以及粘性效應，繼續用於研究這一多相流問題。現有的無粘性CE/SE演算法在追蹤激波及接觸間斷面上顯示了良好的性能。 通過耦合五方程多介質模型，現有的CE/SE演算法已可以成功運算一些可壓縮多介質流體問題。同時， 一個新建成的激波管及附屬的紋影流場觀測系統將被用於實驗驗證數值模擬結果。通過使用一種新穎的基於陰影法基本原理建立的數值模擬流場觀測技術，實驗及數值模擬結論將被相互驗證。此後，大量的數值模擬將被用於深入探討激波後液滴破碎的物理機理。本項目預期成果有望有助於補充前人的研究成果, 並進一步理解這一現象的基礎物理機理。

15215116.label: Realisation of objectives
15215116.value: In this report, the liquid droplet breakup after impinged by a shock wave has been throughly studied with extensive experiments, numerical simulations and theoretical derivations. Our in-house inviscid characteristic space-time conservation element and solution element (CE/SE) method has been further refined for multi-fluid simulations by coupling the five-equation multi-fluid model and implementing the maximum-principle. The current CE/SE code has successfully simulated the compressible multi-fluid problems in this study (Shen et al., JCP, 2017, Jiang et al, AIAA, 2020). Extensive computer simulations were conducted to understand the underlying physics (Guan et al., AIAA, 2018). Simultaneously, a shock tube with a budget shadowgraph visualization system were used to visualise the flow fields of the liquid droplet breakup at different shock Mach numbers (Guan et al., AIAA, 2018 and Liang et al. JFM, 2020). These flow images were used to validate the numerical simulations. Two theories were also developed to explain the numerical and experimental findings (Guan et al., AIAA, 2018 and Liang et al. JFM, 2020). To achieve all the proposed objectives, the investigation was carried out by four steps: 1. A maximum-principle-satisfying space-time conservation element and solution element (CE/SE) scheme was constructed to solve a reduced five-equation model coupled with the stiffened equation of state for compressible multifluids. We first derive a sufficient condition for CE/SE schemes to satisfy maximum-principle when solving a general conservation law. And then we introduce a slope limiter to ensure the sufficient condition which is applicative for both central and upwind CE/SE schemes. Finally, we implement the upwind maximum-principle-satisfying CE/SE scheme to solve the volume-fraction-based five-equation model for compressible multifluids. Several numerical examples are carried out to carefully examine the accuracy, efficiency, conservativeness and maximum-principle-satisfying property of the proposed approach. 2. Shock tube experiments of different incident shock strengths (Shock Mach numbers) were conducted. The flow videos of the droplet breakup after shock impingement were recorded using the shadowgraph system. The maximum-principle-satisfying CE/SE algorithm were successfully validated with these experimental images. 3. The establishment of an internal flowfield inside a single water droplet subjected to shock-wave impact were numerically and theoretically investigated accordingly. The main focus is on the description of the droplet internal flow pattern, which is believed to be one of the dominant factors in initial droplet deformation. The droplet internal flow pattern held steady for quite a long time after the incident shock passage, and a saddle point was observed for the first time. Therefore, the saddle point inside the droplet flow was used as a characteristic point to describe the internal flow. A theoretical prediction was proposed to delineate the correlation between the saddle point steady position and the strength of the incident shock wave. The numerical cases were found to be in good agreement with the prediction. The present study helps to complete the understanding of the overall droplet aerobreakup phenomenon. The breakup of liquid droplets under different conditions (different Weber numbers, Mach numbers, and Reynolds numbers) were also investigated by direct numerical simulations. Through this project, a shock tube experimental system and a CE/SE code were developed, which can provide both the interface evolutions of the droplet under the shock impingement. The experimental and numerical investigation clearly showed the interface instability evolutions of the water drops under the shock impact. The underlying mechanism of the flow instability was further completed by the theoretical efforts. In summary, all the proposed objectives of this research project have been well achieved.

15215116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215116.value: 1. A second-order maximum-principle-satisfying CE/SE scheme was constructed by adopting a very simple limiter which can preserve the conservativeness and accuracy of the scheme. For linear problems, the standard CFL condition is sufficient. For non-linear problems, a more restrictive CFL condition is required. Extensive numerical examples show that the proposed scheme is very robust and accurate in computing compressible multifluid flows even for the cases with a large density ratio and very different thermodynamic properties. Our scheme simultaneously captures shocks and contact surfaces sharply without spurious oscillations, while strictly preserving the conservation law and the positivity of volume fractions. Due to the special time marching strategy associated with CE/SE schemes, high-order maximum-principle-satisfying CE/SE schemes are complex and need further research. 2. The internal flow pattern of a single water droplet under shock impact was investigated numerically and theoretically. Similar internal flow patterns were found in cases with different incident shock strengths, in which the SP (Saddle Point) forms and remains stationary soon after the passage of the incident shock. With the increase in the incident shock strength, the SP position varies, and the droplet presents different morphologies. A aerodynamic theory was proposed to predict the stationary position of SP in accordance with the incident shock Mach number. This correlation connects the shock strength with the droplet internal flowfield. It infers that the droplet internal flow pattern is input into the droplet at the initial impact stage by the shock rather than following the postshock airstream. 3. In the experiments, a vapour cavity formed inside the water droplet was accidentally found. The interaction of a shock wave and a water droplet embedded with a vapour cavity was experimentally investigated in a shock tube for the first time. The vapour cavity inside the droplet is generated by decreasing the surrounding pressure to the saturation pressure, and an equilibrium between the liquid phase and the gas phase is obtained inside the droplet. Direct high-speed photography was adopted to capture the evolution of both the droplet and the vapour cavity. The formation of a transverse jet inside the droplet during the cavity-collapse stage was clearly observed. Soon afterwards, at the downstream pole of the droplet, a water jet penetrating into the surrounding air was observed during the cavity-expansion stage. The evolution of the droplet is strongly influenced by the evolution of the vapour cavity. The phase change process plays an important role in vapour cavity evolution. The effects of the relative size and eccentricity of the cavity on the movement and deformation of the droplet are presented quantitatively.

15215116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215116.value: The developed CE/SE algorithm were further extended to study the Richtmyer–Meshkov instability, which is significant and controls a variety of processes in nature and technology in high- and low-energy-density regimes such as inertial confinement fusion (ICF) and astrophysical problems. As shown in the research output part, 6 more journal papers were published in the application of the developed CE/SE algorithm on the researches of Richtmyer–Meshkov instability.

15215116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215116.value: In this project, the instabilities of the liquid droplet breakup after impinged by a shock wave have been experimentally, numerically and theoretically investigated, due to their importance in the industry applications, such as better ablation management of space vehicles caused by rain droplet impingement during an atmosphere reentry, higher efficiency for combustion in multiphase mixtures, more complete damage evaluation and evacuation plan if a nuclear plant explodes, the national security measures for the terrorist attack of an airborne bio/chemical weapon explosion, etc. The research outcome was further applied to study the Richtmyer–Meshkov instability. Factors such as Weber numbers, Mach numbers, and Reynolds numbers were thoroughly examined to understand their corresponding impacts on the interfacial instability. Through this project, our knowledge of flow physics about the liquid droplet breakup after impinged by a shock wave was extended. This investigation also made it possible to apply the developed CE/SE code to the Richtmyer–Meshkov instability in the nuclear engineering and astrophysical problems.

15218016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218016.value: Our buildings are traditionally designed without seismic provisions. As Hong Kong is now recognized as a moderate seismic region, our government will enact a seismic-resistant building design standard in a few years’ time. As the key structural member, beam-column joints (“BCJ”) will have to be strengthened to ensure structural integrity and stability. Although many strengthening schemes were proposed, they are not suitable to Hong Kong. Recently, the principal investigator has developed a strengthening strategy by enlarging BCJ with chamfers. It offers a practical solution and is highly effective. Due to absence of an analytical tool to design a BCJ with chamfers, the strengthening strategy can only be verified experimental or through complicated analysis. To enable implementation of the strengthening strategy at ease, we need to develop an analytical tool. In the proposed investigation, strut-and-tie model is recommended. It is based on clear structural concept making it readily desirable for engineers. As current studies are aimed at protecting BCJ from failure, joint strength cannot be reached in the tests. It is not possible to extract joint strength from the existing test data. In recognizing the above-mentioned missing studies, a series of experiments will be conducted to evaluate joint strength of BCJ with chamfers. Using this new set of test data, strut-and-tie model will be developed. As demonstrated by the principal investigator, high axial load has a detrimental effect to BCJ and modification to strut-and-tie models is recommended. Following similar approach, high axial load will be taken into account in the proposed investigation. Lastly, parametric studies will be carried out on BCJ with different configurations of chamfers, varied geometries and different axial load ratios using strut-and-tie model. Joint strength will be estimated and compared with American, New Zealand and local design codes to recommend limiting values of joint strength. Significance of the proposed investigation is that this is the first time an analytical tool, namely strut-and-tie model, will be developed for BCJ with chamfers. Through the comprehensive studies on BCJ, the proposed investigation may assist in unifying the international practices on diversified joint strength. 我們的建築物在傳統設計上並沒有抗震要求。鑑於香港被識別為中震區，我們的政府將在幾年後制定抗震建築設計標準。作為結構的主要構件，樑柱節點 (“節點”) 將須要進行加固，以確保結構的整體性和穩定性。雖然現有很多加固的方案，他們都不適合香港。最近本項目的首席研究者，通過擴大節點的倒斜角區，制定了一個非常有效和實用的加固方案。由於缺乏分析工具來設計節點的倒斜角區，加固方案只可經實驗或複雜的結構分析證明。我們需要發展一個分析工具，適用於節點的倒斜角區。本項目建議發展撐-拉杆模型。它是基於清晰的結構概念，易為工程師取用。 當前研究旨在保護節點，測試的結果不能反影節點的抗剪強度。因此，現有的測試資料缺乏節點的抗剪強度資料。基於以上的不足，本項目將進行一系列的實驗來評價節點於倒斜角區加固後的抗剪強度。測試資料將用於確立撐-拉杆模型。按本項目首席研究者的研究結果，高軸向負荷是不利於節點，建議修改撐-拉杆模型。本項目會以類似的方法，考慮高軸向負荷的影響。最後，撐-拉杆模型將用於模擬不同大小的節點，不同形狀的倒斜角區和不同的軸向負荷。節點的抗剪強度會與美國、紐西蘭和本地設計規範的強度極限值比較。 值得關注的時，本項目將會是首次利用撐-拉杆模型為節點的倒斜角區進行分析。通過對節點的綜合研究，本項目可協助統一各國在節點抗剪強度的標準。

15218016.label: Realisation of objectives
15218016.value: This study was instigated by an earlier PhD work carried out by one of the PI’s by then research students. In this earlier PhD work, a strengthening strategy by enlarging beam-column joints (“BCJ”) with chamfers was proposed to increase the joint shear strength. In this study, load path and performance of BCJ with chamfers has been studied experimentally and analytically. Objective 1 is completed: As there is in lack of test data on joint shear strength of non-seismically designed BCJ with chamfers, experiments were carried out on interior and exterior BCJ with and without chamfers. Based on the experimental results, shear strengths of BCJ with chamfers were assessed. Objective 2 is completed: Non-linear finite element model was developed (“the Models”) and analyses were carried out to repeat the test results. Inelastic material behavior of concrete (under tension and compression) were tuned against the experimental results to optimize the accuracy attended by the Models. Based on the above, a compressive strut within chamfer region was identified for the strut-and-tie model. It can be found that peak horizontal force is enhanced only in the direction of chamfer in compression (positive direction). The diagonal compressive strut within joint and an additional strut in chamfer along the diagonal side can be clear found from the results. Benefit from the compressive strut within chamfer the width of diagonal compressive strut is enlarged, which contribute to improve joint shear capacity. Thus, the joint without joint shear reinforcements can be protect by restricting brittle failure under seismic. Objective 3 is completed: The Models were used in subsequent parametric studies to quantify the increase in shear strength against size of chambers, beam-to-column depth ratio, etc. Size of chamfer is identified as a critical factor influencing performance of joints. Joint shear strengths were estimated and compared with design codes: ASCE/SEI 41, ACI-ASCE 352R, NZS 3101, etc. By increasing size of chamfer, joint shear capacity can be effectively improved. Ratio of size of chamfer to minimum beam depth and column width is recommended as 0.67-1.00 considering construction in practice. I only encountered one difficulty while carrying out the study. I proposed to use WCOMD in the finite element analyses. At that time, WCOMD was HK$12,000 at educational price as per detailed in the proposal. After the proposal was successful and accepted, there was no educational price as WCOMD was sold/licensed to another company. The purchase price of WCOMD is HK100,000 and renewable each year at HK$12,000. I am very grateful to Nano and Advanced Materials Institute Limited and Architectural Services Department of HKSAR who kindly lent me one license of WCOMD for around 1 year. As it was not feasible to keep on borrowing WCOMD from others, I later changed the software to ABAQUS as our department has acquired ABAQUS’s license. N.B. Comparison of predictions by WCOMD, ABAQUS and experimental data has indicated that WCOMD and ABAQUS both able to provide reasonable predictions.

15218016.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218016.value: The main impact of the study is to understand the structural performance of beam-column joints (“BCJ”) with chamfers. In particular, it is the first time that load transfer mechanism of BCJ with chamfers has been clearly identified with a strut-and-tie model. (1) Joint shear strength is increased by installing unsymmetrical chamfers on the soffit of beam. (2) The above is effective only when chamfer is in compression thereby forming the strut of the strut-and-tie model. The diagonal compressive strut within joint and an additional strut in chamfer along with the diagonal side can be clear found in the numerical analysis results. Benefit from the compressive strut within chamfer the width of diagonal compressive strut is enlarged, which contribute to improve joint shear capacity. Thus, the joint without joint shear reinforcements can be protect by restricting brittle failure under seismic. (3) Size of chamfer is a critical factor influencing performance of BCJ. Ratio of size of chamfer to minimum beam depth and column width is recommended as 0.67-1.00. The above provides design principle and method to analyze and design a BCJ with unsymmetrical chamfer(s).

15218016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218016.value: In 2019, it was planned to further develop the strut-and-tie model through topology optimization. To this, we have established a research programme with Professor Xiaojia Zhang, Civil and Environmental Engineering Department, University of Illinois. Professor Zhang is specialized on topology optimization. The research programme comprises a 3-month academic attachment (from February to April 2020) by the PhD student Miss Xue Zhi-hang (with studentship funded by this study) to integrate topology optimization with strut-and-tie model for advanced analysis of beam-column joints with chamfers. Unfortunately, the academic attachment was postponed due to COVID. As of today, we will proceed with the above-mentioned academic attachment in spring 2021 or soonest. At present, we are preparing publication on the impact of the study to design and proposing modification to the seismic design code like ACI 352, NZS3101 and Eurocode 8.

15218016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218016.value: In this study, a strengthen strategy for beam-column joints (“BCJs”) is developed. It incorporates installation of unsymmetrical chamfers at the soffit of beams to protect a BCJ from failure. The strengthening strategy has been verified experimentally and mathematically on interior and exterior BCJs designed to local code. Strengths of BCJs with chamfers obtained from the experiments are compared with the seismic design codes worldwide. It has been shown that the seismic design code may not be applicable to estimate the performance of BCJs with chamfers. Through a series of mathematical models, load transfer mechanism is identified showing an additional compression strut within each chamfer. As a result, joint shear capacity is increased thereby suppressing the brittle failure of a BCJ under seismic action. Further, size of chamfer is a critical factor influencing the performance of BCJ and ratio of size of chamfer to minimum beam depth and column width is recommended to be 0.67-1.00.

15219616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219616.value: In recent years, crowdsourced transportation platforms (e.g., Uber, Lyft) have been gaining popularity in the public. By leveraging on a crowd of drivers, they can provide customers with on-demand trip services in a timely manner. To reduce the waiting times of customers, existing platforms adopt simple heuristics to assign trip requests to drivers (e.g., assign each trip request to the nearest available driver). After completing a trip, the customer is charged a fare based on the travel distance and the travel time. Nevertheless, two important issues remain unsolved in those platforms: (i) lack of means for drivers to express their preferences and costs, (ii) fare disputes with customers. First, existing platforms require drivers to specify their availability and expect available drivers to accept assigned requests. This restricts the flexibility of drivers and may discourage new drivers from joining those platforms. It is meaningful to consider the preferences (e.g., familiarities with different districts) and costs (e.g., fuel cost on traveling back) of drivers before assigning requests to them. Second, existing platforms do not provide accurate estimate of the fare when a trip begins. Without any comparison of routes, it is hard for a customer to check whether the driver will travel on a route with reasonable fare and travel time. This project aims to study efficient techniques for managing spatial data in crowdsourced transportation (e.g., map, locations, spatial preferences). Specifically, our objectives are to: (1) develop trip request assignment techniques that consider drivers’ preferences and costs, (2) develop representative route recommendation techniques to prevent fare disputes in advance, and (3) build an open-source testbed system for simulation and performance evaluation. Our first two objectives will improve the satisfaction of drivers and customers, as well as attract them to the platform. Our third objective enables the industry to experiment with different techniques on our testbed before deployment. In our performance evaluation, we will measure the response time of our proposed methods, the number of trips completed, the average earning of drivers, and the average waiting time of customers. Our track record in spatial databases and route planning is essential to the success of this project. Our project will bring advancement to crowdsourced transportation platforms, improving the satisfaction of customers and the earning of drivers. Furthermore, since crowdsourced transportation platforms are growing in the industry, we believe that this project is both important and timely for metropolitan cities like Hong Kong. 近年來，眾包交通平台（例如，Uber，Lyft）日益普及。他們通過司機群為客戶提供及時的行程服務。現有平台採用簡單的啟發式算法分配行程請求給司機。在完成行程後，顧客被收取基於行駛距離和時間的車費。 儘管如此，這些平台上仍然沒有解決兩個重要問題：（一）缺乏方法讓司機表達自己的喜好和費用，（二）避免與客戶有車費糾紛。首先，現有平台要求司機接受已分配的請求。這限制了司機的靈活性，並且阻礙新的司機加入平台。第二，現有的平台不提供準確的票價估計。 該項目旨在研究有效的技術為眾包交通管理空間數據（例如，地圖，位置，空間喜好）。我們的目標是：（1）開發考慮司機偏好和成本的行程分配技術，（2）開發推薦具代表路線的技術，以提前防止車費糾紛，以及（3）建立一個開源的測試平台評估性能。前兩個目標將提高司機和客戶的滿意度，吸引他們到平台。第三個目標讓行業測試不同的技術。在性能評估中，我們將評估我們的方法的響應時間，出行次數，司機的平均收入，客戶的平均等待時間。我們在空間數據庫和路徑規劃的往績對這個項目至關重要。我們的項目會改良眾包交通平台，提高客戶的滿意度和司機的收入。此外，這個項目對於大城市(如香港)是重要和及時。

15225416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15225416.value: Topology optimization is the highest level design phase of a product. It may create a novel topology, which could not be imagined beforehand, of a product in early conceptual and preliminary design phases. Realizing the topology optimization of an electromagnetic device is thus the ultimate goal in electrical engineering. Nowadays, topology optimization has become the paradigm of the predominant engineering techniques to provide a quantitative design method for modern engineering design. In fact, it has been the most active research area in structural and multidisciplinary optimizations in the past two decades The investigators have proposed to develop a numerical methodology for topology optimizations of electromagnetic devices using a cellular division method and evolutionary algorithm. It has focused on: (1) the formulation and modeling methodology of multi-material topology optimization of electromagnetic devices; (2) an evolutionary algorithm for efficient solution of many-objective topology optimizations; (3) an adaptive surrogate based on adaptive moving least squares approximation for performance prediction, and finally (4) the topology optimization of an electric motor.

15226116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15226116.value: Birds of a feather flock together, and a similar phenomenon is observed in graphs. Vertices in a graph usually represent entities in a network, and edges model the relationship between these entities. Roughly speaking, a module of a graph is a set of vertices that cannot be distinguished from outside---all of them share the same relationship with a vertex out of this set. A comprehensive theory on the combinatorial properties of modules has been established, which states that every graph has a unique modular decomposition tree and it can be computed in linear time. For many combinatorial and algorithmic problems, a module can be treated as a whole. For example, an important problem of bioinformatics is to detect small patterns, called graphlets, from a huge biological network, or count the numbers of them. Since the graphlets are tiny, usually having few vertices, they can be found and counted by trivial polynomial-time algorithms. However, due to the size of biological networks, only linear-time algorithms can claim practical. Modular decomposition can be easily applied to this type of problems. For this line of research, we aim for practical implementations that can be applied to real networks. The second type of problems we will consider are those probably having no polynomial-time algorithms. In particular, we are concerned with the problems asking for the minimum number of operations applied to a graph to make it have some specific properties. One widely applied approach to these problems is preprocessing, and the problem is how small can we shrink a given instance. Modular decomposition seems to be a very natural technique for this kind of problems, and several promising results have been reported in literature. However, in the known results, only a very special type of modules (known as "true twins") was used, while the full power of modular decomposition is left unexplored. Another approach to these hard problems is approximation. It is surprising that very few approximation algorithms based on modular decomposition are known in literature. We will design for these problems efficient approximation algorithms. Toward this end, we would need to study the dynamic maintenance of modular decomposition, i.e., to reconstruct the modular decomposition tree after deleting a vertex or an edge. Our proposed algorithms will be using the simple divide-and-conquer approach along with the modular decomposition tree, and thus there would not be huge constants hidden by the big-Oh in their running time. 物以類聚，在圖結構中也有類似的現象。一般來講，圖中的頂點表示網絡中的實體，而邊表示這些實體之間的關係。簡單說來，一個模塊中的頂點從這個模塊外部看來是完全相同的——它們跟這個模塊之外所有頂點有相同的關係。關於模塊的組合屬性已經有了豐富的研究，譬如我們知道每個圖都有唯一的模塊分解樹，並且我們可以在線性時間找到這棵樹。 對許多關於圖的組合和演算問題來說，一個模塊可以簡單的當作一個整體來對待。例如，生物信息學中的一個重要問題就是從一個很大的生物網絡中檢測或點數某些特別的圖樣。因為這些通常只有極少的點組成目標圖樣非常非常小，它們當然可以在多項式時間找到。但考慮到生物網絡本身的龐大，只有線性時間的演算法才有可能是有實用價值。模塊分解技術正好可以在這裡發揮作用。我們在這方面的研究注重可以應用到實際網絡中的可實現結果。 我們要考慮的第二類的問題則可能沒有多項式時間的演算法。我們特別關心的是，如何通過最小數量的修改使得一個圖滿足某種特殊的屬性。對此我們通常會對輸入圖進行預處理，而這個預處理步驟的關鍵就是我們能多大程度的壓縮輸入圖。這時人們會很自然的考慮到模塊分解技術，並且得到了一些很好的結果。然而，我們觀察到這些已有結果都只用到了一種非常特殊的模塊（又叫做孿生頂點），而一般的模塊在這方面的應用還有待發掘。 另一種解決這些難解問題的思路是近似演算法。令人驚訝的是，幾乎沒有任何已知的近似演算法用到了模塊分解技術。我們計劃為這些問題設計有效的近似算法。為此我們將研究動態模塊分解技術，也就是說，在圖中刪除一個點或一條邊後如何有效的重建模塊分解樹。 我們計劃中的演算法將在模塊分解樹上運用“分而治之”技術，這是一種簡單有效的方法，因此我們演算法的運行時間中不會有很大的常數隱藏在O-符號之後。

15226116.label: Realisation of objectives
15226116.value: The purpose of this project is to better understand modular composition in graphs, and find novel applications of it in graph algorithms. A subset M of vertices of a graph is a module if each vertex in M has the same neighborhood outside M; e.g., the whole vertex set, singlet sets, and connected components. A special kind of modules is a pair of vertices with the same neighborhood, called twins. A graph is prime if all its modules are trivial, consisting only one or all the vertices. For many graph problems, we can shrink a module into a single vertex and then work on the resulting graph as well as the subgraph induced by the module. Thus, for many problems, it suffices to deal with prime graphs. The earliest and probably most widely-known applications of modular decomposition is in the recognition of various graph classes, including comparability graphs, interval graphs, cographs, and permutation graphs. We try to find more use of modular decomposition in other algorithmic paradigms. When we proposed this project, one compelling issue in this area was on the relationship between interval graphs and modular decomposition. A graph is an interval graph if its vertices can be assigned to intervals on the real line such that there is an edge between two vertices if and only if their corresponding intervals intersect. An interval graph on n vertices has at most n maximal cliques, and these cliques can be arranged in a linear manner, called a clique path, such that every vertex is contained in a consecutive set of them. It is very easy to draw a graph out of a set of intervals, and the interval representation is ostensibly simple. However, the other direction, reconstructing an interval representation from a given interval graph, is a challenging task. It is actually very nontrivial to decide whether a given graph is an interval graph, called the recognition problem. There had been more than ten algorithms proposed for this purpose, and several of these algorithm suffered from mistakes, some later fixed but some never. Almost all these algorithms use a recognition algorithm for chordal graphs to find the maximal cliques. Since the structures of interval graphs are simpler than those of chordal graphs, one may consider the indirect approaches counterintuitive in a sense. Efforts toward *direct* recognition of interval graphs were made by Corneil et al. [1998, 2009] and Li and Wu [2014]. Their algorithms are direct but more complicated than earlier ones. Attempts of using modular decomposition in recognizing interval graphs were made by Hsu and Ma [1999], based on the observation of Hsu [1995] that a prime interval graph has a unique clique path, up to full reversal. We managed to get a slightly stronger and, more importantly, constructive version of this characterization. Several classic results on interval graph can be easily derived from our characterization. In particular, we revisited the recognition of interval graphs, whose basic idea is as follows. We conduct an BFS-like graph search algorithm, called LBFS, which scan the graph from one end to the other; the critical point is to detect fake modules (a set of vertices cannot be distinguished by the graph search but not really a module of the graph). This aligns the recognition of interval graphs with the recognition of unit interval graphs, where we are concerned with fake twins, and very easy to understand. In a unit interval graph, each interval has the same length, hence easy to deal with. The characterization of modular decomposition of interval graphs also enabled us to solve the problem of enumerating maximal induced interval subgraphs. In general we use the solution map approach, and the key point is to show the that the solution map we constructed is strongly connected. For a given solution S, we fix a clique path of S, and try to add the vertices of S one by one in the order of their positions in the clique path. However, with the existence of modules, the clique paths are not unique. A deep study of these structures and algorithmic finesse enable us to deliver the desired property and develop the first polynomial-delay algorithm for this problem. We also obtained enumeration algorithms for several subclasses of interval graphs, including unit interval graphs and trivially perfect graphs. Graph searches, the processes of visiting vertices in a graph in a specific order, are used in many important algorithms. LBFS, the workhorse of our recognition algorithms also plays a pivotal role in the state-of-the-art algorithm for computing modular decomposition. Toward a simpler algorithm for modular decomposition, we conducted a systematic study of graph search algorithms. Our study was not limited to LBFS. Corneil et al. [2008] observed that the end vertex problem is the starting point of understanding them. (Properties of the end vertex of LBFS are the most important part of our recognition algorithm for interval graphs.) We obtained a sequence of results on the end vertex problems, and almost fully demarcated their complexity border. Another motivation of this project was to explore the use of modules in designing algorithms. As far as we checked, there were no such results in approximation algorithms. The cluster vertex deletion problem asks for deleting a minimum set of vertices to make a graph into a cluster graph, where every component is complete. We show that after dealing with several small subgraphs, we can shrink each class of true twins into a single vertex (with certain weight). We have thus reduced the problem to the same problem on triangle-free graphs, which is the well studied dissociation problem, and admits 2-approximation. The approximation ratio of the whole algorithm is thus decided by how to deal with the small subgraphs. We also show hardness of approximation. The minimum fill-in problem arises from the application of Gauss elimination to a sparse matrix, and is equivalent to the chordal completion problem. We presented a reduction to show that the problem does not admit polynomial-time approximation schemes, unless P = NP. The key of the reduction is to introduce a clique for each vertex, and most of the clique needs to be made true twins by an optimal solution. Other hardness results include the NP-completeness of the vertex deletion problem from an interval graph to a unit interval graph. We also used modules in developing parameterized and kernelization algorithms (preprocessing with rigorous analyses), which are a theoretical formalization of efficient preprocessing for (NP-)hard problems. The key observation is that for many graph modification problems, there are different modules that are preserved by all or some optimal solutions. We produced algorithms for all the modification problems to unit interval graphs. Moreover, we conducted a systematic study of the kernelization of H-free edge modification problems (whether we can edit at most k edges to make a graph contain no induced copy of H) for various H. In particular, we developed the first polynomial kernel for the diamond-free edge modification problems and the first polynomial kernel for the paw-free edge modification problems. We also made significant progress to the major open problem in this area, namely, the claw-free edge modification problem: We developed the first polynomial kernel for the line graph completion problem.

15226116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15226116.value: The first major finding is a simple observation on modular decomposition of interval graphs, which was then used to develop several algorithms for different problems on interval graphs. First, we developed a unified presentation of recognition of unit interval graphs and interval graphs based on their relations to modules (SOSA 2021). Second, we presented the first polynomial-delay algorithms for enumerating maximal induced interval subgraphs, and the first incremental-polynomial-time algorithms for enumerating maximal induced unit interval subgraphs, and a sequence of enumeration algorithms for related problems (arXiv:2004.09885). Third, we developed a linear-time parameterized algorithms for graph modification problems to unit interval graphs, and a constant-approximation algorithm for the vertex deletion problem. Fourth, we proved the NP-completeness of the vertex deletion problem from chordal graphs to interval graphs, together with polynomial-time algorithms of some other modification problems toward interval graphs (TCS 2018). Finally, we presented a characterization for a subclass of interval graphs, namely the paired threshold graphs, and used the characterization to develop the first linear-time recognition algorithm for this subclass (WG'20). We obtained both approximation algorithms and hardness for approximation. We produced the first nontrivial approximation algorithm for cluster vertex deletion. We gave the first proof that minimum fill-in cannot have a polynomial-time approximation scheme, unless P = NP, and we also presented stronger approximation lower bounds based on well-accepted complexity assumptions (I&C 2020). For edge modification problems, we observed that there are different modules that are preserved by all or some optimal solutions. We developed the first polynomial kernels for the diamond-free edge modification problems (ESA'18), the paw-free edge modification problems (TAMC'20), and the line graph completion problem (under submission). We obtained a sequence of new results on the end vertex problem of graph searches. We presented simple characterizations for MCS on chordal graphs and for BFS on interval graphs, and derived from these characterizations polynomial-time algorithms for the end vertex problem for them. We also gave a linear-time algorithm for the end vertex problem of LDFS on chordal graphs. On the negative side, we show that the end vertex problem of MCS is NP-complete on weakly chordal graphs (ISAAC'19). Moreover, we show that the end vertex problem of LDFS and of MCS are NP-complete on bipartite graphs (under review). A CCF summer school based on the outcome of this project was held in Summer 2020.

15226116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15226116.value: The most important course of action we propose is to find further applications of the relationship between modular decomposition and interval graphs, and to generalize it to related graph classes. First, it should be useful for most optimization problems on interval graphs. It should also help us find better algorithms, bother parameterized and approximation, for the interval completion problem, another important problem originating from sparse matrix computation. Since the minimum fill-in problem is also module-preserving, the use of modular decomposition in its algorithms is also a very promising direction to pursue. There is significant progress in the kernelization complexity of H-free edge modification problems. It is believed that only a few of them admit polynomial kernels. We believe modular decomposition should be very useful for designing such algorithms. After that, we will try to generalize from a single forbidden induced graph H to a set of forbidden induced graphs. The use of modular decomposition in approximation algorithms and in the proofs of hardness should also be further studied. Our study has been exclusively focused on graphs. Modules are very natural in many combinatorial structures, and thus similar study is also worth pursuing.

15226116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15226116.value: As the old saying goes, "birds of a feather flock together." A similar phenomenon is observed in graphs, where vertices represent entities in a network, and edges the relationship among these entities. Roughly speaking, a module of a graph is a set of vertices that cannot be distinguished from outside---all of them share the same relationship with a vertex out of this set. A comprehensive theory on the combinatorial properties of modules has been established, which states that every graph has a unique decomposition with respect to modules. The indistinguishability suggests that vertices in a module can be dealt with as a batch instead of individually. How to carry out this plan is the main task of this project. The most important graph class studied in this project is interval graphs, which are most suitable for events and objects in chronological order, as well as DNA data, both having a linear structure. These results were obtained through collaboration with more than ten researchers from four countries, including two undergraduate students. This project supported four postdocs/RAs, who are now faculty members in universities in India, and research scientists in Alibaba and Huawei. A book summarizing the research output of this project is under preparation.

15227916.label: Project Objectives
15227916.value: Propose and realize new approaches to dissect mobile traffic and classify it according to apps. We will design new signatures and employ app analysis methods to extract these signatures from apps. Then, we will leverage control-plane protocols to group mobile traffic to users and segment the traffic according to user activities. Finally, we leverage the signatures to classify traffic in each to apps. These new algorithms and mechanisms will be realized in a system named TAScope. Propose and implement new algorithms to profile mobile traffic and detect mobile malware. We will propose new algorithms to profile mobile traffic and to detect mobile malware by capturing traffic anomalies. We will realize the new algorithms and mechanisms in a system named TADetective. Propose new mechanisms and construct new systems to tackle selected emerging challenges in app analysis. We will propose new methods to automatically recover the executable file from a packed app so that static analysis tools can still examine the executable file. Then, we will design new approaches to facilitate static analysis on dynamically-generated UI. The discovered relationships among UI components of an app can be used to design execution paths for driving this app. Finally, we will develop a new information flow tracking system, which can run in real smartphone, for the new Android runtime

15227916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15227916.value: App经济的繁荣和智能手机的普及使之成为攻击者理想的盈利目标。例如，G Data公司在2015的首6个月手机了1,000,938的安卓恶意App。移动恶意App常进行各种恶意行为，包括泄露用户隐私信息，导致用户被无故收费，浪费网络资源等。 现有的检测移动恶意App的方法主要是基于主机的，通过静态和动态分析来发现恶意App。但使用高级特性的恶意App容易逃避这些检测，例如使用App加壳，动态类加载等。同时，这些基于主机的检测系统无法利用用户的行为和上下文信息来发现移动恶意App。 基于网络的检测系统可以解决这些问题并和基于主机的系统形成很好的互补。原因是不论移动恶意App如何隐藏，它们都将在进行恶意行为时留下网络痕迹。设计一个有效的基于网络的检测系统需要解决两个主要问题，包括如何从网络流量中推测出对应的App和如何从少量的移动流量中发现恶意App。当前对基于网络的检测系统的研究还很少。 在本项目中，我们将提出一种新颖的基于网络的检测恶意App的方法来解决上述两个问题。首先，我们将设计新的特征集并用它们来对流量进行分类。其次，我们将利用流量异常来检测恶意App。最后，我们将解决当前App分析中的几个主要问题，包括App加壳，动态UI，新运行时的信息流追踪。我们将研发并分享实用的系统来推动这个方向的研究。 这个项目深入研究恶意App，将获得对它们的行为，移动流量的特征，和App分析的深入理解。我们将研发新颖的基于网络的恶意App检测系统，构建移动流量分类的特征库，并收集恶意App。

15227916.label: Realisation of objectives
15227916.value: We have realized the three objectives. 1. Propose and realize new approaches to dissect mobile traffic and classify it according to apps. We designed intra-flow and inter-flow features to correlate the network traffic with the apps. We enhanced our static analysis tool for apps to extract flow-level static signatures and developed tools to collect flow-level static signatures and inter-flow features through parsing the captured network traffic. We further characterized fine-grained user actions using the corresponding entry point(EP) methods. To identify EP methods associated with a network flow, we model the spatial-temporal contextual dependency of in-flow bursts within it and infer the EP method associated with each of them based on the conditional random field. We conducted experiments in the open-world setting, which is a more realistic but challenging scenarios. The corresponding paper entitled “FOAP: Fine-Grained Open-World Android App Fingerprinting” was submitted to USENIX Security’21 and received the decision of Major Revision, and it is currently under the second review. To detect mobile malware according to traffic features, we designed a novel neural network named Extended Byte Segment Neural Network (EBSNN). EBSNN first divides a packet into header segments and payload segments, which are then fed into encoders composed of the recurrent neural networks with the attention mechanism. Based on the outputs, another encoder learns the high-level representation of the whole packet. The corresponding paper entitled “EBSNN: Extended Byte Segment Neural Network for Network Traffic Classification” was submitted to IEEE TDSC and received the decision of Minor Revision. We are revising the paper and will re-submit it soon. We observe that when deploying the traffic-based detection methods in real-life networks they may face some new challenges due to unseen traffic. To address it, we propose a novel context-aware traffic fingerprinting method that leverages per-flow traffic analysis and consider the spatial-temporal correlation of multiple neighboring flows. The corresponding paper entitled “Context-aware Website Fingerprinting over Encrypted Proxies” appeared in INFOCOM’21. By analyzing the real mobile traffic collected from a major mobile network provider in mainland China, we leveraged unique identifiers in control-plane protocols to group traffic and developed algorithms to extract features from the traffic. Such data-driven approach empowers us to discover a new vulnerability. Based on this observation, we have prepared a paper entitled “Finding a Needle in a Haystack: Data-Driven Detection and Mitigation of DoS Vulnerabilities in Cellular Data Networks” and will submit it later. We inspected the network traffic of proximity-based mobile apps and find that many such apps are vulnerable to large-scale location spoofing attack(LLSA). We evaluated its impact on proximity-based mobile apps and suggested countermeasures to defend against such attacks. The corresponding paper entitled “Exploiting Proximity-Based Mobile Apps for Large-Scale Location Privacy Probing” appeared in Security and Communication Networks(SCN). When conducting app analysis, we find that existing apps mainly follow the “one-size-fits-all” strategy which can result in software bloat and many serious issues. To solve it, we proposed a novel feature-oriented debloating approach to automate this process in a flexible manner. The corresponding paper entitled “XDebloat: Towards Automated Feature-Oriented App Debloating” was submitted to IEEE TSE and received the decision of Major Revision. We are revising the paper and will re-submit it soon. We supervised an undergraduate student to finish his capstone project entitled "Network-based Mobile Applications Recognition” in 2017/2018. We guided him to design machine learning approaches for recognizing mobile apps according to their network features. We also supervised a MSc student to finish his dissertation entitled “Assessing the Security of URL Protection Mechanisms in Apps” in 2017 by guiding him to design algorithms and develop tools for triggering the network communications of apps and analyze the corresponding network traffic for security assessment. 2. Propose and implement new algorithms to profile mobile traffic and detect mobile malware. We investigated how to quantify the similarity between the traffic patterns of known legitimate/malicious apps and a piece of newly-collected traffic. Besides using clustering algorithms on a set of features, we explored organizing the features into graphs and calculating the graph similarity. Moreover, we propose new approaches to speed up graph alignment, and published the corresponding paper, entitled “DeepMatching: A Structural Seed Identification Framework for Social Network Alignment”, in ICDCS’18. Based on network traffic from/to mobile apps, we present a new paradigm, programmable in-network security(Poise) based on programmable switches. Users of Poise specify concise policies, and Poise compiles them into different configurations of the primitive in P4. Poise can detect mobile malware and other attacks launched by compromised mobile devices. The corresponding paper entitled “Programmable In-Network Security for Context-aware BYOD Policies” appeared in USENIX Security’20. We inspected themed Android malware and inspected them from several aspects, including analyzing the network traffic from/to such malware samples. The corresponding paper entitled “Beyond the virus: a first look at coronavirus-themed Android malware” appeared in Empirical Software Engineering(EMSE). Adversarial examples can render the machine learning based Android malware detection systems useless. We proposed a novel robust Android malware detection approach that can resist adversarial examples without requiring their instances or knowledge by jointly investigating malware detection and adversarial example defenses. The corresponding paper entitled “Robust Android Malware Detection against Adversarial Example Attacks” appeared in WWW’21. We supervised three undergraduate students to work on the capstone project entitled "Network Traffic Based Mobile Malware Detection”. We guided them to develop algorithms to identify the patterns from the traffic of malicious apps and then detect similar mobile malware. 3. Propose new mechanisms and construct new systems to tackle selected emerging challenges in app analysis. We proposed novel methods to automatically recover the Dex file from a packed app so that static analysis tools can scrutinize the Dex file. The corresponding paper entitled “Adaptive Unpacking of Android Apps” appeared in ICSE’17. We proposed new mechanisms to approach several emerging challenges in app analysis. For static app analysis, we have improved our static analysis tool from several aspects. For example, we designed new methods to improve UI analysis, developed new methods to remove infeasible code and integrated our static analysis tool with the Android framework to avoid missing paths, and proposed new data structures for characterizing apps to quickly classify mobile malware. These new techniques resulted in five papers, including “Localizing Function Errors in Mobile Apps with User Reviews” in DSN’18, “Enhancing the Description-to-Behavior Fidelity in Android Apps with Privacy Policy” in IEEE TSE, “Android Malware Familial Classification and Representative Sample Selection via Frequent Subgraph Analysis” in IEEE TIFS, “Demystifying Diehard Android Apps” in ASE’20, “CTDroid: Leveraging a Corpus of Technical Blogs for Android Malware Analysis” in IEEE TR. For dynamic app analysis, we developed a new information flow tracking system based on QEMU for ART. The corresponding paper entitled “NDroid: Towards Tracking Information Flows Across Multiple Android Contexts” appeared in IEEE TIFS. We developed a novel on-device non-invasive analysis platform for ART, and published the corresponding paper, entitled “Malton: Towards On-Device Non-Invasive Mobile Malware Analysis for ART”, in USENIX Security’17. Since mobile malware usually use dynamic class loading(DCL) and reflection along with inter-app communication to conceal malicious attacks, we designed a novel hybrid analysis approach for identifying malicious behaviors concealed within dynamically loaded code through reflective/DCL calls. The corresponding paper entitled “DINA: Detecting Hidden Android Inter-App Communication in Dynamic Loaded Code” appeared in IEEE TIFS.

15227916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15227916.value: We found that it is feasible to actually identify fine-grained user action of Android apps according to the captured traffic in the open-world settings. Specifically, through hybrid mobile app analysis techniques, we can correlate the entry point methods along with the corresponding traffic. Moreover, leveraging advanced machine learning algorithms as well as inter-flow and intra-flow traffic features, we can successfully classify the traffic according to apps and even their fine-grained operations. These techniques can significantly improve the performance of network-centric mobile malware defense mechanisms. Moreover, by examining the mobile traffic, we can not only detect mobile malware but also vulnerabilities in mobile network as well as the attacks exploiting such vulnerabilities. Besides, by inspecting the traffic of mobile apps and their functionalities, we can discover the app’s exploitable vulnerabilities. We proposed new approaches to speed up graph alignment and present a new paradigm, programmable in-network security, by leveraging the emergence of programmable switches. Network administrators can specify concise policies and use our tool to compile them into different configurations of the primitive in P4. This new paradigm can detect mobile malware and other attacks launched by compromised mobile devices in a much more efficient and effective manner. Moreover, we found that adversarial examples pose severe threats to Android malware detection because they can render the machine learning based detection systems useless and proposed a novel robust Android malware detection approach that can resist adversarial examples without requiring their instances or knowledge by jointly investigating malware detection and adversarial example defenses. We developed new techniques to address many challenging issues in mobile app analysis. Specifically, we proposed novel methods to recover the Dex files from packed apps. We developed new static analysis approaches for inspecting UI, improving the analysis accuracy, and collecting more representative information. We developed a new information flow tracking system based on QEMU for the new Android runtime. We also designed a novel hybrid analysis approach for identifying malicious behaviors concealed within dynamically loaded code through reflective/ dynamic class loading calls. In this project, we have published 7 journal papers and 8 conferences papers. Two journal papers submitted to IEEE TDSC and IEEE TSE and one conference paper submitted to USENIX Security Symposium are under review. We trained two Ph.D. students, one M.Sc. student, and several undergraduate students. Moreover, we have been collaborating with the researchers in a number of universities on this research.

15227916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15227916.value: Our proposed algorithms and techniques can detect mobile malware according to their traffic no matter it is encrypted or not. One direction for further development of this research is to develop robust algorithms that are resilient to sophisticated malware using various approaches to evade the detection, such as generating adversarial samples, manipulating traffic features, etc., and the evolving open world setting where legitimate unseen traffic may come and go and lead to concept drift in the traffic features. Since the same algorithms and techniques can be exploited by the attackers to invade the privacy of benign users, another direction for further development of this research is to develop algorithms and techniques to prevent private information leakage due to traffic analysis attacks and keep the additional overhead and potential performance degradation as low as possible. As the mobile apps and Android system are becoming more and more complex with many new features, another direction for further development of this research is to develop efficient methods and tools to inspect such complex apps. Moreover, our methodologies can be extended to cover iOS apps.

15227916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15227916.value: The massive success of app economy and the rapid growth of smartphone penetration pose lucrative and profitable targets for attackers. Our research enabled a deep understanding of the behaviors of mobile malware and the features of mobile traffic. It revealed that it is feasible to detect mobile malware effectively and efficiently by synthesizing traffic and app analysis. This project resulted in a set of novel algorithms and approaches for network-centric mobile malware defense mechanisms that can solve the limitations and complement host-centric solutions. In particular, we designed and developed new methodologies for mobile traffic classification, mobile malware detection, and app analysis, which can also be used to solve other security problems. Our findings are expected to stir more research efforts into mobile malware analysis and have ramification in a potentially broad range of areas, such as mobile app analysis, network privacy protection, and mobile device security, etc.

15229316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15229316.value: 玻璃纖維增強樹脂筋(GFRP)和GFRP土釘在松填土邊坡的不同安裝方法，優點和局限性，應力傳遞和破壞機理的研究

15229316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15229316.value: 在香港、中國、韓國、臺灣及其他許多國家，有很多很難進入、工作空間也有限的陡峭邊坡。在此種陡峭邊坡施工一般會將鋼筋切段成3-5m長，在現場用連接器拼接使用。在許多亞洲國家，對於松散土壤加固的常見方法是利用設計極為不美觀且昂貴的格排。因此松填土邊坡穩定的成本在這些地方非常高。由於水的滲流作用，隨時間推移，土壤結構和強度逐漸退化，對用於加固松填土邊坡土釘的長期性能產生不確定性，也影響了邊坡穩定的分析和設計。一些加固松填土邊坡土釘的抗拔試驗也表明，傳統鋼釘薄弱的粘結強度會導致灌漿的滲漏/收縮，土壤內部滲水會導致其結構的長期退化(參考於許多研究人員和項目負責人的研究)。由於使用傳統鋼筋作土釘加固陡峭邊坡及松散土壤中土釘長期性能都存在各種問題，不同國家開展了很多關於創新性土釘的研究項目。理想的項目方案應該解決以下這些問題:(1)重量輕，強度高；(2)可以實現高質量的灌漿和粘結強度；(3)腐蝕問題；(4)可接受的成本；(5)易於施工-操作、連接和切割；(6)長期條件下降低土壤侵蝕作用；(7)創新性土釘在松散土壤中已知的破壞機理。 項目負責人已與很多不同國家的工程師合作研究利用新材料制作土釘及其安裝方法用於邊坡和隧道的穩定。項目負責人在前期開展過許多理論,實驗和現場施工的項目工作,出版過一系列關於前期工作的論文和書籍，並獲得過利用劈裂灌漿法穩定地基和邊坡的創新方法獎。本項目預案是項目負責人在香港、韓國和澳大利亞開展過的前期項目的擴展。項目涉及在松散填土邊坡使用GFRP /GFRP土釘的優勢、局限性和預防措施，及創新安裝方法的研究，並將與一間總部位於香港的工程公司合作。在香港松散填土邊坡展開一系列現場試驗來評估創新土釘支護體系的實際應用能力。除了實際領域的工作,項目負責人也將研究在壓力灌漿/劈裂灌漿/玻璃纖維增強樹脂筋(GFRP)土釘支護下邊坡的破壞機理, 以及在滲流作用下的長期土壤結構和粘結力的變化。測試結果將采用離散單元分析法進行評估，研究其應力傳遞的微觀性能。完整松散填土邊坡破壞機制也將通過實驗室試驗和離散單元分析法進行評估。本項目將試圖涵蓋GFRP土釘實際方面的應用，以及香港土壤的長期土壤退化作用的基礎研究，以及采用壓力灌漿/劈裂灌漿法制作土釘支護的邊坡的粘結應力和破壞機理。因此本項目在理論和實踐兩方面都有用。

15229416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15229416.value: Channel coordination is known to be a core subject of supply chain management. Over the past decades, much research effort has been devoted to exploring the detailed mechanisms (such as supply contracting schemes) of achieving coordination in supply chains with a single product. In the real world, supply contracting almost always involves multiple products. However, supply contracting with multiple products is under-explored in the literature. In view of this, we propose to comprehensively study supply contracting mechanisms in multi-product supply chains with stochastic demands. We will start by constructing the analytical model for a one supplier one retailer supply chain with multiple products. Demands for the products are stochastic. We will conduct an industrial survey and a thorough literature review to reveal the existing forms of popular and important formats of supply contracts, which are applicable for the supply chain system with multiple products, in two categories: (a) simple contracts (involving one or two parameters), and (b) sophisticated contracts (involving three or more parameters). For each kind of contract, the corresponding expected profits for the retailer, the supplier and the supply chain system are derived, and the respective optimal quantity decisions (for two products) are found. After that, each contract’s abilities of achieving coordination (and the respective conditions) will be analytically explored. We will generate insights on the choice and robustness of supply contracts by comparing the performances and coordination mechanisms among the explored contracts. We will also analytically investigate whether some innovative elements need to be added to the supply contracts so as to enhance their ability in achieving coordination. Insights regarding the required contract features for achieving coordination with the multi-product case (compared to the single product counterpart) will be generated. Finally, we will extend the analysis by exploring a challenging case when there is demand substitution between products. A new taxonomy of supply contracts with multiple products which can provide guidance on how we should select, design, evaluate, and implement the contracts in practice will also be established. We believe that this project will contribute significantly to the supply chain coordination literature and generate many useful academic and managerial insights.
