15229716.value: 本專案旨在發展新的有機-無機納米複合材料，設計和構築智慧超材料結構，構建具有致動、傳感雙功能的光子晶體轉換器。 超材料結構是通過三維結構的精確設計、重複組合微、納米尺度單元而成。 超材料可用於構建隱形斗篷、高效率太陽能電池、生物範本和微致動器等，使其在工業界、仿生學和航空航太工程領域具有重要的應用前景。 另一方面，可逆光致形變有機高分子兼具光傳感、力致動特性，但純高分子材料的機械強度較低，外場刺激時產生驅動力或輸出力較小，使其應用受限。 為此，本專案基於納米科技、高分子複合材料和鐳射光刻技術的最新進展，擬通過發展高性能有機-無機納米複合材料，構造螺旋狀超材料結構光子晶體轉換器，提高光機械致動性能，同時賦予其力和位移傳感功能。 本研究團隊致力於電活性納米碳基高分子複合材料的設計製備、多場有限元分析和發展新的液晶彈性體、納米粒子修飾功能材料，具備了開展智慧高分子納米複合材料的相關工作基礎。 本專案方案中，擬通過以下三個密切關聯的路線來提高超材料性能：(一) 石墨烯負載金納米棒填充液晶彈性體；(二) 製備兼具致動、傳感雙功能的有機-無機納米複合材料；(三) 雙光子聚合可控構築三維結構的光子晶體轉換器。 金納米棒和石墨烯既可協同提高光子晶體轉換器的光機械回應、折射率和回應速率，金納米棒的表面等離子體共振和局域電磁場效應又能促進雙光子聚合、降低光聚合的鐳射強度閾值。 同時，通過電腦輔助設計軟體和鐳射光刻系統，設計和構造高性能化超材料結構。 擬發展的光子晶體轉換器具備雙重功能：其一是致動器功能，通過納米複合材料基體中的金納米棒和石墨烯高效吸收入射光，快速轉換為熱能形成納米尺度「加熱器」，繼而誘導液晶彈性體產生相轉變，促使轉換器發生宏觀機械形變；其二是感應器功能，當入射光輻照螺旋狀超材料結構產生機械致動時， 相應輸出光的透過率改變，提供光回饋信號，通過測定透光率的變化和機械回應之間的相互關係，可用作力和位移感應器。 本專案實施目的在於發展新型有機-無機納米複合材料、構建雙功能光子晶體轉換器、提高傳統光致動器輸出力和深入理解螺旋狀超材料結構的致動 - 傳感相互作用機制和納米複合增強效應。 本團隊扎實的前期基礎能確保本專案的順利實施，並達到預期的研究目標。

15229716.label: Realisation of objectives
15229716.value: Realization of Revised Objective 1 A series of experiments was conducted based on a comprehensive review on the synthesis of gold nanorods and liquid crystal monomers for the complete realization of the objective. These experiments cover two main areas as described below. Similar works were done for other nanofillers, such as nanocarbons, inorganic gold nanorods were found to be suitable for the direct laser writing process (please refer to Part (2) of Realization of Revised Objective 2). (1) Experiments on inorganic nanofillers Photothermal inorganic gold nanorods (AuNRs) were prepared by a modified seed-mediated growth method. The fabrication process and material compositions were investigated and determined. To improve the compatibility of AuNRs and liquid crystal monomers (LCMs), 3-mercaptopropionic acid (MPA) was found to be most suitable for producing thiol-functionalized AuNRs (MPA-AuNRs). (2) Experiments on MPA-AuNRs/LCM organic-inorganic nanocomposite photoresists An intensive effort was made to determine the method for preparing MPA-AuNRs/LCM organic-inorganic nanocomposite photoresists. 1,4-Bis-[4-(3-acryloyloxypropyloxy) benzoyloxy]-2-methylbenze (RM257) and 4-methoxybenzoic acid 4-(6-acryloyloxy-hexyloxy) phenyl ester (C6BP) were applied as the crosslinker and the LCM, respectively. RM257/C6BP LCM mixture with molecular ratios of 1:9 was dissolved in acetone and appropriate amounts of MPA-AuNRs were dispersed in the LCM acetone solution under sonication. The photoinitiator Irgacure 369 (2 mol%) was added into this mixture for initiating the two-photon polymerization during direct laser writing (DLW). After the MPA-AuNRs/LCM photoresists were prepared, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to measure their transition temperatures. It was found that the nematic-isotropic transition temperature (TNI) of unfilled LCM and MPA-AuNRs/LCM mixtures with 1 wt.%, 2 wt.%, and 3 wt.% of MPA-AuNRs were 53.9 °C, 53.7 °C, 53 °C, and 52.3 °C, respectively. With the increasing amount of MPA-AuNRs, the value of TNI was slightly decreased, indicating that the incorporation of AuNRs affects the transition temperature of the LCM. To ensure LCM mesogens at the nematic phase during printing, the temperature of the photoresists should be between room temperature and TNI. Realization of Revised Objective 2 The second revised objective was achieved fully by designing an appropriate DLW configuration and performing printability studies of the nanocomposite photoresists. With the DLW configuration, the laser processing conditions were determined by a parametric approach to meet the polymerization threshold of the photoresists. Three main steps consisting of many experimental details are briefly explained below: (1) Liquid crystal cell preparation and nanocomposite photoresist loading In order to ensure the LCM mesogens at a nematic phase during printing and achieve photomechanical response under stimuli by nematic-isotropic (N-I) phase transition, a liquid crystal cell was prepared by two glass coverslips with a rubbed alignment layer. (2) Printability study of organic-inorganic nanocomposite photoresists Parametric experimental studies applying different laser writing conditions, including laser power range and scanning speed, were conducted to determine the most suitable printing parameters. The laser power was set within a range of 2.5 - 42.5 mW and the scanning speed was set within a range of 1 - 9 mm/s. The printability of the nanocomposite photoresists was accessed by the fidelity of the printed AuNRs/liquid crystalline elastomer (LCE) structures. The morphology of each structure was examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Based on the fidelity of the pyramidal structures, the condition with a power of 12.5 mW and a scanning speed of 9 mm/s was found to be most appropriate. In this printability study, photoresists with different photothermal nanofiller, including graphene oxide (GO) and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), were also prepared for comparative study. During the DLW of GO/LCM nanocomposite photoresist, vigorous bubble formation was observed due to the excessive heat generation by GO after absorbing the laser energy. Moreover, compared with MWCNTs/LCM nanocomposite photoresists, MPA-AuNRs/LCM photoresists showed a lower polymerization threshold due to more effective absorption of the laser energy during the DLW process. It was found that the inclusion of AuNRs can lead to a faster DLW process, which reduces the overall fabrication time. Therefore, graphene, GO, and CNTs were not used as nanofillers for subsequent studies in this project. (3) DLW metamaterial structures on photonic crystal length scale With the printability study and a printing parameter sweeping, an appropriate range of laser power and the scanning speed of 7.5-17.5 mW and 4-5 mm/s, respectively, were determined. Various types of AuNRs/LCE metamaterial structure on the length scale of photonic crystals, such as octet truss, pyramid frame, woodpile structure, cubic lattice, and clamp, were fabricated using the DLW system. The morphologies of these structures were examined and the shrinkage problem was found to be insignificant. A polarized optical microscope (POM) image revealed a high level of molecular alignment along the rubbing direction of the PI layer in the printed structure. This confirmed that using the liquid crystal cell prepared could achieve a good alignment of liquid crystal mesogens, which would play an important role in the photothermal actuation to provide a smart function. Realization of Revised Objective 3 The third revised objective was realized entirely via a comprehensive investigation on mechanical properties, and actuation performance of a 3D AuNRs/LCE micro-actuator with different nanofiller loading ratios. Nano-dynamic mechanical analysis and near-infrared (NIR) actuation analysis were employed. Major research activities taken were summarized below. (1) Nano-dynamic mechanical analysis of AuNRs/LCE The mechanical properties of AuNRs/LCE with different nanofiller loading ratios were studied by nano-dynamic mechanical analysis using a tribo-indenter equipped with a Berkovich tip. Compared with the unmodified LCE, AuNRs/LCE demonstrated better elastic behavior than viscous behavior. The storage modulus (E′), loss modulus (E′′), complex modulus (E*), and hardness (H) were enhanced by the inclusion of AuNRs, which were also increased with the increasing filling ratio from 1 wt.% to 3 wt.%. An enhancement of over 80% in mechanical properties was recorded. At 300 Hz indent frequency, a maximum of 200% enhancement in storage moduli and a 3.7 times improvement in hardness were measured for AuNRs/LCE with 3 wt.%. (2) Light activation analysis for photothermal sensing and actuation performance To study the sensing function of the AuNRs/LCE micro-actuators, laser power ranging from 0.5 - 2.5 W was used. The result showed that the AuNRs/LCE micro-actuators has the light sensing function. The repeatabilities of these micro-actuators were also evaluated. The change in percentage elongation of an actuator was recorded for 300 laser stimulation cycles with an irradiation time of 5 s. The repeatability was found to be reasonable as the variation was within 11%. Near-Infrared (NIR)-responsive photothermal actuation of the AuNRs/LCE 3D microstructure was performed using a diode laser with a wavelength of 808 nm. For comparison, the control experiment was performed using unfilled LCE specimens. A micro-clamp and a photonic woodpile structure were designed and produced by DLW. The reversible shape change was recorded by a CCD camera upon the laser irradiation. A maximum of 40% shape deformation was measured within 2 seconds due to the N-I phase transition of the LCE induced by the photothermal effect of AuNRs. For the unfilled LCE samples, no apparent shape change was observed when upon NIR laser stimulation. The analysis of experimental results indicated that the AuNR inclusion played an enabling role in the actuating function of the LCE nanocomposites and the photothermal sensing and actuation characteristics have nonlinear relationships with the AuNR filler content.

15229716.label: Major findings and research outcome
15229716.value: The major findings and outcomes are listed below: (1) A new light-powered photoresist enabling the realization of organic-inorganic nanocomposite photothermal transducers with metamaterial structures: The new nanocomposite photoresist is compatible with two-photon polymerization, which can be used to produce four-dimensional (4D) printable light-powered materials for the development of emerging functional devices. (2) The material composition and processing conditions to synthesize and thiol-functionalize the photothermal nanofiller AuNRs for developing nanocomposite photoresists meeting the requirement of direct laser writing (DLW). (3) The method to solve the problem of aggregation and surface incompatibility of nanofillers in LCM: 3-mercaptopropionic acid (MPA) was found to be suitable for thiol-functionalizing of AuNRs. The protocol for dispersing MPA-AuNRs in LCM was developed. (4) The knowledge on controlling the photothermal and mechanical properties of the printed AuNRs/LCE structures/devices: The effects of photothermal nanoparticle filling ratios on the actuation-sensing performance of the 3D metamaterial structures have been studied. The information contributes to design and realizing AuNRs/LCE metamaterial structures with controllable behaviors by adjusting the material composition. This enables the fabrication of novel photonic crystals in which the propagation of light can be remote-controlled by photon energy and expands the potential applications of the nanocomposite photoresist. (5) The knowledge on choice of nanofillers and chemicals for DLW the nanocomposite photoresists: The effects of various nanofillers and filler contents have been found. (6) The scheme to DLW metamaterial structures using the light-powered nanocomposite photoresist: Essential printing parameters, such as laser power range, laser scanning speed, and polymerization threshold, have been found for different combinations. Moreover, a two-photon polymerizable adamantane-containing photoresist using 1-adamantanethiol has been developed for DLW diamondoid-based metadevices with biosensing function. Referring to Part C of this report, the major findings have led to 3 journal publications and 1 conference paper. The findings/outcomes mainly relate to Items (1) to (4) were published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces and presented in the 25th Annual International Conference on Composites and Nano Engineering (ICCE-25) while the rest of them were covered by the two journal papers in Nanotechnology Reviews. This project also provided training to students. Chiu Kai Ho was trained using a final year project (Part C of this report). The part-time student assistant, Panyang Tanyaporn, learnt some experimental techniques, who later registered for a MPhil programme (supported by another research grant). The full-time research assistant of this project, Dong Yuqing, also later registered for a PhD programme (supported by another research grant).

15229716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15229716.value: One of the main deliverables of this research is a new light-powered nanocomposite photoresist for 4D printing. Future work can be done to develop metamaterial structures with special optical properties based on this material and topography optimization. Moreover, research can be conducted to use upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) and downconversion nanoparticles (DCNPs) to manipulate input light frequency for remote-sensing or control. For the research on LCE, it is suggested to conduct a comprehensive study on the effect of moieties alignment on the structure transformation induced by the nematic-to-isotropic transition. By executing the proposed works above, more sophisticated transducers with dual actuating-sensing functions with tunable properties can be realized. Scale up production of these devices will then be a research challenge in the field of Advanced Manufacturing Technology.

15229716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15229716.value: This project produces a new light-sensitive material to enable 3D printing of special structures having sensing and actuating functions. This special type of structure is often referred to as metamaterial structures which have a wide range of applications, covering industrial, biomimetics, and aerospace engineering. Based on the knowledge discovered through processing and characterizing nanomaterials, the methods have been developed to prepare the light-sensitive material and to 3D print the special structures having sensing and actuating functions. This study also provides a better understanding of various effects of nanoparticle inclusion on the physical properties and the laser printability of the light-sensitive material, which are useful to design and manufacture light-powered micro- or nano-electromechanical systems.

15234216.label: Project Objectives
15234216.value: We will investigate linearized proximal algorithms with Bregman distance to solve a convex composite optimization problem, and investigate its convergence rates under the assumptions of local weak sharp minima of order p and a quasi-regularity condition. 15234216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15234216.value: The proximal point algorithm has been very popular in solving structured optimization problems for more than half a century. One of the main reasons is that they generate subproblems that always have a unique solution, and are able to avoid the ill conditioning in numerical implementation. A well-known drawback of the proximal point algorithms is that the computational cost of solving each subproblem is as high as solving the original problem. We will employ a linearization technique and a Bregman distance to overcome this drawback, such that the corresponding subproblem is convex, irrespective of the original problem being convex or not, and remains to have a unique solution which lies in the interior of the feasible set so that the constraints are thus eliminated automatically. In recent years, there has been an extensive study on the global convergence of proximal point algorithms for convex constrained optimization problems. However, there is a lack of research on the convergence rates of proximal-type algorithms with Bregman distance for both convex and nonconvex constrained optimization problems. It is well known that the establishment of convergence rates is important in guaranteeing the numerical performance of relevant algorithms. In this project, we will develop a linearized proximal theory with Bergman distance for solving convex composite optimization, including local superlinear convergence rates in terms of both functional values and iterates, under the assumptions of local weak sharp minima of order p and a quasi-regularity condition. We will propose a globalization strategy for the linearized proximal algorithm with Bregman distance based on the Armijo-line search and establish global superlinear convergence results. We will apply the designed linearized proximal algorithms with Bergman distance to a feasibility problem and a sensor network localization problem. The project is of a long-term significant value, with an implication of further investigation on effective solution algorithms for constrained optimization problems and in the training of Operations Researchers with strong mathematical skills. 近几十年，邻近点算法已经广泛用于求解各种结构性的优化问题。一个主要原因是该算法产生的子问题通常只有唯一解，因而能够避免数值应用的病态条件性困扰。然而，邻近点算法的一个主要弱点是它的子问题的求解成本较高，有时和求解原问题相当。我们将采用线性化技巧和Bregman距离来克服这一弱点，使得对应的子问题是一个凸问题，即便原问题是非凸的；而且子问题仍然只有唯一解，且是可解集的内点，因而自动满足约束条件。近年来，求解约束凸优化问题的邻近点算法的全局收敛性已经被广泛研究。然而，基于Bregman距离的邻近点算法的收敛速度研究却寥寥无几，无论是求解约束凸优化和非凸优化问题。众所周知，收敛速度的研究是算法的数值应用效率的重要依据。在本项目中，我们将针对复合凸优化问题，在p阶局部弱尖集和拟正则性条件的假设下，研究基于Bregman距离的邻近点算法的收敛理论，包括所生成函数值和迭代点序列的超线性收敛性。结合Armijo线搜索，我们将设计基于Bregman距离的邻近点算法的全局收敛策略，并构建该算法的全局超线性收敛速度。我们还将应用所设计的Bregman邻近点算法来求解可行性问题与无线传感器定位问题。本项目对于优化算法研究和运筹学应用具有深远的研究价值和应用前景。

15234216.label: Realisation of objectives
15234216.value: Objective 1: We investigated a proximal distance and an induced proximal distance. The Bregman distance is a class of functions where the proximal distance and the induced proximal distance are the same. We proposed an interior quasisubgradient method based on the proximal distance to solve constrained nondifferentiable quasiconvex optimization problems in Hilbert spaces. It was shown that a newly introduced generalized Gateaux subdifferential is a subset of a quasisubdifferential. We investigated the convergence properties, including the global convergence and iteration complexity, under the assumption of the Holder condition of order p, when using the constant/diminishing/dynamic stepsize rules. We obtained convergence rate results by assuming a Holder-type weak sharp minimum condition relative to an induced proximal distance. We also investigated an inexact quasisubgradient method with extrapolation for solving a quasiconvex optimization problem with a closed, convex and bounded constraint set. We established the convergence in objective values, iteration complexity and rate of convergence for our proposed method under Holder condition and weak sharp minimum condition. When both diminishing stepsize and extrapolation rule are decaying as a power function, we obtained explicit iteration complexities. When diminishing stepsize is decaying as a power function and the extrapolation stepsize is decreasing not less than a power function, the diminishing stepsize provides a linear rate of convergence to an optimal solution or to a ball of the optimal solution set, which is faster than any sublinear convergence rate. With geometrically decreasing extrapolation stepsize, we obtained a linear rate of convergence to a ball of the optimal solution set for the constant stepsize and dynamic stepsize. Our numerical testing showed that the numerical performance with extrapolation is much more efficient than that without extrapolation in terms of the number of iterations needed for reaching an approximate optimal solution. 15234216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15234216.value: We investigated a proximal distance and an induced proximal distance. The Bregman distance is a class of functions where the proximal distance and the induced proximal distance are the same. Based on the proximal distance we proposed an interior quasisubgradient method for solving constrained quasiconvex optimization problems in Hilbert spaces. We established various convergence properties, including the global convergence and iteration complexity, when using the constant/diminishing/dynamic stepsize rules. We obtained convergence rate results by assuming a Holder-type weak sharp minimum condition relative to an induced proximal distance. See [5]. We explored an optimality theorem in order to provide the equivalences among a local minimum, second-order optimality condition and second-order growth property of an lp regularization problem and applied it to establish linear convergence properties of an inexact descent method and two inexact proximal gradient algorithms. We extended the linear convergence results to the infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. We observed that our results cannot be established under the framework of Kurdyka-£ojasiewicz theory. See [1]. Exploiting the structure of the sum-minimization problem of finite nondifferentiable quasiconvex functions, we proposed an incremental quasisubgradient method and investigated its convergence properties to a global optimal value/solution. We applied the proposed incremental quasisubgradient method to solve a quasiconvex feasibility problem and a sum of ratios problem. See [2]. For an inexact quasisubgradient method with extrapolation for solving a quasiconvex optimization problem, we established the convergence in objective values, iteration complexity and rate of convergence. When both diminishing stepsize and extrapolation rule are decaying as a power function, we obtained explicit iteration complexities. With geometrically decreasing extrapolation stepsize, we obtained a linear rate of convergence to a ball of the optimal solution set. See [6]. We presented a Newton method for solving a linear complementarity problem with a Z-matrix. We proposed a generalized Newton method for solving a discrete-time linear complementarity system where the linear complementarity problem constraint is solved by the proposed Newton method. We showed that the generalized Newton method converges globally and finds a solution in finitely many iterations. See [3]. We proposed a power penalty method to approximate the discrete equation of a continuous Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman. We established a sharp convergence rate of an exponential order for the power penalty method. We presented a numerical experiment solving an incomplete market optimal investment problem to demonstrate the rates of convergence and effectiveness of the new method. See [4].

15234216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15234216.value: The extrapolation strategy is able to enhance numerical performance of some optimal algorithms for convex and nonconvex optimization problems. It is not clear whether the extrapolation strategy is able to improve a faster convergence rate for nonconvex optimization problems. We will investigate higher order convergence rates of some optimal algorithms by virtue of exploration for some structured convex and nonconvex optimization problems. The separable property or sum-minimization structure appears in many practical applications. We will study efficient randomized incremental optimal methods for solving optimization problems with these structures.

For an inexact quasisubgradient method with extrapolation for solving a quasiconvex optimization problem, we established iteration complexity and rate of convergence. We explored second-order optimality condition and second-order growth property of a nonconvex composite optimization problem and applied them to establish linear convergence properties of an inexact descent method and two inexact proximal gradient algorithms. We established a convergence rate of an exponential order for the power penalty method for solving the discrete equation of a continuous Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman. We presented a numerical experiment to solve an incomplete market optimal investment problem. We proposed an incremental quasisubgradient method for a sum-minimization problem of finite quasiconvex functions and investigated its convergence properties. We applied the incremental quasisubgradient method to solve a quasiconvex feasibility problem. 15237516.label: Project Objectives
15237516.value: To develop an accurate and effective approach that will characterize the 3D geometry of breast shape, size, volume and particularly the under breast curve, with flexibility for application to various breast sizes, which cannot be fully obtained from traditional 3D body scanning systems so as to facilitate the 3D ergonomic design of bra features and embedded components to improve breast support, fit and comfort. To analyse the bra-skin pressure distribution and sensory comfort perception in relation to structural design and material choice of shoulder straps, underband and embedded components, and to formulate numerical prediction models for predicting bra-skin pressure in relation to fabric stress-strain properties, curvature of anatomic sites, etc. To establish a novel efficient approach for assessing breast motion and vertical breast displacement, and to formulate numerical model to simulate the dynamic behavior and mechanical force of the breast for different activity levels, and therefore optimize the design features and fabrication of moulded bras. To design and develop a breast motion stabilizer that is embedded into bra cups so that the 3D shape is thermoformed together in the bra moulding process. The physical and thermal-mechanical properties of various fabric structures and orientations of material will be characterized. To carry out laboratory wear trials to validate the analysis and prediction models so as to provide an effective solution to optimise the design of supportive moulded bras.

15237516.label: Realisation of objectives
15237516.value: In this project, the 5 objectives stated in the project proposal have been fully achieved. First of all, a new casting approach has been designed which aims to characterize the 3D geometry of underbreast curve of different breast shapes and sizes. A thermoplastic sheet which is commonly used for orthosis splinting is used. The material facilitates very precise moulding which conforms to the anatomy of breast curve. It is completely remouldable and can be adjusted easily after reheating locally. Its temporary adhesion feature and tackiness during orthotic fabrication helps orthosis stay in place during fabrication. This 3D shape geometry of underbreast is casted and then compared with the traditional 2D underwire by using 3D laser scanner. A total of 13 subjects ranging from size 34B to 34D were recruited. Results indicated that consistent differences exist between the underwire (under extension during wearing) and the natural shape of the underbreast curves. The angle differences ranged from -0.7° to around +5.8°, with the mean difference of 1.48°. The underband tension (length adjustments) and the properties of underwires have major effects on the underwire angles. Such differences not only contribute to wearing discomfort due to poor fitting, but also adversely affecting the efficacy of the breast support with displacements during body movements. On the basis of the underbreast shape, the 3D shape geometry of the breast support component can be designed. The properties and effects of bra components were systematically analysed. Traditional underwire designs are planar and have different gore heights and wire gauges to support the bra cup. When putting on the bra and pulling the underband backward, the underwire is deformed (or opened) into 3D shape of the breast structure. However, it is difficult for a planar surface to directly fit all breast shapes and mimic the shape of the breast roots. The opening length or underwire shape may not able to accommodate the breast volume or underbreast curve. In this study, to examine the impacts of various bra components on breast support, a changeable bra design that allows adjustment of tension in a flexible manner is adopted. The shoulder straps and bra band are attached with a metal hook. This design allows the shoulder straps and bra band to be changed during the experiment. A total of 15 bra conditions that comprised 3 lengths of shoulder straps and 5 lengths of underbands were established. With the support of a bra fitting expert, the best fit bra condition and tension is defined. Bra-skin interface pressure measurements were taken of breast sizes 34D and 34B by using Novel Pliance-X pressure system. Six measurement points including gore, underwire start point, underwired mid-point, underwire end-point, shoulder point, underband at the back were taken. Similar to previous study on bra pressure, high pressures were found for the tighter shoulder strap and underband combinations. High pressures were also recorded at the mid-point of the underwire. This may be due to the insufficient support from the shoulder straps and underband to support the weight of the breasts. The forces were therefore transferred to the mid-point of the underwire, resulting in high pressure values, poor fit and even discomfort. A soft dummy has been designed and developed in order to replace human wear trials with inconsistent results in breast motion evaluation due to large variations of breast shape and sizes. It has a layer of artificial skin made of silicon. The soft layer of artificial skin allows a certain amount of flexibility and softness. An auxiliary mechanical device with a pneumatic system was designed to mimic the dynamic human movement of walking. The dummy can move up and down continuously, thus corresponding to heel strike in the gait cycle. The speed of the auxiliary mechanical device was controlled by using a motor so that each cycle of the cam movement is half a gait cycle. A VICON motion capture system is used in this study to track breast motion and calculate the breast displacement of different bra conditions and activity levels. Results indicated that bras are important as external support and reduce vertical breast displacement. Compared to the braless condition, the total vertical breast displacement with the best fit combination of shoulder straps and underband is reduced by 40% to 63%, particularly in a reduction of upward breast movement for a breast size of 34B. Total vertical breast displacement is 20.3mm to 9.6 ± 2mm at slow walking (2.3km/h), whilst the reduction in displacement during fast walking (4.08km/h) are comparatively less. In comparing the effects of the shoulder straps and underband, tightening or loosening them also reduces the ability of the bra to control breast motion. Therefore, an appropriate tension should be determined to optimize the support function of bras. To improve the ergonomic design and support function of the moulded bra, an investigation is carried out on the geometric shape of the breasts to gain a better understanding on the effect of the angle of conventional planar underwires. Similar results of the underbreast curvature with different underwires are obtained from the manikin and invited subjects with breast sizes of 75B and 75D. The appropriate shoulder strap and underband length then provide sufficient length to stretch the underwire material with lower bending rigidity into an angle that accommodates the curvature of the breasts without a bra. A new bra insert design is then developed on the basis of the natural curvature of the underbreast and consists of an extended part from the curve to cover part of the breasts. The primary ergonomic feature of the bra insert is that it provides a better fit with the natural curvature of the underbreast. A 3D bra insert made of nylon 12 is found to be the most flexible compared to steel and the more rigid PLA material. The support performance of the 3D bra inserts has also improved. Greater coverage of the breast volume by the supporting components helps to redistribute the weight of the breasts to the torso and therefore redistribute the impact during movement. Nylon 12 with a non-porous material as the bra insert provides the best support among the tested underwire samples and designed bra inserts. Therefore, the insert design for ergonomic bras should be studied in more depth because of its role in supporting the breasts.

15237516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15237516.value: In this project an effective approach to characterize the 3D geometry of the breast shape and the under breast curve has been developed. Results indicated that consistent differences exist between the underwire and the natural shape of the underbreast curves. With reference to the subjects recruited in this study, the angle differences ranged from -0.7° to around +5.8°, with the mean difference of 1.48°. The underband tension and the properties of underwires have major effects on the underwire angles. Such differences not only contribute to wearing discomfort due to poor fitting, but also adversely affecting the efficacy of the breast support with displacements during body movements. A novel design soft dummy and a changeable bra design have been developed to objectively and systematically analyse the bra-skin pressure distribution and comfort in relation to structural design and material choice of shoulder straps and underband. High pressures were found for the tighter shoulder strap and underband combinations, as well as at the mid-point of the underwire. This may be due to the insufficient support from the shoulder straps and underband to support the weight of the breasts. The forces were therefore transferred to the mid-point of the underwire, resulting in high pressure values, poor fit and even discomfort. Wearing of a bra offers external support and reduce vertical breast displacement. Compared to the braless condition, the total vertical breast displacement with the best fit combination of shoulder straps and underband is reduced by 40% to 63%, particularly in a reduction of upward breast movement for a breast size of 34B. In comparing the effects of the shoulder straps and underband, tightening or loosening them also reduces the ability of the bra to control breast motion. Therefore, an appropriate tension should be determined to optimize the support function of bras. A new bra insert design is then developed on the basis of the natural curvature of the underbreast and consists of an extended part from the curve to cover part of the breasts. The primary ergonomic feature of the bra insert is that it provides a better fit with the natural curvature of the underbreast. A 3D bra insert made of nylon 12 is found to be the most flexible compared to steel and the more rigid PLA material. With reference to wear trial, the support performance of the 3D bra inserts has also improved.

15237516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15237516.value: This project proposes a scientific approach that incorporates a method to enhance the precision of acquiring breast geometry information, and a soft mummy to improve the evaluation of bra-skin pressure, breast movement and fabrication materials to advance the design of moulded bras. With reference to the 3D geometric shape of underbreast, ergonomic bra insert has been designed and developed by 3D printing technology. The newly designed 3D bra inserts offers improved breast support and comfort to the wearer. The project outcomes advance knowledge on the ergonomic design of intimate apparel and related products by incorporating breast image analysis, biomechanical evaluation of breast kinetics and material sciences. More importantly, scientific guidelines are provided to expedite the continuous design and development of high-quality moulded bras so that their fit and support performance could be predicted in advance and avoid costly trials-and-errors of the moulding process in today’s short-cycle manufacturing.

15237516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15237516.value: Although there has been substantial growth in the moulded bra market, there is limited study to advance the design of bras for improving fit and support. The planar profile of underwire bras does not conform to the 3D curvatures of the breast anatomy, which adversely affects the supporting functions and inevitably induces excessive pressure, thus causing discomfort. Therefore, a 3D ergonomic design that incorporates suitable bra features and embeds support inserts can effectively improve breast support and comfort. This project proposes a scientific approach that incorporates a method to enhance the precision of acquiring breast geometry information, a novel design of soft mummy and a changeable bra design to improve the evaluation of bra-skin pressure, breast movement and fabrication materials to advance the design of moulded bras. With reference to the 3D geometric shape of underbreast, the newly designed 3D bra insert offers improved breast support and comfort to the wearer. The findings therefore provide a good reference to bra designers to advance the design of bras with suitable choice of bra features for different end-uses and/or activity levels.

15238116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15238116.value: 群智感知是指用戶通過他們移動設備中的各類傳感器將物理信息，例如位置、速度、光強等數據傳送到伺服器的中用于測量某些現象。隨著移動計算的盛行，此類應用正在實時交通信息、環境監測、公共健康、緊急響應、社交媒體以及智慧城市等各領域逐步推廣。然而，此類應用中的一個嚴重問題是個人隱私的洩露。例如在絕大多數現行的群智感知應用中，用戶必須提交位置數據以記錄感知的地點（例如谷歌地圖中的實時交通），但該信息極有可能被伺服器濫用于對用戶進行追蹤和個人背景分析。 儘管一些學術文獻解決了感知數據本身的隱私保護問題，我們強調在上述問題中保護感知數據所對應的元數據（例如位置）才是目前亟需解決的問題。在本項目中，我們將為群智感知設計一個安全劃分和數據採集系統用以保護元數據的隱私安全。我們將利用現代密碼學中的最新工具，包括不經意隨機存取、同態加密和差分私有隨機數產生器等，并提出一個可證明的系統安全模型。 我們相信這一研究能為下一代群智感知系統提供有力的理論基礎，并推動物聯網、雲計算等相關領域類似問題的研究。我們期待本項目的研究成果不僅能貢獻學術界，也能回饋工業界和香港社會。因為我們相信隱私保護在當今的數字化時代是一個非常重要的課題。

15238116.label: Realisation of objectives
15238116.value: After 42 months of research endeavors, we report that most objectives set out in the original proposal have been thoroughly studied and resolved. As for the detailed progress, we have fully achieved objectives 1 and 2 by the end of year 2018, and objectives 3 and 4 by the end of year 2019, and mid 2020, respectively. For objectives 1 and 2, we study the problem that is presented in the first task of the original proposal to protect metadata for aggregation tasks in mobile crowd sensing. First, we identify one security problem in metadata partition, namely, the side channel attacks by I/O access pattern. This is particularly threatening in cloud environment where untrusted hypervisors can easily keep track of VM's activities such as memory and disk accesses. To address this issue, we propose the integration of hardware security (or more specifically CPU enclaves such as Intel SGX) with ORAM for daily aggregation operations such as OLAP queries. We carefully design a lazy persistence scheme together with a path sharing strategy to boost it's performance. The paper has been published in Information Systems, Volume 96, February 2021. Second, we have also investigated the aggregation in mobile sensor network and proposed a group-based encryption and integrity assurance scheme, which is useful when a few nodes are compromised in an adversary environment. This paper has been published as a full research paper in 29th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM '20). Third, we have studied the problem of protecting mobile user's sensor data against stealth location tracking. We have shown that inertial sensor data, whose meta data are not protected properly, can lead to significant privacy breaches. This paper has been published in IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security (TIFS). Fourth, we also studied the aggregation problem a specific data type "set-valued" data, which is commonly seen in sensor networks. We designed an encryption and authentication scheme that can protect both confidentiality and integrity. This paper has been published in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE). Fifth, we have proposed a hybrid approach that integrates both ORAM and homomorphic encryption. The advantage of using a hybrid approach is to better cater for the dynamic workload that is typical in a crowd sensing system. We give some theoretical analysis on the performance savings, and the experimental results also show that such hybrid approach is very robust in terms of various system workload and settings. We have submitted the paper to ACM Transactions on Sensor Networks, and the paper is now under revision. For objective 3, as indicated in the original proposal, we have explored the adoption of differential privacy models for mobile crowdsensing. First, we have studied and proposed a multi-round local differential privacy (LDP) mechanism for mobile phone users to submit their sensitive key-value pairs for approximate aggregation. We formally prove our scheme satisfy LDP and conduct intensive empirical study on the accuracy of estimation. The paper titled "PrivKV: Key-Value Data Collection with Local Differential Privacy", has been published as a full research paper in IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2019 (S&P). Second, we have explored on more complicated data types, namely, network and graph data, and studied the estimation of aggregate graph metrics, such as centrality and degree, under local differential privacy settings. The paper has been published in IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE '20), and an extended version has been accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Data and Knowledge Engineering (TKDE). Third, we have investigated high-dimensional data aggregation in crowd sensing and sensor networks. In particular, we focus on correlated data and aim to reduce the noise imposed on such data. The paper has been published as a full research paper in 18th IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication and Networking (SECON), 2021. Fourth, we have also investigated time series data aggregation, which is also a common data type in crowd sensing and sensor networks. We propose a relaxed version of LDP, namely, TLDP, which significantly reduces the utility loss when such data are aggregated. This paper has been published as a full research paper in IEEE International Conference on Computer Communications (INFOCOM’21). For objective 4, we have studied some computational efficiency problem in crowd sensing and aggregation. First, we investigate the users' social behavior in crowd sourcing in terms of spatial and social locality and propose a recommendation query for group activities while preserving a minimum acquaintance level. This work has been published in The VLDB Journal. Second, we investigate crowdsourcing as a solution to resolve uncertainty in probabilistic databases. In particular, we design an optimal pairwise comparison strategy to efficiently answer top-k ranking queries in crowdsourcing systems. The paper has been accepted and published in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering. Third, we have studied the privacy and efficiency of crowd-based trajectory collection and aggregation problem, under local differential privacy and l-diversity models. These works have been published in ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology (TIST), IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM'19), which receives Best Paper Award, and Distributed and Parallel Databases, respectively. Fourth, the efficiency of an output aggregate machine learning model against adversial attacks, such as model extraction attacks, has been studied. We maximized the query utility and retained low computational cost for various aggregate learning models. These works have been published in European Symposium on Research in Computer Security (ESORICS '19) and IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing (TDSC).

15238116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15238116.value: As for further development, we plan to further build and enhance our existing schemes to make it suitable for commercial demonstration and knowledge transfer. We believe that the promotion of these protection schemes will further make an impact on both research and industry community regarding our privacy-preserving metadata collection for mobile crowdsensing.

15238116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15238116.value: Mobile crowdsensing aims to sense and report users' environmental contexts for the server to aggregate them to measure a phenomenon of common interest. With the pervasiveness of mobile devices, the ubiquity of wireless networks, and the improvement of sensing technology, mobile crowdsensing becomes an essential ingredient of human-machine intelligence, with numerous applications such as real-time traffic analysis, environment monitoring, public health, emergency response, social networking, and smart cities. In this project, we have addressed the critical privacy issue in mobile crowdsensing, as the reported contexts of users can be abused by the server or third parties to infer other user contexts such as current activities, physical condition, and even social relations (based on co-location). We target at protecting the metadata of sensed values that describe them for further analysis (e.g., GPS location of the sensed speed in Google Maps), as these metadata effectively disclose user contexts and may lead to privacy breaches. Our research outcomes are based on several modern cryptography constructions – oblivious RAM (ORAM), homomorphic encryption, and differentially private randomizers. The secure aggregation schemes we have developed can be adopted in real-life crowdsensing applications with a variety of data types and domains.

15240816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15240816.value: Classical inventory models often assume that the demands from all customers are homogeneous. However, due to the practice of price differentiation or the different service level requirements of customers, the demands from various customers may differ in the unit revenues and/or shortage costs. This project targets to address this issue by considering multiple demand classes, where the demand from each class is allowed to have a distinct unit revenue and/or shortage cost. In the meantime, demand forecasting always poses a challenge for the practical implementation of inventory models. Compared with the aggregated demand, it can be more difficult to determine the demand distribution of each demand class. Therefore, we adopt the distributionally robust optimization approach, which only requires the moments (and ranges) of the demand distributions, to enhance the practicability of the proposed models. Four robust inventory management models with multiple demand classes will be studied in this project. The first model considers how to optimize the order quantity of a newsvendor serving multiple demand classes. The preliminary result shows that there exists a compact convex optimization formulation for the robust model that maximizes the worst-case expected profit among all demand distributions specified by moments (and ranges). The closed-form solution for the worst-case distributions has been derived for some special cases. We will analyze the worst-case distributions in other cases, derive the closed-form solution for the optimal order quantity if possible, investigate the possibility of developing algorithms more efficient than directly solving the convex optimization model, conduct various comparative static studies, and determine the value of considering multiple demand classes. A more general model with salvage value and class-dependent shortage costs will also be studied. The newsvendor model will be then extended to three multi-period models, namely, the lost sales model, the lost sales model with rationing decisions, and the backorder model with rationing decisions. The optimal policies of all these multi-period models will be characterized as completely as possible. Efficient numerical algorithms will be developed to obtain close-to-optimal conservative solutions. We will also study the comparative statics and the value of considering multiple demand classes. The proposed project will contribute to the literatures of inventory control, inventory rationing, and robust optimization. The theoretical results and numerical observations will provide insights and guidelines to industrial practitioners when making inventory (and rationing) decisions. The computational algorithms can also be implemented to facilitate the decision making. 經典庫存模型通常假定所有顧客的需求是同質的。然而，由於區別定價或顧客對供貨水平的要求不同，不同顧客的需求可能帶來不同的單位收入，也可能意味著不同的單位缺貨成本。該項目通過考慮存在單位收入及/或缺貨成本差異的多類需求，以彌補經典庫存模型的不足。同時，需求預測是在實踐中應用庫存模型的一項重大挑戰。與總需求相比，確定每一類需求的分佈將更加困難。為了提升模型的實用性，我們採用分佈式魯棒優化方法，僅通過需求分佈的矩（和支撐集）進行決策。 該項目將研究四類魯棒庫存管理模型。第一類模型在報童模型的基礎上考慮存在多類需求的情況下如何優化訂貨量。初步結果表明，如果我們考慮所有滿足矩（和支撐集）約束的需求分佈，並優化最壞情況下的利潤期望，該魯棒模型可化為凸優化模型。在某些特例下，我們已經求得使利潤期望最低的需求分佈的解析解。我們將分析在其他情況下該分佈的性質，盡可能地推導出最優訂貨量的解析解，探討能否開發比直接求解凸優化模型更高效的算法，開展比較靜態分析，並測定決策者因考慮多類需求而獲得的額外利潤。更具一般性的模型將考慮產品殘值和基於需求類別的缺貨成本，我們也將對其進行研究。 報童模型將進而擴展到三類多週期模型，即失去銷售模型，含庫存分配策略的失去銷售模型，以及含庫存分配策略的延期交貨模型。我們將盡量全面地刻畫所有多週期模型的最優策略，開發高效的數值算法以獲得接近最優的保守解。我們也將進行比較靜態分析，並研究因考慮多類需求所帶來的額外利潤。 該項目將進一步拓展庫存控制、庫存分配和魯棒優化等方向的研究。其理論結果和數值觀察可對業界的庫存（和配給）決策提供見解和指導。其模型的計算算法也能應用於實踐，對決策進行支持。

15240816.label: Realisation of objectives
15240816.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The details are provided as follows: 1. Formulation In this project, we propose four distributionally robust inventory models with multiple demand classes, which can be classified into two categories, namely, the newsvendor model and the multi-period models, based on the length of the planning horizon. 1.1 Formulation of the newsvendor model We consider a newsvendor that uses a single product to serve demands from multiple classes. The newsvendor pays a linear cost to order the product from an external supplier and gets a revenue by serving the demands. The objective is to decide the ordering quantity before the realization of the demands. The proposed model is different from the classical newsvendor model in the following two aspects. First, the classical model assumes that all the demands are homogeneous. In our model, the demands of different classes can be heterogeneous, i.e., the unit revenue generated by serving the demand of one class can be different from the unit revenue of another class. Second, the classical newsvendor model assumes that the demand distribution is completely known. However, demand forecasting always poses a challenge for the practical implementation of inventory models. Compared with the aggregated demand, it can be more difficult to determine the demand distribution of each demand class. Therefore, we adopt the distributionally robust optimization approach. In particular, we construct a set of distributions, which is very likely to contain the true joint distribution of demands from different classes, based on some partial information on the demands, i.e., means, variances, ranges, and historical data. This set of distributions is referred to as the uncertainty set. The distributionally robust model then selects the ordering quantity that minimizes the worst-case expected profit among all distributions in the uncertainty set. In order to ensure the tractability of the proposed model, we focus on the following two types of uncertainty set. The first one is constructed based on the marginal moments and range for the demand from each class. The uncertainty set for distributions is set to all joint distributions having the given marginal moments and contained in the given ranges. The second one is built based on the empirical joint distribution obtained from historical demand data. We consider in the uncertainty set all distributions that are sufficiently closed to the empirical distribution based on a given phi-divergence measure. We also consider a generalization of the newsvendor model where a unit shortage cost is incurred if the demand from a class cannot be satisfied and the unused inventory can generate a salvage value. 1.2 Formulation of the multi-period models The multi-period models consider a finite planning horizon. For any given period, we first observe the initial inventory position and then determine the order-up-to level. The uncertain demands for all the demand classes are then realized. Based on how the demands from different classes are served, we obtain the following three models. - Lost sales model. This model assumes that any demand cannot be declined as long as inventory is available. However, if the total demand from all demand classes exceeds the on-hand inventory, we can choose the amount of inventory allocated to each demand class so as to maximize the revenue in that period. - Lost sales model with rationing decisions. This model allows declining demands even when there is on-hand inventory. It might be beneficial to do so because we can reserve inventory for future demands from more important classes by rejecting current demands from less important classes. These decisions of whether to satisfy a unit of demand immediately are referred to as rationing decisions. They are especially important when the supply is limited. Therefore, in this model, we impose an ordering capacity in each period. - Backorder model with rationing decisions. The setting of this model is very similar to that of the lost sales model with rationing decisions, except that all the demands not immediately satisfied are backlogged. Furthermore, we can choose to fulfill any of the backlogged demands at any period during the planning horizon. Just like the newsvendor model, we also adopt the distributionally robust optimization approach, which assumes that the demand distribution in each period is independent and contained in an uncertainty set. The multi-period robust models can be cast into a two-player game. The first player, i.e., the inventory manager, chooses a non-anticipative decision rule that determines the ordering (as well as rationing and fulfilling) decisions for all periods. The second player then chooses a non-anticipative decision rule that selects the demand distribution from the uncertainty set for every period. In each period, the first player receives the expected profit in that period, where the expectation is taken with respect to the distribution chosen by the second player, while the second player pays a cost equal to the reward received by the first player. Therefore, the first player targets to maximize his/her expected reward over the entire planning horizon and the second player needs to minimize the corresponding cost. Based on this game, we then derive the dynamic programming recursion for each of the multi-period models. 2. Newsvendor Model For the newsvendor model, we show that it can be equivalently formulated as a convex optimization problem and hence is computationally tractable. We then focus on studying certain special cases where closed-form solutions and/or more efficient solution algorithms can be obtained. Towards this end, we analyze how the revenue function changes with respect to the on-hand inventory and the demands from different classes. Two cases have been identified to have stronger results than the general model. One is the case where we only know for any demand class the mean of the stochastic demand and an interval containing its support, which is referred to as the mean-range model. The other is the case where we only know the marginal mean and variance for the demand of each class, which is referred to as the mean-variance model. 3. Multi-Period Models For the multi-period models, we first study whether the objective functions in the dynamic programming recursion are concave in the decision variables. The optimal policies are then characterized under the condition that the objective functions are concave. Numerical methods have been developed based on the results of the newsvendor model, the structural properties of the optimal policies, and the approximations of the profit-to-go functions to obtain heuristic policies, which perform strongly in our extensive numerical experiments. 4. Comparative Statics and Value of Considering Multiple Demand Classes For the newsvendor model with closed-form solutions, the comparative statics are analyzed using the closed-form solutions. For the newsvendor model without closed-form solutions and the multi-period models, we use numerical experiments to conduct the comparative statics analysis. We mainly focus on how the worst-case distribution, the optimal decision, and the optimal value change with respect to the number of demand classes, the unit revenue of each demand class, and the length of the planning horizon. The benefit of considering multiple demand classes has also been studied in a similar manner. It shows that even when all the demand classes have the same revenue and cost parameters, considering multiple demand classes can help to reduce the conservativeness of robust optimization.

15240816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15240816.value: This project has led to 1 paper published in Production and Operations Management (Ni et al., 2018), 1 paper accepted by Naval Research Logistics (Jiang et al., 2021), 1 PhD thesis (Ni, 2017), 4 presentations in international conferences, and 1 seminar talk at Southeast University. Furthermore, we are preparing the following working paper, which will be soon submitted for peer review at Production and Operations Management: Ni, W., Shu, J., and Song, M. 2021. Robust Inventory Management with Multiple Demand Classes. Working paper. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The major findings of this project are summarized as follows (see Ni, 2017 and Ni et al. 2021). - Newsvendor model. We show that the generic model is computationally tractable as it can be reformulated as a convex optimization problem. Closed-form solutions and/or more efficient solution approaches are also obtained for two special cases, i.e., the mean-range and mean-variance models. We have numerically compared the robust model with its stochastic counterpart, which demonstrates that the robust model outperforms the stochastic model as long as the joint demand distribution cannot be calibrated precisely. The robust model with multiple demand classes are also compared with the counterpart with one demand class. Comparative statics analysis are conducted to understand when it is more important to implement the model with multiple demand classes. In Ni et al. (2018), we also study an application of a robust newsvendor model with multiple demand classes in disaster relief operations. - Multi-period models. We have identified sufficient conditions for the objective functions in the dynamic programming recursion to be concave, e.g., when the uncertainty set for distributions are constructed based on the empirical distribution using certain phi-divergence measure. Under these conditions, the optimal inventory policy is a (state-dependent) (capacitated) base-stock policy and the optimal rationing (and fulfilling) policy is a (state-dependent) threshold policy. The characterization of the optimal policies helps us to reduce the computational complexity for the dynamic programming recursion. We also develop strongly performing heuristic algorithms by utilizing the results from the newsvendor model and approximating the profit-to-go functions. Numerical studies have been conducted to show the necessity of considering robust models with multiple demand classes. In Jiang et al. (2021), we also study a robust multi-period model with multiple demand classes, which is applied to manage chip inventory in automobile supply chains.

15240816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15240816.value: This project focuses on generic models for inventory management with multiple demand classes. For future research, we can study these problems in specific application scenarios. For example, consider the resources used for epidemic control such as face masks and protective gears. As these resources are indispensable when fighting epidemics, it is important to manage their inventory efficiently. Although their demand can be easily segregated into multiple classes, e.g., according to geographic regions with different epidemic situations, the models proposed in this project cannot be directly applied to the inventory problems of these resources. One reason is that the supply shortage of these resources has a complicated impact on the trajectory of epidemic. For instance, the supply shortage of protective gears may cause epidemic outbreak among healthcare workers. This not only can potentially infect other groups of the society, but also puts another toll on the healthcare system, which is likely to be already overloaded during a pandemic. As a result, sophisticated prediction models are required to quantify the impact of shortage. Incorporating such a shortage cost in the inventory framework will lead to new models that may require innovative solution approaches.

15240816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15240816.value: Classical inventory models often assume that the demands from all customers are homogeneous. However, due to the practice of price differentiation or the different service level requirements of customers, the demands from various customers may differ in the unit revenues and/or shortage costs. This project addresses this issue by considering multiple demand classes, where the demand from each class is allowed to have a distinct unit revenue and/or shortage cost. In particular, we study the inventory management problems in four different settings, namely, the newsvendor model, the multi-period lost sales model, the multi-period lost sales model with rationing decisions, and the multi-period backorder model with rationing decisions. As demand forecasting always poses a challenge for the practical implementation of inventory models, we adopt the robust optimization approach, which only requires partial demand information, to enhance the practicability of the proposed models. For each of the proposed models, we develop efficient solution approaches to find effective solutions. We demonstrate that considering multiple demand classes leads to significantly better inventory decisions. The analysis of comparative statics also reveal insights on when it is more important to incorporate multiple demand classes in the inventory models.

15244316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15244316.value: As most renewable generation by far is connected into electric power grids, the uncertainties inherently involved in their outputs have imposed significant challenges to many aspects of power system operation and planning. Unlike conventional power generation technologies, which are flexibly dispatchable in the sense that their future generation can be precisely planned beforehand to match with the demand, wind or photovoltaic (PV) generation are closely dependent on the weather conditions, which are full of uncertainties. Consequently, accurate forecasts of the power output of a renewable farm for the next few hours or days are of paramount importance to ensure secure and economic operation of entire power grids. Despite many research efforts made previously, highly accurate point predication of wind and solar generations has never been possible due to the chaotic nature of the weather system. Recent advancements on probabilistic interval prognosis shed new lights on effectively quantifying forecasting errors with associated probabilities. This approach can effectively reduce the risks and uncertainties involved in applying wind or solar power prediction results for power system operation and planning purposes. Based on our previous achievements, this project will investigate a novel probabilistic prognosis framework for wind and solar power generation based on granular computing, which is a burgeoning conceptual and computing paradigm enabling structured and granulized information processing dedicated for tackling challenging information analysis tasks in complex systems. By appropriately extracting and forming information granules from the time series of wind and solar generation, ambient temperature and other relevant inputs, the proposed prognosis framework can potentially enable better modeling and characterization of nonlinearities and nonstationarities involved. Consequently, granulized predictors based on e.g. neural networks will be developed to directly generate predication intervals based on input information granules. By leveraging granular computing, the proposed framework provides a holistic approach of information preprocessing(granulation) and interval computation to ensure better forecasting performance, which is distinguished from most existing methods of probabilistic prognosis. The outcomes of the project will contribute to achieving thorough understanding of and enhanced prognosis of variable renewable generation through granular based modeling and analysis to safeguard and optimize power system operation in the future. With rapid development of renewable energy worldwide, the models and methods out of this project will undoubtedly bring forward significant benefits to both Hong Kong and China’s power systems. 目前，大多數可再生能源通過連接到電力網向人類輸送能源。因此，其固有的輸出的不確定性將顯著影響電力系統運行和規劃的許多方面。傳統的發電技術能夠依據精確的事先計劃，從而靈活調度他們未來發電出力以配合電力負荷的變化。相比而言，風或光伏等可再生能源發電密切依賴於天氣條件，並且充滿了不確定性。因此，為了保證整個電網的安全經濟運行，準確預測風電廠或光伏電廠未來幾個小時或幾天的功率輸出是極為重要的。 儘管已存在許多相關的研究工作，由於天氣系統的混沌性質，風電和光伏發電的高度精度點預測從來都沒有成為可能。最新的概率區間預測研究表明該方法能夠有效量化可再生能源預報結構的誤差以及相應的概率。相應的，使用這種方法可以有效地減少因為應用風電或光電預測結果對電力系統進行調度和規劃時可能帶來的風險和不確定性。基於我們之前的研究成果，這個項目將深入研究一種新穎的基於信息粒計算的風能和太陽能發電的短期慨率預測技術。需要指出的是，信息粒子分析是一種全新的結構化顆粒狀信息處理概念和計算模式，專門應用於復雜系統中解決具有高挑戰性的信息分析任務。基於風能和太陽能發電時間序列以及環境溫度等其它有關輸入的信息，通過適當地分析和提取以形成有效的信息粒子，本項目所提出的新的信息粒子預測模型能夠對於模型輸入信息所包含的非線性和非平穩性做出更好的建模和表徵。隨後，基於信息顆粒預測的神經網絡系統將被建立，並能夠根據輸入的信息顆粒直接生成風電或光電的概率預測區間。通過利用信息粒子計算，本項目提供了一個完整的包含基於信息顆粒的預處理和概率區間計算的框架。相比大多數現有的方法， 所提出的方法能夠保障更好的概率預測性能。該項目的成果將有助於通過基於精細的建模和分析，對可再生能源發電的隨機性實現更充分的認知，並增強對其的預測效果，以促進電力系統的優化運行。在全球可再生能源的快速發展的大背景下，該項目提出的方法無疑會為香港和中國的電力系統發展帶來顯著的益處。

15244316.label: Realisation of objectives
15244316.value: This project aims at development of an innovative granular computing framework for short term probabilistic prognosis of renewable power generation with a project duration of three years. By the end of the project, the project objectives have been mostly achieved, of which the details are be provided as follows. The team has achieved project objective 1 on short term probabilistic prognosis framework design, where a novel granular computing framework for probabilistic interval forecasting of renewable generation has been designed. The proposed framework is developed to mainly involve three steps to generate optimal predication intervals for renewable generation, which include data preparation and granulation (to address data uncertainties), granular neural network construction(to address model uncertainties), training of granular neural network to construct optimal prediction intervals. These research activities and achievements have been reported in the interim report. The team has also performed granular analysis for solar time series. Different data granulation methods such as granular representations based on min-max interval values, and fuzzy logic etc have been investigated. The team has also signed up an agreement and obtained the practical measurement data from Hong Kong Observatory to perform detailed data granulation analysis. These research activities and achievements have been reported in the interim report. The team has designed granular neural networks based probabilistic prognosis framework, where the forecaster can adopt different neural networks extreme learning machines and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) etc. to achieve the best performance considering the time series to be forecasted and the forecasting horizon etc. As reported in the interim stage, the team also extend the scope of investigation to develop new probabilistic forecasting methods for electricity market price. A novel day-ahead probabilistic electricity prices prognosis method is developed based on a reliable Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS)-oriented predictive density construction strategy based on Extreme Learning Machine, and a Logistic distribution based ensemble model output statistics (EMOS) technique, of which the details has been published in IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid. In addition, a novel transactive electricity trading framework for distributed generations and demands in power distribution grids is developed, where the proposed electricity forecasting method provides the interval forecasting information as the essential input to the proposed trading framework. A paper summarizing the novel transactive model has been published in IEEE Transactions on Power Systems. These research activities and achievements have been reported in the interim report. With respect to the objective on short term prognosis method using practical measurement data, the team has successfully developed a novel robust spatiotemporal forecasting framework for photovoltaic generation. Distinguished from most existing methods, the new method features a novel robust spatiotemporal deep learning framework that can generate the solar PV generation forecasts for multiple regions and horizons simultaneously considering corrupted samples. The Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network is used in the new method, where the correntropy criterion is integrated to give the unbiased parameter estimation and robust spatiotemporal forecasts against possible data noises or corruptions commonly seen in practical applications. The synthetic solar PV dataset practically measured in 56 locations in U.S. has been used to verify the performance of the proposed model. This work has been recently reported in IEEE Transaction on Smart Grid.

15244316.label: Major findings and research outcome
15244316.value: It is well known that uncertainties widely exist in the time series of renewable generations or original measurement data of wind speed or solar irradiance due to the uncertain nature of renewable themselves and/or the environment noises etc. In addition, the forecasting models can also introduce additional uncertainties due to imperfect parameter estimation. To tackle many uncertainties, this project innovatively introduces the data granulation method for uncertainty modeling and quantification, which can effectively enhance the prognosis performance. Furthermore, it is found that deep learning based neural network models, though with high computational costs, can well outperform traditional neural networks in forecasting renewables that are full of uncertainties. Considering the temporal-spatial correlation of renewable resources across a geographic span, development of holistic framework dedicated for simultaneous solar generation prognosis at multiple sites can largely improve the forecasting performance. To build up proper NN based forecasting model, it is also worthy of developing novel leaning criterion to accommodate contamination noises in input time series. Besides, the research team also extends the research scope to develop a novel probiotic electricity forecasting method based on the Logistic distribution based ensemble model output statistics (EMOS) technique. With forecasted electricity prices, a novel transactive electricity trading framework for distributed generations and demands in power distribution grids is developed. Overall, the research advances and outcomes arisen from the project have been fruitful, and they have been summarized and reported in several publications in top tier journals: S. Chai, Z. Xu and Y. Jia, "Conditional Density Forecast of Electricity Price Based on Ensemble ELM and Logistic EMOS," in IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid, vol. 10, no. 3, pp. 3031-3043, May 2019 J. Li, C. Zhang, Z. Xu, J. Wang, J. Zhao and Y. A. Zhang, "Distributed transactive energy trading framework in distribution networks," in IEEE Transactions on Power Systems, vol. 33, no. 6, pp. 7215-7227, Nov. 2018. S. Chai, Z. Xu, Y. Jia and W. K. Wong, "A Robust Spatiotemporal Forecasting Framework for Photovoltaic Generation," in IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid, vol. 11, no. 6, pp. 5370-5382, Nov. 2020.

15244316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15244316.value: The project has performed in-depth studies on the prognosis of renewable energies. Due to the limited time, the focus has been on novel analyses and methods for solar prognosis by far, while extension to wind generation prognosis can be conducted in the future. It is also noticed in our research that, short prognosis of solar generation can be very much affected by local cloud conditions. Therefore, it is valuable to extend the developed forecasting methods to incorporate cloud images as input attributes to enhance the short term forecasting performance.

15244316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15244316.value: A little improvement on renewable prognosis performance can imply significant cost reeducation and security enhancement for power grid operation, which is worthy of restless research endeavors. This project deals with the renewable energy prognosis, which is an essential challenge facing further development of renewable energy. The project firstly investigates data granulation for uncertainties modeling and qualifications of renewable time series. Considering temporal-spatial correlation of renewable resources, a robust and holistic framework dedicated for simultaneous solar generation prognosis at multiple sites across a large geographic region is developed based on deep learning LSTM neural networks with novel learning criterion accommodating data noises, providing significantly enhanced forecasting performance. The outcome of the project has been fruitful and valuable, based on which further research on the renewable prognosis can be carried out in the future.
