15246816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15246816.value: In this proposal we have outlined a systematic investigation of ferroelectricity in CH3NH3PbI3 (MAPI) thin films and its impact on the photovoltaic (PV) properties of the MAPI-based PV cells. Both planar and cross-sectional ferroelectric domains will be characterized as a function of the growth technique as well as the detailed growth parameter by piezoelectric force microscopy (PFM). A unique structure will be fabricated for the cross-sectional PFM measurement in which an electrode will be fabricated to facilitate the application of a cross-electric field in-situ with the PFM measurement. This will facilitate the observation of the variation of the ferroelectric domains over the thickness of the perovskite layer. This greatly enhances our understanding of vertical transport of the carriers through the thickness of the MAPI layer and the fundamental mechanism through which the ferroelectric domains may impact on the transport properties of the carriers. Furthermore, we will investigate the incorporation of ferroelectric nano-particles such as barium titanate or strontium titanate in the MAPI layer. Alignment of the ferroelectric nano-particles using an external field will be investigated and the impact on the ferroelectric domain will be examined by detailed characterization of the cross-sectional PFM. Detailed characterization of the relationship between the device performance and the properties of the ferroelectric domains, particularly along the thickness of the MAPI layer, will be investigated. From this we hope to further elucidate on the fundamental mechanism of the photovoltaic action for the MAPI-based device. Based on this deepened knowledge of the ferroelectric properties of the MAPI material we will investigate the further enhancement of the device performance of the MAPI-based PV cells by optimizing the ferroelectric properties of the MAPI materials. 本專案計畫書概述了我們進行的CH3NH3PbI3 (MAPI)薄膜的鐵電性及其對鈣鈦礦太陽電池光伏特性影響的系統性研究。我們將根據不同的生長技術和詳細的生長參數，通過壓電力顯微鏡對平面的和截面的鐵電域進行表徵。針對介面壓電力顯微鏡測試，我們會製備一種獨特的結構，其中製備一個電極來實現截面電場應用於線上的壓電力顯微鏡測試。這將便於觀測到鐵電域隨鈣鈦礦層厚度的變化關係，從而深化我們對載流子在MAPI層中垂直輸運以及鐵電域可能對載流子輸運特性產生影響的基本機制的理解。同時，我們將研究將鐵電納米顆粒，例如鈦酸鋇或者鈦酸鍶，加入到MAPI層中。通過外部電場將鐵電納米顆粒進行對齊，通過截面壓電力顯微鏡表來表徵其對薄膜中鐵電域的影響。我們也將對器件性能與鐵電域特性的關係，尤其是在MAPI 層厚度方向上，進行詳細的測試。從中，我們希望能夠進一步闡明MAPI器件的光伏行為的基礎機制。基於對MAPI材料的鐵電特性的深入理解，我們將通過優化MAPI材料的鐵電特性參數來進一步提高MAPI太陽電池的器件性能，並開展相關研究。

15246816.label: Realisation of objectives
15246816.value: In the first half of this research program, we successfully fabricated the high-quality MAPI thin film by using hybrid chemical vapor deposition (HCVD) technique. The CH3NH3PbI3 (MAPI) layers are grown inside a furnace (adopted from traditional Si oxidation process). This is one of the key advantages of this technique as Si processing equipment are highly developed, cost-effective, supports batch processing. The process design ensures elimination of premature crystallization as the precursors are completely separated in the initial phase and, thereby, excellent uniformity in the nucleation sites is assured. It is shown that through detailed control of the thermal profile of the growth process, highly compact and uniform MAPI films can be grown. From our experimental results a carrier gas consisting of N2/O2 (85%/15%) and with a slow post-deposition cooling rate of 0.7oC/min are crucial for the reduction of both the shallow traps and the deep levels in MAPI material. Incorporation of an mp-TiO2 scaffold in the device can further improve the device performance due to further improvement in the crystallinity of the MAPI and enhancement of the carrier transport properties of the devices, leading to higher FF. With the optimized fabrication conditions and device architecture, the champion device with VOC = 1.0 V, JSC = 23.0 mA/cm2, FF= 0.77 giving a PCE of 17.6% was obtained. This work mainly covers Objective 1. Furthermore, standard materials and device characterization such as X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, I-V measurement, EQE measurements, time resolved PL for lifetime characterization etc. have been conducted to investigate the fundamental physical mechanism for high power conversion efficiency (PCE) photovoltaic cells. In particular, two unique characterization techniques (low frequency noise, photothermal deflection spectroscopy) have been introduced to elucidate the impact of material defects and their dependence on deposition conditions and post-growth treatments. Perovskite solar cell field is a fast growing, extremely dynamic research area. The switching from the original PI Prof. Charles Surya to current PI Prof. Gang Li, and the graduation of the former students represent challenge in conducting the proposed research due to the different technical strength of the team. How to make this GRF project a productive and impactful one? For this I have thought a lot and made bald decisions. For the Ferroelectricity related research in Perovskite solar cell, however, not much good news. Using electron microscopy (TEM) to study / observe ferroelectricity in perovskite was found to be very delicate due to the electron beam damage to the samples; and the ferroelectricity (once thought important for perovskite solar cell performance) was arguably not that important any more. Our own research work on the fundamental study and application of ferroelectricity in perovskite also met challenges. Last time, we found the incorporation of ferroelectric nano-particles (SrTiO3) in the MAPI bulk layer can improve device performance, but from the result of many tries in this period, we found the enhancement was only slightly, which is very hard to make conclusive decision. Aiming at productive and high impact research, we unleashed the research to not limited to ferroelectricity, but on perovskite solar cell research as a whole. Considering the new guideline, we gave up the original Objective 2 - Investigation of the dependence of the ferroelectric properties of the MAPI films on the material growth conditions and material growth techniques. With more evidence of the questionable effectiveness of ferroelectric nano-particles in perovskite, we strategically stopped at ~50% of the investigation of Objective 3 - Investigation of the impact on the ferroelectric properties of the MAPI layer due to the incorporation of ferroelectric nano-particles. This say we focused on various important research areas in perovskite solar cells to improve efficiency, printing technologies and in situ scientific understanding. We accomplished two new objectives: 6.Developing Novel electron transport layer materials for high efficiency perovskite solar cells; 7. Device engineering exploration for high efficiency PSCs. The output is great - since the midterm reports, we successfully published 20 publications, many in top notch journals including 1 Nature Photonics, 3 Advanced Materials, 1 Adv. Funct. Materials, 2 Nan Energy, 1 on Joule, 1 on Advanced Science, and 1 on Light: Science & Applications, 2 JMCA etc. In short very productive project.

15246916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15246916.value: 本研究旨在通過結合與地球同步的Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) 衛星影像，太陽同步衛星Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI的影像及HJ-1A/1B的衛星影像開發一套基於集成及智能的海岸水質遙感監測技術，藉此監測不同的水質污染物，如懸浮泥沙和葉綠素A。太陽同步衛星如Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI及HJ-1A/1B擁有高空間分辨率但低時間分辨率；AHI則能提供準實時的衛星影像及中等空間分辨率，因此水質監測和數據分析可以建基於兩種不同的衛星。本研究建議三種算法：一、一組通過地球同步衛星影像實現南中國海大範圍水質提取的遺傳編程算法（genetic programming）；二、一組通過太陽同步衛星影像實現香港地區水質提取的遺傳編程算法；三、一組結合地球同步衛星影像和太陽同步衛星影像的融合算法，達到提供高空間分辨率和高時間分辨率水質監測的效果。本研究的創新性在於研發遺傳編程算法在中國南方河口水域的應用，同時也是香港首個研究項目利用AHI高時間分辨率和高光譜分辨率的特性進行水質遙感監測。

15246916.label: Realisation of objectives
15246916.value: Primary objective 1 The primary objective along with the secondary objectives of this project has been well accomplished in approximately 90%. The development of two major tasks have been accomplished, including the evaluation of machine learning techniques for water quality retrieval at both broader regional scale and detailed local scale, and the development of a spatio-temporal adaptive image fusion algorithm to generate high temporal and spatial resolution synthetic data, using sun-synchronous satellite images and geostationary satellite images. About 3 SCI journal publications (4 more under preparation), 1 book chapter, 3 conference presentations/abstracts have been published in this study and several postgraduate students^ have been trained in this project. The research team had been working closely with the Hong Kong Environmental Protection Department (EPD) since 2017 to arrange the fieldwork for acquiring in-situ water surface reflectances. The first fieldwork was conducted on May 17, 2018, in the Sai Kung Sea area, and water surface reflectances at 13 stations were collected together with EPD water quality sampling. The second fieldwork was conducted on January 23, 2019, in the northwestern waters. Due to the social unrest in 2019 and the outbreak of COVID-19 from 2020 onwards, there was a temporary suspension of the fieldwork. Since the situation of pandemic became stable, our team has been working with EPD for onboarding their vessels of collecting the hyperspectral data. More than 300 sets of data have been collected, and the in-situ data has been used in model development. By using the collected data, the project team has studied the potential of using AHI geostationary satellite images for monitoring water quality parameters at high temporal resolution. An SCI journal manuscript has been published for assessing the potential of geostationary Himawari-8 for mapping Total Suspended Solids (TSS) and its diurnal variations. In addition, two image-based atmospheric correction methods, the NIR-SWIR method and the SWIR method were developed and tested for AHI data. Then, a new model was developed to map TSS and its diurnal variations in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) and neighbouring coastal areas. The results indicated that the SWIR method outperformed the NIR-SWIR method when compared with in-situ water-leaving reflectance data. Moreover, the diurnal variation in the turbidity front, using the Normalized Suspended Material Index (NSMI), demonstrated the capability of tracking diurnal variation in turbidity fronts, due to high TSS concentrations at high temporal frequency. For retrieving water quality parameters on local scale, different standard atmospheric correction models such as Acolite DSF, Acolite SWIR, SeaDAS, C2RCC, and iCOR have been evaluated to correct sun-synchronous Landsat-8 OLI and Sentinel-2 A/B MSI for atmospheric effects. The Acolite DSF methods outperformed all other methods when evaluated against in-situ spectral data. Moreover, prior to developing a machine learning model using multi-sensor data for high spatio-temporal coastal water quality monitoring, the spectral consistency of sensors has also been evaluated. The spectral consistency of Landsat-8 OLI and Sentinel-2 MSI data was evaluated under various atmospheric and aquatic conditions using near-simultaneous nadir overpasses (n-SNO). Different machine learning techniques (e.g., Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Gradient Boost) and empirical techniques (e.g., linear regression, and multiple linear regression) have been evaluated for combined sensor data. The ANN method outperformed all other methods for retrieving concentrations of suspended solids (SS), and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) over the coastal waters of Hong Kong. Secondary objective 1 This objective has been addressed. The results of using Fuzzy c-Means clustering have been generated from Landsat and HJ-1A/1B images with 240 in-situ samples. Results show that there are five existing optically different water types in the study area based on Fuzzy c-Means clustering. The project team has also been extending the Fuzzy c-Means clustering on the relative lower spatial but high temporal resolution geostationary (AHI) satellite images. Secondary objective 2 This objective has been addressed. The project team has tested and validated different machine learning algorithms for water quality retrieval on a detailed local scale with in-situ water quality parameters. An SCI journal manuscript is published for studying different machine learning techniques. Concentrations of suspended solids (SS), chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), and turbidity were estimated with several machine learning techniques including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), Cubist regression (CB), and Support Vector Regression (SVR). Landsat (5,7,8) reflectance data were compared with in-situ reflectance in order to evaluate the performance of different machine learning models. The highest accuracy of water quality indicators was achieved by ANN for both in-situ reflectance and satellite data. The water quality parameters retrieved by ANN model was further compared to those retrieved by the “standard Case-2 Regional/Coast Colour” (C2RCC) processing chain model C2RCC-Nets. The results indicate that NN-based machine learning approaches outperform and, thus, can be used for improving water quality monitoring using satellite data. In addition to water quality parameters retrieval, a study of Deep Learning approach, i.e., Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), has been tested to detect red tides in Hong Kong. Algal blooms were classified using a time-series of Landsat-8 OLI, Landsat-7 ETM+, Landsat-5 TM, HJ-1A/1B CCD sensors from 1987 to 2014. This preliminary study of CNN shows a promising result on the image classification of algal blooms. The CNN also shows a high capability to analyse both the spatial and spectral signatures. The results were presented and acknowledged at an international conference. The layer structure of the algorithm is now being refined by application to a range of image types and on water quality monitoring. Secondary objective 3 This objective has been accomplished in about 90%. The fusion algorithm of high spatial resolution sun-synchronous satellite images with daily moderate spatial resolution sun-synchronous satellite images has been developed. The algorithm derives a synthesized finer resolution image from a coarse spatial resolution satellite image (similar to downscaling), with the use of one fine resolution image at an arbitrary date and one coarse image at a predicted date. The developed algorithm is different from existing spatio-temporal fusion methods as other methods derive a synthesized fine resolution image at a predicted date for the fine-resolution satellite. Several satellite images, e.g., a combination of Landsat 8, Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope covering the areas of Hong Kong were evaluated and the results showed that the developed algorithm was compatible with an existing fusion algorithms, and outperformed in terms of producing lower RMSE and providing higher correlation coefficient and structural similarity (SSIM). The sun-synchronous satellite data have higher spatial resolution for monitoring coastal areas but have low temporal resolution, about 5-16 days. An integrated data fusion algorithm was developed for retrieving nearly daily fine resolution satellite images. A new three-step spatio-temporal fusion method consisting of regression model fitting, spatial filtering, and residual compensation (STR-Fit) was proposed. Several satellite images, e.g., a combination of Landsat 8/OLI, Sentinel-2/MSI and Sentinel-3/OLCI covering the areas of Hong Kong were evaluated. Results showed that STR-Fit method outperformed in terms of high values of correlation coefficient and SSIM and low RMSE. ^Two PhD and two MSc students were trained under this project.

15246916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15246916.value: This project has developed an integrated knowledge-based technique for coastal water quality monitoring using geostationary and sun-synchronous satellites images, in-situ data of water quality parameters and hyperspectral data, machine learning models, and spatio-temporal image fusion methods. The followings are the three major research achievements. At first, a new approach based on a neural network model was developed for the estimation of phytoplankton cell counts associated with algal blooms in Hong Kong using sun-synchronous satellite sensors (e.g., Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI, and HJ-1A/1B). Further, different machine learning models including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), Cubist regression (CB), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) were developed and validated for retrieving Chl-a, TSS and turbidity over the coastal waters of Hong Kong. Another machine learning technique - Gradient Boost has also been tested to study water quality retrieval in Hong Kong using Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI. In addition to water quality parameters retrieval, the project team has also mapped and retrieved the red tides in Hong Kong. It was shown that thin slicks of red tide were detected in highly turbid Pearl River Estuary using Sentinel-2 data. The thin red tide slick and red tide blooms could be detected in presence of high concentration of SS using Sentinel-2 data. Moreover, a study focusing on the Deep Learning approach, i.e. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), has been tested to detect red tides in Hong Kong. Algal blooms were classified using a time-series of Landsat-8 OLI, Landsat-7 ETM+, Landsat-5 TM, HJ-1A/1B CCD sensors from 1987 to 2014. The fusion algorithm of high spatial resolution sun-synchronous satellite images with daily moderate spatial resolution sun-synchronous satellite images has been developed. The algorithm derives a synthesized finer resolution image from a coarse spatial resolution satellite image, with the use of one fine resolution image at an arbitrary date and one coarse image at a predicted date. In addition, a new three-step spatio-temporal fusion method consisting of regression model fitting, spatial filtering, and residual compensation (STR-Fit) was developed and further compared with STARFM and SSTF. The STR-Fit method outperformed the other fusion models in terms of producing the highest R, and SSIM and lowest RMSE.

15246916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15246916.value: This project has developed an integrated knowledge-based technique focused on monitoring the coastal water quality in the Pearl River Estuary and the coastal areas of Hong Kong. The research outcomes can be applied to other geostationary and sun-synchronous satellites for coastal water quality monitoring in other sensitive coastal areas. The new generation geostationary satellite sensors dedicated for earth observation, with high spatial and temporal resolutions, i.e. Gaofen 4 launched by China, GOCI-II launched by South Korea, GEO-CAPE launched by the United States, HRGEO launched by India, and Geo-Oculus launched by European Space Agency have been or will be launched in the recent years. The operation of such geostationary satellites together with Himawari AHI can achieve continuous spatio-temporal monitoring of coastal water quality. Moreover, the research outcome can be applied to the new generation multispectral and hyperspectral sun-synchronous satellites that will be launched under NASA’s dedicated Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, Ocean Ecosystem (PACE) mission. The outcome and deliverable in this project offer a good showcase that can be applied to other geostationary and sun-synchronous satellite images.

15246916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15246916.value: Coastal waters are sensitive as these areas have strong influence and interaction with land, sea, and air. The coastal environment is under stress primarily due to high levels of pollutants from residential sewage, agriculture, industrial run-off, as well as climate change. There is a need to monitor these sensitive and vulnerable marine areas in a routine-basis. Chlorophyll-a, Total Suspended Solids and turbidity are important coastal water quality indicators, and their spatial and temporal information are crucial. Geostationary satellite and sun-synchronous satellite sensors can be used to monitor coastal water quality continuously, remotely, and timely. The new generation of geostationary satellites along with recently launched sun-synchronous satellite sensors offer more wavelengths and with a higher temporal resolution. They can observe dynamic coastal waters of the Pearl River Estuary and Hong Kong. In this study, a set of machine learning models was developed and evaluated for retrieving the water quality parameters. In addition, this study also developed a set of spatio-temporal fusion models for integrating geostationary and sun-synchronous satellite images. The integrated knowledge-based technique developed in this study also provides new research/science achievement and the technologies can be used for monitoring coastal water quality effectively and accurately.

15247116.label: Project Objectives
15247116.value: Design of the photonic chips: To develop designs of the mircoresonators and combinations of mircoresonators and nonlinear waveguides to generate coherent octavespanning optical frequency combs. We will determine the choice of material, and microresonator and waveguide geometries such that the proposed designs can be fabricated in a CMOS compatible platform. The coupling between the photonic devices will also be studied. Modeling of the performance of the mircoresonators and nonlinear waveguides: The properties of the microresonators as a femtosecond optical pulse source, and nonlinear waveguides for spectral broadening will be investigated using the appropriate theoretical and modeling tools which include the finite-difference-time-domain (FDTD) method, coupled-mode equations, generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and short pulse equations.

15247116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15247116.value: 為了“提高全球對光學技術促進可持續發展和解決能源、教育、文化和健康等全球性難題的關注”，聯合國特別指定2015年為“國際光與光學技術年(IYL 2015)”。雖然國際光與光學技術年可能並不為行業之外的普通民眾所熟知，但不可否認，在歷史長河中，光學和光子學的技術發展為人類社會帶來了翻天覆地的變化。望遠鏡、顯微鏡、電燈以及光纖的發明，已經從根本上改變了人類認識和理解世界的方法，徹底改變了人們的生活和溝通方式。相干超倍頻程的光學頻率梳是光子學領域一項最新的技術突破。光頻梳是頻域上由一系列等間距的超窄頻譜線構成的梳狀光譜。基於這種梳狀光譜製作的光學原子鐘，比之前最好的原子鐘還要精准一百倍。光頻梳為計量學、光學原子鐘和精細光譜學等領域帶來一次新的技術革命。在光頻梳技術中，最關鍵的是產生一個超過三分之二倍頻程以上的超寬光譜，從而能夠通過載頻包絡相位(CEP)穩定技術極大地消除脈衝序列的噪聲。 相干超倍頻程的光學頻率梳，可以通過在超短脈衝鎖模激光器產生數個週期的光脈衝獲得，也可以在非線性介質中展寬100飛秒以下的超短脈衝的光譜來獲得。對環境敏感的飛秒激光光源的依賴，限制了光頻梳在實驗室之外的應用。2015年，研究人員已經在微環和光學納米線中產生超過三分之二倍頻程的相干光頻梳。這些集成光子器件的製作是和CMOS技術相容的，這使得其低成本批量生產成為可能。最新的研究方向集中在通過一個單一的光子器件，如微環或者非線性波導來獲得超寬相干光頻梳。在本項目中，研究組將設計、分析和製作一種複合型的光子晶片。此晶片基於微環和非線性光波導，可以在近紅外到中紅外波段產生相干超倍頻程的光學頻率梳。我們將優化微環的設計來產生飛秒脈衝，而光波導將通過針對性的優化設計，基於自相似脈衝壓縮或超連續譜的產生來展寬光譜。在微環和非線性波導中，我們還將採用色散、非線性等物理參數單調和/或週期性變化的波導來控制脈衝的演化。優化的設計方案將在實驗上進行製作和測試。

15247116.label: Realisation of objectives
15247116.value: Both Objectives 1 and 2 are achieved. The following are brief discussions of the achievement and the research output. We proposed and theoretically demonstrated a suspended Ge-membrane ridge waveguide to generate octave-spanning mid infrared supercontinuum (SC) that extends deeply into the “fingerprint” region. The primary light-guiding region of the Ge channel is suspended above the Si substrate with an air gap layer so that light cannot leak into the Si substrate even at wavelength of 12 μm. The waveguide dimension is carefully designed to obtain the expected dispersion and nonlinear characteristics. The SC and SC-based frequency comb generation in the proposed waveguide are numerically studied with a full model which includes the contributions of high-order nonlinear susceptibility (χ(5)), nonlinear absorption, and Raman scattering. (Journal Output Item 2 in Part C). Kerr soliton frequency comb generation in monolithic microresonators enables chip-scale few-cycle pulse generation at microwave rates with smooth octave-spanning spectra for self-referencing. However, it still remains challenging to straightforwardly and deterministically generate and sustain the single-soliton state in microresonators. We propose to directly and deterministically generate single-soliton Kerr comb in a continuous-wave pumped microring resonator by seeding it with a pulsed trigger. Single cavity soliton can be straightforwardly and deterministically triggered by an energetic single shot pulse without going through any multi-stable or chaotic states in the nonlinear microcavity. The feasibility of single shot trigger approach makes it possible to manipulate the number of solitons and their temporal locations inside the cavity by simply controlling the power and temporal location of the single pulse trigger. The proposed trigger approach can be applied to different type of microresonators as long as the microresonators do support cavity solitons. Moreover, we find that even under strong thermal effect the proposed trigger approach is valid to excite single cavity solitons in practically fabricated Si_3N_4 microresonators. No additional complex engineering is required for thermal compensation. (Journal Output Item 3 in Part C). We also numerically demonstrate efficient spectral compression (SPC) of wavelength-shifting soliton in a chalcogenide strip waveguide. It is found that the profiles of group-velocity dispersion (GVD) and Kerr nonlinearity play key roles in determining SPC. After calculating the dispersion of Kerr nonlinearity and Raman spectrum for three kinds of chalcogenide materials, Ge_11.5As_24Se_64.5 is chosen as the material for designing the chalcogenide strip waveguide (CSW). The geometric parameters of CSW are optimized to obtain the desired GVD and Kerr nonlinearity. Simulation results show that in the designed CSW, an input spectrum width of 52.04 nm can be compressed to 7.23 nm along with wavelength shift of 17 nm when the input peak power is 25 W. With the input peak power increasing to 75 W, the SPC is slightly weakened, but wavelength shift can be up to 190 nm. The proposed CSW is applied to integrated all-optical quantization and an effective quantization number of 3.66-bit is achieved. It is expected that our research results can find important applications in on-chip integrated spectroscopy, all-optical signal processing, etc. (Journal Output Item 4 in Part C). We propose an adiabatically suspended silicon waveguide taper to achieve the SPC at the mid-infrared spectral region. The silicon waveguide taper is designed with a dispersion increasing profile along z. With the designed waveguide taper, the optical spectrum of the chirp-free femtosecond pulse is efficiently compressed. The SCF can be up to 10.9, along with the brightness-enhanced factor (BEF) of 8.0 and negligible sidelobe after the 6-cm propagation. By considering the impacts of the HOD, HON, losses (including linear and nonlinear loss), and variation of γ(z) on the SPC, it is found that variation of γ(z) and linear loss are the dominant perturbation to the degradation of the SPC performance. It is believed that the proposed SPC scheme paves the way for obtaining the integrated mid-infrared light sources with narrow spectral width, which can find important applications in developing the on-chip optoelectronic devices and systems. (Journal Output Item 5 in Part C). Frequency comb swept lasers are the enabling technology of circular interferometric imaging, which was proposed to break the bottleneck of data acquisition and processing in optical coherence tomography (OCT) at video rate. We propose and demonstrate a highly coherent frequency comb swept laser by using a high-quality (high-Q) microring comb filter to discretize a Fourier-domain mode-locked (FDML) laser. The microring filter has a Q factor of ∼2 × 10^6 and a linewidth of ∼90 MHz. To demonstrate the improvement in performance, a Fabry–Pérot comb filter with a Q factor of 6.2 × 10^4 and a linewidth of 3.1 GHz is also used in the experiment for comparison. Both comb filters have free spectral ranges (FSRs) of ∼50 GHz for consistence. Stable and clearly discretized temporal waveforms and frequency comb spectra with 50 GHz FSR are observed. Adoption of the high-Q microring filter narrows the instantaneous linewidth of the FDML laser down to 1.5 GHz. The OCT system with the frequency comb swept laser source with a microring filter demonstrates an ultralong imaging range, which has a 6, 10, and 15 dB sensitivity roll-off length of ∼53, ∼73, and over 100 mm, respectively. (Journal Output Item 10 in Part C). We also demonstrate a reconfigurable swept source for OCT by time stretching of a broadband femtosecond pulse train in a CFBG and DCFs. The femtosecond pulse train is generated from an amplified mode-locked fiber laser with a repetition rate of 100 MHz. The output spectrum has a “top-hat” profile with a 1- and 10-dB bandwidth of 73.7 and 102.4 nm, respectively. In the dispersive elements, the femtosecond pulse trains are stretched into long swept pulses. The 100 nm sweep range is comparable to conventional swept lasers with SOA such as FDML lasers, but the sweep rate is increased by 3 orders of magnitude. By incorporating a frequency divider, the sweep rate can be reconfigured in the range of 2.5–100 MHz. By using a long CFBG as the dispersion element, a sharp edge swept signal with 100 MHz sweep rate, 49.7 nm sweep range, and 83% duty cycle is obtained. The swept signal demonstrates a sensitivity roll-off length of 5.7 mm and an axial resolution of 36 μm in the OCT characterization. When the sweep rate of the swept source is reduced by the frequency divider, the sensitivity roll-off length is further increased. When the sweep rate is decreased to 2.5 MHz and a section of DCF with 200 km nominal compensation length is used, the 6 dB sensitivity roll-off length is boosted to 111 mm. It is the first time that the 6-dB sensitivity roll-off length of megahertz Swept Source OCT (SS-OCT) is enhanced to more than 100 mm. Besides the application in SS-OCT to enhance the imaging performance, such a flexible highly coherent ultrafast swept source could also be adopted in detection applications such as LiDAR. (Journal Output Item 8 in Part C). Please note that Journal Output Items 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 are co-authored by Dr. Jinhui Yuan who served in the project as Research Fellow for 16 months from 25 Apr 2017 to 24 Aug 2018. The PI is not one of the co-authors in these publications as even though he initiated and guided the research work, he did not consider his intellectual contribution is sufficient to warrant co-authorship in the publications.

15247116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15247116.value: The current project barely scratches the surface in the research on the on-chip generation of coherent octave-spanning frequency combs in the near- to mid-infrared wavelength band. Because of the cut in the research funding from the requested amount of the original proposal, most of the research work done in this project focused on the first two objectives, i.e., the design of the photonic chips and the modeling of the performance of the mircoresonators and nonlinear waveguides. The third objective in the original proposal on the fabrication and characterization of the designs of the microresonators, waveguides, and photonic chips were largely not carried out. Thus, the obvious next step on further development is to pursue the third objective on the results obtained in this project. Furthermore, alternate and more sophisticated designs of the mircoresonators, multi-microresonators, nonlinear waveguides, and combinations of mircoresonators and nonlinear waveguides to generate coherent octave-spanning optical frequency combs should also be investigated. The material used, microresonator and waveguide geometries should be chosen such that the proposed designs can be fabricated in a CMOS compatible platform. Fabrication and characterization of these new designed should then carried out.

15247116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15247116.value: Optical frequency combs consist of equally spaced sharp lines in the frequency domain which can be utilized to construct optical atomic clocks a hundred times more accurate than the best atomic clocks today. Frequency combs will revolutionize many fields including metrology, optical atomic clocks, and high precision spectroscopy. Coherent octave-spanning optical frequency combs can be generated by using few-cycle mode-locked lasers, by broadening the spectra of sub-100 femtosecond pulses in a highly nonlinear medium, from a microresonator, or photonic nanowires. In this project, we designed, analyzed, and experimented on mock-locked lasers, nonlinear waveguides, and microresonators for coherent octave-spanning frequency comb generation. Some of the key results achieved in this project are: We proposed and demonstrated direct and deterministic generation of single-soliton Kerr comb in a continuous-wave pumped microring resonator by seeding it with a pulsed trigger. We designed a simple inversely tapered silicon ridge waveguide with exponentially decreasing dispersion profile along the propagation direction, and numerically investigate self-similar pulse compression of the fundamental soliton within the mid-infrared spectral region. We also experimentally demonstrated a reconfigurable swept source for Optical Coherence Tomography by time stretching of a broadband femtosecond pulse train in a chirped fiber Bragg gratings and dispersion compensation fibers.

15247816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15247816.value: Microscopy is a universal tool that has given scientists new insights into material science and biology. Despite the spectacular success of microscopy techniques, there are still many challenges. One area we have pioneered is application of the so-called confocal microscope for measurement of surface plasmons. Surface plasmons are waves that are excited on a metal surface, the properties of these waves are highly sensitive to the local environment to measure binding of small molecules for disease diagnosis and drug discovery. Conventional methods for the measurement of surface plasmons have poor spatial resolution so measurement must be performed over a large area. The confocal arrangement overcomes this problem by only detecting waves that have travelled over a well-defined path. Contolling the field in the back focal plane using a commercial device, a phase spatial light modulator, allows one to perform functions not normally associated with a confocal microscope such as measurement of phase with a local interferometer, elimination of the effect external vibrations and signal enhancement. Despite this the confocal arrangement is essentially a point scanning system because the detected light is collected in a pinhole to ensure that its path is well defined. One can use many pinholes simultaneously but if they are placed too close together the light from one pinhole will leak into another and the advantages of the confocal arrangement are lost. An idea borrowed from communications has been used to overcome this problem, essentially by using a code at each point, signals are only detected if they have a matching code, signals leaking from the ‘wrong’ region are eliminated. These two ideas can be combined in a uniquely powerful way to develop a surface wave microscope capable of measuring many points simultaneously, which is very important for the diagnosis of many disease types where a single marker does not give unambiguous information. The parallel arrangement has another major advantage allowing one to eliminate the effect of temperature variations with a reference channel. The novel microscope concept is extremely versatile and we propose a new microscope for cellular imaging. We will demonstrate how the spatial light modulator allows us to produce effectively parallel microscopes for visualizing processes at the cell surface and also image within the body of the cell simultaneously. Overall, we believe we are providing a new imaging format of exceptional versatility and power for both measurement and imaging at the cellular and sub-cellular level.

15247816.label: Realisation of objectives
15247816.value: The objectives of the project: 1. To develop parallel confocal system with advanced processing in the back focal plane and temporal encoding for parallel operation. The objective is fully achieved. The hardware and software construction work was completed. A journal paper [1] was published to report the details of the constructed system. Since the paper was submitted before the current PI took over the project (due to the departure of the original PI), the current PI is not on the author list of that paper. Besides, the project team would like to apologize that the paper has not acknowledged the funding source. The original PI was busy settling down in his new working place when submitting this paper. He forgot to add the acknowledgement statement to the paper. 2. Demonstrate application of system for parallel surface plasmon imaging at multiple points (>1000) The objective is fully achieved. We have demonstrated and shown the experimental results by measuring 64x64 points. A journal paper [1] was published to report the details of the experiment. 3. Estimate sensitivity in terms of minimum number of detectable molecules, optimize system by (i) elimination of microphonics (ii) using supplementary data in image plane and (iii) temperature compensation. The objective is fully achieved. We have found that system stability is an issue in the system. One of the major reasons is the long data acquisition time. To solve the problem, we develop a method that allows single-shot surface plasmon (SP) measurement by projecting an image of the field excited from a defocused sample to a magnified image plane. This has the advantage over previous techniques in that the data can be obtained in a single shot without any changes to the focal position of the sample. It significantly speeds up the data acquisition time and reduces the problem of system stability. A journal paper [2] was published to report the details of the proposed method and the experimental result. 4. Show how system platform can use used for other microscopy methods combining total internal reflection and confocal imaging The objective is largely achieved. We tried to incorporate the coded diffraction pattern (CDP) phase retrieval method in the system platform for recovering the complex back focal plane (BFP). Although the proposed Hadamard coding method can reduce the main interference from the neighbor sample points, some residual interference due to the nonlinear terms in the intensity measurement process can still introduce the instability problem to the system. The problem can be solved if the complex BFP can be recovered through a phase retrieval process. The CDP phase retrieval method is particularly appealing in this case since the added optical masks provide an additional constraint to reduce the number of measurements, which in turn shortens the data acquisition time. However, we found that the traditional CDP phase retrieval approaches often focus on the randomness of the optical masks without considering their non-bandlimited nature. It introduces a lot of high-frequency data to the measurements that the system cannot take care of. In this research, we propose a green noise binary masking scheme for CDP phase retrieval that can significantly reduce the high-frequency contents of the masks while fulfilling the randomness requirement. It thus significantly improves the quality of the recovered phase images. A journal paper [3] was published to report the details of the proposed method. The work was also accepted to be presented at an international conference [4]. The method is yet to integrate into the SP measurement platform. Since the integration is straightforward, we expect a fruitful result can be achieved. 5. Demonstrate system developed for objective 4 for simultaneous evanescent imaging of cell membrane and cytoplasm. Due to the pandemic, the investigation team could not go back to the Mainland to discuss with the research partner the preparation of the required testing samples. The work for this objective could not be restarted as of the time this report is prepared. We hope that with the relaxation of the travel restriction between Hong Kong and the Mainland, we can restart this part of the work in the near future. 6. Show adaptation of the new microscope platform for widefield tunable interferometry with controllable depth. This objective is partly achieved. We have developed a new moving fringe structured light illumination microscopy system that allows measuring the depth with improved axial resolution compared with the traditional approaches. The improvement factor is not a function of the imaging optics bandwidth but depends on the structured illumination only. A paper is drafted and will be submitted for publication in the coming one or two months [5]. We are considering integrating the method into the proposed SP platform to control the depth of the measurement.

15247816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15247816.value: Optical surface waves are guided light on the surface of optical structures. They have proven themselves promising candidates for several applications including, biosensing, optical computing, and optical circuitry. One limitation of the existing systems is they can only perform single-point detection, which in turn leads to a very long detection time. For the first part of this research, we developed a modified confocal microscope integrated with a phase spatial light modulator that allows us to measure the surface wave k-vector simultaneously at multiple points. The proposed system achieves multiple-point detection by integrating another amplitude spatial light modulator in the image plane of the objective lens. We then use the orthogonal illumination patterns to allow the image plane to be sequentially amplitude modulated and post-processed to recover the confocal image. Both the optical hardware and software systems were constructed to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method. A journal paper [1] was published to report the details of the constructed system and the experimental results. One of the major limitations of the proposed multiple-point detection system is its long data acquisition time. To solve the problem, we develop a method that allows single-shot surface plasmon (SP) measurement by projecting an image of the field excited from a defocused sample to a magnified image plane. This has the advantage over previous techniques in that the data can be obtained in a single shot without any changes to the focal position of the sample. It significantly speeds up the data acquisition time and reduces the problem of system stability. A journal paper [2] was published to report the details of the proposed method and the experimental result. To reduce the residual interference from the neighboring detection points, we studied the application of the coded diffraction pattern (CDP) phase retrieval method. The traditional CDP phase retrieval approaches often focus on the randomness of the optical masks without considering their non-bandlimited nature. It introduces a lot of high-frequency data to the measurements that the system cannot take care of. In this research, we propose a green noise binary masking scheme for CDP phase retrieval that can significantly reduce the high-frequency contents of the masks while fulfilling the randomness requirement. It thus improves the quality of the recovered phase images. A journal paper [3] was published to report the details of the proposed method. The work was also accepted to be presented at an international conference [4].

15247816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15247816.value: In this project, a confocal microscope that allows multiple-point surface wave k-vector detection is developed. While the prototype was built and satisfactory results were obtained, there is still room for further improvement. The interference from the neighbor points is still the major cause of the instability in the system. Originally, the use of the Hadamard orthogonal codes is to remove the interference. Since only the amplitude of the BFP can be captured but not its phase, the Hadamard code sequence cannot let the interference be fully canceled out in the post-processing. Rather, some residual interference still exists and affects the system stability. We suggest in this research to use the CDP phase retrieval method to solve the problem. However, it requires introducing another SLM to implement the optical mask which further increases the cost of the system. Recently, we developed a learning-based phase retrieval method such that the phase information of a signal can be recovered by an end-to-end deep neural network without the need for an optical mask. We believe such an approach can also be applied to recover the complex BFP. It is an important extension to the current project to bridge the gap for practical implementation.

15249216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15249216.value: This project proposes the use of high strength steel concrete-filled steel tubular (CFST) column with octagonal shape. This component involves in-filling normal and high strength concrete inside a pre-fabricated octagonal normal and high strength steel tube to form the composite member. The application of traditional concrete-filled steel tubular column has shown to offer fast-track construction as it eliminates the need of temporary formwork for concrete-casting as well as promoting the use pre-fabricated connection units which can be shop-welded on the outer skin of the steel tube. This minimises the on-site labour welding activities. This system has also shown to improve strength, stiffness and ductility by comparing to their reinforced concrete or bare steel counterparts. It is attributed by the fact that the outer steel tube prevents or delays lateral expansion and failure of the concrete core, which in turn mitigates inward buckling of the steel hollow section. The enhanced strength and stiffness encourage the use of smaller column size which improves the usable floor area as well as the working space for workers during construction. Traditional rectangular hollow section can provide flat surfaces to connect incoming members but cannot effectively confine the concrete core. On the contrary, circular hollow section can confine the concrete core effectively but the incoming members may need to have profiled end treatment in order to connect to the curved surface. Therefore, this project propose to use octagonal shaped CFST column which can combine the merits of both rectangular and circular counterparts. This project also proposes firstly to examine the composite effect between the normal strength steel and concrete in this special shape which is within the design remit of the current Eurocode 4 for composite construction and secondly examine high strength steel and concrete materials which advances the current understanding on the composite action on these high strength partners. Both experimental and numerical investigation will be conducted to investigate the structural performance of high strength steel-concrete composite octagonal shaped column under concentric and eccentric compression at cross-section level. 這個研究項目旨在研究八邊形截面的高強鋼管混凝土柱，包括向預製的八邊形普通和高強鋼管中填充普通混凝土和高強混凝土來形成組合構件。傳統鋼管混凝土的應用已經展示了其在建築上的優點：由於澆築混凝土不需要臨時的模板而加快建築進度；可以推廣使用在工廠加工的預製連接節點，減少了在工地的焊接工作量。同時，跟傳統的鋼筋混凝土或者純鋼構件相比，鋼管混凝土也提高了構件的強度，剛度以及延性。這是由於外側的鋼管阻止或延緩了核心混凝土的側向膨脹和破壞，反過來混凝土減緩了鋼管的向內屈曲。強度和剛度的增強可以減小構件的截面面積，提高建築的使用面積以及建設時的工作面。傳統的矩形截面有平面可以方便連接，但是不能有效的約束核心混凝土。相反，圓截面可以有效的約束核心混凝土，但是曲面在連接時需要額外的處理。因此，這個項目旨在研究八邊形截面的高強鋼管混凝土柱，它結合了矩形柱和圓形柱的優點。這個項目首先研究了在歐標4的設計規範下普通強度的八邊形鋼混組合結構的組合效應，然後研究高強鋼材和混凝土的性能來提升對高強材料組合性能的認識。本項目將通過試驗和數值方法來研究八邊形截面的剛混組合結構在軸心受壓和偏心受壓情況下的力學性能。

15249216.label: Realisation of objectives
15249216.value: Objective 1 has been achieved through the following comprehensive investigations. I-S460 steel: The residual stress distributions in fabricated octagonal shaped S460 steel hollow sections have been investigated experimentally in this project. Two fabrication routes involving combined press-braking and welding were considered. The magnitudes and distributions of longitudinal residual stresses from different fabrication routes were examined. The maximum membrane and bending residual stresses were found to be up to 62% and 39% of the material yield strength. In terms of bending residual stresses, magnitudes in the flat regions were relatively low while magnitudes at the corners were much higher due to the cold-formed process. As for the membrane residual stresses, magnitudes near the welding seam were greatly larger than other locations. It was also noted that octagonal shaped steel hollow sections fabricated from different routes exhibited different distributions and magnitudes of residual stresses. Simplified predictive models for the distributions of residual stresses in fabricated octagonal shaped S460 steel hollow sections due to cold-forming and welding were proposed as well based on the test results. II-S690 steel: Furthermore, the residual stress distribution in octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections from three fabrication routes have been investigated experimentally. The distribution and magnitude of longitudinal residual stresses from different fabrication routes were determined using the sectioning method. It was found that both membrane and bending residual stresses existed in the octagonal hollow sections and their magnitudes were determined and plotted. The results showed that the residual stress distribution and magnitudes of the section formed through welding are quite different from those of the sections formed using both press-braking and welding. For the section formed by welding eight steel plates, the membrane residual stresses ranged from 13% to 58% of the 0.2% proof stress of the material while the bending residual stresses were below 7.5% of the material 0.2% proof stress. As for the sections formed by combined press-braking and welding processes, the bending residual stresses in the flat regions were relatively low while the bending residual stresses at the corners which were subject to large plastic deformation during fabrication were quite large and found to be up to 27% of the 0.2% proof stress of the material at corners. The membrane residual stresses in these sections varied between 0.2 and 45% of the material 0.2% proof stress. Residual stress models for the octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections formed from different fabrication routes were also proposed based on the experimental results. Similarly, objectives 2 and 3 have been achieved through the following comprehensive investigations. I-S460 steel and C90/105 concrete: An experimental investigation into effect of concrete infill on the compressive behavior of compact to slender fabricated octagonal shaped S460 steel hollow sections has been conducted. Stub column specimens with different cross section slenderness (from compact to slender) were used. Three grades of concrete with target concrete cylinder strength of 30, 50 and 90 MPa were used to infill the hollow tubes. The stub column test results together with measured geometric properties have been measured in detail. Experimental results indicate that the material strengths of both steel and concrete in the short columns can be fully utilized. The strength index (SI) of all the specimens is greater than unity and SI generally increases with the increase of confinement ratio. The test results were then compared with the strength predictions calculated from EN 1994-1-1, ANSI/AISC 360-16, GB 50936-2014 and the equivalent circle methods. Overall, it has been found that Method 1 in Eurocode EN 1994-1-1 and ANSI/AISC 360-16 safely but conservatively calculate the cross-sectional strength, while Method 2 overpredicts the strength due to overestimation of confinement. The circumcircle method and GB 50936-2014 give excellent cross-sectional strength predictions. The current slenderness limit specified for circular concrete filled steel tubes in GB 50936-2014 can be safely extended to the design of high strength concrete filled octagonal shaped S460 steel hollow sections if the circumcircle method and GB 50936-2014 are used. II-S690 steel and C90/105 concrete: Behaviour of concrete-filled octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections stub columns under axial compression was investigated in this study through experiments and numerical simulations. Three octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections stub columns specimens and twelve concrete-filled octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections stub columns specimens with varying plate width-to-thickness ratios were tested. The test results of ultimate loads, load versus end-shortening and failure modes are reported. In addition to the experimental investigation, numerical modelling was performed on the concrete-filled octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections stub columns with various plate width-to-thickness ratios and cylinder compressive strengths for concrete infill using the validated FE model. The numerical modelling shows that the strength enhancement is higher for the stub columns with relatively lower cross-section slenderness parameter and concrete compressive cylinder strength. The obtained results from stub column tests and parametric studies were employed to evaluate the applicability of existing design approaches for cross-sectional resistance in European and American standards and that proposed by other researchers. Based on the approach in Eurocode 4 for circular concrete-filled steel tubular structures and the approach from other researchers, the ultimate loads were overestimated by 18-28%. The evaluation shows that conservative strength predictions on average were obtained based on the design approach for rectangular concrete-filled steel tubular structures in Eurocode 4, approaches in AISC 360 and the approach from other researchers. Although conservative strength predictions were obtained based on these approaches, the approaches take the strength from steel tubes as the plastic resistance which was found to be higher than the strength from steel tubes estimated in parametric studies for the concrete-filled octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections stub columns. An approach describing the strength contributed from steel tube and concrete infill was proposed and can be applied to obtain more accurate and less scattered strength predictions for the concrete-filled octagonal shaped S690 steel hollow sections stub columns in structural design.

15249216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15249216.value: Fabricated octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow sections from different fabrication routes, including welding and press-braking, were examined. Effect of welding and press-braking on the material properties were also investigated. Material models with due considerations on strength enhancements for fabricated octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow sections were proposed. A comprehensive experimental program was conducted to measure residual stresses to evaluate both the distributions and magnitudes of them. It was noted that octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow sections fabricated from different routes exhibited different distributions and magnitudes of residual stresses. Simplified residual stress patterns for fabricated octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow section due to cold forming and welding are proposed. Detailed findings are summarized in Junbo et al. (2020, Part C) and Fang et al. (2018, Part C). Experimental and numerical investigations were conducted on concrete-filled octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow section stub column specimens. A range of cross-sectional slenderness parameters and grades of concrete were carefully selected to examine their effect on the structural behavior. Experimental and numerical data including, load-deformation histories and failure modes were reported. Existing design approaches in European codes, North American standards and the equivalent diameter approach in relation to circular concrete-filled steel hollow sections were discussed and assessed against structural performance data. Based on the structural performance date, design provisions for the design of C90/105 concrete-filled octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow section stub columns are proposed. Detailed findings are summarized in Junbo and Chan (under review, Part C) and Han et al. (under review, Part C).

15249216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15249216.value: This research focuses on the cross-sectional behavior of C90/105 concrete-filled octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow section stub columns. There is a potential to further develop and investigate the member behavior of such high strength composite member. The future development can focus on characterizing the member behavior of C90/105 concrete-filled octagonal shaped S460 and S690 steel hollow section long columns. The corresponding design provisions can be further developed based on experimental and numerical investigations. To complement the reported research, member specimens can be formed by using high strength steel plates in the grade of S690 and high strength concrete with nominal compressive cylinder strength of 60 MPa and 90 MPa. Octagonal shaped steel hollow sections can be fabricated by cold-forming steel plates into half-sections and subsequently welding half-sections together to form the target shapes. Concrete-filled steel tubular columns will then be formed by in-filling high strength concrete. Such tubular long columns provide the flexibility for the architects and engineers to employ octagonal shape to suit a variety of design and engineering purposes. This future development has the potential to further contribute and facilitate the applications of high strength concrete-filled octagonal shaped steel hollow section columns in construction.

15249216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15249216.value: This project proposes the use of high strength steel concrete-filled steel tubular (CFST) column with octagonal shape. This component involves in-filling high strength concrete inside a pre-fabricated octagonal high strength steel tube to form the composite member. The application of traditional concrete-filled steel tubular column has shown to offer fast-track construction as it eliminates the need of temporary formwork for concrete-casting as well as on-site labour welding activities. This system has also shown to improve strength, stiffness and ductility by comparing to their reinforced concrete or bare steel counterparts. Traditional rectangular hollow section can provide flat surfaces to connect incoming members but cannot effectively confine the concrete core. On the contrary, circular hollow section can confine the concrete core effectively but the incoming members may need to have profiled end treatment in order to connect to the curved surface. Therefore, this project, through comprehensive experimental and numerical investigations, has advocated the use high strength octagonal shaped CFST column which can combine the merits of both rectangular and circular counterparts, in construction.

15249316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15249316.value: Cataract is clouding of the lens of an eye that prevents a clear vision. The only effective treatment for cataract is surgery, by which the cloudy lens is removed and replaced with a clear artificial lens. Nowadays most cataract surgeries are performed with phacoemulsification. Although the surgery is generally successful, complications and operative problems are not uncommon. In particular, the intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) may occur during the cataract extraction, which can cause not only inadequate pupil dilatation that obstructs the surgeon’s view and compromises the surgical outcome, but also damage of the iris tissue via unintentional aspiration of the phacoemulsification probe. Various clinical studies have revealed the cause of IFIS. That is, a medication called tamsulosin may result in relaxation of the iris dilator muscle, affecting iris dilatation and leading to IFIS during cataract extraction. From the mechanics point of view, the relaxation of the iris dilator muscle significantly changes the mechanical properties of the iris. Under this condition, the phacoemulsification-probe generated high-pressure, fast irrigation/aspiration flow injected into/removed from the anterior chamber, as well as the ultrasonic pressure waves and the associated acoustic streaming may jointly result in an unstable and floppy iris during the surgery. To confirm this, the proposed research will explore the physical mechanism of IFIS and develop novel paradigms of phacoemulsification dynamics to avoid IFIS and consequent surgical morbidity. State-of-the-art numerical and experimental models for cataract surgery will be developed. By investigating the roles of the flow phenomena induced by the phacoemulsification probe using these models, the key elements that aggravate floppiness of the iris will be identified. Furthermore, the use of fluidic control for the IFIS mitigation will be explored. Finally, based on the findings from these investigations, alternative surgical protocols to mitigate IFIS will be proposed. Through this research, we will demonstrate the major role of mechanics in causing IFIS and elucidating how modifications to machine parameters and applications of fluidic control can minimise and possibly eliminate IFIS. The outcome of this research will influence existing surgical protocols for cataract removal. Since cataract contributes to 33% of visual impairment, and is the No. 1 cause of blindness worldwide, the longer-term impact of this project will be far-reaching. 白內障是一種眼睛晶狀體發生渾濁的疾病，會嚴重影響視力甚至導致失明。手術是治療白內障唯一有效的方法：摘除已渾濁的晶狀體并植入透明人工晶狀體。目前大部分的白內障手術採用超聲乳化方法，儘管手術成功率比較高，但併發症和術中問題并不罕見。尤其是在白內障去除過程中發生的虹膜鬆弛綜合症（IFIS），不僅會造已散大的瞳孔縮小，遮擋手術視野而影響手術效果，而且會在超聲乳化探頭的灌注過程中不小心破壞虹膜組織。多項醫療研究已經揭示了產生IFIS的原因：一種叫坦洛辛（tamsulosin）的藥物可能會導致虹膜瞳孔開大肌的鬆弛，從而導致IFIS的發生。從力學角度來看，虹膜瞳孔開大肌的鬆弛會顯著改變虹膜的力學屬性，使得由超聲乳化探頭產生的高壓、出入前房的高速灌注流動和超聲壓力波及其誘導出的聲流在手術中共同作用導致虹膜的失穩和鬆弛。為了驗證該力學假設，我們將通過本項目探索IFIS的物理機理并提出新的超聲乳化方法來避免IFIS的發生。在本項目中，我們將會建立幾個最先進的白內障手術模型，并使用這些模型研究由超聲乳化探頭引起的各種流動現象以確定導致虹膜鬆弛的關鍵力學因素。同時，我們也將會第一次探索使用流體控制來抑制IFIS。最後，基於本項目的發現，我們將會提出抑制IFIS的新手術方案。通過本項目，我們將會揭示IFIS發生的物理機理，并闡明如何通過調整儀器參數和使用流體控制來抑制或消除IFIS。本項目的研究結果將會對現有的白內障手術產生影響。由於白內障是全球第一致盲原因并占所有視力損傷的33%，本項目的成功對社會的長期影響將會是深遠的。

15249316.label: Realisation of objectives
15249316.value: 1. To develop state-of-the-art models for cataract surgery (100% achieved) We have successfully developed the planned Mathematical Model A and Model B. Model A is a two dimensional fluid-structure interaction (FSI) model to mimic a simplified version of cataract surgery. This model includes two flexible, clamped-free beams that represent the iris. The flow induced by the torsional oscillation of the phaco-probe is represented by a time-dependent velocity boundary condition that varies with a frequency close to that in actual surgery. However, due to the ultrasonic frequency at which the phaco-probe is operated in the longitudinal oscillation mode, the induced flow is simulated as a constant jet according acoustic streaming theories. In addition, the irrigation and aspiration flows of the phaco probe are also considered and modeled as velocity boundaries on specific surfaces of the probe. Model B is a more complex model, which adopts three-dimensional geometries for both the eye and the phaco-probe. In this model, the iris is modeled as an annulus with its outer edge clamped and inner edge free, and the probe is modeled as a small circular cylinder orientated with certain pitching and rolling angles. The flows induced by the probe are modeled in the same way as in Model A. In both the mathematical models, the fluid dynamics is simulated using the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), the structure dynamics is simulated using the finite element method (FEM), and the coupling of the fluid and the structure is realized using the immersed boundary method (IBM). To speed up the simulations, the developed mathematical models were further parallelized on Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) platforms. Compared to simulations run on a single CPU, the current GPU parallelization achieved a cheerful speed-up ratio of up to 82. These two models have been well validated in various studies presented in the listed publications. 2. To pin down the key elements that aggravate floppiness of the iris through identifying the roles played by the phaco-probe generated irrigation/aspiration flows, as well as by the ultrasonic pressure waves and the resulting acoustic streaming (100% achieved) Using the established mathematical models, we are able to capture and analyze the response of the modeled iris to the phaco-probe-induced fluid loads under various operation conditions. With the simulation results, we identified three distinct dynamics modes for iris, i.e., the repulsion (RP) mode where the iris is repelled by the probe, the attraction (AT) mode where the iris is drawn toward the probe, and the adhesion (AH) mode where the iris is adhered to the probe at some point. The occurrence of these dynamics modes depends on many factors, including the location, orientation, power and frequency of the probe as well as the size and material properties of the modeled iris. To reveal the effects of these factors, a systematic parametric study has been conducted. The influence of the irrigation/aspiration (I/A) flow was also studied. With two different types of phaco probes, i.e. the coaxial and bimanual probes, it is found that the I/A induced flow plays a dominant role in the iris dynamics. It expands the dangerous AH mode zone, and hence increases the iris damage risk. Reducing the I/A strength can help stabilize the iris dynamics and relieve the IFIS risks. In addition, the comparison between the coaxial and bimanual operation patterns reveals that the coaxial probe seems more suitable for cataract surgery in terms of alleviating the risks of iris tissue damage but at the expense of reduction in the nucleus removal efficiency. The iris dynamics was also studied when the phaco-probe is operated in the longitudinal mode. The simulation results suggest that placing the probe above or near beneath the iris within reach of the iris should be avoided, and the proper location for the probe is the central part of the eye. Increasing the probe power can relieve the risk of iris tissue damage by expanding the safe RP mode zone and shrinking the damaging AH mode zone. The longitudinal operation repels the iris away. By comparing with the torsional operation mode, the longitudinal operation mode can expand the safe RP mode zone, especially in the concerned region beneath the iris, but with the expense of reducing the nucleus removal efficiency. 3. To assess the feasibility of using fluidic control to mitigate IFIS (100% achieved) The effectiveness of some clinical management strategies for IFIS, including pupil dilation and M-ring implementation, was explored. The iris dynamics in various scenarios, i.e., with or without the implementation of M-ring, was studied from both the viewpoints of buckling and FSI. In the viewpoint of buckling, both dilated pupil and M-ring implementation can stabilize the iris in routine intraocular surgery. More specially, larger pupil dilation increases the critical pressure required to initiate iris buckling. The M-ring has been shown to significantly inhibit iris buckling even in the event of IFIS, and can be demonstrated as an effective method to mechanically stabilize abnormal iris behavior in cataract surgery. If considering the FSI, the 3D simulation results without M-ring show that operating the probe in the central portion of eye and avoiding the probe’s aspiration port directly pointing to the iris can ensure the safety of iris in the surgery. This is consistent with the findings from 2D simulations. The study with M-ring reveals that M-ring can alleviate the IFIS risk effectively. However, clinicians still need to pay special attention when operating the probe near the iris, considering that the possibility of damaging AH mode still exists. 4. To explore alternative surgical protocols for the mitigation of IFIS (100% achieved) The effect of power modulation was investigated to explore alternative surgical protocols for the mitigation of IFIS. If the probe is operated in the longitudinal oscillation mode, decreasing the duty cycle is found to shrink the safe RP mode zone and expand the AT mode zone, and hence increases the risk of IFIS. However, it is opposite if the probe is operated in the torsional oscillation mode, in which the damaging AH mode zone shrinks due to the weakened attraction of probe on iris. Hence decreasing power duty cycle in the torsional operation mode is a good candidate to alleviate IFIS risks but at the expense of reducing the efficiency of nuclear tissue removal. The probe’s power does not significantly affect the mode distributions of iris dynamics for both operation modes. It is also found that modulating the probe input power temporally can considerately strengthen the repulsion effect of the longitudinally operating probe and the attraction effect of the torsionally operating probe. This suggests that, when operating the probe in the longitudinal mode, doctors could consider modulating power of probe temporally to ensure larger repulsion on iris to relieves IFIS risks, whereas when operating the probe in the torsional mode, modulating power amplitude is a better choice, which weakens the attraction on iris and then alleviates IFIS risks. Moreover, the efficiency of nuclear lens removal is shown to be closely related with the probe’s power level. The torsional operation mode is more effective on nuclear tissue removal considering the absence of probe’s repulsion effect that is observed in the longitudinal operation mode.

15250916.label: Project Objectives
15250916.value: Develop a general unified theory of dc-coil-free hybrid-excited flux-biased PM machine in which the flux linkage can be directly adjusted with zero-sequence components in the armature windings. Develop and optimize the machine design with FEM based global optimization method, and especially optimize the allocation of PMs and electric excitation sources so as to improve its torque density and dynamic performance. With this design and control method, the topology with the best overall performances will be constructed, tested and finally applied to the direct drives of EVs.
