15250916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15250916.value: With increasing concerns on environmental protection and energy conservation, the development of electric vehicles (EVs) has taken on an accelerated pace. For EV drives, both high-torque low-speed capability for hill climbing and low-torque high-speed capability for cruising are desired, so the air-gap flux of EV motors need to be readily adjusted. Hybrid-excited machines (HEMs) are good candidates for EV propulsion for their excellent flux-regulation capability. However, some drawbacks of HEMs limit their wide applications. (i) Auxiliary dc-field windings as the flux regulator inevitably conflict in volume with the armature windings for torque production. The spatial conflict between dc-field and ac-armature systems in stator reduces the torque density of HEMs. Therefore, how to remove the dc-field systems but still maintain a good flux-regulation capability becomes a very challenging problem to be addressed. (ii) For HEMs, especially flux-switching HEMs, the space conflicting between stator windings and PMs degrades the torque performance of machine. (iii) During flux regulation, continually energized dc field currents unavoidably decrease the efficiency. This proposal is devoted to developing a novel dc-coil-free HEM for direct drive of EVs. This high-torque-density high-efficiency direct-drive machine has great potential for EV propulsion in that (1) Dc-excitation systems are completely removed from the stator. With a newly proposed zero-sequence current control strategy, the excitation flux linkage can be directly adjusted with zero-sequence components in the armature windings. Eliminating dc-field systems, a revolutionary progress is brought in the development of HEMs. (2) Stator PMs and electric excitation sources are separately allocated in the dual stator or in different layers of inner stator. The allocation of electric loading and magnetic loading can be optimized to improve the torque density of machine. (3) Hybrid-PM is introduced to reduce the losses due to the field regulation. Low-coercive-force PMs are incorporated with NdFeB PMs to realize effective flux regulation with temporary current excitation. The efficiency of machine will not be sacrificed since this temporary current lasts only for several milliseconds. A criteria of this proposed machine design and control, including stator design (PM shapes, magnetic-flux paths, stator-tooth arc), rotor design (rotor pole-arc/pole-pitch ratio, reliable mechanical design), and advanced zero-sequence-current control strategy will be investigated. The PI and her group have extensive research experiences on machine design and motor control. The idea of using zero-sequence current control to eliminate the dc-field coils in HEMs is original. This creative design method will greatly enhance the performance of EV propulsion system. 近些年來，環境惡化和能源危機引起了學術和工業界越來越多的關注。電動汽車的使用可以從根本上減小的對石油的依賴，降低排放，促進環境改善。發展電動汽車技術成為學術和工業界的當務之急。但電動汽車的運行工況較為復雜，在爬坡過程中電動車轉速低，電機需要提供較大的轉矩，而在正常行駛過程中則需要電機提供較高的轉速，對轉矩要求相對較低。因此根據不同的工況電機的氣隙磁密需要分別加以調節。混合勵磁電機具有比較好的磁場調節能力，因此是一種很合適的電動車驅動電機設計的解決方案。然而，目前針對電動汽車系統應用的絕大多數混合勵磁電機存在一個普遍難題，就是同一個定子空間中存在兩套繞組，勵磁繞組和電樞繞組，勵磁繞組的存在不可避免地占據了電樞繞組原有的一部分定子空間。因此引入勵磁繞組雖然實現了磁場調節功能，但是不可避免的削弱了電機本身的轉矩輸出能力。因此，針對混合勵磁電機設計，存在三個具有挑戰性的問題，第一個問題是怎樣去除勵磁繞組並保持磁場調節能力。第二個問題是針對傳統混合勵磁電機的問題，尤其是混合勵磁磁通切換電機，如何避免電樞繞組和永磁體在定子空間中的衝突，提高電機的轉矩密度。第三個問題，在磁場調節過程中，如果避免連續磁化勵磁繞組減低系統的效率的問題。 本項目針對電動汽車技術，致力於發展一種新的無勵磁線圈混合勵磁電機。這種電機具備較寬的恆功率範圍，從而適應電動汽車復雜的運行工況，其優勢如下：第一，勵磁繞組完全從定子中去除。采用一種創新性的零序電流控制策略，通過控制電樞繞組中的零序電流分量，獲得連續可調的直流勵磁磁鏈。此技術對於電動車電機的發展而言具有革命意義。第二，永磁體和電樞繞組分別分配於內外定子中，消除了二者所占定子空間的權衡和配比問題。從而可以分別優化電密和磁密，提升電機的轉矩密度。第三，記性永磁體的概念可以引入到該電機的設計方案中，從而減少了磁場調節過程中的損耗。基於以上幾點可以預期，本項目所提出的新穎電機控制策略以及設計方法可以顯著地提升電動汽車電機的轉矩密度以及整機效率。 本項目的負責人和她的團隊在新型電機設計，優化和控制方面開展了廣泛的研究。在混合勵磁電機中采用零序電流控制方法取代勵磁繞組是課題組創新性設計，對其在電動汽車應用領域的探索是一個極富挑戰性的課題。

15250916.label: Realisation of objectives
15250916.value: Biased flux machines (BFMs) have biased magnetic flux in the core and allows flexibility to adjust the field with a dc current, which is also named as zero sequence components in the armature windings. [1,2,5] investigates the reluctance machine with DC field coils in stator, which is an emerging brushless candidate for in-wheel direct drive for its wide speed range and robust mechanical structure. While it suffers from relatively low torque density and efficiency, due to the poor excitation ability of DC field coils and worse extra DC saturation effect in stator core. To address this issue, a new hybrid reluctance machine is proposed in this paper [1], in which an integrated dual-layer PM source is introduced into stator slots, aiming to relieve DC saturation and meanwhile evoke flux modulation effect. [2,7,16] proposes a new hybrid-excited dual-permanent-magnet generator with adjustable flux. The proposed machines integrate the stator dc source and permanent-magnet (PM) source in a single brushless structure, which enables coordinated power generation and flexible power adjustment. [3] incorporates the idea of integrated field and armature windings into the design of novel hybrid excited machines with bi-directional flux modulating effect, which results in a new hybrid-excited machine concept that is referred as dual-electrical-port dc-coil-free hybrid-excited machine (DEPDCF- HEM). In the proposed design, dc field windings are eliminated and dc bias currents are injected into the windings to generate dc excitation field. In addition, the armature windings are divided into dual electrical ports, and zero-sequence current flows between these two ports can adjust the air-gap field effectively. Compared with existing HEMs with additional dc coils, the proposed machines can achieve both higher torque density and wider flux weakening range. [4] aims to propose a new Vernier reluctance machine (VRM), which integrates the advantages of a robust rotor structure, good torque density, and flexible flux control ability. The key is to establish the excitation field with both stator slot permanent magnets (PMs) and zero-sequence current. Two excitation sources have different pole pair numbers but share a parallel magnetic circuit and contribute to superimposed torque in this machine. Meanwhile, a flexible flux control can be achieved by regulating zero-sequence current, and little demagnetization risk exists for slot PMs during flux control. In this paper, the machine configuration and operation principle are introduced, along with its integrated ac and dc drive method. Electromagnetic performance of this new machine is evaluated by finite-element analysis. Leading design parameters are determined and optimized considering optimal injection ratio of zero-sequence current. A prototype is fabricated, and relevant experiment results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed solution. [5] proposes a new DC coil free hybrid excited machine concept, which has no external field windings. The technical novelty is the integration of field windings and armature windings. DC bias current is injected into the excitation and the field windings in the traditional hybrid excited machine are eliminated. Compared with traditional hybrid-excited machines with additional field windings, the proposed machine can realize a higher slot utilization ratio, hence achieve a higher torque density and a wider flux adjusting range. Another advantage of the proposed machine is that the voltage drop associated with flux regulation is small due to the small DC resistance, and the torque generating capability at the flux regulating region can be improved accordingly. The rotor is specifically designed with magnet-iron sequences and a consequent-pole, in which the permanent magnet and iron pole are alternatively employed. [6] proposes a new Vernier reluctance machine (VRM) drive for electric vehicle. The key is to incorporate both stator-slot permanent magnets (PMs) and zero-sequence current as the excitation source to establish a parallel magnetic field and interact with armature winding. In this way, two different machines, namely, slot-PM-excited VRM and dc-excited doubly salient machine, are artificially integrated into a single structure, which contributes to enhance the torque density. Moreover, flexible flux control can be realized by regulating zero-sequence current. In this paper, the machine structure and operation principle are introduced, with its feasibility verified by both finite-element analysis and prototype experiments. [8, 10, 14-15] systematically studied a new kind of PM machines with both stator and rotor PM excitations, namely, dual-PM excited machines. The key is to rely on the PM-iron structure in the machine to provide both PM excitation and flux modulation. Besides the fundamental field component in the air-gap, some other predominant harmonics introduced by the flux modulating effect can also contribute to the electromagnetic torque production. Therefore, this kind of machines can be designed with high torque density. Due to the unique flux distribution, biased flux machines (BFMs) could be driven by biased current to realize flexible flux weakening or strengthening control. In [9], the electric machines with biased flux are investigated. The key techniques such as constructing biased flux in coils, exploring topologies, developing coil connection patterns, and designing drive circuits are presented. Based on that, the general design guideline for double stator BFMs is concluded. To verify this analysis, one 12/11 (stator teeth/rotor teeth) double stator BFM prototype is built and tested. The proposed double stator BFM has good torque and efficiency performance. Meanwhile, the biased current including dc zero sequence is used to adjust the exciting field. The simulation and experimental results verify the validity and effectiveness of this machine design method and control strategy. The flexible flux modulation characteristic makes this kind of machines suitable for applications with wide speed range. The conventional topology exploration methods for BFMs are based on the flux observation. It is time consuming and ineffective since the initial structure searching process is guideless. Meanwhile, BFMs usually work with arbitrary magnetic field harmonics instead of the fundamental one. The torque components of these machines and their essential operation principle have not been fully revealed. To solve these issues, in [13], a topology exploration method for BFM based on magnetic field modulation mechanism is proposed, and the torque generating principle is analyzed. With this method, some new BFM structures have been developed and their torque components have been developed. It is shown that various space harmonics have contributed to constant torque rather than the fundamental one. To verify the feasibility of this design method, one double stator BFM is selected as a case study. Simulation and experimental results have verified that this design method is feasible and effective since the prototype has good sinusoidal back electromotive force waveforms and well performance. Besides, it is practical to realize flux weakening and strengthening the control with biased current. [17] proposes a novel modular relieving-dc-saturation Vernier reluctance machine for electric vehicle application, which integrates the merits of a robust structure, controllable excitation field, strong fault-tolerant capacity, and enhanced torque density, benefiting from its special relieving-dc-saturation design. In the proposed machine, zero-sequence current establishes a modular magnetic path and functions as the dominant excitation source for the torque generation. Especially, slot permanent magnets are introduced into each module, which mitigates the saturation effect in stator core caused by dc-biased flux with the zero-sequence current source.

15250916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15250916.value: Relieving-dc-saturation can greatly improve the performance of the biased flux machine for electric vehicle application. In the future design of machine, slot permanent magnets can be introduced into each module, which mitigates the saturation effect in stator core caused by dc-biased flux with the zero-sequence current source. Therefore, the machine can achieve enhanced torque density with relatively high current density. The design can be extended to multi-electric port and multi-mechanical port machine and improve the flux regulation capability of these machines.

15250916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15250916.value: This project proposes to investigate new innovative DC-field-winding free hybrid-excitation electric machines for EVs applications. i. Build up fundamental design and control theory on proposed dc coil free biased flux machine （BFM）for EV applications. The fundamental theory concerns several essential problems: What is the operating principle and general design guideline of the proposed BFMs? How to achieve zero components control for this kind of proposed BFMs? The answers to these questions make revolutionary contribution to the design and theory of hybrid excitation electric machines. ii. Develop a software package for analysis and optimization of proposed BFMs. The developed modeling and optimal design techniques will be served as powerful tools to analyze the complicated operations of the electric system. The success of this project will offer long-term significance in FEM analysis of advanced electric machines. iii. Set technical specifications on manufacturing and assembling of proposed BFMs and promote its practical application on EV motor drives. Setting comprehensive technical specifications on the manufacturing and assembling of the proposed FRMs will supply valuable references to the industrial sectors. It will also greatly promote the practical application on EV propulsion system, so as to make contribute on relieving global warming and energy crisis.

15251016.label: Project Objectives
15251016.value: to develop finite-element body sub-models of various breast shapes using in-vivo material properties; to design and develop a finite-element sports bra sub-model based on the design specifications and directly-measured fabric properties to simulate the stress distribution of the body exerted by a sports bra with different fabrics to a sample of women; to determine the comfort pressure ranges of sports bras made of different fabrics; to predict the skin pressure, and systematically change the material parameters until the pressure is minimized with the constraints of comfort pressure range;
rows: to develop finite-element body sub-models of various breast shapes using in-vivo material properties;
to design and develop a finite-element sports bra sub-model based on the design specifications and directly-measured fabric properties
to simulate the stress distribution of the body exerted by a sports bra with different fabrics to a sample of women;
to determine the comfort pressure ranges of sports bras made of different fabrics;
to predict the skin pressure, and systematically change the material parameters until the pressure is minimized with the constraints of comfort pressure range;

15251016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15251016.value: This project uses a novel approach to couple the nonlinear finite element analysis (FEA) with optimization software to predict the optimum level of comfort in women’s compression sports bras. The optimization of comfort essentially involves the optimization of the fabric properties in the bras. In this respect, the most critical property is the fabric tensile, shear and bending moduli. It is challenging because the interactions between the elastic fabric and visco-elastic breasts are highly complex. Limited previous work has unrealistically modelled the bra only as a single-layer garment imposed onto a rigid body model or arbitrarily-defined soft breasts. Consequently, the calculated pressure on the breasts has yet to be validated. The difficulties are that every human breast is unique in shape and stiffness; sports bras commonly have double layers made of various fabrics; and women have different sensations on comfort and pressure. Commercial sports bras tend to compress the breasts against the rib-cage in order to limit the breast movement during activities, but the excessive skin pressure often cause discomfort. Currently, there is no scientific theory to determine the minimum pressure to achieve the required support to the breasts. Sample making and fitting of bras on women subjects are time-consuming and prone to human errors. To solve this problem, this project aims to develop and validate a new scientific system to couple computer optimization with finite element simulation to determine the optimum pressure and fabric parameters for the comfort of compression sports bras. A series of 1,024 algorithm-driven iterations of FEA will be run to automatically simulate the skin pressure within a double-layer sports bra with different fabric properties. This will build a foundation for the future dynamic simulation of nonlinear body-bra contacts. To simulate the body-bra interactions more realistically, the compression modulus and damping coefficients of the breasts of 30 women of various ages and sizes will be measured using an indentation test and breast vibration analysis respectively. For the fabric optimization, the calculated pressure should fall within the comfort pressure range determined by the subjects. The pressure calculated by the FEA will be validated against the experimental data. Ultimately, this advanced method will also have a fundamental impact on the design of intimate apparel in general. This addresses a common need of the female population, so it has global relevance and applicability. The project will also facilitate further research into 3D CAD of other wearable products.

15251016.label: Realisation of objectives
15251016.value: Wearing a sports bra is important for controlling movement of the breast physical activities due to the substantial displacement which can cause much discomfort and even injury. However, if a sports bra exerts excessive pressure onto the body of the wearer, she may also feel uncomfortable. In response to the first objective, finite element models of fifteen different subjects were developed. Two experiments have been conducted to build precise subject-specific finite element (FE) models of the human bodies – scanning experiment and motion capture experiment. The FE model of the body is constructed with a rigid torso, breasts with hyperelasticity, and a layer of subcutaneous tissues. The geometric model of the body is obtained through 3D laser scanning for authenticity. The dynamic state of the free vibration of the breasts and running were recorded by motion capture experiments. The Mooney-Rivlin material coefficients of the breasts are determined by examining the differences between the FE-modelled results and experimental data, and the damping ratio is directly calculated from the free-vibration test data. To respond to the second objective, a finite element model of compression sports bra has been developed. The geometric model of the sports bra was extracted from the gravity-free model of the body based on commercial sports bras. The initial shape of the FE model of the body was affected by the gravity load. A gravity-free model was then constructed by using a force with the same magnitude as gravity but in the opposite direction. The entire model of the bra was meshed by using 6 mm quadrilateral elements. Five sports bras have been selected, which have different impact ratings (high, medium and low impacts). The mechanical properties of the sports bra components were tested by using an Instron 4411 tester at a constant-rate-of-extension. To respond to the third objective, FE contact models have been established. To solve the penetration problem with the use of a contact model, a method is created which first shrinks and then expands the model, and used to simulate the contact conditions between the female body and sports bra. In the static analysis, the simulated contact pressure values are in agreement with the results of the contact pressure tests. The distribution of the contact pressure is clear and can be easily analysed with computer modelling. The highest contact pressure was found on the shoulders caused by the shoulder strap, and under the arms caused by the elastic bra band. The highest contact pressure between the bra cup and the breasts can be observed at the bottom of the breasts, which is caused by the gravity load. In the dynamic analysis, breast motion is investigated and analysed when a sports bra is donned with contact pressure. The dynamic results showed that the amount of the contact pressure caused by the bra strap and the elastic bra band increases during movement. However, the contact pressure at the bottom of the bra cup is slightly reduced. The greatest change in the contact pressure caused by the strap and elastic bra band is 0.8259 and 0.3788 kPa, respectively. Based on the calculated errors between the results of the FE model and experiments, the model is found to predict the contact conditions with good accuracy. The reliability of this study is thus validated. To respond to the fourth objective, a range of contact pressure, that would be tolerable while wearing a sports bra during running, has been determined. In order to determine this range, two steps are carried out; one is subjective while the other is objective. First, a questionnaire survey is carried out to determine the perceived comfort sensation. The design of the questionnaire is based on two conditions: static and dynamic. The perceived subjective comfort in the dynamic condition is important because sports bras are worn during dynamic activities, like physical exercise. The other step is conducting pressure tests to obtain objective experimental data. As for the factors that affect the level of comfort, the contact pressure in three positions, which are caused by the shoulder strap, elastic bra band and bra cup, could have significant influence on the comfort level for the different parts of the bra and in different conditions. Therefore, the contact pressure needs to be considered in the design of sports bras and the findings can be used to optimize designs. A contact pressure on the shoulders, underarm and at the bottom of the bra cup of 2.08 ± 0.82 kPa, 2.66 ± 0.83 kPa and 0.58 ± 0.57 kPa respectively is most tolerable. The optimum contact pressure allows optimum fabrics for sports bras to be determined. To respond to the fifth objective, machine learning (ML) approach has been used to do prediction and further enhance efficiency. Specifically, the artificial neural network (ANN) results of the contact pressure, which applies the Levenberg-Marquardt learning algorithm, are in good agreement with the corresponding FE results based on the calculated relative errors. Moreover, the effect of the different components of the sports bra on the contact pressure has been analysed, which is that the shoulder strap and bra cup can greatly influence the contact pressure, while the back panel and elastic bra band do not have much influence the contact pressure. These results can be directly used for selecting sports bra materials, and positively benefit a large percentage of the female population worldwide in terms of their bra needs for physical activities.

15251016.label: Major findings and research outcome
15251016.value: The FE body model, including a rigid torso, breasts with hyperelasticity and layers of subcutaneous tissues, can accurately simulate the deformation of the female breasts. Specifically, the Mooney-Rivlin material is highly appropriate to describe the female breasts by examining the differences between the FE-modelled results and experimental data. Building the FE contact model with a new method, the ‘first shrink and then expand’ model, successfully avoids the penetration problem. In the static analysis, the simulated contact pressure values are in agreement with the results of the contact pressure tests. In terms of the distribution of contact pressure, the highest contact pressure is found on the shoulders which is caused by the shoulder strap, and under the arms which is caused by the elastic bra band. The highest contact pressure exerted by the bra cup is found at the bottom of the bra cup. In the dynamic analysis, the displacement of breasts is investigated and analysed based on contact with the sports bra. The calculated errors from the results of the FE model and experiments show that the contact model can predict the contact conditions with good accuracy. A modal analysis has also been conducted by using the FE models and the corresponding natural frequencies are calculated. The natural frequencies of the breasts with a sports bra are found to be much higher than those of the braless condition, which confirms the necessity of wearing a sports bra. The objective experimental data are the tested contact pressure at three positions (on the shoulders and underarm and at the bottom of the bra cups) by using Novel Pliance-X pressure sensors. Furthermore, the subjective perceptions of the bras are derived from a questionnaire that focused on how the subjects felt about the sports bra samples. By analysing these two kinds of data, the range of pressure comfort has been determined. The optimum contact pressure or most tolerable amount of pressure on the shoulders and underarm and at the bottom of the bra cup are in the ranges of 2.08 ± 0.82 kPa, 2.66 ± 0.83 kPa and 0.58 ± 0.57 kPa respectively. The effect of the different components of the sports bra on the contact pressure is then investigated, and it is found that the shoulder strap and bra cup can greatly influence the contact pressure, while the back panel and elastic bra band do not influence the contact pressure very much.

15251016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15251016.value: The methods used in this project can potentially provide the basis for future research work on apparel comfort, elastic materials, intimate apparel and sports activities. Improved sports bra designs will also contribute to the wellbeing of the female population globally. However, the small number of subjects and the sports bra style used is limited. Future work needs to involve more or other types of female subjects and different styles of sports bras, such as encapsulation sports bras. In addition, the FE models of the female body have been simplified in this study. The development of more complex FE models of the breasts that include different components, such as fat and Cooper’s ligaments, are recommended to be carried out in future studies. The material properties of each component should also be determined.

15251016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15251016.value: Wearing a sports bra is important for controlling movement of the breasts during physical activities. However, if a sports bra exerts excessive pressure onto the body of the wearer, she may also feel uncomfortable. Therefore, this project has provided a nonlinear FEA to predict the mechanical behavior of the female breasts when in contact with a compression sports bra with a focus on the optimization of the fabric properties of the sports bra. To achieve this aim, a new scientific and reliable system that uses FE simulation and ML approach was developed and validated to determine the optimum pressure and the fabric properties for the comfort of compression sports bras. This project provided a robust computational method to optimize the design of sports bras. This method can also potentially be applied to solve the contact problem between relatively rigid and hyperelastic materials, or other problems in the area of comfort, elastic materials, intimate apparel and sports activities. The optimization of sports bra can address a common need and contribute to the wellbeing of women globally.

15251816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15251816.value: The recent incidents in security leaks in Hong Kong have put the risk of using remote services under the spotlight. No doubt identity theft and frauds in Hong Kong are on the rise due to the popularity of using mobile phones to access remote services. While remote services bring us convenience, they also open up opportunities for criminals to carry out fraudulent activities. The traditional ways of authentication are no longer sufficient for securing the services. The recent advance in speaker recognition technology has demonstrated that voice biometrics could be an important part of the authentication process. Using voice biometrics, anyone imitating a legitimate user can be identified to prevent security leaks. State-of-the-art speaker recognition systems typically use machine learning techniques to train statistical models based on a large amount of data. While this system works very well under the environment (source domain) for which they are trained, their performance suffers when they are deployed in a new target domain -- a phenomenon known as domain mismatch. This project aims to develop a new deep neural network (DNN) for domain adaptation so that only a small amount of labelled data from the target domain will be sufficient for training a system to work in the new domain. A joined network comprising a regression DNN and a classification DNN will be co-trained by semi-supervised deep learning algorithms that exploit the labelled data from the source domain and unlabelled data from the target domain. The network achieves domain adaption through three perspectives: (1) create a domain-invariant feature space through minimizing the discrepancy between the source and target domain in the kernel reproducing Hilbert space; (2) suppress the noise in the input through the regression DNN; and (3) extract bottleneck features from the classification DNN so that the resulting bottleneck features are not only domain invariant but also noise robust. The proposed DNN will be evaluated on massive amount of data from Switchboard and NIST SRE datasets, following the evaluation protocol defined in Domain Adaptation Challenge. A new evaluation protocol for domain adaptation based on more recent NIST SRE data will also be developed. The proposed work will provide insight into semi-supervised deep learning, co-training, deep denoising networks, bottleneck feature extraction, and noise robust speaker verification. 15251816.label: Realisation of objectives
15251816.value: For Objective 1, we have developed an iterative spectral clustering approach to determining the speaker labels for the iterative retraining of a PLDA mixture model for speaker verification. The method also uses a deep neural network to compute the gender posterior probabilities for the mixture model. The results have been published at an international conference (ICASSP'18). We have also extended the idea of semi-supervised learning to train domain adversarial networks and applied the network to speech emotion recognition. The results have been published in IEEE Trans. on Neural Networks and Learning Systems. For Objective 2, we have developed two new autoencoders, namely nuisance-attribute autoencoder (NAE) and domain-invariant autoencoder (DAE), for multi-source i-vector adaptation. NAE encodes the features that cause most of the multi-source mismatch, which is measured by the maximum mean discrepancy across multiple domains. DAE directly encodes the features that minimize the multi-source mismatch. The results have been published in an international conference (Speaker Odyssey'18) and IEEE Trans. on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing. For Objective 3, we have developed a denoising DNN that produces not only robust features in its bottleneck layer but also denoised senone posterior probabilities. The latter allows us to compute robust i-vectors based on senone posteriors, which we call senone i-vectors. The idea and results have been published in IEEE Trans. on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing.

15251816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15251816.value: We have developed an iterative spectral clustering approach to determining the speaker labels for the iterative retraining of a PLDA mixture model for speaker verification. The method also uses a deep neural network to compute the gender posterior probabilities for the mixture model. It was found that at the end of the iterative re-training, the PLDA mixture model becomes fully adapted to the new domain. Results also show that the PLDA scores can be readily incorporated into spectral clustering, resulting in high-quality speaker clusters that could not be possibly achieved by agglomerative hierarchical clustering. We have also extended the idea of semi-supervised learning to train domain adversarial networks and applied the network to speech emotion recognition. It was found that by forcing the synthetic latent vectors and the real latent vectors to share a common representation, the gradient vanishing problem of DNNs can be largely alleviated. Also, results show that the augmented data generated by the proposed networks are rich in emotion information. Thus, the resulting emotion classifiers are competitive with state-of-the-art speech emotion recognition systems. We have developed two new autoencoders, namely nuisance-attribute autoencoder (NAE) and domain-invariant autoencoder (DAE), for multi-source i-vector adaptation. NAE encodes the features that cause most of the multi-source mismatch, and DAE directly encodes the features that minimize the multi-source mismatch. Using these MMD-based autoencoders as a preprocessing step for PLDA training, we achieve a relative improvement of 19.2% EER on the NIST 2016 SRE compared to PLDA without adaptation. We also found that MMD-based autoencoders are more robust to unseen domains. In the domain robustness experiments, MMD-based autoencoders show 6.8% and 5.2% improvements over the classical method on female and male Cantonese speakers, respectively. We have developed a denoising DNN that produces not only robust features in its bottleneck layer but also denoised senone posterior probabilities. The latter allows us to compute robust i-vectors based on senone posteriors, which we call senone i-vectors. Results on NIST 2012 SRE show that senone i-vectors outperform the conventional GMM i-vectors. More interestingly, the BN features are not only phonetically discriminative, but they also contain sufficient speaker information to produce BN-based senone i-vectors that outperform the conventional senone i-vectors.

15251816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15251816.value: Some of the methods in this project focus on making the speaker embedding vectors (mainly i-vectors) more domain invariant and noise-robust. Recent research has shifted to force the speaker embedding network to produce domain-invariant speaker embedding vectors and noise-robust speaker embedding vectors. Therefore, a possible extension of this project is to borrow the ideas from the MMD-based autoencoder and make it to reduce the domain mismatch in the speaker embedding network. By moving the MMD to the convolutional feature map layers, it is possible to make the speaker embedding network more domain-invariant.

15252816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15252816.value: An explosion occurred when spraying combustible coloured cornstarch powder clouds during a big party on 28 June, 2015 in Taiwan. That incident hurt almost 500 people, with 10 killed and 100 seriously injured. As a series of explosions were reported, some were possibly secondary explosions. However, there have been no moves to ban such coloured powder spraying activities during big parties in the future. In fact, the government finds difficulties in deciding whether to approve or reject applications involving such activities because no scientifically supported explosion hazard control codes are available for this kind of activity. Fires and explosions of powder have been reported over the years all over the world. There has been much research activity, but most of the work on powder explosions relates to factories and storage areas, not in partially confined areas as was the case in the Taiwan incident. Understanding of the causes of explosions in sprayed coloured powder in crowded partially confined areas is very limited. A scientific study is proposed to model the spread of powder in partially confined areas, the mixing of powder with air, how the mixture spreads in regions near the spraying source, the primary explosion mechanisms, flame spread, and the possibility of secondary explosions. The discharge of combustible coloured powder at high, medium and low levels in a partially confined area and the mixing of powder with air will be first studied using numerical Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models and physical scale models. Four CFD models will be used to study fire-induced air flow, the mixing of powder particles with air and the explosions themselves. Scale model explosion experiments will be carried out in an enclosed box. The three sidewalls will be removed one by one to give partially confined areas. Flame patterns will be recorded by a high speed camera. The mixing process of powder with air and explosions will then be studied via full-scale experiments on part of the Taiwan real-scale scenario at a remote site in China. Measured temperature, pressure and powder concentration distributions will be compared with numerical predictions. The results will then be applied to appropriate full-scale tests for evaluating the safety of combustible coloured powder spraying activities, to enable better assessment of applications for the use of powder, with strong scientific support. An explosion hazard management framework will be recommended for use by such approved applications. 2015 年 6 月 28 日，在台灣彩色派對期間發生了嚴重的因噴放彩色玉米澱粉形成的粉塵氣雲爆炸事件。 此次災害造成約500人受傷，100人重傷及10人死亡。 根據現場報導，當時發生了一連串的爆炸，有些可能是二次爆炸。 政府到目前為止仍沒有採取明確態度禁止或容許此類在大型具娛樂性聚會上噴放彩粉的活動。主要 因為當前沒有關於此類爆炸事件的實質科學數據和控制條款，政府難於決定是否禁止類似的活動及宣佈可行性指引。 雖然文獻上有許多關於粉塵氣雲爆炸的研究，但是大多數都是針對工廠和存儲區域的粉塵爆炸，而不是類似於此次事件的局部封閉空間內粉塵爆炸。 目前對於人群密集的局部封閉空間內的彩粉爆炸的認識還比較有限。 此課題旨在研究如何類比局部封閉空間內的粉塵擴散過程，粉塵與空氣混合過程，粉塵源附近的混合物擴散過程，粉塵氣雲的爆炸機理，火焰傳播過程，以及二次爆炸發生的可能性。 首先，利用計算流體力學軟體（CFD）和數學模型研究不同高度範圍內的可燃彩粉氣雲的爆炸過程。 四種計算方案將分別研究爆炸造成的空氣流動過程，粉末顆粒和空氣的混合過程，以及混合之後的爆炸過程。 其次，在特製的封閉實驗箱內進行小尺度爆炸實驗。 箱子的三個側面會被逐一的移除，形成局部封閉空間。 高速攝像技術會用於記錄火焰的傳播過程。 然後，進行和台灣爆炸現場類似的小部份全尺寸實驗，研究粉末和空氣的混合過程。 實測的爆炸溫度，爆炸壓力，和粉塵濃度將會和數值計算結果進行比對。 研究成果會被用於類似場景內噴放可燃性彩粉活動的安全評估，為更合理的使用彩粉指引提供科學依據。 最後，建立對類似活動的爆炸災害控制方案。

15252816.label: Realisation of objectives
15252816.value: The two objectives proposed in this project were studied along the six tasks on dispersion of combustible powder; explosion phenomena; numerical modelling of explosions; experiments with a scale model; full-scale burning tests; and explosion hazard management framework. These two objectives were achieved by the following significant works: On objective 1, To study, experimentally and numerically, the fire and explosion hazards due to the spraying of coloured powders in partially confined areas. 1a. Powder explosion and control studies were thoroughly reviewed first. Updated powder explosion research overseas and in China were reviewed. Experimental studies of deflagration to detonation transition (DDT) in tubes were reviewed. Scaling effects in those experimental data were summarized. 1b. Dispersion of powder from a partially confined area was studied. Upon igniting dispersed combustible particles in air, a powder explosion might occur. Such powder or dust explosions involve rapid combustion. Serious consequences with damages may result in adjacent areas. If the ignited powder cloud is not confined in a chamber, only a flash fire would result. ‘Secondary explosion’ would occur. But if the ignited powder cloud is confined, even partially, the heat emitted from combustion would lead to rapid increase in pressure. Flame would propagate across the powder cloud to evolve large quantities of heat and reaction products. Pressure would rise rapidly and might even cause collapse of the enclosure itself, claiming lives and damaging property even at some distance from the original point of explosion. 1c. The explosion hazards associated with clean fuel (liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and hydrogen) vehicles in confined spaces were compared first in this part, then applied to powder. Explosion hazards of LPG and hydrogen vehicles in a garage were studied using the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) software Flame Acceleration Simulator (FLACS). Explosion due to coloured powder explosion in a partially confined area was studied. The powder was discharged at low, middle and high levels. 1d. The big accidental fire with ‘explosion’ resulting from spraying coloured corn flour powder occurred at the water fun park in Taiwan was investigated with Chang Jung Christian University. The possible fire scenarios were studied using CFD-FLACS. Environmental conditions including wind action and solid boundary conditions were deduced based on government fire investigation and video records, and were used as the input parameters in the simulation. These environmental conditions or parameters and the simulation results together would give a fire scene that agrees with the accident observed, indicating that appropriate environmental parameters had been identified. 1e. An experimental rig with a 16 m long open tube of 0.488 m diameter was constructed for studying the flame propagation characteristics of premixed LPG and powder under different mixing ratios with air. The transient flame propagation distance, flame velocity, pressure and temperature were analyzed. 1f. A flame velocity model in this partially open tube was established. The reliability of the flame velocity model was first verified by experiments available in the literature. Deflagration experiments with LPG/air premixed gas and powder were then carried out to justify the predictions. The traditional empirical formulas are not accurate enough to predict the increase of the turbulent burning velocity. A “sub-relaxation factor” was introduced to make the empirical formulas more consistent with the actual physical law, whose physical meaning is to limit the maximum range of the turbulent burning velocity. 1g. Numerical simulation on turbulent flame propagation in premixed gas and dry powder deflagration process in a tube was also carried out in this project, aiming at identifying the key factors affecting flame shape and flame velocity. Large eddy simulation with premixed gas combustion model was used to obtain results validated by full-scale experimental data available. Turbulence would accelerate the propagation of flame periodically. The cause of flame acceleration of low-intensity and large-scale turbulence originates from two factors, namely, combustion and flow field, which transfer the heat and mass of chemical reaction from diffusion to vortex transport. 1h. A big forest fire with unexpectedly high casualty occurred at Liangshan Yi, Sichuan, China in March 2019. Explosion noise was heard as reported, suggesting the possibility of transiting burning combustible dust available in the forest to deflagration. Explosion due to combustible dust was demonstrated to occur in an erupted forest fire by a physical scale model. Combustible dry powder was put in a balloon. This might explain why this forest fire blowup killed firefighters even though they have appropriate training. 1i. Dispersion mechanism developed was applied to determine the trajectories of the large respiratory droplets. It aims at providing a clear physical picture to elucidate the mechanics involved in single droplet motion and the various factors affecting the range. Assuming an indoor environment with an air temperature of 180C and relative humidity of 50%, the horizontal range L_(x )of large respiratory droplets (diameter 120 µm - 200 µm) in common respiratory activities were reported. On the second objective, To recommend appropriate testing procedures for assessing possible fire and explosion hazards of coloured powder spraying proposals and an associated hazard management framework for partially confined areas: 2a. Performance of natural vents installed at height would be affected under strong wind. Smoke and unburnt fuel vapour might even be pulled downward or inward by wind action if the building is located near to a tall building or on the hillside. The importance of studying aerodynamics around a building located adjacent to a vertical wall while designing venting was studied. Air flow pattern around the buildings depends on many factors including wind speed, fire size, height of the vertical wall and distance away from the building, theoretical study is difficult. Numerical simulations with CFD-Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS) is appropriate to design smoke exhaust system design under these conditions. 2b. Positive Pressure Ventilation (PPV) is commonly used for blowing out flue gas and thus enhancing the visibility inside the fire scene. However, there are different views on operating PPV for firefighting and rescue. Ventilation arrangements, which include the locations of PPV and exhaust openings in a room, were investigated for better understanding of the efficacy of PPV in firefighting with 1:10 scale models. 2c. Water mist fire suppression system on explosion control was studied. A one-zone model was developed to study fire extinguishment using water mist system with both continuous and cycling discharge modes. The model was based on the conservation of mass and energy of the fire enclosure. Two water mist discharge modes for extinguishing fires were calculated using the one-zone model. The results showed that the cycling discharge mode put out fire in a shorter time with less water than the continuous discharge mode. Water mist capability against fires under ventilation conditions was also improved. It was found that the effect of a cycling discharge on fire extinguishment was related to the fire size, ventilation conditions and water mist system characteristics. 2d. Appropriate fire safety management measures, as well as safety precautions and remedial work to upgrade existing systems, are proposed based on the study.

15252816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15252816.value: This project was worked out consequently after an explosion occurred when spraying combustible coloured cornstarch powder clouds during a big party in a Water Fun Park on 28 June, 2015 in Taiwan. Six tasks were studied according to the two proposed objectives. The explosion incident at that water fun park was analyzed. A series of explosion scenarios were investigated by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) Flame Acceleration Simulator (FLACS). The possible fire scenarios were studied with input parameters in numerical simulations to deduce data in fire investigation. Environmental parameters were estimated from the recorded video on appropriate wind action and boundaries. Results show that in addition to a strong enough heat source at some location and the spraying of a large amount of corn flour powder, the conditions of wind direction and speed, together with the presence of objects for forming a dispersed powder distribution, are also decisive in powder explosion or rapid flame spreading. Combustion occurs when there are coloured powder, a sufficient quantity of oxygen and an ignition source of sufficient strength as reported. An explosion can result in an appropriate partially confined environment. The necessary conditions for a powder explosion to occur as reported can be expressed by an explosion pentagon. Required are fuel or the combustible powder, an oxidant or air, an ignition source, mixing of the powder and air in an appropriate ratio and confinement of the mixture. A powder explosion can be prevented or mitigated by removing one of the fire pentagon elements, though, in fact, the explosion hazard scenario is very complicated. Powder particles are solids moving under the influence of gravity. The mixing of powder with air, the primary explosion mechanisms, flame spread, and the possibility of secondary explosions were studied by full-scale tests. Safety evaluation of combustible coloured powder spraying activities were proposed. The explosion hazard management framework is recommended for approving such activities with coloured powder discharging. All key findings above were communicated to the Hong Kong Government Fire Services Department as part of our mentorship programme. Under the scheme, two part-time PhD students studied explosion research. Results on when to approve applications to hold powder spraying activities, and for providing better fire safety provisions, including explosion control, by an appropriate typical suppressing agent were transferred. Papers were published to promote a better understanding of explosions of discharging coloured powder.

15252816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15252816.value: The coloured powder spray explosion occurred in Taiwan revealed that no specific fire safety requirements are imposed by the authorities on controlling such activities. No standard tests exist for evaluating the effects of using different powders. Note that in dense urban areas such as Hong Kong, powder explosions in residential areas could lead to big disasters. Scientific research carried out for better understanding the potential explosion hazards of spraying powder in this project can be transferred to practical design guides and fire regulations. Government in many places encounters difficulties in deciding whether to approve or reject applications involving such activities because no scientifically supported explosion hazard control codes are available for this kind of activity. More full-scale burning tests with coloured powder explosion should be carried out to validate the scale model observations and mathematical modelling results. An important point is to work out appropriate firefighting scheme. As studied in this project, water mist and PPV are appropriate to control coloured powder explosion. This part is recommended to further study thoroughly. Results are useful to hazard assessment applicable to government and regulatory bodies responsible for building fire safety.

15252816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15252816.value: Fires and explosions of coloured cornstarch powder have been reported all over the world since 2015. The biggest disaster was in a water fun park in Taiwan. A scientific study was carried out to better understand the coloured powder explosion. The spread of powder in partially confined areas, the mixing of powder with air, how the mixture spreads in regions near the spraying source, the primary explosion mechanisms, flame spread, and the possibility of secondary explosions were modelled. The discharge of combustible coloured powder in a partially confined area and the mixing of powder with air were first studied using numerical explosion Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models by Flame Acceleration Simulator (FLACS). Further, the big explosion accident in Taiwan was studied by CFD-FLACS. Controlled explosion experiments were carried out in a 16 m tube with 0.5 m diameter. The mixing process of powder with air and explosions was studied analytically first, and then simulated by CFD model. An explosion hazard management framework was recommended for use by the Fire Services Department, while approving applications on discharging coloured powder for fun. Results of this project were compiled into 9 journal papers and 9 conference papers at the moment as listed.

15252916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15252916.value: Research Motivation: This project will create a novel modeling framework to assess and control interdependent components of smart wastewater treatment systems. Climate change is a global phenomenon that requires international action to reduce its damaging impact on society and future generations. Recent studies have highlighted the significance of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from energy use in the water industry, and it has attributed 56% of the industry’s emissions to wastewater treatment systems. However, wastewater treatment systems are complex, comprised of many interdependent components with the performance of one system dependent on the performance of one or more of the others. Understanding the dependencies, synergies, conflicts, and trade-offs between water, energy, and GHG emissions of wastewater treatment systems is necessary to identify and implement beneficial strategies for their management and use. This project will investigate the relationships between the components of smart wastewater treatment systems and analyze how to reduce or enhance these dependencies, where to reduce costs effectively, and where to maximize the benefits of their use. Intellectual Merits: This project will take a multidisciplinary approach, integrating across computation, engineering, and management to create a novel framework that models proposed smart wastewater treatment systems and utilizes data collected from an array of sources to evaluate the current status of wastewater treatment systems and simulate their performance and reliability. The researchers will develop a Water-Energy-Climate (WEC) hybrid computational simulation tool, to integrate Agent-Based Model (ABM) and System Dynamics (SD). SD will be used to investigate the nonlinear relationships of the whole wastewater treatment system. ABM will be particularly used to understand the complex biological processes, including simultaneous partial nitrification, anaerobic ammonium oxidation [Anammox] and denitrification (SNAD) for wastewater treatment, anaerobic digestion (AD) for sludge treatment, and the electricity generation system through a solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC). The developed framework is expected to help decision-makers anticipate, plan and manage transitions successfully, and to re-think policies and strategies in a world of complexity and uncertainty in wastewater management. Broader Impact: The developed WEC in this study can be applied globally to other non-established wastewater treatment systems to simulate the associated environmental, economic, and social impacts with dynamic components. The results of this project will also be integrated into extensive classroom and educational research activities, and can help the next generation of scientists, engineers, and policy makers to understand the complex issues in wastewater treatment systems and obtain multidisciplinary skills. 此研究將開發一個創新模型架構用以控制智慧汙水處理系統的微相關構成部分。氣候變遷已演變成全球現象並須要世界各國一同採取有效方法以降低未來的危害。近來許多研究已指出有相當大部分的溫室氣體排放來自於水工業，且有超過56%的水工業溫室氣體出自於汙水處理設施。然而汙水處理過程是一相當複雜的系統且包含許多相關聯之設施，如果此複雜系統包含設施間相互依連、作用、牴觸、平衡等關係能夠被詳細的理解，將會對未來的管理與相關開發與運作策略產生極大之效益。因此本研究的目的將會著重在發現智慧汙水系統間設施的關聯性，並且分析如何減少成本與將系統之效益極大化。為了達成以上目的，本研究將採取一跨領域之研究方法，結合電腦模型，工程與管理開發一創新架構用以模擬智慧汙水處理系統。我們將運用代理人仿真結合系統動力理論開發一水能源氣候(WEC)模型。透過電腦即時運算能力與相關汙水處理實驗與資料收集分析，此模型將可模擬智慧汙水處理系統之績效與可靠度。代理人仿真模型將主要用於理解複雜的生物反應過程，其中包含厭氧氨氧化(Anammox)處理汙水、厭氧消化(Anaerobic digestion)處理汙泥、還有透過固體氧化物燃料電池發電系統。而系統動力學則用以串聯並模擬這些非線性的智慧汙水處理相關設施。此模型將提供一個虛擬環境並可動態模擬汙水處理系統所帶來之環境、經濟與社會影響。預期研究成果將可為決策者提供有效的策略分析並重新思考相關汙水政策之研擬。

15252916.label: Realisation of objectives
15252916.value: Sewage treatment is a process that protects water resources and human health by preventing the discharge of pollutants collected in sewage into aquatic environments. Conventional sewage treatment is energy-intensive, which translates into operation costs and carbon dioxide emissions. Recently developed processes focus on resource recovery and reducing energy consumption, without compromising water effluent quality. Whilst energy self-sufficiency contributes to reducing environmental impacts, a holistic environmental assessment of sewage treatment is needed to ensure that the impacts are not shifted from one category to another. In addition, economic implications of plant-wide systems combining mature and emerging processes should be assessed to determine the funds needed to retrofit existing sewage treatment plants. An integrated environmental and economic analysis for a whole-plant system could provide further understanding on potential trade-offs and economic competitiveness of water resource recovery facilities compared to conventional sewage treatment. Objective 1 A novel microbial individuality model (MIM) which integrates thermodynamics, microbial energetics, and agent-based modeling to describe microbiomes behavior as heterogenic populations, including homoacetogenic bacteria was developed for anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge. MIM results include daily biogas production and methane content, compound concentrations within the reactor, and microbial community relative abundance changes. MIM was tested with data from laboratory-scale anaerobic digesters. Even though calibration of MIM was limited in this study, MIM identified the emergence of Methanosaetas at low concentrations of acetates. Moreover, this study supports experimental studies confirming homoacetogenesis as an important hydrogen sink. In addition, the need for studies to determine kinetic parameters of Bacteroidales, Thermotogales, Fibrobacterales, WWE1, and Saprospirales populations is highlighted. Validated MIMs are expected to provide insights into syntrophic and competitive interactions among microbiomes in biological systems while testing different operational parameters in a virtual environment. MIM offers a methodological framework with the potential to further our understanding of microbial community dynamics. Objective 2 and 3 A hybrid theoretical-machine learning approach leverages up stoichiometry and kinetics to calculate missing values in limited data sets. Then, calculated data sets are analyzed through machine learning algorithms, which reveal hidden microbial interactions overlooked by fixed theoretical guidelines. Operational parameters, influent and effluent characterization, and microbial community abundance data from a pilot-scale partial nitritation/anammox fluidized bed membrane bioreactor (PN/AFMBR) were used to demonstrate the hybrid theoretical-machine learning model. The PN/AFMBR treated settled sewage with high salinity. Four machine learning algorithms, i.e., artificial neural networks, deep neural networks, random forest, and support vector machine, were applied to predict the change in nitrogen compounds concentrations in the reactor. Testing procedures for nitrogen compounds concentrations were successful and a good agreement was observed between the measured and predicted values. Random forest had better performance than other algorithms with correlation coefficients of 0.89, 0.72, and 0.80 for ammonium, nitrite, and nitrate data sets, respectively. Training sets containing 73 to 88 same-day values reached acceptable predicting performance. Beside pollution load, temperature and pH, different microbiomes were identified as key parameters for the performance prediction of the PN/AFMBR. Paracoccus, Muricauda, Thiosocius, Sulfuriflexus, and Desulfuromusa in suspension sludge; and Marinilabiliaceae, Arcobacter, Thioalkalispiraceae, Chromatiales, and Methyloccoccaceae in the biofilm of granulated activated carbon showed high relative importance for nitrogen compounds concentrations predictions. Objective 4 A novel stoichiometric life-cycle inventory (S-LCI) framework was developed to obtain sitespecific water, air and soil emissions through empirical data combined with stoichiometry and thermodynamics. In addition, the S-LCI provides a benchmark for data collection and processing of energy, chemicals, and materials involved in sewage treatment. The S-LCI helps to reduce uncertainty in LCA studies by enhanced specificity, regionalization, and standardization of data. The features of the S-LCI for environmental assessment were extended to evaluate economic implications of different systems which resulted in more precise costs estimations. Environmental and economic evaluations of different sewage-derived energy systems identified that a hypothetical system consisting of chemically enhanced primary treatment, partial nitritation/anammox fluidized-bed membrane bioreactor (PN/AFMBR) and anaerobic digestion for energy recovery is more eco-efficient than conventional sewage treatment. Integration of the S-LCI into LCA resulted in site-specific environmental and economic assessments of sewage treatment for effective policy decision-making with reduced uncertainty and further understanding of their trade-offs.

15252916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15252916.value: This project mainly generated six journal papers. Four of them have been published in top journals – two in Environmental Science & Technology (ES&T), two in Applied Energy. The other two are expected to be submitted to ES&T by the end of this August. The research findings were also presented at two international conferences. The first paper examines the water-energy nexus associated with the city embedded in the hinterland by using a city-hinterland water-energy mixed-unit input-output methodology. Several indicators in the results compare the interaction between water and energy systems and the dependence on hinterland for different scenarios in Hong Kong. The modeling outcomes show that the current water infrastructures might be able to meet the demand for water treatment in 2050. The second paper presents a novel stoichiometric life-cycle inventory (S-LCI) framework to obtain site-specific water, air, and soil emissions through empirical data combined with stoichiometry and thermodynamics. The S-LCI can help to reduce uncertainty in life-cycle assessment (LCA) studies by enhanced specificity, regionalization, and standardization of data. The third paper integrates the S-LCI into LCA resulted in site-specific environmental and economic assessments of sewage treatment for effective policy decision-making and further understanding their trade-offs. The results suggest future studies focusing on finding alternative materials for the construction of the partial nitritation/anammox fluidized-bed membrane bioreactor (PN/AFMBR) to reduce capital costs. The fourth paper developed an integrated life-cycle data envelopment analysis for techno-environmental performance evaluation on sludge-to-energy systems. The results showed the strong linkage between sludge treatment and energy systems and included all the essential performance metrics in benchmarking the efficiency of the sludge-to-energy systems. The results also informed the appropriate strategies for improving efficiency, such as increasing energy recovery, reducing energy use and scaling up/down the system, for the less efficient systems. The fifth paper developed a microbial individuality model (MIM) which integrates thermodynamics, microbial energetics, and agent-based modeling to describe microbiomes behavior as heterogenic populations., including homoacetogenic bacteria for anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge. The sixed paper presents a hybrid theoretical-machine learning approach leveraging up stoichiometry and kinetics to calculate missing values in limited data sets. Testing procedures for nitrogen compounds concentrations were successful and a good agreement was observed between the measured and predicted values. Besides pollution load, temperature and pH, different microbiomes were identified as key parameters for the performance prediction of the PN/AFMBR.

15252916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15252916.value: The main goal of this project is to achieve environmental sustainability and economic efficiency of sewage treatment systems. Conventional sewage treatment is energy-intensive, which translates into operation costs and carbon dioxide emissions. Emerging processes have been developed but lack of precise evaluations of their benefits. Economic implications of plant-wide systems combining mature and emerging processes should be assessed to determine the funds needed to retrofit existing sewage treatment plants. This project develops various interdisciplinary approaches tightly integrating stoichiometric theory, life-cycle assessment, machine learning, and agent-based modeling to understand and evaluate the trade-offs between economic and environmental impacts of the sewage treatment systems. The further development of the research can focus on 1) stoichiometric equations; 2) integration of heavy metals implications; 3) database expansion; 4) integrating advanced technologies. The project team has been working on developing a virtual sewage treatment system in Python consisting of analytical models. The virtual system will serve as the environment in which the RL agent interacts (take actions) with and ought to generate the most optimal set of control parameters to maximize the reward/efficiency of the system.

15252916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15252916.value: Conventional sewage treatment is energy-intensive, which translates into operational costs and carbon dioxide emissions. Recently developed processes focus on resource recovery and reducing energy consumption, without compromising water effluent quality. Whilst energy self-sufficiency contributes to reducing environmental impacts, a holistic environmental assessment of sewage treatment is needed to ensure that the impacts are not shifted from one category to another. In addition, the economic implications of plant-wide systems combining mature and emerging processes should be assessed to determine the funds needed to retrofit existing sewage treatment plants. An integrated environmental and economic analysis for a whole plant system could provide a further understanding of the potential trade-offs and economic competitiveness of emerging sewage treatment processes. This project developed a series of novel frameworks/tools to help policymakers improve their decision-making for enhancing the sustainability performances of sewage treatment system development. Several strategies and policies are recommended. For example, the study result identified that a hypothetical system consisting of partial nitritation/anammox fluidized-bed membrane bioreactor and anaerobic digestion for energy recovery is more eco-efficient than conventional processes. Site-specific environmental and economic assessment of sewage treatment resulted in more precise environmental impact and cost estimations.

15253916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15253916.value: Magnetostriction materials have received increasing attention due to their promising applications for actuators, sensors and energy harvesting devices, and the achievements in the development of high performance magnetostriction materials over the last few decades. Since the discovery of giant magnetostriction in the TbDyFe alloy (known as Terfenol-D), there have been huge efforts to address the limitations of this alloy such as brittleness, low corrosion resistance and high energy loss. Resulting from these efforts, two new classes of materials, magnetostrictive polymer based composite materials and Gafenol alloys were developed and they have shown a number of attractive properties. Nonetheless, to develop a novel magnetostriction material with a combination of giant magnetostriction at low magnetic fields, good corrosion resistance, good mechanical properties, and low energy loss is still a challenge in this field. As compared to crystalline Terfenol-D, amorphous Terfenol-D films have demonstrated very attractive properties such as high energy density, low field magnetostriction, soft magnetic properties, lower energy loss, enhanced mechanical properties and corrosion resistance. However, the magnetostriction of amorphous films is much below than that of the crystalline alloy, and the amorphous Terfenol-D is still limited to thin films synthesized by sputtering. Most recently, our preliminary findings have demonstrated for the first time that the magnetostriction of rare-earth-transition metal (Tb(Dy)-TM) based glassy ribbons exhibit giant magnetostriction effect. Based on these encouraging findings, attempts will be made to further develop Tb(Dy)-TM metallic glasses with giant magnetostriction at room temperature and good glass forming ability, and to understand their magnetostriction mechanisms. In this project, the glass forming ability and magnetostriction of Tb(Dy)-TM binary/pseudo-binary alloys will be systematically investigated. In order to reveal the magnetostriction mechanisms, the dependence of the microstructure, composition and temperature on the magnetostriction of the amorphous alloys will be investigated. The microstructure of the clusters with short range order will be predicted by a structural prediction method, CALYPSO, and the mechanical and magnetic properties of the clusters and the disordered matrix will be modeled by the first principles electronic structure calculations using CASTEP. A new FEM system constructed by randomly oriented clusters and the surrounded matrix will be employed to simulate the deformation process upon magnetization of the alloys. The composition dependence of the Curie Temperature of the alloys will also be experimentally and theoretically investigated. The project will not only have important applications potential, but will also have significant academic merit in understanding the magnetostriction mechanisms of amorphous materials. 近年来，磁致伸缩材料由于其在传感器、声呐、微波器件、高保真音响和能量收集器方面的应用价值而广受关注，导致了具有优异室温磁致伸缩性能的TbDyFe (terfenol-D)合金的发现。但是这种合金的缺点如容易氧化、比较脆、机械性能低和较低的磁弹性耦合系数限制了其应用范围。为了克服以上缺点，科学家们一方面尝试用聚合物来包裹terfenol-D合金制备成复合材料以改善其机械性能，另一方面加紧开发新型磁致伸缩合金如Fe-Ga (Gafenol）合金。尽管取得了一系列的研究进展，但是寻找具有低场下更高的磁致伸缩系数和磁弹性耦合系数、更低的能量损耗（包括更低的磁滞和更高的电阻）、更高的抗氧化和防腐蚀性能以及更好的机械性能和成型能力的新型磁致伸缩材料却依然是该研究领域的热点。 与晶态材料相比，非晶态TbDyFe材料由于其独特的无序结构和优异的软磁性能，而能够满足上述的大部分性能要求，尤其是非晶态材料具有已知磁致伸缩材料中最高的磁弹性耦合系数。但是非晶态合金的磁致伸缩系数往往远低于晶态合金。值得注意的是，最近申请者和其它研究人员在Tb(Dy)-TM (TM=Fe, Co, Ni)基非晶态条带和薄膜以及一些不完全非晶态的块体材料中发现这些非晶态合金及非晶态复合材料具有从低温到室温的大磁致伸缩系数。在此基础上，我们希望更进一步开发出具有优异玻璃形成能力、室温磁致伸缩性能的Tb(Dy)-TM基非晶态合金，并研究其微观机理。本项目的研究，不仅能揭示非晶态合金中巨磁致伸缩性能的产生机理，具有重要的基础研究价值，而且能够指导设计并开发具有优异综合磁致伸缩性能的新型非晶态材料，具有重大的工业应用前景。

15253916.label: Realisation of objectives
15253916.value: Objective 1. In this project, a series of binary Dy-Co ribbons were synthesized by the melt spinning approach and glassy ribbons were successfully obtained within the compositional range Dy50Co50 to Dy68Co32. The glass formability and magnetic properties of these amorphous alloys were examined. The compositional dependence of glass formability, Curie temperature and magnetic properties of the DyxCo100-x (x=50, 55, 60, 65 and 68) amorphous alloys, as well as the mechanism involved, were determined. Objective 2 The magnetostriction behaviour of a binary Dy50Co50 amorphous alloy at different temperatures was examined. The magnetic behavior of the Dy50Co50 amorphous ribbon is similar to that of canonical spin glass systems, with a Curie temperature of about 106 K and a spin freezing temperature of about 80 K. Hysteresis loops indicate that the amorphous ribbon is paramagnetic at room temperatures, soft magnetic at 60 K to 100 K, and hard magnetic at temperatures well below 60 K. The magnetostriction of the alloy was acquired from 30 K to 90 K, with a high reversible magnetostriction of 320 ppm under a magnetic field of 2T and about 600ppm under a magnetic field of 5T at 60K. The magnetostriction at 30K, however, is irreversible because the magnetostriction of the alloy is still about 37 ppm when the magnetic field returns to zero, which is closely related to the random magnetic anisotropy and the hysteresis of the amorphous ribbon. The reversible magentostriction of the alloy is also found to increase with decreasing temperatures. Objective 3 A series of ternary TbCoFe amorphous ribbons were synthesized by micro-alloying of Fe in the binary Tb60Co40 alloy. The relationship between the glass formability, the Curie temperature and the magnetic properties of the amorphous alloys as a function of the percentage of Fe was examined. It is found that the micro-alloying of Fe can improve the width of the supercooled liquid region but it reduces the glass transition temperature. Meanwhile, the temperature-dependent magnetization curves under a magnetic field of 3.0 T shows a transition from paramagnetism to ferrimagnetism at the Curie temperature, and demonstrates a maximum point below the Curie temperature, which corresponds to the spin freezing point. The Curie temperature is also shown to increase with increasing Fe content, but decrease with increasing Tb. The microstructure of a Tb55Co30Fe15 glassy ribbon and its effect on the magnetic and magnetostrictive properties were further investigated in details.

15253916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15253916.value: During the reporting period, a series of binary Dy-Co ribbons were synthesized and their microstructures, glass forming ability and magnetic properties were characterized. It is shown that the best glass former is Dy60Co40, and the Curie temperature decreases with increasing Dy concentration. The non-linear compositional dependence of the 3d-4f indirect interaction plays a vital role in dominating the Curie temperature of the binary amorphous alloys. Based on these findings, a journal paper entitled “Formability and magnetic properties of Dy-Co binary amorphous alloys” was published in AIP Advances. The magnetostriction of the Dy50Co50 amorphous alloy was acquired from 30 K to 90 K, with a high reversible magnetostriction of 320 ppm under a magnetic field of 2.0 T and about 600 ppm under a magnetic field of 5.0 T, both of which are rather high for Tb(Dy)-TM amorphous alloys. The clusters randomly oriented in the disordered matrix rotate upon magnetization will induce the shear stress on the surrounding matrix, leading to the macro-deformation of the whole sample, and will result in large magnetostriction of amorphous alloys. The findings have resulted in a journal paper entitled “Magnetic properties and magnetostriction of a binary Dy50Co50 amorphous alloy” published in Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids. A low cost Nd50Co50 binary glassy ribbon was further synthesized. The magnetostriction of the Nd50Co50 glassy sample under 5 T reached to 170 ppm, which is not as high as those of Tb(Dy)-based amorphous alloys but much higher than those of TM-based metallic glasses. The binary Nd50Co50 alloy will play a role as basic alloy for developing low-cost multicomponent metallic glasses with outstanding glass formability and magnetostriction. Based on these findings, a paper “Magnetocaloric effect and magnetostriction of a binary Nd50Co50 metallic glass” was submitted to Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids. A Tb55Co30Fe15 ribbon shows typical amorphous characteristics, and its apparent glass formability is better than the binary Tb55Co45 amorphous ribbon. HREM observation has revealed that there are some nanoparticles with an average diameter less than 5 nm distributed randomly in the matrix. The nano-glass structure and the resulting high coercivity of the Tb55Co30Fe15 ribbon led to a rather high value of reversible magnetostriction up to 788 ppm under 5 T, which is almost the highest in the amorphous alloys reported in the literature. Based on these findings, a paper "Microstructure and Its Effect on the Magnetic, Magnetocaloric and Magnetostrictive Properties of Tb55Co30Fe15 Glassy Ribbons” was published in Materials.

15253916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15253916.value: 1. The present project revealed that a ternary amorphous ribbon with giant magnetstriction can be synthesized through composition and microstructural design. It is most worthwhile to further enhance the properties of the amorphous alloys for commerical applications by optimizing their compositions and microstructures. 2. A new low cost Nd50Co50 binary glassy ribbon was reported in the project. Although its magnetostriction is much higher than those of TM-based metallic glasses, it is not as high as those of Tb(Dy)-based amorphous alloys. It is most worthwhile to further enhance the magnetostriction of low cost amorphous alloys for commercial applications. New research funding will be applied for in due course to support these research works.

15253916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15253916.value: Amorphous magnetostriction materials exhibit many unique properties as compared to crystalline alloys. However, the magnetostriction of amorphous materials is still much less than of the crystalline alloys and the amorphous magnetostriction materials are still limited to thin films. The project aims to understand how the microstructure affects the magnetostriction of amorphous alloys in order to develop novel amorphous alloys with giant magnetostriction, and to synthesize alloys in forms other than thin films. In this project, a series of binary and ternary amorphous alloys were synthesized and investigated. A Tb55Co30Fe15 amorphous alloy was found to exhibit good glass formability and a gaint reversible magnetostriciton up to 788 ppm under 5T. Some nanoparticles with an average diameter less than 5 nm distributed randomly in the matrix were observed and the formation of the nanoparticles due to the positive mixing enthalpy between the Tb and Fe atoms has led to a high value of magnetostriction. The findings do not only have significant academic value in understanding the effect of microstructures on the magnetostriction of amorphous alloys, but also have a great impact on the design of new magnetostrictive amorphous materials.

15255416.value: 正倒向帶混合約束隨機系統的最優控制及金融應用

15255416.label: Project Objectives
15255416.value: The first is to develop a general theory on optimal controls of forward-backward stochastic systems with mixed state-control constraints. We plan to apply Ekeland's variational principle to derive a Pontryagin type maximum principle for our problem. The second is to study forward-backward linear-quadratic optimal controls with mixed constraints. We plan to analyze this problem via backward stochastic differential Riccati-like equations derived by virtue of the technique of completion of squares and the general results established in objective (1). The third is to extend the results obtained in objectives (1) and (2) to investigate a mean--semi-variance model with bankruptcy prohibition and no-shorting constraints.

The second is to study forward-backward linear-quadratic optimal controls with mixed constraints. 15255416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15255416.value: 混合約束隨機最優控制問題在許多領域，如管理，工程，經濟以及財務投資的重要應用。近來，對於這種類型的隨機控制問題以及解決其應用領域的研究受到越來越多的關注。在這一領域的理論已經在過去幾十年對正向隨機動態系統获得了很好的發展。然而，學者尚未充分研究倒向帶端終端狀態的隨機系統。本項目旨在解決這一具有混合約束正倒向動態系統特徵的長期難題，它不僅具有理論意義，而且更具有實際意義。在本研究項目中，我們計劃發展一些新的方法克服由隨機系數而自然產生的高難度帶約束隨機控制問題，這與現有文獻中所涉及確定性系數問題有顯著的不同。此外，我們應用所得的理論結果處理以一個具有挑戰性的，但實際上是相關且重要的決策模型， 其為帶破產約束和不可賣空約束的金融投資問題。此模型將幫助投資者更好地理解和有效地管理風險資產，以實現在有限投資期限的最大回報。
