15256816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15256816.value: Hong Kong has recently embarked on two asphalt pavement recycling programs: plant recycling that uses a maximum of 30% of reclaimed asphalt pavements (RAP) in new mixtures and hot in-place recycling (HIPR) that uses 100% of existing pavements. Local and oversea experiences, however, have indicated that cracks develop more rapidly in pavements containing RAP or in HIPR pavements. This behavior is mainly caused by the increase in asphalt binder stiffness in the old pavements due to aging. To offset the aging effects, rejuvenating agents (rejuvenators) are often used. Most rejuvenators, however, are “black boxes” to pavement engineers in that neither their fundamental mechanisms nor specific effects are fully understood. This lack of understanding hinders the effective use of rejuvenators in asphalt pavement recycling. This study aims to investigate the evolutions and connections of asphalt binder properties during the asphalt binder aging, rejuvenation, and re-aging processes. Emphasis will be placed on the impacts of different rejuvenation mechanisms on binder performance. Factors affecting the diffusion efficiency of rejuvenators into aged asphalt binders will also be examined. Insights gained from the above will be verified through laboratory mixture tests and field implementations. Asphalt binders will be aged in a special aging vessel at field temperatures to examine the aging effects and prepare the aged binders for rejuvenation. Commercial and tailor-made rejuvenators will be used to rejuvenate the aged binders, which will be re-aged in the special vessel. During the aging, rejuvenation, and re-aging processes, binders will be tested for the chemical, physicochemical, and performance-related rheological properties. The connections between the properties will be investigated. Diffusion coefficients of rejuvenator and binder combinations will be determined through laboratory tests. Using the coefficients and previously determined binder properties, the effects of rejuvenator types, asphalt binder types and aging states, and temperatures on rejuvenator diffusion efficiency will be quantified. The effects of rejuvenation and diffusion on mixture performance will be verified through rutting, fracture and fatigue resistance tests. Rutting tests will use new mixture samples, while fracture and fatigue tests will use compacted mixture samples subjected to simulated long-term field aging in another special vessel. The effective rejuvenation products and methods will be verified through field trials. The outcomes of the study include: (1) insights into the asphalt binder aging, rejuvenation, and re-aging processes, (2) better rejuvenators, (3) better rejuvenator application methods, and (4) insights into long-term rejuvenation effectiveness. The study is anticipated to improve asphalt pavement recycling practices locally and worldwide. 香港最近開始實施兩種瀝青路面的回收方案：使用不超過30%的回收瀝青路面（RAP）材料的廠拌熱再生和使用100％現有路面材料的就地熱再生。但是，本地和海外的經驗表明，使用回收瀝青材料的路面更容易產生裂縫。其成因 主要是回收瀝青材料中瀝青膠結料的氧化老化。為了抵​​消老化效應，在使用回收瀝青材料時常常加入一些再生劑。但是，對道路工程師而言，市場上銷售的再生劑像“黑盒子”一樣。無論是它們的作用機理，或者是​​長期的使用效果，往往不得而知。對再生劑的不了解阻礙了對它的合理和有效地使用。 這個項目的目的是研究瀝青膠結料在瀝青的老化、再生和重新老化過程中性質的變化和性質的關聯。本項目重點研究再生劑的作用機理以及對瀝青性質的影響。此外，本項目也將研究影響再生劑在舊瀝青中的擴散效率。這些研究將通過混合料實驗室測試和現場試驗加以驗證。 在試驗過程中，我們將用一個特殊設計的壓力老化容器對瀝青進行老化。我們也將購買商業的瀝青再生劑和製備瀝青再生劑。商業的瀝青再生劑和製備的瀝青再生劑將被用來再生老化的瀝青。經過再生的瀝青將在特殊設計的壓力老化容器內被重新老化。在瀝青的老化、再生和重新老化的過程中，我們將測試其基本的化學、物理化學和流變性質，同時研究這些性質的相關關係。 我們將在試驗室研究中確定再生劑的擴散效率係數。使用該係數和瀝青的性質，我們將量化再生劑的類型、瀝青膠的類型和老化程度、溫度等因素對再生劑的擴散效率的影響。 再生和擴散對混合料性能的影響將通過車轍、裂縫和抗疲勞性能試驗加以驗證。車轍試驗將使用新的混合料，而斷裂和疲勞試驗將使用經過模擬長期老化的混合料。最有效的再生產品和方法將通過現場試驗進行驗證。 本項目的研究結果包括：（1）瀝青老化、再生和再老化過程中深刻的物理化學性質變化，（2）更佳的再生劑，（3）更佳的再生劑的使用方法，和（4 ）再生瀝青的長期有效性。這項研究預計將對本地和世界瀝青路面的回收和再生產生長遠的影響。

15256816.label: Realisation of objectives
15256816.value: With generous support from RGC and other stakeholders such as Hong Kong Highways Department, Nano and Advanced Materials Institute (NAMI) of Hong Kong, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and the paving industry in Hong Kong, the project has been satisfactorily completed. The original proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. Fundamental and significant findings have been made based on this project. The realisation of objectives is explained as follows. Objective one: To characterize the evolutions of chemical, physicochemical, and performance-related rheological properties of asphalt binders during the oxidative aging, rejuvenation, and re-aging processes. We have made significant progress in characterizing the fundamental of chemical, physicochemical, and performance-related rheological properties of asphalt binders during aging, rejuvenation, and re-aging. For the first time in the world, we observed the actual asphalt microstructures at the nanoscale, thanks to a patent we developed to prepare special samples for Scanning Transmission Electronic Microscopy (STEM). With this new technique, we can exam the morphology of asphalt binders without solvent extraction. Consequently, the true existing states of nanoscale microstructures in asphalt binders are not disturbed. Asphalt binders from different parts of the world and from different sources were used for investigation. We have aged asphalt binders to different extents by using different methods. We also extracted asphalt binders from field pavements of different ages. Aged binders were also subjected to rejuvenation treatments. Such binder samples were systematically tested for chemical, physicochemical, and performance-related rheological properties, including Corbett fractions, Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), zero-shear viscosities (ZSVs) of the binders and their maltene phases, dynamic shear, fatigue, etc. The research findings from the experiments are reported in several papers published or under review. Objective two: To quantify the impacts of chemical and physicochemical property changes on the rheological and micromechanical property changes. Using the test data from chemical and physicochemical characterization, we systematically evaluated the impacts of fundamental physicochemical properties on rheological and micromechanical property changes. We believe that our findings profoundly reveal the physicochemical origins of asphalt binder performance. The asphaltene contents of asphalt binders from different sources and different aging states were determined, and the zero-shear viscosities (ZSVs) of the binders and their maltene phases were tested at different temperatures. The size of asphaltenes in the asphalt binders was examined and approximately quantified with the assistance of scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and image analysis. Note that solvent was not used in sample preparation; therefore, asphaltene microstructures in the STEM images represent the true states of observable asphaltenes in asphalt binders. It was found that asphaltene content and ZSV can well explain most of the commonly reported properties of asphalt binders, including ZSV, dynamic viscosity, rutting parameter, fatigue parameter, phase angle, crossover frequency, Glover-Rowe (G-R) parameters, relaxation time, etc. However, asphaltene content cannot explain the fracture and fatigue behaviors of asphalt binders, for which the quantity of large-size asphaltene microstructures and maltene viscosities play the most critical role. Objective three: To quantify factors affecting rejuvenator diffusion into aged asphalt binders. Asphalt binder is essentially a nanomaterial with colloidal particles suspended in an oily medium. As asphalt binder ages, the colloidal particles are subject to fundamental physicochemical changes such as agglomeration, which is translated into dramatic engineering property changes of the asphalt binder. In engineering practices, organic rejuvenators are often added to the aged asphalt binder, with the hope to breakdown the nanoparticles and restore its original engineering properties. However, how the nanoparticles evolve during rejuvenation of asphalt binder remains hypothetical. We revealed the fundamental changes of the colloidal particles in asphalt binder during rejuvenation. Moreover, changes in morphology of the colloidal particles are connected to the relaxation spectrum of the asphalt binder. As a result, practitioners do not have to rely on complicated methods and equipment to observe asphalt binders at the microscopic level. Instead, they can employ commonly used engineering tests with a dynamic shear rheometer (DSR) to decipher what occurs at the nanoscale during asphalt binder rejuvenation. This would greatly assist practitioners in material selection and design. Using the methods, we also identified factors affecting rejuvenation diffusion. Objective four: To verify the effects of rejuvenation mechanisms and diffusion on pavement rutting resistance, fracture resistance and fatigue resistance through laboratory tests and field trials. Based on objective 1-3 and collaborated with Nano and Advanced Materials Institute (NAMI) of Hong Kong, we have developed new rejuvenators and also used the new rejuvenators to treat asphalt samples. We tested pavement rutting resistance, fracture resistance and fatigue resistance. We successfully placed two field pavements located in Sheung Shui, Hong Kong. Overall, the research objectives are realised through well-planned experiments, theoretical and methodological developments.

15256816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15256816.value: This research aimed to identify the scientific and engineering principles of asphalt aging and rejuvenation and find ways to improve the performance of asphalt pavement with RAP through effective rejuvenation. We have made the following major findings through this study: (1) The true nature of asphalt binder has been under debate. With the newly developed method, we clearly revealed through scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) that asphalt binder is a colloidal suspension, with asphaltenes as particulate phase and maltenes as liquid medium. (2) We found that asphaltene particles increase by quantity and size with asphalt binder aging. (3) We found that asphaltene particles increase by quantity and size with asphalt binder aging. (4) We found that Changes in asphaltene microstructures after rejuvenation are affected by asphalt binder type and rejuvenator type. (5) Currently, commonly tested and reported asphalt binder properties include stiffness and viscosity, phase angle, rutting parameter, fatigue parameter, crossover frequency, Glover-Rowe (G-R) parameters (indicating asphalt’s fracture tendency). All these parameters can be well explained by just two fundamental physicochemical properties of asphalt binders: maltene viscosity and asphaltene content. (6) We found that the true facture/fatigue behaviours of asphalt binders cannot be well tested through existing test methods as mentioned above. Asphaltene size and maltene viscosity play important roles. (7) We found that the relaxation behaviours of asphalt binders, which determine their thermal cracking and loading-related fracturing behaviors, cannot be revealed through conventional test methods. (8) We found that rejuvenators are indeed effective in improving asphalt pavement performance, especially in anti-cracking and anti-fracturing performance. However, the effectiveness of rejuvenators is not very dramatic. In addition, the effectiveness of the rejuvenators depends on material selection and construction techniques. This research has led to the following major research outcomes: (1) New methods to analyze the physicochemical property changes of asphalt binders in aging and rejuvenation; (2) New models were developed to predict the microscopic property changes of asphalt binders thorough macroscopic tests; (3) New methods to characterize fatigue behaviors of asphalt binders and mixtures. (4) New methods to develop master curves of asphalt binders, and master curves are an essential tool to character asphalt binders; (5) Significant scientific findings on the nature of asphalt binder, especially its changes in aging and rejuvenation; (6) Discovering a serious existing issue in the current analysis method by using gel permeation spectroscopy (GPC). (7) Strategies to improve the durability of asphalt pavements incorporated with RAP.

15256816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15256816.value: The research can be further developed to create greater impact. Using more recycled asphalt pavements (RAP) materials is widely pursued worldwide. However, the deteriorated performance of pavements using high RAP content is a concern. This research developed theories and methods to explain this issue and to help address this issue. Future studies will be more focused on the practical aspects of using RAP and rejuvenators. We will communicate with the Highways Department in Hong Kong on our research findings, with the hope that the research findings and methods can be turned into more practices. In addition, we will very actively promote the research findings through more publications and conference talks, with the hope that more researchers and practitioners can follow the recommended practices developed in this study. We will also apply additional funding to continuously support this meaningful study.

15256816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15256816.value: With increased concern on environmental conservation, the paving industry starts to add more recycled asphalt pavements (RAP) materials into new asphalt mixtures. However, field experiments indicate that using RAP causes early-age cracking of asphalt pavements. In this research, we revealed the true nature of asphalt binder and proved that it is a nanomaterial composed of nanoscale particles and liquid. We analyzed what occurs at the fundamental physicochemical levels of asphalt binders during their aging and rejuvenation. We found that the particles in asphalt binders grow more and much bigger during aging, while the liquid phase stays relatively the same. We found that nearly all the asphalt binder properties can be well explained through the characteristics of the nanoscale particles (quantity, size, shape) and the liquid medium. In using RAP in new asphalt mixtures, we have to understand the asphalt binder deterioration in RAP and take measures to mitigate such effect. It is necessary to use rejuvenators if we want to increase RAP content. However, the effectiveness of rejuvenators depends on multiple factors, including material type, construction techniques, and treatment methods. This research provides new and easy-to-use methods to evaluate pavement performance containing RAP and the effectiveness of rejuvenation.

15259716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15259716.value: In hot and humid climates, such as Hong Kong, air conditioning (A/C) is usually required for more than 7 months from April to October in the year. At different seasons within the 7 months, however, space latent load that directly affects indoor air humidity level can vary significantly. On the other hand, direct expansion (DX) based A/C systems are widely used for controlling indoor air temperature and humidity in various buildings in hot and humid climates. Once installed, however, they have to be operated at different seasonal cooling load situations, and hence have a hard time in trying to maintain the desired indoor thermal environment at all time, unless complicated and costly supplementary measures to supply additional dehumidification capacity when required are provided. In this proposed project, a novel standalone enhanced dehumidification air conditioning (EDAC) system is to be developed. The EDAC system will have two evaporators connected in parallel and is suitable for use in different seasons for improved year round indoor humidity control in hot and humid climates, without requiring any supplementary measures to provide additional dehumidification capacity. An experimental prototype EDAC system will be established and extensive experiments carried out to evaluate its operational performance in terms of indoor thermal environmental control and energy efficiency. A steady-state mathematical model for the prototype will be developed and experimentally validated, and the validated model will be used to further optimize the configuration and design of an EDAC system. The successful carrying out of the proposed project will help achieve better thermal comfort for occupants, improved indoor air quality (IAQ) and reduced energy use, using standalone EDAC systems that are less complicated and costly, so as to save the capital and operational costs, and installation space of the DX based air conditioning in buildings. The long-term significance of the proposed project is its contribution to sustainability by reducing energy use for air conditioning in buildings while improving the thermal comfort of building occupants, and to the advancement of DX A/C technology. While the project outcomes are expected to be applicable to all hot and humid climates, they will be particularly useful to Hong Kong where DX A/C systems are widely used and dehumidification using DX A/C systems has always been a big challenge. 在熱濕地區，例如香港，在一年中4月到10月長達7個月甚至更長的時間內，空調系統(A/C) 是必不可少的。在這段跨越了幾個不同的季節區域的7個月當中，直接影響到室內的濕度水準的潛熱負荷也會出現不同的變化情況。另一方面，在熱濕天氣條件下，直膨式(DX) 空調系統被廣泛應用於不同的建築來控制調節室內的溫濕度。然而，這些空調系統在安裝之後就需要在不同的季節空調負荷下運行，因此很難在所有條件下一直保持室內所需求的熱濕環境，除非採用一些輔助的措施在需要的情況下提供額外的除濕能力，然後這些措施往往都比較複雜和昂貴的。 在所提議的項目中，提出和發展了一個新型獨立的除濕增強型空調系統 (EDAC)。該系統有兩個並聯佈置的蒸發器，可以在不採用提供任何輔助手段來提供額外除濕能力的條件下就能夠滿足熱濕地區不同季節情況下對室內濕度的控制要求，從而有效的改善全年的室內濕度水準。專案中將會搭建該除濕增強型空調系統的實驗樣機並且進行相關的實驗，從室內的熱濕環境的控制以及能效兩個方面來對該系統進行評估驗證。除此之外，還將會建立該實驗系統的穩態數學模型並進行相關的實驗驗證，驗證後的模型可用於進一步優化和改善該除濕增強型空調系統的配置和設計。 該專案的成功實施將會給予住戶更好的熱舒適性體驗和更佳的室內空氣品質(IAQ)，除此之外，得益於該系統相對簡單低廉的優點以及直膨式空調在建築中安裝空間小的特性，能夠説明節約系統初始的投資以及運行的費用，從而大大的節省了能源的消耗使用。從長遠的效果來看，該項目的實施能夠通過改善建築居民熱舒適性以及節約大量的空調能源消耗這兩個方面為可持續性發展做出貢獻，並且對直膨式空調技術的進一步發展完善也能起到了很大的作用。由於該項目主要針對熱濕氣候條件下進行的，因此所獲得的成果對於直膨式空調應用廣泛但除濕難度較大的香港地區具有更加重要的意義。

15260316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15260316.value: This project is to study photothermal (PT) phase modulation due to stimulated Raman-scattering (SRS) in a gas-filled hollow-core (HC) optical fibre and achieve high-sensitivity detection of hydrogen and other gases that have no or very weak absorption in the transmission window of the fibre. Recently we developed an optical fibre PT interferometry (PTI) technique for gas detection. The technique uses a pump-probe configuration: absorption of a modulated pump beam propagating in a gas-filled HC-fibre resulting in localized heating, which modulates the accumulated phase of a probe beam propagating in the same fibre. With all-fibre interferometry, we demonstrated acetylene sensors with detection limit down to ppb level and dynamic range up to six orders of magnitude. However, this technique is only applicable to molecules that are absorptive in the transmission window of the fibre. Here we extend the technique to detect gases that do not necessarily have absorption lines within the transmission window of the HC-fibre. Many gas molecules have characteristic Raman transitions that can be used to identify and detect the concentration of these gases. By propagating a Raman pump and a stimulating (Stokes) laser beam in the same HC-fibre and tuning their frequency difference to the Raman transition frequency, SRS is enabled. This process generates heat that modulates the phase of another beam (probe) propagating in the same HC-fibre, which can be detected with fibre-optic interferometry. Our preliminary analysis shows that such SRS-based PTI would enable hydrogen and other gas sensors with detection limit down to ppm level or below, which would be useful for a range of important applications in energy, aerospace, chemical and medical industries. To our knowledge, such a Raman-based PTI sensor has not been reported previously. SRS, rather than spontaneous-Raman-scattering, is employed here because of its much higher heating efficiency. We plan to investigate theoretically and experimentally the PT phase modulation associated with SRS in HC-fibres; study the effects of different modulation format (pulsed and sinusoidally wavelength-modulated continuous wave (CW)) and parameters (duration and repetition rate of the pulses, frequency of sinusoidally modulated-CW), the power (energy) level, wavelength and linewidth of the Raman pump and stimulating beams, on the magnitude of phase modulation; analyze performance limiting factors such as background noise due to non-linear (e.g., Raman and Kerr) effect in silica, and thermal and pressure dependence of system scale factor; evaluate the performance of the entire gas detection system and the potential widespread application of the technique. 近来我们一直在研究基于光热效应的气体传感技术。这项技术使用泵浦-探测的方法︰ 在充气的空芯光纤中传输的泵浦光被气体吸收后导致局部加热，引起探测光的相位变化。应用光纤干涉仪进行相位检测可实现高灵敏的气体探测。应用这一技术，我们实现了ppb量级的乙炔气体测量，动态范围达6个数量级。 这些性能指标比以前的直接吸收型光纤气体传感器提高了约3个数量级，但该方法只适用于吸收型气体分子。 本项目将研究空芯充气光纤中的拉曼光热过程以及基于该效应的气体传感器，目的是对没有吸收或吸收较弱的气体分子进行探测。我们将进行理论和实验研究拉曼过程引起的相位调制效应，研究不同系统参数对相位调制的影响，分析各种限制传感器性能的因素，评估该检测技术的应用前景。

15260316.label: Realisation of objectives
15260316.value: Objective 1: Photothermal (PT) phase modulation due to stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) in a gas-filled hollow-core fiber HCF was theoretically investigated. We selected molecular hydrogen as the target gas to be measured. The Raman transition of hydrogen includes vibrational and rotational branches. We chose the strongest bands of them, which are respectively the Q1 and S0 branches. We firstly studied the use of SRS spectroscopy for trace hydrogen detection in a gas-filled photonic bandgap HCF. The fiber used was the HC-1550 fiber from NKT photonics and the low-loss transmission band is from 1500 to 1700 nm. We used a pump around 1530 nm and Stokes around 1620 nm, corresponding to the S0(0) transition with a Raman shift of about 354 cm−1. This transition is not the strongest in the S0 branch, however it fits the transmission band of the HC-1550 fiber. With these pump and Stokes wavelengths, we conducted theoretical and experimental studies of hydrogen detection with the HC-1550 fiber and demonstrated both “point” and “distributed” sensors with limit of detection down to a few tens of ppm (parts per million) hydrogen in nitrogen. We conducted further investigation of SRS spectroscopy with optical nanofibers, which were taper-drawn from standard telecommunication single mode fibers, and achieved ppm level detection sensitivity with a 5-cm-long nanofiber. We then studied the PT phase modulation due to SRS. We examined the S0(0), S0(1) and Q1(1) transitions, which have Raman shifts of 354 cm-1, 587 cm-1, and 4155 cm-1, respectively. The wavelength (frequency) differences (shifts) of the S0(1) and Q1(1) transitions do not fit the transmission band of the photonic bandgap HCF (i.e., HC-1550); however, it fits the transmission bands of some of the newly developed anti-resonant HCFs. Similar to SRS spectroscopy, we use the pump and Stokes corresponding the Raman transitions, but an additional probe beam that is away from the Raman transitions; the phase change of the probe is used as a measure of the SRS-induced PT effect or Raman PT (RPT) effect. Extensive theoretical and numerical analysis have been conducted to determine the change of temperature and refractive index distribution and finally the probe phase modulation in the HCF, due to SRS-induced heating. The analysis includes the effects of modulation formats (modulated CW and pulsed), modulation parameters (amplitude and frequency of modulated CW, repetition rate and duration of the pulsed), the three different Raman transitions (i.e., S0(0), S0(1) and Q1(1)), wavelength and power levels and polarizations of the pump and Stokes, gas parameters (concentration and pressure), different HCFs (HC-1550 and anti-resonant HCFs with different core sizes), and different propagation modes (i.e., LP01 and LP11) of the probe in the fibers Eventually, for the HC-1550 fiber, we selected 1530 nm as the pump and 1620 nm as the Stokes (i.e., S0(0) transition) and 1550 nm as the probe, considering the limited transmission bandwidth of the HCF and the availability of the laser sources. For the anti-resonant HCFs, the transmission band is much broader, and hence we selected 940 nm as the pump and 1540 nm as the Stokes (i.e., Q1(1) transition), considering the wavelength dependence of the Raman gain coefficient, the availability of the laser sources, and dependence of heat generation on the Raman frequency shift. The frequency shift of the Q1(1) transition is about 12 time larger than that of S0(0), meaning a significantly higher heat generation efficiency can be obtained . The probe wavelength for the anti-resonant HCFs is also selected to be 1550 nm, taking advantages of the most mature fiber components and laser source technologies. We also studied different probe interferometer configurations for detecting the RPT phase modulation. For the HC-1550 fiber-based system, a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with the HCF placed in one of its arms was identified as the most suitable setup. For the anti-resonant HCF-based system, since the fiber can be designed to operate in a dual-mode regime, a dual-mode HCF interferometer was identified to have a better noise performance as compared with a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Objective 2: Experiment was firstly conducted with the HC-1550 fiber, with pump, Stokes, and probe wavelengths selected as 1530 nm, 1620 nm, and 1550 nm respectively. The 1530 nm and the 1620 nm lasers are combined with a wavelength division multiplexer and launched into a 5-m-long HC-1550 fiber to produce the RPT phase modulation. A Mach-Zehnder interferometer stabilized at quadrature at the probe wavelength was used to detect the phase modulation. However, the output from the interferometer was found very noisy and no clear RPT phase modulation signal can be observed for even large concentration of hydrogen in nitrogen (i.e., 20% to 100%). Analysis of the results showed that several factors may affect the system performance: (i) the Raman gain coefficient reduces with increasing pump wavelength, the gain coefficient at 1530 nm is about 3 times smaller than that at 940 nm, which reduces the RPT phase modulation; (ii) the Raman shift is small (~354 cm-1 for the S0(0)), which further reduces the RPT phase modulation; (iii) the Stokes laser power level is small, which also reduces the RPT phase modulation, since the RPT phase modulation is proportional to the product of the pump and the Stokes power levels; (iv) the HC-1550 fiber is not a good single mode fiber and it supports several cladding modes, which generates considerable noise due to coherent mixing of the these modes. Thanks to the recent advance in anti-resonant HCFs, which overcomes most of the aforementioned problems. The broader transmission windows allow us to use a shorter pump wavelength and the Q1(1) transition, which enhances significantly the RPT phase modulation. The anti-resonant HCFs can operate in the dual-mode regime, which allows to use the dual-mode interferometer to achieve better phase detection sensitivity. By use of a 300-mW, 940-nm external cavity diode laser as the pump, a 1542-nm distributed feedback diode laser (amplified to 300 mW) as the Stokes, and a fiber laser at 1550 nm as probe, we conducted hydrogen detection experiments with a 4-m-long anti-resonant HCF. A dual-mode interferometer was used to detect the differential phase modulation between the LP01 and the LP11 probe modes. The RPT phase modulation signal was measured for varying modulation frequency, pump and Stokes power levels, and hydrogen concentration and gas pressure. With a modulation frequency of 3 kHz and by detecting the 2nd harmonic of the RPT phase modulation signal, hydrogen detection with detection limit from 69 ppm to 3 ppm was demonstrated with integration time from 1 s to 1500 s. This is the first experimental demonstration of RPT interferometry (RPTI) for gas detection! It is exciting and further improvement is expected and the technique can be extended to the detection of other trace chemicals in gas or liquid phases.

15260316.label: Major findings and research outcome
15260316.value: (i) We demonstrated the first distributed hydrogen sensors by use of SRS in hollow-core optical fibers. The approach of distributed Raman measurement represents a new paradigm in fiber sensors, potentially allowing distributed chemical analysis in gas or liquid phase with high sensitivity and selectivity, and over a long distance. [Fan et al, OPTICS EXPRESS, Vol. 27, No. 9, 12869-12882, Apr 2019]. (ii) We demonstrated a nanofiber-based gas sensor that can detect hydrogen from a few ppm (parts per million) to 100% with a response time less than 10 s. The sensor would be useful for a range of applications, including detection of hydrogen leakage as well as monitoring of battery charging, fuel cells, and electric power transformer health conditions. [Qi et al, OPTICA, Vol. 6, No. 5, 570-576, May 2019]. A paper reporting the results received the best conference paper award at the 26th International Conference on Optical Fiber Sensors, Lausanne, Switzerland, 24-28 Sept 2018. (iii) As compared with conventional PT sensors with Mach-Zehnder or other two-beam interferometers, the mode-phase-difference PT spectroscopy demonstrated better noise performance and longer term stability. [Zhao et al, OPTICS LETTERS, Vol. 45, No. 20, 5660-5663, October 2020] (iv) We studied the temperature dependence of PT phase modulation and demonstrated a methane sensor with signal stability better than 2.1% over a temperature range of 296 to 373 K. [Zhao et al, Optics Letters, Vol. 46, No. 11, 2762-2765, June 2021] (v) We proposed a new technique, named Raman PT interferometry (RPTI) spectroscopy. We developed theory, conducted numerical modelling and experimentally demonstrated the detection of hydrogen down to ppm level. [Zhao and Jin, Under Preparation – this paper is still under preparation, but the results are very exciting].

15260316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15260316.value: The Raman PT interferometry (RPTI) is a new spectroscopic technique that has not been reported previously to the best of our knowledge. The technique may be used to detect molecules that are weak in absorption but Raman active. It could be useful for a range of applications in chemical tracing and monitoring of chemical reactions. We plan to further develop the technique by applying GRF or ITF grants, in collaboration with potential users of the technique.

15260316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15260316.value: Conventional optical fiber photothermal interferometry (PTI) is only applicable to molecules that are absorptive in the transmission window of the fiber. Here we demonstrate a novel spectroscopic technique, namely Raman PTI (RPTI). This technique can detect gases that do not necessarily have absorption lines within the transmission window of the fiber. Many gas molecules have characteristic Raman transitions that can be used to identify and detect the concentration of these gases. By propagating a Raman pump and a Stokes laser beams in a gas-filled hollow-core fiber (HCF) and tuning their frequency difference to a Raman transition, stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) is enabled. This process generates heat that modulates the phase of another beam (probe) propagating in the same HCF. By use of a 4-m-long anti-resonant HCF, a 940 nm pump and a 1542 nm Stokes to generate PT phase modulation, and a 1550 nm probe beam in combination with a modal interferometer to detect the phase modulation, we experimentally demonstrated, for the first time to our knowledge, RPTI for gas detection; and achieved detection of hydrogen down to ppm level. This technique would be useful for the detection of wide range of gases for applications in energy, aerospace, chemical and medical industries.

15260416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15260416.value: In Hong Kong, the repair, maintenance, alteration and addition (RMAA) sector become a more significant component of the construction industry with the implementation of the Mandatory Building Inspection Scheme (MBIS) by the Hong Kong SAR Government. Around 2,000 buildings would be targeted each year under the MBIS and it is expected that the volume of RMAA works will continue to increase. The public consultation paper issued by the Housing, Planning and Lands Bureau indicates that the number of private buildings over 30 years’ old in Hong Kong will rise to 22,000 by 2018. The condition of buildings becomes dilapidated as building age increases. Electrical and Mechanical (E&M) installations play an important role and involve a large number of practitioners. Among different types of accident, falls of persons from height and electrocution are the top two E&M works killers. The safety of E&M work has not received sufficient attention. Only a very limited amount of safety research on E&M works especially in the RMAA sector has taken place. This proposed study aims to reveal the causes of accidents on E&M works in the RMAA sector and provide recommendations to improve the safety and health of E&M practitioners. The research will focus on the two major types of accidents, fall of person from height and electrocution. Among various safety analysis of accident causes, Bayesian network (BN) analysis is becoming a popular technique as it represent a set of variables and their dependencies to establish cause-effect relationships with a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Cases collected from the Coroner’s Court and the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department (EMSD) will be analysed. The cause factors of E&M accidents will be preliminarily identified and become the variable of the BN structure. Focus group meetings with frontline workers and experts will identify values for the variables and indicate the direction of each pair of relationships. Structured interviews will solicit views of different stakeholders to fine tune the BN model. A questionnaire survey will be conducted to collect more data for parameter estimation of the model. Research findings will be disseminated via industry forums. The significance of the proposed study lies in providing a thorough E&M accident analysis in the RMAA sector, for the first time. A systematic approach with multidisciplinary inputs will lead to the identification of the causes of accidents and the formulation of holistic and practical measures for preventing accidents on E&M related RMAA works.

15260416.label: Realisation of objectives
15260416.value: Scope of investigation undertaken: 1. An extensive review of related literature from textbooks, professional journals, conference papers, refereed publications, research monographs, and internet materials has been launched to capture and document the background knowledge about E&M works safety especially in the RMAA sector and application of Bayesian network approach in construction. 2. Death investigation reports were retrieved from the Coroner’s Court, the Judiciary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Twenty-one fatal case files related to E&M works between 2011 and 2016 in Hong Kong were collected and examined. The cases include almost all those that occurred during the period and finished the investigation process. Each case file provided witness statements taken from the police officers, death investigation report which summarize of the project background information, information of the deceased taken from family members, co-workers, supervisors and employers and accidents circumstances, autopsy report, toxicological examination report and medical report. 3. An empirical questionnaire survey has been carried out with frontline staff involved in E&M RMAA project. The questionnaire aims to measure E&M frontline workers’ perceptions on safety climate, safety performance and working conditions of E&M RMAA works. All respondents possessed hand-on experience in E&M RMAA projects. They represented different trades in E&M sector includes air-conditioning, lift/ escalator installation, electrical wiring, plumbing and drainage and fire services. 4. A generic BN model was developed to illustrate the interrelationship between safety factors and safety performance and identify the influential factors. Netica software package developed by Norsys Software Corporation was used to establish calculate and assess the probabilities of the different states of each node in the model. The Netica software program facilitates the sensitivity analyses also known as ‘reasoning’ to estimate the effects of the changes of safety factors on the safety performance of E&M RMAA works. Significant results achieved: 1. The current research gained a sound understanding of the knowledge of construction and E&M works safety, RMAA works safety, the rationale for Bayesian Network approach and its application in various research aspects and construction safety. 2. Twenty-one fatal cases were collected from 2011 to 2016 related to E&M works from the Coroner’s Court of the Judiciary of Hong Kong. The investigate process of all collected cases were entirely completed. The purpose of studying the report to identify trends in the type of incidents, record contributory factors and allow to learn from the incidents reported. The Loughborough Construction Accident Causation (ConAC) model was adopted to fatal accident analysis. Characteristics of these accidents, any unsafe factors and the locations where they occur were comprehensively investigated. Each collected fatal case was analysed against the four categories of Loughborough ConAC model: (1) work team, workplace, materials and equipment, and originating influences. Based on the Loughborough ConAC model, 157 total immediate causes, shaping factors and originating influences were identified by reviewing 21 fatal cases investigation files with an average of 7.48 causes, factors or influences per case. The model provides an opportunity for researchers and industrial practitioners with a thorough and useful technique to identify immediate causes, latent personal, technical, environmental and organizational oriented influences. The model was successful as a tool to identify multiple causes and influences. Furthermore, the causes, factors and influences can be analysed to understand how they are co-related in an incident. This can assist to explain how originating influences affect worker action, behaviours and work conditions within construction companies. 3. 730 sets of completed questionnaires were collected in March 2018 to investigate effective measures to improve safety performance and achieve better allocation of safety resources in E&M RMAA projects. The questionnaire was designed to collect their personal attributes, attitudes towards safety factors and accident records. The questionnaires were distributed to related government departments, E&M contractors, E&M subcontractors, E&M trade unions and E&M contractor associations in Hong Kong. 4. The Bayesian network model parameters were developed by using the data from the survey. The survey database was then used to estimate the model parameters (i.e. the conditional probabilities). In the current research, the E-M algorithm was implemented by using the Netica software package developed by Norsys Software Corporation. This algorithm was considered appropriate for the use of the data from the questionnaire survey for parameter learning of the BN. The relationships of the factors in a BN model are quantified by conditional probabilities determined on the basis of the data input from the questionnaire survey. 5. The developed BN model provided a decision support system for management staff and safety personnel in E&M RMAA projects so as to formulate suitable safety strategies to improve the safety performance of E&M works. The BN model illustrates the interrelationship between safety factors and safety performance in E&M RMAA works with BN. Such program can be adopted to investigate the effects of each node’s state on the probability distributions of the other child nodes. The sensitivity analysis facilitates the management and safety teams to make optimal decisions for improving E&M safety. 6. Based on the research results, the research team has successfully identified major factors leading to E&M RMAA works related accidents and formulated a series of pragmatic measures for improving the safety of E&M works. By applying the proposed safety measures in practice, it is envisaged that a safer E&M work environment can be created. Improvement in safety of E&M works will benefit not only practitioners directly related to E&M RMAA works but the industry as a whole as well. Difficulties encountered: 1. A major obstacle of this research is a lack of relevant research on Electrical and Mechanical (E&M) works especially in the RMAA sector for reference. The accident factors of RMAA work have been investigated by a few studies. A key aspect missing from these studies was a lack of specific focus on electrical and mechanical (E&M) work in the RMAA projects. The current study tried to document all literatures on E&M RMAA works safety available in Hong Kong and overseas countries. 2. There were a limited number of completed questionnaires collected for investigation. 730 questionnaire responses were collected for the analysis and establishment of the BN model. To ensure the quality of data collected and response rate, follow-up phone calls or emails were sent to the survey respondents for reminding and clarifying any questions related to the survey. 3. There is a problem of possible bias in research design and degree of accuracy required in the research outcomes. To minimize the problem, the questionnaire survey form was designed and complied based on the opinions from experienced E&M experts in the industry. This procedure was important to ensure that the research fully met the requests and concerns of the E&M RMAA sector in the construction industry.

15260416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15260416.value: 1. The developed Bayesian Network (BN) model was used as a case example for an E&M project. However, the developed BN model is not a universal computational BN model that can be practical for any project. The reliability of the BN relies on input data and experts’ experiences related to BN structures and CPTs in the BN. The information provided by experts directly influences the quality and accuracy of the BN. Thus, additional expert opinions should be obtained to further enhance the BN model. The BN can also be learned from raw data combined with expert knowledge. If reliable raw data are available, then a comprehensive BN framework and parameters can be explored and established. The established BN model can still be further developed when new data sources become available. Data from other countries and expert knowledge can be included in the model to improve its global coverage and the accuracy of future models. A similar model can be developed for other construction work trades. 2. 15260416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15260416.value: The safety concern and volume of repair, maintenance, alteration and addition (RMAA) works have significantly increased in recent years. Electrical and mechanical (E&M) works are regarded as one of the most hazardous trades with numerous complex activities. This study aims to develop a BN model for improving the safety performance of E&M works in RMAA projects. The computational Bayesian network (BN) model demonstrates the effects of the quantitative relationships of safety factors on the safety performance of RMAA projects involving E&M tasks. The significance of this study lies in the proffering of a BN model that reveals the interrelationships of the safety factors and safety performance of E&M works in RMAA projects. The findings help in determining the influential factors to improve the safety performance and formulating effective safety management strategies to improve the safety of E&M RMAA works. The BN model can be a practical technique to diagnose effective safety measures for improving safety performance. The research outputs are particularly beneficial in supporting E&M contractors and subcontractors as they enhance the safety performance of E&M works. This work also provides valuable insights into formulating practical and effective recommendations for minimising the risks of E&M for future RMAA projects.

15260716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15260716.value: Very recently, a new strategy for the synthesis of bulk amorphous alloys (BAAs) which is based on the consolidation of nano-size particulates of glassy alloys has been of much interest. These large-size amorphous alloys-called nanoglasses-have tunable atomic structures and exhibit many novel features of structural and mechanical properties that are very promising for practical applications. However, the major impediment for the widespread application of these novel glassy alloys is that they still lack of tensile ductility, similar with conventional BAAs. In this proposed research we investigate the formability and mechanical properties of single-phase and dual-phase nano-glasses by a hybrid simulation approach combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) and phase-field modeling, for the sake of apprehending the formation mechanisms and deformation mechanisms of these fascinating materials with enhanced plasticity. In the AIMD simulation, the atomic structures of the glass-glass interfacial regions at different temperatures and consolidating pressures are determined to understand their roles in the formation of single-phase or dual-phase nano-glass microstructures. The effects of the interfacial regions on inhibiting shear-band propagation are investigated by phase-field models whose essential parameters are determined by AIMD simulations. The phase-field modeling is very feasible in apprehending the intra-granular and inter-granular shear banding processes in the nano-glasses, and in analyzing the size effects of glassy grains on the plasticity of the nano-glasses. The AIMD simulation and phase-field modeling will unveil the roles of glass-glass interfacial regions in the plastic deformation of nano-glasses at the atomic scales and at the mesoscopic scales, respectively, allowing the Hall-Petch like relation for nano-glasses to be determined quantitatively. Besides providing an in-depth understanding on the roles of glass-glass interfaces in the mechanical deformation and their relations with mechanical properties of nano-glasses, the proposed research opens up further potentials to optimize the glass-glass interface to achieve decent tensile ductility. This proposed research will make a significant contribution to the development of nano-glasses as light-weight, high-strength and ductile structural materials used in electronics, medical implants and aerospace industries. 目前許多先進製造方法可以使大塊非晶合金形成納米尺度的微結構。這些微結構通常由非晶態合金納米顆粒及它們之間的界面相互緊密結合組成的。與通常意義下的大塊非晶合金不同，具有納米尺度微結構的非晶合金可能具有特殊的結構性能和力學性能。例如它們的超大的外形和拉伸塑性是通常意義下的大塊非晶合金所不具備的。本專案結合第一性原理和相場模擬方法，闡述具有納米尺度微結構的非晶合金的形成機制及其力學性能與非晶態相的組成、非晶態合金納米顆粒的大小之間的關係。通過第一性原理研究非晶態合金納米顆粒之間的界面的物理性能，其結果不僅可以表徵這些新型非晶態合金的形成機制，也為研究這些新型非晶態合金的塑性形變的相場模型的建立提供了所需的參數。本專案研發的集成的計算模擬方法，能夠有效地模擬具有納米尺度微結構的非晶合金的形成機制及其力學性能，為這些新型非晶態合金在電子、醫療器械、航空航天領域的實際應用奠定堅實的基礎。

15260716.label: Major findings and research outcome
15260716.value: (a) The mechanical properties of nano-glasses are much affected by the atomic structures or phases at the glass-glass interfaces, as determined by the AIMD and conventional MD simulations. First, the sintering temperature is found to play an important role in affecting the glassy structures at the interfaces. When the annealing temperature is just below the glass transition temperature, the atomic structures at the interfaces are close to those of bulk metallic glasses, as measured by specific enthalpy and atomic volume. Therefore, the adjustment on the sintering temperature is convenient in alternating the mechanical properties of nano-glasses. Second, chemical and structural modifications on the atomic structures through oxidization at the glass-glass interfaces could be effective in alternating the mechanical properties of nano-glasses. Nano-glasses with oxidized interfaces have much improved mechanical strength while maintain 5-7% tensile ductility as compared with conventional nano-glasses. Third, the results of AIMD and conventional MD suggest that interdiffusion of atoms close to the glass-glass interfaces could determine the atomic structures of glassy states or multiple phases at the interfaces. Inspired by such finding, the glass-glass interfaces could be designed through surface oxidization of glassy grains or utilizing glassy grains with different chemical compositions, leading to the formation of diffusion-bonded nano-glasses with large sizes and desirable mechanical properties. The first and second findings mentioned above were published in Research Outcome #3-5 in section 8. (b) The size effects on mechanical properties of nano-glasses can be quantitatively determined by phase-field modeling. Based on the parameters of phase-field formulization and boundary conditions as obtained by AIMD simulation, the phase-field modeling successfully predicts the relationships between the mechanical properties of nano-glasses and the sizes of glassy grains, which are much affected by the atomic structures of glass-glass interfaces as reflected in the boundary conditions for the modeling. The results were published in Research Outcome #3 in section 9.

15260716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15260716.value: Aiming at obtaining nano-glasses with large sizes and desirable mechanical properties by a powder-metallurgy method, the simulation approaches as developed in this project are much useful in the design of glass-glass interfaces in nano-glasses. Although MD simulations combining phase-field modeling as carried out in this project imply that there are disordered phases at the glass-glass interface in comparison with those of bulk metallic glasses, the chemical, structural and thermodynamic properties of the interfacial phases have to be further investigated. In polycrystalline alloys, new ordered or disordered phases formed at grain boundaries, the so-called grain-boundary complexions, have been found to be different with those in the grain interiors, which dramatically affect the mechanical properties of the alloys. Similarly, the results obtained in this project suggest that there could be disordered or ordered phases formed at the glass-glass interfaces in nano-glasses, which could be tuned or designed to enhance the mechanical properties of nano-glasses. Nonetheless, the conditions in the formation of those interfacial phases should be determined by atomic simulation or experiments. Based on the results obtained in this project, it has been pointed out that the formation of oxides by surface oxidization of glassy nano-powders or diffusion-induced phases at the glass-glass interfaces could be practical in obtaining large-size nano-glasses with a good combination of high mechanical strength and decent tensile ductility. Such technical route in developing nano-glasses with desirable mechanical properties could be implemented by experiments.

15260716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15260716.value: Computational methods are developed in this project to investigate the mechanical properties of nano-glasses which are promising amorphous alloys for structural applications. It is the first work that the simulation approach is used to predict and design the nano-glasses with desirable mechanical properties. The mechanical properties of nano-glasses revealed from atomic simulation combining phase-field modeling have extensive implications for the design of large-size amorphous alloys for engineering applications. The simulations indicate that engineering glass-glass interfaces is effective in enhancing the mechanical properties of nano-glasses. It is a breakthrough in the development of nano-glasses that ordered or disordered phases at the glass-glass interfaces can be designed to improve their mechanical properties. The research project opens a new window for the development of amorphous alloys that could be large in sizes and practical in engineering applications.

15262116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15262116.value: 近些年来亚洲地区发展了越来越多的超高层结构。超高层结构施工过程中构件的定位对结构的安全以及后续施工十分重要，一般是通过预抬值来补偿柱或墙在后续施工荷载及收缩徐变作用下的尺寸变化。然而，实际施工中的结构处于不断变化的外界环境（比如温度）之中，结构的位置时刻都在运动之中，使得结构的准确定位十分困难。因此，考虑结构的温度作用以及预测施工中结构的位置对施工的准确度十分重要。 本项目将以一个实际的超高层结构为例，通过现场监测和先进的数值分析方法提高超高层结构的施工精度。具体步骤如下： 1. 第一步是将现场监测与热传导分析有机结合起来，得到超高层结构在关键施工节点的温度场分布。首先在建筑信息模型（BIM）的基础上建立结构在实际施工时详细的三维整体有限元模型，该模型包括结构所有构件及其详细的几何信息、施工顺序、温度信息等，从而能够对结构进行实时热传导分析；分析得到的温度结果与现场实时监测结果进行互相校核，得到结构更准确的温度场。 2. 第二步是计算结构在不同荷载下的响应。将上一步得到的温度场输入到有限元模型中，计算结构在温度荷载、恒荷载以及其它施工荷载作用下的位移，并与现场监测结果校核。随时间变化的混凝土模量和收缩徐变等特性由监测结果得到并计入数值模拟计算中。 3. 第三步是发展卡尔曼滤波方法预测下一步施工节点完成后关键构件的位移。在施工过程中结构状态不断变化，将施工中结构控制点的空间位移作为状态变量。由有限元分析可以预估控制点在本施工阶段完成后的位置，此即为先验估计；在本施工阶段完成后，监测结构控制点的实际位置并综合先验估计值，从而可以得到结构控制点新的更准确的位置，即为后验估计。 上述三个步骤交替进行直到项目施工完成。将为减小超高层结构施工期间温度作用提供设计建议。 本项目将由两位学术界和一位工程界科技工作者共同承担；项目的完成将提高超高层结构施工的安全性和准确性，具有重要的科学意义和显著的经济效益和社会效应。

15262116.label: Realisation of objectives
15262116.value: 1) The present project uses a supertall structure in Wuhan, China as the test-bed. Construction of the supertall structure started in early 2017. A real-time construction monitoring system was designed and implemented in April of 2017. As the construction activities progress, temperature sensors and strain gauges were installed on the 4th, 7th, 10th, 18th, 28th, 38th, 48th, and 58th floors in April, May, July, September 2017, January, May, August and Dec. 2018, respectively. The temperature distribution of the constructed structure was obtained from densely distributed sensors. A global finite element model has been established, in which a virtual sun was generated and the angles between the sun and surface of each structural element were calculated. This enables that the heat radiation on each element can be obtained, the heat-transfer analysis of the entire structure be conducted, and consequently, the 3D temperature distribution of the structure be calculated in real-time efficiently. For the present structure with over 2.2 M nodes, the temperature distribution of the entire structure can be obtained in about 1 second per time step. The calculated temperature was in very good agreement with the field monitoring results. This is the first such study in literature. The numerical results are in excellent agreement with the measurement results. 2) The displacement of key floors (5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th, 30th, 35th, 40th, 50th and 55th floors) of the supertall building at different stages was also monitored using total stations and digital level meters. On the other hand, the temperature data obtained in the above step were directly input to the same finite element model for structural analysis without any modification of the mesh. The temperature-induced displacement of the building at different stages has been obtained. The non-uniform temperature caused stress re-distribution over the building. The study was published in Paper 3. 3) A multi-rate Kalman filtering technique was developed to estimate the more accurate displacement of the structure by fusion the displacement, strain and acceleration data. Dynamic displacement is first derived from the measured longitudinal strains based on geometric deformation without requiring mode shapes. An optimization technique is utilized to optimize the deployment of strain sensors for achieving more accurate strain-derived displacement. The strain-derived displacement is then combined with measured acceleration via a multirate Kalman filtering approach. The technique has been applied to two supertall structures in Wuhan and Guangzhou China. The results were published in Structural Health Monitoring (Paper 4). 4) An analytical formula for the temperature-induced strain of supertall structures is derived based on the simulated temperature field. First, a supertall structure is simplified as a cantilever column and the theoretical relationship between the sectional two-dimensional temperature field and strain is derived. Afterwards, the structure is extended to a generalized cantilever column bounded by springs at the top end, and the theoretical relationship of temperature and strain is derived as well. The formula shows that the sectional strain is composed of the sectional average temperature-induced strain and the gradient temperature-induced strain along with two horizontal directions. A finite element model is established to verify the derived strain formula. Finally, the formula is applied to the supertall structure in Wuhan, on which a long-term structural health monitoring system has been installed. The temperature field of the whole structure is obtained by the FE heat transfer analysis, and the temperature-induced strain is calculated according to the derived formula. The average difference between the theoretically derived and the measured strain is less than 7 με. This study provides a simple theoretical formula for calculating the temperature-induced strain of supertall structures, avoiding the complicated FE structural analysis. The study was accepted for publication in Structural Control and Health Monitoring. 5) 6 groups of concrete specimens (150 mm cube) have been made. Field tests on the specimens at 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28 days were conducted to obtain the real time-varying properties (modulus and strength) of the high-strength low-shrinkage concrete used in the structure. The results are similar to those of Code (CEB-FIP). One year shrinkage and creep tests were also conducted. The shrinkage and creep of the concrete were used in the calculation of the structural displacement. 6) The forward construction stage analysis has been conducted on the supertall structure using finite element analysis. Elastic, shrinkage and creep induced deformation of the external columns and inner core walls at different construction stages were obtained and used for deformation compensation. The axial strain was calculated as well. The monitored and calculated stresses of the structural components have provided the actual safety status of the supertall building at different construction stages, and the displacement results have guided the contractor for the subsequent construction activities.

15262116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15262116.value: Under the support of the grant, seven refereed journal papers have been published; one patent has been documented and the other two under processing; two software packages are registered; and one paper won the HKIE R&D Award. The main findings and outcomes of the project include: 1) An efficient global 3D heat-transfer analysis technique for supertall buildings has been developed for the first time worldwide, which enables the temperature distribution of the entire structure and temperature-induced structural responses can be calculated in real-time efficiently during the construction stage. The study has been published in Engineering Structures (Paper 3). One patent has been applied and is under review. 2) A multi-rate Kalman filtering technique was developed to estimate the more accurate displacement of the structure by fusion the displacement, strain and acceleration data. One paper was published in Structural Health Monitoring (Paper 4). The technique has been registered as a patent in China. 3) The non-uniform temperature distribution of the entire structure during the construction stage and the associated stress re-distribution between the inner core and outer frame has been discovered. Suggestions on reducing the adverse temperature effects have been given. 4) An analytical formula for the temperature-induced strain of supertall structures is derived based on the simulated temperature field. The study was accepted for publication in Structural Control and Health Monitoring. One patent has been applied and is under review. 5) The temperature- and typhoon-induced responses of a supertall structure have been compared through numerical analysis, field monitoring and wind tunnel testing. The study was published in Engineering Structures (Paper 1), which was awarded The 2019 HKIE Structural Excellence Award (Commendation Merit). 6) A computer software package titled “Construction safety monitoring and diagnosis system for supertall buildings” was registered in China in 2018.

15262116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15262116.value: The performance of supertall structures during the service stage has not well been understood adequately. The recent unexpected vibration of a 345 m tall building at Shenzhen China triggered the public’s concern about the safety and construction quality of supertall structures. Although preliminary investigations have been released, the rigorous reasons for the vibration are still unknown. The topic has not been studied. Long-term online monitoring can be carried out in the existing supertall structures.

15262116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15262116.value: Supertall structures have rapidly developed in recent years, especially in Asia. Accurate positioning of structural components during the construction of supertall structures is critical because any deviation in the constructed components will affect the construction precision at later stages. The present project developed an integrated construction safety monitoring and stage analysis framework by utilizing a supertall structure in Wuhan, China as a test bed. Two main techniques have been developed: 1) An efficient global 3D heat-transfer analysis technique for supertall buildings has been developed for the first time worldwide, which enables the temperature distribution of the entire structure and temperature-induced structural responses can be calculated in real-time efficiently during the construction stage; 2) A multi-rate Kalman filtering technique was developed to estimate the more accurate displacement of the structure by fusion the displacement, strain and acceleration data. With the developed technique, the construction error of the structure has been reduced.

15262816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15262816.value: In many densely-populated Asian cities such as Hong Kong, the potential benefits to be gained from development of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) for surveillance of traffic congestion and improvement of road network performance are substantial under both recurrent and non-recurrent traffic congestion conditions. Various fixed sensor systems, which provide fundamental data inputs for different traffic management and control purposes, play an important role in ITS development. Thus, determination of optimal locations of these different fixed sensors is a critical issue for various ITS applications. This project proposes a new modeling approach for optimization of different sensor location schemes for estimating the day-to-day peak hour traffic demand by Origin-Destination (OD) pair and link/path travel times in road network with uncertainty separately and simultaneously. Most of the existing methods can only estimate the mean of OD demands or the mean of travel times using the observed data from one sensor system. However, the OD demands for a typical period of different OD pairs are not deterministic and fluctuate from day to day. Moreover, there may exist correlation (in terms of covariance) between traffic demands of different OD pairs particularly when there are some major changes in the land use and/or seasonal activity variations over the year. Travel time is also stochastic in nature due to the network uncertainties. These uncertainties are mainly due to uncertainties in traffic demand and network supply. To overcome the limitation of the existing methods, both the mean and covariance of OD demands and link/path travel times will be simultaneously estimated with making use of the data from different fixed and coordinated sensor systems. In this project, different types of fixed sensor systems, such as automatic vehicle identification (AVI) system and traffic count detection (video-based) system, will be considered in the proposed models. The effects of availability of probe-vehicle sensor data on optimization of the fixed sensor location schemes will also be investigated. Apart from estimating the stochastic OD demands and travel times separately with the use of multiple sensor data, an integrated model will also be developed for optimizing the multiple fixed sensor locations and then estimating simultaneously the stochastic OD demands and link/path travel times in road network with uncertainty. The proposed study has the potential to help authorities and engineers determine the locations of various fixed sensor schemes to enhance the effectiveness of data collection for ITS development and short-term traffic management purposes.

15262816.label: Realisation of objectives
15262816.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, some effective rules such as origin-destination (OD) covering rule, link independence rule and flow intercepting rule have been investigated and extended for determining the traffic sensor location schemes for estimation of traffic demand by OD pair (see publication nos. (6), (7), (12)). With consideration of these sensor location rules, various optimization models have been proposed to estimate mean and covariance of day-to-day peak hour traffic demand by OD pair in road network with uncertainty (see publication nos. (6), (7), (12)). In these proposed models, locations of the traffic sensors or both the number and locations of traffic sensors, are optimized with consideration of budget and associated constraints. The conventional measure for evaluating the reliability of estimated OD demand, named maximum possible relative error, has been extended to consider the estimation of OD demand covariance. To consider the stochastic effects of congestion, stochastic or random link choice proportions have been adopted in the traffic sensor location models instead of fixed link choice proportions (see publication nos. (6) and (13)). The proposed sensor location optimization models have been further extended to estimate the multi-period OD demands with consideration of OD demand covariance effects (see publication no. (8)). In addition, the possibility of sensor failure has been considered in the traffic sensor location problems. The impact of sensor failure on OD demand and link flow estimation has been investigated (see publication nos. (4), (9), (14)). With use of the traffic data from the multiple-sensor systems, a two-stage model has also been proposed to estimate the OD demands by the time of day over the year (see publication no. (5)). The proposed time-dependent OD estimation model considers the spatial and temporal relationships between time-dependent OD demands and traffic counts from the sensors. In connection to the project objective 2, a new optimization model has been proposed to locate traffic sensors for stochastic travel time estimation with use of multiple types of sensor data (see publication no. (16)). The proposed model aims to minimize the travel time estimation uncertainty. Both the mean, variance and covariance of travel time on different links in the road network are explicitly considered in the proposed model. Based on the stochastic relationship between link and path travel times, the travel time on links with and without sensors can be estimated. A new modelling approach has also been proposed for network-wide on-line travel time estimation with inconsistent data from multiple sensor systems (see publication no. (2)). The proposed model made full use of both the available data from multiple sensor systems (on-line data) and historical data (off-line data). Numerical examples using a local road network in Hong Kong have been carried out to demonstrate the new features of the proposed model. In addition, a heterogeneous data fusion method has been proposed to estimate travel time distributions by fusing heterogeneous data from two types of fixed sensor systems, point and interval detectors (see publication no. (1)). The proposed method can estimate travel time distributions for the path and all links either with or without point detectors with incorporation of the travel time spatial correlations. With consideration of probe sensor data, a novel framework has been proposed for estimation of bus arrival time (see publication no. (3)). Bus data is gathered from passengers via a smartphone application (probe sensor). The simulation results show that bus data can be used to provide the real-time bus arrival time information. However, prediction accuracy can be varied depended on the number of reported bus data sets. With respect to the project objective 3, a new optimization model has been proposed to determine the number and locations of multi-type traffic sensors (such as point sensors and automatic vehicle identification sensors) for simultaneous estimation of stochastic OD demand and link travel time during the peak hour period (see publication nos. (10) and (15)). The covariance relationships and uncertainties of both OD demands and link travel times in road networks are explicitly considered in the proposed model. Numerical examples and a case study in Hong Kong road network have been conducted to illustrate the applications and merits of the proposed multi-type sensor location model for simultaneous estimation with covariance effects. With use of the path journey times and link flows obtained from multiple sensor systems, the study has extended to develop a network-wide journey time prediction framework for journey time prediction in stochastic road networks (see publication no. (11)). Numerical example has been carried out to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency and robustness of the proposed model.

15262816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15262816.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, various optimization models for traffic sensor location problems were proposed to estimate mean and covariance of hourly and multi-period traffic demand by OD pair in road network with uncertainty (see publication nos. (6), (7), (8), (12), (13)). The results of the numerical examples showed that the consideration of OD demand covariance could efficiently reduce the uncertainty of OD estimates and hence increase the estimation accuracy regardless of traffic conditions. The effect of sensor failure was also investigated. Optimization models were proposed to locate the traffic sensors so as to minimize the influence of OD demand and link flow estimation due to sensor failure (see publication nos. (4), (9), (14)). In addition, it was demonstrated in the numerical examples that the effects of spatial and temporal relationships between OD demand and traffic counts from the sensors significantly influence the accuracy of time-dependent OD demand estimation (see publication no. (5)). In respect to the project objective 2, a traffic sensor location optimization model was proposed to estimate the stochastic travel time with use of multiple types of sensor data (see publication no. (16)). Using the traffic data from multiple sensor systems, a new traffic model was proposed to estimate the network-wide on-line travel times. The numerical results showed that the use of data from multiple sensor systems and the second-order statistical property of the sensor data has the potential to enhance the accuracy and quality of the network-wide travel time estimates (see publication no. (2)). A heterogeneous data fusion method was also developed to estimate the travel time distributions for the path and all links either with or without point detectors. It was found that fusion of and incorporation of updated spatial correlations can significantly improve the accuracy of travel time distributions of the path and all links without point detectors (see publication no. (1)). In addition, bus arrival times, which can be considered as a kind of probe sensor data, were estimated by a proposed framework (see publication no. (3)). These probe sensor data can be incorporated into the proposed traffic sensor location optimization model to enhance the accuracy of the travel time estimation. With regard to the project objective 3, a multi-type traffic sensor location model was proposed for simultaneous estimation of OD demands and link travel times (see publication nos. (10), (15)). The covariance relationships and uncertainties of both OD demands and link travel times in road networks were explicitly considered in the proposed model. The numerical results demonstrated that the integrated link flow and travel time information could contribute to a more accurate estimation of stochastic OD demand and link travel time for the entire road network. A network-wide journey time prediction framework was also proposed for journey time prediction using the path journey times and link flows obtained from multiple sensor systems (see publication no. (11)).

15262816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15262816.value: In this project, the number and locations of multiple fixed sensors can be optimized for estimation of mean and covariance of OD demand and link/path travel time over a typical hourly period separately and simultaneously. However, to consider more realistic features in practice, the investigation of further extensions should be of value. Further investigation should be carried out to analyze both spatial and temporal covariance of link travel time and OD demand for different hourly periods, in particular, if most of the OD trips could not be completed within the hourly study period. The quality and reliability of the information provided by traffic sensors are highly dependent on various sources of uncertainties such as sensor measurement error and systematic error from the sensor failure. Thus, such sensor uncertainties should be further explored in the sensor location problems. In addition, the proposed models can be extended to consider multi-user classes and different vehicle types for multi-modal transport networks with uncertainties. With help of the newly developed artificial intelligence, it is worthwhile to investigate the utilization of multi-source data from the allocated traffic sensors for real-time applications, such as real-time route guidance and traffic control purposes.

15262816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15262816.value: For traffic surveillance and management purposes, various types of sensors have become available and affordable with the rapid development of advanced sensing technologies. This project contributes to the theoretical and methodological developments on the optimization of multiple fixed sensor location schemes and estimation of the mean and covariance of origin-destination (OD) demand and link/path travel times in road network with uncertainties. In this project, different effective criteria for optimal allocation of traffic sensors have been proposed together with formulation of the equivalent optimization models. Advanced models have also been developed to estimate day-to-day OD demand and link/path travel time in a peak hour period. The results show that the coordination of multi-source traffic data collected by traffic sensors is helpful to estimate satisfactorily the OD demand and link/path travel times. More importantly, optimally allocated multiple fixed traffic sensors hold great promise to capture the day-to-day travel patterns and traffic congestion for traffic management purposes. This project can substantially help traffic planners and engineers to optimize the number and locations of traffic sensors with a fixed budget so as to obtain reliable traffic information such as OD demand and link/path travel times for short-term traffic management and ITS development.
