15262916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15262916.value: We have met the objectives of the project and come up with results in two international conference papers and two journal papers. The details are as follows. (1) The conference paper “Impact of Targeted Vaccination on Quality and Efficacy of Immunization Programs” was presented at the 335th ISERD International Conference on Medical and Health Sciences (ICMHS-2018), Colombo, Sri Lanka. In this paper, we study the question of how to estimate and increase immunization program efficiency and possible public benefits of nation-wide vaccination programs. First, we suggest a new multi-objective mathematical model of enhancing the targeted vaccination program performance in which the objectives are vaccination quality and program efficiency. Then, for finding the best strategy for vaccination, we use the methodology of multi-criteria TOPSIS with additional constraints. The TOPSIS method examines multiple exact and approximate alternatives, and then selects the best available vaccination program. (2) The conference paper “Optimal Immunization Strategies for Groups at Risk in Vaccine Supply Chain Management” was presented at the 14th International Conference on Industrial Logistics (ICIL 2018), Beer Sheva, Israel. The impact of vaccination on disease spread is dependent on the chosen immunization strategy, and on functional, end-to-end vaccine supply chains, and logistics systems. This paper aims to determine the optimal combination of the various immunization strategies that leads to a decrease in the disease burden. A supply-chain based model is suggested to address this problem. Computational results show that the targeted vaccination significantly outperforms other strategies and prevails over them in terms of cost and efficacy. (3) The journal paper “A Multi-Criterion Approach to Optimal Vaccination Planning: Method and Solution” was published in Computers and Industrial Engineering in 2018. In this paper, we consider the problem of finding an optimal combination of vaccination strategies with a view to decreasing the program cost, enhancing vaccination efficiency, and improving societal benefits. We develop a multiple criteria mathematical programming model to address the problem. We analyze the model and derive the structural properties of the optimal solution. Conducting extensive numerical studies to assess the merit of the model, we find that an integrated strategy embracing early-stage indiscriminate mass vaccination with late-stage targeted vaccination outperforms other strategies in terms of cost and efficacy. (4) The journal paper “Effect of Free-riding Behavior on Vaccination Coverage with Customer Regret” was accepted by Computers and Industrial Engineering in 2021. In this paper, we formulate a vaccine demand model incorporating the free rider behavior and customer regret. Solving the model, we show that, as the coefficient of customer regret increases, more people would like to be free riders, which affects the vaccine market coordination. When the coefficient of customer regret is large enough, there will be no risk-taking customers under the socially optimal vaccination coverage. Extending the model to include incomplete demand information and oligopolistic supply, we find that both inaccurate estimation of customer regret and incomplete supply competition will lead to imbalance of supply and demand. Finally, considering government’s subsidy allocations on both supply and demand sides, we present a subsidy allocation mechanism to help the market achieve the largest equilibrium coverage.

15262916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15262916.value: Further development of the research may include investigation of other vaccination program models, such as multi-period models and oligopolistic market models with different market shares for different vaccine manufacturers.

15262916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15262916.value: Influenza is an acute respiratory illness that rapidly spreads in seasonal epidemics and annually imposes great losses in both human lives and financial expenses. According to the WHO, the average global burden of epidemic influenza may be up to about 4–5 million cases of severe illness and 250,000 - 500,000 deaths annually. The best means of preventing and controlling influenza today is by vaccination. There are three main local goals crucial for the vaccination program: to maximize the vaccination efficacy, to maximize the public benefits of the vaccination, and to minimize the cost of the program. However, these goals are conflicting and should be coordinated and balanced. In this project, we have developed and analyzed appropriate new models of balancing the vaccine efficacy, public benefits and costs in large-scale vaccination programs; and ways of enhancing the vaccination coverage. We believe that the results of this project would contribute to academic advancement in theoretical research and provide management insights on vaccination programs.

15263416.label: Realisation of objectives
15263416.value: Overall Achievement: We have fully addressed the three objectives. Realization of Objective 1: (1) An ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) with a 28-day compressive strength of over 180 MPa was successfully developed using locally available constituent materials, which can be used as the filling material in hybrid rebars. (2) A novel cementitious paste was invented to fulfil the need for capping hybrid rebars and other ultra-high-strength structural members for compression tests. A Chinese invention patent application on this novel cementitious paste has been submitted. (3) Monotonic axial compression tests on hybrid rebars with different fibre winding angles for the external FRP tube were carried out. The effects of fibre winding angles were examined. Additionally, cyclic axial compression tests on hybrid rebars with various fibre winding angles were carried out. (4) A new form of hybrid rebar with a wavy external shape has been proposed for enhancing the bond between the hybrid rebar and the concrete. Monotonic axial compression tests were conducted on such hybrid rebars to investigate their axial performance. Realization of Objective 2: (1) The characteristics of the measured axial compressive stress-strain curves of hybrid rebars were investigated, and a simple method was developed to predict the axial stress-strain behaviour of hybrid rebars under monotonic compression. Realization of Objective 3: (1) Eight FRP rebar/hybrid rebar reinforced concrete columns (FRP-RC columns) were tested under axial compression as a pilot study. The concrete of the columns had an unexpectedly high compressive strength. (2) Eighteen circular-section FRP-RC columns were tested under axial compression. (3) Twelve circular-section FRP-RC columns were tested under eccentric compression. (4) Jiang and Teng’s (2012) column theoretical model was adapted to predict the behaviour of concrete columns with internal longitudinal hybrid rebars.

15263416.label: Major findings and research outcome
15263416.value: Findings Related to Objective 1: (1) Under monotonic axial compression, the behaviour of hybrid rebars is characterised by a four-stage stress-strain relationship, including an initial elastic stage, a stress fluctuation stage, a strain-hardening stage, and finally a residual-stress stage. (2) The axial load resisted by a hybrid rebar at a given axial strain is equal to the axial load resisted by the central FRP rebar plus that resisted by the FRP-confined UHPC annulus. Findings Related to Objective 2: (1) The stress-strain curve of hybrid rebars under monotonic axial compression can be closely predicted using the proposed simple method. Findings Related to Objective 3: (1) Under eccentric compression, hybrid rebar-reinforced concrete columns are superior to FRP rebar-reinforced concrete columns in terms of both ultimate axial load and ductility.

15263416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15263416.value: Much more research is needed to further develop the hybrid rebar technology, including the enhancement of bond via the use of a wavy-shaped external tube and the establishment of design and construction guidelines.

15263416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15263416.value: The performance of fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) rebars is substantially inferior in compression (due to issues such as fibre micro-buckling) than in tension, and thus their use in concrete columns is generally not recommended. This poses a significant challenge when a steel-free structure is needed. This project is proposed to tackle the above problems by developing a novel steel-free hybrid rebar. Such a hybrid rebar typically consists of a central FRP rebar, an external FRP confining tube and an annular layer of high-strength cementitious material such as ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC). A systematic experimental study including tests on hybrid rebars and concentric/eccentric compression tests on hybrid rebar reinforced concrete columns, as well as theoretical analysis, was carried out in this project. The test results showed that: (a) the FRP rebar in a hybrid rebar is well supported against rebar buckling and fibre micro-buckling, and the compressive strength of the FRP rebar can be fully mobilized; (b) the stress-strain curve of hybrid rebars under monotonic axial compression can be closely predicted using a simple method proposed in the study; (c) hybrid rebar-reinforced concrete columns under eccentric compression are superior to FRP rebar-reinforced concrete columns in terms of both ultimate axial load and ductility.

15263616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15263616.value: The fission gases xenon and krypton are unceasingly generated in irradiated nuclear fuel, which is a sintered compact of granular uranium dioxide in the current commercial light water reactors. As a consequence of their low solubility in UO2, the fission gases tend either to precipitate into bubbles or to be released to the free volume in the rod. Fission gas release and gas bubble swelling are critical issues for the fuel performance. Released fission gas can reduce the thermal conductivity of the fuel-clad gap and cause temperature and pressure increases in the fuel pellet, whereas gas bubble swelling can increase the contact pressure between the fuel and clad, and lead to clad failure. The current nuclear fuel performance codes are based on empirical formulas of gas bubble behavior and its effects on the thermo-mechanical properties of the fuels that are derived from important assumptions that significantly limit their predictive capability, especially for the development of new concept reactors and advanced nuclear fuels. Therefore, understanding and predicting the behavior and evolution kinetics of fission gas are essential for enhancing the fuel performance codes and the development of high burn-up reactor technologies. The rapid development of computational methods and the accumulated knowledge on radiation damage mechanisms show great promise for theoretical predictions of the microstructural evolution of irradiated materials. Atomistic simulations, such as first principles, molecular dynamics, and Monte Carlo methods, enable the accurate calculation of thermodynamic and kinetic properties such as the generation, resolution, and clustering of defects in irradiated materials. The mesoscale phase-field method has shown powerful capability in predicting phase stability and microstructure evolution kinetics in chemically and microstructurally complicated systems, not only for systems close to the equilibrium state, but also for systems far from equilibrium. One of the strengths of this method lies in the natural and straightforward way in which multiple material processes, such as multiple species diffusion, migration of gas bubbles, and elastic interaction, are accounted for. In this proposed project, we aim to develop an atomistically informed and microstructurally resolved phase-field model for predicting the fission gas behavior in UO2 and providing accurate thermodynamic and kinetic data to enhance the prediction capability of nuclear fuel performance codes. The analytical tools and methodologies developed in this project may find wide application in the irradiation related micro-electronics, photonics, and biomedical industries.

15263616.label: Realisation of objectives
15263616.value: Objective 1 “To develop thermodynamic and kinetic models for investigating the nucleation of gas bubbles” (100% completed): Due to the very large formation energy of vacancies and noble gas atoms in the form of interstitials in the nuclear fuel (UO2), the thermodynamic equilibrium concentrations of these species are very low in the nuclear fuel matrix even at very high temperature, which imposes difficulties on the quantitative study of bubble evolution via phase-field method. In this project, a quantitative phase-field model is proposed to deal with this problem. The free energy density of the system is derived according to the principles of thermodynamics for regular solutions which has considered distributional entropy, defect formation enthalpies, and equation of state (EOS) both inside fuel matrix and Xe gas bubbles. Two types of EOS were applied, which covered different ranges of gas bubble size from nano to micro-meters. In addition, the elastic effect of vacancies, gas atoms and internal gas pressures inside bubbles are also included in the kinetics formulations with material parameters from experiments and other theoretical study. The phase-field model has been tested under single and multiple bubble environment. It has been shown that the model is capable to study the kinetics of gas bubble growth under dilute concentrations (10-11) of vacancies and gas atoms in the matrix for the first time in the world. Objective 2 “To integrate the irradiation influence into phase-field model” (100% completed): The above model has been applied to study single bubble growth and multiple bubble growth under different irradiation influence represented by different concentrations of vacancies and gas atoms created in the matrix by irradiation and at the boundary of the simulated domains at different temperatures. The elastic effect on the interactions between bubbles and between bubble and vacancies, and the effect of generation rate of vacancies and gas atoms on the bubble growth are analyzed. In addition, the effect of temperature gradients on bubble migration and merging are also simulated and compared to experimental observations with good agreements. The project also resulted in a better understanding on the interaction between defects and grain boundaries.

15263616.label: Major findings and research outcome
15263616.value: A quantitative phase-field model for the study of gas bubble evolution in UO2 is proposed for the first time in literature. The elastic interactions between bubbles, gas atoms and vacancies are studied. Realistic concentrations of vacancy and gas atoms in matrix are used to study bubble growth. The influences of temperature and concentrations on gas bubble growth are studied. The influence of different fission rates on gas bubble evolution is investigated. Phase-field model for thermal diffusion and vapor transport mechanisms are developed, implemented and verified against experiments. Gas bubble shape change during migration under temperature gradients are captured by the simulation, which agrees well with experiments. Center hole formation in the UO2 nuclear fuel pellet is confirmed by our model. Constructing a dislocation climb model to investigate the point defect (created by irradiation) sink strength at low-angle tilt grain boundaries. The sink strength is not only determined by the long-range diffusion but also the short-range reaction rate. Dynamic motion of the grain boundary dislocations exhibits significant effect on the grain boundary sink strength.

15263616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15263616.value: Combined with super-computing system, it is possible to apply models developed in this project to simulate the performance of a whole nuclear fuel element in reactor environment. The models and methodologies developed in this project can be used to study other similar phenomena such as hydrogen bubble formation and evolution in steels.

As a consequence of their extremely low solubility in fuel, the fission gases tend either to precipitate into bubbles or to be released to the free volume in the fuel rod. Fission gas release and gas bubble swelling are critical issues for LWR fuel performance. Released fission gas can reduce the thermal conductivity of the fuel-clad gap and cause temperature and pressure increases in the fuel pellet; Gas bubble swelling may increase the contact pressure between fuel and clad, and lead to clad failure. In this project, we developed a quantitative phase-field model for predicting the fission gas behavior in nuclear fuels and to provide accurate thermodynamic and kinetic data to enhance the prediction capability of nuclear fuel performance codes. This project also provided a good opportunity for training young scientists and engineers in this technologically important area for China. The analytic tools and methodologies developed in this project may find wide applications in irradiation related microstructural evolution in structural materials in nuclear, functional materials in micro-electronics, photonics, and biomedical industries.

15264716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15264716.value: 基於激光刻劃還原氧化石墨烯之超級電容式微加工超聲波換能器

15264716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15264716.value: This proposal aims to study an ultrasonic transducer based on supercapacitive driving mechanism, where compression of electric double layers (EDL) within 0.3 to 0.8nm range occurred when a porous electrode made of reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was immersed in a liquid electrolyte, which simulates a parallel-capacitor based device such as a CMUT but with thousands of stacking rGO layers that acts similar to a piezoelectric transducer working in thickness mode. It takes the advantages of less than nanometer EDL thickness and also large specific surface area to increase the charge storage at low DC bias for 1 to 6 volts depending on the potential window of the electrolyte, which can increase the electrostatic force for higher output pressure and also the charge storage for higher sensitivity. A higher base capacitance can increase the signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) to reduce the effect from parasitic capacitance. The multi-layer rGO electrode can also simulate the vibrating membrane of CMUTs to match with the acoustic impedance of the soft tissue while immersed in the liquid electrolyte. To implement the proposed method, the rGO porous electrode is laser-scribed to designed patterns. Graphite oxide power is dissolved in DI water to be treated with ultrasonic agitation for three hours to exfoliate the powder particle to become a water dispersion of graphene oxide (GO). The GO water dispersion is drop-casted on a PET film that is attached to a Light-Scribe CD/DVD disk and then dried 1~2 days to become a thin GO film of around 1 um thickness. The GO coated disk is ready for laser-scribing using a LightScribe CD/DVD labeling drive. The LightScribe CD/DVD drive has an infrared laser with 788nm wavelength that can easily penetrate the GO film and also allow its energy to reduce the GO to become rGO. The expansion of gas product during the reduction process helps to separate the stacked GO layers of 1um to become multi-layered rGO of around 10um thick which allows the penetration of electrolyte into the porous structure. The LightScribe CD/DVD drive is capable of writing patterns with 1000 dpi (25.4um) resolution, which is sufficient to direct write arrays of ultrasonic transducers of a few hundred micrometers per element width. Arrays of 1-D and 2-D are also proposed to further build the transducers for ultrasonic imaging applications, which can take advantage of x and y addressing method to simplify the 2-D array for 3-D volumetric ultrasonic imaging systems. 本計畫目標為研究基於超級電容驅動機理之超聲波換能器，以還原氧化石墨烯（rGO）製作之多孔電極浸漬於電解液內，可產生0.3至0.8納米範圍的電雙層（EDL）壓縮，其作動方式類似如電容式微加工超聲波換能器（CMUT）中之平板電容，並具有成千上萬堆疊之rGO層，其作用類似於在厚度模式下工作的壓電換能器。它具有小於納米的電雙層厚度，以及較大的比表面積之優點，以增加在1至6伏特下之低直流偏壓的電荷存儲，而此範圍取決於電解質的電位窗，因此可以增加靜電力以產生較高的輸出聲壓，和增加電荷存儲以達到更高的靈敏度。較高的起始電容還可以增加信噪比（S / N），以減少來自寄生電容的影響。多層rGO電極還可以​​模擬CMUT的振動膜，而且沈浸在液體電解質中，還能匹配與軟組織的聲阻抗。 為了實現所提之方法，還原氧化石墨烯（rGO）多孔電極將以激光刻劃來形成所設計的圖案。先將氧化石墨粉溶於去離子（DI）水以超聲攪拌處理3小時，以剝開粉末顆粒形成氧化石墨烯（GO）的水分散液。再將GO水分散液滴鑄在事前已貼在光雕CD / DVD光盤的PET膜上，然後乾燥1〜2天，以形成大約為1微米厚的氧化石墨烯（GO）薄膜。此塗佈了GO的光盤已可使用 CD / DVD光雕打標機進行激光刻劃。 CD / DVD光雕打標機具有788納米波長的紅外激光，可輕鬆穿透GO膜，其能量也足以還原GO成為rGO。還原過程中氣體產物的膨脹也有助於分離1微米層疊中之GO各層，成為10微米厚，可讓電解質滲透到多孔結構中的多層rGO。 CD / DVD光雕機能夠達到1000 DPI（25.4微米）的分辨率，這足以直寫每個單一元件寬度只有幾百微米的超聲換能器陣列。本計畫也提出製作一維及二維陣列，以進一步達成於超聲波成像應用之換能器，並可得利於X及Y尋址方法，來簡化二維陣列以用於三維容積超聲成像系統。

15264816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15264816.value: Majority of ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications aim at spatial subsurface mapping and positioning of embedded objects in engineering structures (bridges, buildings, buried pipes, etc). But studies about near-surface defect diagnosis like water seepage are relatively scarce, and are traditionally carried out by identifying abnormal amplitude and velocity in radargrams and slice scans. This study attempts to study the phase velocity dispersion over the wide-band GPR wave, inversely model and validate its relationships with water seepage in concrete and soil. These local problems of material degradation are the root cause of the deterioration of many of the 1977km long roads, 7000 buildings, 3000km long water mains and other infrastructures in the very humid environment in Hong Kong, and surely elsewhere in the world. The frequency-dependent velocity dispersion of GPR wave velocity will be used to study the effects of water seepage within concrete and soil. For example, slow velocity at a particular bandwidth likely indicates areas of high moisture content led by water seepage of damaged conduits in concrete and pipes in soil. But characteristics of its frequency-dependent velocity dispersion in GPR remain unknown. Such mechanism will be studied by the spectral analysis of surface wave (SASW) propagating through the surface, in a setting of antennae arrays put on a surface, analogous to common mid-point (CMP) or wide angle reflection and refraction (WARR) in geophysical survey. There are two advantages. Firstly, it measures the changes of pulse characteristics as a function of frequency-dependent velocity dispersion by making use of multiple antenna receivers. Secondly, existence of high moisture can be studied by phase velocity through such measurement. In this work, conduit and pipe leak will be simulated in soil and concrete to validate the measurement methods, algorithms and inverse models in two GPR bandwidths, i.e. 450 to 1350MHz (centered at 900MHz) for soil and 1000 to 3000MHz (centered at 2000MHz) for concrete. Preliminary findings have been proven convincing in PI and Co-I’s previous works in Lai et al. (2011a, 2011b, 2014) in the context of cement hydration and evaporation after flooding where the states of water gradually changed with lapsed time. The deliverables will have long term impacts on theoretical and practical sides. The theoretical side refers to development of algorithms and methodology on frequency-dependent phase velocity mapping. The practical side means spatial mapping of GPR phase velocities as a tool to study and map water seepage in concrete and soil. 地面穿透雷達（ GPR）的應用程序都會著眼於空間的地下製圖和工程結構嵌入對象的定位（橋樑，建築，地下管道等），但是對於近表面缺陷診斷的滲水研究相對匱乏。通過識別雷達圖和切片掃描中異常的幅度和速度是傳統進行分析的方法。本研究試圖研究在透地雷達的寬波段，逆模型的相速度頻散驗證滲水與混凝土和與土壤的關係。這些問題是香港1977公里長的道路， 7000棟樓房， 3000公里長水管等基礎設施在香港非常潮濕的環境惡化的根本原因，在世界其他地方也非常常見。

15264816.label: Realisation of objectives
15264816.value: Objective 1: Establish methodology to measure phase velocity dispersion in concrete and soil. The objective is fully achieved through GPR-spectral analysis of surface wave and magnitude coherence plot over full effective GPR bandwidths. Objective 2: Study the effects of water seepage in concrete and soil on the phase velocity dispersion via the methodology established in objective 1, as well as well-established microwave method. The objective is full achieved as it is evident that the water content contained in concrete and soil decelerates GPR wave but this deceleration is frequency-dependent, i.e. it is more significant in lower frequency than in higher frequency regime. Objective 3: Inversely model and validate the algorithms for mapping of water seepage according to the results obtained in objectives ‘1’ and ‘2’. The objective is largely achieved due to the fact that after the inverse model was developed, the repeatability of the measurements on the same objects still varies, which cause doubts on the input of the inverse models. Objective 4: Study the feasibility of applying the established methodology, inverse models and validated lab results on in-situ large scale mapping of variation of water seepage, and other material properties. This objective is fully achieved as a GPR-WARR (wide angle refraction and reflection) was developed and some pilot results indicate good possibility of full-scale implementation.

15264816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15264816.value: As expected, the water content contained in concrete and soil decelerates GPR wave but this deceleration is found to be obviously frequency-dependent which causes dispersion, i.e. it is more significant in lower frequency than in higher frequency regime. An inverse model was then developed for characterization of the frequency-dependent behavior of GPR wave's velocity dispersion. But the repeatability of the measurements on the same objects still varies and causes doubts on the input of the inverse model, which requires further uncertainties evaluation for validating the inverse model.

15264816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15264816.value: The underlying physics, mathematical solutions and coding pave the way for building up a WARR machine which allows characterization of large-scale material properties, damages and durability. In a WARR machine, the group velocity with no frequency-dependency is no longer the point of interest and hyperbolic reflection of any round-shaped reflector is not longer a prerequisite for velocity measurement. Instead, the phase velocity at any particular frequency can be measured with one transmitter and multiple receivers, and then the outcome of phase velocity as a function of any particular GPR wave's frequency plotted spatially and evaluate together with material properties, damages and durability.

15265016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15265016.value: 高強鋼角鋼受拉承載力和力學性能研究

15265016.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15265016.value: Prof Chung, Kwok-fai Dr Fang, Cheng

15265016.label: Project Objectives
15265016.value: The objectives of this research project are i) to conduct an experimental study of the tensile strength of HSS angles with bolted end connections and ii) to develop a finite element model validated by the test results for a comprehensive parametric study, iii) to assess the applicability of the current shear lag and block shear design equations for HSS angles and, iv) to develop a new design model and new design equations, if needed, for predicting the tensile strength of HSS angles. The objectives of this research project will be accomplished by the following tasks: Experimental investigation: Full-scale tension tests will be conducted to investigate the shear lag and block shear strength of bolted HSS angles. The test parameters include steel grade (S690 and S275), connection details (such as bolt spacing and number of bolts), connection eccentricity and specimen size. The specimens will be fabricated using HSS steel plates. Tension coupon tests will also be conducted to examine and establish the stress-strain behaviour of the materials used for angle specimens. Numerical investigation: The structural behaviour of the test specimens will be further examined by finite element analysis. The finite element models of the test specimens will be validated by comparing the experimental test results with those of the FE analysis. The validated FE models will be subsequently employed to conduct a parametric study for further examination of shear lag and block shear behaviour and the strength of HSS angles. Examination of design rules and development of design model: Various design equations (AISC-LRFD, CSA/CAN-S16.1, Eurocode 3, AIJ, and GB50017-2003) for predicting the shear lag and block shear capacity of angles will be evaluated critically to examine their suitability for predicting the tensile capacity of HSS angles. If the current design equations are found to be inadequate, a new design model and design equations will be developed based on the experimental and analytical results.

15265016.label: Realisation of objectives
15265016.value: In general, all the objectives of the research study were achieved according to the planned research activities. A full-scale experimental investigation of the tensile strength and behaviour of high strength steel (HSS) angles including block shear and shear lag was conducted. A series of nonlinear finite element (FE) analysis of the test specimens and the subsequent parametric study were carried out to help interpret the test results and to provide further insights of the structural behaviour and tensile strength of HSS angles. The current design equations for assessing the block shear strength and shear lag of tension angles were revisited. Preliminary design recommendations for the design of block shear strength and net section strength considering shear lag were proposed. The experimental programme consisted of 47 full-scale tests of the HSS tension angles including 18 shear lag specimens and 29 block shear specimens. Extensive tension coupon tests of the HSS (S690) materials were also conducted to determine the important material properties such as the tensile strength (fu) to yield strength (fy) ratio and the ductility of the material at ultimate. For the shear lag specimens, the test parameters included steel grades, connection length and out-of-plane eccentricity. For the block shear specimens, the test parameters included steel grades (S275 and S690) and bolt arrangements (bolt number, bolt-line, pitch, and edge distance). All the shear lag specimens were failed by net section rupture at the first bolt-hole location near the gross section. For the block shear specimens with single bolt-line, eleven of them failed by block shear with tensile fracture and shear failure of a block of material, and the remaining two by shear-out at the last bolt hole. For the block shear specimens with two bolt-lines, the specimens were failed by block shear, however, two specimens failed in block shear with two shear planes whereas the failure mode of the remaining specimens only contained one shear plane. For the shear lag specimens, the test results showed that the behaviour and failure modes of S690 HSS tension angles were similar to those made of S275 steel. The combined effect of material characteristics and connection configurations on the net section resistance of tension angles was also observed. The test efficiency, defined as the ratio of the test ultimate load to the product of the net section area and the tensile strength of the material, ranged from 0.59 to 1.07 and 0.61 to 1.01 for the grade S275 and S690 angle specimens, respectively. In general, the test efficiency decreased with higher steel grade, and this trend was more obvious in cases of angles with a long-leg connection and long connection length. For the block shear specimens with single bolt-line, the test results showed that in general the behaviour and failure pattern of the HSS tension angles resembled those of the normal steel (NS) angles. The block shear resistance of the tension angles increased with the pitch distance, bolt number, and edge distances. It was seen that increasing the outstanding leg length and varying the connected legs did not produce an evident effect on the block shear capacities of either the HSS or NS tension angles. For the block shear specimens with two bolt-lines, the test results showed that the block shear strength increased with increasing bolt row number and parallel pitch since the shear plane area of the block was increased. The block shear strength of the specimens was also increased with increasing transverse pitch and edge distance due to an increased tension plane area. However, the test results showed that the block shear strength of the angles was not affected by the length of the unconnected angle leg. Nonlinear finite element (FE) analysis of the test specimens was conducted. The FE model, validated by the test results, was employed to conduct a comprehensive parametric study. In general, the FE predictions agreed well with the test responses of the shear lag specimens, and the behaviour of tension angles from yielding inception to failure was well reproduced by the FE models. The results confirmed that the outstanding leg of the S690 steel angle might not be fully mobilised to carry the applied load prior to failure of the net section, and the reduced ductility of S690 steel would appreciably affect the net section resistance of bolted tension angles. For the block shear specimens with single bolt-line, the FE results showed that the block shear strength of the specimens was not appreciably influenced by the outstanding leg lengths and the connected leg lengths reconfirming the test observations. For the block shear specimens with double bolt-line, the analysis results confirmed that all FE models were dominated by failure mode with one shear plane. It was shown that an increasing end distance increased the block shear strength of the S690 steel angles by increasing the length of the shear plane. The variation of the connected leg length, which influenced the in-plane eccentricity of the S690 angles, did not have a pronounced effect on the block shear strength of S690 steel angles. The test results of the shear lag specimens were compared to the predictions by the design equations in major design speciﬁcations and to those by the equation proposed by the authors and colleagues. It was observed that the design equations in CSA S16-14 and AISC 360-16, produced unconservative estimates of the net section resistance for S690 steel angles, however, Eurocode 3 and AS 4100 produced conservative estimates. The inconsistent predictions by the codified equations may be explained by the fact that these design methods do not take into account the effect of material ductility. In contrast, the design equation proposed by the authors and colleagues accounting for the combined effect of fu/fy ratio and connection conﬁgurations produced good estimates of the net section resistance of both S275 and S690 angle specimens. The test results of the block shear specimens with single bolt-line were compared with the predictions by the design equations in major design speciﬁcations and those reported in the literature. It was shown that the design equations in AISC 360–2016 and Eurocode 3 generally produced conservative estimates of the block shear capacities for both the S275 and S690 angle specimens. The design equation proposed by Teh and Yazici produced satisfactory predictions of the block shear capacity of the S690 angle specimens. Based on the test results, it appears that the reduced ductility of S690 steel does not have a pronounced effect on the block shear capacity of the tension angles. For the block shear specimens with double bolt-line, it was found that Eurocode 3, CSA S16-14, and the design methods in the literature produced inconsistent predictions of the failure modes of both the S690 and S275 specimens and the FE models. In contrast, the failure modes of the S690 specimens were predicted well by AIJ. AISC 360-16 was able to predict the failure modes of all the test specimens and the FE models. The results showed that Eurocode 3, CSA, AIJ, AISC, and Teh and Yazici generally produced conservative predictions of the block shear strengths of both the S690 and S275 specimens. In comparison, AIJ gave more accurate predictions of the block shear strength of the S690 specimens.

rows: The objectives of this research project are i) to conduct an experimental study of the tensile strength of HSS angles with bolted end connections and ii) to develop a finite element model validated by the test results for a comprehensive parametric study, iii) to assess the applicability of the current shear lag and block shear design equations for HSS angles and, iv) to develop a new design model and new design equations, if needed, for predicting the tensile strength of HSS angles. The objectives of this research project will be accomplished by the following tasks:

Experimental investigation: Full-scale tension tests will be conducted to investigate the shear lag and block shear strength of bolted HSS angles. The test parameters include steel grade (S690 and S275), connection details (such as bolt spacing and number of bolts), connection eccentricity and specimen size. The specimens will be fabricated using HSS steel plates. Tension coupon tests will also be conducted to examine and establish the stress-strain behaviour of the materials used for angle specimens.

Numerical investigation: The structural behaviour of the test specimens will be further examined by finite element analysis. The finite element models of the test specimens will be validated by comparing the experimental test results with those of the FE analysis. The validated FE models will be subsequently employed to conduct a parametric study for further examination of shear lag and block shear behaviour and the strength of HSS angles.

Examination of design rules and development of design model: Various design equations (AISC-LRFD, CSA/CAN-S16.1, Eurocode 3, AIJ, and GB50017-2003) for predicting the shear lag and block shear capacity of angles will be evaluated critically to examine their suitability for predicting the tensile capacity of HSS angles. If the current design equations are found to be inadequate, a new design model and design equations will be developed based on the experimental and analytical results.

15265016.label: Major findings and research outcome
15265016.value: A total of 47 angle specimens were tested in tension with 30 S690 angles and 17 S275 angles. For the bolted shear lag specimens, the test results showed that the specimens failed in net section rupture. It was found that the current design speciﬁcations produced inconsistent predictions of net section resistance of tension angles, whereas the method proposed by the PI and colleagues gave good predictions of net section resistance of bolted S690 steel angles. Eleven block shear specimens with single bolt-line were failed by tension rupture of the tension plane and significant shear deformation in the shear plane. The results indicated that the block shear resistance increased only slightly with increasing lengths of the angle legs, and was not affected appreciably by the relatively lower ductility of HSS. It was also found that the predictions made by AISC 360–16 and Eurocode 3 were conservative, whereas CSA S16–14 provided unconservative predictions. The design equations proposed by Teh and Yazici were preliminary recommended for evaluating the block shear strength of HSS angles with single bolt-line. For the block shear specimens with double bolt-line, the specimens were failed by block shear, however, different fracture patterns were observed. The test results showed that the block shear strength of the specimens increased with increasing bolt row number and parallel pitch. However, the test results showed that block shear strength of the angles was not affected by the length of the unconnected angle leg. Based on the experimental and numerical results, it was found that the design equations in AIJ offered a reasonable predictions of the block shear strength of the HSS angle specimens. The influence of the loading mode on the mechanical properties of S690 steel was also investigated based on an extensive tension coupon test programme with 29 coupon specimens. Based on the test results, a testing procedure involving two displacement-controlled holds was recommended to obtain the mechanical properties of the material. The research findings have resulted in 3 journal papers. The results of the shear lag investigations were published in “Thin-Walled Structures” (Section C, paper 1). The results of the block shear investigations were published in “Journal of Constructional Steel Research” (Section C, paper 2). The results of the investigation of loading mode of the HSS tension coupons were published in “Construction and Building Materials” (Section C, paper 3). Two conference papers were also published as illustrated in Section C.

15265016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15265016.value: The HSS material examined in the study was S690. With the continuous development of metallurgy, higher steel grade material such as S960 is readily available. Since the current study was focused on S690 material, it would be beneficial to conduct additional tests on the net-section and block shear strength of higher steel grade to further substantiate the application of HSS material in steel construction. To improve the understanding of the shear lag and block shear of HSS tension members and to provide more experimental data, tensile tests on other structural sections such as channel and tee sections are recommended. Further study is recommended to examine the deformation limit that is required in HSS tension members to allow sufficient deformation prior to fracture of the connected elements. When more experimental data on the tensile strength of HSS members is available, a reliability analysis of the test data should be conducted to examine the applicability of the partial factors in the current design codes for the design of the tensile and block shear strength of HSS members.

15265016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15265016.value: High strength steel (HSS) has been receiving attention in the civil/structural engineering community due to its higher yield strength, and hence improve the strength-weight ratio. However, the comparatively lower deformation ability of HSS is one of the limitations that may hinder its application in construction, in particular, the use of HSS tension members in steel construction. Hence, it is important to examine the effect of HSS deformation ability on the tensile strength of HSS members. The study examined experimentally and numerically the net-section strength considering shear lag and the block shear strength of HSS steel angles connected by one leg. The effects of the lower deformation ability of S690 HSS material, connection arrangements and connection legs on the net section resistance and block shear strength of bolted tension angles were examined. It was found that the net-section strength of the HSS tension angles examined in this study was appreciably affected by the lower deformation ability of HSS, however, only slight effect on the block shear strength of double bolt-line angles was observed. Based on the results, preliminary design recommendations for evaluating the net-section and block shear strength of HSS angles were proposed.

15265116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15265116.value: 雙元液滴在氣相環境中的碰撞與許多自然和工業過程緊密相關，比如雨滴的形成，大氣氣溶膠環流，噴墨印刷，噴霧燃燒，以及冶金、化學和生物制藥工程中的各種噴霧。目前對牛頓流體雙元液滴碰撞動力學的理解已經有了許多重大的進展。牛頓流體的粘性在給定溫度下是一個不隨當地或全局的流體流動剪切率而變化的常數。 近些年，非牛頓流體雙元液滴在氣相環境中的碰撞動力學受到持續廣泛的關註。盡管許多實際的工業流體都是非牛頓流體，但是針對非牛頓流體液滴碰撞的研究卻非常少。非牛頓流體是其表觀粘度隨流動剪切率而變化的一類流體。最簡單的也是最常見的非牛頓流體是剪切變稀的，也就是流體的表觀粘度隨著流動剪切率的增加而減少。並且幾乎所有的非牛頓流體在特定條件下都會表現出剪切變稀的特性，所以本研究計劃重點針對剪切變稀的非牛頓流體的液滴碰撞展開實驗和數值的研究。我們只考慮標準大氣壓力下的液滴碰撞從而避免增加額外的復雜度。不同氣體環境下（氣體壓力，氣體分子結構，分子質量，粘性等等）的液滴碰撞固然重要，但這是將來所要研究的內容。 本研究計劃將全面地探討標準空氣下剪切變稀的非牛頓流體雙元液滴碰撞動力學的特性；特別關註的是能夠確定和解釋相同粒徑和不同粒徑的液滴在不同韋伯數下正碰的結果。當然非正碰的液滴碰撞也要嘗試研究，畢竟這更符合實際情況。本研究計劃的目的是：（1）搭建合適的實驗裝置來產生穩定的、具有較寬變化範圍的韋伯數、粒徑比和碰撞系數的液滴；（2）系統地、定量地分析韋伯數(We)和大小液滴粒徑比(∆)對液滴正碰結果的影響，並將結果在韋伯數（We=O(10)~O(100)）和液滴粒徑比（∆=1.0-5.0）的二維參數空間上表征為諾模圖；（3）發展和驗證基於格子玻爾茲曼方法的計算機模擬代碼，用來研究液滴正碰及其表現出的非牛頓流的特性；（4）完善實驗裝置和計算機代碼嘗試開展三維的液滴非正碰的研究。其現象和解釋將比液滴正碰豐富的多，也復雜的多。

15265116.label: Realisation of objectives
15265116.value: In the current reporting period, research activities that were carried out in relation to the Objective 1 to 5 are summarized as follows: Objective 1: To establish an experimental apparatus capable of generating stable droplets of shear-thinning fluids with relatively wide ranges of Weber number, size ratio and impact parameter. The apparatus has been established in the proposer's lab and preliminary experimental data have been obtained. Further validation and upgrade of the apparatus are still required. Research activities: To complete the objective, an experimental platform was built up, and adjusted to be able to generate stable shear-thinning droplets in a relatively wide ranges of Weber number We=O(10)-O(100), size ratio ∆=1.0-5.0 and impact parameter B continuously varied between 0 and 1. Two important innovations on the apparatus have been made. First, the exact droplet size determined by the diameter of the valve nozzle can now be changed continuously in the range of O(100)-O(1000)μm. This enables the studies in this project on the effects of surface-volume ratio, which are of significance in microfluidics and chemically reacting droplets. Second, the pressure control of valves can be more accurate to generate stable non-Newtonian droplets which have significantly increased low-shear-rate viscosity of shear-thinning fluid. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 2: To systematically quantify the influence of the Weber number and the size ratio, ∆, on the head-on collision outcomes. The aqueous solutions of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and Carbopol® 934 polymer (Carbomer) with various weight percentages will be used as representative shear-thinning fluids. Research activities: In the project, we have systematically investigated the head-on droplets coalescence by the effect on Weber number and the size ratio. More importantly, we found it is necessary to carry out numerical simulation to interpret our experimental data. Consequently, we extent the original scope of the project by conducting numerical simulation. The coalescence of two initially stationary droplets of unequal size was investigated numerically using an improved VOF method and adaptive mesh refinement algorithm with emphasis on tow key problems: the formation of the internal jet and its effect on mixing between the two droplets. Furthermore, the project for studying the jet-like mixing in the high Weber number collision of unequal size droplets was also numerically studied by using the numerical simulated method with the lattice Boltzmann method. The phase-field multiphase model was employed to capture the liquid-gas interface, and massless particles were tracked by using the 4th order Runge-Kutta method to visualize the internal mixing of the droplet. Two droplets with different size axisymmetric placed in the initially stationary gaseous environment, and the formation of the internal jet with the time evolution of the penetration length. With understanding of the mechanism for internal jet formation, parametric studies were conducted by manipulating the disparity of liquid viscosities and explore the possible strategy for mixing enhancement. The works have been published on Physical Review Fluids, 2017, 2, 113607 and International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer, 2018, 120, 218-227. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 3: To complete a regime nomogram in the We-∆ space with We= O(10)~O(100) and ∆=1.0-5.0 Research activities: To make the experimental results more interesting and useful to the combustion community, we investigated experimentally and computationally for understanding the influence of off-center collision on the hypergolic ignitability of TMEDA and WFNA droplets by head-on and off-center collision. The regime nomogram in the We-∆ and We-B (impact parameter) have been studied. The process is controlled by the mass interminglement and mixing to the droplet coalescence. The ignition delay time was experimentally found to non-monotonically vary with the impact parameter. In addition, we adopted a validated volume-of-fluid simulation to validate the hypothesis. The non-monotonic variation of IDT with varying B has been confirmed for more ranges of We and ∆, and illustrating the non-monotonicity is a general characteristic in the system. The system of binary droplets head-on collision varying sizes was also experimentally investigated with emphasis on the effect of droplet size on the ignitibility and the ignition delay time. The ignitibility regime nomogram in We-∆ space indicates that the reduction droplet size tends to suppress the hypergolic ignition. Droplet size effect on the hypergolic ignition by head-on and off-center collision of TMEDA and WFNA droplets was experimentally stuided and theoretically analyzed. These two studies can apply into the real engine system, to precisely identify the actual distribution of droplet sizes and the range of collision parameters. The works have been published on Combustion and Flame, 2018, 197, 276-289 and International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer, 2019, 139, 475-481. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 4: To develop and validate an in-house computer code based on the lattice Boltzmann method and use it to study the head-on collision of (equal- and unequal-size) droplets of the concerned shear-thinning fluids. Research activities: Numerical simulation based on the lattice Boltzmann method has been established and used to study head-on collision of droplets of both equal size and unequal size. In the project, the in-house computer code has been developed and it was adopted to study the Marangoni-flow-induced partial coalescence of a droplet on a liquid-air interface. Furthermore, a theory on the coalescence of two spherical liquid droplets that are initially stationary was developed. The evolution of the radius of a liquid neck formed upon coalescence was formulated as an initial value problem and solved to yield an exact solution without free parameters, with its two asymptotic approximation reproducing the widely known scaling relation in the inertially limited viscous and inertial. The study unified the previous theories to support the prominent scaling laws as well as crossover behaviors observed from the previous studies and the approach also sets an example of how viscous-to-inertial transition might be dealt with analytically in other similar problems. The works have been published on Physical Review Fluids, 2018, 3, 023602 and Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, 2019, 116(47), 23467-23472. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 5: To attempt to extend the capabilities of the experimental apparatus and the computer code to study three-dimensional, off-center collision. The computationally demanding three-dimensional simulation will be conducted mainly for those cases, in which new collision phenomena are observed and qualitatively different from those in heard-on collisions. Research activities: The three-dimensional experiments have been completed for studying the impact parameters effects on droplet collision outcomes. We also extended the capabilities of the computer code to study three-dimensional, off-center collision. The off-center collision of binary bouncing droplets of equal size was studied numerically by VOF method with tow maker functions, which has been justified and validated by comparing with available experimental results. In the study, a nonmonotonic kinetic energy recovery with varying impact parameters was discovered In addition, we also instigated the off-center droplet bouncing using similar method. The particular interest of the study is on analyzing the velocity and vorticity vector fields and their correlations, such as helicity and enstrophy. The helicity analysis identifies a strong interaction between the “ring-shaped” vortices and the “line-shaped” shear layers in the non-axisymmetric droplet internal flow. A general relation between the total enstrophy and the total viscous dissipation rate for an unsteady free-surface flow was theoretically derived and numerically verified. The works have been published on Physics of Fluids, 2019, 31, 052004; C. He, X. Xia, and Physics of Fluids, 2020, 32 032004. Percentage achieved: 100%

15265116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15265116.value: 1. Vortex-ring-induced internal mixing for initially stationary droplets coalescence The formation of the main vortex ring is to make the emergence of the internal jet. The jet-like structure shows a strong correlation with the main vortex inside the merged droplet. We further developed and substantiated a vortex-ring-based Reynolds number criterion to interpret the occurrence of the internal jet at various Ohnesorge numbers and size ratios. (Physical Review Fluids, 2017, 2, 113607) 2. Marangoni-flow induced a droplet partial coalescence on a liquid/air interface The coalescence of a droplet on a liquid/air interface with lower surface tension was studied by using the phase-field method. The lattice Boltzmann method was employed for solving the flow field as well as the liquid/air interface. Both surface tension and Marangoni stress take the potential form in the simulation to relieve numerical difficulty of interfacial forces. (Physical Review Fluids, 2018, 3, 023602) 3. Hypergolic ignition of TMEDA and WFNA droplets by head-on and off-center collision The hypergolic ignition induced by the head-on and off-center collision between N,N,N',N'-tetramethylethylenediamine (TMEDA) and white fuming nitric acid (WFNA) droplets were experimentally and computationally investigated for understanding the effect of droplet size on the ignitibility and the ignition delay time, and the influence of the system which is controlled by the mass interminglement and mixing subsequent to the droplet coalescence. (Combustion and Flame, 2018, 197, 276-289 International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer, 2019, 139, 475-481) 4. Non-monotonic viscous dissipation of off-center droplet bouncing A non-monotonic kinetic energy (KE) recovery with change of impact parameters was discovered. This can be explained by the prolonged entanglement time and the enhanced internal-flow-induced viscous dissipation for bouncing droplets at intermediate impact parameters, compared with those at smaller or larger impact parameters. Furthermore, we analyzed the velocity and vorticity vector fields and their correlations. (Physics of Fluids, 2019, 31, 052004; Physics of Fluids, 2020, 32 032004) 5. Universality in the viscous-to-inertial coalescence of liquid droplets We provided a theory on the coalescence of two spherical liquid droplets that are initially stationary. The evolution of the radius of a liquid neck formed upon coalescence was formulated as an initial value problem and then solved to yield an exact solution without free parameters, with its two asymptotic approximations reproducing the well-known scaling relations in the inertially limited viscous and inertial regimes. (Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, 2019, 116(47), 23467-23472)

15265116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15265116.value: The project focused on the experimental observations and physical explanations on various collision outcomes also with some help of numerical simulation, in which both these methods are all indispensable to study binary droplet collision. Especially, the experimental method is a most direct way to study binary droplet collision. The theoretical analysis can draw some conclusions but is hardly to predict the entire complicated and unsteady collision process involving multi-scale and multi-physics characteristics. Similarly, the numerical simulation also cannot predict the droplet collision although they are useful to analyze the microscopic flow field once has been validated by experimental observations sufficiently. Compared with extensively studies on the effects of size ratio, We, Oh, and impact parameter on the binary collision, the potential for further development of the research can be extended to the pressure effects on the binary droplet bouncing and the visualization of the internal mixing between two reactive droplets. The experimental facilities are still challenging for the microscopic flow field visualization and analysis. The efficient numerical methods are always desired on the prediction of droplet coalescence and bouncing which is of great significance to understand the fundamental physics of binary droplet collision.

15265116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15265116.value: Droplet collision in a gaseous environment is of fundamental relevance to many natural and industrial processes, such as rain formation, ink-jet printing, spray coating, and spray combustion in engines. Recently, more and more studies were focused on experimental, numerical and theoretical investigations to unravel the rich phenomena and the multi-scale physics, with emphasis on identifying collision outcomes and their dependence on the collision parameters, such as coalescence, bouncing and separation, which strongly influence the number density, the velocity and size distributions of droplets, and in turn the efficiency of a concerned process. Generally, most of the fluids in the engineering applications somehow reflect the non-Newtonian flow characteristics that the apparent viscosity is a function of the local shear rate. The most common shear-thinning (or shear-thickening) liquids are that whose viscosity decrease (or increases) with increasing local shear rate. Due to lack of the experimental and numerical studies of binary collision between non-Newtonian droplets, the practical difficulties are in generating spatially and temporally stable non-Newtonian droplet with large low-shear-rate viscosity and validated numerical method. The project aims to solve these difficulties and understand the fundamental physics of binary droplet collision.

15265216.label: Project Objectives
15265216.value: Formation of the leader and return stroke channel: A lightning return stroke is usually preceded by leader process that starts inside the cloud and extends vertically in both upward and downward directions. The upward leader is positively charged and extends into the upper layer of the cloud. The downward leader is negatively charged and extends towards ground. With the streamer zone ahead of the downward leader touches the ground or connects to an upward connecting leader, the final breakdown occurs hence the return stroke starts. Therefore, the initial condition of the return stroke entirely depends on the preceding leader channel. With the proposer's leader model, equations describing the initial condition of a return stroke in relation with the preceding leader will be proposed, which include the leader initiation potential and height, leader current, leader channel radius, conductance and electric field etc. Evolution of the return stroke channel: The return stroke evolves along the preceding leader and steamer channel. Its channel should include the downward leader portion, the streamer portion, and upward connecting leader portion (if any). The conductance evolution pattern for the 3 channel portions, which are eventually responsible for the return stroke evolution, will be proposed based on existing arc theories and practices. Evolution of channel currents, charges and electric fields can then be linked to channel conductance by Time Domain Electric Field Integral Equation (TD-EFIE). Return stroke-produced optical and electromagnetic radiations: Lightning return stroke produces strong electromagnetic and bright optical radiations. The return stroke channel can be considered as a vertical/bending thin wire standing on conductive ground. With the current output from the above TD-EFIE model, the electromagnetic radiations from the return stroke will be also simulated. Furthermore, with the current and conductance, adequate calculation formula for the light emission power from the channel will be proposed. The calculated waveform of the current, electric field, magnetic field and light power can then be compared with those in literature and observed. Validation of the model based on observations: In collaboration with Meteorological Bureau of Shenzhen, China, a 362 m high meteorological tower will be built up in suburb area of Shenzhen city by May of 2016. The tower will be equipped with lightning current and electric field measuring systems. Meanwhile, a close and a distant stations with comprehensive electromagnetic and optical observation systems will be set up around the tower. For observed lightning strikes to the tower, we can apply the proposed model to them to see how good the model will perform. Understanding of the insights of the leader/return stroke process: There may be different types of leader/return strokes to the tower being observed. Modelling and comparison can be done for all these leader/ return strokes. Once the model is calibrated and generalized with these observed leader/return strokes, it can be used to discuss the relationship between the leader and the following return stroke in all aspects.

15265216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15265216.value: 閃電可發生在雷暴雲間或從雷暴雲到地發生。典型的雲對地放電通常由始發於雲中而下行的先導過程開始。当下行先導触地时便引發自下而上的回擊過程。正是這個回擊過程產生的強大電流，導致地表上各種系統受損。 觀测是了解閃電回擊屬性最直接的方法。但因儀器的局限性，我們對諸如回擊電流、通道半徑、溫度、電子密度及電導率等的特性仍不很清楚。除了觀察，自七十年代起，人们提出來了各種模型用於預測回擊屬性，當中包括物理或動態氣體模型、電磁學模型、分佈電路及工程學模型等。但每種模型都具有明顯的優點和缺點。事實上，回擊總是在下行先導之後，正是在前的下行先導決定着跟隨其後的回擊的屬性。此外回擊的屬性總是時空演變的。但這兩點被大多數現存的回擊模型所忽視。最近，Kumar提出了一個針對首次回擊的宏觀模型。就物理完備性和簡單性而言，Kumar的這個模型在描述回擊的電學和物理學屬性上是最好的，但需要進一步的改進。 因此，本項目旨在以我们的先導模型和Kumar的回擊模型為基礎，開發出一個動態先導回擊耦合模型。首先，我们将基于先導通道和邊界條件，推導出一組控制回擊主要參數的方程，例如通道電流、電荷、通道半徑和電導率等。其次，基於電流和電導，推導出一組可以模擬回擊產生的光和電磁輻射的方程。最後，我们將利用配備電學和光學探測系統的高塔雷擊实验對所建模型及方程進行驗證和修改。

15265216.label: Realisation of objectives
15265216.value: The main purpose of this project is the development of a dynamic lightning leader-return stroke coupled model based the Time Domain Electric Field Integral Equation (TD-EFIE) and the validation of the model based on observation. There are 5 core tasks: (1) To format a suitable leader- return-stroke channel representing the channel condition at the transition time of the leader process to the return stroke process; (2) To establish a lightning return stroke channel evolution scheme for the channel current, charge accumulation, electric field and channel size and conductance based on TD-EFIE; (3) With the current and conductance outputs from the TD-EFIE model, an adequate model for the electric power along the channel and that for the light emission from the channel will be also proposed; (4) To implement the models with various initial conditions and validate its outputs with onsite observations, and (5) to understand the relationships between the return stroke process and the preceding leader process from both the model outputs and the onsite observations. To achieve these tasks, starting from January of 2017 to December of 2019, we have been carried our continuously field observations and numerous lightning data have been obtained and analyzed with the proposed model. (a) Firstly, for the leader-return-stroke channel formation, we have considered that a lightning return stroke is usually preceded by a leader process that starts inside the cloud and extends vertically in both upward and downward directions. The upward leader is positively charged (UPL) with numbers of branches stretching into the upper layer of the cloud. The downward leader is negatively charged (DNL) and extends towards ground. With the streamer zone ahead of the downward leader touches the ground or connects to an upward connecting leader (UCL) from grounded object, the final breakdown occurs hence the return stroke starts. Therefore, the initial condition of the return stroke entirely depends on the preceding leader channels including the UPL, DNL and UCL. Based on such an idea, adequate lightning channel structures and equations presenting the initial condition of a return stroke have been proposed. The initial condition includes the leader initiation potential and height, leader current and electric field, leader channel radius and conductance etc. With this effort, we have achieved 100% of Tasks (1) and 20% of Tasks (2). (b) Secondarily, for the evolution of the return stroke channels, we have supposed that the return stroke evolves along the preceding leader and steamer channels. Its evolution involves 3 different channel portions: the downward leader portion, the streamer portion, and UCL or grounding object portion (if any). The patterns of channel conductance evolution for the 3 channel portions, which are eventually responsible for the return stroke evolution, have be proposed based on existing spark/arc theories with adequate revisions under different conditions. The evolution of channel current, charge accumulation and electric field have been related to the channel conductance by the Time Domain Electric Field Integral Equation (TD-EFIE). With this effort, we have achieved 100% of Task (2). (c) Thirdly, for modeling the return-stroke-produced optical and electromagnetic radiations at remote distance, we have assumed that the return stroke channel could be considered as a vertical/bending thin wire standing on conductive ground. With the current output from the above TD-EFIE model, the electric and magnetic fields produced by a return stroke at different positions have been calculated by using adequate field expressions in terms of current. Furthermore, with the current and conductance, a model for the electric power along the channel and that for the light emission from the channel has been be proposed. The calculated waveforms of the current, electric and magnetic fields and light power have then be compared with those in literature and observed. By this effort, we have achieved 100% of Task (3) and 20 % of Task (4). The outputs of Tasks (1), (2) and (3) have been summarized into a journal paper “A leader-return-stroke consistent macroscopic model for calculations of return stroke current and its optical and electromagnetic emissions”, Journal of Geophysical Research - Atmosphere, August 2017 (doi:10.1002/2017JD026490) and a conference paper “Representation of lightning return stroke channel in FDTD code and its impact on lightning-produced electric field calculation”, 34th ICLP, 02-07 Sep. 2018, Rzeszow, Poland (doi:10.1109/ICLP.2018.8503324). (d) Fourthly, for application and validation of the model, in collaboration with Meteorological Bureau of Shenzhen, China, a set of lightning observation facility on and around the 362 m-high meteorological tower had been established by May of 2017, which includes the on-tower lightning current and electric field measuring systems, a close and a distant observation stations with comprehensive electromagnetic and optical observation systems around the tower. With these facilities, a large number of lightning current, electrical and optical data on lightning strokes to the tower have been obtained, analyzed and compared with the model outputs. The results were published in two journal papers: “Optical and current measurements of lightning attachment to the 356-m-high Shenzhen Meteorological Gradient Tower in southern coastal area of China”, IEEE Access, Oct. 2019 (doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2019.2949127), and “A GPU-based grid traverse algorithm for accelerating lightning geolocation process”, IEEE Transactions on EMC, Apr. 2019 (doi:10.1109/TEMC.2019.2907715). With this effort, we have achieved 100 % of Task 4 and 50 % of Task 5. (e) Lastly, for the relationship between the return stroke process and the preceding leader process, we have observed different types of leader/return strokes to the tower being observed. For each type of leader/return stroke, the detailed channel and electric parameters were analyzed based on a model-observation-combination algorithm. The results revealed that the parameters of lightning return stroke/main discharging process were closely related to the parameters of the preceding leader process, which was in well consistent with the model predictions. Parts of the results were published in a journal paper “The spatial evolution of upward positive stepped leaders initiated from a 356‐m‐tall tower in southern China”, Journal of Geophysical Research - Atmospheres, (doi:10.1029/2019JD031508). With this effort, we have achieved 100% of Task 5.

15265216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15265216.value: Firstly, we have succeeded in developing a new leader-return stroke consistent model based on the time domain electric field integral equation. The model has been further extended to simulate the optical and electromagnetic emissions of a return stroke by introducing a set of equations relating the return stroke current and conductance to the optical and electromagnetic emissions. The model has been tested with different leader initiation potentials ranging from -10 to -140 MV, resulting in different return stroke current peaks ranging from 2.6 kA to 209 kA with different return stroke speed peaks ranging from 0.2 to 0.8 speed of light and different optical power peaks ranging from 4.76 MW/m to 248 MW/m, showing that the larger of the leader initiation potential, the larger of the return stroke current and speed (Ref.: Journal paper No.1 - doi:10.1002/2017JD026490). In addition, we have also proposed a method to represent the lightning return stroke channel for simulative study of lightning effect with the finite-different time-domain method (Ref.: Conference paper No.1 - doi:10.1109/ICLP.2018.8503324). Secondly, with coordinated optical and current measurements, a total of 24 discharges to the Shenzhen 356-m high tower have been well-documented during the project period. It was found that these events can be divided into three types: Type 1 - a connecting upward positive leader (connecting UPL) induced by a downward negative in a downward negative discharge, Types 2 - an upward positive leader (UPL) in the initial stage of an upward negative discharge, and Type 3 - an upward negative leader (UNL) in the initial stage of an upward positive discharge. Features of optical and current parameters associated with the leader stepping and propagation process were analyzed in comparison with the model (Ref.: Journal papers No.2 - doi:10.1109/TEMC.2019.2925140 and No.3 - doi:10.1109/TEMC.2019.2907715). Thirdly, the spatial evolution of upward positive stepped leaders initiated from the Shenzhen 356-m-high tower have been investigated with the high-speed camera and electric field measurements. Particularly, the radius of the leader luminous channel as a function of time and height have been estimated for the firstly. It was found that the channel radius variation features show a very good agreement with the concept of leader corona sheath that used in our model. (Ref.: Journal paper No. 4 - doi:10.1029/2019JD031508).

15265216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15265216.value: By this project, we have proposed and demonstrated a leader-return-stroke-coupled model for describing the relationship between the lightning leader and the following return stroke process as well as the lightning-stroke-produced optical and electromagnetic emissions. The model can be further extended for studies of lightning strokes to various structures on ground, but needs verification and modifications based on onsite observations. The model, after further verification, could serve as a virtual laboratory for simulative study of the effects of lightning strokes to various structures on ground, so that optimal mitigation and protection measures could be made against the lightning-caused hazard. To achieve this goal, a well-coordinated modeling and field observation of lightning strokes to tall structures will be the right direction to head in near future.

15265216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15265216.value: A lightning bolt to ground usually starts inside the cloud with a downward leader process, followed by a return stroke process. It is the return stroke process that produces a strong electric current pulse, causing damages to various systems on earth. Observation is the most direct way to understand the property of a lightning return stroke, but limited by instrumentations, we have little knowledge on the evolution of return stroke current, charge, channel radius and conductance etc. For this sake, many models have been proposed to predict the lightning return stroke property since 1970s. However, the fact that the property of a lightning return stroke is largely determined by the preceding downward leader and always evolves with times, have been ignored or scorned in most existing models. In this project, we have proposed and demonstrated a dynamic leader-return-stroke model based on the time domain electric field integral equation. With a presumed leader condition, the model can predict the space-time evolution of the return stroke property, including the current, charge, channel size and conductance, as well as the lightning-produced optical and electromagnetic radiations. The model has been verified with observed lightning strokes to a tall tower.
