15265516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15265516.value: Secondary organic aerosol (SOA) is a ubiquitous and important constituent of atmospheric aerosols in both urban and rural environment, and has adverse impacts on human health, visibility and climate change. Current atmospheric chemistry models face large challenge in predicting SOA formation to match the field observation because of uncertainties in sources, precursors, formation pathways, and products identification. In addition to the traditional mechanism of gas-phase oxidation followed by gas-particle conversion, recent studies have revealed that heterogeneous and aqueous-phase reactions could also contribute to substantial SOA production. Yet our understanding on this heterogeneous pathway is far from complete, significant knowledge gaps remain in the reactivity of different organic precursors on aerosols and cloud droplets, as well as in the subsequent aqueous production of low-volatile products. Due to their contribution to SOA formation, these heterogeneous processes may also play important roles in the severe particulate and haze pollution in many polluted areas, including Hong Kong and China, which has not been well addressed. Therefore, we propose to conduct field measurements of heterogeneous processes of representative precursors (i.e., glyoxal and methylglyoxal) by using in-situ aerosol flow tube and high resolution real-time mass spectrometer, followed by modeling analysis. The goal is to determine the heterogeneous reactive uptake of glyoxal and methylglyoxal on ambient wet aerosols and cloud droplets in the polluted subtropical environment, to investigate the evolution and partitioning of these carbonyls among gas, aerosols and cloud droplets, and to understand the aqueous-phase reactions and their impacts on SOA formation in Hong Kong. This study will help fill the knowledge gaps on heterogeneous formation of SOA in the costal environment with co-existence of high anthropogenic and natural precursors, and high humidity. It also can be used to improve the performance of current air quality models which are used in the formulation of pollution-control measures. 二次有機氣溶膠（SOA）是城市和區域空氣中氣溶膠/顆粒物的重要組成部分，在影響人體健康、大氣能見度和氣候變化等方面都有重要作用。由於二次有機氣溶膠生成機制較為複雜，目前空氣質量模式在準確模擬SOA含量方面還存在許多不足，特別是與許多地區測量結果相比，模式模擬結果往往低估。除傳統氣相氧化-氣粒分配機制外，最新研究發現，大氣多相和液相反應過程可能對SOA生成也有重要貢獻。然而，目前對於大氣多相過程的研究和認識還不充分，特別是對於氣態前體物在氣溶膠和雲霧液滴等多相介質表面的物理化學過程、及複雜的液相低揮發性產物等方面尚不完全清楚。而液相SOA生成過程可能對許多污染地區嚴重的顆粒物和灰霾污染具有重要的作用，亟需開展深入和詳細的研究。 為此，本項目擬利用高分辨質譜和現場氣溶膠流動管技術，對代表性前體物（乙二醛和甲基乙二醛）的大氣液相過程進行實際測量，並結合多相化學模式進行模擬分析。本項目研究旨在瞭解亞熱帶污染地區乙二醛和甲基乙二醛在吸濕氣溶膠和雲霧液滴上的非均相攝取，研究這些大氣羰基化合物在氣體、氣溶膠和雲霧之間的分配和轉化過程，並進一步探討這些大氣液相過程對香港大氣中SOA生成的影響。本研究的開展預期將有助於完善對SOA在人為污染和自然源前體物共存且高濕度條件下的生成機制的認識，相關研究結果將有利於改善現有空氣質量模式，也可為開展進一步大氣污染控制提供科學支撐。

15265516.label: Realisation of objectives
15265516.value: To achieve the project objectives, comprehensive field measurement, data analysis and modeling simulation were conducted during the project period. 1. Two comprehensive atmospheric multiphase campaigns were carried out at the summit of Tai Mo Shan (TMS) in Hong Kong in the fall of 2016 and spring of 2017. OVOCs in the gas phase, cloud water, and aerosols were concurrently collected or monitored during the campaigns. The abundances of glyoxal (Gly), methylglyoxal (Mgly) and other carbonyls (including formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, propanol, acetone, glycolaldehyde, etc) in the multi-phases samples were characterized and quantified. The oxidation products from the OVOCs, such as carboxylic acids including formic, acetic, pyruvic, oxalic, and glyoxylic acids) in cloud water and aerosols were also quantified. The molecular distribution and stable carbon isotopic composition of diacids, oxo-carboxylic acids, and α-dicarbonyls were analyzed. Through data analysis, the partitioning of different mono-and di-carbonyls among cloud/fog droplet, aerosol, and gas phases was obtained for the first time in Hong Kong. The concurrent multiphase analysis shows that mono-carbonyls (acetone, formaldehyde, and acetaldehyde) mainly present in the gas phase (~98%), whereas Gly and Mgly exist in both gas phase (~50%) and cloud water (30-50%), with only a small fraction (~1%) in particles. Around 20-30% of the formic and acetic acids and 30-40% of oxalic acid were present in the particles, with more abundance in the cloud droplets. The measured aqueous fraction of carbonyl compounds was compared to the theoretical estimation from Henry's law equilibrium considering the hydration reactions. Significant aqueous-phase supersaturation was found for less soluble mono-carbonyls and Mgly, with 1-3 orders of magnitude higher than the theoretical partitioning values. The dependence of partitioning behaviors on different factors was further examined, including the cloud water acidity, liquid water content, salting-in/out effects, adsorption and oligomerization effects, in-cloud aqueous reactions. The acidity of the cloud water can primarily affect the reactive uptake of di-carbonyls on droplets and influence the partitioning of carbonyls. Through the atmospheric multiphase campaigns at HK and in-depth data analysis, we obtained the first insight into the partitioning and processing of glyoxal, methylglyoxal and oxidation products in gas, aerosol and cloud, as well as different influencing factors. Objective 1 is fully achieved. 2. Two aerosol-flow-tube (AFT) systems have been developed for reactive uptake measurement in the laboratory and field. One set of AFT is comprised of a Pyrex tube reactor and moveable injector, and utilizes the kinetic decay method by fitting the decay of measured Gly and Mgly as a function of interaction time, to derive the uptake coefficient on lab-created aerosols. Another set of field-deployable AFT is a Teflon-coated stainless-steel tube, with an aerosol filter manifold. By switching valves in the sample inlet, ambient air can be introduced directly into the flow tube or through a PTFE membrane to remove aerosols. At the exit of the AFT, the difference of reactant gas between aerosol-present and aerosol-absent states can be measured. Then the pseudo-fist order rate coefficient for the heterogeneous reaction of reactants on real ambient aerosols can be determined from this aerosol modulation method. The uptake coefficients of Gly and Mgly were measured on the ammonia sulfate aerosols under different RH conditions, showing positive dependences on RH and aerosol water content, with the average γgly and γmgly of 0.0029 and 0.0004, respectively. The field-deployable ATF was then deployed in the field at a suburban site in the PRD region in 2017, to test its applicability in measuring uptake coefficients of different gases on complex ambient aerosols in polluted environments. The measured uptake coefficient of glyoxal on real ambient aerosols varied from 0.0023 to 0.0143, with an average γ of 0.0062. The results are comparable with the values determined on inorganic/organic mixed particles considering the photochemical process in a previous study, highlighting the importance of aerosol water content and organic aerosol composition on the reactive uptake of di-carbonyls. By integrating the experiment results and literature review, we compiled a heterogenous module that can be directly incorporated into the photochemical MCM model, to represent the heterogeneous process of Gly and Mgly on aerosols. The heterogeneous module parameterizes the reversible partitioning of monomers and oligomers of Gly and Mgly in the aqueous phase, the irreversible ammonium-catalyzed and OH-oxidation volume reaction pathways, and the irreversible surface uptake processes. The developed module was then incorporated into the observation-based photochemical model (OBM) to evaluated its performance and the importance of heterogeneous uptake of Gly and Mgly. The results suggested that without considering the heterogeneous processes, the model would overpredict the mixing ratios of Gly and Mgly by a factor of 3.0-3.5 compared to the observation. The agreement between observation and simulation improved significantly when the heterogenous module was incorporated, which in total contributed 62% to the atmospheric loss of Gly and Mgly during daytime. By combining the laboratory, field measurement, and modeling simulation, the heterogeneous uptake of Gly and Mgly were quantified, and an improved heterogeneous model parameterization was developed. The developed module can be directly incorporated into photochemical box models and improve the model simulation on the levels and budget of Gly and Mgly. Objective 2 is fully achieved. 3. With the multiphase measurement data at TMS, the production of low-volatile organics (e.g., carboxylic acids) from the aqueous and heterogeneous processes during the cloud was investigated. Substantial dissolved organics (DOM) in the cloud water were contributed by the in-cloud aqueous reactions. Gly, showing good correlations with carboxylic acids and DOM, served as an important precursor for the in-cloud formation of SOA. The C-13 isotopic composition of dicarboxylic acids was further examined to evaluate the contribution of different sources, among which atmospheric photooxidation of anthropogenic precursors plays dominant roles. To further evaluate the contribution of heterogeneous chemistry on SOA formation, another intensive field campaign was conducted at a background site during a severe haze episode in HK-PRD during January 2017. Enhanced oxygenated organic matters were observed, and the potential precursors and formation pathways of carboxylic acids and SOA were examined. The improved heterogeneous module was incorporated into the OBM-MCM model to investigate the production and evolution of Gly and Mgly, and their contributions to SOA formation during the haze episode. The photochemical budget analysis of Gly and Mgly showed that the oxidation of aromatics by OH radicals was the major pathway producing Gly and Mgly, followed by oxidation of alkynes and alkenes. Based on the improved heterogeneous mechanism, the contributions of VOC oxidation to SOA formed from gas-particle partitioning (SOAgp) and from heterogeneous processes of Gly and Mgly (SOAhet) were quantified and compared. Anthropogenic m, p-xylene and toluene were found to have dominant contributions to SOAhet formation. Overall, the heterogeneous processes of Gly and Mgly can explain 21% of SOA mass in the PRD region. The results demonstrated the important roles of heterogeneous processes of Gly and Mgly in SOA formation and haze pollution. Through in-depth data analysis and modeling investigation, the source and formation of carboxylic acids in cloud water and aerosols were characterized in the HK-PRD region, and the photochemical budget of Gly and Mgly were investigated during the haze episode. The contribution of heterogeneous processes of Gly and Mgly on low-volatile oxidation products and SOA formation were quantified in the HK-PRD region. Objective 3 is also fully achieved.

15265516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15265516.value: Through three years of continuous research, some novel and scientific findings have been achieved, as summarized below. 1) The first comprehensive multiphase field campaign in Hong Kong gained valuable insights into the formation, partitioning, and transformation of glyoxal and methylglyoxal among gas, aerosol and cloud droplets (Zhao et al., 2019; Li et al., 2020). The partitioning behavior of Gly, Mgly, and mono-carbonyls among different phases was obtained in HK for the first time. Significant aqueous-phase supersaturation was found for mono-carbonyls and Mgly. The abundant Gly played an essential role in the heterogeneous formation of carboxylic acid and SOA in the cloud (Li et al., 2020). 2) A field-deployable AFT system was developed for directly measuring the uptake of reactive gases on real ambient aerosols for polluted environments, and has been successfully applied in the HK-PRD region to measure the uptake of reactive nitrogen and carbonyls (Wang et al., 2018). The heterogenous parameterization derived from in-situ uptake measurement can significantly improve the air quality model simulation on secondary aerosols (Yu et al., 2020). A systematic evaluation of heterogeneous HO2 uptake on wet aerosol and cloud droplets was also performed. The key factors influencing the uptake process were characterized, and uptake coefficients at different atmospheric conditions were recommended (Guo et al., 2019). 3) A heterogeneous module of Gly and Mgly was developed, including reversible partitioning, irreversible volume reactions and surface uptake, coupled with gas-particle partitioning of oxidation products (Ling et al., 2020). Incorporating this heterogeneous module into the photochemical model can significantly improve the simulation of atmospheric level and evolution of Gly and Mgly in the HK-PRD region. The improved model was applied to quantify the contribution of heterogeneous processes of Gly and Mgly on SOA formation during haze episodes (Ling et al., 2020). 4) The improved photochemical model was also utilized to investigate the atmospheric budget and formation of Gly and Mgly, and identified the anthropogenic aromatic VOCs as key precursors. The formation mechanisms of carbonyls from anthropogenic VOCs were identified, and the sources of different precursors were quantified from the box model coupled with PMF analysis (He et al., 2019). The condensation of oxygenated organic vapors from anthropogenic VOCs dominates the formation of SOA in Hong Kong and other Chinese megacities (Nie et al., 2021). The project findings fill in the knowledge gaps on atmospheric heterogeneous chemistry and SOA formation in the polluted subtropical environment, and can support the formulation of air pollution control strategies in Hong Kong. The project has produced 10 peer-reviewed journal papers and 4 conference presentations.

15265516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15265516.value: The findings from this project revealed the complicated partitioning behaviors of Gly and Mgly among gas, aerosols, and cloud droplets, and also the complex factors affecting the heterogeneous uptake of Gly and Mgly on ambient aerosols. Further laboratory and field studies under different conditions and with different aerosol and cloud surfaces are needed to better characterize and quantify those physical processes and chemical mechanisms. The results highlight the importance of heterogeneous Gly and Mgly chemistry on SOA formation. It will be of great interest to extend the heterogeneous study to other oxygenated organic compounds, which may account for a significant fraction of total VOCs in the urban air. Further efforts are also required to improve the heterogenous parameterizations of different species on aerosol and cloud droplets in air quality models to improve the model performance. There has been increasing attention and understanding of OVOCs' importance on photochemical ozone and SOA in the urbanized regions. Continous and long-term monitoring of speciated OVOCs should be performed to better characterize their atmospheric budget, sources, and formation mechanism. Therefore, further control measures can be designed to improve the air quality in the HK-PRD region.

15265516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15265516.value: Secondary organic aerosol is a ubiquitous and important constituent of atmospheric aerosols, having adverse impacts on human health, visibility, and climate change. Heterogeneous reactions of many organic precursors on the aerosol surface can produce substantial low-volatile and oxygenated products, has emerged as a critical SOA formation pathway, and drawn increasing interest. A first concurrent multiphase field campaign was conducted at a mountain site in Hong Kong, and valuable insights were obtained into the partitioning and evolution of glyoxal, methylglyoxal, and their oxidation products in gas, aerosol, and cloud waters. By uniting the laboratory, field, and modeling, the heterogeneous uptake of glyoxal and methylglyoxal was investigated and then parameterized into a comprehensive heterogeneous module. With the incorporation of the developed module into photochemistry models, we examined the atmospheric budget of glyoxal and methylglyoxal, and quantified the contribution of their heterogeneous reactions on SOA formation in the HK-PRD region. This research demonstrates the essential roles of multiphase and heterogeneous reactions in VOC evolution, SOA formation, and affecting the air quality in the HK-PRD region. The findings and developed methodology are useful to improve the model performance in predicting the SOA formation, therefore supporting the formulation of pollution-control measures in this region.

15265816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15265816.value: Optical fibre based distributed sensing systems offer many advantages comparing with their electronic counterparts. With typical sensing range in tens of kilometers and spatial resolution of meters, a distributed optical fibre sensor based on a single piece of fibre is equivalent to thousands of electronic point sensors. It is used in more and more application areas including civil and structural engineering, transportation engineering and aviation industries. Distributed sensing systems based on fibre nonlinearity such as Raman scattering, spontaneous Brillouin scattering and stimulated Brillouin scattering have been investigated extensively in recent years. However, due to very weak nonlinear effects involved, signal at the detection point is often very small. As a result, measurement speed is slow since substantial amount of averaging is necessary to remove the effect of noise. This has limited their application to static measurement. However, in many applications, real time and dynamic sensing information is important and alternative sensing techniques has to be used. An interesting approach that has attracted much research interest is phase optical time domain reflectrometer (phase OTDR or φ-OTDR) based on Rayleigh scattering. Much research studies in recent years have shown the effectiveness of the technique. However, a number of issues have limited the further performance improvement of the sensing system. These include polarization variation within the pulse duration; laser phase noise and frequency drift during measurement. In addition, signal to noise ratio at the detection point is also a significant liming factor for system performance. In this project, we will study techniques that have potential to overcome these limitations. In particular, we propose the use polarization diversity coherent detection with differential phase detection to solve problems discussed above. Various implementation schemes will be investigated and a number of schemes for signal to noise ratio enhancement will be studied. We believe through the study, significant improvement on the performance of distributed optical fibre sensing system can be achieved and will enable the sensing technique to be used in more application areas. 基于光纤的分布式传感系统同电子传感器相比有很多优点。光纤分布式传感系统可以在几十公里传感范围内实现几米的分辨精度。这相当于几千个电子传感器。由于这些优点光纤分布式传感系统被越来越多地用在土木，交通及航空系统中。近年来在基于拉曼，自发布里渊及受激布里渊等光纤非线性光纤分布式传感系统方面已有大量研究。 可是由于这些非线性现象都很微弱，所以信号通常都很小，由于需要大量的平均，检测速度通常很慢。由于这些原因， 光纤分布式传感系统通常只能用于静态检测系统。在动态传感系统， 基于瑞利散射的光相位时域反射仪（相位OTDR）最近几年引起大量关注。为进一步增强其性能，需克服由于偏振变化，激光器相位噪声及频率变化带来的影响。在此研究中，我们将通过相干及相位差分检测及极化分集来减小这些问题的影响。我们将研究实现方法及信噪比提升方法以期将此传感系统的性能大大提高。

15265816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15265816.value: Phase sensitive optical time domain reflectometer has been a key technology for distributed sensing of vibration and acoustic signals. Although direct detected systems have been investigated extensively, due to the square law detection at the receiver, no linear relationship between detected signal and the vibration event can be obtained. To solve this problem, algorithm can be developed to enhance event detection. The adoption of coherent detection can however allow a linear relationship to be obtained. This will simplify system design. This has been investigated in the project. The research has resulted six journal publications in leading journals of the research area. A FPGA based prototype has also be built that allow distributed sensing over 20km with 2 meter spatial resolution.

15265816.value: A prototype system has been built and we are exploring its potential for detecting leaking of water pipe. Some promising results have been obtained already.

15265816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15265816.value: In many monitoring applications such as transportation system, security system and civil structures, we need to detect vibration or acoustic signal over tens of kilometers with few meter spatial resolutions. Although we can use discrete electrical sensors such as those based on Piezo electric sensors, many sensors are needed, this will make installation and sensing signal collection very difficult. For example, if we want to monitor 20km railway track with 2 meter spatial resolution, we need to install 10000 sensors. This problem can be solved using distributed optical fibre sensor based on phase sensitive optical time domain reflectometer(OTDR). In this project we have explored algorithm for enhancing event detection using optical fibre phase sensitive OTDR. In addition, since the adoption of coherent detection can allow a linear relationship to be obtained between detected signal and the vibration event, its implementation has been investigated. Based on the study, a FPGA based prototype has been built that allow distributed sensing over 20km with 2 meter spatial resolution to be realized. Its potential applications in transportation systems and water pipe leaking detection have been explored.

15266316.label: Project Objectives
15266316.value: To develop an operator splitting framework for solving the population balance equation for aerosol dynamics, and to investigate the numerical precision and efficiency of this operator splitting with optimization of the method; To further develop the OSMC method, in order to enhance its numerical efficiency and accuracy; and To study the resampling process in order to provide guidance on how to simulate the evolution of particle size distribution characteristics using the stochastic method.
rows: To develop an operator splitting framework for solving the population balance equation for aerosol dynamics, and to investigate the numerical precision and efficiency of this operator splitting with optimization of the method;
To further develop the OSMC method, in order to enhance its numerical efficiency and accuracy; and
To study the resampling process in order to provide guidance on how to simulate the evolution of particle size distribution characteristics using the stochastic method.

15266316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15266316.value: Population balance equations (PBEs) describe the balance on the population of entities, which can be fluid or solid particles, cells, genes, etc. PBEs have been widely used in many branches of modern science and technology, e.g., aerosol, polymerization, crystallization, chemical reactors, etc. In principle, three typical methods (i.e., direct discretization, method of moments, and stochastic method) have been generally used to solve the PBEs. In the present study, the solution of PBE for aerosol dynamics will be the main focus. It is still a challenging task to obtain a highly accurate and efficient solution of the PBE owing to the complexity of the simultaneous aerosol dynamics processes (i.e., nucleation, condensation, coagulation, breakage, chemical reaction, etc.). Hence, a novel operator splitting (OS) framework is proposed for solving the PBE on aerosol dynamics, which is independent of the concrete solution method. Any of the above-mentioned three typical methods can be casted into this proposed framework. Under this framework, both operator splitting method of moments (OSMOM) and operator splitting Monte Carlo (OSMC) method will be developed to solve the PBE. This OSMOM combines the quadrature method of moments (QMOM) and direct quadrature method of moments (DQMOM), which will greatly alleviate the realizability problem (from which both QMOM and DQMOM suffer), while preserving the efficiency and easiness of QMOM and DQMOM. On the other hand, the stochastic method is extremely flexible for accommodating complex physical models and is able to provide the most complete information on the complicated evolution of particle size distribution characteristics. However, the stochastic method is very computationally expensive. A basic OSMC method has recently been developed by the proposers. This proposed OSMC method will be further developed and improved to obtain much higher numerical efficiency through parallel computing with graphics processing unit (GPU). Besides, variance reduction algorithms will also be investigated to accelerate the parallel simulation. Finally, how to efficiently and correctly resample the particle size distribution for general stochastic methods (not limited to the present OSMC) will also be thoroughly investigated. Resampling is necessary to maintain the number of numerical particles in a suitable range in order to prevent extremely high computational cost (i.e., too many numerical particles) or very high numerical error (i.e., too few numerical particles). During the development and verification processes of this new operator splitting framework, various testing and sensitivity cases will be performed to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed methods.

15266316.label: Realisation of objectives
15266316.value: In the realization of Objective 5.2.1, the operator splitting Monte Carlo (OSMC) method has been developed for solving the population balance equations (PBEs) for aerosol dynamics. PBEs are convection-diffusion equations with the source terms including nucleation, surface growth, coagulation and oxidization. PBEs have been widely applied in the fields of aerosol related problems such as atmospheric aerosols, soot particles in combustion flames, smoke particles from forest fires and nanoparticle synthesis etc. Since PBEs are the partial integral-differential equations, analytical solutions of the PBEs are available for only a few ideal cases. Various numerical methods have been developed for solving PBEs and among these methods, the stochastic Monte Carlo (MC) methods show their high computational accuracy and can be easily incorporated with several particle internal coordinates. However, there are two disadvantages in the MC methods which are stochastic error and high computational costs. In addition, only a finite number of numerical particles can be used, the uncertainty of PSDs function is inevitable. Especially at the tail of the particle size spectrum, only a few number of numerical particles are used which make the PSDs poorly represented. To overcome such inherent limitations, the numerical particles with different numerical weights are always adopted. To increase the numerical precision and efficiency, the PI’s collaborative research team firstly developed the operator splitting Monte Carlo (OSMC) method. In the OSMC method, the nucleation and surface growth are handled with deterministic means, while coagulation is simulated with a stochastic method. The deterministic and stochastic approaches in the algorithm are synthesized under the framework of operator splitting to improve the numerical efficiency and to preserve the flexibility of a stochastic method for the numerical simulation of aerosol dynamics. To investigate the numerical precision and efficiency of the stochastic method, both the systematic and stochastic errors of classical Monte Carlo (CMC) and weighted flow algorithm (WFA) methods are analysed, and an analytical relationship is also derived for the first time to connect the variances in these two methods. In the realization of Objective 5.2.2, the differentially weighted operator splitting Monte Carlo (DWOSMC) and weighted fraction Monte Carlo (WFMC) methods are further developed for improving the numerical efficiency and accuracy in the OSMC method. In DWOSMC method, the multi-Monte Carlo method is combined with the operator splitting technique to reduce the statistical noise of equally weighted OSMC method. The DWOSMC method is validated by both analytical solution and sectional method under different aerosol dynamic processes and shows high computationally efficiency and quantitative accuracy. In the WFMC method, a new weighted scheme is constructed based on the multi-Monte Carlo method to further reduce the stochastic error by introducing an additional fraction function. These newly developed methods have been verified with different numerical cases. The stochastic error in the newly proposed WFMC method is significantly reduced when compared with the traditional multi-Monte Carlo (MMC) method for higher-order moments but only with a slight increase in computational cost. In the realization of Objective 5.2.3, the stochasticity of the resampling process is systematically and thoroughly investigated. Resampling refers to the addition (duplication) or removal of randomly selected particles from the existing ones in order to control the number of numerical particles in a specified range. Resampling is explicitly or implicitly adopted in practically all stochastic simulations of aerosol dynamics. Although resampling introduces no bias on the particle size distribution (PSD), additional stochasticity is usually added except for the doubling operation. A formula is derived to quantify the stochastic effect of resampling. The additional stochastic errors by upsampling and downsampling processes are investigated and show that the variance introduced in resampling is considerably significant in general aerosol dynamics when nucleation is dominant, especially in the CMC method. The study of resampling process provides a quantitative description on the variance caused by the resampling process. In summary, a novel operator splitting framework for solving population balance equation on aerosol dynamics is developed. The numerical precision and efficiency of different splitting schemes are investigated. Based on the framework of operator splitting Monte Carlo (OSMC) method, the differentially weighted operator splitting Monte Carlo (DWOSMC) and weighted fraction Monte Carlo (WFMC) methods are further developed for reducing the stochastic error of OSMC method. These newly developed methods are validated with the analytical solution/existing numerical methods from the available literature. The stochasticity of the resampling process is systematically and thoroughly investigated in order to provide guidance on how to simulate the evolution of particle size distribution characteristics using the stochastic method. The listed Revised Objectives in Section 5.2 of this funded project are completely achieved.

15266316.label: Major findings and research outcome
15266316.value: The operator splitting Monte Carlo (OSMC) method is developed for solving the population balance equations (PBEs) for aerosol dynamics. Nucleation and surface growth are handled with deterministic means, while coagulation is simulated with stochastic method. To investigate the numerical precision and efficiency of the stochastic method, both the systematic and stochastic errors in the stochastic simulations of a population balance equation (PBE) are comprehensively investigated for classical Monte Carlo (CMC) and weighted flow algorithm (WFA) methods. A differentially weighted operator splitting Monte Carlo (DWOSMC) method is further developed to solve complex aerosol dynamic processes by coupling the differentially weighted Monte Carlo method and operator splitting technique. The results show that the DWOSMC method is computationally efficient and quantitatively accurate for simulating complex simultaneous aerosol dynamic processes. These major findings can be referred to our published journal paper in Particuology (2018) (see Part C Research Output). In addition, weighted fraction Monte Carlo (WFMC) method is also constructed based on the multi-Monte Carlo method to further reduce the stochastic error by introducing the additional fraction function. The WFMC method for particle coagulation is validated through three classical cases and shows a significant reduction in stochastic error for higher-order moments with a slightly higher computational cost. These major findings can be referred to our published journal paper in International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat & Fluid Flow (2021a) (see Part C Research Output). Then, the WFMC method is further developed and coupled with Lagrangian particle tracking and detailed soot model which are successfully applied to simulate the soot formation and evolution in the premixed ethylene-oxygen-argon flame. These major findings can be referred to our published journal paper in International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat & Fluid Flow (2021b) (accepted for publication on July 13, 2021; Early Access: Sep 2021) (see Part C Research Output). The stochasticity of the resampling process is systematically and thoroughly investigated. The sample variance is found to depend on three parameters: the resampling rate, the number of numerical particles and the population variance of the particle size distribution to be resampled. The expression of the sample variance has also been derived which provides guidance on how to simulate the evolution of particle size distribution characteristics using the stochastic method. These major findings can be referred to our published journal paper in Applied Mathematical Modelling (2020) (see Part C Research Output).

15266316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15266316.value: The major findings and established methodologies obtained from this funded project can be further developed and widely used in the modelling of nanoparticle synthesis and soot formation. The proposed course of action is as follows: (i) To further extend the present developed algorithm to aggregate formation and evolution in the multi-dimensional turbulent reactive flow with the highly reliable experimental datasets and numerical methods available from the literature. (ii) To further increase the computational efficiency and accuracy by developing the capacity of graphics processing unit (GPU) parallel computing OSMC algorithm in order to repeat the stochastic simulation simultaneously. (iii) To further incorporate the OSMC method with the commercial CFD software for solving the scientific problems in complex aerosol systems based on the developed model schemes and codes.

15266316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15266316.value: This project is fundamental research for developing an accurate and efficient numerical scheme for modelling the complex aerosol systems such as the soot particle formation and evolution in combustion, and nanoparticle synthesis. The significance of this project lies in three aspects. Firstly, it greatly improves the numerical precision and efficiency of the stochastic Monte Carlo (MC) method by applying the operator splitting schemes in the simulation of aerosol dynamics. Both the systematic and stochastic errors in the stochastic simulations of the population balance equation (PBE) are comprehensively investigated. Secondly, the further development of operator splitting Monte Carlo (OSMC) method (i.e., differentially weighted operator splitting Monte Carlo (DWOSMC) and weighted fraction Monte Carlo (WFMC) methods) can reduce the stochastic error which is inevitable in the MC methods. These newly developed numerical methods are validated by both analytical solution and sectional method under different aerosol dynamic processes. A high computational efficiency and quantitative accuracy is obtained from these newly developed methods. Thirdly, the resampling process is systematically and thoroughly investigated which introduces the additional stochasticity in Monte Carlo simulation. The results provide guidance on the formation and evolution of particle size distribution characteristics using the stochastic methods.

15266516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15266516.value: Parallel plate capacitors with ultrafast discharging power (much higher than those of batteries and electrochemical supercapacitors) are becoming increasingly important to a broad range of applications, especially in pulsed power circuit applications, such as hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), medical defibrillators, spacecraft, detonators, and electrical weapon systems. Traditional materials used in the parallel plate capacitor include linear dielectrics and nonlinear dielectrics (ferroelectrics and/or antiferroelectrics). While the nonlinear dielectrics are superior in energy density, most of them contain toxic element of lead. In this project, we propose to fabricate thin film capacitors using lead-free ferroelectric/antiferroelectric materials. Ultra-high energy density of the thin film capacitor can be achieved by proper material design, that is, using the ferroelectric phase to obtain high saturation polarization and the antiferroelectric phase to obtain small remnant polarization. High efficiency of the capacitor can also be achieved by doping on the A-site of ABO3 perovskite structure to break the long range ordering of normal ferroelectrics/antiferroelectrics. Several strategies are proposed to enhance the energy density and efficiency of the thin film capacitor. Although the material in the thin film form has much higher energy density than its counterpart in the bulk form, a large area is normally required in order for the capacitor to store enough amount of energy. To solve this obstacle that hinders the practical application of thin film capacitors, we also propose to use a paper-folding technique, Origami, to stack the thin film capacitors together to achieve a compact capacitor device with sizable total energy. This will be the first big step forward to the potential commercialization of thin film capacitors. 具有大功率放電（遠高於電池和電化學超級電容）能力的平行板 電容器在脈衝電路中的應用（如：混合動力電動汽車、醫用除顫 器、宇宙飛船、起爆器和大功率放電武器系統等），正越來越顯 示其重要性。傳統的平行板電容器所用的材料包括線性和非線性 電介質材料（鐵電或反鐵電材料）。雖然非線性電介質材料的儲 能密度相比較高，但是一般而言它們含有有毒的鉛元素。本項目 我們提出用無鉛鐵電/反鐵電材料來製備薄膜電容器，通過鐵電/ 反鐵電兩相共存來提高能量密度，通過合適的摻雜來提升儲能效 率。最後，通過“摺紙”工藝，將薄膜電容器摺疊起來以實現器件 的小型化。

15266516.label: Realisation of objectives
15266516.value: All objectives are 100% achieved. 1. To deposit high quality epitaxial ferroelectric/antiferroelectric thin films on platinized silicon on insulator (SOI) substrate to achieve high energy density and high efficiency of the thin film capacitors. High quality BCT-BMT and PLZST relaxor ferroelectric/antiferroelectric thin films were deposited on platinized silicon substrates using a sol-gel method. In the preparation of the lead-free BCT-BMT thin films, Bi(CH3COO)3 with 20% excess Bi, Ca(CH3COO)2 and Ba(CH3COO)2 were dissolved in glacial acetic at 80 celsius degree. Simultaneously, Mg(OC2CH5)2 with 20% excess Mg and Ti(OCH(CH3)2)4 were dissolved in a mixture of CH3OCH2-CH2OH and CH3COCH2COCH3. The Bi/Ca/Ba and Mg/Ti solutions were then mixed and stirred for 30 min at room temperature. The final concentration of the BCT–BMT precursor solution was 0.2 M. After aging of the precursor solution for 24 h, the BCT–BMT thin film was deposited on Pt(111)/TiOx/SiO2/Si(100) substrate that were rinsed with acetone and ethanol prior to the deposition. Each layer of BCT–BMT film was spin-coated at 4000 rpm for 30 s. To eliminate the formation of cracks, every wet film was first dried at 150 degree for 3 min and then pyrolyzed at 450 degree for another 3 min on a hotplate. After the deposition of 8 layers, the film was annealed in a chamber furnace at 700 degree for 30 min in air. The final thickness of the film was about 320 nm. In the preparation of PLZST thin films, several different types of bottom electrodes were prepared, including LaNiO3/Si(100), Pt(111)/TiOx/SiO2/Si(100), and LaNiO3/Pt(111)/TiOx/SiO2/Si(100) composite electrode. The PLZST thin films were prepared by layer-by-layer (A-type) and multiple layer (B-type) annealing modes. For the A-type mode, each layer of film was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 30 s. Every wet film was first dried at 150 °C for 3 min and then pyrolyzed at 450 °C for 3 min on a hotplate, and finally was annealed in a tube furnace at 700 °C for 3 min in air. The above process was repeated for 8 times. In the B-type mode, the coating, drying and pyrolyzing processes were repeated for 8 times first. Then the PLZST thin film was finally annealed at 700 °C for 30 min (rather than 3 min) to ensure full crystallization. High quality lead-free KBNNO thin films were also deposited on platinized silicon substrates by pulse laser deposition (PLD) using a KrF excimer laser (Lambda Physik COMPEX PRO 205 F, λ = 248 nm) as the ablation source. Prior to film deposition, the substrates were ultrasonically cleaned with acetone, alcohol, and deionized water consecutively and dried with high‐purity nitrogen gas. The vacuum chamber was pumped to 1 mPa and then high‐purity (99.999%) O2 was introduced into the chamber as the reactive gas. High‐quality KBNNO films were prepared at a substrate temperature of 700 degree under oxygen pressures of 4-6 Pa for 30 minutes with a laser energy of 350 mJ/pulse and a frequency of 5 Hz. 2. To optimize the film composition and deposition parameters for the best energy density and efficiency of the thin film capacitor. Several strategies were used to optimize the film composition and quality in order to maximize the energy density and efficiency of the film capacitors. (1) The composition of the films were fine-tuned around the morphotropic phase boundary of the solid solution, where the ferroelectric and antiferroelectric phases coexist. The ferroelectric phase renders the film a high saturation polarization and the antiferroelectric one keeps the remnant polarization to a minimum. Both contribute to a high energy density of the device. The molar ratio of the ferroelectric/antiferroelectric phases were optimized in order to have the maximum energy density. (2) A small amount of A-site doping on the ABO3 perovskite structure was adopted to break the long range ordering of the normal ferroelectric phase and to obtain the relaxor behavior, which results in a high efficiency of the capacitor. (3) The film deposition parameters were optimized to obtain high quality thin films, leading to a high breakdown field. Key factors that affect the thin film breakdown strength are the quality of the thin film/bottom electrode interface, the quality of the deposited thin films, and the orientation of the thin films, etc. (4) To reduce the film leakage current and to further enhance the electrical breakdown field, several different types of bottom electrodes were tried. They are LaNiO3/Si(100), Pt(111)/TiOx/SiO2/Si(100), and LaNiO3/Pt(111)/TiOx/SiO2/Si(100) composite electrode. 3. To develop a compactible folding process to stack the thin film capacitor array into a compact capacitor device which is able to store an appreciable amount of electrical energy for practical applications. Arrays of thin film capacitors were fabricated. Top electrodes were deposited. Electrical measurements were conducted on the array of thin film capacitors and bad ones were identified. Interconnections were deposited. A polymer—Parylene HT layer (2-4 microns) were firstly deposited and patterned to cover all capacitor array and interconnections. Releasing holes were etched at the gap regions between islands. Secondly, XeF2 dry-undercut etching was performed to get rid of underneath silicon device layer and release the thin film capacitor array. Thirdly, the released capacitor array was transferred onto a soft substrate and a punching mold was used to punch out non-working elements. Finally, the capacitor array was folded and stacked. To add more flexibility and sturdiness to the folding process, serpentine interconnections was used. However, the folding and stacking of the prototype capacitor arrays were performed manually, which resulted in low productivity and many damaged capacitors. Considering the practical application in energy storage, the thin film capacitors have several drawbacks. (1) Although the volumetric energy density is high, the total energy stored is still low due to the low overall volume of the thin films (usually in a thickness of a few hundred nanometers). (2) The productivity of folded capacitors is still quite low under the current technology. Hence we proceed to seek an alternate solution. A simple solution-casting method was developed to fabricate polymer nanocomposite with PLZST nanoparticles. First, P(VDF-HFP) pellets (Aldrich, MKCF7315) were dissolved in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF, 99.5%, Sinopharm) and stirred for 2 h to prepare a P(VDF-HFP) solution. Subsequently, PLZST nanoparticles coated with dopamine were added into the above solution and ultrasonically stirred for 3 h. After that, the PLZST/P(VDF-HFP) mixed solution was cast onto a clean quartz glass substrate to form nanocomposite films and dried at 60 degree for 12 h in vacuum to volatilize DMF. Finally, the films were heated at 210 degree for 10 min, and immediately quenched in ice-water. After vacuum drying, the composite films with a thickness of about 20 microns were stripped from the glass substrate. The film capacitors fabricated in this way can be easily folded and stacked. This process can also be adopted for mass production.

15266516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15266516.value: To find the optimized composition, we first investigated the energy-storage properties of PLZST AFE ceramics with high Sn content because the introduction of Sn can make the hysteresis loop slimmer. The results show that an optimized Sn content leads to the realization of both large recoverable energy storage density and high energy efficiency in a single material. With 46% of Sn, the PLZST AFE ceramic exhibits its maximum room-temperature energy storage properties with a recoverable energy density as large as 3.2 J/cm3 and an energy efficiency as high as 86.5%. In addition, its recoverable energy density varies only slightly (<10%) in the temperature range 20-120 °C (Appl.Phys.Lett. 113, 063902 (2018)). A large positive electrocaloric (EC) effect was realized in PLZST relaxor antiferroelectric thin films. The in-plane residual thermal tensile stress during the layer-by-layer annealing process and the high quality film structure deposited on the LaNiO3/Pt composite bottom electrode are responsible for the large EC effect. A large pyroelectric energy density (6.10 J/cm3) was also harvested by using an Olsen cycle (Nano Energy 47, 285 (2018)). The BCT–BMT lead-free relaxor ferroelectric thin films show an electric field induced structural phase transition (nanoscale tetragonal and orthorhombic to rhombohedral) along the out-of-plane [111] direction. Under optimum composition, a large energy density of 51.7 J/cm3 was achieved at room temperature (Energy & Environ. Sci. 12, 1708 (2019)). P(VDF-HFP) polymer nanocomposites with PLZST nanoparticle fillers show good energy storage properties. With a filler content of 5 wt.% PLZST nanoparticles, the polymer composites exhibit a high breakdown strength of 3.1 MV/cm, and a large discharge energy density of 9.4 J/cm3, with a high energy efficiency of 82% (J.Mater.Chem.A 7, 13473 (2019)). The polymer nanocomposite with 7 wt.% PLZST nanofillers exhibits much improved energy storage properties with an ultrahigh efficiency of 93.4% and a large discharge energy density of 12.5 J/cm3 (ACS Appl.Mater.Interfaces 12, 12847 (2020)). Finally, to better promote the development of lead-free dielectric capacitors with high energy storage density and efficiency, we comprehensively review the latest research progress on the application to energy storage of several representative lead-free dielectric materials, including ceramics (ferroelectrics, relaxor ferroelectrics, and antiferroelectrics), glass-ceramics, thin and thick films, and polymer-based composites. We also summarized some new strategies to improve the energy storage capacity of dielectric materials (Mater. Res. Bull. 113, 190 (2019)).

15266516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15266516.value: Parallel plate capacitors with ultrafast discharging power (much higher than those of batteries and electrochemical supercapacitors) are becoming increasingly important to a broad range of applications, especially in pulsed power circuit applications, such as hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), medical defibrillators, spacecraft, detonators, and electrical weapon systems. Traditional materials used in the parallel plate capacitor include linear dielectrics and nonlinear dielectrics (ferroelectrics and/or antiferroelectrics). While the nonlinear dielectrics are superior in energy density, most of them contain toxic element of lead. In this project, we propose to fabricate thin film capacitors using lead-free ferroelectric/antiferroelectric materials. Ultra-high energy density of the thin film capacitor can be achieved by proper materials design, composition selection, and processing optimization. For practical applications in mobile electric devices, a folding and stacking technique is developed to make thin film capacitor into a compact size. Moreover, a facile solution-casting process is developed to fabricate thick film capacitors, which can be easily rolled, folded, and stacked, attractive for practical energy storage applications.

15267116.label: Project Objectives
15267116.value: Develop multi-dimensional network-based measures for characterizing the redundancy of multi-modal transportation networks for both travelers and planners. Develop a systematic optimization-based approach to design optimal redundant strategies to minimize the vulnerability and maximize the resiliency of multi-modal transportation networks. Develop state-of-the-art solution algorithms for measuring and designing redundant transportation networks using recent advances in random utility models, path-based traffic assignment algorithms, and global optimization methods. Conduct case studies using the Hong Kong multi-modal transportation network for: (a) assessing the network redundancy performance of the current and planned networks, (b) assessing the network redundancy performance under various potential/hypothetical disruption scenarios, (c) identifying critical bridges/tunnels/links using the multi-dimensional redundancy metrics, (d) prioritizing bridges/tunnels/links for enhancing network redundancy, and (e) providing suggestions on strategic transportation network planning and design for enhancing network resiliency.

15267116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15267116.value: The magnitude of societal and economic impacts associated with recent natural and man-made disasters around the world has emphasized the importance of transportation systems. Transportation networks, as a critical lifeline in modern society, are vital to people’s health, safety, comfort, and economic activities. Disruptions to the transportation networks can damage regional and national economic competitiveness and make peoples’ lives difficult. Given that transportation networks are not only important in providing accessibility and promoting the safe and efficient movement of people and goods but also central to the functioning of modern society to support our daily activities and maintain relations in business, social, and family settings, it is important to understand and withstand their vulnerability to planned and unplanned disruptions. Redundancy is vital for transportation networks to provide alternate travel options to travelers and network spare capacity to planners to plan and manage the transportation system during planned and unplanned disruptions. Despite its importance, research in transportation network redundancy is limited due to lack of quantitative measures for characterizing transportation network redundancy from the perspectives of travelers and planners, and therefore often has been overlooked in the transportation science literature. The purpose of this research is to build on the existing limited redundancy research to fully develop an integrated transportation network redundancy analysis framework for measuring and designing redundant transportation networks to enhance the resiliency of multi-modal transportation networks. This integrated analysis framework with emphasis on multi-modal transportation networks entails modeling, evaluation, design, and implementation. The modeling aspect includes the development of multi-dimensional network-based measures for characterizing multi-modal transportation network redundancy from the demand side (travelers) and the supply side (planners); the evaluation aspect involves the assessment of multi-dimensional network-based redundancy measures on a multi-modal transportation network; the design aspect entails designing various network redundant strategies to minimize the vulnerability and maximize the resiliency of the transportation network; and finally the implementation aspect is crucial to making the framework described in this proposal operational and successful. Results of the proposed research will contribute to better understanding transportation network vulnerability, robustness, and resiliency through the important concept of network redundancy. In addition, the proposed theoretical framework has the potential to support long-term strategic planning and design of transportation systems that ensure the redundancy performance of the multi-modal transportation networks for large Asian cities, such as Hong Kong, with high usage of multi-modal public transit. 近年来，世界各地频发的自然和人为灾害，对社会经济产生了巨大的负面影响，更凸显了交通系统的重要性。交通网络作为现代社会的重要生命线，对人们的健康、安全及社会经济活动至关重要。失效的交通网络可降低地区和国家的经济竞争力，降低人们的生活质量。交通网络不仅在提供可达性和促进人及货物的安全便捷流通方面十分重要，在支撑人们的日常生活和保障商业、社会、家庭环境等现代社会运作方面也起到中枢作用。因此，迫切需要深入理解并提升交通网络应对灾害事件的脆弱性。 冗余性对交通网络主要起到两方面的作用：对出行者而言，具有可替代的出行选择；对规划者而言，在交通系统规划与管理中提供网络富余容量，从而应对计划或意外的失效。尽管冗余性十分重要，但由于缺乏从出行者和规划者角度的交通网络冗余性定量评价指标，因此关于交通网络冗余性的研究非常有限，在交通科学文献中经常被忽视。 本研究的目的是，在现有有限的关于冗余性研究的基础上，构建一体化的交通网络冗余性分析框架，对交通网络冗余性进行度量和设计，从而提高多模式交通网络的弹性。该一体化分析框架，针对多模式交通网络冗余性，主要包括建模、评估、设计和实施四个模块。在建模方面，主要包括多维度网络层面冗余性评价指标的构建，从需求方（出行者）和供给方（规划者）两个角度刻画多模式交通网络的冗余性；在评估方面，主要是多维度网络层面冗余性指标在多模式交通网络上的评估计算；在设计方面，设计不同的网络冗余策略，使得交通网络的脆弱性最小化和弹性最大化；最后，实施方面则对于确保本研究提出的分析框架的可行性及有效性至关重要。 通过交通网络冗余性这一重要概念，本研究的成果将有助于更好地理解交通网络脆弱性、鲁棒性和弹性。同时，所提出的理论分析框架能够支撑交通系统的长期规划和设计，从而提升亚洲大城市（如多模式公共交通利用率高的香港）多模式交通网络的冗余性。

15267116.label: Realisation of objectives
15267116.value: Objective 1 is to develop multi-dimensional network-based measures for characterizing the redundancy of multi-modal transportation networks. Specifically, the travel alternative diversity measure and the network spare capacity measure have been developed to address two fundamental questions in the pre-disaster transportation system evaluation planning: (1) “how many effective redundant alternatives are there for travelers in the normal or disrupted event?” and “how much redundant capacity does the network have?” These network-based redundancy measures have been published in Transportation Research Part B (see paper 1 provided in the interim report). In this final report, we continue working on objective 1 by considering vulnerability, reliability, and resiliency measures, which are closely related to the network-based redundancy measures developed in this research project. Paper 2 developed an optimization approach for deriving the upper and lower bounds of transportation network vulnerability under simultaneous disruptions of multiple links. A binary integer bi-level programming model was proposed. In this model, the upper-level subprogram maximizes or minimizes the remaining network throughput under a given number of disrupted links, and the lower-level subprogram checks the connectivity of each origin-destination pair under a network disruption scenario without path enumeration. Numerical examples showed that the vulnerability envelope can effectively consider all possible combinations without the need to perform a full network scan. This paper has been published in Transportation Research Part C. Paper 3 proposed a close-form and flexible approach for estimating the travel time percentile function of diverse travel time distributions based on the Cornish-Fisher expansion without the need to assume/fit a certain type. Compared to five widely-used probability distributions, the proposed method is sufficiently adaptable to estimating percentile function of diverse travel time distributions with lower estimation error. More importantly, the closed-form expression of the travel time percentile function would facilitate characterizing travel time reliability in large-scale network applications. This paper has been published in Transportation Research Part B. Paper 4 provides a summary of the transportation network performance measures under perturbations: reliability, vulnerability and resilience. These three measures are closed related to the network-based redundancy measures suggested in this research project. Numerical examples are conducted to assess these concepts under different perturbation scenarios. This paper has been published in Transportation Research Part E. Objective 2 is to develop optimal redundant strategies for designing transportation networks that minimize the impact of disruptions and/or maximize the resiliency against disruptions. A network design tool for maximizing route diversity in road networks has been developed. Its goal is to minimize the impact of disruptions using redundant design strategies to enhance resiliency against disruptions. Several conference papers have been presented at various international conferences reported in the interim report (e.g., C1 has been presented at the 22nd Hong Kong Society of Transportation Studies Conference: Transport and Society, December 9-11, 2017, Hong Kong, P.R. China; C2 has been presented at the 7th International Symposium on Transport Network Reliability (INSTR 2018), 17-19 January 2018, Sydney, Australia; C5 has been presented at the Eastern Asia Society for Transportation Studies (EASTS) Conference, 18-21 September 2017, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam). In this final report, we provide this new network design problem as a binary integer bi-level program (BLP), where the upper-level maximizes the total number of O-D pairs with alternative distinct routes subject to a budget constraint, and the lower-level determines the maximum number of distinct routes between each O-D pair under a given design scheme. The proposed BLP model is further reformulated as an equivalent single-level mixed integer linear program (MILP), by making use of the equivalent continuous relaxation and optimality conditions of the lower-level subprogram as well as linearization techniques for the complementarity conditions. The details are reported in Paper 7, which is currently under review in Transportation Research Part E. Objective 3 is to develop algorithms for evaluating and designing redundant transportation networks. The development of various algorithms was reported in papers 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 for the assessment of transportation network redundancy, reliability, vulnerability, and resiliency. In addition, two conference papers were presented (i.e., C6 has been presented at the 23rd Hong Kong Society of Transportation Studies Conference: Transportation Systems in the Connected Era, December 8-10, 2018, Hong Kong, P.R. China; and C7 has been presented at the 24th Hong Kong Society of Transportation Studies Conference: Transport and Smart Cities, December 14-16, 2019, Hong Kong, P.R. China). Paper 6 uses the Gomory-Hu tree method to develop two indices (i.e., connectivity vulnerability and capacity vulnerability) for assessing vulnerability of road networks. The advantage of the proposed method is that it can significantly reduce the computational efforts of the minimum cuts between all pairs of nodes, which enables easy cut capacity analysis of large-scale transportation networks. This paper is currently under review in Transportation Research Part B. Paper 8 develops a day-to-day dynamic vulnerability analysis, which explicitly considers two types of uncertainties (i.e., objective uncertainty due to travel time variability and subjective uncertainty due to travelers’ imperfect knowledge about the network state). This paper is currently under review in Transportation Research Part E. Objective 4 is to conduct case studies to demonstrate proof of concept. Three case studies have been conducted: the first one focuses on the road network, the second one uses the metro network, and the third one considers the freight network. The road network case study aims to assess the redundancy of the road network in terms of the two measures developed in objective 1 as well as other related measures under different disruption scenarios (see papers 1, 3, and 6). The metro network case study is to evaluate the route diversity of the metro network under disruptions. The metro network case study has been reported in two conference papers (i.e., C3 has been presented at the 22nd Hong Kong Society of Transportation Studies Conference: Transport and Society, December 9-11, 2017, Hong Kong, P.R. China; and C4 has been presented at the 6th International Symposium on Reliability Engineering and Risk Management (6ISRERM), 31 May-1 June 2018, Singapore) and paper 5, which has been published in the Journal of Transport Geography. This paper evaluates the route redundancy of the current Mass Transit Railway (MTR) network in Hong Kong and the 2021 MTR network with the new Shatin to Central Link (SCL) line. The freight network case study applies the network-based redundancy measures to the Utah’s bi-modal network for transporting coal. This case study is reported in paper 9, which is currently under review in Transportation Research Part A.

15267116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15267116.value: The major research outcomes of this research project are the development of two network-based redundancy measures, namely travel alternative diversity measure and the network spare capacity measure, for characterizing the redundancy of transportation networks, the development of solution algorithms for evaluating and designing redundant transportation networks, and several applications of the models and solution algorithms to different transportation networks, including road networks, metro networks, and freight networks. These research outcomes have been either published or currently under review: Paper 1: Transportation network redundancy: Complementary measures and computational methods. Transportation Research Part B 114, 68-85. Paper 2: An optimization approach for deriving upper and lower bounds of transportation network vulnerability under simultaneous disruptions of multiple links. Transportation Research Part C 94, 338-353. Paper 3: A closed-form estimation of travel time percentile function for characterizing travel time reliability. Transportation Research Part B 118, 228-247. Paper 4: Performance of transportation network under perturbations: Reliability, vulnerability, and resilience. Transportation Research Part E 133, 101809. Paper 5: Evaluating the value of new metro lines using route diversity measures: the case of Hong Kong’s Mass Transit Railway system. Journal of Transport Geography 91, 102945. Paper 6: A vulnerability analysis of cut-capacity structure and OD demand using the Gomory-Hu tree method. Transportation Research Part B (under review) Paper 7: Enhancing network resilience via adding redundancy to road networks. Transportation Research Part E. (under review) Paper 8: A new day-to-day dynamic network vulnerability analysis approach with weibit-based route adjustment process. Transportation Research Part E (under review) Paper 9: Analysis of freight transportation network redundancy: An application to Utah’s bi-modal network for transporting coal. Transportation Research Part A. (under review) The major findings are: (1) the network-based redundancy metrics provide a systematic and quantitative measure for characterizing transportation network redundancy from the demand side (travelers) and the supply side (planners); (2) redundancy is vital to transportation networks for providing alternate travel options to travelers and network spare capacity to planners to plan and manage the transportation system during planned and unplanned disruptions, and (3) results from various case studies provide a better understanding of transportation network reliability, vulnerability, and resiliency through the important concept of transportation network redundancy developed in this research project that can be used to support long-term strategic planning of transportation system.

15267116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15267116.value: Redundancy is one of the four Rs (i.e., Robustness, Redundancy, Resourcefulness, and Rapidity) in characterizing resiliency defined by Bruneau et al. (2003). This research developed quantitative network-based measures to measure the redundancy of transportation networks, solution algorithms for evaluating and designing redundant transportation networks, and case studies to demonstrate the measures and solution algorithms to different transportation networks, including road networks, metro networks, and freight networks. Results from this research project are encouraging and accepted in the international research communities. It would be interesting and worthwhile to further the research development to consider other dimensions of the four “Rs” concept, particularly on the robustness (or vulnerability) of transportation system, which is defined as the ability of the system to withstand a given level of stress without suffering degradation or loss of function. Another useful extension would be using the “4Rs” concept to develop a framework for the dynamic transportation network resilience assessment with an explicit consideration of the entire lifecycle of perturbations. These extensions will have broader impacts on improving the transportation network planning, design, and operations that can possibly help to create more robust and resilient transportation systems that are less disruptive to the society and people’s daily lives.

15267116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15267116.value: Redundancy is vital for transportation networks to provide alternate travel options to travelers and network spare capacity to planners to plan and manage the transportation system during planned and unplanned disruptions. Despite its importance, research in transportation network redundancy is limited due to lack of quantitative measures for characterizing transportation network redundancy from the perspectives of travelers and planners, and therefore often has been overlooked in the transportation science literature. This research project provided the first integrated transportation network redundancy analysis framework for measuring and designing transportation networks to enhance its resiliency. Specifically, this research provided systematic and quantitative measures to characterize the redundancy of transportation networks, developed implementable solution algorithms to evaluate transportation network redundancy, and conducted case studies on various transportation networks to show proof of concept. The results highlighted the importance of redundancy in long-term strategic planning and design of transportation systems to minimize the impacts of disruptions.

15267216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15267216.value: 多尺度影像地图的优化设计

15267216.label: Project Objectives
15267216.value: This project aims to carry out a systematic investigation into the optimum cartographic design of image-maps, i.e. optimum matching between image resolution and map scale, and optimum use of various cartographic variables.
rows: This project aims to carry out a systematic investigation into the optimum cartographic design of image-maps, i.e. optimum matching between image resolution and map scale, and optimum use of various cartographic variables.

15267216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15267216.value: 地圖已經在各行各業得到廣泛的應用。但地圖由於使用幾何符號對許多人來說顯得抽象。另一方面，衛星圖像看起來更逼真，但由於沒有地名、邊界等要素，也很難理解。影像地圖是這兩者的折衷。影像地圖用經過幾何校正的正射影像為背景，在其上選擇性加載地圖符號。谷歌地圖問世後影像圖已經成為流行。其結果是，這種產品的用戶需求越來越多。 現在很多人也批評這種地圖的質量差，就像上世紀80年代的由GIS-製作的地圖。這意味著需要深入研究最佳設計問題。該項目旨在通過對圖像分析於地圖設計加以集成，來解決其中的一些關鍵問題。 優化影像地圖意味著使影像地圖最有效。為了實現這一目標，需要從現有的地圖數據庫中將一些符號（例如地名，邊界，輪廓線和/或道路）上載到正射影像。但是，不同比例尺的地圖有著不同的細節。例如，在大比例尺地圖，可以看到街道的詳細信息，但在小比例尺地圖，人們只能獲得城市街區或城市的輪廓。可以想像，我們不能將城市街區信息上載到高分辨率（例如1M）的影像（它顯示街道信息），因為它們不匹配。所有第一個問題是：給定一幅正射影像確定最匹配的地圖比例尺。接下來的問題是應該上傳多少符號。這應該是依賴於背景的複雜性正射圖像本身。第三個問題是“如何通過考慮影像的複雜來設計有效的地圖符號。這些問題將在這個項目中得到解答。 該項目的成功完成將形成自動化生產影像地圖的一些指導原則。其結果使國家測繪機構（如國家測繪地理信息局和香港LIC）以及地理信息產業的相關的企業都能從中得利。

15267216.label: Realisation of objectives
15267216.value: The completion report of this project should be submitted by June 2020 because the project is to be completed by end of June 2019. The objective of this project is to develop techniques for optimum design of multi-scale image-maps. Two problems are tackled, i.e. to find the best matching between image resolution and map scale, and to design most effective cartographic symbols for image maps. In the latter task, it is most critical to take into proper consideration of the complexity of background images. With this GRF project, a full-time PhD student (PENG Qian) has been funded; one MSc student (LIU Xiaoxuan) are also partially supported and graduated, and one undergraduate (Miss CHOI Wing Kei) has supported for research training. Miss Peng registered in the PhD programme in Sept 2017 and her normal study period is by the August 2020. She is expected to submit her thesis in December 2020. That is, her study is still in progress but an abstract of her thesis is submitted with this report. To produce high quality image maps. A good match between the resolution of background image and the scale of the maps to be displayed on the image is essential. Traditionally, accuracy is the measure to indicate a good match. However, we found that the accuracy of images may be affected by many factors. For example, if registered with low-accuracy reference (control) points, the accuracy of image could be low although the resolution of the image is high and level of detail is also fine. Therefore, in this project, a complexity-based (indicator of LoD) method is developed to match between the image resolution and map scale. The matching is based on the complexity of line features (line networks and individuals) using, as indicators of complexity, length, density, area, and fractal dimension. Experimental evaluations are conducted in 15 areas (urban, rural, and mixed) using seven scales of vector maps and eight resolutions of images in Hong Kong. The complexity-based matching improves the matching by the analysis of indicators of LoD. It is concluded that the proposed complexity-based matching method improves the matching between image resolution and map scale. The study has been presented at the American Association of Geographers’ Annual Meeting 2019, Washington, DC. A paper has been submitted to the International Journal of Geographical Information Science (IF=3.545). As the most important issue is to proper consideration of the complexity of background images, we have reviewed the available measures for image complexity. Special attention was paid to the entropy which was coined by Shannon in 1948 and has been widely used in information science and many other areas such as bio-informatics and environmental informatics. A systematic evaluation on Shannon entropy, improved Shannon entropies and variants of Shannon entropy has been carried out. It has been found that none of entropies is capable of completely characterizing both the compositional and the configurational information of an image. This work has been published in “Entropy” (SCI IF=1.821). Consequently, we tried to answer the recent calls for re-visiting Boltzmann entropy which was proposed by Ludwig Boltzmann in 1872 as this entropy is capable of charactering both compositional and configurational information of images. However, no feasible computation solutions are available as it still remains largely at a conceptual level. The Boltzmann entropy was defined as a function of the number of possible microscopic states (i.e., microstates) for a given macroscopic state (i.e., macrostate) in a thermodynamic system. The difficulty in the computation of Boltzmann entropy for an image lies in the proper definition of macrostate and the precise determination of the number of microstates for the macrostate. To overcome this difficulty, a hierarchy-based (or multiscale) strategy was proposed in this project. Specifically, for a given image, the macrostate is defined as the up-scaled version, and the number of microstates is defined as all the possibility for the up-scaled image to be down-scaled to the original level (scale). In this way, Boltzmann entropy can be computed between images at any two adjacent scales in the hierarchical (multiscale) representation. This entropy is termed as “relative Boltzmann entropy” and there could be a number of relative entropies for a big image. To make the size of image matter, “absolute Boltzmann entropy” was introduced and it is equal to the sum of all the relative entropies. Experimental validation were carried out by using both simulated and real-life images. The results showed that the proposed computation method is effective. This has been published in “Landscape Ecology” (SCI IF=3.615). After the complexity measure is developed, next is to tackle the complexity-driven optimization of multi-scale image-map generation. The legibility of image-maps is influenced by the complexity of the background images and the complexity of the map symbols. Two studies are conducted in this part. (a) The legibility of image-maps with different image transparency is evaluated. Experimental data includes 12 areas in Hong Kong at the map scales of 1:20 000, 1:10 000, and 1:5 000 and corresponding image resolutions of 2m, 1m, and 0.5m. The legibility user test is to conduct questionnaires about the natural landscape features (Mountains/plain/water bodies, etc.) and man-made landscapes features (buildings/roads/parks, etc.) with the experimental data. “The right percent of the answers”, “the certainty of answers” and “the completion time” are recorded to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of the image-maps. With such data, the relationship between the different transparency level and the legibility of image-map can be established. Furthermore, the relationship between the complexity of the background image and the legibility of image-maps can be also be found. A paper studied on this topic is in preparation. (b) Another study is the point-label optimization based on the complexity of background images. As the background of image-map is much more complex than traditional maps, which makes the traditional labelling preference not effective anymore. In this project, automated labelling based on the complexity of the rectangular box is carried out and the results are evaluated via a questionnaire, in term of the “the ease level of finding the corresponding name labels” and “the satisfaction level”. In the next part, both the complexity of map symbols and background images are considered. Self-adaptive amount of map symbols to be uploaded considering the complexity of background image is explored. Ten levels of different percent of map symbols are uploaded to the series of images for experimental data preparation. The visual complexities of image and map, and the perceived complexity of the combination of image and map are considered. The visual complexities are evaluated by calculating the statistical information and structural information of vector maps and raster images. The perceived complexity of image-map is evaluated by the eye-tracking techniques. The percentage of fixation count distributed in the area around the target is used as a criterion for effectiveness; total searching time is used for efficiency evaluation; subjective scores from questions are used for satisfaction evaluation. The analysis of results is still on progress. We have also carried out an investigation into the effectiveness of cartographic symbols with highlighting and semi-transparency for image maps. Different kinds of designs have been made. Results how that Halo and other highlighting do make the perception more effective. The PI have been invited to deliver keynotes/invited paper at one international conferences and one national conferences.

A complexity-based match between image resolution and may scale has been developed. 15267216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15267216.value: Image map is a new type of map, with map symbols superimposed onto background images. To produce such a map, first of all, features at images should match the corresponding features on map so that they will fit each other. After matching, map symbols should be uploaded onto images. The readability of the map will be dependent on the complexity of background image. In this project, a complexity-based match between image resolution and map scale has been developed. Through experimental evaluation, it is found that when the complexity level (or level of detail) is taken into consideration, in addition to the traditional accuracy, much improvement in match quality can be made. A systematic study on the effect of the complexity of background image on map readability has been carried out. It is found that map readability can be improved and optimum design of image maps can be achieved at certain levels. It is also investigated that Boltzmann entropy is a good measure for the complexity of images and the vexing problem of computing the Boltzmann entropy of an image is solved in this project.
