15268716.label: Project Objectives
15268716.value: To quantify ductility of both S690 base plates and welded plates under large cyclic axial deformations. To quantify ductility of practical beam-column joints made of S690 welded sections under large cyclic bending deformations.
rows: To quantify ductility of both S690 base plates and welded plates under large cyclic axial deformations.
To quantify ductility of practical beam-column joints made of S690 welded sections under large cyclic bending deformations.

15268716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15268716.value: High strength steel materials are highly efficient constructional materials with large strength to self-weight ratios, and they offer attractive structural solutions to those heavily loaded structural members in building structures. However, one of the major hindrances to their wide application in building construction is the concern of limited deformation capacities of high strength steel materials and their joints as their elongation limits are somehow limited, when compared with normal strength steel materials. As heating-cooling cycles during welding of high strength steel plates in practice will produce adverse effects at different degrees on various mechanical properties of the welded joints, especially in the vicinity of heat affected zones, many structural engineers are yet to be convinced to adopt high strength steel materials in their design. In general, there is a lack of experimental evidence to establish sufficiency on ductility of these welded connections and joints, especially under large cyclic loadings. This project aims to investigate deformation characteristics of high strength S690 steel plates and welded connections under cyclic loadings. Welded steel plates are welded with two different amounts of heat input according to current welding practice. A total of 126 cyclic axial deformation tests will be carried out on Q690 base plates and welded plates in order to demonstrate their axial ductility under large cyclic loadings up to a maximum strain of 10% . A total of 20 full-scale beam-column joints with different geometrical configurations and material specifications in welded H-sections and Box-sections under cyclic lateral loads will also be tested. Among these tests, reduced beam sections with circular notches will be provided close to the ends of the beam sections of four of these joints in order to enhance joint ductility. These experiments will provide scientific evidence to demonstrate whether ductile connections and joints made of S690 steel materials may be readily achieved with good engineering design in connection details despite the ductility of the base materials are significantly smaller than 15%, which is generally accepted as the minimum elongation limits for structural members to be used in seismic resistant design. Hence, the experimental findings are very important to justify or reject the use of specific grades of high strength steel materials with different chemical compositions and heat treatments in those building structures which are prone to seismic attack.

15268716.label: Realisation of objectives
15268716.value: In order to establish ductility requirements for various steel materials to be qualified and accepted to be used in seismic resistant structures, a number of experimental investigation were carefully planned and executed. Pilot programme A pilot experimental investigation into structural behaviour of S690 steel coupons under both monotonic and cyclic actions was carried out as follows: i) 6 monotonic tensile tests on standardized cylindrical coupons were conducted; and ii) a total of 18 cyclic tests on funnel-shaped cylindrical coupons were also conducted under Loading Protocol V with varying strain amplitudes. The areas of interest include: a) mechanical properties of S690 steel materials, in particular, their ductility at large deformations under monotonic actions; and b) hysteretic behaviour of S690 steel materials at large deformations under cyclic actions of practical ranges of axial strains, loading frequencies, and straining rates; and Based on the findings of the test results, it is concluded that:  Despite a significant reduction in ductility with an increase in yield strengths, all the coupons of S690 steel plates were found to be able to satisfy the following ductility requirements stipulated in EN 1993-1-1 and -12: i) fu / fy ≥ 1.05, ii) εL ≥ 10%, and iii) εu ≥ 15 fy / E where fu is the tensile strength, fy is the yield strength, E is the Young’s modulus, εL is the elongation limit at fracture, and εu is the elongation corresponding to fu. • Hence, these S690-QT steels are readily qualified to be structural steels for construction according to EN 10025: Part 6, i.e. even for seismic resistant structures without any cyclic ductility requirements. • All the cyclic tests with a targeted strain εm at ±2.5%, ±5.0% and ±7.5% respectively have completed all the 20 loading cycles. For comparison, cyclic tests with a targeted strain εm at ±10.0% completed 19 cycles successfully, and fracture in these test coupons occurred during the 20th loading cycle. Test Programme I It was considered to be essential to extend the investigation into the hysteretic behaviour of the S355 steel plates under the same loading conditions so that an effective comparison between the S355 and the S690 steel plates is achieved. Hence, the following systematic research work was carried out as follows: i) 6 monotonic tensile tests on standardized cylindrical coupons were conducted; and ii) a total of 32 cyclic tests on funnel-shaped cylindrical coupons of both S355 and S690 steel plates were also conducted. The critical diameters of both types of coupons are 5.0 mm. The areas of interest include: a) cyclic deformation behaviour of S355 and S690 steel plates at large deformations under cyclic actions of practical ranges of axial strains, loading frequencies, and straining rates; and b) the numbers of cycles completed under i) Loading Protocol V with varying strain amplitudes, and ii) Loading Protocol C with constant strain amplitudes for both coupons of S355 and S690 steel plates. For both loading protocols, a total of four target strains are adopted, i.e. εm = ±2.5%, ±5.0%, ±7.5% and ±10.0% while the loading frequencies f are specified at 0.1 and 1.0 Hz. Based on the test results obtained from the tests, it is found that: i. Contrary to the general understandings on the ductility of both the S355 and the S690 steels, the cyclic deformation characteristics of both steels are demonstrated to be the same under Loading Protocol V with all the four target strains and the two loading frequencies ! ii. The cyclic deformation characteristics of the S690 steels are demonstrated to be inferior to that of the S355 steels under Loading Protocol C with target strain m at ±2.5% and f = 0.1 and 1.0 Hz. This agrees with the general understandings. iii. However, the cyclic deformation characteristics of the S690 steels are demonstrated to be superior to that of the S355 steels under Loading Protocol C with target strain m at ±5.0, ±7.5 and ±10%, and f = 0.1 and 1.0 Hz. This is contrary once again to the general understandings ! Test Programme II Another systematic research work was carried out to compare the hysteretic behaviour of the S690 steel plates and their welded sections as follows: i) 4 monotonic tensile tests on standardized cylindrical coupons were conducted; and ii) a total of 32 cyclic tests on funnel-shaped cylindrical coupons of both S690 steel plates and their welded sections were also conducted. For both loading protocols, a total of four target strains are adopted, i.e. εm = ±2.5%, ±5.0%, ±7.5% and ±10.0% while the loading frequencies f are specified at 0.1 and 1.0 Hz. It should be noted that the heat input energy adopted during welding of the steel plate is kept to be 1.0 kJ/mm through the use of robotic welding system. Based on the test results, it is found that: i) For cyclic tests under Loading Protocol C with εm = ±5.0 % and f = 0.1 Hz The S690 steel plates and the S690 welded sections are able to complete 16 and 8 cycles respectively while the engineering stress-strain curves of both the S690 steel plates and the S690 welded sections do not overlap one another well. Hence, there is a significant softening after a number of cycles completed. ii) For cyclic tests under Loading Protocol C with εm = ±10.0 % and f = 0.1 Hz The S690 steel plates and the S690 welded sections are able to complete only 6 and 1 cycles respectively, and there is a significant softening in the engineering stress-strain curves of both the S690 steel plates and the S690 welded sections. Similar results are found for the cyclic tests under both Loading Protocol V with similar εm and f. Consequently, the effects of welding in the S690 steel plates are shown as follows: a) Reductions in the mechanical properties of the S690 welded sections due to welding are significant when compared with the S690 steel plates. b) The S690 welded sections perform inferior to the S690 steel plates, and they are significantly less ductility under cyclic actions – they complete fewer cycles before fracture when compared with the steel plates. Hence, the proposed testing methods are demonstrated to be effective in quantifying mechanical responses of both the S690 steel plates and their welded sections under cyclic actions. Test programme III In order to examine structural behaviour of the S690 welded sections under cyclic loads in typical applications, such as moment joints, a test programme of a total of twelve T-joints of cold-formed circular hollow sections under both monotonic and cyclic actions was devised. It should be noted that these T-joints of cold-formed circular hollow sections were adopted because they were not susceptible to lateral torsional buckling. Their deformation characteristics under lateral monotonic and cyclic loads were measured. It should be noted that: a) All the T-joints were strong and stiff, and they were able to exhibit monotonic and cyclic deformation characteristics similar to those generally obtained from tests of the S355 steel sections. b) However, those T-joints of the S690 CFCHS were shown to be less ductile than those of the S355 CFCHS under lateral cyclic forces, and the numbers of cycles completed before fracture were found to be significantly smaller than those of the S355 CFCHS.

15268716.label: Major findings and research outcome
15268716.value: High strength steels are widely considered to be highly efficient constructional materials, and many structural engineers are very interested to apply these steels in construction. However, it is important to establish that (Ho et al., 2017) the high strength S690 steels deform with sufficient ductility similar to that of the normal strength S355 steels so that the current design methods are applicable to the S690 steels. This project aims to examine the deformation characteristics of the S690 steels under cyclic actions through carefully devised and executed experiments. Both monotonic and cyclic tests on standard coupons of both the S355 and the S690 steel plates and their welded sections have been carried out (Guo et al., 2019a; Guo et al., 2019b). According to the proposed testing methods (Ho et al., 2017) with specific ranges of target strains, loading application frequencies and loading protocols, it is found that • The S690 steels possess excellent engineering stress-strain curves under monotonic actions in terms of strength and stiffness. Their elongations at fracture are significantly smaller than those of the S355 steels (Guo et al., 2019a). However, after transforming into true stress-strain curves, the S690 steels exhibit a ductility similar to those of the S355 steels. • Under a widely adopted loading protocol for seismic effects, namely, Loading Protocol V with varying strain amplitudes, the S690 steels exhibit good cyclic deformation characteristic that are similar to those of the S355 steels (Guo et al., 2019b; Guo et al., 2020). • Under another widely adopted loading protocol for low cycle high strain cyclic effects, namely, Loading Protocol C with constant strain amplitudes, the S690 steels exhibit similar or even better cyclic deformation characteristics, when compared to those of the S355 steels, at specific target strains, i.e. 5 to 10% (Guo et al., 2020). This is contrary to the general understanding. • In order to examine ductility of welded sections, cyclic tests on both the coupons of the S690 welded sections and the joints between the S690 CFCHS are conducted, and they can only complete fewer cycles before failure (Ho et al., 2020; Hu & Chung, 2018), when compared with those of the S355 steels. Moreover, a scientific method is proposed in the project (Guo et al., 2020) to quantify cyclic deformation characteristics of both normal and high strength steels together with a number of criteria on both strength and ductility of these steels and their sections.

15268716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15268716.value: In this project, reductions to the mechanical properties of the S690 welded sections due to welding have been systematically quantified. While the effects of welding onto the mechanical properties of the S690 steels are shown to be less severe than general anticipated, it is necessary to examine the reasons of these reductions scientifically. References to the Materials Science and Metallurgy reveal that owing to the heating / cooling cycles imposed to the steel plates during welding, there is a change in the microstructures in the vicinity of the heat affected zones of the S690 steel plates. Consequently, it is proposed to collaborate with a materials scientist to work on microstructures of the S690 steels during welding. While the heat input energy during welding is carefully controlled through robotic welding systems, the temperature changes in the vicinity of the heat affected zones are carefully measured. Based on the continuous cooling transformation curves of the S690 steels, the overall distributions of different steel phases within the welded joints are established. The mechanical properties of the welded joints are then determined according to the basic mechanical properties of the steel phases.

15268716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15268716.value: High strength steels are widely considered to be highly efficient constructional materials, and many structural engineers are very interested to apply these steels in constructing highrise buildings and long span bridges. However, there is a general concern on their ductility, in particular, under cyclic actions. This project aims to examine the ductility of the S690 steels under cyclic actions through carefully experiments. Both monotonic and cyclic tests on standard coupons of both the S355 and the S690 steel plates and their welded sections have been carried out. According to the proposed testing methods in terms of specific ranges of target strains, loading application frequencies and loading protocols, it is found that the S690 steels possesses better cyclic deformation characteristics under cyclic actions of constant amplitudes with target strains, i.e. at large strains of ±5.0%, ±7.5% and ±10.0%, when compared with the S355 steels. This is different from the general understandings, and this opens a door for further investigation into the cyclic deformation characteristics of these S690 steels and their welded sections for possible applications in seismic resistant structures.

15269416.value: Identify the key “independent” design parameters to be optimized, the sources of uncertainties at the design stage, and the systems with reliability issues at the operation stage, for the energy systems of the representative ZEBs (grid-connected and standalone) in subtropical regions (Hong Kong and Southern China); Develop methods to quantify the uncertainties of design inputs and the reliabilities of energy systems, and integrate the quantification of uncertainty and reliability in the design optimization; Develop and validate effective models for building energy systems and components involved; Develop “dimension reduction” and “searching range limiting” methods to reduce the computation load and enhance the optimization efficiency; Develop the procedure and strategy to realize the robust optimal design of the ZEB building energy systems; Test the developed robust optimal design method on the representative ZEBs selected.

15269416.label: Realisation of objectives
15269416.value: A few innovative methods are developed for robust optimal design of standalone and grid-connected zero/low energy buildings, which are effective to practically achieve the zero/low energy goal under uncertainties after building occupancy. The methods provide the basis for developing Hong Kong as a zero carbon city and developing design optimization methods and technologies for low carbon districts/communities in subtropical regions. A multi-stage sensitivity analysis approach is developed to identify the key design parameters for design optimization of zero/low energy buildings. A holistic approach integrating sensitivity analysis and design optimization is developed for zero/low energy buildings. A new design optimization objective is developed, which considers annual energy consumption and winter thermal discomfort, for zero/low energy buildings without heating provision. Major uncertain design inputs, which have significant effects on performance of zero/low energy buildings in subtropical regions, are identified. A proper objective function for robust design optimization of zero/low energy buildings is developed by analyzing and comparing the applicability of the commonly-used objective functions. An artificial neural network model is developed for performance evaluation of zero/low energy buildings to reduce computational time. A coordinated optimal design method is developed as a computation cost-effective method for stand-alone and grid-connected zero/low energy buildings and their energy systems on the basis of multi-stage design optimization methods, to effectively consider the interactions between building envelope and energy system design optimizations. A coordinated robust optimal design method is developed to efficiently identify the global optimal design solutions for the entire zero/low energy buildings under uncertainties. 10 journal papers and few conference papers are published and one PhD student is trained.

15269516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15269516.value: Strong earthquakes are one of the most damaging natural disasters, resulting in widespread structural collapse and catastrophic economic and human losses. Methods to prevent such collapse in the face of earthquakes include direct simulation of the seismic collapse of building structures, with the results then used in seismic collapse assessment. However, the seismic collapse assessment of building structures remains fraught with significant uncertainties in structural collapse modeling and ground motion selection. The collapse mechanisms of bridge structures differ from those of building structures. Current assessments of the seismic performance of modern bridge structures typically rely on predictions of structural damage prior to collapse. Developing a better means of such assessment is important because many reinforced concrete (RC) bridge structures have collapsed in recent earthquakes, and many new and irregular RC bridge structures have been built in urban areas. Structural health monitoring (SHM) is a cutting-edge approach, with SHM systems recently installed in a number of important structures to monitor their safety. However, few studies address how the measurement data recorded by SHM systems can be utilized to reduce the uncertainties in seismic collapse simulation and allow evolutionary and accurate seismic collapse assessment. Most current SHM systems are designed on the basis of linear finite element analysis (FEA), which is unable to provide the necessary information for seismic collapse assessment. Thus, their current design needs to be revisited to permit such assessment. In view of these issues, the aim of the proposed research project is to develop a framework for the SHM-based collapse assessment of RC bridge structures under earthquake excitations. The project will involve five major tasks: (1) refinement of the currently used FEA-based seismic collapse simulation method to make it suitable for bridge structures; (2) development of an SHM system with multi-type sensors at optimal locations to improve the seismic collapse assessment of bridge structures; (3) development of linear and nonlinear model updating strategies to reduce collapse modeling uncertainties; (4) proposal of an SHM-based seismic collapse assessment method for bridge structures using recorded ground motion characteristics; and (5) performance of shaking table tests of a bridge model to validate the proposed seismic collapse simulation method. If successful, the project findings will advance scientific knowledge of how to solve this practical problem. 15269516.label: Realisation of objectives
15269516.value: Objective 1. This study explored two different ways to refine the currently-used finite element analysis-based seismic collapse simulation of RC structures. One way is to introduce a new strategy of degree-of-freedom (DOF) release to the beam element-based FE models and the other way is to introduce material-level element failure criteria to the shell/plate element-based FE models. For the beam element-based FE models, the refined method with the new strategy of DOF release can monitor and assess the progressive damage process of vulnerable DOFs of RC members. It can also consider the catenary effect for RC beams and the effect of axial forces on the flexure-shear failure modes of RC columns. With this refined method, the zero-length RC element removal is a natural consequence of the release of all DOFs of the element. The refined method has been implemented in an open source finite element code of OpenSees and applied to a RC beam, a RC column, a two-story RC frame structure, and a two-span continuous RC bridge. A high-fidelity FE model of a long-span cable-stayed bridge has been established by using the general-purpose FE software MSC.Marc. Different types of elements were used to model the structural components of the bridge based on their compatibility and feasibility in the collapse simulation. The collapse of the cable-stayed bridge was simulated by the removal of failed elements based on material-level element failure criteria. The removal of the failed elements was achieved by the elemental deactivation technique. The multi-layered shell element consisted of a number of layers representing concrete and reinforcement steel, respectively. The concrete layers were assumed to be isotropic while the reinforcement steel was modelled by orthotropic smeared rebar layers. At each increment of the time history analysis, the strain values at all integration points of a layer was checked against the predefined material failure criteria. If any of the strain values exceeded the criteria, the corresponding layer was deactivated. Hence, when one layer was deactivated, the external load on the element was resisted by the other layers. When all the layers of a shell element were deactivated, the element was considered as failure and removed from the FE model. If a node was isolated after its surrounding elements were deactivated, all degrees of freedom of the node were removed from the stiffness matrix. Objective 2. A cluster computing-aided FE model updating framework has been proposed for achieving an accurate and high-fidelity FE model of a long-span cable-stayed bridge using the software MSC.Marc, MATLAB and Python. The tasks of searching the global optimum of structural parameters were divided and distributed to the computing resources on the cluster by a job scheduler established in MATLAB. A parallel-computing methodology was developed to enable the program MSC.Marc and Python to receive the tasks and perform the simultaneous numerical simulations and data processing. The parallel-computing methodology also enabled MATLAB to collect the results from MSC.Marc and Python and update the structural parameters based on the objective functions. For linear updating, the structural modal properties were used as the indices in the objective function. The summation of the normalized errors between the simulated natural frequencies and the identified ones were used to construct the objective function. For nonlinear updating, a correlated-updating-parameter-based nonlinear FE model updating algorithm has been proposed. The seismic damage to the bridge was reflected by updating the nonlinear material parameters. The relationship between the degraded stiffness and strength was based on a concrete hysteric model. The simulated and measured displacement response time histories were used as damage indices to form the objective function. The difference between the simulated and measured response time histories was quantified by one minus the absolute value of the correlation coefficient of the two time histories. Parametric studies were conducted to determine a proper objective limit for the objective function. The measurement data from both linear and nonlinear test cases of the shake table test were used to update the FE model of the scaled Sutong bridge. A good agreement was observed between the simulated response time histories of the updated FE models and the measured response time histories for the scaled bridge under small, moderate and strong ground motions. Objective 3. A digital twin-based collapse fragility assessment method has been developed for long-span cable-stayed bridges under strong earthquakes. Three FE models of the scaled Sutong cable stayed bridge, including a design document-based FE model (Model-O), a linearly updated FE model (Model-L), and a nonlinearly updated FE model (Model-NL), were established to demonstrate the necessity of the digital twin-based assessment. Incremental dynamic analyses (IDAs) were conducted to calculate the collapse fragility curves of the FE models. A total of 30 ground motion records were selected according to the design seismic response spectrum of the prototype bridge. Four types of intensity measure (IM) were selected in the collapse fragility analyses of the three FE models, which included peak ground acceleration (PGA), peak ground velocity (PGV), Sa(T1) and Sa(T2), in which Sa(T1) and Sa(T2) were the 5%-damped spectral accelerations corresponding to the first transverse vibration period of the girder and the main tower, respectively. The collapse fragility assessment results of the three different models were compared in terms of collapse damage locations, collapse ground motion intensities and collapse probabilities. The results were also compared with the experimental observations on the physical bridge from the shake table test. The results show that the digital twin Model-NL can provide the closest prediction of the collapse ground motion intensity and collapse probability of the bridge, compared with the design document-based Model-O and the linearly updated Model-L. Moreover, Model-NL can provide a consistent and accurate prediction of the collapse mode of the bridge under earthquake excitation. Objective 4. This study conducted shaking table tests of the two different types of cable-stayed bridges. One is a short-span pedestrian cable-stayed bridge and the other is the long-span Sutong cable-stayed bridge. The shaking table tests of a 1:12 scaled RC pedestrian cable-stayed bridge were conducted at the Structural Dynamics Laboratory of The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The design, construction, and installation of the bridge for shake table tests were first carried out. Dynamic characteristic tests of the bridge were then performed. The progressive collapse of the bridge was finally recorded and analyzed in terms of recorded seismic responses, from which failure-vulnerable components of the bridge under different levels of ground motion were found and their seismic-resistant capacities were assessed. The shake table test results of the scaled Sutong cable-stayed bridge was used to validate the feasibility of the proposed FE model updating method, collapse simulation method and the SHM-based seismic collapse assessment method. The shake table tests was conducted at Tongji University. A geometric scale factor of 1/35 was adopted. After scaling, the total length of the cable-stayed bridge was reduced to 59.66 m and the height of the main tower was 8.58 m. A series of shake table load cases were carried out. The ground motions were input along the transverse direction of the scaled bridge. The bridge was constrained in the transverse direction. The ground motions were input chronologically from test cases E1–E15 with increased peak ground accelerations (PGAs) to study the damage progression of the bridge. The measurement data were used for the validation of the proposed methods .

15269516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15269516.value: (1) The currently-used finite element analysis (FEA)-based dynamic collapse simulation for RC structures has been refined by introducing a strategy of degree-of-freedom (DOF) release. With the new strategy, a RC beam-column element removal is a natural consequence of release of all DOFs of the element. (Xu, et al., 2018). (2) A cluster computing-aided linear FE model updating methodology has been proposed for updating the FE model of large and complex structures. The model updating process of the FE model of a bridge could be finished in 1.82 hours, which accelerates approximately 111 times compared to a conventional serial solution in an individual computer. (Lin et al. 2020a). (3) A fiber frame element-based nonlinear model and a nonlinear model updating method have been developed for a RC pedestrian cable-stayed bridge. The fiber frame element-based nonlinear model is established in OpenSees, accounting for both material and geometric nonlinearities. The new updating method can evaluate not only time-dependent strength degradation but also time-dependent stiffness deterioration so that the current damage state of the bridge can be identified and the future seismic performance and damage state can be predicted. (Zheng et al. 2019) (4) A time history analysis-based nonlinear FE model updating method has been proposed and applied to the scaled Sutong cable-stayed bridge. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses are conducted to quantify the influences of different updating parameters. Three test cases, involving both slight and strong nonlinearities of the bridge, are selected to assess the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed method and the results are very promising (Lin et al. 2020c) (5) A nonlinear FE model updating-based collapse prognosis method has been proposed for long-span cable-stayed bridges. The predicted collapse mechanism and structural responses are compared to the experimental results. The comparative results show that the proposed method is a feasible and accurate tool that can be used in the design optimization and maintenance of long-span bridges. (Lin et al. 2020b). (6) A digital twin-based collapse assessment method has been proposed for long-span cable-stayed bridges under strong earthquakes. The assessment results are compared with the test results in terms of collapse mechanisms, collapse ground motion intensities, and collapse probabilities. It is found that the proposed method is feasible and accurate for seismic collapse assessment of long-span cable-stayed bridges. (Lin et al. 2020d) (7) An experimental investigation has been carried out on the progressive collapse of a 1:12 scaled RC pedestrian cable-stayed bridge through a series of shake table tests. The design, construction, and installation of the bridge for shake table tests were first carried out. Dynamic characteristic tests of the bridge were then performed. The progressive collapse of the bridge was finally recorded and analyzed in terms of recorded seismic responses, from which failure-vulnerable components of the bridge under different levels of ground motion were found and their seismic-resistant capacities were assessed.(Zheng et al. 2019) A total of 7 peer-reviewed papers have been published in the top international journals. Additionally, PI has been invited to present the research results at the 2019 International Conference on Engineering Innovation and Seismic Mitigation of Bridges (ICEISMB 2019), December 20-22, 2019, Hangzhou, China.

15269516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15269516.value: The FE model updating methodology has been developed to update both linear and nonlinear FE models of a long-span cable-stayed bridge. The updated models have been successfully used in the collapse prognosis and fragility assessment of the bridge under strong earthquakes. The comparative results are validated by the shake table test with a good agreement. To fully consider the complex environment of the bridge site, further investigations are required to explore how to deal with the extensive SHM data and the FE modelling of a real long-span cable-stayed bridge under multiple hazards.

15269516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15269516.value: Long-span cable-stayed bridges have been widely constructed around the world, and some of them are built in earthquake-prone regions. The seismic performance assessment of these bridges thus becomes an important issue to the engineering community. This study thus focuses on developing high-fidelity FE models that can closely reflect the service state of real long-span RC bridges. This study first proposes a cluster computing-aided FE model updating methodology for the efficient and accurate linear and nonlinear updating of complex FE models for a long-span cable-stayed bridge. Shake table tests of the bridge are conducted to provide extensive SHM data for the model updating and validation. Comprehensive works are carried out to propose proper objective functions, select representative updating parameters, compare updating algorithms and conduct model validations. The updated model-based collapse prognosis and fragility assessment are conducted to evaluate the seismic performance of the bridge under strong earthquakes. The outcome of this study provides a feasible and accurate tool for nonlinear FE model updating, the subsequent collapse prognosis and the performance assessment of long-span bridges, which can be used in the design optimization and the operation maintenance of the structures.

15270316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15270316.value: 程序修复是改正程序中缺陷的过程。人工进行修复是一项繁琐且非常耗时的工作：程序员花费约25%的时间在修复缺陷上[5]；因为人们报告缺陷的速度超过程序员修复缺陷的速度，即使是广为使用的软件在发布时通常也包含已知但未修复的缺陷。人工修复的代价也是巨大的：如果将上述百分比映射到雇佣程序员的总体成本上，全球修复相关的开销约为年均1,560亿美金[5]。 自动程序修复技术针对程序缺陷自动给出修复建议，从而有助于帮助程序员改善软件正确性及降低修复成本。近年来，自动程序修复领域的研究进展显著，其中一类被称作“生成-验证”的技术在修复真实程序中的简单缺陷时获得了高成功率。生成-验证技术通常基于模板产生备选修复并通过测试来验证各个备选修复的正确性。 然而，为了让生成-验证技术能处理更为复杂的缺陷，我们仍然需要做大量的工作。现实世界中绝大部分的软件缺陷所需的修复代码更复杂（比如，我们可能需要修改多于一条语句），而通过在生成-验证技术中使用多个模板来试图修复这类缺陷是不可行的：多个模板所对应的不同的实例数目随着模板规模的增大而指数级增长；以现有技术的效率，要产生并验证如此大量的备选修复会需要大量时间。 本项目试图开发新技术来高效地产生复合修复。一方面，我们会尝试将一个大的修复任务分解为几个更小规模的修复任务，以此来避免或者缓和备选修复数目指数增长的情况。另一方面，我们会从过去正确的人工修复中学习正确修复代码通常具有的特性，并以此为依据先选择那些更可能正确的备选修复进行验证。 项目中开发的新技术和方法将显著提高自动程序修复的效率，并使得自动程序修复能处理复杂的缺陷。项目的工作也将有助于探索自动程序修复未来的发展方向。 本项目的成果能够帮助香港的ICT行业改善其软件产品的正确性并降低软件维护的开销，其与香港的经济与社会高度相关。

15270316.label: Realisation of objectives
15270316.value: 1. To substantially speed up the automated repair of single-action faults, compared with existing techniques; We have developed multiple novel techniques to enhance both the effectiveness and efficiency of automated repair of single-action faults. I) A correct fix not only has to be applied at the right location but also needs to manipulate the right variables/objects. However, fault localization (FL) in most existing APR techniques only tries to identify program lines that may be faulty, while leaving the decision regarding which objects/variables are implicated with the faults completely up to the fix generation process. In view of that, we proposed the JAID technique that employs program state abstraction based on a rich set of predicates to locate program states as likely fault causes. FL in JAID, therefore, locates not only the likely faulty locations but also the variables/objects that are more likely to be implicated with the faults. For each suspicious program state, JAID then generates candidate fixes to modify the program code to execute or the control flow to follow in that state. In the end, candidate fixes are compiled in batches and validated individually. Only fixes that can successfully pass all the input tests are reported to users as valid repair suggestions. We conducted extensive experiments using 693 faults from three widely used benchmarks of Java bugs to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of JAID. The evaluation showed, among other things, that: 1) JAID is effective: it produced correct fixes for over 15% of all bugs, with a precision of nearly 60%; 2) JAID is reasonably efficient: on average, it took less than 30 minutes to output a correct fix; 3) JAID is competitive with the state of the art, as it fixed more bugs than any other technique, and 11 bugs that no other tool can fix; 4) JAID is robust: its heuristics are complementary and their effectiveness does not depend on the fine-tuning of parameters. II) Fault localization is a crucial step of automated program repair because accurately identifying program locations that are most closely implicated with a fault greatly affects the effectiveness of the patching process. An ideal fault localization technique would provide precise information, while requiring moderate computational resources, to best support an efficient search for correct fixes. In contrast, most automated program repair tools use standard fault localization techniques—which are not tightly integrated with the overall program repair process and hence deliver only subpar efficiency. Therefore, we proposed retrospective fault localization: a novel fault localization technique geared to the requirements of automated program repair. A key idea of retrospective fault localization is to reuse the outcome of failed patch validation to support mutation-based dynamic analysis—providing accurate fault localization information without incurring onerous computational costs. We implemented retrospective fault localization in a tool called RESTORE——based on the JAID Java program repair system. Experiments involving faults from the DEFECTS4J standard benchmark indicate that retrospective fault localization can boost automated program repair: RESTORE efficiently explores a large fix space, delivering state-of-the-art effectiveness (41 DEFECTS4J bugs correctly fixed, 8 of which no other automated repair tool for Java can fix) while simultaneously boosting performance (speedup over 3 compared to JAID). Retrospective fault localization is applicable to any automated program repair techniques that rely on fault localization and dynamic validation of patches. 2. To enable automated repair of a significant portion of 2-action faults within a single routine, which are beyond the fixing power of existing techniques. With more accurate fault localization results produced by RESTORE, we stand a better chance of repairing faults demanding more complex fix actions. We propose the PRIDE approach to automated program repair, which builds on top of RESTORE and utilizes the information collected from fix validation to also better guide the selection of ingredients in generating candidate fixes. We implemented the PRIDE technique into a program repair tool with the same name. In a primitive experimental evaluation on 693 real-world Java bugs from 3 popular benchmarks, PRIDE was able to build correct fixes for more faults than all the other state-of-the-art generate-and-validate program repair tools; Compared with RESTORE, PRIDE reduced the time to the first correct fix by over 50% on most bugs that both tools can correctly fix; A significant number of the bugs correctly repaired by PRIDE have programmer-written fixes that change multiple lines. One major reason for PRIDE's not being able to propose high-quality complex fixes to even more multi-action faults is that, so far we have studied the relation between each fix action and its context code, but we know very little about how the multiple actions involved in individual fixes are related to each other. Knowledge about that relationship could help us quickly prune out complex fixes that are less likely useful. Next, on the one hand, we plan to investigate the correlation between ingredients used in multiple changes of the fixes from the past and use the learned knowledge to better prioritize the candidate multi-action fixes. On the other hand, we will also study how we can lift the current restrictions on fix structures to include more multi-action correct fixes in the fix space explored during program repair.

15270316.label: Major findings and research outcome
15270316.value: We have three major findings. First, semantic information about program executions (extracted by abstracting and contrasting program states) can significantly help locate the faults and generate more promising candidate fixes [9-3, 8-2]. Second, techniques for various tasks in automated program repair should be integrated rather than isolated. Streamlining those techniques can significantly improve the effectiveness and efficiency of not only individual steps but also the overall process [8-1]. Third, the relationship among multiple actions in individual fixes is important for quickly pruning the candidate fixes that are less likely to be correct. The most important outcomes of the research include i) the techniques, namely JAID, RESTORE, and PRIDE, that we developed to advance search-based automated program repair, ii) the tools that we implemented to support the easy application of those techniques, and iii) the experimental evaluations we conducted to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of those techniques and tools. Meanwhile, our work in this project has led to the publication of 6 conference papers (2 at top conferences) and 5 journal papers (all in prestigious journals); The Ph.D. student supported by this project has fulfilled all the related requirements and was awarded a Ph.D. degree in 2021.

The current design of the two tools is still rather primitive and has its limitations. For example, one particular limitation is that both tools only support the generation of candidate fixes with restricted structures. In the future, we plan to investigate how to lift the restrictions on fix structures and produce correct fixes for more bugs. Other things that are interesting to investigate include, e.g., how the actions contained in individual fixes are related to each other and how the knowledge about such relationship could be utilized to facilitate the generation of multi-action fixes more effectively and efficiently.

15270316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15270316.value: Automated program repair (APR) aspires to automatically propose high-quality fixes to program faults. In this project, we studied how to speed up automated program repair and advance the techniques to enable the repair of multi-action faults. We found that semantic information about the programs, the true integration of fault localization, fix generation, and fix validation, and the relationship between actions in individual fixes are key to the effectiveness and efficiency of automated program repair. We developed a series of APR techniques and tools that can correctly fix more bugs than other tools of the same time and achieve substantial speed-up. Our work has been published at venues including top-tier software engineering conferences and prestigious journals; All the tools we developed are publicly available for download.

15270716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15270716.value: This proposed project aims to develop a novel water and phase-change-materials (PCM) based nano-emulsion for active thermal energy storage (TES) applications, which are expected to help reduce the energy consumption of hot-water and air-conditioning systems. PCMs in the form of PCM emulsions and microencapsulated PCM (MPCM) slurries have advantages as heat transfer fluids and as thermal energy storage media in TES systems, involving the great energy storage densities in a small temperature range and the fast charging rates from the enlarged interface area. However, it is difficult to maintain a stable homogeneous flow if the PCM droplets or the particle capsules are not small and uniform in size, which limits their applications. The nano-emulsion, which is an emulsion with the droplets ranging 20 to 500 nm, can exhibit an extremely high kinetic stability and a sufficiently low viscosity as a pump-able energy storage media. In particular, with the specific ingredient formulation, the emulsification of a nano-emulsion can be almost spontaneous by changing the surrounding temperature, which enables the destroyed emulsion to be re-emulsified easily. Taking the advantages of these characteristics, a TES system using the nano-emulsion as the novel functional fluid will be built-up and tested, including the stratified storage tank, charging/discharging units and the functional unit for the re-emulsification of the PCM/water nano-emulsion. The novel device will have the following new features: a) the thermal fluid is stored in a tank that a vertical temperature stratification; b) the nano-fluid will be circulated directly in the pipes and the chiller contributed by its low viscosity and high stability so that a highest theoretical thermal charging rate can be achieved; and c) with the re-emulsification of the PCM nano-emulsion built into a thermal storage system, the performance life can be extended for more cost-effective practical applications. This proposed project will be achieved through multi-disciplinary research collaboration, involving physicochemical research, heat transfer investigation and optimization design. The PCM/water nano-emulsion will be designed, prepared and optimized to obtain the optimal formula and the suitable emulsification pathway. Its performing parameters will undergo detailed investigation and the optimization analysis. The new energy storage media and TES design to be developed is expected to offer good life-cycle carbon reduction performances in building cooling applications. 本專案致力於開發壹種新型相變材料（PCM）納米水乳液，以期通過其於主動熱能存儲裝置（TES）中的應用，滿足樓宇熱環境需求，顯著減低空調系統的能源消耗。 以相變乳狀液和微膠囊漿液為代表的相變功能熱流體利用材料的潛熱儲能，利用儲能側與用戶側間的小溫差儲存足夠冷量，同時極大縮短蓄能所需時間。且與傳統固液相變材料相比，改善了相變儲能過程中的流動性、導熱性及體積變化等問題。然而，常規相變水乳液和微膠囊材料的使用壽命或穩定性較差。依據我們已完成的RGC GRF項目成果，降低乳液液滴粒徑分佈是提高相變乳液穩定性的一種有效手段。納米乳液是指分散液滴粒徑介於20-500nm範圍的乳狀液，擁有接近於水的流動性並具有較高的穩定性，是一種理想的可泵送流體。特別地，如果納米乳液性狀發生改變，在適當配方和條件下，可以通過簡單的溫度循環過程恢復其初始狀態，即納米乳液極易再生。為了充分利用相變納米乳液的優勢，使用納米乳劑作為新型功能流體的TES裝置應包括分層儲罐、充/放單元和再生功能單元。亦具有以下特徵：a）相變儲熱流體儲存在分層儲罐亦存在垂直溫度梯度; b）利用其優異的流動性和穩定性，該納米流體將在TES系統管道內直接循環和熱交換，極大提高充/放效率;和c）在儲能系統中配置乳液再生功能裝置，以延長儲能介質的使用壽命和增進經濟效益。 本專案擬通過多學科的交叉研究完成，包括物理化學實驗，評價傳熱和熱力學參數及優化系統設計。擬設計和製備新型相變材料（PCM）納米水乳液，並評價其性能參數和優化其配方及製備工藝。以期這種新型儲熱介質和TES設計能夠顯著減低由滿足樓宇熱環境需求而帶來的碳排放。

Two low-energy emulsification methods, phase inversion temperature (PIT) and emulsion inversion point (EIP), were applied to prepare the nano-emulsions. Their thermal properties for thermal energy storage applications were examined.

15270716.label: Major findings and research outcome
15270716.value: Use of suitable emulsifiers is effective to generate stable nano-emulsions. However, high supercooling degree has been observed in the PCM nano-emulsions. The addition of nanoparticles such as SiO2 as nucleating agents reduced the supercooling moderately but not completely. In conclusion, the following three approaches are effective for improving the stability of the PCM emulsion, (1) using mixed emulsifiers; (2) reducing the droplet size and distribution, and (3) maintaining a suitable viscosity.

15270716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15270716.value: Phase change material (PCM) emulsions are useful media for fluid-state thermal energy storage systems. However, PCM emulsions are thermodynamically unstable owning to their high surface free energy. Reduction of the droplet size to the nanoscale, i.e. the formation of PCM nano-emulsions, is an effective approach for attaining highly stable PCM emulsions. Through this project, we have attained novle and highly stable PCM nano-emulsions with favorable fluid and thermal properties for thermal energy storage through manilulation and optimization of the major factors. The following areas are recommeded for further research and development: (1) Systematic assessment and optimization of the emulsifiers, conditions and methods for attaining robust and reusable PCM nanoemulsions. (2) Effective measures for the control and reduction of supercooling, scuh as special nanoparticles with modified interfacial properties as the nucleating agents. (3) Evaulation of the performance and effectiveness of PCM nanoemulsions in pilot and large-scale thermal energy storage systems. (4) Exploring wdier applications of PCM emulsions, e.g. for solar energy storage and in food and pharmaceutical industry.

15270716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15270716.value: Global warming is currently recognized as a serious disaster and threat to human life on earth. A major cause for global warming is attributed to the rapid consumption of carbon energy generated by burning fossil fuels. It is imperative to develop and apply effective measures for conservation and efficient utilization of energy. Thermal energy storage is one of the most important means for conservation and utilization of excessive and renewable energy. Phase change materials (PCMs) are indispensable media for latent heath storage. PCM nano-emulsions are dispersions of nano-sized PCM droplets in water. Through our extensive studies in this project, we have made novel and highly stable PCM nano-emulsions, overcoming some of the major technical problems with the previously existing materials. They have several advantages over the conventional energy storage media for thermal energy storage in fluid systems. As fluid materials, the nano-PCM emulsions can achieve more efficient heat transfer between the PCM droplets and the surrounding fluid because of the smaller size and larger specific surface area. They can be reused for many heating-cooling cycles, retaining a much longer service life than other thermal storage materials. The PCM nano-emulsions can be applied to solar energy storage and cooling energy storage for building air-conditioning.

15273616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15273616.value: Hong Kong, as an international financial, trading and logistics hub, is facing ever-growing demand for data center facilities, big data analytics and e-commerce services. Therefore, it is critical to key-value (KV) stores as they are one of the most important building blocks in modern web infrastructures and high-performance data-intensive applications, for instance, serving as web object cache and large-scale distributed NoSQL databases. Grand challenges are posted for KV stores to provide fast, predictable KV access latency. This project aims to solve this problem. There are two major obstacles. Conventional memory and storage techniques are the first one. The performance of KV stores is closely related to the memory pool size. However, the memory pool size cannot be easily increased by packing more RAM into servers due to RAM’s high cost, poor scalability and power/thermal/size constraints. While solid state drive (SSD) with lower cost and bigger capacity can alleviate this issue, it introduces garbage collection for reclaiming free space, and garbage collection causes unpredictable performance degradation. Second, more and more KV-supported applications are running in public cloud such as Netflix’s online movies/TVs and SoundCloud’s online audio. In public cloud, workloads are highly fluctuating, since any user/tenant can submit jobs at any time, thereby introducing unexpected workload surges. KV access latencies will be dramatically influenced by fluctuating workload surges. Emerging memory and storage techniques such as software-defined flash (SDF), Non-Volatile Memory (NVM), and intelligent storage resource management techniques in public cloud provide promising opportunities to overcome these obstacles. However, to fully unleash these opportunities, we need to bridge semantic gaps between KV stores and these techniques. In this research, based on a holistic approach, we aim to develop novel techniques to bridge three semantic gaps, namely, (1) the gap between garbage collection in KV stores and SSD low-level hardware operations in SSD-assisted KV caching systems; (2) the gap between KV stores and complex, less predictable runtime scenarios in public cloud; (3) the gap between organization/management of KV stores and characteristics of NVM. The ultimate goal of this project is to enable KV storage systems to provide faster, more predictable KV access latencies with more than 50% improvement in both the average and worst cases. This project is particularly important for Hong Kong, as key-value-based web caching, distributed NoSQL databases and public cloud play an essential role in supporting international business, trade and finance. 作為國際金融、貿易和物流樞紐，香港對數據中心、大數據分析和電子商務服務的需求一直在增長。Key-Value(KV)存儲是當今Web架構和高性能大數據應用中的一個關鍵技術，例如可以提供有效的web對象緩存及作為大規模分布式NoSQL數據庫，因此研究高效的KV存儲技術極為重要。其中，如何提供快速、可預測的KV訪問是KV存儲中的難點之一。本項目著眼於解決這個問題。 主要有兩個挑戰。其一是由傳統內存及存儲技術所引起的。KV存儲的性能與內存池的大小緊密相關。由於RAM的高成本，低擴展性，及功耗、散熱和尺寸的限制，我們不能放入更多RAM內存條來有效地擴大服務器的內存池。雖然低成本和大容量的固態硬盤(SDD)有助於緩解這個問題，但SDD需要進行垃圾回收操作，這會導致不可預期的性能下降。其二，越來越多的由KV存儲支撐的應用是運行在公有雲之上的，例如Netflix公司的在線電影電視及SoundCloud的在線音頻。在公有雲上，任何用戶或租戶都可以隨時提交作業，因此工作負荷會激烈波動，從而對KV訪問延遲造成極大影響。 軟件定義閃存(SDF)、非易失內存(NVM)和智能存儲資源管理等新興的內存及存儲技術，為解決以上挑戰提供了機會。然而，要充分發揮它們的優勢，需要縮小KV存儲和這些技術之間的語義鴻溝。在本研究中，我們致力於研究新技術，用於縮小以下三方面的語義差距：（1）在SSD輔助的KV緩存系統中，KV存儲的垃圾回收與SSD底層硬件操作之間的語義差距；（2）在公有雲上，KV存儲與復雜且不可預測的運行場景之間的語義差距；（3）KV存儲的組織管理與NVM的特性之間的語義差距。本項目的最終目標是使得KV存儲系統可以提供更快速、更加可預測的KV訪問延遲；具體而言，在平均和最壞情況下都得到50%以上的改進。 基於KV存儲的Web緩存、分布式NoSQL數據庫和公有雲在支撐國際商業、貿易和金融等方面起到舉足輕重的作用，因此，本項目對香港有著特別重要的意義。

15273616.label: Realisation of objectives
15273616.value: The project has been going very well, and all objectives have been 100% achieved. With the support of this fund, one PhD student (SHEN, Zhaoyan) at HK PolyU was recruited and passed his defense in August 2018; another PhD student (GUO, Yang) at CUHK, partially supported by this grant, was enrolled in August 2019 and is expected to graduated in July 2023. One undergraduate student, Siqi SHANG, at CUHK, was recruited to conduct undergraduate research and will graduate in July 2021. In total, 4 journal papers and 4 conferences have been published. Note that PI moved to CUHK from PolyU in August 2018; as such, based on the official financial statements prepared by the Finance Offices of PolyU/CUHK, the institution amount in the completion report is $0 while it is $106,521 in the mid-term report (provided by PolyU and not transferred to CUHK). Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 1, we have proposed a novel flash-based key-value caching technique, called DIDACache [C1, J2]. In DIDACache, we advocate to reconsider the key-value cache system design and directly open device-level details of the underlying flash storage for key-value caching. This co-design approach bridges the semantic gap and well connects the two layers together, which allows us to leverage both the domain knowledge of key-value caches and the unique device properties. In this way, we can maximize the efficiency of key-value caching on flash devices while minimizing its weakness. We implemented a prototype based on the Open-Channel SSD platform. Our experiments on real hardware show that we can significantly increase the throughput by 35.5%, reduce the latency by 23.6%, and remove unnecessary erase operations by 28%. The results have been published in the 15th Usenix Conference on File and Storage Technologies (FAST 2018), one of the top conferences in storage systems. The extended version with more technique details and comprehensive evaluation has been published in ACM Transactions on Storage. Objective 2 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 2, we have studied workload-aware key-value space allocation and live migration that can adapt runtime environments so as to alleviate influences caused by fluctuating workload surges for operating key-value stores in public cloud. We started with applying key-value techniques to optimize mobile database applications [C2, J4]. Specifically, we for the first time propose a new SQLite-like database engine, called SQLiteKV, which adopts the LSM-tree-based data structure but retains the SQLite operation interfaces. With its SQLite interface, SQLiteKV can be utilized by existing applications without any modification, while providing high performance with its LSM-tree-based data structure. In SQLiteKV, we develop a light-weight SQLite to key-value compiler to solve the semantic mismatch, so SQL statements can be efficiently translated into KV operations. We also design a novel coordination caching mechanism so query results can be effectively cached inside SQLiteKV by alleviating the discrepancy of data management between front-end SQLite statements and back-end key-value data organization. We have implemented and deployed SQLiteKV on a Google Nexus 6P smartphone. Experimental results show that SQLiteKV outperforms SQLite up to 6 times. The results have been published in the 23rd Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASPDAC 2018). The extended version with more technique details and comprehensive evaluation has been published in IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems (TCAD). We also investigate this by exploiting SSD storage interfaces. Specifically, in [C4, J3], we propose a flexible storage interface called Prism-SSD that exports the SSD hardware in three levels of abstraction: as a raw flash media with its low-level details, as a group of functions to manage flash capacity, or as a configurable block device. This multi-level abstraction allows developers to choose the degree in which they desire to control the flash hardware in a manner that best suits their applications' semantics and performance objectives. We demonstrate the usability of this new model with Prism-SSD - a prototype of this interface as a user-level library on the Open-Channel SSD platform. We use each of the interface's three abstraction levels to modify the I/O module of three representative applications: a key-value cache system, a user-level file system, and a graph processing engine. Prism-SSD improves application performance by 5% to 27%, at varying development costs, between 200 and 3,500 lines of code. The results have been published in the 39th IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems (ICDCS). The extended version with more technique details and comprehensive evaluation has been published in IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems (TCAD). Objective 3 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 3, we have developed various Non-Volatile-Memory (NVM) techniques to optimize key-value and other big data applications by leveraging the new memory hierarchy and fully exploiting attractive features of NVM [J1, C3]. In [J1, C3], we utilize processing-in-memory (PIM), combined with nonvolatile metal oxide resistive random access memory (ReRAM), to improve the performance of both computation and I/O in graph computing. The idea is to integrate the computation logic into the memory in which the data accesses are located. We propose and implement a new ReRAM-based processing-in-memory architecture called RPBFS, in which graphs can be processed and persistently stored. We also design an efficient graph traversal scheme. Benefited from low data movement overhead and bank-level parallel computation, RPBFS shows a significant performance improvement compared with both the CPU-based and GPU-based BFS implementations. On a suite of real world graphs, our architecture yields up to 33.8× speedup. The results have been published in one conference (NVMSA 2017) and one journal (in ACM Transactions on Storage). We also investigate key-value caching by utilizing open-channel SSDs to serve as NVM as discussed above in [J4]. Objective 4 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 4, we have integrated the above three studies with framework development and evaluation by constructing the experimental platforms to implement and evaluate the proposed techniques and mechanisms. Specifically, we have developed a software-defined-SSD-based experimental platform that can be utilized to evaluate the proposed techniques [C1, J2]. With this platform, we can conduct experiments on a workstation, which features an Intel i7-5820K 3.3GHZ processor and 16GB memory, and an Open-Channel SSD that is used as underlying storage. For the software, we use Ubuntu 14.04 with Linux kernel 3.17.8. Our back-end database server is MySQL 5.5 with InnoDB storage engine running on a separate workstation, which features an Intel Core 2 Duo processor (3.13GHZ), 8GB memory and a 500GB hard drive. The database server and the cache server are connected in a 1Gbps local Ethernet network. Moreover, based on the above experimental platform, we have developed the Prism-SSD model [C4, J3], which offers a powerful tool for developers to optimize their performance with SSDs. By choosing the abstraction level that best suits their needs, application developers can integrate their software design with the hardware management at the right balance between performance and development cost. Developers who desire a deep integration may leverage the low-level abstraction to maximize the achievable performance gains; those who simply desire to leverage the built-in optimizations provided by the library can use the high-level abstraction to achieve performance gains with a lower development cost. Finally, to evaluate the NVM-based techniques, we have implemented a simulation environment by which various experiments with different NVM configurations can be carried out [J1, C3].

15273616.label: Major findings and research outcome
15273616.value: For Objective 1, we have proposed a novel flash-based key-value caching technique, called DIDACache [C1, J2]. Specifically, our novel co-design approach bridges the semantic gap and well connects the two layers together, thus enabling to leverage both the domain knowledge of key-value caches and the unique device properties. Our experiments on real hardware show that our method can significantly increase the throughput, reduce the latency, and remove unnecessary erase operations. For Objective 2, we for the first time propose a new SQLite-like database engine, called SQLiteKV [C2, J4], which adopts the LSM-tree-based data structure but retains the SQLite operation interfaces. With our technique, applications can utilize the SQLite interface, while leveraging the LSM-tree-based data structure for high-performance writes. Experimental results based on real systems show that SQLiteKV outperforms SQLite up to 6 times. Moreover, in [C4, J3], we propose a flexible storage interface called Prism-SSD that exports the SSD hardware in three levels of abstraction: as a raw flash media with its low-level details, as a group of functions to manage flash capacity, or as a configurable block device. This multi-level abstraction allows developers to choose the degree in which they desire to control the flash hardware in a manner that best suits their applications' semantics and performance objectives. Our experiments show that Prism-SSD can fully exploit the trade-off between performance and development cost. For Objective 3, various Non-Volatile-Memory (NVM) techniques have been developed to optimize key-value and other big data applications by leveraging the new memory hierarchy and fully exploiting attractive features of NVM. Specifically, in [J1, C3], we utilize processing-in-memory (PIM), combined with nonvolatile metal oxide resistive random access memory (ReRAM), to improve the performance of both computation and I/O in graph computing. We also investigate key-value caching with open-channel SSDs as discussed above in [J4]. The experimental results show that the proposed techniques can effectively improve system performance. For Objective 4, we have developed several experimental platforms, including a software-defined-SSD-based experimental platform [C1, J2], an application development tool with an optimized SSD model [C4, J3], and a NVM simulation environment with different configurations [J1, C3].

15273616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15273616.value: For flash-based key-value caching, we propose a novel co-design approach by bridging the semantic gap between hardware and software and enabling to leverage both the domain knowledge of key-value caches and the unique device properties. One direction for future work is to further exploit other applications by utilizing this cross-layer approach for performance optimization. In SQLiteKV, as the first exploration of SQLite-like key-value database engines, the translation of SQL operations to key-value operations in SQLiteKV is straightforward. One possible future work is to investigate specific compiler optimization and design to make its translation more efficient and complete. In Prism-SSD, we propose a flexible storage interface that exports the SSD hardware in three levels of abstraction. From the perspective of hardware vendors, a flexible storage interface in the form of a user-level library is a powerful tool for reducing development costs and the time-to-market. It will be interesting to further develop our technique so hardware vendors can easily offer custom-built hardware/software solutions based it. Finally, it should be a promising direction to explore NVM with Processing-In-Memory to enhance other applications’ performance such as for machine learning, AI, and blockchains.

15273616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15273616.value: Hong Kong, as an international financial, trading and logistics hub, is facing ever growing demand for data center facilities, big data analytics and e-commerce services. Therefore, it is critical to optimize key-value (KV) stores as they are one of the most important building blocks in modern web infrastructures and high-performance data-intensive applications, for instance, serving as web object cache and large-scale distributed NoSQL databases. In this research, based on a holistic approach, we aim to develop novel techniques to bridge three semantic gaps, namely, (1) the gap between garbage collection in KV stores and SSD low-level hardware operations in SSD-assisted KV caching systems; (2) the gap between KV stores and complex, less predictable runtime scenarios in public cloud; (3) the gap between organization/management of KV stores and characteristics of NVM. The ultimate goal of this project is to enable KV storage systems to provide faster, more predictable KV access latencies. This project is particularly important for Hong Kong, as key-value-based web caching, distributed NoSQL databases and public cloud play an essential role in supporting international business, trade and finance.

15274316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15274316.value: 破碎波作用下的近岸泥沙輸運過程: 數值模擬研究

15274316.label: Project Objectives
15274316.value: In this study, the main objective is to build a comprehensive numerical model for the investigation of the complex interaction of the air bubble entrainment and transport process, the free surface flow dynamics and sediment re-suspension subject to breaking wave conditions. The governing equations of air bubbles entrainment, bubbles break up and bubbles diffusion are incorporated into the mixture (multi-phase) model to efficiently and accurately simulate breaking wave induced dispersed multiphase flows. Simulations of the suspended sediment transport in the surf zone will be focusing on air bubble effects on sediment particles suspension, the air downburst enhancement effects and breaking wave lift up effects on sediment particles. The influence of turbulence structure on suspended sediment particles will also be studied. The proposed model is based on a well-established Reynolds Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) model which has been successfully applied to simulate general turbulent surface flows. The energy production/dissipation turbulent closure model is applied to obtain the turbulent kinetic energy and the turbulent dissipation rate. The two step projection method is employed to solve the continuity and momentum equations in which the pressure is solved by the pressure Poisson equation. A modified Volume of Fluid (VOF) method is applied to solve the air concentration convection-diffusion equation. The VOF method is adopted to track the surface of air-water mixture when solving the convection term. The upwind scheme is used to solve the air convection in the air-water mixture, and a central difference scheme is used to solve the diffusion term. The interface of air-water mixture and the air concentration distribution is solved simultaneously by this method. Coastlines, in fact, are sensitive to changes in sea level. A small change in sea level may have influence on where the waves will break and how sediments may deposit or erode along the coasts. Many scientific evidences have shown global sea level is rising due to climate change and sea level rise is particularly critical for low-lying regions such wetlands where the ecosystems are vulnerable to inundation from sea level rise. Rise in sea level may also lead to larger waves as the seafloor becomes steeper and higher wave-driven water levels along wetlands. The model developed in this study will help us to gain better understanding on the sediment accretion and erosion processes along the coast under the influence of acute breaking waves due to change in sea level.

15274316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15274316.value: Breaking waves in the surf zone play an essential role in sediment transport and consequently the morphological changes. Previous studies have shown that wave breaking generates large-scale turbulent flow structures known as the obliquely descending eddies and downbursts of turbulent fluids, which may bring intense turbulence to the bottom and erode a large amount of sediments into suspension (please refer to Figure 1 in Part II, 2(c)). At the same time, a large volume of air may enter the flow and quickly evolves into air bubbles with sizes from tens of micrometers to centimeters and interact with the surrounding water flow. The flow turbulence and vorticity fields are strongly influenced by the presence of entrained air bubbles and sediment particles. Because of the complexity of surf zone hydrodynamics, nearshore suspended sediment transport is still not fully understood. In this study, an integrated model is built to study the air bubble entrainment/transport processes as well as the bubbles’ effects on suspended sediment particles subject to breaking waves in the surf zone. To improve the prediction capability, it is essential to describe the dynamics of breaking wave in the surf zone as a multi-phase flow with air bubbles of appropriate size distribution. The air bubble entrainment model is deduced from available experimental data with turbulent dissipation taken into consideration and will be applied to study the breaking process of different types of wave run-ups. The simulated surface displacements will be compared with the existing experimental data, e.g. Rapp and Melville (1990) which was measured by Laser Doppler Anemometer (LDA). The model is then used to study air entrainment and sediment transport processes in a sloping surf zone environment. As sea level rise may lead to larger waves and more acute wave break along the coastline, the present model can improve our understanding of the complex interactions between wave breaking, air entrainment and sediment transport in coastal zones such that a better prediction of the change in coastlines can be achieved. 進岸破碎波對泥沙輸運以及海岸形態演變起著重要作用。研究發現破碎波引起的下切斡旋和下擊流等大尺度紊流結構將對海床泥沙有什大的卷吸作用。同時，波浪破碎過程中大量的空氣被捲入水體並迅速與周圍水流發生強烈地相互作用和能量交換，極大地影響了水流的紊動特性以及渦體發展。由於進岸水動力學的複雜性，目前對進岸泥沙的輸運研究取得了一定的進展，但還有一些關鍵問题尚待解决。 本研究將應用數值模型對波浪破碎下的摻氣過程以及氣泡對泥沙輸運的影響進行研究。為了更加真實的模擬摻氣水流特性，模型中需要考慮合理的氣泡的尺寸以及分佈，這就需要引入合適的摻氣模型。在本研究中，基於實驗測量的破碎波下氣泡分佈規律以及模擬的水體的紊動擴散率，建立起模擬氣泡摻入水體、隨流輸運、擴散、上浮以及溢出水面的完整物理過程的模型，結合描述摻氣水流運動的數學控制方程，對進岸波浪破碎以及摻氣過程進行模擬並將數值模擬結果與實驗測量值進行比較。由於氣候變化海平面上升，進岸破碎波波高增大，破碎增強，該模型的研究結果可以增加對進岸水流以及泥沙輸運特性的認識，對工程設計和應用有很大的幫助作用。
