15275316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15275316.value: 本項目旨在開發具有高壓電和低能隙的鐵電氧化物。基於光伏效應，具有低能隙的材料一直被視為能將太陽能轉化爲電力的新型能源材料。由於鐵電氧化物內的自發極化能將轉化過程中產生的電子-離子對有效分離，從而產生可用的電能，它們也成爲新型能源材料的熱門選擇。這一特性也可簡化太陽能電池的結構，從而降低生產成本。可是，一般鐵電氧化物的能隙比較寬（>3電子伏），可吸收並轉化的太陽能極爲有限（<8％)。這工作主要通過對鈦酸鋇基鐵電氧化物摻雜不同過渡金屬離子，期望能降低它的能隙和增加太陽能吸收量。除了能隙，這工作也會檢測新鐵電氧化物轉化太陽能爲電能的性能。

15275316.label: Realisation of objectives
15275316.value: Perovskite-structured ferroelectric oxides with high piezoelectricity and low bandgap have been developed. The effects of highly electronegative transition metal ions on the crystallite structure, dielectric, ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties as well as the optical bandgap of the ferroelectric oxides have been characterized, and their inter-relationships have been investigated. The photovoltaic and luminescence responses of the oxide ceramics have been studied systematically and the optimum composition of the oxide ceramics for reducing the optical bandgap, retaining the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties, and exhibit good photovoltaic and luminescence responses have then been determined. Because of the excellent piezoelectric properties, Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.9Sn0.1O3 (BCTSn) has been selected as the base material for the study. Transition metal ions Cu+, Ni2+ and Fe3+ with high similar high electronegativity, i.e., 1.90, 1.91 and 1.83, respectively, have been used as dopants for entirely replacing the B-site Sn4+, with the aims of reducing the optical bandgap. It has been reported that a higher electronegativity can significantly reduce the bandgap of a ferroelectric oxide. However, our results reveal that only Fe3+ can reduce the bandgap of BCTSn from 3.30 eV to 2.64 eV, while the others have slight effect on it. These suggest that the electronegativity may not be an essential parameter affecting the bandgap of the ceramics. Apparently, the valence state of the ions may also be another important factor. On the other hand, the replacement with Fe3+ has induced a shift of the Curie temperature from ~60C to below room temperature, causing the Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.9Fe0.1O3 (BCTFe or BCTFe-0.1) ceramic to exhibit no piezoelectric responses. A series of studies has then been conducted to investigate the relations between Fe3+ and the properties such as bandgap, Curie temperature and piezoelectric properties, with the aim of developing a ferroelectric ceramic with low bandgap and high piezoelectricity. Our results reveal that Fe3+ can not only reduce the bandgap but also lower the Curie temperature. For the ceramic containing smaller amount of Fe, the bandgap becomes larger while the Curie temperature increases. A good balance between these two properties is achieved in the Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.975Fe0.025O3 (BCTFe-0.025) ferroelectric ceramic, which exhibits a low bandgap (2.87 eV) as well as a high piezoelectric coefficient (d33 = 170 pC/N). More importantly, it also exhibit a low dielectric loss (tan δ = 1%), suggesting that it could readily be used for practical applications. The ferroelectric response of the ceramics have been investigated using both the in-plane interdigitated electrodes (IDE) and through-plane vertical electrode (VE) configurations. In the measurements, the samples are illuminated with a solar light of intensity 100 mV/cm2 (or 1 sun) and the short-circuit current is observed using a sourcemeter. Although the IDE configuration has advantages of allowing the ceramics to be illuminated directly without any reduction arisen from the electrodes and eliminating the Schottky junction effect, the observed photocurrents for the ceramics, both BCTFe-0.025 and BCTSn, are weak, probably due to the limited illuminated region. On the other hand, both the ceramics with the VE configuration exhibit strong photocurrents, which increase with the poling field (i.e., the degree of polarization alignment or piezoelectric properties) and flows in the opposite direction of the poling field. Moreover, it can be switched by changing the poling field's direction. These confirm that the piezoelectricity is essential in producing photocurrents without the need of special device structures such as the p-n junction normally used in the semiconductor devices. However, the observed photocurrent is contributed not only by the photovoltaic effect but also by other effects such as the pyroelectric effect. In general, it increases sharply in the beginning of the illumination attributed to the pyroelectric effect and/or others, and then decreases and becomes constant demonstrating the photovoltaic effect. Probably because of the lower bandgap and then broadened absorption of the visible spectrum, the BCTFe-0.025 ceramic exhibit a larger photocurrent than the BCTSn ceramic (11 nA/cm2 vs 3 nA/cm2). Our results further reveal that the non-ferroelectric BCTFe-0.1 ceramic also exhibits a strong photocurrent (11 nA/cm2) as well as an open-circuit voltage of 0.2 V that is suggested to form a built-in field to separate the photo-induced charge carries. As the ceramic is non-ferroelectric, it does not exhibit a pyroelectric current and thus the observed photocurrent does not show a sharp peak upon the illumination. This provides not only evidences of the contribution of the pyroelectric effect in the ferroelectric ceramics but also an approach of studying the bandgap based on the photocurrent measurements. Without the effect of the strong pyroelectric current, the ceramic exhibits a clear dependence of the photocurrent on the wavelength of the illumination. In spite of the weakness, a photocurrent is clearly observed under illumination at 580 nm. The estimated bandgap is about 0.4 eV lower than that determined by the transmission technique. Nevertheless, this clearly shows that the bandgap of the BCTFe-0.1 ceramic is extended to visible region. Our results also reveal that the photocurrent can be reversed by an external electric field and restored by thermal annealing. These suggest that the built-in field for separating the photo-induced charge carries is formed by the non-uniform distribution of oxygen vacancies. Because of the good properties, the barium titanate-based ferroelectric ceramics have also been used to fabricate thin films for investigating their applications. For the films fabricated on a piezoelectric crystal substrate, its photoluminescence can be tuned in a reversible and nonvolatile way by electric field. Such a nonvolatile and reversible response is striking, which stems from the intermediate lateral-polarization-induced stable strain state in the substrate during domain switching. The results provide an effective strategy for realizing piezo-luminescent effect in ferroelectric thin-film heterostructures and demonstrates great potentials in designing reconfigurable, low-power nonvolatile luminescent memory devices. Thin films have also been fabricated on flexible transparent mica substrates. Because of the high flexibility of the substrate, the films exhibit strong and reversible photoluminescence response triggered by mechanical bending. The film structure exhibits excellent antifatigue characteristics after 104 bending cycles as well as high optical transparency in the range of 450–780 nm. The results provide a viable route for exploring the correlation between structural symmetry and photoluminescence in ferroelectric thin-film systems and offers new possibilities for developing all-inorganic, reconfigurable, transparent and flexible light sources, photodetectors, and wearable sensors.

15275316.label: Major findings and research outcome
15275316.value: The bandgap of barium titanate-based ferroelectric oxide Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.9Sn0.1O3 (BCTSn) has been reduced from 3.30 eV to 2.64 eV by replacing the B-site Sn4+ with Fe3+. Not only the high electronegativity but also factors such as valence state of the ions have been shown the essential parameters for reducing the bandgap. Like other ferroelectric oxides, the replacement has adverse effects on ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties. The optimum composition for reducing the optical bandgap and retaining the piezoelectric properties have been determined; i.e., Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.975Fe0.025O3 (BCTFe-0.025) ferroelectric ceramic, which exhibits a low bandgap (2.87 eV) as well as a high piezoelectric coefficient (d33 = 170 pC/N). It also has a low dielectric loss (tan δ = 1%), suggesting that it could readily be used for practical applications. Because of the lower bandgap, the BCTFe-0.025 ceramic exhibit a larger photocurrent than the BCTSn ceramic (11 nA/cm2 vs 3 nA/cm2). The observed photocurrent increases with the poling field and flows in the opposite direction of the poling field. It can also be switched by changing the poling field's direction. These confirm that the photocurrent is mainly arisen from the spontaneous polarization. Besides the photovoltaic effect, the observed photocurrent is also contributed the other effect such as the photovoltaic effect, especially in the beginning of the illumination. Oxygen vacancies that are commonly formed in ferroelectric oxides have been shown to be capable of inducing a strong photocurrent without the presence of a polarization. For the non-ferroelectric oxide with low bandgap, i.e., Ba0.9Ca0.1Ti0.9Fe0.1O3 (BCTFe-0.01) in the as-fabricated state, it exhibits a strong photocurrent (11 nA/cm2) and an open-circuit voltage of 0.2 V that is suggested to form a built-in field to separate the photo-induced charge carries. As the ceramic is non-ferroelectric, it does not exhibit a pyroelectric current and thus exhibits a clear dependence of the photocurrent on the wavelength of the illumination, based on which the bandgap is determined to be about 2.24 eV. Our results also reveal that the photocurrent can be reversed by an external electric field and restored by thermal annealing. These suggest that the built-in field for separating the photo-induced charge carries is formed by the non-uniform distribution of oxygen vacancies. The newly developed barium titanate-based ferroelectric oxides, in thin film form, also exhibit an electric field-driven reversible and non-volatile tuning of photoluminescence and a mechanically controlled reversible photoluminescence response when fabricated in thin films.

15275316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15275316.value: The Fe-doped barium titanate-based ferroelectric oxides that exhibit a low optical bandgap and high piezoelectricity should find potential in solar energy harvesting applications. Based on the inter-relationships between the electronegativity of B-site dopants, bandgap, crystallite structure, ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of the ferroelectric oxides established in this work, other ferroelectric oxides with low bandgap can be developed for practical applications.

15275316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15275316.value: The optical bandgap of barium titanate-based ferroelectric oxides has been successfully reduced by the B-site doping of a highly electronegative transition metal ions, i.e., Fe3+ (1.83). Like other dopants, the doping has also affected the crystallite structure and piezoelectric properties of the oxides. At the optimum doping level (i.e., 0.25%), the oxide exhibits a low optical bandgap (2.87 eV) as well as a high piezoelectric coefficient (d33 = 170 pC/N). The reduced bandgap can extend the solar energy absorption to visible light region. As a result, a strong photocurrent driven by the spontaneous polarization that is the unique characteristic of ferroelectric oxides is observed. On the other hand, if the doping level increases to 1%, the bandgap can further be reduced to 2.64 eV, but the oxide becomes non-ferroelectric. Nevertheless, the oxide still exhibit a strong photocurrent partly because of the low bandgap and partly because of the oxygen vacancies that are commonly formed in ferroelectric oxides. Moreover, the oxides also exhibit an electric field-driven reversible and non-volatile tuning of photoluminescence and a mechanically controlled reversible photoluminescence response when fabricated in thin films.

15275716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15275716.value: High spectral efficiency modulation formats and digital signal processing (DSP) are the cornerstones of current optical transceivers for long-haul global optical networks. However, emerging prevalence of pervasive mobile communications, data center, cloud computing, Internet of Things(IoT) and augmented reality applications far out-pace the steady improvements brought about by current technology: transmission performance is still severely limited by fiber Kerr nonlinearity despite years of advanced DSP research to try address the problem. Another fundamental hurdle is ubiquitous optical performance monitoring(OPM): extracted information about the real-time state of the optical network are too convoluted and nearly physically intractable, thus prohibiting elastic optical networks(EON) with intelligent and optimized network traffic engineering enabling much higher network efficiency. To this end, machine learning techniques are based on training an algorithm or set of instructions, or ‘learn’, to perform certain tasks without the explicit physical understanding of the underlying system concerned. Machine learning has been in the arena of computer science research since the 1990s with applications ranging from computer vision, data mining and bioinformatics and they produce fantastic results that are otherwise not achievable by any other class of signal processing techniques. Recently, machine learning is brought into the field of optical communications by a few research groups worldwide and preliminary studies revealed very encouraging results. Nonetheless, the true potentials and power of machine learning techniques in optical communication networks and corresponding experimental demonstrations has yet to be fully investigated and illustrated. The objectives of the proposed research are to thoroughly address key fundamental issues and elucidate how the rich body of machine learning techniques can be appropriately developed and further evolve into a unique and powerful set of signal processing tools for 1)high-capacity long-haul transmissions in presence of fiber nonlinearity and 2)ubiquitous optical performance monitoring for EON. In contrast with the long-standing and core mindsets of physicists and engineers, machine learning takes on a drastically different philosophy in problem solving and has already established remarkable track records unparalleled by other competing techniques in a wide range of science and engineering disciplines. The machine learning tools to be developed in this proposal will provide unique insights and lay the foundations for an entirely new approach in optical communications. Furthermore, the successful completion of the proposed research might very well symbolize the tip of the iceberg of how machine learning can be incorporated into much wider areas of optics research as new indispensable tools with unprecedented impacts. 眾所周知，高頻譜效率的調製格式和數字信號處理技術（DSP）是當前高速光通信網絡技術的算法基礎。但是由於移動終端通信的廣泛流行，和大數據中心、雲端處理技術、物聯網(IoT)、虛擬現實等技術的大規模應用，現有算法基礎的光​​通信網絡將會不堪重負。其中一個限制系統性能提升的主要問題是光纖非線性效應，多年來業界嘗試使用各種先進的統計信號處理技術去破解這一難題，卻始終沒有成功。另一個棘手的問題是對於光網絡的各種性能準確監控，由於光網絡的狀態信息過於復雜甚至於物理上無法分解，這導致傳統的數字信號處理方法在實現任意彈性光網絡的光性能監控變得非常困難。 為此解決上述問題，我們認為人工智能,機器學習技術可以作為一種可行的解決方案。因為這種技術可以無需對底層系統有明確的物理理解，通過訓練算法或者稱之為“自主學習”而獲得系統性能的提升。自1990年代以來，該技術成為計算機科學研究領域內的熱點話題，其應用範圍囊括計算機視覺，數據挖掘和生物信息學等，能達到其他任何其他類型的信號處理技術無法實現的優異效果。最近，一些研究小組將機器學習引入光通信領域，初步的研究已經產生了非常令人鼓舞的結果。因此，我們需要更進一步的調查和研究該技術在光通信網絡中的應用潛力和相應的實驗證明。 對於這項目申請，我們將抓住這一寶貴機會，結合機器學習和光學兩大研究方向進行協作研究。建議研究的目標是要通過機器學習技術盡可能的解決光通信網絡中的關鍵基本問題，並闡明如何使豐富的機器學習技術在光通信領域內進一步發展成為一個新的和獨特的信號處理工具。它將包含兩個目標：1）解決現有的長距大容量光纖通信傳輸中的光纖非線性為題；2）研究下一代彈性光網絡的光信道監控技術。 與物理學家和工程師們長期的研究和解決問題的核心觀念相反，學習機呈現出一種截然不同的理念，並且已經在很多其他的科學和工程領域被證明為最有效的技術。因此，開發人工智能,機器學習這一工具將為光通信研究和實驗提供獨特的思路，也將奠定一個新的光通信領域的研究方向。此外，若這研究項目成功的話，更可以證明結合人工智能,機器學習這一強大的信號處理工具在一般的光學研究領域也具有巨大潛力。

15275716.label: Realisation of objectives
15275716.value: For objective 1, we have developed a DNN for fiber nonlinearity compensation for WDM systems and experimentally verify its performance gain compared to traditional digital back propagation(DBP) algorithm and characterized the corresponding computational complexity. It can be shown that DNN is the optimal form of neural network for fiber nonlinearity compensation as it most resemble the DBP structure which in turn mimics the underlying physical effect of chromatic dispersion and self-phase modulation. This study also presented a first demonstration of a single-channel based DSP with good performance gain in WDM systems. For NFDM systems, the research community has developed various analytical techniques to improve detection since the commencement of this proposal. As a general rule of thumb, one should exhaust all the analytical tools before using machine learning as incorporating domain knowledge in the design of ML models and input features will always help improve ML performance. We therefore have delayed the work on ML in NFDM systems until recent months when we incorporated all the state-of-the-art statistical/analytical techniques so as to obtain the best decision metrics as the starting point of ML-based classification algorithms such as K-means clustering and EM algorithm. Experimental results have been obtained, research paper is currently under preparation and will be submitted to Journal of Lightwave Technology for review by Feb. 2021. On the other hand, an emerged important area of ML for optical communications is Quality of Transmission(QoT) estimation as it holds key to realizing autonomous intelligent adaptive network to maximize throughput. In this connection, we worked on this area and demonstrated the first field trial of ML enabled QoT estimation and transmission rate adaptation together with University of Bristol. We also conducted an in-depth comparison study between ML and analytical methods in QoT estimation and show that ML does have an advantage over analytical models in practical experimental settings. The results provide valuable reference values for academics and industry researchers working in QoT estimation. Objective 2 has been fully achieved as we have developed and experimentally verified a joint OSNR, modulation format and corresponding bandwidth identification technique using deep neural networks that can distinguish between 112 Gb/s polarization multiplexed(PM) QPSK, 112Gb/s PM-16QAM and 240Gb/s PM 64-QAM with 100% accuracy and an OSNR range from 10 dB to 23 dB. The objective has been extended to the study of machine learning techniques such as k-means clustering to identify transceiver phase noise, IQ phase and gain imbalance.

15275716.label: Major findings and research outcome
15275716.value: In long-haul optical communications, fiber nonlinearity is the performance limiting factor and digital back-propagation(DBP) algorithm is a standard nonlinearity compensation technique. In our work, we consider DBP as a deep neural network(DNN) so that all the parameters are optimized(C.8.1). Results show that not only does ML improve transmission performance, the optimized configuration also guide us to deeper understanding of the nonlinear interactions between signals and noise within DBP itself. Other ML techniques such as EM algorithm also helped improve signal detection performance based on Nonlinear Fourier Transform(C.8.9) We also worked on using ANN and DNN for OSNR monitoring with 10-25 dB range and modulation format and bandwidth identification(C.8.3) between QPSK, 16-QAM and 64-QAM. We also show that unsupervised learning algorithm like k-means clustering can identify transceiver impairments such as phase noise and transmitter in-phase and quadrature imbalances(C.8.5). We further showed that convolutional neural networks can be used for joint estimation of IQ phase and gain imbalances(C.9.3). These techniques will be useful tools in future intelligent optical networks with autonomous monitoring of the states of all network components to improve reliability and throughput. In the area of optical networks, ML for Quality of Transmission(QoT) estimation is an important topic. Together with University of Bristol, we demonstrated the first field trial of ML-enabled QoT estimation and transmission rate adaptation(C.9.2) in 2017. Moreover, there's currently no consensus whether ML can outperform traditional analytical models in QoT estimation. Our further work provides the first comprehensive comparison between ML and analytical methods in experimental and simulation settings (C.8.8, C.9.5) and showed that due to parameter uncertainties in experimental settings, ML does have an advantage over analytical models in practice. As an extension of our original objectives, we worked on applying principle component analysis(PCA) for carrier phase recovery of high-order modulation formats (C.8.6) and temperature sensing in Brillouin optical time-domain analysis(C.8.2). We also investigated the effects of finite quantization in transmitting a neural-network-optimized representation of standard data set over an additive white gaussian channel and show that the quantization effects cannot be ignored, which will become a major issue in memory-constrained ML applications(C.8.7) using cell phones and other Internet-of-Things devices. Finally, as a recognition of our work, we have an invited tutorial paper in Journal of Lightwave technology (C.8.4) and a few invited presentations in international conferences(C.9.1, C.9.4) on machine learning in optical communications and networks and they are well cited in the community.

15275716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15275716.value: Since the commencement of the project, the field of optical communications have been exploring machine learning as new tools to tackle complex problems in optical communications and networks. In physical layer communications, the work on DNN for nonlinearity compensation is being further investigated for computationally simpler DSP for commercial implementations and we will submit another paper in the near future. On the theory side, the interpretable ML work can also open up new research directions in ML-assisted insight discovery in Optics. For optical networks, the parameter monitoring and QoT estimation work is now being explored for further research collaboration opportunities with Industry as the field is starting to show interest in low-margin dynamic networks in the near future and ML-based network parameter monitoring is considered as an essential component.

15275716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15275716.value: Global Internet traffic has grown so much in size and become so dynamic over the past few years that existing signal processing techniques and network infrastructure cannot handle the pace of traffic growth. Recently, machine Learning has become a new powerful tool in various Engineering applications and in our project, we showed that 1) Deep Neural Network can learn complex intractable signal distortion patterns from received data and one can derive signal processing methodologies to undo the distortions and improve transmission performance; 2) machine learning techniques can extract important real-time network state information by learning from the transmitted signals(or part of it) which provide valuable information and insights in ensuring network reliability and resource planning to improve overall network capacity

15276516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15276516.value: Human faces are the most common object in images and video, and the research on human face recognition has been conducted over the past three decades. Many different face recognition algorithms have been proposed to deal with faces under different facial expressions, lighting conditions, poses, resolutions, etc. However, only limited research on age-invariant face recognition has been conducted as it is a challenging task. High-resolution (HR) face recognition is a new research area, and the existing face recognition algorithms gain very little benefit from the available HR face images. Our recent research on HR face recognition has found that when a face image has a resolution higher than 700x600 pixels, detection of microscopic features, i.e. pores on facial skin, is possible. We have used pore-scale facial features for face recognition, and excellent results can be achieved. The locations and distributions of pores and pore patterns on face images can be used as new biometrics for face recognition. In this project, we will conduct research on age-invariant face recognition for HR images. Based on our current research results, we will investigate a better representation of facial skin in terms of pore appearance so that detection and localization of facial pores can be more accurate and reliable. Different visual features at the detected pore keypoints are then used for representation. However, the locations of the pore keypoints and their local visual features may change with age progression. Therefore, we will investigate the change of the pore features with age so as to alleviate the effect of age progression on face recognition. In order to achieve accurate matching of two face images based on the pore features on their faces, we will investigate using an optimal feature-matching approach with geometrical deformations of pore keypoints taken into consideration. Based on this research, we aim to perform more accurate pore matching and then the required image resolution can be lowered. More importantly, age-invariant HR face recognition can be achieved. This is a new research area, and the availability of an HR face database is very limited, in particular with HR face images at different ages. In this project, we will build an HR face database with different ages, which will be vital to the development of HR face recognition in the future. The research output of this project is not limited to face recognition only, but also to 3D face reconstruction, subtle facial expression or emotion recognition, etc.

15276516.label: Realisation of objectives
15276516.value: All the objectives of this project have been achieved. The following are the details of what we have achieved for each of the objectives. Objective 1: Study and develop algorithms for mapping pore-scale features from one age to another In this project, we have developed different algorithms for extracting the pore-scale features from face images and for mapping the pore features, across ages, for face recognition. We have also employed a constraint, based on a 3D facial model, for constructing a large number of pore-to-pore correspondences between face images, across ages. These pore correspondences are then used to train a Convolutional Neural Network to generate novel pore-scale facial features, namely Deeply Learned Pore-scale Facial Features (DLPFF). These features are insensitive to age progression, and thus, can achieve a higher accuracy for high-resolution face recognition, across ages, compared to our previous handcrafted pore-scale features. Objective 2: Develop algorithms for reliable and accurate detection of pores and matching of pore features In this project, we have proposed different face-recognition algorithms, which can be applied to face images of different ages and different resolutions. First, we proposed a deep pore-scale feature, which is extracted by a deep neural network, namely PoreNet. This network is adapted from the HardNet, with a slight increase of parameters, by only 0.086%. To achieve better accuracy in matching the deep pore-scale features, between two high-resolution face images, the Grid-based Motion Statistics are employed. Second, we proposed a deep feature-encoding-based discriminative model for age-invariant face recognition. Our method learns high-level deep features, using AlexNet, which are then encoded by learning a codebook. By incorporating the locality information in the whole learning process, a closed-form solution is obtained, for both the codebook-updating and encoding stages. As the features of the same person at different ages should have certain correlations, canonical correlation analysis is utilized to fuse the pairs of training features, for two different ages, to make the codebook discriminative, in terms of age progression. In the testing stage, the gallery and query image’s features are encoded, using the learned codebook. Then, linear mapping, based on linear regression, is employed for face matching. Third, we proposed a face-recognition method, based on the low-rank representations and encoding of handcrafted features, for recognizing face images at different resolutions. Our approach ﬁrst decomposes a multiple of extracted local features of face images into a set of representative bases, i.e. the low-rank matrix and sparse error matrix, and then learns a projection matrix based on our proposed sparse-coding-based algorithm, which preserves the sparse structure of the learned low-rank features, in a low-dimensional or other dimensional feature subspace. Then, a coefﬁcient vector based on linear regression is computed to determine the similarity between the projected gallery and query image’s features. Finally, we propose a low-resolution face-recognition method. In our method, we proposed a novel loss function, called identity-preserved loss, which combines with the image-content loss to jointly supervise CNNs, for performing face hallucination and recognition simultaneously. Therefore, the trained network is able to perform face hallucination and identity preservation, even if the query face is of very low resolution. More importantly, experimental results show that our proposed method can preserve the identities of the low-resolution images from unknown subjects, who are not included in the training set. Objective 3: Conduct comprehensive experiments to evaluate the performances of the algorithms developed in this project The different algorithms proposed in this project have been evaluated comprehensively. The first algorithm, PoreNet, was evaluated on the Bosphorus database and the Multi-PIE database. The gallery set contains the frontal-view face images of 105 subjects. Then, all the face under 5 pose variations: R10, R20, R30, R45, and L45, and 6 facial-expression variations form the query set. This can evaluate the performance of the algorithms under the pose and facial-expression variations. For the deep feature encoding-based discriminative model for age-invariant face recognition, we evaluated it on three publicly available challenging facial aging datasets, FGNET, MORPH Album 2, and Large Age-Gap (LAG). Experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms various state-of-the-art age-invariant face recognition methods, in terms of the rank-1 recognition accuracy. For the two low-resolution face recognition algorithms, we evaluated them and compared them with state-of-the-art methods on ﬁve face datasets, including the Extended Yale-B, Multi-PIE, FERET, LFW, and Remote face databases. These databases contain images with variations in pose, facial expressions, and lighting conditions. In all these experiments, the results show that our proposed methods can achieve state-of-the-art and promising performances. Objective 4: Develop a database of HR face images with different ages Pore-scale facial features are non-contact and discriminative features for human identification. However, without a database with a large number of pore-to-pore correspondences, it is impossible to training a classifier for matching pore-scale features accurately, in particular for those deep-learning-based approaches. In this project, we have been creating a large pore-to-pore correspondences dataset, currently with the maximum age difference among the face images of the same subject being five years. The database contains 80,236 classes of matched pore pairs, produced by using the 3D face constraint. Each class contains the same pore keypoints from 4 face images of the same person with different poses and with different ages. This database should be very useful for the future research on face recognition based on pore-scale features.

15276516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15276516.value: In this project, we have investigated and proposed a number of face-recognition methods, in particular, those based on the pore-scale features for high-resolution face recognition. It is found that deep neural networks can be trained for the extraction of pore features, which can then be used for matching two face images. The matching is reliable, even if the face images have a large pose variation. In order to recognize face images, across different ages, encoding deep features at different ages, being projected into a coherent subspace by using canonical correlation analysis, can greatly improve the discriminant power of the resulting deep features. This approach can also be applied to recognize face images at different resolutions, in particular, for low-resolution face recognition. Furthermore, based on the database created by means of deep neural networks, we found that the trained features can achieve a better accuracy than those learned by using handcrafted features.

15276516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15276516.value: We will continue our research on face recognition, based on pore-scale features. Currently, we only use AlexNet, VGG-Face, etc., for extracting deep features for face recognition. We will further investigate the performance of our algorithms, with the use of other more advanced deep neural networks, such as ResNet, denseNet, etc. In our previous method, based on feature encoding, we considered the deep features, extracted from AlexNet and VGG-Face. We will test the use of deep pore-scale features for face recognition, and investigate methods to further enhance its robustness to age variations. One important task of the project is to create pore-scale features, across ages, for face recognition. We will continue to collect the face images of the subjects in the current database. Currently, the age differences between the face images of the same subject are, at most, only five years. This age difference will increase every year.

15276516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15276516.value: Face recognition across ages is a challenging task, because the facial appearance of a person may have significant differences, after a certain number of years. In this project, we consider the use of pore-scale features for face recognition, which can be detected and extracted, when the face images are of sufficiently high resolution. We have investigated two different deep neural networks to extract the pore-scale features, and a database of pore-to-pore correspondences has been created. This can greatly facilitate future research, using pore-scale features for face recognition. Furthermore, we have also devised an approach for face recognition, based on feature encoding. We encode the features, extracted from face images, and then, project the face images of different ages into a coherent subspace. This can generate discriminant features that can recognize face images, across ages, reliably and accurately. Based on the output from this project, automated face recognition can become more accurate for real-world applications.

15276716.label: Realisation of objectives
15276716.value: Objective 1: Signals with temporal structure are widespread in the engineering community. To reconstruct such nonwhite signals from heterogeneous observation data, a Bayesian blind source separation methodology embedding Gaussian Process (GP) prior (BBSS-GP) has been proposed. The proposed methodology is amenable to handling uncertainty and indeterminacy which have hindered full utilization of the common blind source separation techniques, and is able to explicitly estimate nonidentical noises stemming from different sensor locations. By embedding the GP prior into the Bayesian inference paradigm, the temporal correlation of each source signal is fully captured in the proposed method. A Gibbs-within-Metropolis sampling strategy in the MCMC context was explored to evaluate the posterior distributions and probabilistic characteristics of the sources, mixing matrix, and noise. The superiority of the proposed methodology was validated by comparing it with the conventional SOBI, FastICA, SC-BSS, and BSOS methods by use of numerical and real-world monitoring data. Based on second-order statistics blind separation (SOSBS), a data-driven blind excitation separation and structural feature extraction method for structures subjected to multiple periodic excitations has been proposed. Making use of response measurements under periodic excitations contaminated with noise, the number of excitation sources is identified by the eigenvalues of the correlation matrix of the measured responses. After converting the measurement space to eigenspace with identity covariance matrix and compacting the measurement dimension into independent source dimension, joint diagonalization for covariances with various time shifts is achieved to elicit the mixture feature. A change in the mixture feature matrix alarms the occurrence of structural anomaly or damage. The proposed method was verified by numerical simulation and experimental study. A methodology for the recovery of missing structural health monitoring (SHM) data using Bayesian multi-task learning (MTL) has been proposed. It is formulated to model multiple tasks collectively via a multivariate Gaussian Process (GP) prior, which results in a multi-task GP model (MTGPM) enabling the characterization of correlation among tasks; and the constructed MTGPM is executed to recover the missing data by invoking the shared information across tasks. The use of task-relatedness encoded by MTGPM generates better data reconstruction performance than learning each single task individually. The reconstruction capability of the proposed approach was verified by using real monitoring data acquired from a high-rise structure. Objective 2: While the proposed BBSS-GP methodology has proved to be highly efficient in a diversity of applications with linear instantaneous mixtures, difficulties arise in dealing with nonlinear mixture problems. Different from the steady-state dynamic responses of a structure subjected to single/multiple periodic excitations, the transient dynamic responses of a structure subjected to aperiodic excitations cannot be expressed as linear instantaneous mixtures of the time-varying excitations. To tackle this problem, a hierarchical fully Bayesian BSS-GP approach has been proposed. By decomposing the transient dynamic responses as a convolution product of the impulse response matrix and the external force vector and equivalently representing the convolution effect with the Hankel matrix in segment, we transform the convolution system into a linear system in terms of the so-called linear referenced source matrix and its mixing coefficients, and then the BBSS-GP method is hierarchically implemented in the transformed domain. The proposed hierarchical Bayesian BSS-GP approach was validated with numerical and experimental data. Another challenge arises in the non-stationary problems where source signals are potentially discontinuous (e.g., a source signal which intermittently appears or disappears over time). In such cases, the BBSS-GP and hierarchical fully Bayesian BSS-GP methods embedded with GP’s kernel functions are less satisfactory in performing source identification. To enable the applicability to nonstationary and discontinuous source problems, an improved BBSS-GP method was proposed by invoking a highly flexible time-varying kernel function and pursuing a sequential Metropolis-Hasting algorithm. The proposed method was verified with two real SHM-oriented applications: the multi-source extraction of strain data collected from a suspension bridge and the identification of local defects of train wheels from trackside online monitoring. As for health monitoring and fault diagnosis of general mechanical and structural systems, compressive sensing (CS) has been widely adopted to reduce the data amount. In comparison to rotary bearings or bolted joints in machines that operate in relatively steady working environments, high-speed trains (HSTs) run at varying speeds and the data amount is normally much larger, making it tricky to directly apply the classical CS methods in railway systems. Considering the lack of sparsity and long reconstruction time, we propose an adaptive CS approach for dynamic responses of HSTs by unrolling the iterative soft thresholding algorithm (ISTA) in deep learning and training it into a data reconstruction machine. The proposed approach was validated using real data collected from an HST in routine operation. Objective 3: A benchmark problem on blind source separation (BSS) for the purpose of SHM was developed by establishing a scaled physical model of a building structure. The tested structure is a five-story frame consisting of five steel floors and four steel columns firmly welded on each floor. The multiple dynamic excitations were generated by two electromagnetic exciters deployed at the first and fourth floors, respectively. The two exciters concurrently imposed dynamic forces to the structure, while laser displacement meters and accelerometers were deployed to measure structural dynamic responses. The stiffness reduction of steel columns was introduced to simulate structural damage at different severities. The structural dynamic responses at different damage scenarios were experimentally collected for BSS benchmark study. This testbed has been recognized as one of the SHM-oriented benchmark studies under the auspices of the International Society for Structural Health Monitoring of Intelligent Infrastructure (ISHMII). The proposed BBSS-GP method has been applied to the tested structure for separation and location identification of multiple dynamic excitations by using the measured dynamic responses. By implementing the proposed BBSS-GP method to the measured dynamic responses (the responses at certain floors were artificially polluted with additional noise to generate different noise levels), the estimated results of the sources, mixing matrix, and noises were obtained with satisfactory accuracy. The nonidentical noise variances are well identified, while the conventional SOBI and FastICA methods fail to estimate nonidentical noises. The results from the proposed method correctly indicate the locations of the two excitations even though they are identified from the responses contaminated with nonidentical noises. Both the GP-BSS method and the SOBI method achieve satisfactory results in reconstructing excitations, but the former performs better than the latter in reconstructing the second force. The FastICA method, although being able to obtain the two excitations, is much inferior to the GP-BSS method and the SOBI method in terms of identification accuracy. The proposed multiple-periodic excitation and structural anomaly identification technique based on SOSBS has been applied to the tested structure. In this study, two periodic excitations with different frequencies and amplitudes were concurrently applied to the tested structure on two floors. Using only the measured dynamic responses at three floors, the two periodic excitations as unknowns were accurately separated and identified. It is found that the extracted mixture matrix is more sensitive to stiffness reduction than modal frequencies, and the mixture features that represent local structural dynamic characteristics are effective to indicate structural damage. In addition, the variation of element values in the mixture matrix increases with the damage severity, and damage location can be determined through a synthetic analysis of the element variations.

15276716.label: Major findings and research outcome
15276716.value: 1. A Bayesian multi-task learning (MTL) methodology for reconstruction of structural health monitoring (SHM) data was developed. The proposed methodology stands to model a series of tasks simultaneously rather than modeling each task independently, while explicitly encoding the correlations among tasks that can be learned efficiently from data. The primary advantage of the proposed Bayesian MTL methodology for data reconstruction is that it makes more efficient use of the data available and gives rise to enhanced reconstruction capability by making use of the underlying task relatedness (Journal Paper No. 1); 2. A Bayesian blind source separation (BSS) method was developed for online wheel minor defect detection of high-speed trains through FBG-based wayside monitoring of rail track dynamic strains. Because Bayesian BSS outperforms the conventional BSS techniques in processing signals with temporal structure and quantifying measurement error/uncertainty, the proposed method is competent to decompose the raw signals and obtain useful features that are sensitive to subtle wheel defects (Journal Paper No. 3); 3. With the purpose of diminishing the effect of temperature on the piezoresistive property Self-sensing cementitious composite (SSCC), a Bayesian blind source separation method was developed to separate and reconstruct sources from the SSCC responses to simultaneous temperature and loading excitations. The proposed method has better performance than wavelet transform (WT) and polynomial fitting methods in terms of both accuracy and computational cost on the extraction of temperature-induced resistance variation (Journal Paper No. 4); 4. A technique for model-free identification of multiple periodic excitations and detection of structural anomaly using only response measurements was developed. In this technique, neither structural model nor measurement of excitations is required in this method, and the extracted mixture matrix representative of structural dynamic characteristics can be used for structural anomaly detection and damage diagnosis (Journal Paper No. 5); 5. An adaptive compressive sensing (CS) technique based on iterative soft thresholding algorithm (ISTA) in a deep learning (DL) paradigm was developed for collecting and manipulating dynamic responses of high-speed trains (HSTs). This technique was specifically proposed to handle vibration data which are less sparse (e.g., due to a wide range of varying running speeds of HSTs throughout the traveling mileage) and require high sampling rate (due to containing high-frequency ingredients) (Journal Paper No. 6).

15276716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15276716.value: The applications of the proposed Bayesian Blind Source Separation methods embedding Gaussian Process (GP) prior (BBSS-GP methods) to structural health monitoring (SHM) under various operational and environmental conditions would be further explored. In this project, the GP is utilized to convey the prior information of the patterns in source signals. The non-stationarity of intermittently discontinue signals popular in the SHM field has been well addressed in this project by the development of time-varying complex kernel functions. However, in the complex SHM problems, the nonstationary sources which we meet are not always intermittent, there exist other types of non-stationarities such as variational smoothness due to fatigue, varying-periodicity as a result of damage, and so on. To fulfill the real requirement in SHM, further investigations of nonstationary kernel functions should be pursued to enable capturing a variety of complicated non-stationarities in SHM-oriented problems.

15276716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15276716.value: The Blind Source Separation (BSS) aims to reconstruct n signals of sources and their mixing functions from m observations of mixtures. The word “blind” here indicates that the separation result of BSS is achieved based on the observation signal solely (output-only). Because BSS always starts with the results (observations) and tries to calculate reasons (sources), it can be viewed as an inverse problem that often suffers from the ill-posed inverse problem. To remedy these deficiencies, a novel Bayesian inference framework is proposed to solve the BSS problem. To characterize the temporal correlation of sources, the Gaussian Process (GP) is exploited by assuming that each source is a GP with a covariance function. By incorporating GP into the Bayesian BSS problem as the source prior distribution, the variation of both spatially and temporally statistical patterns in sources could be guaranteed, no matter whether the system is overdetermined or not. The behaviors of the proposed BBSS-GP methods were verified by both simulation and experimental studies. The proposed BBSS-GP methods were also applied to separate the thermal tendency and railway effect from real-world monitoring data collected from a long-span bridge and a high-speed train.

15276916.value: 由于城市化及工业化水平的快速提升，中国已经成为世界上最大的能源消耗国之一。其一次能源消耗量以及二氧化碳排放量分别占到全球排放总量的五分之一和四分之一左右。因此，中国正面临严峻的环境挑战。而建筑业，作为中国能源消耗的主要产业之一，占到了社会总能耗的26%左右。因此，有必要对中国建筑业的物化能耗进行系统和深入的研究。建筑项目物化能，是指建筑物建造过程的直接能耗与生产和提供与建筑活动相关产品以及服务的间接能耗的总和。 本研究旨在分别从国家、地区和项目层面来研究和计量中国建筑业的物化能耗。在国家层面，完成对建筑业总能耗的计量分析，并识别出导致建筑业能耗增加的主要驱动因素，从而在国家层面为建筑业的可持续发展提供改进方法及优化策略。在地区尺度，旨在系统分析和计量中国30个地区由于建筑活动而引发的地区间的能耗传递，并完成对中国建筑业上游产业链间接能耗投入的测算。地区分析的结果不仅可以分别从地区和部门角度极大提升对建筑业能耗流动的认识，还可以识别出在上游产业链中消耗较多能源的关键路径，从而达到促进区域建筑业节能减排，优化供应链路径的目的。在项目层面，将构件一个建筑物建造阶段能耗评估系统，旨在从建设项目立项或者建造初期，就能为指定建筑物提供一个初步能耗评估结果，从而在项目前期就能达到提升项目可持续性，促进项目清洁生产的目的。 在建筑业国家尺度的能耗分析中，结构分解分析法将用作计量和识别中国建筑业的能耗总量及关键驱动因素。在地区分析中，多区域投入产出分析模型将用来系统分析地区之间和部门之间由于建筑活动而引发的能耗传递。在对各个地区建筑业总能耗的计量过程中，还将考虑由于各个地区经济发展和建造水平不同而带来的建造能耗密度之间的差异。此外，本研究还将使用结构路径分析法来系统分析建筑业上游产业链间接能耗和关键路径。最后，本研究将构造一个考虑地区建造特点的建设项目能耗评估系统，包含三个概念模块，分别是各个地区经济部门能耗密度模块，建筑项目过程数据模块以及结构运算模块。 通过对不同尺度下建筑业能耗密度的分析，一方面可以对建筑业的能源消耗有一个更加全面深入的了解和认识，另一方面也可以使得决策者在不同的空间尺度下进行“假设分析”研究，从而使得在不同地区开展的节能减排政策更加具有针对性和公平性。

15276916.label: Realisation of objectives
15276916.value: Objective 1: Quantify the total embodied energy use in China’s construction sector and explore the driving forces behind the increase in energy use The total embodied energy use of China’s construction sector has been quantified and five driving factors have been identified, namely change in total energy intensity, change of energy structure, change of production structure, change in final demand volume, and structural change of final demand. The following specific tasks have been completed: • Quantify the total embodied energy consumption • Identify the most effective structural decomposition method • Review the major trends of the five driving factors for energy increments • Project the trajectory of energy increments in the construction sector • Examine the effect of sector aggregation Objective 2: Investigate the hidden energy connections among construction sectors from a multi-regional perspective The hidden linkages among regional construction sectors at the regional and sectoral levels have been quantified step by step. Firstly, embodiment analysis of the regional energy use and region division regarding different regional construction energy intensities has been conducted. Secondly, sectoral analysis with the identification of major sectoral contributors has been undertaken. Thirdly, by exploring energy transfers through inter-regional imports and exports, an overall distribution map of the total embodied energy use of regional construction sectors has been established. Objective 3: Decompose energy transmissions and identify critical energy paths in the entire supply chain from the sectoral and regional perspectives Systematic structural analysis has been conducted to quantify environmental shifting in the upstream process and to identify the important paths with the potential for energy saving by tracing the intricate production chain. The following tasks have been completed: • Design an optimized algorithm for multi-regional SPA • Extract energy-intensive paths throughout the upstream supply chain • Explore regional characteristics for regional construction sectors • Identify energy-intensive sectors hidden in the higher order of supply chain • Develop an effective strategy for narrowing the system boundary of SPA Objective 4: Develop a multi-scale system for assessing embodied energy consumption at the national, regional, and project level by integrating macro data and micro data The assessment system comprises four layers. The input layer contains the basic profile and material inventory data of the target project. The integration layer has three modules: the region-based sectoral energy intensity module, the process-based energy intensity module, and the computational structure module. The SEIM is the database of sectoral energy intensity calculated by MRIO; PBEIM is the database of process-based energy intensity data for primary energy-intensive construction items; and the CSM is the theoretical foundation for system operation. The energy assessment reports generated by the developed system provided an overview of the total energy consumption at the regional and sectoral level as well as effective energy reduction strategies for the target construction project.

15276916.label: Major findings and research outcome
15276916.value: The study quantified the total embodied energy use and explored the driving forces behind the energy use in China’s construction sector by conducting a structural decomposition analysis (SDA). A multi-regional input-output (MRIO) model has been employed to investigate the hidden linkages and the economic network among construction sectors and other economic sectors in various provinces in China by taking region-specific characteristics and technology differences into consideration. An optimized algorithm based on structural path analysis (SPA) has been designed to quantify indirect energy input to the upstream supply chain of the construction sector. A multi-regional system for assessing the embodied energy use in construction projects has been developed with three integrated modules: a region-based sectoral energy intensity module, a process-based energy intensity module, and a computational structure module. The system has been verified and validated in real cases through comparative and empirical analyses.

15276916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15276916.value: The multi-scale embodied energy assessment system will be an effective tool for comprehensively estimating embodied energy use and enable decision-makers at national, regional, and project levels to conduct what-if analyses and compare various scenarios before decisions are made. The regional analysis of energy flows through the supply chain will improve our understanding of energy use in the construction sector. In addition, recognizing the hidden linkage in the inter-regional trade of China’s construction sector will enable a holistic understanding of the current energy consumption status of regions, and also help policy-makers to develop fair and equitable energy reduction policies.

15276916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15276916.value: The study aimed to investigate and quantify embodied energy use at the national level, regional level, and project level. At the national level, the quantification of the total embodied energy use and identification of the driving forces provided an indication of potential barriers and the means of improving the development of sustainable construction. At the regional level, the systematic analysis of inter-regional energy transfers and the indirect energy inputs in the upstream supply chain of the construction sector not only improved the understanding of the overall energy flows among the regional construction sectors and other economic sectors, but also identified specific energy-intensive paths. At the project level, the embodied energy assessment system provided valuable information concerning preliminary embodied energy use at the early stage of a construction project, which can be used to assess the sustainability of a specific construction project and advance cleaner production in the construction sector.

15279216.label: Project Objectives
15279216.value: Study of micromechanics and SDBP in micro scaled deformation: The mechanics and deformation behaviors in micro-scaled plastic deformation are different from those in macro-scaled one. In this project, the first objective of studying the micromechanics of materials in micro-scaled plastic deformation is to predict the response of materials to deformation loading on the basis of the geometries and properties of grains and the deformation texture of materials. The second objective is to explore the localized deformation behaviors in the local deformation zones to study how they affect SDBP. From SDBP perspective, the scientific nature of SDBP will be delved via micro-scaled deformation experiment, including small-scaled micro-pillar compression in nano-indentation and large micro-scaled deformation experiments using tailor-made tooling and testing system. How to reduce SDBP will be systematically examined and studied. The final goal is to provide a scientific basis for study of UGID. Investigation of UGID formed in microparts: To fabricate quality microparts, UGID must be avoided or significantly reduced. The investigation of UGID must be conducted thoroughly and in-depth understanding of UGID needs to be completely established. Therefore, the classification of UGID will be done first and the detailed initiation and formation mechanisms of UGID will be investigated and identified. All the affecting factors will be figured out via physical experiment, measurement and finite element simulation. In addition, the correlation between SDBP and UGID will be established. The panorama, affecting factors and the detailed mechanisms of UGID will eventually be established. All of these will provide a scientific fundamental for development of methods to avoid or reduce UGID and further improve the dimensional accuracy, product quality and repeatability of microparts produced by micro-scaled plastic deformation. UGID avoidance and dimensional accuracy improvement: The eventual goal for addressing the eluded and tantalized issues of SDBP and UGID is to improve the dimensional accuracy of microformed parts. To reduce UGID and enhance dimensional accuracy, methods to improve the dimensional accuracy of microformed parts based on the fundamental and scientific understanding of SDBP and UGID will be developed. The methods need to be easily implemented in process determination, tooling design and process parameter configuration. By using the selected microforming processes as case study processes, the UGID avoidance and dimensional accuracy improvement will be systematically studied via physical experiment and finite element simulation in such a way to provide a basis for the large-scale application of this micromanufacturing technology and to fully leverage the established microforming knowledge in application.

15279216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15279216.value: In micro-scaled plastic deformation for making microparts, there exists size effect, which could induced some unique deformation behaviors and the scatters of these behaviors and further generate the undesirable geometries and inaccurate dimensions in the microparts produced via micro-scaled plastic deformation. All of these need to be extensively studied. The project has conducted extensive experiments, observations, measurements and simulations to examine the in-depth mechanisms of these induced behaviors and phenomena and studied the way to reduce the degree of the effects and negative impacts. The project generated informative results and developed the needed knowledge in terms of the understudying of phenomena, reduce the degree of the effects and negative impacts and possible ways avoid them.

15279616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15279616.value: 蠕变粘性土的固结沉降的计算一直是一个有着悠久历史的具有挑战性的问题。在对假说A（解耦方法），和假设B法（耦合方法）的问题进行讨论后，申请人提出了一种新的简化假设B法（解耦合法）用于粘土蠕变固结沉降计算。基于不同的应力 - 应变状态的“等效时间”的概念，推导出这种方法主要方程。这种新的简化假设B法可用于计算一维（1-D）固结沉降。使用这种新方法，所有计算可以用手或电子数据表来完成。为了验证这种新方法，申请人将建一个大型物理模型，用于香港海洋粘土试验。此外，两个有限元程序将使用弹粘塑性构模型来验证新的简化的误差范围， 并与物理模型试验结果比较。从这些分析和比较，新的简化假设B法将被验证。 该项目的目标是： •要开发一个新的简化假设B法（解耦方法） 用于蠕变粘性固结沉降计算。 •建立一个大型物理模型，并就香港海洋粘土试验（数据将用来检验新方法）。 •要使用两个有限元程序分析黏性土固结沉降（结果将被用来检查新方法和误差范围）。 •使用物理模型试验数据和现场数据来验证新的简化假设B法，并检查误差范围。

15279616.label: Realisation of objectives
15279616.value: All objectives have been well achieved. More than 10 SCI journal papers have been published. These objectives have been achieved through the original plan: elemental lab tests, physical model tests, development of new simplified Hypothesis B method considering different drainage conditions, validations by existing finite element program, physical model tests and real data from in-situ measurement, and publications of papers. 1. A new simplified method (de-coupled method) was developed for calculating consolidation settlements of a soft soil layer without or with vertical drains for different drainage conditions and stress-strain states. 2. A large-size physical model was built in the Soil Lab of HK PolyU. A series of model tests was conducted on HKMC without or with vertical drains and complicated stress histories. The data of physical model tests was used to validate the new method through comparing the prediction results from new method with the results from both measured data and a fully coupled finite element computer program with an Elastic Visco-Plastic (EVP) model. 3. The data from real projects were well identified. The new simplified method was applied for calculating long-term settlement of real project. At the same time, a fully coupled finite element computer program with an EVP model and Hypothesis A method were used to calculate the consolidation settlements of the same projects. Based on the comparison of all data, it is demonstrated that the new simplified method is much better than the Hypothesis A method and has good accuracy for all the situations analyzed in this study.

15279616.label: Major findings and research outcome
15279616.value: A new simplified Hypothesis B method (de-coupled method) for calculation of consolidation settlement of a clayey soil exhibiting creep without or with vertical drains for different drainage conditions has been proposed. Good data have been obtained from lab elementary tests to understand the time-dependent stress-strain behaviour of HKMD. The physical model with all necessary instrumentation has functioned well to investigate the consolidation behaviour of HKMD with or without vertical drains (VD). The data from physical model tests well validated the performance of the new simplified method. On the other hand, field data have been collected to verify the newly-developed model. With the use of the results from the fully-coupled finite element analysis as the reference, the new simplified method offers a good estimation of the settlement for all the real cases and outperforms the Hypothesis A method in terms of accuracy.

15279616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15279616.value: The works in this project will have great applications for "Lantau Tomorrow" reclamation project and other possible reclamation projects in "Greater Bay Area".

15279616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15279616.value: Many civil engineering structures are constructed on clay soils or soft soil ground. Settlements are a big concern to the safety and functioning of these structures. Vertical band drains plus pre-loading (VD+PL) is being used to improve soft marine soils underneath the reclaimed lands. The third runway in Hong Kong is under construction now with reclamation on the Hong Kong marine deposits (HKMD) in seabed without dredging. A new simplified method that is based on rigorous scientific concepts and easy-to-use for practical engineers is urgently needed. The new method should be capable of considering different drainage conditions. The study completed in this project will not only have significant academic values and new developments , but also make contributions to solving the urgent problem in the analysis and prediction of settlements of highway pavements and the third airport runway in Hong Kong where vertical drains were installed.

15280116.value: 基于先进连续体模型的可扩展综合公共交通运输网络优化设计方法研究

15280116.label: Project Objectives
15280116.value: Develop parsimonious, advanced continuum models for optimally designing integrated transit networks with novel network structure, differentiated modes, service schemes, and innovative access means. Incorporate spatial heterogeneity and elasticity in demand into advanced continuum models. Develop models for designing scalable transit network that evolves optimally in response to long-term changes in demand, city form, and land-use pattern. Apply the models to real cities including Hong Kong. Formulate a new set of practical guidelines for transit network designing.

15280116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15280116.value: Public mass transit systems in megacities (e.g. Hong Kong) serve millions of daily trips, and can shape the spatial form and economic growth of those cities in the longer run. Regrettably, however, the literature on optimal designs of those transit networks offers little guidance to the practice, and the practice still uses suboptimal and myopic methods for transit network designing. In light of this, we propose to bridge the gap between theory and practice by developing advanced network optimization models that are parsimonious and computationally efficient. Models to be developed belong to the so-called “continuum” models, which employs smooth, continuous functions (e.g., for line and stop spacing, and demand density) to approximate numerous parameters and variables that describe local irregularities and constraints of real networks. To furnish a recipe for real-world applications, a number of idealized assumptions of present continuum models will be relaxed. We will further advance the frontier of continuum models in this realm by incorporating: novel network structure and access means, differentiated transit modes and service schemes, spatial heterogeneity and elasticity in demand, and long-term changes in demand, city form, and land-use pattern. By solving a number of key research questions, the developed models will unveil a number of new insights into the cause-and-effect relations between the optimal design and the inputs, and the trade-offs between different cost components imparted to users and the agency. The theoretical designs will be adapted to street networks of real cities including Hong Kong. Through this process we expect to verify the accuracy and applicability of our models when more idealized approximations are relaxed. We also expect to identify a set of empirical rules that can inform practice. Specifically, the application of our models to Hong Kong will unveil how the existing transit network can evolve to best serve the city under the changing operating environment and the specific government policies for transportation and land-use planning. All this will be summarized into a set of practical guidelines that can be used by practitioners for better transit network designing. The methods and guidelines derived in this project will be applicable to a wide range of cities with distinct features, and will furnish cost-effective transit solutions that are competitive with private cars. 大城市（例如香港）的公共交通运输系统每日客流达到数百万。公交网络对于城市未来的空间形态和经济发展有着十分重要的影响。然而遗憾的是，当前在公交网络优化设计领域的学术文献对于实际工程并未起到充分的指导作用，而现实中的公交线网设计往往仍然遵循一些短视、次优的方法与原则。据此，本项目将研发简约而高效的“连续体”公交网络优化模型，以在理论与工程实际之间建立桥梁。连续体模型通过平滑连续的近似函数来表示公交线路和站点间距、需求密度等关键因素，从而取代实际情形中代表道路与公交网络局部细节与约束的海量参数与变量。 为了最终形成可用于实际的一套完整方法，现有连续体模型的许多理想化假设将被放开。同时，我们还将引入更多实际网络的复杂性，包括新的网络结构与接驳方式，多种公交技术与运营组织方式的混合应用，空间异质性，弹性公交需求，以及需求、城市形态和用地模式上的长期演变。这些复杂性问题的解决将推动该领域的学术前沿，并能揭示更多深层次的发现，包括最优网络设计与各关键因素之间的关系，以及使用者和公交运营机构所承担的各项成本之间的关系等。 项目中取得的理论成果将被应用于实际城市（包括香港）的道路网络。通过这些应用，我们将检验理论模型的准确性和实际应用能力。同时我们也将通过这些实际应用的结果总结出一系列对工程实际有指导作用的经验规则，特别是现有的公交网络应通过何种演化途径以最好地服务于社会环境不断改变的城市，以及政府关于交通与用地规划的政策应如何制定。 以上这些将被总结成一套实际应用指南，以帮助公交线网的规划师/设计师进行更好的网络系统设计。本项目所研发的方法将能应用于范围广泛的多种城市，其所实现的最优设计将提高公交系统的性能，以形成与私家车等对环境不友好的交通方式的竞争。

15280116.label: Realisation of objectives
15280116.value: Objective 1. Develop parsimonious, advanced continuum models for optimally designing integrated transit networks with novel network structure, differentiated modes, service schemes, and innovative access means. The above models have been developed for transit networks with: (i) novel network structure like intersecting network (Part C, Q8, paper 1) and hybrid structure (Part C, Q8, paper 3); (ii) differentiated modes like local/express transit modes (Part C, Q8, papers 1 and 5); (iii) novel service schemes like skip-stop service (Part C, Q8, paper 2; Q9, papers 2 and 3); and (iv) innovative access means like shared bicycles (Part C, Q8, papers 3 and 5). Objective 2. Incorporate spatial heterogeneity and elasticity in demand into advanced continuum models. Demand heterogeneity, route/mode choice, and elasticity have been incorporated into the models; please see Part C, Q8, papers 1-3, 5, and Q9, papers 2-4. Objective 3. Develop models for designing scalable transit network that evolves optimally in response to long-term changes in demand, city form, and land-use pattern. Optimal transit network designs involving temporal demand, city size, and land-use pattern changes were studied for a linear city in a conference paper (Part C, Q9, paper 4). Objective 4. Apply the models to real cities including Hong Kong. Real-world case studies of our design models have been performed for skip-stop and local-express networks, see the PhD thesis titled "Optimal design of skip-stop transit service in a corridor under heterogeneous demand" (Part C, Q10, item 1), and journal/conference papers (Part C, Q8, paper 5; Q9, papers 3-4). Objective 5. Formulate a new set of practical guidelines for transit network designing. Practical guidelines for the design of various transit networks have been summarized in journal/conference papers (Part C, Q8, papers 1-3, 5; Q9, papers 1-4), as well as a PhD thesis (Part C, Q10, item 1). In addition, with the support of this project, we also developed continuum approximation models for another type of transportation system optimization (asset management) problems; see Part C, Q8, paper 4 and Q10, item 2 (Chapter 3).

15280116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15280116.value: 1. We find that an intersecting bimodal transit network design can outperform single-mode designs and trunk-feeder designs, and that the conventional practice of designing the local and express networks separately would greatly undermine the benefit of the bimodal system. (Part C, Q8, paper 1). 2. We find efficient methods to optimize special and general forms of skip-stop services, and find that those services outperform all-stop services in a variety of cases, especially when travel demands are high, trip origins are unevenly distributed along a corridor, and patrons have relatively high values of time. (Part C, Q8, paper 2; Q9, paper 2; Q10, item 1). 3. We find that integrating shared-bike systems with a transit network can often reduce costs over walking alone, even when the shared bikes are made to fit a pre-existing transit network. Shared-biking often outperforms feeder-bus service as well. And the joint optimization of trunk transit and shared-bike feeder services can reduce costs not only to users, but also to the transit agency that operates these services. Savings to the agency can be used to subsidize shared-bike services. (Part C, Q8, papers 3 and 5; Q9, paper 1). 4. We show that optimally designed local-express systems also outperform all-stop systems. (Part C, Q9, paper 3). 5. We show that integrating lane-use pattern change would significantly affect the optimal transit network design, and that transit mode has a strong impact on the long-term development patterns. (Part C, Q9, paper 4). 6. We proposed efficient methods for developing optimal designs for real-world transit systems. (Part C, Q8, papers 3 and 5; Q9, papers 2-3). 7. We developed methods for incorporating transit patrons' mode and route choices into the optimal network design (Part C, Q8, papers 1, 3, 5; Q9, paper 3). 8. We developed continuum approximation method for the vehicle fleet management optimization problem. (Part C, Q8, paper 4; Q10, item 2).

15280116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15280116.value: Built upon the present achievements from this project, we will further develop: (i) optimal trunk-feeder transit network under heterogeneous demand; (ii) optimal intersecting transit network under heterogeneous demand; (iii) optimal transit network fed by flexible transit or mobility services; (iv) optimal realistic transit networks that involve multiple transit modes (e.g., local and express), feeder modes (e.g., bikes, fixed- and flex-route feeder buses, scooters), and so on; (v) novel transit network designs with connected and autonomous transit vehicles. These future developments will be conducted through applying for new GRF and CRF projects. In addition, we will also seek to implement our ideas in real cities, by collaborating with local transit planning and management agencies. This may be conducted by applying for ITF projects.

15280116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15280116.value: We have developed advanced continuum models for optimally designing novel transit networks. These novel networks are more efficient and realistic, and some are ready for implementation. New features we incorporate in the project include local and express transit services, skip-stop services, novel feeder services like shared bikes and scooters, etc. They can address realistic, spatially heterogeneous transit demand, patrons' individual choices between transit routes and modes, and long-term interactions with land-use patterns. The models are validated and tested by data collected from real transit systems. Practical guidelines for transit network designing are summarized.

15301616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301616.value: 線性互補問題稀疏解的分析、計算及應用

15301616.label: Project Objectives
15301616.value: We will develop innovative theory for uniqueness and stability of sparse solutions of the LCP with respect to different classes of matrices in the LCP by using the theory of polyhedral multifunctions and the matrix theory in the LCP. Moreover, we will extend the theory for sparse solutions of a system of linear equations and linear inequalities to sparse solutions of the LCP. We will formulate the problem of finding sparse solutions of the LCP as constrained optimization problems where the objective function is the discontinuous cardinality function and the constraint is a system of equations defined by global Lipschtz continuous functions. We will derive new necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for a local optimal solution with suitable constraint qualifications. We will use continuous functions to approximate the objective function and establish graphical convergence of the approximated solutions when the continuous approximation objective function approaches to the original function. We will develop efficient sparse optimization methods for finding sparse solutions or sparse enough solutions of the LCP. We will provide lower and upper bounds for the sparsity of optimal solutions. We will derive global convergence theorems and complexity analysis. We will develop smoothing methods for the optimization problem with the discontinuous objective function and nonsmooth equations in the constraints. We will use the special structure of these functions to construct smoothing functions for both the objective function and the constraint function with desirable properties regarding the consistency of the KKT conditions and convergence of the algorithms. We will conduct comprehensive numerical experiments to test the efficiency and robustness of our theory and algorithms. Moreover, we will compare our codes with some state-of-the-art codes in the terms of sparsity and accuracy of the computed solutions. We will apply our theory and algorithms to sparse portfolio selection based on real strategies, schemes and data in financial information systems. Moreover, we will study the computation of sparse solutions arising from large transportation network systems.
