15301616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301616.value: The linear complementarity problem (LCP) presents optimality conditions of linear and quadratic programming, and has many important applications in engineering and economics. Moreover the LCP is the foundation of the broad subject of equilibrium programming. Theory, algorithms and applications of the LCP have been extensively studied for decades. However, in contrast to the fast development in sparse solutions of linear equations and linear inequalities in signals and image processing, sparse solutions of the LCP seem to lack theory and algorithms. When the LCP has infinitely many solutions, decision makers have to choose a particular element in the solution set. A sparse solution of the LCP is by definition a solution that has the fewest nonzero entries. Finding sparse solutions of the LCP has attracted significant attention in various fields and has an increasing number of practical applications in finance and economics. A typical example is portfolio selection. Sparsity is important for investors who often want to select a limited number of assets for their investment. Moreover, due to the online retail booms in recent years, the interest in sparse inbound flows has rapidly increased in the management of inventory for online retailers. The Markowitz portfolio selection and linear network flow optimization in trasportation network design can be formulated as LCPs. The study of sparse solutions of the LCP involves many challenges, since it is impossible to have a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for a general LCP and the solution set of the LCP is not necessarily convex. Motivated by numerous applications of sparse solutions of the LCP, in this project, we will develop innovative theory and efficient algorithms for the computation of sparse solutions of the LCP. We will derive new necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniqueness and stability of sparse solutions of the LCP and estimation for the cardinality of sparse solutions using special geometry properties of the solution set and theory in polyhedral multifunctions. Moreover, we will develop efficient algorithms for finding sparse solutions via continuous approximations. We will establish convergence theorems of the algorithms and error bounds for solutions of the continuous approximation problem to the sparse solution. We will apply our theory and algorithms to portfolio selection and transportation network design. The outcomes of this project will have long-term high impact, because sparse solutions of the LCP arise naturally in numerous applications and our theory and algorithms will provide urgently needed what for these applications. 線性互補問題可以用於表示線性或二次規劃問題的最優性條件，在工程與經濟學領域中有著廣泛的應用。此外，線性互補問題還是壹大類均衡問題的基礎。有關線性互補問題的理論、算法和應用在最近二十年間已經被廣泛的研究。然而，相對於線性等式方程組和線性不等式方程組的稀疏解在信號處理和圖像處理中的快速發展，線性互補問題的稀疏解缺乏相應的理論和算法。 當線性互補問題有無限多個解時，決策者需要決定選取解集中特定的壹個解。線性互補問題的壹個稀疏解是解集中非0元素最少的解。尋找線性互補問題的稀疏解在多個領域得到了重視，並且在經濟和金融學領域中的有著廣泛的實際應用。其中壹個應用是投資組合問題。稀疏性對於那些希望只選擇有限只資產投資的投資者非常重要。另外，由於在線零售業近年來的發展，在庫存管理方面，在線零售業者對於稀疏采購流的關註在近年來急速增長。而Markowitz投資組合問題和交通網絡設計中的線性網絡流優化問題(linear network flow optimization)都可以表示為線性互補問題。 線性互補問題的稀疏解的研究面臨著很多挑戰。壹方面是由於對於壹般的線性互補問題，無法找到全多項式時間的逼近問題；另壹方面是由於線性互補問題的解集不壹定是凸的。由於線性互補問題的稀疏解有著廣泛的應用，在這個項目中，我們將針對線性互補問題的稀疏解，研究新的理論和有效的算法。我們將研究線性互補問題稀疏解的唯壹性和穩定性的新的充分必要條件，並利用線性互補問題解集特殊的幾何性質和多面體多值函數(polyhedral multifunctions)的理論估計稀疏解集的勢。進壹步，我們通過連續逼近方法，研究求稀疏解的有效算法。我們將建立算法的收斂性理論和由連續逼近問題得到的解的誤差界分析。我們將我們的理論和算法應用於投資組合問題和交通網絡設計問題。由於線性互補問題的稀疏解是從壹系列實際問題中自然產生並迫切需要解決的，而我們的理論和算法正好解決了這些應用對於稀疏解迫切的需求，所以該項目的成果將在長時間內有著很高的影響力。

15301616.value: Sparse solution to the linear complementarity problem (LCP) has many important applications in engineering and economics. A typical example is the portfolio selection. Sparsity is important for investors who often want to select a limited number of assets for their investment. Moreover, due to online retial booms in recent years, the interest in sparse inbound flows has been rapidly increased in the management of inventory for online retailers. The Markowitz portfolio selection and network flow optimization problems can be formulated as the LCP. Motivated by numerous applications of sparse solutions of the LCP, we developed innovative theory and efficient algorithms for sparse solutions of the LCP. We derived new necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of sparse solutions of the LCP and estimation for the cardinality of sparse solutions. Moreover, we developed efficient algorithms for finding sparse solutions via continuous approximations. Our theory and algorithms can be applied to sparse portfolio selection and sparse transportation network design. The outcomes of this project will have long-term, high impact, and provide urgently needed for many applications in economics and enginerring.

15301716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301716.value: 在这亇项目中，我们将对四种重要的张量，即弱对称张量，双对称张量，协正张量和PF张量進行广泛研究。我们计划研讨许多偶数階对称张量的易检査的半正定性条件对偶数階弱对称张量，循环对称张量，弱双对称张量和双对称张量是否还成立。我们将用外積來定义双对称和弱双对称平方和张量，並研讨希尔伯特理论是否对这样定义的平方和张量还对。我们将对协正张量和严格协正张量研讨可检查的充分条件，谱性质和计算检验法。我们将引入PF张量，建立由PF张量所定义的张量互补問题的全局唯一性和可解性，研究PF张量的值域，它们和P张量的关系，以及在解张量互补問题祘法收敛性分析中的应用。

15308516.label: Project Objectives
15308516.value: Extend existing methods for convex feasibility problems to solve nonconvex feasibility problems, and study their global convergence properties. This can enhance the understanding of some important existing algorithms in diverse areas such as phase retrieval and system realization that do not yet have convergence guarantee. 15308516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15308516.value: In this proposal, the PI and his coworkers will study new approaches for solving a class of nonconvex feasibility problems. These problems arise in a wide range of applications including sensor network localization, phase retrieval and system realization from the control community. They are typically in large scale, involving millions of variables. Feasibility problem is a classical topic and has been studied extensively in the convex setting. However, the nonconvex case considered in the current project only receives attention recently and the results obtained so far are very limited. The research in this project will be conducted along two directions. On the one hand, we will extend existing algorithms for solving convex feasibility problems to the nonconvex setting, and analyze the global convergence property. This is done by exploiting the property of the Douglas-Rachford merit function, which was used in analyzing convergence of the Douglas-Rachford splitting method in the nonconvex setting in the recent work by the PI and the co-I. This will lead to new globally convergent algorithms for solving nonconvex feasibility problems. On the other hand, we will explore convergence rate of the extended algorithms in the nonconvex settings. An understanding of the convergence rate will enable the design of innovative acceleration and initialization strategies to speed up the convergence and improve the solution quality. 本項目將研究非凸可行性問題的新解法。 非凸可行性問題常見於傳感器網絡定位、相位恢復及系統識別等應用。 此類問題規模龐大，可涉及上百萬變量。儘管凸可行性問題已被廣泛研究，本項目探討的非凸可行性問題只在最近為人注意，且當前成果有限。本項目將循兩大方向研究：首先，我們會透過研究Douglas-Rachford價值函數試圖將求解凸可行性問題的方法推廣至非凸可行性問題，以期設計非凸可行性問題的新解法；另外，我們亦會分析算法的收斂速度。研究成果將有助制定新算法的初始與加速方案。

15308516.label: Realisation of objectives
15308516.value: One of the goals of this project is to extend existing methods for convex feasibility problems to solve nonconvex feasibility problems, study their global convergence properties, and then design new globally convergent algorithms in some application areas. In this regard, we first studied in “A successive difference-of-convex approximation method for a class of nonconvex nonsmooth optimization problems” an algorithm that is able to deal with nonconvex multiple set feasibility problems and their generalizations. Our methodology combines classical splitting methods (that have been well studied for convex feasibility problems) and the observation that a certain penalty function is a difference-of-convex (DC) function. Our method is largely based on a penalty approach with each subproblem solved by some variants of the DC algorithm, exploiting the DC structure. The work was initiated during an academic visit of Professor Akiko Takeda from University of Tokyo, who then became a coauthor of the paper. We discussed various applications including fused LASSO problems in signal processing and the identification of simultaneous sparse and low rank structures in clustering problems. This work was presented at INFORMS International Conference in 2018. Next, to address the goal concerning contemporary application areas, we considered in “A nonmonotone alternating updating method for a class of matrix factorization problems” a new efficient algorithm for solving nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) problems. NMF is an important class of problems that arise in various applications such as face / landscape feature recognition. Finding meaningful nonnegative factorization of matrices is in general hard. During the development of this work, Professor Nicolas Gillis from University of Mons (a world leading expert in NMF) was invited to visit PolyU. His suggestions were acknowledged at the end of the paper. This work was presented at SIAM Conference on Applied Linear Algebra in 2018 and a local workshop, and formed part of the PhD thesis of Dr Lei Yang, a former student of the PI (the PI acted as a co-advisor). In summary, we have extended some existing methods for convex feasibility problems to solve nonconvex multiple set feasibility problems, and investigated applications such as NMF. The other aim of the project is to explore local convergence rate of algorithms in the nonconvex settings, which may then help design acceleration strategies to speed up the convergence and improve the solution quality. In this regard, we studied in a recent paper “A difference-of-convex approach for split feasibility with applications to matrix factorizations and outlier detection” a new splitting method for a large class of nonconvex feasibility problems. Our investigation was based on difference-of-convex decompositions. We introduced line-search strategies to accelerate our algorithm, and also discussed local convergence rate of the algorithm under standard assumptions in the literature such as linear regularity of a suitable pair of sets, and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of a suitable potential function. We applied our algorithm to various applications such as completely positive matrix factorization, sparse matrix factorization and outlier detections. This study was initiated when the third author, Dr Lulin Tan from South China Normal University, was invited to visit PolyU. The collaboration was reinforced during an academic visit to South China Normal University, supported by this project. The first author of this paper was an MPhil student of Dr Tan. Local convergence rate and acceleration strategies were also studied in “Iteratively reweighted l1 algorithms with extrapolation”. The paper discussed 3 different types of acceleration techniques that can be used for accelerating first-order methods. Moreover, to deal with convergence issue, one potential function was introduced for analyzing each of the extrapolation strategies studied in the paper. Local convergence was then established by imposing Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumptions on these potential functions. This work formed part of the MPhil thesis of Peiran Yu, a graduate student of the PI (as the chief advisor). In short, we have looked into local convergence rate of algorithms and acceleration strategies to speed up the convergence and improve solution quality.

15308516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15308516.value: Four journal papers are published as research outcome of this project. The first paper is “A successive difference-of-convex approximation method for a class of nonconvex nonsmooth optimization problems”, which was reported as a preprint in the midterm progress report. This paper deals with multiple possibly nonconvex set feasibility problems and their generalizations, with applications to signal processing. The investigation is based on difference-of-convex representations. The second paper is “A nonmonotone alternating updating method for a class of matrix factorization problems”, which was also reported as a preprint in the midterm progress report. It studied feasibility issues related to a contemporary application: the nonnegative matrix factorization problems. These problems arise in many important applications such as face / landscape feature recognition, and are highly nonconvex problems. The third paper is “Iteratively reweighted l1 algorithms with extrapolation”, which deals more with acceleration techniques that can help accelerate algorithms in the nonconvex settings. Techniques developed can then be used to accelerate methods for feasibility problems. Finally, a recent paper “A difference-of-convex approach for split feasibility with applications to matrix factorizations and outlier detection” is published. The paper utilized a difference-of-convex based approach to design new splitting methods for a large class of nonconvex feasibility problems, and discussed local convergence rate of the algorithms under standard assumptions in the feasibility problem literature. Results in “A nonmonotone alternating updating method for a class of matrix factorization problems” were presented at SIAM Conference on Applied Linear Algebra in 2018, and results in “A successive difference-of-convex approximation method for a class of nonconvex nonsmooth optimization problems” were presented at INFORMS International Conference in 2018.

15308516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15308516.value: There are several avenues for potential further development. For example, for many specially structured sets, their projections are not available and only some proxy can be computed. Then it is interesting to see whether the algorithms developed and studied in this project can be generalized to this setting and whether convergence can be derived.

15308516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15308516.value: The PI and his coworkers developed and analyzed new approaches for some nonconvex feasibility problems and their generalizations that arise in contemporary applications such as signal processing and matrix factorizations: the latter problems arise in important areas such as feature recognition. On the one hand, we extended some classical approaches for convex feasibility problems to solve nonconvex ones by exploiting difference-of-convex structure, and established global convergence. On the other hand, we looked at local convergence rate analysis based on Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property, and studied various acceleration techniques. The methodology developed in this project can encourage the proposal and study of feasibility-based models in all the aforementioned application fields.

15309416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15309416.value: 氧化物異質結因其所具有的電子自旋性、超導、巨磁阻等豐富的物理特性，以及作為電子元器件的巨大應用前景，吸引了全球科研工作者的廣泛興趣和關注。大量理論計算和實驗數據表明，基於LaAlO3/SrTiO3 異質節界面的二維電子氣(LAO/STO 2DEG)和擁有因極化引起的阻變特性的鐵電隧穿隧道結，兩者獨有的物理性能皆源於其特殊的界面結構。這些因界面結構而產生的不同於傳統塊材或薄膜材料的物理性能，使LAO/STO二維電子氣和鐵電隧穿隧道結均成為研究的熱點。在過往的大量研究中，科研人員通過對界面結構和成分等的控制，實現了對這些氧化物異質結的物理性能的調控。其中，通過不同晶格系數的基片與外延生長的STO層之間的晶格不匹配，改變其原有晶格系，進而改LAO/STO變界面二維電子氣輸運性質研究，成為這一領域的典型案例。然而，這種通過晶格不匹配度將機械應力引入LAO/STO的方法是靜態的，因此限制了對這一結構因動態機械拉伸或壓縮而產生的應變物理性質。除此之外，例如原子相互擴散等復雜的物理現象，都可能成為主導實驗結果的變量，使我們無法准確地對LAO/STO因機械應力而產生的應變進行研究。在本工作計劃當中，磁致伸縮材料和實驗樣品之間的機械耦合的方法將被應用於對LAO/STO因機械應力而產生的動態變化的研究中。這一方法，不僅可以給這一氧化物異質結提供一個動態的機械應力，更可以控制該應力的方向，進而可以在界面上實現不同於晶格不匹配引起的各向同性（雙向）應力的另一種各向異性（單向）的應力調控。晶體界面對稱性的改變可能破壞電子能帶結構的對稱性，並導致電子遷移率在兩個面內方向的不同變化。這種動態應力調節可以作為一個得力的工具被應用在其他氧化物異質節當中，並由此研究其在單一方向應力下的各向異性的輸運性質的改變。 按照此項目計劃，我們將重點研究LAO/STO界面在應力狀態下輸運性質的改變。以下幾方面將作為主要研究方向：（1）不同LAO/STO樣品在不同溫度下，因機械應力而產生的輸運性質的改變，例如不同LAO層厚度或樣品生長所處氧分壓的影響；（2）機械應力和其他可能影響LAO/STO界面性質的因素之間的相互作用和耦合，例如STO 的相變或背柵效應。（3）基於第一性原理計算對應力狀態下的LAO/STO界面的理論模型的研究。 我們在這一研究項目中，不僅可以深化對氧化物界面二維電子氣的理解，這一方法的實現更有助於推進所有其他氧化物材料的研究。這一理念還可以被應用在二維材料等科研領域，將給科研工作者們提供一條全新的途徑對材料進行更加深入的分析，並使得新興電子元器的設計和制造都有了更大想象空間和可能性。

15309416.label: Realisation of objectives
15309416.value: 1. By inducing a strain gradient to theLAO/STO heterostructure, large electrical transport modulation to the interfacial 2DEG has been realized. This result illustrates how the uniaxial strain can influence the complex oxide interface-based electronic devices. This objective has been fully achieved. 2. Deeper understanding to strain effect on transport properties of polar oxide heterostructures has been fully achived. This dynamic strain engineering gives rise to an efficient modulation of ON/OFF ratio due to the variation of BaTiO3 polarization. This result sheds light on the mechanism of electroresistance in the ferroelectric tunnel junctions by providing direct evidence for polarization-induced resistive switching, and also provides another stimulus for memory state operation. 3. To visualize interplay between the dynamic strain and other factors such as spin, domain structure and phase change etc. in this oxide heterostructures. This effect has been observed in multiferroic tunnel junction of NiFe/BaTiO3/LaSrMnO3. 4. To adopt this method to other oxide heterostructures such as ferroelectric oxide tunneling junctions and to understand the ferroelastic effect on the resistive switching. By introducing polarized BaTiO3 thin films, this dynamic strain method has been extended to the study of ferroelectric tunneling junction.

15309416.label: Major findings and research outcome
15309416.value: We have demonstrated dynamic strain modulation on tunneling electroresistance in a four-unit-cell ultrathin BaTiO3 metal/ferroelectric /semiconductor tunnel junction by applying mechanical stress to the device. With an extra compressive strain induced by mechanical stress, which is dynamically applied beyond the lattice mismatch between the BaTiO3 layer and the Nb : SrTiO3 substrate, the ON/OFF current ratio increases significantly up to a record high value of 10^7, whereas a mechanical erasing effect can be observed when a tensile stress is applied. This dynamic strain engineering gives rise to an efficient modulation of ON/OFF ratio due to the variation of BaTiO3 polarization. This result sheds light on the mechanism of electroresistance in the ferroelectric tunnel junctions by providing direct evidence for polarization-induced resistive switching, and also provides another stimulus for memory state operation.

15309416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15309416.value: This method by introducing dynamic strain will be further extended to the study of advanced materials such as 2D materials and devices using 2D materials.

15309416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15309416.value: In this proposed project, we have studied interfacial strain effect on the transport properties of oxide heterostructures LaAlO3/SrTiO3 two dimensional electron gas and ferroelectric tunnel junction oxide heterostructure. We have demonstrated strain effect modulation to the transport properties on the samples with different LaAlO3 film thicknesses and on the samples with different growth oxygen pressures. The coupling and interplay between the strain effect and other factors such as the ferroelectricity has been revealed.

15315216.value: 探究金屬卡賓之催化結合反應及有機手性合成之應用

15315216.label: Project Objectives
15315216.value: To develop a chiral pi-arene ligand library by modular synthesis: We will prepare the cyclopentadienyl and the arene cores from readily available materials involving straightforward synthetic steps. Chiral arenes can be prepared by covalently connecting the arene cores to chiral scaffolds such as functionalized chiral biaryls. Chiral arene ligands with varying electronic and steric properties will be examined for desirable catalytic activities. To develop enantioselective functionalization of metallacyclic enolate complexes of late transition metals en route to catalytic multicomponent carbenoid coupling reactions: We will focus our study on enantioselective functionalization of the metallaenolate complexes of cyclopentadienylrhodium(III) /arene-ruthenium(II) complexes. Employing the chiral pi-arene ligands developed here, reaction of these metallacyclic complexes with some electrophilic reagents including fluorinating reagents will be tested for asymmetric functionalization. To explore the reactivity of metallacyclic sigma-alkyl complexes of late transition metals for oxidative coupling reactions: We considered electrophilic functionalization of metallacyclic sigma-alkylrhodium complexes would be a fruitful approach to effect C-C and C-X bond formations at the quaternery stereocenter. We will prepare and structurally characterize some metallacyclic sigma-alkylrhodium complexes via coupling with diazocarbonyl compounds, and their reactivity toward a series of electrophiles such as N-haloamines will be examined. In particular, reactivity of sigma-alkylrhodacyclic complexes with haloalkanes will be examined for C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation.

15315216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15315216.value: 多组分卡賓交叉偶聯反應是一類高效構建官能團化季碳中心的方法，然而，由于金屬中間體非常易于發生β位氫消除副反應，目前報道的成功例子還非常少。我們研究發現，重氮羰基化合物和铑(III)/钌(II)催化劑通過卡賓遷移插入得到金属環烯醇絡合物中間體，這些中間體不易于發生β位氫消除反應，可以進一步和第三组分反應構建季碳中心。我們推測通過铑/钌環烯醇絡合物中間體，可以構建一個多组分卡賓交叉偶聯反應平台，並將其廣泛應用于帶有sp3雜化碳的C-C及C-X鍵的構建中。另外，通過調控金屬烯醇絡合物中于金屬中間體的修飾，不對稱催化多组分交交叉偶聯反應的目的亦可以實現。通過這项目的實施，我們將可以加深對後過渡金屬環化絡合物的氧化修飾的機理的認知，並且可以構建一個具有廣適用性、高效的不對稱多组分卡賓交叉偶聯反應技術平台。

15315216.label: Realisation of objectives
15315216.value: This project aims to explore pi-basic late transition metal centers (e.g. Ru and Rh) to mediate carbenoid/nitrenoid cross coupling reactions. Especially, the design of chiral metal catalysts for enantioselective cross coupling is of significant impact for atom-economical access to chiral building blocks for drug development. For objectives 1, 2 and 3, we have completed the synthesis of a chiral diene building block for synthesis of chiral arene-ruthenium(II) complex. With 1,1’-binaphthyl amines as precursor, the binaphthylamide-substituted cyclohexa-1,4-diene was prepared in 69% yield (amide coupling with a dibromide precursor). The corresponding chiral arene-ruthenium(II) complex has been prepared by reacting the chiral cyclohexadiene with RuCl3•3H2O in ethanol. The chiral arene-ruthenium complex has been structurally characterized by X-ray crystallographic study. The chiral arene-ruthenium complex has been tested for catalytic carbenoid transfer reaction. For instance, treatment of arylboronic acids with alpha-aryl/alkyldiazoacetate in the presence of the chiral arene-ruthenium complex afforded successfully the corresponding arylation product. However, less than 5% ee of the arylation product was registered. During our investigation on the catalytic activity of the chiral arene-ruthenium complex, we found that treating 1-decene with the chiral ruthenium complex (2.5 mol%) and methyl dioxazolone afforded the 3-amino-1-decene derivative in 60% yield and 10% ee. The success of the dioxazolone coupling reaction provided us a proof-of-concept study on the isolobal relationship of carbene and nitrene ligands for coordination to a Ru(II) center. Chiral Ru complexes of metalloporphyrins and pyridine bis(oxazoline) ligands are also well established to effect asymmetric benzylic C–H amidations with sulfonylazides as nitrene reagents. The analogous nitrene transfer reaction involving carbonylnitrene species are sparse. The pertinent challenge is that the carbonylnitrene is susceptible to Curtius-type rearrangement to form isocyanate, thereby divert the nitrene transfer reaction to non-productive outcome. In this project, we found that arene-ruthenium(II) unit is effective to enable competitive carbonylnitrene transfer reaction versus the non-productive Curtius-type rearrangement. We surmised that the stronger pi-donacity of Ru would destabilize the LUMO of the nitrene ligand, thereby disfavor the Curtius-type rearrangement. We prepared a series of well-characterized [(arene)Ru(L^L)] (L^L = bidentate ligand) for reaction with phenyl-1,4,2-dioxazol-5-lones; successful formation of reactive Ru-nitrene would afford gamma-lactams – a valuable building block for drug synthesis – via nitrene C(sp3)–H insertion. Through extensive ligand screening, phosphines and imines delivered inferior product yields. Reaction of metalacyclic ruthenium complex of 2-arylpyridines with dioxazolones afforded high yielding ortho-amidation product via migratory insertion to Ru–C bond. Prompted by this finding, we tested a series of isolobal amide ligands that form stable metalacyclic ruthenium complexes. Gratifyingly, N-arylsulfonyl diphenyl-1,2-ethylenediamine (dpen) gave the best results, and up to 95% ee were achieved for the gamma-lactam formation. It was found that the dpen derivatives containing electron-withdrawing substituents afforded higher product yields and better enantioselectivity. In general, dioxazolones containing benzylic C–H bonds at the gamma position undergo facile nitrene insertion to form the lactam products in good yields and >95% ee. The analogous cyclizations involving nitrene insertion to non-conjugated C(sp3)–H bonds are also lactam-productive, albeit with lower enantioselectivity. Unlike the classical catalytic amidation based on dirhodium(II, II) carboxylates catalyst, the analogous Ru-catalyzed reactions of the dioxazolones bearing alkene and alkyne moieties exhibit remarkable chemoselectivity. The allylic / propargylic C(sp3)–H bonds exclusively reacted for nitrene insertion to furnish the corresponding gamma-lactams in 60–90% ee. The nitrene insertion was found to proceed with remarkable gamma-regioselectivity. For instance, dioxazolone containing a polyene moiety would undergo lactamization by intramolecular nitrene insertion to the gamma-allylic C–H bond selectively. Gram-scale synthesis of gamma-lactam has also been accomplished using the Ru-catalyzed protocol, and the lactam product can be readily derivatized to selected pharmaceutical products by literature methods. This work has been published in Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2019, 141, 3849. Organofluorine compounds are exceptionally important for drug discovery and development since introducing electronegative fluorine atoms would induce significant changes of chemical and biological properties such as bioactivity, metabolic stability and pharmacokinetics of the parent compounds. To date, over 30% of agrochemicals and 20% of pharmaceutical compounds contain fluorine; notable examples are Efavirenz, Gemcitabine and Fludrocortisone. In this project, we achieved the one-pot Cp*Rh(III)-catalyzed cascade arylfluorination reactions of alpha-diazomalonates with arylboronic acids with NFSI as the fluorinating reagent, and the desired alpha-fluorinated arylmalonates were obtained in >90% yields. Kinetic study revealed a bimolecular rate law, in which the reaction rate exhibits first-order dependence to [Rh(Cp*)(OAc)2] and [diazomalonates] respectively. ESI-MS analysis of the catalytic reaction showed that [Rh(Cp*)(Ar)(OAc)]+ species should be the catalyst resting state. Results of our kinetic and stoichiometric studies implies that the diazomalonate coupling with the arylrhodium(III) complex should be rate-limiting. Indeed, a styryl-Rh(III) complex, prepared in situ by the reaction of styrylboronic acid with Cp*Rh(OAc)2, would react with phenyldiazoacetate to afford the corresponding pi-allylrhodium(III) complex, which has been structurally characterized by X-ray crystallography. To ascertain the nature of the C–F bond formation step, the stoichiometric reactions of some structurally defined diketonato rhodium(III) complexes with NFSI were examined. Consistent with our Hammett correlation study, the C–F bond formation is likely mediated by outer-sphere electrophilic fluorination of the diketonato-rhodium complex by NFSI. It is plausible that the catalytic arylfluorination of diazoacetates should occur by (1) transmetalation of arylboronic acids to the Rh(III) to form arylrhodium(III), (2) coupling of diazomalonates with the arylrhodium(III) complex to form carbene-rhodium, (3) migratory carbene insertion to form diketonato-rhodium(III) complex – probably via rearrangement of the putative sigma-alkylrhodium(III) complex, and (4) electrophilic fluorination of the diketonato-rhodium to form the -aryl--fluoromalonates. This proposed mechanism is in good agreement with our follow-up computational study. This work has been published in Organic Biomolecular Chemistry, 2019, 17, 1191.

15315216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15315216.value: (1) Chiral (arene)ruthenium complexes bearing diphenylethylenediamine ligands have been prepared. These ruthenium complexes are active catalysts for intramolecular nitrene C(sp3)–H insertion to afford gamma-lactams in good yields using dioxazolones as reagents. Notably, by judicious choice of the ligands, the competitive non-productive Curtius-type rearrangement was suppressed. (2) With the use of chiral diphenylethylenediamine ligands, the ruthenium complexes bearing electron-poor N-arylsulfonyl groups are more able to mediate lactamization of aryl-substituted dioxazolones in higher yields and excellent enantioselectivity via nitrene insertion to benzylic C–H bonds. Nitrene insertion to the analogous allylic and progargylic C–H bonds also proceed in enantioselecetively to give lactams in good enantioselectivity (70–80%ee). (3) A gram-scale synthesis for chiral lactams have been accomplished. Transition state model to rationalize the enantioselective nitrene insertion is also established. This work has been published in Journal of American Chemical Society. (4) Cascade arylfluorination of diazomalonates with Cp*Rh(III) as catalyst has been developed. Using arylboronic acids as the aryl source and N-fluorobenzenesulfonimide (NFSI) as the fluorinating reagent, regioselective heterodifunctionalization of the diazomalonates can be achieved to produce the arylfluoromalonates in remarkable yields under mild conditions. (5) Kinetic study established that the rate of reaction is first-order to [Rh] and [diazomalonate], and the arylRh(III) complex is likely to be the resting state. (6) The mechanism has been investigated and key intermediates were isolated and structurally characterized. For instance, reacting styrylboronic acid, phenyldiazoacetate and Cp*Rh(III)(OAc)2 afforded the corresponding pi-allylrhodium(III) complex, which is generated by migratory carbene insertion of the vinyl-Rh intermediate. Stoichiometric reaction of the NFSI with metalloenolate-Rh(III) complex was also examined, and the reaction can be understood by the HOMO (enolate)-LUMO (NFSI) interaction as agreed by computational study. This work has been published in Organic Biomolecular Chemistry.

15315216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15315216.value: Development of catalytic carbonylnitrene insertion to aliphatic C–H bonds using dioxazolones is a significant progress in synthetic chemistry. Dioxazolones can be easily derived from abundant carboxylic acids, which serve as a structurally diverse amide group surrogate for catalytic amide bond formation. By careful electronic tuning of late transition metal centers, the inherent competitive Curtius-type rearrangement can be suppressed. This electronic tuning seems to be feasible by tuning of ligand donacity and oxidation states of the metal centers. It is conceivable that late transition metal in low oxidation state would be attractive candidates for catalytic nitrene transfer reactions using dioxazolones. We recently observed that alkyl-Ni complexes generated by hydrometallation of alkenes would undergo facile cross coupling with a structurally diverse dioxazolones to form Markovnikov and anti-Markovnikov amides from alkenes. The observed regioselectivity is influenced by the nature of the auxiliary ligands and the structure of the dioxazolones. This follow-up study should open a new opportunity in catalytic C–N bond coupling chemistry and would attract interest for applying this catalytic approach for synthesis of pharmaceuticals and advanced materials.

15315216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15315216.value: We examine migratory carbene insertion as an effective approach to transform arylRh complexes to reactive enolate complexes, which would undergo further transformation to quaternary stereocenters. The success of this reaction stems from the favorable electronic modulation of the carbene ligand by the late transition metal center. Inspired by the results from our carbenoid cross coupling reaction platform, we extended our investigation to catalytic nitrene transfer reactions. Based on simple analogy with the carbene ligand, nitrene coordination to late transition metal may also be modulated through careful ligand tuning. We successfully developed ruthenium-catalyzed lactamization of dioxzalones by intramolecular nitrene C–H insertion reaction. With careful screening of ligands and structure modification, the ruthenium complexes bearing chiral diphenylethylene diamine scaffold are effective catalysts to mediate enantioselective nitrene C–H insertion with the chiral lactams being obtained in >95% ee. Apart from the practical value of this nitrene transfer reaction, the success of this carbene/nitrene transfer reaction platform should serve as a good model to explore new cross coupling reactions for innovative organic synthesis.

15320216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15320216.value: 可拉伸柔性電極在生物醫用材料、醫學診斷與治療、電子皮膚、穿戴電腦、顯示和光伏器件等領域有廣泛的應用。目前該柔性電極的研究處於初始階段，其製備需要繁瑣且複雜的微納米加工等操作。與此相仿，生物界有許多可拉伸的材料及結構 。因此，本項目著眼研究生物界那些種類的結構可用于製造高性能的可拉伸柔性電極，並且研究如何簡便的仿造該結構，實現可大面積的製備基礎。本項目的成功實施不僅可以提供全新的仿生知識，還可以衍生出各種用於拉升柔性電極的仿生製備技術，對可拉伸電子領域有重要的意義。

15320216.label: Realisation of objectives
15320216.value: This project aims for developing highly stretchable electrodes with biological structures, which show intrinsic stretchability and high mechanical robustness. Thus, upon the development of novel stretchable electrode material, experiments are carried out through all six objectives to measure its electrical, optical-mechanical properties. All the research objectives have been achieved. A detail description of the realization of objectives is discussed below. Objective 1. To study possible biological structures that can be used as templates for making stretchable electrodes. Objective 2. To fabricate stretchable electrodes directly on the bio-templates and to study their morphological, electrical, optical, and mechanical properties and stabilities. Biomimicking structures including leaf veins, petal structures, and buckles have been studied to fabricate stretchable electrodes. In particular, the petal structures have been found to enable stretchable (transparent) electrodes. The leaf veins have been found to enable highly transparent stretchable electrodes with outstanding figure-of-merit. The buckling structure was found to be useful for both opaque and transparent electrodes, and devices. We also developed haze film which can be used as an optical film to enhance the efficiency of the solar cells. Objective 3. To mimic and optimize useful bio-templates by micro- and nano-fabrication technologies. We used microfabrication technology such as electron-beam lithography and photolithography to fabricate the bio-mimicking structures to achieve large-area and patternable fabrication of the transparent/opaque, highly conductive, flexible and stretchable electrodes. We also developed new fabrication technology termed Electrochemical Replication and Transfer (ERT) to enable large-area fabrication of nanoscale and microscale electrodes with different structures. Objective 4. To fabricate stretchable electrodes on man-made bio-mimicking templates and to study their morphological, electrical, optical, and mechanical properties and stabilities. We mimic the structure and use the fabrication technology mentioned above to fabricate highly flexible and stretchable electrodes on flexible thin film, fibrous substrates, and elastomeric substrates to achieve high conductivity and desirable optical properties. 5. To understand the mechanical deformation/failure and interfacial adhesion/delamination process by computer simulation. We have used finite element simulation to develop simulation to understand the strain/stress behavior of the conductive electrodes with different structures. In addition, we also studied the interfacial properties and found that using a properly fabricated interface with suitable strength and elastic modulus can significantly enhance the stability of the electrodes. 6. To demonstrate the fabrication of stretchable optoelectronic devices with the biomimicking stretchable electrodes and to study the device's electrical, optical, and mechanical properties, especially under repeating bending and stretching conditions. We have fabricated stretchable organic solar cells using the stretchable transparent and opaque electrodes. We have studied the optoelectronic properties of the materials and the devices, and the mechanical properties of the devices at different strains.

15320216.label: Major findings and research outcome
15320216.value: Several important materials and devices have been developed in the project, including a biomimetic haze film (BHF) for light absorption enhancement, the biomimetic transparent electrode (BTE) for solar cells via polymer-assisted metal deposition (PAMD) or electrochemical replication and transfer (ERT), and the application of the BTEs for solar cells, stretchable organic solar cells. Four peer-reviewed journal articles have been published in high-impact journals including Chemical Reviews (1 article), Chemical Society Reviews (1 article), Small (1 article), and Small Methods (1 article). One paper is in the revised review process (revised submission to Advanced Functional Materials) and two more papers are in preparation. PI has also been invited to deliver oral and keynote lectures in many international symposiums, conferences, and workshops.

15320216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15320216.value: The stretchable electrodes can be applied for other types of optoelectronic devices such as, but not limited to, flexible and stretchable light-emitting diodes. In addition, these electrodes can also be used to fabricate flexible and stretchable perovskite-based optoelectronic devices. In fact, the research team has been trying to fabricate perovskite-based stretchable devices. It is found that stretchable perovskite solar cells with ~12% power conversion efficiency can be fabricated in the preliminary experiments. Future research will focus on enhancing the efficiency and stability of the stretchable devices.

15320216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15320216.value: Stretchable electrodes are indispensable components of stretchable electronics, however, the fabrication of these best-performing stretchable electrodes either requires labor-intensive processing, or the use of very expensive nanomaterials, which is difficult to scale up. Unlike man-made systems, biological systems are made of many kinds of stretchable materials and structures. In particular, many surface topography and network structures in biological systems might be useful for providing high stretchability to materials that inherently not stretchable. This project aims for fabricating bio-inspired and bio-mimicking stretchable electrodes for stretchable device applications. In particular, we focus on the development of stretchable organic solar cells (OSCs) which can be used as rollable, wearable, and foldable solar systems that can convert solar energy to electricity. This project not only opens up new knowledge of bio-inspired stretchable electrodes, but will also deliver novel technical know-how for the fabrication of bio-mimicking structures and electrodes. This project demonstrates the first few examples of using biological structures for making stretchable OSCs. The knowledge and skills acquired are significant to other stretchable electronic devices and systems in a long term.

15325816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15325816.value: 相場方程半隱式格式的L-infinity穩定性

15325816.label: Project Objectives
15325816.value: We will prove the unconditional energy stability independent of the time step for a first order in time stabilized semi-implicit scheme for the Cahn-Hilliard equation. This new stability analysis will not require any additional Lipschitz assumption on the nonlinearity, or any a priori bounds on the numerical solution. Higher order stabilization methods will be studied to achieve strict energy stability as in the first order case. The L-infinity stability of these methods will be investigated. General stabilization algorithms instead of the usual Laplacian stabilization will be developed and analyzed. Stabilized large-time stepping numerical schemes for general phase field models with higher order dissipation will be explored.

15325816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15325816.value: This project focuses on the stability analysis on a class of large time-stepping numerical methods for the phase field models. Many recent results in the literature provide computational evidences that stabilized semi-implicit time-stepping methods can efficiently simulate phase field equations involving fourth-order dissipation. The up-to-date theoretical explanation of the numerical stability relies on the assumption that the derivative of the nonlinear potential function satisfies a Lipschitz type condition, which in a rigorous sense, implies the boundedness of the numerical solution. It is highly desirable but challenging to remove these restrictions and establish a more reasonable stability analysis for phase field equations. In this work we will develop an L-infinity stability theory on semi-implicit schemes for some phase field equations including typical models like the Cahn-Hilliard equation and the thin film equation with slope selection. The numerical schemes are semi-implicit in time with a stabilization term and finite difference discretized in space. We will prove unconditional energy stability independent of the time step. New L-infinity maximum principles will be explored for aforementioned numerical schemes. The Lipschitz assumption on the nonlinearity, or a priori bounds on the numerical solution will be removed in the stability analysis. The corresponding error analysis will also be carried out under minimal regularity assumptions. 本項目主要研究針對一些相場模型，例如Cahn-Hilliard方程和薄膜方程，的一類大時間步長數值方法的穩定性。很多近期的文獻數值上驗證了穩定化的半隱式格式能夠高效的模擬含有四階耗散項的相場方程。最新的關於數值穩定性的理論分析要求非線性勢函數的導數滿足Lipschitz條件，嚴格的說，也就是要求數值解有界。移除此類限制，得到針對相場方程更加合理的穩定性分析結果是一項十分重要的工作。 在本項目中，我們將針對包括Cahn-Hilliard方程和有梯度選擇的薄膜方程等一些相場方程進行研究，得到改進的穩定性分析結果。我們研究的數值格式在時間上是半隱式的，在空間上用差分離散。我們將證明不依賴於時間步長的無條件能量穩定性。基於非線性函數的Lipschitz假設，或者基於數值解的先驗假設將會被移除。我們還將建立在最小正則性假設條件下的相應的誤差分析。

15325816.label: Major findings and research outcome
15325816.value: In this project, we have studied the stability and convergence of some efficient numerical schemes for some phase-field problems. The major findings and research outcome are as follows: 1. In [Du, Ju, Li, Qiao, SINUM,2019], we have investigated the discrete maximum bound principle of first-order and second-order ETD schemes. Based on the obtained L-infinity bound of the numerical solution, energy stability has been proved. We further generalized these results to a class of semi-linear parabolic equations and established a framework for the design of maximum bound principle preserving numerical schemes, which has been accepted in SIAM Review as [Du, Ju, Li, Qiao, SIREV, 2020, accepted.] 2. In [Liu, Qiao, IJNAM, 2019], we establish an unconditional and optimal strong convergence rate of Wong–Zakai type approximations in Banach space norm for a parabolic stochastic partial differential equation with monotone drift, including the stochastic Allen–Cahn equation, driven by an additive Brownian sheet. A strong convergence rate has been derived. 3. In [Du, Ju, Li, Qiao, JCP 2018], we developed energy stable schemes for nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equations. The temporal discretization is done by using the stabilization technique with the nonlocal diffusion term treated implicitly, while the spatial discretization is carried out by the Fourier collocation method with FFT-based fast implementations. The energy stabilities are rigorously established for both methods in the fully discrete sense. 4. In [Qiao, Sun, Zhang, Zhang, CICP, 2019; Qiao, Yang, Zhang, PRE, 2018; Qiao, Yang, Zhang, IJHMT 2019], we applied developed numerical schemes in the simulation of diffusive interface models with Peng-Robinson equation of state, which is an important topic in the petroleum industry for hydrocarbon fluids. The numerical results match well with laboratory data.

15325816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15325816.value: Further development of this research is to solve other gradient flows problems with high order diffusion terms by using the developed methods. High order consistency analysis combined with error estimate could be used to recover the L-infinity bound of numerical solutions. Stability analysis on high order methods, such as BDF schemes and exponential time integration, will be conducted.

15325816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15325816.value: This project focuses on the stability analysis of a class of large time-stepping numerical methods for the phase-field models. For Allen-Cahn type equations, we have developed maximum bound principle preserving numerical schemes. Based on the L-infinity bound of the numerical solution, energy stability could be proved. The developed algorithm and proof technique could be used in the study of a large class of semi-linear parabolic equations. For Cahn-Hilliard type equations, we have developed several efficient energy stable numerical schemes with successful applications in simulations of diffusive interface models with Peng-Robinson equation of state, which is an important topic in the petroleum industry for hydrocarbon fluids.

15326416.label: Realisation of objectives
15326416.value: 1. Functionalization and acoustic characterization of nano-bubbles attached with membrane surface protein antibodies GVs were prepared from Anabaena flos-aquae through tonic cell lysis and centrifugally-assisted flotation. They were found to typically be 50 ­ 100 nm in width and 100 ­ 500 nm long. The zeta potential of the GVs was −40 ± 5 mV, indicating a suitable surface charge for colloidal stability. We also found that our prepared GVs were not cytotoxic on their own to primary neurons in culture. Ultrasound is known to induce both stable and inertial cavitation. Generally, stable cavitation occurs at relatively low ultrasound intensities, caused by size changes of gas-filled bubbles in a sustained, periodic manner. We intended to control ultrasound intensity such that it would enable the GVs to generate robust stable cavitation but not inertial cavitation, which required characterizing the GVs’ responses in an ultrasound field. Hence, we performed passive cavitation detection using a setup in a tank of degassed water, where GVs suspensions were exposed to pulsed ultrasound at 0.28 MPa peak negative pressure. We observed the backscattered signals in the time- and frequency-domains to monitor the patterns of cavitation produced. We found no broadband signal and only the appearance of 1st - 17th harmonic signals, indicating that no inertial cavitation occurred when the GVs were sonicated in our setup. Crucially, 0.28 MPa was the highest acoustic pressure used in the entire study, making inertial cavitation unlikely at the range of intensities used in the various following experiments. 2. Protocol optimization of targeting nano-bubbles to neurons and physical effects study of oscillating nano-bubble with neuron cells A possible confounding factor in our experiments was that sonoporation, of the kind that is typically induced by ultrasound in the presence of microbubbles, is known to play a role in initiating Ca2+ response. Although only stable cavitation was detected in our system, that evidence could not address whether our treatment was causing pore formation in the membrane. Thus, we performed a membrane integrity assay to see whether sonoporation was involved in the Ca2+ responses to the GV-mediated ultrasound treatment. We used the membrane impermeable dye propidium iodide (PI) and observed whether it could penetrate the cell membrane during the stimulation. Insonated primary neurons in the presence of GVs evoked Ca2+ influx but no PI could be detected inside the cells; brightfield imaging also showed that the cells maintained their morphology following the treatment. To contrast, Triton X-100 was used as a positive control for membrane permeation, and PI influx was seen within 30 seconds of its addition and continued to increase for the remainder of the assay, while the intracellular calcium signal decreased and the cell was visibly damaged. In general, neither ultrasound alone nor the +GVs condition used in our experiments were seen to trigger PI influx in primary neurons or CLU199 cells. Further, we did not observe obvious cytotoxicity or apoptosis in primary neurons following the treatments. Thus, we concluded that our GVs+US treatment could trigger calcium responses in cells with negligible loss of membrane integrity, which is consistent with stable cavitation hypothesis. Given that we did not observe sonoporation to be the mechanism of calcium dynamics, we were interested in broadly identifying what mechanisms may have been involved in the cellular response to US+GVs. Mechanosensitive ion channels are a well-established way in which cells transduce mechanical forces to cellular signaling. To assess their potential contribution, we used Ruthenium Red (RR, 20 μM), a blocker for a range of mechanosensitive ion channels, to see if the response to GVs+US would be altered. Calcium responses to ultrasound pulses were found to be significantly, but not entirely, suppressed in the presence of RR, and the responses recovered when it was washed away. We observed a similar suppression of Ca2+ influx in the presence of RR in CLU199 cells. We then tried to identify the source of Ca2+ responses by treating cells with GVs+US in EGTA-chelated medium, or pre-treating cells with Thapsigargin (TG, 3 μM) to deplete intracellular calcium stores. Compared to normal conditions, cells in Ca2+-free medium showed much reduced calcium influx (~75% reduction), but the reduction in TG-treated cells was much lesser (~ 25-30% reduction). We thus found that while intracellular Ca2+ release played some role in the GVs+US response, calcium influx from the external medium had a much larger contribution to the observed outcomes. Further, when primary neurons were made to heterologously express the mechanosensitive ion channel MscL-EYFP, or EYFP alone, the MscL-EYFP+GVs showed a Ca2+ response to ultrasound several times that of EYFP+GVs. Altogether, with no significant sonoporation being observed, cellular response being significantly depressed when treated with RR or in Ca2+-free medium but not in TG-treated cells, and much greater response to US+GVs in cells with artificially-enhanced mechanosensitivity, we inferred that activation of mechanosensitive ion channels was an important mechanism of GV-mediated ultrasound stimulation. 3. Physiological investigation of neurons in response to selective ultrasound stimulation We first observed the Ca2+ response in rat primary cortical neurons when stimulated with ultrasound and GVs (1.0 MHz center frequency, 0.20 MPa ultrasound and 0.8 nM GVs unless otherwise indicated). Neurons were made to express the genetically-encoded calcium sensor GCaMP6s under the human synapsin promoter using AAVs, and we monitored its fluorescence upon stimulation. We found that GCaMP6s fluorescence increased quickly and dramatically when stimulated with an ultrasound pulse in the presence of GVs, but not without them, and the fluorescence gradually returned to the baseline without further stimulation. Next, we tested whether neuronal activation could be induced repeatedly. Five 300 ms pulses were delivered to cells at intervals of 3, 5, 10, 20, 30 or 60 seconds in the presence of GVs and the temporal profiles of the cells’ Ca2+ response was charted. Stable and reversible calcium transients were seen to quickly follow each pulse, and the neurons were able to recover after each pulse when given enough time (max ΔF/F = 46 ± 1.8%, five pulses). Aside from primary neurons, we also observed the same pattern of responses, albeit at lower amplitudes, in the mouse hippocampal cell line mHippoE-18 (referred to as ‘CLU199’ in this manuscript). In the presence of GVs, ultrasound triggered robust, repeatable, and rapid calcium responses from cells after which calcium levels would gradually recover, while no response was seen without GVs. Furthermore, the cellular response was found to vary with, both, the concentration of GVs and the acoustic pressure applied, both in primary neurons and in CLU199 cells. These data help to establish that the responses observed were indeed caused by the GVs+US treatment, and also reveal how such a combination treatment can easily be tweaked to suit the degree of response desired. A GV concentration as low as 0.1 nM was sufficient to induce a significantly higher response than without GVs, showing that GVs could indeed lower the acoustic pressure threshold needed for Ca2+ response, which would otherwise require increased ultrasound intensity. Finally, when treated with GVs+US primary neurons showed approximately double the nuclear c-Fos expression, a marker of neuronal activity downstream of Ca2+ influx, than when they were untreated or exposed to only GVs or ultrasound. Thus, we were able to use GVs to efficiently stimulate activity in primary neurons with short bursts of low-intensity ultrasound.

15326416.label: Major findings and research outcome
15326416.value: Non-invasive neuromodulation technologies with high spatiotemporal resolution holds great potential for studying neural circuits and treating neurological conditions. Here we present a GV-mediated non-genetic toolkit for precise neuronal activation. Using a 1.0 MHz transducer, we show that GVs can serve as localized acoustic amplifiers to decrease the threshold of ultrasound intensity for neurostimulation. We achieved controllable calcium signaling in both primary neurons and a neuronal cell line, and increased c-Fos expression in primary neurons with low-intensity ultrasound stimulation in the presence of GVs. We also found that the presence of GVs could activate significantly more neurons in mouse VTAs under a low-intensity ultrasound field, but not without, and similar activation was not observed in other brain regions. Comparable to previously-demonstrated magnetothermal, magnetomechanical, and magnetomechanogenetic approaches, our approach utilized mechanosensitive ion channels already expressed endogenously in the brain, without resorting to genetic modification. The GVs’ safety and the ease of their administration make our scheme easy to apply to other experimental targets in vitro and in vivo, as well as makes it a likelier candidate for clinical translation. Converting an external energy source into localized bio-effects by using nanoparticles is an increasingly-common approach to neuromodulation. Piezoelectric nanoparticles have been developed which are able to efficiently convert ultrasound energy to localized electric stimulation 45. Optoacoustic nanoparticles have been used to convert light to acoustic waves, which can then directly activate individual neurons 46. In contrast, using ultrasound’s ability to penetrate deep through tissue, sono-optogenetics utilizes mechanoluminescent nanoparticles convert sound into light to achieve local neuromodulation in deeper brain regions 47. Recently, Lea-Banks et al. reported that nanodroplets loaded with drugs can be combined with ultrasound to achieve targeted neuromodulation 48. In the same vein, present study, builds upon the status of nano-sized gas vesicles as efficient ultrasound contrast agents 49 to use them as actuators for reliable and reversible neuron stimulation, and to enable spatial targeting of a desired area of the brain.

15326416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15326416.value: Our in vivo scheme was as minimally-invasive as possible, we still needed to perform some surgery to deliver the GVs into the brain. There are two possible ways to achieve non-invasive delivery of GVs in targeted regions: systematic delivery from the bloodstream; genetically-encoded expression. A recent study from our group demonstrated that surface-modified GVs can escape clearance from the reticuloendothelial system and penetrate tumor vasculature through enhanced permeability and retention effects. Recent studies showed that surface modifications on nanoparticles could facilitate the penetration of BBB into targeted brain regions, which could be applied to GVs as well due their conduciveness to surface modification. Another possibility is to use microbubble-mediated ultrasonic bio-effects which have been widely explored and utilized to open blood-brain barrier transiently to deliver the GVs in targeted region. Alternatively, mammalian cells have been genetically engineered to express GVs as acoustic reporter genes to enable ultrasound imaging of gene expression. This approach has the advantage of being able to target specific cell types, easily achieved by placing the ARGs under different promoters in virus design. Combined with the GVs’ molecular imaging capability, we envision that GVs+US could even be developed to have a more theranostic role in the brain.

15326416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15326416.value: Ultrasound is a promising new modality for non-invasive neuromodulation. Being able to limit ultrasound’s stimulatory effects to a targeted brain region would help to improve the treatment’s effectiveness. Nanomaterials-enabled nanotechnology can achieve a high spatial resolution for neural stimulation. Here, we report spatially confined ultrasound neural stimulation in a deep brain area through gas-filled nanostructures (GVs). When exposed to ultrasound fields, vibration of GVs triggered reversible neuronal Ca2+ responses, closely synced to stimuli, and increased nuclear expression of the activation marker c-Fos. Moreover, the ultrasound parameter has negligible influence on cell membrane integrity or temperature which confirms that GVs-ultrasound activates neurons through the mechanosensitive ion channels but not via cavitation or thermal effect. We further confirm that GVs-ultrasound stimulation evoked neural excitation in the targeted ventral tegmental areas (VTA) of mice, and transient Ca2+ response captured by fiber photometry, and the VTA region also showed significantly higher c-Fos expression than the contralateral region as well as other brain regions without GVs. This treatment scheme was also found not to induce significant cytotoxicity, apoptosis or membrane poration in treated cells. Altogether, we demonstrate an effective method to achieve spatially confined neural stimulation of mouse brain in deep brain regions.

15326716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15326716.value: The proposed research will be on the search of new non-radial solutions arising from partial differential equations from Gauge theories in Physics. Gauge theories describe electromagnetic phenomena, including superconductivity and the fractional quantum Hall effect. They are also intimately related to Standard model of Particle Physics. Some partial differential equations (PDEs) that arise from gauge theories are the magnetic Ginzburg-Landau (GL) and Chern-Simon-Higgs (CSH) equations, and the Yang-Mills-Higgs (YMH) equations. The magnetic GL and CSH equations are coupled covariant nonlinear Schrodinger and Maxwell equations that model (macroscopically) the phenomenon of superconductors and the quantum Hall effect, respectively; and the former describes the U(1) Higgs model of particle physics. The systems are especially useful in the study of high temperature superconductors. The YMH equations describe monopoles in three dimensional space. We will find new non-radial magnetic vortex solutions to the GL and CSH equations on the whole plane and new non-radial monopole solutions to the YMH equations on the whole three dimensional space. The discovery of these new non-radial magnetic vortex solutions will give rise to questions on whether these configurations can be observed experimentally in superconductors. The analytical techniques used in finding these solutions will also generate novel ways to find other new solutions to additional elliptic non-linear partial differential equations. Therefore, this research will be of interest to both Physicists and Mathematicians and will explore the multi-faceted relationship between elliptic partial differential equations, analysis and geometry. 物理學中之規範場論應用於電磁現象，範圍包括超導體、分數量子 Hall 效應，與粒子物理學之典型模型有密切關系。理論中研究之偏微分方程有帶磁 Ginzburg-Landau, Chern-Simon-Higgs 及 Yang-Mills-Higgs 等方程。本研究計劃之目標為尋找各方程之新非球對稱解。結果將有助於研究超導體及粒子物理學。所獲新數學方法亦將有助於橢圓型偏微分方程之分析及幾何研究。

15327116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15327116.value: Black phosphorus (BP), a layered anisotropic allotrope of phosphorus, is emerging as a superior two-dimensional (2D) material owing to its exceptional electronic, optical and structural properties. Unlike graphene, BP is a semiconductor with a thickness dependent direct band gap ranging from 0.3 to 2 eV. Another notable feature of BP includes its anisotropic electric conductance and optical responses, distinguishing this material from many other isotropic 2D crystals such as graphene and molybdenum and tungsten chalcogenides. Theoretical calculations have predicted strain not only could tune the band structure but also control the anisotropic electrical conductance of BP. In this regard, it will be extreme exciting to realize these strain-induced anisotropic behaviors in BP. This project aims to perform a detailed and systematic study of anisotropic strain-engineered BP. By applying anisotropic strain to BP using the newly developed bending and electromechanical techniques, we could monitor vibrational and optical properties of BP as a function of applied strain. In addition, the strain-induced anisotropic electrical conductance and the magnetotransport properties of BP will be explored. The realization of modulation of anisotropic electrical conductance of BP by strain will create unprecedented possibilities for novel mechanical-electronic device such as mechanically controlled logic. The highly anisotropic and strain-tunable characteristics of BP offer new applications in thermal management, thermoelectronics, nanoelectronics, and photonics. 作為單質磷的壹種層狀各向異性同素異形體，黑磷是壹種優異的二維材料，具有獨特的電子、光學和結構性質。不同於石墨烯，黑磷是壹種半導體，具有隨厚度變化的直接帶隙，變化範圍為0.3〜2 eV。黑磷的另外壹個值得註意的特點是它具有各向異性的電導和光學響應，這也是它區分於其它各向同性的二維資料（如石墨烯、二硫化鉬和二硫化鎢）的壹個重要特徵。理論計算預測了應變不僅可以調控黑磷的能帶結構，也能調控它的各向異性電導。因而，我們非常期待可以實現應變對黑磷的這些各向異性行為的誘導。 本項目擬詳盡系統地研究在各向異性應變工程下的黑磷。採用新研發的彎曲和電機械科技，對黑磷施加各向異性應變，可以觀測黑磷在應變作用下的振動和光學性質的變化。此外，還可探索黑磷受應變誘導的各向異性電導和磁輸運性質。通過實現應變調控黑磷的各向異性電導，將有可能實現壹些新型的機電器件，如機械控制的邏輯器件。黑磷高度的各向異性和其應變可調的特性使得它在熱管理、熱電、納米電子學和光子學提供新的應用。

15327116.label: Realisation of objectives
15327116.value: 1. To exfoliate monolayer to few-layer BP using various mechanical and solution methods Ultrathin black phosphorus (BP) from 5 to 10 nm were prepared by mechanical exfoliation from bulk BP single crystals using polydimenthylsiloxane (PDMS) film. The ultrathin BP can be transferred Si and PET substrates. Solution exfoliated BP flakes were obtained in various solutions. About 20 mg of BP crystals was added into acetone (4mL), IPA (4mL), NMP (4mL) and ethanol (8 mL) solutions. The samples were ultrasonicated using an ultrasonic bath of 400 W at a temperature of 28 °C for 48 hrs. The obtained BP solution was centrifugaed with rates of 1000 - 4000 rpm for 60 min in order to remove larger particles. The BP solutions with different concentrations can be obtained by tuning the centrifugation rates. We also demonstrated mass production of few-layer BP nanosheets by irradiating pristine BP crystal with a pulsed laser for a few microseconds in a series of low-boiling point solvents including, methanol, ethanol, propanol, and hexane. Without additional ingredients, BP nanosheets with narrow and solvent-dependent thickness distribution and large lateral size can be prepared. 2. To study the anisotropic strain response in band structure and vibrational properties of BP A modified bending technique was developed to apply precise uniaxial tensile strain along the zigzag (ZZ) or armchair (AC) direction of the ultrathin BP encapsulated by a layer of polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA). The Raman shift rates of the , and modes are significantly distinct for strain applied along different directions. For the zigzag case, the Raman shift rate and the Grüneisen parameter of the mode can reach a remarkable value of ~ -11 cm-1/% strain and ~ 2.5 respectively, which are the largest among all the reported values in common two-dimensional materials. It demonstrates that this bending technique can offer a quasi-pure uniaxial tensile strain to ultrathin BP. Our theoretical calculation suggests that the giant anisotropic strain response in ultrathin BP is ascribed to the changes in both bond lengths and angles of the BP upon applied strain. Based on the giant anisotropic strain response in B2g mode, we demonstrate a facile method to identify the crystallographic orientations of the ultrathin BP using the strained ultrathin BP and the conventional non-polarized Raman spectroscopy. Our work paves a way to explore the anisotropic strain-dependent electrical, optical and thermal properties of ultrathin BP devices. 3. To explore the strain-modulated anisotropic electrical conductance of BP The BP flakes on a plastic substrate were patterned to a cross-shape with AC and ZZ directions aligned. The electrical conductance of the BP was measured as a function of applied strain. The electrical conductance of the BP along AC and ZZ directions as a function of stain do not show observe changes. The bending technique is unable to provide sufficient strain to induce the anisotropic electrical conductance. We demonstrated that polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) capping can not only enhance the durability of the ultrathin BP effectively and nondestructively, but also tune the effective Schottky barriers (SBs) formed at the interfaces between the metal and semiconductor dramatically. Particularly, the Schottky barrier (SB) for electron injection from metal to semiconductor is decreased by ~ 13 meV and the performance of the BP field effect transistor (FET) is strongly enhanced with the current on/off ratio increased by 6.8 times for the hole conduction after the PMMA capping. In addition, after the electron beam irradiation to the PMMA layer, the charge neutral point of the BP FET exhibits remarkable negative shift resulting in the electron dominated semiconductor channel at zero gate voltage. Furthermore, through partially capping the BP channel, a prototype of BP p-n diode was demonstrated with a maximum rectification factor of 21.3. The diode performs quite well with just a quarter of the BP channel capped by the PMMA layer. Our findings suggest that the PMMA capped ultrathin BP would be a promising choice for future device applications. 4. To explore the magnetotransport properties of anisotropic strained BP BP flakes were first transferred onto SiO2/Si substrate with 285 nm oxidation layer by pressing the as-grown samples on it. The Hall devices were fabricated by e-beam lithography first and then deposited with 5 nm Ti and 50 nm Au by e-beam evaporation. Magnetotransport measurements were performed by a physical property measurement system (Quantum Design) with magnetic field up to 9 T and temperature from 300 to 2 K. However, the magnetotransport properties of the BP do not seem to vary with the applied strain.

15327116.label: Major findings and research outcome
15327116.value: • A laser-assisted ultrafast exfoliation of BP in solvent with tunable thickness was developed. • A modified bending technique is employed to apply precise uniaxial tensile strain along the zigzag or armchair direction of the ultrathin BP encapsulated by a layer of polymethyl methacrylate. • The Grüneisen parameter of BP is found to be as high as ≈2.5, which is the largest among all the reported common 2D materials. • An alternative method based entirely on the strained ultrathin BP and nonpolarized Raman spectroscopy is demonstrated to determine the crystallographic orientations of ultrathin BP. • We demonstrated that polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) capping can not only enhance the durability of the ultrathin BP effectively and nondestructively, but also tune the effective Schottky barriers (SBs) formed at the interfaces between the metal and semiconductor dramatically. • Through partially capping the BP channel, a prototype of BP p-n diode was demonstrated with a maximum rectification factor of 21.3. The diode performs quite well with just a quarter of the BP channel capped by the PMMA layer. • The knowledge gained in the magnetotransport study of BP enabled us to study the magnetotranaport properties of VSe2. We showed that a linear positive and non-saturating magnetoresistance of 35% from a 35 nm thick VSe2 at 15 T and 2 K due to charge density waves induce mobility fluctuations. • In addition to the publications in the above topics, the works have also led to several review papers in BP and the related topics.

15327116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15327116.value: The laser-assisted ultrafast exfoliation technique could be further developed to produce large quantity and thickness controllable BP flakes. The BP flakes should find applications in batteries. The bending techniques could be extended to study other anisotropic 2D materials. The fabrication and encapsulation techniques for air-sensitive 2D materials could be useful for studying other emerging 2D materials. The device fabrication and magnetotransport techniques of BP could be extended to investigate other newly discovered 2D materials.

15327116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15327116.value: As a rising star in the family of 2D materials, BP has attracted tremendous attention all over the world and demonstrated great potential in energy applications owing to its direct and narrow bandgap, high carrier mobility and theoretical capacity, as well as anisotropic structure. The unique anisotropic nature of this intriguing material creates unprecedented possibilities for the realization of conceptually novel electronics, optoelectronics and non-mechanical devices which are not possible using other 2D materials. The results of this project provide some fundamental understanding of this topic. The highly anisotropic and strain-tunable characteristics of BP offer new applications in thermal management, thermoelectronics, nanoelectronics, and photonics.

15327216.label: Project Objectives
15327216.value: For the SIH model with right-censored survival outcomes, we develop a Nielsen’s nonparametric estimation for the nonparametric function. We hope to show that the proposed profile maximum likelihood estimator of the parameter component reaches the semiparamatric efficient bound. We plan to conduct numerical experiments and theoretical proof. For the SIH model, we plan to develop an alternative yet interesting estimation equations by constructing efficient influence equations suggested in Tsiatis (2007). We investigate computationally feasible solutions to implement the proposed method based on doubly robust equations. Extensive numerical analysis will be conducted. A complete theory proof will be given in the proposed research. For the MIH model, we will transform the dimension reduction problem into a matrix form such that the inference becomes a problem of parametric estimation in the presence of nuisance component. We will establish the efficient influence equations along the line of Tsiatis (2007) so that several important linear combinations could be found. After that, we will investigate an efficient way to estimate the nonparametric functional in the influence equations. Finally we will derive the theoretical proof of the results. To test the validity of density ratio model assumption for right censored data, we propose several goodness-of-fit testing procedures along PI's recent theoretical work of empirical likelihood estimation for CDFs survival and quantile functions. The PI also plans to study the test power as well as bootstrap implementation. Furthermore, we plan to develops simultaneous confidence bands by both Bonferroni adjustment and equal precision methods.

15327216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15327216.value: 本研究项目受两个大型流行病遗传学研究的推动。 项目研究者计划发展一系列新颖的统计工具，以此来解决流行病遗传学中的重要科学问题统计方法论上的急需。拟提出的办法实际上具有一般性，亦能处理其它领域的类似数据。方法论的贡献上关注于找出流行病遗传学中的重要的生物标记，评判这些生物标记对删失的生存数据的效应，以及对由多个中心测量的具有某种共同特征的的失效时间总体的分布函数的比较。特别的，项目研究者集中于两类具有多种高维生物标记协变量的新型的半参数生存指标危险率模型。 计划书有如下四个目标：1）提出灵活的单指标危险率模型以刻画右删失的失效时间与多样性的生物标记，例如结合着蛋白的甲基化酌。我们用一类新的局部线性拟合方法去估计非参数部分，从而再用轮廓似然函数法与有效影响方程去建立参数部分的有效估计；我们会研究两类基于轮廓似然函数建立的估计方程，从而得到计算上可行的估计。2）我们提出一类多指标失效模型，其好处是可以包含不同类型的高维流行病遗传学生物标记。我们拟通过调用hMAVE方法来降维从而使参数部分的估计达到半参数有效界。3）我们提出一类密度比模型，以便比较来源于多个总体的生存数据的分布性质。通过构建一些非参数推断过程我们来检验模型的合理性，我们也会发展生存函数与分位数函数的同步置信带以作整体统计推断。在以上三个目标中，除了高深的理论工作，项目负责人也会执行密集的数值计算以展示比较和验证所提出的方法和理论。发展易于计算的算法也是研究的着眼点。最后，4）立项人与合作者共同致力于将所提出的统计方法与算法去解决重要的实际问题。 首三个目标在数学与数值计算上各有难度但又有机联系到我们的研究重心，带右删失失效时间的半参数模型。项目的研究计划一旦完成，将可填补目前文献中一些关键的代沟，其应用也并不局限于上面所提到的具有多种类型生物标记的右删失实效数据的分析。

15327216.label: Realisation of objectives
15327216.value: Objectives 1 and 2 for single index model (SIH) has been fully completed. For various censored survival outcomes, the PI has had series of studies and results. With the mentoring of Co-I, the PI and her team investigated the impact of a subset of genetic factors on the survival time through the single-index hazard (SIH) semiparametric regression model. We proposed a censored version of multiple local linear regression to attain uniformly consistent estimator of the nonparametric component and the semiparametric efficient bound for the profile likelihood estimator of the parametric component. This method is applied to study data of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), which integrated a large number of gene expression variants and censored survival time of patients with low sample size. We also investigated various causal effects such as for random censored survival outcomes, or for the practically important observational studies with confounders for completely observed data. As mentioned in the proposal, the SIH model is quite general that can incorporate a wide range of other survival models such as Cox’s model and other semiparametric models. For the ultra-high dimensional data setting, we developed sure screening of Cox-LASSO-IHT iteration and presented an efficient non-monotone proximal gradient algorithm. For the semi-competing risks data which includes both terminal and non-terminal events, we presented a robust joint feature screening utility based on distance correlation, and suggested an adaptive threshold rule for implementation. Objective 3 has been completed but focus on recurrent event data. We notice that there are other researchers who applied the slicing inverse regression (SIR) to explore dimension reduction for multiple-index model within random censored data setting. However their method can not apply to recurrent even data since this is much more challenging owing to multiple jumps at the survival times. The PI and her team developed counting-process based approach to implement sufficient dimension reduction and suggested an ADMM algorithm to alleviate the computational load. Objective 4 has been completed for the model adequacy checking based on empirical process based test procedures for complicated data that are repeated measured and covariates are subject to measurement errors. When there is heterogeneity in the data, the PI and her collaborator tried the Bayesian analysis to model the random effects. In addition, during the emergency of the outbreak of COVID-19, the Co-I, Prof. Xihong Lin from Harvard University has led several important public health studies. As echoing, the PI extended the objective of this project to build on a forecasting spread model of the size of confirmed cases. Based on data collected during the early stage of the pandemic by the USTC team, the PI led the big data team integrated from multidisciplinary collaboration from mathematics, management, and data science. Noticing the specific epidemiological characteristics of COVID-19, the PI and her team proposed a new infectious compartmental model named SaucIR, which involves the pathologically separated asymptomatic compartment and dynamic human mobility network. The proposed SaucIR model has high degree of predictability.
