15622016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15622016.value: With the growing use of mobile information, more and more products such as earphones and headsets are designed for the human ear to enhance the hearing capability and various other functions. Improper product design and a misfit between the ear and product reduce sound quality perception and can even cause pain and discomfort. Conversely, many high requirement hearing devices, such as hearing aids, are custom-moulded to achieve the best fitting. These are still very expensive and lower cost hearing devices remain the preferred choice. With the advent of 3D laser scanning technology, 3D human body scans are now possible. Many studies have been conducted on 3D foot, body and head shape to create a better model for design. However, studies on 3D ear shape are limited because of its complex shape and the lack of availability of special purpose ear scanners. Until now, the 3D ear shape has not been investigated in detail, especially for Chinese population. Knowledge of 3D anthropometry, anatomical features and comfort perception are essential in design and evaluation of ear-related products. The aim of this study is to investigate the 3D human external ear shape, classify the 3D ear shape, study the size tolerance and develop an accurate model for ear-related product design. First, a 3D ear database of Chinese population will be captured using a hand-held 3D scanner and moulding of the ear canal. Different methods including Interactive Closest Point (ICP) will be used to merge and align the complex ear shape. Statistical techniques, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), will be used to find variations in 3D ear shapes. Symmetry, gender and age differences of the 3D ear shapes will be analysed. Clustering algorithms, such as K-mean, will be used to classify different ear categories. In addition, experiments will be conducted to find out the perception of comfort while using an ear product with various size and weight settings. From this study, the ear shape variation, classification and subjective perception will be used to create an ear sizing system for ear-related product design. This system will enable designers to create better fitting hearing devices with an acceptable comfort level at a much lower cost for the Chinese population. The ear model can be applied in many industries developing ear-related products. 隨著信息時代的到來，用於助聽等功能的耳機類產品設計需求正逐步增加。不當的產品設計和不佳的適配度都會降低音質，甚至引起疼痛與不適。對於有較高要求的助聽器等設備，很多都采用 定制的方法以達到最佳適配度的要求。然而，由於定制產品通常較為昂貴，低成本的助聽設備依然是多數人的選擇。隨著三維激光掃描技術的發展，三維人體掃描已成為可能。目前，很多針對足部，身體和頭部的三維掃描技術的研究已經為相應的產品提供了更好的設計模型。然而，由於耳部形狀較為覆雜且專用儀器缺乏，耳部的三維研究尚處於初始階段，尤其是針對中國人群的研究更為缺乏。因此，三維人體測量學，解剖特征以及舒適度的研究是耳部相關產品的設計和評估必不可少的。 本研究的主要目標是通過探究三維耳部輪廓，對其形狀進行分類並確定尺碼，以建立耳部相關產品的設計模型。首先，本研究會使用手持式三維掃描儀和耳道成型技術創建中國人三維耳部測量數據庫，並通過不同的算法以合並及校準覆雜的耳部模型。其次，本研究會利用統計分析方法確定三維耳部形狀的差異性，同時分析耳部的對稱性，性別和年齡的差異，並對耳部形狀進行分類。此外，本研究會采用實驗方法對用戶使用不同耳部產品時的舒適度進行評估。耳部形狀的差異，分類及主觀感覺的研究結果會用來建立一個耳部相關產品設計的尺碼系統。該尺碼系統可以幫助設計師以更低的成本在可接受的舒適度範圍內為中國人設計適配度更高的助聽設備，以及應用於其他的耳部相關產品行業。

15622016.label: Realisation of objectives
15622016.value: Objective 1: To collect a large sample of 3D Chinese ear shape data for sizing development. Objective 1 was successfully achieved. 501 participants within the age range between 18 to 70 years were recruited for establishing the anthropometric database. After testing different 3D scanners and molding materials, a clear research method, including data collection, processing and analysis, was developed for 3D ear anthropometry. During data collection, the Artec Eva 3D scanner was used to scan the head and ear region. For earmold model, RangeVision Smart 3D scanner with the use of an automatic turntable was selected for 3D scanning. A molding method using a mixture of addition reaction silicone and its catalyst was appied to mold both the inner and the back parts of the external ear. After data collection, three 3D models, including the scanned ear, scanned inner mold, and scanned back mold, were aligned and merged to generate a complete 3D ear model with the canal entrance, the concha, the pinna, and the back part of the ear. Additionally, the repeatability of the data collection method was examined. The inter-method reliability was checked by comparing the traditional and 3D anthropometric data. Objective 2: To find out a 3D ear alignment method. Objective 2 was successfully achieved. Different alignment methods, including Iterative Closest Point (ICP) alignment, and landmarks alignment, were tested to align the 3D models into specific orientation and locations. All scanning results were cleaned by removing outlier, building bridge, and filling hole. The cleaned models were well filed for further alignment and combination. Landmark alignment was applied to align the three scanned models considering the ear structure and morphological variation. With the scanned pinna as the reference, the inner and back molds were aligned based on the helix and antihelix landmarks. A 3D ear model was generated by deleting irrelevant regions and merging these aligned models together. Alignment methods were investigated for analysing the 3D dataset. Parameterisation can provide an efficient solution to deal with unorganised point cloud for further analysis. In the study, a featured-based cross-parameterisation is used to remesh the 3D models of the external ear with a triangulation and subdivision method. The amount of points remained the same for individual ear models within each triangle. These parameterised models with a fixed number of vertexes can be further studied with multivariate analysis. After several tests, four anatomical points, including otobasion superius, incisura anterior auris posterior, otobasion posterius, and otobasion inferius, were used as the references for the landmark alignment. Objective 3: To find out the differences in 3D ear shapes among symmetry (left vs. right side), gender, and age groups. Objective 3 was successfully achieved. Anthropometric data from the external ear were analysed to reveal morphological characteristics for ergonomic design. Based on the selected landmarks during the parameterisation, dimensions were extracted from the 3D point clouds using programs written in Matlab. In the study, eight dimensions, including ear length, ear width, ear protrusion, earlobe length, earlobe width, concha length, concha width, and concha depth, were selected to describe the main components of the external ear. These dimensions were compared with the traditional measurements. The ear dimensions were then analysed to investigate the ear variances under different variables. Correlation coefficients were computed to evaluate the association between ear dimensions and other variables, including body height, weight, head sizes and ear symmetry. Two-way ANOVA was applied to explore the influences of gender and age. The results provided a general picture of ear variances in the auricle, concha and earlobe parts. Objective 4: To investigate the classification of the ear. Objective 4 was successfully achieved. Cluster analysis was conducted using multiple anthropometric ear dimensions. To clearly show the process, concha region was used as an example to explore the human variability. Based on three concha dimensions, the ear models were classified into five clusters using a two-stage cluster analysis. Since there were quite few numbers of clusters for the ear, multivariate analysis was further conducted to study the 3D ear anthropometry for design use. When considering sizing and grading, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) method was used to transform the dimensionality of the 3D database into a lower dimensional space. After that, the size and shape variance of the external ear was represented with several Principal Components (PCs). The concha models were analysed to generate a set of statistical models with the PCA algorithm. The average model was generated as the initial shape model. In order to reduce the dimensions, three most important PCs were kept to demonstrate the major ear variance and create the statistical models. Objective 5: To create an ear sizing system for ear-related product design. Objective 5 was successfully achieved. To address this objective, the relationship between 3D anthropometric data and human perception of comfort and fit was first investigated. A within-subject experiment with a Likert scale questionnaire was designed and conducted. 3D anthropometry was applied to determine the product size considering the variation of ear shape and size among individuals. A set of prototypes were individually designed and 3D printed for each 3D ear model. Each prototype was tested in two using conditions, static and dynamic. The mathematical models were generated to quantify the relationships between product size and human perception. Based on the above findings, an ear sizing system was developed for the 3D ear database. The average ear model was used as the 3D template for design applications. For a specific design, the region of interest was identified on the template model. The points in the designated area were accordingly extracted from each point cloud in the database. The design range was represented with the statistical models generated using the PCA method. The product shape and size were determined based on the representative models of the extracted region. The average 3D model was then used as the initial product size, and further deformed with the size interval suggested from the experiment on human perception. To provide proper fit, all the product sizes should be selected within the design range. Objective 6: To find out the comfort and fit perception using one ear product with size and weight variations. Objective 6 was successfully achieved. A full-shell in-the-ear (ITE) product was designed to validate the sizing system. The comfort and fit perception of the product was examined with digital evaluation and prototype test. From the above findings on human perception, a size interval was selected to determine the product sizes. After checking the size difference among the statistical models, five preliminary sizes were proposed for further fit evaluation. Digital fit evaluation was conducted to finalise and assess the proposed sizes. The product sizes should provide proper fit for the design range which was represented by the statistical models. The region of interest on each product model was aligned with the 3D statistical models using the ICP algorithm. For each statistical ear model, the best fit product model can be selected. Since the smallest and the largest one cannot provide the best fit for any of the ear models, three product sizes were finalised for this design.

15622016.label: Major findings and research outcome
15622016.value: After a systematic literature review on ear anthropometry and its design application, the entire study was structured with a solid research framework. Potential research methods and techniques were also compared to address the objectives. One peer-reviewed publication (PartC: 8-4) has arisen from this work. The 3D anthropometric database was established with landmark alignment and cross-parameterisation techniques. Accordingly, ear morphology was investigated under different demographic factors, including gender, age, and symmetry. Dimensions on the pinna, concha, and earlobe were extracted and analysed. Strong correlations were found between the left and right ear. Males had larger ear sizes than females. The size changes among the age groups varied for different ear regions. Multivariate analysis of the database was conducted using the PCA algorithm. A set of statistical models were generated to represent the variance of ear size and shape. Analysis of the anthropometric data are valuable for assisting related design and medical applications. This work contributed to three peer-reviewed publications (Part C: 8-1; 8-2; 8-6) and two conference publications (Part C: 9-1; 9-4). To apply anthropometric data into product design, human perception was investigated under different factors. Comfor and fit perceptions were investigated and discussed (Part C: 8-3, 9-2). After several pilot studies (Part C: 9-5; 9-6), a within-subject experiment was designed. The influences of gender, symmetry, concha size, using condition and product size were examined for the comfort and fit perception. The results indicated that product size and using condition had main effects on human perception. Moreover, the relationship between 3D anthropometric data and human perception was quantified for design use. A list of research-driven design guidelines was proposed based on the findings. The main work contributed to one peer-review publication (Part C: 8-5). Lastly, the ergonomic application was studied based on anthropometry and user experience. A sizing system was developed from the above findings, and validated with digital evaluation and prototype test. For ear-related products, the design range was defined within the 5th to 95th percentile of the ear variance identified by the PCA algorithm. ICP algorithm was used to fit the product with the ear region. The fit errors were used to estimate the comfort and fit level. The actual user perception was investigated with a prototype test. Different sizes were 3D printed and tested with a controlled experiment. The results revealed that the selected sizes could provide proper comfort and fit for the participants. Two peer-reviewed publications (Part C: 8-6, 8-7) have arisen from this work.

15622016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15622016.value: The 3D ear anthropometric database in this study contains different ear regions on the external ear. Designers and engineers can efficiently generalise complex anthropometric information from the database for designing various related products. In order to generalise a more holistic understanding of the ear morphology, more data covering other ethnical groups can be added to the database. Other AI techniques can be developed to support further 3D anthropometric study efficiently. In addition, the evaluation of different factors that influence human perception can provide theoretical guidance for product design, particularly for concha-related products. The 3D anthropometry-based research method can be helpful for future research on various products. The mathematical trendlines of comfort and fit perception contributed to a quantitative relationship between human perception and product size, which can help to determine product size based on the expected level of comfort and fit. It can also be used to evaluate the comfort and fitness level for existing commercial products and address whether the products need to be improved. Using the similar research methods, further studies to link anthropometric data with human perception can be conducted to enrich the understanding of user experience for various products.

15622016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15622016.value: Nowadays, various ear-related products are widely used to assist audition or accomplish other functions in everyday life. To provide effective fit, a sizing system should be properly developed considering both ear anthropometry and human perception. A database containing 3D ear models is valuable to provide design references for ear related products design and development. The differences in ear symmetry, gender, and age groups enrich the knowledge of ear morphology based on 3D anthropometry. The size and shape variances of the 3D ear models were explored by statistical analysis. As for user experience, demographic factors and product parameters were assessed based on comfort and fit perception. The relationship between 3D anthropometric data and human perception was quantified. These findings can help to determine product size based on the expected level of comfort and fit, and also be used to evaluate the comfort and fit level for determined product sizes. Moreover, the sizing and grading system considering 3D anthropometry and human perception was developed as a design tool. Both digital and perceived fit evaluation was proposed and validated for ear-related product design.

15622416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15622416.value: 建立社會服務可達性的社會空間模型 - 以食物援助服務為例

15622416.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15622416.value: Dr Ho, Po Ying Amy Dr Pun-Cheng, Lilian Shuk-ching

15622416.label: Project Objectives
15622416.value: To validate and analyze attributions of the four socio-spatial dimensions in service accessibility, To identify concerns and difficulties of users and non-users with respect to their service accessibilities, and thus To develop a socio-spatial model of social service accessibility
rows: To validate and analyze attributions of the four socio-spatial dimensions in service accessibility,
To identify concerns and difficulties of users and non-users with respect to their service accessibilities, and thus
To develop a socio-spatial model of social service accessibility

15622416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15622416.value: Good social service planning is important. It ensures accountable use of public monies and service improvement. Conventionally, programme planners and policy makers often refer to service data and evidence of current provisions for further planning. They usually perform statistical analyses of these data to aid their tasks. Although these analyses definitely generate valuable information, the limitations are negligence towards possible spatial characteristics of these social data and their effects. All human activities have social and spatial dimensions, which mean there always carry some meanings how, where and when they occur, or do not occur. Provisions of social services are of no exception. Users may or may not be provided the services they needed due to various reasons such as accessibility. In this proposed study, the research team suggests a socio-spatial model in understanding service accessibility and applies it to analyze four types of food assistance services in Hong Kong - foodbank, community kitchen, bulk purchase scheme and parity shop. It is believed that better understanding of the socio-spatial concerns and difficulties affecting users’ accessibility to social service will help better planning and delivery of social services to the needy groups in our community, both more efficiently and effectively. The team believes that research outcomes and knowledge developed in this showcase can demonstrate a new direction and method of social service planning, benefiting both Hong Kong and other regions in the long run. 良好的社會服務規劃十分重要。它可確保公共資源用得其所，並協助服務的改進。過往，規劃和決策者經常憑藉服務數據，以統計學的分析方法來進行規劃，其限制是對這些社會數據的空間特徵或會有所疏忽。所有人類活動都有其社會和空間維度，意味著相關活動如何、在何處及何時發生或不發生，都有其空間上的含義。社會服務的交付當然也不例外。服務使用者可能因為各種空間原因而得不到所需的服務。在此研究中，研究團隊提出一個協助理解服務可達性的社會空間模型，並用於分析香港的四類食物援助服務 – 食物銀行、社區廚房、集體採購計劃和平價店之上。我們認為，若更能了解社會空間因素對服務使用者的影響，將有助為社區中的困難群體提供更適切的社會服務。團隊認為，研究成果將會為社會服務規劃提出一個新的方向和方法；長遠而言，有利於香港及其他地區。

15634516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15634516.value: 溝通於年老病人由急症過渡到基礎醫療護理的過程所擔當的重要角色

15634516.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15634516.value: Prof Chan, Engle Angela Dr Lam, Man Kit Marvin Prof Lee, Albert Dr Rider, Elizabeth A. MD Prof Semino, Elena Prof Slade, Diana Dr Tang, Simon YH MD

15634516.label: Project Objectives
15634516.value: Obtain the AED and AEDOP clinicians’ and the elderly patients’ views on the expectations of effective communication during patient transition from the AED to the AEDOC, and the possible factors affecting the continuity of care. Observe, analyse and describe the spoken communication encounters between the clinicians and elderly patients in the final consultations immediately prior to discharge from AED and then during the same patients’ initial visits to the AED outpatient clinic. Combining video/audio-recorded observations, follow-up interviews and a Patient Activation Measure (PAM) to investigate elderly patients’ understanding of their treatment plans and describe the ways in which the patients are involved in decision-making process about their transitions of care. Provide a comprehensive description of language features and discourse strategies likely to increase patient involvement, comprehension and therefore adherence to treatment during their transition of care. Develop Communication Frameworks and recommendations to improve: a) effective transfer of information between AED clinicians and AED outpatient clinicians; b) patients’ understanding of information provided during the transition; c) patients’ willingness and ability to adhere to continuing care plans; d) clinicians’ communication skills development.

15634516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15634516.value: 病人的安全和護理溝通有密切的關係，其於醫護人員交接和其他醫療護理的過渡程序尤其明顯。此等程序涉及醫護人員或護理團隊之間對病人所負責任與問責的移交。不完善的溝通為醫院中不理想事件和可避免的病人重返急症室的主要起因1,2。在本研究計劃的共同研究員 Slade 帶領的三個研究項目，我們的研究團隊已經探討溝通在急症室和護理交接的重要性，並展示溝通問題的程度和影響，和其與病人安全的關聯。以這些研究作為基礎，本研究計劃將辨識與提昇病人護理由急症室轉到門診時，醫護人員與病人之間有效交換診斷和出院資料的關鍵元素。研究對象為六十五歲以上的長者，因為此群組為香港急症室最大的使用群，而且長者對不理想事件與不良醫療結果尤其處於弱勢。 在此混合方法研究計劃，我們的團隊將收集質與量互補的數據，包括觀察的錄音或錄像、面談、以病人主動性尺度（Patient Activation Measure）所量度的醫護人員與病人互動評分等等，以便分析能作三角測定。我們將會紀錄與分析真實的醫護人員和病人在急症室的出院會診，和相同病人在其後門診的會診，以檢視病人護理過渡的有效程度。我們將以不同的調查方法（例如面談與抽查）與文本分析互補，以釐清於出院時和由急症室過渡到基礎醫療護理的過程中，溝通的障礙和與溝通有關的風險。 我們致力於轉化型研究，因此我們將建立適用於香港的醫療溝通框架，以改善急症室與基礎醫療護理間在病人護理的協調。此研究計劃得到主要研究人員麥蒂森和共同研究員 Slade領導的國際醫療溝通研究中心所支持。因此，本研究計劃將得到本地與世界各地在醫療溝通領域的頂尖學者支持。 此研究計劃有五項特別之處，令本計劃與實際情況接軌，適時和具影響力。第一，此計劃將集中研究最處於弱勢的社群之一：年老病人。此群組為香港急症室最大的使用群。第二，此計劃將追蹤病人由出院到基礎醫療護理的首個會診，而此等研究現時並不足夠。第三，此計劃將以語言學分析在重要交接時的真實溝通。第四，透過建立應用性的文本分析框架以描述醫護人員與病人之間的雙語溝通，本計劃將了解醫護人員與病人於高壓力的急症環境的溝通情況。最後，此計劃將提供以證據為基礎的溝通技巧框架。此框架將會領導介入性的發展，以改善醫療過程的溝通技巧，並幫助制訂教學材料，以裨益現在與將來的醫護人員。此計劃的總體目的為增強由急症到基礎醫療護理的持續性。計劃將會有五項可持續與具策略性的成果：描述可改善病人安全的特性，辨識有效溝通的障礙，風險因素的描述，對改善溝通的建議，與溝通框架的發展。

15640416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15640416.value: 中學生在中文(一語)和英文(二語)綜合寫作中的認知過程

15640416.label: Project Objectives
15640416.value: To design and pilot instruments and protocols (including integrated writing tasks, rubrics, especially eye-tracking data collection and analysis system, interviews), collect and analyze preliminary data, thus establish the research questions and plan for the major study. To preliminarily identity the cognitive process which have a significant effect on the IW task performance in Chinese (L1). To preliminarily identity the cognitive process which have a significant effect on the IW task performance in English (L2). To preliminarily examine the similarities and differences between the cognitive processes employed in performing the two tasks of Chinese (L1) and English (L2). To preliminarily contribute to better understanding of the construct of IW tasks and the theory development of IW from the perspectives of cognitive processing.

15640416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15640416.value: Integrated writing (IW) has become increasingly popular in both first (L1) and second language (L2) teaching and assessment; however, most empirical studies were conducted in L2 context, only very few studies looked at IW in Chinese as L1. Furthermore, we noticed that the vast majority of the studies were product-oriented, i.e., with the written output as the primary unit of analysis. There is a dearth of research on writers’ cognitive processes in completing IW tasks. The very few studies that did investigate writers’ cognitive processes involved a small number of adult participants and tended to focus on some limited aspects of cognitive process, without systematically taking into account the complex nature of the dynamics of cognitive process. This proposed study aims to address these research gaps by comparing a large number of Hong Kong secondary school students’ cognitive processes when completing IW tasks in both Chinese (L1) and English (L2). In Stage 1 of the study, 360 Secondary Six students will complete two IW tasks in Chinese and in English. The students’ writings will be evaluated, both holistically and analytically. The analytical assessment aims to understand the extent and type of cognitive processing (see Table 1) involved in the writings; and the holistic assessment, the overall quality of test performance. Structural equation modeling (SEM) will be used to explore the underlying construct and relationships between different aspects of cognitive processing, as well as the relationships between cognitive processing and overall test performance. In Stage 2, another 36 Secondary Six students will complete the two writing tasks on computer, and their eye-movements during the test will be recorded. Immediately after a participant completes the two tasks, we will conduct stimulated recall interview with him/her, using episodes of the recorded eye-movements as stimuli to further explore their cognitive process. The SEM of the cognitive processes identified from the writings, the eye-movements and interviews are the three interrelated data sources, but from different perspectives. Not only the product (the writings they would produce) but equally importantly their cognitive processes as evidenced in their eye-movements throughout the whole duration of the tasks are analysed to explore the dynamics of cognitive process in IW tasks and the similarities and differences between L1 and L2 tasks.

15662516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15662516.value: 貨物多式聯運糾紛案件的管轄權:中國的做法和其他選定司法管轄區的比较研究

15662516.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15662516.value: Prof Chuah, Jason Dr Jessen, Henning Prof Sturley, Michael F.

15662516.label: Project Objectives
15662516.value: To search for and compile a register of jurisdictional rules under a number of national legislations, including those of China (both Chinese mainland and Hong Kong law will be included), the UK, the US and Germany, as well as EU law and international conventions; To evaluate rules identified under Chinese law by comparing them with rules identified in other national laws, and in regional and international conventions; To analyze specific issues related to court jurisdiction and jurisdiction agreement under Chinese law.
rows: To search for and compile a register of jurisdictional rules under a number of national legislations, including those of China (both Chinese mainland and Hong Kong law will be included), the UK, the US and Germany, as well as EU law and international conventions;
To evaluate rules identified under Chinese law by comparing them with rules identified in other national laws, and in regional and international conventions;
To analyze specific issues related to court jurisdiction and jurisdiction agreement under Chinese law.

15662516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15662516.value: Multimodal transport now plays a vital role in the carriage of goods for international trade. The development of multimodal transport in China is maintaining its great opportunistic momentum with continuing governmental support, especially since the more recent “One Belt, One Road” initiative. Therefore, the regulation of multimodal transport and applicable contracts is a matter of urgency and importance, both internationally and within China. Among several emerging issues, developing a coherent legal system for dispute settlement is vitally important, since disputes are an unavoidable occurrence. When a dispute arises, the question comes up as to where the court proceedings can be instituted or whether the dispute can instead be arbitrated. Previous discussions of China’s multimodal transport law largely focus either on liability issues or on the feasibility of China’s entry into an international convention such as the Rotterdam Rules. These studies show the complexity and importance of a coherent legal system to regulate multimodal transport. However, little has been done to directly answer the following questions with regard to Chinese law: Are there any existing legal rules that can be applied to determining jurisdiction? Are such legal rules mandatory? This then leads to another key question: Could those rules be overridden by the contract agreement? Therefore, it becomes both necessary and important for an investigation into the jurisdiction of Chinese courts and the role of jurisdiction agreement, whether for court jurisdiction or arbitration, in regard to multimodal transport under Chinese law. This proposed research aims to accomplish this task. In addition, the fact that similar issues constantly arise within the international multimodal transport system also necessitates a comparative study of jurisdictional rules under other selected jurisdictions, which is another aim of this proposed research. Accordingly, this proposed research will be divided into four interrelated study parts, employing varied research methods over a 36-month period. It is designed so as to identify the jurisdiction of Chinese courts, to explore the validity of jurisdiction agreements within the multimodal transport system under Chinese law and, in addition, to compare the Chinese approach with the approaches adopted in other selected jurisdictions, including the US, UK and Germany (taking into account that EU law also governs this area with direct effect). The expected outcome will serve as a valuable reference work, since transparency, clarity and consistency in this respect is essential to the development of international trade, as well as of international and domestic multimodal transport. 多式聯運已成為國際貿易中貨物運輸的重要手段。在政府的支持，尤其是最近的“一帶一路”倡議下，中國多式聯運的發展也保持了極大的機會勢頭。因此，調整多式聯運和其合同是在國際法和中國法下都具有緊迫性和重要性的问题 。在多式聯運中發生爭端是必然現象，所以一個完整的解決爭端的法律體系是非常重要的。一旦發生爭議， 當事人常常很難抉定是應在法院提起訴訟還是應進行仲裁。 對於中国的多式联运的法律問題，以前的研究主要集中在對责任问题的讨论或中国加入某国际公约如鹿特丹规则的可行性。这些研究證實了一个完整的法律体系来調整多式联运的重要性。然而，几乎還没有研究直接回答以下的问题：中國目前是否有可用于确定管辖權的法律规定？如有，这样的法律规则是否具有强制性？此外，如合同有明確約定，爭端的解決是依據法律規定還是合同約定呢？因此，對中国法下法院對多式联运合同的管辖权和相關管辖协议(无论是法院管辖或者仲裁)的作用進行研究是非常有必要的。這項擬議研究的目標是完成這一任務。同時，類似的問題也不斷的在國際多式聯運系統內出現，因此也有必要對本研究中選定的幾個司法管轄區的法律規則與中國的法律進行比較研究，這也是本研究的另一個研究目標。 本研究將分為四個相互關聯的部分，在36個月期間採用不同的研究方法。該研究主要是為了確定中國法院在多式聯運中的的管轄權，探討管轄協議的效力，同時進行中國法與選定的其他司法管轄區包括美國，英國和德國(同時考慮到歐盟法律的影響）的法律的比較研究。預期的研究結果將会是很有价值的，因為這方面的法律的透明度，清晰度和一致性，對國際貿易，以及國際和國內多式聯運的發展是至關重要的。

15662516.label: Realisation of objectives
15662516.value: All of the three objectives have been achieved. For achieve Objective 1, we firstly conducted a comprehensive literature review of jurisdictional rules in the international conventions. Since multimodal transport is not yet regulated by any international convention, we investigated into the jurisdictional rules in the unimodal transport conventions, and considered their impact on international multimodal transport of goods contract. Secondly, we compiled a register of jurisdictional rules under Chinese (Chinese mainland) law, UK law, German law and US law. In order to provide a thorough discussion, we conducted a comprehensive literature review, including a review of such sources as academic journals, monographs, legislation, legal case reports and others. For achieving Objective 2, we firstly carried out a general review of the rules identified under Chinese law. Then, in order to facilitate a comparative legal study, we identified and summarized the legal provisions or rules specifically related to three main aspects under the four jurisdictions including China, Germany, UK and US. Those three main aspects are: (1) What are the usual options of places in which to institute proceedings in the rules identified? (2) Are there any restrictions on the options? And (3) what are the relations between jurisdiction and arbitration? For achieving Objective 3, we firstly conducted literature review from different resources: including academic publications (including journal papers and monographs in both Chinese and English languages), legislations, as well as legal cases decided in Chinese courts. We worked on two very relevant issues: (1) Forum selection clause in the international carriage of goods contract; and (2) maritime courts in China and their jurisdiction. Furthermore, we examined some other special topic related to multimodal transport of goods: one was about insurable interest in goods under multimodal transport in Chinese law; and the other discussed the use of electronic bill of lading in the transport of goods.

15662516.label: Major findings and research outcome
15662516.value: This research leads to publication of 5 journal articles (with 1 more in writing) and 2 conference papers and training of 5 part or full-time Research Assistants. Given the fact that uniform liability rules for international multimodal transport contracts of goods are still lacking, it is important to undertake a holistic study of the rules for resolving issues that may arise relating both to jurisdiction and to dispute resolutions in a contract for the international multimodal transport of goods. Zhu and Li (2018) thus carry out a general survey of jurisdiction rules in the unimodal transport conventions and discuss the possible impacts of those rules on international multimodal transport of goods contracts; and conclude that, unless the parties have clear and unequivocal agreements in their contracts, a set of jurisdiction rules for contracts for the multimodal transport of goods is both necessary and important. With the further development of China’s foreign trade and maritime activities, multimodal transport disputes in China are expected to be on the rise. Zhu and Li (2019) find that the rules of jurisdiction over disputes arising from the multimodal transport of goods are far from satisfactory. In addition, owning to the complexities and uncertainties in several aspects, Chinese courts may tend to insist on their own jurisdiction with the aim to protect the interests of Chinese parties. As a result, this may lead to conflicts over jurisdiction, which in the long run will have an adverse effect on China’s trade and investment environment. Furthermore, a number of specific issues related to court jurisdiction and multimodal transport under Chinese law are examined. In Zhang and Zhu (2018), we advocate a pecuniary interest approach to recognizing the insurance interest under property insurance; and by employing this approach, that the rightful parties having an insurance interest in goods under multimodal transport has been clarified. In addition to the local people’s courts at all levels, China has gradually established maritime courts specifically to adjudicate maritime claims and disputes within its statutory jurisdiction. Zhu and Li (2021) show that despite all the legislative efforts made so far, conflicts and uncertainties from time to time arise concerning the appropriate jurisdiction over maritime disputes and claims. Greater clarity and direction from the relevant authorities are thus needed for a better and more efficient system for deciding the jurisdiction of maritime cases in China. Furthermore, transport relies on shipping documents to facilitate its operation. Bills of lading, as one of the most important documents, have traditionally been in paper form. However, the last decades have seen continuous progress made in the development of electronic alternatives to the paper bill of lading. Zhu and Pan (2021) conduct a conceptual analysis of electronic bills of lading and identify that it is vitally necessary to adopt legal rules at both national and international levels, so as to clarify the legal status of an electronic bill of lading and facilitate its use in the transport of goods.

15662516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15662516.value: Apart from the importance to develop a coherent legal system for dispute settlement, multimodal transport of goods involves a variety of more issues, including liability, insurance and many others. Particularly, we have identified the importance of shipping documents. The electronic bill of lading emerges as a very interesting topic with a good potential of future development. This is very true given the current COVID-19 and slow/lock–down of many business sectors including shipping and international trade. We have already carried out a conceptual analysis of electronic bills of lading (see Zhu and Pan (2021)) during this research, and further study could be conducted on the challenges and prospects facing use of the electronic bill of lading.

15662516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15662516.value: The fragmented and complex patchwork of laws applying to multimodal transport may lead to involved parties having different consideration for forum shopping when dispute arises. This research examines the jurisdictional rules identified under Chinese law by comparing them with rules in other national laws and in international conventions, in multimodal transport. In particular, it discusses and examines a number of very important issues including the impact of unimodal transport conventions on the multimodal transport of goods; Chinese law approach for jurisdiction over disputes involving the multimodal transport of goods; Chinese maritime courts and its jurisdictions, and some other specific issues. Since disputes are an unavoidable occurrence, developing a coherent legal system for dispute settlement is very important. The findings in this research thus can inform future research and practice in the area of the law of the multimodal transport of goods.

15663716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15663716.value: 超越戶口：中國被城市化的農村居民的城市生活融入

15663716.label: Project Objectives
15663716.value: To implement an innovative and rigorous quasi-experimental survey methodology targeting in-situ urbanized rural residents of areas that have become urbanized since 2000 and develop survey data that are representative of the adult population residing in these newly urbanized areas. To assess the degree of in-situ urbanized rural residents’ integration into urban life according to a range of indicators, including living environment, employment and occupational status, children’s education, health status, psychological well-being, participation in community activities, and affective integration. To explore the range of policy innovations in those cities participating in the National New Urbanization Comprehensive Pilot Program in contrast to a carefully balanced control group. To identify how county-level variations in urbanization policy and government practice condition individuals’ living patterns, experience of urbanization, lifestyle changes, and socio-psychological well-being.

15663716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15663716.value: The speed and scale of China’s urbanization is unprecedented in human history. Local governments have been criticized for seeking financial gains through land sales, thus creating ‘urbanization of place’ rather than ‘urbanization of people’. Of the 440 million people who account for the urban population growth since 1979, about half are rural-to-urban migrants, whereas the rest are in-situ urbanized rural residents. Though there have been numerous studies devoted to the migrant population, scant attention has been paid to the experience and well-being of in-situ urbanized rural residents. Research is urgently needed to ascertain the impact of local government policies and practices on the ‘in-situ’ urbanization process, which affects the general well-being of formerly rural residents, as well as their integration into the various facets of urban life. We propose to develop a policy-driven quasi-experimental household survey that will take advantage of the implementation of the National New Urbanization Comprehensive Pilot Program. The survey will target residents of newly urbanized areas in 30 county-level cities and urban districts under prefectural-level or centrally administered municipalities. Half will be drawn from the ‘treatment’ group (i.e., cities listed in the National New Urbanization Comprehensive Pilot Program). The control group will consist of 15 cases that will be chosen using the Coarsened Exact Matching (CEM) technique. For each selected county-level unit, we will develop a geographical information system (GIS) that aggregates information at the arc-minute level in order to create spatial sample frames of physical areas undergoing ‘in-situ’ urbanization (i.e., newly urbanized areas that were classified as rural before 2000 and were incorporated after 2000 into urban districts under prefectural-level or centrally administered municipalities, or urban centres of county-level cities). At the township or village level, however, the actual selected localities may or may not have been reclassified as ‘urban’ (i.e., street district or neighborhood committee). The study will offer a comprehensive and nuanced examination of the changes in the living environments and lifestyles of in-situ urbanized rural residents, the extent to which they are entitled to urban welfare benefits and integrate into urban life, and the effects of local government policies and the urbanization process on their well-being. It will yield rich materials for analyzing Chinese urbanization and will also make a valuable contribution to the debates on hukou and related policy reforms. 中國人口遷移的規模和速度是人類史無前例的。地方政府經常被批評通過出讓土地來獲取財政收入，從而造成“空間的城市化”而不是“人的城市化。”在自1979年以來的4.4億城市人口增長當中，大約有一半是從農村遷移到城市的，而另一半則是被城市化的農村居民。目前關於從農村到城市的流動人口的研究很多，但對於被城市化的農村居民的經歷和生活關注極少。我們迫切的需要弄清楚地方政府推動城市化進程的政策和實踐的影響，尤其是被城市化的過程對於之前農村居民的福祉以及他們融入城市各方面生活的影響。 我們的研究計畫在國家新型城鎮化綜合試點方案的基礎上進行一項以此政策為導向的准實驗調查。調查的目標人群為居住在30個經歷新近城市化的縣級區域。其中的一半個案會從國家新型城鎮化綜合試點地區名單中抽取，另外一半作為控制組的15個個案則採用粗化的精確匹配技術從其餘的區縣抽取。對於每一個被選取的縣級單位，我們將採用地理資訊技術進一步抽取2000年以後被城市化的空間樣本。在鎮或村一級，最後被選中的地方可能也可能沒有轉為城鎮（街道或居委會）。 這項研究會對中國被城市化的農村居民的生存環境和生活方式、他們享有城市福利及融入城市生活的程度，以及地方政府政策和城市化過程對他們的影響提供更為全面、深入的理解。研究所產生的豐富資料對於分析中國有關戶口及相關政策改革的爭論將有重要意義。

16101116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16101116.value: 研究Arfrp1调控的反面高爾基網絡上的蛋白筛选过程

16101116.label: Project Objectives
16101116.value: To investigate how Arfrp1 achieves its specificity of sorting of Vangl2 at the TGN. We will analyze (a) whether Vangl2 binds the canonical cargo-binding site on AP-1, and (b) whether the binding interface between Arfrp1 and AP-1 is different from the interface between Arf1 and AP-1. To reveal other cargo proteins that depend on the Arfrp1/AP-1 machinery to exit the TGN. We will (a) test whether GLUT2, GLUT4, E-cadherin and PTK7 depend on the Arfrp1/AP-1 machinery for exiting the TGN, and (b) we will systematically reveal the cargo proteins that are co-enriched with Vangl2 in TGN-derived vesicles and test whether they depend on the Arfrp1/AP-1 machinery for exiting the TGN. To analyze Arfrp1-mediated protein sorting at the TGN through super-resolution imaging analysis. We will utilize 2-color super-resolution localization microscopy to analyze (a) the spatial relationship between Arfrp1 and other selective TGN-localized Arfs, (b) the spatial relationship between AP-1 and other selective TGN-localized clathrin adaptors, and (c) whether Vangl2 as well as other identified cargo proteins are specifically associated with AP-1 upon exiting the TGN.

16101116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101116.value: 反面高爾基網絡（TGN）是細胞內部一個重要的物質中轉站。很多的新合成的蛋白在TGN上被篩選到不同的囊泡中，然後這些囊泡被運輸到特定的位點。TGN上的篩選過程如果出現錯誤將導致新合成的蛋白被運送到錯誤的位點從而使它們不能行使正常的功能。TGN上的貨物蛋白篩選過程是由Arf蛋白家族引導的。盡管現今我們在研究Arf蛋白功能上取得了很大的進展，但是很多很重要的問題依然有待解決。比如，在哺乳動物中Arf蛋白家族有20多個成員，我們並不清楚哪些貨物蛋白能夠特異性的被某個Arf成員識別。另外Arf蛋白是如何選擇性的識別貨物蛋白的分子機制有待進一步的研究。並且我們還沒有用熒光顯微鏡直接觀察到貨物蛋白在TGN上被篩選入囊泡的過程。我們的目標是研究位於TGN上的一個Arf蛋白，Arfrp1, 在TGN上行使其蛋白篩選功能的機制。我們將通過分子細胞生物學和生物化學的方法研究Arfrp1是如何與參與貨物蛋白篩選的其他蛋白相互作用從而調控它們識別貨物蛋白。我們還將研究哪些貨物蛋白能夠被Arfrp1特異性的篩選入囊泡。另外，我們將用高分辨率熒光顯微鏡直接觀察Arfrp1所調控的貨物蛋白在TGN上被篩選入囊泡的過程。這些研究將有助於我們對Arf蛋白在TGN上被篩選到的囊泡過程有更加深入的了解。

16101116.label: Realisation of objectives
16101116.value: Realisation of Objective 1: We have performed GST pull down using purified His-tagged dominant active mutant Arfrp1 depleted of the N-terminal amphipathic helix and purified wild type AP-1 trunk domain. The results indicate that Arfrp1 also directly interacts with the AP-1 trunk domain. We found that mutating the key amino acids in the beta subunit of the AP-1 trunk domain that affects Arf1 binding did not interfere with Arfrp1 binding to AP-1 trunk domain. These analyses suggest that the binding interface between Arfrp1 and AP-1 is different from the interface between Arf1 and AP-1. We used yeast two hybrid assay to test whether Vangl2 binds the conventional tyrosine-motif-binding site on the mu subunit of AP-1 (mu1). We mutated the key residues in the conventional tyrosine-motif-binding site on mu1. We also mutated in the binding site that is predicted from the novel binding site of the mu subunit of AP-4. We found that mutations of both of the sites interfere with Vangl2 binding. This result suggests that both the conventional and unconventional tyrosine-motif-binding site on mu1 are important to bind Vangl2. Realisation of Objective 2： Arfrp1 is reported to regulate trafficking of GLUT2, GLUT4, E-cadherin and PTK7. We performed siRNA knockdown analyses and we found that knockdown of the gamma subunit of AP-1 did not interfere with surface delivery of E-cadherin and PTK7 suggesting that AP-1 does not regulate surface delivery of E-cadherin and PTK7. We do not have antibodies against GLUT2 and GLUT4 for immunofluorescence analysis and the tagged versions of GLUT2 and GLUT4 did not localize to the cell surface. Thus, we did not analyze whether AP-1 is important for surface delivery of GLUT2 and GLUT4. We have reconstituted vesicular release of Vangl2 at the trans Golgi network (TGN). Vangl2 and another planar cell polarity protein, Frizzled6, are located on the opposing cellular boundaries. To test whether Vangl2 and Frizzled6 were packaged into vesicles together or separately, we performed the TGN vesicle budding assay using COS7 cells co-transfected with FLAG-Vangl2 and HA-Frizzled6. We found that the immunoisolated Vangl2-enriched vesicles did not contain Frizzled6. As a control for our vesicle isolation experiment, we performed the vesicle formation assay using cells co-transfected with FLAG-Vangl2 and HA-Vangl2 and then immunoisolated the vesicles containing FLAG-Vangl2. We found a fraction of the vesicles enriched with HA-Vangl2 was co-isolated with FLAG-Vangl2, suggesting that the separation of Vangl2 and Frizzled6 was not due to disruption of vesicles. We analyzed the morphology of the immunoisolated vesicles by negative stain EM. The structures in the immunoisolated vesicle fraction containing FLAG-Vangl2 showed donut shapes which are typical morphology of transport vesicles when viewed under negative stain EM procedure. This work has been published in JBC in 2018. We have immunoisolated Vangl2-enriched vesicles in a large scale and performed a label-free quantitative mass spectrometry analysis to identify cargo proteins that specifically co-enriched with Vangl2 vesicles. We found a group of transmembrane cargo proteins that are co-enriched with Vangl2 in transport vesicles. One of the cargo protein is EGFR. Interestingly, we found that Arfrp1 and AP-1 also regulates TGN export of EGFR. Super-resolution imaging analysis indicates that EGFR is spatially associated with AP-1 and Arfrp1 upon TGN exit. We have identified a tyrosine sorting motif in EGFR that is important for EGFR to interact with AP-1 and for its TGN export process. A manuscript about this is in preparation for submitting. In addition, we found a TGN-localized transmembrane protein, Sys1, interacts with Vangl2. Knockdown analysis indicates that Sys1 is important for TGN-to-cell surface transport of Vangl2. Sys1 is reported to interact with Arfrp1 to regulate recruitment of Arfrp1 to the TGN. Interestingly, we found that Arfrp1 is recruited to the TGN independent of GTP binding. In addition, we found that Sys1 interacts with the amphipathic helix of Arfrp1 and this interaction allows the Arfrp1 amphipathic helix to be sufficient to bring cytosolic proteins to the TGN. These analyses uncover a novel mechanism that regulates TGN membrane recruitment of Arfrp1 and suggest the GTP binding and membrane association of Arfpr1 are uncoupled. Some of these findings are published in JBC in 2020. Realization of Objective 3 We performed two color super-resolution (SR) imaging analysis to analyze the spatial relationships between Arfrp1 and other Golgi-localized Arf proteins. We found that Arfrp1 is spatially segregated from Arf1 and Arf3. We then performed super-resolution (SR) imaging analysis to analyze the spatial relationships among TGN- and endosome- localized cargo adaptors, AP-1, AP-3 and epsinR. We found that AP-1 are largely separated from AP-3 and GGA2 at the juxtanuclear area. In contrast, epsinR structures showed two localization patterns: one associated with AP-1 and the other associated with GGA2. Knockdown analysis indicates that TGN export of Vangl2 and Frizzled6 are mediated by AP-1 and GGA2 respectively. Next we visualized these sorting events utilize two-color SR imaging. SR images of Vangl2 and AP-1 in 2-dimention and in 3-dimention showed that Vangl2 was enriched in membrane patches coated by AP-1 upon TGN exit. As a control, we found that the majority of Vangl2 structures were not associated with the AP-3, and the majority of Vangl2 (Y279A,Y280A) punctate structures were not adjacent to AP-1 upon TGN exit. The majority of Frizzled6 puncta were not associated with AP-1, consistent with our previous report that sorting of Frizzled6 is not mediated by AP-1. Moreover, we found that many Frizzled6 structures but not Vangl2 structures were associated with GGA2 upon TGN exit. These analyses indicate that TGN/endosome-localized Arf proteins and cargo adaptors have distinct spatial relationships. The spatially segregated cargo adaptors GGA2 and AP-1 regulate sorting of Frizzled6 and Vangl2, respectively and spatially associated cargo adaptors can cooperatively regulate a specific sorting process. The majority of these super-resolution imaging analyses are published in Frontier in Cell and Developmental Biology in 2019. In summary, we have addressed all of our objectives utilizing biochemical, cell biological and super-resolution imaging analyse, which revealed novel insights into Arfrp1-mediated TGN sorting process.

16101116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101116.value: 1) We found that the binding interface between Arfrp1 and AP-1 is different from the interface between Arf1 and AP-1, and that both the conventional and unconventional tyrosine-motif-binding site on AP-1 are important to bind Vangl2. 2) We have successfully immunoisolated Vangl2-enriched vesicles derived from the TGN. We found that Vangl2 and another planar cell polarity protein, Frizzled6, are packaged in separate vesicles at the TGN. We found a group of transmembrane cargo proteins that are co-enriched with Vangl2 in transport vesicles. One of the cargo protein is EGFR. We found that Arfrp1 and AP-1 also regulate TGN export of EGFR. Part of these findings have been published in JBC in 2018 (Please refer to Part C, 8). 3) We found a TGN localized transmembrane protein, Sys1, regulates TGN export of Vangl2. Further analysis indicates that Sys1 interacts with the amphipathic helix of Arfrp1 to recruit Arfrp1 to the TGN in a GTP-independent manner. The majority of these findings have been published in JBC in 2020 (Please refer to Part C, 8). 4) We performed two-color STORM super-resolution analyses. We found that Arfrp1 is spatially segregated from Arf1 and Arf3; AP-1 is spatially segregated from other TGN-localized cargo adaptors, GGA2 and AP-3; a fraction of epsinR structures is associated with AP-1 and a fraction of epsinR structures are associated with GGA2; the planar cell polarity cargo proteins, Vangl2 and Frizzled6 associate with different cargo adaptors-AP-1 and GGA2 or epsinR, respectively-when exiting the TGN. Our data indicates that TGN/endosome-localized cargo adaptors have distinct spatial relationships. The spatially segregated cargo adaptors GGA2 and AP-1 regulate sorting of Frizzled6 and Vangl2, respectively and spatially associated cargo adaptors can cooperatively regulate a specific sorting process. The majority of these super-resolution imaging analyses have been published in Frontier in Cell and Developmental Biology in 2019 (Please refer to Part C, 8).

16101116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101116.value: Our STORM imaging analysis provides a view of the spatial relationships among the key factors that regulate protein sorting at the TGN at high resolution. Can the spatially segregated cargo adaptors, such as AP-1 and GGA2, function to regulate sorting of distinct groups of cargo proteins? We are currently addressing this question utilizing the in vitro reconstituted vesicle formation assay. Our study indicates that Arfrp1 recruits AP-1 at specific TGN subdomains to regulate packaging of a specific group of cargo proteins, including Vangl2 and EGFR, into transport vesicles. These findings suggest that associations of Arf proteins with cargo adaptors can functionally regulate the specificity of the cargo adaptors to recognize cargo molecules. We are performing biochemical and two-color and three-color super-resolution imaging analysis to test this hypothesis.

16101116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101116.value: This proposal aims to analyse Arfrp1 mediated protein sorting at the TGN. Our previous analysis indicates that Arfrp1 mediates membrane recruitment of AP-1, opening the cargo binding pocket of AP-1 to allow direct interaction of AP-1 with its cargo, Vangl2. Another Arf protein, Arf1, also mediates membrane association of AP-1. In this study, we found that the binding interface between Arfrp1 and AP-1 is different from the interface between Arf1 and AP-1, and that both the conventional and unconventional tyrosine-motif-binding site on AP-1 are important to bind Vangl2. Moreover, we identified several cargo proteins that are enriched with Vangl2 in transport vesicles. One of these cargo proteins, EGFR, also depends on the Arfrp1/AP-1 machinery to be exported out of the TGN. Super-resolution imaging analyses indicate that Arfrp1 is spatially segregated from Arf1. We showed that TGN/endosome-localized cargo adaptors have distinct spatial relationships. The spatially segregated cargo adaptors GGA2 and AP-1 regulate sorting of Frizzled6 and Vangl2, respectively and spatially associated cargo adaptors can cooperatively regulate a specific sorting process. Our study provides novel insights into Arfrp1-mediated TGN sorting process, suggesting that Arfrp1 recruits AP-1 at specific TGN subdomains to regulate packaging of a specific group of cargo proteins into vesicles.

16111616.value: 雖然內耳毛細胞的機械傳導(MT)機制巳經被深入研究了四十年, 但負責的通道分子身份仍然是個謎。 TMC1蛋白最近被認定為在毛細胞的MT中扮演重要角色, 但它的確切功能還不是很清楚: 是MT複合體的通道孔隙還是一個依附其上的蛋白。 要剖析TMC1的功能及調控、必須研究TMC1與其他蛋白的相互作用。據報導TMHS能在不與TMC1相互連結下對其進行調控。 有趣的是, 我們最近的數據表明, TMHS與TMC1能作實體連結、特别是與TMC1的第二個細胞內片段(TMC1-3 F)。 重要的是, P514L 和 D572H這兩個位於TMC1-F3導致失聰的突變似乎能影響與TMHS的實體連結。 此外, TMHS能增加TMC1 在293T 細胞内的表達。基於這些觀察, 我們提出以下的假說: 1)TMHS 能與TMC1(TMC1-3 F) 的細胞内第二個片段作實體連結, 從而穩定TMC1在細胞表面的表達; 2)有些自然發生的失聰TMC-F3突變中, 因其能擾亂 TMC1-TMHS相互作用, 從而干擾TMC1 在毛細胞表面的表達及機械傳導 (MT)。 此外, 因缺乏高質量的TMC1抗體，TMC1在毛細胞内的位置尚未確立。為解决這一重要問题, 我們用 CRISPR/ Cas9 技術構建了TMC1-FLAG 的敲入老鼠株。 我們計畫使用該老鼠株和其他帶有標記的TMC1老鼠株, 分析細胞内源生TMC1的位置, 空間折疊及跟TMHS的連結。 此外, 為了克服傳统Western blotting 和 co-IP 技術研究罕見細胞如毛細胞的局限性, 我們發展微流體技術 microfluidic western blotting 和單分子沉澱技術以便適合于研究 TMC1 和 TMHS 在毛細胞中的作用。 在本研究計畫書中, 我們有四項具體目標: 1) 鍳定TMC1 和 TMHS的生化性質; 2) 檢測TMC1 和 TMHS的實體連結; 3) 研究TMHS 能調控TMC1 在細胞表面的表達; 4) 測試TMHS如何調控 TMC1在細胞表面的表達。 越来越多証據表明, TMC1 和 TMHS 是在毛細胞內至關重要的機械傳導 (MT); 因此, 了解它們之間的實體連結及功能互動尤為重要。 我們的多學科研究將揭示這關键問题的答案,相關的技術平台開發更可以成為研究毛細胞的強大工具。

16111616.label: Realisation of objectives
16111616.value: 1. To characterize the biochemical properties of TMC1 and TMHS a. To develop microfluidic western blotting (μWestern blotting) and single-molecule pull-down techniques for studying hair cells. During this report period, we developed two bead-based single-molecule pull down (SiMPull) techniques: (1) agarose microbead-based SiMPull for cell population; and (2) magnetic nanobead-based SiMPull for cell populations and single cells. The work on microbead-based SiMPull is submitted for publication and currently under review of “Cell Chemical Biology” (see “outcomes” and attachments); the work on nanobead-based SiMPull is being prepared for publication (see meeting abstract in “outcomes”). Moreover, we utilized the simplicity and power of microbead-based SiMPull to investigation physical and functional interactions of TMC1-TMHS (LHFPL5), and this work is currently under revision of “PNAS” (see “outcomes” and attachments). In addition, the techniques have obtained a provisional US patent (see “outcomes”) and is currently under filing for formal patents in US and China, supported by The Technology Transfer Center of HKUST. Please see the paper under review of “Cell Chemical Biology” for additional details. As to uWestern blotting, after 1-year testing, we succeeded in setting up the assay and using it for analysing proteins overexpressed in HEK293 cells. Currently, we are still optimizing the assay for studying hair cells. b. To assess the subcellular localization and topology of TMC1. As to the localization of TMC1 and TMHS, we generated some very valuable tools including TMC1-FLAG knocking mice and anti-TMC1 antibodies and examined the subcellular localization of TMC1 and TMHS in neonatal and adult mice. This work has been published in the prestigious “FASEB Journal”. This part of work greatly exceeds the expectation of the proposal because the original plan was to assess the hair-cell localization of TMC1 only, but not TMHS. Please see the FASEB paper for additional details. c. To test the turnover rate and tonotopic gradient of TMC1 and TMHS. Detection of TMC1 or TMHS is essential for these experiments. To facilitate TMHS detection, we generated TMHS-HA knockin mice as well (see the paper under revision of PNAS). However, we found that TMC1 and TMHS in hair cells, tagged or not, could not be detected by conventional wester blotting. Thus, we used microbead-SiMPull to address these questions. We treated cultured organs of Corti from TMC1-FLAG knockin mice with CHX for different times and the quantified TMC1 levels with microbead-SiMPull. We found that the half-life of TMC1 is about 9 hrs. We also used the microbead-based SiMPull to examine the tonotopic gradient of TMC1 expression. More experiments will be carried out for this part for potential publication. 2. To examine the physical interaction of TMC1 and TMHS. a. To examine the interaction of endogenous TMC1 and TMHS in the hair cells. b. Identification of precise interaction sites. Both sub-aims have been accomplished and the work is submitted for publication and currently under revision of “PNAS” (attachments). The microbead-based SiMPull aforementioned is instrumental for the in vivo examination of TMC1-TMHS interaction. Please see additional details in the attached manuscript. 3. To investigate whether TMHS binding regulates TMC1 surface expression. We found that TMHS stabilizes TMC1 in heterologous system and hair cells, and more importantly, that TMHS enhances TMC1 expression in the tip of stereocilia of hair cells. Furthermore, we demonstrated that deafness mutation D572H/N disrupts TMC1-TMHS mutation. This work (together with the results from Specific Aim 2) is submitted for publication and is currently under revision of “PNAS”. Please see the attached manuscript for additional details. 4. To test how TMHS binding regulates TMC1 surface expression. To test the molecular mechanism underlying the regulation of TMC1 by TMHS as proposed, it is essential to detect cell-surface TMC1 in either heterologous systems or hair cells. Cell-surface expression of TMC1 in heterologous systems is notoriously difficult and is a major technical bottleneck for rigorous assessment of TMC1 channel activity in the field because ectopic TMC1 is trapped in the ER. We used two strategies in an attempt to drive TMC1 into the cell surface: (1) we co-expressed TMC1 with various proteins including the components in the mechanotransduction (MT) complex (TMHS, TMIE, PCDH15, and CIB2) and other proteins that promote cell-surface expression of membrane proteins in general (various Rab proteins); (2) removal of different parts of TMC1. The rationale for this approach is that we speculated some part of TMC1 protein may bind to an ER resident protein that is absent in hair cells and therefore is trapped in the ER in heterologous systems. Unfortunately, neither of the methods appear to achieve any significant cell-surface expression of TMC1 despite of investment of considerable amount of time and efforts. To the best of our knowledge, no laboratory has overcome this problem yet. As to the cell-surface expression of TMC1 in hair cells, we used cell-surface biotinylation combined with the microbead-based SiMPull. However, the initial results are inconclusive, probably because the amount of TMC1 in the cell-surface (or in the MT complex) is already small and the fraction of biotinylated TMC1 is even smaller. Nevertheless, all these experiments provide valuable experience and lay a solid foundation for future endeavour on this extremely challenging yet fascinating key problem.

16111616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16111616.value: This proposal aims to examine the localization, and physical and functional interactions of TMC1 and TMHS (LHFPL5), two key components in the mechanotransduction complex of inner-ear hair cells. During the reporting period of the proposal, we have made the following notable findings: 1) We examined the localization of TMC1 and LHFPL5 in neonatal and adult hair cells. Our findings raise intriguing questions regarding the turnover rate, regulation, additional functions, and functional interaction of TMC1 and LHFPL5. Our study confirms the previous findings in neonatal hair cells and reveals several previously unidentified aspects of TMC1 and LHFPL5 localization in more mature hair cells. This work has been published in the prestigious journal “The FASEB Journal”. 2) We examined the interaction between TMC1 and LHFPL5 by using multiple approaches, including our newly developed ultrasensitive microbead-based single-molecule pulldown (SiMPull) assay. We demonstrated that LHFPL5 physically interacted with and stabilized TMC1 in both heterologous expression systems and hair cells. Moreover, the semi-dominant deafness mutation D572N in human TMC1 (D569N in mouse TMC1) severely disrupted LHFPL5 binding and destabilized TMC1 expression. Thus, our findings reveal previously unrecognized physical and functional interactions of TMC1 and LHFPL5 and provide insights into the molecular mechanism by which the D572N mutation causes deafness. In addition, these findings present a missing link in the physical organization of the mechanotransduction macromolecular complex. Furthermore, this study has demonstrated the power of the microbead-based SiMPull assay for biochemical study of rare cells such as hair cells. This work is currently under revision of “PNAS”. 3) We developed an innovative, agarose microbead-based approach for SiMPull. Relative to the original method by Jain et al., microbead-based SiMPull is considerably faster, easier to use, and more reproducible and yet provides similar sensitivity and signal-to-noise ratio; specifically, with the new method, sample-preparation time is substantially decreased (from ~10 to ~3 h). These crucial features should facilitate wide application of powerful and versatile SiMPull in common biological and clinical laboratories. Notably, by exploiting the simplicity and ultrahigh sensitivity of microbead-based SiMPull, we used this method in the study of rare auditory hair cells for the first time. This work is currently under review of “Cell Chemical Biology.” In addition, we developed another magnetic nanobead-based SiMPull for cell populations and single cells; this work is being prepared for publication. Furthermore, we are applying patents for both micro and nano bead-based SiMPull.

16111616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16111616.value: As a result of the research of the proposal, we made a major technical innovation: microbead-based SiMPull. By demonstrating the power of the microbead-based SiMPull assay for the biochemical examination of rare cells such as hair cells, we opens up a new avenue for the biochemical investigation of MT-complex proteins and other critical non-abundant proteins in hair cells, which proved to be technically challenging in previous research on hair cells and other rare cells. We will use the method to explore various issues such as posttranslational modification, turnover, and stoichiometry of the MT complex and other critical proteins in hair cells.

16111616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16111616.value: This proposal aims to study the properties and interactions of TMC1 and TMHS (LHFPL5), two key proteins for sensing sounds by inner-ear hair cells. We have made the following notable findings: 1) We examined the localization of TMC1 and LHFPL5 in hair cells. Our study confirms the previous findings in neonatal hair cells and reveals several new aspects of TMC1 and LHFPL5 localization in more mature hair cells. Our findings support the important roles of both proteins in sensing sounds. 2) We examined the interaction between TMC1 and LHFPL5 by using our newly developed ultrasensitive microbead-based single-molecule pulldown (SiMPull) assay. We demonstrated that LHFPL5 physically interacted with and stabilized TMC1 in sensory hair cells. Moreover, the deafness mutation D572N in human TMC1 severely disrupted LHFPL5 binding and destabilized TMC1 expression. These findings explain why D572N mutation causes deafness and have important physiological and clinical implications. 3) We developed two innovative agarose microbead-based and magnetic nanobead-based approaches for SiMPull. These methods are super sensitive and easy to use, and enable detection of small amount of proteins. These methods are valuable tools for studying rare cells such as sensory hair cells, circulating tumor cells, and stem cells.

16118416.label: Realisation of objectives
16118416.value: Objective 1: Structure determination of Geminin/Cdt1 complexes containing the newly identified binding regions using multidimensional NMR and crystallization approaches. (100% completed) 1. We confirmed the interaction between the coiled-coil domain of human Geminin and a C-terminal peptide of human Cdt1 by NMR titration experiments. 2. We completed backbone and sidechain assignments for the C-terminal peptide of human Cdt1. 3. We obtained high-quality protein samples for the coiled-coil domain of human Geminin and completed its backbone assignments. 4. We uncovered a new interaction interface between the C-terminus of Geminin and the C-terminal peptide of human Cdt1. 5. We made a fusion protein that links the N-terminus and C-terminus of Cdt1, and completed the backbone and sidechain assignments for this fusion protein. 6. We performed NMR titrations between the Geminin C-terminus and the fused Cdt1 protein. The peak assignments and structure determination are in progress. In addition, we are working on mutational experiment to study the functional impact of disrupting these two Geminin/Cdt1 binding interfaces. 7. We have also started MCM complex binding assay to study the inhibition of Cdt1-recruitment of MCM complex by Geminin. Based on the above findings, we are now preparing a manuscript titled “Structural insight of human Geminin-Cdt1 complex for inhibition of the replication licensing”. Objective 2: Structure determination of Geminin/MCM6 complexes by multidimensional NMR (80% completed). The major difficulty for structure study of Geminin/MCM6 complex is that the stable N-terminal domain of Mcm6 that interacts with Geminin is too large for NMR to cope with. As the single particle cryo-EM becomes a mature technique for structural study of super-biomolecular assembly and HKUST has the high end cryo-EM equipment, we decided to pursue the structural determination of the Cdt1/Geminin/Mcm2-7 complex by cryo-EM assisted with NMR technique for the remaining time of the proposed study. We have successfully obtained soluble human Mcm2-7 complex sample for cry-EM study as follows. The published approaches to obtain recombinant hsMcm2-7 complexes involve the expression of each hsMcm2-7 component in insect cells or E. coli and purification using normal purification schemes, followed by assembly of hsMcm2-7 in vitro. The argument with these approaches is that the assembled recombinant hsMcm2-7 may not represent the native form in human cells. To circumvent this potential problem, we produced new a HeLa cell line with the streptavidin tag inserted into hsMcm6. To our surprise, we are able to obtain endogenous hsMcm2-7. The native and SDS page gels showed all the components of hsMcm2-7 intact with the use of 3 liters of expression medium. With the help of other people in the laboratory, we have obtained the cryo-EM structure of a single hexameric human Mcm2-7 at a resolution of 4.3 Angstrom. It laid foundation for further structure-determination of the human Geminin/Mcm2-7 complex by cryo-EM. As we have expressed large amount of human Geminin, we are ready to purse the structure of Geminin/Mcm2-7 and Cdt1/Geminin/Mcm2-7 by cryo-EM soon. Objective 3: Functional studies of the above complexes by mutations of interacting residues in these complexes and evaluation of their effects on DNA replication in vitro and in vivo (We will carry out this research in collaboration with Prof. Anindya Dutta’s group). As showed in study for objective 1, we have mapped interacting amino acids in the Cdt1/Geminin and Geminin/Mcm6 complexes. We are ready for the collaboration work with Prof. Dutta’s group. However, due to the sudden departure of original PI of this project our progress has drastically slowed down as stated below. Reasons for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems: The project entitled “Structure-function studies of DNA replication protein complexes Geminin/Cdt1 and Geminin/MCM” (HKUST 16118416) had been led by Dr. Zhou Bo (PI) from 01-09-2016 to 31-04-2018 before his unexpected departure for a new appointment in USA in April, 2018. Thereafter, as the Co-I of the project, I took over the remaining research on the structure-function studies of the Geminin/Mcm2-7 complex. At the same time, Ph.D students, Ms. Geng Yanyan and Mr. Miao Haitao, who had been working on the project for several years, graduated and I had to organize a new team to pursuit the proposed research. The sudden loss of experts for these proposed projects, the occurrence of 2019 social events in Hong Kong and the worldwide Covid-19 epidemic have a detrimental effect on our research and have delayed our progress for many years. Meanwhile, as the new cryo-EM technology emerged as the best tool to study the large protein assembly and became available to us in the end of 2018, my group decided to study the human Cdt1/Geminin/Mcm2-7 super-molecular assembly by using cryo-EM assisted by NMR techniques for the remaining project because single particle cryo-EM structure could reveal complete structural features of Cdt1/Geminin/Mcm2-7 complex. We believed that this was the more efficient way to speed up the research process in terms of manpower, time and impact.

16118416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16118416.value: In the study for the objective 1, we are preparing a manuscript entitled “Structural insight of human Geminin-Cdt1 complex for inhibition of the replication licensing” which includes the following findings: 1. The coiled-coil domain of human Geminin interacts with a C-terminal peptide of human Cdt1. 2. The completed backbone and sidechain assignments for the C-terminal peptide of human Cdt1 and the backbone assignments of the coiled-coil domain of human Geminin. 3. A new interaction interface between the C-terminus of Geminin and the C-terminal peptide of human Cdt1. 5. The completed the backbone and sidechain assignments for the fusion protein that links the N-terminus and C-terminus of Cdt1. In the study for the objective 2, we have solved a novel structure of human Mcm2-7 complex at 4.4 angstrom resolution by cryo-EM. The corresponding manuscript is in preparation now. Meanwhile, we have demonstrated that this complex can be recruited to human DNA replication origin by human Orc6 as shown in our recent NAR paper entitled “Structural basis of DNA replication origin recognition by human Orc6 protein binding with DNA”, Nucleic Acids Research, 2020 1 as listed in section C. At the same time, we have shown that Cdt1 and Cdc6 may interact with human G-quadruplex DNA to cooperate the initiation of human DNA replication. In order to understand the detailed molecular mechanism for this action by NMR, we first studied different structures of human G-quadruplexes as shown in the publications listed in section C. Our follow-up study will focus on solving the structures of Cdt1/G-quadruplex and Cdc6/G-quadruplex complexes.

16118416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16118416.value: The foundation laid by and the results obtained from the captioned research projects permit us to purse the aims of determining the structures of human replisome and designing peptide drugs to inhibit carcinogenic mutants of Mcm2-7, Orc1-6, Geminin, Cdt1 and Cdc6. To achieve these goals, we will study the Cdct1/Mcm2-7/Geminin/Orc1-6 by using cryo-EM, x-ray crystallography and NMR techniques with samples and structures obtained from this proposed research.

16118416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16118416.value: Many types of cancers are related to mutations of proteins in human DNA pre-replication complexes, such as origin recognition complex (Orc1-6), mini-chromosome maintenance complex (Mcm2-7), cell division cycle 6 (Cdc6), chromatin licensing and DNA replication factor 1 (Cdt1) and geminin. Understand the structure-function of these protein complexes is critical in fundamental human biology and cancers. The results from this proposed research have paved road for us to purse further the goals of determining the molecular mechanism of human DNA replication initiation and design peptides and small molecules drugs to targets those mutants that cause human cancers.
