Elucidate the downstream signaling mechanisms of liprinα1 and its Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation

16124616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16124616.value: Neuronal activity plays an essential role in guiding synapse development, which underlies the experience-dependent shaping of brain circuitry. Synapse development requires the proper recruitment and localization of postsynaptic density (PSD) protein components to synapses. However, the manner in which neuronal activity precisely coordinates the synaptic components during development remains elusive. We recently showed that liprinα1, a scaffold protein involved in synaptic protein assembly, is phosphorylated by cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5) in an activity-dependent manner during synapse development. Blockade of liprinα1 phosphorylation enhances synapse development, as demonstrated by increased dendritic spine density and surface expression of glutamate receptor subunit GluA2 in cultured neurons. Accordingly, we hypothesize that liprinα1 phosphorylation is an essential modulatory event that mediates activity-dependent synapse development. To elucidate the in vivo function of liprinα1 and its phosphorylation regulation, we will first determine if liprinα1 is required for hippocampal neuronal structural and functional plasticity using the knockdown approach. Second, we will characterize the mechanism by which liprinα1 phosphorylation mediates synapse development. PSD-95 is a dominant postsynaptic scaffold protein involved in excitatory synapse maintenance. Accordingly, we will determine if liprinα1 phosphorylation affects its interaction with PSD-95 as well as the synaptic transport of PSD-95 during development. Moreover, we will examine the in vivo function of liprinα1 phosphorylation through the delivery of small interfering peptide into the mouse brain; neuronal structure and synaptic plasticity will be evaluated after blocking liprinα1 phosphorylation. The study proposed herein will enhance our understanding of the molecular basis of activity-regulated synapse development mediated by Cdk5 signaling.

16124616.label: Realisation of objectives
16124616.value: Synapse development requires the proper localization and recruitment of various components including glutamate receptors, cytoskeletal elements, and scaffold proteins to the postsynaptic density (PSD), a process that is controlled by neuronal activity. The liprinα family comprises abundant scaffold proteins that have been suggested to be critical for synapse organization through their interactions with multiple synaptic proteins. Nonetheless, the molecular mechanisms that regulate liprinα function at synapses, particularly whether and how it is regulated by neuronal activity, remain unclear. Our preliminary finding showed that liprinα1 is enriched at postsynaptic regions and co-localized with PSD-95. Importantly, we demonstrated that knockdown of the endogenous liprinα1 led to severe defects in dendritic morphology and spine density in cultured neurons. Human liprinα1 is phosphorylated by Cdk5 at threonine (Thr) 701, while such phosphorylation is reduced by neuronal activity. Blockade of liprinα1 phosphorylation significantly increased dendritic spine density and maturation ratio, as well as the surface expression of AMPA receptors in cultured neurons (Huang et al., 2017). To further understand the functional roles of liprinα1 at the hippocampal excitatory synapses, we examined the protein regulation of liprinα1 and its subcellular distribution in the mouse hippocampus during development. The level of liprinα1 was highly expressed in the mouse hippocampus at postnatal day (P) 7, and decreasing gradually thereafter until P30. Although liprinα1 protein expression was reduced upon development, the protein became enriched in the PSD at the adult stage. These results support the potential roles of liprinα1 in postsynaptic development. Our in vitro study showed that liprinα1 regulates the density of dendritic protrusions in cultured hippocampal neurons. Thus, to elucidate the roles of liprinα1 in hippocampal synaptic development, we reduced endogenous liprinα1 in the hippocampal CA1 region by infection with the lentivirus-based liprinα1 shRNA. We found a significant reduction of dendritic spine density in CA1 pyramidal neurons. Given that changes in dendritic spine density are associated with synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus, we subsequently demonstrated that liprinα1 knockdown resulted in a ~20% reduction in CA3–CA1 LTP induced by theta-burst stimulation (Huang et al., 2017). Together, our findings suggest that liprinα1 is important for hippocampal synapse formation and synaptic plasticity. Our preliminary data suggest that liprinα1 function is regulated by its phosphorylation at Thr701. We thus examined the developmental profile of liprinα1 phosphorylation during brain development. Intriguingly, liprinα1 phosphorylation decreased dramatically in the mouse hippocampus from P10–P30, which encompasses a period critical for synaptogenesis and circuitry formation in the brain. In particular, the eye opening process during this period, when visual stimuli accelerate synapse development in the mouse visual cortex, is a widely accepted paradigm for studying activity-dependent synapse development. Therefore, we examined the levels of liprinα1 phosphorylation in the mouse visual cortex before and after eye opening (P10–P15), based on that mice open their eyes around P12.5. We found that liprinα1 phosphorylation decreased significantly after eye opening. We also found that liprinα1 phosphorylation is significantly increased in the visual cortex of dark-reared mice, indicating that liprinα1 phosphorylation in the mouse visual cortex is tightly controlled by neuronal activity in vivo (Huang et al., 2017). These results collectively suggest that neuronal activity negatively regulates liprinα1 phosphorylation. Our preliminary data have demonstrated that liprinα1 function in dendritic morphogenesis can be regulated by Cdk5 phosphorylation at Thr701. Thus, we investigated whether liprinα1 phosphorylation is involved in the functional changes of synapses in cultured neuron by overexpressing different forms of liprinα1, including both wild-type and its mutants (phosphodeficient TA mutant and phosphomimetic TE mutant). Synapse development is evaluated by examining the puncta of the postsynaptic marker PSD-95 and the surface targeting of AMPA receptor, specifically the GluA2 subunit, which indicates the maturation of excitatory synapses. We identified that liprinα1 TA mutant-overexpressing neurons exhibited significant increase in PSD-95 puncta density and the surface level of GluA2, whereas decreased PSD-95 puncta and surface GluA2 expression was observed in TE mutant-overexpressing neurons (Huang et al., 2017). Taken together, these results collectively indicate that liprinα1 regulates synapse density and maturation, and its synaptic function is tightly regulated by Cdk5. We subsequently investigated how liprinα1 phosphorylation regulates synapse maturation. For such, we used the stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM) super-resolution imaging system to examine changes in the subcellular localization of liprinα1 at synapses at nanometer scale. We observed that liprinα1 is expressed in clusters smaller than those of PSD-95; inhibition of Cdk5 activity, and hence liprinα1 phosphorylation, by roscovitine (Ros) significantly increased the size of liprinα1 clusters and the expression of liprinα1 surrounding the PSD-95 clusters. Meanwhile, the size of the PSD-95 puncta was not obviously altered during the treatment, suggesting that the increased co-localization between liprinα1 and PSD-95 is not due to the change in the size of the PSD-95 clusters (Huang et al., 2017). Therefore, our STORM results provide nanoscale-level evidence that the suppression of liprinα1 phosphorylation specifically enhances the recruitment of liprinα1 to PSD-95 clusters and its association with PSD-95, which may contribute to postsynaptic development. To provide direct evidence that endogenous liprinα1 phosphorylation affects its association with PSD-95, we treated neurons with a small interfering peptide (siLIP) that specifically targets Cdk5-dependent liprinα1 phosphorylation, and examined the co-localization between liprinα1 and PSD-95 by STORM. siLIP increased the localization of liprinα1 within PSD-95 clusters. Moreover, treatment of neurons with siLIP significantly increased both the density and size of PSD-95 puncta. Notably, time-lapse confocal imaging of PSD-95–GFP-expressing neurons showed that siLIP treatment increased the clustering of PSD-95 in the dendrites, further suggesting that liprinα1 phosphorylation regulates the trafficking of PSD-95 along dendrites (Huang et al., 2017). This finding corroborates the notion that inhibition of liprinα1 phosphorylation through the phospho-interfering peptide increases the synaptic localization of PSD-95. The results presented above demonstrate that liprinα1 phosphorylation is inhibited by neuronal activity, and that reduced phosphorylation of liprinα1 promotes synaptic maturation in cultured neurons. Therefore, we determined whether disruption of endogenous liprinα1 phosphorylation by the in vivo delivery of siLIP regulates synaptic functions in the brain. Injection of siLIP into the mouse hippocampal CA1 region resulted in a significant reduction in liprinα1 phosphorylation. Moreover, siLIP significantly increased dendritic spine density in hippocampal CA1 neurons and increased LTP in the hippocampal CA3–CA1 region, suggesting that inhibition of liprinα1 phosphorylation enhances synaptic plasticity (Huang et al., 2017). Hence, our findings collectively suggest that liprinα1 phosphorylation is critical for synapse development and synaptic plasticity.

16124616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16124616.value: This study aimed to understand the regulatory mechanism of liprinα1 function in synaptogenesis, particularly the activity-dependent Cdk5 phosphorylation of liprinα1. 1. Regulation of Cdk5-dependent liprinα1 phosphorylation by neuronal activity The liprinα1 protein was enriched in the postsynaptic density. The phosphorylation of liprinα1 at Thr701 was found to be significantly reduced in the hippocampus of postnatal mouse, particularly at the critical stage of synaptogenesis and circuitry formation, and also in the mouse cortex after eye opening (Huang et al., 2017). These data collectively demonstrated that the phosphorylation of liprinα1 is regulated by neuronal activity. 2. Cdk5-dependent liprinα1 phosphorylation regulates the structure and function of excitatory synaptogenesis Overexpression of phospho-Thr701-deficient liprinα1 mutant promoted excitatory synaptogenesis with increased dendritic spine density, enhanced PSD-95 puncta and the surface expression of AMPA receptors in cultured hippocampal neurons, whereas phospho-Thr701-liprinα1 mimetic mutant suppressed synaptogenesis (Huang et al., 2017). 3. Cdk5-dependent liprinα1 phosphorylation modulates synaptogenesis via regulation of synaptic localization of PSD-95 To decipher the mechanistic roles of liprinα1 phosphorylation in synaptogenesis, we employed the stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM) super-resolution imaging system to examine the interaction between liprinα1 and PSD-95 at nanoscale level. Nanoscale superresolution imaging revealed that inhibition of liprinα1 phosphorylation increased the colocalization of liprinα1 with PSD-95, disruption of liprinα1 phosphorylation by a small interfering peptide, siLIP, promoted the synaptic localization of PSD-95 and enhanced synaptic strength in vivo. Our results suggest that liprinα1 functions in synaptogenesis via regulating the synaptic localization of PSD-95 (Huang et al., 2017). 4. Cdk5-dependent liprinα1 phosphorylation regulates synaptic plasticity Liprinα1 is required for hippocampal synaptic plasticity. Knockdown of liprinα1 attenuated the LTP in the hippocampal CA3–CA1 region. Moreover, inhibition of liprinα1 phosphorylation enhances LTP, suggesting that liprinα1 function in synaptic plasticity is regulated by its phosphorylation status (Huang et al., 2017).

16124616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16124616.value: The present study showed that the Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation of the scaffold protein liprinα1 promotes the organization of postsynaptic proteins, i.e. PSD-95, and hence excitatory synapses. We have established the technical approaches to examine how the phosphorylation-dependent mechanisms or protein–protein interactions are involved in the postsynaptic organization processes. Specifically, super-resolution imaging allows analysis of the localization pattern of individual proteins at the postsynaptic region at a fine resolution, which enables us to distinguish the spatial relationships of individual specific proteins. Understanding of the interaction and dynamics of specific proteins at the synaptic sites provides insights into the molecular events underlying synapse maturations and functioning. Thus, we will continue to characterize specific proteins/pathways during excitatory synapse development and the dysfunctioning of the process, which may lead to various neurodevelopmental disorders.

16124616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16124616.value: The experience-dependent modulation of brain circuitry depends on changes in synaptic connections that are guided by neuronal activity. In particular, postsynaptic maturation requires changes of dendritic spine morphology, the targeting of postsynaptic proteins, and the insertion of synaptic neurotransmitter receptors. Thus, it is critical to understand how neuronal activity controls postsynaptic maturation. Here, we report that the scaffold protein liprinα1, and its phosphorylation by cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5), are critical for the maturation of excitatory synapses through regulation of the synaptic localization of the major postsynaptic organizer PSD-95. While Cdk5 phosphorylates liprinα1 at Thr701, the phosphorylation decreases in neurons in response to neuronal activity. Blockade of liprinα1 phosphorylation enhances the structural and functional maturation of excitatory synapses. Nanoscale super-resolution imaging reveals that inhibition of liprinα1 phosphorylation increases the co-localization of liprinα1 with PSD-95. Furthermore, disruption of liprinα1 phosphorylation by a small interfering peptide, siLIP, promotes the synaptic localization of PSD-95 and enhances synaptic strength in vivo. Our findings collectively demonstrate that the Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation of liprinα1 is a novel mechanism that controls postsynaptic organization during activity-dependent synapse development.

16124916.label: Project Objectives
16124916.value: To demonstrate that astrocyte-derived lipids, carried by APOE, are critical for the proper formation and maintenance of myelin, in vivo and in vitro. To prove that APOE isoforms, through their effects on lipid metabolism, have profound effects on the dynamics of oligodendrocyte lineages and their myelination – in particular in the aging brain. We will further demonstrate that these effects surpass its role in the clearance of the Aβ peptide.
rows: To demonstrate that astrocyte-derived lipids, carried by APOE, are critical for the proper formation and maintenance of myelin, in vivo and in vitro.

To prove that APOE isoforms, through their effects on lipid metabolism, have profound effects on the dynamics of oligodendrocyte lineages and their myelination – in particular in the aging brain. We will further demonstrate that these effects surpass its role in the clearance of the Aβ peptide.

16124916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16124916.value: Currently, Alzheimer's disease (AD) research is dominated by the amyloid cascade hypothesis. Unfortunately, clinical trials based on anti-amyloid approaches have been largely unsuccessful, even when amyloid-deposits are cleared. Additional approaches to the biology of AD and its treatment are therefore highly desirable. For many years, clinical evidence has mounted that white matter degeneration is found in the aging brain prior to amyloid deposition and neurodegeneration. This suggests that myelin and its constituent cells, the oligodendrocytes, are a potential diagnostic and therapeutic target. This resonates well with data showing that Apolipoprotein Ɛ (APOE) genotype is one of the strongest genetic risk factors for AD. APOE4, an allele found in 24% of the population, significantly increases the risk of developing AD. While this enhanced risk has been attributed to its role as a carrier of β-amyloid, less is known about how the defective lipid/cholesterol-carrying function of APOE4 may contribute to its negative effects. We believe that this aspect of APOE function is ripe for investigation. We note that oligodendrocytes are heavily dependent on fats, in particular cholesterol, for myelination. Therefore, we propose that one important function of APOE that is lost in AD is the efficient transfer of cholesterol and other lipids from astrocytes to oligodendrocytes. Our central hypothesis is that this defective lipid metabolism underlies the white matter abnormalities found in early stages of AD and contributes to the observed cognitive decline. We present preliminary data that white matter degeneration in humans is highly correlated with APOE genotype. Additional data show that DNA damage in oligodendrocytes is correlated with APOE genotype and, similar to the effects of AD on neurons, in mature oligodendrocytes of both white and gray matter this DNA damage is associated with aberrant cell-cycle events. We first propose to investigate the underlying mechanisms linking cholesterol-metabolism, oligodendrocyte cell biology, with white matter defects in vitro as well as in humanized APOE mouse models. We will then confirm our findings in human autopsy specimens that have already been obtained from the Maryland Brain Bank. With the wide range of drugs available to control cholesterol, we believe that controlling its metabolism in oligodendrocytes before irreversible neurodegeneration occurs may be achievable and will have significant clinical benefits in slowing the progress of AD.

16124916.label: Realisation of objectives
16124916.value: The overarching goal for this project is to demonstrate the association or causal relationship between APOE genotype and oligodendrocyte(OL) degeneration in Alzheimer’s disease(AD). We have published our concept of amyloid independent early OL pathology in sporadic AD(Publication#1). With the reduced number of cortical OLs, the cortical neurons demonstrated higher level of genomic damage(Conference#4) A myelin-based alternative hypothesis for AD has been well accepted in the field(Publication#2, with 57 citations since 26 May 2017). We ask if APOE4 affects OLs through its role in cholesterol homeostasis in amyloid-independent way. For Objective 1. As the proof-of-principle experiment, we characterized the astrocytic APOE secretion and their uptake by surrounding OLs(Conference#3). The GFAP+ primary astrocytes derived from wildtype neonatal mice expressed strong expression of LXR in vitro. Application of LXR agonist(T0901317), but not RXR agonist(Bexarotene) stimulated astrocytes to transcribe a serious of lipid transporter and receptor genes including Abca1, Abcg1, Ldlr, Lrp1, Vldlr, and Apoe, indicating astrocytic LXR, but not RXR are functional in vitro. We then co-cultured Apoe-/- primary OLs with primary astrocytes derived from hAPOE4 mice(details below) stimulated with or without LXR agonist in a transwell co-culture system. Indeed, using an antibody specific to human APOE4(clone 4E4), hAPOE4 released by LXR-activated astrocytes was taken up by the Apoe-/- OLs. To investigate if this APOE-mediated uptake is needed for OL during differentiation, we conducted experiments on Apoe-/- primary OLs with HMG-CoA reductase inhibition using Lovastatin(Publication#4). In a murine OL progenitor cell(OPC) model, Oli-Neu, Lovastatin attenuated differentiation in a dose-dependent fashion. Importantly, cholesterol synthesis inhibition by Lovastatin compromised the viability of Oli-Neu cells only during the differentiation, but not proliferative state, supporting that Cholesterol is a key substance for OL differentiation. Such suppression of Oli-Neu differentiation was rescued by the in direct co-culture with primary mouse astrocyte, but not their condition medium, suggesting that active cellular interactions are needed for cholesterol transport in myelination. Indeed, APOE is also required for OLs to differentiation, as OLs formation was reduced in Apoe-/- primary OLs. The inhibitory effects of Lovastatin augmented APOE deficiency in primary OLs culture. Neither conditions affect the preservation of NG2+ Olig2+ OPCs. To ask if astrocyte-derived extracellular lipids can rescue mOL formation in the absence of APOE or HMG-CoA reductase activity, we supplied the Lovastatin-treated Apoe-/- OLs with human plasma derived VLDL(Very low-density lipoprotein; containing 1.61 mg/ml Cholesterol, 7.42mg/ml Triglycerides and 1.31 mg of lipoproteins) and normal differentiation was restored in vitro. Cholesterol supply through APOE is required for OLs differentiation, but the effects of human APOE3 and APOE4 isoforms on OLs remains unknown. In two independent cohorts of human frontal cortex tissues(n=24 and n = 29, respectively)(Publication#1,#3,#4), we reported that APOE4 is strongly associated reduced population of OLs in the grey matter and white matter, especially in the frontal cortex. These reduction of OLs is associated with DNA double strand breaks in the OLs, particularly the mOLs, and the abnormal cell cycle re-entry of these terminally differentiated cells(Publication#1) Importantly, we found that the DNA repair genes strongly negatively associated with myelin transcription in OLs(Conference #4). By culturing primary OLs from hAPOE3 and hAPOE4 transgenic mice, we surprisingly found that endogenous hAPOE4 had no effects on the formation of OLs at the developmental stage, even though hAPOE4 OLs is similarly sensitive to Lovastatin treatment. Importantly, we found that purified recombinant hAPOE3(rhAPOE3) and rhAPOE4 also had no effects on Apoe-/- OPC differentiation or on myelinating Apoe-/- mOLs at non-lipidated state, but rhAPOE4-lipid mixture significantly attenuated MBP+ , to a lesser extent MAG+, mOL formation in Apoe-/- genotype(Publication#4). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the detrimental effects of APOE deficiency and hAPOE4 on OL. To confirm this result, we also tested rhAPOE3 and rhAPOE4 on Oli-Neu OPC cell line as well as N2a neuron-like cell line and found that non-lipidated rhAPOE4 had minimal effects(Publication#3). For Objective2. We model the effects of APOE deficiency and the human alleles of APOE3 and APOE4 by studying an aging cohort of Apoe-/-(Apoetm1Unc), homozygous hAPOE3(RBRC03390, B6;129-Apoe/3SfuRbrc) and hAPOE4(RBRC03418, B6;129- Apoetm(APOE4)Sfu>/SfuRbrc) knock-in mice(JAX lab, USA and RIKEN Japan, respectively)(Publication#3,#4). To examine the age-dependent change of these cohorts, we histologically analyzed the brains of wildtype(C57B/6), Apoe-/- hAPOE3, and hAPOE4 mice at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months old using immunohistochemistry. Human APOE protein expression is only detected in hAPOE3 and hAPOE4 mice and such expression was strongly localized in astrocyte but not OLs both at neocortex and corpus callosum. APOE4 is only found on homozygous hAPOE4 mice. We found selective APOE receptor, Ldlr, increased in the hAPOE4 cortex, but no changes in CYP46A1 expression were found. Therefore altered cholesterol turnover is unlikely in brain, but the increased Ldlr expression may facilitate increased APOE4-Ldlr signaling. From 1 to 6 months, total OLs density(Olig2+) gradually decline in all groups, but the largest reduction was only observed in hAPOE3 and hAPOE4 mice, with the latter shown the lowest OL density in cortex and corpus callosum. mOL labeled by CC1 marker gradually increase in both wildtype and Apoe-/-, but gradually tailed off in hAPOE mice starting from 3 months, with the density in hAPOE4, but not hAPOE3, lower than that in wildtype and Apoe-/-. The overall difference in OL population between hAPOE3 and hAPOE4 mice was minimal compared to that in wildtype and Apoe-/-. Yet, at 12 months, the difference between hAPOE3 and hAPOE4 became remarkable. First, a significant reduction of Olig2+ total OL population were significantly reduced across all GM(frontal cortex, motor and cingulate cortex, retrosplenial cortex and thalamus) and WM regions(genu, body and splenium of corpus callosum, fornix of hippocampus) in hAPOE4 mice. Such demise of OL population in WM was associated with a significant increase of Nkx 2.2 OPC in hPAOE4 mice. As Nkx 2.2 is selective for late OPC prior to differentiation, hAPOE4 OL in the WM is undergoing a phase of compensatory differentiation. The CC1+ mOL population is generally lower in the hAPOE4 with the only significant difference found in the motor/cingulate cortex. These findings suggested that APOE3 and APOE4 have strong implication on the cellular dynamics of the OL population especially at advanced age. Despite the clear change in OL dynamics in human tissues, no changes of MBP+ area or intensity was found in APOE4 carriers. This lack of myelin changes was well recapitulated in hAPOE3 and hAPOE4 mice(Publication#3,#4). The myelinated area and their corresponding gene expression remained constant between hAPOE3 and hAPOE4 from 1 to 12 months old. Furthermore, quantification of cortical neurons revealed no neuronal degeneration in all mice from the four genotypes. This result is completely unexpected, and it indicates that the lipid transport alternation in APOE4 carriers can only implicate on OL dynamics but not their ultimate myelin protein production. Importantly, unlike other transgenic mice model we reported with OL degeneration(Publication#1), none of the APOE-associated transgenic mice harbor mutations in the amyloid cascade hypothesis and our observation is amyloid independent. The key findings are(i) APOE derived from astrocytes support OL differentiation during cholesterol deprivation,(ii) Exogenous lipids supply is sufficient to restore myelin formation by OLs during cholesterol deprivation but compromised by APOE4(iii) The OLs in APOE4 carriers are reduced, differentiation disrupted but required to maintain a normal brain myelination.

To prove that APOE isoforms, through their effects on lipid metabolism, have profound effects on the dynamics of oligodendrocyte lineages and their myelination – in particular in the aging brain. We will further demonstrate that these effects surpass its role in the clearance of the Aβ peptide.

16124916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16124916.value: We have made a number of research findings based on proposed objectives with four publication/manuscripts and four accepted papers on international conferences. First, we showed that APOE4 status is strongly associated with OLs loss in human frontal cortex, and such degeneration occur prior to amyloid plaque deposition (Publication #1, Conference Paper #1). Second, myelinating OLs is highly vulnerable to DNA double strand break with their DNA repair capacity gradually decline with the progress of differentiation (Publication #1 & Conference Paper #4) The idea of DNA damage-driven myelin pathology as an early symptom in age-related dementia is conceptualized and well received in the field (Publication #1 & 2) Third, we demonstrated that APOE4 genotype reduced OL population but not the extent of myelination in both gray matter and white matter in human and mice (Publication #3 & 4, Conference Paper #2). Forth, astrocyte-derived APOE-mediated cholesterol/lipid support is needed for OL to differentiate especially in the decline of de novo cholesterol biosynthesis, and importantly this process is hampered by the presence of human APOE4 (Publication #4, Conference Paper #3) Fifth, the extent of brain myelination in APOE4 carriers is comparable to that in APOE3 carriers, but only supported by a disproportionately small population of surviving OLs (Publication #3 & 4). Finally, the loss of OLs is associated with an increase of neuronal genomic injury (Conference Paper #4) Based on the initial findings of this project, we successfully forged new collation for clinical research where we obtained a Health and Medical Research Fund (HMRF), Hong Kong Gov’t (Ref. 05163736) – “Myelin abnormalities as the symptoms of dementia – harmonizing neuroimaging and cell biology” with Clinical Associate Professor Dr. Henry Mak at the University of Hong Kong and Dr Kannie Chan at the City University of Hong Kong to study the cell biology underlying MRI findings of myelin changes in APOE4 mice. Two research assistants, Mr Gerald Wai-Yeung Cheng and Kingston King-Shi Mok were trained in this project, and both have acquired RPg studentships for other projects after the training.

16124916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16124916.value: First, the key finding in this project is the identification of OL pathology as an early event in the aging brain, especially the APOE4 carrier. As an approach to make this a clinical translational finding, we are currently investigating the cellular mechanism underlying the white matter integrity abnormalities in hAPOE4 mice by pre-clinical neuroimaging with fMRI (HMRF05163736) with radiologist. Second, another key finding in this project is the abnormal cell cycle re-entry of OLs in AD. To better understand the cellular mechanism underlying such DNA-damage induced events and their connection with genetic risk in AD, we are now investigating BIN1, the second strongest genetic risk factor in AD, and it’s connection with ATM in the cellular mechanism controlling OLs cell cycle through an Early Career Scheme project (ECS25104220) funded last year. Finally, we proposed to investigate the genetic risk factor of white matter hyperintensity in APOE deficient mice (GRF application 2021/2022, results pending). All of these studies are stemmed from this project.

16124916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16124916.value: Myelin sheath is the fatty structure in the brain important for cognitive functions. These myelin structures are gradually lost in the aging brain or Alzheimer’s disease. The biology underlying this phenomenon is unknown. In this study, we found that APOE4, the strongest genetic risk factor of sporadic Alzheimer’s disease, affects the survival and function of oligodendrocytes, the only cell type in the brain that can produce and maintain myelin sheath. Our experiments showed that a reduced oligodendrocyte population is left in APOE4 carrying human and mouse, and that APOE4 may hamper oligodendrocytes to acquire lipids from the surroundings for generate myelin. We are the first to demonstrate he surviving oligodendrocytes of APOE4 carriers are therefore maintaining a disproportionate amount of myelination with compromised efficiency and become more vulnerable in the aging brain. The present work may provide an alternative pathway to understand neurodegeneration in the aging brain which shed lights to new research direction for diagnosis and therapy for sporadic Alzheimer’s disease.

16127816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16127816.value: Understanding how organisms acquire, partition, and expense energy is a unifying approach to investigate organismal responses to anthropogenic stress across a wide range of taxa. Applying such bioenergetics principle, the Dynamic Energy Budget (DEB) Model has been widely adopted to predict responses of ecologically and economically important species' fate in the future ocean, including marine bivalves. Like other marine organisms, bivalves have complex life history and their bioenergetics likely vary through ontogeny. This project aims to fill in this knowledge gap by developing a DEB model for the most vulnerable life stage: veliger larvae. Our goal is to overcome challenges of quantifying oxygen consumption and feeding rate of small planktonic larvae with fluorescent based respirometery and micro-Particle Image Velocimetry. 透過瞭解生物如何攝取,分派和使用能量，我們可以分析不同物種對人類活動的反應。動態能量平衡 (DEB) 模擬就採用這個物能量學的原則，並已被廣泛採用於預測多種具生態和經濟價值的物種命對環變的反應，如海洋雙貝類。和其他海洋生物一樣，貝類具有複雜的生活史，而且其生物能量應用會隨發育而變化。通過開發一個幼體專屬DEB模擬, 此項目旨對在提供更全面和準確的族群預測。我們更會改良熒光呼吸測量和微粒子圖像測速來量化小浮游幼體的耗氧量和餵食率。

16128416.label: Realisation of objectives
16128416.value: 1) We have carried out a research cruise in the Pearl River Estuary and its adjacent coastal waters in summer 2017 and 2018. During the cruises, we have collected samples of bacteria, phytoplankton and zooplankton in hypoxic and non-hypoxic waters for microscopic observation and molecular analysis. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, our plan for more research cruises was not realized, but the first objective of this study was well addressed. We collected the samples at all experimental stations and examined them under a microscope to investigate how the community of microzooplankton (protists) respond to the hypoxia. As the microscopic observation took a lot of time, the analysis of the samples is still ongoing. To examine the effects of hypoxia on microzooplankton in the real ocean, we conducted 27 dilution experiments to estimate the microzooplankton grazing rate and phytoplankton growth rate in the summer hypoxic region in Pearl River Estuary in 2017 and 2018. We conducted dilution experiments in both surface and bottom layers. In this eutrophic region, the phytoplankton growth rate was high, and the top-down control from microzooplankton grazing was limited, as we found the grazing rate was lower than the phytoplankton growth rate. In the bottom layers, the grazing pressure on phytoplankton production is a bit lower when hypoxia occurred, but we need to get all the microscopic samples counted to evaluate the grazing activity of individual protist. The hypoxic environment may pose stress on microzooplankton metabolism and may change their community composition. Using molecular techniques, we have unraveled the effect of hypoxia, eutrophication and pollution on microbial community composition and function (Wu et al. 2018, Zou et al. 2019, Li et al. 2020, Lu et al. 2020). We paid specific attention to the red tide forming species Noctiluca scintillans and studied its interaction with other bacteria and protists during its bloom and its metabolic function through peptidomics study (Xia et al. 2020, Zhang et al. 2020, 2021). 2) To address objectives 2 and 3, we conducted both field sampling and laboratory experiments. We collected water samples from hypoxic and non-hypoxic waters for microscopic, metagenomic and transcriptomic studies, and some results have been published. In laboratory, we conducted experiments with 4 representative protists in different oxygen concentrations ranging from normal to hypoxia conditions. We monitored their growth, grazing and respiration rates, and collected RNA samples for transcriptomic study. Unfortunately, the RNA samples and products sent to the sequencing company were not successful. We conducted the experiments again, but then the shipping of the samples to mainland China was delayed by almost a year. This resulted that the transcriptomic study is still on going. We will publish the results as soon as possible. Combining results from this study and results of 3 other species we studied previously (Rocke et al. 2014), we found that the severity of the impact of hypoxia to the metabolism of protists is species-specific, and the smaller the protist cell, the more tolerant to low oxygen, likely resulted from the smaller cells’ larger surface-to-volume ratio that facilitates more efficient oxygen diffusion across the cell membrane at hypoxic environments. I believe that this finding is important for modeling microbial carbon cycling in hypoxic to anoxic water bodies by incorporating taxonomic differences into models that connect ecological fitness with basic bioenergetics (e.g., Kempes et al., 2012). 3) We expanded our study to metazoan zooplankton, such as copepods. Field and laboratory studies were conducted to investigate the physiological adaptability of mesozooplankton to low oxygen environments. At the hypoxic stations, mesozooplankton biomass was higher, species diversity was lower, grazing impact was lower, and the communities were more dominated by small and herbivorous species (copepod: Acartia spp. and Paracalanus spp.), compared with normal stations (Shi et al. 2019). Laboratory experimental study with 3 copepod species reveal similar results with that of protozoan zooplankton, that is that copepod tolerance to hypoxia is species-specific and small-sized copepods were better adapted to hypoxia than large ones, which is in agreement with the findings of the field study. Overall, we have accomplished all objectives of this study, but the transcriptomic results are still under analysis. It will definitely be published in the near future. A total of 25 papers acknowledged this grant.

16128416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16128416.value: 1) We studied the roles of microbial metabolic activity in the formation of bottom water hypoxia by revealing enriched organic degradation related microbial genes in the bottom layer beneath surface phytoplankton bloom. We also detected high abundance of sulfate-reducing genes in hypoxic bottom water, indicating microbial adaptation to oxygen depletion. 2) We found that protists of smaller size are better adapted to low oxygen environment, likely resulted from the smaller cells’ larger surface-to-volume ratio that facilitates more efficient oxygen diffusion across the cell membrane at hypoxic environments. This may cause the plankton community in hypoxic waters to become small species dominated, and enhance the dominance of microbial loop in the planktonic food web. 3) Similar to protozoan, the metazoan zooplankton also had high biomass, low species diversity, low grazing impact, and smaller body size in hypoxic water compared with normal stations. Laboratory experimental study reveal similar results with that of protozoan zooplankton that small-sized copepods were better adapted to hypoxia than the large ones. 4) We investigated the peptidome of a red tide forming species Noctiluca scintillans based on mass-spectrometry (MS) analysis.This is the first attempt to study peptidomics of N. scintillans, which provide important information on the functional studies of peptidomics in N. scintillans, especially food digestion and dietary protein utilization, as well as their relationship with bloom development.

16128416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16128416.value: We are working on a synthesis paper combine our results on protozoan and metazoan zooplankton on their ability to adapt low oxygen condition and predict the effect of de-oxygenation in future ocean. In connection with the above work, we are also working on the synergistic effect of warming and hypoxia on zooplankton metabolism. We are preparing proposal and collaborating with scientists in mainland China and other countries to expand our study to other habitats/ecosystems, such as mangrove forests and the oxygen minimum zone in the Benguela Current of India Ocean off South Africa.

16128416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16128416.value: Pearl River and sewage effluent discharge large amounts of inorganic and organic nutrients, causing eutrophication in Hong Kong coastal water. One of the direct consequences of eutrophication is bottom water hypoxia (DO<2 mg L 1 ), which causes not only the death of fish and benthic animals, but also the decline of biodiversity and habitat carrying capacity. Recent studies show that the area and intensity of the hypoxia in the Pearl River estuary is larger and severer than previous reported. Protistan bacterivory and herbivory constitute a major source of mortality for bacterioplankton and phytoplankton in the ocean and contribute significantly to nutrient remineralization. There are very few studies that have focused on protist community distribution and diversity in hypoxic habitats. In this study, we study how coastal hypoxia affects the structure and function of microbial food web, with a focus on protistan grazers. Both field and lab studies were conducted to characterize the adaptability and changing roles of the protistal microorganism in hypoxic waters. The findings of this study are essential for developing models that provide solutions to mitigate coastal eutrophication and maintain the ecosystem integrity in the scenario of increasing environmental stress from both human activity and climate change.

16131916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16131916.value: Objective I Using genetic and imaging analysis, we were able to show that the RBI- and VDA-derived microglia are regulated by distinctive regulatory networks formed by Pu.1, Spi-b, and Irf8. We found that during RBI-derived microglia development, Pu.1 acts upstream of Spi-b, whereas Pu.1 and Spi-b act in parallel and co-operatively to regulate VDA-derived microglia. Interestingly, the two distinct regulatory networks control the RBI- and VDA-derived microglia development through regulating Irf8. Our study indicates that distinct genetic networks formed by the same repertoire of transcription factors govern the development of microglia from different origins. This study has been published in Blood (129:509-519, 2017). Objective II To uncover the signaling pathway controlling the colonization of the RBI- and VDA-derived microglia, we focused on interleukin 34 (il34) and colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor a (csf1ra) because their highly enrichment in microglia and microglial precursors. We showed that, in il34- and csf1ra-deficient mutants, the RBI-derived microglial precursors developed normally but failed to colonize the brains. We further showed that neuronal overexpression of Il34 is sufficient to attract the RBI-derived microglial precursors into the brains. This study demonstrates that the il34-csf1ra pathway is essential for the migration and colonization of the RBI-derived microglia. This work has been published in Developmental Cell (46:552-563, 2018). To study the colonization potential of the RBI- and VDA-derived microglia, we generated a Tg(mfap4:CreER);Tg(mpeg1:loxp-DsRed-loxp-GFP) reporter line, which can preferentially label the RBI-derived microglia upon tamoxifen treatment at 18 hours postfertilization (hpf) for 6 hours. Fate mapping analysis showed that the number of the RBI-derived microglia reached the peak at 1.5-month old and sharply reduced by 2-months old. TUNNEL staining confirmed that the decrease of the RBI-derived microglia was due to the dead of these cells. In contrast, the number of the VDA-derived microglia rapidly increased from 1-month old and continued to do so until adulthood. Interestingly, from 1.5 months old onward, the overall density of microglia remained steady and the steady density of microglia appears to be regulated by the Il34-Csf1r pathway (manuscript in preparation). Objective III Whole-genome RNA seq analysis showed that the RBI- and VDA-derived microglia are highly similar and may manifest similar function. We noticed that mafba and mafbb, two zebrafish orthologs of mammalian MAFB, a key transcription factor essential for macrophage survival and differentiation, are differentially expressed in these two microglia populations. We are currently investigating their roles in the long-term survival of the RBI-derived and VDA-derived microglia.

16131916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16131916.value: We have also explored the molecular basis governing the survival of the RBI-derived and VDA-derived microglia. Based on the whole-genome RNA-seq analysis, we focused on mafba and mafbb, two zebrafish orthologs of mammalian MAFB, because they are highly enriched in the RBI-derived microglia but undetectable in the VDA-derived microglia. As MAFB is a transcription factor shown to be essential for the survival and differentiation of macrophages in mammals, we hypothesized that mafba and mafbb may play a role in the regulation of the long-term survival of the RBI-derived and VDA-derived microglia. As mafba mutants died during early development and mafbb-deficient fish exhibited not obvious phenotype, we decided to generate an inducible knockout allele of mafba via CRISPR/Cas knock-in strategy. We have recently successfully obtained an inducible knockout allele of mafba and is currently investigating its role in the long-term survival of the RBI-derived and VDA-derived microglia. In parallel, we have also generated a mafba overexpression line to test whether forced expression of mafba will affect the long-term survival of the VDA-derived microglia.

16131916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16131916.value: Microglia are immune cells in the brain, and they consist of two different populations originating from two distinct sources: the RBI and the VDA. The goal of this study is to elucidate the cellular and molecular basis underlying these two microglia populations. Using genetic and imaging analysis, we identified three transcription factors, Pu.1, Spi-b, and Irf8, which form two distinctive regulatory networks to regulate the formation of the RBI-derived and VDA-derived microglia, respectively. With the similar approaches, we also identified the Il34-Csf1ra pathway as a key molecular signaling cascade to regulate the migration and colonization of the BRI-derived microglia. To monitor the colonization potential of these two microglia populations, we generated a transgenic zebrafish line, which allows us to distinguish the RBI-derived and VDA-derived microglia. Using this transgenic line, we went on to determine the dynamic changes of the RBI-derived and VDA-derived microglia in the brain from early embryonic stages to adulthood of zebrafish. We further documented that the Il34-Csf1ra pathway is critical for the maintenance of microglia density. As dysregulation of microglia is associated with the development of various neurodegenerative disorders, the new insights from our study may provide useful information for the therapeutic strategy of related neuronal disorders.

16137516.label: Realisation of objectives
16137516.value: The first objective aims to create Gβ-Gα fusion proteins with the Gα component defective in effector regulation but remaining capable of releasing the Gβ component upon GPCR activation. This objective constituted the major effort of the project as it entailed the annihilation of the effector recognition domain on a Gαi subunit and the subsequent generation of a fusion protein which could respond to receptor activation. In accordance with the proposal, a series of 16 Gαi1 chimeras/mutants was constructed wherein selected residues/regions were substituted with cognate sequences from either Gαt1 or Gαq, and constitutively active versions of each construct were also generated with the introduction of a GTPase-deficient mutation (either Q204L or R178C). Site selection was guided by our prior experience with Gαz and Gαi2 and molecular modeling of Gαi1 crystal structures in the active and inactive states. Selected regions encompassed the switch II region, switch III region, α3 helix, αG/α4 loop, α4 helix and the α4/β6 loop. Several residues (E238, E239, M240, K248, D251, and Y287) were also targeted for mutation/substitution separately or in combination, as they were previously reported to regulate effector interaction in other Gα subunits. Using inhibition of forskolin-stimulated cAMP accumulation as a functional readout, constitutive activities of most RC chimeras (except one) were shown to be abolished, thereby suggesting effective disruption of the adenylyl cyclase (AC) interaction surface. However, all Gαi1/t1 chimeras harboring the QL mutation retained their ability to constitutively inhibit AC, while the two QL chimeras with substitution by Gαq sequences were ineffective. The discrepancies between RC and QL chimeras implied that the lack of inhibitory phenotype of the RC chimeras might not reflect a true disruption of the AC recognition domain, which prompted further investigations through receptor-induced Gαi1 activation. Pertussis toxin (PTX)-resistant Gαi1 chimeras (e.g., C351I for Gαi1) were constructed to facilitate the detection of receptor-induced signals following the uncoupling of all endogenous Gi proteins via PTX-catalyzed ADP-ribosylation. Upon co-expression of the CI chimeras with the Gi-coupled dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) in HEK293 cells, agonist-induced inhibition of AC was examined in PTX-treated transfectants. All Gαi1/t1 chimeras with the C351I mutation responded to quinpirole (a D2R agonist) with a suppression of cAMP accumulation, which suggest that their AC interaction domain was sufficiently intact. In comparison, a CI chimera with the α4/β6 segment of Gαi1 replaced by cognate residues of Gαq was only weakly activated by quinpirole. Collectively, our results suggest that intactness of the α4/β6 region is apparently essential for Gαi1 to interact with AC and that it is more disruptive to substitute Gαi1 residues with Gαq sequence than with Gαt1 sequence. For the second component under Objective 1, we have generated and characterized a series of Gβ1-Gαi1 and Gβ1-Gαi3 fusion proteins in order to establish a functional assay for receptor-induced release of Gβγ. Expression of the fusion protein was confirmed with Western blot detection of anti-Gαi reactivity at ~78 kDa. Using the constitutively active QL versions of the fusion proteins, Gβ1-Gαi1/3 constructs with different linkers were examined for their ability to inhibit forskolin-stimulated cAMP formation. Gβ1-Gαi3QL with a linker of 16 amino acids weakly inhibited AC, while Gβ1-Gαi1QL fusion proteins with linkers up to 26 residues failed to inhibit AC. In HEK293 cells co-expressing β1-16-i3CI (16 linker with C351I mutation on Gαi3) and the Gi-coupled D2R, quinpirole was able to inhibit cAMP accumulation following PTX-treatment. Quinpirole weakly inhibited AC via β1-16-i1CI under identical experimental conditions, thereby suggesting inherent differences between Gαi1 and Gαi3. Comparisons between QL and CI versions of the fusion proteins further revealed that the tethered Gβ1 subunit may interfere with the Gαi’s ability to interact with the receptor/effector, or that the C351I mutant has impaired function in effector regulation. Additional studies tend to support the notion that the CI mutation may indeed affect receptor interaction since its introduction to several Gαi1/t1 chimeras led to spontaneous activity, presumably because it facilitates interaction with endogenously expressed Gi-coupled receptors. In spite of the basal changes associated with the CI mutation, it was possible to detect receptor-induced activation of the Gβ1-Gαi fusion proteins. In the second objective, fusion proteins generated under the first objective were functionally characterized for their ability to interact with different Gβγ effectors. To examine whether the Gβ component of the Gβ-Gα fusion protein can signal independently, the ability of β1-16-i3QL to stimulate the formation of [3H]IP3 was examined in HEK293 cells co-expressing PLCβ2; it is well-established that Gαi3QL is incapable of activating PLCβ2 whereas all combinations of Gβ1γx serve as positive regulators of PLCβ2, and the Gβ component of β1-16-i3QL has been shown to spontaneously bind endogenous Gγ subunit and exist as “freed” Gβγ dimer. Although co-expression of PLCβ2 with Gβ1γ2 in HEK293 cells significantly elevated (~2 to 3-fold increase) basal IP3 formation, the PLCβ activity was unaltered in transfectants co-expressing β1-1-i3, β1-1-i3QL, β1-16-i3, β1-16-i3QL, Gαi3, or Gαi3QL. Likewise, none of the Gβ1-Gαi1 fusion proteins stimulated PLCβ2 under the same experimental condition; linkers up to 26 residues with or without QL mutation all failed to stimulate IP3 formation. Gβγ-dependent stimulation of type 2 adenylyl cyclase (AC2) was also employed to characterize the fusion proteins. PTX-resistant Gαi1CI, but not any of the Gβ1-Gαi1CI fusion proteins mediated agonist-induced stimulation of AC2. Since the Flag tag at the N-terminus of the Gβ1 subunit may prevent productive interaction of the Gβγ dimer with the effector, similar experiments were performed with untagged version of Gβ1-Gαi fusion proteins. Again, none of the Gβ1-Gαi1 or Gβ1-Gαi3 fusion proteins significantly stimulated AC2. Given that control experiments indicate proper responsiveness of both PLCβ2 and AC2 assays, it would appear that linkage of Gβ1 at the C-terminus may interfere with its binding to effectors. This is a rather unexpected finding because the effector domain of Gβ is generally thought to be located at the WD40 repeats. The third objective entails testing the specificity of Gγ subunits in Gβγ signaling. Towards attaining this goal, we have confirmed that the Gβ component of the fusion proteins can spontaneously interact with Gγ subunits, as co-expression with different HA-tagged Gγ subunits led to preferential formation of specific Gβγ combinations on the fusion protein. Flag-tagged Gβ1-Gαi1/3 fusion proteins were capable of associating with HA-tagged Gγ2, Gγ3, Gγ5, Gγ8, Gγ9, Gγ10, Gγ12, and Gγ13 subunits. Such interactions were independent of the linker length or activation status of the fusion proteins. However, co-expression of specific Gγ subunits with Gβ1-Gαi1/3 fusion proteins did not alter the ability of the latter to stimulate PLCβ2 or AC2. The inability of Gγ subunits to facilitate the stimulation of PLCβ2 and AC2 by Gβ1-Gαi1/3 fusion proteins implied that the availability of endogenous Gγ is not a limiting factor. An alternative explanation for both assay systems is the requirement for effector preactivation. Although this concept is not new, it has recently been revitalized with the demonstration of a strict requirement of catalytic activity prior to Gβγ activation of PLCβ2 by Gi-coupled receptors (Pfeil et al., 2020, Mol. Cell 80:1-15). Hence, it might be fruitful to re-examine the ability of Gβ1-Gαi fusion proteins to stimulate PLCβ2 and AC2 in the presence of constitutively active Gαq and Gαs, respectively.

16137516.label: Major findings and research outcome
16137516.value: The overall project goal was to generate molecular tools to enable the delineation of receptor driven Gβγ signals without interfering signals from the concomitantly activated Gα subunits. By means of homology modeling and mutagenesis studies, we have successfully created a series of Gβ-Gα fusion proteins as tools to delineate the mechanism of G protein signaling. We have demonstrated distinct requirements for subunit dissociation upon Gα activation among the different families of G proteins (Abstracts 1 and 4). Our observation that Gβγ dissociation is primarily associated with Gi proteins challenges the classical view of the G protein activation cycle, while it provides mechanistic explanations for Gβγ-mediated signal integration (Abstracts 2 and 3). We have put forth the tantalizing idea of G protein signaling without subunit dissociation in a recent publication (Publication 1 in Part C) and we are in the process of compiling the experimental data into a manuscript for a major publication (Publication 4 in Part C); it should be noted that extensive supportive evidence beyond the scope of the present study need to be generated in order to refute the current dogma of G protein activation, hence the delay in submission. Mapping of the AC recognition domain led to two interesting discoveries. Firstly, the effector domain on Gαi1 is apparently quite distinct from that of other Gαi subunits such as Gαi2 and Gαz. Secondly, the extent or robustness of constitutive activity of GTPase-deficient Gα mutants depends on the precise location of the mutation (Q204L versus R178C). Both findings have important implications on G protein signaling as it is generally assumed that the different Gαi subunits are essentially identical due to their high sequence homology, and that constitutively active Gα mutants are often used interchangeably. Our results call for caution in the interpretation of data pertaining to Gi signaling pathways and the use of GTPase-deficient mutants. Part of the findings have been compiled for publication (Publication 3 in Part C) and reported at scientific meetings (Abstracts 3, 5, and 6). The use of Gαi constructs has also contributed to the delineation of the formation of signaling complexes required for the differentiation of neural progenitor cells (Publication 2 in Part C).

16137516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16137516.value: Although our initial idea of utilizing Gβ-Gα fusion proteins as tools to examine receptor-mediated Gβγ signaling has been met with limited success, our results nevertheless suggest that the approach is feasible upon refinement of assay sensitivity. The weak activity of the fusion proteins in the two Gβγ assays is likely due to the requirement of effector preactivation (PLCβ2 and AC2). Indeed, preliminary results suggest that the Gβγ signal can be more efficiently detected when the effectors are partially stimulated by activated Gαq or Gαs. Careful titration of the preactivation signal will provide an optimum condition for the detection of Gβγ signal. Guided by molecular modelling, further mapping of the effector domain of Gαi1 has resulted in the identification of two additional residues (E216 and K257) which are apparently required for productive interaction with AC. Disruption of these two sites impaired the ability of Gαi1QL to inhibit AC. Incorporation of these two mutations into the Gαi1/q chimera (with the α4/β6 segment of Gαi1 replaced by cognate residues of Gαq) may generate a robust effector-deficient Gαi1 subunit. We will also exploit the use of Gβ-Gα fusion proteins in examining the intricate mechanism of signal integration by Gβγ subunits.

16138716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16138716.value: The initiation of DNA replication in eukaryotes is intricately and elaborately regulated to ensure that the genome is duplicated exactly once every cell division. The sequence of events that precisely describes the staged assembly of the pre-initiation complex (PIC) has been reconstituted in vitro using purified proteins. However, the molecular mechanisms of this assembly process are unknown. In this proposal, we will focus on elucidating the mechanistic details of the very early steps of the initiation process by using state-of-the-art cyroEM structural analysis. We will purify protein complexes of each assembly stage starting from the inactive MCM2-7 double hexamer that binds duplex DNA, to the intermediates that melt and separate DNA strands, and the pre-initiation complex that is poised to form the active replisome. In collaboration with the cyroEM team led by Professor Ning Gao at Tsinghua University, we have determined the structure of the MCM2-7 double hexamer at an overall resolution of 3.8 Å which allowed us to build an atomic model for >80% of the complex (Li et al., 2015). We will build onto our earlier study by sequentially adding specific factors of each defined stage to the MCM2-7 double hexamer purified from yeast G1 chromatin. We will elucidate the conformational changes that occur in the MCM2-7 double hexamer as it brings about the melting of dsDNA and compartmentalization of ssDNA during the early steps of DNA replication initiation. This detailed step-by-step structural analysis of the replication initiation machinery at near atomic resolution will provide unprecedented insight into the molecular mechanism of replication initiation that is universal to all eukaryotes. 真核生物DNA複製起始受到嚴格精確的調控，以保證基因組每個細胞週期只會被完整地複製一次。現今，複製前期複合物階段性組裝的過程，已經可以由體外重組的方法呈現出來。但是，其中許多的分子機理還不清楚。在本研究，我們會利用最先進的冷凍電子顯微鏡，解析複製開始最前期的詳細的分子過程。我們會純化其中的複製複合物，以研究DNA雙鏈打開和解鏈的機制。在以往，我們和清華大學的高寧教授合作，解構了MCM2-7雙複合物3.8埃解析度的蛋白質構象。我們會在這個基礎上，逐步研究其他蛋白組分是如何加添到MCM2-7雙複合物上，將其激活，從而達到解鏈的效果。近原子解析度的構象分析，會為我們提供重要信息，以更清楚認識理解所有真核細胞DNA複製的機理。

16138716.label: Realisation of objectives
16138716.value: During the project period, we have successfully achieved the objective 1 to understand the activation mechanism of MCM2-7 double hexamer by DDK. Using in vitro reconstitution assays, MCM-DH-DDK complex has been assembled for structure determination using cryo-EM. In the end, we obtained a cryo-EM structure of MCM-DH-DDK at an overall resolution of 3.2 Å. The information derived from this structure reveals how Dbf4 and Cdc7 act on DH to target its substrate for phosphorylation as well as the role of Dbf4 in regulating Cdc7 kinase activity. One manuscript about this part is being prepared. Regarding objective 2, we have purified both Sld3-Sld7 and Cdc45, and attempted to assemble them onto the phosphorylated DH for structure determination. Unfortunately, it turned out that the assembled complex was fragile and readily to fall apart, which renders cryo grid preparation very difficult. We are still testing different crosslinking conditions in order to stabilize the assembly for preparing cryo sample. Once this bottleneck is circumvented, we will be able to determine its structure soon.

16138716.label: Major findings and research outcome
16138716.value: Replication of the eukaryotic genome is elaborately regulated at the G1-S phase transition to ensure that a sufficient number of replication origins are activated and that no origin is activated more than once during each cell division cycle. A critical step that commits a replication origin to initiation is the transition of the inactive MCM2-7 double hexameric complex that encircles duplex DNA to the Pre-Initiation Complex that melts and compartmentalizes single strand DNA. It has been well known that DDK plays a determinant role for this transition to activate MCM DH. However, the mechanistic details about the role of DDK in this process are unknown. Using biochemical and structural approaches, we have determined a cryo-EM structure of DDK in complex with MCM DH at 3.2 Å. With the structure, for the first time, we can see how DDK acts on MCM DH to convert it from an inactive form into an active state. This is a breakthrough in the field of DNA replication. One manuscript for our findings is being prepared and will be submitted to a high profile journal.

16138716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16138716.value: The function of DDK is highly conserved among eukaryotes. Interestingly, Cdc7 overexpression is often observed in human cancer cell lines and tumor tissues. Cdc7 knockdown can induce cancer cells into apoptosis in a p53-independent manner. Therefore, Cdc7 has been used as an attractive target for anticancer drug screening and/or design. The findings of this study provide a structural framework for utilizing DDK as targets to develop novel anti-cancer drugs.

16138716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16138716.value: Duplex DNA is a very stable structure designed for the safe storage of genetic information. Replication of DNA requires the separation of the two strands so that each can serve as template for the synthesis of daughter molecules. The molecular mechanisms that destabilize hydrogen bonds holding the duplex then melt and separate the two strands are of fundamental interest to chemists and biophysicists. The mechanism that regulates this very important step is one of the keys to understanding the regulation of cell division and proliferation. One important enzyme catalysing this step is Mcm2-7 helicase. Once activated, MCM can unzip the duplex DNA. In this study, we have successfully resolved the structure of MCM in complex with DDK. This allows us to visualise how DDK acts on MCM complex to activate its helicase activity. Seeing is believing. This work provides novel insights into the mechanism regulating DNA replication initiation.

Using a tripartite split-GFP association assay, we will probe the temporal regulation of AUP1-DGAT-2 interaction by imaging live animals in fed and fasted states. Identify the ERAD pathway and proteasome components required for DGAT-2 degradation. We will test existing mutant C. elegans strains that lack specific ERAD components and engineer additional ones by CRISPR mediated genome editing to define the ERAD module that is necessary for DGAT-2 degradation. Furthermore, we will perturb proteasome function by genetic and chemical methods and assess the stability of DGAT-2 by biochemical and imaging assays. Identify LD associated proteins that are prone to fasting induced degradation. We will engineer transgenic C. elegans strains that express fluorescent protein tagged LD associated proteins with predicted metabolic or structural functions. A ratiometric time-lapse live imaging assay will be used to assess the relative stability of these proteins in fed and fasted states.

16140216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16140216.value: Lipid droplets are evolutionarily conserved organelles for cellular fat storage, which are endowed with a unique set of proteins that serve structural or metabolic functions. The composition of lipid droplet associated proteins must be dynamically maintained to ensure the correct balance of fat synthesis and utilization. Failure to do so may cause excessive fat storage at the cellular and organismal level, and contribute to the metabolic disturbances in obesity and lipodystrophy. However, the molecular mechanisms governing the retention and stability of lipid droplet associated proteins are largely unknown. Our long-term goal is to understand how the lipid droplet proteome is altered in response to changes in cellular nutrient levels. We are particularly interested in the turnover of lipid droplet associated proteins as an animal switches from the fed to fasted state. We hypothesize that fat synthesis enzymes should be displaced or degraded to allow the recruitment of lipolytic enzymes to the lipid droplet surface during this transition. We have previously shown that a diacylglycerol acyl-transferase (DGAT-2), which is the terminal enzyme for triglyceride synthesis, resides on the lipid droplet surface in fed C. elegans animals. Consistent with our hypothesis, DGAT-2 disappears in fasted animals while a lipid droplet structural protein remains stable. Using a candidate gene approach, we found that fasting-induced degradation of DGAT-2 is regulated by the Ancient Ubiquitous Protein 1 (AUP1), which resides on the lipid droplet surface, and the ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway. To extend our observations, we propose experiments to (1) define the molecular determinants for AUP1-DGAT-2 interaction; (2) identify the ERAD pathway and proteasome components required for DGAT-2 degradation; (3) identify lipid droplet associated proteins that are prone to fasting induced degradation. Our results should elucidate the spatial temporal requirement of AUP1 and ERAD pathway components in DGAT-2 degradation in fasted animals. We will also test if the same regulatory logic applies to additional proteins in the triglyceride and phospholipid synthesis pathways. Our work should help define a new mode of regulation of fat synthesis and identify targets for genetic and pharmacological intervention against metabolic disorders. 脂滴是儲存脂肪的主要的保守細胞器，它具備一套獨特的結構性和代謝功能的蛋白質。脂滴相關蛋白的組合物，必須動態維護，以確保脂肪合成和利用的正確平衡。如果不這樣做可能會在細胞和身體水平上導致過多的脂肪儲存，並導致肥胖和脂肪代謝的紊亂。然而，有關脂滴蛋白質的保持性和穩定性的分子機制在很大程度上是未知的。我們的長期目標是要了解脂滴蛋白質組是如何應對細胞營養水平上的變化。我們推測，禁食期間脂肪合成酶應被取代或降解，以便將脂解酶招到脂滴的表面。我們以前曾發現，DGAT-2 是駐留在饋線蟲脂滴表面上三酯甘油合成的終端酶。與我們的假設一致，DGAT-2在動物禁食時消失, 而脂滴結構蛋白則保持穩定。我們發現，禁食誘導DGAT-2的降解需要位於脂滴表面上的AUP1 和 ER 相關降解（ERAD)途徑。為了擴展我們的觀察，我們提出下列的實驗:（1）定義AUP1-DGAT-2相互作用的分子決定因素; （2）確定DGAT-2降解所需的ERAD途徑和蛋白酶體部件; （3）確定其他被禁食誘導降解的脂滴相關蛋白。我們的結果應闡明DGAT-2在禁食動物被AUP1和ERAD途徑組分降解的時空要求。我們還將測試同樣的監管邏輯是否也適用於在甘油三酯和磷脂合成途徑以外的蛋白質。我們的工作應該有助於確定脂肪合成調控的新模式，並發現新一代打擊代謝紊亂的遺傳和藥物干預的目標。

16140216.label: Realisation of objectives
16140216.value: 1. Define the molecular determinants of AUP1-DGAT-2 interaction. In C. elegans, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to generate multiple knockin strains in which the coding sequences for green fluorescent protein (GFP), red fluorescent protein (mRuby), FLAG epitope tag, and HA epitope tag were inserted into the endogenous dgat-2 and aup-1 loci. We demonstrated that mRuby::DGAT-2 and AUP-1::GFP, expressed at the endogenous level, colocalized on lipid droplets (LDs) in the C. elegans intestine. In addition, AUP-1::GFP was also detected on LDs in other tissues such as the hypodermis. Therefore, the targeting of AUP-1::GFP to LDs is not dependent on DGAT-2. Since the expression levels of DGAT-2 and AUP-1 are low relative to other LD resident proteins such as DHS-3, it was challenging to perform co-immunoprecipitation experiments for the detection of physical association of DGAT-2 with AUP-1. Next, we generated a suite of transgenic strains in order to use the reconstitution of tripartite GFP as a readout for DGAT-2/AUP-1 association. To this end, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to generate strains that expressed AUP-1::GFP10 and GFP11::DGAT-2 at the endogenous level. In addition, worms carrying a single-copy transgene that expressed the GFP1-9 fragment under the ubiquitous eft-3 promoter was generated. In worms carrying all three modifications, we did not detect GFP signals on LDs, as would be expected if DGAT-2 and AUP-1 interacted on LD surface. One challenge to the reconstitution of tripartite GFP might stem from the relative configuration of GFP10 and GFP11 fragments when they were presented as fusion proteins with AUP-1 and DGAT-2. Even if DGAT-2 interacts with AUP-1 on LD surface, their conformations may exert steric hindrance that prevents the GFP10 and GFP11 fragments from congregating spatially. To overcome this issue, we propose to lengthen the flexible linker that connects the GFP fragments with AUP-1 and DGAT-2. In parallel, we generated OP9 pre-adipocytes that stably expressed 2xHA::mRuby::DGAT2 and FLAG::AUP1::GFP using the Sleeping Beauty (SB) Transposon technique. Because the SB transposon promotes variable number of insertions into the host genome, we used fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) to select cells that stably expressed similar levels of DGAT2 and AUP1. Similar to C. elegans, we detected co-localization of DGAT2 and AUP1 on LDs when OP9 pre-adipocytes were cultured in the presence of oleic acid. We then determined that the withdrawal of serum from the culture medium mimicked food withdrawal in worms. Live imaging indicated that the levels of DGAT2 and AUP1 progressively decreased over a period of 24 hours, after serum withdrawal. Concomitantly, the size of LDs decreased. Therefore, we have successfully recapitulated our observations made in C. elegans in mammalian OP9 cells. This is not trivial because the experimental conditions for OP9 cells were not well-established, unlike 3T3-L1 pre-adipocytes. We are now poised to carry out further analysis on the physical association of DGAT2 and AUP1 by biochemical and imaging assays. 2. Identify the ERAD pathway and proteasome components required for DGAT-2 degradation. We used the CRISPR/Cas9 technique to generate new deletion alleles of sel-11, marc-6, and sel-1. We carried out in depth analysis of fasting-induced DGAT-2 degradation by live imaging and Western blotting in hrdl-1, sel-11, marc-6, sel-1; hrdl-1, sel-1 sel-11, sel-1; marc-6, cdc-48.1 and cdc-48.2 mutant worms. Taken together, we conclude the following. (1) All three ERAD E3 ligases: HRDL-1, SEL-11 and MARC-6 contribute to fasting-induced DGAT-2 degradation. This is consistent with the notion that these ligases serve partially overlapping functions. (2) Although SEL-1 is predicted to act primarily with SEL-11, based on the functional analysis of their yeast orthologs, we found that SEL-1 acts, to different extent, with all three ERAD E3 ligases, to promote fasting-induced degradation of DGAT-2 in C elegans. (3) Deficiency in CDC-48.2 but not CDC-48.1 retards fasting-induced DGAT-2 degradation. Although both proteins are orthologs of the mammalian AAA ATPase VCP, which acts downstream of ERAD, our results reveal unexpected substrate specificity of the two VCP paralogs. We also analyzed the turnover of AUP-1 in fasted worms. In contrast to DGAT-2, which relied on all three ERAD E3 ligases for degradation, our data indicate that AUP-1 degradation is primarily dependent on the SEL-11 ligase and its canonical partner SEL-1. Therefore, we propose that DGAT-2 disassociates with AUP-1 once they return to the ER, prior to their engagement with the ERAD pathway for their respective degradation. Overall, our results point to discrete steps that promote fasting-induced DGAT-2 degradation. The translocation of DGAT-2 from LDs to the ER in fasted worms is a regulated process that depends on AUP-1. To solidify this important point, we inserted the coding sequence of a photo-convertible protein monomeric Kikume green-red (mKikGR), into the dgat-2 locus. mKikGR can be converted from green to red upon UV excitation. Accordingly, the existing pool of mKikGR::DGAT-2 proteins could be labeled in red under fed condition, and their fate in fasted worms determined by live imaging. Consistent with our observations with GFP::DGAT-2, we detected mKikGR::DGAT-2 on LDs in fed worms before and immediately after photo-conversion. When photo-converted worms were fasted for 10 hours, red fluorescent DGAT-2 was undetectable suggesting the removal of pre-existing DGAT-2 in these worms. Next, we examined mKikGR::DGAT-2 in fasted hrdl-1 and aup-1 mutant worms. Interestingly, photo-converted red fluorescent DGAT-2 could be detected in the ER and on LDs of fasted hrdl-1 and aup-1 mutant worms, respectively. Our results clearly indicate that fasting induced DGAT-2 degradation is dependent on the ERAD pathway, subsequent to its translocation from LDs to the ER in an AUP-1 dependent manner. 3. Identify LD associated proteins that are prone to fasting induced degradation. As detailed in the appended manuscript, we found a clear difference in the stability DHS-3 and DGAT-2 in fasted worms, based on imaging and Western blotting data. Our observations support the hypothesis that the turnover of LD associated proteins can be linked to their function during lipolysis. According to this model, fatty acid mobilization from LDs would be rendered futile if neutral lipid synthesis enzymes, such as DGAT-2, remain active in fasted worms. Therefore, DGAT-2 is selected for degradation, while LD structural proteins such as DHS-3 remain stable. Interestingly, DHS-3 is translocated from LDs to the ER after prolonged fasting (20 hours). Nevertheless, DHS-3 remains stable and evades degradation by ERAD suggesting that translocation to the ER per se is not sufficient to trigger protein degradation. We reason that additional neutral lipid synthesis enzymes will be subject to fasting-induced degradation, similar to DGAT-2. Notably, DGAT-2 is only expressed in the intestine, while LDs are detected ubiquitously. This strongly suggests that additional triacylglycerol (TAG) synthesis enzymes operate in other tissues such as the hypodermis. For example, DGAT1 and DGAT2 are two structurally unrelated enzymes in humans, yet the C. elegans DGAT1 ortholog has not been identified. Accordingly, DGAT-2 deficient worms still have lipid droplets and detectable level of TAG. These results suggest functional compensation of DGAT-2 by additional TAG synthesis enzymes. To this end, we have conducted an RNAi screen in order to identify enzymes that specifically promote LD expansion in the hypodermis. Our preliminary results suggest an enzyme that belongs to the MBOA protein family as the top candidate. Further analysis will be necessary to confirm its function in fed worms, before we attempt to study its turnover in fasted worms.
