16150016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16150016.value: Epithelial cells are highly polarized cells with distinct apical and basolateral domains defined by specific protein complexes. The conserved Scribble module localizes at the basolateral region. It consists of three scaffold proteins, namely Scribble (Scrib), Discs large (Dlg) and Lethal giant larvae (Lgl). The Scribble module was originally identified in Drosophila as a group of “neoplastic tumor suppressor genes” (nTSGs). Drosophila imaginal disc cells homozygous mutant for the Scribble module genes grow into tumors that are disorganized, undifferentiated, lethal and transplantable. In mammals, loss of the Scribble module function is also linked with epithelial tumor progression. We noticed that the cells deficient for the Scribble module show location-dependent growth phenotypes. Specifically, the Scrib and Dlg deficient cells can only grow into tumor-like masses in the highly curved epithelial regions including the hinge region of wing imaginal discs and the polar region of the follicular epithelia. We showed that the ectopic activation of myosin II activity induces folding in the flat wing pouch region and rescues the Scrib and Dlg deficient cells from cell competition-induced elimination. We also showed that the folded wing hinge region exhibits higher Yki activity. Together, these data point us to the hypothesis that the highly curved region in the epithelium exhibits higher Yki activity that promotes the nTSG mutant cell growth. Here we propose to mechanistically dissect how epithelial curvature influences the growth outcome of the nTSG mutant cells in Drosophila and further explore a possible role of epithelial curvature in growth control in mammalian systems. 定位於表皮細胞層側壁的Scribble蛋白複合體是一個進化中高度保守的複合體，它們在生長調控中起重要作用。當細胞中Scribble蛋白複合體功能失調時，細胞會過度增殖形成可轉移的腫瘤。我們發現Scribble蛋白複合體功能失調引發的腫瘤生長具有選擇性。在表皮細胞層曲率高的地方，Scribble蛋白複合體功能失調的細胞易於生長為大塊腫瘤，在平面的表皮細胞層，Scribble蛋白複合體功能失調的細胞常常受細胞競爭的調控而凋亡。我們致力於研究細胞層曲率如何通過調控Yki活性影響Scribble蛋白複合體功能失調的細胞生長和凋亡的機理。

16150016.label: Realisation of objectives
16150016.value: Scrib, dlg and lgl were originally discovered in Drosophila as a group of “neoplastic tumor suppressor genes” (nTSGs). When the imaginal disc cells are homozygous mutant for the Scribble module components, the mutant cells fail to differentiate and continuously proliferate to form large unstructured tumors. However, when the scrib and dlg mutant cells are generated as mosaic clones and surrounded by wild type cells in the imaginal discs, they get eliminated through a cell competition process. In this project we performed a series of experiments to understand the context-dependent growth phenotypes of these mutants. 1. Through quantitative analysis we found that the scrib mutant tumors display dramatically different growth rates and cell cycle profiles over time. Longitudinal bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the scrib mutant tumors revealed that the MAPK pathway, including the JNK and EGFR signaling activities in the scrib mutant tumors, shows quantitative changes over time. We found that high JNK signaling activity causes G2/M cell cycle arrest in the early scrib mutant tumors. In addition, JNK signaling activity displays a radial polarity with the JNKhigh cells located at the periphery of the scrib mutant tumors, providing an inherent mechanism that leads to an overall JNK signaling activity decrease over time. We also found that the EGFR signaling activity, in contrast to JNK activity, increases over time and promotes growth in the late-stage scrib mutant tumors. Finally, high JNK signaling activity represses EGFR signaling activity in the early scrib mutant tumors. Together, these data demonstrated that dynamic MAPK signaling activity, fueled by intratumor heterogeneity derived from tissue topological differences, drives a growth arrest-to-proliferation transition in the scrib mutant tumors. This work was published in Disease Models & Mechanisms. 2. We constructed a single cell atlas of the wing imaginal discs and the scrib mutant tumors. We systematically examine the patterning and differentiation processes in the scrib mutants in comparison with wild type imaginal discs and found that the scrib mutants retain partial differentiation and patterning abilities despite of a complete loss of tissue architecture. This work was published in Development.

16150016.value: The early process of human cancer development, during which a few oncogenic cells are undetectable, remains difficult to study. Our work demonstrated that a well-established Drosophila tumor model, caused by loss of apicobasal cell polarity, harbors a surprising degree of plasticity and evolvability along the temporal axis. The study provided us with the possibility of studying tumor evolution in a genetically-accessible and fast-growing invertebrate tumor model. Our study also highlights that intratumor heterogeneity can arise from tissue architecture intrinsically in the early tumorigenesis stage and shape the tumorigenesis trajectory without de novo mutations.

16150216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16150216.value: The mitochondrial RNA polymerase (mtRNAP) transcribes on mitochondrial genes, which are related to ATP synthesis. The mtRNAP is a single subunit RNA polymerase different from the nucleus eukaryote RNA polymerase II composed of 12 subunits. It is known that the mitochondrial DNA is more susceptible to DNA damages than the nucleus DNA. Here, we would like to investigate the dynamics of the mtRNAP transcription elongation process when mtRNAP encounters DNA damages such as 8-oxoguanine and cisplatin adducts using biochemical and single-molecule optical tweezers transcription elongation assays. We will characterize the transcription enhancing effect of transcription elongation factor TEFM. Furthermore, we will study the transcription repressing effect of another transcription factor TFAM in the mtRNAP transcription elongation. Moreover, we will study the effects of these transcription factors on the mtRNAP transcription elongation process in the presence of DNA damages. 16150216.label: Realisation of objectives
16150216.value: To understand the mechanism of the transcription elongation regulation in mitochondria, we have performed the following experiments. Part of the results have been presented in several conferences and published in Yu et al. 2018 and An et al. 2017, while other results are currently under preparation for another manuscript to be published. Objective 1 We performed biochemical transcription elongation assay using purified mitochondrial RNA polymerase (mtRNAP) in the presence of cisplatin or 8-oxoguanine containing template. These results show that the majority of mtRNAP molecules are stalled at the cisplatin adduct. From the single-molecule transcription elongation assay, we found that single-subunit mtRNAP transcription elongation is similar to multi-subunit RNA polymerase II (Pol II) transcription elongation in transcription velocity, pause duration and pause frequency. The stall force of mtRNAP is slightly lower than that of Pol II. This result indicates that mtRNAP has a lower processivity, which agrees with previous report (1). The majority of mtRNAP molecules are stalled when it encounters to damaged DNA sites, and then terminated transcription in the single-molecule transcription elongation assay. Only a few mtRNAPs could overcome the damaged DNA after short pausing at the damaged site. These results suggest that mtRNAP may prefer to terminate transcription elongation whenever it encounters pausing site or transcriptional barrier. Objective 2 TEFM was first identified as nucleus Pol II elongation factor Spt6 like protein (2). TEFM interacts with the mtRNAP elongation complex and enhances the transcription elongation (1,3). TEFM is thought to be important to regulate the switch between DNA replication and transcription of mitochondrial DNA particularly at the conserved sequence block II (CSBII), which is the mtRNAP transcription termination sequence. Within CSBII, a DNA-RNA G-quadruplex structure is formed to promote termination (1,3). It has been suggested that transcription termination at CSBII may stimulate DNA replication initiation by producing a replication primer (3,4). Therefore, TEFM may be important for regulating the switch between transcription and DNA replication of mitochondrial DNA. A recent structural study shows that TEFM binds mtRNAP near the RNA exit channel and its binding has been proposed to prevent formation of the DNA-RNA G-quadruplex (5). We studied the effects of TEFM on transcription elongation using a single-molecule optical-tweezers transcription assay. We found that TEFM does not change pause-free velocity and short-lived pauses, but enhances transcription elongation by reducing long-lived pause frequencies and long-lived pause durations. Furthermore, our data suggest that TEFM increases the probability of mtRNAP’s passage through CSBII by preventing the formation of the RNA-DNA hybrid G-quadruplex. These results are were published in (6). Objective 3 TFAM is encoded by a nuclear gene and imported to the mitochondria. TFAM binds to DNA as a dimeric form and the footprint of TFAM binding is about 22 bp long (7,8). Several studies show that the mitochondrial DNA compaction by TFAM is highly cooperative and the naked DNA is largely compacted when TFAM is added at the physiological concentration in vitro (9,10). Physiological concentration of TFAM represses the mtRNAP transcription process (10). In addition to its function as a transcription regulator and DNA packing factor, TFAM prefers binding to DNA damages such as cisplatin adduct (11,12). However, it remains unknown whether the TFAM-DNA binding preference plays a role in mitochondria transcription regulation. To understand the function of TFAM as a transcription elongation repressor, we performed the mtRNAP transcription elongation assay using a template containing DNA damage (8-oxoguanine or cisplatin adduct), Guanine repeat sequences that are frequently present in the mitochondrial DNA, or mtRNAP transcription termination sequence Conserved Sequence Block II (CSBII). TFAM prevents mtRNAP transcription elongation as reported previously (10), and its repression can be relieved by addition of TEFM. The effects of these transcription factors are similar at the DNA damage sites. Furthermore, TFAM prefers to bind DNA-RNA G-quadruplex at the CSBII sequence, and represses mtRNAP transcription elongation. Moreover, the transcription repression at the CSBII site caused by TFAM cannot be relieved by TEFM. Neither TFAM nor TEFM affect transcription elongation at DNA-DNA G-quadruplex sequence site since mtRNAP transcription elongation is completely repressed. TFAM might be involved in the protection and maintenance of the DNA-RNA G-quadruplex since it has a preferential binding to the G-quadruplex structure and it might be important to regulate gene expression in vivo. These results are currently under preparation for publication. In addition to these objectives, using the analytical method for the optical tweezers transcripiton assay, we analysed the myosin movements in live Drosophila embryos with high spatiotemporal precision and these results were published in (13). 16150216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16150216.value: Regulation of transcription elongation is one of the key mechanisms employed to control gene expression. The single-subunit mitochondrial RNA polymerase (mtRNAP) transcribes mitochondrial genes, such as those related to ATP synthesis. We investigated how mitochondrial transcription elongation factor (TEFM) enhances mtRNAP transcription elongation using both biochemical in vitro transcription elongation assay and single-molecule optical-tweezers transcription assay, which follows transcription dynamics in real time and allows the separation of pause-free elongation from transcriptional pauses. We found that TEFM enhances the stall force of mtRNAP. Although TEFM does not change the pause-free elongation rate, it enhances mtRNAP transcription elongation by reducing the frequency of long-lived pauses and shortening their durations. Furthermore, we demonstrate how mtRNAP passes through the conserved sequence block II (CSBII), which is the key sequence for the switch between DNA replication and transcription in mitochondria (Yu et al. 2018). Furthermore, we found that it is easier for mtRNAP to go through the cisplatin and 8-oxoguanine damaged DNAs in the presence of TEFM and it is much harder for mtRNAP to go through them in presence of another mitochondrial transcription factor TFAM. The increase of overcome probability are mainly due to the pause-reducing effects of TEFM. And TEFM enhances transcription elongation and relieves the transcription repression caused by TFAM except CSBII site due to tighter binding of TFAM. Our findings elucidate how both TEFM and mitochondrial genomic DNA sequences directly control the transcription elongation dynamics of mtRNAP.

16150216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16150216.value: We have studied one regulation process of transcription elongation, namely transcription pausing, and investigated how the mitochondrial transcription elongation factor TEFM affects the rates of pause entry and recovery from pause. We also investigated how another mitochondrial transcription factor TFAM represses transcription in particular at CSBII site. There are several other transcription factors present in mitochondria. Therefore, using the method established in this study, we will look into the functional roles of other mitochondrial transcriptional factors and DNA sequence effects on transcription. These future studies will help us to elucidate the mechanisms of gene expression regulation in mitochondria, and shed light on mitochondria-related diseases.

16150216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16150216.value: Mitochondrial genomic DNA is a circular DNA that codes for 13 ATP synthesis related genes, 22 transfer RNAs and 2 ribosomal RNAs. Mitochondrial RNA polymerase (mtRNAP) transcribes these mitochondrial-encoded genes. Similar to nucleus RNA polymerase II, which synthesize mRNAs, mtRNAP transcription is regulated at all three stages: initiation, elongation, and termination. The transcription elongation is the stage of RNA synthesis and an important part of transcription regulation by mtRNAP. We have conducted a single-molecule optical tweezers transcription elongation assay, which allows us to monitor the mtRNAP transcription movement in real time. We found that mtRNAP have pause-free translocation and two types of pauses in elongation: short lived and long lived. We also found the mitochondrial transcription factor TEFM did not alter the pause-free elongation rate, but it did reduce the frequency of long-lived pauses and shortened their durations. We also demonstrated that mtRNAP transcription elongation pauses at conserved sequence block II (CSBII), whereas TEFM prevents DNA-RNA G-quadruplexes from forming a barrier for mtRNAP to transcribe through CSBII. Our study provided a mechanistic understanding of mitochondrial gene expression regulation.

16201116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201116.value: Finding the location of a query point on a planar map is a basic operation in various applications as well as a classical problem in computational geometry. After determining the region that contains the query point, the attributes of the region can be used for further processing (e.g., the weather forecast for the town where the user is located). Data structures have been proposed in the past that have a worst-case query time increasing as the logarithm of the planar map size. However, regions in the map often have vastly different access frequencies, and it is beneficial for the query time to be less for regions with higher access frequencies. Having the same worst-case query time for all regions may lead to suboptimal performance when answering a sequence of queries. A data structure with a query time sensitive to the query distribution is highly desirable. Further, the access pattern often evolves over time; for example, the access frequencies of beaches drop from summer through fall to winter. It is not known whether one can design data structures that adapt to an evolving access pattern. In addition, we need efficient methods of updating the point location structure when the map is modified, while preserving a query time sensitive to a given or evolving access pattern. 平面檢定查詢點的位置在很多問題有廣泛應用，亦是計算幾何一個經典問題。確定包含查詢點的區域後，該區域的屬性可用於進一步處理（例如，用戶所在地的天氣預報）。 過去已有平面定點數據結構能保証最差查詢時間與輸入大小的對數有歸線性關係。然而，不同的地區經常有很不同的查詢頻率，查詢有較高訪問頻率的區域時間，應更快捷。只對所有區域保証最差查詢時間可能使處理一序列的查詢點時，用上較多時間。 對查詢點分佈敏感的數據結構是非常可取的。另外，查詢點的分佈往往隨時間演變; 例如，海灘的查詢頻率會從夏季開始下降。目前還不知道能否設計可適應查詢演變的數據結構。此外，我們需要有效的方法去修改地圖，並同時能適既定的或演變的查詢模式。

16201116.label: Realisation of objectives
16201116.value: The distribution-adaptive point location problem is defined as follows. A planar subdivision is given, which is represented in the form of a planar graph embedded in the plane, and we are supposed to provide answers to an online stream σ of point location queries. The coordinates of a query point are specified in each query, and we need to return the region in the subdivision that contains the query point. Moreover, each query must be answered before the next query is revealed. That is, σ is unknown beforehand. Such queries often arise in applications in geographical information systems. Let n denote the size of the input subdivision. Let OPT be the minimum time required by any static linear decision tree to process σ. The ultimate goal is to process σ in O(n+OPT) time, which is asymptotically the best possible running time that one can hope for. We have fully achieved the first project objective of designing distribution-adaptive point location structures for convex and connected subdivisions. Indeed, we have achieved the optimal O(n+OPT) processing time for convex subdivisions. This finds applications in the fundamental nearest neighbor search problem as Voronoi diagrams are convex subdivisions. In addition, we have nearly achieved this goal for the more general connected subdivisions in which every region is a simple polygon, and the outer boundary of the subdivision also bounds a simple polygon. Our processing time for connected subdivisions is O(n + OPT + |σ| log(log*n)) time, where |σ| denotes the length of σ, and log*n is an extremely slowly growing function; for example, log*n ≤ 5 for any n less than or equal to 2 raised to the power of 65536. Note that OPT ≥|σ|. Our results can be viewed as a two-dimensional analog of the celebrated static optimality theorem of Sleator and Tarjan [1] in one dimension. The dynamic planar point location problem refers to the setting that the user can issue two types of operations. First, finding the region that contains a query point. Second, specify some insertions and deletions of edges to modify the planar subdivision. While researchers have been aggressively pursuing an O(n) space solution, O(log⁡ n) query time, and O(log⁡ n) update time per edge insertion or deletion, no result has ever been published on handling updates while guaranteeing an optimal query time with respect to the query distribution. We achieve our second project objective by designing the first dynamic planar point location structures for convex and connected subdivisions that can exploit the query distribution. While it is built upon the multilevel caching technique that we develop for the distribution-adaptive planar point location problem described above, we also invent a new data structure called the slab tree that allows us to exploit the query distribution in the dynamic setting. Consider the case that the query distribution is fixed and there is an oracle that returns the probability of a query point falling into a polygonal region of constant complexity. For convex subdivisions, our dynamic solution achieves the asymptotically optimal expected time, that is, our expected query time is within a constant factor of the expected query time of the best possible linear decision for the current convex subdivision. We can modify the convex subdivision in O(klog^4 n) amortized time, where k is the number of edge insertions and deletions involved in the modification. For connected subdivision, our expected query time is O(OPT+ log(log*n)), which is extremely close to the optimum, and our amortized update time is O(klog^8 n+ log^31 n). We have not managed to construct a dynamic planar point location structure for the distribution-adaptive case yet. It turns out that allowing changes in the query distribution leads to a lot of significant, open research issues that require a separate in-depth study. For instance, in the distribution-adaptive case, one may wish to keep track of the access frequencies of the regions in order to maintain a planar point location structure that can exploit the evolving query distribution. However, when the subdivision is modified, it is highly non-trivial to efficiently retrieve the access frequencies of the modified regions. This problem is known as simplex range counting, and a simplex range counting query cannot be answered in polylogarithmic time using a data structure of linear size. Allowing a data structure of super-linear size does not seem to help either because a larger data structure usually means a more expensive update time when the data structure is modified. [1] D. Sleator and R. Tarjan. Self-adjusting binary search tree. Journal of the ACM, 32 (1985) 652-686.

16201116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201116.value: We propose methods to answer point location queries in convex and connected subdivisions that are presented in an online stream σ. Each query must be answered before the next query is revealed. Let n denote the size of the input subdivision. Let OPT be the minimum time required by any static linear decision tree to process σ. For convex subdivisions, we achieve the optimal O(n+OPT) processing time. For connected subdivisions, we initially achieve an O(n+OPT+|σ| log⁡log n) time. These results have been reported in the conference paper (1) listed in part C. Subsequently, we improve the result for connected subdivisions to O(n+OPT+|σ| log(log*n)). Our results on convex and connected subdivisions have been accepted by SIAM Journal on Computing as listed in the journal paper (1) listed in part C. We have designed the first dynamic planar point location structures for convex and connected subdivisions that can exploit the query distribution. Consider the case that the query distribution is fixed and there is an oracle that returns the probability of a query point falling into a polygonal region of constant complexity. For convex subdivisions, our dynamic solution achieves the asymptotically optimal expected time, that is, our expected query time is within a constant factor of the expected query time of the best possible linear decision for the current convex subdivision. The amortized update time is O(klog^4 n) , where k is the number of edge insertions and deletions involved in the modification. This dynamic method, with a slightly worse update time of O(klog^5 n), first appeared in the conference paper (2) listed in part C. Subsequently, we submitted the full version to a journal. When revising the paper according to reviewers’ comments, we have improved the amortized update time to O(klog^4 n). This paper is currently under review; refer to the journal paper (2) listed in part C. For connected subdivision, our expected query time is O(OPT+ log(log*n)), and our amortized update time is O(klog^8 n+ log^31 n). The result for connected subdivisions is included in my student's PhD thesis.

16201116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201116.value: There are several significant research directions that can be pursued further. The first direction is to achieve the asymptotically optimal processing time of an online query stream σ for connected subdivisions. That is, remove the O(log(log*n)) overhead per query in the online stream in our result. This will close an open problem in computational geometry. In addition, it should lead to an optimal expected query time for dynamic point location in connected subdivisions. Second, there are quite a number of interesting research issues that one can work on to efficiently accommodate updates in the query distribution when processing. For example, it will be interesting to pursue a dynamic point location structure that can adapt to an evolving query distribution; it will also be very interesting to allow for more arbitrarily changes in the query distribution. Changes in query distribution have never been mentioned or studied in the literature for planar point location. Such studies should lead to the discovery of new algorithmic techniques. We have submitted a General Research Fund proposal on studying these research problems to the Research Grants Council.

16201116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201116.value: Finding the location of a query point on a planar map is a basic operation in various applications as well as a classical problem in computational geometry. After determining the region that contains the query point, the attributes of the region can be used for further processing; for example, finding the nearest convenience store, or obtaining the weather forecast at the user’s location. Regions in the map often have vastly different access frequencies, and it is beneficial for the query time to be less for regions with higher access frequencies. We propose methods that can answer an online stream of queries optimally for convex subdivisions, and nearly optimally for connected subdivisions. In addition, we have designed dynamic point location structures that can support optimal expected query for convex subdivisions while allowing the underlying map to be modified efficiently. Similar results also hold for connected subdivisions. These are the first results in these research directions, and we expect that there will be more follow-up works by researchers in the community in the future.

16202716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202716.value: Field monitoring is an effective means for geotechnical risk management. Important engineered slopes are often heavily instrumented and their performance monitored. With the advent of new sensing and wireless communication technologies, low-cost sensors are being massively employed. After acquiring a large quantity of data, how to interpret the data and evaluate the slope reliability is a key scientific issue facing geotechnical engineers. Several pioneers have explored the use of monitoring information in a physical manner to close up knowledge gaps, update design analysis, and prompt necessary design changes or contingency plans. Terzaghi (1961) described a “learn-as-you-go” procedure to incorporate observations in design. Peck (1969), in the 9th Rankine Lecture, formalized the procedure into the well-known “observational method.” Wu (2011), in his Peck Lecture, formulated the observational method mathematically using Bayes’ theory. In this research project, further advancements will be made to formulate the observational method to allow the inclusion of multi-source large quantity observational data from modern sensor networks for interactive, physically based evaluation of slope reliability. The primary objective of this research project is to establish a Bayesian network method to evaluate the on-service reliability of engineered slopes by fusing multi-source large quantity field monitoring information with underlying physical mechanisms. In this project, multiple sources of monitoring information at multiple points on or inside the slope will be integrated using Bayesian networks assisted by sound finite element or finite difference numerical analyses. The reliability of a heavily instrumented high slope will be analysed to illustrate the proposed methods. The uncertainties in the slope material properties, the analysis models and the field observations will be properly considered. The correlations among monitoring information and error terms will also be systematically quantified. Potential fault paths that could lead to distress or failure of slopes will be presented clearly in the Bayesian networks, and the critical factors that contribute significantly to the distress or failure of slopes will be singled out through machine learning in the Bayesian networks. Alert levels in the monitoring parameter space that correspond to designated values of probability of failure or safety factor will be provided for decision making. The outcome from this research project will advance the theoretical formulations for big data analytics in geotechnical engineering, which is a bottleneck in the development of modern geotechnical sensing technologies. The project will also inject momentum to the widely used observational method by enabling the inclusion of multi-source monitoring data. 現場監測是岩土工程風險控制的一個有效手段。隨著新的傳感及無線通訊技術的出現，廉價的傳感儀器得到廣泛應用，經常在重要的邊坡上安裝大量的監測儀器，以對其安全狀況進行監控。然而，在獲取大量監測資料後，如何利用這些資料來評價邊坡的安全度，是岩土工程師面臨的一個重要科學問題。不少著名學者曾通過結合物理機制及監測資料的方法，填補認知缺陷，更新設計方案，提出必要的設計變更或應急計畫。Terzaghi（1961）提出了一種“邊走邊學”的流程，結合監測結果進行岩土設計。Peck（1969）在第9屆Rankine講座上對這個流程進行了歸納，並將其發展為著名的“觀測法”。Wu （2011）在他的Peck講座上，應用貝葉斯原理建立了一個觀測法的數學模型。在本研究中，我們將進一步發展觀測法，創建一個貝葉斯網羅方法，通過融合大量多源監測資料及物理機制，對在役工程邊坡進行互動式安全分析。在本研究中，將通過貝葉斯網絡及有限元或有限差分數值分析對邊坡內外部多個測點採集的多源監測資訊進行有機融合，並應用該方法分析某個安裝了大量監測儀器的高邊坡的可靠度。該方法能合理考慮邊坡材料性質、物理模型及現場監測中的非確定性因素，系統地量化監測資訊的相關性及誤差。貝葉斯網絡還能清晰地展示邊坡潛在的失效路徑，甄別導致邊坡失效的關鍵因素。該方法可為決策者提供與規定的失效概率或安全係數對應的觀測變數預警值。研究結果還將推進大數據分析在岩土工程中的應用，解決現代岩土工程傳感技術發展的一個瓶頸問題。

16202716.label: Realisation of objectives
16202716.value: (1) Objective 1: Interactive Bayesian network approach for slope safety evaluation with multi-source large quantity monitoring information An efficient Bayesian network approach with clear underlying physical mechanisms has been established to evaluate the slope safety using with multi-source large quantity field monitoring information at multiple points on or inside the slope. The Bayesian network involves spatially correlated geotechnical parameters and dozens of observational points. Simplified techniques are developed to solve the high-dimensional Bayesian network problems. The computational efficiency is remarkably improved by discretizing continuous random variables, introducing a critical probability to reduce the size of conditional probability tables, and replacing the finite difference analysis by artificial neural networks. The reliability of slope can be instantaneously evaluated within the Bayesian network once monitoring information is available. Quantitative evaluation of the value of monitoring information obtained from additional observations is also conducted. It is found that, with the increase of the number of observations, the value of information increases sharply at the beginning and slowly later. These findings can be used to determine a proper number of monitoring points considering the trade-off between the value of information and the cost. By using the constructed Bayesian networks, real-time evaluation of slope safety based on multi-source monitoring data can be achieved. A representative output from this task is “Li, X.Y., Zhang, L.M., Zhang, S., 2018. Efficient Bayesian networks for slope safety evaluation with large quantity monitoring information. Geoscience Frontiers, 9(6): 1679-1687.” (2) Objective 2: Learning and identifying slope failure modes in a general Bayesian framework using monitoring information A general framework powered by the Bayesian approach is proposed in this task. The framework first updates the slope reliability and soil parameters using slope performance monitoring information with a novel physically-based method which combines Bayesian networks with slope stability models, followed by learning and identifying slope failure modes using the proposed Bayesian identification method. Slope performance monitoring information is first used to update slope reliability and soil parameters based on a proposed physically-based method which is able to consider both the spatial and cross correlations of soil properties. Then a Bayesian network relating slope reliability to spatially and cross correlated soil parameters is constructed for susceptibility assessment. The correlations among the grid cells and the prior probabilities of the Bayesian network are quantiﬁed utilizing Monte Carlo simulation and random ﬁeld theory. After that, observed slope performance information is used to update the slope reliability and the soil parameters. Two case studies were worked out to illustrate the application of the proposed method. It is found that the integration of performance information of certain cells signiﬁcantly improves the susceptibility evaluation of the adjacent cells and the updated soil properties are closer to the reality. By introducing the Bayesian network to physically-based slope reliability, this method is able to consider the inherent correlations in slope reliability analysis and update the reliability and soil parameters utilizing performance information, effectively improving the accuracy and capacity of slope reliability analysis. Moreover, as a slope can have many potential failure modes, a Bayesian identification method is proposed to identify the most likely failure modes using large-quantity monitoring information. First, a finite number of representative failure modes are selected based on a correlation analysis of all possible failure modes. Then, a random field coupled with Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation technique is applied to generate sufficient numerical samples for each representative failure mode. Subsequently, the deformation patterns associated with each representative failure mode are learnt from these numerical samples. Finally, the monitoring information is inputted into the model, and the most possible failure mode is identified based on the deformation patterns and the monitoring information. It is found that the percentage of correctly identifying the most possible failure mode increases if more pieces of monitoring information are inputted. The percentage of accurate identification of the most possible failure mode also serves as the basis to optimize the monitoring layout. In summary, the proposed methods are able to update slope reliability and soil parameters and learn slope failure mechanisms based on multi-source monitoring data. Representative outputs from this task: Li, X.Y., Zhang, L.M., Xiao, T., Zhang, S., Chen, C., 2019b. Learning failure modes of soil slopes using monitoring data. Probabilistic Engineering Mechanics, 56: 50-57. Wang, H.J., Xiao, T., Li, X.Y., Zhang, L.L., Zhang, L.M., 2019. A novel physically-based model for updating landslide susceptibility. Engineering Geology, 251: 71-80. (3) Demonstrating the proposed new methodologies through case studies A number of case studies have been worked out to demonstrate the proposed new methodologies, including a frictionless slope example with multiple sources of monitoring information at multiple points to validate the proposed efficient Bayesian network; an slope located in Western Lantau Island to validate the proposed slope reliability updating method, and a two-layer undrained soil slope to validate the proposed slope failure mode learning and identification method. Moreover, a detailed case study covering the multi-stage excavation of a high rock slope at the left abutment of Jinping I Hydropower Station using the proposed new methodologies are also implemented. This slope is located at the middle reach of the Yalong River in Southwest China. The slope is very high and steep with a maximum height up to 1700 m and a maximum excavation depth of 530 m. The angle of inclination of the slope varies from 50° to 90°. A three-dimensional finite difference model has been constructed in FLAC3D and used to simulate the performance of the slope. The proposed Bayesian methodologies were applied to combine the numerical analysis with the monitoring data, to evaluate the reliability of the high slope during staged excavation and the service period, and to evaluate the effectiveness of slope stabilisation measures. The monitoring data collected at multiple points were also used to update the parameter distributions and slope reliability. Results from the proposed methods agree well with the reality, showing the feasibility of the proposed methods. In addition, as many high engineered slopes are stabilized using anchors, which may corrode over time, a resilience model is developed for slope maintenance decision by analysing the degradation of an anchor-stabilized slope due to corrosion and evaluating the recovery of slope performance after maintenance. A case study of an anchored rock slope with four rows of rock bolts is used to illustrate the proposed method. Through these case studies, the effectiveness and reliabilities of the proposed methodologies have been validated. Representative works from this task include: Li, X.Y., Fan, Z.B., Lu, T., Xiao, T., Zhang, L.M., 2018. A resilience model for engineered slopes subject to anchor corrosion. 16202716.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202716.value: (1) An efficient Bayesian network has developed to evaluate the slope safety using large-quantity field monitoring information with underlying physical mechanisms. Based on the proposed Bayesian networks, real-time evaluation of slope safety can be accomplished based on multi-source monitoring data (Li et al. 2018). (2) A novel physically-based method which combines Bayesian networks and a slope stability model is proposed to update landslide susceptibility considering both spatial and cross correlations of soil parameters and illustrated with an example in Western Lantau Island (Wang et al. 2019). An integrated Bayesian method is developed to learn slope failure modes from the deformation monitoring information, which can be used to investigate the value of observation information, optimal monitoring layout and role of prior information in failure mode identification (Li et al. 2019). (3) A resilience model is proposed for slope maintenance decision by analyzing the degradation of an anchor-stabilized slope due to corrosion and evaluating the recovery of slope performance is developed considering spatial soil variability (Li et al. 2017). (4) Site characterization, which is essential for slope reliability studies, is subject to spatial variability of soil properties which are normally simulated by random fields. A genetic method which generates multivariate cross-correlated random fields has been proposed (Zhu et al. 2017), and a three-level probabilistic framework is proposed for stratification modeling considering stratigraphic uncertainties (Xiao et al. 2017). To further consider the interlayer and intralayer variabilities of geological profiles, an integrated random field model is proposed to characterize the two kinds of variabilities simultaneously (Li et al. 2018). Moreover, based on results of cone penetration tests, a probabilistic approach is proposed to characterize three-dimensional spatial variability using maximum likelihood estimation (Xiao et al. 2018). A stepwise covariance matrix decomposition method has been developed to enhance the efficiency of generating multivariate, large-scale and high-resolution three-dimensional random fields.

16202716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202716.value: The subject of multi-source data fusion evolves rapidly. Beside the Bayesian methods studied in this project, machine learning and deep learning techniques have drawn considerable attention recently in geotechnical and slope safety studies. Supported with latest data science techniques, a comprehensive dynamic safety evaluation system for engineered slopes can be developed. The proposed course of actions is summarized as follows: (1) Data collection and fusion: Three kinds of historical data need to be collected; namely, meteorological data, site-specific slope monitoring data and historical slope failure and maintenance records. (2) Model design, training and evaluation: Machine learning and deep learning models will be designed and trained with both cumulative and time-series historical data for learning the underlying evolution pattern of slope performance. Detailed evaluation will be then conducted using selected powerful models. (3) Slope performance prediction: The selected models will be used for (a) dynamic slope performance updating with real-time meteorological and monitoring data and (b) predicting the future slope performance. (4) Slope maintenance and early warning: The updated and predicted slope performance can then serve as the basis for slope maintenance or slope failure early warning.

16202716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202716.value: Slope safety is a significant issue in Hong Kong due to its steep terrain and subtropical weather conditions. Important slopes are often closely monitored to prevent unexpected slope performance degradation or failure. How to timely evaluate the safety of a slope using multi-source monitoring information is a fundament question. This research project bridges the gap between the monitoring data and slope performance in an innovative way. A computer science technique called Bayesian network, along with other data-driven methods, are used in this project to combine multi-source monitoring information, physical analysis and expert knowledge, and help answer two main questions: (a) how does the slope performance evolve given specific monitoring information? and (b) what are the underlying failure mechanisms behind the observed monitoring information? By answering these two questions and addressing many other related scientific issues, this research project advances the real-time evaluation of on-service slopes and provides the basis for understanding slope failures, determining slope maintenance schemes, as well as issuing early warnings for imminent slope failures.

16204316.value: 此項目主要通過先進的消聲風洞試驗和氣動聲學計算，為機翼前緣寬頻噪聲提供研究結果。此研究會在現有對前緣噪聲的預測和理解的基礎上有顯著的提高，它不僅研究渦扇發動機主要的噪聲機理，而且在研究風力機、螺旋槳和轉子噪聲方面都將發揮重要作用。此類噪聲源對社會環境和人體的健康，尤其是居住在機場、風電場和高速運輸線路等周圍的居民，造成嚴重的危害。在處理涉及現代運輸系統的環境問題中，解決噪音問題是其中非常重要的一部分。由於此問題所涉及的物體的周圍流場中存在湍流，因此噪音源一般都是由單頻和寬頻噪音組成的。儘管已經有大量的工作對噪音的產生和抑制進行研究，但是仍然存在一些缺陷和疏漏。此項目中的研究對於實現未來航空的降噪目標和減輕環境噪音問題將會是非常重要的一步。此項目提案中，明確了目前在前緣噪聲建模和測試過程中的缺陷和不足。這些問題主要是由於機翼在不同迎角測試和機翼上游方向的有關測試中精確度不夠導致的。針對前述的問題，此項目提出新型的試驗和計算方法來彌補現有前緣噪聲理解中的缺陷，並且為將來的研究和驗證提供有用的實驗數據支持。實驗測試將會在一個全新設計的消聲風洞中進行，聲學計算將會使用計算聲學求解器完成，此求解器已經被成功用於之前的相關研究中。需要強調的是此消聲風洞可以在實驗中可以實現大範圍的上游測試角度和各向異性湍流，這些問題對於研究非常重要，例如發動機的出口導向葉片的噪聲研究。新型的計算聲學理論包括網格質量的提高，聲學邊界以及熵波的研究。此項目主要依賴於研究團隊的專業知識以及過往在氣動聲學、飛機噪音、材料以及製造方面的研究與發展。

16204316.label: Realisation of objectives
16204316.value: The objectives of the project were well achieved, details are listed below: 1. Aeroacoustic experiments of isolated airfoils have been conducted in the anechoic wind tunnel UNITED. Different turbulence grids were fabricated and the turbulence statistics, boundary layer property, and noise patterns are measured. Hotwires were employed to A linear microphone array was manufactured to measure the sound directivity in a wind observer range. The beamforming methods were used to quantify the source distribution. 2. A generic synthetic turbulence method is proposed for the anisotropic turbulence with arbitrary energy spectra. High fidelity numerical simulations were conducted to study the effect of turbulence anisotropy on the leading edge noise. The impacts of integral length scales, turbulence intensity, mean flow distribution, and the turbulence distortion processes were investigated. 3. Systematic numerical simulations are conducted to study the airfoil-turbulence interaction noise in transonic flows. A better understanding of the physics of shock wave-turbulence interaction, airfoil-turbulence interaction, and noise scattering was obtained. The study was the first in this research region to investigate the leading edge noise in the transonic regime with shock waves. 4. Numerical simulations were conducted for the turbulence-cascade interaction. A sliding mesh method was developed and implemented to the numerical solver to account for the rotational motion of the turbulence and fan blades. The geometry of the cascade and the turbulence property were investigated. The blockage effect due to the solid surface on the sound produced by the cascade-turbulence interaction was investigated and the properties of the associated sound modes were analyzed. Besides, a fast semi-analytical model was proposed to study the turbulence-cascade interaction based on the boundary element method. 5. A generic non-reflective boundary condition method is implemented in the numerical solver to prevent the pseudo-reflection of both acoustic waves and turbulence. The study enables the efficient CAA simulation because the size of the computational domain could be reduced. Also, the guidance of high-quality grid generation was proposed for systematic investigations of the geometry impact.

16204316.value: The major output of the projects can be classified into the proposed numerical methods, a better understanding of the acoustic and flow physics, and the high-quality flow and noise database. The details are: 1. A generalized synthetic turbulence method is proposed based on the digital filter approach. A single filter is used to re-reproduce the statistics of anisotropic turbulence. Also, the parameters involved are Mach number (flow speed) independent and the singularity at the filter center is avoided. 2. The influence of the energy spectra, integral length scales of the anisotropic turbulence, and its distortion in the non-uniform mean flow were studied. A theoretical model was proposed to account for the influence of the streamwise fluctuation on the noise generation (which was omitted in the previous studies). The theoretical model explained why there is noise radiation in the upstream direction when the turbulence is presented in the non-uniform mean flow. A correction based on the theoretical model can improve the prediction accuracy of the classical Amiet’s flat plate model. 3. The physical processes of turbulence-airfoil interaction, turbulence-shock wave interaction, sound scattering by shocks, and the shock wave oscillation due to strong oncoming turbulence were identified for the transonic airfoils. The study enhanced our understanding of the leading noise in transonic flows. Also, the impacts of airfoil geometry such as the angle of attack, camber, and thickness were systematically investigated. 4. The aeroacoustics of turbulence-cascade interaction is well studied with parametric investigations. An efficient sliding mesh approach was proposed. The interpolation was simplified for mode stable numerical simulations. The blockage effect was firstly studied in the presence of the rotating fan blades. 5. The project study produced a series of flow and acoustic databases including the CAA simulations results, the far-field directivities measured using the linear microphone arrays, and the source distribution of the airfoil in the anechoic wind tunnel. The database could be employed for the further aeroacoustic study of the airfoil noise.

16204316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204316.value: A continuous study can be conducted to further improve our understanding of the turbulence interaction noise in aero-engines. Below are several points that can be conducted. 1. The synthetic turbulence method could be implemented in the computational fluid dynamics solvers as an advanced turbulence inlet method. 2. Cascade simulations with alternative inlet and outlet boundary conditions can be conducted to simulate the flow and acoustic processes in real engines. 3. Viscous flow simulations can be conducted for the airfoil-turbulence interaction in transonic flows. The interaction of oncoming turbulence, turbulent boundary layer, and shocks and the associated noise production will lead to a better understanding of the airfoil noise.

16204316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204316.value: This project studies the noise generated by the turbulence-airfoil interaction by both experiments and computer simulations. The turbulence means the chaotic flows that are common in real life. Our research is to mimic the scenario in engines that the turbulence is caused by the high-speed blades, which the airfoil is the static blades. The flow properties and noise signatures are studied. The effect of the flow speed, complex geometry, and motion are considered. The study can enhance our understanding of the associated physics with systematic investigations. Different numerical methods and theoretical models are developed, and they will be useful tools in the future’s study for the research topic.

16206416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206416.value: Control of disinfection by-products (DBPs) has been a long battle since the 1970s. More DBPs are being identified, their toxicity examined and control strategies implemented to ensure the provision of safe drinking water. Micropollutant abatement, which is becoming essential in public water supplies, however brings in a new challenge in DBP control. The micropollutants, such as pharmaceuticals and personal care products, pesticides, biocides, etc., are released into our water sources after their human health and veterinary applications. They show potential adverse health effects even at low concentrations but cannot be effectively removed by conventional water treatment technologies, thus demanding additional treatment. Degradation of the micropollutants by the UV/peroxide advanced oxidation process (AOP) has been verified as a viable abatement option in ample studies and trials and is already in engineering practice. Studies have also shown its additional benefit in achieving disinfection goals. However, while micropollutants are being degraded, dissolved organic matter (DOM), ubiquitously co-present in the water, is also subjected to the oxidation and may be altered. The treated water with altered DOM, in many countries, then has to be protected with chlorine or chloramines in distribution systems where DBPs are formed. However, little is known about the impacts of the additional oxidation treatment for micropollutant abatement on the alteration of DOMs and thus their chlorination/chloramination by-product formation potentials. Very few studies have addressed the changes of formation potentials of THMs and HAAs in the subsequent chlorination but the results were inconsistent and causes of the inconsistency essentially unknown. In this project, we intend to establish a few quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometry-based methods for DOM characterization and DBP investigation. These methods, together with other well-practiced techniques, will be used to investigate the changes of DOM’s characteristics and chlorination/chloramination by-product formation potentials as the result of its oxidation by the UV/peroxide AOP at hydroxyl radical exposure relevant to micropollutant abatement. We will also conduct umu genotoxicity screening tests on raw, oxidation treated samples and chlorinated samples to elucidate the changes of whole water toxicity due to the AOP treatment and the following chlorination/chloramination step. We will try to connect the changes of DBP formation potentials with the changes of DOM properties and/or that of the toxicity. Understanding of their interrelation will suggest strategies to balance our health risk from exposure to micropollutants and that to DBPs to safeguard potable water in engineering practice. 自上世紀七十年代起，水體消毒副產物的控制一直是為確保飲用水安全性的持久戰。消毒副產物的鑑定，毒性評價以及控制策略的實施都在不斷的推進。另一方面，水體微污染物的去除也正逐漸成為公共供水系統所必須考慮的問題。然而，微污染物的去除卻為消毒副產物的控制帶來了新的挑戰。微污染物包括藥物與個人護理品，殺蟲劑，農藥等等。在個人護理和牲畜上的使用之後，未能完全降解的微污染物會被排放到水體中。微污染物在低濃度的情況下仍具有潛在的健康危害，而傳統的水處理技術卻不能有效的去除它們，因此需要強化處理技術。紫外光/過氧化氫高級氧化技術已被廣泛驗證為切實可行的微污染物處理技術，並已在工業中實踐。研究還顯示此技術在去除微污染物時還能同時達到消毒目的。然而，水體中不可避免的存在著溶解有機物，在去除微污染物的過程中，溶解有機物同樣的經過了氧化過程而可能造成其特性的改變。為確保水質安全，在許多國家中，這含有被改變溶解有機物的處理過的水在供水系統中又接觸到餘氯或餘氯胺，從而產生消毒副產物。目前，人們對於以去除微污染物為目的的氧化技術過程中對溶解有機物特性的改變及氯化/氯胺化消毒副產物生成潛勢的改變所知甚少。少量研究對在後續氯化消毒中的三鹵甲烷和鹵代乙酸生成潛勢的改變進行了闡述，但研究結果卻相互不一致，造成此不一致性的原因也近乎未知。本項目中，我們擬建立一些新的基於四級桿-飛行時間質譜的方法，來進行溶解有機物的表徵和消毒副產物的鑑定。這些方法將會與其他常規的技術一起用來研究溶解有機物特性及氯（胺）化消毒副產物生成潛勢在以去除微污染物為目的的羥基自由基暴露強度下，被紫外光/過氧化氫高級氧化技術所氧化產生的改變。我們也將對原水，氧化處理後的水及氯（胺）化處理後的水進行umu基因毒性檢測，以闡述高級氧化技術和後續氯化/氯胺化處理對水樣整體毒性的改變。我們擬將建立消毒副產物生成潛勢的改變、溶解有機物特性的改變、毒性的改變三者間的相關聯性。理解它們三者間的相互關聯性將可以提供水處理技術策略以兼顧人體暴露於微污染物及消毒副產物的健康風險，從而保障飲用水的安全。

16206416.label: Realisation of objectives
16206416.value: Objective 1 of this project was completed. The first method for DOM characterization by the full scan mode of Q-TOF-MS was established. We optimized six operating parameters of Q-TOF-MS by Response Surface Methodology, which improved the intensity of the full scan spectra of Suwannee River natural organic matter (SRNOM) by one order of magnitude. Then, size exclusion chromatography (SEC) was added before the Q-TOF-MS to obtain the molecular weight distribution of DOM. This SEC-Q-TOF-MS method enabled the separation of DOM full scan chromatogram into four fractions, and the weighted average molecular weight (MW) of each fraction were obtained. The results formulated one conference presentation. A method for DBP analysis using Q-TOF-MS/MS was established and enabled the detection of the structures of highly abundant DBPs (e.g., C3H3O3Cl3, m/z 190.907; C5H3O4Cl3, m/z 230.901; C5HO3Cl, m/z 212.892; C6H3O5Cl3, m/z 258.897) in 3-day chlorinated SRNOM. Additionally, the MS/MS method was established to identify DBPs generated from 3-day chlorination of model compounds, including 1,2,4,5-benzenetetracarboxylic acid (1,2,4,5-BTetraCA) and 2,6-dihydroxybenzoic acid (2,6-DHBA). However, the resolution of the Q-TOF-MS (mass accuracy of ~ 10 ppm error) was found not high enough to provide accurate masses for the thousands of ions detected in SRNOM. Also, the Q-TOF-MS was completely broken and could not be fixed. To overcome the two problems encountered, FT-ICR-MS of ultrahigh-resolution (mass accuracy of < 1 ppm error) was used thereafter. A new software, HaloFormula, was developed to assign chemical formulas for the FT-ICR-MS mass spectra of DOM. By using this new formula assignment tool, in combination with FT-ICR-MS analysis, accurate masses of over 8,000 ions were detected in SRNOM by FT-ICR-MS and 2179 CHO formulas were assigned to the ions by HaloFormula. Compared to an open-access software, Formularity, HaloFormula showed 16% higher formula assignment ratio. Another function was developed in HaloFormula to automatically calculate molecular indices including O/C, H/C, MW, modified aromaticity index (AImod), double bond equivalent (DBE), DBE/C, Kendrick mass defect (KMD) of CH2 (KMD(CH2), KMD (COO) and KMD (O). Modified data interpretation methods, such as MW vs. KMD (O) plot, were established to capture the changes of MW distribution and the loss or addition of functional groups in DOM due to treatment by advanced oxidation processes (AOPs). A method to characterize DBPs using FT-ICR-MS and HaloFormula was also established. Compared to Formularity, HaloFormula showed 33% higher formula assignment ratio. The DBPs were categorized into clusters of similar elemental compositions that differ only by the number of CH2, COO, and O using KMD (CH2), KMD (COO), KMD (O), respectively. These methods aforementioned were applied to reveal the influence of the UV/peroxide AOP on DOM’s characteristics and the corresponding changes of DBP formation in Objectives 2 and 3. Objective 2 was completed. The changes in DOM, DBP formation, and toxicity due to the UV/peroxide AOP were examined and the correlations between the elemental composition of DOM and DBP formation were built. Tests were conducted with two DOM isolates. For SRNOM, 156 of the 2179 CHO formulas assigned in the untreated SRNOM were removed after the AOP, while 629 new formulas with relatively higher O/C ratios were observed. The higher O/C ratios of the newly formed formulas after the AOP indicated an increased degree of oxidation of SRNOM, likely due to HO• attack of aromatic compounds in DOM. The weighted mean values of AImod of the removed formulas and newly formed formulas were 0.43 and 0.25, respectively, suggesting a shift from more toward less aromatic formulas due to the AOP. The genotoxicity after 3-day chlorination of the AOP-treated SRNOM was 22% higher than that of untreated SRNOM, which can be explained by the changes of the DBP formation caused by the AOP. The total absolute intensity of organic chlorine detected by FT-ICR-MS increased by 19.3% in the AOP-treated sample, suggesting that the activation of SRNOM by the AOP made it more susceptible to chlorine attack. The newly formed DBPs were less aromatic than the DBPs detected in the untreated sample, which is well correlated with the decreased aromaticity of AOP-treated SRNOM. An investigation with two model compounds using the MS/MS method further confirmed the hydroxylation and ring cleavage of DOM by HO• attack during the AOP. Tests were also conducted with the spikes of common water constituents, including HCO3–, HNO3–, SO42–, Cl– and Br–. The changes in the bulk properties of DOM versus the changes of molecular indices of DOM obtained from FT-ICR-MS analysis were correlated. The fluorescence intensity of SRNOM decreased by 36% after the AOP due to the destruction of aromatic compounds, which was consistent with the decreased AImod of the CHO formulas in AOP-treated SRNOM. The correlations between DBPs and the elemental composition of their precursors in DOM were also disclosed. The van Krevelen diagram, which displays the H/C ratio vs. O/C ratio of each formula, was divided into three zones based on the possibility of the formulas located in each zone to match with their corresponding DBPs. The results formulated one journal paper and two conference presentations. Objective 3 was completed. A novel method using monochloramine (NH2Cl) labeled with 14N and 15N at 1:1 molar ratio (14:15 = 1:1N), FT-ICR-MS, and HaloFormula was established to assign formulas and track the origin of nitrogen of nitrogenous DBPs (N-DBPs). Compared to the traditional method of using 15N-labeled NH2Cl, the new approach of using 14:15 = 1:1N labeled NH2Cl can assign the formulas and track the nitrogen origin of N-DBPs with higher accuracy and less workload. Chloramination of 7 model compounds by 14:15 = 1:1N labeled NH2Cl was conducted to evaluate the performance of this method. A total of 133 formulas were assigned using FT-ICR-MS and 53 of them were proposed to be N-DBPs with nitrogen origin tracked. The results formulated one journal paper under preparation and one conference presentation. Tests were conducted to investigate the changes of toxicity and the formation of chloramination by-products from DOM after the UV/peroxide AOP. The genotoxicity after 3-day chloramination of the AOP-treated SRNOM was 17% higher than that of untreated SRNOM. The total numbers of DBPs increased after AOP treatment. More N-DBPs with inorganic nitrogen incorporation (14:15 = 1:1N) were detected with additional AOP treatment, indicated that the activation of SRNOM by the AOP made it more susceptible to chloramine attack. The correlations between DBPs generated during chloramination and the elemental composition of their precursors in DOM were disclosed. The precursor zone of chloramination was located in an oval region having a center point at (O/C = 0.66, H/C = 1) in the van Krevelen diagram, which largely overlapped with that of chlorination. However, only 74% of the formulas in the precursor zone matched with their corresponding DBPs, likely due to the lower reactivity of NH2Cl than chlorine with organic moieties in DOM. Precursors of N-DBPs with the incorporation of 14:15 = 1:1N were also found. For example, C13H11O8N was detected in the sample after 3-day chloramination of AOP-treated SRNOM and was found to be the precursor of C13H9O8Cl2N through electrophilic substitution. The results formulated one journal paper under preparation.

16206416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206416.value: The major findings formulated 2 published journal papers (#1–2), 4 conference presentations (#1–4), and 2 journal papers under preparation (Journal publication #3–4). Major findings are: A Q-TOF-MS method was established and optimized to obtain the chemical formulas of the compounds in DOM. An SEC-Q-TOF-MS method was established to obtain the molecular weight distribution of DOM (Conference presentation #1). For DBP analysis, a MS/MS method was established and enabled the detection of the structures of selected individual DBPs. Novel methods were established using ultrahigh-resolution FT-ICR-MS in combination with a newly developed formula assignment software, HaloFormula, to assign chemical formulas for DOM and DBPs. These methods empowered the identification of the influence of AOPs on DOM’s characteristics and DBP formation at the molecular level (Journal paper #2). The AOP-treated DOM exhibited increased oxygen content and decreased aromaticity, which can be attributed to the HO• attack during the UV/peroxide AOP. The hydroxylated moieties in DOM were more reactive toward chlorine, which led to an increase in TOCl and the total intensity of organic chlorine detected. Besides, the decreased aromaticity of DOM was well correlated with the decreased AImod of DBPs after 3-day chlorination of the AOP-treated DOM. The hydroxylation and ring cleavage of DOM by HO• attack were reconfirmed to be the main alterations of DOM during the AOP. The alterations in the model compounds ultimately affected the DBP formation during subsequent chlorination (Journal paper #2 and conference presentation #2). Links between unknown DBPs and their corresponding precursors in DOM were visualized. Three zones in the van Krevelen diagram were identified based on the possibility of the CHO formulas located in each zone to link to their corresponding DBPs (Journal paper #1 and conference presentation #4). A method was developed to identify and track the nitrogen origins of N-DBPs using 14:15 = 1:1N-labeling of NH2Cl, FT-ICR-MS and HaloFormula. The number of detectable isotope peaks in N-DBPs increased significantly, and the accuracy of formula assignment and nitrogen origin tracking were enhanced. After 3-d chloramination of 7 model compounds, 53 N-DBPs were captured and the origin of the nitrogen atoms in the N-DBPs was identified (Journal paper #3 and conference presentation #3). The total number of N-DBPs detected by FT-ICR-MS after 3-day chloramination of SRNOM increased after the UV/peroxide AOP prior to the chloramination (Journal paper #4).

16206416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206416.value: In this project, we observed and tracking the nitrogen origin of the formation of N-DBPs from chloramination of SRNOM and AOP-treated SRNOM. However, the pathways of the formation of N-DBPs from DOM remained unknown. Besides, only a few N-DBPs were detected and the elemental composition of the N-DBP precursors in SRNOM was not identified. Thus, to better understand the mechanisms of N-DBP formation and characterize their precursors, N-rich DOM, such as effluent organic matter and algal-derived organic matter, should be evaluated and the formation pathways of N-DBPs from organic moieties in DOM should be disclosed. This formulated another RGC/GRF proposal entitled “FT-ICR-MS investigation of nitrogenous disinfection byproducts and tracking their precursors in nitrogen-rich organic matter upon chloramination and UV/chloramine processes”, which was submitted in 2020. The cutting-edge techniques to characterize the changes of DOM and formation of DBPs at the molecular level developed in this study can be applied to illustrate how other treatment processes alter the elemental composition of DOM, and how the alterations in DOM affect the subsequent DBP formation. We will seek for funding opportunities to expand the use of these techniques to other AOPs and examining the major unknown DBP precursors in different fractions of DOM.

16206416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206416.value: Control of disinfection by-products (DBPs) is one priority in providing safe potable water. The increasing need for micropollutant abatement by advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) in potable water supply brings in new challenges to DBP control. In this study, we proposed new analytical methods to connect the changes of DBP formation with the changes of DOM properties due to the AOP to evaluate and select AOPs for controlling DBPs and micropollutants. In this project, we established novel methods, based on two mass spectrometers and our newly developed data processing software, to disclose DOM’s characteristics at the molecular level and identify emerging DBPs. We systematically examined the influence of the UV/peroxide AOP on the elemental composition and structural properties of DOM. We disclosed how the UV/peroxide AOP interacted with the DBP precursors in DOM and consequently affected the DBP formation and toxicity during subsequent chlorination and chloramination. We built connections between DBPs and their precursors in DOM and identified the elemental composition of major DBP precursors in DOM. This project greatly advanced our fundamental knowledge and provided promising approaches to evaluate AOPs and guide the selection of proper AOPs with due consideration for micropollutant abatement and DBP control in real-world engineering practices.

16206516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206516.value: The South China Sea (SCS) is a large marginal sea in the western Pacific Ocean and its ocean circulation shapes the regional ocean hydrodynamics, ecosystem and climate variability. The SCS circulation is mainly driven by seasonal monsoonal winds, but also greatly regulated by the control of inflow/outflow from adjacent seas through the straits around the SCS. Previous studies have been focusing on the wind-driven circulation in the upper ocean. The lateral forcing arising from the time-dependent, three-dimensional inflow/outflow plays a critical role in the spatiotemporal variability and maintenance of the three-dimensional SCS circulation, but has not been adequately investigated. As a result, the holistic dynamic process of the SCS circulation remains largely unclear. This study will use numerical ocean modeling to simulate and investigate the role of inflow/outflow in the SCS basin circulation through dynamic investigation and analysis of the physical processes invoked in the inflow/outflow. We will investigate the characteristics of inflow/outflow in response to extrinsic forcing from adjacent seas and to intrinsic forcing from SCS basin circulation. Subsequently we will study the role of the inflow/outflow on the development, adjustment and sustenance of the SCS circulation by examining their dynamic responses to topography, stratification and the associated Rossby and coastally trapped wave dynamics in the basin circulation. In order to obtain the three-dimensional SCS circulation structure, we will also investigate the process that governs the vertical transports of water mass, momentum and energy induced by the vertically variable inflow/outflow. These inflow/outflow-related dynamics are critical to the SCS circulation. By combining three-dimensional numerical modeling, geophysical fluid dynamics and observations, we will conduct physics-oriented numerical modeling studies with simplified but specific physical forcing to isolate the dominant dynamic processes and forcing mechanisms in the complex inflow/outflow-driven circulation in the SCS. The progressive understanding obtained from these physics-oriented studies will then be consolidated in a SCS realistic numerical modeling investigation to achieve the objective of this study. This study tackles the complex, but fundamental ocean circulation dynamics to bridge our knowledge gap of circulation processes and forcing mechanisms not only in the SCS, but also in the world’s oceans.

16206516.label: Realisation of objectives
16206516.value: The SCS circulation is greatly regulated by the control of inflow/outflow from adjacent seas through the straits around the South China Sea (SCS). Unlike previous studies that have been focusing on the wind-driven circulation in the upper ocean, this study investigated the effect of external forcing via the influx/outflux through the straits on the SCS circulation. Based on the objectives of the project, we first investigate the characteristics of the external forcing, i.e. inflow/outflow in Liu and Gan (2017). We found that the circulation of the SCS is largely determined by westward intrusions of the northwestern Pacific waters in the upper layer (0–750 m) and deep layer (>1500 m), and by an eastward extrusion in the intermediate layer (750–1500 m) through Luzon Strait (LS). We also conducted a process-oriented investigation of external forcing using an idealized the inflow-outflow-inflow structure mimic to the observed one in Cai and Gan (2019). The key objectives of this study are to investigate the dynamic effects of inflow/outflow on the three-dimensional SCS basin circulation and to develop a process-oriented numerical ocean model to achieve the objectives. For these objectives, we have conducted studies to (1) We developed a process-oriented numerical modeling study was conducted to investigate the formation and underlying forcing of an anticyclonic eddy train observed in the northern South China Sea. The simulation and analyses of the vorticity balance indicate that the eddy train’s negative vorticity originates from the beta effect of northward western boundary current and from the subsequent downstream vorticity advection in the jet. The jet separation is a necessary condition for the formation of the eddy train, and the enhanced stratification, increased summer wind stress, and associated negative wind stress curl are favorable conditions for the formation of the anticyclonic eddies (Cai and Gan, 2017); (2) We developed a 3D circulation mode in the SCS to investigate the water pathway and residence time in response to time-dependent, three-dimensional inflow-outflow-inflow in the Luzon Strait. We found that the upper intrusive waters flow cyclonically and have a residence time of ~3 years before they subduct into a deeper layer or exit the SCS through surrounding straits. The intrusive denser waters in the deep layer flow along the northern slope and reside for ~25 years in the northern basin (north of 13N), where a strong subduction occurs. A cyclonic circulation exists in the deep layer in the southern basin (south of 13N), where a subduction of intermediate waters occurs over its eastern side and a deep upwelling exists over its western side. The water in the deep southern basin has a residence time of~40 years. The upwelled deep waters and the subducted waters from the upper layer form the intermediate water, where waters circulate anti-cyclonically toward LS and have a longest residence time (~42 years). These findings are supported by the spatial variation in the observed potential density variance (Liu and Gan, 2017). (3) We conduct a process-oriented numerical study to investigate the underlying coupled external (inflow/outflow)‐internal dynamics in forming and sustaining the acyclonic‐anticyclonic‐cyclonic (CAC) circulation in the upper‐middle‐lower layer in the South China Sea. We found that external sandwich‐like inflow‐outflow‐inflow in the water column through the Luzon Strait forms a three‐dimensional CAC slope current over the curving slope topography in the SCS basin, in which the downward/upward transport associated with the cross‐slope motion is established. The along‐slope current over the basin provides vorticity through the beta effect and accounts for the most external planetary vorticity input through the strait in the upper layer of the SCS, while the vorticity induced by the vertical transport is the major response to the external vorticity flux in the middle and lower layers. We illustrate the critical role of the vertical transport in linking the vorticity among the different layers for the development and sustenance of the CAC circulation. (Cai and Gan, 2019). (4) Since the cyclonic‐anticyclonic‐cyclonic (CAC) circulation of South China Sea (SCS) is mainly driven by the extrinsic lateral vorticity flux due to inflow‐outflow‐inflow through the Luzon Strait (LS) and the associated intrinsic vertical exchange (VE) in the basin, we developed a 3D circulation model to investigate the contribution of spatiotemporal structure of the VE through vortex stretching and squeezing to CAC circulation. We found that during summer, the vorticity flux induced by net upward VEs crossing the upper (750 m) and lower (1,500 m) interfaces of CAC circulation is equivalent to ~40% of the lateral vorticity flux for strengthening the anticyclonic and cyclonic circulation in the middle and deep layers, respectively. During winter, the net downward VE crossing the upper interface squeezes the middle layer and strengthens its anticyclonic circulation, while the net VE crossing the lower interface is too small to affect the circulation. The VE and its seasonality in the basin are largely governed by the cross‐isobath geostrophic transport (CGTb) due to interaction between along‐isobath circular currents and rugged slope topography. Our study revealed how important VE between the layers is to the CAC circulation itself, and our work advanced the understanding of the intrinsic‐extrinsic dynamic coupling that forms, develops, and sustains the CAC circulation in the SCS (Cai and Gan 2020). (5) The inflow and outflow through the Luzon Strait control the SCS circulation. Yet, these inflow/outflow are also greatly by 3-D ocean circulation system in the western Pacific Ocean. Based on a physics-oriented modeling study, we investigate the underlying forcing processes of the North Equatorial Undercurrent (NEUC), which is an important component of the circulation system in the western Pacific ocean and greatly affects the outflow in the mid-depth of Luzon Strait. Made up of large-scale (~90%) and mesoscale (~10%) components, the NEUC weakens eastward with a longitude-independent seasonality. Spatially, the NEUC has a northern (NEUC_N) and a southern branch (NEUC_S), which are mainly attributed to the transports from Luzon Undercurrent (LUC) and Mindanao Undercurrent (MUC), respectively. The LUC of ~3 Sv feeds the NEUC_N in summer, while the MUC of ~4 Sv fuels the NEUC_S in autumn and the two branches do not coexist. The total NEUC transport peaks in August/September, and there exist three distinct periods in a 1-yr cycle: the non-NEUC period in winter, the LUC-driven period in summer, and the MUC-driven period in autumn (Li and Gan, 2020). (6) Based on our studies, we provide a novel new understanding of the ocean circulation in the SCS and its relation with the forcing of inflow/outflow from the Luzon Strait. As a result of research by this project, we have developed a new physical concept for the SCS layered circulation based on Stoke Theorem and based on a novel layer integrated vorticity equation (LIVE) dynamics. These new insights on the ocean circulation and its dynamics connection with the internal-external forcing have been summarized recently by Cai, Gan et al. (2020).

16206516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206516.value: The ocean flow field in the South China Sea (SCS) has a 3D structure. Besides the wind forcing, the flow field in the SCS is regulated by the external inflow/outflow through the straits around the SCS. This study investigates the effect of the external forcing on the 3D flow field in the SCS. We identify that there is a inflow-outflow-inflow in the Luzon Strait, which is the major driver to form the anticlockwise-clockwise-anticlockwise rotating circulation in the upper (<750m)-middle(750-1500m)-deep layer (>1500m) of the SCS. The research of this project also provides a novel theoretical explanation to the above findings.
