16207316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207316.value: 許多現實世界中的機器學習應用，均需要學習輸入與輸出序列之間的關聯。其中一些應用在輸入和輸出均涉及時空序列，被稱為時空序列學習，這課題正是本項目的研究焦點。時空序列學習的應用在現實世界中普遍存在，例子包括氣象預報、可視對象的跟蹤、人群分析，和許多其他視頻處理的應用。 儘管時空序列學習的應用相當普遍，對這課題的研究卻往往在不同的研究界別中獨立地進行。在深度學習最新研究進展的啟發下，我們提出了ConvLSTM模型來解決一些時空序列學習的問題。在這初步研究的基礎上，我們於此項目將把ConvLSTM推廣為更具普遍性的學習框架，並以此框架提出一個具體的時空序列學習模型。為以實驗證明該模型可被用於不同的應用中，我們將利用香港天文台提供的氣象數據來研究降雨量臨近預報及利用無人飛行器收集的視頻數據來研究可視對象的跟蹤。通過使用一個共同的學習框架，我們的目標是要顯著地提高這兩個具挑戰性的應用的準確性。

16207316.label: Realisation of objectives
16207316.value: The objectives of this project include devising a general formulation of spatiotemporal sequence-to-sequence learning (objective 1) and using it as a common framework to design models for two quite different spatiotemporal sequence-to-sequence learning applications, namely, weather radar map nowcasting and visual object tracking (objectives 2 and 3). During the project period, we have successfully achieved all three project objectives leading to seven publications (one book chapter under review and six published conference papers) in highly visible venues, particularly the top conferences in artificial intelligence and machine learning. We first consider spatiotemporal problems in which the spatial domain is defined as a regular grid structure. Examples of such spatiotemporal data are the video data in the visual object tracking and crowd counting applications and the weather radar maps in the precipitation nowcasting application that we studied. We then study more general spatiotemporal problems in which the spatial domain is no longer a regular grid but can only be modeled as a general graph structure such as the traffic data in the traffic speed forecasting application studied. Such generalization allows the model to deal with graph-based operators with learnable attention scope. Our formulation is quite general as these two types of spatiotemporal sequence-to-sequence learning problems essentially cover most if not all of the problems encountered in real applications. By extending the Convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) model which was developed in our previous work (NIPS 2015 paper), we overcome the location-invariant limitation of ConvLSTM by proposing the novel Trajectory GRU (TrajGRU) model which can actively learn location-variant structures for the recurrent connections. This significantly extends the flexibility of the model for spatiotemporal modeling which, among other things, can go beyond simple translation to handle more general operations such as rotation and scaling. We have also tried to incorporate ideas from the Bayesian approach into deep learning models to improve their robustness in situations when training data is sparse. Among all the specific spatiotemporal modeling applications studied, we are particularly proud of the work on precipitation nowcasting because the work is not just highly visible in the academic community but has also aroused a lot of interest from the practitioners. In particular, the Hong Kong Observatory is now adopting our TrajGRU model in their precipitation nowcasting system for production use as it gives significantly more accurate prediction that the optical flow methods they have been used by them for a long time.

16207316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207316.value: Two PhD students and one MPhil student were involved in different parts of this project. The research findings have led to the publication of 2 papers in AAAI, 1 paper in ICCV, 1 paper in IJCAI, 1 paper in NIPS, and 1 paper in UAI. These top conferences are among the best in artificial intelligence, computer vision, and machine learning. In addition, due to our highly visible papers in NIPS 2015 and NIPS 2017 (receiving more than 1,900 Google Scholar citations in just a few years) which proposed the ConvLSTM and TrajGRU models for spatiotemporal sequence-to-sequence learning problems, we were invited to contribute a chapter to a book titled “Deep Learning meets Earth Science: From Hybrid Modeling to Explainability” to be published in 2020. The book chapter is currently under review. Although our proposed common framework was studied by us for only two specific applications, a number of follow-up attempts by others have applied our models to a much wider range of tasks well beyond our original expectation. Among other things, our models have been reimplemented by some other researchers and made available on most of the popular deep learning frameworks, facilitating further research to be pursued by a growing community.

16207316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207316.value: Although we have studied a more general form of spatiotemporal models in which the spatial domain is represented as a graph, so far we assume that the structure of the graph remains fixed. A further research direction that is worth pursuing is to consider dynamic graph structures in the temporal dimension. Nevertheless, this generalization is expected to incur higher computational complexity. To ensure that the problem remains manageable, a feasible approach would be to allow only a set of primitive operations to be performed on the graph. However, combining these primitive operations can still lead to a wide variety of possible changes to the graph. We may turn this further investigation into a new research proposal, probably involving one or two important applications that require the graph structure of the spatial domain to be represented dynamically.

16207316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207316.value: Many real-world applications require associating sequences that are spatiotemporal in nature. On one hand, we proposed in this project a common framework for modeling such problems. On the other hand, we proposed specific models for two real-world applications, namely, weather forecasting and visual object tracking. For the weather forecasting problem, we extended a model called convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) that we proposed before to a new model that only makes less restrictive assumptions on the data. Our models for precipitation nowcasting outperform the models used by the Hong Kong Observatory, leading them to adopt our models to improve their system. Our research has also been followed up by many other researchers both to extend our models and to extend their applications.

16207916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207916.value: As an important ingredient in agricultural and industrial fields, phosphorus (P) has been overused for decades. Excessive P inevitably enters into surface waters mainly as phosphate through agricultural runoffs and sewage discharges. The enrichment of phosphate in water bodies causes eutrophication. Stringent regulations have been launched worldwide striving to lower the P level below 0.02 mg-P/L in natural water and 0.5 mg-P/L in sewage effluent. More importantly, phosphorus is a non-renewable resource and the remaining accessible reserves of phosphate rock will run out in 50 years if the growth in demand for phosphorus fertilizer continues. Hence, a novel technology that can remove and recover phosphate from water media will be desirable. Of the developed technologies such as chemical precipitation, biological process and sorption, sorption is the most favorable option because of its low cost, ease of operation and simplicity of design. However, a sorption process in water and wastewater treatment systems for phosphate removal and recovery has yet to be successfully implemented due to several major obstacles: (i) non-selectivity and low sorption capacity; (ii) poor reusability of sorbents due to poor desorption; and (iii) difficulty of sorbent separation after treatment. Hence, we propose to invent novel magnetic sorbents in a modified sorption process for phosphate removal and recovery with characteristics of (i) strong selectivity and high sorption capacity, (ii) easy regeneration for reuse, and (iii) easy separation by magnetic field, through surface coating/imprinting metal oxides (i.e. La2O3 and ZrO2) and ion-imprinted polymers (IIPs) over the monodispersed magnetic Fe3O4@SiO2 nanoparticles. After screening of the synthesized magnetic sorbents based on their performance in terms of sorption capacity and selectivity to phosphate, the particle size of the screened sorbents will be tuned for optimum sorption capacity and magnetic separation. Various instruments (e.g., SEM, TEM, XRD and VSM) will be applied for magnetic sorbents characterization. Batch experiments will be conducted to investigate the removal and recovery of phosphate by the magnetic sorbents, while phosphate removal mechanisms will also be examined. A prototype flow-through reactor will be adopted to further evaluate the phosphate recovery from natural water and treated sewage effluent using the screened magnetic sorbents by performing a series of sorption/desorption cycles. The results from this study will be expected to advance the selective removal and efficient recovery of phosphate in water and wastewater treatment. 磷 (P) 作為一種重要的成分，在工農業領域長期過量使用。 這不可避免地造成了過量的P通過污水排放和地表徑流等途徑以磷酸鹽的形式進入地表水，從而造成水體富營養化。 近年來，全球各個國家對磷酸鹽排放的標準愈發趨嚴，提出天然水體和污水中的P的濃度分別控制在0.02 mg-P/L和0.5 mg-P/L以下。 更重要地，P作為一種不可再生資源，其主要來源的磷礦石也將會在未來50年內開採耗盡，這對日益劇增的P需求是一個挑戰。 因此，研製一種新型的磷酸鹽去除回收技術已成為當前極需解決的問題。 由於其特有的價格低廉、操作簡便以及裝置簡易等優點，吸附是當前各類磷酸鹽回收技術中最為受到歡迎的一種技術。 但限制于吸附材料選擇性和吸附性能較差、解吸效率低、以及吸附材料分離困難等缺點的制約，吸附技術還無法在實際磷酸鹽回收的水處理技術中得到應用。 針對以上問題，本研究擬通過將金屬氧化物(La2O3和ZrO2)和高分子離子印記(IIPs) 負載在單分散性的磁性納米顆粒，並對材料進行系統表徵(例如SEM, TEM, XRD 和 VSM)；利用批量實驗等對合成的吸附劑材料吸附性、選擇性和磁分離性能進行評估和篩選 ；通過各類固液相表徵技術深入探討吸附劑去除回收磷酸鹽的機理；最後，基於研發的磁分離水處理原型裝置，類比合成的吸附劑從各類實際的水體中回收磷酸的性能，並評估合成的吸附劑電磁分離性能及其長期使用穩定性。 本專案擬開發的具有(i)高效吸附能力和強選擇性，(ii)可再生，以及(iii)可磁分離等特點的新型磁性吸附劑的研究將為從天然水和污水中磷酸鹽回收提供技術支撐。

16207916.label: Realisation of objectives
16207916.value: The whole research study was extremely smooth. The four objectives were not only met but also went beyond the outcomes. Eutrophication of water bodies is a serious and widespread environmental problem. Achieving low levels of phosphate concentration to prevent eutrophication is one of the important goals of surface water management and wastewater engineering. Meeting the increasingly stringent standards is feasible in using a phosphate-selective sorption system. In this study, zirconium-, lanthanum-, cerium-, and iron-based sorbents with magnetic property using Fe3O4 or SiO2@Fe3O4 were developed for selective phosphate removal from water and wastewater. Two zirconium oxide-based sorbents (i.e. ZrO2@SiO2@Fe3O4 and ZrO2@Fe3O4) were developed and compared for phosphate removal. The direct coating of ZrO2 on Fe3O4 to form the core/shell ZrO2@Fe3O4 leaded to a significantly enhanced phosphate sorption kinetics and sorption capacity in comparison to ZrO2@SiO2@Fe3O4. The developed ZrO2@Fe3O4 sorbent showed a high selectivity towards phosphate in the presence of competitive anions, and a high phosphate recovery rate. To further design phosphate-selective sorbents with higher sorption capacity, La(OH)3/Fe3O4 nanocomposites with varied La-to-Fe mass ratios were synthesized through a precipitation and hydrothermal method. The optimized La(OH)3/Fe3O4 (4:1) nanocomposite had fast sorption kinetics, high sorption capacity, and strong selectivity for phosphate in presence of competing ions. Sorption-desorption cyclic experiments demonstrated the good reusability of the La(OH)3/Fe3O4 (4:1) nanocomposite. Mechanism studies indicated that both the ZrO2@Fe3O4 and La(OH)3/Fe3O4 (4:1) removed phosphate by forming the inner-sphere complexation through the ligand exchange process, i.e., hydroxyl groups on the surface of the Zr- and La-based sorbents were replaced by the phosphate. Therefore, increasing the amount of the surface hydroxyl groups of metal-based sorbents can greatly enhance the phosphate sorption performance. Consequently, a straightforward, effective method was proposed for increasing the amount of the surface hydroxyl groups of CeO2 particles. By simply reducing the volume of water used during the ethylene glycol-mediated solvothermal synthesis of CeO2 particles, the amount of surface hydroxyl groups was increased, and the phosphate sorption performance was greatly improved. The current study investigated the removal mechanisms of phosphate by three types of metal-based materials, i.e., Zr-, La-, and Ce-based sorbents. It is found that selective removal of phosphate over other competing anions from water and wastewater can be achieved based on their differences in acid-base properties, geometric shapes, and metal complexing abilities. Consequently, the mechanisms of selective phosphate sorption can be categorized as hydrogen bonding, shape complementarity, and inner-sphere complexation, and typical phosphate-selective sorbents are organic-functionalized materials, molecularly imprinted polymers, and metal-based materials, respectively. Of the above sorbents, metal-based materials are the most widely used phosphate-selective sorbents so far. Based on the concept of hard and soft (Lewis) acids and bases (HSAB), hard Lewis-acidic metals such as zirconium (Zr), lanthanum (La), and cerium (Ce) can preferentially bind to hard Lewis-basic phosphate by an orbital overlap that induces a bonding interaction. Therefore, Zr-, La, and Ce-based sorbents can be used to achieve selective phosphate removal from water and wastewater. The dominant mechanism of phosphate sorption by the Zr-, La-, and Ce-based sorbents is inner-sphere complexation through the ligand exchange process. In this process, hydroxyl groups on the surface of the Zr-, La, and Ce-based sorbents are replaced by a ligand like phosphate, and a covalent chemical bond is formed between the phosphate and the metal atom. Thus, the amount of surface hydroxyl groups plays a major role in determining the phosphate sorption capacity of the metal-based sorbents. Consequently, increasing the amount of the surface hydroxyl groups on metal-based sorbents (e.g., CeO2 particles) can greatly enhance the phosphate sorption performance. The performance of the Zr-, La, and Ce-based sorbents to remove phosphate from the local sewage treated effluent using batch system under a number of sorption/desorption treatment cycles was also conducted, and the findings show their sorption capacity with sustainable recyclability. It indicates the practicality of this technology. Also a new technology, using Fe0/Fe3O4 composites facilitated by Fe2+ for low concentration phosphate removal was developed. The amount of Fe3O4 on the Fe0 surface was tuned and Fe0/Fe3O4 was proved to have best performance in phosphate removal and iron corrosion. Adsorption, co-precipitation and precipitation contributed to phosphate removal, and the main removal mechanism was adsorption, which included electrostatic attraction and inner-sphere complexation. This study highlights a promising new method for the removal of low concentrations of phosphate from river water. Instead of conducting prototype study, a pilot-scale study was establaished. The great news is that the pilot-scale study of this technology using La-based sorbents with magnetic property and without magnetic property in suspension reactor and fix-bed reactor, respectively has been funded by Water Supply Department of HKSAR Government. We have operated the pilot-scale reactor for over 12 months. This indicates the significance of this research study which turns from scientific investigation in batch system to engineering application in pilot-scale system.

16207916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207916.value: 1. Two core/shell zirconium oxide-based sorbents (i.e. ZrO2@SiO2@Fe3O4 and ZrO2@Fe3O4) were developed and compared for phosphate removal. Our synthesizing method resulted in a uniform ZrO2-coating on SiO2@Fe3O4 or Fe3O4, while the SiO2 pre-coating leaded to a notable reducing in surface area from 135.8 to 17.1 m2/g and magnetization from 30.5 to 23.1 emu/g for ZrO2@SiO2@Fe3O4 compared to ZrO2@Fe3O4. Both sorbents exhibited a high selectivity towards phosphate even at a competitive anion (i.e. Cl-, NO3- and SO42-) to phosphate molar ratio of 100:1. Consistent evidences obtained from solid state analyses including zeta potential, FTIR, XPS and XANES, revealed that the sorption of phosphate by ZrO2@Fe3O4 was through the formation of Zr-O-P inner-sphere surface complexation. More importantly, XANES data further demonstrated that ZrO2 accounts for 91.1% of the overall phosphate sorption by ZrO2@Fe3O4. 2. La(OH)3/Fe3O4 (4:1) nanocomposites of various La-to-Fe mass ratios were developed through a facile precipitation and hydrothermal process for selective phosphate removal from wastewater. It exhibited fast equilibrium time of 30 minutes, high sorption capacity of 83.5 mg P/g, excellent selectivity for phosphate in the presence of competing ions, good reusability, and economic merits. Mechanistically, all experimental evidence indicated that phosphate sorption could be attributed to electrostatic attraction exerted by the positively charged surface of La(OH)3/Fe3O4 (4:1) nanocomposite and the inner-sphere complexation between La and P, via ligand exchange. 3. A straightforward, effective method for the in-situ engineering of surface functional groups of CeO2 particles was proposed through adjusting the volume of water in the ethylene glycol-mediated solvothermal synthesis. By increasing the surface functional groups, the phosphate sorption performance was significantly improved. The CeO2 particles have a high sorption capacity of up to 103.7 mg P/g, an ultrafast sorption equilibrium of less than 2 minutes, high selectivity towards phosphate under the presence of competing ions, and the ability to reach an effluent phosphate concentration of 0.01 mg P/L from real wastewater effluent. 4. A new approach using Fe0/Fe3O4 composites facilitated by Fe2+ for low concentration phosphate removal was developed. A dosage of 0.5 g/L Fe0/Fe3O4 facilitated by 0.5 mg/L Fe2+ could reduce the phosphate level from 0.4 to 0.014 mg-P/L in 60 min, with the total iron concentration below 0.3 mg/L after 75 min reaction. Further, phosphate could also be removed from real river water to a low level of 0.010 mg-P/L with the total iron concentration meeting the WHO drinking water standard after 80 min reaction, clearly demonstrating its potential application.

16207916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207916.value: Considering the increasingly stringent phosphorus standards for wastewater treatment and surface water management, there is an urgent need to develop phosphate-selective materials to achieve ultra-low phosphate levels. However, because of the high hydration energy of phosphate and abundance of competing anions, selective phosphate removal from water and wastewater is challenging. The current study developed four types of metal-based sorbents, i.e., Zr-, La-, Ce- and Fe0-based sorbents and investigated their removal mechanisms of phosphate. The ability to tune the amount of surface functional groups is of paramount importance in designing an effective sorbent for the decontamination of water and wastewater. The four sorbents show high sorption capability of phosphate and La-based sorbents with magnetic property can be recycled and reused efficiently. From this study, it is found that selective removal of phosphate over other competing anions from water and wastewater can be achieved based on their differences in acid-base properties, geometric shapes, and metal complexing abilities. According to solid state analyses including zeta potential, FTIR, XPS and XANES, it revealed that the sorption of phosphate by these sorbents was mainly through electrostatic attraction and the formation of Zr-O-P inner-sphere surface complexation. This sorption technology with phosphate-selective materials has a great potential to be applied for wastewater and river water treatment to remove ultra-low phosphate levels.

16209316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209316.value: The accumulation of plaques of insoluble proteins (amyloid beta) in the brain is a pathological marker and is likely to be a cause of dementia in patients with Alzheimer’s disease. These plaques are deposits of excessive quantities of incorrectly folded proteins. Similarly, the incorrect folding of a specific protein that is known to suppress tumors (p53) is a major cause of cancer in half of all cases (including the majority of cases of lung cancer). These are just some of the-well-known examples of protein folding gone wrong. Thus, understanding the mechanism of protein folding is no longer a pure theoretical quest to bridge the gap between the genetic blueprint of a protein and its biological function. It has become the focus of attention in pharmaceutical research because new treatments for such debilitating diseases may lie in the pathways of protein folding. The folding of proteins into a functional conformation is an extremely complex process, and its full description exceeds the capacity of a single experimental technique. Two techniques that have recently been applied successfully to this issue are pursued here: ultrafast laminar-flow micromixers and differential scanning calorimetry microsystems. In the former, proteins are put in a state of nonequilibrium with a rapid change in their surrounding medium by hydrodynamic focusing in which a stream of the protein under study is confined to a thin jet by the outer streams of a chosen medium. This significantly reduces the length scales over which diffusive mixing must occur. Such rapid mixing, when coupled with a detection system, reveals the early events of protein folding at a sub-microsecond time resolution by consuming an extremely small sample volume. However, the reliance upon hydrodynamic sheath flows to form the jet raises the issue of premature mixing, thus confounding the accurate determination of the time resolution. The latter technique, calorimetry, is a label-free method that can measure the thermal stability of proteins and thermodynamic properties of their conformational transitions. However, state-of-the-art miniaturized calorimetry systems still require a relatively large sample volume that compromises their thermal performance. Here, we propose to address these issues using nanofluidic systems based on integrated glass capillaries on silicon in which each capillary has an inner diameter of about 1 μm or less. The capillaries will be transformed into either suspended micronozzles, which can directly issue protein jets without much reliance upon hydrodynamic focusing, or calorimetric bridges, which can probe protein folding in sub-picoliter volumes. 蛋白質的錯誤折疊和聚集會在人體內形成非可溶性蛋白質沉澱（澱粉樣沉積），並被認為與多種人類疾病相關。例如，阿爾茨海默症（老年癡呆症） 患者腦中的澱粉樣沉積作為此症的病理標誌展現了與患者的癡呆症狀很強的相關性。同樣， P53抑癌蛋白的錯誤折疊成為半數癌症致病的重要原因（甚至成為肺癌中絕大部分病例的致病原因）。事實上蛋白質的錯誤折疊還與其它多種人類疾病相關。因此，對蛋白質折疊機理的研究已經不只是單純的為連結蛋白質的基因表達和其生物學功能而進行的理論層面的探索， 而是成為現今藥學研究的焦點之一。對蛋白質折疊過程的探索很可能催生對於上述疾病的新療法。 蛋白質折疊進而形成功能性結構是一個十分複雜的進程，單一的實驗技術很難對這一過程進行全方位解析。快速層流微混合器和基於差分掃描量熱法的微系統在最近被成功應用於對蛋白質折疊的研究。前者通過水力聚焦使蛋白質樣品在鞘流溶液的夾迫下形成窄噴射流，而鞘流溶液的迅速變化使得蛋白質處在非平衡態，極大地縮短了發生擴散混合的長度。此快速混合技術可以在亞微秒（< 10^-6 s）解析度級別並且以極小的樣品體積來檢測蛋白質折疊早期的進程。然而，這種通過鞘流的水力聚焦形成樣品噴射流的方法同時會帶來過早混合的問題，影響時間解析度的準確性。第二種技術，也就是基於差分掃描量熱法的微系統，是一項可以用於蛋白質熱穩定性和蛋白質構象變化過程熱動力學屬性測量的免標記技術。然而現今的微型化量熱系統仍然存在需要較大樣品體積的問題，降低了其熱學測量的品質。 在這份研究計畫中我們針對蛋白質折疊研究及現今已有的研究技術存在的問題提出一項新的納流控晶片技術，該技術採用了基於矽襯底的內徑可達1μm或以下的集成玻璃毛細管陣列。這些毛細管可以形成懸空的微噴管陣，這種微噴管不需要依賴水力聚焦即可直接噴射蛋白質樣品流。同時，這種毛細管也可以應用於量熱系統，從而實現在亞皮升（< 10^-12 L）樣品體積的級別對蛋白質折疊進行研究。

16209316.label: Realisation of objectives
16209316.value: Objective 1 is concerned with the development of an ultrafast micromixer for the sub-microsecond kinetic measurements of protein folding. The micromixer is an advanced version of our previous device featuring a monolithic integrated glass micronozzle inside a flow-focusing geometry (Applied Physics Letters, 2016). In the advanced version, we replaced the silicone elastomer cover with a rigid glass substrate secured in place on a silicon wafer by anodic bonding. This allowed us to introduce protein and buffer solutions into the micromixer supplied at a relatively high pressure. In the fabrication, we faced major challenges which took us some time to address. One challenge was the delamination of the chrome layer of the photomask during UV exposure, which was unusual. This led to the failure of micronozzle pattern transfer to silicon wafers. Our investigation revealed that the delamination is due to photoinduced heating around locations where the micronozzle patterns are located. We addressed this problem by revising the patterns. Another problem was the failure of glass wafer bonding over silicon because of thick dielectric layer. We solved this problem by depositing a thin interfacial layer of amorphous silicon in between the dielectric layer and the glass cover. A further problem was a fluidic leakage at the bonding interface. This was due to a surface groove over the micronozzle as a natural outcome of the reflow process. We addressed this problem by performing a surface polishing step flattening the micronozzle surface before depositing the amorphous silicon interfacial layer. After successfully addressing all these issues, we obtained microchips and characterized them for the micromixer performance. We performed experiments assessing the mixing speed through fluorescent dye quenching by potassium iodide (KI). FITC-dextran was supplied through the micronozzle (the center stream) while KI was added into the sheath flows surrounding the micronozzle (the side streams). Iodide ions are known to quench florescence and the quenching is an indicator of the iodide ion diffusion and thus of the mixing time. Our measurements indicated a mixing time of about 50 s. We tried to lower the mixing time below 1 s by increasing the sheath flow and reducing the center stream width (the diffusion length). However, the center stream became a sub-micrometer filament that was impractical to image through our confocal microscope. This problem could be addressed in the future by a better imaging system than the one currently available to us. We considered several approaches alternative to the proposed concept to attain a sub-microsecond mixing time. However, we found these approaches either already published or carried a high risk. Instead, we decided to focus on our micronozzle fabrication process and put our remaining efforts into the demonstration of structures relevant to practical applications. We transformed the micronozzle into an emitter tip for electrospray ionization that can be coupled to a mass spectrometer. We also demonstrated a nanofluidic memristor based on ion concentration polarization across integrated nanocapillaries. All these structures resulted from the micronozzle fabrication process. Since our mixing time is comparable to the state of the art, we published our results in a conference paper. Objective 2 is concerned with a differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) based on the integrated glass capillary bridges for the measurement of protein unfolding events in sub-picoliter volumes. These glass capillary bridges shared the same fabrication process with the integrated micronozzle featured in our micromixer. In fact, the fabrication process of glass thermal reflow which was introduced into micro/nanofluidics by our group defines the novelty in our proposal; the process allows the fabrication of nanocapillaries without using high-resolution costly patterning tools. The nanocapillaries reduce the sample volume requirement into sub-picoliter range. Considering the possibility of not being able to detect a signal from such a small fraction, we decided to implement a sub-nanoliter DSC first. We were also concerned with the thermal mass of our capillaries in relation to the thermal mass of the sample. This motivated us to turn to buried channel technology (BCT), a well-known process that allowed the fabrication of the capillary bridges with a sub-micrometer wall thickness and thus with considerably reduced thermal mass. Although the BCT process has been introduced to various applications, it has never been demonstrated before for DSC. As we implemented the BCT process for the first time, we had to establish it in our cleanroom first. The literature provided us some data on key process parameters and yet that did not prevent us from encountering major process issues. One was concerned with the self-enclosed feature of the capillaries. We initially failed to form self-enclosed capillaries regardless of the thickness of the SiO2 layer placed as a capillary material. We eventually solved this problem by revising the photomask layout. Another issue was concerned with the formation of capillary bridges by partially etching silicon substrate around the capillaries. During the experiments, however, these capillaries leaked, and the sites of leakage remained hidden. Our investigation identified the cause of the leakage as the sub-micrometer-thick capillary walls being eroded due to poor etching selectivity. We solved this issue by switching the capillary material from SiO2 to low-stress silicon nitride, which showed good resistance to etching. After solving these issues, we obtained sub-nanoliter DSC chips for thermal characterization. Experimental characterization of DSC chips required expertise in thermal measurements. Thus, we collaborated with an expert in the field, Dr Pavel Neuzil from Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi’an. This collaboration helped us establish our measurement system including a vacuum chamber in which we placed our chips to conduct measurements under vacuum to minimize thermal losses. The collaboration also led to a number of joint papers including two papers on thermal measurements in microchannels, one review paper on miniaturized polymerase chain reaction, which requires thermal cycling, and another paper on a script-based method to generate micro/nanofluidic layouts. From DSC chips, we first extracted thermal parameters including thermal time constant, and thermal conductance and capacitance both under atmospheric as well as vacuum environment. We found good agreement between the experimental values and theoretical ones obtained from analytical and computational models. We also introduced a non-contact precision method for the calorimeter temperature calibration based on the melting curve analysis of double-stranded DNA. For protein unfolding experiments, we managed to get a signal from bovine serum albumin, yet at a fairly weak level and with a poor repeatability. Increasing the protein concentration did not help improve the results. Our further attempts convinced us that the chip despite the increased volume capacity (sub-nL) was unable to detect heat released by protein unfolding. Instead, we identified the measurement of photothermal effect as a potential application. Using our DSC chips, we measured the photothermal transduction efficiency of plasmonic gold nanoparticles. For the first time, a calorimeter chip was used to measure the photothermal transduction efficiency. Using the chip, we also measured specific heat capacity of various liquids with reasonable accuracy. We summarized our results in two journal manuscripts one already published and one undergoing revision. Both objectives relied on silicon-based microchip development in cleanroom facility. It should be noted that students joined the project had to undergo a few months of equipment training to become qualified users before they can start fabricating their chips. Moreover, fabrication of each batch took nearly a month and typically required iterations to address the challenges faced.

16209316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209316.value: A major outcome of this project is a sub-nL chip calorimeter for differential thermal measurements of aqueous samples in twin calorimetric arms with a sub-nL enclosed space (see Publications 5 and 8, Section 8, Part C). Each arm features a fluidic microchannel located in close proximity to a thin-film resistance thermometer and heater patterned on a low-stress SiN membrane held over a Si cavity with suspension beams. The chip exhibits a rapid response with a thermal time constant of 15 ms in atmosphere and a residual thermal conductance below 6 μW/K, one of the lowest reported and accounts for the excellent sensitivity registered in vacuum up to 11 V/W. These values are in good agreement with those ones predicted by modeling including finite element method, lumped-capacitance analysis, and calorimeter electrothermal circuit simulation together with the measurement system. Long suspension beams in each arm ensure uniform temperature across its membrane as revealed by the fluorescence-based melting curve analysis. We demonstrated the calorimeter utility on the measurement of the photothermal transduction efficiency of plasmonic nanoparticles, which makes our study further unique in expanding the applications of chip calorimeters. The chip calorimeter has also been tested on the measurement of protein unfolding. However, the results suggest the chip capacity to be increased to enhance the measurement sensitivity and repeatability (Figure 11, Publication 6 in Section 9, Part C). Theoretical modeling and simulation methods validated on the chip calorimeter have also been utilized in the development of an optofluidic chip for the rapid assessment of thermal stability of proteins and DNA (Publication 7, Section 8, Part C). The optofluidic chip and the calorimeter chip share key process steps since both are based on the buried channel technology. Simulations similarly benefited the development of a flow-through microfluidic system in which heat transfer time is determined based on DNA melting curve analysis (Publication 3, Section 8, Part C). A further outcome of this project is a micromixer for kinetic studies of increased accuracy through a prefocused stream injection (Publication 5, Section 9, Part C). Based on the micromixer fabrication process, the project also demonstrated self-enclosed glass nanozzle emitter tips integrated on silicon for electrospray ionization (Publication 3, Section 9, Part C) and a nanofluidic memristor based on integrated nanocapillaries and their ion concentration polarization characteristics (Publication 4, Section 9, Part C). The project trained several MPhil and PhD students (see Section 10, Part C).

16209316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209316.value: Further development of the research should focus on the calorimeter chip. At this stage, the chip can provide a differential calorimetric measurement of one sample at a given time whereas the measurement of a set of samples at once is desired. This requires a calorimetric assay which can be obtained by scaling the calorimeter design (the twin calorimetric arms) into an array where each array element can be selectively controlled and measured. The calorimeter design is suitable for this purpose because the twin calorimetric arms fits into an area of 1 mm by 1 mm. A 5-by-5 array for differential measurements of 25 samples can fit into a single assay chip with a thumb nail size. A custom-designed hardware is also required to operate such calorimetric assay. The calorimetric assay, for instance, can be performed on plasmonic nanoparticles of various sizes and shapes and materials to identify the nanoparticles that exhibit a high photothermal transduction efficiency. Such nanoparticles can be used as highly effective photothermal agents to kill tumor cells in cancer therapy by photoinduced heat. Having an on-chip vacuum encapsulation would render a vacuum chamber redundant simplifying the overall setup but at the expense of the fabrication complexity.

16209316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209316.value: Understanding the mechanism of protein folding has become the focus of attention in pharmaceutical research since new treatments for debilitating diseases such as cancer and Alzheimer possibly lie in the pathways of protein folding. The folding of proteins into a functional conformation is an extremely complex process, a full description of which exceeds the capacity of a single experimental technique. Two complementary techniques include ultrafast laminar-flow micromixers and differential scanning calorimetry microsystems. Despite the progress made in the design of hydrodynamic mixers to achieve fast mixing, the issues inherent in such mixers have been mostly overlooked and caused relatively large uncertainties in the evaluation of mix time. Notable among those is the premature mixing encountered during the formation of the focused stream, the so-called “premixing.” Here, we demonstrated a laminar-flow micromixer with virtually no dependence on hydrodynamic flow focusing to produce a thin liquid jet and hence with minimized premixing. We further demonstrated a chip calorimeter for differential scanning calorimetry that can be applied to the detection of protein unfolding as a means of gaining insight into the protein folding mechanism.

16209916.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16209916.value: 壓縮感知在massive MIMO 上的應用

16209916.label: Project Objectives
16209916.value: Objective A: Model-based Compressive Channel Estimation and Feedback in Massive MIMO In addition to being sparse, there are rich structures in the channel matrices due to physical scattering in massive MIMO channels. For example, each physical scatterer contributes a block of continuous non-zero entries in the MIMO channels (under an appropriate spatial basis). Exploiting these additional “burst sparsity” structures is critical to extend the operating regime of compressive channel estimation and feedback algorithms in massive MIMO systems. However, conventional compressive sensing and sparse recovery algorithms cannot take advantage of these additional structures. We shall develop a new model-based compressive sensing framework (recovery algorithms and the performance bounds) to embrace and exploit these additional structures on sparsity. Objective B: Multi-user Joint Sparse Compressive Channel Estimation and Feedback We will then extend the model-based framework to multi-user systems. In multi-user massive MIMO systems, channels of different users will not be totally independent because they may share some common physical scattering structures. As such, there will be correlations in the sparsity structures between users in the systems. It is critical to exploit these joint sparsity structures to enhance further the performance of compressive channel estimation and feedback in multi-user massive MIMO systems.

16209916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209916.value: 學術界目前對於massive MIMO 系統有很強烈的研究興趣。通過在基站設立大量的天線，系統不僅可以獲得巨大的容量增益（空間復用）還可以增加空間自由度以減小區間干擾。然而基站天線的增加會帶來巨大的導頻和信道反饋的開銷，這也是實現massive MIMO面臨的主要挑戰之一。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一種基於模型的壓縮感知框架，以減輕上面提到的massive MIMO系統裡面的巨大開銷問題。具體而言，massive MIMO的信道裡面有有限的物理散射體，這導致信道矩陣在一個合適的空間基裡面是稀疏的。因此，在massive MIMO系統裡面如果利用信道的潛在稀疏性特徵，可以顯著的降低導頻和信道反饋的開銷。最近有很多文章研究壓縮感知在massive MIMO系統裡面的應用。在接收端可以使用稀疏恢復算法，用較少的導頻數恢復稀疏信道。然而，基於蠻力的標準的壓縮感知算法在massive MIMO系統裡面可能不會有很好的性能。首先，為了成功的恢復信道，標準的稀疏恢復算法對於信道的稀疏水平有嚴格的要求，這嚴重限制了該算法的可利用空間。為了克服這個問題，我們需要利用massive MIMO 信道的稀疏性的附加結構特性。具體來說，根據信道經歷的物理散射的結構特性，在massive MIMO信道矩陣裡面顯著的元素將會成塊的出現。利用信道矩陣的成塊的稀疏結構，我們將開發一種新的基於模型的壓縮信道估計和反饋的方案（包括稀疏恢復算法設計和相關的性能分析）。第二，因為不同用戶之間可能共享一部分散射環境，這導致不同用戶的massive MIMO信道可能是相互關聯的。利用多用戶信道稀疏結構以進一步改善方案的性能是非常重要的。為瞭解決這個問題，我們把前面提出的基於模型的壓縮感知框架延伸到多用戶情況，以進一步利用多用戶信道的聯合稀疏特性。 我們提出的基於模型的壓縮信道估計和反饋方案有巨大的意義，它可以大大減少開銷問題，讓massive MIMO的潛在優點得到充分利用。通過利用信道稀疏性額外的結構，這個項目的成果也將對壓縮感知領域提供非常重要的理論分析依據和更切合實際的稀疏恢復算法設計指導，同時它也可以被應用到信號處理和大數據分析等其他領域。

16209916.label: Realisation of objectives
16209916.value: In this project, we have focused on the execution of objective A and B. Specifically, we have explored the hidden sparsity structure in massive MIMO channels, which is critical to enhance the efficiency of channel estimation and feedback. The hidden sparsity in the massive MIMO channel matrix can be explained by the limited scattering in the environment in which there are only limited scattering paths between the base station and the mobile. Based on that, we have shown that efficient algorithms can be developed to exploit such sparsity and we can achieve substantial savings in pilot and feedback overheads to achieve the same channel estimation quality. In objective B, we studied the additional system level sparsity (in addition to the link level sparsity between the base station and the mobile station) among the multiple mobiles in the massive MIMO system. Specifically, the users in the same environment may share a common scattering environment and hence, they have some common sparsity structure (such as partially overlapping support in the channel matrices). Such common sparsity among users can be exploited to further enhance the channel estimation performance. Furthermore, we have extended our solution framework to explore additional sparsity structures as well as robust sparse representation in massive MIMO systems. Specifically, there might be additional structures such as burst sparsity or group sparsity where the elements of non-zero entries may be clustered (due to the clusters in the scattering environment). We have developed a more general sparsity model that can embrace these fine sparsity structures. Finally, we have developed algorithms for robust sparse representation in massive MIMO system with arbitrary antenna geometry. In this project, we have published 4 IEEE transaction paper and two IEEE conference papers. We have also trained a Ph.D. student and a postdoc.

16209916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209916.value: We have successfully developed a solution framework to reduce the pilot overheads in massive MIMO channel estimation problem. Specifically, the channel estimation problem is formulated as a sparse recovery problem. To reduce the pilot overheads, prior structures of the high dimensional fading channel have to be exploit. In this project, we considered various kinds of sparsity structure from group sparsity and burst sparsity in single user system and common sparsity in multi-user systems. We have developed a generic hidden Markovian model to embrace all these different granularity of sparsity structures. Based on the HMM model, we developed efficient message passing algorithm that can recover the channel under very limited pilot resource. The solution framework can embrace hidden sparsity in massive MIMO channel propagation due to clustered scatterings. The proposed solution can derive computationally efficient algorithms and be applied to various typical scenarios in 4G, 5G wireless systems as well as the next generation WiFi. In this project, we have published 6 IEEE transaction paper and two IEEE conference papers. We have also trained a Ph.D. student and a postdoc.

16209916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209916.value: The framework can be applied to develop efficient channel estimation for other systems such as Extremely Large Array Aperture system and Intelligent Surface for ambient communications. Using the structured sparsity is the key to simplify the pilot overheads in the channel estimation for these modern systems. The proposed solution framework can be extended to develop efficient channel estimation algorithms for next generation WiFi as well.

16209916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209916.value: In this project, we have proposed a solution framework to design efficient channel estimation for massive MIMO system. Massive MIMO offers a huge potential gain on spectral efficiency and therefore, is regarded as the core technologies supporting 5G and 6G wireless networks. However, all these gains rely on accurate estimation of the fading channel, which is challenging due to limited pilot resources. In this project, we tackle this challenge by exploiting various scattering structures in the massive MIMO propagation channels. As a result of the solution, we can reduce pilot overheads by over 10X. The proposed solution fully unleash the potential of massive MIMO systems.

16210216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210216.value: 隨著智能移動設備和移動社交網絡的日益流行，以及物聯網和大數據分析的推動，我們已經進入一個“全移動”的時代。飛速增長的移動應用帶來了全新的性能要求，包括GB/秒級別的超高傳輸速率，微秒量級的超低延時，和超密集無線接入。當前的無線網絡，包括4G網絡，都無法有效的滿足這些要求，所以通信業界正在規劃下一代無線網絡，即5G網絡。目前改進網絡性能的傳統方法已經達到極限，這就需要一個範式轉移以達到無線網絡的可持續演進。毫米波通信正是這樣一種開創性的技術，通過釋放GHz級別的可用高頻帶寬，它能有效的解決當前面臨的頻譜短缺危機。 由於高昂的硬件成本和極高的路勁損耗，毫米波段以前只被用作短距離室內通信。但隨著無線通信近期的發展趨勢，毫米波通信在蜂窩網中的應用前景收到越來越多的關注。首先，CMOS射頻電路的進展極大的降低了毫米波芯片的成本，同時無線網絡密集化的演進也降低了單個基站的覆蓋要求。毫米波信號的短波長特性使得大規模的天線陣列變得可行，這也意味著多天線傳輸技術將會在毫米波通信系統中發揮至關重要的作用。多天線技術可以通過波束形成來抵消路徑損耗，以及暴雨帶來的信號衰減和大氣的吸收。另外，它還能通過空間複用技術同時發送多路數據以提高頻譜效率。 然而，毫米波多天線通信系統也帶來了新的挑戰。由於硬件複雜度和功耗的限制，能夠支持的射頻鏈路數量有限，而且只能利用低精度的模數轉換器（ADC）。另外，由於信道的維度隨著天線數增長，獲取信道信息的複雜度及其帶來的系統開銷將變得難以承受。這個研究項目將致力於開發有效的毫米波多天線技術，尤其會考慮毫米波信道特性以及硬件的限制。我們會開發有效的混合預編碼算法來應對有限數量的射頻鏈路。為了支持有效的多天線傳輸，我們會開發全新的信道信息獲取方法。我們將研究低精度模數轉換器對系統性能的影響，并提出有效的方法來應對壓縮誤差的影響。我們還將分析多天線毫米波網絡的性能，這將揭示方向性傳輸和毫米波信號堵塞效應的影響，同時將有助於網絡性能的優化。

16210216.label: Realisation of objectives
16210216.value: This project investigated a key enabling physical-layer technique for 5G and beyond networks, namely millimeter-wave (mm-wave) communications. The mm-wave band offers orders of magnitude more spectrum than what has been exploited so far in cellular communication systems, and thus deploying wireless networks at such high frequency bands has been regarded as a promising approach to boost the wireless capacity. Nevertheless, the propagation characteristics of mm-wave signals fundamentally differ from sub-6 GHz signals of current wireless networks. Particularly, the tenfold increase of the carrier frequency brings additional free space path loss. Moreover, mm-wave signals are sensitive to blockages, which causes totally different path loss laws for line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) mm-wave signals. Such difference poses two main design problems: to effectively combat the propagation losses and analyze the network performance. Thanks to the small wavelength of mm-wave signals, large-scale directional antenna arrays can be leveraged to provide substantial array gains and synthesize highly directional beams, which help to compensate the increased path loss. This project endeavoured to develop computationally and hardware efficient beamforming architectures and algorithms, and also propose analytical frameworks for evaluating the performance of mm-wave networks. The research objectives of this project focused on the two key aspects identified above, namely efficient beamforming design and network performance analysis. Our investigation closely followed the stated research objectives, which led to fruitful research outcomes. In particularly, research results of this project have been reported in 6 journal papers, 4 conference papers, as well as 1 monograph. One paper [conference paper #4] received the best paper award at the IEEE Global Communications Conference (IEEE GLOBECOM) in 2017, a flagship conference of the IEEE Communications Society. Following is the detailed description of the realization of the objectives. • Research Objective 1, which is to develop efficient hybrid beamforming algorithms for mm-wave communications, forms the foundation of this project. We have spent a significant portion of our efforts on this objective, and developed a few different approaches to improve the computational efficiency of hybrid beamforming. A main finding from our investigation is that the algorithm design of hybrid beamforming is closely coupled with the hardware architecture, which in turn also affects the achievable performance. Thus the hybrid beamform design should account for the computationally efficiency of the algorithm, hardware efficiency, as well as the achievable performance. One of our main solutions is to modify the hardware architecture of hybrid beamforming, which helps to turn the beamforming optimization algorithm into a convex program and can be solved efficiently. This result has opened a new domain to develop computationally and hardware efficient hybrid beamforming systems. We have also investigated different formulations of the hybrid beamforming problem, and found that some formulations, e.g., the one based on the mean square error (MSE), lead to more tractable optimization problems. Given the effectiveness of our proposed methods, they have attracted great attention, not only from mm-wave communication systems, but also from closely related systems including Terahertz (THz) communications and intelligent reflection surfaces (IRS). • Research Objective 2, i.e., effective channel state information (CSI) acquisition, is a critical and also challenging one for mm-wave communications. Effective beamforming requires accurate CSI. On the other hand, given the large-size antenna array, the dimension of the mm-wave channel is enormous, which potentially will lead to a significant training overhead. Based on our research on hybrid beamforming, we first tested the robustness of beamforming algorithms to the CSI estimation error. It was found that the analog beamformer, which only controls the phases of the phase shifters, is more robust to inaccurate CSI. We also investigated two different types of methods to reduce the training overhead of CSI estimation, i.e., to send as fewer pilot symbols as possible. One is based on structured estimation, which exploits the sparsity of the mm-wave channels, and the other is based on deep learning, which exploits the structure of the mm-wave channels in a data-driven manner. Promising results have been obtained, especially for the deep learning-based method. • Research Objective 3 is on hardware efficient architectures for mm-wave communications. One main challenge of deploying mm-wave communication systems is the high cost and high power consumption of mm-wave components, including the GHz rate analog-to-digital converter (ADC), phase shifters, switches, etc. Different approaches have been proposed to reduce the complexity by employing low-cost low-power devices. Most previous studies focused on low-precision ADCs, even 1-bit ADCs. Based on the latest development, we found that hybrid beamforming is more promising, and thus we focused on further reducing the hardware complexity of hybrid beamforming by modifying the hardware architecture. Our main result was a new architecture called the fixed phase shifter (FPS) implementation, which only requires a small number of phase shifters with quantized and fixed phases. We also proposed an efficient algorithm to design such beamformers, which achieved performance close to the fully digital one. Overall, our proposed system excels in the three key design aspects, namely computational efficiency, hardware efficiency, and the achievable spectral efficiency. Given its great potential, the paper reported this result has received the best paper award at the IEEE Global Communications Conference (IEEE GLOBECOM) 2017. It has also attracted lots of attention from both the academia and industry. • Research Objective 4 is on the performance analysis of mm-wave multi-antenna (aka MIMO) networks. Cellular networks are limited by intercell interference. As mm-wave signals have dramatically different propagation characteristics from sub-6 GHz signals, it is critical to develop new analytical methodology to analyze the interference distribution of mm-wave networks and evaluate the network performance. Prior to our study, existing analysis of mm-wave networks either considered the noise-limited case or assumed a simplified antenna pattern, and thus could not accurately characterize the network performance. Built upon our previous experience on analyzing large-scale MIMO networks using tools from stochastic geometry, we developed a general and tractable framework for the coverage analysis of mm-wave MIMO networks with arbitrary distributions for interference power and arbitrary antenna patterns. It allows us to evaluate the performance of mm-wave MIMO networks without time-consuming system-level simulations. For example, our analysis showed that the coverage probabilities of mm-wave networks increase as a non-decreasing concave function with the antenna array size. Being able to handle general fading distributions and antenna patterns, our analytical framework can be applied to study other wireless networks, e.g., it has been applied to analyze cellular-connected UAV networks. Overall, we believe that we have satisfactorily completed this project. By covering all the research objectives in the project (Research Objectives 1 to 4), we are able to produce academically and practically significant research while contributing meaningfully to the training of students in this important area (Research Objective 5). Specifically, as a result of this project, PhD student Xianghao Yu has been trained and graduated.

16210216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210216.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are summarized as follows. As for references, [C1] and [J1] represent conference paper #1 and journal paper #1 in Part C, respectively. • Effective Hybrid Beamforming Algorithms for mm-wave Communications: We investigated hybrid beamforming in a challenging setting, with multiple users, multiple subcarriers (i.e., with OFDM modulation), and a large-size antenna array. Existing algorithms could not handle such a large-scale problem. To enable low-complexity algorithm, in [C1, C3, J4], we proposed a new hybrid beamforming structure which greatly simplifies the beamformer design and is able to approach the performance of the fully digital beamforming. In [J5], we proposed a new design criterion based on the mean square error (MSE), which leads to efficient hybrid beamforming algorithms. • A Holistic View of Hybrid Beamforming Design: Through our investigation of hybrid beamforming, we found it is critical to take a holistic approach and account for the three interrelated aspects: 1) hardware efficiency, i.e., the required hardware components; 2) computational efficiency of the associated beamforming algorithm; and 3) achievable spectral efficiency, a main performance indicator. In particular, dedicated tradeoffs should be made among these aspects, and different options will be preferred under different constraints. Our findings are reported and summarized in [J6]. • Hardware-efficient Hybrid Beamforming Structure: One major obstacle for mm-wave communications is the high cost and high power consumption of hardware components at the mm-wave frequency band. This motivated us to develop a hardware-efficient implementation of the analog network for hybrid beamforming in [C4, J2]. Remarkable, the proposed structure only requires a small number of phase shifters with quantized and fixed phases, and thus dramatically reduces the hardware cost and power consumption. • Coverage Analysis of mm-wave Networks: The propagation characteristics of mm-wave signals fundamentally differ from sub-6 GHz signals, which have important implications to the performance of mm-wave networks. Thus, it is critical to investigate the distribution of interference and analyze the coverage of mm-wave networks. In [J1], leveraging tools from stochastic geometry, we developed an analytical framework for the analysis of mm-wave networks, which can handle generic fading distributions and antenna patterns and lead to closed-form expression of key performance metrics. This framework was further developed in [C2, J3] to be applicable to general multi-antenna networks, and was also reported in the monograph “Stochastic Geometry Analysis of Multi-Antenna Wireless Networks”.

16210216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210216.value: This project has produced promising results on effective beamforming and performance analysis of millimeter-wave (mm-wave) communication systems. Nevertheless, there are still obstacles for the practical implementation of the proposed methods, which demand further investigation. One important direction is to build testbeds to verify the proposed hybrid beamforming architecture with fixed phase shifters, and compare with other approaches such as beamforming with 1-bit ADCs. It will also be of interest to test data-driven approaches based on deep learning for both beamforming design and channel estimation. The proposed methods can also be applied to other systems. As the mm-wave band signal is also used in radar systems, it is interesting to extend our methods to joint communication and radar systems, where radar sensing and data communication are carried over the same band. This will be of particular interest in autonomous driving vehicles. Moreover, to further increase the bandwidth, communicating at the terahertz (THz) band has also been considered, which bears some similarity to the mm-wave system (e.g., hybrid beamforming has also been considered at the THz band). Thus, it is interesting to extend our methods to the THz communication systems.

16210216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210216.value: The mobile data traffic continues to grow at an exponential rate, accompanied with emerging applications (e.g., AR/VR) that require ever higher data rates, which demands further capacity increase in wireless networks. The most effective way to boost the communication data rate is to enlarge the bandwidth. Particularly, moving from the sub-6 GHz band of current cellular networks to the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) band will provide orders of magnitude more spectrum, which has been regarded as a key enabler for 5G and beyond networks. Meanwhile, communicating at the mm-wave band poses formidable challenges in hardware and algorithm design, which requires efforts from both the academia and industry. This project investigated effective beamforming design, hardware architecture, as well as performance evaluation of mm-wave networks. In particular, effective hybrid beamforming systems have been developed, with a holistic consideration of the three key design aspects: computational efficiency, hardware efficiency, and the achievable spectral efficiency. An innovative hardware implementation of hybrid beamforming has also been proposed, with low hardware complexity and power consumption. Moreover, an analytical framework has been developed for performance evaluation of mm-wave networks. Overall, this project has developed algorithmic and analytical tools for the practical deployment of mm-wave communication systems.

16211516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211516.value: Discrete-time nonnegative (state-space) systems are those with nonnegative A, B, C, D matrices. Such systems find applications in modelling economic systems, biomedical systems, dynamic networks, chemical processes, etc. Motivated by the applications, a growing number of researchers have studied various aspects of nonnegative systems. A theory is emerging. However, recent research progress indicates that it is high time to extend the theory of nonnegative systems to semidefinite cone-invariant (SCI) systems. In such a system, the state space is a suitable subspace of the linear space of n by n symmetric matrices, and the A map (which is no longer a matrix but is rather a linear map on the state space) leaves the cone of positive semidefinite matrices in the state space invariant. Such cones are called spectrahedral cones. The B, C, D maps also have certain cone-invariant properties. There are several reasons for proposing this extension: 1. Real practical systems exist that are naturally SCI. These systems cannot be dealt with by nonnegative system theory. 2. Nonnegative systems are special cases of SCI systems. 3. Nonnegative systems have inadequate modelling power. SCI systems are much more powerful as a modelling tool. 4. The extension resembles the leap from linear programming (LP) to semidefinite programming (SDP) which has brought very significant advancement in optimization theory. In that case, SDP, with spectrahedral feasibility sets, can be applied to a much richer class of problems than LP which only deals with polyhedral feasibility sets. Our conviction is rooted in our recent study on realizing nonnegative impulse responses. A nonnegative system always has a nonnegative impulse response. However, a nonnegative impulse response cannot in general be realized by a nonnegative system. It is found that some nonnegative impulse responses that are impossible or difficult to realize by nonnegative systems can be easily realized by SCI systems. However, a fundamental problem remains open: given a nonnegative impulse response with a proper rational Z-transform, is it always possible to find an SCI realization? We expect that the effort in addressing this problem will lead to a rich theory of SCI systems. A possible negative answer to the open problem above would not ring the death knell of our investigation. We can continue the exploration with an even wider class of cones, called projected spectrahedral cones, in case we find that spectrahedral cones are not adequately powerful. 离散动态正系统是一类状态空间矩阵 A,B,C,D 为非负矩阵的系统。这类系统可以应用于经济系统、生物医学系统、动态网络、化学过程等的建模。由于它的广泛应用，越来越多的研究者对正系统的各个方面都进行了研究。一个新的理论正在诞生。 然而，最近的研究进展表明现在正是把正系统理论推广到半定锥不变 (SCI) 系统的时机。对于一个SCI系统，其状态空间是维度为 n×n 的对称矩阵线性空间的某个子空间，映射 A（它不再是一个矩阵，而是状态空间上的一个线性映射）使状态空间上的某个半正定矩阵锥不变。这类锥叫做spectrahedral 锥。同样地，B,C,D 也是有一定锥不变性质的映射。提出这样的推广是基于如下的几个原因: 1. 实际系统存在自然的锥不变系统。这些系统无法使用正系统理论来处理。 2. 正系统是一类特殊的锥不变系统。 3. 正系统建模能力不足，而SCI系统有更强大的建模能力。 4. 这个推广类似于从线性规划 (LP) 到半定规划 (SDP) 的飞跃。 LP只能处理多面的可行域，而SDP的可行域是一个spectrahedral集，因此它能够应用到更多的问题里。所以， 从LP到SDP的推广非常显著的推动了优化理论的进步。 我们对正系统到SCI系统推广的信心来自我们最近对非负脉冲响应实现问题的研究。正系统总是有非负的脉冲响应。但是，一般情况下，非负脉冲响应并不总是可以用一个正系统来实现。研究表明有一些不可能或者非常困难被正系统实现的非负脉冲响应是可以很容易用SCI系统来实现的。然而，一个根本性的问题仍然是开放的，就是给定一个 z 变换为真分有理式的非负脉冲响应，它是否总是可以找到一个SCI实现？我们期待通过努力解决这个问题最终发展出一套丰富的SCI系统理论。 对上述开放问题的可能的负面回答并不会终止我们继续探索的脚步。因为当spectrahdral锥还是不够强大时，我们可以继续探索一类更广泛的锥，称为投影spectrahedral锥。

16211516.value: In this project, we studied three typical matrix cones occurring in systems control theory. They are the set of semidefinite cone-invariant operators, the set of phase bounded matrices, and the set of M matrices. We also studied the linear systems associated with these cones. We have resulted in two published journal papers and one journal submission which is currently under review. The project objectives have been largely achieved.

16211516.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211516.value: In journal paper 1, we developed a theory of SCI systems and applied it to the study of LQ control of linear systems with random input gain. The key technical development is an existence condition for a mean-square stabilizing solution of the so-called modified algebraic Reccati equation (MARE). In journal paper 2, we defined the phases of a complex matrix and studied various properties of the phases. This work laid the mathematical foundation of a phase theory of MIMO LTI systems. In submitted journal paper 3, we studied a generalized version of the classical Frisch-Shapiro problem and investigated its applications to monotone system analysis and system identification. The generalization is from real positive-definite matrices to matrices with eigenvalues in the right hand side of the complex plane.

16211516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211516.value: The matrix phases defined in journal paper 2 lead to a brand new phase theory for multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) systems and dynamic networks. Two RGC GRF proposals have been written for further developments of the phase theory and both are funded. We are now intensively engaging in the research towards the development of the phase theory.

16211516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211516.value: Discrete-time nonnegative (state-space) systems are those with nonnegative A, B, C, D matrices. Such systems find applications in modelling economic systems, biomedical systems, dynamic networks, chemical processes, etc. Motivated by the applications, a growing number of researchers have studied various aspects of nonnegative systems. A theory is emerging. However, recent research progress indicates that it is high time to extend the theory of nonnegative systems to semidefinite cone-invariant (SCI) systems. In such a system, the state space is a suitable subspace of the linear space of n by n symmetric matrices, and the A map (which is no longer a matrix but is rather a linear map on the state space) leaves the cone of positive semidefinite matrices in the state space invariant. Such cones are called spectrahedral cones. The B, C, D maps also have certain cone-invariant properties. Our conviction is rooted in our recent study on realizing nonnegative impulse responses. A nonnegative system always has a nonnegative impulse response. However, a nonnegative impulse response cannot in general be realized by a nonnegative system. It is found that some nonnegative impulse responses that are impossible or difficult to realize by nonnegative systems can be easily realized by SCI systems. However, a fundamental problem remains open: given a nonnegative impulse response with a proper rational Z-transform, is it always possible to find an SCI realization? We expect that the effort in addressing this problem will lead to a rich theory of SCI systems.

16211616.label: Realisation of objectives
16211616.value: Realization of Objective 1: Achievements We have demonstrated lasing in 600nm wavelengths from silicon-oxynitride (SiON)-based microcavities, with a hybrid-integrated dye-doped polymer gain medium as an upper-cladding layer. Under-achievements We have not achieved lasing from coupled deformed microcavities. We attribute the lack of lasing from deformed microcavities to a higher cavity loss with the non-circular-shaped disk cavities, and thus a higher lasing threshold. We encountered the difficulties after submitting the mid-term progress report, and remedial actions have been taken to address the difficulties, as detailed below. Research work To demonstrate microcavity lasing, we have adopted circular microdisks with concentric slot-rings inside the disk rim region. The circular microdisks enable whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) resonances. The slot-rings modulate the refractive index in the radial direction, where the slot-rings are filled by the lower-refractive-index dye-doped polymer gain medium. Compared to integrating the gain medium as a uniform upper-cladding layer on top of the microcavity, the slot-rings filled with the gain medium enable a larger spatial overlap between the cavity modes and the gain medium. We have confirmed this using numerical simulations. The slot-rings enable a distributed feedback in the radial direction. This yields a resonance coupling among the radial-order WGMs. The larger overlap with the gain regions together with the distributed feedback enables lasing with a lower lasing threshold. We leveraged the resulting spatial- and frequency-dependent lasing mode distributions for sensing nanoparticles. We have switched the microdisk medium from silicon nitride (SiN) to SiON to reduce the refractive index contrast Δn of the SiN with the silica under-cladding layer and the polymer upper-cladding layer. The reduced Δn enhances the modal overlap with the gain medium in the upper-cladding layer. We deposited the SiON film on a Si wafer by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition. We have adopted SiON with a refractive index of ~1.7 and a film thickness of ~380 nm, on top of a silica under-cladding layer of 3μm thick. We transferred the device patterns to the SiON layer using i-line photolithography and inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching. The microdisks are 100 μm in diameter, with slot-rings located 10 μm away from the disk edge. The slot-rings have a width of ~1.15 μm, a height of ~380 nm, and are separated by ~350 nm. We have investigated microdisks with one, three, and five slot-rings. We have fabricated microdisks without waveguide output-coupling. This is because the required coupling gap spacing for 600nm wavelengths would be below 300 nm, which cannot be defined using the i-line photolithography. Our experiments indicated that the coupling gap spacing was not opened while the waveguide was over-etched. We spin-coated a layer of dye-doped polymer as a gain medium. We adopted two fluorescent dyes, rhodamine B and rhodamine 6G, and SU-8 polymer as the host. The dye concentration has a mass ratio of 1 wt.% dye mass to SU-8. To expose the evanescent field of the lasing modes on the cavity top surface, we have adopted a ~300nm-thick polymer. We optically pumped the microcavities from the top by over-filling the microdisk using an ns-pulsed laser (532 nm, 7ns pulse width, ~5.5 mJ/pulse, 10Hz repetition rate). We examined the microdisk lasing modes in a spatially resolved manner. We have adopted a tapered silica fiber tip, positioned ~60o tilted from the microdisk surface normal, to collect the out-of-plane scattering of the laser emission near the microdisk top surface. We sampled the microlaser emission at various locations, including the microdisk rim region and the slot-rings region, in both clockwise and counterclockwise directions of the circulating WGMs. We have demonstrated spatial-dependent lasing modes and thresholds. This indicates what lasing modes a nanoparticle can “experience” and induce a perturbation to when it lands at a specific location. Our spatially resolved measurements of the microdisk lasing modes are particularly relevant to guide our studies of applying the microlaser for sensing nanoparticles. One caveat is that we have not decoupled the perturbations to the lasing modes due to the fiber tip as we collect the lasing signals at different spatial locations. Further experiments using two fiber probes, with one fixed and another scanned on the microdisk surface, are underway, to decouple the localized perturbations of the fiber tips from the lasing mode distributions. Our experiments have revealed that the lasing thresholds of the 100μm-diameter microdisks with slot-rings are ~20 μJ/mm^2. The thresholds are in the same order of magnitude with the microdisks (without slot-rings) of 80μm-diameter and 120μm-diameter. The lasing microdisks with slot-rings exhibited multimode spectra, with two disjoint frequency-combs separated by a 20nm-wide “bandgap-like” feature. This is different from the multimode frequency-comb spectra with a continuous distribution observed from lasing microdisks without slot-rings. We attribute the “bandgap-like” feature to the distributed-feedback-induced coupling from the slot-rings. Further investigations are underway. Another major issue we encountered is the fast degradation (due to photo/thermo bleaching) of the dyes. The lasing signals could be halved in ~10 mins for microcavities upon high lasing signals. To minimize the thermo bleaching, we have immersed the aluminium sample holder into a water bath. We have attempted to co-dope the dye-doped polymer with quantum dots as originally proposed to tune the gain characteristics while improving the stability of the gain medium. We have not observed lasing using the quantum-dots-dye co-doped polymer gain medium. Realization of Objective 2: Achievements We have demonstrated detection of local perturbations by a fiber tip (as a model of single nanoparticles) using lasing from SiON-based microdisks with slot-rings. We have examined the microcavity lasing by embedding the microdisk in a water droplet. Under-achievements We failed to demonstrate detection of nanoparticles using the microlasers integrated with microfluidic channels. Research work To demonstrate detection of single nanoparticles, we locally perturbed the microcavity top surface using a tapered fiber, with a tip of below 10 μm in diameter to imitate a “nanoparticle.” This method provides a simple way to control the location of the “nanoparticle” on the microcavity surface and to lift the perturbation afterwards, while it is difficult to manipulate nanoparticles in air/liquid environments and to deposit the particle one at a time onto the microcavity surface in a designated location. We have observed an increased lasing threshold when the fiber tip touches (or made a dent on) the microresonator top surface. Our experiments suggested that the perturbation provides a negative feedback to the microresonator laser. We have adopted a fiber as a carrier to deliver polystyrene microparticles to the edge of the microdisk. However, our experiments indicated that the polymer cladding could be damaged while delivering the particles, and the light-collection fiber could be displaced. Further attempts or other methods to deliver particles are needed. We have demonstrated that the microresonator lases (with an increased threshold) when it is embedded inside a water droplet. This shows the potential of the microlaser as a sensor in a fluidic medium. However, the presence of the fiber forbids us to integrate the microlaser with microfluidic channels. The originally proposed concept was to use an integrated waveguide to output-couple the lasing light. To avoid using the fiber tip, we have attempted to image the lasing emissions from the microdisk sidewall. However, we have only observed weak lasing light even by using a large-numerical-aperture objective lens. Realization of Objective 3: As objective 3 is dependent on objective 2, we need to demonstrate nanoparticle sensing before addressing objective 3.

16211616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211616.value: 1. We have demonstrated dye-doped-polymer-coated SiON WGM microresonator lasers in 600nm wavelengths. The microlaser comprises an SiON circular microdisk resonator, hybrid-integrated with a dye-doped polymer gain medium as an upper-cladding layer. Specifically, we have demonstrated optically pumped lasing from 100μm-diameter circular microdisks with one, three, and five concentric slot-rings, 80μm-diameter and 120μm-diameter circular microdisks without slot-rings, all exhibit a lasing threshold of ~20 μJ/mm^2 by ns-pulsed pumping overfilling the microresonator top surface. (See manuscript in preparation) 2. We have demonstrated a spatial-resolved characterization of the lasing emission from our microdisks by using a tapered silica fiber with a ~10m aperture as a local probe, which was positioned near the microdisk top surface at a tilted angle to collect the out-of-plane scattering of the lasing emission for high-resolution spectral measurements. Such a simultaneous spatially and spectrally resolved characterization method has enabled us to reveal in detail the complex modal structures of the lasing modes. This will provide us with unparalleled insights to using microdisk lasers as active nanoparticle sensors. Our measured lasing modes and intensities are highly spatial-dependent. Specifically, we have demonstrated that microdisks with slot-rings support lasing not only along the microdisk rim region but also along the inner boundary of the slot-rings away from the rim region. This suggests that the slot-rings induce a distributed-feedback-coupling among the higher-radial-order WGMs for lasing. Our experiments suggested that the lasing emissions from the microdisk with three slot-rings are particularly sensitive to the spatial location of the fiber probe along the slot-ring region. This has a strong implication to the potential of such microlasers to be applied as a nanoparticle sensor. (See manuscript in preparation) 3. We have demonstrated that the microlasers are sensitive to its environment. Our experiments have revealed that any perturbations to or local damages on the polymer cladding can increase the lasing threshold. We have also demonstrated lasing from the microdisk immersed in a water droplet, with an increased lasing threshold from the microdisk in air. This suggests a strong potential for the microdisk laser to be integrated with a microfluidic channel as an active sensor in a fluidic ambient. (See M.Phil. thesis of Ching Chi KWAN)

16211616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211616.value: We have attempted to co-dope the dye-doped polymer with quantum dots as originally proposed. Further experiments are required, particularly in term of optimizing the co-doping process and the mixing ratios between the dyes and the quantum dots (up to 100% quantum dots). We will optimize the microdisk with slot-ring cavity design to study in detail the dependence on the spacing and width of the slot-rings, and examine both experimentally and theoretically how the distributed feedback along the radial direction can induce an additional resonant coupling among the whispering-gallery lasing modes that are applicable to sensing nanoparticles. To realize a more practical on-chip active sensor, we will design and fabricate microlasers with integrated waveguides to output-couple the lasing emission for an optical signal readout, instead of using the fiber tip as in our proof-of-concept experiments. Such an integrated waveguide would require a coupling gap spacing of below 300 nm for the visible wavelengths. We could fabricate this using electron-beam lithography. The integrated waveguides for out-coupling are desirable for integration with microfluidic channels.

16211616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211616.value: Detecting nano-sized biological particles (nanoparticles), such as proteins, viruses and DNAs, in a sensitive, fast, and reliable manner is a major technological challenge. It is of vital social importance, particularly during a pandemic. Conventional techniques for optical detection of nanoparticles often rely on fluorescence microscopy that requires fluorescence labelling. However, the fluorescent dyes are toxic, and the process of labelling is laborious and time-consuming. In this project, we have successfully demonstrated an on-chip integrated optical micrometer-sized laser in the visible 600nm wavelengths that can be potentially applied for actively sensing nanoparticles, without using a fluorescent label. The microlaser was fabricated on a silicon oxynitride substrate, with a hybrid-integrated dye-doped polymer cladding on top as an optical gain medium. We have experimentally demonstrated that the lasing modal distributions are strongly spatial dependent, suggesting that a nanoparticle adsorbed onto the microlaser will experience different lasing fields at different locations. Our lasing devices, upon further design and fabrication optimization, will allow an integrated waveguide for optical signals readout and can be readily integrated with a microfluidic channel for nanoparticles delivery. We therefore envision our demonstrated devices will pave the way for future nanoparticle sensing in an integrated on-chip platform.
