16212516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212516.value: Deep learning has been the hottest topic in the machine learning community in the past few years. It is capable of extracting features of multiple levels of abstraction from raw data, and has brought about significant improvements in a wide range of tasks such as speech recognition and image classification. In this project, we are concerned with the application of deep learning to unsupervised text analysis. Deep Belief Network (DBN) has been used for this task. A DBN consists of multiple layers of units. The units at the bottom layer are observed, while the others are hidden. Units on two adjacent layers are fully connected. The number of layers and the number of units on each layer are determined manually. Hierarchical latent tree model (HLTM) is another recently proposed deep probabilistic model for text analysis. It consists of multiple layers of variables. The variables at the bottom layer represent words and are observed. The other variables are latent. A variable is connected to only one variable at the next layer up. An HLTM structure is built in a bottom-up fashion. Co-occurrence patterns among words are first detected and latent variables (at level 1) are introduced to model those patterns; co-occurrences of the level-1 patterns are then detected and level-2 latent variables are subsequently introduced; and so on. HLTM has been shown to produce meaningful topics and topic hierarchies. However, the restriction that a variable may have only one neighbor in the layer above might lead to underfitting and leave interesting topics (combinations of words) undetected. In this project, we explore the middle ground between DBN and HLTM by studying models where each unit is connected to a few units at the next level up. We call such a models sparse DBN. Sparse DBN overcomes an obvious shortcoming of HLTM. In comparison with dense DBN, sparse DBN allows us to automatically find a compact model that fits data well and that is more interpretable. It also enables us to tackle more complex problems, because sparsity of connections implies that more hidden units can be introduced. We will develop algorithms for learning sparse DBNs from text data. Such an algorithm needs to determine model structure (number of layers, number of units on each layer, and connections between units on adjacent layers), in addition model parameters. We will also apply those algorithms to topic detection, document classification, and information retrieval. 深度學習是近年來機器學習領域最熱門的研究方向之一，它可以从原始数据中自動提取不同层次的特征，大幅度提升机器学习算法在诸如图像处理和语音识别等问题上的效果。 我們感興趣的是如何用深度學習方法來分析文本數據。以前，有人用深度信念网络(DBN) 來分析文本數據。 DBN由多层神经元组成，最下层的神经元是可观测的，称为觀測神经元，而其它神经元是不可观测的，称为隐神经元，相鄰兩層的神經元是全連接的，網絡的層次數和每層上的神經元個數是手工確定的。 在以往的工作中， 我們提出了另一種可以用來處理文本數據的深度概率模型，叫做層次隱樹模型(HLTM)，它由多层變量组成，最下层的是觀測變量，而其它層次上的是隐變量。HLTM的整體結構是樹狀的，其中一個變量只與上一層的一個變量相連， 模型的結構是通過數據分析自動確定的。 在本項目中，我們研究介於DBN和HLTM之間的模型，稱為稀疏DBN，其中一個變量與上一層的多個，但不是全部，變量相連。稀疏DBN放寬了HLTM的樹狀結構要求，同時也還放寬了DBN 全連接的限制，使得我們可以通過數據分析，獲得既能很好擬合數據又不過於複雜的模型，從而提升數據分析結果的質量和可解釋性。

We call such a models sparse DBN. … We will develop algorithms for learning sparse DBNs from text data. Such an algorithm needs to determine model structure (number of layers, number of units on each layer, and connections between units on adjacent layers), in addition model parameters. We will also apply those algorithms to topic detection, document classification, and information retrieval.” Based on our work on HLTM (C2), we have developed algorithms for learning sparse Boltzmann machines (C1), sparse feedforward neural networks (C3, C8), sparse latent structures for variational autoencoders(C6), and a novel sparse model for document generation (C7). The algorithms have been applied to topic detection (J1, C4, C5) and clustering (J2, C6). Note that C2 means the second conference listed in the output section, and J1 means the first journal paper.

16212516.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212516.value: Structure learning for deep neural network is a challenging and interesting research problem. We have studied structure learning for Boltzmann machines, feedforward neural networks, and the latent variables in variational autoencoders. For all those settings, we have proposed algorithm from learning sparse structures from unlabeled data. The model architectures learned using our algorithms are better or comparable to previous models in terms of model performance on all kinds of tasks. They contain significantly fewer parameters, and are more interpretable. In particular, we have learned a tree model from a collection of research papers published since 2000 at major AI and Machine Learning venues. It is called The AI Tree and placed at http://home.cse.ust.hk/~lzhang/topic/ai-tree.pdf. I use it regularly in my machine learning classes (3 times a year) to give the students an overview of the field. In addition, a topic hierarchy is extracted from the model and is kept at http://aipano.cse.ust.hk. It is a useful tool that lets you keep track of the latest developments in AI and offers a fast way to find recent highly cited papers on various topics or published at a certain venue.

16212516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212516.value: The role of sparse models in explainable AI (XAI) deserves further exploration. If there are sufficient resoruces, we will keep The AI Tree and aipano.cse.ust.hk updated to serve the AI community.

16212516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212516.value: Machine learning models are becoming increasingly complicated. Often they do not need to be as complicated as they are. In this project, we have investigated ways to build models of the appropriate complexity. This effort is especially interesting in scenarios where users are interested in the model structures themselves. One example is The AI Tree, which captures co-occurrence relationship of key terms in the AI literature and thereby give the reader a “map” of the AI field.

16214716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214716.value: 隨著許多現實世界的應用被當做圖數據來建模和分析, 例如 社交網絡，生物學網絡等，越來越多的研究興趣開始著眼於高效的管理和查詢大規模圖數據。最普遍採用的圖處理系統採用以點位中心的編程模型來將圖處理過程簡化為一系列點狀態更新的超步操作。具體來講，每個單獨的點作為一個獨立的功能單元。在每一個超步操作中，一個點的狀態是在接收到鄰居點的信息的時候決定的並在之後將狀態更新信息傳遞給鄰居點。超步操作是以疊代的方式執行，直到所有點的狀態收斂。眾所周知，這種簡單的模型會導致大量的信息傳遞，並且超步操作的批量化同步執行會成為性能瓶頸。雖然最近的研究工作主要集中於減少超步操作過程中的信息量和超步操作的非同步處理，但是在處理選擇性圖查詢而不是整個圖的分析任務中， 現有的以點為中心的圖處理系統在實際應用中仍然存在巨大的技術差距 。在本項目中，我們將設計一個新的框架能夠減少在大規模圖分析任務中大量的信息傳遞並且加速在分佈式圖數據中的選擇性查詢的速度。我們設計框架主要關注兩個關鍵問題：第一，通過在小規模子圖上預先計算一部分數據從而儘可能的減少在線計算量；第二，通過基於結構的剪枝和物理數據分割從而儘可能的減少所需訪問的數據量。在我們的框架中，1. 我們首先提出了一個簡潔的解決方案來將計算任務轉化為最小圖數據的訪問而不是利用疊代的超步操作從頭開始計算所有的數據。2. 之後我們只在預處理子結構的基礎上進行組裝和更新計算。本項目中三個需要認真考慮和重點設計的模組是：1. 圖抽象和細化模組；2. 基於滑動窗口的圖劃分；3. 基於局部特徵總結的子圖計算。我們將詳細闡述針對這些模組設計的所有可能的解決方案並將在真實的大規模圖數據集上測試整合了三個模組的整個框架。本項目提出的框架與三個關鍵模組將為在分佈式圖數據上做高效查詢處理提供一個新範例。

16214716.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214716.value: In this project, in order to achieve the first objective, we have studied second-order random walk, which is an important and effective summary representation for large graphs. We proposed efficient memory framework for efficient second-odder random walk [1]. In addition, to verify the effectives of different graph abstract modules, we have designed different similarity measures and efficient retrieval approaches [2][3] . All the above queries were benefit from the effective graph partition strategies. For the third objective, we have investigated the distribution graph environment and query workloads thoroughly and developed efficient subgraph listing algorithms [10] , approximate single-source SimRank solutions[11], neighbourhood-guided cache mechanisms [12] and graph fragment strategies [13] in a distributed environment. In addition to fulfilling the objectives listed in the project proposal, we had worked on crowdsourcing on scheme mapping and dynamic classification [14, 15] and consistent protocol on blockchains[16] . 16215816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215816.value: In the last decade, deep learning has been proved very successful in many areas including the field of automatic speech recognition (ASR). As of today, the acoustic models of most state-of-the-art ASR systems are hidden Markov models (HMMs) in which state posteriors are modeled by some form of deep neural network (DNN). These DNNs may be deep multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), multiple layers of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), or recurrent neural networks (RNNs) (particularly long-short-term-memory neural networks (LSTMs)), or a combination of them. It has been shown that deep learning may reduce the word error rate for many ASR tasks by as much as 30%. The targets in the output layer of a DNN acoustic model consist of a set of tied states (also called senones), and the DNN is trained to classify each frame of an input speech as one of these tied states. With few exceptions, the set of target tied states is generally determined by a traditional ASR system that uses HMMs with Gaussian-mixture model (GMM) states. The optimal number of tied states for many ASR tasks is often less than ten thousands from the past experience even when there are large amounts of training data (around several thousand hours); thus, DNNs are usually built with fewer than 10 thousand output units. However, with the higher degree of parameter sharing in DNNs, the PI believes that more acoustic detail can be discriminately modeled by DNNs (but not by GMMs) with many more output units, further improving ASR performance. In this project, the PI will investigate detailed acoustic modeling through robust training of DNN acoustic models with a large number of tied states (some of which may be distinct states) --- in the order of tens of thousands --- for better ASR performance. The major research issues include (a) how to train such big and deep neural networks (BDNNs) robustly? (b) How to initialize these models for DNN training? (c) How to regularize the model training as there will be many model parameters in such BDNNs? (d) How to prevent the model size and training/decoding time of such BDNNs from increasing linearly with the number of output units? 在過去十年中，深度學習在許多領域，包括自動語音識別（ASR）的領域，已被證明非常成功。截至今天，最先進的ASR系統裏的聲學模型大多是隱馬爾可夫模型（HMM），而它的狀態後驗概率是由某種形式的深層神經網絡（DNN）建模。這些DNNs可能是深多層感知器（MLPs），卷積神經網絡（CNNs），復發性神經網絡（RNNs）（特別是長短期記憶神經網絡（LSTMs）），又或是它們的組合。實驗結果証明深度學習可為許多 ASR 任務減少單詞錯誤率多達百分之 30。 DNN 聲學模型的輸出層中的目標包括一組共用狀態 （也稱為 senones），而DNN訓練的目標是要為每一幀輸入的語音劃分為這些共用狀態之一。除了少數例外，所設定的共用狀態目標是由使用HMM模型與高斯混合模型（GMM）的傳統ASR系統來確定的。從以往的經驗，即使有大量的訓練數據（約幾千小時），對許多ASR任務來說最佳的共用狀態數目通常不到一萬，因此DNNs通常具有少於 一萬個輸出單元。然而，隨著DNNs 有更多共用參數，PI 認為DNNs 可以利用更多的輸出單元來為更詳細的聲音資訊建模，從而進一步提高ASR的性能。 在這個研究項目中，PI 將研究通過擁有大量（以萬計的）共用和非共用狀態的DNN聲學模型的魯棒訓練來作詳細聲學建模，從而達至更佳的ASR性能。主要研究的問題包括：（a）如何魯棒訓練這樣龐大和深度的神經網絡（BDNNs）？ （b）如何為這些BDNN模型訓練初始化？ （c）因為BDNN有大量模型參數，如何規範它的訓練？ （d）如何防止BDNN模型的參數數目和訓練/譯碼時間與輸出單元數目線性增加？

16215816.label: Realisation of objectives
16215816.value: For objectives #1, #2 and #3, we had investigated a growing mechanism to increase the number of output acoustic units namely, triphones or senones of a DNN-HMM gradually by following a typical phonetic decision tree which is commonly used to get tied states (senones). However, the results were not better than those from our preliminary work mentioned in the proposal that directly modeled all distinct triphones and senones using multi-task learning (MTL) algorithm. The initialization of distinct triphones weights by cloning their corresponding senones, and the regularization by MTL plus dropout were found already adequate for training big and deep DNN (BDNN) for automatic speech recognition (ASR). As the area of deep learning advances very fast, by the time we started the project, long short-term memory (LSTM) units were shown to give better ASR performance than DNN. Consequently, we also investigated the objectives #1, #2 and #3 for LSTM-based acoustic model. Specifically we investigated higher-order LSTM-based acoustic models in which each recurrent LSTM unit receives multiple histories from the past, resulting in multiple-history LSTM (MH-LSTM) that is a generalization of higher-order LSTM. When MH-LSTM is unfolded in time, it becomes a very big and deep DNN. The width and depth of MH-LSTM can be adjusted by varying the amount of histories to model. Random initialization of MH-LSTM was found adequate. When more histories were included, the MH-LSTM training became difficult and underfitting was observed. The robustness problem of its training was later solved by adopting dilated causal convolution proposed in WaveNet, which can provide a wider receptive field effectively with fewer layers, into our MH-LSTM. We also investigated the use of BDNN in continuous sign language recognition (SLR). Due to the relative small amount of training data currently available for SLR, a major challenge is how to prevent overfitting in training these big SLR model with low resources. We proposed three stochastic modelling techniques for that: firstly, we introduced stochastic fine-grained labelling to model sign glosses with multiple states. The number of states of any gloss is variable and follows a probability distribution which was trained using the REINFORCE algorithm. Secondly, stochastic frame dropping, and stochastic gradient stopping were further used to deal with the severe overfitting problem, resulting in a more robust model and lower computation both in terms of time and space for model training. The three stochastic modelling techniques help achieve the first three objectives in training the BDNN for sign language recognition. For objective #4, we observed that regardless of whether DNN, RNN or other types of neural networks were used, the last layer of a neural net-based acoustic model is a softmax layer with the phonetic targets as outputs. When the number of targets is big, the softmax layer will consist of a large number of model parameters, resulting in great computation cost and slower decoding speed. We proposed a senone weight vector selection method and lazy evaluation to speed up softmax computation with little degradation in the model recognition accuracy. In our method, senone weight vectors were first clustered during training. During decoding, these clusters were ranked by computing the dot product between their centroids and the softmax layer input vector. Exact senone posteriors were computed only for the top N clusters whereas the posteriors of senones in other clusters were replaced by the value computed from the centroid of the cluster they belonged to. On a system with 60,000 senones, the proposed method sped up the softmax computation by 35% with less than 1% relative loss in accuracy.

16215816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215816.value: [ Below, CP=conference paper and JP=journal paper, when we refer our publications from Part C. ] We investigated a growing mechanism to increase the number of output acoustic units of a DNN-HMM gradually by following a typical phonetic decision tree. However, the method did not give better results than those from our preliminary work mentioned in the proposal that directly modelled all distinct triphones and senones using multi-task learning (MTL) algorithm. We also investigated a novel LSTM-based BDNN using higher-order recurrent LSTM units which receive multiple histories from the past, resulting in multiple-history LSTM (MH-LSTM) [CP4]. MH-LSTM could utilize multiple histories to capture long-term temporal dependencies between input frames and output phonetic targets better, and was more resilient to mis-alignments and wrong labels, or noises in the training data. The problem of model underfitting for training MH-LSTM with more histories was solved by using dilated causal convolution and replacing LSTM by simple recurrent unit (SRU) to create our novel WaveNet MH-SRU [CP10]. Empirically, we find the following order of performance among the various models: WaveNet MH-SRU > MH-SRU > SRU > LSTM > DNN. The use of BDNN in low-resource continuous sign language recognition was also studied. We proposed three stochastic modelling techniques for that: (1) stochastic fine-grained labelling to model sign glosses with multiple states. The number of states of any gloss follows a probability distribution which was trained using the REINFORCE algorithm. (2) stochastic frame dropping and (3) stochastic gradient stopping were further used to deal with the severe overfitting problem, resulting in a more robust model and faster training [CP14]. To speed up decoding, we proposed a senone weight vector selection method and lazy evaluation to speed up softmax computation with little degradation in the model recognition accuracy [CP1]. On a system with 60,000 senones, the proposed method sped up softmax computation by 35% with less than 1% relative loss in accuracy. We also trained BDNNs for robust speaker verification (SV) using various regularization techniques: multi-task learning [JP1, JP2], the mixup learning strategy [CP12], and orthogonal training for end-to-end SV [CP13, CP16]. We also created state-of-the-art speaker embeddings for SV by using BDNN with the self-attention mechanism [CP8]. Unsupervised speaker adaptation for BDNN was successfully demonstrated in [CP2, CP5, CP6]. Finally BDNNs were also successfully trained for speech synthesis [CP15], lipreading [CP7], and natural language processing [CP3, CP9].

16215816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215816.value: The area of artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing very fast. Many big and deep neural network (BDNN) architectures are continually proposed and some of them have been shown effective for many applications. Training these BDNNs is always non-trivial and our research in this project investigated some training techniques such as stochastic modelling and a few regularization approaches to help training robust models. We also proposed a softmax weight vector selection method and lazy evaluation to speed up inference with these BDNNs. During the past few years, more advanced and modular neural architectures such as transformer is shown more powerful than simple DNN or LSTM layers. Nonetheless, for those models that make use of the softmax layer as the last layer, our proposed speedup method for decoding should be still effective. On the other hand, how to combine the stochastic modelling techniques proposed in this project for robust training into the new neural architectures is worth further investigation.

16215816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215816.value: The recent advancement of artificial intelligence is mainly attributed to the great advancement in deep learning and the availability of large amount of training data. As a result, deep learning models are getting bigger and deeper --- more complex --- to take advantage of the large amount of training data. Training these big and deep neural networks (BDNNs) is not trivial and it can easily get stuck at local minima or does not converge. Our research originally focussed on the robust training and efficient decoding of BDNNs for automatic speech recognition, but the techniques thus developed were found also effective to other applications such as sign language recognition, lipreading, speech synthesis, speaker verification, and document embedding. We demonstrated that robust BDNNs could be trained using various regularization techniques (e.g., multi-task learning and mixup). When the amount of training data is relatively small, stochastic modelling techniques (such as stochastic frame dropping and stochastic gradient stopping) are also found useful for producing more robust BDNN models. Furthermore, if the last layer of a BDNN is a softmax layer, a softmax layer weight selection algorithm together with lazy evaluation can be used to speed up the subsequent decoding process.

16216116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216116.value: With an increasing demand of fast transportation, high-speed rail (HSR) is gaining global popularity, imposing new challenges to geotechnical researchers and engineers. Compared to conventional embankments, the allowable post-construction ground deformation of HSR embankments is much smaller (e.g., 15 mm in China National Standards). Excessive settlement may induce various problems such as foundation serviceability issues found at the Paris-Brussels-London line. Accurately predicting ground movements and differential soil settlements is therefore extremely important. The deformation of subgrade soils is governed by their stiffness at small strains less than 1% under working conditions. In the field, subgrade soils are subjected to various complex working conditions: firstly, moving trains impose cyclic loads on soils with rotations of principal stresses; secondly, subgrade soils are often unsaturated and subjected to daily variations of temperature and suction resulting from changes of water content. Furthermore, the stiffness of subgrade soils is commonly anisotropic due to soil compaction. So far, there is a lack of fundamental understanding and modelling capability of small strain stiffness of unsaturated soil under cyclic thermo-hydro-mechanical loads. In particular, the effects of principal stress rotation and the degree of stiffness anisotropy at various suctions and temperatures have generally not yet been investigated and understood. The proposed project will address and tackle these technical challenges through laboratory element testing and theoretical constitutive modelling. In the laboratory testing, a new suction- and temperature-controlled hollow cylinder torsional shear apparatus with strain measurement capability by using particle image velocimetry analysis will be developed. Special attention will be given to the investigation of anisotropic small strain stiffness along three important and representative stress paths, including cyclic heating and cooling, cyclic drying and wetting, and mechanical cyclic loading and unloading with considerations of principal stress rotations at various suctions and temperatures. Based on these new experimental results, a novel state-dependent theoretical constitutive model will be developed to capture cyclic thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated subgrade soils, with particular consideration of principal stress rotations and soil anisotropy at small strains under different temperatures and suctions. The success of this project will, no doubt, improve our fundamental understanding and modelling capability of complex unsaturated soil behaviour under cyclic thermo-hydro-mechanical loads. The new laboratory element test results and theoretical model obtained from the proposed project will assist researchers and engineers to accurately analyse soil deformation under complex working conditions, and also benefit society by improving the safety and sustainability of HSR. 隨著人們對快捷交通的需求不斷增加，高鐵在全世界扮演越來越重要的角色。全球的高鐵里程已達30,000公里，並預期在20年內增加到80,000公里。高鐵工程的迅速發展對岩土領域的研究人員與工程師提出了新挑戰，主要原因在於：相比傳統的鐵路路基，高鐵路基的工後沉降允許值非常小（例如，中國的國家標準為15毫米），精確預測路基沉降量甚為重要。此外，土壤在路基日常運作狀態下受到車輛循環荷載、冷熱和乾濕循環三方的共同作用及影響，並且出現顯著的主應力軸旋轉和模量各向異性。目前，國內外對應力-溫度-滲流循環作用下土體的變形特性及其理論尚缺乏完善的認知，特別是缺乏對非飽和土主應力軸旋轉效應和各向異性的研究。 本項目將展開室內試驗和理論建模研究應力-溫度-滲流循環作用下非飽和土的各向異性模量，並考慮主應力軸旋轉效應。在室內試驗方面，研究團隊將研發可控制吸力和溫度的空心扭剪儀，展開試驗研究非飽和土各向異性模量沿三個重要應力路徑的變化規律：溫度循環、冷熱循環、不同溫度與濕度條件下循環剪切。基於新的實驗結果，建立與土壤狀態相關的本構模型描述循環荷載下非飽和土的主應力軸旋轉效應及模量各向異性。該項目的成功將毫無疑問提升對循環荷載下非飽和土的各向異性模量的認識，更能幫助研究人員和工程師更精確預測複雜工況條件下的路基土變形規律，提升高鐵路基的安全性和可持續性。

16216116.label: Realisation of objectives
16216116.value: All of the objectives have been achieved through the following activities along with the original plan: (1) A triaxial apparatus equipped with three pairs of bender elements was developed for investigating the anisotropic shear moduli of soils. Moreover, a hollow cylinder torsional shear apparatus was modified to test unsaturated soil. By using these apparatuses, the anisotropic shear moduli can be tested along various thermo-hydro-mechanical paths such as the cyclic hearing-cooling, cyclic drying-wetting and cyclic shearing. (2) Extensive laboratory tests were carried out on reconstituted, compacted and intact specimens to investigate anisotropic shear moduli of unsaturated soil with different microstructures. The soil fabric of each specimen was evaluated using a scanning electron microscope and a mercury intrusion porosimeter. (3) Within the bounding surface plasticity framework, new constitutive models were proposed for describing the thermo-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soil.

16216116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16216116.value: Key findings and outcome related to Objectives 1 and 2: (a) The compressibility of lateritic clay decreased by about 50% as suction decreased from 150 and 0 kPa. This is mainly because that as the suction decreased to 150 kPa, the sizes of inter-aggregate pores decreased as a result of the aggregate swelling, as revealed by MIP data. (b) A linear increase in dilatancy with suctions ranging from 8 to 230 MPa was observed. (References: Journal papers 7 and 8 in the list shown below) Key findings related to Objective 3: (a) Under cyclic thermal heating and cooling, the reconstituted, intact and compacted specimens all showed continuous contraction. The accumulated plastic strain of the reconstituted specimen was 38% and 68% larger than those of the intact and recompacted specimens, respectively. (b) A temperature-controlled oedometer equipped with bender elements was used to investigate effects of temperature and thermal cycles on the anisotropic elastic shear moduli of soil. The results reveal that at a given stress, the anisotropic shear modulus is smaller at a higher temperature. (Reference: Journal paper 2) Key findings related to Objective 4: As suction decreases, contrary to the typical behaviour of compacted soils, the small strain shear moduli increase in the compacted loess. The increase is most probably because of significant wetting-induced contraction during the wetting process. In contrast, the shear moduli of the intact specimens remain unchanged, owing to slight swelling observed during wetting. The behaviour of the intact loess is likely dominated by the soil microstructure and suction effects are relatively minor. (Reference: Journal paper 5) Key outcomes related to Objective 5: In this project, several interrelated constitutive models were proposed and published for better simulating the cyclic thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soil, considering the influence of anisotropy and principal stress direction: (a) One model was proposed to better capture the cyclic thermal strain. (b) A state-dependent thermo-mechanical model was developed for structured fine-grained soil. (c) A bubble model for unsaturated soil was developed within the framework of kinematic hardening and bounding surface plasticity. The model is capable of well capturing effects of recent suction history on anisotropic non-linear stress-strain relation and shear modulus degradation at small strains, with consideration of both triaxial compression and triaxial extension modes. (References: Journal papers 1, 3, 4, 6 and 10; several models will be published in the next one or two years)

16216116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16216116.value: This project mainly focuses on the thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of compacted soils, in which soil structure and its degradation are not strong. However, some soils like intact loess and cemented soil have significant structure effects. Some preliminary studies in this project reveal that structure can greatly affects the deformation behaviour of unsaturated soil. To fully understand the thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated and structured soils, a comprehensive study is urgently needed.

16216116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16216116.value: High-speed rail (HSR) is gaining global popularity, due to an increasing demand of fast and efficient transportation. The rapid development of HSR networks is posing new challenges to geotechnical researchers and engineers. As compared to conventional railways embankments, the allowable post-construction ground deformation of HSR embankment is much smaller (e.g. 15 mm in China National Standards). Excessive ground movements and differential soil settlements would induce various problems, such as the foundation serviceability issues occurred at the HSR line linking Paris to Brussels and London. Considering the very small soil deformation allowed, an accurate prediction of subgrade soil deformation in HSR embankments becomes extremely important. This project has improved the fundamental understanding and modelling capability of unsaturated subgrade soils. The new laboratory test results and theoretical models from this project will assist engineers to accurately analyse the deformation of subgrade soils under complex working conditions. This project is expected to benefit society by improving the safety and sustainability of HSR. The scientific advancements will also have impacts on the analysis and design of transportation-related facilities such as airport runways, highways, and foundations for vibrating machines, where the essential principles of soil mechanics obtained from this project can be equally applied.

16216216.label: Realisation of objectives
16216216.value: All the four research objectives were achieved through this project study. For Objective 1, “Verification of the proposal 3D light path model of an ideal diamond”, we successfully improved the three-dimensional mathematical model based on diamond optical properties analysis and ray tracing simulation. When a diamond becomes visible by the interaction with electromagnetic radiation, four main types of interaction are considered: reflection, refraction, absorption and scattering. These effects depend on the optical properties of the diamond material and illumination, including nature and position of the light sources. In addition, the imaging system collects the light rays reflected from the inspected diamond and projects the three-dimensional scene into two-dimensional image plane that consists of pixel points on a discrete grid. Finally, the intensity of each point is represented by a suitable finite number of grey values, which is calculated by its absorbed energy. The proposed model and its simulation results help us clearly understand the physical laws of diamond light propagation and how an acquired diamond image is formed from the three-dimensional scene structure, and also achieve model-based image feature localization and tracking. To verify the model based on existing diamond inspection methodologies is also applied in real diamonds inspection, an experiment setup about image acquisition system is built in to capture clear real diamond image with abundant information. The hardware configuration of the image acquisition system includes a new design of integrating sphere, lens and camera. The designed integrating sphere can provide a light source that uniformly illuminates an inspected diamond sample. It also provides a dark background of the imaging area, which makes it possible that inclusions inside the diamond or on its surface can be clearly shown in captured images. The design process emphasizes the optical properties of diamonds in round-brilliant cut and several important concepts in radiometry. In addition, the imaging system includes industrial lenses, CCD cameras and sample loading plate, which is adopted to collect diamond transmitted light and reflected light. Experimental results and a corresponding analysis verified the uniformity of the integrating sphere and practicality of the whole system. For Objective 2, "Development of image processing algorithm for diamond clarity and cut grading”, we developed an image processing algorithm to prepare the original acquired diamond images for feature extraction analysis, and also to fix any problems that would otherwise adversely affect feature description. In addition, the developed algorithm can accurately extract the inclusion regions and transmission regions based on the inspiration of the proposed model. The developed algorithm can accurately separate the regions of interest in an acquired diamond image, and then identify the image features of individual regions to distinguish the inclusion regions and reflection regions based on the analysis of diamond optical properties. The extracted inclusion regions are adopted to evaluate the clarity of the diamond being inspected, while extracted reflection regions, that is the diamond leakage light, can be used to evaluate the diamond cut. This is the most important aspect of achieving the full automation of diamond clarity and cut system. For Objective 3, “Establish criteria and standards for diamond clarity and cut grading”, we established a universal grading system to make the process of classification more efficient, accurate and consistent, and lastly, assign an accurate and objective grade to a diamond. The parameters of the classification model and weights of each criterion and features are calculated based on the general rules provided by GIA. For Objective 4, “Experimental verification of diamond grading algorithm”, we prepared many diamond samples to be inspected and conducted experiments to verify the performance of the whole designed machine vision system for diamond clarity and cut grading, which includes the effectiveness and practicality of the hardware configuration as well as the effectiveness, robustness and repeatability of the developed image processing algorithm. From the experimental results, the extracted diamond inclusions, diamond reflection (light leakage) and the grade of each diamond sample compared with manual results given by the gemological experts show the correctness, robustness and repeatability of the whole developed vision system.

16216216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16216216.value: Realizing automatic detection of diamond quality including clarity and cut is very significant in the gemological industry. Existing image acquisition system cannot acquire diamond images with high signal to noise ratio. These traditional image processing methods cannot accurately remove noise, extract regions of interest and identify image features of the diamond image. In this research, these issues are first resolved from a physical point of view by establishing the 3D light path model of an ideal diamond. From analyzing the optical properties of the natural diamond and implementing the physical laws of diamond light propagation and diamond image formation, this model not only provides design solutions of diamond image acquisition system, but also obtains the image features to distinguish between different signals in a diamond image. Major findings and research outcome are summarized in these four aspects: 1. The three-dimensional mathematical model based on diamond optical properties analysis and ray tracing simulation were established and verified by the newly designed image acquisition system. The insights and findings from the diamond optical properties lead to the method of image acquisition design that can obtain diamond images with high signal to noise ratio for diamond clarity and cut grading. An effective image acquisition system was designed and fabricated by properly optimizing the optical components of the illumination system and imaging system. The design details references can be found in Journal paper No. 1. The signal to noise ratio of the obtained diamond images were high, attesting to the effectiveness of the proposed image acquisition system. 2. From the inspiration of the established diamond model, it was found that a diamond intensity image consists of three types of signals according to their different grey value intervals: inclusion, light leakage (reflection) and diamond background. Different types of signals can be controlled to lie in different image regions by fine-tuning the parameters and relative positions of each optical component in both the illumination system and imaging system. The results of the analysis of diamond optical properties also provide the image features of different types of diamond signals, which are then built into the diamond image processing algorithm. Details can be found in Journal paper No. 2. The finding of the established model and the analysis of diamond optical properties facilitate the image processing development and the goal of reducing complexity and operation time. 3. A new algorithm for diamond image processing was developed to extract the diamond inclusions to evaluate the diamond clarity. The regions of interest, including the inclusion regions and reflection regions, can be easily separated by removing the image noise and diamond background regions and by enhancement operation. The curve enclosing each region of interest is complete, continuous and closed, which proves the accuracy of the image separation. In the next step, optical properties of pure diamond and diamond inclusions are made to distinguish between diamond inclusions and reflections. The effectiveness and robustness of the developed diamond inclusion extraction approach are verified experimentally. Details of algorithm development and its experimental results can be found in Journal paper No. 2. 4. Two methods for automatically evaluating diamond cut are proposed. The first method is diamond proportional calculation, which is developed to precisely measure key proportional parameters that affect how light interacts with a diamond. The second method is based on the diamond light leakage extraction. Detecting light leakage of a diamond where the light is not returned to the diamond, crown caused by diamond non-ideal cutting, takes into account the impact of the facet and inclusion on diamond light path propagation. Details of image processing algorithm for diamond cut grading can be found in Journal paper No. 3.

16216216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16216216.value: The future developments of the research can be distinguished into three aspects: 1. The main solution to further improve the accuracy of diamond inclusion extraction is the further study of diamond complex cutting design that may provide a method to overcome the experimental error caused by the complicated formation of reflections (light leakage) in diamonds, especially for diamond samples with a poor cut design. 2. In the diamond industry, it is important to produce machines to distinguish the fake diamonds from natural ones. Unfortunately, so far there are no reliable existing tests to examine whether a diamond is the natural one. However, diamond imitations contain no inclusions, because inclusions are the result of a gem’s crystal natural growth process. Therefore, the previous analysis of the extraction of diamond inclusions can be used to identify natural and synthetic gems. 3. The proposed model-based approach of understanding how an image is formed based on physical laws and ray tracing simulation has the potential to be extended to other applications based on machine vision, such as quality inspection of other objects. To increase the SNR of acquired image, the design of each optical components of the image acquisition system can be optimized by theoretical analysis of optical properties.

16216216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16216216.value: Clarity and cut are two of the most important criteria globally used to assess diamond quality. They are currently manually evaluated by professional appraisers. However, it takes a long time to train an appraiser, and the job is physically demanding and the grading results from different appraisers are sometimes inconsistent. Therefore, there is a high demand in the gemological industry to replace manual diamond evaluation methods with an automated system. In this research, academic issues are attempted to be solved from a physical perspective. The three-dimensional mathematical model is established to discover the physical laws of diamond light propagation and diamond image formation. Based on acquired diamond physical rules, a new diamond image acquisition system is designed. After acquiring diamond images with high SNR, an inclusion extraction approach and clarity classification method are developed to accurately separate the regions of interest and then to extract the inclusion regions and assign the clarity grade. In addition, diamond cut is graded by calculated diamond proportional parameters and extracted leakage light regions. The experimental results match more than 90% of the gemological experts’ manual detection results. Compared to previous studies, the proposed algorithm for diamond grading is more accurate and less complex.

16217416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16217416.value: Epigenetics refers to changes in gene expression without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Epigenetic regulation of gene expression has been revealed to have profound influence on cellular behaviors and, in turn, human development and diseases. In response to various external stimuli, different cells may have their own epigenomes that are specific for different tissue types, differentiation status, and disease states. Hence, there is an intriguing demand for epigenomics to be conducted at the single-cell level. Conventional epigenetic assays that rely on bulk sequencing fail to extract long-range information in the context of individual genomes, due to extensive fragmentation and population averaging. By bridging nanofluidics and biomolecular imaging technology, optical mapping offers a promising solution for detection of epigenetic patterns on a single genome. We propose here a novel optical mapping platform that consists of dynamically formed nanochannels to confine and stretch DNA molecules for direct fluorescence imaging and detection of epigenetic DNA modifications. By exploiting the pneumatic microvalve control and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer deformation, uniform triangular nanochannels with size of tens of nanometers and length of submillimeter can be formed and continuously adjusted by the applied pressure. These size tunable nanochannels are well suited for linearization of DNA molecules spanning from several hundred Kbp up to a few Mbp. More importantly, the deformed layer will naturally create a gradient in depth and smoothly adjoin the formed nanochannels and the microchannels for DNA loading, which effectively prevents DNA stacking at the entrance of the nanchannels, the challenge faced by most nanochannel devices. By modulating the micro-and nano-fluidic architectures, we will explore the integration of single cell trapping and lysis, genome extraction and purification, fluorescent labeling of epigenetic marks, DNA translation, stretching, and optical mapping. The integrated dynamic nanofluidic platform will allow for single cell manipulation and processing, as well as direct visualization of individual genomes extracted from a single cell. Using this platform, we will detect epigenetic marks by DNA methylation, e.g., 5-methylcytosine (5-mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5-hmC). We expect the development of single-cell epigenome optical mapping will provide a truly comprehensive view of epigenetic DNA modifications along single genomes that were previously inaccessible, and greatly enhance our understanding of cellular development as well as disease diagnostics/prognostics. 表觀遺傳學是指不改變基本的DNA序列而產生基因表達的變化。基因表達的表觀遺傳調控對細胞行為進而人類發展和疾病產生深遠的影響。不同細胞響應於各種外部刺激在特異的組織類型，分化狀態和疾病狀態中可能有他們自己的表觀基因。因此，表觀基因組的研究需要在單个細胞級別下進行。由於需要进行大量碎片化和統計平均，基于測序的常規表觀基因檢查無法提取個人基因組情況下的大片段信息。将納流控和生物分子成像技術结合的光學圖譜技術為檢測單細胞表觀基因提供了可能的解決方案。 在這項研究計劃中，我們提出了一個新穎的光學標測平台，包括動態形成的納米通道，使 DNA分子限制在納米通道中并均匀伸展，以便對DNA分子的表觀遺傳修飾直接進行熒光成像。通過利用氣動微型閥的控制和可變形的聚二甲基矽氧烷（PDMS）材料，通過所施加的壓力連續調節可以形成大小在幾十納米左右和長度為亞毫米的均勻的三角形納通道。這些尺寸可控的納米通道恰好適合於從幾百KBP到MBP的DNA分子的線性化。更重要的是，上述變形層自然會創建深度上的梯度和平滑鄰接形成納米通道和用於DNA加載的微米通道，從而有效地防止了DNA在納米通道入口的堆疊，解決了现有設計中存在的問題。通過調製微納米流體的架構中，我們將探究單細胞俘獲和裂解，基因組提取和純化，表觀遺傳標記的熒光標記，DNA分子的輸送，拉伸，和光學圖譜的整合。我们所搭建的集成動態納米流體平台將使單細胞操作和處理，以及從單個細胞中提取個人基因組的直接可視化。此平台也可以让我們檢測表觀遺傳標記的DNA甲基化，如5-MC和5- HMC。 我們期望此單細胞表觀基因組光學圖譜将提供一個以往無法訪問的單一基因組的表觀遺傳修飾的宏觀識別，進而大大提高我們的細胞發展的理解，以及疾病的診斷/預後。

16217416.label: Realisation of objectives
16217416.value: (1) Objective 1 was fully realized. We developed a low-cost multilayer soft lithography and PDMS molding method for fabricating size-tunable nanochannel arrays. By leveraging the control of a pneumatic microvalve and the deformation of nanoslits made in PDMS, uniform triangular nanochannels can be dynamically formed and continuously adjusted by the control pressure. The nanochannel size and uniformity characterization was conducted by simulation and experiment. We performed finite element analysis using Comsol Multiphysics and image calibration to elucidate the size-tunability of the formed nanochannels. We have achieved nanochannels of an effective channel size down to 20 nm and length up to submillimeter. Unlike traditional direct-bonded nanochannels, the formation of channels can reverse upon the release of the control pressure, facilitating channel surface passivation and buffer solution exchange. Moreover, the curved edges of the microvalve smoothly bridge the depth differences between the formed nanochannels and adjoining microchannels, which resolved the problem of DNA molecule clogging at the step interface in the conventional nanochannel devices. (2) Objective 2 was mostly realized. We have succeeded in specific-site fluorescence labeling of epigenetic DNA modification 5-hmC, using the protocol for bulk solutions off-chip. We also succeeded in developing a super-resolution genome mapping proctocol using a multi-color super-resolution imaging microscope and the size-tunable device developed in Objective 1. We further developed an efficient alignment and data analysis method by using the fluorescent barcodes on DNA backbone as references, and fluorescent markers can be revolved with the resolution down to ~100 bp. However, epigenome optical mapping in nanochannels using DNA molecules extracted from mouse embryonic stem cells or Hela cells was not successful because we were not able to detect the signals from epigenetic marks of a single linearized DNA in a nanochannel. (3) Objective 3 was realized via the fabrication techniques we developed in Objective 1 which has led to a unified micro/nanofluidic device with dynamic controllability and novel gradient interface between the microfluidics and nanofluidics. The tunable device design is capable of smoothly interfacing the microchannels for sample loading with the nanochannels for DNA extension, and therefore it can be readily coupled with cell manipulation modules to analyze the genomic DNA extracted directly from single cells. We demonstrated single-cell genomic analysis that integrates the process steps including single cell capture, cell lysis, DNA extraction, purification, and fluorescent labeling, DNA linearization, and sample collection using Hela cells. However, we did not succeed in optical mapping of the epigenetic patterns due to extremely low epigenetic marks in Hela cells.

16217416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16217416.value: (1) We developed novel and advantageous devices having nanochannels suitable for confinement and alignment of DNA molecules (e.g., for single-molecular analysis), as well as methods of fabricating the same and methods of using the same for DNA analysis. The dynamic and tunable confinement of formed nanochannels effectively overcomes the challenges encountered by traditional techniques for nanochannel DNA stretching. By utilizing low-cost multilayer soft lithography and controllable elastomeric collapse, we create a uniform nanochannel array with confining dimension down to 20 nm and length up to submillimeter. Due to the dynamic control, the reversible formation of nanochannels facilitates buffer exchange, sample loading, and surface passivation. More importantly, the inherent gradient structures smoothly interface the nanochannels and the adjoining microchannels, which facilitate the DNA loading at the enhance of the nanochannels. (US Patent US 10,722,888B2, Chinese Patent CN107614675A, Small 2018) (2) By exploiting the unique advantages of the dynamic and tunable confinement, we developed a hybrid micro/nanofluidic device that integrated cell isolation and lysis, DNA extraction, purification, and linearization for single-cell genomic analysis. The dynamic controllability and novel gradient interface between the microfluidics and nanofluidics of our device makes single-cell genomic analysis an entirely integrated and smooth process. As a demonstration of the device, we linearized the chromosomal DNA extracted from a single HeLa cell and performed DNA denaturing mapping in the nanofluidic device. Mbp-long DNA molecules are extracted directly from a single cell and in situ linearized and observed in the nanochannels. This novel platform has great potential for studying cell-to-cell heterogeneity at the genetic level. (Small 2018) (3) For improve the imaging techniques and data analysis for DNA optical mapping, we coupled a multi-color super-resolution imaging microscope with the nanochannel device for super-resolution genome mapping. We first developed fluorescence specific-site labeling of epigenetic DNA modification 5-hmC using the protocol for bulk solutions off-chip. YoYo-1 dye was used to stain the DNA toe reveal the DNA backbone. We further developed an efficient alignment and data analysis method by using the fluorescent barcodes on the DNA backbone as references. By using the fluorescent barcodes on DNA backbone as references, we overcome the thermal fluctuations along the DNA chains both globally and locally. Finally, using molecules DNA extracted from mouse embryonic stem cells as a demonstration, we show that our platform can improve the resolution of optical maps to ~100 bp, providing a promising approach for identifying small genetic differences between DNA molecules. (MicroTAS 2018) (4) Outstanding tasks/issues: in Objectives 2 and 3, our proposed methods for epigenetic optical mapping using DNA molecules extracted from mouse embryonic stem cells or Hela cells was not successful. The fluorescence labeling of 5-hmC protocol we developed allowed us to detect the marks in bulk solutions off-chip. However, we were not able to detect signals from 5-hmC of a single linearized DNA in a nanochannel, probably due to the marks are too sparse and the signals are too weak. We already tried many rounds of optimization of the current protocol but the results were still not satisfactory.

16217416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16217416.value: (1) We have attempted to develop the fluorescence labeling protocol for epigenetic marks of DNA molecules on-chip but the results were not very good mainly because the signals from epigenetic 5-hmC marks of a single linearized DNA in a nanochannel is sparse and weak for detection. Therefore, in future work, fluorescent labels of higher efficiency (e.g., quantum dots) may be tried in combination with a higher intensity optical system to enable the pattern recognition on a single-molecule. (2) Secondly, we have coupled the super-resolution microscopy with the nanochannel device to improve the spatial resolution, This technology has the potential for quick screening of genomic structural variations and telomere length characterization in linearized DNA molecules. Using optical mapping of single DNA molecules, large structural variants (e.g. large deletions, insertions, and duplications) and telomere length can be detected, which may address the problems faced by the sequencing technology which provides short-read sequences but poor accuracy in long sequences. (3) Lastly, the throughput of the current device is rather low for single-molecule analysis. To make the technology practically useful, the throughput has to be sufficiently high. Microfluidic design and fabrication technologies need to be sought for device penalization and integration.

16217416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16217416.value: DNA contains the basic blueprint of almost all living organisms, and understanding the information along the DNA molecules is a crucial topic for biological research and biomedical engineering. However, in the bulk solution, DNA molecules are usually coiled up. Optical mapping that uses direct fluorescence imaging of linearly extended DNA molecules offers an entirely new way to look at the genome: long reads for an individual genome, pattern and location recognition for epigenetic marks, ability to capture repetitive elements, structural variation, or copy number variation in a DNA sequence, all of which are limited by bulk sequencing or microarray technologies. DNA linearization is the prerequisite and critical step in single-molecule DNA analysis. In this project, we developed a low-cost method for fabricating size-tunable nanochannel arrays with a cross-sectional dimension down to 20 nm and length up to submillimeter, exquisitely suitable for linearization of genomic-length DNA molecules. More importantly, a curved edge is generated to smoothly interface the microchannels for single cell manipulation and the nanochannels for DNA linearization. By exploiting the unique advantages of the dynamic and tunable confinement, we developed a hybrid micro/nanofluidic device that integrated cell isolation and lysis, DNA extraction, purification, and linearization for single-cell genomic analysis.

16219216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219216.value: The hybrid micro biochip with combination of microfluidic and surface plasmon resonance (SPP) aspects will be designed and fabricated. Such micro-RNA (miRNA) profiling microfluidic chip on which the hybridization effect of localized surface plasmon resonance (SPP) and miRNA will be realized for ultrasensitive bio-information detection. When a specific miRNA is hybridized to immobilized probe on the chip, the affinity of miRNA molecules change the dielectric properties of reaction surface and results in the shaft of SPP wavelength. This will affect the optical transmission characteristics with variation of incident wavelength. Therefore, by simply measuring the transmission spectrum of the sample in normal direction, the affinity information of miRNA will be easily obtained. Our proposed project is based the novel conjugation of local surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) and locked nucleic acid (LNA) immobilized on substrate and it shows some prominent features including: 1) Integration of LSPR biosensor into microfluidic system for label free on-site monitoring: We will employ our previous experience on convinced nanocrescent (NC) structure arrays with well controlled shapes and locations on the substrate. This can facilitate integration with the microfluidic system. NC is one of the most commonly adopted plasmonic bio/chemical sensors due to the well-tunable LSPR property, highly confined electric field, etc. 2) Utilization of immobilized LNA on gold nanocrescent as plasmonic probes: LNA are novel RNA analogues with an extra bond connected by the 2' oxygen and 4' carbon "locks" on the furanose ring. LNAs probes considerably improve binding affinities and specificity in detecting miRNAs. Unlike previous SPR based methods for the detection of miRNA, which usually need extra aid from cumbersome operation of antibodies, enzymes etc. or expensive instruments like Raman spectroscopy, a combination of LSPR and LNA which essentially eliminates any extra liquid operation out of the chip, thus will tremendously improve chip’s usability.

16219216.label: Realisation of objectives
16219216.value: In this project, we successfully achieved simple microfluidic chips-based portable nucleic analyzer consisting of a high sensitive optical detection system for real-time multiplex fluorescence detections. For the experiment of DNA amplification, we integrated microfluidic chip with micro-heater to realize fast temperature cycling and an associated optical detection system can achieve image catching with dynamic processing property. Using two components, a fully portable and fast microchip based PCR machine for nucleic acid detection within 40 min can be easily realized. We designed and developed a fully portable and fast microchip based PCR for nucleic acid detection. For the good prospects for development of the portable PCR machine, not only technical issues are important, the cost is also vital for a wide and affordable use globally. In particular, we focused our design on microheater and microchip, which could achieve a fast thermal cycling and a low cost production. In particular, we paid more attention to the design of sample and chip loading scheme in order to implement ultimate simplicity of operations and true portability. In the future, our microchip and detection system would be further modified to accomplish a high throughput detection. We believe that our fully portable PCR machine could be suitable for point of care detection to monitor epidemics. Our PCR system shows some unique properties including 1) the microheater incorporated a very sensitive thermosensor, its heating rate can reach up 30degree/second; 2) a very robotic optical detection system with intelligent data analysis system. In our PCR design, all modules were fully integrated into a compact box which could be portably taken to the site for point of care detection. The instrument mainly comprises of heating, optical and electrical modules which were assembled into a compact architecture as well as a touchscreen control display for parameter setting. By use our PCR system for real sample testing, we first conducted a PCR reaction using the large volume microchip (25µL) for a standard test. The sample is β-actin standard DNA template used as control in real time PCR detection and the original copy number of template is known initially. The original template concentration was approximately 3000 copies /µL and was corresponding to 5 fM. We compared the results from our portable machine with commercial real time PCR instrument (BioRad). To avoid the difference in the Ct value setting on different machines, here we defined the Ct value as the cycle when the fluorescence signal had an inflection on the signal curve. According to this definition, we found that Ct value was about 24 cycle the fluorescence intensity was significantly increased thereafter and the no template control (NTC) group did not encounter a signal increase. Compare with the result from the commercial real time PCR machine, where the Ct value is also 24 cycles, showed that at the fM concentration level, our portable and microchip PCR had an exceptional amplification efficiency and specificity and had a comparable performance to the commercial PCR instrument. Furthermore, we continued to dilute the standard sample by a scale of 10 and 100 so that the template concentration becomes 300 copies/µL and 30 copies/µL, and we found that the Ct value was still remarkably coincides with that on the commercial instrument (28 cycles and 32 cycles, respectively). The results are very good impression and its properties are comparable with commercial PCR machines. To solve the inconvenience of PCR reagent delivery and storage via cold chain transportation. The solid state reagent with robastic characters should be employed. In this report, a novel lyophilized mix containing all necessary components for Real-time PCR, and its production method were designed, and the stability tested at different temperatures. Some cryoprotectants and carriers are required to protect the function of the enzyme and primer as much as possible and provide the cake structure. Formulations with polyhydroxy compounds were considered to have the potential of protecting the enzymatic microstructure and functionality of dried mixes during the whole manufacture and cold-free storage. The final products with the selected formulation were able to provide a totally same testing result and sensitivity with the freshly making mix after 210-day storage at 45 ℃, and can maintain this function at room temperature (22.5 ~ 25.5 ℃) for at least 680 days.

16219216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16219216.value: A fully portable and fast microchip-based PCR machine for nucleic acid detection has been developed which consists of a unique silicon-based microheater and microchip. The micro-heater is able to achieve a fast thermal cycling with 30 degree/second temperature raising rate. The microfluidic chips used for DNA amplification reactor can fully sealed at 100C temperature without any leakage of vapor and liquid showing perfect performance. A very robotic optical detection system with intelligent data analysis system has been completed. In this system, all optical component are fully integrated into a adjustable stage which is easily for further modification. The PCR machine could be portably taken to the site for point of care detection. A reliable, dried real-time PCR reagent and its producing process with high-temperature storage character has been successfully developed using lyophilization. From the monitoring results, this reagent can be stored at a room temperature for about 2 years without degrading, thus showing very promising characteristics. Its stability property provides a cold-free reagent and might be used for future diagnostic tests, especially for micro-qPCR experiments. We believe that it will be beneficial to the so-called intelligent home self-diagnosis in the future.

16219216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16219216.value: In future, we plans to equip our microfluidic PCR machine in the a mobile lab which divide the compartment into reagent preparation area, specimen preparation area, and nucleic acid reaction amplification area. The mobile lab will meet the requirements of biosafety level BSL-2 and prevent cross-contamination by controlling the direction of personnel and airflow; equipped with fully automatic nucleic acid extractor and our developed solid-state reagent and other microfluidic chip reactors. Since the utilization of portable PCR machine, the testing results are accuracy comparable to the results of traditional nucleic acid laboratory. In addition, high throughput PCR reactors will be further investigated in order to meet different demands.

16219216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16219216.value: PCR technology is a molecular biotechnology used to amplify specific deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) fragments for the extraction of viral ribonucleic acid (RNA). The speed of temperature change is the key to determining the efficiency of the DNA’s amplification process, meaning that the faster the temperature rises, the shorter the time in which the device can come up with a test result. Unlike conventional large-scale PCR devices which use a semiconductor to heat up test samples, our device uses a silicon-based micro-heater module for such purpose. Owing to a lower thermal mass and higher thermal conductivity, the micro-heater can speed up the temperature rise to around 30℃ per second from an average of 4–5℃ per second in conventional PCR devices, greatly reducing the detection time. Our device is equipped with a microfluidic PCR chip, a portable PCR analyser, a pre-processing instrument, a bioassay chip and a novel coronavirus nucleic acid detection kit. It can be used on-site samples testing.

16219816.label: Project Objectives
16219816.value: We plan to design both exact and fast algorithms for nearby-fit spatial keyword queries when different forms of the cost function of the answer are adopted. Each original nearby-fit spatial keyword query is to return a single object. In some applications, it is interesting to find multiple objects. We plan to study finding multiple objects with two perspectives depending on whether the multiple objects to be returned are distributed over the spatial database. One application of returning multiple objects distributed over the spatial database is that a user moving to a new city wants to have an overview of real estate offers that satisfy his/her needs such as price and square meters. We plan to study this problem and design efficient algorithms for this problem.

16219816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16219816.value: 現今地理文本數據是無處不在，其中每個對象具有一個位置，並與一些關鍵字相關聯。許多基於地理文本數據的查詢，稱為空間關鍵詞查詢，已被提出，這是用它（們）的位置和關鍵字兩方面去優化目標。在該提案中，我們提出了一種新的查詢類型，稱為空間鄰近配合關鍵字查詢（NSKQ），其中，一個最佳的對象不僅基於位置和對象本身的關鍵字，而且考慮附近對象的關鍵字。例如，在找酒店，不僅酒店的位置需要考慮，而且酒店附近對象的關鍵字（例如：商場，餐館和巴士站）也需要考慮。在我們的初步研究中，我們發現，該查詢的計算是昂貴的，並且為了有效地執行查詢，我們開發了一種快速算法，具有近100％的準確度。我們的初步實驗結果表明，我們提出的快速算法只花了一秒返回近100％準確的答案，但確切的算法需要花長達1小時返回答案。 擬建項目旨在用不同的觀點（例如：不同的度量空間和不同有關的問題）有系統性研究空間鄰近配合關鍵字查詢。預期成果包括空間鄰近配合關鍵字查詢的新技術和有系統性的實驗結果來驗證我們的技術。

16219816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16219816.value: The first objective is to design both exact and fast algorithms for nearby-fit spatial keyword queries when different forms of the cost function of the answer are adopted. We designed both exact and approximate algorithms for nearby-fit spatial keyword queries with different forms of the cost functions. The results, done by my PhD student called Victor Junqiu WEI, were published in [J3] and [C7]. We also considered a special form of the spatial database called "terrain" and proposed efficient algorithms in [C1]. In addition to the spatial perspective, we studied how to consider profit [J2], users' preferences [C8, C4, C2, C5] and textual information [C6] to find something users would like to obtain. In [J2], we would like to find some records with the greatest profit. In [C8, C4, C2, C5], we would like to return some records which satisfy users’ preferences. In [C6], based on the textual information, we would like to return some messages or records which match users’ preferences according to the textual information. Some of these papers were done by my PhD student called Minhao JIANG. The second objective is to find multiple objects instead of a single object based on the spatial perspectives. We also designed algorithms to find multiple objects instead of a single object and published the results in [C3, J1]. In particular, we would like to find a set of objects which collectively represent the preference of a user with a generalized form of the cost function such that our proposed model could capture a variety of existing cost functions. These results were done by my PhD student called Harry Kai-Ho CHAN.

16219816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16219816.value: There are further developments of the research studied in this project. Since the problem studied in this project is to study the spatial keyword queries in a mobile environment, it is expected that a lot of mobile app companies are interested in the results of this project and would like to develop their mobile apps based on this technology. In addition, mobile data becomes much larger nowadays. It is interesting to study how our proposed method could handle larger data in a distributed manner (e.g., cloud computing).

16219816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16219816.value: [Nature] Many types of queries based on geo-textual data, termed as spatial keyword queries, have been proposed, which are to find optimal object(s) in terms of both its (their) location(s) and keywords. In this proposal, we propose a new type of query called nearby-fit spatial keyword query (NSKQ), where an optimal object has the smallest cost defined based not only on the location and the keywords of the object itself, but also on those of the objects nearby. For example, in an application of finding a hotel, not only the location of a hotel but also the objects near the hotel (e.g., shopping malls, restaurants and bus stops nearby) might need to be taken into consideration. [Significance and Values] A nearby-fit spatial keyword query can help a user to find an object (e.g., hotel) which satisfies his/her need because s/he would also have preferences on some objects (e.g., shopping malls) nearby the object to be found, which could not be captured by existing spatial keyword queries considering the locations and the keywords of the objects to be found only. The findings of our project are expected to help companies to take our nearby-fit spatial keyword query in consideration for their business to satisfy the need of a user to improve user’s experience.

16222216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16222216.value: Rail projects are often proposed to satisfy the increasing urban travel demand, especially in Asian cities. One important consideration is how to finance them in a sustainable manner. One strategy getting increasing attention is to finance rail projects through joint property development, which ideally may lead to this situation: residents get to enjoy the new rail service, developers make a reasonable return on their investments, and the government addresses the demand without using public funds. Yet this outcome is not automatic, but requires careful planning to strike a thin balance between rail development cost, property development profit, fare revenue, etc. over the long term, under uncertain demand and cost variations. Not only are rail projects expensive, they also involve risks, e.g., cost overrun, project delay, even project failure. Exposing and mitigating the risks of joint rail and housing development (R&HD) is critical. In particular, the delivery of R&HD via public private partnership (PPP) offers a way to balance the risks and returns among partners, hence enhancing its viability. Reviewing the literature, it is surprising to find only a limited number of studies on this topic; particularly lacking are analytical models that produce prescriptive results, e.g. recommending the best partnership to address the uncertainty at hand. To address this gap in the literature, this project has three objectives. The first is to develop an integrated framework for modeling R&HD delivered via PPP. The framework will analytically express the distribution of risks, benefits and costs to each partner according to the specific PPP configuration. The second objective pertains to analyzing the development phasing of R&HD over time, identifying PPP configurations that would be suitable for different types of R&HD. The third objective is to incorporate uncertainty in the analysis, investigating PPP configurations that are more robust to uncertainty, and those that are sensitive to a particular uncertainty. Such an understanding will be critical in managing the risks, facilitating the formation of appropriate PPP for R&HD. To bring this project to fruition, two major advancements are needed. The first is the development of a tractable modeling framework linking PPP configurations and transport and housing development models in an analytical manner, which is capable of producing prescriptive results. The second advancement is to extend the existing models explicitly with the time dimension and uncertainty analysis. To demonstrate this modeling framework, we will apply it to the TKO new town in Hong Kong as a case study. 鐵路項目是被視為有效解決交通需求增長的有效方法，但當中一重要考慮為如何維持該項目的財政穩健性及可持續性。鐵路加物業綜合發展經營成為一個可行的方案，可能令以下三方達致三嬴局面：居民享受新鐵路帶來的方便，發展商賺取相應的利潤，而政府可以在不使用公帑資助的情況下應付新增人口帶來的房屋和交通需求。而這理想結果是需要一個完善的計畫以考慮人口和建設成本的不確定性，以及平衡鐵路建設成本，鐵路票務盈利及物業發展收益等等。 鐵路項目涉及龐大的資金及風險．而當中的風險，包括成本超出預算，工程延誤，會直接影響整個項目的服務水平，甚至令項目未能完成。所以，適當分配和減輕在鐵路加物業綜合發展所涉及的風險是非常重要。其中，公私營界別合作成為一個平衡各持分者利益以及風險的項目發展方法，增加該項目的財政穩健性及可持續性。然而，在鐵路加物業綜合發展計畫中，考慮不穩定的風險，及與公私營界別合作關係的研究遠遠不足。尤其是欠缺模型框架以顯示在人口及建設成本不確性下，不同公私營界別合作的模式的利與弊。 因此，本項目將研究以下三大部份：第一部份是建立一套完善描述在鐵路加物業綜合發展中，運用公私營界別合作模式的整合框架。該框架包含在不同公私營界別合作模式中，各公共機構和私營夥伴的利益，支出及風險分佈。第二部份是分析在不同公私營界別合作模式下，長遠鐵路加物業分階段發展藍圖。第三部份是研究在不確定性下，各個公私營界別合作模式的利與弊，鑒定那一種公私營界別合作模式更有效處理各種不同的不確定性因素。這結果對分配不同程度的風險及利益到各持分者提供重要的指引，指出在鐵路加物業綜合發展中，最適合的公私營界別合作模式。 本研究在兩方面有重大突破：第一是建立了一個詳盡的數理模型框架以連繫公私營界別合作模式及現有的交通和樓宇發展模型。第二個是把時間性及不確定的風險放入框架的考慮因素中，以研究隨著未知的風險中，鐵路加物業的階段發展。本研究將以香港將軍澳新市鎮為案例作模型分析。本研究不但開拓了理論上的課題，亦為提供實際公私營界別合作模式的方案。

16222316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16222316.value: Internet-of-Things (IoT) is an emerging trend which is foreseen to bring about the next wave of semiconductor following the smartphone and broadband wireless communication era. Innovative business models based on interconnected smart sensor nodes, with enhanced features such as machine-to-machine communication, and the Big Data generated from these sensor networks are envisaged. Due to the astronomical number of sensor nodes, minimal battery maintenance is critical to low cost. Energy Harvesting (EH) is a key enabling technology to extend battery-life, or even in some cases, make the IoT sensor node entirely battery-free. To power IoT nodes, energy sources deriving electrical power from solar energy, mechanical vibrations, and heat are available. Each type comes with a different physical size and power (current-voltage) profile. Despite the infinitely available energy from these EH sources, the source impedance is generally high and also highly influenced by environmental changes. Therefore, a critical circuit, called a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) circuit is necessary to constantly condition the EH source, in order to produce the optimum possible power output. Comprehensive MPPT circuits require complex signal processing and current sensing, which are power hungry. For low power solutions, fractional open circuit voltage (FOCV) or hill-climbing approaches using sample-and-hold technique are often implemented. Nevertheless, the power consumption of such solution is still in the microwatts ballpark due to the power hungry op-amp based comparators blocks. Although the scaling of CMOS technologies greatly benefits digital circuits, analog circuits built using advanced CMOS processes such as op-amps suffer several problems such as reduced signal swings and small-signal gain, and poor on-off switch function due to leakage currents, etc. Since the narrowed voltage headroom is the root cause, time-domain signal processing (TDSP) is being considered as an alternate solution to conventional voltage-mode processing techniques. The core idea of TDSP is to utilize controllable delay elements instead of voltage values to represent the signal to be processed. This project explores a novel MPPT circuit using FOCV and the hill-climbing algorithm, based on the TDSP technique, which will further reduce the supply voltage of the MPPT to levels lower than an op-amp based voltage domain solution. This will reduce the microwatt power consumption of current MPPT by at least an order of magnitude, down to the nanowatt level. Prototypes of a DC-DC converter, i.e. inductor-based switching converter and capacitor-based charge pump leveraging on the proposed TD-MPPT circuits, will also be developed. 在智能手機和寬帶無線通信時代之後，物聯網被認為是半導體行業發展的下一個潮流。基於互相連接的智能傳感器節點，未來的商業模式將伴隨著大量的機器間通訊以及這些傳感器網絡產生的大數據。由於這些傳感器節點數量巨大，減少電池的維護需求是降低成本的關鍵。能量收集技術將是延長電池壽命的關鍵技術，甚至可以實現無電池的物聯網傳感器節點。太陽能、機械振動能和熱能都可以被轉化為電能為物聯網節點供電。每種能量的收集器件都有各種尺寸和能量級別的型號。雖然這些能量廣泛存在且無窮無盡，但是這些能量收集器件的阻抗一般很高，而且受周圍環境的影響巨大。因此，為了能在不同的環境狀況下收集到盡可能多的能量，最大能量點追蹤電路是能量收集系統不可或缺的組成部分。廣泛使用的最大能量點追蹤電路一般需要功耗極高的複雜信號處理電路和電流檢測電路。低功耗的解決方案通常採用部分開路電壓採樣法和爬坡算法，一般用採樣保持的方法實現。即使如此，由於基於運算放大器的比較器模塊功耗較高，這些解決方案的功耗仍然在微瓦級的範圍。 雖然CMOS工藝的尺寸縮小使得數字電路部分極大地受益，但是模擬電路部分卻遇到一些問題，比如運算放大器的設計將會遇到信號擺幅以及小信號增益過小的困難，漏電流導致MOS管糟糕的開關特性等等。狹窄的電壓空間是問題的根源所在，於是時域信號處理被認為是傳統電壓模信號處理的替代解決方案。時域信號處理技術的核心是利用可控的延遲單元而不是電壓值來表示被處理的信號。 這個項目將探索一種基於時域信號處理技術的，採用部分開路電壓採樣法和爬坡算法的新型最大能量點追蹤電路。比起基於運算放大器的電壓域解決方案，它能進一步地降低最大能量點追蹤電路的供電電壓。這將使得現有的微瓦級最大能量點追蹤電路的功耗至少降低一個數量級，到達納瓦級。這個項目將開發一個直流-直流變換器，比如包含時域信號處理技術的最大能量點追蹤電路的基於電感的開關變換器或基於電容的電荷泵。

16222316.label: Realisation of objectives
16222316.value: This project is to develop a time-domain control circuit for a microwatt-power energy harvesting system. There are two main tasks to be achieved. The first task is to study how to develop a very low-power time-domain control circuitry (Objectives 1 & 2) and the second task is to study how to develop a better maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithm for the energy harvesting system (Objective 3). In terms of the development of the low-power time-domain control circuitry, we have successfully designed, implemented and tested a low-power boost converter for thermoelectric energy harvesting with time-domain-based MPPT (Objective 4). With the help of the time-domain control circuitry, the boost converter can start up and maintain its operation down to a sub-threshold voltage of 0.3 V, which is the lowest voltage that have ever been reported. This allows the thermoelectric energy harvesting system can still keep harvesting energy with a smaller temperature gradient between two terminals of the thermoelectric generator (TEG). In terms of MPPT algorithm, the conventional approach is to use the fractional open-circuit-voltage (FOCV) with hill-climbing algorithm. During this project, we found this algorithm is not an effective way to control MPPT. We have invented a novel approach to control the MPPT by using a reconfigurable TEG array. Instead of controlling the impedance of the DC-DC converter to match the internal resistance of the TEG, we control the effective impedance of the TEG array to match the load. By using this new approach, we can get higher power conversion efficiency with much wider range of temperature different across the TEGs. This is the widest range of temperature gradient (more than 22 times) that the TEG can achieve higher than 87% power efficiency.
