16222316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16222316.value: In order to make this project success, several novel ideas, algorithms and techniques have been investigated, proposed and developed. Harvesting energy from TEGs with large temperature gradient is obvious and usually with high efficiency. However, in most of practical environment, the temperature gradient is very small, only a few degrees Celsius. Under this condition, most thermoelectric energy harvesting systems fail to harvest any energy from the TEG. Even some of them can harvest energy, but the efficiency is very low (<70%) or can get high efficiency only at certain fixed conditions. Therefore, it is very critical to design low-power and low-voltage circuities such that the thermoelectric energy harvesting system can operate with a very low temperature gradient across its terminals. In this project. we have developed several low power and low voltage circuities for TEG harvesting system. These includes the low-power voltage references, time-domain control circuits and the interface circuits for energy harvesting systems. These results have been published or being under review in top-tier journal and conference in solid-state circuit design [J2], [J3], [J4], [C2] and [C3]. Novel MPPT algorithm using reconfigurable TEG array has also been developed and experimentally proven to have high efficiency over wide temperature range. This concept and implementation have also been published in the prestige journal and conference for solid-state circuit design [J1] and [C1]. These very important findings for TEG harvesting systems.

16222316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16222316.value: In this project, we have studied many low-power low-voltage circuitries and algorithms for thermoelectric energy harvesting systems. This especially the time-domain circuits can lay the foundation for low-power circuit design methodologies. We believe these circuitries and concepts can be extended to other energy harvesting systems, such as piezoelectric energy harvesting systems.

16222316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16222316.value: Energy Harvesting is a key enabling technology to extend battery-life, or even in some cases, make the internet-of-things (IoT) sensor node entirely battery-free. In order to power IoT nodes, energy derived from thermoelectric energy can be used. However, it is not very effective to harvest energy from thermoelectric generator (TEG) with low temperature gradient across the TEG. In this project, ultra-low-power time-domain maximum power point tracking circuits were developed. The outcome of this project allows TEG to harvest sufficient energy under a small temperature gradient such that IoT devices can be entirely battery-free and receive sufficient energy from the TEG in many different environments.

16222716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16222716.value: We propose to launch a full-spectrum study of security problems that arise in both theoretical analysis and practical implementation of cyber-physical systems. The lack of a unified security-aware control-theoretic framework has limited the development of practical applications. In CPSs, malicious agents can launch cyber attacks aiming at damaging the data availability, integrity and confidentiality, and degrade system performance to the maximum extent at the same time. Although some preliminary works have studied the two widely encountered attacks, the Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks and the integrity attacks, some unsolved problems and challenges cannot be ignored: 1) existing works on DoS attacks mainly concentrate on one-side analysis, i.e., either from the viewpoint of the system or from the attacker. Two-sided decision-making analysis is rare; 2) some simple game-theoretical approaches are proposed to handle the interaction between the system and the attacker, but the strong assumption that the attacker has full knowledge of the system parameters, the strategy space and the previous action history, poses some limitations; 3) existing models of deception integrity attacks are relatively simple, mainly focusing on static parameter estimation. It is necessary to analyze the consequences of such attacks on a dynamic system. To address these challenging problems, we propose to design a novel security-aware control framework which is able to detect and attenuate the consequences of cyber attacks, mainly based on control-theoretic, information-theoretic, and game-theoretic tools. The deliverables after the completion of this project include: 1) a unified security-aware control framework which shall allow one to model the ability of each component (e.g., the attackers, the sensors, and the controllers), and to consider the interaction between the attacker and the system; 2) a comprehensive analysis of worst-case system performance under typical physical and cyber attacks; 3) a set of estimation, intrusion detection and control algorithms as counter-measures to these attacks. Our initial research results in this direction have enhanced our understanding of critical security issues arise in CPSs and have demonstrated that our approach is feasible. Moreover, we expect the deliverable results will enrich the literature as well as provide various tools for practitioners to use. 我們提議在信息物理系統的理論和應用所衍生的安全問題上展開廣泛的研究。現時缺少一個具有安全意識的控制系統框架，而因此限制了實際應用的發展。一個惡意攻擊者能夠藉着對數據的可用性、可靠性和保密性的攻擊於系統性能帶來最大的破壞。雖然現在已對兩大攻擊類別（阻斷服務攻擊和數據完整性攻擊）有初步的研究，但是我們不能忽略仍然存在的問題和挑戰：1）現有工作都是從系統的角度或攻擊者的角度作單方面分析。雙面決策分析是罕見； 2）系統和攻擊者的關係可以博弈論作簡單的描述，但會假設了攻擊者具有系統參數、策略集合及策略歷史的完整知識，而這些強假設會對研究產生局限；3）現時數據完整性攻擊只有比較簡略，主要關乎靜態參數估計的模型。所以有必要研究數據完整性攻擊對動態系統的後果。為了面對這幾個挑戰，我們提議要設計一個有安全意識的控制模型，能以使用控制、資訊及博弈理論的工具偵察並減弱網絡攻擊帶來的破壞。這個項目完結時能预期的成果包括：1）一個可以模擬系統組件功能又具有安全意識的控制框架；2）一個在網絡物理攻擊下最壞情況的全面分析；3）一套對付攻擊的估計、入侵偵察和控制的算法。我們這方面的初步研究結果已經令我們對信息物理系統帶來的安全問題有更深的認識，亦證明我們研究方法的可行性。此外，我們期望所發表的結果能增加文獻和研究工具的豐富性。

16222716.label: Realisation of objectives
16222716.value: We have made excellent progress with this funding. Following the original objectives of the project, we have successfully investigated cyber-physical system security from a control-theoretic point of view. For a number of different application scenarios such as remote estimation and networked control, we evaluated the system performance under typical cyber attacks (including data integrity attacks, denial-of-service attacks, replay attacks, etc.). We proposed novel state estimation, intrusion detection and control algorithms as counter-measures to these attacks. We further analyzed the security and system performance tradeoff. In addition to the original objectives, we have successfully applied the developed tools to other areas such as multi-sensor Kalman filtering, randomized consensus, etc. The results are fruitful which are summarized and published in 8 leading prestigious international journals (five published in the IEEE-TAC and one in Automatica) and 2 leading international conferences. One PhD students are trained during the project period.

16222716.label: Major findings and research outcome
16222716.value: We have conducted a full-spectrum and thorough study of cyber-physical systems security from a control-theoretic angle with applications to remote estimation, multi-sensor filtering, nonlinear filtering, etc. We have fully met the original project objectives and achieved more which is beyond our expectation. The major finding is that security issues in a cyber-physical system cannot be tackled seperately using information-theoretic and encryption methods alone. The dynamics of the underlying system has to be considered as the same time. Otherwise, the system performance may be degraded or even the system becomes unstable under certain carefully designed cyber-attacks. The main research outcomes include publications in 8 leading international journals and 2 leading international conferences as well as training of one PhD student.

16222716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16222716.value: The research outcomes are fruitful and paved the way for a number of exciting future research directions including extensions to general nonlinear systems security, other types of cyber-attacks, better tradeoff analysis, etc.

16222716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16222716.value: We provided a thorough analysis of the system performance under malicious attacks and proposed corresponding effective well-designed countermeasures. Some novel security-aware control frameworks are proposed which are able to detect and attenuate the consequences of cyber attacks based on control-theoretic tools. The developed research results in this project have enhanced our understanding of critical security issues arise in CPSs. These results will not only enrich the theoretical results in cyber-physical security but also contribute to their practical applications, for example, they would be of major strategic relevance to local industries which use CPSs in a networked environment that may encounter malicious attacks.

16222916.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16222916.value: 电召如何重塑出租车行业？

16222916.label: Project Objectives
16222916.value: To develop a new customer-taxi meeting function with e-hailing and model the demand and supply equilibrium of the taxi market under hybrid modes of e-hailing and roadside hailing and under given price and entry regulations. To determine the e-hailing pricing strategy of a single monopoly platform and examine the pricing competition in a duopoly of platforms, and thus look into the impacts of pricing competition on the two-sided taxi market. To analyze optimal governmental regulations in terms of entry restriction and price control in the taxi market under hybrid modes of e-hailing and roadside hailing, and examine the impacts of the e-hailing platforms on the social optimum and government regulation.

16222916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16222916.value: With the fast development of smart mobile and wireless communication techniques, various taxi hailing applications have emerged in recent years. They effectively mitigate information asymmetry and uncertainty between customers and taxi drivers; therefore they have great potential in improving the taxi market efficiency in terms of service quality and taxi utilization. However, while some people enjoy the convenient e-hailing mode, some others are complaining about the deteriorating roadside hailing experience. This has sparked extensive public and media discussion about the necessity of regulation over e-hailing platforms, especially the pricing strategies. In a two-sided taxi market, the pricing scheme of e-hailing platforms in terms of their respective charge rate on taxi drivers and customers plays an important role in determining customers and taxi drivers’ service mode choices between e-hailing and roadside hailing. The mode choice of customers and taxi drivers governs their waiting/searching time of each service mode. The customers and taxi drivers’ waiting/searching time of the two modes in turn influences their mode choices. It is thus of immense interest to examine the impact of e-hailing platforms and their service pricing strategies on the whole taxi industry. This project is proposed to examine the pricing strategies of e-hailing platform operators under different market structures and look into the desirable regulatory regimes for the taxi industry with e-hailing. The first part of the project will develop the new customer-taxi meeting function with e-hailing and examine the demand and supply equilibrium in the presence of hybrid modes of e-hailing and roadside hailing and under given price and entry regulations. The second part will determine the e-hailing pricing strategy of a single monopoly platform and examine the pricing competition in a duopoly of platforms in the two-sided taxi market. The third part of the project will determine the socially optimal taxi fleet size, taxi fare, and platform service charge in the two-sided taxi market and thus set up optimal governmental regulations for achieving the social optimum. Given the recent popularity of taxi hailing apps, and the public debates about the impacts of e-hailing platforms, the proposed research is of great importance in both theory and practice. Besides enhancing our understanding of the taxi market with growing e-hailing applications, the results of the project will help e-hailing platform operators determine pricing strategies and assist the public sector in understanding how the e-hailing platform will benefit the taxi drivers, customers and society as a whole. 摘要 随着智能移动终端和无线通讯网络的普及，各种打车应用近年来如雨后春笋般涌现。它们有效减少了乘客和出租车司机之间的信息不对称性和不确定性；因而对提升出租车市场效率（包括服务质量和使用率）有巨大潜力。然而，电召给一些人带来方便的同时，扬招的用户体验却逐渐恶化。公众媒体也展开广泛讨论，呼吁对电召平台，尤其是它们的定价策略进行监管。 在一个双边出租车市场中，电召平台的定价方案，即平台对司机和乘客的各自收费标准，对用户在电召和扬招之间的服务模式选择扮演重要角色。不同的模式选择，决定了不同的乘客候车时间和司机空驶时间。两种模式下的乘客候车时间和司机空驶时间反过来又影响他们在电召和扬招间的选择。因此研究电召平台及其定价策略对整个出租车行业的影响具有广泛前景。 本课题计划考察电召平台在不同市场结构下的定价策略，并且探寻理想的含电召的出租车市场的监管机制。项目的第一部分会定义含电召模式下的新的乘客-出租车相遇函数，同时明确在给定价格和进入规则下，混招模式下的供需均衡。第二部分会给出单一垄断平台下的电召定价策略，并延伸讨论双头垄断平台下的价格竞争。第三部分会确定系统最优下双边出租车市场的出租车总量、打车费用和平台服务收费，进而设定最优的政府监管以实现社会最优。 鉴于近期打车应用的广泛流行，以及公众对电召平台影响的争论，本研究在理论和实践中都会有重要作用。除了更好理解随打车应用而不断发展的出租车市场，该研究成果还能协助电召平台服务商确定定价策略，帮助监管者制定监管方案，让我们充分地认识电召平台如何重塑出租车行业，整体优化社会资源配置。

16222916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16222916.value: 1. We developed a general framework of the E-hailing taxi and ride-sourcing systems and various cost-sharing strategies in a ride-sharing market. We found that when driving alone is faster but more expensive than public transit, no cost-sharing strategy exists to sustain an active ridesharing platform without inducing transit users to join the ridesharing program. Publications: Wang, H., Yang, H., 2019. E-hailing ride-sourcing systems: a framework and review. Transportation Research Part B: Methodological, Vol.129, 122-155. 2. We investigated customers’ order cancellation behavior using actual taxi service and ride-sourcing data, and formulated the order cancellation behavior as a function of customer waiting time and the platform’s penalty strategy for cancellation, and established a system of nonlinear equations to depict the complex interactions between the ride-sourcing and taxi markets. It was found that the proposed model replicated the order cancellation behavior well, and was useful for designing appropriate penalty strategies for order cancellation. Publications: Wang, X., Liu, W., Yang, H., Wang, D., Ye, J., 2020. Customer behavioral modelling of order cancellation in coupled ride-sourcing and taxi markets. Transportation Research Part B: Methodological, Vol.132, 358-378. 3. We developed hexagon-based convolutional neural networks (H-CNN) for predicting the short term supply-demand of taxi and ride-sourcing services. Validated by a 3-week real world ride-sourcing dataset in China, the H-CNN models were found to significantly outperform the benchmark algorithms in terms of accuracy and robustness. Publications: Ke, J., Yang, H., Zheng, H., Chen, X., Jia, Y., Gong, P., Ye, J., 2019. Hexagon-based convolutional neural network for supply-demand forecasting of ride-sourcing services. IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transport Systems, Vol.20, No.11, 4160-4173. 4. We analyzed multi-modal commute behavior with ride-pooling programs as both feeders and competitors to public transit. We found that a significant number of public transit passengers will shift to long-distance ride-pooling services under low fare ratios; and a high ride-pooling priority can lead to a demand drawback for long-distance ride-pooling, which raises public transit ridership. We also found that a win–win condition can be reached through a separated discount strategy for first- and last-mile ride-pooling services. Publications: Zhu, Z., Qin, X., Ke, J., Zheng, Z., Yang, H., 2020. Analysis of multi-modal commute behavior with feeding and competing ridesplitting services. Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice. Vol.132, 713-727.

16222916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16222916.value: The following development of the research is of interest and being explored: 1) Shareability, traffic congestion, and operational strategies in a ride-sourcing market; 2) Passengers willingness to wait and choice of bundled (ride-pooling and non-ride-pooling) options in ride-sourcing markets; 3) Matching frictions and platform integration in competitive ride-sourcing markets.

16222916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16222916.value: The impacts of e-hailing platforms to the taxi industry are highly dependent on the pricing strategies of the platform operators. In a two-sided market connecting customers and taxi drivers, the transaction-based pricing scheme of an e-hailing platform operator is usually composed of its respective charging rates on customers and taxi drivers for each e-hailing order. The structure of an e-hailing pricing scheme plays an important role in determining customers and taxi drivers’ service mode choices between e-hailing and roadside hailing, which governs the matching efficiency of each service mode. The matching efficiency of the two service modes in turn influences customers and taxi drivers’ mode choices. Given the complex and intriguing interactions between the two modes, it is possible for an e-hailing platform to gain substantial profit by the deterioration of the alternative roadside hailing mode. To understand how such e-hailing apps are reshaping the taxi industry, this study developed a general modeling framework with a focus on the pricing strategies of the platform operators. The impacts of e-hailing pricing strategies on the whole taxi market efficiency were analyzed under different market conditions. Apart from enhancing the public’s understanding of the taxi industry with e-hailing, this project also helped the development of the e-hailing platforms and provided a theoretical basis for the government to establish an appropriate regulatory regime for ensuring a positive role of the e-hailing platforms.

16223116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16223116.value: Nowadays many banks and financial institutions actively offer asset loan services collateralized by various assets, including assets with holding cost such as gold and assets incurring profits such as dividend-paying stocks. Asset loans have gained great popularity among investors because with more convenient application procedures than traditional loans, they are especially appropriate for the customers in urgent need of funds who are reluctant to completely lose the assets, and moreover, they can serve as hedging instruments against a decline in underlying asset prices. Accordingly, the problem of determining rational values of the service fee, the loan amount, and the loan interest rate has attracted much attention from both practitioners and researchers throughout the world, including Hong Kong -- one of the leading international financial centers. To address this important issue, a crucial step is to study the valuation problem of asset loans, which is essentially a problem of pricing a special American call option with a negative dividend and a negative interest rate for loans with assets incurring holding cost (gold-like loans), or that with a positive dividend and a negative interest rate for loans with assets incurring profits (stock-like loans). Although there has been a large body of research on the pricing of stock-like loans, only few studies dealt with gold-like loans, and even then, they were focused on the Black-Scholes model (BSM) without considering jump risk. It is worth pointing out that the continuation region for the gold-like loan pricing problem includes two separate regions rather than one single region for stock-like loans. Moreover, interestingly, gold-like loans pricing with jump risk would be significantly different from that under the BSM because asset prices with jumps can jump from one continuation region to the other before the optimal stopping time. In this project, we will propose analytical pricing methods for both infinite- and finite-maturity gold-like loans under a flexible hyper-exponential jump diffusion model (HEM), which is a generalization of the BSM and the double-exponential jump diffusion model and can be applied to approximate many important option pricing models such as CGMY, VG and NIG models. Specifically, under the HEM we shall attempt to derive a closed-form expression for the infinite-maturity gold-like loan price by solving the associated optimal stopping problem explicitly and to obtain an analytical approximation to the finite-maturity gold-like loan price by transforming the pricing problem into an approximate solvable free boundary problem. 当今很多银行和金融机构提供以各种资产作为抵押的资产贷款服务，这些抵押资产既包括具有持有成本的资产，比如黄金，也包括能够产生收益的资产，比如付红利股票。资产贷款的申请流程比传统贷款更加方便，它们特别适合那些急需贷款但又不愿意完全失去资产所有权的客户。另外，资产贷款还可以用来对冲资产价格下跌的风险。这些优点使得资产贷款深受投资者欢迎。因此，如何确定合理的服务费，贷款金额和贷款利息成为包括世界金融中心之一香港在内的全世界从业者和研究人员共同关心的问题。 解决这一问题的关键是研究资产贷款的定价问题，这个问题本质上是要对一种特殊的美式看涨期权进行定价。具体来说，对于以具有持有成本的资产作抵押的贷款（比如以黄金作抵押的贷款），相应的美式看涨期权具有负的红利和负的利率，而对于以能够产生收益的资产作抵押的贷款（比如以付红利股票作抵押的贷款），相应的美式看涨期权具有正的红利和负的利率。尽管已经有很多文献对后一种情况进行研究，对前一种情况的研究还很少，而且现有的研究主要集中在Black-Scholes模型而没有考虑跳跃风险。 值得指出的是对于以具有持有成本的资产作抵押的贷款，相应定价问题的继续域包含两个分开的区域，而不像以能够产生收益的资产作抵押的贷款，其相应定价问题的继续域只包含一个单独的区域。另外，有趣的是跳跃风险下以具有持有成本的资产作抵押的贷款的定价问题和Black-Scholes模型下的相应的资产贷款的定价问题非常不同。这是因为在跳跃风险下资产价格在最优停时之前可以从继续域的一个区域跳到继续域的另一个区域。 在这个项目中，我们将要对超指数跳跃扩散模型下无限期限和有限期限两种情形下的具有持有成本的资产贷款给出解析定价的方法。超指数跳跃扩散模型是Black-Scholes模型和双指数跳跃扩散模型的推广，可以用来逼近许多重要的期权定价模型，比如CGMY，VG和NIG模型。具体来说，在超指数跳跃扩散模型下，我们将尝试通过解相应的最优停时问题来得到无限期限的具有持有成本的资产贷款的显式定价公式，对于有限期限的情形，我们将尝试把相应的定价问题转化成一个近似的可解的自由边界问题，从而得到显式逼近的定价公式。

16223116.label: Realisation of objectives
16223116.value: In this project, I have achieved the project objectives by solving the pricing problems of infinite-maturity and finite-maturity asset loans with holding cost under the hyper-exponential jump diffusion model (HEM). More specifically, we first consider the pricing problem of infinite-maturity asset loans under general exponential Levy models, which include the HEM as a special case; in two special cases where the model parameters satisfy certain conditions, we have solved the related optimal stopping problems completely and have derived closed-form expressions for the infinite-maturity asset loan prices. Then we consider the HEM in the general case where the model parameters do not satisfy the aforementioned conditions. In the general case and under the double-exponential jump diffusion model (DEM), a very important special case of the HEM, we have obtained a closed-form pricing formula for the infinite-maturity asset loan by solving the associated optimal stopping problem explicitly and by showing that the optimal stopping time is the first hitting time that a modified return process enters a finite, closed interval. An important step is that we propose an integral equation approach to deriving a closed-form expression for the generalized moment generating function of the first hitting time for the hyper-exponential jump diffusion process to enter a finite, closed interval. In the general case and under the general HEM, since the above method for the DEM no longer applies, we have developed an iterative pricing method for the infinite-maturity asset loans, which involves a sequence of simple optimal stopping problems having closed-form value functions that converge to the infinite-maturity asset loan price. Numerical results indicate that our pricing method is accurate and efficient. For finite-maturity asset loans, we have obtained an analytical approximation pricing formula under the HEM by solving a related approximate free boundary problem explicitly. Moreover, we have also proposed a unified approach to pricing the infinite-maturity stock loans under general regime-switching exponential Levy models by studying the related regime classification. Applying this unified approach, we have derived analytical solutions to the infinite-maturity stock loan prices under the general exponential Levy models without regime switching and the regime-switching phase-type jump diffusion models. In addition, we have provided a unified framework to obtain closed-form expressions for some important quantities related to the first passage time of the reflected hyper-exponential jump diffusion process.

16223116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16223116.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are detailed as follows. Under general exponential Levy models, which include the hyper-exponential jump diffusion model (HEM) as a special case, we have derived closed-form expressions for the infinite-maturity asset loan prices in two special cases where the model parameters satisfy certain conditions. Then we consider the HEM in the general case where the model parameters do not satisfy the aforementioned conditions. In the general case and under the double-exponential jump diffusion model (DEM), a very important special case of the HEM, we have obtained a closed-form pricing formula for the infinite-maturity asset loan by solving the related optimal stopping problem explicitly and by deriving a closed-form expression for the generalized moment generating function of the first hitting time for the hyper-exponential jump diffusion process to enter a finite, closed interval. In the general case and under the general HEM, we have developed an accurate and efficient iterative pricing method for infinite-maturity asset loans. An analytical approximation pricing formula for finite-maturity asset loans has also been obtained under the HEM. Moreover, a unified regime classification method has been proposed to derive analytical solutions to the infinite-maturity stock loan prices under the general exponential Levy models without regime switching and the regime-switching phase-type jump diffusion models. In addition, we have also developed a unified approach to obtaining closed-form expressions for some important quantities associated with the first passage time of the reflected hyper-exponential jump diffusion process.

16223116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16223116.value: In this project, we have solved the pricing problems of infinite-maturity and finite-maturity asset loans with holding cost under the hyper-exponential jump diffusion model (HEM). Potential future research problems might include the study of pricing infinite-maturity and finite-maturity asset loans with holding cost under more general Markov process models. This problem is expected to be more difficult due to the model complexity. A potential approach might be to derive analytical approximations to the asset loan prices by constructing a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) to approximate the target Markov process model and by solving the pricing problems analytically under the approximate CTMC.

16223116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16223116.value: Asset loans collateralized by various assets, including assets with holding cost such as gold, have gained great popularity among investors, and the related pricing problems have become increasingly important. However, it is very challenging to price asset loans if jump risk is taken into account. In this project, we have solved the pricing problems of infinite-maturity and finite-maturity asset loans with holding cost under the hyper-exponential jump diffusion model (HEM), which is a generalization of the celebrated Black-Scholes model and the double-exponential jump diffusion model. Theoretically, to the best of our knowledge, our project provides one of the first approaches to solving the pricing problems of infinite-maturity and finite-maturity asset loans with holding cost under a popular jump diffusion model with two-sided jumps. In practice, our results can be used to determine rational values of the practically important quantities involved in the asset loan services, including the service fee, the loan amount, and the loan interest rate, when the market is exposed to jump risk.

16225316.label: Project Objectives
16225316.value: To build up appropriate mathematical models to describe the process of real-time service matching. Our plan includes single-period and multiple-period models. We have already had some ideas on the models, and need to further validate these models. To study the single-period problem. Our preliminary study shows the computational difficulty of the problem. Due to the practical need, we need to design real-time heuristic algorithms. We also plan to design offline optimal algorithms, which may provide insights for designing heuristics, as well as benchmark the heuristics. To study the multiple-period problem. Based on the results from the single-period problem, we then study how to solve the multiple-period problem. More importantly we will look for general managerial insights and guidance. Besides the optimization algorithms, we also develop a simulation model to validate the optimization results. To explore other extensions. We can extend our research to other decisions, in particular, pricing. We plan to study two possible pricing decisions that are coupled closely with operations, how to provide a subsidy to attract more participation, and how to surge price to balance supply and demand.

16225316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16225316.value: This project is motivated by the operations of some new business models under the umbrella of the sharing economy. In recent years, the sharing economy has attracted a lot of research interest in different academic fields such as economics, social science, and legal studies. However, there is not much published work from the OR/OM society, despite the emergence of different operations in these new business models. This project will take an initiative to explore such new operations models. While the concept of the sharing economy is broad, we focus on one class of model where individuals can use their own resources to provide services to other people. Both service providers and consumers rely on an intermediate platform to match each other. When the service matching needs to be done in real time, such as getting a car on Uber, the operations success heavily depends on whether the platform can effectively facilitate the matching. The challenge for service matching is due to the relationship between the platform and service providers. The platform has the demand information from consumers but no physical resources to provide services; the service providers own the resources but not the demand information. As independent decision makers, the interests of the platform and service providers are unaligned, even service providers competing with each other for consumer demand. The process is dynamic with continuously arriving consumer demands and changing availability of service providers. In general, the platform plays a leading role in the process, by strategically releasing demand information to service providers, and by awarding a service request to one bidding service provider. While a platform can make these two decisions by some simple rule of thumb, our preliminary studies show that there is substantial room for improvement by optimization. In this project we aim to build up a mathematical model to describe the decision process of the platform, and develop effective algorithms to optimize the decisions. Besides its practical potential, this project also contributes to optimization theory by introducing a class of new problems. For example, traditionally service matching in its simplest form can be modeled as bipartite matching, a classic optimization model. Our problem maintains the same bipartite structure, but another third party is involved with decisions becoming how to release information. This may motivate us to reexamine other optimization models when the process relies on an intermediate controlling the information release. 本项目源于共享经济范畴中的若干新型运作模式。近年来共享经济快速发展，成为了学术界不同领域的研究对象，例如经济学，社会学，法学等等。但是共享经济在运作管理层面还没有得到充分的研究。本项目将开拓这一未知领域。 共享经济的概念十分广泛，我们将专注于其中一类模式：每个个人可以利用自己的资源为他人提供服务，所有服务提供者和服务消费者通过一个公共平台进行服务匹配。这类模式的成功与否在很大程度上取决于公共平台如何进行服务匹配。 服务匹配的难点在于公共平台与服务提供者的相对独立性。服务平台掌握需求信息，但不能直接控制服务提供者，他们是有着不同利益的独立决策者。与此同时，服务提供者之间也存在竞争关系，使问题变得更为复杂。 简单地讲，公共平台在这个系统中处于主动地位，其功能包括需求信息的发布和服务匹配。初步研究发现，这两个决策的优化可以极大地提升系统性能。本项目将利用数学建模和优化技术来研究这些问题。 本项目的理论贡献在于发现了一类新的优化问题。经典的服务匹配问题都是基于二部匹配模型，假设信息全部公开。在我们的问题里，有一个第三方控制了信息的发放，从而改变了优化模型的结构。这个新的模型在其它涉及信息发布的问题中有潜在的应用。

16225316.label: Realisation of objectives
16225316.value: This project has four objectives. We have achieved all of them, which are summarized as follows. The first objective is to build up appropriate mathematical models which can capture the unique features of independent service providers. This objective is the foundation to support the achievement of other three decision making objectives, and its realization is shown in several research outputs. In Research Output Item 8.3, we consider the basic challenge in handling multiple independent service providers, i.e., each supplier has a preference or availability to a particular demand request, which is unknown to the decision maker. We show that we, by modeling the randomness of the suppliers’ participation and capability, can effectively handle this situation in multi-stage service matching. In Research Output Item 8.1, we further address the risk aversion attitude of the competing suppliers. In Research Output Item 8.2, we study the case of combination of suppliers, where one demand request needs multiple service activities, and the service qualities depend on the selection as well as the sequencing of the selected activities. The second objective is to study the single period service matching problem, i.e., how to respond to a single demand request. We first study the problem by formulating a stochastic optimization problem and developed some solution properties. This is presented in an international conference (Research Output Item 9.1). Following that, we have further extended the project scope by studying not only the selection of suppliers, but also the sequencing effect of the selected services. Specifically, we consider the fact that, in some situations, for a given request which needs multiple service activities, the quality of the services delivered to the request depends on the joint effect of selected activities and the sequence of arranging such service activities. We developed an algorithm to optimize this process and find some interesting managerial insights. For example, it is not always the best to choose services with higher utility. The main result of achieving this objective is reported in Research Output Item 8.2. The third objective is to study multiple-stage service matching with dynamically arrived requests. We build a sequential stochastic resource allocation model which captures the unique features of the independent suppliers. With a specific application of crowd sourcing, we propose a dynamic control policy to decide how to intervene the suppliers’ participation to the requests. We show that our policy consistently outperforms the current practices. We also found some important managerial guidance. For example, it is not always true that we should put more resources (service suppliers) for high valued requests, which is counter-intuitive. We also show that our policy can leverage high market volatility to gain extra reward. Our model can further be used to evaluate some strategy decisions such as market share expansion and firm merging and acquisition. We have presented the above results at an International conference (Research Output Item 9.2). One paper is under major revision with POMS (Research Output Item 8.3). The fourth objective is to explore extensions, especially issues related to supply side pricing and subsidy. In doing the project, we have already addressed both issues in our model of multiple-stage service matching with dynamically arrived requests (One section of Research Output Item 8.3). We can evaluate the impact of such pricing decisions on the suppliers’ participation willingness. Furthermore, we also explore how risk attitude may impact a supplier’s decision. Specifically, we consider the risk aversion suppliers and study how they make their decisions on pricing and quality design, which may lead to even stronger level of risk aversion. This result is published in Research Output Item 8.1. In summary, we have successfully achieved all four objectives. This project has led to three journal papers (one published in Omega, one under minor revision with MSOM, and one under major revision with POM), and two conference presentations. One Ph.D. student has been trained through the project.

16225316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16225316.value: This project aims to study how to manage multiple independent suppliers in the context of crowdsourcing and sharing economy. The key problem to address is to match suppliers to demands under unpredictable supply capacity due to supplier’s independence. We have studied both single period and multiple period problems. The main results can be summarized as follows. In the single period problem, we consider the situation in which a single demand request needs multiple service activities and the quality of the services delivered to the request depends on the joint effect of selected activities and the sequence of arranging such service activities. Empirical literature shows an ideal sequence often entails an interior peak; that is, the peak (i.e., highest-utility) activity is placed neither at the beginning nor the end of the package. Theoretic literature, by contrast, advocates placing the peak activity either at the beginning or the end. Our paper bridges this gap by developing a theory accounting for interior peaks. We developed an algorithm to optimize this process and derived structural properties of the optimal schedule. Our research also provides implications for activity selection by showing the optimal portfolio may consist of activities with the highest and lowest utility values, but not those with medium values. In the multiple period problem, we consider a specific type of crowdsourcing in which a platform utilizes independent professionals, such as designers, to conduct projects of creative work. Typically, clients submit project requests stochastically to a platform which has a pool of registered creators (e.g., designers). In practice, some platforms may control the process by specifying a maximum number of designers working on a particular project. This raises the question about how a platform may be benefited from such a control. We tackle the problem by constructing a stochastic sequential allocation model and analyzing the properties of the optimal control policy. Our study reveals a number of managerial insights. In particular, the advantage of our optimal policy may be increasing with the number of available designers, even though the intuition is that the control is more important with fewer number of designers. We show that the optimal policy may follow an inverted U-shape function of the project value. In addition, the optimal policy may generate higher rewards by taking advantage of market volatility, and it is applicable even if the objective shifts between profit maximization and market share expansion.

16225316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16225316.value: We still have two papers under review. One is under minor revision with Manufacturing and Service Operations Management. The other is under major revision with Production and Operations Management. We will continue working on these two papers for their final acceptance.

16225316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16225316.value: In the past decade, we have witnessed the emergence of many new business models, under the umbrella of crowd sourcing and sharing economy. Eventually the successful adoption and long term sustainability of these new models rely on the support from daily operations. At the operational level, an essential problem is how to match supply and demand. The nature of crowd sourcing and sharing economy, i.e., using services from diversified independent suppliers, determines that the supplying capacity is difficult to control because the suppliers have individual interests, and are not always reliable. Such dynamics and uncertainty brings new challenges to operations management. This project has addressed such challenges by using mathematical modeling, optimization, and game theory. On the completion of the project, we have developed supplying resource allocation models and policies for a specific type of crowd sourcing platforms to manage the supply side. Based on that, we have further derived a few principles for the management of suppliers in more general applications, which provides managerial insights and guidance to participating suppliers, entrepreneurs, and policy makers.

16227016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16227016.value: Ba在La取代的BaFeO3中的偏析：原位和非原位的表征及计算模拟。

16227016.label: Project Objectives
16227016.value: To study the mechanism of Ba segregation in Ba1-xLaxFeO3. The effect of strain, thermal treatment, and surface treatment on the relative Ba enrichment will be investigated experimentally both ex and in situ. To develop a mathematical model that describes Ba segregation in Ba1-xLaxFeO3. The model will include mechanical effects and interactions among the defects and will be verified by an extensive set of experiments. To study the characteristics of Ba1-xLaxFeO3 surfaces in a morphologically well-defined setting using thin films made by PLD. The evolution of the morphology and composition of the films’ surface will be monitored using XPS and operando techniques. To develop an atomic-level understanding of Ba segregation in Ba1-xLaxFeO3. Ab-initio simulations will be carried out and surface phase diagram, density of states, and segregation energetics will be computed and benchmarked against the experimental results.

16227016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16227016.value: 电力生产的可持续发展是人类最紧迫的问题之一。清洁高效技术的发展将是解决这一挑战的关键。固体氧化物燃料电池（SOFC）在这里将起到关键作用，因为它们都远比传统燃烧系统可持续。此外，固体氧化物燃料电池还拥有燃料灵活性，低排放和高效率的特点，甚至在10kW的规模下可达到70％的效率。 尽管他们拥有明确的前景，固体氧化物燃料电池在经济上还不可行，因为材料和部件在高温（800℃以上）操作条件下成本太高。温度降低至500-800℃的范围将降低系统成本与该材料的降解速率。然而，它也将导致输出功率的下降。这种性能上的下降与传统阴极材料表现不佳紧密相连。因此，发展高效的阴极材料是固体氧化物燃料电池技术可行性的关键。 虽然Co基阴极材料是SOFC中最常用的，但是由于Fe的低成本和Fe基材料较低的热膨胀系数，出现了Fe基阴极。特别是，Ba1-xLaxFeO3-δ（BLF）已经显示出与最好Co基材料可比拟的性能。然而，在运行期间，Ba趋于朝BLF的表面迁移，显著影响了阴极的电催化性能。因此理解表面偏析的机理至关重要。然而，这种Ba的富集机理依然知之甚少。特别是，该过程的动力学与该材料的化学计量，操作时间，应变状态和可能的表面处理之间的关系仍是未知数。本项目建议进行系统的实验和计算研究，旨在解开Ba在BLF中偏析的机理。 BLF样品将以薄膜的形式进行研究，以避免在SOFC领域中通常使用的粉末样品的形貌复杂性。该BLF薄膜将被沉积在各种不同的基底上，以研究应变对Ba的偏析的影响。Ba的浓度和样品的形态演变将由原位和非原位的方法跟踪。此外，该材料的性能演变将被作为时间，施加温度，和氧的分压的函数来研究。初步结果表明表面处理可以阻碍Ba的偏析，我们还将探索通过原子层沉积（ALD）直接在薄膜表面沉积一层薄薄的ZrO2的影响。实验结果会通过连续模拟来辅助解释，旨在了解Ba偏析的物理性质。除此之外，密度泛函理论计算将被进行，以确定Ba偏析过程中的热力学。 综上所述，提议的工作将加强我们对Ba偏析机理，尤其对BLF中Ba偏析机理的认识。该项目计划利用脉冲激光沉积系统研究温度，应变，和表面处理的影响，结合连续和原子模拟来了解Ba偏析的物理基础。这一申请的成功对于改善这一充满前景的SOFC阴极材料将是一个重大的飞跃，本申请也会对钙钛矿型氧化物中的阳离子偏析提出普遍的认识。

16227016.label: Realisation of objectives
16227016.value: In this project, the mechanism of Ba segregation in Ba1-xLaxFeO3 by means of strain, thermal treatment, and surface treatment on the relative Ba enrichment were studied. Ba1-xLaxFeO3 epitaxial thin films were prepared by pulsed laser deposition both at HKUST and KAIST. The samples showed excellent crystallinity and were virtually flat (root mean square roughness <0.1 nm). It was found that tensile strain prevents Ba segregation. In contrast, compressive strain favors Ba enrichment at the surface. As shown in the Ph.D. thesis of M. Saccoccio, the thermal treatment of the films led to increased Ba segregation. The relative Ba enrichment was studied in situ by conductivity relaxation and ex-situ by angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. To support the experimental results, surface phase diagrams, the density of states, and segregation energies were computed. The first principle computational results supported the experimental observations regarding the role of strain, indicating that tensile strain prevents surface Ba enrichment and the precipitation of BaO and BaCO3. Related continuum results supported these conclusions as well. On a practical level, it was found that surface treatment (by depositing TiO2 or ZrO2) impedes the Ba surface enrichment. More significantly, it was found that Ti and Zr doping on the B-site prevents segregation. This, however, was not validated under humidified conditions. As it is quite difficult to convey the study outcomes without the aid of pictures, part C expands on findings and the relationship to the objectives in detail.

16227016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16227016.value: The major findings are that 1. compressive strain favors Ba enrichment in BLF 2. tensile strain prevents Ba enrichment 3. Ba enrichment is prevented by B-site doping 4. Accelerated thermal treatment speeds up Ba segregation 5. Ba segregation is linked to strain but also the reconstruction due to the unsaturated bonds at the surface. Surface reconstruction is less pronounced in the case of tensile strain. Point 5 is perhaps the biggest scientific contribution of this project and is further elaborated in an appended document in part C.

16227016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16227016.value: The research offers a new way of interpreting the stability of surfaces of BaFeO3-based materials. One proposed topic of great interest is to expand on this work to study the impact of hydration on the stability of BLF systematically. In fact, the PI’s research group recently found BaFeO3-based materials to be extremely promising for proton-conducting fuel cells and reversible fuel cells. A detailed study of this area would not only be very different from the project just concluded but would also provide a new and exciting view on the stability of surfaces.

16227016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16227016.value: The sustainable production of power is one of the most pressing issues for humanity. Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) will play a key role because they are characterized by fuel flexibility, reduced emissions, and high efficiencies that are 3 to 4 times those of combustion systems. Despite their clear promise, SOFCs are not yet economically viable due to the high costs of the materials and components required to handle the high operating temperatures, typically above 800 °C. The most innovative SOFC materials that work at low temperatures are Co-based, resulting in high costs. Fe-based materials are cheaper but usually less effective. Ba0.95La0.05FeO3-δ (BLF) has shown an activity comparable to that of the best Co-based materials. However, during operation, Ba tends to migrate towards the surface of BLF, significantly affecting the cathode electrocatalytic performance. Understanding the mechanism underpinning segregation to the surface is, therefore, critical. Nevertheless, such Ba enrichment mechanism was still poorly understood. The research team conducted a systematic experimental and computational investigation aiming to unravel the mechanisms of Ba segregation in BLF and strategies to mitigate it. One key finding was that appropriate cationic doping can stabilize BLF, allowing its operation in innovative SOFC devices.

16228216.label: Project Objectives

To confirm the scaling law and obtain a formula for the diffusion coefficient through modeling.

16228216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16228216.value: 蒸汽的凝結有廣泛的應用,包括納米材料合成,海水淡化,和電子器件的冷卻。 在蒸汽的凝結過程中,納米液滴在固體表面上的運動是一個重要環節。 在氣體凝結初期,氣體分子先在固體表面形成極小的液滴,這些小的液滴的擴散使其互相碰撞形成大的液滴。 小的液滴的擴散速度決定了最後液體所形成的狀態。 可能是薄膜,也可能是大的液滴。 總之,小尺度液滴的擴散係數對冷凝有很大的影響。 有必要對納米液滴在固體表面的擴散進行細緻研究。 在本專案中,我們將用分子動力學模擬去研究納米液滴在固體表面的擴散。 並研究液滴的大小,固體表面的親水性,和溫度對納米液滴的擴散係數的影響。 我們還將用理論建模總結出納米液滴的擴散係數的半經驗公式。

16228216.label: Realisation of objectives
16228216.value: We have conducted molecular dynamics simulations to compute the diffusion coefficient of droplets on graphene surfaces. Contact angles of droplets are obtained by changing the surface properties. The temperature effects have also been studied. In particular, how water experiences phase change to ice is numerically investigated and the roles of surface energy and temperature on ice nucleation are studied. In addition, we have proposed a scaling law for the diffusion coefficient based on the numerical results. The scaling law provides a general dependence of the diffusion coefficient on temperature and the contact angle. Therefore, both of the objectives have been achieved.

16228216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16228216.value: A scaling law for droplet diffusion on surfaces is proposed, which is valid for a range of temperatures, droplet sizes, and contact angles. Furthermore, phase change mechanisms (from water to ice) for ice nucleation have been revealed through numerical simulations.

16228216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16228216.value: Further work can be conducted to probe phase change processes for droplets and water at supercooled temperatures. The motion of ions in solutions during water crystallization is another topic, which has many potential applications in sea water desalination.

16228216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16228216.value: In this project, the random motion of small droplets on various surfaces has been studied. Specifically, the diffusion coefficient of droplets is calculated and a general law for the diffusion coefficient is developed by modeling the numerical results. At relatively low temperatures, droplets and water experience phase change from liquid to ice. The microscopic mechanisms of such phase change processes are investigated and a couple of ice nucleation pathways/mechanisms are revealed.

16229216.label: Realisation of objectives
16229216.value: Significant progress has been made in realization of the objectives, producing many original results published in high-impact journals. The efforts made to achieve the objectives are summarized below. (1) Fabrication of graphene woven fabrics (GWFs)/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composite sensors with high elasticity and reversibility (Objective 1) Nickel woven fabrics are used as templates for the synthesis of freestanding GWFs by a template-directed chemical vapor deposition (CVD) method. To achieve the high elasticity and reversibility, two different methods are developed to integrate PDMS elastomer with GWFs. In the first method, a freestanding GWF layer is directly deposited on the half-cured, sticky PDMS thin film at different angles to form GWF/PDMS composite films. Excellent adhesion between the GWF and PDMS matrix is realized after the curing of PDMS thin film. (J01) In the second method, a novel technique is developed by infiltrating liquid PDMS into the hollow graphene tubes (GTs) to improve the stretchability and reversibility under repeated loading cycles. A poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) layer is coated on GWF before etching the Ni template. The hollow GTs are then infiltrated with liquid PDMS under vacuum driven by the capillary effect. The PMMA coating is removed to obtain a freestanding elastomer-filled GWF (E-GWF). The E-GWF layer shows excellent elasticity and reversibility under stretching cycles up to 100% strain with negligible hysteresis. Combining the above two methods by depositing E-GWF on a half-cured PDMS film yields an E-GWF/PDMS composite film with improved linearity, sensitivity and structural stability. (J03) (2) Synthesis of graphene foams (GFs)/PDMS composite sensors (Objective 1) A facile approach is devised to convert three-dimensional (3D) GF to highly stretchable two-dimensional (2D) ultrathin GF/PDMS composites with tunable sensitivity and switching capabilities by simply controlling the thickness of GF. GFs are synthesized by CVD on 3D Ni foams. The as-prepared GF is completely immersed into the PDMS mixture, and the 3D GF/PDMS composite of 1.6 mm in thickness is cut into thin films with different thicknesses of 800, 400 and 200 μm using a scalpel. The thickness is controlled by measuring the cutting position using a Vernier caliper. (J02, C02, C04) (3) Development of graphene aerogels (GAs)/PDMS anisotropic sensors (Objective 1) Graphene oxide (GO) aerogels with highly aligned GO walls are prepared by unidirectional freeze-casting of GO aqueous dispersion (5 mg ml-1) using liquid nitrogen as the cooling source followed by freeze-drying. The GO aerogels are reduced in argon at 900 °C for 2 h to obtain unidirectional GAs (UGAs). To improve the sensitivity, pre-cracks are generated by biaxially compressing the UGA along two orthogonal axes transverse to alignment. The pre-cracked UGA (PUGA) is infiltrated with liquid PDMS under vacuum to form a PUGA/PDMS composite sensor which exhibits highly repeatable responses under repeated cycles at maximum strains of 25%. The piezoresistive performance remains very stable even after 1000 cycles at strain of 20 %, indicating excellent durability of the sensor structure. (J05) (4) GWF/PDMS composite strain sensors with anisotropic sensing capabilities for wearable musical instruments (Objective 2) To achieve tri-directional strain sensing capabilities, we first develop a GWF/PDMS composite sensor with anisotropic sensing properties and establish a theoretical model to correlate the resistance change with the applied strains when loaded at different directions. The sensing performances are characterized in terms of normalized resistance change (R/R0). The highly conductive GTs interwoven in an orthogonal architecture serve as an electrically conductive network in the GWF/PDMS composite to sense the applied strains. Correlations are established between the applied strain and the resistance change when loaded at both 0° and 45° to aligned GTs. The composites loaded at 0° to the GT direction exhibit at least threefold higher ΔR/R0 than those loaded at 45°. Such direction-dependent sensing behaviors are attributed to the different local strain responses when the tensions are applied at different angles with respect to GTs. The GWF/PDMS composites possess a combination of extremely high gauge factors for strain sensing, high flexibility for wearable applications, and the capability to detect multi-mode deformations in tension and bending. The practical application as wearable devices are demonstrated by integrating them into a wearable musical instrument. The semi-transparent and flexible GWF/PDMS composites serve as wearable body motion sensors, which are able to translate human body motions to music. (J01, C01, C03) (5) Highly aligned carbon nanofiber (ACNF) film/PDMS sensors with exceptional selectivity for multidirectional strain sensing (Objective 2) To differentiate in-plane strains acting at different angles, an anisotropic strain sensors based on ACNF/PDMS composites are developed using an orthogonal structure. The ACNF film is first fabricated by electrospinning of a PAN precursor and a novel spinning setup consisting of two aluminum collectors with a 15° inclined gap to achieve nanofiber alignment. The as-spun PAN fibers are stabilized and carbonized to produce conductive ACNFs, which are transferred onto a thin PDMS layer to form a ACNF/PDMS composite. The R/R0 surged with the increasing strain when the tension is applied in the alignment direction, resulting in a high gauge factor of 180. On the contrary, the sensor shows almost constant R/R0 values when loaded in the transverse direction, translating into an ultralow gauge factor of only 0.3. The cross-plied sensor is capable of measuring both magnitudes and directions of strains by monitoring R/R0 in two orthogonal directions. The huge gauge factor difference in two directions leads to a high selectivity of 3.84, making the cross-plied ACNF/PDMS sensor distinguish strain directions. The practical applications of the ACNF/PDMS sensors are demonstrated for monitoring multi-degree-of-freedom body movements in a golf swing analyzer. (J04) (6) 3D anisotropic structure for tri-directional strain sensing (Objective 2) 3D anisotropic structures based on PUGA/PDMS composites are designed and fabricated to deliver tri-directional sensing capabilities. The PUGA/PDMS composite sensor demonstrates unique 3D anisotropic piezoresistivity, giving rise to a high gauge factor of 196 when the strain was applied in the alignment direction while remaining insensitive to transverse strains and normal pressures. An in-plane sensor is prepared by orthogonally stacking two PUGA/PDMS sensors. The in-plane sensor is capable of discriminating both directions and magnitudes of in-plane strains, is also insensitive to normal pressure, a critical characteristic for excluding the signal interference from pressure. The in-plane sensor is integrated with a Au/PDMS pressure sensor showing insensitivity to in-plane strains. The three sub-sensors are directionally selective to individual strain components in one of the three orthogonal axes, enabling excellent discriminability towards various 3D stimuli. The 3D sensors with tri-directional sensing capabilities are utilized in a smart sport assistant which provide real-time evaluation and feedback on sport performance. (J05) (7) Flexible temperature sensors made from ACNF/PDMS composites (Objective 2) The integration of temperature sensing capability is important for emerging wearable applications such as health monitoring. ACNF/PDMS composites are also developed for temperature sensing by controlling the atomic structure of ACNF through carefully tuning the carbonization temperature. The correlation between the atomic structure and the temperature sensing performance of the ACNF sensors is correlated with the sizes and spatial orientations of sp2 carbon crystallites, number of defects, and presence of pyridinic-N functional groups in ACNFs. The ACNF/PDMS sensor carbonized at a low temperature exhibits a high temperature sensitivity of 1.52 %℃-1, while shows insensitive to other external stimuli. The potential applications in emerging healthcare and flexible electronic technologies are demonstrated by monitoring the body temperature. (J06)

16229216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16229216.value: Objective 1: Inherently percolated graphene structures including graphene woven fabrics (GWFs), graphene foams (GFs), and graphene aerogels (GAs) are synthesized and integrated with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer to fabricate flexible composite sensors with high elasticity and reversibility. In addition to depositing GWFs on a PDMS film, a novel process is developed to infiltrate liquid PDMS inside the hollow graphene tubes (GTs). (J01, J03) The infiltrated flexible PDMS core provides sufficient mechanical support to the conductive GTs for high reversibility and durability under cyclic loadings. The liquid PDMS is also infiltrated into the porous GFs and GAs to make composite sensors with high stretchability. The cracking-induced resistance change in the GF/PDMS composite sensor enables both sensing and switching capabilities depending on the thickness of sensor with excellent sensitivity, stretchability and large on/off switching ratios. (J02) The anisotropic structure of pre-cracked unidirectional GA (PUGA)/PDMS sensor manifests a unique 3D anisotropic piezoresistive behavior, allowing the sensor to selectively measure the strains in the alignment direction. (J05) Objective 2: A conceptually new orthogonal assembly technique based on highly anisotropic sensing structures is established to achieve tri-directional sensing of 3D stimuli. Aligned carbon nanofiber (ACNF)/PDMS composite sensor made by electrospinning exhibits a remarkable selectivity of 3.84 because of the huge gauge factor difference between the loadings in the nanofiber alignment and transverse directions. Orthogonally stacking two ACNF/PDMS composite sensor generates a cross-plied sensor capable of distinguishing in-plane strain directions by monitoring the resistance change in two orthogonal sensing directions. (J04) Similarly, two PUGA/PDMS sensors are stacked orthogonally in the plane and combined with an interlocked Au/PDMS pressure sensor to form an integrated tri-directional sensor capable of discriminating the directions of various 3D stimuli including in-plane tension, normal pressure, and shear. The fundamental mechanism lies in the selectively sensing of each sub-sensor towards the strain component in one of the three orthogonal axes by virtue of their 3D anisotropic structures and piezoresistive characteristics. (J05) In addition to strain sensing, highly flexible temperature sensors based on ACNF/PDMS composite films are also developed to supplement the sensing capabilities. (J06) The practical applications of these strain and temperature sensors are demonstrated in emerging wearable electronics such as golf swing analyzer, sport performance assistant, and body temperature monitoring.

16229216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16229216.value: The strain and temperature sensors developed in this project provide a fundamental understanding of the sensing mechanisms for multidirectional strain and temperature of a resistive type sensor, where anisotropic structures are desired for a highly selective strain sensing while disordered sp2 carbon crystallites and large number of atomic defects are necessary for a high temperature sensitivity. Based on these principles, future work will be focused on developing a multimodal sensor capable of simultaneously sensing multidirectional strains and temperature. ACNF films carbonized at different temperatures can exhibit different strain and temperature sensitivity, and a combination of ACNF films of different orientations and carbonization temperatures may provide both strain and temperature sensing capabilities without signal interferences.

16229216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16229216.value: Flexible strain sensors are essential for emerging wearable electronics. In light of the three-dimensional (3D) nature of almost all external stimuli with complex strain states, strain sensors having tri-directional sensing capabilities including in-plane strains in two orthogonal directions and normal pressure are highly desired. This project aims to develop flexible tubular and cellular graphene/polymer composites for tri-directional strain sensing. Various inherently interconnected graphene structures are fabricated to serve as conductive networks for high strain sensitivity while an elastomer matrix is infiltrated into the tubes and pores in graphene structures for much enhanced stretchability. To achieve tri-directional strain sensing, a conceptually new orthogonal assembly technique based on anisotropic structures containing highly aligned graphene tubes, graphene walls, and carbon nanofibers are developed. These aligned structures exhibit highly anisotropic electrical responses towards strains applied in the alignment and transverse directions. The orthogonal arrangements of these highly selective sensors yield an integrated sensor capable of discriminating different 3D stimuli including in-plane tension, normal pressure, and shear by virtue of the 3D anisotropic sensing capabilities of individual sensors. The integrated sensors are attached on different body parts to monitor complex body movements, demonstrating promising applications in real-time sports performance tracking and analyses.

16230716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16230716.value: 停止心的流血：檢測Heartbleed安全漏洞

16230716.label: Project Objectives
16230716.value: Construct a new data flow analysis framework. Heartbleed is a bug with sophisticated source/sink contexts and intricate data flow paths. The conventional taint analysis needs to precisely encode these contexts and path characteristics to produce bug reports with low false positives. Our research objective is to fundamentally change the program representation presented to the taint analysis to make the memory usage history explicit. We refer to this new representation as the Static Single Usage (SSU), a derivation of the standard SSA form. With SSU, taint analysis can be formulated as reachability queries on a label graph, to which many classic graphical query processing techniques can be applied. Overcome the curse of complexity. Software systems such as SSL consist of around half a million lines of code. And many critical systems where flaws like Heartbleed could hatch are of similar sizes. Unfortunately, the performance of static analysis is fundamentally limited by its complexity. The precise resolution of pointers is cubic in runtime and solving path constraints is NP-complete. When no better algorithms is known and, yet, we must handle problems of a large size, we will need to resort to engineering effort to alleviate these performance problems. Our first strategy is to make use of parallelization wherever possible in our algorithmic design. We also plan to open up, to customize, and to adapt the COTS SAT solvers to greatly shorten the SAT solving time

16230716.value: Heartbleed程式漏洞是近十年影響程序安全最重要的安全漏洞之一。它因為程序員編寫程序的錯誤而產生的。它屬於緩衝區溢出，一種非常古老但是依然活躍的安全漏洞，而且至今沒有有效的解決辦法。我們從靜態分析的研究領域出發去嘗試靠近一個可行的解決方案。同以往靜態分析研究不同的是，我們計劃針對這類的安全漏洞而仔細的選取一系列的靜態分析解決辦法。目的是可以在大型的軟件系統中有效的找到類似的問題而沒有很高的誤報率。我們的方法集中解決底層的內存操作以及對於高層分析的抽象模型，這使得傳統的漏洞分析方法會在效果上得到很大的提升，從而向最終解決這個問題有顯著的進步。

16230716.label: Realisation of objectives
16230716.value: We have achieved our objectives satisfactorily. We have accomplished the design and the implementation of the SSU representation, which shows that it is important to model the memory use lifecycle of a heap variable. By encoding the state transitions on the traditional data flow graph, we have successfully reduced the memory leak detection from a multi-path search problem to a simple one-path reachability problem. This gives hope of scaling this type of analysis to realistic programs of large sizes. Our second objective turned out not to be engineering centric but of significant technical innovation. By the first stage, we have created a sound approximation of the possible path where memory use problems might occur. This significantly reduced the amount of SAT verifications need to be carried out, a crucial factor for the eventual precision for large software systems. Our experiments show that the effect is satisfactory and we have discovered many significant problems in mature and widely used open-source programs. Both the methodology and the results are described in a scientific research paper, which is published in the flagship conference of software engineering. The degree of the innovation and the significance of the results have led to the awarding of the paper with a distinguished paper award, a prestigious recognition.

The research community so far have devised many methods to combat this problem with, however, limited success. We have invented a novel approach to address these problems for large software systems of millions of lines of code and achieve unprecedented precision compared to the state of the art. Our results are so impressive that the paper describes our approach has won a top paper award in our flagship conference.

16230916.label: Realisation of objectives
16230916.value: The primary goal of this project is to study chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of monolayer and few-layer 2D semiconductors and their integration with conventional III-V and III-Nitride structures for emerging device applications. We have mostly concentrated on MoS2, but the knowledge and insight gained here could aid study of other 2D materials. Through this project, the process of growing MoS2 onto substrates like SiO2, GaN and sapphire has been developed and optimized. Various characterisation techniques were used to guide the materials development along with analysis facilitated by first principle simulations. Considerable efforts were devoted to improving the surface passivation of MoS2 which led to top-gate and back-gate transistors showing greatly enhanced mobilities. Layer transfer techniques were developed and applied to integrate 2D materials with III-As and III-N low dimensional structures. The interlayer interaction or coupling between 2D layer and the substrate has been studied. Objective 1: Chemical vapor deposition of monolayer and few-layer MoS2 thin films on SiO2, sapphire, GaN and SiC substrates A home-built CVD system was set up and used for MoS2 growth. The synthesized MoS2 crystals on SiO2 substrates are equilateral triangles in random orientations with sizes up to ~40 μm. PL, Raman, XPS, and TEM analysis show high crystalline and optical quality. These obtained MoS2 were used to fabricate field effect transistors and for passivation and integration studies. The growth of MoS2 on c-plane sapphire results in either monolayer flakes or characteristic “nanorod” structures which are composed of vertical aligned multilayer MoS2. The supply of MoO3 has been found to play a decisive role in the shape of MoS2. The nanorods show highly aligned orientations with the adjacent nanorods forming an angle of exact 60º or 120º. The van der Waals interaction between MoS2 and sapphire governs the formation of initial nuclei and only energetically preferable nuclei can grow. The MoS2 nanorod is further characterized through the fabrication of field effect transistors. Finally, on GaN substrates, we were able to grow characteristic single-crystal well-defined equilateral triangles. The typical size of MoS2 triangles is 200 nm, with some coalesced triangles up to 1 μm in size. AFM measurement shows that thickness of triangles is about 1.4 nm, which corresponds to a bilayer MoS2. Objective 2: Study heterojunctions formed by narrow bandgap MoS2 and wide bandgap GaN We have performed Raman measurement to study the MoS2/GaN stack formed by Van der Waals epitaxy. The large vdW interaction between MoS2 and GaN causes further separation of the out-of-plane vibration A1 from the in-plane vibration E2, in comparison to MoS2 deposited on the SiO2 substrates. First-principles simulations were used to investigate the atomic registry in MoS2/GaN stack with rotational angles at 0° or 180°, namely, the R stack and H stack, as observed in our experiments. The interlayer coupling was studied through the analysis of charge transfer. Although there are electrons redistributed around S and Ga atoms, no obvious charge transfer between GaN and MoS2 was noted. The charge transfer directly reflects the interlayer and coupling and confirms that no covalent bonds are formed between the two. Van der Waals interaction governs the interlayer coupling. Further charge analysis based on the Bader method shows that only 0.2 electrons are transferred to each S from the GaN substrate and no obvious electron lost from Ga atoms. Objective 3: Transfer CVD-grown MoS2 to III-V substrates for MoS2/InGaAs van der Waals heterojunctions and study interface properties A layer transfer process was developed in this project to transfer the MoS2 originally grown on SiO2/Si wafers to InGaAs/InP substrates for hybrid quantum well structures and potential device applications. The transferring of MoS2 triangles with size up to 40 μm was achieved. The optical properties of MoS2 was preserved after the transfer process, as evidenced by Raman and PL studies. The interface coupling has not been well identified which could be compromised by the cleanliness of the process. To fabricate MOSFET devices, deposition of high-k dielectric on MoS2 is critical. We have investigated atomic-layer deposition (ALD) of ZrO2 and Al2O3 on MoS2 intensively. Objective 4: Develop MoS2 channel top-gate transistor technology We have developed a low-temperature ALD process that enables growth of ZrO2 layer on MoS2 with full coverage and continuity. MoS2/ZrO2 top gate MOSFET was demonstrate for the first time using a gate-last process. The deposited ZrO2 overlayer can enhance the MoS2 mobility. Gate hysteresis, I-V and C-V measurements suggest good dielectric properties. An on/off current ratio of over 1E7, a subthreshold slope of 276 mV dec−1, and a field-effect electron mobility of 12.1 cm2 V−1 s−1 have been achieved. Photoresponse measurement shows a highly sensitive photoresponsivity of 162.7 A/W. To study the photoswitching behavior of the ZrO2/MoS2 top-gate transistors, a time-resolved photoresponse measurement was conducted by periodic turning the illumination LED on and off at a frequency of 0.1 Hz. The results demonstrate that ZrO2/MoS2 hybrid channel devices can be potentially used for high-sensitive and high-speed photodetection.

16230916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16230916.value: 1.Van der Waals epitaxy of MoS2 on hexagonal lattice substrates CVD growth of MoS2 on both sapphire and GaN substrates have been investigated intensively in this project, building on our work of growing MoS2 on SiO2/Si substrates. In all the cases, the cleaning lever of the starting surface and any subtle change in growth parameters can lead to different outcomes. It is surprising to realise vertically aligned multilayer MoS2 “nanowalls” with highly aligned orientations on sapphire substrates (Y. Hu, “MoS₂/dielectric stack optimization for high performance metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor,” M.Phil. thesis, 2018). Initial electrical characterizations suggest gate-modulated conductivity and on-off ratios of over 1000. Implementation of these 2D layered materials in 3D device geometries such as FinFET could open more interesting opportunities. In terms of the growth on nearly lattice-matched GaN substrates, the synthesized MoS2 crystals are equilateral triangles with two orientations identified. This shows that the weak van der Waals interaction can control the lattice orientation and thus leads to the epitaxial growth behaviour. It illustrates the possibility to create 2D/3D heterojunctions by CVD growth. 2. ALD high-k oxides on MoS2 Atomic-layer deposition of high-k gate dielectrics on 2D materials has been an extremely challenging task. In this project we leveraged a low temperature ALD process to directly deposite ZrO2 and Al2O3 on CVD grown MoS2 with thickness scalable to 3 nm. Its full coverage, high uniformity, and low defect density is in sharp contrast to the patchy and discontinuous Al2O3 or HfO2 layer deposited on exfoliated MoS2 films reported in the literature. Detailed XRS studies suggest the presence of MoO3 acting as nucleation sites in the ALD process. This is of great importance to the successful demonstration of top-gate transistors (Y. Hu, Semiconductor Science and Technology 33 (4), 045004, 2018). 3. Surface passivation of MoS2 by HF treatment In the development of CVD growth of MoS2 on SiO2/Si substrates for back-gate transistors, we have demonstrated improved carrier mobility and hysteresis behaviour via HF-dipping treatment of the initial SiO2/Si substrate. The mobility of MoS2 increases to 42.2 cm2V-1s-1 from 17.9 cm2V-1s-1 and the hysteresis gap of the transistors decreases to 5V from 8V. XPS analysis and first-principles simulation were performed to examine the passivation mechanism. HF-dipping treatment can result in the satisfaction of surface dangling bonds by H atoms. The passivated surface dangling bonds lead to a suppressed Coulomb scattering and reduced interface trap state. Our methods could be extended to other novel low-dimensional semiconductor/substrate system, like ZnO nanowire, carbon nanotube, and graphene.

16230916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16230916.value: 1.Synthesize large-area continuous MoS2 monolayer on GaN GaN is predicted to be a promising vdW epitaxial substrate for growing MoS2, due to its surface inertness and hexagonal crystal structure with perfect matched in-plane lattice constant. In addition, the thermal expansion coefficients of MoS2 and GaN are reported to be of small discrepancy. Initial results from this project already demonstrate the possibility of merging MoS2 triangles with the same/opposite orientation into a partially continuous layer. Further research work could be done to optimize growth conditions towards large area wafer scale growth. 2. MoS2 FinFET devices and MoS2/InGaAs hybrid channel MOSFETs Building on the material platform developed in this project, there are a lot of potential to develop novel device structures. The MoS2 nanowall structures integrated on sapphire could be combined with the ALD dielectrics and used to fabricate FinFET devices. It will be intriguing to compare these ultimately scaled 2D channel devices with Si transistors. The hybrid MoS2/InGaAs quantum well structure could also be integrated with ALD dielectrics, which will be an excellent demonstration of 2D/3D integrated devices.

16230916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16230916.value: In this project, we developed the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of 2-dimensional MoS2 crystals on hexagonal lattice substrates. Compared to the prevailing chemical exfoliation process, CVD growth offers wafer level scalability, high throughput and low-cost manufacturing capability. High-quality, unstrained, and few-layer MoS2 with strict registry to the underlying lattice has been achieved on GaN substrates. By combining various characterization methods and first-principles simulation, we qualitatively determine the interlayer coupling and atomic registry in the MoS2/GaN stack. On sapphire substrates, we were able to realize a new type of nanowall structures with vertically aligned 2D layers exhibiting modulated conductivity. To study potential device applications, we developed surface passivation techniques for improving carrier mobilities and a low temperature process for growing dielectric layers on MoS2. Both top-gate and back gate transistors were fabricated with decent switching behaviours. Finally, layer transfer technique was applied to transfer these 2D semiconductors onto conventional compound semiconductor quantum-well and quantum-dot structures. The unique coupling effect has been studied. The research from this project could provide useful insights for further developing novel heterostructures and 2D/3D integrated devices.
