16231016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16231016.value: The demand for high-performance devices has promoted the rapid development of nanostructured materials in which the desired properties are achieved through the use of nanostructures. For example, a short-period AlAs/GaAs superlattice has a lateral thermal conductance of 3.1 Wm^(-1) K^(-1), which is a remarkable 4x reduction compared to an Al0.5Ga0.5As alloy. The ability to manipulate thermal conductance opens the door for creating a wide range of new materials/devices/systems with performances that could not possibly be achieved previously. Some examples include thermoelectric materials with ZT > 1.5, thermal diodes and thermal cloaking. An important element in this development, particularly towards the goal of commercialization, is the efficient modeling techniques and tools of heat conduction in complex systems with length scales across a wide range. Phonon transport is a main heat conduction mechanism in semiconductors. In nanostructured systems/devices with feature sizes ranging from nanometers to millimeters or larger, both the wave-like and particle behavior of the phonon are important. Currently the modeling approaches of phonon transport can be classified into pure particle based approaches, pure wave approaches and atomic-level simulations. Only atomic-level simulations are able to model both particle and wave behaviors of phonons. However these simulations are known for their high computational costs, and therefore are hardly used to model and design realistic devices. The proposed research aims at the development of an efficient simulation method that can model both the wave and particle natures of phonons. The proposed approach is built on the Monte Carlo method but with a particle model that carries both wave and particle properties. A new interface model is proposed and will be developed with the aid of MD simulations. The developed simulation method and interface model will be validated with measured thermal conductivities of a GaAs/AlAs superlattice and will be applied in a parametric study of phonon transport in superlattices. The successful completion of this project will produce, for the first time, a practical modeling technique for phonon transport without a pre-assumption of whether it is particle dominant or wave dominant, and hence allows the design of nanostructured materials/devices with length scales across a wide range. A new interface model will also result, which will be more realistic and accurate than the existing models. In addition, the proposed parametric study will yield fundamental insights on the formation of coherent phonon transport, and thus provide guidelines on the design of supperlattices as thermoelectric materials in various applications.

16231016.label: Realisation of objectives
16231016.value: The three objectives proposed in the proposal have all been achieved. We successfully developed an interference phonon Monte Carlo (IMC) simulation method, which is capable of capturing both particle and wave nature of phonon transport. As expected, this method can reproduce the conventional MC results in cases when particle behavior dominates. For cases when wave effects become important, the IMC can also capture wave phenomena that were experimentally observed or revealed in molecular dynamic simulations. It is thus applicable for a wide range of phonon transport problems and no prior assumption of phonon behavior is needed during modeling. The developed IMC method was used to study the effects of various factors such as interfacial thermal resistance and interface roughness on the coherent phonon transport inside superlattices. For the second objective, a framework for a new interface model was established. One new feature of this interface framework is that anharmonic collisions at the interface, which are ignored in the previous models, are included in this new interface model. This model also allows phonons to undergo both coherent and incoherent transport at the interface, thus facilitating the modeling of both particle and wave behavior. A major task is to determine the key parameter, that is, frequency-dependent transmission rate, at the interface. We firstly used lattice dynamic and Green’s function approaches to determine the frequency-dependent transmission rate of the interface. We then fit it with a simplified model and verified its accuracy by comparing the cross-plane thermal conductivity of Si/Ge superlattice calculated from IMC with this interface model with that obtained from molecular dynamics simulation. Good agreement was achieved. The developed IMC method was validated by conventional MC method, molecular dynamics simulations and experimental results. First, IMC method was used to study the cross-plane thermal transport inside a Si/heavy Si superlattice. At room temperature, the transport is dominated by particle behavior. The results obtained from the IMC agreed very well with those from conventional MC in which only particle behavior of phonons is modeled. At low temperatures, the simulated thermal conductivity from the IMC method showed a linear increasing trend with the length of the superlattice, a signature result of wave behavior that was experimentally observed. Next, the IMC method was used to study thermal transport inside Si/Ge superlattice. The results were compared with those obtained from full molecular dynamics simulations. Very good agreements were obtained. The IMC method was then used to study coherence phonon transport in both periodic and aperiodic Si/Ge superlattices. Interesting finds were obtained, which are described in Section 6.1. In addition to the tasks proposed in the project, we also developed an efficient MC method entitled MFP-based MC method, which facilitates the simulation of large-scale thermal materials/system. Similar to molecular dynamics method, MC methods are particle-based simulations methods, and thus are computationally expensive. In addition, these methods require frequency-dependent quantities such as relaxation time and dispersion, which are difficult to obtain accurately. The proposed new method adopts an energy-based Boltzmann equation and uses cumulative mean free path (MFP) as the only input, hence greatly improves the efficiency of the method and reduces the computational time. The efficiency is enhanced by incorporating the recently proposed variance-reduction method, and the accuracy is ensured because the MFP-based cumulative thermal conductivity can be accurately obtained by experiments or first principles calculation. Moreover, with the MEP-cumulative thermal conductivity as the input, optical phonons can be naturally included in the calculation, which further improves the accuracy.

16231016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16231016.value: The main research output is the IMC method, which was proposed and developed in this project. This is the only simulation method that can model the wave-particle duality of phonons. The existing methods can only model phonons either as particles or as waves. None of them can model both. Another research output related to methodology development is the MFP-MC method, which is an efficient Monte Carlo simulation method suitable for the modeling of large-scale particle-dominated thermal systems. The IMC method was used to study the thermal transport inside Si/Ge superlattices. Both periodic and aperiodic superlattices were studied. At room temperature, it was found that despite the assumed perfect interfaces, the wave interference effect is highly suppressed by the ballistic phonon transport occurred in the entire lattice, and the increasing thermal conductivity with the increased period number observed in the MD results in both periodic and aperiodic SLs is largely attributed to this ballistic transport, which is not caused by the coherence transport, but by the nearly unity transmission rate of low-frequency phonons. Hence contradictive to the common belief, the linearly increasing trend seen in the thermal conductivity of SLs as the number of periods increases does not necessarily indicate the importance of wave interference.

16231016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16231016.value: There are two possible directions that one can follow to continue this research effort. The first one is on the algorithm development. The current algorithm is only suitable for 2D and simple domains. The extension to 3D and more complex problem domains is necessary in practical applications. Another direction to pursue is on the methodology development. The IMC method was developed primarily for superlattices, which are essentially one-dimensional materials. Extension to two-dimension materials such as nano-ribbons, nano-meshes would create more impact on the development of nanostructured thermal materials.

16231016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16231016.value: Nanostructured thermal materials are a new class of materials that are instrumental in the development of high-performance thermal devices and systems. Phonon transport is a main heat conduction mechanism in semiconductors. Thus, modeling and controlling phonon transport inside micro/nanostructures are of both fundamental and practical importance. A key characteristic of phonons is their wave-particle duality. Currently there is no efficient simulation method that can model both particle and wave behavior of phonons. In this project, a mesoscale simulation framework based on Monte Carlo method that is capable to simulate both particle and wave behavior of phonon transport in superlattices was proposed and developed. This method allows one to model phonon transport without the need of a pre-assumption of whether it is particle dominant or wave dominant, and hence allows the design of nanostructured materials/devices with length scales across a wide range. In addition, the parametric study conducted using the developed method yields fundamental insights on the formation of coherent phonon transport, and thus provide guidelines on the design of superlattices as thermoelectric materials in various applications.

16231216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16231216.value: Users of social networks (SNs) often publish their current location by checking-in at different places and uploading geo-tagged photos and messages, annotated with spatial information (e.g., map coordinates). Numerous location-based services utilize this information to support geo-social (GS) queries that combine social and spatial attributes, such as “find friends of a user located in his/her vicinity”. Moreover, commercial SNs often offer APIs that allow the development of third-party applications involving GS queries. However, the data of different SNs are usually heterogeneous and distributed, may describe complementary or overlapping information, are accessible through diverse indexing schemes, and are organized under different storage schemas and infrastructure. For these reasons, the efficient execution of GS queries constitutes a system-specific and challenging task. To overcome these issues we propose general optimization techniques, aimed at computing efficient execution plans for GS queries, tailored to the underlying system and data characteristics. We first define GSL, a query language that builds upon a set of well-defined and generally accepted primitive geo-social operators, currently supported by commercial APIs. GSL captures the different access patterns of these operators, and, through the use of integrity constraints, their equivalence or overlapping semantics. We then develop algorithms that, given a GSL query, compute the execution plan with the lowest expected cost, based on the system architecture, access methods, equivalence semantics, storage and implementation details of different operators. In addition, our analysis enables novel indices for geo-social data that lead to a much more precise cost estimation of the optimal plan. In detail, our objectives are to: (i) formally define GSL, a query language that captures access and equivalence dependencies across geo-social operators, (ii) design algorithms that generate equivalent GS queries by applying different combinations of primitive operators, iii) develop models and indices for estimating the cost of query evaluation plans and determining the optimal one, given the system/data characteristics, (iv) implement and experimentally evaluate the proposed techniques using real datasets. 通过地点签到、上传或发布含有地理信息（例如，经纬度坐标）的图片或者状态，社交网络用户可以公布他们当前的位置信息。大量基于地理位置的服务利用这类信息来支持结合社交以及空间信息的地理-社交（GS）查询，例如“查找该用户附近的朋友”。此外，商业社交网络通常为第三方应用提供接口(API)以支持地理-社交查询。然而，不同社交网络的数据通常是异构的、分布式的。这些数据可能包含着互补或者重合的信息，需要通过多种索引方式获取，并且以完全不同的存储结构和系统架构进行管理。因此，高效执行地理-社交查询是一个与系统相关的难题。为此，我们提出了旨在高效执行GS查询，并针对底层系统和数据特性的一般性优化方案。 首先我们定义地理-社交查询语音(GSL)。这语言建立在一系列定义清晰、被广泛接受的原始算符上。这些原始算符已被商业接口(API)支持。GSL语言刻画了这些算符间不同的数据访问模式，以及在完整性约束下它们的等价性和重叠语义。接着，我们提出了一个算法。对于一个地理-社交(GSL)查询，这个算法能根据原始算符的系统架构，数据访问方式，等价语义，存储和实现细节，计算出代价最小的执行计划。此外，我们的分析促成了适用于地理-社交数据的新的索引。这种索引对最优执行计划的代价有着更精准的估计。具体来说，我们的目标是:(i)正式定义地理-社交语言(GSL)，一种针对不同地理-社交算符的数据访问特性以及语义等价性的查询语言 (ii)设计算法，利用不同的原始算符组合生成等价的地理-社交查询。(iii)设计模型和索引，在给定系统/数据特征的情况下，给出执行计划的代价预测并选择最优的执行计划。(iv)实现上述的方案，并在真实数据集中完成实验评估。

16231216.label: Realisation of objectives
16231216.value: Regarding objectives 1 and 2, we proposed several query types and information processing tasks for GeoSN. For each query and task, we designed and implemented associated algorithms, as discussed in the following paragraphs. Geosocial classification problems are important for services such as recommendations of social events, or delivery of targeted advertising material to users. An example is the geo-social event organization (GSEO) query: given a set of events, assign each user to a single event in order to minimize (i) the total distance between each user and assigned event, and (ii) the total weight of edges between friends assigned at different events. Ideally, every user should be assigned to a nearby event, which is also recommended to several of his friends. GSEO is an NP-Hard problem and exact solutions cannot be derived for realistic GeoSN. To overcome this challenge, we propose a game-theoretic framework for fast approximate solutions with high accuracy. In this framework, each user constitutes a player that wishes to minimize his own social and distance cost. We demonstrate that the Nash Equilibrium concept is inadequate due to the capacity constraints, and propose the notion of pairwise stability, which yields better solutions. In addition, we develop a second framework that employs local search, and aims at minimizing the global cost. We show that the two approaches can be unified under a common agent-based framework that allows for two types of deviations. In a unilateral deviation, a user switches to a new event, whereas in a bilateral deviation a pair of users exchange events. We develop a number of optimization techniques to improve result quality and facilitate efficiency. We also investigated collective influence maximization, where the owner of multiple competing products wishes to select seeds for each product so that the collective influence across all products is maximized. Assume, for instance, a set of events, competing for the same set of users of a GeoSN. Each event has an integer budget, that corresponds to the number of users (e.g., influencers) to be included in its seed-set. A user has a weight for every event that is inversely proportional to the (Euclidean, network) distance between them, so that the most important users for an event are those nearby. The goal is to select, for each event, a seed-set of cardinality equal to the budget that maximizes the total influence. Intuitively, a seed-set should influence numerous users near the corresponding event because such users have large weights for the event. We developed a novel diffusion model, Awareness-to-Influence (AtI), which distinguishes the concepts of awareness and influence. AtI is based on the fact that often users do not blindly follow the first influence; instead, they collect and reproduce information before they finally decide. AtI exhibits monotonicity and sub-modularity, two important properties that facilitate tight quality guarantees. We designed game theoretic algorithms, considering that each event is a player that selects a seed-set to maximize its own influence. The proposed algorithms considerably outperform certain benchmarks in terms of solution quality, and scale well to large social networks. Another processing task related to GeoSN is spatial keyword search, which takes as input a user location, a set of query keywords, and an integer k. The result is the set of top-k spatial entities (e.g., Chinese restaurants) according to a ranking function that considers both the spatial distance between each candidate entity and the user, and the similarity of the keywords to the entity. Several studies in keyword search indicate that users prefer some diversity in the query results (i.e., the top-k results should not be very similar to each other). To incorporate this notion, we first introduce Ptolemy’s diversity, a novel spatial diversity metric, based on which we define the problem of top-k diversified spatial keyword search. We show that the problem is NP-hard, and propose two algorithms for approximate retrieval with guaranteed error bounds. Extensive experimental evaluation with real data demonstrates the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed approach, and confirms that our framework is preferred by human evaluators. Community detection in conventional social networks aims at identifying groups of users which are inter-connected with edges of high density, compared to connections among users in different groups. In GeoSN, community detection should also take into account the user locations, i.e., a community should contain a group of users that are tightly connected socially and are situated in the same geographic area. To tackle the problem of community detection in GeoSN, we introduce a novel DGCD model, motivated by the notions of spatial density and structural graph clustering. DGCD is based on a novel measure for the geo-social distance between a pair of users that captures well their social strength and also their spatial proximity. The DGCD algorithm discovers all communities that are socially and spatially cohesive, and outperforms existing approaches in terms of solution quality. Regarding objective 3, spatial size estimation techniques, such as multi-dimensional histograms are not suitable for GeoSN since they can only approximate spatial range counts, without considering social information. To overcome this problem, we have designed summarization techniques for efficiently and accurately estimating the size GeoSN queries. These novel structures combine 2D histograms with sketches or 1D histograms. In particular, we first use a 2D histogram to spatially partition the users into buckets according to their location. After constructing such a spatial histogram, we enhance its usability by attaching to each bucket a summary of the number of friends each user has inside. There are two ways to implement this summary: either through a sketch, or a 1D histogram. We experimented with Count-Min Sketch and Count-Sketch, which have error guarantee. As a 1D histogram we used the MaxDiff structure, which is efficient and near-optimal. Moreover, we developed a memory distribution strategy for deciding the sizes of the summaries in each bucket, given the desired level of compression. This work constitutes the MPhil thesis of my student C. Koutras. Regarding objective 4, all the proposed techniques haver been implemented and thoroughly evaluated with real GeoSN. The experimental evaluation includes efficiency, effectiveness and in some cases satisfaction by human users.

16231216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16231216.value: Constrained graph partitioning assigns users of a social network to a set of classes with bounded capacities so that the similarity and the social costs are minimized. The similarity cost is proportional to the dissimilarity between a user and his class, whereas the social cost is measured in terms of friends that are assigned to different classes. A motivating example is the social event organization (SEO) problem in GeoSN, where classes correspond to social events promoted to users. In this case, the similarity cost is the distance between each user and his recommended event, whereas the social cost is the total weight of edges between friends in different events. In J1 we propose two approaches for SEO based on game theory and local search. In location-based keyword search on RDF data, the user inputs a set of keywords, a query location, and a number of RDF spatial entities to be retrieved. The output entities should be geographically close to the query location and relevant to the query keywords. However, the results can be similar to each other, compromising query effectiveness. In view of this limitation, in J2 we integrate textual and spatial diversification into RDF spatial keyword search, facilitating the retrieval of entities with diverse characteristics and directions with respect to the query location. In J3 we consider that the owner of multiple competing products selects seeds for each product so that the collective influence across all products is maximized. To capture the competing diffusion processes, we introduce a novel model that separates the awareness and influence phases. To compute the seed sets, we propose a game-theoretic framework that views the various products as agents, which compete for influence in the social graph and selfishly select their individual strategy. An extensive evaluation with events competing for the users of real GeoSN demonstrates the high solution quality of the proposed methods. Most of the existing work on community detection focuses on the social connections. However, the emergence of GeoSNs motivates the integration of location information. In C1, we define a new measure for the geo-social distance between a pair of users that captures well their social strength and also their spatial proximity. Then, we introduce an efficient algorithm that correctly identifies all communities in a GeoSN, according to a set of spatial and social constraints.

16231216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16231216.value: Geo-social networks provide ample opportunities for novel processing tasks that have practical relevance and research potential. Although in this project we covered various such tasks, there are several more worth investigating. Moreover, even for the covered tasks we focused on centralized architectures, where the entire geo-social network resides at a single server. It would be worthwhile to extend the proposed techniques to distributed architectures, where each server is responsible for a geographic area. Finally, we intend to continue our work on geosocial indexing and query optimization, especially on structures that combine spatial histograms with sketches for selectivity estimation.

16231216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16231216.value: A Geo-Social Network (GeoSN) is a social graph where the nodes represent users, and the edge represent friendships. Using a GeoSN application, usually through mobile devices, users can check in at places, find friends in the vicinity, etc. A GeoSN can be either a conventional social network (e.g., Facebook, Twitter) enhanced with check-in functionality, or a pure GeoSN (Foursquare) focused on location-based services. Given the location information, commercial GeoSNs support multiple query types. For instance, Foursquare’s Radar and Facebook’s Nearby return the friends who are currently in the vicinity of a user. Geoloqi, a platform for location-based services, notifies a user when friends enter a certain range. In general, the integration of social and geographic information in GeoSN provides ample opportunities for novel query processing tasks. In this project, we proposed several query types and information processing tasks for GeoSN. For each query and task we designed and implemented associated algorithms. The efficiency and the effectiveness of the proposed techniques was thoroughly evaluated with real datasets.

16232316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16232316.value: The wireless revolution has changed the way we communicate and created a mobile information society. However wired cable and optical networks remain the communication backbone for these systems as well as the backbone for the delivery of a plethora of other services including those in buildings, transport systems, automobiles and airplanes where they are a fundamental subsystem in the distribution of signals and electricity. For example the length of cables inside cars has increased more than tenfold, from hundreds to thousands of meters, over the past 30 years. The safe and reliable operation of these wired cable networks and the systems they support has become critical and requires the availability of techniques for detecting and locating existing and future faults in them. Currently these techniques are predominately based upon time domain reflectometry where signals are injected into a wired cable network and the reflections are used to locate faults. These techniques are very effective for the detection of hard faults (open and short circuits) but the detection of other types of faults (soft faults) is more difficult and often more critical. Soft faults include smooth and localized changes in cable impedance and are characterized by weak reflectivity and reveal information about the state of the wired network. This information includes changes to insulation, partial cuts, severe bending and can be a precursor to future catastrophic faults. Reflectometry is not effective in detecting these soft faults. In this proposal we intend to use inverse scattering methods to enhance the detection and location of soft faults in intricate wired networks. Inverse scattering is a theoretic framework for directly estimating the impedance profile of the cable from scattering data. For the one-dimensional problem such as a single cable, exact solutions have been derived and can be leveraged to greatly enhance the detection and location of soft faults. We propose to apply these techniques and develop them for detecting soft faults in intricate wired networks. We also propose to develop hybrid techniques which adapt time domain reflectometry approaches by incorporating critical aspects of formal inverse scattering techniques to improve them. In addition we will attempt to extend the formal inverse scattering methods to intricate wired networks where theoretic results do not exist. The long-term significance of this research is that it could lead to the development of new fault detection techniques that increases the reliability and safety of critical wired networks. 無線通訊革命徹底改變了人們的通信方式，打造了一個全新的無線資訊社會。然而有線電纜和光纜網路依然是所有通信網路的基礎。同時，有線的信號傳輸和電力傳輸也在建築樓宇、交通系統、汽車和飛機等應用領域中不可或缺。例如，汽車中的電纜線長度在過去三十年中從幾百米增加到幾千米，漲幅高達十倍。這些有線網路的安全至關重要，因此對有線網路現存或可能產生的故障探測及定位的研究也意義空前。現有的探測方法主要基於時域反射測量技術，這種技術通過測量輸入信號的反射來進行故障定位。這種方法對於探測重大故障（硬故障，例如開路或短路）十分奏效，但是對於其他類型的故障（軟故障）檢測則面臨較大困難。軟故障會引起線路中平穩的和局部的阻抗變化，可檢測到弱反射，反射資訊可以用來表徵有線網路的健康狀況。可能的軟故障包括絕緣層破損、部分開路、嚴重擰轉等，這些問題可能轉化成重大故障和災害。時域反射測量技術對於軟故障的檢測收效甚微。 我們提出利用逆散射法對複雜有線網路的軟故障進行有效探測。逆散射法是一種利用反射資訊對電纜特性阻抗曲線進行直接估計的理論框架。對於單一電纜的一維問題，目前已經可以求解精確解，並且大幅度提高軟故障探測的精確度。我們提出將逆散射方法應用於有線網路的軟故障探測中。我們也提出聯合使用時域反射測量技術和逆散射技術來進一步提高精度。同時我們也將嘗試將逆散射方法應用於多電纜網路中，目前這一問題尚無法理論求解。此項研究的長遠意義在於研發新的軟故障探測技術，以此提高關鍵有線網路的安全性和可靠性。

16232316.label: Realisation of objectives
16232316.value: All three objectives have been met at the completion of this project. In particular for meeting objective 1 we have developed an approximate technique based on the Born approximation that can provide an analytic expression for the impedance profile of transmission lines while maintaining very good accuracy in a wide range of conditions. The analytic formula only requires knowledge of the transmission line reflection coefficient. Theory, simulations and experiments have been reported in a journal publication [J1]. We have also extended this approach to transmission lines with losses and those with both impedance and shunt conductance faults and this has also been published as a journal paper [J2]. A novelty of this approach [J2] is that measurements from both ends of the line allows the impedance and shunt faults to be separated and this is the first time, to our knowledge, that this has been achieved. Theory, simulations and experimental results are provided in the publication [J2]. This approach has also led us to resolve multi-cable faults by treating connections as shunts and identifying them by using our novel technique. In particular branches can be separated from impedance faults straightforwardly. Graph theory has also been investigated to characterize the multi-cable networks. Under restricted conditions on the number of branches and nodes the entire network can be identified. We have also investigated an interesting super-resolution approach in which we can super resolve both impedance and shunt conductance faults [J3,C1]. The approach makes use of new results developed for the super-resolution of 1D inverse scattering problems developed in mathematics. To our knowledge this is the first time the results have been applied to impedance profiling. Together these techniques [J2,J3] meet objective 2. Experimental verification of the proposed techniques has been provided to meet objective 3 [J1,J2]. These are based on utilizing VNA measurements of cables with various faults. Successful detection of both impedance faults and conductance shunts has been achieved. Furthermore we have also investigated whether practical bandpass signals can be utilized for the detection process and optimum sequence design[C2]. It is shown [C2] that using optimum sequences for probing the signals can enhance reconstruction quality when noise is present.

16232316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16232316.value: This research has two major new findings. These include: 1) Accurate analytical expressions have been obtained for impedance faults and shunt conductance faults in transmission lines using reflection measurements [J1,J2]. To the best of our knowledge this is the first time that impedance and shunt faults can be separated [J2]. The results have been demonstrated by experiments [J1,J2] 2) We have applied new 1D super-resolution techniques to identify faults in transmission lines. This allows the location of faults to be found with infinite precision and therefore the bandwidth of the measurements can be reduced [C1,J3].

16232316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16232316.value: The techniques we have developed have demonstrated new results in fault detection in transmission lines. An area that could be focused on in future is active fault detection in “live” networks. That is develop techniques that make use of the signals already present in the network to detect faults. This area is related to passive imaging. It would also be useful to develop inexpensive equipment that can perform the fault detection.

16232316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16232316.value: We have developed techniques that can be used to perform fault detection in cable networks. A novelty of the approach is that different types of faults can be classified. This allows the techniques to not only detect existing faults but also detect abnormalities that are the forerunner of more severe faults. This can provide an important guide to when maintenance needs to be performed. An important discovery was also made in that the location of the faults can be obtained with infinite precision by leveraging recent results developed from super-resolution. This allows potential faults to be found with pinpoint accuracy.

16233316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16233316.value: Injection molding is one of the key polymer processing techniques. It accounts for the consumption of more than 1/3 of all polymers. In the molding process, key process variables must be controlled precisely to ensure the repeatability and reliability of product quality. The mold of course is a key component of the molding process. Multi-cavity molds with a hot-runner system are nowadays widely used in the industry for enhanced productivity by simultaneously producing multiple identical parts within one molding cycle. The industry has been plagued for decades by the problem of cavity-to-cavity part inconsistency, despite the fact that the cavities and runners are made mechanically identical. The problem is attributed to differences in the runner temperatures. Temperature synchronization among the different hot runners to achieve the same thermo-history has thus become a critical factor for quality consistency among parts molded in different cavities. The current algorithm controls runner temperatures separately by focusing only on set point tracking of these, ingrowing synchronization among the runners. The applicant and his group have extensive experience in injection molding process control and monitoring, and have made significant contributions to the industry. In this project, novel synchronization control algorithms will be proposed to address the synchronization problem. A master-slave strategy will be proposed involving first selecting a proper subsystem as the master and the others as the slaves. Another dual mode optimization strategy will be introduced as well, during which the set point trajectory and the control output are optimized simultaneously. The proposed control strategies will be implemented and tested with different multi-cavity hot runner molds on an industrial size injection-molding machine. It is worthy pointing out that the synchronization control strategies developed here may find applications in other industries where synchronization is needed, as in, for example, semiconductor manufacturing. 注塑是重要的高分子加工工艺，如今多模穴热流道广泛应用提高生产率。各模穴产品的一致性取决于流道的平衡， 流道温度的一致性是关键。本项目就各流道间温度进行研究，指出各流道温度必须保持动态一致，并就其温度同步控制方法进行研究

16233316.label: Realisation of objectives
16233316.value: The modelling and control of hot runners in injection molding has been completed successfully both academically and engineeringly. A typical hot runner system consists of multiple runners depending of the number of mold cavities. Trough each runner, polymer melt is injected and packed into its corresponding and respective cavity during the injection molding filling and packing phases. The temperature of each runner affects the melt density and the rate entering the cavities. The overall objective is to ensure that hot runner temperatures are to be controlled to follow the set-point and in synchronization between runners. We conducted this study by treating (a) each runner as an agent running in parallel, and (b) each operation as a repetitive batch process. So, the problem was treated academically as multiagent batch process modeling and control problem. It is interesting to note that runner operating data can be respectively generated by each runner simultaneously. The data across runners and between batches are studied to generate relevant methods for modeling methods for both dynamic identification and process monitoring and analysis. For monitoring, we employed “big data” approach for the monitoring and analysis, monitoring methods exploring similar batch processes were developed, operating performance has been assessed so that local outlier factor can be identified, and finally transfer learning of both qualitative and quantitative knowledge for similar batch process monitoring was developed. This results in a series of journal papers [1-4, 6,7, 9, 11]. For model identification, multiagent model identification methods based on information incremental and state déjà vu methods have been developed to enhance model accuracy by exploring data from the peels (hot runners). The methods were reported in journal papers [6,10]. For control, learning control and adaptive control incorporated with models identified and performance assessment have been developed. This results in a series of journal publications [6,8,10]. Overall, 11 academic journal publication has been resulted to form foundation works on multi-agent monitoring and control and its applications. Engineering wise, a hot-runner control system was developed and tested. The temperature of each runner has been controlled to be within 0.5 deg c to the set-point, and more importantly, the maximal difference between any two runner temperatures can be also controlled within 0.5 degree C, proving effectiveness of our temperature synchronization. It needs to state that the maximal temperature differences between runners were more than 10 deg c using the traditional methods. Our prototype system will be prompted to the molding industry. Furthermore, all data from all runners can be managed and analyzed in the cloud.

16233316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16233316.value: The hot runner system has been treated as a concurrently running multi-agent system. The outcomes are these journals listed in Research Output Section. Corresponding publication are given below. On the monitoring and control for such a system, we find that: (1) Process monitoring may be enhanced by local outlier factor [Publication 7], using orthogonal subspace alignment [Publication 3], and through “big-data approaches” [Publication 1, 4]; (2) Process performance may be assessed by relevance vector machine [Publication 2], hierarchically [Publication 5], through kernel component [Publication 9], and it may be represented qualitatively and quantitatively [Publication 11]; (1) Model identification can be enhanced by using cross-process information by inter-agent learnings [Publication 6,10]; (2) Peel learning synchronization control may be implemented adaptively [Publication 6,10] and by multipoint iterative learning [Publication 8]. Through the above peel modeling and learning control, our synchronization performance can be increased significantly from the typical greater than 10 deg c to below 0.5 deg c.

16233316.value: Through this hot-runner system engineering background, we started our academic multiagent concurrent modeling and control research, this allows us in the future to develop proposals to study further such systems deeper academically, the good engineering performance will also be tested in the industry, we are pushing for possible industrialization.

16233316.value: The injection molding hot-runner has been treated and represented as a multi-agent concurrent running process system. Through this representation, monitoring and control methods have been developed to enhance the performance of the monitoring, modelling and control through peel learning and synchronization. A prototype system have been developed using the methods developed, it can be shown that the difference between runners can be significantly reduced.

16233816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16233816.value: The theory of sequence design dates back at least to 1940s. Significant progress has been made on the periodic correlation of sequences over the past 70 years. However, far less progress has been made on the aperiodic correlation of sequences, which is more relevant to practical active sensing applications such as synchronization, channel sounding, CDMA, MIMO Radar, ultrasonic medical imaging and so on. Some fundamental problems concerning the aperiodic correlation of sequences are still open. The relatively slow progress is partly due to the lack of suitable algebraic tools, unlike the periodic counterparts, for analyzing binary sequences. Recently, some sequence optimization algorithms have successfully produced examples of unimodular sequences with low peak sidelobes and high merit factors. These results provide new inspirations to address the problems of designing unimodular sequences with small peak sidelobes, large merit factors and small maximum aperiodic correlations. Besides, the analytic exponential sum methods of the number theory is found to highly suitable for analyzing the aperiodic correlation of unimodular sequences. This project proposes to partially address these fundamental problems on unimodular sequences by applying the analytical exponential sum methods to the sequence optimization results. The anticipated results will bring insights into the sequence design theory and will result in new families of sequences with particular structures, which should achieve better sensing performance with simpler matched filter implementation. 序列設計的理論發展可以追溯到20世紀40年代，在過去70年間，對序列的週期相關性的硏究已經取得了顯著的進展​​。然而，序列的非週期相關性的硏究是更切合有源傳感的實際應用，如同步，信道探測，CDMA，MIMO雷達，超聲醫學成像等。關於序列的非週期相關性的硏究進展卻比較緩慢，由於缺乏合適的數學工具，一些基本問題仍然有待解决的。最近，一些序列的優化算法已成功產生出低旁瓣峰值的單模序列的例子。這些結果為解決與設計低非週期相關性的單模序列的問題提供了新的靈感。此外，分析數論方法被發現非常適合於分析單模序列的非週期相關性。此項目擬通過應用分析數論和序列優化的方法來部分解決單模序列的這些基本問題。預期的結果將帶來序列設計理論的新見解，新序列設計與其特定結構應帶來較簡單的匹配濾波器實現和更好感知性能。

16233816.label: Realisation of objectives
16233816.value: During the later half of the project period (2019-2020), Hong Kong experienced social unrest, and then the world experienced (and is still experiencing) the COVID-19 pandemic. During the social unrest period, the original plan to recruit a postdoc from mainland China became unrealistic and research assistants/postgraduate students contributing to this project returned to mainland China to ensure their safety. Since Nov 2019, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, recruiting a new postdoc traveling to HK becomes impossible. Thanks to the online meeting software ZOOM, the research productivity of all existing postgraduate students in my team has been maintained. However, due to the lack of a suitable postdoc with sufficiently strong sequence design background to work closely with me to construct the proofs of mathematical conjectures discovered during the first half of the project, Objectives 2 and 3 during the second half of this project are not restricted to root-of-unity/unimodular sequences (i.e. spreading codes) and sequence optimization algorithms but are relaxed to include the optimized design of general codes and decoders. It is considered that this is a necessary measure for maintaining research productivity during the special period 2019-2020. Regarding Objective 1, it is proved that the aperiodic peak autocorrelation sidelobe (PSL) of a class of perfect root-of-unity sequences, called the basic Zadoff-Chu sequences, is of the order of the square root of the sequence length. It is found that under some mild condition on the decimation factor, the PSL of the decimated Zadoff-Chu sequences is also of the order of the square root of the sequence length. This enlarges the class of perfect root-of-unity sequences whose PSL has the smallest known order of growth as the length increases. Regarding Objective 2, it has been discovered via extensive numerical results that the merit factor of the aforementioned class of perfect root-of-unity sequences is of the order of the square root of the sequence length. But the proof of this conjecture is not yet available. To achieve the relaxed Objective 2, for the class of capacity-approach low-density lattice codes (LDLC), a new message passing decoder with complexity being linear in the row/column degree of the parity check matrix, was devised from the lattice viewpoint by analyzing the convergence of the message variances as the code length increases. It improves over the existing M-Gaussian decoder, which has a complexity being exponential in the degree parameter. In addition, for a differential decode-and-forward relay network supporting simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT), a new near-optimal detector/decoder based on the lattice viewpoint was introduced and its analytical performance bound was derived to confirm its near maximum likelihood decoding performance. Regarding Objective 3, we extended and optimized the generalized Levenshtein bound for two or more two-dimensional sequences (also called a quasi-complementary sequence set) with low non-trivial aperiodic auto- and cross-correlation sums. The original optimization problem is non-convex. By formulating the associated optimization problem as the so-called indefinite fractional quadratic programming and analytically deriving an explicit solution, we have successfully tightened the generalized Levenshtein bound of aperiodic correlation sums with a proof that the optimizing parameters are asymptotically locally optimizers. This result also sheds some light on the design of optimal family. To further achieve the relaxed Objective 3, for the class of best-known minimum-distance linear block codes with short block lengths, new codes with much smaller error coefficients (or kissing numbers) were discovered. For example, a new (64,32) PAC code that outperforms the previous best-known code by 0.36dB and is only 0.29 dB from the Polyanskiy-Poor-Verdu information-theoretic bound on finite-blocklength random codes. This record-breaking result was obtained by our new search strategy using Arikan's polarization-adjusted convolutional (PAC) code as a sieve. The target applications of short blocklength codes include (but not limited to) the 5G ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC) and optical camera communications (also called display-camera communications) in the IEEE standard 802.15.7m. Furthermore, using the machine learning approach, two new joint encoder-decoder design for cooperative communication networks based on deep neural networks were proposed. For small networks, they gave superior performance than the conventional design approach.

16233816.value: The major findings of this project have been detailed in Section 5.3. The aforementioned research outcomes associated with Objective 1 have been published partially in one journal paper in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing [J1], and two conference papers [C2], [C8]. Those associated with Objective 2 have been disseminated in one journal paper in IEEE Transactions on Green Communications [J6] and four conference papers [C7], [C9], [C11], [C12]. Those associated with Objective 3 have been published partially in [J1] and in four additional journal papers (including IEEE Transactions on Image Processing [J2], [J3], IEEE Transactions on Communications [J4], and IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications [J5]) as well as six conference papers/video presentation [C1], [C3]-[C6]. 16233816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16233816.value: In this project, it is proved that the peak sidelobe of some perfect root-of-unity sequences can achieve the smallest known order of growth (i.e., order 1/2) as the length increases. It was conjecture that the merit factor of such sequences behaves in the same way. An interesting future work is to construct a rigorous proof of the conjecture so as to shed light on the merit factor of such sequences. Hopefully, the insight will allow more general classes of root-of-unity sequences with excellent peak sidelobe and merit factor to be constructed. Such sequences find important applications in radar, synchronization and channel sensing applications. The lattice interpretation of the message passing decoder for distributed LDLC codes and that of the near-maximum-likelihood-detector for SWIPT-enabled differential decode-and-forward relay networks have resulted in more efficient design of low-complexity decoders. Though the lattice viewpoint is not new, its usage in a more sophisticated form can be applied to simplify a wide range of existing decoders, especially, for cooperative communication systems. Our search strategy based on Arikan's PAC code allows us to discover short record-breaking linear block codes of lengths up to 64 bits. This is a promising approach to discover short codes for low-latency communications. However, codes of lengths up to 256 bits are needed for practical applications. It is therefore important to investigate how to extend the search strategy to codes of short but practical lengths, in spite of the fact that the search space size grows exponentially with the code length. The above lists some promising directions for further development of the research results in this project and new research projects to explore these promising directions and realize their full potentials should be proposed in the future.

16233816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16233816.value: Perfect root-of-unity sequences and quasi-complementary sequences represent two famous families of pseudo-random spreading codes with important applications in radars, synchronization and channel sensing applications. However, the full theoretical characterization of their fundamental properties are far from complete. This research sheds light on their correlation properties which result in desirable performance in applications. In cooperative communication systems (with relays and/or distributed coding), the applicability of near-optimal decoders is significantly limited by their high complexity. This research shows that low-complexity near-optimal decoders can be devised by reformulating the conventional detection problem from a lattice viewpoint so that significant simplification can be achieved. The growing importance of low-latency communications require the use of block codes of short lengths. This research demonstrates that the proposed search strategy based on the polarization-adjusted code framework allows new codes with record-breaking performance to be discovered. They find potential important applications in 5G Ultra-reliable Low-latency Communications and Optical Camera Communications.

16234316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16234316.value: Personalized healthcare wearable sensors are quickly emerging worldwide in recent years. By recording a healthy person’s vital signs routinely, a personalized health database can be formed so that un-healthy/abnormal conditions can be spotted at an early stage. This could greatly improve the quality of life and reduce expenditure on medical treatments. Many research efforts have been made to this end. However, wearable medical sensors are still large, which discomforts customers so as to prevent their wide adoption. A small form factor is critical for such applications, which requires higher level of circuit integration and much smaller batteries. As a matter of fact, the sensing node could be powered by many energy sources around us. Among them, the most reliable is ambient RF power. The typical harvestable RF energy in the urban environment has been measured at about 60mJ/day, which is very little. In order to use this energy to power sensing nodes, there are two major challenges. 1. At this low input RF power level (<-30dBm), existing harvesting structures have very low efficiency (<10%). Hence, most of 60mJ available will be lost; 2. If the sensing node records for 1 minute in every hour, the power requirement of the sensing node should be <40uW, which includes sensing, digitization, digital processing, and wireless communication. Existing circuits consume much more power. Although low-power circuit techniques have been widely studied, it is seldom researched in the context of a complete sensing node, which has special circuit requirements and includes power from all circuits. It is the vision of this project that innovative system-level and circuit-level techniques can be explored to push the circuit power closer to its limit for a wearable sensing node and to improve the harvesting efficiency for weak RF signals. Hence, this project aims to investigate techniques leading to a self-powered ExG (electromyography, electrocardiography, electroencephalography) sensing node. Investigators of the project have extensive experience of relevant energy-efficient sensory circuit design and antenna design. With industrial help, the project team is in a unique position to carry out the research in this proposal. This project will open a door to ubiquitous wearable sensors. By exchanging the ExG sensor in this project for other sensors, a wide range of new Internet-of-things applications can be enabled. It could help to create a huge consumer market comparable to the telecom market.

16234316.label: Realisation of objectives
16234316.value: In this project, we have mainly researched on the design of system and devices to harvest ambient RF energy efficiently. We have also researched in sensing circuitry design with minimized power consumption. We have also researched on the design of energy-efficient transceiver for body-area communication. The project team has made quite a few new designs and findings, which have achieved state-of-the-art performance. The designs and findings from this project have led to the publication of 5 journal papers and 2 conference papers, with 2 PHD students being trained. The detailed achievements of the objectives are as follows. 1. We have made breakthrough in the study of the low-power RF energy harvesting system. We have made new designs of the RF energy harvesting system, which achieve state-of-the-art power efficiency for input power as low as -30dBm. 2. We have studied and made design of energy-minimal sensing circuitry in a 0.18um CMOS process. The design is fabricated and tested. 3. We have studied and made the design of a 16-bit SAR ADC in a 0.18um CMOS process with minimum energy consumption. The design if fabricated and tested. 4. We have studied the minimum-energy transmission in the body-area network, and have made new findings of the BAN power consumption. We are in the middle of the design of the BAN transceiver in the 0.18um CMOS process. This task is behind the schedule due to the limited capability of the student in charge of this design. 5. Due to the slow progress of the transceiver, we haven’t completed the ExG sensing node design yet. However, the RF energy-harvesting module, the sensing circuitries are all ready. Regarding this project, the main problem that the research team has met is the limited experience of the student in charge of the transceiver design. Due to the limited resources form the project, it is not possible to hire another student to work on this task. Nonetheless, the project is still working on the design of the transceiver. It is expected to complete the design in following year.

16234316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16234316.value: In this project, we focused on researching in three major frontiers: ambient RF energy harvesting, low-power sensing circuitry, and the low-power radio transceiver. Progress has been made in all three aspects. 1. Ambient RF energy harvesting We have researched deeply into the ambient RF harvesting problem. We have developed a specialized measurement system to measure the ambient RF power around typical users. From this research, we found the ambient RF power, bandwidth and varying pattern. Based on these first-hand data, we have developed one type of efficient rectifier for the task. We have also studied to harvest such low energy with specially designed small antenna. Eventually, we have developed a complete harvesting system including antenna and rectifier chip to harvest -30dBm ambient RF energy with the highest efficiency ever reported. The designed circuitry can harvest uW ambient RF power. 2. Low-power sensing circuitry We have researched on the low-power sensing system. We have developed low-power voltage sensing circuits and low-power current sensing circuits. We have also developed a SAR ADC with very high energy efficiency to quantize the signal from the voltage sensing circuits and current sensing circuits. The chip was fabricated and tested. 3. Low-power radio transceiver Similar to the study on ambient RF, we started to study the application environment of low-power radio transceiver, which is mainly used in the body-area network. We have developed a specialized electronic system to measure the radio link in the body-area network. From this system, we have measured the link losses for different communication scenarios. Based on this first-hand data, we started to design a low-power receiver with a new architecture. However, this research progress has been a bit slow due to the limited capability of the participating student designer.

16234316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16234316.value: Further development in following directions will be conducted: 1. Radio transceiver The design of the radio transceiver is still under-going. As the involved student is more efficient now, we plan to complete the transceiver design in the following 1 year. 2. Integrated sensing node With the transceiver completed, we plan to integrate the ambient RF harvester, the sensing circuitry and RF transceiver in a module. However, this could take longer time to complete as the RF transceiver needs to be verified first.

16234316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16234316.value: In this project. the project team has researched on developing an efficient way to harvest the very weak RF energy from the ambient environment around us. The team has successfully designed specialized measurement system to gather the RF signal characteristics around us. Based on the first-hand data, we have developed special antennas and rectifiers to efficiently harvest this weak power with very high efficiency. Eventually, our fabricated system can harvest uW power from the environment. This is a major breakthrough in the RF energy harvesting field. The project team also has developed very low-power sensing circuitry and analog-to-digital converters. Those fabricated circuits consume uW power. At the same time, the project team also designed a specialized system to measure the power loss for data communication around the human body. From this system, we have measured the power loss for exchanging data between electronic systems around the human. Such data is very helpful for the design of energy-efficient RF transceivers.

16234716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16234716.value: 過去幾年目睹了生物測序技術的驚人發展，使得對繁多的生物體進行快速且具有成本效益的測序成為可能，此類生物體也包括愛滋病毒與C型肝炎病毒在內的病毒。這產生了大量（公開可用）的序列數據，並開啟了嶄新的研究機會與挑戰。各種現代化的「下一代測序」的實驗，尤其是針對病毒的實驗，都有個主要特性，那就是他們在不同的時間點於多個例子中進行基因組測定，因此涵蓋了關於演化上前所未有的信息。 通過利用此基因序列數據之時間序列的性質，一個重大的挑戰是推論生物學上重要的因素，例如突變的適應度代價。推論特定病毒變體之適應度或者相當於「淘汰係數」的能力是個大問題，可能具有拯救生命之重大意義。舉例來說，Co-I Chakraborty在其近來令人興奮的研究工作中，推論愛滋病毒中某些蛋白質的淘汰係數，並將其用於發展新型疫苗設計。雖然這些貢獻在透過病毒序列數據來推論淘汰係數上，提供了第一次成功的嘗試，這些貢獻並沒有利用時間信息，使其在應用範圍上相當的明確。 基於時間序列信息來推論淘汰係數的任務可以用數學公式表示，從而產生一個高度複雜之非線性優化問題。因此，所獲得之解決方式與相關估計方法僅適用於有兩個病毒變體之簡單系統，這在實作上完全不切實際。此外，傳統的模型一般不納入驅使病毒演化之關鍵因素，像是那些與免疫壓力有關之因素。 此提出之計畫將旨在通過採用統計信息處理之概念來處理這些重要問題，以使用第一次用於任意病毒變體數目之時間序列基因序列數據來建立一個強大的淘汰係數估計架構。在廣泛的矩技術方法與擴散近似之基礎上，具有計算效率之新一類估計式將被發展出來。此採樣雜聲之重要統計問題將藉由應用高維數理統計之創新方法與納入隱馬爾可夫模型來解釋，且該估計式將被設計成能夠明確地解釋關鍵之演化因素，例如免疫系統的影響。 此計畫之主要成果將是一新穎且強大的淘汰係數估計架構，適用於病毒之時間序列數據。作為一個實際應用的例子，此架構將被應用到各種C型肝炎數據集合，且所推論之淘汰係數將與已知的生物實驗數據進行比對驗證。接著，這些結果會被用來提出針對C型肝炎的新疫苗設計，試圖通過迫使C型肝炎病毒從高適應度變異成為低適應度狀態來提供給宿主免疫力。總體策略為對PI 與 Co-Is於[20,37,39]之初步工作提供更詳細的闡述。該初期工作有考慮到C型肝炎與愛滋病毒疫苗設計之問題，但沒有充分利用序列數據中的時間信息基於C型肝炎與其他病毒數據集合是從與時間強烈相關之過程取樣而來，由此計畫發展出之時間序列估計方法所生成的疫苗設計，預計會更有效許多。

16234716.label: Realisation of objectives
16234716.value: Objective 1: Develop a selection coefficient estimator for an arbitrary number of viral variants. This objective was successfully completed, with results in Journal Paper 3. We developed a selection coefficient estimator not only for an arbitrary number of viral variants, but also for a generalized multi-locus model which jointly incorporates selection, mutation, recombination and temporal sampling. This new selection coefficient estimator was designed to estimate the selection coefficients based on genetic time-series data. The estimates were obtained through a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation procedure, which first required forming the likelihood function. To obtain the likelihood function, we first derived a diffusion approximation for the mutant frequency trajectories, which in turn required derivations of the drift vector and diffusion matrix. Based on the diffusion approximation, we then formulated a path-integral representation of the allele frequencies, which characterizes the probability that the observed genetic time-series data follows a certain trajectory. This path-integral representation was then used to form the likelihood function, after which the MAP estimate was obtained. We ran numerous tests to verify that our estimator was not only very accurate, but very fast. We also conducted extensive tests with other estimators, with results indicating our estimator was the most accurate and fastest, in some cases orders of magnitude faster than other estimators. Objective 2: Implement noise-cleaning approaches for providing robust estimates of the proposed selection coefficient estimator. This objective was completely addressed with main results in Journal Paper 3. Here, we accounted for two types of noise. First, we considered noise-cleaning approaches to deal with insufficient samples at each time point. We achieved this by incorporating L2 regularization in the selection coefficient estimate, which has the effect of balancing between overfitting noise, and underfitting the data. We ran numerous robustness tests over a wide range of parameters, i.e., selection coefficient values and mutation rates, and showed a high classification performance even with moderate sampling. The second type of noise is when data is not obtainable at every single time point, i.e., temporal sampling. To deal with this issue, we considered a mathematical approach to obtain the drift vector and diffusion matrix. Conventional approaches to derive these quantities with complete temporal information involved conditioning statistical values on the previous time point. We extended this approach to condition on the previous “observed” time point, thus accounting for temporal sampling. This was not a trivial extension, as it involved new derivations to condition out these missing data. The result was a modified selection coefficient estimate which is a function of the number of time points missing. We ran numerous robustness tests, showing again that our method achieves a high classification accuracy even with a high number of missing time points. Objective 3: Extend the inference framework to account for epistatic forces. This objective was also addressed. The main results were presented in Journal Papers 1 and 2. In Journal Paper 1, we adopted an algorithm which can measure epistatic forces, through the so-called “coupling parameters” of the maximum entropy model. These parameters can be used to predict the fitness of specific viral strains. We showed through comparison with experimentally derived fitness values that our predicted fitness including epistasis resulted in a much better correlation than excluding epistasis, indicating the importance of accounting for epistatic forces. In Journal Paper 2, epistatic forces were also studied in the context of poliovirus evolution. Specifically, by employing the maximum entropy modelling approach, it was shown that epistasis plays a role in spawning spatio-temporally localized outbreaks of polio. Mutations which seeded these outbreaks tended to be those which lead to partial immune escape at the population level, but these tended to be coupled with epistatically linked mutations at other positions. Objective 4: Apply the proposed estimation strategies to viral sequences, in order to identify potential vulnerabilities which may be exploited for vaccine design. This final objective was completely addressed, in Journal Papers 1-3. We applied our computational framework to estimate epistasis parameters to the E2 protein of HCV in Journal Paper 1. This framework was combined with an evolutionary simulation model to predict which antigenic domains are ideal targets of antibodies, as mutations in these domains will result in a low viral load. Specific antibodies targeting these domains are identified, which can inform the rational design of vaccines. In Journal Paper 2, we applied our fitness models to data from the vp1 protein of poliovirus. This analysis demonstrated vulnerabilities than can contribute to polio outbreaks, through mutations occurring at the sites targeted by antibodies induced by the polio vaccine. Moreover, the analysis helped to provide a rational answer to the question of why poliovirus has been relatively easy to develop a vaccine against, whereas for HIV we still do not have an effective vaccine, despite the fact that both viruses have similar mutation rates. A rationale was presented by comparing the fitness models of proteins of both viruses. In Journal Paper 3, we applied our selection coefficient estimator to time-series genetic data from 13 patients with HIV. We predicted driver escape mutations in T-cell epitopes of HIV. This is important as our selection coefficient estimator can distinguish between mutations arising in frequency due to linkage, in other words, “false positive” driver mutations. This knowledge has the potential to design effective T-cell based vaccines which can avoid targeting epitopes with strong escape mutations.

16234716.label: Major findings and research outcome
16234716.value: [Journal paper 1] This paper applied an algorithm which inferred epistasis parameters to HCV sequence data, with the aim find the optimal antibody for a vaccine. This framework combined the epistasis estimated parameters with an evolutionary simulation model, to quantify the relative reduction in viral load of different antibodies for HCV. We were able to determine the ideal antigenic domain to target, and the antibodies which target this domain. This is significant, as our study provided a new framework for quantifying antibody effectiveness, paving the way for effective in-silico vaccine designs. [Journal Paper 2] This paper developed fitness models for the vp1 protein of the poliovirus, to study the mechanisms by which polio outbreaks occur, and to explore why vaccine development for polio has been relatively easy, while for HIV we still do not have an effective vaccine. The analysis demonstrated that epistasis may play a role in outbreak dynamics, by complementing the fitness of antibody escape mutations. It was also shown that polio is more “brittle” compared with HIV, in that its fitness is much more sensitive to mutations. This help to provide a scientific explanation for why polio vaccine development has been far easier than for HIV, despite the fact that both viruses have similar mutation rates. [Journal Paper 3] This paper proposed a new method to estimate selection coefficients from time-series genetic data. Our model included a generalized framework allowing for multiple variants, mutation, selection and recombination. Our estimator is highly robust to both incomplete samples per time point, and missing time points. We also demonstrated higher accuracy and orders of magnitude faster runtimes compared to all competing estimators. The methods in this paper will be of significant interest to any researcher requiring estimation of evolutionary parameters from time series data. We applied our method to HIV data, providing new insights into the key drivers of escape in T-cell epitopes, which can inform vaccine design. Generally, the project has produced high impact publications. Two published papers are in Nature Communications; the third paper has been favorably reviewed in Nature Biotechnology, and a revision has been submitted.

16234716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16234716.value: There are various avenues for future development. One important application is extending the selection coefficient estimation framework to estimate other important evolutionary parameters, such as the mutation rate, recombination rate and population size. This is an important problem as it provides important insights into fundamental evolutionary processes in nature. There has been very limited work considering estimation using our generalized model of evolution. Given the accuracy and efficiency of our selection coefficient estimate, there is significant potential in obtaining accurate estimates for these other parameters. Another avenue for future development is applying our selection coefficient estimator to other viruses and proteins. There is untapped potential to obtain interesting biological insights. For example, applying our estimator to influenza time-series data may reveal important drivers of selection. This can inform the design of more accurate seasonal vaccines.

16234716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16234716.value: This project provided new computational algorithms to estimate epistasis and selection coefficients from genetic data. Our algorithms have been verified through robustness tests and comparisons with competing methods, with our selection coefficient estimator algorithm outperforming all competitors both in accuracy and runtime. We applied our algorithms to important biological problems, e.g., the design of vaccines for viruses. Applications were presented for HCV, HIV, and poliovirus.

16234816.label: Project Objectives
16234816.value: Estimate strain time history characteristics at unmeasured hot spot locations by combining output-only vibration measurements from a sensor network installed at a limited number of structural locations with the information built into a computational mathematical model of the structure. Explore filter estimation techniques (similar in structure to the Kalman filter) in order to simultaneously estimate input and output states and predict strains from either acceleration or strain time history measurements (or a combination thereof). Optimize the sensor configuration for improving strain estimation. An entropy-based method will be developed to optimize the sensor configuration for improving strain estimation at unmeasured hot spot locations. The developed method will be well-suited for making quantitative evaluations and comparisons of the quality of the strain estimates that are achieved using different sensor configurations. Estimate fatigue damage accumulation maps based on monitoring data. In recognition of the uncertainties present and the randomness inherent in the nature of the fatigue phenomenon, it is appropriate to conduct fatigue assessment in a comprehensive probabilistic way, i.e., obtain a reliable probability density function of the fatigue damage accumulation and the residual life. As a result, the failure probability can also be obtained based on such a fatigue damage accumulation model. When continuous monitoring data are available, it is desirable to update the structural failure probability to obtain a more robust assessment of it.
