16241916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16241916.value: The boom in telecom technology has created large numbers of smart-phone subscribers, giving huge volumes of real-time telecommunication records, which we call telco big data. With the popularity of smart-phones and mobile networks, phones have become ubiquitous in peoples’ daily life. Compared with other types of spatiotemporal data, such as taxi GPS data and public transportation data, telco big data have two advantages. First, the number of registered subscribers is very large. Second, the data records, containing around-the-clock spatiotemporal information of signaling, internet connection, application usage, and calling records, are much denser. As a result, telco big data has become a unique data source for analyzing human behaviors. Analysis of telco big data has many important applications such as infectious disease transmission tracking, outdoor advertisement location selection, and people flow monitoring. Though many data mining techniques have been proposed for spatiotemporal data, visualization is used widely to show both the distribution and also aggregate values of the data, as well as results from data mining. However, several issues remain. First, telco big data is biased and incomplete. Fortunately other types of urban data such as taxi GPS data, public transportation data and social media date are available. How to integrate telco big data with other heterogeneous urban data is an interesting research problem. Second, the very fine-grained telco data make it possible for users to conduct visual analytics for social networks within spatio-temporal context in telco data, develop visual classifiers for data analysis, and plan context-aware events with spatio-temporal constraints. In this project, we propose to investigate these problems arising from telco big data and develop novel visual analytical techniques for these problems. The PI's team has worked with Huawei, a big telecommunication company in China, on telco data analysis and some preliminary results have been published in the IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (IEEE VAST 2015). 隨著移動通訊技術的蓬勃發展，大量的智能手機用戶在使用手機服務，從而通訊商的服務管道裡也產生了很多的實時通訊紀錄；我們把這種紀錄中所包含的數據叫做電信大數據。智能手機和移動通訊網絡的普及也使得智能手機服務在人們在日常生活中中無處不在。和其他類型的時空數據相比較，譬如的士數據和公共交通數據，電信大數據有兩大優勢。第一，用戶量大；第二，數據稠密，包括24小時不間斷的信令數據、互聯網連結數據，應用數據，和通話數據。因此，電信大數據對於人類行為分析和研究任務，已然成為獨一無二的數據源。此类研究有很多重要的应用场景，譬如传染病追踪、室外广告选址和人群流动的监控。 許多數據挖掘技術被提出用於解決時空數據的挖掘，可視化技術也被廣泛應用在描述數據的分佈特徵、聚合值、以及數據挖掘的結果。儘管如此，在對時空數據的挖掘和分析中仍然存在若干問題。第一，電信大數據作為一種城市數據源是有失偏頗且不完整的。所幸的是，除了電信大數據，還有的士數據，公共交通數據，和社交網絡數據，可以作為描述城市的數據源。從而，如何把電信大數據和其他類型的城市數據源做數據整合，就成為一個有趣的研究課題。第二，電信大數據中所包含的信息非常細緻，這些信息有助於針對社交網絡做可視分析和研究， 借助構建可視的分類器，在時空限制條件下也能做有效的情景感知和任務計畫。 在本項目中，我們旨在設計和開發新穎的可視分析技術，為解決電信大數據中存在的上述問題做進一步的探索。首席研究員及其領導下的團隊和華為技術有限公司合作已經在電信大數據分析領域產出了一些初步的研究結果，2105年已發表在可視化領域的頂級會議IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (IEEE VAST 2015)上。

16241916.label: Realisation of objectives
16241916.value: We have achieved the objectives of this research project. Objective 1: To develop a visual analytical framework for fusing telco data with other urban spatio-temporal data (e.g. , taxi GPS data, public transportation data and social media data). We have developed MobiSeg [C1], an interactive visual analytics framework which can fuse three types heterogeneous mobility data (i.e., taxi trajectories, metro passenger RFID card data, and telco data) and then conduct joint analysis. Based on the framework, we can segment an urban area into regions sharing similar human activity patterns. We have integrated advanced analytical algorithms (e.g., non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) based method to capture latent activity patterns, as well as metric learning to calibrate and supervise the underlying analysis) and novel visualization designs into the MobiSeg system to provide a comprehensive solution for human activity analysis. Objective 2: To develop novel techniques for visualizing social networks within spatio-temporal context in telco big data to help people gain deeper insight into human activities. We have developed a novel spatio-temporal flow map for visualizing movement and contact patterns [J5]. Based on the telco big data, we can analyze how people move from one place to another place. However, people often meet friends or other people at a common location, which creates contact relationship among them. Flow map is widely used to display the movements of humans from one single source to multiple destinations by representing locations as nodes and movements as edges. However, it could not visualize both movement and contact data. We have proposed a novel spatio-temporal flow map layout to visualize when and where people from different locations move into the same places and make contact. We can integrate the new spatiotemporal flow maps into existing spatiotemporal visualization techniques to form a suite of techniques for visualizing the movement and contact patterns. Objective 3: To design visual classifiers for data analysis in urban context. We have developed TPFlow [J4] as a visual classifier for explorative analysis of large-scale multidimensional spatio-temporal (ST) data in urban context using a top-down, progressive partitioning approach. We have proposed a novel tensor-based algorithm to support automated partitioning and multi-dimensional pattern extraction on ST data. The algorithm is grounded on quantitative measure about how faithfully the extracted patterns can visually represent the original data. This work has won the best paper award at IEEE VAST 2018. We have developed StreetVizor [j2], an interactive visual analytics system based on a visual classifier which can classify human-scale urban forms into different categories (e.g., greenery, sky, building, road, and vehicle) by applying deep learning techniques on Google Street View (GSV) images. Based on real-world datasets containing ∼ 1.7 million of GSV images of four cities: Singapore, Hong Kong, Greater London, and New York City, we have trained SegNet and achieved a global accuracy of 82.8%, out of the different classification techniques that we tried. We further augment the results with various visualization techniques to help urban planners develop high-quality urban spaces through evidence-based design. Objective 4. To develop visual analytics methods for context-aware event planning with spatial-temporal constraints. We developed SmartAdp [j1] to help companies formulate strategies for placing advertisement billboards in a city. A billboard campaign often needs to consider multiple attributes like the total budget, the price of each available billboard, the location and visibility of each billboard, and the movement of the target customers. SmartAdp combines the state-of-the-art data mining and visualization techniques to tackle the problem using large-scale GPS trajectory data. The system can allow people efficiently find good solutions in a huge solution space and then compare the solutions in a visual and intuitive manner. We have also proposed SkyLens [J3], a visual analytic system that assists users in exploring and comparing skyline from different perspectives and at different scales. Skyline queries have wide-ranging applications in fields that involve multi-criteria decision making, including tourism, retail industry, and human resources. By automatically removing incompetent candidates, skyline queries allow users to focus on a subset of superior data items (i.e., the skyline), thus reducing the decision-making overhead. There are multiple skyline query algorithms available. SkyLens augments these algorithms with novel data visualization techniques to help people deal with fuzzy, unstable, and inconsistent preferences when presented with multiple candidates and also reveal the reasons for the superiority of certain skyline points in a multi-dimensional space.

16241916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16241916.value: This research project has resulted in two PhD theses and six papers, four of which have been published in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG), the top journal in data visualization. One paper has won the best paper award at IEEE VAST 2018. We have developed multiple frameworks, techniques and systems for analyzing telco big data as well as other urban big data. These techniques have addressed various challenges arising from analyzing spatio-temporal heterogeneous data. First, we have developed MobiSeg [C1], an interactive visual analytics framework for fusing telco data with other urban spatio-temporal data (e.g., taxi trajectories, metro passenger RFID card data) and conducting joint analysis. Second, we have developed TPFlow [J4] which uses a novel tensor-based algorithm to support automated partitioning and multidimensional pattern extraction on spatio-temporal data, which are more suitable for visualization than traditional representations. Third, we have designed a new visualization called spatio-temporal flow map [J5] to visualize when and where people from different locations move into the same places as well as their contact patterns. Forth, we have developed SkyLens [J3], a visual analytic system which supports multi-criteria decision making using skyline queries. Finally, two practical systems (i.e., SmartAdp [J1] and StreetVizor [J2]) have been developed to help billboard advertisement campaign based on taxi trajectory data and also urban planning based on human-scale urban forms. All these techniques integrate automated data mining algorithms and interactive data visualization techniques to leverage both the machine intelligence and human intelligence.

16241916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16241916.value: There are two research directions which can be pursued in the future. In this project, we have investigated the integration of Telco Big data with traffic data and also RFID data for joint analysis. Other data like air quality and weather data can also be considered as many real world applications in urban context have to deal with environment issues. Second, as deep learning has been widely adopted in anyalzing telco big data and other urban big data and achieved unprecedented performance, how to understand and explain the results generated from the black-box deep learning algorithms becomes an important research issue.

16241916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16241916.value: To build smart city, we need to collect and analyze a lot of data generated by human activities. With the popularization of mobile phones, telecommunication operators can collect enormous amounts of data every day, called telco data. Analyzing telco big data can shed lights on human behaviors and have high research and practical values. In this project, we integrate automatic machine learning methods and data visualization techniques to leverage both the computational power and smart algorithms, and also the human visual systems and human domain knowledge for better usage and analysis of telco big data and other data collected in urban context. Multiple frameworks and systems have been developed and used in various domains. For example, urban planners can use our StreetVizor system to compare the differences in human-scale urban forms of two streets in Brooklyn, New York City and Kowloon, Hong Kong. Companies can use our SmartAdp system to decide where to place advertisements in billboards to best draw attentions of their target customers. Our MobiSeg system has helped experts from an urban planning bureau in Shanghai to segment the city areas into different activity-oriented regions (e.g., shopping malls, residential areas, office blocks) based on telco and other data.

16242016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16242016.value: In the past several decades, massive bridges have been built around the world to satisfy economic development requirements and human travel needs. Cable-stayed bridges are constructed in cases where a relatively long span is needed. Most of the pylons of a cable-stayed bridge are vertical but some bridge pylons were designed with a slope in the past two decades, for not only an artistic appearance but also superior load-bearing performance. In addition, vertical slender structures built on mountain slopes are subjected to pitching flow induced by the slope itself, which is equivalent to an inclined structure being immersed in a horizontal flow. For slender structures, such as bridge pylons and tall buildings, wind-induced vibration is a primary structural design concern. Although the inclined structures or equivalent inclined structures are not rare in reality, there are yet very few studies on their wind-induced vibration. Most previous studies concerned flow-induced vibrations of vertical structures instead. By intuition, we know that inclination alters the flow field around a structure and changes its aerodynamic properties therefore comprehensive research on inclined structures is necessary. Studies have in fact been conducted on infinite length (two-dimensional) circular cylinders inclined from the vertical but most of them have focused on the aerodynamic characteristics of cables. Very little attention has been put on inclined finite cylinders, especially square prisms, which is the prototype of inclined bridge pylons and tall buildings subjected to a pitching flow on the mountain slope. Because circular sections and square sections have very different aerodynamic characteristics, the flow field around an inclined square prism is believed to be significantly different from that around an inclined circular cylinder. Hence, aerodynamic and aeroelastic behavior also differ significantly between the two. To our best knowledge, the fluid-structure interactions, i.e. the interrelationship of flow field and aeroelastic behavior, of an inclined finite square prism have not yet been systematically investigated. The primary goal of the proposed research will be to understand the fluid-structure interactions of an inclined prism at different wind conditions. This is to be achieved by devising and combining novel wind tunnel techniques in order to simultaneously acquire aerodynamic forces, wind-induced vibrations and flow field topology. The influence of inclination on the flow field will be further decoded using PIV measurements and coupled fluid-structure CFD simulations. The benefits of the research will be to characterize the underlying excitation mechanism of an inclined prism and hence to advance the wind-resistant design. 為滿足社會經濟發展和人們出行的需求，在過去幾十年中，大量橋梁日益建成。斜拉橋是大跨橋梁常采用的結構形式。在過去二十年建成的斜拉橋中，大多數橋塔是豎直的，但從美觀和受力的角度，傾斜橋塔也常常受到設計者的青睞。此外，建於斜坡上的豎直結構，由於斜坡的影響，風會以傾斜角的形式作用於結構上，這種作用等效於水平風作用於豎直的結構。 對於柔性結構，如高聳的建築結構和橋塔，風致影響是結構設計首要考慮的問題。風致豎直結構響應的研究較多，但風致傾斜結構的相關研究較少，盡管這些傾斜結構或等效傾斜結構比較常見。傾斜角會改變結構風場的分布以及氣動特性，因而風致傾斜結構的響應的研究十分必要。壹些學者針對無限長（二維）傾斜圓柱結構進行了，這些研究大多關於斜拉索的氣動特性，對有現限長（三維）傾斜結構的研究很少，尤其是對於傾斜方柱或傾斜風作用下的豎直方柱的研究很少，如傾斜橋塔、傾斜風作用下的豎直建築結構等。圓柱和方柱的氣動特性有很大的不同，其周圍的風場分布不同，因而，方柱和圓柱的氣動和氣彈特性也會有很大的不同。傾斜方柱流固藕合的作用，如風場分布和氣彈特性的相互作用，還未見相關系統的研究。 本研究的主要目的是掌握傾斜方柱在不同風場作用下流固藕合的作用。主要通過新型的同步氣彈-測壓-測風場分布綜合的風洞試驗技術來實現課題的研究。傾斜角對風場分布的研究主要結合粒子成像（PIV）和數值模擬（CFD）方法實現。研究成果可以解釋風致傾斜結構作用的機理，從而補充和完善風致結構影響的設計。

16242016.label: Realisation of objectives
16242016.value: A novel hybrid aeroelastic-pressure balance (HAPB) system, i.e. a wind tunnel testing rig, which can be used for simultaneously obtaining the unsteady wind pressure and aeroelastic response of a vertical or inclined prism, was designed and manufactured so as to achieve the project objectives. The nonlinear characteristics/properties of the HAPB system were at the outset identified by employing a nonlinear identification method of equivalent linearization approximation on the basis of Krylov-Bogoliubov averaging method, prior to the subsequent forced vibration tests and HAPB tests. A sequence of wind tunnel tests, including forced vibration tests and hybrid aeroelastic-pressure balance tests, was systematically performed in the boundary layer wind tunnel at the CLP Power Wind/Wave Tunnel Facility at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology using the newly-devised test rig. Unsteady wind pressures acting on the inclined prisms were synchronously sampled together with the structural responses. The unsteady crosswind forces acting on vertical and inclined prisms were analyzed with respect to spectra of generalized unsteady crosswind forces, spectra of pointwise pressures, and Strouhal numbers. The effects of forward and backward inclinations on the characteristics of aerodynamic damping in inclined prisms are found being dissimilar to a vertical prism, and the characteristics have been discussed in terms of the unsteady aerodynamic force and reduced frequency. In order to reveal the galloping mechanism of inclined prisms, two-dimensional instantaneous flow fields and instantaneous surface pressure fluctuation were simultaneously captured by synchronizing the Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) system and the multi-pressure sensing system. Two types of inclinations, i.e. forward inclination and backward inclination, were tested. Two inclination angles, i.e. α = 15° and 30° were tested for each type of inclinations. The flow fields in several horizontal planes at different heights over the whole prism span, as well as the vertical plane parallel to the oncoming flow, were measured. Based on the velocity information at various vertical and horizontal planes, both time-averaged and instantaneous spanwise vorticity distributions were investigated. It was found that the forward inclination enhances the downwash that originally appears behind the upper part of the vertical cylinder, whereas weakens the upwash that is exhibited behind the base part of the vertical cylinder. When the forward inclination angle is large enough, the downwash is enhanced to a downward axial flow, whereas the upwash is completely suppressed. On the contrary, the backward inclination depresses the downwash, while enlarges the upwash. As the backward inclination angle increases, the upwash evolves into an upward axial flow. This phenomenological investigation has identified the potential excitation mechanisms of inclined prisms. At the final stage of the project, a few mathematical or analytical models were derived in order to improve the predictions of unsteady crosswind responses, as well as to advance our understanding on aerodynamic damping and stiffness. Nonlinear mathematical models that are capable to estimate the aerodynamic damping were developed using the forced vibration data. Whilst, a nonlinear unsteady self-excited force (USEF) analytical model was formulated to quantify the galloping responses using the HAPB test data.

16242016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16242016.value: A wind tunnel testing rig was first developed and used in a series of forced vibration tests and hybrid aeroelastic-pressure balance (HAPB) tests. From the forced vibration wind tunnel tests, the characteristics of unsteady crosswind forces imposing on inclined prisms were revealed. The aerodynamic damping of inclined prisms that was identified based on the unsteady crosswind force was found to be significantly dependent on the vibration amplitudes and reduced wind velocity, especially in the proximity of vortex lock-in range. The results not only advance our understanding on aerodynamic damping of inclined prisms, but also provide values that can be used to estimate aerodynamics and aeroelasticity of inclined prisms. Nonlinear mathematical models to estimate the aerodynamic damping of inclined prisms were successfully derived using the wind tunnel measurements obtained from the forced vibration tests. The mathematical models are capable to improve the crosswind-induced vibration estimations. Two papers have been published in the top journal of wind engineering, Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics. The phenomenological flow features around inclined prisms were also captured using Particle Image Velocimetry technique and the excitation mechanisms were consequently characterized. It was found that the forward inclination enhances the downwash that originally appears behind the upper part of the vertical prism, whereas weakens the upwash that is exhibited behind the base part of the vertical prism. When the forward inclination angle is large enough, the downwash is enhanced to a downward axial flow, whereas the upwash is completely suppressed. On the contrary, the backward inclination depresses the downwash, while enlarges the upwash. As the backward inclination angle increases, the upwash evolves into an upward axial flow. In addition, the unsteady crosswind forces measured from the HAPB tests were decomposed into the aerodynamic damping force, the aerodynamic stiffness force and the residual force. The characteristics of unsteady self-excited forces (USEF) were analyzed in terms of pressure distribution, force spectrum, and Strouhal number and hence a nonlinear USEF analytical model was established to accurately quantify the galloping responses of prisms. The research findings have been published in Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics, Engineering Structures, and Nonlinear Dynamics.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16242016.value: In the past several decades, cable-stayed bridges have been built around the world to satisfy economic development requirements and human travel needs. Most of the pylons of a cable-stayed bridge are vertical but some bridge pylons were designed with a slope in the past two decades because of its superior load-bearing performance. In addition, vertical slender structures built on mountain slopes are subjected to pitching flow induced by the slope itself, which is equivalent to an inclined structure being immersed in a horizontal flow. The major outcomes of the research project include the successful development of a series of wind tunnel testing techniques to simultaneously acquire aerodynamic forces (using pressure test), wind-induced vibrations (aeroelastic test) and flow field topology (PIV test). The simultaneously-synchronized testing techniques are particularly useful to reveal fluid-structure interactions and the excitation mechanism of inclined structures in different wind conditions. The results generated from the project in the form of design solutions or guidelines have advanced the wind-resistant design of inclined slender structures, as well as vertical structures immersed in a pitching flow induced by mountain slopes.

16242216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16242216.value: The concepts of wireless transmission of signal and power emerged together in the late 1880's. Certainly, the past century has witnessed the exponential growth of wireless transmission of signal (wireless communication), such as wireless telegraph (1896), AM radio (1906), color TV (1929), mobile radio (1950), GSM phone (1992), digital TV (1999), to iPhone 6 (2015). In comparison, the demonstration of wireless transmission of power (other than through tightly coupled transformers) lags far behind. However, two major applications are driving the development of wireless power transfer (WPT): one is on the (relatively) high-power side of wireless charging, for mobile gadgets and even for electric vehicles; and the other is on the (relatively) low-power side of wirelessly powered bio-medical implants. The bottleneck of WPT has been low power transfer efficiency due to weak coupling and poor directivity. In this research, we propose to first work on the backbone knowledge for designing high-efficiency resonant wireless power transfer (R-WPT) systems. For a WPT system with weak coupling, the link gain (voltage at load / source voltage) and the link efficiency (power consumed by load / power delivered from source) could be enhanced by adding a capacitor to resonate with the inductor both at the primary and at the secondary, such that the imaginary part of the reflected equivalent impedance could be cancelled or minimized. We propose to employ a design-oriented analysis to study R-WPT systems, to arrive at link gains and link efficiencies that could be optimized easily and interpreted physically by circuit-design engineers. The results of this part of research will be useful for both high-power and low-power applications. Our next step is to attend to low-power applications of implantable medical devices (IMDs). We propose to use two coils with different orientations in intercepting fluxes, as such, the associated link gains and link efficiencies has to be derived and optimized together. On the circuit level, we will develop one-stage power processing architectures that integrate AC-DC rectification with DC-DC regulation to reduce loss. We will also develop (integrated) circuit techniques to combine power from the two coils together to enhance directivity. Finally, we will design, fabricate and test the integrated circuit power management unit (PMU), and build and test the power transponder of a low-power 1-primary 2-secondary (1P-2S) R-WPT system for bio-medical implants. We will also develop strategies for testing the PMU and the power transponder individually, and for testing the complete system.

16242216.label: Realisation of objectives
16242216.value: All objectives have been achieved, as can be shown under "Section 6: Research Outcome". A concise review is as follows. (1) Resonant wireless power transfer (R-WPT) systems with a resistive load has been analyzed, and important design parameters such as reflected impedance, link-gain and link-efficiency are derived, and formulae are written using a design-oriented approach, such that engineers can apply them for design [C8J1]. The PI also worked on R-WPT systems with a rectifier load, that is, the resonant circuit drives a full-wave rectifier followed by the output capacitor and load resistor. The manuscript will be ready for submission soon. ([C8J1] is Part C, Journal paper 1) (2) The research team has developed a few one-stage power processing architectures that combines the AC to DC rectification and DC to DC voltage regulation into one stage. The idea is to redesign the four diodes in a conventional diode bridge and turns them into active diodes plus switches. Through mode-switching control schemes discussed in [C9C3] and [C9C5], two such rectifiers have been successfully designed and tested. ([C9C3] is Part C, Conference paper 3) (3) Reverse currents are due to delays in turning on and off the switches, and delay-compensation schemes have been worked out to minimize the delays, and thus reverse currents are reduced accordingly for a 40.68 MHz active rectifier [C9C6, C8J2]. (4) Two integrated power management units (PMU-ICs) of single-stage reconfigurable resonant regulating rectifiers [C9C2, C9C3], two PMU-ICs of delay-compensation schemes [C9C6, C8J2] and one PMU-IC of a 3-coil (primary and secondary plus repeater coils) system [C9C4] have been designed, fabricated and tested. (5) To test the R-WPT systems accurately, the research team has built hardware that can measure the distance and orientation between the primary coil and the secondary coil accurately. Many testing prototypes have been built such that voltages and currents can be measured accurately. To conclude, we considered that our achievements are commeasurable with our research objectives.

16242216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16242216.value: (1) A comprehensive design-oriented analysis of various wireless power links driving a resistive load that include coupled-coils with series-resonant primary and either series-resonant secondary or parallel-resonant secondary has been conducted [C8J1]. The analysis was later extended to include the rectifier load, that is, the resonant circuit driving a rectifier connected to the load current in parallel with a filtering capacitor. The manuscript is under preparation. ([C8J1] is Part C, Journal paper 1) (2) Two one-stage schemes that integrate AC-DC rectification with DC-DC regulation have been developed. The first one is a 2-level reconfigurable resonant regulating rectifier driving a parallel-resonant secondary that is suitable for lower power such as implantable medical devices [C9C3]. The second one is a 3-level reconfigurable resonant regulating (R3) rectifier driving a series-resonant secondary that is suitable for higher power such as charging mobile phones [C9C5]. ([C9C3] is Part C, Conference paper 3) (3) Reverse currents are due to delays in turning on and off the switches, and delay-compensation schemes have been worked out to minimize the delays, and thus reverse currents are reduced accordingly for a 40.68 MHz active rectifier [C9C6, C8J2]. (4) We developed a repeater (r) coil that is placed between the primary (p) coil and the secondary (s) coil. The first advantage is to enhance the effective coupling coefficient between the primary and the secondary coils (kps) by enhancing the coupling coefficient between the primary and the repeater coils (kpr), and that between the secondary and the repeater coils (ksr). The second advantage is this: the repeater, being in-between the primary and the secondary coils, has less misalignments with both the primary and the secondary coils, and power transfer can thus be improved [C9C4]. (5) Two integrated power management units (PMU-ICs) of single-stage reconfigurable resonant regulating rectifiers [C9C2, C9C3], two PMU-ICs of delay-compensation schemes [C9C6, C8J2] and one PMU-IC of a 3-coil (primary and secondary plus repeater coils) system [C9C4] have been designed, fabricated and tested. (6) A special hardware was built to adjust the position of the repeater coil with respect to the primary and the secondary coils, thus improving the accuracy of measurements in terms of distance and orientation.

16242216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16242216.value: There are at least four directions that the research could further address. (1) Analysis of different wireless power transfer configurations have been confirmed by extensive simulation results. Hardware could carefully be built such that the analysis can further be confirmed by experimental results. (2) Better topologies, in terms of efficiency, of the one-stage reconfigurable resonant regulating rectifiers could further be investigated, constructed and measured. Designs of the control loop are functional but not optimal, and there is much to be done to improve the stability and transient responses. (3) The delay-compensation schemes discussed above are all analog implementations. Digital delay-compensation schemes should also be investigated. (4) The study of the 3-coil (primary and secondary + repeater) system has just started, and more in-depth investigation in terms of analysis and measurement could be performed.

16242216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16242216.value: It is known since the 1880's that both electromagnetic (EM) signal and electromagnetic power can be transmitted wirelessly through the atmosphere. Wireless communication technology brings convenient access to information through radio, television, mobile phone and wireless modems, while wireless power transfer (WPT) technology has not been as well established. Our research is to advance the technology of WPT so that one may power and/or charge up portable devices without using cables and adaptors of different sizes and shapes. Our work focuses on resonant wireless power transfer and there are two major obstacles: (1) weak coupling between the transmitter (primary) and the receiver (secondary), and (2) multiple power processing blocks at the receiver. For the receiver, our goal is to integrate the conventional three stages of rectifying, regulating and charging into only one stage, such that efficiency could be greatly enhanced. Effective delay compensation schemes have to be devised such that turning on and off of the switches can be very accurate. For enhancing coupling, our proposal is to investigate the use of multi-secondary coils, and one method is to use a repeater coil. Our accomplishment is the design of a WPT system that achieves better efficiency that prior arts.

16242916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16242916.value: Biopharmaceuticals are an important and fast growing class of products within the pharmaceutical industry. A typical challenge in the manufacture of biopharmaceuticals is separating a protein from a solution with impurities. Chromatography is the current industrial workhorse for separating proteins. Unfortunately, chromatography suffers from inherent scaling limitations. Crystallization is an alternative technology to replace or supplement chromatography. However, protein crystallization processes are notoriously difficult to design and operate. This research aims to develop a novel method for protein crystallization, with the potential to greatly simplify and improve crystallization of proteins, allowing its wide adoption by the biopharmaceutical industry. The method proposed adopts two approaches. First, tiny patterned electrodes introduced into a flow cell will provide spatial and dynamic control over the nucleation of crystals. Second, the proposed process will operate in a continuous flow mode instead of in a batch mode, as is the current practice in the pharmaceutical industry. Continuous operation offers a number of key advantages in the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, including simplified process control, ease of operation and process scalability. Combining spatial and dynamic control over protein nucleation with novel continuous flow technologies can provide design and operational flexibility over protein crystallization processes, alleviating the major difficulties in current manufacturing practice. Protein nucleation from solution is a poorly understood phenomenon that is notoriously difficult to control in a manufacturing process. Usually, protein nucleation is controlled by varying macroscopic variables such as temperature and composition of the protein solution. The proposed research will break with this approach by using well-controlled electric fields to induce protein nucleation at desired places at the required time. Preliminary results obtained by the applicant demonstrated the beneficial effect of electric fields on protein nucleation in a proposed experimental setup. In order to provide a scientific basis for realizing the observed benefit in industrial practice, an experimental and computational program to understand and optimize the mechanism underlying the observed electric-field-enhanced protein nucleation in continuous flow is proposed. Finally, we will investigate using the results to construct a small-scale continuous manufacturing process. Once stable nuclei are obtained, the subsequent growth of crystals will be achieved in a novel tubular crystallizer with controlled crystal growth. The integration of both nucleation and growth steps into one seamless crystallization system will be a major step forward in realizing the full potential of this novel manufacturing concept for separation and purification of proteins in the biopharmaceutical industry. 生物药品是制药工业中一类重要并快速发展的产品。生产生物药品的一个典型挑战是从含有杂质的溶液中分离蛋白质。目前工业界主要采用色谱法分离蛋白质。遗憾的是色谱法的扩展受到自身因素的限制。结晶法是取代或者补充色谱法的一种技术。然而，蛋白质结晶过程很难设计和控制。此项研究的目的是开发蛋白质结晶的新方法，以便大大简化和提高蛋白质结晶，并实现在生物制药工业中的广泛应用。 这里提出的方法分为两步。首先，在流体装置中引进微小的图案化电极，以此实现对晶体成核的空间和动态控制。其次，所提出的方法将在连续流动模式中进行，而不是制药工业中目前采用的分批处理模式。针对药物制造，连续操作法具有简化过程控制，便于操作和过程可扩展性等重要优势。本方法结合了蛋白质成核的空间和动态控制以及新颖的连续流体技术，对蛋白质结晶过程提供了设计和操作上的灵活性，减轻了目前制造业遇到的主要困难。 人们对蛋白质在液体中的成核知之甚少，以至于在制造过程中很难控制这一现象。通常，对蛋白质成核的控制是通过改变宏观变量，比如蛋白质溶液的温度和组成，来实现的。本课题将打破这一方法，通过良好的控制电场来诱导蛋白质在规定时间和地点成核。初步研究结果显示电场对蛋白质成核有促进作用。为了提供将这些益处应用于工业实践中的科学依据，本项目提议进行实验和模拟项目以便理解和优化观察到的流体中电场增强蛋白质成核现象的机制。 最后，我们将利用研究结果构建一个小型连续生产过程。一旦获得稳定的晶核，晶体的后续生长将在新型的管状结晶器中可控的进行。把成核和生长工序整合成一个无缝的结晶系统将是实现生物制药工业中分离和纯化蛋白质全新制造理念潜能的重要一步。

16243116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16243116.value: Low-power radios play a critical role as one of the key enabling technologies for Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications. Among existing solutions, impulse ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) radios have become quite popular mainly thanks to their main features of high data rates and low power. On the other hand, as compared to its competitive technology of multi-band orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MB-OFDM), impulse radios can employ low duty cycling to achieve low power consumption and thus low energy per bit. In particular, non-coherent demodulation has been employed to eliminate the need of a high-frequency phase-locked loops (PLL) for frequency down conversion. However, non-coherent demodulation suffers from a major problem with interference and unwanted signals being down converted to the same frequency as the wanted signals. As a result, these interference signals would not be able to be filtered out and thus would appear as noise, which would significantly degrade the signal-to-noise ratio and in the worst case could even prevent the devices from working properly. The objective of this proposed project is to leverage the investigator’s expertise and strengths in radio-frequency integrated circuits and systems to develop a new system architecture for IR-UWB receivers to achieve not only high tolerance to interferences and blockers but also low energy per bit. Based on the investigation and the system specifications, suitable system architecture will first be proposed for interference rejection, from which building specifications will be derived. After the block specifications are determined and verified, the critical building blocks will be designed and fabricated. The focus will be on novel circuit design techniques to reduce the supply voltage and the power consumption. Finally, all the building blocks will be integrated, and the complete IR-UWB receiver will be fabricated and demonstrated with the proposed interference rejection techniques. 作为一个关键的物联网实现技术，低功耗无线电扮演着重要的角色。得益于它高速低功耗的主要特点，在现有的解决方案中，脉冲超宽带无线电已经变得非常普遍。 另一方面，相比于它的竞争技术-多频带正交频分复用，脉冲无线电能使用低的占空因素来获得低功耗，也就是低的单位比特能量。特别是，非相关性解调已被用来消除对用作下变频的高频锁相环的需求。然而，非相关性解调又受到一个主要问题的困扰，干扰信号和有用信号被同时转换到有用信号的频带。结果，这些干扰信号就不能被滤除而作为噪声存在，这将会严重的破坏信噪比，最坏情况下，甚至会使器件不能正常工作。 所提项目的目标是充分利用研究者的专业知识和对射频集成电路与系统的优势，来构造一个新型脉冲超宽带接受器的系统结构，以实现高的抗干扰和抗阻碍但是又获得低的单位字节能量 。 基于深入探究和系统参数， 抗干扰的合适的系统结构将首先被提出来，各模块的规格参数也将从中推导出。 在各个模块的参数被确定和验证之后，关键的构建模块将会被设计并且制造出来。 这个项目的工作重心在于设计出新颖的电路来减小供电电压和功耗。最后，所有的构件模块将会被集成，应用所提出的抗干扰技术，完整的脉冲无线电超宽带接收机将会被制造并且证明出来。

16243116.label: Realisation of objectives
16243116.value: 1. First, existing solutions for interference-rejection techniques for ultra-low-power wireless receivers for emerging applications in Internet of Things (IoT) have been thoroughly investigated, from which we learned that constant-envelope FSK-type modulation has been quite popular and attractive mainly due to its simple implementation. In particular, phase-tracking receivers (PTRX) performing FSK demodulation in the phase domain can minimize the power and the chip area and thus the cost by eliminating not only a complicated frequency synthesizer and a multi-bit ADC required in the conventional wireless receivers. 2. Accordingly, a novel phase-tracking receiver architecture was proposed, designed, simulated, fabricated, and successfully demonstrated with the state-of-the-art performance. Specifically, a low-power phase-tracking receiver (PTRX) is proposed featuring a sub-harmonic mixer with a local oscillator (LO) operating at half of the carrier frequency. 3. The main idea of the proposed 2nd-order sub-harmonic mixer for phase detection in a PTRX is to efficiently mitigate the phase-pulling issues from both the strong interference and the on-chip coupling. In addition, a current reuse technique is adopted to further improve the power efficiency. Moreover, the 2nd-order sub-harmonic mixer and the harmonic extraction VCO were co-designed for device sharing. Fabricated in a 65nm CMOS process, the PTRX prototype measures noise figure of 7.1dB and sensitivity of -88dBm with 1-Mb/s BLE Gaussian-Frequency-Shift-Keying (GFSK) data while consuming 750μW at 0.4/0.6V supply voltages. The work achieved the state-of-the-art performance and was published in the IEEE Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuits Conference 2018, which is one of the most prestigious conferences in the research area. 4. On the other hand, it was discovered that the architecture suffers from a critical problem with injection pulling of voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) caused by strong interference and on-chip coupling, which introduce demodulation inaccuracy. As a Type-I phase-locked loop (PLL), the locked PTRX provides rejection of phase pulling and analog baseband error sources. However, the injection pulling caused by strong interference and the DC offset can easily saturate the mixer and the baseband amplifier, which would prevent the loop from being locked. 5. As existing solutions, an isolation buffer at the output of the VCO is typically employed for isolation and noise decoupling, However, this buffer not only consumes a lot of power but also occupies a large chip area. 6. As potential improvement, a couple of new design techniques to improve the performance of the VCOs in terms of injection pulling and to make them suitable for the proposed phase-tracking receiver was investigated and proposed. 7. Specifically, a high-order LC tank was proposed for the VCO so that its tank's phase response becomes flattened and less sensitive to the disturbance at the load. A prototype was designed and simulated with interestingly good performance, and it was laid out and submitted for fabrication accordingly. 8. Unfortunately, after the prototype was fabricated, the measurements were not as satisfactory. After months of testing and debugging, we were able to identify two main problems. The first problem was with the inaccuracy and the unpredictability of the performance of the high-order LC tank in the presence of the variations in process, voltage, and temperature, which would require much tedious tuning and more iterations. The second problem, which is even more critical, is the significant substrate coupling due to the lossy and low-ohmic substrate of the standard digital CMOS process used for chip fabrication. A comprehensive model of the substrate coupling was investigated, and it was demonstrated that improved performance could be achieved as expected if a better process was used, such as silicon-on-insulator (SOI) process with high-ohmic substrate and thus good substrate isolation. 9. In parallel, a harmonic extraction technique is proposed to enhance the third-harmonic output amplitude and phase noise of LC oscillators and injection-locked frequency multipliers (ILFMs). Utilizing this technique, a cascaded ILFM-based LO generation is demonstrated. Implemented in a 65-nm CMOS process and consuming only 2.5 mW, the prototype achieves a frequency tuning range of 23.7% while measuring phase noise of -106.8 dBc/Hz at 10-MHz offset, corresponding to FoM of -186.5 dBc/Hz and FoMT of -194.1 dBc/Hz, while occupying a core area of 0.08 mm2. The work was also published in the IEEE Radio-Frequency Integrated Circuits Conference 2018.

16243116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16243116.value: * It has been investigated and confirmed that phase-tracking receivers (PTRXs) performing frequency shift keying demodulation in the phase domain can eliminate not only a complicated and power-hungry frequency synthesizer but also a multi-bit analog-to-digital converter to save much power and chip area. A novel PTRX architecture was proposed, designed, simulated, laid out, and successfully demonstrated. * One of most important finding from the project was that the architecture suffers from a critical problem with the injection pulling of the voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) caused by strong interference and on-chip coupling, which can easily saturate the mixer and the baseband amplifier, thus preventing the loop phase from being locked and tracked accurately. * Instead of using an isolation buffer as in existing solutions, a couple of new design techniques to improve the performance of the VCOs in terms of injection pulling and to make them suitable for the proposed phase-tracking receiver was investigated and proposed. * Specifically, a high-order LC tank was proposed for the VCO so that its tank's phase response becomes flattened and less sensitive to the disturbance at the load. A prototype was designed and simulated with interestingly good performance, and it was laid out and submitted for fabrication accordingly. Unfortunately, the measurements were not as satisfactory due to two main problems. The first problem was with the inaccuracy and the unpredictability of the performance of the high-order LC tank in the presence of the variations in process, voltage, and temperature, which would require much tedious tuning and more iterations. The second problem, which is even more critical, is the significant substrate coupling due to the lossy and low-ohmic substrate of the standard digital CMOS process used for chip fabrication. * Subsequently, a comprehensive model of the substrate coupling was investigated, and it was demonstrated that improved performance could be achieved as expected if a better process was used, such as silicon-on-insulator (SOI) process with high-ohmic substrate and thus good substrate isolation. * In parallel, we have also developed and demonstrated new design techniques to tackle the injection pulling of the VCO and the frequency synthesizer to improve the overall performance of the proposed low-power phase-tracking receiver. Specifically, a harmonic extraction technique is proposed to enhance the third-harmonic output amplitude and phase noise of LC oscillators and injection-locked frequency multipliers. The performance was demonstrated to be improved a lot, but unfortunately, the improvement cannot be achieved effectively without the expense of additional chip area and power consumption.

16243116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16243116.value: With more time and budget, it would be possible and interesting to extend the project proposal to incorporate some of the proposed design techniques to overcome the injection locking of the VCO to the proposed phase-tracking receiver to demonstrate the overall performance.

16243116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16243116.value: To achieve a wireless receiver with ultra-low power consumption for various emerging applications in Internet-of-Things (IoT), a novel phase-tracking receiver was proposed, designed, fabricated, and successfully demonstrated, in which the most critical blocks of the conventional receivers, namely the frequency synthesizer and the analog-to-digital converters are completely removed. In addition, it was also discovered that to make such a phase-tracking receiver practical, the injection pulling of the voltage-controlled oscillator would need to be tackled. Accordingly, a couple of potential design techniques were also proposed and demonstrated.

16243516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16243516.value: The rapid growth of the wireless and mobile Internet has provided an opportunity for wide applications of exchanging resources or services over networks, which go beyond the peer-to-peer (P2P) bandwidth sharing idea. The examples include the Wi-Fi sharing, the mobile data sharing, or even the commodities and services exchange among online platforms. In all the above examples, a participating user contributes its resources to others and benefits in exchange useful resources from others. Therefore, each user is both a supplier and a consumer. To capture all scenarios, three different models are proposed: static pure exchange model, mixed exchange model, and dynamic exchange model. The successes of the exchange markets highly depend on the efficient resource utilization. To encourage users to contribute more, a fair allocation rule is essential. Ideally a user should receive as much as it gives. However, such perfect reciprocation may not be feasible due to the network structure. Then a proportional fairness protocol is a natural approximation. However, its nice property of dynamics convergence to a market equilibrium is only known for static models. Another challenge is to explore whether it is robust to users’ strategic manipulations. The goals of this proposed research are four-fold. (1) To analyze the truthfulness of the proportional response protocol for the pure static model. (2) To compute the incentive ratio if the protocol is not truthful. (3) To study the convergence of the proportional response dynamics for the mixed and dynamic models. (4) To analyze the truthfulness if converge or design new protocols for the mixed and dynamic models. The proposed research is the first comprehensive study of networked resource exchange markets targeting the objectives of fairness, efficiency and truthfulness by the game theory approach. In view of the nature of this problem, it has drawn substantial attention from both practitioners and academic researchers worldwide. The theoretical results derived in this research will serve an important role in the further development of incentive protocols for exchange markets, and has the potential to make a significant contribution to the study of market equilibrium and dynamics convergence. The research will also have significant impact on Hong Kong because of its major importance for the economy, society and technological evolution, and wide applications. 無線和移動互聯網的快速發展提供了更多通過網絡交換資源或服務的機會，從而衍生出超越（P2P）帶寬共享原理的更多應用。這樣的例子包括了wifi共享，移動數據共享，甚至是在線平臺之間的商品和服務的交換。 在所有上述實例中，參與的用戶能夠從與其他用戶交換資源的過程中獲利。因此，每個用戶既是資源的供給者也是消費者。為了更好地模擬現實情形，現在有三種不同的模型：靜態純交換模型，混合交換模型和動態交換模型。 資源交換市場的成功完全依賴於高效的資源利用率。為了鼓勵用戶貢獻更多的資源，公平的分配規則是必不可少的。理想情況下， 提供越多資源的人回報應該也越多。然而，由於網絡結構的特殊性，這種協議往往不可能實現。所以相對的比例公平協議是壹種很好的解決辦法。但是，只有在純靜態模型中比例公平協議能夠動態收斂到市場均衡。另外，我們的另壹個挑戰是這樣的協議是否能夠應對用戶的各種戰略操作。 本研究有四個目的：（1）分析在純靜態模型中比例公平協議的激勵相容性。（2）如果該協議不是激勵相容，相應的需要計算用戶的戰略操作能夠帶來的回報比例。（3）在混合模型和動態模型中比例公平協議的收斂性。（4）如果收斂，分析相應均衡的激勵相容性；如果不收斂，需要為混合模型和動態模型設計新機制。 我們的研究是第壹個通過博弈論的方法針對基於網絡的資源交換市場的公平，效率和激勵相容性進行的全面研究。鑒於這個問題已經引起來自世界各地的從業者和學術研究人員的大量關註，這項研究的成果將服務於網絡交換的激勵相容協議的理論發展，並且能夠對市場均衡和動態收斂研究做出顯著貢獻。這項研究也將因為其對經濟，社會和技術的發展及其廣泛的實際應用對香港產生顯著的影響。

16243516.label: Realisation of objectives
16243516.value: For objective 1: The rapid growth of the wireless and mobile Internet has provided an opportunity for wide applications of exchanging resources or services over networks, which go beyond the peer-to-peer (P2P) bandwidth sharing idea. a participating user contributes its resources to others and benefits in exchange useful resources from others. Therefore, each user is both a supplier and a consumer. To capture all scenarios, three different models are proposed: static pure exchange model, mixed exchange model, and dynamic exchange model. We define these three models. For objective 2: The successes of the exchange markets highly depend on the efficient resource utilization. To encourage users to contribute more, a fair allocation rule is essential. Ideally a user should receive as much as it gives. However, such perfect reciprocation may not be feasible due to the network structure. Then a proportional fairness protocol is a natural approximation. However, its nice property of dynamics convergence to a market equilibrium is only known for static models. Here we define proportional response dynamics for all three model. For objective 3: We first find the proportional response functions in various models. An allocation is called proportional fair, if the amount of resources player i allocate to player j is in proportion to the utility player i received from j. For static pure exchange model, the convergence is guaranteed by bottleneck decomposition and matrix renormalization. For mixed and dynamic models, the convergence holds for a special Fisher market where each player either has resource or budget. For objective 4: To address the truthfulness problem, we need first identify all possible strategic manipulations in different models. A protocol is truthful if an arbitrary player’s dominant strategy is always telling truth no matter what strategies the other players use. As utilities are determined by allocation that depends on players' private information and the network structure, the strategic manipulations of a player will be all possible combination of misreporting private information or/and cheating on its own links. It’s usually not too difficult to check if a protocol is truthful or not. The key challenge here is to compute the incentive ratio. In all models, agent's weight and its neighbor set can be viewed as the private information. As utilities are determined by allocation which depends on agents’ weights and the network structure, there are three possible manipulations for each agent: (1) to misreport its neighbor set; (2) to misreport its weight; (3) to preset the amount of resource for some agent. We proved that no agent can increase its utility by unilaterally cutting off some of its links or misreport its total amount of resources under the proportional response protocol. Thus, the protocol is robust to the type (1) and type (2) manipulations. However, for type (3) manipulation, it is not robust any more. To prove the agent cannot improve its utility by misreporting its total amount of resource, we assume that each agent can not misreport its resource exceeding its true value, since each agent must allocate all its reporting weight to its neighbors. We know that a market equilibrium can be constructed from the bottleneck decomposition. Here we can view an agent's utility function as the function of its reporting value and other players’ values. We show that an agent’s utility is maximized when it reports its true weight by proving a monotonicity property, i.e., each player can get more if it sends more. The agent may improve its utility by splitting itself into several nodes and preset the amount of resource for some of its neighbors. For example for an agent with three neighbors, it can split itself into three different nodes and pretend to be three different agents and report their weights separately for each fake nodes. This type of manipulation is also called sybil attack. For sybil attack, we define a concept called incentive ratio to measure how much extra utility it can gain by sybil attack. We then find the incentive ratio for various network structure and find tight bounds for line, circle, complete graph structures.

16243516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16243516.value: In this project, we explore its resistance to manipulative behavior by considering a kind of strategy that an agent disguises itself by creating several copied false nodes with its resources assigning among them in order to obtain more resources from other users on the network, which called Sybil Attack. For this kind of cheating, we proved that the utility increment is bounded by 2 for several common network types (e.g., circle, tree and complete graph). In the future, we want to find the tight bounds for all network types.

16243516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16243516.value: A persistent challenge for resource sharing is how to motivate each user to participate in the contribution. This kind of distributed resource sharing mechanism generally relies on the user to inform the platform how many resources it can contribute. The incentive mechanism design is to solve the problem that users may misreport its amount of resources. To motivate contribution, ideally a user should receive as much as it gives. However, such perfect reciprocation may not be feasible due to the network structure. In my work, we propose a proportional sharing mechanism where the amount of resources shared to the user from its neighbor is proportion to the amount of resources it contributes to that neighbor. We prove this mechanism motivates each user to truthfully report its resource amount and the dynamics of this distributed mechanism converges to the market equilibrium. Therefore, it shows that the proportional sharing mechanism is truthful, fair and Pareto efficient. Further, we explore its resistance to manipulative behaviour called Sybil Attack. For this kind of cheating, we proved that the utility increment is bounded by 2 for several common network types.

16244116.value: 在地震多发地区，高速铁路的线路总长已达数千公里。而在中国，高速铁路中桥梁的覆盖率高达80%以上，因此地震发生时列车正运行于桥上的可能性大大提高。在高速列车的运行速度区间（250-350公里/小时，即使对桥梁有较小影响的地震也可能对列车的运行带来极大威胁。这种中小地震通常发生在地震少发地区，例如广东省。而在高速铁路短暂的历史中，由于地震作用造成桥梁上运行列车脱轨的现象已有先例。 传统地震工程领域的研究主要关注大震对桥梁的影响，但是高速铁路作为车桥耦合系统，在频繁的中震作用下同样容易遭受损害。该研究着眼于桥梁动力学和车辆动力学的交叉学科领域，以探究该车桥耦合系统的地震响应。对于地震引起振动的桥梁上运行的列车的安全性分析，现有研究通常依赖于间接方法，如根据受力矩阵或几何条件。这种分析方法降低了分析地震对于高速铁路车桥耦合系统的直接与间接影响的准确性，同时给震害风险的量化分析带来困难。 本研究的主要目标是通过解析以及数值方法评价高速铁路车桥系统在地震作用下的安全性与可靠度。为此，本研究将提出一套新的地震解析方法，以模拟车桥耦合系统的不同失效模式，如脱轨、翻车以及桥梁破坏。之后，本研究将考虑地震-桥梁-列车问题的不确定性，首次建立专用于高速铁路车桥耦合系统的基于概率和性能的地震影响评价体系。在此基础上，本研究将进一步评价车桥耦合系统在地震作用下的损失，以及运行中断带来的人身伤害、经济损失及时间损失。同时，此方法将提供一个风险-决策体系，用于评价可能采取的早期预警、运行速度调整以及修订规范等措施的有效性。 在桥梁工程、基础设施工程及地震工程中，关于车桥耦合系统及其安全性评估的研究是主要的优先发展领域，并吸引了国际的瞩目和大量的科研基金，本研究将及时并显著的推动该研究领域的蓬勃发展。

16244116.label: Realisation of objectives
16244116.value: All three research objectives of the project were successfully achieved. In fact, this project exceeded our original goals and expectations in several ways. The first objective aimed at the development of a realistic nonlinear train–bridge simulation for seismic analysis. This requires the effective simulation of the vehicle–bridge interaction (VBI) problem, under the simultaneous effect of earthquake, as well as the realistic simulation of contact between the vehicle’s wheels and the rails. To this end, we developed an original seismic VBI methodology that accounts for the effect of earthquake on the dynamics of coupled vehicle–bridge systems, while considers nonlinear profiles of both rails and wheels (see “Vehicle–bridge interaction analysis modeling derailment during earthquakes” by Zeng and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018, Part C). The proposed scheme determines the contact points and direction of contact forces based on these nonlinear profiles via pre-calculated contact look-up tables. It also accounts for rolling contact in the tangential direction, following the nonlinear Shen-Hedrick-Euristic creep model. VBI analyses can be time-consuming, while, in some cases, a large number of VBI analyses may be needed. Especially when the seismic performance of a railway bridge or of VBI system is of interest, numerous analyses under different ground motions are necessary. Therefore, we developed an original partitioned methodology to simulate the non-linear vehicle–bridge interaction (VBI) problem—the localized Lagrange multipliers approach (see “A localized Lagrange multipliers approach for the vehicle–bridge interaction problem” by Zeng, Stoura and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018, Part C). This methodology hinges upon the introduction of auxiliary contact points between the vehicle and bridge subsystems, which the enable the formulation of two sets of kinematic constraints and, accordingly, two sets of contact forces (i.e., localized Lagrange multipliers), between the vehicle and bridge subsystems. As a result, vehicle and bridge can be solved separately in an accurately and cost effective manner. Numerical applications showed that the proposed approach outperforms existing methodologies in terms of computationally efficiency. For example, compared to a fully coupled algorithm, the localized Lagrange multipliers approach can be almost ten times faster. Following, we extended the localized Lagrange multipliers approach to account also for rolling contact between the rails and the wheels in the tangential direction, as well as for non-linear profiles of the rails and the wheels (see “Vehicle–bridge interaction analysis using the localized Lagrange multipliers approach” by Stoura, Zeng and Dimitrakopoulos, 2019, Part C). Finally, we incorporated the effect of earthquake, which led to an efficient scheme to solve the seismic VBI problem (see “Seismic analysis between train and bridges using the localized Lagrange multipliers approach” by Stoura, Zeng and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018, Part C). The second objective aimed at the modelling of non-smooth contact between rails and wheels. To satisfy this objective, we simulated directly different wheel–rail contact states, including flange contact, detachment, uplifting, wheel–rail climbing up, re-contact, and derailment. In addition, the modelling of the contact in the normal direction relied on the principles of non-smooth dynamics and accounted for continuous contact of finite duration, impact (of instantaneous duration), and transition from continuous contact to detachment (see “Vehicle–bridge interaction analysis modeling derailment during earthquakes” by Zeng and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018, Part C, and Seismic analysis between train and bridges using the localized Lagrange multipliers approach” by Stoura, Zeng and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018, Part C). This analysis stressed the key role of flange contact of a train’s wheel under a large contact angle, which could potentially lead to detachment of the other wheel of the same wheelset. This emphasizes the importance of more realistic train–bridge interaction modelling during earthquakes. For the realization of the third objective, we examined the seismic performance of different vehicle–bridge configurations under different ground motions. Simulations of a three-dimensional (3D) train running over a series of simply supported bridges under different earthquake scenarios showed that both amplitude and frequency of earthquake are important to the safety of trains (see “Vehicle–bridge interaction analysis modeling derailment during earthquakes” by Zeng and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018). Specifically, with reference to pulse ground motions, an unsafe region is specified starting from moderate peak acceleration values and for frequencies close to the natural frequency of the bridge and the bogies. Outside this frequency range, the train does not derail, even for higher acceleration amplitudes. In addition, according to the majority of the cases examined, detachment of wheel typically occurs due to flange contact of the other wheel of the same wheelset, while derailment happens due to wheel–rail climbing up. Lastly, we showed that traditional force-based metrics (e.g., derailment and offload factors) lead to conservative estimations regarding the train’s operational safety. Also, the consideration of linear instead of nonlinear wheel and rail profiles often overestimate the seismic risk of a train running over a bridge. To further elucidate on the factors that mainly affect the coupling between vehicles and bridges, and thus the safety of vehicles, we investigated analytically a multi-degree of freedom (MDOF) vehicle–MDOF bridge system (see “Additional damping effect on bridges because of vehicle–bridge interaction” by Stoura and Dimitrakopoulos, 2020, Part C). We demonstrated that a main coupling parameter between vehicles and bridges, in additional to the well-known vehicle-to-bridge mass and eigenfrequency ratios, is the ratio of the vehicle’s damping with respect to the mechanical impedance of the bridge. In addition, we showed that the effect of VBI on a bridge translates into an additional stiffness, an additional damping and a modified loading term. Particularly, in most cases, additional damping term mitigates the response of the bridge, which is in agreement with the favorable damping effect of VBI encountered in previous seismic VBI studies. For simply supported and continuous bridges, the additional damping can be simplified to a time-invariant additional damping ratio, which can be effectively adopted in bridge design. This analytical study contributed to the better understanding of the mechanisms of VBI, and hence to the justification of the results of numerical studies on VBI and seismic VBI.

16244116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16244116.value: (i) We developed a holistic seismic vehicle–bridge interaction (VBI) analysis scheme that considers non-linear profiles of rails and wheels, while simulates directly different wheel–rail contact states. As a result, the proposed scheme can effectively capture flange contact, detachment, uplifting, wheel–rail climbing up, re-contact, and derailment, outperforming traditional force-based safety metrics, such as the derailment factor and offload factor (“Vehicle–bridge interaction analysis modeling derailment during earthquakes” by Zeng and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018). (ii) Aiming at the accurate and efficient numerical treatment of the coupled VBI, and subsequently seismic VBI, we established a novel partitioning time-integration algorithm. The proposed localized Lagrange multipliers approach introduces auxiliary contact points between the vehicle and bridge, thus formulates two sets of kinematic constraint and two sets of Langrage multipliers, pertaining to the vehicle and bridge, respectively. Consequently, vehicle and bridge can be solved separately, decreasing significantly the involved computational cost (“A localized Lagrange multipliers approach for the vehicle–bridge interaction problem” by Zeng, Stoura and Dimitrakopoulos, 2018, Part C). (iii) To interpret the conclusions derived by numerical analyses, we examined the dynamic VBI response via analytical solutions for simple vehicle–bridge configurations. This analysis revealed that the effect of VBI on bridges comprises an additional damping, an additional stiffness and a modified loading term, while the impedance ratio—defined as the ratio of the vehicle’s damping to bridge’s mechanical impedance—is a major coupling parameter. Focusing on the additional damping term, we showed that additional damping is typically positive (which confirms the favorable damping effect of VBI), while in cases that the mass of the train’s wheels is not negligible it can also obtain negative values. Ultimately, we proposed simplified formulas to estimate the additional damping ratio for simply supported and continuous bridges (“Additional damping effect on bridges because of vehicle–bridge interaction” by Stoura and Dimitrakopoulos, 2020, Part C).

16244116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16244116.value: As a further development of this project, research should focus on the identification of the constituent mechanisms of VBI and the main coupling parameters between vehicles and bridges, when the concurrent effect of earthquake excitation is considered. Following, stress should be put on the development of decoupled analysis schemes that take into account the simultaneous effect of VBI and seismic excitation. Decoupled methodologies are easier to implement and more cost-effective, thus can be effectively adopted in bridge design practice or in cases where a large number of analyses in necessary (fragility analyses, response spectra under different moving speeds). Also, an in-depth probabilistic analysis should be performed on the seismic response of train–bridge systems. This analysis should take into account, for example, the uncertainties in the characteristics of earthquake excitations, speed of the traversing trains, and dynamic properties of trains and bridges. Such an analysis would be of significant importance to the adequate assessment of safety and comfort of transportation under earthquake, with subsequent social and economic benefits.

16244116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16244116.value: Compared with conventional railway lines, high-speed railway (HSR) networks utilize a higher ratio of bridges. As a reference, 80.5% of the Beijing-Shanghai line is made up on bridges, including the longest bridge system in the world. The unprecedented bridge ratios of HSRs increase the likelihood of an earthquake striking when a train traverses a bridge. On the other hand, the high speeds at which HSR trains operate (300–350 km/h) cause even earthquakes of moderate intensity (which do not impose any danger to the structural integrity of bridges) to jeopardize the operational safety of trains. This is confirmed by recent incidents, such as the derailment of a Shinkansen train in Japan in 2004. To contribute to the prediction and prevention of such catastrophic events, this research focuses on the accurate modelling of coupled train⁠–bridge systems subjected to earthquake. Following, it examines the running safety of trains traversing bridges under different earthquake scenarios. This analysis shows that traditional metrics to assess the safety of transportation overestimate the seismic risk, thus more realistic safety criteria should be adopted. Lastly, this research investigates analytically the parameters that affect the interaction between vehicles and bridges, and theoretically validates the obtained numerical results.

16244416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16244416.value: We propose to develop a learning model for the control of binocular vergence eye movements, and to implement it on a mobile robot platform with an active binocular vision system. The key novelty in this system will be the hierarchical integration of information from different image scales, in contrast to past work, in which information from multiple scales was integrated in parallel. Information at different image scales contains information about objects of different sizes, with coarse scales corresponding to larger objects, and finer scales corresponding to smaller objects. We will use hierarchical reinforcement learning to learn independent low-level policies for vergence using information at different scales, and then integrate this information by learning a higher level policy to determine which of the low-level policies to follow. We anticipate that the combined policy will exhibit a coarse-to-fine property, where the policy corresponding to the coarse scale is applied first, followed successively by actions from policies driven by image information at finer scales and over smaller regions. While coarse-to-fine policies have been studied previously, the policy was hard coded in advance, based on prior knowledge. This work will be the first attempt to learn such a policy. A key advantage of learning is that the system will be able to dynamically choose the policy that best suits a particular situation without bias introduced by hard-coding the design. Another novel aspect of this system is that it will incorporate gaze shifts based on a computational model of the saliency of different points in the image. These gaze shifts will direct gaze towards different objects in the environment. This is important since the vergence angles required to align the left and right images on surfaces at different depths will be different. To obtain an efficient algorithm, the binocular image representation used to drive the vergence behavior will be the same as that used to compute saliency. Thus, this work will generalize existing monocular models of image saliency to binocular image input. 我們提出要開發一個用於控制雙目聚散行為的學習模型，並將此模型實現於一個裝有雙目視覺系統的可移動機器人平台上。此系統的主要創新在於把不同尺度的圖像信息分層整合，而不是像過去的研究一樣並行處理不同尺度的信息。不同的圖像尺度中包含物體的不同大小信息，粗尺度對應較大的物體，精細尺度對應較小的物體。我們將會使用分層強化學習方法來訓練利用不同尺度信息的獨立的低級眼球聚散策略，然後通過學習更高級別的策略來決定如何整合各個低級策略。我們預計整合的策略將呈現從粗尺度到細尺度的特點，其中應用於粗尺度的策略會首先選擇，接著依次選擇由更精細和更小尺度的圖像信息驅動的行為。之前關於從粗到細尺度策略的研究都是基於先驗知識提前對策略進行硬編碼。此研究將是學習這種策略的首次嘗試。學習的一個主要優點是該系統可以在特定的情況下動態地選擇最合適的策略而不會產生由硬編碼設計的策略引入的誤差。此系統的另一個創新之處是將結合基於視覺顯著性計算模型的注視轉移。注視轉移會將目光轉向環境中的不同物體。注視轉移是非常重要的，因為對准左右圖像所需的聚散角度在不同深度的物體表面上是不同的。為了得到有效的算法， 用於驅動聚散行為的雙目圖像表示將會相同於用於計算顯著圖的雙目表示。因此，此項工作將把現有的單目顯著性模型推廣到基於雙目圖像輸入的顯著性模型。

16244416.label: Realisation of objectives
16244416.value: Our first objective was to develop a neuromorphic algorithm for learning binocular vergence control, in which information from different image scales is integrated hierarchically. We fully achieved this objective by developing a hierarchical two stage algorithm for learning to integrate information from a coarse scale periphery with a fine scale fovea. The bottom level generates different vergence actions from different image regions, which are sub-sampled at different rates and cover different visual areas, similar to foveal and peripheral regions of the eye. The top level selects one of the generated commands based on the image input. Unlike past architectures, where the flow of the algorithm proceeded in a fixed manner from coarse to fine, in this hierarchical algorithm, the choice of which scale to use is dynamic and can change depending upon the visual input. This makes the algorithm more robust and adaptable. In our system, both perception and behavior are learned simultaneously. We define perception as the mapping from the raw sensory input (images in our case) to an internal representation that captures salient information about the environment relevant to the task at hand. For the perceptual mapping, we used a probabilistic generative model for the image input, the Generative Adaptive Subspace Self Organizing Map (GASSOM) algorithm, which assumes that the high dimensional visual input is generated by sampling from a two dimensional subspace chosen dynamically from a dictionary of K = 324 subspaces. The subspaces are learned through exposure to unlabeled image patches via an unsupervised learning algorithm. We define behavior as the mapping from the learned perceptual representation to an action. To learn this mapping, we used a hierarchical version of the Natural Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning (NACREL) algorithm described by Bhatnagar et al in Automatica (2009). The algorithm is embodied in the sense that it depends critically upon the agent's physical interaction with the environment, and how that interaction alters the resulting sensory input. The second objective was to evaluate its performance and robustness in real-world environments. We fully achieved this objective by testing on both synthesized realistic data sets as well as by implementing it in a robotic platform. We first tested this algorithm on a synthetic stereo dataset, the Tsukuba dataset, which is generated by moving virtual cameras in a parallel geometry through a virtual office environment and rendering the images seen by the two cameras. The advantage of this dataset is that ground truth measurements of disparity are available. Our experiments with this dataset show that the proposed hierarchical approach performs better than prior approaches in realistic environments, which contain objects at different sizes and at different depths. The proposed approach results in better alignment and less oscillation. We then implemented the algorithm on an active binocular vision head maintained in our laboratory. While this system operates in the real world, the disadvantage is that the ground truth is not as readily available. Nonetheless, our experiments on this system are consistent with those with the Tsukuba dataset: better alignment and less oscillation in environments containing objects with different sizes at different depths.
