16244416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16244416.value: There were several major findings resulting from this proposal. The first finding is the development of algorithms that enable systems to adapt the information they exploit and their behavior dynamically depending upon environmental context. This enables more robust and more efficient operation than non-adaptive algorithms, even those that exploit learning in a separate training phase, since the statistics assumed a priori or learned during training may change during deployment. Differences between the input statistics assumed or learned during training and the statistics of the inputs encountered during deployment or testing can cause degradations in performance. In machine learning, this phenomenon is referred to as train/test mismatch. Enabling algorithms to adapt their processing in response to environmental context is an effective way to improve the robustness of performance. We have reported these algorithms and their performance in a journal article that appeared in the IEEE TNSRE and at the SAB 2018 conference (both attached here). The second major finding is that these algorithms can be extended to multi-task learning using a very similar framework with minor extensions. This demonstrates the generality of the approach developed here. This has been reported in a journal article that appeared in the IEEE JETCAS (for the tasks of velocity estimation and object tracking), and at the ICDL2020 conference (for the tasks of vergence, cyclovergence and saccadic eye movements). Both are attached here. The third major finding is that these models lead to insight into biological development. This is reported in a paper appearing at the SAB2018 conference (attached here), which examined development under normal and abnormal rearing conditions. We found that abnormal rearing conditions led to differences in the model’s development that qualitatively match those seen in animal experiments. Furthermore, the model predicted systematic changes in vergence accuracy due to abnormal rearing. These findings had implications for the treatment of developmental disorders of binocular vision such as amblyopia and strabismus.

16244416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16244416.value: This project has focused on finding ways to integrate different cues via learning such that information from different cues is exploited appropriately in different situations. In other words, different cues are used at different times depending upon the situation. This enables the unique advantages of each cue to be exploited appropriately. However, the algorithms studied here have all been taken from the same sensory modality: vision. It would be very valuable to investigate the use of the algorithms and approaches developed in this project for multi-sensory cue integration, e.g. combining visual cues with auditory and/or proprioceptive cues. For example, in dark environments, vision becomes less reliable, and humans and animals rely more on other senses. Automatically learning how to shift reliance between different senses is an important open questions. One promising area is that of emotion recognition, where a person's appearance and voice both convey important information. As a first step in this direction, we have developed algorithms for multitask emotion recognition (reported at AFGR2020 and attached here). We intend to continue along this line of research with proposals submitted to the RGC (under review) and the ITF (granted).

16244416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16244416.value: Humans and animals use vision to gather information about the world to perform tasks like navigation successfully and safely. Vision is also important for mobile robots. However, unlike most robots, where visual perception and behavior is hard coded, humans and animals learn how to exploit vision. This provides them unparalleled adaptability and robustness. To bridge the gap, we have developed a learning model for the control of binocular vergence eye movements, and implemented it on a robotic platform with an active binocular vision system. The key novelty in this system is the hierarchical, rather than parallel, integration of information from different image scales. Different scales contain information about objects of different sizes. Coarser scales correspond to larger objects. Finer scales correspond to smaller objects. Our hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm automatically finds a "coarse-to-fine" policy, where information from coarse scales is applied first, then information from fine scale. While such coarse-to-fine policies have been studied previously, they were hard coded based on prior knowledge, rather than learned automatically. This work has led to both insights into biological development, as well as practical algorithms for adaptive robotics.

16244616.label: Project Objectives
16244616.value: Objective 1: (Testing the Feasibility of the Q-learning Framework for Recommender Systems.) We lay a foundation by introducing a preliminary reinforcement learning solution. We will use a real world recommendation dataset to help us design the model, and evaluate the parameter settings for states and actions in the Q-learning framework. This allows us to verify the feasibility of the agent modeling approach. Because the parameters in this stage of the research are manually tuned, we will have a better understanding of their physical meaning in the model. The adjusted parameters can be used to guide the subsequent design of a fully automatically tuned deep neural-network for learning actions and states. Objective 2: (Automatically Learning the Deep Q-learning Model for Recommender Systems.) We intend to design a fully automatic framework to train a deep neural network model to acquire action and transition probabilities. This deep parametric treatment of the Q-learning framework for recommendation will improve handling of the the complex actions in a real-world recommendation setting. We will explore optimization of the Deep Q-learning model, the use of training data and parallel implementation to speed up the model learning process. Objective 3: (Deep Q-learning with Partially Observable States.) Because the states in real-world settings may not be fully observable, and thus cannot be defined directly, we will need to extend the definition of states to include those that are partially observable. We will introduce a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) model of the agent decision processes and show the utility of the collaborative modeling of states in this POMDP model. Objective 4: (Evaluation.) We will implement a prototype of the Deep Q-learning framework for recommender systems and verify its learning and predictive ability and its capacity to handle the three issues, which cause the RD phenomenon. We will publish research results in the form of high-quality publications and make the software and demonstrations available in an open-source manner.

16244616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16244616.value: 推荐系统在电子学习，在线商城，移动应用等很多场景有广泛的应用。在当下推荐系统中，模型一般是基于用户的正反馈训练得到的。在这种“推荐-反馈-训练”的循环模式下，随着时间，我们发现明显的效果衰减效应。我们把这种效应叫做推荐系统中的“迭代衰退”。迭代衰退效应对当前推荐系统带来三个挑战：(a)缺乏负例引起的模型偏见;(b)加剧的数据稀疏;(c)频繁更改数据分布。 为了解决这些问题，我们提出了一个创新性的框架：深度Q-learning框架。在这个框架里，我们把推荐系统当作一个探索环境的机器人-基于用户长/短期的反馈模拟机器人在高维状态空间的移动。这些状态空间是通过深度学习获得的，并且采纳了协同过滤的思想。通过这个项目，我们会展示深度Q-learning框架可以很好的解决“迭代衰退”效应对推荐系统带来的三个挑战。 我们希望深度Q-learning框架不仅对推荐系统的研究带来指导，也为机器学习领域解决“迭代衰退”效应相关的挑战更进一步。我们将会把深度Q-learning框架部署在现实场景的大规模推荐系统上，如阿里巴巴，腾讯的广告电商平台等。

16244616.label: Realisation of objectives
16244616.value: We have designed novel deep reinforcement learning systems with transfer learning abilities and applied to the real world situations. Our work not only advanced the state of the art, but also advanced AI practice in news recommendation. Below, we summarize our achievements of the objectives of the project. First, we have laid a solid foundation by introducing a preliminary reinforcement learning solution that applies to a real world recommendation dataset to help us design and evaluate the model in the Q-learning framework. Specifically, we have designed a bandit based reinforcement learning algorithm that is capable of transferring to a new task domain. For example, we take the mobile APP store domain and transfer the recommendation knowledge to a news recommendation domain. This algorithm has been applied to the real world data for Lie-Bao data set for mobile news recommendation, and got superior performance. The system is also applied to WeChat news recommendation system and obtained excellent result. The system is being used by nearly one billion WeChat users daily. For the second objective, we designed a fully automatic framework to train a deep neural network model from training data. The system is anchored on a dialog system that drives a task-based conversation with a user. The system advanced the state of the art in identifying deep parametric models of the Q-learning framework for recommendations. It advanced the state of the art in the dialog system area by introducing sophisticated algorithms based on deep reinforcement learning. For objective 3, we have fully considered the cases when we cannot fully observe the environment. In this case, we introduce belief state and train a POMDP model. Under this model, our system can carry out state transitions with high accuracy due to training and transfer learning from auxiliary domains. The system improves the state of the art by considering uncertainties directly. For objective 4, we have implemented a prototype system of the Deep Q-learning framework for a news recommender system which has high accuracy in predictive ability. The system performed well in the WeChat platform and in the Lie-Bao news recommendation platform.

16244616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16244616.value: Our work is to design, development and apply deep Q learning in real world situations to solve real problems. We have designed deep reinforcement learning, transfer learning and recommendation system frameworks to tackle the problems. We have designed bandit algorithms to let system intelligently decide on strategies on which news to recommend to users based on not only the past history but also similar behavior in APP recommendation domains. Q learning algorithm is also designed to drive a task based dialog system engine which is used in a dialog robot for service recommendation. These systems can handle the situations when we cannot fully observe the environment, based on learning the belief states. Finally, we have applied the systems to WeChat and Lie-Bao systems with good performance.

16244616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16244616.value: We will extend the algorithm and system so that they work under the security and privacy requirement when data are fragmented, which is the common situation in the real world. We will also further study how to efficiently compute the Q learning policies under POMDP via transfer learning. We will extend the recommendation engine to multi-party conversation involving multi-agents in the future, when we have a market place to host these agents.

16244616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16244616.value: Online systems should cater to users' personal interests, however, users often have multiple conflicting interests. Furthermore, systems have only partial knowledge of the environment. In such situations, we can use the research results from this project to design an intelligent recommendation and dialog system engine to work with the user. This system not only understands user needs much better than other existing systems due to its ability to balance long term and short term user interests, but also learns new strategies to handle uncertainty and to make decisions. With the result form this research, we can have much more intelligent online systems that can work together with human users.

16245016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16245016.value: 基於深度學習和圖形模型的腦腫瘤核磁共振圖像分割

16245016.label: Project Objectives
16245016.value: To develop new magnetic resonance image segmentation methods for brain tumors by combining deep learning techniques and graphical models. To evaluate the newly-developed segmentation methods by using publicly available medical image datasets as well as clinical datasets acquired from hospitals.
rows: To develop new magnetic resonance image segmentation methods for brain tumors by combining deep learning techniques and graphical models.
To evaluate the newly-developed segmentation methods by using publicly available medical image datasets as well as clinical datasets acquired from hospitals.

16245016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16245016.value: 在這個研究項目中，我們主要關注大腦核磁共振圖像的腦腫瘤分割。在醫學圖像中，分割腦腫瘤比分割正常腦組織的解剖結構更具有挑戰性。這些難點主要來自於腦腫瘤形狀不規則，位置不可估計，這使得難以對其形狀進行建模，並獲得有關其位置的先驗知識。 我們計劃用深度學習的技術獲得初步的分割結果，用圖形模型來產生最終的結果。一個特別的層疊深度網絡將被設計，對從同一對象採集的不同模態的圖像進行腦腫瘤分割。在這個層疊深度網絡中，有兩個主要組成部分，在圖像水平的完全卷積網絡和區域水平的不平衡多尺度結構的卷積神經網絡（MS-CNN）。 在基於深度學習的圖像分割中，傳統的方法是，用一個窗口在整張圖上進行滑動來對每個像素的標籤進行估計，由於相鄰的窗口位置之間的冗余計算，這會導致嚴重的計算負擔。在本研究項目中，無需窗口滑動，充分卷積網絡被用來估算一個初步的像素概率圖，並選擇腦腫瘤的候選像素。基於選擇的像素，一個特定的區域水平的網絡，即深度不平衡MS-CNN，將被用來採集每一個腦腫瘤子區域的有判別力的特徵，並產生輸入圖像的標籤概率圖。由於大腦圖像的背景複雜和測試樣本之間缺乏空間限制，這個層疊深度網絡獲得的初步結果可能是 不夠可靠和不夠光滑的。 為瞭解決這個問題，一個層次化的圖形模型被用來推斷最終對標籤。考慮到腦腫瘤子區域的分層結構，超鏈接被添加在圖形中，使得相鄰子圖中子區域的關係可以在分割過程中被採集和加強。全面的實驗將在五個公開的數據集和從醫院獲得臨床數據集中進行，對圖像分割的質量進行評估。

16245016.label: Realisation of objectives
16245016.value: Regarding Objective 1, in this research project, we have developed several new image segmentation methods based on deep learning techniques and graphical models. This objective has been successfully achieved. First, (refer to Part C.8.[1]), we have introduced a new 3D deep learning network for brain magnetic resonance (MR) image segmentation. We used randomized connections, convolutional long-short term memory, and 3D convolution in the deep learning framework to increase the network capacity and decrease the dependency between layers. Also, an efficient graph-based node selection was proposed in the label inference process to capture spatial-temporal information better and refine the deep learning outcomes. Second, (refer to Part C.8.[2] and C.9.[1]), we have investigated a novel Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based method for fully automatic brain tumor segmentation for both high-grade and low-grade gliomas in MR images. Unlike normal tissues or organs that usually have a fixed location or shape, brain tumors with different grades have shown great variation in location, size, structure, and morphological appearance. To address the challenges, we use the new dynamic focal Dice loss function that can focus more on the smaller tumor sub-regions with more complex structures during training. The learning capacity of the model is dynamically distributed to each class independently based on its training performance. Besides, to better recognize the overall structure of the brain tumor and the morphological relationship among different tumor sub-regions, we relax the boundary constraints for the inner tumor regions in a coarse-to-fine fashion. Third, (refer to Part C.9.[2], C.9.[3], C.9.[5]), we have studied quality assessment and error map prediction for segmentation methods. The application is whole-heart segmentation on the MICCAI 2017 MMWHS dataset. In this project, we use a unified deep learning framework to predict errors in a segmentation task when the ground truth is absent and introduce a quality indicator (QI) to measure the overall quality of the segmentation task. We have obtained an overall Dice score of 0.626 for the error map prediction task and observed a high Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.972 between QI and the actual segmentation accuracy (Acc), as well as a low mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0048 between them, which evidences the efficacy of our method in both error map prediction and quality assessment. We have also proposed a new gland instance segmentation method that learns hierarchical semantic feature matching from histological pairs in an attentive process. Both spatial details and morphological appearances can be well preserved and balanced. Finally, we have developed a novel segmentation method for vasculature in angiograms. The method uses a newly proposed vesselness measure based on the oriented flux, and spherical harmonics transform. Finally, (refer to Part C.9.[4], C.9.[6]), we have investigated the combination of graphs and convolutional neural networks, namely graph convolutional neural networks (GCN), and its application in population-based disease analysis. The advantage is the ability to combine data of different types, e.g., images and non-image data (age, gender, acquisition site, etc.). Unlike previous methods, the method does not hand-engineer a similarity population graph but learns to construct the graph connectivity based on a pairwise association encoder. Regarding Objective 2, the above newly developed methods have been extensively evaluated with the multiple publicly available medical image datasets (LPBA40, BRATS 2019, MICCAI 2017 MMWHS, GlaS and CRAG, ABIDE, ADNI, and ODIR). Therefore, experimental results can be quantitatively compared with other state-of-the-art methods. Clinical image and numerical datasets are also used to test the proposed methods in this project. The results are encouraging and disseminated in the top-tier conference venues (MICCAI, ICIP) and journal papers (a TIP paper published; and a MedIA paper under review).

16245016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16245016.value: The major findings and research outcomes are listed below. First, (refer to Part C.8.[1]), we introduced a new 3D deep learning network for brain magnetic resonance (MR) image segmentation. This work has been published in the IEEE Transactions on Image Processing in 2018. Second, (refer to Part C.8.[2] and C.9.[1]), we have investigated a novel Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based method for fully automatic brain tumor segmentation for both high-grade and low-grade gliomas in MR images. This work has been accepted subject to satisfactory revisions by the Journal of Medical Image Analysis and a revised version of the manuscript has been submitted for review. Third, (refer to Part C.9.[2], C.9.[3], C.9.[5]), we have studied quality assessment and error map prediction for segmentation methods. This work has been presented at the International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention (MICCAI) in 2019. We have also proposed a new gland instance segmentation method that learns hierarchical semantic feature matching from histological pairs in an attentive process, where both spatial details and morphological appearances can be well preserved and balanced. It has been presented at the International Workshop on Machine Learning in Medical Imaging in 2020. We have developed a novel segmentation method for vasculature in angiograms. The method uses a newly proposed vesselness measure based on the oriented flux, and spherical harmonics transform. This work has been published in MICCAI 2020. Finally, (refer to Part C.9.[4], C.9.[6]), we have investigated the combination of graphs and convolutional neural networks, namely graph convolutional neural networks (GCN), and its application in population-based disease analysis. This work has been published in MICCAI 2020 and IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP) in 2019.

16245016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16245016.value: The segmentation methods that we have developed in this research project will be further evaluated and compared with more related state-of-the-art methods with publicly available datasets and clinical datasets.

16245016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16245016.value: This research project has developed and evaluated several new image segmentation methods based on deep learning techniques and graphical models. We have investigated a novel Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based method for fully automatic brain tumor segmentation for both high-grade and low-grade gliomas in MR images. Unlike normal tissues or organs that usually have a fixed location or shape, brain tumors with different grades have shown great variation in location, size, structure, and morphological appearance. To address the challenges, we use the new dynamic focal Dice loss function that can focus more on the smaller tumor sub-regions with more complex structures during training. In addition, we have investigated the combination of graphs and convolutional neural networks, namely graph convolutional neural networks (GCN), and its application in population-based disease analysis. The advantage is the ability to effectively combine data of different types, e.g., images and non-image data (age, gender, acquisition site, etc.). The newly developed methods have been extensively evaluated with the multiple publicly available medical image datasets and compared with other state-of-the-art methods. The results are encouraging and have been disseminated in the top-tier conference venues and journal papers.

16245116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16245116.value: 推動高性能計算：FPGA加速器與多核計算機的接口設計

16245116.label: Project Objectives
16245116.value: Based on our preliminary interface design, we will enhance the architectural support with an automatic synthesis flow for optimization of cache size and access ports targeting the given set of acceleration kernels on FPGA. Polyhedral-model-based static program analysis techniques will be employed to analyze the data reuse pattern (loop nests) within one kernel. Two approaches are proposed to extend the cache size optimization for multiple kernels. Further optimization includes location-aware cache synthesis and mapping which take the FPGA Block RAM location into consideration to reduce access delay. Runtime layer support and intelligent scheduling strategy will be developed to best collaborate with the interface architecture. The runtime layer support includes software and hardware runtime to facilitate the flexible requests of kernels on FPGA and manage the kernel execution. A rapid virtual-to-physical address translation scheme is proposed to allow fast data access. Moreover, an intelligent scheduling algorithm which monitors acceleration kernel execution status and correspondingly optimizes the application scheduling for context switch, will be derived to significantly reduce the processor busy waiting time, and hence improve performance. We will build a comprehensive synthesis, compilation and simulation tool for efficient architecture exploration. The tool takes the input applications, a set of kernels and target FPGA information and automatically creates the application binaries for simulation or execution on the CMP. The RTL description of the entire FPGA-side architecture, i.e., accelerators, cache and the CMP-FPGA interface, will also be generated. 16245116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16245116.value: Increase in clock speed and integration density of semiconductors have begun to give diminishing returns in processor performance. Simultaneously, ever increasing demand for big data analytics and related high performance, low power requirements necessitate investigation into new computing architectures. The Chip-Multiprocessor (CMP) has been proposed to speed up application performance through exploiting application level parallelism. However, limits of available instruction level parallelism and high power consumption of processor cores still make it hard to meet the requirement. To address this challenge, CMP integrated with accelerators has been recommended as the new system driver by the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors (ITRS). Prior design has focused mainly on Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) accelerators and simple interface with CMP, relying on scratchpad memory and private caches for accelerators. However, ASIC accelerators are restrictive as they lack post-fabrication flexibility while the application workload can demonstrate significant variations and performance requirements, such as in big-data applications. In contrast, reconfigurable architecture, such as Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based accelerators are increasingly preferred due to their in-field flexibility and low development cost. Their support of both spatial and temporal parallel execution leads to performance and power efficiency that are orders of magnitude higher than a single processor. Leading IT companies, such as Intel and IBM, have started to integrate FPGA in their high-performance computing systems. However, integrating FPGA with CMP is still a new direction and there lacks a systematic investigation and publicly available evaluation platform for seamless support of FPGA-CMP integration. In this project, we propose to investigate the system-level design for FPGA-CMP integration including architectural and run-time layer support. In particular, we will develop an automatic cache synthesis methodology to optimize the cache size, port number and mapping to best facilitate the data reuse among multiple acceleration kernels mapped on FPGA. On top of the interface architecture, a run-time layer including software and hardware run-time modules, will be developed to allow flexible and efficient sharing of acceleration kernels among multiple applications, and manage the data access from memory and network interface. A dynamic application scheduling algorithm is proposed as well to take the context-switch impact and kernel execution status into consideration to significantly reduce application waiting time and hence improve performance. Finally, a comprehensive synthesis and compilation flow together with a cycle-accurate simulator will be built as the first open-source platform to enable the fast design space exploration of FPGA-accelerated heterogeneous systems. 從增加時鐘速度和半導體的集成密度得到的處理器性能回報已經 開始遞減。同時，對於大數據分析和相關的高性能低功耗的需求 不斷增加。為滿足這些需求，必鬚髮展新的計算架構。多核處理 器（CMP）已經通過並行處理提高了性能。然而，現有的指令級 並行度和處理器高功率的限制仍使得難以滿足要求。為面對這一 挑戰，CMP與加速器的集成已被國際半導體技術藍圖（ITRS）推 薦為（ITRS）未來的系統發展方向。以往的設計主要集中在特定 用途集成電路（ASIC）加速器和與CMP簡單的界面，包括暫存器 和加速器自用緩存的設計。然而，ASIC加速器因為缺乏芯片製造 後的靈活性有很大的局限性，因為應用程序的工作負載和性能要 求可以顯著變化，例如大數據處理應用。 與此相反，可重構體系結構，如可編程門陣列（FPGA），因為 它們的靈活性和低開發成本日益成為加速器的優選。其對於空間 和時間並行執行的支持導致性能和電源效率比處理器高幾個數量 級。領先的IT公司，如英特爾和IBM，已經開始在他們的高性能 計算系統集成FPGA。然而，CMP集成FPGA仍然是一個新的方向， 缺乏系統的調查和評估平台。 在這個項目中，我們将研究FPGA-CMP集成的系統級設計，包括 体系结构和運行時層的支持。特別是，我們將開發一個自動緩存 設計方法來優化高速緩存的大小，端口數量和映射來最好的支持 多個FPGA內核加速之間的數據重用。在接口結構的上層，包括 軟件和硬件的運行控制模塊，將被開發以允許在多個應用程序之 間靈活和高效的共享加速器，並且管理數據訪問存儲器和網絡接 口。我們還會開發一個動態應用調度算法，以將任務切換的影響 和內核執行情況納入考慮，來顯著減少應用的等待時間，從而提 高性能。最後，一個全面的綜合和編譯器，以及一個週期精確的 模擬器將聯合建成第一個開源的平台，以加快FPGA加速異構系統 的設計和探索。

16245116.label: Realisation of objectives
16245116.value: All three objectives have been achieved. For the first objective, we have proposed a hybrid method which is based on static analysis and dynamic cache bypassing control to best utilize the cache on FPGA and minimize the miss rate of the FPGA cache. We have implemented the design based on Intel Harp platform and test the design with read data. When synthesizing the cache on FPGA, we will consider the BRAM location and port limits for best trade-off between the resource usage and latency. For the second objective, our work mainly focuses on the task partition and run-time bypassing control. For the task partition, we have analyzed different applications and summarizes the rules for identify the application which is suitable for cache-coherent interface. Then based on the static analysis of the dataflow graph of the application, the task partition between CPU and FPGA can be derived. It is an extension based on the previous partition algorithm, but considers the cache model based communication between the CPU and FPGA and our hybrid cache management. For the third objective, we have developed the automatic analyzing flow and cycle-accurate simulator for the hybrid system. Various benchmarks have been used to evaluate the system design.

16245116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16245116.value: In order to explore the potential of the cache coherent CPU-FPGA system and perform the automatic mapping on this platform, we have performed the research from different perspectives. First of all, we developed a fast and flexible simulator, called PAAS, to support the exploration of different CPU-FPGA architecture configurations including the traditional DMA based CPU-FPGA system and the emerging cache-coherent co-processor systems. It also considers different on-chip interconnection topologies, memory hierarchy, etc. Secondly, we based on the simulator and also real cache-coherent CPU-FPGA platforms like Harp 1 and IBM CAPI, developed the cache optimization strategy composed of static analysis and dynamic bypassing. We considered FPGA cache miss may incur significant miss penalty and propose a hybrid strategy to minimize the contention on the FPGA cache and improve the acceleration performance. In the static analysis, we analyze memory access patterns of the accelerated kernels on FPGA using reuse distance theory and generate kernel characteristics. Thereafter, a dynamic scheme for cache bypassing and partitioning control based on static analysis is developed to increase the cache hit rate and improve the performance. Experiments based on PAAS show that the proposed strategy can increase the cache hit rate by 22.90% on average and speed up the application by up to 12.52% with negligible area overhead. Then we further improve the design based on the real platform of Harp 1. We performed benchmark implementation including the run-time layer configuration and hardware designs. Experiments based on the benchmarks of Polybench applications demonstrate an average performance improvement of 24.92%. To further extend our research, we considered the source level optimization of application for the accelerator performance improvement with a case study of stereo matching application which is widely used in computer vision. Optimizations are performed through code optimization, high-level synthesis pragma setting and design space exploration. Improvement has been achieved including 6.08% lower error, 2x faster speed, 30% less resource usage and 40% less energy consumption. We also extend to consider design optimization in terms of power consumption because power is an important metrics besides performance especially for submicron technology. We introduce a power modeling framework for FPGA high-level synthesis design based on state-of-the-art machine learning techniques to enable early-stage design optimization and exploration. The framework can achieve a fast and accurate power modeling with less than 5% error compared to on-board measurement. The above research output has been published in 5 peer-reviewed top international conferences.

16245116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16245116.value: There is wide scope of extension which can be done based on current research output. First of all, we can consider different variations of the platform interfaces and further evaluate the trade-offs among them. For example, in the recent CPU-FPGA system-on-chip device, such as Xilinx Ultra-scale Zynq board, different ports between CPU-FPGA fabrics have been provided. However, there is no study to guide which port should be used for application implementation on the platform. Secondly, to further ease the design on modern SoC board, it would be good to develop an automatic design flow to analyze the application characteristics and automatically map the application on the platform. The mapping could include the partition of the task, select the suitable port and implement the accelerator design.

16245116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16245116.value: The fast development of big data processing, such as machine learning, has raised a great challenge for the computing system design. Current general-purpose processor, CPU, has difficulty to meet the fast-increasing demands for computing. Hence, hardware accelerators to speed up the data processing have been widely used at present together with CPU as co-processors. The commonly used hardware accelerators include graphics processing unit (GPU), application specific chip (ASIC), and field-programmable gate array (FPGA), etc. FPGA is becoming popular gradually in the cloud computing due to its overall advantages of high performance, low power and short time to market. However, there are many different interface designs between CPU and FPGA which create difficulties to optimize the design for the user. In our project, we try to provide a systematic design methodology to tackle the difficulties based on our developed simulator and real system. Our methodology can analyze the accelerated function characteristics to adjust the system design to achieve the performance optimization. We also extended our research to consider code optimization and power minimization to achieve the best trade-off of performance and power consumption. We have published our works in five top international conferences and released several open-source tools for community usage.

16245216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16245216.value: Moore法在提高速度和降低通過縮放尺寸的晶體管的功耗受到了制約在達到納米尺度。有正在探索減輕這種限制多種選擇。憑藉我們在III-V材料和設備的經驗和專長，我們的目標是開發集成在Si納米尺度的III-V隧道設備（001）晶面片最常用的，由金屬有機化學氣相沉積（MOCVD）。我們將探究既平坦江崎隧道二極管，共振隧道二極管，和隧道晶體管（TFET），具有源極/漏極再生長，並在面內與3D-柵極構造的III-V納米線。在平面隧道結構設計使用的各種III-V將異質納米圖案的Si利用我們集團開發的技術（001）襯底上生長。不同於晶片接合，直接外延生長需要大晶片尺寸，良好的導熱性和Si基板的機械強度的優點，使得它適用於低成本的批量生產和有Si CMOS集成。我們使用兩種獨特的方式不同的納米圖案化的矽晶片上。我們已經開發了非常高品質的平面的GaAs矽上，並且可被用作外延生長GaAs和InP襯底的代用品InP基上矽模板（柔性襯底）。此外，該納米圖案化的矽也已用於III-V族納米線的選擇性外延生長。與由氧化物分離江崎二極管結構水平納米線已在室溫下用在文獻中報導的納米線中的最高的峰 - 谷比示出負微分電阻（NDR）的特性。 有了這些非常令人鼓舞的初步結果，我們計劃去探索成長在Si（100）襯底等隧道結構。第一部分包括各種隧道設備，雙端子和三端，對平面的GaAs / Si和磷化銦/ Si的柔性襯底，以展示襯底的高品質和優化隧道設備的設計。同一設備的設計將被種植和晶格匹配的GaAs或InP襯底上為標杆製造。這項計劃的第二部分將重點介紹如何使用選擇區域生長探索平面III-V納米線二極管和晶體管在Si（100）襯底。雖然（111）襯底傳統的垂直納米線設備正在長足的進步，在垂直方向的設計使它與平面製造平台，並與國家的最先進的矽CMOS器件的集成富有挑戰性的兼容性。該項目旨在開發使用面內取向納米線，省去了很大的障礙與在同一芯片上矽CMOS器件集成的III-V。上圖案化Si襯底位置控制無缺陷的III-V外延層將通過“寬高比俘獲”而形成。擬議的實驗研究鋪平了道路，以最終實現對邏輯應用III-V高速設備。

16245216.label: Realisation of objectives
16245216.value: 5.3 Realization of objectives The primary goal of this project is to design and demonstrate compound III-V tunneling devices directly grown on industry-standard (001) Si wafers and to exemplify their potential for future high-speed and low-power integrated circuits. This includes the selective area growth of different III-V compound semiconductors with different band structures and electron mobilities (including GaAs, InP and GaSb) on (001) wafers; the design, fabrication and characterization of III-V tunneling devices based on these materials; and the monolithic integration of digital circuits such as inverters, tunable triggers and tri-state memory cells on Si wafers. Through this project, we have successfully grown a complete suite of high-quality III-V compound semiconductors (GaAs, InP and GaSb) on exact (001) Si wafers, and demonstrated tunneling diodes and monolithically integrated digital circuits on Si. Although the device implementations are mainly based on the GaAs/InGaAs material system, similar concepts and device/circuit demonstrations can also be extended to the InP/InGaAs and the GaSb/InAs systems. a. Fin-array GaAs and InGaAs ETDs on (001) Si We first demonstrate the selective area growth of GaAs/In0.2Ga0.8As and GaAs/In0.2Ga0.8As quantum well nano-fins of 65-nm width on exactly orientated (001) Si substrates. By exploiting high aspect ratio trenches formed by patterned SiO2 on Si and a V-grooved Si (111) surface in the aspect ratio trapping process, we are able to achieve excellent material quality and structural properties, as evidenced by x-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy. The fabricated GaAs-In0.2Ga0.8A -GaAs fin-array tunnel diodes exhibit a maximum room-temperature peak-to-valley current ratio of 5.4, and negative differential resistance characteristics up to 200 °C. b. ETDs, RTDs and RITDs on nano-patterned Si by MOCVD and Fin-array GaAs/AlGaAs RTDs on Si by ART To enable the demonstration of different tunneling devices such as RTDs and RITDs on Si, we start with the select area growth of InP/InGaAs nano-ridges on (001) Si wafers, which provides more freedom in the engineering of band structures and subsequent device functionalities. Using the conventional aspect ratio trapping technique, we firstly successfully grown laser-quality InP/InGaAs nano-ridge array on exact (001) Si wafers. Multiple InP/InGaAs quantum wells and quantum wires are embedded inside the nano-ridges, which later enables the first room temperature buffer-less telecom laser. Then we devised a new growth strategy named “lateral aspect ratio trapping” to allow for the lateral growth of dislocation-free and large-dimension InP nanowires and membranes on exact (001) Si wafers. Multiple InP/InGaAs quantum wells with different dimensions and architectures are later demonstrated. c. Tunnel diode based multi-value logic on Si substrate Firstly, using the GaAs/In0.2Ga0.8As fin-array tunnel diodes as basic building blocks, a two-state inverter was fabricated using a forward biased GaAs/In0.2Ga0.8As fin-array tunnel diode as drive and a reverse-biased counterpart as load. On-chip operation and reduced fabrication complexity were achieved by exploiting the resistive characteristic of the reverse-biased tunnel diodes and the pre-defined patterns on the Si substrate. Next, a Schmitt-trigger like behavior was observed under double sweep condition by connecting the tunnel diode with an on-chip load resistor. The tunneling trigger circuit was studied using load line analysis. We found that the circuit hysteresis can be tuned by tailoring of the diode dimensions and load resistor values. Finally, we demonstrate functional tri-state memory cells using multi-peaked GaAs/InGaAs fin-array tunnel diodes grown on exact (001) Si substrates. On-chip connection of single-peaked tunnel diode arrays produces I–V characteristics with multiple negative-differential resistance regions. We designed and fabricated two types of tri-state memory cells. In one design, a double-peaked tunnel diode was used as the drive, and a reverse-biased single-peaked tunnel diode was used as the load. In the other design, the tri-state memory cell was realized by the series connection of two forward-biased single-peaked tunnel diodes. d. InGaAs/GaAsSb TFETs with source/drain regrowth on patterned Si substrate To demonstrate high performance TFETs, we start with the selective area growth of the narrow band gap GaSb and InAs nano-ridges on exact (001) Si wafers. By reducing the growth rate and increasing the V/III ratio, we were able to grow uniform InAs nano-ridges on the GaSb buffer layer on exact (001) Si substrates. We also optimized the growth parameters for both the InAs/GaSb and GaSb/InAs hetero-interfaces and thereby enabled the formation of defect-free hetero-interfaces. Building on these results, we then demonstrated the growth of three and four-stacked nano-ridges inside nano-scale Si trenches while maintaining the uniform morphology and defect-free interfaces. We then fabricated tunnel junctions based on the four-stacked GaSb/InAs nano-ridges and obtained a peak current density over 1.0 kA/cm2.

16245216.value: a. Selective area growth of GaAs/InGaAs fin-array tunnel junctions on (001) Si substrates Using GaAs and In0.2GaAs nano-fins selective grown on (001) Si substrates by the aspect ratio trapping method, we demonstrated the first GaAs/InGaAs fin-array tunnel diodes with record high performance. Compared with other reported nano-scale tunnel junctions, our devices feature an in-plane configuration and a unique compatibility with the traditional CMOS process. The demonstration of the nano-scale tunnel diodes lays the foundation for our follow-up research. Results were published in IEEE Electron Device Letters and detailed in Yu Han’s PhD thesis. b. Monolithic integration of tunneling digital circuits on (001) Si substrates With the demonstrated tunnel junctions as basic building components, various digital circuits including tunneling inverters, tunneling triggers and tri-state memory cells were monolithically integrated on (001) Si substrates. These demonstrations show great potential for ultra-fast and low-power logic circuits on Si substrates. The findings were published in IEEE Electron Device Letters and Transactions on Electron Devices and the research methodology and output were detailed in Yu Han’s PhD thesis. c. Selective area growth of InP/InGaAs and lasers on (001) Si substrates Compared with the GaAs material system, the InP material system benefit the tunneling devices in terms of peak current density and integration flexibility. We utilized the aspect ratio trapping technique to grow high quality InP/InGaAs nano-ridges on (001) Si and later demonstrated room temperature lasing from these nano-ridges. We also devised a novel growth strategy named “lateral aspect ratio trapping” to further improve the quality of the epitaxial InP and the compatibility with the existing CMOS technology. The direct growth laser-quality InP/InGaAs nano-ridge structures attests to the excellent quality of our materials and foreshadows the future demonstration of high performance tunneling devices. Part of the research output are presented in Yu Han’s PhD thesis. The findings were published in Optica, Applied Physics Letters, Optics Letters, Photonics Research, and Nanotechnology. d. Selective area growth of multi-hetero-junction InAs/GaSb nano-ridges and tunneling junctions on (001) Si substrates In addition to the GaAs and the InP material systems, the GaSb and the InAs materials offers even higher electron mobility and the broken-gap GaSb/InAs hetero-structures are ideal candidates for tunneling devices with ultra-high performances. Using the aspect ratio trapping technique, we demonstrated the selective growth of multi-stacked InAs/GaSb nano-ridges on (001) patterned Si substrates and the fabrication of tunneling diodes with high current densities. These InAs/GaSb nano-ridges show great potential for applications in nano-scale tunneling devices as well as long wavelength light emitters and detectors. These findings were published in Nanotechnology and Journal of Applied Physics.

16245216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16245216.value: a. III-V tunneling devices based on the InP/InGaAs and the GaSb/InAs materials systems Compared with the GaAs/InGaAs material system where we demonstrated various III-V tunneling devices, the InP/InGaAs and GaSb/InAs materials with narrow band gaps and higher electron mobility are better candidates for tunneling devices with ultra-high performances. In this project, we have successfully grown high quality InP/InGaAs and GaSb/InAs on (001) Si wafers, and future work could be done to fabricate tunneling devices based on our current materials. b. Demonstration of the first TFET selectively grown on (001) Si wafers Tunneling field effect transistor (TFET) is regarded as the most promising candidate to further reduce the power consumption of microelectronics chips. In this project, we have demonstrated GaAs/InGaAs tunneling diodes and integrated digital circuits on (001) Si wafers. Moving forward to the demonstration of TFETs requires the adoption of the GaSb/InAs materials system and several regrowth steps.

16245216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16245216.value: In this project, we demonstrated the selective are growth of high quality nano-scale III-V materials including GaAs, InP and GaSb on industry-standard (001) Si wafers and designed/fabricated tunnel diodes and monolithically integrated digital circuits on Si wafers. In sharp contrast to most of previous results using vertical nanowires on (111) Si substrates, our devices were fabricated using in-plane fin-arrays formed by catalyst-free growth on CMOS-compatible (001) Si and thereby offers a much better compatibility for heterogeneous integration by direct growth. Firstly, we demonstrate the selective growth of GaAs/InGaAs nano-fins on Si wafers, and then fabricated fin-array tunnel junctions and various digital circuits to illustrate the great potential of the tunnel devices for future low-power logic applications. Secondly, we also realized the selective growth of laser-quality InP/InGaAs nano-ridges on Si wafers using both the conventional aspect ratio trapping method and our designed lateral aspect ratio trapping method. Finally, we moved on to demonstrate the selective growth of narrow band gap GaSb/InAs multi-hetero-junctions as well as tunnel diodes on Si. The direct growth of the complete suite of III-V materials on industry-standard Si wafers shows great potential to further improve the integration density and reduce the power consumption of current IC technologies.

16245516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16245516.value: Thermal radiation detection has been an active area in recent decades. Seeking for efficient, low-cost and high-resolution solutions is continuously driven by the great demands from various areas. Current high-resolution thermal radiation systems are generally very expensive and bulky because an integrated complicated cryogenic cooling system is necessary for the suppression of thermal noise. With the recent development of upconversion materials, luminescence upconversion has begun to receive renewed attention for their potential application in thermal radiation detection. By combining with an upconverter to change long-wavelength infrared to visible light, conventional visible light sensors can be used to detect thermal radiation, therefore providing a compact, low-cost and high-resolution solution. Although upconversion materials open doors to a wide range of new opportunities, they remain too inefficient for most applications. Incorporating plasmonic microstructures provides a promising pathway to highly efficient upconversion. This work is aimed at developing an efficient thermal radiation detection system for infrared with a wavelength longer than 1.5 um on the basis of visible light sensors and luminescence upconverter through enhancing the upconversion efficiency by introducing surface plasmon. Meanwhile, we plan to develop comprehensive understanding for plasmon enhanced infrared upconversion, including absorption, emission, energy transfer and nonradiative transitions. We will focus on Er3+/Tm3+-doped glass system instead of the conventional Yb3+ systems for near infrared upconversion. We will combine experimental characterization with the numerical simulations to optimize the design of the plasmonic structures and analyze the influence of plasmon on the infrared upconversion process. The knowledge obtained will be used to optimize the dopant selection, dopant concentration as well as the plasmonic pattern to develop a high-performance upconverter. Thereafter, the combined thermal radiation system will be characterized and optimized. The proposed research on plasmon enhanced infrared upconversion could potentially benefit many exciting fields such as solar energy harvesting and chemical detection. 熱輻射探測在近數十年來一直是很活躍的領域。各個應用領域都一直在尋求高效，低價，高分辨率的解決方案。現有的高分辨率熱輻射探測系統通常需要集成複雜的低溫冷卻系統來降低熱噪聲，所以非常昂貴，體積龐大。隨著上轉換材料的發展，光上轉換在熱輻射領域的應用得到關注。通過結合一個上轉換器將長波長紅外輻射轉變為可見光，傳統的可見光傳感器可以被用來探測紅外，從而提供了一個緊湊，廉價和高分辨率的解決方案。儘管上轉換材料提供了諸多可能，但是目前的上轉換效率很低。應用表面等離子體結構來提高轉換效率是很有希望的。本項目致力於發展一種高效的能探測波長在1.5微米以上熱輻射的系統，通過採用表面等離子體來增進上轉換效率。同時，我們計劃研究表面等離子體對上轉換的增強機理，包括吸收，發射，和非輻射性轉換。我們將專注于Er3+/Tm3+摻雜玻璃體系，將實驗表征和數學模擬計算結合來優化等離子結構設計并分析等離子體對紅外上轉換過程的影響，所得結果將用來優化摻雜離子，摻雜濃度和等離子結構來提升上轉換器的性能。然後，我們將表征和優化集成的熱輻射系統。本項目的研究也將有助于太陽能收集和化學檢測等領域。

16245516.label: Realisation of objectives
16245516.value: Mr. Dezhao Li and Mr. Yang Li were admitted as PhD students to work on the project. Mr. Dezhao Li was responsible for the infrared characterization and he graduated in August 2018. Mr. Li conducted numerical simulations to design the plasmonic structure, the fabrication and characterization of the plasmonic structure as well as the upconversion tests. He received his PhD degree at HKUST in August, 2019. We have developed theoretical models to predict the antistokes radiation under enhanced electromagnetic field. The light absorption, reflection and emission have been modeled with the enhanced field. It is found that with the enhanced field, the absorption and emission can be significantly enhanced while the reflection will dependent on the incident spectrum. Meanwhile, we have developed plasmonic nanoantennas (PNs) with film-coupled triangular nanodisk for upconversion enhancement. Plasmonic structures, which exploit the unique properties of noble metal nanoparticles, are able to capture light and confine the electromagnetic field at the nanoscale. To significantly enhance the efficiency of upconversion process, those plasmonic structures with extreme field enhancement are desirable because the efficiency enhancement is strongly dependent on the field enhancement factor. We proposed a film-coupled plasmonic structure made of triangular Ag nanodisk array, Al2O3, and Au film. Due to the combination of lightning rod effect with the out-of-plane plasmonic coupling, the calculated electric field enhancement reaches as high as 211, showing great potential for upconversion enhancement. Based on the optimized design, we experimentally exploited equilateral triangular nanodisks and an out-of-plane nanogap of 10 nm, taking advantage of their abilities to confine electromagnetic field components in x-y plane and z direction, respectively. The proposed Ag/Al2O3/Au PNs comprising nanodisks of different shapes and sizes were fabricated on silicon wafers. The absorption spectra of the plasmonic structures were characterized. The proposed plasmonic structures show near-perfect absorption at the resonant wavelength. The resonant wavelength can be easily tuned by changing the geometric parameters of the structures. Both strong field enhancedment and near-perfect light absorption were achieved in the proposed plasmonic structure, which is mainly attributed to the strong magnetic resonance mode. The plasmonic structure with triangular nanodisks display a broader absorption bandwidth when compared with that of circular nanodisks and the square nanodisks, which will benefit the practical application in the upconversion process. With the findings on equilateral triangular nanodisks and the out-of-plane plasmonic coupling in a metal-insulator-metal sandwich structure, we developed high-performance spectrally selective plasmonic absorbers with excellent thermal stability. The plasmonic absorber comprises multiple strategies (structure-, material-, and shape-based) and demonstrate full-spectrum sunlight absorption and greatly reduced infrared emission, ultimately boosting the record-high light-thermal efficiency (1000 K) of plasmonic selective absorber from 66.4% to 77.3% under 100‐sun illumination. This superior performance is not only stable at temperatures of 1000 K, but also robust to the variations in the constituent materials of top nanodisks and dielectric spacers. Moreover, the performance of such PMAs is independent of the lateral periodicity or orientations of meta-atoms, paving the way for their large-scale deployment. To further reduce the cost, we developed solution-processed metamaterial absorbers by facile solution-based processes via through assembling colloidal titanium nitride (TiN) NPs spontaneously into an ultrathin film on reflective substrates (TiN here) to form an asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavity. using a NP film of only ~120 nm thickness, it provides near-perfect absorption over the full sunlight spectrum (~95%) while low mid-IR emission (~3% and ~22% at 300 K and 1000 K, respectively). The plasmonic metamaterial with all-ceramic components endows the SSA excellent stability up to 727 °C. All these properties offer reliable operation and high efficiency over an ultra-wide temperature range from 100 to 727 °C. This work demonstrates the great potential of cost-effective solution-processed metamaterials in spectral control and solar energy conversion.

16245516.label: Major findings and research outcome
16245516.value: 1. Two PhD students were trained in this project and relevant projects. They received their PhD degrees in August 2018 and August 2019, respectively. 2. Seven journal papers have been published based on the research results from this project. 3. A theoretical model has been developed to predict the upconversion behavior of NaYF4:Yb3+, Er3+, and the influence of photon density of states. 4. Numerical simulations have been conducted to find optimal plasmonic structures for selective absorption and emission with much enhanced field. With the optimized design, plasmonic structures with both a near-perfect absorption and strong field enhancement have been fabricated and characterized. A plasmonic MIM structure that is suitable for near infrared upconversion in NaYF4:Yb3+/Er3+ has been developed and characterized. The influence of period and particle size has been experimentally investigated 5. We designed a selective solar absorber based on triangular plasmonic nanodisks by introducing out-of-plane plasmonic coupling between triangular nanodisks and a tantalum reflector in a metal–insulator–metal (MIM) sandwich structure. This design ultimately boosts the record of solar-thermal efficiency of plasmonic absorbers from 66.4% to 77.3% under 100-sun illumination at 1000 K, which is the best performance achieved by plasmonic-based selective absorber. 6. We have developed a plasmonic metamaterials with tunable broadband selective absorption using a facile solution-based process. Enabled by the synergetic in-plane plasmon and out-of-plane Fabry-Perot resonances, the solution-processed plasmonic metamaterial simultaneously achieves high, full-spectrum solar absorption (95%), low mid-infrared emission (3%/22% at 100/727 °C), and excellent stability over a temperature range of 100-727 °C, outperforming most state-of-the-art absorbers at their specific operating temperatures. Such competitive performances are accompanied by a significant cost reduction (~80%) compared with commercial products, rendering it a promising candidate for both low and high-temperature applications. A patent has been filed for this novel metamaterial structure. 7. Based on the developed plasmonic absorbing structure, we have developed a thermoelectric infrared sensor, which show much enhanced responsivity of ~4000 V/W, compared with the predicted value of 2000 V/W for structures without the plasmonic absorber.

16245516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16245516.value: The developed solution-processed plasmonic absorber may be applied for high-efficiency solar-thermal energy conversion owing to its high selectivity, near-perfect solar absorption and excellent thermal stability. In addition to its superior performance, its cost is about 80% lower than the commercial selective absorbers, showing great potential in commercialization. About 2 million fund from industry has been attracted for pre-production investigation.

16245516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16245516.value: Thermal radiation detection has been an active area in recent decades. Seeking for efficient, low-cost and high-resolution solutions is continuously driven by the great demands from various areas. Current high-resolution thermal radiation systems are generally very expensive and bulky because an integrated complicated cryogenic cooling system is necessary for the suppression of thermal noise. By combining the infrared sensor with a plasma-enhanced absorber, a selective near-infrared infrared absorption can be realized. Meanwhile, the plasmonic structure can work as a microscale antenna to concentrate light energy in a small region, which can significantly improve the overall performance. We have systematically investigated the effects of various factors, such as the plasmonic pattern shape and distribution, thickness of the glass layer, the dielectric functions of the glass on the selective absorption and emission. Nanoscale plasmonic antennas have been developed, which enable both the strong field enhancement and near-perfect light absorption simultaneously. Based on the obtained knowledge, we have developed plasmonic selective absorbers, which show much better performance than traditional multilayer absorbers owing to the perfect selective absorption and high local heat flux. Thermoelectric Infrared sensors with the developed absorber demonstrated much improved performance, showing great potential of the plasmonic selective surface in thermal sensing.

16280316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16280316.value: The manufacturing industry is experiencing an incredible paradigm shift motivated by the changing business world where speed, efficiency and flexibility of product development are driven to new heights. The Internet has revolutionized the way business is done and many companies have adapted to this through adaptation of their business models. The new paradigm has been coined ‘Industrie 4.0’, characterized by the digitalization of product lifecycle, horizontal and vertical integration and the concept of cyber-physical systems. In the previous decade, the advance in 3C (computers, communications and consumer electronics) manufacturing of increase level of automation and production can no longer satisfies the appetite of the current consumer market. A more drastic development is needed to move towards Smart Manufacturing. Smart Manufacturing entails improvement in three areas: 1) time-to-market speed, 2) energy and resource efficiency and 3) flexibility to allow fast response to new market needs. The current B2B and B2C businesses enabled by the Internet, demand a new production logistics where innovation cycles of complex products are short, individualized and small lots manufacturing are efficient processes and customization capability increases manufacturers’ competitiveness. Examples of target indices include ability to produce over 1000 different products averaging 1 product per second at 12dpm for a typical 3C manufacturer. Digitalization in all stages of manufacturing (design, planning, engineering, production and services) is the key to the next technical revolution. Part of this digitalization involves enabling greater autonomy in the robots used in the production line by using simulation in the design phase and more streamlined horizontal and vertical integration of these robots in the manufacturing process. Within a work cell of a production line, different modular autonomous robots are employed and the work cell can be optimized to offer the most adaptive and flexible deployment models. However, each robot with respect to the dedicated task, traditionally, still requires time-consuming, off-line engineering to retrofit them in the work flow. The answer to the Industrie 4.0 requirements for 3C robot is an integrated automation framework; integrated engineering, runtime optimization for controllers, distributed I/O, HMI, drives, motion control and motors. In the proposed research, the aim is to develop on-line, high-fidelity model dynamics identification; a core piece of the integrated framework. The dynamics identification and control problem will be studied in the unified framework with special focus in its application on parallel mechanisms, and its performance and robustness will be verified with experimentation.

16280316.label: Realisation of objectives
16280316.value: We choose geometric method to derive robot dynamic equations. Here we prefer to use Newton-Euler method in stead of Lagrange method by applying elegant Lie Group Theory. For torque calculation, we just directly use original recursive form of Newton-Euler equation which guarantees the most efficient way. However, in order to design controller, recursive form is no long suitable and matrix form is in need. What’s more, for preparing dynamic identification, we should transform matrix form into regressive form which is linear with respected to dynamic parameters. Regressive form is also widely chosen for Adaptive Control. We proceed dynamic parameters identification. Successful Identification firstly needs elegant robot modelling as discussed above. Then we regroup dynamic parameters into minimal identifiable parameters for evaluation. In order to reduce sensitivity to noise and disturbance, exciting trajectory for identification should be carefully optimized. Then robot executes trajectory and related data are sampled in experiment. Using weighted least square method and machine learning algorithm, we attain equivalent dynamic parameters given some reasonable assumptions. Non-linear controller design techniques are applied to get computed torque controller formula. Then, based on the identified model, we systemically compare different control schemes both in simulation and experiment. We explore traditional PID control, PID + Feedforward Control, Computed Torque Control and finally Adaptive Control. Base on the dynamic model of robot, we enhance the performance and fulfill the anti-vibration function. The most difficult problem of dragging robot is how to obtain external force. Our method is exploiting dynamic compensations and sampling feedback motor current. The algorithm relies on the assumption identified dynamic model can accurately compensate gravity and friction to create out a virtual zero-gravity and zero-friction environment. Similarly, the collision detection facing the same difficulty. When the feedforward current is obviously inconsistent with feedback current, the collision can be judged.

16280316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16280316.value: We gave a systematic and comprehensive study of designing and implementing dynamics-based controller of industrial robots. Our research almost contains most fundamental aspects for dynamics-based controller, that are dynamics modelling, parameters identification, controller design, trajectory optimization and other dynamics based applications. More importantly, we followed basic principles underlying mode based design which are very popular in automotive and aerospace due to difficulties of practical implementation. The model-based design suggests researchers to fully utilize powerful simulation tools from preliminary to advanced design of controller. We used geometric method to derive the regressive form for robot dynamics. The formulation is in accord with the recursive and matrix form based on Lie Group. By defining basic operations, we can get a concise and explicit regressive form. We implemented dynamics computation in three different forms and thus compare and evaluate their accuracy and efficiency. For dynamics identification, we used geometric method to prove the minimal parameters set in detail for 6R manipulator case. We applied identification algorithms into different manipulators. The identified models are quite convincing and are successfully used for other applications. As for dynamics-based application, we fulfilled the goal of robot teaching by dragging based dynamics model. We proposed a control scheme which exploited dynamics model for compensation to provide assistance force.

16280316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16280316.value: Our goal is to control the motor to following command position with near-zero position error. In this control strategy, we assume the accurate control of motor can bring in precise control of end-tip. This is not the case at all. In practice, shaft and load should have a certain of flexibility not absolute rigid. Sudden change in the acceleration (jerk) will apply a perturbation, resulting in oscillations of the load. While the control loop will overcome these oscillations at motor position level, the load will still oscillate strongly. We need to design vibration suppression controller to reduce the following error and settling time of the load. Although we may sacrifice accuracy at motor and encoder side, the overall performance of system, as evaluated at load position, may be significantly improved.

16280316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16280316.value: Our work provides a highly complete and systematic procedure for successfully applying dynamics-based control of industrial robot into real practice. Dynamics compensation, especially for friction and gravity force, provides satisfying assistant force for easily dragging of robot. Operators are able to teach robot for spraying and painting.

16300016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300016.value: Marine microorganisms are a rich source of novel molecular entities (marine natural products). These marine substances often deliver unique biological activities, such as cytotoxicity, and are promising candidates for development of effective medicine. This project deals with chemical synthesis of a novel class of marine natural products, iriomoteolides, which were isolated from the benthic dinoflagellate Amphidinium species. Iriomoteolides currently consist of eight (8) structural types which belong to a novel family of marine macrolides of different ring sizes. In particular, iriomoteolide-2a and -3a feature an odd number of ring sizes, which is quite rare among the known macrolides. Their proposed structures remain to be confirmed except for iriomoteolide-3a whose structure has been confirmed by total synthesis. The chemical synthesis of these macrolides is very challenging; many total synthesis efforts eventually point to wrongly assigned structures for iriomoteolide-1a and the related iriomoteolide-1b, and -1c. Our continuing interest in total synthesis of marine macrolides has two-fold impact; confirmation of the novel macrolide structures and production of samples for screening biological activity of marine macrolides and analogues. In order to discover lead compounds for drug development, it is important for us to take the challenging task in marine natural product research for determining/confirming the correct molecular structures. Because marine macrolides are often available in few milligram quantities, chemical synthesis provides a powerful tool to confirm or revise the proposed structures and to access the novel entities for biological study. In early 2015, the structure of iriomoteolide-2a was reported as a novel 23-membered macrolide containing eleven (11) stereogenic centers, one bis-tetrahydrofuran subunit, and three double bonds. Iriomoteolide-2a has a complex molecular architecture within the known iriomoteolides and it serves as an excellent target molecule for total synthesis. As a continuation of the PI’s previous studies on diverted total synthesis of macrolides including iriomoteolide-1a stereoisomers, a multimodule assembly strategy will be developed for diverted total synthesis of iriomoteolide-2a and analogues. The possible outcomes of the proposed research are multiple, such as verification of the proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a, confirmation of its absolute configuration, and access to synthetic materials related to iriomoteolide-2a for biological study. 海洋微生物是新型分子實體的豐富來源，這些統稱為海洋天然産物的物質多具有獨特的生物活性，諸如細胞毒性等，是有望開發成為有效醫藥品的候選物質。本項目從事一類新型海洋天然産物的化學合成，它們是從底棲前溝藻屬甲藻（Amphidinium sp.）分離得到的稱為iriomoteolides的新型大環內酯。這個家族目前有8個不同大小環的結搆類型，其中iriomoteolide-2a和-3a含有大環內酯中少見的奇數環結搆。除了iriomoteolide-3a的結搆已被全合成證實以外，其它iriomoteolides的分子結搆還有待確認。這類大環內酯的化學合成具有極大的挑戰性，一個主要原因是iriomoteolide-1a及其相關的iriomoteolide-1b和-1c的指定結搆是錯的，並通過許多研究小組的全合成工作最終得以證明。我們持續研究大環內酯的全合成具有雙重意義：證明新型大環內酯的結搆、和製備海洋大環內酯及其類似物的樣本用于篩選生物活性。確認或證明正確的分子結搆是海洋天然産物研究中的一項挑戰性任務，我們從事這些工作對發現先導化合物用于藥物開發具有重要的意義。因為分離到的海洋大環內酯僅有毫克級的量，化學合成就成為一種強有力的手段用于確認或修正初始建議的結構以及得到生物學研究所需的新型分子實體。2015年報道了iriomoteolide-2a的結搆，它是一個新型的23元大環內酯，含有11個手性中心、一個連二四氫呋喃單元、以及三個雙鍵。在已經報道的iriomoteolides中，iriomoteolide-2a具有復雜的分子搆造，當是一個理想的全合成目標分子。本項目負責人前期進行了大環內酯、包括iriomoteolide-1a立體異構體的多樣性全合成研究，作為前期工作的延續，本項目期間將開發一種多模塊組裝的策略用于iriomoteolide-2a及其類似物的多樣性全合成。本項目預期成果是多重的，諸如確認iriomoteolide-2a的建議結構、確定它的絕對構型、及得到與iriomoteolide-2a相關的合成樣本用于生物學研究。

16300016.label: Realisation of objectives
16300016.value: Iriomoteolide-2a is the first reported naturally occurring 23-membered marine macrolide. The proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a was reported in 2015 by Tsuda and co-workers [Kumagai, K.; Tsuda, M.; Masuda, A.; Fukushi, E.; Kawabata, J. Heterocycles, 2015, 91, 265–274]. The PI’s laboratory submitted the synthetic study proposal in 2016, and begun the funded project by focusing on the synthesis of the originally proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a according to our Objective 1. Three key operations were designed, including (a) the B-alkyl Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction between the C6–C18 alkenyl iodide and the C19–C28 alkyl iodide; (b) esterification of the C23-OH with the C1–C5 acid; and (c) the ring-closing metathesis (RCM) to form the (E)-double bond at C5–C6. It was found later that another two research groups, in Japan and the Mainland of China, respectively, adopted the similar synthetic strategies, leading to the same C6–C18 alkenyl iodide fragment possessing the bis-tetrahydrofuran (bis-THF) core. In January 2018, Fuwa and co-workers reported the first total synthesis of the initially proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a and two other stereoisomers [Sakamoto, K.; Hakamata, A.; Tsuda, M.; Fuwa, H. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 3801–3805.]. The full account of Fuwa’s synthesis and structural revision of iriomoteolide-2a appeared in 2019 [Sakamoto, K.; Hakamata, A.; Iwasaki, A.; Suenaga, K.; Tsuda, M.; Fuwa, H. Chem. Eur. J., 2019, 25, 8528–8542.]. In April 2018, Ye–Guo’s team reported a synthesis of the C6–C28 advanced intermediate of the proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a by coupling of the same C6–C18 alkenyl iodide with an in situ prepared alkyl borane [Wang, L.; Wu, F.; Jia, X.; Xu, Z.; Guo, Y.; Ye, T. Org. Lett. 2018, 20, 2213–2215.]. The PI’s synthesis of the C6–C18 alkenyl iodide was published in December 2018. Therefore, the three research groups independently synthesized the C6–C18 alkenyl iodide using different synthetic routes. Objective 2 has been achieved with successful synthesis of the C6–C18 alkenyl iodide of the proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a. A unique sequence of reactions, being different from the methods used by Fuwa's and Ye–Guo’s teams, was established in the PI’s synthesis. Mainly, the C11–C13 syn,syn-all-OH-containing stereotriad was constructed from the corresponding C(11S)-allylic alcohol via asymmetric dihydroxylation (AD); the latter underwent spontaneously an intramolecular SN2 cyclization to form the C9–C12 tetrahydrofuran (THF). After installation of the C(16R)-propargylic mesylate, a second intramolecular SN2 cyclization, being attacked by the C(13R)-OH, took place to furnish the C13–C16 THF ring. All spectroscopic data of the synthesized C6–C18 alkenyl iodide are consistent with those reported by Fuwa's and Ye–Guo’s teams [See section 8, journal publication #1 & section 10, PhD thesis of Wen ZHANG]. It should be emphasized that the PI’s synthetic sequence featuring stepwise double SN2 cyclization reactions is flexible and could be easily amended for synthesis of the C6–C18 alkenyl iodide of the revised structure of iriomoteolide-2a. Simply starting from the corresponding C(13R)-allylic alcohol, the requisite C11–C13 syn,anti-all-OH-containing stereotriad could be prepared by selecting a suitable chiral ligand for the AD reaction. Objective 3 and Objective 4 are concerned with synthesis of the C19–C28 fragment and assembly of the above mentioned C6–C18 alkenyl iodide, the C19–C28 alkyl iodide with the masked C23-OH group, and the C1–C5 acid fragment into the target structure of iriomoteolide-2a. Since Fuwa and co-workers have completed the total synthesis of the proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a using the same C6–C18 alkenyl iodide, the PI’s synthetic study could be conceptually considered as a formal total synthesis of the proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a. In order to demonstrate the coupling reaction of the C6–C18 alkenyl iodide, a model alkyl iodide was successfully used in the “9-MeO-9-BBN variant” of the B-alkyl Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling to afford the elaborated structure [See section 8, journal publication #1 & section 10, PhD thesis of Wen ZHANG]. Technically speaking, the proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a could be prepared from the PI’s synthesized C6–C18 alkenyl iodide by following the reported methods in the literature. Objective 5 was not possible to pursue due to the significantly reduced funding amount as mentioned in Objective 4. There was insufficient manpower to prepare samples for cytotoxicy experiments.

16300016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300016.value: The marine macrolide, iriomoteolide-2a, possesses the bis-tetrahydrofuran (bis-THF) structural unit with two extra substituents (OH and Me) one each on the THF rings. This structural feature is unique among the known natural products and it might be one of the reasons for the wrongly assigned structure of iriomoteolide-2a. The initially proposed configuration of C11-OH and C12 of iriomoteolide-2a was revised after Fuwa and co-workers’ total synthesis study [Sakamoto, K.; Hakamata, A.; Tsuda, M.; Fuwa, H. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 3801–3805 & Sakamoto, K.; Hakamata, A.; Iwasaki, A.; Suenaga, K.; Tsuda, M.; Fuwa, H. Chem. Eur. J., 2019, 25, 8528–8542.]. In this project, the PI’s lab has established a synthetic approach toward the C6–C18 alkenyl iodide fragment using stepwise double SN2 cyclization reactions to construct the bis-THF ring system [See section 8, journal publication #1 & section 10, PhD thesis of Wen ZHANG]. This synthesis differentiates from those sequences of reactions used by Fuwa's and Ye–Guo’s teams for the synthesis of the same fragment. Specially, the key C11–C13 syn,syn- and syn,anti-all-OH-containing stereotriads could be easily prepared from the corresponding C(11S)- or C(13R)-allylic alcohols, respectively, via asymmetric dihydroxylation (AD). The flexibility of the PI’s synthesis in combination with the AD reaction renders the established synthetic methodology applicable to related structural units with dense functionalities. The other interesting finding is that the configuration of the chiral propargylic mesylate is stable during the SN2 cyclization, being deferent from the chiral allylic mesylate, so that no racemization/epimerization was observed.

16300016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300016.value: The established synthesis of the C6–C18 bis-THF-containing alkenyl iodide for the initially proposed structure of iriomoteolide-2a could be amended for the synthesis of the revised structure of iriomoteolide-2a. The know-how gained in this project in handling the dense oxygenated functionalities should be valuable for synthesis of complex polyketide-type marine natural products by the synthetic community.

16300016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300016.value: Iriomoteolide-2a is a novel and structurally complex molecule isolated from marine benthic dinoflagellate Amphidinium species (HYA024). In preliminary biological activity study, this new substance exhibited cytotoxicity against some cancer cell lines with promising anticancer activity. However, it is found that the originally proposed molecular structure is not correct. The PI’s laboratory along with two other research teams independently initiated research programs to produce the substance through chemical synthesis. Similar synthetic routes were adopted and the same C6–C18 key structural unit was produced albeit using different sequence of reactions. The PI’s team has established a flexible synthesis of the C6–C18 structural unit of the originally proposed molecular structure of iriomoteolide-2a. The Japanese team was the first to complete the total synthesis and revised the structure of iriomoteolide-2a. The PI’s synthetic method could be easily amended for synthesis of the revised C6–C18 structural unit and might be conceptually considered as a formal total synthesis by following the late reactions reported in the literature. In addition, the know-how gained from this project should serve as valuable reference for synthesis of other related natural products with potential bioactivity.
