16300616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16300616.value: 復指數疊加信號的穩健重構

16300616.label: Project Objectives
16300616.value: We will construct approaches based on convex optimization for the recovery of the signal of interest. We plan to propose new semi-definite programmings (SDPs), as well as their fast numerical solvers and performance analysis. There are two specific directions. In the first direction, we aim at better and more robust recovery by incorporating available information on the parameters of the signal into the SDPs. The second direction is to reduce the size of the SDPs significantly for multi-variable signals. All existing convex optimizations require solving an SDP with unknown matrix of size that is the square of the signal size. Our goal is to reduce the matrix size to the same order as the signal size. We will construct approaches based on non-convex optimization for the recovery of the signal of interest. We will use the fact that the recovery of the signal of interest can be converted to (or itself is) a problem of low-rank matrix/tensor reconstruction. We will consider two types of algorithms. In the first type of algorithms, the unknown low-rank matrix/tensor is represented in a low-rank factorization form. We will design algorithms to find the factors. Additional regularizations on the factors will be imposed if necessary. In the other type of algorithms, we view the unknown low-rank matrix as an element on the manifold of all low-rank matrices. This will lead to algorithms based on manifold optimizations and projections. According to existing non-convex optimization for low-rank matrix/tensor reconstruction and our experiences, all these non-convex algorithms are expected to require less memory and less CPU-time than convex optimization methods. Theoretical justification on the convergence is also one of the goal of this project. We will look into the recent development in the literature on the convergence to the correct solution of non-convex approaches for low-rank matrix reconstruction. We will apply the resulting approaches to problems arising from real-world applications. We will pay particular attention to accelerated NMR spectroscopy, an important tool for many tasks in chemical and biological science. On the one hand, the resulting algorithms will be able to recover signals with a high dimension and huge size from their very noisy under-samples, to meet the requirement in a real NMR spectroscopy setting. On the other hand, we will design both convex and non-convex algorithms that are customized for accelerated NMR spectroscopy by considering its specific constraints on parameters. We will also study efficient sampling schemes tailored to NMR experiments to achieve better recovery quality and reduce measurement time. Last but not least, we will actively seek other practical applications of our algorithms developed in this project.

16300616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300616.value: This proposal is devoted to the robust recovery of a signal that is a weighted sum of a few complex exponentials from a small amount of its linear measurements. The signal of interest arises from many practical applications, including wireless communication, medical imaging, seismic data processing, fluorescence microscopy, and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. In all these applications, it is difficult to get a complete sample of the signal of interest, due to the limitation of hardware devices or physical constraints. Instead, only a small number of linear measurements are usually observed, and sometimes these linear measurements are not accurate. Therefore, we have to recover of the signal of interest robustly from its linear under-samples. Because the dictionary for the signal of interest contains infinitely many atoms, the conventional compressed sensing approach with $ell_1$-norm minimization suffers from dictionary discretization error known as basis mismatch. Recently, there is a growing interest in developing approaches that can recover signals with continuous-valued parameters precisely even from very few linear measurements. However, existing approaches either pose too many restrictions on the parameters, such that they can only be applied to only a small number of special cases, or pose no restriction on the parameters, thus ignoring the structures possessed by the real application. Furthermore, when they are applied to multi-variate signals, the resulting optimization problem has a huge unknown matrix even when the signal is of moderate size. This prohibits the application of such methods to practical problems. We will propose new approaches that are able to recover the signal of interest with continuous-valued parameters. The constraints on the parameters can be incorporated to get better formulations than existing approaches. More importantly, for multi-variate signals, our approaches solve matrix optimization problems with the unknown matrix almost the same size as the signal, the minimum size that we can expect. Our new approaches will be based on both convex and non-convex formulations. For convex formulations, we will construct semi-definite programmings (SDPs). For non-convex formulations, our proposed algorithms are based on the fact that the signal recovery can be converted to a low-rank matrix reconstruction problem. Fast numerical solvers will be studied, and their performance analysis provided. Finally, we plan to apply resulting approaches to practical applications, particularly, accelerated NMR spectroscopy. We expect the resulting approaches to be viable alternatives to the current state-of-the-art techniques in applied sciences. 本項目研究怎樣用少數線性測量來穩健的重構一個復指數疊加信號。此類信號在實際應用中廣泛出現，包括無線通信、醫學影像、地質信號處理、熒光顯微鏡、核磁共振波譜等。在這些應用中，由於硬件設備的限制或其他物理原因，人們往往不能觀測到復指數疊加信號的全部信息，而只是一少部分線性測量且這些測量有時還不甚准確。所以，我們必須用線性欠采樣來穩健的重構一個復指數疊加信號。 由於單個復指數信號的頻率和其它參數是連續的，傳統的基於L1-範數最優化的壓縮感知方法必須先離散這些參數，然後構造有限離散字典來稀疏表示信號。然而，微小的參數離散誤差也會令重構信號與真實信號相差甚遠。最近，越來越多研究者考慮毋需參數離散的方法。然而，現存的此類方法要麼對參數限制過多，從而只能夠應用到一小部分特例上；要麼對參數沒有限制，使得實際信號的結構被忽略。而且，當這些方法運用到多變量信號時，需要解超大規模的優化問題，即使信號的大小不是特別大。這些都局限了已有方法在實際問題裡的應用。 本項目將提出復指數疊加信號重構的毋需離散參數的新方法。我們將考慮對參數的約束，進而得到比現存方法更准確的方法。更重要的是，對於多變量信號，我們的新方法只需要解一個小規模的矩陣優化問題，其未知變量多少同信號大小一個量級 。我們的新方法將把信號重構問題表達成凸或非凸優化。對於凸優化，我們用半正定規劃來構造。至於非凸優化，我們將把復指數疊加信號重構轉化為一個低秩矩陣重構問題。我們也會提供相應的數值算法及其分析。最後，我們計劃將所導出之方法應用到實際問題中，包括核磁共振波譜的加速。我們期望我們的新方法成為解決這些實際問題的新工具。

16300616.label: Realisation of objectives
16300616.value: All the objectives in the original application are achieved. For objective 1: We have developed convex methods for robust recovery of sums of complex exponentials from a few of its measurements to reduce the matrix size and exploit the structure. For multi-dimensional signals, the traditional convex approaches solve optimizations on multi-level structured matrices, which is prohibitive for problems of large size. To reduce the number of unknowns, we replaced multi-level structured matrices by some mosaic Toeplitz-Hankel matrices, and we proposed the corresponding semi-definite programming (SDP). To further reduce the number of unknowns and exploit more structure of the underlying signal, we also embedded some convex objective functions into matrix factorizations for the recovery of the sum of exponential signals. For objective 2: We proposed non-convex methods for robust recovery of sums of complex exponentials from a few of its measurements, and for some of them we also provided a theoretical recovery guarantee. All these methods are done through low-rank structured matrix recovery. To recover the low-rank structured matrix, we have represented it either as an element on the Riemannian manifold of low-rank matrices or in a factorization form, and then fast algorithms are developed by using algorithms on Riemannian manifolds and matrix factorizations. To prove the theoretical guarantee, we have mainly used numerical linear algebra techniques combined with concentration inequalities of random variables. For objective 3: We applied algorithms to real-world problems such as NMR spectroscopy and spectral compressed sensing. All these real-world applications are presented as experimental results of our proposed algorithms. We have demonstrated that our proposed algorithms can recover the sum of exponential signals in these applications efficiently. In particular, our proposed algorithms can handle multi-dimensional signals which conventional algorithms are not able to solve.

16300616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300616.value: We have developed both convex and non-convex algorithms for the recovery of the sum of expoential signals from its undersamples, and these algorithms are applied to real-world applications such as NMR spectroscopy and spectral compressed sensing. -- In journal publication No. 1, we proposed a fast iterative hard thresholding (FIHT) algorithm and proved its theoretical guarantee. -- In journal publication No. 3, we proposed a multi-dimensional (>=3) signal recovery method by regularizing its tensor factors and applied it successfully to NMR spectroscopy. -- In journal publication No. 5, we proposed a factorization based algorithm for spectral compressed sensing via low-rank Hankel matrix completion and proved its theoretical guarantee. -- In journal publication No. 6, we proposed a factorization based algorithm by regularizing the factor to be Vandermonde and applied it to obtain fast NMR spectroscopy method. -- In conference publication No. 1, we proposed a memory-efficient convex formulation for two-dimensional signal recovery. -- In conference publication No. 2, we theoretically analyze why there is no separation condition in the theoretical guarantee of Hankel nuclear norm minimization. The algorithms developed for the recovery of the sum of exponential signals were also extended to other similar problems, especially low-rank matrix recovery problems. More specifically, we extended the algorithm to subspace clustering in journal publication No. 2, data recovery on general manifolds in journal publication No. 4, phase retrieval in journal publication No. 7, and matrix completion in journal publication No. 8.

16300616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300616.value: 1. The algorithms developed in this project are for off-the-grid compressed sensing, which is quite different from the traditional compressed sensing. The off-the-grid compressed sensing is based on sparse representation on dictionaries with infinitely many atoms, while the traditional one is on finitely many atoms. There are many other off-the-grid compressed sensing problems. Therefore, we can extend our algorithms to those off-the-grid compressed sensing problems. 2. The main tool we have used in this project is low-rank Hankel matrix recovery. Actually, many signal processing and machine learning algorithms use Hankel matrices. For example, patch-based image processing and dictionary learning can be seen as a Hankel matrix factorization, if we sample all possible patches from one single image. Therefore, the techniques developed in this project can be exploited for those problems. To further pursue our research along with these two directions, we will apply more General Research Fund (GRF) projects from RGC in the coming years.

16300616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300616.value: In this research project, we have developed efficient and effective approaches for the recovery of the sum of exponential signals from its limited samples, which has numerous applications in the real world such as nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and spectral compressed sensing. Our algorithms not only come with a solid mathematical theory, but also are applicable to the scenario in which traditional approaches fail.

16301816.label: Project Objectives
16301816.value: To search for a universal form of the dynamic magnetic susceptibility around ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) when the magnetization dynamics is controlled by the magnetic field only. A recipe on how to experimentally determine the universal form is an item on the agenda. 16301816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301816.value: Interplay of charge, spin and microwaves in magnetic films or heavy-metal/ferromagnetic multilayers is a subject that spans the whole spectrum of physics ranging from classical physics to quantum physics. Dc-voltage is measured in the electrical detection of ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) that results from charge-spin interactions including inverse spin Hall effect. The electrical detection of FMR is a main technique for measuring spin Hall angle and other material parameters. The quantum version of FMR is the strong coupling of photons with magnons in the hybrid system of a magnet in a microwave cavity. Magnons are believed to be good quantum information carriers because of their possible long coherence time. One recent development in the field is the electrical detection of the strong coupling. This new detection method may lead to a new way of reading out the quantum state of a magnet with compact electronics. The interpretation of detected dc-voltage in both classical and quantum regions requires the knowledge of dynamics magnetic susceptibility. In literatures and textbooks, the susceptibility is often assumed to be the Polder tensor that is only true for magnet with special rotational symmetry. In this project, we would like to search for a universal form for the dynamic magnetic susceptibility near the FMR. The universal form should depends on a few parameters that can be fully determined from experiments, instead of a formula that depends on the magnetic anisotropy function which is hard to determine if not impossible. The issue will be investigated under the traditional FMR assumption that only magnetic field affects the spin dynamics as well as the case when the spin dynamics can be affected by both magnetic field and spin torque of all sorts. A good understanding of the dynamic magnetic susceptibility shall be important in correctly extracting the spin Hall coefficient (spin Hall angle or the ratio between the electric current and spin current in metal with spin-orbital interaction), as well as providing insights in quantum magnonics. To understand the dc-voltage sources, we will also reexamine the generalized Ohm’s law for a magnet. We will use general physics principles to determine all possible magnetization-current interactions in a polycrystalline film or bulk. The outcomes of this study could have a significant impact in condensed matter physics in general and in the field of spintronics in particular. 电荷、自旋和微波在磁性薄膜或重金属/铁磁多层结构中的相互作用是一个跨越了整个经典物理和 量子物理的课题。由于包括自旋霍尔逆效应在内的电荷-自旋相互作用，在铁磁共振的电学测量中 能够检测到直流电压。铁磁共振的电学测量是测量自旋霍尔角以及其它材料参数的主要技术手法。 铁磁共振的量子图像是声子和磁振子在铁磁体与微波谐振腔组成的混合系统中的强相互作用。磁 振子由于具有较长的相干时间，因此被认为是一个良好的量子信息载体。近期在该领域中的一个 重要进展是强相互作用的电学测量。这种新的检测技术能够为精巧电子设备中磁体量子态的读取 提供一个新方法。无论是在经典物理还是量子物理的范畴，分析铁磁共振电学测量中的直流电压 信号都需要张量磁导率的相关知识。在过去的文献和教科书中，张量磁导率经常被假设为颇尔德 张量。然而，这个假设只在具有特殊旋转对称性的系统中成立。在本项目中，我们力求找到铁磁 共振中张量磁导率的普适形式。其普适形式应当只依赖于实验中容易测得的若干参数，而不是实 验中难以测量的且与各向异性有关的方程。该问题将在如下两个情形下展开研究：自旋运动只由 磁场驱动即传统的铁磁共振假设，以及自旋运动可同时被磁场及任何来源可能产生的自旋转移力 矩驱动。无论是对于正确测量自旋霍尔系数（自旋霍尔角，或是在具有自旋轨道相互作用的金属 中电流与自旋流的比值）还是为量子磁振子学提供独到的视角，对张量磁导率的好的理解都是至 关重要的。为了理解直流电压的来源，我们也会重新测量磁体中的广义欧姆定律。我们会利用普 适的物理定律来定出多晶薄膜或多晶体中所有可能存在的磁矩-电流相互作用。这项研究的成果将 对凝聚态物理尤其是自旋电子学领域产生重大的影响。

16301816.label: Realisation of objectives
16301816.value: We have realized our objectives. In particular, we have found a universal form of the dynamic magnetic susceptibility around ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) when the magnetization dynamics is controlled by the magnetic field only. This is objective 1. A recipe on how to experimentally determine the universal form is an item on the agenda. The results were published in J. Phys.: Condens. Matter. The analysis has also been extended to spin-transfer torque ferromagnetic resonance (st-FMR). A universal form of the dynamic magnetic susceptibility around st-FMR due to both rf magnetic field and rf-electric field were also found. This is our objective 2. A recipe on how to experimentally determine the universal form provided. The analysis have included all sorts of torques as planned in the original proposal. A generalized Ohm’s law and new spin-Hall and inverse spin-Hall effects in magnetic materials are predicted that are subjected to experimental verifications. This is our objective 3.

16301816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301816.value: We have launched investigations in areas related to our objectives. The universal form of the dynamic magnetic susceptibility around ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) due to magnetic field, electrical field, as well as the spin-transfer torque from spin Hall effects were obtained. The generalized Ohm’s law in a magnetic material was obtained. Interestingly, our simple theory allows us to derive the celebrated anisotropic magnetoresistance formula. These results are in publications 1 and 13. It should be pointed out that we started our investigation after this proposed project application was send to RGC. This is why, we obtained important results in 2017 and even before the fund was available. Of course, the fund allow us to work on other interesting problems closely related to proposed project but beyond. They are anomalous magnon Nernst effect; magnonic topological states; theory on skyrmions; 2D quantum phase transition; electron transport in organic systems. These achievements are in publications 2-12 and 14-20.

16301816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301816.value: Promote experimentalists to use our findings in their future analysis of FMR and st-FMR instead of using less accurate but simple method.

16301816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301816.value: Electrical detections of ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) and spin-transfer magnetic resonances (st-FMR) is an important technique for extracting material parameters. To measure spin Hall angle and other material parameters, one needs to know the dynamics magnetic susceptibility near the resonance point. In literatures and textbooks, the susceptibility is often assumed to be the Polder tensor that is only true for magnet with special rotational symmetry that does not apply to real materials in general. In this project, we found a universal form for the dynamic magnetic susceptibility near the FMR and st-FMR for arbitrary materials. This theory is important in correctly extracting the spin Hall coefficient (spin Hall angle or the ratio between the electric current and spin current in metal with spin-orbital interaction). On the way to find the correct dynamics magnetic susceptibility, we have also obtained the generalized Ohm’s law for a magnet. In summary, we have fully achieved our original objectives.

16302316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16302316.value: 實驗研究膠體晶體的固-固相變

16302316.label: Project Objectives
16302316.value: To study the kinetics of nuclei coalescence. To elucidate the nucleation kinetics of solid-solid transitions in colloidal thin films under a stress field and understand its mechanism.
rows: To study the kinetics of nuclei coalescence.
To elucidate the nucleation kinetics of solid-solid transitions in colloidal thin films under a stress field and understand its mechanism.

16302316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302316.value: A solid can transform into another type of solid with a different crystalline structure by changing temperature or pressure. Such solid-solid phase transitions constitute one of the most fundamental and widespread types of structural transitions in nature and industry, including a large majority of the transitions found in elemental crystals, alloys, minerals and soft matter systems [1,2]. However, their microscopic mechanisms are poorly understood [1,2]. In particular, the phase transition kinetics including the initial nucleation process is crucial but remains poorly understood. The nucleation at the atomic level, especially inside three-dimensional bulk crystals, is difficult to measure, owing to the small spatial and time resolutions required. Colloidal particles are particularly well-suited for investigating phase transitions [3] because the thermal motions of micrometer-sized colloidal particles can be directly visualized and measured by video microscopy. In the past decade, significant experimental efforts have been made to study colloidal crystal melting [4-7], freezing [8] and glass transitions [9], but very limited to solid-solid transitions [10-13]. Recently we discovered that thermal-sensitive repulsive colloidal thin-film crystals transform from square lattice to triangular lattice via forming liquid nuclei [11]. Such surprising intermediate liquid state casts new light on solid-solid transitions. Here we propose to expand this research by applying a directional pressure to mimic solid-solid transitions under stress typically encountered in metallurgy and earth mantel. In contrast to conventional atomic systems where only heterogeneous nucleation can be studied, our system allows both heterogeneous nucleation and homogenous nucleation to be studied by local heating and cooling. Many important questions beyond the classical nucleation theory can be systematically studied. For example, how do external stresses affect the nucleation kinetics? How do nuclei coalesce? In a different type of thermal-sensitive attractive colloidal crystals, we observed an abrupt lattice dilation, i.e. an isostructural solid-solid transition. This is the first direct observation of isostructural solid-solid transition at the single-particle level, which usually occurs in metallic and multiferroic systems [14]. We will study such solid-solid transitions both inside bulks and near surfaces. S-s transition and nucleation are important subjects in physical science with many open questions. The proposed experiments will elucidate their microscopic details, which will dramatically expand our understanding of solid-solid transition. The results will provide valuable guidance for future refinement of the nucleation theory in solids and shed light on atomic systems which are of practical importance for metallurgy, mineralogy and thin-film physics and fundamental interest for condensed matter physics. 固體可以通過改變溫度或壓力轉換為另一種晶格結構不同的的固體。這種固-固相變是最廣泛的一類結構相變，存在于各种晶體如合金，礦石和軟物質系統。然而对它 們的微觀機理，尤其是对相變初始成核過程知之甚少。因为成核发生在原子尺度上，需要极高的空間和時間分辨率，尤其是在三維體晶內部的成核難以观測。膠體粒 子特別適合於研究相變，因為微米尺寸的膠體粒子可以像大原子一样形成各种晶体，胶体粒子的熱運動可以直接在光学顯微鏡下观測。在過去的十年中，很多實驗已 經研究了膠體晶體熔化，结晶和玻璃化轉變，但很少研究固-固相變。 最 近我們發現，熱敏膠體粒子组成的薄膜晶體從正方晶格通過形成液體核轉化為三角晶格。這種令人驚訝的中間態液體为固-固轉變提供了新的理解。在這裡，我們研 究施加外部壓力如何影响固-固相變，这种情况在冶金和地幔中经常遇到。原子系統中只研究了傳統的非均匀成核，而我們的胶体系統允許通過局部加熱和冷卻來研 究非均匀成核和均勻成核。各种超越經典成核理論的許多重要問題都可以系統地研究。例如，两个子相晶核如何合并生长？ 本實驗將为固-固相變提供其他系统难以得到的微觀細節，這將極大地擴展我們对固-固相變的認識。研究結果將為完善固體中相变成核理論提供微观实验证据，对冶金，礦物學，薄膜物理和凝聚態物理中的固-固相變的理解具有基础義線。

16302316.label: Realisation of objectives
16302316.value: The two objectives have been well achieved. For objective (1) about the coalescence of two nuclei, most results are shown in the unpublished manuscript. We discovered surprisingly rich phenomena which takes longer time than we expected for a comprehensive study. The nuclei coalescence in solid-solid transition has not been reported before, thus it takes a relative long time to understand the rich behaviors. Moreover, the student graduated and left the group, thus it takes some time to find a new student and continue the project. We have polished the paper for a long time because we are targeting on a top journal. We will submit the manuscript soon. We observed various novel and different kinetic pathways for nuclei coalescence, and successfully clarify how they are induced under different conditions, e.g. nuclei sizes, facets and distances, crystal’s density, shear strength, and nearby defects. For objective 2, we elucidated the nucleation kinetics in colloidal thin-film crystals under a stress field and understood its mechanism. We discovered that two distinct nucleation pathways under no stress and under a weak stress. We explained the former case from the surface energies and the latter case from the build-up strains. The above results under weak stresses have been published in Nature Communications in 2017, while the results under strong shear will be published in another paper targeting on a top journal. The experiment about strong shear is based on the setup of oscillatory shear which is for another research projects about grain boundary dynamics. Here we apply the setup in solid-solid transition study and achieved new results which can be regarded as an extension of objective 2.

16302316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302316.value: We studied the rich kinetics of transitions from multilayer square lattices to triangular lattices. Applying a small pressure gradient in defect-free regions or near dislocations markedly transform the diffusive nucleation with an intermediate-stage liquid into a novel hybrid kinetic pathway: the generation and collective oscillation of several dislocation pairs at the early stage and a diffusive nucleus growth at the later stage. This kinetic pathway is neither purely diffusive nor purely martensitic as conventionally assumed but a combination thereof, and thus presents new challenges to both theory and the empirical criterion of martensitic transformations. We systematically studied the nucleation of solid-solid transition in defect-free regions, on grain boundaries and triple junctions. We resolve the nucleus growth kinetics at the single-particle level and find that the nuclei form facets with low-energy interfaces. These results about objective 2 was published in Nature Communications, in 2017. We further achieved the first experimental observation of the coalescence of two nuclei in solid-solid transition with single-particle resolution, and discovered rich kinetics, e.g. the small nucleus firstly transforming to liquid and then being absorbed by the large nucleus; the disintegration of low-angle grain boundary, and the migrate and coalescence of high-angle grain boundaries. We have almost finished manuscript and will soon submit these results about objective 2 to a top journal, e.g. Nature Communications. Besides the above solid-solid transition under no shear or tiny shear, we developed a new setup which can strongly oscillate the colloidal crystal when it is undergoes a solid-solid transition. We discovered different pathways including the growing crystalline nuclei wrapped by a layer of wetting liquid phase. In addition, we observed the formation and motion of shear bands and interesting stripe patterns in crystalline lattice. We are writing them into a paper for a top journal. We also studied crystal melting behavior (J. Chem. Phys. 2019) and structural changes from an amorphous solid to a polycrystal (Nature Communications 2020), which are related to the solid-solid transitions.

16302316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302316.value: The current research can be extended along two directions. (1) Instead of using repulsive colloidal particles in this study, we can employ our novel attractive colloids to similarly study the solid-solid transition. Conventional attractive colloidal particles are not well tunable, making it is hard to drive the solid-solid transition. Our recent paper, Nature 531, 485 (2016), reports a novel colloid with tunable attractions and their crystal melting behaviors. We can similar study its solid-solid transition in thin-film samples. Note that only attractive particles can form crystals with free surfaces (i.e. vapor-crystal interfaces), which can better mimic real atomic crystals. Hence studying the solid-solid transition with attractive particles are more novel and important than the current work. We can focus on how free surfaces affect the microscopic kinetics of solid-solid transition which has rarely been explored. (2) We are exploring the solid-solid transition under a strong shear, which exhibit rich new phenomena, such as grain boundary premelting, shear band formation and motions, crystalline structures with stripes etc. How atoms move during a severe deformation of a crystal is crucial in metallurgy, but can hardly be measured. Our colloidal system provide a unique opportunity to study it.

16302316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302316.value: Solid-solid transition between different crystalline states (e.g. graphite-diamond transition) widely exists in metallurgy and earth mantle, but how atoms move to during such phase transition is poorly understood because the motions of individual atoms are not measurable inside a crystal. We employ novel colloidal crystals as model systems to directly observe micron-sized colloidal particles’ thermal motions during a solid-solid transition under an optical microscope. We observed the nucleation process for the first time and discovered a surprising crystalliquidnew crystal pathway (Nature Materials 14, 101 (2015)). Based on this preliminary result, we further discovered a novel nucleation kinetics with collective motions of particles in the early stage and diffusive growth in the later stage by applying a small pressure gradient (Nature Communications 8, 14978 (2017)). We have achieved the first microscopic observation of the coalescence of two nuclei in the solid-solid transition and discovered various novel kinetics, which greatly deepened the understanding of the new crystal formation. In addition, we applied a large oscillatory shear and discovered novel structures and kinetics. These pioneer experiments on microscopic kinetics of solid-solid transition reveal rich novel results not measurable in conventional atomic systems, which is of fundamental importance for materials science and metallurgy.

16302416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302416.value: Variable annuities are long-term unit-linked insurance products that offer various types of financial guarantees. In most common design of variable annuities contracts, policyholders accumulate assets during the accumulation phase and receive incomes during the income phase. The demand for certainty in retirement incomes from the ageing population combined with product innovations (various forms of guarantees and provisions) drove annual retail variable annuities sales to over US$140bn by 2014. The attractive features of variable annuities that are not generally found in other types of investment products include tax-deferred earnings, death-benefit protection options, living-benefit protection options, and lifetime-income options. Due to acute competition in the variable annuities markets, guaranteed “withdrawal benefit for life” that combines the longevity protection of an income benefit with the liquidity of the regular withdrawal benefit was introduced in 2005. By the third quarter of 2014, the guaranteed lifelong withdrawal benefits (GLWB) rider was chosen in close to half of the new variable annuities sales in the US markets. Since the embedded guarantees may be too costly to the issuers and they are difficult to hedge, many insurers of variable annuities faced record levels of failure of their risk hedging strategies, in particular after the financial tsunami in 2008. In a typical contractual design of GLWB, the policyholder pays an upfront premium and the amount is then invested in his / her own choice of portfolio of funds. In some contracts, additional purchases are allowed to be placed by the policyholder during the accumulation phase. The income phase start date is the date on which withdrawals of the lifetime annuities start. The GLWB guarantees the policyholder the right to withdraw a specified percentage of the benefit base as long as the annuitant survives. The initiation of the income phase is chosen by the policyholder based on various considerations, like his / her retirement age and the age-dependent scheduled withdrawal rates. In this project, I will focus on the risk management and hedging of variable annuities with GLWB. In particular, I will start with the comprehensive studies on understanding and quantifying embedded risks, like costs of guarantees, lapse risk and mortality risk. I then consider how to construct both semi-static and dynamic hedging strategies that replicate as close as possible the promised payoffs subject to a certain level of risk tolerance. Also, I plan to examine the optimal contractual design that minimizes potential risks faced by the issuer. 变额年金含多种型式的提取保证，保险公司在发行此类变额年金产品时要考虑如何设计合约，定价及对冲。在典型的含终身提取保证的变额年金中，含有前期储蓄期及后期的终身提取期， 投保人的个人户口如在去世时还有余额，则受益人可提取余额。在2014年，含终身提取保证的变额年金的沽售总额超过所有变额年金的一半。 在此研究项目中，我将分析此含终身提取保证的变额年金产品所包含的风险， 并加以量化。在风险管理方面，我会提出相关的对冲策略及如何优化产品设计，以令买卖双方都能双赢。

16302416.label: Realisation of objectives
16302416.value: There are 4 stated objectives in the project. I would like to summarize at what extent these objectives have been achieved in my progress of the research. The research findings have been organized into the publication of two research publications in SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics and Quantitative Finance. Objective One: Analyze the optimal policies adopted by the policyholders using bang-bang analysis, like optimal initiation of the income phase, optimal amount to be withdrawn from or added into the policy account, and complete surrender. The first phase of our research is the construction of the most comprehensive pricing models of variable annuities products with withdrawal guarantees, like the Guaranteed Lifelong Withdrawal Benefit (GLWB). Mathematically, the pricing models include the optimal stopping rule of initiation and dynamic withdrawal as the stochastic control process. Our pricing models include complex path dependent features arising from the ratchet and bonus provisions, dynamic control of withdrawals and additional purchases, together with optimality in the time of initiation of the income phase. The policyholder has the optionality to choose the initiation of the income phase optimally based on a combination of factors, like the age-dependent scheduled withdrawal rates, penalty charge rate, bonus and ratchet provisions. Through a rigorous bang-bang analysis, we showed that the strategy space of the optimal policies is limited to four choices: maximum allowable purchase, zero withdrawal, withdrawal at the contractual amount or complete surrender. We extended the versatility of the bang-bang analysis via analysis of the convexity and monotonicity properties of the price function. The analytic tools are applicable to many common processes for the policy fund value, like the Heston model. Objective Two: Construct effective pricing algorithms using the fast Fourier transform algorithms. Perform sensitivity analysis of the GLWB price and optimal policies under varying model parameter values. The bang-bang analysis simplifies the construction of the Fourier transform algorithm since the strategy space of the optimal policies is limited to four choices. We constructed the Fourier transform algorithm for effective pricing of the variable annuities products with policy fund value under the general two-dimensional Markov process of the fund value and its variance. In the design of the Fourier transform algorithm, the dimension of the pricing model is reduced by one since the benefit base remains constant between two consecutive event dates. The Fourier transform algorithms have been shown in our comprehensive numerical tests to be efficient, accurate and reliable even under the level of complexities of path dependence in our comprehensive pricing models. As an alternative numerical approach, we also constructed presents the willow tree algorithms for pricing variable annuities products with Guaranteed Minimum Withdrawal Benefits, where the underlying fund dynamics evolves under the Merton jump-diffusion process or constant-elasticity-of-variance (CEV) process. The willow tree algorithms adopt more effective placement of the lattice nodes based on better fitting of the underlying fund price distribution. The dynamic nature of the withdrawal policy allows the policyholder to decide how much to withdraw on each withdrawal date, or even surrender the contract. The design of our pricing algorithms also includes an efficient search method for the optimal dynamic withdrawal policies. Extensive numerical tests were conducted to examine numerical performance of the willow tree algorithm when compared with other numerical algorithms, like the binomial tree method, finite difference method, numerical quadrature and Fourier transform algorithm. These tests reveal high accuracy, efficiency and reliability of the willow tree algorithm, together with significant savings on computational time. Objective Three: Consider the most effective hedging strategies of using available traded derivative instruments and examine the effectiveness of semi-static and dynamic hedging strategies through better understanding the risk characteristics of the GLWB products. We examined the impact of the jump intensity and magnitude on the terminal profit and loss distribution of the variable annuities product with and without delta hedging. The potential losses under strong jumps in the underlying fund value process can be significant under no delta hedging of the variable annuities product. The dynamic hedging strategies produce lower risks compared to the semi-static strategies. We suggested that other derivatives, like options on the asset fund, may be added into the portfolio to improve the hedging performance. We performed comprehensive sensitivity analysis of various model parameters on the fair participating fees and values of the variable annuities products, like maturity of the contract, volatility of the fund dynamics, participating fee, penalty charge, etc. Objective Four: Examine the optimal design of the contractual features of the variable annuities products that minimizes non-hedgeable risk exposure. To stay competitive in the annuities markets, the issuer cannot charge too high rider fees. We considered the impact of the fair rider fees under various parameter values of the underlying fund value processes. The rider fees depend quite sensibly on volatility of the underlying process and correlation coefficient between the underlying and its stochastic volatility process. We also examined the impact of the contractual withdrawal rate and upper bound of additional purchases on the optimal policies for initiation into the income phase. The optimal initiation policies adopted by the policyholders are seen to depend sensibly on the age-dependent contractual withdrawal rate. Policyholders would wait for a more favorable contractual withdrawal rate for optimal entry into the income phase. Also, our studies show that the incentive for initiation into the income phase decreases as the variance of the underlying fund price process and / or the bonus rate increases. Final remark Overall speaking, most of the aspects of the 4 stated objectives have been addressed. More emphasis has been placed on the theoretical development of effective pricing algorithms and some studies have been shed on hedging and optimal contractual designs. In the progress of research, we had taken the research path that expended stronger efforts and interests on the theoretical bang-gang analysis in facilitating the development of pricing algorithms of variable annuities products with withdrawal benefits. The quality of our research findings are evidenced by the publication of two comprehensive research papers in two leading research journals in the field of quantitative finance. The research results have been reported in two research conferences in Japan (Feb. 2017) and Singapore (Jun., 2017).

16302416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302416.value: The research findings and research outcome are summarized in two research papers, the details of journal publications are listed below. Y.T. Huang, P. Zeng and Y.K. Kwok "Optimal initiation of Guaranteed Lifelong Minimum Withdrawal with dynamic withdrawals," SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics, vol. 8 (2017), p.804-840. B. Dong, W. Xu and Y.K. Kwok "Willow tree algorithms for pricing guaranteed minimum withdrawal benefits under jump-diffusion and CEV models," to appear in Quantitative Finance (online publication is available). Both journals are leading research journals in quantitative finance. In the first paper, we present the comprehensive pricing model for the GLWB product with the accumulation phase and income phase,additional purchases, age-dependent scheduled withdrawal rate, bonus and ratchet provisions under the Heston stochastic volatility process for the policy fund value. The pricing model includes the optimal stopping rule of initiation and dynamic withdrawal as the stochastic control process. Through a rigorous bang-bang analysis, we showed that the strategy space of the optimal policies is limited to four choices, thus simplifying the construction of the Fourier transform algorithm for pricing GLWB products with complex path dependent features. We then applied the Fourier transform in the log normalized policy fund value dimension and a quadrature rule in the log-variance dimension. We also performed sensitivity analysis of the GLWB price function with respect to various contractual features and model parameters. We considered the impact of the fair rider fees under various parameter values of the Heston stochastic volatility model. We also examined the impact of the contractual withdrawal rate and upper bound of additional purchases on the optimal initiation policies. In the second paper, we consider pricing and hedging of the GMWB rider in variable annuities associated with sophisticated structural features, like dynamic withdrawals, reset provisions upon excessive withdrawal, surrender provision and mortality. We proposed the willow tree algorithms for pricing the annuities products when the underlying fund process follows Merton’s jump-diffusion model or CEV model. We also proposed an effective optimization algorithm for the determination of optimal withdrawals. We performed comprehensive sensitivity analysis of various model parameters on the fair participating fees and values of the annuities products, like maturity of the contract, volatility of the fund dynamics, participating fee, penalty charge, etc. We also examined the impact of the jump intensity and magnitude on the terminal profit and loss distribution of the annuities product with and without delta hedging.

16302416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302416.value: With the demand for certainty in retirement incomes, Hong Kong announced plans to launch a public annuity scheme through the government-owned Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) in 2017. The variable annuities markets in the local private sectors are quite underdeveloped, just with several simple products and volumes of sales are sparse. On the other hand, the variable annuities markets have well developed over the last two decades in North America and Europe. For example, the annual retail variable annuities sales were over US$100bn in 2018 in the US. The structured features of the variable annuities products analyzed in this project include the newest innovations, like the early phase of accumulation of benefit base and later income phase of annuities, together with dynamic withdrawals in the income phase, and complete surrender right. With the knowledge gained from this project, I acquire better understanding of the complex features of the newest innovative variable annuities products. I may plan to communicate with the local insurance industries and HKMC for future development of variable annuities that gears to the need of the ageing population in Hong Kong.

16302416.value: Variable annuities are long-term unit-linked insurance products that offer various types of financial guarantees. In a typical contractual design of variable annuities product, the policyholder pays an upfront premium and the amount is then invested in his own choice of portfolio of funds. The GLWB guarantees the policyholder the right to withdraw a specified percentage of the benefit base as long as the annuitant survives. In this project, I have developed effective numerical algorithms for pricing variable annuities with guarantees using the fast Fourier transform method and willow tree method. Once the pricing algorithms are available, I analyze the optimal policies adopted by the policyholders using bang-bang analysis, like optimal initiation of the income phase, optimal amount to be withdrawn from or added into the policy account. 16302816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16302816.value: 細胞通過細胞膜與外界交流資訊。在細胞膜上，跨膜蛋白受體獲得胞外刺激信號後，一系列精密調控的蛋白反應隨之啟動，最終導致胞內二級信使的釋放。 乙醯膽鹼受體（AChRs）就是這種分佈在突觸後肌肉細胞膜上的蛋白受體。 作為一種已被清楚描述的神經遞質受體，乙醯膽鹼受體在決定肌肉細胞對神經遞質刺激的反應上發揮關鍵作用。 在先前的一項研究專案（2011-2014）中，我們研究了非洲爪蟾（Xenopus）活肌肉細胞膜上乙醯膽鹼受體的橫向運動。 其中最主要的發現就是乙醯膽鹼受體的運動軌跡的統計不遵循布朗運動的高斯統計。 相反，實驗測得的乙醯膽鹼受體位移的概率分佈呈現一種長尾的指數分佈。這是一個不受位移時間段長短，擴散係數大小，細胞自身的母體來源和培養天數的影響，穩定並且具有普遍意義的分佈。 基於這項實驗發現，我們提出了一個細胞膜結構的動態柵欄模型，通過緊貼細胞膜下的皮層肌動蛋白網絡的主動重構來解釋觀察到的非高斯統計的動態異質性。 這個模型具有重要的生物學意義，並且需要進一步證明。 我們計畫對皮層肌動蛋白網絡（分子馬達驅動的）主動信號漲落的統計特性進行一項系統研究，來揭開它對膜上擴散運動的影響。 在第一組實驗中，我們會用一個新搭建的雙視野片光顯微鏡對吸附到肌動蛋白網絡上的「主動運動」量子點進行三維運動追蹤。 量子點體積小，對環境反應穩定，使它們可以在多孔結構的肌動蛋白網絡中擴散。在第二組實驗中，我們會用雙色螢光顯微鏡來研究主動重構的肌動蛋白網絡和跨膜蛋白受體（如乙醯膽鹼受體）以及其他分佈于皮層的蛋白之間運動的相互影響。 我們研究的主要目標是找到皮層肌動蛋白網絡的大範圍主動重構與膜上或皮層中的蛋白質的小範圍擴散運動的關係。 通過這些實驗，我們可以揭示活細胞主動控制細胞膜的流動性和調控膜上的分子運輸的全新機制。 它還提供了一個量化方法用於獲得活細胞動態性狀的關鍵讀數，以期廣泛應用於描述蛋白活動對某些細胞的生理健康和疾病特徵方面的效能。 這項研究計畫既包括了對非平衡態生命系統的新物理特性的探索，也含有對生物學許多方面具有重要意義的主動環境下的蛋白質擴散運動的研究。 這個專案在科學上的挑戰性要求研究團隊具有軟物質物理，光學和生物學的跨學科團隊合作。我們已經建立了這樣一個團隊。

16302816.label: Realisation of objectives
16302816.value: To fulfill the two research objectives, we carried out two sets of experiments to study the interactions between the transmembrane proteins and cortical actin network and their influence on membrane diffusion. In one set of experiments, we conducted a comparative study of the lateral motion of ganglioside GM1, which is a glycosphingolipid residing on the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane, and acetylcholine receptor (AChR), which is a well-characterized ion channel. Both the lipid molecules and the transmembrane proteins reside on the plasma membranes of live Xenopus muscle cells. Because it resides on the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane, the ganglioside GM1 does not have direct interactions with the underlying cortical actin network. The AChR, on the other hand, is a transmembrane protein and has direct interactions with the cortical actin network. By accurately tracking a large volume of individual molecular trajectories from more than 300 live cells over a wide range of sampling rates (up to 80 fps) and long delay times (up to 200 s), we were able to obtain a number of high-order statistical measures of the molecular displacement x(t) over a long delay time t, such as the mean squared displacement (MSD) 〈x^2(t)〉, probability density function (PDF or normalized histogram) P(x), PDF h(Rg) of the radius of gyration Rg, and PDF f (delta) of the local diffusion coefficient delta. From these statistical analyses, we demonstrate that the GM1s and AChRs share the same dynamic heterogeneity and non-Gaussian statistics. They are also found to have similar distributions of the mobile ratio gamma (∼65%) and long-time diffusion coefficient D_L for cells cultured under the same conditions. To alter the dynamics of the cortical actin network, several drug treatments were introduced in the experiments, including depletion of the adenosine triphosphate (ATP) level in the living Xenopus muscle cells (by 2-deoxy-D-glucose and sodium azide), increase or decrease of actin polymerization (by Latrunculin A and Jasplakinolide), inhibition of mysion II motors (by Blebbistatin and Y27632), and increase of phosphorylation in the rapsyn-MuSK pathway (by pervandate). These drug treatments produced a large body of interesting data, showing various degrees of changes in the diffusion dynamics of GM1s and AChRs. Among all the drug treatments, depletion of intracellular ATP reveals the largest effect on membrane diffusion. In the above experiments, we found that protein/lipid diffusion over a live cell membrane is highly non-Brownian with non-Gaussian statistics and dynamic heterogeneity, which are inherently linked to the interaction potential landscape generated by the underlying cortical actin network in the cell. To pinpoint the molecular mechanism of the observed non-Gaussian statistics and dynamic heterogeneity in living cells, we conducted the second set of experiments to study the diffusion dynamics of colloidal particles over complex potential landscapes: from periodic and quasicrystalline potentials and random potentials. In one experiment, we studied the transport and diffusion of model colloidal particles over a titled periodic potential landscape. The periodic potential was provided by the colloidal spheres in the bottom layer forming a fixed crystalline pattern on a glass substrate. The corrugated surface of the bottom colloidal crystal provided a gravitational potential field U_0(x,y) for the diffusing particles in the top layer. By tilting the sample at an angle with respect to the vertical (gravity) direction, a tangential component of the gravitational force F was applied to the diffusing particles. When a constant force F is applied to the particle, the overall potential becomes U(x) = U_0(x) − Fx. This tilted two-layer colloidal system serves as model system for the study of force-assisted barrier-crossing dynamics over a periodic potential. In the experiment, we measured the forward transition probability density function (FTPDF) P_+(0,x,t) at various values of F and the corresponding reverse transition probability density function (RTPDF) P_-(x,0,t). The measured FTPDF P_+(0,x,t) were found to have a complex functional form with repeated peaks along the x axis. The values of these peaks are well described by a Gaussian-like envelop function. We also studied the effects of the external force F on the non-equilibrium steady state (NESS) dynamics of the diffusing particles over the tilted periodic potential, in which detailed balance was broken due to the presence of a steady particle flux. The measured total entropy production S(0,x) in the NESS is found to increase linearly with the traveling distance x and is superimposed with a periodic modulation by the potential U_0(x). In another experiment, we systematically studied colloidal diffusion over a quenched two-dimensional (2D) disordered potential. In the experiment, a mixture of bidisperse silica spheres was used to form a randomly packed colloidal monolayer on the bottom substrate, which provided a disordered gravitational potential field U(x,y) to the diffusing particles in the top layer. With the techniques of optical microscopy and multi-particle tracking, we measured the population statistics of the diffusing particles in the top layer and constructed the potential U(x,y) via the Boltzmann distribution. The dynamical properties of the top diffusing particles, such as their mean square displacement (MSD) 〈x^2(t)〉, histogram P(t_E) of the escape time t_E, and long-time self-diffusion coefficient D_L, were simultaneously measured from the particle trajectories. The measured MSD exhibits a dual-crossover behavior with an initial short-time diffusion followed by a crossover to the subdiffuion regime caused by the structural disorders in the bottom colloidal layer. When the delay time t becomes more than five times longer than the largest mean escape time (t_E)_max, the particles on average have experienced (or hopped over) many potential barriers, and their motion recovered back to normal diffusion with a reduced long-time diffusion coefficient D_L. Using the simultaneously obtained energetics and dynamics information, we tested the theory and demonstrate the applications of the newly constructed 2D random potential. Via the above two sets of experiments, the two project objectives were fully achieved.

16302816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16302816.value: Dynamic heterogeneity and non-Gaussian statistics for ganglioside GM1s and acetylcholine receptors (AcHRs) on live cell membrane. A central finding of this investigation is that the moving trajectories of the individual GM1 and AChRs do not follow the Gaussian statistics for normal diffusion. Instead, we showed for the first time that the measured probability density function of the GM1’s displacements has a long exponential tail, which is robust and universal for cells under different conditions. This finding supports an important prediction of the recently proposed dynamic picket-fence model that all the mobile molecules on the membrane, including lipids and transmembrane proteins, should have the same dynamic behavior. The experiment thus represents a breakthrough in understanding the microscopic origin of the observed non-Gaussian statistics and dynamic heterogeneity. This work was published in Mol. Biol. Cell. Colloidal dynamics over a tilted periodic potential: Forward and reverse transition probabilities and entropy production in a non-equilibrium steady state. The energy landscape for an equilibrium system is an important concept in science, which has been widely used in many areas of physics, chemistry and biology. This situation is changed completely when an external force F is applied to the diffusing particles, which breaks the detailed balance (DB) condition, so that the system becomes non-equilibrium. While both the measured FTPDF P_+(0,x,t) and RTPDF P_-(x,0,t) have a complex space-time dependence, their ratio was found to be independent of time and obeys a DB-like relation. The experimental results are in good agreement with the theoretical predictions. This study thus provided a better understanding on how entropy is generated and heat is dissipated to the reservoir during a NESS transition process. This work was published in Physical Review E. Colloidal diffusion over a quenched two-dimensional random potential. Our work demonstrated that the two-layer colloidal system is a versatile platform for the study of colloidal diffusion over complex potential landscapes. The disordered configurations generated vary from crystal-like structures with different amounts of defects and grain boundaries introduced by the ‘‘dopant’’ particles to various glass-like structures with either well-mixed states or micro-structured domains. This method provided a well-controlled and convenient way to vary the potential landscapes with different disorders. With the simultaneous tracking of the diffusing particles and determining the underlying potential landscape at the single-particle resolution, one is able to study quantitatively a range of interesting issues involved in colloidal diffusion over random fields. This work was published in Soft Matter.

16302816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16302816.value: Our measurements suggested that the local diffusion of a membrane molecule is determined primarily by the crowding effect imposed by the immobile protein network, which is anchored to the underlying cortical actin network. As the immobile protein network is embedded in the membrane, all the mobile membrane molecules will diffuse through this largely two-dimensional porous network. In this way, the immobile protein network produces a unique crowding effect on all membrane molecules, including both transmembrane proteins and lipids. So far, we have only explored a small number of effects of the immobile protein network on (mobile) protein diffusion experimentally. It would certainly be very interesting to extend our study to other cell types and to the diffusion dynamics inside the cell body, in addition to cell membrane. We plan to seek additional funding to support the research along this direction.

16302816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16302816.value: How a protein molecule moves to a specific location at an appropriate time, finds its target, and performs its biological function in such a crowded environment is an outstanding issue in molecular biology. In this research, we conducted a comparative study of the lateral motion of well-characterized lipid molecules (GM1s) and transmembrane proteins (AChRs) on live cell membrane. From a thorough analysis of a large volume of individual molecular trajectories obtained from more than 300 live cells over a wide range of sampling rates and long durations, we find that the GM1s and AChRs share the same dynamic heterogeneity and non-Gaussian statistics. Our measurements with the drug treated cells further reveal that the diffusion dynamics of the GM1s and AChRs is uniformly affected by the intracellular ATP level of the living muscle cells. These results support the dynamic picket-fence model that we recently proposed in that the immobile and transiently confined transmembrane proteins form a continuous random network, permeating the membrane. This heterogeneous protein network, which is anchored to the underlying cortical actin network, partitions the cell membrane, slows down the diffusion of all mobile membrane molecules, and is strongly coupled to the slow remodeling of the cortical actin network.

16303416.label: Realisation of objectives
16303416.value: The Weather Research and Forecast model coupled with Chemistry (WRF-Chem) was applied for the projection of dust and its impact on regional climate over East Asia from 2011 to 2060. Shao’s dust emission scheme and the Global Ozone Chemistry Aerosol Radiation and Transport (COCART) scheme implemented in WRF-Chem and were used for simulating dust emission, transport and deposition. The Rapid Radiative Transfer Model for Global Climate Models (RRTMG) long-wave and short-wave radiation schemes were used for calculating the direct effect of dust on radiation budget. The newly-developed GOCART-Thompson microphysics scheme was used for calculating the indirect effect of dust on ice nucleation by serving as ice nuclei in the atmosphere. The 6-hourly outputs from the Community Climate System Version 4 (CCSM4) under scenario of moderate emission of greenhouse gases from 2011 to 2060 were used to provide the initial and boundary conditions for the WRF-Chem simulation. Two simulations were conducted using the same configurations, except that one (control run) was run with dust emission, and the other (test run) without. The simulation results were validated by comparing the outputs of 2012 with comprehensive observational data, including meteorological data from the China Meteorological Forcing dataset, the observational PM10 data from surface air quality monitoring network, as well as the aerosol optical depth derived from Aerosol Robotic Network program and satellite observations. The simulation results from 2011 to 2060 were then analyzed to investigate the variations in East Asian dust cycle, including the distribution and trend of dust emission, as well as the distribution, transport and deposition of dust aerosol. More importantly, the impacts of dust on the regional climate system were then evaluated by estimating the dust-induced modification of long-wave and short-wave radiation budgets, surface temperature, and precipitations over East Asia from 2011 to 2060.

16303416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303416.value: 1. The GOCART-Thompson microphysics scheme, which fully couples the aerosols aware Thompson-Eidhammer microphysics schemewith the GOCART aerosol model, was implemented in WRF-Chem, enabling the model to simultaneously calculate the effect of dust in ice nucleation processes along with dust simulation (Su and Fung, 2018a, b). 2. A dataset of future projection for dust over East Asia from 2011 to 2060 under scenario of moderate emission of greenhouse gases was archived. 3. The major conclusions of this study: (1) There is no significant trend for dust emission over East Asia from 2011 to 2060, except for annual fluctuations. (2) The direct radiative effect of dust and the dust-enhanced cloud radiative effect cause a general decrease of net radiation deficit at near-surface layer, and a net radiation gain within the atmosphere. (3) The radiative forcing induced combined with the redistribution of atmospheric water vapor results in an overall decrease in near-surface temperature and an increase in temperature at the middle to upper troposphere over East Asia, leading to a general inhibition of atmospheric stability. (4) Compared with that from the control run (without dust), the spatial mean of surface temperature from the test run (with dust) is slightly (around 0.1°C) lower due to the direct and indirect radiative effects of dust. (5) There is a slightly increasing trend of the mean total precipitation over East Asia from 2011 to 2060, and the spatial mean total precipitation over East Asia from the test run is comparable to that from the control run. However, the spatial mean convective precipitation over East Asia shows a descending trend from 2011 to 2060, and the spatial mean convective precipitation from the test run is around 7% less than that from the control run, which is due to the inhibition of atmospheric instability induced by dust. The spatial mean non-convective precipitation over East Asia exhibit an increasing trend from 2011 to 2060, and the spatial mean non-convective precipitation from the test run is around 8% more than that from the control run, which is likely contributed by more clouds resulted from the ice nucleation processes enhanced by dust. (6) Although the spatial mean number of light precipitation (≤ 10 mm/day) day shows a significant descending trend from 2011 to 2060, The light precipitation days from test run are around 3% more than those from control run due to the enhanced non-convective precipitation induced by dust; the spatial mean number of moderate precipitation (10 mm/day ≤ 50 mm/day) day shows a significant increasing trend from 2011 to 2060, and the moderate precipitation days from test run are slightly less than those from control run, due to the inhibition of convective precipitation induced by dust.

16303416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303416.value: In this study we evaluated the long-term variation of dust and its impact on the regional climate system over East Asia from 2011 to 2060 just under the scenario of moderate emission of greenhouse gases. For further study, projections under other emission scenarios such as low and high emission of greenhouse gases should be conducted such as to estimate the uncertainties in the variation of dust as well as the modification in regional climate system induced by dust.

16303416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303416.value: By applying a regional climate model (WRF-Chem), the variation of dust over East Asia and its impact on the regional climate system from 2011 to 2060 was investigated for the first time under the assumption of current emission of greenhouse gases in the future. The performance of WRF-Chem in projecting dust emission as well as its impact on the regional climate system over East Asia using global climate model outputs was evaluated by comparing with comprehensive observational data, for which a dynamical downscaling method for long-term dust simulation based on WRF-Chem was built, and the GOCART-Thompson microphysics scheme was implemented in WRF-Chem for estimating the impact of dust in ice nucleation processes by serving as ice nuclei. This study has given us a straightforward understanding of the long-term variation in dust activity, distribution, transport, deposition, as well as the dust-induced modification of the regional climate system under the background of climate change in the coming decades.

16304016.value: 具備特殊拓撲相態的兩維材料是現今凝聚態物理學的一個研究熱點，包括量子霍爾效應，量子自旋霍爾效應，量子反常霍爾效應，以及拓撲超導體等。這些相態的一個共同點是邊界態。最近的理論預言在帶有強自旋-軌道耦合的兩維電子氣中附加一個納米尺度的周期勢可以人為造出拓撲絕緣體。這一預言如果可以實現，將會開創許多新機會研究兩維拓撲相。這裡，我們提出一個獨特的實驗方法實現這個想法以及實現其它特異拓撲體系。 首先，我們在矽（111）表面生長重金屬簿膜用以提供帶強自旋-軌道耦合的兩維電子氣。第二步是利用表面配位自組裝在這樣的簿膜表面構建兩維超分子晶格。第三步是使用低溫隧道掃描顯微鏡研究其結構及電子學性質。我們會與一個角分辨光電子能譜的小組合作研究這些體系的能帶結構。 Co-I 將會對這些體係作理論分析。 我們相信這樣一個密切合作的研究團隊將有很大機會實現我們所提出的研究目標。

16304016.label: Realisation of objectives
16304016.value: In this project, we used two approaches to successfully design 2D supramolecular structures on several metal surfaces. The first approach is single-molecule manipulation. We constructed artificial graphene systems with differentiating on-site energy at two sublattices and uniaxially compressed lattice, deformed triangular and hexagonal artificial graphene nanoflakes. The second approach is coordination self-assembly. We used this approach to fabricate extended supramolecular lattices with tunable lattice constant grown on different surfaces. We also grew Bi thin films on Si(111) and Au(111) surfaces. Overall 95% of objective 1 has been achieved. Object 2 has been fully achieved. Using STM and STS, we studied the topological phase transitions in the artificial graphene systems The local density of states resolved by STS signifies a band gap opened at the Dirac point. The deformed artificial graphene systems behave like a real graphene flake under elastic strain. The elastic inhomogeneous strain breaks sublattice symmetry. As a result, an effective vector potential is created, which generates a large pseudo-magnetic field of tens of tesla in the graphene flake without breaking time reversal symmetry. In such a condition, the electrons in the artificially deformed graphene form the pseudo Landau levels. We have studied the distribution of first several orders of pseudo Landau levels (pLLs) in real space. The 0th-order pLL is highly sublattice dependent. In the real space, that state is located at the center region of sublattice A, but the edges of sublattice B. Object 3 has been nicely achieved by a joint work collaborating with two groups in Spain. We study the modification of the substrate’s surface electrons by the interaction with a Cu-coordinated TPyB metal-organic network formed on Cu(111) and disentangle the scattering potentials and confinement properties by means of STM and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find almost unperturbed free-electron-like states stemming from the rather weak electron confinement that yields significant coupling between adjacent pores. Electron plane wave expansion simulations match the superlattice induced experimental electronic structure, which features replicating bands and energy renormalization effects. Notably, the electrostatic potential landscape obtained from our ab initio calculations suggests that the molecules are the dominant scattering entities while the coordination metal atoms sandwiched between them act as leaky channels. These metal atom transmission conduits facilitate and enhance the coupling among quantum dots, which are prone to be exploited to engineer the electronic structure of surface electron gases.

Differentiating the on-site energy of two sublattices breaks the inversion symmetry of the artificial grapheme systems, and uniaxially compressing the lattice merges the Dirac cones. Both open a band gap at the Dirac point. The edge states associated with the gap are present at the armchair edges of a compressed artificial graphene nanoflake. (New. J. Phys. 21, 083005, 2019.) 2. The energy spectra of the artificial graphene systems are influenced by the edges types. And as a result, the unique electronic properties of graphene nano-structures can be tuned. Particularly, the zigzag edges feature a half-filled flat band at the Fermi level, which contributes a zero-energy state located at the edges. (Preprint 5) 3. Substrate modulates the growth of the coordination lattices. The coordination network of 1,3,5-tris(pyridyl)benzene (TPyB) molecules with Cu atoms on various (111) surfaces of noble metals has been investigated by low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) under ultra-high vacuum condition. A distinct distorted honeycomb phase coinciding with the underlying 9×9 loop dislocations is observed on Ag/Cu(111) surface besides of normal honeycomb and triangle phases, of which the latter two also could be fabricated on Cu(111) and Au(111) in analogous configuration indicating an intense inter-network strength. The disturbed adsorption potential caused by the rearrangement of Cu atoms beneath the Ag overlayer is believed to be responsible for this commensurate architecture and could be utilized as template in other design of superstructures. (Preprint 4) 4. We confirm that metal adatoms act as weak scatterers compared to the organic molecular backbones and, due to their strategic position within the array, they provide accessible transmission channels for the surface electrons, further enhancing the interpore coupling. Such findings rely upon mesoscopic scale (by means of the spatially averaging ARPES) and nanoscale [by highly resolved scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS)] experimental electronic characterization of the 2D supramolecular lattice supported theoretically by electron plane wave expansion (EPWE) simulations and electrostatic potential (ESP) maps calculations using density functional theory (DFT). (PHYSICAL REVIEW LETTERS 123, 266805, 2019)

16304016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304016.value: At the later stage of this project, we have found that Bi thin films can be grown underneath existing supramolecuar lattices on Au(111) surface. This finding provides new opportunities for modifying the 2D electron gases. We are continuing to investigate the surface states of the Bi thin films modulated by the supramolecular lattices.

16304016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304016.value: Electrons in metals are conducting. But they can exhibit exotic behaviors when moving under the influence of artificial structures. In this project, we demonstrate that by specifically designing the artificial structures, we can change the conducting electrons to semiconducting, insulating and even insulating in the bulk but conducting at edge. Our work has proved the concept of using molecules to steer the conductivity of electrons, which can lead to new materials of novel properties.

16304416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304416.value: Heterocyclic compounds are components of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and bioactive natural products. Development of synthetic methods for these heterocyclic compounds has attracted considerable interest in organic chemistry. Among the developed methods, cyclization processes from linear substrates have often been used to achieve the synthesis of such compounds. More specifically, because of the bioactivities of the products, stereoselective cyclization processes are usually required. Yet despite vast amount of experimental studies that have been carried out in the field, systematic understanding on the processes especially the stereoselectivity issue is still limited. The lack of theories that allow a priori prediction has limited the possible research scope, and refinement protocols can be no better than trial-and-error, especially because the mechanism for chirality control is unknown. Computational studies, in this sense, can complement the experimental studies, by providing means to validate proposed mechanisms. Compare-and-contrast studies on different substrates are thereby possible, and these studies can provide more systematic trends when combined with known experimental results. In this proposed research, we will focus on a branch of the stereospecific cycloaddition between azomethine ylides and various dipolarophile substrates in the presence of a Cu(I) catalyst. There are numerous recent reports on such system that a wide range of heterocyclic compounds can be generated by applying different substrates. This versatility of reactions allows us to carry out systematic computational studies on a number of scientific issues and questions that cannot be easily deduced from the reaction outcomes. Such systematic computational studies will impact on the experimental synthesis of heterocyclic compounds. 雜環化合物是農藥，藥物和天然產物的重要組成部分。它們合成方法的發展在有機化學中非常重要。環化反應是让我们可得到雜環化合物的一种方便方法。儘管實驗结果很多，對於這些環化反應，尤其反應产產的立體化學選擇，還没有系统的理解。理論研究也很少。對於這些反應的機理也不是很清楚。在這個研究計劃中， 我们將進行系统的理論計算研究。希望解决這些環化反應的一系列科学問題，给實驗提供理論基础，從而促進雜環化合物的合成方法發展。

16304416.value: Objective 1: Mechanisms for a number of copper (or other metal) catalyzed reactions have been investigated with the aid of Density Functional Theorey (DFT) calculations. Factors influencing (and insights into) the reactions studied have been identified. Objective 2: Through our DFT studies, we were able to understand the related regioselectivity, diastereoselectivity and enantioselectivity for the reactions studied, from which we predict some possible reaction outcomes.

16304416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304416.value: Through our theoretical investigation on copper(I)-catalyzed asymmetric desymmetrization of 5-silylcyclopentadienes with azoalkenes, we have revealed the factors influencing the diastereoselectivity and enantioselectivity (see 8(1)). Our DFT studies also allowed us to reveal the factors that affect the regioselectivity of Pd- and Cu-catalyzed C-H arylation of arenes (meta versus ortho arylation) and understand the different catalytic behaviors of the Pd and Cu catalytic systems (see 8(2)). In a study of trifluoromethylcyanation of 1,3-enynes, which is an efficient protocol for allenyl nitriles, we provided theoretical insight into how ligands control the 1,2- and 1,4-additions. Our DFT studies of copper-catalyzed boracarboxylation of alkene with carbon dioxide and diboron offer an understanding of how the 3-component reaction occurs (see 8(3) and 8(4)). In a recent study regarding site-specific allylic hydrogen atom transfer by a Cu(II)-bound N-centered radical, we have showed that a Cu(II)-bound N-centered radical was able to amplify the site-selectivity of hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) among similar allylic C–H bonds in a complex molecule (see 8(5)). A Cu(I)/phosphoramidite catalyzed asymmetric formal conjugate addition of thiochromones with terminal alkynes and an enantioselective alkynylation of benzylic C−H bonds via copper-catalyzed radical relay have been developed (see 8(6) and 8(7)).

16304416.value: Over the years, we have witnessed development of various copper-catalyzed organic reactions. The insights obtained from this project contribute significantly to this expanding development. We will spend our research effort to understand many recently reported relevant reactions and continue to make our contribution to the development of this research area.

16304416.value: In this project, we've investigated issues related to copper catalyzed organic reactions. The results/insights we've obtained are useful for researchers to design copper catalysts for various organic transformation reactions.

16305616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305616.value: In recent years there has been an explosion of network data. The combination of an increasingly pervasive interest in scientific analysis at a system's level and the ever-growing capabilities for high throughput data collection in various fields has fueled this trend. Researchers from biology and bioinformatics to physics, from computer science to the information sciences, and from economics to sociology are more and more engaged in the collection and statistical analysis of data from a network-centric perspective. Accordingly, the contributions to statistical methods and modeling in this area have come from a similarly broad spectrum of areas, often independently of each other. Despite intensive interest in the network study, there remains many challenges ahead. Much of the study on the network problems focused on how to perform community detection, which is key to understanding the structure of complex networks, and ultimately extracting useful information from them. Although there is a bewildering array of techniques for community detection, very little effort has been made to study the sparse networks and the intrinsic underlying structure until recently. The purpose of this project is to look at some of the challenging issues in the network study. 网络数据是现实世界中最常用的数据类型之一。人与人之间的关系、城市之间的道路连接、科研论文之间的引用都组成了网络。随着计算能力的不断提高，越来越多的科研工作者也开始产生浓厚的兴趣。这其中包括计算机，数学，物理，生物，生物信息，信息科学，统计，经济，社会科学等等。 尽管如此，网络数据领域仍然有很多非常挑战性的问题。首先，目前网络方向研究较多较成熟的领域是社区发现，但研究结果都依赖较强的假设条件，在实际当中不一定能得到满足。例如大部分理论结果的文献假设网络是稠密的，但实际的网络（像社交网络）都是稀疏的。其次，网络的增大给计算提出很多的难度，如不能解决会影响理论研究与实际应用。 我们计划在该项目中，去研究包括以上提到的一系列挑战性问题。

16305616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305616.value: There has been an increasing interest in the study of community detection for sparse networks. Here, we propose a new method for detecting communities in sparse networks by using the symmetrized Laplacian inverse matrix (SLIM) to measure the closeness between nodes. The idea comes from the first hitting time in random walks, and it also has a nice interpretation in diffusion maps. Community membership is acquired by applying the spectral method to the SLIM. The SLIM outperforms state-of-art methods in many real datasets and simulations. It is also robust to the choice of tuning parameter, in contrast to spectral clustering with regularization. Theoretical analyses show that, in sparse scenarios of stochastic block model (SBM), the SLIM ensures the same order of misclassification rate in E(degree) as regularized spectral clustering.

16305616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305616.value: There will be several future directions from the above paper. One of these is how to incorporate the node information into the analysis. This belongs to the broader area of knowledge graph. We believe that the idea from our investigation from this project is potentially very useful in our future study of this topic.

16305616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305616.value: Network permeates every corner of our life. Examples include facebook, WeChat group, transportation networks, gene to gene interaction network. One of the interesting topics is how to group members of the network into different communities, which is referred to as community detection, which has many useful and interesting applications. The trouble is that very often the networks we encounter in life are often very sparse, meaning that there might not be enough information to carry out the desired analysis. In our project, we study this issue and find a very promising way to get round this problem. The novel approach should prove to useful in investigating other similar problems.
