16307216.label: Realisation of objectives
16307216.value: The objectives of this research project are to synthesize dinuclear iridium complexes and to explore their redox chemistry and catalytic activity. In this project, chelating ligands with pi or sigma donor groups, including phosphinate, carboxamide, and aryl, have been employed to stabilize iridium and other transition metals in high oxidation states. With these chelating ligands, we sought to synthesize metal complexes bearing multiply bonded ligands, such as oxo, nitrido, imido and carbene. The first system that has been explored is iridium alkyl porphyrins. Although iridium porphyrin compounds have been known for a long time, high-valent iridium porphyrins with multiply bonded ligands such as oxo and nitrido are unknown. We have shown that Ir(III) alkyl porphyrin complexes can serve as a good platform for studying metal-ligand multiple bonding. We have synthesized and structurally characterized a hetero-dinuclear iridium porphyrin nitrido complex, which, to our knowledge, is the first iridium porphyrin complex with the mu-nitrido ligand. X-ray diffraction studies indicated that the Ir/Ru nitrido complex contains metal-nitrogen double bonds, consistent with the Ir(V)=N=Ru(IV) bonding picture. A preliminary study showed that the Ir/Ru nitrido porphyrin complex can catalyze the cyclopropanation of alkenes such as styrene, presumably via a reactive high-valent iridium nitrido carbene intermediate. In addition, we have synthesized iridium porphyrin hydroxo and hydrosulfido (HS-) complexes that can serve as precursors to dinuclear iridium oxo and sulfido complexes. The second ligand system is a tetradentate pyridine-carboxamide ligand (bpb). We have synthesized an Ir(III) tosylate complex, [Ir(bpb){P(p-tol)3}(OTs)], which has proven to be a useful starting material for the synthesis of Ir(bpb) complexes. Ir(bpb) complexes containing a variety of axial ligands, such as carbene and carbamoyl, have been synthesized and structurally characterized. [Ir(bpb){P(p-tol)3}(OTs)] can catalyze the oxidation of alkenes with iodosylbenzene, presumably via a reactive iridium-oxo intermediate. Cyclic voltammetric studies indicated that the Ir(IV/III) redox potential of the Ir(bpb) complexes can be tuned by the axial ligand. Thus, with judicious choice of axial ligands, high-valent Ir(IV) bpb complexes are chemically accessible, and such complexes can display interesting redox and atom transfer chemistry. In addition, we have studied the oxidation chemistry of iridium complexes with cyclometalated ligands. In particular, the reactivity of metal complexes with tridentate bis-cyclometalated C^N^C ligands, such as 2,6-bis(4-tert-butylphenyl)pyridine, has been explored. The redox chemistry of dinuclear Pt(C^N^C) complexes has been studied. We have synthesized heterometallic Pt nitrido complexes M-N-Pt(II) C^N^C (M = Ru, Os) complexes that can be oxidized to M-N-Pt(IV) species. We have shown that the Pt-N pi bonding in M-N-Pt complexes is dependent on the Pt oxidation state and the nature of M and its co-ligands. Moreover, we have developed a new method to synthesize Ir(C^N^C) complexes using the mercury reagent Hg(HC^N^C)Cl. Ir(C^N^C) complexes such as [Ir(C^N^C)(cod)Cl] (cod = 1,5-cyclooctadiene) and [Ir(C^N^C)(HC^N^C)(CO)] have been synthesized. [Ir(C^N^C)(cod)(CF3SO3)] can catalyze cyclopropanation of alkenes, showing the potential of Ir(C^N^C) complexes as catalysts for organic reactions. Very recently, we have synthesized Ir complexes with a tripodal C^N^C ligand that exhibited a low Ir(IV/III) redox potential (~0 V versus the ferrocenium-ferrocene couple), indicating that high-valent Ir(C^N^C) complexes are chemically accessible. The oxidation chemistry of metal complexes with chelating P=O ligands such as the Kläui tripodal ligand [CpCo{P(O)(OEt)2}3]- (LOEt-) has been studied. M-LOEt aqua complexes are of special interest because they can be oxidized to hydroxo or oxo species via proton-coupled electron transfer in water. We have synthesized a Ru aqua complex, [LOEtRu(H2O)3](OTs)2, which can catalyze C-H oxidation in water, demonstrating water-soluble M-LOEt complexes can find applications in aqueous organometallic catalysis. Although attempts to synthesize [LOEtIr(H2O)3]2+ were unsuccessful, we found that organoiridium complexes with bidentate P=O ligands, such as [N(Ph2PO)2]- (tpip), display interesting oxidation chemistry. For example, the Ir aqua complex [Ir(tpip)(coe)2Me(H2O)]+ can catalyze the oxidation of alkenes with iodosylbenzene, presumably via a reactive Ir(tpip) oxo active species. In summary, the results of this project have demonstrated that chelating ligands, such as carboxamide and P=O ligands, can stabilize iridium in high oxidation states. Electrochemical studies indicated that Ir(IV/III) potential can be tuned by the ligands and Ir(IV) complexes are chemically accessible. Ir complexes with these chelate ligands can catalyze oxidation of organic substrates, presumably via high-valent Ir-oxo intermediates. Also, we have developed a general synthetic route to dinuclear iridium nitrido complexes that enables us to probe the influence of coligands on the reactivity of high-valent iridium.

16307216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307216.value: (i) We have synthesized the first heterodinuclear iridium/ruthenium nitrido porphyrin complex. X-ray crystallography revealed that the dinuclear Ru-N-Ir porphyrin complex contains metal-nitrogen double bonds, indicative of the Ru(IV)=N=Ir(V) bonding picture. The Ru-N-Ir complex can catalyze cyclopropanation of alkenes with ethyl diazoacetate, presumably via an Ir nitrido carbene intermediate. In addition, we have isolated Ir(III) hydroxo and hydrosulfido porphyrin complexes that are precursors to dinuclear Ir oxo and sulfido species. (ii) We have synthesized a series of Ir(III) pyridine-carboxamide (bpb) complexes with various axial ligands, including carbene and carbamoyl. The Ir(III) bpb tosylate complex can catalyze oxidation of alkenes with iodosylbenzene, presumably via Ir-oxo intermediates. With judicious choice of axial ligands, Ir(IV) bpb complexes with low Ir(IV/III) redox potentials are chemically accessible. (iii) We have synthesized the first 4-coordinated Ru(II) selenolate complex that exhibits a unique see-saw geometry. Novel Ru(IV) tosylimido complexes have been isolated from the oxidation of the Ru(II) selenolate and thiolate complexes with tosyl azide. These Ru(IV) tosylimido complexes exhibit nucleophilic behavior and can undergo nitrene transfer with phosphines. This work opens up a new avenue for the study of metal-ligand multiple bonds in chalcogen-rich coordination spheres. (iv) We have synthesized and structurally characterized the first heterometallic Ru(IV)-N-Fe(IV) phthalocyanine complexes. Oxidation of the Ru-N-Fe phthalocyanine complexes led to formation of Fe(IV) phthalocyanine cation radical and hydroxylphthalocyanine complexes that have characterized by X-ray crystallography. This is the first report of the formation of a hydroxyphthalocyanine complex by direct oxidation of a metallophthalocyanine precursor. (v) We have synthesized the first heterometallic Pt(II)-N-Ru(VI) complexes with a bis-cyclometalated C^N^C ligand that can be oxidized to Pt(IV)-N-Ru(VI) species. We found that the Pt-N pi bond in the Pt-N-M complexes is dependent on the Pt oxidation state and the nature of M and its coligands. (vi) We have synthesized a water-soluble Ru aqua complex, [(LOEt)Ru(H2O)3]2+, which is an active catalyst for oxidation of C-H bonds in water. This result highlights the potential application of water-soluble metal complexes in aqueous organometallic catalysis. (vii) We have developed a new method of synthesize iridium complexes with bis-cyclometalated C^N^C ligand. [Ir(C^N^C)(cod)(CF3SO3)] can catalyze cyclopropanation of alkenes with ethyl diazoacetate, demonstrating the potential application of Ir(C^N^C) complexes in organometallic catalysis. Also, C^N^C ligand was found to display flexible coordination behavior and can switch between the tridentate and bidentate binding modes through protonation/oxidation and deprotonation.

16307216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307216.value: We have demonstrated that chelating carboxamide ligands such as bpb can stabilize high-valent iridium. Thus, with judicious choice of axial ligands, Ir(IV) bpb hydroxo/amido complexes are chemically accessible. However, the poor solubility of Ir(bpb) complexes in hydrocarbon solvents, e.g. hexane, renders the isolation and crystallization of such reactive Ir(IV)(bpb) complexes difficult. To address this problem, hydrocarbon-soluble Ir complexes with substituted bpb ligands will be synthesized. Moreover, incorporating sulfonato groups into the bpb or axial ligands in [Ir(bpb)(PR3)(H2O)]+ will render the Ir complex water-soluble, and this will offer us an opportunity to synthesize reactive Ir(bpb) oxo species by proton-coupled electron transfer oxidation. Nucleophilic Ru(IV) arylimido complexes are of interest because they can find applications in C-N bond forming reactions. However, the reaction of Ru(II) thiolate with p-tolyl azide gave Ru(IV) tetrazene complexes, via [2+3] cycloaddition of transient Ru p-tolylimido species with the azide. The cycloaddition reaction can be inhibited by using sterically bulky arylimides. Thus, efforts should be made to synthesize sterically bulky Ru(IV) terminal arylimido complexes by reacting Ru(II) thiolates with bulky arylazides (e.g. terphenyl azide). The reactions of nucleophilic Ru(IV) arylimido complexes with unsaturated organic substrates such as alkynes will be explored.

16307216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307216.value: High-oxidation-state iridium complexes are of significance because they have been proposed as reactive intermediates in iridium-catalyzed oxidation of organic substrates and water. Iridium coordination compounds with +III or higher oxidation states are rather rare because they are generally oxidizing and easily reduced to trivalent compounds. In this research project, we sought to stabilize high-valent iridium using electron-rich oxygen, nitrogen and carbon donor chelating ligands. Efforts have been made to synthesize dinuclear iridium compounds containing multiply bonded ligands and investigate their redox and catalytic chemistry. We have synthesized a heterometallic iridium(V)-ruthenium(IV) nitrido porphyrin complex that features iridium-nitrogen double bonds, showing that porphyrin is good platform for studying metal-ligand multiple bonds for iridium. A related iron(IV)-ruthenium(IV) nitrido phthalocyanine complex that could be oxidized to a phthalocyanine cation radical or a hydroxyphthalocyanine complex has also been isolated. Iridium pyridine-carboxamide complexes were found to exhibit low iridium(IV/III) redox potentials, indicating the ability of the carboxamide to stabilize the iridium(IV) state. Iridium pyridine-carboxamide complexes can catalyze oxidation of organic substrates, presumably via high-valent iridium-oxo intermediates. In summary, the results of this project demonstrate that electron-rich chelating ligands can stabilize high-valent iridium complexes that can find potential applications in catalytic organic oxidations.

16307516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307516.value: 该项目将系统地对门限GARCH(p,q)模型进行检验和估计。我们 首先研究GARCH(p,q)模型中一个门限的拟似然比（QLR）检验， 并推导它的极限分布。我们希望证明QLR检验能够被一个具有 无限标记的标记过程的函数所逼近，并且弱收敛到一个高斯过 程的函数。然后我们将研究门限GARCH(p,q)模型中常规参数和 门限的拟极大似然估计。我们希望得到所要估计的门限的收敛 率，并刻画它的极限分布。在这些可能结果基础上，利用门限 GARCH(p,q)模型的平方残差自相关函数，我们将构造一个 portmanteau检验以检查模型是否恰当。我们将用广泛的仿真研 究来评估有限样本中检验统计量的置信水平和功效，以及估计 方法的表现。本项目将运用新的理论和方法研究各类经济和金 融数据，特别是和香港相关的数据

16307516.label: Realisation of objectives
16307516.value: We first studied a special case of threshold GARCH models, called threshold double autoregressive model. We investigated the quasi-maximum likelihood estimator (QMLE) of the structure-changed and two-regime threshold double autoregressive model. It is shown that both the estimated threshold and change-point are n-consistent, and they converge weakly to the smallest minimizer of a compound Poisson process and the location of minima of a two-sided random walk, respectively. Other estimated parameters are root-n consistent and asymptotically normal. We then explored the properties of threshold GARCH models via three aspects as follows. (a). We developed a systematic procedure of statistical inference for the heavy-tailed TAR model . We investigated the self-weighted least absolute deviation estimation for the model. It is shown that the estimated slope parameters are root- n-consistent and asymptotically normal, and the estimated thresholds are n-consistent, each of which converges weakly to the smallest minimizer of a compound Poisson process. Based on this theory, the Wald test statistic is considered for testing the linear restriction of slope parameters and a procedure is given for inference of threshold parameters. We finally construct a sign-based portmanteau test for model checking. This result provides a channel to understand the estimating theory of threshold GARCH models with heavy-tailed noises. (b). We focused on a first-order zero-drift GARCH model. Unlike the classical GARCH model, the model is always non-stationary regardless of the sign of the Lyapunov exponent, but interestingly it is stable with its sample path oscillating randomly between zero and infinity over time when the exponent is zero. Furthermore, we studied the generalized QMLE of the model, and established its strong consistency and asymptotic normality. Based on the general QMLE, a t-test for stability, a unit root test for the absence of the drift term, and a portmanteau test for model checking are constructed. These results include some parts of asymptotic theory of threshold GARCH models and help us to understand the zero-drift threshold GARCH models under which the models may be more useful than the standard threshold GARCH models. (c). To understand the threshold GARCH effect in high-dimensional time series, we proposed several tests for detecting serial correlation and ARCH effect in high-dimensional data. The dimension of data p = p(n) may go to infinity when the sample size goes to infinite. It is shown that the sample autocorrelations and the sample rank autocorrelations (Spearman’s rank correlation) of the L1-norm of data are asymptotically normal. Two portmanteau tests based, respectively, on the norm and its rank are shown to be asymptotically Chi-square distributed, and the corresponding weighted portmanteau tests are shown to be asymptotically distributed as a linear combination of independent Chi-square random variables. These tests are dimension-free, that is, independent of p, and the norm rank-based portmanteau test and its weighted counterpart can be used for heavy-tailed time series, including threshold GARCH models. We further examine the theory and methodology of statistical inferences of thresholds and change-points in threshold autoregressive models. We showed that least squares estimators (LSE) of thresholds and change-points are n-consistent, and that they converge weakly to the minimizer of a compound Poisson process and the location of minima of a two-sided random walk, respectively. When the magnitude of the change in the parameters of the state regimes or in the time horizon is small, we further show that these limiting distributions can be approximated by a class of known distributions. The LSEs of the slope parameters are root-n consistent and asymptotically normal. Furthermore, a likelihood-ratio based confidence set is given for the thresholds and change-points, respectively. The estimated thresholds in the threshold GARCH models do not have a closed form and it is very difficult to be used in practice. To solve this problem, we developed a general approach to approximate the distribution of estimated threshold via Compound Poisson processes (CPP). We proposed a new approximation of a CPP by a Brownian motion and illustrated the above approximation in applications, such as the construction of confidence intervals of threshold parameters in threshold models. We conduct numerical simulations to assess the performance of the proposed approximation. To explore the possibility of extending our new theory and methodology to heavy tailed time series, we studied the heavy-tailed vector error correction models and established the asymptotic theory of the full rank least squares estimator (FLSE). It is shown that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters is n (sample size) and its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when the tail index is in (0,2). Furthermore, we showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is not root-n and its limiting distribution is a functional of two stable processes when the tail index is in (1, 2). However, when the tailed index is in (0, 1), we showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is n and its limiting distribution not only depends on the stationary component itself but also depends on the unit root component. Based on the FLSE, the limiting distribution of the reduced rank LSE (RLSE) is derived. Finally, to explore the possibility of using Lasso method to estimate the thresholds in threshold GARCH models. The Lasso-based approach for variable selection of ARMA models was studied. We showed that the Lasso estimator has the Knight-Fu's limit distribution under a general tuning parameter assumption. With a special restriction on tuning parameters, we showed that the Lasso estimator can achieve the oracle" properties zero parameters are estimated to be zero exactly and other estimators are as efficient as those under the true model.

16307516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307516.value: This project has developed a systematic procedure for testing and estimation of threshold ARCH-type models with various variations . We studied the quasi-likelihood ratio-type test for a threshold under some different classes of threshold models and derive its limiting distribution. We showed that the test can be approximated by a known function or weakly converge to a function of Gaussian process. We established the rates of convergence of the estimated threshold under even more complicated scenarios and characterize its limiting distributions. Based on these results we have constructed a portmanteau test for checking model adequacy. Extensive simulation studies have be used to evaluate the size and power of test statistics and the performance of the estimation approach in finite samples. This project has applied the new theory and approach to analyze various economic and financial data, such as USA Treasury bills and GDP as well as various asset prices in stock markets. Our results will help researchers and practitioners to understand the nonlinear structures of economic and financial data in a new way. The research outputs from this project should be important both theoretically and empirically, and have been published in leading international econometric and statistical journals.

16308016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308016.value: The synthesis of artificial chiral materials has received much attention, as these materials can serve as simple models to deepen our understanding of complex biological systems. Among these materials, those with strong light emission are of particular interest because they enable us to visualize never before seen biochemical structures and processes. They are also promising candidates for optoelectronic applications. Most of the chiral luminogenic materials developed so far are organometallic or organic compounds. The former suffer from high cost and environmental instability, whereas the latter have advantages such as a wide variety and good biocompatibility and processability. However, their strong light emission is partially or completely quenched when they are aggregated in the solution state. The problem of aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) must be tackled because these materials are commonly used as solid films in real-world applications. Our group has observed an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) phenomenon that is the exact opposite of ACQ in some propeller- or shell-shaped molecules. The incorporation of chiral moieties to AIE luminogens (AIEgens) may generate materials with helical conformation and efficient circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). However, this possibility has not been actively investigated because there are no clear design guidelines for their synthesis. Thus, in this proposal, we aim to develop luminogenic materials with both AIE and strong helical properties. We will investigate the structure–property relationships to assist future molecular design. The practical application of the materials in the fields of biological science and optoelectronics will also be explored. Two approaches will be taken to prepare the chiral AIEgens. The chiral moieties will be linked to AIEgens either by covalent bonds or through non-covalent interactions such as hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interaction, and the hydrophobic effect. The effects of the AIEgen structure, linking unit, chiral group, connecting position, and distance between the AIEgen and the chiral group on the properties, especially the CPL, of the resulting adducts will be investigated in the solution and aggregated states. The conditions that influence the self-assembly of chiral AIEgens, such as the solvent, temperature, additive, and substrate, will be optimized to achieve aggregates with novel chiroptical properties. Their potential application for monitoring protein conformational change, chiral recognition, and fabricating liquid crystal displays and organic light-emitting diodes with a CPL signal will be investigated. It is expected that the proposed project will generate a large variety of chiral AIEgens with novel structures, efficient (polarized) light emission, and high-tech applications. 非天然手性材料的合成受到了人們的極大關注，因為這些材料可以作為簡單的模型化合物加深我們對複雜生物體系的理解。具有強發光的手性材料尤其重要，因為它們使得和生物化學相關的結構和過程視覺化。 發光手性材料在光電方面也有潛在的應用。迄今為止，大多數手性發光材料都是金屬配體絡合物以及有機化合物。前者不但價格昂貴而且穩定性不好，而後者則擁有來源廣泛，生物相容性好以及加工性好等優點。然而，對於有機手性發光材料而言，當從溶液中聚集之後，它們的強發光可能被部分或完全淬滅。因此，如何有效克服這種所謂的聚集導致淬滅 (ACQ)成為一項重要的研究課題，因為在真正的實際應用中大部分材料是以固態薄膜形式存在的。和ACQ現象相反，我們課題組近年來發展了一類具有螺旋槳或貝殼狀結構的分子呈現出聚集誘導發光（AIE）的現象。而手性基團的引入有可能使AIE發光體誘導出螺旋構象和有效的圓偏振發光。然而，目前對這些手性發光材料的研究非常有限因為缺乏有效清晰的設計指導原則。因此，在本專案中，我們計畫發展同時具有聚集誘導發光和手性特點的發光材料。我們將對材料的結構性質關係進行詳細的研究以輔助將來的分子設計。我們也將探究這類材料在生命科學以及光電器件方面的應用。 兩種策略將被採用來製備手性AIE發光材料。手性單元將通過共價鍵或非共價鍵（比如氫鍵，靜電作用，親疏水作用）的方式連結到AIE發色團上。各種不同因素如AIE發色團的分子結構，連結單元，手性基團，結合位點以及AIE發色團和手性基團的距離對材料性能尤其是對其圓偏振發光性質的影響將被逐一研究。此外，通過優化溶劑，溫度，添加劑以及底物等影響手性AIE材料自組裝的條件，我們期望能夠實現優異的光學手性特點。我們也將研究手性AIE材料在模擬蛋白構型的變化，手性識別，圓偏振發光的液晶顯示器件和有機發光二極體器件等方面的潛在應用。我們期望能夠通過本專案創制一大批結構特異，具有有效的圓偏振發光以及高端應用的手性AIE材料。

16308016.label: Realisation of objectives
16308016.value: The objectives of this proposal are to design and synthesize new chiral luminogenic materials from aggregation-induced emission luminogens and explore the high-tech applications of the new materials. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. A series of binaphthalene-containing luminogenic enantiomers was designed and synthesized. These molecules emitted weakly in solution but showed intense emission in the aggregated state, demonstrating a phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission (AIE). Lifetime measurement showed the delayed fluorescence character of the light emission. These molecules showed circular dichroism (CD) signal and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in toluene solutions, whose magnitudes increased when they were fabricated into films. Multilayer circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes (CPOLEDs) using doped and neat films of the molecules as emitting layers were fabricated, which exhibited high external quantum efficiency of up to 9.3% and 3.5% and electroluminescence dissymmetry factor (gEL) of up to +0.026/-0.021 and +0.06/-0.06, respectively. Compared with doped CPOLEDs, the non-doped ones showed higher gEL and much smaller current efficiency roll-off due to the stronger AIE effect. By altering the donor unit, the electroluminescence of the doped film could be tuned from 493 to 571 nm. As far as it is known, this is the first example of efficient CPOLEDs based on small chiral organic molecules. Four 1,1′-binaphthyl and tetraphenylethene (TPE)-based chiral AIE polymers were designed and synthesized. Polymers P-1 and P-2 with “open” binaphthyl exhibited a typical aggregation-annihilated circular dichroism (AACD) effect and their CD couplet intensity was largely annihilated in the aggregates. However, the AACD effect was suppressed in P-3 and P-4 as the binaphthyl moieties were locked by methylene, suggesting that the AACD effect is mainly caused by the twisting of naphthalene rings. From the solution to aggregate state, the θ of “open” polymers was largely decreased and part of the conformers relaxed from cisoid to transoid. On the contrary, the “locked” polymers showed a slightly larger θ and their cisoid conformation was preserved during the aggregation process. Thus, CD spectroscopy may be used for real-time and in-situ monitoring of molecular aggregation, especially for biomacromolecular aggregations in physiological conditions. Constructing artificial helical structures through hierarchical self-assembly and exploring the underlying mechanism are important as they help gain insight into the structures, processes, and functions of biological helices. Here, two AIE-active chiral Au(I) complexes were synthesized in this work, in which their specific aggregates underwent spontaneous hierarchical self-assembly to give inverse helical architectures. In situ and real-time CD monitoring for the entire dynamic self-assembly processes revealed an impressive chiral inversion and significant amplification during the hierarchical evolution processes from vesicles to helical fibers. The induction of CPL signals from achiral luminogens by utilizing the present chiral enantiomers as chiral transcription templates was also successfully realized. Two chiral AIE luminogens with rigid cores containing different linkages were prepared. These molecules showed a silent CPL signal when existed as isolated species in THF solution. In contrast, a tunable CPL response was achieved through regulating their aggregated structures in solution and solid states. Opposite CPL responses with glum of the order of 10-3 were obtained from a M-helical nanofibrous structure and complex liquid crystalline (H + S) orientations of DPCE-Ach. Meanwhile, DPCE-ECh exhibited a liquid crystalline assembled system (smectic C*) with a high dissymmetry factor (gCD = -0.20 and glum = +0.38). The intense and apparent CD and CPL of the film stemmed from the intrinsic helical structure of the molecular assemblies with a weak contribution of Bragg reflection, where the lone helical molecular stacking axis was perpendicular to the optical axis and parallel to the direction of the glass substrate. On the other hand, DPCE-ACh could form two coexisting phases of chiral hexagonal and smectic liquid-crystalline phases due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The non-periodic molecular orientations of DPCE-ACh disrupted its helical structure to give a weak negative CPL signal of the order of 10-3. In situ photo-irradiation of trans-2-(4-fluorostyryl)benzo[d]oxazole (t-FSBO) and trans-2-(2,4-difluorostyryl)benzo[d]oxazole (t-2FSBO) with aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) characteristics in the solid-state afforded unprecedented AIE luminogens (t-FPCBO, t-2FPCBO and c-2FPCBO) through [2+2] cycloaddition. Although the photoreaction products were weakly conjugated, they were emissive. Intramolecular or intermolecular through-space conjugation was confirmed to be the key factor for the luminescence of these non-conjugated molecules. c-2FPCBO formed two kinds of crystals with blue and yellow emission, respectively. Furthermore, crystal transformation was observed by measuring its AIE property. This novel in situ ACQ-to-AIE transformation is thus a general approach to obtain solid-state light-emitting materials in a simple and atom-economical manner. The t-FSBO crystals showed mechanically response to photoexcitation, exhibiting a photosalient effect. By coating t-FSBO on a nitrile butadiene glove, a macroscopic mechanical motion was achieved by amplifying the collective molecular motion from the nanoscale up to the macroscopic dimension. Two nonconjugated molecules, namely 1,2-diphenylethane (s-DPE) and 1,2-bis(2,4,5-trimethylphenyl)ethane (s-DPE-TM), were synthesized, and their solid-state molecular motion (SSMM) was investigated. Experimentally, steady-state PL spectra showed that these molecules showed unexpected clusteroluminescence due to the radiative decay of the excited-state through-space complexes was observed along with the ESTSC generation formed by the light-driven SSMM. Time-dependent PL measurements revealed that the ESTSC recovered to its initial structures upon removing the irradiation. Quantum mechanics calculation further confirmed the process of solid-state intermolecular motion and provided the structure of ESTSC. Femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) spectroscopy afforded direct evidence for the formation of new species in the excited state, which should correspond to the ESTSC. Besides, time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy demonstrated that the solid-state molecular motions of s-DPE and s-DPE-TM were accelerated with the increase of their ambient temperature. Based on the skeleton of tetraphenylpyrazine (TPP), a new AIE luminogen, namely TPP-PDCV, was generated by functionalizing TPP with malonitrile group. PDVC could function as a ratiometric fluorescent probe to detect H2S. The probe showed good selectivity against competitive anions and biothiols with a low detection limit of 0.5 × 10−6 M. TPP-PDCV formed crystals with different emission colors attributed to the possible formation of J-aggregates and H-aggregates. The redder emissive powder exhibited a mechanochromic phenomenon with hypsochromic effect in the presence of external stimuli because of the reversible transformation between the crystalline and amorphous states.

16308016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308016.value: The synthesis of artificial chiral materials has received much attention as these materials can serve as simple models to deepen our understanding of complex biological systems. Among these materials, those with strong light emission are of particular interest because they enable us to visualize never seen biochemical structures and processes. They are also promising candidates for optoelectronic applications. However, most of the chiral luminogenic materials developed so far show weak emission when they are aggregated in the solution state. Our group has observed an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) phenomenon that show efficient light emission in the solid state in some propeller- or shell-shaped molecules. The incorporation of chiral moieties to AIE luminogens may generate materials with helical conformation and efficient CPL. However, this possibility has not been actively investigated. In this investigation, a series of binaphthalene-containing luminogenic enantiomers with AIE characteristics was designed and synthesized. Their toluene solutions showed CD and CPL signals in toluene solutions, whose magnitudes increased when they were fabricated into films. Multilayer CPOLEDs using the molecules as emitting layers were fabricated, which exhibited high external quantum efficiency of up to 9.3% and gEL of up to +0.06/-0.06, respectively. On the other hand, the aggregation of molecules plays an important role in determining their function. Electron microscopy and other methods can only characterize the variation of microstructure but are not capable of monitoring conformational changes. These techniques are also complicated, expensive and time-consuming. We, however, found that by using circular dichroism, in-situ, and real-time monitoring the conformational change of 1,1′-binaphthyl and TPE-based chiral AIE polymers during the aggregation process was realized in a simple and fashion. Additionally, the study on spontaneous hierarchical self-assembly transitions, chirality inversion and amplification, and induction of CPL signal generation of chiral, AIE-active Au(I) complexes by in situ and time-dependent CD spectroscopy and scanning electron microscope provides a simple but efficient way to explore the sophisticated self-assembly process and presents a facile and effective strategy to fabricate architectures with CPL properties. As you can see in part C of this report, 20 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

16308016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308016.value: The synthesis of chiral materials is of interest because it may generate artificial (macro)molecules that may serve as simple models to deepen our understanding of their biological counterparts. In this investigation, we have developed new chiral materials with AIE characteristics. These molecules show strong emission and CD and CPL signals in the aggregated and film states. Such characteristics make them promise as emitting layers for fabricating CPOLEDs with high efficiency and dissymmetry factor and chiral templates to induce CPL signals from achiral luminogens. Using circular dichroism, in-situ and real-time monitoring the conformational changes, aggregation processes and self-assembly transitions of these molecules are realized. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore further the properties of our materials and practical applications in various fields.

16308016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308016.value: The synthesis of luminescent chiral materials is of academic interest and practical applications. Unfortunately, most of the materials prepared so far, show weak emission in the solid state, which has limited their high-technology applications. Chiral materials with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics, on the contrary, show efficient light emission in the solid state and they thus hold more promise for real-world applications. In this investigation, we have synthesized AIE-active, chiral materials with strong emission in the solid state. Such a property enables the fabrication of efficient circularly polarized organic light-emitting diodes and the monitoring of chemical structures and processes by circular dichroism.

16308116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308116.value: Fluorescent polymers have attracted much attention for their potential use in low-cost optoelectronic devices. A wide variety of fluorescent polymers has been prepared, with most showing strong light emission in the solution state. However, these polymers become weakly emissive or even non-fluorescent when aggregated, due to strong interactions between the polymer chains. It is important to solve this problem of aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) as fluorescent polymers are commonly used as solid films in their real-world applications. Our research group has observed the phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission (AIE), the exact opposite of the ACQ effect, in some propeller- or shell-shaped molecules. Rather than quenching, aggregate formation induces intense emission by these molecules. Incorporating such AIE molecules (AIEgens) into polymer structures produces macromolecules that not only exhibit AIE characteristics but also have unique properties that are not observed in their low-molecular-weight counterparts. Generally, AIE polymers are prepared either by using polymerization techniques to link monomers that carry AIEgens or by post-functionalizing synthesized macromolecules with AIEgens. The first method requires functional AIEgens to be pre-synthesized in time-consuming synthetic procedures, while the second method may give products with irregular structures due to incomplete reaction. According to this proposal, we therefore aim to develop simple methods for synthesizing AIE polymers. It is known that AIEgens such as 1-cyanotriarylethene and tetraarylethene can be readily generated in high yields by transition-metal-catalyzed reactions of commercially available aromatic internal alkynes, aromatic halides, and potassium ferrocyanide or arylboronic acids or arylmagnesium bromides. We thus aim to develop these organic reactions into useful tools for synthesizing new polymers with AIEgens generated in situ in the backbones. To achieve this, new internal diynes, di- and tri-halogenated arenes, arylboronic acids, and arylmagnesium bromides will be designed and synthesized. New catalyst systems and optimum polymerization conditions will be found for converting the monomers into high-molecular-weight polymers with linear and hyperbranched structures in high yields. Different substituents will be incorporated into the monomer structures to reveal the structure–property relationships of the resulting polymers and endow them with novel electronic, optical, and photonic properties. The use of these polymers in fluorescent chemosensors and bioprobes, polymer light-emitting diodes, and photopatterning will be explored. It is expected that this project will lead to the development of simple polymerization methods allowing facile preparation of AIE polymers with unique structures, novel functionalities, and advanced high-technology applications. 螢光高分子由於其在製備廉價光電器件方面的優勢引起了人們的廣泛關注。大量在溶液中發光很強的螢光高分子材料被製備。然而，當聚集之後，這些材料往往表現出較弱的發光甚至不再發光，這主要是由高分子鏈之間較強的相互作用所致。如何有效的解決這種聚集導致的螢光淬滅(ACQ)變得非常重要因為在真正的實際應用中高分子材料往往是以固態薄膜形式存在的。 和ACQ現象相反，我們課題組觀察到一類具有螺旋槳或貝殼狀結構的分子呈現出聚集誘導發光(AIE)的現象。非但螢光不會淬滅，聚集形式會誘導產生更強的螢光。將AIE分子引入到聚合物骨架中製備的大分子不但表現出AIE特性，而且擁有一些其低分子量所沒有的特殊性質。總的來說，AIE聚合物主要是通過聚合將帶有AIE發色團的單體連結起來或者用AIE發色團對大分子進行後修飾。第一種策略需要預先製備官能化的AIEgens，耗時較長。而第二種策略可能因為反應的不完全製備出結構不規整的聚合物。本專案中我們計畫發展更為簡單的方法來合成AIE高分子。過渡金屬催化商業易得的芳基內炔，芳基鹵化物，和鐵氰化鉀或芳基硼酸或芳基格式試劑可以高效的製備AIE材料如1-氰基三芳基乙烯和四芳基乙烯。因為，我們計畫利用這種反應來製備能夠在骨架中原位產生AIE發色團的新型高分子。 為了實現這個目標，新的內雙炔，二鹵代和三鹵代芳烴，芳基硼酸以芳基格式試劑將被設計合成。新的催化體系和優化的聚合條件將被探索來實現將單體有效的轉化成高分子量的線性和超支化結構。不同的取代基將被引入到單體結構來製備具有不同結構性質的高分子，並賦予其新的電，光，和光子性質。同時我們將探索這些高分子材料在螢光化學傳感，生物探針，聚合物發光二極體，光刻板中的應用。我們期望本專案能夠發展出一些簡單的聚合方法從而實現具有獨特結構，新功能以及高端應用的AIE聚合物的簡易製備。

16308116.label: Realisation of objectives
16308116.value: The objectives of this proposal are to develop new, simple, alkyne-based reaction routes to polymers with aggregation-induced emission characteristics and explore the high-technology applications of the new polymers. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. We have developed a facile, one-pot, three-component polymerization route for in situ generation of polymers with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics. The polycoupling of dibromoarenes, internal diynes and potassium ferrocyanide proceeded smoothly in dimethylacetamide under nitrogen at 120 °C in the presence of palladium acetate and sodium bicarbonate to produce poly(triphenylacrylonitrite)s with high weight-average molecular weights of up to 223000 in high yields of up to 84%. All the obtained polymers show remarkable thermal stability and possess good solubility in common organic solvents. Their spin-coated thin films exhibit high refractive indices (1.6482−1.7682). Due to the triphenylethene chromophore in situ generated during the polymerization, all the polymers are AIE-active and show intense light emission in the solid state. While UV irradiation of the polymer thin films in air through upper masks photo-oxidizes the exposed parts and quenches their light emission, the unexposed parts remain emissive. Two-dimensional fluorescent patterns with good resolution are thus generated. We also developed a series of multifunctional oxazine-containing polyheterocycles with AIE characteristics by metal-free one-pot A3 polymerizations of terminal diynes, dialdehydes, and urea. Most of the polymers are synthesized with high molecular weights in nearly quantitative yields and display intense solid-state emission and remarkable fluorescence response to protonation and deprotonation. Based on this property, a fast, responsive, and reversible fluorescent sensor for sensing ammonia with a detection limit of 960 ppb is achieved and applied for detecting biogenic amines and seafood spoilage. The nanoparticles of the polymers can serve as visualizing agents for specific imaging of lysosome in live cell. They also show ratiometric pH sensing behavior with a broad acid-base response window from pH 1 to 9, which shed light on visualizing physiologic pH in gastrointestinal tract. Taking freshwater Cladocera Moina macrocopa as a model organism, in vivo mapping of its intestinal pH shows an increased pH gradient approximately from 4.2 to 7.8 along the foregut, midgut, and hindgut. We further developed a novel and efficient synthetic strategy to poly(p-arylene dihalodiene)s (PADs) with AIE characteristics. In the presence of PdBr2 and CuBr2, the polymerization of terminal alkynes proceeded smoothly without heating to generate PADs with high molecular weight and high thermal stability. The polymerization had various advantages such as mild conditions, tolerance to air and moisture, high efficiency, and good yield. An excessive amount of CuBr2 could be used for the polymerization without strict control on the monomer stoichiometric balance as required in traditional two-component polycondensation and polyaddition. Monomers with twisted structures endowed the resulting polymers with good solubility and processability. The thin films of PADs showed high refractive indices and could be utilized for fabricating well-resolved fluorescent photopatterns by photolithography. The vinyl bromine functionality of PADs enables them to undergo post-functionalization to afford materials with more sophisticated structures and applications. A series of poly(indazole)s with high molecular weights are obtained in good yields by palladium-catalyzed oxidative polyannulations of internal alkynes and pyrazoles in 1,4-dioxane in air at 120 °C in the presence of 2,6-dimethylbenzoic acid and Cu(OAc)2·H2O. All the formed polymers possess good solubility in common organic solvents. Their thin films on silica wafers show high and tunable refractive indices. Moreover, these polymers possess high thermal stability with high degradation temperatures. The tetraphenylethene-containing polymers show high photosensitivity and visible solid-state emission, which enable the fabrication of two-dimensional fluorescent photopatterns from its thin films by a photolithography technique. A novel multicomponent polymerization route of diynes, 4,4’-oxybis(benzenesulfonyl hydrazide) and diphenyl dichalcogen toward chalcogen-rich polymers was developed, through which a series of poly(vinyl sulfones) (PVSs) with high regio- and stereo-selectivity were synthesized in high yields (up to 92.3%) at room temperature using readily prepared monomers. The rich chalcogen elements endowed the PVSs with distinctive multifunctionalities. For example, the PVSs possessed good solubility and film-forming ability. Their thin films exhibited outstanding refractive indices together with good optical transparency in the visible region. Some of the polymer films can be fabricated into well-resolved fluorescent photopatterns by photolithography. Thanks to their unique redox properties, the selenium-containing polymers underwent post-modification readily to generate their oxidized forms without heavy atom effect for use as fluorescent bioprobes for cellular imaging. We also developed an efficient one-pot polymerization route to in situ generate functional azonia-containing polyelectrolytes using readily accessible non-ionic reactants and commercially available cheap ionic species. The polymerization proceeded efficiently in air with high tolerance to the monomer feed ratio, which generated polyelectrolytes in excellent yields with high molecular weights in high atom economy manner. The emission color of the resulting polyelectrolytes could be easily tuned by changing the electron donor. The polymers were found to be excellent materials for fluorescent photopatterns and promising for optical applications. Notably, the azonia-containing polyelectrolytes possessed a strong ROS generation ability and could impressively kill the drug resistant superbug both in vitro and in MRSA-infected mouse. Functional poly(dihalopentadiene)s, on the other hand, could be readily synthesized by boron trihalide-mediated multicomponent polymerization routes in a stereoselective manner. The stereoselectivity of the polymerization was demonstrated to be highly dependent on the employed boron trihalide species and the reaction conditions. The polymerization of diyne, aldehyde and BCl3 that proceeded at 0 oC for 1 h followed by stirring at room temperature for another 1 h afforded poly(dichloropentadiene)s with a predominant (E,Z)-configuration. When diyne and BCl3 were reacted at 45 oC for 1 h prior to further coupling with aldehyde at 0 oC and room temperature, a high molecular weight polymer with the same composition but mainly (Z,Z)-configuration was obtained in a satisfactory yield. Replacement of the mediator from BCl3 to BBr3 also resulted in polymers with a predominant (Z,Z)-1,4-pentadiene unit in a good yield with a high molecular weight. All the obtained polymers showed high refractive indices with low optical dispersion. This made them promise as coating materials in advanced photonic devices. The introduction of tetraphenylethene moiety enabled the polymers to show obvious aggregation-enhanced emission features. The fluorescence of the polymer nanoaggregates in aqueous media could be efficiently quenched by PA with a superamplification effect and a low detection limit, suggesting that they could be used for the sensitive detection of explosives. Last, a facile one-pot multicomponent polymerization route to functional polymers with unique multi-substituted four-membered heterocyclic structures was developed. The strained rings in the polymer main chains enable them to efficiently undergo ring-opening post-modification under simple acidic conditions to transform into new polymers with amide and amidine units. The obtained azetidine-containing polymers showed obvious solid-state luminescence despite of the absence of large π-conjugated structures. Experimental results and theoretical analyses demonstrated that the clustering of heteroatoms and conformational rigidification-induced formation of efficient through-space conjugation played an important role in such an unconventional luminescence phenomenon. Compared with the parent polymers, the ring-opened ones exhibited brighter solid-state emission and better cell staining ability, which could be utilized as lysosome-specific fluorescent probes in biological imaging. Moreover, all the obtained polymers all possessed good film-forming ability, excellent optical transparency, high and tunable refractive indices, small optical aberrations, and good photopatternability, enabling them to serve as advanced materials for applications in a wide area of fields.

16308116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308116.value: Fluorescent polymers have attracted much attention for their potential use in low-cost optoelectronic devices and biological science. Most of the polymers prepared so far show strong light emission in solution but become weakly emissive or even non-fluorescent when aggregated due to strong interactions between the polymer chains. It is important to solve this problem of aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) as fluorescent polymers are commonly used as solid films in their real-world applications. Recently, some propeller- or shell-shaped molecules have been found to show a phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) that is exact opposite of the ACQ effect. Rather than quenching, aggregate formation of these molecules induces intense emission. Thus, the incorporation of such AIE molecules into polymer structures produces macromolecules that not only exhibit AIE characteristics but also have unique properties that are not observed in their low-molecular-weight counterparts. In this proposal, we have developed new synthetic methodologies for the synthesis of AIE polymers. They are, for example (i) polycouplings of dibromoarenes, internal diynes and potassium ferrocyanide to poly(triphenylacrylonitrite)s, (ii) metal-free one-pot A3 polymerizations of terminal diynes, dialdehydes and urea to oxazine-containing polyheterocycles with AIE characteristics, (iii) PdBr2- and CuBr2-catalyzed polymerizations of terminal alkynes to poly(p-arylene dihalodiene)s with AIE characteristics, (iv) palladium-catalyzed oxidative polyannulations of internal alkynes and pyrazoles to poly(indazole)s, etc. These newly developed methods enjoy the advantages of readily available monomers, simple operation, high efficiency, mild reaction conditions, high regio- and stero-selectivity, and high tolerance to functional groups. The obtained polymers are soluble and show high thermal stability, good-filming ability and high refractive index. Such attributes make them to find high-technological applications such as high refractive materials, photopatterning, fluorescent chemosensors, biological probes, etc. The ability of AIE-active, oxazine-containing polyheterocycles to detect food spoilage of shrimps and scallops is promising for further development of portable prototype. Their emission response to pH change enables the monitoring of acid-base homeostasis in cellular compartments, body fluids, and organs of living organisms. The efficient one-pot synthetic methodology to azonia-containing polyelectrolytes provides prominent functional positively charged polyelectrolytes, which are promising candidates for various biomedical applications, such as tissue engineering, surface modification, and self-healing materials. As you can see in part C of this report, 16 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

16308116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308116.value: Polymers with AIE characteristics show strong light emission in the solid state, which make them promise for real-world applications. In this investigation, we have developed new polymerization routes for their synthesis. These methods show several advantages such as readily available monomers, wide monomer scope, simple operation, high efficiency, mild conditions, high tolerance to functional groups, etc. The obtained polymers are soluble and thermally stable. They can form tough films by simple techniques such as spin-coating and their films show high refractive index and strong light emission. These properties making them promising candidates for high-technological applications such as high refractive materials, photopatterning, fluorescent chemosensors and biological probes. Thus, although the project completion date has passed, we are still working on the exploration of new systems. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore further the practical applications of our polymers in various fields.

16308116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308116.value: The development of fluorescent polymers is a hot research topic due to the increasing demand for organic materials for use in low-cost optoelectronic devices. Most of the polymers prepared so far, show weak emission in the solid state, which has prevented their full potential for high-technology applications being realized. Polymers with aggregation-induced emission characteristics, on the contrary, show efficient light emission in the solid state and they are thus more promise for real-world applications. In this investigation, we have developed simple, efficient polymerization routes for their synthesis. All the polymers are obtained in high yields with high molecular weights. They are soluble, film-forming, light refractive and emissive. They exhibit unique materials properties and are potential for use in various fields.

16308216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308216.value: Graphene is the ultimate thin film, comprising one atomic layer of carbon arranged in a honeycomb lattice. When it is placed on top of a silicon wafer that is covered by a thin layer of silica, a voltage applied between the graphene and the silicon wafer—the so-called gate voltage—can alter the electronic property of the graphene in a controllable manner. If a reasonably large magnetic field is applied perpendicular to the graphene, the remarkable phenomenon of the quantum Hall effect (QHE) can be easily observed. The QHE is attributed to the appearance of the conducting edge states under a magnetic field. These conducting edge states always appear when the interior of graphene is insulating, and they display the following special quantum mechanical properties. (1) Electrons can only propagate along one direction at one of the edges, and along the opposite direction at the other edge. Thus the electrons propagating in opposite directions are spatially separated by the insulating interior. Such conducting edge states are called “topological states.” It follows that as electrons in edge states cannot be back-scattered, the resistance must vanish. (2) The Hall voltage, which appears in a direction perpendicular to both the electric and magnetic fields, can become independent of the magnetic field variation when the edge states appear. This contrasts with the conventional case, in which the Hall voltage varies linearly with the magnetic field. Moreover, the values of the Hall voltage plateau, when divided by the electric field, can appear in discrete quantum steps when the magnetic field is varied, with their values expressible in terms of the fundamental constants of nature. Following the discovery of the QHE, another major development was the discovery that some materials display edge states (or surface states when the sample is three dimensional) even without an applied magnetic field. These materials are denoted “topological insulators.” The proposed project will numerically simulate and experimentally fabricate a graphene-metal composite topological insulator, and will verify its predicted properties. Such a two-dimensional composite material can display special quantum mechanical conduction channels, with gate-voltage tunability. The completion of this project can lead to some exciting new directions for exploring quantum composite materials.

16309316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309316.value: The goal of this project is to further develop efficient numerical methods for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) on hypersurfaces. These PDEs arise in various fields in applied science and engineering. Examples include multiphase flow calculations, simulation of Hamiltonian dynamical systems, dimensional reduction of high dimensional data, pattern formulation on surfaces, and etc. In this project, we propose to extend and develop novel and flexible numerical methods for efficient modeling dynamic interfaces and inverting various operators defined on manifolds. We propose to further develop various efficient operations for surface representation. In the first part of the project, we propose to develop a simple numerical method to better conserve the fluid mass in the multiphase flow simulation by incorporating the Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) method into the PI's previous work on the Grid Based Particle Method (GBPM) and a new Cell Based Particle Method (CBPM) for numerical representation of interfaces. In the second part of the project, we propose a novel and simple fully PDE-based embedding approach to solve evolution equations on surfaces. The idea is to introduce an extra advection term with extension velocity perpendicular to the interface. With such term carefully discretized numerically, we are going to demonstrate that this fully PDE-based approach in the embedded space will correctly capture the solution of the evolution equation on the manifold. Such an idea would be flexible enough to be applied to interfaces represented by various methods including the popular level set method or the GBPM/CBPM. Based on these techniques we have developed, we are going to study two important applications. The first one is an implicit algorithm for the principal component analysis (PCA) with a nonlinear constraint. We will also consider a new level set approach for handling constrained Hamiltonian dynamical systems. The outcome of this proposal should provide alternatives to other numerical methods in various applications and should also be important to many disciplines, including crystal growth modeling, surface regularization in image processing and computer graphics, high frequency asymptotic solution to surface wave propagation in seismology and geophysics, multiphase flows with surfactants, and nanostructure design. 這項課題的目的是進一步建立高效的方法去在超曲面上尋找偏微分方程的數值解。這些偏微分方程出現在應用科學和工程學上的很多領域，比如多項流的計算，哈密頓動態系統的模擬，高維數據的維度縮減，曲面上的圖樣形成 (pattern formulation) 等 。 我們想建立和延伸新穎的並且適應性強的數值方法針對高效地對動態界面進行建模和對定義在流形上的多種算子進行逆推等問題 。我們打算進一步建立多種對於曲面表示的高效運算。對於界面的數值表示，PI曾研究過基於網格的粒子法（GBPM）和基於單元的粒子法（CBPM）。在本課題的第一部分，對於模擬多項流，我們想融合流體體積法（VOF）和PI的研究來建立一個簡單的數值方法去更好地使流體的質量守恆。在本課題的第二部分，我們提出一個新的並且簡單的完全基於偏微分方程的嵌入方法去在曲面上解發展方程。我們的想法是引入一項多餘的平流項，使其擴張速度和界面垂直。通過謹慎地對這新引入的一項數值上離散化，我們將證明這個完全基於偏微分方程的方法在嵌入空間將正確地捕獲流形上發展方程的解。這個想法會有足夠強的適應性去被應用在界面的各種表示方法上，包括比較流行的水平集方法 (level set method) 和GBPM、CBPM。基於我們提出的方法，我們將研究兩個重要的應用。第一個是針對有非線性限制的主成分分析（PCA）問題的一個隱式算法。我們還將考慮一個新的水平集方法去解決有限制的哈密頓動態系統。 通過完成這個課題，對於多種實際應用問題的數值方法，我們將提供可替代的選擇。我們的方法對於多個領域也都很重要，包括晶體生長建模，圖像處理和電腦繪圖的曲面正則化，地震學和地球物理學中表面波傳播的高頻率漸進解，附帶表面活性劑的多項流，以及納米結構的設計。

16309316.label: Realisation of objectives
16309316.value: Objective 1 We are developing an efficient, accurate and robust hybrid approach for moving interface problems by combining the cell based particle method (CBPM) with the volume of fluid (VOF) method. The CBPM is an improvement of the recently proposed grid based particle method (GBPM), which uses meshless Lagrangian particles with Eulerian references to represent and track moving interfaces. The meshfree particle approach with Eulerian reference provides simplicity and flexibility for large deformation, adaptivity and topological change while enjoying both the conciseness and the preciseness as a Lagrangian tracking method. By coupling with the VOF method, we can further improve the mass conservation and the topological stability in the CBPM. Objective 2 We proposed a new and simple discretization, named the modified virtual grid difference (MVGD), for numerical approximation of the Laplace-Beltrami (LB) operator on manifolds sampled by point clouds. The key observation is that both the manifold and a function defined on it can both be parametrized in a local Cartesian coordinate system and approximated using least squares. Based on the above observation, we first introduced a local virtual grid with a scale adapted to the sampling density centered at each point. Then we proposed a modified finite difference scheme on the virtual grid to discretize the LB operator. Instead of using the local least squares values on all virtual grid points like the typical finite difference method, we use the function value explicitly at the grid located at the center (coinciding with the data point). The new discretization provides more diagonal dominance to the resulting linear system and improves its conditioning. We have shown that the linear system can be robustly, efficiently and accurately solved by existing fast solver such as the algebraic multigrid (AMG) method. The PI has developed a method for solving partial different equations on evolving surfaces. The method, based on the grid based particle method (GBPM), can naturally resample the surface even under large deformation from the motion law. We introduce a new component in the local reconstruction step of the algorithm and demonstrate numerically that the modification can improve the computational accuracy when large curvature region is developed in the evolution. The method also incorporates a recently developed regularized least squares (RLS) formulation by the PI which can lead to a better conditioned discretized matrix for computing some surface differential operators. The proposed framework can incorporate with a large class of methods and links various approaches for the same problem. In particular, we are going to demonstrate that the so-called local tangential lifting (LTL) method can be naturally applied in our framework, while a recently developed regularized least squares method with RBF can also be used in our method. We have developed an effective interface tracking method to simulate the incompressible Stokes flow with moving interfaces. The Stokes equations are first rewritten into a system of elliptic equations with singular sources which can be efficiently solved by a simple weak formulation. The key idea is to first split the solution into a singular part and a regular part additively. The singular part captures the interface conditions, while the regular part approximates the equations in the whole domain, which can be solved by the standard finite element formulation. We have carefully designed numerical methods to interpolate the velocity to the moving interface. Numerical tests are carried out to demonstrate the accuracy and other properties of our method. Other than all interface problems as mentioned, the PI has also developed different methods for other time-dependent evolution equations. In a recent work, we derive and analyze the alternating direction explicit (ADE) method for time evolution equations with the time-dependent Dirichlet boundary condition and with the zero Neumann boundary condition. The original ADE method is an additive operator splitting (AOS) method, which has been developed for treating a wide range of linear and nonlinear time evolution equations with the zero Dirichlet boundary condition. For linear equations, it has been shown to achieve the second order accuracy in time yet is unconditionally stable for an arbitrary time step size. We also construct numerical methods based on the ADE scheme for two classes of fractional differential equations. More recently, we have developed a novel method for the numerical solution of the two- and three- dimensional elliptic Monge–Ampere equations. Our methodology relies on the combination of a time-discretization by operator-splitting with a mixed finite element based space approximation where one employs the same finite-dimensional spaces to approximate the unknown function and its three second order derivatives. Objective 3 Published with a PhD student and other collaborators, the PI have proposed a variational formulation for dimension reduction on Riemannian manifolds. The algorithm is developed based on the level set method together with a recently developed principal flow algorithm. The original principal flow algorithm is a Lagrangian technique which extends the principal component analysis (PCA) to dimension reduction on Riemannian manifolds. We propose to incorporate the level set method to obtain a fully implicit formulation so that the overall algorithm can naturally handle various topological changes in the curve evolution. The variational formulation consists of two terms which try to balance the contributions from both the dataset itself and the principal direction by the PCA. We have also demonstrated that the method is insensitive to the initial guess and is robust enough for noisy data. Objective 4 In a series of study on coherent structure extraction in dynamical systems, the PI with some of his MPhil students have proposed and analyzed a new class of Eulerian methods for constructing both the forward and the backward flow maps of sufficiently smooth dynamical systems. These methods improve previous Eulerian approaches by solving a Liouville equation so that the computations of the forward flow map can be done on the fly as one imports or measures the velocity field forward in time. Similar to typical Lagrangian or semi-Lagrangian methods, the proposed methods require an interpolation at each step. Having said that, the Eulerian method interpolates d components of the flow maps in the d dimensional space but does not require any (d + 1)-dimensional spatial-temporal interpolation as in the Lagrangian approaches. In all work above, we have assumed that the flow is known without noise. We also propose an Eulerian approach to compute the expected finite time Lyapunov exponent (FTLE) of uncertain flow fields. The definition extends the usual FTLE for deterministic dynamical systems. Instead of performing Monte Carlo simulations as in typical Lagrangian computations, our approach associates each initial flow particle with a probability density function (PDF) which satisfies an advection-diffusion equation known as the Fokker-Planck (FP) equation. More recently, the PI and his student has proposed a simple numerical algorithm to estimate the finite time Lyapunov exponent (FTLE) in dynamical systems from only a sparse number of Lagrangian particle trajectories. The method first reconstructs the flow field using the radial basis function (RBF) and then uses either the Lagrangian or the Eulerian approach to determine the corresponding flow map. We also develop a simple algorithm based on the Schur complement for updating, rather than recomputing, the reconstruction in the RBF when new trajectory data is made available in applications.

16309316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309316.value: Supported by this project, we have published 12 articles in total and have trained one PhD students. We developed various efficient operations for surface representation. In the first part of the project, we have developed a simple numerical method to better conserve the fluid mass in the multiphase flow simulation by incorporating the Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) method into the PI's previous work on the Grid Based Particle Method (GBPM) and a new Cell Based Particle Method (CBPM) for numerical representation of interfaces. In the second part of the project, we developed a novel and simple fully PDE-based embedding approach to solve evolution equations on surfaces. Based on these techniques we have developed, we also studied two important applications. The first one is an implicit algorithm for the principal component analysis (PCA) with a nonlinear constraint. We have also considered a new level set approach for handling constrained Hamiltonian dynamical systems. There are large number of possible extensions and applications of the numerical approaches developed due to the support of this funding.

16309316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309316.value: Dynamic interface problem is still an extremely interesting and important field of research. There are plenty of problems we can continue to work on. For example, this proposal concentrates on numerical approaches to solve elliptic or parabolic type equations on surfaces. It is interesting to see how well these methods can be applied to hyperbolic or higher order nonlinear equations. Special attentions might be needed to impose constraints due to the physical properties of the equation. For example, when solving a hyperbolic equation on surfaces, one might need the ENO/WENO philosophy in the local reconstruction. This could be a possible future research direction.

16309316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309316.value: This project develops and applies efficient numerical methods for solving partial differential equations defined on hypersurfaces. PDEs defined on interfaces or surfaces arise in many fields in science and engineering. Examples include multiphase flow calculations, simulation of Hamiltonian dynamical systems, dimensional reduction of high dimensional data, pattern formulation on surfaces, and etc. In this project, we develop novel and efficient numerical methods for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) defined on dynamic hypersurfaces. The outcome of this proposal provides alternatives to other numerical methods in various applications and should also be important to many disciplines, including crystal growth modeling, surface regularization in image processing and computer graphics, high frequency asymptotic solution to surface wave propagation in seismology and geophysics, multiphase flows with surfactants, and nanostructure design.

16309816.value: 一个大地震可以觸發它的後續地震序列。一個博客可以觸發一些響應的博客，并進一步引發自己的回應博客。首次卒中發作大大增加了未來中風復發的風險。一個 大訂單放置在證券交易所市場可能觸發多個在相同或相反的方向的後續訂單。所有這些現象都有一個共同的特點：事件發生可能影響並產生更多的事件。建模與分析 復發性事件的數據應用在地震學，社會學，醫療科學，金融等領域。它們應用在模擬和預測地震等災難性事件，在神經科學里研究神經传导模式，評估抑制癌症的藥物的療效，腫瘤的復發和預測微博的信息傳播。復發事件通常伴隨著其它信息。例如， 關於地震發生的關鍵信息包括坐標和震中，幅度度量的深度，和地質情況。對未來事件的發生，這些變量的影響分析对完全理解事件聚類的機制相當重要。在這種情況下聚類統計建模一個重要的工具是霍克斯過程或自激過程。在生存分析，有許多基於強度的加法或乘法統計模型，其中考克斯的比例強度模型是使用最廣泛的之一。該項目將重點開發新的統計模型，擴展這些文獻自激動人心的過程，那些復發事件的生存分析。我們開始对第m记忆考克斯型比例強度模型和目標的分析，開拓更廣泛更普遍的和更複雜半參數模型應用程序。聚類現象的正確建模对未來事件發生的預測， 評估外部解釋變量对事件發生率的影響，和理解整個事件的發生機制是很重要的。

16309816.label: Realisation of objectives
16309816.value: Overall, the objectives set out in the project have been achieved and, in fact, more theoretical and practical results are obtained along the lines but in a much bigger scope. 1. Survival analysis. Survival analysis is an area of statistical science that involves analysis of time-to-event data. In this project, we made extensive exploration of the existing models in survival analysis. More notably, we investigated transformation model, which is one of the most popular class of models that includes proportional hazards model (Cox's model) and proportional odds model. We analysed clustered data with transformation model and random effects and obtained robust estimators [1]. For application to cohort data, we invented a sampling design method, called endpoint sampling, which is specially designed to handle censored data. When the error distribution is rather general, we also theoretically proved that the maximum likelihood estimation would still be valid. This problem has been known to be technically notoriously hard. In order to avoid overfitting, we proposed a broken adaptive ridge approach, which is rather innovative and effective, that can be applied to censored data [4]. In the case of censored data, it is called censored brokend adaptive ridge (CBAR). 2. Beyond survival analysis. By exploring the existing models in and outside survival analysis, we are able to invent and apply models beyond survival analysis. For example, the broken adaptive ridge is shown to be a general methodology of regularization that has wide applications [4]. Moreover, the idea can be applied to metric learning in order to achieve dimension reduction [3]. We also solved the fundamental problem of valid estimation for sparse network [2], which can also be viewed as clustered event data. Indeed, this investigation produced much deeper understanding of event series data, and has led to successful applications to the area of adaptive learning and resulted in improved q-learning [5, 6]. In practice, this research has significantly improved the learning efficiency of learners.

16309816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309816.value: Our research in this project can be divided into two parts: within survival analysis and beyond survival analysis. In survival analysis, out task is to explore the existing models or methods and to discover new models and methods on time-to-event data. Our research has been productive and led to four publications. The major findings are: a) A discovery of a robust estimation methods of transformation model when the data is censored and clustered. b) For censored cohort data, a new design to balance the information in censored and non-censored data is sampling according to distance to the endpoint. c) For transformation model with general and unusual error distributions, we prove that the maximum likelihood estimation is still valid. d) For censored data, one can use a tailored made broken adaptive ridge method that we proposed to accomplish regularization. Beyond survival analysis, we also had some new findings: a) For the usual uncensored data, we found a method of regularization, called broken adaptive ridge, is very effective, comparable to the well known LASSO and ridge approach. b) We also found a cross-validation method for metric learning in order to achieve dimension reduction. c) For the paired comparison data, a nearly necessary condition for the validity of the maximum likelihood approach is obtained. d) The exploration of the models also helped us find and apply deep learning models to adaptive learning.

16309816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309816.value: We can further develop some of the methodologies in this project. In survival analysis of censored and clustered cohort data, there are still some interesting problems unsolved. One is the semiparametric efficient efficient estimation for quantile regression models. We hope that our method of developing robust estimation for transformation model can be applied here to obtain optimal or at least suboptimal. We are working along this direction. Endpoint sampling is an intuitive and useful design when censored data are present. Recently we found another approach called "surprise sampling" that aims at balancing the information in imbalanced case and in control data. It has wide applications in classification problems in machine learning. We hope the endpoint sampling and surprise sampling could be combined together and produce useful sampling procedure for censored and imbalanced data. The method in proving the consistency of sparse Bradley Terry model is highly technical. If the comparison is incomplete or missing to some extent, the problem of consistency becomes increasingly difficult. We are continuing on extending the previously working method to this more complicated data type.

16309816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309816.value: Survival analysis deals with time-to-event data. It is most widely used in medical studies, where the event could be disease or cure or death. Modeling the effects on these event occurrence from covariates is a common subject. This project has contributed to model estimation by constructing new and robust estimation and by proving theoretically the commonly used maximum likelihood method works for some popular models. This project also discovered some new cohort sampling design that can be applied in clinical trials. In this project, we also discovered a state of the art regularization method for statistical models. Regularization method is the most useful to avoid overfitting and increase the prediction accuracy. we also found the answer to a very important question: how sparse a network could possibly be without making network nodes incomparable with each other. Our other contributions are in the learning area that could practically increase the learning efficiency of students.

16311516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16311516.value: The recent development of cooling and manipulating alkaline-earth-like atoms provides new possibilities to study unprecedented quantum systems taking advantage of their unique electronic structure. Fermionic alkaline-earth-like atoms, for example, have a long-lived electronic excited state which is commonly used for the precise atomic clock transition and also reveal SU(N) interactions by which inter-atomic scattering is independent of the nuclear spin state. Indeed, the long-lived metastable state atoms together with the ground state atoms give rise to a new kind of fermionic matter in which the electronic orbital degree of freedom plays an important role. Such two-orbital Fermi gas manifests itself as a promising platform to observe the transport property from the Kondo effect and to implement quantum computing. Despite all those promising possibilities of alkaline-earth-like atoms, the tuning of inter-atomic interaction has not been fully available until the very recent finding of the inter-orbital Feshbach resonance. Such tunable inter-orbital atom-atom interactions would become an essential ingredient for the realization of SU(N) Hubbard model in an optical lattice and manifest the crossover physics between the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) superfluid and Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). In this proposed work, we will realize a strongly interacting two-orbital Fermi gas of ytterbium-173 atoms by means of orbital-induced Feshbach resonance. The proposed experimental work in this proposal provides useful guidance for exploring a strongly interacting regime in a two-orbital Fermi gas of ytterbium atoms. The experiments will be carried out with a working apparatus producing a degenerate quantum gas of the ground-state ytterbium-173 atoms. Laser systems, including a clock-transition laser at 578nm, will be developed to address long-lived 3P metastable states. Several experiments are planned including the verification of the orbital-induced Feshbach resonance between two electronic orbitals, the formation of weakly bound two-orbital molecules near the resonance, and the characterization of collisional properties for useful guidance towards two-orbital molecular Bose-Einstein condensation. With our group’s current progress, the proposed work will be completed successfully. Successful completion of this project will further broaden our knowledge of the two-orbital Fermi gas with strong interactions which will provide important insights into the BCS-BEC crossover physics. 类碱土原子冷却和操控技术的最近新发展为研究具有独特电子结构的量子系统提供了更多的可能。费米类碱土原子，比如，因为具有长寿命电子激发态，经常被用于原子钟的研究。另外，因为原子间散射相互作用与原子核自旋态无关，该类原子也可以用于研究SU(N) 相互作用。事实上，因为电子轨道自由度的重要作用，该长寿命亚稳态和基态原子为研究提供了一种新的材料。由于以上的新特性，类似的双轨道费米原子成为进行基于Kondo效应的量子输运性质研究和量子计算应用研究的可靠实验平台。 尽管具有上述优势的应用前景，类碱金属原子间的相互作用却一直以来难以通过实验操控。直到最近，利用新型Feshbach共振技术，该调控才得以实现。该技术的成功直接奠定了双轨道Yb173费米原子在研究光学晶格中的SU(N) Hubbard模型和Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) 超流体到Bose-Einstein (BEC) 凝聚体渡越区行为的核心地位。在此究课题计划中，我们将通过新型的轨道Feshbach共振技术实现对双轨道Yb-173费米气体相互作用的调制，该研究的内容对探索双轨道Yb费米原子间的相互作用规律具有重要的指导意义。 该研究将会在能制备处于量子简并基态的Yb-173费米气体的装置中进行。为了能操Yb173原子能级中的长寿命 亚稳态，我们将建立一套包括一台工作波长是578nm的钟跃迁激光器在内的激光系统。我们计划进行一系列相关的研究工作，包括验证双电子轨道原子之间的轨道Feshbach共振现象，近共振区域弱束缚双轨道分子的形成，为实现双轨道分子BEC而进行的双轨道分子间碰撞性质的探索。根据我们组现有的工作进度，此项研究计划具有高度的现实可行性。该研究工作的成功将会大大加深我们对于双轨道费米气体在强相互作用区域的理解，并且为我们对BCS-BEC渡越区的物理规律提供更多的认知。
