16311516.label: Major findings and research outcome
16311516.value: (1) 2D SU(N) Fermi liquid. We measured collective excitations of a harmonically trapped two-dimensional (2D) SU(N) Fermi gas of Yb atoms. The quadrupole mode frequency decreases with an increasing number of spin components due to the amplification of the interaction effect by N, in agreement with a theoretical prediction based on 2D kinetic equations. The breathing mode frequency, however, is twice the dipole oscillation frequency regardless of N. The evolution of collective excitations was determined in the crossover from two to three dimensions. [Ref.] Phys. Rev. Research Rapid Comm. 2 012028(R) (2020) (2) Bosonization in a 3D SU(N) Fermi liquid. Whereas textbooks of quantum mechanics have introduced bosons and fermions to us as distinct particles with drastically different properties, modern developments in condensed matter physics and high energy physics have suggested that the boundary between bosons and fermions can, in fact, be blurred. Recently, we performed quantum simulation with multi-component fermions in 3D [57]. We demonstrated a generic approach both in experiment and theory to test bosonization in a multi-component 3D fermionic system based on the so-called contact, the central quantity governing all thermodynamic quantities of dilute quantum gases ranging from energy to pressure. [Ref.] Song et al., Physical Review X 10 041052 (2020) (3) Thermodynamic study using machine learning We also measured density fluctuations, and revealed SU(N)-dependent thermodynamic compressibility with tunable N with possible connections. In this study, machine learning was adopted to guide our analysis. Zhao et all, Under review. arXiv:2006:14142 (2020) (4) Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) band for ultracold fermions We realized a new type of SPT phase in an optical lattice with spin orbit coupling. The observed SPT phase is beyond the traditional understanding, and was the first time for the experimental observation of a SPT phase for ultracold atom, and our work highlights the remarkable capabilities to realize and explore new topological states for ultracold atoms beyond natural conditions. [Ref.] Science Advances 4, eaao4748 (2018) (5) 3D nodal line semimetal for ultracold atoms We realized, for the first time, the 3D topological band for ultracold atoms. Our work breaks through the experimental complexity allowing the researchers to create and probe 3D topological bands. In our work, we realized a 3D topological semimetal with nodal lines by implementing 2D SO coupling in optical lattices (within the x-y plane) together with a 1D linear SO coupling (along the z direction). [Ref.] Nature Physics 15 911-916 (2019)

16311516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16311516.value: Following up the developments made in the projects, we will implement a magic wavelength lattice trap for the quantitative characterization of the two-orbital system.. This will allow us to leverage our expertise in the study of high spin SU(N) symmetry in both the ground and excited manifolds of ytterbium atoms. We are now in the process of developing such trapping potentials in the system, and expect to try out the experimental measurement accordingly. As an immediate follow-up experiment, we envision characterizing collective excitations in a two-orbital system.

16311516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16311516.value: In this project, we aimed at creating complex quantum matter that is not easily available in nature. For this goal, we used ultracold atoms, prepared near the absolute zero temperature in an atomic quantum simulator, and investigated novel properties induced by atom-atom interactions, large spin and non-trivial topology. Owing to the unprecedented controllability of ultracold atoms, our experimental studied have allowed the researchers to gain a better understanding of complex quantum systems. This project is forward-looking and exploratory, but highlights the full benefits of quantum simulation with ultracold atoms.

16311616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16311616.value: Privileged chiral molecules, known to be versatile for multiple purposes (typically coined for chiral ligands/catalysts in asymmetric reactions), are invisibly influencing our everyday life. For example, many of the pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and materials are chiral, and their manufacturing processes may involve the use of privileged chiral catalysts/ligands. As a result, the efficient synthesis of these privileged chiral structures are of great significance. Recent advances in organocatalysis have provided new tools and concepts that can be employed to approach some of the previously less-explored or challenging topics. Here we propose to employ chiral Brønsted acid catalysis to address challenges in three subareas, including the unprecedented catalytic asymmetric synthesis of the privileged SPINOL and its derivatives as well as the designed spirocyclic structures based on the SPINOL chemistry, and the unprecedented Piancatelli rearrangement and its variants. The realization of these catalytic symmetric processes will not only represent fundamental advances in asymmetric control of the previously challenging reactions, but also provide potential applications, such as biomass conversion, chiral drug development, and other important aspects of human life. 特權手性分子，即通用於多種用途的手性分子（一般為手性配體或不對稱催化劑），正在間接地影響著我們的日常生活。例如，許多藥物、農用化學品和材料是手性的，並且它們的製造工藝往往使用特權的手性催化劑/配體。因此，這些特權手性結構的有效合成具有重要意義。最近，有機分子催化的發展為不對稱合成中具有挑戰性的主題提供了新的工具和概念。這裡我們提出採用手性布朗斯特酸催化實現三個子課題，包括特權SPINOL及其衍生物的新型不對稱合成、基於SPINOL化學的螺旋結構設計和合成、以及不對稱Piancatelli重排反應。這些催化對稱過程將不僅實現先前挑戰性不對稱反應的理論新方案、而且還將具備潛在的應用價值，如生物物質的轉化、手性藥物的開發等人類生活的其他重要方面。

16311616.label: Realisation of objectives
16311616.value: In this project, a range of important catalytic processes have been achieved for the synthesis of chiral privileged molecules. In particular, we have made pioneering contribution to the catalytic asymmetric reactions of quinone methide and aza-quinone methides. The new reaction design has been followed by various research groups in the world to access other important chiral building blocks. The objectives of this proposal have been realized as expected. (1) We have developed a range of new asymmetric reactions of quinone methide and aza-quinone methides for the synthesis of a wide range of diaryl alkanes with benzylic chiral centers. With chiral Bronsted acid catalysis, these reactions all led to highly enanthioenriched useful chiral building blocks. These are privileged molecules with broad applications in medicinal chemistry. (2) We also realized an asymmetric strategy for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral 1,1'-spirobiindane-7,7'-diol (SPINOL). With chiral phosphoric acid catalysis, good to high enantioselectivity could be achieved. (3) We have developed a new catalytic approach for the asymmetric Piancatelli rearrangement from furan 2-carbinol starting materials using chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. Highly enantioenriched amino cyclopentenones were obtained via this approach.

16311616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16311616.value: In this project, we have developed the following new organocatalytic processes leading to the synthesis of useful chiral privileged molecules. (1) We achieved the first catalytic asymmetric reaction of aza-para-quinone methides. (2) We developed an enantioselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition of o-quinone methides and vinyl sulfides for indirect access to generally substituted chiral chromanes. (3) We developed an organocatalytic synthesis of chiral tetrasubstituted allenes from racemic propargylic alcohols via 1,8-conjugate addition to para-quinone methides. (4) In our effort to develop organocatalytic synthesis of chiral diarylmethyl alkynes, we demonstrated a rare example of improving synthetic procedure by understanding the role of additive. (5) We developed the first catalytic enantioselective desymmetrization of azetidiniums. (6) We developed the first organocatalytic approach for direct conversion of racemic diarylmethanols to valuable chiral diarylmethylamines. (7) we developed a new organocatalytic addition of azlactones to quinone methides for the efficient synthesis of chiral β,β-diaryl-α-amino acid derivatives. (8) We have developed the first general trifluoromethylation at the γ position of carbonyl compounds by NHC-catalysis. (9) We have developed the first catalytic asymmetric functionalization of unactivated benzylic C(sp3‒H) bonds of indoles. (10) We developed a catalytic enantioconvergent House‒Meinwald rearrangement for the synthesis of both cyclic and acyclic ketones bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. (11) A highly efficient enantioconvergent asymmetric 1,8-addition of aza-para-QMs has been developed. (12) A highly efficient synthesis of hydrodibenzofurans has been developed, which is a new addition to the small family of general strategies available for this useful target.

16311616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16311616.value: As an extension of this project, the development of additional useful organocatalytic asymmetric processes will continue to be our topic of pursuit in this area. In particular, we will continue to expand the utility of chiral Bronsted acids in asymmetric catalysis for the synthesis of other privileged chiral molecules. Our effort in asymmetric strained ring opening, such as oxetanes and azetidines, and the asymmetric addition of quinone methides will still be a topic for further research.

16311616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16311616.value: In this project, we have discovered a range of new organic processes with excellent efficiency and selectivity. These processes utilized organocatalysts that do not involve metals, which are environmentally friendly. These reactions provide new approaches to build intermediates for the synthesis of chiral drugs and functional materials. These findings will contribute to the advances in drug discovery and environmental protection.

16311716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16311716.value: Alotaketals A-C and phorbaketals A-K are structurally related, biologically active marine natural products. Alotaketals A-C have been found to activate the cAMP cell signaling pathway, while phorbaketals A-C are cytotoxic against human colorectal, hepatoma, and lung cancer cell lines. Although they are from different marine sponges with different bioactivities, alotaketals and phorbaketals share a structurally unprecedented tricyclic spiroketal framework, which is very challenging to synthesize. This is evidenced by the fact that only total synthesis of alotaketal A has been achieved by two research groups using a nearly identical synthetic strategy, which suffers from low efficiency in the key coupling step and an inability to access structurally related natural products. This proposal describes the development of a new synthetic strategy that is amenable to the collective total synthesis of alotaketals A-C and phorbaketals A-C and H-K from a common tricyclic spiroketal intermediate. This new strategy features i) the invention of a new cascade cyclization to construct the key tricyclic spiroketal framework and ii) late stage C-H functionalization of the complex tricyclic spiroketal framework. The feasibility of these two key transformations has been verified by our preliminary studies on a model compound, particularly with the support of single crystal X-ray crystallography of the products produced by these two key transformations. The synthesis of the model compound has been accomplished in only six steps from commercially available materials and an unexpected racemization problem that emerged and was solved by critical mechanistic analysis. These successful model studies coupled with some exciting new chemistry findings prompt us to further explore the synthetic applications and limitations of this new cascade cyclization strategy. Therefore, we propose a two-stage study: i) methodology development such as further optimization of the cascade cyclization and expansion of the substrate scope and ii) collective total synthesis of the alotaketals and phorbaketals. In the latter case, a common tricyclic spiroketal intermediate is rationally designed and synthesized by two plausible synthetic routes to ensure its availability. Subsequently, the collective syntheses of alotaketals A-C and phorbaketals A-C and H-K are conceived within 10 steps from this common intermediate by fully exploiting classic organic reactions such as Dess-Martin oxidation, Wittig olefination, and Mitsunobu reaction. The last section of this proposal focuses on i) a study of biogenetic relations of alotaketals and phorbaketals (and within phorbaketals) by exploring their chemical interconversions and ii) an evaluation of the biological activity of all synthetic alotaketals and phorbaketals. Alotaketals A-C 和 phorbaketals A K 是結構上相關的、 具有生物活性的海洋天然產物。Alotaketals A-C已經被發現可以激活的cAMP的細胞信號傳導途徑，而phorbaketals A-C是具有針對人結腸直腸癌，肝癌和肺癌細胞系的細胞毒性。雖然alotaketals和phorbaketals是從不同海綿分离得到且具有不同的生物活性，但是，它們結構上具有前所未有的相同的三環螺縮酮框架，這在化学合成上是非常具有挑戰性的。目前，兩個研究小組通過使用幾乎相同的合成策略完成alotaketal A的全合成事實也證明合成的难度：其中关鍵聯的偶联效率低且無法应用于結構相關的天然產物的全合成。此提案描述了發展一種新的合成策略从而能從一個共同的三環螺縮酮中間體對alotaketals A-C和phorbaketals A-C和H-K實現集體全合成。這個新的策略具有以下兩個重要的特點：一）發明一種新的串聯環化反應來構造複雜的三環螺縮酮框架；二）後期C-H官能化。這兩種關鍵反應的可行性已經在模型化合物得到初步驗證。單晶X射線準確無誤的證明這兩個關鍵反應的產物結構。模型化合物的合成只需六步合成而且也解決了令人意想不到的消旋問題。這些令人興奮的新化學發現和成功的模型研究促使我們進一步探索這種新的串聯環化反應的綜合應用以及其極限。因此，我們提出了一個兩階段研究方案：一）發展方法學，如串聯環化反應的進一步優化和底物普適性的擴展，二）alotaketals和phorbaketals的集體全合成。其中在全合成方面，我們合理設計了兩種可能的合成路線以保證合成共同的中間三環螺縮酮。隨後，我們將充分利用經典的有機合成反應例如Dess-Martin 氧化，如戴斯 - 馬丁，Wittig烯烴化，Mitsunobu反應等等對共同的中間體進行轉換，希望在10步之內以達成對alotaketals A-C和phorbaketals A-C和H-K集體合成。此提案的最後一節將研究：—）此類天然產物的化學互變及生源合成的關係，二）對所有合成的alotaketals和phorbaketals進行生物活性的測試評價。

16311716.label: Realisation of objectives
16311716.value: Objective 1: We have developed a novel and efficient cascade cyclization for the asymmetric synthesis of the key tricyclic spiroketal framework present in alotaketals and phorbaketals. This cascade involves TfOH-promoted cyclization of vinyl epoxy δ-ketoalcohol (VEKA) to afford the spiroketal core in 80% yield, which structures were confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis. This cascade laid the groundwork for our adventure of total synthesis. Objective 2: We have developed a flexible and robust synthetic route to the common intermediate for the asymmetric synthesis of alotaketals and phorbaketals. On the basis of our newly-established cascade cyclization for the synthesis of tricyclic spiroketals (Objective 1), we explored the cascade cyclization of fully functionalized (two hydroxyl groups designed for the total synthesis) vinyl epoxy δ-ketoalcohol (VEKA) and achieved the spiroketal with 56% yield in a gram scale. The molecular structure of this cyclization product was also confirmed by X-ray diffraction analysis of the single crystal. This fully functionalized common intermediate could be obtained with 4.5 g in 13 steps from commercially available materials. Objective 3: We have achieved the unified asymmetric total syntheses of alotaketals A-D in about 30 steps in a collective way for the first time. The key features of the strategy included (i) a new cascade cyclization of vinyl epoxy δ-ketoalcohol (VEKA) to forge the common tricyclic spiroketal intermediates, (ii) a late-stage allylic C-H oxidation, and (iii) olefin cross metathesis to install the different side chains. This synthetic work was published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (2017). Objective 4: We have achieved the asymmetric total syntheses of phorbaketal A in about 30 steps in a collective way for the first time. The key features of the strategy included (i) a new cascade cyclization of vinyl epoxy δ-ketoalcohol (VEKA) to forge the common tricyclic spiroketal intermediates, (ii) a late-stage allylic C-H oxidation, and (iii) olefin cross metathesis to install the different side chains. This synthetic work was published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (2017). We also achieved the synthesis of phorbaketals B and C but encountered an unexpected difficulty in purifying the final products. This was the reason why we did not include these two natural products in the paper. Objective 5: We have achieved the first, asymmetric total syntheses of ansellones A and B, and phorbadione in 16-23 steps from sclareolide. Ansellane-type sesterterpenoids including ansellone A-G and phorbadione are structurally and biogenetically related to phorbaketals with anticancer and anti-HIV activity. Our synthesis features the first regioselective cyclization of vinyl epoxides with internal alcohol nucleophiles in a 1,4-addition manner, which resembles our newly-established cascade cyclization of VEKA (Objective 1). Additionally, the allylic C-H oxidation was exploited at a late stage of the synthesis. This work was published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (2017).

16311716.label: Major findings and research outcome
16311716.value: This project (Synthetic Studies of Alotaketals and Phorbaketals) led to many exciting findings in synthetic methodology development and total synthesis of natural products, which are summarized below. (1) Alotaketals and phorbaketals: Alotaketals and phorbaketals are structurally related, biologically active marine natural products. Alotaketals A-C have been found to activate the cAMP cell signaling pathway, while phorbaketals A-C are cytotoxic against human colorectal, hepatoma, and lung cancer cell lines. The previous synthetic efforts led to total synthesis of alotaketal A, which suffers from low efficiency in the key coupling step and an inability to access structurally related natural products. The major findings of this project include (i) the development of a new efficient strategy that is amenable to the collective total synthesis of alotaketals and phorbaketals from a common tricyclic spiroketal intermediate, and (ii) the development of a new cascade cyclization (of VEKAs) that might find application in organic synthesis. The key findings were published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017, 56, 9096. (2) Ansellones: Ansellones are structurally related to alotaketals and phorbaketals but exhibits different biological activity. There are no synthetic endeavors reported for these structurally intriguing molecules, although further SAR-driven (SAR=structure–activity relationship) improvements in the therapeutic index and pharmacological properties by chemical modifications and/or supply of the rare materials for biological activity testing call for chemical synthesis. As one of the major achievements of this project, we accomplished the first, asymmetric total syntheses of three representative ansellane members: ansellone A, ansellone B, and phorbadione. In addition, the strategy highlights the employment of Barbier-type reaction of carvone-derived triene iodide, and the first regioselective cyclization (6-exo-trig and 8-exo-trig) of alcohol-tethered vinyl epoxides in a 1,4-addition manner. This finding was published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017, 56, 4787. (3) Inspired and supported by this project, we have explored and achieved several green oxidation protocols (Green Chem. 2019, 21, 64; Org. Lett. 2019, 21, 315; Nat. Comm. 2019, 10: 4754; , function-oriented transformations of (aza-)Achmatowicz rearrangement (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 458; J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 6663) and total synthesis of siladenoserinols (Org. Lett. 2019, 21, 9704).

16311716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16311716.value: The potential for further development of the research is identification of an anti-cancer drug lead from the library of synthesized natural products and analogues, which requires a large scaled total synthesis to supply materials of natural products and analogues for biological activity studies. These subsequent activities are more “applied” in nature and lack novelty for further financial support (funding) from government funding agency. Since this project funding has been used up, we have to stop the synthetic work temporarily. In the future, we will seek for financial support to further improve the chemical synthesis of alotaketals and phorbaketals and study the biological activity.

16311716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16311716.value: Natural products are the main source of new drugs for all types of diseases and the major obstacle of translating a natural product into a new drug is the scarce of the natural product. This research project is to solve the supply problem of some natural products by developing new and efficient chemical synthesis. On the basis of our preliminary study, we have developed a new, efficient synthetic strategy that allows for the collective total synthesis of bioactive alotaketals, phorbaketals, and ansellones. One of the key findings is the development of a new cascade cyclization that leads to the complex tricyclic framework common to this family of natural products. Now, a viable and sustainable supply of this family of marine natural products and their analogues can be secured by chemical synthesis, laying the critical groundwork for further biological studies and allowing us to study the structure-activity relationship (SAR).

16312116.label: Project Objectives
16312116.value: To improve the methodology for disentangling different Higgs boson production modes in ATLAS. Focus on the separation of gluon-fusion, vector boson fusion and associated production contributions accessible with the LHC Run-II dataset. To identify observables allowing for such separation both in SM and BSM cases. To develop and implement new methodology for measuring the tensor structure of Higgs couplings to bosons and fermions. Focus on development of the Effective Field Theory-based Monte Carlo framework that allows to model the effects of simultaneous presence of several BSM contributions in the Higgs boson production and decay processes. To identify physics observables for disentangling various BSM contributions to Higgs decays. To perform a comparative study of available techniques to combine such observables into BSM-sensitive discriminants: machine learning, Optimal Observables etc. To perform the experimental studies of the structure of Higgs boson interaction with fermions and bosons using the dataset accumulated by the ATLAS experiment until the end of 2018. To produce limits on the corresponding BSM contributions.

16312116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16312116.value: In July 2012 the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) announced the discovery of a new neutral particle. Both experiments have recently completed studies of new particle’s properties using the data obtained during the Run-I of the LHC. The measured production and decay mechanisms, main quantum numbers and couplings to other known elementary particles were found to be consistent with the Higgs boson as predicted by the theoretical framework known as the Standard Model (SM). The precision of these measurements will be improved during the high-intensity Run-II of the LHC, which started in Spring 2015. The priority for the coming years will remain to study the exact nature of the newly discovered particle, in particular its interactions with other SM particles. These studies will provide insights about the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking which is responsible for generating the masses of the elementary particles. Potential observation of deviations from the SM predictions will provide information about the nature of new physics beyond the SM (BSM). This project addresses one of the most important aspects of characterizing the new particles: searches for BSM contributions through its interactions with other elementary particles, namely fermions, elementary building blocks of matter, and vector bosons responsible for electroweak interactions. This project also builds a solid foundation to develop physics program for future high-energy accelerators, such as the Chinese electron-positron collider initiative. The ATLAS group of the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong (JCFP) is formed by members of CUHK, HKU and HKUST. Over the last year, the members of this group have made a significant contribution to the analysis of the LHC Run-I data, development of methodology for the new studies during the LHC run-II, to the upgrade of the ATLAS detector and to the development of its reconstruction software. Building on the success of the Hong Kong JCFP ATLAS project, we propose to enhance this effort by expanding the HKUST experimental particle physics group. To strengthen the HKUST contribution to ATLAS and to the study of future particle accelerators, one additional Senior Research Assistant and one Research Postgraduate Student positions will be created. The primary goals of the expanded HKUST group will be to make central contributions to the study of the Higgs boson properties along with other JCFP members and some international ATLAS collaborators, and to determine the corresponding sensitivities for the future colliders. 在二零一二年，大型強子對撞機(LHC)的超環型儀器實驗(ATLAS)和緊湊緲子線圈實驗(CMS)宣佈發現了新的中性粒子。利用LHC於第一階段(Run - I)收集到的數據，兩個實驗的研究團隊均完成了此粒子的性質研究。經測量所得的產生和衰變機制、主要量子數和與其他已知基本粒子的耦合均與標準模型(SM) 內所預測的希格斯玻色子吻合。於二零一五年第一季開始，LHC開始了高強度的第二階段(Run - II)對撞，令這些測量的精確度將有所提高。 在未來數年，最首要的研究將仍是這新粒子的準確性質，特別是此粒子與其他SM粒子的相互作用。這些研究將為負責產生大多數基本粒子質量的電弱對稱性破缺機制帶來新的啟示。在測量中得到和標準模型預測數值的任何偏差將有機會為超越標準模型的新物理(BSM) 帶來更多資料。此項目涉及這新粒子的其中一個最重要的表徵：從此粒子和其他基本粒子，即費米子，物質的基本構成粒子，以及矢量玻色子，負責電弱相互作用的粒子，兩種基本粒子的相互作用尋找BSM的供獻。同時，此項目亦為未來的高能加速器，如中國的正負電子對撞機(CEPC)的物理計劃建立了堅固的基礎。 加入ATLAS 的香港基礎物理聯合研究中心 (Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong) 由來自香港中文大學、香港大學以及香港科技大學的成員所組成。在過去的一年，這團隊成員在LHC第一階段數據分析、有關第二階段的新學術研究方法、以至ATLAS的升級和重建軟件等各方面均作出了重大供獻。 有見於JCFP 項目的成功，我們希望透過擴充香港科技大學粒子物理學實驗組提高此方面的工作。為增加香港科技大學對ATLAS 的以及未來的粒子加速器的供獻，我們將增加一個高級研究助理以及一個研究生職位。這次研究組擴充的主要目標為與其他JCFP 成員和ATLAS國際合作者一起為希格斯玻色子的性質作主要供獻，以及測定未來的對撞機的靈敏度。

16312116.label: Realisation of objectives
16312116.value: All the objectives related to this project were realised at 100% or nearly. The methodology to disentangle different Higgs production mechanisms was studied using several different machine learning approaches. The methodology presently used by the HZZ group in ATLAS was improved towards the better separation between the gluon fusion and vector boson fusion production. The different Effective Field Theory approaches to study BSM contributions to the Higgs boson production and decay were tried. A particular attention was payed to the so-called Higgs basis. Its comparison to the SM EFT and similar approaches was carried out at the Monte Carlo level. By agreement with the other Higgs study groups in ATLAS, the SM EFT was chosen as the framework to be used for parametrisation of further studies and for eventual combinations with other channels. The Monte Carlo production scheme for SM EFT in the HZZ channel was developed. The observables related to the effects produced by the BSM operators of the SM EFT were identified for two branches of the analysis: the search for BSM operators and dedicated search for the CP-violation in the Higgs sector. The Optimal Observables technique was chosen for the CP-violation branch of the analysis. For the BSM operators branch of the analysis, the observables sensitive to the individual operators were identified. Taking the existing Simplified Template Cross Section as the base, additional bins sensitive to BSM effects were introduced and their sensitivity demonstrated. The analysis framework is generally prepared to be applied on data. An intermediate publication, featuring the measurement based on Simplified Template Cross Sections was made. The Monte Carlo production for the final analysis is currently on-going. The application of the analysis on data, based on new SM EFT Monte-Carlo will take 2-3 months. After that, the final publication will be prepared and submitted to a refereed journal. The remaining part of the work is purely technical, it only concerns the application of developed strategies on the existing dataset. The project in terms of defined objectives should then be considered as complete.

16312116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16312116.value: The performed research allowed to introduce a new generation of searches for the BSM effects in the Higgs sector to be performed at the LHC. Initially based on the Simplified Template Cross Section binning schema, these analyses extend it towards dedicated fits of individual BSM operators. As result, our approach appears to be more precise and more sensitive. The final publication summarising our findings should follow within next year. Several oral and poster presentations on topical meetings and conferences were already done. The analysis is to be still applied on data, which may take next 2-3 months. It is now clear that the results to be obtained will provide better limits on the BSM operators that in the recent paper on the STXS measurements cited in Section C. While awaiting for the final publication to be ready, the group has participated in preparation in several journal publications of the HZZ group, which are mentioned in the Section C. These can be regarded as steps towards the final publication, which is now in progress. In each of these publications, the RGC support was acknowledged according to the rules of the ATLAS collaboration: through the general list of sponsors. During this project one PhD thesis (H.Lu, CUHK) was defended under my supervision. Three additional students from CUHK and HKUST are currently preparing their thesis write-up. The MPhil student N.Tz have left the programme for personal reasons.

16312116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16312116.value: The analysis performed will be the final analysis of the data obtained by ATLAS during the Run 2 of the LHC in the HZZ channel. The first important development will be the combination of obtained results with other channels, such as Hgamma gamma and HWW. At the later stages, it might be interesting to come back to the idea of the Higgs basis parametrisation of the BSM effects. After the restart of the LHC, the data of the Run-3 of the LHC will allow to enhance the searches or to improve the obtained limits by the factor 1.5 at least. At the end of the LHC programme, the combined result between all sensitive channels and also between ATLAS and CMS should be prepared. The corresponding publication will be the last available information on the subject before the start of the High-Luminosity LHC programme later in this decade.

16312116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16312116.value: The methodology developed in this project allows to improve sensitivity in searches for new physics. In particular, we are looking for the effects not predicted by the currently established theory of particle interactions, the Standard Model. Such effects may help us to explain why the Universe around us is mostly composed of the ordinary matter and why the matter-antimatter balance was broken at some early stage of its existence. The last part of the project - the application of developed analysis methodology on the experimental data is currently on-going. The results will be published within a year and will bring us one step forward in our understanding of basic structure of our Universe.

16312216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16312216.value: Carbon cathode based hybrid organic/inorganic perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) have a great potential for commercialization due to the low-cost and solution-based materials and processes used for their fabrication as well as their good stability. One of the distinctive features of C-PSCs is the direct C/perovskite contact without using any hole transport materials (HTM) thanks to the unique ambipolar property of the perovskite. However, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of our simplest C-PSCs is still relatively low at present (< 12 %). There are several issues that limit the performance of C-PSCs needing to be addressed, which motivates the submission of this proposal. The first is the interface of C/perovskite, which needs to both electrically and mechanically robust. Second, the quality of the perovskite layer needs to be ensured for fast electron and hole transport with minimal recombination. The commonly used mesoporous carbon made of carbon black nanoparticles has very weak mechanical property, and tends to crack and peel off during the chemical conversion process. On the other hand, the chemical conversion in the MAI solution using the relatively high polar isopropanol (IPA) solvent induced the Ostwald ripening process to generate large perovskite crystals, which loosened the perovskite layer and worsened the interface contact. To tackle these problems, we propose to design and prepare physically stable mesoporous carbon electrodes with high electronic conductivity and network-forming property by exploiting the low-dimensionality of some carbon nanomaterials such as carbon nanotubes and their composites. The chemical embedment technique we developed previously will be used to covert the PbI2 film underlying the carbon electrode to guarantee the interfacial contact with the finally transformed perovskite layer, leading to enhanced hole extraction and final charge collection. In parallel, we will exploit a new solvent engineering strategy to suppress the Ostwald ripening process during the chemical conversion of the PbI2 layer, which aims to produce a compact perovskite layer that can seamlessly interface with the mesoporous carbon electrode and further improve the hole extraction at the carbon/perovskite interface. The effects of carbon nanostructure and perovskite crystallization on the formation of and hole extraction through the carbon/perovskite interface will systematically studied. This project will provide important insight at the nanometer scale into the relationship of the carbon electrode structure, the perovskite layer quality, the carbon-perovskite interfacial hole-extraction dynamics and the overall photovoltaic performance of the C-PSCs. Such insight will significantly promote the commercialization of C-PSCs. 碳基有機/無機雜化鈣鈦礦太陽能電池（碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池），由於其低成本、溶液法製備和高穩定性，具有巨大的商業化潛力。基於鈣鈦礦獨特的雙極性特性，碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的顯著特點之一是採用直接的碳/鈣鈦礦介面接觸而不使用任何昂貴的空穴傳輸材料。然而，目前製備的碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的光電轉換效率仍然相對較低（< 12%）。因此，我們提交的這個方案致力於解決限制碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池性能的一系列問題。首先是要求具有電學性能和機械性能穩定的碳/鈣鈦礦介面。其次是保證高品質的鈣鈦礦層，從而實現快速的電子和空穴的傳輸和極小的電荷複合。目前常用的由炭黑納米粒子組成的多孔碳膜具有非常弱的機械性能，容易在化學轉化過程中發生破裂和脫落。另一方面，在碘化鉀胺溶液中進行化學轉化時使用極性相對高的異丙醇作為溶劑，容易引起奧斯特瓦爾德熟化效應並形成大的鈣鈦礦晶體，大的晶體將破壞碳材料和鈣鈦礦之間的介面接觸。 為了解決這些問題，我們提出設計並製備具有高導電性和網路成膜特性的物理性能穩定的多孔碳電極，如採用低維碳納米管及其複合材料。我們先前開發的化學包埋技術將被用於轉化位於碳電極之下的碘化鉛膜，以保證碳材料和最終轉化的鈣鈦礦層之間形成有效的介面接觸，從而提高空穴的提取和電荷的收集。與此同時，我們將採用一種新的溶劑技術抑制碘化鉛化學轉化過程中的奧斯特瓦爾德熟化效應，致力於形成可與多孔碳電極形成緊密介面的緻密的鈣鈦礦層，並進一步改善碳/鈣鈦礦介面的空穴提取。我們將會系統研究碳材料的納米結構和鈣鈦礦的結晶性對碳/鈣鈦礦介面的形成及空穴提取的影響。該課題將會在納米尺度上對碳電極結構、鈣鈦礦晶體品質、碳/鈣鈦礦介面空穴提取動力學以及碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的整體光電性能之間的關係提供重要的思路。這些思路將會顯著地促進碳基鈣鈦礦太陽能電池的商業化。

16312216.label: Realisation of objectives
16312216.value: (1) Polyethyleneimine-functionalized carbon nanotubes as an interlayer to bridge perovskite/carbon for all inorganic carbon-based perovskite solar cells All inorganic perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted tremendous attention because of their intrinsic structural stability, but they suffer from uncompetitive efficiency, especially the carbon electrode-based PSCs (C-PSCs), wherein the insufficient perovskite/carbon contact and interfacial recombination are of particular concern. To address these problems, we designed and fabricated a polyethyleneimine-functionalized carbon nanotube (PEI/CNT) interlayer and used it as a bifunctional bridge in all inorganic CsPbI3 based C-PSCs. This functionalized PEI/CNT bridge connects the perovskite layer and the carbon electrode to improve the quality of the perovskite/carbon interface and also works as an interfacial passivation layer due to the coordination ability of the anchored PEI molecules on CNTs. Systematic investigations revealed that the interfacial charge transfer resistance was reduced, and surface trap states in the perovskite film were passivated. This effort led to a remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 10.55% with a high fill factor (FF) of 0.71 for the all inorganic C-PSCs. By contrast, those without the PEI/CNT bridge only attained a PCE of 7.41% and FF of 0.56. Moreover, non-encapsulated PEI/CNT based devices also showed higher stability under high humidity or high temperature conditions. Therefore, the PEI/CNT interface bridging strategy has the potential to achieve high efficiency and high stability for the all inorganic C-PSCs. (2) HxMoO3−y nanobelts: an excellent alternative to carbon electrodes for high performance mesoscopic perovskite solar cells Carbon-based hole-conductor-free perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) are considered as a promising photovoltaic technology toward commercialization, owing to their low cost and superior stability. However, efforts to further improve their efficiency have been hampered by the hole-extraction barrier at the Schottky contact between carbon and the perovskite. A conventional approach to resolve this issue is incorporating a hole-transport material (HTM) into the mesoscopic skeleton or chemical modification of the carbon electrode. Here, we show an innovative strategy that uses solution-processed hydrogen molybdenum bronze (HxMoO3−y) nanobelts, an n-type HTM with high work function and electrical conductivity, as the sole electrode material to enhance the hole-extraction process and realize efficient PSCs for the first time. The mesoscopic cell configuration of FTO/c-TiO2/m-TiO2/m-Al2O3/HxMoO3−y with perovskite infiltration delivered a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.5%, which compares favorably with 13.3% of typical high temperature C-PSCs. This increase in cell efficiency stems primarily from the enhancement in open circuit voltage and short circuit current, which is due to the HxMoO3−y electrode with more favorable energy alignment and higher hole-extraction ability than the carbon electrode. These results show the potential of HxMoO3−y nanobelts as an efficient electrode for realizing high-performance mesoscopic PSCs. (3) An Ultrathin Ferroelectric Perovskite Oxide Layer for High‐Performance Hole Transport Material Free Carbon Based Halide Perovskite Solar Cells The hole transport material (HTM) free carbon based perovskite solar cells (C‐PSCs) are promising for its manufactural simplicity, but they currently suffer from low power conversion efficiencies (PCE) largely because of the voltage loss. Here, a new strategy to increase the PCE by incorporating an ultrathin ferroelectric oxide PbTiO3 layer between the electron transport material and the halide perovskite is reported. The resulting C‐PSCs have achieved PCEs up to 16.37%, which is the highest record for HTM‐free C‐PSCs to date, mainly ascribable to the ferroelectric layer enhanced open circuit voltage. Detail measurements and analysis show an enhanced built‐in potential in the C‐PSCs as well as suppression of the non‐radiative recombination due to the ferroelectric PbTiO3 layer incorporation, accounting for the boosted V OC and photovoltaic performance. (4) Excess Cesium Iodide Induces Spinodal Decomposition of CsPbI2Br Perovskite Films We report an exploratory study on the crystal formation behavior of CsPbI2Br perovskite films by adding excess cesium iodide (CsI). Surprisingly, facile co-crystallization of CsI and CsPbI2Br in the form of spinodal decomposition is observed. Significantly, the two phases spontaneously form morphing into a remarkably uniform bicontinuous nanoscale blend with high orientational correlation through the well-matched (110) plane of CsI and the (200) plane of CsPbI2Br. The CsPbI2Br films produced by the spinodal decomposition method not only enjoy a compact surface, low defect concentration, and long carrier lifetimes, they also retain their excellent charge transport property. By employing such a CsPbI2Br film for carbon-based perovskite solar cells, power conversion efficiency exceeding 10% is achieved with remarkable thermal stability. Our results provide valuable insight into the role of CsI in perovskite crystallization and a promising approach for designing inorganic halide perovskite-based devices. (5) Versatility of Carbon Enables All Carbon Based Perovskite Solar Cells to Achieve High Efficiency and High Stability Carbon‐based perovskite solar cells (PVSCs) without hole transport materials are promising for their high stability and low cost, but the electron transporting layer (ETL) of TiO2 is notorious for inflicting hysteresis and instability. In view of its electron accepting ability, C60 is used to replace TiO2 for the ETL, forming a so‐called all carbon based PVSC. With a device structure of fluorine‐doped tin oxide (FTO)/C60/methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3)/carbon, a power conversion efficiency (PCE) is attained up to 15.38% without hysteresis, much higher than that of the TiO2 ones (12.06% with obvious hysteresis). The C60 ETL is found to effectively improve electron extraction, suppress charge recombination, and reduce the sub‐bandgap states at the interface with MAPbI3. Moreover, the all carbon based PVSCs are shown to resist moisture and ion migration, leading to a much higher operational stability under ambient, humid, and light‐soaking conditions. To make it an even more genuine all carbon based PVSC, it is further attempted to use graphene as the transparent conductive electrode, reaping a PCE of 13.93%. The high performance of all carbon based PVSCs stems from the bonding flexibility and electronic versatility of carbon, promising commercial developments on account of their favorable balance of cost, efficiency, and stability.

16312216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16312216.value: (1) Design of new type of 2D hole conductor for improved performance and stability of Perovskite Solar Cells. We developed a new type of low temperature solution-processed 2D inorganic material CuCrO2 as hole-transporting layer for highly efficient PSCs. A 45 nm thick compact CuCrO2 layer is incorporated into an inverted planar configuration of ITO/c-CuCrO2/perovskite/PCBM/BCP/Ag, to result in the high steady-state power conversion efficiency of 19.0% versus 17.1% for low temperature solution-processed NiOx-based devices. We conclude that the CuCrO2 hole conductor can have superior performance due to its higher electrical conductivities and higher VBM. More importantly, the optimized CuCrO2-based device exhibits a much enhanced photostability due to the greater UV light harvesting. These results demonstrate the promising potential of CuCrO2 nanocrystals as an efficient HTL for realizing high-performance and photostable inverted Perovskite Solar Cells. (2) Boron Doping of Multiwalled Carbon Nanotubes Enhance Hole Extraction for Highly Efficient Carbon-Based Perovskite Solar Cells. Carbon-based hole-conductor free perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) have suffered from inferior power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) for the inefficient hole-extraction at the perovskite−carbon interface. Accordingly, we show an element doping strategy using boron (B) doping of multiwalled carbon nanotubes (B-MWNTs) as counter electrodes that results in the enhancement of hole-extraction. We modified MWNTs by thermal annealing its source in the presence of H3BO3 under inert gas atmosphere. Structural and elemental analysis show that B-doping can lead to the formation of an acceptor state in the lattice of MWNTs, as a result of increasing its work function, carrier concentration, and conductivity. Finally, a 20 um thick B-MWNTs network was successfully incorporated into a mesoscopic configuration of FTO/c-TiO2/m-TiO2/B-MWNTs, to improve device performance from 10.7 to 14.6% as well as its durability and stability. (3) Ultrasound-spray deposition of multi-walled carbon nanotubes on NiO nanoparticles-embedded perovskite layers for cost-efficient and scalable Carbon based Perovskite Solar Cell. Common drop-casting multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWNTs) film as electrode often suffer from uncontrolled morphological variations. We have developed an ultrasound spray technology to prepare MWNTs film. Morphological analysis confirms the formation of a compact and uniform MWNTs film on perovskite layer, boosting the power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of C-PSCs to 14.07%. A sub-monolayer of nickel oxide nanoparticles was employed as hole transport material to enhance the PCE up to 15.8%. Thus, combining ultrasound spray with nanoparticle embedment technologies, it opens a new way to cost-efficient, mechanical stable, and scalable production of C-PSCs.

16312216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16312216.value: (1) The low temperature solution-processed 2D inorganic material CuCrO2 as hole-transporting layer for highly efficient PSCs developed in this project holds great potential for further development. The PI is in contact with colleagues in solar cell industry to plan for stringent test of stability of the inverted planar configuration of ITO/c-CuCrO2/perovskite/PCBM/BCP/Ag fabricated in this project. (2) The boron doped multiwalled carbon nanotubes (B-MWNTs) as counter electrodes for hole extraction is another noteworthy potential technology. In this project, a 20 um thick B-MWNTs network was successfully incorporated into a mesoscopic configuration of FTO/c-TiO2/m-TiO2/B-MWNTs, to improve device performance from 10.7 to 14.6% as well as its durability and stability. The subsequent integration of this B-MWNTs is currently being scheduled for full cell characterization. (3) The demonstrated better morphological control with ultrasound spray technology, when compared with drop-casting one, shed light on a cost-efficient, mechanical stable, and scalable production of C-PSCs. The dialogue with colleagues in solar cell industry is currently ongoing to explore the opportunity of collaborations.

16312216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16312216.value: To make perovskite based solar materials ready for commercial applications, a composite approach was performed in this project by studying effects of carbon nanostructure and perovskite crystallization on the formation of and hole extraction through the carbon/perovskite interface. The low temperature solution-processed 2D inorganic material CuCrO2 as hole-transporting layer for highly efficient PSCs was developed with high electronic conductivity and mechanical stability. Furthermore, the boron doped multiwalled carbon nanotubes as counter electrodes demonstrated better hole extraction capability. Lastly, the demonstrated better morphological control with ultrasound spray technology, when compared with drop-casting one, shed light on a cost-efficient, mechanical stable, and scalable production of C-PSCs.

16312716.label: Project Objectives
16312716.value: Pursue data-driven phenomenological analyses and theoretical studies on Higgs physics. Develop strategies to measure Higgs physics at the LHC, and use Higgs boson as a tool to probe physics beyond the SM.
rows: Pursue data-driven phenomenological analyses and theoretical studies on Higgs physics.

16312716.label: Realisation of objectives
16312716.value: The first objective of this project is to pursue data-driven phenomenological analyses and theoretical studies on Higgs physics. Regarding this, we explored the implications of a LHC anomaly on the lepton-flavor-violating Higgs decays for Higgs phenomenology (No. 2). Explicitly, in the simplified Higgs-tau-mu Yukawa texture of type III Two-Higgs-Doublet-Model (THDM), we showed that a nonzero Higgs coupling with tau and mu leptons generically implies the existence of a new Jarlskog invariant in the leptonic Yukawa sector and this quantity can be applied to drive the generation of cosmic baryon asymmetry via electroweak baryogenesis. As a “smoking gun” at colliders, the CP-violating Higgs decay to a pair of tau leptons is predicted. More than these, we discovered a new format of the ``naturalness'' sum rule for the Higgs coupling with top quark sector in the ``natural'' composite Higgs models such as little Higgs models (No. 3). We have also calculated at quantum level the contributions of quartic Higgs self-interaction to di-Higgs productions (No.5). The second objective of this project is to develop strategies to measure Higgs physics at the LHC, and use Higgs boson as a tool to probe physics beyond the SM. During the funding period, we developed the strategies to search for neutral Higgs siblings (No. 1) existing in the THDM at colliders including LHC. We also designed collider strategies to measure the interaction patterns of the SM-like Higgs boson which allow us to probe physics beyond the SM such as the ``naturalness'' theories (No. 3, No. 4) (In No. 3, the collider strategy was designed using the new format of ``sum rule'' introduced above as a guideline). Additionally, we developed strategies to measure the Higgs self-couplings at colliders (No. 5, No. 7). (In No. 5, the strategy was designed, using the quantum-level effect introduced above.) It has been known for a while that these couplings can serve as a probe for the nature of electroweak phase transition in the early universe. At last, in order to advance the collider searches for unexpected signals including those of Higgs physics, we made a proof of concept of applying the Machine Learning techniques of novelty detection to its data mining (No. 6). This method is model-dependent and greatly complements the traditional wisdom.

16312716.label: Major findings and research outcome
16312716.value: (Below No. 1-7 represent the seven publications in this project listed in Section 8) No. 1: We designed strategies to search for heavy neutral Higgs bosons (extensively existing in physics beyond the Standard Model) at hadron colliders. Explicitly, we proposed to use the three top quark and four top quark productions to achieve this goal, and showed that this strategy can push the mass limits for such Higgs bosons to above one TeV at high-luminosity LHC, in a well-known difficult parameter region. No. 2: Partly motivated by the LHC anomaly on the lepton-flavor-violating Higgs decay, we studied the Higgs couplings with tau and mu leptons in the simplified Higgs-tau-mu Yukawa texture of type III Two-Higgs-Doublet-Model. We showed that a new CP-violating Jarlskog invariant generically exists in this set up, which can be applied to explain the baryon asymmetry in the universe today. No. 3: We discovered a new format of the ``naturalness'' sum rule for the Higgs coupling with top quark sector. This sum rule can serve as a guideline for testing the ``naturalness'' theories at colliders which were proposed to explain why the squared Higgs mass is stable at quantum level. No. 4: We studied the capability of the future e-e+ colliders to probe the 6D Higgs operators, which effectively describe how Higgs boson interacts with other particles at low-energy scale, in comparison to the LHC. No. 5: We first calculated at quantum level the contributions of quartic Higgs self-interaction to di-Higgs productions, and then designed strategies to measure such an interaction at colliders with this effect. We showed that the quartic Higgs self-interaction can be probed then with a precision better than the theoretical unitarity bounds. No. 6: We provided a proof of concept on applying the machine learning techniques of novelty detection for searching for unexpected signals at colliders (such as exotic Higgs decays). This method is model-independent, complementing most of the ongoing new physics search strategies at LHC. No. 7: We designed strategies of measuring the tthh physics at High-Luminosity LHC. With a systematic study, we showed that its production could be measured with a significance close to one sigma at HL-LHC.

16312716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16312716.value: Given the role played by Higgs boson in particle physics, exploring and revealing the nature of Higgs boson will be one of the top priorities for particle physicists within next decades. In this project, we have tried to look into this from different angles. But, there is still a long way to go before we are able to finally achieve the goal. Largely following this line, a new GRF project with the grant number (16305219) ``Exploring Higgs Physics in the Light of New Experimental Progress '' started from Jan 1st, 2020. The PI will continue his study on Higgs physics, with new inputs expected to be accessible during the funding period.

16312716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16312716.value: Higgs boson was the last missing piece in the SM of particle physics before its discovery. It could be the key to solve some well-known fundamental problems in nature. For example, to explain how the electroweak phase transition (during which the massive particles in the SM are predicted to obtain their mass by talking to Higgs boson) naturally happens in the early universe, the Higgs physics is expected to be different from the SM prediction, in terms of Higgs siblings, interaction patterns, CP properties, etc.. Therefore, measuring Higgs physics provides us a powerful tool to explore the fundamental rules in nature. In this project, we have developed strategies to search for Higgs siblings (No. 1) and explore Higgs interaction patterns (No. 3, No. 4, No. 5, No. 7). Partly motivated by the LHC anomaly, we explored the CP properties of its couplings to tau and mu leptons and the implications for explaining why there is more matter than antimatter in the universe today (No. 2). At last, to advance the collider searches for the unexpected signals including the ones of Higgs physics, we provided a proof of concept of applying the Machine Learning techniques of novelty detection to data analysis.

16313316.label: Project Objectives
16313316.value: To prove by rigorous analysis the minimum energy scaling laws and the properties (such as solution existence, step bunch size and slope) for the equilibrium states of the step bunching phenomenon on epitaxial surfaces due to elastic effects using the discrete model in [22] and the continuum model in [23,24]. To generalize the obtained existence, uniqueness, and minimum energy scaling laws for equilibrium states models with a more general (m,n)-type of pairwise elastic interactions. The above properties are for discrete and continuum models in 1+1 dimensions in which the surface steps are straight. We will also study the solution existence and minimum energy scaling laws for the equilibrium states of the surface profiles using discrete and continuum models in 2+1 dimensions, in which there is a new instability of step meandering in addition to the step bunching stability in 1+1 dimensions.

To generalize the obtained existence, uniqueness, and minimum energy scaling laws for equilibrium states models with a more general (m,n)-type of pairwise elastic interactions.

The above properties are for discrete and continuum models in 1+1 dimensions in which the surface steps are straight. We will also study the solution existence and minimum energy scaling laws for the equilibrium states of the surface profiles using discrete and continuum models in 2+1 dimensions, in which there is a new instability of step meandering in addition to the step bunching stability in 1+1 dimensions.

16313316.label: Realisation of objectives
16313316.value: The three objectives of this project have been fully achieved. Objective 1: We have analyzed the step bunching instability and asymptotic properties in epitaxial growth with elasticity effects by using the discrete model (J. Tersoff, Y. H. Phang, Z. Zhang, and M. G. Lagally, Phys. Rev. Lett. 75, 2730–2733, 1995) and a generalized discrete model with (m, n)-type interactions. We have rigorously proved the existence and energy scaling laws of the energy minimum states in the step bunching regime. We have also rigorously analyzed the structure of the step bunches in the energy minimum states, and have obtained scaling laws of the step bunch size (which is associated with the average slope of the step bunch) and the minimal terrace length (the minimal inter-step distance) in the step bunch. These results using discrete models are summarized in Ref. [1]. We have also analyzed the step bunching properties in epitaxial growth with elasticity effects by using the continuum model derived earlier by the PI (Y. Xiang, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 63, 241-258, 2002; Y. Xiang and W. E, Phys. Rev. B 69, 035409, 2004) and a generalized continuum model that is obtained by taking continuum limit from the discrete model with (m, n)-type interactions [2]. Such analysis is challenging due to the nonlocal elastic interaction and two different length scales involved in the continuum model. We have written the solution of the continuum model as the minimizer of a total energy and have shown the existence and regularity of the minimizer. We have also rigorously analyzed the structure of this minimizer. In particular, we have proved that the slope function of the optimal bunching profile is unimodal. The maximal slope as well as the bunch size have also been obtained. These results are summarized in Ref. [2]. We have studied the convergence from a full atomistic model to the PN model with gamma-surface for the dislocation in a bilayer system (e.g. bilayer graphene) [3]. This is a generalization of the analysis of the convergence from discrete to continuum models for steps. The dislocation core region is similar to the step bunch on an expitaxial growth surface. The Peierls-Nabarro (PN) model for dislocations is a hybrid model that incorporates the atomistic information of the dislocation core structure into the continuum theory. We have proved that the displacement field of and the total energy of the dislocation solution of the PN model are asymptotically close to those of the full atomistic model. Our work can be considered as a generalization of the analysis of the convergence from atomistic model to Cauchy-Born rule for crystals without defects in the literature. Mathematical validation of the Peierls-Nabarro model for edge dislocations has been performed in Ref. [4]. Objective 2: We have studied the energy scaling and asymptotic properties of the one dimensional system with Lennard-Jones (m, n) interaction using the discrete model [1]. This is a generalization of the elastic interactions on epitaxial stepped surfaces (where (m, n)=(0,2)) with 1/r^{m+1} attractive interaction force and 1/r^{n+1} repulsive interaction force between steps, where r is the distance between two steps. We have examined the linear instabilities of a uniform step train and have identified bunching and non-bunching regimes. The energy scaling laws, minimal terrace length, and system size in different regimes (bunching or non-bunching) have been rigorously obtained. We have also derived a continuum model from the discrete (m, n) interaction model. Existence and regularity of the energy minimum solutions that have the step bunching structure have been proved. Energy scaling and asymptotic properties of these energy minimum solutions (bunching formation, bunch size and slope) of the generalized continuum model have been rigorously analyzed [2]. Objective 3: We have analyzed the existence and energy scaling law using the continuum model in 2+1 dimensions where the steps are allowed to be curved (H.Y. Xu and Y. Xiang, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 69, 1393-1414, 2009; X.H. Zhu, H.Y. Xu and Y. Xiang, Phys. Rev. B 79, 125413, 2009). The results are obtained based on conditions that are consistent with the discrete model, from which the continuum model was derived. These results of the continuum model also apply to the discrete model under some smoothness assumptions. Existence of energy minimizer of the equilibrium equation is obtained. Note that in addition to the step bunching stability in 1+1 dimensions, there is a new instability of step meandering in 2+1 dimensions. The step meandering in the equilibrium solution is controlled by the balance of the destabilizing 1/r interaction force and the stabilizing 1/r^3 stabilizing force. Energy scaling law that reflects both instabilities are obtained and influence of these two instabilities on the scaling law are examined. These results are summarized in Ref. [5]. Remark: Part of the results of this project were obtained in collaboration with a PhD student of mine, Tao LUO, and were included in his PhD thesis [6]. In fact, the student started to work with me on this project from the early stage of proposal preparation (more than one year before the beginning of this project). The student received the 2019 Best Thesis Award of the Hong Kong Mathematical Society. References [1] T. Luo, Y. Xiang, and N. K. Yip, Energy scaling and asymptotic properties of one dimensional system with Lennard--Jones (m, n) interaction, Journal of Nonlinear Science, in revision, 2020. [2] T. Luo, Y. Xiang, and N. K. 16313316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16313316.value: We have analyzed the step bunching instability and asymptotic properties in epitaxial growth with elasticity effects by using the discrete model and a generalized discrete model with (m, n)-type interactions. We have rigorously proved the existence and energy scaling laws of the energy minimum states in the step bunching regime. We have also rigorously analyzed the structure of the step bunches in the energy minimum states, and have obtained scaling laws of the step bunch size and the minimal terrace length in the step bunch. (Luo, Xiang, Yip, Journal of Nonlinear Science, in revision.) We have also derived a continuum model from the discrete (m,n) interaction model. Existence and regularity of the energy minimum solutions that have the step bunching structure have been proved. Energy scaling and asymptotic properties of these energy minimum solutions (bunching formation, bunch size and slope) have been rigorously analyzed. Our results show that there is a phase transition between the bunching and non-bunching regimes. These results of the continuum model are consistent with those of the discrete models. (Luo, Xiang, Yip, preprint.) We have analyzed the existence and energy scaling law using the continuum model in 2+1 dimensions. The results are obtained based on conditions that are consistent with the discrete model, from which the continuum model was derived. These results of the continuum model also apply to the discrete model under some smoothness assumptions. Note that in addition to the step bunching stability in 1+1 dimensions, there is a new instability of step meandering in 2+1 dimensions. The energy scaling law shows that there is a transition between the step bunching and step meandering instabilities, and in general the step meandering instability dominates, unlike the step bunching stability in 1+1 dimensions. (Fan, Luo, Xiang, preprint.) We have also studied the convergence from a full atomistic model to the Peierls-Nabarro model with gamma-surface for the dislocation in a bilayer system (Luo, Ming, Y. Xiang, Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis, 2018). This is a generalization of the analysis of the convergence from discrete to continuum models for epitaxial surfaces. This work is also a generalization of the rigorous validation of Cauchy-Born rule for crystals without defects in the literature. Mathematical validation of the Peierls-Nabarro model for edge dislocations has been performed (Gao, Liu, Luo, Xiang, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems B, in press).

16313316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16313316.value: The analysis results for the solution existence and energy scaling laws for the discrete and continuum models for steps on epitaxial surfaces will provide a basis for deeper understandings of the epitaxial surfaces and nature of the elastic interactions. In this project, we have focused on the stepped epitaxial surfaces under elastic effects, and the analysis can be generalized to include other effects, e.g. the Schwoebel effect (step edge barriers). The analysis for the discrete and continuum models and their relationships can also be generalized to the study of properties of other line defects such as dislocations or disconnections, as we did for the Peierls-Nabarro models in this project. Finally, more robust numerical methods can be developed based on the analysis results obtained in this project.

16313316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16313316.value: In epitaxial film growth, elasticity-driven surface morphology instabilities have important applications in semiconductor industry. In this project, we have employed rigorous analysis tools to study this elasticity induced step bunching on epitaxial surfaces, using both the discrete and continuum models. We have proved by rigorous analysis the minimum energy scaling laws and the properties (such as solution existence, step bunch size and slope) for the equilibrium states using the discrete and continuum models. We have generalized these existence, uniqueness, and minimum energy scaling laws to discrete and continuum models for a more general (m,n)-type of pairwise elastic interactions. We have also studied the solution existence and minimum energy scaling laws for the equilibrium surface profiles using discrete and continuum models in 2+1 dimensions, and have shown that in this case, a new instability of step meandering dominates over the step bunching stability. The obtained results provide valuable insight into the nature of the elasticity induced step bunching in the dynamical process of the stepped surfaces. These results also provide a basis for further analytical validation of the continuum models.

16313916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16313916.value: Using our developed isotope-dilution liquid chromatography−tandem mass spectrometric (LC−MS3) method, and in combination with chemical derivation using fluorenylmethyloxycarbonyl chloride, we identified a novel protein modification, cysteine thiazolidination, through reaction with endogenous and exogenous formaldehyde with cysteine residues in proteins. Despite of its yet to be determined physiological significance, the results from our study suggest the possibility of using cysteine thiazolidination in proteins as a potential biomarker for oxidative stress and formaldehyde exposure. These novel findings were published in a peer-reviewed journals paper, Chem. Res. Toxicol. (2016, 29, 1865−1871). We then investigated the sequence-specific bioincorporation of thioproline into cellular proteins using shotgun proteomics. In an E. coli strain auxotrophic for proline, thioproline was found widely incorporated in lieu of proline when the cells were incubated with thioproline. The study identified in total 1428 proteins and 235 distinct thioproline-containing peptides. Label-free relative quantitation revealed 102 differentially expressed proteins (82 up-regulated and 20 down-regulated) in the thioproline-treated cells (with thioproline in the medium) relative to the control group (with proline in the culture medium). Pathway enrichment analysis of the differentially expressed proteins showed that amino acid biosynthesis and protein synthesis has been most affected by thioproline exposure. Phenotypically, the thioproline-treated group was found to exhibit slower cell growth and stronger antioxidant capacity relative to the control. Nevertheless, these results shed light on the potential antagonistic effect of thioproline in protecting cells from oxidative stress. These results were published in a peer-reviewed journals papers, Journal of Proteomics and Chem. Res. Toxicol. (attached).

16313916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16313916.value: Because results of the studies showed cells treated with thioproline have a better tolerance to oxidative stress, further studies can focused on investigating the potential health benefits of using thioproline as a health supplement. The cellular response to different dosage of thioproline and thioproline derivatives can be topics for further studies.

16315116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16315116.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to study phase diffusion of self-sustained oscillations induced by dynamical backaction in micromechanical resonators. Micromechanical resonators are widely used as sensors and actuators. In resonant sensors, vibrations of the micromechanical element are often excited by a periodic drive near the resonance frequency. By tracking changes in the resonance frequencies, the devices can be used in applications that range from inertial sensing to high-sensitivity force and mass detection. When a mechanical resonator is coupled to an optical, microwave or phonon cavity, the effective damping can be changed due to dynamical backaction. By controlling the backaction so that the energy gain compensates the energy loss due to intrinsic damping, self-sustained oscillations take place even when there is no periodic drive near the resonance frequency. As the phase of the self-sustained oscillations can take on arbitrary values, it fluctuates in the presence of noise. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the various mechanisms that affect the phase diffusion of self-sustained oscillations induced by dynamical backaction. Two vibrational modes of a micromechanical resonator will be involved, with the mode at the higher frequency acting as a phonon cavity that plays a similar role as optical cavities. Preliminary measurements indicate that self-sustained oscillations are induced not only in the mechanical mode, but also in the cavity mode. Remarkably, the phase fluctuations of the two modes show near perfect anti-correlation. We propose to explore how well the phases of the two modes follow each other and the feasibility of stabilization of the phase of one mode by measuring that of the other mode. Furthermore, we plan to investigate how different types of noise affect the time dependence of the variance of the phase. Successful implementation of the proposed projects will not only stimulate new theoretical research and verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, but could also lead to micromechanical detectors of improved sensitivity and functionality. The PI has extensive experience with fluctuational phenomena in micromechanical devices. In the past few years, his group performed an extensive investigation of the switching between coexisting vibration states induced by Gaussian and Poisson noise on a nonlinear micromechanical torsional oscillator under strong periodic drive. The PI will work closely with Prof. Mark Dykman, a theorist at Michigan State University to reveal novel behaviors in the phase fluctuations of self-sustained oscillations in micromechanical resonators. 我們建議的實驗研究的目標是研究微機械諧振器在動力學反作用下引起的自激震蕩中的相擴散現象。微機械諧振器被廣泛應用于傳感器和制動器。在諧振傳感器中，微機械部分的震動通常由近共振頻率的週期性驅動力引起。通過監測共振頻率的變化，器件可以被應用於從慣性傳感到引力和質量的高精度測量。當機械諧振子與光，微波，或者聲子腔耦合，有效阻尼常量由於動力學反作用而發生變化。通過控制動力學反作用，諧振器得到的能量能夠補償固有阻尼耗散的能量，即使沒有近共振頻率的週期性驅動，自激震蕩也能夠發生。 由於自激震蕩的相位是任意的，噪音的存在使相位發生波動。提案中實驗的重點在於揭示影響由動力學反作用引起的自激震蕩的相擴散的多種機制。實驗包含微機械諧振子的兩種震動模式，高頻模式作為聲子腔，其作用與光子腔類似。初步的測量表明，自激震蕩不僅發生在機械模式，也發生在腔模式。重要的是，兩種模式的相位波動有近乎完美的負相關關係。我們計劃研究兩種模式相位的關聯有多好，以及通過測量一種模式的相位來穩定另一種模式的相位的可行性。與此同時，我們打算研究不同類型的噪音如何影響相位的時域變化。提案中實驗的成功實施不僅能夠催生出新的理論研究，驗證多種理論方法，還能夠提高微機械探測器的靈敏度和功能性。 主要研究者在研究微機械諧振器的波動現象方面有豐富的經驗。過去幾年裡，他的團隊在強周期性驅動下，非線性微機械扭轉諧振器在受高斯噪聲和泊松噪聲的激發而產生的共存振動狀態之間的跳轉方面做了大量的研究。主要研究者將會與來自密歇根州立大學的理論物理學教授Mark Dykman緊密合作，揭示微機械諧振器在動力學反作用下引起的自激震蕩中的相擴散現象。

16315116.label: Realisation of objectives
16315116.value: During the reporting period, we carried out an investigation of the correlated phase diffusion induced by dynamical backaction in micromechanical resonators. We achieved the project objectives of investigating the anti-correlation of the phase fluctuations of the self-sustained oscillations of the mechanical mode and the cavity mode, studying the normal and anomalous phase diffusion of self-sustained oscillations and exploring the dynamical bistability of self-sustained oscillations. Our findings were presented in four international conferences and published in Nature Communications. Two PG students were trained. One completed his PhD degree and the other one will have his qualifying exam soon. To achieve the project objectives, we designed and fabricated a micromechanical resonator with two nonlinearly coupled modes, the frequency and decay rates of which differ significantly from each other. Following the convention of cavity opto- and electro-mechanics, we call the upper and lower modes cavity mode (with frequency omega_c) and mechanical mode (with frequency omega_m) respectively. The coupling creates sidebands around the cavity mode resonance frequency at omega_c pm omega_m For a weak driving at the blue sideband omega_c + omega_m, the mechanical resonator undergoes a decrease in damping and an increase in effective temperature, and the cavity exhibits optomechanically induced absorption. When the driving amplitude increases beyond a threshold, the damping of the mechanical resonator becomes negative and a parametric instability develops. In the steady state, self-sustained oscillations of the resonator take place, the amplitude of which is limited by nonlinear effects. Previous experiments on self-sustained oscillations mainly focused on the mechanical mode. Self-sustained oscillations of the cavity in the deep resolved sideband limit have remained largely unexplored. We study the self-sustained oscillations of the coupled modes under blue-detuned driving. The onset of the parametric instability is a Hopf bifurcation. We observe that the number of stable states of the coupled modes changes with the driving frequency omega_F. The change is accompanied by hysteresis. A crucial element of our experiment is that it is done in the sideband resolved regime. We find that self-sustained oscillations are induced not only in the low frequency mechanical mode as measured previously, but also in the high frequency cavity mode. Our setup allows simultaneous measurement of the amplitude and phase of both modes, which provides a means to reveal the discrete time-translation symmetry of the system. As expected, the phases of the self-sustained oscillations fluctuate. Remarkably, we find that the phase fluctuations of the two modes are strongly anti-correlated, so that the measured sum of the two phases remains constant within our detection limit. When external additive noise, which mimics thermal noise, is added to the system, the variance of the phase of each mode increases linearly with time in accordance normal phase diffusion. Without the external noise, the intrinsic mode eigenfrequency fluctuations (the frequency noise) are the dominating source of phase fluctuations. The variance of the phase increases with time superlinearly following a power law, making the diffusion anomalous. We show that the corresponding exponent is determined by the exponent of the 1/f type frequency noise. The presence of frequency noise has recently become one of the crucial factors that affect the performance of mechanical resonators. A number of schemes were developed to isolate the contribution of frequency noise from thermal or detector noise. Our results provide a novel way to identify and study frequency fluctuations via the phase diffusion of self-sustained oscillations. Furthermore, our findings of the strong phase anti-correlation of the two modes allow us to implement a feedback scheme that holds promise in significantly improving the phase stability of resonators in frequency standards and resonant sensing. The main problem encountered and solved include the necessity to achieve strong sideband pumping to achieve the regime of self-sustained oscillations. The sideband pumping relies on the Lorentz force generated by an ac current in a magnetic field. However, the electrical resistance of the polysilicon led to too much ohmic heating. We spent much effort in developing a process based on evaporation of a thin layer of gold over a shadow mask to reduce the resistance and to generate a Lorentz force large enough to excite self-sustained vibrations.
