16315116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16315116.value: The first finding is that in the regime of self-sustained oscillations, the phase fluctuations of the mechanical mode and the cavity mode are almost perfectly anti-correlated. The strong anti-correlation opens the possibility of stabilizing the phase in one mode by feedback control, using the measured phase fluctuations in the other mode as an error signal. The second finding is that the phase diffusion can be either normal or anomalous. With broad band electrical noise is injected into the system, the mean square phase change of the beam mode increases linearly with time for such noise. The measured phase fluctuations are in good agreement with standard diffusion expected for a broad-band noise. The slope of the linear dependence gives the diffusion constant D. We find that D varies inversely with the square of the amplitude of self-sustained vibrations, in agreement with theoretical predictions. When the external noise source is removed, the phase fluctuations change qualitatively. The mean square change of phase no longer depends linearly on time. Instead, its time dependence is best fitted by a power law with exponent ~ 1.62, giving rise to anomalous diffusion. A plausible source of the anomalous diffusion is frequency noise associated with the fluctuations of the eigenfrequencies of the modes. The third finding is that the self-sustained oscillations are bistable for sideband driving frequencies omega_F that are detuned from omega_c + omega_m by more than a threshold value. The zero amplitude state is one of the stable states because omega_F is comparatively far from omega_c + omega_m. However, at large vibration amplitudes the dispersive coupling of the modes and the Duffing nonlinearities lead to an increase in the sum of the amplitude-dependent mode frequencies, so that the resonant conditions can be satisfied. Besides being interesting on its own, the observed phase diffusion enables probing the frequency noise of oscillation modes even when this noise is weak. The anti-correlation of the phase fluctuations of the two modes allows manipulation and stabilization of one phase by using the measured other phase deep into nonlinear regime. The outcome of our research includes two papers (one published in Nature Communications and one in preparation) and 4 presentations at conferences. Two PG students were trained. One has completed his PhD degree. The other one will have his qualifying exam soon.

16315116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16315116.value: The strong anti-correlation observed opens the possibility of stabilizing the phase in one mode by feedback control, using the measured phase fluctuations in the other mode as an error signal. The results enable tunable noise-free downconversion of the driving frequency to a frequency close to the eigenfrequency of the mechanical mode. We have developed and implemented the feedback algorithm. A manuscript is under preparation. The ability to generate vibrations with low phase noise is of paramount importance in mechanical oscillators, enabling sensitive resonant detection and high stability precision clocks.

16315116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16315116.value: The frequency stability of mechanical resonators plays a central role in applications such as time keeping and sensing. While clocks in integrated circuits are largely based on quartz resonators, silicon micro- and nanomechanical devices have become viable alternatives because of their small size, low power consumption and reliability in extreme conditions. However, the phase of self-sustained oscillations fluctuate in the presence of noise, affecting their usage as precision clocks. In this project, we design an electromechanical resonator with two vibrational modes with different frequencies and decay rates. We find that the phases fluctuations of the two modes show near perfect anti-correlation. A feedback scheme can be designed to measure the phase of the lower mode and stabilize the phase of the upper mode. Our findings represent an important step in noise-free downconversion of the driving frequency to a lower value.

16317416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16317416.value: 眾所周知在(0,1)區間上平方可積函數都可以展開成Fourier級數， 並且是唯一的。這是在科學和工程眾多的應用中最重要的事實之一。在數學術語中，該組整數頻率的指數函數形成我們所說的在(0,1)區間平方可積函數空間上的一個標準正交基。 事實證明，區間不是唯一一個有指數函數（其中的頻率可能不是整數）正交基的集合。例如，兩個不相交區間的並集也具有這個特性，以整數加上整數平移1/4做為頻率。這樣的一集合被稱為譜集 。 但我們可以描述所有此類集嗎？在 70 年代初，由 Fuglede 推測了今天臭名昭著的Fuglede 猜想，認為一個譜集的充分必要條件是它可以用平移鋪滿整個空間。這個猜想得到廣泛地研究，並在各種特殊情況得到證明。但其一般形式持續了近 30 年，直到Terrence Tao在 2004 年給出反例。後來在維數大於 2中在兩個方向都找到反例，但是在維數1 和 2 中仍然沒有解決。 雖然在其原來的形式Fuglede猜想已經被推翻，但平移鋪滿和譜集之間有著明顯的聯繫。光譜測量和平移鋪滿之間的精確關係依然誘人而神秘。許多有趣的問題依然存在。尤其是，如果我們需要放寬約束，將正交替換成一個Riesz基的存在或一個或框架 （以後再定義），是否這樣的指數函數集合也存在？此外，在許多應用中，我們更感興趣的是測度。有指數函數正交基的測度被稱為 譜測度。他們往往也表現出與平舖的強烈關係。有趣的是，雖然我們可以構造 譜測度，並且在一些特殊情況下甚至分類，但是對自相似測度譜框架和Riesz基即使進行分類，我們幾乎一無所知。其中最有名的懸而未決的問題的是標準的中間3康托測度是否有Fourier框架，即由指數函數組成的框架。最近，PI取得了傅立葉框架測度問題的進展。在擬建項目的PI希望擴展技術來解決更多的問題。 總體譜框架的研究是研究分形幾何，時頻分析和應用諧波分析一個充滿挑戰和活躍的領域。我們將討論最近在該提案的主體做出進展。在這項研究中建議，我們將重點放在選定的一組具體的挑戰，將會在提案中詳細註明。

16317416.label: Realisation of objectives
16317416.value: I have been satisfied with the progress toward achieving the objectives of this project. The work on Fourier frames has very much addressed what the problems outlined in the project, namely to construct Fourier frames on self-similar measures that are not spectral. The most famous conjecture on the nonexistence of Fourier frames for the classic Cantor self-similar measure is still being tackled by many researchers. Our work also shows how difficult it is to construct any Fourier frame on self-similar measures with uniform contraction ratio, as our construction uses different contraction ratios at leach level. During this period I have also studied tiling and its relationship to spectral measures. Given the strong connection between the two areas, there are many interesting questions one may ask. Note here tiling can be a very general notion going beyond the traditional tiling. A simple example of this general notion is that a Borel set S with measure 0 can also be a "tile" in the sense that there exists another set T such that {S+t: t is in T} is a partition of the space (where the overlaps have strictly small Hausdorff dimension than S). We have analyzed a class of self-similar measures is the complex Bernoulli convolution, which are generated by two self-similar maps with equal contraction ratio and equal probability weights on the complex plane. We have discovered a number of spectral measures that were not known previously. They all have the generalized tiling property, which further strengthen the link between spectral property and tiling. The interplay of geometry and algebra is another important area in the study of spectral sets and measures. The study of complex Bernoulli convolution, even under this simple setting, shows the complexity. We have show that the contraction ratio needs to be algebraic. The rationality of spectra in the one dimension is again a result along this direction. Our next goal is to prove the rationality property without added conditions. Unfortunately I have not been able to achieve full objective regarding the Gabor bases. My coauthor Chun-Kit and I have discovered a number of interesting nonseparable Gabor bases, but we would like to obtain more general results, as we believe there are more general structures than what we have now. We are confident that progress will be made in this direction.

16317416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16317416.value: One major problem in this area concerns the structure of spectra of a spectral set. In a joint work with Chun-Kit Lai we have shown that under some conditions the spectra of a spectral set in 1 dimension is rational. Another main question raised in the proposal is on the spectrality of self-similar measures. A famous class of self-similar measures is the Bernoulli convolution, which is generated by two self-similar maps with equal contraction ratio and equal probability weights. In the real case, this problem was studied extensively and was eventually solved by the combined effort of a number of researchers. We have considered the complex case, which is far more challenging because of the varieties of spectral measures we have discovered. Unlike the real case, we didn't even have a conjecture on what the final result should be like. Recently, Chun-Kit Lai and I have discovered a large number of spectral measures that we did not think they existed. The approach we took was to construct the so-called Hadamard triples, which was first introduced by R. Strichartz several years ago. We were able to show that under some algebraic conditions on the contraction ratio we can construct Hadamard triples, which lead to spectral complex Bernoulli convolutions. We conjecture that there are the exact conditions for spectral measures. Right now we have a chance, at least to make significant gain here. Spectral measures and spectral sets are closely related to the problem of tiling as stated in the proposal. Recently I have considered a special type of tiling called multiplicative tiling. The basic notion here is that mostly of the time in the study of spectral sets we look at transnational tiling, namely we take a set and translate it to tile the whole plane or space. In multiplicative tiling we take a set and we dilate or contract the set through a set of dilations and contractions to tile the Euclidean space. The motivation for doing this is that combining with spectrality we can construct orthonormal wavelets. But multiplicative tiling is not well understood at all. In a recent work, Kolountzakis and I have completely solved the multiplicative tiling problem in the one dimension. I am also working on a number of other problems related to project, including nonseparable Gabor orthonormal bases. We have obtained examples where the results are totally unexpected. In addition we are also looking at finding Fourier frames that are not orthonormal bases for Cantor measures.

16317416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16317416.value: The rationality problem is a well known problem and we have a chance of cracking. The key is to combine certain algebraic and geometric tools. Self-similar Bernoulli convolution is also a very promising area. In fact this problem is also related to the classification of self-similar two-tiles. This problem has been around for a while, and is related to the work of Nobel Prize winning physicist Roger Penrose, who first discovered the so-called Penrose Tiles which have self-similar structures. This area requires some of the deepest tools in analysis and algebra, and it is a good area to pursue for very mathematically talented PhD students.

16317416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16317416.value: Self-similarity is everywhere in nature. A fern, for example, exemplifies a self-similar geometric shape. Fractal geometry is the area of mathematics that studies self-similarity. In fact, when we observe our world from different scale we see common occurrences of fractal structures. Traditionally mathematical models for the physical world are often build on more traditional domains, such as a rectangle, a disk, a triangle, where plenty of mathematical tools are available to tackle problems. However, these tools often fail if our mathematical model must be built on fractal structures. Our study can be viewed as developing mathematical tools on fractal structures that are similar to the traditional mathematical tools on more regular domains. It turns out that those mathematical models have strong connection to classical areas of mathematical study such as tiling and algebra. Our work explores these connections, and we hope that by understanding them we will be able to model more complex physical world problem using new tools.

16318816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16318816.value: microRNAs (miRNAs) play an important role in regulating more than half of protein-coding human genes by recognizing messenger RNAs (mRNAs) and inhibiting their translation. Malfunction of miRNAs can lead to cancer and many other human diseases. In order to properly recognize their mRNA targets, miRNAs need to form complex with Argonaute (Ago) proteins (known as RNA-induced silencing complex). Therefore, understanding molecular mechanisms of how Ago facilitates the mRNA recognition is of great importance and can also inspire the development of miRNA-based therapeutics in the long term. Our proposed studies aim to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of the mRNA recognition at two essential sites of miRNAs: the seed region and the 3' supplementary site. As current experimental methods are inadequate to describe these dynamic processes in sufficient details, we will use computer simulations particularly all-atom Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations to provide high-resolution conformational dynamics that is inaccessible to the current experimental methods. Our proposed studies will help reveal the role of hAgo2 in facilitating the sequence specific recognition of mRNA by miRNAs. Moreover, critical hAgo2 residues critical as well as metastable intermediate states during the recognition process will also be identified. In order to overcome the timescale gap between experiments and simulations, we will construct Markov State Models (MSMs) to extract long timescale dynamics from short MD simulations. While MSMs are useful for making quantitative comparisons with experiments, they typically contain a large number of states and thus are too complicated to gain mechanistic insights. To address this issue, we propose a new algorithm that can identify the optimal way to coarse-grain MSMs into macrostate models containing only a few states. These macrostate models are not necessary to be Markovian, but can preserve the order of events and thus greatly help understanding the mRNA recognition mechanisms. An important emphasis of our theoretical work will be to generate hypothesis that will be tested by our experimental collaborators. Guided by the experimental results, we will further refine our theoretical models. In this way, we hope to achieve a detailed understanding of how the miRNA recognizes its mRNA target, and the role of hAgo2 during this process. 通过識別信使RNA（mRNA）并抑制其基因翻譯的方式，microRNA（miRNA）在调控超过一半的人類編碼基因的过程中都起着重要的作用。miRNA的功能故障可導致癌症和其他诸多的人類疾病。miRNA需要结合Argonaute蛋白質（AGO）形成RNA誘導沉默複合物來正確地識別自己的基因標靶。因此了解Ago蛋白质如何帮助miRNA識別mRNA的分子機制在科研上是非常重要的，长远来看也有助于启迪开发基於miRNA的基因療法。 我们提出的研究将着眼于miRNA的两个基本位点（种子位点区域和3‘端的补充位点）来阐明miRNA识别mRNA的分子机制。由于目前的实验方法尚不能提供足够的细节来描述这些动态过程，我们将使用全原子分子动力学（MD）的计算机模拟来得到高分辨的构型动力学信息。我们提出的研究将有助于揭示hAgo2蛋白质在miRNA识别特异序列mRNA过程中起到的作用，同时我们将进一步找到在该识别过程中起重要作用的hAgo2氨基酸残基和稳定的中间构象态。 為了克服實驗和模擬之間的時間差距，我們將通過構建馬爾可夫模型（MSM）來從大量短時間的分子動力學模擬中提取長時間尺度上的信息。雖然MSM可以有效的幫助試驗和模擬之間的定量比較，但是MSM往往包含大量的構象態，不利於了解生物機理。針對該問題，我們提出一種可以有效的大量減少MSM包含態個數的新算法。該算法得到的模型也許不再滿足馬爾可夫假設，但是能正確描述事件發生的順序，從而極大地幫助理解mRNA的識別機制。 我們強調理論研究的一個重要目的是產生能夠被試驗驗證的假設，同時這些實驗的數據也將進一步優化我們的理論模型。這樣我們將可以最終了解miRNA識別mRNA的機理，並進一步闡明hAgo2蛋白在其中所起的作用。

16318816.label: Realisation of objectives
16318816.value: microRNAs (miRNAs) play an important role in regulating human genes by recognizing messenger RNAs (mRNAs) and inhibiting their translation. To properly recognize their targets, miRNAs need to form complex with Argonaute (Ago) proteins (known as RNA-induced silencing complex or RISC complex). Research supported by this grant aims to elucidate molecular mechanisms of the mRNA recognition at essential sites of miRNAs. To achieve the first objective, we have constructed Markov State Models (MSMs) from sub-millisecond molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to reveal dynamics of the recognition at the seed region of miRNA by the human Ago 2 protein. Our results reveal a backbone-coordination dominant mechanism facilitated by the Helix-7 domain, and therefore the vital role of protein-RNA interaction in miRNA recognition by the Ago protein (Zhu et al. “Critical role of backbone coordination and Helix-7 in the seed recognition by human Argonaute 2”, see Paper #10 in Sec C). We have also reported the latest understanding of RISC-mediated RNA interference processes (Prog. Biophys. Mol. Biol., 128, 39-46, (2017). For the second objective which is focused on the last step of the mRNA recognition (3’ supplementary site), we have studied the full-length mRNA recognized by the Ago protein and examined the role of its glutamate finger in subsequent translation suppression via target cleavage. Interestingly, our work shows that the glutamate finger plugged-in (critical for target cleavage) occurs before the completion of the mRNA-miRNA base pairing (with 3’ site as the last step) for eukaryotic Ago proteins, while the glutamate finger plugged-in conformation is formed after the mRNA-miRNA recognition in prokaryotic Ago proteins (Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 116(3) 845-853, (2019)). In this work, we have also revealed distinct functions of two positively charged residues that locate symmetrically around the plugged-in finger domain in a prokaryotic Ago protein. For the third objective, we have developed a theoretical framework for MSMs based on the projection operator approach (WIREs Comput. Mol. Sci., e1343, (2017)). We have further developed a new algorithm that can obtain the optimal state decomposition for constructing coarse-grained MSMs containing only a few states (J. Chem. Phys.,149, 072337, (2018)). To facilitate the MSM construction, we have developed a new density-based clustering algorithm to decompose the conformational space for MSM construction (J. Comput. Chem., 38(3):152-160, (2017)) and a new Path Lumping algorithm to group numerous pathways in self-assembly processes into metastable path families according to their connectivity in kinetics (J. Chem. Phys., 147, 044112, (2017) and Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 20, 6767-6776 (2018)). Based on these new algorithms, we have developed an integrative and tailor-made protocol to construct MSMs to investigate protein functional conformational changes such as the recognition of miRNA being by the RISC complex (Curr. Opin. Struct. Biol, 49, 54-62, (2018)). Using this protocol, we have revealed dynamics of another protein-nuclei acid complex in addition to RISC: i.e. molecular mechanisms for a DNA motor protein to search through genomic DNA for lesions (Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 117 (36), 21889-21895, (2020)).

16318816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16318816.value: Elucidating molecular mechanisms of the mRNA recognition by the RISC complex is of vital importance for both the fundamental understanding of gene regulation and the development of miRNA-based therapeutics. With the support of this grant, we have elucidated molecular mechanisms of the mRNA recognition of miRNAs in the RISC complex via computer simulations and MSMs. To enable simulations of large-scale conformational changes of Ago during these recognition events, we have developed a tailor-made protocol to construct MSMs for functional conformational changes (Curr. Opin. Struct. Biol, 49, 54-62, (2018) and Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 117 (36), 21889-21895, (2020)). To facilitate the MSM construction, we have developed a new kinetic lumping algorithm (J. Chem. Phys.,149, 072337, (2018)), and several other new methods for analyzing MD conformations (e.g. J. Comput. Chem., 38(3):152-160, (2017) and J. Chem. Phys., 147, 044112, (2017)). Using our protocol to construct MSMs, we revealed a backbone-coordination mechanism, where the protein-RNA interactions (between phosphate groups of the mRNA and the positively charged residues of Ago including K355, K525, K550, R554) play an important role in miRNA recognition (the seed region) by the Ago protein. Interestingly, we found that a conserved Helix-7 motif facilitates the dynamics of recognition (Paper #10 in Sec. C). We have also studied the full-length mRNA recognized by the Ago protein and examined the role of its glutamate finger in subsequent translation suppression via target cleavage ((Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 116(3) 845-853, (2019)). We show distinct functions of two positively charged residues that locate symmetrically around the plugged-in finger domain in a prokaryotic Ago protein. Our work further suggests that the glutamate finger plugged-in (critical for target cleavage) occurs before the completion of the mRNA-miRNA base pairing (with 3’ site as the last step) for eukaryotic Ago proteins, while the order of these two recognition events are reversed in the prokaryotic Ago proteins. In addition to miRNA recognition, our protocol holds promise to be widely applied to study functional conformational changes of protein-nucleic acid complexes (e.g. DNA motor protein: Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 117 (36), 21889-21895, (2020)). Due to the above achievements, the PI has been invited to give talks in prestigious international conferences. Three Ph. D and one M. Phil. students partially supported by this grant have successfully obtained their degrees. The PI has won the 16th China Youth Science and Technology Award in 2020.

16318816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16318816.value: With the support of this grant, we have performed computer simulations and constructed MSMs to elucidate molecular mechanisms underlying the recognition of miRNA by the RISC complex. Based on these mechanistic understandings, our future studies can further explore the sequence-dependent mRNA recognition by miRNAs, and in the long term the outcome of our research could benefit the rational design of artificial miRNAs for therapeutic purpose. In addition, we expect that our tailor-made protocol and new algorithms for the MSM construction can be widely applied to reveal kinetic mechanism of functional conformational changes of biological complexes.

16318816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16318816.value: microRNAs (miRNAs) play an important role in regulating gene expression by recognizing messenger RNAs (mRNAs) and inhibiting their translation. Malfunction of miRNAs can lead to cancer and other human diseases. To properly recognize their mRNA targets, miRNAs need to form complex with the Ago protein. Therefore, understanding molecular mechanisms of how Ago facilitates the mRNA recognition is of great importance. However, it is difficult for current experimental methods to describe these dynamic recognition processes in molecular details. To address this challenge, we have adopted all-atom molecular dynamics computer simulations and developed new algorithms to construct Markov State Model (MSMs) based on simulations to elucidate high-resolution conformational dynamics of miRNA target recognition. Using MSMs, we revealed a backbone-coordination mechanism for the miRNA target recognition, where interactions between mRNA backbone and Ago protein play an important role. Furthermore, we have studied the full-length mRNA recognized by the Ago protein and examined the role of Ago’s glutamate finger domain in target cleavage. We revealed distinct functions of two positively charged residues that locate symmetrically around the plugged-in finger domain in a prokaryotic Ago protein. Our studies are beneficial for the future rational design of artificial miRNAs targeting oncogenes.

16320816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16320816.value: Energy is one of the most challenging problems for mankind today. Renewable energy is the future, and energy storage is very important for effective renewable energy utilization because of the mismatch between supply and demand. Lithium ion batteries (LIBs) offer a highly promising energy storage system for power grid load leveling and the transportation of power supplies. The properties of the electrode particles significantly affect the performance of LIBs. To enhance the electrical or ionic conductivity, service life, and/or rate performance of the electrodes, a conductive polymer coating has proven effective. Although thickness control and conformality are very important factors for the effective coating of such polymers, conventional coating is conducted either in a liquid or solid phase, leading to non-uniform coating or aggregate formation on the electrode particles. Oxidative chemical vapor deposition (oCVD) of polymeric materials has been shown to be a “green” process as it can produce a conformal polymer layer on small particles without the involvement of solvents. The desired morphology and thickness can be achieved by changing operating conditions such as the temperature, pressure, type of initiator, rate of particle agitation, and coating time. In this proposed work, the oCVD method will be employed to coat three common types of conductive polymers on solid particles typically utilized in LIB production. Specifically, PEDOT, PPy, and PAni will be coated onto lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a cathode material used in high-capacity LIBs. Operating conditions such as the substrate temperature, vacuum of the reactor, initiator, and monomer will be investigated to identify coating conditions for the optimal electrochemical performance of the batteries, mainly in terms of rate performance, coulombic efficiency, and service life. The reasons behind the enhanced performance of the coated materials will be found by comparing the effects of coating type and composition. The success of the project will have an important effect on the production of durable LIBs for power supply and energy storage applications. 能源是當今人類面臨的巨大挑戰之一。 可再生能源是未來發展的方向。 由於可再生能源供需上存在時間差,儲能對該能源的有效利用尤為重要。 鋰離子電池(LIBs) 為電網調峰以及交通動力提供了非常具有優勢的儲能系統。 電極顆粒材料的性能對電池功能有至關重要的影響。 為了提升電極的電子、離子的傳導率,使用壽命,及功率效應,人們已經證明了導電高分子包覆的作用。 雖然包覆曾的厚度控制以及均勻性是決定導電高分子包覆優劣的重要指標,基於液固相塗覆的傳統方法不僅包覆曾厚非均勻甚至導致電極顆粒間的團聚。 氧化式化學蒸氣沉降法制備高分子材料已經展示為「綠色」加工過程。 它可以將高分子均勻包覆在任何形狀的小顆粒表面並且不需要任何化學試劑。 理想的形貌及厚度可以通過調節溫度、壓力、引發劑、顆粒擾動、反應時間等來實現。 本課題旨在運用氧化式化學蒸氣沉降法將三種導電高分子包覆在常用的鋰離子電池正極顆粒材料表面。 具體來講,聚乙烯二氧噻吩 (PEDOT), 聚吡咯 (PPy), 聚苯胺(PAni) 三種導電高分子將包覆在鎳鈷錳酸鋰顆粒表面。 該顆粒是製備高容量鋰離子電池的正極材料。 通過重點研究如下操作條件諸如底版溫度、反應器真空度、引發劑以及單體分子種類等,來獲得優化的包覆條件以達至電池最好水準。 檢測指標為功率效能, 電荷效率以及工作壽命。 研究還包括通過比較包覆的種類以及表面成分的分析,發現包覆顆粒的性能改善之機理。 本課題的成果將對動力及儲能應用的耐用電池的生產具有重要的影響。

16320816.label: Realisation of objectives
16320816.value: All objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. The experimental facility was initially assembled in HKUST with the help from our Co-I. Then, different operating conditions, including selection of oxidants, monomers, vacuum level, reaction temperature, as well as flow rate and coating time, particles agitation, particle chemical content, etc. For objective 1. Coat PEDOT on the model cathode material, namely, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and find the relationship between the coating thickness and operating conditions. Characterize the electrochemical performance of the coated samples in terms of power delivery (rate), coulombic efficiency, and service life (cycling). This part is completed with the following conclusions obtained: i) The PEDOT coating significantly enhanced the cycling performance of NCM111 from less than 50% retention rate to 92% over 200 cycles at 1C in the voltage window of 3.0-4.6V. ii) Coulombic efficiency of the coated sample in the coin cells (half-cell) is maintained above 99.2% over 200 cycles after the initial 3 activation cycles; iii) PEDOT coating has very limited effect on the rate performance due to the quantity is marginal (1-2 wt.%). For objective 2. Coat PPy on the model cathode material, namely, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and find the relationship between the coating thickness and operating conditions. Characterize the electrochemical performance of the coated samples in terms of power delivery (rate), coulombic efficiency, and service life (cycling). This part is completed with the following conclusions obtained: i) PPy coating for NCM111 shows a slightly better retention rate of 93.2% over 200 cycles cycled between 3.0-4.6V. ii) Coulombic efficiency of the PPy coated NCM111 can maintained above 99.3% over 200 cycles in the coin cells. iii) PPy also shows limited effect on the rate performance. For objective 3. Coat PAni on the model cathode material, namely, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and find the relationship between the coating thickness and operating conditions. Characterize the electrochemical performance of the coated samples in terms of power delivery (rate), coulombic efficiency, and service life (cycling). This part is completed with the following conclusions obtained: i) PANi can also be coated on NCM111 particles with high degree of conformity; ii) The cycling performance improvement is less impressive compared to PPy and PEDOT with 77.7% retention rate obtained over 200 cycles, between 3.0-4.6 V. iii) Coulombic efficiency can be maintained above 99.1% for 200 cycles and the rate performance improvement is not significant. For objective 4. Compare the electrochemical performance of the different types and thicknesses of conductive polymer coating to find the optimal composition, and identify the reasons behind the enhanced performance of different coating compositions. This part has been completed with the following conclusions: i) For different conductive polymer coating, the main improvement on the NCM111 electrochemical performance is on the cyclability, which is one of the most urgent concerns for successful application. ii) The cycling performance enhancement depends on the polymer type and coating thickness. The optimal coating thickness for PEDOT is about 21 nm while 12 for PPy, indicating that PPy is a more effective polymer for NCM111 coating. It should be mentioned that PANi coating has less significant improvement probably due to the less conductivity feature of the PANi type conductive polymer (PANi conductivity is 10-100 times smaller than PPy and PEDOT, respectively). Furthermore, the cycling enhancing effect is believed to be related to both physical protection and the acid scavenger effect of the conductive polymers as: PEDOT+HF=(H-PEDOT)F PPy+HF=(H-PPy)F. The physical protection is useful to shield the NCM111 from the uncontrollable oxidation reaction between the electrolyte and cathode material. Meanwhile, the chemical protection, which was confirmed by the acid-base titration, can scavenge the harmful HF so as to inhibit the loss of transition metal from active materials. In addition, the coating is found to preserve the NCM layered structure observed by the in-situ synchrotron XRD. As a result, the cycling performance of the coated sample is remarkably improved.

16320816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16320816.value: The conformal coating of polymers can be achieved using oxidative chemical vapor deposition method with controlled thickness by using proper oxidant and coating time. The conductive polymers tested, PEDOT and PPy in particular, can significantly enhance the performance of NCM cathode materials in terms of stability and safety. Such enhancement was found to be the consequence of the following fundamental reasons: the physical protection of the materials from the oxidation of HF from the electrolyte, the separation of individual particles from getting agglomerated, the protection of the morphology of the NCM particles, and the inhibition of the release of oxygen from the NCM. The performance improvement was confirmed by high density X-ray synchrotron analysis, as well as TEM and other physical, chemical and electrochemical characterizations. One paper was published in Nature Energy.

16320816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16320816.value: The research was conducted in a rotary batch reactor with a few grams of samples treated each time. In order for the proven technology to make contributions to industry, it needs to have a scale-up study, especially to speed-up the coating rate and manufacture the coated products in a continuous operation. There will be more engineering fundamental investigations in order to take the technology out of lab.

16320816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16320816.value: Electric vehicles are the future in transportation for the protection of environment and also the effective usage of renewable energy. The key hurdle for the current electric vehicles to compete with the gasoline internal combustion engines powered automobiles is the energy density of the batteries. Presently, lithium ferrous phosphate based batteries can only have a driving range of less than 200 km per charge. The higher energy density cathode materials, such as NCM layered metal oxides, suffer from the problem of short service life and not good safety. This study shows a method to successfully overcome the two above mentioned problem by building ultra-conformal protective layers on the cathode material particles, using oxidative chemical vapor deposition method. The protective layer is composed of conductive polymer formed in situ on the surface of the particles. Its thickness, about one hundredth of the thickness of a typical human hair, can be tuned to obtain an optimal value for the best performance. The stability can be increased by more than 10 folds at the optimal coating conditions for NCM111, similarly for high Nickle content materials coated by PEDOT polymer. The coated materials can withstand high temperature and high charge voltage.

16321516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16321516.value: Alkyne metathesis is an important reaction that can be used to make molecules with an alkyne functional group. Highly efficient alkyne metathesis catalysts have been developed on the basis of well-defined high valent W(VI) and Mo(VI) carbyne complexes. With these catalysts, alkyne metathesis can now be performed with a variety of internal alkynes. However, reactions involving terminal alkynes with these high valent catalysts have met with limited success because terminal alkynes tend to give polymers. In view of the wide uses of user-friendly low valent ruthenium carbenes for olefin metathesis, it is worthwhile to explore the catalytic property of low valent carbyne complexes for alkyne metathesis to expand the scope of substrates. Surprisingly, reported work in this direction is extremely rare. We have recently found that a Re(V) carbyne complex can undergo metathesis reactions with alkynes and slowly catalyze alkyne metathesis. In this proposed research, we plan to conduct a systematic study, with a joint experimental and theoretical effort, on alkyne metathesis reactions of low valent rhenium carbyne complexes with the intention of discovering low valent carbyne complexes that can more effectively mediate alkyne metathesis reactions. The chemistry developed from this project will lead to the development of new routes by which to make rhenium carbyne complexes that may not be easily accomplished by classical routes. It may also enable us to find effective alkyne metathesis catalysts based on low valent rhenium carbyne complexes that are stable to air/water and applicable for a variety of substrates, including terminal alkynes. The knowledge gained will be useful for future work in the design of alkyne metathesis catalysts using low valent carbyne complexes of other metals. 炔烃复分解反应是非常重要的有机化学反应。已知的炔烃复分解反应的催化剂主要是一些高价的钨（六价）和钼（六价）的卡拜配合物。然而，由于端炔倾向于形成聚合物，这些高价态的催化剂应用在端炔的催化反应时很受限制。鉴于低价钌卡宾配合物在烯烃复分解反应中的广泛应用，低价卡拜配合物催化的炔烃复分解反应是非常值得探究的。近期我们发现五价的铼卡拜配合物可以和炔烃发生复分解反应并且可以缓慢的催化炔烃复分解反应。在这个研究项目中，我们计划系统地研究低价铼配合物参与的炔烃复分解。这项研究可以帮助我们合成使用经典方法无法得到的铼卡拜配合物。同时也可以帮助我们发现基与低价态铼卡拜配合物的高效稳定的炔烃复分解催化剂。研究结果也有助于将来设计其它催化炔烃复分解反应的催化剂。

16321516.label: Realisation of objectives
16321516.value: The main objectives of the project are (i) to synthesize new low valent metal carbyne complexes that are potentially active for alkyne metathesis, (ii) to explore the scope of alkyne metathesis reactions of low valent metal carbyne complexes and (iii) to explore applications of the carbyne chemistry in organometallic synthesis and catalysis. To achieve the objectives, we have carried out the following research work. We have explored the reactions of ReH5(PR3)3 with alkynes (HC≡CR) for the synthesis of Re(V) carbyne complexes. Through the activity, we have successfully made a series of rhenium(V) carbyne complexes supported by the metal fragment ReCl2(PR3)3. We have also studied reactions of the rhenium polyhydride ReH5(PR3)3 with propargyl alcohols HC≡CC(OH)R2’ in the presence of HCl. These reactions enabled us to prepare γ-hydroxycarbyne, vinylcarbyne or η2 -vinyl complexes with the metal fragment ReCl2(PR3)3. In effort to prepare Re(V)-carbyne complexes with other ligand environments, we have studied reactions of the Re(I) complex [Re(dppm)3]I with internal propargyl alcohols. The investigations led us to make a series of vinylidene complexes with the metal fragment [ReI(dppm)2], which can be converted to Re(V) carbyne complexes upon protonation. We have also explored the possibility of preparing rhenium carbyne complexes through reactions of alkynes with rhenium complexes such as ReCl3(PMePh3)3 and ReCl3(MeCN)(PPh3)2. Vinyl complexes and azavinylidene complexes were obtained from the investigations. As an alternative approach to make rhenium(V) carbyne complexes with different ligand environments, we have carried out ligand substitution reactions of cabyne complexes Re(≡CR)Cl2(PR3)3. A number of new carbyne complexes have been obtained through this strategy, including five- and six-coordinated complexes with various monodentate, bidentate and tridentate ligands. We have tried to make low valent carbyne complexes of Os, Pt, and Rh. New carbyne, and carbene complexes have been isolated from these investigations. To investigate metathesis activity of Re(V) carbyne complexes, we have studied stoichiometric reactions of a series of rhenium(V) carbyne complexes with a variety of alkynes, including both internal and terminal alkynes. Through this activity, we have identified several systems that can undergo alkyne metathesis reactions and found that ligand environment is very important for the metathesis activity. New Re(V) carbyne complexes have been obtained from the metathesis reactions. To investigate the reaction mechanism of the metathesis reactions and to understand ligand effect on the activity for metathesis reactions, we have calculated the reaction profiles of alkyne metathesis reactions with Re(V) carbyne complexes, for example, Re(≡CCH3)Cl2(PR3)3 (PR3 = PMe3, PMe2Ph, PMePh2, and PPh3). We have evaluated catalytic properties of a series of Re(V) alkylidyne complexes for homometathesis of internal alkynes. Several Re(V) complexes were found to be catalytically active for the reaction. The most effective catalyst we discovered so far is a Re(V) carbyne complex bearing two PO-chelating ligands and a labile pyridine ligand. We have explored the substrates scope for alkyne metathesis reactions catalyzed by the rhenium carbyne complex.

16321516.value: (1) One-pot reactions of ReH5(PR3)3 with alkynes (HC≡CR’) in the presence of HCl provide a convenient routes for Re(V)-carbyne complexes Re(≡CCH2R)Cl2(PR3)3 and Re(V)-vinylcarbyne complexes (Publication 4). (2) Reactions of ReH5(PR3)3 with propargyl alcohols HC≡CC(OH)R’2 in the presence of HCl can produce γ-hydroxycarbyne, vinylcarbyne and η2 -vinyl complexes. The selectivity for the products were found to be related to the steric and electronic effect of the substituents of propargyl alcohols (publication 15). (3) Re(V) Carbyne complexes Re(≡CR)Cl2(PR3)3 can be derivatized by ligand substitution reactions to give rhenium carbyne complexes with various ligand environments, including six-coordinate and five-coordinate complexes (publications 4 and 13). Os(VI) carbyne complexes Re(≡CR)Cl2(PR3)3 can be similarly derivatized (Publication 2). (4) The Re(I) complex [Re(dppm)3 ]I can promote C-C bond cleavage reactions of internal propargyl alcohols to give vinylidene complexes, which can be protonated to give Re(V) carbyne complexes (Publication 6). (5) Rhenium(III)-phosphine complexes ReCl3(PR3)3 can react with organonitriles (NCR’) to give novel azavinylidene complexes ReCl3(PR3)2{=N=C(PR3)R’} (publication 14). (6) Reactions of OsCl2(PPh3)3 with alkyne-functionalized phosphorus ylides can be used to make polycyclic mataalarynes, for example, metallaanthracynes and metallaphenanthrynes (Publication 7). Reactions of OsCl2(PPh3)3 with alkyne-carbonyl compounds can give 2-furanyl carbene complexes (Publication 11). (7) Platinum vinylcarbene complexes PtCl2(=C(OR”)-CH=CRR’ )(PPh3) can be conveniently prepared from the reactions of [PtCl2(PPh3)]2 with propargyl alcohols HC≡CC(OH)RR’ in the presence of alcohols R”OH (publication 9). (8) The thermodynamic stability of carbene complexes LnMX(=CRR) with respect to the formation of the corresponding migratory carbene-insertion products LnM(C(X)RR) were found to be strongly dependent on M, X and R (Publications 3, 10, 12). (9) Re(V)-carbyne complexes can undergo stioichiometric alkyne metathesis reactions. The reactivity was found to be strongly dependent on the the ligand environments. For example, the complexes Re(≡CCH2Ar)Cl2(PR3)3 (PR3 = PMe3, PMe2Ph, and PMePh2) as well as Re(≡CCH2Ph)I2(PMePh2)3 can undergo alkyne metathesis reactions with PhC≡CPh, while the complexes such as Re(≡CPh)(S2CNEt2)2(PMePh2), [CpRe(≡CPh)(PMePh2)2]Cl, and Re(≡CCH2Ph)(mnt)(PMePh2)2 are inactive (Publications 4 and 13). (10) Several Re(V) carbyne complexes were found to be catalytically active for alkyne metathesis. An air-stable d2 Re(V) alkylidyne complex bearing two PO-chelating ligands and a labile pyridine ligand was found to catalyze homometathesis of internal alkynes with a broad substrate scope, including alcohols, amines, and even carboxylic acids. The catalyst can tolerate heating, air, and moisture in both solid and solution states, and the catalytic metathesis reactions could proceed normally in wet solvents (Publication 13).

16321516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16321516.value: We found that Re(V) carbyne complexes can undergo alkyne metathesis reactions. It is worthwhile to study the activity of other low valent carbyne complexes for alkyne metathesis reactions. We found that some Re(V) carbyne complexes can catalyze homo-alkyne metathesis reactions. It would be of interest to explore the applications of these catalysts for other types of alkyne metathesis reaction, for example, ring closing metathesis reactions. The activity of the Re(V)-carbyne catalyst we developed so far is moderate. It is of interest to further modify the ligand environments to obtain more active alkyne metathesis catalysts. Metathesis reactions promoted by Re(V) carbyne complexes presumably proceed through rhenacyclobutadiene intermediates. It is of interest to prepare and isolate the related rhenacyclobutadiene complexes.

16321516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16321516.value: Alkyne metathesis is a synthetically very useful reaction that can be used to make molecules with an alkyne functional group. To conduct the reaction under mild condition, a catalyst is needed. Known efficient alkyne metathesis catalysts are mainly those high valent W(VI) and Mo(VI) carbyne complexes. These catalysts, however, have limitations including moisture sensitivity and limited functional group tolerance. In view of the wide uses of user-friendly low valent ruthenium carbenes for olefin metathesis, it is desirable to explore the catalytic property of low valent carbyne complexes for alkyne metathesis to expand the scope of substrates. Surprisingly, reported work in this direction is extremely rare. In this project, we have prepared a series of new Re(V) carbyne complexes and studied their activity for alkyne metathesis reactions. Our work has demonstrated that Re(V) carbyne complexes can indeed promote alkyne metathesis reactions. The knowledge gained is useful for future development of user-friendly alkyne metathesis catalysts.

16322016.label: Project Objectives
16322016.value: Develop mathematical models to describe the degradation of polymer-polymer hydrogel. Provide a quantitative description of the release of protein therapeutics from degradable polymer-polymer hydrogel. 16322016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16322016.value: Hydrogel, an especially in situ hydrogel, offers unique advantages as a localized depot for the release of therapeutic protein. Hydrogel being a network of hydrophilic polymers is compatible with protein-friendly formulation in aqueous media. As gelation takes place inside the body for in situ hydrogel, the hydrogel precursor which exists in solution form is injectable. As the society ages, the management of chronic diseases is becoming increasingly important, and so does the demand of minimally invasive methods to supply therapeutic protein over a long time span. With the aforementioned properties, in situ hydrogel is considered an attractive platform. We and others have identified that the design of degradable hydrogel depot for prolonged release of protein as a promising direction. To manage the release of protein over a period of multiple months, the mesh size of the hydrogel network must be carefully controlled. Smaller mesh size hinders the (diffusion) movement of protein and slows down its release. As the hydrogel degrades, mesh size becomes larger, and mass loss from hydrogel takes place. These phenomena add up to the complexity of this process. On the other hand, it is important to develop a theoretical framework to quantitatively correlate the material properties with the protein release profile. The mathematical models will help to advance the understanding of degradable hydrogel, and therefore accelerate the development of practical applications. We will develop mathematical models for a particular type of in situ hydrogel, which we term polymer-polymer hydrogel from chemical crosslinking. A statistical kinetics approach will be combined with the Blob theory to describe the change in mesh size during degradation, and hence its effect on the release rate of protein. Taking advantage of the unique feature of polymer-polymer hydrogel intended for long-term protein release, we propose that surface erosion will take place from a hydrolytic hydrogel, which can be quantitatively accounted for to explain another protein release mechanism. We will engineer a new experimental system to complement the effort in mathematical modelling. It consists of vinylsulfone (VS)-modified and thiol (SH)-modified dextran, which crosslink under mild conditions. Ester linkers of varying half-lives will be incorporated in the pendant groups to allow degradation of the crosslinks. Theoretical prediction will be compared with experimental data. A depot optimized for the delivery of therapeutic antibody for multiple months will be evaluated in rabbits. Our comprehensive approach towards the quantitative understanding of degradable hydrogel depots will accelerate their development into practical applications.

16322016.label: Realisation of objectives
16322016.value: Objective 1: Degradation behavior of polymer-polymer hydrogels has been modelled using Monte Carlo concept. Initial Distribution of cross-linked nodes within network has been estimated based on the polymer concentration, degree of modification and volume of hydrogel. A randomized life-time span was assigned to each node based on first order kinetics of hydrolysis of degradable nodes. As time passes, current time step is compared to the lifetime of each node. A node expires when its lifetime is smaller than the current iteration time step. When all nodes have expired on one chain, the polymeric chain can be counted as detached chain and can be released from the network. Counting the number of intact small chains between crosslink nodes and relating it to the swelling ratio of hydrogel through the well-known Bray-Merrill equation, one can profile the degradation of hydrogel over time. Mass loss of hydrogel can also be quantified using this method. In another approach, effort has been made to model hydrogel disintegration time. Disintegration time is the time at which hydrogel network no longer maintains its shape and structure and becomes a polymeric solution. It is a reverse process of gelation. From a mathematical point of view, when the molecular weight of developing molecules in the crosslinking process diverges to an infinite value, gel is formed. We exploited the reverse approach and used recursive nature of nodes degradation to track the molecular weight of the supramolecular structure until its disintegration. Required parameters are the number of intact active groups on both polymer chains and the kinetic rate constant of cleavable bonds. Objective 2: We developed a three-dimensional lattice model to describe the multiphase release of macromolecular drugs encapsulated in a non-degradable and degradable polymer-polymer hydrogel. To reflect the heterogeneity in distribution of hydrogel mesh size, two distinct diffusion coefficients are used to describe the transport of a macromolecule in a non-degradable hydrogel network. Drug moves between lattice sites in a stochastic manner to simulate the random nature of diffusion. To generate the drug release profiles for experimental validation under the limitation of computational cost, a simple scaling relationship was employed. Sensitivity analysis reveals the dominance of the distribution fraction over the absolute values of diffusivity. Model developed for non-degradable hydrogels were further modified to include initial and degradation induced heterogeneous hydrogel structure. A unimodal beta distribution for diffusion coefficient has been adopted to represent the nature of the heterogeneity of mesh distribution in the hydrogel network. A three-dimensional hydrogel matrix is discretized into small lattice sites, having different number of degradable nodes based on the chosen distribution obtained by fitting to total initial degradable node numbers. As time passes, nodes are degrading following first order kinetic. Small lattice’s diffusion coefficients are updated according to the remaining number of cross-link nodes at each time step. Solute molecules are allowed to move independently in a stochastic manner within the network when their resident time exceed the maximum limit based on the updated diffusion coefficient. In order to fit the model results to experimental data, random walk equation was used to build up a scaled diffusion coefficient distribution for hydrogels of larger volume from smaller size network. Objective 3: We formulated polysaccharide-based, in-situ forming hydrogels crosslinked by Michael addition. We designed and synthesized a series of ester linkers with hydrolytic half-life (t0.5) ranging from 5 hours to 5 months and incorporate them into the hydrogels crosslinked by conventional polymer-polymer crosslinking, so that the hydrolytic degradation time of hydrogels could be adjusted over days to months. In addition, we invented a “backbone-lysable” strategy to prolong the hydrogel degradation durations without changing the ester linker chemistry. The key value of backbone-lysable strategy was to decouple the degradable moieties from the crosslinkers, so that the formation and disintegration of the hydrogel network can be controlled separately. Objective 4: We evaluated the models by comparing the results with experimental data. Figure 2A-D show the effect of polymer concentration and degree of modification on the swelling profile and disintegration time of hydrogels. As concentration increases, fitted kinetic rate constant for hydrolysis slightly decreases. It leads to decrease in the mass swelling ratio for higher concentrations. It also causes the gel to disintegrate over slightly longer time. However, degree of modification has a more pronounced effect on both hydrogel swelling ratio and disintegration time. The model fitted the experimental data yields a higher kinetic rate constant for hydrogel composed of polymers at lower degree of modification. It is also obvious from the results that disintegration time is more sensitive to the degree of modification than concentration. Experimentally, we observed discrepancies between the measured value of the pseudo first-order hydrolytic cleavage rate constant (kobs) in polymer solutions and the model predicted one in hydrogels. Based on the 1 H NMR spectrometry-based method, we directly measure kobs of methacrylate-derived ester crosslinkers in polymer solutions and in hydrogels, and discovered that the kobs is significantly affected by the local environment in the hydrogel. Within the formulations being studied, the esters in the crosslinked polymer network (gel state) degraded 1.8 times faster than esters of similar chemistry in soluble polymers (solution state). The presence of the negatively charged carboxylate groups in the polymer chains decreased kobs in gel state, while only minimally affecting kobs in solution state. The finding solved the model-experiment discrepancies, resolve conflicting views about hydrogel degradation, and to guide the rational design of degradable hydrogel. Polydispersity of polymer chains and the random nature of cross-linking often result in a heterogeneous hydrogel network with nonuniform mesh sizes, posing problems for modeling the release kinetics with single diffusivity. We have shown that proposed Dual diffusivity model for non-degradable hydrogels the dual-diffusivity model showed good agreement with the experimental data in describing the release profiles of macromolecular drugs of three different sizes from chemically cross-linked dextran hydrogels in contrary to single diffusivity model. The model is able to describe the experimental data of release satisfactorily at both “early” and “late” times. The results from degradable distribution model were compared with experimentally measured released profiles for IgG encapsulated in hydrogels composed of cross-linked dextran with same formulation while one of them are non-degradable. There are several possible solutions from the fitting procedure for each specific formulations. The fitted distribution for degradable hydrogels were used to predict the release from non-degradable hydrogel. Model shows that only when the distribution was wide enough (extended distributions) the effect of degradation rate can be reproduced. Objective 5: First, the polymer concentration was used as the critical parameter to control the proportion of releasable versus physically trapped protein molecules in the initial hydrogel meshwork. Subsequently, the dynamic change of the hydrogel meshwork was modulated by the crosslinking density and the cleavage rate of ester linkers. Sustained release of Fitc-labelled IgG (F-IgG) was demonstrated in two degradable hydrogels, with release durations of 3 months and 6 months respectively. Hydrogels encapsulating another therapeutic model proteins, bevacizumab was injected in the vitreous chamber of rabbit eyes, and maintained active bevacizumab concentration the eye for more than 6 months. The intraocular hydrogels were well tolerated in the rabbit eyes until being degraded.

16322016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16322016.value: • Developed a model to describe the degradation profile of polymer-polymer hydrogels and examining the effect of hydrogel composition on the it (Publication No. 1 & conference No.1&3) • Developed a dual diffusivity model to explain the release profile of macromolecular of different sizes from non-degradable hydrogels (Publication No. 4 & conference No.6) • Designed and synthesized a series of ester linkers with hydrolytic half-life ranging from five hours to five months, successfully incorporate them into in-situ hydrogel formulations and achieved adjustable degradation durations from about one day to more than six months. (Publication No. 5 & conference No.4) • Achieved tunable, sustained release of model protein IgG from degradable hydrogels over 3-6 months. (Publication No. 5 & conference No.5) • Experimentally confirmed hydrogel local milieu significantly influences ester hydrolysis, resolve conflicting views about hydrogel degradation and provided quantitative evidence to assist theoretical modelling and to guide rational formulation design. (Publication No. 3) • Demonstrated good in vivo biocompatibility and measured pharmacokinetics of hydrogel released bevacizumab as model protein in rabbit eye model. (Conference No.8 & 9) • Developed a diffusivity distribution-based model to describe the protein release profile from a degradable hydrogel (Publication No. 6 & conference No.10)

16322016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16322016.value: The project enables a comprehensive and systematic understanding of relationship between formulation parameters (such as polymer size, half-life of hydrolytic bonds, degree of modification, etc) and the protein release profiles, from both the theoretical and practical perspectives. The project has led to a set of design principles to manipulate protein release from short-term to long-term in in situ hydrogelm which are valuable for different biomedical applications. Based on this knowledge, the PI's lab is currently exploring an application of an hydrogel-based protein release for immunotherapy.

16322016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16322016.value: This project has advanced the hydrogel-based technology for the the prolonged release of protein molecules. While hydrogel is an important type of biomaterials and has already been used widely in various medical and life science applications, it has been challenging to control the long-term release of protein from the the material, especially when the material is also degradable. This research of this project provides a theoretical framework and employes mathematical model to describe the degradation of hydrogel as well as the release of proteins from the hydrogel. In parallel, experimental techniques have been developed to prepare hydrogels that can yield different release profiles, with promising results demonstrated in animals. The findings are expected to expedite the development of medical applications using hydrogels, including therpaeutic delivery and regenerative medicine.

16322416.label: Project Objectives
16322416.value: Develop novel non-fullerene molecular acceptor materials with twisted 3D molecular structures. Increase the size of the core unit to reduce the extent of intramolecular twisting. Introduce a thiophene spacer to reduce twisting and tune the optical properties of the molecule. Attach an end group on the molecule to further tune the optical properties. Develop novel trimer, tetramer and pentamer acceptors based on electron-deficient units such as PDI. The proposed synthetic route should allow us to systematically explore the oligomeric acceptors materials that are believed to be better performing than typical dimers. Develop donor polymers that maximize the performance of molecular acceptors. Our donor polymers will incorporate the 2nd position branched alkyl chains sitting between two thiophenes. This polymer design rationale will enable a strong temperature dependent aggregation property for the donor polymer, which was utilized to control polymer:fullerene morphology in our previous work and can also be used to control polymer:MA morphology in this project. Once the materials are available, we will study the morphology and device performance of various polymer:MA blends to establish the relationship between chemical structures and their electronic and photonic properties.

16322416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16322416.value: Bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) organic solar cells (OSCs) are based on a pair of electron-donor and -acceptor materials. Historically, the most dominant choices of acceptors have been fullerenes. However, fullerenes have many drawbacks such as poor absorption properties, limited tunability of energy levels and high costs of productions. The goal of this proposal is to develop efficient OSCs based on non-fullerene molecular acceptor materials. We will develop two families of molecular acceptors described as follows. One of the main challenges in developing high-performance molecular acceptors is that they either have strong aggregation tendency leading to excessively large BHJ domains or weak aggregation that results in poor pi-pi stacking and charge transport ability. It is challenging to achieve both small domain size and good charge transport property using the same acceptor material. We have recently demonstrated that twisted 3D structured molecules can achieve a unique combination of properties that can overcome this paradox. In this project, we will fully explore this promising strategy via a systematic design of twisted 3D molecules incorporating four structural components (core, spacer, acceptor and end groups), which allow for fine-tuning of the extent of intramolecular twisting as well as the absorpotion properties of the material. For the second family, our design is inspired by the recent success of helical-shaped trimer and tetramer materials that show improved performance over corresponding dimers. Here we design new routes to synthesize PDI-based trimer, tetramer or pentamer with or without benzene linker. This new family of oligmeric acceptors should have less rigid molecular structures than the reported helical-shaped molecules and offer a promising material class for non-fullerene OSCs. Importantly, the fabrication of an efficient non-fullerene OSCs also relies on the choice of a matching donor polymer, which plays a critical role in controlling the morphology of the BHJ blend and the OSC performance. In this project, we will also design donor polymers based on our temperature-dependent aggregation rationale that offers an excellent morphology control and has yielded multiple cases of efficiency polymer:fullerene OSCs with 10-11% efficiencies. The donor polymers (especially the alkyl side chains) will be tailored to match our molecular acceptors. Given our previous successes and promising preliminary results, the proposed project goals are feasible. The proposed materials, once available, will provide an excellent platform to study the interaction between polymer and molecular materials and the morphology and device performance of non-fullerene OSCs. 基于本体异质结结构的有机太阳能电池一般是由电子给体和电子受体材料共同组成。传统的电子受体材料多数基于富勒烯及其衍生物，然而，富勒烯及其衍生物的缺点如在可见光区域吸收很弱，能级难以调节，且生产升本昂贵等，限制了其发展和应用。因此，本课题的目标就是发展一系列基于非富勒烯受体材料的有机太阳能电池。我们将从以下两方面探索小分子受体材料的器质关系。 在发展小分子受体的过程中，分子间的聚集是一个亟待解决的问题。小分子受体要么因为过强的分子间聚集而导致分子结晶过大，要么因为过弱的聚集而导致电子传输效率偏低。因此，如何在形成较小的分子结晶的同时又保持较高的电荷传输效率，也就成了小分子太阳能电池领域的一个巨大挑战。我们最近的研究发现，具有扭曲3D结构的小分子有望解决这一问题。在本课题中，我们将系统的探索具有扭曲3D结构小分子的设计合成与表征。我们设计的具有扭曲3D结构的小分子由4个部分构成：核心部分，桥连部分，受体部分和端基部分。通过调整这四部分的修饰，我们可以有效的设计出符合预期能级，在可见光区域有较强吸收的小分子，同时解决分子扭曲过强的问题。 同时，最近有文献报道，螺旋状结构的三聚/四聚体小分子相对于二聚体具有更好的器件表现，但分子间的聚集仍然过强。受此启发，我们设计了使用苯环做桥连部分的PDI二聚体小分子。我们预测，这一系列的寡聚受体具有较弱的刚性结构，可以有效改善这一系列小分子聚集过强的问题。 值得一提的是，在非富勒烯太阳能电池的设计中，匹配的给体材料也是一个必须考虑的因素。因为给体材料同样会影响器件的微观形貌，进而对器件的表现产生很大的影响。在这一课题中，我们同样设计了一系列的具有温度依赖聚集特性的给体材料。实验证明，具有这一特性的材料通常能容易的获得较好的微观形貌，在达到10-11%效率的报道里，基于这一设计理念的给体材料占了相当大的部分。本课题组一直致力于这一系列给体材料的设计，具有丰厚的实验经验，并取得了较好的成果。因此，我们希望对给体材料进行进一步的结构调整，以使其能与受体材料具有更好的匹配性。倘若能实现这一目标，我们将为给受体材料的相互作用，以及该作用对形貌和器件的影响的研究，打下坚实的基础。

16322416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16322416.value: Firstly, we reported a novel small molecule acceptor (SMA) named FTTB-PDI4 obtained via ring-fusion between the thiophene and perylene diimide (PDI) units of a PDI-tetramer with a tetrathienylbezene (TTB) core. A small voltage loss of 0.53 V and a high power conversion efficiency of 10.58% were achieved, which was the highest value reported for PDI-based devices to the reported date. Then, we combined with a small molecule acceptor (SMA) ITIC-Th, PTFB-M yields a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 10.4%, whereas the PCE is only 8.4% for PTFB-P:ITIC-Th-based cells. This provides a useful approach to tune the morphology of donor polymers and to enhance the performance of NF-OSCs. Afterwards, we implement a novel concept of introducing intramolecular π–π stacking for the design of PDI-based acceptors. We synthesized and systematically studied two isomeric PDI-tetramers with different functionalization positions (α- and β-positions) of naphthalene, and thus different extents of intramolecular packing. Last but not least, to further enhance light harvesting of the single-junction semitransparent organic solar cells while maintaining a decent transmittance, we fabricate a semitransparent tandem organic solar cell by incorporating a medium-bandgap P3TEA:FTTB-PDI4 blend as the front sub-cell. A high efficiency of 10.5 % is recorded with an average transmittance of 20 %.

16322416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16322416.value: On the one hand, our work demonstrates the superior potential of the non-fullerene acceptors in tandem ST-OSCs and will promote the development and commercialization processes of ST-OSCs. What's more, our work is different from the previously reported low‐Vloss systems like P3TEA: SF‐PDI2, and we present the first example of efficient charge separation in a non-fullerene OSC despite both small Egap, D − ECT and Egap, A − ECT offsets, which will have fundamental significance and implications on the understanding of charge transfer processes in OSCs. On the other hand, our work proves the important role of low bandgap SMAs in the field of OSCs to achieve higher Jsc and PCEs of OSCs, and that the modulation of EGs can really optimize the performance of A-D-A-type SMAs based OSCs. Finally, It is foreseeable that FE-T-based new materials will be demonstrated in the short term, leading to further growth of the PCE in the field of organic solar cells and potentially performance enhancement in other organic electronics. Further insight into the observation of high EQE along with very low Eloss in this system will be investigated in our future work.

16322416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16322416.value: The molecular design of non-fullerene acceptors is critically important for the development of the organic solar cells field. However, previous non-fullerene acceptors have problems in their charge mobility and domain size. It has been difficult to achieve high-performance materials that can form a crystalline domain and small domain size. We demonstrate a new type of molecular design with double-decker geometry that allows us to achieve our more crystalline small molecular with pure domains. At the same time, these molecules' design enables the relatively small domain size. This molecule design would have an important impact on the research community and inspire others to develop molecules with similar properties.

16322616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16322616.value: Natural and artificial neural systems receive and process information from different modalities, such as visual, auditory, olfactory, and sense of movement (vestibular) inputs. When the inputs from different modalities are consistent, they are integrated to provide a reliable picture. When they are inconsistent, however, confusion may result. Hence, the ability to integrate consistent information and to segregate inconsistent information is crucial for network performance. However, in the past decades, it remained largely unknown how the integration and segregation of information are achieved in neural systems. Thus, it is essential to investigate this issue. It has been demonstrated that the brain can optimally integrate information across different modalities and different tasks. Research using a Bayesian approach from statistics provides experimental evidence that neural systems can achieve optimal integration and segregation in multisensory processing. To model the essential ingredients that enable neural systems to perform optimally, we adopt a recently developed successful decentralized network structure, in which the inputs of each modality are fed to a module. It is possible that in each module, there are two groups of neurons, one group operating on the assumption of integrated information, and the other group on segregated information. These two groups compete, and the winner reveals whether the inputs are better explained by the integrated or the segregated assumption. Alternatively, there exists only one group of neurons in each module, without differentiated operations. The two-group hypothesis is inspired by the existence of the so-called congruent and opposite neurons that are found in the visual-vestibular area of the brain. Congruent neurons respond to similar visual and vestibular stimuli, whereas opposite neurons respond to differing visual and vestibular stimuli. Although the role of congruent neurons in integrating multisensory information is widely recognized, the role of opposite neurons remains unknown. As opposite neurons exist in quantities comparable to those of congruent ones, it is plausible that they both play a role in information segregation. We will propose a theoretical framework for information integration and segregation, develop plausible network implementations that fulfill these tasks, compare the two-group and the one-group hypotheses, and then analyze the experimental data from our collaborator to assess the models. 天然和人工神經系統接收和處理不同模態的資訊，諸如視覺、聽覺、嗅覺，還有前庭輸入移動感的資訊。當來自不同模式的輸入是一致時，它們會被整合，以提供一個可靠的圖像。但是當它們不一致時，就可能導致混亂。因此，整合一致資訊的能力，和分隔不一致資訊的能力，對於網絡性能是至關重要的。然而，在過去幾十年，神經系統怎樣整合和分隔資訊，仍然所知不多。因此，有必要研究這個問題。 已經證實，大腦可以用最優化方式，整合不同模式和不同任務的資訊。利用統計學上貝葉斯方法的研究提供了實驗證據表明，神經系統可以在處理多感官資訊時，用最優化方式作整合和分隔。為模擬神經系統需要包含什麽要素以達成最優化表現，我們採用一個最近開發成功的分散式網絡結構，其中每個模態的輸入被饋送到獨立的模塊。在每個模塊中，可能有兩組神經元，其中一組基於綜合資訊的假設操作，另一組則基於分離的資訊。透過這兩組神經元的競爭，勝者便可顯示整合抑或分隔的假設，可以更好解釋資訊。另一個模型，是每個模塊中僅有一組神經元，在操作上沒有區別。兩組神經元的假說，是因在視覺-前庭腦區發現了所謂全等神經元和相反神經元的存在，而得到啟發。全等神經元對相似的視覺和前庭刺激，會有相同的反應，而相反神經元對不同的視覺和前庭刺激，才有相同的反應。雖然全等神經元在整合多感官資訊上的作用得到廣泛認可，相反神經元的作用仍然未知。由於相反神經元數量媲美全等神經元，它們在分隔資訊上應有一定作用。我們將提出一個資訊整合和分隔的理論框架，開發能完成這些任務的網絡結構，並比較兩組神經元和一組神經元的假設，然後再分析我們合作者的實驗數據，以評估模型。

16322616.label: Realisation of objectives
16322616.value: We proposed a normative framework to integrate and segregate information from different modalities. This framework is a decentralized neural circuit model consisting of two reciprocally connected modules, representing respectively the dorsal medial superior temporal area (MSTd) and the ventral intraparietal area (VIP) in the brain. Each module carries out multisensory processing via cross-talks between modules. This decentralized architecture achieves integration in a distributed way and is robust to local failure, and it agrees with the experimental findings that neurons in MSTd and VIP both exhibit multisensory responses and that the two areas are abundantly connected with each other. At each module, there exist two groups of excitatory neurons: congruent and opposite neurons. Each group of neurons is modeled as a continuous attractor neural network (CANN), mimicking the encoding of heading-direction in neural systems. In CANN, each neuron is uniquely identified by its preferred heading direction with respect to the cue. The neurons in the same group are recurrently connected, and the recurrent connection strength decays with the disparity between two neurons’ preferred directions. Pools of inhibitory neurons in each module provide mutual inhibition between congruent and opposite neurons. Between modules, neurons of the same type are reciprocally connected with each other. For congruent neurons, they are connected with each other in the congruent manner, that is, neuronal connections are stronger for neurons with more similar preferred directions. For opposite neurons, they are connected in the opposite manner, that is, neuronal connections are stronger for neurons with more different preferred directions. To calculate the disparity information between two cues, the neuronal response to the combined cues should integrate its responses to the direct cue and its response to the indirect one but with the cue direction shifted (through the offset reciprocal connections). The proposed neural circuit of congruent and opposite neurons successfully models the integration and segregation of visual and vestibular signals as observed in experiments. In both the Bayesian and the neural circuit frameworks, we discovered that the probabilistic model of multisensory processing can be interpreted geometrically as vectors whose directions and magnitudes represent the means and reliabilities of the likelihood distributions. Cue integration is the sum of the two vectors, and cue disparity information is their difference. The tuning properties of the congruent and opposite neurons have an excellent agreement with experimental observations. Opposite neurons have been found in experiments for years, but their functional role remains a mystery. There have been few studies investigating this issue, and previous works showed that opposite neurons are essential, as they provide complementary information to congruent neurons necessary to accomplish the required computation. This result is consistent with our idea that opposite neurons are indispensable in multisensory processing, but our study goes one step further by theoretically proposing that opposite neurons encode the disparity information between cues and that congruent and opposite neurons jointly realize concurrent multisensory processing. We extended the model to the case that the prior distribution of multisensory inputs consists of both a correlated and an independent component, since multisensory cues in the real world may originate from either the same source or independent ones. Our work proceeds in two steps. First, we showed that by incorporating output dependence in the noise of the neural dynamics, the model is able to yield estimates with excellent agreement with Bayesian inference in the weak input limit, and fairly good agreement for stronger inputs. Moreover, the output dependence of noises can be achieved by the translational fluctuations of the bump-shaped firing profile since the network is a continuous attractor network. To deal with the composite prior with both correlated and independent components, we proposed additional neuron groups associated with both the congruent and opposite modules. The additional group associated with the congruent module is fed by both direct inputs and the outputs from the congruent module, but is decoupled from the opposite module. Similarly, the additional group associated with the opposite module is fed by both direct inputs and the outputs from the opposite module, but is decoupled from the congruent module. The model achieves Bayesian inference in the framework of the composite prior. Our work will be ready for submission in the near future. We also considered how the couplings in a neural network model are shaped by the prior information when it encodes the whole profile of the posterior and performs optimal multisensory integration in a Bayes-optimal way, as suggested by extensive studies. To process stimuli of two modalities, a biologically plausible neural network model consists of two modules, one for each modality, and cross-talks between the two modules are carried out through feedforward cross-links and reciprocal connections. We found that the reciprocal couplings are crucial to optimal multisensory integration in that their pattern is shaped by the correlation in the joint prior distribution of sensory stimuli. At a more fundamental level, we studied the dynamics of bimodular continuous attractor neural networks with static and moving stimuli. In particular, we are interested in the effects of the inter-modular couplings being excitatory or inhibitory. For static inputs, we found that the bump-shaped firing profiles in the respective modules are attracted by their counterparts through excitatory couplings and repelled through inhibitory couplings. An interesting case is that one of the inter-modular couplings is excitatory and the other is inhibitory, in which population spikes can be generated. These populations spikes can be used for temporal coding and may be useful in resolution enhancement of similar inputs. We also extended our study to model the response of the retina to external stimuli driven by stochastic processes and compare with experiments on the retinas of bullfrog. When inertia is present in the dynamics of the stochastic process, we found that the mutual information between the response and the stimulus has a peak in the future component at both the system and neuronal levels, showing that the retinal response is anticipative. Our analysis showed that inhibitory feedback plays a dominant role in this effect. The analysis further elucidates the response to moving stimuli, the position dependence of the anticipation time and the mutual information peak, which can be verified in future experiments. Another extension of our work involves the push-pull dynamics in neural information processing. We proposed that neural feedback, which is widely observed in the brain but whose function remains largely unknown, disentangles interferences due to correlated memories. We studied a neural network storing the hierarchical categorical information of objects. Information retrieval goes from rough-to-fine, achieved by the push (positive) and the pull (negative) components of the feedback that suppresses the interferences due to correlations of objects from different and same categories, respectively. Our model reproduces the push-pull phenomenon observed in neural data. Our study involved the statistical physics of many interacting components such as neurons and other similar systems. We also made progress in elucidating the nature of intermittent strain releases in complex systems, finding evidence of tipping points in heterogeneous systems, symmetry breaking in unsupervised learning, the effects of prior knowledge on phase transitions, and the dynamics of congestion. These studies are relevant to understanding the dynamics of neural systems.
