16322616.label: Major findings and research outcome
16322616.value: As described in the previous section on the realization of objectives, and with reference to Part C, our major findings include the following. 1. We proposed a model of multisensory integration and segregation for information received from different modalities [8]. The model explains the role played by opposite neurons and produces results in excellent agreement with experiments. 2. We showed that the model can be extended to include the case that the prior distribution of multisensory inputs consists of both correlated and independent components. This is achieved by additional neural circuitry and incorporating output-dependent noise [17]. 3. We found that when a bimodular neural network processes inputs of two modalities at Bayes optimality, the reciprocal couplings and cross-links are faithfully shaped by the prior information [3]. 4. In our study of the dynamics of bimodular continuous attractor neural networks with static and moving stimuli, we demonstrated the attraction and repulsion of the bump- shaped firing profiles, and the existence of population spikes [4,14]. 5. In modeling the response of the retina to external stimuli driven by stochastic processes, we found that the retinal response is anticipative, and showed that inhibitory feedback plays a dominant role in contributing to this inertial anticipative effect [6]. 6. We elucidated that the push and the pull components of the feedback in the brain can suppress the interferences during the retrieval of hierarchical patterns, reproducing the push-pull phenomenon observed in neural data [15]. 7. We demonstrated how continuous attractors can be learned in neural networks from a family of correlated real images after their semantic relationships have been extracted by pre-processing [5]. 8. In unsupervised learning of information, we discovered symmetry-breaking phenomena when the number of learning examples increases [9]. We further discovered the effects of incorporating prior knowledge on phase transitions [11]. 9. In complex systems with external inputs, we elucidated the nature of intermittent strain releases when they are driven by external inputs [1]. We further proposed resource allocation schemes in these systems [10]. 10. In studying collective behaviors of populations with competition, we found evidence of tipping points in heterogeneous systems [2]. We found insightful ways of describing the dynamics of congestions [16], and the study was accompanied by observing their induced switching behavior and controlling policy [13]. Competitions among the populations produce non-trivial time series and we have used Gaussian process to extract their correlations in making predictions [7,12].

16322616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16322616.value: This project has opened the gateway to several future research directions. So far, the paradigm of this project is the model averaging approach to multisensory integration, that is, the integrated output is the average of the estimates from the two modalities. However, in both biological and artificial information processing, there is also a need for the model selection approach, in which the integrated output is the prevailing estimate among the two modalities. This is known as causal inference. Causal inference requires a stronger competition between the two modalities, but the congruent and opposite modules should still play important roles. The opposite module will continue to play the role of detecting disparity, and the disparity information will be used to determine the coupling between the congruent modules. The control of the coupling can be achieved by gating neurons or laterally inhibited modules. This will be a very meaningful extension of the present project. Another possible research direction is the multisensory integration of non-Euclidean information. So far, we have focused on information in the Euclidean space, but it is common that information in the brain is represented in semantic space. Other directions that worth exploring are anticipative information processing and applications to artificial neural networks.

16322616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16322616.value: Natural and artificial neural systems receive and process information from different inputs. The ability to integrate consistent information from different modalities and to segregate inconsistent information is crucial for network performance. Experimental evidence showed that neural systems can achieve optimal integration and segregation in multisensory processing. We proposed a model inspired by the existence of the so-called congruent and opposite neurons that are found in the visual-vestibular area of the brain. Congruent neurons respond to similar visual and vestibular (sense of movement) stimuli, whereas opposite neurons respond to differing visual and vestibular stimuli. Although the role of opposite neurons remains unknown, it is plausible that they play a role in information segregation as they exist in quantities comparable to the congruent ones. We adopt a recently developed successful decentralized network structure, in which the inputs of each modality are fed to a module. In each module, there are two groups of neurons, one group operating on the assumption of integrated information, and the other group on segregated information. These two groups compete, and the winner reveals whether the inputs are better explained by the integrated or the segregated assumption. Efficient multisensory information processing is achieved.

16324216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16324216.value: Transistors, used to amplify and switch electronic signals, are the fundamental building blocks of modern electronics. It is one of the most important inventions in the last century. A single commercial computer central processing unit (CPU) nowadays can contain more than 5 billion transistors. Moreover, as predicted according to the Moore’s law, the number of transistors in a single CPU in the past four decades has been doubling every two years. However, the large number of transistors consumes energy and results in heating, which would limit the density of transistors and the computing power of CPUs. Therefore, there is an urgent need to find materials that can be used to build low power consumption transistors. Recently, a class of two-dimensional graphene-like materials called transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) has attracted much attention. Moreover, similar to graphene, TMD have relatively high electron mobility, chemical stability and low dimensionality and they are considered a candidate material for next generation transistors. Interestingly, electron spins in TMD materials are coupled to the orbital motions of the electrons through so-called spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Particularly, in monolayer TMD, the SOC is referred to as Ising SOC, which pins electron spins to out-of-plane directions. More interestingly, some TMD materials, such as NbSe2, are superconducting down to monolayer thickness. It is shown that superconductivity in monolayer TMD can endure several times higher magnetic fields than in bulk TMD. It was proposed by the PI and collaborators that this is due to the Ising SOC, which weakens the effect of in-plane magnetic fields by pinning electron spins to the out-of-plane direction. We called this new type of superconductors Ising superconductors. More recently, the PI and students showed that Ising superconductors can be used to engineer a new type of superconductor called topological superconductor which hosts Majorana fermions and has potential applications in quantum computations. We believe that the study of monolayer and few layer TMD are important both for technological applications and the understanding of this novel superconducting states. In this proposal, we propose to: 1) Explain the in-plane upper critical field data of monolayer NbSe2, 2) Study the superconducting properties of monolayer NbS2, 3) Study bilayer and multi-layer superconducting TMD materials, 4) Study the superconducting proximity effect of s-wave superconductor on TMD nanoribbons. 晶体管能放大或者調控電子信號，是現代電子學的基礎，也是上世紀最重要的發明 之一。如今，一個商業計算機的中央處理單元（CPU）可能有超過50 億個晶体管。 而且正如摩爾定律所預測，在過去40年中單個CPU上的晶体管數目每兩年就翻一 倍。然而，大量的晶体管消耗能量并發熱，從而限制了 CPU上晶体管的密度。因 此，尋找能用于製造低能耗晶体管的材料就變得緊迫。 最近，一類與石墨烯相似的二維材料受到廣泛關注，那就是過渡金屬與第VI族元素 的化合物（簡稱TMD）。TMD 如石墨烯一般有較高的電子遷移率，化學穩定性，並 且其低維樣品的製備很簡單，這些性質讓它可用于新一代的晶体管。有趣的是，在 TMD材料中，電子的自旋與 軌道角動量相互耦合（即自旋軌道耦合，簡稱SOC）。 特別是在單層的TMD中，SOC也被叫做伊辛自旋軌道耦合（Ising SOC）, 因為這里的SOC將電子的自旋鎖定 在垂直于樣品面的方向。 更有趣的是,一些TMD材料，例如二硒化鈮（NbSe_2, 當厚度僅為單個原子層厚度時也可以是超導體。實驗顯示，單層TMD材料的超導性可承受的磁場高達體材料的好幾倍。项目负责人 和他的合作者提出這種奇特的性質是由於伊辛自旋軌道耦合將電子的自旋鎖定在垂直樣品面的方向，從而減弱了平行於樣品面方向磁場的作用。我們把這種新型超導體稱為伊辛超導體 (Ising Superconductors)。最近，项目负责人和他的學生的工作顯示伊辛超導體可以用來實現拓撲超導體。拓撲超導體中存在馬約拉納費米子(Majorana fermions)，它在量子計算領域具有潛在的應用價值。我們相信單層和多層TMD材料對於技術應用和理解伊辛超導態都很重要。 在這個提案中，我們計劃做以下兩點研究 1）解釋單層二硒化鈮（NbSe_2）在平行於樣品面方向的臨界磁場實驗數據。 2）研究雙層和多層TMD超導材料。

16324416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16324416.value: The contact angle is the angle, conventionally measured through the liquid, where a liquid/vapor interface meets a solid surface. It quantifies the wettability of a solid surface by a liquid via the Young equation. Experimentally, the contact angle of a droplet on a surface has been observed to take a range of values. The phenomenon is termed the contact angle hysteresis (CAH) and is defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum contact angles. The origin of CAH is mainly attributed to surface roughness or chemical contaminants. The CAH is one of the most important phenomena in the wetting of liquid droplets on surfaces. It plays a crucial role in many industrial applications. Despite its relevance, there is still a lack of mathematical theory for the CAH. In this project, we will study both the quasi-static CAH and the speed-dependent CAH on rough and chemically patterned surfaces in a two dimensional channel. We will derive the dynamic equations of the contact angle and contact point. The mechanism of the CAH will then be revealed by studying the behavior of its solutions. 接触角是意指在液体/气体界面接触固体表面而形成的夹角。 它是描述液体和固体表面润湿现象的重要参数。接触角滞后是润湿效应中一个十分重要的物理现象, 广泛存在于自然界中且在许多产品的工业生产中起着关键作用。随着人们对润湿的理论和实验研究不断深入,接触角滞后现象逐渐引起科研工作者们的广泛关注。尽管如此,迄今为止,有关润湿过程中接触角滞后形成的原因以及润湿中接触角滞后模型的研究还不够深入,许多问题还未得到解决。本研究计划通过推导接触角和接触线在的运动方程以及对解的形态的研究对接触角滞后现象形成机理进行了数学理论的分析。

16324416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16324416.value: In this project, we study the contact angle hysteresis on a slowly moving rough boundary using a phase-field model with a relaxed boundary condition. In particular, we want to model the recent experimental observation in [D. Guan et al., Phys. Rev. Lett., 116 (2016), 066102]. The speed of the moving boundary is slow enough so that the fluid flow effect is negligible. From asymptotic analysis, we derive an ordinary differential system for the dynamics of the apparent contact angle and the contact point. The system enables us to understand the contact angle hysteresis in the experiment, including the asymmetric dependence of the advancing and receding contact angles on the boundary velocity. We also studied the initial value problem for the generalized Allen--Cahn equation for the real matrix-valued field which is the gradient field of some free energy. Our main contribution is to use asymptotic methods to study the solution of the initial value problem. If the initial condition has a single-signed determinant, the solution evolves towards the closest orthogonal matrix at a fast O(varepsilon 2t) time scale. At the O(t) time scale, the solution evolves according to the O(n) diffusion equation. At a slow O(varepsilon t) time scale, the interface is driven by curvature and the surface diffusion of the matrix-valued field. For n = 2, the interface is driven by curvature and the jump in the squared tangental derivative of the phase across the interface. In particular, we emphasize that the interface when n geq 2 is driven by surface diffusion, while for n = 1, the original Allen--Cahn equation, the interface is only driven by mean curvature.

16325016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16325016.value: Classical Galois theory allows scientists to distinguish whether one can express the roots of a polynomial equation in terms of known numbers obtained under basic arithmetic (additions/substractions/multiplications/divisions) plus taking roots in a finite number of steps. Similarly, differential Galois theory allows scientists to distinguish whether certain solutions to a linear differential equation can be expressed in terms of known functions under simple "arithmetic" including differentiation and integration in finite steps. Differential Galois theory has been known since the end of 19th century. Yet the theory has only very recently been applied in different mathematics disciplines to find closed form solutions. The PI and his collaborators/students discovered that differential Galois theory could help to make precise the many new solutions found for certain prototype Hill's equations (second order linear differential equations with periodic coefficients) in complex oscillation theory, both in infinite sum forms and finite forms. They then discovered that such solutions are precisely those finite/semi-infinite band-gap solutions that correspond to those Hill's equations (under a previous GRF in which the application of Galois theory was not originally anticipated). Hill's equations have an old origin that can be traced back to Hill's work in lunar perigee of the moon in the 19th century (1886). The Hill equations appear in a diverse area of research, ranging from solid state physics (with periodic lattice) to non-linear dynamics (i.e., integrable systems (solitons)) where periodic phenomena are involved. In mathematics the Hill equations are related to Floquet theory. Prompted by a recent surge in activities of mathematicians applying differential Galois theory to different areas of mathematics where finding closed-form solutions are their main interest, the PI realises that the theory would help them to clarify solutions of different forms that they previously obtained for certain prototype Hill's equations. Although the main advantage of differential Galois theory can be used to identify the closed-form solutions of the equations, it also sheds light on new and strange infinite expansion solutions expressed by known hypergeometric type functions. Differential Galois theory allows researchers to form a unified view of results scattered in different research areas. This PI proposes to apply the powerful theory of differential Galois groups to study special solutions obtained from complex oscillation theory as well as those solutions related to finite (semifinite) band-gap problems. 我們將用微分伽羅華的最新理論及計算方式來研究在復域上線性微分方程的解的復震盪理論。復域上線性微分方程的解的復震盪理論是用經典的值分佈理論研究全純及亞純函數的理論，因此這研究計劃將是一個創新的計劃。

16325016.label: Realisation of objectives
16325016.value: Objective 1 (achieved): A paper has been written and submitted regarding the research development described in the mid-term progress report. A new theory that may have further developments has been proposed to tackle the issues raised in this objective. We summarise the main ideas and major findings here. The objective of a modification of Picard-Vessiot construction to explain infinite hypergeometric type series solutions to Heun type equations is essentially achieved. The main point of our modification to replace usual Picard-Vessiot extension by a quotient D-module. In fact, we developed a very general theory that can incorporate all types of solutions in the forms of infinite sums to ordinary differential equations in a “comparison” viewpoint with applications of Weyl algebra in the following sense. Classical power series solutions around an ordinary point of ODEs are regarded as “comparisons” with the solutions of the simplest ODE y’=0. Similarly, Frobenius series solutions around a regular singularity of an ODE are regarded as “comparisons” with solutions of the next simplest ODE xy’=ay for some non-zero constant a. Hypergeometric type expansions solutions of an ODE are regarded as “comparisons” with solutions of specific hypergeometric equations, etc. Moreover, our new theory can single out for “good expansions” if the comparison is a “good one”, thus it gives, for the first time, an effective viewpoint that explains many known classical solutions to well-known ODEs from mathematical physics. The word “comparisons” here means D-linear maps between D-modules. Such D-linear maps are rare. However, iterative Newton’s method in I-adic topology/valuation (I is a suitably defined maximal ideal) allows one to solve equations in the form of remainder maps. The vanishing of the remainders guarantees the existence of such D-linear maps wanted. We have achieved such constructions for doubly Confluent Heun and biconfluent Heun equations, but fall short of the general Heun equations and Confluent Heun equations as written in the mid-term progress report. Although our theory does not give more information on the coefficients of these infinite expansion solutions than existing theories (except in the terminating cases which leads to a confirmation of a conjecture of factorization of generalized hypergeometric type operators by Takemura). In fact, we have not just fulfilled the first objective as stated but achieved far beyond the scope of the original project written several years ago in two significant ways (i) the theory so developed can equally be applied to linear ordinary difference equations by altering the differential operator into different types of difference operators in the Weyl algebra setting in future work. Indeed, we have discovered that, e.g., there is only one “Bessel Weyl algebraic symbolic equation” (xD)^2+x^2-n^2=0, where x, D represent any operators that satisfy the commutator relation [D, x]=Dx-xD=1 instead of many different types of Bessel equations, such as the classical Bessel equations, Jackson’s q-Bessel equations, etc; (ii) a new way to explain series expansions central to classical complex function theory in terms of Weyl algebraic language that would better generalise to handle difficulties in existing theory of special functions that satisfy difference operators. These new viewpoints far exceed the original expectation and thus compensates the relatively less progress towards the following objectives 2 and 3. Objective 2 (essentially achieved): The main achievement in this part is the application of the celebrated Kovacic algorithm, which contains Banks’ algorithmic, from the Picard-Vessiot theory to identify, if any, Liouvillian solutions of a number of important classical linear ODEs that appear in mathematical physics but still escape the attention of researchers. The three equations are (i) Whittaker-Ince equation (1915), (ii) Ellipsoidal Wave equation and (iii) (a special case of) Picard-Fuchs equation of periods of a K3 surfaces as a family of elliptic curves. The findings and algorithms are contained in the master thesis of Mr. Cheung, Tsz Yung, a master of philosophy student graduated in August 2018 (attached). All these three equations have complicated singularity structures than Heun type equations. New Liouvillian solutions (seems not encountered in the past literature) have been found only in case (i), i.e., the Whittaker-Ince equation, while it has been proved that no Liouvillian solutions could exist in cases (ii) and (iii). Unfortunately, Mr. Cheung did not pursue the findings further after his graduation. Further work that investigate properties of these newly found Liouvillian solutions is waiting to be done. Objective 3 (not yet achieved): This is partly the responsibility of the PI/Co-I who distributed the effort in too many directions too thinly in a limited time frame (the original proposed objective 3 is unrealistic); and partly new findings in Weyl algebraic approach that is too important and exciting to ignore while it is beyond the scope of this project. However, the PI/Co-I feel that a proper use of gauge transformations would lead to a way to study the relation between the non-oscillatory solution of DEs and its finite-gap solutions. The viewpoint would have to be dealt in a future project.

16325016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16325016.value: 1) The construction of a modified Picard-Vessiot construction in explaining a reason for the existence of infinite hypergeometric type series solutions to Heun type equations. The main point of our modification is to replace usual Picard-Vessiot extension by a quotient D-module, and the idea of comparison of D-modules by means of D-linear transformations which plays the role to compare the solutions of two differential equations. Such an approach unifies differential types of expansions exist in the literature. This includes not only the various types of special function expansions important for differential equations from applications derived from mathematical physics (some have ancient origins), but also usual power series or Frobenius series. Our approach leads to the confirmation of a conjecture of factorization of generalized hypergeometric type operators by Takemura. The findings and applications are written in the paper “Series solutions of linear ODEs via linear maps between completions of quotient D-modules” submitted for journal publication and as attached in Part C. 2) Non-oscillatory solutions of certain classes of ODEs with periodic coefficients can be transformed into finding Louvillian solutions of linear ODEs with polynomials coefficients. Hence Kovacic’s algorithm can be applied. A master student has been trained to learn the Picard-Vessiot theory and to implement the Kovacic algorithm successfully to investigate the existence of Liouvillian solutions of three classes of important linear differential equations taken from mathematical physics. In particular, new Liouvillan solutions have been derived for the Whittaker-Ince equations for the first time in the literature. The findings have been recorded in the student’s thesis (see Part C). Part of the joint paper with Professor Guofu Yu on applying Kovacic's algorithm to identify non-oscillatory/Liouvillian solutions of the Biconfluent Heun equations was prepared in this project period (but I forgot to include the GRF number of this project during the publication stage).

16325016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16325016.value: 1) The idea to transcribe solutions to linear DEs in terms of D-linear maps between D-modules successfully used in this project turns out to be relevant in the study of both classical and contemporary special functions, as already touched upon in section 5.3 above. In particular, we have already obtained partial results that is effective in obtaining generating functions of special functions taken from the well-known contemporary “Askey-scheme” by studying appropriate classes of holonomic systems of PDEs. Our approach applies equally well to difference-differential operators which appears to be new. (These new findings in terms of Weyl algebraic structures and D-modules mentioned in objective 1 reinforce the believe that our new approach is a proper one.) 2) Since series expansions are also instrumental in the development of classical complex function theory such as power series, (e.g. Newton) interpolation series, q-series, etc, so this new D-modules approach also suggests the existence of a corresponding “complex function theory” that also incorporates a theory of residues, Cauchy formulae, etc. Indeed a preliminary version of “Liouville theorem” for difference operators has been obtained. We plan to further develop these two ideas in two future GRF projects.

16325016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16325016.value: We have developed an algebraic theory that explains a reason of existence of different types of historically important solutions of both classical and contemporary differential equations for the first time in literature. These differential equations are of important values in many branches of mathematical physics. Major ideas consists of applying appropriately set up algebraic theory in place of commonly used analytical methods, an old idea of iterative methods to find roots of equations that dates back to (and named after) Sir Issac Newton.

16325116.label: Project Objectives
16325116.value: To fabricate a multi-layer patterned artificial tissue. To configure physicochemical gradients in a hydrogel. To construct hydrogel scaffolds with controlled sizes and geometries. To explore possible applications of our technology in biomedical study and tissue engineering.

To construct hydrogel scaffolds with controlled sizes and geometries.
To explore possible applications of our technology in biomedical study and tissue engineering.

16325116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16325116.value: The emergence of three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting has enabled us the power to configure a 3D tissue or even an integrated organ from the bottom up for both regenerative medicine and basic studies in biomedical science. However, as a powerful tool for engineering artificial tissues, it still suffers from several main drawbacks such as high costs, limited geometrical structures of scaffolds that can be printed, and long-time stay of cells in a non-cultivating environment. Because of that, new technologies for manufacturing artificial tissues that can overcome these shortcomings are still needed. Herein, we propose a new, general replica molding technology for 3D structures (which can be created with 3D printers) for the fabrication of artificial tissues with well-defined controls on various critical parameters for cell growth and differentiation such as cell alignment, chemical and mechanical gradients, and arbitrary 3D geometry. The basic principle for this is to take any object from conventional 3D printing as the sacrificial templates for the construction of various types of tissue. Preliminary studies in our group demonstrate that it is highly robust and can achieve a good fidelity in replicated hydrogel scaffolds. Our technology not only obviates those drawbacks of 3D bioprinting, but also shows versatility for a wide range of biomedical applications. Moreover, the processes involved do not need high manipulation skills and expensive equipment so that it is affordable to most laboratories. Based on our preliminary results, we will exploit the full potential of our technology. We aim to accomplish three important technological goals, which are: 1) how to fabricate multi-layer patterned artificial tissue with well-controlled, independent alignment in each layer; 2) how to configure physicochemical gradients in a hydrogel; and 3) how to shrink the size of 3D artificial tissue with controlled geometries. If the work goes smoothly, we will, based on our experience, try to explore its applications in biomedical study and tissue engineering; they are: to make 3D biomimetic cardiac tissues; to study the mechanism of cancer metastasis and screen drugs in cancer cell-encapsulated hydrogels with physicochemical gradients; and to construct artificial blood vessels. The proposed works will make much contributions with new technological tools to both regenerative medicine and cancer treatment, which are two of the major challenges for mankind in the 21st century. In addition, our technology is expected to find applications in other fields of biomedical science and engineering such as stem cell differentiation, single-cell analysis, disease diagnosis and biosynthesis. 三維生物打印技術的出現使得我們有可能從下至上的方式構建三維人工組織甚至器官，它們將可應用在重生醫學和生物醫學的基礎研究中。然而，作為人造組織工程學中功能強大的工具，它仍然存在幾個主要的不足之處，如價格高、可打印的幾何結構有限以及打印期間細胞長時間處於非正常培養的環境中。因此，有迫切急需開發能克服這些缺點的新技術。這裡我們提出一個全新的，可以普遍適用的三維結構鑄模技術來製備能對細胞生長和分化的多個重要參數進行準確調控的人造組織，如細胞排列、化學及力學性能的梯度、和任意的三維結構。該技術的基本原理是用傳統三維打印技術產生各種物體結構作為製備所需組織的犧牲模板。我的科研組的初步研究表明該技術非常強大，可以得到保真度高的水凝膠複製結構。該技術不僅可以避免三維生物打印的缺點，而且在生物醫學的廣泛應用中體現出其多功能性。此外，它的操作不需要很高的技巧或者昂貴的儀器，因為它對大部分實驗室都很實用。基於我們初步的實驗結果，我們將全面開發該技術的所有潛能。我們將完成以下三個重要的技術目標：（1）製備多層圖案化、準確控制並每層各自對齊的人造組織；（2）在水凝膠內形成物理化學梯度；和（3）縮小所製備的三維人造組織結構的尺寸。如果工作進展順利，基於以往積累的經驗我們將進一步探索該技術在生物醫學研究和組織工程中的應用，包括：製備仿生的心臟組織；研究癌症轉移的機理和癌症藥物的篩選；以及形成人造血管結構。我們這裡擬議的工作將對21世界人類的兩個重大挑戰，即再生醫學和癌症治療，提供新的技術工具而作出重要貢獻。另外，該技術還將在其他生物醫學領域，包括幹細胞分化、單細胞分析、疾病診斷和生物合成，發揮作用。

16325116.label: Realisation of objectives
16325116.value: Let me show the realization of the objectives one by one below: 1. To fabricate a multi-layer patterned artificial tissue. we have developed a novel and facile approach for the formation of microporous chitosan hydrogel scaffolds, which relies on self-crosslinking reactions between amine and maleimide on the modified chitosan even below the freezing point. The method is simple and does not require any sacrificial porogen, toxic initiator/catalyst, harmful irradiation, or sophisticated equipment. The formed hydrogel scaffold is applicable to various cell types for the generation of artificial tissues with its pore size, porosity, and mechanical properties of our hydrogels readily tunable. In addition, we developed a biomimetic nano-engineering composite material for functional tissue engineering of cartilage superficial zone (SZ) by combining our expertise in bioMEMS and artificial tissue in hydrogel. Our implantable smart platform which mimics the SZ of articular cartilage not only delivers topographical cues, but also releases biomoleculesto sequentially recruit, organize, and differentiate hAMSCs to chondrocytes, which shows large potential in tissue engineering. Please refer to #3 and #9 papers in Part C. This Objective is successfully completed. 2 To configure physicochemical gradients in a hydrogel. In our work, we studied the physicochemical properties in various hydrogels and configure corresponding gradients in hydrogels. We systematically studied the mechanical properties of and also chemical diffusions in a microporous chitosan hydrogel that we developed for 3D cell culture and tissue engineering. Also, in the work on tissue engineering of cartilage superficial zone, we tested many physicochemical aspects of our hydrogel and selected the optimal conditions for implantation study. In the development of injectable in-situ-forming kartogenin-loaded chitosan hydrogel, the hydrogel physicochemical properties are critical and we finally generated a drug-loaded, injectable hydrogel with tunable rheological properties for cartilage tissue engineering. Furthermore, we generated stiffness gradients in hydrogel and studied the response of cells to the established gradients. Please refer to #3, #8 and #9 papers in Part C. This Objective is successfully completed. 3 To construct hydrogel scaffolds with controlled sizes and geometries. By combining three-dimensional (3D) printing techniques and tissue engineering, we developed a new molding technique that can convert 3D-printed complex structures (which is in some printable materials such as photocrosslinkable resins and cannot be directly use for cell study and tissue engineering) into functional hydrogel materials that can support cell culture and tissue engineering. We have tried the printed structures from cm-scale to micron scales; our molding method works very well for 3D objects in all the different scales. We also tried to build microfluidic networks inside the hydrogels to mimic the circulatory system in our body to deliver nutrients to the cells and remove metabolic wastes from the cells. Please refer to #3, #5, #8, and #9 in Part C. This Objective is successfully completed. 4 To explore possible applications of our technology in biomedical study and tissue engineering. We have explored possible applications of our technology in a few biomedical study and tissue engineering. we developed a biomimetic nano-engineering composite material for functional tissue engineering of cartilage superficial zone (SZ) by combining our expertise in bioMEMS and artificial tissue in hydrogel. Our implantable smart platform which mimics the SZ of articular cartilage not only delivers topographical cues, but also releases biomolecules to sequentially recruit, organize, and differentiate hAMSCs to chondrocytes, which shows large potential in tissue engineering. Also, we developed new in situ forming thermosensitive hydrogels based on chitosan with a wide range of properties such as shear modulus, gelation time, gelation temperature and swelling coefficient. These hydrogels can fill the defects with various shapes by a simple injection and temperature enhancement to 37 °C. Furthermore, we have just started collaborations with a hospital in Guangzhou to apply our technology for implantable materials used in tissue engineering. Please refer to #8, #9 papers in Part C. This Objective is also successfully completed

16325116.label: Major findings and research outcome
16325116.value: Our major findings and research outcome are the following: 1. We developed a new concept for facile formation of a microporous chitosan hydrogel based on self-crosslinking, which has a great potential in 3D cell culture and tissue engineering. 2. We developed a convenient method to establish tunable stiffness gradients for cell studies. 3. We generated an injectable in situ forming kartogenin-loaded chitosan hydrogel with tunable rheological properties for cartilage tissue engineering. 4. We developed a biomimetic nano-engineered platform for functional tissue engineering of cartilage superficial zone. We also applied our technology for various cell studies, which is closely related to this proposal. For example, we developed several microfluidic devices for single-cell study, study of cell-cell interactions, and fast optimization of the combination of multiple factors on stem cell differentiations. Also we built a vasculature biomimicry microfluidic system. (Refer to the papers in Part C, particularly #3, 8, 9 papers)

16500916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500916.value: Central banks around the world implement policies to achieve a variety of goals. Price stability is a principal goal of monetary policy but other goals including exchange rate stability, business cycle stability and financial stability. In many cases, these goals are complementary, but not in every circumstance. This paper will try to identify the behaviour of central banks in periods when their goals come in conflict. The paper will focus on a set of 20 central banks that have implemented an inflation-targeting, monetary policy framework. Within this framework, central banks set a numerical guideline for the future path of inflation and adjust monetary instruments (typically the interest rate) when inflation forecasts deviate from the explicit guidelines. Such a framework is ripe for study because price stability is so transparent and well-defined. The project will identify the degree and frequency with which different policy goals conflict. We compare inflation forecasts with the stated numerical guidelines in order to find periods in which monetary policy is constrained to address price stability. The project will construct forecasts for each of the inflation-targeting countries under study. These will be compared with an updated database of historical inflation targets and the acceptable ranges for inflation drawn from central bank publications. The first part of the project examines outcomes for measures of business cycle stability, financial stability, and exchange rate stability, which can be constructed according to standard statistical methods. We can identify periods when monetary policy might be necessary to address each of these dimensions of the economy and compare this needs with the mandate. The next step is to assess how central banks adjust their policy behaviour during these periods of conflict. The second part of the project examines the stability of inflation expectations and how they are impacted by the existence of policy conflicts. Inflation targeting central banks adjust policy through adjustment in short-term interest rates. Inflation expectations pass through into long-term interest rates. 全球的中央银行（以下简称央行）执行不同的政策以达到不同的目标。物价稳定是货币政策的主要目标之一， 但其它货币政策的目标还包括汇率稳定，商业周期稳定和金融稳定。在很多情况下，这些目标是互补的，但不能说任何情况下这些目标都是互补的。这篇论文尝试识别在这些目标存在冲突的情形下中央银行的行为。本文集中讨论20个执行通货膨胀目标制（inflation-targeting）的货币框架的中央银行。在这种货币框架下，中央银行设定数值化的准则以引导通货膨胀的未来轨迹，同时在通货膨胀的预测值偏离目标值时调整货币工具（通常为利率）。 这种框架适合我们的研究，因为物价稳定的目标在该框架中很透明和明确。 这个项目将识别不同政策目标冲突的程度和频率。为了找到货币政策因需要稳定物价而受到约束的时期，我们对通胀预测和声明的数值化准则进行比较。同时，该项目将针对每一个研究样本内的国家建立预测。这些预测将与来自最新数据库的历史通货膨胀目标和央行公开发布的通货膨胀可接受范围进行比较。 该项目的第一部分将测试衡量商业周期稳定性、金融稳定性和汇率稳定性的指标的结果。这些指标均是根据标准的统计方法建立。我们能够识别在某些时期货币政策需要考虑这些经济中的各个维度，并且把这种需要和央行颁布的法令做对比。下一步我们将评估在这些目标冲突的期间，央行如何调整政策行为。 项目的第二部分测试通货膨胀预期的稳定性以及这个稳定性是怎样受到政策目标冲突的影响。执行通货膨胀目标制（inflation-targeting）的央行能够通过调控短期利率来调整政策。通货膨胀预期将传递到长期利率。

16501316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501316.value: As illegal reproduction of copyrighted works, piracy is a serious issue confronted by digital content providers nowadays. Just as rapid improvements in information technology have created more diverse digital content, they have also exacerbated the threat of piracy by making the process of reproducing and spreading pirated products much easier. Piracy has caused serious threats to the profitability of legal makers of digital products. In this project, we investigate how a firm selling digital products is influenced by piracy in terms of pricing, information disclosure policy and profitability. Specifically, we consider a monopolist, the quality of whose products is unknown to customers. It may choose to disclose the quality to the public at a positive cost. We are particularly interested in the following questions regarding how the firm fights piracy in such an asymmetric information setting: How does the firm jointly use the anti-piracy enforcement level, quality disclosure option and price to counter threats from piracy? Is it really the case that weak enforcement of copyright protection would always hurt the firm's profit? What would be the welfare implications if the public policy toward piracy exogenously changes? Besides, we are also interested in finding out the impacts of consumer behavior on the firm’s strategies. For example, many consumers may consider piracy to be morally unacceptable, and do not regard pirated products as proper substitutes for authentic digital products. However, other consumers have no problem with using the pirated versions. The magnitude of this group of consumers will be a key factor in shaping the strategies of the firm. In addition, the presence of piracy would cause a brand value loss to the brand owner. Some consumers that originally stuck to the authentic product would leave the market when they found out that many people were using the pirated products, and as a result they would not value the brand as high as before. We strive to find out how such consumer behaviour would impact the firm with information asymmetry. 數碼侵權對許多數碼服務公司構成嚴重的威脅。資訊科技的發展令到此種數碼侵權行為更容易出現，例如現在更容易抄襲和傳播盜版軟件。許多正版軟件公司利潤因此受到侵害。 在本方案，我研究一間數碼產品公司的產品定價，資訊披露和利潤如何受到侵權行為的影響。我研究一個壟斷者，顧客並不清楚其產品質量。這公司可選擇披露產品質量。當資訊並不對稱時，公司如何決定打擊侵權，披露產品資訊和定價? 保障侵權力度不足是否一定對公司不利？對社會效益如何影響？ 我亦研究顧客態度如何影響公司策略。侵權行動令許多買正貨的顧客影響對正品貨的觀感，對公司商譽亦帶來影響。當信息對顧客相對公司並不對稱時，侵權行為的作用是我研究的要點。

16501316.label: Realisation of objectives
16501316.value: Objective 1: I successfully created a research problem to investigate how a firm selling a newly developed digital product is affected by piracy in terms of pricing, quality disclosure strategy and profitability. The model represents a monopolistic digital-good firm and the quality of its product is unknown to prospective customers. The firm’s decision is regarding whether to disclose the quality information at a fixed cost to resolve the quality uncertainty faced by the customers. Objective 2: The problem is solved via a game-theoretic approach. This allows us to find that when the quality of the product is not too high so that the firm does not disclose the quality information, the firm may be surprisingly better off when pirating is costlier. This is because, with higher piracy cost, the firm has more incentives to disclose the quality, and, as a result, rational customers’ quality belief conditional on nondisclosure is lower, which leads to a lower profit. Objective 3: In positioning the paper with motivating examples, I collected some actual examples of software piracy and explored the extent and depth of their impacts. To this end, this paper helps to relate these real examples to our theoretical framework. By applying the lessons obtained from this study, the industry, hopefully is better equipped to combat piracy. A couple of research papers were completed during the period. The first one, “Digital Piracy and and Quality Disclosure,” was coauthored with Professor Zelong Yi of Shenzhen University and Professor Zike Cao of Erasmus University. The paper was submitted to Information Systems Research and went through the first round of review. Unfortunately, it was rejected during the second round, though the editor encouraged us to overcome the main concerns raised by the referees and resubmit the paper again. Therefore, I am working with my coauthors now to address their concerns. We plan to resubmit it afterwards. The second paper, “Impacts of Counterfeiting in a Global Supply Chain,” was coauthored with Professor Man Yu of HKUST and Professor Zelong Yi of Shenzhen University. The paper was submitted to Management Science and now undergoing major revision after the first round of review.

16501316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501316.value: The most novel insight arising from this project is that the publicly observable cost or difficulty of pirating digital goods may exert a strategic negative influence on a legal firm's profit, in addition to the deterrence effect it has on users of unauthorized copies of the digital product. The strategic impact exists because piracy cost alters the firm's quality disclosure strategy and thus consumers' expectation about the product quality. Consequently, the firm may obtain a larger profit when the copyright protection is less tight. Importantly, this strategic negative impact only applies to a firm whose product has a less favorable mix of attributes (e.g., compression rates of recorded music, definitions of movies, visual effects of video games) that consumers generally prefer (i.e., its vertical quality is lower). Therefore, for those star and signature products (e.g., blockbuster films, triple A video games, killer apps), the strategic negative influence of copyright protection is irrelevant and the profits from these products would always gain from tightened copyright protection. So, our analysis offers a new explanation for the fact that large companies are always eager to strengthen copyright protection while small indie companies seem not so worried about the threats from piracy. As widely acknowledged in both academia and practice, the gain in social welfare due to increased product variety is substantial in digital goods industries like eBooks, music, movies, software, etc., even though those increased niche products may not be as widely received as the hit products due to a less desirable mix of vertical quality attributes. So maintaining profitability of the niche products in these industries is crucial for the interests of social welfare. Unlike common wisdom, our study shows that the existence of piracy or slack copyright protection needs not to be devastating to the profitability of a niche product, although it is indeed detrimental to the profitability of a hit product. Moreover, when consumers are heterogeneous in their tastes of digital products and may sample pirated versions to ascertain their fits with the legal products (which is arguably more likely to be the case for niche products), niche-product firms have more incentives to tolerate the existence of piracy. The reason, in essence, is that piracy offers consumers a relatively less costly and risky option to discover products on the "long tail" that perfectly fit their individual tastes, even though these products do not necessarily deliver the highest values from the vertical quality attributes.

16501316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501316.value: This research funding also facilitated us to complete the other paper “Impacts of Counterfeiting in a Global Supply Chain”. In that paper there is perfect information between all the parties involved in the supply chain, whereas, asymmetric information is the central theme of the privacy paper. As one can image, counterfeit/privacy is a huge problem and yet to this date research in this area is still limited. Therefore, there exists ample opportunities for future research. The current study can be extended in several meaningful directions. First, it is reasonable to assume that consumers may not know the disclosure cost accurately. So formally incorporating consumers’ uncertainty about the true disclosure cost might be a good direction to extend the model, because consumers’ belief about the true disclosure cost will aﬀect how they attribute the ﬁrm’s non-disclosure decision. Second, one may extend the model to take into account the government’s decision on copyright enforcement level. Moreover, the government may achieve this through various instruments, like ﬁne on detection, tax on copying medium, or subsidy for legal purchase. Third, one can consider incorporating consumers’ learning of product quality over time via, e.g., word-of-mouth, in a dynamic setting.

16501316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501316.value: Piracy is commonly believed to be devastating to proﬁtability and innovation. For instance, the recent Business Software Alliance (BSA)’s Global Software Survey (GSS) estimated that software piracy rate is approximately 43% globally in 2013, resulting a total $62.7 billion lost revenue worldwide. Government agencies also tend to sympathize with the industry practitioners about the adverse consequences caused by piracy. However, this belief has been constantly challenged by academic researchers. In practice, the past decade has also witnessed increasingly divisive attitudes toward piracy in the industry. For example, EMI Music has completely abandoned DRM in all its tracks sold on iTunes Store. We aim to contribute to this debate through a perspective that is largely neglected by previous research—the ﬁrm’s quality disclosure incentives under the inﬂuence of piracy. As a result, we identify an important boundary condition for the common belief that tightening copyright enforcement beneﬁts a legal ﬁrm, i.e., whether the common belief holds or not is contingent on the vertical quality of the ﬁrm’s product.

16502816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502816.value: 笑一笑，十年少 “A heartfelt smile makes you ten years younger” – Chinese proverb The 2015 United Nations World Happiness Survey found that Hong Kong was ranked 72nd amongst the 158 surveyed countries, slipping 26 places from its rank of 46th in the first such survey conducted in 2012. Indeed, while our society scored well on objective indicators such as per capita GDP and life expectancy, which are known correlates of happiness (but only imperfectly so, Diener et al. 2015), the real “downer” came in the subjective questions that arguably tap emotions more directly. In these questions, Hong Kong scored an average of 5.75 on a scale from 0 (worst) to 10 (happiest) – barely above the mid-point mark. Occurring simultaneously with this negative development, the last few years have seen a large, but positive, trend in a different domain. Hong Kong is now almost exclusively a service-based economy. As of April 2015, according to the HK Government Information Services Department, the service sector contributed as much as 92.9% of our GDP. Indeed, social and personal services accounted respectively for 25% and 17% of GDP in 2013, and these proportions are only growing. Might these two trends be related to each other? Might they be in conflict? Received wisdom recommends service providers always deliver “service with a smile”. For example, the staff manual at a Disneyland restaurant states: “Make a big smile. The smile is necessary.” Correspondingly, research suggests that services delivered with smiles facilitate positive outcomes ranging from immediate satisfaction to long-term customer relationships (Hennig-Thurau et al. 2006). But what happens if service providers smile when they themselves are not happy? When, how, and under what conditions does smiling signal good service? Should people try to smile, to make their transaction partners and themselves feel better? This research investigates these questions. We study the value of a smile, in the contexts of commercial transactions and subjective wellbeing. We break this down into a “micro” set of questions regarding the effect of smiling in individual service transactions, and its more “macro” effect on subjective wellbeing (also known as “Gross National Happiness”; Kahneman and Krueger 2006). The first set will be studied experimentally in our lab, while the second set will be investigated using cross-national surveys. Our aim is to shed new light on the role of emotions in commercial behaviors and outcomes.

16502816.label: Realisation of objectives
16502816.value: Objective 1 has been realized fully (i.e., 100% completed). An article titled "Smiling Signals Intrinsic Motivation" is forthcoming at the Journal of Consumer Research. Objective 2 is proving harder to achieve. While data have been collected, the patterns that are emerging are not stable. The major attributable reason for this is that there have been significant socio-political changes around the world in recent years. Events such as Brexit, the election of Donald Trump, and the ongoing social situation in Hong Kong have large and relatively longlasting effects on subjective wellbeing. Evidently, the effects of smiling and beliefs pertaining to smiling are in contrast relatively less strong and tend to get drowned out. This is a particularly great challenge given that one of the key components of this effort was to assess cross-country differences and correlate with economic indicators. These issues are important and we are continuing to think about them, and revisit the data collected so far, to investigate possible leads that might give insights into how to proceed in terms of generating a publishable manuscript.

16502816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502816.value: In the published JCR article, we find that when the nature of an actor’s motivation is ambiguous, observers infer greater intrinsic motivation from the actors’ larger and more Duchenne-like smiles, and, correspondingly, actors strategically display larger and more Duchenne-like smiles if they want to signal intrinsic motivation to observers. In study 1, when ambiguity about endorsers’ motivation was primed, participants inferred greater intrinsic motivation underlying the testimonials if they saw endorsers displaying large Duchenne smiles compared to small smiles. Such inferences disappeared when ambiguity of motivation was not primed. Study 2a decomposed the sizes of smiles and their Duchenne-ness by adding a large non-Duchenne smile condition. Results suggested that in order for smiling to signal intrinsic motivation, size alone is not enough; the Duchenne feature is necessary. Study 2b replicated these findings and showed that the effect was mainly driven by positive inferences from large Duchenne smiles. This study also demonstrated the consequences of smiling on anticipated service quality, mediated by inferred intrinsic motivation. In study 3, participants who role-played endorsers submitted headshots with larger and more Duchenne-like smiles if they were given a goal to signal intrinsic (vs. extrinsic or no specific) motivation. Similarly, in study 4, participants who role-played entrepreneurs chose a larger and more Duchenne-like smile profile photo for their crowdfunding web page if they were given a goal to signal intrinsic (vs. extrinsic or no specific) motivation. Open-ended explanations of their choice revealed that they did so consciously and strategically. (This summary is taken from the General Discussion of the published article.)

16502816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502816.value: In the published article, we discuss several possible areas for future investigation based on the extant results. These include extending the investigation to video images from still photos, the possible roles of negative emotions and the signaling value of serious (versus smiling) faces, and characteristics of observers, including emotional intelligence and lay beliefs. As mentioned above, we are also interested in pursuing the multi-country investigation, and associating emotional gestures, responses, and wellbeing with more macro-level socio-economic indicators. Many areas of the world are undergoing intense socio-poliitical change these days, and the emotional toll on citizens is high. According to the South China Morning Post (10 January 2020), a recent study found that 2 million HongKongers (i.e., over 25% of the population) was suffering from Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder possibly attributable to the civil unrest that started in June 2019. This makes this research question extremely important and timely, and we hope to be able to study it systematically.

16502816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502816.value: In this research, we study how people may non-verbally communicate their intrinsic motivation. The nature of a person’s motivation (whether it is intrinsic or extrinsic) is a key predictor of how committed they are to a task, and hence how well they are likely to perform at it. However, it is difficult to reliably communicate and make inferences about such fine nuances regarding another person’s motivation. Building on the social functional view of emotion and the evolutionary and psychophysical characteristics of facial expression of emotions, this research suggests that displayed enjoyment, as evidenced by the size of someone’s smile, can serve as a strong non-verbal signal of intrinsic motivation. Across four studies, taking the perspective of both actors and observers, we find that people infer greater intrinsic motivation when they see others display big (vs. small) smiles, and that actors intuit this relationship, strategically displaying bigger smiles if they are given a goal to signal intrinsic (vs. extrinsic or no specific) motivation.

16507816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16507816.value: With proliferation of Web 2.0, an important information source for consumer purchase decisions is online reviews posted by others. Increasingly, online reviews have moved beyond written reviews and numeric ratings. Various platforms now encourage consumers to include photos of the purchases in their product reviews. The objective of this study is to examine the joint effects of text and photos posted by users. Specifically, we examine how text and photos in online reviews work in tandem to affect (i) review helpfulness and (ii) consumer behaviour. We hypothesize that consistency between text sentiment and photo appeal in an online review positively affects review helpfulness (H1). Furthermore, we expect the level of elaboration in the text to negatively moderate the impacts of text-photo consistency on review helpfulness (H2). In addition, we hypothesize an online review with a high-appeal product photo to engender stronger purchase intention than one with a low-appeal product photo (H3). However, due to negativity bias, we believe the relationship between photo appeal and purchase intention is positively moderated by text sentiment (H4). We intend to conduct an online experiment (Experiment 1) to test our hypotheses. We further propose to conduct another experiment (Experiment 2) to extend H3 and H4 by examining how online reviews affects consumers’ choices among multiple purchase options. 随着Web 2.0的扩散，影响消费者购买决定的一个重要信息来源是其他用户发布的网上评论。越来越多的网上评论已经不仅仅局限于文本评价和数字打分。如今，很多的网上平台鼓励消费者在撰写产品评论时加入产品的图片。这项工作的目标是研究用户评论中文本和图片的联合效应。具体来说，我们研究网上评论中的文本和图片是如何协同起来影响 (1) 评论的有用性；(2) 消费者行为。我们猜测，网上评论里文本情感和照片吸引力之间的一致性对评论的有用性有积极影响 (H1)。此外，我们预计，文本的详细程度负向调节文本-照片一致性对评论有用性的影响 (H2)。另外，我们预期一个包含高吸引力照片的评论比一个包含低吸引力照片的评论能引发更强的购买意向 (H3)。然而，由于负性偏见，我们相信文本情感对照片吸引力和消费者购买意向的关系有正向调节作用 (H4)。我们打算用在线实验（实验1）去测试我们的一系列假设。我们还提出进行另外一个实验（实验2）去研究网上评论如何影响消费者在多个购买选项中的选择，以此来扩展H3和H4。

16507816.label: Realisation of objectives
16507816.value: The aim of this project is to understand how users' product photos (or purchase images) and review text affected review helpfulness and consumers' purchase behaviors. We conducted a literature review of research that examines online reviews and found that (1) most studies focus on the effects of review text and (2) little attention has been paid to the impacts of consumers’ purchase images in online reviews. Moreover, the existing studies of purchase images emphasize primarily the presence and/or quantity of the images. Our research goes beyond the quantitative aspect of purchase images but consider the attributes of the images (specifically, visual appeal). More importantly, by looking at how attributes of the images and review content jointly affect consumers, this study better captures the information set that drives todays’ consumers decisions and behaviors. Based on our theorizing, we developed a set of hypotheses that relate to Objectives 1 and 2 of this project. Specifically, for Objective 1, we hypothesized: H1A: Reviews that are text–image consistent are more helpful than those without images. H1B: Reviews that are text–image inconsistent are less helpful than those without images. H2: The effect of text–image consistency on review helpfulness is stronger (weaker) when the review text is less (more) elaborated. For Objective 2: H3A: Including a high-appeal image in a review increases purchase intention. H3B: Including a low-appeal image in a review decreases purchase intention. H4A: Including a high-appeal image in a review increases purchase intention more when the text is negative than when it is positive. H4B: Including a low-appeal image in a review decreases purchase intention more when the text is positive than when it is negative. To test our hypotheses, we conducted a 3 (no image vs. high-appeal image vs. low-appeal image) ×2 (positive text vs. negative text) ×2 (elaborated text vs. non-elaborated text) ×2 (male vs. female) between-subjects online experiment. We included gender as a factor in our experiment as gender differences could occur in various aspects of online consumers’ attitudes and behaviors. Subjects were workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT), a popular and convenient platform for recruiting subjects for behavioral research, and our sample consisted of 844 subjects. The results show that show that including an image in a review improves the perceived review helpfulness only when the visual appeal is consistent with the text sentiment, and this effect is negatively moderated by review elaboration (Objective 1). Moreover, including a high-appeal image in a review weakly increases purchase intention, whereas including a low-appeal image strongly hurts purchase intention; both are attenuated by text–image consistency (Objective 2). Additional analyses suggest that females are more susceptible to purchase images than males when making purchase decisions. Objective 3 proposes to examine how online review affects actual purchasing behaviors and decisions. However, manipulating online reviews and random assignment of potential consumers in a field setting (in order to examine actual purchases) is highly challenging. More importantly, the fact that the treated reviews, especially the negative ones, could affect actual consumer’s perceptions and merchants’ sales in a field experiment raises ethnical concerns. We thus decided not to implement a field experiment to examine actual purchases. Nonetheless, as prior studies indicate strong correlation between intended and actual behaviors, we believe Objective 2 contributes to Objective 3 to some extent.

16507816.label: Major findings and research outcome
16507816.value: Our results show that adding an image improves review helpfulness when the image is consistent with the review text, supporting H1. However, the review does not become less helpful if the added image is inconsistent with the text. Thus, H1B is not supported. In addition, the effect of text–image consistency on review helpfulness is weaker when the review text is elaborated than when it is non-elaborated, supporting H2. The results also show that adding a high-appeal image to a text review marginally increases subjects’ purchase intention, weakly supporting H3A. However, adding a low-appeal image to a text review decreases purchase intention, supporting H3B. Finally, adding a high-appeal image to a text review enhances purchase intention when the text is negative but not when the text is positive, supporting H4A. On the other hand, adding a low-appeal image reduces purchase intention, regardless of whether the review text is positive or negative. However, such a negative effect is much stronger when the review text is positive, supporting H4B. Our findings have important theoretical implications. New studies should be mindful of not only the types and attributes of individual cues in the reviews but also the consistency among cues. This is important given that online reviews more and more include diverse cues (e.g., text and images), a trend that is likely to persist as (1) merchants and platforms increasingly encourage consumers to incorporate photos in their reviews and (2) consumers find it easy and convenient to supplement their textual reviews with rich media given the advances in technology. Research on online reviews should also recognize that a particular factor could have different and even contrasting effects on different outcomes of interest. Such a perspective can lead to interesting insights into and a more balanced picture of the impacts of online reviews. Our findings have implications for online platforms in which consumer reviews are critical. As adding purchase images may unexpectedly hurt purchase intention, it is not beneficial for platforms to highlight all reviews with these images. Instead, platforms can apply deep learning techniques to evaluate the visual appeal of purchase images and strategically highlight both positive and negative reviews in which the images are consistent with the review sentiment. Platforms could also incorporate text–image consistency into their review ranking systems to reduce the visibility of inconsistent reviews. For consumers who are satisfied with their purchase, platforms can provide guidelines on improving their images’ visual appeal.

16507816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16507816.value: First, our findings are based on a carefully controlled online experiment with a single review. An extension is to examine scenarios where multiple text-only and/or text and image reviews coexist. Second, our experiment is effective in identifying the causal effect of purchase images under different combinations of text and images, but the net effect depends on the mix of all the possibilities in real-life settings. Future research can use field or natural experiments on actual platforms to assess the overall effect of introducing the image feature in product reviews. Third, our experiment focused on clothing, which is an experience good whereby the quality and utility cannot be judged based on information about its attributes. Therefore, consumers may rely on additional visual cues to facilitate their decision-making. Expanding this study to search goods would give a more complete picture of the impact of consumers’ purchase images in product reviews.

16507816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16507816.value: Referring to online reviews is a key activity in today's consumers purchasing decision and these reviews increasingly contain both text and images. We examine how images in online reviews affect consumers' perception of review helpfulnesses and their purchase intention. While including purchase images increases the amount of information to potential customers, whether doing so makes the reviews more helpful depends on whether the images and textual comments elicit a consistent consumer response. Moreover, the positive effect of visual appeal of purchase images on purchase intention depends on review sentiment. A purchase image with high (low) visual appeal improves (hurts) purchase intention more when the review is negative (positive) than when it is positive (negative). One implication from this study is that well-intentioned, satisfied customers who provide purchase images in their positive reviews might not necessarily improve their reviews’ helpfulness and other consumers’ purchase intention.

16508416.label: Project Objectives
16508416.value: Develop an analytic model of strategic certifiers in e-commerce. Certifiers can exert effort to assess the reliability of retailers. Higher effort leads to higher accuracy in their assessment, but perfectly accurate assessment is prohibitively costly to obtain. In addition, certifiers may or may not disclose their true assessment results. This model highlights the impact of certifiers' strategic behavior on the accuracy of certifications. Develop a model of competition between two certifiers. With competing certifiers, one with more accurate assessment technology than the other, certifiers' differing incentive to collude as well as retailers' strategic choice of certifiers further complicate the resulting quality of certifications. How does competition affect the accuracy of certifications? Will the more accurate certifier be chosen more or less often by retailers? How would consumers interpret retailers' choice of certifiers? This model allows us to answer these interesting questions that are of great practical values as well. Design several regulation schemes that penalize collusion between certifiers and retailers. Such schemes will be designed to account for these aspects: Who should be punished once a collusion is suspected; that is, an unqualified certification is discovered? To what extent should the colluding parties be penalized? Extend the model to examine the different equilibrium outcomes when regulation is in place. Specifically, how would certifiers, retailers, or consumers adjust their strategies knowing collusion may be penalized? Conduct welfare analysis and comparative statics to offer policy implications regarding the design and choice of different regulation schemes.

16508416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16508416.value: 电子商务经历了飞速的发展。以美国零售业为例，在2000年，0.07%的销售来自电子商务，而这一数字在2015年的第二季度已增长至7.2%。根据高盛的一份报告，2013年美国的电子商务总额高达9.63亿美元。尽管电子商务已经有了如此快速的进展，其发展空间依然很大。其中一个关键性的阻碍来自于消费者在购买过程中信任和保障的缺失。在线下购物中，零售商的选址，以及与客户面对面的交流都能有效的让消费者获得相关的质量信息。而这些渠道在电子商务中都很难实现。尽管一些大型电子商务网站可以依靠自身的品牌效应以及信誉获得客户，绝大多数网站都需要其他的途径。而电子商务的低门槛特质以及网络的匿名化都让信誉问题更加严峻。为了解决这一现状，很多网上零售商都通过第三方认证机构来获得消费者的信任。通过认证的零售商通常在他们的网站上列明认证证书以取信客户。类似的认证机构，比如TRUSTe主要包含网站的安全及隐私保护程度，而VeriSign则侧重交易的安全性。虽然第三方认证的本意是让增加消费者的信任，现有的研究发现认证机构在有些情况下并不能达到这一目的。本项目的课题是用博弈论的方法去分析认证机构，网上零售商以及网上消费者三方之间的互动和决策，从而研究认证机构的有效性以及需要的条件。认证机构与网上零售商之间有可能存在经济利益，从而提供有偏差的信息给消费者。同时，认证机构之间的竞争更对认证的有效性造成威胁。在项目中，关于如何规范管理认证机构也会提出相应的分析和实施建议。

16508416.label: Realisation of objectives
16508416.value: The PI has addressed the project objectives through developing an game theory model with competitive certifiers/auditors and analyzing their interactions as well as their responses to regulations. We study two variants of the model, one with non-strategic auditors who report their internal results no matter what they are, and one with strategic auditors who have the latitude to exercise their judgement in choosing their report. We assume that the power is in the hands of the retailers and competition between the auditors drives their economic profits to zero. We also provide a useful benchmark, the non-strategic auditor case is of independent interest. In both the strategic and the non-strategic auditor analysis, our focus is on equilibria with: active competition between the certifiers; certifications containing useful information; and investors earning a market rate of return on their purchases. Active competition is the requirement that, in equilibrium, both auditors have clients. The production of useful information is the requirement that, in equilibrium, investors are willing to invest after the auditors assert that the retailer claim to be in a good state is supported. The investors earning a market rate of return in equilibrium is the requirement that investors' prior belief for a good situation is in an intermediate range: if their prior belief is too high, investors would earn higher than a market rate of return; however, the rate of returns from both types of firms will adjust according to investors' high demand and eventually bring the prior belief back to the intermediate range. Similar adjustments will happen if the prior belief is too low, and the rate of returns are not under market pressure only when the prior belief is in the intermediate range. Through analysis of this sophisticated model, several meaningful insights relating to the stated objectives are produced. 1. The only outcomes satisfying the above three requirements arise from a set of mixed-pooling equilibria in which different proportions of both types of firms patronize the different auditors. In working with the indifference conditions that characterize a mixed strategy equilibrium, one determines the likelihood that one person will make a choice between options that seem equally good to them by the condition that someone else be made indifferent between their options. This can be counter-intuitive, and we follow the large population interpretation of equilibria with randomization and interpret as there being a small amount of smoothly distributed, independent, private information about perturbations to player payoffs to different actions. In the game with perturbations, with probability 1, every player has a strict preference for their choice of actions, and when the perturbations are small, the outcome is arbitrarily close to the mixed strategy equilibrium. From this perspective, investors' randomization in the investment decision is a population distribution of judgement calls after reading the same firm statement and auditor certification, but bringing to it a different set of experiences and investment needs. In the same way, firms' randomization over auditors reflects a steady state proportion of a population of firms, and the steady state proportion has stable dynamics. The auditors' randomized decisions about whether or not to support a firm's statement of being in a good state is also a population distribution, here it is a proportion of the judgement calls, some of them perhaps quite close and difficult, that go in the firm's favor. 2. Auditor liability is ineffective at increasing the accuracy of the certification market, but management liability is effective. To put it another way, fines/punishment for failures to detect management deception are less effective than fines/punishment for the deceptive practices. This is because, when audit services are demanded inelastically, fines levied on competitive auditors are entirely passed through, as a fixed cost, to the firms purchasing the audit services. Unless these costs are sufficiently large to close the market, they have no other effect. 3. Differences in auditor quality reduce investment, and in the case of strategic auditors, competition introduces pressures for the better auditors to lower their accuracies and to act more like the weaker auditors. 4. In the presence of liability and/or reputation concerns by auditors, contingent fees, even if only implicit, are necessary to induce quality reporting. 5. When the proportion of firms in a good situation is lowered, e.g. after a cyclical downturn or a significant negative macro shock, loosening audit standards can only make matters worse. Lowering audit standards will either further reduce investment, or, if the shock has seriously disrupted investment, lowering audit standards increases the degree of recovery necessary to return investment to regular levels.

16508416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16508416.value: This project examined the role of regulation determining the quality of information produced by certifiers in a competitive market. As a benchmark model, we began with non-strategic certifiers, and then turned to the case of strategic certifiers. The mistakes of non-strategic certifiers are due only to limitations of auditing technology. In this case, market equilibrium accuracy is produced by a combination of firms' choice of certifiers, which is in turn influenced by the certifiers' abilities and costs. We found that penalties levied on certifiers have no effects on firm behavior, essentially because such penalties are passed through, as a fixed cost of doing business, to the firms being audited. However, the presence of such fees effectively reduces investor confidence in the certification process. By contrast, provided it is the decision makers, management and not the shareholders, who pay, penalties levied on firms for their mis-statement have a strong positive effect on the certification market. A useful auxiliary result is that decreasing certifier accuracy is a bad policy response to market downturns. With only relatively minor caveats, these result carry through to the case of strategic certifiers when we focus attention on the equilibria that are optimal for the firms buying the certification.

16508416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16508416.value: While all proposed objectives are thoroughly addressed, there are other potentially interesting and relevant issues to explore in the future. For instance, investors with differing experience may interpret the certification differently, which can result in varying investment/purchase decisions. It could be worthwhile to extend the analysis by considering investors' heterogeneity and the corresponding effect on firms' and certifiers' decisions.

16508416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16508416.value: Organizations face a competitive certification market for their statements, the statements do not convince third parties unless certified, the organizations are sometimes better served by a lie, and honest mistakes are possible. In our model of such a market: if certifiers are liable for mistakes, certifier contracts must be contingent; when certification is inelastically demanded, increases in certifier liability effectively reduce third party trust; organizational liability for mis-statements has a strong deterrent effect on mis-statements and increases third party trust; and after a strong negative shock to the financial system, loosening certification standards can only make it harder to raise third party trust levels.
