16510416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16510416.value: Gift giving is a multibillion dollar industry and people frequently buy gifts for friends, family members and corporate partners. However, buying the right gift is difficult, because people need to imagine what the receiver would like to get. As a consequence, many resources (money, time and effort) are wasted in buying gifts that are not valued by the receiver. This deadweight loss of gift giving is estimated by economists to be between 10 percent and one-third of the total value that is spent on gifts. Not surprisingly, there is a lot of academic interest in understanding how consumers make gift choices and which factors influence them, but there are no quantitative choice models that analyze gift choices. Choice models are powerful tools for providing deeper insights into the underlying factors that drive consumer decisions. The overall aim of this research project is to fill this gap through the development of a new gift-choice model. A challenge in testing this choice model empirically is to obtain gift-choice data that have information about both the gift giver as well as the receiver. To obtain such information, a second goal of this research is to extend choice-based conjoint experiments for gift giving situations. Choice-based conjoint experiments are popular tools in marketing to analyze choice behavior of consumers, but this tool needs to be extended to investigate gift choices. The proposed methodology aims to provide novel insights into the effects of different marketing strategies on gift choices, in particular pricing, gift cards, and customer reviews and sales ranks in situations where consumers purchase gifts online. The outcomes of this research may result in practical tools for managers and policymakers to help consumers make better gift choices. The proposed methodology will help the understanding of which marketing activities, such as pricing, reviews or gift cards can help reduce the deadweight loss of gift giving. 禮物的購買每年創造了上千億美元的消費額，人們會經常性的為朋友、家人、以及同事購買禮物。然而，選擇“正確的”禮物並不容易，因為送禮者需要預估收禮者喜歡收到的禮物。因為沒有準確的偏好資訊，送禮者往往會在送禮上浪費很多有用的資源（金錢、時間、和努力）但卻並不被收禮者所看重。經濟學家估計送禮造成的無謂損失約為禮物價格的十分之一到三分之一。因此可以想見，有很多研究希望理解人們是如何做出送禮選擇的，以及人們的選擇受到哪些因素的影響。儘管選擇模型是一個深入研究消費者行為決策的有力工具，文獻中並沒有研究使用定量的選擇模型來分析人們的禮物選擇。 此研究專案的主要目的是填補缺少禮物選擇模型的這一理論空白。然而我們面臨的一大挑戰是缺少合適的資料，使得我們可以同時獲得關於送禮者以及收禮者的偏好資訊。為了克服這一障礙，我們的研究專案的另一個目標是擴展基於選擇的聯合實驗方法，使之適用于研究送禮行為。基於選擇的聯合實驗是一種廣泛應用于分析消費者選擇行為的方法，我們把這種方法改為兩個步驟用來研究送禮行為。改進後的聯合實驗使得我們可以深入研究各種市場行銷策略對消費者禮物選擇的影響，特別是定價，禮品卡，消費者評價，線上上購買情境下銷量排名等的影響。通過此研究，管理者和政策制定者可以幫助消費者做出更好的決策，也可以使我們更好的理解採用哪些行銷方法，例如通過何種定價方式、評價、以及禮品卡的銷售可以減少送禮過程中的無謂損失。

16510416.label: Realisation of objectives
16510416.value: We achieved the objectives of this project successfully. One paper has been published in the Journal of Marketing Research (a leading journal in the field). This paper was impactful and was selected as runner-up for the 2019 Lehmann award for best dissertation-based article published in Journal of Marketing Research and Journal of Marketing. As noted by the RGC panel in the midterm report, the first round of this paper was submitted in September 2016, just before the official start of this project. To clarify this, as acknowledged and cited in the proposal, we already finished a successful pilot study that was part of Sherry (Shi) Wang’s MPhil thesis (Wang 2015). After submitting the proposal, we decided to continue working on this project. This process went faster than expected and we were able to submit a first version of the paper in September 2016. To obtain feedback before initial submission, it was successfully presented at two international conferences in 2016 (Marketing Science in Shanghai: June 2016, and Marketing Dynamics in Hamburg: July 2016). RGC funding was used to execute the revision, which was significant and involved data collection and modeling efforts. After this major revision, the paper was quickly accepted, highlighting its quality, which is also in line with the selection as runner-up for the award. Furthermore, RGC funding contributed to the dissemination of the paper, as it was used as Wang’s job market presentation at the AMA conference in Boston (job market papers are not part of the conference schedule, and therefore it is not reported in the conference output in Section 9). It was also disseminated at leading universities, such as Ohio State University, Tilburg University, Erasmus University, Bocconi, University of Amsterdam, and University of New South Wales. Based on this work, Sherry obtained a job as assistant professor at Ohio State University. In addition, follow-up (eye-tracking) studies were executed. These studies were discussed at the Marketing Science Conference (Los Angeles 2017), where it was efficient to meet with the Co-I. Below, I describe how we addressed the five objectives of this project. 1. Developing a Bayesian choice model for gift giving that is based on behavioral theories of gift giving: This was the core of our modeling efforts and our proposal. We developed a new Bayesian choice model that can predict gift choices, depending on the characteristics of the giver and the receiver. Compared to previous choice models that incorporate attribute preferences and price sensitivity, the gift choice model considers both the preferences of the giver and receiver. In addition, it also captures the givers’ uncertainty about receivers’ preferences. This component is critical, as it captures the relative importance of both givers’ and receivers’ preferences and it is also an important factor to explain price sensitivity. The model is implemented in Matlab, and all the posterior distributions are published in our Journal of Marketing Research paper. 2. Development of a choice-based conjoint experiment that allows us to collect data about gift choices, as well as other important information such as the relationship between gift giver and receiver: We developed a new conjoint methodology to understand how gift preferences are formed. Compared to traditional choice-based conjoint experiments, our choice-based conjoint experiment for gift giving has the following important components. First, subjects are invited in pairs instead of alone. Second, in addition to choosing for themselves (as in traditional conjoint experiments), subjects also choose gifts for their partner in a second stage. The two choice stages allow us to analyze the role of preferences of both givers and receivers in gift choices, and we are the first to do this. Third, we manipulated the uncertainty of givers about receivers’ preferences by providing feedback of receivers’ choices depending on the experimental conditions of subjects. This conjoint experiment provides detailed choice data that is input for our Bayesian choice model for gift giving. 3. Understanding the underlying factors that determine price sensitivity in gift giving and how this relates to uncertainty about the receivers’ preferences. Our newly designed choice-based conjoint experiment for gift giving, in combination with our Bayesian gift choice model, allowed us to understand the role of givers’ uncertainty about receivers’ preferences. We found that givers who face high uncertainty rely more on their own preferences. This can be explained from a Bayesian learning perspective, in which givers own preferences are used as prior for gift preferences. Moreover, givers update their gift preferences based on their information about receivers’ preferences. Importantly, we also found that givers’ uncertainty strongly impacted their price sensitivity. In contrast to situations where people buy for themselves and become more price sensitive when they are uncertain about their preferences, we found the opposite for gift giving. To be specific, givers are less price sensitive when they are uncertain about the receivers’ preferences. This is a new finding and has important theoretical and practical implications. 4. Understanding how consumers value gift cards when choosing gifts: We were able to answer this question by analyzing the data from our choice-based conjoint experiments for gift giving. Our results show how givers form preferences and when they are more likely to buy gift cards. In addition, in one of our experiments we asked follow-up questions that allowed us to directly measure why customers buy gifts, which revealed that customers avoid being perceived as cheap. These results imply that givers value gift cards more when they are uncertain about receivers’ preferences. In such situations, givers are more likely to buy gift cards. Hence, givers value gift cards more when they are uncertain about the receivers’ preferences. 5. Understanding the role of reviews and sales rank information in online shopping for gifts: To address this question, we first collected eye-tracking data in a choice-based conjoint study of gift giving to understand how customers process information in online shopping. Our hypothesis was that givers process information differently compared to when they are choosing for themselves. To our surprise, we did not find significant differences in our eye-tracking study between buying for self or choosing gifts. Subsequently, we ran another eye-tracking study at HKUST, to understand how online ads influences gift choice behavior. Similar to sales rank and reviews, advertising is able to reduce customer uncertainty and affect gift choice and preferences. We found that such information affected the speed with which customers choose their gifts. The findings of this experiment are presented in a working paper that is under review at Journal of Consumer Research. Second, given that we did not find differences between gift giving scenarios and own choices, we started to investigate how customers process reviews and use this information to update their preferences. Using a large online customer panel in the US, we recruited 800 participants who participated in a choice study in which they could select different online reviews before making a final choice. Interestingly, we find that customers are more interested in reading negative reviews, but these reviews do not necessarily have a negative impact on the final choice outcome. We are currently in the process in developing a new study and synthesizing our findings that should appear in a new working paper that we plan to submit to Journal of Marketing Research.

16510416.label: Major findings and research outcome
16510416.value: This research provided both methodological and substantive findings. Methodologically, we developed a new gift choice model that can be easily estimated using Bayesian techniques. An important output of this project is therefore our estimation algorithm, and the detailed estimation steps are published in the Web Appendix of our Journal of Marketing Research article. Compared to previous choice models, our model considers preferences of both the giver and the receiver, and integrates these two components depending on the givers’ uncertainty about receivers’ preferences. In addition to the Bayesian model we developed a new experimental method to collect gift choice data based on choice-based conjoint experiments. A choice-based conjoint experiment is a popular methodology in academia as well as in practice to understand how consumers form preferences for products. However, as we showed in this project, gift preferences are formed differently, which cannot be understood using traditional conjoint experiments. Substantively, our research provided new insights on how people choose gifts for others. First, we find that givers are less price sensitive compared to buying for themselves. This is an important finding and provides a novel explanation about the deadweight loss of gift giving. Second, we find that gift preferences are a weighted average between givers own preferences and the preferences of the receivers. The weight of these two components depends on the givers’ uncertainty about receivers’ preferences. Third, we illustrate the important impact of givers price sensitivity on total welfare loss. Especially in product categories where there are small differences between products (i.e. wines and perfumes), most of the welfare loss is driven by price sensitivity, and not by inaccurate predictions of receivers’ preferences as argued in previous research. Fourth, we show that advertising can reduce uncertainty, which facilitates gift choice process.

16510416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16510416.value: Our model and findings provide many opportunities for future research, and some of them we already implemented as reflected by a working paper that is currently under review. In particular, it would be interesting to use our methodology to study the effects of different marketing strategies on gift choices. In a current working paper, we show that people implement their gift choices faster after seeing an ad that reduces their uncertainty. Furthermore, it would be valuable to apply our Bayesian choice model to actual sales data. Such information could potentially be obtained through household panel data that provides information about whether a specific purchase is a gift. While traditional panel data does not indicate whether a purchase is a gift, such information may potentially be available from online stores. Customers frequently buy gifts online that are subsequently sent directly to receivers of the gifts. In the future, we hope to collaborate with online stores that can share with us such data.

16510416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16510416.value: Gift giving generates large revenues for businesses, corresponding to 17.6 percent of retail sales in Hong Kong. Despite their importance, retailers tend to follow the same marketing strategies for gifts as for other products or services. Moreover, gift giving may also lead to a welfare losses, as receivers often attach lower values to gifts than givers paid for. This project developed new research methodologies to better understand how consumers choose gifts. These methods provided new insights on how givers form preferences, and under what conditions these deviate from receivers’ preferences. Interestingly, in addition to inaccurate preferences as reported in previous research, this project also found that givers are less price sensitive, explaining why they overspend on gifts. The reason for this bias is that givers use price to signal the importance their relationship with the receiver, especially when they don’t know what the receiver likes. Importantly, depending on market conditions, this reduced price sensitivity contributed stronger to welfare losses than inaccurate gift preferences, explaining why givers may run into financial problems. In addition, our research provides important insights to retailers and policy makers to improve their marketing strategies to help givers to improve their gift choices.

16511916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16511916.value: What happens when CEO and chair positions are separated in a corporation? Do the two corporate leaders get along? Can they work together productively to serve the best interests of shareholders? A decade after the reform of corporate governance since 2002, which fostered an environment favoring the separation of the two roles (Cullinan, Roush, & Zheng, 2012), these questions remain largely unanswered. The lack of studies on factors affecting chair-CEO interactions does not match the growing trend of chair-CEO role separation (SpencerStuart, 2014). We aim to address this unsatisfactory state of current research. We recognize that, although the chair is given the formal authority to monitor and advise the CEO, informal and social forces may either hinder or facility his/her capacity to exercise this authority. We highlight the status difference between the chair and CEO as the social cue guiding the interactions between the two leaders. Specifically, we propose that a chair with higher social status than the CEO is in a better position to effectively monitor the CEO and thus can help reduce managerial agency problems. Furthermore, both formal and informal forces exist to moderate the baseline relationship to either the chair’s or the CEO’s favor. Such forces may include the demographic similarity between the chair and the CEO, other directors’ demographic similarity with the chair or the CEO, and board independence. These propositions will be tested based on a sample of U.S. public firms. The proposed study has the potential to enrich corporate governance literature by focusing on the question of “when”, rather than “if.” The increasingly prevalent chair-CEO separation movement will gain practical insights from our research. It helps unearth an array of factors that potentially influence the effectiveness of the interactions between the two corporate leaders and will likely provoke more future studies along this important line. Our research will also shed light on social status research by focusing on dyadic interactions between social elites. By implication, this study should be able to provide actionable suggestions with regard to how to maximize the fit between the chair and the CEO as well as how to facilitate a constructive relationship between the two. 董事長不再兼任CEO之後會發生什麼？這兩名公司最高層的領導可以和睦相處嗎？他們能夠有效發揮作用共同為股東利益服務嗎？雖然2002年開始進行公司治理改革，提倡將這兩個職位分開已經十年有餘(Cullinan, Roush, & Zheng, 2012) ，這些問題仍然沒有答案。 董事長不兼任CEO的趨勢日漸增強(Spencer Stuart, 2014)，研究影響二人互動因素的學術論文卻很稀缺。因此，本項研究意在填補相關空缺。我們認識到，雖然董事長擁有監督和指導CEO的權利，但是非正式的、社會性的因素有可能影響董事長能否有效發揮這一正式的權威。我們特別指出，兩位領導人之間社會地位的差異是引領二人互動的信號。具體地說，我們認為董事長的總體社會地位要高於CEO才能做到有效監督，從而減少CEO的委託代理問題。同時， 其他正式和非正式的因素能調節上述假設關係。這些因素包括董事長和CEO的背景相似性、其他董事與董事長或CEO的背景相似性、董事會獨立性等等。我們計劃從美國上市公司中採樣，對我們的理論假設進行實證。 有別與以往的公司治理研究，此項研究回答的不是董事長和CEO要不要分開的問題，而是什麼情況下的分開好的問題。我們的研究結果將為董事長和CEO職位的設置和人選提供系統性的證據，從而找到更為匹配的董事長和CEO組合，幫助提高二者互動的有效性。未來的學術研究可以沿此方向，進一步探索社會地位如何影響社會菁英間的互動。

16512016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16512016.value: During the last few years, many countries including most EU members have mandated the engagement partner signatures in audit reports. One important rationale for such legislation is to enhance audit quality by increasing audit partner accountability. This argument sounds intuitive, in that if engagement auditors anticipate that they will be held responsible for low quality audits, they would have incentives to ensure audit quality. While poor audit quality seems to negatively affect the entire audit firm or a specific audit office (e.g., Weber et al. 2008; Skinner and Srinivasan 2012; Swanquist and Whited 2015), we notice that there is little evidence about how audit quality affects engagement auditors on a personal level. In this study, we will visit this issue by investigating whether engagement audit partners in China suffer career downgrades when audit failure occurs. Notably, China has mandated the signature of two signing partners in audit report of public firms’ financial filings for more than two decades (Gul, Wu, and Yang, 2013), which gives us enough sample period to trace the audit partners’ career path subsequent to audit failures. Following prior studies (e.g., Knechel, Niemi, and Zerni 2013), we will use the incidence of client financial misstatements to construct two types of audit failures: (1) Type I error (Overconservatism): if the audit partner issues a modified opinion to a client that ends up having no restatement afterwards for that specific financial report; and (2) Type II error (AuditFailure): the audit partner fails to issue a modified opinion on a client’s financial reports that turns out to be restated later. For career downgrades, we consider the following two types of penalties: (1) if the engagement partner leaves the current audit firms and moves to a smaller audit firm which can only provide attestation service to private clients; or (2) the engagement partner cease to sign any audit report for public clients for at least three consecutive years subsequent to the announcement of client restatements. Audit partners subject to these penalties basically lose the status of auditing publicly listed clients, which is much more serious than a mere reduction in compensation (e.g., Knechel, Niemi, and Zerni 2013). Our study aims to examine whether individual audit partners experience a career downgrade if either one of two audit errors occur.

16512016.label: Realisation of objectives
16512016.value: The first objective has been fully achieved. We find that signing auditors experience career downgrades when their clients experience accounting restatements. specifically, This study examines the personal career outcomes of auditors who experience client restatements. Using information on individual auditors from China, we find that auditors are more likely to lose the privilege of auditing public clients or to be forced to leave the firm if their clients experience restatements. We also find that signing auditors are not held accountable if they issue “relevant” opinions to specifically indicate the restated account(s) during the misstatement period. In contrast, issuing a modified audit opinion that is irrelevant to the misstatement does not shield the signing auditors from being disciplined. In a cross-sectional analysis, we find that signing auditors are disciplined for failing to detect client restatements in advance, regardless of whether they work for a Big 4 firm, local Big 10 firm, or other local firm. We further find that auditors with client restatements are more likely to be penalized when the error occurs with more important clients or when individual auditors work in a less concentrated audit market. We have also shown three benefits for audit firms that discipline auditors for audit errors: (1) among audit firms with client restatements, those that penalize auditors are less likely to have client restatements in the future than those that do not; (2) audit firms that discipline signing auditors for audit errors experience a significantly larger increase in market share relative to those that do not; and (3) the clients of audit firms that hold signing auditors accountable for audit errors experience an increased earnings response coefficient (ERC) during the disciplinary year. These results indicate that taking disciplinary action against signing auditors reflects the audit firm’s determination to improve audit quality and increases clients’ and investors’ confidence in the firm and the audited financial reports. Our findings are consistent with the evolutionary economics claim that for institutions such as audit firms, establishing a mechanism to punish/discipline misbehavior is crucial for ensuring cooperation, fairness, and trust within the organization. Such social norms are particularly important for organizations such as audit firms, which rely heavily on human capital to succeed. Further, having a clear reward/disciplinary system also helps audit firms attract and retain capable auditors, which may be particularly critical for local Chinese audit firms in competing with the international Big 4. To summarize, our study suggests that even with low litigation risk, audit firms in emerging countries such as China have incentives to discipline audit failures to maintain audit quality. The second and the third objectives are fully addressed too. While our findings suggest that individual auditors are penalized when audit errors occur, such disciplinary action comes at a cost. For example, the audit firm loses the disciplined auditor’s expertise and experience when he/she is forced to quit or stop auditing public clients. In addition, the incoming auditor needs time to become familiar with the audit team and clients. These adjustment costs suggest that audit firms will not penalize signing auditors unless the benefits outweigh the costs. We argue that a major reason for audit firms to discipline auditors who commit errors is to signal their determination to improve audit quality and restore the audit firms’ damaged reputation (e.g., Mande and Son [2013]; Hennes, Leone, and Miller [2014]). Such a signal motivates audit staff to exert more effort and apply more due diligence in their future work. Thus, we predict that relative to non-disciplining audit firms, audit firms that penalize auditors for audit errors are subsequently associated with a more pronounced improvement in audit quality. In addition, we expect that by disciplining auditors for errors, audit firms can mitigate market share loss or even increase the firm’s market share if existing clients’ confidence in the audit firm increases. Our results confirm the predictions related to the benefits of disciplinary action against auditors who have committed errors. We find that relative to non-disciplining firms, disciplining audit firms experience a significant decrease in client restatements after disciplinary action. Furthermore, the disciplining firms experience higher client growth. In addition, their clients experience higher earnings response coefficients in the year after disciplinary action. Together, these results demonstrate the benefits of the signaling effect conveyed by disciplinary action.

16512016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16512016.value: Our study suggests that individual auditors experience career downgrades in China if they exhibit low audit quality. This suggests that individual auditors could be penalized for audit failure even when litigation is low. The next question to explore is whether our findings can be generalized to other countries with higher litigation risk. This is ex ante an empirical question. On one hand, countries with high litigation costs typically are developed countries with competitive audit profession , so holding auditors for audit failures sounds natural. On the other hand, countries with high litigation risk may rely on the legal system to incentivize auditors so audit firms are less likely to penalize signing auditors for audit failures. This question can be easily address by using US or UK data, where signing auditors are identified in the audit report.

16512016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16512016.value: This study shows that auditors who sign the audit reports of public clients face negative career consequences when there are client restatements. Specifically, we find that signing auditors in China are downgraded to auditing private clients or leave the firm after experiencing client restatements, but disciplinary action is less likely if signing auditors issue a modified audit opinion related to the potential misstatement. Further analyses show that auditors are more likely to experience career downgrades when located in a less concentrated audit market or when such errors occur with more important clients. Notably, we find some positive outcomes of audit firms’ disciplinary action against auditors, including a reduction in the rate of client restatements and prevention of market share loss. In sum, our findings suggest that individual auditors in China face adverse career consequences when they produce poor-quality audits.

16512916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16512916.value: Margin borrowing is a widely used tool for investors to build leveraged positions. Margin buying has been heavily blamed for the 1930s market crash in the United States and the recent downturn of the Chinese stock market. Previous studies suggest that borrowing constraints have important implications for asset prices. Several theoretical studies show that when investors face borrowing constraints, they tilt their investment portfolios toward high beta stocks. While this result is theoretically intuitive and appealing, empirical evidence is limited. Frazzini and Pedersen (2014) show that a betting against beta (BAB) factor, which buys leveraged low-beta assets and sells de-leveraged high-beta assets, generates a significant positive alpha. However, they find that there is a negative relation between the BAB factor return and the level of funding constraints, which is puzzling since it is contrary to the theory. In contrast, Jylha (2014) finds that the security market line (SML) flattens when margin constraints tighten, which suggests a positive relation between the return of the BAB factor and the level of margin constraints. The mixed evidence on the relation between the SML and funding constraints may be due to measurement errors and omitted variable problems. The TED spread used in Frazzini and Pedersen (2014) may not be a perfect measure of funding constraints. More importantly, changes in funding constraints may be correlated with other aggregate variables, which cloud the identification of the effect of funding constraints per se. This proposal attempts to identify the effect of margin constraints using a unique setup in the Chinese stock market. During 2010-2014, China gradually allows stocks to be purchased on margin and sold short. The designated list starts from 90 stocks and is later expanded to 893 stocks as of December 2014 after four major revisions. Since stocks are added to the list at different times, we can use stocks included in the designated list as the treatment group and stocks left outside the list as the control group. This staggered addition allows us to more cleanly identify the effect of margin trading on asset prices, including the SML, volatility, and market crash behavior. The results of this project will contribute to the literature on how borrowing constraints and margin trading affect asset prices. It will provide a better understanding of risks under market imperfections. The findings should be useful and important for investors and governments in Hong Kong, mainland China, and around the world. 保證金借款是為投資者建立槓桿頭寸廣泛使用的工具。人們一直在大力指責保證金買盤是導致美國上世紀30年代股市崩盤和近期中國股市低迷的原因。以往的研究表明，借款約束對資產價格產生重要影響。幾個理論研究表明，當投資者面臨借貸約束時，他們的投資組合傾斜的向高系統性風險(貝它)的股票。 雖然這個結果在理論上是直觀的，吸引人的，但經驗證據是有限的。Frazzini和Pedersen (2014）發現，一個針對系統性風險(貝它)對賭的因子(BAB), 就是說槓桿買低貝它值資產和賣出去槓桿高貝它資產的投注，可以賺取顯著超額正面的回報。然而，他們發現的是BAB因子和資金緊張程度成反比，這是令人費解的，因為它違背了理論之間的正相關關係。相比之下，Jylha（2014）發現證券市場線（SML）在保證金約束收緊時比較平坦，這表明了BAB因子和保證金限制程度之間的關係是正相關的。 SML和資金的限制之間的關係的證據混混雜不清的原因可能是由於衡量誤差和變量遺漏的問題。在Frazzini和Pedersen（2014）所使用的TED利差可能不是資金緊張完美的衡量。更重要的是，資金緊張的變化可能與其他匯總變量有相關，這使獲得資金緊張效果的鑑定模糊不清。 本提案試圖找出使用了中國股市保證金約束作用的獨特設置。從2010 - 2014年期間，中國逐步允許股票進行保證金購買和賣空。指定的名單由90股開始，經過四次重大修訂後，擴大到2014年12月的893股票。由於股票在不同的時間添加到列表中，我們可以使用不包含在指定名單的股票作為對照組，而列表中的股票則作為治療組。這樣交錯允許股票進行保證金購買和賣空，使我們能夠更清晰地識別保證金交易對資產價格，包括SML，波動性和市場崩潰行為的影響。 本項目的結果將對借貸約束和融資融券如何影響資產價格的文獻有重大的貢獻。它將提供我們對在市場缺陷下的風險有更好的理解。調查結果應該對香港，中國內地和世界各地投資者和政府有用和重要。

16512916.label: Realisation of objectives
16512916.value: The major objectives of this project are to test whether the relaxation of margin trading restrictions affect (i) asset prices, (ii) stock return volatility, and (iii) whether the effects are more pronounced during market down turns. We also extend to examine the real effect of the relaxation of margin trading restrictions on corporate investments and investment efficiency. We find that the relaxation of margin trading restrictions affect asset prices. In particular, after margin trading restrictions are lifted, the security market line (SML) becomes more positive. Moreover, the expected cost of capital and the return volatility of marginable stocks significantly decrease, especially during the period of the market crash in 2015. We also find that corporate investments increase and investment efficiency also increases. The results are summarized in three papers. The papers have been presented in many international academic conferences (the 2019 and 2017 Conference on the Theories and Practices of Securities and Financial Markets (SFM) in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, the 2019 Advanced Economics and Management Forum, in Wuhan, China, the 2018 International Conference in Accounting, Finance, Economics, and Law (ICAFEL) in Taipei, Taiwan, the 2017 annual conference of the China Finance Annual Meeting (CFAM) in Shanghai, China, and the 2017 Conference on Pacific Basin Finance, Economics, Accounting, and Management (PBFEAM) in Singapore as well as many universities. The paper on the SML and the paper on the margin-based CAPM are related. The former focuses on the SML, while the later on testing the margin-based CAPM proposed by Gârleanu and Pedersen (2011). We are currently revising these two papers by incorporated the comments and suggestions by discussants and by journal referees. Once the revisions are done, we intend to submit the margin-based CAPM paper to Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis. The paper on corporate investment won the Best Research Award at the 2019 SFM and is currently under review at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis. The outcomes of the project have clearly demonstrated that the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

16512916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16512916.value: This project has generated the three following papers. These paper were presented at many international conferences. 1. Clack Liu, Shujing Wang, and K.C. John Wei, 2020, “The Margin-Based Asset Pricing Model: Evidence from the Chinese Stock Market” Summary: We examine the staggered relaxation of margin trading restrictions in China to identify the effect of margin requirements on asset prices. After margin trading restrictions are lifted, expected returns and the return volatility of marginable stocks significantly decrease, particularly during the period of the market crash in 2015. We also find that after stocks become eligible for margin trading and thus are less exposed to changes in the shadow cost of capital, they comove more with marginable stocks but less with non-marginable stocks. Our results are consistent with the predictions of the margin-based CAPM that Gârleanu and Pedersen (2011) propose. 2. Clack Liu, Shujing Wang, and K.C. John Wei, 2019, “Borrowing Constraints and Asset Prices: Evidence from the Chinese Stock Market” Summary: We use staggered relaxation of margin trading restrictions in China during the period 2010-15 to identify the effect of borrowing constraints on asset prices. We find that after margin trading restrictions are lifted, the security market line (SML) becomes more positive and stock volatility decreases. Further analysis shows that during the market crash, stocks that are allowed for margin trading experience significantly higher returns than those are not. Our results suggest that relaxing borrowing constraints helps improve stock market price efficiency. 3. G. Nathan Dong, Ming Gu, Weiwei Huang, and K.C. John Wei, 2020, “Margin Trading and Corporate Investments: Evidence from a Quasi-natural Experiment in China,” under review at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis Summary: What is the real effect of margin trading on firms’ corporate policies? Using a quasi-natural experiment in China, we identify the causal impact of relaxing margin trading restrictions on the level and efficiency of corporate investments. Capital and R&D expenditures dramatically increase when a company’s stock becomes eligible for margin trading, especially for financially constrained firms. Investment efficiency, measured by investment-to-Q sensitivity, also increases. Our findings are consistent with the argument that corporate investment reacts to changing market conditions. Investment increases and capital allocation efficiency improves dramatically due to reduced financing costs and relaxed financing constraints.

16512916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16512916.value: The relaxation of borrowing constraints or allowance for margin trading is a very important regulation for financial markets. Marginal trading can relax investors’ borrowing constraints and potentially for firms’ financing constraints. As a result, it will have both the financial and real effects. The financial effect means that margin trading can make the market more efficient, while the real effect means that it can reduce a firm’s cost of capital. As a result, firms can reduce the financing constraints and invest more. Moreover, when the stock market is more efficient, managers can learn more useful information from the stock market and make their investment decisions more optimal and efficient. Overall, the allowance of margin trading not only affects investor trading behavior but also manager corporate decision behavior. In this project, we study the financial effect of margin trading on asset prices and the real effect on corporate investment. A natural extension is to study other impacts of investor trading behavior, such as liquidity and institutional holding. We can also extend to other real impacts on managers’ corporate decisions, such as capital structure, innovations, earnings quality, and others. All of these are in our future research agenda.

16512916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16512916.value: This project uses the staggered relaxation of margin trading restrictions in China to study the effects of the relaxation of borrowing restrictions on asset prices and corporate investments. We find that after margin trading restrictions are lifted, the stock market becomes more efficient and the expected cost of capital reduces. As a result, firms invest more and their investments become more efficient. All these results suggest that the relaxation of margin trading restrictions is beneficial not only for investors but also the whole economy.

16513216.label: Project Objectives
16513216.value: Using data on two CEOs of unrelated firms sharing seats of the board of directors on a third firm, identify whether such appointments lead to more citations in new patent applications between the two firms. Any relationship would indicate knowledge transfer has taken place. In addition to directly capturing citation counts following the same board appointments, I will also look into whether the board appointments are associated with greater overlap in the patent technology classes of new patent applications by the two affected firms. This would be an alternative indication of knowledge spillover. In a further analysis, explore the dynamics of these relationships, i.e., how long it takes for the knowledge transfer to occur. To further strengthen identification, sample size permitting, look at whether the breakup of sharing of external board that comes from CEOs retiring, getting medical conditions or passing away, delivers a similar effect. Explore the heterogeneity of any effect. In particular, whether such technological spillovers are facilitated by the presence of (a) CEO equity incentives, (b) geographical closeness (or distance), (c) past relationships in attending same educational institutions or sharing a similar work background, (d) frequency of board meetings, and (e) the innovation activities of the third firm where the two CEOs share seats on the board.

16513216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16513216.value: One of the primary research questions in the literature on economic growth and innovation is whether and how technological investments create knowledge spillovers to other firms or research institutions. In addition to being of academic interest, the issue is extremely relevant from an economic policy standpoint. High positive technological spillovers mean that social returns to R&D are larger than private returns to R&D and thus provide a basis for subsidizing R&D investments through, for instance, R&D tax credits or subsidies. Most of the literature on knowledge transfers has looked at geographic spillovers, when firms are located in the close geographic areas, or spillovers that come from firm interactions in product markets, e.g. if they are each other’s rivals, customers or suppliers. However, this past research has underexplored the mechanisms how the technological transfers actually occur. In this research, I would like to explore the knowledge transfers that happen at the CEO level. While literature on innovation economics and corporate governance has emphasized that CEOs have a significant influence on firm investment in innovation, I would like to study how much the actual path of firm technological growth is influenced by CEOs and their interactions outside of the firm. In my empirical setup I will look into the cases where the two CEOs are appointed to the board of directors of a third, unrelated firm. More frequent interactions between the two CEOs should make it more likely that they would share insights about each other firm’s technological progress. Since the two CEOs are appointed to a third firm, the endogeneity problem that plagues the studies on technological spillovers will be reduced. If the two firms have no other observable interactions (and I would make sure to control for that), the appointments to a third firm will likely to be driven by external considerations rather than the two firms starting to cooperate together. I will then look at whether after such appointments to a third firm, the firms run by these two CEOs start citing each other’s patents more in their new patent applications, which is a widely used measure of technological diffusion of knowledge. My tests will provide insights whether there are any technological transfers at the managerial levels, or rather whether any such spillovers are solely driven by scientists and engineers. In addition, I will be able to show whether technological spillovers travel further than spatial and industrial limits. 对于创新技术的投资是否会知识溢出到其他公司或研究机构，以及它的溢出途径是经济增长和创新文献中的主要研究问题之一。除了在学术圈引起广泛兴趣，这个问题从经济政策的观点而言也非常重要。积极的技术溢出效应意味着，研究与开发（R&D）对社会产生的回报高于对私人产生的回报。因此，相应的学术研究可以对政府是否应该补贴研发投资（例如，研发税收抵免和研发补贴） 提供依据。 大多数研究知识转移的文献专注于研究当各家公司都位于相邻地理区域的地理溢出效应，或是通过公司产品市场交互（例如，公司彼此间互为竞争对手，客户或供应商）产生的溢出效应。然而，这些过去的文献却未彻底研究技术转让的产生机制。 尽管创新经济学和公司治理文献强调了CEO对公司的创新投资具有显著的影响，在这项研究中，我想探索发生在CEO层面的知识转移。我想研究公司技术发展的传播途径具体是如何受CEO们， 以及CEO们在公司之外的互动所影响。 在实证检验部分，我会研究当两家公司CEO被任命为第三家无关联公司董事会的案例。当CEO们被任命董事会成员后，两者之间更频繁的交往会使得他们更容易分享彼此企业技术方面的进步和见解。由于两位CEO被任命为第三家公司董事会成员，困扰技术溢出效应研究的内生性问题将会减少。 如果两家公司没有其它可观察的到的互动（我会控制其他可观察的互动），那么两家公司CEO 被任命为第三家公司董事会成员极有可能是受到外部因素驱动，而不是两家公司开始合作。然后我会深入调查在被任命之后，由这两位CEO管理的公司们是否会在专利申请中引用对方的专利。互相引用专利是使得知识技术扩散的一种广泛措施。我的实证将会为是否存在管理层面的技术知识溢出效应提供深入的见解，或者说是否技术知识溢出效应是完全由科学家和工程师单独驱动。此外，我将能够提供证据是否技术溢出可以不受空间和产业的限制。

16513916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16513916.value: When a client hires an agent to conduct certain activities, the agent may cause harm to third parties and therefore bear liability or other legal costs. Should the client provide indemnification to the agent, i.e. reimburse the agent’s liability and legal costs? How would indemnification impact the agent’s effort, potential harm to third parties, and social welfare? In practice, the clause "indemnification" is widely used in contracts between clients and agents. There have been policy debates on whether such contractual indemnification should be enforced by courts and whether agents can ask clients to indemnify them for their liability costs, even when the original contracts do not include such a term. This project intends to examine firms’ incentives to adopt indemnification in their contracts, using both theoretical and empirical analysis. The results will lead to empirical evidence and implications for contract design and policy discussions. This project includes two parts. The first part provides empirical evidence on how the legal environment and firms’ characteristics affect the adoption of indemnification in contracts. There have been some theoretical studies but no empirical analysis. In particular, by using a rich data set about R&D contracts between pharmaceutical firms and their research agents, we expect to show that agents’ R&D capabilities and clients’ experience in the industry affect the adoption of indemnification clauses. Additionally, if the law is restrictive in supporting agents’ requests for non-contractual indemnification, firms would have more incentive to adopt indemnification in their contracts. The second part of the project includes theoretical analysis of firms’ incentives to use indemnification and examine the impact on social welfare. We will formulate an agency model where the joint benefit of a client and his agent depends on the agent’s R&D effort, and the client’s precaution to reduce harm to third parties. Intuitively, providing indemnification can motivate agents to take more R&D effort, but can also increase the likelihood of causing harm to third parties. Clients may take monitoring or precaution to prevent such harm. If agents have better R&D capabilities, or clients have more experience, their R&D effort or precaution can be more effective. In such scenarios, firms would have more incentive to adopt indemnification. This theoretical analysis will provide mechanisms explaining the empirical findings. More importantly, it will address the interactions between the client’s precaution and the agent’s R&D effort, as well as the impact of indemnification on social efficiency.

16513916.label: Realisation of objectives
16513916.value: All the project objectives have been achieved and the results have been included in a research article, currently under review at the American Law and Economics Review. The article presents the theoretical analysis before the empirical findings, so we shall start with the achievement of the second objective. (1) The second objective: An indemnification contract between a firm and its agent commits the firm to reimburse the agent for liabilities and other legal costs if the agent’s activities harm third parties or violate the law. When firms are less risk-averse than agents, such contract clauses can achieve efficient risk-sharing and motivate agents to take productive activities. The literature contains theoretical studies on firms’ incentives in offering indemnification to their agents, but abstracts away from firms’ monitoring and does not provide any empirical analysis. We first reviewed the relevant literature in detail, read many R&D agreements between pharmaceutical companies and biotech research agents, and investigated relevant lawsuits in all the fifty states in the U.S. Although all the state laws allow for indemnification contracts, in practice, not all firms provide such protection to their agents and many state laws forbid indemnification against liabilities arising from agents’ negligence. Additionally, firms often take monitoring effort during collaboration with their agents. Given these observations, we construct a theoretical model where a risk-neutral client hires a risk-averse agent to conduct R&D activities that, however, may harm third parties and bring liabilities to the agent. The client can offer a royalty payment and an indemnification clause in the contract with the agent. The indemnification payment is contingent on precautions taken by the agent. The agent’s precautions can reduce potential harm, while the client can (but could not commit to) conduct costly monitoring to generate a signal about whether the agent has taken precautions. The agent is financially constrained, so absent indemnification, he may not be able to compensate the third parties for the full harm caused. This model differs from the literature by considering the client’s monitoring incentive and the impact of commitment failure. The model and the theoretical analysis have been revised several times after we received comments from conference attendants and other experts in the field. Within this framework, we characterize the optimal contract for the client. The analysis has successfully captured the client’s incentives to adopt indemnification clauses. In particular, it is shown that indemnification achieves efficient risk-sharing but may reduce the agent’s precaution incentives which could be restored by the client’s monitoring. However, when the contract contains the contingent indemnification clause, since the client cannot commit to monitoring, both the client and agent use mixed strategies in taking precautions and conducting monitoring. This commitment failure creates inefficient monitoring so that the client would not adopt indemnification in the contract when the agent’s potential liability is small. Moreover, when the agent’s potential liability is overly large, the client would not adopt indemnification as the agent can escape some of the liability via bankruptcy. To summarize, the client offers the indemnification clause only when the agent’s potential liability is neither too large nor too small and the client’s monitoring is not too costly. (2) The first objective: Our theoretical analysis suggests that firms are more likely to offer indemnification to their agents when their monitoring costs are lower and when the agents’ potential liabilities are not too large. To empirically identify firms’ incentives in adopting indemnification clauses, we use the Thomas Reuters Recap Dataset (Recap), which contains many R&D alliance deals between pharmaceutical firms and biotech agents during 1974-2009. Since Recap only provides the original agreements but does not summarize most of the contract terms, we read through entire agreements to identify the relevant indemnification clauses. We also collected data about the distance between each client and its agent as well as financial data about each client. After this intensive data collection and refinement process, we construct a dummy variable for the indemnification clause as the dependent variable. There is no direct measure about a client’s monitoring cost, so we create several indirect measures: the distance between the client and its agent, the client’s experience in clinical trials, and the client’s experience in R&D collaboration in the past. Intuitively, a client who is closer to its agent and has more experience in clinical trials or R&D collaboration can more easily identify the agent’s negligent behavior. Creating the measure for liabilities needs more innovative thinking. Biotech R&D projects typically involve different stages of drug development, while we observe from industry articles and lawsuits that R&D activities in the later stages such as clinical trials are more likely to cause large liabilities than in the earlier stages. Therefore, we use a dummy variable “late stage” as an indicator for larger potential liabilities. In various empirical specifications, we also control many other factors including R&D project size, whether the client has used indemnification clauses before, the client’s asset size and financial status, whether the agent has received funding from venture capitalists, year fixed effects, and certain disease fixed effects. Using the above specifications, we have obtained empirical evidence that R&D agreements are more likely to contain contingent indemnification clauses when the distance between a client and its agent is shorter and when the client is more experienced in clinical trials. We also observe that the client and the agent are less likely to adopt indemnification clauses for projects involving the later stages of drug development. All these empirical findings are consistent with our theoretical predictions. Our analysis generates the first set of empirical observations regarding the use of indemnification contracts in the literature. (3) The third objective: The above theoretical and empirical findings not only contribute to the academic literature but also provide implications for firm strategies and government/court policies. First of all, although indemnification achieves efficient risk-sharing, clients and agents may not adopt such a clause when agents’ potential liabilities are overly large and agents can escape some liabilities via bankruptcy. Policies allowing non-contractual indemnification could mitigate this inefficiency. Second, our analysis demonstrates the importance of clients’ monitoring in restoring agents’ precaution incentives under indemnification contracts. Therefore, it is meaningful to establish monitoring mechanisms such as joint steering committees or information disclosure in R&D or other types of collaborations. Finally, the lack of commitment to monitoring may cause insufficient or excessive monitoring activities. Insufficient monitoring happens when agents’ potential liabilities are in the intermediate range and indemnification contracts are adopted. In this case, clients use mixed strategies on monitoring and agents take precautions only with some probabilities. If clients could commit to conduct monitoring for sure, agents’ precaution incentives and social welfare can be increased. This calls for policies requiring clients’ monitoring. One of such policies is to implement “joint and several liabilities” under which clients would share liabilities when agents’ activities cause harm to third parties. It is also important to notice that clients may conduct excessive monitoring when agents’ potential liabilities are small and indemnification contracts are adopted. This problem reduces the clients’ incentives to offer indemnification. Policies allowing non-contingent indemnification can overcome this problem.

16513916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16513916.value: This project has generated both theoretical and empirical findings on firms’ incentives offering indemnification clauses in R&D agreements. In the theoretical part, we have constructed a model where a risk-neutral client hires a risk-averse and financially-constrained agent to conduct R&D activities that, however, may harm third parties and bring liabilities to the agent. The client can offer a royalty payment and an indemnification clause in the contract with the agent. The indemnification payment is contingent on precautions taken by the agent. The agent’s precautions can reduce potential harm, while the client can (but could not commit to) conduct costly monitoring to generate a signal about whether the agent has taken precautions. It is shown that indemnification achieves efficient risk-sharing but may reduce the agent’s precaution incentives which could be restored by the client’s monitoring. However, commitment failure creates inefficient monitoring. The client offers the indemnification clause only when the agent’s potential liability is neither too large nor too small and the client’s monitoring is not too costly. In the empirical part, using the Recap dataset about R&D agreements between pharmaceutical companies and biotech agents, we have identified indemnification clauses and constructed measures of monitoring costs and agents’ potential liabilities. We have found empirical evidence consistent with the theoretical analysis. In particular, R&D agreements are more likely to contain contingent indemnification clauses when the distance between a client and its agent is shorter and when the client is more experienced in clinical trials. Moreover, clients and agents are less likely to adopt indemnification clauses for projects involving the later stages of drug development (implying larger potential liabilities). Our analysis generates rich implications for firm strategies regarding when and how to adopt indemnification contracts, as well as for court policies regarding whether indemnification contracts should be enforced and whether non-contingent and/or non-contractual indemnification should be allowed. The above findings have been included in a research article “Indemnification and Monitoring: Theory and Evidence from R&D Contracts” (Please see part C). We presented the findings in the leading conference in the field of law and economics, the Annual Meeting of the American Law and Economics Association in May 2019. After revisions, we submitted the article to one of the major journals in law and economics, the American Law and Economics Review, in August 2019. The article is still under review in April 2020 when this report is submitted.

16513916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16513916.value: As mentioned above, the findings have been included in the attached article, which is under review at American Law and Economics Review (please see part C). In the short run, after receiving comments from the editor and referees, we plan to revise the article accordingly. In the long run, there are a few potential directions for future research. First, in the current article, we restrict our attention to contract forms observed in practice. It would be meaningful to examine whether the observed contract forms are indeed optimal mechanisms. Second, our empirical results are obtained under some data limitations. Given that we only have a dummy measure on agents’ potential liabilities, we could not test the non-monotonic relationship between the use of indemnification and the liability level, as predicted by the theoretical analysis. Finally, we have ignored possible mergers between clients and agents and we could not observe whether agents have purchased liability insurance plans or not. Future studies combining the various contractual and organizational arrangements for the allocation of liability risks would be desirable.

16513916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16513916.value: Clients hire agents to conduct R&D or other activities that may harm third parties and bring liabilities to the agents. Anticipating this, clients can offer an indemnification contract to reimburse agents for future liabilities. By examining clients’ motivations to offer indemnification, this project provides valuable implications for business strategies and policy discussions. First, the project formulates a theoretical framework and shows that indemnification achieves efficient risk-sharing between clients and agents but may reduce agents’ precaution incentives which could be restored by clients’ monitoring. Clients offer indemnification contracts only when agents’ potential liabilities are neither too large nor too small and clients’ monitoring is not too costly. Moreover, policies allowing non-contractual or non-contingent indemnification can increase social welfare. Second, consistent with the theoretical findings, we obtain empirical evidence that R&D agreements are more likely to contain contingent indemnification clauses when the distance between a client and its agent is shorter and when the client is more experienced in clinical trials. Moreover, clients and agents are less likely to adopt indemnification clauses for projects involving the later stages of drug development which are associated with larger potential liabilities. These findings provide useful implications for practical contract design.

16514016.label: Project Objectives
16514016.value: To identify the contents of and develop a measure for team crisis events and therefore provide a theoretical and empirical foundation for future research. By doing so, we advance the threat-rigidity theory by specifying the conditions under which team crisis benefits creativity. 16514016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16514016.value: As the environment becomes more turbulent, teams experience crisis (e.g., competitors surpass the team’s product design) from time to time. While limited research has examined organizational crisis and firm performance (Brockner & James, 2008), no research has examined team crisis and creativity, especially in R&D teams which generate innovations. We define team crisis as a set of unexpected events that can exert a significant impact on team functioning, even survival, through allowing fewer possibilities for problem-solving within the current structure (e.g., plans, routines, work methods, and resources) (Drazin, Glynn, & Kazanjian, 1999; Habermas, 1975). Team crisis provides a potential opportunity for creativity because it demands constructive changes in the current structure. Little research has examined team crisis, its contents, and impacts on creativity. We develop the construct of team crisis and identify crisis events in the context of R&D teams through literature review and focus group interviews. We then examine when and how team crisis may turn into creativity. Because transformational leadership is suited to the task of transformative changes that a crisis situation calls for (Bass, 1998), we examine the facilitating role of transformational leadership in turning team crisis into creativity. We also examine the facilitating role of promotion focus, defined as the extent to which teams and individuals are oriented toward achieving gains (Higgins, 1998), in turning team crisis into creativity because teams and individuals with a strong promotion focus are likely to see opportunities for gains or growth in a crisis situation. Finally, we examine creative process engagement, the involvement in creative problem-solving activities (e.g., problem identification, information searching and encoding, and idea generation) (Zhang & Bartol, 2010), as the mechanism linking team crisis and creativity under transformational leadership or promotion focus. We make three contributions. First, team crisis occurs in the increasingly dynamic and turbulent environment, but its contents and impacts on creativity have received little attention. We develop the construct of team crisis and associated crisis events in R&D teams. Second, we advance knowledge regarding the paradoxical nature of team crisis in R&D teams – it poses a threat but can also stimulate creativity under the right conditions. We identify and examine transformational leadership and promotion focus as conditions under which team crisis turns into creativity. Finally, we advance creativity research by formulating and examining the thesis that team crisis can enhance creativity through stimulating creative process engagement (under strong transformational leadership or promotion focus). 由于环境更加多变，团队经常经历危机（比如竞争对手超越团队的产品设计）。目前为止，还没有关于团队危机和团队创新的研究。团队危机指没有预期的事件，并且这些事件通过限制在现有结构（比如计划，工作方法，资源）下来解决问题的可能性对团队的运作甚至生存产生显著影响。团队危机为创新提供了机遇，因为它对现有结构提出建设性变革的要求。对团队危机的内涵及影响的研究几乎是空白。本研究开发团队危机概念，界定团队危机事件的内容，并检测其对创造力的影响的中介机制（比如创造性过程从事）和边界条件（比如变革型领导，提升聚焦，学习导向）。

16514016.label: Realisation of objectives
16514016.value: All stated objectives are fully achieved. We conducted three studies. In the first study, we identified (via interviews) crisis events in R&D teams and developed a measure of employee experienced team crisis. In study 2, we collected field data from more than 100 R&D teams to test hypotheses. We found that the impact of employee experienced team crisis on creativity is through job anxiety and creative process engagement, and that implicit belief is an important boundary condition for the relationship. In study 3, we conducted an experimental study and showed the causality of the interactive effect of crisis and implicit belief.

16514016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16514016.value: 1. Major Research Findings In an increasingly dynamic and turbulent environment, crisis occurs from time to time when employees work in teams. We defined employee-experienced team crisis as the magnitude of impact an employee experienced from crisis events when carrying out team tasks or projects. We examine when and how employee-experienced crisis stimulates or stifles creative performance. Drawing upon and extending sense-making perspective, we hypothesize that employee experienced team crisis stimulates creative performance via enhanced creative process engagement when an employee has high incremental (low entity) belief. On the other hand, building on and extending threat-rigidity theory, we theorize that employee-experienced crisis stifles creative performance via increased job anxiety when an employee has low incremental (high entity) belief. We conducted an experiment (317 working adults) and a field study (544 research and development employees in 114 teams and their direct leaders) to test the predictions. Results largely supported the hypotheses. We advance sense-making and threat-rigidity perspectives by showing incremental belief as an important boundary condition for their predictions regarding employee-experienced team crisis and creative performance. 2. Research Outcomes. I have used the project funding to support a few projects, some of which have been published in journals or conferences. I will give three examples here. (a) Liu, Gong, Zhou and Huang (2017) publication at Academy of Management Journal (acknowledged). (b) Gong, Kim and Liu (in press) at Human Relations (acknowledged). Accepted in 2019. (c) Jeong, Gong and Zhong (2019) presented at Academy of Management Conference in Boston.

16514016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16514016.value: This research has significant theoretical and practical implications. Theoretically, it extended threat-rigidity theory by showing that employee experienced team crisis can actually stimulate employee creativity (via increased creative process engagement) when an employee embraces incremental belief (i.e., a belief that people's attributes can be changed). Practically speaking, our research suggests that firms can turn crisis event into a potential opportunity for enhanced creative performance. Yet, to maximize the potential, managers should recruit those with incremental belief because they will engage in creative process when they experience team crisis. Managers should avoid hiring those with entity belief because they will be highly anxious and react rigidly to experienced team crisis, and thus demonstrate less creative performance. Beyond recruitment, managers and firms should also consider how to deploy existing employees. They could assign those with incremental belief to certain tasks that are more likely to experience crises.

16515216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16515216.value: Adverse selection occurs when a low-quality product drives a high-quality product away from the market due to information asymmetry between the buyers and sellers. A textbook example is Akerlof's market for lemons as used cars. Adverse selection is also widely believed to be an important source of market failure in the financial markets. Much of the work is based on static partial equilibrium models. The purpose of this project is to explore the macroeconomic consequence of adverse selection in dynamic models. We can study the implication of adverse selection on business cycles and confront models with actual macroeconomic data, generating many new insights beyond the static models. For example, allowing for more short-term borrowing backed by collateralized real assets may be dangerous in the presence of adverse selection, as it induce firms to hoard high-quality assets, resulting in a liquidity dry-up in the asset market and even a market breakdown. Our model hence justifies the common proposed macro-prudential policies regarding bank lending. 買者和賣者之間存在信息不對的市場中，由於優質產品無法獲利，而使得市場中次品氾濫。經濟學家把這一現象稱為逆向選擇。逆向選擇廣泛得存在金融市場中，是一個公認的市場缺陷。現有的文獻研究， 多基於一些靜態局部均衡模型。與現有文獻不同，本研究課題的著重點是逆向選擇的宏觀影響。我們將在標準的宏觀動態一般均衡模型中討論金融市場中的逆向選擇對經濟波動的放大和傳導機制。 比如， 寬鬆的信貸可能導致企業惜售優質金融資產 （股票），加大金融資產市場的風險。另外， 本研究課題也將討論各種宏觀謹慎政策的效果。

16515216.label: Realisation of objectives
16515216.value: This project has 5 objectives. Objective 1 is to incorporate adverse selection into the financial market to study the possibility of self-fulfilling expectation driven equilibria. This objective is fully achieved in a published paper entitled “adverse selection and self-fulfilling business cycles”. The title explains itself that the paper studies self-fulfilling business cycles in the financial markets due to adverse selection. The second and the third objective are to introduce adverse selection into a modified Kiyotaki-Moore model with borrowing constraints to study the interplay of funding liquidity and market liquidity and their efficiency. The fifth objective is to study the consequence of government policies such as macro-prudential policy and monetary policy in the presence of adverse selection. These three objectives are achieved the second published paper entitled “The perils of credit booms”. This paper presents a dynamic general equilibrium model of asset bubbles with adverse selection in the financial market to study the interaction between funding liquidity and market liquidity. Asset bubbles arise endogenously as more liquidate asset due to adverse selection by the classic Gresham’s law that bad money drives out good. High funding liquidity allows firms to borrow more but discourages firms to sell high quality assets and leads to a severer adverse selection problem in the long-term asset markets, resulting a liquidity dry-up in the market for long-term assets and even a financial crisis due to the market breakdown. Macro-prudential policy that limits firms’ borrowing is productive in preventing financial crises. The fifth objective is further achieved in two working papers that extend “The perils of credit booms” to study monetary policies. The paper entitled “Asset Bubbles and Monetary Policy” studies a model of rational bubbles in a Dynamic New Keynesian framework. It shows that monetary policy affects the conditions for the existence of a bubble, its steady-state size, and its dynamics including the initial size. The leaning-against-the-wind interest rate policy reduces bubble volatility, but could raise inflation volatility. Whether monetary policy should respond to asset bubbles depends on the particular interest rate rule and exogenous shocks. The paper entitled "Asset Bubbles and Foreign Interest Rate Shocks" studies how monetary policies in advance economies affect emerging economies in an extended model of “The perils of credit booms”. It provides some complementary insights to the interaction of monetary policy and macro-prudential policy in the open economy. It suggests that counter-cyclic capital control and other macro-prudential policies are useful in mitigating foreign monetary policy risks. The forth objective is to introduce endogenous information acquisition in the financial market with adverse selection to study possible asymmetric business cycles. It has been mainly achieved. In work in progress, I and one of former PhD student Zhou Jing have studied information acquisition in the asset market. Information acquisition triggers a regime switch in credit market, which generates asymmetric responses to asset quality shocks. In the good time, lenders do not acquire information and hence borrowers can access to credit regardless of their asset quality. But when the perceived quality of assets is low, lenders have a strong incentive to distinguish good and bad borrowers. As a result, only borrowers with good quality assets can borrow. This endogenous regime switch can generate a large recession. But in response to a good shock in asset quality, the economy will stay in the same regime. The resulted boom is hence small. This explain the asymmetric business cycles observed in the data. However, solving a model with endogenous regime switch in full bloom business cycle is very challenging and time consuming. We are still improving our algorithm. We have set up the main model. But once we improve the algorithm, the remaining task is just subsidiary.

16515216.label: Major findings and research outcome
16515216.value: This project produces two published papers and two working papers. The paper entitled “adverse selection and self-fulfilling business cycles” is published by Journal of Monetary Economics, one of the leading journals in economics. The paper finds adverse selection can generate both multiple steady states and both global and local indeterminacy, which give rise to periodic fluctuations in credit, consumption, investment and employment. The second published paper entitled “The perils of credit booms”. One of the key finding is that fundamentally useless asset can be traded together with interest bearing assets as they are free of adverse selection. Another key finding is that funding liquidity can erode market liquidity. High funding liquidity discourages firms to selling their good long-term assets since these good assets have to subsidize lemons when there is information asymmetry between sellers and buyers. This can cause a liquidity dry-up in the market for long-term assets and even a market breakdown, resulting in a financial crisis. The paper entitled “Asset Bubbles and Monetary Policy” studies a model of rational bubbles in a Dynamic New Keynesian framework. It shows that monetary policy affects the conditions for the existence of a bubble, its steady-state size, and its dynamics including the initial size. The leaning-against-the-wind interest rate policy reduces bubble volatility, but could raise inflation volatility. The paper entitled "Asset Bubbles and Foreign Interest Rate Shocks" studies a small open economy with both domestic and international financial market frictions. Our estimated model based on Bayesian methods find foreign interest rates are important drivers for high volatilities of consumption and stock prices relative to output, countercyclical trade balance, and procyclical stock prices observed in the Mexican data over the period 1990Q1-2011Q4. It suggests that counter-cyclic capital control and other macro-prudential policies are useful in mitigating foreign monetary policy risks.

16515216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16515216.value: In the future, I will continue to work on information acquisition in financial market and their implication for macroeconomics. Extending the literature on information acquisition to dynamic models will be very interesting.

16515216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16515216.value: The project studies asymmetric information and adverse selection in the standard macroeconomic model, advance the literature on adverse selection from static setting to dynamic models, offering many new insights . First, adverse selection can generate new multiplicity of equilibrium even the static equilibrium is unique. Second, fundamentally useless asset can be traded together with interest bearing assets as they are free of adverse selection. Third, high loan to value ratio can cause financial crisis by exacerbating adverse selection in the asset markets. Forth, he leaning-against-the-wind monetary policy and macro-prudential policies are in general useful in mitigating economic volatility.

16515316.label: Project Objectives
16515316.value: To compare credit rating quality across countries, in terms of conservatism, accuracy, timeliness, and the incremental informativeness of credit ratings beyond other public information. To identify determinants at firm and country levels that shape a CRA’s incentive to provide high quality credit rating. To identify determinants at firm and country levels that shape a CRA’s incentive to provide high quality credit rating.
To provide insight into the feasibility and effectiveness of proposed and ongoing rating reforms, such as increasing industry competition and the legal accountability of rating agencies.

16515316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16515316.value: The purpose of the proposed project is to examine the impact of institutional factors and regulatory reforms on credit rating quality around the world. We plan to explore the international differences in the properties of credit ratings and the incremental informativeness of the ratings to stock prices. In addition, we plan to examine the effect of reforms on rating quality worldwide. Credit rating agencies (CRAs) have been subjected to great scrutiny by regulators and investors for their failure to predict several high-profile bankruptcies and for providing overly optimistic ratings for structured finance products. Critics often attribute the alleged poor rating quality of CRAs to weak legal accountability, conflicting compensation models and the oligopolistic structure of the rating industry. Not surprisingly, numerous regulations have been proposed or implemented to reform the rating industry, including the CRA regulations under European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), created in 2011 in the European Union (EU) and the Dodd-Frank Act of 2010 in the U.S. An investigation of credit rating quality in a global setting can provide insights for informing these proposals and debates in several important ways. First, the heterogeneity of information environments around the world provides a better setting for testing when credit ratings are more accurate and convey incremental information beyond other public information, thereby providing evidence of the competency of CRAs. Second, the multiplicity of functions of CRAs in the U.S. has opposing effects on CRAs’ incentive to provide high quality ratings. For example, the information intermediary role makes CRAs update ratings promptly while the certificating role in debt contracts and financial regulations discourages CRAs from changing ratings frequently. A slow rating change can be driven by either the failure of CRAs to fulfill their informational role or their commitment to the certification role. The heterogeneity of the demand for CRA services around the world will help distinguish alternative drivers of CRA incentive and the resultant rating quality. Finally, differences among countries in the legal accountability of CRAs will shed light on the debate about the effect of increasing CRAs’ legal liability (Dimitrov, Palia and Tang 2015). 该项目旨在研究全球范围内，制度因素以及监管改革对信用评级质量的影响。我们计划去探查国家之间在信用评级特征上的差异，以及信用评级能否在股价之上提供额外的信息。我们还计划检查全球范围内改革对信用评级质量的影响。 由于信用评级机构未能成功预测几次重大破产事件以及他们对结构性金融产品提供过于乐观的评级，他们受到全球监管者和投资者的高度审视。批评者常常把评级机构低质量的评级归咎于薄弱的法律责任，矛盾性的偿付模型和信用评级市场的垄断性结构。意料之中， 很多旨在改革信用评机行业的监管制度被提上日程或者已经在实施之中，包括欧盟于2011年成立的欧洲证券与市场权威制定的信用评级监管以及美国2010年通过的Dodd-Frank法案。 通过研究全球范围内信用评级质量，可以为以上的倡议和争论从以下几个方面提供重要启发。第一，国家之间信息环境的差异提供了一个强有力的背景来测试相比其他公共信息，信用评级何时能提供更准确更多的额外信息，从而佐证信用评级机构的才干。第二，在美国市场，信用评级机构扮演的多重角色对他们提供高质量的信用评级产生了相反的影响。比如说，信息中介角色会鼓励信用评级机构及时更新信用评级，但是在债务合同以及金融监管中的公证人角色不鼓励信用机构频繁更新评级。国别之间对信用评级机构的服务需求上的差异能帮助区分影响信用评级机构的动机与相关评级质量的不同因素。最后，国别之间法律责任的差异能对当前通过监管比如Dodd-Frank 法案来增加信用评级结构的法律责任的争论提供启发。

16515316.label: Realisation of objectives
16515316.value: For Objective 1, we examine rating conservatism for 32,934 non-financial firm-years from 27 developed markets from 1994 to 2016 in our main analysis. In our additional analysis, we explore the accuracy, timeliness, and informativeness of the ratings. For Objective 2, we identify that CRA's market share and regulatory certification shape their reputational incentives to issue stringent ratings. For Objective 3, regulators point to the dominance of a few actors in the rating industry and call for increasing competition to reduce incumbents’ market power. Our finding suggests that Global CRAs’ market power may contain the conflicts of interest and lead to tightened rating standards in corporate bond markets. While market power may have a disciplining effect on rating standards through reputation building, it may have other side effects such as discouraging innovation and investment.
