16600916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600916.value: Comparative research shows the outcome of democratic struggle hinges on the contest between pro-democracy and anti-democracy mobilization (Diamond, 2013). A high degree of public support for democracy, though not a sufficient condition, has been a good predictor of the level of democracy based on a global survey (Inglehart, 2003). Explaining public support for democracy is thus crucial for understanding Hong Kong's democratic development. In 2014, Hong Kong’s Umbrella Movement was distinguished by its long duration, large-scale of participation, and a radical turn in movement tactics when large-scale occupation of roads and confrontation with police occurred. Based on a survey, participants were mostly driven by a desire to achieve democracy (Cheng & Yuen, 2014). The movement featured the largest civil disobedience in Hong Kong’s history, having created a watershed with an enormous challenge to Beijing. However, public support for the movement dwindled over time, raising questions about societal division and the importance of democracy to Hongkongers. There are practical and theoretical reasons for understanding Hongkongers' support for democracy: First, initial surveys performed during the Umbrella Movement show a higher degree of support for the movement and democracy among the more educated respondents. This outcome may have reflected the effect of emancipative values, which tends to be stronger among the more educated public (Welzel, 2013). Those who identify with 'emancipative values' stress freedom of choice, equality of opportunities, and self-expression. The emancipative values can also raise public support for democracy (Welzel & Inglehart, 2006), empower individuals to engage in democratic mobilization, and lead to higher levels of democracy. This research will be a pioneering research assessing the level of 'emancipative values' and its possible causal effect on support for democracy in Hong Kong. Second, many existing research on mass support for democracy has overstated the level of the support by including citizens who conceive pseudo-democracies as genuine ones (Shi, 2015; Shin, 2015). I will measure the degree of respondents committing to a genuine conception of democracy to more accurately assess the level of public commitment to genuine democracy and explain the mass support for genuine democracy. Third, public support for the Umbrella Movement dwindled as the occupation dragged on, reflecting the societal divisions over democracy among Hongkongers. This research will reveal the social and cultural bases of divisions concerning support for democracy in Hong Kong, which can trigger severe political conflicts. 跨國研究發現，民主過渡能否發生取決於親民主與反民主力量的較量。公眾對民主的支持度，雖不是民主過渡的充分條件，卻可以解釋民主的發展水平。因此, 有效解釋理港公眾對民主的支持度, 將幫助我們預測香港未來的民主發展。 這項研究目的是了解香港人對民主的支持度; 本研究有實際和理論方面的意義： 1.雨傘運動期間初步調查顯示運動和民主為有較高的教育受訪者支持。這一結果可能反映了"解放價值觀"的效果。這項研究將是一個開拓性研究, 評價“解放價值觀”對香港的民主支持，其可能的因果關係。 2. 其次，許多研究發現公眾對於民主的錯誤理解導致我們誇大公眾對民主的支持度。這項研究將更準確地評估公眾對民主的真正支持程度。 3. 雨傘運動反映了香港人對民主發展的不同意見, 這項研究將探索港人對民主發展不同意見的社會和文化基礎。

16600916.label: Realisation of objectives
16600916.value: The above objectives have been fully achieved, with the related hypotheses tested. The emancipative value is found irrelevant to explaining the mass support, as the related variables have failed to cluster around the vlaue syndrone of emancipative value after performing factor analysis. Instead, tests show that following variables are statistically significant for explaining the mass support for democracy. The post-materialist value has been found effective in explaining the support for democracy. Based on the theory of post-modernization, continuous economic development in advanced industrial societies during the last few decades has triggered a gradual change from materialist values to post-materialist ones, i.e. toward greater emphasis on freedom of speech and participation in public policy. Advocates of the theory argue that post-materialists are more likely to buttress democracy than materialists for at least three reasons. First, post-materialism implies a stress on self-expression and participation that is inherently conducive to political participation to attain democracy. Second, post-materialists tend to consider democracy as an intrinsic value and therefore provide more secure support for democracy than materialists. Third, post-materialists like to embrace a wide range of fundamental democratic values. This result tallies well with the existing literature in Hong Kong studies too. Another pivotal variable found to be statistically significant for explaining the level of support relates to the liberal conception of democracy. While different types of conceptions of the democracy have been raised, the liberal conception of democracy is the major type of democracy reckoned by most as truly democratic in accordance with political theory as championed by Rawls (1971), Dahl (1973) and Sartori (1984). Conceivers of liberal notion are those who identify with free elections, referendum votes, civil liberties and equal political rights (Welzel & Alvarez, 2014). Among the four conceptions, only the liberal one is widely accepted as the proper definition of democracy as it aligns well with political theory. Still another crucial cause for the support of democracy revolves around the political trust towards the Chinese Government. Extensive research shows that the level of political trust is a strong predictor of political participation, with low levels of trust likely in campaigns or movements against the government. Scholars agree that distrust is correlated with non-institutionalized or mobilized participation because citizens who do not consider the government prepared to address their interests are more likely to contest it. In both Western democracies and developing countries, distrust in the government has been associated with support for street protests and confrontations, and with actual involvement in riots, civil disobedience and violence, land invasion and strikes, boycotts, demonstrations, protests, civil disorder, and anti-system activities. In Hong Kong, the legitimating bases for Hong Kong’s non-democratic political system have been quickly and continuously battered by deepening social inequality, blatant cronyism, incomplete economic restructuring, an unaccountable political system, and threats of decreased freedoms since its handover to mainland China. The aforementioned scenarios have fostered cumulative public distrust of the Chinese Government.

16600916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16600916.value: After using factor analysis, it has been found that the related variables have not clustered into the value syndrome of emancipative value in Hong Kong. Therefore, there is no evidence that the emancipative value is conducive to greater public support for democracy in Hong Kong. That said, a related variable of the value, i.e., post-materialistic value, has been found statistically significant in acconting for the mass support for democracy. Besides, the liberal conception of democracy among our respondents has been found statistically significant for accounting for the level of mass support for democracy. This result is unsurprising, given the strong theoretical anchorage of the variable of "liberal conception of democracy" in explaining the mass support. Third, education has been found relevant to explaining the mass support too, with higher education triggering higher level of support. This finding has supplemented some of the earlier findings in the liteature of Hong Kong. Fourth, the political efficacy does matter for the level of support, which has confirmed the mainstream literature that greater efficacy would lead to higher support. Last but not least, the low level of trust of Beijing's willingness to honor One Country Two Systems has been confrmed to have led to greater support for democracy. This result is understandable given the strong theoretical support and the similar findings in previous Hong Kong studies.

16600916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600916.value: A major hypothesis has been rejected, i.e, the claim that emancipative value may have explained greater public support for democracy. Instead, it has been found that post-materialistic value has been proven conducive to heightened support for democracy. The fact that the cluster of emancipative value is not found in Hong Kong is intriguing. In future, comparative studies should be conducted to see if the existence of emancipative value is conditioned upon cultural zones, levels of economic development, or other structural characteristics. The fact that the liberal conception of democracy can explain the level of public support for democracy carries huge practical significance. Again, cross-national studies need to be conducted in future to explore whether the level of economic development, duration of colonalization, identity of former colonial regime (if any), and the cultural zone would matter for shaping the level of liberal conception of democracy. Answers to such questions would help predict the level of support for democracy and therefore the public pressure for democracy. The results of the survey will likely be published in a peer-reviewed journal, titled, Communist and Post-Communist Studies. I have been invited by a professor at UCLA to co-edit a special issue of it, in which the Sino-Hong Kong relationship will be covered. I will use the current research to publish an article in that journal, highlighting how the issue of democracy has been a pivotal factor shaping the Sino-Hong Kong relationship and their tension.

16600916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600916.value: One key finding has been that while the emancipative value is statistically insignigicant, the post-materialism has been found powerful in explaining the mass support for democracy. For Hong Kong, since the 1960s, its enjoyment of more or less sustained economic growth and relatively high level economic development in East Asia has fostered post-materialism among some of its citizens. Besides, mainland China’s threats to Hong Kong’s continued enjoyment of freedoms before and after its handover, and a tendency for the pre-handover government to consult public opinion when making public policies, have also encouraged a gradual rise in post-materialism over the last few decades. How likely is it that post-materialism will grow among the younger and more educated generation in Hong Kong? In the regression analysis of age, education, and income on post-materialism for Hong Kong, the adjusted R-square is only having a single digit. More research is needed to access the social bases of post-materialism so as to project the practical implicaiton of its vissicitudes on the mass support for democracy. Whether higher support for democracy will trigger larger backing of democracy movements should also be gauged in future to assess the possible impact of post-materialism on the democracy movement.

16602916.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16602916.value: 社交媒体运动在中国：新兴的政策议程设置渠道？

16602916.label: Project Objectives
16602916.value: To identify social media campaigns in China over the course of 2011 to 2015 that have the following characteristics: - Posted on Sina Weibo and Tencent Weibo - National in scope - Concerns a public interest issue subject to (potential) regulation by the central and/or local government; To build a database of micro-charity campaigns on the dominant social media platforms in China (2011-2015) To trace the evolution and outcome of six social media campaigns through process-tracing of in-depth case studies To develop a typology for charitable social media campaigns To understand the relationship between on-line activism and other forms of expressing support for social issues To develop hypotheses about social media campaign attributes and conditions that produce policy impacts
rows: To identify social media campaigns in China over the course of 2011 to 2015 that have the following characteristics: - Posted on Sina Weibo and Tencent Weibo - National in scope - Concerns a public interest issue subject to (potential) regulation by the central and/or local government;
To build a database of micro-charity campaigns on the dominant social media platforms in China (2011-2015)
To trace the evolution and outcome of six social media campaigns through process-tracing of in-depth case studies
To develop a typology for charitable social media campaigns
To understand the relationship between on-line activism and other forms of expressing support for social issues
To develop hypotheses about social media campaign attributes and conditions that produce policy impacts

16602916.label: Realisation of objectives
16602916.value: Realising the objectives of this project entailed the following tasks: 1) Compiling a database of micro-charities that concern public interest issues at the national level; 2) Developing descriptive summaries of the relative frequency of different social issues and extent of public policy aspirations; 3) Conducting in-depth case studies of social media campaigns to trace the evolution and outcome of projects in different issue areas; and 4) Proposing hypotheses on the conditions under which social media campaigns are more likely to have agenda setting or policy impact. All of the research objectives were realised. 1) DATABASE OF MICRO-CHARITIES: The selection criteria for our database of micro-charity projects was as follows. First, to target campaigns with more enduring appeal, only “branded projects” (pingpai gongyi juankuan, 品牌公益捐款) were included rather than “individual projects” (geren gongyi juankuan, 个人公益捐款). Initiated by foundations with registered names, so-called “branded projects” (in Chinese) are more appropriately called, “public interest projects” (in English), because they encourage on-going contributions from supporters to address a widely-shared issue. By contrast, individual projects specify a monetary funding goal to help a private citizen and such projects terminate when the requested amount is raised. Our database focused on projects posted on the Sina Micro-Online Donation platform (2011-2017) because there are more public interest projects on Sina than Tencent, and the Tencent projects overlap with those on Sina. Second, the database only included projects that are national in scope, and relate to a public issue subject to (potential) regulation by the central and/or local governments. As of November 1, 2017, all of the 188 “branded”/public interest projects on Sina Weibo met the criteria for inclusion in the database 2) DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARIES: The descriptive data recorded for each project included: name; initiation date; sponsoring foundation; issue area; number of donors; donation size; total amount mobilized (on Weibo, from other online sources, and offline); and number of project supporters (zhichi, 支持) and microblog followers or “fans” (fensi, 粉絲). The next step assessed whether projects had explicit policy aspirations. This entailed content analysis of self-reported objectives on the Weibo listing and was coded dichotomously. Although all of the branded/public interest projects concern needs that could plausibly be addressed by public policy measures, many campaigns simply raise funds for people affected by the issue rather than trying to enlist government support or lobby for policy changes. For projects with policy aspirations, evaluating each project’s public impact involved: i) content analysis of official news through the Xinhua search engine to measure the frequency that particular issues are covered; and ii) process-tracing developments in particular issue areas by reviewing policy statements from government bureaus and ministries. The following 3-point scale was used to code public impact: 1-no government response, 2-agenda-setting influence, and 3-policy impact. Agenda-setting influence is indicated by the following: 1) whether deputies to the Chinese People’s Consultative Conference (CPPCC) and National People’s Congress (NPC) have demonstrated willingness to submit proposals or already submitted proposals for consideration at the annual meetings of the CPPCC and NPC; and 2) the extent to which governmental entities at the local or central level acknowledge the existence and severity of the problem, have publicly expressed commitment to addressing it, or taken initial efforts to address the issue in collaboration with relevant NGOs. Policy reform is indicated by reform of existing policies, the introduction of new institutions or policies, and/or enhanced budgetary commitment to addressing the issue. 3) CASE STUDIES: To understand the circumstances under which charitable crowdfunding campaigns have agenda-setting or policy impact, we conducted four case studies of projects ranking among the top ten in mobilized funds on Weibo: Free Lunch for Children [Free Lunch (mianfei wucan, 免费午餐)], Love Save Pneumoconiosis [Love Save (da’ai qingchen, 大爱清尘)], Support Relief of Rare Diseases [Rare Diseases (zhuli hanjianbing, yiqi dongqilai助力罕见病，一起冻起来)], and the China Water Safety Project (zhongguo shuianquan jihua, 中国水安全计划). The selection criteria of these projects was that they represent the most popular microcharities in their categories on Sina Weibo in the monetary amount mobilized. We also selected a popular public interest project (Rare Disease) that had already delisted from Sina Weibo to trace its advocacy activities beyond the crowdfunding phase. Although all four campaigns are hosted by national foundations, they had differential impact on the central government’s policy agenda as of late 2017. Free Lunch was exceptionally successful. Love Save encountered political resistance during its initial phase, but eventually attracted attention from central governmental entities and stimulated public legislative discussion. Rare Disease raised the most money from Weibo out of all the micro-charity projects ever posted to date, which helped to generate both popular support and emergent central governmental attention to its concerns. While Water Safety was initiated at the same time as Free Lunch and also raised significant funds, its advocacy efforts have yet to yield meaningful impact on policy agenda-setting. Process-tracing the origins and evolution of these campaigns provided insight into their variation in impact. 4) EXPLAINING POLICY IMPACT: We developed three hypotheses/observations about the conditions under which social media campaigns are likely to have agenda-setting or policy influence. First, campaigns are more likely to be successful when they partner substantively with government entities from the outset even if they were initiated by grassroots NGOs. This is evident in all 14 out of the 34 projects that achieved policy impact. Furthermore, among the 14 campaigns that have had tangible policy impact, all are concentrated in the areas of children’s welfare, environment protection, and poverty alleviation. Second, crowdfunding campaigns that amplify existing policy priorities with concrete proposed solutions are more likely to elicit a constructive governmental response than politically sensitive issues. Third, initial viral support for a charitable crowdfunding campaign may mobilize public concern—but is not sufficient—for garnering governmental action. Even when a campaign rouses popular fervor and possesses sympathetic allies within the party-state, effective communications and management are required for project implementation.

16602916.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602916.value: The research process revealed that the best way to understand the universe of on-line micro-charities was to summarize them by social issue and relative impact, respectively. Out of the 188 public interest micro-charity projects on Sina Weibo, over half concern either children’s welfare (56 projects) or education (39 projects). Health care (18 projects) and environmental protection (16 projects) are the next two most popular categories. Based on the total amount of donations mobilized, the top three categories are children’s welfare (7.5 million yuan), environment protection (2.9 million yuan), and veteran’s welfare (2.8 million yuan). In terms of the aggregate number of donors, children’s welfare, veteran’s welfare, and healthcare/diseases are the three most popular programs, respectively. As for the scale of individual donations, veteran’s welfare mobilized the largest average size (553,520 yuan on average), which is nearly three times larger than the next largest average donation, mobilized by environment protection projects (180,502 yuan on average). The five projects devoted to veteran’s issues also attracted the largest average number of donors. Among the 188 public interest projects on Sina Weibo, 34 (18% of the total) have policy aspirations. The plurality of impactful projects concern children’s welfare (38% of the total), followed by environmental protection campaigns (23.5%) and healthcare (14.7%), respectively. Crowdfunding campaigns relating to education, animal protection, and children’s health issues each account for less than three percent of the total number of long-term projects. In terms of relative impact, among the 34 programs with public policy objectives, 14 resulted in some degree of official policy reforms/initiatives (41.3%), 12 raised public awareness of the issue but without eliciting any governmental response (35.5%), and eight had agenda-setting influence in the sense of receiving public support from CPPCC or NPC deputies, but without concrete policy reform (23.5%).

16602916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602916.value: An interesting extension of this study would be to focus on charitable crowdfunding projects that are “boundary spanning” (i.e., more politically sensitive). It is possible that as micro-charities become more financially independent, they may also operate more autonomously from the party-state. It is not clear, however, the extent to which micro-charities exert such autonomy in their daily operations. We also have much to learn about how charitable crowdfunding compares with traditional funding sources in terms of influence by donors, impact on project execution, and the nature of competition among different projects/NGOs working in the same issue area. Meanwhile, the Chinese government’s position on charitable crowdfunding is still evolving. Although Beijing actively partnered with Tencent Foundation to establish September 9th as China’s Charity Day, there are residual concerns about campaigns that may push the boundaries of political acceptability. Overall, the popularity of charitable crowdfunding provides an opportunity to rethink conventional frameworks for understanding state-NGO relations in China. The M.Phil. graduate student trained in this GRF is now enrolled in a doctoral program in the US and will be writing her dissertation on the social media campaigns of rights-oriented NGOs.

16602916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602916.value: Social media in China has not only become a popular means of communication, but also expanded the interaction between the government and online citizens. Why have some charitable crowdfunding campaigns had agenda-setting influence on public policy, while others have had limited or no impact? Based on an original database of 188 charitable crowdfunding projects listed on Sina Weibo between 2011-2017, we observe that over 80 per cent of long-term campaigns do not have explicit policy aspirations. Among those pursuing policy objectives, however, nearly two-thirds have had either agenda-setting influence or contributed to policy change. Such campaigns complement, rather than challenge existing government priorities. Based on field interviews, case studies of four micro-charities – Free Lunch for Children, Love Save Pneumoconiosis, Support Relief of Rare Diseases, and Water Safety Program of China – are presented to highlight factors that contributed to their variation in public outcomes at the national level. The study indicates that charitable crowdfunding represents a novel channel for potential policy influence in China, albeit within closely monitored parameters.

16604516.label: Project Objectives

16604516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16604516.value: Internal migration in China has reached an unprecedented scale since the late 1990s. The migrants are increasingly heading for a few metropolitan regions in the east, and more of them bringing their families with a plan of long-term stay, and contributing to a significant portion of China’s rapidly growing urban population. While numerous studies have documented the socioeconomic disadvantages of migrants, often attributable to their lack of local hukou, few have paid attention to how the concentrations of migrants in certain residential areas and industries/occupations sectors could provide a mechanism to mitigate migrants’ socioeconomic disadvantages in cities. Moreover, while migrants are typically treated as a single group to compare with local residents, they are indeed heterogeneous, often forming their social networks and communities to facilitate their adaption to the new urban life. This project aims to investigate social-spatial differentiations of migrants in a Chinese metropolis, Shenzhen. Drawing from the western urban sociological literature on ethnicity and immigration, the PI proposes to distinguish among migrants by their place of origin (often associated with distinctive culture and dialects) and to perceive them as different “ethnic” groups. Based on the micro-data from the population and economic censuses, the PI plans: 1) to identify certain native-place “ethnic” enclaves in Shenzhen and the temporal changes from 2000 to 2010; 2) to analyze the formation of these native-place enclaves in association with spatial locations of certain industries and community characteristics; and finally, 3) to examine the role of the native-place enclaves in affecting migrants’ socioeconomic attainment and returns to human capital in the metropolitan labor markets of Shenzhen. Findings from the project will not only provide new evidence on how migrants are socially organized and shape China’s urban structure in their destinations, but also shed new light on how migrants’ disadvantages are created but also mitigated by their spatial and social concentrations. Such a comprehensive understanding of internal migrants’ adaptation and socioeconomic attainment in metropolitan settings under different institutional arrangement will contribute to the further theorization in urban sociology and offer a solid basis for policy research to address urban issues related to migration and community. 中國的國內移民自1990年代後期已達至史無前例的規模。移民人口正大規模地向東部沿海幾個主要的大城市遷移，他們大部分帶著家庭成員，以長期定居為目標，成為中國城市人口快速增長的一個重要組成部分。以往的研究往往只把移民人口在社會經濟地位的不利歸因於他們沒有本地戶口，卻甚少關注移民在某些居住地和行業／職業領域的聚集，這一現象如何成爲减輕他們在社會經濟上不利條件的一個機制。再者，移民一般被視為有別於本地居民的同質群體，但他們其實是由來自不同地方的人們組成的，並會透過建立社交網絡和社團，協助他們適應城市的新生活。 本項目旨在研究移民人口在中國的一個大城市──深圳的社會空間分化。受西方城市社會學中有關種族與移民的文獻的啓發，首席研究員 (Principal Investigator, PI) 旨在以來源地（一般指有區別性的文化和方言）來區分移民人口，把他們視作不同的「族群」。根據人口和經濟普查的微觀數據，PI計劃：1）識別某些籍貫「種族」在深圳的聚居地，及他們在2000至2010年期間的變化，2）分析某些行業空間位置和社區特點如何形成籍貫「種族」的聚居地；最後，3）驗證籍貫的聚居地在影響移民人口的社經成就所扮演的角色，以及在深圳這個大城市的勞動力市場中人力資本的回報。 本項目所得的研究結果將不僅提供新的實證來解釋移民人口如何被自我組織，及如何形成中國的城市的社會結構；同時揭示移民人口的社會經濟地位的不利是如何造成，但亦因他們在空間及社會的集中而得到舒緩。如此全面地瞭解國內移民在不同制度下對大城市環境的適應，及其社經成就，將進一步有利於城市社會學的理論化，也為政策研究提供一個實證基礎，以解決與移民和社區相關的城市問題。

16604516.label: Major findings and research outcome
16604516.value: 1. Migrants from different place of origin (the county of hukou registration) tend to concentrate in neighborhood communities and industries in the labor market in Shenzhen. 2. Migrants accounted for 80.4% of the population in Shenzhen, and they came from 2509 counties in mainland China. 3. We identified 72 native-place “ethnic” groups in Shenzhen, and we found that they formed "ethnic" enclaves in residential neighborhood and industry in Shenzhen. 3. Regarding the determinants of migrants' enclaves participation, we found that human capital is negatively associated with enclave participation, and new arrivals are more likely to be in nativeplace enclaves in Shenzhen. Furthermore, self-employed and emplyers are more likely to participate in residential enclaves. 4. We found that migrants working in native-place industrial enclaves are more likely to live in nativeplace residential enclaves. 5. Native-place enclaves are associated with migrants’ socioeconomic attainment and returns to human capital in the metropolitan labor markets. First, migrants who live in native-place residential enclaves tend to earn less than those who do not, but migrants who work in industrial enclaves tend to earn more than those working in the open economy. Second, the earnings disadvantage of new arrivals relative to established migrants is smaller in a residential enclave than that outside an ethnic enclave, and the advantage of working in industrial enclaves disappears for those new arrivals, compared to migrants who have left their place of origin more than five years. Third, the earnings return to years of schooling is smaller for migrants who live in or work in native-place enclaves than for those who do not. Finally, migrants in residential or industrial enclaves are more likely to be self-employed or to be employers. The positive association between living in a residential enclave and working in an industrial enclave suggests that, although residential enclave and industrial enclaves are correlated with each other, they are associated with migrants’ labour market outcomes in different ways.

16604516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16604516.value: Empirical data generated from this project (neighborhood level aggregate data and indrustrial aggregate data) can be further used to address relevant research topics in migration study. We are now extending the project work to compare nativeplace enclave groups with different dialects, including Hakka, Chiu Chau, and Cantonese, to study the impact of enclave participation on labor market outcomes and its relations with culture (or features of laoxiang network). We presented our results in an academic conference. We are also working on a comparative study, as a extension of this project, to compare Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen in terms of nativeplace enclave and its impacts on labor market outcomes.

16604516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16604516.value: This project investigates social-spatial differentiations of migrants in a Chinese metropolis, Shenzhen. Drawing from the western urban sociological literature on ethnicity and immigration, we distinguished among migrants by their place of origin and to perceive them as different “ethnic” groups. We studied residential enclaves based on concentrations in residential neighbourhoods, and industrial enclaves based on concentrations in two-digit industrial sectors. Based on population survey data, we found that participation in residential enclaves is negatively associated with earnings, but migrants working in industrial enclaves tend to earn more than their counterparts working in the open economy. The associations between residential and industrial enclaves and earnings differ for new arrivals and for those who have left hometown for longer periods of time. While the earnings disadvantage of new arrivals relative to migrants who have left their origin for more than five years is smaller in the native-place residential enclaves than outside enclaves, the advantage of working in industrial enclaves disappears for those new arrivals. Both residential enclaves and industrial enclaves are protective for migrants with fewer years of schooling. Our findings regarding residential enclaves echo the spatial assimilation perspective. Our findings regarding industrial enclaves partially supported the segmented assimilation theory.

16605016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16605016.value: Anti-mainland sentiment has been expanding over the past decade due to the massive influx of tourists and immigrants from the mainland. The simmering of anti-mainland sentiment finally triggered the emergence of a new wave of anti-mainland protests since 2012 against mainland parallel traders, mainland pregnant mothers, mainland school children, and mainland musicians. Protesters denounced mainlanders as “locusts” eating up the city’s resources and held up signs that read “Go back to China” and “Reclaim Hong Kong.” Anti-mainland protesters often clashed with mainland tourists, counter-demonstrators, and Hong Kong police. Despite the importance of anti-mainland protests to Hong Kong's social and political stability and national reunification with China, they have not been carefully studied in the literature. Other than news reports, which have tended to be rely on journalists' impressionistic assessments rather than on rigorous analysis, why and how these protests emerged and spread, and what their meaning is with respect to contemporary social sentiment and politics in Hong Kong has not been investigated. The aim of the proposed research project is to investigate the external factors, the political economy, and the changing pattern of mobilization in Hong Kong that gave rise to this new wave of protests, the sustainability of the movement, and to compare the mobilization to others in the region, including that whichtook place in Taiwan. Analyses will be based on the synthetic resource mobilization/political process approach, which combines the two dominant strains of social movement research and has been advocated by Staggenborg. The approach identifies key social movement organizations (SMOs) and prominent movement entrepreneurs, and traces their strategies and collective action frames. It also examines the interactions among movement organizations, the mass media, and the state. This dynamic approach takes into account the changing political climates and shifting coalitions. Analyses will be based on documentary materials, in-depth interviews, and participant observations. 由於中國內地的遊客和移民大量湧入，所以反中國內地的情緒在香港過去十年一直加深。自2012年以來反對水貨客、雙非孕婦、跨境內地學童以及內地音樂工作者的聲音不斷上升，一觸即發的反中國內地情緒終於引發新一波反中國內地的抗爭。抗爭者譴責中國內地人為“蝗蟲，蠶食這個城市的資源，並高舉起“回到中國”及“光復香港”的橫額。反中國內地示威者往往與內地遊客、反示威人士以及香港警方發生衝突。 雖然反中國內地抗爭對香港社會和政治的穩定性及中國國家統一有重大影響，但現時仍未有研究對它們作出深入仔細的探討。雖然新聞報告會探討這些議題，但往往流於記者印象中的主觀評估，而非嚴格分析。對於這些抗爭為什麼及如何會出現和蔓延，以及它們對現時香港社會情緒和政治環境的意義仍未有深入的研究。 這個研究目的探討導致新一波反中國內地抗爭的外部因素、政治經濟學和動員方式的轉變，以及抗爭運動的可持續性。另外，這研究亦會與其他地區如台灣的 抗爭動員方式進行比較。 研究分析將會綜合資源動員理論/政治過程理論的方法，結合了斯塔根博格倡議的兩大主流的社會運動研究方法。該方法能辨認出重要的社會運動組織（SMO）和著名的運動倡導者，並且追溯他們的策略和集體行動的框架。這亦能夠探討運動組織、大眾傳媒、以及國家之間的互動，所以這個動態研究方法會考慮到不斷變化的政治氣候和聯盟。 研究分析將會以翻查文獻資料、深入訪談和參與觀察的方式進行調查。

16605016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16605016.value: This research project studies the making of the anti-mainland protests in the 2010s from a social movement perspective. We find that anti-mainland protests are divided into three phases: the budding phase in 2011-12, the politicization phase in 2013-14, and the radicalization phase in 2015-17. The budding phase started in 2011. The protests were centered against mainlanders (mainland immigrants, mainland tourists, and mainland pregnant mothers who come to Hong Kong to give birth). Anti-mainland protests were spontaneous and loosely organized through the internet or social media. The protests were a response to the sudden influx of mainland tourists and immigrants after the Individual Visit Scheme came into effect. We argue that since the pan-democrats were too busy fighting for universal suffrage in 2012, civic society rose up in the form of anti-mainland protests to protect its community and lifestyle. Anti-mainland protests in this budding phase had few linkages with the political parties in Hong Kong. Anti-mainland protests then moved on to a new phase of politicization in 2013-14 when protesters developed a fragile alliance with the Neo Democrats, People Power, and Civic Passion parties. The populist democrats injected more resources and raised movement discourse to a higher level. Whereas the anti-mainland protests in the budding phase focused on a specific issue (such as parallel traders), anti-mainland protests in this politicization phase used a new “anti-mainlandization” discourse, a general discourse which could focus on any issue (such as mainland musicians, mainland students, mainland investors, the use of Putonghua, etc.). Under this master frame of “mainlandization,” all the social problems in Hong Kong were said to be caused by the mainlanders. Thus, anti-mainland protests could spread to any area in Hong Kong society, economics or polity. Anti-mainland protesters in this phase were more prone to adopt a “valiant,” “militant,” or “confrontational” strategy to achieve their objectives. The experience of Umbrella Movement served to raise anti-mainland protests to a new radicalization phase during 2015-17. This phase is characterized by adopting a new discourse around “Hong Kong independence,” the formation of many new Hong Kong independence organizations during the election year of 2016, and the increasing incidence of violence reported in anti-mainland protests. Anti-mainland protesters felt empowered when their representatives won seats in the Legislative Council elections. But they faced strong repression not only from the Hong Kong government but also from Beijing, which called for a “zero tolerance” approach to organizations which advocated Hong Kong independence.

16605016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16605016.value: Social movement is a dynamic process. Anti-mainland protests have mutated into by the anti-extradiction protests in 2019, which results in several very large-scale historical protests in the months of June, 2019. I retired from HKUST on June 30th, 2019. If I am still a member of HKUST, I would like to apply for another GRF grant to study the anti-extradiction protest. It would be interesting to study the intrictate connections between anti-mainland protests and anti-extradiction protests, how anti-mainland protests both provide the impetus to give rise to the anti-extradiction protests and create a divison between the peaceful peaceful, democratic middle class protesters and the militant, "violent" working class protesters. Indeed, the outcome of the anti-extradiction protests in 2019 depends very much on whether the two kinds of protesters can cultivate a strong bonding and can develop a unified protest plan among them.

16605016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16605016.value: Anti-mainland protests consist of three phases. (1) The budding phase in 2011. Protests were centered against mainland immigrants, tourists, and pregnant mothers. Protests were spontaneous and loosely organized through the social media; they were a response to the sudden influx of mainland tourists/immigrants and had few linkages with the political parties. (2) The politicization phase in 2013-14 when protesters developed a fragile alliance with the Neo Democrats and People Power. Populist democrats injected resources and developeda a new “anti-mainlandization” discourse which focused on any issue (such as mainland students and investors, Putonghua) and blame mainlanders for causing all the social problems in Hong Kong. Protesters were also prone to adopt a “militant” strategy to achieve their objectives. (3) The failure of Umbrella Movement triggered a new radicalization phase during 2015-17, which is characterized by adopting a “Hong Kong independence” discourse, the formation of Hong Kong independence organizations during the 2016 election year, and the increasing incidence of violence. Anti-mainland protesters felt empowered when their representatives won seats in the Legislative Council elections. But they faced strong repression not only from Hong Kong but also from Beijing government, which called for banning Hong Kong independence organizations.

16606016.value: 在每一個社會裡，大部份的人都必須常與其他人互動，這些互動以及我們的個人行為往往成為我們能否在社會生存和成功的關鍵。我們也常常會觀察其他人的行為，用觀察結果來猜測他們的人格及塑造對他們的印象；這個過程，在心理學稱為「個人知覺」。在此研究中，我們即將探討兒童何時並如何掌握個人知覺的能力，以及個人知覺的能力是否在不同文化也有所不同。第一，我們將檢查 CHILDES 資料庫已有的學齡前兒童（美國、中國大陸、香港）會話記錄，查看小孩子是在什麼情況下接觸種種不同的個性語詞〈例如：好、壞、聰明的、傻傻的〉以及對該個性語詞的認識。第二，我們將會邀請美國、中國大陸、及香港的小孩子參加實驗，以進一步理解學齡前兒童的個人知覺能力。透過我們的研究，我們期待能夠更廣泛，更深入地了解個人知覺的發展。

16606016.label: Realisation of objectives
16606016.value: Our first (revised) objective was to determine when and how person perception emerges in young children across disparate cultures. Specifically, we aimed to locate the time points at which selected personality trait terms (e.g., nice, mean, smart, silly) emerge in children’s conversations with familiar adult figures. We have achieved this objective, through extensive coding of four selected corpora from the CHILDES database. We began by referencing the children whose transcripts were examined by Bartsch and Wellman (1995) and reviewed the transcripts available in the CHILDES English—North American Corpora to ensure that all potential English-speaking children were considered. We selected children who were comparable in age range—approximately 2 years to 5 years of age, consistent with the age range at which person perception has been found to emerge (Liu, Gelman, & Wellman, 2007); and opted to have an equal number of boys and girls for the study. Three of our children were European American, while one child was African American. Children came from families who were either middle class or working class at the time of testing. We also searched through the transcripts available in the CHILDES Chinese (both Cantonese and Mandarin/Putonghua) Corpora and reached out to researchers who had collected longitudinal recordings of children’s conversations with their parents; our search only yielded one child who fit the same criteria we applied to the English-speaking children. We then spent an extensive amount of time developing a coding scheme for the Chinese transcripts; however, an inability to achieve inter-rater reliability and issues that became apparent with the database (i.e., the researchers who had collected the data from this child had made mistakes when recording the child’s age and other pieces of demographic information) forced us to cease this line of data analysis. We therefore focused on addressing our objective with the transcripts of the English-speaking children, who did come from a variety of racial and socioeconomic status backgrounds. Through our analyses, we were able to determine that person perception emerges in the earliest transcripts available to us (1 years, 6 months), initially from parents while speaking to their children. Our second objective was to investigate the extent of person perception in young children, as indexed in recorded conversations and in controlled experimental settings. Specifically, we intended to test whether person perception for the selected set of personality traits emerges concurrently or at different times. We addressed the first half of our second objective through our analysis of the selected children’s transcripts, which included developing a coding scheme for the transcripts, searching and coding through approximately 500 transcripts, and then examining the person perception terms (and the contexts in which they were produced by the parents and children). Through our analysis, we were able to trace how the person perception terms were used by both children and parents (as trait terms describing a person or personified being directly or as action description terms describing behaviour implying a certain trait) and the extent to which parents and children used these terms as the children aged. Through our analysis of the CHILDES data, we identified ten person perception terms in total—good, bad, nice, mean, smart, silly, quiet, careful, funny, and friendly. Although the wide range of person perception term usage is encouraging to see in children’s cognitive and language development, after lengthy discussions, we realised that testing children’s understanding of all ten terms in an experimental setting would pose too much of a burden for them, both in terms of their memory and in terms of the time needed for them to complete the study. Upon further discussion, we have decided to focus on children’s understanding of ability (“smart” from our analysis of the CHILDES data, or competence) instead, and are examining children’s judgments regarding natural ability versus effort in a new study. Our third and final objective was to examine whether person perception leads to children’s preferences for and identification with informants possessing particular personality traits over others. As mentioned in the previous paragraph, we realised from our coding and analysis of the CHILDES data that testing children on all person perception terms (personality traits) would be difficult, given their young ages. Instead, we examined our CHILDES data further. We selected four of the more evaluative person perception terms: nice, good, mean, and bad, as these represented some of the most commonly studied person perception terms in previous literature (Bretherton & Beeghly, 1982; Boseovski & Lee, 2006; Chen, Corriveau, & Harris, 2016). We considered nice and good together as a positive valence category and mean and bad as a negative valence category. Our findings indicate that children and parents used terms in the positive valence category more often than terms in the negative valence category, which could suggest a preference for individuals who possess positive valence over those who possess negative valence. Also as mentioned, we have been collecting experimental data on children’s preferences for and identification with informants who are characterized either by their natural ability (their “smartness”) or by their effort, which should shed further light into how these types of labelling can impact children’s attitudes and decisions.

16606016.label: Major findings and research outcome
16606016.value: With relation to our objectives, our major findings are as follows. First, children were producing person perception terms as early as 1 year and 8 months of age, as soon as they were recorded in natural conversations; all four children were producing person perception terms by their third year. Given the young age in which person perception emerged, children were most likely learning these personality trait words from their primary caregivers—in the case of the four children studied, both of their biological parents. As children got older, the way in which they used the person perception terms increasingly resembled their parents, moving from simpler descriptions of individuals to characterizations of the individuals’ behaviors and of the situations in which the individuals may find themselves. Much of these terms were evaluative (positive or negative) in nature, with positively valenced terms being more commonly applied to individuals the children knew more intimately (as the conversations were typically about the children’s friends, family members, or preferred personified beings). Most of the terms were used in relation to the four target children; that is, parents used person perception terms often to describe their child or the child’s behavior, while the children used these terms to describe themselves. These findings indicate that young children are trait theorists, helped along by their parents or primary caregivers to understand the people in their immediate social world. As noted in Part C, the funding we have received (which largely went to providing the salary of a full-time research assistant and several part-time research consultants) has supported other projects involving young children as well, in that our research assistant and consultants were used to run experiments during the lengthy coding process for our study and to examine the experimental data. We have acknowledged this General Research Fund support in the publications that resulted from these experimental studies.

16606016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16606016.value: Person perception, which involves how people form impressions of one another, is a cornerstone for the fields of personality and social psychology, with potential implications for how we might stereotype other individuals, judge others for their actions, and behave towards them. Understanding how person perception emerges is therefore crucial to surmising how children will form impressions and experience their social environment, especially as they enter school and spend increasingly more time with people other than their immediate family. Given that personality trait terms were observed in the earliest transcripts available in our study, one goal would be to examine conversations of children who are 18 months of age or younger, to know under what circumstances children first learn about person perception (e.g., do children learn about person perception as soon as they learn to speak?). We would also like to examine the impact of person perception understanding on children’s judgments regarding unfamiliar individuals; as discussed in previous sections, we intend to focus first on children’s understanding of natural ability (smartness) and how labelling someone as smart may then influence their decisions subsequently.

16606016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16606016.value: Are you my friend, or my foe? The impressions we form of other individuals—for instance, whether they are nice or mean—can drive our subsequent attitudes and behaviors towards them. As adults, we often form impressions of strangers immediately, and these impressions can remain robust for an extended period of time. In this study, we sought to examine the emergence of person perception, by analyzing the transcripts of conversations that occurred naturally between young children and their parents. We found that children heard personality trait terms (e.g., nice, mean, smart, silly) from their biological parents and were producing these terms well before they reached two years of age. Both parents and children often used these terms to evaluate the target individual positively or negatively. Finally, the trait terms most often were used to describe the children themselves, suggesting that children were learning about person perception with regards to themselves first. Our findings suggest that children learn to think about personality traits and to form impressions at an early age, possibly as soon as they are capable of extended conversations, and are helped along by their primary caregivers to understand the people in their immediate social world.

16631916.label: Project Objectives
16631916.value: Construct a new narrative of the European political-theological reception of Chinese philosophy in relationship to the development of European modernity. Provide a more comprehensive interpretation of changing European attitudes towards Chinese political culture and thought from the image of Confucian "philosopher kings" (Leibniz, Wolff, and Voltaire) to the idea of "oriental despotism" (Kant, Herder, Hegel). Offer an account of the shift in European perspectives on Chinese religious thinking from the early Enlightenment interpretation of Confucian "natural theology” to more negative assessments of paganism, pantheism, and atheism in the late and post-Enlightenment period.

16631916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16631916.value: My thesis is that the interpretive encounter with non-Western cultures played a crucial role in the formation of European modernity. The ethical-political and political theological notions of autonomy and rationality, interpreted as unique achievements of modern Western civilization, arose through processes of exchange and struggle with non-Western ideas, cultures, institutions, and practices. I will explore through archival research and close reading of primary and secondary materials a test case for this thesis: the engagement of early modern European philosophy with China and Chinese thought. There are three phases of the philosophical encounter with China that I will trace: Initially, Chinese philosophy was condemned as pagan and the Chinese were seen as a people in need of Christian salvation. In a second phase, proto- and early Enlightenment thinkers looked at non-European cultures and China in particular as sources of learning and wisdom in ethics, politics, and natural religion. In a third phase, late Enlightenment and Romantic thinkers interpreted Chinese culture and thought through the interpretive lens of “Oriental despotism" that indirectly represented the politics and theology of the old regimes of Europe. It was contrasted with "European liberty" achieved through Enlightenment rationality and autonomy (Kant) or a renewed notion of "Christian liberty" for thinkers associated with Romanticism (Herder, Schlegel). I examine these shifting attitudes towards China and Chinese philosophy through a contextual analysis of the sources for key figures in Early Modern European Philosophy (Leibniz, Wolff, Kant, Herder, and Hegel). Through a review of their historical contexts and sources, my research shows that the accounts of European travelers and missionaries in China are a primary factor in explaining the shifting attitudes about China from the positive enthusiasm of the early Enlightenment (Leibniz, Wolff, Diderot, and Voltaire) to the negative assessment of the late Enlightenment (Kant) and post-Enlightenment period (Herder, Schlegel, and Hegel). This study elucidates the category of “political theology” to explain how European thinkers interpreted the Chinese political system and Confucian political thought as providing a model of benevolent enlightened kingship rooted in natural theology in the early Enlightenment (Leibniz, Wolff, and Voltaire) and then became an example of the abuses of absolute power and obedience. The idea of China is shaped by disputes over the appropriate relationship between politics and religion and enlightened kingship and popular self-determination. The construction of the “West” and “China” as its other during this period continues to shape the later Western reception of Chinese culture and thought. 本課題試圖闡明， 與東方文化的詮釋性交流與交鋒，在歐洲現代化的形成過程中扮演了至關重要的角色。在倫理政治學和政治神學的理念中，如自主性(autonomy)和理性(rationality)，雖然被視為歐洲現代文明的獨有成就，但它們卻產生于與東方的觀念、文化、體制和習俗的交流與交鋒之中。通過文獻研究，對一手和二手資料的深入分析，筆者將用一主要的文化場域──早期歐洲現代哲學與中國和中國思想的交匯──來確證此觀點。我的研究會追溯西方與中國哲學交鋒中的三個階段：最初，中國哲學被判為異教，而中國人則被視為是需要被基督救贖的人民。在第二個階段中，原創和早期的啟蒙思想家卻視歐洲以外的文化（尤其是中國）為模範，倫理、政治和自然宗教方面的智慧資源。在第三個階段，晚期啟蒙思想家和浪漫主義者則以「東方專制統治者」的有色眼鏡詮釋中國文化，这种阐释亦間接地代表了歐洲古老政體中的政治與神學觀念。這種專制迥然對立於「歐洲人的自由」，這種觀念產生於啟蒙理性和自主性概念（如康德），或是在那些受浪漫主義影響的思想家（如黑爾德爾和施勒格爾）那裡重新得到關注的 「基督教自由」理念。笔者將透過對早期現代西方哲學的重要人物(如萊布尼茲、華夫、康德、黑爾德爾和黑格爾)的思想脈絡進行分析，考察三種對中國和中國哲學態度的轉變。通過追溯他們思想的歷史背景和來源，筆者的研究指出，在對中國的態度由早期啟蒙思想(如萊布尼茲、華夫、狄德羅和伏爾泰)的熱衷追捧到晚期啟蒙(如康德)和後啟蒙時代(如黑爾德爾、施勒格爾和黑格爾)的負面評價的轉變當中，歐洲旅行者和傳教士在中國的記述是至關重要的因素。此研究亦通過闡明「政治神學」此一範疇，解釋歐洲思想家如何詮釋中國的政治制度和儒家政治思想，被認為是早期啟蒙思想中的自然神學(萊布尼茲、華夫和伏爾泰)提供了一個開明與仁愛的君權理念的典範，而此典范亦成为了滥用絕對权力與驯從的例證。對中國的認知，亦由關於政治與宗教、開明的君權與大眾的自我決斷間如何取得有效平衡的論爭中逐漸形塑而成。在此過程中，對「西方」與作為他者的「中國」的建構，持續地影響了日後西方對中國文化與思想的反應與接受。

16633316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16633316.value: 中国政府与纠纷解决: 以医疗纠纷为例

16633316.label: Project Objectives
16633316.value: To build a dataset of medical disputes in a few cities where I will collect data on medical dispute cases. The dataset will be used to analyze dispute resolution and the role of the mediation committee and state agencies. To understand the motivation behind the authoritarian state’s motivation to institutionalize civil disputes if the state has taken measures to shift the responsibility for civil dispute resolution. To analyze the reasons for the (in)effectiveness of the state’s withdrawal from the resolution of civil disputes if the withdrawal does indeed occur.

To understand the motivation behind the authoritarian state’s motivation to institutionalize civil disputes if the state has taken measures to shift the responsibility for civil dispute resolution.
To analyze the reasons for the (in)effectiveness of the state’s withdrawal from the resolution of civil disputes if the withdrawal does indeed occur.

16633316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16633316.value: This proposed research aims to address the issue of how an authoritarian government like China can institutionalize the resolution of social conflict. In recent years, China has witnessed a great deal of social conflict, but not all of these disputes are caused by the state. Instead, the majority of the disputes are between social actors or citizens, and they are not caused by, or tied to, the state. These disputes constitute a heavy burden on the party state because it has to address not only state-citizen disputes but also many civil disputes. For this reason, the party state is likely motivated to institutionalize the resolution of civil disputes by distancing itself from conflict settlement. This research addresses this question: If the party-state is motivated to withdraw from the resolution of civil disputes, what makes the state’s withdrawal effective? In other words, how can civil disputes be resolved without the (heavy) involvement of the state? This proposed research will use the case of medical disputes in China to examine the state’s avoidance of the responsibility for civil dispute resolution. Medical disputes between hospitals and patients or their families have become a serious concern of the government because of both their large number and the tension involved. Some of the medical disputes have turned into disruptive actions. As a result, the government encourages the creation of the mediation committee for medical disputes. The mediation committee is not a state agency but a third-party mediator or civil institution. The committee has proven to be an important channel through which citizens settle their disputes. This research will examine the operation of the mediation committee to discover how it can play the role of an effective third party. It will also analyze whether and how the party-state influences the operation of the mediation committee. In doing so, it will address how the state has delegated the power of mediation to the mediation committee as well as whether and how the government intervenes in the mediation, if there is intervention. The research will shed light on the rationale for institutionalizing conflict resolution in China. If the state is willing to delegate power to civil institutions in an effective way, it may avoid at least part of its responsibility for conflict resolution without endangering social stability. 该研究旨在探讨像中国这样的威权政府如何使纠纷解决制度化。近年来中国发生了大量的社会纠纷，但这些纠纷并非都是政府引发的。其中很多纠纷是与政府没有直接关系的民事纠纷，而解决民事纠纷成了政府沉重的负担。政府因此有动力让民事纠纷的解决制度化。该研究具体探讨政府如何才能有效地摆脱民事纠纷解决的负担。换句话说，本研究考察民事纠纷如何在政府不深入参与的情况下得以解决。 本研究以医疗纠纷为例探讨中国政府如何避开解决民事纠纷的责任。医疗纠纷因其巨大的数量和激烈程度而引发政府的高度关注。部分医疗纠纷甚至演变成了破坏性的集体行动。为此，政府鼓励或者直接成立了医疗纠纷调节委员会。该委员会不是国家机关，而是类似第三方的民间机构。医调委成了解决医疗纠纷的重要渠道。 本研究通过考察医调委的运作分析其如何成为有效解的决纠纷的第三方机构。本研究也会分析政府是否 (和如何) 影响医调委的运作。通过分析政府如何向医调委让度解决纠纷的责任和政府在必要的时候如何介入医调委的纠纷调解，本研究旨在揭示中国纠纷解决制度化的逻辑。如果政府有效地让度权力以便解决纠纷，同时又不影响其对社会的控制，政府就有让纠纷解决制度化的动力。

16633316.label: Realisation of objectives
16633316.value: 1. I have collected about 2,000 case of medical disputes, in addition to interviewing more than 80 medical staff members and government officials. This dataset has been used to analyze the resolution of medical disputes by focusing on the role of the mediation committee and state agencies. 2. By examining medical disputes and interviewing government officials and hospital management people, my study shows that Chinese local governments are motivated to diffuse the pressure of managing social conflict, especially civil disputes. As the Chinese government monopolizes political power, it also shoulders broad responsibilities of governance in society. Some citizens have approached the government for solving their civil disputes. Addressing these many disputes requires resources, energy, and time. Local authorities are thus motivated to shift the burden to social or quasi-social organizations in order to reduce its own burdens. In managing medical disputes, Chinese local governments created, or supported the creation of, the mediation committee of medical disputes to reduce its own burden. 3. My research finds that in the management of medical disputes, the government is able to partly withdraw from the dispute resolution. The government’s intervention in medical disputes can be divided into three categories: as the decision maker, as an advisor, and delegation of full responsibility to the medication committee. When the government becomes the decision maker, it becomes directly involved in the resolution of disputes. As direct intervention requires costs and encourages patients and/or their families to approach the government for solution, this mode is less frequently used. In our collection, direct intervention was used in less than 16 percent of the total cases that were interviewed by the government. To sum up, the goals have been realized.

16633316.label: Major findings and research outcome
16633316.value: 1.The government’s motivation for creating the mediation committee and the modes of intervention. My research shows that both the central and local governments are motivated to shift the burden of dispute resolution to civil organizations. It also finds that the government is not able to entirely withdraw from dispute resolution because of its monopoly of political power. Based on the degree of involvement, the intervention can be divided into three types: intervention as the decision maker, intervention as an advisor, and delegation of full responsibility to the mediation committee. I presented the findings in a paper entitled “Addressing Medical Disputes in China: Government and Responsibility Shifting.” 2. The government’s response to citizens’ online complaints. As some citizens may report their grievances, including those caused by medical disputes, online, the government also needs to respond to such online grievances, I find that the government has selectively responded to online complaints, depending on the number of people involved in a complaint and the severity of grievances. These findings were presented in the paper “Online Political Participation in China: Local Government and Differentiated Response.” 3. Government and conflict management in China The management of medical disputes is part of the management of social conflict in China. I have also examined the government’s broad strategies of dispute resolution in a changing context in recent years. I found that the government’s tolerance of radical modes of dispute resolution like collective protests has declined in recent years. I presented these finding in a book manuscript “Shaping Political Opportunity: State and Social Protests in Contemporary China.”

16633316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16633316.value: My research on the government's management of medical disputes reflects its rationale for dealing with civil disputes that constitute a large portion of social disputes in China. Civil disputes account for more than 80 percent of the cases accepted by Chinese courts each year. Thus, how to manage civil disputes remains a constant issue faced the government. I will continue to examine how the Chinese government deals with medical disputes in order to understand the political logic of its management of civil disputes. My plan is to continue to collect cases of medical disputes and interview medical staff and government officials.

16633316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16633316.value: Medical disputes have become an important source of social conflict in China, and some disputes have escalated into violent or bloody confrontations between medical staff and patients and/or their families. This project examines how the Chinese government has managed social conflicts, including medical disputes. In China, as the government monopolizes political power, it is expected to shoulder broad responsibilities for governance, including dispute resolution. However, the broad responsibilities constitute heavy burdens on the government. As a result, the government is motivated to shift or diffuse the burden to non-government actors. This rationale of responsibility shifting is reflected in the government’s management of medical disputes. The Chinese government created, or encouraged the creation of, the mediation committee of medical disputes in order to diffuse the responsibility. This mediation committee is not a government agency. By having this organization shoulder the responsibility of dispute resolution, the government succeeded in shifting some of the burden and only needed to intervene in a limited number of medical disputes.

16642516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16642516.value: At present most historians conceptualise Yunnan as an area both remote from the Chinese political centre and isolated from the outside world. This project proposes to analyse historical data concerning Tai polity formation and transportation routes in order to investigate economic, social and cultural connections with Mainland Southeast Asia. Hitherto this type of empirical study has never been attempted, and it will offer a vibrant perspective for understanding Yunnan, not as an area at the margins of Chinese and Southeast Asian history, but as an area connecting mainland Southeast Asia with the Chinese world. By illuminating hitherto unknown interlinks this study will disclose the extent of Chinese dynastic impact on the course of history in western mainland Southeast Asia. It seeks to reveal the reality of local political conditions, and highlight the Southeast Asian characteristics of Tai polities in southern Yunnan. One long term impact will be to revise past biases which stipulate that the world of Southeast Asia ends at the present day international border in Yunnan. This research project has three objectives. First, to empirically prove that the rise and fall of Tai polities in western mainland Southeast Asia had close linkages with political change in Yunnan between the thirteenth and the mid-fifteenth centuries. Second, to verify the process of Tai polity formation through a case study of the largest and most important contemporary Tai polity in western mainland Southeast Asia known to history as Mäng Maaw (Ch: Luchuan麓川; Bur: Mawdon Mawke; Th: Müang Mao) using Tai chronicles and Chinese sources. Third, to clarify empirically how Mongol/Yuan war routes into western mainland Southeast Asia facilitated the growth of transportation routes, and spawned new autonomous Tai polities. The data to be collected and analysed includes historical documents and stelae (stone inscriptions) preserved in libraries, museums and archives. Most of these sources are written in Tai (Dai/Shan) and Chinese, and some of the most valuable sources are the stelae that still remain standing in western Yunnan villages. Stelae honouring the indigenous leaders of western Yunnan who participated in Mongol/Yuan campaigns in western mainland Southeast Asia provide detailed data concerning the role that they played in the administration of Mongol territory in western Southeast Asia and Mongol/Yuan activities that contributed to the rise of the Mäng Maaw polity. 歷史家往往視雲南為，既離中國王朝政治中心遙遠, 又與外界隔離的區域。 本研究旨在透過分析傣族政權之建立和交通史料為例來闡明，自13世紀至15世紀，雲南與東南亞大陸西部的經濟社會以及文化關係。 期待通過此研究闡明一些新的觀點；目前歷史界經常將雲南僅當做處於中國與東南亞周邊的一個區域，本研究以改變此類之固定概念為目標。在史料研究中，雲南的歷史地位不容小覷，雲南扮演一個連結東南亞和中國文化圈的重要角色。 此研究顯示中國王朝對於東南亞大陸西部歷史究竟有過何種程度的影響，同時亦能解讀當地政治的實況和雲南傣族政權所帶有的東南亞文化特色。此研究旨在有助於更好的了解東南亞文化圈的界限，不應僅以現在雲南國境線為止。 本研究有三個目標。第一，證明 自13世紀至15世紀，在東南亞大陸西部傣族政權的興亡與元明兩朝統治雲南的政策有密切關係。第二， 根據傣文編年史和漢文史料分析當時在東南亞大陸西部最強大的傣族政權， 傣文稱勐卯弄（漢文：麓川； 緬文：Mawdon Mawke; 泰國文: Müang Mao）的興亡，以此為例來闡明傣族政權的形成過程。第三，實證 自雲南至東南亞大陸西部，蒙元所用之行軍道路促進了交通道路的發展，助於傣族政權的形成。 將要收集的史料包括圖書館，博物館以及檔案館收藏的傣漢文史書，文書和碑刻。其中，滇西的碑刻，學術價值特別高，提供有關在蒙元統治下的東南亞大陸西部，滇西土官擔任過何種行政工作，而且蒙元的政策如何促成了勐卯弄政權的出現等資料。

16642516.label: Realisation of objectives
16642516.value: First Objective: The first objective of empirically proving the close link between the rise of Tai polities in western mainland Southeast Asia and political change in Yunnan between the thirteenth and the mid-fifteenth centuries has been achieved. I have demonstrated that Mäng2 Maaw2 (Moeng Mao, Ch. Luchuan麓川), the largest political Tai confederation in the western mainland during the fourteenth century, emerged due to changes in Mongol-Yuan administration of northern Mainland Southeast Asia (see 6.1). I realized this objective by thoroughly investigating stelae from the greater Dali area of Yunnan which recorded the relationship between magnate families and the Duan family, the former Dali royal house. These stelae provide data, not recorded elsewhere, that indicate the implications Mongol-Yuan restoration of political authority to the Duan and their appointment as the most important administrator of local society in western Yunnan. They are particularly important for revealing the intermediary role played by the Duan family in the Mongol-Yuan advance into northern mainland Southeast Asia. The Duan, acted as intermediaries and their restoration ended up preserving many features of Dali administrative and cultural practices, including their crucially important patronage of the Buddhist religion. In particular, these local level sources reveal the Duan family’s connections with northern mainland Southeast Asia, especially their facilitation of Mongol-Yuan military campaigns into mainland Southeast Asia, and administration in the upper Mekong and upper Ayeyarwady river areas. It was this local level data that made possible the re-interpretation of accounts in the Yuan History and other standard texts to demonstrate how political changes in Yunnan at the core area of the former Dali kingdom affected Tai polities in northern Mainland Southeast Asia. The finding that the Mongol-Yuan retained the Duan family as administrators reveals that fundamental political change in Yunnan that led to the incorporation of Tai polities into the Chinese empire, came not with Khubilai Khan’s conquest of Dali in 1254 as previously thought, but after the Ming conquest of Yunnan in 1382. Therefore, the Mongol-Yuan foundation of Yunnan as a province in 1276 did not create a great rupture with the past, it was the Ming state that initiated the transformation of local society into a province after 1382. Past research has clarified the Ming dynasty’s 60-odd year military conflict with the Mäng2 Maaw2 kingdom that led to its elimination in c. 1444. To put relations between the Ming dynasty and the Mäng2 Maaw2 kingdom in the context of a Southeast Asian polity influencing Yunnan, I have used the concept of internal frontiers to illustrate that the Mäng2 Maaw2 at the height of its power affected Ming governance in fifteenth century Yunnan. Internal frontiers were upland spaces which the Ming could not administrate either directly, or indirectly through native officials. Their existence bespeaks how imminent threat of invasion from the Mäng2 Maaw2 kingdom limited the ability of the Ming to govern all the uplands in Yunnan. The Ming’s choice to abandon administrating parts of northern Southeast Asia through the the mediation of the Duan family as practised from the Dali Kingdom period afforded Mäng Maaw the opportunity to expand northwards into Yunnan. The Ming only managed to dismantle the Mäng Maaw kingdom after much preparation and a long war. The emergency situation with the Mäng2 Maaw2 kingdom constrained the ability of the Ming to implement policies for governance of local society in Yunnan. Second objective: I have verified the process of Tai polity formation through the case study of the Mäng2 Maaw2 kingdom. In order to understand polity formation and its relations with Chinese dynastic power from the Tai perspective, rather than the Chinese dynastic perspective, it is imperative to use Tai sources. I have used the Mäng Maaw Chronicle and Hsienwi Chronicle to include the Tai perspective in clarifying the historical background to the rise of the Mäng2 Maaw2 polity c. 1335-50s in the context of Mongol-Yuan relations (see 6.1). The main source in Tai script, the Mäng Maaw Chronicle, was published under the title Meng Guozhanbi Ji Meng Mao Gudai Zhu Wang Shi (猛果占璧及猛卯古代諸王史) by the Yunnan Minzu Chubanshe in 1988. I have had to spend time working on the verifying the text because of the peculiar circumstances surrounding its publication. The published text is a photolithographic reproduction of a handwritten copy of the original text which is housed in the Dehong zhou archives in Mangshi. The original was authored during the 18th century, and is probably a copy of 1778. Some wording in the reproduction of the handwritten copy have been changed from Tai into Chinese by the scribe in the process of hand-copying in the 1980s, but the texts are basically the same. I have been through the difficult passages with local Tai consultants conversant with the old script, and I have completed consulting the 16th century manuscript of the earliest known Sino-Tai vocabulary, the Huayi Yiyu 華夷譯語 (Translated Words of the Chinese and Barbarians) at the Toyo Bunko, Tokyo, Japan. I am in a position to translate the text for publication in the future in order to outline the dismantlement of the Mäng Maaw kingdom by the Ming dynasty in the mid-15th century from the Tai perspective. The opening chapter of the Mäng Maaw Chronicle traces the kingdom to walled cities along the Ayeyarwady river in the Dali Kingdom period and earlier. The events in this chapter cannot be verified by other sources and are suffused with myth. Local consultants claim that a detailed chapter of the foundation of the kingdom in the fourteenth century exists as a separate manuscript. Despite spending much time searching, I have not been able to locate this “missing” chapter, but this has not affected the realisation of the objective. Third Objective I have achieved the third objective of clarifying the role of how the new autonomous Tai polity of Mang Maaw emerged along the communication routes used by the Mongol-Yuan, and the findings have published (see 6.1). This was achieved by investigating by linking the ethnic polities conquered by the Mongol-Yuan to communication routes known from Ming/Qing sources. This investigation showed that Tai polities emerged along the important communication routes after the Mongol-Yuan withdrew in 1303 from the upper Ayeyarwady river region. An attempt was made to use the communication routes recorded in nineteenth century Tai documents in the Scott Collection at the Cambridge University Library to verify communication routes. However, it proved difficult to identity the Tai names of villages recorded in these documents with those in Chinese sources of the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. Therefore, I changed the approach and investigated communication routes in the pre-thirteenth century period. I clarified that the conquest of the upper Ayeyarwady and upper Mekong river regions by the Nanzhao kingdom in the eighth century opened up the communication routes used by the Mongol-Yuan, and were essential for Sinitic control over the region, see Daniels (2020). Therefore, as soon as Sinitic control over the upper Ayeyarwady and upper Mekong weakened, local ethnic groups such as the Tai gained domination over the communication routes, and used them to consolidate and strengthen their political power.
