17111016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111016.value: Esophageal cancer is the sixth most common cause of cancer-related deaths in the world and the prognosis is generally poor. China alone accounts for approximately half of all new esophageal cancer cases per year, with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) being the predominant histologic subtype. The lethality of esophageal cancer is attributed to early dissemination of tumor cells. Understanding the molecular mechanisms that promote migration and invasion of cancer cells is therefore essential to tackle this highly aggressive disease. We have established (through in vitro selection) human ESCC cells that are highly invasive as cell line models that can be used to identify important regulators of cancer invasion. Gene profiling identified serglycine as the top upregulated gene in highly invasive ESCC cells. The function of serglycin in esophageal cancer has not been documented previously. Data from our pilot study show that ectopic overexpression of serglycin significantly promoted esophageal cancer cell invasion in vitro and experimental metastasis in vivo. Bioinformatics analysis and further comparison of gene profiling of serglycine-overexpressing ESCC cells with control cells suggested that CXCR2 (CXC chemokine receptor 2) may mediate the function of serglycin in ESCC invasion and metastasis. Our data showed that forced expression of serglycin increased the expression levels of CXCR2, p-ERK (phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinase), and MMP-2 (matrix metalloproteinase 2). Notably, blockade of CXCR2 with neutralizing antibody abrogated the stimulating effects of serglycin on the ERK pathway, MMP2 expression, and esophageal cancer cell invasion. We therefore hypothesize that serglycin can promote cancer invasion and metastasis in ESCC through activation of a CXCR2-MEK/ERK-MMP2 signaling axis. This regulatory mechanism has not been reported previously. In the proposed study, we will explore the clinicopathological significance of serglycin by studying and correlating the expression level of serglycin in primary esophageal cancer and lymph node metastases. The potential of serum serglycin as a non-invasive diagnostic and prognostic marker of ESCC will also be explored. We will also perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to examine the effects of serglycin, and the mediating role of CXCR2-MEK/ERK-MMP2 pathway, on esophageal cancer invasion and metastasis.

17111016.label: Realisation of objectives
17111016.value: OBJECTIVE 1: To determine the potential of serglycin as a diagnostic and prognostic marker in esophageal cancer We compared serglycin (SRGN) expression in tumor tissue and normal tissue in TCGA and GTEx databases using Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis. SRGN was found to be overexpressed in esophageal cancer. Data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases showed that SRGN expression was significantly higher in both esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and esophageal adenocarcinoma tumor samples than in adjacent non-neoplastic tissue, which suggests that SRGN has diagnostic significance in patients with esophageal cancer. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis of the TCGA esophageal carcinoma cohort showed that high expression of SRGN in tumor was associated with poorer survival. We also evaluated serum SRGN expression level as a non-invasive prognostic marker of ESCC, and found that patients with higher serum SRGN had significantly poorer overall survival rates. Multivariate analysis showed that SRGN level in admission serum was an independent prognostic factor. In summary, we have obtained first evidence that high expression of SRGN in primary tumors has diagnostic significance, and that elevated serum SRGN has prognostic significance in patients with ESCC. OBJECTIVE 2: To investigate whether serglycin promotes proliferation, invasion and metastasis of esophageal cancer cells using in vitro and in vivo assays ESCC cell lines with stable overexpression of wild type SRGN, SRGN lacking the GAG attachment site (designated ΔGAG) and mutated SRGN (mGAG) were established. shRNAs and siRNAs were used for stable and transient knockdown, respectively. The results from cell viability assays showed that forced expression of SRGN, ∆GAG or mGAG did not affect the viability of ESCC cells. In the cell invasion and migration assays, ESCC cells with SRGN overexpression showed enhanced invasive and migratory potential, which was abolished by perturbation of the GAG attachment domain, indicating that the GAG chains of SRGN are crucial for SRGN to promote cell invasion and migration. Using the experimental metastasis model, we found that intravenously injected SRGN-overexpressing ESCC cells had a superior ability to metastasize to the lungs of nude mice. The ability of parental ESCC cells to form tumors and lung metastasis was decreased after SRGN-knockdown. Western blot analysis of conditioned medium (CM) showed that SRGN was secreted from ESCC cells in a glycosylated form since digestion with chondroitinase ABC reduced it to the size of its core protein. We collected the CM from the CON-, SRGN-, ∆GAG- and mGAG-expressing ESCC cell lines and compared them as chemoattractant in cell invasion assays. The results showed that only the CM of SRGN-expressing could induce the invasion of ESCC cells. These data indicate that SRGN can exert autocrine pro-invasive effects on ESCC cells, and that the GAG-binding domain of SRGN is crucial in this function. We also studied the effect of SRGN on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), which is an essential process in cancer metastasis. Western blotting analysis showed that epithelial cell markers (including claudin-1, ZO-1 and E-cadherin) and mesenchymal markers (including N-cadherin, Slug, Snail and β-catenin) were not affected by SRGN overexpression in ESCC cells. Knockdown of SRGN had no effects on EMT program in ESCC cells. In addition, analysis of pathway activity data in the ESCC subgroup of TCGA-ESCA dataset showed no correlation between SRGN expression and EMT pathway. Thus, the pro-invasive function of SRGN is likely to involve mechanisms other than EMT. In summary, this objective was fully achieved by obtaining solid in vitro and in vivo data to support that SRGN plays a functional role in promoting metastasis-related functions in ESCC. OBJECTIVE 3: To study the role of CXCR2-ERK-MMP2 signaling axis in mediating the effects of serglycin on esophageal cancer cell motility and invasiveness Although our preliminary data showed that SRGN overexpression increased the expression levels of CXCR2 in two ESCC cells, subsequent experiments using other SRGN-overexpressing ESCC cell lines failed to show consistent CXCR2 upregulation. On the other hand, Reverse Phase Protein Array (RPPA) analysis confirmed that SRGN activated the MAPK/ERK pathway. PANTHER pathway and Gene Ontology (GO) analysis showed that SRGN positively regulated the ERK1/2 cascade. Western blotting showed that SRGN upregulated ERK-associated factors such as p-MEK1/2, p-ERK1/2 and p-p90RSK, but ∆GAG and mGAG overexpression had no such effects, indicating that the SRGN-induced activation of ERK1/2 cascade was GAG-dependent. Matrix metalloproteases (MMPs) are essential degrading enzymes of the extracellular matrix. Western blots showed that MMP2 was elevated in both cell lysates and CM of SRGN-overexpressing cells. Gelatin zymography assay revealed increased MMP2 activity in SRGN-overexpressing cells, but not in the ∆GAG- or mGAG-expressing cells. Furthermore, treatment of SRGN-overexpressing ESCC cells with a MEK inhibitor, trametinib, decreased cell invasiveness and MMP2 expression, thus confirming that the pro-invasive function of SRGN was mediated by activation of ERK-MMP2. Since our results in Objective 2 showed that SRGN stimulates ESCC cell invasion and migration in an autocrine manner, we screened for differentially expressed chemokines in SRGN-overexpressing cells using a multiplex chemokine array. Midkine (MDK) was identified as the top upregulated protein in the CM of SRGN-overexpressing cells. Phospho-Kinase Array analysis showed that MDK upregulated p-ERK1/2 expression. Immunofluorescent staining, in situ proximity ligation assay (PLA) and co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) analysis demonstrated that MDK was bound to the GAG chains of SRGN in ESCC cells and was secreted together with SRGN. Moreover, SRGN could also bind to and upregulate the secretion of MMP2. Taken together, our data showed that SRGN-induced MDK secretion and the ERK-MMP2 regulatory axis play an important role in mediating the effects of SRGN on ESCC cell motility and invasiveness. We also studied the regulatory function of SRGN on MMP9, which is another MMP frequently upregulated in many types of cancer. Like MMP2, the induction of MMP9 by SRGN was GAG-dependent. However, unlike MMP2, the increase of MMP9 in cell lysates and CM of SRGN-overexpressing cells was not abolished by treatment with trametinib, which suggests that its upregulation was ERK-independent. OBJECTIVE 4: To study the mechanism by which serglycin regulates CXCR2 signaling This objective came about because GO analysis suggested involvement of CXCR2 signaling pathway in the functional role of serglycin, which led us to postulate that the pro-invasive/metastatic function of serglycin might be mediated by a CXCR2. However, as mentioned above, we did not find consistent upregulation of CXCR2 receptor amongst SRGN-expressing ESCC cell lines. In addition, chemokine array analysis did not show significant increase in CXCL-8/IL-8 (a known ligand of CXCR2) in the CM of SRGN-overexpressing cells. We therefore decided not to further pursue this hypothesis, and instead focused on MDK as an alternative mediator of SRGN, and as a possible ligand that interacts with SRGN receptor(s) to activate this axis. Co-IP results showed that MDK could interact with CD44, a known SRGN receptor. Furthermore, exogenous MDK stimulated the ERK pathway in a CD44-dependent manner, indicating that CD44 was a crucial receptor in this autocrine stimulatory mechanism. Although our experimental data did not support a significant role of CXCR2 in the pro-invasive/metastatic function of serglycin in ESCC cells, we obtained important data showing that MDK can bind to GAGs of SRGN to form a SRGN/MDK/CD44 complex. This novel finding provides a better understanding of CD44 as a receptor and mediator of SRGN in autocrine stimulation of ERK signaling in ESCC cells. We therefore considered this objective mostly accomplished.

17111016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111016.value: (i) High SRGN expression in ESCC is associated with cancer invasion, poor patients’ survival rate and metastasis: Highly invasive ESCC sublines have elevated SRGN expression, while forced expression of SRGN can increase invasion and migration of ESCC cell lines. In patients with ESCC, high serum SRGN level is associated with poor survival. (ii) SRGN promotes cancer cell invasion in an autocrine and GAG-dependent manner: SRGN is secreted in a glycosylated form into the tumor microenvironment by ESCC cells. The integrity of the GAG attachment domain is critical in the pro-invasive function of SRGN. Cancer cell-secreted SRGN can increase the invasive potential of nearby ESCC cells in an autocrine manner. (iii) SRGN stabilizes c-Myc by autocrine activation of ERK pathway: CHX chase assay showed that SRGN increased the stability of c-Myc protein in ESCC cells. This stabilizing effect was found to be autocrine and GAG-dependent. (iv) SRGN-induced MDK mediates the pro-invasive and ERK/c-Myc-upregulating effects of SRGN: SRGN upregulates MDK expression in ESCC cells and promotes its secretion. It is through this mechanism that SRGN promotes cancer cell invasion, activation of ERK pathway, and increase the stability of c-Myc. (v) SRGN upregulates and binds to matrix MMPs: SRGN upregulates and increases secretion of MMP2 and MMP9. MMP2 binds to glycosylated SRGN, while MMP9 can bind to both glycosylated SRGN and SRGN core protein. The experiments were mostly the effort of a PhD student (Yun ZHU) whose thesis was submitted in October 2020 (Part C10 #1). It is shortlisted for Dr KP Stephen Chang Gold Medal. The findings were presented at six international scientific meetings (Part C9 #1-6) and won awards in two of the meetings (Part C9 #3 & #4). A full-length research article is accepted for publication in the journal Theranostics which ranks 10/139 under the category “Medicine, research & experimental category”, and has a 5-year impact factor of 9.108. The 2019 impact factor is 8.579 (Part C8 #1).

17111016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111016.value: Besides having an autocrine function, we found that SRGN-overexpressing ESCC cells had the ability to enhance the blood vessel-forming ability of endothelial cells in culture, which may be mediated by MDK. Importantly, this suggests that SRGN and/or its binding partners have paracrine function(s) in the tumor microenvironment during cancer progression. We also found that serglycin could be secreted in an exosome-associated form by highly invasive ESCC cells. We therefore extended our study to investigate the roles and mechanisms of serglycin in the tumor microenvironment of esophageal cancer. This project was awarded a RGC GRF grant of $1,107,909 in 2019.

17111016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111016.value: Esophageal cancer is the sixth most common cause of cancer-related deaths in the world and the prognosis is generally poor. Our earlier study showed that serglycin, a proteoglycan decorated with glycosaminoglycan side chains, was overexpressed and secreted by highly invasive esophageal cancer cells, but little is known about the roles of this unique proteoglycan in esophageal cancer. In this study, we investigated the clinical relevance of serglycin in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and found that patients with elevated serum serglycin level had poorer survival rate, which suggests that serum serglycin may be used as a novel non-invasive biomarker for prognosis. We also obtained in vitro and in vivo data to prove that serglycin and its binding partners could promote ESCC cell invasion, migration and metastasis. Our results also showed that the glycosaminoglycan chains of serglycin are important in these functions. For example, they bind midkine, which was one of the chemokines that was upregulated and secreted by serglycin-overexpressing ESCC cells. Through this interaction, serglycin and midkine can in turn bind to the CD44 receptor of cancer cells to activate the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway. Strategies that target serglycin or its glycosaminoglycan chains may be a new direction in ESCC therapy.

17111516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111516.value: EB病毒（EBV）感染與未分化型鼻咽癌的相關性幾近100%。然而，在體外培養條件下，若無選擇優勢，EBV附加體極易丟失。而病毒附加體得以在體內腫瘤中保留，意味著病毒必定有助於腫瘤的生長和/或存活。大多數促進生長的EBV潛伏蛋白是具有免疫原性的，其在腫瘤中的表達量通常較低且具有異質性。因此，大量從EBV編碼的BART轉錄產物中衍生出的，非免疫原型的miR-BARTs可能與鼻咽癌的致病機制有關。我們的前期數據表明，EBV感染可促進鼻咽癌的體內生長，而非體外培養條件下。重要的是，miR-BARTs在體內生長的情況下高表達。已知miR-BARTs具有抑制細胞凋亡的作用。基於此，我們假設miR-BARTs可在體內腫瘤快速生長、營養物質供給不足所導致的代謝應激條件下，發揮其抗凋亡的作用。在體外實驗中，我們觀察到EBV感染可保護細胞在低葡萄糖和氨基酸的培養基中不致凋亡。並且，miR-BARTs在代謝應激狀態下表達量升高。在本研究中，我們旨在研究miR-BARTs在代謝應激下的抗凋亡與促腫瘤生長中的功能。通過敲除miR-BARTs的啟動子及後續的逐一過表達miR-BARTs，可研究miR-BARTs的生理學靶點。我們已報導了通過CRISPR技術編輯EBV基因組，並沉默所有miR-BARTs的可行性。我們實驗室也建立了一個新的鼻咽癌細胞株，HKU43，並已對其基因背景進行全面研究。 HKU43可作為一株新的EBV陽性的鼻咽癌細胞，與C666-1一起被用於鼻咽癌研究領域。在EBV感染的細胞中，我們也將研究miR-BARTs是否對LMP1有調節作用。我們也將發展體外活細胞成像以及體內的活體成像系統，來闡釋BART啟動子在代謝應激情況下的活化機制。我們相信通過全面研究miR-BARTs的功能，可增強我們對於EBV致癌特性的了解，並有助於開發對鼻咽癌更有效的治療方案。

17111516.label: Realisation of objectives
17111516.value: Aim 1: To investigate the roles of miR-BARTs in EBV-infected cells under metabolic stress in vitro and in vivo. The detection of clonal Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) genomes in all cases of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and the continued expression of viral gene products suggest that EBV contributes to the neoplastic transformation of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells and malignant growth in vivo. In NPC, miR-BARTs are abundantly expressed and can constitute up to 60% of the total miRNAs. In this project, we aim to unveil the importance of miR-BARTs in promoting in vivo tumor growth by resisting apoptosis via metabolic reprogramming. In the earlier stage of this project, we have compared the in vitro and in vivo growth of EBV-ve and EBV+ve HONE1 cell lines. In vitro, these two cell lines were shown to have comparable proliferation rates. However, when these cells were allowed to grow as in vivo subcutaneous tumors in the same nude mice (at the left and right flanks), growth of EBV+ve HONE1 cells was much faster than EBV-ve HONE1 cells. This indicates EBV infection promote in vivo growth. Later, we have established a new and representative NPC cell line (NPC43) with endogenous EBV infection. We were also able to get a subclone of NPC43 which has lost the EBV genome. This give rise to another pair of EBV+ve and EBV-ve NPC43 cell lines for understanding the roles of EBV infection in NPC pathogenesis. In vitro, EBV infection protected the cells from apoptosis if they were grown in culture medium deprived of glucose and amino acids. Moreover, the expression levels of miR-BARTs were also upregulated in this metabolically stressed condition. In vivo, the tumorigenicity of EBV+ve NPC43 was also much higher than the EBV-ve NPC43 cells. To further investigate the roles of miR-BARTs, we infected NPC cells (EBV-ve NPC43) and immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells (NP460) with either wild-type M81-EBV (M81/WT) or mutant M81-EBV with a deletion of genome encoding the cluster 1 & 2 of miR-BARTs and miR-Bart2 (M81/dBART). We found that NP460-M81/WT showed a general trend of higher resistance to starvation-induced cell death than NP460-M81/dBART. Besides in the spheroid cultures of the pair of NPC43-M81/WT and NPC43-M81/dBART, the WT cells could grow into bigger spheroids, reflecting they could sustain their growth under a gradient of nutrient deficiency which is present in the 3D structure of a spheroid. When examining the glucose metabolism, we found that both the glucose consumption and lactate production were much higher in the NPC43-M81/WT cells compared to the NPC43-M81/dBART. Western blotting analysis also showed the WT cells had higher expression of multiple glycolysis enzymes. Besides, we have recused the expression of miR-BARTs in NPC43-M81/dBART by transducing plasmids containing miR-BART clusters 1 & 2. A significant increase in glucose consumption, lactate production, and glycolysis-associated proteins expression could be observed in the miR-BARTs re-expressing cells. These results support a role of miR-BARTs in reprogramming glucose metabolism to promote glycolysis in EBV-infected NPC cells via enhancing the expression of glycolysis-associated proteins. Since enhanced glycolysis was shown to promote survival of cancer cell treated by chemodrugs, we then examined if miR-BARTs could repress the sensitivity of NPC cells to cytotoxic action of cisplatin, a commonly used chemotherapeutic agent in NPC. The sensitivity to cisplatin was less prominent in EBV+veNPC43 and NPC43-M81/WT cell lines than in the EBV-veNPC43 and NPC43-M81/dBART cell lines. Importantly, co-addition of glycolysis inhibitor, 2-DG, potently increased the sensitivity of EBV+veNPC43 and NPC43-M81-WT cells to the cytotoxic effect of cisplatin. The involvement of miR-BARTs in glucose metabolism and resistance to chemodrug is implicated. The enhanced sensitizing effect of 2DG was also observed in NPC43-M81-WT but not in NPC43-M81/dBART cells using colony formation assay. Taken together, our results indicated that miR-BARTs could promote glycolysis for resisting cisplatin-induced apoptosis. In vivo experiments were also performed using NPC xenografts in mice. Combined treatment of 2-DG and cisplatin could greatly suppress the tumor growth of xeno76 and xeno32 if compared to single treatment of 2-DG and cisplatin. Aim 2: To examine the in vitro and in vivo promotor activation of miR-BARTs in EBV-infected cells under metabolic stress Promoter activity is regulated by DNA methylation, which typically acts to repress gene transcription. miR-BARTs are initiated from two promoters P1 and P2. Another EBV-encoded gene, latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1) has been reported to activate cellular DNA methyltransferases, resulting in methylation of both host and EBV genomes. Interestingly, another role of miR-BARTs is to modulate the expression of LMP1, which can exert growth promoting effects but is also reported to induce apoptosis especially when being expressed in high level. Therefore, a balanced expression of miR-BARTs and LMP1 may be crucial for maintaining NPC development. In this project, we have investigated if LMP1 could affect the methylation status of the promoters of miR-Barts. We have re-infected EBV-veNPC43 with M81-EBV harboring the deletion of LMP1 (M81/dLMP1). The loss of LMP1 in this cell line (NPC43-M81/dLMP1) was confirmed by Western blot analysis. Pyrosequencing was performed in these cell lines to determine the methylation profile of a panel of EBV-encoded and host genes, including the P1 and P2 promoters, which regulate the expression of miR-BARTs. Compared to NPC43-M81/WT, a decrease in the methylation of BART P2 promoter was detected in NPC43-M81/dLMP1, indicating repression of LMP1 expression is essential for activating the transcription of miR-BARTs. Moreover, decreased in the methylation of BART promotor positively correlated with expression of miR-BARTs. Higher expression of miR-BARTs was demonstrated in the NPC43-M81/dLMP1 cells compared to the NPC43-M81/WT cells. Further, addition of demethylation agent, 5-Aza-2'-deoxycytidine (5-Aza-CdR) restored the expression of miR-BARTs, indicating the expression of miR-BARTs is controlled by methylation. Importantly, re-expression of LMP1 in the NPC43-M81/dLMP1 cells could down-regulate the expression of miR-BARTs. Apart from methylation, the BART promotors can also be regulated by cellular proteins. IRF7, c-Myc and C/EBP- β and NF-kB subunits (p50 and p65) have been reported to activate BART promoters. 3D growth conditions, in which different layers of cells are exposing to variable levels of nutrients and metabolic conditions, may contribute to the regulation of miR-BARTs. miR-BARTs showed consistent up-regulations from the NPC43 spheroid samples than the monolayer cells. We have also monitored the in vivo growth of NPC43-M81/WT and NPC43-M81/dBART. The tumorigenicity of NPC43-M81/dBART is around 3-folds lower than that of NPC43- M81/WT. To understand the promoter activity of miR-BARTs under metabolic stress in vivo, we have tried to clone the sequence which encompasses both the P1 and P2 BART promotors into a fluorescent reporter. However, intravital imaging showed that the fluorescent signals are intrinsically heterogenous within a tumor. Therefore, we decided to use single-cell sequencing to study the involvement of miR-BARTs in affecting the RNA profiles of metabolism-related genes. Indeed, this experiment was done in humanized mice. Engraftment of CD34+ human hematopoietic stem cells from fetal cord blood into the marrow of sub-lethally irradiated NSG mice enables the development of a functional human immune system in mice. NPC43-M81/WT and NPC43-M81/dBART were subcutaneously transplanted into two humanized mice. Single-cell RNA-seq was performed using ultra-high-throughput droplet-based system (10x genomics platform). Transcriptome analysis tools were used to catalogue the differentially expressed genes, metabolic signaling, proliferative and apoptotic pathways among the tumor or stromal cells, and to deduce their association with EBV genes or miR-BARTs.

17111516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111516.value: To demonstrate the association of EBV infection in regulating metabolic or apoptotic responses and their contribution to NPC pathogenesis, we have done RNA-sequencing to profile the differentiated gene expression among the EBV-infected and non-infected nasopharyngeal cell lines. Using gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), genes involved in glycolysis and pyruvate metabolism were statistically enriched in EBV-infected cells, supporting a role of EBV infection in metabolic reprogramming. Research Output 1 (Zhang J et al, Oncogene, 2019) reported the EBV infection induces the addiction of glycolysis in nasopharyngeal cells. To further understand the roles of miR-BARTs and the interactive role of LMP1 in managing metabolic stress and apoptosis, we have established EBV-veNPC43 cell line re-infected with EBV-M81 wild-type (M81/WT) and mutants with deleted regions encoding for miR-BARTs and LMP1 (M81/dBART & M81/dLMP1). The background and establishment of these cell lines can be found in Research Output 2 & 3 (manuscript attached; Lin W et al, Nature communications, 2019). Interestingly, the promoters regulating the expression of miR-BARTs were shown to be methylated more in NPC43-M81/WT than NPC43/dLMP1, indicating the LMP1 may suppress the expression of miR-BARTs by promotor methylation (Research Output 2). Furthermore, the glycolysis status of NPC cell lines with or without EBV infection, and with or without miR-BART expression was reported in Research Output 4 (manuscript attached). It demonstrates that miR-BARTs promote glycolysis of NPC43 cells with an upregulation of extracellular acidification ratio (ECAR) and oxygen consumption ratio OCR. This manuscript will also report the impact of miR-BARTs in resisting chemodrug-induced apoptosis by enhanced glycolysis in NPC cells. The roles of EBV viral genes and miR-BARTs in metabolic reprogramming has been reviewed in Research Output 5 & 6 (Zhang J et al, Adv Exp Med Biol, 2018; Tsao SW et al, Phil Trans B, 2017). In this project, we have tried to develop way to assess the expressions of miR-BARTs at a single-cell level in in vivo tumor, so as to associate their expression profiles according to metabolic signalings which can assembles to those in human patient. Therefore, we have developed single-cell RNA sequencing of EBV-positive and EBV-negative tumors in humanized mice. All these are included in Research Output 7 (manuscript attached). The interplay of EBV-infected cells with the tumor microenvironment in the pathogenesis of NPC has been reviewed and published in Research Output 8 (Huang SCM et al, Cancers, 2018). The continuous investigation in understanding the pathogenic roles of EBV and its encoded viral genes may provide direct and indirect druggable targets for effective NPC therapies. Focused preclinical and clinical investigations on these new directions will insight for novel strategies to further improve survival of NPC patients (Research Output 9 – 11: Tsang CM et al, Semin Cancer Biol, 2020; Xue Z et al, J Exp Clin Cancer Res, 2020; Hau et al, Front Oncol, 2020).

17111516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111516.value: In NPC, the EBV-encoded proteins or genes are involved in balancing cell metabolisms to meet requirement of cell growth and to control nutrient assimilation. Particularly in a solid tumor, nutrient deprivation is a challenge for survival of the cancer cells. Recent publication has shown nutrient deficiency may lead to enhanced glycolysis for driving cancer cells to produce ATP. This also contributes to protect cells from apoptosis upon nutrient deprivation. In future, we can investigate more on the mechanistic roles of miR-BARTs in metabolic reprogramming when facing the changes of nutrient levels or microenvironment during the carcinogenesis. It will open another avenue to provide some novel therapeutic alternatives to traditional cancer treatments.

17111516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111516.value: NPC is a distinctive histological subtype of head and neck cancer arising from the nasopharynx. Its undifferentiated subtype is always associated with EBV infection. The persistence of the viral episome within the tumors therefore implies that the virus must be contributing to the growth and/or survival of the tumors. In this project, we have established new NPC cell lines infected with M81-EBV WT, dBARTs and dLMP1. All these are valuable cell systems for understanding the roles of EBV in NPC pathogenesis. In this project, we have shown that EBV infection induces glycolytic addiction in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. In EBV-infected cells, miR-BARTs could upregulate glycolysis enzymes and downregulate oxidative phosphorylation enzymes. An enhanced glycolysis phenotype was also observed in miR-BARTs-expressing cells than the knockout cells by comparing their extracellular acidification ratio (ECAR) and oxygen consumption ratio (OCR). This metabolic reprogramming also contributes to the resistance of cisplatin-induced apoptosis in EBV-positive NPC cells. We have also explored the potential factors which can transcriptionally activate the expression of miR-BARTs. Both 3D spheroidal and in vivo tumor growth conditions, could upregulate the expression of miR-BARTs. Moreover, the promoters of miR-BARTs were also regulated by LMP1-mediated methylation. Defining the interactive roles of miR-BARTs and other viral genes against metabolic stress may provide new insights into the role of EBV in NPC, and therefore provide effective therapeutic targets for clinical management of this disease.

17112416.label: Realisation of objectives
17112416.value: In this project, we proposed to investigate the regulatory functions of Kif7 in enteric nervous system (ENS) development by 1) elucidating how loss of Kif7 interferes ENS development to define the disease mechanism underlying enteric dysmotility of ciliopathy patients; 2) delineating the molecular mechanism underlies how Kif7 regulates Hedgehog signaling and ENS development to identify potential therapeutic targets; and 3) characterizing the gut motility defects of Kif7 conditional knock-out (cKO) adult mice in order to establish a model of a ciliopathy associated gut motility disorder for future therapeutic interventions. We have addressed all these objectives and following is the summary of our key findings: KIF7 encodes a cilia-associated protein and is causally associated with various ciliopathies. Kif7 is also a key regulatory of Hedgehog pathway, it can positively or negatively regulate Hedgehog signalling in different cellular contexts. In this study, we generated a neural crest (NC) specific Kif7 knockout (Kif7 cKO) mouse mutant to elucidate how the development of ENS is affected when Hedgehog signalling is interrupted. (1) Most of Kif7 cKO could survive and exhibited gastrointestinal motility defect with remarkable reduction in number of late-born neurons. (2) We showed that Kif7 serves as a negative regulator of Hedgehog pathway in enteric NC cells (ENCCs). Deletion of Kif7 led to up-regulation of Gli activator and interfered the neurogenic versus gliogenic lineage differentiation of ENCCs. Through analysing the single cell transcriptomes of control and mutant ENCCs, we further (3) identified the core gene set that mediates the neurogenic-to-gliogenic switch of ENCC; and (4) defined Ezh2 as the master regulator underlying these cellular processes. (5) We also defined how the dual regulatory roles of Ezh2 contribute to the neurogenic and gliogenic lineage differentiation of ENCCs. To our knowledge, our data represent to date the best mechanistic understanding of the interactions between EZH2 and Hedgehog signalling. (6) Using human pluripotent stem cell-based model, we also showed that EZH2-mediated core gene regulatory network underlying ENCC development is largely conserved among human and mouse. Given Kif7 mouse mutants display ciliopathy and ENS -associated phenotypes, KIF7/Hedgehog signalling may represent one of the primary causes underlying ciliopathies and gastrointestinal motility disorders. Perturbation of Hedgehog signalling represents a common pathogenic mechanism underlying various congenital disorders. Our findings suggest that ciliopathy patients harboring mutations in Hedgehog pathway genes are genetically more likely to suffer from gastrointestinal disorders of different clinical severity, ranging from intestinal aganglionosis (Hirschsprung disease) to chronic constipation (chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction or enteric dysmotility). This information would be useful for guiding the clinical management for patients with various congenital diseases. A manuscript entitled “Ciliary protein Kif7 regulates Gli and Ezh2 for neurogenic-to-gliogenic switch of enteric neural crest cells during development” is currently under review by Science Advances. The manuscript is attached in this report.

17112416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112416.value: Summary of the key findings: Gastrointestinal motility disorders occur frequently in ciliopathy patients, but the underlying genetic link is unclear. A ciliary protein Kif7 can positively or negatively regulate Hedgehog signaling in different cellular contexts. Mice with neural crest cell (NCC)-specific Kif7 deficiency show a remarkable reduction of enteric neuron-to-glia ratio. Malformation of enteric nervous system (ENS) causes growth retardation and gut motility defect in mice. Mechanistically, Kif7 inhibits Gli2 in enteric NCCs (ENCCs), where Gli2 positively regulates the expression of Ezh2 via inhibiting the miR124 mediated-suppression. In developing ENCCs, Ezh2 is a master regulator of 102 core genes underlying the neurogenic-to-gliogenic switch. Deletion of Gli2 or inhibition of Ezh2 favors the neurogenic lineage differentiation of mouse and human ENCCs and rescues the ENS defects of Kif7 mutants. In sum, Hedgehog signal, via Kif7-Gli-Ezh2, controls the timely expressions of the core genes to mediate the neurogenic-to-gliogenic fate switch of ENCCs. 17112616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112616.value: Understanding the process of speciation and the patterns arising from the sequence of past divergence events lies at the core of evolutionary biology. The proposed research aims to elucidate the role of key evolutionary innovations and biogeographical founder events as potential drivers of speciation, using evolutionary tree reconstructions to pin-point the occurrence of such phenomena, and applying comparative phylogenetic methods to find and test correlations between accelerated evolutionary diversification in lineages with putative key evolutionary innovations and biogeographical founder events. The research will focus on Meiogyne, a genus of c. 30 species of trees belonging to the Annonaceae, an early-divergent family of flowering plants. Robust knowledge of early-divergent evolutionary lineages provides a key foundation for understanding the patterns and processes involved in subsequent evolutionary diversification, and the Annonaceae is consequently of considerable importance in systematic and evolutionary research. Meiogyne is an ideal candidate for such studies, with compelling evidence for floral specialisation in response to pollination system and fruit specialisation in response to different frugivores, and evidence for evolutionary shifts in both pollination and seed dispersal mechanism. There is therefore great potential for identifying key evolutionary innovations. Meiogyne is also an ideal candidate for the proposed research as it shows evidence of contrasting evolutionary processes, with speciation in western Southeast Asia likely to have been driven by long-term palaeoclimatic changes that created or removed barriers to dispersal and gene flow (vicariance allopatry), whereas speciation in Australasia appears to have been driven by founder events involving the dispersal of small genetic subsets of the source population across barriers. The latter speciation process (peripatry) is hypothesized to have accelerated diversification rate because of the availability of previously unavailable resources and lack of competition in the newly occupied geographical regions. The proposed research will apply several recently developed analytical approaches to assess the importance of possible key evolutionary innovations and founder events by identifying correlations with changes in speciation and diversification rates. Australasian Meiogyne lineages furthermore show evidence of parapatric speciation, driven by divergent selection with regard to different precipitation zones in Australia and different edaphic conditions in New Caledonia. The proposed research aims to develop ecological niche models for extant Meiogyne species based on their climatic and edaphic tolerances and hence to reconstruct the most likely niche models for ancestral nodes in the phylogeny, thereby enabling the identification of possible evolutionary shifts in ecological preferences. 理解種化過程及其演化歷史衍生出的模式是演化生物學研究的核心議題。本項研究計畫透過重構鹿茸木屬的演化樹，鎖定進化創新結構和奠基者事件在演化過程中發生的位置，以及評估相關進化多樣化的速度改變，並闡清兩者在種化的潛在角色。本研究將以鹿茸木屬為研究物件。該類群是原始被子植物番荔枝科下的一個屬，多為喬木或小喬木，共有約30種。對原始被子植物類群的深入瞭解能為後續的進化研究打下基石。因此，番荔枝科在被子植物的系統發生學及演化生物學研究中有著重要的地位。 鹿茸木屬擁有幾項特點，令它成為這類研究的理想物件。有證據顯示該屬植物的花部和果實形態特化以適應不同的傳粉及種子傳播機制，然而屬下不同類群的傳粉及種子傳播機制亦顯示進化轉變。因此，有很大潛在可能可以在鹿茸木屬中辨認出進化創新結構。除此以外，該屬的進化歷史可能涉及不同的種化過程。在東南亞西部，長期的古氣候變動持續改變水平線高度，因而重複聯合及分隔地域，有助種群散播以及阻隔基因流動，繼而推動異域種化。然而，對於澳大拉西亞的鹿茸木屬譜系，奠基者事件似乎是推動種化的一個重要基制。後者涉及一少部分的個體從母種群越過屏障，擴散到新生境的過程。推測這類的種化機制（邊域種化）有助加速進化多樣化，因為子種群能在新的領域獲得以前無法獲得的資源及擺脫以往的競爭。本項研究計畫將利用近年發展出的分析方法，評估進化創新結構和奠基者事件的重要性及其與種化和進化速率變化的關聯。 此外，亦有證據指出臨域種化推動澳大拉西亞的鹿茸木屬譜系的演化。澳洲地域上的雨量差別以及新赫里多尼亞的土壤異質性有可能對此譜系施加強力的分化選擇壓力。此計畫將基於現存鹿茸木物種對氣候和土壤的容忍度，發展生態位元模型，繼而重塑譜系中祖先節點的生態位元模型，藉此鑒定出由於生態位偏好所導致的進化轉變。

17112616.label: Realisation of objectives
17112616.value: The objectives of this research can be broadly classified into three areas: (1) taxonomy and phylogenetics; (2) historical biogeography; and (3) reproductive biology. The latter two areas are considerably more important than the first, although a clear understanding of taxonomic delimitations and a robust molecular phylogeny are both essential foundations for the research. All three areas have been tackled and were largely successful, although as with all scientific research some of the original research ideas proved to be less valuable and were replaced by novel ideas based on our new data. Progress during the latter half of this research project has been hampered by two major events that were beyond our control: wildfires in Australia that postponed fieldwork and necessitated changes to target species and field site selection; and the COVID pandemic which again constrained fieldwork in Australia, but which also reduced opportunities for us to present our results in academic conferences. These events necessitated a delay in the submission of the PhD thesis funded by this grant, although the thesis is now almost completed and will be submitted to The University of Hong Kong by the end of August 2021. As highlighted in our earlier progress report, we have clarified several taxonomic problems in the genus (Objective 1). We have confirmed the taxonomic synonymy of the generic names Oncodostigma and Meiogyne (resulting in the transfer of O. microflorum to Meiogyne in Xue et al., 2017). We have also validated several new species from Thailand (Johnson et al., 2019) and follow-up work in collaboration with others will result in additional new species descriptions. We have also contributed to the on-going Flora of Thailand project (Johnson et al., in press). We have generated a robust phylogeny (Objective 2) that has enabled the identification of several taxonomic problems, including the exclusion of Meiogyne papuana from the genus (requiring transfer to Monoon), and the non-monophyly of Meiogyne cylindrocarpa (requiring resurrection of the name Meiogyne wilsonii). Our molecular phylogeny has also served as a solid foundation for our biogeographical research (Objectives 4, 5 & 6). We undertook a trait-dependent study of Meiogyne to evaluate the role of fruit morphology on long-distance dispersal (LDD). Although LDD is a rare stochastic process, some functional traits are likely to increase chances for LDD. Our findings supported an Indomalayan origin of Meiogyne and identify two traits that are associated with dispersal by birds. This research has been written up as a thesis chapter, and will soon be submitted to the Journal of Biogeography. We also used our phylogeny to assess the impact of sea-level fluctuations on diversification rate and its implication on macroevolutionary dispersal in Meiogyne. We found a negative correlation between sea-level fluctuation and diversification tempo. Furthermore, the best-fitting time-stratified biogeographical models suggest that sea-level fluctuation reduces macroevolutionary dispersal of Meiogyne in the Australasian-Pacific region, providing a possible explanation for negative sea level-diversification dependency. Again, the thesis chapter is completed and will be submitted for publication in a journal such as Frontiers in Plant Science. Our research into the reproductive biology of Meiogyne (Objective 3) has proved to be particularly fruitful, giving rise to three thesis chapters (to be submitted for publication as separate articles). We have identified an unusual tripartite pollination system in Meiogyne hainanensis involving a mutualistic filamentous fungus. Plant-pollinator relationships are sometimes enhanced by fungi that can promote pollinator attraction and reward quality. Meiogyne hainanensis flowers are pollinated by staphylinid beetles and have a corrugated adaxial surface on the three inner petals that serves as a brood-site reward for the beetles, with the larvae feeding on fungal mycelia growing on the corrugations. DNA meta-barcoding allowed the characterization of the fungal community on the petals and the larval gut, suggesting the mycophagous nature of the larvae. This research will be submitted for publication in a journal such as American Journal of Botany. We have also identified evidence for signal advergence in a mushroom-mimicking species, Meiogyne hirsuta. The flowers are pollinated by curculionid beetles, which are attracted by a mushroom-like odour with 3-octanone as one of the major compounds. Eight-carbon ketones are known to be characteristic volatiles of mushrooms. The work will be submitted for publication in a journal such as International Journal of Plant Sciences. We also report a novel floral mimicry system in which flowers of Meiogyne heteropetala possess the visual and olfactory cues that adverge to the surrounding aerial leaf litter to attract the erotylid beetle Loberus sharpi. The flowers emit a blend of monoterpenes and monoterpenoids dominated by 1,8-cineole. We used floral transcriptomics to identify the monoterpene synthase MhTPS-3 as a likely candidate responsible for floral scent biosynthesis, as it had much higher expression in flowers revealed by RT-qPCR. Characterization of MhTPS-3 demonstrated that the monoterpene synthase converts the universal substrate geranyl pyrophosphate into 1,8-cineole as the major product. Bioassay is needed to determine whether the products of MhTPS-3 alone can sufficiently attract pollinators and whether imperfectly mimicry olfactory signal has any functional significance in pollinator attraction. We aim to publish this work in a leading journal such as New Phytologist.

17112616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112616.value: As noted in Section 5.3 of this report, the objectives of this research can be broadly classified into three areas: (1) taxonomy and phylogenetics; (2) historical biogeography; and (3) reproductive biology. The taxonomic research was largely undertaken as a foundation for the phylogenetics, historical biogeography and reproductive biology: the major outcome from the taxonomic research has been the clarification of several outstanding problems, new species descriptions, and contributions to on-going international floristic projects. We have integrated our molecular phylogenetic results into the historical biogeographical research. This work has largely focused on assessments of specific traits (especially fruit traits that influence seed dispersal mechanisms) and the impact of this on transoceanic long-distance dispersal in Meiogyne. We have therefore advanced our understanding of how traits can affect the long-distance dispersal of island taxa, and the conclusions are of significance for many plant lineages that disperse across maritime barriers. We have also investigated the impact of sea-level fluctuations on evolutionary diversification rate and its role in macroevolutionary dispersal. Our work sheds light on diversification and dispersal patterns for other island lineages whose diversification and dispersal patterns are likely highly susceptible to sea-level changes. Our research into the pollination ecology of Meiogyne species has focused on species mutualisms and mimicry. Although three-way mutualisms are not new to science, our discovery of a plant-beetle-fungus mutualism is new for the family Annonaceae and opens up new research directions: there are several other Annonaceae species that have characteristics of adaptations for the possible cultivation of fungal mycelia, albeit in different ways. Our study of mushroom mimicry in Meiogyne significantly advances our understanding for pollination in the Annonaceae and mushroom mimicry in general. We have refined our previous application of floral scent analysis to investigate advergence with surrounding aerial leaf litter and its role in attracting pollinating beetles. Aerial leaf litter provides an important yet often neglected microhabitat for fungi and arthropods in rainforests. The current study is the first report on a floral mimicry system exploiting the interactions between insects and this resource.

17112616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112616.value: A previous family-wide study of the Annonaceae identified multiple ancient floristic exchange events, although many smaller-scale transoceanic dispersal events were probably overlooked owing to inadequate taxon sampling. We identified a diminishing effect of sea-level fluctuation on Meiogyne diversification and transoceanic dispersal. It would be promising to confirm whether ancient sea-level fluctuation would have a similar effect on diversification and dispersal patterns in other taxa. We also reported the role of the perianth as a brood site for pollinators, where the larvae feed on fungal hyphae that grow on the corrugated perianth substrate. Petal corrugations have evolved independently multiple times in the family, and the role of the corrugation as a substrate for mutualistic fungus might extend to these genera. Reports of general brood-site pollination in Annonaceae is surprisingly rare, although the flowers often serves as a mating and tryst site for beetle pollinators and petals are often fleshy or bear food bodies. The small beetle larvae and petal abscission after anthesis might have created a bias leading to an underestimation of the prevalence brood-site pollination. In addition, since such systems can potentially locally amplify pollinator populations, it might promote founder population establishment and thus spur transoceanic dispersal and diversification.

17112616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112616.value: Understanding the process of speciation and the patterns arising from the sequence of past divergence events lies at the core of evolutionary biology research. Our research elucidates the role of key evolutionary innovations and biogeographical events as potential drivers of speciation in the flowering plant genus Meiogyne (Annonaceae). Meiogyne is an ideal candidate for such studies as there is compelling evidence for floral specialisation in response to pollination system and fruit specialisation in response to different frugivores. We reconstructed a robust molecular phylogeny for the genus, which we used to resolve several outstanding taxonomic problems as well as the basis for biogeographical and reproductive biology investigations. We studied specific fruit traits that potentially enhance successful long-distance dispersal over marine divides. Our findings supported an Indomalayan origin of Meiogyne and two traits that promote dispersal by birds. We also assessed the impact of sea-level fluctuations on diversification rate and its implication for macroevolutionary dispersal in Meiogyne. We found a negative correlation between sea-level fluctuation and diversification tempo. The best-fitting time-stratified biogeographical models furthermore suggests that sea-level fluctuation reduces macroevolutionary dispersal in the Australasian-Pacific region, providing a possible explanation for negative sea level-diversification dependency.

17113116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113116.value: Met受體酪氨酸激酶可以激發活一系列生理性信號通路。然而Met自身的激活則常見於癌症，因此Met也成為了有前景的治療靶點。最新證據表明核Met（nMet）在癌症組織及在癌細胞系中表達，提示nMet在細胞核里有不為人知的功能。這對目前針對Met表面受體的治療方式提出了挑戰。我們之前的研究第一次證明了nMet在人類肝癌中的臨床意義。nMet過表達與肝癌靜脈侵襲及較差的預後顯著相關。相應的，nMet過表達促進了肝癌的生長和轉移。我們隨後的研究闡明了nMet驅使肝癌轉移的機制并發現了外泌體在這之中的重要性。近年來關於外泌體的研究主要集中在細胞間交流，特別是外泌體參與癌症轉移及轉移前微環境的形成。外泌體分泌具有功能性的分子傳遞至身體內特定的其他遠端組織，促使其形成適合癌細胞轉移的微環境。我們的研究表明表達nMet的肝癌細胞釋放的外泌體增加了肝癌早期細胞的轉移和侵襲能力。動物實驗顯示靜脈注射nMet-外泌體增加了肝癌得轉移的機率。經蛋白組學分析，TGF-1參與調節肝癌侵襲性。同時表達nMet的肝癌細胞顯示了比對照組細胞更高的TGF-1含量。因此我們假設表達nMet的肝癌細胞源性外泌體促使肝癌轉移及促進遠處器官轉移前微環境的形成的功能與產生TGF-1有關。在此次研究中，我們將探討nMet表達細胞源外泌體的功能及機制。我們將1）功能性的探討外泌體在肝癌細胞遷徙，侵襲及遠處轉移的作用，2）闡明TGF-1在肝癌侵襲性的作用及3）評價外泌體促使轉移前微環境建立的機制。此次的研究將會給肝癌轉移的研究提供新的看點及給與腫瘤源性外泌體對腫瘤轉移提供了新的機制。

17113116.label: Realisation of objectives
17113116.value: The project objectives as per original application has been thoroughly assessed and revised for better research improvement and outcome. Generally, the term “extracellular vesicles” (EVs) was used to replace “exosome” in whole study as suggested by the nomenclature criteria reported by the International Society of Extracellular Vesicles (ISEV). We have successfully accomplished objective 1 by characterization of the functional effect of EVs derive from nuclear Met (nMet) cells in HCC cell colony formation, migration and invasion ability. Nonetheless, we also demonstrated the effect of nMet-EVs in promoting distant metastasis in mice. For objective 2 and 3, we have revised the pre-proposed protein target TGF-beta 1. Our further study of TGF-beta 1 failed to deliver favorable outcome that warrants further investigation. In order to find the new potential candidates, we performed protein profiling using Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid mass spectrometer, which is more powerful in detecting minute protein inputs, on our EV samples. We identified a panel of proteins that belong to three family clusters that are important in catalyzing protein synthesis. We validated these candidates by quantitative PCR and immunoblotting. We performed both in vitro and in vivo functional assay to comprehensively elucidate the role of these candidates within EVs in promoting cancer metastasis. Our study has revealed the new evidences on how cancer cells utilized EVs to deliver key components that enhance cancer aggressiveness.

17113116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113116.value: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) were isolated from the conditioned medium of MHCC97L cells that express nuclear Met (nMet) by ultracentrifugation. The integrity of isolated EVs was validated by transmission electron microscopy, western blotting and nanoparticle tracking analyzer. nMet-EVs exhibited an augmented potency to promote colony formation, migration and invasion ability of naïve parental MIHA, Huh7 and PLC/PRF/5 cells when compared to vector control EVs (Vec-EVs). The effect of nMet-EVs in promoting metastasis was also observed in the in vivo experimental metastasis assay by the coinjection of EVs and murine p53-/-;Myc-transduced hepatoblasts. These findings suggest that nMet-EVs could facilitate the extravasation and colonization of tumors cells in lungs. To ascertain the differential biological activities between Vec- and nMet-EVs, we compared their proteomic profiles using mass spectrometry. We identified a panel of proteins that belong to three protein complexes, namely eukaryotic initiation factors (eIFs) that are involved in the initiation of eukaryotic translation, ribosomal protein L (RPL) and ribosomal protein S (RPS) that are responsible for the assembly of 60S and 40S subunits, respectively. Both 60S and 40S are founding subunits of eukaryotic 80S ribosome that catalyzes the synthesis of proteins. A total of 13 protein candidates that are upregulated by more than 2-fold in nMet-EVs were selected for further validation by quantitative PCR and immunoblotting. The data revealed the increased expression of these proteins in nMet cells and established the association between cellular overexpression and enrichment in the EVs. To elucidate the functional role of these protein candidates in nMet-EVs, EIF3I, EIF4G2, RPS3A, and RPL10 were selected for further study. We employed lentiviral based knock-down approach where sh-EIF3I, shEIF4G2, shRPS3A and shRPL10 clones were established in nMet cells. EVs were collected from these knock-down clones and subjected to in vitro functional study. The effect of these EVs on colony formation, migration and invasion was diminished when compared to control nMet-EVs. In vivo experimental metastasis model also provided similar evidence. To investigate whether nMet expressing cells could evade from the effect of rapamycin, which actions on mTOR signaling pathway that regulate protein synthesis, naïve PLC cells were co-treated with rapamycin and nMet-EVs. Such combination treatment could rescue the expression of c-Myc protein, where it is normally suppressed by the effect of rapamycin. However, co-treatment of rapamycin with EVs of knock-down clones failed to rescue the c-Myc expression, suggesting those proteins within nMet-EVs are involved in protein translation that are important in driving cancer aggressiveness.

17113116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113116.value: Our data has revealed nuclear Met (nMet) expressing cells secrete extracellular vesicles (EVs) enriched with a panel of proteins involved in the regulation of protein translation to promote cancer aggressiveness. However, the detailed regulatory mechanism of how these proteins being packaged into EVs remained to be unanswered. Further study focuses on molecular sorting machinery and biogenesis of EVs could unravel the mechanistic basis underlying the oncogenic activities of tumor cell derived EVs. Also, our data provided new evidences on how cancer cells could evade from the effect of rapamycin, an inhibitor for mTOR signaling pathway that regulates cell growth and metabolism, through the action of EVs. Our findings provide insights into the innovative treatment leading to the blockage of EVs biogenesis or EVs activity, alone or in combination with rapamycin may serve as a therapeutic option beyond the current limited treatments for HCC.

17113116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113116.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for most primary liver cancers. World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that more than 1 million patients will die from liver cancer in 2030. Understanding the underlying mechanism of how HCC acquires cancer aggressiveness is crucial to improve the current diagnosis and treatment for HCC patients. Our previous study provided the first evidence about the presence of truncated Met receptor, a well-known oncogene that was frequently deregulated in many types of cancer, in the nucleus of HCC which has profound prognostic value. These observations have led to current study in which we demonstrated that extracellular vesicles (EVs), in nanometer-sized, released by nuclear Met expressing cells, promote cancer metastasis. Within these oncogenic vesicles, we identified a panel of proteins belong to the same family cluster that are mainly involved in protein translation and functioning as the potent modulators of cancer aggressiveness. By reducing the expression of these protein targets in the EVs, cancer metastasis was profoundly attenuated in mice. The outcome of study suggests an unreported underlying mechanism that involves nuclear Met for the enhancement of cancer metastasis and provides important insights into the development of therapeutic strategies against aberrant Met in human cancers.

17113416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113416.value: 糖尿病患者數量將從2013年3.82億猛增到2035年5.92億人[1]。僅2013年因糖尿病所造成的負擔達5480億美元，占所有健康總支出的11%[1]。其中在發展中國家中有69%的糖尿病患者未被診斷，而發達國家爲20%[1,2]。糖尿病患者中超過三分之一（36%）來自于中國和印度[3]。糖尿病腎病（CKD）是糖尿病的主要幷發症之一。約20%至30%的糖尿病患者在患病20年內發展爲糖尿病腎病，糖尿病腎病患者占發達國家中50%的新發終末期腎病[4]。估計10年中全球因糖尿病腎病而需洗腎的費用高達1.1兆億美元[5]。 我們研究團隊早前發現炎症和纖維化是糖尿病腎病的主要發病機制[9-12]。我們前期預實驗發現latent TGF-β能抑制鏈脲佐菌素誘導的糖尿病腎病小鼠中腎臟T細胞侵潤及炎症因子升高。我們也發現latent TGF-β轉基因小鼠16周糖尿病腎病模型中GARP基因下調而Treg特徵性轉錄因子Fox3基因上調。因Treg細胞在糖尿病腎病中起到抑制炎症和纖維化的作用，我們提出假設：latent TGF-β通過調節糖尿病腎病中GARP，上調Treg 細胞的免疫而起到抗炎的作用。 本研究旨在利用鏈脲佐菌素誘導的糖尿病腎病小鼠模型，研究 latent TGF-β是否通過調節GARP，上調Treg 細胞的免疫而起到抗炎的作用。同時通過超聲微泡導入latency associated peptide (LAP)，研究LAP是否作用于GARP起到抑制炎症的作用。 本研究將可能發現latent TGF-β保護糖尿病腎病的可能機制，幷探索超聲微泡LAP基因導入防治糖尿病腎病可能的臨床應用。本研究對科學和臨床均有借鑒意義。

17113416.label: Realisation of objectives
17113416.value: In the study, we have addressed the first three objectives and revised the last objective to prove the therapeutic potentials for latent TGF-β1 and LAP. Objective 1. To determine whether latent TGF-β protects against renal inflammation in STZ-induced DKD in latent TGF-β Tg mice. The protective role of latent TGF-β was assessed by the renal function and renal inflammation in STZ-induced Tg and Wt mice. The pathological stainings indicated that mice overexpressing latent TGF-β1 (Tg) were protected against the development of mesangial matrix expansion and thickening of the glomerular basement membrane as seen in the diabetic kidneys of WT mice. Similarly, the development of urinary microalbumin in the diabetic WT mice was also significantly inhibited in Tg mice. However, latent TGF-β1 did not alter the levels of blood glucose, indicating that latent TGF-1 may protect against diabetic kidney disease (DKD) locally without influencing the blood glucose. The levels of plasma latent TGF-β1 in both normal Tg and diabetic Tg mice were significantly higher compared to the WT mice, but the levels of active TGF-β1 had no significant difference between Tg and WT mice. In the kidneys, the levels of latent TGF-β1 in normal and diabetic mice are higher than the WT mice, while the level of active TGF-β1 was higher in diabetic WT mice compared to the diabetic Tg mice. The finding consistently indicated that latent TGF-1 may protect against DKD locally. We next examined whether overexpression of latent TGF-1 inhibits renal fibrosis and inflammation by suppressing the TGF-β/Smad and NF-κB signaling. We found that fibrosis markers in diabetic kidneys, were increased in WT mice but attenuated in latent TGF-β1 Tg mice. Similarly, renal inflammation including F4/80+ macrophages, CD3+ T cells and expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1 and TNF- was also increased in the diabetic kidneys of WT mice but blunted in the diabetic kidneys of Tg mice. We found that latent TGF-β protects against renal inflammation in STZ-induced DKD in latent TGF-β Tg mice. 2. To determine whether Treg cells are involved in the protective effect of latent TGF-β against renal inflammation in DKD. We first assessed T cells in diabetic kidneys of WT and Tg mice. The renal infiltration of CD3+ T cells was increased in the diabetic WT mice but significantly reduced in those latent TGF-β1 diabetic Tg mice. We measured the proportions of CD4+ T cell subpopulations, including Tregs, Th1 and Th17 in the spleen, kidney and peripheral blood in diabetic WT and Tg mice. Notably, diabetic Tg mice had a reduced proportion of CD4+IFNγ+ Th1 cells and CD4+IL17A+ Th17 cells compared to diabetic WT mice. However, in comparison to diabetic WT mice, the diabetic Tg mice had a significant increase of CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ Tregs in the spleen, kidney and peripheral blood. Notably, the ratios of Th1/Treg and Th17/Treg in diabetic Tg mice were significantly reduced when compared with those diabetic WT mice, suggesting that latent TGF-β1 is critically involved in immune tolerance during DKD development. To further elucidate the role of latent TGF-β1 on Tregs in diabetic mice, using an anti-CD25 neutralizing antibody, Tregs in diabetic Tg mice were kept at levels similar to those at a steady state. Reduced CD25+Foxp3+ Tregs in peripheral blood, spleen and kidney were validated by flow cytometric analyses. Notably, blockade of Tregs in diabetic Tg mice completely abolished renoprotective effects, showing enhanced, but did not affect blood glucose. Latent TGF-β1 significantly attenuated T cell infiltration and suppressed cytokines (TNF-α and IL-1β) in diabetic Tg mice compared to the diabetic WT mice. However, latent TGF-β1-mediated immunomodulation was completely abolished upon anti-CD25 antibody treatment. Simultaneously, the depletion of Tregs restored the decreased Th1 and Th17 cells in diabetic Tg mice, indicating that latent TGF-β1 might directly act on Tregs, which, in turn, led to the suppression of Th1 and Th17 cells. 3. To determine whether GARP-latent TGF-β-mediated activation of Treg cells is the key mechanism in the protective effect of latent TGF-β against renal inflammation in DKD. GARP is known as the receptor of latent TGF-β1 and is expressed by Tregs. Interestingly, we detected a significantly increased proportion of GARP+ Tregs in diabetic Tg mice. The CD4+CD25+ Tregs from the spleen were sorting-purified and analyzed by western blot. Results showed that latent TGF-β1 significantly up-regulated the expression of GARP in Tregs. The expression of GARP on Treg cells was also confirmed by the colocalization analysis in confocal microscopy. To determine whether the increase of GARP+ population in Tregs was attributed to exogenous latent TGF-β1, splenic CD4+ T cells from diabetic WT mice were sorting-purified and treated with recombinant human latent TGF-β1 protein. Consistently, flow cytometry analysis suggested significantly increased the proportion of CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ Tregs and their GARP expression upon recombinant human latent TGF-β1 protein treatment. Next, we assessed the role of latent TGF-β1 in Tregs differentiation by knocking down the GARP. Latent TGF-β1 up-regulated the Tregs (CD4+CD25+Foxp+) proportion, but the knockdown of GARP significantly blocked the increased proportion of Tregs mediated by latent TGF-β1, indicating latent TGF-β1 activates Tregs through the GARP pathway. We also assessed the productions of IL-10 and CTLA-4, the immunosuppressive mediators in Treg cells from naïve controls, which were significantly increased upon the treatment of recombinant latent TGF-β1 protein in vitro. Consistently, IL-10 and CTLA-4 production by Tregs were also significantly increased in diabetic Tg mice compared with those in diabetic WT mice. Moreover, we performed a functional assay by co-culturing Tregs with naïve CD4+ T cells upon TCR activation. Compared with Tregs in diabetic WT mice, Tregs in diabetic Tg mice had a stronger potency in suppressing the proliferative expansion of effector T cells, indicating that latent TGF-β1 plays a critical role in maintaining the regulatory functions of Tregs upon DKD induction. 4. To determine whether overexpression of LAP in spleen using non-invasive ultrasound-microbubble gene delivery is able to prevent DKD in STZ-induced mice. In the aimed study, we are unable to overexpression of LAP in spleen using non-invasive ultrasound-microbubble gene delivery. Alternatively recombinant latent TGF-β1 protein were administrated into STZ-induced DKD mice by the intraperitoneal injection. So the objective was changed to “To determine whether recombinant latent TGF-β1 is able to prevent DKD in STZ-induced mice.” We found that the recombinant latent TGF-β1 reduced the microalbuminuria and T cell infiltration in kidneys but not affected blood glucose in 16-week diabetic mice. The analysis of PAS staining also revealed that the treatment of latent TGF-β1 attenuated glomerulosclerosis and tubulointerstitial fibrosis in STZ-induced diabetic kidney disease. As expected, phenotypic analyses suggested that latent TGF-β1 treatment also restored the Th1/Tregs and Th17/Tregs ratios in the periphery. Consistently, western blot analysis also showed reduced inflammatory cytokine TNF-α and IL-1β secretion in STZ induced diabetic kidneys in response to latent TGF-β1 treatment. Thus, latent TGF-β1 may be a novel therapeutic approach for diabetic kidney disease. 5. To determine how latent TGF-β1 prevents renal fibrosis in DKD. In our study, we found latent TGF-β1 not only suppresses renal inflammation but also reduces renal fibrosis in DKD. In the study, we also found another mechanism in which latent TGF-β1 attenuates TGF-β1/Smad3-mediated renal fibrosis and NF-κB-driven renal inflammation in the diabetic kidney through inhibiting Arkadia-mediated Smad7 ubiquitin degradation.

17113416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113416.value: Recent studies indicate latent TGF-β1/GARP complex involves in the activation of Tregs. In the present study, we determined whether latent TGF-β1 could protect against DKD through the latent TGF-β1/GARP complex-mediated Treg activation. Interestingly, we found that T cells infiltration and the proportion of inflammatory Th1/Th17 cells were largely reduced in diabetic Tg mice, accompanied by the increased proportion of Tregs and GARP expression on Tregs. Mechanistically, overexpressing latent TGF-β1 induces Tregs activation through latent TGF-β1/GARP pathway and autocrine active TGF-β1-mediated Treg differentiation. Both pathways restored the impaired immunosuppressive function of Tregs in diabetic mice by releasing immunosuppressive mediators, IL-10 and CTLA-4. Finally, the recombinant human latent TGF-β1 protein treatment protected against diabetic kidney injury in mice, indicating the therapeutic potential for DKD patients. The findings have been submitted to the journal. We also found latent TGF-β1 attenuates renal fibrosis on DKD by the inactivation of both TGF-β/Smad and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling pathways. These protective effects were associated with the prevention of renal Smad7 from the Arkadia-induced ubiquitin proteasomal degradation in the diabetic kidney, suggesting protection of renal Smad7 from Arkadia-mediated degradation may be a key mechanism through which latent TGF-β1 inhibits DKD. This was further confirmed in vitro in mesangial cells that knockdown of Arkadia failed but overexpression of Arkadia reversed the protective effects of latent TGF-β1 on high glucose-treated mesangial cells. Latent TGF-β1 may protect kidneys from TGF-β1/Smad3-mediated renal fibrosis and NF-κB-driven renal inflammation in diabetes through inhibiting Arkadia-mediated Smad7 ubiquitin degradation. The findings have been published in the International Journal of Biological Sciences. In conclusion, latent TGF-β1 protects against DKD via multiple mechanisms locally and systemically. Systemically, latent TGF-β1/GARP mediated activation of Tregs restores the impaired immunosuppressive function of Tregs, inhibiting the inflammation. In the local kidney, latent TGF-β1 inhibits Arkadia-mediated Smad7 ubiquitin degradation; in turn, Smad7 suppresses the activation of TGF-β1/Smad3 and NF-κB pathways.

17113416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113416.value: (1) Macrophages may also contribute to inflammation and fibrosis of DKD. Our pilot study also found that the latent TGF-β prevented macrophage infiltration. We will also study whether latent TGF-β1 could regulate macrophage differentiation in DKD. (2) The research platform could be employed to screen the effects and mechanisms of Chinese medicinal herbs for DKD. For example, Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BHD) is commonly used for DKD, but the molecular mechanism remains largely unclear. Using the research platform, we found that BHD attenuated renal inflammation and fibrosis in STZ-induced diabetic kidney disease via inhibiting the TGF-β1/Smad3 and NF-κB signaling pathway while suppressing the Arkadia and restoring renal Smad7. Notably, calycosin-7-glucoside (CG), one of the compounds in BHD, significantly inhibited the high glucose-induced cell inflammation and fibrosis by regulating TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling, suggesting that CG could be a promising therapeutic drug for DKD.

17113416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113416.value: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), the common complication in diabetes patients, is characterized by chronic renal inflammation and fibrosis. As no regimens can completely stop the pathological progress of DKD, most patients eventually develop into end-stage renal disease in decades. Latent transforming growth factor (TGF)-β1 has been reported to protect against obstructive kidney disease and crescentic glomerulonephritis. In the study, we find that latent TGF-β1 protects against DKD via multiple mechanisms locally and systemically. Latent TGF-β1 inhibits Arkadia-mediated Smad7 ubiquitin degradation; in turn, Smad7 suppresses the activation of TGF-β1/Smad3 and NF-κB pathways. Systemically, latent TGF-β1/GARP mediated activation of Tregs restores the impaired immunosuppressive function of Tregs, inhibiting the inflammation. The findings from the project uncover the underlying mechanism of the protective role of latent TGF-β in DKD, which will help us to develop and screen drugs or Chinese herbs as the clinical treatment for DKD. The outcome of the research project will be highly significant both scientifically and clinically.

17113816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17113816.value: Kif5b調控間充質干細胞的粒體轉移用於挽救線粒體病引起的視網膜神經節細胞退化症

17113816.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17113816.value: Dr Chiu, Kin Prof HUANG, Jiandong

17113816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113816.value: Mitochondrial dysfunctions, either inherited or acquired, are tightly linked to the death of high energy-demanding retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). We have recently demonstrated that mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) could directly transfer mitochondria to injured airway epithelial cells and protect against smoke-induced lung failure. While investigating the molecular basis, we unexpectedly discovered that higher levels of the mitochondrial motor protein kinesin-1 heavy chain Kif5b in MSCs resulted in more efficient intercellular mitochondrial transfer. Based on our preliminary data, we hypothesize that manipulation of Kif5b could be used to enhance MSC-mediated intercellular mitochondrial donation and rescue mitochondrial dysfunction-mediated RGC death. To investigate the role of Kif5b in regulating the potency of MSC mitochondrial donation and in protecting against RGC death, we will focus on the following specific aims: 1. To characterize the potency of MSC mitochondria regulated by Kif5b. 2. To validate functions of mitochondrial donation via MSCs to rescue ganglion cell death in vitro. 3. To examine transplantation of engineered MSCs to protect against RGC death in a mouse model of genetic mitochondrial disorder. These proof-of-concept studies will be conducted in co-cultures of primary RGCs and Kif5b engineered MSCs, and in a mouse model of genetic mitochondrial disorder. The knowledge acquired from this study will provide evidence to improve our understanding of stem cell-mediated retinal repair. We expect these novel findings to generate a paradigm shift in the future application of stem cell therapeutics to other chronic diseases caused by mitochondrial damage.

17115116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115116.value: 該項目將開發體內分子MRI成像方法用於观察阿爾茨海默病(AD)早期的β澱粉樣蛋白(Aβ)病理。 AD影響老齡化社會, 儘管這種疾病的社會經濟代價巨大，早期診斷和有效的治療進展緩慢。一個顯著的障礙是在診斷，藥物開發和治療監測方面缺乏有效的方法。可溶性Aβ寡聚體（AβOs）和不溶性Aβ斑塊是AD腦的病理特徵。目前迫切需要發展有效和早期發現這種Aβ病理學有針對性的腦成像方法。在這個項目中，我們將開發和優化具有高靈敏度和空間分辨率檢測Aβ病理的分子MRI方法。我們的主要假設是，薑黃素共軛磁性納米顆粒（CUR-的MNP）將定標AD腦中AβOs和Aβ斑塊，並允許我們影像其分佈和變化。 AD轉基因小鼠模型表現了許多人的AD病理生理，為我們提出的分子成像方法的驗證和評估提供平台。我們有3個具體目標：（1） 開發用於在小鼠腦中的Aβ病理檢測的體內分子MRI方案：我們將實施和優化7T MRI掃描採集和分析方法。（2） 體內MRI檢測和在AD小鼠模型AβOs和Aβ斑塊的表徵：我們將驗證比較MRIAβ病理檢測的靈敏度。（3） 观察驗證这个分子MRI方案是否能夠檢測體內表徵AβOs和Aβ斑塊的減少。

17115116.label: Realisation of objectives
17115116.value: Specifically regarding the three proposed objectives, (1) we have experimentally developed and established an optimal high-resolution MRI protocol on a 7 Tesla MRI scanner for directly detecting and quantifying Aβ pathology in mouse brains in vivo. (2) We then systematically tested our hypothesis by examining the Aβ pathology in three widely used AD mouse models of different ages. Postmortem histological analysis has been performed to validate and assess the in vivo MRI results. (3) We have applied our developed 7T MRI protocols together wtih Cur-MNPs to evaluate this molecular MRI approach for its ability in monitoring Aβ pathology changes in response to a well-characterized Aβ-lowering drug. 1. Objective 1 has been 100% accomplished. We have developed high resolution and high sensitivity in vivo MRI protocol on a 7 Tesla MRI scanner. In this context, we have also innovated several MRI data acquisition and image reconstruction methods. 2. Objective 2 has been mostly accomplished. We have examined the performance of our proposed contrast agent in 3 different type of AD mouse models and obtained positive findings as expected. 3. Objective 3 has only been completed by ~60% though we have performed most of the proposed experiments in year 3. However, the quality of the experimental results is not sufficient convincing for publication because the laboratory facilities where we performed contrast agent Cur-MNPs synthesis were changed in year 3 and have suffered from quality and reproducibility problems. Note that our results have been presented in recent annual conferences of ISMRM, the leading MRI research society. Among two presentations have attracted attentions from the community, receiving the Summa Cum Laude Awards that are reserved for top 5% of all >5000 presentations. 17115116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115116.value: 1. We have designed a new curcumin-conjugated magnetic nanoparticles (Cur-MNPs) approach for direct imaging of Aβ plaques and AβOs in AD brains by MRI. Curcumin, a natural, safe product extracted from turmeric, possesses the ability to bind to Aβ species. 2. We have comprehensively characterized Cur-MNPs for their size, morphology, structure and chemistry, the results demonstrating that Cur-MNPs have a mean particle size less than 100 nm, low cytotoxicity, and BBB penetration potential. 3. Our experimental results in MRI and histological analyses indicates that Cur-MNPs can penetrate the BBB and bind to Aβ plaques in aged transgenic (Tg2576) AD mice, and that MRI can reveal Cur-MNPs targeted Aβ plaques. We have performed comprehensive MRI examinations of three groups of young and old AD mice. Our findings above directly support that Cur-MNPs can bind to AβOs in the absence of Aβ plaques, enabling detection of early Aβ pathology by MRI.

17115116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115116.value: 1. The molecular MRI of Aβ pathology early in AD progression with high sensitivity and spatial resolution present a powerful imaging tool in our pursuit of AD drug development, early diagnosis, and treatment. 2. The future study will involve expanding present evaluation to monitoring drug effects in vivo. We are pursuing new funding opportunities from other sources to continue this line of research. 3. MRI method development in Objective 1 has enabled us to develop a new research direction on how to reconstruct high quality and artefact-free images through computing and analysis.

17115116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115116.value: In this project, we have developed, optimized and evaluated a molecular MRI protocol to detect Aβ pathology early with high sensitivity and spatial resolution. Our experimental results have largely confirmed our original primary hypothesis that curcumin-conjugated magnetic nanoparticles (Cur-MNPs), via intravenous administration, can target AβOs and Aβ plaques in AD brains, and enable detailed visualization of their distributions and changes in vivo by high-resolution and quantitative MRI. The experimental results from this preclinical project have significantly advanced our ability to detect AβOs and Aβ plaques and their changes early in living brains by providing unprecedented 3D, quantitative and dynamic information to study AD progression and treatment in both transgenic mouse models and human AD patients. It presents a powerful imaging tool in our pursuit of AD drug development, early diagnosis, and treatment.
