17115916.label: Realisation of objectives
17115916.value: # How the project objectives have been achieved: 1. Preparation for realization of the objective To perform a baseline survey of this proposed study, we recruited a population-representative sample of 12-year-old children from Hong Kong in 2011. The first follow-up survey was conducted in 2014, when the participants were 15 years old. To maintain consistency and to ensure sufficient data homogeneity, the data collection time periods were limited to two months after the 12th and 15th birthdays of the participants in 2011 and 2014, respectively. The same trained and calibrated examiners conducted both examinations using the same measurement methods and criteria. The same questionnaires were issued to the participants in each survey. 2. Sample selection For the baseline surveys, the sampling frame was all local primary schools in Hong Kong (all children are required to attend primary school by law). A random sample of 52 schools (10% of all local primary schools) from 18 districts in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region was selected. The primary schools were the primary sampling unit. Within each school, all 12-year-old children were invited to participate in the survey, and 823 children were recruited at baseline in 2011. The exclusion criteria were students who were not of southern Chinese ethnicity and those who had systemic diseases or syndromes that would affect development and growth. In the first follow-up survey in 2014, 708 15-year-old adolescents were successfully surveyed, representing a dropout rate of 14.0%. All of the students who participated in our baseline survey and the first follow-up survey were invited in the second follow-up survey in 2017. Written informed consent was obtained from both the participants and their parents/primary caregivers prior to data collection in their secondary schools. 3. Data collection Clinical examinations to assess oral health (OH) status were conducted for 589 students in 54 schools. To comprehensively assess each participant’s OH status, their caries experience and periodontal condition were recorded following the recommendations of the World Health Organization (WHO) for oral health surveys. The oral health examinations were conducted by 2 trained and calibrated examiners. Intra- and inter-examiner reliability was assessed among 10% of the participants randomly selected from the study sample. Dental caries experience was recorded by counting the numbers of permanent teeth that are decayed (DT), missing due to caries (MT), and filled (FT) to generate a DMFT score. The same type of intraoral disposable mouth mirror with good operating light and a blunt probe was used throughout the study. Periodontal condition was recorded using the Community Periodontal Index (CPI). This was scored on a scale of 0 to 4 that represents a progressively deteriorating periodontal condition from healthy periodontal status to deep periodontal pockets. The dentition was divided into six sextants. One index tooth was selected from each sextant (16, 11, 26, 36, 31, and 46). The index teeth were examined with a mouth mirror mounted with LED light and a WHO CPI probe. The CPI scores were recorded as follows: CPI = 0, normal; CPI = 1, bleeding on probing and no pocket ≥3.5mm; CPI = 2, calculus present and no pocket ≥3.5mm; CPI = 3, a shallow pocket with depth of 3.5–5.5mm; and CPI = 4, a deep pocket depth ≥ 5.5mm. An approximately 20 g probing force was applied during periodontal examination. At age 12, only scores of 0, 1, and 2 were given. At age 15 and 18, all five scores were used. The highest CPI score among the six index teeth was used to indicate periodontal status of a participant. For anthropometric assessments of adiposity status, the following measurements were taken: 1. Body height (BH) - recorded to the nearest 0.001 m with a stadiometer 2. Body weight (BW) - recorded to the nearest 0.001 kg with a self-zeroing digital scale (Tanita, Japan) 3. Waist circumference (WC) - recorded to the nearest 0.1 cm with a non-stretchable tape 4. Hip circumference (HC) - recorded to the nearest 0.1 cm with a non-stretchable tape 5. Triceps skinfold thickness (TRSKF) - recorded to the nearest 0.1 mm with a skinfold calliper (Harpenden, UK) Adiposity status was assessed through the following categories: 1. General adiposity - weight-height ratio (W/H) and BMI (BW in kilograms ÷ the square of BH in meters) 2. Central adiposity - WC and waist-hip ratio (WHR) 3. Peripheral adiposity - TRSKF The same self-administered questionnaires used in the baseline and the first follow-up survey were distributed to the participants and their parents through their schools. Information on the participants’ key OH behaviours relating to diet (food frequency questionnaire), oral hygiene practices (e.g., frequency of tooth brushing and type of toothpaste), utilization of dental services, OH-related quality of life, and dental fear was collected. 4. Statistical analysis Baseline socioeconomic and behavioral characteristics were compared between participants who successfully completed all 3 phases of data collection and those who were lost to followup through the Cohen effect size (w). Comparisons of baseline anthropometric data and DMFT were performed with the Cohen effect size (h). Intra- and interexaminer reliability was determined through the intraclass correlation coefficient. Nonparametric Friedman 2-way ANOVA was used to compare anthropometric measurements and DMFT collected at age 12, 15, and 18 years. Bar charts were used to describe distributions of obesity status among the participants at age 12, 15, and 18 years. Differences of anthropometric indices were tested by sex, parental employment status, family income, frequency of tooth brushing, use of fluoride toothpaste, and snacking frequency with the Mann-Whitney U test, Kruskal-Wallis test, 2-sample t test, and 1-way ANOVA. Negative binomial regression was performed to evaluate the effect of BMI,WC, WHR, WHtR, and TRSKF on future dental caries status. To assess the longitudinal effect of DMFT on future adiposity status, binary logistic regressions were carried out. In both regression models, DMFT was calculated as continuous data; BMI was classified into 2 groups: the underweight/normal weight group and the overweight/obese group (reference group).Median values were used to dichotomizeWC, WHR, WHtR, and TRSKF. Participants belonging to the upper 50th percentile constitute the reference group. Potential covariates for the regression models include sex, parental employment status, family income, frequency of tooth brushing, use of fluoride toothpaste, and snacking frequency. All potential covariates were treated as categorical variables. Three models were used in the negative binomial and binary logistic regression analysis. Model 1 adjusted for sex. Model 2 adjusted for sex and socioeconomic status. Model 3 adjusted for participants’ oral health-related behaviors in addition to covariates in Model 2. Binary logistic regression was also performed to evaluate the longitudinal association between adiposity indices and CPI. Three models were employed in all binary logistic regressions. In Model 1, only gender was adjusted. In Model 2, gender and socioeconomic factors (parental employment status and family income) were adjusted. In Model 3, gender, socioeconomic factors and behavioral factors (frequency of tooth brushing) were adjusted. All statistical tests were 2-sided, and the level of statistical significance was set at .05. SPSS 23.0 (IBM Corp, Armonk, New York) was used for all analyses. # To what extent the project objectives have been achieved: The project objective has been completely achieved. # Give reason for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems, if any: Nil.

17115916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115916.value: The intraclass correlation coefficient for DMFT, CPI, height, weight, WC, HC, and TRSKF ranged between 0.94 and 1.00. (Paper 1-6) The prevalence of caries was 25.5%, 53.2%, and 62.1% and mean (SD) of DMFT was 0.46 (0.94), 1.57 (2.13), and 2.13 (2.48) at 12, 15 and 18 years, respectively. (Paper 4-6) Approximately 60% participants had a CPI score of 2 at 12 years. The prevalence increased by 19.2% at 15 years and by 25.2% at 18 years. In contrast, the prevalence of CPI = 0 decreased progressively from 19.9% at 12 years to 10.3% at 15 years and 5.7% at 18 years. (Paper 4-6) A significant regression coefficient for the group indicator suggested a difference in the rate of disease progression from age 12 to 15 years compared to that from age 15 to 18 years for caries experience (p < 0.05) and for periodontal health (p < 0.01). (Conference Abstract 1) A significant association between WHR at 15 years and DMFT at 18 years was noted in all 3 models. There was a slight increase in strength of the association when more covariates were adjusted in the model. Mean DMFT of participants belonging to the lower 50th percentile of WHR at 18 years was 0.707 times lower than the mean DMFT of those in the upper 50th percentile (95% CI 0.52-0.96; P = 0.028) after adjusting for sex, parental employment status, family income, frequency of tooth brushing, use of fluoride toothpaste, and snacking frequency. For the longitudinal effects of dental caries on obesity status, model 3 revealed that for every unit increase in DMFT at 15 years, the odds of being in the upper 50th percentile of WHR at 18 years will be increased by 13.5% (95% CI 1.01-1.28; P = .041). (Paper 1 and 3) For the longitudinal association between periodontal status and adiposity indices, model 1 showed that the chance for participants with lower WHR (lower 50th percentile) to have less extensive periodontal inflammation was 1.75 times as likely (95% CI:1.05, 2.91) compared to those with higher WHR (upper 50th percentile). The fully adjusted model 3 revealed that participants in the lower BMI (underweight/normal weight) group had significantly higher probability (P = 0.022) of having more than 50% index teeth free from periodontal inflammation (OR: 2.78; 95% CI: 1.16, 6.64) than participants in the higher BMI group (overweight/obese group). (Paper 2 and Conference Abstract 2 and 3)

17115916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115916.value: # Potential for further development of the research: First, despite the observed association between WHR and experience of dental caries, the exact mechanism through which central obesity and dental caries are related remains elusive. Second, only the frequency of snacking between meals was considered as the dietary confounder in this study; more nutritional information should be included in future studies. Third, although the effects of various potential contributory factors on dental caries and obesity were explored, studies specifically designed to investigate the effect of one particular contributor to dental caries are necessary to provide finer resolution of the associations. It is desirable that salivary flow rate, hormone changes, and cariogenic bacteria be considered in future studies. # Proposed course of action: In this study, we found that overweight/obese secondary school students showed worse oral health awareness compared to underweight/normal weight individuals, and more caries lesions and more severe periodontal conditions at age 18. As obese adolescents might lack health knowledge, related education and instructions are recommended to help this group of adolescents. Given the negligence of oral health care among obese secondary school students, oral health promotion programs are necessary to improve their oral health conditions.

17115916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115916.value: The prevalence of obesity, the fifth leading cause of attributable global mortality, has markedly increased since 1980. The most common oral diseases are dental caries and periodontal disease. Oral health and adiposity status may influence the growth and development in early life, as they have a common reliance on nutrition, parenting, lifestyle, physical and social environments, as well as psychosocial factors. Hence, the association between oral health and obesity in children and adolescents has become a growing public concern. In this study we found that there were longitudinal associations between central obesity and dental caries experience among adolescents aged 15-18 years, and between higher BMI at 15 years and periodontal inflammation at age 18. The associations identified in our study add to the scant body of knowledge on the development of oral diseases and obesity, and draw attention to any problems related to this association. The findings from the study help clinicians when making diagnoses and formulating treatment plans, and when explaining and discussing relevant matters with patients and their parents. The collected data also help in the formulation of age-specific intervention programs and public policies with the aim to prevent oral diseases and enhance public health in Hong Kong.

17116416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17116416.value: 鼻咽癌(NPC)在東南亞特別是包括香港在內的中國南部地區是常發癌癥. Epstein-Barr 病毒 (EBV) 感染被認為是NPC的關鍵病原因子. EBV 可在惡變前鼻咽上皮中檢測到. 然而, 因為EBV在被感染的培養細胞中的持續丟失, 關於EBV在NPC特別是早期NPC的形成過程中的基本機制的研究受到了嚴重阻礙. 被EBV感染的正常鼻咽上皮細胞通常會進入長時的細胞周期停止, 表現出細胞老化的形態, 所以難以增殖生長. 鼻咽上皮細胞獲得支持EBV持續感染的能力, 是NPC發展過程中的關鍵步驟之一. 至今, 推動EBV持續感染的分子和細胞因子知之甚少. 目前的概念是, 宿主細胞的遺傳變異和細胞微環境的配合, 對EBV持續感染有重要作用. 值得特別註意的是, NPC有大量的淋巴細胞浸潤, 由此形成富有炎癥細胞因子的微環境. 白介素-6(IL-6)是參與炎癥反應的主要細胞因子之一, 是從急性炎癥轉化到慢性炎癥的關鍵因子. 慢性炎癥被認為是癌癥發展的培養器. IL-6通過結合到IL-6受體(IL-6R)而發揮其功能. 我們已檢測到NPC樣本中浸潤的淋巴細胞有IL-6的強表達, 同時NPC的IL-6R也有高表達. 我們的前期實驗揭示了一個沒有被描述過的IL-6/IL-6R信號激活的功能: 促使EBV在惡變前鼻咽上皮細胞中的持續感染. 本項目將研究IL-6/IL-6R信號激活在支持EBV在惡變前鼻咽上皮細胞中的持續感染的機制. 由於NPC具有富含炎癥細胞因子的特別微環境, 同時IL-6是促慢性炎癥的主要細胞因子, 定義IL-6/IL-6R信號激活在支持EBV在惡變前鼻咽上皮細胞中持續感染的作用, 將對了解NPC的早期發生有重要貢獻, 也會對NPC的幹預和治療提供有益的新見解.

17116416.label: Realisation of objectives
17116416.value: Objective 1: To define the role of IL-6/IL-6Rα signaling activation in long-term EBV maintenance in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial (NPE) cells. Objective 1 was fully realized using our hTert-immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial (NPE) cell lines as premalignant cell models The immortalized NPE cell line was permissive to EBV infection. Early dynamics of EBV maintenance in infected immortalized nasopharyngeal cells was monitored using the Akata-EBV tagged with GFP (green florescence protein) enabling real-time monitoring of growth behavior of EBV-infected cells using live-cell imaging approach. In the immortalized NP460hTert cell line, we observed rapid decreases in the percentage of EBV-infected cells in cell population as well as the average EBV copy numbers per cell within the first 72 hours post infection. The percentage of EBV-positive cells rapidly decreased from 80% to ~ 40% and ~ 20% at 48 and 72 hrs post-infection, respectively. We then examined the involvement of IL-6 signaling activation in EBV dynamics in freshly infected NPE cells. We have fully characterised the effects IL-6 treatment on the dynamics of EBV persistent in infected immortalized NPE cells. The results were published in Journal of General Virology (Pang et al., 2019 Pub. 1 in Part C). We found that the infected EBV in the presence of IL6 signaling axis supported the latent infection by suppression of lytic reactivation. Stable EBV-infection of NPE cells was achieved after multiple rounds of sorting of EBV-maintaining cells. The frequency of EBV-positive (GFP-positive) cells with IL-6 treatment was significantly higher than that without IL-6 treatment. The average EBV copy numbers in EBV-positive cells with IL-6 treatment were also significantly higher than that in cells without IL-6 treatment. These findings support our hypothesis that IL-6/IL-6Rα signaling activation may enable persistent EBV infection in premalignant NPE cells in the early stage of EBV infection. Some of the underlying mechanisms involved were further investigated in Objective 2, 3 and 4. Objective 2: To examine the specific pathways involved in IL-6/IL-6Rα signaling-mediated counteraction of cell cycle arrest and cellular senescence in EBV-infected NPE cells The IL-6/IL-6Ralpha signaling may have difference consequences in primary nasopharyngeal epithelial (NPE) cells, EBV-infected premalignant NPE cells and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) cells. We observed that EBV infection of primary nasopharyngeal epithelial cells induces growth arrest. However, stable and latent EBV infection could be established in immortalized cells with p19 deletion and/or cyclin D1 activation. We have also reported in our earlier studies that IL6 supported growth of c666-1 (an EBV-positive NPC cell line). However, In primary and some of the immortalized NPE cells, we observed that IL-6 could inhibit cell cycle progression and p53 activation. The response of primary and immortalized NPE cells appears to be different to EBV infection compared to NPC cells. The responses of NPC cells are more generally stimulatory to IL6 stimulation. In one of the recently established EBV-positive NPC cell line (NPC43; Lin et al., Nat. Comm 2018), we observed convincingly, that IL6 signaling plays important role in establishment of latent EBV infection in NPC. In particular, we found that the growth advantage of EBV-infected cells under IL-6 treatment (under stress conditions) may play a particularly important role in maintaining long-term EBV persistence in NPE cells by suppressing lytic reactivation of EBV in infected NPC cells. (See Objectives 3 and 4 for more detail investigations). Objective 3: To investigate if IL-6/IL-6Rα signaling activation decreases DNA damage induced by EBV infection in NPE cells EBV could trigger a DNA damage response (DDR) during primary infection and lytic reactivation. We and others have reported that the EBV-encoded viral proteins have been implicated in deregulating the DDR signaling pathways (Hau PM and Tsao SW, 2017 J. Virology). The activation of IL6 signaling support latent EBV infection and expression of EBV-encoded BART-microRNA. Using our EBV-positive NPC cell lines and EBV-infected immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells, STAT3 activation by IL6 could suppress EBV-induced DNA damage response in EBV-infected cells and EBV-encoded microRNA was involved. This objective was passed on to him to further define some of the underlying mechanisms involved. Through collaboration, a comprehensive transcriptional profile of EBV-encoded miRNAs was defined by small RNA sequencing in NPC xenografts and EBV-positive NPC cells established in our laboratories. Among the abundantly expressed EBV-miRNAs, BART5-5p, BART7-3p, BART9-3p, andBART14-3p was shown be to negatively regulate the expression of a key DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair gene, ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM). Modulation of ATM expression by BART5-5p, BART7-3p, BART9-3p, and BART14-3p was also observed in the transient transfection assays. By suppressing these endogenous miR-BARTs in EBV-positive NPC cells, a novel function of miR-BARTs in inhibiting Zta-induced lytic reactivation (which is known to induce DNA damages) was observed. These findings were reported (Lung et al., J Pathology 2018). Objective 4: To study if IL-6/IL-6Rα signaling activation may support latent infection of EBV in NPE cells Our findings in Objective 1 indicate that IL-6 treatment in immortalized NPE cells supported EBV persistence in the later stage of EBV infection. The ability of EBV to establish latent infection is another important factor in maintaining long-term persistence of EBV in infected cells. Transcription of lytic EBV genes was silenced in stably-infected NPE cells after repeated sorting for EBV-positive cells. IL6 treatment become less essential in suppression of lytic reactivation of EBV in stably infected NPE and NPC cells. Our results are in line with the general hypothesis that the stable EBV infection is established after epigenetic modifications of viral genome during the long-term process of establishment of latent infection. Using our recently established NPC cell line models (Lin et al., Nat. Comm 2018), we were able to dissect some of the key events involved in latent infection of EBV in NPC The NPC43 cell line was used extensively as the cell model. IL6 effectively suppressed TPA-induced lytic reactivation in NPC43 cells and effectively suppressed spontaneous lytic reactivation at their early passage (Population doubling 25). In c666-1 and C17 cell lines (established from NPC xenografts), such effects could not be demonstrated. We then carried out extensive study on NPC43, the new EBV+ve NPC cell to define the role of STAT3/IL6 signaling in regulating latent-lytic switch in EBV-infected NPC cells (basis of one Ph.D thesis). Knock down of STAT3 (by siRNA) effectively induces lytic reactivation in NPC43 cells supporting the important role of STAT3/IL6 axis in suppressing lytic reactivation of EBV in infected NPC cells through suppression of squamous differenitation Expression of KLF4 and BLMP1 in NPC43 is associated with IL6/STAT3 inhibition of lytic reactivation. This is first demonstration of essential role of IL6/STAT in regulation of lytic reactivation in authenticated and endogenously infected NPC models (unpublished results).

17116416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116416.value: 1. Establishment of efficient cell-free EBV infection protocol for nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. EBV infection is closely associated with NPC. In the past, it has been difficult to infect and establish stable EBV-infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. In this study, we have established for the first time the protocol to effectively infect through cell-free infection to infect both primary and immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells as well EBV-negative NPC cell lines, hence producing the field useful tools for investigation. We have used the models created by this approach to study the key signaling pathways involved in EBV maintenance. The maintenance of EBV in infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells is a highly dynamic events (Pang et al., J. Gen. Virology , 2019 (Publication 1). While EBV infection could be achieved by our protocol, surprisingly, we did not observe any growth advantage of EBV-infected cells. This would explain the continuous loss of EBV grow NPC cell lines ever reported. 2. IL6/STAT support latent infection and may provide growth advantage to EBV-infected cells under nutrient deficient and hypoxic conditions in vivo. The use of IL6 could activate STAT3 signaling and support latent infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. However, lowering the serum level and growth factors in the growth medium revealed growth advantage of EBV infected NPC cells to IL6 (unpublished observations). Our recent findings showed that EBV in infected NPC cells readily undergo lytic reactivation under stress conditions notably hypoxia. Our findings suggested that EBV-infected NPC may exhibit selective advantage in vivo through IL6 signaling to suppress hypoxia induced lytic reactivation of EBV (unpublished results). 3. IL6 secretion from EBV-infected cells may modulate stromal cells to support growth of EBV-infected NPC cells in vivo. Another major growth advantage of EBV infection in NPC is our recent identification of IL6 secretion in form of exosomes in our newly established NPC cell line (NPC43) (Wang et al., Cell and Molecular Immunology, 2021. Publication 4). IL6 has pronounced effects on recruitment of stromal cells notably macrophages and other undefined cell types to support growth of EBV-infected NPC cell in vivo. 4. Activation of EBV-encoded miRNA is involved in suppression of DNA damage induced by EBV infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells contributing to latent EBV infection. Using our new established NPC xenografts and cell lines, we have profiled the EBV-encoded microRNA involved in suppression of DNA damage. Specific BART-miRNA involved in the suppression of DNA damage response (DDR) and ATM were identified. Detailed of the study was published by our collaboration paper (Lung et al., J. Pathology 2018, Publication 6) 5. IL6/STAT is an essential signaling pathway to suppress lytic reactivation in EBV-infected NPC cells under stress conditions (e.g. hypoxia). Understanding the key signaling pathways involved in latent infection of EBV support the long-term EBV maintenance. A common phenomenon of NPC cell line established in the past is the loss of EBV and the contamination of the line by HeLa cells. Using the knowledge gain in this study, we were able to establish two new NPC cell lines (NPC43 and C17) harboring EBV for the field (Lin et al., Nature Communication, 2018, Publication 5; Yip et al., Lab Investigation 2018, Publication 7). These newly established NPC lines are now used widely in collaborative study in EBV/NPC studies (Nature comm., 2021 Publication 3; Siddigi et al., J. Virology, 219, Publication 2)

17116416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17116416.value: We have demonstrated the dynamic nature of EBV infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells and the important of IL6/STAT3 signaling in suppression of lytic reactivation of EBV in NPC cells. Successful suppression of lytic reactivation has contributed to our success in establishing new EBV-positive NPC cell lines for the EBV/NPC field. An important role of IL6 secretion induced by EBV-infection highlights the important of stromal in pathogenesis of EBV/NPC. The proposed course of action is to introduce the humanized mouse model to study the role of latent EBV infection and their effects on NPC progression and response to drug treatment. We observed a striking difference in EBV dynamics when the EBV-infected NPC cells were growth in vivo (in immune deficient mice and humanized mice) and also as 3D-organoid models. The stromal cells in NPC is likely to contribute the maintenance of latent infection of EBV in NPC which should be further investigated by the now well-developed 3-dimensional culture model of air-liquid interphase and tumour/stromal cells co-culture. Many of the EBV-infected cell lines could be used in these 3-dimensional culture model of NPC.

17116416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17116416.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is closely associated with EBV infection. Maintenance of EBV infection in NPC is believed to be an important property of NPC contributing the pathogenicity of NPC. Yet the underlying mechanism involved in the maintenance of EBV in infected NPC remains undefined. In this project, we have established an efficient protocol to infect culturing nasopharyngeal epithelial cells with EBV and examined its dynamics and potential growth advantage of EBV in infected NPC cells. We did not observe growth advantage of EBV infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells in culture, but confirmed that IL6 treatment could efficiently suppressed lytic reactivation of EBV in infected cells using our newly established NPC43 cell models. Suppression of lytic reactivation of EBV by IL6 is essential for establishment of latent EBV infection in NPC. This study defines various underlying mechanisms involved. Interestingly, IL6 secretion was found in our newly established NPC43 cells which may modify recruitment of tumour stroma into NPC, a major investigation direction for future investigations. The cell models established in this study will support these future studies to elucidate the role of EBV infection in NPC.

17117716.label: Project Objectives
17117716.value: To elucidate the post-receptor signaling for GH-induced PIAS1 & 4 expression and establish their role as feedback repressors for GH-induced IGF1 expression in carp liver cells. . To examine the effects of PIAS1 & 4 expression on signal transduction coupled to carp GHR and GH-induced IGF1 promoter activation via a STAT binding site in the proximal promoter region. . 17117716.label: Realisation of objectives
17117716.value: (1) PIAS1 & PIAS4 were cloned in grass carp and confirmed to be single-copy genes in carp genome. In silico protein modelling based on a.a. sequences deduced also revealed that the 3D structure of carp PIAS1 & 4 were highly comparable if not identical to their human counterparts. Functional expression of the two carp PIAS in cell line transfected with a STAT-responsive Luc reporter was shown to suppress the transactivation activity mediated by STAT5 over-expression, implying that the newly cloned cDNAs encode functional PIAS proteins with inhibitory effect on STAT signalling. Using RT-PCR for tissue expression profiling of PIAS, PIAS1 & 4 were found to be widely expressed in different tissues/organs & with high levels of transcript expression in the liver. Using LC/MS/MS, peptide fragments of PIAS1 & 4 could also be detected in lysate prepared from the carp liver, confirming that the two forms of PIAS are expressed at hepatic level, both at transcript & protein levels, and presumably play a functional role in modulating JAK2/STATs signalling in carp liver cells. (2) To test if PIAS can serve as regulatory target by GH and play a role in IGF1 regulation in carp liver, grass carp liver cells were used as a model to study the effects & underlying mechanisms for GH regulation of PIAS1 & 4 related to the parallel changes in hepatic expression of IGF1. In this cell model, GH treatment could elevate IGF1, PIAS1 & PIAS4 mRNA levels with the PIAS1 & 4 responses preceding/overlapping with the period of gradual loss in IGF1 responsiveness caused by prolonged treatment of GH. Using Western blot, GH induction was found to induce rapid phosphorylation of JAK2, STAT1, STAT3, STAT5, MEK1/2, ERK1/2, PI3K & Akt in carp liver cells and GH-induced IGF1, PIAS1 & PIAS4 gene expression could be reduced/totally negated by the inhibitors for JAK2/STATs pathway (including AG490, FA, ETTDC & IQMMA for JAK2, STAT1, STAT3 and STAT5, respectively), MAPK pathways (including PD98059, FR180204 & SB203580 for MEK1/2, ERK1/2 & P38 MAPK, respectively) and PI3K/Akt pathway (including Ly294002, HIMOC & rapamycin for PI3K, Akt & mTOR, respectively). These findings imply that GH-induced IGF1 and PIAS expression were mediated by overlapping post-receptor signalling via JAK2/STATs, MAPK and PI3K/Akt pathways. The data for signal transduction for GH-induced IGF1 expression have been published in Front Endocrinol (9:336. doi:10.3389/ fendo.2018.00336). (3) Our attempts of using both lentivirus & retrovirus for transfection in carp liver cells to study PIAS1 & 4 over-expression on GH-induced IGF1 expression were not successful. As a backup plan, we also used nucleofection for transfection but the serious problems of cell death & cell-cell fusion had precluded the use of the approach for further study. Therefore, we were forced to switch the cell model to CHO GHR cells with stable expression of carp GH receptor (GHR) for transfection study using a Luc reporter carrying a 1077 bp 5’promoter of carp IGF1 gene. Based on our testing of 7 cell lines, CHO GHR cells were the only cell line with GH inducibility of IGF1 promoter activity and GH-induced IGF1 promoter activation could be reduced/abolished by inhibiting JAK2, STAT1, STAT3, STAT5, MEK1/2, P38 MAPK, PI3K & Akt using the same blockers used in our liver cell studies, implying that CHO GHR cells could faithfully mimic the signal transduction coupled with GHR in carp liver. In this cell model, IGF1 promoter activity induced by GH could also be mimicked by over-expression of carp STAT1, STAT3 & STAT5, respectively. Furthermore, IGF1 promoter activation caused by GH/STAT expression could be suppressed in a dose-dependent manner by over-expression of grass carp PIAS1 & PIAS4, respectively. These results suggest that GH-induced IGF1 gene transcription via promoter activation may be under the negative modulation of PIAS, presumably by interference with the JAK2/STATs signalling coupled to GHR activation. (4) Sequence analysis of carp IGF1 promoter reveals the presence of a STAT5 binding site (SBE) located in close proximity to a CREB binding site (CRE) & HNF1 binding site (HBE) in the proximal promoter region. This tripartite arrangement of SBE, CRE & HBE was found to be well-conserved in IGF1 promoter of fish species. In carp liver cells, GH treatment was found to up-regulate STAT5, CREB & HNF1 transcript levels parallel to the rise in IGF1 gene expression. Using protein pull down coupled to immunoblotting, HNF1 association with STAT5 & CREB could also be elevated by GH. In CHO GHR cells transfected with Luc reporter carrying the IGF1 promoter, GH-induced IGF1 promoter activity could be further enhanced by co-transfection with the expression vectors for carp STAT5, CREB & HNF1. Using 5’deletion analysis, the responsive sequence of IGF1 promoter for GH induction as well as for STAT5, CREB & HNF1 over-expression could be mapped to the promoter region downstream of -112 with the clustering of 3 binding sites for the respective transcription factors. The functionality of these binding sites was further confirmed by EMSA gel shift assay & site-directed mutagenesis. These results suggest that GH could induce STAT5, CREB & HNF1 signals in carp liver to up-regulate IGF1 gene transcription via a novel tripartite cis-element complex composed of SBE, CRE & HBE in the proximal region of IGF1 promoter. Our manuscript on the tripartite cis-element complex mediating IGF1 gene transcription is currently under review in Mol Cell Endocrinol (Manuscript uploaded in Part C, Research Output for details.) (5) Since PIAS is known to alter gene transcription via modification of promoter binding with transcription factors & HDAC recruitment/activation by SUMOylation, carp liver cells were exposed to GH followed by SUMO2/3 pull-down coupled to LC/MS/MS. In this case, a total of 850 SUMOylated proteins could be identified, with 138 proteins up-regulated & 195 proteins down-regulated in SUMO2/3 signals with GH treatment. As revealed by heatmap hierarchical clustering, HDAC1 SUMOylation was enhanced while STAT3, 5a & 5b SUMOylation were reduced with GH stimulation. GO enrichment analyses also revealed that pathways for GHR signalling via JAK/STAT, histone deacetylase binding & transcription corepressor activity were also up/down-regulated by GH treatment. In carp liver cells, GH-induced IGF1 mRNA expression could be blocked by HAT inhibitors (C646 & Ab144556) but parallel inhibition of HDAC (by TSA & VPA) or SUMOylation (by GA & AA) was without effect. In CHO GHR cells transfected with Luc reporter carrying IGF1 promoter, the inhibitory effects of PIAS1 & 4 over-expression on GH-induced IGF1 promoter activation could be reverted by co-treatment with the inhibitors for HDAC (TSA & VPA) or SUMOylation (GA & AA). In the same model, PIAS1 over-expression was also effective in reducing STAT3 phosphorylation & increasing STAT5:PIAS1 association with GH treatment. These findings suggest that HAT activation (presumably caused by JAK2/STATs signalling) is involved in GH-induced IGF1 expression in carp liver. Meanwhile, the parallel PIAS signals induced by GH may exert a negative feedback at hepatic level to tune down/turn off IGF1 gene transcription by inhibition of STAT3 phosphorylation, protein:protein interaction for STAT5 sequestration & HDAC recruitment/activation by SUMOylation. Since our progress was delayed by (i) our unsuccessful attempt in setting up the transfection system in liver cells and (ii) the lockdown caused by COVID pandemic, we are still in the process of preparing the manuscript for this part and it is expected to be really for submission in 4-6 weeks.

17117716.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117716.value: Using carp liver cells as a model, we have showed that (i) PIAS1 & 4 could be up-regulated by GH treatment along with its stimulatory effect on IGF1 expression, and (2) the stimulatory effects of GH on IGF1, PIAS1 & PIAS4 expression were mediated by JAK2/STATs, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. Our study for the first time demonstrated that, along with GH induction of IGF1 expression in carp liver, PIAS can also serve as regulatory targets for GH at hepatic level and the stimulatory effects on IGF1, PIAS1 & PIAS4 by GH are mediated by overlapping post-receptor signaling mechanisms coupled to GHR activation. Using CHO GHR cells transfected with Luc reporter carrying the carp IGF1 promoter, we also have the novel findings that a tripartite cis-acting element complex composed of SBE, CRE & HBE located in the proximal promoter of carp IGF1 gene could mediate the stimulatory effect of GH on IGF1 gene transcription via up-regulation of STAT5, CREB & HNF1α expression at hepatic level. In the same cell model, PIAS1 & PIAS4 over-expression were found to suppress both basal & GH-induced IGF1 promoter activity. These inhibitory actions were sensitive to the blockade of HDAC & SUMOylation but not proteasome activation, and occurred with a drop in STAT3 phosphorylation & with increased association of STAT5 with PIAS1 during the period of GH induction. These findings, as a whole, suggest that the parallel rises of PIAS1 & 4 during GH-induced IGF1 expression in the carp liver may act as intracellular feedback signals to tune down/turn off the IGF1 response, probably by inhibiting IGF1 gene transcription by blocking STAT3 activation, sequestration STAT5 by protein:protein interaction & recruitment of HDAC via SUMOylation. Our studies not only provide new insight on transcriptional regulation of IGF1 by GH via a tripartite cis-acting complex within the proximal promoter of IGF1 gene in carp model, but also shed light on a novel intracellular feedback for IGF1 signal termination via PIAS1 & 4 expression at the hepatic level. Regarding the research output, besides the posters & abstracts presented in the annual meetings of the Endocrine Society (USA), papers based on the results of this project & other related studies tagged with our program (published /under review) have been covered in Section 5.3 & uploaded in Part C as requested.

17117716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117716.value: In our study, HDAC & SUMOylation, but not proteasome activation, were both involved in the inhibitory actions of PIAS1 & 4 on GH-induced IGF1 gene transcription. However, PIAS1 expression could reduce STAT3 phosphorylation & induce STAT5 association with PIAS1, which may mediate the inhibitory effect of PIAS1 on the JAK/STAT pathway. Interestingly, similar phenomenon was not observed in our parallel experiment with PIAS4 expression, implying that there may be subtle difference between the two forms of PIAS in IGF1 regulation. Since specific inhibitors for PIAS1 & 4 are not yet available, it may be a good idea to switch our model from grass carp to zebrafish. With CRISPR/Cas7 knockout of PIAS1 & 4 in zebrafish liver, alone or in combination, it may be possible to decipher the functional difference of the two PIAS in IGF1 regulation at hepatic level. Another direction based on our study is also worth pursuing. At present, it is still unclear if the role of PIAS as a feedback inhibitor for IGF1 expression can be observed in other speceis. To shed light on the comparative aspect of our findings, further studies in mammalian models (e.g., rodents) are clearly warranted.

17117716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117716.value: In this study, using grass carp liver cells & CHO GHR cells as models, we have showed that (i) GH induced IGF1 expression in carp liver via transcriptional activation of a novel a tripartite cis-acting complex located in the proximal promoter of IGF1 gene, (ii) hepatic expression of PIAS1 & PIAS4 could be up-regulated by GH via JAK/STAT, MAPK & PIK/Akt pathways along with GH stimulation of IGF1 gene transcription, (ii) PIAS1 & PIAS4 expression could suppress both basal & GH-induced IGF1 gene transcription and these inhibitory effects were sensitive to the blockade of HDAC & SUMOylation and occurred with inhibition of STAT3 phosphorylation & increased association of STAT5 with PIAS1. Our results, as a whole, suggest that GH could induce IGF1, PIAS1 & PIAS4 expression in the carp liver through overlapping post-receptor signaling and the subsequent rises of PIAS signals may constitute an intracellular feedback to down-regulate the IGF1 responses via inhibition of STAT3 activation, STAT5 sequestration by protein:protein interaction, and HDAC recruitment /activation by SUMOylation. Our findings not only provide new information on the transcriptional regulation of IGF1, but also shed light on a new facet on feedback regulation of IGF1 by GH at the hepatic level.

17117816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117816.value: Socioeconomic inequality and ageing are important social and public health concerns, and with huge human, medical and social cost. It is widely known that individuals in lower socioeconomic status (SES) are disproportionally vulnerable to a wide range of adverse physical and mental health outcomes. In Hong Kong and many neighboring Asian countries, socioeconomic inequality is continuously widening. According to the official statistics, there are approximately 1 million people in Hong Kong living in poverty, and many of which are the elderly populations. The Hong Kong population is aging very rapidly and it is projected that, by 2031, 30% of the total population will be aged 65 or above (2.7 million). Health issues of the elderly, particularly those who are economically disadvantaged, present an eminent challenge to our society. There is growing evidence showing not only individual-level SES affects health, but socioeconomic inequality (deprivation) at the neighborhood level also affects health outcomes. However, there is not yet a large-scale and systematic investigation on how individual-SES and neighborhood-SES and their interactions affect health among elderly populations in Hong Kong or in other neighboring Asian countries. The aim of this study is to investigate how socioeconomic inequality at individual- and neighborhood level and their interaction, affects health disparities among older adults in Hong Kong. Our work will focus on the common adverse physical and mental health outcomes among this age group, that is, depression and mortality outcomes (all-cause and several major causes including stroke, ischemic heart diseases, cardiovascular diseases, suicide etc.) Our findings will provide much needed information on social and public health policies that promote physical and mental health well-being among the older population. Our work can identify key neighborhood characteristics that affect older age’s health, and thus allows targeted interventions that mitigate (promote) their adverse (protective) impacts. As Hong Kong share similar economic development and social welfare systems with several neighboring East-Asian countries, our findings will provide key insights for our neighbor communities as well. 隨著老年人口在全世界範圍內不斷增加，政策制定者、醫療機構和研究者們對於決定老年人口健康的因素也越來越關注。研究表明老年人的健康受到包括個人層面和區域層面的多重因素影響。近年來，香港的老齡化日益加劇但針對香港老年人健康的大規模實證研究卻十分有限。現有研究或者只關注了個人層面的影響因素或者只採用橫斷性的研究設計。因此，本研究將基於長者健康中心的數據，以總慣性和橫斷性的研究設計，研究個人與鄰里層面的因素對香港老年人健康狀況的影響。 此次研究計劃的目的包括： 1. 評估個人與鄰里的社會經濟地位及其交互作用對老年人抑鬱症狀的影響； 2. 探求在控制了鄰里（個人）社會經濟地位后，個人（鄰里）社會經濟地位在多大程度上影響著老年人的抑鬱症狀； 3. 探索鄰里社會經濟地位對老年人抑鬱症狀的緩解作用； 4. 前瞻性地評估個人和鄰里社會經濟地位及其交互作用對老年人全因死亡率和原因別死亡率風險的影響； 5. 識別社會經濟地位特征對老年人死亡率的影響途徑。

17117816.label: Realisation of objectives
17117816.value: In this project we have evaluated the impact of individual-level SES and neighborhood-SES on depressive symptoms among Chinese elderly population. Specifically, (i) would individual-SES, after controlling the effect neighborhood-SES, contribute to older adult’s depressive symptoms, and vice versa; (ii) would individual-SES interact with neighborhood SES characteristics in affecting older adult’s depressive symptoms (relative poverty hypothesis) we have produced a paper entitle on Guo, Y., Chang, S.S., Chan, C.H., Yip, P.S.F. (2019). Association of neighbourhood social and physical attributes with depression in older adults in Hong Kong: a multilevel analysis. J Epidemiol Community Health. 2019 1:13 We have also showed the happiness and life satisfaction demonstrated weak inverse associations with suicide rate at the district level (r = -0.32 and -0.36 respectively) but very strong associations at the LSB quantile level (r = -0.83 and -0.84 respectively). There were generally very weak or weak negative correlations across sex/age groups at the district level but generally moderate to strong correlations at the LSB quantile level. The associations were markedly attenuated or became null after controlling for area characteristics. The paper appeared in Hsu, C., Chang, S., & Yip, P. (2017). Individual-, household- and neighbourhood-level characteristics associated with life satisfaction: A multilevel analysis of a population-based sample from Hong Kong. Urban Studies, 54(16), 3700-3717. Finally we published a paper the data supplied by the Department of Health prospectively evaluate how individual- and neighborhood-SES affect all-cause and cause-specific mortality risk among Chinese elderly population. And through which pathways do SES characteristics affect older adults’ mortality. The paper is going to appear in BMJ Open The combined effects of the individual and neighborhood socioeconomic status on older adults’ mortality: a retrospective follow-up study in Hong Kong BMJ Open The results showed that non-medical and suicide mortality did not show significant difference across the SES groups. Cancer, cardiovascular-, ischemic heart disease- and stroke- specific mortality showed unique pattern compared to others. The “double tragedy theory” (i.e., lower SES persons living in lower SES neighborhoods have worst health outcomes) was more related to cancer, while the “psychosocial comparison theory” (i.e., lower SES persons living in higher SES neighborhoods have worst health outcomes) was more related to other diseases. We have also had explored socioeconomic and environmental factors and the mechanisms underlying their associations. Chang, Q. S., Guo, Y., Yip, P., Conwell, Y., & Wu, D. (2019). A study on household headship, living arrangement, and recipient of pension among the older adults in association with suicidal risks. Journal of Affective Disorders, 256, 618-626. Peng, C., Kwok, C., Law, Y., Yip, P., & Cheng, Q. (2019). Intergenerational support, satisfaction with parent-child relationship and elderly parents' life satisfaction in Hong Kong. Aging & Mental Health, 23(4), 428-438. Totally we have produced five research papers in relating to the projects which have demonstrated the individual-level SES and neighborhood SES and its interaction on the depressive symptoms among Chinese Elderly population.

17117816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117816.value: We have shown that neighbourhood poverty was positively associated with elderly depression outcomes (ie, depressive symptoms and depression) in Hong Kong. ► Neighbourhood elderly concentration, recreational services and walkability were negatively associated with depressive symptoms but not depression in the elderly. ► The association between neighbourhood poverty and elderly depression symptoms was found in women only and not in men. ► The strong correlation between happiness/life satisfaction and suicide found provides evidence supporting the utility of both happiness and life satisfaction as indicators for population mental health that can help with population suicide risk assessment. Socioeconomic factors should be considered when developing interventions aimed at increasing wellbeing, especially in settings with a large income disparity. The strong associations of suicide with poverty/deprivation and social fragmentation also indicate that these dimensions could be potential targets for social policies aimed at suicide prevention. There were interaction effects between neighbourhood and individual factors on mortality, and the patterns across specific-caused mortality were different. The present study suggests that health promotion policies should well consider health disparities among the combined individual and neighbourhood SES groups.

17117816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117816.value: There is a need for more research to explore the inter-relationship between wellbeing, suicide, and socioeconomic and environmental factors and the mechanisms underlying their associations. Also, longitudinal data is much needed to enhance the research findings. At this moment, it is still very difficult to access data from Hospital Authority and Department of Health

17119916.label: Project Objectives
17119916.value: To quantify the degree of intratumour heterogeneity in LACC by IVIM histogram analysis Hypothesis: IVIM histogram analysis derived imaging biomarkers are feasible and can potentially reflect intratumour heterogeneity in both the cellular and microcirculatory tumour environment of LACC. Rationale: The unchecked proliferation and disorganised angiogenesis in LACC are hallmarks of solid tumour growth. These biological properties of LACC occur in a non-uniform way resulting in intratumour heterogeneity. Approach: Whole-tumour volumetric evaluation of LACC using IVIM histogram analysis to determine mean, median, skewness, kurtosis and percentiles as measures of tumour heterogeneity. Impact: The information generated will allow us to quantify the degree of intratumour heterogeneity and will help to improve our understanding of the intratumour heterogeneity within the LACC tumour environment with reference to its proliferative and angiogenic potential without related problems due to sampling error of small tissue samples. To determine the relationship between the degree of intratumour heterogeneity as determined by IVIM histogram analysis, and the clinicopathologic features and treatment outcome of LACC. Hypothesis: IVIM histogram analysis of intratumour heterogeneity correlates with known adverse clinicopathologic characteristics of LACC (for example, adenocarcinoma histology, high FIGO stage, large tumour size, and presence of lymphatic spread) and poor treatment outcome. Rationale: Heterogeneous tumour is prognostic of adverse tumour biology and is partly responsible for the development of tumour resistance to therapy. It is usually characterised by necrosis and poor perfusion, providing an unfavourable tumour environment for selecting the survival of the more resistant clones. Approach: The mean, median, skewness, kurtosis and percentiles values generated from IVIM histogram analysis will be correlated with the histology, FIGO stage, tumour size, lymphatic spread and treatment outcome of LACC. Impact: This study may provide the basis and direction for further research in treatment response assessment and monitoring of the changes in intratumour heterogeneity throughout CRT. Ultimately, the role of intratumour heterogeneity in disease prognosis can be further studied.

17119916.value: 相當比例宮頸癌的病人接受了同步放射化療將會出現局部復發和轉移性傳播的情況，可見同步放射化療對宮頸癌病人的治療效果存在變數。我們已從基因組學研究中得知，臨床進展不佳風險增加與克隆多樣性增多，以及腫瘤內異質性增加有關。早期證據顯示腫瘤內異質性對宮頸癌的轉歸產生影響，但難以臨床描述其特性及量化。 磁力共振成像(MRI) 是宮頸癌治療前期評估的基礎。 磁力共振擴散加權成像(DWI)和動態增強磁力共振成像(DCE-MRI)分別提供了腫瘤內微結構和微血管的環境資料。由於細胞增殖和血管生成，是實體腫瘤生長程度的關鍵特徵 ，這些功能參數被廣泛認為包含了預測住後病情的重要數據。一個新的方法-磁力共振體素不相干運動擴散加權成像(intravoxel incoherent motion , IVIM)能夠改善識別宮頸癌內微結構和微血管組成部分。它能同步地評估腫瘤中細胞微結構和毛細管網絡環境，而不需外加顯影劑，同時改進微觀尺度(~ 10μm)上的靈敏度。儘管其臨床應用上已所增加，目前尚未有探討IVIM用於宮頸癌患者中，以其腫瘤表觀(細胞構造和微血管分布)的生物學特性的變異，去反映腫瘤內的異質性。 我們初步發布指出用IVIM直方圖分析宮頸癌的可行性，及觀測到在不同的FIGO分期標準下宮頸癌直方圖的差異特徵。這些研究發現支持現計劃的核心假設: 透過IVIM(細胞及微血管的)中得知宮頸癌的生物學特性，可以用作腫瘤異質性的生物標志物。 這個假設將會以下列具體目標去進行測試: (1 )以IVIM直方圖分析法去量化宮頸癌腫瘤內異質性的程度； (2) 測定從IVIM直方圖分析法中得出的腫瘤異質性的程度，與宮頸癌的臨床病理特徵和治療效果，兩者之間的關係。 我們期望以IVIM直方圖分析法，這個非侵入性以及定量的分析方法，能在未來應用於監測放射化療過程的效果評估，反映宮頸癌腫瘤異質性的生物標志物。

17119916.value: 1. To quantify the degree of intratumour heterogeneity in LACC by IVIM histogram analysis Extent of Realisation: 100% • Development and optimisation of IVIM estimation algorithm IVIM requires post-processing calculation work to calculate the three IVIM parameters: pure diffusion coefficient (D), perfusion fraction (f), and pseudo-diffusion coefficient (D*). Originally the plan was to use a software by the MRI vendor Philips Healthcare; however, it was found to be inefficient and inflexible. We developed our own in-house IVIM calculation routine on MATLAB (The Mathworks Inc., Natick, MA), to have greater control over DWI post-processing. This also allowed us to efficiently compare IVIM with other diffusion models, such as the conventional monoexponential model and diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) model as done in the works by Lee et al. (2017) J Magn Reason Imaging, Wang et al. (2019) Acad Radiol, and Perucho et al. (2020) Cancer Imaging. IVIM requires more b-value acquisitions compared to conventional DWI, leading to long scan times. Furthermore, the choice of b-values critically affect IVIM estimation, but there is limited guidance on which b-values to acquire. In the work by Perucho et al. (2020) Korean J Radiol simulation and in-vivo data were used to determine optimal choice of b-values and proposed a shorter protocol that did not sacrifice IVIM’s diagnostic capabilities. • Development of Texture Analysis Framework Histogram analysis is the main method described in the proposal to quantify intratumour heterogeneity. However, histogram analysis falls under an umbrella of descriptive statistics known as texture analysis. Since then, there has been a large interest in texture analysis in medical imaging as it introduced more imaging biomarkers to characterise tumours. Originally, the plan was to use a software designed by Philips; however, this software was limited to histogram analysis. Therefore, we shifted to MATLAB and Python for greater flexibility and streamlined analysis. 2. To determine the relationship between the degree of intratumour heterogeneity as determined by IVIM histogram analysis, and the clinicopathologic features and treatment outcome of LACC. Extent of Realisation: 100% Associations between IVIM, DWI, DKI parameters and clinicopathologic features were examined and compiled in the following published works: • Association with FIGO stage: IVIM parameters in Perucho et al. (2020) Korean J Radiol; mean DKI parameters and ADC in Wang et al. (2019) Acad Radiol. • Association with nodal stage: ADC texture features in Becker et al. (2020) Korean J Radiol; ADC texture features in Becker et al. (2017) Acta Radiol Open; Mean DKI parameters and ADC in Wang et al. (2019) Acad Radiol. Associations between IVIM, DWI parameters and treatment outcome were examined and compiled in the following works: • Association with haematological toxicity (HT): Change of D across treatment in (published) Lee et al. 17119916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119916.value: • Demonstrated the feasibility of a parameter-free IVIM approach Conventional IVIM fitting methods require setting an arbitrary b-value and this choice critically affects the overall estimation of IVIM parameters. In the work Ref 1 an alternative fitting method that did not require the setting of an arbitrary b-value was used, and the resulting IVIM parameters were able to differentiate histological sub-types. • Classification of clinicopathological factors using MRI texture features. Histogram analysis is also known as first-order texture analysis, and the interest in the use of first- and higher-order texture analysis in medical imaging has increased. In the pilot study Ref 2, a small set of patients were used in a pilot study to examine the feasibility of texture analysis of ADC in LACC. There were associations between certain texture features and grading as well as subtype. In a follow-up study Ref 7 Eur Radiol 2020, predictive models combining texture features of T2W images, ADC maps, and contrast-enhanced T1W images, were used to classify histological subtype, tumour grade, FIGO stage, and nodal status. • Prediction of haematological toxicity in LACC patients treated with CCRT Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) is the standard treatment for LACC; however, pelvic radiation that treats a large volume of the pelvic bone marrow causes injury to the bone marrow microenvironment that could lead to haematological toxicity (HT). In the work Ref 3, it was found that the change in the pure diffusion coefficient (D) was able to differentiate early cellular environment changes in the bone marrow after CCRT. • Concordance of FDG-PET/CT, DW-MRI, and T2-Weighted tumour volumes MRI is the modality of choice for anatomical delineation of LACC tumour extent; however, there is evidence that functional imaging techniques such as DW-MRI and FDG-PET/CT provide information for more precise radiation target delineation. In the work Ref 4 it was found that only the 30th percentile of the metabolic tumour volume (MTV30) determined by FDG-PET/CT was not significantly different from the gold-standard of anatomical tumour volume (ATV) determined by T2W. • Demonstrated the feasibility of diffusion kurtosis imaging in LACC Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging (DKI) is another diffusion model that examines the non-Gaussian water diffusion when higher b-values are acquired. In Ref 5 it was found that DKI parameters could differentiate tissue types in the cervix as well as histological subtype, tumour grade, and FIGO stage in LACC. Furthermore, delineation from a single slice of a DKI map was sufficient in observing these differences. • Optimised the b-value acquisition of IVIM sequences for LACC patients IVIM requires a number of b-values to be acquired thus requiring long scan times. Reducing scan time would make this sequence more clinically appealing. Furthermore, the choice of b-values critically affects the estimation of IVIM parameters. In Ref 6 simulation and in-vivo data were analysed to propose a reduced scan-time protocol with optimal b-value acquisition that still retained the same diagnostic capability. • Detection of sub-centimetre metastatic lymph nodes using IVIM parameters MRI is routinely used to assess lymph node metastasis, but is known to have low accuracy, especially in the detection of sub-centimetre metastasis. In Ref 8 a prediction model using IVIM features was developed to improve the detection of sub-centimetre metastasis. • Prediction of early treatment response using DWI parameters Early prediction of patients who would have poor treatment response is important for patient management and provides opportunity for early intervention. In Ref 9 T2W and ADC features were used to predict patients with poor treatment response.

17119916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119916.value: • IVIM Contrast-to-noise ratio improvement Development: It was found that low b-values (b < 300 s/mm2) have low contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) – or the true signal difference between two consecutive b-values versus measurement uncertainty – and it was proposed that these low b-values should be acquired multiple times and signal averaged. Improved CNR in low b-values would greatly increase estimation accuracy of perfusion-based parameters. Proposal: The measurement variability of low b-values would be evaluated in phantom and patient data. • Bayesian-based IVIM modelling Development: Conventional fitting methods make use of a non-linear least squares (NLLS) estimator. A Bayesian-based IVIM modelling approach does not require user-defined constraints and has reduced estimation uncertainty. Proposal: Develop a Bayesian-based modelling approach. • Automated segmentation Development: One requisite step in texture analysis studies is the manual delineation of tumours by one or more radiologists. With sufficient patients and observer delineations, deep learning algorithms can be explored and trained to automatically delineate tumours. Proposal: Collect more patient data and observer delineations, as well as train deep learning for automated segmentation. • Multi-centre verification of the robustness of imaging biomarkers Development: DWI and IVIM features have been shown to have associations with various clinicopathological characteristics and can predict early treatment response. To test the generalizability of the presented studies, future studies should include cohorts from multiple centres to gauge the robustness of the imaging biomarkers and prediction modelling. Proposal: Establish collaborations with co-Investigators from other centres.

17119916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119916.value: Cervical cancer (CC) is one of the most common gynaecological malignancies. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an important diagnostic tool in the evaluation of CC. It is considered the standard for anatomical assessment of the primary tumour of CC. However, conventional MRI is not very accurate at identifying lymphatic and distant metastasis. Furthermore, chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the standard treatment for CC, but there currently is no method to predict which patients would have poor response to this standard treatment. In this research project, we exploited the unique flexibility of MRI to investigate the functional characteristics of CC – through the use of the intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) technique – to supplement the conventional anatomical assessment of CC. Furthermore, we believe that there are certain patterns to an image that are imperceptible to the human eye but are useful in better characterising tumours. These patterns can be objectively measured and quantified using a technique called texture analysis (TA). In our research we have found that a combination of the IVIM and TA techniques could improve the diagnosis of patients and identify patients that would respond poorly to standard treatment. If used in clinical practice, it could lead to better patient management.

17121016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121016.value: The lethality of the novel Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) infection in humans, together with its ability to cause self-limited outbreaks in humans has raised fears of the emergence of another widespread epidemic reminiscent of SARS in 2003. It is therefore important to understand the pathogenesis of these coronavirus infections in humans which will in turn facilitate development of novel therapeutic interventions. This is particularly important in view of the lack of specific countermeasures for this MERS-CoV and the poor clinical outcome associated with the current non-specific therapeutic options for both MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV. Acute lung injury leading to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is the basis of the adverse clinical outcome associated with severe MERS and SARS. In this research proposal, I propose to use a physiologically relevant in vitro human lung injury model to compare the direct and indirect (paracrine) effects of MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV infection as well as the less pathogenic human coronavirus 229E, on alveolar fluid clearance and protein permeability using primary human alveolar epithelial cells and to investigate the beneficial effect of cell-based therapy with human mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) on reducing the severity of lung injury and accelerating the resolution of lung edema, both experimental models in vitro and in specialized in vivo mouse models. I hypothesize that paracrine mediators released from virus infected cells contribute to reduced alveolar fluid clearance and enhanced protein permeability and that treatment with MSC will reverse these pathogenic processes. Comparative studies of these pathogenic coronaviruses and less pathogenic coronaviruses (229E) will provide useful insights on pathogenesis and will offer new insights and treatment options for patients infected by the pathogenic coronaviruses such as MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV. 新型中東呼吸綜合症（MERS冠狀病毒）感染人類的致死率，以及其導致人類自限性疫情的能力讓人聯想到2003年另一項廣泛的疫情- SARS的出現。鑑於目前缺乏MERS冠狀病毒的特異性治療方法，加上用於MERS和SARS冠狀病毒的非特異性治療方案未能帶來理想的臨床效果。因此，了解這些冠狀病毒感染人類的發病機制及促進發展治療措施顯得尤為重要。與MERS 和SARS相關的不良臨床結果是基於急性肺損傷導致急性呼吸窘迫綜合徵（ARDS）。在這項研究建議中，我建議使用一個生理上相應人類肺損傷的體外培養模型來比較MERS冠狀病毒和SARS冠狀病毒感染的直接和間接（旁分泌）後果，以及致病力較弱的人類冠狀病毒229E，對人類肺泡上皮細胞清除肺泡內的液體和蛋白滲透性的影響，並以體外培養和活體小鼠模型調查基於人類間質幹細胞（MSC）的療法在減少肺損傷的嚴重程度和加速分解肺水腫上的有益效果。我推測，感染病毒的細胞釋放介質旁分泌會導致減少肺泡液體清除和提高蛋白質的滲透性，MSC治療將扭轉這些致病過程。這些高致病性的冠狀病毒和致病力較弱的冠狀病毒（229E）的比較研究將釐清發病機理和提供新的見解和治療方案予受高致病性的冠狀病毒如MERS冠狀病毒和SARS冠狀病毒感染的患者。

17121016.label: Realisation of objectives
17121016.value: In objective 1, in vitro lung injury model derived from primary culture of human alveolar epithelial cells in transwell culture inserts were established to study the change in AFC and APP upon infection of highly pathogenic coronavirus, e.g., SARS-CoV-1 and MERS-CoV and to compare the change in AFC and APP with the low pathogenic coronavirus, e.g. the 229E and OC43 in objective 1. All infection experiments have been performed for more than 3 time and consistence results were obtained and this objective is well achieved. However, for the low pathogenic coronavirus OC43 control coronavirus virus, the infectious viral titer is very low (virus titer not as good as the other low pathogenic coronavirus 229E and newly added coronavirus NL-63) to achieve good infection rate (with MOI=2) in primary culture of human alveolar epithelial cells derived. Since similar results was obtained between the two low pathogenic coronavirus, 229E and NL-63, therefore we have used 229E and NL-63 as the low pathogenic coronavirus control in all in vitro experiments. In objective 2, the extent of the proposal is well achieved. Since along with impairment in AFC and APP after SARS-CoV-1 and MERS-CoV infection in alveolar epithelial cells, we further demonstrated the significantly down-regulation of the major epithelial sodium and chloride transporters, Na+K+ATPase, ENaC and CFTR mRNA and protein by the MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1 but not with the low pathogenic 229E virus. Besides, hyper-induction of pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine was observed upon infection with both MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1 infected alveolar epithelial cells. In objective 3, specific inhibitor of Na+K+ATPase, ENaC and CFTR has been applied to the in vitro lung injury model before infection and to determine their role in regulating the impaired AFC and APP. In this objective, several specific inhibitors and activators of epithelial ion channels were used to test in in vitro lung injury model upon coronavirus infection which well demonstrated further additional impairment in both AFC and APP in alveolar epithelial cells which provide important mechanistic role of these epithelial ion channel inhibitor in regulating the AFC upon coronavirus infection. However, severe cell toxicity was observed in cell culture with activator of Na+K+ATPase and CFTR upon treatment. We have tried three different brand of ion channel activators and similar toxicity was demonstrated, therefore we are unable to study the role of ion channel activator in the in vitro lung injury model. In objective 4, using the transwell culture system of the in vitro lung injury model with the co-culture (without direct cell contact) of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) and alveolar epithelial cells infected with MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1. We are able to well addressed the proposed objective as to demonstrate the potential therapeutic effect of MSC in reducing the damage/impairment in AFC and APP upon coronavirus virus infection. Furthermore, MSC reduce AFC and APP impairment and also restore the down-regulated epithelial ion channels (Na+K+ATPase, ENaC and CFTR) expression through modulated the robust innate pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine responses. In objective 5, in vivo mouse experiments using female Balb/C mice transduced with human DPP4 expressing adenovirus (Ad5-hDPP4) and infected with MERS-CoV and to study the therapeutic role of MSC in treatment of MERS-CoV infection. This objective is well addressed and we are able to demonstrate the novel and potent therapeutic effect of MSC in reducing the adverse impairment in alveolar fluid clearance and lung injury through up-regulating the inhibited expression of epithelial ion channel by modulating dysregulated proinflammatory cytokines response in vivo upon MERS-CoV infection. 17121016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121016.value: Objective 1: In vitro human lung injury model was applied to study the impairment of AFC and APP upon MERS and SARS-CoV-1 infection, and we showed that SARS-CoV-1 and MERS-CoV significantly impaired AFC and APP when compared to 229E and NL-63. Objective 2: Along with impairment in AFC, Na+K+ATPase, ENaC and CFTR mRNA and protein expression are significantly down-regulated by MERS-CoV and significantly more severe in SARS-CoV-1 infected cells. No down-regulation of ion channels in 229E and NL-63 infected cells. Hyper-induction of pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine was accompanied in MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1 infected cells. Objective 3: Specific inhibitor of Na+K+ATPase (Ouabain) and CFTR (Ivacaftor) incubation before coronavirus virus infection, showed further impairment in AFC and APP, that suggested that the mechanistic role of ion transporters in regulating the AFC. Objective 4: The co-culture of MSC with MERS-CoV/SARS-CoV-1 infected cells reduces the adverse effect on AFC, APP and cytokine responses. Viral effects on AFC and APP were significantly moderated which shown levels similar to mock-infected cells through regulating the dysregulated cytokine response and by prevents down-regulation of Na+K+ATPase, CFTR and ENaC. Objective 5: We assessed MSC treatment on survival, body weight, alveolar fluid clearance and lung pathology of MERS-CoV virus–infected mice. Balb-c transgenic mice (Ad5-hDPP4 mice) infected with MERS-CoV and treated with intravenous injection of MSC (5 x 105.5 cells) at day 5 post-infection (p.i.). Survival and body weight gain were significantly greater in MSC-treated mice than control. MSC-treated mice had a significantly lower wet-to-dry lung weight than control at day 10 p.i. MSC treatment reduces vascular leakage of plasma protein in mice. Protein concentration in BAL fluid was significantly less in MSC-treatment at day 10 p.i BAL fluid with significantly more macrophages/ monocytes and NK cells. Cytokine proteins were significantly lower in the BAL fluid of MSC-treated mice at day 10 p.i. Besides, Na+K+ATPase and CFTR protein were significantly higher in the lung lysates of MSC-treated mice by Western blot analysis. Furthermore, MSC-treated mice had significantly less lung pathology at day 14 p.i. when compared to control mice after infection. The peribronchial, perivascular, and overall histopathology scores of the MSC-treated mice were significantly lower than those of controls at day 14 p.i.

17121016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121016.value: This research provides important and novel information on mechanisms underlying the development of ARDS associated with highly pathogenic coronavirus MERS-CoV. We learn (1) how MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1 cause acute lung injury leading to ARDS, (2) whether approved drugs currently in market (inhibitor for CFTR and Na+K+ATPase) can modulate the lung injury by restoring the down-impairment in AFC and APP after severe coronavirus infection, (3) whether MSC can reverse pathogenic mechanisms, and (4) MSC can improve survival and lung pathology of mice infected with MERS-CoV. I envision future clinical trials building on these results to study the mechanism of MSC on alveolar fluid transport in an injured alveolus infected with MERS-CoV, and more importantly to apply these knowledge towards the potential novel treatment for current pandemic of COVID-19 which caused by SARS-CoV-2 infection which have shared the similar respiratory pathogenesis in human population.

17121016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121016.value: Acute lung injury, including impairment in alveolar fluid clearance, is a life-threatening complication of severe emerging respiratory virus infection, like human infection with SARS-CoV-1 and MERS-CoV and more recently the COVID-19 pandemic (SARS-CoV-2), and effective and specific treatment is lacking. Understanding the mechanism of this complication may suggest novel therapies. Here we found that in vitro, SARS-CoV-1 and MERS-CoV infection impaired alveolar fluid clearance and protein permeability more than coronavirus 229E and NL-63, mimicking its greater severity in patients. We demonstrated that this impairment is mediated by the release of inflammatory soluble factors from infected cells, leading to down-regulation of alveolar sodium and chloride ion transporters. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) prevented or reduced this effect in vitro and in vivo in MERS-CoV-infected mice.

17121616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121616.value: 了解癌症基因和藥理學的關係可加速個性化治療的發展。頭頸癌（HNC）的基因組特徵顯示 ALK 基因突變，基因擴增，可能與Crizotinib和Ceritinib敏感性有關，具有潛在的臨床益處。在美國HNC樣品進行深入的臨床數據分析表明，所有的可識別HNC個案中，ALK的基因組畸變僅在晚期（階段3和4）HNC患者中發現，暗示ALK和/ ALK-相關的基因組的事件的關鍵作用在HNC進展/侵略性。隨後的基因組分析顯示，ALK-改變HNC腫瘤共窩藏另一個癌基因，PIK3CA的擴增，揭示ALK選擇性耦合和PIK3CA擴增與HNC進展相關。ALK和PIK3CA “共同驅動”HNC形成和侵略性。在這裡，我們建議：1）比較亞洲和美國，HNC患者腫瘤中ALK和PIK3CA基因組譜來定義的2個主要基因在頭頸癌的臨床相關性; 2）確定ALK / PIK3CA耦合機制; 和 3) 研究ALK和 PIK3CA 的相關HNC模型的治療功效。該研究可加速頭頸癌的個性化治療的發展。

17121616.label: Realisation of objectives
17121616.value: These results included are in addition to what we reported in the mid-term report previously. In summary, for Aim 1: we identified that in both TCGA and our Asian cohort, there is an association between ALK genomic aberrations and PIK3CA mutation/amplification by next-generation sequencing. Furthermore, we perform correlation analyses for top 10 frequently mutated genes in HNSCC and found that this co-occurrence is only for ALK/PIK3CA aberrations, confirming the validity of our proposed hypothesis. The rate of ALK mutations is highly similar to that in TCGA-HNSCC cohort, ~3-4% rate. There is no ethnic differences. For aim 2, we found that engineered ALK mutations could induce a marked growth, clonogenicity, invasion in HNSCC cells bearing PIK3CA aberrations. More importantly, abrogation of PIK3CA by shRNA experiments and PI3K inhibition indicated that PIK3CA is needed for HNSCC growth, demonstrating the functional importance of PIK3CA in this ALK/PIK3CA coupling event found in HNSCC. Transcriptomic characterization followed by GO ontology analysis showed massive increases in RNA metabolism by ALK mutants, supportive of driver events induced by these ALK mutations in HNSCC cell models. For aim 3, we found that ceritinib, but not crizotinib, has growth inhibitory effects against a number of ALK mutations, not wildtype in our FaDu-engineered models expressing ALK mutations. The inhibition is about 30-40% in vivo tumor growth with statistical significance. Immunohistochemical staining showed that there was increase in apoptosis by TUNEL staining, reduction in tumor cell proliferation by Ki-67 staining, and reduction in pan-cytokeratin staining indicative of reduction of tumor cell population in the tumors treated with ceritinib. ALK-WT patient-derived xenograft (PDX) was not sensitive to ceritinib, yet, we could not identify any ALK-mutated PDX models in our cohort for subsequent in vivo studies. More importantly, combination with PI3K inhibitor, BYL-719, showed a more dramatic inhibition (~70-80%) of tumor growth of FaDu-ALK mutation xenografts. Our findings established for the first time that ALK aberrations co-exist with PIK3CA aberrations and combination or even single agent treatment with ALK inhibitor can be potentially effective for HNSCC subset of patients bearing ALK mutations. This will translate to ~332,000 patients per year worldwide. Difficulties: waves of COVID-19 hits greatly impeded the research progress. It was extra works from the group to complete this project in the past 2 years. We are grateful for the support of the GRF. Thank you!

17121616.value: Nature: Precision medicine development in head and neck cancer is slow. We need to harness more drug-sensitising genetic events for this devastating cancer to promote the development of precision medicine development. Therefore, this study focused on the identification of the drug sensitivity nature of ALK mutations in head and neck cancer. Significance: At the end of the study, we found that somatic mutations of ALK in head and neck cancer are drivers for cancer cell growth.
