17122916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122916.value: Ecosystem change is a frequent outcome of decadal modifications to the physical and chemical environment. Whilst we know that these changes often involve degradation of productive states, leading to less productive ecosystems, the changes are often unexpected and abrupt. Only recently has it been recognised that the unexpected nature of these changes is because ecosystems contain internal mechanisms which resist change. When this resistance fails the ecosystem changes. For example, in many tropical marine systems ocean acidification (OA) and warming are predicted to cause a shift to domination by by mats of filamentous algae at the expense of corals. Currently, grazing by benthic herbivores suppresses the excess growth of these algal mats, conferring resistance to the system. If these grazers are lost from the system, such as through ocean warming, this resistance is lost and the system is likely to shift to an algal-dominated state. Yet, a critical gap in our ability to predict such shifts is our limited understanding of the physiological limits of these grazers and under what conditions they will fail to provide this service to the ecosystem. Here, I propose to evaluate the effects of long-term ocean acidification and warming on the physiological performance of the key subtidal grazes in Hong Kong (sea urchins and gastropods). By using long-term mesocosm experiments, I will identify the extent to which these grazers are able to continue to provide a mechanism of resistance to the ecosystems which they inhabit through consumption of algal mats. I will take experiments a step further than other physiological studies, however, by assessing whether there is ecological redundancy in this system. Different species have different physiological limits and while one species may become lost from the local system under future conditions, others may fill that gap. Therefore, mesocosm experiments will be used to assess if gastropods, which have higher physiological tolerance limits, can indeed provide the same ecosystem service as urchins. By identifying the relative performance of these different species, I will be able to refine predictions on not only the likelihood of these subtidal systems changing to domination by algae but also whether there will be an abrupt (no redundancy) or gradual (redundancy) loss of resistance. 生態系統變化是長期對物理和化學環境修改的常見結果。雖然我們知道這些變化往往涉及生產狀態的退化，從而減少生態系統的生產力，這些變化往往是出乎意料和突然。直到最近，我們才得知生態系統含有內部機制去拒絕變化。當這個阻力失敗，生態系統便會變化。例如，在許多熱帶海洋生態系統的海洋酸化（OA）和氣候變暖中，我們會預計將導致絲狀藻類墊來代替珊瑚。目前，底棲食草動物抑制這些藻墊的過量生長，抗性到系統中。如果這些食草動物從系統中消失（如通過海洋變暖），這種阻力便會失去，該系統是可能轉移到藻類為主的狀態。然而，我們不能預測這種轉變的關鍵是不能完全明白這些食草動物的生理極限及他們在什麼情況無法對生態系統提供這種服務。 在這裡，我建議評估一下長期的海洋酸化和氣候變暖對主要食草動物（海膽和腹足綱）的生理影響。通過使用長期圍隔實驗，我將確定這些食草動物對藻墊的消費能否繼續對生態系統提供阻力。然而我的實驗將比其他生理學研究更進一步，去評估在該系統中是否有生態冗餘。不同品種有不同的生理極限，當一個物種即將從本地系統中消失，其他物種可能會填補這空缺。因此，圍隔實驗將用於評估海膽和腹足綱（具有更高的生理耐受性的限制）是否可以確實提供海膽對生態系統相同的服務。通過識別這些不同物種的相對表現，我就不僅對這些潮下系統變作藻類為主作出預測，同時預測到是否會出現突然（無冗餘）或逐漸（冗餘）的阻力損失。

17122916.label: Realisation of objectives
17122916.value: Goal 1: Quantify the physiological limits of the key urchins and gastropods. The experiments for Goal 1 were successfully completed and the outcomes published in 1 paper, with a second to be resubmitted to review by the end of 2021. The first step of the project was to identify the physiological limits of urchins and gastropods to increased temperatures. We successfully completed three independent experiments on two urchin species and three of the more abundant grazing gastropods to assess their physiological (metabolic) responses to warming and thermal tolerance limits (mortality). Individuals at 34°C had metabolic rates three-fold higher than at 28°C and were pushed past their CTmax (temperature at which competency is lost) but recovered function within 24 hours after being returned to summer temperatures. The manuscript from this experiment was initially sent to review in Limnology and Oceanography Letters, but it was rejected because of the need for molecular data to support the physiological responses. To achieve this, we re-ran the experiment collecting both more physiological data and tissue samples for analysis. Tissue samples have now been analysed for heat shock protein and fatty acid oxidative stress markers. The manuscript from this experiment will be submitted to Climate Change Ecology before the end of 2021 (publication 6, Part C). We then tested for the ability of different gastropod species to physiologically adjust to longer heating events consistent with projected marine heatwaves (MHW) and monitored the physiological responses both during and following the heatwaves. Interestingly, exposure to moderate heatwave conditions (31°C) caused metabolic depression, not increases, in both species tested. Importantly, heatwaves caused increased mortality, with 100% of individuals dying in the extreme heatwave (34°C) conditions. These outcomes are published in Hemraj et al. (2020) (publication 2, Part C). These experiments demonstrate that while these subtidal organisms can recover from short-term exposure to temperatures up to +6°C for three days and acclimate to slower warming for extended periods (publication 1), marine heatwave exposure causes physiological decline and mortality (publications 2, 3, 6). Goal 2: Experimentally assess the potential of urchins and gastropods to acclimate to ocean acidification and warming. The experiments for Goal 2 were successfully completed and the outcomes published in 2 papers. Our experiments successfully demonstrated that the effects of ocean warming (OW) and ocean acidification (OA) had contrasting effects on the physiology of the gastropod Trochus maculatus, which showed the ability to acclimate to higher temperatures (+3°C), resulting in an increase in the temperature at which maximum metabolic rate was expressed. In contrast, OA at moderate levels caused metabolic depression which drove a decrease in the upper lethal temperature of almost 9°C (publication 3). Interestingly, OA expected by the end of the century caused metabolic depression in gastropods to the point that individuals did not metabolically respond to increased temperatures, ultimately leading to the inability to feed and 100% mortality (publications 1,3). Importantly, the urchin H. crassispina did not undergo metabolic depression under OA conditions, was able to acclimate to moderate OW, and did not show any mortality when OA and OW are imposed slowly (cf. heatwaves) (publication 1). Goal 3: Experimentally assess the ability of these key grazers to fill their ecological function under future conditions, in particular whether they can compensate for increased growth of algal mats. The experiments for Goal 3 were successfully completed and the outcomes published in 1 paper. The extension of this work was also published in 1 paper, with another to be submitted by the end of 2021. The inability of all of the gastropods to metabolically acclimate to combined OW and OA conditions was initially expressed in a decline in the consumption of algae. As the primary ecological role for these species, this therefore meant that they were no longer filling their ecological role and could not compensate for increased algal growth. Importantly, the high mortality under predicted future conditions means that populations may decline, further restricting these species to fill this role (publication 1). In contrast to predictions, the urchin H. crassispina did not undergo substantial metabolic depression or mortality under combined OA and OW, but did have suppressed rates of algal consumption (publication 1). Therefore, while individuals were still filling their ecological role, it was at a diminished rate and so they may not be able to compensate for increased algal growth. Importantly, we recognised as part of the experiments in this Goal that it is the ability to survive and reproduce that will determine the population-level outcomes and maintenance of ecosystem functions. Therefore, we developed a new collaboration with a leading expert in urchin reproductive biology (Prof. Maria Byrne, University of Sydney) to run extra experiments to assess the effects of marine heatwaves (as the main driver of effects in other experiments) on the reproductive ability of adults and larval survival. We found that marine heatwaves increased the incidence of disease and mortality in adults of the urchin Heliocidaris erythrogramma (a conger of H. crassispina found in Australia) (publication 4). For individuals that survived and spawned, larval survival was initially high and the larvae from parents in heatwave conditions grew faster even under higher temperatures. However, there was no indication of beneficial carryover effects of parental exposure to heatwaves, with larvae from these conditions ultimately having high mortality (publication 5). Therefore, it seems that marine heatwaves could potentially further cause population declines even if adults successfully reproduce, further reducing the ecosystem functions of these important grazing species. The potential for parental effects and heat hardening of larvae and juveniles is now under investigation in a newly funded GRF led by Russell (2022 – 2025). Goal 4: Establish continuous, long-term monitoring of shallow subtidal conditions. Goal partially successful – long-term monitoring was established but the equipment was damaged by extreme weather, so needed to be re-established. The first of the long-term monitoring sites was established in the Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park (north-eastern Hong Kong) in January 2017. The main monitoring station continuously recorded temperature, pH, salinity, turbidity, and chlorophyll fluorescence. This site was continuously recording for approximately two years before the equipment failed and was not able to be repaired. In addition, an array of temperature sensors was deployed across approximately a 1 km2 area to monitor the spatial variation of temperature among subtidal reefs in the area. These data are directly applicable to the conservation of corals within the Marine Park and so have been curated by the HK Agriculture, Fisheries, and Conservation Department (AFCD) for Government and public use. The second monitoring site in the Cape D’Aguilar Marine Reserve (south-eastern Hong Kong) was initially delayed by equipment supply but was successfully established in June 2018. Unfortunately, we were unable to retrieve the equipment prior to the arrival of Super Typhoon Mangkhut (September 2018) because of the speed at which conditions deteriorated, so all equipment was severely damaged, and data lost. To re-establish ongoing monitoring, we have joined an international network for continuously recording marine temperatures for ecosystem monitoring (Aqualink: https://aqualink.org/reefs/2975). The data are automatically uploaded to the network website and immediately available for public use, providing the first continuous, long-term temperature data at an ecologically relevant scale available in Hong Kong.

17122916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122916.value: The overarching goal of this project was to understand if subtidal grazing gastropods and urchins which nominally fill the same ecological niche are functionally equivalent and if they can maintain their ecological role under future ocean warming (OW) and acidification (OA). The first step of the project was to identify the physiological limits of the different species to increased temperatures and then whether they could acclimate to future conditions. Overall, all species of gastropods tested seemed to be susceptible to metabolic depression and increased mortality from marine heatwaves (MHW; publication 2, Part C), gradual OW and OA (publications 1 and 3, Part C). They were also unable to maintain the rate at which they consume algae under predicted future conditions, and so are unlikely to maintain their ecological role to the same level and suppress the increased growth of algae (publication 1, Part C). In contrast to the gastropods, the urchin Heliocidaris crassispina seemed to be more resilient to short-term spikes in temperature (publication 6, Part C) and could acclimate to slow warming over the longer term (publication 1, Part C). Under these environmental conditions, urchins were able to acclimate their thermal physiology and continue to consume algae, albeit at a reduced rate (publication 1, Part C). Therefore, urchins should be able to maintain at least some of their ecological role under future conditions if OW and OA increase slowly and do not reach extreme levels. MHWs, which are rapid warming events of ~10 days or more, are cause for concern, however. As with the gastropods, MHWs cause physiological stress, increased susceptibility to disease, and increased mortality in the urchins we exposed to predicted future MHW intensity and durations (publication 4, Part C). Importantly, an indication of beneficial carryover effects (i.e., heat hardening) in offspring of adults exposed to MHW conditions suggesting that MHWs will drive declines in subsequent generations of urchins if they are frequent enough (publication 5, Part C). Therefore, it seems that marine heatwaves could potentially further cause population decline even if adults successfully reproduce, further reducing the ecosystem functions of these important grazing species. The potential for parental effects and heat hardening of larvae and juveniles is now under investigation in a newly funded GRF led by Russell (2022 – 2025).

17122916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122916.value: The vast majority of research to attempt to predict the potential effects of climate change on marine species is done using adult organisms. While the response of adults to environmental stress can be informative of short-term population effects, there is the potential that exposure to stressful conditions may lead to more resilient larvae and juveniles, i.e., carryover effects. Therefore, one of the biggest questions that remains unanswered is whether exposure of adults to extreme conditions, such as marine heatwaves, can confer physiological coping mechanisms to offspring, and the molecular mechanism for any effects. Following on from the work developed in this finalised GRF project, Russell is leading a newly funded GRF led by Russell (2022 – 2025) to investigate the potential for exposure to MHWs to cause parental effects and heat hardening of larvae and juveniles in subsequent generations.

17122916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122916.value: Climate change is predicted to drive changes in marine ecosystems through the loss of key species which maintain ecosystem function. Of particular concern are species of sea urchin and gastropods which consume seaweeds and maintain the health of tropical marine systems. In this project, we show that marine heatwaves, ocean warming, and ocean acidification will cause urchins and gastropods to be physiologically stressed and eat less seaweed, thus reducing the protection of these systems to overgrowth. However, urchins seemed to be more resilient to the effects than gastropods and so were able to maintain some function. This information helps guide actions to maintain populations of the key species which will help maintain ecosystem function (in this case sea urchins) under future climate change.

17123016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123016.value: 成體組織中的各類細胞在內穩態平衡及損傷應答過程中，依靠終末細胞的自我複製或幹細胞分化，能夠維持細胞數量的穩定，其機理研究仍是發育生物學和再生醫學領域的一個重大挑戰。在成體神經組織中，大腦的某些區域存在神經發生，但脊髓卻不具備神經元再生能力，因此，在創傷性脊髓損傷後，脊髓神經元連接斷裂和軸突脫髓鞘是不可逆的，其將導致運動和感覺的永久喪失。神經元難以再生的原因在於脊髓創傷誘導星形膠質細胞在損傷部位急劇增生和填充，形成膠質瘢痕，其能夠防止組織的進一步損傷，然而其本身形成的理化屏障也限制了神經元的生長。瘢痕週邊區域的星形膠質細胞來源於定居在脊髓實質內星形膠質細胞的自我複製，而瘢痕核心區域的星形膠質細胞則依靠脊髓室管膜內的星形膠質細胞來補充，後者具備多能神經幹細胞的特性，並且在脊髓損傷後能夠被啟動動員，從而形成瘢痕。揭示上述兩種來源的星形膠質細胞在正常和損傷脊髓中細胞命運的分子調控機制，有望充分發掘其對創傷性脊髓損傷的治療潛能。 本實驗室及該領域已有研究表明，Sox9對於維持神經幹細胞的幹性和星形膠質細胞、少突膠質細胞的形成至關重要，然而其對神經元形成作用尚未闡明，同時，在創傷性脊髓損傷後，Sox9在室管膜來源和脊髓實質定居來源星形膠質細胞中均呈現高表達；敲除Sox9基因後，膠質瘢痕標記物的表達減少，神經纖維形成增多，運動功能恢復增強，這些實驗結果顯示，操控Sox9的表達可以作為治療創傷性脊髓損傷的潛在策略。目前有待證實的是，在Sox9表達缺失時，室管膜來源和脊髓實質定居來源星形膠質細胞是否對脊髓損傷具有治療作用，更重要的是，該策略是否適用於人神經幹細胞。本專案前期研究發現，Sox9敲除人神經幹細胞的自我更新能力增強，並且有助於神經形成，同時能夠在軸突髓鞘形成過程中維持少突膠質細胞命運。據此，我們推測，通過抑制人神經幹細胞中Sox9的表達來治療脊髓損傷是一個可行的策略，為證實上述假說，我們將操控成年小鼠室管膜來源和脊髓實質定居來源星形膠質細胞的Sox9表達，探究Sox9對維持兩種細胞命運的調控機理，並且在脊髓損傷模型中驗證兩種細胞對膠質瘢痕形成和脊髓功能恢復的作用。此外，我們還將驗證Sox9敲除的人神經幹細胞移植大鼠脊髓損傷模型後的治療潛能。本研究將揭示Sox9在創傷性脊髓損傷前後的作用機制，通過調控其內源性表達，為提高脊髓損傷後的功能恢復提供新的治療策略。

17123016.label: Realisation of objectives
17123016.value: Objective 1: Elucidating the role of Sox9 in the ependymal layer and resident astrocytes of the adult mouse spinal cord Our previous data using FoxJ1-CreERT2:EGFP to induce genetic ablation of Sox9 in ependymal cells of the adult spinal cord after tamoxifen (4-OH) administration demonstrated that Sox9 is required for the maintenance of signature genes in ependymal cells and the self-renewal capacity of neural stem cell in vitro. To examine whether Sox9 is required for maintaining the resident astrocyte cell fate in the spinal cord parenchyma, we established mating cross between connexin 30 (Cx30)-CreERT2 transgenic mice with Sox9+/flox and Sox9flox/flox mice to generate mice with genetic ablation of Sox9 specifically in the resident astrocytes. These mice were on a R26R-EGFP Cre-reporter background to follow the fate of Sox9 mutant cells. Following daily 4-OHT administration for 5 days, we analyzed mutant mice after 2 weeks to determine the recombination efficiency for the loss of Sox9 protein in GFP+Sox9-/- resident astrocytes. However, we still detected the presence of Sox9 protein in GFP+ astrocytes. We tried another Cx30-CreERT2 line, but the recombination efficiency remained low. We did not detect significant alteration of Sox9, GFAP and S100beta expression in astrocytes. We speculate that this could be due to inefficient Cre-loxP recombination or perdurance of Sox9 protein after gene excision. To determine whether overexpression of Sox9 in ependymal cells or resident astrocytes might either maintain their cellular state or acquire other lineages, we established mating cross of Z/Sox9 transgenic mice with FoxJ1-CreERT2::GFP or Cx30-CreERT2 mice, creating adult mice with high levels of Sox9 expression in ependymal cells or resident astrocytes respectively upon 4-OHT treatment. By immunofluorescence and Western blot, we detected a moderate increase in the level of Sox9 protein expression from spinal cords of FoxJ1-CreERT2::GFP;Z/Sox9 mice but not from Cx30-CreERT2;Z/Sox9 mice. However, expression of ependymal markers CD133, Vimentin and neural stem cell marker Sox2 remained unaltered. We speculate that the lack of effect on ependymal markers expression could be due to subtle increase in the Sox9 expression level which did not cause dramatic change to the ependymal state. Objective 2: Assessing the fate and responses of Sox9 knockout ependymal cells and resident astrocytes in spinal cord injury (SCI) Our previous data using FoxJ1-CreERT::GFP; R26RCAG-tdtomato; Sox9flox/+ or flox/flox mice showed that Sox9 is required for proliferative and migratory wound response in vivo following SCI as well as the enhancement and maintenance of neurosphere-forming capacity of ependymal cells in vitro after SCI. Expression of markers characteristic of astrocytic scar such as CSPGs, Col2a1 and GFAP (a maker of astrocyte activation) were reduced in Sox9-/- cells and compared to Sox9+/-. However, these changes in gene expression were not accompanied by locomotor recovery. Our results differed from a previous report which show Sox9 conditional knockout mice using ubiquitous promoter-driven Cre-based recombination resulted in reduced levels of astrocytic scar markers expression that were associated with improved hind limb function and locomotor recovery following contusion SCI at T9. This could be due to compensatory contribution of glial scar from astrocytes in the parenchymal of the injured spinal cord. However, the inefficient of Cx30-CreERT; Sox9flox/flox recombination precluded us from studying the role of Sox9 depleted resident astrocytes in glial scar formation and the improvement of locomotor recovery in response to SCI. Considering the substantial amount of time and resources devoted to mice breeding and the intermittent suspension of access to the animal unit due to COVID-19 pandemic, we have focused our efforts and resources to establish and characterize SOX9 knockdown (SOX9 KD) human neural stem cells (hNSCs) in vitro and their differentiation potency after transplantation into the contusion injury rodent model of spinal cord injury as detailed below in objective 3. Objective 3: Investigating the therapeutic potential of Sox9 knockdown human NSCs in rodent SCI model Our previous data showed high level of SOX9 expression was detected in embryoid bodies (EBs) and hNSCs and overlapping expression of SOX9 and SOX2 in hNSCs, confirming neural stem cell identity of SOX9 expressing cells. After 7 days neuronal differentiation, we detected lower level of SOX9 expression in SOX2-ve cells which acquired early neuronal lineage expressing HuC/D. On day 21, SOX9 expression remained in undifferentiated hNSCs but was not detected in cells expressing pan-neuronal marker MAP2 and motor neuron maker ISLET1/2. Similar patterns of alteration were observed at the mRNA levels. These results suggest that progressive loss of SOX9 expression in hNSCs is associated with acquisition of neuronal lineage. To further examine this issue, we generated three hESC cell lines (H9, HES-2 and IMR-90) stably expressing doxycycline (Dox)-inducible short hairpin RNA against SOX9 (shSOX9) to bypass initial undesirable phenotypes and used IMR90 as a representative for the rest of the studies as the other two cell lines gave rise to the similar findings. Following treatment of different Dox concentrations (0.5 to 2.0 ug/ml) and DMSO as a control, expression levels of SOX9 mRNA and protein in hNSCs were reduced in a dose-dependent manner. We found hNSCs treated with 0.5 ug/ml (50% SOX9 gene dosage) remained viable, were able to form similar number and size of neurospheres to the control, acquired precocious pan-neuronal markers expression (NGN2 and HuC/D) and ventral motor neuron progenitor markers expression (Nkx6.1 and OLIG2) compared to the control. These changes of genes expression were accompanied by extensive neurite outgrowth and motor neuron differentiation and maturation. Moreover, SOX9 KD hNSCs can differentiate into O4+ oligodendrocytes but not astrocytes. Together, these results suggest that 50% reduction of SOX9 expression in hNSCs results in an early onset of neuronal fate biased to motor neuron lineage without altering their potency to form oligodendrocytes and inhibition of astrocyte formation. RNA-seq revealed sonic hedgehog (SHH) ligand and its downstream signaling factors were among the most upregulated genes in shSOX9-hNSCs compared to control shLuc-hNSCs, indicating an autocrine SHH signaling to promote shSOX9-hNSCs to differentiate into motor neurons. These data also imply that SOX9 has a role in maintaining human neural stem cell state and/or inhibiting neuronal/motor neuron differentiation through suppression of SHH signaling. We transplanted GFP labeled hNSCs with shLuc as control and with 50% SOX9 dosage into the epicenter of SCI rat model. After 2 months of transplantation, we observed GFP expression in both control and SOX9 KD cells at and around the lesion site, indicating graft survival. Importantly, no tumors were formed. We detected GFAP expression in the periphery of the epicenter of the formed glial scar and surrounding the shLuc graft cells, whereas shSOX9-hNSCs infiltrated into the lesion site and inhibited GFAP expression and glial scarring process. In addition, SOX9 KD hNSCs exhibited extensive axonal outgrowth whereas neurite outgrowth was barely observed in shLuc hNSCs. Consistently, SOX9 KD hNSCs showed increase expression of HuC/D, ISLET1/2 and mature motor neuron marker, choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) compared to the control. Importantly, grid walking test revealed significant improvement of locomotor recovery by SOX9 KD grafted rats whereas rats grafted with control shLuc hNSCs remained defective locomotion. Altogether, these results demonstrate the therapeutic potential of SOX9 KD hNSCs in restoring the locomotor capability of SCI rat model. All the work mentioned above was conducted by a postdoc, Jessica Aijia Liu.

17123016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123016.value: We have established collaborations with Prof Wong, Gary Ka-Leung in Department of Chemistry at Hong Kong Baptist University and Dr Law Ga-Lai in Department of Applied Biology and Chemical Technology at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University to develop SOX9 specific targeting peptide linked with a fluorescence group at the N-terminus (responsive emission upon specific binding) and the nucleus-penetrating RrRK motif at the C-terminus of the sequence. The peptides without RrRK or with mismatched peptide sequences will serve as negative controls. 17123016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123016.value: Most traumatic spinal cord injuries (SCI) lead to axonal damage, loss of motor and sensory neurons, and often results in permanent paralysis. The ineffectiveness of the current clinical management and treatment regimen put the vast majority of SCI patients with disabilities and suffering through the whole life. This is due to the formation of glial scar by SOX9+ reactive astrocytes around the injured site, which form a barrier to inhibit regrowth of spared exon through the lesion site. Although genetic ablation of SOX9 specifically in ependymal cells which contribute partly to astrocytic scar reduced glial scar markers expression, the mutant mice did not show improvement in locomotor recovery after SCI rodent suggesting a compensatory contribution of glial scar from astrocytes in the parenchymal of the injured spinal cord. Importantly, transplantation of human neural stem cells (hNSCs) with halving SOX9 gene dosage into the injured rodent spinal cord resulted in robust differentiation into motor neurons without forming glial scar at the lesion site and also improved locomotor recovery. Our findings reveal a dose-dependent role of SOX9 in controlling the onset of hNSCs lineage differentiation and its survival with half of its dosage favorable for the transplantation therapy for spinal cord injury.

17123816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123816.value: SIRT6, NAD+ dependent mono-ADP ribosylase and deacylase mediating removal of acetyl groups from histone and non-histone proteins, is involved in a broad range of biological processes such as metabolic regulation, DNA damage repair, inflammation, aging and tumor suppression. It regulates DNA-damage repair through participating in the homologous recombination (HR) and non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) and is regarded as the “Guardian of the genome”. Its activity is primarily controlled by MDM2-mediated ubiquitylation and proteosomal degradation as well as posttranslational modifications such as acetylation and phosphorylation. In response to various stresses such as irradiation, p53 is acetylated and p53 signaling pathway is activated, leading to either cell cycle arrest, or cellular senescence or apoptosis. p53 acetylation is mediated by p300/CBP, Tip60/MOF and PCAF while its deacetylation, to our understanding so far, is carried out by HDACs and SIRT1. Loss of Sirt6 in mice results in premature aging, primarily attributable to the impaired DNA-damage repair. Interestingly we found that loss of Sirt6 in mice activates p53 signaling pathway and haplodeficiency in p53 significantly ameliorate the premature aging and remarkably extends the lifespan in Sirt6 deficient mice, suggesting potential involvement of SIRT6 in the regulation of p53 signaling pathway. Further study showed that SIRT6 directly interacts with and deacetylates p53. We therefore hypothesized that (1) SIRT6 modifies p53 to maintain p53 homeostasis; (2) Loss of Sirt6 results in enhanced p53 acetylation and activated p53 signaling which in turn leads to accelerated aging. To test our hypotheses, we propose to examine how SIRT6 maintains p53 stability by determining the major types and sites of post-translational modifications on p53 protein mediated by SIRT6. In addition, we propose to examine the molecular mechanisms underlying the dramatic extension of lifespan in compound mutant mice and to determine if loss of SIRT6 deacetylase activity is responsible for the increased p53 activation and accelerated aging. The proposed study will elucidate how SIRT6 maintains the homeostasis of p53 and to reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying the lifespan extension in compound mutant mice. This study will not only provide new insights into how p53 signaling is fine turned by SIRT6 in response to stress but may also help to find novel strategy to fight against aging and cancer. SIRT6，做为NAD +依赖性单ADP ribosylase和介导组蛋白和非组蛋白除去乙酰基脱酰酶，涉及广泛的生物过程，如代谢调节，DNA损伤修复，炎症，衰老和肿瘤抑制的。它通过参与同源重组（HR）和非同源末端连接（NHEJ）调节DNA损伤修复和被视为“基因组的守护者”。其活性主要由MDM2-介导的泛素化和蛋白酶体降解以及翻译后修饰，例如乙酰化和磷酸化控制。响应于各种胁迫如照射，p53被乙酰化导致p53信号传导途径被激活，引发细胞周期停滞或细胞衰老或凋亡。 p53的乙酰化是由P300 / CBP，Tip60/MOF和PCAF介导，而其脱乙酰化，至今我们的理解，是由HDAC和SIRT1进行调节。Sirt6缺失导致的小鼠过早老化，主要是由于DNA损伤修复缺陷。有趣的是，我们发现，在缺失SIRT6小鼠中， p53信号通路激活。 p53基因缺陷显著改善Sirt6缺失导致的过早老化并能显着地延伸SIRT6缺陷小鼠的寿命，这表明在p53信号传导途径的调控SIRT6的潜在参与。进一步的研究表明，SIRT6直接结合并去乙酰化P53。因此，我们假设，（1）SIRT6修饰p53而保持p53的稳态; （2）SIRT6缺失导致p53乙酰化并激活p53信号从而导致加速老化。为了测试我们的假设，我们提出研究SIRT6如何修饰p53并保持p53稳定。此外，我们提出研究潜在的分子机制，并确定是否SIRT6脱乙酰酶活性损失导致p53活化和加速老化。本研究将阐明SIRT6如何维护p53的稳态和并揭示复合突变小鼠的寿命延长的分子机制。这项研究不仅为SIRT6如何激活p53提供新的见解，也可能有助于找到新的战略对抗衰老和癌症

17123816.label: Realisation of objectives
17123816.value: Objective 1. To determine the major types and sites of modifications on p53 protein that are modified by SIRT6 (100%) To determine the potential connection between SIRT6 and p53, we first examined the interaction between two proteins by immunoprecipitation. To determine the changes in p53 modifications, p53 protein was purified from the wild-type HEK293 cells and SIRT6-deficient HEK293 cells by CRISPR/Cas9 with ectopic p300. The protein modifications were determined and compared by MS and Western blotting using specific antibodies. The significant change was found only at K381 not other sites. This was further confirmed by Western blotting in MEFs deficient for Sirt6 derived from Sirt6 deficient mice. To further demonstrate K381 is responsible for the increased p53 levels due to enhanced protein stability, K381 and K382 mutant p53 were expressed in cells, respectively, in the presence or absence of SIRT6. We then determine how the total deacetylation is changed. Indeed, total acetylation level of p53 is only correlated with the level of K381 not any other site. Mutation at K381 diminished changed in p53 acetylation due to the loss of SIRT6 whereas mutation at K392 did not. We also checked the ADP-ribosylation of p53 and it does not seem to be affected by loss of Sirt6. In addition, No other modifications seem to be affected either examined by MS. Objective 2. To determine the contribution of up-regulation of p53 signaling to premature aging in Sirt6 deficient mice (100%) To determine the contribution of p53 signaling to the accelerated senescence and premature aging in Sirt6 deficiency, we first examined downstream targets of p53 by qPCR in the presence or absence of SIRT6. The protein level of p53 by Western blotting and qPCR in various tissues in mice were also examined and compare between wild-type and Sirt6 deficient mice. To determine whether inhibiting p53 rescues cellular senescence in Sirt6-/- MEFs, we treated Sirt6-/- MEFs and HEK293 cells deficient for SIRT6 by CRISPR/Cas9 with Pifithrin-α (a specific p53 inhibitor). The proliferation and senescence were then examined by BrdU labelling and β-Gal senescence staining. qPCR was employed to determine the transcription of p53 downstream target genes. To determine if deficiency in p53 extends lifespan of Sirt6-/- mice, we generated either Sirt6-/-p53-/- mice or Sirt6-/-p53+ /-. Their growth (body weight), mobility, lifespan, osteoporosis, muscle atrophy, hair loss, aging phenotypes) were recorded or examined. In addition, p53 deficiency on tumorigenesis in Sirt6-/- mice was also examined in the compound mutant mice to determine if the loss of Sirt6 results in genomic instability is p53 dependent. Objective 3. To investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying lifespan extension in Sirt6-/- mice by p53 deficiency (100%) We first examined DNA damage repair, cell cycle arrest, apoptosis and cellular senescence in the compound mutant mice by qPCR, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, β-Gal senescence staining and by Annexin V staining. We then examined stem cell declines in the compound mutant mice in HSCs and MSCs including the colony formation and senescence. To determine if loss of SIRT6 deacetylase activity contributes to the elevated p53, we specifically examined the acetylation of total p53 and acetylation at K381. To examine if SIRT6 directly regulates the transcription of genes in p53 signaling pathway, We performed ChIP-Seq assay using SIRT6 specific antibodies. DNA was then sent for sequencing to determine the genes/loci that directly controlled by SIRT6.

17123816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123816.value: We have determined the changes in acetylation in all potential sites on p53 and compared the levels between wild-type and SIRT6 deficient cells. This allowed us to identify Lysine381 as the major site on p53 protein which is modified by SIRT6. This modification is critical to the p53 protein stability and loss of SIRT6 resulted in increased p53 expression at posttranslational level. The significance of this deacetylation modification at K381 on p53 is mediated only by SIRT6 not by SIRT1. It is the acetylation at this site determine the total level of p53 acetylation, therefore its stability. For the first time we demonstrated that SIRT6 is the major deacetylase for p53, therefore a major regulator of p53 activity. To further determine the contribution of increased stability of p53 in senescence and premature aging in Sirt6 deficient mice, we generated the compound mutant mice which showed significant lifespan extension in Sirt6 deficient mice with haploinsufficiency of p53. However, completely depletion of p53 did not result in further rescue but leading to even short lifespan. The mechanisms for the extended lifespan was found to be correlated with the stem cell rescue and down regulation of p53 downstream targets, suggesting that the up-regulation in p53 pathway contribute significantly to the accelerated aging in Sirt6 deficient mice. Our results has been published in journal of eLife (8. Ghosh S, Wong SK, Jiang ZX, Liu B, Hao Q, Gorbunova V, Liu X, Zhou Z*. Haploinsufficiency of Trp53 dramatically extends the lifespan of Sirt6-defircient mice. eLife, 2018，DOI：10.7554/eLife.32127.001)

17123816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123816.value: The Sirt6-/-:Trp53+/- compound mutant mice live 8-14 times longer than the Sirt6 deficient mice. However, they did showed accelerated aging and retarded growth, suggesting additional mechanism other than p53 up-regulation exists. Further investigation in these compound mutant mice will reveal p53 -independent mechanism of SIRT6 in aging.

17125916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125916.value: 肝硬化現在是已發展國家中第二常見的消化系統疾病相關死亡原因。肝硬化及它的前身肝纖維化會增加門靜脈高壓相關的並發症和肝癌風險。在香港和亞太地區，慢性乙型肝炎是引致嚴重肝病的首要原因。 抗乙肝病毒藥是可以成功有效控制病毒複製,但並非每個乙肝病人會有肝纖維化逆轉.有初步臨床證據顯示肥胖及其他代謝因素會影響纖維化逆轉，但這在亞太乙肝病群中未經證實。 我們提出了一個前瞻性觀察研究，調查代謝因素如何影響乙肝服藥期間肝纖維化逆轉。利用無創肝纖維化檢查(一種非侵入性超聲技術)，我們會調查乙肝服藥期間肝纖維化逆轉率，也會評估不同代謝因素對肝纖維化逆轉的影響。這些代謝因素包括臨床因素，如體重指數, 代謝綜合徵, 及反映脂肪肝嚴重性的控制衰減參數。也包括實驗室的標誌物，如胰島素抵抗（HOMA-IR）及不同血清脂肪因子。透過3年期的前瞻性跟進，我們將確定代謝因素是否影響肝纖維化逆轉率。 這研究將提供寶貴的臨床數據及可以透過代謝因素的控制優化慢性乙肝的治療，減少肝硬化相關的並發症和肝癌。

17125916.label: Realisation of objectives
17125916.value: As from our published article Mak LY et al. Liver International 2019, we were able to achieve the primary objectives. We determined the association of different metabolic parameters with persistent fibrosis or lack of fibrosis reversal, including body mass index, diabetes mellitus, and also a high serum adipocyte fatty acid-binding protein (AFABP) and low serum fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21). Hepatic steatosis as determined by controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) measurements via transient elastography was not a significant factor. Via multivariate analysis, we determined the odds ratio and 95% confidence intervals of body mass index, diabetes mellitus, serum AFABP and serum FGF21, demonstrating the relatives strengths of association. We also determined a synergistic effect of different factors: With a high body mass index, presence of diabetes and a high AFABP, the odds ratio of persistent fibrosis (lack of fibrosis reversal) was 3.712 (95%CI 1.36-38.1). From our cohort of 415 patients, after a median nucleoside analogue treatment duration of 6.2 years, 264 (63.6%) no longer had severe fibrosis / cirrhosis, while persistent severe fibrosis / cirrhosis was still noted in 151 (36.4%) of patients. We have hence achieved the various study objectives of this project.

17125916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125916.value: Concerning major findings, a total of 415 patients [mean age 59.6 years, 71.6% male, median treatment duration 6.2 years] were recruited. Patients with F3/F4 (N = 151) had lower FGF‐21 (11.7 vs 13.6 pg/mL, P = 0.055), higher AFABP (126.8 vs 84.1 pg/mL, P < 0.001) and HOMA‐IR (7.1 vs 5.1, P = 0.004) levels compared to those without F3/F4 (N = 264). Multivariate analysis showed that FGF‐21 level was associated with hepatic steatosis (OR 1.005, 95% CI 1.001‐1.009) and F3/F4 (OR 0.993, 95% CI 0.989‐0.998), while AFABP level (OR 1.001, 95% CI 1‐1.002), body mass index (BMI) (OR 1.107, 95% CI 1.037‐1.182) and presence of diabetes mellitus (OR 2.059, 95% CI 1.206‐3.516) were associated with F3/F4. With the combined presence of BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2, diabetes and AFABP > 105.9 pg/mL, the odds ratio for F3/F4 was 3.712 (95% CI 1.364‐10.105, P = 0.010). To conclude, a low FGF‐21 and high AFABP levels were associated with advanced fibrosis/ cirrhosis in CHB patients on antiviral treatment. Plasma AFABP, together with other metabolic risk factors, may aid identification of patients lacking fibrosis improvement during nucleoside analogue therapy.

17125916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125916.value: Serum AFABP elevation can be secondary to incrased hepatic production of AFABP by Kupffer cells, leading to a heightened inflammatory response and fibrosis in the liver. Low FGF21 can be secondary to reduce synthetic function of the liver in advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis. These hypothesis will need confirmation in mechanistic studies involving models combining HBV infection with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

17126216.label: Realisation of objectives
17126216.value: Objective 1. Functional characterization of Cripto-1 in HCC Endogenous Cripto-1 expression was examined in a panel of HCC cells by western blot including SMMC7721, BEL7402, Huh7, Hep3B, HepG2, PLC/PRF/5, MHCC97L, MHCC97H and also immortalized liver cell line LO2. LO2, Hep3B, HepG2 and SMMC7721 showed minimal expression of Cripto-1, while a relatively high expression was detected in Huh7, PLC/PRF/5, MHCC97L and MHCC97H. With reference to the relative endogenous expression, stable Cripto-1 knockdown clones were established with Huh7 and PLC/PRF/5 with shRNA approach, and stable overexpression clone was established with Hep3B. Efficiency of knockdown or overexpression was confirmed by both qPCR and western blotting. Expression of a number of stemness genes and chemoresistance-related genes was examined by qPCR in the knockdown clones including BMI-1, CD24, CD133, NANOG, NOTCH1, OCT4, SOX2, ABCB1, ABCG2, ABCC6. We then proceeded to perform in vitro functional assays to interrogate the effects of Cripto-1 manipulation in HCC cells. Cell proliferation, migration and invasion assays were performed. The self-renewal ability was tested by tumorsphere formation assay with serial passages; the number of tumorspheres were measured at experimental endpoint. Besides, we examined the effect on chemosensitivity of HCC cells toward cisplatin and sorafenib upon altered expression of Cripto-1 by means of Annexin V apoptosis assay. The same assay was also performed with sorafenib-resistant HCC cells. The regulatory role of Cripto-1 in tumor growth and stemness properties of HCC in vivo was investigated using NOD/SCID mouse model with serial transplantation in a limiting dilution approach (500 cells and 1000 cells). Tumor incidence, tumor mass, latency period and estimated T-IC frequency were compared between control and knockdown groups at experimental endpoint. In vivo effects on metastatic potential was studied using both orthotopic liver injection model and tail vein injection model with NOD/SCID mice using luciferase-tagged HCC cells. The study on this objective was accomplished. Objective 2. Delineation of molecular mechanisms of Cripto-1 in HCC To delineate the molecular mechanism mediating the effect of Cripto-1 in HCC, we examined the expression of key molecular targets of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway upon manipulated Cripto-1 expression, which include β-catenin (nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions by western blotting), c-myc and axin2 by qPCR. The pathway activity was measured with TOP/FOPFlash reporter assay. To ascertain that the stemness properties endowed by Cripto-1 were mediated through Wnt/β-catenin signaling, we carried out rescue experiments through stable expression of constitutively active β-catenin in Cripto-1 silenced HCC cells (both Huh7 and PLC/PRF/5 cell lines). Reinforcement of β-catenin expression and activity was confirmed by western blotting and TOP/FOPFlash reporter assay, respectively. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments were carried out (tumorsphere assay and subcutaneous injection assay with 1000 cells and 5000 cells). Next, we further explored how Cripto-1 regulates the Wnt/β-catenin pathway by examining the expression of DVL3 at mRNA and protein levels upon manipulation of Cripto-1 in HCC cells. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments were then performed using anti-Cripto-1 and anti-FZD7 for pulldown. in attempt to identify the binding interaction among Cripto-1, Dishevelled-3 (DVL3), FZD7/LRP6. Lastly, we interrogated the mechanism through which Cripto-1 increase the protein expression of DVL3 by cycloheximide chase assay using Cripto-1 overexpression and EV Hep3B cells. The study on this objective was accomplished. Objective 3. Validation of in vitro and in vivo findings in HCC clinical samples Cripto-1 expression was evaluated in our in-house RNA sequencing data, in-house primary HCC clinical cohort (77 cases) and the TCGA database. Correlation with clinicopathological parameters was carried out with our in-house cohort. β-catenin immunostaining was performed in the primary HCC cohort. Separate cohorts of dysplastic nodules as well as paired primary and metastatic HCC samples were stained for Cripto-1 by immunohistochemistry and analyzed by a pathologist. Appropriate positive and negative controls were used for IHC staining. Staining was scored in a semi-quantitative manner according to the percentage of the tumor cells showing positive staining. Correlation between Cripto-1 and NANOG or AXIN2 mRNA expressions was performed with the in-house cohort and TCGA dataset. Correlation between Cripto-1 expression and methylation status of its promoter region in the TCGA database was carried out. Cripto-1 transcript level in low-expressing HCC cell line (Hep3B) was compared with and without 5-Aza’ treatment. The study on this objective was accomplished. Majority of works carried out on this project has been published in: Cripto-1 contributes to stemness in hepatocellular carcinoma by stabilizing Dishevelled-3 and activating Wnt/β-catenin pathway. Cell Death Differ. 2018 Aug;25(8):1426-1441. [Impact factor 2019 -10.7]

17126216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126216.value: Objective 1. Upon silencing of Cripto-1, stemness markers and chemoresistance-related genes were downregulated. Silencing of Cripto-1 suppressed HCC cell proliferation, migration and invasion, tumorsphere formation, and increased the proportion of HCC cells in apoptotic phase upon treatment with sorafenib or cisplatin. Knockdown of Cripto-1 re-sensitized sorafenib-resistant BEL-7402 cells towards sorafenib. Forced expression of Cripto-1 enhanced self-renewal in vitro increased chemoresistance of HCC cells. In vivo, knockdown of Cripto-1 suppressed tumorigenicity in both primary and secondary animal recipients. With orthotopic implantation assay, a decrease in incidence of lung metastasis was observed upon Cripto-1 knockdown (shCtrl: 4/8 versus shCripto-1: 1/8). A similar result was observed with tail vein injection model (shCtrl: 5/6 versus shCripto-1: 3/5). Objective 2. Knockdown of Cripto-1 downregulated β-catenin expression in total cell lysate and nuclear fraction, while forced expression of Cripto-1 enhanced β-catenin expression, accompanied by corresponding alterations in TOP/FOPFlash reporter assay readouts and expressions of AXIN2 and C-MYC. The functional effects on in vitro self-renewal and in vivo tumorigenicity upon silencing of Cripto-1 were partially rescued by forced expression of β-catenin. Cripto-1 positively regulated the protein expression of DVL3 while it did not significantly alter its mRNA level. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments showed that Cripto-1 bound to DVL3 in both Cripto-1-overexpressing HEK293 cells and parental Huh7 cells. A binding interaction between Cripto-1 and FZD7/LRP was also observed. By cycloheximide chase assay, DVL3 protein degradation was slowed down upon Cripto-1 overexpression. Objective 3. From our in-house RNA-sequencing data and TCGA database, Cripto-1 was upregulated in HCC tissues. High Cripto-1 expression was associated with poorer 5-year and 10-year disease-free survival in our in-house cohort. Fifty percent (7/14) of the dysplastic nodules showed focal Cripto-1 expression; 66.7% (16/24) and 79.1% (19/24) primary and metastatic HCC samples expressed Cripto-1 respectively. Staining score in the metastasis was higher than the paired primary tissue in 37.5% cases, suggesting that Cripto-1 overexpression is possibly implicated in HCC metastasis. Nuclear expression of β-catenin was detected in 17% cases, among which 56% was associated with Cripto-1 overexpression in tumor tissue. From our analysis of both in-house and TCGA cohorts, expressions of Cripto-1 and AXIN2 were positively correlated, but not with NANOG. Analysis of TCGA showed a negative correlation between the DNA methylation status of Cripto-1 promoter and Cripto-1 expression in HCC. 5-Aza’ treatment to Hep3B cells remarkably restored Cripto-1 mRNA expression. A list of miRNAs potentially regulating Cripto-1 expression in HCC was identified with computational analyses.

17126216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126216.value: Deregulation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling cascade is a key molecular event in liver cancer. Modulators of the pathway hence carries potential clinical significance in the treatment of liver cancer. Findings from this study open up new perspectives in targeting Cripto-1 in HCC to modulate Wnt/β-catenin activity and stemness properties in HCC. These targeted therapies could take the forms of specific monoclonal antibodies, anti-sense oligonucleotide or novel biotechnologies such as aptamers. Hence further works could be done to specifically study the therapeutic effects of combined anti-Cripto-1 and immune-checkpoint inhibitors therapy. Notably, activation of the Wnt/β-catenin was found in recent years to be tightly associated with immune-cold tumor microenvironment and poor clinical response to immune-checkpoint inhibitors. From a basic science perspective, further works on the mechanistic delineation of Cripto-1 in Wnt/β-catenin pathway, in particularly on the formation of signalosomes, could be a rewarding research direction. The clinical relevance could be further investigated by incorporating Cripto-1 expression in a multi-marker panel in the prognostication of HCC and investigation of serum Cripto-1 as a biomarker for HCC patients.

17126216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126216.value: Our findings in the present study suggest that Cripto-1 binds to DVL3 and FZD7/LRP6, stabilizes DVL3 protein and activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling. The chain of molecular events triggered by Cripto-1 altogether augments HCC stemness. By in vitro experiments, Cripto-1 fostered cell proliferation, migration and invasion. It also enhanced self-renewal ability and conferred chemoresistance of HCC cells. Consistently, silencing of Cripto-1 suppressed in vivo tumorigenicity and self-renewal. On downstream signaling mechanism, expression of major components of Wnt/β-catenin pathway β-catenin, AXIN2 and C-MYC, accompanied by β-catenin activity, was reduced upon Cripto-1 knockdown. The suppressive effects on stemness properties with Cripto-1 knockdown in vitro and in vivo were partially rescued by forced expression of constitutively active β-catenin. Further elucidation revealed the binding of Cripto-1 to Frizzled-7 (FZD7), low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 6 (LRP6) and Dishevelled-3 (DVL3) of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway and stabilized DVL3 protein. Analyses with clinical samples validated Cripto-1 overexpression in HCC tissues. High Cripto-1 level in tumor was associated with poorer disease-free survival of HCC patients. Taken together, our study findings substantiated the role of Cripto-1 in determining stemness phenotypes of HCC through modulating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling cascade, one of the most frequently deregulated pathways in liver cancer.

17128816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128816.value: The ability to associate danger with environmental stimuli is essential for animal survival, while adapting to new rules is equally important. Here we will use fear conditioning and extinction as learning paradigms to investigate how learning and unlearning of fear toward auditory cue affect the auditory cortex circuitry by studying dendritic spine plasticity. Despite the previous understanding that the functional organization of tonotopic map is smooth and continuous in the primary auditory cortex, recent findings by two-photon microscopy showed that it is actually fractured with mixed frequency response on cellular level (1, 2). Nonetheless, how fear learning affects structural and functional plasticity of the auditory cortex on dendritic branch and synaptic level is largely unknown. Our previous findings show that fear learning and unlearning induce reversible dendritic spine plasticity in the frontal association cortex in a cue- and location-specific manner (3). We hypothesize that the location- and cue-specific reversible dendritic spine plasticity we observed in the frontal cortex in fear learning and unlearning also applies to the auditory cortex. Furthermore, we hypothesize that frequency specific input induces functional plasticity of individual dendritic spines and leads to the location- and cue-specific structural plasticity on dendritic branches. To test these hypotheses, we aim to determine the structural and functional plasticity of dendritic spines in the mouse auditory cortex. First, we will determine the structural plasticity of dendritic spines in response to fear conditioning and fear extinction by in vivo transcranial two-photon imaging in Thy1-YFP transgenic mice. We will investigate the effects of cue-specific fear extinction and reconditioning on the dendritic spine plasticity reversibility by examining the spatial distribution of dendritic spine plasticity on the individual dendritic branches. Second, we will use calcium imaging to investigate the functional plasticity of individual dendritic spines in the auditory cortex and the axonal projections from the auditory thalamus in awake behaving mice in response to conditioned stimulus and other frequency tone to compare their tuning properties. Third, we will further probe the underlying mechanism of cue-specific associative learning by manipulating the activity of principle neurons of auditory thalamus output to the auditory cortex at specific timing during CS presentation by optogenetics to study its effect on the location- and cue-specific dendritic spine plasticity. Taken together, our work will provide important insights into the basic mechanisms of associative fear learning and unlearning, which could help to better understand psychiatric disorder such as post-traumatic stress disorder. 危險與環境刺激關聯的能力是動物的生存關鍵，同時動物適應新的規則的能力也同樣重要。我們將使用恐懼學習和恐懼消退的學習範例研究聽覺恐懼學習和消退如何通過樹突棘的可塑性影響聽覺皮層迴路。恐懼學習如何影響聽覺皮層的結構與功能的樹突棘可塑性是知之甚少。我們假設我們之前在額葉皮層中觀察到的樹突地點和聲音頻率線索的特異性也適用於聽覺皮層。為了驗證這些假設，我們的目標是研究小鼠聽覺皮層樹突棘的結構和功能的可塑性。我們將使用Thy1-YFP轉基因小鼠，通過雙光子成像研究恐懼學習和恐懼消退對樹突棘結構可塑性的應響。我們亦會使用鈣成像研究樹突棘和聽覺丘腦軸突的功能可塑性。我們的工作將提供對關聯學習和消退的基本機制重要的見解，這將有助於更好地了解精神疾病如創傷後應激障礙或焦慮。

17131816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17131816.value: Our goal is to find keys to expand the neuronal repertoire/capacity for plasticity of sensorimotor circuits in adult life. Our pilot study of the vestibular circuitry for spatial navigation found behavioral performance (dead reckoning) of adult rats as normal following chronic dosing of the animals with the antidepressant fluoxetine (a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor). This drug also stimulated increase in the number of new parvalbumin (PV)/gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-expressing neurons in the vestibular nucleus (VN). Blockade of GABA-mediated effects in the adult VN during fluoxetine dosing led to derangement in dead reckoning among the animals, similar to that observed in neonatal rats that had been subjected to similar blockade but without fluoxetine dosing. The results suggest that the new PV neurons in the VN are no bystanders, but are involved in re-opening a plastic period for tuning/re-setting sensitivity of the VN circuit according to experience in this plastic period. We therefore hypothesize that integration of new PV neurons in the VN is key to tuning/re-setting synaptic plasticity and sensitivity of the vestibular circuit for coping with spatial recognition and navigation. We aim (1) to enhance generation of PV neurons in adult rats with relevant dosing of fluoxetine; (2) to show that plasticity of the vestibular circuit is enhanced by GABA-mediated integration of new PV neurons; (3) to demonstrate spatial navigation as a functional outcome of integration of new PV neurons the vestibular circuit. Results will (i) provide pointers to tune GABAergic transmission in PV neurons for turning on plasticity in the existing circuit and (ii) reveal the mechanisms that underlie functional wiring of inhibitory neuron networks both during development and in the adult stage. We expect findings to apply across complex vital hindbrain and spinal cord circuitries where the local inhibitory networks are subject to tuning in therapeutic and training paradigms with prospects for improvements in posttraumatic recovery and rehabilitation.

17131816.label: Realisation of objectives
17131816.value: Objective 1: To enhance generation of PV neurons with relevant dosing of fluoxetine. 1.1 We optimized the fluoxetine (FLX) dosing conditions for inducing adult neurogenesis in both rats and mice. 1.2 Adult neurogenesis in the brainstem was demonstrated by colocalization of BrdU staining of proliferative cells and the neuronal marker NeuN. 1.3 Ependymal/ subependymal cells lining the fourth ventricle on the dorsal surface of the vestibular nucleus (VN) were labelled using AAV carrying mCherry expression plasmid or in a transgenic mouse for lineage tracing. Subsequent FLX dosing resulted in migration of a small number of these labelled cells into the VN. 1.4 We show that 5-HT1A receptors act as a gain modulator in mature VN circuits. Direct infusion of specific 5-HT1 receptor agonist into the VN concurrent with FLX-dosing further revealed 5-HT1 receptor as a key receptor for inducing adult neurogenesis. Objective 2: To show that plasticity of the vestibular circuit is enhanced by GABA-mediated integration of new PV neurons. 2.1 Local inhibition of GABAergic transmission in the neonatal rat VN with bicuculline (BIC), the specific GABAA receptor antagonist, affected induction probability of long-term depression in GABAergic transmission (LTD-GABA) and excitation-inhibition (E/I) ratio. This resulted in long-lasting deficits in vestibular function as evidenced by delayed emergence of vestibular reflexes and irrecoverable derangement in navigation performance in adulthood. Such deficits are not seen when BIC is applied to the consolidated VN circuits in the young adult stage. 2.2 FLX dosing in young adult rodents enhanced vestibular circuit plasticity by increasing LTD-GABA back to neonatal-like levels in VN neurons. Neonatal-like sensitivity to perturbation in GABAergic neurotransmission was restored in young adult rodents with FLX-treated. Blockade of GABAergic neurotransmission using BIC in young adult rodents resulted in long-lasting deficits in vestibular function. 2.3 Connectivity of PV neurons in the VN were revealed by mono-transsynaptic anterograde tracing by modified Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV). Objective 3: To demonstrate spatial navigation as a functional outcome of integration of new PV neurons into the vestibular circuit. 3.1 Both chemogenetic activation and inhibition of PV neuron firing in VN resulted in navigational deficits in control rats. This demonstrated that relevant firing of PV neurons is crucial for function of VN circuits for navigation. 3.2 We harnessed FLX-induced plasticity and robust vestibular stimuli to correct navigational deficits generated by neonatal exposure to BIC at P1. Optogenetic-coupled whole-cell patch-clamp recording in VN output neurons of PV-Cre mice was used to discern the synaptic basis for such rehabilitation. Results revealed significant change in connectivity between VN output neurons and PV neurons within the VN after BIC-treatment at P1, and in mice after rehabilitation of vestibular function with FLX + stimuli treatment.

17131816.value: Oral dosing of the antidepressant fluoxetine resulted in newborn neurons in the adult brainstem. Results thus open new avenues for lifelong learning and for the development of therapeutic strategies against neurodegenerative disease by stimulating the otherwise dormant self renewal capacity of the adult brain.

17135816.value: 驅動蛋白KIF5B對神經元樹突中mRNA運輸作用的研究

17135816.label: Project Objectives
17135816.value: To identify and validate the mRNAs that are differentially expressed in the synaptoneurosome of KIF5B heterozygous mice To verify the differential localization and transport of specific mRNAs in KIF5B-knockdown or KIF5B heterozygous neurons
rows: To identify and validate the mRNAs that are differentially expressed in the synaptoneurosome of KIF5B heterozygous mice
To verify the differential localization and transport of specific mRNAs in KIF5B-knockdown or KIF5B heterozygous neurons

17135816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17135816.value: Neuron in the brain is highly polarized and contains structurally distinct subcellular compartments, such as the axon terminal and the dendritic spines, which serve radically different functions. This subcellular division of labor is fundamental to information processing in the brain, and depends on the unique local protein compositions in different compartments. Although the classic view is that proteins are synthesized in the cell body and then selectively transported to different subcellular regions, compartment-specific protein composition can also result from asymmetric targeting of mRNAs and local protein synthesis. Translation of mRNAs occurs locally near synapses and is essential for the proper development and functioning of the brain. For synaptic protein synthesis to occur, specific subsets of mRNAs must first be carried to distal dendrites, and this can be achieved through transport along the microtubules by molecular motors. Many key questions on RNA trafficking in neurons remain unanswered. For example, which mRNAs are carried to the synapses, and whether different molecular motors are involved in the transport of different mRNAs that show distinct motility and destination? There are numerous motor proteins for intracellular transport, and one of them is KIF5B. Our preliminary findings revealed that the number and motility of RNA granules in neuronal processes were significantly altered in primary neurons derived from KIF5B heterozygous mice. These observations prompt us to hypothesize that KIF5B may be crucial for the transport and localization of specific subsets of mRNAs near synapses. To test this hypothesis, we will examine the synaptic localization and motility of RNA granules in neurons isolated from control and KIF5B heterozygous mice. By comparing the synaptic transcriptome of wild-type and KIF5B heterozygous mice using RNA sequencing, we aim to identify the mRNAs whose synaptic localization depends on KIF5B. In situ hybridization and live imaging will be performed to verify the role of different KIF5 homologs on the localization and motility of selected candidate mRNAs. The proposed study will substantially increase our understanding on mRNA transport mechanism in neurons by delineating the role of specific molecular motors in transporting distinct mRNAs. The identification of synaptically-localized mRNAs should also uncover novel molecular players that control synapse function. Given the emerging importance of local protein synthesis and its dysfunction in brain disorders, the current study will provide significant insights into brain function in both normal and diseased states.

17135816.label: Realisation of objectives
17135816.value: Objective 1: In this objective, we aim to identify mRNAs that show relative enrichment at neuronal synapses, and determine whether the synaptic transcriptome is affected in KIF5B-depleted neurons. We set up a protocol to extract total RNA from synaptoneurosome (SNS), which contains vesicularized pre- and postsynaptic components to retain the local RNAs. Quality of the SNS was validated by the enrichment of synaptic protein PSD-95 and the absence of nuclear protein RNMT. Total RNA was then extracted from the SNS and crude homogenate from two wild-type and three Kif5b+/- littermates, and the samples were subjected to high-throughput polyA paired-end RNAseq. Over 90% of filtered reads were mapped to the reference genome. We first focused on the SNS of wild-type mice to identify transcripts that showed synaptic enrichment. Genes with transcript per million (TPM) lower than 1 in either of the two biological replicates were eliminated, and only protein-coding genes were analyzed. Based on these criteria, transcripts of 12,789 genes and 11,608 genes were detected in Homogenate and SNS, respectively. After excluding non-neuronal transcripts, there were 6,090 genes detected in the SNS, with 1,723 being relatively enriched (FDR < 0.05) in the SNS compared to homogenate from the same mice. Ontologies related to synapse structure and function are preferentially enriched in those transcripts with highest SNS/homo ratios. About 66% of the SNS-enriched transcripts overlap with the previously reported hippocampal neuropil mRNAs, while the remaining 492 genes represent novel transcripts in the synaptic transcriptome identified by our study, including 12 encoding presynaptic proteins and 17 encoding postsynaptic proteins. One of the novel synaptic transcripts, C1qtnf4, was selected for validation of localization by high resolution single molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization (smFISH). We detected the localization of C1qtnf4 puncta in both proximal and distal dendrites of hippocampal neurons. By unraveling additional dendritic mRNAs not previously reported, our RNAseq data expands the scope of local translation for synaptic proteins. To confirm the synaptic localization of mRNAs, we selected five different transcripts for dual-colored smFISH followed by immunocytochemistry with anti-MAP2 antibody on dissociated hippocampal neurons. All five mRNAs are previously detected in the neuropil and encode PSD proteins, but they show different enrichment in SNS based on our RNAseq data. Notably, smFISH revealed that these five transcripts had diverse distribution in dendrites. The SNS-enriched transcripts Apc and Homer2 showed more distal distribution to dendrites (> 100 microns from soma) as compared to the non-enriched transcripts Homer1 and Strn4, which were more prominent in proximal dendrites (< 25 microns from soma). We further investigated their localization in dendritic spines after transfecting the hippocampal neurons with GFP. Consistent with our RNAseq data, much higher fractions of Apc and Homer2 mRNAs were localized at dendritic spine head than Homer1. The number of Homer1 and Homer2 puncta was similar in the dendrites, suggesting that the difference in synaptic localization is not attributed to expression level but more likely due to difference in targeting sequences or secondary structures. Our results suggest that mRNA localization at dendritic spine may represent a post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism that allows fine-tuning of the composition of individual synapses through local synaptic translation in response to specific stimuli. Next, we investigate the importance of KIF5B on RNA transport by comparing the synaptic transcriptome of Kif5b heterozygous-knockout mouse (referred to as “KO” thereafter) with that of wild-type littermates based on our RNAseq dataset. Over 12,000 transcripts and 24,000 transcript isoforms were detected in both the wild-type and KO homogenate; while over 11,000 transcripts and 18,000 transcript isoforms were detected in the SNS of both genotypes. The number of transcripts and transcript isoforms were similar between genotypes. Reduction of KIF5B by about 50% in the heterozygous KO mice did not disrupt the general synaptic transcriptome, but enrichment of specific transcripts in SNS was altered in the KIF5B KO mice. Differential expression analysis between genotypes showed that 219 transcript isoforms were differentially expressed (FDR ≤ 0.05) in the SNS samples; while their expression was not significantly changed in the homogenate between genotypes. These represent the putative transcripts whose transport in neuron might be disrupted upon KIF5B depletion. To understand whether these regulated transcripts perform specific biological functions, DAVID functional clustering analysis was carried out on the genes either significantly upregulated or downregulated in SNS but not significantly different in Homogenate. Functional terms related to “transmembrane” and “glycosylation” were found to be enriched in the transcript isoforms that were up-regulated in the SNS of Kif5b KO mice. For the transcript isoforms that were down-regulated in the SNS of Kif5b KO mice, functions related to cytoskeleton and transcription were specifically enriched. The mRNA that showed the greatest reduction in the SNS of Kif5b KO mice was Arf4, which encodes the small GTPase ADP-ribosylation factor 4and has been implicated in dendritic spine development of neuron. Our RNAseq data therefore suggests that KIF5B depletion may have an isoform-specific regulation mechanism on transcripts related to synapse development and organization of cytoskeleton. Objective 2 To examine the role of KIF5B in dendritic mRNA transport, we employ shRNA-mediated knockdown of KIF5B in dissociated hippocampal neurons. We demonstrated that the specific knockdown of KIF5B but not the homologous KIF5A significantly reduced the mature mushrooms spines, and rescue experiments with RNAi-resistant constructs confirmed the non-overlapping functions of the two kinesin motors. Electrophysiological recording of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents validated the decrease in synaptic transmission upon knockdown of KIF5B but not KIF5A. We then focus on the RNA-binding protein FMRP which causes Fragile-X syndrome and is required for dendritic spine maturation. We performed pull-down experiments to show that KIF5B binds significantly better than KIF5A. To ask whether KIF5B might selectively regulate FMRP transport, we performed rapid time-lapse live imaging (1 second per imaging interval) of GFP-tagged FMRP in hippocampal neurons using spinning disk confocal microscope. Consistent with previous study on the trafficking of RBPs, most FMRP granules were either stationary or exhibiting oscillatory movement, with only a small proportion showing unidirectional or bidirectional movement. Compared to control shRNA, knockdown of KIF5B significantly reduced the density of GFP-FMRP granules on dendrites. However, only the density of stationary but not motile granules was significantly decreased. In contrast, KIF5A knockdown increased the density of motile granules but decreased that of stationary granules, hence no net change in the number of total dendritic GFP-FMRP granules. To determine whether KIF5A and KIF5B differentially regulates dendritic mRNA transport, the localization of Camk2a and Grin2b which are mRNA cargoes of FMRP, was examined by smFISH. Consistent with the GFP-FMRP data, knockdown of KIF5B but not KIF5A also significantly reduced the density of both Camk2a and Grin2b mRNA puncta on dendrites. Our findings demonstrate differential functions of the two kinesin motors in dendritic RNA transport, with KIF5B participate in the formation of FMRP granules while KIF5A is involved in fine-tuning the motility of RNA granules. Given that dendritic mRNA transport is implicated in spine remodeling and synaptic plasticity, we address whether KIF5B depletion affects dendritic spines in vivo. By generating conditional knockout mice that led to late-onset depletion of KIF5B in the forebrain, we found that the number of dendritic spines was significantly reduced only in neurons in the hippocampus but not prefrontal cortex. Electrophysiological recordings further demonstrated that KIF5B conditional knockout mice exhibit reduced excitatory synaptic transmission and long-term potentiation in hippocampal neurons.

17135816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17135816.value: A subset of mRNAs are delivered to dendrites for local protein synthesis that is important for synaptic function. How mRNA trafficking is mediated in neuron remain incompletely understood. The motor protein kinesin carries cargoes along microtubule. The kinesin I family consisting of KIF5A, KIF5B and KIF5C are implicated in RNA transport, but their functional specificity is not clear. We show that selectively knocking down KIF5B, not KIF5A, reduces dendritic spine number and excitatory synaptic transmission of hippocampal neurons. The two KIF5s bind differentially to the RNA-binding protein FMRP. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirms reduced localization of the FMRP cargoes Camk2a and Grin2b mRNAs in dendrites upon KIF5B knockdown. Live-imaging shows that KIF5B is crucial for FMRP granules formation, while KIF5A regulates their motility in dendrite. The role of KIF5B in RNA transport is further examined by studying the transcriptome of synaptoneurosome (SNS) from wild-type and Kif5B heterozygous knockout mice using high throughput RNA sequencing, which identifies 219 transcripts differentially expressed in the SNS of Kif5B heterozygous mice. Finally, forebrain-specific Kif5B conditional knockout mice exhibit dendritic spine deficits and memory impairment. Together our findings demonstrate non-redundant functions of KIF5A and KIF5B and provide compelling evidence for the importance of KIF5B in dendritic RNA transport. Majority of these findings is published in eLife. With thousands of transcripts present in axons and dendrites, one key question is whether they exhibit selectivity in localization. Based on our RNAseq data, we identify 1,723 mRNAs being more abundant in the SNS than homogenate and represent putative synapse-enriched transcripts. 492 of these are novel synaptic transcripts not previously reported. Single molecule FISH on dissociated hippocampal neurons show that two SNS-enriched mRNAs, Apc and Homer2, are transported more distally in dendrites and more abundant in dendritic spines than the non-enriched transcript Homer1. These findings reveal the heterogeneity of dendritic mRNAs and raises the interesting possibility that synaptic localization represents an under-studied post-transcriptional mechanism to regulate individual synapse composition. Manuscript reporting these findings is under preparation and attached with the report. Related to this project, we have characterized dendritic mRNAs that encode novel synaptic signaling proteins (Striatin-4, PRMT8 and TBC1D24). These studies are published in J. Biol. Chem., Cell Reports and PLoS Genetics, respectively. Moreover, manuscript on a collaborative study on how m6A methylation regulates the expression of the dendritic mRNA Apc and function of its encoded protein has been deposited in bioRxiv.

17135816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17135816.value: We have identified 492 novel mRNAs in our study of the synaptic transcriptome. Based on previous proteomic studies, 29 of them encode proteins located at synapses. Many of these proteins have unknown function in the brain, and it would be of immense interest to study their function at synapses. One of them is C1QTNF4, which is known to regulate inflammation and energy metabolism. Using single molecule FISH, we have validated the localization of the C1qtnf4 mRNA in distal dendrites of hippocampal neurons. It was recently demonstrated that maternal complement factor C1q is associated with Schizophrenia, which involves impaired synapse development and function. Further investigation on the synaptic role of C1QTNF4 in the brain may provide new insights on the molecular basis of the disorder. Despite the implication of local synaptic translation in the brain, whether and how selective mRNAs are delivered to neuronal synapses has not been addressed. Our RNAseq data and FISH validation of selective mRNAs provide new evidence of the heterogeneous synaptic localization of mRNAs. The numerous SNS-enriched transcripts identified by us will be valuable for future bioinformatics investigation to identify potential cis-acting elements and the molecular basis underlying the selective mRNA transport.

17135816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17135816.value: Transporting proteins within a neuron is daunting because of the long length of neuronal processes called axon and dendrite. One alternative way to enable the availability of proteins at distal sites is to transport mRNAs along these processes by motor proteins called kinesin, after which the mRNAs can be translated to make proteins locally. Deficiency of mRNA transport may decay neuronal connections (the synapses) and impair learning and memory. While a neuron has up to 45 different kinesin motors, whether each one performs a distinct task is unclear. We have studied two similar kinesins, KIF5A and KIF5B, in rodent neurons. When KIF5A and KIF5B were depleted separately from neurons extracted from brain region called hippocampus, only removing KIF5B interfered with the formation of neuronal connections. The two kinesins differentially affect the trafficking of a RNA-binding protein called FMRP, whose deficiency causes autism and intellectual disability. Depletion of KIF5B leads to fewer delivery of FMRP-binding mRNAs to dendrites. High-throughput sequencing further identified the differential mRNAs in synapses between the control and KIF5B-depleted mice. Our findings provide new insights into the functional diversity of motor proteins and how RNA is transported in neuron, which are crucial for maintaining neuronal connections and learning/memory.

17138616.label: Project Objectives
17138616.value: We aim at a series of technical developments to further refine the design of DW-Propeller-EPI pulse sequence with less susceptibility to cardiac motion for acquiring liver DWI under free-breathing condition. First, we plan to develop a DW-Propeller-EPI pulse sequence compatible with oblique plane and off-centre FOV acquisition on clinical MRI scanner. Second, we plan to integrate VC diffusion preparation into developed DW-Propeller-EPI pulse sequence to enable the compensation of signal dropout due to cardiac motion in liver DWI. We plan to develop a reconstruction algorithm for free-breathing liver DW-Propeller-EPI data, to eliminate the need of extra reference scan time and the image blurring due to respiratory motion. Since DW-Propeller-EPI also suffers from Nyquist ghost artifact as well as DW-EPI, a reference-free ghost removal method, phase cycled reconstruction (PCR), will be applied to each blade data prior to Propeller-EPI reconstruction. Afterward, the motion correction steps will be embedded into Propeller-EPI reconstruction to accommodate the data set acquired under free-breathing condition. We will assess the image quality and measure apparent diffusion coefficient value of free-breathing DW-Propeller-EPI. For the qualitative assessment, the free-breathing liver DW-Propeller-EPI image will be compared to three routine liver DWI methods (i.e., breath-hold DW-EPI, free-breathing DW-EPI, and respiratory-triggered DW-EPI) in terms of distortion and signal dropout. For the quantitative assessment of free-breathing DW-Propeller-EPI, the SNR, measured ADC value, and reproducibility of ADC measurement will be evaluated.
