17142516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17142516.value: Epigenetic alterations immensely contributed to human carcinogenesis. Conventional epigenetic studies predominantly focused on DNA methylation, histone modifications, and chromatin remodeling. Recently, diverse and reversible chemical modifications on RNAs emerge as a new layer of epigenetic regulation. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most abundant chemical modification on eukaryotic mRNA and is important to the regulation of mRNA stability, splicing, and translation. Using transcriptome sequencing, we discovered that METTL3 (methyltransferase like 3), a major RNA N6-adenosine methyltransferase, was significantly up-regulated in human hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and multiple solid tumors. Clinically, overexpression of METTL3 was associated with poor prognosis of HCC patients. Functionally, we proved that knockdown of METTL3 drastically reduced HCC cell proliferation, migration, and colony formation in vitro. Knockout of METTL3 remarkably suppressed HCC tumorigenicity and lung metastasis in vivo. On the other hand, using the CRISPR/dCas9-VP64 activation system, we demonstrated that overexpression of METTL3 significantly promoted HCC growth both in vitro and in vivo. Through transcriptome sequencing, m6A-Seq and m6A MeRIP qRT-PCR, we identified SOCS2 (suppressor of cytokine signaling 2) as a target of METTL3-mediated m6A modification. Knockdown of METTL3 substantially abolished SOCS2 mRNA m6A modification and augmented SOCS2 mRNA expression. We also showed that m6A-mediated SOCS2 mRNA degradation relied on m6A “reader” protein YTHDF2 dependent pathway. In conclusion, we demonstrated that METTL3 was frequently up-regulated in human HCC and contributed to HCC progression. METTL3 repressed SOCS2 expression in HCC via the m6A-YTHDF2 dependent mechanism. Thus, our findings suggested a new dimension of epigenetic alteration in liver carcinogenesis.

17142516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17142516.value: This is the first report to show the oncogenic functions of METTL3 in human cancer. Our study provided the rationale for the development of METTL3 specific inhibitor for cancer treatment. We also provide a proof-of-concept model to demonstrate cancer cells can epigenetically suppress a tumor suppressor gene through METTL3/m6A/YTHDF2 axis, we expect this will shed light on the understanding of the molecular mechanism of human carcinogenesis. Future studies should focus on delineating the comprehensive m6A modification landscape in the human HCC transcriptome.

17142516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17142516.value: We discovered for the first time a new key oncogene METTL3. METTL3 is an epigenetic regulatory factor that is responsible for catalyzing the m6A (N6-adenosine methylation) of mRNA (messenger ribonucleic acid), which in turn promotes the decomposition of mRNA. Patients with high METTL3 have a significantly poorer survival rate. Because the overexpression of METTL3 in liver cancer will lead to an increase in m6A levels, which in turn reduces the expression of tumor suppressor gene SOCS2 and increases the occurrence of liver cancer. Studies have proved that METTL3 can be used as a potential target for the treatment of liver cancer in the future, providing new hope for liver cancer patients

17143516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17143516.value: Arginine methylation is a post-translational modification that plays pivotal roles in signal transduction and gene transcription during cell fate determination. We found protein methyltransferase 6 (PRMT6) to be frequently downregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and its expression to negatively correlate with aggressive cancer features in HCC patients. The silencing of PRMT6 promoted the tumor-initiating, metastasis, and therapy resistance potential of HCC cell lines and patient-derived organoids. Consistently, loss of PRMT6 expression aggravated liver tumorigenesis in a chemical-induced HCC PRMT6 knockout (PRMT6-/-) mouse model. Integrated transcriptome and protein-protein interaction studies revealed an enrichment of genes implicated in RAS signaling and showed that PRMT6 interacted with CRAF on arginine 100, which decreased its RAS binding potential and altered its downstream MEK/ERK signaling. Our work describes a critical repressive function for PRMT6 in the maintenance of HCC cells by regulating RAS binding and MEK/ERK signaling via methylation of CRAF on arginine 100. This project is done in collaboration with overseas PIs including Hans Clevers of Hubrecht Institute, Stephane Richard of McGill University and Yun-Fei Yuan and Dan Xie of Sun-Yat Sen University Cancer Center.

17143516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17143516.value: This PRMT6 project resulted in two spin-off projects where we found a novel role of PRMT6 in regulating autophagy and glycolysis. Specifically, we found PRMT6 deficiency to induce autophagy in the hostile microenvironment of hepatocellular carcinoma tumors by regulating BAG5-associated HSC70 stability. The manuscript of this work was recently submitted to Cancer Letters for consideration. We also found CRAF methylation by PRMT6 to regulate aerobic glycolysis-driven hepatocarcinogenesis via ERK-dependent PKM2 nuclear relocalization and activation. This work is now published in Hepatology.

17143516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17143516.value: RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathway signaling is known to be frequently activated in cancers, in which it regulates cell growth, malignant transformation, drug resistance, and stemness. Using hepatocellular carcinoma as a model system, we describe a mechanism by which this oncogenic signaling pathway is regulated by PRMT6 at the post-translational level via arginine methylation.

17143716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17143716.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most frequent human malignancies worldwide. The prognosis of HCC is extremely poor and five year overall survival is less than 8%. The most important contributor to the HCC mortality is metastasis, which involves increased cell invasion and angiogenesis. Therefore, understanding of key factors promoting cancer metastasis is critical to improve HCC outcome. In our preliminary work, we found that Angiopoitein 3 (ANG3) was frequently down-regulated in HCCs, which was negatively correlated with tumor metastasis and poor outcome. Functional study finds that ANG3 can inhibit cell proliferation, migration and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Although the effect of ANG1 and ANG2 on angiogenesis and metastasis have been widely studied, little is known about the effects of ANG3 on cancer development and progression. Therefore, the tumor suppressive function and mechanism of ANG3 will be characterized in this proposal. First, the expression status of ANG1 in HCC and its clinical significances will be investigated in more HCC cases by mmunohistochemistry (IHC) using an HCC tissue microassay (TMA). The causes of ANG3 down-regulation will be addressed by detecting allele loss and promoter hypermethylation. Second, the tumor suppressing roles of ANG3 will be characterized by in vitro and in vivo functional assays (cell proliferation, migration, invasion and angiogenesis) in both ANG3-overexpressing and ANG3-silencing cell lines. The third part of this proposal is to explore the inhibiting mechanisms of ANG3 in metastasis and angiogenesis. At least three issues will be addressed including: 1) to investigate the effect of ANG3 on EMT; 2) to explore whether the metastasis inhibiting role of ANG3 is involved in the integrin signaling pathway, and what is the downstream signaling pathways downstream of integrins; and 3) to determine if ANG3 is able to bind Tie-2 receptor, and whether Ang3 can inhibit angiogenesis through Tie2 receptor. Taken together, our research will shed light on the mechanism of HCC progression, especially in metastasis and angiogenesis. ANG3 may be a promising prognostic biomarker and therapeutic agents for HCC. Outcomes from this study may facilitate the development of novel and effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies in HCC clinical management. 肝癌是全球發病率最高的癌症之一，而轉移是導致肝癌患者死 亡的最重要因素。腫瘤轉移過程包括癌細胞侵襲和血管生成。 最近，一種結構上類似于血管生成素的蛋白家族被發現，稱爲 血管生成素樣蛋白。與血管生成素類似，這類蛋白家族可調控 血管生成，其中一些還會對腫瘤行爲產生影響。我們以前的研 究發現，血管生成素樣蛋白1在肝癌中的表達顯著下調。儘管 血管生成素樣蛋白1被認爲具有抗血管生成作用，并可抑制内 皮細胞的增值、遷移和血管形成，但其中的作用機制尚沒有 完全闡明。另外，血管生成素樣蛋白1在肝癌的發生和發展中 所起的作用尚不明確。我們的臨床相關性分析表明，血管生 成素樣蛋白1可能參與調節肝癌的轉移和血管生成：1）與癌 旁組織相比，血管生成素樣蛋白1的表達水平在肝癌中顯著下調。2）肝癌患者中血管生成素樣蛋白1的表達與血管侵襲，癌栓，腫瘤復發和轉移呈負相關。3）血管生成素樣蛋白1的下調與較差的臨床預後顯著相關。因此，我們推測血管生成素樣蛋白1可抑制肝癌的發展，轉移和血管形成過程。爲徹底瞭解血管生成素樣蛋白1的功能和作用機制，我們打算開展以下研究：1）血管生成素樣蛋白1在肝癌中的下調機制；2）血管生成素樣蛋白1對腫瘤細胞生長，遷移，侵襲和血管生成的體内和體外作用；3）血管生成素樣蛋白1對腫瘤細胞生長，遷移，侵襲和血管生成的作用機制；4）血管生成素樣蛋白1是否可作爲肝癌預後的生物標記物，因其是一種分泌蛋白并可能分泌至患者血清中。總之，我們的研究將給肝癌的發生和發展提供綫索，血管生成素樣蛋白1有望成爲有效的肝癌預後生物標記物以及治療藥物。

17143716.value: Objective 1: To study the down-regulation and underlying mechanism of ANG3, as well as its clinical significances in HCC. To determine whether downregulation of ANG3 was a common event in HCC, qPCR was used to detect the expression level of ANG3 in 122 pairs of HCC samples. Downregulation of ANG3 was detected in 64 of 122 (52.5%) HCCs. Compared with non-tumor tissue, the relative level of ANG3 was significantly lower in its tumor counterparts (paired Student’s t-test, P<0.0001). In a Kaplan-Meier survival analysis comparing patients with different ANG3 expression levels, lower ANG3 expression was significantly correlated with a shorter overall survival (OS) (log-rank test, 10.487; P = 0.001) and shorter disease-free survival time (log-rank test, 4.073; P = 0.044). Lower expression of ANG3 was also significantly correlated with serum AFP level (P = 0.014), vascular invasion (P = 0.029), poor differentiation (P = 0.022), metastasis (P = 0.043) and tumor thrombus (P = 0.049). Objective 2: To investigate the suppressive role of ANG3 in cell proliferation, migration, metastasis and angiogenesis. To explore whether ANG3 possesses a tumor suppressive function in HCC, ANG3 was cloned into a lentivector and infected HCC cell lines PLC-8024 and Huh7. The tumor suppressive role of ANG3 was addressed by cell proliferation, foci formation and soft agar assay. Compared with control cells, ANG3-transfected cells showed impaired abilities of foci formation and colony formation in soft agar. To assess the in vivo tumor suppressive ability of ANG3, LacZ- and ANG3-transfected cells were injected subcutaneously into the left and right dorsal flank of nude mice (n=5), respectively. Tumors induced by ANG3-transfected PLC-8024 cells (tumor formation in 1/5 of mice) showed significantly longer latency and smaller mean tumor volume than tumors induced by LacZ-transfected cells (tumor formation in 5/5 of mice) (P< 0.01). A similar result was obtained when using ANG3-transfected Huh7 cells in xenograft mouse experiment (P< 0.05). In order to confirm cell proliferative status in xenograft tumors, IHC staining of proliferative index Ki67 was performed. Results demonstrated that tumors induced by 8024- or Huh7-ANG3 cells showed a significantly lower percentage of Ki67 positive signals compared with 8024- or Huh7-LacZ cells, indicating the tumor suppressive function of ANG3. To confirm whether ANG3 is required for the tumor suppressive phenotype of HCC cells, we silenced ANG3 expression with short hairpin RNA (shRNA) against ANG3. Two shRNAs (ANG3-sh4, ANG3-sh5) were introduced into the HCC cell line QGY-7703 and immortalized liver cell line LO2. Functional assays revealed that ANG3 silencing could increase the efficiency of foci formation (P< 0.05) and colony formation in soft agar (P< 0.05), compared with Vector-transfected cells. For in vivo xenograft experiments, 7703-shANG3 and 7703-Vec cells were subcutaneously injected into nude mice (n = 5). The average volume of tumors induced by shANG3-transfected cells (tumor formation in all 5 mice) was significantly larger than that induced by Vec-transfected cells (tumor formation in 4 mice). Since downregulation of ANG3 was associated with vascular invasion and metastasis, we next investigated the effect of ANG3 on tumor cell migration and invasion. In vitro cell transwell migration and Matrigel invasion assays found that the migratory and invasive abilities of 8024-ANG3 and Huh7-ANG3 cells were inhibited compared with control cells. To test the in vivo suppressing effect of ANG3 on metastasis, 8024-LacZ and 8024-ANG3 cells were injected into spleen of nude mice (n=5), respectively. Liver metastatic nodules were counted 6 weeks after injection. Liver metastatic nodules were formed in 5/5 and 2/5 mice injected with 8024-LacZ cells and 8024-ANG3 cells, respectively (Figure 5D). The number of metastatic nodules formed on the surface of the liver was significantly lower in mice injected with 8024-ANG3 cells (6.4 ± 9.2) than in mice injected with 8024-LacZ cells (48.6 ± 27.3; P< 0.05). Objective 3: To explore the inhibiting mechanisms of ANG3 in tumor metastasis and angiogenesis. As Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) is a critical step in metastasis that involves diverse biological mechanisms, we next studied the effects of ANG3 on EMT process. Western blot analysis found that ANG3 could upregulate epithelial markers (E-cadherin and β-catenin) and downregulate mesenchymal markers (N-cadherin, fibronectin and vimentin) and transcription factor SNAIL and SLUG in HCC cell lines. These data suggest that ANG3 can inhibit EMT and subsequently inhibit tumor metastasis. In addition, we found that ANG3 could inhibit angiogenesis. To further confirm the effect of ANG3 on HCC angiogenesis, the microvessel formation frequency was compared between xenograft tumors induced by shANG3- and empty vector-transfected LO2 cells. The in vivo tumor growth rate of tumors induced with shANG3 cells was significantly higher than tumors induced by vector-transfected cells (P<0.01). To further explore the underlying molecular mechanism, we tested if ANGPTL1 could affect ERK and AKT signaling pathways, both of which play important roles in angiopoietins-mediated endothelial cell behavior. Results showed that ANG3 could effectively inhibit the phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and AKT in serum starved HUVECs, suggesting that ANG3 inhibits endothelial cell proliferation, migration and tube formation by blocking AKT and ERK signals, which likely underlie the inhibitory activity of ANG3 on tumor angiogenesis and metastasis. As ANG3 proteins have been reported to deliver their signals via integrin receptor-related pathways, we next studied whether ANG3-mediated effect is through integrin signaling pathways. In order to identify candidate integrin receptors for ANG3, immunoprecipitation was performed to analyze the immunoprecipitates from Flag-tagged ANG3-transfected PLC-8024 cells. Our data revealed that ANG3 interacted with the integrin α1β1 receptor. ANG3 binding with integrin β1 was also confirmed by immunofluorescence result of treating PLC-8024 cells with rANG3.

17143716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17143716.value: Here we find that ANG3 gene is frequently downregulated in liver cancer, which is associated with cancer metastasis and poor outcome. To study its roles in tumor development and metastasis, we introduced ANG3 into liver cancer cells. Functional studies find that ANG3 could inhibit tumor growth and tumor formation in mouse. ANG3 could inhibit cell migration and invasion, as well as tumor metastasis in mouse. We also investigated the molecular mechanism of ANG3 in liver cancer development and progression. Our results find that ANG3 decreases cell migratory and invasive abilities by inhibiting Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (a key step for cancer cell metastasis) via downregulating transcription factors SNAIL and SLUG expression. Furthermore, ANG3 could inhibit angiogenesis (blood vessel formation) by inhibiting ERK and AKT signaling. Molecular study found that ANG3 interacted with integrin α1β1 receptor and suppressed downstream FAK/Src-JAK-STAT3 signaling pathway, thus affects HCC cell survival, metastasis and angiogenesis. ANG3 might be used as a prognostic biomarker and a novel therapeutic agent for HCC treatment.

17143816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17143816.value: 聲帶上的良性病變、一般是由聲帶本身過度互相撞擊產生的表層組織變異。這包括聲帶小結、息肉、囊腫和慢性喉炎。現代醫學建議、第一選擇是保守聲線治療、包括改善發聲方法和矯正發聲行為。有時或許要加上手術治療。 針灸治療、已被證實是對良性聲帶病變有顯著療效。一周兩次的針灸、經過四周的治療，對發聲功能（Yiu et al., 2006; Yiu, Chan, Kwong et al, 2016) 和聲帶傷口癒合 (Yiu, Chan, Li et al, 2015) 都有 明顯改善。 香港大學由美國衛生研究基金所贊助的一個近期研究，更發現僅用針在穴位表皮上的轉動刺激、亦已明顯改善發聲功能（Yiu, Chan, Kwong et al, 2016) 。 本項目將採用隨機雙盲設計，研究用針在與聲線有關的穴位表皮、與聲線無關的穴位表皮丶和非穴位表皮的刺激、對發聲功能和聲帶病變的影響。 本項目假設： （一）刺激與聲線有關的穴位表皮，將會比剌激非聲線有關的穴位或非穴位表皮，更能擴寛發聲功能中的音域、和改善聲質。 （二）聲線病患者用一套家居穴位表皮刺激療法、配合針灸療法、會更顯著對發聲功能、聲帶病變的體積、和抗炎細胞因子的正面影響。

17143816.label: Realisation of objectives
17143816.value: Study 1 (Jan - June/July 2017) Study 1 was conducted to address Objective 1- to compare the effect of skin surface stimulation of voice-related acupoint; non-voice related acupoint and non-acupoint stimulation on vocal function. The major difficulties in recruiting participants for Study 1 was that participants perceived this as not a traditional method used in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) practice and the duration of intervention took a relatively longer time than the participants anticipated. The team decided to suspended Study 1 (around June/July 2017) after 21 participants (out of 78 inquiries and 28 of them were recruited) went through the protocol. There were, however, nine subjects who did not complete the protocol. The termination of Study 1, however, had little impact on Study 2 as the acupoints used in Study 2 were all voice-related acupoints that have been validated previously in a separate published study (Yiu et al., 2016) Study 2 (July 2017- Feb/Mar 2019) Study 2 aimed to investigate the effectiveness of a Home AcuStim protocol in addition to traditional acupuncture, with 1) one group employing a dental probe for acupoint stimulation and 2) another group using a skin-tag for acupoint stimulation compared to 3) a group without the use of Home AcuStim. Outcome measures including maximum pitch produced; laryngoscopic examination of the vocal fold and supraglottic functions; quality of life measures and voice risk calculator were all taken. Salivary secretions were also collected for cytokine analysis. Study 2 took about 20 months for data collection. This study included a total of three experimental groups: 1) Acupuncture with AcuStim using dental probe for stimulation; 2) Acupuncture with AcuStim using “skin-tag” for stimulation; and 3) Acupuncture WITHOUT AcuStim. The protocol was also amended by reducing the number of attendance to one session per week (twice per week in the original proposal) in order to ensure participant compliance. A total of 140 inquires and responses to our recruitment exercises. All of them were screened and interviewed. Out of these, 75 individuals were recruited to participate in the program. However, only 33 of them completed the program and had a complete set of outcome measures at the pre-intervention, immediate post-intervention and one month post-intervention. This completion rate (44%) is relatively low and disappointing. The remaining 42 participants had various degrees of outcome measures completed. With the social unrest starting in March/April 2019 and the running out of budget with the traditional Chinese medicine practitioner finished his contract, further recruitment of participants was impossible to continue. The final sample size for each group in Study 2 were: Acupuncture + Probe AcuStim = 14; Acupuncture + Tag AcuStim = 11; Acupuncture only = 8, Control group (voice rest) = 13. Four sets of data were available for analysis: 1) Salivary cytokine level 2) Maximum pitch produced 3) Voice-related quality of life 4) Laryngoscopic images of lesion size Under achievement The first 4 sets of outcome measures have been completed but the laryngoscopic images analysis needed to be re-done as video images were used in the initial analysis but there were much variabilities in inter-rater evaluation since different raters used different segment of each video in arriving at a rating. So, static frames from each video were first selected by one investigator and these are to be used for panel rating. However, due to the coronavirus pandemic, preparation of the images and panel analysis have been greatly impacted. And there has been a delay of about 12 months of work. Attempt to overcome the problem A PhD student has been assigned to undertake the video editing and a program has finally been compiled for different panel judges to carryout online evaluation using video-conferencing facility. This last stage of panel analysis of laryngoscopic images will be conducted in January/February 2021. Nevertheless, based on the data we currently have, we are confident that we have achieved 90% of the objective, as significantly better outcomes have been found in the vocal function of the participants who undertook acupuncture AND Home AcuStim treatment than those who took only acupuncture treatment. 17143816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17143816.value: 1) Due to small sample size with Cytokine data (AcuStim-Probe = 5; AcuStim-Tag = 4 and Acupuncture = 6), no significant results were found in the IL1 Beta change (chi square- 0.36, df=2, p = 0.86) or IL10 change (chi square- 0.35, df=2, p = 0.84) following treatment. 2) Vocal function based on maximum pitch level that could be produced were found to be significantly better with the AcuStim-Probe when compared to the Control group. One-way ANOVA showed significant difference between the 1-month post acupuncture and pre-acupuncture data (F=4.45, df=3,39, p=0.009). Post hoc Scheffee tests showed significant difference between the AcuStim (probe) and no-acupuncture group (p=0.014). No significant differences were found between the post- and pre-acupuncture data (F=0.62, df=3,42, p=0.61), nor the 1-month post- and post-acupuncture data (F=2. 34, df=3,39, p=0.09). 3) Voice related quality of life (Self-perceived severity, Voice Activity & Participation Profile score and Voice Risk Calculator Score) showed significant main time effect in all three measures (p<0.01) but no time x group interaction effect (p>0.4) (see Figure 2 for trend in self-perceived severity). In summary, the self percpetion of problem improved over time following the intervention (or even voice rest), but there was a resurgence one-month after intervention.

17143816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17143816.value: The study showed significant improvement in sustaining the effect of acupuncture in treating voice problem by combining it with skin surface stimulation on acupoint. The study was limited by the small sample size and would therefore need studies with larger sample size as well as in other research centers to ensure that the results are replicable. This study adds further evidence to support that acupuncture is effective therapy regime in treating voice problems. This should be promoted as an treatment option in addition to surgical and conservative treatment options available for individuals with voice problems.

17143816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17143816.value: Acupuncture is an evidenced-based treatment option that has been shown to be effective in treating people with voice problems. One short-coming of acupuncture is that the effect seldom lasts beyond one month. The present study found that the use of a dental probe to stimulate the skin surface of the voice-related acupoints on a daily basis at home could prolong the treatment effect of acupuncture. This additional treatment option can be carried out by individuals at home. The relative low cost of this option and the reduction of clinic contact time, individuals with voice problems would find this as a welcoming alternative.

17146216.label: Project Objectives
17146216.value: The first objective is to identify the impact of ω-alkynyl-AA-PKM2 conjugation on macrophage M2 polarization. In pilot experiments, we discovered that ω-alkynyl-AA formed covalent conjugate with glycolytic enzyme PKM2. PKM2 not only govern energy metabolism via glycolysis but also regulate the transcriptional activity of HIF-1α. We postulate that ω-alkynyl-AA may regulate macrophage polarization via suicide inhibition of PKM2 activities. We will discover which and how ω-alkynyl-AA metabolites form covalent conjugate with PKM2. We will also determine whether the conjugation of ω-alkynyl-AA with PKM2 alters the effects of PKM2 on macrophage polarization. The second objective is to clarify whether ω-alkynyl-AA promotes macrophage polarization via regulating the cross-talk between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α. Other scientists have demonstrated that PKM2 and iNOS could individually regulate the transcriptional activity of HIF-1α. Our results indicated that ω-alkynyl-AA not only formed covalent conjugate with PKM2 but also down-regulated PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α expression.Thus, we hypothesize that ω-alkynyl-AA may promote macrophage polarization via regulating the cross-talk between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α. We will address three important questions: 1) Does the formation of ω-alkynyl-AA-PKM2 conjugate cause down-regulation of PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α? 2) Does PKM2 suppression down-regulate HIF-1α and iNOS expression or iNOS suppression lead to the decrease in PKM2 and HIF-1α expression? 3) Does ω-alkynyl-AA promote macrophage polarization in PKM2-, iNOS- or HIF-1α-dependent manner? The third objective is to determine the in vivo cardioprotective efficacy of ω-alkynyl-AA in mice. The abnormalities of arachidonic acid metabolism may cause myocardial infarction. However, we found that ω-alkynyl-AA reduced infarct size and cardiac damage in mouse model. Thus, we hypothesize that ω-alkynyl-AA attenuates cardiac injury via promoting anti-inflammatory M2 polarization of macrophage. After inducing myocardial infarction in mice by coronary ligation, we will determine the efficacy of ω-alkynyl-AA to reduce infarct size, myocardial injury and redox status. We will also investigate the effects of ω-alkynyl-AA on the phenotypic kinetics of resident cardiac macrophages and myocardial fibrosis in the infarcted hearts.

17146216.value: 急性心肌梗塞病人常常會因心肌功能修復不完全而發生致命的心臟衰竭。巨噬細胞從炎症性M1型轉化成抗炎性M2型的時間點決定著梗死心肌中炎症消解和功能恢復的進程。在早前幾個GRF基金如775812M, 17120915的支持下，我們研究發現黃芪和赤芍等中藥可以調控花生四烯酸的代謝從而誘導巨噬細胞的表型和功能的轉換。本課題著眼進一步鑒定出有活性的花生四烯酸代謝物，並研究活性脂肪分子與何種信號傳導蛋白作用以促進巨噬細胞朝著有助於梗死心肌功能修復的方向極化。我們起初以含端尾炔基花生四烯酸代替正常花生四烯酸在鼠原巨噬細胞株RAW264.7細胞中探索脂肪酸與蛋白之間形成的共價加合物。利用點擊化學的炔烴-迭氮環加成反應引入生物素基團，再用結合素修飾過的超順磁性氧化鐵微粒進行親和分離，我們鑒定出葡萄糖代謝酶丙酮酸激酶PKM2為潛在的靶標蛋白。有趣的是，我們發現含端尾炔基花生四烯酸在RAW264.7細胞中有效地抑制了LPS誘導的炎症性iNOS和COX-2的上調。其他科學家則發現PKM2和iNOS各自都能調控轉錄因數HIF-1α的活性。這些結果刺激我們進一步求證PKM2，iNOS和HIF-1α是否協作調控巨噬細胞的侵潤和極化。通過分析細胞的蛋白，我們發現含端尾炔基花生四烯酸下調了PKM2的表達。我們的前期實驗進一步表明含端尾炔基花生四烯酸刺激巨噬細胞朝抗炎性M2型極化也維持著吞噬能力。重要的是，含端尾炔基花生四烯酸在小鼠心肌梗塞模型中顯著地減少了心肌的梗死面積。所以，我們提出假設：含端尾炔基花生四烯酸通過調控PKM2， iNOS與HIF-1α之間的交叉作用誘導巨噬細胞的表型和功能的轉換，從而實現消解炎症反應和促進心肌再生。我們將通過達成以下三個子目標來求證我們的科學假設：其一，確認含端尾炔基花生四烯酸與PKM2結合後對巨噬細胞的功能極化的影響；其二，闡明含端尾炔基花生四烯酸是否通過調控PKM2， iNOS與HIF-1α之間的交叉作用來促進巨噬細胞的極化；其三，測定含端尾炔基花生四烯酸在小鼠模型中在體保護心肌的功效。我們提出的研究將首次揭示PKM2， iNOS與HIF-1α之間的交叉作用在巨噬細胞朝抗炎性M2型極化過程中的重要作用。能與PKM2結合的含端尾炔基花生四烯酸代謝產物可成為開發新型治療心肌梗死和心臟衰竭的既抗炎又促進再生的雙效藥物的先導化合物。

17146216.label: Realisation of objectives
17146216.value: Persistent chronic inflammation and atherosclerosis not only increase the prevalence of myocardial infarction but also delay the recovery of cardiac functions in patients. Therefore, novel pharmacological interventions are pressingly needed for the resolution of inflammation and suppression of adverse cardiac remodeling in post-MI patients. With the support of previous GRF grants (i.e., 775812M, 17120915), we focused on the Chinese medicines for targeting macrophage polarization from pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2 towards the resolution of inflammation and recovery of cardiac functions. We discovered that Radix Astragali and Radix Paeoniae Rubra could modulate arachidonic acid metabolism and subsequently induce phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages. The goal of this project was to further identify the active arachidonic acid metabolites and investigate the interactions between lipid mediators and signaling proteins in macrophage polarization towards resolution of inflammation and anti-fibrosis in infarcted heart. In this project, we employed ω-alkynyl arachidonic acid (ω-alkynyl-AA) to mimic arachidonic acid in cell culture and animal models. Indeed, ω-alkynyl-AA not only suppressed the induction of pro-inflammatory inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) in LPS-stimulated macrophages but also markedly reduced infarct size in mouse model of myocardial infarction. Following the treatment with ω-alkynyl-AA, the cellular proteins were isolated from murine macrophage RAW264.7 cells, biotinylated by Click chemistry “Azide-Alkyne Cycloaddition” and isolated by affinity to superparamagnetic streptavidin beads. Importantly, we identified glycolytic enzyme pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) as a potential protein target. PKM2 and iNOS were previously found to regulate the transcriptional activities of hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) in separate studies. Thus, it is important to clarify whether PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α could orchestrate macrophage infiltration and polarization. Indeed, Western blot analysis revealed that ω-alkynyl-AA decreased the protein levels of PKM2 and HIF-1α. Furthermore, ω-alkynyl-AA induced anti-inflammatory M2 polarization and maintained active phagocytosis in macrophages. Thus, our initial hypothesis was that ω-alkynyl-AA could induce phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages towards the resolution of inflammation and cardiac regeneration via regulating the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α. To test this hypothesis, we have pursued the following three specific aims: 1) to identify the impact of ω-alkynyl-AA-PKM2 conjugation on the functional polarization of macrophages; 2) to clarify whether ω-alkynyl-AA promotes macrophage polarization via regulating the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α; 3) to determine the in vivo cardioprotective efficacy of ω-alkynyl-AA in mice. Another key finding was that 15-Oxo-PGF2α was identified for forming covalent conjugate with PKM2. As result, this project for the first time demonstrated the key role of the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α in anti-inflammatory M2 polarization of macrophages. The results from this project may help the discovery of novel 15-oxo-PGF2α analogs as dual anti-inflammatory and regenerative drugs for myocardial infarction and heart failure. For Specific Aim 1, the goal was to identify the impact of ω-alkynyl-AA-PKM2 conjugation on the functional polarization of macrophages. In practice, we firstly demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA promoted macrophage polarization towards the anti-inflammatory and resolving M2-like phenotype. We discovered that ω-alkynyl-AA was metabolized to specific metabolites and formed covalent conjugate with glycolytic enzyme PKM2. On the other hand, PKM2 plays important role in the regulation of energy metabolism via glycolysis and the expression of inflammatory gens via interacting with transcriptional factor HIF-1α. A key finding was that ω-alkynyl-AA could regulate macrophage polarization via suicide inhibition of PKM2 activities. We successfully isolated the peptide covalently modified by ω-alkynyl-AA metabolite and subsequently identified 15-keto-PGF2alpgha for forming covalent conjugate with PKM2. Moreover, we also found that ω-alkynyl-AA skewed macrophage polarization via covalently binding to PKM2. The results have been published in Biochim Biophys Acta- Molecular and Cell Biology of Lipids, 2017 Sep 28;1862(12):1595-1605 Cheng Y and Rong J Cell Physiol Biochem. 2018;47(6):2544-2557 and reviewed in Expert Opinion on Therapeutic Targets, 2019 May;23(5):423-436. The proposed work has been completed by 100%. For Specific Aim 2, the goal was to clarify whether ω-alkynyl-AA promotes macrophage polarization via regulating the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α. We successfully demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA formed covalent conjugate with PKM2 and thereby down-regulated PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α expression. We further investigated whether ω-alkynyl-AA promoted macrophage polarization via regulating the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α. In practical, we clarified that PKM2 suppression might down-regulate HIF-1α and iNOS expression. We also demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA promoted macrophage polarization in PKM2-dependent manner. Other important findings included: 1) PKM2 inhibition also suppressed the expression of iNOS and HIF-1α; 2) the formation of ω-alkynyl-AA-PKM2 conjugate down-regulated the expression of PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α; 3) ω-alkynyl-AA promoted macrophage polarization in iNOS- or HIF-1α-dependent manner. The results have been published in Biochim Biophys Acta- Molecular and Cell Biology of Lipids, 2017 Sep 28;1862(12):1595-1605 Cheng Y and Rong J Cell Physiol Biochem. 2018;47(6):2544-2557 and reviewed in Expert Opinion on Therapeutic Targets, 2019 May;23(5):423-436. The proposed work has been completed by 100%. For Specific Aim 3, the goal was to determine the in vivo cardioprotective efficacy of ω-alkynyl-AA in mice. We focused on the in vivo cardioprotective efficacy of ω-alkynyl-AA in mice. The dysregulation of arachidonic acid metabolism is implicated in myocardial infarction. Interestingly, we found that ω-alkynyl-AA reduced infarct size and cardiac damage in mouse model of myocardial infarction. Presumably, ω-alkynyl-AA attenuated cardiac injury via promoting anti-inflammatory macrophage M2 polarization. In this project, we induced myocardial infarction in mice by ligating left coronary artery. We subsequently demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA markedly reduced infarct size, affected myocardial redox status and skewed macrophage polarization. We also investigated the effects of ω-alkynyl-AA on the phenotypic kinetics of resident cardiac macrophages and myocardial fibrosis in the infarcted hearts. We further demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA formed covalent conjugate with PKM2 in myocardial infarction. The results have been published in Biochim Biophys Acta- Molecular and Cell Biology of Lipids, 2017 Sep 28;1862(12):1595-1605 Cheng Y and Rong J Cell Physiol Biochem. 2018;47(6):2544-2557 and reviewed in Expert Opinion on Therapeutic Targets, 2019 May;23(5):423-436. The proposed work has been completed by 100%.

17146216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17146216.value: Adverse cardiac remodeling is implicated in the pathogenesis of heart failure after myocardial infarction. The main goal of this project was to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which arachidonic acid metabolites modulate macrophage polarization to resolve the inflammation and suppress adverse cardiac remodeling in myocardial infarction. We focused on the identification of covalent conjugates between arachidonic acid metabolites and the cellular proteins. We employed ω-alkynyl arachidonic acid (ω-alkynyl-AA) to mimic arachidonic acid in cell culture and animal models of myocardial infarction. As results, this project led to the following key findings: 1) We firstly demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA promoted macrophage polarization towards the anti-inflammatory and resolving M2-like phenotype. We discovered that ω-alkynyl-AA was metabolized to specific metabolites and formed covalent conjugate with glycolytic enzyme PKM2. ω-Alkynyl-AA could effectively inhibit PKM2 activities. We successfully isolated the peptide covalently modified by ω-alkynyl-AA metabolite and subsequently identified 15-keto-PGF2alpgha for forming covalent conjugate with PKM2. Moreover, we also found that ω-alkynyl-AA skewed macrophage polarization via covalently binding to PKM2. 2) We successfully demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA formed covalent conjugate with PKM2 and thereby down-regulated PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α expression. We further investigated that ω-alkynyl-AA promoted macrophage polarization via regulating the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α. We also demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA promoted macrophage polarization in PKM2-dependent manner. 3) We validated the in vivo cardioprotective efficacy of ω-alkynyl-AA in mice. In this project, we induced myocardial infarction in mice by ligating left coronary artery. We subsequently demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA markedly reduced infarct size, affected myocardial redox status and skewed macrophage polarization. We also investigated the effects of ω-alkynyl-AA on the phenotypic kinetics of resident cardiac macrophages and myocardial fibrosis in the infarcted hearts. We further demonstrated that ω-alkynyl-AA formed covalent conjugate with PKM2 in myocardial infarction. The research outcomes include two publications, one research grant and academic trainings. The results of this project have been published in Biochim Biophys Acta- Molecular and Cell Biology of Lipids, 2017 Sep 28;1862(12):1595-1605 Cheng Y and Rong J Cell Physiol Biochem. 2018;47(6):2544-2557 and reviewed in Expert Opinion on Therapeutic Targets, 2019 May;23(5):423-436. Moreover, the results from the present study were used as the important preliminary results for a successful NSFC grant #21778046. The results may facilitate the development of ω-alkynyl-AA and 15-keto-PGF2alpgha for inducing pro-resolving macrophages and suppressing cardiac fibrosis in experimental myocardial infarction. The grant supported the academic training of four PhD students, one MPhil students and one post-doctoral fellow.

17146216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17146216.value: The present project was designed to investigate the endogenous arachidonic acid metabolites for treating inflammation and cardiac fibrosis in experimental myocardial infarction and the underlying mechanisms. We focused on the identification of covalent conjugates between arachidonic acid metabolites and the cellular proteins. We employed ω-alkynyl arachidonic acid (ω-alkynyl-AA) to mimic arachidonic acid in cell culture and animal models. As result, that ω-alkynyl-AA was metabolized to specific metabolites and formed covalent conjugate with glycolytic enzyme PKM2. PKM2 plays important role in the regulation of energy metabolism via glycolysis and the expression of inflammatory gens via interacting with transcriptional factor HIF-1α. A key finding was that ω-alkynyl-AA could regulate macrophage polarization via suicide inhibition of PKM2 activities. On the other hand, we successfully isolated the peptide covalently modified by ω-alkynyl-AA metabolite and subsequently identified 15-keto-PGF2alpgha for forming covalent conjugate with PKM2. Moreover, ω-alkynyl-AA not only skewed macrophage polarization via covalently binding to PKM2 but also reduced myocardial injury and adverse cardiac remodeling. Therefore, the results of this project suggest a novel endogenous cardioprotective mechanism and promote the development of novel arachidonic acid analogs as therapies against myocardial infarction.

17146216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17146216.value: Myocardial infarction is a highly prevalent and life-threatening disease. Patients often suffer from heart failure due to the incomplete recovery of cardiac functions. The long-term goal of the present study is to discover the novel pharmaceutics for the resolution of inflammation and suppression of adverse cardiac remodeling in post-MI patients. Through previous GRF projects (i.e., 775812M, 17120915), we discovered that Chinese medicines induced phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages via modulating arachidonic acid metabolism. The present project was designed to identify the active arachidonic acid metabolites and investigate the interactions between lipid mediators and signaling proteins for promoting macrophage polarization towards the functional recovery of infarcted heart. The key findings include: 1) ω-alkynyl-AA-PKM2 conjugation controls the functional polarization of macrophages; 2) ω-alkynyl-AA promotes macrophage polarization via regulating the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α; 3) ω-alkynyl-AA is in vivo cardioprotective in mice. The results from this project for the first time demonstrate the key role of the cross-talks between PKM2, iNOS and HIF-1α in anti-inflammatory M2 polarization of macrophages. Importantly, ω-alkynyl-AA metabolite may be a novel lead compound for the discovery of dual anti-inflammatory and regenerative drugs for myocardial infarction and heart failure.

17146616.value: 全基因組關聯分析（GWAS）已顯著推進了我們对複雜疾病包括系統性紅斑狼瘡（SLE）的理解。然而，今天所識別的SLE的易感性變種到目前為止遠遠沒有完全解釋疾病的基因遺傳本质。進一步增加關聯研究的效力變得越來越困難。此外，对易感性變體的作用機制的認識也是很分散和缺乏深度的。為了檢測更多的SLE易感基因，更重要的是，要更好地了解SLE信息转导途徑和網絡干擾的遺傳机制，基因數據的綜合分析與充分利用基因組功能信息是非常必要的。本研究中，我們建議利用現有的香港，安徽和英國三個以前的SLE GWAS數據，把它們與其它類型的數據一起分析，包括關於SLE患者的功能研究的數據（基因表達和DNA甲基化），遺傳變異的基因組功能註釋，相關基因組區域与其他自身免疫性疾病的關聯結果等，以發現更多的易感基因位點，並更好地了解SLE的機制。機器學習模型將被用来開發評估各种功能改变參數的意义，以选择最可能的SNP进行进一步验证。這項研究有望揭示一些新的對SLE有关的易感位點，並從遺傳學，基因組學和功能研究的資料綜合分析角度讓我們確定新的与SLE有关的信息通路，並为臨床表现的异质性解释提供遗传依据。

17146616.label: Realisation of objectives
17146616.value: First, immense gratitude towards panel for supporting this project, which allowed our genetic studies to go on. The first two objectives are to prioritize/select variants for replication and to uncover novel susceptibility variants. In the end, the cost of genome-wide genotyping dropped to a point that selected replication was no longer making sense. Instead, we have used genome-wide genotyping on the remainder of our samples in our Hong Kong cohort and formed new collaborations by including additional cohorts from Guangzhou China and Jining, Shandong province, China. We collaborated also with Zhang et al from Anhui Medical University and Vyse et al from King's College London and the collaborative consortium has the largest SLE genetic study collection up to date. This effort allowed identification of 38 novel loci and a systematic comparison of the genetic differences between East Asians and Europeans (see part C publication by Wang et al, Nat Commun. 2021 Feb 3;12(1):772. doi: 10.1038/s41467-021-21049-y. PMID: 33536424). Additionally, we have eight other publications in prestigious journals in human genetics or rheumatology, including recently joining hands with scientists from Korea and Japan for a focused SLE genetics study on East Asians (Yin et al, Ann Rheum Dis. 2020 Dec 3:annrheumdis-2020-219209. doi: 10.1136/annrheumdis-2020-219209. Online ahead of print.). Based on the above information, we believe we have achieved the objectives 1 and 2 of this project. Objective 3 is to make use of the genetic findings to gain mechanistic understanding of the disease and to help clinical practice. In our recent publication ( Wang et al, Nat Commun. 2021 Feb 3;12(1):772. doi: 10.1038/s41467-021-21049-y. PMID: 33536424 ), we systematically analyzed the genetic findings on SLE, on loci both reported previously and identified in our own study, through eQTL, pathway enrichment, etc, and have gained a much better understanding of the molecular mechanisms of the disease. By overlapping the susceptibility loci with cell-specific histone modifications and open chromatins, we concluded that although most immune cells are relevant in SLE pathogenesis, B cells are the most involved in the disease. The loci showed population differences are much more enriched in functions of antibody production and in evolutionary genetics, these risk alleles were likely positively selected in East Asians but not in Europeans. Using genetics to predict disease risk has always been a major goal of genetic studies. Although individual variant only confers small effect for complex diseases such as SLE, the calculation of polygenic risk scores (PGS) to evaluate the collective effect of genetic susceptibility has shown very promising performance in risk prediction in cardiovascular diseases. Focusing also on population differences of SLE, we have shown that using Asian data as training set for risk prediction in Asian cohort, we can achieve a much better accuracy (ROC=0.76) compared to using European data as the training set (ROC=0.67). As genetic studies tend to have an European bias, our study highlights the importance of conducting genetic studies on the local populations and the promises of using genetics for risk prediction and patient stratification in the future, which are the stepping stones for precision medicine. In this sense, we believe we also have achieved objective 3.

17146616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17146616.value: 1. We have identified more than 40 novel SLE susceptibility loci in East Asian populations. 2. We have systematically compared the differences between Europeans and East Asians in SLE genetics and have some interesting findings both on the level of individual locus and on the level of functional characteristics and population evolution. 3. We have achieved so far the best performance of SLE risk prediction using polygenic risk scores. 4. We have trained four PhD students and one postdocteral fellow through the study of SLE genetics. 5. We have cultivated a broad collaboration network that will be an great asset for future studies.

17146616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17146616.value: Through this project, we have expanded our consortium, significantly increased our sample size, and generated valuable data. Further exploration of the data and broader collaboration effort is already underway. In addition to the "common variants common disease" theory applied in our current project, we are planning to explore the role of rare variants and copy number variation in this disease. It is very likely that the common variants identified in this project and rare variants and structural variants interact to form the architecture of SLE genetics and pathogenesis. Thus, the significance of the findings of this project is far beyond the current publications. Instead, they will be the backbone for our further effort in understanding the genetics of this complex, prototype autoimmune disease. Clinical application of genetic findings is still at its infancy. The good performance of our PGS in risk prediction is a good start. These data will be further explored in the future to translate the genetic findings into better clinical practice.

17146616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17146616.value: SLE is an autoimmune disease mainly affects women of child-bearing age. Genetics play a major role in the disease. In this study, we have collected blood samples on thousands of SLE patients and thousands of healthy controls. Using whole genome SNP genotyping, we have compared genetic variant frequencies between cases and controls. By so doing, we have identified more than 40 genetic variants that shown significantly higher allele frequencies in cases compared to those of the controls, indicating that these variants increased the susceptibility of the disease. Making use of the genetic findings, we could better understand the molecular mechanisms of the disease. Furthermore, we have used the findings to calculate a collective risk score for each individual and have shown that the score is much higher in patient group than in control group. The same principle can be used in the future to use genetics to predict individual risk on SLE. The future goals of the genetic studies on SLE also include using genetics to understand disease mechanisms, to better understand patient differences, and to guide clinical treatment and diagnosis.

17148416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17148416.value: The determinants for influenza transmission remain poorly understood. Especially, there is limited knowledge on the mechanisms driving the formation and release of virus-laden particles from the infected individuals. Influenza virus replicates predominantly in the respiratory tract of mammals, which is anatomically divided into extra-thoracic, tracheal-bronchial, and pulmonary regions that functionally separate the conducting zone and the respiratory zone with mucociliary clearance and gas exchange activities, respectively. Transmission of influenza is mediated by virus-laden particles generated from infected hosts during coughing, sneezing, talking or breathing. The aerodynamic size of the infectious particles determines the mode of transmission as well as the site of particle deposition within the respiratory tract of a susceptible host. The site of deposition determines the initial site for viral replication in the respiratory tract, which may in turn affect disease progression, clinical presentation, and the subsequent generation of virus-laden particles for onward transmission. Breath aerosols, predominantly at particle size < 1 μm, are generated via fluid film rupture at the respiratory bronchioles during inhalation. As such, viral replication in close proximity to the respiratory bronchioles should be advantageous in generating droplet nuclei that confer efficient airborne transmissibility. This concept is not in agreement with the experimental approach of yielding aerosol transmissible influenza variants in ferrets through serial passages and viral adaptations in the ferret upper respiratory tract. There is limited knowledge of the mechanisms driving the formation and release of infectious particles. We hypothesize that the initial site of deposition and replication within the respiratory tract may subsequently influence the size and quantity of infectious particle formation and onward transmission. Furthermore, the differential aerosol formation efficiency in different anatomic sites of the respiratory tract will define the size and genetic diversity of the viral population passed from the infected host to a naïve host during transmission known as the genetic bottleneck. The proposed study will evaluate the significance of the initial site of virus deposition and replication on disease progression, infectious aerosol formation, and onward influenza transmission. Tracing the onward transmission of the genetic-barcoded virus and the wild-type virus deposited at different anatomic site within the respiratory tract will help to assess the genetic bottleneck and the site where transmissible virus-laden particles are formed. This knowledge may aid in the development of antiviral regimens that target specific anatomic sites at the respiratory tract to reduce influenza transmission. 我們對於流感傳播的決定因素仍知之甚少，尤其是對於含有病毒的氣溶膠的形成過程及其從宿主的釋放過程的認知還是有限的。流感病毒主要在哺乳動物的呼吸道複製。從解剖學上，呼吸道可以分胸腔外區，氣管，支氣管和肺泡區；在功能上，可以分為有粘膜纖毛清潔的傳導區和有氣體交換的呼吸區。流感的是以宿主咳嗽，打噴嚏，交談或者呼吸時產生含有病毒的氣溶膠作為傳播媒介的。這些有傳染性氣溶膠的空氣動力學粒徑決定了病毒的傳播模式以及氣溶膠沉積在易感者呼吸道的位置。沉積的位置決定了病毒最初的複製地點，這可能會轉而影響疾病的進展，臨床表徵以及含有病毒氣溶膠的再次產生和進一步傳播。呼吸產生的氣溶膠主要是小於1μm的顆粒，它是通過吸入空氣時呼吸道細支氣管的液膜破裂產生的。假設病毒在靠近呼吸道細支氣管的位置進行複製，將有利於產生能夠高效空氣傳播的飛沫核。但與此相悖的是，目前實驗室製造出來的能夠空氣傳播的流感變異株，是利用雪貂模型進行連續傳代，並使得病毒適應在雪貂上呼吸道複製生長。我們關於傳染性顆粒的產生和釋放機制的認識是有限的。我們推測流感病毒在呼吸道的沉積和複製的最初位置，會影響後續產生的含有病毒的顆粒尺寸和數量以及繼續傳播的能力。 此外，由於呼吸道不同的解剖位置產生氣溶膠效能並不一致，也決定了從原宿主傳代到新宿主的病毒數量和基因多樣性也不一致，即所謂的遺傳瓶頸。這個研究計畫將評估病毒沉積和複製最初位置的對疾病進展，傳染性氣溶膠的產生及其後續的進一步傳播的重要性。我們將追蹤帶有基因條碼的病毒和相應野生型病毒在進一步傳播時沉積在呼吸道的解剖學位置。這會説明我們評估遺傳瓶頸和具有傳播能力的病毒顆粒的產生位置。這個研究將會幫助我們制定針對特定呼吸道解剖位置抗病毒方案，最終達到減少流感的傳播的目的。

17148416.label: Realisation of objectives
17148416.value: Influenza viruses are transmitted via virus-laden aerosols released from infected airway mucosa through breathing, talking, or coughing. The mechanisms driving the formation and release of virus-laden particles from influenza-infected airway mucosa remain poorly understood. Aerosols are a collection of solid or liquid particles in air of various sizes. Gravity determines the distance that large and fine infectious aerosols may travel and the mode of transmission. The aerodynamic size of the inhaled aerosols also determines their site of deposition along the respiratory tract of a susceptible host. Large droplets are known to deposit at the upper respiratory tract while fine particles <5 μm may reach the lower lungs. The initial anatomic site of viral replication at the respiratory tract may affect disease progression and clinical presentation. This project aims to investigate the impact of the initial site of viral replication on the subsequent virus-laden particle formation for onward transmission. We hypothesize that influenza virus deposited at the upper or lower respiratory tract may subsequently influence infectious particles formation for onward transmission. To address this question, we evaluated the onward transmission potential of donor ferrets infected with influenza virus at the nasal mucosa or at the lower lungs. Introducing synonymous mutations as barcodes, we traced the onward transmission of genetic variants deposit at different regions of the respiratory tract to assess the transmission bottleneck and the site where transmissible virus-laden particles are formed. Objective 1. To assess the impact of the initial site of deposit and replication at the respiratory tract on infectious particle formation and onward airborne transmissibility. We hypothesized that the initial site of virus deposition at the upper or lower airway via large and fine particles, respectively, will affect the onward transmissibility of the virus. To specifically deliver influenza virus at targeted anatomic sites, we developed the techniques for intra-nasal and intra-tracheal inoculation to directly deposit influenza virus to nasal mucosa and lower lungs, respectively. Specifically, intra-nasal delivery was done by inoculating anesthetized ferrets with 1000 PFU of A/CA/04/09 virus diluted in 50 μL of media. Intra-tracheal delivery was done with the use of endotracheal tube assisted by a laryngoscope; anesthetized ferrets were inoculated with 1000 PFU of A/CA/04/09 virus diluted in 500 uL media that was delivered to the bronchus through the endotracheal tube. Ferrets inoculated intra-nasally showed significant higher viral load in the nasal turbinate than that in the lung lobes on day 3 post-inoculation. In contrast, higher viral load was detected in the lung than that in the nasal turbinate on day 2 and 3 post-inoculation in ferrets inoculated intra-tracheally. The experiments demonstrated the feasibility of intra-nasal inoculation and intra-tracheal inoculation in delivering influenza viruses at upper and lower respiratory mucosa, respectively. We then inoculated donor ferrets intranasally or intra-tracheally with 1000 PFU of A/CA/04/09 virus and compared their onward transmission potential. Naïve ferrets were exposed to the exhaled breath of inoculated donors for 8 hours on day 2 post-inoculation (of the donors). The transmission experiment was performed using 2-3 pairs of donor:contact at 1:2 ratio (eg. each donor is donating breath to two contacts). Two donor ferrets inoculated intra-nasally efficiently transmitted the virus to 4/4 naïve contacts. In contrast, none of the three donor ferrets inoculated intra-tracheally was able to transmit the virus to 6 exposed naïve contact ferrets (0/6). This result demonstrated the importance of infecting nasal mucosa to support onward influenza transmission. Objective 2. To assess the genetic bottleneck during transmission and the anatomic site of infectious particle formation by tracing the genetic variants deposited at different regions of the respiratory tract. To study the genetic bottleneck during transmission, we generated recombinant A/CA/04/09 (H1N1) viruses with synonymous mutations as barcodes in each of the eight genes. Specifically, recombinant wild-type (WT) and barcoded (BC) A/CA/04/09 viruses were constructed by reverse genetics. Common synonymous mutations (at minimal frequency= 2 %) were identified from available A(H1N1)pdm09 sequences from Genbank in 2016 and were introduced into each of the eight gene segments of the BC virus by site-directed mutagenesis. In each gene segment, we selected two nearby common synonymous mutations as the barcode sequences that will not alter known splice sites, ORF, or packaging signals. The two synonymous mutations have a maximal distance of 33 nucleotides to facilitate Illumina short-read sequencing. The introduced mutations were stably maintained as confirmed by Illumina sequencing of the stock virus. To evaluate the fitness of the BC virus, we compared the replication efficiency of WT and BC viruses in MDCK cells with MOI= 0.001 PFU/cell. BC virus showed slightly better growth than that of the WT virus under multi-cycle replication kinetics. We further evaluated the competitive fitness of the WT and BC viruses by infecting MDCK cells at MOI of 0.005 PFU/cell with WT and BC viruses mixed at 100:0, 80:20, 50:50, 20:80, and 0:100 ratios, respectively. Viral RNA was extracted from the viral inoculum and culture supernatants collected at 24h and 48h post-infection and amplified by RT-PCR. Sequences were determined using Illumina MiSeq. WT:BC mixed at 100:0 or 0:100 ratios remain stable at 24h or 48h post-infection. When WT:BC viruses were mixed at 80:20, 50:50, or 20:80, BC virus tend to gain dominance over the WT virus under the competitive condition. To further investigate onward transmission potential and transmission bottleneck of influenza viruses deposited at upper and lower respiratory tract, we inoculated donor ferrets with WT virus intra-nasally and BC virus intra-tracheally or vice versa. Nasal turbinate, bronchus, and the left lower lung lobe were collected from the inoculated ferrets on day 2 post-inoculation for Illumina sequencing. From ferrets inoculated with WT virus (intra-nasally) + BC virus (intra-tracheally) (n=3), gene segments derived from the WT virus were detected from the nasal turbinate and genes derived from the BC virus were predominantly detected in the bronchus and the left lower lung lobe. From ferrets inoculated with BC virus (intra-nasally) + WT virus (intra-tracheally) (n=3), gene segments derived from the BC virus were detected from the nasal turbinate and gene segments derived from the WT virus were detected in the bronchus and the left lower lung lobe. There was limited detection of mixed WT: BC sequences, suggesting limited genetic reassortment between WT and BC viruses at the sampled anatomic sites. We then monitored the genetic variant(s) transmitted to naïve ferrets from donors inoculated with WT virus (intra-nasally) + BC virus (intra-tracheally) or vice versa. Two naïve contacts were exposed to the exhaled breath of one inoculated donor for 8 hours on day 2 post-inoculation (of the donor). Nasal washes were collected from the donors and contacts to monitor the genetic variant that were passed from the donors to the contacts. Donor ferrets inoculated with WT virus (intra-nasally) + BC virus (intra-tracheally) shed WT virus in the nasal washes and transmitted the WT virus to exposed naïve contacts. In reverse, donor ferrets inoculated with BC virus (intra-nasally) + WT virus (intra-tracheally) shed BC virus in the nasal washes and transmitted the BC virus to exposed naïve contacts. The results further confirmed the importance of nasal infection for onward influenza transmission as observed in Aim 1. Collectively, our results demonstrate that onward aerosol transmission of influenza virus was mediated by airborne particles formed and released from the nasal epithelium cells of infected ferrets. Both research objectives were fully addressed.

17148416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17148416.value: This project aimed to investigate if influenza virus deposited at the upper or lower respiratory tract may subsequently influence infectious particles formation for onward transmission. Using intra-nasal and intra-tracheal inoculation as well as recombinant wild-type and barcode virus carrying synonymous mutations in each of the eight genes, we demonstrated that onward aerosol transmission of influenza virus was mediated by airborne particles formed from the nasal epithelium cells of infected ferrets. Early treatment with effective antivirals that block viral replication at nasal mucosa may help to reduce influenza onward transmission. Since avian influenza viruses are known to replicate more efficiently in the lungs with higher expression of alpha2,3-linked sialyl receptors, our results highlight the importance for avian influenza viruses to further adapt at the upper respiratory tract before they can acquire efficient transmissibility among humans. A manuscript describing the results of this study has been summarized and will be submitted for peer review. This project provided valuable opportunity to build collaboration with local and international investigators with different expertise, which may provide synergy for future research.

17148416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17148416.value: We demonstrated that influenza infection of nasal epithelial cells is critical for onward transmission. However, we did not determine the particle size formed and released from the infected nasal mucosa. With the use of the transmission chamber and impactors (Zhou et al. PNAS 2018), we may further investigate the particle size range mediating efficient onward transmission.

17148416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17148416.value: Influenza viruses are transmitted via virus-laden aerosols released from infected airway mucosa through breathing, talking, or coughing. The mechanisms driving the formation and release of virus-laden particles from influenza-infected airway mucosa remain poorly understood. We investigated if influenza virus infection at the upper (nasal mucosa) or lower (lungs) respiratory tract may subsequently influence infectious particles formation for onward transmission. Using intra-nasal and intra-tracheal inoculation as well as recombinant wild-type and barcode virus carrying synonymous mutations in each of the eight genes, we demonstrated that onward aerosol transmission of influenza virus was mediated by airborne particles formed from the nasal epithelium cells of infected ferrets. Effective antivirals that block viral replication at nasal mucosa may help to reduce influenza transmission during epidemics.

17149016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17149016.value: ABSTRACT Biodiversity is essential to ecosystem function and for provision of ecosystem services, and therefore preserving biodiversity is an important goal for society. The principal driver of biodiversity loss today is habitat destruction and loss. Urbanization is a growing factor leading to habitat loss, particularly in Asia. Urban habitats differ in significant ways from those they replace, and characteristics of both the physical and acoustic environment are altered. Cities are noisy, largely due to anthropogenic activities, particularly traffic noise. Chronic noise exposure is known to have deleterious effects on humans, and there is growing evidence that animals are affected similarly. One major effect of high amplitude low frequency traffic noise is to mask auditory communication signals essential for both territory defense and mate attraction. Potential consequences of masking include higher population densities, smaller territory sizes, and reduced reproductive success (i.e. fitness), suggesting that noise may pose significant selection pressure on such signals. Recent studies have shown that some bird species can adapt their signals to partially overcome masking effects, however, the consequences of this behaviour are unknown. We also know little about the relative costs and benefits related to signal changes. I propose to examine species’ response to urban noise by measuring song characteristics of several bird species in areas with different levels of exposure to traffic noise across Hong Kong. I will measure the costs of altered signals using two methods: 1) playback studies to evaluate whether altered signals equate to a loss of signal potency and 2) transmission studies to determine whether signal adjustments in noisy areas equate to increased transmission efficiency. Biodiversity conservation is an important goal in today’s society, Hong Kong included, and understanding the factors that lead to loss of diversity can critically inform conservation decisions. Anthropogenic noise is ubiquitous in urban areas, and the negative effects of chronic exposure to high levels of noise is a growing concern. Understanding which species can adapt and what the consequences are is essential to maintaining diversity in urban areas. 摘要 生物多樣性對發揮生態系統功能及提供生態系統服務至關重要，因此保護生物多樣性是當今社會的重要目標。目前生物多樣性喪失的主要驅動力是棲息地的毀滅和損失。城市棲息地與那些因城市化而被取代的棲息地有著顯著不同，無論是物理環境還是聲學環境特徵都有所改變。城市化是導致棲息地損失的一個愈發重要的因素，特別是在亞洲。例如，主要由於人類活動，特別是交通噪聲，城市很嘈雜。目前已知長期的噪音暴露會對人類造成有害影響，並且有越來越多的證據表明動物也受到相似的影響。其中，由高振幅低頻率的交通噪音造成的一個主要影響是屏障聽覺交流信號，而這種信號對於領土防禦和吸引配偶都至關重要。這種屏蔽的可能後果包括使種群密度變高，領土大小收縮，繁殖成功率下降（例如適應性），從而説明噪音可能造成對這種信號的顯著選擇壓力。最近的研究表明一些鳥類物種能夠調整信號去適應並部分克服屏蔽效應，然而，這種行爲的後果仍然未知。同時，我們對與信號變化相關的成本和收益也知之甚少。我提出通過測量全港不同交通噪音暴露水平地區的幾種鳥類物種歌聲特徵來檢驗物種對城市噪音的反應。我將採用以下兩種方法來測量信號改變的成本：1）通過回放研究評估信號改變是否等同於信號效力的損失；2）通過傳輸研究確定在嘈雜地區的信號調整是否等同於提高傳輸效率。保護生物多樣性是包括香港在內的當今社會的重要目標，理解導致多樣性損失的因素可以為保育決定提供重要信息。人類噪音在城市範圍無処不在，長期暴露於高水平噪音所帶來的消極影響正日益受到關注。理解哪些物種可以調整適應及其後果對維持城市地區的多樣性至關重要。

17149016.label: Realisation of objectives
17149016.value: Objective 1: Quantify the response of urban species to anthropogenic noise in Hong Kong. We recorded songs from all target species, plus seven additional species, across a range of background noise levels in Hong Kong. In total, we recorded more than 800 target individuals across Hong Kong, with sufficient samples recorded from fifteen species to include in our analyses. For each individual, we measured several characteristics of each least ten songs, including minimum frequency, maximum frequency and peak frequency, then correlated these values with background noise levels. We collected additional recordings of Oriental magpie-robins (hereafter 'magpie-robins') including extensive recordings across the territory and detailed mapping and recording of territories on campus, allowing us to look at song type sharing between neighbors and across the region. We discovered that in addition to calling in the winter non-breeding season, females also sing during the breeding season, so conducted analysis of both male and female songs. This lead to a collaboration with Cornell University on the form and function of female songs. For the amplitude measurements, we focused on one species, the black-collared starlings, as they often sing on exposed perches and we were able to get fairly accurate song measurements (this was prohibitively difficult in other species which often sing from within dense undergrowth). We measured frequency and amplitude and test the hypothesis that song frequency increases with song amplitude. Objective 2: Explore whether song repertoires differ between urban and rural populations, with the prediction that urban repertoires will be smaller than those of rural populations. We recorded sufficient magpie-robin samples to investigate repertoire size, and found that males typically have a single “advertising song” but several shorter songs/calls. We are continuing to work on this analysis, which will include analysis of variation within a vocal neighborhood (e.g. HKU campus) and across Hong Kong. In other species, we looked at variation across the noise gradient in different vocalization types for several species including Swinhoe’s white-eyes (comparing two different song types and alarm calls) and fork-tailed sunbirds (testing calls vs songs). For common tailorbirds, we extended the analysis by downloading song samples from sound recording libraries to represent variation throughout the range of this species, and using spatial analysis techniques tested whether range-wide song variation can be predicted by human-induced habitat changes (urbanization in particular). Objective 3: Determine whether any detected shifts in urban songs are biologically significant through the use of playback experiments. We conducted playback experiments with three focal species which showed significant shifts in song frequencies across a noise gradient: oriental magpie-robins, yellow-bellied prinias and common tailorbirds. For magpie-robins, we conducted playback experiments in two consecutive years in order to explore what factors contributed to the lack of differentiation between noisy and quiet songs. Objective 4: Measure sound transmission of urban and rural songs in urban habitats. We measured sound transmission in two species: common tailorbirds and oriental magpie-robins. For tailorbirds, we measured sound transmission in both noisy and quiet habitats, measuring excess attenuation, signal-to-noise ratio and tail-to-signal ratio at increasing distances from the playback speaker. For magpie-robins, we first conducted an analysis of perch height during vocalization behavior, creating a vertical behavior profile. We found that magpie-robins most typically sing from high vantage points >3m up to 30m high (from rooftops). We hypothesized that magpie-robins might sing higher in areas with more dense buildings as this might help increase the active space of their songs (ie around buildings). We made a first attempt to test this by measuring vertical and horizontal sound transmission for this species, with the prediction that songs would transmit clearly over larger distances in the vertical compared to the horizontal plain. Our preliminary work suggests that this is the case, but more work is needed on this particularly aspect of the project in order to test the actual active space of the songs from different vantage points.

While we don't have further objectives, we did extend this study to test the role of song in territorial defense and mate-guarding by conducting playback experiments on breeding and non-breeding territories. We found that males responded strongly to playbacks in the both seasons, while females responded more strongly to simulated intrusions in the winter than in the breeding season. This suggests that both female and male song have important fitness- related functions and that both are likely to be impacted by noise. We have also initiated a collaboration with a researcher at Cornell University to study the role of female song, and to investigate whether female song is influenced by the same environmental factors that impacts male songs.

17149016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17149016.value: Output 1: While many species sing with higher frequencies in noisy urban areas, it is not clear whether this is an adaptation to noise or a byproduct of singing louder in noisy areas (the Lombard effect). Few studies test song amplitude in the field as this is very difficult to measure. We tested the relationship between song amplitude and frequency in response to noise with black-collared starlings in Hong Kong. We found that this species sings with higher frequencies in noisy areas, but there was no correlation between urban noise and song amplitude. Contrary to the predictions, we found that frequency decreased when birds increased the amplitude of their songs, suggesting that the frequency shift itself is the adaptive response to noise. This paper has been written and will be submitted for publication imminently. Output 2: We recorded songs for 15 species across a noise gradient in Hong Kong, 3 with low frequencies (<1kHz), 6 with medium frequencies (1-3 kHz) and high minimum frequencies (>3kHz). Our prediction was that we would see the biggest shift in Fmin for birds in the medium frequency range, whose songs would overlap most with traffic noise, than for birds in the high frequency category. Those below 1000hz might not shift as too far to go. We found overall that 12 of the 15 species sang with higher frequencies in urban areas – 1 of the low frequency, all of the medium frequency, and surprisingly 4 of the 6 high frequency birds. The data have been analyzed and the manuscript is in preparation for the Journal of Animal Ecology. Output 3: To test whether songs with higher minimum frequencies lead to better transmission in the field, we combined playback experiments with tests of signal transmission in the environment. We predicted that birds in noisy areas would respond more aggressively to songs with higher Fmin as these songs transmitted more accurately in the noisy environment. We also predicted that noisy songs would transmit further in noisy environments. We conducted playback experiments on three species (magpie-robins, common tailorbirds, and yellow-bellied prinias). For magpie-robins, although we found that songs differed between noisy and rural sites, birds did not respond differently to songs from noisy or quiet areas, suggesting that magpie-robins do not differentiate between urban and rural songs. The manuscript is in preparation and will be submitted to Animal Behavior.

17149016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17149016.value: One logical extension of this project would be to expand the study regionally. We began expanding this work during the course of the study, in collaboration with Prof. Liu Yang at Sun Yat Sen University, recording oriental magpie robins in ten cities throughout the Pearl River Delta area. Studies of impacts of noise on communication have focused on either low frequency noise (e.g. traffic noise) or high frequency noise (e.g. cicadas in forest areas), but no studies have looked at the impacts of both high and low frequency noise simultaneously. In tropical urban areas, birds are often exposed to both low and high frequency noise simultaneously as cicadas are often present within cities. An interesting next step would be to study how birds would respond to being ‘squeezed’ from the top and bottom. The ultimate question is whether behavioral adjustments to noise have a positive or negative impact on and individual’s fitness. The next step would be to conduct studies on pairing and nesting success in noisy and quiet areas in order to understand the impacts of noise on fitness.

17149016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17149016.value: Anthropogenic noise in urban areas has impacts both on people and on wildlife, impacting communication, health and fitness. Low frequency background noise form traffic and machinery can mask animal signals, interrupting important processes of mate choice and territory defense. Some birds may try to avoid signal masking by altering their songs in urban areas, raising the frequency of their songs to be heard over the noise. Birds that are not able to shift their frequencies might be excluded from noisy urban areas. Even those that can adjust their songs could face other negative impacts such as decreased mating success (because female prefer males with lower songs), increased attenuation of higher frequencies, or lower reproductive success (because low quality males tend to be found in noisier habitats). We found that 11/15 bird species in Hong Kong sing with higher frequencies in Hong Kong, confirming that noise has a significant impact on urban birds. We found that for some species, these urban songs had higher transmission rates in noisy areas, and that the often small shifts were perceived by local birds. Understanding behavioral responses to urban noise will help us to better understand the impact of urbanization on local wildlife.

17149716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17149716.value: 乾燥綜合征（Sjogren's syndrome，SS）是一種常見的系統性自身免疫性疾病。 該疾病在臨床上主要表現為外分泌腺組織如淚腺和唾液腺受累，並呈現眼幹和口乾等主要症狀。雖然大量淋巴細胞浸潤唾液腺並形成灶狀聚集，但是浸潤的淋巴細胞對腺體破壞的病理學的機制還並不完全清楚。近期的研究揭示了白介素17（IL-17）可能在SS的疾病發展中起重要作用，然而，IL-17在調節自身免疫反應以及對腺體功能的破壞的分子機制還並不清楚。 我們的前期研究成功建立了實驗性乾燥綜合征（ESS）小鼠模型。該模型很好地模擬了人類SS的主要臨床症狀，並揭示了Th17細胞在SS發病過程中的關鍵作用。雖然目前的研究證實了IL-17在ESS疾病發展中對促進免疫炎症反應起了重要作用，但IL-17對外分泌腺，尤其是對唾液腺細胞的生理功能的調節作用尚不清楚。我們的前期研究發現IL-17對唾液腺泡上皮細胞的類膽鹼功能的激活有調節作用，從而導致腺體功能減弱，分泌唾液減少。另外，我們還觀察到慢性期ESS小鼠的唾液腺內呈現異位淋巴樣結構（ELS），而IL-17缺失的小鼠在免疫後無明顯的ELS。這一發現提示IL-17在慢性炎症中對腺體中ELS的形成有重要的作用。在此課題中，我們將研究IL-17調節腺體組織的炎症反應以及腺體功能的細胞學和分子學機制。並運用靶向IL-17分子的策略研究其對ESS疾病的治療作用。 我們預期的結果將進一步闡明IL-17在SS發病中的作用，並推進以此作為治療SS病人新靶標的研究。
