17154516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17154516.value: 鼻咽癌的一個最重要的特徵是與EB病毒的相關性，因為所有癌細胞都感染EB病毒。然而EB病毒在鼻咽癌發生發展的作用仍然不清楚。EB病毒在鼻咽癌細胞中最顯著的特點是表達一組BARTs 非編碼RNA和兩簇的miRNA， 但幾乎不表達其他病毒蛋白。根據這種現象，很自然的推測BARTs 的表達可能同鼻咽癌的致癌狀態有關。的確，我們的工作發現並已經報導了鼻咽癌病人血漿中的EB病毒miRNA，miR-7和miR-13，的水平可以作為鼻咽癌診斷和治療的標記物。所以，EB病毒BARTs 非編碼RNA和miRNA表達的調節機制可能對解開這些病毒表達物在鼻咽癌和其他EB病毒相關腫瘤的功能密切關聯。我們以前的工作發現C/EBP調節BARTs表達，我們前期的研究發現鑒定了BARTs啟動子帶有NF-κB調節位點， 並實驗證明這些位點可被NF-κB信號調節， 提示NF-κB信號傳導可能參與鼻咽癌細胞中BARTs表達的調節。因為EB病毒LMP1可激活NF-κB信號傳導， 而LMP1表達同時激活細胞免疫反應， 本課題提出EB病毒在鼻咽癌胞形成一個自動調節環來維持病毒的潛伏態， 在這個機制裏NF-κB信號和LMP1介導NF-κB激活正向調節BARTs表達，而EB病毒的BARTs 非編碼RNA和miRNA反過來保持EB病毒在鼻咽癌細胞的潛伏態不被免疫系統發現。 本研究將利用下面實驗來驗證上面提出的假設：首先我們將分析NF-κB信號和LMP1介導NF-κB激活如何還有在多大程度調節BARTs 非編碼RNA和miRNA在鼻咽癌細胞的表達；其次，因為BART miRNA已經報導可以負調節LMP1表達，我們將進一步鑒定調節LMP1表達的BARTs 非編碼RNA和miRNA具體類型；為證明NF-κB信號異常在鼻咽癌的作用並鑒定這信號是否可以作為一個可能的藥物靶標，研究將利用不同的NF-κB抑製劑來測試對BARTs 非編碼RNA和miRNA表達的影響；最後，研究將利用系列實驗方案來鑒定BARTs 非編碼RNA在鼻咽癌細胞中的功能。這個課題總的目標是揭示NF-κB信號傳導與BARTs 非編碼RNA和miRNA之間的自動調節環，和這些EB病毒表達產物在維持EB病毒在癌細胞惡性演變過程中保持潛伏態的作用。

17154516.label: Realisation of objectives
17154516.value: This project has completed all the objectives proposed in the original proposal. Major achievements are summarized below: 1. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) expresses a family of BART transcripts, composed of miR-BARTs and lnc-BARTs, in all forms of latency. The mechanisms by which these BART RNAs are regulated may be important to understand the function of BART miRNAs in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and other EBV associated tumours. We identified NF-κB motifs in the BART promoter region and investigated whether and to what extent the BART promoter is activated by NF-κB signaling and showed that the BART promoter responds to activation by p50/p65 and is bound by p50. Using inhibitor specifically targeting NF-κB signaling, we found expression of EBV BARTs is significantly downregulated, suggesting targeting constitutively activated NF-κB signaling may be a therapeutic strategy for NPC (Research output 1-3, 5 and research output conferences 1). 2. Furthermore, we found the BART promoter is also activated by LMP1 mediated NF-B signaling, while mutated LMP1 with a defect in the ability to activate NF-kapaB fails to up-regulate the BART promoter. BART miRNA has been previously reported to negatively regulate LMP1. Our results show that several BART miRNAs target the 3-UTP of LMP1 to down-regulate LMP1 expression. In EBV infected NPC cells, besides EBV expressed viral RNAs, BARTs and EBERs, only the EBNA1 and LMP1 proteins of EBV are expressed (Research output 1-3, 5 and research output conferences 1). 3. We found that Qp, which drives EBNA1 transcription in NPC cells, is also, at least partly, regulated by NF-kapaB signaling, suggesting NF-B is the critical cellular signaling pathway in EBV latency and aberrant signaling of NF-kapaB is associated with NPC oncogenesis (Research output 1, Verhoeven RJ. et al., Cancers 2018). 4. Our results demonstrate that there is an auto-regulatory loop for maintenance of EBV latency in NPC cells, in which LMP1 mediated NF-kapaB signaling regulates EBV gene expression while BART miRNAs in turn keep the levels of LMP1 in check to evade immune surveillance. Aberrant NF-B signaling and expression of BARTs form an autoregulatory loop for maintaining EBV latency in NPC cells. Thus, targeting NF-kapaB signaling to interrupt EBV latency may provide new options for NPC treatment. 5. To further delineate biological significance of BART transcripts (miR-BARTs and lnc-BART), we characterized BART transcripts as nuclear lnc-BART and function as epigenetic modulator in NPC cells. We identified lnc-BART regulated IKAROS family zinc finger 3 (IKZF3/Aiolos) in NPC cells. BART lncRNA associated with the CBP/p300 complex and RNA polymerase II (Pol II) in the nucleus, suggesting that BART lncRNAs may mediate epigenetic regulation of gene expression through interaction with the chromatin remodeling machinery (Research output 2. Verhoeven R et al., Frontiers in Oncology, 2019, and Research output conferences 1-3)

17154516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17154516.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is one of the key etiological factors associated with oncogenic progress of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). In NPC cells, EBV expresses very few viral proteins in its latent state, which is believed to facilitate evasion of immune surveillance, but consistently high levels of long non-coding RNAs, (lnc-BARTs), which are derived from multiple exons in the BamHI-A rightward transcript (BART) region of the EBV genome. However, details of the biological functions of these EBV-encoded long non-coding RNAs remain elusive. This project has provided experimental evidence to show that lnc-BARTs function as regulatory RNAs in modulating core network activity through epigenetic to maintain EBV latency in NPC cells. Key findings include: 1. We have systematically characterized that NF-kapaB signaling regulates EBV lnc-BARTs in NPC cells; 2. We first identified that EBV lnc-BARTs localize in nuclear speckles, highly dynamic subdomains of the nucleus enriched with transcription, elongation and splicing factors. To better understand the role of lnc-BARTs in NPC cells, CRISPR-Cas technology was used to achieve stable-knockdown of lnc-BARTs in the EBV-harbouring C666-1 NPC cell line; 3. EBV latent genes EBNA1 and LMP1 is also down-regulated following the knockdown of lnc-BARTs; 4. It is discovered that knockdown of lnc-BARTs resulted in downregulation of the oncogenes MYC and BCL2. In addition, ATAC sequencing showed that the depletion of lnc-BARTs induced apoptosis and decreased accessibility of open chromatin in NPC cells; 5. Our study found that lnc-BARTs physically interact with a complex consisting of several transcription factors, including BRD4 and KDM1B. 6. Notably, we found that lnc-BARTs co-localize with BRD4 and positive transcription elongation factor (P-TEFb) in nuclear speckles; these complexes can be disrupted by treatment with JQ1, a competitive inhibitor of BRD4. 7. This study demonstrated that lnc-BARTs bind directly to BRD4 and act as a scaffold to mediate an association between BRD4 and the splicing factor SC35. Moreover, EBV lnc-BARTs are also involved in the P-TEFb regulatory machinery via their association with BRD4. 8. BRD4-ChIP analysis further demonstrated that lnc-BARTs recruit the BRD4-mediated epigenetic modulator complex to the promoter regions of MYC and BCL2. In summary, this project provides the first experimental evidence of the mechanisms underlying the critical role of lnc-BARTs in maintaining EBV latency and driving tumorigenesis in NPC. EBV lnc-BARTs modulate the expression of genes associated with tumor apoptosis during EBV latency through functional interaction with BRD4- and KDM1B-associated regulatory machinery in NPC cells.

17154516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17154516.value: Advances in understanding the versatility of various host lncRNAs in cancers and immune cells in recent years has provided a unique opportunity for studying the role of high-level expression of BART lncRNA in NPC. EBV utilizes a strategy to express non-antigenic lnc-BART RNAs, which act as epigenetic modulators, affecting host gene expression to generate a cellular microenvironment conducive to EBV latency in NPC. Aberrant expression of genes regulated by BART lncRNA may consequently lead to evasion of the immune response, cancer progression and acquisition of metastatic properties in NPC cells. EBV lnc-BART RNAs are among the few viral products expressed in EBV reservoirs in vivo and findings from this study will also provide insight into the role of lnc-BART RNAs in resting B cells latently infected with EBV. More importantly, understanding the cellular mechanisms/pathways regulated by lnc-BART RNAs will help identify novel biomarkers for the detection and treatment of EBV associated cancers, and aid in development of new drugs targeting aberrantly expressed host genes in NPC.

17154516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17154516.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is one of the etiological factors for several human cancers including nasopharyngeal carcinoma. One of the important factors hampered the study for understadning the role of EBV oncogenesis is that EBV maintain latency and express few viral proteins in NPC cells. About 30 years ago, a family of transcripts, designated as BamHI-A rightward transcripts (BARTs), was first identified at high level in NPC cells but no function was identified. This project for the first time characterized BARTs as a functional long non-coding RNA (lnc-RNA), lnc-BART, in NPC cells by interacting with cellular regulatory complex including BRD4 and splicing factor SC35. It is found that EBV utilize this mechanism to achieve a cellular environment for the latency in NPC cells. However, interaction between lnc-BART and BRD4 results in the aberrant other genes including oncogenes such as MYC and BCL2 which has antiapoptotic effect. Therefore, this study revealed that EBV lnc-BART modulates host gene expression and maintains EBV latency by interfering with host epigenetic mechanism leading to aberrant expression of a subset of host genes. The altered host gene expression in EBV-infected cells lead to immune evasion, progression, and metastasis of NPC.

17154816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17154816.value: The vegetable/meat soups are popular in our diet for their appealing taste and nutritional value. More recently, the health benefits of their nutrients and phytochemicals, such as flavonoids found in vegetables, are well recognized. However, the presence of flavonoids in foods including soups subjected to thermal processing would very likely directly interact with electrophilic compounds that arise at different stages of the Maillard and/or lipid peroxidation reaction to form novel chemicals, thus affecting the potential health benefits of the food products. Our pioneering research work has suggested that naringenin, a flavonoid rich in tomato had high reactivity towards Maillard intermediates, thus suppressing the formation of genotoxic heterocyclic amine, PhIP in fried beef patties with the formation of two new bioactives, 6-CEPN and 8-CEPN. These two newly formed compounds showed excellent anti-cancer activity. We also discovered that phloridzin and epicatechin could effectively trap methylglyoxal and acrolein, two key Maillard and lipid peroxidation reactive intermediates even at room temperature to form novel adducts. These studies strongly support our hypothesis of an active role of flavonoids in these reactions and the formation of new beneficial compounds in fried meat products. However, little is known about the stability, reactivity, bioactivity change of flavonoids in vegetable/meat soups which is one typical food with high flavonoid content and more related to our daily dietary habit. In the current research, we want to employ one major dietary flavonoid, quercetin and one quercetin-containing vegetable, onion to investigate the mechanism of their chemical changes in beef soups; with the application of total cellular antioxidant assay, we are planning to study the impact of soup stewing on the antioxidant activity of flavonoids; with the application of cell culture studies using colon cancer cell lines, we will further evaluate whether the chemical changes of quercetin or its derivatives can induce stronger/weaker tumor cell-selective cytotoxicity, and impact differently on the related molecular signaling pathways (programmed cell death and cell cycle and etc.) through genome-wide transcriptome expression profiling by high through-put RNA-seq in combination with molecular biological and biochemical experiments. This research will help to figure out the reactivity and bioactivity change of quercetin and related compounds in real cooked food systems, providing guidance for similar type of phenolic compounds. It may also help us to discover new bioactives from soups and fully enjoy the health benefits of soups. 蔬菜肉湯因為特有的口感和營養價值在我們的日常生活中大受歡迎；它們富含的營養素及植物化合物的健康功效也廣為認可。但是在熱加工過程中，它們的營養素和植物化合物，特別是蔬菜中的黃酮，可能發生複雜的化學變化從而影響他們的營養價值。美拉德反應，脂質過氧化反應及焦糖化是食品中最重要的反應；它們被認為是食品風味、色澤、營養變化，及食品中生成有毒的/有益成分的主要貢獻者。傳統上一般認為黃酮僅僅作為抗氧化劑來調節上述的反應的氧化過程。但是近年來，越來越多的證據傾向於支持某些黃酮由於它們的親核化學屬性，可能直接參與美拉德/脂質過氧化中不同階段的化學反應；在最終食物產品形成有益於人類健康的新的化學物質。然而以前很少有人關注這方面的研究。 我們前期的開拓性研究工作發現在油炸的牛肉餅中，柚皮素（番茄中富含的黃酮）不僅可以抑制有致癌、致基因突變的雜環胺的生成，而且可以通過參與美拉德反應誘導有優異的抗腫瘤活性的化學物質6-CEPN和8-CEPN的生成。 同時我們也發現其他黃酮，如根皮苷和表兒茶素能有效地捕集美拉德和脂質過氧化反應的兩個關鍵中間體，甲基乙二醛和丙烯醛；即使在室溫下也能形成新的加合物。所有这些发现都有力支持了我們的推断：黃酮在复杂食品反应中发挥着积极作用及热加工会影响黃酮的生物活性。以上前期工作為我們考察富含黃酮的蔬菜肉湯中的黃酮在燉湯過程中的化學和生物活性變化提供理論基礎。 在本研究中我們將研究一個重要的膳食類黃酮，槲皮素和洋蔥（一種富含槲皮素的蔬菜），在牛肉湯中的化學變化及其對肉類養分釋放的影響; 通過應用總細胞抗氧化法，我們計劃研究湯燉對黃酮類化合物的抗氧化活性的影響; 通過使用結腸癌細胞系，我們將進一步評估槲皮素及其相關物質在燉湯過程的化學變化是增強抑或減弱槲皮素的抗癌活性，以及如何影響槲皮素預防癌症的分子機理。 本研究將有助於弄清槲皮素在燉湯過程中的化學和生物活性變化；為槲皮素及其相似類型的酚類化合物在食品中的應用提供理論基礎。 本研究還可以幫助我們從蔬菜肉湯中發現新的生物活性物質，讓大眾更好地享受湯的健康益處。

17154816.label: Realisation of objectives
17154816.value: In thermally processed foods, some key food reactions including the Maillard reaction play important roles in improving food quality (sensory, nutritional and safety). In recent years, emerging evidence tends to support that certain flavonoids might directly interact with reactive intermediary compounds that arise at different stages of the Maillard reaction to form novel compounds. More interestingly, some of the newly formed adducts have been shown to be potential antioxidative and/or cancer chemopreventive agents. These studies suggest an active role of flavonoids during thermal processing of food and the potential to form new beneficial compounds in these food products. This research work is studying the active role of some representative polyphenols, such as quercetin in a soup system. 1. Evaluation of the chemical changes of quercetin and onion in beef soup by application of instrumental analysis (HPLC, LC-MS/MS, and NMR) and classic chromatographic methods. In this research to achieve our research goals, we have designed the onion/beef soup model food system to study the chemical changes of flavonoids in cooking. Through the instrumental analysis (HPLC, LC-MS and NMR), we found the formation of new chemicals in soups with the chemical reaction between flavonoids (quercetin) and Maillard reaction intermediates. The newly formed chemical was found to be 8-CEPQ [8-C-(E-phenylethenyl)-quercetin], 6-CEPQ [6-C-(E-phenylethenyl)-quercetin], and related degradation, oxidation, and reaction products (such as 3',5,7-trihydroxy-4'-methoxyflavanone, myricetin, isoquercetin, benzoquinone). 2. Evaluation of the total antioxidant change of quercetin-fortified beef soup or onion/beef soup at different time points, correlate the bioactivity changes with the chemical change. Quercetin and cinnamaldehyde, two representative polyphenols were further selected to study their impacts on soups’ antioxidant activity, plus their effects on the release of total sugar, solid matter, water-soluble protein, fatty acids, minerals and amino acids in soups from beef for a period of 240 minutes. The fortification with quercetin was found to enhance the antioxidant activity of the soup. Although quercetin might react with certain soup ingredients or degrade during the heating process, however, the antioxidant activity did not show significant change during the heating time (240 minutes). However, quercetin was found to prevent the loss of unsaturated fatty acids. The addition of quercetin and cinnamaldehyde would lead to a decrease in methionine and aspartic acid in beef soup. Quercetin increased the zinc content in beef soup, while cinnamaldehyde caused it to decrease. Furthermore, different cooking methods were tried to evaluate their impact on the formation of beneficial/potential harmful compounds (such as PhIP) in beef soup preparation. LC-MS was applied for the comparison of PhIP formed in chemical models using microwave heating and conductive heating. Results showed that PhIP was produced time dependently under both heating conditions. Microwave heating produced a smaller amount of PhIP compared with conductive heating. Moreover, quercetin showed a more potent inhibitory effect on PhIP formation in microwave heating systems than in conductive heating models. The amount of beneficial 6-CEPQ and 8-CEPQ produced in chemical models and onion/beef soup using microwave heating was about 5 and 1.5 times more than using conductive heating, respectively. Our results demonstrate that microwave heating was a much safer and healthier thermal processing technology than conventional heating in terms of formation of less mutagenic PhIP and production of more human beneficial compounds 6-CEPQ and 8-CEPQ. 3. Evaluate whether the chemical changes of quercetin can induce stronger/weaker tumor cell-selective cytotoxicity, and impact differently on the related biological processes (cell cycle and programmed cell death and etc.) through genome-wide transcriptome expression profiling by RNA-seq in combination with molecular biological and biochemical experiments, and identification of some new bioactives from soups. We further evaluated the anticancer activity difference between their newly formed chemicals and quercetin. We determined the inhibitory effect of on human colon cancer cells and did not find any apoptotic features that we examined in colon cancer cells, including Hoechst 33342 staining and cleaved PARP in response to 8-CEPQ treatment. Moreover, the pancaspase inhibitor Z-VAD did not attenuate the increased cell death induced by 8-CEPQ, further confirming 8-CEPQ-induced cell death is not via caspase-dependent apoptosis in colon cancer cells, different from the original compound, quercetin. The inability to link apoptosis to the cell death observed in SW620 and HCT116 cells exposed to 8-CEPQ prompted us to consider whether the compound induced a non-apoptotic form of cell death. We next examined autophagy, as this process has recently attracted increasing attention as a means to induce cancer cell death. Indeed, we found that colon cancer cells exposed to 8-CEPQ showed distinct morphological and biochemical features of autophagy. Subsequent evaluation found that inhibition of autophagy with specific siRNAs targeting two key autophagic proteins Atg7 and Beclin-1 attenuated rather than aggravated cell death in response to 8-CEPQ treatment. These results support that 8-CEPQ induces autophagy-mediated cell death in colon cancer cells. MAPK signaling pathways have been shown to regulate autophagy. Interestingly, our results showed that JNK pathway is not involved in 8-CEPQ induced autophagy as evidenced by the fact that 8-CEPQ did not modulate JNK phosphorylation, and that the JNK inhibitor SP600125 could not block the 8-CEPQ-induced decrease in cell viability in SW620 and HCT116 cells. Moreover, treatment with 8-CEPQ induced phosphorylation of extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK). Inhibition of ERK phosphorylation by the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK)/ERK inhibitor U0126 attenuated 8-CEPQ-induced autophagy and reversed 8-CEPQ-mediated cell growth inhibition. These findings demonstrate a key role of ERK in the 8-CEPQ-mediated autophagic process in colon cancer cells. These results showed the newly formed 8-CEPQ showed different inhibitory activity against colon cancer cell from the original compound, quercetin with different action mechanism.

17154816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17154816.value: In summary, the results from the present study provide strong evidence that flavonoids in soup have an active role, and they can participate into food chemical reactions with the formation of new chemical adducts during the cooking process. Meantime with the fortification of flavonoids in soup, the antioxidant activity would be enhanced. In addition, flavonoids have an impact of the release of soup nutritional components such as the release of total sugar, solid matter, water-soluble protein, fatty acids, minerals and amino acids in soups with a positive role to preserve beneficial polyunsaturated fatty acids. Furthermore, we found that different cooking methods had different effects on the formation of harmful/beneficial compounds. Our results demonstrated that microwave heating was a much safer and healthier thermal processing technology than conventional heating in terms of formation of less mutagenic PhIP and production of more human beneficial compounds 6-CEPQ and 8-CEPQ. With biochemical/molecular biological approach we demonstrated that the newly adduct 8-CEPQ suppressed proliferation and caused G2 phase arrest in colon cancer cells. Based on immunofluorescent staining assay, western blot assay, and RNA knockdown data, we found that 8-CEPQ did not cause apoptotic cell death. Instead, it induced autophagic cell death. Moreover, treatment with 8-CEPQ induced phosphorylation of extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK). Inhibition of ERK phosphorylation by the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK)/ERK inhibitor U0126 attenuated 8-CEPQ-induced autophagy and reversed 8-CEPQ-mediated cell growth inhibition, with different action mechanism from the original compound, quercetin. Our data indicates that quercetin in onion/beef soup, which is widely consumed in many countries, could be converted to some novel adducts such as 6-CEPQ, 8-CEPQ. The anticancer activity of these adducts demonstrated in multiple in vitro assays implies that the consumption of this kind of soup and other similar food products processed under similar conditions may have the potential to confer extra health benefits. The research work has resulted into publication of 5 research papers, mainly in tier 1 SCI journals in the area of Food Science and Technology such as Molecular Nutrition & Food Research, and Food & Function.

17154816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17154816.value: The change of flavonoids and the participation of flavonoids in Maillard reaction in soup should be investigated in a more complicated system with the consideration of the participation of other food components. More detailed metabolomics analysis should be performed to analyze all kinds of metabolites in soup.

17154816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17154816.value: The vegetable/meat soups are popular in our diet for their appealing taste and nutritional value. More recently, the health benefits of their nutrients and phytochemicals, such as flavonoids found in vegetables, are well recognized. However, the presence of flavonoids in foods including soups subjected to thermal processing would very likely directly interact with electrophilic compounds that arise at different stages of the Maillard and/or lipid peroxidation reaction to form novel chemicals, thus affecting the potential health benefits of the food products. Through our study, we found that certain flavonoids could participate into complex food chemical reaction resulting the formation of beneficial bioactives. These bioactives showed better anticancer activity than the original flavonoids with a new action mechanism.

17155216.label: Realisation of objectives
17155216.value: Antimicrobial resistance is one of the major global healthcare issues. Persisters as a tiny subset of microbial survivors are highly tolerant to lethal dosage of antimicrobials and critically account for the persistence/recurrence of chronic infections/inflammatory diseases. Periodontitis as a common biofilm-associated inflammatory disease is one of the major oral disease burdens worldwide. It badly affects oral health and is closely associated with various systemic diseases/disorders like diabetes/cardiovascular disease. Porphyromonas gingivalis is the ‘keystone’ periodontopathogen and significantly drives the shift of microbe-host symbiosis to dysbiosis, thereby contributing to the pathogenesis of periodontitis. The main research work, findings and outputs are summarized as follows: 1) Characteristics of metronidazole (MTZ)-treated P. gingivalis persisters (M-PgPs). Our pioneering study shows for the first time the existence of non-heritable MTZ-tolerant P. gingivalis (ATCC 33277) persisters, and identifies their underlying survival mechanisms including regulating cellar redox state, repressing heme/iron utilization, dormancy and enhanced stress response (Li et al 2018/Paper 4). The microscopic characters of M-PgPs cannot be affected by MTZ (Wang et al 2020, Paper 5). 2) Adhesion and invasion ability of M-PgPs to human gingival epithelial cells (HGECs). The M-PgPs remain to adhere to the cell surfaces and invade the cytoplasts as P. gingivalis, while heat-killed M-PgPs lose such pathogenic abilities. M-PgPs alter their cell membrane structure and lead to the generation of membrane ruffles, thereby facilitating their invasion of HGECs. Similar proportions of HGECs can be adhered to or invaded by M-PgPs and P. gingivalis. These findings suggest that M-PgPs essentially retain pathogenic virulence and facilitate their invasive propensity and evasion of host defence (Wang et al 2020, Paper 5). 3) The inhibitory effects of M-PgPs on the expression of pro- inflammatory cytokines in HGECs. Live P. gingivalis cells enable to markedly suppress the upregulated expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines in HGECs. Notably, the M-PgPs exhibit similar inhibiting effects on the expression of IL-6 and IL-8 through their thermosensitive proteins. These findings suggest that P. gingivalis intrinsically develops core strategies like formation of persisters to escape host defense mechanisms for survival and recurrence under harsh conditions like lethal dosages of antimicrobials, and critically contributes to periodontal pathogenesis (Wang et al 2018/2019, Abstracts 3/4; Wang et al 2020, Paper 5). 4) M-PgPs perturb innate immunity in HGECs via upregulating FOXO signaling pathway. The pro-inflammatory cytokines are significantly downregulated, while anti-inflammatory cytokines are upregulated in M-PgPs-treated HGECs. Importantly, the forkhead box protein O (FOXO) signaling pathway like FOXO1 is upregulated in both groups. There findings indicate that M-PgPs enable to perturb innate host response, via upregulating FOXO signaling pathway, and therefore targeting FOXO pathway could be a potential approach to tackling P. gingivalis-related diseases (Wang et al 2020a, Abstract 5). 5) M-PgPs upregulate the immuno-inflammatory response in THP-1 cells via manipulating the imbalance of M1/M2 macrophages. M-PgPs markedly upregulate the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines in THP-1 macrophages. The expression levels of M1 macrophage surface receptors (e.g., CD 40) increased, while those of M2 macrophage surface receptors (e.g., CD 163/CD 206) decreased. Our findings suggest that M-PgPs-induced destruction of periodontal tissues may be related to the imbalance of M1/M2 macrophage phenotypes. Thus, targeting the polarization of macrophage could be an alternative strategy to favourably modulate M-PgPs-induced immuno-inflammatory response for promoting tissue homeostasis. 6) Bismuth drugs and nanomedicines as novel approaches to dampening P. gingivalis and P. gingivalis persisters formation. We have synthesized the mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) with two featured morphologies (nanosphere and nanowire), and then chlorhexidine (CHX) has been successfully encapsulated in these nanoparticles for testing their antibacterial effects on selected oral pathogens (Seneviratne et al 2014). The nano-encapsulation enhances the efficiency of CHX via a prolonged releasing mode/close interactions with the microbes, while the nano-encapsulated CHX cannot effectively eliminate all the bacteria (Li et al 2016). Therefore, we have further exploited the potential effects of other approaches against P. gingivalis/P. gingivalis persisters. Bismuth drugs have been commonly used for controlling Helicobacter pylori infection in medical practice. Our recent pioneering study demonstrates that bismuth drugs like colloidal bismuth subcitrate (CBS) markedly suppress P. gingivalis in its planktonic, biofilm and intracellular states, via disturbing iron acquisition, energy metabolism/virulence and inactivating key enzymes (Cheng et al 2019, Paper 9). Herein, the internalized P. gingivalis in human cells can be effectively suppressed by bismuth, but not the antibiotics like MTZ. The immuno-inflammatory responses perturbed by P. gingivalis are favorably modulated by bismuth drugs in host cells like THP-1 macrophages. We have developed the novel bismuth-doped carbon dots (Bi-CD) (Li et al 2019) to target multiple pathogens like Candida albicans and P. gingivalis. The constructed Bi-CD with good water solubility exhibit potent anti-bacterial effects on P. gingivalis. The as-synthesized Bi-CD present traceable intense blue fluorescence with maximum excitation/emission wavelengths around 360/445 nm. Particularly, Bi-CD obtained from citric acid and ammonium bismuth citrate with equal mass display the lowest minimum inhibitory concentrations. These findings show the potent suppression of Bi-CD on P. gingivalis. Further study would be undertaken on P. gingivalis persisters. 7) Synergistic effects of bismuth drugs plus commonly used antibiotics for dampening P. gingivalis persisters formation. Then, we have further explored the potential synergistic effects of bismuth drugs like CBS combined with antibiotics like MTZ on the formation of P. gingivalis persisters. Importantly, P. gingivalis persisters can be totally eradicated in planktonic mode (PFR: 0) and remarkably supressed in biofilm mode (PFR: 10-6), by CBS plus MTZ. No significant cytotoxicity is found. These exciting results reveal that synergistic use of bismuth drugs and metronidazole can dramatically tackle the formation of P. gingivalis persisters, and such novel approach may contribute to effectively controlling periodontitis and P. gingivalis-related systemic diseases (Wang et al 2020b, Abstract 6). 8) Development and refinement of amine-modified mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) containing antimicrobials/anti-inflammatory agents. Micro-environmental conditions like uncontrolled inflammation significantly affect the pathogenicity of P. gingivalis (Jin 2020). Based upon our recent RGC-funded work on development of MSNs-encapsulated antimicrobials (Seneviratne et al., 2014; Leung et al., 2016; Li et al., 2016), we have newly synthesized the MSNs with amine-modification to successfully encapsulate baicalein/baicalin, and assessed the cellular uptake of MSNs-encapsulated baicalein. Nano-encapsulated baicalein exhibits remarkably anti- inflammatory effects in HGECs, via effective loading, releasing and cellular internalization approaches (Li et al 2017, Paper 1). This finding highlights the great potential of nanomaterial-based drug delivery systems, and helps further develop novel anti-inflammatory agents/antimicrobials for oral/periodontal healthcare. This innovative work encourages us to further investigate the potential effects of MSNs-encapsulated antimicrobials on the formation and eradication of M-PgPs. 9) Identifying Raman features for P. gingivalis/M-PgPs. We have also tried to identify the Raman features for P. gingivalis and its persisters, using the latest Raman-Activated Cell Sorting technology in collaboration with our co-workers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Our preliminary study suggests that it is rather challenging to precisely isolate P. gingivalis persisters at extremely low abundance from un-lysed P. gingivalis cells after MTZ treatments. Anyway, we have successfully tested ampicillin-treated E. coli persisters as our first experimental model. As such, the Raman features for E. coli persisters have been identified, and meanwhile D2O-based single-cell Raman microspectroscopy (D2O-Raman) has been used to investigate the metabolic activities of Type I and Type II E. coli persisters. These promising results facilitate our further investigation on the phenotypes and functionality of P. gingivalis persisters in the near future.

17155216.value: 1) We confirm for the first time the existence of non-heritable metronidazole (MTZ)-tolerant P. gingivalis persisters (M-PgPs), and identify their microscopic characters, and reveal their underlying survival mechanisms including regulating cellar redox state, repressing heme/iron utilization, dormancy and enhanced stress response (Li et al 2017, Abstract 1; Li et al 2018, Paper 4; Wang et al 2020, Paper 5). 2) M-PgPs retain their pathogenic virulence (e.g., adhesion to/invasion of host cells like human gingival epithelial cells, HGECs) and facilitate their invasive propensity and evasion of host defence (Wang et al 2020, Paper 5). 3) P. gingivalis intrinsically develops core strategies like formation of persisters to escape host defense mechanisms for survival and recurrence under harsh conditions like lethal dosages of antimicrobials, and critically contributes to periodontal pathogenesis (Wang et al 2020, Paper 5). 4) M-PgPs perturb innate immunity in HGECs through upregulating the FOXO signaling pathway, thereby targeting the FOXO pathway like FOXO 1 may be a potential approach to tackling P. gingivalis-related diseases for oral and general health (Wang et al 2020a, Abstract 5). 5) M-PgPs upregulate the immuno-inflammatory response in THP-1 cells via manipulating the imbalance of M1/M2 macrophages. Thus, targeting the polarization of macrophage may be an alternative strategy to favourably modulate M-PgPs-induced immuno-inflammatory response for promoting tissue homeostasis. 6) Our pioneering study demonstrates that bismuth drugs like colloidal bismuth subcitrate markedly suppress P. gingivalis in its planktonic, biofilm and intracellular states, via disturbing iron acquisition, energy metabolism/virulence and inactivating key enzymes. The internalized P. gingivalis in human cells can be effectively suppressed by bismuth drugs, but not the antibiotics like MTZ; and the immuno-inflammatory responses perturbed by P. gingivalis are favorably modulated by bismuth drugs in host cells like THP-1 macrophages (Cheng et al 2019, Paper 9). 7) Our newly developed bismuth-doped carbon dots (Bi-CD) have good water solubility and potent anti-bacterial effects against P. gingivalis. 8) There are synergistic effects of bismuth drugs plus antibiotics (e.g., colloidal bismuth subcitrate + metronidazole) for dampening the formation and eradication of M-PgPs. Such novel approach may contribute to effectively controlling periodontitis and P. gingivalis-related systemic diseases (Wang et al 2020b, Abstract 6). 9) Nano-encapsulated baicalein exhibits remarkably anti- inflammatory effects in HGECs, via effective loading/releasing and cellular internalization approaches (Li et al 2017, Paper 1), highlighting the great potential of nanomaterial-based drug delivery systems as novel anti-inflammatory agents/antimicrobials for oral/periodontal healthcare via tackling the formation and eradication of M-PgPs.

17155216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17155216.value: 1) This study demonstrates for the first time i) the existence/characters of P. gingivalis persisters (M-PgPs), ii) their underlying survival mechanisms/abilities to adhere to and invade host cells and iii) M-PgPs-induced disturbance of innate immunity in HGECs/THP-1 cells. As P. gingivalis is the ‘keystone’ pathogen of periodontal disease, our new discoveries on P. gingivalis persisters are of great importance for further understanding on the essence of this key pathogen/its pathogenicity, and contributing to developing novel tackling strategy/approaches for precision intervention. 2) Our findings on M-PgPs-induced perturbance of innate host defense via manipulating FOXO signaling pathway suggest that targeting the pathway like FOXO 1 may be a new approach to tackling P. gingivalis-related diseases. We would conduct further investigation along this line. 3) Our exciting findings on bismuth drugs against P. gingivalis, bismuth-doped nanomedicines and the synergistic bismuth drugs-metronidazole effects tackling the formation/eradication of M-PgPs, strongly encourage further investigations on these novel approaches to precisely controlling periodontitis and P. gingivalis-related systemic diseases for oral/periodontal and general health. 4) It is encouraging to seek major competitive grants to deepen basic research and relevant translational/clinical studies, and commit to publish high-impact papers and file patent applications for technical/clinical innovation and advancing oral/periodontal healthcare.

17155216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17155216.value: Periodontal/gum disease (gingivitis and periodontitis) attracts big public attention worldwide. It is the most common disease in humans (Guinness World Records, 2001) and closely links to major systemic diseases like diabetes. The 1st global burden of disease study shows that severe periodontitis is the 6th most prevalent one of all diseases/conditions investigated with 11.2% of global population affected (Kassebaum et al 2014) and huge socio-economic impacts (Listl et al 2015). Everyone should enhance the awareness of oral/gum diseases and healthcare for better quality of life and wellbeing. Porphyromonas gingivalis is the key bug/bacterium of gum disease and involves in common systemic diseases like heart disease/dementia. It is essential to understand its molecular profiles and particularly how it remains survival after various treatments. This study finds for the first time i) the existence/characters of P. gingivalis persisters (a tiny subset of survivors following killing dose treatments of metronidazole), ii) their survival mechanisms/abilities to disturb innate immunity; and iii) bismuth drugs/bismuth-doped nanomedicines against P. gingivalis and the synergistic bismuth drugs-metronidazole effects on P. gingivalis persisters. These new discoveries enhance our understanding on the essence of this pathogen and contribute to developing novel strategy/approaches to precisely controlling gum disease for oral/general health.

17156016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17156016.value: Equilibrative nucleoside transporter-2 (ENT2) is very special among nucleoside transporters. In addition to nucleosides, ENT2 also transports nucleobases such as hypoxanthine. ENT2 is highly expressed in skeletal muscle but its physiological function is not known. ENT2-knockout animal model is not available. The use of knockout animal model may also be limited by the possibility that other nucleoside and/or nucleobase transporters are up-regulated to compensate the genetically knockout of ENT2. Another approach to study the functions of ENT2 is to use a pharmacological agent which can block ENT2 specifically. Unfortunately, all nucleoside transporter inhibitors in the market are specific to ENT1 but not ENT2. Recently, a series of novel compounds were screened in our laboratory. We found that 4-{[4-(2-fluorophenyl) piperazin-1-yl] methyl}-6-imino-N-(naphthalen-2-yl)-1,3,5-triazin-2-amine (FPMINT) may be a potential specific inhibitor of ENT2. 10 µM of PFMINT could completely inhibit ENT2 activity but had no effect on ENT1. We believe that PFMINT may serve as an important tool to reveal the physiological functions of ENT2 in our body. We hypothesize that ENT2, through the control of hypoxanthine transport, is important in regulation of adenine nucleotide pool and the production of reactive oxygen species. To support this hypothesis, our preliminary study has demonstrated that PFMINT could increase the intracellular levels of ATP and reactive oxygen species. There are three objectives in this proposed study. First, the mechanism(s) of inhibition of PFMINT on ENT2 will be investigated. A transfected ENT2 cell model will be used and the substrate specificity, potency of inhibition and inhibition kinetics will be determined. Second, the effects of PFMINT on skeletal muscle will be studied. Cultured cell model, in vitro model of hypoxia and muscle contraction, as well as the in vivo exercise model will be used. The levels of interstitial and intracellular purine levels, as well as reactive oxygen species will be measured. Last but not least, the effects of PFMINT on purine levels and oxidative stress in skeletal muscle microvascular endothelial cells will also be studied. We hope that this study could advance our knowledge and understanding on the functions of ENT2, particularly in the physiology of skeletal muscle. Pharmacologically, PFMINT may serve as a lead compound for further drug development. 平衡型核苷轉運體-2 (ENT2) 在眾多的核苷轉運體中較為獨特，因為它除了能運送核苷，也能運送核鹼基例如次黃嘌呤。ENT2在骨骼肌上的數量很多，但它的生理作用依然不清楚。世上仍未有ENT2基因剔除動物模型， ENT2基因剔除動物模型的應用也可能因其他核苷轉運體或核鹼基轉運體的正調控而受到限制。另一個可以研究ENT2功能的方法是使用選擇性ENT2抑制劑，但市場上只有選擇性ENT1抑制劑而未有選擇性ENT2抑制劑。最近我們對一系列新的化合物作篩選，發現10 μM 的FPMINT 可完全抑制ENT2的活性但對ENT1沒有作用，所以FPMINT可能是一種選擇性ENT2抑制劑，並可用於研究身體內ENT2的功能。我們假設ENT2透過控制次黃嘌呤的運送，從而調節了腺嘌呤核苷酸的庫存及活性氧化物的產生。初步的研究結果也支持這個假設，因為FPMINT能增加細胞內三磷酸腺苷及活性氧化物的水平。 這研究計劃有三個目標：第一，研究FPMINT抑制ENT2的機制。ENT2基因轉染的細胞模型會被用作研究基質特異性，抑制強度及抑制動力學。第二，以培養細胞模型，缺氧和肌肉收縮的體外模型，及運動的確體內模型來研究FPMINT對於骨骼肌的影響。細胞內及細胞之間的嘌呤和活性氧化物水平也會被量度。第三，研究FPMINT對骨骼肌微血管內皮細胞的嘌呤和活性氧化物水平。 我們希望這項研究計劃能增加我們對ENT2功能，特別是其在骨骼肌的生理作用的的了解。藥理學上來說，FPMINT可作為閞發選擇性ENT2抑制劑的先導化合物。

17156016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17156016.value: The three objectives have been achieved. For the first objective, we did not only study the mechanism by which FPMINT inhibits ENT2, but also developed a derivative of FPMINT which is even more potent and specific. The result showed that this new derivative is a non-competitive inhibitor of ENT2 and free from any effect on Rho-associated protein kinase (which may be inhibited by FPMINT in high concentration). A manuscript has been prepared and submitted to the Act Pharmaceutica Sinica (impact factor: 5.8). For the second objective, our results showed that FPMINT and its derivative can increase the intracellular level of reactive oxygen species in skeletal muscle cells and the mechanism was likely related to the blockade of ENT2, which reduced the outflux of hypoxanthine and led to the increased metabolism of hypoxanthine by xanthine oxidase, hence reactive oxygen species were produced as the by-products. The results indicate the importance of ENT2 in the regulation of oxidative stress in skeletal muscle. A manuscript is under preparation and will be submitted by the end of 2019. For the third objective, our results also showed that FPMINT and its derivative could similar increase the reactive oxygen species in the microvascular endothelial cells and the mechanism was the same as that observed in skeletal muscle cells. A manuscript will be prepared and submitted in 2010. Part of the findings were presented in the 8th Scientific Meeting of Asian Society for Vascular Biology, Shanghai, in November 2018. Part of the studies was carried out by a Bachelor of Pharmacy student as his final year research project. His findings were written in a dissertation.

17156016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17156016.value: There are two findings in the study which have potentials for further development. First, in addition to FPMINT, we also develop a derivative of FPMINT known as FP1, which is even more potent for inhibiting ENT2. This new derivatives may be serve as the lead compound for further development of drugs that may be used clinically or at least, for the research purpose (especially in the field of ENT2). Second, our findings indicated that ENT2 is an important regulator of the reactive oxygen species in skeletal muscle. It may open up a new revenue of research in the research area of skeletal muscle disorders or sport science.

17156016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17156016.value: In this study, we have developed FPMINT and its derivative as the potent and specific ENT2 inhibitors. Using these inhibitors, we could further investigate the functions of ENT2 in the skeletal muscle. Our experimental results have indicated that ENT2 can control the hypoxanthine transport across cell membrane that in turn regulates the generation of reactive oxygen species in skeletal muscle. These findings open up a new revenue of research in the field of skeletal muscle disorders and sport science.

17156416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17156416.value: 脊柱側彎是一種常見的脊柱畸形以及影響全球的人口。最常見的類型是青少年特發性脊柱側彎（AIS）。 AIS主在十幾歲在兒童發病，主要影響女孩。如果不進行治療，這些曲線可能會加重或惡化，尤其是在青春期當孩子的增長是最快的。在年幼的孩子，這惡化曲線造成外貌毀容，較差的自尊，並在嚴重的情況下甚至影響心肺功能。在不太嚴重的曲線，如果早期診斷可以通過支撐治療;然而，如果他們繼續惡化，需要脊柱手術矯正畸形。 需要脊柱側彎手術的原因基於自然史的研究，這表明在側彎超過45°的曲線很可能會 在成人期間惡化，因此值得手術融合。雖然這已被採納為一般準則，全球對AIS的臨床標準並非有共識。例如，醫生不能只考慮曲線的幅度，還包括其他手術指徵，如美容效果（外貌保存/恢復），病人的信念和衛生保健系​​統的限制。因此，有些醫生可能會提供手術治療在45°或更小的曲線，而其他醫生都滿足觀察較大的曲線。 外科手術技術，植入物，手術後的治療都有改進。手術矯正是更安全和有更好的外觀和功能的結果。因此，基於曲線幅度來考慮手術“不能”完全解決患者的需求。儘管我們有最好的意圖對AIS做矯正手術，在這個現代化和時代我們必須考慮社會衛生經濟學，任何管理也必須平衡衛生保健費用。對此，醫院管理人員正把他們的信任放在我們身上來提供最好的治療，同時有限度地降低成本。 我們的目標是用成本效益和數學模型進行比較結果的研究，以找出理想曲線幅度來治療。我們的機構是全球領先來治療脊柱柱側，並一直保持著一絲不苟的記錄。因此，我們的目標是收集AIS患者的長期觀察治療，支撐和/或手術評估（> 10年）數據來做大規模分析。治療和成本的衛生保健和社會相關的患者感覺效果，並發症將不同的治療方法之間進行比較。我們的項目有提高臨床決策和有影響香港和全球對AIS患者護理的潛力。 我們的最終目標是要確保AIS患者得到最好的照顧，甚至全球患者受益。通過分析結果，外科醫生將能夠有信心地選擇最佳和最經濟有效的治療。

17156416.label: Realisation of objectives
17156416.value: The first objective was completed through multiple publications as listed in C. The second objective is partially completed through the publications in C. The cost-effectiveness analysis study is under preparation. The fund successfully assisted a brilliant student complete her PhD studies as well. 17156416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17156416.value: 8 high impact studies were published as listed in part C. Specifically, the outcomes of brace treatment, indications of bracing and stopping treatment, prediction modeling and health related quality of life outcomes were published. These provide clear advancements in the management of scoliosis with brace treatment and prediction of curve progression utilizing growth parameters. With regards to the final manuscript in preparation. The overall findings are as follows: From the study cohort (with 54.0% direct surgery versus 40.3% with braced then proceeded to surgery), we found that despite a significantly smaller Cobb angle at initial presentation (40.9 deg +/- 13.9) as compared to those directly operated (56.7 deg+/- 16.3), the braced then surgery group still requires surgery despite bracing for a mean duration of 20.0 months. As we found that bracing group has a proportion of patients who will experience progression despite good compliance, it is advisable to identify the cut-off Cobb at initial presentation that these are the cases who will experience failure of bracing and can proceed to surgery without the expense of medical costs (fabrication of orthosis, multiple visits and consultations) as well as patient’s quality of life during bracing. The cut-off Cobb angle at presentation for surgery was found to be 41.9 deg (70.9% sensitivity, 65.8% specificity, p = 0.001) – hence this is an indicator suggestive of surgery regardless of bracing is prescribed and worn. Previously perceived difference of bracing patients experiencing psychological burden can be transient, however, it is inevitable the patients need to adapt to this treatment modality which can be different for each individual. Among surgical patients with any postoperative complications, 2.4% were related to the implant construct (screws- or hooks-related) whereas superficial or deep infection of wounds were 6.0% and 6.4% respectively. These can provide reference values of the prevalence of any surgical complications in this local cohort during consultation of differential treatment options including surgical intervention. Moreover, another important finding of this study is the back pain that patients have at initial presentation. There was significantly larger proportion of patients experiencing back pain when first presented and required direct surgery (14.0%). Hence, patients presented with a major coronal Cobb angle reaching the threshold together with back pain should be considered for direct surgery, based on both clinical and radiological indicators derived from our cohort.

17156416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17156416.value: Based on the work produced here. Bracing and surgical indications are revisited and a prospective cohort of these patients are currently studied for validating our algorithm. Future study should be performed to determine whether the model constructed can serve as a good tool for management allocation of new scoliosis patients. This will allow us to set evidence-based public policies and provide a basis for resource allocation.

17156416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17156416.value: Scoliosis is the most common spinal pathology in children. The work described here has refined the understanding of when brace treatment should be offered and what identifiers can predict a better or worse outcome. Our new management criterion provide better treatment indications for brace and surgical treatment, reduce the risk of prolonged brace treatment, and provide the most cost-effective treatment protocol that is individualized to the patient's background, curve type and clinical demographics.

17156516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17156516.value: Acute and chronic liver diseases affect millions of people around the world. They are linked to end-stage liver disorders, such as acute liver failure, cirrhosis and cancer, with high morbidity and mortality. There have been a few effective therapies for these diseases because majority of the treatment are non-specific. Therefore, elucidating the detailed molecular mechanisms during the pathogenesis of these diseases is essential for the development of novel therapies. Cyclooxygenase (COX) is an enzyme family responsible for the formation of prostanoids such as prostaglandins (PGEs) and inflammatory mediators. COX-1 is the constitutive form that is primarily involved in the production of prostanoids, whereas COX-2 is the inducible form that activates in response to a spectrum of pathological stimuli. Although the role of COX-2 in inflammatory responses has been extensively studied, the functional role of COX-1 in acute and chronic liver injury remains largely unknown. We aim to investigate the protective functional role of COX-1 in both acute and chronic liver injury. We hypothesize that a basal level of COX-1 is essential for the protection of the liver against acute and chronic inflammatory injury. To test our hypothesis, we will use COX-1 knockout mice to investigate the effect of COX-1 genetic deletion on the progression of liver injury. COX-1 deficient mice will be injected once with CCl4 or acetaminophen to form the acute liver injury models. Chronic liver injury models were established by feeding mice with a high-fat diet (HFD) for 12 weeks to induce non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) or by bile-duct ligation to induce severe hepatic fibrosis. Signaling pathways that contribute to COX-1-induced hepatic injury will also be evaluated in these four animal models. Liver-specific knockout of COX-1 in mice by an adeno-associated virus 8 (AAV8)-Cre approach will be used to confirm the source of the functional COX-1 protein, either in the liver or induced by systemic inflammation. Our preliminary studies showed that knockout of COX-1 gene significantly aggravated the severity of CCl4-induced acute liver injury and NASH model. Addition of PGE2 (a biological product of COX-1) partially reversed the adverse effects caused by the COX-1 deficiency, which suggests a possible protective role of COX-1. We will further study the functional role of COX-1 in other models and explore the signaling pathways involved in its protective function. Elucidation of the role of COX-1 in regulating liver injury may offer opportunities for the development of better therapeutic strategies centered on COX-1pathways.

17156516.label: Realisation of objectives
17156516.value: Objective No. 1: We used COX-1 knock-out mice model and induced acute and chronic liver injury using a chemical toxin such as carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) and methionine choline deficient (MCD) diet to induce steatohepatitis, which is a form of chronic liver inflammation. CCl4 induced immediate cellular damage to hepatocytes through necrosis and inflammation. For acute liver injury with CCl4, the mice were divided into 6 groups (n = 6/group): (1) wild-type control mice with vehicle administration (olive oil or phosphate buffer); (2) wild-type mice with CCl4 single-dose treatment (50 μl/kg in olive oil; intraperitoneal injection); (3) heterozygous knockout of COX-1 (COX-1+/-) mice with CCl4 single-dose treatment; (4) homozygous knockout of COX-1 (COX-1-/-) mice with CCl4 single-dose treatment; (5) SC-560 (specific COX-1 inhibitor) pre-treated wild-type mice with CCl4 single-dose treatment; and (6) PGE2 pre-treated COX-1-/- mice CCl4 single-dose treatment. The dose of single CCl4 treatment was 50 μl/kg (in olive oil, through i.p. injection), based on our previous study. In order to pharmacologically inhibit the activity of COX-1 in mice, its specific inhibitor SC-560 was injected one week before CCl4 intoxication (30 mg/kg in 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing 40% DMSO, pH = 7.4, one i.p. injection per day). On the last day, SC-560 was given 30 min before CCl4 challenge. To test the possible ameliorative effects of PGE2, synthetic PGE2 was intraperitoneally injected to COX-1-/- mice at 3 mg/kg (6% ethanol in saline) per day for one week before CCl4 challenge. Vehicle used for PGE2 preparation showed no hepatic toxicity in mice (data not shown). AA-861 (60 mg/kg dissolved in 0.1 mL DMSO) was intraperitoneally injected 24 h before the Gal/LPS administration. After 8-hr CCl4 intoxication, the mice were killed by an overdose of anaesthesia. The blood and liver samples were collected for histological, molecular biology and biochemical analysis such as ELISA, western blotting, QPCR, H&E and TUNEL assay. For the induction of chronic liver injury, we used a methionine choline deficient (MCD) diet to induce liver fatty accumulation and inflammation. The deficiency of these essential elements affected the hepatocytes metabolism which led to fatty accumulation then induced inflammation. The animals were kept in a standard environment before the start of the experiment with free access to animal chow and tap water. The mice were divided into 3 groups (n= 8 in each group): (1) wild-type control mice on chow diet; (2) wild-type mice fed with MCD diet for 6 weeks; and (3) Homozygous COX-1 knock-out mice fed with MCD diet for 6 weeks. After 6 weeks, the mice were sacrificed with overdose of pentobarbital sodium (150 mg/kg, intraperitoneal injection). Bodyweight and food intake of each mouse were recorded every week. The blood and liver samples were collected for histological, molecular biology and biochemical analysis such as ELISA, western blotting, QPCR, H&E and TUNEL assay. All experimental procedures were conducted according to the protocols approved by the Committee of Animal Use for Research and Teaching at The University of Hong Kong. Other parameters measured were the following: Serum ALT and AST; mRNAs of antioxidant enzymes (Catalase and glutathione peroxidase); oxidative markers (nitrotyrosine and MDA); cytokine markers for proinflammation (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, Cox-2, iNOS, MCP-1); apoptotic markers (Cyto C, Bak-1 BCl-2, cleaved caspase 3, TUNEL assay) and anti-apoptotic markers (FasL, cleaved caspase 8); transcriptional regulators for inflammation (NFkβ; Ikβα alpha and C/EBP α); Leukotrienes (LTC4,/LTD4/LTE, LTC4S); 5- Lipogenase; regeneration factors (OSM, OSMR, TIMP1 and STAT3). We extended the study to autophagy using AML 12 COX-1 knockdown cell line. These two animal models and AML12 COX-1 knockdown cell line partly established the protective mechanisms of COX-1 to the liver in both acute and chronic liver injury/inflammation. In short for the first time, we demonstrated the signaling pathways on how Cox-1 protected the liver and we fully achieved this objective. Objective No. 2 Although we have established that COX-1 is beneficial for the basic hepatic protection against both acute and chronic liver injury, we need to determine the source of the functional COX-1. Identifying the functional source of COX-1 will help us to further elucidate the mechanism of action, whether locally produced in the liver or induced by systemic inflammation. We have partly established the source of COX-1 from the liver through loss of function experiments but we have not identified the specific cell type in the liver. We also needed to determine the systemic source of COX-1 if any. To completely accomplish this goal, we needed to achieve liver-specific COX-1 deletion. We used liver-specific knockout of COX-1 mice [Alb-Cre/COX1fl/+ mice (heterozygous) and Alb-Cre/COX1fl/fl mice (homozygous)], which were backcrossed with COX-1fl/fl mice, (generated by flanking the critical exons, encoding the COX-1, with loxP sequences) into Alb-Cre mice, in which Cre recombinase expression was under the control of the albumin promoter (Provided by a key collaborator of this project, Dr. Jia Xiao, Jinan University, China). Then CCl4, acetaminophen, D12451 diet formula, and bile-duct ligation operation will be treated or used as previously described to repeat the experiments. This approach will help us to validate the source of COX-1 during liver injury. We partly failed to achieve this objective because our collaborators were not able to successfully breed the mice needed for these experiments since there was a high rate of mortality after birth. We spent ample time in breeding these mice but they were short lived and not able to continue the experiments. In theory, we thought how to prove the hypothesis but in real terms, it was not achievable due to the limitations we encountered. We were not able to modify and continue the experiments partly due to Covid-19 restrictions imposed on all animal experiments and for risk control. Objective No. 3 In addition to the above experiments on COX-1-mediated signalling pathways in both acute and chronic models, we also investigated whether there is a compensatory mechanism between COX-1 and COX-2 by using COX-1/COX-2 double knockout mice. Previously, we have generated our COX-1 and COX-2 knockout mice using single targeting gene technique (Tang et al., 2005). We have backcrossed COX-1-/- and COX-2-/- mice for more than nine generations to create COX-1-/-/COX-2-/- knockout mice deficient in both COX-1 and COX-2 (Provided by a key collaborator of this project, Dr. Jia Xiao, Jinan University, China). We will repeat the CCl4, acetaminophen, D12451 diet formula, and bile-duct ligation experiments in these mice as previously described. Lastly, we will evaluate the therapeutic value of COX inhibitors (e.g. aspirin and SC-560) in treating both acute and chronic liver injury. Studying both acute (toxin- and drug-induced) and chronic (NASH and early cirrhosis) animal models will provide us with a better understanding of the functional role of COX-1 in the entire spectrum of liver diseases. However, for similar reasons stated above, we partly failed to achieve this objective because our collaborators were not able to successfully breed the mice needed for these experiments since there was a high rate of mortality after birth. We spent ample time in breeding these mice but they were short lived and not able to continue the experiments. In theory, we thought how to prove the hypothesis but in real terms, it was not achievable. We were not able to modify and continue the experiments partly due to Covid-19 restrictions imposed on all animal experiments and for risk control.

17156516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17156516.value: We investigated the role and mechanism of COX-1 in acute and chronic liver injury. Carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) was administered to induce acute liver injury and methionine choline deficient (MCD) diet was fed to wild-type or COX-1-deﬁcient mice to induce chronic liver injury. Both genetic (partially or completely) deletion of COX-1 expression and pharmacological inhibition of COX-1 activity in mice exacerbated acute liver injury induced by CCl4 and chronic liver injury induced by a methionine choline deficient (MCD) diet, and revealing the following: (1) Deficiency of COX-1 exacerbated acute and chronic liver injury induced by CCl4 and MCD, which showed histopathological changes of fatty accumulation in the hepatocytes, necrosis and inflammatory infiltrations and increased serum levels of aminotransferases; (2) COX-1 deletion did not protect the liver from oxidative stress with significant reduction of oxidative enzymes such as catalase and glutathione peroxidase, partly through the action of cytochrome P450 2E1-dependent pathway; (3) Deletion of COX-1 aggravated pro-inflammatory response in mice liver and enhanced inﬂammatory and chemo-attractive responses such as TNF α, IL-1β, IL-6, MCP-1, and COX-2 with increased number of activated macrophages (ED1 expression); and (4) Apoptosis was worsened after COX-1 deletion through both intrinsic (Bak-1, Bcl-2 cleaved caspase 3) and extrinsic (FasL and cleaved caspase 8) apoptotic pathways. (5) NFkβ and C/EBP α were involved in COX-1 protection against CCl4 toxicity and MCD induced diet partly through the modulation of transcription factor-dependent pathways. (6) Pre-treatment with prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) or 5-lipoxygenase (5-LO) inhibitor in homozygous COX-1 knockout mice signiﬁcantly ameliorated CCl4-induced hepatic injury. Exacerbation of liver injury was partially through the 5-Lipogenase (5-LO/Cysteinyl Leukotrienes pathway). (7) In addition, level of hepato-protective molecules (eg, OSM and OSMR) and associated liver regeneration pathway were signiﬁcantly inhibited by the deﬁciency of COX-1 but restored by the addition of PGE2 or the inhibition of 5-LO. (8) Furthermore, the alternative arachidonic acid metabolism pathway of 5-LO, which induced additional inﬂammation in the liver, was activated in response to the deﬁciency of COX-1. (9) COX-1 knockdown inhibits autophagosome-lysosome fusion in AML12 cells and it is required for mature autophagosome biogenesis. (10) COX-1 is required for general endocytosis pathway. (11) COX-1 knockdown induces synthesis of enlarged functional lysosomes. (12) Hepatic deletion of COX-1 exacerbated diet-induced non-alcoholic steatohepatitis in mice. In conclusion, basal expression of COX-1 is essential for the protection, autophagy and homeostatic maintenance of liver against chemical-induced hepatotoxicity and methionine choline deficient induced chronic inflammation.

17156516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17156516.value: We have partly understood the mechanism on how Cox-1 protected the liver from liver injury. Although we were partly successful in developing the animal models for determining the source of Cox-1 either from the liver or systemic as well as testing the therapeutic value of Cox inhibitors, we still believe that we can still fully achieve these goals by slightly modifying our animal models for the experiments in the near future. There are several C0x-2 inhibitors in the market such as NSAID which are widely used. However, there are no drugs that can enhances the expression of COX-1. If we are able to well characterise the function of Cox-1, it may lead to the development of drugs that can promote the expression of Cox-1 which can have clinical and therapeutic applications in acute and chronic liver diseases. There are multiple bioactive lipids inhibitors that can be tested which can disrupt the inflammatory signalling pathways. These findings have significant therapeutic implications for future drug development.

17156516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17156516.value: Acute and chronic liver diseases affect millions of people around the world. They are linked to end-stage liver disorders, such as acute liver failure, cirrhosis and cancer, with high morbidity and mortality. There have been a few effective therapies for these diseases because a majority of the treatments are non-specific. Elucidating the detailed molecular mechanisms of these diseases is essential for the development of novel therapies. Cyclooxygenase (COX) is an enzyme family responsible for the formation of prostanoids such as prostaglandins (PGEs) and inflammatory mediators. COX-1 is the constitutive form that is primarily involved in the production of prostanoids, whereas COX-2 is the inducible form that activates in response to a spectrum of pathological stimuli. Although the role of COX-2 in inflammatory responses has been extensively studied, the functional role of COX-1 in acute and chronic liver injury remains largely unknown. In this study we have shown that the absence of Cox-1 enhanced liver injury and inflammation in acute and chronic liver injury by modulating key master gene regulators of inflammation and inhibiting liver regeneration. We concluded that a basal level of COX-1 is essential for the protection and homeostatic maintenance of the liver against acute and chronic inflammatory injury.

17157416.value: 銀屑病（Psoriasis），一種慢性皮膚炎症，現近兩萬至三萬人感染是香港主要的健康問題，其中約三分之一將發展為致殘性銀屑病關節炎。其他並發症包括糖尿病、心血管疾病、中風、惡性腫瘤、抑鬱症的高發以及低生活質量。銀屑病目前無法根治，只有少數有效療法。而且許多其他療法有嚴重副作用，部分療效亦隨時間推移而減弱。近來有發現表明：皮膚微生物群可能扮演此複雜疾病的潛在致病源。宏基因組學和宏轉錄組學技術為我們提供了一個認識皮膚複雜微生物群落的契機。本研究旨在運用宏基因組學和宏轉錄組學來分析銀屑病患者破損和健康皮膚以及其家庭成員皮膚的微生物群。銀屑病患將從“愛+人”計劃全港大型住戶隊列研究中選取。 借此綜合及人口代表性隊列，我們將可開展大型基於中國人群的皮膚生物群落宏基因組學和宏轉錄組學研究。這也將會是第一個測序家族微生物組成和表達的研究。本研究的假設包括：1）人皮膚微生物群表徵將提供對微生物群失衡在銀屑病潛在致病源的認知；2）皮膚微生物群觸發免疫系統反應，引發銀屑病。對這些微生物組數據進行綜合統計分析，將有助於解決很多懸而未決的問題，並可為銀屑病患者提供轉譯工具。具體而言，本研究的目的有：1）通過宏基因組學研究評價銀屑病患者（患處及健康皮膚：發病前期、發病期、痊愈期）及其家庭成員（健康皮膚對照）的皮膚微生物群落的功能多樣性和代謝多樣性；2）通過宏轉錄組學為患者及其家庭成員對照的表達譜提供信息。本研究成果將指引優化銀屑病的診斷與管理，以及對新型抑微生物療法和協微生物療法的靶向藥物的識別。

17157816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17157816.value: 端粒結合蛋白Rap1 作為端粒蛋白複合體中的一部分，在維持端粒長度和結構完整性中發揮著重要作用。在之前的報導中，Rap1被認為只是結合於染色體末端的DNA重複序列，但目前更多的認為它還可以結合位於染色體臂上的過氧化物酶增殖體啟動受體γ 輔激啟動因數-1 （PGC1α）啟動序列，進而介導PGC1α的轉錄啟動。PGC1α是一個參與基因轉錄活性調節的關鍵啟動因數，可以調節能量代謝中很多基因的表達。敲除Rap1基因的小鼠表現出明顯的非正常體征，包括肥胖，葡萄糖不耐受症，胰島素抵抗，脂肪肝和脂肪組織過度肥大。 我們的前期資料表明在敲除Rap1基因的小鼠動脈中，乙醯膽鹼啟動的內皮依賴性血管舒張功能受損，但是對一氧化氮（NO）供體硝普酸鈉介導的內皮非依賴性血管舒張中，則無明顯差異。這些證據表明在敲除Rap1基因的小鼠中，內皮依賴性血管舒張功能的降低極有可能是由於NO的釋放或者生物利用度的降低，而不是由於平滑肌細胞對血管內皮分泌的介導性物質的敏感性的變化而引起的。NO是維護血管平衡穩態中一個最重要的舒血管因數，我們的發現意味著Rap1在調節NO 的過程中起到重要作用，同時也開闢了對端粒結合蛋白在生理性方面作用的全新認知。 過量的活性過氧化物和較弱的抗氧化防禦系統可以降低NO的生物利用度。而PGC1α 也是一個清除ROS的有力介導因數，它通過增加內皮細胞中ROS清除蛋白的表達來實現降低ROS濃度。因此我們有理由推測Rap1通過PGC1α在轉錄水準上增強抗氧化能力，同時降低內皮細胞的氧化應激，從而改善血管內皮功能。事實上，我們的前期資料已發現，與野生型正常小鼠相比，敲除Rap1基因的小鼠的內皮細胞中，PGC1α的表達水準明顯降低。當我們把敲除Rap1基因的小鼠的主動脈環和抗氧化劑同時培養時，可以避免內皮依賴性血管舒張受損。因此，在血管內皮中，Rap1極大可能是一個全新的抵抗氧化應激的決定因數。除此之外，我們更多的前期證據顯示Rap1可以延緩由氧化應激誘發的血管內皮衰老。 目前，對於Rap1在血管內皮功能及調節ROS內穩態中作用的研究還是一片空白。這個課題的研究目的是探索Rap1是否可以增強NO的釋放以及生物利用度，並且是否可以通過抑制氧化應激而延緩血管內皮衰老。在我們即將開展的研究中，我們將綜合利用基因學和藥理學的理論和技術，同時在體外（利用新鮮的動脈組織，以及培養小鼠源和人源內皮細胞株）和體內（不同小鼠模型，包括老化模型，糖尿病模型和血管內皮損傷模型）證明Rap1在保護血管內皮功能紊亂中的重要作用。我們期待這個課題可以明確這個最保守的端粒結合蛋白Rap1，在建立端粒穩態與血管功能的潛在關係中起到的重要作用。如果Rap1被證實能夠通過降低氧化應激，實現改善與提高血管內皮功能，那麼Rap1蛋白在血管內皮功能紊亂中起到的重要作用必將成為衰老及與衰老有關的疾病研究與防治的重要靶點，具有重要意義。

17158316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17158316.value: 理解在月經期間子宮內膜細胞對內膜間質幹細胞活性的調節機制 子宮內膜的外粘膜是一個動態組織。在每一月經周期，子宮內膜的功能層會脫落，剩下的基底層會分裂和分化，產生新的功能層。這種不簡單的組織重塑在每一位育齡的女性發生約400次。雌激素和孕激素調節這種再生周期。我們首次確定在人類和小鼠子宮內膜存有幹細胞。這些稀少的細胞被認為是負責子宮內膜的再生周期。 一般認為圍繞內膜幹細胞的微環境（幹細胞小生境）決定了幹細胞是否進行分裂以複製自己，或分化成形成大量子宮內膜的成熟細胞。幹細胞小生境的作用可以通過子宮內膜幹細胞與其鄰近細胞之間的直接接觸來介導，或通過微環境的分子，包括由小生境細胞產生的可溶性因子介導。子宮內膜小生境在月經期間對幹細胞命運調控的細節過程還不清楚。 子宮內膜再生在月經期間開始。因此，在這一階段的子宮內膜小生境啟動幹細胞，從而使子宮內膜修復是合乎邏輯的推論。這與我們發現在月經期間子宮內膜的幹細胞有好的增殖和自我更新的能力是一致。在體外，月經期的子宮內膜上皮細胞或間質細胞與子宮內膜幹細胞共培養能對幹細胞產生同樣的效果，周期中其他階段的細胞不影響幹細胞的活性。數據提示這些現象是由子宮內膜上皮細胞和基質細胞分泌 Wnt/β-catenin 信號的可溶性因子介導。 基於以上觀察，本項目推測這些在月經期子宮內膜的基底層細胞分泌促進內膜修復的因子。這項目的目的是確定和表徵參與調節子宮內膜幹細胞的分子及其受體。 項目的結果將使我們能夠更好地理解在月經期間的小生境和在子宮微環境內調節子宮內膜幹細胞功能的信號。研究將開闢新的途徑用於重新創建子宮微環境，從而控制子宮內膜幹細胞在體外和體內的增殖和活性，其結果將對內膜生理學和子宮內膜組織工程有很大的用處。

17158316.label: Realisation of objectives
17158316.value: Objective 1: To characterize the endometrial niche (epithelial and stromal) cells activated CD140b+CD146+ cells. We have examined the properties of endometrial stem/progenitor cells at different stages of the menstrual cycle. Co-expression of CD140b and CD146 was used as the endometrial mesenchymal stem-like cells (eMSCs) surface markers. We found that endometrial tissues from menstrual and proliferative phase had higher percentages of eMSCs than those from secretory phase. The menstrual phase eMSCs also underwent more rounds of self-renewal and enabled a greater total cell output than those form the proliferative and secretory phases indicating that the menstrual phase eMSCs are activated. We have characterized the endometrial niche (epithelial and stromal) cells activated eMSCs. Purified stromal cells isolated from total abdominal hysterectomy samples or menstrual blood underwent sequential microbeading against antibodies to CD140b and CD146. Large and small colony forming units (CFUs) formed after 15 days in culture. Co-culture with niche cells from menstrual phase significantly increase the colony forming ability of eMSCs, in particular the formation of large CFUs which are likely to be initiated by stem cells. Using flow cytometry, we detected an increase in the phenotypic expression of eMSCs after co-culture with menstrual niche cells. Niche cells isolated from the proliferative phase did not display the same phenomenon. The observed declining trend in the proportion of CD140b+CD146+ cells when cocultured with proliferative niche cells suggested that the stem cells are undergoing differentiation in such scenario. Hence, the maintenance of eMSCs appears to be “phase specific”. The cell type specificity of the observed effect on eMSCs was assessed by using cell lines derived from human foreskin fibroblasts and human oviductal epithelial E6/E7. Unexpectedly, foreskin fibroblasts have similar effect in stimulating self-renewal of eMSCs. It is possible that these cells may secrete common factor(s) for eMSC maintenance. An alternate possibility is that different factors from various muscle cells exert the same effect on eMSCs. Since the endometrial niche cells from menstruation phase promoted both cell proliferation and self-renewal potential displayed by the eMSCs at menstruation, the search for the candidate secretory factor(s) focused on endometrial niche cells. To elucidate the role of cytokines and chemokines from niche cells on eMSCs maintenance, we compared monoculture with coculture of menstrual epithelial and stromal cells using cytokine arrays. Densitometric analysis revealed increase of several cytokines C-X-C motif ligand 1 (CXCL1), CXCL5, interleukin-6. Treatment with these cytokines increased the clonogenic activity and phenotypic expression of eMSCs. Objective 2: To determine the role of WNT signaling in the endometrial niche cells-induced increase in clonogenicity and proportion of CD140b+CD146+ cells. We assessed the effect of a pan WNT ligand secretion inhibitor (IWP-2) on the clonogenicity and proliferation of eMSCs. Our findings demonstrated IWP-2 can suppress the stimulatory action of the menstrual niche cells by decreasing the formation of CFUs. Next we used the WNT taqman probe array to search for prospective WNT-molecules derived by menstrual niche cells. WNT5A was one of the WNT ligands found to be abundantly expressed by endometrial epithelial and stromal cells at menstruation. We assessed the effect of Wnt5a conditioned medium (CM) on the clonogenicity and proliferation of eMSCs and found that Wnt5a CM can enhance the formation of CFUs and the expression of the eMSCs markers. In addition, the WNT agonist RSPO1 can contribute to the stimulatory effect observed when co-cultured with menstrual phase niche cells. To determine whether RSPO1 was responsible for the stimulatory action, we functionally neutralized the effect with the antibody against RSPO1 and found to reduce the cloning efficiency, percentage of eMSCs and the TCF/LEF luciferase activity. Objective 3: To study the role of WNT receptors in mediating the stimulatory action of endometrial niche cells on clonogenicity and proportion of CD140b+CD146+ cells. Since we postulated that the observed action is via the WNT signaling, the WNT receptors expressed on eMSCs was explored. WNT ligands can elicit WNT dependent or independent responses depending on the receptor context on the cell surface, therefore we selected a panel of receptors which have been reported to bind to WNT5A. Our findings revealed that eMSCs contain a higher expression of frizzled 5 (FZD5), low-density lipoprotein receptor related protein 5 (LRP5) and leucine rich repeat-containing G-protein 5 (LGR5) when compare to their unfractionated counterpart. Expression of ROR2 and RYK – receptors which can inhibit the TCF-mediated transcription was relatively low or undetectable. Using immunofluorescent staining, coexpression of FZD5 and LRP5 was found to be expressed in eMSCs. The LRP component was biologically active, as eMSCs responded to DKK-1, a secreted Wnt antagonist that binds to LRP5/6 Wnt co-receptor. DKK-1 reduced the number of colonies and the proportion of eMSCs. The role of FZD5 in Wnt5A induced Wnt signal was assessed by knock down of FZD5-siRNA. The treatment reduced the niche CCM induction of TCF/LEF luciferase activity when compared to the siRNA. Similarly, the recombinant Wnt5A induced increase in TCF/LEF luciferase activity was abolished upon treatment of eMSCs with FZD5-siRNA. To confirm the WNT5A-FZD5/LRP5 interaction, we used fluorescence-labeled WNT5A protein to assess the bound signal on eMSCs after siFZD5 transfection or addition of DKK-1. Overall, the fluorescent intensity bound WNT5A was reduced suggesting the Wnt ligand-receptor interaction on eMSCs.

17158316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17158316.value: Understanding the stem cell niche composition and the signals within the uterine microenvironment during endometrial repair is challenging due to rarity of adult stem cells within the tissue and the specified time for endometrial sampling. In this proposal, the following outcome was achieved: The human endometrium undergoes proliferation and differentiation in a cyclic manner, therefore resident stem/progenitor cells are likely to be responsible for this remarkable regenerative capacity. Firstly, we examined the spatial and temporal characterization of endometrial mesenchymal-like stem cells (eMSCs) across the menstrual cycle and between the functionalis and basalis layers. Our findings showed a constant population of eMSCs exists throughout the menstrual cycle. eMSCs at menstruation exhibit better proliferative and self-renewal activity, suggesting that stem cells are activated during endometrial repair. In addition, more eMSCs reside in the basal layer, confirming that the basalis serves as a reservoir for endometrial stem cells (Xu et al., Experimental Cell Research, 2017). In vitro co-culture of endometrial niche cells from menstruation with eMSCs enhanced the colony forming and self-renewal abilities of eMSCs when compared with culture of eMSCs alone. The coculture effects were observed even when there was no direct contact between the endometrial niche cells and the eMSCs, indicating that the niche cells derived secretory factor(s) were responsible for maintaining the stem cell properties of eMSCs in vitro, including expression of endometrial mesenchymal stem cell phenotypic markers, short and long-term expansion. During inflammatory events - menstruation, cytokines such as CXCL-1, CXCL-5 and IL-6 may modulate secretion in endometrial cells to enable eMSCs for the regeneration of the human endometrium (Xu et al., Stem Cell Research & Therapy, 2020). Secretory factors associated with the activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling promoted eMSC proliferation and self-renewal. Wnt5A was found to be the candidate molecule since it was among the highly expressed Wnt ligands in primary human endometrial cells at menstruation. RSPO1 was another candidate molecule base on (a) anti-RSPO1 antibody reduced the stimulatory action of endometrial niche CCM on colony formation, self-renewal, and TCF/LEF transcriptional activities of eMSCs; and (b) recombinant RSPO-1 protein increased the formation of colonies and phenotypic expression of eMSCs. We further demonstrated expression of Wnt receptor – FZD5 and LGR5 and co-receptor - LRP5 in eMSCs. Thus, Wnt5A and RSPO1 can activate the Wnt canonical depending on the receptor context (Li et al, under preparation).

17158316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17158316.value: A fundamental issue that needs to be addressed is to understand the control over stem cell response in terms of self-renewal and differentiation. The secretory factors produced from the endometrial cells at menstruation offer a specialized microenvironment for human eMSCs. By gaining a better understanding of the niche composition and the signals within the uterine microenvironment, it will be possible to recreate a milieu for stem cell expansion and control their in vitro biological activities. Since we now have supporting evidence that Wnt/β-catenin signaling is a prominent candidate for stem cell regulation in human endometrium. Besides Wnt5A and RSPO1, we propose other Wnt ligands or Wnt agonist may also participate in stem cell regulation. The Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway was mainly focused in this project. However, the interplay between adult stem cell and their niche are highly dynamic and complex in vivo. Therefore, future studies should explore other signaling pathways (i.e. Notch signaling, TGF-β signaling) which may also modulate the stem cell fate in human endometrium.

17158316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17158316.value: Little is known about the local niche signals of endometrial stem cells self-renewal. The microenvironment surrounding the endometrial stem cells decides whether they should divide to replicate themselves or differentiate into mature endometrial cells that form the bulk of the endometrium. Aside from niche cells, local paracrine signals within the microenvironment are important in maintaining stem cells. Our findings showed differences in the properties of putative stem cells from different menstrual phases. Also, the secretory soluble factors from endometrial-cells at menstruation modulate the activities of endometrial stem cells. The biological actions of Wnt activators and inhibitors together with the presence of appropriate receptors are in line with a functional role of Wnt signaling on eMSCs proliferation and self-renewal.
