17158616.value: 糖尿病患者在圍手術期心肌梗死風險極大，且對心肌缺血再灌注損傷（Ischemia-reperfusion injury，IRI）耐受較差。其中的機制目前尚未完全明瞭，且缺乏有效治療手段。在非糖尿病個體中，在延長的缺血後立刻進行短暫的間歇性動脈閉塞/再灌注作為缺血後處理（Ischemic postconditioning，IPostC），可減少心肌IRI。在心臟手術中應用IPostC是可行的，然而，IPostC在糖尿病個體中心臟保護作用減弱乃至消失，其中機制仍然是未知的。 我們前期研究發現脂聯素（一種抗糖尿病特性的蛋白）可以通過微囊膜蛋白微囊蛋白-3（Caveolin-3,cav3）/脂聯素受體-1（Adiponectin receptor-1，AdipoR1）依賴的信號通路活化線粒體STAT3，在IPostC中發揮重要作用。此外，糖尿病個體中心臟脂聯素表達減少和/或脂聯素信號通路受損，因而無法活化STAT3，發揮心臟保護功能。在早期糖尿病大鼠中，補充脂聯素可以恢復IPostC的心臟保護功能，但在晚期糖尿病大鼠中無法實現該效應，原因尚未可知。 蛋白激酶C-ε（Protein kinase C-ε，PKCε）是一種可以在心肌IRI中調節多種細胞效應反應的激酶。在非糖尿病個體中，PKCε作為IPostC信號轉導的關鍵分子，啟動以後可以增加心肌對缺血的耐受。通過促進PKCε和Cav3的相互作用發揮心臟保護功能實現對缺血的處理。有趣的是，我們發現在糖尿病齧齒類動物的心臟中，PKCε是逐步活化的，然而，在糖尿病個體的心臟中，IPostC的心臟保護功能消失，伴隨心肌和血漿中脂聯素、Cav3/AdipoR1結合及STAT3活化減少，並且補充脂聯素並未能恢復糖尿病心肌對IPostC的敏感性。相反，在晚期糖尿病中，在適度抑制PKCε的同時補充脂聯素可以活化心肌STAT3並恢復IPostC的心臟保護功能。 最近的一項研究表明過度活化PKCε導致PKCε和Cav3解離，結合我們的初步研究結果，我們設想：在糖尿病中，高糖導致PKCε過度活化同時減少了Cav3並阻斷了PKCε和Cav3的結合，繼而損害了脂聯素信號通路，使IPostC無法活化STAT3來發揮心臟保護功能。 我們將使用在體、離體模型心肌IRI模型及體外細胞心肌缺氧再複氧模型，包括應用基因敲除/過表達PKCε和Cav3來闡明其中機制。該研究將促進心肌IRI對糖尿病失耐受的病理生理學認識並有助於發展新的更佳治療方案以管理糖尿病人的缺血性心臟病。

17158616.label: Realisation of objectives
17158616.value: In the present project, series of in vivo, ex vivo and in vitro experiments were performed and we demonstrated that PKCε over-activation renders the diabetic heart prone to myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI) and compromises IPostC cardioprotection; and it does so via impairing adiponectin signaling (Cav3/AdipoR1). We confirmed the role of PKCε in myocardial IRI in diabetes by using type 1 diabetic (T1DM) model in wild-type mice and PKCε conditional knockout mice, with or without the presence of PKCε overexpression. We found that over-activated PKCε exacerbates myocardial IRI in diabetes, which is associated with reduced expression of cardiac Cav3. Furthermore, cardiac specific Cav3 gene knockout (CKO) mice were induced to type 1 diabetes and subjected to myocardial IRI and IPostC to investigate the interaction between PKCε and Cav3 in regulating IPostC protection in diabetes. Finally, PKCε siRNA was applied in vivo in combination with adiponectin supplementation restored the diabetic hearts sensitivity to IPostC cardioprotection. Therefore, the objectives 1, 2 and 3 are fulfilled. Additionally, we have extended our study and we found that reduction of cardiomyocyte cavelin-3 is the major mechanism for the cardiomyocyte to be more vulnerable to hypoxia/reoxygenation injury and less responsive to the cardioprotection effects of propofol (an anesthetic that can enhance adiponectin) in the context of hyperglycemia and upregulation of caveolin-3 can facilitate while knock-down of caveolin-3 cancels propofol cardioprotection. Besides PKCε/Cav3/AdipoR1 signalling, we also proposed several potential targets, including repressor activator protein 1, prostaglandin E receptor subtype 4, which were closely involved in the mitochondrial energy metabolism and their roles in myocardial IRI in diabetes are worth further investigation.

17158616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17158616.value: We have found that over-activated PKCε exacerbates myocardial IRI in diabetes, which is associated with reduced expression of cardiac Cav3. Whilst inhibition of over-activation of PKCε significantly attenuated myocardial IRI in diabetes. PKCε is a critical molecule for IPostC cardioprotection. IPostC confers cardioprotective effects in non-diabetes by activating adiponectin, which enhances cardiac PKCε and leads its binding to Cav3 and activates STAT3, while in diabetic, moderate PKCε inhibition facilitates IPostC to confer cardioprotection. Cardiac specific knockout of Cav3 block the cardioprotective effect of the inhibition of over-activated PKCε in myocardial IRI in diabetes, indicating that PKCε over-activation renders the diabetic heart prone to myocardial IRI and compromises IPostC cardioprotection; and it does so via impairing adiponectin signaling (Cav3/AdipoR1). In conclusion, an intact PKCε/Cav3/AdipoR1 signaling is required for IPostC to activate STAT-3 and to confer cardioprotection in both non-diabetes and diabetes.

17158616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17158616.value: The research findings from the current project will increase the knowledge about the molecular mechanism why IPostC cardioprotection is attenuated/abolished in diabetes and provide a rationale for more informed pharmacotherapies during reperfusion in diabetic patients. Based on the positive findings, clinicians can justify clinical trials and pharmaceutical companies can develop drugs (activators/inhibitors) related to our proposed signalling pathway (PKCε/Cav3/AdipoR1), which may open a new avenue for treatment of ischemic heart disease in diabetes.

17158616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17158616.value: PKCε is indispensable for IPostC cardioprotection. In non-diabetes, IPostC confers cardioprotection by activating adiponectin, which enhances cardiac PKCε and leads its binding to Cav3. However, in diabetes, cardiac PKCε is over-activated. Inhibition of PKCε over-activation restores IPostC cardioprotection, and the underlying mechanism involves Cav3/AdipoR1 signalling pathway. These research findings gained from this study will facilitate the development of novel and better therapies for the management of ischemic heart disease that is common in diabetic patients.

17159316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17159316.value: The organ of Corti in the mammalian inner ear consists of an ordered array of mechanosensory hair cells. The spatial arrangements of the hair cells in the cochlea are important for the hearing function. Disarrangement of hair cell differentiation leads to severe cochlear sensory defects and hearing loss. The Sonic hedgehog (Shh) pathway plays important roles in mammalian inner ear development. Mutations of the Shh and Smoothened genes have been shown to cause abnormal patterns of cochlear hair cell differentiation. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying Shh signaling in the control of hair cell differentiation remain elusive. We have investigated the roles of Sufu (Suppressor of fused), a negative regulator of the Shh signaling pathway, and the Gli genes in mediating cochlear hair cell differentiation. Our analysis of the Sufu, Gli3-P1-4 and Gli3-Δ699 mouse mutants have demonstrated that the dynamic progression of cochlear hair cell differentiation were affected, and the expression of the N-Myc gene in the cochlear epithelium was significantly changed in these mutant mice. Therefore, we hypothesize that N-Myc is a downstream factor of Shh signaling and is required to control the differentiation of hair cells in the mammalian cochlea. The aim of this project is to elucidate the molecular mechanisms mediated by N-Myc, Sufu and the Gli transcription factors during the dynamic progression of hair cell differentiation in the developing cochlea. The specific objectives of this projects are: 1) To investigate the functions of Sufu and Gli transcription factors in the temporal basal-to-apical progression of cochlear hair cell differentiation; 2) To investigate the interactions of Gli2 and Gli3 with N-Myc during cochlear hair cell differentiation; 3) To elucidate the roles of N-Myc in the regulation of Atoh1 and cochlear hair cell differentiation in the mammalian inner ear. A series of gain-of-function, loss-of-function, and inducible gene expression transgenic mouse mutants will be investigated in this study. This project will contribute to our understanding of the development of mammalian cochlear hair cells, and shed light on the pathogenesis of human hearing loss.

17159316.label: Realisation of objectives
17159316.value: Objective 1. To investigate the functions of Sufu and Gli transcription factors in the temporal basal-to-apical progression of cochlear hair cell differentiation We characterized the expression profiles of Gli genes during cochlea sensory development in control and Pax2Cre;Sufuf/f as well as Emx2Cre;Sufuf/f mutants from E13.5-18.5. In normal embryos, Gli1 was mainly expressed in the spiral ganglia and in the apical region of the cochlea, but not in the cochlear epithelium. Gli3 was expressed strongly in the cochlea mesenchyme. Gli2 displayed dynamic expression in different populations of non-sensory cells in the cochlea epithelium. To address the roles of Sufu, we examined the Emx2Cre;Sufuf/f mutant and found that there was a specific delay in outer hair cell (OHC) differentiation. At E16.5, no OHCs could be found in the mutant. The Atoh1 mRNA could be found in the HC progenitors, but the levels were significantly reduced. By immunostaining, we showed that Atoh1 and its downstream targets Pou4f3 and Myo7a were absent in the OHCs. At E18.5, OHCs could be detected but their alignment was severely disrupted and supernumerary OHCs could be found. For the supporting cells, we found that the differentiation of p75NTR+ inner pillar cells was not affected, but the differentiation of Prox1+ outer supporting cells was significantly delayed, while Sox2 expression was retained in the outer hair cell progenitors. Therefore, deletion of Sufu in the cochlea epithelium specifically caused a delay in differentiation of OHCs and supporting cells, possibly through dysregulation of Sox2. In Emx2Cre;Sufuf/f mutants, prolonged expression of Sox2 was detected. Using the Sox2-EGFP mouse, we found that at E16.5, the undifferentiated progenitors in the cochlear apical region expressed higher level of Sox2 compared with the basal region. Using compound mutants of the Sox2Ysb hypomorphic allele and the Sox2EGFP knock-in allele, we found that the level of Sox2 was significantly reduced and detectable only in the apical region. In Emx2Cre;Sufuf/f;Sox2EGFP/Ysb mutant, Sox2 expression was largely restored. Our results showed that Shh signaling regulates differential expression level of Sox2 along the basal-apical axis of the cochlea, thereby controls the directionality of HC differentiation. We have successfully completed Objective 1, the functions of Gli factors are further analyzed as described in Objective 2 below. Objective 2. To investigate the interactions of Gli2 and Gli3 with N-Myc during cochlear hair cell differentiation To understand the roles of Gli factors in the cochlear HC differentiation, we analyzed cochlea of Gli3-/- and Gli3P1-4/P1-4, in which no Gli3 repressor could be produced. We found that HC differentiation was normal in both Gli3-/- and Gli3P1-4/P1-4 mutants, suggesting that Gli3 repressor was not required for HC differentiation. However, Gli2-/- mutant exhibited premature HC differentiation as revealed by accelerated progression of differentiation at both E15.5 and E16.5. Analysis of E16.5 Emx2Cre;Sufuf/f mutants showed that Gli2 was ectopically expressed in the organ of Corti. In the Emx2Cre;Sufuf/f;Gli2f/f compound mutants, OHCs were detected in the cochlea, indicating that deletion of Gli2 in the Sufu mutant context could restore HC differentiation defect. Therefore, elevated Gli2 in Sufu mutant would prevent hair cell differentiation. To modulate the levels of Gli2, we used Spop which normally promotes ubiquitination and degradation of Gli2 activator. In the compound mutant Emx2Cre;Sufuf/f;Spopf/f, robust Gli2 activation was observed and HC differentiation was severely disrupted at both E16.5 and E18.5. Consistently, activation of Gli2 and severe HC differentiation defect were also observed in Emx2Cre;Ptch1f/f mutants. In summary, our mutant analyses clearly demonstrated that Gli2 inhibits cochlear HC differentiation, and it functions via regulating the expression level of Sox2 as described in Objective 1 above. We had initially examined the interaction of Gli3 and N-Myc during HC differentiation. We found that N-Myc exhibited an apical-to-basal expression gradient in normal control, while high level of N-Myc expression could be detected in the basal region of Pax2Cre;Sufuf/f mutant cochlea at E16.5. High level of N-Myc expression could also be observed at the basal region of Gli3P1-4/P1-4 mutant cochlea, but undetectable in the cochlear ducts of Gli3Δ699/Δ699 mutants. To address whether Gli3 repressor could inhibit N-Myc expression, we examined Pax2Cre;Sufuf/f;Gli3Δ699/Δ699 compound mutants. In the presence of the Gli3699 repressor protein, N-Myc was only expressed at very low level in the compound mutant. As our analysis described above had clearly showed that Gli3 repressor was not required for hair cell differentiation, the negative regulation of N-Myc expression by Gli3 was likely to be an upstream effect, in the regulation of progenitor cells. We have completed Objective 2, and the functions of N-Myc in hair cell differentiation was investigated as described in Objective 3 below. Objective 3. To elucidate the roles of N-Myc in the regulation of Atoh1 and cochlear hair cell differentiation We hypothesized that N-Myc might inhibit cochlear HC differentiation directly by transcriptional regulation of Atoh1, or indirectly by cellular and/or other signaling mechanisms. Our in vitro ChIP and luciferase assay experiments suggested that it was unlikely that N-Myc could suppress Atoh1 expression by directly binding to Atoh1 genomic regions. The role of N-Myc was likely to affect HC differentiation through other cellular mechanisms. To investigate how N-Myc could negatively regulate HC differentiation, we used an inducible N-Myc over-expression transgenic mouse system, employing either Pax2Cre or Emx2Cre, to cross with Rosa-rtTA-IRES-EGFP and tetO-N-Myc mutant mouse lines to generate compound mutants for analyses. We treated the Pax2Cre;rtTA;N-Myc and Emx2Cre;rtTA;N-Myc mutants with doxycycline at E10.5 and E11.5 and examined the mutant cochlea at different stages. At E13.5, the expression of Sox2 and Jag1 were expanded, the prosensory region at the basal turn was much broader than the mid-apical turn. In the expanded Sox2+ domain, a large number of progenitors entered S-phase and were labelled with BrdU. To investigate whether prosensory cell cycle exit was affected, p27Kip1 staining was performed. In the medial and apical part of the mutant cochlea, p27Kip1 was not expressed. However, by E14.5, p27Kip1 was upregulated at the basal and medial turn but not in the apical region. Our results suggested that the cell cycle withdrawal was delayed and occurred in an altered direction in the N-Myc mutant cochlea. Wholemount staining of HC marker indicated that the differentiation of sensory progenitors was delayed upon N-Myc upregulation. Continuous rows of HCs spanning the basal and medial turn but the prosensory cells of the apical region remain undifferentiated at E16.5. However, when N-Myc overexpression was induced at E14.5, at the stage when prosensory cell cycle exit was largely completed, hair cell differentiation was not affected when examined by Myo7a staining at E16.5. Therefore, N-Myc contributes to the spatio-temporal control of proliferation and cell cycle exit of cochlear sensory progenitors, which is crucial to the correct timing of hair cell differentiation at later stage. To investigate the role of N-Myc in the organization and patterning of hair cells, Pax2;rtTA;N-Myc mutants were treated with doxycycline at E11.5 and the cochlea analyzed at E18.5. The medial part of the mutant organ of Corti was severely disorganized, with supernumerary inner and outer hair cells, with a markedly expanded population of Sox2+ supporting cells, further supporting that N-Myc is required for cellular patterning of sensory cells in the organ of Corti. In summary, we have shown that N-Myc and Shh signaling function in parallel in the sensory progenitors and in hair cell differentiation in the developing organ of Corti. We have fully completed Objective 3.

17159316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17159316.value: In this study, we have made the following discoveries: (1) We showed that Sufu is essential for controlling the timing and progression of cochlear hair cell (HC) differentiation. We found that down-regulation of Gli2, the major transcriptional activator of Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) signaling pathway, is a prerequisite for HC differentiation. Using a series of mouse mutants of Shh signaling factors, including Sufu, Spop, Ptch1, Gli2 and Gli3, we modulated the expression of the Gli activator and repressor in the developmental cochlea genetically. Our study revealed that Gli2 could activate Sox2 and prevent HC differentiation through maintaining the sensory progenitor cell state. (2) Shh signaling is required for the coordinated spatiotemporal regulation of timing and progression of hair cell differentiation, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We found that the spatiotemporal differentiation pattern of HCs is achieved by progenitor cells along the basal-apical axis sensing the level of Gli2: cells with low Gli2 could differentiate, whereas cells with high Gli2 are locked in the progenitor state. This study provides novel molecular insights on Shh mediated HC differentiation in the mammalian cochlea. (3) We found that Sox2 expression level is higher in the progenitor cells than the differentiated cells along the basal-apical axis of developing cochlea and is down-regulated from base to apex during cochlear development. Using a series of Sufu;Sox2 compound mutants which expressed different levels of Sox2, we showed that the differential level of Sox2 expression is controlled by Shh signaling, leading to the basal-apical directional differentiation pattern of HCs. (4) While both Pax2Cre;Sufuf/f and Pax2;rtTA;N-Myc mutants exhibited increased proliferation of sensory progenitors and delayed hair cell differentiation, we conclude that Shh signaling and N-Myc have different functions in the formation of organ of Corti and differentiation of HCs. In Pax2Cre;Sufuf/f inner ear, N-Myc was upregulated in the basal turn, sensory progenitors failed to exit the cell cycle and continued to proliferate at E14.5. In Pax2Cre;Sufuf/f mutant, sensory progenitors at medial and apical turn were properly organized and already exited cell cycle before E14.5, yet displayed delay HC differentiation, suggesting that Shh signaling has a direct suppressive effect in HC differentiation. However, up-regulation of N-Myc in the gain-of-function mutant after cell cycle exit did not affect the timing/progression of HC differentiation, indicating an indirect effect.

17159316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17159316.value: In this project, we have focused on the roles of Shh signaling in the differentiation of cochlear sensory hair cell differentiation. However, the control of non-sensory cell differentiation, including the stria vascularis in the dorsal cochlear epithelium, is largely unknown. During the course of this study, our mutant analysis showed that Shh signaling also controls the formation of non-sensory cells. We found that the development of the stria vascularis was also affected in the Sufu and Ptch1 mutants. Therefore, it is possible that Shh signaling affects the growth, patterning, and differentiation of different cell types of the developing cochlea. To address the specific functions of the Shh signaling factors, we propose to make use of the single cell RNA-Seq technology platform to investigate the developmental trajectory of different sensory and non-sensory cells, and decipher the roles of Shh signaling factors in their development and functions. We will seek research funding from the RGC and other research grant sources to support these further studies.

17159316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17159316.value: Development of mammalian organ of Corti requires precise control of progenitor proliferation, cell cycle withdrawal and differentiation. Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) signaling is required for the coordinated spatiotemporal regulation of prosensory progenitors and differentiation into hair cells (HC). Using loss-of-function and gain-of-function genetic approaches, we showed that Sufu is essential for controlling the timing and progression of cochlear HC differentiation. We found that Gli2 is pivotal for the regulation of Sox2 expression; down-regulation of Gli2 is required for HC differentiation. Deletion of both Sufu and Spop caused robust Gli2 activation and severe disruption of HC differentiation. Down-regulation of Gli2 by Spop restored HC differentiation in the Sufu mutant. The spatiotemporal dynamic regulation of Sox2 expression level is controlled by Shh signaling. While both Pax2Cre;Sufuf/f and Pax2Cre;rtTA;N-Myc mutants exhibited increased proliferation of sensory progenitors and delayed HC differentiation, we found that Shh signaling and N-Myc have different functions in the organ of Corti and differentiation of HCs. We showed that N-Myc is required for the spatio-temporal control of proliferation and cell cycle exit of cochlear sensory progenitors, which in turn affects HC differentiation. Our findings have shed light on our understanding of cochlear hair cell differentiation, and the pathogenesis of human hearing loss.

17159616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17159616.value: Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism of GPx3 on liver graft injury will lay the foundation for further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent graft non-function and late phase consequences. The further application of therapeutics by GPx3 will be worthwhile for exploration. The anti-cancer effect of GPx3 will be also the potential treatment for liver cancer as well as for the cancer recurrence after liver transplantation for liver cancer patient. Actually, we have collaborated with Prof Sun (City U) for developing the micro-robot carrying MSC-GPx3 for cancer therapies in mouse models. Therefore, GPx3 will not only be able to attenuate the liver injury, but also to inhibit the tumor growth/recurrence of HCC.

17159616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17159616.value: Orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT) has been regarded as the best curative treatment for the patients with end stage of liver diseases including advanced liver cirrhosis and acute liver failure. However, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury is still an inevitable consequence during liver transplantation. Hence, elucidating the mechanism and minimizing the adverse consequences of hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury would be important for improving liver transplantation outcomes and the survival of patients in the long run. Representing the efforts for basic, translational and clinical research, we have not identified Glutathione Peroxidase 3 (GPx3) as a functional biomarker for liver graft injury in our clinical series, we have also tackled the basic issues of molecular mechanism for GPx3 regulating liver graft injury after transplantation. We have further explored the therapeutic value of GPx3 delivered by human induced pluripotent stem cell derived mesenchymal stem cells (hiPSC-MSCs) using a series of in vitro functional studies and different types of animal models. Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism for the liver graft injury will lay the foundation for further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent graft non-function and late phase consequences.

17160016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17160016.value: DNA methylation has been demonstrated to be a key regulatory mechanism for genomic imprinting, heterochromatin formation, X chromosome inactivation, transcriptional repression and the maintenance of genome stability, etc. Aberrant DNA methylation has been observed in various cancer cell types. DNMT3A and DNMT3B together with a non-catalytic paralogue DNMT3L establish de novo DNA methylation, whereas the maintenance DNA methyltransferase DNMT1 is responsible for propagation of DNA methylation patterns through cell divisions. Although DNA methylation has been extensively studied over the past several decades, recent breakthroughs have dramatically expanded our understanding of the underlying mechanisms. A number of studies have suggested that DNMT1 alone is not sufficient for the faithful maintenance of DNA methylation during DNA replication, which is consistent with the recent structure-based analyses indicating that DNMT1 is a self-inhibitory enzyme. Therefore, additional allosteric factors are required to regulate DNMT1 enzymatic activity. UHRF1 has emerged as a critical protein to promote the maintenance of genomic DNA methylation patterns. UHRF1 SRA domain specifically recognizes hemi-methylated DNA, which helps recruiting DNMT1 to its targeted substrate sites. UHRF1 tandem Tudor domain and PHD finger bind favorably to methylated histone H3K9 mark, which is important for targeting DNMT1-UHRF1 complex to the proper genomic loci. The UHRF1 C-terminal RING domain functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase towards histone H3, the ubiquitinated histone H3 is subsequently recognized by DNMT1 RFTS domain, which helps recruit DNMT1 to DNA replication sites. Interestingly, RFTS domain not only is important for targeting DNMT1 to replication loci, but also exerts an inhibitory effect on DNMT1 enzymatic activity. Although previous studies have demonstrated UHRF1 physically associates with DNMT1, the detailed molecular mechanism of this interaction remains unclear. Also, UHRF1 contains a N-terminal ubiquitin-like domain (UBL) whose function remains to be explored. In this proposal, based on the preliminary results, we will develop a structure-based paradigm for functional profiling of UHRF1 and DNMT1 including the following aims: (1) To provide the molecular basis of faithful DNA methylation maintenance mediated by histone H3 ubiquitination; (2) To characterize the molecular interaction of DNMT1 with UHRF1; (3) To characterize the UHRF1-regulated DNMT1 enzymatic activity in vitro; (4) To evaluate genomic DNA methylation level in UHRF1-/- ES cells expressing UHRF1 mutants. The overall goal of the proposed research is to understand the fundamental molecular mechanisms of DNMT1-UHRF1 complex in maintenance of DNA methylation patterns and regulation of gene expression. DNA甲基化已被证明是基因組銘印，異染色質形成， X染色體失活，基因沉默和基因組穩定性的關鍵調節機制。在多種類型的癌細胞中可觀察到異常的DNA甲基化。DNMT3A和DNMT3B連同非催化旁系蛋白DNMT3L負責從頭DNA甲基化，而DNMT1 在細胞分裂過程中負責維持細胞DNA 的甲基化模式。雖然DNA甲基化在過去的幾十年中已經被廣泛的研究，但最近的研究突破大大擴充我們對其基本機制的理解。 大量的研究表明，僅有DNMT1在DNA複製過程中是不足以去維持DNA甲基化的水平，這與最近基於DNMT1的結構的分析認為它是一種自我抑制酶是一致的。因此，在DNA複製過程中需要有額外的變構因子來調節DNMT1的酶活性。 UHRF1已被證實為一個關鍵蛋白來促進維護基因組DNA甲基化模式。 UHRF1能與DNMT1形成復合物，UHRF1 SRA結構域特異性地識別半甲基化的DNA，這有助於招募DNMT1到其底物的位點。UHRF1串聯Tudor域和相鄰的PHD能選擇性的識別甲基化組蛋白H3K9標記，這有利於靶向DNMT1 - UHRF1複合物到適當的基因組位點。 UHRF1 C端RING結構域是一个靶向組蛋白H3 的E3泛素連接酶, 在S期泛素化的組蛋白H3能被DNMT1 RFTS域識別，這有助於招募DNMT1到DNA複製叉的站點。有趣的是， RFTS域不僅是針對DNMT1招募到複製位點很重要，但也發揮了上DNMT1酶活性的抑製作用。儘管有以前的研究認為UHRF1與DNMT1形成復合物，但這種相互作用的詳細分子機制尚不清楚。另外， UHRF1包含一個N-端UBL結構域，其功能還有待探索。 我們這個項目是基於已有的初步結果去進一步剖析UHRF1和DNMT1復合物的結構與功能。具體包括以下目標： （1）為組蛋白H3泛素化調控的維持DNA甲基化提供分子機制; （2）詳細表徵DNMT1與UHRF1的分子相互作用; （3）在敲除UHRF1 的ES細胞中表達不同的UHRF1突變體進而評估UHRF1不同結構域 對細胞DNA甲基化水平的貢獻。 總之，我們研究的總體目標是要了解DNMT1-UHRF1複合物在維護DNA甲基化模式和基因表達調控過程中的的基本分子機制。

17160016.label: Realisation of objectives
17160016.value: Mammalian DNMT1 is mainly responsible for maintenance DNA methylation that is critical in maintaining stem cell pluripotency and controlling lineage specification during early embryonic development. A number of studies have demonstrated that DNMT1 is an auto-inhibited enzyme and its enzymatic activity is allosterically regulated by a number of interacting partners. UHRF1 has previously been reported to regulate DNMT1 in multiple ways, including control of substrate specificity and the proper genome targeting. UHRF1 functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase to target histone H3, DNMT1 was found to bind subsequently to ubiquitinated H3 via its RFTS domain, which helps recruit DNMT1 to DNA replication sites. Interestingly, RFTS domain not only helps target DNMT1 to replication loci, but also exerts an autoinhibitory effect on DNMT1 enzymatic activity. On the other hand, auto-inhibition of DNMT1 is relieved during DNA replication, but it remains elusive if the interaction of DNMT1 RFTS domain with ubiquitinated histone H3 has an impact on DNMT1 enzymatic activity. Over this funding period, we have fully achieved all three project objectives. First, we determined the crystal structure of DNMT1 RFTS domain in complex with ubiquitin. Furthermore, we presented evidence that UHRF1 N-terminal UBL domain directly interacts with DNMT1 by NMR titration and ITC measurement. Interestingly we found that ubiquitin and UHRF1 UBL bind DNMT1 differently although UBL domain structurally resembles ubiquitin. Results from in vitro DNA methylation assay indicate that binding to UHRF1 UBL domain but not ubiquitin could stimulate DNMT1 enzymatic activity towards hemimethylated DNA substrate. On the other hand, binding to ubiquitinated histone H3 but not ubiquitin or histone H3 alone could alleviate DNMT1 self-inhibitory effect. Lastly, our cell-based data showed that introducing DNMT1 wild-type but not the mutants with impaired ubiquitin binding into DNMT1 knockout mouse ES cells can effectively restore the global DNA methylation pattern. We also showed that expression of UBL deleted or RING finger deleted UHRF1 mutant cannot restore the proper DNMT1 nuclear localization and thus cannot rescue DNA methylation defects in UHRF1 knockout mouse ES cells. Overall, our study demonstrates that the interaction between UHRF1 and DNMT1 mediated by UBL domain, as well as the interaction between DNMT1 and ubiquitinated histone H3 established by UHRF1 are required for faithful propagation of DNA methylation during DNA replication.

17160016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17160016.value: In this project, we provide a detailed molecular basis of DNMT1 mediated ubiquitinated histone binding at replication foci by solving the high-resolution crystal structure of DNMT1 RFTS domain in complex with ubiquitin. Interestingly, one RFTS domain can bind two ubiquitin molecules simultaneously. Ile44-centered and Ile36-centered hydrophobic patches of ubiquitin 1, as well as Ile44-centered hydrophobic patch of ubiquitin 2 are involved in the RFTS interactions whereas electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding and salt bridges also contribute complementary to the complex formation. This mode of ubiquitin binding is quite different from most of other ubiquitin recognition patterns. We also found that DNMT1 RFTS domain can interact with UHRF1 N-terminal UBL domain thus mediates the interaction between UHRF1 and DNMT1. Unlike ubiquitin, UHRF1 UBL domain binds to both DNMT1 RFTS domain and DNMT1_621 (aa: 621-1616). The results from in vitro DNA methylation assay suggest that the binding of ubiquitinated histone H3 to RFTS domain of DNMT1 alleviates DNMT1 autoinhibitory effect. Strikingly, binding of ubiquitin or histone H3 alone failed to show the stimulatory effect on DNMT1 enzymatic activity. On the other hand, the N-terminal UBL domain of UHRF1, which structurally resembles ubiquitin, not only binds to DNMT1 but also stimulates its methyltransferase activity. Considering ubiquitinated histone H3 is enriched at replication foci, we postulate that ubiquitinated histone H3 binding to DNMT1 not only helps accumulate DNMT1 at replication foci, but also alleviates DNMT1 autoinhibitory effect. Lastly, we performed structure guided genetic complementation experiments to show the binding of DNMT1 to ubiquitinated histone H3, as well as the interaction between DNMT1 and UHRF1 UBL domain plays equally important role in efficient DNA methylation maintenance. It is conceivable that all modular domains of UHRF1 participate and act in concert with DNMT1 to maintain DNA methylation pattern during DNA replication.

17160016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17160016.value: Future structural analysis is required to unravel the detailed molecular basis of UHRF1 UBL binding to DNMT1.

17160016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17160016.value: DNA methylation was the first epigenetic alteration to be observed in cancer cells, and a long list of genes affected by promoter CpG island methylation have been reported in cancers and aging. Several inhibitors target on DNMT1 and HDAC1 have now been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration or are in clinical trials with good prognosis for tumor regression. UHRF1 is over-expressed in many human cancer cell lines and down-regulation of UHRF1 leads to growth arrest of cancer cell lines. UHRF members are regulated by tumor-suppressor genes but are also able to regulate the expression of these genes such as p21, p16INK4A, p14ARF. Thus, both UHRF1 and DNMT1 are perfect targets for developing new anticancer drugs. To understand their structures and catalytic mechanism is pivotal for unravelling the molecular basis of related human diseases and developing the future therapeutic strategies.

17160916.value: 我們利用紅系細胞蛋白質組分析以了解血紅素和鐵的代謝，確定在紅細胞分化過程中乙型膽綠素還原酶（Biliverdin Reductase B, BLVRB, 也被稱為黃素還原酶, Flavin reductase, FLR）之表達上調至甚高水平。在文獻中，FLR/BLVRB具有重要藥理學性質（在高鐵血紅蛋白血症中，通過亞甲藍還原高鐵血紅蛋白）和多方面體外生化特性（作為黃素及非甲型膽綠素異構體的還原酶和氧化還原循環劑，以及可以在分離過程中呈現為血紅素蛋白）。從生物信息學分析及試點研究中，FLR/BLVRB在那些有高水平的血紅素合成（如發展和成熟的紅細胞，肝臟）或有潛在高血紅素降解活性（鐵回收巨噬細胞，內皮細胞）的細胞或組織中有高水平表達。我們已經證明，純化的FLR/BLVRB對鐵血紅素具特定結合親和力。此外，利用shRNA敲低分化中紅細胞的FLR/BLVRB導致血紅蛋白水平有些微下降。雖然這些觀察結果暗示FLR/BLVRB與紅細胞及巨噬細胞相關，及具有與血紅素分子有關的屬性，此蛋白質的生物學功能仍不清楚。為了更了解FLR/BLVRB的生物學作用和分子功能，我們將有系統地分析（1）在體外和細胞內FLR/BLVRB與血紅素結合的特性;（2）FLR/BLVRB的血紅素合成紅細胞血紅素分解代謝的巨噬細胞的調節;（3）在紅系細胞和巨噬細胞敲低FLR/BLVRB所帶來的影響;（4）FLR/BLVRB在斑馬魚模型中器官水平上的表達。擬議進行的研究將有助破解FLR / BLVRB的功能之謎。這顯然與細胞內血紅素的處理及周轉有很大關係，結果將為血紅素的生物學及相關健康和疾病增添重要的知識。

17160916.label: Realisation of objectives
17160916.value: Summary of research activities in relation to the project objectives : 1. To characterize the heme binding properties of purified FLR/BLVRB by spectrophotometric methods and site-directed mutagenesis of key amino acid residues that are possibly involved in heme-coordination; and to analyze the heme binding of FLR/BLVRB in cells by immuno-isolation and mass spectrometric techniques. - Biochemical characterization of the heme binding properties of purified FLR/BLVRB and that of a mutant of histidine near the tetrapyrrole binding site has been performed. Heme binding of FLR/BLVRB in cells has been demonstrated by heme peroxidase staining on native 2D protein gels followed by mass spectrometric identification, and also by heme-sepharose pull down. Cellular Engagement Thermal Shift Assay was employed to reveal the intracellular targeting BLVRB by heme. 2. To study the regulation of FLR/BLVRB expression in heme-synthesizing erythroid cells and heme-catabolizing macrophages in response to modulation of heme levels and during cell differentiation/activation; and to identify the interacting proteins through proteomic analysis of the immuno-isolated protein complexes. - The regulation of FLR/BLVRB expression in erythroid MEL cells in response to modulators of heme synthesis, iron and oxidative stress has been studied. Proximity dependent cellular biotinylation have been applied to identify interacting proteins of BLVRB. A number of antioxidant proteins and glycolytic enzymes were identified as potential interacting partners of BLVRB. 3. To determine the effects of FLR/BLVRB knockdown in mouse erythroid cells and macrophages on cellular heme levels and related protein expressions. -The effects of FLR/BLVRB shRNA knockdown in erythroid MEL cells on hemoglobinization, oxidative status, protoporphyrin IX levels and cell survival have been investigated. A proteomic analysis of BLVRB knockdown has been performed. J774 mouse macrophage cell line with FLR/BLVRB depleted by shRNA has been established, and corresponding analyses on antioxidative responses have been performed. 4. To examine the expression of FLR/BLVRB at organismal level in zebrafish at embryonic stage by whole mount in situ hybridization. -Morpholino knockdown of FLR/BLVRB has been performed and the effect of hemoglobinization was assessed. Results: • BLVRB is a cellular heme binding protein showing heme-inhibitory NADPH-dependent reductase activities In this work, we are working toward a model to elucidate the functional role of BLVRB in erythroid cells in terms of its heme-associated properties. We have demonstrated BLVRB/FLR display apparent heme binding activities in vitro and in cells. Recombinant mouse BLVRB could be readily isolated as a reddish brown heme binding protein in E. coli. It has a submicromolar specific binding affinity to ferric heme with a 1:1 stoichiometry. It has very weak interaction with protoporphyrin IX, suggesting the iron centre of heme participate in the protein binding. Ferric heme (Fe(III)) appears to be the preferred binding form of heme for BLVRB. The NADPH-dependent reductase activity of BLVRB is potently inhibited by heme. BLVRB in the erythroid cell extracts exhibits heme-dependent peroxidase activity when resolved on a native gel and could be isolated by hemin-agarose, supporting that BLVRB may bind heme under cellular condition. Furthermore, the heme binding property of BLVRB was further supported by Cellular Engagement Thermal Shift Assay which indicates the targeting of BLVRB by added heme as revealed by its enhanced thermal protein stability inside the cells. • The BLVRB expression is tightly linked to erythroid differentiation and play a modulatory role in optimal production of hemoglobin The BLVRB protein expression is markedly up-regulated upon induction of erythroid differentiation in mouse erythroleukemia MEL cells, but is insensitive to cell treatment with modulators of oxidative stress, heme and iron. This suggests that the expression and function of BLVRB is highly specialized for erythroid differentiation irrespective of cellular stress status. Upon complete depletion of BLVRB by shRNA in MEL cells, there was a modest decrease in the hemoglobinization. The results indicate BLVRB does not directly participate in the heme/hemoglobin synthesis pathway but rather play a modulatory role for optimal production of hemoglobin and/or erythroid differentiation. Furthermore, upon induction of differentiation, the BLVRB depleted MEL cells is more sensitive to growth inhibitory effects of heme synthesis inhibitor (succinylacetone) when compared to control shRNA cells, suggesting that BLVRB may play a role in maintaining cell survival under heme deficient condition. A translation blocking morpholino was microinjected into zebrafish embryos at the one-cell stage, and hemoglobinization was assessed at 72 hpf using o-dianisidine staining, showing subtle decreases in hemoglobinization. • BLVRB participates in cellular oxidative balance As developing erythroid cells are subjected to augmented oxidative stress owing to accumulation of heme, which is intrinsically a toxic proxidant, the role of BLVRB in the antioxidant regulatory activities in developing erythroid cells was investigated. Depletion of BLVRB results in increases in antioxidant activities as assessed by NRF2/ARE reporter activity and also increases in the apparent NRF2-dependent HO-1 expression in both induced differentiating and uninduced MEL cells. These results imply that BLVRB may play a role in the cellular antioxidant function and depletion of which triggers compensatory increase in NRF2 activities to maintain proper redox balance. Upon induction of differentiation, the BLVRB depleted MEL cells are more susceptible to cytotoxicity mediated by thiol depleting agent (diethylmaleate, DEM) when compared to control shRNA cells, suggesting that BLVRB may play a role in maintaining cell survival under oxidative stress condition. Furthermore, SA and DEM treatment stimulated increase in cellular oxidants and the depletion of BLVRB appeared to further augment the cellular oxidant levels particularly in induced MEL cells, suggesting that BLVRB may play a role in antioxidant function in the hemoglobinizing cells. • BLVRB regulates protoporhyrin levels in hemoglobin-synthesizing cells While induced MEL cells have low levels of protoporphyrin (the ligand of iron in heme) BLVRB depleted MEL cells have markedly elevated levels of protoporphyrin IX compared to the control cells upon induction of differentiation and reintroduction of BLVRB can abrogate the increases, strongly suggest that BLVRB regulates the protophyrin levels (Fig. 12). The blockade by heme synthesis inhibitor succinylacetone and further stimulation by supplementation of cells with holotransferrin, which is known to stimulate heme synthesis via stimulation of translation of erythroid aminolevulinc acid synthase indicates that the accumulated proptoporphyrin was derived from nascent synthesis. Treatment of the cells with ascorbate or N-acetylcysteine could reduce the protoporphyrin content suggesting that the proptoporphyrin accumulation is dependent on the cellular oxidative status. Since the heme content and heme synthesis enzymes of MEL cells was not appreciably affected by BLVRB to the extent as that of protoporphyrin level, the accumulation of protoporphyrin mediated by BLVRB depletion is likely due to a deficiency in intracellular transport or efflux mechanism.

17160916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17160916.value: Our data demonstrates that several unrecognized biological roles of BLVRB/FLR which is, in the literature, often simply regarded as a biliverdin reducing enzyme in the heme degradation pathway. We have provided evidence that BLVRB is an erythroid active, heme-associated protein with NADPH-dependent reductase activities. BLVRB is shown to play a role in cellular redox balance as knockdown of BLVRB in the induced pro-erythroid cells aggravates intracellular oxidation and loss of viability mediated by thiol depleting agent or heme synthesis inhibitor. Granting the fact that heme excess or deficiency are known to impose cellular stress and the levels of heme are dynamically modulated in developing erythroid cells under physiological or pathological conditions, it is tempting to speculate that the heme binding functions and reductase activities of BLVRB are integrated into regulation of erythroid heme levels and oxidative balance. Another novel finding of this study is on regulation of cellular protoporphyrin levels by BLVRB. The significance of maintaining appropriate levels of cellular protopophyrin in hemoglobin-synthesizing cells is important as these cells have capacity to produce overwhelming levels of protoporphyrin. BLVRB depletion results in marked increase accumulation of protoporphyrin, suggesting that BLVRB may regulate the protoporphyrin levels via an intracellular transport or efflux mechanism.

17160916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17160916.value: We have characterized BLVRB as an erythroid active, heme-regulated NADPH-dependent reductase. It confers cytoprotection in developing erythroid cells under oxidative stress conditions in connection with cellular heme levels. Several outstanding questions remain: (1) What are the physiological substrate(s) of NADPH reductase ? While BLVRB/FR is known to be a promiscuous reductase, the exact physiological (protein) substrates are still unknown. To this end, some emerging proteomic methods like System-wide Identification of Enzyme Substrates by Thermal Analysis (SIESTA) (BioRxiv, doi: https://doi.org/10.1101/423418) can be employed to find out the possible substrates through a thermal proteome profiling approach which is practiced in the PI’s laboratory. It is also interesting to note that BLVRB contains a protein kinase like ATP binding domain and its phosphotransferse activities is worthy to investigate. (2) While BLVRB is also found to be expressed in quite abundant levels in other non-erythroid cell types, its functional roles in a broader aspect is still not clear. For examples, there are several reports on the expression of BLVRB is found to be linked with some cancer cells or tumors. Thus it will be desirable to examine the roles of BLVRB in cancer in aspects like cell proliferation, tumor formation, metastasis and stemness properties.

17160916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17160916.value: Biliverdin reductase B(BLVRB), also known as flavin reductase(FLR), is especially expressed in cells having high levels of heme synthesis (e.g. developing erythroid cells, fetal and adult liver). BLVRB exhibits NADPH-dependent reductase activity toward non-alpha isomers of biliverdin, flavins and redox cycling agents. Nonetheless, the physiological function of BLVRB is obscure. In this work, the functional role of BLVRB in developing erythroid cells in relation to its heme-associated properties is elucidated. Recombinant mouse BLVRB binds ferric heme with a submicromolar affinity in association with inhibition of the NADPH-dependent reductase activity while displaying heme peroxidase activity. Upon induction of erythroid cell differentiation , the BLVRB protein expression is markedly up-regulated and associated with heme as demonstrated by its apparent peroxidase activity. Knockdown of BLVRB in the induced MEL cells aggravates intracellular oxidation and loss of viability mediated by thiol depleting agent or heme synthesis inhibitor, suggesting that BLVRB may maintain the cell survival under oxidative stress or heme deficient conditions. Our study suggests that BLVRB/FLR, which is usually regarded as a biliverdin reducing enzyme in the heme degradation pathway, is an erythroid active, heme-regulated NADPH-dependent reductase. It confers cytoprotection in developing erythroid cells under oxidative stress conditions in connection with cellular heme levels.

17161116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17161116.value: EB病毒编码的LMP1诱导鼻咽上皮细胞永生化的研究 鼻咽癌是一类常见的高发于中国南部地区的癌症，尤其是香港和广东人口。EB病毒感染与鼻咽癌（NPC）密切相关。EB病毒编码的 LMP1能在鼻咽癌病人的早期阶段表达, 其表达可能是导致鼻咽癌发病的主要原因。 LMP1被认为是EB病毒所表达致癌基因，并且能够转化啮齿动物的成纤维细胞（RAT）和人永生的角质形成细胞（HaCaT细胞）为恶性癌细胞。 我们最近的研究揭示LMP1能够诱导鼻咽上皮细胞永生化。端粒酶诱导的鼻咽上皮细胞永生化是一个低效率的过程。然而, LMP1与hTert(人类端粒酶)共同表达可以有效的诱导鼻咽上皮细胞永生化。EGFR过表达可以促进LMP1诱导的鼻咽上皮细胞永生化。 我们的进一步研究表明LMP1通过激活mTORC1和mTORC2信号传导通路促进鼻咽上皮细胞永生化。mTORC1特异性抑制剂， 雷帕霉素可以有效的抑制LMP1诱导的鼻咽上皮细胞生长。 LMP1抑制AMPK信号的活化是一个潜在的mTORC1的上游调节因子。 干扰mTORC2相关的底物, Rictor, 可以诱发永生化的鼻咽上皮细胞进入衰老的过程。然而，有关LMP1诱导的鼻咽上皮细胞永生化的机制还需进一步研究。 在这项研究中，我们将探讨（a）诱导鼻咽上皮细胞永生化的信号通路以及相关的通路的激活的机制以及与mTORC1和mTORC2的活化途径的关系; （b）EGFR在LMP1诱导的原代鼻咽上皮细胞永生化过程中的作用。特别是，我们将探讨mTORC1 在永生化过程中的激活与AMPK的活性的抑制是受EGFR调节还是直接由LMP1调节。 如上所述，鼻咽上皮细胞中LMP1表达激活mTORC1信号。AMPK信号是mTORC1上游的一个抑制调节因子。有趣的是，LMP1可以抑制AMPK的活化（Lo et al，J path 2013）。我们推测，LMP1抑制AMPK的活性可进一步激活mTORC1通路而参与鼻咽上皮细胞的的永生化过程中。LMP1抑制AMPK活性的机制尚未明确阐明。 LMP1被认为是能够激活多种细胞信号传导途径的信号分子。 其中有两条可能参与AMPK活性调节的通路：MEK-ERK通路以及PI3K /Akt信号通路。AMPK在Thr172的磷酸化激活可能与LKB1的磷酸化有关。MEK-ERK信号传导主要是通过EGFR活化，可能抑制LKB1的磷酸化作用从而进一步抑制AMPK的活化。PI3K / Akt信号也可以通过诱导AMPK的Ser487的磷酸化从而有效的抑制LKB1参与的AMPK Thr172磷酸化激活。我们将集中研究可能参与的介导LMP1诱导的AMPK抑制以及其在鼻咽上皮细胞的永生化过程中的作用。 有关mTORC2信号通路激活相关的调节因素尚不明确。IGF1/ IGFR信号通路可以介导mTORC2信号通路的激活。最近的一项研究表明，IKK能激活mTORC2。无论IGF1/ IGFR还是IKK都已经被证实是LMP1的下游信号通路。这些通路参与的mTORC2的活化以及在永生化过程中的作用将在我们的课题中进一步研究。 研究LMP1诱导的鼻咽上皮细胞永生化的过程，将有助于我们理解EB病毒感染和它的编码基因在鼻咽癌发病机制中所起的作用。除了理解EB病毒感染在鼻咽癌发病机制中作用，该研究还有助于开发鼻咽癌诊断以及治疗靶点。

17161116.label: Realisation of objectives
17161116.value: Objective 1: To define the key functional domains and signaling pathways of LMP1 involved in the immortalization of primary nasopharyngeal epithelial (NPE) cells. Using a series of LMP1 mutants, we have examined their abilities to immortalize primary culture of immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We found that LMP1 mutants defective in either CTAR1 and/or CTAR 2 have diminished ability to immortalize nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Our recent report have showed that NF-kB activation is common in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Hence, it is not surprising to observe the role of CTAR1 and 2 of LMP1, which are the key domains involved in activation of NF-kB, are required for immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Furthermore, we delineated that the activation of mTORC1, and possibly also mTORC2, is involved in immortalization involving the activation of Art and NF-kB. Treatment of immortalized cells with rapamycin which block mTORC1 affects the growth of immortalized nasopharyngeal cells. Similarly, inhibition by IKK inhibitor, eg. the NBD (Nemo binding domain) also effectively inhibited proliferation of immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Objective 2. To determine the role of EGFR overexpression in LMP1 immortalization of NPE cells Our earlier study showed that some of the nasopharyngeal epithelial cells failed to be immortalized by LMP1 despite elongation of life span. Overexpression of EGFR is essential in rescuing the nasopharyngeal epithelial cells undergoing immortalization by LMP1. However, EGFR overexpression alone is not sufficient to immortalize nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We found that EGFR overexpression activates PI3K signaling pathways which activates mTORC1 and mTORC2 to immortalize nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Objective 3. To define signaling events involved in LMP1 inhibition of AMPK activity and its impact on mTORC1 activation and immortalization. According to previous published report, LMP1 could inhibit AMPK activity which may impact on mTORC1 activation to achieve immortalization. We have repeated the findings in these reports using our immortalised nasopharyngeal epithelial cell models. Our immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cell models have low AMPK activity but high mTORC1 activation. Overexpression of AMPK suppressed the proliferation of immortalised nasopharyngeal epithelial cells supporting a role of AMPK in immortalisation. LMP1 immortalised nasopharyngeal epithelial cells has low AMPK activity. The influence of LMP1 on AMPK may be indirect as direct regulation of AMPK expression by LMP1 was not observed. Objective 4. To investigate the activation mechanisms of mTORC2 by LMP1 and their involvements in immortalization We have characterized the activation mechanism of mTORC2 by LMP1. LMP1 activates the secretion of IGF to activate mTORC2. In EBV-infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells, mTOR2 activation also activates glycolysis via LMP1. We have further characterized the phenotypes downstream of mTORC2 activation of glycolysis. Genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of the mTORC2/AKT signaling blocks the LMP1-induced glycolysis and its phenotype. We also characterize the invasive phenotype induced by LMP1-mediated glycolysis involved epigenetic regulation of SNAIL promoter. The results has been accepted for publication in Oncogene, 2019.

17161116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17161116.value: NPC is closely associated with EBV infection. The LMP1 is commonly expressed in nasopharyngeal carcinoma and in particularly at early stage of development. An immortalization property of LMP1 has been proposed. In this study, we have examined the immortalisation property of LMP1 using primary cultures of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. LMP1 could immortalise primary culture of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells in combination of activation of telomerase. The immortalization activity of LMP1 is greatly improved by co-expressing EGFR in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells undergoing immortalization. In elucidation of the immortalization actions of LMP1, we found that EBV-LMP1 could effectively reprogrammed glucose metabolism to support cell immortalization. Reprogramming of glucose metabolism is essential in cell immortalization and is commonly in cancer cells. Detail analysis of the action of LMP1 in glucose metabolism revealed that LMP1 could up regulate glucose transporter 1 trancription via the mTORC1/NF-kb singling pathways (Zhang J et al., J. Virology, 2017). The mTORC2 singling pathway is also activated by LMP1 through an autocrine secretion of IGF1 and activation of PIK3/Akt. Interestingly, we also observed that mTORC2 activation could further induce nuclear translocation of PDHE1alpha which contribute to cancer metastasis by promoting H3K9 acetylation on the Snail promoter to enhance ell motility, thereby possibly driving metastasis (Zhang J et al., Oncogene, 2018). Hence, we have linked the glucose metabolism activation by LMP1 to invasive property of nasopharyngeal carcinoma which is closely associated with EBV infection.

17161116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17161116.value: Our study revealed an important role of EBV in the pathogenesis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) in reprogramming glucose metabolism which has profound effect on the growth and invasive properties of NPC cells. LMP1 plays an essential role in glucose metabolism. We observed that LMP1 could alter multiple crucial properties of NPC cells in addition to immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Our findings showed that epigenetic modification of chromatin is involved. The action of EBV infection and LMP1 on chromatin modification could be further pursued to reveal the full function of EBV infection in NPC pathogenesis.

17161116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17161116.value: Cellular immortalization is a prerequisite property of all cancer cell. Activation of human telomerase (hTERT) is an essential property of immortalised cells. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is a common feature of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and has long been postulated to play an causal role in the pathogenesis of NPC. The LMP1 is an EBV-encoded viral gene commonly expressed in NPC particularly in early stage of NPC pathogenesis. In this study, we have examined the ability of LMP1 to immortalize primary nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. We observed that the expression of LMP1, in combination with human telomerase, could facilitate immortalisation of primary epithelial cells. Activation of EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor) is involved. Furthermore, we observed that expression of LMP1 could reprogram glucose metabolism in EBV-infected immortalised nasopharyngeal epithelial cells and activation of mTOR pathway is involved. Another novel finding is that LMP1 expression influenced epigenetic chromatin modification to activate expression of SNAIL gene which enhanced the invasive property of EBV-infected NPC cells. The results from this study support a role of EBV infection and expression of LMP1 in immortalization of nasopharyngeal epithelial cells and its transformation into invasive cancer cells.

17163316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17163316.value: Human explosion in the past 1000 years was responsible for much of the biodiversity loss in China. This research project will for the first time investigate the impacts it may have had on coastal marine mammals. Demographic history of a species is a dynamic process that responds to environmental change and stochastic events, and in turn impacts the genetic makeup of populations. Either paleo-events such as climate, or geological events or, more recently, human activities can alter the food supply, size and patchiness of habitat, or cause direct removals, which can ultimately lead to a drastic demographic change. Population decline or bottleneck makes it vulnerable to natural disasters or demographic stochasticity. Therefore identifying the primary factors that determine population history represents an important focal point in population ecology. Since whaling was absent in the history of China, the habitat quantity and accessibility was likely the primary factor shaping the current populations of dolphins and porpoises in these waters, as expressed in their genetic makeup. Demographic analyses of marine mammal are extremely difficult due to the lack of long-term monitoring programs and huge financial burden of boat-based survey. However, given that bottleneck causes loss of genetic diversity, recent advances in molecular genetics provide a powerful tool for investigating demographic history of populations. In this project, we reconstruct the demographic history of two sympatric cetacean species that are found year-round in Hong Kong and Pearl River Delta coastal waters, the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin and the Indo-Pacific finless porpoise. They show overlapping habitat use, similar proximity to human activities, but differ greatly in their life history and current genetic diversity. Equipped with sophisticated analytical and modelling techniques in molecular genetics, we will first tested the presence or absence of bottleneck. A demographic change model will then be built based on our prior knowledge of the species and environment. Subsequently, the genetic demographic parameters, including the ancestral population size, actual population size and the time of decline, will be inferred using maximum likelihood methods. The demographic history of the two species will be further compared to the current and historic availability of habitat, coastline evolution, human demographic expansion and regional development in southern China, helping us to determine the major force(s) that shape the evolutionary history of these two species, and providing valuable insights into a historic perspective on interactions between coastal marine mammals and human activities in China. 過去1000年人口急速膨脹，導致中國的生物多樣性大幅下降。本研究項目將首次調查其中對沿海海洋哺乳動物的影響。 物種的種群歷史是一個動態的進程，會因應環境變化和隨機事件而改變，進而影響種群的基因結構。無論是遠古事件如氣候或地質活動，或更近期的人類活動，都可能改變棲息地的糧食供應、面積大小和完整性，甚至直接移除個體，最終可導致急劇的種群數量變化。當種群的數量下降或遇上瓶頸情況時，種群就會更容易遭受自然災害或種群隨機性所影響。因此，鑑定種群歷史的決定性因素成為了種群生態學中的一個重要焦點。過去中國並沒有捕鯨的歷史，所以棲息地的數量及可使用性很可能成為當中首要的因素，塑造出目前在這水域的海豚和鼠海豚種群，並於他們的基因結構中顯示出來。 由於缺乏長期的監測計劃以及船基調查的巨大財政負擔，海洋哺乳動物的種群統計分析往往極其困難。然而，基於瓶頸情況會減低遺傳多樣性的現象，近期在分子遺傳學的進展為調查種群歷史提供了一個有力的研究方法。在本研究項目中，我們會重建常年出現在香港和珠江三角洲沿海水域的兩種同域的鯨豚類－印度太平洋駝背豚和印度太平洋江豚－的種群歷史。這兩物種使用重疊的棲息地，而且同樣地靠近人類活動範圍；但他們的生活歷史以及當前的遺傳多樣性卻大相逕庭。透過分子遺傳學方面的精密分析和建模技術，我們將首先測試瓶頸現象是否存在；然後再建基於我們之前對物種和環境的了解來構造一個種群變化模型。隨後，各項遺傳種群參數，包括祖先種群數量、實際種群大小和種群下降的時間，將以最大似然性方法去作推斷。最終這兩個物種的種群歷史將進一步與現今和歷史上的棲息地可用性、岸線的演變、人類人口膨脹及南中國的區域發展作出比較，以幫助我們確定這兩品種進化史的主要原因和動力，並在歷史層面上對沿海海洋哺乳動物和中國人類活動之間的互動提供重要的見解。

17163416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17163416.value: 核酸適體是引導性分子進化中一個相當成功的例子，其於治療及診斷上的重要里程碑均在近二十五年內達成。一般而言，適體透過與不同生物分子的分子辨識而發揮作用，當中的鍵聯具高獨特性及吸引力。用以篩選適體的配體指數增強系統進化技術（Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment，SELEX），經過不斷改良及發展後，現已能獲得針對各種不同目標，具緊密鍵聯的適體。此外，生物學對核糖酶功能及最近受注目的核糖體結構的研究，顯示核酸富有催化作用的潛在多樣性。現有適體的功能受制於一般配體指數增強系統進化技術中基於鍵聯的篩選，數個以核酸催化作用而篩選的〝適體酶〞，也僅只透過間接方式獲得。若要開拓核酸適體於生物醫學應用上的功能多樣性，直接篩選是有迫切需要的。 於此，基於催化作用而進行篩選的螢光激活液滴分選，可作為篩選適體的新途徑。本團隊具有橫跨不同領域的專業知識及豐富經驗，包括適體科學（首席研究員，醫學院）及微流體液滴式分選（合作研究員，工程學院）。透過融合各方專長，制定三個以初步合作數據為穩固基礎的研究目標，以應對發展螢光激活液滴分選篩選核酸適體所帶來的挑戰。 目標一，以概念驗證的形式來展示適體能於新開發的微流體液滴系統中被包裹、結合、分析及演化。 目標二，將此方法應用於篩選具過氧化酶特性的適體上，此適體能模擬分子生物學中的主要工具—辣根過氧化酶（horse radish peroxidase，HRP）的過氧化作用。 目標三，透過此創新的液滴式引導性進化途徑，基於催化作用而對核糖核酸（RNA）作出直接篩選，從而演化出新型自我複製核糖核酸酶。 此研究將從應用及基礎的層面上，展出螢光激活液滴分選及催化適體的重要性。其發展更將衍生出與進化起源的基礎相關，研究自行催化及自我複製核酸的實驗方向。

17163416.label: Realisation of objectives
17163416.value: There were three objectives in our original proposal for this grant: 1. Perform a proof of concept study to show that aptamers can be encapsulated, combined, assayed and evolved by fluorescence activated droplet sorting. 2. Apply fluorescence-activated droplet sorting to select for peroxidase-activity nucleic acid aptamers that mimic horseradish peroxidase. 3. Apply fluorescence-activated droplet sorting to evolve new classes of self-replicating RNA enzymes. In this final report, we report completion of 100% of stage 1, 90% of stage 2 and 80% of stage 3. We have published several papers, both primary research articles and reviews, and presented the work at several conferences. The work has also been the main part of the research of PhD student Soubhagya Bhuyan who will be submitting his PhD at the end of Feburary 2021, and has been an important part of the work of post-doctoral fellow Dr. Andrew Kinghorn in the group. We worked together with the Professor Anderson Shum group in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at HKU together with his PhD student Guo Wei. We present some details of objectives individually below: 1. Perform a proof of concept study to show that aptamers can be encapsulated, combined, assayed and evolved by fluorescence activated droplet sorting. We initially performed a bioinformatics study which is related to this in terms of understanding the principles behind aptamer selection which would be required (Aptamer Bioinformatics, Int J Mol Sci, 18, 2516 (2017)). This paper helped to guide us towards the particular microfluidic technology which would be necessary which we described in Advanced Biosystems (Advanced Biosystems (2019, 2 1900012). We developed a particular angle for encapsulation which could also be linked with DNA nanostructure evolution for evolution of nanostructure within droplets which we described in a further two papers (Chembiochem 2018, 19, 1900 and Methods Mol Biol 2021, 2208, 69). We proved the principle of encapsulation and amplification, demonstrated exonuclease activity in droplets, and developed methods for monitoring of activity in droplets, and also optimized times of incubation and fluorescent sorting parameters as per the original grant proposal. Some elements of these steps are within the published papers and others are described in the upcoming two papers in preparation from our group. Overall we report 100% completion of this first objective. 2. Apply fluorescence-activated droplet sorting to select for peroxidase-activity nucleic acid aptamers that mimic horseradish peroxidase. The second objective has been closely linked to the overall PhD study of Soubhagya Bhuyan. We report successful completion of each the steps of objective II as described in the original proposal. We designed a library for aptamer selection which had been optimized for G quadruplex aptamer selection. This work was described in several conference presentations, including at the HKU 22nd RPG symposium in 2017 “An efficient droplet-based nucleic acid amplification methods for direted evolution of functional nucleic acids”. We then in the second experimental step incorporated the library into FADS droplet system and performed selection for peroxidase activity. The main part of this work is in both the conference abstracts and in the two papers in preparation, particularly the development of droplet-digital polymerase chain reaction in preparation for Analytical Chemistry. We have also sequenced and characterized the winning aptamers. We have evolved several G-quadruplex aptamers with the best peroxidase activity yet discovered. This is the main part of Soubhagya Bhuyan’s PhD thesis which will be submitted in early 2021 with accompanying papers to be published at that time. We report completion of 90% of this stage – whilst all experimental steps are complete we are awaiting the final submission of the final papers relating to this work. 3. Apply fluorescence-activated droplet sorting to evolve new classes of self-replicating RNA enzymes. The third objective related to the development of catalytic activity in a droplet. The first sub-aim of self-replicating RNA system proved somewhat challenging so we modified this sub-aim towards the development of fluorescence which was a better fit with the experimental strategy. We reported this work at the EMBS micro and nanotechnology conference initially in Hawaii. This manuscript is presently in preparation for Nucleic Acids Chemistry” “Droplet-assisted evolution and screening of RNA aptamer/fluorogen fluorescence light-up pairs” in collaboration with Professor Shum. We anticipate publication during 2021 as some final experiments were somewhat delayed by the COVID situation. We further developed the fluorescent monitoring method as described in the original proposal. We report completion of 80% of this stage – some final paper submissions related to this stage have been somewhat hindered by the COVID situation and we aim to have all related publications published within 2021.

17163416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17163416.value: In this project we have successfully developed in vitro evolution methods for nucleic acid aptamers. We have developed fluorescent-activated droplet sorting integrating aptamer science with microfluidic approaches. We have successfully shown that aptamers can be encapsulated, combined, assayed and evolved in our microfluidic droplet system. We then used this system to select for DNAzyme peroxidase enzymes that have the highest catalytic activity of any peroxidase DNAzyme yet reported. Furthermore we selected for fluorescent aptamer variants which can extend the applications of aptamers in cell biology nucleic acid tracking experiments. Our results have been published in several strong academic journals and at several conferences. The results have also been the central idea of Soubhagya Bhuyan’s PhD thesis in the group of the PI. The work has been an important component of award of the 2018 research student supervisor award to the PI.

17163416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17163416.value: This work has shown that it is possible to select for aptamers by microfluidic approaches. In other work of the PI which was recently published in PNAS in 2020 the PI has selected non-natural nucleic acids which can incorporate hydrophobicity and other chemistries which are not observed in normal DNA or RNA chemistry aptamers (cubane-modified aptamers). To date, no-one globally has evolved a non-natural nucleic acid in a droplet system. We anticipate that this is an important next stage of this research, and the PI is in discusssions with Professor Anderson Shum to take this research to the next stage with larger scale funding such as via CRF or other international funding schemes. In another route we anticipate using such approaches to select for aptamers for direct diagnostic application. For example, the PI has recently started an ITF grant for diagnosis of COVID-19 using aptamers. Furthermore, in collaboration with Baptist University and CUHK we are developing diagnostic aptamers for early stage pancreatic cancer diagnosis under the 2020 awarded TBRS scheme. There is no doubt that using droplet-based selections to the discovery of diagnostic aptamers will be an important and useful approach for which this grant has provided a critical foundation.

17163416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17163416.value: DNA and RNA are generally thought as being informational molecules providing the code of life. However, they can also directly participate in biological reactions by providing shape for binding and can even be catalysts. It is impossible to design such catalysts made of these molecules from first principles and therefore we need to do evolution in a test tube experiments to discover molecules with such properties. In this grant, the investigators developed a method to select for such molecules in a droplet emulsion system. In this system every droplet has millions of copies of the DNA to be observed, and the droplets can be individually sorted. We developed and used this system to identify DNA molecules which can catalyse chemical reactions. These DNA molecules can now be used to help us understanding the biology of DNA and RNA in the cell, for example allowing us to understand the other molecules they bind to and where they are inside the cell. This may be important for applications such as for diagnostics or for drug delivery. This is an important new tool for molecular biology that expands the function and application of DNA and RNA in new directions.

17164016.value: 滑膜關節(synovial joint)的形成是一個複雜的發育過程， 在骨骼發育中的軟骨模板細胞變化需要十分精確。趾關節的形成是其中一個具研究價值的模型。此外，對有關趾關節遺傳性疾病的研究有幫我們解開當中分子信息的影響。此項目立論建基於我們已發表的短趾症A1型 (BDA1)小鼠模型研究，當中IHH基因突變導致趾關節發育畸形。BDA1患者的中間趾骨比平常人短小甚至消失。我們發現BDA1突變增加IHH蛋白的信息擴散範圍至發育中關節間區 (INTERZONE)而影響趾骨增長。這能夠解釋中間趾骨縮短的成因。然而在某些情況下，中間趾骨缺少的成因我們並是不理解。我們已經知道在BDA1小鼠模型，關節最初有開始發育，但最終趾骨間的空隙並沒有形成，導致關節未能成形。我們認為细胞程序性死亡（細胞凋亡）可能是正常趾骨發育中關節空隙形成前的一個重要過程。細胞凋亡並沒有在中間趾骨缺少的情況出現。我們提出IHH蛋白的水平調控細胞的凋亡，而在BDA1情況下 IHH蛋白的過度擴散至INTERZONE可能抑制細胞凋亡導致BDA1的趾骨表型。眾所周知，IHH信息對細胞的存活十分重要。此項目希望理解它對趾骨關節形成時細胞凋亡的機理。 我們的理論牽涉到與經典膜受體不同的依賴性受體功能。經典受體僅在配體的存在下有生理活性; 如果配體不存在，並無功能。取決於配體的可用性，依賴性受體可具有雙重功能。配體不存在時，這些受體激活細胞凋亡。CDO和GAS1是HH的結合配偶體，介導HH的信號轉導。最近，CDO被證明具有依賴性受體的特點，而GAS1可以誘導細胞凋亡。CDO和GAS1表達於發育中的間區，其中IHH的起始表達水平為低，除着間域的擴大，其水平進一步下降至可以激活依賴性受體的功能，包括誘導細胞凋亡。在BDA1小鼠模型中，IHH的突變改變了其擴散範圍，因此在發育中關節間區保持着較高水平的表達，抑制細胞凋亡的程度，趾骨間的空隙無法形成，導致關節未能成形。此研究旨在利用小鼠來驗證我們的假設，引證IHH與CDO /GAS1功能的新關係，提供正常的關節形成和BDA1發病的機理。因為HH信息跟許多發育過程和疾病的調控有關，包括癌症引發和轉移，我們的實驗成果將會對相關生理學提供資訊。長遠來說，這將有助於骨關節炎和創傷後，制定更好的關節修復及受損軟骨再生的治療策略。

17164016.label: Realisation of objectives
17164016.value: Objective 1: To study the relationship between level of IHH and apoptosis in the developing joint To decipher the potential cellular and molecular changes upstream of the changes, we performed single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) of interzone cells. Using the M/P1 interzone at E14.5, we capture the cellular and molecular changes would reflect key functional outcomes that have provide valuable insights into events leading to failure of joint formation from abnormal Hh signaling to the interzones. Using the 10X Genomics, we capture and sequenced 3,828 and 8,361 cells from the WT and BDA1 samples, respectively. Following data quality assessment and filtering of erroneous cells, we obtained 618 and 1,067 interzone (Gdf5+) cells, and 3,210 and 7,294 non-interzone (Gdf5-) cells from WT and BDA1, respectively. We performed thorough assessment of the data in various cross comparative analyses and identified unique clusters of cells and differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Analysis of DEGs identified cellular differences in the interzones between WT and BDA1 mice with GO (gene-ontology) term enrichment for cell-death or apoptosis related activities, consistent with our hypothesis. Further, we performed additional DEG comparison between IZ and NIZ cells for each sample (WT or BDA1), with especial focus on the genes that are higher in the interzone and/or in the mutants, and identified only two genes, Gli3 and Cdon to be relevant. Both are related to Hh signaling, and we have shown that CDON is normally expressed strongly in the developing interzone that is elevated in the expanded phalangeal interzones in BDA1 mice. Next, we established the role of apoptosis in phalangeal joint formation clearly identified TUNEL positive apoptotic cells in the developing WT joints, just prior to (E13.5), during (E14.5), and just after (E15.5), and at completion (E16.5) of cavitation, that were significantly reduced corresponding joints in BDA1 mice. We showed the necessity of cell death in cavitation by chemical inhibition of cell death using zVAD-FMK, a pan caspase inhibitor that correlated with failure of joint cavitation analogous to BDA1, and conversely, activating cell death in mice genetically that renders interzone cells sensitive to diphtheria toxin rescued the BDA1 lost-of-a-joint phenotype. From these, we concluded that a precisely regulated/balanced level of cell death is critical in the fine tuning of phalangeal joint cavitation. Objective 2: To assess the role of CDO and/or GAS1 in the pathogenesis of BDA1 Reduction of cell death and the prominent increase in Cdon expressing cells prompt us to place an emphasis on CDON instead of GAS1. This is also impacted by the reduced funding and shortened period from 3 to 2 years. Our focused investigation of the Cdon function was indeed productive, and we systematically demonstrate a strong relationship between expression of Cdon in the developing interzone and cell death, as we hypothesized it can function as a dependence receptor. Whereby, in the presence of ligand, CDON assists in Hh signaling, but ligand-free CDON can induce cell death. We generated various genetic crossed and investigate the impact of reducing Cdon expression in BDA1het and BDA1 mice to address its relationship to apoptosis and joint formation. We showed that at E16.5 and stage matched E17.5 BDA1, a P2/P3 interzone can be detected in all genotype albeit the abnormal fusing P2/P3 phenotype is observed in both BDA1het/Cdon+/- and BDA1, indicating reducing Cdon is not critical for initiation of interzone formation to this developmental stage. However, level of apoptotic cells , while we see no significant differences in the M/P1 interzone between WT, Cdon+/- and Cdon-/-mice, the levels of apoptotic cells are markedly reduced in all genotypes with E95K alleles, that become more drastic in the more distal P1/P2 and P2/P3 interzones; in particular, when the levels of Cdon expression is reduced or inactivated completely. Thus, there is a direct relationship between the expression of Cdon and apoptosis in BDA1het or BDA1 mice, perpetuated by the excessive level of IHH in the developing interzone. Consistent with our hypothesis that the P2/P3 interzone failed to progress in digit V of BDA1 mice, the progression of this joint in BDA1het/Cdon+/- also failed by P0, and the P2/P3 interzone is no longer detectable, whereas this joint is well formed in BDA1het mice. The fact that this also correlated with further reduction in cell death is indicative of a link between Cdon expression and thus level of CDON to cell death. To explain this, we propose a model whereby for a joint that has been initiated and progressive to cavitation, it requires a permissive environment, where a low level of IHH reaches the most inner region of the interzone, but with higher concentrations of interacting partners (PTCH, CDON, GAS1), and thus sufficient unbound partners (CDON and GAS1) functioning as dependence receptor, to induce cell death and cavitation proceeds in this permissive interzone as in WT mice. Our findings are novel and we have not only provide an extensive analysis of the molecular pathogenesis of BDA1, but provide conceptual relationship between HH and partners in the regulation of cell death in vivo. We have completed the draft of a manuscript ready for submission with the aim to try top tier journals in the first instance.

17164016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17164016.value: Mutations in the Indian hedgehog (IHH) results in brachydactyly type A1 (BDA1), with unique digit abnormalities of shortened and/or missing middle phalangeal bones. Previously, we provided molecular and cellular insight into the consequence of the mutations that alter the capacity and range of IHH signaling into the developing joint. This disrupts distal IHH and BMP signals at the digit tip, and recruitment of mesenchymal cells into the condensing cartilage anlagen is reduced leading to a shorter middle phalange when the last joint is formed. However, the reason for a missing middle phalange has not be resolved. Here, we showed it is the result of impaired progression of the developing joint (interzone) that did not undergo cavitation in a mouse model for BDA1 with a E95K mutation in the Ihh gene, and a joint is not form, thus the middle phalange is deem absence. Importantly, we demonstrated that cell death is needed to initiate the cavitation progress in this context and is related to a balanced levels of the ligand (IHH) with its interacting partners (PTCH, CDON, GAS1) in the interzone. We postulate the existence of permissive and non-permissive environment for interzone cavitation whereby CDON and/or GAS1 function as dependency receptors in normal joint development, where IHH level is low and the ligand-free CDON and/or GAS1 activate cell death and permissive for cavitation. In BDA1 joint, the dependence receptor function of CDON/GAS1 cannot function because of excess IHH and a joint is not formed in this non-permissive environment. Indeed, genetic ablation of Cdon influences the outcome of the BDA1 phenotype consistent with dependency receptor relationship. Our findings provided new insights into the relationship between IHH and CDON in joint formation and the pathogenesis of BDA1, with relevance to IHH signaling in general biology.

17164016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17164016.value: While the exact mechanism by which CDON regulates cell death in the interzone is not yet clear. The fact that Cdon null mice do not have exhibit abnormal joint development suggest the presence of a redundant mechanism that may involve GAS1, as Gas1 null mice exhibited BDA1-like characteristics This is intriguing and given that we have generated the conditional mouse for the activation of Gas1, we could directly test the relationship to cell death in Cdon+/+, Cdon+/- and Cdon-/- genotypes. Given that GAS1 is GPI-anchored membrane protein and do not have an intracellular “death activating” domain, its dependence receptor functionality would require a partner. Thus, it is possible that GAS1 partners with CDON in its presence for dependence receptor activity, and this is reduced in BDA1het/Cdon+/- mice. But in a complete absence of CDON, GAS1 has an alternative partner for dependence receptor activity facilitating cell death. Conceptually, it would be relevant to further delineate the partnership of dependence receptors in the developing joint that will provide further insights to the mechanism by which the cell death event is regulated, as the downstream pathways transduce by the unbound receptors are largely unknown.

17164016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17164016.value: In this project, we investigated the pathology of disease in humans called brachydactyly type A1 where the affected individuals have very short figure and one of their finger joint is missing. This is caused by mutations in a gene known as Indian Hedgehog (IHH). Because this gene is a morphogen, a molecules that can bind to a receptor on a cells to activate an event in the cells, the mutation changes its ability to bind and their reduce their signalling capacity and range. Also, as it is a defect during developmental, we created a mouse model for the diseases that show all the human defects. From analyses of these mice, we provided a new information on how IHH may affect joint formation, and in particular, how this morphogen can also regulation cell death when it interact with other partners. We showed cell death is necessary in finger joint formation. This relationship has not been shown before, making our discovery novel Importantly, because this morphogen is also related to many other cellular events in diseases such as cancer, and if we can use our understanding to direct cell death in cancer cells, this would be very exciting indeed in the treatment of cancer, highlighting how different studies of diseases can be inter-connected.

17164116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17164116.value: 早期軟骨發育是軟骨發育過程中關鍵的階段。兩種細胞相互作用: 細胞和細胞, 細胞和基質相互作用激活軟骨形成。間質基質豐富的I型膠原和纖維連接蛋白是在這一階段切換到富含軟骨基質II型膠原和蛋白聚醣，並作為間充質細胞向成軟骨細胞系分化佔主導地位。敲除膠原蛋白或纖連蛋白時，軟骨形成是有缺陷的，這表明間充質基質的重要意義。 體外模型模擬-軟骨預充質縮合已被廣泛用來研究軟骨形成過程。這些模型包括自發的或力驅動的間質細胞的移動和聚集。然而，大多數模型不包括無細胞外基質。因此，細胞和細胞相互作用, 結合細胞和基質相互作用，應是一個更好的早期軟骨發育的體外模型。 微膠囊化是一個製造支架的過程，用以在生物材料內包封活細胞。常用的材料包括例如像聚乙二醇的合成材料，和例如像海藻酸鈉的天然材料。然而，大多數細胞在這些材料中不表達特定的基質相互作用分子，如整合素，因此不能更好地模仿在軟骨發育過程中的細胞和基質的相互作用細胞。 我們建立了一個膠原蛋白微囊化的平台，用以重組I型膠原納米纖維從而為細胞製造支架。間質幹細胞膠原蛋白微球已被用來作為三維細胞培養，細胞遞送的微載體，和作為組織工程的構建塊。包封期間，幹細胞朝向結構中心遷移，產生牽引力收縮膠原蛋白，大幅收縮微球體積和局部增強細胞密度。幹細胞能夠在微球內存活，增殖，遷移，分化和表現出生理相關的細胞基質相互作用。 這些現象提示我們推測，間充質幹細胞膠原微囊化代表早期軟骨發育階段。這對準備間充質幹細胞軟骨化起了非常關鍵的作用。 我們的目標是調查（1）膠原蛋白微囊化是否重演早期軟骨發育; （2）膠原蛋白微膠囊化是否激活細胞外基質驅動的信號轉導途徑; 及（3）是否在膠原微囊化過程中調節細胞外基質細胞外基質組合能夠激活相關的信號轉導途徑，並促進軟骨化過程。 這個項目的短期影響是（1）成功發展細胞外基質驅動的體外模型來研究軟骨的形成;和（2）合理化在間充質幹細胞軟骨化過程中製造支架的策略。從長遠來看，該項目有利於開發創新的軟骨療法。
