17214516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17214516.value: 骨創傷和骨相關疾病如骨質疏鬆症會引起大段骨缺損。手術治療是日常處理的手段，但在骨骼再生上依然是一大挑戰 。目前採用自體骨植入是最普遍的方法， 然而，其供應量有限，而且供區也有機會出現術後感染和出血的風險。因此，異體骨移植提供了另一個選擇，但其骨傳導性相對較差，導致術後骨延遲癒合 。因此，生物活性因子如骨形態發生蛋白-2（BMP-2）、甲狀旁腺激素（PTH）、和富含血小板的血漿（PRP）都分別被研究，用來提高異體移植骨癒合。由於這些生物分子的成本很高，如考慮作為常規應用，必然加重治療成本。 在我們團隊的研究中，我們發現特定濃度的鎂離子對於成骨細胞和人類間質幹細胞的成骨標記物如ALP、 COL1A1、OPN）和Runx2可以有效地提高 。此外，當特定濃度的鎂離子注入正常和骨質疏鬆的大鼠中， 新骨形成的效果顯然而見。因此，我們通過使用等離子體浸沒離子注入與沉積（PIII＆D）的技術，把定量的鎂離子注入異體骨，期望異體骨因表面的鎂離子濃度增加，可以有效地促進手術後原位骨癒合。

17214516.label: Realisation of objectives
17214516.value: 1. To fabricate magnesium-enriched bovine and rat allogenic bone allografts by applying optimized plasma treatment parameters, and to systematically study mechanical and in vitro biological properties as compared with untreated controls The 1st objective has been fully achieved in this research. The preparation of magnesium-enriched allogenic bone graft involved a two-step treatment (i.e., plasma immersion ion implantation (PIII) and plasma deposition (PD)). We had separately investigated how the acceleration voltage and implantation time of PIII altered magnesium content on bone graft surface. The magnesium contents were only slightly increased while prolonging the acceleration voltage and implantation time. The prolonged acceleration voltage and implantation time would reduce the quality of the decellularized bone matrix, especially the micro-structure of collagen fibers. However, the osteogenic properties of those magnesium PIII or PD bone grafts were significantly upregulated as compared with the control. In summary, the samples treated with twenty kilovoltage and 1-hour implantation time PIII presented with superior osteogenic up-regulation when they were cultured with the cells in vitro 2. To further characterize detailed surface properties of the plasma-treated allogenic bone, such as chemical composition change and magnesium compounds distribution in bone matrix, as compared with untreated controls; and, The 2nd objective has been fully executed as well. The surface chemical composition of the Mg-treated bone allografts was confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The elemental depth profiles of untreated and Mg-treated bone grafts were also obtained via an XPS sputtering technique. Apart from XPS, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) was also utilized to detect the magnesium content and distribution on the Mg-treated samples and the control. Furthermore, the interfacial and spatiotemporal magnesium distribution of the magnesium-treated and controls samples were consequently assayed by scanning ion-selective electrode technique (SIET) and inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES), respectively. With these results, we are able to identify how Mg ions distribute in the tissue microenvironment of bone graft when the graft is treated with different PIII and PD techniques. 3. To comprehensively study the in vivo biological response of optimized Mg-enriched allogenic bone grafts by using established rat models with large bone defect. The quantity and quality of newly formed bone, as well as their biomechanical properties, will be analyzed and compared to untreated controls. Results obtained may pave the way for future substantial animal studies and human clinical trials. A rodent model with large bone defect, which replicates the clinical scenario, was selected to investigate the osseointegration of the optimized Mg-enriched allogenic bone grafts as compared to the untreated and Mg-treated controls. The quantity of the newly formed bone was characterized by using micro-computed tomography, whereas the quality of new bone was examined by histological and immunochemical analyses. Additionally, the mechanical properties were also determined by using nano-indentation approach. Therefore, the Young’s modulus of the newly formed bone could be obtained and compared with others. Lastly, the magnesium distribution within the bone defect and subsequent bone formation were also comprehensively analyzed by molecular biology approach.

17214516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17214516.value: In this GRF project, we have successfully established a Mg-enriched interfacial microenvironment on the surface of bone allograft using a customized magnesium-plasma treatment. This specifically treated bone allograft was able to maintain a fine-tuned interfacial microenvironment over a period of time. This Mg-enriched interfacial bone microenvironment was able to facilitate in vitro cell adhesion, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation, as well as new bone formation and osseointegration of the allograft to host bone. These superior features were likely initiated by the upregulation of integrin α3 and α5 receptors of mesenchymal stem cells. Lastly, this study identifies a robust approach that can effectively enhance the bioactivity of an allograft bone and its subsequent osseointegration to a host bone without the aids of biological growth factors or stem cell therapy. These results have been summarized and submitted to a journal, namely Bioactive Materials (real-time impact factor =14.01) and it is now under 1st revision. The details can be seen in the “Research Output (No. 13)”. In addition to the invited talks in several international conferences, the PI and his team have also published 12 SCI journal papers and 1 U.S. patent granted. Besides, a review paper published in Bioactive Materials journal, namely Bone Grafts and Biomaterials Substitutes for Bone Defect Repair: A review, has become a highly-cited paper in the journal and also listed as the top 1% ESI Highly Cited Paper.

17214516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17214516.value: In addition to the large bone defect in long bone, we are confident that our findings can also apply to other bone defect models, e.g., mandible bone defect and cranial bone defect. Prior to the application, we have to identify the pathway of bone formation induced by Mg-enriched bone graft that may help address the problem of potential carcinogenicity. In addition, a comprehensive evaluation with the use of large animal model is needed before we apply for human clinical trials. Also, our approach should benchmark with the commercially available products such as the bone graft embedded with bone morphogenetic protein 2 or beta-tricalcium phosphate granules for head-to-head comparison. If successful, we may commercialize the Mg-enriched bone graft together with relevant industrial partners in the future.

17214516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17214516.value: Trauma patients paralyzed by large segmental bone defects are mainly managed by applying a variety of bone substitutes and instrumentation, in which bone autografts and allografts are the major substitutes clinically used today. Bone autograft is the mainstream application due to its excellent osteoinductivity and osteoconductivity. However, donor site morbidity and limited tissue availability are major concerns. Allografts have since become an alternative, but its insufficient ability to induce bone healing has resulted in bone non-union and even bone graft fracture. Our team proposes to modify the bone regeneration ability of allografts by implanting magnesium ions to the bone matrix with the use of plasma surface technique. Our findings demonstrated that specific amount of magnesium ions could significantly enhance the proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells, and augment new bone formation in animal models. With these positive results, we expect that our magnesium-enriched bone allograft can benefit patients with large segmental bone defect, as well as those with osteoporotic fractures and bone tumors requiring bone augmentation procedures in future clinical applications.

17217716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17217716.value: This project will investigate new variants of several classical optimization problems that are central to theoretical computer science. In the famous traveling salesman problem (TSP), the points in the metric space represent the cities to be visited, and the goal is to find a shortest tour that visits all required cities and returns to the starting point. In the steiner tree problem, the terminal set is a subset of points that represent cities to be connected, and the goal is to build roads with minimum cost to connect all required cities, possibly using extra cities as intermediate hubs. It is known that for general metric spaces, these problems are NP-hard to approximate with a ratio better than some constant strictly larger than 1. Researchers have shown that for low-dimensional Euclidean metrics, these problems have polynomial time approximation schemes (PTAS’s) that have approximation ratios arbitrarily close to 1. Instead of using the geometric properties of the Euclidean dimension for algorithm design, there has been a long line of research that exploits the combinatorial properties of the underlying metric space via the doubling dimension. A STOC 2012 breakthrough paper achieves a PTAS for the TSP on doubling metrics. We will consider more challenging variants of these problems. For the group version of a problem, the input consists of a collection of subsets of a metric space. In the group TSP, the goal is to find a shortest tour that visits at least one point from each subset. This project has preliminary results in an upcoming SODA 2016 paper, which achieves a PTAS for the group TSP on doubling metrics. This provides new insights and powerful techniques to tackle the following problems that have applications in logistics and dynamic network design. (1) Variants of the group TSP. In the group prize collecting TSP, each unvisited subset incurs a certain penalty, and the goal is to minimize the length of the tour plus the penalties due to unvisited subsets. (2) Group connectivity problems. In the group steiner forest problem, the input consists of a collection of pairs of subsets, and the goal is to return a forest with minimum cost such that each pair of subsets are connected. (3) Fully dynamic setting. For instance, the input is updated by inserting a new subset or deleting an existing subset. The goal is to update the solution efficiently instead of recomputing from scratch. 此專案將探究幾個理論電腦科學研究中核心經典問題的新變種。在著名的旅行商問題中，度量空間中的點可看作一些需要被訪問的城市，而問題的目標是找到一條最短的、訪問所有城市至少一次並回到出發點的路。在斯坦納樹問題中，終端點集合是一個需要被連接的城市的集合，而我們的目標是在允許使用其他不在終端點集的中間點的情況下，修建最小長度的路來連通所有的城市。現在已知上述問題在一般度量空間下即使達到某個比1大的常數近似比都是NP完全的。已有研究表明，這些問題在低維歐氏空間中可以在多項式時間內被近似到任意接近於1的相對誤差，亦即存在多項式時間近似方案。不同於利用歐氏空間的幾何性質來設計演算法，很多研究者利用加倍維度來研究度量空間中的組合性質。在2012年，一篇突破性的STOC會議論文給出了一個旅行商問題在加倍空間下的多項式時間近似方案。我們將考慮這些問題更具挑戰性的變種。 在一個組版本的優化問題中，輸入將含有若干度量空間點集的子集。在組旅行商問題中，目標變為尋找一條最短的經過每個子集中至少一個點的回路。我們在該專案的一個前期成果中得到了對於組旅行商問題的多項式時間近似方案，並發表在SODA 2016會議上。該成果為下述在運輸領域以及動態網路設計領域中有重要應用的問題，給出了深刻的洞悉並且提供了有效的技術。 （1） 組旅行商問題的變種。在組獎金收集旅行商問題中，每個未被訪問的子集會產生一定的懲罰。該問題的目標是最小化路徑長度與懲罰的加和。 （2） 組連通性問題。在組斯坦納森林問題中，輸入將包含若干度量空間點集的子集對。該問題的目標變為尋找一個最小代價的連通所有子集對的森林。 （3） 完全動態化的問題設定。比如，輸入可以要求演算法動態維護插入或者刪除一個子集後的解。這類問題的研究目標是有效地更新解，並避免重新計算。

17217716.label: Realisation of objectives
17217716.value: Objective 1 To realize the first objective, we have considered the Traveling Salesman Problem with Neighborhoods (TSPN) in doubling metrics. The goal is to find the shortest tour that visits each of a given collection of subsets (regions or neighborhoods) in the underlying metric space. We have given a randomized polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) when the regions are fat weakly disjoint. We combined the techniques in the well-known Arora framework, together with the recent PTAS for TSP [STOC 2012: Bartal, Gottlieb, and Krauthgamer 2012] to achieve a PTAS for TSPN. In particular, the following approaches have laid down the technical foundation for this project: (1) Heuristic to detect sparse instances. In the STOC 2012 paper, a minimum spanning tree heuristic is used to estimate the portion of an optimal tour within some ball. We have adapted this for TSPN, in which the challenge is that it is not known if an optimal tour would use points inside the ball to visit regions that intersect the ball. (2) Partially cut regions in the recursion. After a sparse ball is identified by the heuristic, the PTAS framework for TSP uses dynamic programming to solve the instance restricted to the sparse ball and recurse on the remaining instance. For TSPN, it is an important issue to decide whether each region partially intersecting the sparse ball should be solved in the sparse instance or considered in the remaining instance. We have shown that both issues can be resolved by conservatively making the ball in question responsible for all intersecting regions, and we have developed a sophisticated charging argument to bound the cost of combining tours in the recursion. The result is that we have improved the running time’s dependence on the doubling dimension, which has appeared in TALG 2018. The above techniques have allowed us to design a PTAS for the prize collecting traveling salesman problem as well. The cost is the length of the tour plus the penalty due to uncovered points. We have augmented the standard the dynamic program which employs divide-and-conquer strategies and sparse instance decompositions, and the result has been published in ESA 2018. Objective 2 To realize the objective of applying our techniques to connectivity problems, we have achieved a randomized PTAS for the Steiner forest problem in doubling metrics. Before our work, a PTAS was given only for the Euclidean plane in [FOCS 2008: Borradaile, Klein, Mathieu]. We have extended the techniques developed in Objective 1 to connectivity problems in the following ways: (1) We have proved a technical lemma showing that Steiner points have to be ``near"" the terminals in an optimal Steiner tree. This enables us to define a heuristic to estimate the local behavior of the optimal solution, even though the Steiner points are unknown in advance. (2) We have developed a novel algorithmic technique known as ``adaptive cells"" to overcome the difficulty of keeping track of multiple components in a solution. Our idea is based on but significantly different from the previously proposed “uniform cells” in the FOCS 2008 paper, whose techniques cannot be readily applied to doubling metrics. Our results have appeared in FOCS 2016 and SICOMP 2018. The approaches that we used for the prize collecting TSP in Objective 1 have also inspired solutions for the connectivity counterpart. Indeed, we have developed a unified framework for designing PTAS’s that can be applied to both TSP and Steiner tree variants of the prize collecting problem in doubling metrics. Given a metric space and a penalty function on a subset of points known as terminals, a solution is a subgraph on points in the metric space whose cost is the weight of its edges plus the penalty due to terminals not covered by the subgraph. Under our unified framework, the solution subgraph needs to be Eulerian for TSP, while it needs to be a tree for Steiner tree. However, since it is unknown which part of the optimal cost is due to edge lengths and which part is due to penalties of uncovered terminals, we have developed new techniques to apply previous divide-and-conquer strategies and sparse instance decompositions. Specifically, we have revisited the sparsity structural lemma in the literature for TSP-like problems. Intuitively, it says that if a solution is sparse, then there exists a structurally light approximate solution. We have given this lemma a more formal treatment and the result has appeared in TALG 2020. Objective 3 In order to employ our techniques to the fully dynamic settings in Objective 3, we first design algorithms for finding dense regions in the input evolving graph. Tatti and Gionis [WWW 2015] presented a novel graph decomposition (known as the locally-dense decomposition) that is similar to the well-known k-core decomposition, with the additional property that its components are arranged in order of their densities. We have devised an efficient algorithm which is able to compute exact locally-dense decompositions based on the classic Frank-Wolfe algorithm, which is similar to gradient descent and can be efficiently implemented. Efficiency is important as the input graph can be rapidly evolving. We have provided a rigorous study of our algorithms and their convergence rates. Our results have appeared in WWW 2017. Since our PTASs are based on identifying instances with critical densities, we have studied the problem of maintaining densest subsets in fully dynamic graphs. The goal of the problem is to find a subset of nodes that induces a graph with maximum average degree. We have considered hypergraphs, which generalizes the problem to a wider class of networks in which edges might have different cardinalities and contain more than 2 nodes. We have developed both exact algorithms and a near-linear time r-approximation algorithm for the problem, where r is the maximum cardinality of an edge in the hypergraph. In the dynamic setting, an adversary can insert or delete an edge from the hypergraph in each round and the goal is to maintain efficiently an approximation of the densest subgraph. Our dynamic approximation algorithms have amortized polylogarithmic update times. Extensive experiments have been performed on large real datasets to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithms. The results have appeared in CIKM 2017. We have further investigated fully dynamic approximation algorithms in the context of clustering, which provides a fundamental tool for decomposing a metric space. In particular, the net decomposition technique for doubling metrics can be achieved by a k-center algorithm. We have designed an approximation algorithm for the k-center clustering problem with small amortized cost under the fully dynamic adversarial model. Our results have appeared in WWW 2018. Finally, we have also designed algorithms to maintain approximate core values in dynamic hypergraphs. The results are published in TKDD 2020.

17217716.label: Major findings and research outcome
17217716.value: For Objective 1, we have designed a PTAS for the Traveling Salesman Problem with Neighborhoods (TSPN) in doubling metrics. Based on the well-known Arora divide-and-conquer framework, we have developed a sophisticated charging argument to analyse the cost of recursion. We have improved the running time’s dependence on the doubling dimension and the results have appeared in TALG 2018. The techniques have also allowed us to design a PTAS for the prize collecting traveling salesman problem as well. In particular, we have extended the divide-and-conquer strategy by sparse instance decompositions, and the result has been published in ESA 2018. For Objective 2, we have achieved a randomized PTAS for the Steiner forest problem in doubling metrics. In particular, we have defined a heuristic to estimate the local behavior of the optimal solution, even though the Steiner points are unknown in advance. Moreover, we have developed a novel algorithmic technique known as ``adaptive cells"" to overcome the difficulty of keeping track of multiple components in a solution. Our results have appeared in FOCS 2016 and SICOMP 2018. Furthermore, we have developed a unified framework for designing PTAS’s that can be applied to both TSP and Steiner tree variants of the prize collecting problem in doubling metrics. The key technique is a sparsity structural lemma that states that if a solution is sparse, then there exists a structurally light approximate solution. The result has appeared in TALG 2020. For Objective 3, we have designed algorithms for finding dense regions in an input graph. Specifically, we have devised an efficient algorithm which is able to compute exact locally-dense decompositions based on the classic Frank-Wolfe algorithm, which is similar to gradient descent and can be efficiently implemented. The results have appeared in WWW 2017. We have also studied the problem of maintaining densest subsets in fully dynamic hypergraphs. We have designed both exact and approximate algorithms with amortized polylogarithmic update times. Extensive experiments have been performed to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithms. The results have appeared in CIKM 2017. Finally, under the fully dynamic settings, we have achieved an approximate algorithm for the k-center problem in WWW 2018 and an algorithm to maintain approximate core values in TKDD 2020, where the update time is poly-logarithmic.

17217716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17217716.value: In this project, we have developed algorithms for various variants of TSP and connectivity problems in doubling metrics. One important insight is that these algorithms identify sparse regions in the input instance. Future research directions can investigate other notions of sparsity or density, which can facilitate decompositions with desirable properties that are pertinent to more general problems. In the fully dynamic settings, the input to the problem changes as time progresses and the algorithms developed in this project have fast poly-logarithmic time, but use polynomial amount of memory. Further research can consider the streaming setting in which the algorithm only has (sub-) linear memory. A major focus of this project is on metric spaces which capture a binary relationship between nodes in the input. Towards the end of the project, we have considered hypergraphs that can capture higher-order relationships between different entities. We have started to consider hypergraph decompositions which will offer a useful tool to design divide-and-conquer and recursive algorithms for future research. An interesting challenge is to achieve practical algorithms whose performances scale desirably as the sizes of the hyperedges increase.

17217716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17217716.value: In this project, we have developed mathematical tools utilizing recent technical breakthroughs regarding metric space dimension, and designed algorithms for several variants of the traveling salesman problem (TSP) and connectivity problems, which have influence on the wider computer science community in general. A highlight of our results is a unified framework that captures the prize collecting variants of both TSP and the Steiner tree problem. We have also considered the more realistic fully dynamic settings in which the input changes as time progresses. We have shown that for several decomposition and clustering problems, it is possible to update the solution quickly without recomputing from scratch. We have designed dynamic data structures that can achieve theoretical tradeoffs between the approximation ratio and the update time, which have been verified by experiments on real-world data. We believe that this project has developed new techniques in combinatorial optimization and approximation algorithm design, which will have significant impacts on both theoretical and application-driven research.

17218916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17218916.value: Road pricing has been proposed and tested as a method of tackling road congestion. The main aim is to charge the right toll in the right location at the right time to discourage driving. The toll revenue collected is considered part of social surplus because it is redistributed in full to society. This revenue can be used to improve public-transit operations, as in London, or to subsidize passengers’ fares. In both cases, traveling by public transit becomes more attractive than driving and the public-transit system becomes more cost-effective due to greater demand. A classical static modeling approach can be used to analyze and quantify the benefits of the above strategies. However, this approach takes into account neither the temporal characteristics of the problem, such as variation in daily demand and demand changes over longer periods (e.g., years) in modeling horizon, departure-time choice, and schedule delay, nor the interaction of different types of vehicles across time and space. Therefore, the classical approach does not enable researchers to accurately estimate the benefits to travelers in each reference period, or to determine whether and how these benefits differ between reference periods. The analysis is even more complicated if transit operators are private companies that seek to maximize their own profit, as in Hong Kong. Maximizing profit and maximizing social-surplus do not always lead to the same outcomes, keen competition may arise between operators, and operators may receive a considerable amount of toll revenue from the government, raising political concerns. The proposed project will develop a novel dynamic traffic assignment modeling framework and a methodology to determine time-dependent road tolls, transit frequency, and fares. Variation in traffic flow both within a reference period and over successive similar reference periods (i.e., doubly dynamics) will be modeled. The framework will take into account multiple user classes differentiated by the value of time along with the abovementioned considerations and complications. The properties of the resulting models, various tolling and redistribution strategies under different transit-market regimes, and the effects of regulating fares and frequencies in markets with private transit operators on total discounted social surplus and various equity measures will be analyzed. The models, methodology, and results of the analysis will help the government to mitigate congestion, regulate the transit market, and increase the attractiveness of the transit system. 道路收費已經成為解決道路擁堵問題的一種方法，其主要目的在於在合適的時間，合適的地點收取恰當的費用來抑制交通需求。道路收費所得被視為社會剩餘的一部分，因為這一款項又全部重新分配給了社會。比如在倫敦，道路收費所得收益被用來改善公共交通設運作，或者去補貼乘客的票價。在這兩種情形下，相比自駕，公共交通出行顯得更加有吸引力；與此同時，因為更大的需求量，公共交通系統變得更加有效。 以上策略的分析和出行者收益可以用經典靜態模型的方法來實現。然而，這種方法既沒有考慮問題的時間特性，例如每天和長期階段（比如以年為記）內的需求變化；也沒有考慮在時空層面上不同種類車輛的相互作用。因此，經典方法不能讓研究者準確估計在每個研究時間段內出行者的收益，或者去確定在這些研究時間段內收益是否變化並且會怎樣變化。如果公共交通運營方是私人企業，比如在香港，而他們往往尋求最大商業利益，在這樣的情況下，分析將會變得更加複雜。最大化利益和最大化社會剩餘並不總是能殊途同歸；公共交通運營方之間會劇烈競爭，並且他們會從政府方得到一筆可觀的道路收費收益，這又會帶來政治利害關係。 所提議的項目會建立起一個全新的動態交通分配模型體系和一套完整的方法論，以此來確定基於時間的道路收費，公共交通發車頻率和票價。在研究所選單位時間段內以及在連續的多個類似時間段內（即雙動態）的交通流將會被建模。在如上所述的因素和複雜情況下，這個體系將同時考慮不同時間價值的多種用戶類型。同時，我們還會對模型的屬性，在不同公共交通市場架構下的不同道路收費和再分配策略進行研究；在私人交通運營方的市場中，調節收費和發車頻率對貼現的社會剩餘和各方權益的影響也將得到分析和評估。 這些模型，方法論和分析結果將會為政府緩解交通擁堵，調節公共交通市場和提升公共交通吸引力提供有力的支撐。

17218916.label: Realisation of objectives
17218916.value: The ultimate objective of this project is to develop a doubly dynamic modeling framework to determine road tolls, public-transit frequency, and/or fares. As mentioned in the proposal, to gain a better understanding of road pricing and subsidy strategies in various market contexts, and to aid analysis of model properties (especially model convergence and stability), simpler models, e.g., day-to-day dynamic models, were developed in the earlier phases and extended to produce more complicated versions in the later phases. Variation in traffic flow both within a reference period (i.e., within-day dynamics) and over successive similar reference periods (i.e., day-to-day dynamics or period-to-period dynamics) were modeled eventually. To achieve the stated specific objectives, 4 submodels [J1]-[J4] and one doubly dynamic model [J5] were developed and the corresponding solution methodologies were proposed. The properties of a full model also include the properties of the submodels. Therefore, most of the focuses were on analyzing the properties of the submodels [J1]-[J4], but [J5] also reported some properties of the doubly dynamic model that cannot be found in the previous submodels. The framework in [J5] is flexible and can be further enhanced to capture all modeling details in [J1]-[J4] if time and budget permit. The time for reviewing four out of the five aforementioned journal papers was quite long and the review processes for these papers sometimes required our research team to make 3 to 4 revisions. Moreover, the provided budget is also much less than the requested budget but the PI did not cut the content of the project. Still, our research team could achieve the main objectives as explained as follows. To achieve objective 1, a doubly dynamic model and an adaptive pricing strategy were developed [J5]. This study [J5] estimates and manages the stochastic traffic dynamics in a bi-modal transportation system, and gives hints on how increasing data availability in transport and cities can be utilized to estimate transport supply functions and manage transport demand simultaneously. In the bi-modal system, travelers’ mode choices are based on their perceptions of the two travel modes: driving or public transit. Some travelers who have access to real-time road (car) traffic information may shift their mode based on the information received. For the roadway network, the within-day traffic evolution is modeled through a Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram (MFD), where the flow dynamics exhibit a certain level of uncertainty. A non-parametric approach is proposed to estimate the MFD. To improve traffic efficiency, our research team develops an adaptive pricing mechanism coupled with the learned MFD. The adaptive pricing extends the study of Liu and Geroliminis (2017) to the time-dependent case, which can better accommodate temporal demand variations and achieve higher efficiency. The study has several key features. Firstly, the network-level stochastic within-day traffic dynamics are embedded into the day-to-day framework to develop a stochastic doubly dynamical system. Secondly, time-dependent traffic conditions and information provision are incorporated in the travelers’ decision process, where both travelers with and without information are modeled. Thirdly, a learning mechanism for the MFD of the network is developed, which can take advantage of the day-to-day traffic observations. Fourthly, the learned MFD is coupled with an adaptive and time-dependent pricing strategy. The learning and managing framework holds the potential to adaptively enhance network performance. To achieve objective 2, the properties of the doubly dynamic model [J5] and submodels [J1]-[J4] were analyzed and illustrated. To achieve objective 3, our research team considered social cost/surplus [J4], different market regimes (such as the bimodal market in which the government acts as a public-transit operator [J1] and bimodal markets with single or two private transit operators [J3]-[J4]), adaptive tolling under both within-day and day-to-day dynamics [J5], and tolling and redistribution strategies [J1]. [J1] particularly considered two tolling and redistribution strategies, namely Pareto improvement and zero-sum revenue. The Pareto improvement refers to that the net travel cost of each commuter is reduced under the implementation of the control scheme, compared with the initial state, i.e., each commuter becomes better off. The zero-sum revenue means that, on each day, some commuters are charged; at the same time, some commuters are subsidized so that the total revenue of the transportation authority from tolls and subsidies is zero. To achieve objective 4, private transit operators in monopoly [J4] and duopoly markets [J3] were considered.

17218916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17218916.value: The research outcomes (in forms of the modeling framework, submodels, solution methodologies, and properties of studied models) and major findings were published in five journal papers [J1]-[J5] and were presented at an international conference [C1]. 4 papers were published in the prestigious international journal in the field of transportation, namely Transportation Research Part B. The following summarizes the major findings. [J1] shows that a “static” Pareto-improvement toll/subsidy scheme can be ineffective for achieving Pareto improvement when it is implemented in the day-to-day adjustment process of traffic flow. It is necessary to implement a dynamic version. Moreover, [J1] shows that although commuters have different perceived travel costs for using the same travel mode, the authority need not know the probability distribution of perceived travel costs of commuters to achieve the Pareto improvement target. [J1] also shows that under zero-sum revenue schemes, we cannot guarantee that a Pareto-improvement target is realized at the stationary state. [J3] shows that for the transit monopoly, (i) the operator can choose to operate one of its transit lines to maximize its profit, and hence it is essential to examine the optimal solution at the boundary of the feasible set of network user (flow) distribution; (ii) to make the profit of the transit operator more than a certain value, the government can improve the toll charge to private car users. For the transit Bertrand-Nash duopoly, (i) under the implementation of the operational scheme, the trajectory of flow distributions can evolve to either a stationary point located at the boundary or in the interior of the feasible set of flow distributions; (ii) when both transit operators are willing to set a small initial transit fare, the trajectory of flow distributions evolves to a stationary point in the interior of the feasible set, and the profits of both transit operators are not globally optimal at the interior stationary point. [J4] indicates that it is unnecessary to know the function of in-vehicle congestion costs and the distribution of perceived travel cost errors to optimize the system time cost or operating profit of a multi-modal transport system. However, to optimize the social/system cost of the transport system, the distribution of perceived travel cost errors must be known. [J5] demonstrates that when supply uncertainty is smaller, the total percentage error of flow and cost can approach smaller values with a faster speed. When information service penetration is larger, the system approaches more similar states faster.

17218916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17218916.value: The proposed framework in [J5] does not consider route choice, departure time choice, the direct interaction between public and private transport, and multiple types of information service provision. In addition to the modeling details in [J1]-[J4], the framework can be extended to consider them in the future to improve the realism.

17218916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17218916.value: Road pricing has been proposed as a method of tackling road congestion. This revenue collected can be used to improve public-transit operations, as in London, or to subsidize passengers’ fares. In both cases, traveling by public transit becomes more attractive than driving and the public-transit system becomes more cost-effective. A classical static modeling approach does not consider the temporal characteristics of the problem such as time-varying daily demand and the day-to-day learning behavior of travelers. Therefore, this classical approach does not enable researchers to analyze and accurately estimate the benefits of toll revenue redistribution strategies. The analysis is even more complicated if transit operators are private companies that seek to maximize their own profit, as in Hong Kong, and keen competition may arise between operators. This project developed a novel doubly dynamic modeling framework and a methodology that can determine time-dependent road tolls, transit frequency, and/or fares. The framework can consider the abovementioned complications. The properties of the resulting models and various tolling and redistribution strategies under different market regimes were analyzed. The models, methodology, and results of the analysis will help the government to mitigate congestion, regulate the transit market, and increase the attractiveness of the transit system.

17221016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17221016.value: Hong Kong is vulnerable to extreme weather events due to its rugged topography and dense urban development. Ground stabilization measures are intrusive and use concrete, steel, polymers and glass fibres as reinforcement elements, so more sustainable approaches that require fewer raw materials are strongly recommended. This project will explore the use of synthetic water repellent soils in ground infrastructure. New laboratory research by our team has demonstrated that wetting in soils can be controlled by inducing and adjusting water repellency. Existing soils can be treated on a construction site to become water repellent; once treated, they are non-intrusive, integrate with the surrounding environment and are mechanically stable (due to their non-wettable behaviour). However, research on the durability of water repellency is required to determine if it is a temporary or permanent technique and to elucidate applications. We hypothesise that whilst synthetic water repellent soils will degrade over time, through contamination by wettable fine particles deposition, growth of vegetation (roots), soil microbial biomass and organic matter, they have sufficient longevity for engineering applications. In natural water repellent soils, water repellency can last years, so it should be possible to construct very long-lasting synthetic water repellent soils for ground infrastructure. Therefore, the timescales of man-made water repellency systems need to be established, as do the causal agents of its decay. The first step in the development of durable synthetic water repellency is to identify time-stable water repellent treatments. Three approaches will be examined: impregnating an initially wettable soil with organic coatings such as dissolved organic carbon; changing the surface chemistry with silanes; and enhancing water repellency by altering the soil particle attributes (shape and size). In the second step, the spatial and temporal evolution of the treated soils will be tracked by monitoring their response to forced degradation and to microbiology and vegetation scenarios similar to those they would be exposed to in the field. This will identify the limit conditions under which water repellency may revert to its original (wettable) state. This research will provide Hong Kong with a novel technology for constructing water-tight barriers and fills that is both inexpensive and reliant on an abundant local resource – soils. Our research will verify its stability, so that perceived risks to practical implementation are identified and alleviated.

17221016.label: Realisation of objectives
17221016.value: This project aimed at investigating the degradation of hydrophobized soils under abrasion and weathering, in order to optimize their use in ground infrastructure. The specific objectives were met to all the extent. At first, we proposed the use of Tung oil, an economic and natural compound to hydrophobized soils, and compared its performance deterioration to dimethyldichlorosilne, which has been used in the literature. Soils were mixed with Tung oil and heated at different temperatures and durations to develop and optimize soil hydrophobicity. Tung oil induced severe and persistent hydrophobicity with heating, enhancing hydrophobicity until a critical temperature and duration threshold was reached. The results provided a sustainable and cost-effective soil hydrophobization method. Performance deterioration was split in two parts, one aimed at identifying the physical processes and the other aimed at identifying the chemical processes that drive deterioration. For the physical processes, the interaction effect between soil hydrophobicity and particle breakage was investigated by Micro-Deval abrasion tests. During abrasion both particle breakage and hydrophobicity reduction occurred. Hydrophobicity degradation was driven by the particle breakage, which was also affected by coating type and concentrations. To investigate the degradation under weathering (i.e., driven by chemical processes), the soils were subjected to thermal ageing, water immersion, cyclic wetting-drying and cyclic freezing-thawing. The results revealed declined hydrophobicity under thermal ageing and water immersion conditions, driven by oxidation of the hydrophobic coatings (thermal ageing) and hydrolysis (water immersion). Cyclic wetting-drying induced hydrolysis and detachment of coatings. Soil hydrophobicity was stable during freezing-thawing cycles. Finally, we also assessed the ecotoxicity and environmental risks of hydrophobized soils by biological assays and leachate tests respectively. Biological assays revealed minimal impact on soil microorganisms by hydrophobization. Total concentrations of heavy metals measured by leachate tests remained below the guidelines, indicating the leachate hazard will be negligible. The results demonstrate the environmental safety of hydrophobized soils as fill materials. These results haven't been submitted yet for publication. This research has shed light on the understanding of the degradation behavior of hydrophobized soils, and therefore provides a basis for their long-term use in ground infrastructure.

17221016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17221016.value: Tung oil: To provide a sustainable and low-cost solution to create an engineered water repellent soil, this study explored how Tung oil, a Chinese traditional vegetation oil, affected a Hong Kong completely decomposed granite (CDG). Tung oil has already been used in historical structures and suggested as a self-healing agent for concrete. A natural wettable soil from Hong Kong, CDG, was mixed with Tung oil and heated at different temperatures for different durations. The results reveal that the presence of Tung oil developed severe and persistent water repellency with heating, enhancing water repellency until a critical temperature threshold and heating duration was reached. The newly formed Tung-oil impregnated aggregates were found to be (1) stable when immersed in water, regardless of the temperature and heating duration, (2) and to have increasing tensile strength with aggregate size up to a temperature threshold. Please see publication 3 in part C. Physical degradation: The Micro-Deval test is proposed and used for the first time to assess the degradation of the hydrophobized sands. The testing programme investigates the effect of the Micro-Deval testing conditions (number of revolutions and pore fluid or medium – dry/wet) and hydrophobicity (concentration and type of hydrophobic compounds) on the particle degradation and hydrophobicity degradation. The results revealed that (1) hydrophobic degradation is more pronounced in dry conditions; (2) DMDCS-treated sands are both able to hold hydrophobicity and to limit particle degradation. (3) Hydrophobicity degradation is driven by the particle degradation (the median particle size). Please see publication 4 in part C. Chemical degradation: When placed at the interface ground–atmosphere, environmental factors such as temperature and rainfall are expected to impact their performance and impair their durability. Laboratory samples were subjected to thermal ageing, water immersion, cyclic wetting–drying and cyclic freezing–thawing and analysed for their hydrophobic degradation (magnitude and persistency) including controlling mechanisms via surface imaging and analysis. The results revealed that (1) elevated temperature and prolonged water immersion degraded hydrophobicity, albeit with differences between the coatings: dimethyldichlorosilane-treated sands were stable under thermal ageing; (2) a greater concentration of hydrophobizing compounds could minimize hydrophobic degradation during cyclic wetting–drying; (3) freezing–thawing had a negligible effect on hydrophobicity. Please see publication 5 in part C. Supporting research was also conducted: ecotoxicity of hydrophobized soils, and smaller studies, a 2-year outdoors monitoring of hydrophobic decay and seminal work on recovering hydrophobicity. Publications 1 and 2 in part C represent introductory studies where durability was first mentioned.

17221016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17221016.value: Field monitoring: In the current study, the laboratory-scale durability assessments is aimed at the properties and characteristics of hydrophobized soils as a granular material. The long-term service performance of a hydrophobized layer as part of a geotechnical structure (e.g., embankment, fill) should be studied and naturally follows this study. Biology-driven degradation: Biological activities can lead to hydrophobicity change (degradation or enhancement), which depends on the organisms and environmental conditions. From the outdoor weathering results (a small study conducted at the end of the project), microorganisms on hydrophobic coatings may lead to hydrophobic degradation. This assumption is also supported by other works in which PDMS and Tung oil coatings can be degraded by biological activities in soils. However, fungi have been reported to induce soil hydrophobicity. Therefore, the degradation caused by biological activities should be investigated under a controlled environment. Hydrophobic recovery: While we know have an idea of the factors that drive degradation of these materials, future work could encompass methods to recover hydrophobicity and maintain in the long-term. We have started investigating the potential of microencapsulation to recover hydrophobicity.

17221016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17221016.value: Soils are a construction material used for building infrastructure, such highways and railways embankments, slope retaining structures, flood defences and in other engineering projects. Soils are frequently water-loving. This mean’s water easily infiltrates because they are porous. However, infiltration and saturation of soils with water frequently causes issues, from landslides to swelling clays. Therefore, creating soils that are water-hating would be beneficial. Such soils (called hydrophobic) are not yet commercially available because little is known about them. One of the big questions is how long the water-hating effect lasts and what drives its disappearance. This proposal addressed this question by conducting a dedicated laboratory study. We investigated the effect of both physical factors (such as abrasion between soil particles) and chemical factors (such as hydrolysis and oxidation). We found that these new soils can last for decades. However, their lifespan is strongly dependent on the type of water-hating compound (or chemical) used and the environmental conditions including temperature, medium: water versus air, cyclic wetting-drying.

17223916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17223916.value: Layered magnetoelectric (ME) composites are developed by alternating piezoelectric layers and piezomagnetic layers during stacking. Such composites, which possess a superior ME coupling effect and can be easily manufactured, have been widely used in sensors, transducers, acoustic wave devices, etc. During service life, the layered ME materials and structures are subjected to dynamic mechanical and electromagnetic loads which can lead to interface cracking and failure. To date, most fracture analyses reported in the literature have been associated with static fracture problems related to the interface cracking of ME bimaterials. Thus, it is important to explore the dynamic fracture behavior of interface cracks in layered ME materials. In this project, advanced theoretical, numerical and experimental studies will be conducted to investigate the crack tip properties of interface cracks, which move at subsonic, transonic and/or supersonic speeds, in layered ME structures under plane deformations. The main constituents of this study are: (a) the establishment of new plane problem models for piezoelectric/piezomagnetic layered composite structures with interface cracks moving at different speeds, and the derivation of inhomogeneous Riemann-Hilbert equations and corresponding solutions for different crack surface electromagnetic conditions; (b) an exploration of the application of the extended finite element method (X-FEM) to moving interface crack problems of layered piezoelectric/piezomagnetic structures; and (c) the carrying out of a comprehensive experimental study on the dynamic fracture of piezoelectric/piezomagnetic laminates. The primary objective of this study is to reveal the effects of material properties, electromagnetic boundary conditions, geometric sizes, loading types and magnitudes on the fracture behaviors of interfacial moving cracks in multilayered ME composite structures, with different propagation speeds. The success of this project will offer a greater understanding of the dynamic fracture of interface cracks under plane deformation and will additionally provide a theoretical basis for the design and reliability analysis of layered ME materials and structures. 層狀磁電複合材料是將壓電和壓磁層交替層疊而成。這種複合材料具有優異的電磁耦合效應，並且容易製造，已被廣泛應用於換能器，傳感器，等器件。在使用期間，層狀電磁材料和結構經常受到衝擊和電磁負載影響，導致接口開裂。迄今為止，大多數層狀磁電複合材料器件有關的斷裂案件都與界面開裂問題有關。因此，探索層狀磁電複合材料界面裂紋在衝擊作用下的斷裂反應是非常重要的。 這項目將利用先進的理論，數值模擬和實驗，研究層狀磁電複合材料界面裂紋在不同擴展音速的情況下的變形和反應。 這項研究的主要組成部分是： （一）為壓電/壓磁分層界面裂紋在不同速度運動建立新的平面模型，在不同的裂縫面的電磁條件下推導理論方程和尋解; （二）用擴展有限元法(X-FEM)對移動分層壓電/壓磁結構的界面裂紋問題進行探索; （三）對分層壓電/壓磁材料的動態斷裂開展有關的實驗研究。 這項研究的主要目的是揭示材料特性，邊界條件，荷載的類型等對多層磁電複合結構界面裂縫在不同擴展速度的斷裂行為和影響。這項目將對界面裂紋平面內變形下的動態斷裂提供更深入的了解，並為分層磁電材料的分析和結構的設計提供可靠的理論依據。

17223916.label: Realisation of objectives
17223916.value: 1. An impact test and a three-point bending test are designed and carried out. The specimens are made by bonding two PZT-5H prisms with dimensions of 10×10×20 mm. Two kinds of bonding materials, superglue and silver paint, are used and following the impact test standard, a strip of free surface of 10 mm by 2 mm is left at the interface to serve as an initial crack. The energy consumed and the loading-displacement curve are obtained by the impact test and the three-point bending test, respectively, which can be used to evaluate the impact toughness and fracture toughness of the bonded specimens. 2. Assuming that the crack moves at different speed, plane-strain problems and anti-plane problem of moving cracks at the interface of two dissimilar magnetoelectroelastic (MEE) materials are considered under different crack-face boundary conditions. Employing the Lekhnitskii–Eshelby–Stroh representation and performing the appropriate coordinate transformation, the corresponding problems are formulated into inhomogeneous Riemann-Hilbert problems and usually can be solved analytically. The fracture parameters, for example, field intensity factors (FIFs), are derived and their numerical results are presented to study the influence of various factors on stress singularities and fracture parameters. 3. Considering the multi-filed coupled properties in MEE materials, novel and more suitable crack-tip enrichment functions for interfacial cracks in MEE composite structures are newly derived and and applied to analyze the dynamic fracture problems and the growth paths of interface cracks in MEE bimaterials and structures. 4. In the aforementioned theoretical and numerical studies, numerical examples and results are presented, in which the influence of the speed of the moving crack, poling direction, material volume fraction, load magnitudes and geometric sizes on the fracture parameters and stress singularities is investigated. 5. In the tests and published research papers, the effect of various factors on the fracture behavior of MEE and structures is investigated and discussed. Moreover, a review paper is completed to summarize the state-of-the-art research on crack problems in MEE materials and structures, including both theoretical and numerical methodologies. In particular, the influence of ME loadings on crack propagation is thoroughly discussed. All these will provide a basic theoretical reference for the design and reliability assessment of ME devices. It is remarked that MEE materials can be reduced to piezoelectric materials or magnetic materials by varying the volume fraction of the former in MEE composites. Therefore, the results related to MEE bimaterials in the aforementioned works can be readily degenerated to the ones related to piezoelectric/piezomagnetic bimaterials.

17223916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17223916.value: 1. Impact tests show that the impact toughness of the bonded PZT-5 specimen is around 37,500 N/m and 25,000 N/m when superglue and silver paint are adopted as the bonding materials, respectively. According to three-point bending tests, it is evaluated that the fracture toughness of the bonded PZT-5 specimen is 5.18 N/m and 3.08 N/m, respectively (Mok Ming Fai, 2018). 2. When the moving speed of the interface crack is less than critical shear wave of the bimaterial system, increasing both the speed of a moving crack and the difference of the material properties between the upper and the lower materials causes increases in the Mode-II SIF (Ma et al., 2017). However, when the moving speed of the interface crack is larger than critical shear wave, the real part of the singularity power, appears to be less than . The generalized stress fields are singular not only in the vicinity of the crack tip but also for all of the rays that emanate from the crack tip. (Ma et al., 2018). For a Yoffe conductive crack moving along the material interface, as the moving speed increases, three different kinds of singularities may emerge. These singularities are quite different from those of an anti-plane crack (Ma et al., 2020b). 3. Employing the new crack-tip enrichment functions of the X-FEM, the dynamic fracture problems of interface cracks in MEE bimaterials is investigated. The validation of the proposed formulation is verified (Yan et al., 2019). 4. As previously mentioned, increasing the difference of the material properties and shear load will improve the crack propagation. Load position and load ratio have more significant effects on the Mode-II SIF (Ma et al., 2017). The X-FEM numerical results show that increasing the heights of piezoelectric or piezomagnetic layer will impede the crack growth (Yan et al., 2019). 5. Based on the aforementioned theoretical and experimental results, it is demonstrated that the binding materials have a significant influence on the fracture toughness of layered structures (Mok Ming Fai, 2018). Moreover, the shear stress and layer height play an essential role in the fracture analysis of piezoelectric/piezomagnetic layered materials (Ma et al., 2018; Yan et al., 2019). The propagation speed of the interface crack exert a significant influence on fracture behaviors, so special attention should be paid to this aspect in the design of MEE structures and devices (Ma et al., 2018; Ma et al., 2020a; Ma et al., 2020b).

17223916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17223916.value: For piezoelectric/piezomagnetic layered materials and structures, the electric and magnetic hysteresis as well as the domain switching should be further taken into account. In fact, at present, non-linear MEE fracture mechanics is still not well understood and convincing fracture mechanical concepts have not been developed yet. Here, a great challenging task is the determination of the asymptotic fields around the crack-tip on the basis of the multi-field coupling effects, which usually requires the development and implementation of appropriate non-linear constitutive laws. The main concern hereby is to illuminate the effects of the aforementioned non-linear features on the fracture behaviours in theoretical and experimental points of view. Another topic which needs to be further explored is the fatigue crack growth under combined magnetoelectromechanical loadings. Again, further improvements lie in the understanding of the crack propagation behaviours in the process zone during cyclic fully reverse loading within the framework of both linear and non-linear fracture mechanics. Another open and inevitable question is the choice of the fracture criterion, which can satisfactorily predict the direction and the speed of the fatigue crack propagation in the mixed magnetoelectromechanical loading environment.

17223916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17223916.value: The investigation of the dynamic fracture behavior of interface cracks in layered ME materials is necessary and meaningful since interface cracking of layered ME materials and structures usually develops and further leads to their failure under the dynamic mechanical and electromagnetical loads. In this project, advanced theoretical, numerical and experimental studies have been conducted to investigate the crack tip properties of interface cracks. This study reveals the effects of material properties, electromagnetic boundary conditions, geometric sizes, loading types and magnitudes on the fracture behaviors of interface moving cracks in multi-layered ME composite structures and with different propagation speeds. This project enhances a better understanding of the dynamic fracture of interface cracks under plane deformation and provides a theoretical basis for the design and reliability analysis of layered ME materials and structures.

17225516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17225516.value: This project studies efficient online algorithms for long-term optimal operation of Network Function Virtualization (NFV) systems. Network functions (or middleboxes) are modules in a network infrastructure that provide special treatment to traversing traffic flows, e.g., intrusion detection systems, firewalls, NATs, proxies, WAN optimizers. Today a new form of network function typically emerges as a one-off solution to a specific need, implemented using dedicated hardware and "patched'' into the infrastructure through manual installation, which are costly and difficult to maintain. NFV is a recent paradigm advocating to implement network functions using software that can run in standard virtualized platforms, e.g., virtual machines (VMs) on industry standard servers, instead of dedicated hardware. Deploying a new virtualized network function (VNF) is as easy as launching a VM instance, enabling dynamic orchestration of service chains (i.e., an ordered sequence of VNFs such as firewall->IDS->proxy) and dynamic scaling of their traffic processing capacity, at much lower costs than deploying hardware. To enable NFV, existing efforts have been focusing on implementing better software middleboxes to approach the performance of specialized hardware, and designing management systems for VNF deployment and traffic routing. Going beyond the enabling technologies, there has been a lack of efficient online algorithms to guide optimal deployment and scaling of VNFs over time, to best serve fluctuating traffic at the minimal overall cost. In addition, with the very recent springing up of the NFV marketplace, efficient pricing mechanisms are being called for, to charge dynamically assembled service chains according to demand and supply of various VNFs at different times. This project proposes a set of efficient online algorithms and mechanisms for dynamic optimal deployment, scaling and pricing of VNF service chains in cloud platforms. We start by studying dynamic service chain packing on servers within one datacenter, which is common in cases such as provisioning access service in an enterprise's on-premise datacenter. We next investigate service chain deployment/scaling across multiple geographically distributed datacenters, needed for processing flows between geo-dispersed sources and destinations. Competitive online algorithms are sought to minimize the overall cost of the NFV system over its long run. Then we study service chain pricing in a representative NFV marketplace with three parties of cloud providers, NFV providers and NFV users, and design efficient mechanisms through online auctions, targeting social welfare maximization. We seek rigorous theoretical analysis of our algorithms and mechanisms, as well as real-world testbed implementation and evaluation in practical settings.

17225516.label: Realisation of objectives
17225516.value: We have achieved Objectives 1-4 in this project to 100%. For object 1, regarding Goals a) and b), we thoroughly investigated the problem of online VNF service chain scaling in a cloud data center and formulated the problem as an integer linear program (ILP). We leveraged the regularization technique adapted from online learning literature to decouple the original online ILP into a series of regularized sub-problems; we relaxed each offline sub-problem as a linear program (LP) and solved it efficiently using a convex optimization algorithm to obtain a fractional solution. We then adopted a novel online rounding algorithm based on linear algebra and dependent rounding to derive the integer solution, guaranteeing a good expected competitive ratio. The results were reported in publication 5 in Part C-8. For Goal c), time-varying traffic change ratios have been considered in our formulation in publication 5 in Part C-8 as well. Further, we investigated service chain deployment/scaling in a datacenter where the flow rate of traffic may change after being processed by a network function, the servers are heterogeneous with different capacities and are inter-connected through a fat-tree switch network, and the available bandwidth between two VNF instances deployed on two servers is time-varying. We designed an online learning algorithm to estimate the available bandwidth based on flow routing in the switch network, and then decided VNF instance deployment and scaling accordingly. We showed that our online learning algorithm achieves a sublinear regret with T, a desirable target for online learning algorithm design. The results were reported in publication 1 of Part C-9. We have also studied a similar problem in the scenario of virtual machine deployment and scaling in a cloud data center, with results reported in publication 3 of Part C-8. Further, we studied more generic service chains with stateful middleboxes (e.g., stateful firewalls, TCP optimizer) in terms of system and algorithm design in publications 7, 8 in Part C-8 and publication 7 of Part C-9. For Objective 2, regarding Goals a) and b), we designed an efficient dependent rounding algorithm to round the fractional numbers of VNF instances and schedule flows to guarantee feasibility; we also handled end-to-end delay constraints in our online algorithm design, and similar delay requirements, e.g., some NFs need to be deployed within certain RTTs from the flow sources/destinations, can be handled in a similar framework. The online algorithm we designed achieves a good competitive ratio based on solid theoretical analysis. The results were reported in publication 1 of Part C-8. We have also studied delay-constraint virtual network coding function deployment and scaling over multiple data centers, and reported the results in publication 2 of part C-9. For Goal c) we propose a deep learning-based framework for scaling of the geo-distributed VNF chains, exploring inherent pattern of traffic variation and good deployment strategies over time, by novelly combining a recurrent neural network as the traffic model for predicting upcoming flow rates and a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent for making chain placement decisions. The results were reported in publication 6 of Part C-8. Related to inter-server flow routing, we have proposed an efficient and scalable multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) method for inter-domain routing, as reported in publication 10 of Part C-9. For Objective 3, regarding Goals a) and b), we studied an occupation time-oblivious pricing mechanism for cloud jobs (including service chains deployed in a cloud), and designed efficient online learning based algorithms to set the prices and allocate resources to the jobs. The results were reported in publication 4 of Part C-9. We also studied online cloud resource pricing and allocation in a number of other scenarios (within a cloud data center and across edge clouds) as in publication 4 of Part C-8 and publications 8, 9 in Part C-9, which are all useful for service chain resource pricing and provisioning. For Goal c), we studied optimal cloud resource pricing mechanisms under generic linear resource cost functions; the results can be readily applied to service chain pricing, considering costs due to buying VNF software or deploying/managing service chains. We reported the results in publication 5 of Part C-9. For Objective 4, we have implemented and enhanced our NFV testbed, by emulating link capacities, delays, and VM/bandwidth costs following those of real-world data centers. We have evaluated our algorithms reported in the publications above using our NFV testbed or simulated systems with workloads produced following the Google cluster-usage data and other real-world traces, and reported evaluation results in terms of social welfare, profit, etc. In publication 2 of Part C-9, we designed a WAN-based NFV testbed, implemented prototypes of the virtual network coding function chains on top of it, and deployed them onto geo-distributed Amazon EC2 cloud sites for evaluation; we have reported the experimental results (regarding throughput and delay under different realistic traffic situations) in the paper. In addition, we have studied geo-distributed service chain deployment and dynamic scaling using the IMS system as a case study, and deployed and evaluated our solution on distributed IBM cloud cites in publication 2 of Part C-8. We have also designed and implemented real GPU-accelerated NFV systems, as reported in publications 7, 8 of Part C-8 and publications 6, 7 of Part C-9. On the real-world cloud based distributed environments, we have evaluated the impact of real Internet delay and bandwidth on real-time service chain scaling and flow transmission. We found geo-distributed cloud sites are sufficient for implementing WAN-based NFV testbed and hence did not resort to interconnecting institutional platforms in this research.

17225516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17225516.value: In publication 1 and publication 5 of Part C-8, we designed an online algorithm for dynamic placement and scaling of VNF service chains across geo-distributed datacenters and within one data center, respectively, to serve flows between dispersed source and destination pairs, for operational cost minimization of the service chain provider over the entire system span. We adopted a regularization-based approach from online learning literature to convert the offline optimal deployment problem into a sequence of one-shot regularized problems, each to be efficiently solved in one time slot, and an online dependent rounding scheme to derive feasible integer solutions from the optimal fractional solutions of the one-shot problems, and to guarantee a good competitive ratio of the respective online algorithm over the entire time span. In publications 3, 4 of Part C-8, publications 4, 5, 9 of Part C-9, we designed efficient online algorithms for cloud resource pricing and allocation to jobs (which can be readily applied for service chain deployment and provisioning on cloud data centers), and rigorously proved competitive ratios achieved by the respective online algorithms. In publication 6 of Part C-8, publications 8, 10 of Part C-9, we novelly adopted reinforcement learning based approaches for making service chain placement, cloud resource allocation and flow routing decisions, respectively, and showed with experiments the good performance of such reinforcement learning-based approaches. In publications 6, 7 of Part C-9, we designed GPU-accelerated NFV systems; in publications 7, 8 of Part C-8, we designed efficient NFV flow processing systems for stateful network functions; solid experiments show excellent performance of our designed/implemented systems. In publication 2 of Part C-9, we designed and implemented the network coding function as a network function, and proposed an efficient algorithm for coding function deployment, scaling in and out, in the presence of system dynamics, across geo-distributed cloud sites; we evaluated performance of our algorithm/system by experimenting over geo-distributed Amazon EC2 sites. In publication 2 of Part C-8, we proposed proactive and reactive approaches for timely, cost-effective scaling of practical IMS service chains across geo-distributed cloud sites, and demonstrated our system's excellent performance over geo-distributed IBM clouds.

17225516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17225516.value: This research has mainly resorted to (online) optimization approaches for algorithm design. We have made some attempts on applying reinforcement learning in designing adaptive algorithms. It will be intriguing to further investigate machine learning based approaches in dynamic environment learning, for better algorithm design.

17225516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17225516.value: This project studies efficient online algorithms for long-term optimal operation of Network Function Virtualization (NFV) systems. We designed a set of efficient online algorithms for dynamic optimal deployment, scaling and pricing of VNF service chains in both centralized and geo-distributed cloud platforms. Our algorithms were proven to be highly optimized, minimizing the overall cost of the NFV system over its long run. We also built NFV systems with hardware acceleration and framework support, to be used in a number of real-world scenarios. No known online strategies existed to optimally guide capacity scaling of VNF service chains. Our study is the first to systematically examine the tradeoffs in dynamic VNF service chain provisioning, and to design practical algorithms and systems for optimal operation of dynamic NFV service chains.

17227616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17227616.value: 立體定向和功能性神經手術是一種治療多種慢性神經系統疾病的有效手段。腦深層刺激手術是其中一種常見的立體定向手術，應用於治療帕金森病引起的衰弱症狀和肌張力障礙。在該手術中，電極將在立體定向裝置的引導下放置於腦深部的底丘腦核中。通過對底丘腦核的慢性刺激，帕金森病的運動障礙症狀將得到緩解。功能性或擴散磁共振成像可用於揭示與腦深部核團相關的關鍵結構，如皮質脊髓束、紅核和第三神經核等。該圖像將用於構造立體定向導航腦深部刺激手術的初始三維大腦路線圖。然而這是靜態的，且由術前掃描的圖像建構而成。在立體定向手術中，由於重力和腦脊液外流顱內物質將發生顯著變形，即“腦移位”（包含皮層和皮層下）。這將必然導致實際解剖學位置與術前規劃路徑間約10-30毫米的錯位。在當前基於框架的立體定向手術流程中，附加的固有誤差還包括框架精度誤差，配准誤差，圖像融合誤差和計算誤差。因而，有效地規劃和操控一支修長（17-18cm）纖細（≤∅1.3mm）的電極針在亞毫米級的精度內到達腦深部的底丘腦核仍是一項重大挑戰。 該項目的總體目標是開發和驗証一個集術中磁共振成像、實時磁共振跟蹤系統與加速磁共振圖像配准導航為一體的核磁兼容（或條件性核磁兼容）的機器人系統，以提高電極放置精確度，從而促進腦深層刺激手術的臨床療效。本項目將提出一種可解決計算瓶頸的新型異構計算加速器，用於在連續更新的術中磁共振圖像中進行快速配准。 應用於腦深部刺激手術器具位置及機器人形態追蹤的基於核磁共振的半主動位置跟蹤系統也將被應用。這些反饋數據將檢測從治療目標到瞄准角度間的差距，以及沿途的潛在風險，如腦實質出血等。 本項目提出的系統將從根本上區別於現有的遠程操作立體定向系統。在現有系統中，低效能的機器人控制主要源於有限的圖像導引和不可靠的手術器具位置跟蹤反饋。針對此問題，我們將運用微制造技術在纖細的腦深部刺激手術器具上（∅2mm）整合微型磁共振跟蹤線圈電路（1.2×5mm^2）與多路光纖，以達到在核磁共振圖像下對多個線圈（>8）的監視和跟蹤。該系統將是該領域首個集合了術中核磁共振圖像處理加速，實時核磁共振跟蹤系統和高精度反饋控制的手術機器人，為提高該類機器人在立體定向和功能性神經手術中的性能提供了一種手段。相關的性能指標及其詳細的定量驗証方法也將在實驗室和基於核磁共振圖像的實驗中被提出。 該項目的成功將代表著在大幅腦移位等復雜情況下，手術機器人朝著更安全，更准確，更有效的目標邁進的重要一步。本項目所提出的技術將通過簡化反復的微電極記錄（MER）以及頭部框架與圖像配准流程，顯著減少手術時間（至少40-50％ ）。進一步地，該技術還將減少局部麻醉的復雜性與並發症，通過以圖像取代在術中與清醒病人進行互動的術后評估方式。這些都是在當前最先進的機器人輔助介入手術中也難以解決的問題。

17227616.label: Realisation of objectives
17227616.value: The PI and his collaborators have developed the world’s first magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided neurosurgical robotic system capable of performing bilateral stereotactic neurosurgery. The compact design of robot enables intra-operative (intra-op) operation within the constrained standard imaging head coil to enhance imaging performance. The team also conducted pre-clinical validation of the system on cadaver with CUHK neurosurgeons, Dr Danny Chan Tat-ming and Professor Poon Wai-sang. The feasibility of this innovation has been proved in the current pre-clinical setting, which may facilitate the treatment of Parkinson’s disease and other neuropsychiatric disorders. The robot could achieve a maximum stiffness coefficient of 24.35 N/mm, with the transmission fluid preloaded at 2 bar. The surgical safety and accuracy are particularly demanding for instrument manipulation in stereotactic neurosurgery, which has to offer precise coordination of at least two DoFs (e.g., rotation and insertion) and requires an average accuracy within 2 mm. Our proposed platform provides sufficient targeting accuracy to meet this requirement. In a needle insertion task for deep brain stimulation (DBS) procedure, the average error is ⩽ 1.73 mm. In the intra-op adjustment of robot, real-time monitoring of the 3D instrument position is achieved by our customized wireless MRI tracking coils. The small (8 mm × 1.5 mm) micro radiofrequency (RF) coils can be attached to a brachytherapy applicator, providing rapid (up to 40 Hz) and precise and (resolution: 0.6 mm × 0.6mm × 0.6 mm) using an MR-tracking sequence for gynecologic brachytherapy in a Siemens 3T MR scanner, without affecting the image quality. The tracking coil is in four-layer planar form, and its quality factor is 28.5. It outperforms the conventional method of using low-contrast passive fiducials that can only be revealed in the MR image domain. Two wireless tracking units/markers are integrated with the robot, which are two miniaturized coil circuits in size of 1.5 × 5 × 0.2 mm3, fabricated on flexible thin films. A navigation test was performed under the standard MRI settings in order to visualize the 3-D localization of the robotic instrument. MRI compatibility test was also carried out to prove the minimal interference to MR images of the presented hydraulic robotic platform. The magnetic resonance (MR) safe and high-performance hydraulic transmissions are incorporated. The proposed motor can provide continuous bidirectional rotation with unlimited range. It also features fast response (rise time < 40 ms), precise open-loop control of position (average error of 0.64°) and high output torque (0.49 N·m) through 10-meter long hydraulic pipelines. Currently, there is no such kind of MR safe hydraulic master-slave follower. Both kinematics and dynamics models of the motor have also been devised to identify the key design parameters that govern the system performances, e.g. transmission stiffness and latency. The master-slave actuator has fast step response (< 40 ms), high payload (0.49 N·m), quick frequency response (60 ms at 1 Hz and 0.2 MPa), and precise feed-forward control (ave. error of 0.64°). The performances in step response and frequency response have demonstrated the sufficiently low latency of force/position transfer within the range of 0.1-2 Hz. It can achieve an accuracy of 0.64°/1.50° (avg./max).
