17227616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17227616.value: The world-first magnetic resonance imaging (“MRI”)-guided neurosurgical robotic system capable of performing bilateral stereotactic neurosurgery was successfully designed and validated. The compact design of robot enables intra-operative (intra-op) operation within constrained imaging head coil. The team also conducted pre-clinical validation of the system on cadaver with CUHK neurosurgeons, Dr Danny Chan Tat-ming and Professor Poon Wai-sang. The feasibility of this innovation has been proved in the current clinical setup, which may facilitate the treatment of Parkinson’s disease and other neuropsychiatric disorders. In neurosurgeries, the surgical safety and accuracy are particularly demanding for instrument manipulation in stereotactic neurosurgery. Our proposed platform provides sufficient targeting accuracy (⩽ 1.73 mm) to meet the operation requirement (2mm), which has been validated in a simulated deep brain stimulation task. Reference Publication: Part C [1] [2]. Real-time monitoring of the 3D instrument position is achieved by our customized wireless MRI tracking coils, in order to provide real-time feedback for robot closed-loop control. It outperforms the conventional method of using low-contrast passive fiducials that can only be revealed in the MR image domain. A navigation test performed under the standard MRI settings demonstrates the visualization performance via robotic instrument 3-D localization. MRI compatibility test also proves the minimal interference to MR images of the presented hydraulic robotic platform. The magnetic resonance (MR) safe and high-performance hydraulic transmissions are incorporated to guarantee the dynamic performance. The proposed motor can provide continuous bidirectional rotation with unlimited range. It also features fast response (rise time < 40 ms), precise open-loop control of position (average error of 0.64°) and high output torque (0.49 N·m) through 10-meter long hydraulic pipelines. Reference Publication: Part C [20] [14] Besides the above-mentioned research efforts, the team was recently conferred the Best Conference Paper Award in the IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation 2018 (ICRA’18), which was held in Brisbane, Australia, from May 21 to 25, 2018. This year, the team was conferred the final best out of 35 finalists in all the nine robotics categories, including robot vision, cognitive robotics, robot manipulation, and unmanned aerial vehicles. Other shortlisted universities and companies include MIT, Harvard, Stanford, and DeepMind. The team project was also shortlisted as a finalist for the Medical Robotics paper award at the same Conference.

17227616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17227616.value: In our future work, we will develop a multi-stage semi-automated needle positioning system for bilateral stereotactic neurosurgery. Our proposed system will be with locking mechanism for fine and coarse adjustment, which will ensure precise alignment of the needle after automated positioning. We will develop omni-directional wireless tracking coils to provide fast and seamless registration between intra-op MR imaging and the needle position on the basis of a patient-mounted robot docking frame. Similar mechanism would also be applied in percutaneous ablation. This is a kind of standard therapy for most cases of hepatocellular carcinoma, which is a general type of primary liver cancer. We will also design a semi-automated robotic system for MRI-guided percutaneous needle insertion procedures. Performance such as stiffness, needle positioning accuracy and frequency response will be experimentally evaluated. Negligible interference to MR imaging will also be validated by an MR compatibility test. Apart from the current version of MR-semiactive tracking approach, we will also explore and improve the 6D tracking micro-unit. Using a properly programmed MR sequence that detunes/triggers the isolated resonant circuit, the semi-automated device can be visualized in the MR images, enabling the real-time localization feedback for robot control and instant image-guided surgical planning.

17227616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17227616.value: A high-performance neurosurgical robotic system is proposed to perform bilateral stereotactic neurosurgery inside a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanner. The system is hydraulically driven, thus does not generate any electromagnetic interference or affect imaging quality under MRI. A manipulator is designed to perform dexterous operations on the left and right brain targets, and the area required for an invasive anchorage is very small. The compact robot can fit inside a standard MRI head coil, and advanced three-dimensional tracking markers enable fast localization of robot instruments in MRI in real time. This is the first robotic system capable of performing brain surgery inside an MRI scanner, paving the way for more accurate and efficient treatment of illnesses such as Parkinson’s disease and other neuropsychiatric disorders. It also greatly reduces the time needed for neurosurgery, which can last up to a whole day, as simultaneous work on both sides of the brain may be required. The following elements in this system are considered to be novel, light-weight and compact robot design enabling surgical operations within a confined workspace; magnetic resonance (MR)-safe actuators offering precise bilateral navigation; real-time positional tracking with wireless MR-based tracking coils, avoiding offline MR image registration process so as to reduce procedural time.

17229116.label: Project Objectives

We will also design novel solutions to support the effective and efficient execution of interactive QBE.

17229116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17229116.value: Heterogeneous information networks (HINs) such as YAGO, Freebase, and DBLP record a gigantic number of interrelated entities. For instance, YAGO contains over 10 million entities, and 120 million facts about those entities. The research and industry communities use HINs in various applications, including search engines, product recommendations, and health intelligence. In the proposed project, we will introduce the meta-graph, which describes the relationships among different types of HIN entities (e.g., “author” and “paper”). Meta-graphs provide insights on the interaction of HIN objects, and are useful for query recommendations, information retrieval, and similarity analysis. However, obtaining good meta-graphs manually from a large and complex HIN can be very difficult. Hence, we plan to investigate algorithms and data structures for extracting meta-graphs in a convenient, effective, and efficient manner. We will further investigate query evaluations of HINs, with a focus on the query-by-example (QBE). In the QBE paradigm, a query user provides one or more examples (e.g., famous football players and their countries, such as “Beckham, UK”), and a QBE produces results similar to these examples (e.g., “Messi, Argentina”). Because existing search engines (e.g., Google and Bing) often return results that are focused on the query input (e.g., photos of “Beckham” and the “UK”), QBE answers can be used to enrich the search results returned by these applications. QBE can also be used for product recommendations on online shopping sites (e.g., Amazon). QBE is easier to use than traditional HIN queries, which require a user to understand the query language and the HIN structure. However, QBE evaluation on HINs is an under-studied problem. We will develop novel QBE algorithms that use meta-graphs. We will also examine interactive QBE, which allows a user to provide feedback on query outputs to our algorithm, which then learns the user’s intent and yields better answers. We will design effective and efficient interactive QBE algorithms, which have not been studied before. We will perform extensive experimental evaluations to validate the efficiency and accuracy of our proposed methods, and will also prototype a system that enables meta-graph discovery and QBE evaluation on Freebase. The system will also support interactive QBE. Existing solutions for managing HINs are inadequate, and our work will thus advance the state-of-the-art. Moreover, HINs are prevalent in search and recommendation applications, which are common in the Hong Kong SAR and China. Our solutions are thus highly relevant to these regions. 異構信息網絡 (Heterogeneous Information Network, HIN)含有龐大複雜的信息。例如，YAGO包含超過1000萬個實體，與及關於它們的1.2億個信息。其他的例子有FreeBase和 DBLP。此類網絡已廣泛應用搜索引擎、產品建議、和健康應用。在此項目，我們提出元圖 (meta-graph)，它描述了不同類型的實體之間的關係（例如，「作者」和「論文」）。Meta-graph 可用查詢建議，信息檢索，和相似性分析。從一個龐大而複雜的HIN獲得Meta-graph是非常困難的。所以，我們計劃開發算法和數據結構以高效率的方式提取Meta-graph。 我們會研究HIN的Query-by-Example（QBE）查詢方法。在QBE中，用戶提供一個或多個實施例（例如，足球運動員和他們的國家，像「貝克漢姆，英國」）。QBE會產生類似這些實例的結果（例如，「梅西，阿根廷」）。QBE答案可以用於補足搜索引擎（像谷歌和Bing）的搜索結果。 QBE也可用於網上購物網站的建議。我們將使用Meta-graph 來開發QBE算法。我們也會研究互動式QBE，以允許用戶提供關於查詢結果的反饋；我們的方法能從這些反饋學習，從而獲得更準確的答案。我們會在真實的HIN進行大量的實驗評估，以驗證我們方法的效率和準確度。

17229116.label: Realisation of objectives
17229116.value: We have achieved the objectives stated in the proposal, as detailed below: 1) We have performed an extensive study on fast and accurate meta-graph extraction algorithms. Meta-path measures are computationally expensive to compute, and so it is necessary to have fast solutions. We have developed approximate efficient solutions (ICDM 2018, Part C(9).7). We further examined the k most important meta-path patterns between two graph nodes in a HIN. The main issue is to study (1) how current meta-path similarity metrics and other measures (e.g., occurrences of a meta-path) can be used to quantify the importance of a meta-path; and (2) the use of efficient algorithms and advanced data structures provide online performance. The results have been published in IEEE TKDE (Part C(8), No. 5). 2) We have further studied the problem of discovering meta-graphs between two entities in a Heterogeneous Information Network (HIN), which can serve the purpose of long-tail web query recommendation (QR). The QR is the process of using web users’ query history (or query log) to recommend to them queries that they are interested. Traditional QR solutions do not focus on the problem of long-tail queries, i.e., those that are rare queries and are not well represented in query logs. With the use of our solutions, which tap into the rich resources in HINs, we are able to achieve a better QR result than existing works. We have published an IEEE CIKM’16 paper (a top IR conference) based on this, and have published an extended journal version recently in ACM TKDD 2018 (Part C (8), No. 1), a top journal in data mining. 3) We have studied the issues of finding important graph structures from social networks, which is a form of HINs. Particularly, we studied community search on a large spatial network (VLDB 2017, Part C(8), No. 3), which is a kind of HINs with spatial information of users. The community (or a subgraph) depicts the complex relationship pattern between social users, which can be further leveraged to find the “meta-structures” between them, in order to understand how they are connected. We have also studied the finding of patterns in spatial databases. The main idea is convert the spatial data into a large graph, and derive the related meta-graph pattern, and then adopt techniques similar to graph pattern matching. The paper has been published in ICDE 2018. We also studied an adaptive indexing scheme on k-NN queries on road networks (VLDB 2018). 4) We have performed extensive studies on query evaluation based on meta-graphs. We studied the discovery of meta-graph discovery techniques, and extract pairs of nodes connected by meta-graphs, given a set of node pair examples (WWW15, KDD16, ICDM18, TKDE20). Moreover, we studied the finding of motif cliques in large graphs, which are essentially cliques defined based on meta-graphs. The allows us to study how to use meta-graphs can be used to explore interesting subgraph structures, which can be used to identify interesting patterns in e-commerce and bioinformatics (ICDE19, Part C(9).5). Recently, we propose the concept of motif-paths, in order to help us to understand how meta-graphs are connected between two nodes (VLDB21, Part C(8).8). The result allows us to find higher-order connections among nodes, and also makes it possible to perform better in data mining applications (e.g., clustering, classification, and prediction on graphs). Recently, we have developed and demonstrated a motif discovery prototype, which provides automatically motif discovery and visualization in a web browser (ICDE19, Part C(9).6). Last year, we further developed a graph query language (GQL), which are extended to support meta-graph patterns, so that a suer query user can specify the use of motifs in a GQL (e.g., count the number of patterns, find motif-paths etc.) (CIKM20, Part C(9).4). 5) We have recently studied the problem of discovering densest subgraph discovery on large graphs (VLDB19, Part C(8).7) and directed graphs (SIGMOD20, Part C(9).3; SIGMOD Record, Part C(8).10), allowing us to extract relationship among nodes, and can be used in the applications such as fraud detection in advertisement networks. It is interesting to examine whether the densest subgraph found can shed insights on meta-graphs (because the nodes are tightly connected). The work was recognized as by getting a SIGMOD Research Highlights 2020, and has been published in SIGMOD Record March 2021 issue. Previously, we have studied how to process shortest path queries in evolving graph sequences (IS, Part C(8).4). We further studied a network kernel density visualization algorithm, allowing us to visualize a graph based on their density (VLDB21, Part C(8).9). It is interesting to study how this visualization techniques can allow us to visualize and discover meta-graph patterns. 6) We have studied two problems related to uncertain graphs, which is a kind of graphs in which edges exist with a probability. First, we study novel embedding techniques on an uncertain graph in CIKM 2017 (Part C(9).2). The embedding converts the graph into a matrix space, enabling existing ML solutions. We further investigated the counting of motifs and meta-graphs in uncertain graphs in VLDB 2019 (Part C(8).6).

17229116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17229116.value: 1) We have studied real-time and accurate meta-path extraction algorithms. We have developed approximate efficient solutions (ICDM 18, Part C(9).7). We further examined the k most important meta-path patterns between two graph nodes in a HIN. The results have been published in IEEE TKDE (Part C(8).5). 2) We have studied the problem of discovering meta-paths between two entities in a Heterogeneous Information Network (HIN), which can serve the purpose of long-tail web query recommendation (QR). We have published these results in top venues (IEEE CIKM’16 and ACM TKDD 2018 (Part C (8).1)). 3) We have studied the issues of finding important graph structures from large spatial networks, which are a form of HINs (VLDB 2017, Part C(8).3). We have also studied the finding of patterns in spatial databases based on graph pattern matching in ICDE 2018. We also studied an adaptive indexing scheme on k-NN queries on road networks (VLDB 2018). 4) We studied the discovery of motif cliques in large graphs, which allow us to study how meta-structures can be used to discover interesting subgraph structures (ICDE19, Part C(9).5). We propose the concept of motif-paths, which help us to understand how meta-structures are connected between two nodes (VLDB21, Part C(8).8). A prototype has been developed (ICDE19, Part C(9).6). Recently, a graph query language extended to support meta-structures, has been developed (CIKM20, Part C(9).4). 5) We have recently studied the densest subgraph discovery on large graphs (VLDB19, Part C(8).7) and directed graphs (SIGMOD20, Part C(9).3; SIGMOD Record, Part C(8).10), allowing us to extract relationship among nodes, and can be used in the applications such as fraud detection in advertisement networks. We have also studied how to process shortest path queries in evolving graph sequences (IS, Part C(8).4). We further studied a network kernel density visualization algorithm, allowing us to visualize a graph based on their density (VLDB21, Part C(8).9). 6) We have studied novel embedding techniques on an uncertain graph, which is a kind of graphs in which edges exist with a probability, in CIKM 2017 (Part C(9).2). The embedding converts the graph into a matrix space, enabling existing ML solutions. We further investigated the discovery of meta-structures from uncertain graphs in VLDB 2019 (Part C(8).6).

17229116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17229116.value: 1) We studied the use of meta-paths in query recommendation, which were published in CIKM and TKDD. We will study how meta-structures can be used for this purpose. We are also investigating how to use meta-paths in other problems (e.g., graph embedding and visualization). 2) Design a graph query language (GQL) that supports meta-graph discovery. Given our research results in this project and our experience in developing a motif-clique explorer (Part C.9 (6)) and GQL for supporting motif s (Part C.9 (3)), it is interesting to examine how a GQL can be extended to handle meta-graphs, as well as extending a graph database system (e.g., Neo4j) to support meta-graph discovery and related queries. 3) Apply our results in real applications. The PI has been working on a HKD $4M ITF project, which aims to build a graph for matching elders and helpers for providing services to them. We have used meta-path-based recommendation solutions in the project, and will investigate the use of the results in this project. The PI is also working with a television company on knowledge-graph-based recommendation. Again, we can study how our meta-graphs discovery solutions can be used, to improve the recommendation quality of movies to customers.

17237316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17237316.value: 化疗栓塞疗法是一种非手术且对人体侵入性极小的治疗方法。通过引入栓塞剂，化疗栓塞法既能选择性地阻塞血管又能准确地将更高剂量的化疗药物释放到患病组织。在栓塞目标组织后化疗药物无法从其血管床中释放出来，因而这种疗法同时能直接降低化疗药物对正常组织的毒副作用。化疗栓塞作为现代介入治疗的主要分支之一已经广泛用于治疗包括肿瘤在内的各种人体器官病变。为了获得较好的临床治疗效果以及降低施用复杂性，化疗栓塞微球必须得形状尺寸均匀，而且能够有效可控地进行药物装载和释放。传统加工方法不能精确设计制造微球的形状，尺寸及其微结构，且不能有效地控制药物的装载和释放，至今治疗过程中所用栓塞微球的效果依然不够让人满意。 在此我们提出一种加工方法能够制造可控进行药物封装和释放的化疗栓塞微球。这个技术的关键是将传统的“自上而下”的加工过程替换为利用微流控双乳液模板的“自下而上”的方法。微流控技术能够精密地操纵微小液体，因而可以精确地控制双乳液及核-壳微球的形成，最终制造出各向性质高度均一的微球颗粒。基于微流控技术的优势，提出的方法将利用微流控装置来生成双乳液模板。微流控装置中圆形毛细管通道与热力学中最低界面能原理共同作用能生产出各向尺寸均一的完美球形液滴和微球颗粒。每个生产出来的微球都趋于完美球形且形状和尺寸都高度一致。微球颗粒上的药物装载是封装在每个微球中的，因而能达到100%的药物装载率。如此高的装载率是通过在液滴形成之初就将药物注入进每个液滴中。药物的释放能够准确便捷地通过调节微球颗粒的核壳结构来调控。而微球颗粒的核壳结构可以通过调节微流控双乳液模板的形成来达成。 我们的目标是利用这项技术的巨大潜力来实现精确控制微球形貌和药物释放且将加工制造参数与形成的微球形貌和释放曲线相关联。我们通过制造分别装载有亲水和疏水药物的海藻酸钙-聚乳酸乙醇酸和聚乳酸乙醇酸-海藻酸钙的核-壳化疗栓塞微球来研发表征所提出的方法。我们之所以选择海藻酸钙和聚乳酸乙醇酸是基于它们优异的性质，包括高生物兼容性，生物可降解性以及可压缩性。 这个项目的成功将会改变化疗栓塞微球的制造方法以及高质量功能性微颗粒的精密加工和研发方法。这个项目的发现也将为未来每位患者进行定制治疗而调控生产高度匹配于个人的具有特定形貌和释放曲线的化疗栓塞微球而铺平道路。此外，这个项目将会提供革命性的化疗栓塞微球以帮助建立用微球治疗包括肝癌和肺癌的各种疾病行业新标准。

17237316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17237316.value: A technique was developed and characterized for precise fabrication of uniform chemoembolization microparticles with effective and controllable encapsulation and release of drugs. The key is to replace the “top-down” bulk process conventionally used with a “bottom-up” approach of microfluidic double emulsion templates. The technique uses a microfluidic device to generate the required double emulsions, which exploits the microfluidics-offered capability of precisely handling small fluid volume, allows an accurate control over the formation of double emulsions and core-shell microparticles and thus enables the generation of highly uniform particles. The circular shape of the microfluidic capillary channels used, together with the thermodynamic principle of minimum interfacial energy, facilitates the formation of perfectly spherical droplets and particles whose size is invariable along all directions (geometrical isotropy). The shape and size of the fabricated particles, therefore, do not vary from particle to particle or from direction to direction in individual particles. The drug-loading into the particles is via encapsulation at the individual level, which is achieved by injecting the drug into each droplet, enabling a 100% drug-loading efficiency. The release of the drug can be precisely tuned by manipulating both the shell and core of the particle via tuning the microfluidic double emulsion templates.

17239016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17239016.value: The 2005 exchange rate reform has widened the upper and lower limit of the RMB exchange rate. This policy was seen by the global market as an initial step toward subsequent gradual appreciation of the RMB to reflect the accumulation of China’s huge trade surplus over the years. The expectation has led to influx of speculative funds into China, some of which might have gone into the property markets. The 1994 fiscal reform has reduced the local government’s the share of tax revenue but retain all revenue from land sales (land use right fee). Land sales revenue is classified as extra-budgetary fund. Local government has more freedom in using such fund. There is a strong incentive for local governments to sustain the property prices so that they can maintain or increase their income from land sales. This study examines the impact of the 2005 RMB exchange reform and the 1994 fiscal reform on property prices in China. Since China is a big country, the impacts of these two policies are unlikely to be uniform across the entire country. This study will investigate their differential impact on property markets in different regions of china. 2005年的匯率改革擴大了人民幣匯率的上限和下限。國際投資者一般預期這政策是人民幣的後續的漸進式升值的第一步，以反映中國多年來積累的巨額貿易順差。此一預期導致了大量投機熱錢流入中國，當中包括湧入房地產市場的游資。 1994年的財稅體制改革(税制改革)減少了地方政府在稅收收入中所佔的份額，但保留土地出讓收入全部（土地使用權費）。土地出讓收入被列為預算外收入。地方政府在運用該項收入有更大的靈活性。因此，地方政府有強烈的誘因維持樓價，以便他們能夠維持或增加預算外收入。 這項研究探討中國1994年財稅體制改革及2005年人民幣匯改對住房價格的影響，。由於中國是一個大國，這兩項政策的影響在全國各地不盡相同。本項目將集中研究這兩項政策對中國各地房地產市場的影響。

17239016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17239016.value: Using provincial panel data from 1999 through 2015, our empirical results suggest that fiscal independence measured by real per capita extra-budgetary revenue has a positive impact on real housing prices. This support the conjecture that local governments that rely more on extra-budgetary revenue are more likely to uphold housing prices using their monopoly power in the land market. However, distance from Beijing does not affect the impact of fiscal independence. Based on the same dataset, we found that the 2005 RMB exchange reform has an overall positive impact on the nationwide housing price trends. The results provide evidence that support the conjecture that the 2005 exchange rate reform has led to highly predictable medium to long term RMB appreciation, which has attracted influx of international hot money into China and fueled a housing price boom that cannot be easily tamed by market cooling measures implemented by central and local governments. The impact of the 2005 RMB exchange rate reform is not constant over time and across provinces. The impact is stronger when a province has experienced an increase in the RMB exchange rate and also in provinces with a more developed service sector.

17239016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17239016.value: The result of this study has raised the issue of sustainability of the land financing system adopted by local governments in China. The the local governments' reliance on land sales revenues has caused high housing prices. This has intensified the uneven distribution of wealth and income, which may lead social unrest and political instability. The incentive of the local government to maximize land sales revenue is a structural institutional issue that needs to be addressed. Further research on how to resolve this problem by institutional design would be an impactful area of study.

17239016.value: The 2005 exchange rate reform has widened the upper and lower limit of the RMB exchange rate. This policy was seen by the global market as an initial step toward subsequent gradual appreciation of the RMB to reflect the accumulation of China’s huge trade surplus over the years. The expectation has led to influx of speculative funds into China causing asset price inflation, include housing prices. The 1994 fiscal reform has reduced the local government’s the share of tax revenue but retain all revenue from land sales (land use right fee). Land sales revenue is classified as extra-budgetary fund. Local government has more freedom in using such fund. There is a strong incentive for local governments to sustain the housing prices so that they can maintain or increase their income from land sales. This study show s that the impact of the 2005 RMB exchange reform and the 1994 fiscal reform have driven up housing prices. Also, housing prices increased more in regions with a more developed service sector.

17245716.label: Project Objectives
17245716.value: To evaluate and extend the use of RDD as the abstract model of computations in hybrid FPGA-CPU clusters. To develop a high-level design and compilation framework for developing and deploying RDD processing applications on a hybrid FPGA-CPU cluster. 17245716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17245716.value: 當代的科學發現越來越依賴能高速處理大量非結構化數據的高性能計算設備。在很多重要的應用領域如機器學習和數據挖掘，研究者們利用可定制架構的計算設備多次的展示了FPGA-CPU混合可重構集群高效和高性能的特點。然而，達到期望的性能優勢需要針對應用進行繁重的軟硬件開發。這些開發工作即使在同一個​​應用領域的相關問題上也很難重用。 這個項目希望通過在FPGA-CPU混合可重構集群中引入彈性分佈式數據集（RDD）作為用來開發大規模並行數據處理應用的中間層計算模型來解決上面提到的生產力挑戰。 RDD的中間層可以讓使用者專注於把應用映射到RDD計算模型上，剩下的優化工作由底層的系統框架實時進行。把應用的映射和系統優化隔離減輕了應用的開發工作，同時讓系統級的優化工作可以在多個應用上重用。 選擇RDD的原因是它通過一系列的變換和動作為並行數據處理提供了函數式的抽象。這個項目將會探索在軟硬件混合系統中實現上述變換和動作所必需的理論和機制。 FPGA細粒度的可重構性與粗粒度的集群結構構成互補，這種純軟件的粗細混合粒度RDD並行處理將形成一種新的系統優化範式。 本項目提出的設計框架將會和當前流行的RDD處理的軟件實現Spark兼容。這樣大量已存在的軟件可能會很簡單的推動異構FPGA-CPU的應用開發，同時本項目所提出的加速系統也會通過FPGA自動提高現有的軟件性能。 為了輔助上述異構應用的開發，本項目需要開發一個允許用戶快速實現FPGA上RDD操作的編譯環境。智能的實時函數操作和FPGA的結合需要生成用來進行後期綁定操作的可重定位的可執行文件。最終數據集的處理工作將會由本項目所提出的可重構集群上的實時系統所調用，調度和管理。

17245716.label: Realisation of objectives
17245716.value: This project has successfully explored the idea of using FPGA-CPU cluster for distributed acceleration of computationally demanding tasks. The project set out to explore the use of resilient distributed datasets (RDD) as the basic computing model for such distributed operations, and has narrowed down into accelerating machine learning applications as its focus. In the early phase of the project, an attempt to accelerate Spark, which employed RDD as its underlying distributed computing model was made. Using SVM training as a case study, this early attempt successfully explored various tradeoffs involved while using FPGA in combination with CPU for acceleration tasks using the RDD model (Ho et al, 2017). The result from this early work concluded that while the basic RDD model was well-suited for modelling distributed computing tasks, they imposed significant challenges to the underlying computing machine due to the highly irregular data communication between tasks that execute in a distributed cluster. The large volume of irregular communications among computing nodes undermine the benefit brought by the acceleration of computational tasks with FPGAs. It was concluded that future work should devote efforts into accelerating data communications with the RDD execution model. Nevertheless, this early work has demonstrated the significant benefits of using FPGAs to accelerate distributed machine learning applications. For that, a distributed graph processing framework was developed, which employed the vertex-centric graph processing model for distributed computing. The resulting work, GraVF-M (Engelhardt and So, 2019), addressed a similar challenge of shuffling data in the RDD computing model. In this work, a high-level design and compilation framework using a Python-based language called Migen was developed, which automatically generated distributed computing structures that were optimized for the target platform. By formulating the distributed graph processing problem using the vertex-centric computing model, users only needed to supply the algorithm-specific kernels that described the operations of each graph node. Since all hardware were generated automatically, the GraVF-M framework was able to optimize the distributed design based on the actual hardware platform. Using a wide range of graph kernels as benchmark, GraVF-M demonstrated an effective processing throughput of up to 5.8GTEPS (billions of traversed edges per second) on a 4-FPGA system while achieving 94% of the performance limit of the target system. Furthermore, good scalability with respect to both problem size and in the number of FPGAs being used have also been demonstrated. In terms of computational efficiency, significant efforts have been devoted to the study of the tradeoffs between numerical accuracy, number representation and hardware implementation. This tradeoff is particularly important in the training process of modern machine learning algorithms, as demonstrated by our early SVM training acceleration effort using RDD. On the one hand, high numerical accuracy is desirable from an algorithmic design perspective because it is essential to ensure successful training in many scenarios. On the other hand, ensuring high numerical accuracy requires the use of complex datatypes such as single- and double-precision floating point representations, which are large and incur high computational latency. For efficient hardware implementations, fixed point arithmetic or low precision floating point numbers are preferred. To that end, a family of configurable hardware floating point units have been designed (Jaiswal and So, 2018, 2019). In this family of designs, configurable single-, double-, and quadruple -precision floating-point hardware units for add, subtract, multiplication and division have been proposed. With the configurability built-in, the same unit may be subdivided to perform multiple operations with reduced precision in parallel. Such ability to reuse the same hardware for different numerical precisions allows efficient use of hardware to accelerate applications where the numerical requirements may change during run time, such as for deep neural network training. In this series of works, not only have we demonstrated that such configurability was feasible even with the complex division operator, but they were highly-efficient in terms of operation per silicon area. In addition, we have developed an hardware-efficient and accurate non-linear function generator called NNCore (Ho and So, 2017). Based on the user provided numerical accuracy requirements, NNCore automatically produced the optimal hardware for the target FPGA platform using irregular piecewise linear approximation. A combination of lookup table and analytical computational techniques were employed to guarantee the necessary numerical accuracy without significantly increasing the size of the produced hardware. At single-precision setting, NNCore generated cores that consumed up to 65% fewer BRAMs, 63% fewer shift-registers, and ran at up to 2.2x the clock speed when compared with the state-of-the-art. Currently, NNCore supports generation of common non-linear functions employed in machine learning applications including arctan, tanh, sigmoid and their derivatives. In terms of FPGA overlay design, significant efforts have been devoted to the task of accelerating neural network inference. One of the major challenges from an application developer’s point of view is the ability to design, incorporate and produce efficient neural network accelerator rapidly. As a result, not only is the efficiency of an inference machine important, but the ability to produce accelerators that are customized to an application specific neural network is equally important. To address this need, a series of FPGA overlay designs that allow systematic production of neural network inference accelerators have been developed. In the work of FTDL (Shi et al, 2020), the inference operations with convolutional neural network (CNN) was accelerated using an FPGA-specific overlay. In this work, the cascading connections between digital signal processing (DSP) blocks of FPGAs were optimized to produce highly compact accelerators for CNNs. Furthermore, a double-pumping scheme was employed to ensure a balanced data transfer rate between the on-chip memory and the DSP blocks. As a result, FTDL achieved up to 7.7× higher performance and 1.9× more power-efficient than the state-of-the-art. In the work of E-LSTM (Shi et al, 2019), a highly-efficient accelerator framework for the challenging LSTM family of neural networks have been proposed. Unlike feedforward neural networks such as CNNs, the feedback paths in LSTM networks make them particularly challenging to accelerate with hardware. In this work, the sparsity of the LSTM networks was exploited to allow this family of challenging networks to be accelerated. With data compression and reorganization, the LSTM network inference operations were cast to a sparse matrix-sparse vector multiplication problem for which an efficient hardware SpM-SpV multiplier was designed. With the optimized operations, E-LSTM achieved up to 2.2x improvement in performance over existing designs. In the work of CSB-RNN (Shi et al, 2020), similar compression techniques using compressed sparse block (CSB) were employed to address the challenge of accelerating general RNN inference. In the work of CSB-RNN, the weight input RNN was similarly compressed and reordered into individual RNN cells. The individual RNN cells were further scheduled to run on a hierarchy of processing elements that were optimized to perform sparse matrix operations with the CSB coding. With experiments performed on 10 different benchmark RNNs, CSB-RNN was able to achieve 1.12×-12.57× lower latency and 3.53×-58.89× better power-efficiency when compared with the state-of-the-art. Furthermore, in terms of reducing inference latency, we have also developed a fully integrated and deeply pipelined architecture to perform single cell classification (Wang et al, 2021). By integrating computation with imaging frontend, we have achieved an ultra-low inference latency of 34.2 microsecond per cell image.

17245716.label: Major findings and research outcome
17245716.value: This project has demonstrated the performance and power-efficiency benefits of using a cluster of FPGAs to accelerate a wide range of machine learning applications from the perspective of computational model, design flow, as well as hardware implementations. In terms of computational model, we have studied the case of accelerating SVM training using a distributed cluster of FPGAs with the Spark framework that operated with the RDD model. We found that while the model fit very well for distributed parallel computation with FPGA accelerations, the irregular data communication among the processing nodes quickly became the performance bottleneck, which undermined the benefits brought by the FPGA accelerators (Ho et al, 2017). Besides, we have explored the vertex-centric graph processing model for distributed processing and found that it can be effectively leveraged for scalable distributed FPGA acceleration (Engelhardt and So, 2018, 2019). In terms of design flow and hardware implementation, multiple works have been done to accelerate machine learning inference operations. For FPGA overlay designs, we have developed FTDL (Shi et al, 2020), E-LSTM (Shi et al, 2019) and CSB-RNN (Shi et al, 2020) that efficiently accelerated inference operations of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), long-short term memory (LSTM) networks, as well as general recurring neural networks (RNNs), achieving superior performance and power-efficiency improvements over the state-of-the-arts. For practical applications, we have also developed an ultra-low latency cell image classification system (Wang et al, 2021). In terms of hardware design, a family of floating-point units that support configurable multi-precision floating point operations have been developed (Jaiswal and So, 2018, 2019). Furthermore, an efficient hardware non-linear function generator has been developed (Ho and So, 2019).

17245716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17245716.value: This project has identified an important challenge regarding data communication when accelerating applications using the RDD model. Similar to many large-scale distributed computing systems, communication and computation must be balanced to ensure optimal overall system performance. For the RDD computing model being studied, since extensive delayed computations have been incorporated into the underlying computing implementation, the communication pattern between different computing node becomes difficult to predict and to optimize for. As a result, while FPGAs and other accelerators may be useful to accelerate some of the computations on each compute node, the unpredictable and heavy data communication between compute nodes greatly undermines the benefits of accelerating computations alone. For future work, more emphasis should be placed on the integration between compute and communication for such distributed model. One potential research direction is to explore the use of FPGAs to perform real-time in-network processing (INP) in combination with other acceleration techniques on each compute node.

17245716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17245716.value: Field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) are advanced integrated circuits that allow their functions to be reconfigured during run time. Using such special abilities, researchers have demonstrated the advantages of accelerating software programs by construction specialized hardware system optimized for the target program. Leveraging their reconfigurability, this project explored the use of multiple FPGAs to accelerate machine learning applications running on distributed parallel computing systems. The main conclusion resulting from this study is that in a distributed computing system, data communication among different computing nodes remains the major performance bottleneck. To accelerate large scale parallel applications, the performance of the entire system, including both the compute operations in a compute node and the data communication infrastructure, must be considered holistically. FPGAs are useful for such whole system acceleration. FPGAs should be used not only in accelerating computation in a compute node, but they should also be used to facilitate migration of data in the communication network. Future research should devote efforts studying the benefit of using FPGAs for in-network processing (INP) in which computations are carried out inside the communication network while data are being transferred.

17246116.value: to develop an innovative solution-processed fabrication strategy for high-aspect-ratio sub-micron metal-mesh transparent electrodes embedded in flexible and stretchable substrates to investigate electrical, optical, and mechanical properties on embedded metal-mesh transparent electrodes and their scaling behaviors to evaluate the performance of embedded metal-mesh transparent electrodes in flexible and stretchable resistive heating and photovoltaic devices

17246116.label: Realisation of objectives
17246116.value: All objectives have been achieved. 1) We have developed an innovative solution-processed fabrication strategy for high-aspect-ratio sub-micron metal-mesh transparent electrodes embedded in flexible and stretchable substrates. This fabrication strategy includes lithographic patterning of mesh or network patterns on an insulating mask coated on a conductive substrate, electrochemical deposition for metallization of the mesh or network patterns, and imprint transfer of the metalized patterns to flexible and stretchable substrates. High conductivity and high transmission have been achieved using this strategy. 2) We investigated the electrical, optical, and mechanical properties of the fabricated metal-mesh electrodes using various modeling methods. Finite element analysis was done on metal mesh under stretching conditions to study their fracture and fatigue properties, and how these properties change with the mesh geometry and sizes. Finite-difference time-domain modeling using Lumerical software was used to understand the scaling behavior of optical transmittance on the sub-micron metal mesh electrodes. We have also studied the scaling behavior of the electrical conductivity of metal mesh with various geometric parameters. 3) We have demonstrated a number of various applications that are enabled using our metal-mesh transparent electrodes to evaluate their performance in actual devices. We fabricated flexible and stretchable electroluminescent lighting devices, thin-film heating devices, perovskite solar cell devices, etc. Our electrodes contribute to the impressive flexibility and stretchability of these devices. Overall, the successful completion of our work established a solid ground for us to further explore more complex fabrication processes and device applications and also facilitate the commercialization of our technology.

17246116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17246116.value: 1. Invented a fabrication process that combines lithographic and templated electrodeposition with imprint transfer for fabricating high-performance flexible and stretchable metal-mesh electrodes; 2. Understood electrical, optical, and mechanical properties on flexible and stretchable metal-mesh electrodes and their scaling behaviors using various modeling methods; 3. Demonstrated multiples applications of our metal-mesh electrodes in solar cells, flexible heaters, flexible and stretchable displays 4. In addition to the planned objectives, we have further extended the fabrication methods towards nanoscale metallic devices and demonstrated flexible plasmonic sensors fabricated using the methods developed in this project. Most of the above findings have been wrapped up and published in prestigious academic journals, including Advanced Functional Materials, Journal of Material Chemistry C, Advanced Optical Materials, ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, etc., and presented in main-stream international conferences.

17246116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17246116.value: Based on the achievements in this project, more development towards practical applications and commercialization is promising. A cost-effective, scalable manufacturing process for highly conductive and highly transparent metal-mesh conductors is the key for the new generation of consumer electronic devices. Our method has proven to be promising and superior to many existing methods. Therefore, we have founded a start-up company, Flectrode Technology Limited, and received sizeable private investment to mass-produce metal-mesh electrodes based on our technology. The PI has also been awarded an Innovation and Technology Fund project to carry out follow-up research based on this GRF project towards industrial applications. Academically, the current project can be further developed towards new patterning methods for narrower linewidth, denser mesh. Templates formed using self-assembled nanowires, or cracks, are possible towards this direction. The electroless deposition may also be useful in the metallization step. It’s possible to extend the current two-dimensional mesh structures into three-dimensional functional structures using our method for new applications. The course of action towards above directions include: 1) wrapping up existing results and publishing on leading academic journals to generate more impact of this work; 2) pushing forward for commercializing our technology through collaboration with industrial partners; 3) applying for new research grants for the development of new improved processing steps and exploring new applications.

17246116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17246116.value: Modern consumer electronic devices demand high-performance transparent conductors as the electrodes for displays, sensors, touch screens, smart windows, etc. Conventional indium tin oxide materials face significant challenges in meeting the high requirement of emerging electronic devices, many of which are demanding flexibility and even stretchability. In this project, we have explored a novel type of embedded metal-mesh-based transparent electrodes for burgeoning flexible and stretchable optoelectronic devices. We developed innovative approaches to large-area fabrication of embedded metal-mesh transparent electrodes with sub-micron linewidth and reduced gap size, investigated many important properties of these metal-mesh electrodes, and demonstrated how these improved embedded metal-mesh transparent electrodes can enhance the performance of flexible and stretchable optoelectronic applications. Our research outcomes have led to one issued patent and a spin-off company for further commercialization.

17246416.label: Project Objectives
17246416.value: Formulation of a tensor-based MIMO Volterra series -- The series is composed of Volterra kernels of increasing order. From second order up, the tensor mode product notion applies to elegantly represent the effect of all cross terms. Even more, once the kernel core is shaped into a tensor, it eludes the matrix framework to enjoy all available tensor decomposition/synthesis algorithms that often result in highly efficient computation and storage. Development of efficient MIMO Volterra series modeling and simulation tools -- Starting with a nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) or a set of blackbox input-output samples, the high-order Volterra kernels are calculated or identified for subsequent simulation tasks such as model order reduction or signal integrity analysis. To provide working computer codes and benchmarks for nonlinear MIMO system modeling and simulation -- The best way to promote and verify the effectiveness of the developed algorithms is to make them available to the public. The algorithms are then refined and improved, and more examples can be worked out through collective talent and effort. The long-term impact of this project is warranted by the ever-increasing need of accurate nonlinear system modeling in EDA, as well as the intense heat in tensor-based algorithmic research. We expect that the theoretic investigation and numerical implementations of tensor-based MIMO Volterra series, due to its generality, can also be extended to other engineering fields involving nonlinear systems. By coding the tensor-based MIMO Volterra algorithms and examples in the popular Matlab/Octave languages and making them freely available, researchers can easily verify their ideas and chip designers can readily embed the routines into conventional EDA flows and enjoy the speedup of the design cycle. Through the execution of tasks in the project, students, researchers and practitioners are also benefited with the breadth (general tensor knowledge) and depth (specialization into Volterra modeling algorithms) of knowledge necessary to contribute to the academia and industry. The advanced content of the project can also spin off into postgraduate courses and seminars at HKU to provide interdisciplinary training in advanced multi-linear tensor algebra, numerical algorithms, nonlinear theory and circuit modeling.

17246416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17246416.value: 由於非線性系統的複雜特性和高階信號乘積項的相互作用，非線性系統的準確模擬一直是電子設計自動化（EDA）研究中的一個棘手的問題。然而，隨著混合信號電路和其底層的非線性器件（如混頻器和振盪器）的快速普及，對這些模塊快速和穩健的模擬和仿真成為了必須。在近似非線性系統這個領域有一個長期存在的工具是Volterra級數。由於對輸入波形歷史的依賴，它可以被理解為是帶記憶效應的泰勒級數與記憶效應。然而，傳統Volterra級數只允許標量輸入信號，而不允許矢量輸入。這阻礙了其在更常見的多輸入多輸出（MIMO）系統中的應用。一種解決方法是分別處理每個輸入輸出對，但是這給MIMO非線性建模帶來了很大的計算負擔，並且無法利用可能的輸入輸出中的相關關系，更不用說由於其指數增長的複雜度，在實踐中能使用的Volterra級數至多只能到達3階。所有這些實際考慮限制了基於Volterra級數的建模與仿真大多只能應用於弱非線性系統。 近來，在數值代數領域中出現了利用張量來處理高維數據的的研究熱潮。簡而言之，張量是將標量（0維），矢量（1維），和矩陣（2維）擴展到一般d（≥3）維的數據結構。將高維數據表示成張量，並對其進行類似矩陣中的有效分解，已經取得了巨大的進展。通過張量運算，我們第一次發現Volterra的標量輸入限制是代數性的，並且我們可以通過張量非常自然地將Volterra級數推廣到相對應的MIMO系統。 因此，該項目有雙重目標，即“填補”Volterra級數在MIMO應用上的空缺，以及在此框架中研發有效的建模和仿真算法。為了實現這些目標，我們制定了三個主要目標： 1）設計一個基於張量的解析MIMO Volterra級數及其相應的公式。 2）推導高效的基於非線性常微分方程的MIMO Volterra級數的算法微分方程或完全黑盒子方法。 3）開發適用於非線性MIMO系統建模和仿真的計算機代碼和例子。 事實上，我們提出的基於張量-MIMO Volterra級數不僅僅是一個術語上的改變。它同時帶來了Volterra級數的一個全新的解析公式，並開啟了一系列高效張量算法以克服傳統方法中的高緯度詛咒。該PI和Co-I合作多年，是促進基於張量算法在EDA領域中應用的開拓者。該項目的研究成果將具備高度的理論和實用價值，並滿足當今尖端混合信號電路設計對有效的非線性建模與仿真算法的需求。

17246416.label: Realisation of objectives
17246416.value: In short, this project is completed successfully with all objectives fulfilled (and actually to an extent well beyond their original scopes). In particular, 6 top-tier journal papers have been published focusing on theory and algorithms, plus another 7 top-tier conference papers with emphasis on the application. Below we list the major research activities alongside each objective. Objective #1. Formulation of a tensor-based multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) Volterra series -- For the FIRST TIME in the literature our team has worked out a natural generalization of the Volterra series (previously restricted to only single-input single-output or SISO systems) to its MIMO counterpart. The key is to recognize that higher order Volterra kernels are intrinsically symmetric higher order tensors, and that higher order convolutions in the nonlinear I/O response evaluation are simply cast into tensor mode product operations. This exciting new framework then allows nonlinear Volterra series modeling of the general MIMO systems, and extends the traditional (restrictive) single-input single-output (SISO) setting to its most general & usable form. Objective #2. Development of efficient MIMO Volterra series modeling and simulation tools --Once the MIMO Volterra series formulation is in place, the next step is to compute entries of its Volterra kernels. These kernel entries can either be obtained analytically from the system nonlinear ordinary differential equations, or alternatively from the I/O samples of the nonlinear system through measurement or simulation. In this regard, highly effective kernel identification algorithms have been developed by our team based on the economic alternating least squares (ALS) approach. A novel extension by Kalman filtering further improves the robustness of the kernel entry identification process, even under noisy I/O conditions. Objective #3. To provide working computer codes and benchmarks for nonlinear MIMO system modeling and simulation -- Matlab and Octave codes have been archived and provided for many test cases in nonlinear circuit modeling and simulation. The list of available codes are archieved under https://www.eee.hku.hk/~kimb/software.html and https://sites.google.com/view/kim-batselier/code Objective #4. Long-term impact -- The successes of the above three objectives then directly contributes to this goal which is an integration and natural consequence of the aforementioned techniques and results. One highlight is that our tensor-train input-output modeling has led to an interesting and exciting application in machine learning, in which our team have derived a first-of-its-kind parallelized tensor train learning of polynomial classifiers to be used in neural network classifiers.

17246416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17246416.value: We are the first and pioneering team to propose tensor-based modeling of Volterra series (nonlinear) multiple-input multiple-output systems. Specifically, our work largely extends the traditional, restrictive single-input single-output Volterra series modeling of nonlinear systems. It turns out this approach, besides its theoretical advancement from SISO to MIMO modeling, is also numerically and computationally efficient, making our framework both theoretically sound and practically useful for nonlinear system capturing and simulation. The values are reflected in the high number of high-quality publications generated from this project. It is important to note here that a BONUS outcome has resulted from the project, namely, we discovered that a neural network can readily be "tensorized" into a tensor network used in the MIMO Volterra series formulation. As such, the techniques and algorithms arising from our project have been utilized to train a polynomial classifier in machine learning with good results, leading to a journal publication in the IEEE Trans. on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, also included to this report. Another exciting application of our tensor-based modeling is in image completion, work is on-going along this line and promising results are already coming out.

17246416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17246416.value: The tensor-train-based multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) modeling is in fact highly generic and versatile for modeling nonlinear input-output behavior. We are exploiting and expanding its use to beyond circuit modeling. Two particular directions are in machine learning and imaging, which have already resulted in top journal & conference publications in their respective fields.

17248216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17248216.value: Resilient and smart communities underpin the success of modern society as human nature is facing unprecedented challenges and uncertainties caused by changing climate, high-speed urbanization and increasing globalization. The failure of any system in the built environment may cascade to other interdependent infrastructure systems which could lead to disruptions and/or catastrophic effects to a community if not the entire city or country. Community resilience has been recognized and adopted as a foundation for developing pragmatic regional or national resilience strategies and operationalizing resilience measures. However, due to the complexities and multi-faceted characteristics of modern communities, it is a challenging task to evaluate, monitor and track the progress of resilience building efforts; compare the potentials and pitfalls of resilience strategies; and prioritize the resilience measures. Existing idiosyncratic resilience frameworks, indicators and modeling approaches cannot adequately tackle the community resilience problems in a holistic and reliable manner. An ensemble approach being applied as transdisciplinary research platform to study complex adaptive systems may open up new ways for modeling community resilience. This research aims to develop a multi-paradigm based framework to enable communities in Hong Kong leveraging the existing resilience methodologies, analytical process and knowledge to improve the planning and execution of resilience programs in the built environment. The results should help Hong Kong moving towards resilient, smart and sustainable urban development. The different components of the proposed research, viz. literature review, interview, case study, focus group meeting and Delphi study, will unveil the strengths and challenges of the current practices of community resilience and smart infrastructures within a community. A workshop will be convened to devise a set of community resilience metrics. An ensemble-based framework consisting of the metrics, a demonstration resilience evaluation ensemble model and a knowledge-based resilience decision-making workflow model will be developed. The framework will be validated through prototype development and by piloting with two representative types of communities in Hong Kong, i.e. public housing estate and new town. The research would not only help lay a solid foundation for Hong Kong’s urban resilience and sustainable development through the establishment of more resilient and smarter communities, it should also contribute significantly to the existing resilience research and practices by providing a multi-paradigm framework for community resilience management, formulating a multi-dimensional community resilience indicator model, unfolding the need for holistic and integrated solutions to operationalize the resilience concepts, and unveiling the benefits and challenges of implementing the holistic and integrated community resilience solutions.

17248216.label: Realisation of objectives
17248216.value: Objective 1: To review the current community resilience practices and their strengths and weaknesses (100% realized) A desktop study was carried out with relevant literatures and guidelines on community resilience being comprehensively reviewed. Experts were interviewed to examine the role of integrated infrastructure asset management in resilient infrastructure management context; vulnerability analysis in infrastructure systems; hazard or disruption delineation; restoration of failed components in infrastructure systems; and performance metrics for assessing infrastructure resilience. Case study was carried out to unveil the infrastructure resilience analytics processes, and an open source tool Ergo v4.0.0 was used to examine the analytics workflow formulated with the proposed framework to assess the resilience of the water utility network. In addition, aged high-rise residential building and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area were used as case studies to understand the aspects of community resilience and the regional infrastructure resilience within city clusters respectively. Objective 2: To identify essential built environment systems and components sustaining a community and conduct interdependency and cascading impact analysis (100% realized) To understand the preparedness of those critical built environment systems in Hong Kong for resilience, the electricity; road and railway; water-related sectors by investigating their plans for reducing any potential risks and increasing the reliability, vulnerability and robustness. Experts were invited to share their opinions on the critical built environment systems according to the policies, strategies and objectives; condition monitoring and performance assessment; risk analysis and criticality identification; operation, maintenance, capital investment plans; information system / database; and human resources. Survey was carried out to uncover the strengths and weaknesses of each of those aspects. Interdependency and cascading impact analyses were carried out based on the stormwater drainage and road sectors. Objective 3: To devise a set of resilience metrics for communities in developed high-density cities (100% realized) Based on the findings of the preceding research stages in particular the information collected from domain experts, a set of resilience metrices for community resilience was formulated. Acknowledging that the resilience analysis concerns the dynamic process of system performance before, during and after disruptive events, an overall metric would constitute an indispensable ingredient to deliver the terminal representation of time-varying system performance. The metrices involve interrelated dimensions, which cover the technical, organizational, social and economic aspects. By referring to the literatures and published guidelines, he research team then identified representative performance metrics for each of the four dimensions in the metrices. Besides, the class definitions were derived to describing the relationship with other interdependent infrastructure systems. Objective 4: To develop an ensemble framework to facilitate communities conducting resilience initiatives and making informed decisions towards continuous improvement (100% realized) Based on the findings of the preceding stages, an ensemble resilience decision framework was developed. At this stage, the research team developed a master data management strategy which aligns with the existing policy and strategy of an organization or a city to implement the infrastructure asset management and smart city initiatives; established the master data management metrics and incorporated them into the hierarchy of infrastructure asset management performance measures and metrics; derived an information governing mechanism; defined the structure of the existing infrastructure asset operators to create a cross-departmental organizations to orchestrate the master data management initiatives; formulated an agreed master data lifecycle management process; deployed a master data management system being developed in-house and integrated the master data management system into an organization’s overall information architecture; and improved the master data management framework through continuous capability assessment, deliberate extension and upgrade of the initial master data management programs. Objective 5: To implement a big data enabled software prototype system based on the proposed ensemble framework for community built environment resilience (100% realized) With the developed ensemble resilience decision framework, the research team integrated the building information model and geographic information system. A prototype system was then built using the data of one of the urban flooding blackspots in Hong Kong – Wanchai. In the prototype system, data pertinent to the alignment the road network and stormwater pipes was captured and represented in ArcGIS. On the other hand, the design details of the road network, stormwater drainage system, and design of buildings near the commonly reported flooding areas were stored in the building information model. A feature manipulation engine was employed to facilitate the interoperability of data between the geographic information system and building information model. Data pertaining to the weather condition was solicited from the Hong Kong Observatory. The data collected forms the basis of the big data enabled software prototype system. Finally, the InfoWorks and VISSIM platforms were integrated into the big data enable software prototype to conduct flooding and traffic simulations and analyses respectively. Objective 6: To validate the resilience metrics, the ensemble framework and the software prototype (100% realized) The resilience metrics, ensemble resilience decision framework, big data enabled software prototype system were verified for their relevancy, practicality and reliability. Wanchai district of Hong Kong, which has been frequently affected by urban flooding, was identified as the study region. To examine the reliability of the developed big data ensembled model on complex densely populated old district like Wanchai, the disruptions to the road network brought by interdependent stormwater drainage system was scrutinized. By obtaining the physic-based data related to the road network and stormwater drainage system and fed into the big data enabled software prototype system under different urban flooding conditions, results were generated to determine the model robustness. The simulation findings were then presented to relevant stakeholders for validation and refinement to the model was made according to their comments.

17248216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17248216.value: A multisector resilience framework has been developed to integrate the lifecycle information of various infrastructure systems; facilitate the processes of diverse infrastructure systems to be integrated; delineate the interdependency of related infrastructure systems; and use the consolidate information solicited from interdependent infrastructure systems to generate resilience decisions (Journal 3). From that, an analytical workflow for resilient infrastructure assessment and management model has been identified (Journal 2), while the information requirement including the classes and relationships of sources of information have been defined (Journal 5). A master data management schema has been designed and its interaction with interdependent infrastructure systems has been examined. Information pertaining to the infrastructure systems serves to enable their performance be measured under normal and extreme conditions (Journal 1). To facilitate analysis, the resilience analysis boundary has been set and its interaction with the resilience management cycle has been established (Journal 4). To address the limitations of risk-based disaster analysis, a physics-based approach which focuses on the topological network has been put forwarded to ensemble interdependent civil infrastructure systems resilience analysis through the elicitation of domain knowledge to depict the operating state of the road network and stormwater drainage system and their relationships (Journal 4). Acknowledging the difficulties of capturing all necessary physical knowledge to portray certain heterogeneous infrastructure networks, an ensemble model which integrates the physics-based approach with a data-driven approach is developed to help demystify the failure propagation among interdependent infrastructure systems (Journal 7). A concise and generic framework has been devised to orchestrate ‘infrastructure’, ‘approach’ and ‘interface’ to enable infrastructure failures be investigated. The framework first strives to understand the target infrastructures and requirement, and it then selects suitable approaches to model the failure of infrastructure systems (Journal 7). To address the issue of resources prioritization in the pre-disruption mitigation process, a federated approach has been proposed to assess the pre-event socio-technical community resilience (Journal 6). A socio-technical community resilience ranking can be generated based on the results assembled from the topological-based evaluation and physics-based performance simulation to improve community’s hazard preparedness (Journal 6). Through the physics-based approach, the overall transport network performance of ex-ante and ex-post flooding events can be identified and adaptation strategies can be put forwarded (Journal 4). The results are further improved by the integrated data-driven and physics-based approaches as it allows for the heterogeneities of individual be retained and explored as demonstrated in the case results (Journal 7).

17248216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17248216.value: The physics-based approach adopted could better capture the micro effects. Therefore, further research should dynamically integrate the hydrodynamic stormwater model and traffic flow model to investigate the impact on the road transport system during the course of node overflow and induced flooding event, and the system-wide traffic impacts shall be evaluated according to the changing magnitude of flooding. Parameters calibration and results verification are challenging for rare disruptive events because there are limited historic data. Operational data should be accumulated through the real-time sensors or online citizen reporting system. With that, error correction algorithms can be developed to calibrate the controlling engineering parameters used in the physics-based approach. The ensemble infrastructure resilience framework could be extended to study various types of infrastructures (e.g. power, gas, oil, water, transportation, telecommunication, healthcare, and commercial facilities), as it provides great compatibility and flexibility to be exploited for the investigation of the interdependencies amongst these infrastructures. Further development can also be extended to other modeling approaches. For example, infrastructure-specific physical models should be built to characterize infrastructure failures. Other data-driven methods, e.g. Bayes-related methods, operational techniques, hidden Markov chain, key-linkages analysis, etc. can also be harnessed for depicting the failures of interdependent infrastructures.

17248216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17248216.value: An ensemble resilience framework has been developed using the data driven and physics-based approaches. The framework has filled the research gap of using a unified platform for investigating the cascading failures of heterogeneous independent critical infrastructure systems in the community. Through the ensemble resilience framework, the critical failure patterns including the hotspot areas, high incident time, and potential consequences of any infrastructure systems and the cascading impacts like level of performance degradation being brought to another interdependent infrastructure network can be systematically and accurately predicted. The ensembled resilience framework also allows for pre-event community resilience assessment. With that, policy and decision-makers as well as community leaders can clearly delineate which are the most affected communities so that scarce resources can be directed to the prioritized communities during the pre-disruption mitigation process in order to improve the hazard preparedness. The ensembled resilience framework is applicable to different types of hazards. More importantly, policy and decision-makers can define the potential hazards that could threaten the community and thus performance various simulations to predict the failure patterns and cascading impacts to the community so that suitable measures can be put in place to improve the resilience of the community against future hazards.

17249616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17249616.value: In the built environment, bacteria and virus particles can transfer from/to hands when we touch an inanimate surface (fomite). A substantial amount of measured data exists for the transfer rate of various microbes, though in most experiments the parameters that are thought to drive the mechanics of the process have not been measured. Although the fomite route is known to transmit diseases, the mechanisms of contact microorganism transfer have not yet been explored. Such lack of understanding makes it difficult to predict the efficiency of microbe transfer for new surfaces, pathogens and contact types. Our new hypothesis is that contact microorganism transfer involves basic processes of trapping, relocating and choosing, each of which can be described by adapting the well-developed theories of contact mechanics and particle-surface adhesion. In analog with the contact thermal/electrical transfer, we propose to name it as “contact particle transfer”. For two contacting surfaces, the real contact area is much smaller than the nominal area. The relocation or movement of particles on both contacting surfaces impacts on the particle distribution on the valleys and summits of the asperities. Only trapped particles within the real contact areas have a chance to transfer. The transfer of a particle from a surface to another requires its detachment from the donating surface and subsequent adhesion to the receiving surface. Both detachment and adhesion are the effect of major forces (van der Waals and capillary forces) acting between the trapped particles and each of the surfaces. If the resultant adhesion force is greater to one surface than the other, then the particle detaches from the less attractive surface, and chooses to adhere to the less repulsive surface. In our preliminary study, the above proposed mechanisms are shown to predict well the trend of contact transfer rate over a wide range of roughness. We have developed/proposed complementary theoretical and experimental methodologies for a systematic investigation. Our theoretical approach uses existing theory of contact mechanics, skin micro-tribology and cell adhesion to describe the basic processes of contact particle transfer. Our new experimental set up can reproduce both static and dynamic touch, with the forces and action duration accurately controlled and measured, with all relevant parameters properly characterized. Our work will provide a prediction model for obtaining the contact transfer rate for new pathogens and surfaces. 17249616.label: Realisation of objectives
17249616.value: We shall report our work for each individual tasks as in the original proposal. Objective 1 was achieved with Tasks 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4, Objective 2 with Task 1.2-1.4, and Task 2.1-2.3, and Objective 3 with Task 2.4. Task 1.1 Existing data of properties of surfaces and microorganisms, and contact transfer rates We systematically reviewed and analyzed the existing data of contact transfer as well as the available morphological, mechanical, physical, chemical and biological parameters of human skin, commonly touched surfaces and virus/bacteria particles. The data was tabulated and analyzed to identify the major dominating parameters of particle contact transfer for mechanism study. Significant errors have existed in experimental data in existing studies. These data are used for two purposes, identifying the dominating factors that affect the transfer rate and validate our newly developed model. Thirteen factors were quantified or determined for each microbial transfer rate data in these studies. Principal component analysis and stepwise multiple linear regression were used to identify the most significant factors that correlate with microbial transfer rate. Output: Zhao P, et al 2019. Building and Environment. 158, 28-38. Task 1.2 and 1.3 Static contact transfer of spherical and rod particles, and modeling dynamic (sliding) contact transfer of spherical and other particles We developed a new trap and choice theory which has also resulted in a prediction simple model for the static contact transfer of particles. This was developed in analog with the adhesive friction, wear, and thermal/electrical contact transfer. The contact particle transfer from fomite to skin is assumed proportional to the ratio of real area and nominal contact area. Particles can be transferred on a surface network by touch. We also evaluated the equilibrium of particle distribution between each pair of surfaces, and developed and tested a new concept of transitivity of particle distribution at equilibrium. When the surfaces were touched, the particle transfer between the contacted surfaces reached equilibrium experimentally. At equilibrium, a rubber surface always adhered more particles when in contact with other tested surfaces, while relatively few particles adhered to the steel surface. The contact parameters influenced the particle transfer speed but had no significant effect on the final equilibrium state. Particle distribution between surfaces was attributed to the variation in adhesion force on each surface. An inherent equilibrium of particles existed between any pair of surfaces, independent of contacts. The equilibrium was approximately transitive, implying that the particles reached relative stability as contact occurred in a surface network, even when some surface pairs never made direct contact. We developed a new model to evaluate the van der Waals force between a rough surface and a deposited particle. In the new model, a surface was not modelled with any given geometrics, and no artificially defined coefficients were involved, but with a concise function, where the particle-surface force was derived inversely proportional to the particle’s normal position on the surface. Atomic force microscopy experiments were performed with a novel method to validate the new theory. A target particle was used to scan an area of a surface twice to obtain a height map and a force map. Data of the measured particle’s normal positions and adhesion forces were fitted with the derived function. The new model reveals the effect of surface roughness on van der Waals force from a completely new perspective and significantly simplifies the process of force evaluation. Two papers published Zhao P, et al (2018). Building and Environment, 143, 461-472. Zhao P and Li Y. Colloids and Surfaces A: Physicochemical and Engineering Aspects. 585, 2020 Task 1.4 Consideration of the surface properties of microorganisms We explored the effect of surface properties of microorganisms. It turned out that the surface properties of microorganisms are not very important in our context, as shown in a large of number of tests, as well as the collected 21 existing studies. The measured microbial transfer rate and the corresponding applied parameters were analyzed. We also modeled the microbial transfer with four different surface touch behaviors, including a single touch, sequential touches, repeated touches and a touch with rubbing. The effects of surface roughness, touch force, inoculation volume and number of touches, on the microbial transfer rate were found to dominate. Experiment results with smaller standard deviations than the existing data and a higher consistency to the model prediction demonstrated that the new model worked very well, and controlling the governing factors during the tests are important. Task 2.1 Preparation of test surfaces and skins We selected and tested a number and ranges of surfaces for the reliable contact particle transfer measurement as planned. The physical and chemical properties of these surfaces were measured. Task 2.2 Designing and evaluating the experimental set up for surface touching tests We have constructed our second generation new touch machine, followed the prototype of the set-up. It turned out that the planned construction of the small chamber is not possible with the budget. Fortunately we have obtained a RGC CRF project in which a relative large climate chamber is in the process of construction with much wider environment conditions and better control at a cost of HK$500,000. The entire touching machine was placed into this chamber chamber with controlled temperature and humidity conditions (0-35oC and 10-90% RH). A major paper is in preparation Zhao P, Leung A and Li Y. Microbial transfer via surface touch. Manuscript in revision. Task 2.3 Test, analyses, comparison with and evaluation of the proposed theory New measurement of transfer rate during surface touch were carried out using the new touching machine. In addition to the four significant factors identified from the data analysis, i.e. donor wetness, microbial transfer direction, donor roughness and existence of rub five other factors were also investigated, including three factors that have received wide attention, i.e. surface material, bacteria species and touch force, and two factors that are newly found to be significant, i.e. medium of bacterial suspension and bacterial growth phase. The microbial transfer rate was quantified by PCR. Task 2.4 Application and test of the developed prediction method in analyzing outbreaks Our purpose here was to apply and test the developed new transfer models in a fomite transmission model to simulate three reported inflight/hospital norovirus outbreaks and also develop new understanding of infection control measures. It turned out, as expected, that the accurate transfer data is only one of the essential data for analyzing the fomite-dominated outbreaks such as for noroviruses. Other data such as dose-response parameters are also essential. We have published a few papers using the developed model, but only two cited the support of this grant, and in others we only acknowledged the support of another related RGC GRF project (No 17211615).
