17249616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17249616.value: For the first time, we identified the contact particle transfer phenomenon in analog with the contact thermal/electrical transfer, and developed a new theory. The theory has been validated using extensive experimental data using a new touch machine and also those in the literature – a total of 21 studies (Zhao et al., 2019, Building and Environment, 158, 28-38). The contact microorganism transfer involves trapping, relocating and choosing, each of which can be described by adapting the well-developed theories of contact mechanics and particle-surface adhesion in contact mechanics, skin micro-tribology and cell adhesion. For two contacting surfaces, the real contact area is much smaller than the nominal area. The relocation or movement of particles on both contacting surfaces impacts on the particle distribution on the valleys and summits of the asperities. Only trapped particles within the real contact areas have a chance to transfer. The transfer of a particle from a surface to another requires its detachment from the donating surface and subsequent adhesion to the receiving surface. Both detachment and adhesion are the effect of major forces (van der Waals and capillary forces) acting between each trapped particle and each of the surfaces (Zhao and Li, 2019, Colloids and Surfaces A, 585, 124096). If the resultant adhesion force is greater to one surface than the other, then the particle detaches from the less attractive surface, and chooses to adhere to the less repulsive surface. Additionally, we also evaluated the equilibrium of particle distribution between each pair of surfaces, and developed and tested a new concept of transitivity of particle distribution at equilibrium (Zhao et al., 2018, Building and Environment, 143, 461-472). When the surfaces were touched, the particle transfer between the contacted surfaces reached equilibrium experimentally. At equilibrium, a rubber surface always adhered more particles when in contact with other tested surfaces, while relatively few particles adhered to the steel surface. The contact parameters influenced the particle transfer speed but had no significant effect on the final equilibrium state. An inherent equilibrium of particles existed between any pair of surfaces, independent of contacts. The theory has important implications to disease transfer, and developing new methods for particle transfer rate (Zhao and Li, 2019, Journal of Applied Microbiology). We applied our new understanding to develop a paired hand/surface hygiene idea (Lei et al., Indoor Air, 2019) and also improved intervention for MRSA (Xiao et al., Building and Environment, 161, p.106246).

17249616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17249616.value: The contact particle transfer phenomenon is newly identified, and many knowledge gaps exist. One can find numerous textbooks on contact thermal/electrical transfer, which indirectly reveal the amount of work that need to be done. Note that the particles differ from electrons, and the size effect in contact thermal/electrical transfer is negligible, but not in contact particle transfer. The importance of particle transfer phenomenon to fomite transmission of diseases and particle exposure due to the dermal route suggests the huge potential for further theoretical and analytical studies. The potential application of the new theory in developing new technologies for surface transmission control, new surface sampling methods, and new infection intervention can be significant based on our preliminary work. We have recognized this potential during the early stage of the project, and new CRF grant was secured to explore the virus transfer in the surface contact network in a city like Hong Kong. We are considering new proposals to RGC, ITF and elsewhere.

17249616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17249616.value: Bacteria and virus particles can transfer from/to hands when we touch an inanimate surface (fomite). A substantial amount of measured data exists for the transfer rate of various microbes, though in most experiments the parameters that are thought to drive the mechanics of the process have not been measured. Although the fomite route is known to transmit diseases, the mechanisms of contact microorganism transfer remained unknown before our study. For the first time, we identified the contact particle transfer phenomenon in analog with the contact thermal/electrical transfer, and developed a new theory. The contact microorganism transfer involves basic processes of trapping, relocating and choosing, each of which can be described by adapting the well-developed theories of contact mechanics and particle-surface adhesion. In analog with the contact thermal/electrical transfer, we propose to name it as “contact particle transfer”. Our new experimental set up can reproduce both static and dynamic touch, with the forces and action duration accurately controlled and measured, with all relevant parameters properly characterized. Our work has provided a prediction model for obtaining the contact transfer rate for new pathogens and surfaces. It also sheds light on development of new control methods for the fomite transmission of diseases.

17250116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17250116.value: Around the world governments are setting out ambitious environmental targets and endorsing ever more comprehensive visions of sustainable development, including environmental, social and economic goals coupled with new legislation and regulations. Within the built environment policy makers and key stakeholders increasingly emphasise the importance of buildings for national carbon reduction targets and for sustainable development. Hong Kong is no exception and sustainability, and particularly carbon and energy reduction, is high on the political agenda as evidenced by the establishment of ‘The Steering Committee on the Promotion of Green Building’ in 2013. This is not surprising as the buildings are commonly held to be responsible for more than 40% of overall carbon emissions. The building industry is clearly accountable for important sources of environmental damage and is an industry with the potential for vast improvements. Past attempts to make the building process more sustainable have led to the introduction of a variety of new or improved technologies, materials, processes, and management tools into firm and project settings. In broad terms, these attempts have led to advances in some areas, but they have had very little impact in many others. The overall progress towards sustainable practices has been repeatedly criticised for being slow, patchy and failing to have any significant impact; with a chasm existing between practice and what is technically possible. At present much focus, and hope, is put on Building Environmental Assessment Methods and the associated certification of buildings. Over the past 20 years, assessment schemes such as HK BEAM and LEED have been promoted as a means to achieve more sustainable and environmentally friendly (green) buildings, as well as promoting more sustainable practices in the building process at large. Indeed, they are considered to be one of the most effective voluntary mechanisms to transform building markets and to play a significant role in the mainstreaming of green building practices. The research explores the impact of Building Environmental Assessment Methods on the Hong Kong building industry. Focus is on whether their increased use and implementation has had any effect at the industry level, and if they have generated new sustainable practices on projects, within firms and across the industry at large. The findings promise to support the development of green building policies and practice. They also promise to contribute to the academic literature on sustainable construction and environmental policy. 世界各國政府都積極訂立宏遠的環境目標以及更確切的可持續發展展望，並透過制定新的法例以配合有關的環境、社會和經濟目標。於建築環境中，決策者和主要持份者越來越強調綠色建築在達致全國減少碳排放和可持續發展上的重要性。香港於2013年成立了「推動綠色建築督導委員會」，可見政府亦毫不例外地將可持續發展，特別是減碳和能源的減排，定為一重要議題。建築物的碳排放量佔總量的四成以上，故其於此問題中的獨特位置亦不足為奇。顯而易見，建造業為破壞環境的其一主要源頭，而與此同時業界於有關方面仍有很大的改善空間。以往建築過程中的可持續發展作業方式促使企業和項目引進一系列嶄新或改善了的技術、材料、施工以及管理模式，但籠統而言這些嘗試只於某些方面取得進展，但卻於其他問題上卻收效甚微。可持續發展的緩慢進展以及其零碎而欠影響力的措施一再為人垢病，同時於實踐和技術上仍然存在著鴻溝。目前各界把關注和希望都寄託於建築環境評估法和相關的認證上。在過去的二十年，類似香港建築環境評估（HK BEAM）和美國環保建築認證（LEED）的評價體系一直被認為能夠推動樓宇邁向更可持續發展和環保的方式，同時亦可以令整個建築過程達符可持續發展的模式。而這些體系也被視為其一最有效的自願性措施以改革建造業市場，並在主流綠色建築的計劃中扮演著重要角色。本研究旨在探討建築環境評估法對香港建造業的影響；計劃將聚焦於提高了應用相關的法則有否對業界帶來成效，以及這些方法可否在項目中、各企業又或對整個業界，帶來更符合可持續發展的新工作模式。研究結果將有助於發展綠色建築的政策和規劃，同時也會對有關可持續發展建設和環境政策的學術研究作出貢獻。

17250316.label: Project Objectives
17250316.value: To explore the role of fine particles in altering the mechanical response and liquefaction potential of sand-fines mixtures through a comprehensive experimental program at the macro scale and the micro (grain) scale. To characterize and quantify the effects of particle characteristics (including their shape, size, plasticity, and proportion) in a sound theoretical framework using the systematic datasets yielded from the experimental program. To elucidate the mechanisms behind the observed effects of fines by means of a grain-scale modeling technique in which the packing patterns and interactions of the particles can be traced throughout the loading process. To qualitatively evaluate how the findings from the experimental, theoretical and numerical investigations may affect the current practice of liquefaction evaluation in the light of case histories in recent earthquakes.

17250316.label: Realisation of objectives
17250316.value: • A comprehensive experimental program has been carried out to study cyclic loading behavior and liquefaction resistance of sand-fines mixtures under a wide range of initial states in terms of void ratio, confining pressure and initial static shear stress. • A series of monotonic loading tests have also been performed on sand-fines mixtures to assist in the development of consistent interpretations in the framework of critical state soil mechanics (CSSM) and to explore the link between the monotonic loading behavior and the cyclic loading behavior. • Bender element tests have been carried out to measure shear wave velocity (Vs) of sand-fines mixtures under several specific conditions similar to those in cyclic loading tests. The test data together with the data from the cyclic and monotonic loading tests provide a useful reference for the calibration and validation of advanced elastic-plastic models for describing the behavior of sand-fines mixtures. • The characteristics of particles (e.g. shape, size, size disparity and grading) have been accurately measured for each test material using the laser scanning method to assist the interpretation of the role played by particle attributes in the overall mechanical behavior of sand-fines mixtures. • A series of numerical simulations have been carried out by using the discrete element method to investigate the mechanisms behind the small-strain and large-strain behavior of sand-fines mixtures observed in the laboratory tests. Particular attention has been paid to the effects of particle shape, gradation and fines content. • A critical review of the current methods for liquefaction evaluation has been conducted with special reference to the way they account for the effect of fines. The deficiencies of these methods have been examined with reference to the results and findings from our laboratory experiments and interpretations and with reference to the carefully-selected case history data.

17250316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17250316.value: • The cyclic resistance of sand-fines mixtures (silty sands) depends on the initial packing density and the initial effective confining pressure. Similar to clean sand, the cyclic resistance of silty sand decreases with increasing initial void ratio and initial effective confining pressure, and vice versa. But the presence of an initial static shear stress can affect the effects of void ratio and confining pressure on cyclic resistance. When compared at the same initial void ratio and effective confining pressure, the addition of silica fines reduces the cyclic resistance (CRR) of silty sands for all initial shear stress levels (i.e. α levels). • The effects of α on cyclic resistance can be beneficial or detrimental depending on the initial packing density and the initial confining pressure. The concept of threshold α, originally developed for clean sand, can also be applied to silty sands. The threshold α is affected by the initial packing density and initial effective confining pressure. • The cyclic resistance of silty sands can be characterized by the initial state parameter ψ. Unified correlations between CRR and ψ can be obtained for different fines contents at a given α level. The CRR-ψ lines rotate clockwise with increasing α. The threshold α can also be characterized for various fines contents by using the initial state parameter. • In the framework of CSSM, the fines-content induced reduction of CRR is attributed to the downward shift of the CSL with the addition of non-plastic fines (FC < FC_th). This shift results in an increased ψ when compared at the same initial void ratio and at otherwise similar conditions. Similarly, varying gradation can impose a marked impact on the liquefaction susceptibility of clean and silty sands. Under similar post-consolidation conditions, a well graded sand tends to be more susceptible to liquefaction than a uniformly graded sand. • The correction factor Kfc may reflect the amount of variation of CRR due to change of FC. It is little affected by initial void ratio and eﬀective conﬁning pressure. However, the base sand can affect the Kfc-FC relationship for diﬀerent sand-ﬁnes mixtures. The CSSM framework allows a reasonable prediction of the Kfc-FC relationship and a sound explanation for the mechanism of the base-sand eﬀects. • The unified CRR-ψ platform together with the unified αth-ψ correlation suggests that the cyclic resistance of both clean and non-plastic silty sands can be consistently characterized, thus providing an attractive, unified framework for understanding the effects of initial static shear stress on soil liquefaction and for quantifying such effects for engineering practice. • When studying the effect of particle shape and the effect of fines, it is important to rule out other effects (e.g. size disparity and mineralogy), and also it is important to properly account for the influence of void ratio and confining pressure. Under otherwise similar conditions, the shear wave velocity or the associated small-strain stiffness tends to decrease as sand grains become rounded, and that a fairly good correlation exists between stiffness parameters and a shape index known as overall regularity that accounts for grain shape in a collective manner. • A critical state-based constitutive model for sand with varying fines content has been formulated based on the new laboratory findings. A marked feature of the model is a unified description of the state-dependent elastic modulus as well as a unified description of plastic hardening modulus such that only one set of elastic and hardening parameters is required for sand with different fines contents. The model has been calibrated and validated using the laboratory tests and shown a reasonably good performance for a range of void ratios, confining stresses and fines contents.

17250316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17250316.value: The effect of fabric has been identified as a fundamental issue affecting the cyclic resistance of clean and silty sands. It may also affect the current understanding of the liquefaction assessment charts. Further work in both experimental and numerical aspects toward a better understanding of this issue is worthwhile. Under the in-situ condition, seismic loading can result in principal stress rotation. There are limited studies on the behavior and liquefaction resistance of sand-fines mixtures considering the principal stress rotation. Further research on this issue is also desirable.

17250316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17250316.value: Soil liquefaction remains one of the most complex phenomena in geotechnical engineering. Liquefaction-induced ground deformation has been recognized as a main cause of the substantial damage and financial loss during large earthquakes. This project was aimed to develop a fundamental understanding of the liquefaction of sand-fines mixtures through a specifically designed experimental program in conjunction with interpretation and analysis in a sound theoretical framework. Emphasis has been placed on elucidating the role of particle characteristics in the overall mechanical behavior and in altering the liquefaction resistance of sand-fines mixtures. The research has produced new datasets and insights that are useful for the clarification of existing uncertainties on the effects of fines and to the development of improved methods for liquefaction evaluation. The outcome of the project can contribute to the development of safer and more cost-effective designs against the hazard of earthquakes, one of the most destructive natural hazards to our built and social environment.

17250616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17250616.value: Using Gaussian models for pollutant plume dispersion is well-received in the industry for decades. The key components, dispersion coefficients, are parameterized empirically by assuming the fully developed atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) over statistically uniform ground features such as flat terrain. Land surfaces are seldom homogeneous. A typical example is the flow across different urban morphologies behind a discontinuity in surface roughness. An internal boundary layer (IBL) grows at the bottom of the urban ABL (UABL) in which the flows and transport processes are substantially modified. Under this circumstance, the conventional assumption of horizontal homogeneity is questionable, resulting in uncertain air-quality assessments. The drawback is indeed more complicated because most pollutants are chemically reactive. To bridge the aforementioned knowledge gap, this project, LESChem for flows over surface discontinuities, is conceived to elucidate the dynamics in developing IBLs and UABLs after an abrupt change in surface roughness, together with the subsequent effects on reactive plume dispersion. As a pilot attempt, hypothetical urban morphology and generalized chemistry mechanism will be employed to address the core scientific question: “How the changes in ground feature in the forms of discontinuous surface roughness affect the plume dispersion, secondary pollutant production, and street-level air quality at micro scales”. In particular, we will extend our theories to the parameterizations of dispersion coefficient, handling the physics/chemistry nonlinearity in pollutant plume over discontinuous surface roughness. A complementary approach, consisting of wind tunnel measurements and mathematical modeling, will be sought for an in-depth understanding. Sensitivity tests will be performed using large-eddy simulation (LES) with gas-phase chemistry, LESChem, to formulate a solid knowledge base. Because the velocity scale in the lower UABL is reasonably assumed to be constant (uniform-stress surface layer), we hypothesize that the changes in length scale in response to a surface discontinuity largely govern the transport processes, constituting the conceptual model for the (modified) mechanism of reactive plume dispersion over inhomogeneous urban morphology. This project will arouse the scientific community by the unprecedented findings of pollution physics/chemistry coupling due to changes in surface roughness. The improved dispersion coefficients will offer more accurate air-quality estimates to the professions. The data archives will refine the current practice, serving society well by innovations in urban planning guidelines and environmental management strategies. The research output from LESChem will address our major technical concern: The steps to ameliorate the classic Gaussian models for more reliable reactive plume dispersion calculations over surface inhomogeneity in the engineering perspective. 採用高斯模型計算污染物擴散羽在業界廣受歡迎數十年。其中的擴散係數，一般通過假定在充分發展的大氣邊界層（ABL）中，如平坦地勢。陸地表面很少均勻。一個典型的例子是不連續的城市形貌。內部邊界層（IBL）生長在城市ABL（UABL）中，其中的流動和運輸過程起了基本變化。在這種情況下，傅統的平均常規假設是可疑的，從而導致不確定的空氣質量評估。其缺點更加複雜，因為大氣污染物大多是化學反應性。 為了彌補上述知識缺口，這個項目，LESChem對不均表面上的流動，主要目的是闡明動力學在不均粗糙表面的變化和其對反應羽擴散的影響。作為試點，假想城市形態和可靠的化學機制將被用來解決最核心的科學問題：“在不連續的粗糙表面，地貌如何影響羽擴散，二次污染物的生產和路旁的空氣質量“。特別是，我們將最新的理論擴展到離散係數的參數化，處理污染物擴散羽在非連續粗糙面的非線性物理/化學。風洞測量和數學建模會一同使用以尋求一個深入的了解。透過大渦模擬（LES）與氣相化學的敏感性測試，LESChem將制定一個堅實的知識基礎。因為在較低UABL的應力一般是恆定的，我們於是假設運輸過程中最大的變化取決於長度尺度，構成反應羽擴散的基本概念模型。 這項目的結果將引起科學界的興趣。改進後的擴散係數將為業界提供更準確的空氣質量預測。數據歸檔將改進目前的做法，優化城市規劃和環境管理。LESChem的研究結果將解決我們的主要技術關注：改善高斯模型對於反應羽在不均表面擴散計算的可靠性。

17250616.label: Realisation of objectives
17250616.value: The solution approaches consist of the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) turbulence model, large-eddy simulation (LES) and laboratory experiments. The computation domain includes sinusoidal wavy surface and natural topography at the bottom. The RANS shear-stress transport (SST) k-omega turbulence model is used in this study. It possesses the favorable performance of both k-omega and k-epsilon turbulence models that is capable of handling adverse pressure gradient as well as flow separation. The governing equations consist of the mass conservation for incompressible flows, momentum conservation, together with the conservation of turbulence kinetic energy (TKE) k and specific dissipation rate omega. On the other hand, the subgrid-scale (SGS) properties in LES is modeled by the Smagorinsky model in eddy viscosity form. The one-equation SGS model is employed to ensure SGS conservation. The finite volume method (FVM) is used to solve the governing equations. The implicit Euler scheme is used in the time integration while the cell limited Gaussian integration with linear interpolation (second-order-accurate central differencing) is employed in the spatial discretization. The pressure-implicit with splitting of operators (PISO) is used to handle the pressure-velocity coupling in incompressible flows. The geometric algebraic multigrid (GAMG) is used to solve the linear equation systems for pressure and the preconditioned bi-conjugate gradient (PBiCG) method for velocity, turbulence and scalar. The residual of iterations is less than 10E-12. The spatial domain consists of upstream (surface 1) and downstream (surface 2) wall boundaries with different roughness. Instead of parameterizing the rough-surface flows by wall models (controlling the roughness length in the log-law), roughness elements in the form of sinusoidal wavy walls or natural topography are adopted to explicitly resolve the dynamics in the roughness sublayer (RSL). The use of wavy walls avoids the flow separation at singularity, such as angles and edges. Various domain configurations, including different values of amplitude and wavelength, are tested. The elevation of the bottom solid boundary is described by sinusoidal wave. The aerodynamic resistance over sinusoidal wavy surfaces increases with increasing amplitude-to-wavelength ratio that is used to modulate the drag force. The theory formulated based on the idealized cases above is then tested by the natural topography of Hong Kong (HK) Island over which the internal boundary layer (IBL) is initialized by the sea-land transition and the flows are adjusted by the topography elevation. HK Island is situated in the southern area of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR). It has hilly terrain that faces the South China Sea. Its three-dimensional (3D) digital model is built to investigate the flows above offshore islands. Unlike RANS, different inflow turbulence generators have been proposed for LES. The synthetic turbulence method (STM) had increasing attention recently. It attempts to fabricate the inflow turbulence boundary condition (BC) that mimics artificial eddies according to the flow conditions. However, prior setting of turbulence statistics and adaption distance is essential to the modeling accuracy. The most straightforward approach is the library-based method (LBM) that provides pre-generated, realistic inflow turbulence data with good phase information of the dynamics. Whereas, prior separate computations or experiments are required. In this project, the internal plane mapping is employed to generate inflow BCs for IBL development after surface roughness transition. The velocity on the recycled plane is extracted then is mapped back onto the domain inlet. A constant background pressure gradient is exerted in the upstream recycling section to drive the prevailing flows. The laboratory experiments are performed in the wind tunnel of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Hong Kong. The dimensions of the test section are 6 m (length), 0.56 m (width) and 0.56 m (height). The blockage ratio of the roughness elements is less than 5% that marginally fulfills the practice recommended for low-speed wind tunnel experiments. The free-stream wind speed is in the range of 8.8 m/sec to 9.6 m/sec and the thickness of turbulent boundary layer (TBL) is about 0.18 m. Hence, the Reynolds numbers based on the free-stream wind speed and TBL thickness is about 170,000 that is sufficiently high for negligible molecular viscosity. The roughness elements are fabricated by the 3D printing machine Stratasys FORTUS 250 mc using fused deposition modeling (FDM). The material is high density functional ABS with resolution about 150 micro m. Constant-temperature (CT) hot-wire anemometry (HWA) is used to measure the velocities. The CT HWA probe is made of copper electroplating on platinum-plated tungsten wires, leaving a pair of 2-mm sensing elements. Afterward, the wires are mounted on needle-shaped prongs with an include angle of 100 degree to improve the accuracy of near-wall turbulence measurements in highly turbulent flows. The voltage signal across the CT HWA probe, which is mounted downwind of the measurement zone to minimize the instrumentation disturbance to the flows, drops from 40 mV to 10 mV in 40 micro sec, ensuring the time response. The Wheatstone bridge is kept in balance by an amplifier to control the current to the CT HWA. The wire resistance and hence the temperature, which depend on the cooling imposed by the flows, is kept constant. The bridge voltage is the CT HWA output signal that is subsequently converted to the velocity readings by the voltage-to-velocity calibration scheme. Fast response to voltage changes (within 40 micro sec) is achieved by the low thermal inertia of the tungsten wires and the high gain of the servo loop amplifier. The analog CT HWA output voltage signal is digitalized using the National Instrument (NI) data acquisition module (24-bit, NI 9239). A desktop computer with LabVIEW software then acquires the data through the NI CompactDAQ chassis. The sampling frequency is 2,000 Hz and the sampling duration is at least 60 sec at each point. Measurement uncertainty arises from various sources such as the dimensions of individual roughness elements, the position of sampling probe (spatial resolution 1 mm), the include angle of the hot-wire pair and the CT HWA sensitivity. The offset error in the analog-to-digital signal conversion by the NI data acquisition module NI 9239 is around 0.05% for analog input +/-10.52 V. The wind speed measurements by the CT HWA are also calibrated by the Pitot tube upstream the test section. The slope of the calibration curve is within 0.97 to 1.03 and the coefficient of determination is up to 0.9998. The measurement uncertainties of mean wind speed and turbulence are hence estimated to be less than 3% and 9%, respectively. The three objectives are achieved. The major technical difficulties faced were comparing the results between mathematical modeling and laboratory experiments. As there are two different types of rough surfaces so are two different roughness length scales. This technical challenge is solved by extensive literature review and the detailed examination of our results. Similarly, refining the current parameterizations of winds and dispersion is challenging because of the broad spectrum of length scale in urban morphology. In this project the drag coefficient is used in the parameterization. More advanced statistical methods could be used in future studies.

17250616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17250616.value: Aerodynamic resistance changes in the atmospheric surface layers (ASLs) for flows over dissimilar land surfaces, such as coastal zones and rural-urban interface, that complicates the transport processes, leading to the development of internal boundary layer (IBL). The effect on ASL transport is examined by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) in this project. Instead of surface parameterization, the roughness elements at the ASL bottom are explicitly resolved by sinusoidal wavy surfaces. The aerodynamic resistance is modulated by the amplitude and wavelength so as to contrast the interaction among roughness sublayers (RSLs), inertial sublayers (ISLs) and IBLs. The adjustments of mean winds and turbulent flows after an abrupt surface transition are first investigated by the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) turbulence models (Li et al. 2020). Three configurations of smoother-to-rougher transition are examined to contrast the dynamics. After the change in (increasing) surface roughness, the flows decelerate and the momentum flux increases to overcome the augmented drag. The growth of IBL and ISL signifies that the influence from the upstream surface is being weakened while the flows are developing in equilibrium with the downstream (new) surface. The dynamic response of flows and turbulence to an abrupt surface transition is further studied by large-eddy simulation (LES). It is found that the flow adjustments initiate at the RSL during the development of the IBL so the flows hardly establish self-similarity immediately after surface transitions (Li and Liu 2021). Unlike those analytical solutions or surface parameterizations available in literature, the current LES unveils a slower IBL growth in the streamwise direction, demonstrating the importance of resolving the roughness elements and the RSLs explicitly. Besides, augmented turbulent diffusion is observed over the rougher surface. In addition to the mean and fluctuating properties, the gradual adjustment of higher-order moments along with developing IBL suggests that IBL height is a physically significant length scale. The spatial behaviors of skewness and kurtosis, which suggest coherent events, are visualized across the surface discontinuity. Furthermore, comparing the frequency spectra in the wall-normal direction shows that the energy-carrying turbulence shifts to higher (lower) frequency after smoother-to-rougher (rougher-to-smoother) transition. The shift completes substantially on large-scale RSL turbulence, demonstrating the significance of RSL. The budget analysis of momentum flux illustrates that RSL complicates the transport processes. Shear production and pressure-velocity interaction are dominant above RSL. Along with the IBL growth, these two terms evolve spatially that spread the impact of surface transition upward.

17250616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17250616.value: In this project, the internal boundary layer (IBL) growth after surface transition is investigated. However, the IBL development is limited by the size of computation domain (both in the streamwise and vertical extents). Compared with previous analytical solutions, the length that provided for the IBL development is not sufficiently long (only ten times of the IBL height in this LES study). To obtain fully developed turbulent flows over the downstream new surface, the computation domain should be enlarged. The change in surface roughness is also limited in this project. It is smaller than that in conventional studies using land-surface parameterizations by two to five times. It is because of the explicitly resolved, identical roughness elements in which the resistance is rather small. A larger change in surface roughness, such as using inhomogeneous roughness elements, should be attempted in the future. The roughness elements employed in this study is homogeneous in the spanwise direction. Whereas, realistic land surface is more complicated (in terms of size, shape and orientation). The influence of heterogeneous surface roughness, such as in the spanwise direction, should be further investigated to enrich our understanding of IBL flows.

17250616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17250616.value: Flows across an abrupt change in surface roughness, such as sea-land breeze and rural-urban interface, lead to the development of an internal boundary layer (IBL). In this project, the effect of surface discontinuity on the structure of flow and turbulence is unveiled by the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) turbulence model and large-eddy simulation (LES). Various configurations of smoother-to-rougher and rougher-to-smoother transitions, which are fabricated by sinusoidal wavy surfaces, are examined to contrast the flow adjustment. Unlike most of the conventional studies, the changes in surface roughness are induced by explicitly resolved roughness elements (instead of land-surface parameterizations) so the dynamics in the (inhomogeneous) roughness sublayers (RSLs) is calculated. The changes in friction velocity and roughness length follow the conventional power law. The development of RSL and inertial sublayer (ISL) characterizes the flows adjustment clearly. The growth of IBL and ISL signifies that the influence from the upstream surface is being weakened while the flows are developing in equilibrium with the downstream surface. The findings help elucidate the (local) winds over complex terrain and/or sea-land effect on atmospheric flows. The results show that the flow dynamics and structure over natural topography are consistent with those over idealized surfaces.

17251716.label: Project Objectives

17251716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17251716.value: 本項目旨在推進無源控制器綜合理論的發展及其在機械振動系統中的應用。由於其可靠性高和成本低等優勢，無源控制器綜合理論具有深遠的實際意義。其中，作為一類特殊的無源控制器，僅由無源元件組成的無源網絡在諸如車輛懸架系統、隔振系統和動力吸振系統等動態系統中有著廣泛的應用。因此，本項目將研究基於各類機械振動系統的無源網絡綜合問題。 自1931年Brune的開創性成果以來，無源網絡綜合已成為了系統理論重要的分支之一。然而，作為電路綜合研究的核心問題，最小實現問題至今仍有許多尚未解決的難題，其中涉及的技術難題至今未有一般化的解決方案。特別是近年來，由於一個新的雙端點機械元件慣容的問世，使得這些技術問題重新具有了新的研究意義。慣容定義為兩端點相對加速度與兩端點承受的力成正比的雙端點機械元件。慣容的出現為無源控制器設計，尤其是在實際應用中最小元件數量成為關鍵性的限制條件時的機械系統設計中如懸架系統設計等，提供了系統化的設計方法，同時也是需要進一步深入研究的問題。 本項目的研究工作將不但促進系統理論和控制工程領域的發展，更將直接對懸架控制系統、隔振系統和動力吸振系統等應用領域產生深遠影響。從長遠角度來看，鑒於網絡綜合理論在聲學、彈性動力學網絡和彈性超材料等領域的深遠影響，本項目的研究工作也將促進這些領域的發展。 本項目的研究目標如下： （1） 建立低階阻抗/導納無源控制器最小實現問題及其在懸架系統、隔振系統和動力吸振系統中的無源控制器設計問題。 （2） 研究一端口機械網絡綜合問題如有限制條件的機械網絡綜合問題及其在懸架系統中的應用，同時建立適於任意階正實函數實現的一般化步驟。 （3） 通過應用現代系統理論并基於n端口電阻網絡的研究基礎，進一步拓展多端口無源網絡綜合的研究工作。 （4） 針對連續質量系統，建立最優的基於慣容的隔振器設計方法。 （5） 在已有實驗室中，建立無線半主動慣容的物理原型并給出相應的模型預測控制算法。

17251716.label: Major findings and research outcome
17251716.value: 1. An optimization and design method for the passive and semi-active vehicle suspensions by using low-degree admittance passive networks are proposed. The performances of these low-degree one-port networks as vehicle suspensions are evaluated and compared. 2. An semi-active suspension design method by dividing the whole system into a passive part and a semi-active part is proposed and verified based on a quarter-car and full-car model. 3. A new foot strike pattern describing the instinctive human running manner and the performance of a group of adults is obtained. The newly defined foot strike pattern can be considered as an alternative option to reduce the injury of running activities. It would be possible to apply the foot strike pattern mechanism in humanoid robots, not only to extend the service life from the collision and vibration damage of the components, but also to make robots more human-like. 4. The highly representative bipedal humanoid robots are summarized, and the potential to move the ideas and models forward from laboratory settings into the real world is discussed. The current clinical understanding of the walking and running dynamics is also reviewed. 5. The controller design problem for systems with communication uncertainties including delays and data losses is studied. Two approaches are proposed to design aperiodic estimators. A measurement retransmission scheme is proposed, and the estimation performance is improved as compared with the commonly used methods.

17251716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17251716.value: 1. The research will advance the theory of passive network synthesis with restricted complexity. From the viewpoint of redundancy, we will start with a class of simple positive-real functions such as biquadratic functions to seek the optimal realization in terms of the number of circuit elements used, which will be then generalized to any given positive-real function. In practice, the intended results will take practical constraints into consideration to lower the cost of suspension systems. Model reduction techniques will also be introduced. Vehicle suspension design and vibration isolation will be investigated, extended to the semi-active cases, and verified by experimental testing. 2. The research will broaden the potential applications of inerter in mechanical and mechatronic systems. For example, the proposed methods for vehicle suspensions and vibration isolators are directly applicable to wind turbines, wave energy converts, bridges, robots, etc. 3. The fundamental theories for vibration control systems will be updated considering the addition of inerter and inerter-based devices. For example, the zero and pole placement problems for inerter-based systems are different from the traditional one, where new analysis and synthesis methods are demanded for inerter-based systems.

17251716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17251716.value: 1. A systematic design method for inerter-based systems including vehicle suspensions, isolators, dynamic vibration absorber etc, is proposed, where the inerter-based systems have a low-degree complexity. 2. A structure composed of a passive part and a semi-active part is proposed for semi-active suspensions, where the effectiveness is demonstrated based on two kinds of simplified vehicle models. 3. The dynamic analysis and modelling problem for humanoid robots is investigated, which can lay a foundation for the application of inerter and inerter-based devices for robots. 4. The communication uncertainties including delays and data losses in the controller design of control systems are studied, which would strength the control part of inerter-based vehicle suspensions, isolators etc.

17252416.label: Realisation of objectives
17252416.value: Objective 1: Investigate the potential relationship between environmental information transparency, trust in government, and public perception of ecosystem services; compare the differences between developed and developing countries. This objective has been fully achieved. Using questionnaire surveys, we collected 271 valid responses from Shaoguan, 519 responses from Guangzhou, 247 responses from Brussels, and 331 responses from Antwerp. We built a simple multiple causes multiple indicators model (MIMIC) to investigate the potential relationship between exposure to environmental information and trust in government, then conduct a cross comparison amongst the four cities. Our results suggest that in all sampled cities trust in government is associated with the quality of environmental information, but not the frequency and ways (passive or active) of accessing to environmental information. Public perception pertaining to the importance of various ecosystem services is associated with recreational use of urban rivers, but not environmental information exposure. Objective 2: Explore the impact of environmental information transparency on societal preference heterogeneity, such as respondents’ decisions to be willing to pay, stay opt-out, give protest responses, and prefer certain attributes or specific levels of urban river restoration scenarios. This objective has been fully achieved. We used Latent Class Model to identify the characteristics of the latent classes amongst the samples, and then applied the Mixed Logit Model with WTP space to elucidate the impact of environmental information access, trust in government, and respondents' preference heterogeneity. Objective 3: Build the linkages between environmental information, public perception of ecosystem services, trust in government, and public heterogeneous preferences and decisions about urban river restoration. This objective has been fully achieved. We constructed a Hybrid Mixed Logit Model to link all observable variables together through latent variables, which allows for a simultaneous identification of possible latent linkages between environmental information accessibility, protest attitudes, and choice behaviours. We found different latent linkages amongst four sampled cities, including environmental information sufficiency, distrust of government, and individual environmental responsibility. For Chinese respondents, frequent access to environmental information is associated with distrust in government and unsupportive decisions for urban river restoration projects. For Belgian respondents, frequent access to environmental information is not associated with trust in government, but their frequent use of urban rivers will lead to supportive decisions for river restoration.

17252416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17252416.value: Governments across the world respond to a wave of information transparency policies that aim to deliver transparent policymaking and align public environmental preferences. These initiatives were mostly successful in Western democracies that have a strong culture of public participation. How and through what ways an increased flow of environmental information in the absence of democracy, such as the authoritarian context of China, could led to favourable public participation and support for environmental/ecological restoration project remain under-investigated. we attempt to explore the association between various sources of environmental information traits and citizens’ choice decisions regarding urban river restoration projects in two contrast social and political contexts, using Guangzhou and Shaoguan (China), Brussels and Antwerp (Belgium) as case studies. We found that Chinese people trust environmental information from their social contacts, and Belgian people trust those provided by academic research institutions. And similarly in both countries, more trust in environmental information leads to supportive decisions to the proposed urban river restoration projects.

17253216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17253216.value: Dynamic networks are frequently encountered in science and engineering for modeling complex dynamical systems where entities of interest interact with each other over time and give rise to various behaviors or phenomenon. Gene regulatory networks (GRN) and brain connectivity networks are two important examples in biomedical engineering. Both of them are central themes of genomic and neuroscience, respectively. With the advances of technology, measurements which depend on the states of the interested entities can be collected, though they may still suffer from various limitations/imperfections. For instances, large number of gene expressions under certain biological conditions can now be measured using high-throughput gene microarray technologies. Similarly, brain connectivity (BC) can be studied using EEG, fMRI or simultaneous EEG/fMRI (sEEG/fMRI). A key problem facing the analysis of such data is the time-varying nature of the process and the large number of quantities to be estimated so as to characterize their interaction, say genes in dynamic GRN identification and brain regions in BC. Conventional approaches usually focus on static phenomenon or assuming that the system parameters remains unchanged over a sufficiently long time so that statistics with lower variance can be computed. Another interesting problem is to identify functionally related sub-networks so as to understand how they interact over time. This may benefit our understanding of the underlying phenomenon or making prediction/diagnosis of diseases. This proposal aims to develop a novel methodology for dynamic network analysis with particular emphasis on time-course gene expression microarray and fMRI/EEG Data. More specifically, we shall develop methods for 1) estimating a large-scale time-varying model of the GRN from time-course gene microarray data, from which possible dynamic interaction of genes over time can be identified, 2) estimating the sub-networks by performing clustering of the resulting network using appropriate topology measure and functionality extracted from existing gene database, 3) performing brain BC analysis using fMRI data using a similar approach and correlating the results with advanced nonstationary signal/spectral analysis of associated EEG signals. The methodology will be evaluated and compared with existing literature using the time-course C-elegans gene microarray data, task-based as well as resting state EEG/fMRI data. Since promising preliminary results have been obtained, we expect more findings or targets can be revealed through this study. Our long-term goal is to develop a powerful yet comprehensive dynamic network analysis tool for researchers/practitioners in the field so that new scientific findings can be revealed more efficiently. 動態網絡的研究在科學和工程建模/分析中具有重要的應用。 其中，基因調控網絡和腦連接網絡分析更是在生物醫學工程中兩個重要的研究領域。隨著技術的進步，大量的測量數據已經可以從基因芯片及腦電圖/磁共振成像等設備收集。在分析這等大數據時，一個關鍵的問題是有關的過程可能是動態的。這使要估計的參數大大增加。與此同時，有限的數據和不確定時間變化更為數據分析帶來極大的挑戰。這項提案旨在研究一種新穎的動態網絡模型和其分析方法。此方法將被應用到有時間序列的基因芯片數據和磁共振成像/腦電圖數據。籍此，我們希望進一步了解生物的不同過程和腦功能。我們的長期目標是開發一個有效的動態網絡分析系統，有利研究人員對基本現象進行了解或預測/診斷相關疾病。

17253216.label: Realisation of objectives
17253216.value: In this project, we have developed several novel methodology for revealing the connectivity in two types networks encountered in physical science, namely gene regulatory networks and brain networks. We mainly focus on techniques for revealing the Ganger causality of nonstationary signals using both time-varying autoregressive (TVAR) and nonlinear TVAR models. The project objectives are successfully accomplished and the major research results and findings are summarized below. Gene Regulatory Network from Time-course Gene Microarray Data ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- In [R1], we have proposed a Maximum-A-Posteriori-Probability method with a multi Laplacian Prior for identifying putative transcript factors (TF) and regulatory networks for gene microarray data using the nonlinear TVAR model. An effective solution based on Augmented- Lagrangian method is also proposed. The multi-Laplacian prior allows connections to/from a gene to be better preserved for putative TF identification as compared with conventional L1-based penalties. On the other hand, the ALM allows the resultant nonsmooth L1-based penalties to be de-coupled from the remaining smoothness terms, so that the former and later can be efficiently solved using a low-complexity proximity operator and smooth optimization technique, respectively. Experimental results show that the proposed method gives better accuracy and higher computational speed than our previous work using smoothed approximation. Moreover, its performance, without the use of ChIP-chip data, is found to be highly comparable with other state-of-the-art methods integrating both ChIP-chip and gene microarray data. It suggests that the proposed method may serve as a useful exploratory tool for putative TF identification with reduced experimental cost. We have also analyzed the dynamic gene regulatory network of a large-scale time course microarray data of Saccharomyces cerevisiae [R2]. We can process all the gene expressions as a whole and the results are very encouraging. Moreover, we have completely analyzed a large-scale gene expression data of a C-elegans development data [R3]. The results will be reported in future publication. Furthermore, we have extended the ALM approach mentioned above and developed a distributed approach for robust nonlinear estimation with equality constraints, which includes the dynamic gene regulatory network analysis above as a special case [R4]. The approach is very general and it can also be applied to distributed power system state estimation [R5]. Moreover, the results reported in [R2] are further investigated where we process all the gene expressions as a whole. More precisely, 16 GRNs at different time points have been estimated from the time-course gene microarray data. We found that the behavior of many groups of genes correlate well with the cell cycle. We also found that the identified time varying gene interactions agree well with literature in both the nature of the genes and the stage of the cell cycle process. This demonstrates the usefulness of the proposed approach in identifying these meaningful gene interactions. Analyzing Brain functional Connectivity using simultaneous fMRI data and EEG signals ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- We have studied the Brain Functional Connectivity of subjects under meditation using coherence in the short-time Fourier transform domain. We found that there was significant decrease in brain connectivities in most of the spectrum band, including delta 1-4Hz (hubs mainly in the right frontal lobe, right parietal and bilateral occipital lobe), theta 4-8Hz (mainly in the right frontal lobe, right parietal lobe and bilateral occipital lobe), alpha 8-12Hz (mainly in the right parietal lobe and slightly in the right frontal lobe) and beta 12-30 Hz (mainly in the left temporal lobe). Only sporadic brain regions have increased connectivities mainly in the alpha1 and gamma band. This explains meditation corresponds to a relaxed brain states with reduced brain activities. The findings are reported in [R6]. Moreover, we have developed a novel adaptive fading Kalman filter for estimating the time-varying AR model to reveal the functional connectivity from a simultaneous fMRI/EEG data on the visual "odd ball experiment" [R7]. The spectrum as well as other interesting connections at various frequency bands are successfully identified with p-values less than 0.01. These activations and connectivities are also compared with those from the activations in the fMRI data. The results are very encouraging and it reflects many interesting findings on the overall coordination of the brain during this visual task. We have also developed a more sophisticated estimation method based on local polynomial modelling. The spectrum and connectivities at different frequency bands are characterized. The findings are also compared with the fMRI data. It reveals the frequency bands and possible locations of the classical N100 and N200a which are related to auditory stimuli [R8], which are different from those in the visual stimulus. More results can be found in [R9]. Finally, we have also made use of the functional connectivity for detection of various psychiatric and developmental diseases such as ADHD, ASD, Schizophrenia and Major depressive disorder (MDD). 17253216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17253216.value: In this project, we have developed several novel algorithms for revealing connectivity in large-scale networks using time-varying autoregressive (TVAR) model. We have 1) developed a maximum-a-posteriori-probability method for estimating the model parameters with L1, continuity and multi Laplacian priors [R1] and studied the identification of gene regulatory network (GRN) from large-scale time-course gene microarray data using the nonlinear TVAR model. Moreover, the multi Laplacian Prior has been applied for identifying putative transcript factors and regulatory networks from time-course gene microarray data; 2) developed an effective distributed solution of large-scale problem based on Augmented- Lagrangian method. This allows us to analyze the dynamic GRN of a large-scale time course microarray data of Saccharomyces cerevisiae [R2] as well as c-elegan [R3]. We process all the gene expressions as a whole and the results allows us to better understand the underlying biological processes. In the Saccharomyces cerevisiae case, 16 GRNs at different time points have been estimated and most of the genes identified correlate well with the cell cycle, which agrees well with literature. In the c-elegan case [R3], the networks identified offers much insight into the embryonic development of the c-elegan and its underlying processes from a data driven perspective; 3) extended the ALM approach above and developed a novel distributed approach for robust nonlinear estimation with equality constraints with the GRN above as a special case [R4]. The approach is very general and it can also be applied to distributed power system state estimation [R5]. We have also investigated the brain functional connectivity problem using the TVAR model. Due to the longer time span, we mainly focus on recursive algorithms using Kalman filtering (KF) and more sophisticated local polynomial modeling (LPM) approach. Particularly, we 4) studied the Brain Functional Connectivity (FC) of subjects under meditation using coherence in the short-time Fourier transform domain and characterized the significant decrease in BC in different spectrum band [R6], 5) developed a novel adaptive fading KF for estimating the TVAR to reveal the FC from a simultaneous fMRI/EEG data on the visual "odd ball experiment" [R7]. The spectrum as well as other interesting connections at various frequency bands are characterized. These activations and connectivities are also compared with those from the fMRI data. The results reflect many interesting findings on the overall coordination of the brain during this visual task. 6) developed an estimation method based on LPM. Similarly, the spectrum and connectivities at different frequency bands are characterized. The findings are also compared with the fMRI data. It reveals the frequency bands and possible locations of the classical N100 and N200a (also P300 etc) which are related to auditory stimuli [R8] and their causal relations.

17253216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17253216.value: Due to the generality of the formulation and the effective solution of the distributed robust estimation with equality constraints, this new framework will find many applications in practice. Generalization to inequality constraints will be of great interest. Since the amount of useful information offer by the analysis is very rich, a systematic network-based method and an automatic method for mining relevant information in the literature for comparison deserve further research and investigation. Our finding and results on the EEG analysis offer another dimension for visualising the temporal evolution of the various frequency components and information flows over electrodes over different regions and time. This yields new insight into the overall coordination of the brain. Future research should focus on a holistic studies in the time domain involving the locations and variation of the various ERPs, frequency coherence and coupling of the various oscillations in order to study how these oscillations interact over time and space.

17253216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17253216.value: Dynamic networks are frequently encountered in science and engineering. Gene regulatory networks (GRN) and brain connectivity networks are two important examples in biomedical engineering. A key problem facing the analysis of such data is the time-varying nature of the process and the large number of quantities to be estimated so as to characterize their interactions, say genes interactions and connectivity of brain regions. This project developed a novel methodology for dynamic network analysis with particular emphasis on time-course gene expression microarray and fMRI/EEG Data. We have developed methods for estimating large-scale time-varying GRNs from time-course gene microarray data. This allows us to identify key genes involved and their putative interactions over time in a data driven manner. The embryonic development of c-elegans and the cell cycle of Saccharomyces cerevisiae have been studied, which largely agree with existing literature. Similarly, we have developed novel methods for spectral/connectivity analyses of highly nonstationary EEG signals and correlated the results with fMRI data. This reveals the important frequency content as well as the information flows between electrodes at different brain regions over time. Experimental results reveal the various responses due to the target stimuli, which facilitates further analysis of the role of different frequencies, their coupling and coordination. Overall, this project developed powerful tools for analysis of dynamic GRN, EEG and related applications, which facilitates new scientific findings to be revealed more efficiently.

17253616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17253616.value: There is a growing trend in extracting knowledge from the Web and organizing it in large knowledge bases like DBpedia and YAGO. The data are most typically represented by the Resource Description Framework (RDF) model, in which all information is in the form of (subject, predicate, object) triples. Thus, RDF models data as entities (subjects) which are linked to other entities and/or types or descriptions (i.e., objects could be entities, types, or literals). Many RDF knowledge bases have been enriched to include spatial semantics, opening the road to additional search and analysis operations, such as location-based retrieval. RDF data are traditionally accessed with the help of a structured query language, like SPARQL. Users are required to understand the language and the data domain. Hence, SPARQL is not friendly to common users, limiting data access mostly to domain experts. Given this, a keyword search model on RDF data emerged. A keyword query retrieves a set of small subgraphs of the RDF knowledge base where the vertices of each subgraph collectively cover all keywords. Although RDF stores that support spatial search have been developed, none of these systems supports keyword search on RDF data that considers the query issuer's location. On the other hand, spatial keyword queries on text repositories are already a popular search paradigm in information retrieval. In this project, we will study the problem of spatial keyword search on RDF knowledge bases. The motivation is to facilitate finding entities in the RDF graph that are spatially near the user location and at the same time related to the query keywords. We will first investigate appropriate models for the relevance of spatial RDF entities to a set of query keywords, by extending existing work on RDF keyword search. These models will be evaluated by real users for their effectiveness, to select the most suitable one. Based on this model, we will study the efficient evaluation of spatial RDF keyword search, by investigating appropriate indexing and algorithmic techniques. In addition, we will study the efficient maintenance of indexes in a real environment where the RDF data are continuously updated. Finally, we will implement of a distributed engine, which will scale out spatial RDF keyword search. A successful completion of the project will bring out a novel search paradigm for RDF knowledge bases and improve their utility. The results of the project will benefit the general public and the research community. 現今一個新的熱門趨勢是從網絡中提取信息、並利用DBpedia、YAGO等大型數據庫組織這些信息。這些數據大部分以資源描述框架（RDF）模型來表達，其中所有的信息均以主體-屬性-屬性值的三元組形式存儲。這樣，數據可以是指向其他對象、或定義為類型或描述的對象（屬性值可以是其他對象、類型或文本信息）。現在很多RDF數據庫都拓展包含了空間信息，從而使得基於位置的查詢等更多搜索與分析操作成為可能。 RDF數據的查詢通常依賴於一些結構化的查詢語言，如SPARQL。使用時用戶需要理解這門語言以及具體的數據類型，所以SPARQL對普通用戶而言並不易用，導致很多時候只有領域專業人士才能獲取數據。考慮到這些情況，利用關鍵詞搜索RDF數據的模型得以出現——一個關鍵詞查詢會從RDF數據庫中獲取一系列節點能夠共同覆蓋所有關鍵詞的子圖。儘管支持空間搜索的RDF數據庫已經出現，現有的系統卻都不支持同時考慮查詢者位置的關鍵詞搜索。而另一方面，在信息檢索領域，文本數據庫中的空間關鍵詞查詢已經成為一種流行的搜索模式。 在本項目中，我們將研究RDF數據庫中的空間關鍵詞搜索。這一搜索的目的是在RDF圖中查詢在用戶位置附近、同時與查詢關鍵詞相關的條目。我們首先會拓展現有的RDF關鍵詞搜索，從而尋找一些適合定義空間RDF對象與查詢關鍵詞關係的模型。我們會利用實際用戶來評估它們的效果，並選擇最合適的模型。基於這個模型，我們會研究適宜的索引與算法技術，以進一步實現高效的空間RDF關鍵詞搜索。同時，在真實環境中RDF數據會持續地更新，我們亦會研究高效的索引維護方法。最後，我們會開發一個分佈式的、可以支持空間RDF關鍵詞搜索的引擎。這一項目的成功實現會推出RDF數據庫中的一種創新性的查詢模式，並提高RDF數據庫的適用性。公眾與科研界均會從項目成果中收益。

17253616.label: Realisation of objectives
17253616.value: The objectives have been achieved 100%. In conference publication "Top-k Relevant Semantic Place Retrieval on Spatial RDF Data", we first defined the concept of places and how they are described in large RDF knowledge graphs. For all entities in the graph, we extracted a textual description using the terms that appear in their URIs, the predicates that have these entities as subjects and the literals connected to these entities. Then, we labeled as places all entities that are associated to spatial locations. Given a keyword query and a reference location, we defined the relevance of a place to the query, by combining (i) the spatial distance of the place to the reference location (ii) the textual relevance of the place to the query keywords. For (ii), we extended an existing model for RDF keyword search. According to our extension, for a candidate place, we find the nearest occurrences of the query keywords in the graph to the graph vertex that corresponds to the place entity. We experimentally found that this search model provides good results in terms of relevance. Going one step further, we designed efficient algorithms that spatially search for nearby places and verify their textual relevance to the query, until a point where the best retrieved places so far are guaranteed to be the best query results. Finally, we used reachability indexes and augmented spatial indexes to further improve efficiency. This result directly addresses objectives 1 & 2. Journal paper "Top-k Relevant Semantic Place Retrieval on Spatio-temporal RDF Data" extends publication "Top-k Relevant Semantic Place Retrieval on Spatial RDF Data" to add temporal semantics to the spatial RDF queries. We use two ways to incorporate temporal information. One way is considering the temporal differences between the keyword-matched vertices and the query timestamp. The other way is using a temporal range to filter keyword-matched vertices. The indexing and search methods were extended and improved with four optimizations to evaluate spatiotemporal RDF queries. Extensive empirical studies on two real datasets demonstrate the superior and robust performance of our system compared to baseline methods. This result directly addresses objectives 1 and 2. In many situations, the results of spatial RDF queries are very similar to each other, compromising query effectiveness. In journal paper "Diversified spatial keyword search on RDF data" extends our search model to diversify query results. Specifically, we integrate textual and spatial diversification to RDF spatial keyword search, facilitating the retrieval of entities with diverse characteristics and directions with respect to the query location. Since finding the optimal set of query results is NP-hard, we propose two approximate algorithms with guaranteed quality. Extensive empirical studies on two real datasets show that the algorithms only add insignificant overhead compared to non-diversified search, while returning results of high quality in practice (which is verified by a user evaluation study we conducted). This result directly addresses objectives 1 and 2. In journal paper "SRX: Efficient Management of Spatial RDF Data", we studied the effective handling of dynamic spatial RDF data. In particular, we present a general encoding scheme which approximates the geometries of the RDF entities inside their (integer) IDs and can be used, along with several operators and optimizations we introduce, to accelerate queries with spatial predicates and to re-encode entities dynamically in case of updates. We implement our ideas in SRX, a system built on top of the popular RDF-3X system. SRX extends RDF-3X with support for three types of spatial queries: range selections (e.g. find entities within a given polygon), spatial joins (e.g. find pairs of entities whose locations are close to each other), and spatial k nearest neighbors (e.g. find the three closest entities from a given location). Since the encoding does not interfere with the normal handling of RDF triples, our scheme can directly be used in distributed systems that apply subject-based partitioning of the data to different computer nodes. In fact, we have tested an implementation of this scheme in a distributed environment but the results were not innovative enough to warrant a publication. This work directly addresses objectives 2, 3, and 4. In conference publication "On Spatial Pattern Matching", we investigated the retrieval of place combinations that satisfy some spatial constraints collectively and keyword searches individually. This is another model of spatial keyword search that has not received adequate attention to date. We defined appropriate search algorithms for this problem based on multiway spatial joins and spatio-textual indexing. We also developed a demo system for assessing the usefulness of this query type. Since the used indexes are dynamic to data changes, updates are also efficiently handled. This study was extended in journal paper "Evaluating Pattern Matching Queries for Spatial Databases", where efficient solutions to address two related problems: (1) find top-k matches that are close to a query location and (2) return partial matches for a query pattern. The results are directly related to Objectives 1, 2, and 3 of the project.

17253616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17253616.value: The project was very fruitful in terms of research results. We have published four journal papers and two conference papers in top venues of data management (SIGMOD, ICDE, VLDB Journal). The major findings of this project are as follows: 1) Spatial keyword search over RDF graphs retrieves highly relevant results and meets the expectation of users, according to our qualitative studies. In addition, we need specialized data structures and algorithms, for the efficient retrieval of query results, as brute-force solutions that first perform keyword search and then verify the spatial distance (and vice-versa) are performing slowly. We have successfully developed such methods by applying (i) branch-and-bound search, (ii) keyword reachability techniques for large graphs, (iii) augmentation of spatial access methods that capture the proximity of keywords to regions in space (SIGMOD 1996 paper). This work addresses objectives 1 and 2. 2) We developed appropriate extensions of the basic spatial keyword search model to consider a) temporal semantics (VLDBJ paper, July 2020) and b) diversification of results (VLDBJ paper, September 2020). In both cases, we developed appropriate data structures and algorithms for efficient query evaluation. Furthermore, we applied qualitative studies and user studies to prove the usefulness of the query and diversification models. These works address objectives 1 and 2. 3) We developed an appropriate encoding of location information into the identifiers of RDF entities, in order to avoid spatial indices as much as possible. Our developed spatial RDF management system (SRX VLDBJ paper, October 2019) greatly improves search performance compared to previous work, supports updates efficiently and can be easily transferred to a distributed environment, while supporting a wide range of query types. This work addresses objectives 2, 3, and 4. 4) The project initiated research on advanced spatial pattern search using keywords. We studied the retrieval of place combinations that satisfy some spatial constraints collectively and keyword searches individually (ICDE 2018 paper). We also developed a demo system for assessing the usefulness of this query type. Since the used indexes are dynamic to data changes, updates are also efficiently handled. We also developed an extension of the system to support additional types of searches based on spatial patterns and keywords (Pattern Matching VLDBJ paper, October 2019). This work addresses objectives 1, 2, and 3.

17253616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17253616.value: Our work motivates additional research directions in analyzing and searching geo-enriched RDF graphs. The challenge is the complex nature of the data, which calls not only for efficient indexing approaches but also for meaningful and practical search models that should be evaluated with real users. Our plan is to study the potential of further improving the quality of spatial RDF keyword search, by combining structured queries (in SPARQL) with subgraph search queries based on keywords, taking under consideration the location of the user. In addition, we plan to develop encoding models for the keyword identifiers similar to our encoding scheme for RDF entities.

17253616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17253616.value: Large knowledge bases like DBpedia include facts extracted from the web and organized as RDF graphs. Vertices of the graph are entities (subjects) are linked to other entities and/or values. Many entities include spatial semantics, enabling spatial search and analysis operations. Although structured query languages (like SPARQL) are available for RDF data, they are hard to use by users who are unfamiliar with the structure of the RDF graph. In this project, we have studied the problem of location-based retrieval of spatial entities in a knowledge base, considering their distance to a query location and their relevance to a set of query keywords. We have developed and evaluated a search model that gracefully combines the two components of the query and produce high-quality results. We also developed suitable data structures and algorithms for efficient retrieval. Our model has been extended to support temporal semantics and result diversification. Moreover, we have proposed an appropriate encoding scheme for the spatial information in the RDF graph and an additional spatial pattern operation based on keywords. The results of the project were published in top journals and conferences of data management, opening the road for further research in location-based retrieval over RDF knowledge bases.

17254016.label: Project Objectives
17254016.value: [Knowledge Base and Benchmarking] To evaluate the performance of TAQA, we need to collect a large number of n-tuple assertions and create an n-tuple OKB. We explore various ways of collecting assertions via web crawling. Moreover, we aim to collect at least 10,000 complex questions and to devise semi-automated methods to pair the questions with their corresponding gold-standard answers. All this data will form a valuable benchmark, which will benefit the research community in evaluating the performance of open KB-QA systems in answering complex questions. [Question paraphrasing, question parsing, query answering, and answer ranking] Answering questions in a KB-QA system is a complex process that involves many steps. In particular, question paraphrasing, question parsing, query answering and answer ranking are the most critical ones that need to be redesigned when we migrate from a triplet-OKB to an n-tuple OKB. We investigate new algorithms for implementing these steps. [Canonicalizing an n-tuple OKB] Open KBs that are extracted automatically from web sources using Open IE techniques are highly redundant in the sense that factual knowledge is often repeated and scattered across multiple assertions. This high-degree of redundancy makes the KB unnecessarily large and significantly slows down the response times. We investigate techniques that canonicalize an n-tuple OKB by removing redundant assertions and integrating related ones into integrated assertions. [Prototyping and evaluation] We integrate our research ideas by developing a prototype of TAQA. Extensive experiments will be conducted with TAQA to evaluate our ideas.

17254016.label: Realisation of objectives
17254016.value: There are four objectives of the project. Much of the details of the works done towards achieving the objectives have been previously reported in the progress reports. Here, we summarize these works. [Objective 1: Knowledge Base and Benchmarking] Our first objective is to explore automatic or semi-automatic methods for constructing a question-answer (QA) benchmark. We have devised a number of methods and have built a system implementing such methods. We have collected thousands of QA pairs whose answers are verified. These QA pairs are further classified into simple/complex questions. Also, we have devised methods that annotate questions in existing benchmarks. The idea is to categorize questions and label them with respect to certain identifiable features. For example, we have devised algorithms and a system that labels questions in terms of their complexity, length, and interrogatives among others. We have also done a statistical study on the correlation between these labels and how well KB-QA systems answer corresponding questions. Moreover, we have built a system that collects users’ feedback on questions. Specifically, given a question Q and an answer A returned by a KB-QA system, we ask a human user to provide further information about Q. This feedback includes e.g., a clarification of the entity and/or relation mentioned in Q. Based on the feedback, the system would modify the question to obtained a revised one Q’. The system then registers the revised answer A’ returned by the KB-QA system. The data obtained via question annotations and question feedback provide information for us to construct higher-quality benchmarks. These benchmarks data allows researchers to better understand the weaknesses of existing KB-QA system techniques. Our study on benchmark construction algorithms and question annotation are documented in four Masters’ dissertations. We have also published a paper documenting a prototype system that collects users’ feedback on questions. [Objective 2: Question paraphrasing, question parsing, query answering, and answer ranking] Our second objective is to improve the various steps of the KB-QA pipeline, which typically involves the steps of question paraphrasing, question parsing, query answering, and answer ranking. We studied these components to evaluate how they generally affect the performance of a KB-QA system. Such an analysis would allow us to focus on the component that has the biggest performance impact. We put forward and studied the question answerability problem: Given a question Q and a KB-QA system X, we say that Q is answerable by X if X returns a correct answer of Q. The answerability problem is about predicting the likelihood that a given question Q is answerable by a system X. We have devised algorithms for solving the question answerability problem. Moreover, based on our algorithms, we have designed a system called iQA, whose objective is to analyze a question Q and (if necessary) to engage the enquirer in minimal and simple interactions to improve the weakness component of the KB-QA system in answering Q. We published our findings in WSDM 2020 conference. [Objective 3: Knowledge base canonicalization] An open information extraction (open IE) system is a system that extracts information from corpora and store the extractions into a knowledge base. Such knowledge bases store the extractions in the form of triples: ⟨subject; predicate; object⟩, each is called an assertion. A problem of extracted KB is that a real-world entity could have multiple surface names across assertions. This leads to ambiguity and redundancy. Our third objective is to perform canonicalization on an extracted KB to group assertions based on the entities (despite their forms) they mention. We devised the FAC algorithm, which applies various pruning and bounding techniques that tremendously speed up the canonicalization process. Our results are published in ACM CIKM 2018 conference. In that paper we provide an in-depth analysis on our techniques. We show that our pruning strategies are particularly effective for datasets whose assertions form few but dense clusters. Through extensive experiments, we evaluated FAC over a number of large datasets. Our results show that our strategies are highly effective and scalable. [Objective 4: Prototyping and evaluation] We have built two prototype systems. The first one is an interactive KB-QA system, iQA, that analyzes questions, collects feedback from enquirers, and reformulates questions for more accurate answers. Our second prototype system is one that canonicalizes assertions. The prototype system also provides an interface for users to query the assertions and to view the canonicalization results.
