17254016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17254016.value: Our work in this project has resulted in multiple MSc and PhD dissertations and 6 conference publications. Our papers in WWW’17, WWW’18, and AAAI’19 study the problem the problem of clustering entities in heterogeneous information network (for which a knowledge base, such as Freebase, is an example). These works form a component in knowledge base canonicalization, which is based on cluster analysis. We put forward the SCHAIN algorithm for performing attributed entity clustering and the ROSC algorithm for clustering multi-scale data. Our paper in CIKM 2018 addressed the efficiency issue in KB canonicalization. The canonicalization problem was first put forward by Galarraga et al. In their approach, hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) is adopted to group assertions. Although they show that their approach is successful in entity resolution, their algorithm is quite slow. For example, in their experiments, canonicalizing a subset of 34K assertions extracted from ReVerb4 takes 15 minutes. When we scale the dataset to 250K assertions, the algorithm takes more than 10 hours to finish. It is thus impractical to apply their algorithm in real practical systems that consist of millions or even billions of assertions. We put forward the FAC algorithm, which employs various pruning and bounding techniques to speed up the canonicalization process. The FAC algorithm is orders-of-magnitude faster than other approaches. Our paper in WSDM’20 studies the various components of a KB-QA system pipeline. We study the intrinsic difficulty of a KB-QA system in answering questions. We put forward the problem of estimating the likelihood that a KB-QA system would successfully answer a given query and design the iQA system that interacts with a user in case the system suspects that the given query is unlikely to be answered correctly. iQA collect feedbacks from users to rectify a question. Our experiment shows that our approach can significantly improve KB-QA systems’ accuracies.

17254016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17254016.value: KB-QA systems are a hot research topic. It involves a number of interesting research areas such as machine learning, natural language processing, human-computer interaction, and machine comprehension. We are extending our research work and focusing on domain-specific question-answering systems. In particular, we are applying our techniques in legal knowledge management. One of the objectives is to extract legal knowledge from legal data so as to make it easily accessible to both legal professionals and the general public. We are also investigating the possibility of applying KB-QA systems to assist legal research.

17254016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17254016.value: A knowledge-based question-answering system (KB-QA) is one that answers natural language questions with information stored in a large-scale knowledge base (KB). Example applications of KB-QA systems include Apple Siri, IBM Watson, and Wolfram Alpha. While existing systems work fairly well in answering simple factoid questions, they fall short in answering questions with complex prepositional or adverbial constraints. In this project we focus on building KB-QA systems that can handle large-scale KBs and complex natural language questions. We study in-depth the various components of a KB-QA system and propose various approaches and algorithms to improve KB-QA systems’ efficiency and accuracy.

17255016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17255016.value: In recent years, there has been an increasing demand for high-performance steels for the construction of energy-efficient and lightweight structures in aerospace and automotive industries. High-performance steels, in general, require ultrahigh strength as well as good ductility. Nevertheless, strength and ductility are mutually exclusive. It is extremely challenging to design an ultrahigh strength steel with good tensile ductility, especially steels with yield strength higher than 2 GPa. The present project, for the first time, proposes a new method to meet such a challenge to produce an ultrastrong and ductile steel with a yield strength of 2.1 GPa and an unexpected large tensile uniform elongation of 20%. To the best of our knowledge, this steel may be the best so far in terms of the combination of yield strength and uniform elongation compared to those reported in the open literature. The present novel steel possesses a dual-phase hierarchical nanostructure consisting of nanosized precipitates, nanotwins, and lamellar nano- and ultrafine-grained austenite and ferrite. This novel steel has been strengthened by all the available strengthening mechanisms, including solid-solution, precipitation, dislocations, grain boundary and twin boundary strengthening. Besides dislocation plasticity, the novel steel also experiences transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) as well as twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP). In other words, all available strengthening mechanisms and plasticity modes have been incorporated. The extremely high yield strength is achieved by the combination of the multiple hierarchical strengthening mechanisms, while the excellent ductility is due to the combination of dislocation plasticity, TRIP and TWIP. More importantly, different to other lab-scale methods of producing ultrahigh strength alloys, such as the severe plasticity deformation (SPD) technique, the present novel steel has been produced by conventional processing routes currently used in the steel industry. No additional facilities are required for the steel industry to produce this novel steel, which will facilitate its future industrial application. However, the fundamental understanding of the deformation mechanism and microstructure-property relationship of the novel steel has not yet been accomplished. For instance, the quantitative contribution of each strengthening mechanism on the yield strength is not known. The quantitative contributions of dislocation plasticity, TRIP and TWIP on the macroscopic stress-strain behaviour have also not yet been studied. Consequently, the aim of the proposed project will be to provide systematic experimental and modelling investigations towards the fundamental understanding of the deformation mechanism and microstructure-property relationship of the novel steel, leading to potential industrial application in the near future. 高性能鋼鐵材料可以幫助汽車和航空界實現結構輕量化和提高能源效率，是結構材料領域的研究熱點之一。高性能鋼鐵材料一般要求超高強度，同時也需要兼備好的韌性。對於超高強度的鋼鐵材料，特別是屈服強度高於2 GPa的鋼鐵材料，要保證它們的拉伸塑性是非常具有挑戰性的。本項目首次提出一種全新的鋼鐵材料設計生產理念，用於設計和生產一種超強度的鋼鐵材料（屈服強度為2.1GPa），同時獲得非常出色的均勻延伸率（20%）。在我們所知的文獻範圍內，對比綜合屈服強度和均勻延伸率，該新型鋼鐵材料很可能是目前最好的鋼鐵材料。 本項目所發明的新型鋼鐵材料具有多尺度、雙相納米微觀結構。微觀組織包含納米尺寸的沉澱析出相、納米孿晶、層狀的納米及亞微米奧氏體和鐵素體。該新型鋼鐵材料採用了所有的強化機理，包括固溶強化、沉澱強化、位錯強化、晶界強化、孿晶強化。另外，該新型鋼鐵材料同時也採用了多種塑性變形機制，包括位錯、相變誘導塑性(TRIP)、孿生誘導塑性。換句話說，該新型鋼鐵材料採用了所有的強化機制和塑性機制，所以獲得超高的強度和很好的塑性。這裡值得指出的一點是生產該新型鋼鐵材料所需的工藝設備都是目前鋼鐵工業界所普遍採用的工藝，不需要額外的設備來生產該新型鋼鐵材料。這點與大變形(SPD)工藝製備高強材料完全不同，這是因為SPD工藝適合實驗室製備小樣品，很難進行大規模工業化應用。基於這點分析，該新型鋼鐵材料將來很有可能在工業界得到廣泛的應用。 然而，目前對該新型鋼鐵材料的變形機理和微觀組織結構-性能關係還缺乏深入的基礎研究。例如，各種強化機制對屈服強度的貢獻並沒有研究結果。同時，位錯塑性、相變誘導塑性、孿晶誘導塑性對宏觀應力-應變的貢獻也是未知的。因此本項目的目的是對該新型鋼鐵材料的變形機理以及微觀組織結構-性能關係進行深入的試驗及模擬基礎研究，為將來的工業應用提供堅實的理論基礎。

17255516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17255516.value: Drainage systems in many cities are inadequate, particularly when future climate and land use changes are considered. Upgrades and retrofits are therefore often required to minimize flooding. Hard engineered retrofits are effective in draining water but are not environmentally friendly. Low impact development (LID) practices use semi-natural on-site controls (e.g., bioretention systems, vegetated swale, and porous pavements) to enhance infiltration and retention. LID practices have recently received more attention, and their effectiveness in reducing stormwater peak runoff and pollutant load are now commonly recognized. However, research has shown that LID practices cannot manage stormwater alone, and convectional stormwater drainage structures (CSDS) are still essential, particularly in extreme storm events. To retrofit existing drainage systems in a more environmentally sustainable way, both CSDS and LID practices should be implemented. However, standardized design manuals and detailed design procedures are not currently available for the integration of LID and CSDS. This project will develop a LID/CSDS simulation-optimization framework, which can provide an optimal overall retrofit plan (e.g., layout of retrofit measures) and detailed optimal designs (e.g., type and dimension of each LID practice). The system-wide optimization problem will be broken down to several smaller problems, to reduce complexity and computational cost. Geographic information system (GIS) tools will first be used to divide the watershed-scale study site into several plot-scale blocks, and to identify potential retrofit locations and options. Plot-scale LID practice hydrological/hydraulic models will then be built to simulate and optimize the detailed LID practice design. Next, a watershed-scale CSDS/LID practice simulation-optimization model will be developed, connecting each plot-scale block by CSDS. Algorithms will be used to find the optimal retrofit solution, with information exchange between the plot-scale and watershed-scale optimization. The LID/CSDS simulation-optimization framework will be applied to four cities with different natural and urbanization characteristics. The potential benefits in surface water quality improvement and rainwater harvesting from the LID of these cities will also be examined. Finally, an adaptive multi-criteria decision analysis framework will be combined with the simulation-optimization framework to account for social-environmental considerations and possible future changes. This project explores the best LID retrofits to existing drainage systems, and will provide sustainable, robust, and flexible urban drainage solutions to cities worldwide. The four case studies and the insights generated can serve as a reference or roadmap to future, green, drainage systems.

17255516.label: Realisation of objectives
17255516.value: This project has three major objectives, all of which have been successfully achieved. 1. Objective 1. Objective 1 aims to develop an integrated modelling system that is capable of simulating the hydrological/hydraulic processes in both the conventional stormwater drainage structures (CSDS) and the low impact development (LID) practices. The existing modelling tools and methods were first reviewed, and several challenges were identified. Data-driven methods and model coupling were then identified as potential solutions, based on which new modelling tools and methods were developed. The first challenge was related to the difficulties in characterizing the complex hydrological processes in LID practices. In the commonly used process-based models, the involved hydrological processes are characterized using physically-based or empirical equations. However, due to the high complexity of the involved hydrological processes, the prediction accuracy of these models can be affected by their structure or insufficient measurement data for model setup. Data-driven methods do not require the information on the involved processes of the studied system. They can be trained to learn the correlations between the state variables of a system given only observation data. However, they have been rarely used in LID related studies due to challenges of high-dimensional data and uncertainties in model training. In this research, a specific type of data-driven methods, deep learning method, was used to solve problems associated with high dimensional data. Additionally, a study to compare the uncertainties of various data-driven methods was conducted. These studies showed that data-driven models can achieve comparable or higher prediction accuracies when compared to calibrated process-based models. The second challenge was the lack of integration of the modelling tools built for the LID practices and the CSDS. The LID practices models are typical of small scales and may be coupled with CSDS models to simulate large-scale drainage systems. However, there exist few tools to support the coupling of the LID practices models and the CSDS models. This project developed a method to couple practices LID models and a popular urban drainage model — SWMM. A file-based coupling method is used, in which the output hydrographs of the areas controlled by LID practices are modelled by a LID practices model. These outputs are then used as input flows to SWMM in the form of routing interface files. This project also developed open-source software to implement the proposed coupling method. In summary, this project improved the flexibility of the current LID modelling practices by adopting data-driven methods, and a set of methods and software were developed to enable the use of different LID practices models with CSDS models in catchment-scale studies. Therefore, objective 1 was successfully addressed. 2. Objective 2. Research objective 2 aims to develop tools for optimizing the designs of LID practices considering the CSDS networks. The limitations of the current LID performance evaluation framework to support multi-objective optimization were first reviewed, and then the relative performance evaluation (RPE) methods were identified as a potential solution. In addition, optimization algorithms were coupled with the modelling system developed earlier to solve the LID design optimization problems. It is essential to collectively account for the multiple benefits provided by LID practices during optimization. However, most of the current performance assessment frameworks of LID practices involve a tedious parametrization process for valuing the intangible hydro-environmental impacts and do not explicitly account for the preferences of stakeholders. This research developed a comprehensive assessment framework that uses RPE methods to tackle this challenge. In this framework, the performance of a LID design option for each impact of interest is measured by its relative effectiveness as compared to the other considered options. The relative effectiveness obtained for different impacts can be then aggregated to derive the overall effectiveness of a design option. During aggregation, specific weights can be assigned to different impacts to reflect the preferences of stakeholders. The framework was used in several case studies, the details of which are presented in the section below. The modelling system developed earlier can be extended easily due to its modular structure. This research coupled a metaheuristic optimization algorithm, AMALGAM, with the modelling system to identify the optimal size of each roadside bioretention cell in a treatment train for minimizing runoff volume. Moreover, the comprehensive assessment framework was coupled with the modelling system to form an integrated simulation-optimization framework for identifying the optimal type and location of LID practices in urban a catchment considering the existing CSDS networks. In summary, this project improved the current performance assessment framework for LID practices by incorporating RPE methods. And then optimization algorithms and performance framework were coupled with the modelling system developed earlier to form a comprehensive simulation-optimization framework. Thus, objective 2 was successfully addressed. 3. Objective 3. Research objective 3 aims to apply the comprehensive simulation-optimization framework developed in this project to various studies and to generate insights to support future drainage system designs. To accomplish this goal, several cases studies were conducted to identify optimal implementation levels of LID practices to concurrently achieve multiple stormwater quality and quantity management targets, and to develop useful methods to support the design optimization of LID practices in various contexts. A case study in New York City was conducted, and the results indicate that both bioretention cells and green roofs can effectively alleviate the negative hydro-environmental effects of urbanization, such as increased surface runoff volumes and high flows. The effectiveness of a green roof that covers the whole catchment in terms of stormwater management equalled that of a bioretention of 3% to 5% of the area of the green roof. The benefits provided by a bioretention cell were roughly doubled when its surface area increased from 2% to 10% of the catchment area. A case study of Hong Kong was conducted to identify the optimal surface and contributing areas of bioretention cells that concurrently achieve multiple performance targets. The results showed that bioretention cells were effective at reducing first flush and runoff volume and that the performance of peak flow reduction varied in storms of different intensities. Even bioretention cells with large implementation areas may not be able to replace the CSDS and may not lower the design standard of the CSDS. To select a suitable LID practice type and its surface area during the preliminary design phase, it is necessary to rapidly estimate the hydrologic performance of various LID practices designs under design storms. This project thus proposed a method for rapid assessment of the hydrologic performance of various LID practices under the design storms across the U.S. The simulation-optimization framework was also used in identifying the optimal layout of the LID practice in existing CSDS, designing the optimal LID treatment train, selecting the optimal LID practices and storage unit combinations to minimize peak flow, and assessing the robustness of current LID practices design standard under climate change scenarios and shallow groundwater environment, etc. In conclusion, the simulation-optimization framework was used in a number of case studies in catchments of various geographic conditions, climatic characteristics, and urban development settings. The effectiveness of various LID design options was assessed, and the optimal designs were identified. The insights generated from this research can be useful for developing sustainable, robust, and flexible urban drainage solutions to cities worldwide. Thus, the objective 3 was successfully addressed.

17255516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17255516.value: This research project focuses on developing a comprehensive simulation-optimization framework for optimizing the design of low impact development (LID) practices. As listed in Part C, this research project has generated four peer-reviewed research articles in leading international journals, more than 10 conference publications, and a set of open-source software. This project has trained two PhD students. The major outcome and findings are discussed as follow. A comprehensive simulation-optimization framework was developed in this research project. It consists of process-based models, data-driven models, relative performance evaluation (RPE) methods, and optimization algorithms. The framework overcomes several common challenges confronting the modelling and assessment of LID practices. First, the accuracy of process-based hydrological models is sometimes affected by their model structures and the availability of field measurements. Data-driven models used the framework alleviate this problem by directly modelling the statistical correlation between rainfall and the hydrological responses of LID practices, the applications of which are presented in conference publications #10 and #13. Second, most of the current performance assessment frameworks do not explicitly account for the preferences of stakeholders. The RPE methods used in the framework solve this problem by allowing the preferences of stakeholders to be reflected in the weights assigned to the relative performances of the LID design options. Journal papers #1 and #3 presents the applications of the RPE methods. The framework has been used in various case studies to identify robust, cost-effective, and sustainable drainage solutions in cities worldwide. These include optimal sizing of bioretention cells in Hong Kong (journal paper #1), optimal type and surface areas of various types of LID practices in New York City (journal paper #3), and optimal layout of LID practices considering existing drainage networks (conference paper #11). The insights generated from the case studies can serve as a reference to future, green drainage systems. Several methods and open source-software were generated from this research, including a method to rapidly estimate the hydrological performances under design storms (journal paper #2) and a piece of software to couple various LID models with a popular stormwater model, SWMM (journal paper #4). The methods and software can be useful to researchers and engineers. In conclusion, the simulation-optimization framework developed in this project improves the current practices of identifying and deriving optimal LID designs. This research contributes to the realization of sustainable development of cities by prompting a greener way to manage urban stormwater.

17255516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17255516.value: This research project developed a comprehensive simulation-optimization framework, which comprises of process-based hydrological/hydraulic models, data-driven models, relative performance evaluation methods, and optimization algorithms. The modular structure of the framework allows its components to be updated easily. Future research can verify the usefulness of various models and methods in the framework when applied to different case studies in cities worldwide, or further extend the framework by coupling it ecological models to investigate the impacts of LID practices on urban ecosystems. Various types of LID practices were found to be effective in managing the quality and quantity of stormwater runoffs, however, their efficiency can drop considerably during heavy storms. Thus, the simulation-optimization framework can be applied to examine the effectiveness of LID practices under climate change scenarios, where rainfall pattern changes. This project uses the relative performance evaluation method to allow the preferences of decision-makers and stakeholders to be reflected in the assessment results of the hydro-environmental impacts of LID practice. However, this high level of engagement requires the model results and the hydro-environmental consequences to be effectively communicated among decision-makers, stakeholders, and researchers. Further studies on effective communication in the context of LID design evaluation are recommended.

17255516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17255516.value: Low impact development (LID) practices refer to sustainable urban drainage systems, which manage urban stormwater runoffs through natural drainage processes, such as interception and infiltration. LID practices, compared to the conventional stormwater drainage infrastructures, offer additional water quality improvement benefits. This research project explores the roles of LID practices in retrofitting and improving the current urban drainage systems. A comprehensive simulation-optimization framework was developed in this project, which derives the optimal overall retrofit plan and the optimal detailed designs of the practices through a computer modelling approach. In addition, relative performance evaluation methods are used in this framework to allow the preferences of stakeholders to be accounted for during the comparison of design options. The framework has been adopted in various cases studies in cities worldwide, such as Hong Kong and New York City, to identify robust, cost-effective, and sustainable drainage solutions. The insights generated from the case studies can serve as a reference to future, green drainage systems. In summary, this study contributes to the development of urban sustainability schemes at the catchment scale, which increase the resilience of cities in managing their stormwater against the uncertainty of climate change, and the inevitable increase in development.

17255916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17255916.value: 恶劣气象条件，如暴风雪，台风，龙卷风等造成的高压线路故障经常会导致大规模的断电事故。这些事故在包括中国在内的世界各地时有发生。2008年中国雪灾导致的大规模电力中断造成了超过1000亿元的损失，也因此促进了学者开始研究对高压电缆线路的实时监控。其中一个重要的难题是这些实时监控系统本身需要一定功率的电源供应。之前有一些在线监控系统使用太阳能技术提供能源，但是并不能够稳定有效地投入实用。主要原因是在国内的气候条件下，每年有连续多个月阴雨天气导致太阳能能源不够稳定。因此，在这个系统上十分需要一个可靠的可以提供连续稳定的能源的技术。由于实时监控系统直接挂靠在高压线路上，所以从高压线路上直接取电然后供应给监控系统是个可能的方案。 在这个方案中最大的挑战在于取电装置是在高压线路甚至是超高压线路上（22kV至500kV），而监控装置是安装在铁塔上。两者之间需要有1.5米至3米的安全距离（基于IEC标准，普通环境每千伏16mm距离，重度污染环境每千伏31mm距离）。在这个距离上直接使用能量收集的方法，或者是直接无线能量传输的方式，无论是使用磁场还是电场都不能够保证效率。 本研究项目提出一个陶瓷、强化玻璃或复合材料组成的高耐压绝缘子串结构，其内部嵌有中继共振线圈。利用短程中继无线输电的方法可以在保证较高效率的情况下，将一定功率的能量传输较长的距离。绝缘子串的结构可以是刚性的或者是柔性的。刚性的绝缘子串可以代替现有的绝缘子串对输电线机械支撑。柔性的绝缘子串可以跨在已有的引流跳线到铁塔横梁上。 本研究项目同时关注在两点上，第一是无线能量传输，第二是高压绝缘的能力。 之前的一些初步研究已经证实了满足这两点的技术可行性。本方案提出的可用于的无线输电的刚性或柔性绝缘子串结构是全新的设计。中继共振线圈可以（1）将绝缘子前后链接形成绝缘子串，或者（2）将绝缘子串在绝缘棒上，形成本项目提出的无线输电绝缘子串。这样的无线输电绝缘子串提供一条由安装在输电线路上的能量采集装置到安装在铁塔上的监控装置的无线能量传输的引导通路。本方案是中短程中继共振无线输电的一个新应用，并提供较好的能量效率。

17255916.label: Realisation of objectives
17255916.value: For objective 1, we have successfully designed and tested several hardware prototypes comprising AC-DC power converter to turn the harvested energy into a DC voltage source, an high-frequency DC-AC power converter for driving the transmitter coil-resonator and a series of relay coil-resonators in a domino form as the wireless power flow path, and a receiver coil-resonator with a diode rectifier and DC load. The initial tests were successfully conducted at HKU and some high-voltage tests were done with the help of Guangdong Power of China Southern Power Grid. In our HKU tests, we confirmed the idea of energy harvested can be wirelessly transmitted through a high-voltage insulation string structures with embedded coil-resonators. The transmitted power in our tests exceeded 20W. We also demonstrated in our video submitted with our Journal-Paper-1 that the transmitted power can wirelessly power an online monitoring camera. This video demonstration was shown during my Keynote Speech presented in November 2020 in the joint IEEE Wireless Power Conference held in Seoul, Korea. After the feasibility of the proposal has been confirmed, for objective 2, we focused on the optimal design and operation. We conducted a detailed circuit analysis and examined the frequency-dependent impedance and frequency-dependent energy efficiency of the proposed system. It was found that high-efficiency can be achieved when the operating frequency exceeds about 400kHz. We designed a system that can operate in the range from 300kHz to 500kHz for practical evaluation. We demonstrated that an energy efficiency above 50% could be achieved. We had the help of an industrial company to embed the coil-resonators into the insulation discs, with which we repeated our tests. It was found that the insulation materials covering the coil-resonators do not affect the wireless power capability of the relay-resonators. With the successes in achieving objectives 1 and 2, we turned to the study of the high-voltage capability of the new insulation strings according to objective 3. With the help of Guangdong Power, our hardware setup was tested in the high-voltage facilities of the China Southern Power Grid. It was found that at about 600kW, electric arc discharge could occur and damage the discrete capacitor. This important results imply that discrete capacitors should not be used in the coil-resonators. This prompted us to look into the new designs of Printed-Circuit-Board (PCB) coil-resonators. The PCB resonators have the advantages that the inductance and capacitance in the resonator is distributed, thus avoiding local electric discharge. We have the design procedure of such PCB resonators reported in Journal-Paper-5. In the process of this investigation, I have also investigated the future application aspects, the safety aspects of the wireless power transfer issues in the other three journal papers (Journal-Paper-2,3,4). These aspects are relevant to the proposed idea in terms of the future commercialization potential.

17255916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17255916.value: In this project, we have investigated a new high-voltage insulation string structure with embedded coil-resonators for wireless power transfer (WPT) functions. This new idea was briefly discussed in my invited 2016 journal paper (Journal-paper-2) as part of future trend of wireless power applications in the Inaugural Issue of CPES. After the hardware implementation of the idea, the feasibility of the proposal has been proven in both theoretical/simulation studies and practical evaluation. These results were reported in 2018 (Journal-paper-1). In the process of research investigation, we discovered that in a multi-coil WPT system, we can use switching actions to develop Reconfigurable WPT to achieve wide load range. This discovery was reported in a 2018 journal paper (Journal-paper-3). In addition, we also addressed the general but important safety issues in a 2018 article in the IEEE EMC magazine. Based on this proposal, we obtained the support from Guangdong Power Company (part of China Southern Power Grid) to assist us in building a prototype for high-voltage tests in their HV test laboratory. China Southern Power Grid independently confirmed the wireless power transfer capability of our proposal. HKU has filed 3 patent applications on our behalf. The initial results indicated that discrete capacitors cannot be used at a high voltage above 550kV, because electric arc discharge could occurs between the leads of the capacitors. This important test information prompted us to study the double-layer printed-circuit-board (PCB) resonators. We just submitted a paper (Journal-paper-4) to IEEE on this aspect. China Southern Power Grid tested this PCB resonators and found that no corona discharge occurred even at 600kV. HKU has filed two patent applications on this invention.

17255916.value: The next step is to develop the complete solution for demonstration and attracting industrial interests for commercialization.

17255916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17255916.value: Increasing online monitoring systems have been mounted on the high-voltage transmission towers for a monitoring weather conditions, bush fires, operating conditions of the power transmission systems etc. Prior to this project, the power supply for these monitoring systems solely depend on solar or wind energy (that is weather-dependent). In this project, we have confirmed the feasibility of harvesting energy from the magnetic field around high-current cables in high-voltage towers. Such energy can be wireless transferred through printed-circuit-board coil-resonators embedded in the insulation string structure. This invention provides, for the first time, an weather-independent power supply to power the online monitoring systems mounted on the high-voltage transmission towers for ensuing safety and reliability of the power systems. The feasibility of this invention has been independently confirmed by power industry.

17256516.label: Project Objectives
17256516.value: To develop a systematic cooperative control method, in particular, to design fully responsive and non-disruptive load-side controllers to maintain frequency stability for a system with high renewables. To develop an effective identification method to model the dynamics of aggregate loads in transmission networks. To establish new frequency stability criteria for power systems with the designed load-side controllers and high renewables, and identify the system capability of absorbing renewable power.

17256516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17256516.value: Modern power systems have worked under highly stressed conditions and are more fragile to contingencies. With the recent power blackouts taking place worldwide (e.g. American Queens and European blackouts in 2006 and the most recent blackout in July 2012 in India), stability is becoming an increasingly important issue. To operate a stable power system, the basic requirement is to keep a stable frequency at its nominal value by maintaining instantaneous power balance between generation and demand. To achieve this requirement, traditional power systems control generation to follow demand changes. However, the integration of renewables challenges the limits in capability of this control paradigm. Moreover, different countries announced their long-term plans to increase renewables capacity in order to reduce emissions of greenhouse gas. These plans will continuously increase the risk of instability for power systems. In addition, in order to accommodate the increasing penetration of renewables, the balancing costs may increase significantly. The concept of load-side control or demand response provides new opportunities and cost-effective way to all of these issues by creating a new control paradigm that demand follows generation. But there is a lack of systematic analysis and design method to integrate load-side control into a system without bringing new issues. The proposed research aims to establish a new framework for frequency control and stability analysis by using load-side controllers, and to build a more reliable and cost-effective power system with high renewables. The research project will integrate distributed control, cooperative control, switching control and event-triggered control to develop a systematic load-side control method to secure power system operation with high renewables. We will focus on transmission networks, and extend the obtained results to the entire grid. The designed controllers will be fully responsive to contingencies and non-disruptive to end-users. Particular attention will be given to the design of an optimal communication network for implementing distributed control of controllable loads and how neighboring controllable loads share useful information effectively. New frequency stability criteria will be established based on a nonlinear system model and the designed controllers by combining results and methods developed in power systems, control systems, network science and optimization theory. The obtained results will help us discover the limits in capabilities that how much renewable power a system can absorb with the designed load-side controllers. 隨着經濟及工業的高速發展，現今電力系統的運作已經接近飽和狀態，其抗干擾能力大大減低。近年來世界各國陸續發生大規模的停電事故（例如︰2006年美國紐約皇后區停電事故、2006年歐洲大陸停電事故以及2012年7月印度停電事故）。因此，如何確保電力系統的穩定性變得愈來愈重要。要保持電力系統運作安全及穩定，我們必須控制發電量及用電需求的平衡，使系統的頻率鎖定在一個恆常值。 傳統的電力系統是通過控制發電站的電力生產水平以達致電量供求平衡。但是，未來的智能電網將會引入大量可再生能源，使這種傳統的控制策略不能再次採用。另外，為了減少溫室氣體的排放，世界各國紛紛宣布了增加可再生能源容量的長期計劃。這些計劃將進一步增加電力系統遭受不穩定性的風險。同時，為消納這些持續增長的可再生能源而產生的費用也將急劇增高。需求方控制或需求方響應技術開創了需求方跟隨發電方的新型控制結構。目前，我們還缺乏一種有效和低成本的系統分析和設計方案來解決以上問題。因此，本研究項目的宗旨是利用用電需求管理技術開發一種全新的電力系統頻率控制與穩定性分析的理論框架。本研究項目將整合分佈式控制方法、協同控制方法、切換控制方法以及事件驅動控制方法來開發一套用電需求管理的方案，使現有的電力系統能夠採納更多可再生能源。與此同時，電力系統可以在更安全、可靠、及低成本之下運行。 我們先將本研究項目應用在輸電網絡，然後逐漸拓展到整個電網中。本研究項目所設計的控制器不但能有效地克服因干擾或故障而引致系統的不穩定性（即是對干擾或故障的全響應特性），而且能大幅度降低干擾或故障對終端用戶的影響（即是對用戶的無干擾特性）。本研究項目的另一重點是優化通訊網絡結構，使相鄰的可控負載能有效地傳遞訊息，來實踐一個高效能的負載控制器。我們將結合電力系統、控制系統、網絡科學以及優化理論等領域，利用電力系統的非線性模型和所設計的負載控制器，來建立電力系統頻率穩定性的準則。而所得的理論和數據可幫助計算電力系統可以採納可再生能源的最大水平，並分析該負載控制器的極限。

17256516.label: Realisation of objectives
17256516.value: This project has proposed a new frequency control framework for power systems by coordinating different types of controllable devices. The three objectives have been divided into small targets which were accomplished one by one. These includes power balance management, conventional generator-side control improvements, renewable generator controller design, load-side controller design, cooperative control between different controllable devices, granular control, distributed event-based communication design, aggregate load modelling, and stability analysis. The research accomplishments are summarized in 11 journal papers and 4 conference papers. Regarding journal papers, one published in Automatica as regular paper; three in IEEE Trans. Automatic Control; one in IEEE Trans. Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems; one in International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems; two in IEEE Control Systems Letters; one in IET Generation, Transmission & Distribution; one in Electric Power Systems Research; and one in Asian Journal of Control. The following are the details of the realization. Distributed algorithm for power balance management. A generalized mathematical model for power balance control problem, i.e., distributed robust resource allocation has been investigated. The worst-case scenario has been studied to guarantee the robustness. A continuous-time distributed projected-based algorithm has been designed to solve the problem [Part C Conference Cp2]. This idea has been used to solve the multi-time slot economic dispatch (MTSED) problem for power systems with synchronous generators (SGs) and energy storage units (ESUs). Again, a distributed projection-based algorithm has been proposed to solve the problem which achieves two targets. First, it is to optimally coordinate the active power of SGs and ESUs to meet a certain net load demand profile over a finite time horizon. Second, it is to enforce physical constraints on the active power of all controllable units, ramping rates of SGs, energy stored in ESUs, and power flows along transmission lines [Part C Conference Cp3]. Generator-side control improvements. To improve the frequency control performance for multi-area power systems, novel event-triggered control approaches have been developed to replace the traditionally periodic sampling/communication mechanism in automatic generation control (AGC). For each control area, decentralized event-triggering conditions that only depend on locally available information have been designed for the control center to determine time instants when to sample the frequency and when to broadcast corresponding information. A periodical and dwell-time based triggering conditions have been designed in [Part C Conference Cp1] and [Part C Journal Jp4], respectively. The latter one has also been extended to deal with uncertainties caused by renewables to guarantee L∞-gain of the system in [Part C Journal Jp5]. Control of renewable generators. To address the challenging issue of wind power regulation, an artificial intelligence (AI) enabled control scheme has been developed to optimally coordinate all wind turbines in wind power plants. Distinguished from the conventional optimization-based methods, online control is achieved via the proposed framework. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control framework and suggests a high potential of AI edge computing in future wind power management [Part C Conference Cp4]. Optimal distributed frequency control. A novel distributed frequency control algorithms for multi-area power systems with different types of controllable units such as SGs, flexible loads and ESUs has be developed to deal with frequency issues caused by renewables [Part C Journal Jp6]. Further, to make system variables such as the power output/consumption of each controllable unit, ramping rates of SGs, and stored energy levels of ESUs meet their operational constraints, a novel distributed model predictive control method has been designed, which was also implemented by a distributed projection-based algorithm [Part C Journal Jp7]. Load-side controller design and cooperative control between generator-side controller and load-side controller. Frequency regulation by using both AGC and load-side control has been studied for multi-area power systems. A switched distributed control method has been developed for the load-side controller design to overcome the two conflict targets, i.e., to be fully responsive and to be non-disruptive. Particularly, the distributed consensus idea has been used to achieve the first target, whereas the switching control idea has been used to achieve the second target. Cooperative control between the new designed load-side controller and the existing AGC has been established to regulate frequency and the tie-line powers between control areas [Part C Journal Jp2]. Granular control. Loads in transmission networks are aggregations of lower voltage networks. Therefore, the load-side control scheme in transmission networks needs to be granulated down to subtransmission networks. However, both frequency and bus voltage will be affected by active power changes in subtransmission networks due to a higher R/X ratio of transmission lines. To overcome these issues, granular frequency control schemes has been developed where a distributed leader-following consensus algorithm has been designed for each ES aggregator to obtain the new active power setpoint, and decentralized PI control has been adopted for each ES aggregator to avoid the consequent voltage variation [Part C Journal Jp1]. Distributed event-based communication design. To implement distributed control, communication mechanism between cyber-connected buses has been studied. To overcome drawbacks of conventional periodic sampling/communication methods, distributed event-triggered control methods have been developed from different research aspects. Dynamical event-triggered control method for multi-agent systems have been developed to achieve consensus without Zeno behavior [Part C Journal Jp3]. A synchronization scheme via event-triggered aperiodic intermittent control has been proposed for master-slave chaotic systems [Part C Journal Ja2]. A discrete-time novel event-triggered communication mechanism has been designed for distributed optimization problem with input feedforward passivity properties [Part C Journal Jp8]. Aggregate model for smart loads. Aggregate load models consisting of frequency dependent loads, constant power loads, and flexible loads have been used in load-side controller design [Part C Journal Jp2] and distributed optimal frequency controller design [Part C Journal Jp6, Jp7]. Further, an aggregate model for smart loads with ESs has been used in subtransmission networks to discover effects of controllable loads in substransmission networks [Part C Journal Jp1]. Stability analysis for generator-side frequency control with event-triggered control. Frequency stability analysis of power systems under different types of event-triggered control methods has been investigated. Sufficient stability criteria have been established for multi-area power systems with event-triggered based communications. Thresholds for the periodic [Part C Conference Cp1] and dwell-time [Part C Journal Jp4] based event-triggered control have been identified to guarantee small signal stability. Sufficient stability criterion for L-infinity stability with essentially bounded net load disturbances has also been established [Part C Journal Jp5]. Stability analysis for distributed optimal frequency control. Studies on asymptotic stability of power systems with distributed optimal frequency control algorithm have been carried out. The nonlinear structure-preserving models including the first-order turbine-governor dynamics has been used to describe the dynamics of the whole system. Sufficient conditions under which the closed-loop system is asymptotic stability has been established by using Lyapunov function method and optimization theory [Part C Journal Jp6]. Stability for hybrid systems. The closed-loop systems of power systems with event-triggered/switching controller are hybrid systems. Therefore, stability analysis of hybrid systems has also been carried out. Stabilization to exponential input-to-state stability via aperiodic intermittent control has been studied in [Part C Journal Jp9]. Also, contraction analysis for stochastic switched impulsive systems (SSISs) has been studied in [Part C Journal Ja1]. Criteria on almost sure contraction has been established for SSISs by using Ito’s formula and martingale theory and by the Lyapunov-like function method, respectively.

17256516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17256516.value: The major findings are summarised in the following 5 aspects. Generator-side controller design. Event-triggered control approaches have been developed to replace the traditional periodic sampling/communication mechanism in AGC for multi-area power systems, which includes periodical event-triggered control [Part C Conference Cp1], dwell-time based event-triggered control [Part C Journal Jp4], and L-infinity gain guaranteed event-triggered control [Part C Journal Jp5]. An artificial intelligence control scheme has been developed to optimally coordinate wind turbines. Load-side controller design. Switched distributed control methods have been developed for the load-side controller design to achieve two targets, i.e., to be fully responsive and to be non-disruptive [Part C Journal Jp1, Jp2], where the combined switching distributed consensus control idea was used to balance the two conflict targets. Cooperative controller design. A generalized model for power balance control problem has been solved by a distributed projected-based algorithm [Part C Conference Cp2]. This idea was further used to solve multi-time slot economic dispatch problem for power systems with different types of controllable devices [Part C Conference Cp3]. Cooperative control between generator-side controllers and load-side controllers has been developed [Part C Journal Jp2]. Distributed optimal frequency control [Part C Journal Jp6] and distributed model predictive frequency control [Part C Journal Jp7] have been established to coordinate contributions from different controllable devices. Granular control and aggregate load model. To implement the load-side controllers designed for transmission networks in a more practical way, granular control methods between transmission and subtransmission networks have been developed where each subtransmission network is treated as an aggregate load to derive the load-side control signal in the transmission network. Aggregate model for smart loads with electric springs has been established [Part C Journal Jp1]. Event-trigger based communication mechanism design. Different types of distributed event-triggered control mechanisms have been developed to solve communication issues in distributed control. This includes dynamical event-triggered control for multiple agent system [Part C Journal Jp3], event-triggered aperiodic intermittent control for synchronization [Part C Journal Ja2], and discrete-time event-triggered communication for distributed optimization problem [Part C Journal Jp8]. Stability analysis. Stability analysis has been carried out for power systems with proposed control methods as well as hybrid systems that includes power systems with hybrid nature as special cases. Stability criteria for power systems with generator-side event-triggered based frequency control [Part C Conference Cp1, Journal Jp4, Jp5], distributed optimal frequency control [Part C Journal Jp6] and for hybrid systems have been established [Part C Journal Jp9, Ja1].

17256516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17256516.value: With load-side controllers and new devices connected to the grid at different voltage level, load dynamics will change much faster than ever before, and thus angle, frequency, and voltage issues will be strongly coupled. For one thing, the fast response property of the load-side controllers may help to solve angle stability issues after a severe contingency. For another thing, as smart loads may also have ability to regulate voltage, the designed load-side control can also apply to deal with voltage issues.

17256516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17256516.value: A key issue for operating a stable power system is to keep instantaneous power balance between generation and demand. To achieve this, the frequency whose deviation indicates power imbalance has to be maintained nearly constant during normal conditions and within a specified range under abnormal conditions. Otherwise, load shedding may be started to restore frequency, and customers may be affected. If this cannot stop frequency dropping, protection systems may disconnect generators to protect them from physical damage, which may further enlarge power deficiency and lead to cascading failures or blackouts. To maintain frequency, traditional control method makes generation follow demand. But the high inter-temporal variation and limited predictability of renewables limit controllability of generation and challenge this control paradigm. This project proposed a new frequency control framework to handle these challenges, which includes new control methods for generator side, load side, and their cooperation. Particularly, by integrating ideas of switching control, distributed control, and cooperative control, novel load-side control was established to achieve balance between to be fully responsive to disturbances and to be non-disruptive to end-users. These novel frequency control methods will help us to build a more reliable and cost-effective power system with high renewables.

17257016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17257016.value: By facilitating the exchange of water molecules across the cell membrane, aquaporins (AQPs) can significantly affect cellular functions such as apoptosis, proliferation and migration. For this reason, many pathological processes like tumor growth, metastasis and angiogenesis have been found to be heavily influenced by these water channel proteins. Interestingly, our pilot studies indicated that, due to the overexpression of AQPs, lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells will undergo larger volume changes and have a much higher death rate (compared to their normal counterparts) in response to osmotic stimuli. However, the question of exactly how the behavior and fate of these tumor cells are regulated by the presence and functioning of AQPs remains to be elucidated. Our preliminary investigations also showed that lung and nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells can move much faster in a confined microenvironment. Unfortunately, a quantitative link between the concentration level, as well as polarization characteristics, of AQPs and the migration capability of cells has not been established. In addition, a theoretical model capable of explaining the transient and oscillatory movements of cells in the microchannel, as observed in our initial experiments, is still lacking. In this project, we plan to conduct a combined experimental and modeling study to address these unsettled issues. Specifically, utilizing techniques such as electroosmotic manipulation, microfluidics and gene knockout, the AQP-dependent response and death of different lung and nasopharyngeal tumor cells under osmotic stress will be systematically examined. In addition, carefully designed experiments, in conjunction with simultaneous theoretical modeling taking into account important features that are neglected in previous studies, will also be carried out to elucidate how the expression level and polarization dynamics of AQPs affect the migration of these carcinoma cells. If successful, results from this project will unambiguously confirm or refute our primary hypothesis that the volumetric response and motility of lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells can all be regulated by the functioning of AQPs, and hence greatly enhance our basic understanding of the role of AQPs in various biological processes. Findings here could also provide critical information for the identification of new treatments for lung and nasopharyngeal cancer, two diseases that have particular relevance to public health in Hong Kong. 17257016.value: 1. By changing the medium osmolarity in a programmable manner, we have developed a method to apply precisely controlled osmotic stress to lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells (with distinct AQP-expression levels) and then systematically examine their AQP-dependent volumetric and apoptotic response. 2. A microfluidic device has been designed and fabricated to study the AQP-regulated migration of lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells in different sized microchannels. 3. By taking into account the AQP-mediated cross-membrane water transport , a model has also been developed to describe the movement of cells, triggered by a osmolarity gradient imposed to them, in confined microchannels.

17257016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17257016.value: 1. By varying the voltage applied across a Nafion membrane that separates the cell culture medium from a reservoir, we have developed an electro-osmotic manipulation device to introduce precisely controlled volume change to cells (refer to item 8-1 in Part C). Interestingly, it was found that, when subjected to the same applied voltage, different lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells will undergo larger volumetric changes and have a higher death rate compared to their normal counterparts. Furthermore, we showed that such distinct response is largely caused by the overexpression of aquaporin-4 (AQP-4) in tumor cells, with knockout of this water channel protein resulting in a markedly reduced change in the cellular volume. In addition, the possibility of using the membrane undulation spectra of lung cancer cells (during their volume/shape fluctuations) in the detection of their mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition was also explored (item 8-9 in Part C). 2. A novel microfluidic device has also been developed to apply osmolarity gradients to cancer cells in micro-channels and trigger their movement (refer to item 8-7 in Part C). We showed that adhesion is not required for cells to migrate in such confined microenvironment. However, the migrating velocity of cells is strongly influenced by the interactions between the cells and the channel wall, with a stronger adhesion leading to diminished cell motility. Furthermore, through examining more than 20 different types of lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells, a linear positive correlation between the protein concentration of the aquaporin-4 (AQP4) and the cell migrating speed was observed. Knockdown of AQP4 in invasive re-populated cancer stem cells reduced their migration capability down to the level that is comparable to their parental tumor cells. Finally, we have also examined the influence of confining wall stiffness on the growth dynamics of lung cancer cells (item 8-4 in Part C). 3. A theoretical models was developed to describe the osmolarity gradient-induced (directional or oscillatory) movement of cells in confined microchannels where factor like the exchange of water molecules across the cell membrane and possible cell-outside interactions have all been taken into account (item 8-7 in Part C). Furthermore, by considering the local weakening and rearrangement actin cytoskeleton during cellular movement or deformation, models have also been proposed to explain the observed formation/growth of cellular blebs (refer to items 8-2 and 8-5 in Part C) as well as the development of cellular anisotropy and plasticity in the elongating embryo wall (item 8-11 in Part C).

17257016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17257016.value: 1. Our findings that the expression level of AQP4 in lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells can significantly influence their volumetric, apoptotic and migratory response may lead to new strategies for the selective killing and sorting of tumor cells which could have great clinical implications. 2. The models developed could be extended to examine other interesting phenomena such as adhesion and volume-regulated cell migration during cancer metastasis and homeostasis regulation of cells.

17257016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17257016.value: Novel methods have been developed to interrogate the volumetric, apoptotic and migratory response of cells. We showed that, under the same applied stimuli, different lung and nasopharyngeal cancer cells will undergo larger volumetric changes and have a higher death rate than their normal counterparts because of the elevated aquaporin-4 (AQP4) concentration in these tumor cells. In addition, a positive correlation between the migration speed of cancer cells in a confined microenvironment and their AQP4 expression level was also observed. Findings from this study will enhance our understanding of cancer and could provide valuable information for the development of new strategies for the selective killing and sorting of lung and nasopharyngeal tumor cells.

17257416.label: Project Objectives
17257416.value: Develop a GPU-based big-little Heterogeneous Multi-Processing (HMP) ecosystem for exploiting integrated GPUs and discrete GPUs through a big.LITTLE scheduling approach. Based on OpenCL, data-parallel kernels can be mapped to them, as well as the CPU, according to their memory access patterns and footprints, and the processing capacity of the target device. Investigate techniques for performing runtime profiling-based analysis in an efficient manner. The techniques include lightweight checking for data dependencies, profiling for branch divergence, and tracking memory access ranges and patterns, leveraging the integrated GPUs. The profiling results will be used to guide kernel transformation and scheduling in the HMP environment. Design a new abstraction for workload partitioning. By introducing a new concept called polymorphic kernel transformation, we aim at generation of task objects that can adapt to the compute devices by code/data layout transformation such as data partitioning and iteration remapping. Study advanced scheduling techniques for adaptive mapping of polymorphic kernels onto different compute devices in the HMP ecosystem. We propose a concept called symbiosis-aware kernel scheduling to optimize an overall symbiosis metric, which reflects a cost-benefit analysis on factors like data transfer cost, dependence density, branch divergence, and working set shared between kernels.

17257416.label: Realisation of objectives
17257416.value: Objective 1 (100% achieved): To support collaborative, heterogeneous multiprocessing, we have built a new compiler and runtime framework, called Japonica. Japonica enables a high-level sequential program (Java or C) to be dynamically transformed to massively multithreaded OpenCL code and executed on heterogeneous compute devices. These devices are equipped with multi-core CPUs and various types of GPUs, including desktop/server-grade (“big”) GPUs or embedded (“little”) GPUs used mobile devices. Japonica encapsulates the compute and memory resources of CPUs and GPUs, and enables ﬁne-grained and dynamic control over resource partitioning and tasks scheduling via OpenCL kernel reshaping and transformations, such as kernel slicing and stretching (More in Objective 3). Japonica uses a frontend compiler JavaR to parse the Java code and extract the Java code snippet containing the loops to parallelize. The extracted code is converted to C and analyzed by the PPCG (Polyhedral Parallel Code Generation) compiler to generate OpenCL kernel code. The steps involved in the PPCG-based processing include: (1) Calculating the loop bound and memory access patterns; (2) Adding memory/buffer management code for transferring flexible amount of data to/from GPU; (3) Wrapping all irregular data access in function calls to circumvent confusion led to the PPCG’s code generating backend; (4) Parallelizing the loops without data dependency and wrapping dynamic loops with additional dependency checking code. During the runtime, Japonica’s symbiosis-aware scheduler distributes the transformed OpenCL kernels to run on GPU devices, which allows multiple kernels to run on a single GPU concurrently to maximize the use of GPU resources (Discussed in Objective 4). The design details of the Japonica ecosystem are discussed in a Ph.D thesis “Fine-grained Concurrent Kernel Execution on SM/CU Level for GPGPU Computing” written by Wu Hao. Currently, Japonica can generate the OpenCL code to run on standard discrete GPUs (Nvidia GTX980, Nvidia GTX1080, AMD R9 290X, AMD Vega 64) and mobile GPUs (Qualcomm Adreno 540/640 and ARM Mali-G72 MP12 GPU). Objective 2 (100% achieved): We designed and implemented several light-weight profiling techniques which can be deployed at runtime on GPUs for detecting: (1) Non-deterministic data dependencies (i.e., loops with non-afﬁne loop bounds or subscripts), (2) Control flow (branch) divergence, and (3) Runtime resource usage (occupancy) of OpenCL kernels with respect to GPU memory (e.g., L1/L2 cache, shared memory, global memory) and computing resource (e.g., scalar/vector units, special function units). To detect non-deterministic data dependencies, we generate our own inspector kernels, which intentionally remove un-necessary compute-intensive code based on dead code elimination method used commonly in compilers. Thereby, we only keep the code needed to detect inter-loop data dependency or track the control flow divergence, which is very lightweight. Our profiling techniques have been applied to detect non-deterministic dependency during kernel execution. In our paper “Lightweight Dependency Checking for Parallelizing Loops with Non-Deterministic Dependency on GPU” (ICPADS’16 Best Paper Award), we report two lightweight dependency checking schemes, namely two-pass inspector-executor (Two-Pass) and warp-intrinsic speculative execution (WISE), which can check loops with non-deterministic WAW, RAW, and WAR dependencies. Experiments show that our schemes can achieve 2.2 × speedup over existing solutions in dependency-free cases while only taking about 20% of time compared to existing solutions in the case with statically unproven loop-carried dependencies. We also proposed profiling techniques to detect the control flow (branch) divergence. In our paper “On-GPU Thread-Data Remapping for Branch Divergence Reduction” (published in ACM TACO 2018), we reported our design of WAGNERR, the first on-GPU Thread-Data Remapping (TDR) solution for solving the branch divergence problem on GPUs. We evaluated WAGNERR with seven third-party divergence benchmarks. WAGNERR achieved the highest speedup of 2.72. We further applied the on-GPU thread-data remapping for solving Nested Branch Divergence problem. The results are published in our JPDC 2020 paper “On-GPU Thread-Data Remapping for Nested Branch Divergence”. The on-GPU TDR was also applied in high-speed packet processing. The main results are included in our JPDC 2019 paper “Efficient Low-Latency Packet Processing Using On-GPU Thread-Data Remapping”. Objective 3 (100% achieved): To enable the fine-grained control of GPU resource usage of OpenCL kernel, we proposed a code refactoring technique called “polymorphic kernel transformation” (PKT) for bounding the resource usage of single kernel execution on CUs/SMs. PKE provides a fine-grained control on the allocation of registers and working memory for individual OpenCL kernels by restructuring loops and restricting the use of local variables (thus limit the number of registers used per thread) in an OpenCL kernel code. The new technique enables adaptive spatial partitioning on GPU hardware resources at the CU/SM level, while avoiding potential interference among co-running kernels on CUs/SMs due to such multi-tenant execution. We implemented two kernel transformation techniques, namely kernel slicing and kernel stretching. Kernel slicing partitions a big kernel into multiple smaller work-groups to avoid a kernel to launch big elephant work-groups which occupy the most resources in each CU and forbid us to mix its execution with other kernels. Kernel stretching does in the reverse way, which merges multiple small work-groups from the same kernel into a larger work-group. By increasing the workload of each work-group, kernel stretching can increase data reuse rate and reduce context switch overhead, which is favorable for compute-bound kernels. We have shown that kernel slicing and kernel stretching can calibrate the runtime resource usage of individual kernels and make our predictive model more accurate. To infer the kernel execution time, we analyze the results of 18 OpenCL kernels collected from the PolyBench and Rodinia benchmark suites. A linear model was built to extrapolate the total execution time of the entire kernel in preparation for the design of our symbiosis-aware kernel scheduling (Objective 4). The average error of all tests is 6.6%, 6.3%, and 8.9% for the busy time estimation of scalar ALUs, vector ALUs, and memory unit, respectively. The full results are reported in our ACM TACO 2020 paper “A Model-Based Software Solution for Simultaneous Multiple Kernels on GPUs”. Objective 4 (100% achieved): Based on our kernel transformation techniques discussed in Objective 3, we further propose a symbiosis-aware kernel scheduling policy to resolve resource underutilization issue by co-schedule mixed job types to run on a single GPU. Our symbiosis-aware scheduling seeks to co-schedule kernels that have complementary resource requirements, or otherwise avoid co-schedule “mis-match” kernels to run at the same time. We adopted two approaches: (1) Ensure enough wavefronts to run on each CU/SM to hide memory access latency with a mix of compute-bound and memory-bound kernels to run on a GPU concurrently, (2) Maximize the use of all GPU’s hardware resources, including scalar/vector ALUs, and memory bandwidth, which is modeled as a multi-dimensional resource allocation problem. We proposed a new metric, called “symbiotic factor” to quantify the execution slowdown due to the contention on the use of GPU’s scalar/vector unit and memory load/store units, while multiple kernels are running at the same GPU. We validate our model with 18 OpenCL kernels. A total of 56 pairwise combinations of the kernels with different slicing and stretching factors were tested. Our results show that the new scheduling scheme can achieve an average of 29%, 18%, and 51% performance improvement on AMD R9 290X, RX480, and Vega 64, respectively. Detailed results were reported in our ACM TACO 2020 paper “A Model-Based Software Solution for Simultaneous Multiple Kernels on GPUs.

17257416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17257416.value: (1) GPU-based Heterogeneous Computing ecosystem: The proposed Japonica framework allows the user code written in traditional Java or C be converted to OpenCL code and execute across heterogeneous hardware platforms consisting of CPUs, GPUs, and other processors, which promises fully portable solutions. (2) Japonica can generate the OpenCL code to run on standard “big” GPUs (Nvidia GTX980, Nvidia GTX1080, AMD R9 290X, AMD Vega 64) and “little” GPUs (Qualcomm Adreno 540/640 and ARM Mali-G72 MP12 GPU). (3) Runtime Profiling-based Analysis: Our profiling techniques leveraged the on-GPU Thread-Data Remapping for non-deterministic dependency analysis and branch divergence reduction, which offloads CPU workload to GPU and largely exploit the massive parallelism in GPU. These techniques have been proven effective in our experiments, which can be applied to perform more complicated scientific computing (e.g., code containing complicated if-then-else constructs and runtime data dependency) on modern GPUs. Key results were reported in our ICPADS 2016, ACM TACO 2018, and JPDC 2019 papers. (4) Polymorphic Kernel Transformation: Our novel code transformation technique, call Polymorphic Kernel Transformation (PKE), is one of the most powerful compilation-time optimization techniques. PKE provides a fine-grained control on the allocation of registers and working memory for individual OpenCL kernels by restructuring loops and restricting the use of local variables. This can effectively bound the resource usage of individual kernel execution on CUs/SMs, while enables more effective and accurate decision on the runtime kernel scheduling. Key results were presented in our ACM TACO 2020 paper. (5) Performance Modeling and Scheduling on GPU: Recently proposed performance models on GPUs always focus on the single-kernel executions on GPUs. They fail to address the interferences between co-running kernels. Our symbiosis-aware kernel scheduling can effectively avoid “mis-match” kernels to run at the same time. Results were presented in our ACM TACO 2020 paper.

17257416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17257416.value: For further development of this research work, we will focus on the following three aspects: (1) Integration of the developed kernel reshaping techniques and the on-GPU profiling solutions (dependency-checking, kernel splitting, on-GPU TDR) into the Japonica runtime system. Due to the weak support of OpenCL from Nvidia, our OpenCL-based profiling solutions can only collect performance counters on Nvidia Maxwell and order generation architectures. We need to port the performance model of AMD to Nvidia GPUs based on additional software-based measurements. (2) Design of more more accruate performance predictive model. Our current performance model is based on a simple probability model (multiplication rule of independent events), which can be further improved. In addition, the memory-bound kernels require a more advanced model to analyze the memory behaviors. (3) Improvement of symbiosis-aware kernel scheduling with consideration of more kernel types. The current kernel selection algorithm could be extended to support the selection of multiple kernels. We are currently developing a high-speed kernel preemption technique to enable efficient context switching which targets to support more applications with real-time response requirements that are impossible to be achieved by traditional draining and flushing techniques.

17257416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17257416.value: Today, we are witnessing a significant growth of heterogeneous computing in high performance computing (HPC) workloads and artificial intelligence (AI) converge. This calls for a unified and scalable programming model to harness the power of diverse computing architectures. Japonica demonstrated and delivered a unified and friendly programming environment to developers, which largely reduced the cost of the implementing separate code bases, or the use of multi-programming languages. Our solutions could be applied in those data centers that make of GPU farms for better sharing and utilization of GPU resource. It could have a great impact in the GPU virtualization technology, such as the new Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) launched in the NVIDIA A100. The proposed Polymorphic Kernel Transformation technique alone could be applied in those resource-restricted mobile devices for adjusting the resource usage by code transformation and achieve real-time response on the architecture of their choice, without compromising performance.

17257516.label: Project Objectives
17257516.value: [Full Feedback Model] Characterize the sample complexity of Myerson's optimal auction and the VCG auction with reserves in the single-parameter domain, and the sample complexity of common multi-parameter problems such as multi-item auctions. Design poly-time algorithms with nearly optimal sample complexity. [Partial Feedback Model] Characterize the sample complexity and regret upper bound of multi-item auctions in the partial feedback model. Design poly-time algorithms that obtain nearly optimal sample complexity and regret bound. [Signal Model] Characterize the sample complexity of single-item auction in the signal model for both single-dimension and multi-dimension signals. Design poly-time algorithms that obtain nearly optimal sample complexity. [Empirical Evaluation] Implement auctions incorporating the theoretical findings in this project. Compare their performance with that of existing methods on simulated data.

17257516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17257516.value: 机制设计中的贝叶斯模型通常假设买家对所求物品的价值是从一个先验概率分布中随机采样得来，而这个先验概率分布对于卖家是已知的。然而在实际应用当中，卖家往往只能从以往的用户数据中提取出关于这些先验概率分布的一些信息。这些用户数据可以认为是服从先验概率分布的独立同分布采样。此项目将从严格的数学模型出发研究如何从数据中获取关于先验概率分布的信息并根据这些信息设计机制。

17257516.label: Realisation of objectives
17257516.value: All objectives have been achieved. 1. The PI has fully characterized the optimal sample complexity for Myerson's optimal auction; the results are published in STOC 2019, a flagship peer-reviewed conference in theoretical computer science. 2. The PI has designed near optimal online learning algorithm with bandit feedback. Further, the PI has considered game-theoretical behaviors of bidders and introduced algorithms that are robust to such game-theoretic considerations. The results are published in NeurIPS 2018, a flagship peer-reviewed conference in machine learning. 3. The PI has obtained near optimal algorithms for learning single-item auctions in the signal model. 4. The PI has implemented the algorithms developed in this project and evaluate on simulated data.

17257516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17257516.value: - There is a "universally-optimal" algorithm for learning Myerson's optimal auction for all families of distributions considered in the literature. - The optimal sample complexity of auction design relies on exploiting the independence of data dimension, which is fundamentally different from the existing literature building on learning dimensions. - It is possible to design a multi-scale online learning algorithm which achieves regret bounds based on the magnitude of rewards of the best option. - Single-dimensional and multi-dimensional signals can be handled similarly.

17257516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17257516.value: - Optimal sample complexity of multi-dimensional revenue maximization remains elusive, despite partial progress made in this project. - It is unclear whether learning in the presence of strategic behavior of bidders is strictly harder than the nonstrategic counterpart.

17257516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17257516.value: This project has developed a toolkit for learning optimal auctions from data, providing a set of theories and algorithms that can be applied to practical scenarios. In almost all settings, the results obtained in this project are either theoretically optimal, or the current best in the literature.

17257616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17257616.value: 新型納米硫化物穩定劑脫汞機制研究

17257616.label: Project Objectives
17257616.value: Nano-structured metal sulfides will be fabricated using different precursors and synthesis methods. The crystal growth of the sulfide products and the development of nano-structural features will be systematically observed through high-resolution scanning and transmission electron microscopies (SEM and TEM). Quantitative material characterizations, for instance, of the surface area, particle/pore size distributions and surface roughness using atomic force microscopy (AFM), will further assist in confirming the achievement of the material design goals. Our unique QXRD analysis skill (using Rietveld refinement method with the fundamental parameter approach and an amorphous content quantification protocol) will then report the quantities and structural characteristics (lattice parameters, cation distribution, crystal size, etc.) of different sulfide phases in the stabilizers through high-resolution diffraction data. The amorphous content quantification will use commonly available calcium fluoride and silicon carbide as internal standards to assist the development of a reliable quantification method for the amorphous content in multiple-phase sulfide samples. The mercury removal performances of the fabricated sulfide products will be assessed using self-regulating fixed-bed reactors, and the influences from different gas components and process operation parameters will be evaluated. By combining material structural features and their mercury adsorption characteristics, key factors related to the effective enhancement of mercury capture by sulfide surfaces will be revealed. Moreover, the uses of surface-sensitive characterization techniques such as X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to observe the reacted samples will further provide direct evidence to support the discussion of reaction behavior. In addition to the observation of mercury capture behavior, the subsequent stabilization mechanisms occurring on the sulfide surfaces will be evaluated through leaching and chamber reemission experiments. Electron microscopies and surface-sensitive characterization tools will again provide direct comparisons for mechanistic analyses. Moreover, molecular interaction simulations based on the density functional theory and the material property parameters will be carried out to assist in the comparison and explanation of the observed mercury transport and reaction behavior on the sulfide surfaces. Based on the mechanistic understanding of the mercury adsorption and stabilization behavior on the different sulfide surfaces, techniques will be elaborated for fabricating the desired nano- and micro-structural features necessary to create efficient stabilizer products, together with designs for their subsequent beneficial use strategies. The optimal operational parameters associated with different stabilizer designs will also be provided to extend the technological flexibility to different practical application requirements. Overall, the implementation of this project will facilitate the goals of enhancing mercury removal from combustion flue gas and reliably immobilizing mercury with the new sulfide stabilizers through a scientifically sound and economically feasible strategy.
