17257616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17257616.value: The updated inventory of air emissions confirms coal combustion as a continuing major emission source, responsible for around 475 tons of toxic mercury emissions annually. Although activated carbon injection has been commercialized as a method to reduce such emissions from flue gas, serious drawbacks associated with the carbon-mixed ash materials, such as low operating temperature and the prevention of beneficial uses of the ash, have already emerged. Therefore, a new technology using non-carbon sorbents is urgently needed to control mercury emissions from coal combustion. The adsorption of gas-phase mercury on sulfides has proven to be highly promising, and thus sulfide impregnation is currently an attempt to enhance mercury removal with conventional adsorbents. However, obtaining sufficient surface coverage with reliable sulfide-adsorbent bonding under high temperature has proven to be critical but extremely challenging. To overcome the problems of surface coverage and beneficial ash use, inorganic sulfide-matrix stabilizers featuring highly rich and active sulfide sites will be developed in this project. Another important goal is to unambiguously identify the roles of different sulfide phases (e.g., crystalline or amorphous) in mercury adsorption and stabilization. The key breakthrough will be based on a thorough and systematic investigation of the mechanisms of interaction between the surfaces of differently nano-structured sulfides and mercury in the gas flow. This proposed study is based on our extensive experience in designing functional nano-structured inorganic materials, particularly with precise crystal growth control, for a variety of environmental applications. High-resolution X-ray diffraction technique and a state-of-the-art Rietveld refinement analysis with amorphous content quantification will be implemented to quantify the crystal growth processes in the nano-structured sulfide minerals. Mercury sorption and stabilization efficiencies will be compared using a self-regulating fixed-bed reactor, and the influences from different gas components and process operation parameters will be systematically quantified. Subsequently, the stability of the mercury-containing sulfides will be evaluated through ligand-promoted leaching and chamber re-emission experiments. In addition to characterizing these experimental samples with our very strong surface-sensitive spectroscopy and electron microscopy skills, molecular interaction simulations based on the density functional theory will be performed to assist in explaining the mercury adsorption and stabilization mechanisms occurring on our fabricated sulfide surfaces. Based on these important results, the ultimate goal of developing an efficient and environmentally friendly technology for removing mercury from combustion flue gas will be achieved through these scientifically and experimentally proven novel sulfide stabilizers. 根據最新的大氣污染物排放清單，煤燃燒仍然是主要的人為汞排放源，每年約向大氣排放475噸汞。雖然活性炭噴射技術已成為商業化的煙氣脫汞方法，但是該方法仍然存在明顯的不足，如較低的操作溫度以及碳材料對飛灰後續利用的不利影響等。因此，迫切需要開發一種新的基於非炭基吸附劑的技術來控制燃煤煙氣中汞的排放。硫化物對氣相汞具有較強的吸附能力，因此硫化物負載也通常被用來增強傳統吸附劑的脫汞能力。然而，在高溫條件下通過穩定的硫基-吸附劑成鍵來獲得足夠的表面覆蓋度是非常關鍵而又極具挑戰的技術。為了克服吸附劑表面硫覆蓋率低的問題，利於飛灰的後續利用，本專案將開發充滿高活性硫位點的無機硫化物穩定劑。此外，專案的另一個重要目的是明確區分不同形態（晶相或無定形相）硫化物在汞吸附和穩定中的角色。關鍵的突破點在於對不同納米結構硫化物表面與煙氣中的汞相互作用機制進行全面系統的研究。 這項研究將基於我們在設計功能性納米結構無機材料，尤其是在精確控制晶體生長及其多種環境應用方面的豐富經驗。我們將採用高分辨率X射線衍射和先進的可對非晶相含量進行量化分析的Rietveld精修技術對納米硫化礦物的晶體生長過程進行量化分析。自主設計的固定床實驗台將用來比較汞吸附及固定效率，並對不同的煙氣組分及操作参数的影響進行系統的量化。隨後，我們將採用滲濾浸出實驗和箱體再釋放實驗評價載汞硫化物上汞的穩定性。除了採用高表面靈敏度光譜分析，電子顯微分析等手段對實驗樣品進行分析，我們還將採用基於密度泛函理論的分子間相互作用模擬分析來協助解釋汞在硫化物表面的吸附和穩定機制。專案的最終目標是基於該科學的且被實驗證明可行的硫化物穩定劑，開發高效且環境友好的煙氣脫汞技術。

17257616.label: Realisation of objectives
17257616.value: We have successfully synthesized different stabilizers based on nano-structured sulfide (ZnS, CuS, FexZn1-xS, CoxZn1-xS, NixZn1-xS, CuxZn1-xS, and magnetic rattle-type Fe3O4@CuS) based on the precipitation or hydrothermal method. The SEM characterization proved that the particle sizes of the stabilizers as obtained were in nanoscale and the morphologies were well structured. The TEM results indicate that exposed surface, structure defects, and crystal phase of stabilizer exhibited influences on structural properties like pore size/distribution, and hence affect the mercury capture performances. Our unique QXRD analyses were conducted to further consolidate the conclusions made based on the microscopies. Rietveld refinement method with the fundamental parameter approach and an amorphous content quantification protocol provided clear evidence on quantitative properties of the stabilizers, i.e., lattice parameters, crystal sizes, etc. Moreover, the quantification of amorphous content was also achieved with the assistance of a reliable protocol using commonly available calcium fluoride and silicon carbide as internal standards. The mercury removal performances over different stabilizers were subsequently tested and compared. Key influential factors like flue gas atmospheres, gas flow rates, stabilizer dosages, operation temperatures were investigated. The stabilizers developed are generally insusceptible to most typical coal-fired gas components like O2, SO2, HCl, CO2, and H2O. Besides, at a relatively low dosage, stabilizers based on sulfides exhibit excellent mercury capture performance at high gas flow rates within a wide temperature range. The origin of different influential patterns by various factors was further analyzed by surface-sensitive characterization techniques like XPS, FT-IR, Raman spectra, etc. The comparison of surface, compositional, and valence properties between fresh and reacted samples clearly identified the reaction behavior. The final product and Hg-laden stabilizer were further exposed to environmental weathering to explore the stability and reemission feature. The leaching mercury was tested by an AFS-based facility and compared with previously reported techniques. It is found only a negligible amount of mercury was leached out from Hg-laden sulfides when they were environmentally exposed because the adsorbate, i.e., HgS, exhibited excellent stability. The formation of HgS was further proven by results obtained from electron microscopies (TEM and STEM-HADDF) and surface-sensitive characterization (FTIR, XPS) tools. In addition, molecule-level methods like simulation and calculation based on density functional theory were used to clarify the reaction pathway and desorption/reemission mechanism. Stepwise reaction behaviors were established, and the mercury transportation/transformation pathway was correspondingly proposed. Based on the theoretical and practical understandings of the mercury capture over different nano-structured sulfide stabilizers, techniques were optimized to fit different samples and application scenarios. Considering the stability, recyclability, and reusability of the stabilizers, together with the operating conditions of different coal-fired power plants, two technically feasible strategies, i.e., injection and fixed-bed, were proposed. The optional stabilizer and strategy aim to provide a wide variety of application scenarios with cost-effective and long-termly sustainable flexibility when abating mercury pollutions. Hence, it is reasonable to conclude that this project has successfully facilitated the goals of enhancing mercury removal from combustion flue gas and reliably immobilizing mercury with the new sulfide stabilizers.

We have successfully built three self-regulating fixed-bed reactors to test the mercury removal performances of the fabricated stabilizers. Influences of typical flue gas components like O2, CO2, SOx, NOx, HCl, and H2O were widely investigated for different sulfides. In addition, different process operation parameters (temperature, dosage, flow rate, etc.) simulating real-world conditions were also considered and tested to give a full picture. Based on the abovementioned studies, key influential factors enhancing mercury capture performance were identified. These findings were further supported by comparing the compositional and valence characteristics of fresh and reacted samples.

Leaching and chamber reemission experiments were conducted by using atomic fluorescence spectrometry to test the amount of re-emitted mercury. Electron microscopes (TEM and STEM-HADDF) and surface-sensitive characterization (FTIR, XPS) tools were used to identify the functional ligands primarily responsible for mercury stabilization. After grasping a full picture of the key influential factors and involved mechanisms, technically applicable scenarios like injection and/or fixed-bed reactor were proposed for different stabilizers. Moreover, according to the environmental stability, magnetic recyclability, and reusability of the samples, beneficial use strategies were designed to achieve cost-effective and long-termly sustainable processes. Based on different operation conditions, optimal performances could be achieved by adopting optional stabilizers or their combinations.

17257616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17257616.value: Mercury, widely concentrating in coal-fired flue gas, was known for its environmental persistence and neurological hypertoxicity. In this work, various sulfide-based stabilizers, i.e., ZnS, CuS, FexZn1-xS, CoxZn1-xS, NixZn1-xS, CuxZn1-xS, and magnetic rattle-type Fe3O4@CuS, were developed with different precursors and synthesis methods. From the SEM and TEM results, it is found with the assistance of advanced processing methods, the stabilizers as obtained exhibited well-structured morphology and well-controlled particle size in nanoscale. The fabricated pore size and the mesopore-enriched properties also fully agree with the material synthesis goals. Our unique QXRD technique with high-resolution diffraction data was adopted to further quantify the crystal phase, particle size, and lattice parameters of the samples. The amorphous content in the stabilizers was also identified and found to be beneficial for mercury capture in specific scenarios. Three self-regulating fixed-bed reactors were built for assessing mercury capture performances of the stabilizers. Influential factors like flue gas atmospheres, operation temperatures, and gas flow rates were evaluated. Most flue gas components like O2, SO2, HCl, CO2, and H2O showed negligible effect on mercury capture by sulfides. The detrimental effects of SO3 and NOx on mercury removal were for the first reported in this study, and corresponding solutions were proposed. Besides, the sulfide-based stabilizers exhibited > 99% mercury capture efficiency under high gas flow rates within a wide temperature range. Surface-sensitive characteristic methods, e.g., XPS and FT-IR, identified the main active species and found the mercury was finally converted into HgS, a mercury form that is stable when environmentally exposed. Thus, during the leaching process, < 0.01% of the adsorbed mercury was leached out. Hence, the Hg-laden stabilizer can be directly dumped and landfilled. Molecule-level simulation and calculation based on density functional theory were used to further clarify the mercury transportation/transformation pathway as well as reason the outstanding stability of the adsorbate (HgS). Two technical strategies, i.e., injection and fixed-bed, were proposed as practical ways for the stabilizer application in real-world conditions. According to the features of different stabilizers, this work successfully extends the technological flexibility to different application requirements.

17257616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17257616.value: This project primarily provides solid lab-scale foundations on the mercury capture by sulfide-based stabilizers. Further studies may focus on pilot-scale, or full-scale, tests to further justify the applicability of the stabilizers as obtained and compare the cost-effectiveness with traditional mercury remediators. Another direction is using synchrotron-based tools to monitor the real-time intermediate changes along the reaction pathway and provide direct evidence to the theoretical prediction made from density functional theory simulations. These two directions are expected to extend the macroscopic and microscopic understandings of the novel sulfide-based stabilizers and help the optimization of the material synthesis and technical strategy.

17257616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17257616.value: Mercury that often concentrates in the coal-fired flue gas is highly hazardous for the environment and toxic to the ecosystem. This project synthesized various sulfide-based materials that are cost-effective and/or magnetic-recyclable to achieve one-step mercury immobilization from coal-fired flue gas. Characterizations using electron microscopic techniques determined the crystal properties and structural features of the stabilizers. The X-ray diffraction technique was adopted to further quantify the lattice parameters and amorphous contents. After the tests by self-regulating reactors, sulfide-based stabilizers exhibited excellent performance for mercury capture and transformed mercury into the stable mercury sulfide (HgS). The theoretical calculation was subsequently conducted to predict and simulate the reaction behavior and mercury transportation/transformation pathways. With the different properties of stabilizers, a wide range of strategic choices can be offered to fit the operating requirements of various coal-fired power plants.

17258816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17258816.value: RapidPL ：有關快速編程語言實現語義模塊化

17258816.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17258816.value: Prof Lau, Francis Chi Moon Dr van der Storm, Tijs

17258816.label: Project Objectives
17258816.value: To demonstrate that semantic modularization techniques can be combined with self-optimizing run-time systems to create a practical and effective software-product line of programming language components. To improve the state-of-the-art and develop new techniques for semantic modularity, and to show that these techniques scale-up to real-world problems. To conduct an extensive empiral evaluation to assess the results of work. In the empirical evaluation we will develop various programming languages implementations by assembling modular programming language components. The language implementations will include real-world programming languages, such as Python or Ruby.

17258816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17258816.value: 新的编程或领域特定语言（DSL）的实现都需要所有的时间。但是创造新的语言是很难！有有助于这种困难两个主要因素：1）工程的努力的量; 2）需要在语言设计专业知识。有很多参与创建工程工作，和语言的维护。一种编程语言是由各个部分组成：句法和语义分析，编译器或解释器和工具，用于支持计划在该语言的发展（例如：IDE的或调试器）。此外，该语言已经被保持，臭虫必须是固定的，而新的功能，必须实现。除了这些工程问题，软件工程师的缺乏适当的训练，错过了知识，做好语言设计。由于这两个因素，创造一种新的语言的费用通常是望而却步，或只是很难找到具有合适技能做的编程语言实现的工程师。 应对这些挑战的一个方法是重用语言组件。编程语言共享了很多功能。例如，如Java或C语言有许多共同的特点。这两种语言有机制来声明变量，支持基本的算术运算的原语，具有循环结构，或有变数类似的作用域规则。即使语法是许多语言构造相似。此外，几乎所有的新的语言将从现有语言“复制”了许多功能，而不是一个全新的功能集。因此，在编程语言中的固有概念重用。可惜的是这是很难兑现的概念重用到软件工程重用。问题是我们不知道的模块化技术，强大到足以表达这种语言成分，不放弃必要的软件工程特性，如模块化的类型检查和独立的编译。正因为如此，几乎所有现有的编译器的实现是建立在一个单片的方式。 该提案将制定RapidPL：模块化语言实现一个基于Java的框架。随着RapidPL，而不是从头构建的语言，软件工程师将能够简单地选择，组合和可能的自定义语言组件迅速组装完整的编程语言实现。这个所谓的软件的产品线的方法将大大减少两者所需的工程工作，以及在语言设计的需要知识。为了实现这一目标，将RapidPL建立和完善了一些对面向对象程序语义模块的最新发展。对比于现有元编程技术，得到句法模块化，语义模块化技术允许不仅在单独的文件中指定的语言的组件，而且还支持单独的编译和模块化类型检查。在RapidPL每种语言组件/功能将模块化的方式作为一个普通的Java组件来定义。功能组成，以组成一个完整的语言，将采用新的Java 8的功能支持多重继承的形式来完成。为了保证从模块化语言成分组成的语言有良好的运行时性能，RapidPL将建立在甲骨文的研究格拉尔VM和松露框架之上。格拉尔VM包含新技术的自我优化的运行时系统。与松露框架结合，格拉尔VM允许高性能的抽象语法树（AST）口译员的创建。因此，对的模块化优势外，RapidPL将提供高性能的编程语言实现，而不需要编译器优化的显著知识。最终，与RapidPL，这将是可能的模块化语言组件，同时保存于模块化类型检查和单独编译，并克服了工程的努力以及缺乏专业知识的，使得程序设计语言实现硬。

To improve the state-of-the-art and develop new techniques for semantic modularity, and to show that these techniques scale-up to real-world problems.

17258816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17258816.value: Our major finding was that using current mainstream programming languages and annotation frameworks (such as those in Java or Scala) we can create powerful & modular frameworks to develop programs. This has been a recurring theme in the work in this project. To demonstrate the potential of our work to quickly prototype language implementations, we developed case studies using the Types and Programming Languages book and showed that a large amount of the implementations and language features covered in that book can be modularized using our frameworks.

17258816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17258816.value: In our view the next step is to look at the limitations of using current programming languages for modularisation frameworks such as those developed by us, and look at new programming language designs that can make such modularisation techniques more powerful and simple to use.

17258816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17258816.value: Building new programming languages is often necessary. Sometimes the need arises from the need for domain specific languages (such as languages for chemistry, finance, or some other domains). However, developing good implementations of programming languages is hard: it requires a lot of coding effort and technical knowledge about programming languages. This project shows that it is possible to develop programming languages from existing reusable components, thus greatly lowering the cost to develop new programming languages.

17259316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17259316.value: 用於高速立體成像之編碼平面陣列照明顯微技術

17259316.label: Project Objectives
17259316.value: This project primarily aims to establish a new type of volumetric fluorescence imaging, called EPAM, by exploiting parallelized 3D encoded illumination and detection – a feature generally absent in the current imaging modalities. The rationale is that mechanical sample or light-beam scanning, and system synchronization are completely eliminated by parallelization in 3D. Not only can it guarantee high volumetric frame-rate and signal-to-noise ratio, but also minimize the exposure and thus photobleaching and phototoxicity. The encoding nature in EPAM also inherently provides optical sectioning and digital structured illumination for realizing 3D isotropic resolution without compromising the speed. Toward these goals, we specifically aim to: Develop encoded planar-illumination array multiplexing – To realize 3D parallelization, we will develop a unique imaging strategy central to EPAM, featuring multiplexed planar-illumination array generation and encoding. The core element is an angle-misaligned mirror pair, which functions as an array of actively reconfigurable virtual sources that automatically generate a dense and incoherent 2D light-plane array – a unique and crucial element for high-quality illumination in EPAM. We will construct this planar-illumination array generator combined with an encoding module, which temporally modulates each of the 2D illumination planes with a unique code. In effect, the entire 3D image stack, which is captured simultaneously by a 2D image sensor, can be digitally demultiplexed (decoded) to reconstruct the 3D image. Such 3D multiplexing not only result in high volumetric frame rate with high SNR, it innately enables the optical sectioning capability. Particularly, we will adopt frequency-division multiplexing and coded-division multiplexing, which are routinely used in telecommunication, to the planar-illumination array, and investigate their compatibility to EPAM, in terms of imaging quality and speed. Establish the EPAM prototype for high-speed volumetric imaging – We will integrate the encoded planar-illumination array generator in a microscope geometry resembling that typically adopted in light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM), i.e. one objective lens for excitation from one direction whereas another for fluorescence image capture from the orthogonal direction. This is motivated by the compatibility of this dual-objective-lens configuration with the working principle of EPAM. Also, EPAM in this configuration can inherit the key advantages (e.g. high speed, high spatial resolution), and thus the applications brought by LSFM. More importantly, the mechanical-scan-free nature of EPAM relaxes the physical limitation on the specimens/system. By incorporating the technique of extended depth-of-focus, which has broadly been applied in other microscope systems, we will establish the EPAM prototype that can record all optically-sectioned, in-focus 2D image planes simultaneously at a volumetric frame rate >10 Hz. We will characterize the performance of the EPAM prototype particularly in terms of the balance between spatial resolution, imaging speed, and detection sensitivity, and photodamage. Leveraging the encoded nature of 3D image stack, we will also implement structured-illumination digitally in the axial dimension without modifying the system and compromising the frame rate, favoring close-to-isotropic resolution. Explore the potential applications of EPAM – Brought by the 3D multiplexing capability, which significantly minimizes the required exposure, another unique feature of EPAM is its unprecedentedly low photobleaching and phototoxicity. As a result, EPAM is thus well suited to address the unmet need in fundamental biology for long-term fast volumetric cellular/tissue/organism imaging at the sub-second temporal resolution. Built upon the prototype, we will, with the support from Faculty of Medicine at HKU, employ EPAM for two potential applications. First, we will use EPAM for large-scale monitoring dynamical changes in repair and regenerative processes of a live and freely-moving planarian – a unique regenerative worm model system used in stem cell biology due to its striking regenerative capability. Second, we will explore the use of EPAM for real-time 3D microparticle tracking, e.g. monitoring and understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of the engineered bacteria (Salmonella) and the tumor vasculature system – a critical, yet missing, tool in the emerging field of bacterial cancer therapy.

First, we will use EPAM for large-scale monitoring dynamical changes in repair and regenerative processes of a live and freely-moving planarian – a unique regenerative worm model system used in stem cell biology due to its striking regenerative capability. Second, we will explore the use of EPAM for real-time 3D microparticle tracking, e.g. monitoring and understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of the engineered bacteria (Salmonella) and the tumor vasculature system – a critical, yet missing, tool in the emerging field of bacterial cancer therapy.

17259316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17259316.value: 此項目的主要目的通過利用並行3D三維並行的照明和檢測概念，建立一種新型的立體熒光成像技術，稱為EPAM。此技術完全消除一般成像對機械樣品或光光束掃描，和系統同步要求。它不僅可以保證高容積幀率和信噪比，而且大大地減低了曝光，及其帶來漂白和光毒性的問題。EPAM編碼性質本身上還提供了「光學切片」功能，在並不會影響速度下實現3D全方位高分辨率的數字結構照明。

17259316.label: Realisation of objectives
17259316.value: All objectives (from system design, development to optimization) have been achieved. We have developed the core element of EPAM, which is an angle-misaligned mirror pair that functions as an array of actively reconfigurable virtual sources that automatically generate a dense and incoherent 2D light-plane (or light-sheet) array (> 40 light sheets). The density and incoherency of the light sheets can be flexibly reconfigured by the geometry of the mirror pair. Parallelized volumetric detection is accomplished by multiplexed light-sheet encoding, inspired by the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) in wireless communication. We particularly adopted a spinning patterned reticle that provides frequency-chirped intensity modulation across the light-sheet array. We have established the EPAM microscope system based on the parallelized 3D illumination and detection. We have configured the system with the 100% spatial duty cycle in detection, which implies long voxel dwell time. In other words, EPAM requires less intense illumination and thus further reduces photodamage and photobleaching without sacrificing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). It thus relaxes the illumination power and thus outperforms other modalities in reducing photobleaching/phototoxicity. The system enables simultaneous capture of all optically-sectioned image planes in a continuous volume at >10 vol/sec, obviating the need for bulky objective scanning or beam scanning/dithering. We have demonstrated the utility of EPAM in different imaging scenarios, including light-scattered medium, optically cleared tissue, and microparticles in fluidic flow.

17259316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17259316.value: We have successfully establish a new type of volumetric fluorescence imaging, called EPAM. This is done by developing a new strategy of parallelized 3D encoded illumination and detection, which is a feature generally missing in the current 3D imaging modalities. It allows complete parallelized 3D imaging without any mechanical scanning. Harnessing the concept of “infinity mirror”, EPAM generates an array of light sheets with reconfigurable sheet density and coherency. It thus bypasses the widely adopted coherent multi-light-sheet generation concept and its complication in precise phase control and mechanical scanning/dithering. Another enabling feature is multiplexed plane-wide encoding which allows simultaneous capture of all optically-sectioned images within the continuous volume. We demonstrated the utility of EPAM in different imaging scenarios, including light-scattered medium, optically cleared tissue, and microparticles in fluidic flow. Not only can such CLAM maximize spatial duty-cycle and signal-to-noise ratio, but also can outperform the majority of the scanning-based 3D imaging modalities in further reduction in photobleaching. We also made EPAM as a flexible implementation in both hardware and software so that it is compatible with any light-sheet imaging modalities and could thus be instrumental in a multitude of areas in biological research. We have also extended the utility of the infinity mirror for multiplexed illumination in the area of multiphoton imaging. We used this technique to demonstrate the kHz full-frame two-photon fluorescence microscopy for in-vivo voltage brain imaging in awake mice (Nature Methods, 2020). The 3D imaging technology is selected as "Laser Focus World’s top 20 photonics technology picks for 2020" - https://www.laserfocusworld.com/home/article/14187586/laser-focus-worlds-top-20-photonics-technology-picks-for-2020 Apart from the more than 20 publications (in Journals and Conferences), we have filed a US patent application based on this 3D imaging technology. Potentially it will be licensed to a startup company commercializing high-throughput imaging for medical diagnosis.

17259316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17259316.value: EPAM could be particularly well-suited for long-term dynamical volumetric imaging of live cellular, tissue, and organism, as well as high-throughput volumetric visualization for 3D histopathological investigation of archival biological samples – both are instrumental in a wide range of biological research, notably in neuroscience and developmental biology.

17259316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17259316.value: We have developed a new form of 3D microscopy technology, called EPAM. This system allows efficient volumetric imaging approach that could particularly well-suited for long-term dynamical biological imaging of live cellular, tissue, and organism. It thus could be applicable to a wide range of biological research, notably in neuroscience and developmental biology.

17259416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17259416.value: 在下一代网络，基于云协作的密集分布天线和小蜂窝基站将构成虚拟大规模分布式（LSD）阵列。这种阵列在空间上产生了更大数量的自由度（DOF），从而可以实现密集移动用户的高速率空间复用接入，也为2020年预期100倍的流量增长提供了可行的解决方案。大规模分布式阵列的多输入多输出（MIMO）信道会受到几何特征的影响，例如位置，阵列的形状和拓扑结构以及散射集群。然而，经典的MIMO统计模型对于这些几何信道的描述过于粗糙，基于统计信道模型的传统分析方法不足以研究大规模分布式MIMO。因此，关于大规模分布式MIMO的本质特征仍处于未知，从而促使提出该研究。在这个项目中， 根据大规模MIMO信道的确定几何模型，提出了分析信道空间自由度的一种新方法。这种简洁的分析方法利用了天线理论来分析传输阵列的辐射模式和接收阵列的响应模式，利用传播理论来刻画集群散射场的响应。最后，根据几何分解理论， 这些传播方程将会被分解为球面谐波，从而建立了空间自由度和信道几何特征的关系。根据这种新方法，我们将得到多种大规模分布式MIMO阵列信道的空间自由度，包括单用户，多用户，和多小区信道。在下一代密集网络中，这些结果阐明了大规模分布式MIMO的本质特征，并且该项目为研究确定几何信道中的大规模MIMO提供了一种新的分析框架。

17259416.label: Realisation of objectives
17259416.value: Objective 1: Analyze the spatial DoF for a single-user LSD-MIMO channel. The number of DoF will be derived as a function of the projection regions of scatterer clusters onto transmit and receive arrays. The objective has been achieved by analyzing the spatial DoF for a single-user LSD-MIMO channel in different types of systems including mmWave MIMO systems [Publication 1], MIMO relay assisted communication systems [Publication 2], and cache enabled small cell MIMO systems [Publication 3], joint adaptive MIMO and content placement [Publication 4]. In these systems, their number of spatial DoF have been derived as a function of the area of the region from projecting scatterer clusters onto transmit and receive arrays. The results are then applied to improve the efficiencies of backscatter sensing featuring random encoding at sensors and statistical inference at readers [Publication 5]. The results are also found to be useful in understanding the limit of the connectivity of mm-wave networks [Publication 6] and even MIMO systems for mobile edge computing [Publication 7]. Objective 2: Analyze the spatial DoF for a multiuser LSD-MIMO channel. The number of DoF will be derived as a function of the union of the sets of projection regions for individual-user channels. Furthermore, the DoF tradeoff between individual user channel will be investigated by analyzing the relations between the said sets. We have achieved this objective in this project with results reported in a series of papers published in leading journals. The spatial DoF for a multiuser LSD-MIMO channel has been analyzed for a number of different types of LSD-MIMO channels/systems including heterogeneous networks based on HARQ [Publication 8], latency constrained edge computing systems [Publication 9], and energy efficient systems [Publication 10]. The understanding and insights from the analysis were then applied to derive the energy-efficient control policies for computation offloading system [Publication 11], multiuser wirelessly powered crowd sensing system [Publication 12], MIMO backscattering systems [Publication 13], D2D underlaid massive MIMO systems [Publication 14], analyzing connectivity in mmWave A2X network [Publication 15], high-mobility data acquisition in edge learning [Publication 16], MIMO beamforming for wirelessly powered-AirComp framework [Publication 17]. Objective 3: Analyze the spatial DoF for a multi-cell LSD-MIMO channel. The number of DoF will be derived by analyzing the relation between two sets of project regions corresponding to data and inter-cell interference channels. We have achieved the objective by analyze the spatial DoF for a multi-cell LSD-MIMO channel in different scenarios including multifunction AirComp for MIMO high-mobility multimodal sensor networks [Publication 18], broadband MIMO analog aggregation [Publication 19], automatic non-coherent MIMO modulation recognition [Publication 20], MIMO vehicle sensing [Publication 21],MIMO AirComp framework for IoT network [Publication 22]. We also summarize the results in the context of mIMO mobile edge computing [Publication 23].

17259416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17259416.value: The major findings and research outcomes from this project are reported in a series of journal papers as summarized in the list below. [Publication 1] We present systematic DoF maximal design for hybrid beamforming for multi-cell multiuser massive MIMO systems over mmWave channels. [Publication 2] We derive the achievable DoF region of wirelessly powered two-way communication with fixed relay is derived. [Publication 3] We investigate problem of how to conduct LSD-MIMO caching placement on SBS and on mobile devices leveraging user mobility. [Publication 4] We present a novel idea of content adaptive MAC for LSD-MIMO channels where adapting MAC schemes to content ensures that all signals carrying identical content are encoded. [Publication 5] We propose novel framework of backscatter sensing over LSD-MIMO channels featuring random encoding at sensors and statistical inference at readers. [Publication 6] We investigate blockage effect on the connectivity of mm-wave networks in a Manhattan-type urban region modeled using random regular lattice, with LSD-MIMO channels, while base stations are Poisson distributed in plane. [Publication 7] We characterize structure of the optimal policies and propose algorithms for policies for co-computing system over LSD-MIMO channels where user offloads computation of input data to helper. [Publication 8] We study effects of BS spatial interdependence on interference correlation and performance of HCNs with HARQ over LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 9] We investigate network-constrained latency performance of multi-cell LSD-MIMO systems, namely communication latency and computation latency, under constraints of radio-access connectivity and computer server stability. [Publication 10] We studied energy-efficient resource management policy for asynchronous mobile-edge computation offloading systems over LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 11] We design energy-efficient control policies in a computation offloading system over LSD-MIMO channels with random channel and helper with a dynamically loaded CPU. [Publication 12] We propose multiuser wirelessly powered crowd sensing system model with LSD-MIMO channels and investigate joint control of power allocation, sensing, compression, and transmission. [Publication 13] We introduce basic principles for BackCom system and network architectures with LSD-MIMO channels, and discussed emerging advanced BackCom techniques. [Publication 14] We have studied robust rate scheduling and average goodput performance of D2D underlaid massive MIMO systems. [Publication 15] We propose analytical framework to characterize the connectivity in mmWave A2X network with LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 16] We propose novel transmission scheme, namely FAT, for high-mobility data acquisition in edge learning over LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 17] We propose wirelessly powered-AirComp framework for the joint design of wireless power allocation, energy and aggregation beamforming over LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 18] We propose framework of multifunction AirComp for MIMO high-mobility multimodal sensor networks. [Publication 19] The effects of broadband analog aggregation on learning performance are quantified targeting single-cell random network over LSD-MIMO channels [Publication 20] We propose automatic modulation recognition approach for Grassmann constellation based on data clustering over LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 21] This work presents technologies for sensing hidden vehicles, its position, orientation, and size over LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 22] We propose multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) AirComp framework for IoT network with LSD-MIMO channels. [Publication 23] This paper provides comprehensive survey of MEC research for MIMO systems.

17259416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17259416.value: The further development of the research can be in several promising directions as listed below: 1) Understanding the effects of DoF LSD-MIMO channels for 6G terra-hertz systems; 2) How to design edge AI networks with LSD-MIMO channels? 3) The integrated computation and communication for edge computing over LSD-MIMO channels.

17259416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17259416.value: With spatial multiplexing, MIMO technologies have been a breakthrough in wireless communication and a core enabler for 5G and 6G systems. It is crucial to understand the limitation of such technologies using a practical LSD-MIMO channel model where scatter physical properties are modeled. This task is more challenging than traditional studies where abstracted and oversimplified MIMO channel models are used. By completing the task, the successful completion of this project has deepened our understanding of MIMO technologies and closing the gap between theory and practice. This pave the way to deploy such technologies in next-generation massive MIMO networks.

17260616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17260616.value: 機械性調整光學腔的共振頻率

17260616.label: Project Objectives
17260616.value: To prove the feasibility of stretchability and compressibility of GaN thin films: to exploit the “elasticity” of GaN crystals for dimensional fine-tuning of microstructures and nanostructures. To verify whispering-gallery mode resonance tunability in GaN thin-film microdisk: the project aims at demonstrating wavelength tuning from GaN thin-film microdisk laser diodes by the application of compressive and tensile forces. To show photonic bandgap tuning in a GaN photonic crystal: by varying the pitch between nano-pillars in an air-spaced photonic crystal, the photonic bandgap can be adjusted continuously. To demonstrate wavelength tunability of a GaN photonic crystal defect laser: with adjustments of the photonic bandgap, the resonant frequency and thus lasing wavelength of the laser can be tuned continuously.

To verify whispering-gallery mode resonance tunability in GaN thin-film microdisk: the project aims at demonstrating wavelength tuning from GaN thin-film microdisk laser diodes by the application of compressive and tensile forces.
To show photonic bandgap tuning in a GaN photonic crystal: by varying the pitch between nano-pillars in an air-spaced photonic crystal, the photonic bandgap can be adjusted continuously.

17260616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17260616.value: Tuning is always a feature that enhances the flexibility of a system. For light emitters, the ability to tune colors allows full-color display panels to be assembled, or the tuning of color temperatures in mood lighting luminaires. On the scientific front, tunable lasers widen the flexibilities and functionalities of spectroscopic and microscopic techniques. Unlike conventional gas lasers where the gain medium or the optical cavity can be accessed and adjusted readily, the laser diode is a rigid crystalline block that permits little modifications. Indirect means of tuning through thermal effects are possible but offer tuning ranges that highly limited. Resonance in an optical cavity is always related to its dimensions, be it cavity length in a Fabry-Perot mode laser, or radius in a whispering-gallery mode microdisk laser. If such dimensions are adjustable, the resonance conditions will be adjusted accordingly to achieve wavelength tuning. Can the cavity dimensions be adjusted in a crystalline GaN optical cavity? Why not? After all, atoms are held in place by coulombic forces which are elastic. Also, GaN films are always in a state of compression or tension due to lattice mismatch with its most common substrates of sapphire and silicon. This is also supported by molecular simulations, predicting that the GaN can be stretched and compressed by up to ±15% before cracking. Therefore, cavity dimensions and thus cavity resonance can be tuned, provided the cavity stretching or compression can be controlled. Realistically, cavity dimensions should be small for any realistic stretching or compression. The thin-film microdisk laser satisfies all these requirements, with lateral dimensions of microns and sub-micron thicknesses. By bonding the microdisks onto a flexible substrate, their diameters can be adjusted continuously, giving continuous tuning of its resonant frequencies and thus lasing wavelengths. The photonic crystal defect laser is another candidate to benefit from this flexible platform. By forming the hexagonal air-spaced nano-pillar array onto a flexible substrate, the pitch of the ordered structure can be adjusted continuously, offering ample control over the photonic band gap. Based on this innovative approach of semiconductor resonance tuning through mechanical means, wide tuning ranges can potentially be achieved, representing a major breakthrough in optical cavity technology.

17260616.label: Realisation of objectives
17260616.value: The project objectives were realized through careful design and planning, implementation through device fabrication and device characterization. The scheme of applying mechanical strain to the was investigated. The first approach studied in this project is based on heterogeneous integration by transferring the high quality GaN films from sapphire substrates to flexible plastic platform. Compared with typical chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) process, laser lift-off (LLO) process adopted in this study is a simple yet effective method to instantly detach GaN layer from its sapphire substrate by rapid thermal decomposition at the interface accomplished by pulsed-laser irradiation through the transparent sapphire. To mechanically tune the micro- and nano-structured devices in a controllable manner, the subsequent transfer to a flexible polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) film through the optimized LLO process will be implemented in this work. In addition, a low-cost and high-efficiency patterning technique - nano-/micro-sphere lithography (NSL) is employed to define 2D photonic crystal (PhC) and microdisk structures on GaN layers. The GaN-PDMS configuration enables optical tuning in photonic bandgap (PBG) from stretchable PhCs and whispering-gallery (WG) mode laser emission from bendable microdisks. Since a PhC comprising closed-packed pillar structure as fabricated by NSL do not produce a PBG, finite spacing between pillars must be introduced. The PhC-on-PDMS configuration with high stretchability provides possibility of fine-tuning of PBG by altering pitches into various extents. To predict the existences and positions of PBGs in nanopillars-based PhCs, band diagrams are computed using Rsoft BandSOLVE which implements the Plane Wave Expansion (PWE) algorithm for band computations. Their optical properties, being sensitive to the change in geometries, are comprehensively characterized, complemented by numerical simulations, aiming to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed GaN-PDMS platform for developing flexible micro- and nano-structured optical devices. The other approach of inducing strain is through nanostructuring. For the group III-nitrides, the In content in the quantum wells not only determines the color of emission, but also the extents of strains. The strain in the quantum wells give rise to the Quantum Confined Stark Effect (QCSE) which reduces IQEs and make emission wavelengths sensitive to current injection levels. Nano-structuring of the quantum wells has been demonstrated to alleviate the effects of QCSE in many reports via the strain relaxation effect. Nevertheless, strain relaxation via nano-structuring can only lead to spectral blue-shifting, while the ability to spectral red-shift will find invaluable applications in longer wavelength emitting InGaN LEDs, including the possibilities of red InGaN LEDs. As such, we attempt to modify the nanostructure configuration so that an increase of strain in the quantum wells can be achieved, as opposed to relaxing the strain, adopting a top-down fabrication approach. According to our previous studies on the strain relaxation mechanism of micropillars and its relation to emission color, a relative spectral red-shift at the edges of microdisks with low Indium content quantum wells compared to the centers of the microdisks has been observed through scanning near-field optical spectroscopy (SNOS), attributed to a local increase in strain field. Such unexpected observations inspire the design of the currently proposed structures. In this study, we report on the design, fabrication and characterization of an inverted nano-conical-frustum array that is capable of inducing spectral red-shifts in InGaN/GaN quantum wells via strain induction. Molecular dynamics simulations and k∙p calculations are employed to design and analyze the nanostructure, while photoluminescence (PL) and Raman studies are carried out on the fabricated nanostructures to verify the validity and feasibility of the proposed approach.

17260616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17260616.value: The optical effect of stretchable PhC structures on InGaN/GaN MQW emission are evaluated by room-temperature photoluminescence (PL) measurement. Compared with an unpatterned sample, the stretched PhC with a= 260 nm exhibits relatively high intensity at 420 nm. When enlarging the pitch to 280 nm and 300 nm, two spectral peaks appear at 454.1 nm and 471.5 nm respectively. Significant increase in PL intensities are obtained from spectral ranges within the PBGs (shaded regions), revealing that the PBG structure play a remarkable role in manipulating spontaneous emission by extracting guided modes to air. More pronounced enhancement is observed from the PhC with a= 280 nm, owing to the PBG overlapping optimally with the center emission region from InGaN/GaN MQWs. For wavelengths beyond PBGs, a lesser degree of enhancement is attributed to “weak” PhC effect originated from folding of dispersion curves of Bloch modes at the Brillouin zone boundaries. To evaluate the optical properties of microdisk cavities, a room-temperature micro-photoluminescence (μ-PL) measurements is conducted. Under low excitation, the spectrum exhibits a weak broadband peak at center wavelength of ~443 nm, corresponding to spontaneous emission from InGaN/GaN MQWs. As the excitation energy density exceeds the threshold of ~7 mJ/cm2 (Eth), a sharp peak emerges at a center wavelength of 440.6 nm with a linewidth of 0.65 nm and a Q-factor of 678. A nonlinear increase in the integrated PL intensity is clearly observed beyond the threshold value, confirming a transition process of spontaneous emission to stimulated emission with the microdisk. An inverted nano-conical frustum array for inducing spectral red-shift by increasing strain in InGaN/GaN quantum wells has also been demonstrated. Molecular dynamics simulations show that the out-of-plane strain can be induced at the base of the nanostructure, causing a spectral red-shift of as much as ~10 nm as estimated from k·p Schrödinger calculations. Experimentally, red-shifts of up to 7.6 nm have been observed. The shortfall is explained by the existence of the tensile-strained AlGaN/GaN EBL, as well as the multiple quantum well layers at different depths that are subjected to different magnitude of strain due to the strain gradient induced by the nanostructure. The IQEs of the samples with the inverted nano-conical frustum array have been demonstrated to be higher than the as-grown counterparts at the corresponding emission wavelengths.

17260616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17260616.value: There is huge market demand for optoelectronic devices that are flexible and wavelength tunable. The results of this project demonstrated that such capabilities is not limited to the organic materials; the inorganic GaN material is also capable of being flexible in terms of being stretched or compressed, so that their optical properties can be tuned. There is plenty of room for further development in the direction. This includes extending the scope of application to lighting and display applications based on the platforms having been developed in this project.

17260616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17260616.value: Unlike organic semiconductors that are made up of polymers or molecules, inorganic semiconductors are crystals that are typically hard and rigid. However, some degree of flexibility can be achieved as demonstrated in this project. By transferring thin films of semiconductors onto flexible substrates such as PDMS, the semiconductor films themselves can demonstrate some degrees of bendability. Further, by structuring such thin films into arrays of regular microstructures or nanostructures, the separation of such structures can be altered by stretching or compressing the flexible substrate. This is exploited for the development of tunable photonic structures on GaN thin films. GaN-based photonics crystals are fabricated on such films, so that the period of the photonic crystals can be changed by mechanical stretching of compression. As the optical properties of photonic crystals are sensitively dependent on the period, tuning of the photonic crystal properties can be achieved.

17261316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17261316.value: 無線電力傳輸（WPT）採用磁耦合技術去掉電器產品的電源電纜。使我們的生活更加方便，舒適。在不久的將來， WPT將完全融入我們的日常生活提供電力給我們的個人電子設備，可穿戴/植入電子，家電和電動車。乍看，WPT似乎是一個相當成熟的技術和多項產品已成為商用。然而，這些產品大多是固定式電池充電和穩定負載。在動態無線充電應用上，挑戰仍然是顯著。用動態無線電動車充電為一個實例，充電系統的動態響應是直接影響系統的效率和可靠性的一個關鍵問題。 將電力供應到在道路上移動的電動汽車（EV），充電系統的響應時間慢導致減少有效充電時間，並限制傳送到EV的能量。一些應用需要精確的功率控制（如生物醫學電子學）。過量的磁場激發會損壞病人的電子醫療植入物。相反，激勵不足，可能會導致不理想的電源造成不正確的操作或關機。 在這些應用中，我們需要一個反饋控制設計，保證WPT系統的可靠，穩定，精確，高效。通常，反饋控制的設計涉及系統執行穩定性分析和系統優化的動態模型。然而， WPT採用磁共振原理，採用開關電源轉換器。高階諧振網絡和非線性分量使過程非常複雜並且難以實現。在這個項目中，我們試圖解決這個控制問題: 1) 我們將開發一個完整的2線圈WPT系統的動態模型來預測系統的低頻和高頻動態行為 2) WPT動態模型特性將被明確記錄和制定。該模型將以計算機仿真和實驗測量來驗證 3) 我們將以實驗證明適當設計的反饋控制系統能夠改進系統的性能。 這個為期兩年的項目，無疑將推動WPT技術的研究和發展到了一個新的高度。動態WPT系統，解決負載要求的設計將變得比以前容易得多。這項目的成果有兩個： 1) 新的理論開發，將提供新的見解，知識和激發技術創新。學生和工人將獲得新的知識和技能。 2）項目將展示一個實際的解決方案，推動行業和從業者開發新的硬件和應用。 WPT技術的不斷發展，必將有利於各個行業領域，從而促進人類的生命。

17261316.label: Realisation of objectives
17261316.value: - This project is proceeding well. A modeling technique using phasor transformation technique for a two-coil wireless power transfer (WPT) system has been studied. The dynamic perform of a WPT system can be successfully predicted. - PI leaded his research student Mr. Jialong Qu to investigate into the principle and design procedure of a domino-resonator WPT system using printed-circuit-board (PCB) technology. This new proposed method takes the advantages of both winding inductance and intra-winding capacitance of a PCB coil to form a LC resonant circuit. The relation between quality factor of the coil and the ratio of inner/outer radius (i.e. Rin/Rout) is investigated to optimize the resonator design. - PI leaded his research team to integrate the planar PCB resonator coils into a high voltage insulation rod, so that this high voltage insulator can not only provides isolation between high voltage transmission line and transmission tower but also able to transfer energy from the high voltage transmission line to the transmission tower using WPT. - The modeling technique has been extended to multi-coil domino-resonator WPT system. It is well known that accurate electrical characteristic and parameters are difficult to measure in high frequency. We proposed a new methodology to obtain precise parameters based on the time-domain waveforms and Genetic Algorithm Optimization.

17261316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17261316.value: The evolution of wireless power transfer technology has dramatically changed our society. Over the past decade, it has tremendously transformed the way that electrical and electronic devices receive their power. Wireless power transfer technology has simplified the power solution needed in industry, medicine, communication and transportation. In this two-year research project, new understanding and theory of modelling, control and stability for wireless power transfer systems have been studied. The knowledge is formulated into three research publications (i.e. two published conference papers, one submitted journal paper and on journal paper in preparation) Students working in the project have been trained with necessary knowledge in the wireless power to contribute to the industry. New design knowledge and principle are applied to a novel high voltage insulator with the capability of harvesting and transferring the energy from a high voltage transmission line to the transmission tower. The energy is stored in a battery for powering the smart grid online monitoring equipment . Outcomes of the project benefits various fields of industry to meet the need of more flexible, efficient and safe power delivery solutions.

17261416.label: Project Objectives
17261416.value: Design a novel smart vehicle-to-grid aggregator (SVA): We will devise SVA for the provision of real-time power balance by employing V2G while meeting the charging demands of EVs. The architectural design of SVA will be investigated to define the functions, interactions, and protocols of SVAs among EVs and a utility grid operator. Devise a novel unified theory of EV charging/discharging control and grid power balance (EVCB): We will propose EVCB to model and identify a set of optimal mechanisms for coordinating both EV charging/discharging control and grid power balance jointly. The system model for EVCB can be formulated and thus optimal distributed control mechanisms can be found. With the support of solid theoretical analysis, we can gain a better understanding on the validity and feasibility of the control mechanisms for the desired services. Develop a set of distributed protocols for SVA: Based on the findings from the theory of EVCB, we will develop a set of distributed protocols among a set of SVAs, a utility grid operator, and a set of EVs, known as SVA protocols, so as to yield near-optimal real-time grid power balance, via frequency regulation and/or capacity firming for renewables, while meeting the charging demands of EVs. The proposed protocols will help guide the charging/discharging activities of EVs while accommodating the regulation signals, thereby maintaining the reliability and stability of the grid. The performance of these protocols will be evaluated using real data traces, such as those collected from Southern California Edison (SCE) and Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnection (PJM).

17261416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17261416.value: Balancing power generation and demand in real time is critical for reliable and stable operation in electrical grids. The deviation of the utility frequency from its nominal value is a simple and prevalent indicator of such real-time power imbalance. Frequency regulation, which maintains the utility frequency at its nominal value, is the most expensive ancillary service. Concerns with global warming prompted governments throughout the world to pursue policies aiming at the reduction of greenhouse gases, say, by mandating increased renewable energy penetration in electricity generation. Unfortunately, the current real-time power balance mechanisms are inadequate because 1) the uncertainty and variability of intermittent renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar, make the power generation outputs difficult to forecast and follow, posing new challenges to real-time power balance, and 2) the provision of generators supplying regulation would reduce their power outputs to the energy market, since some portions of their rated capacities are reserved exclusively for regulation. Recent studies show that the power electronics and batteries in electric vehicles (EVs) can respond very well to regulation signals through frequent charging and discharging of the batteries. In this project, we propose a novel set of aggregators, known as smart vehicle-to-grid aggregators (SVAs), to coordinate a group of plug-in EVs in a multi-level vehicle-to-grid (V2G) system. An aggregation of these EVs forms a collection of dynamic, scalable, and distributed energy storage units for the provision of real-time power balance services, such as frequency regulation and renewables capacity firming, in electrical grids. The architectural design of SVA will be investigated to define the functions, interactions, and protocols of SVAs among EVs and a utility grid operator. We will devise a novel unified theory of EV charging/discharging control and real-time grid power balance (EVCB) so that the system model for EVCB can be formulated. Based on the findings from the theory of EVCB, we will develop a set of distributed protocols among a set of SVAs, a utility grid operator, and a set of EVs, known as SVA protocols, so as to yield near-optimal control supporting real-time power balance while meeting the charging demands of EVs. With these efforts, we expect that this project will impact the design and development of the next-generation control mechanisms for real-time power balance in electrical grids. The basic science developed in this project will be important contributions to the research community, while the knowledge gained will be valuable to industry. 維持發電和負載的實時平衡是保證電力系統的可靠性和穩定性的關鍵。電網頻率相對標準頻率的偏離量是判斷電網有功功率實時平衡的一個簡單而常用的指標。頻率調整服務使電網頻率維持在標準頻率，是最昂貴的一種電網輔助服務。全球變暖問題促使全球各地政府力推溫室氣體減排政策，比如硬性要求提升可再生能源在總發電量中的比重。然而遺憾的是，現有的實時功率平衡機制不足以應對這樣的要求。主要原因為以下兩點。第一，間歇性可再生能源，比如風能和太陽能，的不確定性和可變性使得發電端變得難以預測和跟隨，從而給維持實時功率平衡帶來新的挑戰。第二，為保證引入可再生能源后的功率平衡，傳統發電機需要預留更多的預備電力來提供頻率調整服務，導致傳統發電機產電能力的下降。 近期研究表明，電動汽車中的電力電子設備和電池可使其及時響應頻率調整的信號，對電池進行相應的充電和放電。本項目提出了一種新穎的整合商概念，名為智能車輛到電網服務整合商,用於協調多級車輛到電網系統中的一組電動汽車的充放電行為。通過對多輛電動汽車的整合，可形成一組動態、可擴展、分佈式的儲能單元，用以提供實時功率平衡服務，例如頻率調整和可再生能源產能整合。本項目將研究服務整合商的架構設計，明確定義服務整合商在為電動汽車和電網運營商提供協調服務時，所需要的功能、交互及協議。將設計一套創新的電動汽車充放電控制有實時功率平衡的統一理論，并完成相應的系統建模。基於此理論框架及發現，將研發一系列針對電網運營商、整合商及電動汽車的協同動作的分佈式協議，從而實現支持實現功率平衡及滿足電動汽車充電需求的近似最優控制。 通過這些努力，我們預期本項目將對下一代電網實時功率平衡的控制機制的設計和研發帶來重要影響。本項目所建立的科學理論將給科研界作出重要貢獻，而從中獲得的知識和經驗將對工業界有很大價值。

17261416.label: Realisation of objectives
17261416.value: We have achieved the three objectives proposed in this project. To overcome these problems, under Objective 1 of our project, we have proposed, in [1], a system architecture for the utility grid operator and aggregators to coordinate multiple grid-connected electric vehicles (EVs) so as to provide electric-power ancillary services accounting for quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees for EV charging in a multilevel vehicle-to-grid (V2G) system. This architecture includes applying consensus-algorithm-based distributed control, designing the control objective functions and constraints for providing ancillary services, and designing the constraints for charging/discharging power schedules and the individual QoS requirements of EVs. The consensus-algorithm-based distributed control consists of operation protocols for control and communication among the utility grid operator, aggregators, and EVs, calculating the control signals in the utility grid operator and aggregators, determining the optimal charging/discharging power schedules of EVs so as to provide a required type of ancillary services as well as satisfy the QoS requirements of EVs. Building on this architecture, Objectives 2 and 3 have been achieved through developing a set of theoretical models and distributed protocols for EV charing/discharging control and grid power balance. In [2, 11], we have formulated the joint storage configuration problem for the energy storage system and devised a scheme inspired from the idea of the leaky bucket mechanism for smoothing the power output from a renewable energy system. In our proposed method, the settings of energy storage size and power output level have significant effects on the system performance and thus needs to be determined. An optimization framework was thus proposed for storage and power output planning of the renewable energy system. To operate our proposed scheme practically, a load-adaptive power smoothing algorithm was devised aiming to match the power output level with the actual load in the grid, thereby reducing the operation cost and maintaining high renewable energy utilization. In [3, 7], a generic hierarchical framework for V2G system to provide frequency regulation services has been developed to address how to coordinate the participating EVs to provide such ancillary services. A practical multi-level online V2G algorithm is proposed for the hierarchical V2G scheduling and it requires no forecasting information for regulation signals. The work has further been extended and generalised the interactions of the power flows in a smart grid. In [5, 12], we have proposed a hierarchical system model to jointly optimize power flow routing and V2G scheduling for providing regulation service. By installing power flow routers (PFRs) inside the power grid, we formulated the problem of optimal power flow (OPF) routing at the grid level. Through the utilization of the semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation, the original non-deterministic polynomial-time hard (NP-hard) problem was transformed into a convex problem. The tree decomposition method was then used to further reduce the complexity of the system network. After solving the grid-level OPF routing problem, a forecast-based scheduling problem was formulated at the EV level to coordinate EVs by providing the V2G regulation service. To cope with the forecast uncertainties, an online scheduling problem was in turn devised. In order to solve these problems in a scalable manner, we developed decentralized algorithms for determining the EV schedules. In [4, 6, 10], game theoretic approaches using non-cooperative and cooperative game have been proposed to motivate selfish EVs to provide frequency regulation services for the power grid. In a non-cooperative V2G system, the interaction between the EV aggregator and EVs was formulated as a non-cooperative Stackelberg game. The EV aggregator as the leader decides the electricity trading price, and EVs as the followers determine their charging/discharging strategies. In a cooperative V2G system, a potential game was formulated to achieve the optimal social welfare of the V2G system. Our proposed game theoretic approaches can effectively motivate EVs to smooth out the power fluctuations from the grid while EVs schedule their charging/discharging activities to maximize their utilities. This work has been extended in [8], where each EV does not have any private information of other EVs. To find the Nash equilibrium of this game, a machine learning-based algorithm was proposed based on fictitious self-play. In [9, 13], we have proposed a novel smart cross-system framework to support V2G regulation service in a smart city. Specifically, by considering electric buses (EBs) as a particular group of EVs with large battery packs installed and predictable operation schedules, we jointly solved the problems of EB allocation and scheduling with V2G regulation service. By using the deep learning approach, the short-term city traffic conditions can be predicted via the gated recurrent units (GRUs) neural network. With the predicted traffic conditions, we then formulated the EB allocation and V2G scheduling as a mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) problem. In order to solve this problem effectively, we utilized the Lagrangian dual decomposition method to decouple the main problem into subproblems for EBs and devise a distributed algorithm to solve each subproblem. Through efficient EB routing strategies under accurate predicted traffic conditions, the power fluctuations of the city power grid can be well flatten by providing the V2G regulation service. 17261416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17261416.value: There are several research directions worth further investigation: 1. Optimal placement of charging infrastructure: We have investigated the operational algorithms for V2G regulation. It would be interesting to extend the work for studying the optimal placement of charging infrastructure, such as charging poles and charging stations, in a citywide area with respect to the road conditions, traffic flows, and mobility patterns of EVs. 2. Dynamic energy reserve estimation: We have studied the day-ahead frequency regulation reserve in a general power distribution system. This provision of the frequency regulation service only handles the active power fluctuations. It would be interesting to extend the work to consider and deal with the reactive power imbalance.

17261916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17261916.value: Rapid industrialization and urbanization often cause serious water pollution as evidenced in Hong Kong, mainland China and many other regions. However, conventional wastewater treatment systems still rely on the core technologies developed more than half century ago that are no longer capable of coping with the increasing pollutant load and more stringent effluent standards. Nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorous) in wastewater discharge induce eutrophication and frequent algal blooms in natural waters. Compared to organic degradation, nutrient removal from wastewater is much more difficult and costly. For biological N removal, a sufficient organic carbon content is requested for denitrification. However, the organic carbon/nitrogen ratio in municipal wastewater is becoming lower in recent years. To make up for the organic deficit, an external organic carbon source (e.g. methanol) has been increasingly added into wastewater for N removal. On the other hand, there is a large amount of organic in the waste sludge discharged from the treatment process. The organic in wastewater can be valuable materials that should be recovered and utilized instead of being degraded or wasted into sludge. This project is proposed to recover organic from the primary sludge to provide the extra organic carbon for denitrification in wastewater treatment. The new process will apply chemical coagulants, polyaluminium chloride (PAC) or ferric chloride (FeCl3), to enhance the primary sedimentation, which not only concentrates organics into the primary sludge but also reduces the pollutant (organic and P) load on the downstream treatment. The sludge will be fed into a side-stream anaerobic reactor for sludge hydrolysis and acidogenesis, producing volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and other soluble organic substances. The organic-rich supernatant of the sludge after fermentation will be supplied to the main wastewater stream for denitrification. During the study, various pretreatment means will be tests for improvement of the sludge hydrolysis result. DNA-based molecular techniques will be applied to characterize the microbial communities during the sludge fermentation process. The novel process can be readily modularized and adopted not only for the design of new treatment plants but also for retrofitting existing treatment systems. The innovation will help improve the pollutant removal efficiency, achieve resource utilization, and reduce the overall energy consumption and sludge yield in wastewater treatment. The technology also can be specifically applied to the upgrading of the chemically-enhanced primary treatment currently used by the main sewage treatment works in Hong Kong to the level of secondary biological treatment. 隨著經濟社會的發展，水污染問題日益嚴重，香港、中國大陸以及世界很多地區的自然環境都承受著越來越大的污染壓力。傳統的污水處理技術沿用至今已超過半個世紀，難以應對當今工業化和城鎮化所帶來的不斷增加的污染負荷。生活污水中含有大量的營養元素(氮和磷)，若未妥當處置即排入自然水體會導致水體的富營養化和藻類的瘋長，水質惡化。與處理有機物相比，營養元素的去除更加困難、昂貴。生物法脫氮的反硝化過程需要消耗大量的有機碳源，但近年來市政污水所含的有機碳源嚴重不足，既碳/氮比例低，無法滿足脫氮要求。為了彌補污水本身碳源的不足，越來越多的外部有機碳源（如甲醇）被投加到污水中以滿足脫氮需要，進一步提高了污水處理成本。另一方面，作為污水中主要的污染物，大量有機物進入剩餘污泥被排放。然而這些有機物也是寶貴的資源，應該加以回收利用而不是隨剩餘污泥棄置浪費。 本項目旨在從初沉污泥中回收有機碳源，將其作為污水脫氮處理過程中的補充碳源加以利用。這項新技術將採用聚合氯化鋁（PACl）或氯化鐵（FeCl3）實現污水中污染物的一級強化沉澱，不僅將有機物高度濃縮與初沉污泥中，同時減小了下游污水處理的污染負荷。強化沉澱的污泥將進入側流厭氧發酵罐進行水解酸化，以獲得揮發性脂肪酸（VFAs）及其他有機資源。發酵之後富含有機碳源的污泥上清夜用於反硝化脫氮。本項目將研究不同的預處理手段以有效提高污泥的水解效率，并採用分子生物學手段監控污泥發酵過程中微生物群落的變化。本項新技術還能集成為單元模塊的形式，不僅能夠運用於新的污水處理廠，還能順利配合現有污水處理的基本系統，直接添加到所需處理階段，方便實現處理設施的升級換代。本項創新技術能高效提高污水處理效果，實現資源回收，還能減少整個污水處理過程的能耗和污泥產量。此外，該項技術能針對性地運用到香港的污水處理廠，將主流的一級化學混凝處理過程提升至二級生物處理水平。

17261916.label: Realisation of objectives
17261916.value: All of the research objectives have been well achieved. Following the proposal, a novel chemical-biological process with coagulants-facilitated sedimentation, enhanced sludge hydrolysis, and carbon self-sufficient biological nitrogen removal has been developed for enhanced wastewater treatment with resource recovery. Chemically enhanced primary sedimentation (CEPS) was applied to achieve the pollutant redirection from the sewage to sludge. With the addition of coagulants, followed by sedimentation, over 70% of chemical oxygen demand (COD) and 90% of total phosphorus (TP) were effectively concentrated into the primary sludge for resource recovery, which is much higher than the removal efficiencies of 30% and 15% of the conventional primary sedimentation process without chemical coagulation. For further improving the removal of fine CEPS flocs and reducing the footprint for primary sedimentation, a novel integration of CEPS and flat-sheet ceramic membranes (FSCM) has been developed. Raw domestic sewage was collected from Stanley Sewage Treatment Works (Stanley STW), Hong Kong, for the membrane filtration experiments. The sewage flowed through the coagulation chamber for approximately 2 min under a rapid mixing condition at 200 ± 20 rpm. The sewage after coagulation flowed into the membrane tank for the rapid solid-liquid separation. Using polyaluminum chloride (PACl) based FSCM filtration, approximately 90.0% of COD and 99.0% of phosphorus were removed from the sewage influent and retained in the concentrated sludge, with less than 25.0 mg/L COD left in the effluent. Compared to the direct filtration of municipal sewage without coagulation, the chemical dosing and coagulation step greatly increased the membrane filtration flux to about 1.0 m/d (~41.7 LMH). By pre-coagulation, foulants in the sewage influent were aggregated into flocs, which effectively prevented the foulants from entering the membrane pores. With the pre-coagulation of sewage before FSCM filtration, the fouled ceramic membranes can be readily and effectively cleaned to recover their permeability via simple chemical backwashing once every 3–5 d for approximately 10 min with a diluted acidic, alkaline, H2O2, or chlorine solution. With the effective solid-liquid separation of the CEPS-FSCM filtration, the majority of organics and phosphorus in the municipal wastewater can be redirected to the sidestream for resource recovery, while the CEPS-treated effluent flows into the biological treatment units for the nitrogen removal. Due to the low organic strength and low COD/N ratio of the CEPS effluent, COD and NH4+-N could not be effectively removed by the commonly used suspended sludge-based bioreactors because of its poor sludge retention performance. Thus, a moving bed biofilm reactor (MBBR) filled with sponge-like LEVAPOR biocarrier cubes was utilized for the further pollutant removal and nitrification. With a high and stable biomass content, the concentrations of COD and NH4+-N can decreased to <50 mg COD/L and <5 mg NH4+-N/L in the MBBR effluent, showing a much better performance than the counterpart of the suspended sludge-based bioreactor (about 100 mg COD/L and 10 mg NH4+-N/L). With the excellent organic removal by the CEPS, the low concentration of residual COD in wastewater cannot provide sufficient electron donors for nitrate reduction. Efforts have been made to recover organic carbon sources from CEPS sludge by fermentation. The CEPS sludge with the SS of 6,210 mg/L and total COD of 8,259 mg/L was fermented under anaerobic conditions at 35°C±1°C for 5 days, during which the organic sludge underwent hydrolysis and acidogenesis to produce volatile fatty acids (VFAs). The supernatant, named CEPS-FL, was then obtained from the sludge fermentation liquor by centrifugation. With the CEPS and sludge fermentation, about 20% of organic substances in municipal wastewater could be recovered as the VFAs-rich fermentation supernatant to provide the carbon source for denitrification. Batch tests were conducted to determine the effectiveness of CEPS-FL, methanol, and sodium acetate (NaAc) for heterotrophic denitrification. Compared to methanol, the CEPS-FL exhibited a higher denitrification rate (410.3 g N/kg VSS/d) and a lower N2O emission potential (1.14%) without fire risk, and the operating cost of the CEPS-fermentation-denitrification combined system is 28.3–44.6% lower than the municipal wastewater treatment supplemented with methanol or sodium acetate. Since the sedimentation of fermented CEPS is difficult, the feasibility and effectiveness of using the CEPS sludge liquor without solid-liquid separation for enhanced biological nitrogen removal was also investigated. During the over 180 days of operation, the new system with the integration of CEPS and acidogenic sludge fermentation stably removed 89% of TP and 83% of the TN from the wastewater, which was much higher than the 65% and 50% of the conventional biological treatment process. However, along with the decomposition of organic substances during anaerobic fermentation, the organic nitrogen in proteins, amino acids, and nucleic acids can be converted to ammonium in the fermentation supernatant, limiting the potential utilization of VFAs. Although the amount of ammonium nitrogen returned with the CEPS-FL will not have a great effect (12.1% of TN) on the overall nitrogen removal performance of the municipal wastewater treatment, effective recovery of ammonium nitrogen from the CEPS fermentation liquor could further improve the overall nitrogen removal efficiency in the CEPS-fermentation-denitrification combination. Besides, restricted by the fermentation organic load, solution pH, and sludge age, less than 10% of TP in CEPS sludge can be recovered from the sludge fermentation supernatant. In this project, the electro-fermentation (EF) technology was also developed to enhance the separation and concentration of nutrients from the CEPS sludge. Using a two-chamber bioreactor with a cation exchange membrane and an exterior voltage (0.5–1.0 V), the EF treatment of Fe-sludge significantly improved the efficiency of P dissolution from the sludge from 8% to 56% after 4 d. Meanwhile, about 70% of released ammonium ions and 50% of Fe in the sludge were driven by the current from the sludge suspension into the cathode chamber for potential recovery. With a similar yield of VFAs but less ammonium remaining, the CODVFA/NNH4 of the sludge supernatant from the EF reactor could reach 67.7, much higher than that from the single-chamber fermenter at 13.0. Besides the conventional nitrogen removal via the nitrification-denitrification process, a novel CEPS-partial nitritation-anammox (PNA) combination was also developed for autotrophic nitrogen removal. In view of the slow growth rate of anammox and the long start-up time of the autotrophic nitrogen removal systems, research was conducted on the rapid development of anammox and PNA biofilms and the fast start-up of PNA reactors for autotropic nitrogen removal. The packed bed biofilm reactor, instead of the commonly used MBBR, was developed as an effective means for the formation and growth of anammox biofilms in the reactor. Mature anammox biofilm was well developed and the nitrogen removal capacity increased rapidly from 77.6 to 876.8 mg N/L/d in less than 2 months. By using the pre-acclimated anammox biofilms, a new sludge seeding and operating strategy was developed for the rapid start-up of the PNA-integrated fixed-film activated sludge (IFAS) system for autotrophic nitrogen removal. Different from the common inoculation of suspended PNA sludge with bare biocarriers, the seeding of anammox biofilms on biocarriers, together with the suspended PNA sludge, can shorten the start-up time of the PNA-IFAS system from more than half a year to one month or so. Moreover, compared to the control bioreactor with the conventional seeding and operating approach, the bioreactor seeded with anammox biofilms exhibited a higher nitrogen removal capacity (707.3±45.1 vs. 395.1±11.1 mg N/L/d), a lower nitrate yield (9.4±1.1% vs. 19.5±4.6%), and improved stability in long-term operation.
