17307916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307916.value: Statin drugs like simvastatin, rosuvastatin, atorvastatin and others are among the most widely prescribed drugs in the world since they can help with the primary and secondary prevention of coronary heart disease. However, some statin drugs may have adverse health effects such as subacute cutaneous lupus, dermatomyositis, lichenoid drug eruptions, and photoallergic reactions after the patient is exposed to sunlight. It is important to better understand how sunlight excitation of different statin drugs induces these adverse health effects that are the result of the photochemistry of these compounds. So far, there has been limited research to study the photophysics and photochemistry of statin drug compounds. Some research studies have been done to identify and characterize the photoproducts of several statin drugs. For several statins, nanosecond time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy investigations have directly observed some intermediate species on the nanosecond to microsecond time-scales but the identity and structure of these intermediates remain unclear. There are not yet any ultrafast (femtoseconds to picoseconds) time-resolved spectroscopy experiments reported in the literature. To gain additional and missing information about the photophysics and photochemistry of selected statin drugs, several different types of time-resolved spectroscopy methods will be used to directly observe and characterize the excited states, intermediates and products from femtoseconds to final products. Femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy will be used to examine the excited states and intermediates to provide new insight into the early time photophysics and photochemistry of these compounds. Next, nanosecond time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy and photoproduct analysis experiments will be done. This work combined with the femtosecond time-resolved spectra will enable a comprehensive characterization of the photophysics and photochemistry from initial excitation on the femtosecond time scale all the way to formation of the final products for the statin compounds examined. To gain missing information about the structure and properties of the excited states and intermediate species, picosecond and nanosecond time-resolved resonance Raman experiments will be performed for the statin molecules of interest. This new data will help to clearly identify as well as to elucidate the structure and properties of the excited states and intermediate species involved in the photophysics and photochemistry of the statin compounds investigated. The new information for the photophysics, photochemistry, excited states and reactive intermediates for the statin compounds examined in this project should be useful for future research to help design and develop new and improved statin compounds for a variety of applications. 摘要 他汀類藥物（辛伐他丁、瑞舒伐他汀、阿托伐他汀等）是世界上目前最廣泛的處方藥，它們能幫助初級和次級預防冠狀動脈心臟疾病。然而，有些他汀類藥物可能對健康產生不利影響，例如患者曝露在陽光下時會產生亞急性皮膚紅斑狼瘡、皮肌炎、苔蘚樣藥疹和光過敏反應等。因此探索太陽光照射不同他汀類藥物誘導產生這些不利於健康的影響是非常有意義的，而這些有害健康的副作用主要是藥物光照后光化學反應引起的。目前，只有非常少的工作開展他汀類藥物的光物理和光化學過程的研究。其中已有的一些研究只是指認和表征了一些他汀類藥物分子的光產物。目前已有一些研究利用納秒瞬態吸收光譜直接考察納秒和微秒時間範圍內可觀察到的一些反應活性中間體，但是這些中間體的化學特性和結構仍然不清楚。目前，還沒有任何文獻報道他汀類藥物的超快（飛秒到皮秒）時間分辨激光光譜研究。為了獲得一些重要的他汀類藥物分子的光物理和光化學所缺失的信息，在本項目研究中，幾種不同類型的時間分辨光譜方法將用於直接探測和表征從起始到最終產物過程中產生的激發態、活性反應中間體和產物。飛秒時間分辨瞬態吸收光譜將用於考察激發態和中間體，為這些藥物的光物理和光化學過程提供超快時間範圍內新的認知和視野。然後，將開展納秒時間分辨瞬態吸收光譜和最終光產物分析實驗。納秒時間分辨光譜、最終產物分析并結合飛秒時間分辨光譜將使我們能夠全面地表征和考察他汀類藥物的飛秒時間範圍內的起始激發態和形成最終產物的所有反應路徑的光物理和光化學過程。為了獲得缺失的激發態和中間體的結構和化學反應特性信息，將會開展他汀類藥物分子的皮秒和納秒時間分辨共振拉曼光譜研究。這些新數據將有助於明確識別和闡明所考察的他汀類藥物分子的光物理和光化學過程中的激發態和中間體的結構和化學反應特性。在這個研究項目中，所考察他汀類藥物分子新的光物理、光化學、激發態和反應中間體的信息將非常有助於將來設計和開發新的藥物，改進和提高他汀類藥物的各種應用。

17307916.label: Realisation of objectives
17307916.value: For Objectives 1 and 2 we have performed femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA) and other time-resolved spectroscopy methods to characterise the excited states and intermediates associated with the photophysics and photochemistry of Blebbistatin and selected derivatives like deoxyblebbistatin and blebbistatin-O-benzoate in aqueous solutions. Additional experiments like ultraviolet/visible absorption, resonance Raman spectroscopy and mass spectrometry techniques were also used to characterise any photoproducts produced. Reaction mechanism(s) were deduced and proposed from the preceding data in conjunction with results from some supporting density functional theory calculations. The research for these objectives found that Blebbistatin can be excited by either a one-photon blue photon of light or by two-photon photoexcitation using near infrared light and Blebbistatin can perform as a photocage to directly release a hydroxyl radical (•OH) in the absence of oxygen in aqueous solutions. By using fs-TA and chemoselective ROS fluorescent probes, we investigated the dynamics and fate of Blebbistatin during photolysis under blue light. The water-dependent photochemistry of Blebbistatin reveals a a key process of water-assisted protonation and excited state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) which induces the generation of short-lived intermediates that unexpectedly results in the release of •OH but not superoxide or singlet oxygen from Blebbistatin. CASPT2//CASSCF computations confirm that hydrogen bonding between water and Blebbistatin is responsible for this process. We further discovered that blue light allows Blebbistatin to result in mitochondria-dependent apoptosis which is an property favorable for the development of photochemically activated cancer therapy (PACT) compounds. Our results for the different Blebbistatin derivatives were reported in publications 1,3 and 6 as well as conference presentations 1, 2 and 3 of section C of this completion report. We estimate that we have realized about 100% of objectives 1 and 2 to date. For Objectives 3, 4, 5 and 6 we have attempted and in some cases were able to obtain new time-resolved spectroscopy and product analysis results for other statins like simvastatin, lovastatin and pravastatin that are naturally derived type I statin drugs and rosuvastatin fluvastatin, pitavastatin and atorvastatin that are synthetic type II statin drugs in order to learn more about their mechanism(s) for phototoxicity. We found that the fs-TA were more difficult to acquire for these other statins in comparison to Blebbistatin and its derivatives so we could only obtain limited experimental data and we are currently preparing these results for publication in due course in conjunction with on-going DFT computations that are being done to help interpret the experimental results we have obtained for selected examples of the type I and II statins. These statins are composed of several different chromophores so we looked for a drug that was also composed of several different chromophores whose individual components are phototoxic but the drug itself when the phototoxic parts are added together becomes much less phototoxic and more photostable. We searched the literature and found that the cancer drug, Imatinib is this kind of drug but it is not known why it has low phototoxicity and high photostbility so we chose to study Imatinib for comparison purposes to better understand how interactions between different chromophores can lead a drug to have less phototoxicity and higher photostability than its individual component chromophores. This new work on Imatinib found that an intramolecular charge separation can account for the relaxation of its excited state between different chromophores that helps substantially reduce phototoxicity and increase the photostability of the Imatinib drug. These results for Imatinib were reported in Publication 4 of Section C of this completion report. These new Imatinib and Type I and II statin results can be employed in due course to help aid in the design of statin drugs to have lower phototoxicity or improved photostability using chromophore-chromophore interactions as was done for the Imatinib drug. We estimate that we have realized about 80% of objectives 3, 4, 5 and 6 to date. For Objective 7 we have made comparisons between the results of different statin compounds and in particular between different Blebbistatin derivatives as reported in publications 1,3 and 6 as well as conference presentations 1, 2 and 3 of section C of this completion report. We estimate that we have realized about 80% of objective 7 to date.

17307916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307916.value: We have performed time-resolved spectroscopy and product analysis experiments for Blebbistatin and its derivatives like deoxyblebbistatin and blebbistatin-O-benzoate in aqueous solutions. This research to better understand the blue light photoinactivation and phototoxicitiy of blebbistatin discovered an unexpected mechanism for blebbistatin phototoxicity, in which water-assisted excited state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) induces a novel direct photorelease of •OH from blebbistatin in aqueous solutions which is one of the major findings of this project. This unprecedented mechanism bypasses the generation of singlet oxygen or superoxide that would be expected for conventional photodynamic therapy (PDT) and this new discovery indicates that such photorelease of •OH involves hydrogen bonding between water molecules and blebbistatin via concerted protonation and ESIPT. A second major finding was the discovery that two-photon photoexcitation using near-infrared light was also able to photorelease •OH in an efficient and controlled manner. This means that near-infrared light can photorelease •OH in in a spatially and temporally controlled way which makes this system very attractive to develop for applications as a photochemically activated cancer therapy (PCAT) agent. Unlike conventional PDT agents that are functionally dependent on molecular oxygen to generate singlet oxygen, Blebbistatin can photorelease of •OH without the need for the presence of molecular oxygen in the surrounding environment which makes it particularly have potential for PCAT applications for drug delivery to deep tissues or hypoxic tumor microenvironments that are difficult for conventional PDT agents. A third major finding of this project was that similar photolease of other leaving groups (like O-benzoate) attached in the same position as the OH group in Blebbistatin could also be photoreleased by either one-photon of blue light or two-photons of near infrared light. These results indicate the potential fr developing Blebbistatin derivatives for applications as photocages to release a wide variety of different species for a wider range of applications in biology and materials science. We have also obtained new time-resolved spectroscopy and product analysis results for other statins like simvastatin and pravastatin that are naturally derived type I statin drugs and rosuvastatin and atorvastatin that are synthetic type II statin drugs as well a benchmark cancer drug, Imatinib for comparison purposes to better understand interactions between different chromophores. These new results will be utilized to help give insight to aid in the design of statin drugs to have lower phototoxicitiy or improved photostability using chromophore-chromophore interactions as was done for the Imatinib drug.

17307916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307916.value: In this GRF project a major finding was the discovery that the small molecule Blebbistatin can be excited by either one-photon of blue light or two-photons of near infrared light to directly release a hydroxyl radical (•OH) without the presence of oxygen in the surrounding environment. Another related finding is that other leaving groups at the same position of the OH group in Blebbistatin can also be released in a similar fashion and this indicates the potential use of Blebbistatin derivatives for applications as a photocage to release a wide variety of different species. These discoveries suggest potential further development of Blebbistatin derivatives as chemically tunable photocage compounds for photoactivated chemotherapy (PACT) agents and more generally as photocages to release other biological effectors for use in physiology and chemical biology experiments to better understand biological functions. The new information obtained regarding the photophysics, photochemistry, excited states and reactive intermediates for the blebbistatin and related compounds in this project will guide future research to help design and develop new and improved blebbistatin derivatives and related compounds for use as PACT agents and more widely as phototrigger compounds for a broader range of applications.

17307916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307916.value: Some statin compounds have found use as drugs for primary and secondary prevention of coronary heart disease while others like Blebbistatin have found utility as a myosin II inhibitor in chemical biology. However, statin drugs and compounds can display unwanted phototoxicity effects after being exposed to sunlight. It is therefore important to better understand how sunlight excitation of different statin compounds induces these adverse effects that are the result of the photochemistry of these compounds. This research project used time-resolved spectroscopy and other experiments to obtain additional and missing information about the photophysics and photochemistry of selected statin drugs. We discovered that Blebbistatin can be excited by either one-photon of blue light or two-photons of near infrared light to directly release a hydroxyl radical (•OH) that can have potential for use as a photoactivated chemotherapy (PACT) agent. The new information for the photophysics, photochemistry, excited states and reactive intermediates for the selected statin compounds investigated in this project will steer future research to aid the design and development of new and improved statin compounds for a variety of applications including as photocage compounds for PACT agents and more generally as photocages to release other biological effectors.

17308316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17308316.value: The fossils of the Cretaceous Jehol Biota are exquisitely preserved and extraordinarily diverse. Strata interpreted to be correlative with the classic Jehol localities occur throughout Eastern China, as well as in Korea, Japan, Mongolia, and Siberia. It has been previously hypothesized based on fossil assemblages that the Jehol Biota originated from the classic Jehol area in NE China and then expanded, with younger representatives covering progressively larger geographic ranges. Researchers have not yet established a detailed stratigraphic correlation between the classic Jehol outcrops and less well-studied localities. In the past three decades, fossils of the Jehol Biota, including mollusks, conchostracans, ostracods, insects, fish and plants, have been identified at localities throughout South China. Here, we propose high-precision geochronologic analysis of correlative Jehol units recently identified in Fujian and Zhejiang Provinces. Resultant chronostratigraphic constraints will enable precise correlation of these units with the classic Jehol strata and help evaluate the Jehol radiation and migration hypothesis. 自1990年起，中外古生物學家和地質學家投入大量人力、物力挖掘熱河生物群化石，主要的研究區域集中在遼寧西部和河北、內蒙一帶，研究成果大大提升我們對有羽毛恐龍、哺乳動物、鳥類及早期開花植物的認識，同時，也讓我們得以一窺白堊紀的生物樣貌。過去20年來，偶有零星的熱河生物群動物在南中國出土，但尚未有大規模的挖掘和研究，本研究旨在建立南中國熱河生物群地層高精確的年代，我們的結果可以提供與北方化石層的準確對比。

17308316.label: Realisation of objectives
17308316.value: 1. During three field trips, we collected several rhyolites, and tuffaceous sandstones from the Jehol related outcrops. Zircons, k-feldspars and biotites are selected from these samples. However, we didn't find any fresh sanidine and biotite for 40Ar/39Ar. To get reliable ages, we decided to analyse zircons instead. All zircons have been analysed using Laser Ablation Multiple Collector Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer (LA-MC-ICPMS) at Department of Earth Sciences, HKU. The age results from U/Pb analysis are convincing as they indicated all Jehol fossil-rich strata from South China are ~135-125 Ma. 2. We collected abundant invertebrate fossils and more than 15 vocalic samples from Fujian and Zhejiang Provinces. Fossil assemblage is similar with the one from the NE China. Based on the paleontological and geochronological correlations, the Jehol formations in the less-studied outcrops of South China should be correlated with the Jiufotang Formation in the classic outcrop of Liaoning, NE China. 3. Our study indicated that the Jehol fossil-bearing formations in South China were deposited at the same time with the Jiufotang Formation. This robust result suggested that the Jehol fossils from Fujian and Zhejiang should be correlated with the last stage of the Jehol migration. We proposed that the widely accepted hypothesis for Jehol radiation and radiation needs to be revised. 4. Two HKU postgraduate student Daran Zheng and Yuling Li participated in this project. They both joined the field work in South China and analysed zircons at the lab. Under my supervision, they are able to interpret paleontological and geochronological data well. Now Daran Zheng is a postdoc researcher at HKU. This project also provided golden opportunities for HKU undergraduate students. I used fossils which collected from South China to teach EASC3417 "Earth Through Time". Students observed and discussed how these fossils formed and preserved.

17308316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17308316.value: We revised and recalculated ages from the classic outcrops in Liaoning, NE Chia. We summarized previous age data for the Yixian Formation and recalibrate previously reported 40Ar/39Ar ages by using new age interpretations for the same standard. We also reported new high-precision ages of 125.8 ± 1.0 Ma and 126.0 ± 0.8 Ma for two basaltic samples from the Lujiatun Unit, a unit of previously uncertain age. The new age data and re-calibrated published data indicate that the Lujiatun Unit was deposited contemporaneously with the Jianshangou Unit. The widely accepted stratigraphic column for the Yixian Formation therefore requires reinterpretation. Our study provided significant clues for reconstructing sedimentary environment for the fossil-rich Yixian deposits and allows to constrain evolutionary rates for early mammals, primitive birds and feathered dinosaurs (Part C-1). During the period of this research, we also discovered abundant invertebrate and plant fossils from the less-studied Jehol outcrops in South China. Well-preserved insects particularly suggested that this region was a paradise for diverse animals during Cretaceous. We noticed that vertebrate fossils have never been found from the Jehol formations in South China. During the middle to late Mesozoic Era, research areas were located near the margin of the Yangtze block, far removed from the classic Jehol localities in NE China. As habitats, basins of South China experienced recurrent acid and intermediate volcanic events. We proposed that environmental barriers may have prevented the spread of Jehol dinosaurs, mammals, and birds to South China. Jehol invertebrates on the other hand are abundant in South China sections, suggesting that putative environmental barriers would not have affected invertebrate expansion. Our age results for the Jehol formations in Fujian and Zhejiang Provinces indicated that these fossil-rich strata are time-equivalent to the second phase fossils from the lower Yixian Formation in the western Liaoning, NE China, and the deposition of these beds is at least 8 Ma older than previously estimated. Results refute the widely accepted hypothesis for the Jehol radiation and migration. Furthermore, our studies on other fossil-rich formations across the South China suggested that the hypotheses for the middle-late Mesozoic biological evolution are more complicated then previously thought (Part C-2).

17308316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17308316.value: Our research refuted several hypotheses related Jurassic and Cretaceous biogeography and evolutionary history. We plan to extend our sampling localities to Central Asia and South Asia. One proposal entitled "High-precision geochronological constraints on the evolution of Cretaceous ecosystems in NW China" has been submitted to GRF/RGC in fall 2020. This new proposal intends to establish a high-precision radiometric age framework for the fossil-bearing units in the northern and southern rims of the Junggar Basin. Resultant chronostratigraphic constraints will enable correlation of these Cretaceous units with other terrestrial successions elsewhere and help advance understanding of reptile evolutionary history in the middle-late Mesozoic. The results will also help test widely accepted evolutionary hypotheses related to Cretaceous key vertebrates.

17308316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17308316.value: The fossils of the Cretaceous Jehol Biota exhibit excellent preservation and extraordinary diversity. Terrestrial fossils, including plants, insects, dinosaurs, birds, mammals and freshwater invertebrates have been found from the classic outcrops in NE China and the newly discovered outcrops in South China. Articulated skeletons, soft tissue, including skin, feathers, and claw sheaths, color patterns, and even stomach contents can be found in Jehol fossil deposits. Due to their exceptional preservation, the Jehol Biota has been referred to as a “Mesozoic Pompeii” . The Jehol Biota provide a critical and detailed snapshot of terrestrial ecosystems during a time frame that has been traditionally constrained and characterized by the Solnhofen Lithographic Limestones and Posidonia Shales from the classic Jurassic sections of Europe. Our paleontological and geochronological investigations on the Jehol Biota have refuted several models for animal migration and biological evolution. This research improved our understanding of the Mesozoic world in general.

17309616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309616.value: Peptide ligation methods, chemoselectively merging two side chain unprotected peptide segments, have been successfully and effectively used to chemically prepare long peptides and proteins over the past two decades. The synthetic proteins can serve as useful tools to discover the biological functions and significance of the naturally occurring proteins. Thus, the development of enabling methods and strategies has attracted a lot of attention in the field of synthetic protein chemistry. We have previously developed a new peptide ligation method, named Ser/Thr ligation. This method involves a chemoselective reaction between a peptide with a C-terminal salicylaldehyde ester and another peptide with an N-terminal Ser or Thr to form an N,O-benzylidene acetal linked product. Subsequent acidolysis releases the resultant N,O-benzylidene acetal moiety to reveal the natural peptidic Xaa-Ser/Thr linkage at the ligation site (Xaa represents any amino acid). Ser/Thr ligation has been successfully used to synthesize peptides, proteins, and cyclic peptides. Among the 20 amino acids, serine and threonine are relatively abundant in naturally occurring proteins; hence, this strategy should find wide potential applications in protein chemical synthesis. Continuing the efforts to further develop and extend the repertoire of Ser/Thr ligation in synthetic protein chemistry, we propose to address several aspects in this project: (1) a new method for the peptide salicylaldehyde ester synthesis, (2) traceless on-resin Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization, (3) homoserine ligation enabling the ligation at an Asp site, and (4) new methods and strategies for successive Ser/Thr ligation and iterative ligation for protein synthesis. The success of this project will facilitate Ser/Thr ligation for wider applications. For instance, the peptide salicylaldehyde ester is a requisite component for Ser/Thr ligation, thus the development of efficient methods for its preparation will be important. On-resin Ser/Thr ligation, which has not been explored, will significantly simplify the process of Ser/Thr ligation. Effective strategies for successive Ser/Thr ligation will allow the assembly of proteins with sizes above 200 amino acids. 多肽連接反應作為實現側鏈非保護片段間的化學選擇性連接的重要方法，在過去的二十年中被成功地應用於長鏈多肽與蛋白質的高效合成。合成所得的蛋白質作為工具分子，在天然蛋白質的生物功能研究中具有重要意義。因此，發展相應的合成方法與策略成為蛋白質合成化學領域的研究重點。本課題組近年來發展了基於絲氨酸/蘇氨酸殘基的新型多肽化學連接反應。該方法通過多肽片段C-末端的水楊醛酯與另一片段N-末端的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸殘基間的化學選擇性縮合反應，生成具有N,O-亞芐基縮醛結構的連接產物，再經酸解反應生成Xaa-Ser/Thr（其中Xaa為任意氨基酸殘基）的天然肽鍵連接。這一基於絲氨酸/蘇氨酸殘基的連接反應已被成功應用於多肽、蛋白質及環肽的合成。由於絲氨酸/蘇氨酸殘基在天然蛋白質中具有較高的豐度，因而該方法在蛋白質化學合成中具有良好的應用前景。 為進一步發展基於絲氨酸/蘇氨酸殘基的多肽化學連接反應並拓展其在蛋白質合成化學中的應用，本課題組計劃在本項目中研究下列問題：（1）開發製備多肽C-末端水楊醛酯的新方法。 （2）通過樹脂上進行的無痕跡絲氨酸/蘇氨酸連接反應合成環肽。 （3）通過高絲氨酸連接反應合成連接位點具有天冬氨酸殘基的多肽。 （4）發展序貫式和迭代式的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸連接反應策略及相關方法，進而用於蛋白質的化學合成。上述研究問題的成功解決，將使絲氨酸/蘇氨酸連接反應的應用得到大幅擴展。具體言之，水楊醛酯作為該連接反應的必要結構基元，發展其有效製備方法至關重要。實現樹脂上的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸連接，將顯著簡化該反應的操作，而相關研究尚待開展。發展序貫式和迭代式的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸連接反應，將使長度多至200個以上殘基的蛋白質的合成成為可能。

17309616.label: Realisation of objectives
17309616.value: Re Objective 1: Develop a new method to prepare peptide salicylaldehyde esters via Boc-SPPS The peptide salicylaldehyde ester is requisite for Ser/Thr ligation; hence, development of efficient methods for its preparation is important if this ligation method is to be widely used. Previously, we developed methods for the synthesis of peptide SAL esters via Fmoc-solid phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) by on-resin phenolysis of the peptide-N-acyl-benzimidazolinone (Nbz) and via Boc-SPPS by on-resin ozonolysis. The on-resin ozonolysis-based Boc-SPPS method is an efficient method for the synthesis of peptide salicylaldehyde esters, but some oxidizable amino acid residues such Trp, Cys and Met are not compatible with this method. Here, we have developed an alternative Boc-SPPS method to synthesize the peptide salicylaldehyde ester, which can tolerate all amino acids, in which the hydrazide immobilised onto the AM resin can react with salicylaldehyde forming a semicarbazone linkage, followed by the Boc-SPPS. Upon the completion of the peptide sequence, a TFA/TMSOTf/pyruvic acid cocktail can be used to remove the side chain protecting group and regenerate the aldehyde group. This method has been successfully used for various peptide salicylaldehyde esters of different length. Re Objective 2: Develop on-resin Ser/Thr ligation and traceless on-resin ligation-mediated peptide cyclization Cyclic peptides have found diverse applications in chemical biology, medicinal chemistry, and drug discovery. The development of effective methods enabling peptide cyclization has drawn a lot of attention. Previously, we have shown that Ser/Thr ligation could be used intramolecularly to facilitate peptide cyclization, and its effectiveness has been demonstrated by us and others in the synthesis of many natural cyclic peptides of various sizes (4-9) and a 31-membered cyclic peptide antibiotic, daptomycin. To further improve the strategy by minimizing the laborious chromatographic purification of the peptide SAL ester prior to cyclization, we have successfully developed a method of on-resin Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization. Salicylaldehyde was first linked to the resin through the substituted phenyl ring. The aldehyde functionality was protected by hydrazide. Upon completion of the peptide via Boc-SPPS, acidolysis in presence of pyruvic acid was used to remove all side chain-protecting groups and restore the aldehyde group, which was still be attached to the resin. Under the on-resin cyclization condition, the hydrolyzed product, if any, was easily removed by filtration, with only the desired cyclic peptide, N,O-benzylidene acetal product, remaining on the resin. Subsequently, the N,O-benzylidene acetal was removed by acidolysis to generate the desired cyclic peptide, which was in the filtrate solution while the salicylaldehyde remained on the resin. This method provides an easy approach to rapidly synthesize cyclic peptides. Re Objective 3: Develop a method to improve Ser/Thr ligation using a solubilizing salicylaldehyde ester One of the practical hurdles for chemical protein synthesis via chemical ligation is the problem of solubility of the ligating peptide segment. Normally, the ligation will not be smooth for peptide segments with poor solubility; for example, chemical synthesis of membrane proteins is rather challenging. Strategies to overcome this problem include redesigning the ligation site or using a removable solubilizing auxiliary tag (e.g., Arg tag). Here, we have identified that using a peptide SAL ester with a solubilizing tag substituted SAL can serve this purpose, not only by increasing the solubility of the peptide salicylaldehyde ester but also the ligated product. Upon acidolysis, this group could be readily removed. We have successfully applied this method for chemical synthesis of 2B4 protein and FCER1G protein. Re Objective 4: Develop new methods and strategies facilitating successive Ser/Thr ligation and apply this to the synthesis of the contra protein. For N to C Ser/Thr ligation, we will introduce a peptide salicylaldehyde ester (off/on) concept. To enable the C-to-N Ser/Thr ligation, the middle peptide fragment with free N-terminal Ser/Thr and the protected C-terminal salicylaldehyde ester played the central role. After the preceding ligation at the N-terminus, the aldehyde group of the peptide SAL ester should be regenerated under the mild conditions to facilitate the next ligation. To achieve this goal, after extensive investigation, we found that the semicarbazone was a good surrogate of the aldehyde group for the peptide SAL ester protection. The peptide SAL ester protected as semicarbazone (switch-off) could survive the TFA-mediated global deprotection of peptides and keep inert under the STL condition, while the aldehyde could be regenerated (switch-on) by TFA-pyruvic acid cocktail for further ligation. We have applied this strategy in the total synthesis of glycosylated interleukin-25.

17309616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17309616.value: Chemical protein synthesis provides a useful tool to study the biological functions and significance of the naturally occurring proteins and to generate unnatural proteins with new properties. Chemical protein synthesis involves mainly two steps: 1) preparation of short peptide segments by solid phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). SPPS normally works well for the synthesis of peptides with less than 50 amino acids but becomes difficult for longer peptides due to its linear synthesis feature; and 2) chemoselective peptide ligation joining the short peptide segments together to form longer peptides of protein domain-size. The peptide ligation allows for peptide assembly with side chain unprotected peptides specifically at the C-/N- terminus with high chemo-, regio- and stereo- selectivity. Thus, the development of enabling methods and strategies has attracted a lot of attention in the field of synthetic protein chemistry over the past two decades. We have previously developed a new peptide ligation method, named Ser/Thr ligation. This method involves a chemoselective reaction between a peptide with a C-terminal salicylaldehyde ester and another peptide with an N-terminal Ser or Thr to form an N,O-benzylidene acetal linked product. Subsequent acidolysis releases the resultant N,O-benzylidene acetal moiety to reveal the natural peptidic Xaa-Ser/Thr linkage at the ligation site (Xaa represents any amino acid). Ser/Thr ligation has been successfully used to synthesize peptides, proteins, and cyclic peptides. Among the 20 amino acids, serine and threonine are relatively abundant in naturally occurring proteins; hence, this strategy should find wide potential applications in protein chemical synthesis. To further develop and extend the repertoire of Ser/Thr ligation in synthetic protein chemistry, we have successfully addressed several aspects in this project: (1) a new method for the peptide salicylaldehyde ester synthesis, (2) traceless on-resin Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization, (3) a new method to improve Ser/Thr ligation using a solubilizing salicylaldehyde ester and (4) new methods and strategies for successive Ser/Thr ligation and iterative ligation for protein synthesis. The findings from this project will facilitate and promote Ser/Thr ligation for wider applications for chemical protein synthesis.

17309616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17309616.value: The successful completion of this project has generated findings for further developments in two areas. Firstly, the traceless on-resin ligation-mediated peptide cyclization method potentially provides a platform to generate cyclic peptide library for biological screening. Cyclic peptides represent a class of modalities for disrupting protein-protein interactions. We will next apply this new methodology to prepare a library of cyclic peptides to screen for XIAP or PD-1 binders as potential inhibitors. Secondly, to demonstrate the effectiveness of our newly developed methods and strategies, such as Boc-SPPS chemistry to prepare peptide salicylaldehyde esters, Ser/Thr with solubilizing tags and successive Ser/Thr ligation, we have synthesized several proteins with post-translational modifications, including phosphorylated HMGA1a protein, acetylated histone protein and phosphorylated 2B4 protein. With these proteins in hand, we will continue to study their functions correlating to the posttranslational modification structure using chemical biology approach.

17309616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17309616.value: Proteins as the key building block for life, which previously can only be obtained from living systems, can be chemically synthesized by chemists in the chemical laboratory now. Chemical protein synthesis can be used to generate not only proteins which are otherwise difficult to obtain by biological approaches, but also “unnatural” proteins with new biological functions and properties. Contemporary chemical protein synthesis relies on effective chemical ligation method to hook up short peptide fragments into long peptide and proteins. In this regard, we have developed the original Serine/Threonine ligation method. In this project, we have successfully developed new methods and strategies to further expand the repertoire of Serine/Threonine ligation in synthetic protein chemistry. We expect that these findings will promote this ligation for wider applications to produce proteins for biological studies and biomedical research.

17310916.value: 星系中心區的活躍過程

17310916.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17310916.value: Prof Dogiel , V.A. Prof Zou, Yuan-Chuan

17310916.label: Project Objectives
17310916.value: Studying different processes inside and outside the galactic centers, which include tidal disruption, jets formation and their dissipation in the nearby medium by heating of the interstellar plasma, propagation of shocks produced by the tidal disruption in the exponential atmosphere of galactic halos, parameters of shock acceleration in the halo or acceleration by MHD turbulence excited behind the shocks, processes of emission by the accelerated particles in shocks etc. One important emission region is the Fermi Bubbles. Studying other active processes in central regions of galaxies, which include the long term X-ray emission processes of Swift J1644 +57, origin of large positron annihilation rate in the Galactic center, origin of X-ray emission lines, origin of sub-relativistic cosmic rays etc. All these phenomena may provide important clues for understanding what have been happened in the past in our Galactic center.

17310916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310916.value: It is generally believed that supermassive black holes existed at the center of almost all galaxies. Hence central regions of galaxies are one of the most interesting targets for observations and theoretical investigations. In particular at the center of our own galaxy, Milky Way, a supermassive black hole with ~4 x10^6 solar masses has been identified by measuring trajectories of stars in the Galactic central region. It is expected that processes of energy release in different forms, which cannot be observed in other parts of galaxies, can occur there. It is not surprising, therefore, that the galactic centers are the main object of observations by almost all space missions and ground-based telescopes, and extensive exposure time is planned just for measurements of emission from there. The distance to our Galactic black hole is estimated to be 8.4 kpc, which is much closer than to any other center of galaxy. This circumstance makes investigations of our Galactic center very attractive. Space missions in the X-ray and gamma-ray ranges like INTEGRAL, Suzaku, XMM-Newton, Chandra, NuSTAR, Fermi etc. and ground-based radio and VHE gamma-ray telescopes have provided very important information about activities and processes around the central supermassive black hole. These observations showed that although at present the central black hole is not active, the central region is a harbor of enigmatic events of huge energy release in different ranges of emission which include huge positron annihilation rate ~10^43 s-1 ; dense molecular clouds in the Galactic central region emit hard X-ray continuum and 6.4 keV iron line radiation; possible dark matter annihilation signals; unknown processes of TeV emission regions (dark accelerators); Fermi Large Area Telescope (Fermi LAT) gamma-ray telescopes discovering a mysterious, diffuse gamma-ray emission in the range 1–100 GeV from the central portion of the Milky Way, which is seen as a giant feature (Fermi Bubbles) elongated over 50 deg (∼10 kpc) perpendicular to the Galactic plane etc. In this project we aim to study the active processes resulting in these phenomena and possible origins of the high energy activities in the central regions of galaxies. 普遍認為黑洞幾乎在所有星系的中心存在。因此， 星系的中部地區是最有趣的目標之一。 觀測和理論研究證明在我們銀河系的中心存在 一個超大質量黑洞〜4百萬個太陽質量。 在銀河系中心區域測量了不同形式的能量釋放， 這是不能在銀河其他部分可以觀察到的。 因此，星系中心幾乎是所有的太空衛星任務的主要觀察對象。 我們的銀河黑洞的距離估計為8.4kpc，這比其他銀河系的中心 更近地球。這種情況使得調查我們的銀河系中心非常有吸引力。 X射線和伽瑪射線衛星，例如朱雀，XMM-牛頓，錢德拉， NuSTAR，費米等，並和地面的無線電，光學望遠鏡和 VHE伽瑪射線望遠鏡提供了非常重要的關於圍繞中心 超大質量黑洞的活動和進程的信息。這些觀察表明， 雖然目前中心黑洞不活躍，過去中部地區是巨大能量釋放的 神秘事件的港灣。其中包括巨大的正電子湮沒率〜10-43 /s ; 分子雲團發射連續的硬X射線和6.4千電子伏鐵輻射線; 可能的暗物質湮滅信號;未知起源的TeV的發射區域 （暗加速器）; 和費米大視場望遠鏡（LAT費米）伽瑪射線 望遠鏡發現的一個神秘的，瀰漫的伽瑪射線發射區域 （費米氣泡）。這些高能量現象的活動可能起源於中部地區。

17310916.label: Realisation of objectives
17310916.value: (1)We first study a possible connection between different non-thermal emissions from the inner few parsecs of the Galaxy. We analyze the origin of the gamma-ray source 2FGL J1745.6−2858 (or 3FGL J1745.6−2859c) in the Galactic Center (GC) and the diffuse hard X-ray component recently found by the Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array, as well as the radio emission and processes of hydrogen ionization from this area. Our goal is to examine whether the hard X-ray and gamma-ray emissions have a common origin. We have tested different models and comment on their possibilities. We then study the time variability of the 6.4 KeV line in the GC and check if this can give some hints of their X-ray origins and possible connection between X-rays and gamma-rays. The properties of the cloud also play essential role. We also the study the connection of cosmic ray penetration into molecular cloud and the gamma-ray emission in the Galactic Center region as the probe for studying the properties of cosmic rays in the central region of the galaxy. (2)In studying other active processes in the central region of galaxies, we focus two important astrophysical phenomena, i.e. formation of double massive black hole binaries in the center of active galactic nuclei and the possible origin of fast radio bursts resulting from the transient accretion processes in the GC.

17310916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17310916.value: In pub. 1-4 we study the X-rays and gamma-ray emission from the active region of galactic center. We try to test different theoretical emission mechanisms and to compare that with the observed data. We find that these multi-wavelength data can provide useful information for us to probe the molecular cloud properties as well as the cosmic ray properties in the center of Milky Way. In pub. 5 we propose a new formation scenario for the double massive black binaries, which are the sources of gravitational wave detected by LIGO and other gravitational detectors. We argue that a low mass double black hole can be formed in vicinity of supermassive black hole in a conventional way. Then the low mass double black hole binary can be trapped in the accretion disk of supermassive black hole. Due to accretion the low mass double black hole binary can grow to massive double black hole and accelerate the shrinkage process and eventually merge to emit intense gravitational wave. In Pub. 6 we propose that the fast radio bursts, which is intense radio emitted from sources located in cosmological distances, can be associated with active galactic nuclei. Every time when the neutron star passing through the accretion disk of the active galactic nuclei an intense radio burst can be emitted. Consequently this model predicts that fast radio burst sources resulting from such mechanism are repeatable and associate with the active galactic nuclei. This predication can be tested in near future when more fast radio bursts are detected.

17310916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17310916.value: The most interesting discovery we have in this project probably is to propose a new formation scenario of double massive black hole binaries forming in the accretion disk of supermassive black hole in the active galactic nuclei. In our scenario, the double massive black hole is formed and merged in the center of the active galactic nuclei, which can radiate intense gravitational wave hence some the gravitational sources detected by the gravitation wave experiments, e.g. LIGO, should associate with the active galactic nuclei. In particular this formation process implies the double black holes should be Kerr black hole because of accretion. This can confirmed when such events are found.

17310916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17310916.value: We have studied some possible models for X-rays and gamma-rays emitted from the galactic center and conclude that these multi-wavelengths can provide some probe for the molecular cloud and cosmic ray properties in the galactic center. The most interesting discoveries proposed in this project are the origin of fast radio bursts, which are intense radio pulsation with sources located in the cosmological distances, as well as a new formation process for double massive black hole binaries. If these proposals are correct then at least some fast radio bursts as well as gravitational source emitted by the merger of double massive black holes are associated with the active galactic nuclei.

17311116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17311116.value: 单层二硫化钼的自旋与谷输运

17311116.label: Project Objectives
17311116.value: In this project we will study parametric pumping of valley current in both adiabatic and non-adiabatic regimes. In the presence of disorder, we will investigate valley Hall effect and spin Hall effect and distributions of their conductance in monolayer MoS2 nanoribbons and try to identify new universality class. We will investigate transient current of monolayer MoS2 nano-devices from first principles calculation. Finally we propose to use rotating magnetic field as well as parametric pumping to generate spin/valley Leviton in MoS2. We will study transport properties of Levitons including spin and valley Levitons in MoS2.

17311116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311116.value: 石墨烯自从被发现以来，由于其表现出的半整数量子霍尔效应、 高电子迁移率等丰富的下一代纳米电子学必不可少的物理性质， 吸引了人们的广泛关注。然而，纯石墨烯并不具有本征带隙， 这极大限制了它在纳米电子学上的应用。以层状的过渡金属硫 化物如二硫化钼(MoS2)为代表的另一类材料则带来了新的物理 现象。二硫化钼晶体是一种间接带隙半导体，而单层的二硫化 钼是一种直接带隙半导体。近来的实验表明，单层二硫化钼表 现出了比晶体材料高106倍的发光量子效率。由于单层二硫化钼 具有直接带隙，它可以被广泛应用于发光二极管、光检测器、 太阳能电池以及用来构造光场效应晶体管。最近，实验制备的 单层MoS2晶体管，在室温下表现出最高的导通电流和与石墨烯 纳米条带相媲美的高电子迁移率。同时，它还保持了高达108的 室温电流开关比以及超低的待机功耗。与石墨烯相类似的，二 硫化钼价带和导带的带边都位于六角布里渊区的两个不等价高 对称点K和-K处。这提供了一个与自旋自由度相类似的可被用 来携带信息的谷自由度。另外，由于强烈的自旋轨道耦合和破 缺的反演对称性，单层MoS2自旋简并的价带会发生150 meV的 劈裂，从而表现出谷霍尔效应与自旋霍尔效应的相互作用。这 种强烈的谷-自旋耦合使得谷电子学和自旋电子学可以在单层 MoS2上结合起来。最近的实验数据还证实了单层MoS2在高对 称K点处带间跃迁的光学选择定则。由于单层二硫化钼在科学 和应用上的重要性，我们将及时研究它的各种谷/自旋量子输运 性质。同时，我们也将会研究单层MoS2的暂态输运性质。

17311116.label: Realisation of objectives
17311116.value: The control and generation of spin-polarized current (SPC) without magnetic materials and an external magnetic field is a big challenge in spintronics and normally requires a spin-flip mechanism. In this Rapid Communication, we show the theoretical discovery of all-electrical generation of SPC without relying on spin-flip spin-orbit coupling (SOC).We find that the SPC can be produced as long as an energy-dependent phase difference between the spin up and down electrons can be established. We verify this through quantum transport calculations on a gated stanene zigzag nanoribbon, which is a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator. Our calculations indicate that the transient current as well as ac conductance are significantly spin polarized, which results from the genetic phase difference between spin up and down electrons after traversing the system. Our results are robust against edge imperfections and generally valid for other QSH insulators, such as silicene and germanene, etc. These findings establish a different route for generating SPCs by purely electrical means and open the door for interesting applications of semiconductor spintronics. The entanglement entropy generated by quantum transport, similar to any physical observable quantity, is a stochastic variable that has its distribution and can fluctuate. The fundamental question is how to define the entanglement entropy operator which allows one to discuss entanglement entropy fluctuation. By introducing the entanglement entropy operator, we develop a theoretical framework to calculate the entanglement entropy fluctuation as well as its higher order cumulants generated by electronic transport in open systems. The distribution of entanglement entropy generated by opening or closing a quantum point contact (QPC) is solved exactly. When the transmission coefficient of QPC is one-half, the entanglement entropy is maximized and fluctuationless. We also establish a general relation between the generated entanglement entropy fluctuation and charge fluctuation. We apply our theory to electronic transport through a quantum dot and study the generated entanglement entropy in the transient regime. Universal behavior is found for the cumulants of entanglement entropy at short times. We investigate the full-counting statistics (FCS) of energy transport carried by electrons in molecular junctions for the Anderson–Holstein model in the polaronic regime. Using the two-time quantum measurement scheme, the generating function (GF) for the energy transport is derived and expressed as a Fredholm determinant in terms of Keldysh nonequilibrium Green’s function in the time domain. Dressed tunneling approximation is used in decoupling the phonon cloud operator in the polaronic regime. This formalism enables us to analyze the time evolution of energy transport dynamics after a sudden switch-on of the coupling between the dot and the leads towards the stationary state. The steady state energy current cumulant GF in the long time limit is obtained in the energy domain as well. Universal relations for steady state energy current FCS are derived under a finite temperature gradient with zero bias and this enabled us to express the equilibrium energy current cumulant by a linear combination of lower order cumulants. The behaviors of energy current cumulants in steady state under temperature gradient and external bias are numerically studied and explained. The transient dynamics of energy current cumulants is numerically calculated and analyzed. Universal scaling of normalized transient energy cumulants is found under both temperature gradient and external bias. By employing the nonequilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) method, the transient current and the transient behavior of the spin transfer torque (STT) of the magnetic layered system are investigated within the framework of density functional theory (DFT). To reduce the huge computational cost of the transient calculation, especially when the dense mesh of k sampling is present for layered systems, the complex absorbing potential (CAP) and the Padé spectrum decomposition are used so that the energy integrals in calculating transient current and STT can be performed analytically using residue theorem, which dramatically reduces the computational complexity of the first-principles calculation of transient behavior. As an application of the NEGF-DFT-CAP formalism, the transient current and current-induced STT of the Co/Cu/Co trilayer system are studied under an upward bias pulse for different angles of magnetization direction between two leads. The transient current shows a damped oscillatory behavior with the oscillation frequency proportional to the applied bias, leading to a relaxation time of hundreds of femtoseconds. The time-dependent STTs show roughly the same profile for systems with different rotating angles. The oscillation behavior is also observed as the transient STT approaches the steady state value. Such oscillations can be attributed to the interface resonant states. We study the short-time dynamics of a molecular junction described by Anderson-Holstein model using full-counting statistics after projective measurement. The coupling between the central quantum dot (QD) and two leads was turned on at remote past and the system is evolved to steady state at time t = 0, when we perform the projective measurement in one of the lead. Generating function for the charge transfer is expressed as a Fredholm determinant in terms of Keldysh nonequilibrium Green’s function in the time domain. It is found that the current is not constant at short times indicating that the measurement does perturb the system.We numerically compare the current behaviors after the projective measurement with those in the transient regime where the subsystems are connected at t = 0. The universal scaling for high-order cumulants is observed for the case with zero QD occupation due to the unidirectional transport at short times. The influences of electron-phonon interaction on short-time dynamics of electric current, shot noise, and differential conductance are analyzed.

17311116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17311116.value: The spin-filter transport and magnetoresistance effects are of particular interest in the field of molecular spintronics. In this work, based on first-principles quantum transport calculations, we report on the spindependent transport properties of a molecular junction made of two manganese phthalocyanine (MnPc) molecules linked by single-walled carbon nanotubes. Owing to the half-metallicity of MnPc around the Fermi energy, a perfect spin-filter effect and a giant magnetoresistance effect are observed in the molecular junction. The current–voltage characteristics show nearly ohmic behavior for the junction in an anti-parallel magnetic configuration, while a very low-bias negative differential resistance effect is observed for the junction in a parallel magnetic configuration. The results are well understood from the analysis of molecular frontier orbitals, scattering states and transmission spectra. Our results provide some fundamental understanding of spin-dependent transport in molecular junctions that are useful for the design of future spintronic devices. Quantum transport is a stochastic process in nature. As a result, the conductance is fully characterized by its average value and fluctuations, i.e., characterized by full counting statistics (FCS). Since disorders are inevitable in nanoelectronic devices, it is important to understand how FCS behaves in disordered systems. The traditional approach dealing with fluctuations or cumulants of conductance uses diagrammatic perturbation expansion of the Green’s function within coherent potential approximation (CPA), which is extremely complicated especially for high order cumulants. In this paper, we develop a theoretical formalism based on nonequilibrium Green’s function by directly taking the disorder average on the generating function of FCS of conductance within CPA. This is done by mapping the problem into higher dimensions so that the functional dependence of generating a function on the Green’s function becomes linear and the diagrammatic perturbation expansion is not needed anymore. In terms of the nonequilibrium Green’s function framework, we formulate the full-counting statistics of conjugate thermal spin transport in a spin Seebeck engine, which is made by a metal-ferromagnet insulator interface driven by a temperature bias.We obtain general expressions of scaled cumulant generating functions of both heat and spin currents that hold special fluctuation symmetry relations, and demonstrate intriguing properties, such as rectification and negative differential effects of high-order fluctuations of thermal excited spin current, maximum output spin power, and efficiency. The transport and noise depend on the strongly fluctuating electron density of states at the interface.

17311116.value: Since the discovery of graphene, it has attracted a lot of attention because it exhibits rich physics such as half-integer quantum Hall effect and high mobility that is an essential requirement for the next generation of nano-electronics. However, graphene does not have an intrinsic band gap which limits its applications in nano-electronics. Layered transition metal dichalcogenides such as MoS2 represent another class of materials which give rise to new physical phenomena. The bulk MoS2 crystal is an indirect band gap semiconductor and becomes a direct band gap semiconductor for monolayer structure. Because monolayer MoS2 has a direct band gap, it can be used in light-emitting diodes, photodetectors or solar cells and to construct interband field effect transistors. Very recently, single layer MoS2 transistors was produced experimentally at room temperature showing the highest on-current. Similar to graphene, both of the conduction and valence band edges are located at two inequivalent corners K and -K of the hexagonal Brillouin zone which offers valley degree of freedom that can be used to carry information. Due to the importance of monolayer MoS2 from both scientific and application point of view, it is timely to exploit various quantum transport properties through monolayer MoS2.

17311316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311316.value: Polar regions are well known as climatically sensitive. Especially, polar North Atlantic-Arctic oceans are important to understand global climatic system, because of various factors including deep- and intermediate-water formation, sea-ice coverage, methane seepage, and brine formation. Reconstructing brine formation and methane seepage is relatively new effort and standard paleoceanographic proxies do not work well to detect these activities. Thus, development of new proxies is needed. Here we try to develop new faunal proxy for brine formation and methane seepage using microfossil ostracodes in surface sediment and Holocene sediment core samples around Svalbard. The preliminary results suggest that ostracodes can be promising proxy to detect brine formation and methane seepage in the geological past. The results will significantly contribute to our better understanding of paleoclimatic and paleoceanographic changes in this climatically sensitive region. 南北極地帶一向是容易受氣候轉變影響的地方。要理解全球氣候系統，彙集多項控制氣候的因素(如深層水區與中層水區的形成、海水的構成及其與冰的覆蓋比例和甲烷渗漏)的大西洋至北極海洋尤其重要。 重建以往海水形成和甲烷渗漏的境況是比較新穎的研究方向。鑑於典型古海洋學指標工具不能精確地反映這兩項活動的變化，發展新的指標方法是必需的。 我們嘗試在挪威的斯瓦巴群島附近採集表層沉積物樣本及鑽取屬全新世年代(從11700年前至今)的沉積物岩芯，並運用處於樣本中的介形蟲(一種微型化石)作為新式動物群指標去測量海水形成和甲烷渗漏的改變。初步結果顯示利用介形蟲來探測以上兩項環境活動的遠古狀況是成效可期的。這項研究將有效地令我們更深入了解古氣候及古海洋如何在這個對氣候變化敏感的區域中轉變。

17311316.label: Realisation of objectives
17311316.value: 1. To reconstruct regional deglacial-Holocene paleoceanographic and paleoecological changes around Svalbard. We successfully reconstructed the deglacial-Holocene paleoceanographic and paleoecological histories around Svalbard, and published relevant papers, including one in a top journal Quaternary Science Review (Tian et al 2020; see Part C). Notably we discovered the robust evidence of an abrupt sea-level change event known as the meltwater pulse 1B, that was formerly elusive. It's the main discovery of Tian et al 2020. Thus, the objective has been achieved well. 2. Develop ostracode faunal proxy for brine formation. As discussed in Tian et al 2020, we successfully used ostracod proxy to reconstruct Svalbard paleoceanographic history in the brine formation region including the salinity and temperature changes. We found different species with different salinity and temperature ranges that are useful for reconstructing past brine formation. Thus, the objective has been achieved well. 3. Develop ostracode faunal proxy for methane seepage. We discovered a distinct ostracod species restricted in the methane seepage area in their distribution (Yasuhara et al., 2018; see Part C). This species can be a good proxy of paleo cold seepage. Thus, the objective has been achieved well. 4. Establish better ostracode-based paleoceanographic reconstruction in the Arctic Ocean. As we published multiple ostracod papers on the Arctic ocean, we successfully showed that ostracod are very useful for Arctic Paleoceanography. Thus, the objective has been achieved well.

17311316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17311316.value: We investigated Arctic paleoecology and paleooceanography successfully. We have found cold-seep endemic ostracod species Rosaliella svalbardensis and described it as a new genus and new species. This species is relatively large and well calcified, and so will be good paleo-indicator of cold seep activities in the Quaternary. We also reconstructed temperature, salinity, and sea-level histories in the Arctic near Svalbard for the deglacoal-Holocene period. Abrupt environmental changes related to the meltwater pulse were clearly recorded in ostracod fossil data. Gradual changes in temperature and salinity during the Holocene are also recorded. We published 13 papers successfully. Several of them are on the top journals and can be 3-4 star papers. One PhD student finished successfully, and another PhD student is doing her research well. PI Yasuhara obtained Biwako Award, an international award for aquatic ecology.

17311316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17311316.value: We are preparing a paper using cold seep proxy ostracod species to reconstruct late Quaternary cold seepage activity in this region. It's based on a Final Year Project (by undergraduate student, Rachel Wai Ching Chu) and we have very good results. We are also interested in distribution of circumstances polar species. Their main distributions are in the Arctic Ocean, but they are also distributed in the high-latitude North Atlantic and North Pacific Oceans, constituting the circumpolar distributions. We plan to reconstruct the southern expansion and northern shrinkage of their distributions in different geological times with colder and warmer climates than the present. Based on this line of research, we will be able to learn about the effect of ongoing anthropogenic warming on the cold water species distributions.

17311316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17311316.value: We studied past climatic and environmental conditions in the Arctic Ocean for the last 13000 years by using a fossil proxy Ostracod (seed shrimp), small crustacean with calcareous shells that are well preserved as fossils. We found environmental changes related to rapid sea-level change, known as meltwater pulse 1B, as well as more gradual temperature and salinity changes in the Holocene of the last 11700 years. We also discovered a new genes and species Rosaliella svalbardensis as a biological indicator of cold (methane) seep activity in the seafloor in the present and geological past of the especially Quaternary (for the last 2.6 million years). Our results substantially improved the ostracode-based paleoceanographic reconstructions in the Arctic Ocean.

17311816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17311816.value: The first major research outcome is the understanding of the relationship between coastal plant communities and tidal levels has been greatly enhanced by the works in Hangzhou Bay (Xiong et al., 2020) and Malaysia (Tam et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2021). In these studies, we established the elevational relationship between micro-fossil pollen and diatom zones and mudflat-saltmarsh and mudflat-mangrove environments. Such relationship can help scientists reconstruct past histories of sea-level and coastal change. The second major outcome is the use of mangrove/saltmarsh sediments as a palaeo-sea-level indicator for reconstruction of the sea-level history of the Common Era for the South China Sea (Tam et al., 2018). It reveals for the first time the sea-level lowstand during the Little Ice Age and the possible amount of post-Little-Ice-Age sea-level rise in the tropical region. The third major outcome is that we reconstructed the Holocene sea-level histories and simulated hydro-isostatic processes for three locations of the western North Pacific coast. Whereas the works in Hangzhou Bay and Malaysia reveal continental-coastal levering effects of the postglacial sea-level rise (Xiong et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2021), the work in Pearl River delta indicates effects of the long-term regional tectonic processes (Xiong et al., 2018).

17311816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17311816.value: Because the research methods were tested in this research, it can be applied to research work to places in other tropical and subtropical regions. This research will be continued in the coasts of Fujian (collaboration with Xiamen University), Guangdong (collaboration with Sun Yatsen University) and the Hainan Island.

17311816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17311816.value: This research tested the methods that are applicable to tropical and subtropical regions for reconstructions of the past sea-level history. Each of the publications from this research project has new findings that have improved our understanding of nature.

17312016.label: Project Objectives
17312016.value: The accurate crystallo-chemistry of magnetite from BIFs of Archean-Palaeoproterozoic eons. The chemical composition will be measured by electron microprobe and the Fe(II)/Fe(III) stoichiometry will be measured by Mössbauer spectrometer at the Department of Earth Sciences. XRD measurements of purified magnetite crystals will be used to calculate their accurate lattice constants. Using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) to measure the heterogenesity of euhedral magnetite crystals of about 30 um in BIFs that have different genetic environments. The result of this objective will be used to explain why Fe-isotopic studies without detailed mineralogical information could only provide ambiguous explanations. Wet-chemical methods in the Geobiology Laboratory to measure Fe(II) and Fe(III) concentrations in various solid and aqueous samples by spectrophotometer. Standard curves of spectrophotometric measurements of solution with a wide range of soluble Fe(II) to Fe(III) ratios will be established. The characterization of ferric oxides produced in the environmental sites of Gallionella sp. and from laboratory culturing of nitrate-reducing coupled Fe(II)-oxidation by high resolution SEM and TEM observations. The same materials will be used for synthesizing GR and magnetite afterwards. Synthesis and characterization of GR synthesized at different temperatures and pH conditions. The kinetic evolution from the fibrous structure to the intermediate GR phases, and the final production of magnetite will be captured by SEM and TEM observations. This study also includes a system with the addition of siliceous acid to trace the formation of Si-containing magnetite by this pathway. The measurement of Fe(II) and Fe(III) species separated from magnetite from various BIFs, wet-chemical synthesis and those from biomass of Gallionella sp. and culture of bacteria with nitrate-reducing coupled Fe(II)-oxidation. Synthesis of silician magnetite via the GR pathway. The determination of the structural stoichiometry of Si on the lattice of magnetite from BIFs and experimental systems. The measurement of Si-isotopes of the aqueous-magnetite in experimental systems and the magnetite-hematite-chert system of BIFs.

17312016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17312016.value: 條帶狀矽鐵建造是地球生物圈的最初20億年歷史中微生物與其地質環境之際相互作用的沈積記錄。雖然其中已經沒有原生礦物，赤鐵礦可能是最初的生物氧化二價鐵產生水合物直接脫水的產物並且其初始礦物學特征可以保存至今；而其中的磁鐵礦則已知有多種成因。磁鐵礦的這種復雜的特征使得難以使用其礦物學特征或鐵同位素特征解釋太古代海水－礦物－微生物之間的相互作用。現在一般認為光合作用的鐵氧化細菌是在太古代到元古代之間產氧光合作用出現之前將海洋中溶解的二價鐵氧化和沈積成三價鐵氧化物的主要原因。然而我們發現矽鐵建造的時代越老，其中所含磁鐵礦越多。比如保存於加拿大和西南格陵蘭島的最古老的矽鐵建造中的鐵氧化物僅有磁鐵礦。我們認為：1.在鐵溶解的還原海水中，初始的三價鐵來源於氧化二價鐵的光合作用，而這種三價鐵是赤鐵礦和磁鐵礦中三價鐵的來源；2. 微生物代謝產生的三價鐵氧化物可以與多期次上湧的來自深海的含二價鐵的高溫流體反應直接生成磁鐵礦；3.因此磁鐵礦中三價鐵來自於微生物的直接氧化而二價鐵直接來源於海水。在嚴格厭氧條件下，用各種二價鐵氧化細菌所產生的鐵氧化物(含微生物有機質)與水溶二價鐵之間的反應模擬這個過程。二價和三價鐵在水溶液和礦物晶格上隨時間的變化將用了推測鐵氧化菌席所含有機質對磁鐵礦結晶的影響。各種磁鐵礦晶格中的二價和三價鐵離子將被分離和分別測量其鐵同位素特征。該結果將用於示蹤赤鐵礦和磁鐵礦中的三價鐵都來自於鐵氧化的光合作用，進而證明地球上最早的矽鐵建造不僅是最早的沈積建造，而且也是鐵氧化光合作用出現的巖石學證據。

17312016.label: Realisation of objectives
17312016.value: Banded iron formation (BIF) is a sedimentary rock that uniquely deposited in the first half of Earth’s history with life. It is characterized by the petrological compositions of alternative bands of iron oxides and silica. The iron oxides are dominantly hematite and magnetite. The geneses of these two iron oxides are still questions of hot debate, especially their applications to contemporary life in the oceans. This study is one of my serial research projects funded by RGC (4 from 2008 to 2016) to explore the co-evolution of the crust, ocean, atmosphere, and life in the early Precambrian eons. In my previous projects, we investigated the crystallography of silica in BIFs with the least post-depositional metamorphism. We find that those silica makes polyhedrons of a few micrometers in microbands, implying the preservation of their pristine structure as chemicals precipitated on the seafloors of the early oceans. We use high-resolution transmission electron microscopy to characterize the mineral hematite in BIFs. We find the well-preservation of its nanoparticles of 4-6 nanometers. This is strong evidence of its mineralization from the dehydration of ferrihydrite, an amorphous oxyhydroxide precipitated from the biological oxidation of water-soluble Fe(II) in the ferruginous ocean by photoferrotroph. One interesting finding is that the interior metamorphic fluid produced from the dehydration of silica facilitated the further coarsening of some hematite crystals to tens nanometers. We have also experimentally tested the hypothesis of the genesis of magnetite by the reduction of ferric oxides to magnetite from ferrihydrite by dissimilarity iron-reducing bacteria. We explained the coarsening of the magnetite crystals from super-paramagnetic particles to micro-scaled magnetite crystals at the early stage of diagenesis. However, it is widely observed that magnetite can make almost pure bands of micron-scale and up to huge ore deposits. It is more so in BIFs with older ages. Those phenomena cannot be explained by biomineralization and diagenetic re-mineralization. So, we raised the hypothesis in this proposal that magnetite could be directly deposited in the early Precambrian oceans that represents the result of the combined biological and chemical process. This is the mission of this study. Here below are reports based on objectives listed in our proposal. There are also approaches that we have made, which were not presented in our published papers, but were gained as knowledge, and made a background for our future studies. In Sun & Li (2017, Precam. Res, 298, 292-305), we addressed many problems raised in the objectives listed in our proposal. We used scanning electron microscopy to reveal the banding structures of magnetite, which is essential for further investigations of the crystallographic features of crystals and the chemical compositions of minerals in and around those bands. We used electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) mapping to show the gradual changes of the structures of magnetite coexisting with hematite, which is the first time that we observed the overgrowth of hematite on magnetite. By using this technology, we also showed the existence of hematite and maghemite within the morphological structure of magnetite. Our further investigation of those EBSD revealed structures by measuring their chemical compositions. Overall, this study addressed questions in Objectives 1, 2, 5, 6, and 7. There are still studies that support that magnetite in BIF was mineralized due to the bacterial reduction of bioavailable ferric iron precipitated to the ocean floor. We, therefore, examined modern hot springs with the detection of Thermoanaerobacter, the dissimilatory iron-reducing bacteria that thrive at temperatures as high as the age of the Neoarchean. We observed and examined the crystallography of various pyrite crystals. The particular crystallographic feature of biogenic minerals has long been investigated if it could be used as a biosignature of planetary materials indicating the existence of (past) life. In our publication on Crystals (Tang & Li, 2020, 10, Article 535), we used geochemical, scanning electron microscopy, and Moessbauer spectroscopy to study the stable environments of pyrite in hot springs. We observed the existence of paramagnetic Fe(II) on the authigenic silicates in the hot springs. We presented the detailed crystallographic features of pyrite with a wide spectrum of size and morphologies and proposed the coexistence of diverse types of crystallographic habits indicates the physiological mediation resulted in a difference of conditions of mineralization and this phenomenon could be considered a mineral biosignature. This concept may have a potential implication for the searching for mineral biosignature on Mars. In this study, we addressed problems in Objectives 1, 4, 6, and 7. BIFs bear information on the interactions between the atmosphere, ocean the contemporary biosphere. In our publication on Frontiers in Earth Sciences (Hao & Li, 2018), we explored the interaction between the early Earth’s crust and atmosphere. With a thick CO2-H2O atmosphere and high temperature, the atmosphere was likely had the properties of a supercritical fluid. We experimentally show that the interaction between this atmosphere and the ultramafic rocks produces massive carbonate that is a way of atmospheric CO2 sequestration and the reaction between Fe(II) on the structure of silicates with CO2 can produce a substantial amount of hydrocarbons. These hydrocarbons can be a potential source for the early biogeochemical cycles, from which the heterotrophic life could be supported. In this study, the wet-chemistry investigation, including the speciation of iron in the aqueous part were systematically approached. However, this part of the results was not good enough for publication. The isotopic, elemental geochemistry and petrological observations show that BIF changes along with the evolution of atmospheric and ocean chemistry. The formation of Earth’s earliest ozone is believed to have happened during the later deposition of BIFs. In the later Archean oceans, oxygenic photosynthesis emerged. This respiration produces free oxygen that eventually oxidized the ferruginous ocean and led to the termination of the deposition of BIF about 1.8 billion years ago. Some of the singular oxygenic cyanobacteria evolved pigments that were used biologically to filter the short-wavelength ultraviolet radiation. We hypothesize that the pigment, as a resistant biogenic molecule, can stay in sedimentary environments for a long geological time. Upon the examination of sedimentary rocks from the early BIF to the very young sedimentary materials, we found the clue is probably in the young sedimentary rocks (Sun et al., GRL, 2019). We eventually focused our study on carbonates from Qaidam Basin, which is a potential rock that can trap such molecules. And we detected the molecule and suggest that the molecule can be preserved in the sedimentary environments for at least 30 kyr. In this part of the study, we addressed the approaches planned in Objectives 1, 2, and 3.

17312016.value: 1. Magnetite crystals have fine structures, varied crystallography, and chemical compositions. 2. Pyrites crystallized with the mediation of microorganisms may have a wide range of crystal habits that is a potential mineral biosignature. 3. The interaction between the early atmosphere and crust was a rapid way to fix the atmospheric carbon dioxide and cool the Earth's climatic temperature. 4. Scytonemin as the biosignature of oxygenic cyanobacteria cannot be preserved for a long geological time. It can only be detected in recent sedimentary rocks.

17312016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17312016.value: Magnetite is a simple but magical mineral that makes a major mineral composition of banded iron formation, a historical archive of Earth only in its early history. We studied this mineral, the other minerals precipitated in similar environments, the atmosphere-rock interactions at the time when it was mineralized, and the possibility of whether it can hold organic biosignatures.
