17312916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17312916.value: Exciton-polaritons are half-light, half-matter quantum particles in hybrid structures of semiconductors embedded in optical microcavities. They are of key interest for the exploration of many-body phenomena of fundamental interests such as Bose-Einstein condensation and optoelectronic application such as polariton lasing. Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have recently emerged as a new class of 2D semiconductors, with appealing properties including the strong exciton-light coupling, and the exotic physics associated with the valley pseudospin of carriers and excitons. With the demonstrated feasibility of embedment into optical microcavities, TMDs monolayers and their vertically stacked van der Waals heterostructures offer a new platform to explore exciton-polaritons, favored by the strong exciton-photon coupling observed in TMDs. Our earlier works have discovered exotic physics related to the valley pseudospin of two types of optically active excitons in TMDs van der Waals layered structures: intralayer excitons have circularly polarized valley selection rule in their coupling with photon, and strain tunable strong valley-orbit coupling in their dispersions; while interlayer excitons in twisted TMDs heterobilayers have six-fold light cones anomalously located at finite velocities, with elliptically polarized valley optical selection rules. In this theoretical project, we will study fine-structures of polaritons formed from the hybridization of these two types of excitons with quasi-2D cavity photons, focusing on the novel dispersion relations, pseudospin-orbit splitting and pseudospin textures, and Berry phase effects of the exciton-plaritons, and the resultant new transport and light emission properties. In particular, we will examine how novel properties of the exciton-polaritons can be introduced by several unique features in TMDs layered structures including: the excitonic fine structures and light-coupling properties associated with its valley pseudospin; the controllable twist angle between the constituent layers that can engineer the optoelectronic response in the heterostructures. With the rapidly growing interest on TMDs van der Waals layered structures for the exploration of semiconductor optics and optoelectronics, it can be anticipated that the exciton-polaritons studied in this project will soon become an active topic of research of both scientific and technological interest. The research proposed here would be a timely study on the intriguing properties of these quantum quasiparticles, forming the basis for the exploitation of them in search of new many-body physics and technological applications. 激子極化激發是壹類在半導體－光學微腔雜化結構中的半光－半物質的量子激發，對於研究玻色愛因斯坦凝聚等量子多體現象和極化激發激光等光電應用具有重大意義。僅有原子尺寸厚度的二維過渡金屬二硫化物是新近出現的壹類二維半導體，具有壹系列的有趣屬性，包括激子和光的強藕合，以及跟載流子和激子的能谷自由度相關的奇特物理現象。把過渡金屬二硫化物的單層和堆疊的範德瓦爾斯異質結放入光學微腔形成雜化結構已經在技術上被證明可行。這樣的雜化結構提供了壹個研究激子極化激發的全新的平臺，特別是由於過渡金屬二硫化物中的激子和光的強藕合。我們早期的工作在兩種可與光場藕合的激子系統中發現了和能谷贗自旋相關的壹些奇特物理現象： 單層內的激子具有圓偏振的能谷光學選擇定則，以及可由受力形變調控的能谷－軌道的等效藕合；過渡金屬二硫化物的異質雙層中的層間激子具有六重簡並的光錐，光錐內的激子具有有限速度和橢圓偏振的能谷光學選擇定則。在這個理論研究項目中，我們將會對這些激子跟二維光學微腔中的光子藕合形成的極化激發的精細結構進行研究，側重於探索新穎的色散關系，內部量子自由度（贗自旋）和質心自由度的藕合帶來的能量劈裂和贗自旋結構，以及激子極化激發的貝裏相效應和隨之而來的新的輸運性質和發光屬性。我們會著重研究激子極化激發的屬性會怎樣被過渡金屬二硫化物層狀結構的壹些特有性質影響，包括其中由能谷贗自旋導致的激子精細結構和光藕合；以及在異質結中可由層間轉角調控的光電響應。隨著對過渡金屬二硫化物範德瓦爾斯層狀結構在半導體光學和光電應用領域日益增長的廣泛興趣，可以預期這個項目所研究的激子極化激發將會成為壹個熱門的研究課題，具有基礎研究和應用方面的重大意義。這個項目將對把這類量子激發用於探索新的多體量子現象和新的應用構成基礎。

17312916.label: Realisation of objectives
17312916.value: Objective 1 This objective has been achieved. We have systematically explored the exciton-polariton formed with interlayer excitons (IX) in van der Waals layered structures of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) embedded in planar microcavities. IX in TMDs heterobilayers features a permanent electric dipole that enables the desired electrostatic control to direct its flow, as well as the gate tunability of IX resonance. And the formation of moiré pattern due to the lattice mismatch and twisting of the heterobilayers leads to a superlattice landscape that endows IX an extra pseudospin, characterizing its trapping at different locales with distinct optical dipoles in a moiré supercell. We found that these have led to exciting possibilities for engineering of polariton dispersion, pseudospin textures (and Berry curvatures) by the tunable exciton-photon detuning through interlayer bias control of IX resonance, and by the spatial location (in the out-of-plane direction) of the TMDs inside the cavity. We revealed the exciting possibility to engineer two types of moiré exciton-polaritons that inherit gauge structures in different ways from the photon constituents. These two types exciton-polaritons exhibit distinct forms of topological transport phenomena including the spin/valley Hall and polarization Hall effects, which feature remarkable electrical tunability through the interlayer bias. These discoveries point to unprecedented opportunities to explore the physics and optoelectronic application in a new polariton system, such as the polariton circuits with spin/valley functionalities. Objective 2 This objective has been achieved. We have investigated the optical properties of both spin-singlet and spin-triplet neutral interlayer excitons (IX) in MoX2/WX2 heterobilayers. Surprisingly, the optical transition dipole of the spin-triplet exciton is found to be in the same order of magnitude to that of the spin-singlet exciton, in sharp contrast to the monolayer excitons where the spin-triplet species is considered as dark compared to the singlet. Unlike the monolayer excitons whose spin-conserved (spin-flip) transition dipole can only couple to light of in-plane (out-of-plane) polarisation, such restriction is removed for the interlayer excitons due to the breaking of the out-of-plane mirror symmetry. We find that as the interlayer atomic registry changes, the optical transition dipole of interlayer exciton crosses between in-plane ones of opposite circular polarizations and the out- of-plane one for both the spin-triplet and spin-singlet species. As a result, excitons of both species have non-negligible coupling to photon modes of both in-plane and out-of-plane propagations, another sharp difference from the monolayers where the exciton couples predominantly into the out-of-plane propagation channel. At given atomic registry, the spin-triplet and spin-singlet excitons have distinct valley polarisation selection rules in coupling with cavity photon. The formation of a moiré pattern due to the lattice mismatch and twisting between the two TMDs layers further results in a superlattice potential. We found that in such moiré superlattice potential, the neutral IX dispersion splits into mini-bands with energy spacing controlled by the moiré periodicity can be tuned by the twisting angle. The lowest three IX mini-bands have the largest optical dipoles for coupling to cavity, and remarkably, these three split IX mini-bands feature optical dipoles with distinct valley polarization selection rules, allowing them to be selectively coupled to cavity TE and TM modes to form moiré exciton-polaritons. Twisting angle that determines the mini-bands splitting, and interlayer bias that tune the overall IX-cavity detuning, and the singlet-triplet splitting determined by the SOC of the Bloch bands, provide rich possibilities to engineer polariton pseudospin textures and Berry curvatures, underlying the aforementioned electrically tunable topological transport properties. Objective 3 This objective has been achieved. We have investigated charged interlayer excitons (IX) in the MX2/M'X'2/MX2 heterotrilayers with the staggered band alignment, where the two electrons (holes) energetically favour the top and bottom MX2 layer, and the single hole (electron) favours the middle M'X'2 layer. Such heterotrilayers have two independently configurable interfaces, controlled by the twisting angle theta_t between top-middle layers, and theta_b between middle-bottom layers respectively. These lead to two pair-wise long-wavelength moiré patterns at small angles: moiré-t between top and middle layers, and moiré-b between middle and bottom layers. The trilayer atomic texture at given location is then described by two pair-wise local stacking registries as functions of lateral position R: r_t (R) accounting for the moiré-t, and r_b (R) accounting for the moiré-b, which uniquely specify how the three layers are vertically stacked at any given R. For a charged IX wavepacket at R, its light coupling properties are characterized by r_t (R) and r_b (R), for the two channels where the middle M'X'2 layer hole (electron) recombines with top and bottom MX2 layer electron (hole) respectively, with optical dipoles having the same dependence on the stacking registries as the neutral IX in MX2/M'X'2 heterobilayer. Our first principle calculations further reveal that moiré superlattice potentials for IX in such TMDs heterotrilayers have an electrostatic origin from the spontaneous charge transfer across the heterointerfaces dependent on the atomic registries r_t (R) and r_b (R). This allows engineering tunable bi-chromatic superlattice potential through the interference of moiré potentials from the two independently configurable heterointerfaces in trilayers, which can be strain switched from multi-orbital periodic superlattices, to quasi-periodic disordered landscapes. The trilayer moiré also hosts two independently configurable triangular superlattices of interacting neutral IX with opposite electric dipoles.

17312916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17312916.value: (1) We investigated optical properties of neutral interlayer excitons (IX) in heterobilayer TMDs, where spin-singlet and spin-triplet configurations are shown to have comparable optical dipole strength. We find that as the interlayer atomic registry changes, the optical transition dipole of IX crosses between in-plane ones of opposite circular polarizations and out-of-plane one. As a result, spin-singlet and triplet excitons have non-negligible coupling to photon modes of both in-plane and out-of-plane propagations. At given atomic registry, the spin-triplet and spin-singlet excitons have distinct valley polarisation selection rules for coupling to photon. See publication 2. (2) We discovered fine structures of polaritons formed by hybridization of interlayer exciton (IX) in TMD heterobilayer with photons in planar 2D cavity. We show that in moiré superlattice potential there are three split IX eigenmodes that feature opposite circular, and out-of-plane polarized optical dipoles respectively, which can be selectively coupled to cavity TE and TM modes with distinct mode profiles and polarizations. These lead to two types of moiré exciton-polaritons that inherit gauge structures in different ways from the photon constituents. These polaritons exhibit distinct forms of topological transport phenomena including spin/valley Hall and polarization Hall effects, which feature remarkable electrical tunability through the control of IX-cavity detuning by inter-layer bias. See publication 5. (3) We reveal that moiré superlattice potential in TMDs heterostructures have an electrostatic origin from spontaneous charge transfer across the heterointerfaces dependent on the atomic registry. This allows engineering tunable bi-chromatic superlattices for charged interlayer excitons through interference of moiré potentials from independently configurable heterointerfaces in MX2/M’X’2/MX2 trilayers, which can be strain switched from multi-orbital periodic superlattices to quasi-periodic disordered landscape. The trilayer moiré also hosts two independently configurable triangular superlattices of neutral interlayer exciton with opposite electric dipoles. See research output 9. (4) We have systematically studied the stacking-registry-dependence of interlayer coupling and electronic structures in TMDs bilayers with moiré superlattices (publication 1, 3), which form the basis of our understanding of interlayer exciton and their light coupling properties. Besides, in presence of twin-domain-boundaries in one TMDs layer which leads to line defects in moiré superlattices controlled by interlayer translation and twisting angle, we discovered defect-confined 1D interlayer exciton modes of topological origin (research output 7). (5) Our collaboration with experimental groups reported the observations of layer-hybridized excitons in commensurate TMDs heterobilayers featuring both large optical and electric dipoles (publication 4), and remarkably rich exciton complexes in ultraclean monolayer TMDs (publication 8).

17312916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17312916.value: Findings of this project have pointed to interesting directions for further development of the research. We plan to explore exciton-polariton formed with the layer-hybridised valley excitons in TMDs heterobilayer (c.f. publication 4), which feature both large optical dipole from its intralayer component, and large electrical dipole from its interlayer component. This shall lead to polariton with much larger vacuum Rabi splitting while retaining an electric dipole comparable to the IX-polariton, which can be highly desirable for both optoelectronic applications and study of quantum many-body phenomena of polaritons. We also plan to explore polariton formed with the charged interlayer exciton in the MX2/M'X'2/MX2 trilayers, where the bi-chromatic trilayer moiré pattern can lead to rich fine structures because of the complex energy landscape and light coupling properties that can be separately engineered at the two heterointerfaces controlled by the two twisting angles.

17312916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17312916.value: Exciton-polariton is the hybrid of a photon in optical microcavity, with an exciton which is the elementary excitation key to optical responses in semiconductors. Exciton-polarition has been a highly interesting system for the exploration of fundamental many-body physics and technological applications such as lasing. Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) is a new class of semiconductors with appealing optoelectronic properties, and stacking different TMDs monolayers further provide exciting opportunities to tailor optoelectronic properties through forming moiré superlattices from spatial interference of two slightly misaligned TMDs lattices. We found that TMD heterostructures and moiré superlattices host exciton systems of unique features that well distinct them from conventional semiconductors, including the spatially varying optical dipole in moiré landscape and extra degree of freedom in moiré superlattice potential. We show these lead to highly tunable exciton-polaritons featuring novel fine structures and topological transport properties, when TMDs are embedded in planar optical microcavities. Exciton-polaritons in such hybrid systems are becoming an active field of research of both scientific and technological interest, with experimental advances in coupling TMDs structures to microcavities. The research finding here would be a timely contribution in understanding the fundamental properties of these quantum quasiparticles, underlying potential novel optoelectronic applications.

17313616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17313616.value: In 1960s, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer (BSD) conjecture was posed. Although there are many important progressive works, it remains unsettled today and was included in the seven Millennium Prize problems of the Clay Mathematics Institute. In a refined version of the conjecture (also called the full BSD conjecture), it is further predicted the role of an arithmetic data, called the order of the Tate-Shafarevich group. At present the full BSD conjecture is known for a few elliptic curves. One source of the known cases (for the full BSD) is due to a recent joint work of Coates, Li, Tian and Zhai. Later, motivated by Professor Coates, the research team of Dabrowski, Jedrzejak and Szymaszkiewicz carried out an extensive numerical calculation of these orders. Some conjectures on the asymptotic behaviour of the cumulative sum of the order of the Tate-Shafarevich group are formulated. There is an important connection, via the Shimura correspondence and Waldspurger formula, between the orders of these Tate-Shafarevich groups and the square of the Fourier coefficients of a certain half-integral weight modular form. Thus the cumulative sum of these orders corresponds to the mean square formula of the Fourier coefficients with weights. On the other hand, it was recently studied by various researchers some related sums of the Fourier coefficients for their purposes. These studies lie within a typical scope in analytic number theory -- the asymptotic analysis of cumulative sums of arithmetical functions. In this project, we carry out a study of the Fourier coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms. The project work addresses to the problems having interested other researchers and to provide heuristic and theoretic supportive results to some conjectures on the group orders. We shall propose new treatments, and consequently, obtain improvement upon some previous work.

17313616.label: Realisation of objectives
17313616.value: Objective 1: We derived the method of building a Voronoi-type series approximation for the local weighted mean of an arithmetical function that is associated with Dirichlet series satisfying a functional equation with gamma factors. This new tool can be combined with the method of Heath-Brown and Tsang to evaluate the gap width between sign-changes for coefficients of automorphic L-functions. Objective 2: We attacked the problem by starting with the approach in the joint paper of Hulse at el. Next we apply the work of Shimura to understand the Fourier coefficients of a Hecke eigenform of half-integral weight at various cusps. But to achieve the result, it is necessary to carry out quite delicate computation to explore the underlying cancellations. Objective 3: We evaluated the scattering matrix of the Eisenstein series for the congruence subgroup of level 4, and computed the Rankin-Selberg L-functions associated to cusp forms at each cusp. We then apply the Dirichlet convolution formula to relate a squarefree number and the moebius function at the root of square divisors of the number. We obtained a non-trivial region of holomorphicity of the Dirichlet series of Rankin-Selberg convolution of the Fourier coefficients over squarefree numbers as well as its growth there. Objective 4: We carried out numerical computations which supported the validity of the conjecture. Objective 5: A student is recruited to pursue a M.Phil. degree and the student is now switched to a Ph.D program.

17313616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17313616.value: A Voronoi-type series for the local weighted mean of the coefficients of Dirchlet series satisfying a functional equation with gamma factors is established. Applications on various L-functions are worked out, cf. Output 1. We showed that the Dirichlet series associated to the Fourier coefﬁcients of a half-integral weight Hecke eigenform at squarefree integers extends analytically to a holomorphic function in the right half-plane of complex numbers of real part greater than one-half. This result improves the known result in the literature. cf. Output 2. We evaluated the number of sign changes of Fourier coefficients of half-integral weight cusp forms over arithmetic progressions. cf. Output 3. Related to the project work, we considered the location of the occurrence of the first negative sign for the Hecke eigenvalues for self-dual irreducible cuspidal automorphic representations of GL2. cf. Output 4.

17313616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17313616.value: In this project, we only considered holomorphic forms in the case of half-integral weight. It would be interesting to study the Maass forms. In addition to the sequence of squarefree numbers, the case of other sequences with arithmetic structures is significant but perhaps more challenging.

17313616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17313616.value: The study of the Fourier coefficients of a half integral weight modular form is important in light its many connections with other mathematical objects and problems. One way to understand these Fourier coefficients is to investigate the L-function associated to them. We have successfully developed some techniques to study the properties of sequences whose associated L-functions are well-behaved. Using our techniques, we can have a better understanding on their average sizes and oscillatory properties.

17315316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17315316.value: The main objective of this work is to facilitate the interpretation of satellite gravity data from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) mission and its follow-up. GRACE has successfully mapped movement of mass on and beneath the Earth’s surface. For example, GRACE is able to quantify the rates of ice loss in Greenland, Antarctica and other large ice sheets, which has led to a better understanding of their contribution to global sea level rise and its future threat to coastal cities around the world. Another important application of GRACE is the detection of changes in continental groundwater storage and thus future water supply and water resource management. However, GRACE detects all mass movements and not just the signals due to continental groundwater storage or mass exchange between the ice sheets and the ocean. In particular, GRACE also detects the gravity signal due to the flow of mantle rocks induced by the melting of the ice sheets during the last Ice Age and the associated loading of the oceans by the melted ice water (i.e. the Glacial Isostatic Adjustment or GIA process). Thus, the signal due to GIA must be removed from the GRACE data before they can be used to interpret for current ice loss, sea level rise, climate change or groundwater storage. Currently, gravity signals predicted by GIA models are used for filtering GRACE. However, it is not satisfactory because only one ice history-earth viscosity model combination is used as the input to GIA model and the uncertainty of the predictions due to uncertainties in these model input have not been addressed. Moreover, many studies neglect the important effects of lateral heterogeneity, which is clearly seen in near surface geology and seismic tomography. The objective of this proposal is to study the contributions of GIA to GRACE data and quantify its uncertainty. The novelty is to quantify the uncertainties of the “best GIA model prediction” by considering various combinations of ice and earth models that include lateral heterogeneity. The research outcome includes the spatial-temporal variation of gravity, land uplift, sea level change due to GIA and their uncertainties in a 3D earth. This outcome can be used to remove GIA contributions from data of GRACE or its follow-up missions for the interpretation of other mass changes (e.g. groundwater storage, mass exchange between the ocean and glaciers or other climate change signals).

17315316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17315316.value: Most models of glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) assume that the Earth is 1-D, i.e. laterally homogeneous. However, seismic and geological observations show that the mantle is laterally heterogeneous. Previous studies with lateral heterogeneity mostly focused on its effect or on GIA predictions, and it is not clear to what extent can lateral heterogeneity solve the misfits between GIA predictions and observations. The aim of this research is to search for the best 3-D viscosity models that can simultaneously fit the global relative sea level data, the peak uplift rates (u-dot from the Global Navigation Satellite System) and peak gravity-rate-of-change (g-dot from the Gravity Recovery And Climate Experiment satellite mission) in Laurentia and Fennoscandia. However, the search is dependent on the ice and viscosity model inputs—the latter depends on the background viscosity and the seismic tomography models used. In this study, the ICE-6G_C ice model, with Bunge and Grand’s seismic tomography model and background viscosity models close to VM5 are used. A coupled Laplace finite element method is used to compute sea level change with time-dependent coastlines and rotational feedback in addition to changes in deformation and gravity. Our results of Objective #1 prefer an elastic lithosphere that has maximum thickness of 140 km under continental cratons in North America and northern Europe but reduces to 60 km underneath the oceans. The preferred depth of the asthenospheric bottom is around 190–200 km with asthenospheric viscosity around 1.E20 Pa s. The best fit to the GIA data is obtained when lateral heterogeneity both in the lithosphere, sublithosphere and mantle are included (model HetM-MHLMin60-Max_140-Sub). To study the uncertainties of 3D GIA models in North America, the best models from Objective #1 are used to compute the mean and the standard deviations (i.e. uncertainties). The pattern of uncertainties using 3D model is shown to be different from studies using 1D earth models, showing the importance of using 3D earth. The results of this research will be very useful in monitoring anthropogenic driven climate change, recent hydrology changes, or recent changes in oceanic processes because many geodetic observations (e.g. from satellite missions) detect not only signals from these recent processes but also strong signals from GIA due to the end of the last Ice Age.

17315316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17315316.value: This study focus on the search for 3-D viscosity structure and the uncertainties underneath North America using ICE-6G_C. This is because ICE-6G_C performs very well here. However, ICE-6G_C performs less well in northern Europe and so the 3D viscosity structure there is less well constrained. This situation for northern Europe can be improved in the near future and the GIA uncertainties there can be found. Indeed our recent work with improvement in the ice history in northern Europe (Huang, Wu & Steffen 2019, EPSL) is a good starting point for this. In Antarctica and Greenland, the change in their ice thickness history and the 3D viscosity structure underneath are even less well constrained due to the lack of observational data and the complication due to recent melting. Much more effort has to be done to get new data and resolve issues related to recent melting before the 3D viscosity structure underneath can be constrained and the GIA uncertainties resolved.

17315316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17315316.value: Modern Space-Age instruments (e.g. GRACE satellite mission) can detects signals due to recent climate change, recent changes in groundwater storage under continents, or recent oceanic processes. However, these modern instruments also detect the signal due to the flow of mantle rocks induced by the melting of the ice sheets during the last Ice Age (i.e. the Glacial Isostatic Adjustment or GIA process). Thus, to reveal the desired signals from recent processes, the signal due to GIA must be removed from the observational data. Currently, signals predicted by GIA models are used for this purpose. However, it is not satisfactory because the inputs, and thus outputs, of GIA models have uncertainties. Moreover, many studies neglect the important effects of lateral change in mantle properties. This research provides the GIA signal and its uncertainty required for filtering the observational data in North America. The novelty is to include the important effects of lateral changes in mantle properties.

17316016.label: Project Objectives
17316016.value: We have developed the in-house non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) based quantum mechanical methods for both transient and steady-state current calculations. Efficient numerical algorithms are required for the proposed project, and will be developed. Besides, parallel computing is necessary, and the computer codes will be parallelized. With the efficient algorithms developed and computer codes parallelized, the transient and steady-state currents through model photocatalytic cells and photovoltaic devices will be calculated, and the charge generation and separation mechanisms will be examined. Both inorganic and organic devices will be modeled and simulated, in particular, organic photovoltaic devices will be studied. Charge separation depends very much on the detailed size, dimention, structure and geometry of interfaces. Simulation on a seires of model interfaces with different sizes, dimensions and morphologies will be carried out to study systematically these factors and understand their influences. Pump-probe microscopy is a powerful experimental tool to probe charge carrier dynamics in real time. Employing our time-domain quantum mechanical method, we can simulate the pump-probe microscopy experiment. p/n junctions made of doped sillicon nanowire will be modeled, and the calculated pump-probe microscopy will be compared to the existing experimental result. Mechanism of charge generation and separation will be investigated. Two-dimensional photocurrent spectroscopy (2DPS) is a newly developed multidimentional electronic spectroscopy, and can be used to probe electronic dynamics of optoelectronic devices. We will calculate the 2DPSs of the photocatalytic cells and photovoltaic devices which will be analyzed to understand the corresponding charge transfer mechanisms. 2DPS is a new experimental tool, and relatively few experiments have been carried out. Collaboration with experimental groups will be sought.

17316016.label: Realisation of objectives
17316016.value: Basing on the in-house non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) based quantum mechanical methods for both transient and steady-state current calculations, we have developed further the efficient numerical algorithms, such as single value decomposition (SVD), and the new algorithms are much faster and can be applied to much large systems, for instance, the steady state currents of the systems containing hundred thousands of electrons have been calculated. In addition, the codes have been parallelized and subsequently employed. With the efficient algorithms developed and computer codes parallelized, the transient and steady-state currents through model photocatalytic cells and photovoltaic devices are calculated, and the charge generation and separation mechanisms have been examined. An organic photovoltaic device made of PCBM and P3HT has been modeled and simulated. Charge separation depends very much on the vibronic coupling near the donor-acceptor interface, and long time coherent charge transfer was observed, and the results have been published in Nano Lett in 2019. The entire photo excited generation of electron-hole pairs, their migration to and separation at the donor-acceptor interface, and subsequent emergence of photocurrent have been simulated; and a manuscript has been submitted to Science Advance. Moreover, a resonant phonon-assisted charge separation mechanism has been discovered, and found to play an important role to accelerate the charge transfer across the donor-acceptor interface. A manuscript is in preparation. Pump-probe microscopy is a powerful experimental tool to probe charge carrier dynamics in real time. Employing our time-domain quantum mechanical method, we have simulated the pump-probe microscopy experiment under a scanning tunnelling microscope (STM), and demonstrated that this ultrafast STM spectroscope can probe the electron dynamics in real space-time. It is thus possible to probe the electron dynamics in real space-time. We find that it is a fourth order nonlinear response of light. The results was published in Nano Lett in 2018. Note that recently experimental attempts have been made to probe electronic dynamics in real time with ultrafast STM spectroscopy. Our method is the only practical technique to simulate the ultrafast STM. Two-dimensional photocurrent spectroscopy (2DPS) is a newly developed multidimentional electronic spectroscopy, and can be used to probe electronic dynamics of optoelectronic devices. We have developed the formalism to simulate the 2DPSs of the open quantum systems and applied to calculate the 2DPSs of the model systems and realistic optoelectronic devices, and comparison to the existing experiment has been carried out. 2DPS is a new experimental tool, and relatively few experiments have been carried out. Our method provides important guidance to the experimental efforts. A manuscript is in preparation.

17316016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17316016.value: 1) It has been proposed that photo excited excitons migrate to the donor-acceptor interfaces in organic photovoltaic devices and the excitons dissociation occurs at the interfaces, i.e. the electrons in the excitons transfer across the interfaces from the donors to acceptors while the holes leave via the donor materials; and the migration of the dissociated electrons and holes lead to the photocurrent. However, there has been neither direct experimental observation nor computer simulation to confirm the mechanism. We performed the first quantum mechanical simulation to simulate directly each of the processes involved in the proposed mechanism. Besides confirmation of the mechanism, we find that the charge transfer across the donor-acceptor interface is a coherent process where the vibronic coupling plays a pivotal role. Moreover, we find that the charge transfer across the donor-acceptor interface is a resonant process. One manuscript was published, one submitted, and the third in preparation. 2) Probing electron dynamics in real space-time has been a dream. In this project, we have proposed the ultrafast STM spectroscope, the combined ultrafast laser pulse and STM system, to probe the real space trajectory of the electron dynamics with sub-nanometer spatial and femtosecond temporal resolutions. The signal is the integrated current through the STM which can be readily measured. The time delay between the pump and probe sub-femtosecond pulses can be tuned, and the variation of the electric signal measure the trajectory of the electron dynamics in time. The STM tip can be placed in different locations, which probes the trajectory in real space with sub-nanometer resolution. 3) Several years ago the two-dimensional photocurrent spectroscopy (2DPS) was developed to examine the electronic dynamics of the nano-electronic devices. However, there lacks theoretical method to calculate the 2DPS. In this project, we have developed the theory and computation algorithm to simulate 2DPS employing our TDDFT-OS developed in 1) above. This enables the correct interoperation of the 2DPS and may extend its realm of application.

17316016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17316016.value: 1) We will extend our quantum mechanical simulation of organic photovoltaic devices to other open quantum systems, for instance, the electrochemical cells. It has been difficult to simulate electrochemical process suing quantum mechanics. The method we developed here, TDDFT-OS, can be generalised to simulate the electrochemical cells such as lithium ion battery. 2) Experiments have been coming out to probe electronic dynamics directly. We will apply our TDDFT-OS to help interpret the experiments and examine the mechanisms. Note that our TDDFT-OS is the only quantum mechanical method available for such experiments. 3) For 2DPS, we need to speed up our calculations further, as it is the fourth order opt-electrical response, and thus, very time consuming to model.

17316016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17316016.value: In this project, we have developed the fast algorithm for our first-principles quantum mechanics method for open quantum systems, and applied it to simulate the generation of photocurrent in organic photovoltaic devices, the two-dimensional photocurrent spectrum. We also propose to employ the ultrafast STM spectroscopy to probe the trajectory of electron dynamics with sub-nanometer spatial and femtosecond temporal resolutions for the first time. For organic photovoltaic, we have confirm the coherent charge transfer process and discovered the new resonant phonon-assisted charge transfer process across the donor-acceptor interface. Six manuscripts have been published, one submitted, and another in preparation.

17316416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17316416.value: 極調和Maass 形式上的微分算子與k-fold 微分形式

17316416.label: Project Objectives
17316416.value: Construct a basis of Poincaré series for the space of polar harmonic Maass forms. This involves solving a differential equation to determine the elliptic coefficients of an arbitrary polar harmonic Maass form, paralleling what is known for Fourier coefficients when considering poles at the cusps. Compute the image of the xi-operator on these Poincaré series. Compute the image of the repeated holomorphic differential operator on these Poincaré series. Split the meromorphic modular forms into three categories: The first category should include all of the cusp forms and (hopefully) will have a restriction on the order of the poles. The second category will be defined by taking the pre-image of the first category under the xi-operator and then taking the image under the repeated holomorphic operator. The intersection of the first and second category should be trivial, and the first category is taken as large as possible so that the intersection may remain trivial. The third category should contain forms whose pre-images under both differential operators are essentially the same. Determine whether the entire space is then spanned by forms of the 3 above categories. Assuming the splitting of the space of meromorphic modular forms given in the last objective, determine whether the spaces are orthogonal. This will involve an application of Stokes Theorem and a pairing of Bruinier and Funke. Use the results above to form a splitting of k-fold differential forms and study the resulting properties of the differential forms coming from forms in each of the three categories above. Parallel and contrast this with the known splitting for differentials.

17316416.label: Realisation of objectives
17316416.value: The primary goals of the proposal were realized and publications arose from these studies. The construction of a family of polar harmonic Maass forms was constructed using the ideas brought out in the proposal and this resulted in the successful completion of the first objective. The second and third objectives were also carried out at the same time and the images under these operators were studied. The realization of the first three objectives also resulted in a result involving the elliptic coefficients of these objects and a study with two collaborators yielded a result known as duality for these objects; duality of a different type for Fourier coefficients had been studied by others but this result appears to be the first of its type for elliptic coefficients. The construction from the first objective and the investigation of its image under the operators in objectives 2 and 3 resulted in a natural splitting of the space of meromorphic modular forms as predicted by the proposal, yielding a successful completion of objective four. The study of the inner product between these meromorphic forms yields the duality results mentioned above and also the fact that these forms are not fully orthogonal. The study of the orthogonality yields another natural interpretation of the splitting of these spaces and has resulted in another submitted preprint that resolves the fifth objective. The last objective is partially resolved in the sense that the splitting has been formed as a result of the results obtained, but the geometric interpretation is only partially addressed. In two of the three categories described in objective 4, the geometric interpretation can be obtained, but the last category appears to be difficult to investigate from a geometric point of view. This is the reason why the final objective was not fully achieved and lies as a question to be addressed in the future.

17316416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17316416.value: There are a number of primary results coming out of the project. Firstly, in the publication "Differential operators on polar harmonic Maass forms and elliptic duality" the main construction was carried out. This also led to a duality result as a side effect. In the same paper, the splitting of the space into three natural groups was also achieved. The properties of these subspaces and a study of the orthogonality of these forms is what results in the duality result. The study of inner products in this setting also contributed to other investigations, benefitting the paper "Regularized inner products of meromorphic modular forms and higher Green's functions" by investigating the connection between the inner product and the higher Green's functions, a well-studied mathematical object. Following this central theme, there were results obtained by investigating the inner product of these basis elements in the paper "An extension of Rohrlich's Theorem to the j-function". There an identity of Rohrlich was extended in another direction by viewing it as a special case of an inner product of the basis elements constructed in this project. By considering the inner product with other basis elements, one obtains new and interesting identities generalizing Rohrlich's result.

17316416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17316416.value: There is still some potential to study the geometric implications of the research in a further direction. The subspace of meromorphic modular forms that emulates the space corresponding to differentials of the third kind in the weight two case appears to be a particularly interesting case. Information about this space appears to be quite difficult to obtain from a geometric perspective due to the types of singularities that these functions have, while the method laid out in this project allows for some investigation and the implications on the geometric side may still be further explored in the future.

17316416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17316416.value: In the project, we investigated functions that have certain symmetries (known as modularity) and may "blow up" as one approaches certain points (much like the function f(x)=1/x "blows up" as x gets close to zero). The functions are smooth in a certain sense, which roughly speaking means that small changes in the input of the functions do not result in huge changes in the value. A set of functions (called a basis) was constructed from which all of the other functions of this type can be formed. Studying the basis elements, we split up the functions into three different categories and study the properties of functions in each of these categories. We furthermore study orthogonality properties of these functions; two functions are orthogonal if they are independent of each other in a certain sense, so this study is helping to understand the dependence between these functions.

17317316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17317316.value: The atomic 2 dimensional crystals have been attracting tremendous attentions from both fundamental research and application-oriented research. For scientists in solid state physics, the atomic 2D crystals offer an unprecedented platform for exploring physics in 2 dimensional systems. As the material dimension shrinks to atomically thin, quantum confinements and enhanced Coulomb interactions dramatically modify the electronic structure of the materials from the bulk form and incur sophisticated consequences. The reported paradigms include the massless Dirac fermion behaviour in graphene, the bang gap transition from indirect gap in bulk form to direct gap in monolayer group VI transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDC) and the enhanced excitonic effects. Besides these popular 2D crystals, there are other families of emerging 2D crystals which are potential candidates as a platform to investigate physics in the reduced dimensions. In this application we propose to experimentally study physics properties of emerging 2D crystals, specifically monolayers and multilayers of monochalcogenides (GaS, GaSe, InSe, etc) with optical spectroscopy and electric transport. The goal is to explore the potential quantum phase transition in 2D crystals. 基礎科學和新興電子學正在掀起一股二維原子晶體的研究熱潮。 對於固體物理研究者而言，這種原子層厚度的二維晶體提供了一個完美的研究低維世界中物理性質的平台。而且隨著空間尺寸縮小到量子效應的尺度， 一些在三維世界中難以觀察到的物理現像會顯著呈現。 這激勵了固體物理研究者對這些二維原子晶體新奇物理現像的探索。 當前的研究熱點集中在石墨烯及二維六族硫屬化物。 而對另一個二維半導體家族， 三族硫屬化物 （(GaS, GaSe, InSe等）的研究還停留在體材料階段。 本研究計劃建議利用固體光譜手段對二維三族硫屬化物進行系統研究。

17317316.value: we studied the optical properties of 2D monochalcogenides (InSe and GaSe). We collected the direction-resolved photoluminescence of 2D GaSe at various thickness, which gives a momentum space dispersion of band-edge exciton in GaSe. The momentum space dispersed photoluminscence spectral were analyzed and the in-plane and out-plane excitons were identified. The exciton evolution as a function of thickness was studied. We observe that the in-plane dipole radiation survives but out-of-plane dipole radiation fades at 2D limit. The objectives are fully addressed.

17318316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17318316.value: P-波共振费米子的普适性质

17318316.label: Project Objectives
17318316.value: We will construct the many-body theory to calculate explicitly the values of p-wave contacts and compare with actual experimental data. Our aim here will be two-fold. First we want to explain the observed dependences of contacts on the scattering parameters at low temperature. Secondly, we want to gain a deeper understanding of the physical significance of the contacts, in particular, the contact that is related to the effective range of p-wave scattering. We will discuss and extend the concept of p-wave contacts to one-dimensional Fermi gases using an exactly solvable model. Here we will aim to compute the full exact temperature dependence of the contacts as well as their dependence on scattering parameters. We will also make an effort to understand the physical significance of the contacts from the view of exactly solvable models.

We will discuss and extend the concept of p-wave contacts to one-dimensional Fermi gases using an exactly solvable model. 17318316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17318316.value: The study of universal properties of degenerate quantum gases is one of the most important and fruitful directions in cold atom research. In the case of the s-wave Feshbach resonance, a set of universal relations involving a central quantity called “contact” has played an important role in unveiling the underlying correlations of the many-body state and correlating various physical quantities that apparently have no connections at all. Recently, these relations have been extended to p-wave resonances, where it is pointed out that the structure of the “contact” theory becomes much richer, mainly because the complexity of the p-wave Feshbach resonance that requires two types of scattering parameters for its complete description. The extended set of universal relations has been partially verified in recent experiment, but detailed comparison still awaits exploration. In this proposal, we shall address two aspects of the p-wave contact theory: (1) The explicit computation of the values of p-wave contacts using many-body diagrammatic theory and comparison with experimental observations and (2) extension of the concepts of p-wave contacts to lower dimensions, in particular, to an exactly solvable one-dimension p-wave model. While the general theory (or the formal definition) of p-wave contacts and its various implications are known, there has been no explicit calculation of their values except at high temperature. In the first part of the proposal, we will develop a diagrammatic theory based on the so-called two-channel model of p-wave Feshbach resonance and will try to resolve an apparently counter-intuitive experimental observation (see later). In the second part, we will extend the definition of p-wave contacts to lower dimension and in particular, will make use of an exactly solvable one-dimensional model to exhibit their full temperature dependences. This should afford us with an opportunity to check the universal relations with an explicit and exact many-body calculation. In both parts, we shall make efforts to address the physical significance of one of the p-wave contacts, related to the effective range of p-wave resonance. 对于强相互作用量子气体普适性质的研究是冷原子研究的一个重要且富有成果的方向。对于s-波散射而言，这些普适性质由单个“接触量”给出。它描述了体系的一些普适性结果。最近的研究将这些普适结果推广到高波散射，尤其是p-波散射的情形。这些推广表明接触量理论在高波散射的情况下的理论结构比较丰富，尤其是必须要计入两类散射参数。这些基本结论在最近的实验中被验证了。在这个项目中，我们主要的目的有以下两方面：（1）通过多体理论计算接触量的大小以及和实验参数的关系。（2）把接触量的理论推广到低维的情形，尤其是一维可积模型。我们将利用两通道模型来计算接触量，并和实验相比。在低维计算中，我们将用Bethe方法来计算接触量的大小。在研究过程中，我们争取更好的理解与有效长度相关的接触量。

17318316.label: Realisation of objectives
17318316.value: Both objectives have been completed in several publications. Objective One: Our calculation based an extension of Nozieres-Schmit-Rink to p-wave case has been useful in explaining the contact data at finite temperature and their dependences on the interaction parameters. It also reveals, to some extent expectedly, the simplicity of the p-wave gas, at least for energetics, that the nearly complete decoupling of the atom and molecular degrees of freedom. Objective Two: In this case, a calculation based on Bethe-Ansatz has been completed in which the explicit expression for contact in terms of many-body wave function is obtained and evaluated. It is shown that the contact related to effective range is related to the gradients of the wave functions and its dependences on the scattering parameters are evaluated completely in various limit. Numerical calculation is also carried out to see the dependences of contact on scattering parameters.

17318316.value: The major findings of the research are the following: 1. A complete calculation of the p-wave contact at finite temperature and their dependences on the scattering parameters. We show that the calculated contacts compare well with the experimental results. 2. Contact theory is extended to p-wave in 2D and their consequences on the collective mode of the 2D Fermi gas is discussed, especially the role of scaling symmetry. 3. A Bethe-Ansatz calculation is completed for the 1D p-wave Fermi gas and the analytic expressions for the contacts have been computed. 4. Analytic expressions of contacts have also been computed in the weak coupling limits; in the same limit, the Fermi liquid properties have also been investigated.

17318316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17318316.value: The research is related to a unique feature of the dilute quantum systems, namely the range of interaction is much less than the inter-particle distance. Such separation of scales leave us with a scaling region where the many-body wave function is identical to the two-body one and as a result, is completely determined by the two-body physics, except for its normalisation. This fact leads to the universal relations that were presented in the papers published. There are differences and subtleties in systems in 2D and 1D, however, they share the same universal relations. These relations have important constraints on the physical observables in experiments.

17318616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17318616.value: Protein tyrosine nitration (PTN)—a hallmark of nitrative stress markers—is one of the most important stable and irreversible oxidative post-translational modifications in vivo and in vitro. PTN is regioselective at the ortho-position of the tyrosine side chain and is site-specific: only particular tyrosine residues within a protein are susceptible to nitration. Nevertheless, the mechanisms behind the formation of PTNs remain unclear and largely explored. The challenges in determining their energetic and kinetic properties arise from the rich chemistry of radical-mediated PTNs, with complex permutations of hydrogen atom abstraction, proton transfer, isomerization, and rearrangement, with various transient precursors and intermediates. In this proposed study we aim to elucidate the detailed mechanism of radical-mediated peptide tyrosine nitration by using an integrated approach involving gas phase synthesis of prototypical tyrosine-containing peptide radical cations through ion–molecule reactions in a specially configured hybrid linear ion trap mass spectrometer, collision-/surface-induced dissociation experiments, isotopic labeling experiments, and ion spectroscopy in combination with density functional theory calculations and Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus modeling; in particular, we will attempt to explore fundamental factors governing the regioselectivity and site-specificity of the ortho-tyrosine nitration. Our preliminary studies have revealed that gas phase tyrosine nitration involves radical recombination between •NO2 and the prerequisite phenoxyl radical structure of the tyrosine residue, followed by a concerted proton rearrangement, resulting in the generation of the stable closed-shell 3-nitrotyrosyl residue. Elucidating the precise mechanism of radical-mediated ortho-tyrosine nitration could have implications in deciphering the high site specificity and regioselectivity of biological endogenous PTNs. 蛋白酪氨酸硝化標誌在體內和體外的最重要的穩定和不可逆的氧化翻譯後修飾中的一個。 蛋白酪氨酸硝化在酪氨酸側鏈的鄰位區域選擇性和是位點特異性的：一個蛋白質內只有特定酪氨酸殘基易受硝化。蛋白酪氨酸硝化形成背後的機制仍不清楚。在確定他們的活力和動力性能的挑戰，從自由基介導蛋白酪氨酸硝化豐富的化學反應產生的，與氫原子抽象，質子轉移，異構化，重排和複雜的排列組合，各種瞬態前體和中間體。在這個建議的研究中，我們的目標是通過使用綜合方法涉及通過專門配置的混合線性離子阱質譜儀離子分子反應典型含酪氨酸肽陽離子自由基的氣相合成闡明自由基介導肽硝化的詳細機制，碰撞的/表面誘導解離實驗，同位素標記實驗，並理論計算，我們將嘗試探索治鄰硝化的區域選擇性和部位特異性的根本因素。闡明自由基介導鄰硝基酪氨酸的確切機制可能在破譯蛋白酪氨酸硝化的高點特異性和區域選擇性的影響。

17318616.label: Realisation of objectives
17318616.value: The research project on in Radical-Mediated Protein Tyrosine Nitration In Vavuo: Experimental and Theoretical Examination has been funded for 2016 Competitive Earmarked Research Grants application. Protein tyrosine nitration (PTN) is a hallmark of nitrative stress markers. The complexities of the radical-mediated PTN reactions involve the possibilities of several intermediate structures, and the difficulties in generating these transient species with well-defined radical sites mean that such experimental investigations are challenging and difficult. Very little precise chemical mechanistic insight has been elucidated, partly because of difficulties in generating such precursor and intermediate species and partly because of their transient nature. The widely accepted pathway for radical-mediated ortho-tyrosine nitration in vitro involves a transient phenoxyl radical in a radical-recombination reaction between the nitrogen atom of the free •NO2 species and a carbon atom of the phenol ring of the tyrosyl residue at the ortho position. Our fundamental investigation stems from our ongoing interest in obtaining an in-depth understanding of this hallmark of radical-induced peptide chemistry to shed light on the mechanisms of biological processes under oxidative stress. In order to systematic design, generate, and characterize peptide system(s) leading to the gas phase formation of stable 3-nitrotyrosyl-containing peptides, our investigations suggest that PTN is feasible for various precursor tautomers, with favourable isomerization barriers, leading to the prerequisite key intermediate prior to the radical recombination PTN reaction, as proposed. Our approach has synergized the study of elementary ion-chemistry processes (i.e., hydrogen atom, electron, and proton transfers during isomerizations; dissociations) that form a scientific basis underlying PTN reaction. After probing the isomerization processes involving pi– and alpha-carbon–centered precursors in detail, we then focused on the wider and systematic design, preparation, and examination of various prototypical tyrosine-containing radicals with different radical/charge centers and well defined, initially at least, locations; for example, sigma epsilon–, -carbon–, pi -, nitrogen–, and thioyl–centered radicals from medium-sized down to tripeptides. The initial phase of the project was devoted mainly (a) to investigate on favourable isomerization barriers, leading to the prerequisite key intermediate prior to the radical recombination PTN reaction; (b) to probe the isomerization processes involving pi– and alpha-carbon–centered precursors in details. A manuscript describes describing the work of “Isomerization versus dissociation of phenylalanylglycyltryptophan radical cations” has been published {research output 1} Two more research articles seeking to further our fundamental understanding of radical-mediated protein chemistry have been published {research outputs 3, and 5}. In collaboration with Co-I (Dr. Chi-Kit Siu), we have provided the first evidence for the elementary radical-mediated reaction mechanism of gas phase tyrosine nitration, helping us to understand the regioselectivity of tyrosine nitration in biology. {research output 4: Evidence for the Prerequisite Formation of Phenoxyl Radicals in Radical‐Mediated Peptide Tyrosine Nitration In Vacuo Chemistry—A European Journal} Furthermore, we have conducted an exploration of the gas-phase dissociation of a prototypical system, [CuII(dien)G(G/A)W]˙2+, to gain structural insights into peptide radical cations, knowledge which will ultimately assist our understanding of radical behaviour in protein systems. {research output 5}The aforementioned model developed have been used in the other publications were and will continue to be of use in pursuing radical-mediated peptide tyrosine nitration studies. }. An invited review article describing this radical mediated reactions work has been accepted for publication. {research output 2} With PTN having extremely low abundance, estimated to affect less than 0.001% of tyrosine residues, detection of PTN-modified peptides using mass spectrometry is a challenge. Given the relative sparsity of known PTN sites, in order to fully characterize this modification, including the chemistry of its radical-mediated mechanism and substantial degree of selectivity for certain protein sites, it is necessary to enlarge the number of known PTN sites. This task can be addressed from a number of angles, from improvements in mass spectrometry instrumentation and liquid chromatography for better sensitivity to low abundance PTN peptides, to bioinformatic analyses enabling the identification of PTN-modified peptides which could not be identified by routine protein sequence database search. To initiate an exploration of potential relevance to endogenous protein tyrosine nitration (objective 3), we have invested efforts in developing new liquid chromatography separation technologies, such as multiple fraction concatenation 2-dimensional liquid chromatography, in order to improve the duty cycle usage during proteomics experiments, in this case leading to increases of approximately 10% in both peptide and protein identifications. {research output 7} Due to limitations in the ability of protein sequence database search algorithms to identify post-translationally modified peptides, and the fact that many biological samples cannot be readily re-acquired for analysis using new technologies, we have also developed a bioinformatic tool, rPTMDetermine, which employs a machine learning algorithm to retrieve post-translationally modified peptide identifications from the mass spectra left unassigned by database search. {research output 6} Through application of this methodology to a Macaca fascicularis data set, we have demonstrated its ability to vastly improve the PTN coverage of a proteome. By tackling PTN from all angles (fundamentals, analytical and bioinformatics), we will ultimately be able to fully characterize this modification from different aspects, understanding the chemistry which leads to its occurrence in biology, and the key role played by the modification in certain neurodegenerative disease pathways. This project has been widened to our investigations into the molecular discovery of biomolecule oxidation (nitration in particular) in radical-induced diseases—extending our fundamental studies to biophysical, bioanalytical, and biomedical applications using a combination of experimental and computational approaches. Three postgraduate students, Xiaoyan Mu and Lai Chulk Kuen, and MengZhu(third year Ph.D. student- publications of 5-7) have been involved and trained to perform research in fundamental mass spectrometry; he is co-supervised by the Co-I of the project-Andy Siu from the Department of Biology and chemistry, City University of Hong Kong for our interdisciplinary mass spectrometry-DFT calculation research. Xiaoyan Mu attended intensive DFT calculation training in Winter 2016 at the CityU. This project also serves as a training tool for introducing our collaborating graduate students to experimental (MS and IRMPD) and computational approaches (DFT calculation) on our MS data regarding PTN mechanism: Structural, energetics, and kinetics aspects.

17319316.label: Project Objectives
17319316.value: Robust Lens Models: Our team has developed a hybrid scheme to model lensing by galaxy clusters that includes cluster member galaxies but which makes no assumptions about the distribution of matter on larger spatial scales. Referred to as WSLAP+, this method is well suited to the complexity of the massive merging clusters chosen for HFF. With a reliable correction for lensing, we are able to obtain the intrinsic properties of all the lensed galaxies, including those more weakly lensed and do not produce multiple images. The lensed galaxies reach typically 2–3 magnitudes fainter than those found in the deepest blind-field surveys, and provide the crucial leverage for distinguishing between competing theories for galaxy formation that incorporate different forms of dark matter. We also plan to construct robust lens models for the most powerful lensing clusters in the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) program. Intrinsic Properties of Multiply-Lensed Sources: With robust lens models in hand, we can maximize the effectiveness of finding multiply-lensed images belonging to the same galaxy by accurately predicting the positions of their counter-images. We also can securely identify each set of lensed images belonging to a given source, derive the geometric redshifts of all the multiply-lensed sources to check against their photometric redshifts (sometimes ambiguous for, especially, galaxies at very high redshifts), and reliably derive their intrinsic properties (luminosity and size). Finally, we can accurately reconstruct the delensed images of well-resolved sources to study their morphology. Galaxy Luminosity and Size Functions: With knowledge of the intrinsic properties of the lensed galaxies, we can then compute the luminosity and size functions of galaxies. More practically, we can derive their luminosity and size distributions. To derive these distributions, we have developed algorithms to correct for the varying magnification over the cluster and hence the different surface areas at different redshifts probed at different source locations. By comparing the measured luminosity and size distributions against those predicted by theory, we will test competing theories for galaxy formation that incorporate different forms of dark matter. Specifically, we can address whether the galaxy space density increases with decreasing luminosity as might be expected if DM is cold and collisionless, or whether there is an abrupt decrease (turnover) at a particular luminosity indicative of a lower limiting mass for DM halos imposed by its wavelike nature. Mass distribution of massive cluster members, including mass and location of their supermassive black holes: For lensed images that happen to be projected close to and which therefore experience significant lensing also by individual cluster members, we are able to probe in detail the mass distribution of these cluster members. In particular, such instances provide an opportunity to infer the properties of a supermassive black hole.

We also plan to construct robust lens models for the most powerful lensing clusters in the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) program.

Intrinsic Properties of Multiply-Lensed Sources: With robust lens models in hand, we can maximize the effectiveness of finding multiply-lensed images belonging to the same galaxy by accurately predicting the positions of their counter-images. We also can securely identify each set of lensed images belonging to a given source, derive the geometric redshifts of all the multiply-lensed sources to check against their photometric redshifts (sometimes ambiguous for, especially, galaxies at very high redshifts), and reliably derive their intrinsic properties (luminosity and size). Finally, we can accurately reconstruct the delensed images of well-resolved sources to study their morphology.

Galaxy Luminosity and Size Functions: With knowledge of the intrinsic properties of the lensed galaxies, we can then compute the luminosity and size functions of galaxies. More practically, we can derive their luminosity and size distributions. To derive these distributions, we have developed algorithms to correct for the varying magnification over the cluster and hence the different surface areas at different redshifts probed at different source locations. By comparing the measured luminosity and size distributions against those predicted by theory, we will test competing theories for galaxy formation that incorporate different forms of dark matter. Specifically, we can address whether the galaxy space density increases with decreasing luminosity as might be expected if DM is cold and collisionless, or whether there is an abrupt decrease (turnover) at a particular luminosity indicative of a lower limiting mass for DM halos imposed by its wavelike nature.

Mass distribution of massive cluster members, including mass and location of their supermassive black holes: For lensed images that happen to be projected close to and which therefore experience significant lensing also by individual cluster members, we are able to probe in detail the mass distribution of these cluster members. In particular, such instances provide an opportunity to infer the properties of a supermassive black hole.

17319316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17319316.value: We have completed our effort to construct robust free-form lens models for all 6 galaxy clusters in Hubble Frontiers Field (HFF) program, the last of which published in fulfillment of this proposal (Paper 2). All but perhaps one of these galaxy clusters are in the process of merging, and therefore have complex mass distributions that cannot be easily or completely captured by parametric lensing algorithms, as is the common approach used in other works. In addition, we have pioneered an iterative method to construct free-form lens models based on multiply-lensed images having a mixture of spectroscopic and photometric redshifts, and applied this method to a galaxy cluster in the Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH) program (Paper 5). We have applied the lens models constructed to: (i) determine the geometric redshift of the most distant gravitationally lensed galaxy discovered to date (Paper 1) (ii) determine the geometric redshift of multiply-lensed galaxies having only photometrically determined redshifts (Papers 2, 5) (iii) pinpoint the position and measure the mass of a supermassive black hole in a galaxy at an intermediate redshift, constituting the first direct measurement of the mass of a supermassive black hole beyond the local universe (Paper 4) (iv) measured the luminosity function of galaxies at high redshifts, and demonstrated that the luminosity function of these galaxies is inconsistent with the predictions of Cold Dark Matter but consistent with those of wave-like Dark Matter (Paper 3)

17319316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17319316.value: The astrophysical applications of gravitational lensing - the first step of which is to construct a robust lens model for the lensing object - is one of my core research projects. The work conducted for (and before) this proposal laid the foundation for the follow-up proposal RGC/GRF 17304519, which received excellent reviews and was maximally funded.

17319316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17319316.value: Gravitational lensing by galaxies constitute natural cosmic telescopes to magnify the brightnesses and sizes of distant background galaxies - permitting the detection of galaxies otherwise too dim to be seen, and the study of their morphology otherwise too small in size to show any features. Under suitable geometries, the background galaxy is multiply lensed, so that each image constitutes a magnified, brightened, but distorted view of the actual background galaxy. We use the geometrical arrangement of such multiply-lensed images in the sky to derive lens models for the lensing galaxies - i.e., the distribution of matter, including invisible Dark Matter, in the lensing galaxies. From the lens models thus constructed, we can reconstruct the actual appearance of lensed galaxies, and even derive - based on geometry - their distances. In this project, we use the lens models constructed for massive galaxy clusters to: (i) determine the geometric redshift of the most distant gravitationally lensed galaxy discovered to date (ii) determine the geometric redshift of multiply-lensed galaxies having only photometrically determined redshifts (iii) pinpoint the position and measure the mass of a supermassive black hole in a galaxy at an intermediate redshift, constituting the first direct measurement of the mass of a supermassive black hole beyond the local universe (iv) measured the luminosity function of galaxies at high redshifts, and demonstrated that the luminosity function of these galaxies is inconsistent with the predictions of Cold Dark Matter but consistent with those of wave-like Dark Matter

17321916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17321916.value: 組蛋白去乙酰化酶是一類對組蛋白乙酰基進行水解，從而能夠對組蛋白所在的染色質的結構進行調控。染色質結構的變化將會引起DNA的空間位阻變化，從而最終影響細胞內的基因表達。因此組蛋白去乙酰化酶在包括細胞增殖、細胞凋亡、分化、血管增生、免疫反應等多個細胞生命過程中起著重要作用。也因此組蛋白去乙酰化酶一直被作為一類重要的藥物靶點，有多個以組蛋白去乙酰化酶為靶點的藥物被研發成功。在細胞中，大部分的組蛋白去乙酰化酶以蛋白質複合體的形式存在；而該複合體的大小、組成、動態變化等，都和組蛋白去乙酰化酶的生物活性息息相關。然而，現今能夠有效地對組蛋白去乙酰化酶複合體，而不是獨立的組蛋白去乙酰化酶進行研究的方法非常有限，成為本領域研究中的一個很大的局限所在。近期我們實驗室發展了一種新穎的基於DNA的光交聯探針方法(DPAL)，能夠利用DNA模板控制效應，高度靈敏和特異性地識別細胞中蛋白質和小分子配體的相互作用。在本項目中，我們提出將DPAL進一步延伸，使之能夠研究組蛋白去乙酰化酶蛋白質複合體中的蛋白質=蛋白質相互作用。本項目的研究將以三個部分組成。一、我們將利用DPAL的多探針的優勢，去標記和捕獲組蛋白去乙酰化酶複合體中多個和組蛋白去乙酰化酶直接或間接相互作用的蛋白質；二、我們將進行比較性的蛋白質組學研究，以識別在不同細胞類型中組蛋白去乙酰化酶蛋白質複合體的成分的不同，從而為進一步研究組蛋白去乙酰化酶複合體生物功能與其蛋白質組分之間的關係。第三、我們將以組蛋白去乙酰化酶-6位一個主要目標進行研究。由於組蛋白去乙酰化酶-6存在眾多的非組蛋白底物，因此對組蛋白去乙酰化酶-6蛋白質複合體的研究將為進一步闡明其在細胞生命過程，尤其是和惡性腫瘤相關的過程中的作用和機制。總之，本項目的研究將促進對組蛋白去乙酰化酶這一重要蛋白質家族的生物功能在分子層面上的理解。我們預期DPAL也不僅僅限於組蛋白去乙酰化酶蛋白複合體，而能夠被廣泛應用於多種其它蛋白質-蛋白質相互作用的體系，成為化學生物學研究中的一種有力工具。

17321916.label: Realisation of objectives
17321916.value: Objective 1: We have further developed the DNA-programmed affinity labeling (DPAL) method for characterizing protein-protein interactions and applied the method to studying HDAC complexes. The method was validated with recombinant HDAC complex proteins in vitro and in cell lysates. After the initial validation, we have conducted systematic profiling of HDAC complex proteins in HeLa cells using two pan-HDAC inhibitors, SAHA and TSA. The labeling specificity and efficiency have been validated and optimized at this stage. In principle, the developed method is expected to be broadly applicable to other protein complexes. Objective 2: We have validated that DNA-based probes have sufficient stability in cell lysates and in live cells, provided the probes are short and are modified with small molecules at the 5’- and/or 3’-termini. For example, we incubated fluorescence-labelled DNA probes in cell lysates overnight and then quantified the residual DNAs. Results have shown little degradation of the DNA probes (< 5%) occurred. Furthermore, we delivered two DNA probes into live cells via chemical agent (saponin). The probes are complementary and the formation of the DNA duplex brings the fluorophores at the ends of DNAs to proximity and thereby generate fluorescent signal. We quantified the cell fluorescence using flow cytometry. Although the degradation rate is slightly higher than in cell lysates, the probes still have sufficient stability in live cells. Finally, we also observed sufficient nuclear translocation of the DNA probes, consistent with literature reports. Objective 3: In the initial methodology development, we prepared twelve CPs which have different “n” values (spacer length). A positive n value indicates a protruding CP on the BP template, while a negative n value indicates a recessive CP. By using recombinant HDAC complex proteins, we noticed that large “n” values resulted in very low capture efficiency, probably due to the long and flexible spacer. Thus, in the profiling experiments, we employed nine different “n” values range from +12 to -15, and the results showed that they were able to cover the majority of the HDAC complex proteins. Furthermore, the performance of the DPAL probe set has been validated in buffer and in cell lysates. It is worth noting that, smaller “n” values (+6 +3, 0, -3, and -6) contributed to the majority of the captured proteins (> 90%), indicating that HDAC interacts with many proteins directly or within a short distance, or distal interactors are difficult to be captured, which may be a limitation of this method. Objective 4: This is the major objective of this project. We have conducted a systematic profiling of HDAC complexes in HeLa cells. We have used both SAHA- and TSA-based binding probes to guide the labelling. Both SAHA and TSA are pan-HDAC inhibitors and we reasoned that they would provide a wider coverage of different types of HDAC complexes in the cell. In addition, a comparative analysis between the two probes would exclude non-HDAC-related binders. Certainly, HDAC-isoform-specific inhibitors is better for profiling a specific type HDAC complex; however, there are very few specific HDAC inhibitors available with limited target specificity. In total, we have identified 267 HDAC complex proteins using the SAHA-based probe. Among them, 112 proteins are potential novel HDAC interactors. A comparison with the TSA-based probe helped us prioritize the top 30 proteins for validation. We used co-IP, either in buffer with recombinant proteins or in cell lysates with endogenous ones, and have confirmed three novel, indirect HDAC binders. The other proteins are either direct HDAC binders or have been reported to be associated with HDACs in the literature. We also investigated the cells under different conditions. In a key experiment, HeLa cells, either untreated or treated with the cytotoxic agent doxorubicin, were profiled and the results showed that the DPAL probes are also responsive to the changes of cellular conditions (HDAC1-PARP1 disassociation). Moreover, using non-stimulated and EGF-stimulated cells, we have identified a potential novel mechanism of PKM2-mediated histone modification. Collectively, using PARP1 and PKM2 as representatives, we have demonstrated that this method could reveal new biological implications for HDAC-associated proteins. Objective 5: In our previous experiments, we used pan-HDAC inhibitors (SAHA and TSA) to engage multiple HDAC complexes, which is better for identifying large number of HDAC interactors; however, additional steps were necessary to deconvolute the protein-protein interactions (e.g. separate co-IP validation using isoform-specific HDAC antibodies). Tubacin is reported to be an HDAC6-specific inhibitor; thus, we used it to conduct isoform-specific HDAC complex profiling. However, in our study, we observed considerable non-specificity from tubacin-based probes. Besides HDAC6, tubacin-DNA probe also captured HDAC1, HDAC2, and their associated proteins in vitro. Endogenous HDAC profiling showed very similar results based on mass spectrometry data. We also attempted to use free tubacin as the soluble competitor; however, again tubacin was able to compete for HDAC1/2 binding. Thus, tubacin-based probes were not further used for isoform-specific HDAC complex profiling. We reasoned that this non-specificity might due to DNA conjugation or the type of cells used in this study. In fact, development of isoform-specific HDAC inhibitors have been a challenging problem in HDAC research. In addition, most of the reported HDAC inhibitors were tested in biochemical assays and they might exhibit different specificities in the cell when engaging different HDAC complexes. Objective 6: The results of this project have been published in top chemistry journals. The main results are published in Angew. Chemie. Int. Ed. in 2020. The additional applications of this DPAL method have been reported in several other publications. Based on the results from this project, we have identified a potentially new mechanism for PKM2-mediated histone modulation, which could be further investigated. Moreover, an important future direction is the application of this DPAL method in other protein complex systems.
