17321916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17321916.value: 1) Histone deacetylase (HDAC) is a major class of deacetylation enzymes. Many HDACs exist in large protein complexes in cells and their biological functions strongly depend on the complex composition. The identification of HDAC-associated proteins is highly important in understanding their molecular mechanisms. Although affinity probes have been developed to study HDACs, they were mostly targeting the direct binder HDAC, while other proteins in the complex remain underexplored. To address this issue, we have developed an affinity labelling approach for characterizing protein-protein interactions in protein complexes. Affinity probes are powerful tools to explore biology, but they are mostly designed to engage the direct target protein, and using affinity probes to capture indirect binders in protein complexes remained underexplored. In this project, we developed a DNA-based affinity labeling (DPAL) method capable of presenting different probe configurations without the need for preparing multiple probes. Using one binding probe, nine probe configurations were created to profile HDAC complexes and a large number of HDAC interactors were identified. Notably, this method identified indirect HDAC binders that may be inaccessible to traditional affinity probes. Moreover, the method is responsive to the change of cellular conditions and it has also revealed new biological implications for HDAC-associated proteins. Specifically, a potential new mechanism of PKM2 in modulating histone modification has been identified. The probe system is modular and the guiding ligand could be easily changed to interrogate other protein complexes beyond HDACs; thus, this method provided a simple and broadly applicable method for characterizing protein-protein interactions. These findings have been published (Angew. Chemie. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 17525-27532). 2) As stated in Objective 1, we aimed to develop DPAL to be a method to characterize protein-protein interactions in general. Besides HDAC complexes, we have also extended this method to label membrane proteins directly on live cells, in which an antibody for the target membrane protein is used to guide the labelling. After the labelling, the DNA tag enabled, for the first time, selection of large-scale DNA-encoded chemical libraries (DELs) against endogenous membrane proteins on live cells. This work has been published very recently (Nat. Chem. 2020, published online, DOI: 10.1038/s41557-020-00605-x). 3) The multi-probe approach based on DPAL developed in this project has been applied in several additional applications, including DNA-encoded dynamic library (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 14965; Biochem. Biophy. Res. Commun. 2020, 533, 215; J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2018, 140, 15859), selection of DEL against non-immobilized proteins (ACS Combi. 17321916.value: 1) Application of the multi-probe DPAL method to study other protein-protein interactions (PPIs) and protein complexes. The principle of the developed method should be generally applicable to PPIs. Indeed, we have demonstrated this aspect in several additional PPIs (e.g. publications mentioned in 3), Section 6.1). For example, we plan to use this method to characterize the extracellular ligands of integrins (project on-going), E3 ligase complexes (grant application submitted), and profiling of transcriptional factors (project on-going). 2) We plan to conduct more in-depth study of HDAC complexes using this method. On one hand, more types of cells and cell phenotypes will be used to study the function-composition relationship of HDAC complexes. In addition, if isoform-specific HDAC inhibitors could be identified, they will be used to profile/study specific types of HDAC complexes. Finally, we will attempt to conduct multiplexed DPAL labelling/profiling by using multiple binding probes targeting multiple protein complexes.

17321916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17321916.value: HDACs are of high significance in biomedical sciences. Dysfunction of HDACs has been implicated in many human diseases. Recent studies found HDACs also had important roles in cancers, neurodegenerative diseases, inflammation, and developmental disorders. HDACs have been long pursued as a major drug target, and a number of HDAC inhibitors are approved to treat cancers, including cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, multiple myeloma, and pancreatic cancer. These success stories highlight the significance of HDAC as a class of important drug targets. However, despite decades of research, a clear understanding of how they operate in cells and their pathological implications are still lacking. This research provides a versatile tool to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of HDACs, and it may facilitate the development of new therapeutics based on HDAC complexes as the drug targets. In addition, the developed method may be extended to other protein complex systems, leading to even more opportunities for drug discovery.

17324016.value: 保險風險理論裡對資金演變過程相關的隨機變量的綜合分析

17324016.label: Project Objectives
17324016.value: To further accommodate path-dependent random variables into the Gerber-Shiu expected discounted penalty function, which include e.g. the area under the curve of the surplus process until ruin, the amount of time the surplus stays within a certain range before ruin, and the discounted small perturbations of the insurer’s surplus until ruin that are not accounted for by insurance claims. To compute the (joint) moments of the above variables by developing recursive algorithms in terms of the order of moments, which can be used to fit the full (joint) distributions using moment-based approximations or other related statistical methods. To approximate the distribution of the average surplus before ruin using the Gerber-Shiu function containing the area under curve, and to perform analytical and numerical study of convergence. To analyze whether the above ruin-related quantities tend to move in the same or opposite directions using covariances and correlations that are readily obtainable from their joint moments, allowing better assessment of risks faced by the insurance companies. To apply the derived information on the average surplus before ruin and occupation times (and hence maximum/minimum surplus levels before ruin) to gain economic insights for making business decisions of setting aside the right amount of capital. To extend the above study to risk processes with dependencies among claim amounts and/or their inter-arrival times and to analyze the effect of dependency along with some probabilistic interpretations. To extend the above study to allow cash flows such as dividend payments, taxation and capital injections, resulting in better strategies on dividend and reinsurance implemented by the insurers.

17324016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17324016.value: The proposed project is about insurance risk theory, which involves the application of mathematical tools and statistical models to assess how the income (e.g. premium) and expenses (e.g. claims) of an insurance company affect its financial status. From a risk management point of view, it is very important for an insurer to ensure that there is sufficient capital to deal with adverse claims experience. Risk theory provides solid and quantitative ways of measuring risks, leading to risk measures such as the probability that the company ever defaults, the time of default, and the amount of shortfall (or deficit) in case of bankruptcy. Much of the above information is contained in a mathematical function known as the Gerber-Shiu expected discounted penalty function introduced in 1998. Over the years, researchers have been mostly studying the classical Gerber-Shiu function, which involves information of random variables defined only at the time of ruin. In order to gain insights on how the undesirable incident of default could be caused by a series of events, in this project we propose to extend the Gerber-Shiu function by accommodating additional random variables that depend on the entire evolution of the insurer’s surplus. For example, we are interested in the time duration that the surplus level stays within a certain range before default (e.g. higher than a safety level or lower than a critical level) as well as the maximum, minimum and average surplus levels before ruin. Although a higher surplus level keeps the company further away from bankruptcy, the opportunity cost of maintaining unnecessarily large amount of capital is high. Therefore, the study of these ruin-related quantities is important for the insurer to strike an appropriate balance when making business decisions, and it will also be interesting to see whether these random variables tend to move in the same or opposite directions. The above analysis will be first performed under some simple model assumptions at the very beginning of the project, and then refinements will be made to better reflect reality. In particular, we will consider risk processes involving dependence between the claim amounts and/or the elapsed times between claims. In addition, other provisions such as dividend distribution to shareholders, government taxation on profits and risk sharing via reinsurance will be incorporated into the model as well. The present values of cash flows resulting from these provisions can also be jointly analyzed with the afore-mentioned ruin-related quantities. 我們提出的研究項目是關於保險風險理論，當中會涉及到利用數學工具和統計模型來評估保險公司的收入（如保費）和支出（如索賠）如何影響其財務狀況。從風險管理的角度來看，保險公司必須確保有足夠資金來應付可能發生的大額保險賠償。風險理論提供了穩固和定量的方法來衡量風險，從而衍生出各種風險度量，如公司的破產概率、破產時間以及破產時的虧損。在一九九八年推出的Gerber-Shiu期望折現罰金函數正載有大部份上述信息。 多年來，大部份研究人員一直在研究傳統的Gerber-Shiu函數，即只包含了破產時刻的隨機變量信息的Gerber-Shiu函數。為了更深入了解一系列隨機事件是如何引致保險公司破產，我們在這個研究項目中提出在Gerber-Shiu函數中加入與保險公司資金的整個演變過程相關的隨機變量。舉例來說，我們感興趣的隨機變量包括在破產前公司資金維持在一定範圍內的時間（例如大於安全水平或低於臨界水平）以及破產前最大、最小或平均資金水平。雖然較高的資金水平可以減低公司破產的概率，但是維持過多的流動資金亦會引致很高的機會成本。因此，這些相關隨機變量的研究對商業決策非常重要，它不但能幫助保險公司在決策時取得不同範疇之間的適當平衡，還能讓我們了解到這些隨機變量之間的相關性，是同向還是反向變動。 在項目的開始階段我們首先會根據一些簡單的模型假設展開上述分析，然後我們會進一步完善模型使其能更複雜、更能準確反映現實。我們會特別考慮賠償額度和索賠間隔時間具有相關性的風險模型。此外，我們亦會把其他模型伸延納入其中，如公司對股東的紅利分配、政府對公司利潤的稅收或公司通過再保險與其他再保公司分擔風險。我們也可以將這些事件所導致的現金流量的現值併合與破產相關的隨機變量一同分析。

17324016.value: During the entire period of the project, CI Cheung (who was originally the PI before leaving the University of Hong Kong to join the University of New South Wales in July 2017) has published 8 research papers that are supported by this research grant, and the grant is acknowledged in all these publications). The realization of the objectives is summarized below (in relation to the publications in Part C of the report, and the numbering of publications follows that in Part C). • The 1st objective (about accommodating path-dependent random variables into the Gerber-Shiu expected discounted penalty function) has been addressed in the publication items 2, 4, 6 and 8. • The 2nd objective (about computing the (joint) moments of the path dependent variables) has been addressed in the publication items 4 and 6. • The 3rd objective (about approximating the distribution of the average surplus before ruin) has been addressed in the publication item 4. • The 4th objective (about analyzing covariances and correlations of path-dependent variables) has been addressed in the publication items 4 and 6. • The 5th objective (about gaining economic insights for making business decisions) has been addressed in the publication items 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8. • The 6th objective (about extending the study to risk processes with dependencies) has been addressed in the publication items 4 and 5. • The 7th objective (about extending the study to allow cash flows such as dividend payments, taxation and capital injections) has been addressed in the publication items 1, 2, 3 and 7. Therefore, all the project objectives have been achieved.

17324016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17324016.value: CI Cheung has produced a total of 8 research outputs as a result of this research grant. In particular, 1 of them was published in European Journal of Operational Research, which is a top journal in operations research. 4 of the outputs were published in top journals in Actuarial Science, which include 1 in Insurance: Mathematics and Economics, 1 in ASTIN Bulletin, and 2 in the Scandinavian Actuarial Journal. The interdisciplinary nature of the project and the outputs is also evident in the output items 2 and 6 published in optimization and applied mathematics journals respectively. The major findings are concerned with the analysis of path-dependent ruin-related quantities in insurance risk theory and their joint behaviour, and this could be be done via Gerber-Shiu type functions. For example, output 6 studies the joint moments of the discounted gains and discounted losses, and it is demonstrated that the sign of the correlation depends on whether the interclaim times are light-tailed or heavy-tailed. Output 4 proposes the use of fluid queue to analyze a risk model with Incurred But Not Reported and Reported But Not Settled Claims, and the correlation of related claims is also studied. Other path-dependent quantities in the project include for example dividends (outputs 1, 2 and 7) and capital injections (output 3). In particular, output 4 proposes a new periodic capital injection scheme, and it is shown that purchasing a reinsurance contract that injects capital at appropriate moment can effectively reduce insurer’s ruin probability. Moreover, output 7 proposes a novel periodic dividend strategy that allows for a ruin probability of less than one (as opposed to other periodic dividend strategies that commonly lead to certain ruin). These findings can potentially lead to better business decisions. In most numerical illustrations, we are also able to provide probabilistic interpretation of the results.

17324016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17324016.value: While the funded project focuses on path-dependent quantities in insurance risk theory, the ideas and techniques developed in the project can possibly be applicable to related areas such as operations research applied probability and queueing systems. The stochastic models in these related areas often bear similarities with those in actuarial science. In particular, these processes are subject to random upward jumps and/or random downward jumps, and decision parameters may be updated and controlled to optimize certain objective function possibly under some constraints. It will be important to discuss these ideas with other researchers in conferences and seminars and explore the opportunities for international collaboration.

17324016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17324016.value: Insurance companies need to ensure that it has the capacity to fulfill its obligations to deal with adverse and unexpected claims experience. The traditional ruin probability, which is the chance that the insurer ever becomes bankrupt, may no longer be sufficient for quantifying the risk faced by the insurer. In order for the companies to better manage risks and to make better business decisions, the analysis of more exotic quantities, such as those that depend strongly on how the surplus evolves, becomes crucial. The funded research project has proposed new models, new quantities and new techniques to analyze these exotic quantities, which help solve important problems such as determining whether ruin-related quantities tend to move in the same or in opposite directions; how capital can be injected to reduce risk; and how dividend payments can be paid to the shareholders in an optimal way.

17324516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17324516.value: 再保險是由保險公司購買保險。由於沒有保險證券和適用的套期工具，再保險實質上是保險公司責任風險管理的唯一有效手段。它在保險業有一個重要的和根本性的作用。分出公司的最終目標是通過傳遞一部分風險給再保險公司，以減少他們的責任風險。通過適當的再保險安排，分出公司能夠創造更易於管理的保險風險和投資組合。這反過來會降低投資組合結果的可變性，從而導致一個更可預測和更流暢的收入現金流。再保險是實現這些目標的主要工具，它是非常重要的研究，以系統和科學的方法，優化設計和再保險合同的定價，也是再保險市場的最佳結構。這就解釋了為什麼優化再保險決策問題長期以來一直是在經濟理論和精算學最熱門的研究課題之一。 這一研究項目旨在加強我們從數學和經濟的角度對再保險市場的運作的理解。這研究有兩個主要目標。第一個是繼續並通過提出和分析更現實的再保險模型概括最優再保險標準方面的研究，使理論成果可以有更大的實際意義。我們建議通過整合和研究再保險兩個非常現實但在現有的文獻大多沒有實現的基本特徵，即要求到達的隨機性，以及潛在風險的不確定性分佈的存在。我們將制定和研究（一）動態優化再保險模型，及（二）柏拉圖最優再保險模型，分別解決這兩個問題。第二個目標是了解保險公司與再保險公司之間的相互作用。我們提出了再保險公司以最佳設計他們的再保險合同的菜單和以最佳的價格合同健全科學的框架。我們也會研究再保險公司和保險公司協商如何實現互惠互利的再保險安排的機制。我們建議通過制定和分析​​幾種模式，即（一）優化再保險定價模型，（二）帕累托最優再保險模型，以及（三）根據逆向選擇最佳的再保險設計，以實現這一目標。在這個項目中獲得的模型和理論結果可為保險業更有效的風險管理提供了科學依據。

17324516.label: Realisation of objectives
17324516.value: Overall speaking, the project has been executed satisfactorily, with most of its objectives achieved fully. Objective 1. This is partially achieved. It turns out that a fully dynamic reinsurance design with stochastic claim arrival times requires much preparatory results and a deeper understanding on how the heterogeneity of discounted claim severities arising from the stochastic arrival times affect the overall risk of the insurance portfolio. The problem is non-trivial because one must take care of the possible dependence of the claim occurrence probabilities and claim severities. This problem was fully studied in output #2. Under the assumption that the claim occurrence probabilities are left tail weakly stochastic arrangement increasing, two commonly adopted dependence structures have been fully analyzed, namely, when claim severities are comonotonic or right tail weakly stochastic arrangement increasing. Since it is natural to impose the budget constraints when one consider optimal reinsurance problems, a fundamental problem to tackle is the minimization of separable convex functions subject to linear constraints. This problem was completely solved in #10 by a probabilistic method, which yielded concrete expression of the solutions in terms of the distribution functions of some random vectors that represent the convex functions. Due to the limitation of time, application of such results to examine the problem of optimal reinsurance design with stochastic arrival times is still in progress. Objective 2. This is fully achieved. The robustness of Value-at-Risk and expected shortfall (two most commonly used risk measures in the finance and insurance industries), and how they should be modified under model uncertainties were fully addressed in output #7. The model and risk preference uncertainty was then incorporated in output #1 and output #4 (under budget or risk constraints). In output #1, the robust optimization was solved by linear programming techniques after discretization, while in output #4, the objective and constraint functions admitted the so-called Kusuoka’s integral representations. The minimax theorem for infinite dimensional spaces was applied to interchange the infimum on the space of indemnities and the supremum on the space of probability measures. The resulting infimum was then solved by using the Neyman–Pearson methodology. In both outputs, analytic and transparent expressions for the optimal reinsurance policy were derived. Objective 3. This is fully achieved. Bowley solution (also known as Stackelberg equilibria) of equilibrium reinsurance pricing were extended from the traditional expected utility framework to the modern risk management framework in output #5 and output #10. In both outputs, we adopted the setting of general premium principle for the reinsurer and distortion risk measure for the insurer, which covers most of the models studied in the literature. In output #10, Bowley solutions were derived under asymmetric information. Both the optimal pricing kernel for the insurer and the optimal ceded loss function for the reinsurer were determined. Objective 4. This is fully achieved. The problem of designing reinsurance contracts in terms of Pareto optimality under various practical constraints was fully addressed in output #1. Pareto optimal contracts, with indemnity schedule and premium payment, were solved in the cases when the risk preferences of the buyer and seller are given by Value-at-Risk or Tail Value-at-Risk. The effect of the constraints and the relative bargaining powers of the buyer and seller on the Pareto optimal insurance contracts were highlighted. It was demonstrated that robust optimal contracts may not be Pareto optimal. Numerical methods were developed for constructing insurance contracts that are Pareto and robust optimal. Objective 5. This is fully achieved. In output #3, the reinsurer (principal) aims to maximize his average profit, under information asymmetry, by designing an optimal policy provision (menu) of reinsurance contracts for every insurer from one of the two groups with hidden characteristics. The insurers were assumed to adopt Value-at-Risk as their risk preference as stipulated by Solvency II. The problem was then extended to more general concave distortion risk measures in output #8. In both outputs, the problems were solved analytically, and many interesting economic insights were gained.

17324516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17324516.value: Key findings are summarized here: (Objective 1, outputs #2, #10) If claim occurrence probabilities are left tail weakly stochastic arrangement increasing, and that claim severities are comonotonic or right tail weakly stochastic arrangement increasing, an insurance portfolio with the largest vector of scale parameters in the sense of the majorization order often turns out to be more dangerous for the insurer. The constrained minimization of separable convex functions was solve by a probabilistic method, and was applied to a myriad of capital allocation problems in insurance and finance. (Objective 2, outputs #1, #4, #6, #7) Two robust methods were proposed, namely the worst-case and worst-regret. We showed that the worst-case method outperforms the worst-regret method for CVaR-based decisions. The worst-case method proved to be more robust than the worst-case CVaR method proposed by Zhu and Fukushima (2009). We demonstrated that the VaR-based decisions were not efficiently robustified for all sample sizes, and in robust optimization the optimal decision may be economically unacceptable. We resolved this issue by devising a numerical scheme to identify an optimal Pareto and robust decision that was efficient for reducing the model risk. Robustness of VaR was also examined from an extreme perspective under the realistic dependence of upper tail comonotonicity. (Objective 3, outputs #5, #10) Under general assumptions on the premium principles and risk measures, both the optimal pricing kernel for the insurer and the optimal ceded loss function for the reinsurer were determined. Bowley solutions were then derived under asymmetric information. We showed that the optimal ceded loss function has the form of layer reinsurance, depending on the cost coefficient and the structures of the distortion functions. In contrast to the case with symmetric information, the insurer may strictly benefit from buying reinsurance. Asymmetric information is a natural framework for reciprocal contracts. (Objective 4, outputs #1) Pareto optimal contracts were solved in the cases when the risk preferences of the buyer and seller are given by VaR or TVaR. The effect of the constraints and the relative bargaining powers of the buyer and seller on the Pareto optimal insurance contracts were investigated. A numerical scheme was devised to further study the case of TVaR and the Proportional Hazard Transformation; reasonable interpretations were obtained. (Objective 5, outputs #3, #8) In general, the high-risk agents might mimic the low-risk agents to enjoy a lower reinsurance cost. The reinsurer has to provide an incentive to the high-risk agents to avoid this problem. When the expected profit from the low-risk group cannot compensate the incentive cost provided to the high-risk group, the reinsurer has to give up the low-risk market. When the difference between the losses of the two groups is large while the reinsurer wants to keep the low-risk market, the coverage of the policy for the low-risk group has to be reduced via quota-share arrangement. The results reveal the inadequacy of deductible policy and the importance of introducing a quota-share component in a market with adverse selection. All results have been published in top international journals in actuarial science/optimization.

17324516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17324516.value: (1) Optimal reinsurance models with multiple constraints. In almost all existing literature, only one risk/budget constraint is imposed. The problem of dealing with multiple constraints simultaneously is known to be a difficult problem, as current methodologies in optimal reinsurance cannot effectively handle it. Yet, it is rather important to have be able to model various practical constraints at the same time and examine how they affect the reinsurance arrangement. Possible methods include framing the problem in an infinite-dimensional linear programming problem, and then examining the dual problem, which is then a finite-dimensional convex minimization problem. The high-dimensional Neyman-Person type results might also be useful. (2) In outputs #3 and #8, only the case of two types of possible hidden information was studied. It would be mathematically challenging, yet of practical relevance, to examiner the situation when there are more than two types of agents, or even a continuum of types in the extreme. The difficulty of course is then to tackle the infinite-dimensional individual-rationality and individual-compatibility constraints. Following existing literature in mechanism design in Economics, transformation using indirect utility might simplify the problem.

17324516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17324516.value: Reinsurance is insurance purchased by insurance companies. It plays a vital and fundamental role in the insurance industry by helping insurance companies better manage their risk. Hence it is very important to study systematically and scientifically the optimal design and pricing of reinsurance contracts, and also the optimal structures of the reinsurance markets. This project aims at enhancing our understanding and deepen our insights for the functioning of reinsurance markets from the mathematical and economic perspective. We can gain deeper understanding of (1) how the decisions of insurance companies and reinsurance companies are affected by their risk preference and their perception of the accuracy of the model assumptions, (2) what kind of reinsurance arrangements are mutually beneficial and optimal to both the insurance companies and reinsurance companies, (3) how a menu of reinsurance contracts is designed and priced. This project answers the above important questions by using modern economic and mathematical techniques. The models and results obtained can provide a firm scientific basis for a more effective and efficient risk management in the insurance industry.

17325416.label: Project Objectives
17325416.value: Study the probability properties of the linear double autoregressive model. This will be achieved by introducing the new model, and deriving the conditions for the existence of the strictly stationary solution to the new model. We will also discuss the available parameter space, and hopefully the original novel properties of the double autoregressive model can be preserved. Develop an estimating method for the new model. This will be achieved by considering a new composite quantile estimation, based on a doubly weighted approach. One set of weights are used to improve the efficiency of the estimator as in the weighted composite quantile estimation. The other set of weights are used to remove the restriction of moment since the first order moment is necessary for the commonly used quantile estimation. Develop a diagnostic tool to check for the adequacy of the fitted linear double autoregressive model. This will be achieved by applying the quantile autocorrelation. Computer programs will be developed to study the large-sample property and the finite-sample performance of results in Objectives 1-3 and applications to real data such as the estimation of VaR will be considered. Clearly, the objectives only reflect part of the possible developments in this area. Many other developments are also possible if time permits.

17325416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17325416.value: It is an important task in financial risk management to model the volatility of asset prices, and many conditional heteroscedastic models have been proposed since the appearance of ARCH model in 1982. Recently the double autoregressive model has attracted more and more attentions due to its simple and flexible structure. In the meanwhile, many quantities used in financial management are estimated quantiles such as the value-at-risk; however, the double autoregressive model is not compatible with the quantile estimation. This motivates us to consider a new conditional heteroscedastic model, which is more suitable for quantile estimation but still enjoys the good properties of double autoregressive models. It leads us to consider the linear double autoregressive model. The probability properties of the new model are first discussed in this project. To keep the efficiency of the estimated parameters without the restriction of moment conditions, a doubly weighted composite quantile estimation is then suggested. Finally, to check for the adequacy of the fitted time series model, a diagnostic tool is constructed based on the quantile autocorrelation. 对资产价格的波动性进行建模是金融风险管理中的一个重要课题，为此自1982年ARCH模型提出以来，又陆续涌现了许许多多的条件异方差模型。特别是最近出现的双自回归模型，由于其简单灵活性逐渐引起了越来越多的注意力。同时风险管理中的许多统计量例如VaR本质上都是估计的分位数，但是双自回归模型却不能与之相对应的分位数回归兼容。因此本项目希望提出一个新的条件异方差模型，使之既能与分位数回归兼容，又兼具双自回归模型的简单灵活性。本项目命名这个新的模型为线性双自回归模型。 本项目首先讨论了新模型的概率性质，然后提出了一个双重加权的条件分位数回归估计来去掉矩条件的限制，最后构建了一个基于分位数自回归的诊断工具来检验拟合模型的充分性。

17325416.label: Realisation of objectives
17325416.value: 1) By collaborating with Dr. Qianqian Zhu and Dr. Yao Zheng (my two former PhD students), I have accomplished Objectives 1-3, and these results were summarized into a paper published at the Journal of Econometrics (No. 2 econometric journal) in 2018. 2) When working on Objective 3, motivated by referees' comments, I have reached a new idea of designing a robust diagnostic tool for conditional heteroscedastic models. It was applied to the GARCH model since it is the most commonly used conditional heteroscedastic model. This piece of work was published at Biometrika (one of top 4 statistical journals) in 2018. 3) When working on this project, I have also considered a diagnostic tool for parametric quantile regression models, which is also called the lack-of-fit test, and it is related to Objective 5. This piece of work was published at the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (one of top 4 statistical journals) in 2019. 4) Along the lines of Objective 3, I have applied the bootstrap method to the robust inference (least absolute deviation method) for GARCH models, and this piece of work was published at the Journal of Time Series Analysis in 2020. 5) In the process of this project, Objective 2 gave us a sparkle of unbalanced designs, which, together with our previous work (Wu and Li, 2004), leads to a moment-based test for random effect in an unbalanced panel data. This is related to Objective 5. This piece of work was published at the Economic Modelling in 2018. 6) Objective 4 is about computer program, and it is involved in all research papers mentioned in the above. Especially Dr. Q Zhu, Dr. Y Zheng, Dr. J Wu and Dr. C Dong have contributed a lot to this objective.

17325416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17325416.value: 1) This project proposed a new conditional heteroscedastic model, which is with a conditional mean structure but compatible with the quantile regression, and its complete inference tools have also been established. This finding was published at the Journal of Econometrics (No. 2 econometric journal). Refer to Zhu, Zheng and Li (2018) at Part C. 2) This project proposed a robust diagnostic tool by first transforming residuals with a bound function. This finding was published at Biometrika (one of top 4 statistical journals). Refer to Zheng, Li and Li (2018) at Part C. 3)This project proposed a novel lack-of-fit test for parametric quantile regression, which is conducted by checking the equality of two conditional distributions of covariates. This finding was published at the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (one of top 4 statistical journals). Refer to Dong, Feng and Li (2019). 4) The generalized bootstrap method was applied to approximate the least absolute deviation-based diagnostic tool for GARCH models. This finding was published at the Journal of Time Series Analysis. Refer to Zhu, Zeng and Li (2020). 5) This project extended Wu and Li (2014)’s moment-based tests for random effects to the case with unbalanced panel data. This finding was published at the Economic Modelling. Refer to Wu, Li and Xia (2018).

17325416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17325416.value: The proposed linear double autoregressive time series model required a very little moment of time series, and it hence can be applied to very heavy-tailed time series, which is commonly encountered in real applications. Moreover, we may further introduce the asymmetry into the model, say to proposed an asymmetric linear double autoregressive model. Finally we may consider multivariate linear autoregressive models, or even high-dimensional models.

17325416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17325416.value: It is an important task in financial risk management to model the volatility of asset prices, and many quantities used in financial management are estimated quantiles such as the value-at-risk. While the existing toolbox in the literature is lack of such type of tools. This project constructed a new conditional heteroscedastic model, the linear double AR model, and it is suitable for quantile inference even when there is a conditional mean component. It can be regarded as a modification of the double AR model along the lines of the linear GARCH model, but enjoys greater tractability for the quantile regression than both models. This project has added an important tool into the toolbox, and the proposed model is supposed to play an important role in the literature.

17325516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17325516.value: Hydrological variations in response to a changing climate could be very different in various regions that are dominated by different circulation systems. The rainfall brought by East Asian monsoon feeds a large population of people in this area. Therefore, studies of how monsoonal rainfall changed under past natural climate variability could provide useful clues to future changes in an anthropogenic era. It is of particular importance for those water-stressed regions, where any further reduction of rainfall would cause devastating effects. Previous studies support a general notion that over the last millennium wet conditions persisted during cool periods in regions dominated by the westerly circulation system (i.e. northwestern China), but during warm periods in regions dominated by the Asian monsoonal circulation system (eastern China). However, at the boundary between the two circulation systems, commonly defined as the 300 mm annual rainfall line, existing results appear to be controversial and further investigation is required in order to better understand hydroclimatic changes in the marginal regions. Here we propose to investigate hydroclimatic variations in the marginal region over the last millennium by reconstructing biomarker records from lacustrine sediments. Building on previous success in reconstructing hydroclimatic changes in the westerly-dominated Qaidam Basin (supported by RGC GRF), we will extend the biomarker approach to the marginal monsoon area. Biomarkers to be analyzed include alkenones, GDGTs and n-alkanes. We aim to infer hydrological changes based on the percentage of alkenone C37:4, with the supplement of n-alkane distribution pattern and the GDGT-ACE index, and temperature changes from the alkenone unsaturation index (UK’37), with the supplement of the tetraether index (TEX86) and the soil temperature index (MBT/CBT). We will collect surface lake sediments to validate the proxies proposed to be used in this region and take short sediment cores from selected lakes. Key issues we hope to address include: How did the moisture and temperature vary over the last millennium in the marginal monsoon area? What are the relationships between the moisture and temperature changes? Has the boundary between the westerly and monsoon circulation systems shifted over time? Can the regional moisture and temperature changes be linked sunlight changes? Our preliminary results from three lakes, Daihai, Huangqihai and Qinghai suggest that major scientific objectives can be successfully achieved. 在不同環流系統控制的區域，由氣候變化引起的水文變化不盡相同。東亞地區大量的人口利用夏季風帶來的降雨。 因此， 研究過去的自然氣候變化說引起的區域水文變化有利於我們預測將來的水文變化。水文變化對水資源缺乏的區域尤其重要，任何進一步的降雨減少會導致災難性的後果。前人的研究結果支持近千年來在由西風環流控制的中國西北乾旱區氣候偏冷時期較濕潤，而在亞洲季風環流控制的東亞地區氣候偏暖時期較濕潤。而在兩環流的邊界區，通常定義為300毫米年降雨區，現有的研究結果並不一致，因此有必要進一步的研究季風邊緣區的水文變化。 這裡我們想從湖泊沉積物中利用生物標誌物來調查近千年來季風邊緣區的水文氣候變化。 建立於我們以前成功地利用生標重建中國西北乾旱區柴達木盆地裡的水文變化的基礎上 （由香港RGC資助），我們把這一套研究方法延伸到季風邊緣區。將要分析的生物標誌物包括長鏈烯酮，GDGT和直鏈烷烴。我們試圖以長鏈烯酮的C37:4含量，並輔以直鏈烷烴的分佈特徵和GDGT-ACE 的指標，來重建過去的水文變化。以長鏈烯酮的不飽和度(UK’37)， 並輔以GDGT的TEX86和MBT/CBT指標，來重建近千年來季風區的溫度變化。我們將採集湖泊表層沉積物來驗證指標的可靠性，並選擇理想湖泊以獲取沉積柱恢復過去的水文變化。我們希望能研究的關鍵問題包括：近千年來季風邊緣區的水汽和溫度是怎樣變化的？水汽和溫度變化的關係是怎樣的？ 西風和季風環流的邊界線有沒有隨時間變化？此區域的水汽和溫度變化是否能和太陽輻射的變化聯繫上？ 我們從岱海，黃旗海和青海的初步研究結果顯示此項研究能成功解答這些科學問題。

17325516.label: Realisation of objectives
17325516.value: During the investigation period, we have extended collection of lake surface sediments to northwestern China and Central Asia (Southwest Siberia) through collaborations with mainland China and Russian scientists. We have also taken sediment cores in the marginal monsoon area to investigate moisture and temperature changes over the last millennium. All the proposed objectives in this project have been successfully achieved. Objective # 1: We have collected more than 50 lake surface sediments from monsoon margin to northwestern China to southwestern Siberia. With the large dataset, we have systematically how alknenone and GDGT biomakers respond to environmental parameters, temperature, salinity and lake water depth in particular, which provides basis for downcore reconstructions. The studies of lake surface sediments have resulted in two publications (Output # 3 and 7 in Part C), with two additional manuscripts in review. Objective # 2: We have retrieved sediment cores from three lakes, Lake Bayinluori, Daihai and Juyanze, and analyzed alkenones in sediments, along with some XRF-scanning results to infer temperature and moisture changes over the last millennium. The preliminary results from Lake Qinghai has been published (Output # 1) and the remaining results are in preparation for scientific publication. Objective # 3: Based on the alkenone results from the three lakes, it appears that moisture changes in the marginal region follows the monsoonal pattern, that is, enhanced monsoon circulation and moisture in relatively warm periods and reduced moisture in cool periods. Objective # 4: Based on the result from Lake Juyanze, located to the west of the monsoon boundary (the 300 mm annual rainfall line), it appears that during the Medieval Warm Period, the monsoonal limit did shift northwestward. The results from all three lakes suggest substantially enhanced monsoon circulation and moisture during the Medieval Warm Period. One technical issue here is that large carbon reservoir effect existed in Lake Juyanze so that a reliable chronology has not been established yet. We are working on this issue by dating additional sediment samples from this lake. Inspired by this carbon reservoir issue, we have also studied how carbon reservoir ages changed with lake status over the last millennium, which has been published (Output # 8). The result helps selection of sediments for radiocarbon dating. Objective # 5: Assessing whether moisture changes are associated with TSI changes largely relies on the accuracy of constructed chronology. We consider that the constructed chronology from Lake Daihai is reliable and in turn the moisture and temperature records from this lake do suggest that both moisture and temperature changes were associated with sunlight changes. We have found that not only the general temperature and moisture background during the Medieval Warm Period but also the fluctuations within this period corresponded to sunlight changes. Objective # 6: One PhD student, partially supported by this project, submitted his thesis in August 2020 and just passed his oral exam this month.

17325516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17325516.value: Major findings and research outcome could be summarized as follows: 1. We have found that the salinity indicators, alkenone %C37:4 and the GDGT-based ACE index can be used for downcore salinity reconstructions (Output # 7); the GDGT-based %Thaum index can indicate lake water depth (Output # 3); the isomerization of brGDGTs is strongly related to lake salinity and thus could be used a new salinity indicator, which also implies that the recently proposed temperature proxy MBT'5ME could be potentially impacted by salinity changes (manuscript in review). 2. The results consistently suggest that at the monsoonal margins, enhanced moisture did occur during warm periods following the monsoonal pattern (enhanced moisture associated with warm conditions, Output # 1), and the monsoonal limit likely shifted northwestward during the Medieval Warm Period. 3. We have found that the downcore reservoir ages changed with lake status/water depth, which could be eventually linked to the relative amount of terrestrial old carbon input (Output # 8). 4. We have extended our research region to Chinese marginal seas and found that Asian summer monsoon (# 2) , winter monsoon (# 5) and ocean current (Yellow Sea Warm Current) (# 4), as well as tropical cyclones (# 6), have systematically responded to global climatic changes over the last millennium. During relatively warm periods, summer monsoon and tropical cyclones strengthened while winter monsoon and ocean current weakened.

17325516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17325516.value: During this investigation, we have discovered two unexpected/novel features. First, it appears that Asian summer monsoon was particularly strengthened around 4000-3000 years ago, the so-called Middle Bronze Age. This is opposite to the presumed cool/dry conditions in current literature, and such assumed climatic context is used in studies of human-environment interactions. We have developed a new RGC proposal to investigate monsoonal behavior during this particular period. Second, we note that moisture changes are generally coupled with temperature changes in both westerlies and monsoon regions, despite different associations. However, during climatic transitions from one state to another, this association could be temporarily broken down. This has important implications for terrestrial lake temperatures, which could be delayed due to lake processes. We plan to investigate this phenomenon in future.

17326116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17326116.value: Planetary Nebulae (PNe) are among the least understood of celestial phenomena, being transient shells of glowing gas made when ordinary stars convulse and die. They form when a dying red giant star expels its atmosphere, and the exposed hot core ionizes the surrounding gas. Despite being a common end-point of stellar evolution, many aspects of their formation and evolution are very poorly understood. This project uses the first complete census of PNe in the local universe to shed light on the many physical processes that occur when a star reaches the end of its life, and how PNe influence the chemical evolution of the Milky Way. This project will be a major advance in our understanding of late-stage stellar evolution. Determining the ages, masses, and chemical compositions of a complete census of PNe has never been possible before but it is the key to understanding how low to intermediate mass stars influence the evolution of our Galaxy. The full evolutionary status, type and abundance range of the phenomena needs to be studied if their true nature and property diversity are to be properly understood. This proposal will be able to uniquely achieve this via a detailed, multi-parameter population analysis of the most robust "local volume" sample of Galactic planetary nebulae ever compiled that is near complete in various distance sub-samples. It can can be considered as the first true 'archaeological' study of these objects and their progenitor stars as our meticulously acquired and carefully vetted data over many years is put to scientific use. Such an analysis is needed to address a number of key questions in our understanding of the death of mid-mass stars as outlined in this proposal. 行星狀星雲（PNe）是目前了解最少的天文現象之一，是當普通恆星震動和死亡時製成的發光氣體。它們是由一個垂死的紅巨星排出氣層，並由其熱核心電離周圍的氣體而形成。儘管PNe是恆星的一個共同終點，我們對它們的眾多方面的形成和演化都了解甚少。本項目採用PNe在本地宇宙的第一個完整普查去研究壽命末期的恆星發生的許多物理過程，及PNe如何影響銀河系的化學演化。這項目將是我們對後期恆星演化的一個重大進展。PNe的全面普查的完成之前，確定PNe的年齡、質量和化學原素是沒有可能的，但這些關鍵因素對於理解低到中等質量恆星如何影響我們的銀河系的演變十分重要。要是我們要真正理解PNe的真實性質和多樣性，完整的進化狀態、類型和豐度量程等現像都需要被研究。這提案將能針對這接近完成的眾多“本地”銀河行星狀星雲樣品進行詳細，多參數的分析。這些經過多年的精心採集，並經過精挑細選數據將可被視為第一個對這些行星狀星雲和前身星的“考古”研究，並放置到科研上使用。我們需要這種的分析以解決我們在本建議中概述中對中等質量恆星死亡的一些關鍵問題。

17326116.label: Realisation of objectives
17326116.value: This GRF was the first awarded to my group when we moved from Australia to HKU in March 2015. During early 2017 the previous project PI Dr. D. J. Frew left HKU only 2 years into a 3 year RAP appointment to return to Australia for family reasons. He also permanently left this research field. This left an enormous hole in the available project effort, especially in terms of management and supervision. This has not filled at a more senior level, several years later in terms of lost project capacity. This is particularly given Dr Frew's profound in depth knowledge and enormous expertise. Though it was still possible to make project progress in his absence as I took over as project PI this was not, understandably, at the level originally hoped for given my already distributed effort. As a result some of the original objectives were only partially met by the official end of the project. However some have at least partially been folded into the current PIs related GRF projects under the overall research umbrella of late stage stellar evolution that remains an overall highly productive endeavour at HKU. Of course all project objectives were originally made on the assumption that the full requested grant funding of $1,265,012 requested was awarded. However, this was not the case. Only $554K over 3 years was awarded. This amounts to ~44% of the original request. This was insufficient to pay for a full time postdoc to work fully on the project over the 3 years of the grant. Hence, other funding was used to employ a full-time postdoc that could only be partially supported by this grant. Hence, effort to this project was only possible on a pro-rata basis. This also effected project progress in meeting the original objectives. As this was our first GRF grant the implications of the typically reduced funding under the GRF scheme was not appreciated before so our objectives turned out to be more ambitious than allocated resources permit in practice. Specific comments on each objective are given below. Objective 1. Progress on objective one under previous PI Frew relied heavily on his collaboration with colleague Orsola de Marco at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia. This connection was broken with the departure of previous PI Frew. As a result progress on this specific objective essentially stopped so I would now rate this objective as only completed at the level of ~20% with little immediate prospect of improvement. Objective 2; Some modest progress with this objective, which is closely related to objective one, was also possible and I again rate the completion level at ~20%. Again, the prospect of immediate further progress is limited without additional resources. Objective 3; Good progress has been made with this objective. Although the overall objective is ambitious the first two parts of uncovering the demographics of the Galactic planetary nebula population, and to better understand their physical properties has been largely accomplished. This is thanks to the on-going development of the HASH research platform (Hong-Kong AAO Strasbourg H-alpha Planetary Nebula project). This globally significant resource, developed at HKU under the umbrella of this project in particular since 2016/17, has now has more than 400 registered users in more than 30 countries (see HASH PN Database4.6: http://hashpn.space). HASH is the most tangible legacy of this GRF project and has had the most impact. A major refereed journal publication is in train for this but two conference papers on the HASH resource lead by the PI have already accrued 51 and 8 citations respectively. Objective 4 has been effectively realised already based on our own and independent work. Effectively it has been shown that stars of at least 1 solar mass will go through a Planetary Nebula phase.

17326116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17326116.value: Over the full project period the late-stage stellar evolution group, under the leadership of current PI Parker, has published a number of directly relevant papers. One major paper actually appeared under this project between the project original submission period and the award itself: D. J. Frew, Q. A. Parker, and I. S. Bojicic, 2016, "The Hα surface brightness- radius relation: a robust statistical distance indicator for planetary nebulae"; Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 455:1459–1488. This is a seminal RAE 4* paper that already has amassed ~130 citations and helped set the scene for the project and received world wide publicity. The major research outcome from the project is the provision, to the global community working in the field of late stage stellar evolution, of the HASH (Hong Kong/ AAO/ Strasbourg H-alpha Planetary Nebula) research platform and database. This resource has more than 400 users across 30+ countries and delivers citations and global exposure to HKU's Planetary Nebulae research group. Three refereed papers and three conference papers (as reported) form the published outputs from this GRF. One refereed paper, led by the current PIs previous PhD student, concerns the use of radio observations to uncover otherwise hard to locate Planetary Nebula. This paper points the way to further discoveries and exploitation of extant radio surveys. Another referred journal paper from our group, lead by the PhD student of my closest collaborator Prof. A.Zijlstra (who is a CI on several of my later GRF grants and a Hung Hing Ying distinguished visiting Professor to HKU), concerns addressing the Planetary Nebulae binary fraction using our access to the VPHAS+ wide-field survey of the Southern Galactic Plane. The final refereed publication concerns a paper that led last year to the submission of a successful GRF in its own right by CI Parker. It concerns the study of a Planetary Nebula in an old Galactic open star cluster. This paper made a major contribution to this field and several further publications are promised - one, a Nature astronomy paper - will be reported later for that new GRF. The three conference papers reported all concern the power, use and value of the HASH research platform.

17326116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17326116.value: Planetary Nebulae (PNe hereafter) represent a very brief (~10,000 to 30,000 years) but highly visible late evolutionary stage for stars with initial masses in the range ~1-8Msun. PNe are aalso a relatively rare but powerful population in terms of what we can learn about stellar evolution. Their ionized shells exhibit numerous and strong emission lines over a wide range of the electromagnetic spectrum. They represent highly useful “laboratories” for studying plasma physics. The Galaxy currently has a known population of about 3,600 PNe as compiled by our group and ingested into the Hong-Kong/AAO/Strasbourg Hα PNe research platform (HASH). HASH is a relational database that provides fast effective data search and manipulation for the most accurate, up-to-date and complete compendium of Galactic and Magellanic cloud PNe ever compiled (www.haspn.space). It is the major project legacy used by more than 400 users across 30+ countries. The scientific exploitation of the PNe phenomena is now, thanks to HASH on a far more robust footing having been hampered by non-PN contaminants in previous samples. This was long-standing problem but our group developed reliable processes to eliminate interlopers giving confidence that with HASH we are working with high integrity PNe samples.

17326316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17326316.value: Change-point detection plays a critical role in data processing, modeling, estimation, and inference. Most of the research work has focused on continuous data, while many applications involve data measured on a classification scale or naturally of some categorical structures. When the dimensionality of the data is high, e.g., comparable to or even larger than the sample size, existing approaches tend not to work well. We propose using a latent variable, which follows a normal or Student’s t distribution, to facilitate detection of multiple change-points with binary or polychotomous data by casting the problem into a sparse regression model. To accommodate distributional changes over time, we further propose a new homogeneity test through power enhancement, which can sequentially move through a large stream of multinomial data for surveillance. To detect regression changes, we propose a nonparametric likelihood-based approach to residual analysis in conjunction with robust rank regression. We will develop user-friendly software for free downloading to facilitate the routine use and broad application of our proposed methods. 在數據的處理、建模、估計和推斷中，變點檢測問題起着關鍵的作用。大部分相關的研究都着手於連續的數據類型，但是在實際應用中，數據可能按照分級劃分或從屬於幾個種類。當數據的維度很高時，例如，數據維度和樣本數量大小相當甚至更多，現有的方法往往表現不佳。我們提出通過使用隱性變量的方法，將問題等同於稀疏化的回歸模型，來解決在數據按兩個或多個種類劃分時的多個變點的檢測問題。為了適應統計分佈隨時間變化的情況，我們進一步提出一種增大統計效能的同質性測試，該方法可以逐個監測大量的多項型數據變量。為了檢測出回歸模型的改變，我們提出非參數下基於似然函數的殘差分析方法以及穩健的秩次回歸模型。我們會开发所提出方法的计算軟件，以進一步促進方法的廣泛使用。

17326616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17326616.value: Quantum technologies are advancing at a fast pace. Quantum machines for simulating complex systems promise to break the limits of today’s supercomputers, while small-scale quantum devices are expected to transform mobile technologies, such as smartphones and navigation systems, enabling secure communication and enhanced performances in GPS tracking and clock synchronization. However, as quantum technologies approach real-life applications, energy efficiency is bound to become a critical issue. Quantum computers will likely require effective cooling systems, whose energy costs could easily overshadow the quantum advantages. Mobile quantum devices will have to perform multiple tasks using a limited battery shared with classical applications. In many setups, implementing quantum gates will require more energy than implementing classical gates, leading to a competition between the benefits of quantum information processing and its increased energy demand. This project will identify efficient strategies that reduce the energy requirements of quantum devices to the minimum set by quantum mechanics. Previous works focused the energy requirements for the accurate implementation of individual gates. However, the opportunities for energy saving when multiple gates are connected into a circuit have remained largely unexplored so far. To identify these opportunities, we will develop a systematic optimization method for the use of energy resources in quantum circuits, providing analytical and numerical techniques. Our techniques will be applied to concrete tasks, such as searching for an item in a magnetic memory, computing the Fourier transform of a time-varying signal, and testing the response of an unknown quantum device. In collaboration with experimental partners from the Universities of Queensland, the Institute for Quantum Computing (Waterloo), and the University of Rome, we will design and implement demonstrations of novel energy-optimized strategies in photonic systems and superconducting circuits. Our project will advance the state of the art in quantum technologies, spawning new prototype experiments and catalyzing progress in the control of quantum systems. In the long term, this research will contribute to the realization of energy-efficient quantum computers, to the development of mobile quantum technologies, and to the design of quantum-enhanced detection techniques capable to probe complex systems with minimum amounts of energy. The success of the project will promote the quantum information area in Hong Kong, strengthening its position and increasing its visibility on the international scene. 量子技術正在高速的發展中。大型量子計算機有望打破當今超級計算機對於複雜系統模擬的極限；而小型量子設備則有望徹底改變諸如智能電話和導航系統等移動技術，實現安全通信并提高GPS追蹤和時鐘同步的精度。然而，當量子技術被應用於現實生活中時，其能源效率勢必將成為一個關鍵問題。量子計算機需要高效率的冷卻設備，而這些設備的高能耗極可能抵消量子計算的優勢。移動量子設備則需要通過與經典設備共享有限的電池來執行多個任務。很多情況下，實現量子羅輯門比實現經典羅輯門需要更多能源，使得我們不得不權衡其高性能與高能耗的利與弊。本項目將開發有效策略，將量子設備的能耗降至最低。先前工作集中研究實現單個量子門的能耗，而很少涉及多個量子門被接入同一量子線路時如何降低能耗。我們將填補這一空白，為能源在量子線路中的應用開發一套系統的優化方案，并提供解析的和數值的工具。我們會將該技術應用於具體案例中，如磁存儲器中的搜索，執行隨時間變化信號的傅里葉變換，測試未知信號對於量子器件的響應等。我們將於來自昆士蘭大學、滑鐵盧大學量子計算中心以及羅馬大學的實驗組合作，設計并實現光學系統和超導線路中的全新能源優化策略。本項目將推動量子技術發展，產生新的典型實驗方案，并促進量子系統控制方面的進步。從長遠角度看，我們的研究將有助於實現高效節能的量子計算機，促進移動量子技術的開發，設計通過最小能耗實現對複雜系統的精確量子探測的方案。本項目的成功將推動香港在量子信息領域的發展，穩固其地位并提高其國際影響力。

17326616.label: Realisation of objectives
17326616.value: 5.3 Realisation of objectives (Maximum 1200 words; please state how and to what extent the project objectives have been achieved; give reason for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems, if any) The objectives have been achieved to a high degree, as articulated in the following point-by-point list. [Objective 1: Optimization of energy-preserving circuits] We developed a general framework for the optimization of quantum circuits subject to general linear constraints, including in particular the constraint of energy preservation. The main result is that the performance of the optimal quantum circuit is equal to an entropic quantity, which we called the “entropy of the quantum circuit”. The general method has been published in G. Chiribella and D. Ebler, Optimal quantum networks and one-shot entropies, New J. Phys. 18 093053 (2016). Building on this method, we worked out explicit examples of its application to the problem of optimizing energy-preserving circuits, using both analytical and numerical techniques. Semidefinite programming is a top-down method, which optimizes quantum circuits as a whole. We also explored a complementary, bottom-up approach, where individual quantum operations are optimized under the constraint of energy-preservation. We identified two key ingredients in the optimal energy-preserving approximation. The first, called “Eigenstate Alignment” is a rotation within the degenerate energy eigenspaces of the target system. The second, called “Lüders Reduction” is a construction that allows us to maximize the coherence among different energy eigenstates. The results of this investigation are published in G. Chiribella and Y. Yang, Optimal quantum operations at zero energy cost, Phys. Rev. A 96, 022327 (2017). [Objective 2: Design of energy-efficient implementations] We identified the ultimate efficiency limit to the use of energy in quantum computation, developing a new architecture of quantum computer that achieves the ultimate limit up to a constant factor. We focused on reversible quantum computers, for which the energy cost associated to Landauer’s principle is zero. In this scenario, energy efficiency is measured by the amount of energy that needs to be supplied to the computer at the start of the computation. Our first key result is that the energy requirement for the implementation of a reversible quantum gate must be larger than the maximum energy change induced by that gate, divided by the square root of the error in the implementation, the error being measured by the fidelity between the operation implemented by the computer and the desired gate. This result implies that (1) the exact implementation of an energy-non-preserving gate requires infinite energy, and (2) for a fixed error, the energy requirement grows linearly with the energy scale of the system, as in the case of classical conservative computation. Our second key result is that the ultimate energy efficiency can be attained by a suitable architecture of quantum computer, consisting of a multiqubit register coupled with a quantum battery, namely a quantum system that exchanges energy with the register. We have shown that, by suitably choosing the initial state of the battery, our bound on the energy requirement can be achieved up to a constant. Remarkably, we found out that the energy requirement of quantum computation is independent of the time-complexity: in general, long computation do not require more energy than short computations. As it turns out, the key parameter determining the energy requirement is not the time complexity, but rather the space complexity: the energy requirement of a quantum computation grows linearly with the number of energy non-degenerate qubits used during the computation. For quantum computations with a classical input and a classical output, such as Shor’s algorithm, we showed that the same energy requirement is exactly the same as that of classical computations with the same inputs and outputs. In other words, the use of coherent quantum superpositions in intermediate steps of a quantum algorithm does not increase the energy requirement. For classical problems, quantum algorithms can be as energy-efficient as the most efficient classical algorithms, while at the same time offering computational speedups. The results of this investigation are written in G. Chiribella, Y. Yang, and R. Renner, The energy requirement of quantum processors, under review in Physical Review X. In addition to energy-efficient quantum computation, we have studied the optimal implementation of other quantum tasks under general conservation laws, such as conservation of the total angular momentum. [Objective 3: Development of energy-savings strategies] We focussed on energy-saving strategies for quantum communication, where the energy is related to the number of particles that have to travel from the sender to receiver. A major achievement has been the development of a new communication protocols where information is sent through noisy communication channels in a coherent superposition of alternative orders. We showed that the possibility of superposing the order of noisy processes can increase the amount of information carried by each individual particle. The results of this investigation have been published in Daniel Ebler, Sina Salek, and Giulio Chiribella, Enhanced Communication With the Assistance of Indefinite Causal Order, Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 12050 (2018) and has received 55 citations before March 31st 2020. Another major achievement has been the development of efficient tests of quantum channels. We developed a way to test quantum communication channels using a single entangled state, whose average energy is equal to the average energy of the input ensembles used by conventional methods. Our result implies that one can achieve a greatly increased statistical efficiency while maintaining the same energy requirement. The result of this investigation has been published in G. Bai and G. Chiribella, Test one to test many: a unified approach to quantum benchmarks, Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 150502 (2018) and has been highlighted by PRL as an Editors' Suggestion. [Objective 4: Extension to noisy scenarios and design of prototype demonstrations]. Coping with noise is the main challenge in the implementation of quantum information processing. In our work we investigated how energy constraints affect the ability of quantum devices to cope with noise in the surrounding environment. We developed strategies for the purification of quantum coherence at zero energy cost [G. Chiribella and Y. Yang, Optimal quantum operations at zero energy cost, Phys. Rev. A 96, 022327 (2017)], showing ways to convert noisy input states into less noisy output states exhibiting coherence between different energy levels. In addition, we identified the optimal operations for the amplification and purification of noisy coherent states, showing that the latter can be optimally implemented at zero energy cost, while the latter require an injection of photons into the system [X. Zhao and G. Chiribella, Quantum amplification and purification of noisy coherent states”, Phys. Rev. A 95, 042303 (2017)]. On the experimental side, we focussed on photonic implementations of protocols using superpositions of orders. Since the latter attracted considerable interest in the community, we faced some time pressure, which led us to omit the study of superconducting qubits, originally included in our workplan, because this platform was less compelling for the implementation of our protocols. We collaborated with the experimental team of Prof. G.-C. Guo at USTC and experimentally demonstrated high-fidelity transmission of quantum information, with fidelities as high as 98%, in close agreement with the theory. Our work has been published in Y. Guo et al, Experimental Transmission of Quantum Information Using a Superposition of Causal Orders, Phys. Rev. Lett. 124, 030502 (2020).

17326616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17326616.value: We determined the ultimate energy efficiency achievable by quantum computers, showing that, surprisingly, the minimum energy requirement does not grow with the time complexity of a computation, but only on the energy scale of the qubit on which the computer operates. We developed a new architecture that achieves the ultimate efficiency limit up to a constant factor, by recycling energy from one step of the computation to the next. In the special case of quantum computations with classical inputs and classical outputs, such as Shor's algorithm for integer factoring, we showed that the minimum energy requirement of quantum computation is exactly equal to the minimum energy requirement of a classical computation, even though the quantum computation is faster. At the fundamental level, we have developed concepts and methods for the optimization of quantum devices under constraints on the available energy. We determined how conserved quantity such as energy and angular momentum affect the storage and transmission of information, and we developed new quantum communication protocols that achieve an enhanced transmission of information for fixed energy of the transmitted signals. Some of our protocols have been experimentally realized on a photonic platform, showing an excellent agreement with the theory.

17326616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17326616.value: Our project has opened up new research directions, which are currently being pursued by our research group. Among them, a major research direction is the study of new communication protocols where information is sent along multiple paths in a coherent superposition. The study of these communication protocols has been the subject of a new GRF project (17307719), which started on 1-1-2020. At the same time, we are exploring the combination of our results on the energy requirement of quantum computation with the quantum speed limits studied earlier on in the literature. Indeed, most of our results refer to a quasi-static scenario where energy-preserving evolutions have negligible energy cost. Going beyond this idealization and adding time into the equation is important, especially for the design of realistic implementations, which need to be fast enough in order to cope with decoherence. On this front, we are currently obtaining the first preliminary results, on which we plan to build up in the coming few years. Finally, the experimental collaboration with the group of G.-C. Guo at USTC, initiated in this project, is expected to continue in the next years with the experimental demonstration of new quantum communication protocols.

17326616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17326616.value: Quantum computation promises spectacular speedups in the solution of hard computational problems. But what is the cost of these speedups in terms of energy required by the computation? Existing implementations have high operation costs, and use a considerable amount of energy even for calculations of moderate size. In principle, however, the next generations of quantum computers could achieve much higher levels of efficiency. Our project investigated the ultimate limits set by the laws of quantum mechanics to energy efficiency. We determined limits that every implementation of quantum computing will have to satisfy, no matter how technologically advanced. Our efficiency limits set the target for the future generations of quantum computers, and will play an increasingly important role in the regime where the size of the computations will become large, so that the intrinsic energy cost of the computation dominates over the cost of building and operating the hardware. In addition to quantum computation, we explored how the counterintuitive features of quantum mechanics can be harnessed to enhance the energy efficiency of quantum communication networks and quantum sensors. Our findings pave the way for new quantum technologies that achieve enhanced performances using the minimum amount of energy resources.

17327316.value: 分子束外延过渡金属硫化物薄膜的缺陷与掺杂

17327316.label: Project Objectives
17327316.value: Establishing the properties of native defects in epitaxial TMDs: Intrinsic or native defects are common in as-grown MoSe2 and WSe2 films by MBE. Some properties have already been characterized, while many others remain open. For examples, the atomic detail of inversion domain boundary in epitaxial MoSe2 is still ambiguous, the nature of the point defects in both MoSe2 and WSe2, their dependence on MBE condition, etc. remain uncharted. Here, we will perform a combinational study by experiments and theory to unlock the very nature of these defects. It is hoped that the native defects can be controlled or contained for better sample quality. Achieving intentional doping of the TMDs by impurities: To tune material’s conductivity, we shall experiment doping of TMD films by dopants or impurities. In particular, substitutional doping by transition metals that are candidates for the p- and n-type dopants will be experimented during MBE of MoSe2 and WSe2. Doping by adsorption of metals and molecular ions on surfaces will be attempted in parallel and the stability of such adsorbate will be followed. The effects of dopants on electrical, optical and magnetic properties of the material will be examined.

17327316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17327316.value: Ultrathin layers of transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are of great current research interests due to their novel electronic, optoelectronic and valley and spin electronic properties and the promise for nanodevice applications. In the past two years, the PI has employed molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE) to grow MoSe2 and WSe2 ultrathin layers from elemental sources and carried out scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/S) experiments to reveal both line and point defects in the as-grown TMD layers. These defects give rise to specific properties and some dramatic effects on TMDs. Because pristine TMD monolayer (ML) is a semiconductor, defects expectedly play important roles dictating the electronic characteristics of the material. A systematic investigation of defects in ultrathin TMDs is therefore quite relevant to the application of the materials. In this proposal, we shall probe both the intrinsic defects in as-grown TMDs and intentional dopants for their structural and electronic properties and effects. More specifically, the structural identity and formation mechanism of the common defects in as-grown TMD epifilms will firstly be investigated by combinational STM/S, high-resolution electron microscopy and density functional theory. The aim is to not only understand the defects but also contain them in order to improve the quality of the samples. Second, intentional doping of TMDs by impurity during MBE growth will be attempted with the aim of tuning material’s conductivity. In addition to the electrical effect brought about by defects/dopants, others such as magnetic and optical effects will be followed as well. This research will expectedly generate results of great scientific and practical value for future exploration of the materials in device applications. 过渡金属硫化物（TMD）薄膜由于其在电光以及自旋与谷电子学 方面特性和的应用潜质而为大家所关注。在过去的两年中，申请 人利用分子束外延方法制备了MoSe2和WSe2 薄膜并用隧穿扫描 电镜（STM/S）的手段揭示了其中的点缺陷与线缺陷及其性质。 由于TMD单原子层薄膜是半导体，材料缺陷往往决定着材料的 性质。所以，系统地研究TMD薄膜材料中的缺陷对材料的应用 是十分相关和重要的。 本项目将对分子束外延TMD薄膜中的本征缺陷及掺杂缺陷的结构 特征、电学性质和效应等进行探讨。具体上讲，我们将结合 STM/S，高分辨电子透射电镜及泛函计算等手段，对材料中常 形成的本征缺陷的结构、形成机理进行研究，其目的不仅仅在 于对其性质的理解，还要实现对它的控制，以提高材料的质量。 另外，为提高材料的导电性，我们将尝试对外延薄膜进行有意 掺杂。除了电学性质，我们也将跟踪该缺陷与掺杂给材料带来 的磁、光等效应。我们预期该项目能产生于科学和应用两方面 都有益的科研成果。

17327316.label: Realisation of objectives
17327316.value: 1. Towards objective 1, intrinsic defects, particularly that of the mirror twin domain boundaries (MTBs) in epitaxial MoSe2, have been intensively studied by combinational STM/S and STEM. In collaboration with Prof. C.H. Jin of Zhejiang University, we have also examined some point defects such as vacancies and antisites in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides. Besides establishing the structural identities of the native defects, their electronic properties have been characterized. Conditions for tuning the concentrations of various defects have also been established. The experiments were complemented/support by the DFT calculations. 2. On objective 2, intentional hole doping has been experimented by co-depositing P with Mo and Se, and by postgrowth N-plasma treatment of as-grown MoSe2. Both methods have demonstrated success of hole doping by the experimental observations that the doped P and N atoms replace Se in MoSe2, and that Fermi level shifts towards the valence band. Doping by a metal element in WSe2 during MBE is also investigated. Again, the experiments were supported by theory and DFT calculations. Although issues remain and new problems arise, e.g., new structural defects are identified, and the effectiveness of substitutional doping in monolayer TMDs and its detrimental effect on crystallinity of the films are questioned, the original objectives set out in the proposal are fully achieved. And because of the new issues/problems discovered, continuation of the project may be worthy.

17327316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17327316.value: Firstly, the atomic structure of the MTBs are firmly established (publication 2). Second, an interesting electronic structure of the 1D-MTBs are discovered - evidences are provided for the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid in graphene-supported MTBs but a Fermi liquid in a gold-supported sample, suggesting the important tunneling and/or screening effect of the substrate (publication 3). Particularly, we have ruled out the Peierls-instability induced charge density waves in the MTBs as previously reported. On hole doping, both co-deposition of P with MoSe2 and by postgrowth N-plasma treatment of as-grown samples were found successful (publication 1 and 4). However, it is also found that P is a more effective dopant for holes than N, showing a shallower impurity level. This conclusion is supported by DFT studies. On the other hand, impurity doping inevitably degrades the crystallinity of the sample, which is disadvantageous for transport applications. So special strategies still need to be explored for effective doping so as to tune the Fermi level and in the meantime maintain its crystallinity. Finally, doping by metal elements, such as Nb, has been experimented. A surprising effect of Nb doping on the MTB formation is found and explained (publication 5).

17327316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17327316.value: As elaborated above, issues remain open and worthy studying further in future. These include new structural defects found in epitaxial TMDs, some of which are related to doping. Their structures and electronic properties remain to be fully characterized. As for impurity doping, though we have found that substitutional doping can indeed be implemented by co-deposition or postgrowth treatment of the samples, a side and detrimental effect is the degradation of crystallinity, not to mention that the energy level of the dopant, especially dopant of lighter elements, are relatively large, ineffective in Fermi-level tuning. Therefore, new strategies besides by gating are still needed.

17327316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17327316.value: Single atomic-layer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as monolayer MoSe2, is an important class of two-dimensional materials that promise for future electronic applications. However, to meet the application demands, one has to minimize native defects and in the meantime, be capable of tuning the electron/hole concentrations in the materials. In this project, we set firstly to investigate the various native defects in monolayer MoSe2 grown by a technique called molecular-beam epitaxy. These include, for example, mirror twin domain boundaries and atomic vacancies. We not only established the atomic structure of these defects, but also probed their electronic properties, important for fundamental physics as well as for application purposes. Secondly, we attempted to tune the electrical carrier concentration by introducing impurities in MoSe2, and showed successful doping by phosphorous and nitrogen atoms, leading to "hole" doping in films.
