17329216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17329216.value: 基於現代保險模型的優化問題研究

17329216.label: Project Objectives
17329216.value: The first objective is to investigate the optimal capital injection, dividends and reinsurance for a risk model with the thinning dependence. Under non-cheap reinsurance and variance reinsurance premium principle, the proposed problem of study becomes more interesting but challenging. In the presence of capital injection, one can consider two suboptimal problems when the surplus goes below zero: (i) capital injection must take place; and (ii) capital injection is not a must, and hence bankruptcy is allowed. For both bounded dividend rate and unbounded dividend rates, our goal is to derive optimal results that maximize the expected discounted dividend payments minus the discounted costs of capital injection. The second objective is to study the optimal investment and reinsurance problem in a financial market with a jump-diffusion risky asset, where the insurance risk model is modulated by a compound Poisson process. The investment and insurance jump-number processes are correlated through a common shock, and the expected value of the jump size in the risky asset can be negative. The idea of making the investment and insurance processes dependent in the optimal control problem is not only new but also practically sensible especially when some human or natural disasters cause a period of economic adversity. Our plan is to derive optimal investment and reinsurance strategies under the criterion of maximizing the expected the expected exponential utility. The third project objective is to examine the optimal investment and reinsurance problem with common shock dependence in a regime-switching financial market under the mean-variance criterion. Here the market modes are divided into a finite number of regimes, and the nonnegative constraint of the investment-reinsurance policies are considered. These indeed introduce some technical difficulties since the optimal strategies derived in the usual way may not meet the restriction. It is hoped that the problem can be fixed by adding some conditions on the initial amount of wealth. Within this framework, our aim is to derive closed-form expressions for the mean-variance efficient strategies and efficient frontiers by using the techniques of stochastic linear-quadratic control.

17329216.label: Realisation of objectives
17329216.value: In the actuarial literature, the incorporation of realistic features into the basic insurance risk process has generated a lot of interesting research on optimality in the past two decades. Although many insightful results in the direction have obtained, most of them are derived under the assumption of independent risks. As the rapid growth of insurance products makes the financial analysis more and more complicated, research on the relationships between various lines of insurance risks or between investment and insurance risks is crucial to the development of more sophisticated tools for dynamic financial analysis. In reality, a natural disaster often causes various kinds of claims, and the claim sizes among different classes of business are usually positively correlated. In daily life, medical and motor insurance claims occur due to a severe car accident. These are just two obvious examples that justify the importance of the study of dependent classes of insurance business. In view of the complex nature of modern investment and insurance products, there should be many interesting and challenging optimality problems with dependence remaining to be solved. To the best of our knowledge, not much research on optimality problems with dependent risks has been done in the actuarial literature. Hence, we consider three optimality problems for risk models with certain dependence structures. The three problems are summarized in the list of objectives. For Objective 1, we investigate the problem of optimal dividends and reinsurance with capital injection in a diffusion approximation risk model with thinning-dependence structure. Here proportional reinsurance can be purchased under the variance premium principle, and a proportional transaction cost is charged for capital injection. Furthermore, we adopt non-cheap reinsurance which is more difficult to deal with. Non-cheap reinsurance under the expected value principle has been investigated in the literature. It was assumed that bankruptcy is forbidden and dividend rates are unbounded. However, in some situation, it might be unwise to prevent bankruptcy by forced capital injection. Hence, we assume that both ruin and capital injection are allowed, and study the problem for both bounded and unbounded dividend rates. For unbounded dividend rates, we consider the case with forced capital injection in the presence of proportional transaction cost whenever the reserve level drops below zero. We then scrutinize the optimal problem in the general case that capital injection is optional. Using the technique of stochastic control theory, we derive closed-form expressions for the optimal strategies and the corresponding value functions for two classes of insurance business with thinning dependence. Under the assumption of non-cheap reinsurance, we obtain results that are quite different from those existing results for both bounded and unbounded dividend rates. The study of Objective 1 has been successfully completed. The research outcomes can be found in the publication entitled "Optimal dividends and reinsurance with capital injection under thinning dependence", which appears in Part C, Item 9. For Objective 2, under the criterion of maximizing the expected utility of terminal wealth, we study both optimal reinsurance which is constrained to the unit interval and optimal investment with a jump-diffusion risky asset and no short selling. Moreover, the aggregate claims and the stock price are correlated by means of a common shock. This kind of model assumes that there exists a common shock affecting the stock market as well as the insurance market. In reality, a common component can depict a big event which has negative impact on both the financial and insurance markets. For example, severe events like earthquakes or prolonged extreme weathers not only has immediate adverse impact on financial markets, but also induce various insurance claims. Similar argument applies to other detrimental incidents caused by human or natural disasters. Hence, we consider the case where the aggregate claims process and risky asset process are dependent. Furthermore, we impose the assumption of negative expected value of jump, which allows the inclusion of positive jumps, and at the same time also meets the observed fact that the stock market reactions to negative shocks are usually significantly stronger than the reactions to positive ones. Therefore, the model of study is practically more reasonable, and definitely makes the optimization problem more complicated and challenging. Using the technique of stochastic control theory and the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, we adopt a nonstandard approach to examine the existence and uniqueness of the optimal strategy, and derive the closed-form expressions for the optimal strategy and the value function not only for the expected value principle but also for the variance premium principle. Also, we investigate the effect of the common shock parameter as well as some other important parameters on the optimal strategies. Objective 2 has also been successfully completed; and the results are presented in the publication entitled "Optimal reinsurance and investment in a jump-diffusion financial market with common shock dependence". This publication can be found in Part C, Item 1. For Objective 3, in order to build a model which is close to the real-world financial market, we extend the study of the optimal investment-reinsurance problem in a regime-switching market under the mean-variance criterion to a common shock risk model with two dependent classes of business. Specifically, the insurer can invest its surplus in a Markov regime-switching financial market with one bank account and one stock. It is assumed that short selling of the stock is not allowed, and that the parameter values of the insurer's surplus process can switch over time according to the state of the Markov chain. One of the challenges in the proposed problem is that we have to deal with the nonnegative constraints on the investment-reinsurance strategies. The nonnegativity constraint on the investment strategy is due to the assumption of no short selling of the stock, while the nonnegative constraint on the reinsurance strategy is due to the adoption of proportional reinsurance. These nonnegative constraints are reasonable ones in real financial markets and have been studied extensively in the literature. These constraints definitely make the problem harder in the sense that the resulting optimal strategies may not satisfy the restrictions. Interestingly, this difficulty can be tackled by adding some conditions to the initial amount of wealth. Moreover, we consider a more challenging problem by incorporating a common shock into the risk model with two classes of business. As a result, the number of control variables increases. Such an increase introduces further complexity to the optimal analysis. In particular, we need to discuss the optimization problem in three different cases owing to the nonnegative constraint on the reinsurance strategy. All these suggest that the problem of study is a meaningful one, and most importantly, the research outcomes generalize the existing results from the case of independent risk model to the case of dependent risk model. Despite the difficulties, we are able to solve the problem by using the techniques of stochastic linear-quadratic control. Under the mean-variance criterion, we obtain analytic expressions for the optimal investment and reinsurance strategies, and derive closed-form expressions for the efficient strategies and the efficient frontiers which are based on the solutions to some systems of linear ordinary differential equations. Based on these results, we have published a paper entitled "Optimal mean-variance investment/reinsurance with common shock in a regime-switching market", and thus Objective 3 is complete. For details, see Part C, Item 8.

17329216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17329216.value: For Objective 1, we adopt the variance premium principle to investigate the problem of optimal dividends and reinsurance in a diffusion approximation risk model with thinning-dependence structure. We first study the optimal problem without capital injection. We then consider the incorporation of forced capital injection into the model whenever the reserve level drops below zero. We finally turn to the general problem in which capital injection is allowed but not compulsory. For the three optimal problems, we apply the technique of stochastic control theory to obtain closed-form expressions for the optimal strategies and the corresponding value functions for two classes of insurance business with thinning dependence. Furthermore some numerical examples are presented to show the effect of parameter values on the optimal policies. For details, see Part C Item 9. For Objective 2, we study the optimal reinsurance and investment problem in a financial market with jump-diffusion risky asset. It is assumed that the insurance risk model is modulated by a compound Poisson process, and that the jumps in both the risky asset and insurance risk process are correlated through a common shock. Under the criterion of maximizing the expected exponential utility, we adopt a nonstandard approach to examine the existence and uniqueness of the optimal strategy. Using the technique of stochastic control theory, closed-form expressions for the optimal strategy and the value function are derived not only for the expected value principle but also for the variance premium principle. Also, we investigate the effect of the common shock parameter as well as some other important parameters on the optimal strategies. For details, see Part C Item 1. For Objective 3, we consider the problem of optimal investment-reinsurance with two dependent classes of insurance risks in a regime-switching financial market. In our model, the two claim-number processes are correlated through a common shock component, and the market mode is classified into a finite number of regimes. We also assume that the insurer can purchase proportional reinsurance and invest its surplus in a financial market, and that the values of the model parameters depend on the market mode. Using the techniques of stochastic linear-quadratic control, under the mean-variance criterion, we obtain analytic expressions for the optimal investment and reinsurance strategies, and derive closed-form expressions for the efficient strategies and the efficient frontiers which are based on the solutions to some systems of linear ordinary differential equations. Finally, we carry out a numerical study for illustration purpose. For details, see Part C Item 8.

17329216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17329216.value: In relation to the project theme, there are still many other interesting problems that one may consider. During the project duration, we have published quite a number of additional research papers related to the study of insurance risk models. These papers appear in various journals including Scandinavian Actuarial Journal, Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics, and Journal of Industrial and Management Optimization. These publications are listed in Part C. Specifically, Part C Items 2 and 3 study mortality risk with applications to modern financial products; Items, 4, 5, 7, 14 and 15 focus on ruin analysis of insurance risk modes; and Items 6, 10, 11, 12 13, 16, and 17 investiagte the optimal reinsurance, dividends, and/or investment problems for various insurance risk models with realistic features such as transaction costs, taxes, premium control, delayed claims and heavy-tailed claims. For further research, one may consider studying the optimal reinsurance and investment problems with various realistic features under the concept of absolute ruin. Of course, these optimization problems become more complicated and challenging. In fact, the principal investigator has proposed some of these problems in the GRF 2020 grant application, and the grant application was successful.

17329216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17329216.value: In practice, insurance companies need to study the potential risks of their business carefully, so as to minimize the chance of having an unexpectedly large amount of claims. Reinsurance is an important activity for insurers. As the financial impact of huge claims on the insurance industry could be considerable, an insurance company with certain reinsurance strategy can reduce its risks at the expense of sacrificing its potential profit. Therefore, the insurer would like to seek the optimal reinsurance strategy that can strike a balance between risks and profit. Furthermore, dividend payment strategy has also become an increasingly important issue for various financial institutions. Due to its practical importance, one has to be very cautious when assessing the impact of dividend payments on insurance business. Another important feature in real situations is capital injection which allows companies to raise capital if necessary. All these indicate that the study of insurance risks together with realistic features is of great importance to both practitioners and researchers. This project studies several optimization problems with reinsurance, dividends, and/or capital injection. It is believed the findings provide useful insights into some practical problems, and that the research outcomes are of theoretical significance for further research.

17329516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17329516.value: The cost and speed of solution-based assays for biomedical applications, such as diagnostics, depend critically on the size of the containers holding the solutions. By miniaturizing the containers from a centimeter well to a sub-millimeter droplet, solution consumption can be reduced by over 1000 times. The resultant “droplet microfluidic” approach has achieved great prominence as a next-generation technology for high-throughput biomedical applications. Flowing droplets can be manipulated within a complex network of channels, allowing controlled mixing between droplets containing different reactants and detection of reaction products in a single pre-defined device. However, the complex networks of tubings and microvalves in the device cannot be re-configured during operation, significantly reducing the flexibility to refine and redesign the processes in case of malfunctions or unforeseen operational circumstances. Another type of microfluidic technologies, often known as “digital microfluidics”, allows a large number of droplets to be addressed individually in a single device using computer software without modifying the hardware. However, the droplets must wet the surface of the device, leading to carry-over and cross-contamination between samples within the device, particularly for tests, such as sensitive polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays, where any contaminant will be significantly amplified. An approach that does not rely on the wetting of the substrate is therefore much needed. One way to reduce wetting is by coating liquid droplets with particles, which prevent the liquid from coming into direct contact with the solid substrate. These particle-coated liquid droplets in air, often known as “liquid marbles”, have been proposed for use in cosmetics and pharmaceutical formulations, but their use in digital microfluidic operations has so far been limited due to the lack of strategies to actuate, coalesce and mix liquid marbles for triggering diagnostic reactions and biomedical detections. The targets of the proposed project are to (1) elucidate the physics behind the responses of liquid marbles to electrical charging, (2) develop an electrical-charging approach to coalesce liquid marbles and mix the contents inside them, and (3) demonstrate how liquid marbles can be manipulated electrically on reconfigurable electrodes. In the short term, the study provides a fundamental understanding of the interactions between liquid marbles, and brings new approaches to manipulate them by electrical charging. In the long term, it will further contribute to the advancement of next-generation platforms for sample preparation and analytical chemistry, and promise faster and cheaper clinical diagnostics for a wider range of disease conditions. 基於試劑化驗的生物醫學應用，如醫療診斷，其成本和速度主要取決於盛放試劑的容器大小。通過將容器從一厘米的試管微縮到不足一毫米的液滴，試劑的消耗可以減少超過1000倍。隨之產生的“液滴微流控”(droplet microfluidic) 的方法已脱颖而出成為下一代高通量生物醫學應用技術。在單一預先製作的裝置里，流動的液滴可以在複雜的通道網絡內被操控，含有不同反應物的液滴得以受控混合，從而檢測其反應產物。然而，這個裝置里的通道和微型閥的複雜網絡在使用中不能重新配置，這極大降低了裝置在故障或不可預見的操作環境下進行改善和重新設計的靈活性。另一種類型的微流控技術，通常被稱為“數字微流控”(digital microfluidics)，允許在單一裝置上通過計算機軟件來同時獨立操控大量液滴，而無需改變裝置的硬件配置。然而，這些液滴必須浸潤所使用裝置的表面，導致了裝置內樣品間的殘留和交叉污染，這對一些測試如敏感的聚合酶鏈反應（PCR）檢測試劑的影響尤其顯著，其中的任何污染物將顯著擴增。因此非常需要一種能不依賴於浸潤裝置表面而操控液滴的方法。 減少液滴浸潤的一種方法是用固體顆粒包裹液滴，這樣可防止液滴與固體底板直接接觸。這種用固體顆粒包裹的置於空氣中的液滴通常被稱為“液體彈珠”(liquid marbles)，其已被提議用在化妝品和藥物製劑中，但是它們在數字微流體控制操作中的使用迄今有限，其原因是缺乏相應驅動、融合及混合它们的策略以觸發診斷反應和生物醫學檢測。 提议項目的目標是：(1) 解釋液體彈珠對充電效應的反應背後的物理原理，(2) 發展一種利用充電效應的方法来融合液體彈珠及混合其內部液體，(3) 展示如何在可重構的電極上用電場操控液體彈珠。 在短期內，這項研究提供了對液體彈珠間相互作用的基本理解，並帶來了新的通過充電效應操控它們的方法。從長遠來看，這將進一步促進下一代樣品製備和分析化學平台的發展，並允諾了為更廣泛的病情提供更快、更便宜的臨床診斷。

17329516.label: Realisation of objectives
17329516.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1. We have investigated the stability of electrically charged liquid marbles of different types of liquids under different conditions, such with different viscosities, stabilizing particle type and sizes, and under different geometries of electrical charging. We have characterized the behaviors into different coalescence regimes under different dimensionless numbers, such as electro-capillary number and aspect ratios. We have also expressed our findings in polar plots and compared with other relevant particle-stabilized systems 2. We have studied electrically driven behaviors, such as electro-coalescence, electro-mixing, electro-actuation, under different geometries in electric fields applied under different configurations. Our understanding has enabled new ways to manipulate liquid marbles for microreactions, and for biomedical applications, such as detection of DNA and cell cultures. 3. We have introduced and demonstrated an approach based on electrical charging to manipulate liquid marbles, both with electrodes immersed into the liquid marbles, and with embedded electrodes. With embedded electrodes, the versatility of the manipulation is enhanced and can be tailored for a wider variety of applications. We have also compared the different dynamics for different liquid samples stabilized with different particles that exhibit specific functions, such as conductivity. Adjustment of these different parameters leads to different coalescence behaviors and morphologies that would be useful for different needs and applications. Besides, we have also demonstrated a novel way of coupling our electro-microfluidic approach with an optical method for further manipulation of the liquid marbles. .

17329516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17329516.value: - Understand the behaviors and dynamics of liquid marbles induced by electrical charging under different charging geometries - Investigate the different regimes exhibited by electrostatically manipulated liquid marbles of different liquids stabilized by different particle type and size - Demonstrate a range of operations, such as coalescence, actuation, mixing and reactions that can be performed using liquid marbles subject to different electrostatic conditions - Integrate the advantages of electrostatically manipulated liquid marbles with conventional understanding of liquid marbles for illustrating their applications, such as in microreactions and cell culture. Most of the results have been presented in various international conferences (e.g. MicroTAS 2020, International Symposium on Microchemistry and Microsystems 2019, 8th International Conference on Bioelectronics, Biosensors, BioMedical Devices, BioMEMS/NEMS and Applications 2019 (Bio4Apps2019), ChinaNano 2017, etc.) and published in respected international journals (e.g. Lab on a Chip, ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces, Advanced Functional Materials, etc.), as shown in Part C. While some papers have been submitted and are being reviewed, other results are being integrated with other applications and wrapped up for publication due to their potential for a greater impact.

17329516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17329516.value: The ability to encapsulate the components without easier contamination makes the platform a great candidate for rapid applications, such as diagnostics. The choice of the stabilizing particles also facilitates incorporation of additional functions, and surface properties. The demonstration of the embedded electrodes paves the way for design of portable devices using these liquid marbles. Hence, the ideas and tools may also benefit the development of new devices in point-of-care and point-of-consumption uses. The proposed course of action includes publishing the remaining works, while discussing the attracting aspects with potential academic and/or industrial collaborators who may need to manipulate liquid samples that need to be rapidly generated and processed. We also propose to explore the large-scale prototyping and production of our lab-scale devices through collaborations with large companies or startups, facilitated by research grants, such as the Innovation and Technology Fund (ITF), and other funds that connect the industries and academia in Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Guangdong province. The potential for manipulating the liquid marbles optically approaching the end of the projects also represents an exciting direction used either on its own or in combination with the electrostatic manipulation. Some of the project outcomes also benefit other research projects indirectly.

17329516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17329516.value: Droplets represent emerging unit of liquids underlying many new applications, ranging from cell cultures to rapid diagnostics. While miniaturization of the droplets to micro- and nano-meter diameters reduces the amount of liquid samples needed and reagents consumed, the machinery and equipment needed to operate and manipulate such small droplets also become more specialized. A balance in terms of the sample reduction and equipment versatility should be stroke. This is where this project fills the niche. In this project, we characterized the dynamics of millimeter-sized droplets stabilized by different particles, in terms of size and surface properties under different conditions. These droplets can be easily generated without specialized equipment. We identified and explained different coalescence regimes and dynamics. We also overcame the difficulties in manipulating them by introducing devices with electrodes placed in different geometries. The actual applications will require operation, including but not limited to actuation, coalescence and mixing on demand. We demonstrated the integration of these steps and highlighted their promise in performing application such as cell culture and microreactions. These results will provide the foundation and tools for evaluating the feasibility of an electrostatic liquid marble platforms, and inspire new applications, particularly in biomedical areas.

17330216.value: 金屬集群和溶劑化水熱蒸汽：IRMPD光譜學與量子化學研究。

17330216.label: Project Objectives
17330216.value: The main objectives of the work proposed under theme1 are: i) to probe interactions between water molecules and geochemically important metal ligand clusters using IRMPD spectroscopy and ESI/FT-ICR mass spectrometry, ii) to examine how changes in water solvation shell size and structure influence the stability of the metal-ligand core, and iii) to establish a molecular-scale link between solvated metal clusters and metal fractionating processes occurring in low density aqueous fluids. The objectives of Theme2 are i) the experimental study of the water hydration shell surrounding clusters containing heavier 4d and 5d metals, including Pd, Pt and Au, Ag, using FT-MS, IRPMD spectroscopy and ab initio theory suitable to handle molecular systems with strong relativistic effects. These ion cluster studies are to be undertaken in order to examine how water molecules bind to metal halide ions, such as [AuCl2]+, [Au2Cl5]+, and larger metal clusters, and to examine the effect that water molecules have on the structure and thus on the propensity toward dissociation of the metal-halide cluster. The objectives of Theme3 are i) to investigate the composition of H2S- and NH3-microsolvated coinage metal (Cu, Ag Au) halide clusters, building directly on results obtained under theme1 and theme2, ii) to experimentally characterize the structure of the solvation shell, via IRMPD spectroscopy, and to calculate vibrational frequencies for OH, SH and NH stretching modes in H2O, H2S, and NH3 molecules surrounding coinage metal-halide clusters, and iii) to determine the relative strength of these interactions, in other words, the affinity of H2O, H2S, and NH3 to bind to metal centers in [MmCln]+.

17330216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17330216.value: 溶剂化的方法对于发生在地壳分子尺度的相互作用, 水圈 和低大气层地带是非常重要的。溶剂化发生在矿物和细菌表面的地方，与溶液内离子的周围。它发生在生物分子的表面上，以对蛋白质折叠和早期地球上生命的起源具有重要含义。水是地球表面上无处不在，但大量的H20存储在地壳和地幔，锁定在矿物质或矿物表面为H和OH，或为水分子。当这种水从地壳中上升到较浅处时，沸腾就会发生并导致低密度水的状态（蒸气）和共存流体，两体都具有不同的化学性质。此蒸气状态是处于高流动性的，但更重要的是，它类似于有机溶剂的极性。换句话说，地壳沸腾产生大量的水蒸汽，这水蒸汽含有甲醇状溶剂的特性。这种蒸汽的存在有助于增进我们 对于 在地壳金属运输和沉积的理解。然而, 我们对于分子级溶剂化和金属物种的稳定性于水蒸气里的理解还有相当大的距离，特别是对于分子金属簇。目前, 金属簇正在接受越来越多的关注，因为他们同时拥有气体和固体的理化特性，而且还因为这些集群表现出大小依赖反应特性. 源于这种特性，它将有望成为地球科学里一目新兴的研究领域。我们在香港大学的研究小组与这项研究计划的主要目标就基于探讨红外多光子解离的金属 - 配体簇（IRMPD）光谱研究 ,特别是，以探测由录音质量选择的分子离子溶剂化层在水中IRMPD光谱OH伸缩区域。

17330216.value: Realization of research objectives under project GRF#P17330216. As of November 2021 we have completed all experimental studies that have been described under project P17330216. In particular, we have been successful in applying for IRMPD beam time at the FELIX facility in Nijmegen, NL, that produces IR radiation from ~300-1900 cm-1. These experiments have been critical in complementing some of our in-house FT-MS IRMPD studies of metals complexes, clusters and their responding water solvation shells. 17330216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17330216.value: GRF#P17330216 objective1: The work outlined under P17330216 obj.1 has been completed, in particular, we have successfully characterized using FT-MS and IRMPD spectroscopy, the structure and properties of small gold halide clusters with water solvation shells. These experimental studies have also been complimented with theoretical ab initio electronic structure calculations and, in select cases, with first principles molecular dynamic simulations. This work and related material pertaining the speciation of vapor-phase Au has been published in Lemke & Seward, Rev. Min. Geochem, 84, 57-83, 2018, and more recently in Lemke, Phys.Chem.Chem.Phys, 34, 18990-18998, 2021, in which we demonstrate the effect of water solvation shell size, structure and composition (H2O vs H2S) on the speciation of gold-halides clusters, hydroxide ions and their propensity to dissolve into water vapor. GRF#P17330216 objective2: This work focuses on the characterization of nano hydrated metal complexes using FT-MS, IRMPD spectroscopy, and electronic structure calculations. We have completed all IRMPD spectroscopic studies under this sub-theme, and we are currently in the final stages of write-up for these FT-MS, IRMPD studies. The main focus of this work has been to probe the water solvation shell around various 4d and 5d transition metals, in particular Au but also Pd and Pt. For example, in the case of AuCl2+(H2O)n, we have discovered that the gold chloride ion shifts from an ion-neutral Au+-Cl2 configuration to an L-shaped triple-ion complex as the solvation number increases from n=1-4, in other words, gold exists as Au(I) in the former, whereas the L-shaped AuCl2+ complex containing formal Au(III) dominates for n=2-4, with fundamentally different IR spectral features, solvation shell structures and thermodynamic properties. GRF#P17330216 objective3: These spectroscopic studies have being conducted using our in-house OPO/OPA IRMPD laser and are also being complimented using the FELIX facility, NL, that is capable of delivering IR radiation from 50-1800 cm-1, and thus can be employed to probe low-frequency H2O libration, dihalide stretching, as well as Au-O and Au-Cl stretching motions. We have over the last 12 months undertaken extensive structure scans of nano-solvated clusters of the type [MnX2n+1]+(H2O/H2S)2-10 in order to build a reliable database of isomers that will be used for DFT/aVDZ and higher level MP2/aV(D,T)Z optimizations; this work is currently in progress, and results of these theoretical studies will be used for anharmonic VPT2 type MP2 frequency simulations and spectral assignments related to HOH bending, OH stretching and water libration bands of experimental IRMPD spectra of [MnX2n+1]+(H2O/H2S)2-10.

17330216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17330216.value: Results from our FT-MS IRMPD studies conducted under GRF 17330216 have important consequences for our understanding of metal transport and speciation in low-density aqueous fluids. One interesting outcome of this experimental FT-MS IRMPD work is the study of gas-phase metal complexes and clusters using state-of-art ab initio simulation techniques, in particular, Carr-Parrinello Molecular Dynamics (CPMD). Prompted by these results we have been awarded an RGC project GRF 17308120 “Metals in Ore Nanodroplets: Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics and IR Spectroscopic Characterization of Hydrated Gold and Copper Clusters.” in 2020/2021, and we are currently preparing a stand-alone proposal in which we propose to employ CPMD techniques to probe the nature of metal clusters in aqueous environments. Under GRF 17308120 we have initiated three new sub-projects that focus on the interactions between ionic and neutral metal species with low-density aqueous media at elevated temperatures. Systems under investigation include, but are not limited to, mono- and polynuclear Aun and Cun clusters in H2O/H2S, their structure, solvation dynamics and thermodynamic stability. Interestingly, clusters such as Aun are probably early stage molecular precursors leading to colloidal forms of gold that then flocculate giving rise to economic levels of gold deposits.

17330216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17330216.value: Recent experimental studies have shown that steam is enriched in Au and Cu by a factor of up to 105-106 relative to its coexisting fluid phase. We now also know that this metal-enriched vapor phase is a multi-phase system, consisting of water molecules, clusters with 5-20 waters and larger nanodroplets with up to several 1000 water molecules. These nano-droplets interact and hydrate metal species at their surface, near-surface and bulk region, with different site propensities for each metal ion type. For instance, protons occupy surface sites, whereas the hydroxide ion is positioned at the droplet near-surface, resulting in large pH variations across just nanometer length scales, however, very little is known as to the site propensity of metal ions in these environments. Understanding the solvation dynamics of metal and metal ions in and around nanodroplets is therefore at the core of understanding metal solubility, reactivity and mobility in volvanic and hydrothermal ore vapors. It is this knowledge gap that has prompted us to examine nanosolvated metal species using molecular spectroscopy and simulation techniques. Our interest in such metal-nanodroplet interactions has led us to probe the structure of water hydrated Cu and Au clusters using structure-sensitive spectroscopies (IRMPD) and first principles molecular dynamics (CPMD).

17330316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17330316.value: This project studies Sklyanin algebras and noncommutative instantons on quantum projective planes. Sklyanin algebras were discovered in the early 80s in the study of quantum inverse scattering in quantum and statistical physics. In the late 80s, mathematicians re-discovered them as the first few interesting examples of noncommutative projective schemes. In the past three decades, there have been plenty of exciting works about Sklyanin algebras influenced by ideas from quantum physics, integrable systems, quantum groups, and in particular, noncommutative geometry. Noncommutative geometry provides a mathematical framework for the quantisation process in physics. To give a simple example, 4 dimensional space-time can be viewed as a complex projective plane with the projective line at infinity removed. The ring of “functions” on the projective plane is the polynomial algebra of three variables. A quantisation of the projective plane, which we call a quantum projective plane, has as its ring of functions a deformation of the polyomial algebra. A 3-dimenisonal Sklyanin algebra is precisely such a deformation, i.e. it can be viewed as the ring of functions on a quantum projective plane. In this project, the PI aims to study the geometry of the moduli space of coherent sheaves on the quantum projective planes. A coherent sheaf on a quantum projective plane is an equivalence class of representations of the Sklyanin algebra. Among all coherent sheaves, there is a speical class of sheaves called noncommutative instantons. They are noncommutative analogues of instantons on C2. Atiyah, Drinfeld, Hitchin and Manin (ADHM) construct the moduli space of instantons on C2 as a symplectic quotient. The main objective of this project is to give an ADHM type construction for the moduli space of noncommutative instantons. This is a first step to understand the quantisation of gauge theory on quantum projective planes. The key objects are the elliptic r-matrices, which are elliptic solutions of the Yang-Baxter equation. In this project, we will study the geometric nature of these elliptic r-matrices, in particular, how they determine the symplectic/Poisson structures on moduli spaces of noncommutative instantons. 在此項目中，我們將研究Sklyanin代數和量子平面上瞬子的模空間。 Sklyanin代數最早出現于80年代初期的對於量子逆方法的研究。數學家對其的研究始於80年代末期的非交換幾何。 再過去30年，在Sklyanin代數的研究中產生大量傑出的成果。這些成果將數學中的很多分支和理論物理聯繫起來，如可積系統，量子群和非交換幾何。 在這個項目中，申請人將研究非交換瞬子的模空間的ADHM構造。在交換幾何當中，Atiyah Drinfeld Hitchen 和 Manin用代數幾何的方法構造了規範場中的瞬子模空間。我們將嘗試推廣ADHM構造至非交換的情形。這個問題的關鍵在於分析量子逆方法中r/R矩陣的幾何意義。

17330316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17330316.value: A major finding of the project, published in a joint paper with Alexander Polishchuk on Adv. in Math (2018) is a construction of shifted Poisson structure on moduli stack of bounded complexes of vector bundles on smooth projective CY varieties. This result extends the seminal result of Pantev-Toen-Vaquie-Vezzosi, which is the symplectic counter part of our result. As a very special case of this result, we understand the Poisson structure on the moduli space of (noncommutative) instants on quantum projective plane, constructed originally by Nevins and Stafford, via shifted Poisson geometry. Another class of examples that fits into our general framework is the quadratic Poisson brackets constructed by Feigin and Odesskii. Our theorem leads to a series of new results on Poisson geometry of Feigin-Odesskii manifold (see research out put of GRF no, 17308818).

17330316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17330316.value: Project GRF no. 17308818 is a follow-up of this one. We have used the above-mentioned result to solve some classical problem in Poisson geometry. Another potential direction is to apply our theory to the study of Artin-Schelter regular algebras.

17330316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17330316.value: Derived algebraic geometry is one of the most exciting subjects in recent years. Our result is an attempt to apply techniques in derived algebraic geometry to solve open problems in classical Poisson geometry. So far our attempt is successful. We have solved some old open problems and greatly simplify some traditional theory using the new techniques.

17330416.label: Realisation of objectives
17330416.value: We have completed the project and achieved all the objectives listed above. 11 papers have been published in peer-reviewed journals: 3 in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 1 in Chem. Sci., 1 in Chem, 1 in Adv. Sci., 1 in J. Am. Chem. Soc., 1 in Chem. Eur. J., 1 in Inorg. Chem., 1 in Adv. Opt. Mater. and 1 in J. Mater. Chem. C. 7 presentations were delivered in international conferences. These contributions (11 papers and 5 presentations) have acknowledged the support from this RGC grant. The important findings are summarized below: [1] Objectives 1 and 2: We have prepared a series of tetradentate gold(III) complexes via microwave assisted synthesis. The emission of these complexes can be tuned from blue-green to red by varying the substituent on the ligand. Importantly, some of the complexes show photoluminescence with quantum yields of up to 94% with short lifetimes of 0.6–1.6 μs, the origin of which has been identified to be thermally activated delayed fluorescence(TADF). Vacuum-deposited OLEDs fabricated with tetradentate Au(III)-TADF emitters show maximum EQE of up to 22% at a luminance of 1000 cd m-2, which is the highest value among reported gold(III)-OLEDs. The operational lifetime LT95 of one of the OLEDs has been measured to be 1.97 h at an initial luminance of 10390 cd m 2, corresponding to 5280 h at 100 cd m-2. A patent application based on these findings has been filed.[Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 6375-6382; highlighted as the Inside Back Cover] [2] Objectives 1 and 3: Three platinum(II) complexes supported by tetradentate bis(phenolate-NHC) ligands were prepared. They show intense blue phosphorescence (λmax=434–447 nm) with quantum yields and lifetimes of up to 24% and 6.7μs respectively in solution at room temperature, and highly reducing triplet excited states with E([Pt]+/*) of over -2.6 V versus Cp2Fe+/0. These platinum(II) complexes were found to catalyze light-driven reductive coupling of carbonyl compounds and reductive de-bromination of a wide range of unactivated alkyl and aryl bromides.[Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 14129-14133] [3] Objectives 1 and 3: A palladium(II) complex supported by tetradentate N^C^C^N ligand bearing a diphenylamino substituent has been prepared. This complex displays sky-blue(484 nm) photoluminescence with quantum yield and lifetime of 81% and 11.6 μs respectively in degassed toluene at room temperature.[Unpublished work] [4] Objectives 1 and 3: A series of platinum(II) complexes supported by O-bridged tetradentate N^C^C^N ligand has been prepared. By modifying the N-donor moiety, the emission of these complexes can be tuned from deep blue (429 nm) to red (613 nm) with quantum yields and lifetimes of up to 76% and 98μs respectively in degassed dichloromethane at room temperature.[Unpublished work] [5] Objective 1: A platinum(II) complex support by dianionic O^N^C^N ligand has been employed in conjunction with an iridium(III) emitter to fabricate white-emitting OLEDs with a high PE of up to 71.9 lm W-1. The electroluminescence spectrum of the white OLED is stable over a large luminance range from 87 to 5100 cd m-2 attributed to the evenly distributed excitons in both co-host emissive layers.[J. Chem. Mater. C 2018, 6, 9890-9896] [6] Objective 1 and 5: A class of tetradentate platinum(II) complexes exhibit deep-red/near infrared emission due to strong intermolecular interaction in the solid state. The emission is assigned to mixed excimer triplet π-π* and metal-metal-to-ligand charge-transfer excited state according to DFT calculations. An NIR OLED with emission maximum at 700nm and EQE up to 11.2% has been fabricated.[ Adv. Optical Mater. 2019, 7, 1801452] [7] Objectives 4 and 5: We have developed a series of photoluminescent tungsten(VI) dioxo complexes supported by Schiff base ligands. By installing strongly electron-donating arylamino substituents in the ligand scaffold, the emission quantum yield of these complexes could reach 56% in solution and 84% in thin films. Importantly, by conducting ultrafast time-resolved measurements and DFT calculations, one of these complexes was found to display efficient TADF at room temperature, which is the first example of W(VI)-TADF emitter. The OLED fabricated with this TADF emitter shows high EQE and luminance of up to 15.56% and 16890 cd m-2 respectively. Furthermore, a PCT Patent application based on these findings has been filed.[Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2019, 58, 14896-14900] [8] Objectives 4 and 5: A tungsten(VI) complex having diphenylamino substituent was found to be an efficient photocatalyst for a broad array of light-induced organic transformation such as borylation of aryl halides, reductive homocoupling of benzyl bromides. The mechanism of photo-redox catalysis with the tungsten(VI) complex has been examined with time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy, steady state photolysis and cyclic voltammetry. DFT calculations have been conducted to understand excited state properties of this complex.[Chem. Sci. 2020, 11, 6370-6382; highlighted as the Front Cover] [9] Objective 5: A series of cyclometalated gold(III) alkyl complexes has been prepared. They exhibit emission quantum yields and lifetimes of up to 40% and 180μs respectively in solution at room temperature. The emission color of these complexes is tunable from yellow to sky-blue by modifying the cyclometalating ligand. DFT/TDDFT calculations have been performed on some of the complexes to account for their photophysical properties.[Inorg. Chem. 2017, 56, 5046-5059] [10] Objective 5: A class of donor–acceptor type cyclometalated gold(III) alkynyl complexes have been prepared. Some of them display efficient TADF with quantum yield up to 88% in thin films and emission lifetimes of ~1–2μs at room temperature. DFT calculations have been conducted to substantiate the emission origin assignment of these complexes. Vacuum-deposited OLEDs fabricated with these thermally stable gold(III) TADF emitters show high maximum EQE of 22.1% at a luminance of 1000 cd m-2.[Adv. Sci. 2019, 6, 1802297] [11] Objective 5: Two sky-blue luminescent arylgold(III)-TADF complexes with emission peak maxima at 470-484 nm in thin films were synthesized. These gold(III)-TADF emitters show high emission quantum yields of up to 0.82 and radiative lifetimes less than 1μs. Photophysical studies and time-dependent density functional theory calculations revealed that the emission nature of these gold(III) complexes is most consistent with TADF. OLEDs fabricated with these gold(III) complexes showed maximum EQE of up to 15.3%.[Chem. Eur. J. 2020, 26, 15718-15726] [12] Objective 5: We have prepared cyclometalated gold(III) allenylidene, acetylide and isocyanide complexes and examined their photophysical properties and self-assembly. The gold(III)-allenylidene complex displays a close Au−Au contact of 3.367Å between neighboring molecules in its X-ray crystal structure. Gold(III) isocyanide complexes show a broad red-shifted absorption band and phosphorescence upon aggregation that was influenced by an attractive Au(III)-Au(III) bonding interaction in the excited state. The nature of the emissive excited state(s) of the gold(III) aggregates is assigned to a mixture of major triplet [π-π*] and minor triplet ligand-to-metal−metal charge transfer states based on combined spectroscopic and DFT/TDDFT studies.[J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2019, 141, 11572-11582] [13] Objective 5: We developed a supramolecular ‘doping’ approach to fabricate highly phosphorescent supramolecular polymeric materials. By doping a small amount of Pt(II) complexes (2mol%) into the Pd(II) assemblies, the emission quantum yield and radiative decay rate constant changed from Φ=3.7%, kr=1.83x10^4s-1 in PdII assemblies to Φ=76.2%, kr=58.6x10^4s-1 in Pt(II)-Pd(II) co-assemblies. DFT calculations revealed that during a co-assembly process, the frontier dz2 orbitals of Pd(II) and Pt(II) complexes significantly overlap, giving rise to a delocalized triplet [dσ*π*] excited state, subsequently making the co-assemblies strongly phosphorescent due to the external heavy-atom effect from the platinum.[Chem 2020, 6,945-967]

17330416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17330416.value: The research conducted with this RGC funding has led to the development of new classes of luminescent Pt(II), Pd(II), Au(III) and W(VI) complexes showing long-lived excited states and application in photocatalysis and OLED. In summary, we have accomplished the followings: [1] 11 publications in international chemistry journals including Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Journal of the American Chemical Society, Chem, Advanced Science and Chemical Science. [2] 7 presentations on this research topic were delivered in international conferences. [3] An important work on luminescent Au(III) complexes supported by tetradentate trianionic ligand showing high emission quantum yields and lifetimes of up to 0.94 and 225 μs respectively have been published.[Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 6375]. The emission color is tunable from blue-green to red, and the emission origin can be switched from phosphorescence to TADF, the latter of which is highly advantageous for reducing efficiency roll-off and increasing the device lifetime of OLEDs. [4] Deep-blue to sky-blue emitting tetradentate Pt(II) and Pd(II) complexes have been prepared. [unpublished result] [5] Strongly luminescent tungsten(VI) dioxo complexes supported by Schiff base ligands have been prepared. The emission origin of these complexes can be tuned from phosphorescence to TADF with quantum yield up to 0.84 in thin film, which is the highest value in literature.[Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2019, 58, 14896] An OLED fabricated with W(VI)-TADF emitter showed EQE up to 15.56%, establishing its potential as practical OLED emitters. A W(VI) complex exhibiting long-lived excited state have been harnessed as a photocatalyst for a broad array of light-induced organic transformation such as borylation of aryl halides, reductive homocoupling of benzyl bromides with performance comparable to that of commonly used photocatalysts [Ir(ppy)3] and [Ru(bpy)3]2+.[Chem. Sci. 2020, 11, 6370] [6] DFT calculations and time-resolved spectroscopic measurements have been conducted to understand the excited state properties of Pt(II), Pd(II), Au(III) and W(VI) complexes. Importantly, the emissive excited state of some Au(III) and W(VI) complexes were identified to be TADF instead of phosphorescence.[Adv. Sci. 2019, 6, 1802297; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2019, 58, 14896; Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 6375] This finding fundamentally alters our understanding of photophysical properties of heavy transition metal complexes and leads to novel design strategies for preparing metal-TADF emitters in addition to Cu(I)-TADF emitters. With the use of these highly luminescent metal-TADF emitters, efficient Au(III)- and W(VI)-OLEDs have been fabricated, which confirms the competitiveness of these materials in OLED industry.

17330416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17330416.value: The results of this project have further revealed the usefulness of luminescent Pt(II), Pd(II), Au(III) and W(VI) complexes as photo-functional materials with tunable photophysical properties and broad application. The success of employing tetradentate ligand for preparing highly luminescent Pt(II), Pd(II) and Au(III) complexes demonstrated in this completed project further re-affirms that the “one ligand + one metal” approach could afford robust metal complexes with properties comparable to the widely studied Pt(II) and Ir(III) complexes supported by bidentate and tridentate ligands. With the insight obtained in these studies, we will continue to expand the structural diversity of tetradentate d8 metal emitters. Besides, the unprecedented discovery of TADF in Au(III) and W(VI) has unveiled their uniqueness compared to other noble metal complexes. With TADF serving as an efficient radiative decay pathway, the OLED efficiency roll-off issue associated with their long phosphorescent lifetime can be greatly mitigated. With emission quantum yields and lifetimes approaching that of Ir(III) and Pt(II) complexes, Au(III) and W(VI) TADF emitters are envisioned to possess enormous potential for further development and to be used in diverse areas.

17330416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17330416.value: Luminescent metal compounds have useful applications in diverse areas such as OLEDs and sensing. The practicality of these materials in these applications depends on their luminescent properties as well as their stability and robustness. In this research, we have prepared luminescent platinum, palladium and gold compounds that are supported by a rigid ligand scaffold. These ligands bind strongly to the metal by forming metal-carbon bond(s), endowing high stability to these compounds. The rigidity of the ligand also reduces non-emissive deactivation pathways, which in turn increases the luminescence efficiency of these compounds. By modifying the ligand, the emission color of these metal compounds covers the whole visible spectral region and even to near infrared. We also found that the emission origin of gold and tungsten compounds can switch between phosphorescence and thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), the latter of which is a promising strategy for increasing the radiative decay rate of luminescent materials. Importantly, we have discovered the first examples of tetradentate gold- and tungsten-TADF compounds which show excellent performance in OLEDs. Overall, the accomplishments achieved in this project have revealed the structural design for improving the robustness of materials and the bright prospect of gold- and tungsten-TADF compounds.

17330816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17330816.value: Optimal dividends policy, optimal reinsurance policy and optimal investment strategy are effective ways to manage the insurance portfolios. We shall address these problems and provide methodologies and solutions under various insurance risk models. The insurance company can purchase reinsurance if necessary. We introduce the dividend payments into the insurance risk model, and further complex the problem by allowing the company to inject capital if necessary in order the company to continue its business. This will allow us to consider the problem of optimal reinsurance, dividends and capital injection and formulate the problem in many different ways. There are many problems in this area. First, mathematically, the existence and uniqueness of the solution need to be addressed. We shall investigate this problem under various models. For the optimal dividends and capital injection problem, we will introduce the proportional and fixed transaction costs in the model. In this case, the control problem becomes an impulse control problem. Another formulation is that we assume that the company pays dividends and can buy reinsurance, to solve this problem we again need to solve an impulse control problem. We propose to use the technique of quasi-variational inequalities to solve this kind of optimal control problems. In lieu of seeking closed-form solutions, we will study some simple models first and then extend the results to more general problems. Further, due to the complexity of the generalized stochastic models, it is virtually impossible to obtain closed-form solutions except in some simple cases. Thus numerical schemes are a viable and in many cases only alternative. Effort will be given to obtain some numerical results, and to construct feasible numerical approximation algorithms that can be extended to carry out effective computations on a wide variety of optimization problems arising in actuarial science and finance. . We believe that our work paves a way to stimulate the development of some new and appropriate ideas and methodologies to manage risks of insurance portfolios, and generate plenty of opportunities for further research. We shall adopt some methods and techniques from operations research and mathematical finance in our study, and our study can also provide solution to some problems in finance. Our research will advance our knowledge in decision-making process and risk management, and make significant impact on both actuarial science and finance. 最優分紅，最優再保險和最優投資策略是保險公司資產管理的有效方法。我們會研究這些問題並在不同保險風險模型下解決問題和提供解決問題的方法。 我們的模型包括保險公司可購買再保險，可分紅，也可以融資。我們可以從很多不同的角度考慮問題。首先，從數學上講解的存在唯一性需要研究。 我們會考慮在模型中加入比例和固定交易費，考慮最優分紅和最優融資。我們也會考慮最優分紅和最優再保險模型。為了解決這些問題，我們會用到麥沖控制的一些方法。對一些簡單的模型，我們會給出解析解。而對比較一般的模型，我們會給出有效的數值方法。 我們相信我們的工作會對保險公司資產管理給出一些新的想法和方法，也會推動這一領域的進一步研究。在我們的研究中，我們將會採用運籌學和數理金融學中的一些方法。我們的研究會對精算和金融的發展起到推動作用。

17330816.label: Realisation of objectives
17330816.value: We have addressed all the objectives of this project and obtained very satisfactory results. 10 papers have been published and one has been accepted for publication on the themes of this project. Five of them are in top actuarial science journals and two of them are appeared in a top operational research journal. In Gerber et al. (2018), we study an optimal reinsurance problem in which the first insurer maximizes its expected utility and the premium principle used by the reinsurer is known. Closed-form expressions for the optimal reinsurer's payment and the reinsurer's premium are obtained. In the paper with Chen and Zeng, we use game theoretical approach to study the optimal financing and reinvestment problem, existence of equilibrium strategies is proved. For an exponential utility maximizing game and a probability maximizing game, we obtain semiexplicit solutions. In the paper with Li and Zeng, robust optimal investment and reinsurance strategies are investigated, optimal strategy and optimal value function are derived by applying the stochastic dynamic programming approach. With CI, Dr. Zhu, we have two joint papers on the project. We extend the model to a so called constrained multivariate risk control model and investigate the problem of optimal dividend and refinancing. The second paper appeared in a top OR journal (EJOR) is on dividend optimization for a linear diffusion model with time inconsistent preferences. With CI Dr. Jin, we have one paper on optimal liability ratio and dividend payment strategies with partial information and this paper has been published in EJOR. With Dr. Jin we have two papers i top actuarial science journals, these two papers propose a hybrid deep learning Markov Chain approximation approach to find optimal reinsurance, investment, and dividend strategies for an insurance company in a complex stochastic system.

17330816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17330816.value: We have obtain many very interesting results on the themes of this project. Our findings cover all the objectives of the proposal. First under some relatively simple models, we obtain closed form solutions for optimal reinsurance, optional dividend and optimal investment strategies. We have three papers published on this direction. We consider some models which are more realistic and/or include more factors which are important in real life. for example, in Zhu et al. (2020), using the idea from behavioral economics, we investigate strategic decision making on dividend distribution policies of insurance companies when the management adopts a more realistic way for discounting, namely stochastic quasi-hyperbolic discounting. In Jin et al. (2020), we consider the optimal consumption and investment strategies for households throughout their lifetime. Risks such as the illiquidity of assets, abrupt changes of market states, and lifetime uncertainty are considered. We propose numerical approach to solve optimal reinsurance, optimal dividend and optimal investment problems in more complex models. For example, in Jin et al. (2018), we develop a numerical method to find optimal ergodic (long-run average) dividend strategies in a regime switching model. Using the advantage of recent development of AI and data science, we propose a a hybrid deep learning Markov approximation approach to find optimal reinsurance, investment and dividend strategies for an insurance company in a complex stochastic system. This approach has the advantage of solving high dimensional problems without too much computational cost.

17330816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17330816.value: We have obtained a series considerably interesting results on the theme of this project. Both expected and unexpected results are obtained. There are many possible future research topics on this line. First, we can consider using AI and data science approached to deal with problems with many control variables and/or many state variables. The PI and one of the CI are working on problems on this direction now. The PI has submitted another GRF grant application on this topic.

17330816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17330816.value: Optimal insurance strategy plays an important role in the risk management of insurance portfolios. In this project, we have addressed this problem and provided methodologies and solutions under various insurance risk models. The insurance company can purchase reinsurance if necessary. We introduce the dividend payments into the insurance risk model, and further complex the problem by allowing the company to inject capital if necessary in order the company to continue its business. This will allow us to consider the problem of optimal reinsurance, dividends and capital injection an formulate the problem in many different ways. We have investigated these problems under various models and obtained many considerable interesting results. We have published 11 journal papers under the support of this project. We can further investigate related problems using AI and data science methodologies. We believe that our work paves a way to stimulate the development of some new and appropriate ideas and methodologies to manage risks of insurance portfolios, and generate plenty of opportunities for further research.

17330916.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17330916.value: 新奇的Z2拓撲金屬的量子模擬

17330916.label: Project Objectives
17330916.value: We plan to construct and to look into several physics models of Z2 topological metals (or semimetals) that can be quantum-simulated using artificial systems like cold atoms and superconducting quantum systems. We intend to study the unique topological properties and related exotic effect in this kind of systems, and especially to elucidate how to detect them in the above-mentioned artificial systems.
rows: We plan to construct and to look into several physics models of Z2 topological metals (or semimetals) that can be quantum-simulated using artificial systems like cold atoms and superconducting quantum systems.
We intend to study the unique topological properties and related exotic effect in this kind of systems, and especially to elucidate how to detect them in the above-mentioned artificial systems.

17330916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17330916.value: Since the discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, a lot of research interest has been attracted to explore exotic topological matter both theoretically and experimentally. In particular, significant experimental progress has so far been made for generating various artificial electromagnetic fields and spin-orbit couplings using cold atoms, which may be closely related to topological physics and make cold atom systems a new platform for exploring topological matter, including novel Z2 topological metals whose general theory was very recently established. Considering that cold atoms can now be used to mimic various novel quantum models that may difficultly been implemented in real materials, in this project, we propose to conduct the following cutting-edge research: (1) to design feasible experimental schemes to quantum simulate Z2 topological metals in cold atom systems; and (2) to study in-depth some exotic and unique physical properties of Z2 topological metals and to work out how to detect them with the current cold atom technique. It is expected that the proposed research will make a timely and significant contribution to the fields of topological metals and cold atoms. 自拓撲絕緣體被發現以來， 拓撲量子物質的研究引起了極大的理論和實驗興趣。 鑑於人造系統（如冷原子等）具有很大的調控性， 它們被建議用來模擬和探索拓撲量子物質， 特別是新奇的Z2拓撲金屬。 鑒於此，本項計劃擬開展下例研究。（1）設計可行的實驗方案來量子模擬新奇的Z2拓撲。 （2）深入研究它們的各種拓撲屬性。 預期該項研究將對拓撲金屬和基於人造系統的量子模擬等領域作出及時和有價值的貢獻。

17330916.label: Realisation of objectives
17330916.value: 1. We theoretically proposed and experimentally realized the joint PT invariant Z2-type topological semimetal-bands, via an analogy between the momentum space and a controllable parameter space in superconducting quantum circuits. We clearly imaged an exotic tunable gapless band structure typical of Z2-topological semimetals. Two topological quantum phase transitions, from a topological semimetal to two kinds of insulators, were manipulated by continuously tuning the different parameters in the experimental setup, one of which captures the Z2 topology of the PT semimetal via merging a pair of nontrivial Z2 Dirac points. The topological robustness was demonstrated unambiguously, by adding a perturbation that breaks only the individual T and P symmetries but keeps the joint PT symmetry. Moreover, the novel chiral magnetic effect was emulated for the first time using superconducting quantum circuits 2. We theoretically studied a two-dimension photonic crystal with a kind of honeycomb lattice structure which possesses the joint PT symmetry while P or T symmetry can be broken individually. We found that this kind of Z2 gapless system may be achieved by requiring nonzero imaginary off-diagonal terms in the matrices of permittivity or permeability of the rods in two sub-lattices. This unique two-dimensional band has two gapless Z2 Dirac-like points in its dispersion, which are topologically protected by the PT symmetry and characterized by a Z2 topological charge. Moreover, we studied and found theoretically exotic topological currents in two-dimensional PT-invariant Z2-topological band systems, and especially elucidated how to emulate the unique topological currents arising respectively from the dipolar parity anomaly and chiral magnetic effect in two- and three- dimensional optical lattices.

17330916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17330916.value: A critical concept of topology is fundamentally important in both mathematics and physics. Significant research interest has been paid to topological metals over the years. In this project, based on artificial superconducting quantum circuits and cold atoms, we have proposed and developed new methods for simulating novel topological phenomena that can hardly observed and manipulated in the natural world, which may impact not only on fundamental science but also potential applications. Our research results have been published in top/leading physics journals, and made timely and notable contributions to topological quantum physics.

17332416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17332416.value: 重尾變量的大維協方差矩陣和應用

17332416.label: Project Objectives
17332416.value: Develop a solid probabilistic theory for the eigenvalues of a large sample covariance matrix from a statistical population which is heavy-tailed; By using the theory constructed in (1), develop new statistical techniques applicable to heavy-tailed high-dimensional data; Develop financial applications of the theory derived in the project by analyzing heavy-tailed stock return data from various stock exchange markets such as stock prices listed in the Heng Seng Indexes.

By using the theory constructed in (1), develop new statistical techniques applicable to heavy-tailed high-dimensional data;

Develop financial applications of the theory derived in the project by analyzing heavy-tailed stock return data from various stock exchange markets such as stock prices listed in the Heng Seng Indexes.

17332416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17332416.value: Multivariate methods such as principal components, canonical correlations or factor analysis are well-established tools for data exploration and analysis. However when the number of the variables say p is large compared with the sample size say n, we are faced with a new statistical context, namely the high-dimensional data context. An example of this context is the daily returns of Standard & Poor stocks over two years where the number of variables (returns) is about p=500 and the sample size is about n=500. Another example is the micro-arrays of gene expression data where the number of tissues (sample size n) is in the hundreds while the number of expressed genes (value of p) can be several thousands. In these types of situations, the aforementioned multivariate methods lose their efficiency dramatically; in some situations it is simply impossible for them to be implemented. Statisticians are faced with the modern challenge of developing new tools to handle high-dimensional data. Following several studies that we have previously undertaken in this general area, we propose in this project to investigate several mathematical and statistical problems from a statistical population which is high-dimensional and heavy tailed, the latter property meaning that the population tends to take very large values more frequently than in a standard population where observations tend to group around their averages (or medians). In addition to the already mentioned difficulty of high-dimensions, the new challenge met here in this project is that such heavy-tailed phenomenon implies a larger dispersion, or volatility of the data so that their analysis is more intricate. Based on very recent results from the theory of random matrices, this project aims at the development of new asymptotic theory for a large-dimensional sample covariance matrix from a heavy-tailed population. This theory will cover several types of limiting theorems. In the second phase, we will develop new inference tools constructed from this theory in order to produce appropriate statistical toolboxes for the analysis of high-dimensional and heavy-tailed data. 傳統多元分析方法如主成分、典型相關係數和因子分析已經是完善的數據探索和分析工具。然而，當變量的數目（記作 p）接近或者超過樣本量的數目（記作 n），我們就面臨一個新的統計問題，即高維數據的問題。這種情況的一個例子可以是標準普爾的股票數據：總共p=500個股票，加上在過去兩年裏的的日收益，也就是樣本數約為n = 500。另一個這樣的例子是microarray基因表達數據，樣本數目n是數百個，而表達的基因的數目p 可以是幾千個。對於這樣的高維數據，上述傳統多元分析方法會顯著地失去效率; 有些情況下更是無法使用。統計學因此面臨新的挑戰，需要開發新的工具來處理高維數據。 基於我們先前在這個領域的一些研究，我們在這個項目中建議研究幾個關於一個高維和重尾的統計總體的數學與統計問題。這裏重尾的含義是指該統計總體會更頻繁地生出非常大的數據，而一個常規的總體生出的數據往往圍繞在總體的平均值周圍。如此，除了已經提到的高維數據分析的困難，這個項目會有一個新的挑戰，就是重尾總體意味著觀察數據會有較大的波動，會更加分散，從而導致對它們的分析會變得更複雜。 根據隨機矩陣理論新近的研究結果，該項目旨在開拓重尾總體生成的大維樣本協方差矩陣新的漸近理論。這一理論將涵蓋多種類型的極限定理。在這個理論的基礎上，我們接着會構建用來分析高維和重尾數據的、新的統計工具。

17332416.label: Realisation of objectives
17332416.value: The achievement of the three objectives of the project is as follows. Objectives (1) and (2): --------------------------- As reported in the previous mid-term report, research during the first half period of the project (01/2017-06/2018) has addressed the Objectives (1) and (2) quite completely. The main research output that achieves these two objectives is the JRSS-B paper (Reference [1] below). In this paper, we analysed in detail a sample covariance matrix from a special case of heavy-tailed model, namely high-dimensional spherical mixtures. Limiting distribution of the eigenvalues of such sample covariance matrix is found. Moreover, a new central limit theorem for eigenvalue statistics is also established. The paper contains also applications of the new probabilistic theory to a statistical testing problem. The Objective (1) has been pursued in a follow-up work (Reference [3]). This work extends the theory for the eigenvalues of a large sample covariance matrix from a statistical population which is heavy-tailed in the context of high-frequency stock prices data. In total, these two objectives are achieved fully with the work published in these two papers (References [1]-[3]). Objective (3): ----------------- This objective is first addressed in the work published in the paper [2] during the first half of the project (reported in the mid-term progress report). This work initiated an empirical and exploratory analysis on some selected financial data which have heavy tails. 17332416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17332416.value: In this project, we analysed in detail sample covariance matrices from heavy-tailed data, including high-dimensional spherical mixtures and stock retrun prices from financial markets. Limiting distributions of the eigenvalues of such sample covariance matrices are discovered. Moreover, a new central limit theorem for eigenvalue statistics is also established, see Reference [1] (Section 5.3). Subsequently, we also developed an estimation theory for volatility matrices from high-frequency trading prices in stock markets (References [2]-[3]-[4]). The analysis in [3] establishes the fact that integrated covariance matrices of high-frequency stock prices have a spiked structure. The same paper proposed an effective algorithm to identify such underlying spiked structure. Applications of these tools to data from US and Hong Kong markets confirmed the validity of the proposed model and inference tools. The work in [4] proposed a new forecasting method for the daily volatility matrix using the theory developed in Reference [1] and from the literature of random matrix theory in general. Extensive empirical data analysis established the competitiveness of the proposed forecasting method.

17332416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17332416.value: The spiked model developed in the paper [3] is particularly appealing for the development of a detector for changes in the volatility/co-volatility of high-frequency trading prices in stock markets. A future research could focused on the construction of an efficient detection of sudden changes in price volatility. Such early and efficient detection would be very helpful for markets monitoring in financial industry. Combining the theory and methodology developed in this project, it will be indeed possible to build such efficient detector of sudden market shifts or changes from financial data analysis.

17332416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17332416.value: In this project, we have investigated novel statistical methodology for analysing variations (or volatilities) of trading prices of stock returns. Such financial data have an unique feature called “heavy tails” in mathematical literature. By developing new theories and methods in this project, we are able to provide an accurate description of such price variations in both scenarios of high-frequency trading or accumulated daily prices. The new methodology devised in this project is innovative and its potential impact seems promising. Also one Ph.D student worked on this project and gained cutting-edge knowledge in these fields during the completion of the project.

17333316.label: Project Objectives
17333316.value: To develop a sample preparation method of biological cells based on the freeze-drying method for rapid single-cell ICP-MS assessment of the distribution of the bulk and trace elements in the cells. The sample preparation method should preserve the intracellular elemental contents and prevent loss of mobile ions, such as potassium, during re-suspension of the dried cells in water. To apply the sample preparation method and single-cell ICP-MS to the study cellular response to external stresses of heavy metals and inflammation-inducing agents. The study will be based on the changes in the distribution of ICP-MS intensity of essential and absorbed elements of the biological cells. We propose that the distribution of the ICP-MS intensity of the essential and absorbed elements of the normal cells can be used as the reference for the assessment. The target essential elements include Na, K, Ca, Mg, Co, Cu, Mn, Mo, Zn, and P. The difference in the distribution (peak intensity, peak width, and peak symmetry) of the cells compared to the baseline level and the correlation of the distributions of element pairs (e.g., K/Na and Cr/Mg) may be used for the recognition and possible identification of the type of stress.
