17333316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17333316.value: 我們將會開發一個快速測量大量個體單細胞中主要金屬含量的方法，以評估這些細胞的狀態。金屬是生物的重要組成部分。細胞為確保其正常運作，會維持稳定的細胞金屬－例如鉀和鈉－濃度（金屬穩態）。然而這些金屬含量會因應外來干擾如重金屬和炎症而改變。 我們將使用單細胞電感耦合等離子體質譜法（SC-ICP-MS）來測量個體單細胞的元素含量。SC-ICP-MS是一個非常靈敏的分析技術，可以測量小至十萬個原子或幾個阿克（一克的十億份之一的十億份之一）的元素。因應細胞的天然變化性，SC-ICP-MS測量可產生細胞群體中目標元素的ICP-MS訊號強度的分佈。這些分佈是評估細胞活力的基礎。這些分佈或不同元素的分佈的相關性的變化可以是細胞受到外來干擾的指標。檢視分佈的相關性也可能是研究細胞變化性的可行方法。 該研究項目的主要部份在於開發細胞的樣品製備方法，以確保細胞內的元素含量沒有流失或受到污染。當前應用離心機分離和使用生理鹽水漂洗的方法嚴重干擾細胞的滲透平衡。在細胞清洗過程中，細胞可能會失去部分可移動的基本元素(例如鉀)和吸收了一些外來元素（例如鈉）。改變細胞中鉀和鈉的比例會影響細胞的活力。我們建議使用冷凍乾燥的方法去保存细胞的元素含量。使用了這個新的樣品製備方法，將可快速和準確地用SC-ICP-MS去測量細胞的基本元素－尤其是可移動元素－的分佈，從而快速地評估這些細胞的狀態。 我們將使用綠藻和巨噬細胞作為該研究項目的細胞模型。綠藻的生命力頑強而且易於處理，是方法開發的理想工具。巨噬細胞沒有細胞壁、易受樣品製備過程中滲透作用的影嚮，是評估冷凍乾燥樣品製備法的可行性的理想模型。同時，這些細胞對外來刺激反應迅速，是研究細胞因外來刺激而改變金屬含量的合適工具。

17333316.label: Realisation of objectives
17333316.value: We have investigated the proposed freeze-drying method for the preparation of single cells for sample introduction to the ICP. We have developed a custom setup with the aim of rapid freezing and drying of biological cells in its original culture medium. We used microliters of suspension of a model biological cell (Chlorella vulgaris) in Bold's basal medium (BBM) in the investigation. We have encountered problems in the drying process of the 1-mm frozen droplet under vacuum (0.1-10 mtorr). The problems stem from the slow evaporation rate of the solvent. It took approximately 20-30 minutes to completely evaporate the solvent (water). Fast drying is essential to avoid melting via the mechanism of freezing-point depression. During the prolonged drying process, the frozen droplets melted and the salts in BBM formed micron-sized crystals. The relatively large crystals interfere with single-cell ICP-MS measurement as the crystals give large ICP-MS intensity spikes when they are introduced into the ICP along with the single cells. We have tested several methods to enhance the evaporation rate, but melting and crystal formation persisted. These include introduction of an argon stream to sweep away the evaporated water vapor, use of different temperature to freeze the sample droplets in order to produce ice of different morphology (large crystal versus amorphous crystalline), and commercial freeze-drying instrument. We have also spread the sample on various substrate (alumina, paraffin, and cellulose) to increase the surface area of the sample so as to increase the evaporation rate. The evaporation rate was indeed increased. However, the dried cells adhered to the substrate strongly and were difficult to dislodge for suspension in argon for sample introduction. We have switched our main effort in the development of a different approach of sample preparation by using electrospray to produce single cells in the atmosphere for sample introduction into the ICP (more details in the next paragraph). Nonetheless, we have continued to test different approaches to enhance the freeze-drying method. These include dilution of the BBM with water immediately before freezing in order to reduce freezing point depression, mixing the BBM with various proportion of solvents of low boiling point such as methanol, and spraying the cell suspension to produce fine droplets (micron sized) and deposition of the fine droplets on PTFE film for freezing drying. We have succeeded in enhancing the evaporation rate and avoiding the formation of large micron-sized crystals. However, the freeze-drying sample preparation method requires further development to enhance the sample introduction efficiency. We have also investigated electrospray methods for preparation-free sample introduction to the ICP for single-cell analysis. We hope that the new method will allow us to investigate cellular responses to external stresses as indicated in Objective Number 2. We have developed electrodes of different materials (graphite and stainless steel) and shape and dimension (fine metal pins, sharpened graphite rods, and stainless-steel nibs with micron-sized central channel) for direct spraying of the sample-cell suspension into fine aerosols. We have also optimized the pH of the cell suspension for efficient cell spraying. We have achieved reproducible electrospray of the microliters of algal cell suspension in BBM. The cell collection efficiency is approximately 20%. The sprayed aerosols contain single cells that appear to be intact despite application of strong electric field to the cell suspension for hundreds of seconds. We are in the process of building a complete experimental setup with (1) corona discharge to neutralize the electrical charges on the sample cells which are acquired in the electrospraying process and (2) Venturi pump to collect the suspended neutralized single cells in an argon stream for sample introduction into the ICP. Preliminary results of the electrospray method have been presented in an international conference (European Winter Conference of Plasma Spectrochemistry (EWCPS 2019), February 3-8, 2019, Paris). We anticipate a further 6 to 8 months for the completion and optimization of the setup. Unfortunately, the PI is due to retire by the end of June 2019 and was asked by the University to complete and submit the final report before retirement. This final report will be not able to document the development and application of the electrospray method for single-cell ICP-MS analysis of cellular contents of biological cells under external stresses. We have also investigated the fundamental processes of particle vaporization in the ICP. The work is essential for efficient and accurate single-cell analysis using ICP-MS. We have identified a previously unknown factor, namely the difference in the ICP gas temperature and the boiling point of the sample particles, which has strong effect on the accuracy and precision of single-particle ICP-MS measurement. We have used a sheath flow device to confine the sample particles at precise radial location of ICP and conclusively demonstrated the effects of plasma gas temperature at different radial position on the precision and accuracy of the single-particle analysis. We have also refined our thermal model for computing the degree of vaporization of the model particles (ytterbium oxide) to identify the critical factors under the conditions of small difference in the gas temperature and boiling point (100 degree Celsius or less). We have shown that the calibration curve of measured intensity versus particle mass is non-linear and large particles may give intensity smaller than small particles because of their large heat capacity. The potential errors can be avoided by measurement of the single-particles at ICP vertical location of gas temperature at least a few hundred degree higher than the particle boiling point. The findings have been presented in EWCPS 2019.

17333316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17333316.value: We have developed a preparation-free sample introduction method for single-cell ICP-MS measurement by direct deposition of biological cells in culture medium onto an electrode and application of high electric field to the cell suspension. The method potentially will allow rapid and accurate measurement of the cellular elemental contents because the biological cells are not subjected to the osmotic stresses of cell cleaning and mechanical stress of solution nebulization. Further development and optimization of the experimental setup, however, is required for the application of the method to the target analysis. We have gained experience and insight into freeze-drying of biological suspension. We have investigated methods to improve the evaporation rate of the solvent in order to avoid melting of the frozen sample due to freezing point depression and formation of crystals of the culture medium which may interfere with the single-cell ICP-MS measurement. We have also gained new insight into the particle vaporization process in the ICP. The difference in ICP gas temperature and particle boiling point is identified as a critical parameter for accurate and precise single-particle and single-cell ICP-MS measurement.

17333316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17333316.value: The electrospray method is potentially a rapid preparation-free method for single cells introduction to the ICP. Further development of the experimental setup may result in a device that has commercial value as an attachment to the ICP for single-cell analysis.

17333316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17333316.value: Measurement of the cellular elemental contents of individual biological cells provides useful information of the status of the cells, such as the growth phases of the cells and the presence of external stresses. Such information is lost in bulk analysis of biological cells. Single-cell ICP-MS is sufficiently sensitive for the measurement of the elemental cellular contents of individual cells, such as magnesium, sodium, and potassium. However, conventional sample introduction method of ICP-MS by solution nebulization introduces excessive mechanical stress on the cells which may change the cellular contents of the mobile elements unintentionally. Cleanup of the culture medium is also necessary using solution nebulization in order to reduce the ICP-MS background. The procedures introduce osmotic stress which may also change the cellular contents. The electrospray method developed in this project is a preparation-free method for introduction of biological cells into the ICP without mechanical and osmotic stresses. The method will allow rapid analysis of biological cells in its original state for the diagnosis of diseases such as the presence of inflammation-inducing agents (bacteria and toxins) and the investigation of environmental toxicology of heavy metals and other environmental pollutants on the cells.

17333616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17333616.value: 鉍化合物已被用於治療各種疾病一個多世紀，鉍藥物於抗生素一起的三聯和四聯療法目前用於治療幽門螺桿菌感染的臨床上。更重要的是，鉍的藥物是在消除抗生素抗性幽門螺桿菌菌株沒有明顯的毒性，並且有效。 幽門螺桿菌是一種革蘭氏陰性細菌，超過半數人口的胃中有該病菌。為了在人的胃腸道生存, 幽門螺旋桿菌採用複雜的調控網絡，尤其金屬調控網絡為代謝提供能量，維持最佳生長pH, 獲取必需的營養金屬和抵禦環境壓力。這樣的系統的功能性破壞將導致細菌定植和發病機制失敗，最終導致其消滅。之前我們已經進行了廣泛的體外研究對鉍藥物金屬蛋白/金屬酶或金屬伴侶蛋白的相互作用從幽門螺旋桿菌，包括Hpn, HspA, HspB和HypA。使用一個綜合金屬蛋白質組學技術，包括我們自己設計的GE-ICP-MS, 我們已經確定了鉍結合蛋白和結合位點，隨後分析了這些蛋白質。根據這些數據，我們推測鉍藥物可以結合到關鍵酶的活性位點，從而導致多種必要的（病理）生理學途徑的中斷是用於細菌生存和定植至關重要。 我們已初步克隆，過表達和純化假定鉍目標AhpC，UreG和DnaK，並進行了一些初步的生物活性測試，這表明幽門螺桿菌AhpC和脲酶的酶活性在補充次枸櫞酸鉍均顯著抑制細菌培養基。在本項目中，我們將通過金屬蛋白質組學與生化/生物物理與分子生物學的方法驗證目標蛋白，了解鉍藥物抗幽門螺旋桿菌的抗菌作用的分子機制。具體地講，申請人打算： 1）進行鉍抗菌藥物的推定蛋白指標的分子克隆和過表達和純化蛋白，包括AhpC，UreG，及DnaK; 2）通過生化和生物物理技術在體外測定鉍藥物與蛋白質結合性質，包括結合化學計量; 3）通過生物測定研究含鉍藥物對蛋白質靶點功能的影響; 4）運用基因敲除進一步驗證鉍藥物对體內蛋白質的功能的破壞; 本研究將大大提升對鉍抗菌藥物對致病菌幽門螺旋桿菌的分子機制，並为金屬類抗菌劑對微生物的作用機理提供新的啟示。本研究的長期目標是建立一個金屬藥物機理研究的綜合平台，以了解金屬在生命過程和醫藥中的作用，並培養年輕一代科學家。

17333616.label: Realisation of objectives
17333616.value: Metal ions have been historically used as antimicrobial agents and disinfectants even prior to the discovery of antibiotics. Certain metal ions have the ability to disrupt antibiotic-resistant biofilms and even kill multi-drug resistant bacteria e.g. MRSA. Very recently, silver has been demonstrated to boost antibiotic efficacy 10-1000 times against Gram-negative bacteria and to restore antibiotic susceptibility to a resistant bacterial strain Bismuth compounds have long been used for bacterial infection, particularly Helicobacter pylori infection. Importantly, bismuth drugs are even effective in eradicating antibiotic-resistant H. pylori strains without apparent toxicity, leading to development of a single capsule triple-therapy which was approved for clinic application years ago. The applicant and his coworkers have previously carried out extensive in vitro studies on the interactions of bismuth drugs with metalloproteins/ metalloenzymes or metallochaperones. Using an home-made metalloproteomic approach including our home-made GE-ICP-MS, we have identified bismuth binding proteins and binding motifs, and subsequently analyzed these proteins via bioinformatics. We hypothesize that bismuth drugs might bind to active sites of key enzymes, leading to disruption of multiple essential (patho)physiological pathways which is crucial for bacterial survival and colonization. As proposed, in this project, we have carried out large amount of work in the following: We overexpress and purify the proteins including Ahpc, UreG, Fur and Dnak. Alkyl hydroperoxide reductase subunit C (AhpC) is the most abundant 2-cysteine peroxiredoxin, crucial for H. pylori survival in the host by defense of oxidative stress. We demonstrated that CBS binds to the highly conserved cysteine residues (Cys49 and Cys169) with a dissociation constant (Kd) of Bi(III) to AhpC of 3.0×10−24 M. Significantly the interaction of CBS with AhpC disrupts the peroxiredoxin and chaperone activities of the enzyme both in vitro and in bacterial cells, leading to attenuated bacterial survival. We also demonstrated that Bi(III) also perturbs AhpC relocation between the cytoplasm and membrane region in decomposing the exogenous ROS. Our study suggests that disruption of redox homeostasis by bismuth drugs via interaction with key enzymes such as AhpC contributes to their antimicrobial activity. The work was published in J Biol Inorg Chem (2018) Using an integrative metallopmics approach, we uncover 63 bismuth-binding and 119 bismuth-regulated proteins from Helicobacter pylori. Through bioinformatics analysis in combination with bioassays, we demonstrate that bismuth drugs disrupt multiple essential pathways in the pathogen including ROS defense and pH buffering by binding and functional perturbation of a number of key enzymes. Moreover, we discover that DnaK may serve as a new target of bismuth drugs to inhibit bacterium-host cell adhesion. The effect of bismuth drugs on the function of the protein was examined. Our approach provides a novel strategy to unveil molecular mechanisms of antimicrobial metals against pathogens in general. This study sheds light on the design of new types of antimicrobial agents with multiple targets to tackle current crisis of antimicrobial resistance. The work was published in Chem Sci (2017) and Inorg Chem (2019), and Curr Opin Chem Biol (2020). We have successfully completed all objectives as proposed. Our studies significantly improve our understanding on the molecular mechanism of bismuth antimicrobial drugs against pathogenic H. pylori and other bacteria, and shed light on the mechanism of other metallo-antimicrobials against microbes and probably on virus. Through this study, we have strengthened the home-made integrative platform for mechanistic study of metallodrugs to understand the roles of metals for medical applications. We have tentatively established a HKU-CAS joint laboratory of Metallomics on Health and Environment very recently. Our data have been published and we were invited to write reviews and book chapters. Junior scientists were trained and their work was recognized as revealed from awards in international conferences. The PI was also invited to serve as a guest editor to edit a special issue of “bismuth- a magic element” for Inorganic chemistry (ACS) which was published March 16 issue (2020, 59(6)). Croucher advanced study institute (ASI) on Metals in Medicine was awarded to the PI to organize an ASI in Hong Kong, December, 2019 (postponed due to the unrest and pandemic). Through this study, new medicinal applications of bismuth drug were found. For example, we have found that bismuth drugs can serve as an adjuvant to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and effectively suppress SARS-CoV-2 replication and relieves virus-associated pneumonia in Syrian hamsters. Both works are worth continuing in view of their impacts to the current society. I believe that anti-SARS-CoV-2 of bismuth agents is highly original, and it is truly created in Hong Kong. A RGC RIF project was awarded partially based the data from this project and a CRF (as well as ITF) application was submitted for the latter. The only problem is the limited funding size (HK$560,824). It will be much better to increase the funding size to 1-2-1.8 million for three years.

17333616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17333616.value: Bismuth compounds have long been used for bacterial infection, particularly Helicobacter pylori infection. Importantly, bismuth drugs are even effective in eradicating antibiotic-resistant H. pylori strains without apparent toxicity, the underlining mechanism is not well understood. The applicant and his coworkers have previously carried out extensive in vitro studies on the interactions of bismuth drugs with metalloproteins/ metalloenzymes or metallochaperones. Using an integrative metalloproteomic approach including our home-made GE-ICP-MS, we have identified bismuth binding proteins and binding motifs, and subsequently analyzed these proteins via bioinformatics. We hypothesize that bismuth drugs might bind to active sites of key enzymes, leading to disruption of multiple essential (patho)physiological pathways which is crucial for bacterial survival and colonization. In this project, we have cloned, overexpressed and purified putative bismuth targets AhpC, UreG and Fur and carried out extensive bioassay. We showed that the enzymatic activities of H. pylori AhpC and urease were significantly inhibited upon supplementation of bismuth agents to bacterial culture medium. We further validated binding properties such as binding stoichiometry, affinity of bismuth drugs with these proteins. We also examined the effect of bismuth drugs on the function of the protein targets through variety of bioassays including gene knock out. These studies significantly improve our understanding on the molecular mechanism of bismuth antimicrobial drugs against pathogenic H. pylori and shed light on the mechanism of other metallo-antimicrobials against microbes and importantly on virus. Through this study, we have established an integrative platform for mechanistic study of metallodrugs to understand the roles of metals for medical applications, and tentatively establish a HKU-CAS joint laboratory of Metallomics on Health and Environment. Our data have been published and we were invited to write reviews and book chapters. Junior scientists were trained. Through this study, new medicinal applications of bismuth drug were found to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and anti-SARS-Co-V-2. A RGC RIF project was awarded partially based the data from this project.

17333616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17333616.value: The integrative approach consisting of metalloproteomics, bioinformatice and deep learning can be readily extended to understand and predict function of metalloproteins, the role of metals in medicine and environmental science. Subsequent mechanistic study of Bi(III)-proteome in H. pylori allows us to discover new drug targets (e.g. UreG and DnaK) (please see the publication list) in the pathogens, leading to discovery of new medicinal applications of Bi(III) drugs. The anti-SARS-CoV-2 of Bi(III) drugs both in vitro and in vivo opens a new horizon for fighting against the virus. We believe that these new medicinal application of Bi(III) complexes/drugs are worth doing downstream work. A patent is filed on the new applications and a paper was published in Nature Microbiology (5, pages1439–1448) which attracted enormous attention. Over 20 media reported the discovery. A proposal was submitted towards COVID-19 by Bi(III) drugs.

17333616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17333616.value: Metal compounds have long been associated with medicine. Due to its low toxicity, bismuth compounds have been used for bacterial infection, particularly Helicobacter pylori infection for decades. Interestingly, bismuth drugs are even effective in eradicating antibiotic-resistant H. pylori strains, a single capsule triple-therapy was approved for clinic application years ago. It is long believed that proteins and enzymes are targets of bismuth drugs/agents. In this project, we have established an integrative platform to identify Bi(III)-binding protein in pathogens. We then overexpressed, purified and carried out extensive bioassay. We further validated binding properties such as binding stoichiometry, affinity of bismuth drugs with these proteins. We then examined the effect of bismuth drugs on the function of the protein targets. Our study significantly improves our understanding on the molecular mechanism of bismuth antimicrobial drugs against pathogens. Through this project, we have established an integrative platform for mechanistic study of metallodrugs to understand the roles of metals for medical applications. and tentatively established a HKU-CAS joint laboratory of Metallomics on Health and Environment. Junior scientists were trained through this study. Importantly, new medicinal applications of bismuth drug were found, e.g. overcoming antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and anti-SARS-Co-V-2 activity.

17334216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17334216.value: There has been a long-standing interest and history in one-dimensional or quasi-1D chain-like structures and materials. The most well-known are the platinum chains as exemplified by the famous double salts. These 1D chain structures have attracted much attention not only from chemists in terms of their structure and bonding, but also from solid-state physicists given their unique electronic, optical and potential “molecular-wire” properties. These 1D chain double salts show a linear array of metal centres separated by short metal-metal contacts, which was believed to be a result of mainly electrostatic interactions between alternating cationic and anionic square-planar metal-ligand moieties. Interestingly, 1D chain structures have also been observed in square-planar metal complexes that bear the same charge, which is to the contrary of electrostatic or coulombic repulsion. Non-covalent metal-metal interactions are thought to be responsible for the observed supramolecular ordering. Relativistic effects and dispersion forces also account for the short metal-metal contacts. As electrostatic interactions alone cannot account for the observed findings in double salts and given their high insolubility that often renders their studies difficult, in the proposed project attempts will be made to design highly soluble metal-ligand chromophoric complexes of various different metal centres and their double salts for an in-depth systematic study to elucidate a complicated array of factors and the interplay of the different interacting forces that govern their structural arrangements, namely coulombic versus dispersion forces and metal-metal interactions as well as the involvement of π-π, hydrophobic-hydrophobic and hydrophilic-hydrophilic interactions. Efforts will also be made to explore the supramolecular homo- and hetero- assembly and oligomerization/polymerization of the metal-ligand chromophoric building blocks and to determine the thermodynamics and kinetics of the 1D and 2D supramolecular assemblies and networks, their growth dynamics, mechanisms and their associated thermodynamic and kinetic parameters, which should lead to an understanding of the thermodynamic and kinetic control of the supramolecular assembly and oligomerization/polymerization processes. It is envisaged that an understanding and correlation of the spectroscopic, electronic absorption, luminescence and functional properties as well as the underlying factors that lead to the control of their homo- and hetero- assembly and supramolecular oligomerization/polymerization as well as morphologies would provide insights into their structure-property relationships and guiding principles important for the future directed assembly and construction of functional supramolecular assemblies. 對一維或準一維鏈狀結構和材料的研究已經有長久的興趣和歷史。其中最廣為人知的就是以其複鹽為代表的金屬鉑鏈狀化合物。這些一維鏈狀結構不僅在結構和成鍵形式方面引起了化學家們的關注，其獨特的電學、光學和潛在的分子線的特性也讓固態物理學家對它們產生了極大興趣。這些一維鏈狀复鹽由短金屬—金屬鍵的金屬中心呈現線性排列，一般認為這是由陰陽離子交替的平面四邊形金屬配體模塊之間的靜電作用導致。然而有趣的是，帶有同種電荷的平面四邊形金屬配合物之間也能形成一維鏈狀結構。這一現象是違反靜電或庫侖排斥作用的，因此相信非共價的金屬—金屬相互作用導至這種超分子的有序排列。此外，相對論效應和色散力也有助於形成這種短的金屬—金屬相互作用。但是僅僅有靜電作用力的存在並不能解釋复鹽中的這種現象，而且其產物的低溶性給這方面的研究增添了難度。在本研究項目中，我們將努力設計出高度可溶的不同金屬中心的金屬—配體有色配合物及其複鹽，並通過對它們的深入和系統的研究來闡釋導致結構重排的不同力之間的相互作用，包括有庫侖色散力、金屬—金屬相互作用以及π-π、疏水—疏水和親水—親水相互作用的各種複雜因素。此外，我們還將努力探索基於這些金屬—配體有色構築模塊的超分子均向和異相組裝以及低聚或高聚反應，並確定一維和二維超分子組裝體和網狀結構的熱力學和動力學、生長動力、機理及相關的熱力學和動力學參數，從而對超分子組裝和低聚或高聚過程中的熱力學和動力學控制有所了解。可以預見的是，對光譜及電子吸收、發光功能性質；控制均相和異相組裝、超分子低聚或高聚以及超分子形貌及形態結構的潛在因素的相關性的理解，有助於進一步深入了解結構與性能的關係，為未來的導向組裝和構建功能性超分子組裝體提供重要的指導作用。

17335616.label: Realisation of objectives
17335616.value: I initiated the theory of sub-VMRT structures. Earlier works of the theory included an article of Mok in Sci. Chin. Math (2008), 2 joint articles of Hong-Mok in 2010 (JDG) and 2013 (JAG), and an article of Mok-Zhang in 2019 (JDG). The main objective of the current project was to generalize the existing theory and to apply them to problems in Algebraic Geometry and Complex Analysis. OBJECTIVE 1: The problem of rigidity for substructures for a pair (X’;X) of rational homogeneous subspaces of Picard number 1 of sub-diagram type such that X’ is non-linear, e.g., a sub-Grassmannian of rank ≥ 2 of a Grassmannian, was solved in the affirmative by Mok-Zhang. Writing Y for the VMRT of X at a point z on X’, and Y’ for the sub-VMRT at X defined by tangential intersection, then Y’ is the same as the VMRT of X’ at z. Write P for the parabolic subgroup of G = Aut(X) at z. For the proof of the rigidity of the pair (X’;X) it was essential to make use of a notion of parallel transport of sub-VMRTs along a minimal rational curve, which relies on the fact that for any p in P such that p.Y’ is tangent to Y’ at one point, we have p.Y’ = Y’. This uniqueness property relies on the compactness of the P-orbit of [Y’] in the Chow scheme of X, which fails when (X’;X) is not of sub-diagram type. A proto-typical case not of sub-diagram type is given by the pair (Z’;Z) where Z = G(n,n) with n at least 3 and Z’ is the Lagrangian Grassmannian, i.e., type-III Grassmannian of rank n. A general sufficient condition which works in particular for the proto-typical case of (Z’;Z) was established in [1]. Let (X’;X) be an admissible pair of irreducible Hermitian symmetric spaces of the compact type such that X’ is non-linear and denote by (Y’;Y) the pair of VMRTs of X’ resp. X. In [1] a new method by means of dilatation of sub-VMRT structures using Harish-Chandra coordinates was invented, and a fitting condition (F) was introduced for the pair (Y’;Y), which can be checked in terms of the projective geometry of the embedding of Y’ in Y, and we proved the following general result. MAIN THEOREM: Let (X’;X) be an admissible pair of irreducible Hermitian symmetric spaces of the compact type of rank ≥ 2, 0 ∈ X’ ⊂ X. Suppose the corresponding pair of VMRTs (Y’,Y) of X’ resp. X at the base point 0 is nondegenerate for substructures and it satisfies Condition (F). Assume furthermore that the restriction map r : Γ(X,T(X)) → Γ(X’,T(X)|X’) defined by r(η) = η|X’ is surjective. Then, (X’;X) is rigid. OBJECTIVE 2: Given a local complex submanifold S on a uniruled projective manifold (X,K) equipped with a minimal rational component such that S is equipped with a sub-VMRT structure defined by tangential intersection with VMRTs, sufficient conditions were found in Mok-Zhang (2019) to guarantee that S is saturated in (X,K) in the sense that the germ of a minimal rational curve tangent to S at some smooth point must necessarily lie on S. Denoting by Y the VMRT of X at a general point s on S, and by Y’ the sub-VMRT at s of S obtained by tangential intersection, the most important part of the sufficient conditions was based on the computation of the common kernel of a family of linear operators defined by a modification of the second fundamental form of Y’ in Y. The criterion was made quantitative by introducing a certain notion of q-nondegeneracy for substructures. In the current project I realized that when X is a general linear section of sufficiently small codimension in a Grassmannian, and S is modelled on the family of corresponding linear sections X’ a sub-Grassmannian G(r,s) of G(p,q), the Recognition Problem should be solved for S ⊂ X by using the notion of q-nondegeneracy for substructures and the decomposition of the tangent bundle of a Grassmannian as a tensor product. Since the former concept had already appeared in print (Mok-Zhang 2019), the problem was used for research training. The method was communicated to Wang Chuwen in 2019, a senior undergraduate student at HKU, who worked out a result in this direction in his report written for the Mathematics Project done under my supervision. [Wa] Wang, C.: Geometric substructures on uniruled projective manifolds and the recognition problem OBJECTIVE 3: For a pair (X’;X) with VMRTs (Y’;Y) the existence of a projective compactification for VMRT substructures modelled on (X’;X) has been proven under some strong pseudoconcavity condition on the cycle D ⊂ K’, where D corresponds to the Chow scheme of minimal rational curves passing through a general point of X’. OBJECTIVE 4：We found important applications of the sub-VMRT theory. In Algebraic Geometry, going beyond Hong-Mok (2013), Hong-Mok[2] (in the prestigious journal Selecta Mathematica) proved Schur rigidity of all non-linear smooth Schubert cycles on a rational homogeneous space of Picard number 1. Theorem 1.1. Let S = G/P be a rational homogeneous space of Picard number 1 and S’ be a non-linear smooth Schubert variety on S. Let Z ⊂ S be a cycle homologous to a positive integral multiple of [S’]. Then, Z is a finite sum of translates g.S’ by elements g ∈ G. In Complex Analysis, making use of sub-VMRT theory, including the novel result [1] of Mok for the case of Hermitian symmetric subspaces S’ ⊂ S for S = G/P of Hermitian symmetric type, Kim-Mok-Seo[3] studied proper holomorphic maps between irreducible bounded symmetric domains of type I, II or III. In what follows for positive integers p and q, D(p,q) denotes the type-I domain consisting of q-by-p matrices Z with complex coefficients satisfying the matrix inequality I – Z*Z > 0, where Z* denotes the conjugate of the transpose of Z, a type-II (resp. type-III) domain of rank n consists of skew-symmetric (resp. symmetric) n-by-n matrices with complex coefficients satisfying the same inequality. Theorem 1.2. Let Ω and Ω’ be irreducible bounded symmetric domains of rank q and q’ respectively such that q, q’ ≥ 2. Suppose q’ < 2q – 1, and that furthermore either 1) Ω and Ω’ are of the same type I, II or III, or 2) Ω is of type III and Ω’ is of type I. Then, up to compositions with automorphisms of Ω and Ω’, every proper holomorphic map f : Ω → Ω’ is of the form f(z) = L(g(z)), where for some irreducible bounded symmetric domain Ω” we have g: Ω → Ω × Ω”, g(z) = (z,h(z)) for some holomorphic map h: Ω → Ω” , and where L: Ω × Ω” → Ω’ is a totally geodesic holomorphic embedding. Theorem 1.3. There exists no proper holomorphic map from Ω to Ω’ if (1) Ω is a type-I domain D(p,q) and Ω’ is a type-III domain of rank q’ such that q’ < 2q-1; or (2) Ω is a type-II domain of rank n and Ω’ is a type-I domain D(p’,q’) or a type-III domain of rank q’ such that 3 ≤ q’< 2[n/2] – 1, where [y] stands for the largest integer not exceeding the real number y.

17335616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17335616.value: The theory of varieties of minimal rational tangents (VMRTs) on uniruled projective manifolds X, to be called VMRT geometry, was a geometric theory invented by Hwang-Mok in the 1990s characterized by the specification of tangents to minimal rational curves (belonging to a minimal rational component K). Taking minimal rational curves on (X,K) as being analogues to geodesics in Riemannian geometry, there is the notion of sub-VMRT geometry analogous to sub-Riemannian geometry. Sub-VMRT geometry is the study of (local) complex submanifolds of (X,K) defined by sub-VMRTs which are intersections of VMRTs with tangent subspaces. Whereas in sub-Riemannian geometry there is the class of distinguished subsets S called totally geodesic subsets, characterized by the property that the germ of a geodesic curve tangent to S at a smooth point must necessarily lie on S, there is the analogue of K-saturated (complex-analytic) subvarieties S on (X,K) characterized by the fact that the germ of a minimal rational curve tangent to S at a smooth point must necessarily lie on S. The current project focuses on the study of K-saturated subvarieties S on (X,K) and their compactifications inside X as uniruled projective subvarieties. It was found in [1] that, in the case of sub-VMRT structures modelled on admissible pairs of rational homogeneous spaces (X’;X) of the Hermitian symmetric type, a rigidity phenomenon holds under conditions verifiable in terms of the projective geometry of the pair (Y’;Y) of VMRTs, where Y is a VMRT of X, and Y’ is the intersection of Y with a projectivized tangent space of X’, without the assumption that (X’;X) is of sub-diagram type. As an outcome from the project, the scope of applicability of sub-VMRT geometry is much widened. It has now been applied in Hong-Mok[2] to prove the Schur rigidity of any pair (Z’;Z) consisting of a rational homogeneous space Z=G/P of Picard number 1 and a non-linear smooth Schubert cycle Z’⊂Z. Furthermore, passing to moduli spaces of characteristic submanifolds, it was found in Kim-Mok-Seo[3] that sub-VMRT geometry is a powerful tool in the study of proper holomorphic maps between irreducible bounded symmetric domains of rank ≥ 2, yielding semi-rigidity theorems and nonexistence theorems for various such pairs (Ω’;Ω). Coupled with works of the PI and his students on holomorphic isometries in Kähler geometry, sub-VMRT geometry has now provided an interface for the study of rigidity phenomena in Complex Differential Geometry, Algebraic Geometry and Several Complex Variables.

17335616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17335616.value: The problem of rigidity for sub-VMRT structures has been formulated in Mok-Zhang (2019) for admissible pairs of rational homogeneous spaces of Picard number 1. In the current project the rigidity problem has been studied for pairs (Z’;Z) where Z is an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space of the compact type and Z’ is also (necessarily) Hermitian symmetric, and on pairs (Z’;Z) where Z = G/P is an arbitrary rational homogeneous space of Picard number 1, and Z’ is a smooth (and not necessarily homogeneous) Schubert cycle on Z. There are two directions for generalizations. On the one hand, we can study admissible pairs in the case where Z is not Hermitian symmetric and Z’⊂ Z is not necessarily a Schubert cycle. On the other hand, we can restrict to Schubert cycles on Z = G/P of Picard number 1 and consider singular Schubert cycles on Z. These problems also have applications both to the question of Schur rigidity for singular Schubert cycles and for rigidity of horizontal proper maps between flag domains on rational homogeneous spaces, and the aggregate of such problems may be formulated as a future proposal for a GRF grant of the HKRGC.

17335616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17335616.value: On smooth manifolds there is the theory of Riemannian geometry, where one measures lengths of tangent vectors and angles between them. Geometric structures modelled on VMRTs, as developed by Hwang-Mok, constitute a geometric theory on important projective manifolds such as Fano manifolds arising from the sets of tangents to minimal rational curves on the manifolds. Of special interest in Riemannian geometry are the geodesic curves, and in VMRT theory the analogues are the minimal rational curves (“lines”). Taking these heuristically as geodesics, a major difference is that such geodesics only exist for special sets of tangent directions (corresponding to null geodesics in the example of the complexified Minkowski space in Special Relativity). In analogy to the characterization of totally geodesic subvarieties in Riemannian geometry, we consider the set of linearly saturated local complex submanifolds S on a uniruled projective manifold X, characterized analogously by the property that the germ of a line of X tangent to S at one smooth point must necessarily lie entirely on S. We have been able to characterize such S by means of the projective second fundamental form on VMRTs and found important applications to Algebraic Geometry, Several Complex Variables and Complex Differential Geometry.

17501516.label: Project Objectives
17501516.value: To empirically document the transformation and characteristics of the mass media market. To build a framework that captures the key features of the mass media market and characterize the equilibrium in that market. To investigate how the quality of the media affects the attention allocation of readers and how readers' decisions in turn affect the quality and influence of the media. To analyze the comparative statics of the equilibrium in this model, which will shed light on a number of important and relevant issues in the media market, including the effect of new media entrants on existing news outlets, the effect of the changing cost of readers' attention on the media market structure, and the effect of correlation in information production across news outlets on the media industry.

17501516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501516.value: 數位化時代裡，有關資訊傳遞的技術進步讓傳播媒體經歷了重大的轉變。比如與互聯網這一資訊載體的發展刺激了舊媒體向新媒體的過渡。本研究項目綜合了日益變化的大眾傳媒的主要特徵，為新時代下的媒體競爭提供了研究框架。 首先，讀者可以以近乎零成本來從大量的資訊媒介獲取資訊，而非傳統的從有限的媒體機構購買資訊資料。然而，這勢必產生了新的局限:資訊氾濫以及關注有限。其次，獲取資訊的廉價成本表明一個媒體機構受到的關注度遠比其讀者數量這一空洞的數字更具代表性，因而媒體機構開始關注前者而非後者。進一步說，讀者量增加帶來的關注度增加（集約邊際）比單純讀者量的增加（廣義邊際）更重要，於是對前者（吸引關注）的競爭就比後者（最大化讀者數）更意義深遠。第三，壟斷競爭最能代表媒體機構間的競爭，原因有三：媒體機構的產品（新聞）總是相似但不同質的；資訊生產商的數量巨大；每一個中間媒介並不能影響到整個市場的資訊容量。第四，媒介機構在資訊品質上競爭:他們不僅注重如何清晰的呈現新聞，同時也強調資訊來源的準確度。由於公民新聞或者說市民新聞的繁榮加重了人們對新聞品質退化的擔憂，新聞的品質競爭也就更加突出。 我們將結合這些新的特徵建立模型，研究媒介品質，媒介影響力以及讀者的注意力分配如何互相影響。模型框架會基於發送者-接收者模型以及注意力分配和內生資訊獲取的相關文獻，同時也會結合已有媒體經濟學理論研究的成果。模型將概括大量媒體機構（資訊發送者）和讀者（決策者）。雙邊的遊戲參與者都會做出內生的資訊選擇。發送者選擇資訊的品質和呈現資訊的方式。接收者決定關注哪一個發送者以及以多大程度關注。媒體獲取的關注度會帶來收入，這讓媒體機構有動力投資耗費成本的資訊。 我們期望這個研究項目可以提供一個研究新媒體特徵的框架，並給予以往文獻裡缺失的理論預測。我們初步的研究顯示讀者的資訊決策對媒體市場的架構以及總的信息量有深刻的影響。而資訊生產供給方的特徵同樣也會影響均衡和讀者的福利。模型框架易於處理大量異質媒體機構的情況，同時也適用於研究新的媒體機構的出現對現存媒體的影響。

17501516.label: Realisation of objectives
17501516.value: Our research identified four key developments in the news media industry: the proliferation of media outlets, attention as the new currency of business, allocation of attention to multiple news providers, and the varying quality of news production. These four stylized facts form the backbone of our new model of monopolistic competition in the media market. Our main research objective is to build a general equilibrium framework that can incorporate the salient features of news production and news consumption. The model we constructed consists of three interacting sets of actors. Editors transform news sources into news stories; readers rationally allocated the attention to different news firms and aggregate the information so obtain to decide their best course of action; and owners of news firms decide on the level of investment in news collection that determine the accuracy of news sources. The interaction between editors and readers can be viewed as a sender-receiver game with multiple senders who possess conditionally independent information. The equilibrium outcome of this game leads to the demand (expressed in terms of attention) for news, which provides the basis for monopolistic competition among owners of news firms. The framework we provide is tractable and allows us to study comparative statics and shed light on recent developments in the news industry. We find that the interaction between readers and editors exhibit complementarity: the more effort editors provide to send clear news stories, the greater attention readers will give to such stories; and likewise if readers give more attention to an editor's story, he or she will have a larger incentive to spend effort to write clear and informative stories. On the other hand, the interaction among news editors themselves exhibits strategic substitution. In our model, editors care about informing the public as well as reducing the cost of effort. The benefit is a public good while the cost is privately incurred. Therefore, editors have incentive to free ride on other editors' effort when other editors are already writing clear and informative stories. The interaction of strategic substitution and strategic complementarity produces interesting effects (e.g., discontinuous demand functions) that are further explored in our paper. We focus on two applications of the model. Our first application looks at the limits of media proliferation. We argue that the public will not be fully informed even if the cost of news production becomes increasingly low. There are two reasons for this conclusion. One is that readers' attention is costly: they will not spend so much attention to become fully informed. The more interesting reason is that the endogenous interaction between news editors and news readers imposes a constraint on the number of news firms that can be supported in equilibrium, even if there are no entry costs and no entry barriers. If there are too many firms, readers will be spreading their attention so thinly over each firm that the editor of each firm would have no incentive to provide informative news at all. The discontinuity of the demand function for news imposes an endogenous constraint limits the number of active media outlets in the industry, which in turn limits the informativeness of the media industry as a whole. Our second application looks at the effects of entry of new firms into the news industry. We identify two effects. First, because the news sources of different firms are conditionally independent, having more firms increases the amount of information available to readers. Counteracting the first effect is a second effect. As more firms enter the industry, demand for news from the incumbent firms falls, and owners have less incentive to invest in infrastructure to collect accurate news, so the quality of news gathered decreases. However, the balance of this trade-off is not ambiguous. Our theoretical model provides a summary measure of aggregate informativeness of the media industry, and we can show that the aggregate informativeness necessarily increases. We also relate this finding to empirical patterns of news consumption in our paper. Finally, we also explore the effect of correlation in information production across outlets. We show that an increase in such correlation reduces media informativeness in equilibrium.

17501516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501516.value: We have two major findings. First, we show that there is an endogenous limit to the number of active media firms that can be supported in the industry, even if the cost of entry is zero. This endogenous limit arises from the interplay between strategic substitution and strategic complementarity. It implies that readers will not evenly divide their attention very thinly across all news outlets, even if the quality of news from each outlet is equal. It also imposes an endogenous constraint on how informative the media industry as a whole can be. Our second main finding is related to the effects of new entry into the media industry. We find that (1) the total amount of news available increases; (2) the quality of news from incumbents--both in terms of the accuracy of their news sources and in terms of the clarity of news stories written by editors--deteriorates; and (3) the quantity effect outweighs the quality effect to provide an improvement in the informativeness of the media as a whole. We relate these predictions to empirical findings which suggest that the public find that the media has become more biased and less reliable (consistent with our second prediction), while at the same time they are spending more time on news consumption (consistent with our third prediction, which relates the informativeness of the media to the amount of attention that readers pay to the media).

17501516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501516.value: Our paper provides a workhorse model of media competition that can be extended in different directions. One possible extension is to look at how the competition between "hard news" and "soft news" for readers' attention affect the collection and distribution of such news by media firms. Our paper does not consider the re-distribution of news by social networks (e.g., Facebook) affect the media business. As social networks become an increasingly important source of news for readers, an examination of news aggregators and news re-distribution becomes a ripe topic for future research.

17501516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501516.value: We provide a framework for analyzing the new media environment, where consumers allocate their attention among multiple heterogeneous news outlets. A large number of news outlets compete for their attention by investing in the accuracy of news gathering and choosing the clarity of news reporting. Entry of news outlets raises the overall informativeness of the industry unambiguously, but reduces the quality—accuracy and clarity—of news reports produced by existing firms. Further, there exists an endogenous limit to media proliferation: the number of firms that can be supported in equilibrium is bounded even when entry cost is zero.

17505516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17505516.value: 自然災害是自然和偶然發生的災難性事件。除了造成經濟損失和人員死亡，自然災害還破壞供應鏈和企業運作。不幸的是，直到今天，大部分的自然災害仍然是不可預知的和不可避免的。因此，政府和私營部門必須作出明智的準備工作，以盡量減少死亡人數，財產損失和環境破壞。這項研究旨在了解自然災害對公司業績的直接和間接影響（通過供應鏈），並提出戰略，為這些災難做準備。 我們首先研究自然災害對公司業績的影響，並提出了多樣化的技術作為一種工具來為這樣的衝擊做準備。而在經濟學文獻中以往的實證研究主要集中在國家一級的經濟損失和因自然災害人員傷亡，我們計劃通過估計自然災害於企業的影響，以突顯本計畫的貢獻。隨後，我們將研究技術的多樣化在幫助企業減少因自然災害損失的作用。 第二，我們要擴大供應鏈和研究自然災害對公司通過供應中斷造成的間接影響範圍。世界在2011年經歷了兩次大的供應鏈中斷：三月的東日本大地震和海嘯嚴重影響了許多於仙台的企業和以及迫使豐田推遲它的兩個新的普銳斯車型發表，以及十一月的曼谷洪水影響了汽車和硬盤行業。這些影響不僅衝擊位於這些地區的企業也衝擊了他們在同一個供應鏈的合作夥伴。由於數據收集的難度，這樣的間接影響很少被量化並研究。 最後，我們還研究如何對自然災害的間接影響做好準備。在供應鏈管理文獻中，數學理論模型建議從多個供應商採購。本文將實證檢驗供應鏈結構如何影響的自然災害的間接影響，特別是，我們也將研究其他可能的企業戰略的有效性。 總而言之，該項目有助於運營管理和供應鏈管理的文獻。首先，它通過提出一種新的方法（即實證模型）以防止和減輕自然災害直接損害企業運營。就我們所知，自然災害量化影響的研究仍然缺乏。本研究和過去使用理論模型的研究者不同，我們採取實證方法來研究企業創新戰略對於減輕自然災害的經濟影響可能，並分析可能的解決方案。其次，本項目也可通過實證研究，於供應鏈管理文獻提供不同的分析視角，即分析供應鏈對企業經營造成的間接影響。此外，使用我們提出的方法，我們終於可以在全球數據進行大規模分析，以研究如何供應鏈結構，特別是供應商的多元化，作為一種減輕自然災害的間接影響工具。

17505516.label: Realisation of objectives
17505516.value: During the project duration, we have completed the data collection for supplier-buyer information, we analyzed corporate strategies that may mitigate the impact, and we link the natural disasters with suppliers as an instrumental variable to explanation the impact of disasters through supply disruption and we also explore supply-chain strategies. In sum, we have completed the realisation of the four objectives, and we detail the output below. In a published paper, "Natural Disasters, Technology Diversity, and Operating Performance," published at a top economics journal (Review of Statistics and Economics), we empirically measure the impact of natural disasters on firm-level operating performance and examine if such impact can be mitigated by technology diversification. Using major natural disasters specified by Barrot and Sauvagnat (2015) and factory location data from the toxic release inventory (TRI) database, we first find that firms with factories located in states affected by natural disasters are much less profitable. Secondly, we find that firms with diversified technologies are significantly less subject to the impact of natural disasters, suggesting that technology diversity enhances firms’ sustainability. We realize objective [1] and [2]. To further address the concern that technology diversity might be endogenous, we use changes in suppliers’ technology diversity (using the pair information realized in [4]) as an exogenous substitute variable for a focal firm’s technology diversity. Moreover, to show that our results are robust to this concern, we collect data on the geographic locations of plants’ and suppliers’ focal firms. Presumably, firms with more geographically diversified plants are more likely to be connected to an extensive network (i.e., connected to more firms). We utilize the data collected in [3] and study the indirect impact of disruption. Moreover, we finished another paper (under review now), "Corporate Social Responsibility and Firms' Resilience to External Disruptions." We propose that corporate social responsibility (CSR) investment serves as an intangible investment in stakeholder relationships to guard against external disruptions to firms’ operations and tangible assets. Using a difference-in-differences setting and a database of factory locations, we show that manufacturing firms with higher CSR ratings are much less affected by major natural disasters in terms of operating performance. We then propose two mechanisms through which CSR engagement shields manufacturing firms against external disruptions: employee motivation and customer loyalty. Empirical evidence suggests that CSR helps manufacturing firms survive major natural disasters by motivating employees, which leads to higher post-disaster productivity, and keeping customers, which leads to more stable post-disaster sales. This paper also serves as a realized objectives for [1] and [2]. Finally, another working paper, "Product Recall Delay and Product Cycle," use the data in [1], as a side project. When a safety defect occurs, manufacturers often use product recalls to mitigate potential consequences. Our empirical observation on large recalls in the automobile industry suggests that the timing of a recall is a key decision, as we find that only recalls made in an early stage of a product cycle significantly influence future product sales. Motivated by this observation, we study the optimal recall timing for a prot-maximizing manufacturer by endogenizing a product's life cycle into our model.

17505516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17505516.value: In this project, we explore corporate actions that may mitigate the negative impacts of supply disruptions (especially natural disasters). Natural disasters are unpredictable events that not only cause significant fatalities and property loss, but also disrupt corporate operations. Our empirical analysis not only identifies the magnitude of the damage of natural disasters on firms’ profitability, but also highlights how firms might use technologies to mitigate the damage. Our empirical results of the impacts of natural disasters provide new evidence to the economics literature stream that explores this phenomenon. Specifically, we propose that an innovation strategy that emphasizes technological diversification helps firms survive and endure natural disasters, for such a strategy enhances flexibility, adaptability, and resourcefulness—all associated with technology diversity—that firms require to respond resiliently to natural disasters. This proposition is supported by our empirical results, which confirm that firms with diversified patent portfolios are significantly less subject to the impact of natural disasters. This study highlights the role of innovation strategies with respect to corporate sustainability, and our findings point to the advantage of technology diversity to mitigate operational risks. See the published paper for more details.

17505516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17505516.value: In the working paper "Corporate Social Responsibility and Firms' Resilience to External Disruptions", we propose that corporate social responsibility (CSR) serves as an intangible investment in stakeholder relationships to guard against external disruptions to operations and tangible assets. We find that firms with higher CSR investment are much less affected by major natural disasters compared with those firms without such investment. Our design, which is based on exogenous disasters, enables us to test our proposition that high-CSR firms are more resilient to external disruptions in a difference-in-differences setting. Further empirical evidence rules out three alternative explanations including capable managers’ preference for CSR, firms’ cash holdings, and firms’ CSR choice serves as a signal. We plan to continue the submission process to publish this paper.

17505516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17505516.value: Business environments change drastically in the past decades. Trade wars, the COVID-19 pandemic, natural disasters, and so much more disruption events slow, if not stop, trades worldwide. Some firms are more resilient to these disruptions and some are not. In this project, we aimed to find and successfully identified two corporate strategies that may increase firm resilience. In particular, we encourage firms to be technologically diversified so to be able to change over their production and design quickly to react to changes and build employee and customer relationships, as outcomes of corporate social responsibility actions, to create loyalty from both parties. In sum, this project highlights its value in that it provides actionable managerial insights for managers to react to disruptions.

17506316.label: Realisation of objectives
17506316.value: All of the objectives have been at least partially achieved. Both survey and experimental data were collected. The core constructs, along with additional variables relevant to other research questions, were measured. The study hypotheses were tested. I found that coworker voice indeed positively predicted employee voice. I also unpacked the main psychological mechanisms underlying the contagion process. I have also found that perceived peer competition and instrumentality were significant correlates. Exchange relationships, especially those with coworkers, had moderating effects, as expected. Moreover, I have found evidence that different types of voice changed over time. Finally, while employee and coworker voice were observed to be correlated cross-sectionally, I did not find direct evidence that changes in coworker voice caused changes in employee voice, perhaps because the intervals used in my data collection (3-6 months) were too stringent for dynamic contagion effects to occur. A day-level or week-level design in future research might be more appropriate. Taken together, the abovementioned research activities have helped realized the project objectives successfully in general.

17506316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17506316.value: I examined whether and how voice can be contagious. I proposed that witnessing the voicing of coworkers increased the focal employee’s propensity to voice via two main psychological mechanisms – self-efficacy and instrumentality beliefs. I further propose that whether voice contagion occurred depended on perceived coworker warmth and competence, captured by coworker exchange quality and perceived coworker capability, respectively. A low level of coworker exchange quality attenuated the self-efficacy mechanism, whereas a high level of perceived coworker capability attenuated the instrumentality mechanism. Data collected from a field study (N = 549) and an experiment (N = 661) provide empirical evidence to support the abovementioned proposed relationships. This paper is currently under second review at Journal of Management Studies, which is a faculty-approved journal and a FT-50 journal. The results have laid the groundwork for me to continue my research on exploring the social-relational antecedents of voice. Therefore, I have conducted an additional project that examined perceived respect as an antecedent of voice. That study’s core premise is that when employees believe they are respected by coworkers, they experience psychological changes to their control beliefs and positive mood, which then motivate voice. I further consider another social-relational variable, perspective taking, as a predictor of received respect and therefore as an indirect predictor of voice. Through a multi-method, multi-sample research program comprising four studies (e.g., vignette experiments, field surveys of employee-coworker and subordinate-supervisor dyads), I provide empirical evidence to support the aforementioned proposed model. This paper has been accepted for publication in Journal of Management, which is a faculty-approved journal and a FT-50 journal. I have also used the extra survey space to measure variables pertinent to a project on corporate social responsibility (CSR). I showed that CSR created pride that made employees feel embedded in their current organizations, which in turn lowered their turnover tendency. This paper has been published in Personnel Psychology, which is a faculty-approved journal. This grant has also partially helped fund a project that focuses on voice and ethical leadership. This project again expands my research on exploring the social-relational antecedents of employee voice and the dynamic effects of voice over time. It shows that changes in ethical leadership promoted changes in emotions that are associated with changes in voice. This paper is under third review at Journal of Applied Psychology, which is a faculty-approved journal and a FT-50 journal.

17506316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17506316.value: This project guides future research on voice in several important ways. First, voice theories lag behind on the effects of coworker voice on the focal employees’ voice, exemplified by the scarcity of research in which focal employees’ and coworkers’ voice were simultaneously considered. The current project suggests that voice can be socially infectious, which in turn should motivate researchers to identify more social-relational antecedents of voice, especially those related to coworkers, peers, and team-members. Second, this research has gathered evidence to show that both the self-efficacy and instrumentality mechanisms can explain the voice contagion process. These two mechanisms, therefore, should be more thoroughly addressed in future research on voice, especially when social-relational antecedents of voice are examined. The instrumentality mechanism is especially promising, as recent evidence suggests that employees are calculative. Finally, I have identified two social-relational moderators of voice contagion, including coworker exchange quality and perceived coworker capability. The salience of these characteristics suggests that not all coworkers can make an influence on a focal employee. Future research should continue to examine coworker qualities as significant moderators of voice contagion. In so doing, researchers can gain a stronger understanding of the social dynamics surrounding voice contagion.

17506316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17506316.value: This project is value-adding in multiple ways. I have shown that employees speak out more when they see others speak out. The main reason is that people become more confident in speaking out and that they are more aware of the values of voice after seeing others speak out. Hence, an important message garnered from this study is that managers can consider creating or facilitating voice contagion to take place so that employees naturally recognize the benefits of and feel comfortable speaking out. Accordingly, instead of targeting a single individual, an organization’s voice promotional strategies can target all employees such that when one employee speaks out, others will be more inclined to do so as a result of social contagion. In an auxiliary project, I also observed that being respected by others is also related to voice and that perspective-taking is an important precursor of gaining others’ respect. Thus, it is clear that voice can be socially motivated. Taken the findings together, these two studies suggest that there is still much we do not know about how social relationships at work shape voice and that social contagion is a fruitful way to unpack some of these social dynamics.

17507216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17507216.value: Mortgage lenders have the right to foreclose on properties, either by court or by the operation of law, if borrowers default on their payment obligations. Real estate foreclosures have a substantial economic impact. For example, the US housing market experienced a 35% price drop since the post-2006 collapse. Foreclosures played an even larger role during the 2007-2008 financial crisis. Nearly four million families lost their homes to foreclosure and another four and half million slipped into the foreclosure process. Ensuing academic studies on this crisis have devoted extensive attention to its root cause, its damage to macro economic performance, and accordingly the policy guidance for recovery and prevention. Much less effort, however, has been made on understanding the implications from the foreclosure process. The loan lenders and other potential buyers often possess different information regarding the properties being foreclosed. The main objective of this project is to develop new economic and econometric methods for analyzing the interactions between the market participants in the foreclosure sales process. We intend to develop insights into information asymmetry between the agents in transactions. This type of information asymmetry consumes efficiency from reallocations, diminishes public confidence in the competitive process, and undermines the benefits of a competitive marketplace. At worst, such information imperfection issues may potentially hurt borrowers who are financially constrained and default on payments. The ultimate methodological goal of this project is to develop a widely applicable economic framework that can identify the presence and composition of information asymmetry among market participants in foreclosure practice. We will adopt a structural approach to study foreclosed properties across different states in the US real estate markets. The structural empirical inference will not only enable a formal test of the theory’s adequacy, but also allow an evaluation of counterfactual policies. In particular, the project will address the following questions: (1) Are the model primitives uniquely recoverable from the observables? If so, how can the model primitives be best estimated? (2) Are information asymmetry and transmission empirically identifiable from relevant models? If so, do they play a prominent role in applications? (3) How much of the difference between the true value and transaction price could be attributed to information friction from foreclosures? (4) How do we design a market mechanism so that the efficiency of transaction can be achieved? 17507216.label: Realisation of objectives
17507216.value: We extended a standard second-price auction model with a signalling device by the reserve price for seller's private information to study the foreclosure sales. We manage to characterize the equilibrium of such an extended model. The derivation and analysis are rather involved and not straightforward, as the discontinuity feature exhibited in the equilibrium characterization demands a new and innovative approach for the striking results. As a matter of fact, we have spent quite some efforts in extending the model to a general setting as much as we could. As a result, our study shows that the identified equilibrium feature is unique but genuine in nature. We therefore expect it to elicit more attention and broader application in the future studies in academia. We also put the information asymmetry under the focus of this project. It then brought the role of securitization and the securitized mortgage issuers to the centre in the applied aspect of this project. We hired research assistants and exploited various information resources to identify the nature of mortgage in the sample under our study. The purpose is to identify the differences that securitized mortgages played in the foreclosed sale markets. The idea is that the mortgage issuers for securitized properties tended to commit less resources and efforts in pursuing quality of loans, and thus possessed less accurate and useful information at hand. If it were the case, then the mortgage issuing banks would not have any information advantage in foreclosed sale procedures. We managed to show it is the case in Florida, US, on the sample that we studied. Beyond matching various information sources to identify the impact of securitization, we also encountered the problem of measuring the property quality and any other effects that may matter to determine the values of properties. To overcome this complication, we combined different approaches in the literature and invented a quality index to proxy and isolate various effects for the value of houses. This is also another aspect that our study contributed to the literature on the know-how in methodology. On the policy aspect, we focus on the role of information revealing in the process of foreclosed sales. We also consider how to regulate the securitized banks in issuing loans in terms of information collection and processing. As the work in this project itself is not structural, we were unable to quantify any policy simulation. But we were able to suggest that informational asymmetry, not only about the probability of default of a mortgagee, but also about the loss given default (due to the value of the collateral) is relevant.

17507216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17507216.value: This project produced two output as research papers to be published. 1. Foreclosure Auctions. Currently under second round revision request by the Rand Journal of Economics. The main purpose of this paper is to provide a theory of foreclosure auctions, derive testable implications of the theory, and to test the validity of our theory. This study determines participants’ equilibrium bidding strategies in foreclosure auctions, in which the lender potentially has a private signal about the quality of the property being sold. The theory predicts that there is a bunching of lenders’ bids at the judgment amount, regardless of whether or not the lender has a private signal. Bunching occurs when the lenders switch their role from seller to buyer around the judgment amount. Notably, when a price is below the judgment amount (i.e., when the lender is acting in the role of a seller), the lender is incentivized to increase their bid to increase their revenues. Conversely, when a bid reaches the judgment amount, any additional revenue goes to the original owner and, as such, price increases do not benefit the lender. This leads to bunching. We show that when the bank has private information about the quality of the property, an additional, surprising empirically testable implication arises: the lender’s bidding strategy changes discontinuously just below the judgment amount. Such a discontinuity in lenders’ bidding strategies can be empirically tested by examining patterns in the probability of sales of properties. 2. Linkage Effect with Affiliated Signals. To be submitted to top tier journals. We study a second-price auction model with both interdependent values and affiliated signals in this paper. The value interdependence in our model gives rise to a linkage effect. Such an information channel offers the seller an incentive to price opposite to the information rent concern. Moreover, the affiliation of signals between the seller and the buyers causes the linkage effects to differ in magnitudes across sellers. We examine the conditions for existence and uniqueness of a separating equilibrium in our model. We show that the equilibrium works when the linkage effect increases with sellers’ signals at a moderate rate. This is the case when value interdependence and signal affiliation are weak. Instead, when both of them are strong, we also show a reverse signalling equilibrium is possible in which better sellers signal through lower reserve prices.

17507216.value: The research in this project can be extended in modeling. It is expected to develop another solid piece of research work for the research postgraduate students. Upon publication, the research finding in Foreclosure auctions should be inspiring for policymakers in the government to understanding the design of foreclosure process and aiming to improve society's welfare.

17507216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17507216.value: A foreclosure auction is run by a government agency following a mortgagee’s failure to make payments to the lender. A lender (typically a bank) and third-party bidders (typically real estate brokers) participate in such an auction. One important feature of foreclosure auctions is that only payments up to the judgment amount (which is essentially the amount owed by the mortgagee) are paid to the lender. Any payment above the judgment amount are paid to the owner of the property. Thus, the bank essentially has the incentives of a seller for prices below the judgment amount and the incentives of a buyer above the judgment amount. Another important feature of foreclosure auctions is that the lender is likely to have superior information about the quality of the property, as lenders typically expend significant resources on appraisals to obtain a precise value of the collateral before granting mortgages. The asymmetry of information between the lender and third-party bidders is further heightened by the fact that buyers are not permitted to inspect the property being sold before the auction. The main purpose of this paper is to provide a theory of foreclosure auctions, derive testable implications of the theory, and to test the validity of our theory.

17507916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17507916.value: We explore how a specific type of uncertainty, political uncertainty, affects exports and foreign direct investment (FDI) of multinational enterprises (MNEs). Specifically, we study how the dispute over Diaoyu (or Senkaku) islands between China and Japan in 2012 has affected Sino-Japan trade and cross-border investment differently. Reportedly, the escalation of this dispute, which led to large-scale protests in the third quarter of 2012, was unexpected and unprecedented. Using aggregate data, we document two interesting findings. First, although Japanese exports to China and local sales of Japanese MNE affiliates in China plummeted after the escalation of the dispute, they had recovered and even surpassed their original levels one year afterwards. However, FDI flows from Japan to China dropped significantly after the outbreak of dispute, and there has been no recovery to date. We investigate why exports and FDI have behaved differently after the island dispute. The most appealing explanation for this differential change is increased political uncertainty. Since investment and FDI especially incur substantial sunk costs such as large-scale capital investment, irreversibility is the key feature of them. However, sunk costs of exporting are presumably smaller. Therefore, when political uncertainty increases, there should be more firms stopping doing FDI than firms that stop exporting. Conversely, fewer firms should start doing FDI than firms that start exporting. Furthermore, the difference in sunk costs also make the recovery of FDI longer than exporting, since the value of waiting increases more for FDI. In total, increased political uncertainty leads to larger and longer-run negative effects on FDI than on exports, which is consistent with our findings. In order to provide direct evidence and take into account other potential channels, we utilize firm-level data of Japanese MNEs and their affiliates. We show how various measures of firm-level uncertainty have changed after the escalation of the dispute. Furthermore, we build up a dynamic model to tease out the pure effect of increased political uncertainty on exports and FDI. Our research fills several important gaps in academic research such as the lack of causal evidence of uncertainty on investment and the lack of long-run impact of political events on trade-related variables. Importantly, it points out one hidden economic cost of geopolitical conflicts. Even if anti-Japan movement does not influence Chinese consumers' behavior in the long run, it negatively affects Japanese firms' investment in China, which might lead to substantial losses in welfare and wages of Chinese consumers. 本研究利用在2012年第三季度发生的钓鱼岛事件研究突发的政治 事件如何影响跨国投资。本研究发现尽管中日间的贸易和日本在 华企业的销售并没有在中长期受到钓鱼岛事件的影响，日本在华 企业的直接投资和设备投资却在钓鱼岛事件之后大幅降低。数据 显示日本在华企业在钓鱼岛事件之后长期调低了他们对于在中国 市场的销售预期。这样的态势即使在日本在华企业在中国市场的 实际销售大幅增加之后仍然存在。本研究表明短期的政治事件可 以通过改变企业的长期预期来影响诸如投资这样的长期的经济变 量。

17507916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17507916.value: The major findings of our research are (1) A sharp but temporary fall in the local sales of Japanese multinational corporations (MNCs) in China led to a persistent downward deviation in the trend of foreign direct investment (FDI). Moreover, despite the quick recovery of local sales, Japanese MNCs in China have continued to underestimate this figure, which has generated pessimistic and more dispersed forecast errors since the island crisis. (2) Firms with more market experience are better at forecasting their future sales and therefore face less uncertainty. A more volatile economic environment makes it harder for firms to choose the most efficient mode to enter the foreign market.
