17508016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17508016.value: In the proposed research program, we investigate how experience utility (i.e., the enjoyment derived during consumption) of products changes when they are part of a group of other unrelated products. In particular, we propose that merely framing products as a combination versus independent will change their individual experience utility and the qualitative value of the experience. The intuition for this phenomenon lies in real world product combinations such as the McDonald’s Happy Meal, where simple food and toy combinations create consumer experiences that is often greater than the sum of their parts. We plan to examine two specific phenomena: 1) how the enjoyment of product A affects the enjoyment of product B during consumption when they are combined (versus considered to be independent), and 2) how value-generating marketing placebo effects such as branding differentially affect the enjoyment of different components (products) of a set during consumption. For the first project explores the basic mechanisms governing experience utility for independent versus combined experiences. We hypothesize that when two unrelated products are framed as combined, their experience utilities interact; this effect would not occur if the two products were framed as independent experiences, even if they happen to be jointly consumed. Specifically, we expect the experience utility of products to assimilate towards the less enjoyable product. The second project extends the findings by exploring how value-generating marketing actions interacts with the mechanisms discovered in project 1. We hypothesize that the impact of marketing placebo effects such as branding can be more complex than a simple change in absolute value, but can also stem from shifts in the relative weighting of the component products in a set (e.g., of a product line). In both projects, the basic tenet is that experience utility (enjoyment derived during consumption) of two products change when they are considered to be independent versus combined experiences. These two projects serve as an initial exploration of a set of market-relevant phenomena that contributes to previous research on hedonic experiences and marketing placebo effects by examining how the experience utility of sets of products, rather than individual products, is determined. They create a foundation for future research streams on how individual experiential components interact and combine to generate utility and value. This is both a theoretical contribution to the study of consumer behavior, consume experiences, and utility theory, but has direct managerial applications for branding, customer experience design, and value creation. 在该研究计划中，我们将探讨产品的体验效用（消费或使用该产品带来的享乐感）如何被其他与之搭配的产品所影响。具体的研究假设是：将目标产品描述为与其他产品绑定，或者描述为独立于其他产品，可能会对目标产品的体验效用产生不同的影响。对该现象的直觉来源于真实世界中的产品绑定案例。例如麦当劳的“欢乐儿童餐”将食物与玩具绑定，其产生的综合体验效用，胜过了简单将二者体验效用直接加总。 我们计划探讨两个特定的现象： 1）当产品A与产品B被绑定（vs.彼此独立）时，产品A的享乐程度如何影响到产品B的享乐程度，以及2）一些产生价值的营销安慰剂效应（如品牌效应）如何影响到对产品组合中每个产品的享乐程度 第一个研究项目探讨了产品独立或绑定如何影响产品的体验效用。我们假设，当两个产品被绑定在一起时，彼此的体验效用会互相影响。而当两个产品彼此独立时，这一现象不会出现。具体地，我们预期，对两个产品中更喜爱的那个产品的体验效用会更容易受到较不喜欢的那个产品的影响。 第二个研究项目则试图探索常用的营销增值手段如何与前述项目中发现现象的背后机制产生交互。我们假设，营销中的安慰剂效应（如品牌效应）不仅来自于对产品价值的改变，也同样来自于形成评价过程时对组合中每个产品权重的重新分配（如产品生产线）。 在这两个项目中，核心的机制是两个产品的体验效用（从消费产品中产生的享乐）在彼此绑定或者独立时会有所不同。通过检验绑定如何对产品组合的体验效用产生影响，这两个研究项目拓展了过去对享乐体验与营销安慰剂效应的研究。同时，这两个研究项目也进一步为未来探索个体产品之间体验的交互，以及如何通过绑定增加体验效用奠定了基础。总而言之，该研究项目不仅对于消费者行为、消费者体验与效用理论有积极的理论意义，也对一系列营销实践，如品牌、顾客体验设计、价值创造具有直接的指导意义。

17508016.label: Realisation of objectives
17508016.value: Three related but distinct streams of research and multiple papers have organically emerged from this grant. This not only reflects the natural, branching development pathway of experimental research, where hypotheses and empirical findings do not always align and new exciting possibilities emerge unexpectedly, but also reflect changes in the marketing field the last few years. Namely, since the grant was proposed, there has been a marked increase in relative importance of digital consumer experiences (i.e., new media based consumer experiences) or digitally enabled physical consumer experiences in the marketplace. To catch this trend, multiple projects emerging from this grant have focused on media stimuli and experiences (i.e., visual and audio-visual consumer experiences), the second stream of research relates to visual perception processes (which are the cognitive mechanistic bases of media consumption), and the third stream of research relies on digital data directly. The first stream of research, which was the basis for the initial grant proposal, relates to how experiential utility derived during consumption can be affected by perceptual factors such as framing, information processing, and information environment. Methodologically, it is closest to the experimental paradigms proposed in the initial GRF proposal. In terms of output, this stream has realized one paper published in a top social psychology journal ("Change Appeals: How Referencing Change Boosts Curiosity and Promotes Persuasion”, Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin), one paper under advanced review at a top marketing journal (“The Impact of Previews on the Enjoyment of Multi-component Extended Multimedia Experiences”, 3rd round Revise and Resubmit at Journal of Consumer Research; “), as well as a third paper that is a work in progress (“Hedonic Combinatorics: How Framing Products as Bundles Changes Enjoyment”). The The second stream of research relates to how consumer choice and perceptions of products (i.e., predicted utility) is affected by visual perception effects and visual information environment. Methodologically, this stream has developed new experimental paradigms that fall closer to cognitive and visual psychological paradigms. In terms of output, this stream has realized one paper under advanced review at a top marketing journal (“The Effect of Slow Motion Video on Consumer Inference”, 2nd round Revise and Resubmit at Journal of Marketing Research), one completed paper under review at a top marketing journal (“Advertising Blink: Seeing but not Remembering Serially Presented Visual Marketing” under review at Journal of Consumer Research). Across these two papers, we show how that how visual information is distributed across time and space can change people’s qualitative visual experiences. These two papers use a wide range of ecologically valid and complex visual stimuli, develop new visual psychological experimental paradigms, and use eye-tracking to derive deeper process insight. Although the applied contexts of these two papers are in the context of advertisements, the documented effects reduce people’s liking (i.e., experiential utility) derived from the visual stimuli (i.e., ads). These effects have downstream effects on ad persuasiveness and choice, and thus have high application value. The third stream of research relates to using digital trace data to study consumer experiences: these differ qualitatively from traditional consumer behavior research in their emphasis on combining verifiable field behavior, big data (i.e., constructs that are hard to reliably observe in a lab), and causal instruments. One was published as a Research Article (i.e., long paper, one of 12 per issue) in a top psychology journal (“The Role of Hedonic Behavior in Reducing Perceived Risk: Evidence from Post-Earthquake Mobile App Data”, Research Article at Psychological Science, 2020); the other is a completed working paper under preparation for submission at Psychological Science (“The Social Characteristics Driving Mobile Social Response to Strangers”). The former paper is significant because it was one of the earlier papers using big data that was accepted in the entire field of social psychology and showed how big data can be used in psychology (at a time when there were few papers that have done so; many more papers using digital trace data to study psychology have emerged since). The editor, Prof. Bill von Hippel, felt the paper would have a “major impact” and thought it was “a great paper, one of the most exciting ones I’ve handled in a long time”. Brief summaries of each paper and which objectives for the grant proposal have been realized (as well as expanded and adapted) in each paper. 1. “The Impact of Previews on the Enjoyment of Multi-component Extended Multimedia Experiences”: Combines study of information placebo effects with a multi-component perspective on experiences. We find that the impact of previewing on enjoyment is mediated by how much a preview affects the upcoming multimedia’s ‘experiential coherence,’ or how well the different parts of a multicomponent experience fit together. Relates to Objectives: 1, 2, 3, 4 (most related to experiential utility) 2. "Change Appeals: How Referencing Change Boosts Curiosity and Promotes Persuasion”: Framing products and policies as having changed can enhance a message’s persuasive impact. Five studies reveal that this occurs because the mention of change sparks curiosity, which in turn boosts processing of information about the changed entity. Experimental paradigm is largely in the context of looking at whether participants ‘click through’ after reading an ad. Relates to Objectives: 2 (we study whether another form of framing affects preferences for combinations of information), 4 3. The Effect of Slow Motion Video on Consumer Inference We demonstrate that slow motion (vs. natural speed) can backfire and undercut product appeal by making the influence agent’s behavior seem extrinsically motivated and subsequently undermine attributions to intrinsic product quality. This effect is mediated by the perception of greater intentionality of human actors in slow motion. Relates to Objectives: 2, 3, 4; marginally related to 1 – since we measure liking of visual stimuli 4. Advertising Blink: Seeing but not Remembering Serially Presented Visual Marketing We show that when multiple advertisements for the same product or brand are displayed in sequence (i.e., consecutively), despite being relatively commonplace visual presentation strategy in the marketplace, can backfire by making the information presented less memorable, an effect we call “advertising-amnesia”. We develop a novel visual experimental paradigm called Continuous Serial Visual Processing to test our hypotheses. Relates to Objectives: 2, 3, 4; marginally related to 1 – since we measure liking of visual stimuli 5. The Role of Hedonic Behavior in Reducing Perceived Risk: Evidence from Post-Earthquake Mobile App Data Uses large scale mobile metadata from populations that have been subject to a natural shock (which also helps tackle endogeneity) to study how social network dynamics are affected by exogenous stressor such as environmental disorder. My Psychological Science paper is the first to be published from this stream and studies how utilitarian and hedonic behaviors change in response to different levels of risk (operationalized by earthquake intensity) by looking at their mobile app behavior using a dataset of the individual level mobile metadata (and their geolocations) for 157,358 victims of the 2013 Ya’an earthquake in Sichuan China. Relates to Objectives: 5 6. “The Social Characteristics Driving Mobile Social Response to Strangers” Investigates what drives social response from strangers using large scale mobile field experiments (N = 18,000), where we sent real communications solicitations, combined with subjects’ individual mobile metadata, to test whether popularity, reciprocity, sociability, or status drives real response behavior. Relates to Objectives: 5

As an additional objective, and as a methodological contribution, I would like to use new digital technologies to explore the aforementioned research objectives. New phenomena investigated may include exploring digital products, virtual products, augmented reality products, etc. New methodologies encompassed may involve in-lab VR goggles as well as digital data, e.g., from mobile app usage.

17508016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17508016.value: The paper that emerged which most directly relates to the original research proposal is “The Impact of Previews on the Enjoyment of Multi-component Extended Multimedia Experiences”. One major difference in our eventual approach (versus the original proposed project) is our pivot to how the organization of multiple constituent components of consumer experiences affect utility (rather than investigate experiential effects for the organization of multiple products/experiences). Overall, we show that when consumers watch previews for multi-component experiences (e.g., movies, television shows, music, etc., which are structurally defined and composed of multiple components), the previews can change pre-experiential information processing. We find that the impact of previewing on enjoyment is mediated by how much a preview affects the upcoming multimedia’s “experiential coherence”, or how well the different parts of a multicomponent experience fit together (e.g., how the story flows). The paper contributes to the literature by showing how marketing actions affect more structurally complex consumer experiences. Previous research studying time courses of experiences did not investigate how information processing could qualitatively changes those time courses; previous literature studying how marketing qualitatively changes experiences (e.g., information placebo effects) typically focused on structurally simple stimuli (e.g., taste of chocolate or sip of wine). The following specific findings have emerged from other projects in the three streams of research that this grant has supported: 1) Utility may be affected by framing of whether object has changed or not 2) Visual presentation speed of marketing experiences can change based on presentation speed, which affects how the human agents in videos/their intentions and motivations. 3) Distribution of visual information pieces across space and time affects our ability to retain relevant information: Multiple advertisements for the same product or brand are displayed in sequence (i.e., consecutively), despite being relatively commonplace visual presentation strategy in the marketplace, can backfire by making the information presented less memorable 4) We used consumer behavioral big data to investigate how human interests (operationalized by mobile app usage patterns) change in response to different levels of risk (operationalized by earthquake intensity). We find that utilitarian, communications, and hedonic (e.g., games, reading, videos, etc.) mobile app usage increase in a graded manner at each level of earthquake intensity. We used instrumental variable models to conduct causal hypothesis testing between the change in app usage and subsequent psychological recovery (which we measured in a large-scale phone survey a week after the earthquake).

17508016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17508016.value: The completed papers represent just a start of the possibilities in exploring how different combinations of consumption experiences can have different qualitative values under different circumstances. For example, in the first stream, the paper on how previews (mediated by the effect of narrative structure) affect the enjoyment of multi-component experiences can be extended to other product types and categories. The paper also identifies an analogous effect for experiences that do not have literal narrative structures (e.g., art exhibits). It may thus be possible extend the research to other types of consumption experiences in the latter categories ranging from dining to travel itineraries, etc. We also plan to continue research using the visual experimental paradigms designed for the second stream of research outlined above. In particular, our current results can be extended to other forms of multiple advertisements. For example, we can investigate if the effect occurs for video stimuli, or even non-visual stimuli such as radio ads. The third stream of research can be extended based on data availability. I am currently investigating the possibility of examining app usage changes before and after COVID-19.

17508016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17508016.value: Across multiple projects, we show that experiential utility, or the enjoyment that is derived during consumption, is not objective or absolute, but rather can be affected by subtle changes in information environment, information processing, and perceptual factors such as framing. Such effects are particularly interesting for experiences that have multiple subparts (e.g., parts to a movie, chapters of a novel, etc.) that not only add a layer of conceptual complexity, but are also more ecologically valid (i.e., reflect experiences that dominate the actual consumer landscape, such as multimedia experiences). By identifying the different effects that can affect how much people enjoy such experiences, our research makes a theoretical contribution to the understanding of consumer psychology. From a practical side, our research can be used to design better consumption experiences, more engaging multimedia experiences, and more effective advertisements. The research has also opened the path forward to three different streams of research (discussed above), which relate to 1) the architecture of consumer experiences, 2) the principles of visual perception, and 3) the methodology behind studying consumer experiences using digital big data.

17509716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17509716.value: This project develops methods of estimating social interaction models with unknown networks. The methods allow us to estimate the magnitudes of social influences and social networks simultaneously and just require some moderate and conventional assumptions on the network structures. The literature of social interactions is large. But most of the works assume that the social networks which transmit social influences are known to researchers. Misspecification of social networks could lead to biases in estimating the magnitudes of social influences. Thus the methods developed in the present project would be an important contribution to the literature. In my previous work, Kwok (2015), I developed two identification methods for social interaction models with unknown networks. The first method identifies the network matrix and parameters in a model by using matrix triangularization technique in linear algebra. The second method identifies the network matrix entries and parameters in a model by interpreting the social interaction model as a simultaneous equation system and using ideas in the literature of simultaneous equation system identification. Kwok (2015) is a theoretical paper which focuses on identification. That is, it essentially assume that we have infinitely many samples so that some estimation problems are bypassed. This project develops the estimation methods corresponding to the two identification methods in Kwok (2015) and applies the estimation methods to real data. 這個研究計劃建立估計方法去估計社會互動模型的參數與網絡矩陣。這些估計方法能同時估計社會互動的大小程度（參數）與社會網路結構（網絡矩陣）。這些估計方法只需要一些溫和與常規的網絡結構假設。 在社會互動研究中，大多數研究都假設社會網路結構（網絡矩陣）是研究人員已知的。但如果社會網路結構的假設有誤差，估計的參數也會有誤差 。所以這研究計劃會是一個重要貢獻。 在我之前的研究中，我建立了兩個識別方法去識別社會互動模型的參數與網路矩陣。第一種方法應用線性代數中的矩陣三角化來識別參數與網路矩陣。第二種方法把社會互動模型視為聯立方程式系統，再應用識別聯立方程式系統的方法去識別參數與網絡矩陣。 我之前的研究文章集中於建立識別方法，所以假設有無限多樣本。這個假設避開了一些用真實數據去估計時會遇到的問題。這個研究計劃會以我之前建立的兩個識別方法為基礎去建立估計方法。而且這些估計方法會應用到真實數據。

17510016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17510016.value: 信用违约互换会减少公司关联人士的信息优势吗？

17510016.label: Project Objectives
17510016.value: To understand the impact of the multi-trillion dollar credit derivatives market on corporate managers. To understand the role of financial markets and especially the derivatives market in corporate governance. To understand corporate managers’ decision making in trading own company stocks. To understand the evolving role of creditors including banks when they have new trading opportunities besides their traditional function.
rows: To understand the impact of the multi-trillion dollar credit derivatives market on corporate managers.
To understand the role of financial markets and especially the derivatives market in corporate governance.
To understand corporate managers’ decision making in trading own company stocks.
To understand the evolving role of creditors including banks when they have new trading opportunities besides their traditional function.

17510016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17510016.value: One of the most important developments in financial markets over the past twenty years is the credit default swaps (CDS) market. CDS contracts are written on the credit risk of corporations, countries, and pools of reference entities and are traded over the counter. CDS trading presents new opportunities for institutional investors to exploit their potential information advantages. Such trading may also have profound impact on corporate insiders, including the management team and major blockholders. This study aims to understand the effect of CDS trading on the profitability and trading strategies of corporate insiders. The notional value of outstanding CDS contract is above twenty trillion dollars, more than equity derivatives. Market players are almost entirely institutional investors. Commercial banks, investment banks, mutual funds, hedge funds, insurance companies actively participate in the CDS market. Such institutions can exert pressure on the managers of the firm and their major owners. Understanding the interaction of CDS trading and insider trading will be useful for corporate finance and market efficiency. Given the rise of activists in the market, the interactions of CDS trading and insider trading will also be of the interest of regulators. 过去二十年来金融市场最重要的发展之一是信用违约互换。信用违约互换能应用在公司，国家，以及资产组合的信用风险上并在场外市场交易。信用违约互换交易给机构投资者利用他们潜在信息优势提供了投资机会。这类交易可能对公司关联人士包括管理层和大股东的交易策略和盈利可能会造成深远影响。 信用违约互换的活跃名义头寸超过二十万亿美元，大于股权衍生物市场。信用违约互换市场参与者全部是机构投资者。商业银行，投资银行，共同基金，对冲基金，保险公司都积极的参与该市场的交易。这些机构能给公司管理层和大股东施加压力。理解信用违约互换的机构投资者和公司管理层交易的互动对公司金融和市场效率很有用。最近市场维权投资者开始兴起，信用违约互换市场和公司管理层交易的互动对监管机构也是很有意义的。

17510016.label: Realisation of objectives
17510016.value: All four project objectives are fully achieved. In the paper published in the Journal of Financial Economics, we show that corporate managers hold more cash after the inception of credit default swaps. Managers become more precautious and manage their companies more conservatively in terms of financial policies. One concern is due to tougher creditors during debt renegotiations. Moreover, they will demand looser covenants when they borrow money from banks, as we show in the paper published in the Journal of Accounting and Economics. Banks are willing to relax loan covenants as they can buy CDS in the derivatives market to hedge their credit exposures. Credit derivatives also help corporate governance in terms of deterring the hoarding of bad news. Such information revelation facilitated by CDS trading makes insider trading less profitable, as shown in one of my working papers. Moreover, CDS trading helps improve financial market stability. Another of my working papers provide evidence that stocks are less like to crash when there is CDS trading on the firms’ debt. Insiders are also less likely to sell their company stocks in anticipation of negative news. One potentially negative effect of CDS trading is that banks will monitor their borrowers less when they can buy CDS. If bank monitoring is valuable to the firm and other stakeholders, then the reduction of bank monitoring can be bad for social welfare. In the end, banks may take more risks and grant more loans. Such an increase in credit supply may have spillover effects and benefits companies that may not be financed in the pre-CDS era. We further show that CDS trading can increase product market competition. When firms face a less stringent financing environment, they may become more aggressive against their product market rivals. They invest more in research and development, lower markups, and encroach the rivals’ market space. Such competition induced by CDS trading is good news to consumers as they can enjoy more products at lower prices.

17510016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17510016.value: We find that CDS trading substantially changes the behaviors of corporate managers, bank lenders, and other stakeholders. After the inception of CDS, managers take more conservative financial policies as they hold more cash. They are also more cautious in terms of insider trading as they sell their own company stocks less in anticipation of bad news. On the other hand, bank lenders take more risk when there are CDS contracts available. They provide credit to borrowers in more generous terms. Armed with such credit supply, firms engage in more fierce competition. They make more innovations in products and cut prices. In other words, while managers become more conservative in terms of financial policies after CDS trading, they become more aggressive in operating policies. This research project helped to produce two top journal publications in JFE and JAE and several promising working papers (some are in R&R stage of good journals). Those papers were also included in international conference programs.

17510016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17510016.value: While my research project reveals many interesting effects associated with CDS trading, many important issues are yet to be resolved. One is the overall welfare implications of CDS trading. Is there net benefit or net cost for CDS trading? Answering this question is important for policy makers as many new regulations are being introduced and implemented. CDS is now a relatively mature market in the U.S. and Europe. However, it is still a nascent market in Asia including China. China made at least three attempts to boost the CDS market. Given the rising default risk in China, a functioning CDS market is important for hedging and trading of credit risk as well as the real economy. Future research on how the development of CDS market in the Western economies can be replicated in China and other emerging markets will be valuable. One initial step is to understand the differences in distress resolution including bankruptcy laws. CDS buyers need to be assured that their rights will be protected in bankruptcy events and after they make the insurance payments.

17510016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17510016.value: My research shows that everyone should care about CDS. Although CDS is a pure institutional market with large transaction size, it has profound implications to corporate managers, banks, policymakers, and even consumers. CDS trading allows more risk-taking by banks in terms of lending money to corporations and by managers in terms of product innovation. On the other hand, CDS market helps discipline corporate managers by curbing their opportunistic behaviors. The CDS market has faced many criticisms since the 2008 global financial crisis. We should realize that CDS is mere a financial tool and can serve the society well if it is used properly. This market is worth more attention and research as we are directly and indirectly affected.

17511316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17511316.value: This project is a theoretical investigation attempting to understand the difference in reform strategy choices between Russia and China from a demographic perspective. China started its reform in 1978 with a gradual approach that allows steps to be reversed and experimentation, while Russia started its reform with a big bang approach in early 1990's. Although the gradual reform approach is generally credited as a key to Chinese reform’s success, the lesson is of limited value if we are uncertain about the circumstances under which the approach is applicable. In a recent working paper (Chiu 2015), I explore the role of demography--both the structure and dynamic--in enabling a generic, gradual reform. The paper shows two theoretical results. First: a younger population structure is more favorable to economic reform; second, a lower fertility rate among young couples leads them to be more endurable to hardship under reform, and hence the one-child policy in China might have played a subtle role in gathering support for economic reform. The paper further argues (only verbally) that, in the absence of such favorable population conditions, the government might push through a big bang reform, when a window of opportunity arises, to avoid future opposition under gradual reform. I plan to further develop this line of ideas in this project. First, I will introduce uncertainty to the model. Uncertainty is an important element for large-scale economic changes, while in Chiu (2015) only deterministic outcomes are considered. Second and relatedly, I will model gradual reform and big bang reform in a more elaborate manner. In the working paper, while big bang reform is not modelled at all, the gradual reform is modelled as a single act of reform, hence making its gradual nature oblivious to the reader. Third and more importantly, the main focus of this project is to model and study the choice between big bang and gradual reform. Instead of using the aforementioned window-of-opportunity argument, I want to investigate why and when the same unfavorable demographic conditions and trends that deter the gradual reform might still allow the big bang reform to be implemented. By so doing, I will be able to check the robustness of the ideas and make a better connection with the existing literature. Hence, a more convincing theory that reconciles the different strategy choices between the two countries. 這個項目試圖從人口學的視角，分析俄羅斯和中國之間在改革的速度和策略為何有所區別。中國在 1978 年以漸進的方式開始其改革，俄羅斯在 90 年代初就開始其大爆炸改革。雖然一般認為中國改革成功在於其漸進方針，如果我們不能確定這種方法在何種情況下可行，則這個教訓仍然是有限的價值。在最近的工作論文（Chiu, 2015），我探討人口 ----其的結構和動態 ----在這方面的作用。 該論文給出兩個理論的結果。第一︰ 一個年輕的人口結構是比較有利於經濟改革; 第二，年輕夫婦低生育率會導致他們更能接受在艱苦條件下的改革，因此中國的獨生子女政策可能對支持經濟改革起了意想不到的支援作用。進一步論證是：在缺乏這種良好的人口條件下，要是有一個機會之窗時，政府可能推動通過大爆炸式的改革，以避免在未來的反對下難以進行漸進式改革。 在這個項目中，我打算進一步開展這方面的想法。首先，我將在模型中引進不確定性。不確定性是一個重要的因素，對大規模的經濟變革尤其如此，而在之前的工作論文中（Chiu 2015 ），我沒有考慮不確定性。第二，與此相關的是，我將以更精細的方式模型漸進式改革和大爆炸式改革。 在工作文件中，並沒有模擬大爆炸式改革，漸進式改革被模擬為單一的改革，從而使其漸進性難於識別。第三，更重要的是，這個項目的主要重點是模擬和研究大爆炸與漸進式改革的選擇，而不是使用上述的機會之窗的考慮，我想要調查為何以及何時同樣不利的人口狀況和阻止漸進式改革的趨勢，可能仍然允許大爆炸式改革付諸實施。通過這樣做，我將能夠更好地與現有文獻連接起來，因而得出一個更令人信服的理論，兼顧這兩個國家之間的不同策略選擇。

17511316.label: Realisation of objectives
17511316.value: I have successively completed objectives one to four and made some progress on objective five. Let me elaborate as follows. My model consists of two components: first, an overlapping generational model in which an agent bears the costs of raising children and the number of children she has will have effects on her attritudes towards whether to accept a reform package; second, the reform package can be of two types: big bang versus gradualism. In the first component, we consider a generic reform that brings long run benefits but short run costs. We construct an overlapping generation model in which each agent lives for four periods: childhood, young worker, middle-aged worker, and retiree. A child depends on her parents for consumption and makes no decisions. A young worker works and bears children and raises them until they become young workers in the next period. We assume that the number of children each young worker has is exogenously given. A middle-aged worker works, but does not need to bear or raise children, because her children have already grown up. A retiree does not work and lives on her previous savings. Agents from an earlier stage move on to the next stage with certainty except that retirees will die at the end of their retiree stage. As a result, the country's population size and structure are completely determined by the initial conditions and the fertility rates. Our analysis shows that (1) reform is more likely to occur when the population structure is young as young workers who will live longer will benefit more fully from reform than older people do; and (2) under reasonable specification of the utility function (CCRA utility function with inelastic intertemporal substitution), the maximum reform costs a representative agent is able to endure is greater, the smaller the number of children they have. Hence, objective one—to study a representative agent’s attitude towards reform—and objective three—to study how the population structure is a factor in determining a generic reform’s success--is achieved. In the second component, we assume that there are two reforms and they can be sequenced in two different packages: big bang versus gradualism. In a big bang reform, the two reforms are completed at the same time; in gradualism, they are implemented in sequence and the outcome of the first reform gives useful information as to how the second reform should be implemented and gradualism as such is more efficient. Reforms are reversible. The two reform packages differ in the reversal costs. The reversal cost is greater under big bang than under gradualism. In the literature, the closest to our model is that of Dewatripont and Roland (1995). There are two major differences. First, in their model the payoffs from reform are of a larger range so as to entertain the possibility that a reform is undesirable under some state of nature and hence there is an option value of reversal. In our model, we allow a smaller range of payoffs and any policy reversal reflects a setback of reform and is undesirable. Second and more importantly, there are identical, infinitely lived agents in their model while there are OLG agents in ours and the heterogeneity manifested as intergenerational conflict is the focus of our analysis. The OLG assumption in our model also creates a wedge between the interest of the (current generation) agents and that of the benevolent social planner. Hence, objective two—to model both big bang and gradual reform—is achieved. Assume the government is benevolent, we study two types of collective decision mechanisms: simple majority voting and unanimity with transfers. For both mechanisms, we are able to establish conditions under which big bang is chosen over gradualism or vice versa. Hence, objective four is also completed. We have not made much progress in objective five--empirically testing the theory. The main difficulties are twofold. First, while we assume the government is benevolent, governments in the real world differ among themselves. Governments are in really self-interested and the degree of self-interestedness differs. Thus in empirical testing, we need another empirically measurable variable that describe the degree of benevolence. Second, it is often hard to classify a transitional economy’s reforms into just two categories: big bang versus gradualism. The reality is that there is a continuum of degree of gradualism. We hope to make progress once we have thought through these two issues.

17511316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17511316.value: There are two groups of results. For the first, we are concerned about a generic reform under a four-period overlapping generation model. The reform requires support from the public for implementation. Specifically we consider both the case where the reform decision is made through simple majority voting among workers as well as the case where unanimity between all workers is required and transfers are allowed (we assume away the role played by retirees, whose role if considered is likely to strengthen, rather than weaken, our main results). We show that (1) reform is more likely to occur when the population structure is young as young workers who will live longer will benefit more fully from reform than older people do; and (2) under reasonable specification of the utility function (CCRA utility function with inelastic intertemporal substitution), the maximum reform costs a representative agent is able to endure is greater, the smaller the number of children they have. For the second, we focus on the benevolent government’s choice about the packaging of two reforms amid the political constraints of public approval. While both reforms are supposed to finish in one period (which means one fourth of a person’s life time), they can be implemented at the same time (big bang) or in sequence (gradualism) within the period. We focus on the case where gradualism is by assumption more efficient than big bang reform because the outcome of the first reform will provide useful information regarding the implementation of the second reform. There is a trade-o¤ between the two approaches of reform. On one hand, gradualism is more efficient and can be easily reversed with low costs. On the other hand, big bang reform is less efficient and can be reversed only with high costs. We show that there exist parameter values over which, while gradualism will be reversed (due to unfavorable demographic conditions), big bang reform will not. In real world reform decisions, the threat of reversal is noted and fast changes were proposed precisely because of this consideration.

17511316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17511316.value: Right now, a working paper has been written. There are indeed two interconnected, yet separate models. The first is the public support towards a generic model and the roles of both population structure and the one-child policy are studied. The second is the benevolent government’s choice between two packages (big bang versus gradualism) amid political constraints from the population. With more thought, it is better to split these two parts into two papers so that each can be given more thorough attention without burdening the reader too much. Another aspect needs to be considered is the case of heterogeneous governments. Thus far we have assumed a benevolent government. In reality, governments are seldom benevolent and differ among themselves in degree of self-interested. It is useful to add this additional element to have a more complete mapping between theory and real world cases. This may also lead to plausible empirical testings.

17511316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17511316.value: This project explores a demographic perspective to understanding the choices of reform strategies of China and Russia at the beginning of their reforms. There are two demographic aspects in China that are worth noticing (For example, in 1980, China’s median age was 22.0 while Russia’s median age was 31.2). First, its population was much younger than its Russian counterpart at the time they began reform. Second, the second aspect is the one-child policy which was started in 1980, arguably the most unswerving economic policy in the reform era. This project studies a political economy model of reform in which population structure and dynamic play a central role. We show that in a country like China, its young population structure, together with the one-child policy, allows the public to be more patient towards reform setbacks and hence gradualism, with the merits of allowing experimentation, involves little risks of being blocked indefinitely and will be chosen; in a country like Russia, the older population is not as patient and big bang is chosen to ensure irreversibility.

17511516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17511516.value: Nobel Laureate Akerlof’s (1970) study on information asymmetry (or the market for lemons) has enlightened our understandings about behaviors like moral hazard in the past four decades. However, empirical studies are far from adequate because of identification and measurement problems. Limited attempts have been made in the used cars, cherry, wheat, childcare, mortgage-backed security and initial public offerings etc. This study postulates that the overpricing premium commanded by the lemons is one of the major incentives to induce people to commit moral hazard. To better gauge the economic effects arising from information asymmetry, this study attempts to measure the overpricing premium of durable lemons in Hong Kong’s housing market. The market is so chosen because of the ample transaction records and also the culprit it contains that leads to the lemon problem - overstated floor areas. In Hong Kong’s primary housing market, significant discrepancy between the saleable and actual usable floor area is prevalent. It was because according to the regulations governing information disclosure, the housing developers were lawful to withhold the information of usable floor area in the sales brochures when they sold the presales units in the primary market. In stark contrast, to a large extent the asymmetrical information vanishes in the secondary housing market because the perspective buyers are made free to inspect the premises. The nature experiment settings in the primary and secondary housing markets have enabled us to measure the overpricing premium of the durable lemons. Based on Akerlof’s (1970) theoretical framework, Chau and Choy (2011)’s cross-sectional hedonic price model and Chau (2006)’s repeat sales techniques, this study will measure how much more homebuyers in Hong Kong had paid for the overstated floor areas under information asymmetry. This study will have profound long-term impacts to the study of information asymmetry and the understanding of moral hazard behaviors. It will provide compelling empirical evidence to Akerlof’s (1970) study, which can be generalized to other domains such that our understandings of the economic system at work can be enhanced. This study will also contribute to the theoretical development of Akerlof (1970) by extending the analysis of economic behaviors under different legal regimes. Some public policy implications concerning information disclosure for sales items in general can also be derived. It will help policy makers and scholars to revisit the debates of McKean (1970), Buchanan (1970), Goldberg (1974) and Grossman (1981) concerning product liability rules. 是項硏究是以諾貝爾得奬者阿克洛夫(1970)有關訊息不平衡的硏究理論為基礎，利用特徵價格模型和重復銷售指數方法，量度買家在香港一手房屋市埸因俗稱「發水樓」現像所多付的金額。 跟據香港過往的一手房屋開發及銷售法規，因為每戶要分擔公用面積的關係，某程度上實用面積少於建築面積是容許的。但由於開發商量度實用面積的凖則不盡相同，而發售是樓花的關係，一手買家並不可能如二手買家一般視察樓宇的實際面積，而要在收樓才知悉真實的「發水」程度。在市場訊息不平衡的情況下，是項硏究將透過大約十萬個本港的住宅物業的一、二手成交數據，嘗試用實證數據驗證阿克羅洛夫的訊息不平衡，亦稱「檸檬市場」的理論。

17511516.label: Realisation of objectives
17511516.value: Objective 1: Measure the overpricing premium The key task of the project is to measure the exclusive usable floor areas of residential units in 60 selected popular housing estates in Hong Kong, and then gauge the overpricing premium of those units with excessive area inflation ratios attributed to information asymmetry. We proposed engaging an architectural professional to measure the carpet areas of these units. Ultimately, we managed to measure the carpet areas 75,190 units, to which about 5% have been spot-checked. It is proven a very cost-effective approach to obtain the floor area information. We have matched the carpet area information to the EPRC property transaction database subsequently. An exciting development of the research project is the generous provisions of related datasets supplied by Centaline Ltd, a leading agency company in Hong Kong with around 40% market share, in April 2020. One of the salient elements of these datasets is the Usable Floor Area (UFA) directly purchased from the Rating and Valuation Department (RVD). It costs HK$9 each for the records. The datasets cover a total of 182,598 units in the 113 popular housing estates enlisted in RVD’s housing price index, and 552,895 transaction records between 1997 and 2019. Technical difficulties, however, are encountered to match the transaction records between EPRC and Centaline because of the different address structures. To maximize the number of usable transaction records for the empirical tests, we will revise an earlier paper base on the Centaline’s datasets. The following summarizes the number of transaction records for the empirical tests in the paper under revision: Hedonic price models: 156,197 (with housing attributes and carpet areas) Repeated sales analysis: 171,725 pairs for all 113 estates with UFA An earlier paper was prepared in which a hedonic price modelling was conducted with 75,190 units with housing attributes and carpet area information. To cross-check the outcome, a repeated sales analysis of 45,939 pairs of transactions was conducted. Furthermore, an adverse selection analysis was conducted to investigate whether units with higher area inflation ratios were tended to be flipped by the purchasers vis-à-vis those of lower ratios. Objective 2: Further develop Akerlof (1970) theoretical framework To explain the pricing behaviors of the units with various floor area inflation ratios, we have developed a theoretical framework by extending Akerlof (1970) model by incorporating different legal institutions underlying the property transactions. The major legal institutions governing property transactions are namely i)caveat venditor, or let the seller beware, for presales in the primary market, and ii) caveat emptor, or let the buyer beware, for units in the secondary market. The model is based on a game-theoretical framework, in which a key element is about the perceived risk of litigations of not disclosing the floor inflation ratios information to the perspective buyers. Generally, a higher risk of litigation is associated with property transactions underpinned by the caver venditor doctrine, and vice versa for the caveat emptor doctrine. As a result, so long as the law allows, a higher propensity should be observed for real estate developers to overprice housing units with higher floor area inflation ratios, and vice versa for those with lower ratios. The illustration of the framework is by economic modelling, which is incorporated in the earlier version of the paper. 3. Policy implications with reference to international experiences An international experience survey has been conducted, of which the major findings have been presented in the earlier version of the paper. In Hong Kong’s context, The Residential Properties (First-hand Sales) Ordinance (Cap 621) was enacted which has imposed higher liabilities to the real estate developers to disclose floor area information to the perspective buyers. An unintended consequence, however, is resulted from the change of institutions: moral hazard. Now because the real estate developers have presented the floor area information in the sales brochures as per the requirements of Cap 621, literally it lowers the litigation risk in our economic model and hence pricing behaviours of overcharging the “lemons” could be resulted. Besides, there are also evidence that the real estate developers have overinvested the property related information of which the margin value is close to zero to the perspective buyers. To the social points of view, the new legislation may not bring about optimal outcomes at the end.

17511516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17511516.value: Ma, Choy and Chan (2018) showed that the adverse selection process is taking place in Hong Kong’s housing market. A survey of 16,946 units of 55,227 transactions show that the carpet areas fell short between 23%-49% of the proclaimed gross floor areas. An AVONA test found that it shows that the turnover rates of units with the highest shrinkage ratios are about 45% more than those with the smallest shrinkage ratios. Choy, Ho and Chau (under revision) conducted a survey of 75,190 residential units and found that the carpet areas fall short between 1% to 58% of the proclaimed gross floor areas. The mean shrinkage ratio (carpet area / gross floor area) was about 20%. The empirical evidence showed that for Class E residential properties (UFA >160 sf m), an 1% increase of shrinkage ratio is associated with HK$135,775 of overpricing premium. A repeated sale analysis was conducted for 45,939 pairs of repeated transactions. It was found that the repeated sales index of property units with shrinkage ratios below the mean (i.e. 20%) was significantly above (10 to 20 points out of 100) compared to the rest. An adverse selection analysis concurred with the major findings of Ma, Choy and Chan (2018) that residential units with higher shrinkage ratios were tended to be flipped by the purchasers compared with those of lower ratios. Ma, Choy and Chan (2018) and Choy, Ho and Chau (under revision) have surveyed the international experiences and literature about the institutions governing property transactions. Practices such as legislation, mandatory vs voluntary information disclosure, third party information service providers and self-governance mechanisms have been covered.

17511516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17511516.value: With the datasets provided by Centaline Ltd., a few studies concerning property market anomalies and pathology can be further developed. These studies, inter alias, include price discrimination over various buyer groups (youth in HK’s context who mainly bought Class A properties – saleable areas < 40 sq m), building age adjusted housing price indexes, and constructing tailored-made repeated sales index for a wide variety of research questions.

17511516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17511516.value: By measuring the carpet areas of over 75,000 housing units in Hong Kong, this study found that on average the exclusive usable floor area fell short 20% of the proclaimed total floor area for sales. Units will higher area inflation ratios were flipped in the secondary market by the purchasers 45% more often than those with lower ratios. By chasing the subsequent transactions of these units, this study found that 1% increase of the floor area inflation ratio was associated with HK$135,775 of overpricing premium during the presales. This study surveyed international experiences and literature regarding the formal and informal rules governing property transactions. The market will be benefited by practices like legislation, mandatory and voluntary information disclosure, third party information providers, but harmed by overinvestment of property related information.

17511716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17511716.value: 置换风险和价值溢价：全球分析

17511716.label: Project Objectives
17511716.value: We aim to construct an extensive international panel data, and for the first time incorporating firm-level innovation measures (patents, citations, etc.) into individual firm stock returns and accounting variables. Further, we also consider cross-country differences in technological advances which is critical to the asset pricing implications of the displacement risk factor. The country variables thus include general technological level and spillovers from/to other countries. The asset pricing tests also crucially depend on the market efficiency of different equity markets, thus we also consider degrees of limits-to-arbitrage. We then conduct comprehensive portfolio analysis and predictive regressions to discover whether our empirical measure of displacement can predict returns on the international stage. To ensure the robustness of our results, we also construct alternative measures of innovation to confirm the economic and statistical significance of return predictability associated with displacement risk around the world. Based on our hypothesis, we will further examine the comovement between the displacement factor and value premium in each country. Finally, we study whether a new two-factor international asset pricing model with displacement return spread can outperform a model with a value factor. We will also examine whether the newly developed factor model is comparable to the existing ones such as involving momentum and valuation ratios.

17511716.value: 最近的文献提出，由于代际风险分担的缺乏，创新提高竞争力，却减少了现有企业的利润和侵蚀工人的人力资本，从而产生一个系统性的置换风险。价值溢价可因对此风险的不同敞口产生。 在本文中，我们测量国际市场上的公司股票与置换风险的关系。这样做可以让我们回答以下研究问题：（i）可否预测股票收益？ （二）此预测力与价值溢价有关吗？ （ⅲ）置换风险与国家特性有关吗？ （四）如果我们以置换风险取代价值因子，新的资产定价模型会更优吗？ 我们计划建立一个全面的全球面板数据，合并每个公共企业的创新措施（例如，专利和引文）股票收益，公司的会计变量，和国家解释 变量。有了更多的资金和人力资源，我们将能够继续下去彻底检查是否股票收益可预测性随国家和模型而变化。我们的结果最终将有助于开发一种新的国际资产定价模型。

17513816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17513816.value: Shareholders own modern corporations but managers are in charge of day-to-day operations. Where this separation of ownership and management exists, shareholders elect a board of directors to appoint and remunerate senior management, approve important business decisions, and oversee the overall operation of the company. Outside directors are hired to reduce conflicts of interest and to strengthen the independence of board decisions. The appointment of independent directors has been promoted as good corporate governance practice globally (e.g., see the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) of 2002 in the US). Directors therefore owe fiduciary duties to shareholders, and a company’s success crucially depends on the quality and diligence of its directors. In US shareholder litigation, directors may be held liable for breaches of fiduciary duties. However, directors are risk averse, and the potential for legal liability constitutes a credible threat to them. How much legal liability to impose on directors is a longstanding debate among academics and practitioners as evidenced by several legal reforms in US history. Proponents of more director liability emphasize the deterrence value of legal liability; opponents, however, argue that a high degree of liability prevents firms from hiring and retaining high-caliber outside director candidates and induces directors to be overly conservative in business decisions, both of which are detrimental to shareholders. Therefore, personal legal liability can affect the board of directors and thereby a company in two important ways – in ex ante director recruiting (which determines director quality) and in ex post director incentives (which determine director behaviors). There are many studies on the latter aspect examining, for example, how director liability affects firm risk taking and performance. Evidence on the former aspect (i.e., director protection helps firms recruit and retain high-caliber candidates, hereafter referred to as the “talent attraction and retention hypothesis”) is remarkably sparse. The purpose of this project is to address this research gap by testing the talent attraction and retention hypothesis with the staggered passage of “universal demand” (UD) laws in different states in the US as a quasi-natural experiment. As I will explain in detail in hypothesis development, UD laws create substantial barriers for shareholders to bring (derivative) litigation, thereby significantly lowering director exposure to liability. The research finding will contribute important evidence to the ongoing controversy over merits of director protection. 现代公司由股东拥有但经营由管理层负责。在公司所有权与经营权分离的情况下, 股东选举董事会, 由董事会来选聘经理人、确定其报酬，董事会也批准公司重大决策及监督公司的运营。在全球范围内，公司聘请外部独立董事来增强董事会的独立性被视为一种好的公司治理手段。董事对股东负有受托义务，公司的成败与董事的素质及勤勉有很大的关系。 在美国, 公司董事可能因为违反受托义务而被股东起诉。这种诉讼风险对于通常厌恶风险的董事来说构成了现实的威胁。学术界与业界对于公司董事应承受多少诉讼风险长期存在争论，美国历史上的立法实践对于这一问题的态度也时有反复。支持者们认为诉讼风险能有助于公司董事履行受托义务; 反对者则认为高诉讼风险一方面妨碍公司聘请、挽留高质素的董事人选，另一方面也令公司董事在决策中变得过于保守，以至于偏离股东利益最大化的目标。文献中已有很多关于董事个人面临的诉讼风险影响其决策行为的研究，但关于诉讼风险能否真正影响公司董事的质量和流失率的研究则寥寥无几。本课题的目的旨在填补这一空白。具体而言, 通过测试美国一些州通过Universal Demand法律前后公司新聘请的董事的质量及高质量董事人选的流失率的变化来回答这一重要的问题。Universal Demand法律的通过大幅度地提高了股东诉讼的门槛，从而降低了董事的诉讼风险。

17514516.label: Project Objectives
17514516.value: To study the direct effect of average product rating on perceived diagnosticity in online reviews. To study the interaction effect of average product rating and information disparity on perceived diagnosticity in online reviews.

17514516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17514516.value: In online markets, a product’s average review rating is often displayed at a marked place on the product page. While the average rating presents a collective evaluation of a product, its presence might also influence the way people perceive other information. We hypothesize that the average rating, as a piece of collective information, acts as 1) a predisposition which affects people’s perception towards other information; and 2) a risk level of product’s performance which changes the way people perceive consensus or information disparity from online reviews. In this research, we propose to empirically test our hypotheses with datasets from Amazon and TripAdvisor. Our study will improve our understand of the impact of the collective rating on consumers’ diagnosticity perception and shed light upon some of the conflictive results in prior studies. By studying the impact of average rating and information disparity on consumers’ diagnosticity perception, our research generates implications to both theories and business practices. 在網上市場中，一個商品的平均評價分數通常被顯示在商品主頁的顯著位置上。這個平均分在集合了人們對商品的評價的同時，也可能影響人們對其他信息的感覺。對此，我們提出兩個假設。第一，展示在商品主頁的商品平均分提供了一種傾向性，從而影響人們對一致性或差異性信息的感覺。第二，商品的性能風險調節了這種影響。本研究將採用Amazon和TripAdvisor的數據，通過實證方法檢測我們提出的假設。這項研究可以幫助人們更好地了解平均分對於消費者對評價實用性感覺的影響，同時，也對以往研究中出現的衝突結論提出解釋。通過了解平均分及信息差異和消費者對評價實用性感覺的關係，本研究將會從理論和商業實踐兩方面作出相應貢獻。

17514516.label: Realisation of objectives
17514516.value: In this project, we study the effect of average product review rating on the perceived diagnosticity, as measured by review helpfulness, in online reviews. We conducted a comprehensive review of recent literature on the research topic, and developed several hypotheses based on our review. A computer program was developed to collect hotel, user, and review data from TripAdvisor. We also obtained an archive of Amazon review data collected by Stanford University. The general information and review data of about 4,000 hotels was collected. Another computer program was developed to process both textual and numeric content in both data sets. The data sets were analyzed to empirically validate our hypotheses. Overall, our two research objectives have been successfully achieved.

17514516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17514516.value: Our analysis results confirmed that there is a direct effect of average product rating on the perceived helpfulness of an online review. Specifically, a review with a rating closer to the average product rating is more likely to be perceived diagnostic. In addition, we also found that information disparity, which measures the review opinion’s differences from the aggregated opinions, interacts with the direct effect. In particular, for reviews with high information disparity (i.e., a rating that is deviant from the average product rating), those for products with a high average rating is perceived less diagnostic than those for products with a low average rating. Four conference papers and two journal paper have been submitted for publication. Unfortunately, one journal submission was rejected by a top journal in our field after two reviews and we are currently preparing for a resubmission to another journal. Details are provided in Part C.

17514516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17514516.value: There is potential for further research on (1) studying what other factors may moderate the impact of aggregated opinions from existing reviews, and (2) studying how the display format of reviews affect the perception of reviews. We are currently conducting preliminary research in both directions. In particular, we have been studying the use of review tag functions in online marketplaces to improve user perception of reviews.

17514516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17514516.value: This project investigates how the helpfulness of a review is affected by the product's average rating and how the rating given by this particular review deviates from the average rating in online marketplaces. The relationships are validated through two large data sets collected from Amazon and TripAdvisor. Our findings indicate that consumers' information perception is affected by the consensus information provided by prior buyers. Based on our findings, platform owners can adjust their review display strategy according to a product's prior reviews.

17515416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17515416.value: 唤起新奇寻求驱动的用户创新产品购买--产品定位序列对同行领域和非同行领域推广的影响

17515416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17515416.value: 用户创新，定义为最终用户开发的新产品或服务，以成为当今最重要的创新战略模式之一。用户创新不仅推动了许多重要的新产品和工艺研发，还被高达40％的企业所广泛采用。然而，用户创新战略经常面临市场推广和购买的瓶颈。这一瓶颈直接威胁用户创新战略的生死存亡。 由于用户创新主要起源于用户发明者自己的需要而不是广大市场或消费者的需求，其产品的市场推广面临难以跨越的鸿沟。由于用户创新缺乏广大市场或消费者的外部信息输入，这种创新经常成为发明家的孤立的，一次性的项目。虽然最近的研究提倡用户创新应利用用户发明家群体或社区早期参与共同发展，这种策略可能只对用户创新在同行领域的推广有效（例如，其它同行业专家）。目前的学术研究尚未探索如何促进用户创新在同行领域和非同行领域的扩散。 为了填补这一学术研究空白，我们以创新理论和序列查询理论为基础，并探索如何通过设计用户创新的产品定位序列而激发其在同行领域和非同行领域的“新奇寻求”购买。“新奇寻求”购买指以寻求新的体验和应用而驱动的购买，而不是以解决现存问题而驱动的购买。我们建议“先目标后性能“产品定位序列促进同行领域的“新奇寻求”购买，而“先性能后目标” 产品定位序列促进非同行领域“新奇寻求”购买。这一产品定位序列战略有助于平衡消费者对用户创新产品的具体信息与抽象信息处理，从而推动“新奇寻求”购买。 本研究旨在扩动创新理论和消费者行为学的研究，同时为市场营销者提供切实可行的，在同行领域和非同行领域兼效的用户创新推广策略。

17516516.value: 中外合资企业的双元性战略：制度驱动要素与绩效影响

17516516.label: Project Objectives
17516516.value: To investigate the institutional drivers of ambidexterity by examining how institutional distance between partners’ home countries, i.e., economic distance, cultural distance and political distance, drive IJVs to engage in ambidextrous innovation. To develop a contingent view of ambidexterity by assessing how its effect on IJV performance is contingent on the competitive relationships between foreign and local partners, such as internal power competition and external market competition. To examine how the impact of ambidexterity on IJV performance is contingent on the coordinative relationships between foreign and local partners, such as contractual coordination and relational governance. To help IJV managers to better understand how to facilitate the successful implementation of ambidexterity to achieve superior performance.

17516516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17516516.value: International joint ventures (IJVs) are critical means by which multinational enterprises enter emerging markets, yet IJVs also face substantial challenges from the dynamic and complex environments of those markets. Therefore, IJVs must exploit the existing skills and capabilities of their foreign and local partners, as well as explore new opportunities and develop products for customers in the emerging markets. As a result, IJVs must develop ambidexterity, the ability to simultaneously pursue both explorative and exploitative innovation, to achieve sustainable competitive advantage in the host market. Despite rising interest in ambidexterity in both academic and industry circles, its impact on IJV performance may not be straightforward. Whereas ambidexterity has a number of benefits, including generating resource combinations, enjoying complementary benefits, and building dynamic capabilities, its implementation is challenging because of inherent conflicts in the procedures and routines involved in exploitation and exploration. Such an implementation challenge is particularly salient in the IJV context because foreign and local partners not only coordinate to pool their resources together and mitigate resource constraints, but also compete for decision-making power and take advantage of shared resources to maximize private benefits at their partner’s expense. By shaping resource allocation and usage, partner coordination and competition play important moderating roles in affecting the efficacy of ambidexterity. Also, because IJV partners differ widely in their institutional backgrounds, institutional distance, namely, economic, cultural, and political distance, likely imposes significant pressure on IJVs to pursue an ambidextrous strategy. To address these research gaps, we will incorporate institutional and relational theories into ambidexterity research and investigate the interplay among institutional distance, ambidexterity, partner competition and coordination, and IJV performance in China. Specifically, we will examine the following questions. (1) How does institutional distance, including economic, cultural, and political distance, drive IJVs to engage in ambidextrous innovation? (2) What is the impact of ambidexterity on IJV performance? How is that impact moderated by the competitive relationships between foreign and local partners? (3) How is the impact of ambidexterity on IJV performance contingent on the coordinative relationships between foreign and local partners? By addressing these research questions, our project will not only enrich the ambidexterity literature by uncovering its institutional drivers and boundary conditions, but also have direct implications for foreign companies, including Hong Kong firms, providing them with information on how to collaborate with local firms to develop ambidexterity and achieve superior performance in China. 合资企业是跨国公司进入新兴市场的重要方式，但该方式亦受到新兴市场日益变化的环境带来的巨大挑战。合资企业必须利用现有资源与能力，同时又必须开拓新的市场机会，以取得成功。因此，双元性成为跨国公司在新兴市场成功的重要战略。 尽管双元性战略受到学术界与业界的一致关注，它对合资企业绩效的影响还有待考量。虽然双元性有一系列的益处，包括资源组合，利益互补，即动态能力等等，其实施充满了挑战，因为利用与开拓需要不同甚至相冲突的过程与程序。 在合资企业中，中外双方不但合作以资源互补，并且竞争以获取控制权。合资双方的竞争合作关系对双元性战略的实施具有关键的影响。同时，合资双方的制度背景差异巨大，其经济，文化，与政治差异对合资企业追求双元性战略带来显著压力。 为解决这些问题，我们引入制度和关系理论来研究制度距离，双元性战略，合资双方的竞争合作关系，与合资企业绩效之间的关系。研究问题如下： （1） 制度距离（包括经济，文化，与政治距离）如何影响合资企业追求双元性战略？ （2） 双元性战略如何影响合资企业绩效？合资双方的竞争关系如何调节该影响？ （3） 合资双方的合作关系如何调节双元性战略对企业绩效的影响？ 本项目的研究结果将揭示双元性战略的制度驱动要素及绩效影响；这不仅会丰富双元性战略的文献，还会对外资公司（包括香港公司）如何与中国公司合作以建立双元性并获得卓越绩效提供重要的指导。

17516516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17516516.value: 1) Ambidexterity strategy, by balancing exploitation and exploration, is difficult for IJVs to achieve and implement. As a result, when compared to a more focused strategy, an ambidexterity strategy leads to lower IJV performance. Institutional distance, however, does not significantly affect a firm’s engagement in ambidextrous innovation. 2) IJV foreign parent control moderates the ambidexterity-IJV performance link. The focused strategy generates better IJV performance when foreign parent control is lower, but the intensity of ambidexterity leads to greater IJV performance when foreign parent control is higher. 3) Partner coordination moderates the ambidexterity-IJV performance link. The focused strategy generates better IJV performance when relational governance is lower, but the intensity of ambidexterity leads to greater IJV performance when relational governance is higher. 4) Both foreign control and trust promote IJV radical innovation (i.e., exploration); moreover, legal inadequacy strengthens the impact of foreign control but weakens that of trust on IJV radical innovation; on the other hand, government intervention weakens the positive role of foreign control yet strengthens that of trust. Outcome: two working papers under review at peer-reviewed journals 1) “Is Ambidexterity Strategy Beneficial to International Joint Venture Performance? Evidence from China”, under 1st review at Journal of World Business. 2) “Foreign control, trust, and radical innovation in IJVs in China: A contingent governance perspective,” under 2nd review at Industrial Marketing Management. Two papers published in peer-reviewed journals. 1) Ju M, JJ Lu, KZ Zhou (2018), “How Can International Ventures Utilize Marketing Capability in Emerging Markets? Its Contingent Effect on New Product Development,” Journal of International Marketing, 26(4): 1-17. 2) Lu JJ, C Shu, KZ Zhou (2019), “Product Newness and Product Performance in New Ventures: Contingent Roles of Market Knowledge Breadth and Tacitness,” Industrial Marketing Management, 72(Jan): 231-241.

17516516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17516516.value: One potential way is to study how the role of ambidexterity varies in different institutional settings. We could develop a model to examine, for example, how economic development and legal development moderate the impacts of ambidexterity and IJV performance.

17516516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17516516.value: This project examines whether ambidexterity strategy is beneficial to firm performance of IJVs in China. In particular, we have the following major findings: 1) Despite its conceptual appeal, ambidexterity strategy actually hurt IJV performance in China. In contrast, a focused strategy on either exploitation or exploration is better for IJV performance. 2) If IJVs decide to pursue ambidexterity strategy, they should hold high levels of foreign parent control. In such conditions, ambidexterity leads to greater IJV performance. 3) Alternatively, if IJV partners hold strong relational governance, ambidexterity leads to greater IJV performance. 4) IJVs should match their control and trust mechanisms with external institutional environments to foster IJV radical innovation (i.e., exploration). The findings of this project not only enrich our understanding of the roles of ambidexterity in IJVs, but also provide important managerial implications for IJVs to match different types of innovation strategies with contextual conditions to enhance firm performance.

17517816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17517816.value: Over-the-counter (OTC) markets, as opposed to central trading, are where many assets including government and corporate bonds, asset-backed securities and derivatives are traded. In OTC markets, almost all trades go through dealers, and empirical findings have suggested that interdealer trades count for a large proportion of overall transactions. Recent papers have documented several empirical findings regarding interdealer trades. (1) The directions of interdealer trades are persistent. (2) The trading relationships have a core-periphery structure. Central dealers are more interconnected and peripheral dealers connect mainly with central dealers. (3) Central dealers hold more inventories and the duration is longer. Existing studies have provided theoretical explanations for one or more of these findings but cannot simultaneously address all of them. We propose a tractable investor-dealer dynamic random search model. The nuance is the assumption of heterogeneous inventory capacities: a dealer either has large or small inventory capacity. This may result from heterogeneous financial costs or risk management considerations. In each period, dealers first randomly meet investors, which are governed by a certain matching technology. In the meeting, dealers can buy from a low-value asset owner only if they have storage space and can sell to a high-value non-owner only if they have inventory. Dealers then trade in a competitive interdealer market to re-balance inventories. We expect the equilibrium outcomes to match the above stylized facts. Each type of dealer has his/her optimal inventory level. Due to search frictions, the inventories after trading with investors may be higher or lower than the optimal level. Interdealer trades then emerge out of the re-balancing needs. Such needs and hence the direction of interdealer trades are persistent in steady state. Moreover, the structure of the trading relationships should have large dealers in the center and small ones in the periphery, as there are gains from trade between small and large dealers and among large dealers, but not among small dealers. Finally, it is more costly for a small dealer to hold inventory, as it means missing more potential buying opportunities. Therefore, central dealers hold more inventories. In addition, we can characterize how the direction of trade between small and large dealers depends on the underlying environments. We can also generate testable implications regarding prices and volume based on comparative statics analysis, which can provide reference for future empirical work. The results also have policy implications regarding regulations and market design. 在場外交易市場中，擁有不同庫存容量的中介商為了更好的與投資者買賣資產，會進行中介間交易，以將自己的資產庫存調整至合適的水平。實證研究顯示，中介商之間的交易關係呈現出一種核心 – 邊關交易網絡。在這項研究中，我們期望構建一個基於搜尋模型的理論框架，來解釋這一核心 – 邊緣交易網絡以及其他有關中介間交易的實證研究發現。根據我們的理論預測，擁有較大庫存容量的大中介商處於網絡的中心位置，而擁有較小庫存容量的小中介商處於邊緣位置。當市場上資產供給較為緊缺時，資產從邊緣的小中介商流向中心的大中介商。而當市場上資產供給較為充裕時，則是邊緣的小中介商為中心的大中介商提供流動性。同時，我們也可以通過比較靜態分析得到一系列關於中介間交易價格和交易量如何取決於市場因素的結論。這些理論預測可供未來的實證研究進行進一步的檢驗。

17517816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17517816.value: In an OTC market where dealers' inventory capacities differ, dealers trade among themselves, whenever the opportunities arise, to rebalance inventories for facilitating the sale and purchase of the asset to and from their investor clients. In equilibrium, the small-capacity dealers sell to the large-capacity dealers to provide them inventories when the asset supply is at a low level. When inventory is easy to come by but inventory capacity is scarce, as in a market with a large asset supply, the small-capacity dealers buy from the large-capacity dealers to help them free up inventory capacities for trading with their investor clients. The prediction, though counterintuitive, is supported by some available empirical evidence.

17517816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17517816.value: 1. The theoretical predictions can be empirically tested using rich data set available recently such as TRACE. Our prediction that small-capacity dealers provide immediacy to large-capacity dealers has not been directly tested in the empirical literature. This would have policy implications on regulation especially when market is in stress. 2. Our current model assumes that asset is indivisible. Future analysis can extend the current model to divisible asset. The characterization about dealers' and investors' decision on the intensive margin could lead to interesting new results.

17517816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17517816.value: Many financial assets, including government and corporate bonds, asset-backed securities, and derivatives, are traded in over-the-counter (OTC) markets instead of in centralized exchanges. Two distinguishing features of OTC markets are that trades are almost always intermediated by dealers of various kinds and that the dealers do not just trade with investors but also among themselves. An important question on inter-dealer trades in OTC markets that seems to have attracted scant attention is how market conditions help shape the directions of trade among heterogeneous dealers. In this project, we study how dealers trade with one another for managing inventory levels for trading with their customers and how the directions of trade among dealers is determined. The major point of departure from the existing literature is that, in our model, dealers are heterogeneous in their inventory capacities. We make novel prediction that small-capacity dealers provide immediacy to large-capacity dealers.
