17518516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17518516.value: Short product life cycle and rapidly changing market environment have made demand forecast a challenging task in high-tech component product markets. High-tech component buyers (i.e., device manufacturers such as Apple, Dell, and Lenovo) form complex networks in these markets and influence each other in decision making, further complicating the diffusion process of new technologies. This project focuses on the semiconductor industry and tries to help semiconductor companies such Intel, NVidia, and AMD understand how major customers influence each other when adopting new products. By learning such knowledge, sellers would be able to identify the most possible adopters and the most influential customers, make better demand forecasts, and optimize their development and sales efforts. First, we empirically examine two major possible sources of inter-firm influences, strategic reactions and network externalities, using a logit regression model and a set of sales data we collected from a major microprocessor company. Through the empirical analysis, we can obtain insights about the significance and possible effects of network influences. Although both types of influence may be at work, they need not always be positive influences. For example, firms may prefer not to adopt a technology if it has been adopted by their competitors. We will test the conditions under which negative influences could occur. Second, we will develop a demand forecast model that is based on network influences. Given the empirical estimations, we will derive the probability of adoption for each potential customer of a new product. Finally, we will estimate the distribution of the total demand given different initial adopters. Based on this result, we will explore the best product design and sales effort for a new product. In sum, this project can contribute to the literature of technology adoption by offering a new angle to investigate the diffusion process. Previous studies mostly focus on new product adoption in consumer markets and use models that are based on the Bass diffusion model. In contrast, we focus on firm interactions in business markets and use a network-based adoption model. We not only conduct empirical analysis and estimations, but also develop analytical models to generate prescriptive insights on how to design products and allocate sales efforts. 在高科技部件产品市场中，短促的产品生命周期和迅速变化的市场环境已经使得对未来需求的预测变得极端困难。在此之上，众多高科技部件的买方企业（例如苹果，戴尔，联想等）又交织成为网络结构并在其中相互施加影响。这使得新技术的传播过程变得更加复杂和难以预测。本研究项目着眼于半导体行业并致力于帮助诸如英特尔，英伟达，AMD等高科技企业理解下游买方企业在采纳新技术产品的过程中如何相互影响。通过了解这些知识，上游生产企业将能够找出那些最有可能采纳新产品的客户以及最有影响力的客户，由此做出更准确的需求预测，并优化研发和营销的投入。 首先，我们将通过实证研究来检验两种可能的企业间影响机制：策略性回应和网络外部性。在实证研究中，我们将用到逻辑回归模型和来自于一个主要的微处理器生产商的销售数据，并检验不同的网络影响机制的显著性和可能的效应。虽然两种机制可能同时存在，但它们并不一定是都起到了正向的作用。例如，有的企业可能倾向于不采纳某些已经被其他竞争企业所采纳的新产品和技术。我们将检验在何种条件下企业的采纳行为将产生负效应。 其次，我们将建立一个基于网络影响机制的需求预测模型。通过统计估算，我们将得到每一个潜在顾客在不同的网络条件下对于一个新产品的采纳概率。最终，我们将可以估算给定不同初始采纳者的总需求概率分布。基于这些结果，我们将探讨如何优化新产品研发和销售的投入。 概括来说，本研究项目将能为技术采纳领域提供一个关于技术扩散的新的视角。之前的研究大多集中在新技术在消费者市场中的扩散，而且之前的模型大多是基于Bass扩散模型。相比之下，我们更关注企业市场，使用的是网络模型。我们不仅将进行实证分析和检验，而且将对网络影响机制进行数学建模和优化分析。

17518516.label: Realisation of objectives
17518516.value: We have fully achieved three out of the six objectives, and the other three objectives have been realized to a great extent. We now list the results corresponding to each objective below. 1. The first objective has not been fully achieved. Although we have obtained a comprehensive and large data set from a major microprocessor seller in the global market, we still need extra data to address the endogeneity issues in our research problem. There are two ways to address the endogeneity issues, and both directions are extremely difficult. The first solution is to obtain the pricing data from the other major microprocessor sellers in the global market during the period covered by our data set. This is because microprocessor buyers’ purchase decisions are affected by the selling prices offered by different sellers in the market and vice versa. We have been trying to contact other major microprocessor sellers. The other solution is to find good instrumental variables that can affect one buyer but are not related to other buyers’ decisions and the sellers’ decisions in other ways. We have also been trying to think and find such variables. Due to these difficulties, we decided to shift the focus of our research from empirically testing the impact of inter-firm influences to theoretically analyze the impact of inter-firm influences in new product adoption. 2. We used a Cox Proportional Hazard Model to analyze how the time a buyer takes to start the purchase a new processor is affected by or related to various factors, especially the number of buyers that have adopted the new processor so far. Our analysis shows that the number of current adopters is significantly and nonlinearly related to the hazard ratio of adoption. In particular, the relationship is like an inverted U, which might be the net result of strategic reactions and network externalities among the buying firms. 3. Because we have not been able to address the endogeneity issues, it is not possible to identify the network influences empirically. Hence, we developed a game-theoretic model to achieve this goal. Specifically, we try to offer one plausible and novel mechanism to explain when negative inter-firm influences could occur—that is, the hazard of a buyer’s first purchase of a new product could be negatively related to the number of current adopters. We considered a simple dynamic price bargaining model between a buyer and a seller of a new component product. The seller has a limited capacity, and the only uncertainty is the number of manufacturers to adopt this new component, which determines the seller’s outside option in the negotiation. With this uncertainty, delaying the price agreement could be preferable because the buyer may receive a price cut if the seller’s outside option turns out to be weak. However, delay could also be costly as the seller may refuse to sell or ask for a high price if many adopters show up later. Thus, the timing of price agreement and the first purchase for the buyer is a trade-off between the benefit of collecting more information and the risk of losing the limited supply (or paying for a high price). Given that the firms are rational, information is symmetric, and the buyer’s outside option is to use older technologies, we derive the buyer’s optimal timing strategy—how to set the negotiation deadline and whether to delay the agreement. Interestingly, we find that the buyer can benefit more from waiting when there is a greater chance that the new component will be popular among the manufacturers (i.e., the buyers). Our result partially explains the negative correlation between the hazard of a buyer’s first purchase of a new product and the number of current adopters. This theoretical work has been accepted by Production and Operations Management. 4. Based on our research, we proposed to forecast the demand of a new product in two steps. First, we propose to use the Cox Proportional Hazard Model to predict the chance of adoption for each potential buyer and then estimate the average number of adopters. Second, we modified the Bass diffusion model by including the average number of adopters as an additional explanatory variable. 5. We compare our method against the traditional Bass diffusion model without the average number of adopters, and we find that our method can significantly improve the average absolute prediction error by 63.09%. 6. Our theoretical analysis allows us to discuss about the optimal sales efforts for the seller of a new product. Our model offers two important insights for the seller to negotiate with a buyer regarding the adoption of a new product. First, the seller can benefit from delay of a buyer’s first purchase of a new product, because delay allows the seller to learn whether it can sell the limited capacity to buyers that would like to offer higher prices. Second, the seller can benefit from setting a loose deadline for the price negotiation with a buyer, because a wider time window allows more opportunities to learn. Once we address the endogeneity issue involved in our empirical analysis, we could be able to discuss about the optimal product design and capacity decision for the seller according to the empirical findings.

17518516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17518516.value: In this research project, we have done both empirical analysis and theoretical modeling work. On the empirical side, we used a Cox Proportional Hazard Model to analyze how the time a buyer takes to start the purchase a new processor is affected or related to various factors, especially the number of buyers that have adopted the new processor so far. Our analysis shows that the number of current adopters is significantly and nonlinearly related to the hazard ratio of adoption. In particular, the relationship is like an inverted U, which might be the net result of strategic reactions and network externalities among the buying firms. Through theoretical modeling, we try to offer one plausible and novel mechanism to explain when negative inter-firm influences could occur. We find that, when the seller of a new product has a limited capacity and number of buyers is uncertain, both the seller and buyer can benefit more from waiting when there is a greater chance that other higher-value buyers exist. Accordingly, it is possible to observe a negative correlation between a buyer’s time of first purchase of a new product and the number of current adopters. Contrary to most existing theories of bilateral negotiation, delay can benefit both the seller and buyer and the joint expected payoff always weakly increases as the deadline is extended. This logic holds even if we extend the model is various ways. However, we also find that extending the deadline could hurt the buyer if side payments are not allowed. Although extending the deadline can improve the joint payoff, tighter deadlines are preferred by the buyer when the buyer has a sufficiently low bargaining power. In addition, when learning is fast enough and/or the chance of higher-value buyers showing up (in a strong market) is relatively low, the buyer will sometimes have time-inconsistent interests regarding the timing of agreement: although the buyer prefers a tighter deadline ex ante, delaying the agreement may be optimal for the buyer once the negotiation starts. This is because learning in this case mainly benefits the seller, and a tighter deadline weakens the value of learning as well as the seller’s bargaining position; with a loose deadline, it is difficult for the buyer to achieve an agreement on a low price in early periods. Hence, from the seller’s perspective, it is optimal to prevent a weak buyer from setting a tight deadline by offering side payments.

17518516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17518516.value: We believe our empirical work also has a great potential. Hence, we will continue our effort for the empirical work by asking other major microprocessor sellers for their pricing data and at the same time finding instrumental variables to identify the network influences. We will try to publish our work in the near future.

17518516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17518516.value: In this research project, we have done both empirical analysis and theoretical modeling work. On the empirical side, we use a comprehensive data set offered by a major microprocessor seller and a Cox Proportional Hazard Model to analyze how the time a buyer takes to start the purchase a new processor is affected by or related to various factors, especially the number of buyers that have adopted the new processor so far. Our analysis shows that the likelihood of a buyer’s first purchase increases with the number of current adopters first and then decreases, which might be the net result of both positive and negative influences among the buying firms. Through theoretical modeling, we try to offer one plausible and novel explanation for negative inter-firm influences. We find that, when the seller of a new product has a limited capacity and number of buyers is uncertain, both the seller and buyer in a price negotiation can benefit more from waiting when there is a greater chance that other higher-value buyers exist. We also show that it is optimal for the seller to offer side payments to a weak buyer in order to prevent the buyer from setting a tight deadline.

17520016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17520016.value: Company CEOs are often appointed with an internal position in the subsidiary company as the director of board or the executive manager. Such CEO’s subsidiary position is not required to be disclosed in the annual reports in the U.S. market. In 2004, China Securities Regulatory Committee (CSRC) revised the disclosure rules. Since then the information about CEO’s subsidiary position has been the mandatory disclosure for Chinese listed companies. In our research proposal, we will provide systematic evidence on the prevalence of the CEO’s subsidiary position and the determinants of the likelihood of CEO taking a position in the subsidiaries. We then investigate the effect of CEO’s subsidiary position on corporate policy decisions of the tax avoidance strategies. By taking a position in the subsidiaries, the CEO can have a better understanding of the subsidiaries’ operations and hence better capture tax planning opportunities through intra-company transactions among the company’s subsidiaries. We hypothesize a negative relation between the company’s effective tax rate and the indicator for CEO’s subsidiary position. We further propose to examine whether the hypothesized relation between effective tax rate and the indicator for CEO’s subsidiary position is more pronounced when these subsidiaries are located in the provinces different than the location of parent company and when these subsidiaries are operating in the industries different than the industry of parent company. Moreover, we propose the hypothesis that the effect of CEO subsidiary position is more pronounced for the firms with higher percentage of intangible assets (or more R&D expenditures), because the transfer pricing scheme is expected to be more subjective for these companies and tax authorities face difficulty in determining the fair prices of the intra-company transactions. Last, we propose to use the 2SLS method to address the endogeneity issue by using the logistic regression for the likelihood of CEO taking a subsidiary position. 上市公司首席執行官(CEO)經常會同時兼任子公司的行政職務，作為子公司的董事會成員或者是管理層成員。在美國市場這些信息是不需要披露給股東的。在2004年，中國證券監督委員會(CSRC) 修改了上市公司披露準則，把CEO的子公司任職列為強制披露的信息。通過利用最新披露的信息，在本研究計劃中我們將會提供一系列的實證證據來考察CEO子公司任職的普遍性，以及任職背後的決定因素。我們還會進一步考察CEO子公司任職對上市公司避稅行為的影響。具體而言，通過在子公司的任職，上市公司的CEO 能夠對子公司的運營狀況有更好的了解，從而有利於把握稅收籌劃的機會通過子公司之間的公司內部交易達到避稅的目的。因此，在我們的主要研究假設中， CEO擔任子公司職務的指標跟上市公司實際稅率應該是負相關的。我們將進一步研究是否這種負相關會對一些上市公司更明顯，包括那些子公司和公司總部在不同省份的上市公司，以及子公司跟母公司在不同行業的上市公司。除此之外，我們預計CEO子公司職務對稅收籌劃的影響會對那些有較多無形資產的上市公司更顯著。 因為對這些公司而言，相關子公司之間的轉移定價會變得更加抽象，使得稅收執法機構難於確定公允的轉移定價。最後，在本研究中我們將會使用2SLS方法來解決樣本的內生性問題。

17520016.label: Realisation of objectives
17520016.value: We successfully accomplished all the research objectives and demonstrated our findings in the paper titled “Parent−Subsidiary Common Managers and Corporate Tax Planning”. This paper is currently under the Revision & Resubmission (R&R) for consideration for the publication at Journal of Management Accounting Research (JMAR). Note that JMAR is ranked as the B+ journal according to the journal list of Faculty of Business and Economics, The University of Hong Kong. Please see the editor's letter for details (in Part C). The reviewers' suggestions and concerns are relatively easy to address. It looks like that the editor wants a quick turnaround and we need to submit the revised version back to JMAR by September 6. The revision procedure is going well. I am optimistic about the chance of our paper being accepted by JMAR in the next few months. Our paper explores the dual role of top managers within the organization. For the purpose of governance and oversight of subsidiary companies, top managers of listed firms are often appointed as the board members or senior managers of significant subsidiaries (“parent-subsidiary common managers”). The role of parent-subsidiary managers in corporate decisions is not well understood, largely due to the lack of data. Using a unique dataset of parent-subsidiary managers during 2009-2015 in China, we document the prevalence of parent-subsidiary managers and analyze the quality of internal information environment for these managers to make decisions of tax planning. Our main findings are as follows: 1. 41.1% of our sample firms have their top managers (CEO, CFO or Chairman) take a position in at least one subsidiary. Our determinant analysis further shows that the appointment decision is associated with some firm- and manager characteristics. These findings are pertinent to objectives #1 and #3 in the GRF application. 2. The effective income tax rate is lower for firms which appoint parent-subsidiary common managers. The tax-avoiding effect is more pronounced for firms with more intangible assets, more related-party transactions, and more diversified business. These evidence answer the questions related to research objectives #2 and #3. 3. The characteristics of subsidiary companies also affect the role of parent-subsidiary managers in tax planning; tax-avoiding effect is more pronounced for economically significant subsidiaries, subsidiaries entitled to preferential tax treatments, and subsidiaries where common managers involve the daily operations to a greater extent. These analyses achieve the goals for the research objectives of #2 and #4.

17520016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17520016.value: In this GRF project, we successfully develop a high-quality paper, “Parent−Subsidiary Common Managers and Corporate Tax Planning”. This paper is now under the Revision & Re-submission (R&R) of Journal of Management Accounting Research (JMAR). The editor's comments are encouraging and the reviews' concerns can be addressed empirically. The revised version will need to be submitted back by September 6 and we are optimistic about the outcome. As an interesting but neglected governance mechanism of firm’s subsidiaries, top managers of the parent company often take a position in significant subsidiaries (“parent-subsidiary common manager” hereafter). These parent-subsidiary common managers have better access to subsidiary-level information and, therefore, possess greater knowledge for tax planning. Using the unique disclosure of senior executives’ subsidiary positions for Chinese listed firms, we find that the effective income tax rate is lower for firms which appoint parent-subsidiary common managers. The results are more pronounced for firms with more intangible assets, more related-party transactions, and more diversified business. Moreover, the tax-saving effect is stronger when top managers take a position in the subsidiaries which are economically significant and entitled to preferential tax treatments, and when common managers involve in the operations of subsidiaries. To the best of our knowledge, this paper is the first study about the role of parent-subsidiary common managers in corporate decisions.

17520016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17520016.value: We develop a novel measure to capture the extent to which the top managers (CEO, CFO and Chairman) take a position in subsidiary companies. This measure can be a very useful proxy for firm's internal information environment and hence can be used for many other research topics, such as the internal capital allocation and the quality of management earnings forecasts.

17520016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17520016.value: In this project, we show that when headquarters' managers (CEO, CFO and Chairman) are also appointed as the managers of the subsidiary companies, these top managers are more informed about tax-planning opportunities and better skilled in coordinating tax-avoidance. Consequently, the appointment of top managers with divisional titles is associated with better firm performance.

17520516.label: Realisation of objectives
17520516.value: 1. Summary of outputs We have a 100% degree of completion for our research objectives. The paper has been accepted and presented in the Hawaiʻi Accounting Research Conference (2019). The paper has also been accepted by the annual conference of the European Accounting Association (2019) (but was not presented at this conference due to the presenting author's visa issue at that time). Both conferences are internationally recognized high-quality conferences. RGC funding is acknowledged in our paper. Also, we have circulated the paper in several world-class research universities, including the University of British Columbia, Simon Fraser University, and the University of Hong Kong. The paper was well received by the conference participants and seminar attendees. The paper is currently under review at Management Science. This project was extended only once rather than the maximum allowable times (twice) of extensions even though we do need an extension for the long review process of a journal paper. By the first extended deadline, we thought that we did not have much balance of funds left so we did not further extend the fund period. It turns out that the fund still has a positive balance because one student RA who did a large amount of data collection work left Hong Kong and has not yet claimed for the payment even though I have reminded her several times. If the payments were made to her, we should have a zero balance. The circulation period and the review process of journals are usually relatively long. We expect that our paper will ultimately be published in a top journal. 2. Motivations, challenges, solutions, and new findings External auditors are crucial capital market gatekeepers. Whether and how institutional forces shape auditor behavior has long been of interest to both regulators and researchers. A central theme of audit regulation studies is how the auditing institutional environment determines the assurance level of audit services and how the differential audit quality produced by various auditors characterizes the audit market. This project intends to better understand how auditors’ going-concern reporting decision is shaped by institutional forces. To achieve our project objectives, the initial setting we adopt is the inception of credit default swap (CDS) trading on client firms. After finishing the data cleaning and data analysis, we find robust results that audit fees increase following the inception of CDS trading. The evidence is consistent with the conjecture that the inception of CDS trading increases clients’ business risk, therefore affecting auditors’ perceived litigation risk. When analyzing auditors’ going concern reporting incentives, we find that firms in our sample are mostly large firms that are not financially distressed. However, auditors’ going-concern reporting is relevant mostly for financially distressed firms. Using our current sample, we find that very few clients receive going-concern modified audit opinions. Given this evidence, we recognize that the variation of litigation risk within the U.S. is a more fundamental institutional force that influences auditors’ going concern reporting incentives. To better understand auditors’ tradeoff when making going concern reporting decisions, we analyze whether and how federal level litigation risk shapes the going concern reporting incentives of the two fundamental tiers of suppliers in the audit market: Big 4 and non-Big 4 public accounting firms. Before conducting empirical analysis, we first analytically analyze auditors’ loss function and going concern reporting incentives. We model the auditor’s going concern reporting problem as a 2-action, 2-state going concern reporting decision that an auditor faces after completing all necessary audit tests that yield “sufficient appropriate evidence” that the financial statements are, indeed, free of material misstatements. In that case, the auditor’s optimal decision is to issue an unqualified opinion (i.e. clean opinion) on the client’s financial statements. However, the unqualified opinion may or may not be modified to explain that there is “substantial doubt” that the client is a going concern and therefore may not be able to continue to operate in the foreseeable future. So the auditor’s possible actions are: {unqualified opinion (UN), or unqualified opinion with a going concern modification (UNGC)}. The two states of nature concern the future operations of the business, namely: {success (S), or failure (F)}. At the equilibrium, the auditor is choosing a threshold value for the probability of bankruptcy at which she will be indifferent in issuing either unqualified opinion or going concern modified opinion. Based on the model, the effect of variations in a litigation risk on auditors’ going concern reporting threshold depends on not only the amount of variation but also the base level of litigation risk in the legal regime. The analysis suggests that litigation risk will have differential effects on Big 4 and non-Big 4. If the base level of litigation risk for Big 4 is sufficiently greater than that for non-Big 4, the marginal effect will be greater for non-Big 4 (relative to Big 4) and the two tiers of audit firms will converge in their going concern reporting incentives as the federal level litigation risk associated with judge ideology increases. We predict that, all else equal, the effects of variation in federal judge ideology on auditors’ going concern reporting incentives will be different for Big 4 audit firms than for non-Big 4 ones. For empirical tests, it has been particularly difficult to measure the variation of litigation risk within one country, and prior studies usually explore cross-country variation in the rule of law. We address the measurement challenge by following Huang et al. (2019) in using the political ideology of judges to infer variation in litigation risk in the U.S. Using a large sample of financially distressed companies, we find that Big 4 and non-Big 4 auditors converge in their going-concern reporting decisions as federal litigation risk increases. The results remain when the regression models control for firm- and circuit- fixed effects, suggesting that the results not driven by time-invariant firm characteristics which may affect the likelihood of auditor choice and client bankruptcy. Rather, the results are associated with the time-varying perceived federal level litigation risk associated with judge ideology. We find that the result is caused by the greater effect of judge ideology on non-Big 4 than on Big 4 auditors. These results suggest that the heightened litigation risk associated with more liberal judges motivates the non-Big 4 firms to be more independent of their clients’ interests and more “defensive” in their reporting decisions. The evidence is consistent with the analytical prediction that the federal level litigation risk will have a greater effect on non-Big 4 auditors than on Big 4 auditors because the former has a much lower base level of federal litigation risk. Concerning reporting accuracy, we find that the Type II error rates do not vary significantly between the Big 4 and non-Big 4 audit firms, irrespective of the litigation risk associated with judge ideology. Our evidence consistent with non-Big 4 firms being less independent and concerned with client retention when litigation risk is relatively low. However, as investor litigation risk increases thereby increasing the cost of Type II reporting errors, the heightened legal liability associated with more liberal judge ideology motivates a change in the behavior of non-Big 4 audit firms that makes them more similar to the Big 4 firms in terms of the likelihood of issuing a going concern modified opinion.

17520516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17520516.value: Conference proceedings: the paper has been accepted and presented in the Hawaiʻi Accounting Research Conference (2019) and is currently under review at Management Science. Our analyses generate sound analytical theory and robust empirical results. The research outcome is quite relevant to the current discussion by the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) on the necessity of providing a more clear bankruptcy probability threshold for auditors to issue going-concern opinions. We believe that our paper will be ultimately published in top journals. The key takeaway from our analytical model is that, with auditors trading off between Type I and Type II reporting errors, the threshold value (of client bankruptcy probability) above which auditors issue going-concern reports is decreasing and convex in the level of federal litigation risk. Our empirical results are consistent with the prediction based on our model. We find that Big 4 and non-Big 4 auditors converge in their going-concern reporting decisions and Type I reporting error rates as federal litigation risk increases. This is caused by the effect on non-Big 4 auditors rather than Big 4 ones. This evidence is novel to the auditing literature and adds to the literature on the economic incentives of auditors and the impact on the observable consequences. Our findings that the two classes of audit firms tend to converge in their going concern reporting as litigation risk increases is important because as these audit firms become more similar, the market for audit services becomes more competitive. That is, the set of suppliers offering similar high-quality audits becomes larger thereby fostering competition and greater client choice. Our findings suggest that a “one size fits all” threshold for going concern reporting will have different economic consequences for audit firms depending on the varying federal level ligation risk. More specifically, our findings are informative to investors in interpreting the implication of modified going concern audit opinions. Also, the findings are particularly relevant for regulators who are currently assessing the proposal of changing the existing auditing standard regarding auditors’ going concern evaluation of their clients. To improve the going concern reporting structure, the PCAOB has been considering clarifying the term “substantial doubt” since 2012 (PCAOB, 2012, 2015). A significant portion of investors seems to support the use of a relatively tough (i.e., low) bankruptcy probability threshold “more likely than not (> 51%)” to define a “going concern” (PCAOB, 2015). Even if a threshold is clarified, determining a bankruptcy probability still involves substantial judgment (unless a uniform equation of bankruptcy estimation is provided by in the auditing standards). Specifying a low threshold will ultimately be translated to a higher legal liability for Type II reporting errors. Further, the evidence that non-Big 4 auditors increase the likelihood of issuing going concern reports in more liberal circuits without decreasing the likelihood of Type II reporting errors implies that the going concern reporting structure may not be improved if the regulators’ objective is to reduce Type II reporting errors.

17520516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17520516.value: The big picture issue of our research scheme is the economic incentives of auditors and their impact on observable outcomes, such as audit quality. In our current study, we focus on auditors’ going concern reporting behaviors because whether or not a firm will continue as a going concern determines the basis upon which financial statements are prepared. Understanding auditors’ going concern decisions provides the basis for analyzing other audit outcomes. We did not analyze other audit outcomes, such as accrual quality, because accrual quality is the joint output of the financial statement preparation by managers and the verification and correction of financial statements by external auditors. It would be quite useful if audit adjustment data becomes available (for research purpose) for a relatively large sample in the U.S. Audit adjustment is the difference between pre-audit earnings and post-audit earnings. It directly reflects the degree and amount of corrections made by external auditors. Such data is available for a small sample of clients inspected by the PCAOB currently. When the data becomes available for a larger sample of companies, we can investigate the association between federal level litigation risk and the degree of audit adjustments. Such an investigation would be particularly informative of the effect of litigation risk on audit production. It will also be novel in the auditing literature on audit production in the U.S., most of which basically uses either discretionary accruals or restatements to infer audit quality.

17520516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17520516.value: A central theme of audit regulation studies is how the auditing institutional environment determines the assurance level of audit services and how the differential audit quality produced by various auditors characterizes the audit market. There is virtually no prior research on how the difference between the Big 4 and non-Big 4 audit firms varies with the legal strength within one country. Going-concern is a fundamental basis for financial statement preparation and is important for financial statement users when interpreting companies’ accounting numbers. The delivered paper addresses a fundamental problem on going concern reporting: how the two basic tiers of auditors in the audit market tradeoff their costs and benefits differently when making going concern reporting decisions. We theoretically and empirically show that the difference between Big 4 and non-Big 4 converges as federal level litigation risk increases. This is driven by the greater effect of litigation risk on non-Big 4 auditors, not Big 4 auditors. The finding is useful for both investors and regulators to better understand the product difference in the audit market. It enables investors to better interpret audit outcomes. For regulators, it suggests that a “one size fit all” policy may not be feasible.

17520716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17520716.value: Endogeneity and structural shifts are commonplace in many economic relationships. Endogenous threshold regression, which recognizes both characteristics, is now becoming popular in econometric practice. In Yu and Phillips (2015), we solve part of the estimation problem, showing that the threshold point can be identified even when no instruments are available and proposing a new estimation procedure. However, the asymptotic distribution of this estimator is complicated and not well suited for statistical inference. Further, no specification tests were developed to assess evidence for endogeneity or the presence of structural shifts with endogeneity. This project is designed to solve these two challenging problems of inference and specification testing. For inference concerning the threshold point, we propose four different methods, each applying under certain conditions (such as the availability of suitable instrumentation) and each having its own advantages. Practitioners can then choose an inferential procedure based on the available information. For specification testing, we extend the idea of the score test to this new environment. Accordingly, all the new test statistics will be constructed under the null, which facilitates implementation as well as asymptotics. In testing for the presence of structural shifts, these tests will be valid irrespective of whether instruments are available and they are easier to apply than Wald tests, both advantages making them well suited for empirical work. 内生性和结构变化是在许多经济关系中司空见惯。内生性阈回归包含了这两个特点，所以在计量经济学中很流行。在于萍和菲利普斯（2015）中，我们部分的解决了估计问题，表明阈值点即使在没有工具变量的情况下仍然可识别，并提出了新的估计方法。然而，这个估计量的渐近分布很复杂，不适合进行统计推断。此外，没有设定检验可用来评估是否存在内生性或结构转变。该项目旨在解决统计推断与设定检验中这两个具有挑战性的问题。 关于阈值点推断，我们提出了四种不同的方法，每一种方法可在一定的条件下应用（如是否有工具变量可用），所以各具优点。使用者可以根据可用信息选择一种推断方法。对于设定检验，我们把得分检验推广到这一新情形下。因此，所有新的检验统计量都在零假设下建构，这有利于实际操作和渐近分布的推导。在检验结构转变中，不论工具变量是否存在，这些检验都是有效的。而且，它们比沃尔德检验更容易应用。这两个优势使得它们非常适合于实证工作。

17520716.label: Realisation of objectives
17520716.value: In this project, we put forward three inference methods for the threshold point and two specification tests in threshold regression with endogeneity. We finished all objectives on time. We also presented a paper generated from this project in the following conferences or seminars: CMES2018, CUHK, ESAM2018, ESEM2018, HU-HUE-SMU Tripartite 2018, NASMES2018, QNU, TAMU, TEC2018 and Tsinghua University. During the project, we also extended one point in the original project to a separate paper. Specifically, we show that the estimator of Kourtellos et al. (2016) is not generically consistent. We also put forward two alternative estimators of the threshold point and three estimators of the slope parameters which are consistent generally. We present this paper in the following conferences or seminars: CUHK, QNU, UWAC2018, Korea University and Tsinghua University.

17522116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17522116.value: 動態制度視角理解外國公司績效

17522116.label: Project Objectives
17522116.value: Develop a dynamic institution-based view of foreign firm performance. Explore the effects of pace and rhythm of institutional change on foreign firm performance. Examine how foreign firms can better handle changing institutional environments by developing certain resources and designing a particular governance structure. Provide suggestions for policy makers on how they should implement market-oriented institutional change.
rows: Develop a dynamic institution-based view of foreign firm performance.
Explore the effects of pace and rhythm of institutional change on foreign firm performance.
Examine how foreign firms can better handle changing institutional environments by developing certain resources and designing a particular governance structure.
Provide suggestions for policy makers on how they should implement market-oriented institutional change.

17522116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17522116.value: Market-oriented institutional change is a widely acknowledged phenomenon in emerging economies. The major role of institutions is “to reduce uncertainty by enabling a stable structure to human interaction” (North, 1990). However, the process of market liberalization, decentralization of state control, and corporate governance reform in emerging markets renders the business environment complex, unstable, and unpredictable. For multinational corporations (MNCs) operating in this context, how to strategically handle the changing institutional environment is a key challenge. While the dynamic nature of institutions has been widely recognized, the literature examining their influence on firms’ strategic choices and performance still adopts a static view. Numerous institution-based studies investigate how the development level of institutions shapes foreign firms’ entry strategy, governance structure and performance, but the impact of a transitioning institutional environment is somewhat less examined. It is still not clear how MNCs can strategically cope with institutional environments that are in flux. In this project, we advance a dynamic view of institutions by examining the effects of institutional change on foreign firms as they, as outsiders, experience greater challenges in tackling the fluctuating environment. This study will specifically examine three questions: (1) Which type of institutional change, rapid or gradual, is more beneficial for foreign firms? (2) How does the rhythm of institutional change influence foreign firm performance? (3) How can foreign firms better respond to market-oriented institutional change? By addressing these research questions, this project makes theoretical contributions to the institution-based view and provides practical suggestions for MNCs that operate or plan to operate in emerging economies. The results of this study can also provide insights for policy makers on implementing market-oriented institutional change in emerging economies. 市場導向的制度變遷是新興經濟體中的一種普遍現象。眾所周知，制度的主要作用是“通過構建一個有助於人際互動的穩定結構來减少系統中的不確定性”（North，1990年）。然而，在新興市場上，市場自由化行程，國家控制力下放，以及公司治理改革都使得企業商業環境愈加複雜、多變、與不可預測。對於在這樣情景下運營的跨國企業，如何戰略性的應對變化的制度環境是一個重要挑戰。雖然制度的動態特性已被廣泛認可，但是有關企業戰略決策和績效研究的文獻仍多採用靜態視角研究制度的作用。現有基於制度的研究已經探討過制度發展水平是如何决定外國企業進入戰略、治理機制和績效水平，但是針對制度環境變化對跨國企業影響的研究仍很少。現時仍不清楚跨國公司是如何戰略性地應對不斷變化的制度環境的影響。相較本國企業，作為外來者的外國公司，在應對波動的環境時將遇到更大的挑戰。因此，在這個項目中，我們通過探究制度變遷對外國公司的影響，提出一個基於動態視角的制度理論。本研究將具體考察三個問題：（1）哪些類型的制度變遷，比如快速或漸進，對外資企業更有利？（2）制度變遷的節奏如何影響外國公司的績效？（3）外資企業如何更好地應對市場導向的制度變遷？通過解决這些問題，本研究對基於制度視角的理論發展做出貢獻，並針對正在或即將進入新興經濟體的跨國企業提供實踐建議。同時，這項研究的結果也為政策制定者提供在新興經濟體中實施以市場為導向的制度變遷的卓見。

17522816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17522816.value: 早期父母不良教养方式对领导力发展的影响：一项基于成人依恋的研究

17522816.label: Project Objectives
17522816.value: To develop and test theory with regard to how and why leaders' early experience of parental abuse is related to subsequent abusive supervision against their followers through leaders' avoidant attachment style To develop and test theory with regard to how and why leaders' early experience of parental neglect is related to subsequent laissez-faire leadership through leaders' anxiety attachment style To examine the moderating role of higher-level supervisory behavior in shaping the relationship between leaders' insecure attachment styles and leadership behaviors

To develop and test theory with regard to how and why leaders' early experience of parental neglect is related to subsequent laissez-faire leadership through leaders' anxiety attachment style
To examine the moderating role of higher-level supervisory behavior in shaping the relationship between leaders' insecure attachment styles and leadership behaviors

17522816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17522816.value: 本研究基于依恋理论（Bowlby, 1969), 旨在探索领导者早期经历的不良父母教养方式如何影响他们在组织中的领导行为。在领导力的发展过程中，个体的成人依恋方式可能起到关键的中介作用。具体而言，早期经历父母虐待的个体倾向于形成回避型依恋，而这种不安全的成人依恋方式在组织中的领导岗位上会表现为辱虐型领导行为。而早期被父母忽略的个体倾向于形成焦虑型依恋，而这种不安全的成人依恋方式在组织中的领导岗位上会表现为放任型领导行为。此外，上级的领导行为作为组织中重要的环境因素，可能会激发和调节领导者的依恋方式对其领导行为的影响。本研究拟通过两项多层多源的问卷调查来验证上述理论假设。

17522816.label: Realisation of objectives
17522816.value: With our findings from two studies in both organizational and educational settings, the three main objectives in the project proposal have been fully realised. Our first objective was to develop and test theory with regard to how and why leaders' early experience of parental abuse is related to subsequent abusive supervision against their followers through leaders' avoidant attachment style. By drawing from the attachment theory and the literature in abusive supervision and workplace aggression, we have developed new theory not only on the overall notion that adult attachment serves as a crucial psychological mechanism that bridges a leader's past experience with authority (e.g., parents), but also argued specifically how and why early parental abuse would shape an avoidant style of attachment which further triggers abusive behavior when one himself/herself is in an authority position (e.g., business unit or student leader). Our findings in both studies have fully supported this hypothesised overall effect of parental abuse on abusive supervision (H1a) and the indirect effect via attachment avoidance (H2a and H3a). Our second objective was to develop and test theory with regard to how and why leaders' early experience of parental neglect is related to subsequent laissez-faire leadership through leaders' anxiety attachment style. In addition to original theory development as mentioned above, our findings in both studies have fully supported the overall effect of parental neglect on laissez-faire leadership (H1b) and largely supported the indirect effect through attachment anxiety (H2a and H3a). Specifically, although the relationship between attachment anxiety and laissez-faire leadership was only approaching statistical significance (p = .08) in Study 1, it was significant at the contingent level when supervisor's laissez-faire leadership was high. The corresponding hypothesis was fully supported in Study 2. Overall, we consider this hypothesis supported and the objective fully realised. Our third objective was to examine the moderating role of higher-level supervisory behavior in shaping the relationship between leaders' insecure attachment styles and leadership behaviors. Drawing from the trait activation literature, we have developed original theory that identifies one's current supervisor's leadership style as a magnifier of one's attachment effects. In both studies, we not only analysed the moderation and plotted the interactions, but also tested the difference between the overall indirect effects at high and low levels of the moderator - a moderated mediation model. Our hypotheses were fully supported in Study 1, but not in Study 2. We recognise that as Study 2 was designed to capture parental influence as it is lived rather than from retrospection, it is possible that the influence of student leaders' faculty supervisors was suppressed as the student leaders are still living at home and under direct influence of their parents. But overall, we are confident about our findings in Study 1 and would consider the moderation hypotheses supported and this objective fully realised.

17522816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17522816.value: Using one organizational sample with 214 leaders and 436 followers and one student sample that contains 684 high school student leaders and their parents and 3,265 student followers, our research project has developed original theory with regard to how and why leaders' early experience of dysfunctional parenting (e.g., parental abuse and neglect) may affect their current counterproductive leadership behaviours (e.g., abusive supervision and laissez-faire leadership) through shaping one's adult attachment styles. We further developed and tested theory suggesting that the dysfunctional leadership of the leaders' current higher-level supervisors will serve as a context that triggers and magnifies the attachment effect in shaping dysfunctional leadership behaviours. Our findings from both samples have provided consistent and sufficient support for all of our hypotheses. We presented findings from Study 1 (the organizational sample) at a specialised attachment conference (International Attachment Conference 2017) to collect feedback from attachment experts from development and clinical psychology that are outside the PI's normal circle of management researchers. As indicated in the extension request, our first few attempts of securing the student sample for Study 2 were unsuccessful due to the sensitive nature of some of our measures (e.g., dysfunctional parenting and leadership). With the extra time allowed by the extension (Thanks very much!), we have communicated thoroughly with a school in Henan province and established a trusting relationship with the school administration team and the students. We were fortunate enough to have finished the data collection in late 2019 before the COVID-19 epidemic starts, but the survey mailing and data input were delayed due to the lockdowns in early 2020. The PI was finally able to receive all the data for Study 2 in September 2020. We synthesised the findings from both Study 1 and Study 2 and prepared a manuscript for the 2021 Annual Meeting for Academy of Management in order to gather feedback from management researchers. We plan to continue polishing the manuscript for submission to Academy of Management Journal, the flagship empirical journal in management, by mid 2021. My doctoral student, Ms. Ying ZHANG, has been working as a part-time RA under the support of this GRF grant. She has developed many different aspects of research skills through helping out in this project, and developed a passion on the topic of laissez-faire leadership. She decided to further examine the concept of laissez-faire leadership from a team knowledge exchange perspective and successfully defended her dissertation in August 2020.

17522816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17522816.value: Our research has showcased the value of theorising leadership as a dependent variable. In contrast to the majority of leadership research that focuses on the consequences of leadership (e.g., follower and organizational outcomes), it is also important, and very interesting, to ask why leaders are behaving in certain ways. Our research goes beyond the popular trait perspective (e.g., personality predictors of leadership) and looks at leaders' childhood experience with the first authority figures in their lives (e.g., parents). Although we only examined the links between dysfunctional parenting and counterproductive leadership, we plan to (and encourage future research to) look at the bright side of this developmental process, too, by examining the relationship between parenting experience and leadership development in a comprehensive manner. Our research has highlighted the value of adult attachment in bridging one's early experience and current organizational life. We believe this psychological concept has a tremendous amount of potentials in furthering our understanding of one's work and life experiences.

17522816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17522816.value: Our research takes a unique perspective by looking at how a leader's childhood experience of parenting may shape their current leadership styles. Specifically, our findings suggest that leaders who experienced parental abuse are more likely to abuse their current subordinates whereas leaders who experienced parental neglect are more likely to be absent when their current subordinates are in need. We believe that the insecure attachment styles that leaders have gradually developed from childhood to adulthood may account for these findings, and the dysfunctional leadership from higher-level supervisors in the organization will trigger and exacerbate the influence of these insecure attachment styles. Our research has highlighted the value of extending the time frame for leadership development further to one's early childhood and provide important implications for leadership development in both organization and education settings.

17524816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17524816.value: 重回公平竞争：中国民营企业的佐证

17524816.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17524816.value: Prof Du, Julan Dr Lu, Yi

17524816.label: Project Objectives
17524816.value: We will examine if donation for the reconstruction after the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake has a positive impact on abnormal stock returns of private enterprises, but no effect on those of state-owned enterprises. We will investigate if the positive impact of the donation is greater for private enterprises located in regions with poorer economic institutions.
rows: We will examine if donation for the reconstruction after the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake has a positive impact on abnormal stock returns of private enterprises, but no effect on those of state-owned enterprises.
We will investigate if the positive impact of the donation is greater for private enterprises located in regions with poorer economic institutions.

17524816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17524816.value: The Chinese economy is characterized by the strong role of the state versus the market in the economy, and the extensive undertaking of economic activities by the state in the form of widespread state ownership (or Chinese-style state capitalism). Despite thirty plus years of economic reform, China has maintained a significant percentage of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in most industries as a way of fulfilling multiple social and political responsibilities, while developing private enterprises (including both domestic private enterprises and foreign affiliates) on the margin. Our preliminary work, however, provides strong evidence of discriminations against private enterprises in China, as reflected in the administrative monopoly power enjoyed by SOEs over their privately owned counterparts of the same industries. The administrative monopoly power enjoyed by SOEs has squeezed the living space and undermined the interests of private enterprises, which is the engine of growth in China. The proposed study is to examine whether donations by China’s private enterprises for the reconstruction after the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake allow them to show their allegiance to the government and hence alleviate the discrimination they have encountered in both the input and output markets, and whether such effects may differ across China’s regions of different quality of economic institutions. This project will help us understand the Chinese-style state capitalism in which both the advantageous SOEs and disadvantageous private enterprises co-exist under a government that plays a dominant role in the economy. It will also generate strategy implications for privately owned enterprises to get back a level playing field so as to overcome its inherent competitive disadvantage. 中国经济的特色是：政府相较于市场在经济活动中扮演了强势的角色；政府通过社会主义公有制（或者称为中国特色国家资本主义）深入、全面地介入了经济活动的方方面面。在经历了三十几年市场化改革的今天，中国政府为了履行多重社会和政治责任，仍在绝大多数行业保留了相当比例的国有企业，而始终将发展中的国内民营企业和外资企业置于边缘。我们现阶段的研究展现了同一行业内国有企业相较于民营企业所拥有的行政垄断权力，为民营企业在中国受到不平等待遇提供了强有力的佐证。 民营企业是中国的增长引擎，但是国企的行政垄断挤压了民营企业生存空间，损害了民企利益。此研究通过检验私企通过为08年地震重建的捐款向政府表忠心是否减少了他们在要素市场和产出市场受到的歧视，以及捐款的效果在制度环境质量不同的中国地区间是否有差异。这项研究有助于了解中国的国家资本主义，及在其中共存的占有利地位的国企和占弱势地位的民企，和在两者之上在经济中占统治地位的政府。此研究也对私企如何克服不利因素获取平等竞争环境提供了策略指导。

17524816.label: Realisation of objectives
17524816.value: Corporate donations are an important aspect of strategic corporate social responsibility, which plays an increasingly significant role in firm survival and growth in contemporary market economies. Corporate expenditure on community services, philanthropic programs, environmental protection and employee welfare can create value added for firms through improved corporate image, the goodwill and loyalty of customers, the enhanced employee morale, and the more lenient or favorable treatment by regulators. However, it is much less understood what roles corporate donations play under state capitalism, where governments use markets to extend their own political and economic leverage through state ownership and control of enterprises, through allocation of credit to privileged companies (e.g., national champions), etc., and most of non-state-owned companies are often disadvantaged in product and factor markets. We address this question by conducting a study of corporate donations in the wake of Wenchuan earthquake in China on May 12, 2008 to investigate this issue. China provides an ideal setting. The country has grown rapidly over the past few decades, but has also developed into a leading example of state capitalism. Furthermore, the Chinese political system is a leading authoritarian regime, which reinforces the state control of the economy and leads to an authoritarian state capitalism model. We first collect information on the donations made by listed firms in the wake of the Wenchuan earthquake from several sources: (1) corporate announcements on special corporate donations for the earthquake victims; (2) information on corporate donations for earthquake relief that is released in the relevant companies’ websites; (3) information disclosed by media news reports on earthquake donations made, typically, by a group of corporations; (4) donations announced by firms in the earthquake relief fund raising party called The Giving of Love organized by the CCTV on May 18, 2008. Eventually, we obtain the information on donations made by 1379 non-state-controlled listed firms. The information collected on corporate donations includes the date of the donation made, the date of the public announcement or media coverage of the corporate donation, the amount of the donation (donation size), the types of donation (i.e., in-kind/materials donation or cash donation), etc. The data on individual stock trading come from the Dataset on Stock Prices and Returns in China’s Capital Markets produced and maintained by the SinoFin Financial Information, a financial data company, and China Center for Economic Research (CCER), Peking University. The firm-level stock returns are individual companies’ daily stock returns that are adjusted for distributions and splits. The market return is daily market return derived on the basis of the Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 index, which is a widely-used capitalization-weighted stock market index designed to replicate the performance of 300 stocks traded in the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges. By combining the firm-level donation data with the individual stock trading data, we obtain a balanced panel data set which covers 1230 firms and 600 continuous trading days for each firm (i.e., approximately 340 pre-event trading days as estimation window to derive the estimated beta coefficient for each firm, and six calendar months both before and after the quake as event window). The objective of our study is to assess the impact of corporate donations in the wake of the earthquake on the stock market value of firms. Ideally, we would like to compare a donor firm’s stock returns with the returns the firm would have experienced in the absence of donation. The event-study method provides a good approach to estimating this counterfactual return. Inspired by Lee and Mas (2012), we employ a relatively long panel (up to six months) of high frequency data on daily stock returns for each firm, and carry out DID analysis by comparing the evolution patterns of abnormal stock returns for the treatment group firms (i.e., donor firms) and the control group firms (i.e., non-donor firms). The first set of analysis focuses on the effects of donations on abnormal returns, particularly, the contrasting patterns between state owned firms and non-state-owned firms. This is the first stated objective of the study. It is found that there are significant positive market reactions to corporate donations made by non-state-controlled companies. In contrast, we find that state-controlled donor firms did not produce significantly stronger stock market performance than those state-controlled non-donor firms. We also conduct a series of robustness checks about the donation effect on abnormal returns to address various concerns about our estimation, and obtain consistent and robust results regarding the differential impacts of donation on abnormal returns. This basically allows us to achieve the objective #1 of this study. Next we examine the differences in market reactions to corporate donations made by non-state-controlled firms operating in regions which exhibit different degrees of government control over markets. Regions with a greater degree of government intervention in the economy and bureaucratic corruption are expected to have a higher level of bureaucratic discretion and generally have more discrimination against non-state-controlled firms in the first place. In China’s transition economy, government intervention in the regional economy typically relies considerably on SOEs to fulfill socioeconomic objectives; bureaucratic corruption may aggravate discrimination against privately-owned enterprises as discriminatory regulations force or induce private entrepreneurs to bribe bureaucrats in order to obtain permits for business operation, etc. Both contribute to the non-level playing field for privately-owned enterprises. At the same time, these are also the regions where government officials have more discretion in providing a level playing field for those non-state-controlled donor firms that cooperate with them. We find that the significant positive valuation effects only exist for those companies operating in regions with strong bureaucratic discretion represented by a high (above-mean) degree of government intervention or bureaucratic corruption where discrimination against non-SOEs is expected to be larger and the effect of corporate donations in redressing this discrimination could also be more salient. This allows us to accomplish the second stated objective of the study. To summarize, under state capitalism, corporate donations are likely to contribute to the realization of the political, economic and social objectives of governments. Consequently, for privately controlled companies, donations not only improve the corporate image to the public but also signal the loyalty of corporations to bureaucrats and the cooperativeness of corporations in the pursuit of government-favored causes. This may help corporations to win the trust of governments, which subsequently remedies the ownership-type-based discrimination in business operation. Hence, corporate donations could become a powerful instrument of government-business cooperation under state capitalism, and their effects on business operation and firm valuation are likely to stem from an underlying force different from that in free-market economies: retrieving a level playing field in business operation.

17524816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17524816.value: We employ the event study approach to investigate the impact of corporate donations on listed firm valuation in the wake of Wenchuan earthquake. It is found that there are significant positive market reactions to corporate donations made by non-state-controlled companies. In contrast, we find that state-controlled donor firms did not produce significantly stronger stock market performance than those state-controlled non-donor firms. We then further look at the market responses to non-state-controlled donor firms located in regions with different institutional quality, and find that the significant positive valuation effects only exist for those companies operating in regions with strong bureaucratic discretion represented by a high (above-mean) degree of government intervention or bureaucratic corruption where discrimination against non-SOEs is expected to be larger and the effect of corporate donations in redressing this discrimination could also be more salient. Furthermore, we analyze the changes in operating performance indicators of donor firms from the three years before to the three years after corporate donations, and compare them with the corresponding changes of non-donor firms. Donors displayed significant improvements in total sales, total costs, the ratio of sales to costs, the amount of loans obtained, the size of on-going projects, and the amounts of fixed assets and total assets. Moreover, listed firms in regions with a higher degree of bureaucratic discretion (proxied by government intervention and corruption) exhibited more significant improvements in those performance indicators, which suggests an expansion of business opportunities and government procurement contracts. These results are consistent with and substantiate the findings from market response analysis. We interpret these findings as suggesting that corporate donations can serve as one instrument of government-business cooperation to get back the level playing field for disadvantaged non-state firms under the authoritarian state capitalism model. Compared with SOEs that are favoured by governments, non-SOEs are typically disadvantaged in resource allocation (such as obtaining bank credit), etc., in an economy dominated by the government. Non-SOEs, however, can conduct philanthropic activities to support government-favoured causes and show their allegiance to the government. In turn, the government would regard them as trustworthy and provide a level playing field for them.

17524816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17524816.value: The rise of state capitalism is a striking development in the world economy, and China is one leading example. Under China’s authoritarian state capitalism, non-state-controlled corporations typically face discrimination in business operations, and have adopted the strategy of making donations to government-favored causes to facilitate government-business cooperation, which helps donor firms win governments’ trust and retrieve a level playing field. With an event study of corporate donations to Wenchuan earthquake relief campaign in 2008, we detect strong and positive market reactions to non-state-controlled donor firms, especially those operating in regions with high-level bureaucratic discretion, where the ownership-based discrimination is particularly severe and donations can be especially effective in redressing discriminatory treatments. Donor firms also display improvements in long-term performance indicators, which suggests an expansion of business opportunities and government procurement contracts. This strategy is fundamentally different from corporate political or campaign contributions in mature democracies or corruption (bribing bureaucrats).

17526016.label: Realisation of objectives
17526016.value: As the project is finished, we have achieved all the three objectives. Besides the current project, we also apply some part of data collected/constructed in this project to a new project. I elaborate as the following. 1) To provide a good measure of the anti-corruption campaign intensity for economists to do empirical studies in the field. To construct the measure, we combine the data that we extracted from newspaper digital archives of WiseNews with the Chinese newspaper directory data compiled by Qin et al. (2018). We tried several measures as proposed in the application, but finally stick to the method that uses the weekly ratio of newspaper articles discussing corruption as the intensity index for the anti-corruption campaign. In each newspaper, we find the articles including corruption key words in each week and take the weekly average of the ratio from all general newspapers in the archive. Furthermore, we defined two measures: the general anti-corruption index that is constructed by the articles mentioning corruption and the policy implementation index is by the ones discussing implementation or corruption charges/cases. We plot the two index and find that the spikes of the index are consistent with the big corruption cases were revealed or the new wave of anti-corruption activities initiated. (refer to the attached paper section 3.2). It confirms the propriety of the measures. We then apply the weekly measures to the regression analysis, we find the anti-corruption campaign, by itself, improves the average performance of all listed companies while at the same time dampens the performance of politically connected listed companies (Table 3). Besides this, in a newly started project, we apply this intensity measure of anti-corruption campaign on firms’ R&D investment, we also find salient positive impact. 2） Identify the value of political connection for Chinese firms & 3）Provide the lower bound estimation of the value of political connection in China and the impact of anti-corruption campaigns As the two objectives are integrated, I discuss them together. To construct the political connection measure, we collect the name list of the delegate of NPC/CPPCC and then match with the one of the top managers/board members of listed companies, which is defined as the explicit political connection. We explore the working experience of the top managers/board members of listed companies to find out those whose previous jobs in governments at or above prefecture levels and define it as the implicit political connection. To identify the value of political connection and the impact of the anti-corruption campaign, we interact the political connection with the intensity measure of anti-corruption campaign as the variable of interest in the differences-in-differences model. We find the statistically significant negative estimate for the coefficient, while its absolute value represents for the lower bound of the value of political connection, which is there if it hadn’t been the anti-corruption campaign. For the aggregate value of the political connection, we need to add the positive coefficient of the political connection, which is comparably smaller when we deduct the part that is curbed by the anti-corruption campaign. Because there have been many anti-corruption activities going on in decades, the weekly newspaper articles could also pick up the intensity of these scattering activities. To track down the anti-corruption campaign initiated by President Xi in November 2012, we apply one more specification in the analysis - the triple differences-in-differences methodology. The triple difference term is obtained by interacting the above interaction term with a “Post” dummy indicating for the time period after November 2012 campaign. The results lend support to the evidence that anti-corruption campaign does reduce the market value of politically connected listed companies. And, we find that the impact of anti-corruption is actually all driven by the anti-corruption campaign initiated in November 2012 as the simple interaction term between political connection and the intensity of anti-corruption campaign loses the statistically significant effect after the triple interaction term Is added. It suggests that the anti-corruption campaign is effective. (for details, please refer to the attached paper). The cumulative impact of the anti-corruption campaign on politically connected listed companies in two years can easily exceed 10% deduction on the market value, compared with listed companies without political connections. Furthermore, we examine the impact on different types of listed companies, which provides possible impact of anti-corruption campaign above the lower bound. We find that the impact is much larger for non government-owned companies (twice as large), companies located in the regions with higher corruption levels (triple as large), and companies with lower labor productivity. Beyond the lower bound estimation of the impact of anti-corruption campaign initiated in 2012, we prolong the study to examine whether the impact exists in long run. It is important for the field of study because very few studies find the long-term impact of the anti-corruption campaign. First, in the main analysis, we use long run CAR as the performance measure to estimate the two years impact. The findings are summarized above. Furthermore, we investigate whether the impact is a transient shock or permanent shock. If the anti-corruption campaign only affects the stock market performance, it is likely that the impact is transient and might die out soon after the campaign is done. However, if the campaign has changed economic activities of the companies and the market situation, the impact of the campaign is then a long-term effect. To evaluate such an impact, we investigate the change in some business cost and income items. For the operating concerns, we check the administrative expense, marketing expense and operating income; for the financing concerns, we check the financial expenses and interest payable; for the foreseeable future, we check the retained profits. Listed companies with one more implicit connection will have 2.6% higher administrative expense and 2.8% higher operating income, while such numbers decrease by 1.5% and 1.6%, respectively, after Xi's anti-corruption campaign. Listed companies with one more implicit connection incur a 1.7% increase in the marketing expense after Xi’s anti-corruption campaign starts. Listed companies with the explicit connection experienced a cut in financial expenses of 9.5%, implying a decrease in financial loans. Meanwhile, their interest payment slows down, as the interest payable is increased by 20%. The financing situation became harsher for those politically connected companies. The results suggest that the politically connected companies benefit from their connection before Xi's anti-corruption campaign, while they suffer a considerably negative impact afterwards:

17526016.label: Major findings and research outcome
17526016.value: 1. We finished the paper "The long-run impact of anti-corruption campaign on politically connected listed companies" and submitted (The submitted version is attached in part C). In this paper, by measuring the time-varying policy intensity by the proportion of relevant newspaper articles, we evaluate the impact of an anti-corruption campaign on listed companies initiated by Chinese President Xi Jinping in 2012. We find significant negative effects on the market value of politically connected companies, where the cumulative impact over two years can easily exceed 10%. The study is one of the very few papers that have found the comparatively long-run impact of anti-corruption campaign. We further investigate the heterogeneous effect and find the results are driven mainly by non government-owned companies and regions with higher corruption levels, and the impact is stronger for companies with lower labor productivity. We also find that the campaign has worsened the business operation and financing situation of politically connected listed companies. It provides an evidence that the impact is not transient but permanent. 2. We apply the measure of anti-corruption campaign and political connection on a newly started project which examines the anti-corruption campaign and the enterprises' R&D activities. We obtained very promising preliminary outcome.

17526016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17526016.value: We use the data collected in the project to a new paper: the anti-corruption campaign and R&D. As we have find that the anti-corruption campaign affected some accounting terms indicating for economic and financial activities, it is reasonable to believe that the market environment and the competition mode is changed. Therefore, firms might develop new strategies to catch up and thrive. R&D is of the most important activities that will affect the firms and then the whole industries' development in decades. So far the preliminary results suggests positive impact of anti-corruption campaign on firms' R&D activities. Next, we are going to investigate whether this effect is motivated by the subsidy that firms seek to substitute the resource brought by the political connection before the campaign or motivated by the transit of company development strategy. If it is former, we should expect to see more registered patents but no increase in the application of the patents. If it is the latter, we should observe more application and broader business. We will also examine the mechanisms that drive up such decision.

17526016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17526016.value: Whether corruption plays the role of “grabbing hands” or “helping hands” in decades growth of Chinese economy? This project studies the impact of anti-corruption campaign on politically connected listed companies and shed some lights on such question. Compared with the companies without political connection, we find the anti-corruption campaign significantly reduces the market value of politically connected companies and worsens off their business operation and financing situation, while political connection itself brings positive payoff for the company. It at least suggests that the anti-corruption campaign improves the fairness of market competition, which is an important and good index for market-oriented economy. The evidences about whether the political connection is good or bad for companies are mixing. Exploring the exogenous shock of anti-corruption campaign, we identify the positive effect of political connection on the companies. Furthermore, by the results of exogenous effect check, we also show that non government-owned and low productivity (bad) companies tend to use more of their political connections. Both types of companies are in a comparatively low position in the market and the results show that the political connection might help them in the non-market way, potentially to be illegal way.
