17651516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17651516.value: In recent years, the advent of massive open online courses (MOOCs) has fueled much attention among educators. However, despite the high interest they generate, we still understand little about student engagement in these large scale online courses (Anderson et al., 2014). Existing studies have mostly employed clickstream analysis (e.g., what pages students visit) to examine student activities in MOOCs or predict student dropout or completion. Although studies such as these are useful, they fall short of explaining the reasons why participants find the activities or course engaging. Unlike many previous studies, this proposal specifically seeks to uncover what factors related to MOOC pedagogy, or to the individual instructor may encourage or discourage student engagement. It aims to contribute to the theorization of engagement in large scale online courses using the framework of self-determination theory of motivation. This study also aims to generate a set of practical implications that can help inform future course designs. A total of 6 MOOCs (3 highly-rated courses and 3 not so highly-rated ones) will be examined. Data sources include scores on student course assignments, student online survey, and telephone interviews. Specifically, we aim to achieve a sample of 2,400 survey respondents (400 students x 6 MOOCs). The survey will measure the students’ engagement (behavioral, affective, cognitive), motivation (sense of autonomy, relatedness, competence), and perceived learning. After the survey, 120 purposively sampled students (20 students x 6 MOOCs) will be invited to attend semi-structured interviews. They will be chosen so as to be representative of the degree of engagement as revealed by their earlier questionnaire responses. Descriptive statistics will be used to explore the extent of students’ engagement and motivation in each course. Multiple regression analyses will be conducted to investigate which components of engagement (behavioral, affective, cognitive) may make significant contributions to students’ perceived learning and achievement. Student interview data will be transcribed and analyzed to help us explicate the specific factors or strategies that could engage or disengage students. Overall, this study will contribute to a better theoretical understanding of how measures of engagement are related to the components of self-determination theory of motivation. This study will also generate a set of practical strategies for engaging students. An understanding of these strategies can yield guidelines to instructors of future MOOCs, as well as those interested in engaging their students in conventional online, blended, or even face-to-face settings (Educause, 2013). 近年來，大規模在線開放課程（MOOCs）的出現引起了教育者們的廣泛關註。盡管我們對MOOCs有著很高的關註度，但是我們對於學生在這些大規模開放型課程中的學習投入度（engagement）了解仍然很少（Anderson et al., 2014）。現有的研究主要采用的點擊流分析式（如，哪些頁面被學生訪問過）， 並以此來分析學生在MOOCs上的參與的活動或者預測學生的流失率或完成率。盡管這些研究有壹定的意義，但是他們並沒能解釋哪些原因可以讓學生對所提供的活動或課程感興趣，並且專註投入到這些活動或課程中來。與許多已有的研究不同， 本研究主要探究，在MOOC的課程設計 或者授課者方面，哪些因素會對學生的學習投入度（engagement）產生積極或者消極的影響。本研究旨在運用自我決定理論（self-determination theory）這壹理論框架推進在大規模在線課程的學習投入度方面的理論研究發展。另外，本研究希望能夠歸納出實用的策略來幫助指導將來的課程設計。總共6門MOOCs （3門排名較高的課程 和 3門排名普通的課程）將作為本研究的研究對象。研究數據將包含學生課程得分，學生在線問卷，電話訪談等。具體而言，我們希望能收到2400個問卷反饋(400問卷參與者X 6 MOOCs). 問卷將測量學生的學習投入度（行為、情感、認知），動機值（自主、關系、能力），及學習感知。在問卷之後，120位學生將被選取邀請參加半結構式訪談（20 學生X 6 MOOCs）。這些學生將代表不同層度的學習投入度者，他們的問卷反饋會作為選取半結構式訪談的參考依據。描述性統計將被用於分析學生在每門課的學習投入度程度和學習動機值。多線性回歸統計將用於分析何種學習投入度要素（行為、情感、認知）會影響學生的學習感知與學習成效。學生的訪談數據將被轉錄並加以分析，以幫助闡釋哪些具體因素或策略會促進或降低學生學習投入度。綜上所述，本研究將在理論上深化運用自我決定理論的相關要素測量學習投入度的探究。本研究將同時提出壹系列提升學生學習投入度的實用策略與建議。 了解這些實用策略可以幫助MOOCs設計者們建立有效的課程設計原則，也可以幫助到在傳統在線課堂、混合式課堂、或者面對面課堂裏想要提升學生學習投入度的授課者們（Educause, 2013）。

17651516.label: Realisation of objectives
17651516.value: All three objectives have been successfully achieved. Specifically, the following items were realised: (1) Development and validation of a MOOC Engagement Motivation (MEM) Scale based on the self-determination theory of motivations (i.e. perceived autonomy, sense of relatedness, and perceived competence), and the theory of engagement (i.e. behavioural engagement, emotional engagement, and cognitive engagement). More specifically, the MEM scale was adapted from the existing validated instruments: (a) Motivation scale: perceived autonomy (Standage, Duda, & Ntoumanis, 2005), sense of relatedness (Furrer & Skinner, 2003), and perceived competency (McAuley, Duncan, & Tammen, 1989); (b) Engagement scale: behavioural engagement and emotional engagement (Skinner et al., 2008), and cognitive engagement (Rotgans & Schmidt, 2011). All of these scales used 5-point Likert rating (1 = “Strongly disagree”, 2 = “Disagree”, 3 = “Undecided”, 4 = “Agree”, 5 = “Strongly agree”) in this study. (2) The overall structure of motivational components and engagement components in the MOOC context were tested via confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Four indices assessed the model fit: (a) NC (Normed Chi-square), (b) RMSEA (root mean square error of approximation), (c) CFI (comparative fit index), and (d) AIC (Akaike information criterion). NC is often considered instead of Chi-square because Chi-square is highly dependent on sample size (R. B. Kline & Santor, 1999). In addition, internal reliability in different models was assessed with Cronbach’s alpha coefficient. The overall results of CFA and internal reliability tests suggested that the measurement model of the motivation scale and engagement scale were both validated and reliable in the MOOC context. (3) Through the use of statistical tests (e.g., Mann-Whitney U Test, correlational analyses, multiple regression), the research team has successfully examined the various relationships between the 3 components of self-determination theory and the 3 components of engagement. • All the psychological needs were significantly related to all the components of engagement above the moderate level. • These relationship coefficients were stronger for those completers when they were compared to those non-completers in terms of the relationship between psychological needs and engagement. • The research team has also investigated the predictive power of SDT components on the components of engagement. These engagements components also showed a positive impact on the perceived learning of MOOC participants. Furthermore, these engagement components also had a slightly predictive power on the course completion. (4) Through content analyses of more than 4,400 participants’ reflection data, six key factors that can engage MOOC students were found. Nine main reasons for MOOC student disaffection were also found. A follow-up study that examined more than 5,800 participants’ reflections were also conducted to test the earlier findings on factors that participants perceived as engaging in MOOCs. (5) Five main implications that could provide practical guidelines to other instructors of large online courses. The findings can offer useful tips for instructors of traditional e-learning courses. For example, from our interview data, we found several strategies reported by the participants through which the MOOC instructors attempted to make themselves more available, including providing weekly feedback (instead of daily) to common problems raised by learners and setting aside regular online hours per week to interact synchronously with learners. Instructors may also offer a fee-paying consultation scheme for students who wish to receive personalized feedback.

17651516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17651516.value: (1) Overall, the MOOC completers watched more videos, posted more forum messages, and did more peer interactive activities than the non-completers. The components of SDT (autonomy, relatedness, competence) and the components of engagement (behavioural, emotional, cognitive) were all significantly correlated with one another. Compared to the completers, the association between perceived competence and emotional engagement was much lower for the non-completers. MOOC completers reported significantly higher perceived sense of competence and cognitive engagement levels than the non-completers, but they reported significantly lower on the sense of relatedness than the non-completers. [Paper under review by Educational Sciences: Theory & Practice (ESTP)] (2) According to the results of multiple regression analysis, the SDT model accounted for a large variance of each type of engagement (44.3% for BE, 54.7% for EE, and 48.4% for CE). The component of perceived competence had the largest positive impact on engagement, while the component of the sense of relatedness had a slight negative impact on engagement. Furthermore, the components of engagement accounted for a large variance of perceived learning (78%). The component of emotional engagement had the largest positive impact on the perceived learning. However, the components of engagement only accounted for a very small variance of course completion (2.2% ~ 3.3%). [Paper under review by ESTP] (3) Six key factors that can engage online students and nine reasons for student disaffection were found. The engaging factors include: (a) problem-centric learning supported by clear explanations, (b) instructor availability, (c) instructor attributes (e.g., passion, humor), (d) peer interaction, (e) active learning with timely feedback, and (f) course resources to address participant learning needs or preferences. The two most commonly reported student disaffections were due to forum- and peer-related issues [paper published in Teachers College Record] (4) Some of the major implications include the following: [papers published in Teachers College Record and International Review of Research in Open and Distance Learning] (a) Students preferred a problem-centric style of teaching that focused on meaning-making with relevant examples of how the principles or concepts taught can be applied in the real world. (b) Students desire moderately challenging courses assignments, instead of assignments that merely test factual recall. (c) Students desire short lecture videos of not more than 10 minutes. Lecture videos that featured different settings or instructor faces were perceived to be more engaging. (d) Interrupting the videos with questions (in-video quiz) or segmenting the whole chunk of lecture into a series of smaller video sequences of about 6-10 minutes each with quiz at the end of each small video segment helped sustain students’ attention to lecture content.

17651516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17651516.value: The project team has collected a very rich dataset which enables an ongoing exploration. Thus, the following development will be carried out. We plan to investigate the possible relationship and interactions between MOOC participants’ self-regulated learning (SRL) and learner engagement. SRL can be defined as “self-generated thoughts, feelings, and actions that are planned and cyclically adapted to the attainment of personal goals”. We will examine the MOOC participants’ self-regulated learning (SRL) processes involved in the three components of engagement (behavioural, emotional, and cognitive). This investigation will provide an in-depth picture on how the participants engage in their SRL processes and implicate what the course instructors and designers could do to better facilitate the individual learning in a MOOC.

17651516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17651516.value: The main purpose of this project is to understand what factors related to MOOC pedagogy, or the instructor may encourage or discourage student engagement. The research team has conducted survey questionnaire, interviews, and content analyses of MOOC participants' reflection data. Overall, six key factors that can engage online students and nine reasons for student disaffection were found. The engaging factors include: (a) problem-centric learning supported by clear explanations, (b) instructor availability, (c) instructor attributes (e.g., passion, humor), (d) peer interaction, (e) active learning with timely feedback, and (f) course resources to address participant learning needs or preferences. The two most commonly reported student disaffections were related to online forum- and peer-related issues. Collectively, the findings of this project provide practical guidelines to other instructors of large online courses. In addition, we found that the MOOC completers watched more videos, posted more forum messages, and did more peer interactive activities than the non-completers. Completers were more motivated to earn the course certificate, join the social community, and prepare for advanced placement exams. The relationship between perceived competence and emotional engagement was much lower for the non-completers. MOOC completers reported higher perceived sense of competence and cognitive engagement levels than the non-completers.

17655316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17655316.value: As signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES), Hong Kong has long had an obligation to implement and enforce legislation which effectively prevents illegal trade in endangered wild animals into and through the Territory. With the extension of mainland China’s membership of the United Nation’s Convention on Biological Diversity to Hong Kong, in 2011, the government is now further obligated to provide effective controls to protect international biodiversity by regulating the movement of endangered species through Hong Kong, whether the species is listed in CITES or not. The majority of trade in endangered species in Hong Kong is unregulated. The only law targeting the protection of endangered species is the Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance, Cap 586 which regulates the import, export and possession of CITES listed species; a small percentage of the wildlife trade. Endangered animals not subject to CITES restrictions can be traded freely in the Territory. Such animals may be vulnerable in their country of origin and sourced illegally or unsustainably but are not protected under Cap 586. Due to this omission, Hong Kong acts as a gateway to China and other Asian countries where such animals are sought for food, medicine and sometimes exotic pets. This project will study whether Hong Kong’s legislation intended to protect endangered species from illegal trade is effective. In particular, it will consider whether Cap 586 is effective to control the trade in CITES listed species and examine the legal loophole which currently allows Hong Kong to act as a major trade route for endangered and vulnerable species not prohibited for trade under CITES. The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department and the Customs and Excise Department are charged with enforcement of the legislation to control trade in wildlife. The project will consider the powers provided to those enforcement agencies and evaluate whether they are fit for purpose, through interviews with various stakeholders involved with the trade. The project will study the legislation in place in overseas jurisdictions that have been effective in controlling trade in endangered species and, where appropriate, make recommendations for similar legislative reform in Hong Kong. The project will consider whether effective sanctions on the illegal trade in wild animals are being provided by Hong Kong’s courts. The project will review recent sentencing decisions taken by local judiciary and make comparisons with international sentencing practices for similar wildlife crimes.

17655316.label: Realisation of objectives
17655316.value: The objectives of the project were fully achieved. A full review of the Hong Kong government's obligations under the CBD and the effectiveness of Cap 586 and Cap 60 was undertaken. The adequacy of licensing conditions and sentences were reviewed and a comparative study of sentencing in comparable jurisdictions made. The practicality of applying the USA Lacey Act (and similar European legislation) to Hong Kong was fully considered. We found that between 2013 and 2017, Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department (CED) had made over 2,000 seizures of illegal wildlife, valued at over $560 million. However, legislative control of the trade was lenient. At the commencement of our project, trafficking in endangered species was able to be punished with a maximum sentence of two years’ imprisonment. In many cases, traders of high value, critically threatened species got off with low fines or very short terms to imprisonment The initial findings of the research on penalties was conveyed by the PI to the Legislative Council (LegCo) Panel on Environmental Affairs on 6 June 2017 and assisted the Environmental Bureau in securing amendments to Cap 586, in May 2018, which raised the maximum penalties for smuggling and possession of endangered wildlife to an indictable offence of 10 years' imprisonment and banned continued trade in ivory from 2020. The Agricultural Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) are charged with providing permits for legal trade in endangered species and with ensuring trade is compliant with local licensing requirements. Where permits are found to be irregular (e.g. the wrong species is listed), the Department can refuse to issue import or possession permits and may seize animals possessed in contraband of CITES restrictions. Our research found that, as has been the case with ivory, permitting licensed trade in shark and live reef fish has allowed legitimate permits to be widely used to launder illegally obtained specimens, amongst legally sourced animals. We found that the problem was compounded by legislative changes in 2006. At that time, in an effort to remove what was regarded by government to be excessive control of the trade, Cap 187 was replaced with Cap 586. Cap 586 now permits AFCD to issue import permits based on individual consignments, or keeping premises, regardless of the number of species involved. Companies trading in controlled species may seek possession licenses for multiple species, which are valid for 5 years. Without requirements for individual tagging of animals which identifies their origin, this licensing practice has provided opportunities for unscrupulous traders to launder illegally sourced animals. Low inspection rates for sea vessels, lax controls on locally registered fishing boats, readily provided permits for import and export of CITES listed species, and Hong Kong’s generally open attitude to commerce have all assisted in making the Territory an epicenter for trade in endangered species. We found that Hong Kong has made no legislative changes to comply with the extension of the UN Convention on Biological Diversity to Hong Kong in 2011. This is despite the fact that Article 3 of the CBD places a duty on Hong Kong to ensure that local trade in wildlife does not negatively impact on vulnerable species in other jurisdictions. We recommended that a list of positive species for import and a review of local fauna and flora, along with a marking system for import, breeding and sale of endangered species be introduced. In determining the powers of CED, under Cap 60, to deter wildlife smuggling we found a significant problem with the Department's use of the Ordinance to pursue wildlife crimes. Although the offences of importing or exporting unmanifested cargo (section 18, Cap 60) and assisting in carriage of prohibited articles and money laundering are specified offences under Cap 455 of the Organised and Serious Crimes Ordinance, Cap 455, no use of OSCO provisions by CED has ever been made in connection with wildlife crime and very few cases involving wildlife crimes have been pursued as smuggling under Cap 60. This has resulted in most cases involving wildlife smuggling being prosecuted by AFCD, under Cap 586. However as Cap 586 offences are not included in Schedule 1 to OSCO as ‘specified crimes’ neither CED nor AFCD can utilise the special and necessary investigative powers under section 4 of OSCO to gain access to materials related to the proceeds of wildlife crime. Where a person has been convicted of a wildlife crime, the Courts are not empowered to use section 8 of OSCO to confiscate the proceeds of that crime, nor can judges use OSCO to issue restraint or charging orders over property representing the benefits of wildlife crime. Where a person has been convicted of a wildlife crime which the prosecution allege to have been organized, the Courts are not permitted to pass enhanced sentences under Cap 586. We have recommended that these problems are rectified with an amendment to Cap 455's Schedule of specified offences. We also reviewed the controls used in the USA (Lacey Act) and the EU (Council Regulation (EC) No 338/97). Under the Lacey Act, importers to the USA must show they took precautions to ensure the import was legally sourced: they must submit an import declaration stating the country of origin, the supplier, species, volume and value. The EU utilise a similar system with the EU Timber Regulations. We surveyed current import controls in Hong Kong and found that for Appendix 1 species, limited details of supplier are required and only where an Appendix II specimen is live and wild caught, is an import permit required. By way of comparison in the USA, all specimens must be shown to be legally sourced to allow for import permits. The same is required under EU Basic Regulation Annex A and B species (effectively requiring import permits for CITES App I, II , some III and non-CITES species to the EU). We recommended Hong Kong reform its licensing requirements and require import permits for all Appendix 1 and II species and proof of legal take, before entry.

17655316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17655316.value: Our evaluation of Hong Kong's obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and Cap 586 found that the current licensing conditions are lax and permit trade of endangered species in contravention of the spirit of the CBD and the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES). Our evaluation of international legislation in Europe, the USA and Australia found that Hong Kong sentencing practices were well below international standards and our maximum penalties required significant reform. During the course of our study, government acted on our early findings and passed amendments raising the penalties for illegal wildlife smuggling and possession to 10 year's imprisonment and permitting wildlife crimes to be prosecuted as indictable offences. Finding that the District Court judiciary would need assistance with the application of new penalties, the PI prepared 50 victim impact statements for Hong Kong's most smuggled species and was invited to conduct the Hong Kong Judicial Institute's first online training series to train judges to more effectively sentence wildlife crime. The PI was also invited to train prosecutors in the Dept of Justice, CED and AFCD in more effective prosecutions and investigations of wildlife crime. The PI's victim impact statements have been used by judges and prosecutors in 25 cases since the amendment to Cap 586 in 2018 and have resulted in significantly improved sentences for wildlife smugglers in Hong Kong. Her victim impact statement for rhinoceros, used by prosecutors to advise the District Court in HKSAR v Wei Bin, in October 2018, resulted in the highest sentence ever passed in Hong Kong for the smuggling of rhino horn. Two articles detailing the project's findings (one published and one in press) were accepted in international journals and two Knowledge Exchange reports prepared: one published with collaborators in December 2018: 'Trading in Extinction' and a supplementary report reflecting new practices since the 2018 amendments to Cap 586 to be published in February 2020. These reports have not only resulted in an ongoing dialogue with the HK administration and legislators about the need for further reforms but have generated public interest in and attention to wildlife crime. The PI has been invited to participate in radio and press interviews about the research and was invited to prepare an article on the project's findings for 'The Hong Kong Lawyer', by the Law Society of Hong Kong, published in June 2019.

17655316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17655316.value: Our further report focusing on the need for amendments to The Organised and Serious Crimes Ordinance, (Cap 455) will be released to the government and the public in February 2020. This second report will supplement our findings in the 2018 Report 'Trading in Extinction" and the two journal articles. The 2020 report will be used to support our recommendation to make legislative amendments to Cap 455, to define wildlife crime as an 'organised and serious' criminal offence in Hong Kong. With the assistance of staff from the Kadoorie Farm and Botanical Garden and KE funding from HKU and outside donors we are continuing to add to and update the Victim Impact Statements we prepare for Hong Kong's most smuggled endangered species. The PI has been invited to provide further training to the judiciary in 2020.

17655316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17655316.value: Every year millions of live animals, plants and their derivatives are illegally trafficked into and through Hong Kong, by transnational companies and organised crime syndicates. There is an urgent need for the Hong Kong government to enhance its current enforcement strategy against wildlife smuggling. Over the last decade, the diversity of endangered species imported into Hong Kong has increased by 57%. At the same time, the estimated value of the trade has increased by 1,600%. Since 2013, seizures of illegal ivory, pangolin scales and rhino horn have been made by Hong Kong authorities, potentially equating to the deaths of 3,000 elephants, 96,000 pangolins and 51 rhinoceros. Our research addresses the legal shortcomings which have permitted Hong Kong to become a wildlife trade hub. We analysed the legislative gaps and have made recommendations to government to improve law and policies which impact of wildlife smuggling. Our initial findings supported the 2018 amendment to Cap 586, significantly raising the penalties for wildlife smuggling and possession and closing the ivory trade. Our further recommendations include an amendment to the Organised and Serious Crimes Ordinance which would allow wildlife crimes to be prosecuted as the organised and serious crimes they are.

17655816.label: Project Objectives
17655816.value: Develop a systematic and comprehensive account of the ethic of a “fair fight” in warfare by meeting the following objectives: Describe and analyze in detail, drawing on warrior codes, descriptions of military practice, and legal and philosophical scholarship, the ethic of a “fair fight” in warfare and its different justifications. Demonstrate the scope, limits, and implications of the ethic of a “fair fight” in warfare and of each of its justifications. Describe and analyze the tensions between the ethic of a “fair fight” in warfare and the Augustinian and Thomist-based principles that dominate contemporary just war theory, practice, and international law. Apply these findings to special issues in contemporary warfare, such as persistent military asymmetries, remotely piloted aircraft (i.e., drone) strikes, cyberwarfare, and terrorism. Draw some general conclusions about just war theory as body of ethics and international military law and recommend some possible amendments to international law, in light of these contradictions. Complete the book manuscript by Dec 2017.

17655816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17655816.value: 這個探索參考了我之前對於正義戰爭和交戰雙方合作倫理的研究。它全面地分析合作倫理在「公平對戰」中的角色，以及這個角色與其他正義戰爭原則和軍事倫理的關系。西方正義戰爭理論對於現今國際法有非常重大的影響，可是那些理論本身卻是來自一系列不同甚至互相矛盾的道德原則，例如奧古斯都和阿奎那的學說、「戰士法典」的道義規範、功利主義等等。 正義戰爭理論其中一個價值觀是「公平對戰」的重要。儘管歷史上戰爭充斥著爾虞我詐、不擇手段、蓄意破壞和純粹暴力，但是當中卻有例外，其中包括不同文化中對於參戰士兵行為的規範以及國際法對於戰爭的約束。而一個反複出現的例外是一種對於交戰雙方能夠在接近程度的武裝、警覺和準備下「公平對戰」的追求。雖然戰場上真正的平等是不可能甚至是不需要，但歷史上總不乏希望能夠減少敵對雙方實力差距的嘗試。例如發動戰爭的一方會被期望出兵前向敵對一方發表明確的宣戰聲明。而在第一次世界大戰中，狙擊手會拒絕射擊一些因燃點香煙而暴露位置以及在戰埸上掉著褲子奔跑的敵人，因為他們認為殺害那些敵人是「謀殺」而非「戰爭」。另一個例子是在第二次印巴戰爭（1965）期間，交戰雙方空軍曾以「沒有體育精神」（unsporting）為由臨時協議不轟炸在卡奇鹽沼地（Rann of Kutch）的軍隊。而在1863年，有重要影響力的《利伯守則》（Lieber Code）就已經禁止若干欺敵（「休戰旗是如此神聖…對它的濫用是極其令人髮指的罪行」，§114）和伏擊（「不可對哨崗、哨兵和巡邏兵開火」，§69）的行為。有關「公平」對戰的規定能夠在不同文化對於參戰人員的行為規範中找到其根源。不論是日本《武士道》中有關不與明顯弱於自己的對手決鬥的教誨，或者是印度《法論》（Dharmaśāstra）中涉及不加害已經解除武裝敵人的條文，又或者是《亞瑟王之死》（Le Morte d’Arthur）中關於騎馬者不攻擊已墮馬者的記載，我們可以看到不同文化對於公平對戰都有著共同的關心。 當然，絕大多數的戰爭都並非公平地進行，但「公平對戰」仍然是戰爭倫理中一個重要的概念。我將會首先詳細描述和分析戰爭中「公平對戰」的特徵和支持它的理由。然後，我會把它們應用到一些當代戰爭的獨特問題，例如持續的軍事不對稱、利用搖控飛機（無人機）進行空襲、網絡戰爭、以及恐怖主義。在討論當代戰爭中對「公平戰鬥」追求的體現及其倫理問題的過程當中，我將論證「公平戰爭」與其他重要的正義戰爭原則之間的張力，而那些原則包括戰爭的政治模型（例如克勞塞維玆的理論）、正當理由原則和修正理論（revisionist theory）中有關交戰雙方的道德不平等。這個張力會使得戰爭參與者在應用國際法制定軍事戰術和實踐正義的時候，追尋著分歧和矛盾的目標。結合我的其他研究，我所得出的結論是正義戰爭的理論和實踐都需要透過不同方法使其內部更加一致。不過，更大的一致性卻可能導致其他問題，例如延長衝突和做成更多傷亡。這個研究的結論與正義戰爭理論和軍事倫理的論述有密切的關系。另外，它也涉及其他更加廣泛的題目，包括公平、互惠、權利、軍民關系和政治行動。

rows: Identify the neural bases of multi-tasking training for promoting automaticity of technical skills in surgery
Examine whether multi-task training facilitates learning of more complex technical skills in surgery

17656116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17656116.value: Like expertise in any education domain, surgical expertise is highly valued. Acknowledgement of the many challenges junior surgeons face (e.g., multi-tasking environment in the operative theatre, intraoperative stressors, and time constraints imposed on training) have moved leaders in surgical education to develop and validate training interventions that help junior surgeons to attain identified markers of expertise (e.g., automaticity and resilience of technical skills) in a more efficient manner. Multi-task training, which requires trainees to simultaneously conduct an attention demanding cognitive task whilst practicing their technical skills, is a training program that may carry such qualities and warrants examinations. Our preliminary proof of concept study has shown that multi-task training is a viable means for a simple laparoscopic skill training and offers added value by providing resilience in the face of a secondary task load, indicative of skill automaticity. However, it remains unclear how multi-task training exerts specific effects on functional brain architecture to promote automaticity of technical skills and whether it facilitates the learning of more complex laparoscopic tasks. To characterize neural correlates of multi-task training, Study 1 will recruit two groups of participants without prior experience to practice a simple laparoscopic skill on a validated training simulator in multi-task or single-task training way until they reach the suggested proficiency. Participants’ performance will be tested 1 week later, during which cerebral hemodynamics will be measured by functional near infra-red spectroscopy (fNIRS). Based on neuroimaging literature, it is predicted that the pattern of brain activations will be dissociable between multi-task and single-task trainees. Study 2 will invite all participants back to continue their training on a more complex laparoscopic skill until they reach suggested proficiency. Again, participants’ performance will be tested 1 week later, during which additional low-level cognitive distraction and high-level cognitive processing conditions will be introduced. Based on our preliminary findings, it is predicted that the skill performance of single-task trainees will be disrupted by both low-level distractions and high-level processing, whereas, the skill performance of multi-task trainees will be resilient to both, indicative of greater technical skill automaticity. This proposal has both theoretical and practical significance. First, it will advance the knowledge in how the human brain adapts, functionally, to different forms of skill learning strategies in general. Second, surgical educators may have better understanding of different forms of training interventions from a neuroergonomics perspective in order to promote the automaticity and resilience of technical skills.

17656116.label: Realisation of objectives
17656116.value: In this project, we established an experiment platform with Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery (FLS) simulation trainer, fNIRS neuroimaging, multi-channel electroencephalography (EEG) and brain computer interface (BCI) based neural feedback(NF). 1) The FLS peg transfer task training module, developed by the Society of American Gastrointestinal and Endoscopic Surgeons, was used as the to-be-learnt task in the first study. In this task, participants were asked to handle laparoscopic graspers to pick up, transfer, and place six plastic triangular objects, one by one, from one side of the pegboard to the another side. The first half of the task required transfer from the laparoscopic grasper held by the non-dominant hand to the dominant hand, while the second half of the task required the reverse procedure. Task completion time was the measure of performance. Volunteers were recruited from medical students to join this study. They were randomly assigned to two groups in single-task training or a multi-task training strategy. Two groups of participants were asked to practice a simple laparoscopic skill on a validated training simulator until they reached a target proficiency on the first day. The multi-task group performed multi-task training, while the single-task group performed single-task training. On the second day, both the multi-task and the single-task participants completed a retention test and a secondary task loading test, during which cerebral hemodynamics were measured by fNIRS. We previously reported that multi-task training helps to develop technical skill automaticity, and that participants in a multi-task group were less disrupted by a secondary task loading than those in a single-task group. As automaticity of technical skills is a defining characteristic of expertise, the technical skill automaticity developed with multi-task training proved that multi-task training is an effective method to train novices into experts. Neuroimaging literature shows that because there is no technical skill automaticity in novices compared with experts, novices will recruit more PFC when performing multiple tasks.This study confirms that multi-task training is a viable means to promote automaticity of a simple laparoscopic skill, as indicated by more robust hand movement efficiency, compared with single-task training. The findings in behavior test also prove that the multi-task training facilitates learning of more complex technical skills. 2) In the second study, we investigated the high-level alpha oscillation EEG in correlation of learning performance during laparoscopic skills training. Neurofeedback (NF) has been reported effective in enhancing alpha oscillation. A further study is to verify the usefulness of Neurofeedback (NF) in improving the learning efficacy. This prospective study was performed in a group of medical students without laparoscopic experience. All subjects completed the FSL training with peg transfer task. EEG was recorded using a 64 channels system during the training and testing blocks. Training performance was assessed based on the task completion time. All subjects participated in the first experiment comprising eight training blocks and one testing block. Subjects were ranked based on performance, classified good performance and fair performance groups. In the second experiment, the fair performance group were randomly divided into the NF and control groups. The steady-state visual evoked potential(SSVEP)-based brain computer interface (BCI) was used as a NF tool. Spectral analysis of EEG signals was used to calculate alpha power and alpha band coherence. Training performance and EEG alpha powers were compared between the NF and control groups. The features of alpha EEG oscillations were compared in students with different performance abilities during laparoscopic skills simulator training. Students with good performance in laparoscopic skills training had higher alpha EEG power than students with fair performance. The group with good training results had strong alpha EEG coherence in the temporal and occipital lobes. Subsequently, NF training of the students with fair performance resulted in increased alpha power and strength of alpha coherence, in association with good training results in comparison to controls. This suggests that students with higher alpha power were more efficient to learn laparoscopic skills during training than students with lower alpha power. Most importantly, the present study demonstrated the potential of alpha EEG NF to enhance the efficacy of laparoscopic skills simulator training.

17656116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17656116.value: 1) Multi-task training was demonstrated as an efficient training to improve automaticity of motor skills. Functional neuroimaging measured by functional near infra-red spectroscopy and behavioral data have been applied to investigate the neural bases of multi-tasking training for promoting automaticity and facilitating learning of technical skills in surgery. The performance of the multi-task training group showed more robust than that for single-task training. Hemodynamic responses in the prefrontal cortex regions showed significant lower oxyhemoglobin concentration in the multi-task tan single-task training strategies. Results of this study proved that multi-task training provided robust performance under the cognitive-demanding secondary task and higher neural efficiency of the learnt skills. 2) The performance in laparoscopic skills training was associated with alpha oscillation in the posterior electrode clusters. Subjects with good performance in laparoscopic skills training had high alpha power and strong alpha coherence. NF may effectively enhance the alpha oscillation and improve the learning efficacy of laparoscopic skills.

17656116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17656116.value: This study explored the neural bases of multi-tasking training for promoting automaticity of technical skills in surgery. It is a scientific evidence to support our design of multi-tasking training for medical students and junior surgeons. In addition, the finding of this project can be used for other motor learning courses. We also proved the usefulness of Brain computer interface as a neural feedback tool to enhance skill training. The output of this project motivate our further studies on developing efficient and user friendly BCI technology for education.

17656116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17656116.value: Technical skills training for surgeons, especially for laparoscopic surgeon, is an exceedingly difficult and time-consuming education. Surgeons in operation room are usually face to multi-tasking environment. Established training endpoints for surgical skills training tasks can be reached with relatively little deliberate practice, but these short bouts of intensive training are not sufficient to protect trainees’ skill performance against increased task demands. Surgical educators need also to ensure that training curricula effectively operate within work reform policies that impinge upon surgeon’s training time. Multi-task training, which requires trainees to simultaneously conduct an attention demanding cognitive task whilst practicing their technical skills, is a training program that may carry such qualities and warrants examinations. This study explores the effect of multi-task training on the functional brain architecture, as well as the features of brain activity associated with robust performance of learning. The understanding of neural bases of the multi-task training would help educators have better understanding of different forms of training interventions from a neuroergonomics perspective to promote the automaticity and resilience of technical skills. The findings of this study can be also used for other complex skill training like astronauts, pilots, or professional athletes.

rows: This study aims to compare the effectiveness of (1) AT-NMT, (2) NMT alone, (3) AT alone, and (4) control (care as usual) for improving reactive balance performance among children with DCD.

17658516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17658516.value: An increasing number of children are being diagnosed with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) and the need for improved rehabilitation services is critical. Children with DCD have marked motor function impairments and poor balance performance, as demonstrated in our previous studies. Inferior reactive balance control in these children is a major concern because it predisposes them to unexpected falls and injuries, affects their motor skills development and self-esteem. Rehabilitation of children with DCD primarily involves physical training that counteracts neuromuscular (nerve-muscle) deficits and enhances reactive balance performance. Recently, we discovered that attention deficit, found in about 50% of children with DCD, can also harm their balance reactions but this is not usually factored into the treatments. A holistic approach that treats both the attention and neuromuscular impairment is needed to improve these children’s reactive balance performance and thus overall development. Electroencephalographic (EEG) biofeedback training can improve attention in children through established neurological mechanisms. In this study, we will pioneer the treatment of both attention and neuromuscular deficits in children with DCD. We will incorporate EEG biofeedback attention training into conventional perturbation-enhanced neuromuscular training (NMT). Based on the results of our pilot trials, we hypothesize that the reactive balance performance in children with DCD can be best improved by treating both their attention and neuromuscular deficits. This hypothesis will be supported by the prediction that EEG biofeedback attention-neuromuscular training (AT-NMT) is superior to either just NMT or EEG biofeedback attention training (AT) in improving these children’s reactive balance performance. Objective: To compare the effectiveness of AT-NMT, NMT, AT, and control (usual medical care) for improving reactive balance performance among children with DCD. Design: A single-blinded, randomized controlled trial. Sample: 172 children with DCD. Interventions: AT-NMT, NMT, AT, or care as usual for 12 weeks. Major outcomes: Outcomes will be evaluated at baseline, post-intervention, and 3-month follow-up. A motor control test (MCT) will give a composite latency score, EEG recordings during MCT will measure the attention level, and surface electromyography recordings during MCT will indicate the lower limb muscle onset latency. Anticipated results and significance: Children with DCD who receive AT-NMT will have the best reactive balance performance outcomes. Assuming the results are positive, this novel training regime can be readily adopted into regular clinical practice. AT-NMT will improve overall well-being in these children and have positive socio-economic implications such as shorter rehabilitation periods and reduced healthcare costs in the long run. 越來越多的兒童被診斷患有發展性協調障礙（DCD），因此，改進康復服務是至關重要的。我們以往的研究證實，DCD兒童有顯著的運動功能障礙和平衡能力較弱。較差的平衡反應是最令人關注的，因為這容易導致DCD兒童意外跌倒和受傷，影響他們的運動技能發展和自尊。 DCD兒童康復治療主要包括身體機能訓練來彌補神經肌肉的缺陷及提高平衡反應能力。最近，我們發現專注力不足（約佔50%DCD兒童）也會防礙平衡反應，但現時專注力訓練通常不包括在治療計劃內。所以，我們需要設計一個全面的訓練計劃 (包括治療神經肌肉缺陷及專注力不足) 來改善這些孩子的平衡反應及整體發展。 通過特定的神經機制，腦電圖（EEG）生物反饋訓練可以改善患兒的專注力。在這項研究中，我們將開拓一個新的治療方案，就是結合腦電生物反饋訓練及傳統的神經肌肉訓練（NMT），來改善DCD兒童專注力不足和神經肌肉缺陷的問題。根據我們的初步測試結果，我們預計，結合腦電生物反饋訓練及神經肌肉訓練最能有效改善DCD兒童的反應性平衡能力。如果研究結果顯示腦電生物反饋-神經肌肉訓練（AT-NMT）組優勝於神經肌肉訓練（NMT）組或腦電生物反饋訓練（AT）組，這証明我們以上的預計是正確的。 目的：比較AT-NMT、NMT、AT和對照組（接受常規治療）對改善DCD兒童的平衡反應的有效性。 研究設計：這是一個單盲、隨機對照試驗。 參加者：172位DCD兒童。 訓練：AT-NMT、NMT、AT或常規治療，為期12週。 主要測量結果：將在訓練前、訓練後和訓練後的3個月進行評估。電機控制試驗（MCT）會給出一個綜合平衡反應評分，腦電圖將記錄在進行MCT時的專注程度，肌電圖將記錄在進行MCT時的下肢肌肉反應。 預期結果和臨床意義：接受AT-NMT的DCD兒童將有最好的反應性平衡表現。如果研究結果是正面的，這種新穎的治療方案，可以應用在臨床實踐中。 AT-NMT將全面改善這些兒童的福祉，具有正面的社會經濟影響，例如縮短康復期，從長遠來看，可降低醫療開支。

17658516.label: Realisation of objectives
17658516.value: This project was completed successfully and the objective was achieved. The following summary describes how and to what extent the project objective was realised. Objective: This study compared the effectiveness of (1) electroencephalographic (EEG) biofeedback attention-neuromuscular training (AT-NMT), (2) neuromuscular training (NMT) alone, (3) EEG biofeedback attention training (AT) alone, and (4) control (care as usual) for improving reactive balance performance among children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD). The balance associated attention and leg muscle activation were also explored. Methods: This was a single-blinded, randomised controlled trial. A total of 198 children with DCD were recruited and screened for eligibility. Only 175 children (age: 6–9 years) were qualified and they were randomly assigned to the AT-NMT (n = 43), NMT (n = 44), AT (n = 44) and control groups (n = 44). Children assigned to the AT-NMT, NMT and AT groups attended twice-weekly 40-minute training sessions for 12 weeks. The AT-NMT group received two levels of training: AT using EEG biofeedback and NMT supplemented with EEG biofeedback. During the AT, each participant wore a Mindwave Mobile EEG headset with an active electrode fixed to the prefrontal cortex. The participant then used his/her mind to control the attention meter included in the NeuroSky BrainWave Visualizer software. Each participant was instructed to use intense mental concentration to push the attention meter index to 100, the highest level, and then hold it at that level. Five 1-minute trials were performed. After completing AT, the participant received NMT supplemented with EEG biofeedback training. During NMT practice, participants focused continuously on the stability of their centre of gravity (CG). They were instructed to imagine their CG as a stable point inside the pelvis that could not be moved by external disturbances. They were trained in the concept of maintaining CG stability until their attention level reached 60. Then, the trainer disturbed the participant’s body balance unexpectedly by moving the supporting platform in a random direction. The participant reacted by remaining upright. After that, the participant was required to attend to the timing of the lower limb muscle contractions while maintaining an attention index of >60. During this trial, the participant resisted the movement of the supporting platform by contracting his/her leg muscles as needed. The NMT group practiced the neuromuscular balance manoeuvres repeatedly for 40 minutes. The AT group received intensive EEG biofeedback attention training for 40 minutes but did not participate in NMT. Children in the control group did not receive any training within the study period but they continued their normal daily activities and usual medical care. Outcomes were evaluated at baseline, 3 months (post-intervention) and 6 months (follow-up) by blinded assessors. A motor control test (MCT; reactive balance test) administered via a computerised dynamic posturography machine with concurrent EEG and surface electromyography (EMG) were used to determine the MCT composite latency score (a primary outcome), attention level and leg muscle onset latency before and throughout MCT forward and backward platform translations (secondary outcomes), respectively. In addition, the expectation about treatment credibility was measured post-intervention using a questionnaire (maximum score = 10). The intention-to-treat assumption (last observation carried forward) was made to handle missing data. Mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of covariance followed by post hoc tests were conducted, as appropriate. The alpha level was set at 5% (two-tailed). A Bonferroni adjustment was applied to post hoc multiple comparisons. Results: A total of 130 children with DCD completed the interventions and 3-month assessments but only 117 completed the 6-month assessments. The average attendance rates for the AT-NMT, NMT and AT interventions were 80%, 72% and 77%, respectively. There were no significant differences in demographic characteristics among the 4 groups (AT-NMT group: mean age = 7.8 years, 34 boys and 9 girls; NMT group: mean age = 7.6 years, 33 boys and 11 girls; AT group: mean age = 7.2 years, 37 boys and 7 girls; and control group: mean age = 7.2 years, 41 boys and 3 girls). At 3 months, the mean differences of the MCT composite latency score in the AT-NMT , NMT and AT groups relative to the control group were -59.27 ms (p < 0.001), -90.60 ms (p < 0.001) and -54.37 ms (p < 0.001), respectively. At 6 months, however, only the AT-NMT group exhibited a significant improvement in the MCT composite latency score relative to the baseline value (-43.34 ms; p = 0.008). At this later time point, the differences in the AT-NMT, NMT and AT groups relative to the control group were -92.10 ms (p < 0.001), -102.57 ms (p < 0.001) and -66.71 ms (p < 0.001), respectively. Moreover, from baseline to 3 months, the attention index before the backward platform translation improved only in the AT group (9.15 points; p = 0.005). At 3 months, the mean differences in the AT group relative to the control and NMT groups were 12.93 points (p = 0.001) and 8.53 points (p = 0.004), respectively. At 6 months, the attention index was still higher in the AT group than the control group (11.87 points; p < 0.001). In the AT-NMT group, the attention indices throughout the backward platform translation and before the forward platform translation improved significantly from the baseline at both 3 months (7.15 points; p = 0.008 and 11.01 points; p = 0.001, respectively) and 6 months (8.71 points; p < 0.001 and 12.07 points; p < 0.001, respectively). In all groups, however, the attention index throughout the forward platform translation remained relatively stable over time. No within- or between-group changes were observed in the leg muscle activation onset latency. The treatment credibility scores were 8.1, 8.2 and 8.2 for the AT-NMT, NMT and AT groups, respectively. No major adverse events were noted. Conclusions: AT-NMT, AT and NMT yielded equal improvements in the reactive balance performance of children with DCD. However, only AT-NMT and AT improved attention during or before a postural disturbance, and none of the interventions improved leg muscle reflex contraction latency.

17658516.label: Major findings and research outcome
17658516.value: Major findings: AT-NMT, AT and NMT were equally effective in terms of improving the reactive balance performances of children with DCD. Therefore, all of these interventions could be implemented in clinical practice. However, only AT-NMT and AT were shown to improve attention during or before a postural disturbance, while none of the interventions improved leg muscle reflex contraction latency in response to a postural threat. (Please refer to the “realisation of objectives” section for a detailed description of the findings). Research outcome: This research work has yielded the publication of 4 papers in high-quality peer-reviewed journals. The study findings have also been presented at 2 local and 1 international conferences, and 3 abstracts have been published. A PhD student and a post-doctoral fellow were supported financially to conduct this study. They have published more than 3 papers. The principal investigator has disseminated the findings through the mass media (1 newspaper article and 1 TV program) and was invited to give a talk about the study in Taiwan. (Please refer to the “research output” and “other impact” sections.)

17658516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17658516.value: Exploring the underlying physiological mechanisms associated with AT and/or NMT is crucial to further understand its clinical efficacy. Our research team intends to use a multi-channel EEG device to further exam the neurophysiological correlates associated with reactive balance control in children with DCD. Moreover, whether the improved reactive balance performance can be carried over to daily functions such as walking should be further examined. A research postgraduate student currently investigates the postural reactions and gait pattern (and the use of taping) in children with DCD. A grant proposal is being prepared to test the effects of AT+/-NMT in improving walking pattern and postural stability of children with DCD. Further research work could also investigate the effectiveness of AT-NMT among other paediatric populations such as children with autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.

17658516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17658516.value: This study examined whether muscle reaction training alongside mental attention training (AT-NMT) was superior to muscle reaction training (NMT) alone, mental attention training (AT) alone, or no training for improving body balance and the associated mental attention and leg muscle reaction time in children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD, clumsy children). This investigation is important because children with DCD often exhibit balance difficulties that predispose them to injurious falls in daily life. A typical ‘randomised controlled study design’ was used. A total of 175 children with DCD (age: 6–9 years) were randomly allocated to the AT-NMT (43 children), NMT (44 children), AT (44 children) and control groups (44 children). The 3 intervention groups received the indicated treatment twice weekly (40 minutes per training session) for 12 weeks. Body balance and the associated mental attention and leg muscle activity were measured before and after the training period and 3 months after its completion. The results revealed that AT-NMT, AT and NMT yielded equal improvements in the balance performance of children with DCD. However, only AT-NMT and AT improved mental attention during or before a balance threat, and no intervention improved leg muscle reaction time.

17660616.label: Project Objectives
17660616.value: To examine possible cultural differences between Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong and English-speaking children in America in their early knowledge of multi-digit numbers and place-value concept prior to formal schooling. To explore how well preschool children’s early, partial knowledge of multi-digit numbers and place-value concept acquired in everyday life predicts their numerical performance in elementary school, and whether such predictive relation applies to both Chinese- and English-speaking children. To explore which kinds of everyday activities or events are beneficial to young children’s development of early knowledge of multi-digit numbers and place-value concept prior to formal schooling.

17660616.label: Realisation of objectives
17660616.value: Objective 1: We recruited 158 Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong via local kindergartens, and our collaborator in the U.S. helped to recruit 81 English-speaking children there. All children completed a battery of multi-digit number tasks. The children fell into three age groups: 4-, 5-, and 6-years-old. We found that there were some cultural differences in the performance of number writing and number comparison. In number writing (in which children were asked to write out a number in Arabic), Hong Kong children from all age groups were more accurate than the U.S children in writing two-digit numbers. When writing three-digit numbers, the 5-year-olds in the U.S. were more accurate than their counterparts in Hong Kong, whereas the 6-year-olds in Hong Kong were more accurate than their counterparts in the U.S. However, no cross-cultural difference was observed in four-digit number writing. In number comparison (in which children were asked to choose the bigger number in a pair), cross-cultural difference was found only in the 6-year-olds, where children in Hong Kong were more accurate than their counterparts in the U.S. These findings suggest that young children possess some knowledge of multi-digit numbers prior to formal instruction, and cross-cultural differences may appear during this early stage. Objective 2: We recruited 146 children of upper kindergarten (mean age 5.6 years) in Hong Kong who completed a set of multi-digit assessment tasks. Sixty-six of them were assessed again for their place-value understanding and mathematical achievement when they were in Grade 1 (mean age 7 years). Using this longitudinal data, we examined the relation between early multi-digit number understanding and later mathematical outcome. Results showed that multi-digit number understanding in upper kindergarten was a significant predictor of children’s mathematical achievement in Grade 1, after controlling for their IQ and visuospatial working memory. Such relation was mediated by their knowledge of place-value in Grade 1. Objective 3: We asked the parents of the 146 children studying in upper kindergarten (mentioned in Objective 2 above) to complete a survey. In the survey, the parents had to report how frequently they did specific kinds of activities with their children. Results of subsequent factor analysis on the parents’ responses revealed four meaningful and distinctive types of activities, namely school math (activities related to reading and writing numbers), games, activities involving educational tools (e.g., base-ten blocks), and spatial activity (e.g., doing a puzzle). The frequency of these activities was significantly correlated with children’s performance in multi-digit number understanding, place-value concept, and mathematical achievement in Grade 1. We further ran a series of multiple regressions and found that, after controlling for children’s IQ and visuospatial working memory, the frequency of spatial activities in upper kindergarten remained predictive of children’s place-value concept in Grade 1. To further examine the effectiveness of specific activities in enhancing children’s multi-digit understanding, we carried out two separate interventions studies to look into number line board games and (number) story reading in particular – two common home activities. In the study of number line board games, we invited 91 local children studying in the lower kindergarten to play some board games for six days. They were randomly divided into four groups. Three groups of children played number line board games (i.e., roll the dice and move one’s token forward the number of spaces as rolled on the dice) in a specific way. In mapping condition, children were helped to map numbers onto their magnitudes on the number line while playing the game; in ordinal condition, children were asked to focus on the ordinal sequence of the numbers; the mapping and ordinal condition was the combined condition of the two. Another group of children were the control group who played colour board games which had nothing to do with numbers. Results showed that, after controlling for their pre-test performance, the mapping group performed significantly better than the ordinal group in the number comparison task in the post-test. This suggests that playing number board games, especially when the number-magnitude mapping is highlighted, can help young children to make sense of multi-digit numbers. In the study of number story reading, 89 local kindergarteners were invited to participate in a series of story reading sessions across two weeks. They were divided into three conditions. In the without-cardinal-label condition, the stories did not use numbers to label the exact quantities of items shown, but they did in the with-cardinal-label condition. In the with-cardinal-label-and-counting condition, numbers were used to represent the quantities of items and the researchers counted with the children from one. Results showed that children in the with-cardinal-label-and-counting condition showed the best mapping between numbers and quantities in the post-test, after controlling for their pre-test performance. This suggests that counting activities in number story reading can enhance children’s mapping between multi-digit numbers and quantities.

17660616.label: Major findings and research outcome
17660616.value: We discovered cross-cultural difference in early multi-digit number understanding among children in Hong Kong and U.S. Such difference depended on age. The findings were presented in Mathematical Cognition and Learning Society Conference (Part C 9.2) and are being written up for publication (Part C 8.3). In addition, we designed a new task for assessing kindergarteners’ automatic processing of place-value (i.e., place-value Stroop task). Results showed that when comparing the face-value of the digits in a multi-digit number, young children were inevitably affected by the place-value held by the digits. This suggests that young children can automatically activate the place-value of digits. The findings were published in European Journal of Developmental Psychology (Part C 8.1). In a longitudinal study, we found that children’s multi-digit number understanding measured in upper kindergarten was significantly predictive of their mathematical achievement in Grade 1. This relation was mediated by children’s place-value understanding. This confirms the importance of early, informal understanding of multi-digit numbers in later mathematical achievement. The finding was presented in the symposium of Mathematical Cognition and Learning Society Conference (Part C 9.1). In addition, we examined the cognitive correlates of early multi-digit number understanding. We constructed a path model among children in upper kindergarten, which showed that children’s multi-digit number understanding was predicted by their knowledge of number sequence via their ability to map between numbers and their underlying quantities. This highlighted the importance of counting knowledge and mapping skills in early development of multi-digit number understanding. The findings are being written up for publication (Part C 8.4). From the longitudinal data, we found that early home activities were significantly correlated with children’s mathematical performance in Grade 1. Using multiple regression, we discovered that early spatial activities were significantly predictive of children’s place-value concept, after controlling for some related cognitive skills. Additional intervention studies investigated two specific activities, namely number line board games and number story reading. Results showed that playing number line board games with a focus on the mapping between numbers and quantities is beneficial to young children’s multi-digit number understanding. The findings were presented in Mathematical Cognition and Learning Society Conference (Part C 9.3). As for number story reading, we found that counting with children during reading was useful to improve their mapping between numbers and quantities. The findings were published in Frontiers in Psychology (Part C, 8.2).

17660616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17660616.value: Given that there are cross-cultural differences in early multi-digit number understanding, it is worthwhile to further investigate the factors underlying such understanding and the long-term consequence of such early differences. Moreover, it is important to trace the development of multi-digit number understanding to see if such cross-cultural differences remain, change, or disappear over time. As we have developed task for assessing automatic place-value processing among kindergarteners, it would be interesting to trial it out among non-Chinese speaking children to see if there exists any cross-cultural difference in automatic processing of multi-digit numbers as well. The present research revealed the cognitive correlates of early multi-digit number understanding, the relation between home activities and early multi-digit number understanding, and the mediation relation between early multi-digit number understanding and later mathematical achievement. The next step would be putting these together in a fuller model to obtain a coherent picture of how early multi-digit number understanding develops in preschool years, and how such understanding affects mathematical achievement in elementary school years.

17660616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17660616.value: Although kindergarteners do not formally learn multi-digit numbers at school, they do have some knowledge about them. This is true for both children in Hong Kong and in U.S. Interestingly, cross-cultural difference was observed among these children depending on their age. In a longitudinal local study, we found that multi-digit number understanding among children in upper kindergarten well predicts their place-value understanding in Grade 1, which in turn predicts their mathematical outcome. This highlights the important role of early multi-digit number understanding. Based on our findings, home activities can be useful to promote children’s multi-digit number understanding. In particular, the frequency of spatial activities is predictive of kindergarteners’ understanding of multi-digit numbers. In sum, the present findings support the importance of early multi-digit number understanding to later mathematical achievement, and point to home activities as a potential means to support such early understanding.

17662116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17662116.value: 中国可持续发展城市的构建：珠三角和京津冀城市群可持续发展与城市转型

17662116.label: Project Objectives
17662116.value: To delineate the characteristics of sustainable development as an urban strategy; To interrogate the reasons behind Chinese local officials’ growing interest in sustainable development; To assess the social and economic consequences of sustainability-guided development in China’s urban regions.
rows: To delineate the characteristics of sustainable development as an urban strategy;
To interrogate the reasons behind Chinese local officials’ growing interest in sustainable development;
To assess the social and economic consequences of sustainability-guided development in China’s urban regions.

17662116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17662116.value: 本研究结合中国城市化与环境变化的理论探索，调查和分析近年来兴起的可持续城市发展与规划之形成过程及其影响。研究的目的是：界定可持续城市发展策略的特征，调查地方政府热综于可持续发展城市的根源，评估可持续发展城市策略的社会和经济影响。 本研究选择华南珠江三角洲和华北的京津冀两个在实施可持续城市发展策略方面领先的地区。研究方法结合对有关统计资料的系统分析和面谈以及实地考察，研究成果不仅填补现有中国城市化与环境变化理论研究的空白，而且为中国内地以及香港各级政府推动和有效管理可持续城市发展规划提供重要依据。

17662116.label: Realisation of objectives
17662116.value: The three objectives identified in the original proposal have all been accomplished successfully and fruitfully. Below is a summary of what we have done. Objective 1 has been successfully accomplished through a cross-sectional analysis of the data collected for China’s 297 cities at and above the prefectural level and a longitudinal study of the two city-regions chosen for focused investigations. We have managed to divide all of our sampled cities (after eliminating 11 “bad samples” for which data are either missing or in poor quality) into two groups, one that has since 2005 completed at least one eco-city project or an ecological restoration program and the other has not, for a comparative analysis. Comparison has included the intensity of capital input (per capita fixed asset capital investment), the level of economic growth (per capita GDP), level of urbanization (percentage of urban population to total population), characteristics of the urban built-environment (per capita urban built-up area, housing floor area, length of paved road, area of urban park and green space), and degree of openness (ratio of export to total GDP or ratio of foreign direct investment [FDI] to total fixed asset investment). The result has identified an intriguing pattern that does not confirm popular perception. No significant and positive relationship is found between the promotion of a sustainable city and the growth of the urban economy. Upgrading and improvements of the urban-built environment are evident, but the impacts upon the quality of air and water are found to be short-lived. Longitudinal analysis of the two cases of Beijing and Guangzhou has generated consistent findings. Objective 2 has been accomplished satisfactorily through in-depth field investigations conducted in Beijing and Guangzhou as originally planned. In Beijing, our field work has focused on the city government’s campaign to improve air quality by shutting down all the quarries within the municipality since the early 2000s as part of its preparation to host the 2008 Olympics. Our focused study of this interesting process of “quarry-to-dump conversion” has uncovered not only the different stakeholders and winners/losers involved in the promotion of sustainable city but also their different motivations, strategies, and actions taken in the process. In Guangzhou, our research has focused on the government’s campaign for “low-carbon urbanization”, “waste-to-energy incineration”, and “zero-waste neighborhood” construction that has become so fashionable since the late 2000s. Our in-depth field investigations (interviews, questionnaire surveys, and archival documentary research) have unfolded an interesting dynamism in which eco-urbanization has been driven by bottom-up environmental activism that challenged the state’s top-down imposition of waste-to-energy incineration. Together, our focused studies of Beijing and Guangzhou have generated important findings to challenge the popular perception that takes eco-urbanism as either the technological product of global climate controls from above or the result of a “sustainable fix” of the crises of global capitalism from outside. Objective 3 has been successfully accomplished in accordance with the original plan. We have collected and analyzed regional economic data such as per capita GDP, per capita income, level of urbanization, FDI, exports, and municipal revenue for the Pearl River Delta region and the Jing-Jin-Ji region since the year 2000. The changing position held by Guangzhou was evaluated against the Pearl River Delta region and the case of Beijing was evaluated in the regional context of the Jing-Jin-Ji. We have also gathered information regarding incidents of social discontent and protests against enforcement of environmental laws, relocation of rural households, and undercompensated expropriation of farmland in the name of urban development. Our research has generated novel research findings published in leading international journals with acknowledgements of funding supports from this grant (see Research Outcome and Research Output below for details). Overall, we are highly satisfied with the results of our research as what we have originally planned.

17662116.label: Major findings and research outcome
17662116.value: This project has generated a large number of important findings, some of which have already been published in leading internationally refereed journals and presented in international conferences while others are in the pipeline of submission and publication. Our research findings include: 1. Contrary to the mainstream perception that urbanization in China facilitates the process of local state building, urban redevelopment as a means of capital mobilization in fact often involves a concentration of resources in certain sectors of the local government with a concomitant and significant weakening of the governing capacity in other sectors; 2. Chinese municipalities’ long-standing neglect of waste management has created leeway for a strategy of self-protection at the grassroots level of the society; 3. As a part of the grassroots society, rural villages at the urban peripheries have played an important role in the expansion and the management of urban resource frontiers of large metropolitan regions; 4. In contrast with the prevailing interpretation of eco-urbanism as the product of the top-down logic of climate control, local practices and struggles may significantly change the nature, dynamics and landscape of eco-urbanism; 5. The bottom-up anti-incineration activism that emerged in large municipalities since the early 2010s has significantly helped the spread of eco-urbanism in China; 6. Sustainable development projects have been (mis)used by the city governments involved as a means to deploy (overdraft) resources from the future and elsewhere for an improvement of the urban built-environment. 7. Implementation of sustainable development is found to have a significant but short-lasting effect upon the instant improvement of the environmental quality of the city. 8. Sustainable urban development has been used by the governments as a means to create temporarily at least a unified social space in which social discontents are effectively sidetracked and covered up in the name of sustainability and collective interests. Deeply rooted problems and built-in crises are simply delayed and postponed without any fundamental solution. 9. Sustainable urban development has brought significant benefits to selected social groups in the city but displaced and marginalized the laid-off workers from state-owned enterprises and the migrant population exacerbating the problems of segregation, exclusion, and social discontents. Geographically, sustainable urban development has further enhanced the leading position held by the central city and hence led to increased regional inequality.

17662116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17662116.value: This project has helped push forward the research frontier in urban China studies. Two important issues arisen from this project are believed to have significant potentials for further research and development. First, this research has focused on the practice of a sustainability-driven urban developmental strategy in the two leading Chinese cities. Further research is needed to investigate cases in other Chinese cities and compare the Chinese experiences with others found elsewhere in the world (e.g. Japan, South Korea, USA, Canada, Australia, etc.). Second, this research has identified a general pattern in which sustainable urban development has been used as a justification for urban renewals involving the removal, relocation and redevelopment of old factories, neighborhoods, and villages-in-the city. Is this phenomenon simply accidental and isolated, or is it indicative of a new trend whereby China’s urbanization shifts its emphasis from the mode of urban sprawl into urban renewal? Further research is needed.

17662116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17662116.value: This research investigates how and why sustainable urban development has been practiced as a new strategy of urbanization in China and what social and economic effects this strategy has had focusing on the cases of Beijing and Guangzhou. Sustainable urban development is found to be a strategy to (over)draft capital from the future for momentary improvements of the urban infrastructure, create tangible and visible records of political accomplishments, and temporarily dispel grievance and social discontents. The growth of sustainable cities has not simplistically strengthened the governing power of municipal governments as generally believed but has instead involved a concentration of resources in certain sectors and a simultaneous weakening of the governing capacity in other sectors. Contrary to the popular perception of eco-urbanism as the product of the top-down imposition of global climate governance, local environmentalism at the grassroots level is found to have changed significantly the nature, dynamics and landscape of eco-urbanization. No convincing evidence is found to suggest a significant and positive relationship between the promotion of a sustainable city and urban economic growth. Special attention needs to be paid to the unfortunate victims of the practicing of eco-urbanism—displaced factory workers, landless farmers, and excluded migrant population.

17662316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17662316.value: 競爭法與買方權勢：從理論和香港方面探討

17662316.label: Project Objectives
17662316.value: To develop general theories of harm which help to explain the motivation behind and predict the consequences of unilateral buyer power abuses. To comprehensively specify conditions for illegality for different types of unilateral buyer power abuse and workable legal remedies under generally accepted principles of competition law. To apply the theoretical/legal framework developed as part of objectives (1) and (2) to analyse and make legal and policy recommendations for rectifying problems of unilateral buyer power abuse in different industries in Hong Kong. To help nurture undergraduate researchers by engaging them in a serious academic research project in the hope that they will be attracted to academia.

To comprehensively specify conditions for illegality for different types of unilateral buyer power abuse and workable legal remedies under generally accepted principles of competition law.

To apply the theoretical/legal framework developed as part of objectives (1) and (2) to analyse and make legal and policy recommendations for rectifying problems of unilateral buyer power abuse in different industries in Hong Kong.
