17662316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17662316.value: This project seeks to propose a theoretical framework for understanding and analysing unilateral buyer power abuses under competition law (issues of buyer cartels, buyer joint ventures or buyer mergers are excluded). Competition law has always devoted greater attention to abuses of seller market power, which is what the abuse of dominance jurisprudence in the various jurisdictions has traditionally focused on. Some commentators have paid attention to unilateral buyer power issues, but mostly in a piecemeal fashion focusing on specific aspects, such as the waterbed effect, private labels, anti-competitive overbuying, and bargaining power issues. This project seeks to bridge the gap in the literature by canvassing the various kinds of competition law issues that arise from the abusive use of unilateral buyer power to exploit sellers or exclude competitors, in order to categorise and analyse such issues according to various general theories of harm, such as exploitation of sellers, foreclosure from access to sellers, predation, and leveraging of power by a vertically-integrated retailer. The project will suggest that many abuses of buyer power harm competition through their foreclosure effect to competing buyers, either of the strong kind, whereby foreclosure is complete, or of the weak kind, whereby access to an important input or product is impaired (as in the case of the waterbed effect). Based on the general theories of harm developed in this project, we will formulate conditions for illegality and workable legal remedies for various types of unilateral buyer power abuse. The project will then seek to apply the theoretical/legal framework developed at the initial stage to Hong Kong. The Hong Kong Competition Ordinance will come into effect in December 2015. One of the longest standing competition law issues in Hong Kong is allegedly abuse of buyer power by supermarkets in the grocery sector. Moreover, media reports suggest that issues of unilateral buyer power abuse permeate the economy. The Competition Commission will undoubtedly be confronted with buyer power issues in its enforcement. However, judging from the Guideline on the Second Conduct Rule (regulating abuse of power) issued by the Competition Commission, it seems that the Commission has, like most other jurisdictions, focused its attention on unilateral abuse of seller power instead of buyer power. Therefore, this project seeks to provide guidance to the Competition Commission on this very important enforcement issue in Hong Kong. 此研究項目旨在提出一個理論框架，從而了解和分析買方單方面濫用權勢的競爭法問題。不同司法管轄區的競爭法一直著重賣方濫用市場權勢的問題，並設有相關法例規管。部份學者有關注買方單方面濫用權勢的問題，但大部份相關研究都側重於狹窄的的議題，比如「水床效應」、自家品牌、反競爭超買，及議價能力的問題。此項目旨在根據不同的競爭損害競爭理論進行分類，並分析買方單方面濫用權勢的問題，例如反競爭封鎖效果的強弱方面。基於這些競爭損害競爭理論，我們將就不同類型的買方單方面濫用權勢的情況制定違法條件及可行的法律補救措施。我們會把建立的理論及法律框架應用於香港。香港競爭條例於2015年12月全面生效。香港一直受雜貨市場的據稱買方濫用權勢的問題困擾，媒體亦有就不同的買方單方面濫用權勢的議題作出報導，而競爭事務委員會很可能要面對這些問題。儘管如此，針對濫用權勢的《第二行為守則》與很多其他司法管轄區的指引一樣，將重點放於賣家單方面濫用權勢方面，而非買方。因此，此項目亦旨在向競爭事務委員會就買方單方面濫用權勢的競爭法問題提供一些指導。

17662416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17662416.value: 為甚麼在網上披露個人信息?：中國社交媒體上的隱私與面子

17662416.label: Project Objectives
17662416.value: Assess the types of information disclosed on WeChat, Examine the factors that contribute to variations in disclosure tendencies, Investigate strategies for protecting online privacy.
rows: Assess the types of information disclosed on WeChat,
Examine the factors that contribute to variations in disclosure tendencies,
Investigate strategies for protecting online privacy.

17662416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17662416.value: With the increasing popularity of social media in China, privacy has become a key issue. While controversies related to the disclosure of information on social media have been the subject of widespread media attention in China, very little is known about why people disclose personal information online, and why some tend to disclose more than others. Studies on online privacy and privacy control behavior in Western countries suggest that people care about privacy and use various strategies to protect it while sharing information on social media. At the same time, as sociologists and anthropologists suggest, privacy is contextual and situational; that is, it depends on the context and the relationship with the audience. In terms of online audience in the Chinese context, users of the most popular social media app in China called WeChat differ from other popular social media apps in two aspects: WeChat allows a more closed and private setting for sharing information, and in Chinese culture, face (mianzi), hierarchy of social status, and interpersonal harmony play a more prominent role in communication. To fill the gap in knowledge about how Chinese social media users manage their privacy and the conditions in which they disclose information, this project focuses on users’ disclosing activities and seeks to understand: 1) the types of information disclosed; 2) the factors that influence online disclosing behavior; and 3) the strategies used to control privacy online. A qualitative study will be carried out with research procedures based on a previous study on online disclosure in the U.S. conducted by the PI. These procedures include focus-group discussion, in-depth interviews, and content analysis. The project will contribute to knowledge on online privacy both empirically and theoretically. Empirically, it will provide a timely description of online disclosure in the context of growing and pervasive use of social media in China, assessing perceptions of online privacy and privacy control strategies. These findings can inform efforts to increase online privacy protection. Sociological theories have been developed in the Western context, where privacy is considered a primary individual legal right and equality is assumed between those interacting. In China, face, hierarchy, and interpersonal harmony have more precedence. Therefore, an understanding of the behavior of social media users in the Chinese context will contribute to the theoretical development of online interaction in contemporary societies.

17662416.label: Realisation of objectives
17662416.value: All the three objectives as stated in the original proposal have been fully achieved. 1. Assess the types of information disclosed on WeChat WeChat users disclose three major types of information: 1) Information that can enhance one’s self-face and positive self-image, and can help increase one’s social standing. WeChat users make many “showing-off” posts that cover various kinds of face, such as announcing career achievements (competence face), social gatherings (inclusion face), and posting pictures of one’s children (to show that one is a responsible mother, reliability face). Those who have recently achieved upward mobility or experienced positive changes (such as engagement, marriage, and promotion) are likely to post more frequently. 2) Information to honor others’ face. A major difference between Chinese WeChat users in this study and social media users in the West (as described by existing literature) is that the Chinese respondents tend to use WeChat primarily as a platform to manage their offline relationships by honoring others’ faces (paper 1). When posting, commenting or giving “likes”, the primary concern is to give face to others. Chinese WeChat users “like” and sometimes post or repost in order to build relationships, show agreement, and to demonstrate (to other group members) relationships in public. Many users also post on their WeChat Moments as a favor to others, which is called renqing post. They help others repost certain messages that require wide distribution. The posts are usually commercial in nature, which is self-serving for the requesting party but aggravating to the poster. Even so, users typically do not refuse renqing post requests, especially if it is from a strong tie. 3) Information that aims at showing deference or compliance in public in order to please workplace superiors (paper 2). This includes sharing work-related content on WeChat Moments per the request of workplace supervisors, making positive comments under workplace superiors’ posts, re-posting content posted by superiors, etc. WeChat users in Chinese workplaces, especially those of a lower hierarchal position, are compelled to constantly express their loyalty or appreciation and thus publicly submit to their superordinates by clicking “like” or commenting on their WeChat posts. They are also forced to provide immediate and polite responses to their superordinates in WeChat group chats after work hours or to non-work-related issues. Such disclosures are usually against the will of those workers, finding constant demonstration of submission in public to be demeaning. But they soon realize they must comply because of the structural power of supervisors and because past conversations on WeChat are recorded and traceable. There is no time or space for the workers to escape from this type of online disclosure. There are also three types of information that users are reluctant to disclose online: 1) Information that reveals too much personality, including personal opinions, especially on political issues or public affairs. Since the target audience on WeChat often includes offline contacts, users tend to avoid conflict because there is a cultural expectation to maintain harmonious relationships. To avoid conflicts, they rarely post genuine opinions and anything that might be seen as controversial. Since users continuously post content that is acceptable to the majority, mainstream values are further reinforced (paper 1). 2) Information that is framed in a negative tone. Over time users realize that negative content would not be appreciated on WeChat (paper 1) because WeChat is considered as space for “circulating positive energy”. An analysis of some users’ WeChat posts shows that they tend to have mixed positive and negative content when they first started using WeChat. But over time, the content began to be dominated by positive content. Negative content, such as complaints, become rare over time. 3) Information that could be interpreted to challenge the status quo, especially the workplace hierarchy. Users are wary of potential but undetectable audiences of their posts or interactions. Junior staff avoid posting anything that might make them appear to be more intelligent or knowledgeable than their supervisors, such as discussions of international politics (paper 2). 2. Examine the factors that contribute to variations in disclosure tendencies The research was carried out in three cities in China: Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou. But no significant regional difference was identified. No obvious gender difference was observed either. Rather, the main difference lies in age: younger users tend to disclose differently from older ones. More specifically, the main factor is whether the person is located in an explicit hierarchy. Those who have entered the workplace (an explicit and well-structured hierarchy) disclose differently from those who are still students (not yet entered an explicit hierarchy). Therefore, I wrote two separate papers based on the research findings: one paper draws on data mainly from university students (both undergraduate and graduate) and some university non-faculty staff members, the other paper focuses exclusively on those who have already entered the workplace. For those who are not in an explicit hierarchy, such as students, the main factor that contributes to variations in disclosure tendencies is whether they have experienced breaches from influential outsiders or not. This finding is similar to a previous study conducted by me and my colleague about U.S. bloggers (Tian and Menchik 2016). How much and what content they disclose depends largely on the feedback loop. At first, comments and “likes” from a few core members of their WeChat contacts will encourage them to share personal information online. But later, breaches from those unexpected silent observers would make them aware that they have presented themselves in an unflattering way, and they will begin to adjust their patterns of disclosures on WeChat Moments. For those who are embedded in an explicit hierarchy, such as the workplace, the main factor that influences their tendency of disclosure is their position in the hierarchy. The subordinates, especially those who are new to the organization or low in the hierarchy, tend to actively use WeChat as a platform to show appreciation and respect to superiors, in order to build a better relationship with them and to gain favorable treatment (paper 2). The superordinates understand the power difference and deliberately distance themselves from their subordinates on WeChat. 3. Investigate strategies for protecting online privacy. The respondents indicate concern about their online privacy and strategies to protect their online privacy include: 1) Disclose less personal information. Over time, people on WeChat Moments tend to disclose less and less original content (personal comments, pictures, showing off), and disclose more non-original content (third party website links). This is especially obvious among the university student respondents. 2) Change the technical settings to control audience. Some users take advantage of the technical settings such as “hide Moments from some users” or grouping functions (paper 1) to control whom in their WeChat contact list can view their posts. WeChat’s “grouping” function allows users share a particular post with only selected members on the contact list. Users can add each contact to different audience categories, and then selectively share with or block certain categories. 3) Engage in cynical performance of compliance, making disclosing activities, especially those related to showing submission to superiors, a role performance rather than an expression of their real self (paper 2).

17662416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17662416.value: Different from other social media apps such as Facebook, WeChat provides a more private and therefore “safe” online space for sharing. Disclosures on WeChat are influenced by Chinese culture of face, hierarchy, and interpersonal harmony, and the distinctive features of WeChat as a communication platform. The unique technical layout of WeChat Moments creates an acquaintance community consisting of small circles of friends. Because the audience are largely offline acquaintance, the online disclosure of Chinese WeChat users is calculated with the intention of maintaining one’s own face and honoring the face of others. As noted earlier, hierarchy, especially for those in the workplace, also greatly influences people’s online disclosures. As a digital communication tool, WeChat has three distinct features: elimination of physical interaction spaces, recordability of past WeChat conversations, and the n-adic nature of online disclosures. Now that physical co-presence is no longer necessary for supervisors to contact their workers, adding colleagues, especially superiors, on WeChat extends the workplace hierarchy into the private domain. Most notably, responding to supervisors after work hours, during holidays, at home, or on vacation is unavoidable. Because of the recordability of past conversations and posts on WeChat, digital media has turned the workplace into a panoptic environment; permanent visibility (now and past) is possible, and workers are conscious of it. Now, because of the prevalent use of social media in the workplace, for the first time in history, it is possible for supervisors to trace subordinate interpersonal interactions with accuracy and certainty, and this surveillance is not restrained by time. Interactions on WeChat also heighten sensitivity to the power hierarchy because of the n-adic nature of online interactions: both subordinates and superordinates know that unknown others might be watching or will read their posts at some point in time. Therefore, if subordinates do not show absolute compliance, supervisors risk losing face in front of their own supervisors. So even if flattery is despicable, the hierarchal expectations and ensuing consequences render it necessary. Unlike the original anticipations of the internet as a platform for more freedom and self-expression, WeChat is not a space for free self-expression for Chinese users. How posts might be interpreted and the subsequent influence on relationships are carefully considered. Genuine opinions or true feelings are muted to avoid complications in handling face and power hierarchy. There is little space for free speech and even the right to silence is lost.

17662416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17662416.value: When researching for this project in Shanghai, I interviewed some social workers and social work students, who showed some very interesting posting patterns on Moments. There was a major discrepancy between their interview accounts and posts. During interviews, they expressed anxieties about choosing Social Work as their career or major, such as high turnover rate, lack of job security, the lack of social recognition of the occupation, and mismatch between institutional and cultural expectations, etc. However, on their WeChat Moments, they post about the benefits of Social Work, such as better interpersonal skills, improved horizons, enriched meaning of life, etc. To explore these contradictions, I will conduct qualitative research about social workers in Shanghai to examine the micro-level processes of how culture influences action. I successfully applied for HKU seed funding for this project titled “Professional Dilemma and Everyday Redemption: Face and Status of Social Workers in Shanghai” (see attached grant proposal). I have obtained ethical approval for conducting this research and will start data collection in April 2019. Data will be collected through in-depth face-to-face interviews with social workers and Social Work students, and online observations of their WeChat Moments posts.

17662416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17662416.value: Online self-disclosure is a prevalent phenomenon, but existing literature is often collected from a US sample. Little is known about online self-disclosure with Chinese populations. This qualitative research project examines how Chinese users of WeChat disclose information and interact with others on WeChat. Data collected from Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou reveal that Chinese users employ various strategies to control privacy, such as changing the technical settings of their WeChat account. However, they rarely consider that information posted on WeChat Moments can be easily transmitted to another context, even if the original post is shared with a very limited circle or deleted. This study contributes to understanding online disclosure in China, and answers the theoretical question: has digital media reduced or reinforced inequality in society? Chinese users’ online disclosures are shaped by Chinese interpersonal culture (face, hierarchy, interpersonal harmony), and the distinctive features of online interaction afforded by the unique technical affordance of WeChat. WeChat Moments has become a platform for maintaining the normative requirements of showing agreement, sustaining superficial harmonious relationships, and looking “the same” as others. As a result, true opinions or personalities are rarely expressed on WeChat, and the power inequality between subordinates and superdordinates has been reified.

17663416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17663416.value: It is widely recognised that China’s late Ming period (1550-1644, Ming 1368-1644) witnessed an unprecedented flourishing of pornographic genres across multiples art forms (fiction, popular songs, drama, painting and woodblock prints). In contrast to earlier periods, when expressions of licentiousness were largely limited to court elites, iconoclastic cultural developments in the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries encouraged widespread interest in the body and desire. For the last half-century of the Ming in particular, pornography became a staple of the book publishing trade, a situation we now know continued beneath the strict gaze of the high Qing censors. Of the non-elite works that emerged through the historical processes outlined above this project will concentrate on a small number of surviving short fiction collections and associated works of literature and art which focus thematically on urban commoners’ sexual lives and their perspectives on love and sensual pleasure. Given the extent to which they stand out in terms of theme, style and language, I will be proposing that they be recognised as belonging to a cultural trend and literary genre of their own—provisionally identified as “urban commoner pornography,” or “popular pornography”. In the literary realm at least, most intellectual attention given to iconoclastic cultural developments is dominated by a focus on libertine cultural rebellion associated with sections of the privileged literati or scholar-official elite—this project will be the first extended study dedicated to a cultural historical analysis of this alternative plebeian cultural seam and its representative works of literature and art. Through the lens of early seventeenth-century textual and visual pornography this project will develop a cultural historical analysis of plebeian practices of reading and leisure between 1620 and 1670, contributing to the ongoing quest to recover knowledge of the plurality of forces and themes influencing the emergence of Chinese cultural modernity. As well as new cross-disciplinary methods in social and cultural/textual history which treat reading and consumption as a form of cultural participation, this focus on a carefully delineated circle of plebeian cultural expression will break new ground in the study of the relation of social and cultural processes in Chinese history, at the same time contributing insights into the evolution of the idea of “the consumer” in world historical terms. 晚明社會突然出現的色情消費品(小說、戲曲、民歌、繪畫和木版畫)的繁榮，近年來成爲學者們討論晚明社會文化的一個熱門話題。繼承了明代中晚期以士人為主導的色情作品注重張揚個性、尊重身體慾望、以及挑戰正統道德價值觀的風氣，明末清初的色情品成為了一種書商推銷的大眾消費品，并因此在清代一直受到官方的審查和禁燬。本課題將聚焦於幾種以前極少為學界注意到的明末清初（1620-1670）以江南都市平民生活為題材的短篇色情小說集、雜劇集以及色情木版畫刊，通過比較分析這些作品的主題、風格和語言，研究當時社會出現的城市平民新的性愛道德價值觀念及其社會影響。我認為這個時期存在一種新的文學潮流——都市平民的色情文學（也包括一部份視覺藝術）。當晚明士人的色情寫作以其對正統道德價值觀的叛逆而受到近二十年學界持續不衰的關注，本課題將偏離士人的話語而把注意力投向明末江南的平民色情文化。通過對這一系列文學和視角藝術等色情品的研究，本課題將進一步探討這個文學和文化潮流與中國本土的現代性的聯繫，希望能夠由此打開一片新的文化、性愛和性別研究的領域。

17663416.label: Realisation of objectives
17663416.value: 1, My cultural historical analysis of plebeian practices of reading and leisure in the final decades of the Ming dynasty has been conducted through an extensive survey of fiction, drama, folksongs, ballads, as well as other forms of expressive culture such as paintings and woodblock prints from the period. As most of the sources examined were unavailable in HK, support for several periods was organised to view materials in BnF (National Library of France, Paris), BSB (Munich), Helsinki University Library, National Library of Fenland, National Library of Russia (St Petersburg), Russian State Library (Moscow), Fu Sinian Library (Taipei), Tokyo University Library, Waseda University Library, Capital Library (Beijing), as well as in museums, private collections and research institute reading rooms. This schedule of research activities provided me access to rare period materials, the contents and physical condition of which, following paratextual analysis, I have used to piece together otherwise inaccessible details of the cultural horizon and values of urban lower class participants in public culture, expanding our knowledge of China’s past. 2, Central to identifying patterns of seventeenth-century urban commoner cultural consumption and leisure in the Lower Yangtze has been an analysis of two rare items. The first, kept in the Russian State Library, is the massive late-seventeenth century scatological novel Guwangyan (Preposterous Words), and my work as focused on identifying its earlier sources as a means of tracing its inspiration. The second, in the collection of the Muban Education Trust (London), is the late-Ming erotic magazine Jingyuan michuan dongfang chunyice, which includes erotic short stories, erotic pictures, and descriptions of aphrodisiac preparation. I have conducted research on the dates, authorship, publishers and readerships of these major finds and other difficult to document non-mainstream literary items. 3, Citing analysis of wide selection of materials from the period, I have been able to demonstrate an growing presence of urban commoners’ voices and values’ in seventeenth-century literary output, and in particular within the two genres of love stories and erotic fiction. I am also able to demonstrate that this new cultural output played a significant role the late-Ming reassessments of cultural authority, a pattern that enables us to align this period with early-modern urban culture in other parts of the world. Additionally, while misogynistic views are still widespread in these materials, a picture emerges of lower-class urban women gaining comparative independence in their sexual lives through their economic independence, their contributions to supporting the family recognised by their husbands as well as the society at large. 4, During the time spent on this project I have published two (2) international referred journal articles, one (1) scholarly book chapter, one (1) co-edited book (Leiden: Brill 2016). Among these the co-edited book has received excellent reviews in international journals in Asian studies. I have also attended six (6) key international conferences and presented my research findings in the USA, Australia, The Netherlands, Mainland China, and Hong Kong during this period. There are further items in production (or in press). As the Head of School it has not been easy to fit writing in between administrative tasks and research travel. Two (2) papers from this project are under review with international academic journals, and several additional papers from the project are still in preparation and will be published over the next 2-3 years. Conference presentations and opportunities for discussion with international colleagues has been enormously helpful for testing and refining finding that in many instances go against the grain of received wisdom. 5, I was the initiator and organiser of a very large international conference in Ming and Qing Studies in HK (HKU, 2017), as well as a smaller international workshop focusing on gender and sexuality in traditional China (HKU, 2018). I have also been invited to present my findings as an invited speaker at several prestigious universities, including Peking University, National Taiwan University, and the Baptist University of Hong Kong. 6, Having produced a consistent flow of output during the research projects I am now in a position to gather my separate arguments and findings into a broader thesis in monograph form. A heavy schedule of administrative tasks as Head of School is likely to delay completion of my monograph on plebeian practices of reading and leisure in the seventeenth century until June 2021. 7, This is an ambitious project that aims, through its papers and monograph, to establish a basis for an ongoing reassessment of literary innovation in late-imperial and modern Chinese cultural history. Moving beyond accepted images and positions based on the authority of elite, literati perspectives on the past is not something that can be achieved by a lone researcher, and outreach and exchange have played an integral part in this project achieving its aims and impact. I am fortunate to have several past and present research students who have taken up the quest for subaltern perspectives on late-imperial Chinese cultural life.

17663416.label: Major findings and research outcome
17663416.value: Beginning with “The Plebification of Male-Love and the Positioning of Catamites (xiaoguan) in Late-Ming Fiction: The Forgotten Tales of Longyang” (C7), a trend in early seventeenth century to the mid nineteenth-century homoerotic fiction novel was identified which breaks away from romantic master-servant themes to pursue a more free-floating understanding of ‘sublime love’ between literati men and boy-actors. Similarly, in “Pornographic Modes of Expression and Nascent Chinese Modernity in Late Imperial China” (C3) seventeenth-century short story collections were used to examine how “good” adulterers and even “good” unchaste women were introduced into the literary landscape by works seeking to undermine traditional Confucian morality. My analysis in “Reading Two Reworked Erotic Stories in Jingyuan michuan dongfang chunyice as Examples of Commoner Values and Morality in Late Ming Popular Erotica” (C5) examines popularisation of courtly debauchery, detailing how themes and stories for popular consumption were “translated” stylistically and morally. In Wanton Women in Late-Imperial Chinese Literature: Models, Genres, Subversions and Traditions (C6), collaboration with a team of experts in gender and literature allowed exploration of the hypersexualized “wanton woman” (yinfu) trope’s importance in the gendering of order and disorder, as well as reflecting tensions experienced between ideal and lived worlds in China’s early modern period. My own contribution to that volume, “Late Ming Urban Life and Wanton Women in Huang Fangyin’s Short Plays” (C1) examines how the hold that chastity had on their identity begins to loosen as urban commoner women’s agency expanded. In “Suzhou Dialect, Social Status, and Gender in Sancaifu, a Rediscovered Mid-Qing Chuanqi Play” (C2) I continued analysis of subaltern women in drama, this time examining a playwright’s subversive play with dialect to elicit sympathy for girls from struggling families, concubines, maids, nuns, elderly beggars, midwives, and go-betweens, ordinarily the butt of sardonic humour. With “Commoners’ Love Songs: Low Social Strata Perspectives on Gender and Sexuality as Represented in Late-Qing Popular Songbooks from North China” (C4) I examine urban commoner women’s perspectives through their own literature, which requires use of popular songbooks preserved from the mid-nineteenth century. This material will become the basis for my next major project. Far more than any of the material from the seventeenth century, these songs place us within reach of personal experiences of the urban streetscape and the women who made their way through them.

17663416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17663416.value: During the course of this project I discovered from the catalogue a significant number of nineteenth-century songbooks in the collection of the National Library of Russia (St Petersburg). These very roughly produced items promise to provide a very rich picture of the lives and desires of urban women in northern China, particularly when combined with what can be learned from similar fonds in libraries in Taiwan and Japan (as well as a Yangzhou related Hugo Lund Collection in Finland). The holdings of this genre in the Fu Ssu-nien Library of the Academia Sinica, Taibei, is enormous, and its recent facsimile publication in entirety is bound to attract new research in this neglected area. I have developed my preliminary research into this popular genre into a new GRF project. Through a study of international archival collections of popular North China urban narrative verse, the new project will identify and contextualise nineteenth- and early twentieth-century cultural themes that are not available in other literary forms. Adapting methods focused on materiality of the book and common everyday experience, analysis of this corpus popular with urban women will expand understanding of China’s literary history beyond perspectives dominated by elite cultural production.

17663416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17663416.value: It is widely recognised that China’s late Ming period (1550-1644) witnessed an unprecedented flourishing of pornographic genres across multiples art forms (fiction, popular songs, drama, painting and woodblock prints), a situation we now know continued beneath the strict gaze of the Qing censors (1644-1911), by which time something similar was taking shape in Europe. While the familiar story of this “underground” literary output associates it with the privileged scholar-official class, through examining a number of rare works only recently rediscovered, this project has demonstrated that less privileged residents of late-Ming cities produced their own “urban commoner pornography,” a “popular pornography” that shared a very different outlook to better-known works: more egalitarian, more pragmatic, and less concerned with social boundaries. As the first extended study of this low social strata cultural seam and its representative works of literature and art, the project has improved our knowledge of the diversity existing in Chinese societies in the past. By linking these same developments to the rise of the city and commercial printing it also contributes to better understanding the evolution of “cultural consumers” in world historical terms.

17665116.label: Project Objectives
17665116.value: To examine and critique the two most important and pervasive assumptions underlying the theory and practice of UK corporate governance: first, directors are and ought to be accountable to shareholders; and second, shareholders generally do not and should not owe duties to the company. To propose and defend new enforcement measures of promoting directorial and shareholder accountability.

17665116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17665116.value: Promoting oversight and accountability in boards of directors is a central and critical issue in company law and corporate governance. Directors are regarded as being accountable to shareholders. I seek to challenge this conventional view of accountability to shareholders by exploring the following theses: (a) the central purpose of accountability is to safeguard and promote the long-term interests and welfare of the company as an entity separate and distinct from its shareholders, not solely or even primarily to maximise shareholder value; (b) the prevailing notion that directors are and should be accountable to shareholders ought not to be endorsed unless it takes into account the central purpose of accountability stated in point (a); and (c) certain shareholders under certain circumstances should be made accountable to the company. This new conception of board and shareholder accountability not only has significant implications for the design and structure of mechanisms for promoting accountability, but also direct implications for the formulation of the key issues to be addressed in corporate governance debates. Theoretical, doctrinal and contextual analysis and methods will be adopted. The focus will be on English company law and corporate governance because the corporate governance laws, policies and practices of other common law jurisdictions, including Hong Kong and Singapore draw their inspiration from the English position. I will write and publish at least four peer-reviewed articles in top-tier journals. 在董事會推進監督和問責制是在公司法和公司治理的核心和關鍵的問題。董事認為是對股東負責。我尋求問責制這一傳統觀念挑戰，股東和探討以下論斷：（一）問責制主要目的是維護和促進公司的長遠利益和福祉作為一個實體的獨立和獨特的從它的股東，不完全或主要股東價值最大化; （二）當時的概念，即董事，並應負責向股東不應該被認可，除非它考慮到問責制點規定的主要目的（一）; （三）在某些情況下某些股東應作出負責任的公司。這種新的董事會和股東問責的概念對設計和促進問責機制結構不僅顯著影響，但對關鍵問題制定有直接影響公司治理的討論加以解決。關鍵，理論，學說，經驗和背景分析和方法將被採納。重點是英國公司法和公司治理，因為公司治理的法律，政策及其他普通法司法管轄區的做法是從英國位置的。這就是說，我也會考慮法律與其他司法管轄區如美國和澳大利亞進行比較的目的的做法。

17665816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17665816.value: This study aims at exploring a cumulative (dis)advantage theory (Merton 1968,1988; Oleksiyenko and Sa 2010) in the light of changes tackled by academic innovators in post-Soviet higher education systems. The study will examine how these innovators have been mitigating systemic and institutional legacies to reduce disadvantages and create new positions of advantage after the departure from the Soviet model of higher education. The analysis will explore legacy-innovation tensions in the academics' efforts to replace excessive bureaucratic control with shared governance, indoctrinated learning with critical thinking, segregated research and teaching with synergies between inquiry and learning, as well as ideological internationalization with meritocracy-driven global outreach. The study will identify critical factors that have been driving some academics to succeed in creating cumulative advantages, while others to continually mitigate disadvantages or end with hybrid effects in the process of innovations. The findings in this project will be informed by a qualitative data analysis of innovative academic practices in China, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, Russia, and Ukraine. In each country, the data set will triangulate inputs from scholarly, institutional and technical assistance reports, self-directed questionnaires, and focus group discussions with academic innovators in social sciences and humanities, natural sciences and engineering, and health sciences. The cross-country analysis will be conducted to identify variances among major drivers of cumulative advantage or disadvantage for the academics who initiated research and teaching innovations discarding the practices and entitlements developed by the Soviet model of higher education and pursuing meritocratic and accountable norms evaluated by scholarly communities internationally. The cross-cultural perspective will provide opportunities to understand specific systemic and institutional interventions managed by the post-Soviet academics on the move from closed to open knowledge development systems. The research will enrich the theory of cumulative advantage in higher education by shedding light on cross-cultural perspectives in the studies of opportunities and challenges generated by innovative practices in the academe. The resultant publications will stimulate scholarly debates on legacy-innovation tensions that tend to emerge in academic practice in general, as well as on challenges of sustaining academic excellence in the systems coming out of political and socio-economic hardships. The study will inform how successes, failures, reversals and hybrid solutions emerge in the times of modernization of professional and institutional norms in post-Soviet universities. Finally, the study will contribute to a better conceptualization of developmental dilemmas and strategies in the post-Soviet academic contexts that are often stigmatized by tensions between legacies and innovations. 高等教育去蘇維埃化：跨文化角度看傳統與創新的張力及累積優(劣)勢 摘要 這項研究旨在根據學術創新者在對應蘇聯解體後高等教育系統的轉變以探索累積優(劣)勢理論（Merton, 1968,1988; Oleksiyenko and Sa, 2010）。本研究將審視這些創新者如何緩解制度和體制的傳統以減少劣勢，同時在高等教育脫離蘇維埃模式後創造新位置的優勢。分析將集中探討學者在成就以共同治理取代過度的官僚​​控制、以批判性思維取代灌輸式學習、以探究與學習的協同作用取代分離的研究與教學、及以精英全球拓展取代意識形態國際化中面對的傳統與創新之間的張力。這項研究將識別出推動一些學者在創造累積優勢成功的關鍵因素，而另一些仍持續緩解劣勢，或結束在創新過程中所產生的混合效果。

17665816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17665816.value: This research project has developed a cross-cultural perspective on the theory of cumulative (dis)advantages in academic research and graduate education by drawing on the experiences of scholars who were subjected to the Soviet model of university administration. While previous studies focused primarily on insights from scholars living and working in successful institutions and sustainable societies, this research project delved into the challenges faced by those in disadvantaged university systems and unstable societies. Hence, it was possible to refine the framework of cumulative effects in academic sciences by examining the practices and lived experiences of scholars immersed in the transition from closed to open systems of knowledge development, and managing legacy-innovation tensions at their universities after the collapse of the Soviet Union. The analytical outcomes of this study point to strong interdependencies between academic legacies and innovations in higher education contexts affected by political and socio-economic transformations. Universities and systems of higher learning can only thrive under stable and sustainable conditions created by the societies in which they exist. Moreover, the reputational and competitiveness capacity of universities is subject to a society’s ability to empower professors and students to freely operate in the complex global networks of science. As the research papers produced as part of this project demonstrate, national higher education systems and universities are able to achieve a sustainable cumulative effect of reputation and academic performance when they do not compromise on academic principles of openness, intellectual freedom, and integrity. The published papers on legacy-innovation tensions, presented in part C of this report, provide a unique perspective on the challenges and shortcomings of post-Soviet universities in the context of global science. The research identifies a range of concerns that researchers in post-Soviet environments have and encourage their international partners to take into consideration when designing methodological approaches for collaborative work in global science. Given that in (post-)totalitarian academic communities retrospective and introspective analyses are often affected by legacies of indoctrination, distrust, and anxiety, it is critical for international partners to be aware of any possible deficiencies of integrity in research, administration and communication. Creating cumulative advantages that enable successful, sustained engagement with global science as well as generate inter-generational learning for such engagement can be a challenge in these communities when resistance to global transparency and internationally peer-reviewed standards of academic excellence persists, and there are few and feeble attempts to counteract parochial dogmas and indoctrination.

17665816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17665816.value: This research has strong potential for further development in the post-truth era. In view of the problems of integrity in research and communication, which diminish the quality of social sciences and humanities, and undermine their ability to facilitate critical inquiry and open discussion in post-totalitarian contexts, research on best practices of academic communities and leaders who advance innovations that stimulate independent and critical thinking and social engagement is crucial. Studying academia in post-totalitarian societies can be a particularly important source of insights to prevent authoritarianism and state failures, and for increasing the sustainability of democratic reforms, the rule of law, and social justice initiatives, which secure global stability. Since legacies have the capacity to either drive academic development or thwart innovation, it is important to continue asking questions, so as to understand how these legacies generate values and impacts on the development of affected societies, thereby making it possible to identify the mechanisms by which positive change can be effected.

17665816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17665816.value: This project advances knowledge about the social and institutional challenges that prevent the reputational development of post-totalitarian universities and constrain their equitable participation in global science. By examining problems faced by professors in post-Soviet systems of higher education, this research develops the theory of legacy-innovation tensions in higher education, in addition to spearheading potential solutions to enable successful academic transformations in post-totalitarian states and post-truth contexts. The study generates constructive resonance and creates impact in societies that are seeking opportunities to establish highly-reputable and innovative universities and academic professions on a local level, and become re-integrated with open systems of knowledge development on a global level.

17666316.label: Realisation of objectives
17666316.value: We completed the proposed longitudinal study. The data collected and results speak directly to the six objectives of this project. DATA COLLECTED A total of 168 Hong Kong Chinese mother-toddler dyads (83 boys; 85 girls) completed the baseline assessment (Time 1) when the toddlers were around 12 months old; 160 of them returned when the toddlers were around 18 months (79 boys; 81 girls) and completed the follow-up assessment (Time 2). The actual sample size at Time 1 exceeded the proposed n=120 by 40%. The attrition rate from Time 1 to Time 2 (< 5%) was substantially lower than the 20% anticipated in the proposal. So, the data collection was quite successful. Each mother-toddler dyad during each visit (Time 1 and Time 2) provided these kinds of data: 1. Mother’s and toddler’s visual attention to pairs of photos of human faces showing different emotions (happy-angry, or happy-fear) displayed on a computer screen. Their looking data were collected with a Tobii T120 Eye Tracker. The preferential-looking paradigm was used to measure their looking behaviors when shown pairs of emotional faces. 2. Mother’s responses to questionnaires about family demographics, maternal anxiety, child temperament. 3. Mother’s and toddler’s behaviors were video-recorded while the mother was filling out the questionnaires and the toddler was playing about 5 feet away on a floor mat with some toys. An adult stranger approached and interacted with the toddler (following the Stranger Anxiety Paradigm; Murray et al., 2008). DATA CODING and PROCESSING 1. Eye-tracking data were processed, and variables of interest (e.g., time to 1st fixation, duration of 1st fixation, number of 1st fixations directed at an angry faces, dwell time for looks directed at angry faces). 2. Maternal and child behaviors video-recorded in the Stranger Anxiety paradigm were coded for parenting behaviors (e.g., intrusiveness, encouragement) and child behaviors (e.g., avoidance upon stranger approach, avoidance when picked up by stranger, fear). Inter-coder reliability was good. 3. Questionnaire data were processed. DATA ANALYSIS Our analyzed the eye-tracking data with widely adopted methodology, and the results are summarized in Section 6.1 Major findings and research outcome. Subsequently, recognized that existing data analysis methods focus on group averaged data rather than individual looking pattern, and temporal information is often overlooked. To overcome these limitations, we started a collaboration with Dr. Janet Hsiao and Antoni Chan, who have developed the Eye Movement analysis with Hidden Markov Models (EMHMM) method that provides quantitative measures of individual eye movement patterns taking both spatial and temporal dimensions of eye movements into account (Chuk, Chan, & Hsiao, 2014;Chuk, Crookes, Hayward, Chan, Hsiao, 2017). We expect to complete the data analysis using EMHMM in October, 2020. RESULTS WRITE-UP: We have already submitted a manuscript to the journal Social Development on the video-recorded maternal and child behaviors in the Stranger Anxiety Paradigm and the maternal questionnaire data. Once the eye-tracking data have been re-analyzed using EMHMM, we will integrate them with the stranger anxiety data and questionnaire data for a fuller account. We expect to have a 2nd journal submission by December 2020.

17666316.label: Major findings and research outcome
17666316.value: 1. Toddlers look to their parents for cues in uncertain situations (i.e., social referencing). Maternal intrusiveness may signal anxiety and danger to toddlers. 12-month olds experiencing more maternal intrusiveness were also more fearful of strangers and generally shyer than those experiencing less. Moreover, path analysis revealed that they became even more so by age 18 months. 2. Maternal low-key encouragement at 12 months predicted reduction in fear/avoidance of strangers 6 months later, although the effect was not as marked as maternal intrusiveness. 3. Parenting behaviors when toddlers interact with a stranger can directly predict developmental changes in stranger anxiety during the second year of life, as well as indirectly mediated by changes in child temperament. 4. Infants with initial-gaze-direction bias and gaze-dwell-time bias for angry faces at age 12 months significantly predicted more avoidance than infants without these bias when approached by a stranger at 18 months, even after controlling for their stranger avoidance at 12 months. Further details about Major Finding #4: ANCOVAs were used to compare infants with vs. without an attention bias for angry faces at age 12 months on their stranger anxiety (Objective 3) and behavioral inhibition (Objective 5) at 18 months, with the respective dependent variable at baseline (age 12 months) as a covariate. Results showed that: Infants with initial gaze direction bias for angry faces at age 12 months showed more avoidance (M = 2.64, SD = 0.10) than infants without this bias (M = 2.38, SD = 0.10) when the stranger approached (F=3.16, p = 0.077) at 18 months after controlling their avoidance at 12 months ; Infants with gaze-dwell-time bias for angry faces at age 12 months showed more avoidance (M = 2.64, SD = 0.10) than infants without this bias (M = 2.34, SD = 0.10) when the stranger approached (F=4.22, p = 0.04) at 18 months after controlling their avoidance at 12 months.

17666316.value: To build on the recently commenced collaboration with Dr. Janet Hsiao and Dr. Antoni Chan, I have begun another collaboration with them to use their Eye Movement analysis with Hidden Markov Models (EMHMM) method to quantify individual eye movement patterns of children with different kinds of developmental disabilities.

17666316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17666316.value: Babies’ avoidance and fear of strangers generally begin around 6 months and peak around 12 months of age. If persistently intense, stranger anxiety may develop into social anxiety. What can be done about babies’ stranger anxiety? Our study revealed that the more mothers intrude (e.g., leaning, gesturing, talking, physical contact)—which can signal anxiety and danger to babies—when their 12-month-olds interact with a friendly stranger, the more fearful of strangers and shyer the babies become around age 18 months. Low-key encouragement (e.g., smiles, nods) seems to have the opposite effect. By tracking babies’ looking patterns (e.g., first gaze, duration of gaze) for angry faces that can signal social threats, we also found that 12-month-olds with stronger looking biases for angry faces were at risk for more intense stranger anxiety by age 18 months. These results suggest that as early as age 1 year, how babies react to social threats (e.g., angry faces) and how their mothers react to strangers approaching and interacting with the babies can affect how intense and persistent stranger anxiety become during the 2nd year of life.

17667116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17667116.value: 幼教老師對早期數學之教與學的想法與實踐： 積木玩耍教學的跨文化比較研究

17667116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17667116.value: 在美國的學前教育，數學引發愈來愈多的關注，主要基於三項因素：（一）當幼兒入讀幼稚園或小學一年級時，已明顯表現出因社會經濟的影響，而造成知識和技能上的差異；（二）近期在幼兒到高中階段，對不同數學範疇之學習軌跡的研究發展；以及（三）美國和亞洲學生的學習成就落差。然而，現今缺乏在學前教育的教室中，提供數學學習機會之相關研究，且多數的研究都與數字相關，幾何和量度卻沒有得到太多的重視。過去只有少數研究嘗試了解因幼年的潛在因素，而導致美國和亞洲學生的成就落差。 是項研究將會描述與比較香港和美國的幼教老師，在積木玩耍的情境下，其對早期數學之教與學的想法，以及積木玩耍能促進特定的益處時教師所扮演的角色。我們亦希冀了解教師自陳的數學教學信念，與我們在實際課堂教學行為觀察的一致性與差異處。是項研究會在香港和美國伊利諾州招募三十位參與者，研究參與者須在課堂使用積木教學、持有早期幼兒教育文憑、教導3至5歲的幼兒。我們會對研究參與者進行一次訪談和兩次積木玩耍之教學的課堂觀察。是項研究所蒐集的資料，將以質性取徑分析訪談的內容之相關主題和類別；以量化取徑分析課堂之觀察。我們亦會以機率來計算益處和角色出現的頻率，藉此了解積木玩耍在自身的文化和跨文化的益處及教師角色之間的關聯。 是項研究對教師培訓有重要的意涵，尤其是針對幼兒數學學習之內容和教學方法的培訓課程。在罕有的幼兒數學之教與學的研究中，是次研究結果將能有所貢獻。此外，透過跨文化研究早期數學之教學，是次研究或許對探索早期幼年因素而導致美國和亞洲學生的成就落差之相關研究帶來長遠的影響。

17667816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17667816.value: 羅馬天主教會由一開始就自許為給全人類的普世宗教。雖然這普世野心受地理所限，一直不出 歐洲文明所影響之地域，但是到了大探索時代，天主教蛻變成為真正的全球宗教。過程中，傳 教士及學者發展出一種「天主教東方主義」，深深影響了全球對歐洲整體的文化想像。天主教 擴張的研究可謂汗牛充棟。可是，雖然知識的視覺化和視覺傳播對天主教發展至為關鍵，對早 期現代藝術在該過程起何作用的研究卻付之闕如。 放在環球背景中的早期現代歐洲藝術歷史，本計劃對該歷史的持續重新書寫作出貢獻。計劃著 眼於十六世紀末至十七世紀初從日本、波斯、剛果等地出使到羅馬的領使，概觀調查和詳細分 析他們如何呈現在紀念碑、繪畫、雕塑、版畫中。迄今為止，要了解天主教環球傳播的視覺文 化，主要透過研究貿易商品和傳教藝術品，在羅馬的視覺文化藝術反倒沒有引起多少學者注意 。雖然跨文化的接觸多是在「邊陲」發生，但是「中心」這概念卻是在羅馬發想與維持的。而 這些權威意象以羅馬為源頭，廣傳於歐洲。本計劃處理在十七世紀首幾十年期間（1622年「傳 佈信仰聖部 」（今「萬民福音聖部」）創立之前），羅馬教宗如何用藝術去定義天主教開拓中 的環球身份。 天主教擴張其一特點是其保持中央集權和階級結構的能力。 凸顯於教宗的象徵和(很多時)實際 權威。在早期現代時期，天主教強烈的中央集權對文化和藝術有重大影響：由於教會的權力集 中，羅馬成為天主教歐洲跟非西方世界接觸的中心，既扮演斡旋的角色，又直接操控雙方接觸 的方式與內容。由於遠道而來的各國領使皆集中於羅馬，所以教宗和各派傳教仕在羅馬謀求能 在此栽培傳教這遼闊的事業。也是在羅馬，巴洛克天主教的全球野心能實現其最絢爛的視覺形 式，如貝尼尼的《四河噴泉》(1648-51)和G.B. 高尼的《耶穌聖名之捷》(1676-79)。 其實羅馬教宗的寰宇觀，在這之前早已以藝術大力宣揚、正傳化丶和傳播 。以上這些作品並非 殊例，而只是其延續而已。 本計劃的重點，歌納茲耶利宮室(又稱「女王宮室」) 中的灰泥壁畫 ，乃波基西保祿五世(1605-21)最具野心的藝術委託案之一。位於奎里納雷宮中的歌納茲耶利宮 室，是教皇接待各國來使和海外貴賓之所。受委託時正值對歐洲以外世界產生濃厚興趣之時， 且更有非洲、中東、和東亞洲人的描繪，可追溯至取材於1616灰泥壁畫創作之前出使羅馬的領 使大臣人像圖。本計劃可望對這重要古迹的圖意學作更新而全面的研究，也望可作為了解羅馬 式生產的繪畫、版畫丶和其他亞丶非裔人物形像的研究起點。這樣做，可對十七世紀初期意大 利藝術史作出貢獻，也望可加深了解羅馬教宗文化政治史中，其早期全球化的關鍵時刻。

17672816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17672816.value: 长期社会排斥和抑郁症状： 人生意义认知的中介机制

17672816.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17672816.value: Dr Lo, Barbara Chuen Yee Dr Poon, Kai Tak

17672816.label: Project Objectives
17672816.value: To test the association between long-term ostracism and depressive symptoms; To examine the mediating role of meaningful existence for the effect of long-term ostracism on depressive symptoms.
rows: To test the association between long-term ostracism and depressive symptoms;
To examine the mediating role of meaningful existence for the effect of long-term ostracism on depressive symptoms.

17672816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17672816.value: Ostracism is defined as being excluded or ignored by groups and individuals. Because people desire positive and lasting social relationships, it is unsurprising that ostracism is detrimental to people’s physical and psychological well-being. The literature has shown that short-term ostracism can lead to various undesirable outcomes, such as it can increase negative mood, reduce social need satisfaction, impair cognitive functioning, and increase antisocial and risk-taking behaviors. However, our knowledge about the impacts of ostracism is still very limited because most of the previous investigations focused on its short-term immediate impacts. Given a significant portion of people in our society may experience or risk long-term ostracism, it is important to examine its potential impacts on people’s well-being. The present research aims to contribute to the literature by testing whether long-term ostracism is associated with depressive symptoms among non-clinical adult population, and whether threatened meaningful existence can mediate the relationship between long-term ostracism and depression. Social relationship is one of the most important sources of meaning. When people experience long-term ostracism, they may perceive a lower presence of meaning in their lives because they question their sense of purpose, self-worth, value and the ability to control their own goals and outcomes. Such threatened feelings of meaningful existence may make ostracized individuals more vulnerable to depression because humans prioritize a presence of meaning in their lives. Therefore, threatened meaningful existence should mediate the potential association between long-term ostracism and depression. When chronically ostracized individuals’ threatened meanings were restored, the association between long-term ostracism and depression should be weakened. A series of studies will be conducted to provide empirical tests to our hypotheses through a multi-method approach. Given the significance of social relationships in influencing our well-being, it is important to examine the potential relationship between long-term ostracism and depressive symptoms, and to examine how to weaken the association between long-term ostracism and depression. A better understanding of why long-term ostracism influences depression and how to effectively weaken this detrimental relationship can guide the development of intervention programs aiming at helping people cope with the pain of long-term ostracism. The present research can also benefit society in areas of promoting a positive social environment and provide guidance for facilitating social interactions among members in local and international communities, schools, and organizations. 社会排斥指人体被群体和他人排斥或忽视的社会现象。因为人们渴望积极和持久的社会关系，所以社会排斥会对生理和心理健康带来负面影响。过往二十年的研究表明，短期的社会排斥会导致各种不良后果，它可以增加负面情绪，减少社会需求的满意度，损害认知功能，以及增加反社会和冒险行为。大多数以前的研究集中于社会排斥的短期直接影响，这不能充分反映社会排斥对个体的影响。许多人在日常生活中经历长期排斥或有被长期排斥的风险，因此， 研究长期排斥对个体的影响是个重要课题。本研究关注长期排斥是否会诱发普通（非临床）成年人的抑郁症状。 本研究进一步关注社会排斥如何影响抑郁症状。社会关系是人生意义的重要来源。经历长期排斥，人们容易怀疑自我价值及存在意义。同时，对人生意义的怀疑容易诱发抑郁症状。因此，对生命意义的认识应该调解长期排斥和抑郁症之间的潜在联系。本研究采用多重方法检验我们的研究假设。具体而言，本研究探讨长期排斥与抑郁症状之间的潜在关系。更好地理解为什么长期排斥影响抑郁症状，可以指导发展干预计划帮助人们更好地应对长期被排斥潜在的影响。另外， 本研究还可以为促进本地及国际社区，学校和组织成员之间的健康互动提供指导。

17672816.label: Realisation of objectives
17672816.value: In our grant application, four objectives were proposed. The panel suggested us to work on the first two objectives. And the duration of the project was 12 months (an extension of 6 months was granted later). Objective 1: To test the association between long-term ostracism and depressive symptoms We tested the association between long-term ostracism and depressive symptoms. Our research provided converging evidence that ostracism or being excluded/ignored is associated with depressive symptoms. Objective 2: To examine the mediating role of meaningful existence for the effect of long-term ostracism on depressive symptoms. We tested the proposed mediating role of meaningful existence and found evidence consistent with our prediction, such that long-term ostracism decreases people’s perceived meaning in life which further leads to depressive symptoms.

17672816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17672816.value: Major findings: First, although the literature on loneliness has repeated shown its association with depressive symptoms and suicidal thoughts, the literature on ostracism (being ignored or excluded) has not paid enough attention to how ostracism is related to depression and suicidal thoughts. Our research showed, with converging evidence, that ostracism is associated with depressive symptoms (Jiang & Chen, 2019) and it can lead to suicidal thoughts (Chen, Poon, DeWall, & Jiang, 2019). Second, according to Baumeister’s model of meaning (1991), humans prioritize a presence of meaning in their lives, and ostracism or rejection reduces perceived meaning in life. And past research has shown that lower levels of belonging are linked to lower levels of perceived meaning in life (Lambert et al., 2013; Stillman et al., 2009). Our research continued this line of research to examine the role of perceived meaning in life in accounting for people’s responses following ostracism. Jiang and Chen (2019) showed that perceived meaning in life accounts the association between ostracism and depressive symptoms, and Chen et al (2018) found that perceived meaning in life mediates the effect of ostracism on suicidal thoughts. Third, we further examined whether our reported effect can be moderated. Jiang and Chen (2019) showed that self-compassion, a personal trait that involves extending compassion to oneself in instances of perceived inadequacy, failure, or general suffering, can mitigate depressive symptoms associated with ostracism. And Chen et al (2019) found that self-affirmation, a brief intervention of affirming one’s core values, is effective in reduce suicidal thoughts following ostracism. Major research outcome: The duration of this project is rather short. So far, we have produced two manuscripts which are under revision and resubmission: one at Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (3rd round of revision and submission) and another at Journal of Social Psychology (2nd round of revision and resubmission; see Part C). In addition, findings of the project will be presented at the 2019 World Congress on Psychological Science (WCPS) this November in Vienna, Austria. Further, the project supported the training of one PhD student, Tonglin Jiang, and one Mphil student, Enci Zhang.

17672816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17672816.value: Our studies primarily focused on the role of perceived meaning in life for the negative responses (e.g.., depressive symptoms and suicidal thoughts) following ostracism. Situational factors, which ought to moderate our reported effect of ostracism, were not examined. Ostracism from significant others can be more distressing than ostracism from strangers or less important others. Also, being ostracized by one’s society or community should be more detrimental, thus leads to stronger negative consequences, relative to being ostracized by individuals. In future studies, we will examine how these situation factors contribute to depressive symptoms following ostracism. In addition, we did not directly manipulate perceived meaning in life in our studies. To understand the mechanism of an observed effect, the manipulation of the proposed mediator is in general preferred over the measurement of the mediator. Yet, it can be challenging to manipulate the mediator precisely (Spencer, Zanna, & Fong, 2005; Bullock, Green, & Ha, 2010; Pirott & MacKnnon, 2017), as perceived meaning in life is highly intertwined with constructs (e.g., life satisfaction, positive affect, etc.). We aim to discover an effective approach to manipulate people’s perceived meaning in life in future research.

17672816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17672816.value: Human beings have an innate drive to maintain positive and long-lasting social relationships. When the feeling of belonging is threatened, people can experience pain and engage in self-defeating behaviors. Our investigation further examined whether and under what conditions ostracism would lead to depressive symptoms. More importantly, we focused on the role of people’s perceived meaning in life in account for the association between ostracism and depressive symptoms. Responses following ostracism were extensively studied during the last two decades. And many mechanisms were proposed to explain why people respond to ostracism in certain ways. Although scholars concur that to feel belonged is critical for perceived meaning in life. The role of meaning in accounting for responses following ostracism was relatively neglected. Our research highlighted the significance of meaning in understanding how people respond to ostracism. Our research further showed that self-affirmation (Chen, Poon, DeWall, & Jiang, 2019) and self-compassion (Jiang & Chen, 2019) moderate negative responses following ostracism. These findings suggest that interesting future directions in developing simple yet effective interventions in countering the negative responses following ostracism.

17673216.label: Realisation of objectives
17673216.value: The proposed two objectives have been fully achieved. More precisely, we have achieved more than the proposed objectives, which were indicated by the research outcomes (over 16 peer-review journal articles), the number of participants tested, the number of tasks designed, and the number of successful completion of final-year dissertations and theses by our research postgraduate students. The details are summarized below. First, we proposed to assess statistical learning of 180 Hong Kong Cantonese-speaking children (60 dyslexics and 60 age-matched controls from Grade 4, and 60 reading-level matched controls from Grades 2). With the enthusiastic support from local parents and the great endeavour of our research team, we tested 424 Cantonese-speaking children with developmental dyslexia (Grad 2: N= 125; Grade 3: N=112; Grade 4: N = 102; Grade 5: N =57; Grade 6: N = 28), and 595 typically developing children for reading-level and age-matched controls (Grade 1: N = 119; Grade 2: N = 132; Grade 3: N = 181; Grade 4: N = 174; Grade 5: N =82; Grade 6: N = 44). Since each participant was individually tested and at least two hours was needed for each participant, our team has worked extremely hard for the last four years, and have managed to complete such a large-scale project successfully. Second, with the support of the GRF fund, we were able to develop a few authentic and influential statistical learning tests that can be used to precisely evaluate statistical learning capacities of Chinese children with developmental dyslexia. Specifically, we have developed and validated four visual statistical learning tests including visual linguistic and non-linguistic statistical learning (learning of positional, phonetic and semantical regularities) and two auditory tasks including auditory non-linguistic and linguistic statistical learning, tone identification with noise, and tone discrimination. These tests have been developed on the basis of Chinese visual-orthographic features and tonal language features, and they are available for the direct use of assessment for Chinese children with developmental dyslexia. The details of these tests are described below. General and Chines-specific Visual Statistical Learning Tests: 1)Visual Triplet statistical learning test: It consisted of 12 newly invented figures that were formed by combining characteristics of two or more common shapes (e.g., circle, star, triangle, rectangle, arrow, cross, ellipse, hexagon, and diamond). These 12 figures were grouped into four triplets. Participants were presented with a stream of figures in the familiarization phase and they were asked to extract the embedded temporal order from the familiarization phase. 2)Visual Chinese-Specific Statistical Learning-Positional Regularity Learning: This test consisted of 30 pseudocharacters that were created using Geba characters, the ancient Chinese scripts used by the Naxi minority in west China in the seventh century, which are completely unfamiliar to our Hong Kong participants. Three levels positional consistency (100%, 75%, and 50%) of radicals was systematically manipulated. 3)Visual Chinese-Specific Statistical Learning-Phonetic Regularity Learning: This test consisted of 20 left-right structured pseudocharacters—five for each of the four phonetic consistency levels: high [100%], moderate [80%], low [60%], and random [20%]—were created by using Geba characters as the target phonetic and control radicals. Participants were presented with pseudocharacter-sound mapping for pseudocharacters with different consistency level. Participants were asked to identify the sound that matched the learned phonetic radicals. 4)Visual Chinese-Specific Statistical Learning-Semantic Regularity Learning: It consisted of 15 pseudocharacters that were created by using Dongba scripts and the level of consistency (100%, 75%, and 50%) of mappings between semantic radical and pictures. Participants were exposed to the pseudocharacters comprising target semantic radicals and the pictures. In the recognition and generalization tests, participants were asked to select the picture that matched the learned semantic radicals. General and Chines-specific Auditory Statistical Learning Tests: 1) Auditory Linguistic Statistical Learning: An artificial language was created using six pseudosyllables and four tones. In each block, each of the six pseudosyllables appeared four times, forming 24 tokens which were concatenated together in random order to form a continuous stream of tonal pseudosyllables. In the recognition test, participants were presented with the tonal syllable which they had been exposed to in the familiarization phase (i.e. word), and the other one which the participants had not been exposed to but was composed of the same pseudosyllables and tones in a different combination (i.e. non-word). They were asked to decide whether the tonal pseudosyllables presented in the test appeared in the previous familiarization phase. 2)Auditory Non-linguistic Statistical Learning: The stimuli consisted of non-linguistic sounds that were created using sinusoidal waves. In each block, each of the six pseudosyllables appeared four times, forming 24 tokens which were concatenated together in random order to form a continuous stream of tonal pseudosyllables. In the recognition test, participants were asked to identify the token that previously appeared in the familiarization phase. Third, with the GRF funding support, two final-year undergraduate dissertation students Marco Fong Tsz Ho, Marco and Sana Ng Mei Shuen have accomplished two final-year dissertations regarding statistical learning in Chinese children with developmental dyslexia. Marco’s dissertation focused on examining visual non-linguistic and linguistic statistical learning of children with dyslexia in Chinese. His dissertation showed that Children with dyslexia exhibited significant impairment in both non-linguistic statistical learning and linguistic statistical learning, specifically on the learning of phonetic regularities, compared with chronological-age matched controls. Sana Ng’s dissertation targeted at auditory linguistic and non-linguistic statistical learning in Cantonese children with developmental dyslexia. She found that Chinese children with developmental dyslexia exhibited deficits in auditory statistical learning of tone sequence as compared with typically developing age-matched controls. Our PhD student Lee Man Kit, Stephen was trained to examine whether and, if so, how statistical learning affects Chinese character writing of Hong Kong Chinese children with and without developmental dyslexia in Grades 2 to 5. His analyses showed that when compared with age-matched controls, children with developmental dyslexia were less sensitive to statistical properties of radicals and exhibited prolonged use of phonology at the character level as grade level advanced. Furthermore, the children with developmental dyslexia relatively relied more on phonology at the radical level than younger, reading level-matched children. These findings underscored the role of statistical learning in character writing and showed that the prolonged use and overreliance on phonology in character writing by Chinese children with developmental dyslexia may reflect their difficulties in statistical learning (Lee & Tong, under review). On the basis of this project, we have conducted a systematic meta-analysis examining statistical learning deficits in children with developmental dyslexia across different writing systems and different task paradigms (Lee, Cui, & Tong, submitted).

17673216.label: Major findings and research outcome
17673216.value: Based on the large scale of the data, we have found that relative to reading-level and age-matched controls, Chinese children with developmental dyslexia were impaired in statistical learning when the number of exposures to a repeated sequence was small (He & Tong, 2016). Moreover, these children with dyslexia performed significantly worse than their age-matched controls on both the visual statistical learning tasks. Visual statistical learning was significantly associated with orthographic awareness and word reading, which suggested that visual statistical learning deficits may be related to disrupted orthographic learning abilities, thereby contributing to their reading difficulties (Tong, Leung, & Tong, 2019). With regard to Chinese-specific visual statistical learning tasks, Chinese children with developmental dyslexia exhibited positional regularity learning performance that was comparable to the controls. However, those children showed difficulties in mapping a given sound or meaning to a specific character compared with the typically developing controls (Tong, Zhang, & He, in press). Additionally, Chinese children with developmental dyslexia also performed worse in auditory linguistic SL than their age-matched control, but not in non-linguistic auditory statistical learning. Together, our findings suggest that children with dyslexia have deficits in some, though not all, aspects of statistical learning of character orthography, which may reflect their difficulties in coping with distractors and inconsistency of orthographic input. These findings have all been published or accepted to be published in internationally prestigious, peer-reviewed journals.

17673216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17673216.value: Given the constraint of our cross-sectional design of the present project, future longitudinal research should further explore whether atypical statistical learning strategies exhibited by children with dyslexia are the sources of their reading difficulties. One possible extension of the current project is to conduct a longitudinal study by following those children at family risk of dyslexia. This would allow us to determine whether children’s early deficits in statistical learning is a potential cause of later reading difficulties. It should be also noted that the present study has focused on exploring whether, and if so, how Chinese children with developmental dyslexia exhibited statistical learning difficulties. The present project focused on assessment only, and a new avenue of this research is to conduct an intervention study by exploring whether training statistical learning can promote the development of reading skills. In fact, our team has started pursuing this direction by providing randomized control trial on those children with developmental dyslexia.

17673216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17673216.value: Our project addressed a broad question concerning the role of distributional statistical learning, or learning based on the frequency and variability of input exemplars, in reading difficulties. We asked whether and, if so, how Chinese children with developmental dyslexia extract Chinese-specific orthographic statistical properties, such as positional, phonetic, and semantic consistencies, from a nonalphabetic Chinese orthography. These questions are important because approximately 10% of the world’s school-age children have dyslexia. Understanding the source of reading difficulties can help make early diagnosis and remediation possible. Because of its quasi-regularity and rich distributional structure, Chinese provides a fascinating window into the role of statistical learning in reading acquisition. We found that Chinese children with dyslexia demonstrated intact statistical learning of positional regularity, but showed difficulties in phonetic and semantic regularities compared with their typically developing controls. These results show for the first time that children with dyslexia have deficits in some, though not all, aspects of statistical learning of character orthography, which may reflect their difficulties in coping with distractors and inconsistency of orthographic input. This finding is critical to parents, school teachers, and clinical practitioners by suggesting that consistent orthographic input may be the key to improving those children’s reading difficulties.

17675816.label: Project Objectives
17675816.value: Trace the genealogy of the term teito (imperial capital), including its usage in official and popular discourse, from the 1880s to the 1930s. Illuminate the relationship between modernity and urban space, with particular attention to the spatial inflections of Japanese imperial power. Develop a comparative understanding of Tokyo in relation to other imperial capitals. Document the connections between Tokyo and colonial cities in East Asia, particularly the movement of writers, artists, and intellectuals between the colonies and the metropole. Discover how writers engaged with other mediums, such as film and photography, to express the experience of the modern city. Explore the history of the neighborhoods, sites, and buildings that appear in literary representations of Tokyo. What parts of the city do authors describe, and how does these literary geographies respond to the image of Tokyo as an imperial capital?

17675816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17675816.value: The primary aim of this project is to understand the different ways in which writers, artists, and government officials imagined the city of Tokyo in the age of Japanese imperialism. During the period of rapid modernization that followed the Meiji Restoration in 1868, the Japanese capital underwent a dramatic transformation. Edo, the seat of shogunal power for over two hundred and fifty years, became Tokyo, the capital of the Empire of Japan. What visions of the city shaped this transformation? What did it mean for the city to become a modern imperial capital? And how did individuals respond to these changes? Employing an intercultural and interdisciplinary methodology, I will argue for a comparative understanding of Tokyo as an imperial capital (teito). I will consider the city in relation to other imperial capitals, such as London, Paris, and Berlin. Like Tokyo, these cities were emblematic of modernity, and functioned as symbolic sites for displays of imperial power. At the same time, I will also examine the connections between Tokyo and colonial capitals in East Asia, such as Seoul and Taipei. The links between Tokyo and these cities depended on the circulation of labor and capital, sustained by the colonial system. I argue that these connections are visible not only in the grand visions of Tokyo espoused by the political elites, but also in literary representations of the city. I will situate these representations of Tokyo in relation to rapid technological development, burgeoning discourses of architecture and urban planning, and an emergent visual culture rooted in the experience of the modern city. Engaging with cartographic, photographic, and filmic representations of urban space, I will explore the different ways in which authors navigated and imagined Tokyo. How do these writers contest or unsettle the image of Tokyo as an imperial capital? How do other places inform their writing of Tokyo? In what ways does Tokyo’s past affect the physical form and cultural particularity of the present? This study will break ground in the fields of modern Japanese literature, urban studies, and cultural history. Culminating in a research monograph, my project will attend to the spatial dimensions of modernity and imperialism, revealing the different ways in which cities are experienced, lived, and imagined. 本研究的目標是了解多樣的大日本帝國時代的東京觀念。 1868年的明治維新以來，東京急速現代化。幕府首都的江戶變成大日本帝國首都的東京。這變化是由於什麼樣的都市計畫？成為「帝都」是什麼意思？作家與畫家怎麼想像這個東京？ 使用跨文化與跨學科的方法，我支持比較的觀念為了形容帝都東京。一方面，我分析帝都東京和帝都倫敦，巴黎，柏林的關係。如東京一樣，這些城市象徵摩登與帝國主義。另一方面，我也分析帝都東京和殖民首都臺北與首爾的關係。這關係依靠帝國主義下的資本與勞工流通。 我認為這種都市關係不但在都市計畫可見，而且在文學中的都市描寫也明顯。 我研究的「文學的都市」反映同時代的技術發展，建築論，與視覺藝術。參考地圖，照片，電影等，我分析作家怎麼想像東京。他們怎麼反對或批評「帝都東京」的觀念？ 東京的過去與現在有什麼關係？別地方對東京有什麼影響？ 這研究開創新發現在多個學科：日本近代文學，城市研究，文化史。我所寫的專著探索近代性與帝國主義所創造的空間，分析各式各種的都市經驗。
