17675816.label: Major findings and research outcome
17675816.value: My project has examined Tokyo as an imperial capital (teito), showing how the city’s dramatic growth in the early twentieth century coincided with the expansion of the Japanese empire. As an intercultural and interdisciplinary endeavor, my project has broken ground in the fields of modern East Asian literature, urban studies, and cultural history. By reimagining Tokyo as an imperial capital, I offer a provocative new way of thinking about a city that has been the focus of scholarship on Japanese literature and Japanese modernity. My comparative approach has revealed significant connections between the colonies and the metropole, positing Tokyo both as a symbolic center of Japanese imperial power and as a key site for the experience of modernity in East Asia.

17675816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17675816.value: As an object of scholarly inquiry, Tokyo offers many opportunities for further exploration. While my research spans the Meiji (1868–1912), Taishō (1912–1926), and early Shōwa (1926–1989) eras, I have concentrated on a period of approximately two decades, from the Great Kantō Earthquake (Kantō daishinsai) in 1923 to the Great Tokyo Air Raid (Tōkyō daikūshū) in 1945. There is more research to be done on the history, literature, and visual culture of the city before and after this period. Furthermore, additional comparative research on empire and modernity is needed to understand more fully the connections between Tokyo and other cities in Asia, Europe, and the rest of the world.

17675816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17675816.value: In the years of rapid modernization that followed the Meiji Restoration of 1868, the Japanese capital underwent a profound transformation. Edo, the seat of the shogunate’s power for over two hundred and fifty years, became Tokyo, the capital of the nascent Empire of Japan. What did it mean for this city to become an imperial capital (teito)? My project uncovers traces of Tokyo’s imperial past in the literature of the city, focusing on a period punctuated by two disasters: the 1923 Great Kantō Earthquake and the 1945 Great Tokyo Air Raid. I reimagine Tokyo as an imperial capital through a comparative reading of Japanese, Taiwanese, and Korean texts. Through archival research, I situate these literary texts in relation to a rich visual culture of modern urban life, including maps, photographs, films, illustrations, and woodblock prints. The resulting image of Tokyo brings to life a formative period in the city’s history that has been obscured in the postwar era.

17675916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17675916.value: Spanning the period from 1884 to 1942, this project will investigate how foreign missionaries, native converts, and government officials manipulated the ambiguities in Korean Christianity’s status as both “Korean” and “Christian” to enforce their respective visions for this religion on the peninsula. This work offers a corrective to the conventional practice of emphasizing the agency of Koreans in the transformation of Christianity from a foreign to “Korean” religion. Though Koreans certainly had agency, a fixation on native actors has led to an elision of the global influences that have informed the development of Christianity in the country. In particular, during the “open ports” period (1876-1910) and the Japanese colonial era (1910-1945), missionaries and government officials possessed both the means and desire to shape Christianity’s presence on the peninsula. For these reasons, simplistic binary frameworks that emphasize native agency fail to fully capture the transformation of Christianity from a foreign to Korean religion. The central argument of this work will be that the creation of the category Korean Christianity was a product of a struggle between missionaries, converts, and officials to define how this religion should be structured and practiced. Though these three groups operated with competing interests, the Western practice of linking “freedom of religion” to modernity and the concept of Christian universalism required that these three groups act in partnership and discounted violence as a legitimate means of struggle. Instead, these three groups manipulated the dual discourses of union and separation to advance their goals. Specifically, they called both for union, based on transnational solidarity, and separation, justified by national division, as they maintained that they were united in goals but separated in functions. Supposedly when each adhered to their respective sphere of legitimate action then a harmony of purpose could be achieved. However, the language of partnership was equally, if not more, effective in creating hierarchies of unequal and coercive power relations. Reinterpreting key events in Korean history, including the Kapsin Coup (1882), the Educational Rights Conflict (1915-1919), the March First Independence Movement (1919), and Shinto Shrine Obesience for Christian institutions (1931-1942), this project explores the strategies employed by missionaries, converts, and officials to assert their authority to control Chrisitanity on the peninsula. Ignoring this dynamic and process not only limits our understanding of the formative years of this religion’s development in Korea, but also limits our understanding of how many Christian communities in South Korea operate today.

17675916.label: Realisation of objectives
17675916.value: I am currently in the final stages of meeting or exceeding all of my project objectives. The only objective that I have not met to date is the production of one monograph and two articles. I have one article published by the Journal of Korean Religions on this research project published in 2019. The Journal of Korean Religions is the premier English language journal on religions in Korea. My book monograph is currently under contract at the University of Hawai'i Press. This press is one of the leading presses for Korean Studies. Furthermore, it is the leading press for studies on religion and Christianity in Korea. I have one article under second review at the Journal of Korean Studies. This journal is the premier English language journal on Korean Studies. My first set of reader reports were highly favorable. The suggested reviews were minor. I revised the manuscript and hope to receive a positive result soon. I have one more article under review based on this research project. This article is a contribution to a special issue for the Korea Journal on missionaries during the Korean War period. The Korea Journal is also an English language journal and considered to be one of the leading journals in the field of Korean Studies. The common theme of all my research outputs is that viewing the history of Christianity in terms of native agency is insufficient to capture its complexities and development. My outputs have done this by reincorporating missionaries into the examination of Korean Christianity. The problem of balancing between religious and political citizenship caused friction between missionaries and Korean Christians. At the same time, however, the language of Christian universalism also provided a means for these fractious relations to be reimagined and reformed. My outputs stress that this is a major aspect of daily life for religious actors in the modern world. In addition to my outputs, I have also been active in participating in international conferences and giving talks abroad. I organized a panel for AAS-in-Asia (June 2017) and the Annual Meeting of AAS held in Washington, DC (March 2018). I also organized a panel for the Annual Meeting of AAS to be held in Boston, MA (March 2020). Though the presentation falls outside of this GRF period, the paper I will present is based on the research I conducted during this GRF period. In addition, I was also invited to prevent my work at the "New Geopolitical Order in East Asia and the Transformation of Christianity Conference" held at Ewha University (December 2018). I have also been invited to give public talks at Colgate University (Hamilton, NY) and SUNY-Binghamton (Binghamton, NY). Though these talks will be given in March 2020, the presentations will be based on researched I conducted during this GRF period. Through these venues, I have been able to engage the international community on my research. Finally, I have given numerous interviews to local and international newspapers and journals on religion in South Korea. In particular, given the recent Coronavirus crisis, I have fielded a number of interviews for El Pais and Quartz Magazine on the relationship between religion and government in South Korea.

17675916.label: Major findings and research outcome
17675916.value: My research has found that the history of Korean Christianity cannot be fully understood in national terms. An understanding of the international networks through which Korean churches and Christian actors operated is key to comprehending the development and growth of this religion, which significantly one scholar of Brazilian Christian has dubbed a regionally Christian superpower. In particular, my research has demonstrated that one aspect to everyday life for religious actors in the modern period and in modern societies is balancing the demands of belonging to both religious and political communities. Both Christianity and nation-states place totalizing demands on members. Importantly, Christianity was a minority religion in Korea during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The Korean and, after colonization, Japanese governments viewed this religion as a potential threat to their power and rule. My research demonstrates the complex processes and strategies members of minority religions, or rather religions that state powers view as potential threats, to reconcile these competing demands. Key to my research findings is the demonstration of how Christians actors move back and forth between political and religious identities in order to achieve certain objectives (religious or political) or mitigate potential risks (religious or political). I argue that this process continues to the present day. Indeed, another finding of my research is that the unequal power relations between missionaries and Korean Christians and the influence of the state continued well beyond 1945. As scholars of religious studies have repeatedly emphasized, the secularization thesis, or argument that religion would become a limited or insignificant part of the public sphere as societies became more "modern," is false. Religion and religious actors continue to be visible and often powerful forces in the public sphere and politics. This is especially true in South Korea. My research offers scholars one paradigm to understand how religious actors negotiate the tensions that exist between political and religious citizenship in the modern period

17675916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17675916.value: This research will flow naturally into other research projects. The next project I plan to pursue concerns faith-based humanitarian aid work in South Korea. Though the Japanese repatriated missionaries in 1942, they returned in force after 1945. Because of the division of the peninsula and the Cold War, missionaries quickly regained positions of influence. A similar process of balancing between religious and political communities would inform these relationships. However, moving forward, I hypothesize that at least one major difference must be accounted for. In short, the function and shape of Christianity shifted in the Western world rapidly after 1945. In part as a reaction to imperialism or colonialism, many Western Christian churches became increasing sensitive to avoiding perceptions of acting in an imperialistic manner. Furthermore, these church institutions felt increased pressure to focus on humanitarian aid. This was because the 1945 period witnessed the rise of private and voluntary humanitarian aid organizations. Mission organizations no longer held a monopoly over the provision of aid and access to the West in countries like South Korea. This would shape the influence of mission societies.

17675916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17675916.value: Scholars of Korean Christianity conventionally have approached the study of this religion in terms of nationalism. The focus has been on how Koreans used this religion to struggle against Japanese colonialism. While not without merit, this line of inquiry has overlooked the transnational aspect of Christianity's development in Korea. By reincorporating missionaries more critically into the study of Korean Christianity, this work provides a more nuanced and complex understanding of this religion. The major significance of this work is calling attention to a fundamental struggle that many who belong to a religious community face in the modern period. Balancing the demands of both religious and political community is a constant source of tension today. Regardless of whether one is a Christian, Buddhist, or Muslim--just to name a few religions--religious and political demands often are at odds.

17676216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17676216.value: Visual crowding limits the otherwise robust object recognition in human peripheral vision. Objects presented to peripheral vision become unrecognizable when they are surrounded by flankers in crowding. Despite its important role in understanding object recognition, the mechanisms behind visual crowding are still not well understood, especially when English letters are used as the targets. Studies in letter crowding typically compare recognition accuracy or contrast threshold for recognition between single and crowded conditions. However, such measures fail to differentiate crowding from other ways of reducing recognizability. Crowding with non-letter stimuli has shown that crowding not only reduces recognizability, but also changes the appearance of the target. Although crowding is also believed to change the appearance of letter targets, it has not been empirically tested. Here we propose to study letter crowding through examining the error distributions. Some pairs of letters are more confusable with each other than other pairs in letter recognition. If crowding changes the appearance of letter targets, it should change the letter confusability as well. In particular, we hypothesize that errors become more evenly distributed among all alternatives in letter crowding. The current research plan consists of two studies. In Study 1, we will examine the error distributions in crowding with different types of flankers. It is often observed that crowding strength increases with target-flanker similarity. We will test the hypothesis that errors in a crowded letter recognition task become more evenly distributed as target-flanker similarity increases. In Study 2, we will examine the error distributions in crowding with increasing target-flanker distance, which is the most robust way to manipulate crowding strength. We will test the hypothesis that recognition errors become less evenly distributed as target-flanker distance increases. Results from the new method of recognition error analysis in this proposed project will further our understanding of visual crowding. 視覺擁擠使原本非常穩健的物件識別能力在週邊視覺變得很有限。當一件物件被投放在週邊視野，並且被其他物件圍繞着的時候，視覺擁擠就會使這物件變得難於被識別。雖然明白物件如何能夠被識別是很重要，但我們對視覺擁擠如何運作的理解卻很少，尤其當牽涉的物件是英文字母時。有關字母擁擠的研究通常會比較單一字母出現的情況和字母被擁擠的情況下，字母識別的準確性或字母識別所需要的亮度對比會有甚麼變化。然而，這些比較的測度並不能將視覺擁擠從其他同樣會使物件變得難以識別的情況分辨出來。當用到的是非字母物件時，視覺擁擠不單使物件變得難以識別，亦會改變物件的模樣。雖然視覺擁擠理應同樣改變字母的模樣，但暫時並未有被實證檢驗過。正因如此，我們在此提議透過觀察字母識別中的誤差分佈來研究字母擁擠。在字母識別中，一些字母彼此會比較容易被混淆。如果字母擁擠確實會改變字母的模樣，同時亦應該會帶來字母間混淆度的轉變。我們推測字母擁擠會使識別誤差更平均地分佈在不同的可能答案中。我們的研究計劃包括兩個系列的實驗。在系列（一）中，我們將會觀察字母在被不同類型物件圍繞的情況下的識別誤差分佈。過去的研究發現：當目標物件和鄰近物件的相似度增加時，視覺擁擠的强度往往會隨着增加。因此，我們推測在字母擁擠中，當目標物件和鄰近物件的相似度增加時，識別誤差亦會更平均地分佈在不同的可能答案中。改變目標物件和鄰近物件之間的距離是最有效改變視覺擁擠强度的方法。在系列（二）中，我們將會觀察當目標物件和鄰近物件之間的距離改變時，字母識別誤差的分佈會如何相應改變。我們推測當目標物件和鄰近物件之間的距離減短時，識別誤差亦會更平均地分佈在不同的可能答案中。我們所提出對識別誤差分佈的分析將會加深我們對視覺擁擠的理解。

17676216.label: Realisation of objectives
17676216.value: A detailed report is attached in Part C. Objective 1. To examine the error distribution in letter crowding. We finished two psychophysical experiments investigating how error distribution changed in letter crowding. We proposed using entropy of the letter confusion matrix as a measure of crowding strength. Consistent with our hypothesis, errors became more randomly distributed in letter crowding. The effects of crowding on error distribution were quantified and summarized through the entropy measure. The two experiments laid the foundation for subsequent experiments. Objective 2. To investigate the effects of target-flanker similarity on error distribution in letter crowding. We finished two psychophysical experiments examining the effects of target-flanker similarity on error distribution in letter crowding. Target-flanker similarity was manipulated through using letters or Arabic numerals as flankers in letter crowding or changing the contrast polarity of the flankers. We found that error distribution in letter crowding became more random as target-flanker similarity decreased. Objective 3. To investigate the effects of target-flanker distance on error distribution in letter crowding. We finished one psychophysical experiment examining the effects of target-flanker distance on error distribution in letter crowding. We found that error distribution in letter crowding became more random as target-flanker distance decreased.

Entropy in a letter confusion matrix was a valid measure of crowding strength, and could potentially provide more information about the mechanisms of crowding. 3. 17676216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17676216.value: Findings from the experiments supported by this grant laid an important foundation for further understanding of letter crowding. Error patterns provide valuable information about the decision-making process in letter crowding. Further studies can follow up on modeling the error patterns in letter crowding. Models derived according to different theories of crowding can be tested and compared.

17676216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17676216.value: This project aims to understand how visual information about a target object is lost or degraded when the target is presented in a visual clutter. We proposed examining the errors observers made in a letter recognition task to understand how a target letter was perceived in isolation or with flanking letters presented next to the target. We conducted five behavioral experiments to examine the errors patterns in a letter recognition task under different conditions. Our findings laid important and necessary foundation for further investigation of the visual process in object recognition. Such investigation can have important clinical implications on helping people with visual impairments recognize objects better even in a visual clutter.

17676316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17676316.value: Uneven temporal and spatial distribution of water resources, coupled with entrenched regional inequalities, has resulted in escalating trans-boundary water conflicts between and among an enlarging group of stakeholders in China. Since the beginning of the reform era, China’s water governance system has faced serious challenges in maintaining the sustainability of basin-wide ecological systems. To tackle such challenges, a variety of water Ecological Compensation Mechanisms (ECMs) and water conservation projects have been implemented in the last two decades. However, very little research has been conducted to critically evaluate the extent to which ECMs’ institutional set-ups fit with local conditions. It is also not clear in regard to the questions of what pre-conditions, and what formal and informal activities, are considered necessary and sufficient for the successful implementation of water ECMs. The proposed research aims at investigating the institutional properties of water ECMs and examining the problems of, as well as counter-measures to tackling, institutional misfits through a case study of the Dongjiang (East River) in southern China. Dongjiang has been inflicted by intensifying water conflicts between the urban and rural sectors, between upstream and downstream jurisdictions, and between providers of ecosystems services and the beneficiaries of such services. Using questionnaire surveys and in-depth semi-structured interviews, this study will examine the implementation and outcomes of water ECMs in Dongjiang’s watershed, at both the intra-provincial scale and inter-provincial levels. The analytical framework of institutional fit and interplay will be used to inform the research design and analysis. In particular, the research will examine and contrast the institutional properties of formal policies and informal strategies associated with the implementation of water ECMs. It will investigate the questions of how, and to what extent, water ECMs have impacted local ecology and society. The key variables associated with the outcomes of water ECMs will be identified through testing several hypotheses that pertain to (i) formal rules on boundaries of rights; (ii) monitoring, rewarding and sanctioning systems; and (iii) informal co-opting strategies. Through a critical analysis of water ECMs already implemented in Dongjiang, the research will produce a diagnosis of the institutional fit and interplay between water ECMs and their socio-economic and bio-physical contexts. An assessment of their social and ecological outcomes will also be conducted. The findings will help decision-makers to formulate a more effective approach to undertaking institutional reform and achieving the goal of long-term sustainability in governing China’s trans-boundary water resources. 中國的水資源時空分佈不均，加上長久以來的區域不平等，跨界衝突在數量日漸增多的持份者之間因而加劇。自改革開放，中國的水資源管治在維持整體流域生態系統的可持續發展方面一直面對嚴峻的挑戰。中國爲處理此挑戰，在過去二十年間推行各種生態補償機制及水利項目。然而，甚少調查曾針對生態補償機制的體制設定與地區情況的配合程度作出評估。所以，要成功推行水資源生態補償機制所需的先決條件目前仍未明確。 本研究項目旨在探討水資源生態補償的制度特點，通過對東江流域的現況的分析，探討體制錯配的問題及其解決方案。東江流域正面對日趨嚴重的水資源衝突，除了城鄉之間、上下游之間，還包括生態系統服務的供應及受益者之間的矛盾。本研究項目將透過問卷調查和半結構式深度訪談，調查水資源生態補償機制在東江流域内的落實情況和成效。本研究項目設計將會以體制配合及互動的分析框架為基礎，集中探討水資源生態補償機制的相關政策和持份者之間非正式合作策略的制度特點，藉此了解水資源生態補償機制對地方生態和社會有多大影響。透過仔細分析以下三方面的問題:（一）水權制度；（二）監測、獎勵以及懲罰制度；（三）持份者之間的非正式合作策略，從而確認與水資源生態補償機制成效相關的關鍵變數。本研究項目的成果將有助決策者制定更有效的方法推行體制改革，以達致中國跨界水資源管治的長遠的可持續發展目標。

18202116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18202116.value: Pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) are a large group of micropollutants that are widely recognised in the world because of their harmful effects in aquatic environments. In the past few decades, research efforts to combat this problem have grown immensely. Most work has been focused on investigating the occurrence and fate of PPCPs in sewage and their elimination efficiency. However, not much work has been made to investigate the removal mechanisms of PPCPs, their inhibitory effects process stability and reliability of the biological treatment processes in a pilot or full-scale operation for PPCPs removal. In this project, an in-depth study on the removal mechanisms of PPCPs in biological treatment systems with varying designs (i.e., activated sludge process (ASP), ASP with nitrogen removal, and ASP with nitrogen and phosphorous removal), which are commonly used in Hong Kong, China, and Scotland, will be carried out by: (1) a comprehensive sampling and measurement of PPCPs in various locations in STPs in Hong Kong, Guangzhou and Scotland; (2) dose-response experiments using lab-scale bioreactors for the kinetics study, and bacterial community analysis; (3) DNA-based molecular techniques to understand the bacterial community composition and antimicrobial resistance analysis; and (4) process optimisation of the pilot-scale bioreactors with different designs for various purposes (i.e., ultimate discharge and water reclamation). The overall aims of this study are: (1) to compare the distribution and removal efficiency of targeted PPCPs and to establish their mass balance in biological sewage treatment plants with different designs; (2) to investigate the effects of the identified PPCPs on the removal efficiency and microbial community in lab-scale bioreactors with different designs; (3) to investigate the ecotoxicological scrutiny of the removal rates of the identified PPCPs in the presence and absence of the acclimated enhanced culture; and (4) to optimise the treatment performance of the identified PPCPs in different biological wastewater treatment systems for ultimate discharge and water reclamation. Eventually, the latent crisis of PPCPs to humans and the environment could be further controlled if they can be effectively removed in sewage treatment plants (STPs) before final release into the environment. 近年來，因為藥品和個人護理產品及其殘餘物 (PPCPs)會對水體環境有持久性的影響，而被廣泛視為新興的環境問題。但大部分研究只集中於這類污染物在水體的存在，宿命及風險評估。然而，沒有在對PPCPs在污水處理廠的去除機制，對生物處理過程的抑製作用，以及處理的系統穩定性和可靠性作詳細的研究。

18202116.label: Major findings and research outcome
18202116.value: Wastewater and sludge samples were collected from different locations of the selected sewage treatment plants (STPs) to compare the distribution and removal efficiency of 4 targeted classes of PPCPs with adverse effects on treatment performance and to establish the mass balance of the targeted PPCPs in biological sewage treatment plants with different designs in Hong Kong, China and Scotland. The corresponding analytical methods for the targeted PPCPs were successfully developed, modified and verified. The lab-scale biological treatment systems were designed and constructed for kinetics study to under the PPCP removal mechanisms. The effects of the identified PPCPs with different concentrations on the removal efficiency and microbial community were evaluated by using dose-response experiments in the lab-scale bioreactors. A screening of bacterial populations against the PPCPs of interest has been confirmed in Stages 1 and 2. The tracking of resistance, which is triggered by many PPCPs or substrate utility, was involved culture-based methodologies. Any cultures showing any sign of resistance were selected be further investigated using Minimum Inhibitory Concentration assays, where cultures were challenged to increasingly higher levels of chemical stress. Cultures showing enhanced survivability were selected become candidates for further assays. The experiment protocols for the ecotoxicological scrutiny of the removal rates of the identified PPCPs in different bioreactors in the presence and absence of the acclimated enhanced culture of aerobic microorganisms were developed. The seeds of aerobic microorganisms and the corresponding cultures were collected, selected, and maintained. Based on the experimental results collected from Stages 1, 2 and 3, the relationship between the removal efficiency of PPCPs in lab-scale bioreactors and the shift of microbial community was evaluated. Potential measures to improve and optimise the treatment performance of the identified PPCPs in different biological wastewater treatment systems for ultimate discharge was proposed. Kinetic models of the lab-scale bioreactors were also developed to explain: (1) the microbial population and activities in the bioreactors with varying designs; and (2) the adsorption behaviour. The results will eventually serve as a useful tool for future operation of the exiting STPs for the effective removal of PPCPs and BOD and water reclamation. The technologies have been evaluated in the laboratory-scale systems at EdUHK, pilot-scale bioreactors at South China University of Technology, and in a full-scale STP in Guizhou Province since 2017 respectively, and also tested in a constructed wetland system in the Eco-garden at EdUHK.

18202116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18202116.value: Biochar has recently attracted significant scientific interest due to its relatively large specific surface area, the wide availability of the necessary feedstock, and its low-cost, highly porous structure, and stable carbon matrix. However, in-depth studies of the added values of engineered biochars in bioreactors and the PPCP removal mechanisms in engineered biochar-enhanced bioreactors are rare. These findings of the funded GRF project can provide a theoretical and practical basis upon which to propose biological treatment systems for stable and efficient PPCP removal. The synergistic effects of engineered biochars on treatment performance and microbial community in biochar-enhanced bioreactors during microbial immobilization and operation will be further investigated. Bioreactors using the engineered biochars with improved efficiency, controllability, and stability for removal of selected PPCPs could be designed and developed to realise stable and efficient biological processes for real application in water purification and sewage treatment facilities. The most original aspect is the suggestion of using more-or-less conventional water/sewage treatment plants to deal with the plethora of micropollutants, instead of implementing costly tertiary treatment alternatives to target these compounds of emerging concern. If successful, this approach would enable very rapid adaptation of the existing infrastructure to the new trend.

18202116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18202116.value: In this project, 4 targeted PPCP classes with low removal efficiency were identified and investigated in the to evaluate the adverse impacts on PPCPs removal mechanisms in STPs with different designs of biological treatment systems. The distribution of the PPCPs in the different systems were also determined through establishing mass balances of PPCPs. The effects of identified PPCPs on removal efficiency and microbial community were evaluated using dose-response experiments with different bioreactor designs. The biodegradation rate and the key PPCP-degrading bacteria were investigated and identified. The findings of the proposed study will form a fundamental understanding on the removal mechanisms of PPCPs and provide valuable information to improve the efficiency of biological treatment systems in reducing the release of PPCPs into aquatic environments and/or promote water reclamation for irrigation.

18303716.label: Realisation of objectives
18303716.value: (i) Activation of PE/PP/PVC polymers. The activation of the polymers was preceded by chlorosulfuric acid-mediated sulfonation of the carbon-hydrogen bonds and followed by the grafting of Fe(III) onto the polymer chains. Recently, a study demonstrated that the photo-Fenton process was capable of completely mineralizing polystyrene (PS) into CO2 if the sulfonation and grafting of Fe(III) on the polymer chains was achieved. Although it is well known that activation can be conveniently achieved by sulfuric acid through the sulfonation of the phenyl moieties of the polystyrene chains followed by the grafting of Fe(III), unlike PS, PE/PP/PVC does not possess any functionality for ordinary sulfonation which was found to be ineffective to C-C and/or C-H activation. To overcome this, a stronger sulfonating agent, chlorosulfuric acid, was used. PESFe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe were prepared using a modified sulfonation reaction by reacting the virgin PE/PP/PVC beans with 12.5 vol% chlorosulfuric acid in chloroform in an open atmosphere at 80 ºC, followed by grafting Fe(III). We found that sulfonation of all the polymers was efficient. PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe were isolated as an air-stable black precipitate, which were insoluble in water and all common organic solvents. The sulfonation and grafting of Fe(III) onto the polymer chains was confirmed by an IR spectroscopy, where two sets of new peaks at 1164 and 1034 cm-1 (S=O) and 535 cm-1 (Fe–O) were found in the activated polymers. The sizes of the PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe particles were found to be ~150 to 176 μm as the average value. Their chemical compositions were determined using EDS where the peaks of C, O, S, and Fe were recorded in the materials. Elemental and ICP-MS analysis indicated that the S/Fe mole ratios in all the polymers was ~1 suggesting that every sulfonate functionality in the activated polymer chelated to one Fe(III) ion. While the carbon to sulphur (C/S) ratio in the polymers was found to be 8.3 as the average value indicating that every four ethylene units in the activated polymer was activated. In addition, Ihata and Kaneko indicated that the sulfonation of PE with gaseous SO3 or fuming sulfuric acid, respectively, resulted in the formation of C=C double bonds. We also found that the PESFe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe generated contained alkene functionality by FTIR. (ii) Degradation of PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe using the Fenton Reaction. Suspensions of 100 mg of the polymer materials (PE/PP/PVC and PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCSFe) under dark ambient conditions with 650.0 mmol/g H2O2 and pH 2.2 were followed by the course of a Fenton reaction. 95% degradation (i.e., 95% dry weight loss) of PES-Fe/PPSFe/PVCS-Fe was achieved within 25 minutes. The DOC content of PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCSFe mixture increased rapidly in the beginning and reached its maximum at ~340.0 mg/L at 25 minutes. The decreasing dry weight and the increasing DOC content of the reaction mixture of PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe at the onset of the Fenton process could be explained based on the oxidative cleavage of the carbon-carbon polymer chains to produce water-soluble and lower molecular weight organic fragments in the reaction mixture, and most importantly, the hydrophilic fragments remained intact in the Fenton reaction. This explains the plateau in DOC content during the later stage of the degradation. No evidence of any degradation or mineralization of the virgin PE/PP/PVC polymer was observed after 7 hours of the same Fenton reaction treatment. (iii) Identification of Products from the Degradation of PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe plastic using the Fenton Reaction. Carbon dioxide was found as 26.7-35% during the degradation of PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe via the treatment. The dissolved organic matter from the degradation was found to be 73.3-82.2% (Fig. 3a). We envisioned that the dissolved organic matter could be used as a resource. Through a simple solvent extraction using methanol, the dissolved organic matter in the aqueous reaction mixture could be isolated. The extract from the dissolved organic matter of the degraded PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe was characterized and quantified by HPLC-DAD and GS-MS. Organic carboxylic acid (monocarboxylic and dicarboxylic acid) was the major group in the extract while sulfonic acid contributed a little proportion. Through the standard addition analysis, more than 85% of the extract was determined to be carboxylic acids. Butanedioic acid, an industrial important chemical for nylon synthesis, contributed the major proportion (33.4-51.0%) of the extract. There were less than 10% of unidentified organic molecules in the organic extracts from the dissolved organic matter of the degraded PESFe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe mixture. (iv) Recovery of Organic Products from Real PE/PP/PVC Wastes. The activation of PE/PP/PVC substrates was conveniently achieved using the developed protocol. This enabled the recovery of useful organic products via the Fenton degradation process to be applied to real waste polymers. We initially demonstrated this by using commercially available plastics including: (i) detergent bottles made with high density polyethylene (HDPE); (ii) various carrier bags made with low density polyethylene (LDPE), flexible water pipe (PVC), stationery (PVC), and microwave container (PP) which were ground into powders with particle sizes in the range 125–250 μm. The established sulfonation and the established Fenton reaction conditions were applied for the degradation of the polymer substrates. The degradation efficiencies of the real samples were found as 96.4-99.2% within 2 hours. Over 95% degradation suggested that the Fenton process was significantly insensitive to any additives (dyes or other plasticizers) in the polymer materials. 85.1-87.1% of the organic products extracted from the Fenton degradation of PE/PP/PVC were determined to be carboxylic acid in which all the monocarboxylic acids (formic and acetic acid) and the dicarboxylic acids (oxalic, propanedioic, and butanedioic acid) found in the recovery of the virgin polymers appeared in those of the real samples. (v) Study the feasibility of using mechanochemical method to activate and degrade PE and to recover organic products generated. A new mechanochemical method was developed to convert polymer wastes, PE, PP, and PVC, to fuel gases (H2, CH4, and CO) under ball-milling with KMnO4 at room temperature. By using various solid-state characterizations (XPS, SEM, EDS, FTIR, and NMR), and density functional theory calculations, it was found that the activation followed the hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) mechanism. Two metal oxidant molecules were found to abstract two separate hydrogen atoms from the –CH and –CH units of substrates, [–CH2–CH(R)–]n, where R = H in PE, R = CH3 in PP, and R = Cl in PVC, resulting in a di-radical, [–CH–C(R)–]. Subsequently, the two unpaired electrons of the di-radical were recombined into an alkene intermediate, [–CH = C(R)–], which underwent further oxidation to produce H2, CH4, and CO gases.

18303716.label: Major findings and research outcome
18303716.value: In this study, we aimed to address the following critical factors in order to make the chemical process practical: (i) to study the thermodynamic and kinetic parameters of controlling the effectiveness of polymer activation, the Fenton degradation process, and the product selectivity of the organic products generated from the Fenton degradation process; (ii) to understand the mechanisms of the cracking pathway of PE via the Fenton reaction that lead to the observed products; (iii) to extend the fundamental findings obtained from the PE system to PP. Our results demonstrated that via “Fenton reaction”, PE, PP and PVC plastic wastes could be effectively cracked into small organic compounds such as mono- and di-carboxylic acids. These recovered organic chemicals could be potentially used as valuable raw materials for industrial applications such as nylon polymer production and cosmetics. For the conditions we examined, the powder of plastics was initially activated by chlorosulfuric acid to introduce sulfonate groups (-SO3-) on the polymer backbone chains and followed by grafting of Fe (III) ions on to the polymer chains to produce the ready-to-degrade polymers (PES-Fe/PPS-Fe/PVCS-Fe). The polymers can be degraded via Fenton reaction into soluble matters and carbon dioxide gas in an aqueous medium at pH 2.2 with H2O2 solution in ambient dark conditions and under UV irradiation respectively. The dissolved organic matter in the aqueous reaction mixture were isolated by extraction and the organic extracts that were identified were mainly monocarboxylic acids (19.5-22.5%) and dicarboxylic acids (41.8-60.8%), in which the majority components were acetic acid (12.4-20.5%) and butanedioic acid (33.4-50.8%). By applying this developed chemical process, fine organic products were able to be recovered from common plastic wastes, which include: (i) detergent bottles made with high density polyethylene (HDPE); (ii) various carrier bags made with low density polyethylene (LDPE), flexible water pipe (PVC), stationery (PVC), and microwave container (PP). Furthermore, a new mechanochemical method has been developed to convert polymer wastes, to fuel gases (H2, CH4, and CO) under ball-milling with KMnO4 at room temperature.

18303716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18303716.value: A further development is to explore the feasibility of using other similar and milder chemical activation and degradation methods to degrade PE/PP/PVC and to recover organic products generated. C-H activation is required to bind the Fenton reagent to PE and PP polymers. Chlorosulfuric acid will be primarily used for the first three objectives, as it is one of the strongest sulfonating agents available. However, due to its highly corrosive property, other mild activation approaches, such as (i) ozonolysis by ozone/UV; and (ii) surface modification by high valence oxo-metal complexes, will also be explored. As far as we know, these proposed alternative chemical activation methods or treatments have been studied for small hydrocarbon molecules, such as cycloalkane, their feasibility for our purpose on macro-molecules, such as synthetic polymers, has to be further investigated.

18303716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18303716.value: Plastic waste management are critical issues, and the development of breakthrough technology for these purposes is a challenging task. In this study, it explored the feasibility of waste degradation of inert plastic wastes, through effective chemical processes including surface activation and Fenton and photo-Fenton technology. Under ambient dark conditions, the activated PE/PP/PVC were successful converted into water-soluble organic matter and carbon dioxide (CO2) within 40 min, while the photo-Fenton reaction under UV-vis illumination was able to achieve complete mineralization within 80 min as determined by the analysis of the reaction solutions. In addition, the dissolved organic matter generated from the reaction was identified as belonging to three main classes: monocarboxylic acids, dicarboxylic acids, and diols. The study revealed that the concentration of H2O2 used in the Fenton reaction significantly affects the amount of diols and carboxylic acids recovered, where the ratio could be tuned from 37.2 to 2.1% for diols and from 55.9 to 93.1% for carboxylic acids, under dark conditions. Moreover, under photo-Fenton degradation conditions, due to rapid decomposition, a positive pressure was observed (CO2 gas: 550 kPa/g of material) from complete degradation of the polymers. The gas pressure could potentially be converted into mechanical energy for further applications.

18304316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18304316.value: Optimization corresponds to the task to identify a configuration of variables to maximize or minimize an objective function. It is implicitly implemented in a wide range of daily activities, as well as numerous tasks in research, industry and commerce. Computer scientists, operations researchers and applied mathematicians have devoted great efforts to develop optimization algorithms to tackle specific tasks, and found that some optimization problems are more difficult to solve than the others. Yet, the origins of such difficulties are not fully understood and are not a major interest in conventional studies. Definitely, a clear understanding will lead to stimulating clues to improve optimization algorithms and their ability to tackle hard problems. Physicists play an important role to develop a fundamental understanding of optimization problems by drawing an analogy with physical systems which tend to achieve the state with the lowest energy, analogous to an optimal state. Nevertheless, physicists are interested in aspects of optimization problems that conventional optimization researchers find unrealistic, irrelevant or impractical. This leads to a limited recognition of the physics-based results among conventional optimization researchers and thus, isolated developments in the two individual areas. We propose to better integrate and bridge physics and combinatorial optimization problems, by (1) using physical tools to study aspects of optimization problems where optimization researchers find most practical, (2) improving methodologies in both areas instead of improving merely the methodologies from physics, and (3) converting the new understandings into new applications. Specifically, we will apply physical tools to (a) study practical finite-size optimization problems, instead of conventional infinite-size systems studied by physicists, (b) understand and analyze non-physics optimization algorithms with the tools of physics, (c) understand the origins of problem-specific performances of the physics-inspired optimization algorithms, which is a major criticism by conventional optimization researchers on these algorithms, (d) connect features in the space of variables which interest optimization researchers most, to characteristics in the space of states which interest physicists most, and (e) finally, apply the new understandings to improve both existing physics-inspired and non-physics optimization algorithms, and to introduce new, readily applicable algorithms which work beyond the limits of existing algorithms. 優化是指求出把目標函數最大或最小化的變量組合。它在日常生活中擔當重要角色。因其廣泛性，計算機科學家、運籌學家和應用數學家透過大量研究發展出各種優化算法。當中存在一些特別難解決的優化問題，傳統研究對這些特難問題的難度起源未有清楚了解。物理學家透過優化問題及物理系統的共通性，對特難問題的基本原理有了深入理解。然而，部分傳統優化研究學家認為物理學家在優化問題上的研究結果不切實際，導致這些成果在傳統優化研究領域中未有廣泛的認可及應用。 我們建議通過以下途徑更有效地整合物理學手法及組合優化問題：（1）以物理手法研究實際的優化問題，（2）以物理改進兩個領域所得的算法，包括基於物理學的算法及傳統算法，（3）將物理手法所得的基本理解發展成可應用的工具。具體而言，我們將利用基於物理學的研究手法，（a）研究變量數目適中的優化問題，而不是物理學中趨於無限多變量的系統，（b）以物理手法理解和分析傳統優化算法，（c）理解物理學算法在不同問題中的優化表現差異，（d）找出解空間及變量空間的特徵及其關係，（e）應用新的結果改善現有的物理和非物理優化算法，並引進不受現有算法限制的新算法。

18304316.label: Realisation of objectives
18304316.value: OBJECTIVE (1) (a) In [4] (Po and Yeung, under review), we introduced a new approach called “Coarse-grained Energy Landscape” (CEL) to reveal the energy landscape of combinatorial optimization problems; we applied the approach on spin glasses and K-Satisfiability problems to demonstrate the capability of this new method. For small systems, their energy landscapes can be completely characterized by CEL, where the global minima, local minima, intermediate configurations connecting the minima and high energy configurations are clearly shown, as shown in Figures 1, 3 and S2 of [4]. For larger systems, we introduced a variant of the approach called “Partial Coarse-grained Energy Landscape” (PCEL) to extract partially a specific regime (e.g. the low-energy configurations) of the energy landscape of combinatorial optimization problems. As shown in [4], our introduced approaches allow us to obtain the statistics of local minima, as well as the non-equilibrium dynamics when the system is trapped in local minima, at an arbitrary temperature for an arbitrary long time, out of reach by existing approaches and computational capability. OBJECTIVE (2) (a) In [5] (Yeung, 2019), we converted a spatial network into a space-time network by adding a time dimension, and applied the cavity approach developed in the studies of spin glass to derive an optimization algorithm capable for finding optimal spatial-temporal solutions for dynamical coordination of routes in networks. We compared the results obtained by our algorithm with a non-physics-inspired algorithm, namely mutli-start greedy search, and show that our physics-inspired algorithm for this specific optimization problem outperforms the selected non-physics algorithm in minimizing the total traveling time of vehicles. (b) In [6] (Liao, Liu, Huang, Lu, Yeung and Zhang, accepted), we studied an important type of non-physics-inspired algorithms, namely ranking and reputation evaluation ranking algorithms. By introducing a new algorithm which articulates the quality of users or products through their cumulative impact, we compared the performance of our algorithm with other non-physics ranking algorithms and found that our algorithm outperforms others in identifying important users and quality products in most of the studied datasets. (c) In [7] (Zhu, Yeung and Liem, 2021), we studied another type of important non-physics-inspired algorithms, namely friend recommendation algorithms. Specifically, we studied the common neighbor algorithm and found that over-reliance on the algorithm in identifying new friends can lead to sub-optimal grouping of users who have sub-optimal match in their attributes or interests. All the above studies have led us to a better understanding on the working principles underlying non-physics-inspired optimization algorithms. OBJECTIVE (3) (a) In [2] (Xu, Yeung, Zhou and Saad, 2018), we studied combinational optimization problems characterized by entropy-energy profiles where an inflection point exists. We then applied a representative and widely adopted physics-inspired algorithm, namely “Simulated Annealing” (SA), which identifies optimal solution by decreasing temperature; interestingly, we found that in contrary to our common belief, SA is unable to identify the ground state of the problem when temperature decreases in this specific type of optimization problems, since the infection point in the entropy-energy profiles lead to the association of low-energy configurations with high free energies, and hence lowering temperature does not necessary lead to lower energy configurations. The findings in [2] has re-shaped our understanding on the essence of physics-inspired optimization algorithms, i.e. the association of low temperature with low system energy or cost in optimization problems, can be violated. (b) In [4] (Po and Yeung, under review), we introduced CELs and used them to obtain a clear, complete and new fundamental physical picture of the obstacles encountered by physics-inspired algorithms in finding solutions in optimization problems; we showed in [4] that local minima are competing with global minima for the systems’ probability in constant-temperature Monte Carlo dynamics, and the ground-state probability may decrease as temperature decreases, since the system is trapped in local minima for a long time. Other than the specific optimization problems characterized by an inflection point in entropy-energy profiles studied in [2], our new proposed method of analyzing non-equilibrium dynamics through energy landscapes in [4] led us to insights on the limitations of physics-inspired algorithms on general combinatorial optimization problems. The works [2,4] improved our fundamental understanding of the nature of optimization problems and the limitations by physics-inspired algorithms. OBJECTIVE 4 (a) In [1] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2018), we studied the emergence of self-sustained clusters (SSC, originally introduced by the PI and the Co-I for the study of spin glasses in 2013), in 3-spin models; these SSCs are spin clusters in the real space that are self-sustained within the clusters and are less affected by spins outside the clusters, leading to meta-stable local regions hindering optimization algorithms in identifying ground states. The emergence of SSCs in real space would be the manifestation of energy barriers and local minima in energy landscapes, which fulfil our major objective to connect features in the real space to those in the configuration space. We showed both theoretically and empirically in [1] that SSCs exist in 3-spin models. (b) In [3] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2019), we further provided evidence to connect SSCs in the real space with local minima in the configuration space. By introducing an algorithm to compute the probability of a variable of an optimization problem to be in a SSC, we run the algorithm on spin glass on random regular graphs and found that spins in SSC are less likely to flip, which we call “slow-spins”. There results further consolidate our understanding of how energy barrier and local minima in energy landscapes are manifested as SSCs in the real space. OBJECTIVE 5 (a) In [2] (Xu, Yeung, Zhou and Saad, 2018), since SA fails in identifying ground states by merely lowering temperatures due to the inflection point in the entropy-energy profile of the problem, we introduced a new physics-inspired optimization approach called “clamp-energy” optimization algorithms, which keeps energy instead of temperature of the system to specific values. We applied it on the defensive alliance problem in [2] to overcome the inflection point in entropy-energy profiles to identify ground states. (b) In [3] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2019), based on our understanding of the relationship between SSC and meta-stability, we derived an algorithm to identify variables which are likely to be in SSCs in optimization problems; after these SSC variables are identified, one can use various methods to weaken these SSCs to facilitate optimization algorithms in identifying optimal solutions. (c) In [5] (Yeung, 2019), we employed space-time networks to derive algorithms with optimization for both spatial and temporal dimensions, which makes static analytical approaches (e.g. cavity approach) capable to identify spatiotemporal optimal solution; such success has important implications on other static physics-inspired and non-physics-inspired optimization approaches which can be extended to include the time dimension using the same framework. (d) In [6] (Liao, Liu, Huang, Lu, Yeung and Zhang, accepted), we introduced an accumulative time-based algorithm to evaluate iteratively the reputation of users and products; such approach would have implications on other algorithms which aim to accumulate specific measures on individual variables in optimization problems.

18304316.label: Major findings and research outcome
18304316.value: (1) Improved understanding (a) In [2] (Xu, Yeung, Zhou and Saad, 2018), we discovered that there exists an inflection point in the entropy-energy profile of some optimization problems, and in this case, low-energy configurations are associated with a high free energy; lowering temperature in physics-inspired optimization algorithms does not lead to the ground states of the system, which is a new finding and understanding on optimization problems. (b) In [3] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2019), we showed that variables in self-sustained clusters (SSC) are less likely to switch their value during optimization; this improved our understanding on the features in the real space manifesting local minima in the configurational space. (c) In [4] (Po and Yeung, under review), we introduced the method called coarse-grained energy landscapes (CEL) to analyze the non-equilibrium dynamics of disordered systems, leading to analytical results at an arbitrary temperature for an arbitrarily long time inaccessible by existing theories and simulations; we found that it can be less likely to identify ground states when temperature decreases, due to trapping in local minima; this is a clear, complete and new physical picture of non-equilibrium dynamics of complex disordered systems. (2) Advances in methodology (a) In [4] (Po and Yeung, under review), our new method of CELs has been applied to characterize the energy landscape of spin glasses and K-satisfiability problems, and can be applied to other optimization problems with discrete variables. (b) In [5] (Yeung 2019), we applied space-time networks to convert static optimization approaches for dynamical problems with both spatial and temporal dimension; this can be readily applied to other dynamical problems. (3) Applications (a) In [2] (Xu, Yeung, Zhou and Saad, 2018), we introduced a new physics-inspired clamp-energy optimization algorithm for optimization problems with an inflection point in their entropy-energy profile. (b) In [3] (Rocchi, Saad and Yeung, 2019), we derived a new message-passing algorithm to identify variables which are more likely to be in SSC, which can be used to destabilise SSC to facilitate optimization in optimization problems. (c) In [5] (Yeung, 2019), we applied space-time networks to derive a spatiotemporal algorithm using an originally static analytical tool, which can be readily generalized to other dynamical problems. (d) In [6] (Liao, Liu, Huang, Lu, Yeung and Zhang, accepted), we introduced an accumulative time-based algorithm to evaluate specific quantities of network nodes, which has been tested on various real datasets and can be adopted for other problems.

18304316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18304316.value: To further improve our understanding on combinatorial optimization problems, we will apply our new method of coarse-grained energy landscapes (CELs) to analyze the energy landscapes and non-equilibrium dynamics of more high-dimensional complex disordered systems, for instance, the learning process for deep neural networks. In addition, we will further understand algorithmic hardness by further investigating the relationship between self-sustained clusters (SSCs) in real space and metastability in configurational space, or the existence of inflection points in entropy-energy profiles and their impact, in physical systems and optimization problems. Such findings are inaccessible in conventional studies and will have great impact on our fundamental understanding on optimization problems and algorithms. In terms of methodology, we will further improve analytical approaches related to CELs and SSCs proposed in the project and develop new methodology in understanding optimization problems and the limitation of optimization algorithms. Such approaches would lead to new tools to analyze glassy physical systems and optimization problems. As for applications, we will generalize the algorithms such as the clamp-energy algorithm or the space-time message passing algorithm which have incorporated the physical insights gained in the current project to other optimization problems, to further disseminate these insights to other areas of studies.

18304316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18304316.value: We applied analytical tools in statistical physics to unravel various fundamental aspects of combinatorial optimization problems. Specifically, we developed a method to completely characterize the high-dimensional energy landscapes of physical systems and optimization problems with discrete variables, which allows us to analyse their non-equilibrium dynamics at an arbitrary temperature for an arbitrarily long time, out of reach by existing theory and empirical studies. We also discovered features such as inflection point in the entropy-energy profiles and self-sustained clusters (SSCs) in the real variable space, which lead to fundamental understanding on the limitations of optimization algorithms. These findings are accomplished by new methodology we introduced in the project. In terms of applications, various algorithms have been derived based on the insights and improved fundamental understanding gained in the project. These include algorithms which identify optimal solutions by keeping the energy instead of temperature constant in the system, identify variables which are more likely to be in SSCs, identify spatiotemporal solutions based on static analytical approaches. Many of these algorithms have incorporated the physical insights obtained in the project that are inaccessible in other areas, which can be generalized and incorporated into the design of other optimization algorithms leading to fundamental impact in different areas.

18600816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18600816.value: During the late nineteenth and early twentieth century, Manchuria was fiercely disputed between the Chinese, Russian and Japanese empires. As a result, it was also the destination of migrants from diverse backgrounds. In consequence, Manchuria, and especially the city of Harbin, soon developed into a microcosm of transcultural interaction. The first influx of Russian arrivals occurred with the construction of the Chinese Eastern Railway in the 1890s. Among the supposedly Russian migrants were in fact many Poles. Poland had lost its independent statehood for more than one hundred years (1795-1919), being divided between the Russian, German and Austrian empires. Poland is usually displayed as a ‘victim’ of imperial politics. However, scholars have recently argued for the existence of a genuinely Polish form of ‘colonialism’ and have analysed the rhetoric of a Polish ‘civilizing mission’. In light of these debates, this project analyses the Polish community of Harbin from its beginnings in the 1890s to its end in the 1940s by focusing on institutions and practices of Polish schooling in that city. In particular, a Polish high school (Gimnazjum im. Henryka Sienkiewicza) with an adjacent elementary division opened in 1915 and was actively supported by the new Polish state and its Harbin consulate from 1919 onwards until its forced closure in the 1940s. Next to this (semi-)official landmark school, the Marian, Franciscan and Ursuline orders established several Catholic institutions for boys and girls where instruction was at least partially provided in the Polish language. It will be argued that these schools were powerful instruments of cultural diplomacy by which the Polish Second Republic tried to get hold of its diaspora and extend its influence internationally. Simultaneously, this project looks at the strategies deployed by Polish families on the spot in Harbin who sent their offspring to these schools. This research makes use of global and transnational approaches to historiography. It is part of a larger second-book project on schools for Western children in China, Korea and Japan before the Second World War that will discuss the East Asian beginnings of international schooling. Located on the crossroads of European and East Asian history, it engages with debates both in ‘general’ history and the history of education. 在 19 世紀後期以及 20 世紀初期,滿洲地區成為中國、俄國和日本的爭奪對象 。因而,滿洲也聚集了很多來自不同地區的移民。滿洲,尤其是哈爾濱 很快就 發展成了跨文化交流的據點。第一批俄國人蜂擁而至之後,建成了 1890 年代 中國東部的鐵路。其中一些俄國移民實際上是波蘭人,而當時波蘭已經喪失了 主權獨立超過 100 年(1795-­‐1919)。波蘭經常被認為是帝國體制的犧牲品, 一度被俄國、德國和奧地利瓜分。然而,學者們最近發現一種波蘭化的「殖 民 主義」,并在探究這種波蘭式的「文明教化任務」。本課題將延續這一命題的 討論,研究哈爾濱的一個波蘭社區,從 1890 年代出現到 1940 年代消亡的過 程。其中又會重點研究當地的波蘭教育機構,尤其是其中一所波蘭高中 (Gimnazjum im. Henryka Sienkiewicza)及其在 1915 年設立的初中部。這所學校 在 1940 年代被關閉之前,一直得到波蘭新政府以及其在哈爾濱的領事館的大 力支持。在 這所半官方學校的旁邊, 聖母會(Marian Order), 方濟各會、 圣 于爾絮勒會都建立了天主教的教育機構,而至少部分教學採用波蘭語。學校是 文化外交的有力工具,當時的波蘭第二共和國正是以此來凝聚流徙的國民以及 增強國 際影響力。與此同時,本文將探討波蘭家庭將子女送到此類機構的考量 。這一研究將全球化和跨國研究的方法融入了歷史研究。這一課題也可以被視 為二戰前在中 國、韓國以及日本的西方兒童教育這一系列的第二部,仍然探討 東亞國際學校的開端,在歐洲和東亞歷史的交融之下,本文既回應廣廣泛意義 的歷史問題,又回應教 育史的探討。

18600816.label: Realisation of objectives
18600816.value: For more than two years this PI has been working on Polish schooling in Manchuria during the first half of the twentieth century. This PI is extremely grateful to the URG for making the research possible. After preliminary work in the initial project phase, all relevant primary source materials could be collected, thanks to a two-months stay in Poland in 2017. Similarly, all relevant secondary literature not available in local libraries could be collected in Poland or purchased from the grant money. This is an important and lasting achievement, as this documentation constitutes the basis for future research work. The systematic analysis of the collected materials is still in progress. Notwithstanding the very limited time that this PI could invest in the project due to teaching constraints (no teaching relief granted; seven courses to teach during the academic year 2018-2019, four of them for the first time and far beyond this PI’s area of expertise), an initial screening of the source materials already allows us to understand the basic mechanics of Polish schooling in Manchuria. First preliminary results were presented at ten international workshops and conferences. The conferences addressed audiences in different fields of history, including global history, history of education, Asian history and Polish history. This PI could make himself a name as a researcher competent with Polish communities and schooling in East Asia. On these occasions this PI also received positive feedback that helped to further finetune the approach. These presentations constitute the basis for future publications. The following journal articles are currently in progress: - “Beyond Harbin: Educational Mobilities of Polish Students in East Asia, 1920s-1940s”, part of a special issue of the Zeitschrift für Ostmitteleuropaforschung on “Polish Worldwideness” edited by Markus Krzoska to appear in 2021. - “Das Gimnazjum im. Henryka Sienkiewicza in Harbin, 1915-1949: Eine polnische Schule in Ostasien”, to be submitted to Geschichte und Gesellschaft or similar. - “Poles in Manchuria: Challenging Dominant Perceptions of Transnational Lives”, to be submitted to the Asian Studies Review or similar. - “Poles in Transit: Registering for Polish Citizenship in Tianjin, 1918-1920”, to be submitted to the Journal of World History or similar. The research objectives have been fulfilled and, despite their preliminary character, clear statements can be made: - Institutionalised Polish education in Harbin started at the primary level. The Doctor Łazowski Primary School (Szkoła początkowa im. Doktora Łazowskiego) was founded in 1908, followed by the Primary School at the St. Stanislas Bishop Martyr Church (Szkoła początkowa przy kościele Sw. Wincentego à Paulo) in 1912. Later on one more primary school connected to another Catholic church was created (Polska szkoła przy kościele św. Jozafata). Moreover, small-scale schools (szkółki) that comprised only the initial grades temporarily operated in other cities with sizable Polish communities along the Chinese Eastern Railway. Eventually the Sienkiewicz High School (Gimnazjum im. Henryka Sienkiewicza) was established in 1915. As the only post-primary Polish school in East Asia, it played a key role for the Polish community in Manchuria. In addition, the Franciscan, Ursuline and Marianist orders ran schools in Harbin that partly employed Polish personnel and used Polish language. These institutions remained peripheral to the Polish presence in Harbin. - In the years before the First World War Polish primary schools were established from two groups of actors, the Polish parishes of the Catholic church and the cultural association Gospoda Polska which was run by middle class representatives of the Polish community in Harbin. The high school emerged out of the activities around the influential priest Władysław Ostrowski. After the creation of a Polish state in 1918 the Polish consulate in Harbin as well as the Polish Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also played a role in school administration. Influential individuals during the interwar period included the community leader and director of the Sienkiewicz High School Kazimierz Grochowski. Tadeusz Szukiewicz, teacher at the school during the early 1920s, became an influential promotor of Polish-Chinese relations after he returned to Warsaw. Jan Jaworski, professor of sinology at the University of Warsaw, was sent to Harbin as a diplomat and educational advisor in the early 1930s in order to carry out school reform. Aleksander Macedoński was particularly influential during the Second World War before being sent to a Soviet gulag in 1945. - The initial rationale for establishing Polish schools was to preserve Polish language and culture in a diasporic situation. In particular, Polish community leaders wanted to distinguish themselves from the Russian-dominated environment in Harbin. Accordingly, they saw Polish schooling as a means to counteract the perceived danger of “Russification” and “de-nationalisation”. While this motivation continued to play a role throughout the interwar years, a second rationale was brought forward from the 1920s on: Expert-activists in Harbin and Warsaw alike increasingly saw the Polish community in Manchuria as a resource for the new nation-state. In their eyes, schooling should play a role to train young people for Poland’s economic and cultural expansion in East Asia. Formally equipped with knowledge about East Asia, graduates were potential imperial agents in the service of Polish industry. - In the first decade of the twentieth century Russian authorities in Manchuria only permitted the operation of primary schools in Polish. Russians allowed for the creation of Polish high schools, both in Russia and the imperial extension of the railway zone, only in 1915 when this became opportune in light of developments at the eastern front of the First World War. After the end of Russian privileges in Manchuria school administrators had to cope with a new reality. Although Poland and China only concluded a Treaty of Friendship in 1928, Chinese authorities allowed Polish institutions to operate in Manchuria and interactions were comparatively smooth. This situation curiously continued when Harbin came under the administration of Manzhouguo in 1932. The schools were only forced to close after the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbour. From 1945 until its closure in 1949 the Sienkiewicz High School could operate under Soviet administrative and ideological oversight. - The Sienkiewicz High School catered for the Polish community of Manchuria. Apart from foreign language classes instruction was exclusively in Polish. Starting in the 1930s, Chinese and later Japanese were added to the curriculum as compulsory subjects. Already in 1923 the school had been officially recognised by the Polish Ministry of Education. As a result, graduates could directly enter Polish universities. - Polish children also patronised other international schools in Harbin, including the YMCA College, the German Hindenburg-Schule and various Russian institutions.

18600816.label: Major findings and research outcome
18600816.value: Beyond the findings outlined above, this PI would like to insist on the following. The ramifications of the Polish presence in north-eastern China considerably changed from its inception around 1900 to its end in 1949. Poles arrived to north-eastern China as Russian subjects. They were part of a Russian continental migration regime that promoted Tsarist imperial expansion towards the East. There is a small but significant detail that underlines how Poles distinguished themselves from the more Western European presence in East Asia: They arrived to East Asia by train, whereas representatives of other European nations usually arrived by steamer. The end of Russian imperialism in north-eastern China and the creation of a Polish nation-state after WWI changed the situation decisively. Experts and activists in Harbin and Warsaw tried to push the Manchurian diaspora out of the Russian-dominated sphere and to better connect it to the Western presence in the East Asian treaty-port world. The Manchurian Poles were increasingly seen as a resource for the Polish nation and as potential agents for Polish economic and cultural expansion in East Asia. From half-Russians in a Russo-Chinese borderland they turned into Europeans in East Asia, at least in the eyes of key decision makers. The Sienkiewicz High School was supposed to play an important role in this shift. From the early 1930s on, English instruction was considerably enhanced with native British teachers. The school also offered Chinese (and later additionally Japanese) as a compulsory component of the curriculum. A new subject “Oriental Studies” (Orientalistyka) was introduced. The school’s graduation diplomas became bilingual in Polish and Chinese. Moreover, fellowship programmes were set up to allow Poles attending colleges in China and Japan. Polish graduates from Harbin entered the University of Hong Kong from the early 1930s on. Poles also entered Chinese colleges, for example in Tianjin, that were usually frequented by Chinese students only. These examples indicate that Poles nurtured at times a closer and more egalitarian with their Chinese environment compared to what can be observed in the case of other European nations. Plans of Polish expansion in East Asia came to an end with the outbreak of WWII. Placing Polish schooling in Harbin in the context of the changing and intertwined dynamics of Poland, Russia, China and Japan was and remains the most fascinating aspect of this GRF project.

18600816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18600816.value: The first priority is to finalise and publish the research articles that are currently in progress. This work will be carried out during the coming years on a continuous basis. More importantly, the research on Polish schooling in Harbin is part of a larger project. In the years to come further international schools in East Asia will be researched, including German, French, British, American and Jewish institutions, enabling a comprehensive picture of the beginnings of international schooling in China, Korea and Japan. These further case studies will profit from the experience accumulated during the reported project period. They will allow to make comparisons and analyse entanglements with the Polish case. This PI has already located relevant source materials in European and East Asian archives. In particular, this PI is in contact with the German School Tokyo Yokohama where a history teacher is conducting the digitalization of the school archive. This PI is planning and preparing applications for GRF projects and other external funding in order to conduct this research in the future. Besides journal articles, the larger project will eventually result in a monograph published with a major academic press.

18600816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18600816.value: This project discussed the Polish community of Manchuria that consisted of several thousand individuals who initially arrived to north-eastern China in the late nineteenth century as Russian subjects when the Tsarist power started construction of the Chinese Eastern Railway. The project’s main focus was on Polish schooling in Harbin. Whereas primary schools opened during the first decade of the twentieth century, the Sienkiewicz High School was founded in 1915 and operated until 1949 when the last Poles were repatriated to Poland. The high school was a key institution for Poles in China. It played an important role for maintaining Polish language and culture far away from the mainland. Moreover, Polish activists saw it increasingly as a means for Polish economic expansion in China during the 1920s and 1930s. This research is important because it discusses a minor European diasporic community in China that has rarely been studied. Furthermore, the project studied this community through the lens of education. This is an innovative approach, as schools for foreigners in China only start to become the object of historical research. In this way the project contributes to the study of the beginnings of international schooling in East Asia.

18601616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18601616.value: 僅限會員：殖民地時期香港的私人俱樂部和社交生活

18601616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18601616.value: Despite the fact that Hong Kong retains a reputation of being one of Britain's most successful colonies in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it remains comparatively under-researched within the context of British imperial and global history. Despite a growing volume of work over the past two decades that focuses on the important role played by former colonies in the shaping, timing and diffusion of British culture throughout the world, Hong Kong has, to date, not been sufficiently factored into these recent trends in historical scholarship. In an attempt to redress the existing paucity of work that examines Hong Kong's history in a wider imperial and global context, this study will examine the history of private members' clubs in Hong Kong during the colonial period. In doing so, it will shed light on the ways in which private members' clubs became a key component of a broader associational life that connected Hong Kong (and its subsequent growth and development) to a wider British world during the colonial era. It will focus on the emergence of private members' clubs that were exclusive to both Chinese and Europeans alike, in addition to those that were open to other nationalities and races, women, sojourning businessmen as well as multiple religious communities. It will demonstrate how, contrary to the popular conception of these institutions as being distinctly insular, closed and local, private members' clubs were in fact complex transnational entities that operated within a much broader associational network spanning the British colonial world and that served to link Hong Kong to regions of the empire as diverse as Singapore, Shanghai and Delhi. In particular, this study will examine how within the imperial networks generated by colonial clubs, members, their families and affiliates were able to move freely across the empire - often facilitated by formal club affiliations and reciprocal memberships - readily exchanging ideas, information and material goods in the process. Moreover, it will explore how as largely self-governing, voluntary associations, private members' clubs in Hong Kong were spaces grounded in the civil behavior of the public sphere. As such, this study will examine how private members' clubs had the power to exert tremendous social, political and economic influence in their own right, whether serving as important nurseries for the spread of western democracy, ideas of free trade and political culture, or in providing forums and platforms for Chinese political resistance and social reform. 研究香港的學者，很少將香港史看作英帝國史和全球史的一部分。為了填補這個空隙，本計劃將集中研究殖民地時期香港各種會員制的私人俱樂部。這個計劃將揭示這些私人俱樂部如何成為連接香港和英帝國其他部分的更廣義的社交生活的一個重要組成部分。 本計劃將集中研究只限中國人、歐洲人的私人俱樂部如何出現，同時也會涉及一些開放給其他國籍、其他種族、女性、生意人和不同宗教團體的私人俱樂部。一般認為私人俱樂部是封閉的。然而，本計劃卻指出這些俱樂部實際上是複雜的跨國組織。 具體而言，本研究揭示這些殖民地俱樂部構成了一個帝國網絡，通過這個網絡俱樂部的會員及其家人、朋友均可以在帝國的範圍內自由行動，可以自由交換意見、信息和物質利益。同時本研究也探討這些俱樂部所產生的社會、政治和經濟影響，如傳播西方民主、自由貿易的觀念和政治文化。
