18615216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18615216.value: Computer programming has always been one of the core and compulsory modules in computer science education. In recent educational reform, there has been a tremendous and growing interest in introducing computational thinking to the K-12 education, via coding education. Coding curriculum has transformed K-12 education in the United States and United Kingdom. One of the key purposes of coding education is to enhance problem-solving skills by equipping students with programming-related capabilities (e.g. computational thinking, modelling and testing, and logical analyzing). In fact, the Department of Education in England has recently revised the national curriculum for K-12 education, to treat computer programming as a core subject in all four key learning stages. In Hong Kong, however, the benefits and challenges of coding education in the present K-12 curriculum have not been well addressed. Some schools have already introduced coding to their computer lessons, yet the impact of computational thinking and the influence of these learning activities are not studied. Therefore, it is imperative to study how coding can enhance essential skills for primary school students, particularly under the unique educational challenges in the local context. The objectives for this project are threefold: (1) Investigate the impact of computational thinking through coding education on children's learning and problem solving skills in the Hong Kong context. (2) Identify the challenges and develop appropriate strategies of coding education so as to maximize its benefits. (3) Evaluate the sustainability of the students’ computational thinking capabilities in learning in the medium to long term. Based on the experience gained in the implementation and the data analysis, the challenges and appropriate strategies for coding education in the local context will be identified, from which a pedagogical model and theoretical framework of computational thinking in learning can be derived. This model will contribute to both the field of learning science and K-12 curriculum development in Hong Kong as well as other similar education environments by providing research-informed advice on the strategies to adopt in coding education. 電腦編程一直被視為計算機科學教育的主要及必修科目。在近期的教育改革中，當中在K-12教育透過編程教育而引入計算思維（Computational Thinking）確有顯著增加關注的趨勢。編程課程已經轉化了美國及英國的K-12教育，而其中一個編程教育的目的就是透過引入相關編程的能力（如：計算思維、模型建立和測試、邏輯推理等），優化學生的解難能力。事實上，英國的教育局已剛剛修訂了現行K-12的課程，並把電腦編程納入四個學習階段的必修內容。但是，編程教育對於香港兒童的益處和挑戰就未曾作完整的 剖釋。雖然香港某些學校已經在電腦科引入了電腦編程內容，但是計算思維和相關學習活動的影響就暫未有研究結果。所以，研究編程如何在香港獨有的小學教育挑戰下培養學生的重要技能極為重要。本研究旨在：（1）探討透過編程教育訓練香港兒童的計算思維對於他們學習及解難能力的影響；（2）辨識編程教育的挑戰和發展出合適的策略來強化其益處；（3）鑑定學生的計算思維能力對於學習的中期及長期持續發展能力。在實踐經驗和數據分析的基礎上，找出在本地實踐的挑戰以及編程教育的策略，從而形成一個計算思維的教學模型和理論框架。這個模型將會對香港以及其他類似的教育環境的學習科學和K-12課程發展作出貢獻，並透過研究來指出合適的編程教育策略。

18615216.label: Realisation of objectives
18615216.value: A total of six schools were recruited and sampled to participate in the three-year longitudinal project, where each school was handled as independent cases in order to help realise different objectives. Since each school had a very unique teaching and learning arrangement as well as the teachers’ competence and readiness for teaching computer programming (or coding), the project was managed so as to work with these schools with unified research requirements, yet provided with flexibility to alter the teaching pace for each school as well as inviting them for different study within the project scope. Such that, all three objectives could be addressed through these different schools. A total of 506 4th grade students in the primary schools and 21 teachers were involved in different studies within this project, with 4 - 5 classes and approximately 30 students per class in each school. One of the schools was dedicated as a pilot school for scales validation and piloting the procedural aspects, including the administration of pre- and post-tests, testing the programming platforms in school computer labs, reviewing the computational learning contents and coding activities as a part of the classroom intervention. The researchers with computer science background provided regularly trainings to the school teachers, and participated in the teaching preparation meetings. More than 300 hours were used for the classroom observation and the meetings (including before and after each lesson) with the school teachers as a part of the design-based research approach to satisfy the objectives. To address the first objective, this study adopted a mixed-method approach, based on the analysis of students’ pre- and post-tests, self-reported questionnaires on intrinsic and extrinsic learning motivation (i.e. interest/enjoyment, perceived competence, value/usefulness, relatedness), classroom observation field notes, and semi-structural interviews with both students and teachers. A three-year coding curriculum was designed as the intervention to cover the basic concepts of computational thinking and coding skills. A hybrid approach mixed with programming and unplugged (learning with “paper and pencil”) activities was developed to engage students in computational learning. To be more specific, the children’s computational thinking concepts and coding skills, such as sequencing, if-then-else conditionals, looping, algorithmic thinking, debugging, and parallel processing were measured. Due to the limited time and tight schooling schedule, only those concepts/skills taught in that the year were measured, except in the final year when students were in grade six that all the constructs were measured as the exist point. The final project in grade six adopted the problem-based learning approach to allow students to develop a program using Scratch programming, so that we can examine the impact of computational thinking in empowering students to express their ideas (i.e. building a game to promote the value of community service) through solving computational problems. To go beyond, children’s perceptions on developing 21st century skills (creative thinking, critical thinking, problem-solving) through computational thinking and programming were examined and compared to the whole student populations in Hong Kong primary schools. To address the second objective, teachers were interviewed each year after the intervention to reflect on the challenges and appropriate strategies of coding education, which aims to develop children’s computational thinking. The teachers were asked to explain their perception about coding education, the observation of the students’ learning during the instructions in classroom, and the challenges they faced when implementing the design of intervention. In addition, students’ motivation of plugged approach and unplugged approach was compared to examine whether these two common teaching approaches a meta-analysis was conducted to examine whether collaborative problem-solving had a higher effect compared to individual problem-solving in programming. To address the third objective, we tracked the same cohort of students from Grade 4 to Grade 6 for three years, and evaluated their developmental progress over the project duration. A pre-post-test was administered each year to measure the differences of their computational and programming knowledge. A final project was implemented to measure the accumulative effect of students in applying the taught computational thinking concepts and programming skills. The methods for analysing survey data mainly included descriptive statistics, paired-sample t-test, one-way and two-way ANOVA, and linear regressions, and factor analysis with R language and SPSS 24.0, for scales validation, content validation (supplemented with interviews of students and teachers), and measuring changes between pre- and post-test in each year. Interview data and observational field notes were analysed through qualitative coding process and thematic analysis to identify possible themes concerning the challenges and strategies of coding education implementation. Based on the above data analysis, two journal articles and one book chapter were published, and five journal articles were under review or soon to be submitted due to a large amount of data being handled from this project and intensive design-based work with six schools. One journal article will be drafted and submitted within one year. The realisation of the objectives as well as new objectives will be an ongoing process in this area of research, which will contribute to the general computer science education in Hong Kong and elsewhere.

18615216.label: Major findings and research outcome
18615216.value: (1) The grade 4 students who were a novice in coding during the first year of study generally demonstrated learning gains in simple computational concepts (i.e. sequences of instructions, if-then-else conditionals, looping). The students were able to operate a block-based programming tool, Scratch, to develop simple computer programs. The result also showed a significant increase in their learning motivation, creative thinking, critical thinking, and general problem solving. The learning gain was higher with plugged (programming) activities compared to unplugged (paper-and-pencil) activities. In addition, teachers who taught programming for the first time reported their teaching experiences that programming can enhance students computational problem-solving skills. (2) Students’ computational competence continued to improve differently across different schools. From two of our participating schools, the statistical results showed that students’ algorithmic thinking and debugging skills significantly increased through our intervention, with girls gaining more on algorithmic thinking. During the students’ learning process, we found that they demonstrated behavioral, affective, and cognitive engagement while acquiring these skills in schools. As the students became 5th and 6th graders, more learning contents and harder levels were added to the learning outcomes, which may cause the changes in their learning motivation and interest. In addition, a developmental progression exists among the aged 9-13 children in their computational thinking, but gender differences did not affect the acquisition of computational thinking. Collaborative problem solving and pair/individual programming was also examined through a meta-analysis, and found that the performances varied among different learners in different existing studies. (3) The sustainability of coding education in primary school is high with long-term impact. The students generally retain their computational thinking competences, while different teachers perceived the effect of computational learning differently across different schools. Given that policy support of the government, coding education has now become one major concern in primary school guided by a new educational policy document. (4) Analysis of observation and interviews with teachers showed that there several major challenges in bringing computational thinking education through programming primary schools. The findings revealed that a lack of supports for teachers education and in-service teachers professional development prevents schools from expanding the depth of computational learning. Lack of time for technology education in primary school is an ongoing challenge. One feasible solution may be to consider re-arranging teaching time for coding and value the career pathway for technology teachers. Innovative pedagogies with advanced educational technologies for coding need to be developed and examined.

18615216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18615216.value: Continued research on children’s development of computational thinking across different ages, definitions of computational learning competences, pedagogical approaches, and assessment of computational thinking is needed. Follow-up studies may involve in-depth investigation of age differences in the development and designing a through-train primary school curriculum with different pedagogical approaches, then examine how students develop their computational thinking since Grade 1 until Grade 6, and to what extent the designs of learning and other psychosocial attributes may affect the different outcomes. It is also important to consider the perception and attitudes of students on computational participation through programming in early childhood, primary and secondary education and how to contextualise their computational learning experiences in schools. Besides, out-of-school experiences can vary, and parental influences and socio-economic status can certainly affect their levels of students' participations. It is crucial to explore how school can determine the levels of supports to provide an equitable approach for students to participate in computational activities.

18615216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18615216.value: This project aims to advocate the computational thinking development through coding (or programming) in Hong Kong primary schools. We examined: (1) the impact of computational thinking education through coding in primary school, (2) the sustainability of students in developing their computational thinking competences through coding, and (3) the challenges in the implementation process of this educational reform. To investigate the objectives, the research valued the nature of longitudinal study to track a group of students from six primary schools, beginning in Grade 4 until Grade 6, and measured their performances within each year both their academic and psychosocial outcomes. The findings show a positive impact of computational thinking education through coding in Hong Kong on students’ learning in solving computational problems, as well as teachers’ teaching coding in primary schools. To the best of knowledge, all the participating schools are now implementing and evolving their own school-based curriculum and approaches on coding education. Hong Kong education policy has also included coding as one essential learning area in primary school. Multiple studies were also extended which branch out different research agenda, including but not limited to developmental perspective on computational thinking, collaborative computational problem-solving, and impact on artificial intelligence education.

18615816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18615816.value: Public support is an essential component in the legitimacy of welfare policies. Because the financing and provision of welfare ultimately depends on citizens’ willingness to pay taxes and insurance contributions, it is vital to understand public attitudes towards the social policy system and individual sectoral policies. This is even more critical for less developed countries which are undergoing major social policy expansion, such as China. While the structure of the Chinese social policy system is largely in place, low benefits, heavy contribution burden and unequal entitlements have been a major source of public discontent. Compounding these problems is the fragmentation of the system. As the country’s decentralized approach to social policy has resulted in different “worlds of welfare”, this remarkable sub-national variation may have shaped public attitudes, which in turn will determine popular support for social policy reforms in the future. In social policy literature, the self-interest thesis and ideology thesis have explained popular support for social policies, while in recent years the institutional set-up was found to be a critical factor in explaining cross-national variations. As the sheer size of China and the fragmented social policy system are analogous to a cross-national comparison, it is thus reasonable to hypothesize that the notable variation in local welfare systems also determines people’s attitudes. Which “regime type” tends to engender greater support? To what extent can institutional set-up, self-interests and ideologies account for the variation at both the individual level and collective level? Is there significant variation in public attitudes towards different sectoral social policies? What are the implications for future social policy reform and state legitimacy? These questions are of theoretical as well as policy significance but remain unanswered. This project aims to fill this gap with rigorous interdisciplinary investigation. We will select Guangdong Province and Gansu Province, which represent regions of high- and low-economic development as well as different provincial welfare regimes, for analysis. A series of local welfare regime types will also be identified within these provinces. Employing a sequential exploratory research design, this study will use a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods in data collection and analysis. Upon completion, it will advance scholarly understanding on public attitudes toward social policy in a populous country with substantive regional disparity, examine the robustness of existing theories in the Chinese context, and provide policy-makers with evidence-based recommendations on popular support for social policy reforms. 公眾支持對於社會福利政策之合法性至關重要。福利的融資和供給皆最終仰賴公民納稅及繳納保險費，因此理解公眾對於社會政策體系及具體政策領域的態度非常必要；這對於包括中國在內的很多正在經歷社會政策擴張的發展中國家更有重要意義。儘管中國大陸社會政策體系已經基本構建完畢，但較低的保障水平、較重的繳費負擔、以及不平等的福利待遇也為公眾廣為詬病。中國社會政策體系的嚴重碎片化使得這些問題更加複雜。由於中國大陸推動社會政策發展很大程度上依靠向地方分權，這實際上造就了很多個不同的『福利世界』。既然在社會福利上的區域分化如此顯著，我們或許可以認為它在很大程度上亦塑造了當地民眾對於社會政策的態度，而後者則會影響未來民間對於社會政策改革的支持。 在社會政策的研究中，自利動機理論和意識形態理論常被用來解釋公眾對於社會政策的支持態度。近年來，制度背景也開始被用於解釋公眾支持方面的跨國差異。鑑於中國大陸幅員遼闊，社會政策體系碎片化導致的地區分化已經類似於很多中小國家之間的跨國差異。因此，我們有理由假設，中國大陸地方社會福利體制的顯著差異已經對當地民眾的態度造成影響。何種福利體制能帶來更大的公眾支持？自利動機、意識形態和制度背景等理論能在多大程度上解釋個體層面及集體層面的態度分化？公眾對於不同領域社會政策的支持態度是否有明顯差異？這些支持和分化對於中國未來的社會政策改革乃至政權合法性有何影響？以上這些問題既有重要的理論意義，又有現實的政策意涵，但已有的研究尚未很好回答。 本研究旨在透過嚴謹的跨學科調查填補上述的研究空白。研究將選取中國大陸的廣東省和甘肅省展開分析。上述兩省分別代表了不同的經濟發展水平及省級的社會福利體制。每個省內也將進一步區分出不同的縣市級社會福利體制。本研究將採用次序性探索研究設計（sequential exploratory research design），並透過量化和質化方法蒐集數據。研究完成之後，將對在人口眾多且區域分化顯著的國家中公眾對社會政策的支持態度有更為深入的理論認識，並可以在中國大陸檢視國外既有理論框架的解釋力，並且為政策制定者規劃未來的社會政策改革提供實證建議。

18615816.label: Realisation of objectives
18615816.value: Through concerted efforts of the research team, this project has realized its research objectives. As stated in the mid-term progress report, Dr Ratigan, one of the co-investigators managed to secure additional funding that enabled us to include Hunan Province from central China into our sample. In the end, we had Guangdong Province, Hunan Province, and Gansu Province, representing eastern, central, and western China, respectively in the study. The geographic and socioeconomic representativeness has therefore been enhanced. Due to the difficulties encountered in household survey in Guangdong, as explained in the mid-term progress report (which was generously endorsed by the RGC panel member), we used telephone survey in Guangdong and Hunan while data were collected through household survey in Gansu. This decision was made collectively by core members of the research team in a serious manner, based on budgetary constraints and the keen desire to maintain essential standard in data collection. Overall, we are satisfied with the quality of quantitative data. The sample included 4,768 valid responses from three provinces. Aside from quantitative data mentioned above, we also conducted a series of in-depth interviews with ordinary citizens, researchers, and government officials, which helped better understand the attitudinal patterns shown in quantitative results. This project will lead to three publications in peer-reviewed international journals. As of the time of submitting this final report, one article has been published, the second paper was accepted for publication, while the third paper was under review. The research team is planning for a fourth paper that may be published beyond this reporting cycle. Two conference presentations were made, with generous support from this project. In brief, we have found marked variation in Chinese people's attitudes towards social policy, as far as our data show, and the variation appears to be shaped by the sub-national variation in social policy and welfare systems. Clearly, the fragmentation of China's social welfare system, compounded by the decentralized ways of social policy reforms in the past three decades, has resulted in discernible cleavages in people's welfare attitudes. The three mainstream theoretical theses, namely, the self-interest thesis, the ideology thesis, and the institutional thesis, have all been found of explanatory power to varying extent in urban China. As reflected in the research outputs, this project draws important social policy implications; some of the key implications are summarized below. The first output arose from the pilot study of this project, entitled "Popular support form the social security system in urban China: evidence from a cross-sectional survey in a Chinese city". Published in the Journal of International and Comparative Social Policy (by Routledge), this sub-project analyzed quantitative survey data that we collected in Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province. In this paper, we examined Chinese people’s attitudes toward contributory social security programs. We embraced the bi-dimensional conception of welfare attitudes that synthesized the dual roles played by individuals in social security and examined their respective attitudes. Self-interest and ideology models were both tested in the Chinese context. As ordinary citizens, people’s expectation for governmental responsibility in social security appeared to be high. As contributors to the system, their willingness to pay premiums was also on the high side. Based on multivariate analysis, this sub-project provides contextual explanations for the attitudinal patterns observed in Zhuhai and interprets the results in reference to the international literature. Through this paper, we found that the social security system of Zhuhai received fairly high level of popular legitimacy that was arguably supported by the recent progressive reforms towards more inclusive social security system. The second output was entitled "Attitudes towards welfare spending in urban China: evidence from a survey in two provinces and social policy implications". This paper was accepted for publication at the Journal of Chinese Governance (by Roultedge) and is forthcoming in 2020. This sub-project focused on preference for welfare spending, a specific welfare attitude, and analyzed the sub-sample data from Guangdong and Hunan. In this paper, we focused on three social policy domains with distinctive characteristics: education, healthcare, and poverty alleviation. Empirical results show that all domains received fairly high levels of support for increased spending. Multivariate analysis suggested that self-interest and ideology were both associated with welfare attitudes in urban China, but some factors operated in unexpected ways, reflecting the distinctive socioeconomic and cultural context in which welfare attitudes are formed. Our data suggest that attitudinal cleavages in China may not follow a clear class line, but that support for welfare is strongly associated with ideology and personal values. This paper, too, draw useful policy implications. As quality of life improves in China, citizens may be hoping that the government will offer more robust social services. The CCP’s ability to meet rising expectations may be crucial in maintaining its popular legitimacy. The third research paper is entitled "Attitudinal feedback towards sub-national social security policy: a comparison of popular support for social health insurance in urban China". Submitted to the Journal of Comparative Policy Analysis (by Routledge), the paper is currently under review. In this sub-project, we engaged the policy feedback theory and focused on health care, a very specific social policy field. By analyzing the full-sample three-province data, this paper seeks to examine if attitudinal feedback explains the motivational basis of people’s monetary contribution to social security in urban China, a highly tangible issue for ordinary Chinese. The significant sub-national variation in China’s social health insurance (SHI) system and the co-existence of multiple policy programs offer an excellent avenue to do so. Quantitative results reveal clear attitudinal feedback effects. The structural characteristics of local SHI policies and personal experience with the policies appear to shape individuals’ motivation through interpretive effects and individual learning effects. This paper suggests that local policy institutions do shape people's welfare preferences and attitudes. As of the time of submitting this final report, we are working on the fourth paper that investigates if rapid internal migration in China leads to welfare chauvinism, by analyzing the data from Guangdong. GRF funding will be gratefully acknowledged in this paper. As the summary above demonstrates, this GRF project has yielded meaningful academic outcomes. We sincerely thank the RGC for generous funding and panel members for intellectual support.

18615816.label: Major findings and research outcome
18615816.value: Major findings and research outcomes have been elaborated in Section 5.3. Below is a brief summary. We have found marked variation in Chinese people's attitudes towards social policy, and the variation appears to be shaped by the sub-national variation in social policy and welfare systems. The three mainstream theoretical theses, namely, the self-interest thesis, the ideology thesis, and the institutional thesis, have all been found of explanatory power to varying extent in urban China. In output #1 (Popular support form the social security system in urban China), we examined Chinese people’s attitudes toward contributory social security programs. As ordinary citizens, people’s expectation for governmental responsibility in social security appeared to be high. As contributors to the system, their willingness to pay premiums was also on the high side. Both self-interest and ideologies are found to shape Chinese people's attitudes towards contributory social security system. In output #2 (Attitudes towards welfare spending in urban China), we analyzed people's preference for welfare spending in education, healthcare, and poverty alleviation. Empirical results show that all domains received fairly high levels of support for increased spending. Multivariate analysis suggested that self-interest and ideology were both associated with welfare attitudes in urban China, but some factors operated in unexpected ways, reflecting the distinctive socioeconomic and cultural context in which welfare attitudes are formed. Our data suggest that attitudinal cleavages in China may not follow a clear class line, but that support for welfare is strongly associated with ideology and personal values. In output #3 (Attitudinal feedback towards sub-national social security policy), we engaged the policy feedback theory and focused on health care. This paper seeks to examine if attitudinal feedback explains the motivational basis of people’s monetary contribution to social security in urban China. Quantitative results reveal clear attitudinal feedback effects. The structural characteristics of local SHI policies and personal experience with the policies appear to shape individuals’ motivation through interpretive effects and individual learning effects.

18615816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18615816.value: The study on welfare attitudes is not a trivial matter in authoritarian states. It is wrong to assume the inconsequentiality of these investigations in non-western-democratic societies simply due to the absence of competitive electoral links. Quite the contrary, the lack of such links in authoritarian states such as China actually prompts political elites to rely on public opinion data to understand popular attitudes and make policy responses accordingly. As indicated in the mid-term report, the fieldwork of this study was constrained by finance. The costs for conducting household surveys have galloped rapidly in urban China, especially in wealthy regions such as Guangdong. The proliferation of middle- and upper-class apartment complexes in Chinese cities has essentially made household surveys even more difficult because private security usually restricts enumerator access to units within the building. Yet, telephone surveys as an alternative means of data collection, are often questioned about reliability due to inherent weaknesses related to sampling. Social policy scholars thus need to develop stronger research protocols in response to these societal changes when conducting attitude studies.

18615816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18615816.value: This project seeks to analyze Chinese people's attitudes towards social policy and particularly examine if sub-national variation in social policy has resulted in discernible attitudinal cleavages in the society. While China is undergoing rapid societal changes and social policy expansion, the economic downturn and various socioeconomic challenges such as ageing population and reduced fiscal space, however, require the policy-makers to better respond to popular welfare attitudes of the citizenry. In particular, the fragmentation of China's welfare system has essentially led to different "worlds of welfare" within the same country. This project strengthens scholarly understanding on this fragmented welfare system and its attitudinal consequences. The insights generated from this project not only further theoretical knowledge on public opinions in social policy, but are also of reference value for scholars on other developing countries that are experiencing similar societal transformations and social policy reforms.

18618416.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18618416.value: 概念化與本土化如何彰顯在香港融合教育三層支援模式的實踐

18618416.label: Co - Investigator(s)
18618416.value: Dr Ho, Fuk Chuen Miss LEUNG, Ka-wai Prof Yuen, Celeste Yuet Mui

18618416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18618416.value: All schools in Hong Kong receiving the Learning Support Grant (LSG) are required to adopt the 3-tier support model (formerly 3-tier intervention model) within the whole-school approach framework as the means to achieve effective inclusive education. This model originated from the Response-to-Intervention (RTI) model in the U.S. that has been experimented with by researchers within the framework of a systematic instruction and assessment cycle since the 1980s. After a decade of implementation, scrutiny of the conceptualization and practice of the 3-tier support model from relevant stakeholders in Hong Kong has yet to be conducted. To offer theoretical, policy, and practical insights into the 3-tier model in building effective inclusive schools, the proposed project involves two phases adopting qualitative and quantitative mixed research methods. The first phase consists of qualitative case studies through interviews and class observation to examine from principals, special educational needs coordinators (SENCOs), and core subject teachers of 16 primary and secondary schools the following: (a) conceptualization of the model and roles of principals and middle leaders; (b) practice of the cycle of instruction-assessment and progress monitoring among teachers; and (c) participant challenges and suggestions for policy refinement, personnel preparation, and practices. A total of 32 parents of children receiving Tiers 2 and 3 services and their children will be randomly selected for interviews to gain insight into their understanding of the model and its effect on these children’s learning. Findings from the case studies and the existing literature will be used to finalize the territory-wide quantitative survey of the second phase. The effect of similarities and differences related to variables such as school size, grade levels, and number/types of students given different tiers of support will be plotted. Through capturing a territory-wide situation of how school personnel and parents conceptualize the 3-tier support model and its actual practice among core subject teachers (e.g., definition of quality teaching, decision-making and predictors for tier movements, and barriers in participants’ respective capacities), the project aims to provide much needed local data and indicators highly significant to local policy refinement, strengthening teaching quality, personnel preparation, and inclusive education practice in Hong Kong. In addition, the outcomes of this project will offer significant contribution to the international literature on cross-cultural conceptualization and practice of problem-solving multi-tiered intervention theories, as Hong Kong is the only region outside the U.S. to make such an approach the central feature of inclusive education. 香港所有享有“學習支援津貼”的學校均要在全校參與體系內運用三層支援模式(原三層干預模式)，以期達到有效的全納教育。該模式源於美國的干預-反應模型（RTI），後者自20世紀80年代在系統化教學與評估循環框架下廣泛受到研究者的各種測驗。然而在香港實行三層支援模式十年之後，關於該模式的概念化與實踐審查仍未展開。本研究旨在提出關於三層支援模式的理論，政策以及實踐的見解，以建設高效的全納學校。第一部分由質性個案研究構成，本研究通過訪問以及課堂觀察法調查來自十六所中小學的校長、特殊教育統籌主任及主課老師[1]對該模式的概念及理解領導們的角色；[2]教師在教學評估循環以及監管學習進度的實踐；[3]參與者面對的挑戰及對政策、人才培訓和實踐的建議。本研究还会隨機抽取32名接受2層以及3層支援服務的學生及其家長進行訪問，以調查他們對於三層支援模式的理解以及該模式對兒童學習的影响。個案研究與對現有文獻分析成果將會被用於編制第二階段的量化研究問卷，進而展開全港範圍的量化調查。各種相關變量，如學校規模，年級高低，及學生所獲得的不同數量/類型的支援等對模式產生的影響將會進行具體区分。通過對校長老師及家長學生們對三層支援模式的理解，以及主課老師的具體實踐调研[如：教學質量的定義，層級運作的決策和預測，以及參與者各處境中遇到的障礙等]，本研究計劃期望能夠提供所需的本地數據與資料庫，並設立本地政策精化，加強教學質量，人才培訓，以及全納教育實踐的預測指標。並且，由於香港是除美國本土以外唯一彩用該途徑進行全納教育的地區，本研究成果將會為多層次干預理論和實踐的跨文化研究的國際文獻提供重要資料。

18619616.label: Co - Investigator(s)

18619616.label: Project Objectives
18619616.value: To experimentally determine the effects of a daytime nap on three kinds of emotion-related cognitive functions, including (1) emotional memory, (2) emotional reactivity, and (3) inhibitory control in the affective domain in healthy young adults. To examine if the electroencephalographic (EEG) characteristics, namely REM sleep duration and latency in the nap are associated with post-nap changes in emotional and cognitive functions. To investigate the impact of prior chronic sleep restriction on the relationship between napping and emotional processing. To explore the potential effects of pre-existing sleep patterns on the EEG features of the experimental nap. To explore the potential associations between the EEG features of the nap and subsequent nighttime sleep.

18619616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18619616.value: 儘管長期以來白天小睡存在於許多文化中，其對認知和情緒功能的影響只是最近的科研課題。而相對於一些廣泛研究並已發展得相當成熟的課題，如有關夜間睡眠時間和情感功能質量關係的研究，過往關於小睡的研究只集中探討小睡對新知識或技能的影響。透過已驗証過的實驗，此研究旨在探討日間小睡對受試者 (正常/慢性/習慣性地限制睡眠的在校大學生)三種情緒處理的影響：情緒記憶，情緒反應，對情感方面的抑制。我們的主要研究假設是：（1）與沒有小睡機會的組別相比，有小睡機會的組別會：（一）對情緒的刺激物有更好的識別記憶; （2）對負面價值的刺激物反應度降低; 和（3）較好地抑制; （二）小睡對情感處理的效益將與睡眠結構/腦電圖（EEG）功能相關，如小睡，主軸睡眠及慢波睡眠期間快速動眼期的持續和延遲時間; 以及（三），小睡對習慣睡眠限制的小組會比平時睡眠正常的小組有較大的好處。此外，我們將探索小睡腦電圖結構對現有睡眠質量的潛在影響及其與實驗後夜間睡眠可能的關聯。我們計劃測試80位報稱習慣睡眠限制和80位報稱習慣睡眠正常的大學生。參與者將被隨機分配到"小睡"或"清醒"狀況。所有參加者將於第1天完成情緒，智能，睡眠，小睡習慣和看法的評估。參加者將在第6日於"小睡"或"清醒"的前和後進行情感和認知功能測試。參與者在睡眠期間將接受多導睡眠圖的檢測，他們的睡眠習慣也將會以腕動計和睡眠日記來檢測。研究結果將對睡眠科學帶來新的知識，尤其是白天小睡對情感處理中電生理性的作用，及其與原有睡眠模式的互動。此新資訊將會協助大學生和其他人群善用午睡以提高白天的情緒運作，及補償夜間睡眠不足等問題。

18619616.label: Realisation of objectives
18619616.value: All study objectives were realized. As mood problems are common in emerging adults, we conducted structured clinical interview and self-reported mood measures on all participants, and the presence of depressive/anxiety disorders was used as another between-subject factor in some outputs. Regarding Objectives 1 and 3 on inhibitory control, results from our factorial model with test session (pre/post), group (chronic sleep restriction/normal sleep) and condition (nap/wake) revealed a significant 3-way interaction effect on the discriminatory index towards neutral, F1, 162=9.084, p=.003, η2=.053 and negative, F1, 162=5.635, p=.019, η2=.034 information, but not positive information, F1, 162=.305, p=.581, η2=.002. Participants with chronic sleep restriction who did not nap had significantly greater deterioration in their ability to inhibit responses towards neutral information, F3, 162=3.143, p=.027, η2=.120, than individuals with both chronic sleep restrictions who napped, individuals without chronic sleep restriction but had a daytime sleep opportunity, and individuals without chronic sleep restriction who did not nap. (Output 7) We further divided the nap group into those with or without a depressive disorder, and conducted another factorial design with one within-subject factor, time (Test 1/Test 2) and one between-subject factor, Group (Depressed-nap, Control-nap, Control-wake). There was a significant Time x Group interaction effect on the False alarm rate in the block with neutral face as target and happy face as non-target on inhibitory control task, F2,61=5.145, p=.009. Follow-up analyses showed that while Depressed-nap group showed improved performance on the false alarm rate after nap, t(19)=2.942, p=.008, the Wake-Ctrl and Nap-Ctrl groups showed no significant change across sessions, p>.05. (Output 2) For emotional reactivity, we compared the effect of daytime napping on emotional reactivity among individuals with and without an anxiety disorder. Results from the mixed factorial model with one within-subject factor, time (Test 1/Test 2) and one between-subject factor, group (Anxiety /Control) showed a significant interaction effect on valence for positive, F1,28=5.964, p-.021, and negative, F1,28=4.810, p=.037). There was also a significant interaction effect on arousal for negative information, F1,28=5.454, p=.026. Post-hoc analyses showed that non-anxious controls’ valence rating on positive, p=.017 and negative eyes, p=.008 become more towards neutral valence with arousal rating decreased, p=.019 while the anxiety group showed similar rating on these measures across sessions, ps>.05, without moderation effects of prior chronic sleep restriction/sleep duration. These results suggested that individuals without anxiety disorders benefited from a daytime nap in attenuating emotional arousal and valence rating towards emotional information. (Output 9, Output 5) For emotional memory, results from the factorial model showed a significant interaction on the response bias of stimuli with positive valence, F1,72=4.432, p=.039 and negative valence, F1,72=5.895, p=.018. Follow-up analyses showed that among depressed group, those who had a nap had significantly more negative response bias on the positive, p=.049 and negative information, p=.026, than those who stayed awake. The control groups were not significantly different on the response bias of both positive and negative information, ps>.05. Daytime sleep appeared to help depressed individuals to have a more biased memory recollection, including a balance between both positive and negative experiences. (manuscript under preparation) For objective 2, regarding inhibitory control, we found that the change in d’ among short sleepers with a nap correlated negatively with amount of REM sleep during nap, r(36)=-.406, p=.014, suggesting that REM sleep is involved in modifying responsiveness to emotional stimuli (Output 7). When we categorized those in the nap group into depressed and non-depressed subgroups, among the depressed-subgroup, we found that the improvement in false alarm rate towards neutral information (with positive information as distractor) was correlated with longer Stage 2 Sleep, r(20)=.788, p<.001 and greater number of fast spindle detected at O1 during Stage 2 Sleep, r(18)=.692, p=.001. (Output 2) Regarding emotional reactivity, after a daytime nap, non-anxious participants showed attenuated valence rating on the positive information, and such change correlated with duration of REM, r=-.444, p=.017. The non-anxious control group also had decreased arousal rating towards negative eyes and such change was found to correlate with duration of Stage 1 sleep, r=.478, p=.008. (Output 9) In relations to emotional memory, while we found the depressed group had increased response bias towards negative and positive information after the daytime nap, such change in response biases were not found to correlate with REM or other physiological factors measured during the daytime nap. (manuscript under preparation) Addressing the exploratory objectives 4 & 5, we computed correlation between EEG features of the experimental nap with pre-existing sleep patterns and subsequent nighttime sleep. Adjustment for multiple comparison was conducted following the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure with .15 false discovery rate, given the exploratory nature of the current correlation analyses. In terms of sleep quantity, 6-day average of actigraphy-measured sleep duration, was found to correlate with lower sleep efficiency, r=-.193, p=.03 during the nap. For sleep quality, poor sleep quality, measured by the total score of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, was correlated with longer sleep duration, r=.182, p=.031, and higher sleep efficiency, r=.190, p=.025, and shorter latency in entering rapid-eye-movement sleep stage (REM latency), r=.217, p=.033, during the nap. For circadian factors, inclination towards an eveningness chronotype, measured by the Composite Scale of Morningness, was correlated with higher sleep efficiency, r=-.184, p=.033, and longer duration of REM, r=-.193, p=.026, during the nap. Later sleep-wake timing, indicated by average midsleep time (computed by taking the average of bedtime to waketime, measured by actigraphy for 6-day before the nap) was correlated with shorter REM latency, r=-.238, p=.023, longer REM duration, r=.305, p<.001, and longer duration of Stage 1 sleep, r=.234, p=.008, during the nap. Higher variability of sleep-wake timing, measured by standard deviation of midsleep time, was correlated with longer sleep duration, r=.269, p=.002, higher sleep efficiency, r=.306, p=.001, shorter sleep onset latency, r=-.251, p=.005, and shorter wake after sleep onset, r=-.193, p=.031 during the nap. Poorer sleep quality, shorter sleep duration, later sleep-time, and more variable sleep-timing were associated with higher efficiency and certain REM features during a daytime nap, suggesting that the experience and the potentially the subsequent effects of a daytime nap might be moderated by one’s habitual sleep characteristics. On the other hand, no EEG features of the nap were significantly correlated with the subsequent nighttime sleep quantity, quality or circadian measures after adjustment for multiple comparison. (Output 12).

18619616.label: Major findings and research outcome
18619616.value: H1: Fully supported. For emotional memory, while individuals with depression exhibited a bias in discounting mood-incongruent information, they had increased negative memory bias to both positive and negative stimuli, indicating a “balancing effect” of daytime nap. For emotional reactivity, participants had reduced reactivity to stimuli of positive and negative valence after the nap, as indicated by decreased valence rating to both positive and negative stimuli and decreased arousal rating to negative stimuli, which supported sleep’s role in optimizing emotional processing and reactivity. (outputs 5 & 9). For inhibitory control, we found that participants with depressive disorders have improved inhibitory control, measured by decreased false alarm rate in responding to neutral face with happy face as distractor. While depression is associated with a bias to discount positive experience, our data indicated daytime nap reversed such bias. (outputs 2, 6, 8) H2:Partially supported. For emotional reactivity, the reduction of positive valence rating and arousal rating towards negative information was correlated with duration of REM and Stage 1, respectively (output 9); Improvement in inhibitory control was negatively correlated with REM sleep duration among healthy population, and fast spindle detected at occipital region at Stage 2 sleep (outputs 2, 6, 8). However, improvement in response bias in the emotional memory task was not correlated with EEG measures during the nap. Therefore, some particular EEG features were associated with improved emotional reactivity and inhibitory control after nap. H3: Partially supported. Regarding inhibitory control, participants suffering from sleep restriction and stayed awake during the day were found to have greater deterioration of inhibitory control ability than those who also stayed awake but without sleep restriction, or those who had a nap opportunity, while napping benefit inhibitory control to a similar degree on those with or without sleep restriction (output 7). Therefore, daytime napping seems to benefit emerging adults’ emotional processing, regardless of their baseline sleep duration. Habitual sleep patterns, e.g. self-reported poor sleep quality and later sleep-wake timing correlated with higher sleep efficiency and other polysomnographic measures during the nap (see section 5.3 for details). Furthermore, higher habitual napping frequency was correlated with longer REM duration, and higher rating on the belief that napping would improve their work efficiency was correlated with longer Stage 1 duration. Taken together, consistent with our exploratory hypotheses, baseline sleep condition and individual belief and habit on napping were found to affect nap architecture, though not the subsequent benefits.(output 12)

18619616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18619616.value: Having tested 200 participants, we noted some individual factors, e.g. napping frequency and baseline sleep quality, influenced the nap architecture. We plan to analyse the data on whether these individual factors (apart from sleep restriction as in H3) might influence napping effect on our emotional functioning measures. Having measured participants' negative mood and affective states, we plan to further analyse if mood and affective state might influence napping effect on emotional processing and whether sleep and manipulation on sleep might affect in mood and emotional functioning among specific populations. For instance, with this funding support, we have studied how sleep problems affected anxiety and memory functioning in compulsive checking symptoms (outputs 3 & 11). Partially supported by this grant, we also have explored the effect of daytime nap on risk-related decision making, which is highly relevant to emotional processing (outputs 1 & 10). Also partially supported by this grant, we studied attentional bias to emotional face (an additional emotional processing measure) among individuals with depression (output 4). Pending for further funding support, we plan to study the directional relationship between sleep patterns and napping habits with emotional functioning with a longitudinal cross-lagged panel design with some follow-up data we collected.

18619616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18619616.value: The primary aim of this study is to assess the effect of an additional sleep opportunity in benefiting emotional processing, a function which underlies various physical, psychological and social/occupational functioning. Our results showed that an extra daytime sleep opportunity of 90 minutes benefited how we feel, recall, and control our responses in face of emotional information, regardless of whether we restrict our sleep habitually, and without negative impact on subsequent nighttime sleep condition. Some specific brain electrical activities during the nap were found to associate with the degree of improvement of emotional functioning, providing solid foundation for further investigation of the neural mechanism underlying sleep’s impact on cognitive and affective functioning. In addition, individual differences in napping habits and beliefs, as well as habitual sleep-wake timing, variability and sleep quality condition all have significant relationships with one’s brain activities during nap, which potentially explains why individuals might have different perceptions towards napping or feeling after taking a nap. Our findings of the effects of napping on emotional processing provide scientific bases for napping practices for the general public and sheds light on the development of guidelines for napping as an intervention strategy in clinical populations.

18623516.value: 貧困人士的儲蓄與資產：一項在香港的干預性研究

18623516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18623516.value: Modern states extend a variety of social welfare benefits to their most vulnerable citizens. However, there are doubts concerning the effectiveness of various transfer programs. Alternative approaches to addressing poverty and related issues have been gaining currency around the world. One such approach is an “asset-based social policy” that empowers low-income people by helping them to better manage their financial assets. Through nurturing a habit of saving for the future and undertaking long-term planning, the poor can improve their financial capability to an extent that benefits themselves and society as a whole. By examining the impact of peer support groups and earmarking mechanisms on the saving habits of low-income families, this proposed study aims to shed light on asset-based policies in the Asian context. We intend to evaluate the effect of peer support group on savings among low-income families in Hong Kong, as well as to investigate the mechanism underlying peer support group operations in this population. Furthermore, we aim to assess the impact that earmarking savings for the education of children has on overall savings levels; this will be done by allocating funds equally between two bank accounts among low-income families in Hong Kong. In addition, this study will identify the mediators on the impact of earmarking on private savings. Finally, we will investigate the interaction effect of peer support groups and earmarking savings. When completed, the proposed study will be the first to offer insights into the impact of peer support groups and earmarking mechanisms on the savings rates of low-income families, and the related social policy in Hong Kong. The policy implications derived from this proposed study will be relevant not just to Hong Kong, but to policymakers elsewhere. 許多國家都為弱勢社群提供社會福利。不過，現實中，人們對各種福利性質的轉移支付的有效性產生懷疑。各國政府都在尋找解決貧困問題的新方案。其中一種新的方案是 “資產為基礎的社會政策”。此政策可以透過幫助貧困階層更好地管理自己的金融資產來改善他們的生活。通過培養其儲蓄資產和進行長遠規劃的習慣，窮人們可以提高他們自己的經濟能力來改善自我的處境。通過朋輩支援小組和對低收入家庭儲蓄習慣專款專用機制，本研究的目的是為亞洲國家提供“基於資產的社會政策”的經驗。 我們打算評估朋輩支援小組對香港低收入家庭的儲蓄的影響以及探討背後的機理。此外，我們希望評估子女教育儲蓄專款專用對低收入家庭儲蓄水準的影響。此外，這項研究將研究影響此儲蓄的對專款專用的機制。最後，我們將探討朋輩支援小組和專款專用儲蓄的互動效應。 這是香港的第一個觀察朋輩支援小組和對低收入家庭儲蓄的專款專用機制的研究。這項研究的結論將不僅有利於香港政府做出扶貧政策的決策，也對其他地區的扶貧政策有所啟發。

18665516.label: Major findings and research outcome
18665516.value: The major findings and research outocme are as follows: (1) Hong Kong’s retail demands for electricity and town gas are highly price-inelastic, with a -0.0194 aggregate electricity elasticity estimate, and a -0.1275 aggregate town gas elasticity estimate. (2) A 40% electricity rate increase reduces Hong Kong’s total electricity demand by only 0.81% and increases Hong Kong's total town gas consumption by 5.12%, chiefly because electricity and town gas are substitutes. (3) The decremental emissions of declining electricity consumption are weakened by the incremental emissions of rising town gas consumption. Therefore, the net impact is only a 0.24% reduction in Hong Kong's CO2 emissions. (4) The electricity demands' low price responsiveness has two important policy implications: (a) Hong Kong's demand-side-management should rely more on energy-efficiency improvements than price-induced consumption reductions; and (b) restructuring Hong Kong's electricity industry to introduce wholesale competition should consider the potential for large electricity price spikes and market power abuse in connection to price-inelastic electricity demands.

18665516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18665516.value: The potential for further development is to use a similar approach to estimate Hong Kong's vehicular fuel demands: gasoline, diesel and LPG. The course of action includes data collection, model specification, estimation of the demand system, and discuss the results in terms of price-management of fuel demands and other demand-side strategies to reduce Hong Kong's car dependence.

18665516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18665516.value: Hong Kong is an international metropolis with a strong economic performance that could not have been possible sans a superbly reliable electricity supply. The major source of local emissions, including CO2, is the 6,608 MW of coal-fired generation that accounts for 52.3% of Hong Kong's 12,625 MW of total generation capacity. The Hong Kong government's fuel mix decision to use more natural gas will likely trigger a 40% electricity rate increase. The project aims to answer three substantive questions: (1) What is the estimated reduction in Hong Kong’s electricity demand due to the projected 40% electricity rate increase? (2) What is the estimated increase in Hong Kong’s town gas consumption due to the same electricity rate increase? (3) What is the CO2 impact based on (1) and (2)? The answers are as follows. The 40% electricity rate increase is estimated to reduce Hong Kong’s electricity demand by only 0.81% and increases Hong Kong's town gas consumption by 5.12%. Further, the decremental emissions of declining electricity consumption are weakened by the incremental emissions of rising town gas consumption. Hence, the net impact is only a 0.24% reduction in Hong Kong's CO2 emissions.

21104716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21104716.value: The cortical sensory map has been a key object for studying expression, mechanism, and plasticity of perception. The brain map has been continuously reorganized through experience, which has been utilized as an indicator for detecting neurons’ adaptation, learning, and plasticity. In schizophrenia, one of the most common mental disorders in modern society, cortical sensory maps are often reorganized as a consequence of auditory hallucination. About 1% of the population is diagnosed with schizophrenia, which causes chronic cognitive and emotional deficits and is also comorbid with anxiety and depression. To date, development of diagnostic tools for schizophrenia has been limited. This is mainly because of unclear cellular and molecular mechanisms of the psychiatric disorder, which challenges tool development. Here, we propose to investigate neurobiological mechanisms of schizophrenia via utilization of brain mapping. Our preliminary results showed that a graphene-based electronic can successfully visualize the reorganization of a cortical map efficiently and reliably compared to a conventional brain mapping method. Furthermore, we found that an NMDAR-dependent cellular substrate, short-term postsynaptic plasticity (STPP), can be causally linked to aspects of schizophrenia. To empirically test this hypothesis, we will propose three objectives to identify a cellular and molecular substrate underlying schizophrenia via graphene-based wearable electronics. Objective 1 is to design a diagnostic tool for map reorganization via graphene-based wearable electronics. Objective 2 is to demonstrate a role of STPP in brain map reorganization, using two-photon calcium imaging, in vivo whole-cell recording, and electronic-based brain mapping. Objective 3 is to investigate the role of STPP in schizophrenia, using animal models of the disease and electronic-based brain mapping. These results would provide an invaluable asset for mechanistic understanding and clinical application for several psychiatric disorders in humans. 摘要 皮質感覺映射(cortical sensory map) 在近年來一直視為重要的科學研究項目，用於研究感覺的表達，機制，和可塑性。腦細胞定位(brain map) 透過經驗不斷重組，這已被用於檢測神經元的適應，學習和可塑性的指標。精神分裂症，在現代社會中最常見的精神障礙之一，cortical sensory maps通常因受到影響導致出現幻聽。人口中大約1％的診斷患有精神分裂症，這會導致慢性認知和情感障礙，並且也伴隨焦慮和抑鬱。迄今為止，開發治療精神分裂症的診斷工具為數不多。主因為目前對精神分裂症的細胞和分子機制的認識仍然不清楚。所以，我們提出透過腦細胞定位研究精神分裂症在神經生物學的機制。由我們的初步結果所顯示，可穿戴式石墨烯電子設備可以成功高效率地影像化皮質映射的重組，和相比以前傳統式的腦映射方法更為可靠。除此之外，NMDA受體依賴的細胞基質，短期突觸的可塑性(short-term postsynaptic plasticity, STPP) 和各方面的研究精神分裂症有不少因果關係。在實證假設的階段，我們憑著可穿戴式石墨電子設備來識別細胞和分子基質隱含的精神分裂症，從而提出三個目的。 一. 設計一個可穿戴式石墨烯的電子裝置用作診斷腦細胞定位重組的工具 二. 以雙光成像，體內腦整細胞記錄和電子腦細胞定位方法演示STPP在腦細胞定位重組的角色 三. 以患有精神分裂症的實驗動物和電子細胞定位方法研究STPP在精神分裂症的角色 在這次研究的實驗結果將可以對精神疾病的病理機制有更多的了解和提供臨床上作應用。

To test whether stimulating glucose uptake by GLUT1 and/or BSG1 overexpression can provide neuroprotection to cones.

21105916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21105916.value: 感光細胞是視網膜中將光信號轉化為電生理信號的神經元，是人類視力不可或缺的組成部分。視錐細胞對於人類尤為重要，因為它們負責高敏和色彩視覺，但是在常見的遺傳性失明如色素性視網膜病變中不可避免地死亡。視錐細胞的死亡不是直接由遺傳突變引起，而由包括氧化應激負荷和葡萄糖代謝不足在內等多種压力因素導致。我們的長期研究目標是通過調節視錐細胞的氧化應激負荷和葡萄糖代謝這兩個緊密關聯的因素，以研發挽救失明的基因治療方法。這個研究項目中，我們將針對葡萄糖代謝有關基因在正常和疾病的感光細胞中的功能展開研究。該研究的成功完成不僅將對感光細胞糖代謝通路提出更完整的分子機理，為糖代謝失調在神經細胞退行死亡的致病作用提供依據， 並且可能為視網膜變性疾病找到新的治療靶點和方案。

21105916.label: Realisation of objectives
21105916.value: Objective 1: To characterize the functional importance of GLUT1 and BSG1 in photoreceptor glucose uptake. The first part of this objective was to confirm that GLUT1 is the essential glucose transporter in photoreceptors. Out of the 10 glucose transporter genes, Glut1 is highly expressed in the photoreceptors. Glut1 expression was knocked down in the photoreceptors by shRNA, and as a consequence of Glut1 knockdown glucose intake was suppressed as assessed by the glucose uptake assay. Long-term Glut1 knockdown led to shortening of photoreceptor outer segment and reduced light response by electroretinogram. The second goal of this objective was to dissect the function of BSG1 in a photoreceptor cell-specific manner. There are two BSG splicing variants, BSG1 and BSG2, and BSG1 is the predominant form expressed in the photoreceptors. We found that BSG1 expression is greatly reduced in the retinas of several different retinal degeneration mouse models. As BSG1 has been shown to bind to GLUT1 and form a complex with GLUT1, we tested whether BSG1 is functionally important for glucose uptake in the photoreceptors. We designed a shRNA that specifically knocks down BSG1 without affecting BSG2 expression. Similar to, but to a lesser extent of, Glut1 knockdown, BSG1 knockdown resulted in glucose uptake reduction. There was a mild loss of visual function by optomotor assay and electroretinogram, which manifested in the BSG1 silenced mouse retinas later than the GLUT1 silenced retinas. Together, the completion of Objective 1 confirmed our hypothesis that Glut1/BSG1 complex is the key glucose import machinery in photoreceptors. Objective 2: To test whether stimulating glucose uptake by GLUT1 and/or BSG1 overexpression can provide neuroprotection to cones. The goal of this objective was to test the hypothesis that GLUT1/BSG1 downregulation is the major stress factor contributing to cone degeneration. AAV-mediated gene delivery was used to force GLUT1 or BSG1 expression in the cone photoreceptors in the retinal degeneration mouse model rd10. However, when GLUT1 or BSG1 was expressed singularly in the cone photoreceptors, no rescue effect was observed. When dual AAV vectors that express GLUT1 and BSG1 together, a small yet significant rescue effect was detected. At the same time, we also observed that AAV-CMV-GFP, which was used as a control, induced faster degeneration compared to untreated rd10 retinas. We further investigated and found that CMV is a cis-regulatory sequence that, when used in the AAV vectors, induces strong inflammation and toxicity in the retina. Therefore, the rescue effect of AAV-CMV-GLUT1 and AAV-CMV-BSG1 was underestimated. Our study suggested that GLUT1/BSG1 is the relevant therapeutic target for retinal degeneration, and optimal viral vector and cis-regulatory sequence are required to deliver the maximal neuroprotection to cone photoreceptors.

21105916.label: Major findings and research outcome
21105916.value: Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) is the predominant glucose transporter in the retina, and Basigin-1 (BSG1) is a transmembrane protein that has been proposed to facilitate GLUT1 to take up glucose as the main energy source for photoreceptors. We found that GLUT1 and BSG1 are highly expressed on the outer segments of photoreceptors, while they are significantly downregulated in the same cell type in the retinal degeneration (rd) mice. Via loss-of-functional study in wild type mice, we found that suppressed expression of GLUT1 or BSG1 induces shortening of photoreceptor outer segments and reduced visual function. When GLUT1 was overexpressed in the photoreceptors in rd mice, no rescue effect was observed; however, when GLUT1 and BSG1 were overexpressed together, a small but significant rescue of cone survival as well as cone functions was observed. The mild rescue effect may be due to the AAV toxicity, which was further investigated and discussed below. Our major findings suggest that glucose deficiency due to the lack of GLUT1/ BSG1 complex function may be a major contributing factor to cone cell death in retinal degeneration and that gene therapy that upregulates GLUT1 and BSG1 together is a possible method to slow down cone degeneration. During the course of this study, we discovered that AAV can cause toxicity to the retina. AAV is considered as a safe gene therapy vector. However, we discovered that some control AAV vectors could cause inflammation and toxicity in the mouse eyes, which induced retinal cell death and visual functional loss. The toxic effect of the AAV vector also reduces or abolishes the rescue effect of the same vector. We further found that the toxicity was associated with certain cis-regulatory sequences in the virus genome, but not with viral capsid or viral prep contaminants. The toxic cis-regulatory sequences commonly drive broad and strong gene expression in the eyes, especially in retinal pigment epithelial cells. We published these findings in Proc Natl Acad Sci USA in 2019 (Part C research output publication #2). This work guides us to further develop safer vectors that can be used in gene therapy clinical trials for retinal diseases.

21105916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21105916.value: For further development, we will screen for nontoxic AAV vectors with the cis-regulatory sequences that can drive specific and strong transgene expression in the two types of photoreceptor cells. Safe and efficient vectors will not only benefit our own research but can be useful to the eye research community. With the screened vectors, we will re-test the treatment of AAV-GLUT1/BSG1. The rescue effect of GLUT1/BSG1, which was underestimated by the toxicity of the AAV-CMV-vectors that were used in the study, may be further manifested. Another future direction is to combine AAV-GLUT1/BSG1 with the other neuroprotective genes to treat degenerating retinas. Our previous study has shown that NRF2 protects cone photoreceptors from oxidative stress while GLUT1/BSG1 protects cone photoreceptors from metabolic stress during retinal degeneration. Additive rescue effect of AAV-GLUT1/BSG1 and AAV-NRF2 may further prolong cone cells and vision in retinal degeneration.

21105916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21105916.value: Many types of inherited blindness are caused by the death of the light-sensing neurons in human retinas, and they are currently incurable. To understand why the light-sensing neurons die is the key step towards the development of therapies to prevent vision loss. In this study, we tried to study whether cone photoreceptors, the most important light-sensing neurons which are responsible for human daylight vision, undergo cell death at the late stage of the blinding diseases due to insufficient energy supply. Our study focused on two key proteins, which are called GLUT1 and BSG1, that regulate glucose intake in the cone photoreceptors, and we investigated the functions of these two proteins in the healthy and degenerating retinas in mice. Our research is both basic and translational, as it not only provided new insights of the metabolic regulation in the light-sensing neurons and the disease mechanism of retinal degeneration, but it also pointed out new methods to treat these diseases. The gene therapy vectors that were developed in this study and tested in mice are possible prototype of the therapeutic vectors that can be used in clinical trials in the future.

21106616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21106616.value: 在肿瘤转移中，肿瘤分泌的miR125-b对成纤维细胞分化的作用机制研究

21106616.label: Project Objectives
21106616.value: Quantify the uptake of tumor-secreted miR-125b by fibroblasts that reside in the niche of primary and metastatic tumors. Examine the influence of miR-125b uptake on the differentiation of fibroblasts to CAFs and identify miR-125b targets that mediate this effect.
rows: Quantify the uptake of tumor-secreted miR-125b by fibroblasts that reside in the niche of primary and metastatic tumors.
Examine the influence of miR-125b uptake on the differentiation of fibroblasts to CAFs and identify miR-125b targets that mediate this effect.

21106616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21106616.value: 全世界每年上万名女性死于乳腺癌。其中，癌症转移是其中最主要的致死因素。因此开发高效治疗癌症转移疗法至关重要。为了达到这个目的，这就需要了解在不同的肿瘤转移阶段，肿瘤细胞是如何与周边环境互相交流。在癌症转移时，肿瘤细胞释放大量外泌体。这些小体能携带并传送大量的蛋白和核酸到其他细胞中。最近的研究证明这些小体含有大量能影响基因表达的微小RNA(miRNAs)和小RNA。我们证明了分泌在外泌体中的一个miRNA家族,miR-200，能刺激癌症转移。我们的预实验表明了高癌转乳腺癌细胞分泌的一个微小RNA，miR-125b，同样在外泌体聚集。同时，miR-125b 在乳腺癌病人的血液中也升高。但是高表达的miR-125b对癌症转移的意义未知。正常细胞吸收miR-125b之后是否癌转？为了证明正常细胞能自然的吸收肿瘤细胞分泌的外泌体，我们建立能释放荧光小体的乳腺癌细胞。这些荧光小体大多被肿瘤成纤维细胞吸收。同时我们发现对成纤维细胞分化的抑制蛋白多为miR-125b的潜在目标。近来研究证明在心脏中，miR-125b对成纤维细胞分化肌成纤维细胞至关重要。我们推测在肿瘤发生中，外泌体中的miR-125b也能推动成纤维细胞向肿瘤相关的成纤维细胞进化。因此我们将定量检测在乳腺癌部位和在肺部的成纤维细胞是如何吸收外泌体中的miR-125b。进一步检验miR-125b的吸收是否影响成纤维细胞的分化。这项研究将证明外泌体中的miR-125b在肿瘤细胞和肿瘤基质细胞交流的作用机制。这些机制将为设计新的抗癌药物提供帮助。

21106616.label: Realisation of objectives
21106616.value: We have completed all the experiments proposed and published 2 articles in Nature Communications (IF 11.8) and Journal of Extracellular Vesicles (IF 11). There was no problem in archiving the proposed objectives. 1. Objective 1: Quantify the uptake of tumor-secreted miR-125b by fibroblasts that reside in the niche of primary and metastatic tumors. To label EVs from tumor cells, we transduced mouse breast cancer 4TO7 cells with a lentiviral plasmid expressing a CD63-GFP fusion protein. 4TO7-CD63-GFP cells were implanted into the mammary fat pad (MFPs) of SCID mice. We were able to detect GFP in 30% of the total population of dissociated cells from the 4TO7-CD63-GFP tumor. FACS analysis revealed that CD140a+ fibroblasts took up GFP-labeled EVs from 4TO7-CD63-GFP cells at the highest frequency. To examine the distribution of EVs derived from human tumor cells, we transduced the human breast cancer cell line MCF10CA1a (CA1a) with a lentivirus carrying the CD63-GFP expression vector. Compared to the unlabeled CA1a tumors, 41.8% of the CD140a+ cells were positive for GFP, which was higher than the percentage of GFP+ cells within the endothelial and leukocyte populations. To confirm the distribution pattern of tumor EVs, we generated a CA1a cell line expressing an mCherry transgene that had a transmembrane domain. CA1a with surface mCherry cells were implanted in the MFPs of NSG mice and tumors were analyzed as described for the experiment with CA1a-CD63-GFP cells. The uptake of mCherry+ EVs by fibroblasts was higher than by leukocytes and endothelial cells. Furthermore, the uptake of mCherry+ EVs by CAFs was confirmed by the colocalization of mCherry and αSMA in sections of CA1a-SmCherry tumors. We confirmed the presence of miR-125b in the SEC-purified 4T1 EVs using qRT-PCR. Treatment of the EVs with RNase did not reduce the level of miR-125b significantly unless the EVs were co-treated with Triton X, which degraded the EV membrane. Hence, miR-125b was protected within the intact EVs from RNase degradation, as expected for a bona fide EV-miRNA. We isolated primary adult tissue fibroblasts (mATFs) from mouse ears and incubated them with PKH26-labeled 4T1 EVs for 24 hours. Treatment of mATFs with EVs from 4T1 cells resulted in the uptake of the EVs by 90-99% of the cells with little background uptake from the PBS control fractions. Furthermore, incubation of mATFs with 4T1 EVs significantly increased mature miR-125b. The uptake of 4T1 EVs also led to upregulation of CAF markers, including Acta2 (the gene encoding for αSMA), Mmp2, and Mmp3 in mATFs. Taken together, these data indicate that cultured fibroblasts are efficiently targeted by tumor EVs, which deliver miR-125b cargo to the fibroblasts. AIM 2: Examine the influence of miR-125b uptake on the differentiation of fibroblasts to CAFs and identify miR-125b targets that mediate this effect. To examine the effect of tumor EVs in vivo, we co-injected 4TO7 cells with 4T1-derived EVs into the flanks of wildtype mice. After 3 weeks, CD140a+ fibroblasts significantly increased by flow cytometry analysis in tumors treated with 4T1 EVs. Consistent with these data, immunohistochemical analysis showed a significant increase of the CAF marker αSma in tumors treated with 4T1 EVs To test the function of miR-125b in 4T1 EVs, we electroporated the EVs with antisense oligonucleotides (ASO) against miR-125b and co-injected 4TO7 cells with these EVs. The percentage of CD140a+ fibroblasts increased in 4TO7 tumors after treatment with NC-ASO-loaded 4T1 EVs but not after treatment with 125b-ASO-loaded 4T1 EVs. These data suggest that miR-125b activates resident fibroblasts into CAFs, which is mediated by uptake of miR-125b from tumor EVs, in combination with endogenous miR-125b. To examine the functional impact of miR-125b-activated fibroblasts on cancer progression, we isolated fibroblasts from 4TO7 tumors, transfected them with NC-ASO or 125b-ASO to inhibit miR-125b and co-injected them with 4TO7 cells at a 2:1 ratio into the MFP of BALB/c mice. As expected, transfection of 125b-ASO suppressed the level of mature miR-125b, including both endogenous miR-125b and EV-delivered miR-125b from 4TO7 tumor cells, in fibroblasts. Tumor growth was significantly reduced with knockdown of miR-125b in tumor fibroblasts. The metastatic areas in the lungs were significantly reduced in mice bearing tumors with miR-125b-depleted fibroblasts compared to the controls. Therefore, miR-125b plays an important role in activating fibroblasts to support tumor growth and metastasis. To understand the mechanism of miR-125b action, we overexpressed miR-125b in mATFs by transfection of miR-125b mimics. miR-125b transfection led to more than 50-fold overexpression of miR-125b and upregulation of several CAF markers including Acta2, Fgf2, Mmp2 and Mmp3, compared to transfection with NC mimics. Both immunostaining and Western blot confirmed the upregulation of αSma protein in mATFs upon overexpression of miR-125b. Overexpression of miR-125b also increased invasion of mATFs dramatically according to a matrigel transwell invasion assay. qRT-PCR analysis revealed that miR-125b suppressed several targets in the p53 network, which we identified previously, including Bak-1, Ppp1ca, Ppp2ca, Prkra, and Tp53inp1. Because Tp53inp1 was downregulated the most by miR-125b mimics, we selected it for further investigation. Incubation of mATFs with EVs purified from 4T1 cells significantly downregulated Tp53inp1. qRT-PCR analysis confirmed the knockdown of Tp53inp1 and demonstrated significant upregulation of CAF markers including Acta2, Cxcl12 and Mmp2 after transfection of Tp53inp1 targeting siRNAs. Knockdown of Tp53inp1 also upregulated αSma protein. These data suggest that Tp53inp1 is a key target that mediates the function of miR-125b in differentiation of fibroblasts in mice. As models of human breast cancer, we implanted CA1a cells or two other human triple-negative breast cancer cell lines, BPLER and MDA-MB-231, in the MFPs of nude mice and let tumors develop for 12 weeks until they reached ~15 mm in diameter. We found that the level of miR-125b in total blood RNA was significantly higher in mice bearing CA1a tumors, BPLER tumors or MB-231 tumors compared to those without any tumor. qRT-PCR revealed that miR-125b was abundant in the purified CA1a EVs and was protected from RNase degradation. To examine further the function of miR-125b in human fibroblasts, we overexpressed miR-125b in human fetal tissue fibroblasts (hFTFs) by transfecting miR-125b mimics. This approach increased miR-125b ~30 fold, and resulted in upregulation of CAF markers, including ACTA2, FGF2 and TGFB1 relative to cells transfected with NC mimics. As expected, αSMA protein was also upregulated by overexpression of miR-125b. We also found that TP53INP1 is a target of miR-125b in humans, given the sequence conservation of both miR-125b and its binding site within the TP53INP1 3’UTR between mice and humans, and other mammals. Knockdown of TP53INP1 in hFTFs upregulated CAF markers ACTA2, TGFB1 and HGF significantly, as judged using qRT-PCR. αSMA protein also increased after TP53INP1 knockdown in human fibroblasts. We previously identified TP53 as a target of miR-125b in humans, but not in mice. Therefore, we knocked down TP53 in hFTFs and found that it upregulated multiple CAF markers, including ACTA2, CXCL12, CAV1, FGF2, MMP2 and HGF. TP53 knockdown also resulted in upregulation of αSMA protein. Taken together, we therefore propose a model of fibroblast differentiation into CAFs, in which EVs from breast cancer cells promote the activation of fibroblasts into CAFs by transferring miR-125b from EVs to fibroblasts. Furthermore, EV-borne miR-125b functions to suppress the expression of both TP53INP1 and TP53 in human fibroblasts. The same model is proposed in mice except that miR-125b acts through Tp53inp1, but not Tp53.

21106616.label: Major findings and research outcome
21106616.value: Our research supported by this grant illustrates the function of miR-125b in oncongenesis and in the intercellular communication of the tumor microenvironment. In summary, to identify host cells that naturally take up EVs from tumor cells, we created breast cancer cell lines secreting fluorescent EVs. These fluorescent EVs are taken up most robustly by fibroblasts within the tumor microenvironment. RNA sequencing indicated that miR-125b is one of the most abundant microRNAs secreted by mouse triple-negative breast cancer 4T1 and 4TO7 cells. Treatment with 4T1 EVs leads to an increase in fibroblast activation in isogenic 4TO7 tumors, which is reversed by blocking miR-125b in 4T1 EVs; hence, miR-125b delivery by EVs is responsible for fibroblast activation in mouse tumor models. miR-125b is also secreted by human breast cancer cells and the uptake of EVs from these cells significantly increases cellular levels of miR-125b and expression of multiple cancer-associated fibroblast markers in resident fibroblasts. Overexpression of miR-125b in both mouse and human fibroblasts leads to an activated phenotype similar to the knockdown of established miR-125b target mRNAs. These data indicate that miR-125b is transferred through EVs from breast cancer cells to normal fibroblasts within the tumor microenvironment and contributes to their development into cancer-associated fibroblasts. This research was published in Journal of Extracellular vesicles (2019). To develop an anti-miR-125b therapy, we created RBCEVs as a versatile delivery system for therapeutic RNAs, including short RNAs such as ASOs and gRNAs, as well as long RNAs such as Cas9 mRNAs. ASOs and CRISPR–Cas9 can be designed and programmed to target any gene of interest, including undruggable targets such as oncomiRs and transcription factors, for therapeutic purposes. Intratumoral injection of 125b-ASO-loaded RBCEVs significantly suppresses breast cancer growth and metatasis. We have filed a patent for this method and published another research article in Nature Communications (2018).

21106616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21106616.value: We have developed a new platform for RNA delivery based on red blood cell EVs and used it to deliver miR-125b inhibitors that suppress tumor growth. This is applicable to several types of cancer in addition to breast cancer. We are working on the therapy against miR-125b in leukemia and lung cancer. We are optimizing the surface modification of RBCEVs with nanobodies and peptides targeting cancer markers such as EGFR so that the delivery is specific to cancer cells. This would help us to increase the efficacy and reduce side effects of the treatments.

21106616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21106616.value: Every year, thousands of women around the world die of breast cancer. 90% of breast cancer deaths are due to metastasis, a stage at which cancers have spread to distant sites and treatments become ineffective. The development of effective therapies for cancer metastasis is an urgent unmet clinical need. This requires a thorough understanding of the evolving interaction between tumor cells and their environment at different stages of metastasis. Tumor cells release large quantities of small vesicles that can deliver proteins and nucleic acids to other cells. Recent studies demonstrated that these vesicles contain large amounts of microRNAs (miRNAs), small RNAs that regulate gene expression. We illustrated that one of the most abundant miRNAs secreted by metastatic breast cancer cells is miR-125b, which is also enriched in the circulation of mice bearing human metastatic tumors. Moreover, miR-125b levels are elevated in the circulation of breast cancer patients with metastasis or chemotherapy resistance. We showed that the secretion of miR-125b is important for metastasis. The uptake of miR-125b from tumor cells is essential for the differentiation of fibroblasts and endothelial cells to cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). As CAFs play a key role in supporting tumor growth and metastasis, small vesicles from tumor cells deliver miR-125b to fibroblasts to promote the conversion of these cells into CAF and promote tumor growth and metastasis. This study illustrates a novel contribution of secreted miR-125b to the crosstalk between cancer cells and stromal cells during metastasis. Such a mechanism suggests therapeutic approaches to targeting miR-125b in tumor vesicles for the treatment of breast cancer metastasis. Hence, we have developed a novel method to deliver the inhibitor of miR-125b to tumors, suppressing tumor growth and metastasis.
