21106716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21106716.value: 中樞神經退化性疾病包括帕金森氏症、阿滋海默症、杭丁頓氏症廣泛存在世界各地。然而因為神經的再生在中樞神經細胞是相當少有，目前對於這些疾病的治療仍是束手無策。因此，臨床上，當神經退化性疾病被診斷出來時，如何有效的減緩退化的過程在治療上更顯重要。 在我們先前的研究報告指出組織蛋白去乙醯酶1(HDAC1), 一個轉錄輔抑制物,扮演相當重要的角色在連接晝夜節律鐘的機制以及神經退化的過程。研究發現在神經退化的過程會誘發組織蛋白去乙醯酶1(HDAC1)移至細胞核外，以至於核內組織蛋白去乙醯酶1(HDAC1)含量下降。同時我們也發現組織蛋白去乙醯酶1(HDAC1)的缺乏會導致帶有轉錄負抑制回饋特質的晝夜節律鐘改變。晝夜節律鐘是一個內化性的節律器，負責調控許多基因的表達進而控制細胞傳訊的過程而產生每日生理的節律。因此，我們不難想像干擾晝夜節律鐘藉著其轉錄的過程會影響許多生理機制進而與許多疾病有密切相關。目前相當的資料顯示在帕金森氏症、阿滋海默症、及杭丁頓氏症的病患有不正常的晝夜節律鐘的呈現。同時，在缺乏晝夜節律鐘基因的小鼠細胞培養中發現突觸前神經細胞有退化現象以至於神經元和神經元之間失去聯繫。儘管如此，現階段對於晝夜節律鐘的干擾如何影響和參與神經退化的過程仍未有任何顯著的研究進展。 在先前的論述中，我們提到兩個要點：在神經退化的過程中，組織蛋白去乙醯酶1(HDAC1)的核內含量下降，以及在細胞缺乏組織蛋白去乙醯酶1(HDAC1)的情況下，晝夜節律鐘會受到干擾進而影響基因的表達。因此，我們假設神經退化會因著干擾晝夜節律鐘的機制進而加速其退化性的過程。根據這個假設，三個主要的研究目標將會進行測試：1）驗證在神經退化的過程中，組織蛋白去乙醯酶1(HDAC1)移至核外會進而干擾晝夜節律鐘；2）延伸於第一個研究目標，我們將會測試於不同腦區的神經元來察驗此現象是神經特有亦或廣泛性的存在。3)確認干擾晝夜節律鐘是會加速亦或延緩神經退化過程。於此研究計劃，聯接神經退化和晝夜節律鐘的機制將會更加明朗進而能解釋晝夜節律鐘的干擾如何參與及影響神經退化性的過程。

21200216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200216.value: 本研究提出FuseFab,一個新的基於光固化成型（SLA）的3D打印技術。本技朮將利用光固化樹脂的液態特性，支持打印成形過程可以直接在已有的物體表面進行，免去了精確測量和容錯調教的需要。我們的前期成果證明了在液態樹脂中插入已有物件並打印新的與插入物件相吻合的部件的可能性。我們將設計開發FuseFab的軟件界面，支持直觀的物件插入過程，並控制硬件部分進行精確打印。其中需要解決的研究問題包括，設計直觀的用戶交互，3D模型分析，以及改進現有的SLA 3D打印機的硬件結構，以實現把現有物件結合到建模和打印的過程中。在完成系統開發之後，我們將進一步評估系統的易學性、易用性以及對創意的支持。

21200216.label: Major findings and research outcome
21200216.value: We developed FusePrint as a proof of concept for FuseFab. It is a DIY 2.5D printing technique exploring the possibility of inserting everyday artifacts in SLA-based 2.5D printing. We experimented with how lighting condition affected the height of a printed object, derived a mathematical model, and applied it to the software part of FusePrint. We also explored the possibilities of inserting physical objects and conductive gel into the printing process. The workshops on FusePrint suggest the technique is easy to adapt for making objects that fit well with existing ones, and users are highly engaged in the printing process. More importantly, the workshops revealed various possible applications of FusePrint: mechanical fabrication, toy design, wearable accessories, rapid prototyping for interactive system, bioengineering, etc. With the FusePrint prototype, we fabricated the rings, the watch frames, and the twistable structures, to further support the exploration of tangible and wearable user interfaces. Expanding the FuseFab concept, we developed DupRobo, an interactive robotic platform for tangible block-based design and construction. DupRobo supported user-customisable exemplar, repetition control with command markers, and physical autocompletion by the robotic arm. A user study with 12 participants showed that the participants rated DupRobo as easy to learn and use. More importantly, DupRobo significantly reduced participants’ perceived physical demand, overall effort, and frustration in the process of block-based repetitive structure design and construction, while being compared to the situation without DupRobo. While this system is currently limited by the variety of the command marker and the speed of the autocompletion process, it can be considered as the first attempt to explore building repeated assembly blocks structure using physical marker-based command. The current system can be easily expanded with more functionalities. With DupRobo, we envision that the robotic assistant could provide tangible creative design support by duplicating, iterating, and experimenting complicated structure design with minimum input from the human designers, yet preserving the craftsmanship, the materiality, and the intuitiveness of physical artefact design.

21200216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21200216.value: The participants in the presented workshop studies were not asked to set up the FusePrint system from scratch, thus the ease of setup for FusePrint was not evaluated explicitly. However, one participant mentioned it would be time saving and cost saving to set up FusePrint at home. One important future direction is to modularize the FuseFab framework and ease the setup process. Another important further development is to expand the FuseFab concept beyond 3D printing, and explore the possibility of involving physical artefacts in other fabrication processes, such as laser cutting, to increase the accuracy of fabrication.

21200216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21200216.value: We investigated the concept of FuseFab which involves the insertion of physical objects during the digital fabrication process to increase the fitness of the fabricated product. As a proof of concept, we developed FusePrint. Using FusePrint, one can simply place an external screw thread or a cup, for example, into the photo-reactive resin during the printing process to print an internal thread or a cup holder that perfectly matches the shape of the inserted objects. In addition, by mixing liquid conductive gel with the resin, one can print customized touch-sensitive interactive objects that can detect multitouch points as well as gestures. We further expanded the FuseFab concept with DupRobo, an interactive robotic platform for tangible block-based design and construction. DupRobo supported user-customisable exemplar, repetition control with command markers, and physical autocompletion by the robotic arm.

21200816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200816.value: In human, the protein-DNA binding interactions are the central activities in gene regulation. In particular, DNA motifs such as transcription factor binding sites are the key factors. On the other hand, we observe that chromatin interactions are yet to be incorporated into the current genome-wide DNA motif identification studies in a systematic and computationally exhaustive way at the time of writing. To assess its feasibility, the PI has conducted a preliminary study to reveal the coupling DNA motifs on chromatin interactions in the human K562 cells. It has been accepted as a discovery note on the Oxford Bioinformatics journal in September 2015 with the PI name carrying the sole first authorship as well as the sole corresponding authorship. However, the preliminary study is based on an ad hoc computational pipeline and limited to a single cell type. Therefore, this project aims at developing novel computational methods, first-of-its-kind, for identifying the coupling DNA motifs on long-range chromatin interactions. It is novel because the past methods did not explicitly take the long-range coupling relationships into consideration. As evidenced by previous successes, it is planned to develop novel probabilistic graphical models for identifying the coupling DNA motifs. A mathematical example is given in the main text. (Phase A; Objective 1) Another aim is to generalize the computational methods (either the existing ad hoc pipeline developed by PI or the novel methods proposed in this proposal) to at least four human cell types for novel comparative genomics (e.g. K562, GM06990, IMR90, and H1-ESC). After the novel DNA motifs are identified, we propose to develop our own competitive-edge genome informatics techniques (with PI's past experience from the kmerHMM and SignalSpider studies published in Nucleic Acids Research 2013 and Bioinformatics 2015 respectively) to characterize the novel functions and properties of the identified DNA motifs. (Phase B; Objective 2) To achieve long-term impact, the identified DNA motifs will then be applied to high-impact cancer association and gene expression prediction studies (with PI's past human disease experience from the SNPdryad study published in Bioinformatics 2014). At the end of the project, the deliverables (the developed methods and the identified DNA motifs) will be released as open-source software and database respectively. PI's past PhD supervisor from Toronto, Zhaolei Zhang, has agreed to provide wet-lab cross-validations according to the support letter attached. (Phase C; Objectives 3 and 4) The overall research plan is outlined in Figure 1. 在人類中，蛋白質-脱氧核醣核酸相互結合作用是在基因調控的中心活動。其中，脱氧核醣核酸模體是轉錄因子結合點的關鍵因素。 另一方面，我們觀察到染色質相互作用還沒有被考慮於目前全基因組上脱氧核醣核酸模體的系統性鑑定研究。為了評估其可行性，本研究團隊已進行了初步研究揭示在人類K562細胞上的染色質相互作用的脱氧核醣核酸模體。研究結果在2015年9月已被接受及發表在牛津大學生物信息學雜誌上(本研究團隊攜帶唯一第一作者以及唯一的相應作者)。然而，初步的研究是基於一個特設的計算管道，並限制於單一細胞類型。因此，這個項目的目標是要開發獨一無二的的計算方法以識別遠距離染色質相互作用的耦合脱氧核醣核酸模體。根據以前的成功經驗，本研究團隊計劃開發新的概率圖模型用於識別耦合脱氧核醣核酸模體，相關的數學例子可在正文找出。 另一個目的是要應用及測試該些計算方法（無論是本研究團隊現有的特設計算管道或在此專案所提出的新方法）到至少四個不同的人細胞類型作比較基因組研究，以發現遠距離染色質相互作用上的耦合脱氧核醣核酸模體。我們建議，結合本研究團隊過去的經驗，來開發獨門的基因組信息技術來描述所發現的耦合脱氧核醣核酸模體特徵及其新穎特性。 為了實現長期的影響，已確定的耦合脱氧核醣核酸模體將被應用到高影響度的生物信息研究。最後，本專案所提及的計算方法及獨家數據將被釋放作為開源軟件和公共數據。多倫多大學的張兆雷教授已同意作出交叉驗證。

21200816.label: Realisation of objectives
21200816.value: (Objective 1) We have fully developed a computational pipeline [Wong et al., Bioinformatics 2016] and a customized probabilistic model (namely, MotifHyades) for discovering DNA motif pairs on the long-range interacting promoter-enhancer pairs with chromatin interactions [Wong, Bioinformatics 2017]. Two model training algorithms have been developed for efficient model building with linear computational complexity. In particular, we have limited ourselves to the promoter–enhancer regions since those regions are known to be enriched for functional DNA motif occurrences. In particular, we have generalized the model and discovered 18,879 DNA motif pairs in six human cell types (i.e. K562, GM12878, IMR90, HUVEC, HeLa-S3, and NHEK). (Objective 2) We have fully characterized the previously identified 18,879 DNA motif pairs in terms of their biological function and properties. The 18,879 DNA motif pairs are characterized in comprehensive genomic contexts: pairing distance, DNase accessibility, evolutionary conservation, gene ontology (GO), and motif pairing multiplicity. The results indicate that, if two discovered motifs under pairing are far from each other, they are under strong evolutionary selection pressures and could result in functional specificities as reflected by the GO terms. The results also indicate that evolutionary selection pressures may lead to functional specificity of the DNA motifs on chromatin interactions; such a hypothesis is supported further by the GO term overlapping fraction which is positively correlated to evolutionary conservation. In addition, we have characterized motif pairing transitivity which is defined as the phenomenon where, given one motif pair found on promoter-enhancer pairs, the motif pairing multiplicity of the first motif on promoters can be positively proportional to that of the second motif on enhancers and vice versa. Since DNA motif pairing transitivity has also been observed in the K562 cell line, we seek to investigate the motif pairing multiplicity again. However, since the previous study adopted an association rule approach to combine individual DNA motifs to form motif pairs, the original motif pairing multiplicity cannot be adopted in this study. Therefore, we have defined a general pairing multiplicity measurement in this study. With the defined motif pairing multiplicity normalized metric, we seek to study the possible generalization of the DNA motif pairing transitivity phenomenon to six human cell lines in this study. Interestingly, it can be observed that such motif pairing transitivity phenomenon is only slightly observable in the cell types other than K562. Lastly, we have also studied and found that the motif pairing multiplicity normalized metric is consistent across the 6 human cells. Very strong correlations are observed (r > 0.88, p < 0.001), indicating that the motif pairing multiplicities are consistent and transferable across the 6 cell types. In other words, if a DNA motif is found to be associated with multiple DNA motifs on chromatin interactions in one cell type, it is very likely that it will also be associated with multiple DNA motifs in another cell type of this study. (Objective 3) We have fully released the methods and identified DNA motifs as open software and public datasets on the following websites for public access: http://bioinfo.cs.cityu.edu.hk/MotifHyades Documentations have been provided for others to use the software and data. 21200816.label: Major findings and research outcome
21200816.value: We have formulated a probabilistic model framework for DNA motif pair discovery on paired sequences (namely, MotifHyades). In particular, two computationally efficient algorithms have been developed for probabilistic model fitting with linear complexities, MotifHyades(EM) and MotifHyades(Gibbs). With those algorithms, we have successfully run MotifHyades to discover 18879 novel DNA motif pairs on chromatin-interacting promoter-enhancer pairs. Those 18879 DNA motif pairs are characterized across different biological features, revealing novel insights into the gene regulation mechanisms under long-range chromatin interactions at the 3D genome level. The algorithms and resultant data have been publicly released for scientific reproducibility.

21200816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21200816.value: The MotifHyades framework is general and can be extended to more than 2 sequences. However, the expanded search space should be carefully studied and explored. Global optimization techniques may be needed for avoiding locally optimal model fitting. The MotifHyades framework can be run on the promoter-enhancer pairs in other cell types, revealing additional biological insights into the 3D gene regulation mechanism.

21200816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21200816.value: The nature of the research undertaken in this project is a basic research project with a strong emphasis on the intersection between computer science and biology. From the computational perspective, novel algorithms have been developed for pattern recognition on DNA sequences. From the biological perspective, the novel algorithms can be run for revealing novel insights into the gene regulation patterns at the 3D genome level. The significance of this project lies in the future precision medicine development where people will rely on the findings in this project to develop precise medical solutions according to the human genetic mechanisms discovered in this project, leading to side effect mitigation. The project also provides a platform for cross-disciplinary collaborations in Hong Kong.

21201216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201216.value: Robotics is identified as one of the key technologies for the next industrial revolution. Nevertheless, most of the focuses are on the robotic design of the control algorithm and the artificial intelligent system. In the meantime, the key component of the driving system for robotics, i.e., the electric machine still stagnates quite a lot. In fact, current research works on motor designs for robotics obviously does not match the robotic development. In particular, the motor drives for the robotics have two main driving strategies – indirect-drive and direct-drive. The indirect-drive strategy takes the merit of inheriting the high-speed motor design but suffers from the mechanical gear losses of wear-and-tear to achieve the desired high torque. Instead, by adopting the conventional low-speed motor design, the direct-drive strategy is free from any gearing problems but suffers from definite lower performances. Thus, a new breed of high-performance motor drives is pressingly needed to solve the above problems for direct-drive industrial robots and biomorphic robots, which should achieve the desired high torque around the speed range from 50rpm to 300rpm without any mechanical gears. Two major challenges are faced by the proposed motor design and control for direct-drive robotics. The first key challenge is how to design the motor topologies to incorporate the multipole winding arrangement or magnetic-gearing feature into the double-stator topology while offering the high performance and reliability for robotic operation. Another key challenge is how to control the motor drives to accomplish the speed-range extending and fault-tolerant operation. The purpose of this proposal is to develop a novel breed of double-stator direct-drive motor drives for direct-drive robotics. The objectives are: (1) to develop the double-stator direct-drive motor topologies, which offer the low-speed high-torque performances; (2) to develop the armature winding connection approach for range extension in the low-speed regions; (3) to develop different operation modes for fault-tolerant operation; (4) to develop a new numerical co-simulation approach to optimize the design parameters and motor performances; (5) to develop a new power electronic module to perform the double-stator motor control with different modes of operation; (6) to evaluate the whole motor drive system in terms of technical performances for robotic application and market values. 機器人技術被認為是下一次工業革命的關鍵技術之一。而當前機器人的研究主要集中於控制算法和人工智能系統的開發。與此同時，作為機器人技術核心的驅動系統部件，電動機的發展卻嚴重滯後。實際上，當前機器人驅動電機的研究已不能跟上機器人快速發展的步伐。 現今，機器人電機驅動策略主要分成兩大類，即間接驅動方式和直接驅動方式。間接驅動方式繼承了傳統高速電機設計的優點，但是需要採用機械齒輪減速的方式來獲得需要的低速大轉矩輸出，從而無法避免的帶來機械磨損和能量損耗。反之，如果採用傳統低速電機設計的思路，雖然可以實現直接驅動和消除齒輪帶來的問題，但是無法避免整體性能的降低。因此，開發一種可以有效解決上述問題的新型高性能的電機驅動系統則顯得尤為必要。該電機驅動系統應可以在低速區間50rpm到300rpm下運行，並為直驅型工業機器人和生物形態機器人提供所需要的大轉矩輸出，而無需機械齒輪。 針對所提出的電機驅動系統設計要求，存在兩個具有挑戰性的問題。第一個問題是怎樣設計合理的電機拓撲結構，從而可以把多極繞組或者磁齒輪效應的特點加入到雙定子拓撲中，以最終獲得機器人運行所需要的高性能和高可靠性。第二個問題是怎樣控制電機驅動系統，從而可以獲得速度區間的擴展和容錯運行的實現。 本項目針對直驅型機器人，致力於開發一種新型的直驅雙定子電機驅動系統。其目標是：（1）開發新的直驅雙定子電機拓撲結構，藉此提供低速大轉矩輸出；（2）開發兩套電樞繞組的連接模式，藉此擴寬電機在低速下的運行區間；（3）開發不同的電機容錯運行模式；（4）開發該類電機數值聯合仿真的方法，藉此優化電機設計和提高運行性能；（5）開發相應的電路模塊，以達到驅動電機和容錯運行的要求；及（6）在技術性能和商業價值方面評估該機器人電機驅動系統。

21201216.label: Realisation of objectives
21201216.value: The objectives are listed as below. 1). To develop the novel double-stator motor topologies for direct-drive robotics which can possess the high-torque output at low speeds with multipole winding arrangement or magnetic-gearing feature, and can achieve the speed-range extending by six connection modes of two-set of windings, as well as can offer the fault-tolerant operation with electrical-phasor reconfiguration of two-set of windings. 2). To formulate the design equations and models for the proposed motor drives with the analytical methodology; then to analyze the electromagnetic performance and optimize the motor design by electromagnetic field analysis approach. 3). To develop the new power converter topologies for the motor drives, which can perform the motor driving and the six-mode connections for two-set of armature windings. 4). To develop the new control strategies, which can directly drive the robot, and straightly extend the low-speed operation range, as well as readily accomplish the electrical phasor control for fault-tolerant operation. 5). To implement the whole motor drive system under the emulation of the robotic operation and evaluation of the technical soundness and performance. Based on the abovementioned objectives, the project has been successfully carried out as below. The project aims at design, modelling, optimization, analysis, and control of high-performance double-stator motor drives for direct-drive robotics. Specifically, the first objective is to develop novel double-stator motor topologies for direct-drive robotic applications, with the high winding-configuration flexibility and fault-tolerant capability. Three machine types, including magnetless machine, permanent-magnet (PM) machine, and hybrid-excited machine have been proposed for the direct-drive double-stator machine designs, in accordance with different power levels of applications. High-fidelity simulations are mainly implemented with the JMAG Designer tool. Two proposed PM vernier machines and a hybrid-excited flux-switching (FS) PM machine are selected for prototype manufacturing. Both the simulated and experimental results have proved the validity of the machine designs. The application performance for robotics are also studied. Double-stator machine topologies inherently accommodate the high flexibility and fault-tolerant capability thanks for their special configurations. Taking the newly proposed toroidal-winding PM vernier machine as an example, with the combination of the winding configuration and terminal connection diversities, the high winding-configuration flexibility and multi-mode operation have been achieved. So, it leads to the effective speed-extending capability. Also, through the integration of high winding-configuration flexibility and the electrical-phasor reconfiguration, the high fault-tolerant capability has been achieved. Furthermore, on the basis of the current research objective, further fault-tolerant strategies are under investigation for high-robust machine performances even under faulty occasions. The first objective has been well realized. The second objective is to formulate the design equations and models for the motors with analytical methodology. Then, the machine electromagnetic performance analysis and optimization are conducted. A magnetomotive-force (MMF) permeance and inductance model is built for the proposed hybrid-excited FSPM machine, which is with auxiliary of the JMAG Designer, Wolfram Mathematica, and MATLAB tools. Also, the effects of the double-stator coupling, hybrid excitation, and flux barriers have been included in the model. The proposed model serves as a reference for other double-stator machines. Moreover, the modelling of the proposed interior-spoke-PM vernier machine is also carried out. The complex configuration and the high non-linearity saturation under on-load mode increase the modelling difficulty. The sub-domain method has been adopted, with the rational structure simplification and consideration of saturation. Furthermore, the archive-based multi-objective genetic algorithm is employed into the optimization of the proposed machines, which is well fit into the contradictory optimization objectives. The archive is the depository of non-dominated solutions, which effectively avoids degenerate problems in evolutionary algorithms. The optimization procedure is conducted in JMAG Designer simulation tool. Meanwhile, when considering the different machine topologies, various multi-step optimization strategies have been proposed to reach the higher optimizing efficiency and accuracy. Moreover, the finite element method (FEM) is carried out for the electromagnetic performances of the machines. The multi-physics simulation is employed into the optimization of the double-stator PM vernier machines, which can reach a comprehensive assessment. The second objective has been achieved. The third objective is to develop new power converter topologies for the motor drives, which can perform the motor driving and the six-mode connections for two-sets of armature windings. For the three-phase double-stator machines, a six-phase voltage source inverter (VSI) has been designed and manufactured to meet the requirements of double-stator independent or joint control strategies. Furthermore, the mode switching strategy can be realized through the winding-connection change control, which realizes various operating modes. This objective has been achieved. The fourth objective is to develop the control strategies, which fit for the robot driving, speed extending under low-speed operating range, as well as the electrical phasor control for fault-tolerant operation. In general, the double-stator motor control is similar to the control of traditional single-stator motors. The field-oriented control (FOC) has been adopted for the proposed double-stator prototypes. The stable machine operation well emulates the robot driving, under the low-speed operation, from 20 r/min to 500 r/min. Also, a fault-tolerant motor control strategy has been proposed without the adoption of reconfiguration. Thus, for different faults, the reconfiguration process can be avoided, which can effectively reduce the control complexity. Thus, the fourth objective has also been basically realized. The fifth objective is to implement the whole motor drive system under the emulation of the robotic operation and evaluation of the technical soundness and performance. Three prototypes have been manufactured, including the two proposed double-stator rotor-PM vernier machines and a double-stator hybrid-excited FSPM machine. The whole motor drive testbed has been established, including a PC-based DS1103 dSPACE controller board, a DC power supply, a torque transducer, two oscilloscopes, a motor testing cabinet, a magnetic powder brake and a VSI. The basic prototype performances have been performed, which well fit into the direct-drive robotic applications. Combining the high flexibility of the double-stator structure, the multi-mode operation has been further verified. Therefore, the fifth objective has been well achieved.

21201216.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201216.value: In this project, the design, modelling, analysis, optimization, and control of the high-performance double-stator machines have been proposed for the direct-drive robotic applications, which generates abundant outputs. First, new machine designs have been proposed and achieved, including the magnetless machine, permanent-magnet (PM) machine and hybrid-excited machine. Specifically, a double-stator magnetless vernier machine has been studied for low-power-level robotic applications, with the high flux-modulation capability and high cost-effectiveness. The simple current control contributes to the strong flux weakening capability of the machine. Furthermore, in the double-stator PM machine design, a series of rotor-PM vernier machines, a new stator-PM flux-reversal (FR) machine with complementary stators, and a rotor-stator-PM flux-modulated machine have been proposed and achieved with different torque levels. In addition, the double-stator hybrid-excited FSPM machine has been proposed and studied. Compared with pure PM-excited counterparts, the hybrid-excited machine possesses the higher flux-modulation ability, with more complex configuration. Different machine designs well fit into different power-level robotic applications, and also serve as effective references for other double-stator machine designs. Second, based on various machine configurations, the different multi-step multi-objective optimization strategies have been proposed and achieved, which fit for different double-stator machine types. Also, the MMF-permeance model of the proposed hybrid-excited FSPM machine has been built, with the consideration of double-stator magnetic coupling, hybrid excitation and flux leakage. Furthermore, the electromagnetic-structural multi-physics simulation has been adopted into the machine optimization, for comprehensive performance evaluation. Third, the control strategies for the proposed double-stator machines have been developed and explored. Firstly, the double-stator winding configuration control has been proposed and investigated for the toroidal-winding PM vernier machine. With the integration of winding configuration and terminal connection diversities, the multi-mode operation has been realized. So, it can effectively achieve the speed extending under low-speed operation. Secondly, the DC-biased current control has been utilized on a newly proposed double-stator FSPM machine. Through directly injecting the DC current into the armature windings, the DC-biased operation realizes both the flux-weakening and flux-enhancing capability, without extra space occupation. Moreover, due to the double-stator structure, the inner and outer DC-biased current can be optimized independently, which has further improved the machine output torque. In addition, the FOC strategy has been employed for the proposed motor control. With the high winding configuration flexibility and fault-tolerant capability, the multi-mode low-speed operation of the proposed motors has been further verified. Thus, it proves that the proposed double-stator machines can well fit into the direct-drive robotic applications.

21201216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201216.value: This project has successfully developed the design, analysis, and control of the high-performance double-stator machines for the direct-drive robotics. However, there are still many unexplored areas in the direct-drive double-stator machine research. First, although the multi-objective genetic algorithm has been well employed in the proposed machine optimizations, other multi-objective algorithms can be further adopted. Comparison and discussions should be developed to find the optimal algorithms for different double-stator machine types. Also, the electromagnetic-structural multi-physics simulation has been included in the multi-objective optimization of the double-stator interior-PM vernier machines. Based on that, the thermal and vibration performances can also be included in the multi-physics optimization, which leads to a more comprehensive evaluation. Furthermore, the FOC motor control has been adopted, with integration of high winding configuration flexibility and fault tolerant capability. In the following research, more control strategies can be employed into the motor control, which may further improve the machine performances. Additionally, the double-stator machines accommodate the complex structure. Thus, the four-bearing double-side configuration has been adopted into the mechanical design. In the future, the more mechanical configurations with lower weight should be explored, which further improves the torque-weight density of the machine.

21201216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201216.value: Currently, robot systems are welcome for industrial applications, especially for repetitive or inaccessible missions. Compared with indirect-drive robotic system, the direct-drive counterpart leads to the higher efficiency, lower vibration and longer service life. While the direct-drive machine should fit into the low-speed operation with high torque and high applied force. The project presents the new double-stator motor drive topologies for direct-drive robotic systems. Double-stator machine is well fit into direct-drive robotics. The double-stator structure leads to the high torque. Also, as one stator breaks down, the other can still work, which improves the fault-tolerant capability. Moreover, double stators cooperate for different torque outputs, which improves the flexibility and extends the speed range. Based on the basic nature of double-stator machines, the novel designs have been proposed, which fit for the direct-drive robotics with different scales. The machine performances have been specifically analysed. Also, the machine geometrical topology optimization has been conducted, with different optimization strategies. Furthermore, the analytical modelling has been carried out, which illustrates the machine design from the mathematical perspective. Moreover, the current and winding control strategies have been explored to further improve the machine performances, which can well meet the requirements in direct-drive robotic applications.

21201316.label: Realisation of objectives
21201316.value: Objective 1-To design and fabricate electrospun nanocomposite super-hydrophobic membranes by enhancing the integral structure and surface of nanofibers to improve MD productivity and prevent membrane from wetting. We have successfully achieved our goal in Objective 1 by fabricating a super-hydrophobic nanocomposite membrane with enhanced permeability and acceptable mechanical strength by using Titanium dioxide (TiO2) and Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) as additives and a PVDF copolymer (Polyvinylidene fluoride hexafluoropropylene: PVDF-HFP). We achieved a contact angle (CA) >150 without any negative tradeoffs in other characteristics, including liquid entry pressure, thermal stability, and mechanical strength. Nanocomposites, versatile materials that enhance the performance of membranes used in membrane distillation (MD) applications, were demonstrated to be a simple and effective functionalization method for electrospun membranes. We incorporated TiO2 nanoparticles into electrospun membranes fabricated with different nozzle configurations (including single, coaxial, and dual nozzles). The addition of these particles to the dope solution increased the contact angle of membranes produced by the single and coaxial nozzles to 149.0° and 149.8°, respectively. Moreover, TiO2 particles deposited on the nanofiber surfaces resulted in a higher membrane porosity when compared to the electrospun membranes that did not incorporate TiO2 particles. Therefore, this study suggests that TiO2 embedded electrospun membranes have great potential in seawater desalination and RO brine treatment applications. Additionally, MD tests were performed with the CNTs composite membranes. The contact angle of the CNT membranes increased with increasing CNT concentration (> 150°), indicating greater hydrophobicity. Thus, functionalizing the membranes to increase their surface roughness increased water contact angles and hydrophobicity of the membrane. CNT membranes demonstrated a higher average water flux value (48.1 L/m2∙h) which was about 60% higher than that of the commercial PVDF membrane (20.2 L/m2∙h). Permeability increases with larger pore sizes, which is effective as long as membrane hydrophobicity is high enough to efficiently retard pore wetting. Including CNTs in the polymeric solution allowed us to achieve a hydrophobic surface and good MD performance while requiring a relatively small amount of nanofillers compared to other nanocomposite membranes. Based on these results, the CNT membranes fabricated in this study are suitable for seawater desalination MD operations, and more importantly, are an innovative solution to environmental challenges in water treatment. Objective 2- To demonstrate a sustainable membrane fabrication process using non-solvent polymers for developing robust, economical and eco-friendly membranes for MD Achieving this objective was challenging due to the large fiber diameter of the electrospun polypropylene (PP) membranes. A mounted heating nozzle was used for melt-electrospinning and we trained one master student and one undergraduate (Final Year Project) student throughout this objective. We added polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), a versatile material for modifying polymers with low surface tension and surface energy, to overcome the challenges posed by the fiber diameter. Through this process, we achieved a facile approach for membrane surface modification, which involve coating of the membrane surface with PDMS polymeric microspheres to lower the surface energy. This led to the E- PDMS membrane having a high productivity (34 LMH, 50% higher than that of commercial PVDF membrane) without fouling or wetting. We found this E-PDMS membrane to be a promising candidate for use in MD applications, such as concentrate and wastewater treatment. This outcome has been published in the Journal of Membrane Science and Environmental Science & Technology (ES&T). Dr. Alicia An’s paper "PDMS/PVDF hybrid electrospun membrane with superhydrophobic property and drop impact dynamics for dyeing wastewater treatment using membrane distillation" is listed as one of the Journal of Membrane Science’s most cited articles (top journal in the field of membrane science). Objective 3- To understand heat and mass transfer in electrospun nanofiber membranes when processing concentrate to enable long-term performance of MD Experimental results and mechanisms were validated by the proposed step-modeling approach. In order to theoretically investigate the performance of the MD process using electrospun membranes, a one-dimensional simulation model which considered both heat and mass transfer, as well as a transport model were employed. The driving force of the MD process is attributed by the difference in water vapor pressures (by temperature gradient) between liquid-vapor interfaces of the feed and permeate sides. As the transmembrane temperatures on both sides could not be measured directly, a theoretical approach had to be conducted to estimate those temperatures to predict MD performance. Our outcome was the first modeling approach dealing with heat transfer for explaining the enhanced flux in MD using E-CNT membranes. Objective 4- To innovate MD system design to reduce specific energy consumption by integrating AD In Objective 4, we found the experimental and simulation results demonstrated the great potential of the proposed MD-AD system using the composite adsorbent to sustainably provide fresh water and produce a cooling effect. The PI has been building an MD-AD hybrid system in which the AD’s evaporator is used to increase the evaporation efficiency at ambient temperatures while reducing the energy consumption of the MD component using the cooling effect generated by AD. Similarities between MD and AD systems, namely low operational temperatures and an ability to utilize renewable energy sources, draws positive consideration to their coupling. The PI has closely worked with a mechanical engineer, Dr. Edwin Tso, to realize this objective in the local context. In our recently accepted paper ‘Study of the Salinity Effects on the Cooling and Desalination Performance of an Adsorption Cooling cum Desalination System with a Novel Composite Adsorbent’ to Journal of Applied Thermal Engineering, we achieved this objective. To summarize, the synergetic effects of combined MD-AD cycles are expected to reduce the internal dissipative losses of evaporative distillation processes, resulting in a significant increase in water production rate and unprecedentedly low energy consumption. Last but not least, reducing specific energy consumption through the integration of AD into the design of an innovate MD system has led to two industry-ITC grant successes, which will allow further investigation into MD’s commercial availability.

To understand heat and mass transfer in electrospun nanofiber membranes when processing concentrate to enable long-term performance of MD
To innovate MD system design to reduce specific energy consumption by integrating AD

21201316.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201316.value: This research has advanced the fundamental understanding of the physiochemical qualities of optimal membranes for MD and a total of 13 papers were published in top journals while also contributing to two book chapters. The success of this project has created a foundation for MD’s application in coping with the future challenges facing the desalination market, with potential applicability to many other areas including wastewater reclamation, ultrapure water production, and the concentration of brines, which will subsequently continue with two ITF projects and two GRF projects. 1. We have fabricated a super-hydrophobic nanocomposite with enhanced permeability and acceptable mechanical strength using TiO2 and CNTs as additives and PVDF copolymer (Polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene: PVDF-HFP) as the matrix. J. Memb. Sci. 2017, 524, 712–720. J. Memb. Sci. 2017, 526, 395–408 Desalination 2019, 468 (June), 114054. Desalination 2019, 456 (January), 74–84. 2. We have further developed and tested the membranes with PDMS additives that are economical and eco-friendly, while keeping the enhanced qualities of the membranes. J. Memb. Sci. 2017, 525, 57–67. Environ. Sci. Technol. 2017, 51 (17), 10117–10126. J. Memb. Sci. 2019, 573, 570–578. 3. We presented the heat and transfer coefficient of the membranes created through this project. The membranes surface morphology will be further analysed using electron microscopy (Carl Zeiss, EVO MA 10) and transmission electron microscopy (Philips CM20 TEM). A capillary flow porometer (Porometer, POROLUX™ 1000) will be used for the measurement of membrane pore size, pore size distribution, and liquid entry pressure (LEP). Sci. Rep. 2017, 7 (41562), 41562. J. Memb. Sci. 2017, 526, 395–408. Desalination 2020, 475 (April 2019), 114148. 4. As the final stage, the hybrid system was tested for long-term performance and economical aspect study of the MD+AD hybrid system compared to that of MD or AD alone. J. Clean. Prod. 2020, 271, 122684., Applied Thermal Engineering (In press) 5. Two PhD students, two Master graduate, three FYP were trained through this project. 6. Outcome of this project had led to two ITF fund (ITS/262/17FX: A Novel Membrane Distillation-crystallizer (MDCr) for Zero Liquid Discharge and Valuable Resource Recovery and ITS/206/18FX Design and Development of a Novel Membrane Distillation Process for Textile Wastewater Treatment and Reuse for Zero Liquid Discharge).

21201316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201316.value: Like many other membrane applications, MD processes are not immune to membrane fouling and wetting issues, which are two the major issues that present hurdles to MD’s long-term performance. Based on what we have learnt from this ECS study, we intend to continue our MD research into membrane wetting and fouling, which occur due to the interaction between the membrane surface and the various foulants. This much-needed systemic study will analyse the role of the surface charge in attaining anti-fouling and anti-wetting properties in MD membranes, which will invigorate further research in this direction, bringing MD commercialization closer to fruition. In addition, we are currently working closely with local industry partners for the application of MD in water and wastewater treatment through an ITF project at the pilot scale. We are in the process of optimizing the system’s energy requirements and preparing an economic analysis to evaluate the scale-up or commercialization of the MD process in the near future.

21201316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201316.value: Scientists and engineers have continuously strived to advance desalination technology to ensure sustainable water production while reducing cost, lowering energy consumption, and minimizing environmental impacts. While seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) has become one of the most popular desalination methods, the process remains energy intensive and generates large amounts of concentrated brine as a by-product, which presents a major environmental challenge to most plants and is costly to dispose or manage. To overcome these drawbacks, membrane distillation (MD) has been gaining recognition, and studies on the development of more suitable membranes for MD have been growing. In this study, we designed and fabricated super-hydrophobic MD membranes by modifying their integral structure and surface to make them stronger and more permeable using an environmentally friendly process. We also gained an in-depth understanding of how these nanofibers work, providing much needed performance data. Finally, we have designed an innovative system that integrates MD with adsorption distillation (AD), which allowed for energy recovery, reducing the energy usage of the process.

21202816.label: Project Objectives
21202816.value: To design and develop an online learning framework for lifelong learning of a deep hierarchical neural network. The resulted approach will provide the ground for coupling experience and new observations as a robotic perception model. To design and implement a C/C++ library, namely libdeeprobot, that enables lifelong learning in an efficient and effective manner. The library will be lightweight, and its application will be in approximately real-time. To demonstrate the feasibility and performance of the deep-learning-based mobile robotic tasks, without using any hand-crafted visual features. The tasks include visual exploration and visual navigation using the proposed online learning framework. To construct an open-source dataset for both indoor and outdoor dynamic environments. It will be provided as benchmark for further comparison with other methods in the future.

21202816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21202816.value: We develop an online learning framework for mobile robotic tasks, such as visual exploration and visual navigation. Although these typical problems have been studied over the past decades, existing approaches mainly focused on geometric models (such as representations of occupancy grids and cost-maps) which could only be regarded as low-level intelligence without any cognitive processes. They encounter particular difficulties, such as system complexity and high computational cost, which quickly leads to systematic failure in large-scale and long-term use-cases. The objective of the proposed framework is to fulfill typical mobile robotic tasks using deep-learning, where the network is trained online with minimal samples. Generally, raw images are taken as the only input to the target mobile robot system, instead of hand-crafted features such as corner or line features. Though it is a difficult task, in an effort to use raw images as input, we propose and implement online learning algorithms for lifelong learning. It means that as long as the robot is in use, its experience and knowledge-base will be enlarged, such that difference situations will be adapted autonomously and incrementally. As far as we know, this will be the first framework of using deep learning for practical mobile robotic tasks, especially in visual exploration and visual navigation. Considering the state-of-the-art of the development of deep-learning, we regard this is the right timing to develop such a framework for robotic real-time applications. Since robots are working in a practical environment with realtime requirements, high efficiency of algorithms is required. Meanwhile, it is specifically challenging considering the variant illumination and perspective changes. For robotics, probabilistic approaches are usually adopted to deal with these uncertainties. However, these constraints are often not reviewed by existing libraries nowadays. Therefore, a novel library is necessary to deal with the special requirements raised by mobile robotics. As part of the outcome, the library named libdeeprobot will help with several practics of mobile robotics, including visual navigation with incremental learning, adapting to the environment dynamics. Reinforcement learning will also play a part in the library to realize adaptive control based on experience, instead of deterministic system modeling. A dataset that consists of both indoor and outdoor scenarios will be further provided as benchmarks for future comparison. The outcome of the project will also show high potential to use generic controllers or system-on-chip solutions for mobile robotic tasks, with applications of service robots, industrial AGVs and advanced human-robot interfaces. 本項目面向自主移動機器人視覺導航進行在線終身強化學習關鍵算法的研究。視覺探索與視覺導航已經成為移動機器人多年來的熱點。但是目前的方法通常是基於幾何模型的（如利用佔據柵格地圖進行建模）。由於系統的複雜性和高性能計算和存儲硬件的開支較大，通過此類方法很難在大範圍內，有效果的長時間運行，並適應不同天氣和環境的變化。 通過本項目的研究，我們將基於深度學習建立在線終身學習的最小性框架結構。將以原始的傳感器信息作為輸入，如原始圖片等，而不是常用的離散圖像特徵點等。通過長時間的經驗積累，機器人通過在線學習不斷更新其經驗，以適應環境動態。 作為項目的產出，我們將建立一個開源函數庫，實現在線深度學習系統，並提供相應的數據集。數據集將包括室內和室外同一場地的多種不同場景，這對於其他研究人員的研究也會是很好的對照平台。 同時所產生的系統將有望形成導航系統芯片，大量用於服務機器人和工業UGV系統。

21202816.label: Realisation of objectives
21202816.value: We have finished all the previously defined research objectives. For each objective, the realization is described in the following paragraphs. Objective1 We propose an online learning framework called Neural-SLAM for agents to explore and cover unknown environments based on sensor data. We achieve this by interacting reinforcement learning agents with external memory architectures, in which the external memory acts as an internal representation of the environment for the agent. We embed procedures mimicking that of traditional simultaneous localization and mapping inside a completely differentiable deep neural work, that encourages the evolution of cognitive mapping behaviors during the process of learning. We show that this approach can help reinforcement learning agents to successfully explore and cover new environments, where long-term memory is essential for making informative planning decisions. We validate our approach in both challenging grid-world environments and preliminary Gazebo experiments. We further extend it to real-world indoor and outdoor visual navigation scenarios. leading to publications: Jingwei Zhang, Lei Tai, Joschka Boedecker, Wolfram Burgard, Ming Liu "Neural slam: Learning to explore with external memory." arXiv preprint arXiv:1706.09520 (2017). Jingwei Zhang*, Lei Tai*, Peng Yun, Yufeng Xiong, Ming Liu, Joschka Boedecker, Wolfram Burgard "Vr-goggles for robots: Real-to-sim domain adaptation for visual control." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 4.2 (2019): 1148-1155. We propose a cloud robotic system, called RSE-PF, to support the hierarchical architecture for robotic perception (HARP) on a centralized server, and evaluate the feasibility, robustness and elasticity of the system with robotic perceptual tasks, including visual localization, semantic segmentation and remote driving tasks. It leads to the publications: Yun, Peng, Jianhao Jiao, and Ming Liu. "Towards a cloud robotics platform for distributed visual slam." International Conference on Computer Vision Systems. Springer, Cham, 2017. Jiao, Jianhao, Peng Yun, and Ming Liu. "A cloud-based visual slam framework for low-cost agents." International Conference on Computer Vision Systems. Springer, Cham, 2017. Objective2 We implement the cloud robotic system to support the HARP on a centralized server and implement a C/C++ library, called CppRobotics, for most robotic tasks including localization, mapping, perception, path planning and navigation tasks. It has been open-sourced at https://github.com/onlytailei/CppRobotics and has got great attention from the robotic community (600+ stars). Objective3 We propose an approach to provide deep reinforcement learning agents with long-term memory capabilities by utilizing external memory access mechanisms. We embed SLAM-like procedures into the soft-attention based addressing to bias the write/read operations towards SLAM-like behaviors. Our method provides the agent with an internal representation of the environment, to guide it to make informative planning decisions to effectively explore new environments. For more details about the exploration and experimental results, please refer to our paper: Jingwei Zhang, Lei Tai, Joschka Boedecker, Wolfram Burgard, Ming Liu "Neural slam: Learning to explore with external memory." arXiv preprint arXiv:1706.09520 (2017). We propose a learning-based map-less motion planner by taking the sparse 10-dimensional range findings and the target position with respect to the mobile robot coordinate frame as input and the continuous steering commands as output. We show that, through an asynchronous deep reinforcement learning method, a map-less motion planner can be trained end-to-end without any manually designed features and prior demonstrations. The trained planner can be directly applied in unseen virtual and real environments. The experiments show that the proposed map-less motion planner can navigate the nonholonomic mobile robot to the desired targets without colliding with any obstacles. The details of the planner and the evaluation results can be referred to our published paper: Tai, Lei, Giuseppe Paolo, and Ming Liu. "Virtual-to-real deep reinforcement learning: Continuous control of mobile robots for map-less navigation." 2017 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS). IEEE, 2017. We propose an approach for mobile robots to learn to navigate in dynamic environments with pedestrians via raw depth inputs, in a socially compliant manner. To achieve this, we adopt a generative adversarial imitation learning (GAIL) strategy, which improves upon a pre-trained behavior cloning policy. Our approach overcomes the disadvantages of previous methods, as they heavily depend on the full knowledge of the location and velocity information of nearby pedestrians, which not only requires specific sensors, but also the extraction of such state information from raw sensory input could consume much computation time. Our proposed GAIL-based model performs directly on raw depth inputs and plans in real-time. Experiments show that our GAIL-based approach greatly improves the safety and efficiency of the behavior of mobile robots from pure behavior cloning. The real-world deployment also shows that our method is capable of guiding autonomous vehicles to navigate in a socially compliant manner directly through raw depth inputs. The details about the indoor navigation and the experimental results can be referred to our published paper: Lei Tai, Jingwei Zhang, Ming Liu, Wolfram Burgard. "Socially compliant navigation through raw depth inputs with generative adversarial imitation learning." 2018 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA). IEEE, 2018. We propose an approach for mobile robots to learn to navigate in challenging dynamic environments via RGB images. To achieve this, we have to deal with the deal with the reality gap, existing between transferring deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies learned in simulated environments to the real-world domain for visual control tasks. We seek to tackle the problem by translating the real-world image streams back to the synthetic domain during the deployment phase, to make the robot feel at home. We propose this as a lightweight, flexible, and efficient solution for visual control, as first, no extra transfer steps are required during the expensive training of DRL agents in simulation; second, the trained DRL agents will not be constrained to being deployable in only one specific real-world environment; and third, the policy training and the transfer operations are decoupled, and can be conducted in parallel. We validate our visual control approach in indoor and outdoor robotics experiments. The details about the navigation in challenging environments and the experimental results can be referred to our published paper: Jingwei Zhang*, Lei Tai*, Peng Yun, Yufeng Xiong, Ming Liu, Joschka Boedecker, Wolfram Burgard "Vr-goggles for robots: Real-to-sim domain adaptation for visual control." IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 4.2 (2019): 1148-1155. Objective4 We release a dataset for indoor socially compliant navigation in an indoor dynamic environment for further benchmarking for the literature. The first-person view depth image, RGB image, social force, desired force and velocity of the agent are all recorded and included in the dataset. The final dataset contains 10,000 state-action pairs collected from social scenarios. The initial configuration (the position and velocity information) of the pedestrians and the agent are perturbed by random noise for each episode. The dataset is available at https://ram-lab.com/file/tai_icra_2018_dataset.zip. We also release a dataset for navigation in outdoor dynamic environments. It contains the raw data of a set of stereo cameras, a 16-beam LiDAR, an IMU and a GPS under both daytime and nighttime. The dataset was collected within the campus of HKUST and consists of the data of multiple rounds of the 1-KM loop. The dataset is available at http://gofile.me/4jm56/b21c5o4Lm.

21202816.label: Major findings and research outcome
21202816.value: As a summary, we have achieved the following facts in the period of this project. - We have published 7 journal papers, including those in the International Journal of Advanced Robotic Systems (IJARS), Biomaterials, Robotics and Automation System (RAS), IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (TASE), and IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). The topics range from robot navigation and exploration, deep learning, reinforcement learning, etc. - We have published 16 international conference papers, including ICRA, IROS, IPIN, IST, ICVS, and ROBIO. The topics range from robot navigation, exploration, deep learning and reinforcement learning, etc. - We have been finalized or won 5 best conference paper awards, including the best conference paper award of IPIN2019 and ROBIO2019. - The PI received the 2018 IROS Toshio Fukuda Young Professional Award and being recognized “For outstanding contributions to mobile robot path planning and control”. - We have graduated 4 Ph.D. students from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. - We have supported 3 international exchange students from Switzerland.

21202816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21202816.value: There are several aspects to further develop in the research route: Scalable learning system. The current hierarchical architecture for robotic perception (HARP) is able to achieve life-long learning for a specific robot among various tasks. The next step is to extend this system to multiple robot systems. It can be based on our recent research on multi-robot localization systems: M Usman Maqbool Bhutta, Manohar Kuse, RuiFan, Yanan Liu and Ming Liu. Loop-box: Multi-Agent Direct SLAM Triggered by Single Loop Closure for Large Scale Mapping. IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, 2020. Multi-sensor fusion. We did extensive research on the visual navigation of autonomous mobile robots. Most of the works are based on RGB or depth images. Since traditional cameras may crash in some challenging situation, such as the case with large illumination variation, we plan to explore the visual navigation with multi-sensor configurations, like Lidar-camera system and RGB-event-camera systems

21202816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21202816.value: The project completed the necessary know-how and prototype systems for an online life-long learning system for visual navigation of autonomous mobile robots. We propose a hierarchical architecture called Neural-SLAM for agents to explore and cover unknown environments based on sensor data, and conduct extensive research on extending the proposed visual navigation architecture to different types of challenging real-world scenarios, ranging from indoor walking pedestrian scenes to outdoor autonomous driving scenes. Both qualitative and quantitative results of our proposed visual navigation methods in various challenging dynamic environments validate the effectiveness of our visual navigation architecture. The research directly led to 7 journal papers and 16 conference papers, including two best conference papers. The conducted results may lead to a boost in not only robotics but also analytic research or neural science.

21203216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21203216.value: 多機器人自動倉儲物流

21203216.label: Project Objectives
21203216.value: Task planning for multiple agents: We plan to study how to achieve an optimal task allocation among multiple mobile manipulators, in order to maximize the throughput of the entire logistics pipeline. We will improve the traditional task planning techniques to make it scalable to the complex warehouse/factory environments and tasks. Multi-agent navigation: We plan to study the distributed multi-agent navigation technique in order to guarantee the safe navigation of mobile manipulators in cluttered warehouse/factory environments. We choose to use distributed techniques to avoid the centralized scheduling solution's problem in flexibility, scalability and robustness. Manipulation in limited space: We would utilize advanced grasping and regrasping algorithms to help a mobile manipulator to finish complex manipulation task in a limited workspace. We aim to improve the completeness and efficiency of the regrasp graph approach. Collaborative manipulation: Some complex logistics tasks may require the collaboration between more than one mobile manipulators. We plan to extend the dual-arm (re)grasping techniques to enable collaborative operations with multiple agents.

21203216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21203216.value: 倉儲物流的效率是目前很多工業應用的瓶頸。例如在電子商務中，物流的低效率導致了丟包、延誤等問題。在制造業中，物流的效率也限制了生產線的效率和可靠性。在本項目中，我們將使用多個移動機器人來實現倉庫的有效和可靠的管理。我們將研究如何使用優化在多個機器人之間規劃任務的分配；我們將研究如何使用分布式的避障算法來保證多個機器人可以在擁擠的庫房環境中進行高效的運作；我們將研究機械臂抓取和操作的技術來使得機器人可以自動地完成物品的抓取。

21203216.label: Realisation of objectives
21203216.value: For Task 1 and 2 (100% achieved): We have developed a novel data-driven approach for multi-robot collaboration, with publications C8.4, C8.9, C9.1, C9.4. Our method uses deep reinforcement learning techniques to get rid of fragile centralized control and allow for fully decentralized control without communication among the agents. The results have shown near-optimal behavior in dense warehouse scenarios with many static obstacles and even dynamic obstacles like human co-workers. Some of our papers are well cited: C8.4 got 93 citations, and C9.4 got 170. The developed techniques have been used in some of our industrial collaborators such as Dorabot Inc. in Shenzhen and Baidu Research in Beijing. In Baidu, some of our algorithms have been implemented in their Baidu Cloud system, and then have been used in some clients such as Beijing Airport. For Task 3 (100% achieved): We have developed autonomous robotic manipulation for complicated tasks of deformable object manipulation (Task 3), with publications C8.1, C8.5, C8.6, C8.7, C9.3 and C9.5. We have tried different learning approaches, including online learning, imitation learning and reinforcement learning to allow a robot to either learn from humans or learn by itself via trial-and-error. Our system has been demonstrated on a dual-arm robot and attracts wide attention in the robotics community. For instance, C8.1 has obtained 42 citations. C9.5 also won the Best Student Paper award in 2019 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Mechatronics Conference. We also enable a 6-DOF robotic arm to generate task-specific trajectories, by leveraging the algebraic structure (the Lie group) in the robot kinematic skeleton and developing GPU algorithms to accelerate the fundamental forward/inverse dynamics computation. Our method achieves> 60x acceleration, as reported in C8.2 and C8.3. We also contributed a survey paper about optimal robotic trajectory generation in C8.10. For Task 4 (100% achieved): We also studied whether and how the collaboration between more than one agent can help solve challenging tasks in an efficient manner (Task 4). We have developed systems for collaborative robotic manipulation using machine learning techniques, with publications C9.2 and C9.6. To achieve intelligent robotic grasping/manipulation task, it is necessary to develop robotic grippers similar to a human’s hand. Thus, we made significant effort to develop a brand-new underactuated robotic five-finger gripper which was published in C8.8.

21203216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

21203416.value: 擋土結構在地震作用下之受力變形關係與漸進式破壞機制

21203416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21203416.value: 擋土結構物是用來維持兩相鄰但具不同地表高度的土壤之間的穩定性的岩土工程系統。據估計（GEO 2002年），為了緩解因擋土牆崩塌而導致的死亡風險，香港政府每年需投入相當於港幣一千萬元的投資。除了死亡風險之外，每年由於擋土牆過度位移而引起的額外經濟損失風險（包括因相鄰建築物或設備受損導致服務中斷而損失的間接經濟成本）也相當可觀。因此雖然香港並不是位於地震強震區內，香港政府屋宇署已聘請顧問公司為香港量身定制適用於香港地理環境的建築耐震設計標準，這其中也包括擋土牆設計法規。在香港，擋土結構的設計目前仍採用傳統的極限狀態設計法（LSD）。這類方法只考慮安全性卻忽視性能，因此面對地震的不確定性時，可能會導致做出非常保守的結構設計。 目前，結構設計方法有從極限狀態設計法（LSD）往性能設計法（PBD）發展的趨勢，特別是在地震工程領域。性能設計法之所以會開始流行，是因為它不僅以明確的方式去考慮在抗震設計中不可避免的不確定性，也使得結構物整體的功能性目標（例如，“確保生命安全”）得以透過工程和財政手段予以實現。前述所提及的政府所聘用的顧問公司，也有考慮在香港抗震設計標準中採用PBD方法。然而，PBD的概念以前從未被應用於擋土系統的設計。為了將PBD應用於擋土結構系統的設計，所會面臨的主要挑戰在於如何精確地預測擋土結構的位移。這是由於結構物的變形直接關係到材料損壞，而材料損壞程度則是用來量化某系統的“性能表現”的重要指標。目前文獻資料中大多數的研究都著重於剛性擋土牆的位移估計（例如，滑動塊模式和偽動態方法），但這類方法所預測的結果的準確度是有疑問的，因為它們通常會忽視擋土結構的旋轉或平移位移模式中的其中一個模式。 本研究計畫旨在開發一種評估擋土結構頂端位移的分析模型。通過分析土體內部的應力和應變的分佈，在同時考慮旋轉和平移兩種位移模式的情況下，推導出擋土結構系統的力與位移關係。為了校正分析模型的準確性，將製作兩個中等規模的擋土牆結構模型，以實驗方式取得擋土牆在外力作用下的實際變形。最終的目標是訂出擋土結構的性能設計標準，並可被香港正在研擬中的新的耐震設計準則所採用。

21203416.label: Realisation of objectives
21203416.value: Objective 1: Extend the recently published Log-Spiral-Rankine model to enable the assessment of full stress and strain distributions in soil mass behind retaining walls during earthquakes. I had guided one of my Ph.D. students to discretize the backfill of the earth-retaining structure (ERS) into dices to observe the stress variations in the vertical and horizontal direction. Equilibrium equations were then drawn for each dice to connect the internal forces between dices with the external loads. A series of local and global iterative schemes were developed to solve the highly coupled equilibrium equations of the ERS system. Once the stress distributions are known, we developed another analytical method to compute the strain distributions from the stresses. The said approach correlates the stress to strain considering realistic nonlinear relationship between shear stress and shear strain, the effects of confining pressure, and strain compatibility via Mohr’s strain circle. Consequently, it implicitly takes the Poison’s ratio into account and its solution doesn’t violate the Generalized Hooke’s Law. I have already published a journal paper on the “dice method” for assessing the stress distribution in the backfill. Another manuscript for computing the strain distribution from the stress distribution is under preparation. Objective 2: Construct a relationship between the input seismic forces and surface displacements of earth-retaining systems. My research group have developed a simplified PYCAP model utilizing the hyperbolic function to correlate the input pseudo-static seismic forces with the horizontal surface displacement of the earth-retaining structure (ERS). The hyperbolic function essentially describes the pushover curve of the ERS, and it requires the knowledge of the system's peak strength, initial stiffness, and a parameter known as the "failure ratio, Rf". The peak strength can be determined using the Log-Spiral-Rankine (LSR) method my colleagues and I developed. However, the LSR method is tedious and complex to implement. Therefore, we proposed a semi-analytical approach to replace it. The initial stiffness of the ERS can be derived analytically from an elastic model proposed by Douglass and Davis (1964). Lastly, we reviewed a large number of published experimental test data then came up with an empirical equation to estimate the parameter, failure ratio Rf. With these parameters, the pushover curve of the ERS can be evaluated using the hyperbolic function. I have composed a paper on this topic (simplified PYCAP approach), which is currently under review. Objective 3: Investigate potential danger zones in retained ground during earthquakes. Over the past 3 years, I had recruited a few undergraduate and Master students to conduct a series of retaining wall tests to observe the development and evolution of shear-concentration-belt within the backfill behind the retaining wall. I utilized the digital image correlation (DIC) technique to observe the movements of soil particles so as to estimate the strain distribution in the backfill. Base on the shifting of the shear-concentration-belt, we can visualize the evolution of the potential danger zones behind the ERS. Objective 4: Perform experimental tests and numerical simulations to verify the analytical model. As mentioned above, in this project I have arranged a series of retaining wall test to collect the information regarding the stress distributions, evolution of the shear-concentration-belt, the influences of wall's movement modes, and the effects of sloping ground surface. Unfortunately, the test program was interrupted several times since early 2019, due to the disorder of actuator at the lab, the shutdown of university during the social turmoil in Hong Kong, as well as the preventive measures taken against the COVID-19 pandemic. As such, the progress of the experimental test program is significantly affected, and I was unable to complete this objective within the planned time frame. Nonetheless, I have collected sufficient data to publish one to two more papers. One of my Ph.D. students will continue to work on the experimental test program. My Ph.D. students and I have prepared a technical report, providing all the details of the abovementioned analytical models and the experimental test program.

21203416.label: Major findings and research outcome
21203416.value: -- We developed an analytical approach (known as the dice method) to estimate the stress distributions behind the earth-retaining structure (ERS) without resorting to the finite element method. -- We have proposed a nonlinear constitution relationship to evaluate the stains distribution from the stress distribution within the backfill behind the ERS. -- We investigated the significance of the key parameter, the failure ratio, in the force-displacement relationship of the ERS. We have come up with a simplified PYCAP method to predict the pushover curve of the ERS. -- We adopted the digital image correlation (DIC) technique and successfully disclosed the development and evolution of the failure surface behind the ERS. The potential dangerous zone is thus revealed. -- We have conducted a series of retaining wall tests to collect the first-hand data for verifying the analytical models we proposed. Unlike in most existing tests, our test program can provide new data that have seldom been reported in the literature, such as the distribution of stress and strain in the backfill, the evolution of failure surface, the influences of the wall's movement modes, and the effects of the sloping ground surface.

21203416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21203416.value: -- The knowledge regarding the strain distribution in the backfill of ERS can be used to estimate the displacements in the backfill. The results, in turn, can be utilized to develop the performance-based design criteria for the ERS. -- The pore water pressure can be introduced into the dice method to take into account the effects of the ground water. That being said, the dice method I proposed possesses the potential to evaluate the liquefaction problems. -- It is doable to extend the dice method for assessing the slope stability problems.

21203416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21203416.value: The project investigates the behaviors of the earth-retaining structure from both the macro (i.e., the force-displacement curve) and micro (i.e., the stress and strain distributions) points of views. A few computationally effective analytical models have been developed to estimate the stresses, strains, forces, displacements, and evolution of potential danger zone of the earth-retaining structure. An experimental test program has been carried out to obtain the first-hand data that can be utilized to verify the proposed analytical models and clarify some debatable assumptions commonly made by the researchers in this field. This study paves the foundation for future development of the performance-based design criteria for the earth-retaining structure.

21203516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21203516.value: 用戶與環境移動外包式交互的三位一體框架

21203516.label: Project Objectives
21203516.value: Human-ambiance interactions usually take contexts as input from dual sides, which are both the user's surrounding circumstances and subtle intentions. In this proposed project, we plan to investigate, 1) attention-awareness sensing, 2) emotion-awareness sensing, and 3) behavioral-awareness sensing, three crucial user intention sensing areas that cover a large application space. For this part of research, we will develop key technologies to address unique issues in different sensing scenarios caused by the contact-less nature of mobile sensors, so that our solutions could achieve accurate and robust human sensing results. Sensing data need to be handled within stringent delay deadline for promptly reacting to users. To this end, we plan to coordinate on-site mobile computing resources from the environment, and outsource the processing tasks to this formed computing edge for a local data digestion and prompt reaction. For this part of research, we plan to investigate: 1) user-centric outsourcing task optimization, and 2) system implementation and prototyping to support example application. This framework could substantially decouple the infrastructural dependence, and thus can be applied to broadly useful scenarios.

21203516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21203516.value: 用戶與環境的交互系統會對用戶在物理世界里的行動以及意圖做出智能的感知和響應，是智能空間不可或缺的功能組件。該系統設計的關鍵在於對用戶意圖和行動的智能感知與及時的反饋。為了滿足這兩點的設計需求，傳統方法通常部署大量定制的傳感器用於感知；同時借助遠程數據中心的計算能力來實現及時的數據處理和用戶反饋。但這樣設計的主要問題在於高額的系統部署和維護成本；有限的覆蓋空間；以及對於高速互聯網接入的依賴。現如今，移動穿戴設備越來越普及。這些設備已經擁有非常強大的中央處理器和各式各樣的傳感器。實際上，這些設備已經形成了一張巨大潛在的感知網絡；並且滲透在人們日常生活的方方面面。這啟發我們可以將上述感知的任務外包給這些移動穿戴設備。同時我們進一步將每個用戶周圍閒散的計算資源整合起來形成一個局部的計算邊界用來就地消化感知到的數據并立即處理，給用戶及時的反饋。 為了實現這一設計目標，需要解決兩點關鍵的挑戰。第一點是弱接觸式的感知。用戶與環境的交互通常需要對於環境和用戶意圖同時做出感知。對於環境的感知已經有很多研究成果存在。但是對用戶意圖的感知需要進一步深入的研究。挑戰主要在於移動設備上的傳感器經常與人體是弱接觸甚至非接觸的。但是在交互的過程中避免不了由於用戶本身或者周圍環境的移動和干擾破壞穩定的感知條件。第二點是閒散的計算資源。雖然計算邊界可以使計算環繞在用戶身邊。但是這些計算資源都是周邊設備義務貢獻的。這些設備本身也有自己的計算任務，動態移動，能量預算等諸多限制。因此如何能夠有效的激勵和調度這些資源亟待解決。同時在感知，計算和反饋整個的信息流上，如果有一環出現瓶頸，就會影響整個系統的性能。因此節資源需要動態調節與分配來保證系統整體的性能。針對以上兩點挑戰，我們在這個項目里提出了一系列創新性的對於戶意圖的智能感知設計，資源的優化分配算法以及感知的調整策略三位一體的用戶與環境交互框架。 這項研究探索了將計算部署在感知周圍，并再將其整合為一個有機整體對的設計理念。以此推動用戶與環境的交互技術的研究與發展。

21203516.label: Realisation of objectives
21203516.value: This project is proposed to investigate a novel sensing and computing system design using mobile and wearable devices to enable more intelligent human-ambient intelligence. There are two major objectives in this project and we have completed both of them. The first objective aims to design a set of novel and useful techniques, by using the sensors from commercial mobile or wearable devices, to sense the user’s attention (objective 1.1), emotion (objective 1.2) and behaviour (objective 1.3) three important aspects for the human-ambiance interaction designs. To sense the user’s visual attention using a mobile device for objective 1.1, we found that the relative position between the device’s front camera and the user’s eyes may vary over time, which could make the existing sensing techniques inaccurate and unreliable. We have developed an effective method to address this issue, which can look at a group of the gaze tracking points and leverage their collective feature to estimate the user’s visual point of interest on the mobile device. To sense the user’s emotion for objective 1.2, we utilized the commercial wearable EEG band and smart glass to fulfill the design. In particular, we identified and addressed a unique challenge stemming from the possible electrode movement due to the head movement, different from the static setting in previous approaches, for achieving a more reliable emotion recognition. To sense the user’s behaviour for objective 1.3, we first focused on the user’s upper limbs and proposed novel techniques to sense the user’s arm. For instance, we proposed a technique to achieve a real-time 3D arm skeleton tracking by using one wrist-worn wearable device only. Then, we also investigated new approaches to sense the user’s lower limbs, such as the step counting, stride estimation, etc. The results of these approaches could indicate the user’s instant moving status or location information. In summary, the techniques proposed for the first objective could enable innovative human-ambiance interactions to cover a large application space. The second objective considers that the sensing data need to be processed efficiently, so that the system can react or interact with the user in time. For the second objective, we aim to investigate a user-centric task outsourcing design by leveraging the available mobile computing resources from the environment. To this end, we first proposed a compact neural network design for different types of recognition tasks on the user’s mobile device directly. The key idea is to decompose the recognition task into context recognition and the context-oriented recognition two lightweight sub-tasks. Because all the computations are performed on the user’s mobile device directly, no extra delay is introduced and the latency will be small. Furthermore, we have also considered the scenario that the computation cannot be afforded by a mobile device. In this case, we further proposed a task outsourcing method to achieve a user experience-oriented outsourcing to tackle this issue. Moreover, we also addressed one unique missing sensor issue when the sensor data are collected from mobile and wearable devices. With this design, even when some sensors are not available and their sensing data are missing, we only need to train one neural network for the recognition task, while it can behave similarly as a series of dedicated networks to handle different types of missing sensor inputs to avoid the training of multiple ones. Finally, we developed and prototyped our proposed designs. Based on the development, we evaluated the system performance and examined the benefits of our techniques for useful applications, like fitness, gesture-based control, etc. In summary, all the objectives proposed in this project have been achieved.

In this proposed project, we plan to investigate, 1) attention-awareness sensing, 2) emotion-awareness sensing, and 3) behavioral-awareness sensing, three crucial user intention sensing areas that cover a large application space.
