Sensing data need to be handled within stringent delay deadline for promptly reacting to users. To this end, we plan to coordinate on-site mobile computing resources from the environment, and outsource the processing tasks to this formed computing edge for a local data digestion and prompt reaction. For this part of research, we plan to investigate: 1) user-centric outsourcing task optimization, and 2) system implementation and prototyping to support example application. This framework could substantially decouple the infrastructural dependence, and thus can be applied to broadly useful scenarios.

21203516.label: Major findings and research outcome
21203516.value: The major findings and the research outcomes of this project are as follows. 1) We find that to achieve human-ambient intelligence, it is important to sense the user’s intentions, which can be captured and aware from several crucial aspects, including the user’s visual attention, emotion and behaviour, to cover a large application design space in practice. In this project, we have studied each of these aspects and proposed effective techniques to sense the users. Our attention-awareness design was reported at IEEE INFOCOM 2017 (Part-C-9-[1]) and the emotion-awareness design was published at ACM TOSN (Part-C-8-[2]). For the behavioural-awareness, our techniques have covered both the user’s upper and lower limbs, which were reported at ACM TOSN (Part-C-8-[3]), IEEE TMC (Part-C-8-[4], Part-C-8-[5]), IEEE ICDCS 2017 (Part-C-9-[2]) and ACM MobiSys 2019 (Part-C-9-[4]). 2) We find that to process the sensing data in time for promptly reacting to the users, we do not need to offload the computation to the remote cloud every time. There are many available and also powerful computing resources in the environment usually, and we can leverage them to process the sensing data efficiently. To this end, we propose to decompose the recognition task into lightweight sub-tasks and perform the computation on the mobile device directly first. The designs were published at IEEE/ACM TON (Part-C-8-[6]) and IEEE SECON 2018 (Part-C-9-[3]). If the mobile device cannot afford the computation, we further proposed a user experience oriented task outsourcing method, which was reported at IEEE ACCESS (Part-C-8-[1]). Finally, we proposed a new method to train only one neural network to handle the issue of missing sensor inputs to make the recognition design more efficient. This method was reported at ACM MobiSys 2019 (Part-C-9-[4]).

21203516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21203516.value: There are a number of directions that can be further explored in the future. 1) Identify and sense new aspects of the user’s intentions to achieve a more comprehensive human sensing. 2) Propose effective solutions that can leverage the new sensor signals on mobile or wearable devices to achieve more intelligent sensing designs. 3) Develop the mechanism to manage the sensing and computing resources jointly.

21203516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21203516.value: This project investigates a system design by using mobile and wearable sensors for human-ambiance interactions to assist people for achieving a more intelligent life style and quality. The technical designs in this project involve the sensing and computing two parts of research. For the sensing part, we aim to achieve intelligent human sensing. The research of this project suggests that the sensors from existing mobile and wearable devices are powerful enough already to fulfill the design by addressing the unique issues identified in this project. Therefore, we can outsource the sensing tasks to these sensors to avoid deploying dedicated devices. On the other hand, we also observe that there are many available computing resources in the surrounding environment. This project shows that we can leverage these useable resources to efficiently process the sensing data for promptly reacting to users, because they perfectly reside on the human-ambiance boundary, which can reduce the dependence on the high-speed Internet access and leave remote clouds as the last resort for backup merely. Overall, this project shows the benefit to bring computing to surround the sensing, and further assemble them as an organic entirety to accommodate the whole human-ambiance interaction process in a self-sufficiency manner.

21203816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21203816.value: 建立關於靈活空間的空間使用分析

21203816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21203816.value: Improving building space efficiency is important because the floor area of a building is strongly related to its CO2 emissions and energy use, which affect the global temperature and sea levels. To improve the space efficiency, architects first need to predict the utilization (a measure of space efficiency) of the building space, based on their design and user information. Some utilization prediction methods have been recently developed to support this initiative, but they still cannot deal with flexible space (i.e., space that changes its configuration using movable components) although the use of such space has increased as it offers ease of re-configuration and higher building space efficiency. This lack of formalization of flexible space in predicting space utilization requires architects to make such prediction on an ad-hoc basis, which can be inaccurate and slow. To solve this problem, this project aims to formalize flexible space in space-use analysis, the most recent and advanced method for predicting space utilization. To fill the gaps in the existing theories, this project will (1) identify and define flexible space-use types that might affect space-use analysis, (2) develop ontologies to represent spaces and user activities, which distinguish between different flexible space-use types, (3) formalize a method for mapping user activities onto flexible and non-flexible spaces, and (4) develop a model view definition to connect the developed theories with a building information model (BIM), from which space information can be derived automatically and seamlessly. The final deliverable will be an Autodesk Revit add-on software that predicts the utilization based on the space information, taken directly from the BIM, and the user activity information entered into the software. Upon successful completion, this project will contribute to performance-based building by allowing architects to predict the space utilization of their designs quickly and comprehensively, and to revise them to include more efficient spaces. Such an improvement in efficiency will significantly contribute to both the sustainable environment and the building economy. For example, if architects could have reduced the floor area of the current projects in Hong Kong by 10%, they would have saved 350 Gg of CO2-equivalent in construction and 900 TJ of energy annually in operation, assuming that the buildings were office buildings. Architects would also have saved HK$10 billion in the construction costs of the buildings by the reduced floor area. 改善建築物的空間效率是一個非常值得關注的問題，因為建築物的建築面積和碳排放及能耗是息息相關的，而碳排放及能耗則影響全球的氣溫和海平面。為改善建築物的空間效率，建築師首先需要基於其設計方案和用戶信息，預測建築物的空間使用率（用於衡量建築物的空間效率）。而現今建立的一些關於預測空間使用率的方法，仍不適用於靈活空間（空間可以通過移動隔斷來改變空間的佈局）。因為靈活空間的佈局易於變更，同時能提高建築物的空間效率，因此靈活空間也被更多地接納和使用。由於現今仍未建立關於靈活空間的空間使用率預測方法，建築師仍需要人工專門去預測這類空間的使用率，但這個預測的過程緩慢，同時這個預測的結果亦會不精確。 為了解決這個問題，這個項目會建立關於靈活空間的空間使用分析，這是一個最新最先進的預測空間使用率的方法。為了補充現今的理論體系，這個項目將會：（1）確定靈活空間使用的種類，這是一個空間使用分析中的影響因素；（2）建立表達空間和用戶活動的相關本體，這部分能用於分辨不同靈活空間使用的種類；（3）建立一個能連接用戶活動和靈活空間或用戶活動和非靈活空間的方法；（4）建立模型視圖體系來將已經建立的理論和建築信息模型（BIM）相連接，建築信息模型支持無縫自動地提取相關的空間信息。最後，本項目會研發一個可以在Autodesk Revit平台裡面預測空間使用率的插件，該插件的預測是基於從BIM中直接提取的空間信息和該插件中已經導入的相關用戶活動信息。 該項目的順利完成，能允許建築師快速以及全面地預測其設計方案的空間使用率，亦能幫助建築師去修訂其設計方案從而能更高效地使用空間，這將有利於建築物性能化。空間效率的提高，將大大有利於可持續環境以及建築經濟這兩個方面。舉個例子，如果建築師將香港現有建築項目的建築面積減少10%，假設這些建築項目為寫字樓項目，那建造過程中將會相應減少350Gg的碳排放，建築物投入使用後每年亦會節省900TJ的能耗。建築師亦可幫這些建築項目節省價值港幣100億元的建造成本。

21204316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21204316.value: 高效的有约束仿真优化算法

21204316.label: Project Objectives
21204316.value: Develop an NP-based algorithm for the simulation optimization problem under consideration. Develop a COMPASS-based algorithm for the simulation optimization problem under consideration. Investigate the benefits and implementation of parallel computing environments for the proposed algorithms in Objective 1 and 2.
rows: Develop an NP-based algorithm for the simulation optimization problem under consideration.
Develop a COMPASS-based algorithm for the simulation optimization problem under consideration.
Investigate the benefits and implementation of parallel computing environments for the proposed algorithms in Objective 1 and 2.

21204316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21204316.value: Stochastic simulation is a powerful tool for evaluating large-scale complex engineering systems, since closed-form analytical models generally do not exist for these systems. Simulation allows one to accurately specify a system through the use of logically complex, and often non-algebraic variables and constraints. Detailed dynamics of the system can therefore be modeled. This capability complements the inherent limitation of traditional optimization toward large-scale complex systems, and makes simulation optimization a popular tool for improving the performance of these systems. In this project, we consider stochastically constrained simulation optimization over discrete solution space, where the objective function is deterministic and the constraint measures are evaluated via stochastic simulation. This problem is challenging primarily because: the solution space often lacks rich structure that can be utilized in identifying good-quality solutions (difficulty 1); and the feasibility of a solution cannot be known for certain, due to the noisy measurements of the constraints (difficulty 2). In order to handle difficulty 1, we will exploit two different types of search methods to effectively explore the solution space: a globally convergent search framework (nested partitions, NP) and a locally convergent search framework (convergent optimization via most promising area stochastic search, COMPASS). The high efficiency of both methods has been widely tested, and the new optimization algorithms will be developed based on these two search frameworks. For difficulty 2, we will design an efficient feasibility detection procedure for the sampled solutions. The feasibility detection procedure is used when the objective value of a sampled solution is better than that of the current observed best feasible solution. Therefore, a large number of solutions visited by the search algorithms do not need to be simulated, which opens up the possibility for the computing efficiency to be significantly improved. For problems with very large scale, we also explore the use of parallel computing to further improve the efficiency of the proposed algorithms. Some preliminary empirical results suggest that the proposed research is very promising. In particular, this project consists of three objectives: 1. Develop an NP-based algorithm for the simulation optimization problem under consideration; 2. Develop a COMPASS-based algorithm for the simulation optimization problem under consideration; 3. Investigate the benefits and implementation of parallel computing environments for the proposed algorithms in Objective 1 and 2. 仿真是考察大规模复杂工业系统表现的常用工具。由于此类系统的内部动态往往非常复杂，显式的数学公式难以表述，而仿真可以精确地展现系统内部的动态变化，因而可以提供对系统表现的精确估计。 在这个项目里，我们考虑有确定性目标函数和随机约束的离散仿真优化问题。该问题的主要难点在于：1)解空间往往缺少可以用来帮助寻找最优解的结构; 2)每个解的可行性并不能完全确定。 为了处理难点1，我们将探索两种搜索方法来搜索解空间：一种是全局收敛的算法和一种局部收敛的算法。对于难点2，我们将设计一种高效的探测可行性的方法。对于大规模的问题，我们将利用并行计算进一步提高以上算法的效率。 本项目的三个目标是： 1. 为目标问题开发一个高效的全局收敛算法； 2. 为目标问题开发一个高效的局部收敛算法； 3. 为目标1和2里的算法设计并行计算框架。

21204316.label: Realisation of objectives
21204316.value: In summary, the first and second objectives have been well achieved, but the third objective is not realized. For the first objective, the PI has developed NP-based algorithms for constrained simulation optimization under a number of different settings, including determining the feasibility of all the solutions in the solution space, and search algorithms with the help of regression models. For the second objective, the PI has developed COMPASS-based algorithms for constrained simulation optimization under a number of different settings, including find the optimal subset instead of the single best solution and robust simulation optimization. For the third objective, the PI explored parallelization of the algorithms developed in objectives 1 and 2, and found that it indeed empirically improves the performance of the algorithms significantly. However, the PI noticed a few theoretical issues brought by parallelization of the algorithms which turned out difficult to handle. It brought difficulty to show the theoretical performance of the algorithms.

21204716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21204716.value: 距離邊界協議安全通道的研究

21204716.label: Project Objectives
21204716.value: Define a framework for the consistent design and comparison of distance-bounding channels. Develop a basic security model for distance-bounding channels. Investigate the link between protocol security in noisy environments and the underlying exchange channel design choices.
rows: Define a framework for the consistent design and comparison of distance-bounding channels.
Develop a basic security model for distance-bounding channels.
Investigate the link between protocol security in noisy environments and the underlying exchange channel design choices.

21204716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21204716.value: Authentication decisions often need to be based on physical proximity to a location. For instance, a wireless car key first has to be close to the car before the doors unlock or a contactless payment card must first be presented to a payment terminal before payment is taken. Linking the physical proximity of a device to a cryptographic authentication protocol is however a challenging problem. One of the most prominent approaches to addressing this challenge is distance-bounding protocols. These protocols work on the basis of measuring the round-trip time of carefully defined cryptographic challenge-response exchanges. In theory, the round-trip time is simply used to estimate an upper bound on the distance to the authenticated device. In practice, the security of these protocols very much depends on the device’s communication channel as its characteristics directly influence the round-trip time measurement and secure transmission of the challenges. Only if the protocol and the channel implementation are both secure can we have confidence in the distance bound determined. Progress is being made on protocol analysis frameworks and provably secure protocols, and there are a number of implementation proposals for secure channels, but there is currently no unified approach to do security analysis of the channel implementation. This proposal sets out to provide a reference framework for the design and comparison of distance-bounding channels, which will define consistent notions of the channel requirements, adversaries and attack strategies. We will also propose a security model for distance-bounding channels, whereby the security properties of the channel could be reliably quantified. Finally, we also study the impact of the channel implementation on the protocol security in noisy environments for both binary and multi-state signals, and determine whether the channel design could be optimised to reduce the security impact of using a large acceptance threshold allowing for channel bit errors. We hope this this will serve as the first step towards a situation where academics and system engineers will have a set of reliable tools to determine the security properties of any given channel design and to obtain an accurate comparison between different designs. 很多時候，認證協議的執行結果與物體的實際位置緊密相關。例如，用汽車的無線鑰匙打開車門的前提要求是該鑰匙貼近車門；在非接觸支付系統中，卡必須要貼近支付終端才能付款。然而，基於物理距離的密碼學認證協議的設計仍然是一個挑戰。 距離邊界協議是一個解決上述挑戰的有效方法。該協定的工作原理是測量一個認證方案中消息在通信雙方傳遞所需的往返時間,以此判斷雙方的物理距離是否在給定的閾值內。 理論上,有了往返時間就可以估算出通信雙方之間物理距離的上限值。但是在實踐中,距離邊界協議的安全卻非常依賴通信通道的特徵,因為通信通道的好壞會直接影響到往返時間的測量以及消息的安全傳輸。只有當協議的設計和通信通道都是安全的情況下,我們才有信心認為距離邊界協議是安全的。 已有的相關工作包含設計出可證明安全協議以及實現一些安全通道方案,但是目前為止還沒有任何統一的方法去做通道實現方案的安全分析。我們的項目就是去努力實現一個距離邊界協議安全通道的參考框架,同時我們也致力於提出一個安全模型,該模型使得通道的安全屬性能夠量化。最後,我們還研究在嘈雜環境中不同的通道實現方案對協議安全的影響。 我們希望我們的工作能夠給科研人員和系統工程師提供一組可靠的工具,用來確定任何給定通道的安全特性並能夠以此精確地比較不同設計方案的優劣。

21204716.label: Realisation of objectives
21204716.value: All three objectives were fully addressed. Over the course of the project Objective 1 and 2 converged to a single body of work comprising of a framework of physical layer attack methods related to distance bounding, and a generalised basic security model to allow the evaluation of protocol design with regards to physical layer security. We considered published works on distance-bounding channel implementations and channel related security analysis. This is a small but disparate body of work with no consistent security analysis methodology or set of terminology. From this we developed overarching classifications for different attack strategies and identified the channel components targeted and exploited by each strategy. The framework categorizes attack strategies as either aiding in distance fraud or mafia fraud. It further maps attack strategies down to different channel components, which either independently or cumulatively contribute to the manner that adversaries can circumvent distance bounds. As an example, strategies for speeding up the prover’s reply aid mafia fraud, and potentially maps to the implementation of the response function, the prover’s system clock, and the channel data (both data coding, and message packet formatting). This work serves as a reference of channel attack strategies on distance-bounding channels, indicates what channel components need to be included in a secure channel design, and can provide a starting point for methods to evaluate the security implications of the channel design in Objective 2. Guidelines are also provided for mitigating attack strategies in channel components. For Objective 2, we developed a basic security model for physical layer security of distance-bounding protocols. The model provides a consistent set of terminology and security metrics, which could be used to define attacks, channel components and channel security performance. Essentially, we have formulated a security model around the properties of the core building blocks of a distance-bounding channel, such as the response function, prover clock recovery, etc. As originally proposed our model includes both attack success probability and the amount of time an attacker can reduce the distance bound by (attack time t_A). Attack success probability is relatively easy to substantiate theoretically, it is already used in other models and our research community is familiar with such an approach. The attack time is a new concept to integrate into the model and is very dependent on channel implementation choices like data coding and modulation (and the common methods used to realize these choices in practice). These implementation choices influence t_A in several channel components, such as time measurement, receiver architecture and clock recovery methods. Our model takes this into account with reasoned assumptions based on underlying communication and networking principles. These assumptions are further supported by selected experiments to implement proof-of-concept exploitation and extend practical attack results already in literature. The experimental work supporting Objective 2 (and to some extent Objective 1) was challenging and we were unfortunately also restricted in terms of resources/manpower due to external factors beyond our control in latter 2019 and in 2020. The seriousness of this situation was such that we were granted two six-month extensions to the project. This allowed us to finish the two objectives, but the delay cost us somewhat in impact of our results, because in the interim period work with similar intention (security model of physical aspects/attacks on DB channel) already appeared mid 2020 (e.g. Leu et.al., IEEE S&P 2020). As result, we focused on using the knowledge gained from accomplishing our objectives rather than publishing the direct outcome. As such, we considered novel proximity protocol formulation and new applications of proximity protocols (Journal article #1, conference outputs #1 and #3, PhD by Ledwaba, in addition to a workshop presentation). For Objective 3, we investigated the implications of using multi-state (m-ary) exchanges for distance bounding protocols. From the protocol perspective, if a challenge or response can be more than two states this decreases the probability that an adversary can guess the correct values, e.g. if we have n rounds each with a single binary responses the guessing probability is (1/2)^n, and with m-ary it is (1/m)^n. However, in practice the channel design chosen to implement multi-state exchanges also impacts on the security. Transmission errors during the timing phase of the distance bounding protocol also impacts on the security of the protocol, as the verifier needs to allow a certain threshold of incorrect responses – introducing false accept/reject probabilities. We studied this trade-off between lowered attack success probability and increased error tolerance considering the channel design with regards to modulation and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the symbol energy ES, the environment noise N0 and the channel design. We considered simple channels implemented using amplitude and phase shift keying (ASK and PSK is indicative of channels used by contactless devices needing to implement distance bounding). We extended selected, well-known protocols to multi-state versions and derived new attack probabilities for distance and mafia fraud also taking into account that allowance is made for errors using a threshold. We first work under the assumption that the device is limited in term of the symbol energy transmitted. We show that if ES is fixed the channel implementation choice significantly impacts on the choice of acceptance threshold and security performance, e.g. PSK gives lower attack probabilities than ASK for equal values of m. It is also shown that in practice security does not significantly increase, and actually decreases as m increases. We then also considered other parameters, such as choosing an appropriate number of exchanges n to achieve a desired security level at a specified SNR. This work lead to conference output #2 and journal article #2 (still under review), which both form part of the PhD by Zhang.

21204716.label: Major findings and research outcome
21204716.value: Objective 1+2 developed a framework of physical layer attack methods related to distance bounding, together with a generalised basic security model to allow the evaluation of protocol design with regards to physical layer security. As described in Section 5.3, due to delays outside our control we have taken an alternative approach to use this knowledge and its dissemination. Our initial work, presenting selected physical-layer security issues were presented at the FutureDB workshop. We used knowledge gained on contactless channels, and how demodulation/decoding are implemented in current transceivers to develop a novel protocol for verifying the proximity of a group of RFID tags, which was published in IEEE IoTJ. The protocol leverages the property that all the tags’ responses should be, and can be, synchronised with any tag being late with its response at over approximately 2.4 us causing an invalid response. The protocol achieves improved efficiency in that all tags are truly authenticated simultaneously (tags transmit at the same time), rather than in a timing interleaved/multiplexed manner. We also published the design of an off-the-shelf security testing platform for contactless systems at SECITC 2020, based on our experience building such a platform for validating our work for Objective 1 and 2. In addition, we studied new applications and approaches to proximity verification, developing a method for sensor data consensus based on node proximity, published at IECON 2020 and in thesis of Ledwaba, and developed a location-limited vibration channel for mobile devices (work by undergraduate student as part of Education Plan), published at IECON 2021. Objective 3 evaluated the security implications of implementing multistate DB protocols using common m-ary modulation schemes. We showed that the expected security gain obtained from multistate exchanges was counteracted by higher transmission error rates. This resulted in a trade-off leading to security only improving up to point, and then decreasing as number of states increased. We first considered only mafia fraud success probability, demonstrating the channel security trade-off and providing guidance for choosing number of states and exchange rounds to achieve a chosen success probability. This work was published at CPS-SPC'19. We then extended the work to consider both distance and mafia fraud in multi-state protocol constructs with and without a verification stage. We also consider the feasibility of the participants committing energy resources to fewer exchanges and higher SNR. This work is still under review (almost 6th month) and contained in PhD thesis of Zhang.

21204716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21204716.value: We are using the framework and model developed in Objective 1+2 to evaluate the suitability of existing channels for distance-bounding. We are continuing experimental work on evaluating and demonstrating attack strategies on communication standards for contactless technology, e.g., ISO 14443 near-field communication used for secure high-frequency RFID applications (payments/e-ID/access control). In doing so we are considering the physical layer defined in the standard and its implementation in HF RFID transceiver chipsets by prominent semiconductor providers.

21204716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21204716.value: Distance-bounding protocols verify the physical proximity of two devices. The security of these protocols depends both on cryptographic and time-of-flight channel design. Our work provides a framework for the design and comparison of distance-bounding channels, with a security model whereby the security properties of the channel could be reliably quantified. These are useful tools to determine the security properties of any given channel design and to obtain an accurate comparison between different designs. We further applied our knowledge of the physical layer in channels we studied to design a new protocol verifying the proximity of a group of devices. We also evaluated the impact of multi-state channels on protocol security in noisy environments. We determined that such multi-state protocols could provide better security but gains as the number of states increase are practically limited by channel design parameters and environment. Our results allow for a design to choose an appropriate number of states and cryptographic exchanges to achieve a required security level for a given channel signal-to-noise ratio.

21204816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21204816.value: Construction companies incur financial losses and negative impacts to reputation due to labor fatalities and injuries. In Hong Kong, more than 25% of all workplace injuries and fatalities occur in the construction industry. Since more than 70% of all accidents are related to human activities, detecting and mitigating risks associated with human behavior can improve the negative public perception of the construction industry. Because construction environments are dynamic and human behavior is unpredictable, conventional observational approaches to detecting these risks have proven to be time-consuming and unreliable. Therefore, sensing technologies such as RGB-D cameras, IMUs and RFIDs have been introduced to automatically detect human motion in relation to its surrounding environment. Thus, sensing technologies can potentially address many of the difficulties in hazard detection and safety assessment on construction sites. Integrating existing sensing tools will improve hazard detection and safety assessment by generating data from a variety of perspectives capable of better reflecting the interdependence of human behavior and the environment on construction sites. However, existing sensing technologies currently lack a universal data integration and processing framework, which is problematic because it results in noisy, incomplete, and incompatible data. These problems create fundamental obstacles for improving safety assessment. This proposed research aims to develop an agile framework to: 1) accurately collect multiple human behavior-related sensing data, 2) efficiently detect anomalies and hazards, and 3) correctly assess jobsite safety conditions. The goal of the research is to design a generic and self-adaptive framework that can integrate new and cumulative data sources. Specifically, the framework will: 1) define an agile protocol to collect, clean, unify and merge data from multiple sensing sources, 2) propose procedures and models to automatically recognize dangerous activities through temporal data segments processed according to the protocol, and 3) assess safety conditions on specific projects and validate the proposed framework. The framework will be able to provide project managers and workers with an automated system to identify, record and assess onsite hazards, which will improve the effectiveness of safety management practices in the construction industry. In turn, improvements in safety management will result in a reduction of costs related to labor injuries and fatalities, and an increase in the safety and health of construction workers in Hong Kong. 21204816.label: Realisation of objectives
21204816.value: Obj 1: define an agile protocol to collect, clean, unify and merge data from multiple sensing sources. Sensory information collected from different sources or equipment results in differences in data type, sampling rate, data structure, data resolution. This project selected several motion-capturing systems to illustrate how multi-sensory data can be integrated with a properly designed protocol. The research team designed a data framework that established a formal process for data collection and implemented signal processing techniques to resample different data types, such as time series, videos, and multi-channel EEG data. The innovative solution for multi-sensory data source integration is the proposed tensor decomposition method. The method allows data compression at the same timescale and agile tracing and filling problematic data points. Two experiments have been conducted in 2017 and 2019. The first experiment captures construction workers’ body movement with a multi-channel IMU system. The aim of this study is to integrate multiple data sources, who have similar data structures. The second experiment captures hybrid motion and EEG signals to illustrate how data from the completely different structure and type can be integrated with the proposed framework. These findings have been published in international peer-reviewed journals, including [1] Jiayu Chen*, Jun Qiu and Changbum Ahn, “Construction worker’s awkward posture recognition through supervised motion tensor decomposition”, Automation in Construction, 2017, 77:67-81. In the above work, a motion tensor approach has been proposed to define a data protocol to clean, unify, merge, and compress complicated multi-sensory data. The validation experiment has more than 17 channels (each channel has 9 degrees of data sources). The proposed method successfully collected and processed reliable data that treated with the proposed protocol. [2] Di Wang, Heng Li, and Jiayu Chen*, “Detecting and measuring construction workers’ vigilance through hybrid kinematic-EEG signals”, Automation in Construction, 2019, 100:11-23 In the above work, the research team utilized the proposed data protocol for heterogeneous data sources, motion data, and EEG signals. Both types of data have been integrated as hybrid kinematic-EEG signals with the tenderized data protocol. In summary, research objective 1 has been successfully achieved. Obj 2: Propose procedures and models to recognize human-related hazards through processed data. With the support of sensory datasets, procedures and models can be composed to automatically recognize and assess human-related hazards. For this research objective, the research team proposed to develop a theoretical framework to investigate the source of unsafe behaviors and properly assess human-related hazards. This project proposed to utilize mental workload as a quantitative indicator to assess the vulnerability of construction workers. Both mental load and physical load require great effort from workers. Some construction tasks with high mental requirements can be as demanding as physically intensive tasks. Negligence or wrong estimation of mental load can easily lead to mismatches in task demand and worker capacity. When task demand exceeds capability, the loss of control may result in quality defects, accidents, and failure of teamwork. The compliance between task demands and laborer capability leads to higher productivity and lower error rates. Therefore, we can quantitatively assess the human-related risk level by comparing the level of mental workload and task requirements, such as levels of complexity, involvement, repetition, and etc. To validate the proposed model, the research team also applied a task design based on the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration and the training materials of the H.K. Occupational Safety and Health Council. The mental workload then was assessed with a mature NASA task load assessment framework as a benchmark. The proposed model and findings have been published in peer-reviewed journals, including [1] Jiayu Chen*, John E. Taylor and Semra Comu, “Assessing Task Mental Workload in Construction Projects: A Novel Electroencephalography Approach”, ASCE Journal of Construction Engineering and Management, 2017, 143(8): 04017053 In the above work, the quantitative assessment framework has been proposed and explained, the human-related hazards have defined a mismatch between mental workload and task requirements. A validation experiment has been conducted to validate the findings. [2] Wei Wang, Tianzhen Hong, Nan Li, Ryan Qi Wang, and Jiayu Chen*, “Linking energy-cyber-physical systems with occupancy prediction and interpretation through WiFi probe-based ensemble classification”, Applied Energy, 2019, 236:55-69 In the above work, although the research target is not human-related hazard assessment, it incorporates human activity as the data interface to interfere with building facility operation. This study also implements a similar data procedure to recognize human activities and assessment on their impacts. Obj 3: Assess the project safety conditions and validate the proposed system. The hazard assessment models and integrated/processed sensory data allow a flexible and agile assessment of safety conditions (from the perspective of labor) of a project. As construction laborers are major participants of construction project execution. Assessing their activity and physical conditions can provide an effective insight into the safety level of projects. Therefore, for this objective, the research team mainly focus on the entire project process and proposed two models. One model focuses on investigating the sustained attention of construction laborers and the other model focuses on pre-service safety assessment with pre-service fatigue screening. The proposed model and findings have been published on peer-reviewed journals, including [1] Jiayu Chen*, Ryan Qi Wang, Zhenghang Lin, and Xiaoyang Guo, “Measuring the Cognitive Loads of Construction Safety Sign Designs During Selective and Sustained Attention”, Safety Science, 2018, 105:9-21 In the above work, the safety condition of a construction task can be measured by the cognitive load of Selective and Sustained Attention when a worker conducts that task. The quantitative assessment method is similar to the models proposed for objective 2. In the published paper, the research team uses safety sign recognition as an example for task safety assessment. [2] Jiayu Chen*, Xiaowei Luo, and Heng Li, “Pre-service fatigue screening for construction labor through hybrid kinematic-EEG signal processing and workload assessments”, ASCE Construction Research Congress 2020: Safety, Workforce, and Education, Tempe, Arizona, March 8–10, 2020 In the above work, the proposed safety assessment framework was utilized to assess the fatigue level of construction workers. A higher fatigue level before work usually indicates higher risks during task execution.

21204816.label: Major findings and research outcome
21204816.value: There three major findings from this research: (1) Tensorization and decomposition can effectively fuse multiple sensory systems Tensorization utilizes timestamps and sampling frequency to align data from different sensing systems as one dimension of the composed tensor. By doing so, the data can be easily unified as a high-dimension vector that cross-references each other for cleaning and merging purposes. The enriched dataset provides additional and supplementary information for a more reliable and accurate safety assessment. (2) Mental workload assessment is an innovative and evolutionary approach for human-related safety assessment This finding interprets the potential human-related hazards as a quantitative mismatch between human laborers’ mental workload and task requirements. Overloading the construction workers’ will results in lower vigilance during task execution and increase their vulnerability. Different from the conventional questionnaire and supervision methods, this finding concludes that sensory data of metal workload can be a direct indication of safety level. (3) Fused multi-sensory data can be used for task-specific attention assessment and decomposed project safety evaluation As construction projects are usually composed of multiple schedule tasks, a proper assessment of the safety condition of the entire project can be substitute by assessment at each task level. Also, pre-task screening can eliminate potential risks before execution. The major research outcomes of this study including 5 international peer-reviewed journal papers and 2 international conference papers. Also, one patent was inspired by the findings of this study and currently are seeking approval.

21204816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21204816.value: The proposed multi-sensory data fusing approach can be utilized for broader applications in different scenarios in the construction industry. For example, for labor efficiency assessment, productivity evaluation, and construction equipment management. These developments involve a new type of sensing technology and passive monitoring system. Developing such a data integration platform and framework would enable smarter project control and implementation of artificial intelligent management in practice. On the other hand, as the mental workload can be used for safety assessment, it is necessary to develop a more reliable data acquisition method. One of the major constraints of current fused sensor data is the complexity of hybrid kinematic-EEG signals. The research team proposed this new type of data format for mental workload assessment during task execution, but usually, high muscle voltage may contaminate EEG signals. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a completely new system to decompose different frequency bands and reveal their relevance with physical activities.

21204816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21204816.value: Safety assessment in the construction industry is an ambiguous process that highly relies on the subjective opinions and experience of site managers. With the development of sensing technologies in recent years, acquiring different sensor data from construction workers on-site becomes possible. The significant value of this study is to develop a quantitative method to assess the safety condition of construction workers based on sensing data instead of experience. It is based on the theoretical background of attention assessment and near-miss accidents and allows an objective assessment based on a quantitative comparison between construction workers’ capacity and task requirements. To lay a technical foundation of this theory, this study also proposed a data fusing framework that can integrate different sensing systems and generate rich, consistent, and reliable sensory datasets.

21205016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21205016.value: The brain accounts for more than 20% of total oxygen consumption even at the resting state. Oxygen metabolism is not only closely associated with neuron activities, but also plays a key role in many life-threatening brain disorders, such as ischemic stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, seizure, neurodegeneration, and brain tumors. In vivo imaging of cerebral oxygen delivery in small-animal disease models is of crucial importance for understanding pathogenic mechanisms and exploring new therapeutic strategies in translational medicine. Because of the highly dynamic nature and close interconnections among different sub-regions in the brain, imaging of cerebral oxygen delivery does not only require high spatial resolution, but also needs to achieve high imaging speed over a large field of view. However, it is still challenging for existing biomedical imaging techniques to meet all of these requirements in a single imaging modality. In 2013, the PI demonstrated that voice-coil photoacoustic microscopy can quantitatively image oxygen release from single red blood cells in a capillary, which sheds light on functional brain imaging with an unprecedented single-cell resolution. Here we propose a major technical advance based on voice-coil photoacoustic microscopy that can image oxygen release from single red blood cells in large-scale vessels in the brain. The proposed project will build a new photoacoustic microscope based on an ultrafast scanning mirror and a voice-coil stage to achieve video-rate three-dimensional imaging over a large field of view. A dual-pulse-width method will be used to determine the oxygen saturation in each flowing red blood cells with 800-kHz pulse repetition rate. This novel brain imaging capability enables monitoring oxygen delivery with the ultimate single-cell resolution and a large field of view. This allows us study the interconnections among different sub-regions in the brain cortex with single-cell resolution. In addition, we can simultaneously quantify multiple important state parameters, such as total hemoglobin concentration, blood oxygen saturation, and blood flow speed, in multiple capillaries and trunk vessels. These state parameters can provide insights into the mechanisms behind the oxygen supply changes in the brain. The in vivo imaging of oxygen delivery at the single-cell resolution in large-scale blood vessels represents a powerful enabling technique for functional imaging—potentially opening up many new applications in preclinical brain imaging, such as studying coupling between neuron activities and single-cell oxygen release in a large area, or monitoring the progress and therapeutic outcomes of ischemic stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, or glioblastoma. 大腦的氧消耗量即使在休息狀態下也佔縂消耗量的20%以上。氧代謝不僅與神經活動緊密相關，而且在許多重大腦疾病中起到關鍵作用，例如中風、老年痴呆、癲癇、神經退化、和腦部腫瘤等。對小動物疾病模型中腦部氧輸送進行活體成像是理解病理機制和探索新的治療策略的重要手段。由於腦中高度動態的活動和不同區域閒的緊密聯係，對腦部氧輸送成像不僅需要高空間分辨率，而且也需要高成像速度和大視野範圍。然而，現有的生物醫學成像技術還不能滿足這一要求。 2013年，項目申請人演示了一種音圈電機光聲顯微鏡技術，它能夠定量對單個紅細胞的血氧釋放進行成像，使單細胞尺度腦功能成像成爲了可能。基於音圈電機光聲顯微鏡，本項目提出一個主要的技術提升，即開發一種新的用于腦的大規模單細胞血樣釋放成像技術。本項目將基於超快掃描鏡和音圈電機技術開發下一代光聲顯微鏡，以實現大範圍視頻速率三維成像。800 kHz的雙脈寬方法將用來測定流動中的單個紅細胞的血氧飽和度。這個新的技術將使在大範圍内監測單紅細胞尺度的血氧輸送成爲可能。基於此，我們將可以在單細胞尺度上研究不同腦部區域閒的相互連接的情況。此外，我們還能夠在多個毛細血管和大血管中同時定量測量多個重要的狀態參數，如雪紅蛋白濃度，血氧飽和度，和血流速度等。這些狀態參數能夠使我們深入了解腦部血氧供應變化的深層機制。在單細胞尺度對血氧輸送進行大規模成像是一種有力的功能成像技術，使很多腦成像研究成爲可能，例如研究大面積上的神經活動和單細胞血氧輸送閒的耦合關係，或者檢測腦中風、老年痴呆、和神經膠質瘤等疾病的治療效果。

21205016.label: Realisation of objectives
21205016.value: The three objectives have been successully achieved. We have developed a kHz water-immersion resonant MEMS mirror for ultrafast photoacoustic scanning. Flexible hinges, fast polygon scanner and optical/acoustic relective mirror were designed and fabricated. With testing, the MEMS mirror has a high reflectivity, large scanning range, and ~1kHz scanning rate. Based on this key component, we built an new optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy system based on the kHz MEMS mirror and a voice-coil scanner, achieving three-dimensional photoacoustic imaging with video-rate speed, sub-cellular spatial resolution, millimeter-sized field of view, and high SNR, implemented single-cell functional imaging over large field of view, and demonstrated in vivo mouse brain imaging.

21300116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21300116.value: 对耦合量子点自旋量子比特之抗噪操控之理论研究

21300116.label: Project Objectives
21300116.value: To benchmark existing noise-compensating control protocols under realistic noises having a range of power spectra. To understand the problems arising from manipulation of a scaled-up spin qubit array, in particular the gate crosstalk and leakage. To obtain a theoretical understanding on multi-electron multi-qubit devices through microscopic calculations.

To understand the problems arising from manipulation of a scaled-up spin qubit array, in particular the gate crosstalk and leakage.
To obtain a theoretical understanding on multi-electron multi-qubit devices through microscopic calculations.

21300116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21300116.value: Quantum information processing is presently an active research area due to its potential in technological applications that may be far more powerful than present day electronics. A qubit, or quantum bit, can be encoded in the spin states of electrons confined in semiconductor quantum dots. Although reasonably long coherence times and high control fidelities have been demonstrated in spin qubits, challenges remain for their application in scalable quantum information processing. There are two major hurdles in the field: decoherence and scalability. The quantum information carried by spin qubits inevitably deteriorates through interactions with the environment, causing decoherence. Various control techniques are developed to combat such forces, including the Dynamically Corrected Gates. On the other hand, problems have been identified to concur with the scaling up of spin qubits, the most important ones being the gate crosstalk and leakage. In this project, we will develop theoretical methodologies that can help in overcoming these hurdles. In particular, we will benchmark existing control protocols under experimentally realistic noises, and will optimize them so as to facilitate their applications in laboratories. We will quantify destructive factors of gate crosstalk and leakage in a scaled-up spin qubit array and will search for effective and practical ways to reduce these errors. We will develop a comprehensive theory on multi-electron multi-qubit devices through microscopic calculations, including a quantitative understanding on how charged impurities may be screened by the multi-electron states. Finally, we will further the studies to a wider range of realizations of spin qubits including the resonant-exchange qubit and hybrid qubit. The results of this research are expected to bridge the gap between theoretical control protocols and their experimental realization, and will provide new insights on operating a spin qubit array in a noise-resistant manner. Successful completion of this project will contribute to a more comprehensive theoretical picture of the robust manipulation of coupled quantum dot spin qubits, and will be of great help in the on-going effort using them for scalable fault-tolerant quantum information processing. 量子信息处理是近年来一个热点研究领域。一个量子比特可以用半导体量子点中电子的自旋态来编码，称为自旋量子比特。尽管对自旋量子比特体系的操作已经具备足够长的相干时间和控制精度，但是距离可扩展的量子计算还有很多挑战。障碍主要来自于两个方面：退相干和可延展性。一方面，退相干指的是量子体系因为与其环境的相互作用而失去其所存储的量子信息。为了降低退相干的影响，研究者发展了很多控制技术，其中包括动力学修正量子门。另一方面，在从一及多的扩展自旋量子比特的过程中遇到了很多问题，其中最重要的是门串扰和信息泄露。在这个项目中，我们将发展能够协助克服这些困难的理论方法。特别是我们将在实际实验体系中标定现有的控制技术，并对其进行优化使得它们更容易地在实验中被应用。我们将把大尺度自旋量子比特体系中的门串扰和信息泄露进行定量化，并且找到有效而现实的改进方法。我们将经由微观计算而发展对于多电子多量子点体系的全面理论，包括定量地研究多电子态对带电杂质造成的干扰的屏蔽效果。最后，我们把这些技术推广到其他类型的量子比特，如纯交换耦合量子比特和混合量子比特中。该研究将为理论和实验架起桥梁，并且对自旋量子比特的抗噪操控提供新的思路。

21300116.label: Realisation of objectives
21300116.value: All objectives set forth in the project have been realized with abundant results. We provide details below. For Task 1, "To benchmark existing noise-compensating control protocols under realistic noises having a range of power spectra", we have published two papers that use the tool of randomized benchmarking to assess the applicability of dynamically corrected gates to noisy environments (already reported in the mid-term report). From the results, we have also made optimizations that could be useful for their experimental realization. The two papers are (labels refer to the ordering in Part C, point 8): [2] Randomized benchmarking of barrier versus tilt control of a singlet-triplet qubit, Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 216802 (2017). [4] Fast pulse sequences for dynamically corrected gates in singlet-triplet qubits, Phys. Rev. B 96, 195424 (2017). In a related paper, we have also tried to use neural network to generate noise-compensation pulses sequences. We found that the new technique of machine learning may help in robust quantum control. [7] Neural network designed pulse sequences for robust control of singlet-triplet qubits, Phys. Rev. A 97, 042324 (2018). In fact, we followed up and applied reinforcement learning, another key technique of machine learning, to quantum control problems and have seen interesting results (to be detailed below). For Task 2, "To understand the problems arising from manipulation of a scaled-up spin qubit array, in particular the gate crosstalk and leakage", we have some results on the gate crosstalk and leakage in two-electron and three-electron systems in the mid-term report: [1] Energy spectrum, exchange interaction, and gate crosstalk in a system with a pair of double quantum dots: A molecular-orbital calculation, Phys. Rev. A 95, 052325 (2017). [8] Leakage and sweet spots in triple-quantum-dot spin qubits: a molecular orbital study, Phys. Rev. A 97, 042326 (2018). We have further investigated the gate control problem in a spin qubit or its array. In particular, we studied how the minimal decomposition of an arbitrary single-qubit gate is related to the directions of the axes. From these results, we have found that we can shorten and optimize the pulse sequences compared to commonly-used methods. This result is published in [11] Minimal nonorthogonal gate decomposition for qubits with limited control, Phys. Rev. A 99, 052339 (2019). We have also tried to introduce the idea of geometric quantum computation to the problem of controlling a quantum-dot spin qubit, and we have found that the geometric method can be a useful way to suppress the effect of environmental noises and improve the operation fidelities. The results is published in [12] Plug-and-play approach to nonadiabatic geometric quantum gates, Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 100501 (2019). As stated above, we have spent a lot of efforts trying to apply the new technique of machine learning to quantum control problems, in order to gain new insights and to extend the forefront of research. We have applied the reinforcement learning to three problems. We have studied how a spin state can be quantum mechanically transported on a one-dimensional spin chain and found that the new method can provide an even higher transport speed than previously conceived. We also studied a problem on quantum parameter estimation and found that the method from reinforcement learning is more generalizable, i.e. a neural network trained at one parameter value can be straightforwardly extended to other values, implying a higher efficiency compared to conventional gradient-based methods under certain situations. We have also compared, in detail, a few reinforcement learning methods and two conventional methods on the problem of quantum state preparation, a fundamental problem in quantum control. We found that the reinforcement learning methods are overall the most efficient one, and is more adaptive, i.e. it can find the optimal solution to the specific situation concerned. The aforementioned results are published as: [9] Automatic spin-chain learning to explore the quantum speed limit, Phys. Rev. A 97, 052333 (2018) [13] Generalizable control for quantum parameter estimation through reinforcement learning, npj Quantum Inf. 5, 82 (2019). [14] When does reinforcement learning stand out in quantum control? A comparative study on state preparation, npj Quantum Inf. 5, 85 (2019). For Task 3, "To obtain a theoretical understanding on multi-electron multi-qubit devices through microscopic calculations", we performed some microscopic calculation on few electron systems, and found that the geometry of quantum-dot devices is key to noise suppression. These results (reported in the mid-term report) are published as [3] Suppression of charge noise using barrier control of a singlet-triplet qubit, Phys. Rev. A 96, 012318 (2017). [5] Magic angle for barrier-controlled double quantum dots, Phys. Rev. A 97, 012304 (2018). [6] On the validity of microscopic calculations of double-quantum-dot spin qubits based on Fock-Darwin states, Sci. China Phys. Mech. Astron. 61, 040313 (2018). As the calculation of four-dot devices is quite difficult, we have then focused on triple-dot devices. We have studied how a barrier-controlled triple-quantum-dot is tunable, providing a way to improve the fidelity of manipulation. We have also shown, for a charge qubit in triple quantum dots, leakage can be largely suppressed if the triple quantum dots form a triangle. These results are published as: [10] Tunable charge qubit based on barrier-controlled triple quantum dots, Phys. Rev. A 98, 032334 (2018). [15] Suppression of leakage for a charge qubit in triangular triple quantum dots, Adv. Quantum Technol. 2019, 1900072 (2019).

We used neural network to generate noise-compensating pulses, and found that the new technique of machine learning may help in robust quantum control [7]. 6. We found that the reinforcement learning methods are overall the most efficient one, and is more adaptive, i.e. it can find the optimal solution to the specific situation concerned [14]. 9. 21300116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21300116.value: Our finding of this project can be further extended to multi-quantum-dot multi-qubit devices. In particular, calculation of four-dot devices is underway and may reveal important insights on how the quantum-dot qubits can scale up. Further application of machine learning techniques on a wide range of problems related to quantum information processing should also be considered, as our preliminary results have found that the machine learning techniques have offered new advantages than conventional methods. Regarding the geometric design of quantum devices and its relationship with the control fidelity, further study is also underway as simulating a device on a computer would be tremendously helpful in future development of quantum computing.

21300116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21300116.value: In this project, we studied several theoretical aspects related to quantum control of quantum-dot spin qubits, one of the most promising candidates for quantum computation. We studied how the quantum control can be achieved accurately under noises, and ways to improve the manipulations. We have also found that certain geometric design of the quantum-dot devices can help in suppressing noises. We have also introduced some new techniques, including machine learning, to quantum control problems, which have given some insights on how the accuracy of quantum control can be improved. Overall, the outcome of this project may be useful for experiments aiming to achieve high-accuracy quantum computation.

21504216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504216.value: This study proposes a new mechanism to explain stock returns movement based on news co-mentions. Research on empirical finance found that firms in the same industry tend to move in the same direction (also known as returns comovement). If investors are interested in a stock, they pay close attention to its competitive environment (e.g., industries). When favorable (unfavorable) news occurs to an industry, the price of the stock increases (decreases) accordingly. As a result, returns comovement exists. However, traditional classifications of industry are static in nature. They do not capture the evolving nature of business operations over time. For example, Microsoft was a pure software company but is now engaging in smart phones and other hardware businesses. Nowadays, as companies span across various business domains, it becomes difficult to assign them to a single industry code using traditional industry classification schemes (e.g., SIC, NAICS, and GICS). Several studies empirically show that traditional schemes are not precise to explain stock return movement. To address such limitation, we propose a new approach to identify dynamic boundary of industries based on news co-mention collected from online infomediaries (e.g., Factiva and Reuters). News is a major source of information where investors gather to make investment decision. When two firms are frequently mentioned together in news, investors are likely to pay keen attention to both companies. The frequently co-mentioned companies may form an “information habitat”. According to information diffusion theory in finance, firms in the same habitat are likely to exhibit returns comovement. Taking into account of coverage and persistency of co-mentioned news, we construct a dynamic industry classification scheme with the hope that it can outperform traditional approaches to classify firms into relevant industries. A prototype has been developed to visualize industry boundaries based on co-mention news. In the long run, we will enhance the prototype to include real-time news and heat-map visualization to alert users the immediate changes in information habitat. Our study contributes to both disciplines of Information Systems (IS) and finance. Firstly, it enriches existing IS literature on network economics by demonstrating the inferential power and economic implications of news co-mention networks. Secondly, the new industrial classification is useful to capital market research. Thirdly we use a large-scale network analysis to analyze large volume of news, showcasing a big data application in finance. Finally, we provide industrial practitioners with new prediction models and visual analytic tools to forecast stock returns. 是次研究提出新的方法，研究新聞共提及收益聯動的關係。傳統研究法常依賴不變的行業分類，進行研究分析。由於企業運作隨時間不斷變化，業務亦不斷改變，傳統研究法不能有效地推算企業之間的收益聯動。為了解決這問題，是次研究根據金融訊息擴散理論，提出了以新聞共提估量行業變化，從而推算收益聯動及預測股票收益。是次研究提出嶄新的行業分類法，豐富現有的網絡經濟學。此外，此研究亦利用大型網絡分析法，展示金融大數據應用。

21506616.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21506616.value: 外部選擇權和不對稱信息的議價

21506616.label: Project Objectives
21506616.value: Develop a new model of bargaining with an interplay between asymmetric information and outside options. Apply the model to develop a theory of delay in bargaining. Apply the new model to contemporary economic issues.
rows: Develop a new model of bargaining with an interplay between asymmetric information and outside options.
Apply the model to develop a theory of delay in bargaining.
Apply the new model to contemporary economic issues.

21506616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21506616.value: This project develops the theory of bargaining with information asymmetry and outside options. This project focuses on informational effect of outside options. For example, in a wage negotiation, a firm's outside option can disclose internal information relevant to the negotiation. The firm will therefore strategically reveal or conceal its outside option. The project argues that such an informational effect is crucial in understanding bargaining problems. The project analyzes a two-person bargaining problem with asymmetric information. The key features are that (i) the informed party has an outside option available during negotiation, (ii) the value of the outside option and the value of gain from agreement are the informed party's private information, and (iii) the two values are correlated either negatively or positively. Hence, the uninformed party can infer the informed party's private information based on how the informed party addresses the outside option. The project employs both sequential bargaining and mechanism design approaches. The sequential bargaining approach assumes a specific bargaining protocol, and analyzes the bargaining outcome as an equilibrium of the extensive-form game. The results from this approach are easy to interpret and apply, but sensitive to bargaining protocol assumed. The mechanism design approach complements the sequential bargaining approach to produce a robust insight that holds for any bargaining protocol. Bargaining and negotiation are longstanding decision-making mechanisms that remain popular in both public and private spheres. Moreover, both outside options and information asymmetry are prevalent in bargaining situations. The project will therefore provide widely applicable insights, including the following expected applications. 1. The project develops a theory of bargaining impasse. A preliminary result suggests by an example that the informational effect of outside options can be a source of bargaining impasse. The idea in the example will be extended and generalized. 2. The project is expected to deliver insights into current economic issues. For example, the project examines the recent advancement of information technology. In particular, the improvement of search technology makes it easier and more effective to locate outside options during negotiations. The comparative statics with respect to the outside option's arrival rate will provide insights to this change. 3. The project extends search-and-matching models. An agent in a search-and-matching market may negotiate with an existing partner before he or she leaves and searches for new partners. Current search-and-matching models, however, abstract from such a negotiation process. The aim of the project is to extend search-and-matching models by incorporating an explicit model of negotiations.

21506616.label: Realisation of objectives
21506616.value: Objective 1. The project developed an economic model of bargaining with outside options and asymmetric information. Following the original application, the project has made use of both mechanism-design and noncooperative-game approaches. The mechanism-design approach is presented in the paper titled “Optimal Sales Mechanism with Outside Options,” and the noncooperative-game approach is presented in the paper titled “Bargaining with Outside Options: Commitment and Delay.” Objective 2. These models are applied to develop a theory of delay in bargaining, which fulfills the second objective. The results can be found in two papers attached to the report (see Part C), which are also briefly summarized below: The first paper (Optimal Sales Mechanism with Outside Options) shows that a delay can occur in price negotiation due to the seller’s motive to avoid negotiation break-offs. Negotiation break-off inevitably results in information rent to the buyer types with valuable outside options. Hence, the seller can increase his or her profit by delaying the negotiation rather than breaking it off immediately. The paper contains the result that formally confirms this intuition by proving that the seller’s profit-maximizing mechanism always induces a delay. This result stands in contrast to the no-haggling theorem in the mechanism design literature, which proves that the seller’s profit-maximizing mechanism induces no delay in the absence of the buyer’s outside option (Stokey N. L., “Intertemporal Price Discrimination,” Quarterly Journal of Economics, 1979). The results in the first paper assume that the seller can commit to the profit-maximizing mechanism. The second paper (Bargaining with Outside Options: Commitment and Delay) investigates if the same result remains to hold even if the seller lacks such commitment power. In a nutshell, the paper shows that the answer to this question is positive if and only if there is a positive measure of buyer types with zero outside options. This result differs from the Coase conjecture (Coase, R. H., “Durability and Monopoly,” Journal of Law and Economics, 1972), which argues that the seller’s lack of commitment power results in no delay in the absence of the buyer’s outside option. Overall, these two papers theoretically confirm that the buyer’s outside option accounts for a delay in bargaining. Objective 3. These papers also discuss how the developed models can be used to extend our understanding of economic activities observed in the real world, accomplishing the third objective. For example, the first paper (Optimal Sales Mechanism with Outside Options) shows that the seller’s optimal negotiation mechanism can be implemented by offering the buyer a menu of European call options. This result suggests that outside options can explain the popularity of option contracts in various markets.

21506616.label: Major findings and research outcome
21506616.value: The paper “Optimal Sales Mechanism with Outside Options” has been submitted to the Journal of Economic Theory and received the request of Revise and Resubmit. A part of the results in this work (under the old title “Delay in Selling to Buyers with Outside Options”) was presented in international conferences in economics, including the 9th Biennial Conference of Hong Kong Economic Association (12-13 December 2016), and the 2017 Asian Meeting of the Econometric Society (3-5 June 2017) among many others. The paper “Bargaining with Outside Options: Commitment and Delay” is ready to submit to an academic journal for publication. Previous versions of this paper (under the old title under old titles “Equilibrium Delay in Bargaining with Buyer’s Outside Option”) were presented in international conferences in economics, including the 2018 East Asian Contract Theory Conference (1 December 2018), 2019 North American Meeting of the Econometric Society (27-30 June 2019), and 2019 Annual SAET Conference (1-6 July 2019) among others.

21506616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21506616.value: The project focused on the simple case that the buyer’s outside option is given exogenously, with no explicit account for how this outside option could be formed in the first place. The future research may aim to fill this gap. One possibility is that the outside option is simply the opportunity to purchase the same good from other sellers in the market. This direction of research would require to develop a dynamic game with multiple sellers competing for a single buyer. Another potential direction of future research is to incorporate the idea of information design into the model developed in this project. A seller is often more informed of alternative products available in the market and hence is more knowledgable about the buyer’s outside options. It will be interesting to investigate how this information should (or should not) be revealed to maximize the seller's expected revenue.

21506616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21506616.value: This project analyzed the role of outside options in bargaining. The project focused on the informational effect of outside options. For example, in wage negotiation, a firm’s outside option can disclose its private information relevant to the negotiation. Therefore, the firm will strategically reveal or conceal its outside option. The project demonstrated that such an informational effect is crucial in understanding bargaining problems. One of the the project’s main findings is that the interplay between outside options and asymmetric information can account for a delay in bargaining. A bargaining delay can be puzzling at a glance; given that a delay imposes immense costs on both sides of the negotiation, why can’t the negotiation parties make the apparent Pareto improvement by making a deal earlier? This is one of the longstanding questions in economic theory. The project shedded light on this problem by demonstrating that a delay can occur in bargaining due to the seller’s motive to avoid negotiation break-offs. More specifically, the project found that negotiation break-off inevitably results in information rent to the buyer. Thus, the seller can increase his or her profit by delaying the negotiation rather than breaking it off immediately. The project also applies this insights to current economic issues in the real world.

21610716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21610716.value: 中國1992年海商法下對中國FOB賣方的保障：司法實踐中是否已經獲得？

21610716.label: Project Objectives
21610716.value: Examine the provisions in the Chinese Maritime Code 1992 concerning the protection of the Chinese FOB seller and discuss the ambiguity of law. Collect and study relevant judgments and interview judges to determine why protection for the Chinese FOB seller has not been provided by some courts. Select some typical cases and recommend them to the SPC for consideration as guiding cases in China to unify the relevant judicial practice. Summarise the collected judgments and work out draft amendments to relevant provisions in the CMC to resolve the problem of legal ambiguity.
rows: Examine the provisions in the Chinese Maritime Code 1992 concerning the protection of the Chinese FOB seller and discuss the ambiguity of law.
Collect and study relevant judgments and interview judges to determine why protection for the Chinese FOB seller has not been provided by some courts.
Select some typical cases and recommend them to the SPC for consideration as guiding cases in China to unify the relevant judicial practice.
Summarise the collected judgments and work out draft amendments to relevant provisions in the CMC to resolve the problem of legal ambiguity.

21610716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21610716.value: In international sale of goods using FOB term, normally the buyer is the shipper and the seller has no contractual relation with the carrier. Because foreign buyers control the international market, the majority of Chinese export is done with FOB term. The main risk of the Chinese FOB sellers is that they may not obtain the bill of lading from the carrier and therefore lose the important security for payment from foreign buyers. The Chinese Maritime Code 1992 (the CMC) provides that the shipper means the contractual shipper and the person who actually delivers the goods to the carrier. It seems that the Chinese FOB sellers could be protected because they become the shipper in the CMC. However, the CMC has not clarified whether the Chinese FOB seller has the same rights like the contractual shipper. This ambiguity of law directly resulted in the uncertainty of Chinese judicial practice. Based on a preliminary study of relevant Chinese judgments, it has been found that some courts actually rejected the Chinese FOB sellers’ application for delivery of bills of lading to them. Thus the position of the Chinese sellers remains uncertain and even worse in judicial practice. The previous research work on these problems was mainly theoretical. Although some discussed a few judicial decisions, the study of judicial practice is extremely insufficient comparing with hundreds of judgments concerning these problems of the Chinese FOB seller. The study of Chinese judgments was neglected because those judgments are not precedents and sources of Chinese law. In 2010, the Supreme People’s Court (the SPC) of China set up a guiding cases system. In 2015, the SPC stipulated that guiding cases shall be followed by all Chinese courts if applicable. It is a golden opportunity to solve the aforementioned problems. The investigation of this project aims to examine relevant Chinese judgments and find out reasons for the unsuccessful protection in judicial practice. The method of investigation is an empirical study including the study of judgments and interview of Chinese judges. The outcomes of the investigation will hopefully lead to the selection of typical cases concerning the protection of the Chinese FOB seller to recommend as guiding cases to the SPC and a draft amendment of the CMC concerning the Chinese FOB seller status to the legislature of China. Those outcomes will contribute to the certainty of relevant judicial practice and the improvement of Chinese maritime law. 在使用FOB術語的國際貨物買賣中，買方通常是托運人，而賣方和承運人沒有合同關係。因為外國買方控制國際市場，中國的出口貿易主要使用FOB術語。對於中國賣方，主要的風險是不能從承運人獲得提單，從而失去對外國買方付款的重要保障。 中國1992年海商法（海商法）規定，托運人包括契約托運人和將貨物交給承運人的實際托運人。中國FOB賣方看起來得到了保障，因為他們在海商法下成為托運人。但是，海商法沒有澄清中國FOB賣方是否與契約托運人有同樣的權利。這個法律的模糊性直接導致中國司法實踐的不確定性。根據對中國相關判決書的初步研究可以發現，有些法院事實上拒絕了中國FOB賣方要求獲得提單的請求。因此，在司法實踐中，中國賣方的境遇仍然不確定，甚至惡化。 對於上述問題，過往的研究偏向理論。儘管有一些司法判決的討論，但相對上百個關於中國FOB賣方問題的判決而言，對司法實踐的研究仍然非常有限。對於中國判決書的忽略，主要是因為判決不是中國法律的先例或法源。 2010年，中國最高人民法院（最高院）設立指導案例制度。2015年，最高院規定，中國法院應當遵循指導案例。這是一個解決上述問題的黃金時間。本專案調研的目的在於研究中國法院的判決和尋找司法實踐中沒有有效保護的原因。調研的方法為實證研究，包括對判決的解讀和對法官的訪問。調研的結果有望遴選出對中國FOB賣方進行有效保護的判決，並向最高院推薦為指導案例，同時就中國FBO賣方的地位問題對海商法提出修改建議。上述研究結果將對相關司法實踐的確定性和中國海商法的改善有所貢獻。

21610716.label: Major findings and research outcome
21610716.value: In Chinese judicial practice, the FOB seller is recognised as the actual shipper under the Chinese Maritime Code once he has delivered the goods to the carrier. By such delivery performance, the FOB seller is recognised as the party to the contract with the carrier. As the party to the contract, the FOB seller is thus entitled to take the bill of lading from the carrier. He, by holding the bill of lading, thus has the rights of suit against the carrier. Consequently, the FOB seller has vested in him the contractual rights and may become subject to the contractual liabilities. These exceptions to privity of contract are for the benefit of the FOB seller but do not convincingly balance the interests of parties involved in international sale and carriage transactions. This is a policy-oriented practice for the protection of the Chinese seller’s benefits in FOB export trade.

21610716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21610716.value: The FOB seller may be protected by using the CIF term, or by reserving his rights in the sale of goods contract, rather than the exceptions to privity of contract in carriage of goods by sea. The difference between Chinese law and English law lies in the adoption of different rules, i.e. Chinese Maritime Code brings in the concept of actual shipper in the Hamburg Rules and English law incorporates the Hague-Visby Rules. Regarding who is entitled to demand a bill of lading from the carrier, it is suggested that China should abandon the concept of actual shipper in the Chinese Maritime Code so as to keep the doctrine of privity of contract in carriage of goods by sea. China also needs a legislative device like the COGSA 1992 to provide the FOB seller with the rights of suit in certain circumstance as a legal exception to the privity of contract of carriage of goods by sea.

21610716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21610716.value: The shipper and the carrier are the parties to a contract of carriage of goods by sea. Chinese Maritime Code however provides that a Chinese seller of goods who is not a contractual party to the carriage contract is a shipper. It thus provide the Chinese seller who act as actual shipper a contractual right against the carrier. It breaks the contractual relation between the carrier and the contractual shipper and causes difficulties in shipping carriage of goods by sea. Chinese law and judicial practice are inconsistent with internationally recognised law of carriage of goods by sea. It is necessary to find out the difference between Chinese law and international rules. The concept of actual shipper recognised by Chinese courts is to protect the interests of Chinese sellers. It should be abandoned so as to recognise the contractual relationship between the carrier and the contractual shipper. Chinese sellers should find protections from sale of goods contract, rather than the carriage of goods by sea contract.

21610816.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21610816.value: 悔意：刑事量刑以被告懺悔作為減刑因素之跨學科及綜合方法研究

21610816.label: Project Objectives
21610816.value: To advance an improved understanding of remorse generally and from a legal philosophical perspective, as well as more specifically with regard to the underlying theoretical foundation and justification for its recognition as a legitimate mitigating factor in criminal justice sentencing practices. To make a direct contribution to the development of the sentencing frameworks in terms of, and policies underpinning the recognition and quantification of remorse in mitigation of sentences in Hong Kong, the United Kingdom and South Africa. To establish, by way of empirical research, three datasets on the recognition and quantification of remorse in the sentencing practices of Hong Kong, the United Kingdom and South Africa. These datasets are not only valuable for this research project but will also be used for future research projects on related topics and particularly with regard to culture-specific conceptualisations, demonstrations, and legal recognitions of remorse.
