21610816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21610816.value: The recognition and quantification of remorse in mitigation of sentence is generally accepted in most criminal justice systems. In terms of the law, every aspect with regard to the type and the nature of the offence, the impact thereof on victims, and the behaviour of offenders throughout the ordeal, are carefully analysed to determine if remorse is present and whether such remorse justifies a mitigation in sentence. In addition to this legal-penal significance of remorse, the display of remorse also has a societal significance in that public discourse and communal values generally offer redemption and reintegration to the remorseful offender but dehumanise those who lack remorse. Yet, the concept of remorse, both in terms of its expression as well as the accurate observation thereof, remains murky and generally indeterminable. Likewise, the underlying theoretical foundation and justification for remorse as a legitimate mitigating factor in sentencing is also unclear and serves as an impediment to certain and consistent judicial decision-making on the recognition and quantification of remorse in sentencing. In fact, it is hypothesised that a more mindful deliberation of the content, role and place of remorse in terms of penal theories, and a more explicit articulation of when and how the presence or absence of remorse should influence quantification of sentence are essential in ensuring a just and transparent sentencing regime. This research project offers a trans-disciplinary and mixed-method study of the concept remorse, and has at aim to provide a principled-approach to the recognition of remorse as a mitigating factor in sentencing. The project centres on three research questions: (i) What exactly is remorse as an affect of relevance to the law? (ii) How is remorse (appropriately) demonstrated by an offender and correctly identified as such in a criminal justice setting and in different sentencing frameworks? (iii) How - if at all - should remorse impact on, and be quantified in terms of sentencing? These three research questions will be considered through a combination of research methodologies, including comparatively and empirically in terms of the sentencing frameworks of three common law and historically connected jurisdictions: Hong Kong, the United Kingdom, and South Africa. The outcomes of this project will ultimately provide for an improved understanding of remorse generally and from a legal-philosophical perspective, and more specifically in terms of the sentencing frameworks and practices of the three selected jurisdictions. 大部份法律制度均接受懺悔作為減刑因素有一定的認受性及可量化性。就法律的角度而言，罪行的種類及性質、對受害人造成的影響以及被告於案件調查以至審訊其間的表現和所受到的待遇，均被仔細分析以判斷被告是否有悔意，而該悔意又是否足以被視為減刑的理由。悔意除了在刑法的懲罰制度中有上述的意義外，悔意的表達同時亦有一定的社會意義。這是源於公眾的價值觀一般會對有悔意的人予以接納及包容，反之對毫無悔意的表現給予去人性化的反應。然而，悔意一詞無論在字面意義或在精確考究下，其概念仍是模糊不清且難以界定的。同樣地，悔意背後的理論基礎以及悔意本身作為減刑的考慮因素，此等概念也是有欠清晰。亦因其概念不清的原因，故窒礙了法庭判刑時以被告人懺悔而減刑的肯定性及一致性。事實上，悔意於懲罰理論中的內容及角色的討論，及一個更明確的指標指示悔意該何時和如何形響量刑準則，以上兩點對達至一個公義及透明的判刑體制至關重要，故我們須視以上兩點為必要的討論。 本研究透過跨學科及綜合方法研究悔意的概念，旨在為悔意於量刑時的認受性提供一個原則性的方法。本研究圍繞三個問題進行： （一）悔意與法律有何直接關係？ （二）悔意如何恰當地由被告表達以及在不同的量刑框架下於犯罪司法體系中被正確辨認出？ （三）如悔意對量刑準則有影響，那些影響該如何量化呢？ 本研究將以比較法律及實證研究法去分析香港、英國及南非，三個由普通法及歷史因素連繫的法律管轄區，以解答上述三個問題。本研究最終會為悔意的法律哲學概念，包括量刑框假以及在上述三個法律管轄區的實際應用提供一個更全面的理解。

21612716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21612716.value: Urban slums, home to one third of the urban population in developing countries, are evident in many rapidly growing cities in countries like China, Brazil and India (UN-Habitat, 2012). Though each country has its own term for slums, these slums are commonly characterized by inadequate basic infrastructure provisions of water and electricity, poor sanitation, overcrowded and dilapidated housing, and insecure tenure. One type of slums in China is urban villages (Chengzhongcun), which provide low-cost accommodation to migrant workers. From a planning perspective, slums are eyesores in cities that are being modernized, and sooner or later they will need to be redeveloped. In China, a typical redevelopment procedure is to demolish existing buildings and construct new ones in accordance with planning regulations, a process widely known in the West as slum clearance. This approach exacerbates the shortage of low-cost housing units available to low-income migrant workers, which constitute a large portion of village tenants. Yet resettlement plans that come together with clearance projects rarely take into consideration the interest of tenants, including low-income migrants. This means that they have simply been excluded from the decision-making process, with no influence over how their home neighborhood would be redeveloped. In other words, as a marginalized social group, they are visible in size but mute in voice. Based on my previous research on urban villages, I have observed that low-income migrant workers as well as a sizable number of creative people in the art and design professions, which scholars term “the creative class” (Florida, 2002), live in village settlements. In this project, I explore how creative people residing in urban villages help build up a sense of community among village residents, particularly migrant workers, thus contributing to a shift of slum development practices from complete clearance to incremental upgrading. Most importantly, this project sheds light on a broader theme, that is, how marginalized migrant workers become empowered during the process of China’s urbanization. I plan to adopt a case study method with a focus on two cases—Songzhuang in Beijing and Baishizhou in Shenzhen. Given that the emergence of the creative class in urban villages is a fairly recent phenomenon, the rationale behind my case selection is that these two cases represent a unique situation, which documents the positive influence of creative people on migrant workers’ engagement in neighborhood change. I will collect data through site visits, document reviews, surveys and interviews. 联合国人居署2012年报告表明，中国、巴西、印度等发展中国家快速增长的城市，贫民窟容纳了三分之一的城市人口。尽管贫民窟的定义因国而异，它们却有类似的特征：水电等基本供给设施匮乏、卫生状况差、住房拥挤破旧、及居住权稳定性无保障。中国的城中村，这个提供给上亿农民工廉价住房的地区，往往被比作中国城市的贫民窟。 从规划的角度看，贫民窟是城市现代化的绊脚石，迟早要被推倒重建。中国的城市往往按照贫民窟清除的模式开发城中村，即拆除并清理所有现存建筑物，然后依据规划构筑全新房屋。这个开发模式事实上极大缩减市场上廉价房的供给，使得大量依赖城中村低廉房租的农民工无处可居。即便清除式开发包括重新安置计划，但是此类计划中很少考虑租户的权益，这也意味着农民工在城中村开发过程中没有任何参与度、影响力或话语权。简言之，他们是一群被社会边缘化的群体，量多而声哑。 笔者对城中村的研究发现，城中村的租户不仅有低收入农民工，而且有相当多的创意人群体，从事着艺术设计类职业。这类人就是学者们笔下的“创意阶层”(Florida, 2002)。本研究旨在探索居住在城中村的创意人在社区建设中的积极作用，他们如何通过组织文化活动提高城中村居民的参与度，拉近各类居民的距离感，增强居民的社区感，进而有利于城中村改造模式从推倒式清理到渐进式改善的过渡。广义上讲，本研究通过详细实例阐述了，中国城市化过程中，特殊的创意群体如何帮助增能赋权被边缘化的农民工。

21612716.label: Major findings and research outcome
21612716.value: Urban villages as a special form of urban slums in the Chinese context have provided low-cost housing to rural-urban and inter-urban migrants, among whom are creative people. The project takes a special perspective on the development of arts clusters in multiple Chinese cities. The findings are summarized below: First, urban villages can better nurture creative people than planning-made arts districts because they can provide an environment with a flexible and autonomous land development arrangement, frequent interactions between artists and village residents, and a broad spectrum of entrepreneurial opportunities. This finding was first presented at two international conferences (2017; 2018) and then published by a peer-review journal (Li and Liu, 2019). Second, even among urban villages-turned arts clusters, the government should take a supervision role, rather than a leading role in arts cluster development because too strong top-down policy intervention may damage their creative nature, for which creative people rely on. Such nature is characterized by openness, inclusiveness, flexibility, diversity and tolerance. This finding is articulated in a paper under review (Li, Chen and Talamini, 2021) and was presented at an international conference (2019). Third, for arts clusters that specialized in traditional arts creations (e.g., Chinese embroidery), local adaptive and networking capabilities are essential in creating a new path out of the tension between culture and industry. And these capabilities are largely determined by local openness/ flexibility, entrepreneurship, and linkage capacity. This finding was presented at an international conference first (2017) and then published by a peer-review journal (Li, Jiang and Nam, 2020).

21612716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21612716.value: It has been observed that the number of urban villages has been diminishing in all Chinese cities caused by gentrification, urban renewal, and urban village redevelopment. Low-income households, many of which are migrants and used to be urban village tenants, have faced formidable difficulty in finding affordable living spaces in the urban area. Is it equitable to ignore housing needs of low-income families for urban development? How can the local government offer housing welfare service to these marginalized groups? Following the urban village development studies, a potential research topic is public housing studies that target urban village settlements. Questions worth exploring include what types of low-cost rentals can fill in the demand from former urban village tenants? To what extent existing public housing policies is (in)equitable across social classes? What can be done to mitigate this inequality in housing welfare?

21612716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21612716.value: This research project investigates the trajectory of arts cluster evolvement in urban villages in several Chinese cities with a focus on the importance of a nurturing environment to the creative class (i.e., the young artists). The project highlights several conditions of a nurturing environment to creative people. The cluster should not be rigidly planned and administered; tenancy rules should be flexible and inclusive; villagers and artists display quite positive social mix; there is plenty of alternative business opportunities for both villagers and artists. These findings can help urban planners design effective creative cluster policies to sustain the creative nature of these clusters. In the meantime, this project contributes to urban villages studies by raising another positive impact of urban villages to the Chinese society.

21614616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21614616.value: 在十七世紀中後期清初的遺民寫作中，空間想象是一個顯著的現象。遺民回憶舊朝遺跡，在現實或想象中建築庭園，歎惋無地可居的現狀，也著力描繪夢境中的奇幻空間。朝代更替亦為遺民的空間書寫增添了獨特的悲愴意味。我的初步研究表明遺民的空間書寫集中于殘山剩水與瑯環夢境這兩個相輔相成的意象。在動蕩的政治局勢中，兩者展現出摧毀與重建的辯證關係。我希望在進一步的研究中描繪出清初文學與文化中空間書寫與想象的各種層面，分析其重要性，並且探討這種現象的成因，追索現象背後的社會歷史因素。 這是一個跨學科研究項目，將運用文學史、藝術史、文化史、以及思想史等領域的研究方法。因為大量遺民身兼作家、畫家、鑒賞家等多種身份，有必要比較他們如何在文字和視覺材料中處理同一主題，以便考察同一種思想如何在不同媒介中展現，以及不同媒介表現力的側重。文化史和思想史研究可以為遺民文學研究提供恰當的語境。很多遺民具備史才與哲思，因此必須將他們的空間書寫與他們的史學和哲學思想聯繫起來加以考察。他們的書寫跨越各種文類，包括筆記、野史、尺牘等等。將這些異質的材料結合起來有助於對大量文學與非文學文獻的比較，以建立較為全面的遺民文化研究。

21614916.label: Realisation of objectives
21614916.value: The current research project contains the following four research objectives, they include: 1. investigate the effectiveness of faith-based addiction treatment in Hong Kong and the underlying delivery mechanisms that bring the treatment effects into play in a comparative fashion by simultaneously inviting addict patients in secular-based treatment as controls. 2. inform local practitioners of faith-based addiction treatment and related parties in the government and NGOs of the findings of this study to enhance treatment service. 3. lay the groundwork for more overarching research on addiction in Asian regions in the future. 4. enhance our knowledge and understanding of substance abusing behaviours indigenous to the non-western context. Generally speaking, the current research project provides an adequate opportunity to attain the above-mentioned research objectives. Specifically, for objective 1, the current research project recruited both recovering substance addict participants from faith-based and secular-based intervention services to investigate effects of religiosity and other psychosocial factors, such as life meaning, psychological distress, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and in contribution to their subsequent abstinence of using substances after completion of treatment. Apparently, it is found that recovering substance addict participants who received treatment in both faith-based and secular-based approaches significantly showed growth in their religiosity, especially for the former group, in which religiosity is an imperative contributor to enhance their life meaning, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy, as well as reduced psychological distress that acted together to lead to their subsequent abstinence. Furthermore, substance user participants’ growth in religiosity can be singled out as an important predictor of their abstinence subsequently, which may be related to its implications of life transformation, embodiment of life purpose, and meaningful existence. Besides, enhancement of life meaning, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy, and decrease of psychological distress are also crucial contributors to lead abstinence of substance user participants, which together mediate and interplay with religiosity of recovering substance addict participants in relation to their subsequent abstinence after completion of treatment intervention. Hence, both faith-based and secular-based treatment services should consider the importance of religious and spiritual growth and other related psychosocial factors concomitantly in order to achieve optimal efficiency of their interventions. For more details, please refer to the book chapter, two journal articles (under review), and the research report generated from the current research project, which are attached in this report. For objective 2, the research report attached in this report has sent to practitioners of local substance addiction services for their reference to enhance their current service delivery. The service agents that have been sent the research report include Barnabas Charitable Service Association, Christian New Being Fellowship, Christian New Life Association, Christian Zheng Sheng Association, Ling Oi Centre, Glorious Praise Fellowship, Jockey Club Lodge of Rising Sun, Mission Ark, Operation Dawn, The Society for the Aid and Rehabilitation of Drug Abusers, The Society of Rehabilitation and Crime Prevention, Wu Oi Christian Centre, Evergreen Lutheran Centre and Rainbow Lutheran Centre, Hong Kong Christian Service PS33, Hong Kong Children & Youth Services Sane Centre, Caritas HUGS Centre, Enlighten Centre, Neo-Horizon, Cheer Lutheran Centre, and Caritas Lok Heep Club. Besides, the PI has contacted some participating agents, such as Ling Oi Centre, Mission Ark, Operation Dawn, and The Society of Rehabilitation and Crime Prevention to verbally explain them the main findings of the research, except the provision of the research report. Furthermore, the contact information of the PI has also given to the above-mentioned parties of substance abstinence services for their inquiries of the current research findings, through which related parties could contact the PI to seek explications if concerns arisen. Hence, it is hopefully that the current research can provide practitioners and management of local substance abstinence services some useful insights and findings to enhance their service interventions. For objective 3, the current research project found significant relationships of substance user participants’ development of religiosity and psychosocial factors in contribution to their subsequent abstinence after treatment, in which the psychosocial factors, such as life meaning, psychological distress, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy are closely related to substance user participants’ development of religiosity during treatment and also have coalescent impacts on their after-treatment abstinence with their growth in religiosity. In addition, it is found that family support and pro-abstinence friendship are crucial interpersonal resources of substance user participants’ subsequent abstinence, which may reflect the importance of collective consciousness and interpersonal influences to affect substance-using behaviors in Chinese and Asian societies and cultures. For this, this research can be a valuable foundation for future addiction research conducted in Chinese and Asian contexts. Specifically, comparative and cross-culture research can be conducted in the future. For example, future study can compare cultural differences across countries/ regions in Asia to scrutinize whether culture is moderator to differentiate the effects of religious/ spiritual, psychological, family, interpersonal, and mental factors on recovery of recovering substance addict participants during and after treatment. Furthermore, due to significant distinct societal, ethnic, political, and cultural divergences between Asian and Western countries, cross-nation research can be conducted to examine and explore how different systems at religious/ spiritual, cognitive, psychological, family, interpersonal, and mental levels contribute to after-treatment abstinence of recovering substance addict participants in Asian and Western contexts. If the above-mentioned research suggestions can be carried out in the future, it is believed that new insights and discoveries concerning substance using behaviors are to be obtained. To our knowledge, as regarding to objective 4, the current research is the first attempt to investigate both faith and psychosocial factors of recovering substance addict participants developed during treatment in relation to their subsequent abstinence after treatment in Chinese context, in which development of religiosity, life meaning, psychological distress, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy were significantly and interactively predictive of their subsequent abstinence after treatment. Hence, the current research confirmed the importance of multilevel intervention to help recovering substance addict participants to achieve complete desistance from abusing substances, which supports the use of multi-system approach as an intervention strategy to help recovering substance addict participants cultivate resources at spiritual, cognitive, psychological, family, social, and mental levels simultaneously. Hence, future indigenous research should examine and compare the effects of different systems concomitantly at spiritual, cognitive, psychological, family, social, and mental levels in relation to abusing behaviors.

21614916.label: Major findings and research outcome
21614916.value: The current research project mainly investigated the effects of development of religiosity, psychological distress, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy of recovering substance addict participants in faith-based and secular-based treatment on their subsequent recovery and abstinence after treatment. First, the main findings are that religiosity of recovering substance addict participants was found as a developing and dynamic variable that has been observed to cultivate and grow during treatment and significantly contributive to their after-treatment abstinence and also significantly predictive of their better development of life meaning, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy, as well as decreased psychological distress during the treatment process. Nevertheless, it has been confirmed that levels of religiosity of recovering substance addict participants in faith-based treatment were significantly higher than their counterparts in secular-based treatment. This is valid as the former treatment approach more acknowledges the use of the Christian theory of substance addiction to deliver services and interventions. Second, the development of life meaning, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy, as well as psychological distress of recovering substance addict participants was not only directly predictive of their after-treatment abstinence, but also significantly mediated the effects of recovering substance addict participants’ development of religiosity on their subsequent abstinence. Hence, these psychosocial factors should be of important concern for future service delivery of substance addiction recovery. It should be noted that life meaning, psychological distress, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy of recovering substance addict participants were also found as a dynamic and changing concept and construct, meaning that their growth or decline in these cognitive, psychological, family, interpersonal, and mental variables are not only directly affected by other external factors, such as their development religiosity, but also directly contributed to their successful abstinence later on. Third, it is found that development of religiosity of recovering substance addict participants not only significantly predicted their growth in life meaning, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy, as well as decease in psychological distress, but also its developing and changing nature was significantly related to the development and growth/ decline of substance user participants’ life meaning, psychological distress, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy synchronously, which together contributed to their subsequent recovery and abstinence after treatment. Therefore, as aforementioned, researchers and practitioners of substance addiction services should adopt a social systems and ecological perspective to consider, examine and tackle substance abusive behaviors in long run.

21614916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21614916.value: For further development of research, scholars should consider to conduct 1) more extended longitudinal research to examine the abstinence and relapse processes of recovering substance addict participants 2) cross-culture research to explore whether cultural and societal differences are contributive to and moderate effects of religiosity and psychosocial factors on subsequent recovery and abstinence. 3) more complicated multilevel research to compare effects of religiosity / spiritual, cognitive, psychological, family, interpersonal, and mental domains on subsequent recovery and abstinence of recovering substance addict participants. For action to be taken, practitioners of substance addiction services should consider 1) recovery and abstinence of substance addiction is a progressive process that is simultaneously affected by multiple systems at religious, cognitive, psychological, family, and interpersonal levels. Hence, integration of the impacts of respective systems is needed. 2) collaboration is suggested for both faith-based and secular treatment services to exchange their good practices in order to improve their service delivery. 3) prevention of relapse is critically needed as some of the recovering substance addict participants in the current study re-assumed substance use after treatment. Manifestly, high relapse rates are reported in research. Therefore, a comprehensive follow-up service is needed for keeping released recovering substance addict participants’ desistance.

21614916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21614916.value: The current research investigated effectiveness of faith-based treatment on abstinence of recovering substance addict participants while simultaneously taking their counterparts in secular-based treatment as comparison. Results of the study showed that development of religiosity was a significant and robust contributor in prediction of recovering substance addict participants’ after-treatment abstinence and also their growth in life meaning, family support, pro-abstinence friendship, and abstinent self-efficacy, and decrease in psychological distress that in turn significantly predicted their after-treatment abstinence and mediated the effects of religiosity on their after-treatment abstinence. Apparently, implications of the current study reveal that recovery and abstinence of substance addiction are progressive process simultaneously affected by multiple systems at religious, cognitive, psychological, family, interpersonal, and mental levels. Hence, integration of these systems concurrently in future research on investigating substance abusive behaviors and provision of optimal intervention services is much needed. Besides, development of religiosity is important for recovering substance addict participants’ after-treatment abstinence. The current research project lays a solid foundation for future cross-culture and comparative research, and acts as a reference for more complicated longitudinal studies locally to further examine the transition of recovering trajectories of recovering substance addict members in different treatment services.

21615316.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21615316.value: 後圖像：電腦映像年代的類比

21615316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21615316.value: This project questions, within the theoretical framework of image studies, the way the development of automated image recognition transforms the concept of resemblance, focusing on the particular case of visual similarity search engines that use image recognition algorithms to find visually similar images to an input image. The project asks whether the traditional criteria of resemblance still apply here, or whether image recognition algorithms foster a new concept of resemblance – and of the image. Despite the growing scholarship on the effect of automated vision on the relation between humans and machines (Virilio 1994, Farocki 2004, Paglen 2014), the relation between image and posthuman theory has not been made explicit, with the exception of David Tomas’ 2013 study of machine vision and the posthuman. Yet, if machines are increasingly in charge of vision and recognition we need to understand what they see, how they recognise and how this alters the notion of the image. The project tackles the issue of posthuman vision in the relatively limited yet paradigmatic area of Internet vision, focusing on the particular case of visual similarity search engines. It will test a series of about 100 exemplary images culled from the PI’s own image library (including images taken by the PI and found on the Web), using both Google Search by Image and visual similarity software developed by researchers at Carnegie Mellon University. The comparative evaluation of the test results will form a basis on which to address the following questions: 1) With what types of images do visual similarity search algorithms fail, and why? 2) What are the key characteristics of resemblance for a computer, and 3) How does this affect our (humanist) understanding of vision and visual resemblance? The answers to these questions will shed light on the profound challenges posed by computer vision to the human(ist) notion of visual resemblance that has historically been based on human vision. Drawing on posthuman theory, the project aims to propose a preliminary theory of the ‘post-image’ in the age of computer vision. The results of the project will be of interest to scholars and students in the fields of visual, media and communication studies, particularly image studies, and also to the general public. 這項目詰問，在影像學的理論框架下，自動化影像辨識的發展路向，如何對類比概念造成轉變。聚焦於視像類同搜尋器的特殊情況，利用圖像辨識計算法以找尋與輸入影像相似的東西。我們想知道傳統的類比規範是否仍然有效，又或者影像辨識是否巳培育出一個新的類比圖像概念。儘管人類與機器之間的視像效應愈被深究(Virilio 1994, Farocki 2004, Paglen 2014) ，影像與後人類關係的理論卻並不明確，David Tomas 於2013關於機器視像與後人類的研究是一個例外。假若機器愈來愈主宰視覺與㸤識，我們便有需要了解它們看到了甚麼？它們怎樣辨認東西？它們怎樣改變圖像的概念？這項目抓住一個後人類視覺的問題：互聯網的視像範式相對有限，故聚焦於搜尋器的個別特殊情況。我會從私人庫存中撮取大約一百個示範圖像（有些來自互聯網），利用「谷歌」圖像搜尋器作測試，試驗結果的比對評測形成基礎，解答以下問題：（一）算法對甚麼圖像無法生效？（二）電腦類比的主要特性是甚麼？（三）這怎樣影響我們對視覺視像類比的理解？這些問題的答案，揭示一個由電腦視覺向人類影像類比概念的高深挑戰，借鑒於後人類理論，這項目的目的就是在這電腦視像的世代，提出一個「後圖像」的初步理論，而這結果，對於研究視覺、媒體及信息的學生及學者，以至普羅大眾，都相信是相當有趣的。

21615416.label: Project Objectives
21615416.value: To critique the drawbacks of existing approaches that ignore the effect of RS on person ability estimates, item difficulty estimates, and psychometric properties of scales; To develop a new methodology under the IRT framework that accounts for the impact of multiple types of RS simultaneously; To create a class of simple and effective procedures under the M-H and LR frameworks to examine test equality when multiple types of RS are involved; To investigate the applications of the proposed procedures to a small study in Hong Kong and an international educational assessment and to compare the performance of new procedures; To develop a platform from which practitioners and researchers can conduct the proposed procedures to examine RS and test fairness.
rows: To critique the drawbacks of existing approaches that ignore the effect of RS on person ability estimates, item difficulty estimates, and psychometric properties of scales;
To develop a new methodology under the IRT framework that accounts for the impact of multiple types of RS simultaneously;
To create a class of simple and effective procedures under the M-H and LR frameworks to examine test equality when multiple types of RS are involved;
To investigate the applications of the proposed procedures to a small study in Hong Kong and an international educational assessment and to compare the performance of new procedures;
To develop a platform from which practitioners and researchers can conduct the proposed procedures to examine RS and test fairness.

21615416.label: Realisation of objectives
21615416.value: Objective 1 The PI has leaded the research team, including full-time and part-time research assistants, and undergraduate students, to conduct comprehensive literature review in related issues. We found that most studies have concentrated on extreme response styles (ERS, the tendency to endorse extreme response categories) and proposed simple to complicated strategies incorporating with raw scores or using latent ability estimation, respectively. For instance, researchers might use items from multiple scales and then an independent external measure is created to measure ERS (Greenleaf, 1992). The most critical problem of this approach is its psychometric properties that might vary across subgroups (De Jong et al., 2008), suggesting a possibility of biased conclusions in measurement invariance. We therefore conducted a series of simulation studies and analyzed empirical datasets to investigate if the conclusion of differential item functioning (DIF) detection is based. In our studies (Chen, Jin, & Wang, 2017; Jin & Chen, 2020), we have found that a difference in extreme response style (ERS) between groups caused inflated false-positive rates and deflated true-positive rates in conventional DIF approaches (e.g., logistic regression or multiple-indicators and multiple-causes, MIMIC) when ERS was not considered. We also found that the literature has suggested using a mixed-format design (a combination of positive-worded, PW, and negative-worded, NW, items) to control acquiescence and ERS. This design has been commonly used in personality assessments such as Rosenberg’s self-esteem scale and the Big Five Inventory. We conducted analyses in International Personality Item Pool and Attitude toward Peace Walls in Ireland and findings to investigate if a mixed-format design functions as expected. Our findings suggested that such design can only control acquiescence but did not function well in removing the impact of ERS on survey questionnaires (Chen & Jin, 2020). Objective 2 Studies have reported that 3.5% to 70% might give the same answer to all questions, and there is no objective criterion to classify a specific pattern of aberrant responses (e.g., Costa & McCrae, 2008; Johnson, 2005). As existing approaches have not well addressed the detection of other types of response patterns, this project extended the item response theory (IRT) to account for the impact of random selection and consistent endorsement of a specific response category in survey questionnaires. We adopted the idea of confirmatory mixture model “in that (a) the number of latent classes is specified in advance, and (b) the probability of the response categories in each inattentive class is specified in advance.” (Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018). The model is a general model with great flexibility and can account for different types of inattentive responses simultaneously. Practitioners and researchers can easily adjust the number of classes and probability of endorsing each response category that might happen in their studies in advance. Objective 3 Although RSs have been commonly studied in survey research, it remains unclear how they may influence the performance of non-IRT approaches in differential item functioning (DIF) assessments, a way to examine measurement invariance and to test fairness in IRT terminology. We selected two of the most popular, conventional non-IRT methods, logistic regression (LR) and Mantel-Haenszel (M-H), and carefully examined whether or not the performance in DIF assessment would be influenced by ERS. As expected, these methods are vulnerable to ERS and yielded severely inflated type I error rates when there were no DIF items in a scale. As the difference in ERS between two groups increased, the performance of conventional approaches got worse (Chen et al., 2017). Studies have suggested that a RS would lead to an additional domain to the originally designed factor structure of a scale, which might lead to a biased conclusion of DIF detection. We also examined the impact of multidimensionality on the performance of conventional LR and M-H approaches and found multidimensionality lead to problematic DIF detections in LR and MH methods (Chen & Jin, 2018). However, as the estimation and complexity in M-H approaches increase as the dimension and response categories increase, we failed to develop new approaches under the M-H framework to solve the above issues. We therefore stayed in the development of LR approaches for RSs and intended to develop a class of new procedure under the framework of MIMIC. (Details are stated in the following paragraph). Under the LR framework, we proposed using variances of observed scores to indicate the magnitude of ERS (e.g., Chen & Jin, 2018; Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018). The impact of ERS on DIF detection could be controlled by incorporating the two variables (total score and the variance of observed scores on items) as covariates into logistic regression to control false-positive rates across situations and then yield trustworthy true-positive rates (Chen et al., 2017; Jin & Chen, 2020). We also developed a new class of MIMIC approach for detecting DIF when RSs were involved in datasets. MIMIC has been found to perform as well as conventional LR and M-H approaches and is particularly preferable when sample sizes are small. We found that ignoring ERS in dataset would lead to inflated false-positive rates in the conventional MIMIC approach. By incorporating the two variables (total score and the variance of observed scores on items) as covariates into the MIMIC, false-positive rates across situations were dropped back at the nominal level (.05) and true-positive rates became trustworthy (Jin & Chen, 2020). Objective 4 We have applied the proposed approaches to international datasets, including the International Personality Item Pool (Chen & Jin, 2020) and the Egypt and Saudi Arabia Survey (Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018), as well as regional studies, such as the 2011 Transport Customer Survey in South Wales (Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018), the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System by the US National Institutes of Health (Chen, Jin, & Wang, 2017), Attitude toward Peace Walls in Ireland (Chen & Jin, 2020), and the scale of Chinese Martial Resilience in Taiwan (Jin & Chen, 2020). These applications support the use of our proposed models across countries and regions. Objective 5 To meet Objective 5, Winbugs syntaxes, R codes or Matlab syntaxes are available in the published papers and/or upon request. Researchers and practitioner also can follow the suggested procedure in published papers and conduct the proposed approaches in commercial software (e.g., SPSS or Mplus). In addition, to facilitate the use of the proposed models, the PI delivered talked and illustrated how to conduct these approaches in software at Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences, Survey Design and Methodology, Mannheim, Germany; Department of Psychology, University of Mannheim, Germany; and Institute of Statistics, Academia Sinica, Taiwan.

21615416.label: Major findings and research outcome
21615416.value: Our studies found that a difference in extreme response style (ERS) between groups caused inflated false-positive rates and deflated true-positive rates in conventional differential item functioning (DIF) detections when ERS was not considered (Chen, Jin, & Wang, 2017; Jin & Chen, 2020). Even though the literature has suggested using a mixed-format design (a combination of positive-worded, PW, and negative-worded, NW, items) to control acquiescence and ERS, our study (Chen & Jin, 2020) found that such design can only control acquiescence. Thus, this project extended the mixture item response theory (IRT) to account for the impact of multiple types of RS simultaneously (Objective 2), such as random selection or consistent endorsement of a specific response category in survey questionnaires (Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018). As the IRT framework might be challenging for practitioners, this project created a class of simple and effective procedures for DIF detection (e.g., Chen & Jin, 2018; Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018) and extended existing DIF approaches to account for the impact of RS (Objective 3). We found that the impact of ERS on DIF detection could be controlled by incorporating the two variables (total score and the variance of observed scores on items) as covariates into logistic regression and multiple-indicators and multiple-causes (MIMIC) approaches to control false-positive rates across situations and then yield trustworthy true-positive rates (Chen et al., 2017; Jin & Chen, 2020). To investigate the applications of the proposed procedures and compare their performance against conventional methods (Objective 4), we have applied the proposed approaches to international datasets, including the International Personality Item Pool (Chen & Jin, 2020) and the Egypt and Saudi Arabia Survey (Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018), as well as regional studies, such as the 2011 Transport Customer Survey in South Wales (Jin, Chen, & Wang, 2018), the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System by the US National Institutes of Health (Chen, Jin, & Wang, 2017), Attitude toward Peace Walls in Ireland (Chen & Jin, 2020), and the scale of Chinese Martial Resilience in Taiwan (Jin & Chen, 2020). These applications support the use of our proposed models across countries and regions. In addition, to facilitate the use of the proposed models, R codes are available in the published papers and/or upon request (Objective 4).

21615416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21615416.value: With technological development, computerized and online administrations have gradually become more popular than traditional paper-pencil administrations. Delivery software and equipment can store all examinees’ behaviors, including response time (RT) to individual items. However, as researchers are unable to monitor respondents’ behaviors during the data collection process, it is essential to make use of indicators (e.g., RT) other than item responses to ensure data quality. Given the promising findings in the present study, it is possible that the PI and the research team can integrate the proposed approaches with cognitive and social psychology to develop innovative, flexible frameworks that can simultaneously estimate participants’ intended-to-be-measured attitudes and personalities by taking into consideration RS, RT, and a mixed-format design. We have adopted a hypothesized decision-making process of answering using a Likert scale into our proposed IRT model to develop an alternative tree-like IRT model termed the unfolding tree model and submitted the findings for publication. We expect to examine the relationship between RSs and RTs to PW items using a mixed-format design. To this end, we will adopt a two-level mixture model, combining both the UDtree and the response time model, in the future.

21615416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21615416.value: The project investigated the impact of response preferences on test fairness and quality of survey data. We not only developed approaches under advanced psychometric methods (e.g., item response theory) for professionals to use but also created a class of simple and effective framework for practitioners. The findings are convincing and can enhance our knowledge of test fairness when self-report questionnaires are used to understand people’s attitudes and personalities. The findings are particularly valuable for cross-cultural studies and group comparisons, as the preferences of people with diverse backgrounds might apply to a particular response category. For instance, Asian people always avoid extreme response categories and prefer the middle range (e.g., neutral). As a result, their responses do not reflect their true attitudes and may lead to biased conclusions in group comparisons. Our proposed procedures provide more precise methods to ensure fairness, equality, and the validity of the measures for several fields of study and practice in which surveys and questionnaires are used, including education, policy, business, and clinical areas. The present project fills a knowledge gap in the literature, helping to transfer expertise and skills in higher education to society. A broad range of researchers and practitioners will benefit from the findings.

22301916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22301916.value: Increases in air temperature and changes in precipitation regimes caused by global warming lead to considerable variations in heat waves and droughts, two of the most costly natural hazards for society. Droughts and heat waves are mainly caused by large-scale abnormal weather systems, such as ENSO and Atlantic Multi-decadal Oscillation. At the same time, the land-atmosphere interactions between droughts and heat waves can enhance each other. Such co-occurrences of droughts and heat waves are self-perpetuating and often associated with record-breaking drought-heat wave events. Although investigations of co-occurrence events have been conducted over Europe and the United States, similar studies for the Pearl River Basin (PRB), which is under a different climate system, are very limited. The PRB is located in the south China under subtropical monsoon climate and plays an indispensable role in providing water resources for the socioeconomic development of the Pearl River Delta (PRD), Hong Kong and Macau. Although the PRB is usually considered as with abundant precipitation, the high water demand and large population coupled with the changing climate make the PRB vulnerable to both droughts and heat waves. Droughts can cause salinity intrusion by seawater as water tables fall and thus causes threats to coastal drinking water supply, as well as adverse impacts on agricultural productivity, shipping and hydropower generation across the PRB, and heat waves can trigger heat-related diseases and deaths. The proposed study will investigate the changes, interactions and impacts of the co-occurrence of droughts and heat waves across the PRB under the changing climate. Datasets for observations, reanalysis data and Global Climate Model (GCM) outputs will be developed. The Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) and Weather Research and Forecasting model (WRF) will be configured for the PRB to simulate droughts and heat waves and conduct sensitivity experiments of the land-atmosphere interactions. The objectives of the proposed study are three-fold: (1) to characterize the spatio-temporal changes in the duration, intensity and joint return period of the co-occurrence across the PRB during the 21st century; (2) to analyze the sensitivity of land-atmosphere interactions to the development and evolution of the co-occurrence events under the changing climate, and; (3) to evaluate the impacts of the co-occurrence on society in terms of affected areas and heat stress to humans with the consideration of humidity. The expected outcomes of the proposed study will help decision makers to make predictions, give early warning, and plan for potential extreme drought-heat wave events. 全球暖化引起氣溫上升和降水變化，從而導致可能對人類社會造成巨大威脅的熱浪和乾旱兩大自然災害發生變化。乾旱和熱浪主要由大尺度異常天氣系統引起，例如厄爾尼諾/南方濤動和北大西洋長週期年代際震盪。同時，乾旱和熱浪之間的陸氣互動使乾旱熱浪互相增強。這種乾旱熱浪共現具有自身維持的特性，而且通常與極端乾旱或極端熱浪事件有關。相關研究已經在歐美等地區展開，在珠江流域的類似研究卻十分缺乏。珠江流域位於華南地區，主要受亞熱帶季風氣候控制，為珠江三角洲、香港和澳門的社會經濟發展提供水資源，扮演着重要角色。雖然珠江流域降水充沛，但是氣候變遷、人口增加和高需水量使得珠江流域對乾旱和熱浪的響應非常脆弱。乾旱可能導致海水入侵從而對沿海地區食水供應構成威脅，以及對農業生產、河運和水利發電等產生不利影響。熱浪可能引發熱相關疾病和傷亡。 本課題主要致力於研究珠江流域乾旱熱浪共現現象在氣候變遷下的變化、相互作用及影響，建立基於觀測、再分析數據和全球氣候模式輸出的數據庫，並使用水文模型Variable Infiltration Capacity和區域氣候模式Weather Research Forecasting模擬珠江流域的乾旱和熱浪，以及對其陸氣互動進行敏感性分析。本課題的研究目標包括：（1）預估21世紀珠江流域乾旱熱浪共現的歷時、強度和重現期等特徵的時空變化；（2）分析這種共現事件對陸氣耦合的敏感性；（3）評估共現事件對社會的影響，包括影響範圍和濕度對人體產生的熱壓力影響。本課題的結果將幫助決策者針對潛在極端乾旱和極端熱浪事件進行預測、預警和規劃。

22301916.label: Realisation of objectives
22301916.value: The project aims to investigate the changes, interactions and impacts of drought-heat wave co-occurrence in the Pearl River Basin (PRB). Based on hydrological modeling and analysis, the project has generated research findings of scientific importance and practical reference to address three key questions: (1) how heat waves, droughts, and their co-occurrence change under global warming? (2) what are the roles of land-atmosphere interactions in the evolution of drought-heat wave co-occurrence? and (3) how do the changing temperature and humidity affect the society? To realize the objectives, the research team first focused on characterizing the spatio-temporal variations in droughts, heat waves, and their co-occurrence. The consistency and discrepancy in variations of soil moisture from datasets developed by various techniques, including remote sensing (i.e. Essential Climate Variable), reanalysis (e.g. ERA-Interim and MERRA), hydrological simulations (e.g. GLDAS driven by assimilation of satellite- and ground-based meteorological observations and ISI-MIP driven by climate models), and Global Climate Model (GCM) simulations (i.e. CMIP5) were compared to identify the trends in soil moisture and evaluate the reliability. Because the soil moisture datasets have different specifications such as soil depth and resolution, preprocessing was conducted to reduce the impacts of different data specifications on the comparison and assessment. The modified Mann-Kendall test, a commonly used nonparametric trend test, was employed to identify the significance of linear trend in time series. Since the linear trend can not reflect the time-varying nature of changes in time series, we also used the Ensemble Empirical Model Decomposition (EEMD) method to extract the intrinsic trend of time series. Statistical metrics, including mean absolute error, mean bias error, root-mean-square error, unbiased root-mean-square error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, were used to evaluate the consistency and discrepancy of soil moisture variations. Moreover, we conducted hydrological simulations based on the Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) model and employed Maximum Covariance Analysis (MCA) to evaluate the contributions of precipitation and temperature to seasonal soil moisture changes in the PRB. VIC is a commonly used semi-distributed macroscale hydrological model. In the project, VIC was driven by meteorological observations from the China Meteorological Administration, and was implemented in the PRB. Other than the physically-derived parameters, parameters in the model were calibrated based on the optimization of an objective function. The objective function compared the VIC simulations against daily observed discharge at hydrological stations in the three sub-basins of the PRB, namely East River Basin, North River Basin, and West River Basin. MCA is a singular value decomposition analysis to identify the coherent patterns in the temporal and spatial patterns of two time series. Soil moisture and temperature outputs from GCMs were analyzed to evaluate their future changes under various future climate scenarios. Extreme temperature indices (e.g. heat wave duration index and warm nights) in different seasons estimated from GCM outputs were statistically downscaled based on transfer functions trained by the quantiles of temperature extremes at the coarse and fine resolutions. Meteorological outputs from the bias-corrected ISI-MIP GCMs were used to drive VIC to simulate hydrological conditions across the PRB under different future climate scenarios. Co-occurrence events of drought and heat waves were defined as days with heat waves (i.e. temperature higher than a prescribed threshold based on climatology) and droughts (i.e. soil moisture lower than a prescribed threshold based on climatology). The frequency and duration of the co-occurrence events were analyzed to evaluate their spatial-temporal variations. Areas in the PRB with higher risks of co-occurrence events were identified. Second, we conducted numerical experiments in the Weather Research and Forecasting model (WRF) to analyze the land-atmosphere interactions in a drought-heat wave co-occurrence event. WRF is a physically-based mesoscale numerical weather prediction model. In this project, three two-way nested domains with grid spacings of 27 km, 9 km, and 3 km were configured in WRF. The largest domain covered the southern part of China and the northern part of Southeast Asia, and the innermost domain D03 included the core area of interest in Southwest China in the upstream of the PRB. The co-occurrence of drought and heat wave at the beginning of the 2009/2010 extreme drought in Southwest China was simulated. Meteorological inputs from the NCEP FNL reanalysis dataset were used to conduct the simulations. WRF configured in Southwest China was validated by comparison of hourly temperature observations in the region. To evaluate the impacts of heat wave on drought and impacts of drought on heat wave via regional land-atmosphere interactions in this co-occurrence event, two suites of numerical experiments were designed. In the first suite of experiments, the total volumetric soil moisture content of each soil layer at each grid was perturbed proportionally, i.e. increase/decrease by 12.5%, 25%, 37.5%, and 50%. The perturbed soil moisture fields and other controlled lateral boundary conditions were used to drive WRF. The land and atmospheric variables and surface fluxes, such as air temperature, humidity, sensible heat and latent heat in these experiments were compared to evaluate the impacts of drought on heat wave. In the second suite of experiments, air temperature of all vertical layers is raised or reduced by 1 oC, 2 oC, ..., 5 oC. Third, we focused on the evaluations of the impacts of changing temperature and humidity on society. Apparent temperature, the human-perceived equivalent temperature, is determined by a number of meteorological factors, such as air temperature, humidity, and wind speed. The 3-hr outputs of GCMs and reanalysis datasets were used to estimate apparent temperature. In our study, three commonly used indices of apparent temperature for hot, normal and cold conditions were combined to consider apparent temperature in all conditions. The three indices included heat index for hot conditions, universal apparent temperature index for normal conditions, and wind-chill equivalent temperature for cold conditions. We also used apparent temperature and air temperature to define thermal discomfort in summer/winter and on extremely hot/cold days. The frequencies of these temperature extremes were also considered. To evaluate the contributions of air temperature, humidity and wind speed to the increases in apparent temperature, we compared the changes in apparent temperature if only one contributing factor was altered while other factors were controlled.

22301916.label: Major findings and research outcome
22301916.value: In this project, research findings of variations, interactions and impacts of droughts, heat waves, and their co-occurrences have been produced. First, the past and future changes in droughts, heat waves, and their co-occurrences have been characterized. Gu et al. (2019) found consistent drying trends in surface soil moisture in the past decades among soil moisture datasets developed by various techniques (e.g. remote sensing, hydrological models, climate models), although datasets based on climate models underestimated the magnitude of drying. Zhang et al. (2018) showed significant drying trends of soil moisture in the Pearl River Basin (PRB) in autumn, which was the combined effects of significant decreases in precipitation and increases in temperature. Continuously drying trends were projected based on outputs of Global Climate Models (GCMs) under the Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) 2.6, RCP4.5, RCP6.0, and RCP8.5 scenarios (Gu et al., 2019). Chen et al. (2018) and Li et al. (2018) indicated that the duration and frequency of heat wave, as well as other temperature extremes were projected to increase under future scenarios. Because of more frequent heat waves and droughts, the occurrence and duration of their concurrent events increased in the past decades and were projected to continue to increase under future climate scenarios. The percentage of area in the PRB affected by the co-occurrence was found to increase from the past to the future. Second, the roles of land-atmosphere interactions in the development of drought-heat wave co-occurrence have been analyzed using numerical experiments in the Weather Research and Forecasting model. Our results showed that in a co-occurrence event, a drought event with low soil moisture can enhance the severity of heat wave through the decrease in latent cooling. On the other hand, heat wave can enhance drought by reducing soil moisture through the increase in latent heat. Third, the impacts of changing temperature and humidity on apparent temperature have been evaluated. Li et al. (2018) found that apparent temperature, as a function of air temperature, humidity and wind speed, increases faster than air temperature under global warming. The increase in air temperature is the major reason for the faster increase in air temperature. The faster increase in apparent temperature than air temperature is more considerable in summer. The increase in thermal discomfort in summer defined by apparent temperature was expected to outpace the increase in winter.

22301916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22301916.value: Large population and high water demand make the Pearl River Basin (PRB) vulnerable to droughts and heat waves under global warming. The project has produced scientific results of variations, interactions, and impacts of drought-heat wave co-occurrence in the basin. These research outcomes help provide scientific reference for water management and public health agencies to enhance adaptation measures for droughts and heat waves under climate change. Therefore, we consider the following directions as potentials for further developing our research: (1) to prompt our research findings to the public to enhance their awareness of climate change impacts on the society; (2) to extend our study to evaluate the impacts of drought-heat wave co-occurrence on agriculture, water supply, and heat-related health issues; and (3) to strengthen our study by further evaluating the roles of urbanization in the co-occurrence of drought and heat wave. The potential directions will continue to improve our understanding of climate change impacts on various aspects of the society, which is important to achieve sustainable development of the basin under the changing climate.

22301916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22301916.value: Droughts and heat waves are two of the costliest natural hazards for the society. These two climatic extremes can be physically correlated because they can be triggered by large-scale abnormal weather systems and can affect each other through land-atmosphere interactions. The large population and high water demand in the Pearl River Basin (PRB) make it vulnerable to both drought and heat waves. The co-occurrence of droughts and heat waves can bring about considerable impacts on regional sustainability. The variations, interactions, and impacts of the drought-heat wave co-occurrence in the PRB have been investigated in this project. Drying trends in soil moisture, more intensive heat waves, and more frequent co-occurrences of droughts and heat waves were detected under the past and future climate scenarios. Our numerical experiments showed that drought and heat wave can mutually enhance each other through their interactions with land surface fluxes in co-occurrence event. Because of the changes in air temperature and humidity, apparent temperature, the human-perceived equivalent temperature, increases faster than air temperature under global warming. The thermal discomfort and frequency of temperature extremes measured by apparent temperature were projected to increase faster than those measured by air temperature.

22500716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22500716.value: 20世紀90年代以來，全球銀行間的國際索賠已經增長了十倍。流動性狀況跨越國界。全球銀行從美國獲得流動資產，並向沒有控制資本流動的經濟體輸入全球流動資產。對於這種經濟體，無論探用甚麼匯率制度，國內利率政策已經不足以來控制當地的信貸條件和經濟週期。為了分析這種現象，我建議建立一個兩國動態隨機一般均衡模型(Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium Model)，模擬全球銀行以及美國和世界其他地區的貨幣政策不對稱。此模型會利用美國和歐洲的資料進行校準，並且進行模擬運行。 這個模型能説明以下問題：(a) 當美國受到實際衝擊，金融動盪和不確定衝擊時，國際銀行是否會使經濟週期和信貸週期更加同步? (b) 我們是否能預期外部融資溢價，銀行杠杆率和跨境資金流的聯動性？ (c) 像蒙代爾—弗萊明模型建議的那樣選擇浮動匯率制度，是否能使一個經濟體免受國際信貸週期的影響？ (d) 資本管制是必要的麼？ 這個項目為國際宏觀經濟學提供了“dilemma-versus-trilemma”爭論的理論基礎。此外，現今世界金融市場高度融合，開放經濟體如何制定貨幣政策和匯率政策，本文將帶來一些啟示。

22500716.label: Realisation of objectives
22500716.value: I fulfill all four project objectives. Below I discuss each of them: I have constructed a two-country DSGE model with a centre economy (US) and an emerging economy. Each economy is populated by representative households, goods producing firms and capital producing firms as in standard New-Kenyesian models. The production part follows closely BGG (1999) and Ueda (2012) and the open economy part follows Gali and Monacelli (2005). In addition, there are investors, banks and entrepreneurs in both economies who borrow and lend subject to financial frictions and an exogenous global banking network. This global banking network part of the model is new. In each economy investors lend to banks and banks lend to entrepreneurs. A crucial assumption is that entrepreneurs in the emerging economy borrow from both local banks and banks in the centre, and so the banks in the centre are called global banks. Moreover, each of the five types of loan contracts above is subject to financial frictions because lenders face a costly state verification problem identical to BGG (1999). I analytically derive the optimal financial contracts when global banks maximize their profits subject to participation contracts of the investors and entrepreneurs. Regarding monetary policy, the centre uses a simple Taylor rule that only cares about its own economy. For the emerging economy, I explored a flexible exchange rate with a calibrated Taylor rule, a Taylor rule with optimally chosen coefficients and a fixed exchange rate regime. The model is simulated using perturbation method around the non-stochastic steady state. I use MATLAB and DYNARE to solve and simulate the model. For welfare comparison, the model is approximated up to the second order. I study the impulse responses to the system when (a) the centre faces a monetary policy shock; and (b) there is a rise in global bank risk (a rise in dispersion of idiosyncratic return of the global banking sector). For both cases, I turn on and off cross-border bank lending. Moreover, I assume that the emerging market uses a calibrated Taylor rule which responds to domestic PPI and output. When cross-border bank lending is turned off, output and investment in the two economies are positively correlated in response to a monetary policy shock, but negatively correlated in response to a rise in global bank risk. When cross-border bank lending is turned on, the business cycles of the two economies are more synchronized. In particular, the correlation of output and investment in the two economies become positive in response to a rise in global bank risk. I study the business cycle effects and welfare implications of the emerging economy when it adopts different monetary-exchange rate policies. I focus on the financial shock. I find that a fixed exchange rate regime is not helpful in absorbing the spillover effect of this external shock. The shock induces a monetary policy easing in the centre, and the emerging economy cuts the policy rate strongly to maintain the peg, which leads to a relatively smooth real exchange rate path. Although an immediate fall in output is prevented and investment falls less, the dynamic adjustment paths of output and inflation are more volatile and persistent. Monetary easing also makes cross-border bank lending less attractive, reducing its amount. The fact that a fixed exchange rate regime generates too much volatility in the real economy and is suboptimal is well-understood from the traditional open-economy models such as Gali and Monacelli (2005). Under the optimal monetary policy, the interest rate falls by much less, keeping the CPI inflation stable and output less volatile. On the other hand, because monetary policy is less accommodative, the initial fall in investment and the price of capital is large. Comparing the responses of the two exchange rate regimes, it is evident that monetary policy carries the burden of maintaining macroeconomic and financial stability. Finally, under either exchange rate regime, there is a similar, sizable fall in global bank lending to the emerging economy. Consistent with the impulse responses, I find that welfare loss associated with a fixed exchange rate regime is always larger than a flexible exchange rate regime with optimal feedback coefficients, regardless of the degree of financial openness. (I have also checked that partial exchange rate targeting does not improve welfare.) Moreover, as financial openness increases, even using the optimal flexible exchange rate rule results in large welfare loss. This is because cross-border lending is an additional channel through which shocks from the centre affect the emerging economy and monetary policy cannot smooth the business cycle and capital flow at the same time. This is the sense in which financial integration weakens the stabilisation effect of independent monetary policy. Indeed, as Rey (2018) point out, a larger degree of financial integration reduces the welfare gap between flexible and fixed exchange rate regimes. This leads one to think about alternative policies such as temporary controls. Following Farhi and Werning (2014), capital control is assumed to be a tax/subsidy on capital outflow in the emerging economy. I show that when capital controls are used along with the optimal simple monetary rule. Following a rise in global bank risk, the tax rate becomes negative, which means that the emerging economy provides a subsidy to cross-border bank lending. This capital account policy effectively limits capital outflow and the increase in the external finance premium, which moderates the amplification effect of the financial accelerator. As the capital control policy partly takes care of financial stability, the nominal interest rate need not fall as much to bolster investment and focuses on maintaining macroeconomic stability. Temporary capital controls improve welfare in a flexible exchange rate regime. This agrees with the observation that capital controls smooth fluctuations in the impulse response functions. Moreover, capital controls improve welfare in a fixed exchange rate regime as well. This policy works from the bank lending channel and is independent of the choice of exchange rate regimes. Finally, the extent to which temporary capital controls improve welfare depends crucially on the financial openness of the emerging economy. The more financially-integrated is an economy the more useful are capital controls. When the emerging market is sufficiently open capital account policies appear to be more useful than an optimal simple rule. To summarise, as degree of financial integration increases, exchange rate flexibility becomes less beneficial whereas capital account control becomes more useful.

22500716.label: Major findings and research outcome
22500716.value: Using a two-country DSGE framework with a global banking network, we have the following major findings: 1. When cross-border bank lending is turned on, the business cycles of the two economies are more synchronized. I show analytically that the rise in business cycle synchronisation comes from the common-lender effect. A rise in cross-sectional risk in global banks increases their default probability and monitoring costs faced by investors in the centre. In equilibrium, investors require higher external finance premium for entrepreneurs in both the centre and the emerging economy. This makes international comovement more positive. 2. I find that a fixed exchange rate regime is not helpful in absorbing the spillover effect of this external shock. Although a flexible exchange rate allows the emerging economy set a nominal interest rate different from that of the centre, it carries the burden of maintaining macroeconomic and financial stability. Although a flexible exchange rate achieves higher welfare than a fixed exchange rate, when the emerging economy is sufficiently financially open, even the optimal flexible exchange rate rule entails large welfare loss. 3. Temporary capital controls improve welfare in a flexible exchange rate regime. Moreover, capital controls improve welfare in a fixed exchange rate regime as well. This policy works from the bank lending channel and is independent of the choice of exchange rate regimes. Finally, the extent to which temporary capital controls improve welfare depends crucially on the financial openness of the emerging economy. The more financially-integrated is an economy the more useful are capital controls. The paper has been presented at a few conferences, and is currently submitted to the Journal of International Money and Finance.

22500716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22500716.value: This project can be further developed in a few dimensions. First, there is a gap in the empirical literature to be filled. Several papers study how monetary conditions in the US spill over to emerging economies. There are relatively few empirical investigations as to how and through what channels financial shocks in the US spill over to emerging economies. Second, in the model part, I abstract from the portfolio choice problem of the borrowers. To be precise, I fix the share of borrowing from global banks and local banks exogenously, as in Ueda (2012). Dedola and Lombardo (2012) study a system with endogenous portfolio choice. This decision may be included in future to allow for richer dynamics of the system. Finally, the actual international banking network is much more sophisticated than the one here. For instance, some recent work shows that the behaviors of within-bank cross-border remittances and of direct bank lending to a foreign firm are very different. A future version should somehow account for this.

22500716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22500716.value: The global financial crisis was characterised by heightened financial risk in the US, which spread to the rest of the world, including emerging economies. This paper constructs a core-periphery model with a global banking network and financial frictions. Due to a common-lender effect, when global banks lend to an emerging economy, heightened financial risk in the centre depresses cross-border lending to the emerging economy and reduces real activities. I explore the welfare gains of using active monetary policy and capital account policy to insulate the emerging economy from external financial risks. First, I find that a peg creates excessive inflation and output volatility, which reduces welfare. Incorporating a global banking network does not overturn this result. Second, temporary capital controls improve welfare when there is cross-border bank lending. Capital controls in the form of a tax/subsidy help stabilise capital flows, moderates the jump in the external finance premium and supports capital investment. Moreover, as capital controls act on the bank-lending channel directly, this policy improves welfare under both fixed and flexible exchange rate regimes. Third, the effectiveness of capital controls increases with the degree of financial integration.

22502016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22502016.value: 隨著各主要城市希望透過舉辦大型運動賽會來提升國際形象和聲譽，運動賽會越來越受到重視 (Gelan, 2003; Smith, 2006)。在觀察到運動賽會為居住城市帶來的變化之後，民眾對於運動賽會的觀感也會隨之改變 (Kaplanidou et al, 2013)。許多研究曾探討運動賽會如何改善本地居民的生活品質，部分研究更指出運動賽會能為主辦城市帶來許多經濟之外的無形效益，例如，凝聚社區意識、增加國家及市民榮譽感、促進文化及身份認同感、提升運動參與度，和改善居住與生活品質，等等 (e.g., Crombie, 2011; Freeman, 2012; Garcia, 2004)。但是，由於直接證據取得困難，在缺乏充分有效的實證下，運動賽會對居民的生活品質所帶來的影響容易被忽視或過分強調。 2015年，渣打香港馬拉松的参加人數上升至73,000人，成為香港最大型的參與型運動賽會。渣打香港馬拉松亦連續11年獲得香港體育委員會轄下大型體育活動事務委員會頒授「M」品牌賽事資格，以肯定此賽會的獨特地位和其對本地居民生活的深遠影響。香港政府每年投入可觀的資源協助舉辦大型賽會，而這些資源投入能否營造一個有利的環境，為香港市民帶來正面且可持續的影響，便成為一個值得深入探討的重要課題。 ¬本研究計畫希望藉由了解本地居民對運動賽會的認知及觀感的變化，進而探討這些認知上的變化對居民生活品質及參與運動之動機帶來的影響。透過長期的追蹤，研究將深入探討渣打香港馬拉松在提倡體育文化和改善本地社區的生活品質上的效果，亦會建構並驗證一個由八個可變量組成的理論模型。透過大量的文獻分析和試驗研究，本研究將建構一個研究量表並檢測其信效度，以做為之後資料蒐集的工具。在為期兩年的研究中，一共會進行八次資料蒐集，分別是每年賽會舉行的前三個月、進行期間和舉行後(三個月及六個月)。本研究採用追蹤性研究法，並蒐集不同人口族群的樣本 (i.e. 參與者、觀眾、非參與者)。此一設計對於了解賽會對不同族群的影響和可變量之間的交互作用，有著莫大的幫助。研究結果將會與鄰近地區的同類型研究作比較，並檢驗在研究中提出的理論模型的效度和概化效果(generalizability) 。因此，研究結果預期會在知識層面上，對重複性大型體育賽事的社會影響作出重大貢獻。

22502016.label: Realisation of objectives
22502016.value: To achieve the objectives of the project, the primary method of data collection was in-person intercept surveys (i.e., questionnaire). The questionnaire was developed through undertaking an extensive literature review, double translated into Chinese and reviewed by three experts. One pilot study was conducted from January 3rd to 7th 2017, to further modify the questionnaire. Targeted samples of this study were local event participants, spectators and residents (non-participants). Through a comparison of these groups (different involvement levels), indirect evidence would be obtained to assess the changes in perceived impacts of and the attitude towards SCHKM over time. A total of five independent data collections were conducted in pre-selected time periods using the following procedures: (1) During the first and fourth data collections (during the 2017 and 2018 event), more than 30 student helpers were recruited and trained, and on the day of the event they randomly intercept participants, spectators as well as non-participants to complete a questionnaire onsite in multiple points along the marathon's route, including the public viewing area at the Victoria Park, as well as the prize awarding area and the meeting point in the Causeway Bay Sports Ground. They were instructed to explain the purpose of this study and then asked people to voluntarily participate in this study. (2) For the second, third and fifth data collections (May, October, 2017 and April, 2018), groups of trained student helpers administered the questionnaires at selected high traffic public areas (e.g., shopping centers, popular squares, business districts, community recreation and sport centers) for about two weeks for each data collection period. Site selections were designed to approximate a representative sample of the population. During the first data collection the team collected 1757 questionnaires overall, including 332 residents, 316 spectators and 1109 participants. The second collection compiled 971 questionnaires, including 371 residents, 304 spectators and 306 participants. The third data collection, there were a total of 1009 questionnaires collected, including 403 residents, 301 spectators and 305 participants. The fourth data collection we obtained 1239 questionnaires, including 184 residents, 325 spectators and 730 participants. In the last data collection, the helpers amassed 1009 questionnaires, including 374 residents, 348 spectators and 287 participants. As shown in the results, one of the biggest issues in data collection was to meet the target sample size for each subgroup. For the first and fourth data collection (during event), participants were much more reachable than residents and spectators, while for the remaining collection period, residents were easier to collect. The research team had to extend the data collection period and spend extra money for student helpers in order to collect enough samples for data analysis. At the end of each collection day, the numbers of questionnaires collected were recorded. This allowed the collection plan for the following day to be adjusted so that the targeted sample size for three subgroups could be achieved. The first objective in the research proposal is related to how residents’ perceptions of the event’s social impact influence their attitude and support toward the event, and the research team was able to realize this objective. Through analysis of the collected data, the current study was able demonstrated residents’ perceptions of both the positive and negative impacts from the event indeed contributed to their support to SCHKM conjointly. Specifically, findings suggest that residents’ perceptions of benefits of the event have positive effects on their support to the event while the perceived costs of such event have negative effects on their ultimate support, and these relations were identified in both near- and distant-past sample. In addition, as evidenced by the magnitudes of the relationships between perceived impacts of and support towards hosting the event, residents seem to place more emphasis on the benefits of an event than on negative aspects when forming their support toward the event. Secondly, the objective of examining how residents’ perceptions of quality of life (QOL) might influence by their perceived impact of the event was also realized. After data analysis, it was able to confirm that the perceived benefits derived from the hosting of a sport event was positively associated with residents' overall evaluations of life quality across time. Furthermore, it was also confirmed that the perceived negative impact influenced the perceived QOL in a negative manner within the near-past group. However, for the distant-past sample, this study failed to identify a significant relationship between residents’ perception of costs and their QOL assessment. Additionally, the objective of investigating how QOL influence residents’ event support was also realized, as the finding was able to identify the indirect effect of perceived benefits through QOL on residents' support were significant for both two groups (near- and distant-past). For the third objective, residents’ intention to participate in sport/physical activities were found positively related to their attitudes toward the SCHKM. However, a longitudinal fluctuation was not significant. A manuscript focus on the event’s impact on sport participation is under preparation. The objective is well realized by the team. The last main objectives of this research involve the issue of how residents’ perceived event social impacts are influenced by the factors of community concern and level of attachment to the event. These objectives were realized as well. It was found that there were significant temporal differences regarding the strength of the relationships between residents’ community concerns and their perceptions for both benefits and costs of hosting the event between two samples. In particular, the relationships were shown to be stronger in the near-past sample than the distant-past sample, suggesting diminishing effects of community concerns on the perceptions of event impacts as time goes by. At the same time, findings also indicated that there was a significant increase, instead of a decrease, in the magnitude of the relationship between event attachment and perceived benefits of the event in the distant-past group compared to the near-past group. Similarly, the association between event attachment and perceived costs of hosting the event was also stronger in the distant-past group than in the near-past group. However, this path difference was trivial and non-significant, thus not able to derive any meaningful interpretation. In summary, findings from this study revealed longitudinal changes in the impact perceptions of the SCHKM, as residents' perceptions did fluctuate at different times of a year. In February, during the event, residents demonstrated the highest concerns on the two negative social impact dimensions (social problems, and traffic congestion and pollution) while demonstrating lower positive social impact perceptions for economic and recognition dimension. Despite the aggravated negative perceptions on the day of the event, it is noticeable that overall residents' perceptions of negative social impacts were relatively low, which suggest residents did not feel burdened by the cost the community incurred for hosting the SCHKM.
