23607616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23607616.value: Metaphysics addresses the question of what things there are and what those things are like. Part of this question concerns whether there are any abstract objects, such as properties, numbers or sets. Property anti-realists hold that there are no properties, while property realists hold that there are properties. More generally, nominalists hold that there are no abstract objects, while realists about abstracta (or realists, for short) hold that there are abstract objects. Property anti-realists, and nominalists more generally, do not hold the crazy view that the White House is not white, or that there aren’t eight planets in the solar system. Instead they hold that, while the White house is white and there are eight planets in the solar system, there is no additional entity that is the property being red or the number eight. This research project will provide a new defence of property anti-realism and will make progress towards defending the more general thesis of nominalism by developing a new response to the most powerful argument for realism about abstracta, which is the Quine-Putnam indispensability argument. According to the indispensability argument, just as we should believe in the theoretical entities of science, such as electrons, because our best overall theory entails there are electrons, we should believe that there are abstracta because our best overall theory entails that there are abstracta. This project will respond to this argument by first arguing that the argument needs to be reformulated in a way that makes it easier for nominalists to respond to the argument without contradicting themselves. The project will then argue that a number of phenomena that realists have claimed we need abstracta to account for can be accounted for just as well (or even better) without abstracta. Examples of such phenomena include counterfactuals, modal comparatives, intrinsicality, resemblance, numeric quantification and natural language semantics. From this, together with parsimony considerations, the project will conclude that we should hold that there are no properties, roughly because (assuming there are theories) the best theory (relative to how we are evidence-wise) is not one that entails that there are properties, but is instead one that entails there are no properties. The project will also provide reason to think that the kind of response given in the project can be extended to show that we should endorse the more general claim that there are no abstracta.

23607616.label: Realisation of objectives
23607616.value: Broadly construed, the project of this completion report was on the nature of properties and whether there are any such entities as properties. The main aim of the project was to contribute to the defence of the nominalist (or anti-realist) claim that there are no such entities. The components of the project as originally planned in the grant proposal were: (I) Foundational Issues (II) Nominalism and Analysis (III) Nominalism and Semantics (IV) Resemblance and Nominalism As the project evolved over time, the focus of the project underwent three changes. First, in light of advice from the referees of the project that the original planned project was too ambitious, and in light of the fact that I received less teaching relief than applied for in the grant application, I requested (and received) a revision of the objectives of the project that eliminated objectives 3 and 7. Second, as noted in the mid-term report, component III of the project (associated with objective 4) turned out to be much more complicated and challenging than originally anticipated. In light of this, I decided to cut component IV of the project (and its associated objective 5) and to focus on the other three components (and their associated objectives). Finally, the main focus of component I shifted somewhat so that, instead of focussing on the issue of how to precisely state theories of properties and how to make sense of the notion of a total theory (and do the philosophical work total theories are meant to do), component I focussed on the topic of what the individuation conditions of properties (and their 0-place counterparts, states of affairs) are. The focus on this topic was prompted by the need to justify an argument made in component III of the project against one type of realist theory about properties, which might be called metaphysical structuralism. (Roughly, according to metaphysical structuralism, instantiation is held to be a fundamental multigrade fundamental relation and every property is analysed in terms of instantiation and other broadly logical notions.) In addition to this application of the topic of the individuation conditions of properties, how properties are individuated is important in itself and is important with regard to a number of other topics this project concerns, such as the topic of how to formulate the best realist theories of properties and what is required for a theory to be ideologically parsimonious. Component III (which despite its label was the first component to be worked on), resulted in the completion of the lengthy paper `How to do semantics without semantic values’ (approximately 20 000 words). This paper is currently under the review process. (Note that the time taken from first submission to acceptance at leading philosophy journals is often multiple years due to leading journals commonly having an acceptance rate of around 5% and having lengthy turn around rates.) Component I of the project focussed on the nature of properties (or in other words, the question of what properties would be like if there were such entities). As noted above, the research project evolved so that this component focussed on the question of what the individuation conditions of properties and states of affairs are. I address this question by proposing and defending a novel theory of the individuation conditions which I call the object aboutness theory. Work on this topic faced less difficulties and challenges than the work done on component III and resulted in the completion of the following papers: 1. ‘Intrinsicality and the classification of uninstantiable properties’, published in Philosophical Studies 2. ‘Plate’s account of intrinsicality’, forthcoming in Inquiry 3. ‘Object aboutness’, forthcoming in Inquiry 4. ‘The object aboutness theory and attributive aboutness’, under review 5.‘Causation and fact granularity’, under review 6. ‘The dual-detector argument’, under review Papers 1-3 discuss the notions of intrinsicality and aboutness, which play a crucial role in the object aboutness theory. Paper 4 defends the object aboutness theory from an objection from aboutness, while papers 5 and 6 defend the object aboutness theory (and the more famous modal theory of properties and states of affairs) from objections from causation. These papers contributed to objectives 1 and 6. The final component of the project that I worked on was component III. The work on this component resulted in the completion of the lengthy paper `Counterfactuals and the argument for possible worlds from theoretical virtues’ (approximately 20 000 words). (This paper is currently waiting on final feedback before being put under review for publication.) The paper argues that nominalists (or anti-realists) about properties can give an account of counterfactuals that is at least as good as the account given by realists about properties, which undermines one of the most important considerations in favour of realism. The kind of argument used in this paper can be used to argue that anti-realists can also give accounts of the other notions---such as modal comparatives and duplication---that are at least as good as the accounts realists can give, which further undermines considerations in favour of realism. In addition to completing the above paper, I gave a number of talks at conferences and departmental seminars on my work in this component, including the following talks: 1. ‘Against Linguistic Ersatzism’. Presented at: Issues on the (Im)possible Conference, Institute of Philosophy of the Slovak Academy of Sciences, May 2019 2. ‘Metaphysical Structuralism’. Presented at: Modality in Naturalistic-Structuralist Ontologies Conference, Lingnan University, March 2019 3. ‘Property Pythagoreanism’. Presented at: CCPEA 2018, National Chengchi University, August 2018 4. ‘Nominalism and Ideological Parsimony’. Presented at: Departmental Seminar, University of Gothenburg, May 2018; and at Departmental Seminar, Academy of the Sciences of the Czeck Republic, May 2018 5. ‘Nominalism and the Indispensability Argument’. Presented at: Departmental Seminar, University of Edinburgh, March 2018; and at The Fourth Taiwan Metaphysics Colloquium, National Taiwan University, January 2020 6. ‘Heavy duty realism’. Presented at: Australasian Association of Philosophy Conference, University of Adelaide, July 2017; (Only the talks at conferences are listed in part C of this completion report.) Talks 2, 3 and 6 are on the same topic: each attacks metaphysical structuralism (which is a realist theory of properties). Talk 1 raises a problem for linguistic ersatzism (and indirectly raises a problem for certain realist theories of properties). Talks 4 and 5 are closely related to the above described paper ‘Counterfactuals and the argument for possible worlds from theoretical virtue’, though they focus on notions other than counterfactuals. Talk 4 focuses on the claim that anti-realists about properties can give just as good an account of modal comparatives as realists, while talk 5 does the same for the notion of `finitely many’ and defends anti-realism about abstracta in general rather than just anti-realism about properties. The above paper and these talks contributed to satisfying objectives 2 and 6 of the project. As a result of the above work on components I-III of the project, all the (approved revised) objectives of the project were accomplished apart from objective 5. As discussed above, objective 5 (which was associated with the cut component IV of the project) was cut due to the focus put on the challenging component III associated with objective 4.

23607616.label: Major findings and research outcome
23607616.value: The major results of this project were: i) The formulation and defence of a novel account of the individuation conditions of properties. The completed papers that contributed to this are papers 1-6 as listed in part C. ii) An argument that any Montagovian semantic theory can be transformed into a Davidsonian theory that is at least as good as the original Montagovian theory (and can easily account of unrestricted quantification). The completed paper 8 as listed in Part C contributed to this result. iii) An argument that anti-realist theories of properties can provide an account of counterfactuals and other notions, such as modal comparatives, duplication and finitehood, that is at least as good as the best accounts of these notions provided by realist theories of properties (and other abstracta). The completed paper 7 as listed in Part C contributed to this result, as did the relevant talks described in Part B section 6.1.

23607616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23607616.value: Potential further projects arising from the current project include: Project A: Further developing my defence of property anti-realism and extending it to a defence of anti-realism regarding all abstract objects. Project B: Providing a systematic account of resemblance and arguing that anti-realists about abstracta can give as good a version of this account as realists can. Project C: Further develop my defence of the Davidsonian approach to semantics by extending it to account for presuppositions, respond to arguments from Scott Soames and Jeff Speaks against the Davidsonian program, and show that good Davidsonian theories can be relieved of their commitment to abstracta. Project D: Extend and make comprehensive my defence of the object aboutness theory of the individuation conditions of properties and states of affairs, and formulate and defend its nominalist-friendly counterpart. This would include responding to other arguments against the object aboutness theory not considered in this project, such as arguments that appeal to grounding and arguments that appeal to propositional attitudes, and evaluating positive arguments against rival theories. I have submitted a GRF grant proposal earlier this year on roughly project B. I also plan over the next 5-10 years to pursue the other three projects.

23607616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23607616.value: This research project makes three important contributions to one of the central perennial questions in philosophy: namely, the question of whether properties (and other abstract objects) exist and, if they do, what are they like? First, the project defends a novel account of the individuation conditions of properties and, more neutrally, the ``granularity of reality’’. According to the proposed theory, for example, if being F and being G is a matter of how one is, as opposed to how one is related to other things and how other things are, then: to be F is to be G if and only if, necessarily, something is an F if and only if it is a G. Secondly, the project provides a novel defence of anti-realism about properties from the objection that realists can offer better accounts of counterfactuals and other notions than anti-realists can. Finally, the project argues that Davidsonian semantic theories of natural language (which are more friendly to anti-realism about properties than orthodox semantic theories) can be developed so that that they are at least as good as any other semantic theory of natural language.

24100716.label: Project Objectives
24100716.value: To characterize the complete genomes of novel primate papillomaviruses from our biobanked monkey and human specimens to enrich the sequence data bank for evolution studies. We hypothesize that a repertoire of human and non-human primate papillomavirus genomes will provide the foundation to explore papillomavirus evolutionary mechanisms and understand the genetic basis driving viral carcinogenicity. We have previously detected several novel primate papillomaviruses with a short fragment sequenced from our large scale of monkey and human sample cohorts. We will characterize their complete genomes using high-throughput metagenomic analysis to establish a comprehensive sequence database of monkey and human papillomaviruses. Multiple evolutionary algorithms will be applied to determine the phylogenetic positions and relationships. To elucidate the evolutionary dynamics driving primate papillomavirus divergence to understand the genetic basis underlying the mechanisms of papillomaviruses carcinogenicity. We hypothesize that natural selection has resulted in the emergence of genetically related cancer-causing papillomaviruses. Utilizing the available full resource of primate papillomavirus complete genome sequences together with the additional genomes obtained in Objective 1, we will test and verify the evolutionary assumptions such as early primate papillomavirus radiation, niche adaptation, virus-host codivergence, natural selection and genetic variability on papillomavirus genus-species-type-variant levels. We have a large set of sequence database containing all of oncogenic human papillomavirus variant genomes and will use analytic tools of evolution and systems biology to characterize the diversifying selection and genetic metrics across the full 8,000bp genomes. To identify and compare the abilities of E6 proteins encoded by phylogenetically related genital monkey and human papillomaviruses for host p53 protein degradation to evaluate the evolutionary interaction of viral oncogenic function with the host proteome. We hypothesize that primate papillomavirus carcinogenicity was the success of niche adaptation amongst their common ancestors necessary for viruses to complete their life cycle. The alpha-12 species (MfPV3 and relatives) and alpha-9 species (HPV16 and relatives) contain genital monkey and human papillomavirus types inducing cervical neoplasia; both groups are phylogenetically related and share a common viral ancestor before host speciation. We will clone and express several E6 proteins encoded by types from these two species groups to evaluate their interactions with different host p53 proteins in different cell lines using in-vitro experiments, the best characterized E6 oncogenic function to degrade tumor-suppressor gene p53.

24100716.label: Realisation of objectives
24100716.value: Objective 1: Through the completion of this project, we have recruited 1426 healthy Hong Kong residents for collection of oral rinse samples, and conducted genotyping for the whole spectrum of alpha-, beta-, and gamma-HPVs. Overall, the prevalence of oral HPV infection was 15.5%, with beta-HPVs as the most common oral infection (11.9%). Epidemiological analysis indicated that men had higher prevalence of oral HPV infection than female. Smoking, drinking, oral sex, and more sexual partners were associated with alpha-HPV. Teeth brushing before sleep was protective for beta/gamma-HPVs. The epidemiologic factors associated with oral infection with alpha-HPVs are different from those of beta/gamma-HPVs, suggesting different modes of acquisition and persistence. This work has been published in Journal of Infectious Disease in 2018 (IF=6.273): • Wong MCS, Vlantis AC, Liang M, Wong PY, Ho WCS, Boon SS, Sze RKH, Leung C, Chan PKS, Chen Z. Prevalence and Epidemiologic Profile of Oral Infection with Alpha, Beta, and Gamma Papillomaviruses in an Asian Chinese Population. J Infect Dis. 2018;218(3):388-97. doi: 10.1093/infdis/jiy160. Between August and December 2016, paired swab samples from oral, perianal and genital (vaginal sites from female macaques, and penial sites from male macaques) sites of 117 noncaptive wild rhesus macaques, including 84 females and 33 males, were collected from Kam Shan Country Park, Hong Kong, China. Using two next-generation sequencing (NGS) amplicon assays developed by our own research group, we detected 75.2% (88/117) macaque animals were positive for PV DNA, mostly common from genital swabs, followed by oral and perianal sites. All putative macaque PV types phylogenetically clustered into the genera Alpha-, Beta-, and Gammapapillomavirus, with a strong phylogeny-tropism association as observed in human papillomaviruses. The findings identifying evolutionary and biological relatedness between human and nonhuman primate PVs lay a genetic foundation for research on parasite-host interactions and carcinogenic outcomes, which will prove useful in further study of viral pathogenesis and host specificity. This work has been published in Frontiers in Microbiology in 2019 (IF=4.235): • Chen Z, Long T, Wong PY, Ho WCS, Burk RD, Chan PKS. Non-human Primate Papillomaviruses Share Similar Evolutionary Histories and Niche Adaptation as the Human Counterparts. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2019;10(2093):2093. doi: 10.3389/fmicb.2019.02093. A total of 9 and 65 potential novel human and monkey PV types were identified in our achieved sample cohorts; among them, one HPV (HPVTG550) and six macaque PVs (MfPV2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7) have been characterized for the complete genome. Particularly, we identified three non-human primate Gamma-PV types for the first time. These genomes have been shared with research community via GenBank/NCBI and published in Genome Announc and Microbiol Resour Announc in 2017 and 2018, respectively: • Chen Z, Wong MCS, Wong PY, Ho WCS, Liang M, Yeung ACM, Chan PKS. Microbiol Resour Announc 2018;7(22) doi: 10.1128/MRA.01414-18 Objective 2: In collaboration with Prof. Paul Chan (Department of Microbiology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong), Prof. Robert Burk (Department of Pediatrics, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, USA), Dr. Lisa Mirabello (NCI/NIH, USA) and several other laboratories worldwide, we sequenced >400 complete genomes of high-risk HPV type variants and utilized available full resource of papillomavirus partial and complete genome sequences (>5000). The genomic diversity and evolutionary dynamics of primate papillomaviruses and high-risk HPV types were studied. Our findings revealed an ancient and complex evolutionary history of Papillomaviruses in general and high-risk HPV types in specific. The evolution of oncogenic HPVs follows a methodical pathway of first adapting to a specific host ecological niche, followed by co-divergence in archaic human ancestors and subsequent natural selection within specific human genetic backgrounds. Objective 3: We aligned the amino acid sequences of macaque and human p53 genes and identified three mutations locating at the binding surface of p53-E6/E6AP complex potentially discriminating the species-specific barrier. We constructed 14 mutated human and macaque p53 expression plasmids containing one, two or three changes at aa site 104, 129 or 206 and tested in vitro the ability of E6 target for degradation. We found when human p53 was simultaneously mutated at both Q104H and A129D, MfPV3 E6, but not HPV16 E6, can specifically target human p53 for degradation, and vice versa. Results indicate that p53 aa site 129 is critical for forming the p53-E6/E6AP complex and potentially serve species-specific targets for gene therapy and drug development. Meanwhile, the E6 proteins encoded by the majority of macaque PV types within the species Alpha-12 (MfPV3-7, MfPV9-10, MmPV1, and PhPV1) were able to significantly degrade host p53. In contrast, expression of E6 from MfPV8/11 and MmPV2/3/6 (Alpha-PVs), MfPV2 (Beta-PV) and MmPV4/5/7 (Gamma-PVs) did not reduce p53 levels. Alignment of NHP PV E6 ORFs found two amino acid sites potentially correlated with the biochemical ability to degrade p53 that are under current investigation. The data indicate that human and macaque PVs able to degrade host p53 molecules may share a most recent common ancestor that contained the determinants associated with this phenotype. It suggests an important role of niche adaptation shaping similar tissue tropism and pathogenic properties between high-risk human and macaque PVs, and lays a foundation for determining the origin of carcinogenicity of oncogenic HPV types and species. 24100716.label: Major findings and research outcome
24100716.value: This funded project has directly generated seven peer-reviewed publications in international journals (accumulated impact factors of 24.680) and three presentations in international conferences. One manuscript is actively under preparation. This project also provided the training opportunities for one PhD and one MPhil postgraduate students, as well as the internship/summer attachment for seven undergraduate students. In addition, the Principal Investigator has established collaborations with local and oversea scientists and contributed key roles in three publications. The research group has developed and optimized two Next-Gen sequencing PV genotyping assays to screen multiple sample cohorts isolated from human and macaque, and revealed high genomic diversity and strong phylogeny-tropism of primate papillomavirus infections. A total of 9 and 65 potential novel human and macaque PV types were identified, including one HPV (HPVTG550) and six macaque PVs (MfPV2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7) being characterized for the complete genome. Utilizing the available full resource of primate papillomavirus complete genome sequences together with the additional sequences generated by our own research group, we have proposed the taxonomy classification on papillomavirus genus-species-type-variant levels. We found several amino acid changes under positive selection in HPV16 and HPV58 genomes that might be associated with higher cervical cancer risk. The finding will provide foundations for the design of screening assays and selection of types for vaccine. Critically, we observed an ancient and complex evolutionary history of Papillomaviruses in general and high-risk HPV types in specific. The evolution of oncogenic HPVs follows a methodical pathway of first adapting to a specific host ecological niche, followed by co-divergence in archaic human ancestors and subsequent natural selection within specific human genetic backgrounds. Understanding the evolution of papillomaviruses should provide important biological insights and suggest mechanisms underlying HPV-induced cervical cancer, since niche adaptation rather than oncogenicity drives viral fitness. Using in-vitro cell models, we have established phenotype-genotype co-evolution of primate PV carcinogenicity, and identified one key amino acid in host p53 tumor suppressor gene that is associated with p53-E6/E6AP interaction and degradation. The data indicate that human and macaque PVs able to degrade host p53 molecules may share a most recent common ancestor that contained the determinants associated with this phenotype, which lays a foundation for determining the origin of carcinogenicity of oncogenic HPV types and species. The findings in this funded project largely enrich our knowledge on primate papillomavirus genetic heterogeneity, phylogeny and carcinogenicity.

24100716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24100716.value: Although prophylactic vaccines for the major oncogenic HPV types causing cervical cancer are available, they are underutilized and do not have therapeutic effects for women with cervical HPV and related abnormalities. Hence, it becomes critical to translate the findings from basic research to cervical screening, viral diagnosis and next generation vaccine development. We will devote our efforts in these areas in the near future. Our ultimate gold is to fill in knowledge gaps on the virus-host interactions that underlie oncogenic mechanisms in HPV-associated cervical cancer for formulating more effective preventative and interventional strategies to control this fatal cancer.

24100716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24100716.value: Although epidemiologic studies have demonstrated that persistent infection of high-risk HPVs is the main cause of cervical cancer, understanding the exact genetic basis of papillomavirus oncogenicity is highly challenging and not well known. The findings in this funded project elucidate the high genomic diversity of papillomaviruses, and the complex evolutionary relationship at genetic and functional levels between primate papillomaviruses (including HPVs) and their hosts, which lays a foundation for determining the origin of HPV carcinogenicity. The findings also have clinical implications for long-term use of papillomavirus DNA screening, premalignant diagnosis and intervention, and next generation vaccine development. Ultimately, this project advances our knowledge on HPV-causing cervical cancer which account for ~15% of human cancers.

24103516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24103516.value: Clostridium difficile is an anaerobic, gram-positive, sporulating bacterium that can give rise to a spectrum of gastrointestinal presentations, including diarrhoea, pseudomembraneous colitis and toxic megacolon. It is a main cause of hospital-associated infections with about 3 million cases per year worldwide, with reported mortality rates up to 30%. The incidence is increasing in many developed countries with the common hyper-virulent ribotype 027 causing major outbreaks and deaths in North America and Europe. Nevertheless, the disease epidemiology is different in Asia. The hyper-virulent ribotype 027 was only found sporadically; rather, the ribotype 002 was common in Asia. Our recent work showed that the ribotype 002 was the most common ribotype in Hong Kong (22.8%), and was associated with increased mortality compared to other ribotypes (47.6% versus 12.7%). Despite its importance in this locality, there is a paucity of data regarding the virulence mechanism of this ribotype. This project aims to investigate the virulence mechanisms of C. difficile ribotype 002, by analysing its growth, cytotoxicity, and metabolite production in vitro and in vivo. We also aim to compare these virulence mechanisms with other common ribotypes in Asia, and correlate these with important clinical outcomes. Our data suggested that the ribotype 002 might grow at a faster rate and produce more cytotoxin than other ribotypes. Furthermore, addition of the C. difficile ribotype 002 supernatant could reduce colonic cell viability by 47.8% at 24 hours. These findings may help to explain the higher mortality associated with this ribotype. It is anticipated that findings from this study will elucidate the virulence mechanisms of C. difficile, especially on the ribotype 002 which is common and important in this locality. It will also help pinpoint targets for therapeutic development and identify correlates of clinical outcomes. The data will be useful for the gastroenterologists, microbiologist, infectious diseases physicians and public health specialists in the Asia-Pacific region. 難辨梭狀芽孢桿菌﹝難辨梭菌﹞感染是常見的醫院內道感染，症狀包括發燒、腹痛及腹瀉等。其中超毒核糖型 027 在外國曾經引起嚴重的爆發，引致多宗的死亡個案。儘管在亞洲難辨梭菌核糖型 027 並不常見，但其他核糖型如 002 等卻屢見不鮮，而我們對這些核糖型的難辨梭菌的致病機制實在認識不多。這個研究計劃旨在透過研究核糖型 002 難辨梭菌的生長、細胞毒性、生理及病理特性，增加我們對這細菌的認識，為將來對抗及預防難辨梭菌作好準備，為香港的公共衞生作好把關。

24103516.label: Realisation of objectives
24103516.value: Clostridium difficile is an anaerobic, gram-positive, sporulating bacterium that can give rise to a spectrum of gastrointestinal presentations, including diarrhoea, pseudo-membraneous colitis and toxic megacolon. It is a main cause of hospital-associated infections. Serious infections and fatalities have been associated with the hyper-virulent ribotype 027 (BI/NAP1) strain in the West; nevertheless, this ribotype only occurs sporadically in Asia. Notably, the ribotype 002 was found to be the most common and associated with high mortality in Hong Kong. Despite its importance, the virulence mechanisms of this ribotype were poorly characterized. The bacteriological factors including its growth cycle, toxins and metabolites production remain understudied. This project aims (1) to investigate the in vitro virulence mechanisms of the C. difficile ribotype 002, (2) to evaluate the phenotypes of C. difficile ribotype 002 in mouse models, (3) to correlate the levels of the toxins with the clinical phenotypes, and (4) to build a platform for translational research into gastrointestinal infections. We have realized all the objectives of this study, and published our results in two international journals (Kong KY et al, Emerg Microb Infect 2020) (Ho J et al, Emerg Infect Dis 2017). We have characterized the detailed biological characteristics associated with virulence in Clostridioides difficile ribotype 002 in Hong Kong. A total of 53 different ribotypes of C. difficile were collected and we have performed experiments on common ribotypes, including 012, 014, 027, 046 and 087 ribotypes. Bacterial cultures were first inoculated in BHI medium and grown for 16 hours, and the grown cultures were resuspended with fresh media to adjust to optical density 600nm. Briefly, culture broth was collected at designated time points and spread onto BHI agars for enumeration of bacterial counts in colony-forming units (CFUs) after 24 hours incubation anaerobically. Cell cytotoxicity and neutralization assay was used to check for the presence of bacterial toxin, and the level of toxin production from different bacterial strains were measured by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Sporulation frequencies were calculated as CFUs of heated samples divided by those of unheated samples plated on BHI agars with 0.1% sodium taurocholate. Germination was used to assess the ability of spores to outgrow in the absence of taurocholate, and were calculated as CFUs of heated samples on agars without sodium taurocholate divided by those on agars with sodium taurocholate. A C57BL/6 mouse infection model was built to study the ribotype virulence in vivo. We studied the in vitro dynamics of bacterial growth in culture. Despite a similar growth at the lag phase at 4 hours, higher CFUs were reached for C. difficile ribotype 002 at stationary phase. The average generation time for ribotype 002 was 100.09 minutes, which was much shorter than other common ribotypes of 123.22 minutes. Remarkably, ribotype 002 had significantly higher vegetative cell numbers than other common ribotypes at 20 hours (4.13×108 CFU/ml versus 1.85×108 CFU/ml, p < 0.05). All strains tested in this study had the presence of pathogenic toxin B, indicated by the rounding of epithelial cells upon addition of the growth supernatants, and lack of cell rounding in the presence of anti-toxin. Quantitative analyses showed that all C. difficile non-027 ribotypes produced low levels of toxins at 48 hours; nevertheless, at 72 hours, ribotype 002 produced significantly higher levels of toxin A (179.7ng/ml versus 80.07ng/ml, p < 0.05) and toxin B (108.5ng/ml versus 40.44ng/ml, p < 0.05) when compared to other common ribotypes. For sporulation, it increased during the time from 48 to 120 hours, especially with ribotypes 002 and 027, which showed significantly higher sporulation rates than other common ribotypes at 72 hours (75.05% versus 40.57%, p < 0.01). The sporulation rates of other ribotypes increased at 96 and 120 hours, with no significant differences between the groups at these later time points. For the germination rates of different C. difficile ribotypes, we observed increased rate of ribotype 002 compared to other ribotypes at 24 hours (3.472% versus 0.113%, p < 0.0001) and 48 hours (1.245% versus 0.111%, p < 0.01). This indicates that a higher proportion of spores in ribotype 002 can germinate spontaneously than other common ribotypes. The germination frequencies dropped in the subsequent time points. C57BL/6 mice were used to establish the C. difficile oral gavage infection model. All groups experienced body weight drop, with a mean weight loss of 2.9% on Day 1 and 5.8% on Day 2 after oral gavage of C. difficile. At Day 2, ribotype 087 experienced the most significant body weight drop of 12.32%, followed by ribotype 002 with 6.32% weight loss and was statistically significant when compared to other common ribotypes (6.32% versus 1.97%, p < 0.001). The remaining three groups did not show significant differences in weight from Day 0 to Day 2. On Day 2, three out of eight mice gavaged with ribotype 027 (37.5%) and two out of seven mice gavaged with ribotype 087 (28.6%) were found to be dead. Although all mice survived in other groups, one mouse in ribotype 002 showed signs of distress, as indicated by a hunched posture, sluggish movement, and rough hair coat. No obvious appearances or behavioral abnormalities were observed in mice from other groups. The intestinal inflammation and injury in the colon of the mice as induced by C. difficile were graded. Notably, ribotype 002 had significantly higher scores than other common ribotypes (4.296 versus 2.324, p < 0.001) and BHI control (4.296 versus 0.9511, p < 0.0001), indicating severe inflammation and tissue injury in the colon. There was no statistical difference in the histology score of ribotype 002, 027 and 087. Representative histological sections of the colon revealed significant submucosal edema, neutrophilic infiltration and epithelial cell damage with ribotypes 002, 027 and 087. However, the level of toxins did not associate significantly with the in vivo clinical phenotype or the severity of histological damages. In this study, we sought to investigate further the bacteriological characteristics of ribotype 002. Ribotype 002 showed extended stationary phase, heightened sporulation and germination frequencies, and higher toxin production. It was suggested that the rate of sporulation was associated with the severity of CDI outbreak. C. difficile with enhanced sporulation capacity was also suggested to be associated with greater spread or persistence in hospital settings. Here, we demonstrated similar pattern of earlier onset and higher sporulation frequencies for both ribotypes 002 and 027. This may indicate that prevalence of ribotype 002 in Hong Kong is related to its virulence in terms of sporulation. Our study showed that ribotype 002 had a better ability to germinate when compared to all other ribotypes, including ribotype 027. The virulence characteristics of ribotype 002 may relate to a high prevalence and higher mortality of ribotype 002 in Hong Kong. Although clinical features on mice gavaged with C. difficile ribotype 002 were not as severe as those with hypervirulent ribotype 027 and high-toxin-producer standard strain VPI 10463, obvious differences existed in terms of body weight lost and higher histology scores when compared to other common ribotypes. This demonstrated that ribotype 002 had a higher ability to cause disease with clinical complications on animals than other common ribotypes. Our study demonstrated the fitness and a potentially important strain from transmission and severity that deserve further attention and surveillance.

24103516.label: Major findings and research outcome
24103516.value: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a common cause of nosocomial diarrhea and can sometimes lead to pseudo-membranous colitis and toxic megacolon. We previously reported that the PCR ribotype 002 was a common C. difficile ribotype in Hong Kong that was associated with increased mortality. In this study, we assessed in vitro bacteriological characteristics and in vivo virulence of ribotype 002 compared to other common ribotypes, including ribotypes 012, 014 and 046. We observed significantly higher toxin A (p < 0.05) and toxin B (p < 0.05) production, sporulation (p < 0.001) and germination rates (p < 0.0001) in ribotype 002 than other common ribotypes. In a murine model of C. difficile infection, ribotype 002 caused significantly more weight loss (p < 0.001) and histological damage (p < 0.001) than other common ribotypes. These findings may have contributed to the higher prevalence and mortality observed, and provided mechanistic insights that can help public surveillance and develop novel therapeutics to combat against this infection.

24103516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24103516.value: Our study demonstrated the fitness and a potentially important strain from transmission and severity that deserve further attention and surveillance. This project has enabled us to understand the local epidemiology, and furthermore joined the Clostridioides difficile Asia-Pacific Study Group, a large consortium to study the epidemiology across 13 Asia Pacific countries. We have contributed important data and published as consortium member in the publication (Collins DA et al, Emerg Microb Infect 2019) (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/22221751.2019.1702480). Building upon the ground works from this study, we will continue to surveil and study the epidemiology of C. difficile infection.

24103516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24103516.value: Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) is a common cause of hospital-acquired diarrhea. We have previously reported that one bacterial strain called ribotype 002, is a common and deadly subtype in Hong Kong. In this study, we evaluated the bacterial properties and virulence of this ribotype. We observed that this bacterial strain produced significantly more toxins than other common subtypes. It also has higher growth rate and sporulation rate than other subtypes. Using a mouse model, we further demonstrated that the subtype 002 caused significantly more weight loss than the control groups. These insights on the disease mechanism can help the public to monitor and develop new treatments to combat this infection.

24103816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24103816.value: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of death worldwide, representing an enormous burden in terms of healthcare costs. Atherosclerosis, characterized by persistent inflammation and accumulation of lipid-rich plaques in arterial walls, is the major cause of CVD. Atherosclerotic plaques can either behave in a benign fashion, causing no symptoms, or can become unstable leading to acute complications, such as stroke and myocardial infarction. Despite medical advancement, substantial residual risk remains even when treatment goals are fully met. Currently, it is impossible to accurately identify at-risk patients as conventional imaging tools can only determine the degree of artery stenosis. It is recognized that luminal stenosis alone does not adequately reflect the true disease burden in atherosclerosis. Recent research has focused on macrophages, the most abundant component in atherosclerotic plaques. Macrophages play a pivotal role in instigating plaque inflammation, instability and complication, rendering them prime targets for both novel imaging and therapeutics. By integrating therapeutic and diagnostic capability in a single system, we propose to develop and utilize a novel two-pronged theranostic strategy that enables simultaneous in vivo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of plaque inflammation and local delivery of statin to directly inhibit inflammation. We use spherical nucleic acids (SNAs) to act as a delivery vehicle of statin nanotherapy and superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) MRI contrast to target mouse macrophages in the in vitro stage. Subsequently, the thus-synthesized theranostic nanoparticles, i.e. SNA-SPION-Statin, will be used to target plaque macrophages in aortic root to allow simultaneous detection by in vivo MRI and local delivery of statin nanotherapy in an atherosclerotic Apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE-/-) mouse model. By combining molecular MRI functionalities with targeted statin delivery, this advanced two-pronged theranostic strategy enables: i) efficient and potent therapeutics, where statin is delivered locally to a target plaque lesion, maximizing therapeutic benefits and minimizing side-effects. ii) Precise diagnostic imaging based on the plaque macrophages as surrogate markers of plaque inflammation. This allows accurate risk stratification of individual patients, affording the opportunity for early prevention treatment. This could potentially pave the way for personalized management of cardiovascular diseases as it facilitates therapy selection, response monitoring and follow-up therapy planning. Although the initial work focuses on the aortic root, the potential applications could extend to arterial disease in all vascular beds. It will form the basis for a translational study with direct clinical relevance to patients with cardiovascular diseases. 使用他汀類藥物和球形核酸治療診斷鐵納米粒子和核磁共振以達至目標成像和抑制動脈粥樣硬化斑塊炎症 心血管疾病是全球的主要死因，標誌著在醫療費用方面上的巨大負擔。動脈粥樣硬化，其特徵在於持久性炎症和動脈壁富脂質的斑塊的積累，是心血管疾病的主要原因。粥樣硬化斑塊可以是良性的，沒有症狀，或會變得不穩定，導致急性的後遺症，如中風和心肌梗塞。儘管醫學的進步，治療的目標得都可以達到，但是仍然還伴隨著實質性的風險。目前，這是不可能準確地識別高風險患者，因為常規成像工具只能確定動脈狹窄。而且，單憑動脈狹窄並不能充份反映動脈粥樣硬化的真實病況。最近的研究專注於巨噬細胞 ― 在動脈粥樣硬化斑塊裡最豐富的成份。巨噬細胞可引致斑塊炎症 ﹑斑塊不穩定，以及後遺症，這些特性因此令他們在新型成像和治療上成為首要偵測目標。 透過融合治療和診斷的單一系統裡，我們建議開發和利用一種新型且擁有治療和診斷合二為一的策略，能夠同時透過體內核磁共振成像（MRI）偵測斑塊炎症之餘，又可以局部遞送他汀類藥物以直接抑制炎症。在體外階段，我們使用球形核酸（SNA）作為一個他汀類藥物和超順磁性氧化鐵納米顆粒的造影遞送載體（SPIONs）去偵測小鼠巨噬細胞。之後，此合成的治療診斷的納米顆粒，即SNA-SPION-Statin，將用於偵測在主動脈根部斑塊的巨噬細胞，允許同時檢測的體內核磁共振和遞送他汀類藥物納米治療給有動脈粥樣硬化的載脂蛋白E缺乏（載脂蛋白E - / - ）的小鼠模型。 通過結合分子核磁共振功能與他汀類藥物交付目標，這種先進的雙管齊下診斷策略達到：一）高效和有效的治療，他汀類藥物是本地交付給一個目標斑塊病變，提高療效，減少副作用。二）精確診斷成像技術，基於巨噬細胞作為斑塊炎症的替代標記。這項技術達到精確的個體患者的危險分類，為早期預防治療提供機會。這可能為個人化管理心血管疾病的促進治療選擇，反應監測和後續治療計劃展開了新的一頁。儘管最初的工作側重於心臟主動脈根部，潛在的應用可擴展到動脈疾病在所有動脈疾病。它將形成的基礎研究可直接轉化到臨床相關性心血管疾病患者。

24200516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24200516.value: Musculoskeletal robots are a unique class of bio-inspired robots that possess not only the appearance of humans, such as bones and joints, but also muscle-like actuators. By mimicking the human morphology, musculoskeletal robots have the potential to be used as a human proxy in biomechanics, biomechatronics and robotics applications. For example, the replication of motor impairment caused by stroke or muscle tearing on the robots would be greatly beneficial in motor impairment diagnosis and treatment. Compared with in-vivo (in living humans) or in-silico (in computer simulation) approaches, musculoskeletal robot experiments are not only physical like in-vivo studies, but also systematic and repeatable like in-silico methods. Existing studies for this class of robots have focused on the hardware development, where the development of control systems to produce motion still remains a major challenge and is imperative in using musculoskeletal robots as a human proxy for experimentation. The overall goal of this project is to develop and validate motion control strategies for musculoskeletal robots to produce motion within the operational space. The operational space refers to space where the desired actions take place, for example, the position of the hand while reaching. The controller must resolve the muscle actuation redundancy while satisfying the muscle constraints. A predictive control approach will be used to maintain the robot joint trajectory within the workspace of the system. The analysis of the function of muscles responsible for motion will be used to study motion primitives to improve the feasibility of the control problem. Furthermore, a prototype of a muscle-driven human-like arm with human-inspired shoulder and elbow joints will be developed. The choice of the upper limb is motivated by the heavy societal need on upper-arm rehabilitation due stroke and other muscular diseases. Using this prototype, the studied controllers will be implemented to replicate a range of different motions and scenarios. Examples of pathological scenarios include rotator cuff tear and scapula winging. The challenges in this project include: development of anthropomorphic joints, muscles, ligaments and cartilage; implementation of real-time control strategies; and improvement of controller robustness. The developed robot will be the first musculoskeletal robot with an operational space control system. This platform could be used for a wide range of future applications and collaborations. For example, as a neurorobotic platform for neuroscientists, development of rehabilitation devices for roboticists and in the investigation of injury and rehabilitation exercises for clinical physiotherapists. 肌肉骨骼耦合型機器人是一種仿生類機器人，它不僅擁有骨骼和關節等人類的外形特徵，在驅動上，還採用類似肌肉功能的驅動器。通過模擬人的形態，肌肉骨骼耦合型機器人作為人類的模擬器，在生物力學，生物機電工程和機器人應用等領域充滿潛力。例如，在機器人上重現由於肌肉撕裂或者中風所造成的運動功能損傷，能夠極大的幫助損傷的診斷與治療。相較于人體實驗或數值模擬等方法各自的局限性，使用肌肉骨骼耦合型機器人進行實驗既有人體實驗的真實性，又具備數值模擬方法的系統性和可重復性方面的優勢。目前對於這一類機器人已有的研究主要著重於硬件的開發，針對它們的運動控制系統的開發依然是一個很大的挑戰，而控制系統是使用肌肉骨骼耦合型機器人作為人類模擬器在實驗過程中的必不可少的部分。 本項目的主要目標是開發並驗證肌肉骨骼耦合型機器人在執行域內產生運動的控制方案。其中執行域指的是機器人完成要求動作時所到達的空間。例如在做手臂前伸運動時手的位置。控制器必須求解出肌肉驅動器的冗余度，同時也要滿足肌肉約束條件。一種預測控制方法將會被使用，以保證機器人關節運動軌跡始終處於系統的工作空間內。對肌肉功能的分析，將會被應用到研究運動基元方面上，從而提高控制中的可行性。此外，本項目還將會開發一個肌肉驅動的擬人手臂的樣板機，在該手臂中模擬出類似人體的肩關節和肘關節。本項目選擇人體上肢部分進行研究的原因在於其巨大的社會需求，例如由於人體中風或者其他肌肉疾病所帶來的上肢康復領域。利用這個樣板機器人，研究出的控制器可被用於復現一系列不同的上肢運動和病理學情況。例如模擬出肩袖損傷和翼狀肩胛等病理情形。 本項目中的主要挑戰包括：類人關節，肌肉，韌帶以及軟骨的研究和開發；實時控制系統的應用；以及控制器魯棒性的提升。研發出的機器人，將會是世界上第一檯擁有執行域控制系統的肌肉骨骼耦合型機器人。此機器人可以被應用於未來很廣泛的合作研究中。例如它可以給神經系統科學家提供神經系統機器人平台，給康復類機器人研究者提供一個康復設備的改進裝置，或幫助臨床理療師研究機體損傷和康復動作等。

24200516.label: Realisation of objectives
24200516.value: Objective 1: To develop a prototype of a muscle-driven upper-arm, with human-inspired joints, bones, ligaments, cartilage and muscles, that possesses the range of motion and capabilities like that of humans In this project, several muscle-driven upper-arm robots were developed. First, a 4 degree of freedom (DoF) system, named BioMuscular-Arm (BM-Arm), was developed. The BM-Arm consists of two links, link 1 is connected to the body base through a mechanical spherical joint (3 DoF) and link 2 is connected to link 1 through a revolute joint (1 DoF). This prototype is designed to allow for easy reconfiguration of cable attachment locations both at the base and links of the robot arm. Second, the Roboy 3.0 (3rd generation) robot was developed in collaboration with Roboy team from the Technical University of Munich (TUM). Our team’s involvement in this is primarily in the design of the cable attachment locations of the shoulder and arm. With the support of the CUHK Academic Equipment Grant, a copy of the designed Roboy 3.0 has been built for CUHK. Finally, a cable-driven cadaver prototype was also developed. Beginning with a cadaveric pig shoulder, a first prototype was developed where actuated are connected to the pig bone. In this prototype, the motion of the shoulder was excited through kinematic cable length control of the cables. Objective 2: To emulate the actuation properties, such as muscle and ligament dynamics, on the anthropomimetic system In order to emulate actuation properties for anthopomimetic systems, a simulation framework and force controlled direct-drive actuator for musculoskeletal robots were developed. Relating to the simulation of musculoskeletal robots, a ROS version of CASPR (named CASPR-ROS) was developed in order to control the kinematics (cable lengths) and dynamics (cable forces) of cable-driven robots in real-time. However, since the simulation environment of CASPR-ROS was simplistic, unable to emulate realistic physics and lacks user convenience in developing new models, a new design and simulation software framework, named CAble-driven Robot Design and Simulation Flow (CARDSFlow), was developed. CARDSFlow aims to serve as an end-to-end development and simulation platform, allowing users to design the musculoskeletal robot within Fusion 360 CAD software, with auto-conversion to the format (URDF and SDF files) for the Gazebo physics simulator, the analysis and simulation through CASPR and finally the control on real robot hardware. Within this framework, different skeletal structures can be easily imported into the simulator, and more importantly, different types of actuator models can be also incorporated to represent various types of active and passive cables, such as muscles and ligaments. Moreover, an interface between OpenSim and CASPR (CASPR-OSIM), to allow the simulation of realistic biomechanical models from OpenSim to be simulated using the methods developed for CASPR. Objectives 3 and 4: To understand the function and roles of the set of muscles for the purpose of performing motion within the operational space; and to develop a library of motion primitives through the analysis of operational workspace for musculoskeletal robots To understand the function and roles of muscles, analysis techniques to generate workspace based on poses and trajectories were developed. First, the ray-based wrench-closure workspace (WCW) was proposed to be applicable to arbitrary types of cable-driven robots and any type of degrees-of-freedom (DoF). It was shown that for any single link and multilink CDPRs, the ray-based WCW condition can be expressed as a set of univariate polynomial equations that can be efficiently solved. A method to determine the coefficients of the polynomial equations for any type of CDPR is proposed. To represent workspace of higher dimensions, typical for musculoskeletal robots, a novel graph workspace representation is introduced to represent the workspace of CDRs with any arbitrary number of DoFs. Second, extending from the ray-based workspace analysis methods that is limited to a single DoF at a time to form a lattice workspace, a trajectory verification approach was developed. In this the ray-based trajectory verification, it is shown that by representing the trajectory as a parametric polynomial equation for the translational coordinates and also using the quaternion representation for the robot orientation, the resulting wrench-closure condition (WCC) and cable interference-free condition (IFC) can be solved through computing the roots of polynomial equations. Given the polynomial nature of the equations required to be solved, the feasible and infeasible trajectory sections can hence be efficiently computed. Finally, a systematic study was performed on the operational space workspace of the shoulder and the impairment workspace analysis. In this study, the workspace variation under different “impaired” muscles (lowering it’s maximum cable force) was investigated. From this, the correlation between muscle groups to the impairment were classified. This provides a significant understanding on the function and roles of how different muscles contribute to the operational space motion. Objective 5: To develop predictive motion controllers for musculoskeletal robots using knowledge of muscle function to operate directly within the operational space The control of cable-driven robots is inherently challenging due to the following factors: 1) the existence of positive cable force (input) constraints that must be satisfied; 2) actuation redundancy of cable-driven robots; and 3) non-linearity of the system equations of motion. To address such critical issue, model predictive controllers (MPC) can be employed. However, the standard MPC formulation cable-driven robots are also non-linear and non-convex (NMPC). In this project, we proposed a new workspace-based MPC controller for musculoskeletal robots that linearise and convexify the MPC using the workspace analysis results of the system. The results demonstrate that the developed methods have higher computational efficiency compared with existing NMPC methods. Furthermore, proofs and properties have on the controller stability, recursive feasibility and robustness have been rigorously developed to fundamentally support the W-MPC. This work represents the first type of workspace governed MPC controller for robotics, by using offline robot workspace computation to make the online control more efficient and robust. Objective 6: To validate the developed controllers on the musculoskeletal arm to test its performance on a range of motion experiments and case studies The results from objectives 5 and 6 were validated on the robots developed in objective 1, and were used to support the controllers developed for the publications produced during this project. This is also important to support future development of both the hardware and controllers. Summary In summary, the objectives of this project were well achieved, as demonstrated by the software, hardware and algorithms that were developed as a result of the project. Furthermore, this project resulted in 3 journal publications (two in IEEE Transactions on Robotics and one in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters), several conferences and also the training of 1 PhD and 2 MPhil students.

24200516.label: Major findings and research outcome
24200516.value: Musculoskeletal systems and cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) are analogous due to their similarities in actuation and topology. In this project, the modelling, analysis and control of musculoskeletal CDPRs were investigated. Such problems are challenging due to the actuation constraints, actuation redundancy and the non-linear relationships between the actuation, joint and operational spaces. Relating to modelling, new ROS-based software platforms were developed, CASPR-ROS and CARDSFLOW. CASPR-ROS allows the simulation of musculoskeletal CDPRs through ROS and real-time hardware control. CARDSFLOW is a new modelling and simulation workflow for musculoskeletal robots. It allows CAD models of musculoskeletal systems to be imported to CASPR, with the muscle model and attachment configurations considered. Compatibility with Gazebo allows realistic physics can be realised. Moreover, significant improvements have been made to the dynamics computational speed for generalised multilink CDPRs. The developed modelling and software platforms greatly benefit other robotics researchers or those interested in studying musculoskeletal systems. For the analysis of CDPRs, several works relating to the inverse dynamics, calibration and workspace analysis were studied. These are important to the understanding and operation of musculoskeletal CDPRs. In particular, the first generalised ray-based workspace analysis approach was proposed, that allows the wrench-closure analysis for multilink CDPRs of any type to be studied both with high accuracy and efficiency, alongside with a mathematical representation that can visualise and present higher degree of freedom workspaces. Moreover, the work was then extended to consider curved trajectory motions, to compute the wrench-closure and interference feasibility sections. Furthermore, the control of CDPRs was also studied within this project. A new type of model predictive controller (MPC) was developed, the workspace-based MPC (W-MPC). This is a novel type of control technique that combines the workspace analysis of CDPRs with MPC to convexify and linearise the inherently challenging non-linear problem. This new concept results in a formulation that has exact dynamics, efficient to solve and robust, this work also forms the basis for future workspace-based controllers for both CDPR systems and beyond. Finally, several hardware prototypes were developed, namely the BM-Arm (shoulder and elbow robot), the design for the 3rd generation Roboy in collaboration with Technical University of Munich, and a cable-driven shoulder cadaver platform. These hardware platforms allow the theoretical contributions of the project to be demonstrated, and also to show the potential in the development of cable-driven musculoskeletal robots, such as for biomimetic platforms, humanoids and even biomechanics cadaveric studies with actuated cables.

24200516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24200516.value: Through this project, the modelling, analysis, software and hardware platforms for musculoskeletal-type of cable-driven robots were developed. Such results aim to provide a greater understanding and platforms for the study of human-like robots and biomechanical systems. One aspect for further development is the continual study of the workspace-based MPC, as the framework can be extended to the control of a wider range of robot systems, such as humanoid walking and serial robots. This will be performed as on-going research in existing and future research projects. Another important aspect of further development from the completed project is to develop robotic platforms for human and biomechanics study. In particular, the early prototype develop of a cable-driven robotic cadaver is one with high potential for future studies. During this project, we have established collaboration with Prof. Patrick Yung from the CUHK Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology, where a cable-driven pig shoulder robot was tested. We are currently planning future project extensions and grant applications to develop a cable-driven cadaver platform for studying the human motion for orthopaedic treatment.

24200516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24200516.value: Musculoskeletal systems and cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) are analogous due to their similarities in actuation and topology. The modelling, analysis and control of musculoskeletal CDPRs are challenging due to the actuation constraints, actuation redundancy and the non-linear relationships between the actuation, joint and operational spaces. Major outcomes of the project include the development of a new simulation workflow and software for musculoskeletal CDPRs, CASPR-ROS and CARDSFLOW, allowing robots to be designed using computer-aided design software and imported into our realistic robot simulator. Moreover, novel techniques to generate the operational region of musculoskeletal robots were developed, which are more accurate, computationally more efficient and can work with systems with high degrees-of-freedom. Another important achievement of the project is the development of a new class of model predictive control (MPC), called workspace-based MPC, which uses the workspace of CDPR to transform the challenging non-linear and non-convex problem into one that can be much more efficient for real-time control. Finally, several hardware prototypes were developed through the project, the BM-Arm shoulder and elbow robot and a cable-driven shoulder cadaver platform. This project provides greater insight into musculoskeletal CDPRs to serve as biomimetic platforms, humanoids and even biomechanics cadaveric studies with artificial muscles.

24201816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24201816.value: This proposal aims (1) to develop an electrically-aided stamping process for fast replication of micro-surface geometry, (2) to design and analytically model an ultrasonic resonant vibration tool; and (3) to study the process mechanics by developing a constitutive model to account for both the dynamic electroplastic behavior and size effects. Micro-structured surfaces, with defined periodic structures, usually have enhanced functional performance, such as tribological, wetting, thermal, biological, and optical properties. Various applications have been implemented based on the research in micro-structured surfaces including self-cleaning, icephobic, antiseptic, and friction reduction surfaces. Their huge potential for industrial applications, however, is limited by the current manufacturing capability. The manufacturing of these surfaces, referred to as surface texturing, to date could not achieve the targets of low cost, great efficiency, and high precision. The proposed research presents an attempt to solve aforementioned problems. We propose an ultrafast stamping system for surface texturing of micro-scale features. The system is supported by three novel engineering concepts, i.e., (1) the utilization of ultrasonic resonant vibration as the actuation motion for high productivity; (2) the employment of electrical current in addition to mechanical deformation for enhanced formability; and (3) the design of a frequency-and-amplitude-tunable elliptical vibration resonator for process parameter matching. A constitutive model will be developed, as a numerical study of the process, by combining a phenomenological flow stress model and a dislocation model, in order to take both the electroplastic behavior and size effects into consideration. The outcome of this research will significantly upgrade the capability of surface texturing over any current commercially available system, by enhancing its productivity, formability, dimensional accuracy, flexibility, and scalability. It will consolidate the scientific and technological base of micro-manufacturing, as well as aid the creation and design of new functional surfaces for current and future needs in this fast-evolving area. 表面微結構可以提高原表面的摩擦、潤滑、光學等性能。基於表面微結構的功能性表面，例如自清潔、抗菌和減摩表面，已經被研發並應用。微結構表面的巨大工業應用前景目前仍受限於製造能力的限制。本研究提出一種超快的表面微織構沖壓系統。該系統由三個創新點，即（1）使用超聲波振動作為壓印的執行元件；（2）利用輔助電流改善金屬表面成型性；（3）創新設計一個振動頻率和幅度可調的超聲波橢圓振動壓印器。

24202316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24202316.value: We plan to study the various aspects of optimization problems and algorithms. We propose to study the limitations of general convex optimization algorithms as a refutation algorithm. This will help us gain deeper understanding on the complexity of computational problems (both decision and optimization problems). We also plan to study convex programs beyond semideﬁnite programs, in the hope that new understanding of different convex programs will lead to new approximation guarantees. We mention a few concrete problems in this direction. We also study how optimization algorithms may be applied to problems in statistical learning and machine learning, or obstacles in doing so.

24202316.label: Realisation of objectives
24202316.value: The project is still ongoing and has not yet reached the desired milestone. For Objective 1: As a first step, we now have a simplified proof of sum-of-squares lower bounds for random constraint satisfaction problems (that satisfy a technical condition known as pairwise uniform), a result first shown by Kothari, Mori, O'Donnell, Witmer (STOC 2017). Our cleaner mental picture is vital for the next step: generalizing the lowerbounds from sum-of-square hierarchy to semidefinite extended formulations. However, lowerbounds for extended formulations turned out much more challenging than original anticipated. In the past few years, we have sharpened our goals, which are now as follows: 1) Study minimally unsatisfiable instances 3XOR first (and try to prove extension complexity lowerbounds for them) 2) Prove necessary and sufficient condition for an inequality that refutes a minimally unsatisfiable 3XOR instance 3) Model extended formulation as a proof system (like a variant of resolution) 4) Consider the dual space of the lifting map in an extended formulation (the lifting map is defined in Gouveia, Parrilo, Thomas (Math. Oper. Res. 2013) 5) Construct injective mappings from the dual subspaces of a lifting map to resolution steps We can now characterize an inequality that refutes a minimally unsatisfiable 3XOR instance (point 2 above), but the remaining steps prove very challenging. We now know the following counterexamples to our naive conjectures at the beginning of the project: * To refute a non-minimal 3XOR instance, the inequality may not correspond to any resolution step. This is why we now focus on minimally unsatisfiable 3XOR instances * The previous discovery prompted us to look at a “sub-step” of a resolution step. We searched for the right way to deal with these sub-steps for a long time. We then realized sub-steps may not be the right object to study for sum-of-squares extended formulations. This suggests side-stepping the concept of “sub-steps” altogether. * Refuting minimally unsatisfiable 3XOR instances that share a common factor graph (as defined in Kothari, Mori, O'Donnell, Witmer (STOC 2017)), the inequalities used need not be exactly of the canonical form that we originally proposed. There can be a “full-dimension” of freedom in choosing these inequalities. The combinatorial structure of an extended formulation refutation for 3XOR has given rise to many unexpected complications and surprising discoveries. We are inching much closer to be able to fully describe the structure, but isn’t quite there yet. With our current progress, we expect to b able to describe the structure within the next year. In the past few years, other groups have worked on related extended formulations lowerbounds, such as Kothari, Meka and Raghavandra (STOC 2017), and Brown-Cohen and Raghavandra (SODA 2020). However, these works are based on junta approximation, and they can never show a lowerbound for every NP-hard problem, which is our main goal. For Objective 2: We spent most of our effort in Objective 1, and relatively little time on Objective 2. We did understand geometric programming better. This may be useful for proving extended formulation lowerbounds for geometric programs, which is wide open. But we did not have time to study how geometric programming may be useful to problems that weren’t known to be useful.

24202316.label: Major findings and research outcome
24202316.value: While we are still working on our main objective, we have some partial results on smaller, related projects. Our SODA 2017 paper ruled out random walk algorithms for approximating small-set expansion, a close cousin of the unique games problem and a central open problem in approximation algorithms. This refutes a conjecture that was mentioned in Oveis Gharan. In an unpublished work with my MPhil student LI Sing Hei, we improved the integrality gap lowerbound of Nikolov approximation algorithm for the largest simplex problem to 2^k/(k+1).

24202316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24202316.value: We plan to complete the lowerbound for extended formulation for NP-hard problems in the coming year or so. If all goes well, this will complete the main objective (Objective 1) of this project. That would give a completely new technique for proving extended formulation lowerbounds, different from Fiorini et al (STOC 2012 Best Paper), Rothvoss (STOC 2014 Best Paper) and Lee, Raghavandra, Steurer (STOC 2015 Best Paper), shedding new lights on their combinatorial structure.

24202316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24202316.value: We plan to show limitations of a huge family of algorithms based on convex programming, known as extended formulation. We aim to prove their limitations on randomly generated instances of constraint satisfaction problems, and of problems that are at least as hard. We aim to characterize the structural properties of such algorithms. By contrast, existing works merely prove what these algorithms cannot be, without showing how they must behave. As such, current techniques fail to completely show their limitations.

24300516.label: Project Objectives
24300516.value: to investigate the effects of liquid-liquid phase separation on the heterogeneous OH oxidation of aqueous droplets comprised of inorganic salts and carboxylic acids
rows: to investigate the effects of liquid-liquid phase separation on the heterogeneous OH oxidation of aqueous droplets comprised of inorganic salts and carboxylic acids

24300516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24300516.value: Atmospheric aerosols are small particles suspended in the air and have pronounced effects on human health, air quality, and climate. Organic compounds are abundant in atmospheric aerosols and are subject to oxidation reactions with gas-phase oxidants such as hydroxyl (OH) radicals at the aerosol surface. These oxidative processes can change the composition and properties of atmospheric aerosols, leading to large uncertainties in predicting their impacts on air quality and climate. Studies on the OH radical initialized oxidation of organic aerosols have clearly shown that the aerosol phase state plays an important role in the heterogeneous chemistry. Atmospheric aerosols may exist as aqueous droplets. Recent studies suggest aqueous droplets composed of inorganic salts and organic compounds might undergo liquid-liquid phase separation into two separated liquid phases: an aqueous inorganic-rich core phase and an organic-rich phase near the aerosol surface. Such complex phase behavior may significantly influence the heterogeneous chemical reactivity. This proposed study aims at investigating how liquid-liquid phase separation in aqueous droplets containing an inorganic salt (e.g. ammonium sulfate, ammonium nitrate, and sodium chloride) and an organic compound (e.g. polyols and carboxylic acids) controls the molecular transformation of the aerosols oxidized by gas-phase OH radicals using an aerosol flow tube reactor over a range of relative humidities. An atmospheric pressure aerosol mass spectrometer, which combines an atmospheric pressure soft ionization source (Direct Analysis in Real Time, DART) with a high resolution mass spectrometer, will be used to obtain the detailed molecular information about reaction products in real time. One of distinct advantages of this technique is that the chemical composition of aqueous droplets can be analyzed in the original phase state under atmospheric pressure conditions. Additionally, in contrast to other higher energy ionization techniques, the DART ionization source can ionize many organic compounds with minimal fragmentation. The molecular identities of the compounds are typically retained, facilitating a proper reaction product identification. In this proposed study, we will provide new molecular and mechanistic information for the heterogeneous OH oxidation of aqueous inorganic-organic droplets. Such results will aid in a better understanding of the role of the aerosol phase state on the chemical evolution in the composition of atmospheric aerosols by heterogeneous oxidative processes. 大氣氣溶膠是懸浮在空氣中的小顆粒，它對人類健康、空氣質素和氣候變化有着明顯的影響。大氣氣溶膠含有豐富的有機化合物，這些有機化合物能與羥基自由基(OH)在氣溶膠的表面進行氧化反應。這異構氧化過程可以改變大氣氣溶膠的成分及其屬性，因此讓我們在預測氣溶膠對空氣質素和氣候變化之影響上有着更大的變數。有機氣溶膠的異構氧化研究清楚指出有機氣溶膠的形態在異構化學反應上擔當着重要角色。大氣氣溶膠能以水滴的形態出現，最新研究提出蘊含無機鹽和有機化合物的水滴有機會進行液相分離，從而產生兩層分離的液體形態，即氣溶膠表面充滿着有機物，而其核心則充滿着無機物，這複雜的氣溶膠形態可能對異構化學反應有着極大的影響力。是次研究旨在探討包含無機鹽(例如：硫酸銨、硝酸銨和氯化鈉)和有機化合物(例如：多元醇和羧酸)的水滴在液相分離下如何控制異構氧化的氣溶膠的分子改組。這異構氧化過程將會在氣霧流管式反應器上透過調校一系列的相對濕度進行。大氣壓軟電離源(DART)和高分辨率質譜儀將會用來收集反應物的即時詳細分子資料，這項技術的優勝之處是能有效地分析氣溶膠在大氣壓自身形態下的化學結構。此外，相對其他高能量離子化技術，DART電離源能妥善地電離很多有機化合物，使化合物的分子信息得以保留，從而促進反應物的鑑定。透過是此研究，我們將可為異構氧化的氣溶膠提供新的分子資料，從而讓我們能更了解氣溶膠的形態在異構氧化過程上起了多大的化學作用。

24300516.label: Realisation of objectives
24300516.value: In this project, we investigated how liquid-liquid phase separation in model aqueous droplets containing an inorganic salt and a dicarboxylic acid governs the heterogeneous reactivity of organic compounds toward gas-phase OH radical. We gratefully acknowledge that the project objective has been fully addressed. The details of the realization of objectives are given below. To achieve the project objective, we first demonstrated that model aqueous droplets containing an inorganic salt (e.g. ammonium sulfate) and a dicarboxylic acid (e.g. 3-methyglutaric acid, 3-MGA) with an organic to inorganic (OIR) mass ratio of one can undergo liquid-liquid phase separation using a linear-quadrupole electrodynamic balance (LQ-EDB) and a flow cell coupled to an optical microscope. We found that at high RH, aerosols were aqueous droplets with a single liquid phase. When the RH decreased, aqueous droplets underwent phase separation (separation RH (SRH) ~ 73%). Once the droplets were phase-separated, they exhibited different morphologies with an organic-rich outer phase and an inorganic-rich inner phase. We proposed that the phase separation mechanism is very likely spinodal decomposition based the formation of many small inclusions at the onset of phase separation. Thermodynamic phase equilibrium calculations were also performed using the Aerosol Inorganic–Organic Mixtures Functional groups Activity Coefficients (AIOMFAC) liquid–liquid equilibrium (LLE) model to confirm the results of the experimentally observed phase separation and onset mechanisms. In addition to thermodynamic modeling, we performed molecular dynamic (MD) simulations to illustrate that organic molecules tended to stay near the surface while the dissolved inorganic ions preferred to stay in the droplet bulk. This was in qualitatively support of the finding from thermodynamic modeling. Second, we investigated the molecular composition of aqueous droplets before and after heterogeneous OH oxidation using an atmospheric pressure aerosol flow tube reactor coupled with a direct analysis in real time (DART) ionization source and a high-resolution mass spectrometer at different relative humidity (RH) levels. The heterogeneous OH oxidation of aqueous droplets, consisting of either a single liquid phase (RH > SRH) or two separate liquid phases (RH< SRH), was investigated by varying the RH. We found that the heterogeneous reactivity of phase-separated droplets was higher than that of aqueous droplets with a single liquid phase. This phenomenon can be explained by the inhomogeneous distribution of organic molecules within the droplets created by liquid-liquid phase separation, with higher concentrations present at or near the droplet surface, as demonstrated by phase separation measurements and model simulations. This increased the probability that organic molecules collide with OH radicals at or near the aerosol surface, leading to a higher overall rate of reactions. Additionally, same major reaction products were formed upon the heterogeneous OH oxidation of dicarboxylic acids in the presence and absence of inorganic salts. This suggested that the presence of dissolved inorganic ions does not significantly affect the formation pathways of major reaction products upon the heterogeneous OH oxidation, but alter the rate of reactions with OH by changing the surface concentration and morphology of aqueous droplets. We would also like to note that the findings of this project had clearly demonstrated that the molecular distribution of organic species within aqueous droplets is crucial in determining heterogeneous reactivity. This led to a new research direction on the heterogeneous OH reactivity of organic compounds that are surface-active and preferentially partition near the aerosol surface for oxidation. From that, we had investigated the heterogeneous OH reactivity of some model surface active organosulfur compounds (e.g. methyltetrol sulfate esters, methylsulfate, and methanesulfonic acid) commonly found in atmospheric aerosols. Kinetic data revealed that all these surface active organic species were highly subjected to heterogeneous OH oxidation given their high surface propensities. Overall, all these findings from this project had led to five publications in the top scientific journals in the area of atmospheric science and presented in regional and international aerosol conferences.
