24300516.label: Major findings and research outcome
24300516.value: In this project, we investigated how liquid-liquid phase separation in model aqueous droplets containing an inorganic salt and an organic acid determine the heterogeneous reactivity of organic compounds toward gas-phase OH radical. We firstly demonstrated that liquid-liquid phase separation could be commonly occurred in aqueous droplets containing both inorganic salts and organic compounds. Once aqueous droplets were phase-separated, they exhibited different morphologies (e.g. core–shell, partially engulfed or a transition from core–shell to partially engulfed structure, with an organic-rich outer phase and an inorganic-rich inner phase). Plausible phase separation mechanisms (i.e. spinodal decomposition) were proposed based our experimental results and modelling simulations. We further showed that phase-separated droplets exhibited higher reactivity towards gas-phase OH radicals, compared to droplets with a single liquid phase at higher relative humidity (RH). This can be explained by the uneven surface distribution of organic species within the phase-separated droplets with more organic species at the droplet surface, increasing reaction probability between organic molecules and OH radicals. The overall rate of reactions is likely governed by the surface concentration of organic species, which determines the reactive collisions between organic molecules and gas phase OH radicals. For both single-phase and phase-separated aerosols, the heterogeneous reactivity exhibited a decreasing trend as RH increased. It can be attributed to higher organic species concentration at lower RH which intensifies the oxidation. Additionally, the presence of dissolved inorganic salts could alter the heterogeneous reactivity of organic compounds with gas-phase OH radicals at the surface by varying the surface concentration of organic compounds under different environmental conditions (Please see publications 1 and 2). Overall, we clearly demonstrated the liquid-liquid phase separation processes could potentially change the surface composition of the droplets, which ultimately govern the heterogeneous reactivity based on our experimental and modeling results. The molecular distribution of organic species is an important factor in governing the reactivity. We also found that the surface active organic compounds, which are more likely concentrated on aerosol surface, were highly subjected to heterogeneous oxidation (Publications 3 - 5) . The findings of this project clearly demonstrated the significance of liqui-liquid phase separation and molecular distribution on the heterogeneous OH reactivity and atmospheric fate of organic compounds, which often coexist with inorganic salts in atmospheric aerosols.

24300516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24300516.value: We would like to propose that further development in thermodynamic and molecular dynamic (MD) modeling would be important to gain better fundamental insights into how liquid-liquid phase separation alters the heterogeneous reactivity of atmospheric aerosols. For instance, in this project, we performed thermodynamic phase equilibrium calculations to understand the phase separation of our model systems. The model simulations had provided a reasonable explanation for the phase separation mechanism consistent with the experimental observations. Further development of predictive group contribution models like AIOMFAC-LLE used in this project would be highly desirable to better predict phase separation and other composition-dependent properties of the typically highly complex organic–inorganic mixtures representative of atmospheric aerosols. Additionally, considering the detailed molecular-level resolution by which molecular dynamics (MD) simulations allow us to probe surface and near surface inhomogeneities in composition, this method provides an additional perspective on the bulk–surface partitioning of organic species with or without liquid-liquid phase separation occurring. We thus would like to propose that more effort is needed to further optimize the molecular models, e.g., with more elaborate search for better parameters, functional forms and/or more sophisticated models.

24300516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24300516.value: Organic compounds present at or near the surface of atmospheric aerosols can be subjected to oxidation initiated by gas-phase oxidants, such as hydroxyl radicals (OH). However, uncertainties in the heterogeneous reactivity of aqueous droplets containing organic compounds and inorganic salts remain to date. Additional uncertainties in heterogeneous reactivity of organic compounds arise when these droplets undergo liquid-liquid phase separation. In this project, we found that the heterogeneous reactivity is highly sensitive to the surface concentration of organic molecules, which could be determined by liquid-liquid phase separation behavior. We demonstrated that once the atmospheric aerosols were phase-separated, they exhibited different morphologies with an organic-rich outer phase and an inorganic-rich inner phase. We further showed that the heterogeneous reactivity of phase-separated droplets was higher than that of aqueous droplets with a single liquid phase. The change in reactivity could be explained by the change in the surface composition of the aerosols due to the presence or absence of phase separation. This finding of this project emphasizes that the effects of liquid-liquid phase separation and potentially distinct aerosol morphologies add further complexity to the understanding of the heterogeneous reactivity and atmospheric fate of organic compounds in aqueous organic–inorganic droplets in the atmosphere.

24301416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24301416.value: The aim of this project is to develop a statistical model and accompanying inference methods for transcription factor networks, which are heterogeneous across the genome and dynamic over biological conditions. Gene expression is largely controlled by a family of proteins called transcription factors (TF) in a collaborative manner. Therefore, understanding TF cooperation is crucial for elucidating gene regulation and ultimately disease mechanism. The interactions among TFs can be represented by networks, one network for each genomic position and each node inside a network representing a TF. Since TF collaborations differ from genomic position to position and from one biological condition to another, the networks are heterogeneous and dynamic. However, there is a shortage of statistical methods for heterogeneous dynamic networks, let alone for TF networks. Although there have been active researches on modeling multiple networks jointly, these methods enforce the network structures for all the samples within a single condition to be the same. In contrast, the emerging works on estimating heterogeneous Gaussian graphical models do not consider multiple non-temporal conditions, and they are not applicable to counts data, which are the cases for TF experiments. Moreover, despite the recent statistical developments, the previous construction of TF networks lacks solid statistical model, analyzes each biological condition on its own, and ignores heterogeneity within condition. For TF experimental data, single condition analysis suffers from low detection power; according to our pilot study, disregarding genome heterogeneity can result in extremely misleading conclusions about TF associations. In this project, we propose a novel Bayesian nonparametric dynamic Poisson graphical model to handle both heterogeneity and multiple conditions simultaneously. By accounting for heterogeneity, our model will offer a legitimate measure of TF association strength; via pooling information across multiple conditions, our model will improve signal detection from small sample size, high-noise data. To take care of the large data volume, we will develop efficient highly parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithms to conduct statistical inference for the proposed model. We will make our algorithms freely available and design an online genome browser, which delivers the dynamic TF networks learned from the enormous amount of experimental data stored in public repositories. This Big Data project, as a typical example with data of large volume, high complexity, and low veracity, will make substantial contributions to statistical modeling, statistical computing, parallel programming and genomics. The scientific discoveries from this project will help to solve health problems related to Hong Kong and elsewhere. 轉錄因子網絡一方面在基因組不同的位點有著不同的結構，另一方面其結構也隨著細胞類型的變化而動態變化。本項目旨在研究轉錄因子網絡的統計建模和推斷方法。 基因表達很大程度上由一類稱為轉錄因子的蛋白共同調控。因此，理解轉錄因子的協同作用對揭示基因調控的原理至關重要。轉錄因子之間的相互作用可以用網絡來表達。每一個基因組位點對應一個網絡，而網絡的每個節點表示一個轉錄因子。由於轉錄因子間的協同作用隨著基因組位點和細胞類型的不同而不同，所以轉錄因子網絡是非均一併且動態變化的。 然而文獻中少有針對非均一動態網絡的統計方法，更不要提對轉錄因子網絡的統計建模。最近有許多對多個網絡同時建模的統計方法，但它們都要求同一個條件下所有樣本都服從同一個網絡。另一方面，現有非均一高斯圖模型的統計方法都不同時考慮多個條件。並且現有的這些方法都不適用於對離散性數據建立網絡模型，而這恰恰是用於學習轉錄因子網絡模型的數據的特點。因而，儘管最近針對網絡的統計方法有快速的發展，轉錄因子網絡依舊沒有嚴格的統計模型。 在本項目中我們提出一個新的貝葉斯非參數動態泊松圖模型來同時處理網絡結構的非均一性和動態變化。我們的模型不僅提供了一個對轉錄因子協同作用的合理度量，同時通過整合不同條件下的樣本提高了推斷網絡結構的準確度。我們開發了一個高度並行的Markov Chain Monte Carlo的算法來對所提出的模型進行統計推斷。 這個大數據項目是一個大數據量、高數據複雜度、低信噪比的典型例子，它將對統計建模、統計計算、並行計算和基因組學作出重要貢獻。其中的科學發現也將有助於解決與香港有關的健康問題。

24301416.label: Realisation of objectives
24301416.value: We have fully achieved the objectives of the proposal. The reference number is indexed according to the references listed in Part C. We have developed a Bayesian nonparametric dynamic Poisson graphical model－HDPGM mdoel－for inferring transcription factor networks from ChIP-seq data [1]. Our proposed model allows the network structures to vary both across the whole genome and across different biological conditions. We developed a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to conduct statistical inference. We parallelized the algorithm and implemented the parallel MCMC algorithm in C under the message passing interface (MPI) framework. We provide our code and instructions of how to apply the algorithm to ChIP-seq data freely available at https://github.com/XiangyuLuo/HDPGM. We applied our developed algorithm to investigate the network structure of a total of 30 transcription factors that were assayed in all of the three Tier 1 cell lines of the ENCODE project by August 30, 2017 at the promoter regions of all the genes in the human genome [1]. We constructed an online browser https://angus-gm-chan.shinyapps.io/tf_network_shiny/ to deliver our learned transcription factor networks. Among the three ENCODE Tier 1 cell lines, only K562 is a cancer cell line. When inspecting the co-activation patterns of transcription factors at the promoter regions of the genes that have been associated with liver cancers, such as IQGAP2, IQGAP1 and IGF2R, we found that the pair MYC and MAX and the pair CTCF and RAD21 always co-activate. Therefore, although K562 is an immortalized chronic myelogenous leukemia cell line, the results suggest that we should prioritize the ChIP-seq experiments for MYC, MAX, CTCF and RAD21 for liver cancer cell lines. Moreover, we not only investigated the heterogeneity of transcription factor networks but also adapted the developed statistical methods to tease out heterogeneity for microbiome data [2] and DNA methylation data [3, 4].

24301416.label: Major findings and research outcome
24301416.value: Gene expression is largely controlled by transcription factors in a collaborative manner. Therefore, an understanding of transcription factor collaboration is crucial for the elucidation of gene regulation. The co-activation of transcription factors can be represented by networks. These networks are dynamic in diverse biological conditions and heterogeneous across the genome within each biological condition. Existing methods for construction of transcription factor networks lack solid statistical models, analyze each biological condition separately, and enforce a single network for all genomic locations within one biological condition, resulting in low statistical power and misleading spurious associations. To tackle these challenges, we proposed a novel Bayesian nonparametric dynamic Poisson graphical mode that builds upon the Dirichlet process－the HDPGM model [1]. HDPGM clusters the whole genome into several unknown clusters such that genomic locations in the same cluster share the same dynamic transcription factor networks. HDPGM can automatically learn the number of clusters. We designed a Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm to conduct posterior inference and develop a parallel scheme to handle the large data volume. We determined the network structures by controlling the Bayesian false discovery rate at the targeted level. We compared HDPGM with three traditional approaches to estimating transcription factor networks: (I) learning a transcription factor network for each genomic location under each condition separately, (II) learning a single transcription factor network for all genomic locations given an individual condition, and (III) learning multiple heterogeneous transcription factor networks for an individual condition without pooling information across conditions. Our simulation studies showed that at low false positive rates HDPGM can achieve much larger statistical power than the other three types of analyses. Therefore, borrowing strengths across conditions and genomic locations improves edge detection substantially. We applied the HDPGM to study the collaborations of 30 transcription factors at all the promoter regions across all the three ENCODE Tier 1 cell lines. The HDPGM discovers 37 clusters of dynamic TF networks for all of the promoter regions. Our analysis confirms that transcription factors’ collaborations vary across conditions and are heterogeneous across the genome. We also compared the marginal distribution of the read counts of the model with the observed data and observed a close match. Therefore, HDPGM fits the real data very well. We provided the learned dynamic transcription factor networks via an interactively online browser. We further developed statistical methods to model the heterogeneity for microbiome data [2] and DNA methylation data [3, 4].

24301416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24301416.value: Although thousands of ChIP-seq data have already been stored in public data repositories, such as ENCODE, we are still hungry for more ChIP-seq data to comprehensively study transcription factor networks. The major obstacle is that the number of transcription factors whose ChIP-seq experiments are available for a large number of common biological conditions is still very small. Nevertheless, given the exponentially decreasing sequencing costs and statistical developments in imputation methods for genomic data, transcription factor networks with a larger number of nodes and conditions can be expected in the near future. As more data accumulate, our scalable HDPGM model will continue to update our understanding of transcription factor co-activation, gene regulation, and ultimately phenotype diversity and diseases. In particular, we will further focus on liver cancer related biological samples.

24301416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24301416.value: For a single person, the same copy of a genome can give rise to hundreds of distinct cell types. To understand this phenotype diversity and decipher disease mechanisms, it is crucial to reveal gene regulation mechanisms. Gene regulation is largely controlled by a family of proteins called transcription factors. Accurate gene expression regulation requires extensive collaborations among transcription factors. Because transcription factor collaborations differ among biological conditions (or cell types), the network at each genomic location is dynamic. Moreover, as transcription factor interactions change across the genome, all dynamic etworks are heterogeneous across the genome rather than sharing the same structure. The success of this project provides solid statistical methods to learn the heterogenous, dynamic transcription factor networks from noisy experimental data. The scientific discovery from this project greatly deepens our understandings of gene regulation. The statistical methods developed in this project provide new approaches to integrative analysis of heterogeneous genomic data.

24301516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24301516.value: The discovery and intensive study of topological phases of quantum matter, e.g., fractional quantum Hall effect(FQHE) in strongly correlated systems have been an important part of modern condensed matter physics. The revolutionary concept of topological phases of quantum matter is that their excitations carry fractionalized statistics, that is, a particle with exchange phases in between of bosons and fermions. Such a broadly interesting and interdisciplinary field has become more and more important recently, showing evidence of its evolutionary impact on modern physics. It might dramatically change our knowledge of fundamental physics and eventually lead to a new revolution of modern industries, for example, the possible realization of topological quantum computers. Recently, it has been shown that topological order and fractionalized excitations do not only exist in FQHE systems, but also exist in certain class of superconductors, namely, topological superconductor. In particular, Read and Green pointed out that a single vortex of 2D spinless p+ip superconductor traps a topological Majorana zero mode and carries non-Abelian statistics. In the past few years, the possible realization of p+ip topological superconductor and topological Majorana zero mode has become a very important subject both theoretically and experimentally. Major efforts have been put forward along a few directions e.g, evidences for p+ip pairing symmetry in Sr2RuO4 and topological Majorana zero mode in half-vortex are reported; the ideas of realizing topological Majorana zero mode on the surface of topological insulator and at the end of 1D nanowire have been tested experimentally. In recent studies, PI and collaborators have proposed a novel superconductivity mechanism mediated by ferromagnetic skyrmion current in strongly correlated electron systems, e.g., Hubbard model with infinite repulsive U on honeycomb lattice. In particular, due to the presence of spin-charge separation with fermionic holons, the pairing symmetry turns out to be p+ip-wave. These findings can have an important impact on the realization of p+ip topological superconductors in strongly correlated systems. 24301516.label: Realisation of objectives
24301516.value: We followed closely our plan. The majority of the objectives were addressed. (a) We have developed Grassmann tensor network renormalization algorithm to accurately simulate the ground state energy of honeycomb lattice Hubbard/t-J model. A p+ip topological superconductivity was discovered in the extremely strong coupling limit(e.g., infinite U limit) at low doping(<20%). We find that the p + ip SC state has an instability towards a potential non-Fermi liquid with a large but finite U. Nevertheless, by applying an in-plane Zeeman field, such a p+ip SC state can be stabilized with finite U in a very wide range of doping. Very recently, we further obtain the global phase diagram of Hubbard/t-J model with generic doping and coupling strength. (b) In the strong coupling limit, our discovery suggests a new mechanism for p+ip SC state in generic strongly correlated systems based on spin-charge separation and charge current-current coupling scenario. For intermediate coupling strength, we further proposed to use a trilinear term as phenomenological theory to explain the novel mechanism of emergent d+id/p+ip topological superconductivity in Hubbard/tJ model on honeycomb lattice. (c) Based on the physical picture of skymion condensation, we further proposed an effective quantum field theory description for the potential non-Fermi liquid phase arising at large but finite U. We also found some preliminary numerical evidence for the emergence of deconfined quantum criticality around 10% doping where anti-ferromagnetic order vanishes in honeycomb lattice Hubbard/tJ model (d) We predict that the doped InV_{1/3}Cu_{2/3}O_3 would be a potential candidate to realize the honeycomb lattice Hubbard/tJ model and our experimental collaborators have already made some samples on this material. We expect that a d+id or p+ip topological superconductivity will be discovered in this material very soon. (e) Very recently, we further discover that in interacting fermion systems, there exists a new class of the so-called anomalous symmetry protected topological (ASPT) states which are only well defined on the boundary of a trivial fermionic bulk system. This new discovery also opens a new door towards experimental realization p+ip topological superconductivity on the surface of 3D strongly correlated electron material.

24301516.label: Major findings and research outcome
24301516.value: Very recently, the research field of p+ip topological superconductor and topological Majorana zero modes are rapidly growing and there is an urgent need for new proposals to realize p+ip topological superconductors. However, the real challenge is to find a generic and robust way to make p+ip topological superconductors in a large class of 2D solid state materials, just like we realize BCS superconductor, high-Tc superconductor and iron-based superconductor. In this research project, we first simulated the global phase diagram of honeycomb lattice Hubbard/tJ model based on the state-of-the art Grassmann tensor network renormalization algorithm. We discover a p+ip topological superconductivity ground state in the strong coupling limit and a d+id/p+ip coexistence phase in the intermediate coupling region. We further propose to use the spin-charge separation and charge current-current coupling scenario, together with a phenomenological theory based on a trilinear term to understand the emergence of p+ip topological superconductivity in such a strongly correlated systems. We further discovered a potential non-Fermi liquid in the phase diagram and developed a effective field theory to understand such a non-Fermi liquid. Finally, we also discover that in interacting fermion systems, there exists a new class of the so-called anomalous symmetry protected topological (ASPT) states which are only well defined on the boundary of a trivial fermionic bulk system. Such a discovery shed new light on the realization of p+ip topological superconductivity on the surface of a 3D bulk of strongly correlated electron systems. Our experimental collaborators have also successively made some strongly correlated electron material based on our discovery.

24301516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24301516.value: In the future, we expect two major directions: (a) Develop an effective field theory to understand the deconfined quantum criticality in honeycomb lattice Hubbard/tJ model. (b) Experimental realization of p+ip topological superconductivity in both 2D strongly correlated electron material and surface of 3D strongly correlated electron material.

24301516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24301516.value: In the past few years, the possible realization of p+ip topological superconductor and topological Majorana zero mode has become a very important subject both theoretically and experimentally. In this project, we propose a completely new way on the realization of p+ip topological superconductors in strongly correlated electron systems. In particular, we obtain the global phase diagram of Hubbard/tJ model on honeycomb lattice based on the state-of-the-art Grassmann tensor network renormalization algorithm. We also proposed to use the spin-charge separation and charge current-current coupling scenario to explain the emergence of p+ip superconducitivity in the strong coupling limit and proposed to use a trilinear term as phenomenological theory to explain the novel mechanism of emergent d+id/p+ip topological superconductivity with intermediate coupling strength. Based on the physical picture of skymion condensation, we further proposed an effective quantum field theory description for the potential non-Fermi liquid phase arising at large but finite U. Regarding experimental realization, we also proposed two scenario based on purely 2D strongly correlated electron material and surface of 3D strongly correlated electron material.

24500416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24500416.value: The low cost of labor has been an important driver of the Chinese economy over the last 40 years. Yet, can the Chinese economy continue to grow with the rising cost of labor? The answer depends on whether the country can increase its labor productivity. In particular, we examine whether policy aimed at substantially increasing rates of post-secondary education can boost the labor productivity of a country. Macro-economists have used cross-country comparisons to argue that a nation's ability to increase per capita income is strongly related to its education level. A cross-country comparison, however, does not reveal the causal impact of human capital investment policy. To evaluate how the expansion of post-secondary education affects aggregated labor productivity, we use the college expansion at city level in China as the source of identification. The scale of this college expansion is unique to China (to our knowledge, the only other example is that of Israel, where expansion has developed at a less rapid but steady pace since the 1990s). In this project, we develop an aggregated human-capital framework and separate the total impact of college expansion into three channels: (1) the externality induced by the human capital investment; (2) the price effect due to the supply surge of human capital; (3) the change in human capital stock in the economy due to college expansion. By combining data on worker's wage (Urban Household Survey), firm level production data (National Economic Census), and city-level GDP data, we can estimate the importance of each channel. For the first channel, we apply the model of human capital spill-over to estimate the externality of human capital. For the second, we use firm-level economic census data to estimate the aggregated production function, with labor and human capital as separate factors. To estimate selection-corrected human capital accumulation, we use the residual accounting method to calibrate sorting in college attendance, which is the first attempt to consider heterogeneous return to education in an aggregated human-capital framework. 人力資本投資是經濟增長的源泉。雖然經典的經濟增長模型（Lucas,1988）很早就提出這個理論，但是相關的宏觀實證研究還停留在國際比較的層面（見Romer，1990; Benhabib & Spiegel，1994; Barro & Lee，1994; Gregorio & Lee， 2002; Barro et al. 2013) 。人力資本投資對內生性增長的因果效應需要比國際比較更微觀的數據支持。本項目利用中國在1999年開始大規模的高校擴招作為自然實驗，通過比較城市間在大學擴招前後的經濟增長趨勢來估計人力資本投資對經濟增長的因果效應。此外，本項目還估計出中國勞動力的邊際生產率和人力資本的外部性。這些研究結果將對中國乃至世界的勞動力市場政策將起到重要的指導作用。

24500516.label: Project Objectives
24500516.value: Develop an overlapping generations model in which economic agents make education and career choices. The model allows for two types of intergenerational transfer, including ability transfer and money transfer. The model will incorporate three major mechanisms in entrepreneurship: ability endowment, education attainment, and capital accumulation. These factors also affect the performance of an entrepreneur and lead to different business paths (incorporated business versus unincorporated business). We also plan to extend the model to allow individuals to learn about their entrepreneurship ability through education and parents' entrepreneur experience. Establish the intergenerational mobility pattern on education, career and earnings, using one of the most widely used data sources for studying intergenerational transmission process - the Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID). This data set allows us to link individuals with their parents so that we can examine the impact of parents' careers, income and family transfer on the child's decision to pursue, and success in, entrepreneurship. We also obtain the restricted access education data, which contains information on the school that the respondent attended. Therefore, we are able to examine the impact of different types of college on career decisions. Calibrate the model and use the model to understand the mechanisms behind the decision and performance of entrepreneurship and analyze the importance of each of the following channels: human capital transfer and monetary transfer from parents, and the impact of attending different types of college. We will use the model to predict individuals' career choices after we shut down these three channels one by one. Evaluate the effectiveness of policies that aim to encourage entrepreneurship. Counterfactual experiments include providing government loans to entrepreneurs to reduce their borrowing constraint, and offering student loans or direct subsidies for elite-college students. We will analyze the impact on the number of entrepreneurs and the success of their businesses, as well as the impact on intergenerational mobility in earnings.

24500516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24500516.value: Aim To create and use a model to quantify the contribution of different factors in people’s decisions to become entrepreneurs, and in their success as entrepreneurs, and to use that model further to develop policy guidance for the encouragement of successful entrepreneurship. Background It is increasingly recognized that entrepreneurs play a vital role in making economies successful, but too little is known about how they are generated. Research to date has established that parents play a major role in determining who becomes an entrepreneur and who does not, but not enough is known about the importance of the different factors in play – inherited ability, exposure to entrepreneurial activity as a child, encouragement by parents, financial support; and even less is known about the influence of different types of education. This project aims to start filling those gaps. Moreover, most of the previous studies did not distinguish between two types of entrepreneurship: owning an incorporated business and owning an unincorporated business. The two types entrepreneurs (incorporated vs. unincorporated) have a distinct combination of demographic and family traits, and the former type earns much more than the later. Therefore, the second contribution of this project is to understand the importance of the above factors on shaping an incorporated entrepreneur. Project Description The project will develop an overlapping generations model in which individual agents inherit different abilities from parents, receive different amounts of parental support, and make education and career choices. The model will draw on the existing research in these areas, as well as a large public dataset from the USA, to enable the creation of appropriate algorithms. Policy experiments will then be run on the model to elucidate and measure the relative importance of different factors in people’s education and career choices, and in their degree of success. Further experiments will be run to provide guidance on the likely effectiveness of different policy prescriptions in generating more, and more successful, entrepreneurs. Significance of Project This project will add greatly to the understanding of a subject of critical importance to economies in general and Hong Kong in particular, as an economic unit highly dependent on commerce. It will also generate information which can guide policy makers in the best ways to use public resources to encourage the emergence of successful entrepreneurs in the future, thus improving the economy of Hong Kong and the wellbeing of its people. 研究目標 建立並且運用一個模型來量化不同機制對於人們選擇成為企業家以及是否成功的影響，並且運用這個模型來提供培養成功企業家的政策指導。 研究背景 企業家在經濟發展中的作用不斷顯現，但是我們對於企業家是如何培養的卻所知甚少。現有研究發現父母在孩子的職業選擇中起到了重要作用，但是少有研究是關於不同渠道的相對重要性。這些渠道包括：從父母處繼承的能力，孩提時期的創業經歷，來自父母的鼓勵，經濟援助，以及不同教育類型的影響。這個項目致力於回答這些問題。並且，大部分之前的研究沒有區分兩種企業家：創立股份有限公司和創立非股份有限公司。這兩種企業家有截然不同的人口和家庭特徵，前者的收入遠高於後者。這個項目的第二個貢獻在於研究以上因素對成就一個創立股份有限公司的企業家的重要性。 研究描述 這個項目會建立一個世代交替模型，在模型中人們從父母繼承不同的能力，收到不同的來自父母的經濟支持，並且進行教育和職業的選擇。本研究是對該領域文獻的拓展，並且使用了一個美國的大型數據。運用這個數據估計的經濟模型，將會用來進行模擬政策實驗，來分析和量化人們教育和職業選擇中不同影響因子的相對重要性。我們還會進行更多的模擬實驗，來為培養更多成功企業家提供政策指導。 研究的重要性 由於創業在經濟中的重要性，該項目會增加我們對於經濟發展，特別是香港的進一步了解。另外，它還能更好地指導政策制定者更好地運用公共資源來鼓勵更多未來成功的創業，使之促進香港的經濟發展和人民的福祉。

24500516.label: Realisation of objectives
24500516.value: I have achieved all the project objectives. We study the effects of attending an elite college on entrepreneurship decisions and career dynamics. We first document that having an elite college degree is positively correlated with entrepreneurship (i.e., owning an incorporated business) but not with other self-employment (i.e., owning an unincorporated business). We then develop an overlapping generations model which captures the self-selection in education and career choices based on heterogeneous ability and family wealth endowments. Our estimates show that different career paths (employee, entrepreneur, and other self-employed) demand different types of human capital (employee, incorporated, and unincorporated human capital) and elite colleges improve these three types of human capital more than ordinary colleges. Our counterfactual experiment finds that shutting down elite colleges reduces the number of entrepreneurs but has little impact on other self-employed individuals. Providing subsidies to elite colleges is more efficient than giving grants to non-elite colleges in encouraging entrepreneurship, improving intergenerational mobility, and increasing welfare.

I will make use of the same data collected from the Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID) in this study with information on career choice and income, and will further collect information on asset holdings from the PSID. I want to analyze whether entrepreneurs are more or less likely to hold risky assets compared to employees.

24500516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24500516.value: In this paper, we study whether elite colleges matter and how they matter. We analyze the effect of elite college attendance on entrepreneurship decisions and career dynamics. We find that elite colleges contribute more to different kinds of human capital than non-elite colleges do, which in turn increases the chance that elite college graduates become entrepreneurs relative to non-elite college graduates. However, the elite college premium is negative, meaning that the tuition for elite colleges is too high to justify the benefits. Our paper also suggests that elite colleges are important engines for producing successful entrepreneurs but that high tuition and borrowing constraints prevent some would-be entrepreneurs from attending an elite college.

24502216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24502216.value: Historical migration has a long-term positive impact on the receiving economy since migrants can be carriers of talents, knowledge, human capital, and even institutions. But, its potential costs are also fairly evident. In pre-modern period, migrants needed to fight with natives over resources in order to prevent the extinction of their linkage. Such kind of competition could raise mistrust, reduce cooperation, and thus adversely affect economic performance. Against this background, I seek to argue that the `dark side’ of migration could have a beneficial effect on economic development: migrants could either invest in the quantity (family size) or the quality (human capital) of their children to maximize the probability of the family’s long-term survival. When human capital rather than family size is more useful in the fight over resources, the migrants tend to invest more in quality rather than quantity. The increase in the level of human capital might be persistent, and thus historical migrants could impact today’s economic prosperity. This was the case in late imperial China, when the civil exam became the primary method of recruiting government officials. I attempt to identify such effect by focusing on the latest and largest wave of southward migration of the Han Chinese, which took place during 1127–30 and was caused by the abrupt demise of the Northern Song Dynasty in 1127. During this short period (1127–30), around 5 million people fled from the north to the south. By constructing a prefecture-level dataset and exploiting the spatial variation in the settlement of migrants, I propose to examine the effect of migration: (a) on population density to identify its quantity effect, (b) on the level of human capital to identify its quality effect, and (c) on today’s income to identify its long-term economic impact. I hypothesize that migration had a significant positive effect on population density initially, but its effect gradually decreased over time; while its effect on human capital was insignificantly during early period, but gradually increased when the civil exam became the primary channel of selecting government officials. Since migration had no effect on human capital during the early period, we can rule out the possibility that migrants were the carriers of human capital, which suggest that competition could be the possible channel of the beneficial effect of migration. It is a historical study, but it can help us understand the interaction between migrants and natives in today's society. 移民能夠帶來新的資本、知識、文化與制度，從而促進經濟發展。然而，與本地居民之間的競爭也不可避免。這種競爭會降低社會的信任程度，阻礙社會協作，對經濟發展產生不利影響。 這一負面因素，在某些情況下，卻可稱為經濟發展的催化劑。例如，在前現代中國，外來移民需要與本地居民競爭資源。為了延續族群，一個家庭可以增加子女的數量，也可以提高子女的品質。但兩者之間存在一個權衡。當子女的數量或者家庭的規模作用更大時，父母會增加生育，對一個地區而言，人口規模會隨之增大；而子女品質的作用更大時，父母更多地投資於子女教育，從而地區人力資本水準會相應提高。在第二種情況下，移民和與之而來的競爭會提高這一地區的人力資本。由於人力資本的延續性，歷史上的移民可以長遠地影響今天的經濟發展水準。 中國歷史上大規模的人口遷移可以幫助我們驗證這一假說。源于中國北方的漢人，過去2000年曾經三次大規模地向南遷移。最近一次發生在1127年到1130年。由於北宋滅亡，五百萬北方漢人在短短四年間遷移定居到中國南方。 我們基於歷史記錄，可以構建一個市（府）級數據，來描述北方移民的地理分佈，識別其對人口密度和人力資本的作用，並且估計其對當前經濟發展水準的影響。從而可以驗證以下假說：第一，移民在早期顯著提高了人口密度，但是這一影響隨著時間而逐漸衰減；第二，於此相反，在早期，對人力資本沒有顯著影響。但是，由於明清時期採用科舉制選拔官員，這提高了教育的回報。自此之後，移民較多的地區，人力資本水準逐步提高；第三，對人力資本的影響延續到今天，進而提高了這一地區現在的經濟發展與收入水準。 在全球化的今天，移民對政治、經濟與文化產生了深刻影響。雖然本研究基於歷史資料，但卻有助於我們思考這一現實問題。

24502216.label: Realisation of objectives
24502216.value: All objectives have been fully realized. 1. To examine the effect of migration on the quantity of population over time during historical period (across at least one thousand years, during 960-2000). (1) The PI has constructed a panel database, which includes the number of population or households at the prefecture level in 741, 1080, 1102, 1290, 1391, 1776, 1820, 1851, 1880, 1910 and 2000. I take the log term of the number of households/populations per squared kilometer to measure the population density during different historical periods. (2) The results show that the effect of migration on the quantity of population decreases over time when China adopted civil exam as the primary channel of selecting government officials, which supports the hypothesis listed in the proposal. 2. To examine the effect of migration on the level of human capital over time during historical period (across at least one thousand years, during 960-2000) (1) The PI has constructed a panel database, which employs the number of successful candidates in the higher level Imperial Civil Service Exam (known as “Jinshi” or “Presented Scholars”) of each prefecture normalized by population as a proxy for educational level during Ming and Qing dynasties (1368-1910). Based on China’s population census data in 2000 and 2005, the PI has calculated “the percentage of the population that was educated to the level of high school or above” and “average schooling year” as the pertinent proxies of today’s education. (2) empirically that the migrant effect on human capital is statistically similar to zero during the early period after migration (e.g., during the Southern Song period, 1127-1279) but gradually increases and turns significant during the Ming and Qing dynasties (1368-1904) when the civil service examination became the primary channel for selecting government officials. 3. To identify the effect migration on today’s economic prosperity (1) The PI has constructed a cross-sectional database, which employs both GDP and nighttime lights per capita in the year 2000 as proxies for contemporary development,. (2) The PI finds that southward migrants have indeed had a positive long-term effect on today’s economic prosperity, even though the inclusion of controls for a wide range of variables (e.g., geography, initial economic conditions, the impacts of Sino-nomadic warfare, and crop suitability) moves the migrant coefficients toward zero. (3) The PI addresses the potential endogeneity issues associated with migrant settlement by employing the number of northern-born officials governing in southern prefectures during the migration period as an instrumental variable based on the assumption that the network effect would lead prefectures governed by northern-born officials to receive more migrants. The effect of historic immigration on contemporary development remains significantly positive. 4. To identify whether education is the main channel of the effect of migration on today’s economic prosperity (1) The PI assesses the extent to which the migrant effect on economic prosperity occurs via human capital (led by migrant-local competition), showing not only that educational level has a large and significant correlation with economic prosperity but that once education is controlled for, this significant migration effect disappears. (2) To verify that the main effect of historical migrants comes through education, the PI also estimates the instrumented effect of migrant population size on economic prosperity while accounting for education’s endogeneity by restricting its effect only to consistent estimates. After bounding the range of the estimated economic returns to education to 40 percent below and above their OLS estimates, the results show that migrants cease to be associated with economic prosperity net of the human capital effect, which suggests that most of migrations’ positive effects come from education. 5. To examine the effect of migration on other socio-economic outcomes (1) The PI directly tests the effect on other socio-economic outcomes, including the level of (cultural) diversity as measured by an ethnolinguistic fragmentation (ELF) index. The results confirm that migrants do indeed increase cultural diversity.

24502216.label: Major findings and research outcome
24502216.value: This project finds that the 1127–30 Han migration indeed had a positive long-term effect on today’s economic prosperity of the host region. I address the potential endogeneity issues associated with migrant settlement by employing the number of northern-born officials governing in southern prefectures during the migration period as an instrumental , and find that the effect of historic immigration on contemporary development remains significantly positive. (Object 3) I hypothesize that the link between historic migration and today’s economic prosperity could be explained by the migrant-local competition under the civil examination system, which induced both groups to make more investment in human capital (the “competition hypothesis”), it is possible that migrants may carry and diffuse advanced technology or human capital to the host region (the “diffusion hypothesis”). I test the auxiliary predictions of the two competing hypotheses (competition vs. diffusion), which provides strong support for the local-competition channel. First, using the ratio of successful examination candidates (Jinshi) to population as a measure of human capital in each prefecture, I show empirically that the migrant effect on human capital is statistically similar to zero during the early period after migration (e.g., during the Southern Song period, 1127-1279) but gradually increases and turns significant during the Ming and Qing dynasties (1368-1904) when the civil service examination became the primary channel for selecting government officials (Object 2). Conversely, the migrant effect on population density decreases over time (Object 1). These observations invalidate the carrier hypothesis, which predicts a higher educational level in the regions with more migrants during the early periods after migration. I then assess the extent to which the migrant effect on economic prosperity occurs via human capital (led by migrant-local competition), showing not only that educational level has a large and significant correlation with economic prosperity but that once education is controlled for, this significant migration effect disappears. Moreover, I find that migrants cease to be associated with economic prosperity net of the human capital effect, which suggests that most of migrations’ positive effects come from education (Object 4). As a final step, I directly test other channels, including the level of (cultural) diversity as measured by an ethnolinguistic fragmentation (ELF) index. Although the results confirm that migrants do indeed increase cultural diversity (Object 5), inclusion of the index cannot explain migration’s positive impact on today’s economic development.

24502216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24502216.value: Neo-Confucianism is a philosophy or a religion predominated in the intellectual and spiritual life of East Asia prior to the modern period. We seek to argue that the historical formation of Neo-Confucian culture in China was caused by the Jurchen’s defeat of Han Chinese (culminated in the demise of the Northern Song dynasty, circa 960-1127)—a shock that resulted in 5 million people migrating from north to south China. Using the migration information (which I have gathered from this research project) and employing a DID setting of a panel of 292 prefectures during 220 BC – 1820 AD, we could test whether competition for survival between the two groups is positively correlated with the rise of Neo-Confucianism; the latter measured by the magnitude of purity steles conferred upon the so-called “chaste women”—women who for the sake of demonstrating fidelity to their deceased husbands wowed not to remarry or even committed suicide. The possible channel might be that the competition for survival between the natives and migrants make them value more on the loyalty to the family, and began to demand such type of philosophy.

24502216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24502216.value: Historical migration has a long-term positive impact on the receiving economy since migrants can be carriers of talents, knowledge, human capital, and even institutions, however, its potential costs are also fairly evident: immigrants introduce intense competition between themselves and regional natives, which can generate social and political problems. Against this background, I seek to argue that the `dark side’ of migration could have a beneficial effect on economic development, if the competition between locals and migrants is based on human capital and thus capable of incentivizing both groups to invest more in human capital to better compete with their rivals. Using data systematically collected from historical records, I show that the 1127–30 Han migration southward in historic China had a significantly positive effect on economic prosperity in the year 2000 (as measured by GDP and nighttime lights per capita) and that around 90 percent of this effect came via human capital. One possible explanation is that, rather than migrants carrying and diffusing human capital to the host region, the competition between migrants and locals since the implementation of the imperial civil service examination has incentivized both migrants and locals to invest in education to better compete with their rivals.

24503016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24503016.value: This project aims to understand the network structure of prime brokers and hedge funds, and its implications to asset prices and financial stability. Both anecdotal evidence and the theoretic literature suggest that the network structure of financial institutions can serve as an amplification mechanism that propagates a moderate, institution-level liquidity shock into a market-wide crisis. Finding systematic evidence to the hypothesis, however, remains a challenge, because of the lack of data that could fully describe the network of major financial institutions in certain asset market. This project tries to fill the gap by focusing on the financial network of hedge funds and prime brokers and linking it to the public equity market. Hedge funds are active players in equity markets and prime brokers are their key counterparties. Two hedge funds can be linked with each other through some channels such as common stock holdings and the usage of the same prime broker. Liquidity shock can travel and propagate through these linkages. By hand collecting the key information from newly available SEC filings by hedge funds, this project can quantitatively describe the network architecture of hedge funds and brokers. For its main empirical analyses, this project will first try to demonstrate some basic and important characteristics of financial network, such as the distribution of linkages. Next, the project will use the standard methodology in the network literature to measure how central a hedge fund or broker is in this financial network, namely the centrality measure. According the literature, institutions with high centrality play the key role during the propagation process, and therefore are more subject to large shocks. Then, I will link hedge funds’ centrality to the price of stocks they hold. The main testable hypothesis is that stocks held by funds with high centrality are prone to crashes in prices. I hope this project to be the first one that empirically examines how the network structure of financial institutions influences asset prices.

24504416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24504416.value: 在信息系統領域，近期有很多行為學研究加深了我們對於新科技使用行為的理解。這些研究中的關鍵是，用戶在初期接受科技時的行為與後期使用它的行為是不同的。出於提高信息科技接受度的目的，我們需要用戶接受並且持續不斷使用該技術。接受科技初期與後期使用科技之間的行為差異成為了公司要考慮的實際問題，公司需要根據用戶的實際情況來傳播新的科技。 出於這個考慮，我們的目標是建立一個模型，使用初期使用者的顯示出的偏好，預測他們後期使用情況。我們根據用戶的初期使用模式，預測其後期對該技術持續使用頻率及強度。由於信息技術作為一種體驗性的產品，用戶在剛接觸它時無法確定其好壞，需要在後續使用過程中才能確定。這是因為科技的價值不只體現在科技本身，還取決於用戶與技術之間的配合度。當用戶親身體驗新技術時，他們才可以對此技術的優劣有全面的評估，這個評估將反映到他們早期的使用模式上。總之，用戶對於新技術的早期使用模式中包含了很多有用的信息，比如用戶的偏好和他們對於技術的認同度。使用這些信息，我們可以提出一個模型來預測他們的之後對此技術使用情況。 具體而言，使用大量的移動應用程序下載和使用數據，我們提出一個模型來預測應用程序的後續使用頻率和使用強度，并用實證方法驗證了模型的有效。我們關注應用程序下載後的早期使用情況，如首次使用時間，第二次使用時間和重訪時間，並證明這些信息對於預測應用程序後續使用情況非常重要。另外，我們的模型還考慮了用戶群體和不同應用之間的差異性。 這項研究不僅對研究人員也對從業者具有重要意義。雖然很多研究指出科技在被接受初期和後期用戶的使用行為有差異，但很少有研究能夠從初期使用者的行為中辨別出後期持續活躍用戶。由於不是所有接受了新科技的用戶之後都會成為活躍用戶，所以分辨潛在活躍用戶至關重要，特別是在他們使用技術的早期階段。通過識別用戶，企業可以把更多的資源投放在可能持續活躍的用戶上，並且對於可能流失的客戶採取跟進措施，例如定期推薦產品給他們。

24504516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24504516.value: “Pay to play” in public pension funds refers to the practices of making political contributions or related payments to the government officials in charge of selecting the investment advisers of public pension funds to win the advisory business (S.E.C. 2010). This exercise, caused by the governance problem in public pension plans, distorts the selection process of investment managers and hence may harm pension plans and their beneficiaries. Following the notorious “pay to play” scandals, the Securities and Exchange Commission (S.E.C.) adopted so-called the “pay to play rule” on June 30, 2010 to restrain these practices and foster fair competition. Main element of the rule prohibits investment managers from providing compensatory advisory services to public pension funds for two years following a political contribution by the firm (or certain of its executives) to the government officials in a position to influence the management of these funds. This paper investigates whether the newly adopted “pay to play rule” is effective in reducing the political influence on public pension funds and how it affects the management of public pension assets. Specifically, this study focuses on the rule’s influence on investment portfolio and the rate of return of public pension funds. The findings will provide implications not only to the regulators in evaluating the effectiveness of the rule but also to the millions of public pension fund beneficiaries and taxpayers who could suffer from the political exploitation of public pension assets. This paper will also contribute to the governance of public pension fund literature by providing the evidence of the regulatory role in improving pension fund governance. 美國公共養老基金中的“pay to play（付費玩）”現象，是指投資咨詢公司向相關政府官員提供政治獻金，以獲得能夠在公共養老基金管理中操縱投資顧問的選擇，並贏得咨詢業務的行為（美國證券交易委員會S.E.C.，2010）。這壹現象表明，公共養老基金的管理當中存在較為嚴重的治理問題，投資經理的選擇過程可能會被操縱及扭曲，繼而損害養老金計劃及其受益者的權益。由於臭名昭著的“付費玩”醜聞影響較為嚴重，美國證券交易委員會（S.E.C.）在2010年6月10日通過了“pay to play rules（付費玩規則）”，以抑制這些操縱養老金管理的做法並促進公平競爭。這壹規則的最主要內容是：當壹家公司（或者其高管）向那些能夠影響養老基金管理的政府官員提供了政治獻金時，其投資經理會被禁止在兩年內向公共養老金計劃提供有償咨詢服務。本文研究這壹最近通過並執行的“付費玩規則”是否能夠有效降低施加於公共養老基金計劃的政治幹預影響，以及這壹規則如何影響公共養老基金資產的管理。本文尤其關註這壹規則如何影響公共養老基金管理中的投資組合以及回報率的問題。本研究的意義在於：本文不僅能夠為評價這壹規則的有效性提供指引；也能夠為那些可能由於公共養老金的政治掠奪而受到影響的成百萬公共養老金受益人和納稅人提供指引。另外，本文提供了實證證據以幫助改進公共養老基金治理的問題，是對現有關於公共養老金治理文獻重要補充。

24601416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24601416.value: Aim This project is the first attempt to assess the impacts of the new choice-of-law regime of China on international contracts since the new choice-of-law statute came into force in 2011. Project Background The Law on the Application of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Legal Relationships (New Law) came into force on 1 April, 2011. Its stated goals are to “clarify the application of laws concerning foreign-related civil relations” (Certainty), “reasonably solve foreign-related civil disputes” (Reasonableness) and “safeguard the legal rights and interests of parties” (Parties’ Rights). Should these goals be achieved, the New Law shall make Chinese courts more popular for international commercial disputes. However, official data show that the percentage of foreign-related disputes has actually declined for each of the years since 2011. This project will investigate the reasons behind this anomaly, particularly testing the thesis whether it is due to the uncertainty of the “closest connections” test. Brief Project Description This project involves three separate but related surveys. A primary survey will be conducted on all the foreign-related contract cases decided by Chinese courts in the ten-year period between 1 January 2008 and 31 December 2017, covering both the past (2008-2010) and the present (2011-2017) regimes. Since the primary survey is to be based on court cases, it will not cover cases that have gone through arbitration or settlement and other practical perspectives. Two supplementary surveys will be conducted to collect non-court data. The first will be through interviewing leading Chinese legal practitioners, while the second will be by surveying the dispute resolution clauses of international contracts of Chinese listed companies. To assess the viability of the primary survey, a preliminary survey covering the six-month period between 1 January 2012 and 30 June 2012 was conducted (Preliminary Research). This Preliminary Research shows that the New Law’s problem might lie in the vagueness of the “closest connections” test which in turn causes an unusually low number of cases applying foreign laws (only nine during the six-month period). This project will test this thesis and suggest new guidelines for improvement of the regime. Significance of the Project A good dispute resolution system is essential to international transactions and a fair choice-of-law regime is a mainstay thereof. This project serves the dual purposes of finding the New Regime’s problems and suggesting guidelines by utilizing empirical data. It will contribute to the healthy developments of dispute resolutions of both of China and Hong Kong, her largest trading partner.

24601416.label: Realisation of objectives
24601416.value: 1. Objective One (To test whether the New Law suffers from vagueness of “closest connection” test): this objective was fully achieved by the review of 15,266 cases decided by Chinese courts between 8-8-2007 and 31-12-2018 (“Empirical Research”). The database “Bei Da Fa Bao” was first utilized to identify relevant cases involving foreign-related contracts. This process produced 112,222 “raw cases”. These cases were then each reviewed for relevance for choice of law, resulting in 15,266 relevant cases. During the review process, relevant data from each of these relevant cases were collected in spreadsheet. They were eventually analyzed by the PI (note that the ECS proposal originally set 31-12-2017 as the end date of the survey period. However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it took longer than usual for the submission process of the publications. The PI therefore conducted additional review of the 2018 cases (2,832 cases) himself so as to make the research more up-to-date). More specifically regarding the “closest connection” test, it was found that more than half of the relevant cases (8,434) were decided under the closest connection test, i.e. did not involve a choice by the parties, and that only 50 such cases (0.59%) applied foreign law (see Table 4 of Publication 2). Thus, China clearly suffered from a “homeward trend” towards the application of Chinese law by Chinese courts in its “closest connection” approach. The vagueness of new law (i.e. the Act on the Application of Laws over Foreign-related Civil Relationships) was clearly the main reason of how the Chinese judges could achieve the homeward trend. This was established by collecting data on the factors considered by the Chinese courts in the cases. Of the 8,434 cases, the court cited at least a factor in 6,296 cases while conducting closest connection analysis. In total, 9,650 factors were considered, but only 328 factors that were cited are foreign-related. On average, courts only cited 0.05 foreign factor in a case (see Table 8 of Publication 2). Thus, the “homeward trend” was achieved by this “cherry picking” exercise by Chinese courts of only China-related factors. They can do this because (1) the new law does not have a mandate on which factors the court needs to consider; (2) Article 41 of the new law literally (and wrongly) provides that the courts can choose between closest connection and characteristic performance (which imposes rebuttable presumption on applicable law). As a result, only 544 of the 7,890 applied characteristic performance (see Table 9 of Publication 2); (3) Article 2 of the new law also allows courts to apply Contract Law, Maritime Law and General Principles of Civil Law in lieu of the new Act. None of these laws contains provision regarding characteristic performance, thus allowing the courts to bypass the test. The new act was only cited in 66.79% in closest connection cases (see Table 10). 2. Objective Two (To suggest improvements to the New Law): this objective was fully achieved by the Empirical Research. Having regard to the findings referred to in Objective One, China suffers from the blackletter law being disjoined from the actual judicial practice. The PI therefore suggested that China should either: (1) amend the law by a new Supreme People’s Court Interpretation to provide for a mandatory application of characteristic performance and/or a mandatory laundry list of factors (including foreign related factors) to be considered by Chinese courts in their application of the closest connection test, thereby changing the future practice of the courts to align with the current law; or (2) amend the law such that the default law to be applied but for parties' choice is Chinese law, thereby aligning the law with the current practice (see Part V.4 of Publication 2). 3. Objective Three (To provide empirical data for future study): this objective was fully achieved by the Empirical Research. To the knowledge of the PI, the Empirical Research is the largest empirical research conducted on the choice of law practice in China. It covers plenty of data on the choice of law practice of China. For example, apart from the closest connection cases, it also covers the choice of law practice in cases where parties have made a choice (see Tables 4, 5, 6, 7 of Publication 2). There is also general information regarding the breakdowns for years, provinces, size of judgment and lawyer’s fees. All these will not only be beneficial for future studies on Chinese choice of law, but choice of law by scholars around the world given the international nature of private international law. 4. Objective Four (To serve as a practical guideline for practitioners in drafting foreign-related contracts): this objective was fully achieved by the Empirical Research, interviews with practitioners, and review of material contracts of listed companies. It is clear from the empirical findings that the inclusion of an express governing law clause designating a foreign law offers the best chance for Chinese court to apply foreign law (see Table 7). This is confirmed by Chinese practitioners interviewed by the PI as well as the consistent inclusion of Hong Kong governing law clause in material contracts of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong. Accordingly, the conventional wisdom of including an express governing law clause is proven to be correct. 5. Objective Five (To facilitate Hong Kong courts in making China-related conflict-of-laws decisions): this objective was fully achieved by the Empirical Research. As the Empirical Research has identified a clear “homeward trend” in the application of Chinese law (98.35% of all cases applied Chinese law, see Table 1 of Publication 2), that can facilitate Hong Kong court in making decision on forum non conveniens, the decline of Hong Kong courts’ jurisdiction in favor of the alternative forum (here, the Chinese court). In making such decision, Hong Kong court will now know that if it decline jurisdiction in a particular contract case in favor of a Chinese court, it is most likely that Chinese court will apply Chinese law on the matter, regardless of other connecting factor save perhaps for an express governing law clause. In other words, Hong Kong courts will now be fully aware of forum shopping motive of litigants (going to Chinese courts means getting Chinese substantive law to apply). In addition, a specific empirical research has been conducted on the choice of law regarding limitation period and forum non conveniens in Hong Kong courts, see Parts III, IV and V of Publication 3. 6. Objective Six (To observe the extent of judicial involvement in the development of Chinese law): this objective was fully achieved by the Empirical Research. The whole Empirical Research reflects on the importance of judiciary in the development of Chinese law. As the research traces the development of the law since 2007 (across both the old and new regimes), it is clearly seen that Chinese courts always found a way to apply the lex fori, Chinese law (see Table 2 of Publication 2). This is so regardless of what the law literally provides, both in terms of its official goals (such as reasonableness and protection of private interests), and its operation articles (such as characteristic performance). It is expected that they will continue to have such influence in the future development of the law.

24601416.label: Major findings and research outcome
24601416.value: The Empirical Research provides numerous major findings on the choice of law practices of Chinese courts. The major findings are set out below: 1. China has a clear “homeward trend” in applying Chinese law in foreign related contract cases. Cases that applied Chinese law account for 98.35% of the all reviewed cases. This homeward trend is the same (1) whether under the old or new regime and (2) throughout the survey period. See Tables 1 & 2 and related section in Publication 2. 2. Among foreign laws applied, more than half are Hong Kong law. See Table 3. 3. The choice of law basis most utilized by Chinese courts was “closest connection”, accounting for more than half of the relevant cases (8,434). See Table 4 of Publication 2. 4. Cases with parties’ choice have a slightly higher foreign application rate (2.76%), see Table 5 of Publication 2. 5. Express choice of law clauses designating foreign law as governing law has the best chance to get Chinese courts to apply foreign law, see Tables 6 and 7 of Publication 2. 6. In applying the closest connection test, Chinese courts consistently conducted “cherry picking” of Chinese related factors. See Table 8 of Publication 2. 7. They were able to do so by applying the characteristic performance test and the new law arbitrarily. See Tables 9 and 10. 8. There is no evidence that the homeward trend is attributable to lack of training of Chinese judges. See Table 11. 9. Rather, given that disputes going to Chinese courts are generally small disputes, it does not make sense in most cases for costly and sophisticated choice of law analysis be conducted. The low-cost dispute resolution is a strength of Chinese courts. See Table 12-13. 10. The PI therefore suggested that China should either: (1) amend the law by a new Supreme People’s Court Interpretation to provide for a mandatory application of characteristic performance and/or a mandatory laundry list of factors (including foreign related factors) to be considered by Chinese courts in their application of the closest connection test, thereby changing the future practice of the courts to align with the current law; or (2) amend the law such that the default law to be applied but for parties' choice is Chinese law, thereby aligning the law with the current practice (see Part V.4 of Publication 2).

24601416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24601416.value: Of the three major private international law questions, i.e. jurisdiction, choice of law, and enforcement of foreign judgment, the PI has conducted and completed empirical research of the latter two in relation to China. The PI plans to apply for a new GRF funding to conduct empirical research on the last topic, jurisdiction. The new proposal will utilize similar research methodology to gather data from Chinese courts judicial decisions. The experience of managing the completed project will greatly facilitate the new project. In addition, while the research questions are different, the two projects will complement each other. For example, it will be interesting to see whether there is any correlation between the jurisdictional basis and choice of law basis applied by the courts. The new proposal will also be very timely given that the Hague Conference on Private International Law has recently restarted the Jurisdiction Project which aims at creating a new convention to harmonize the world’s conflicting jurisdictional practices. The PI has already prepared a proposal on jurisdiction that has been submitted to CUHK LAW to secure internal funding to conduct a feasibility research that will facilitate the preparation of the final proposal for the GRF in fall 2021.

24601416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24601416.value: One of the most important issues in international commercial litigation is which country’s law governs the dispute. It is often said that Chinese courts prefer to apply their own substantive law, the lex fori, over foreign law. This phenomenon is known as the “homeward trend” in conflict of laws which was widely attributed to courts’ arbitrary judicial practice. This project examines three issues: To what extent is there a “homeward trend” in China? If there is such “homeward trend,” what caused it? What should be done with the “homeward trend”? Through an empirical research conducted on 15,266 foreign-related contract cases between 2007 and 2018, this article found the answers as follows: First, with 98.35% of the surveyed cases ruled by the courts to be governed by Chinese law, the homeward trend is confirmed. Second, the law’s vagueness allows judges to apply Chinese law in most cases. Third, China can certainly change the law to rein in courts’ discretion. Alternatively, given the homeward trend fits the dispute resolution system of China and offers certainty to litigation, a viable alternative is to simply amend the statute so that it reflects the existing judicial practice.

24602516.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24602516.value: 中國審查/豐裕信息環境下的意義生成：反思性媒介使用所致的政治傾向變遷

24602516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24602516.value: 在政治管控嚴苛的權威體制中，對新媒体的使用如何能促進政治變遷？對此，大量研究的關注點放在使用信息科技來動員、組織政治抗爭與綫上行動。然而這些研究所聚焦的都是已對政權具有批判意識的反對派或個人。未被系統研究的是：在一個被霸權意識形態長期統領的社會，人民如何發展出與之相異的政治見地？ 中國是全球最強大的權威體制國家，並且被認爲擁有最大的網絡化媒介市場，因此是推進這一調研的最宜場所。近些年，中國歷經一系列族群動蕩、天然災害、北京奧運會以及全球經濟衰退，一種以“大國崛起”為内核的民族主義情緒在官方論述、大衆媒體和網絡上日漸鼎盛。與此同時，數量可觀的人群堅持著反民族主義的政治文化信念。本研究意圖關注這樣的另類意見是怎樣流行起來的。在這個過程中，中國互聯網的作用不再是服務于抗爭激進運動的工具（這是大量既有研究的重點），而是人們在上網實踐中價值觀得以變化的場域。 要解釋政治理念的變遷，本研究的落腳點是：人們對控制和審查所開展的種種具有反思性的互動。具體的研究問題： 1。中國網民如何看待他們所處的審查過的媒介環境？ 2。人們對媒介環境的特定理解如何影響他們的媒介使用模式？ 3。這樣的反思性媒介使用如何能促進另類政治理念的發生？ 本研究依賴多樣研究方法和數據。解答問題1包含細讀檔案（看有關信息控制的文化描述經歷過什麽歷史變遷）、網絡文本挖掘分析（普通網民如何討論媒介和審查）。基於對問題1的回應，解答問題2和3則需要口述史材料來研究人們一直以來有關媒介的想法、對各類媒介的使用、以及其背後的考量。 本研究最終回答的是：在政治管控嚴苛的權威體制中另類政治意見如何發生壯大。它將呈現批判性政治意識形成的路徑，以及在什麽樣的社會、政治、文化環境下，個體更易于重檢並調整他們已然形成的政治信念。更寬泛地，本研究理論化和實證化如下假設：人們對他們所處媒介環境的理解對他們的行爲有引導作用。研究發現將加深學界對人與媒體之前關係的理論化（尤其關於這一關係能夠怎樣影響個人思想的發展），因而對接受研究和政治傳播文獻有所貢獻。本研究所推進的理論框架適用於其他見證人口政治理念變遷的地域。此類研究需要研究者同時調查人們的媒介使用和媒介理念——這些在地流行的媒介理念都將不同于中國大陸網民的媒介理念，例如，它們所含有的焦慮感、自信感的源頭都可能不同。

24607916.value: 本項目之目的，乃以漢時期最重要的農業和軍事戰略物質—鐵—為研究對象，通過考古學的方法，理解漢帝國如何以鐵資料的控制為手段，管理新開拓的的南部邊境。本項目以綜合性的分析方法，考察廣州地區—即漢時期越人集團的大本營—漢墓所出土鐵器背後的生產和流通體系，借以判斷漢帝國在多大程度上控制鐵器的生產和流通體系，以達到對南部邊境和征服族群的有效管理。 漢帝國是當時整個東亞最強大的帝國，與歐亞大陸西端的羅馬帝國足可匹敵。但到底漢帝國如何將不同征服而來的邊境地域整合到帝國的系統中，目前的認識卻是眾訴紛紜。特別是南方和東南沿海一帶，由于出土文獻尤其稀缺，對于統治策略的認識更是一片空白。過往不少研究以為，漢帝國採用高壓政策，使各族群被迫接受較“高端”的漢文化。但正如其它研究漢朝和其它古代帝國的學者指出，這種基於文獻的看法，往往高估了古代帝國的統治能力，同時又看低了原來族群在與漢帝國政治角力中的能動性。對漢式器物系統的考古學研究，將從實際的角度，推進我們對漢帝國管治方式的認識，但在以往的文獻中如此重要的研究卻是少之又少。 要解決如此具爭議性的問題並填補學術空白，本項目提出用綜合性的方法，分析廣州地區漢墓出土的鐵器。方法包括: I. 金相分析，以判斷鐵器的技術，以及II. 統計分析，以找出鐵器的消費模式。儘答廣州地區是漢代南方邊境中墓葬的主要發現區，上述問題卻從來沒有過很好的分析。這些方法提供的資料，更可進一步回答以下宏觀的歷史問題：1) 到底這些鐵器是否根據中原的技術所製作；2)到底鐵器的消費是否僅限于特定的群體，而其流通是否又被國家所控制；3) 到底漢朝在111 BC 征服了這一區域後，鐵器的技術和流通是否出現了較大的年代區別? 鐵器的考古學分析可為上述問題提供前所未有的新資料，幫助我們由下而上檢視到底漢朝的控制能力有多強大。 本項目的最終結果，將在如下層面產生更大的影響力。首先，項目提供了第一手新資料，顯示鐵器技術如何傳播到嶺南地區，並說明新技術對鞏固漢朝的統治有多大的作用。其次，新分析的結果，有助于建構漢朝在南方統治的理論框架。最終，鐵器的考古學研究在更大層面上，將推動我們對早期帝國的擴張，族群互動和帝國管理方面的認識。

24607916.label: Realisation of objectives
24607916.value: For objectives #1 and #2, the PI realized these two objectives via conducting fieldworks in Guangzhou collecting iron samples from Han tombs that were excavated by the Guangzhou Municipal Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology. More than 100 pieces of iron samples were collected by the PI for metallurgical analysis. The correct identification of various types of iron manufacturing techniques is essential for achieving objective#1 and #2, but the differentiation of some techniques (e.g., bloomery iron and fined iron) is very difficult given the lack of the study of identification criteria before. Thus, the PI addressed this difficulty via studying iron objects from Guanzhong, Shaanxi, from which iron objects were usually made of cast iron technology, and examined various identification methods introduced in the literature, especially the multivariate statistical method developed by the research team in France. The study of identification criteria (output #6) not only helped the PI identified various manufacturing techniques represented by iron objects in Lingnan more confidently, but also provided a solid foundation for the PI to conduct a comparative study of the iron manufacturing techniques appeared in Lingnan (the southern peripheries of the Han empire) and Guanzhong (the core of the Han empire) (output #10). In addition, the PI also studied the potential origins of bloomery iron objects identified in Guangzhou based upon the chemical compositions of slag inclusions, but concluded that the bloomery iron objects were unlikely to be manufactured by any known production site in Lingnan. Since the PI argues that the appearance of cast iron or related technology was a key indicator of external supply in the research output (#10), the identification criteria developed by the PI laid down a strong foundation to achieve objectives #1 and 2. Even though the PI has to submit the manuscript about the analytical report to a disciplinary journal after the editorial polishing by a professional editor, the PI basically achieved the objectives #1 and 2 outlined in the proposal. For objectives #3, 4, and 5 (the distribution pattern of iron implements and supply/exchange system of iron objects in the region), the PI recognized the difficulties given the fact that evidence of iron manufacturing during the Han period in Lingnan has not yet been confirmed. However, the PI overcame the difficulties via studying the supply and exchange system first in the Guanzhong basin, in which the PI could access to first-hand materials related to iron production. Through studying materials related to iron-manufacturing and previously published data, the PI generated several articles (output #1, 2, 3, 5, 8) for this project discussing the types of organization of ironworks in the Han period, indicators showing various types of iron production , and theoretical models illustrating various types of exchange or distribution scenarios. Based on the patterns derived from the core region, the PI confirmed that cast iron manufacturing was unlikely to be taken place in Lingnan during the Han period. Meanwhile, the PI employed the models conceptualizing various types of exchange in the Han period based on the statistical analysis of iron objects contained in tombs in Lingnan (output #7). The analytical results suggested that relatively developed distribution network of iron daily-tools between Lingnan and other parts of the Han empire must have existed in the Han period. In other words, the PI already fulfilled and achieved the aims mentioned in objectives #3, 4, and 5. In addition, the PI presented the results in various venues, including the SAA conference in US, BUMA conference in Bushan, and invited lectures by Academia Sinica in Taipei, and discussed potential problems encountered when the PI was conducting the analysis. The conference paper also generated a paper (output #4) that allowed the PI to introduce the idea of studying iron object distribution pattern to other archaeometallurgists in the field. The PI already generated a database including all published Han tombs in Lingnan via this project (objective #3) for the statistical analysis, and the database will be uploaded to the Archaeology GIS platform managed by the digital scholarship lab, CUHK library, 2020.
