24607916.label: Major findings and research outcome
24607916.value: One major output generated by this ECS-RCG-funded project was the article published in Journal of Archaeological Science (output #6) that discusses analytical methods and criteria for identifying various kinds of steel/iron manufacturing skills in ancient China, which is the first article published in the top disciplinary journal for this topic. This article not only lied down a solid foundation for understanding the iron technology in other regions beyond Lingnan (output #9), but also provided an important identification-tool for the PI to study the iron objects from Guangzhou collected via the PI’s fieldwork (output #10) and to compare the manufacturing skills between the core and the peripheries of the Han empire (objectives #1 #2). According to the analytical results, the PI identified that both fined iron, cast iron, solid-state decarburization of cast iron, and bloomery iron were employed in the manufacturing of iron implements found in Guangzhou. Also, since products that were made of cast iron or cast-iron related steel-making technology were the majority in the assemblage of samples collected for metallurgical analysis, the PI argues in output#10 that the supply system of iron implements in Lingnan is closely related to the external sources beyond the region. In addition, this project generated several papers that clarified and conceptualized various organizations of iron production (output#8), archaeological indicators of various types of ironworks (output#2 and 8), and the distribution mechanism of iron products evidenced in archaeological records during the Han period (output #1, 3, and 5). These preparations allow the PI to discuss the distribution mechanism of iron objects in Lingnan based on the database of iron objects from Han tombs, and further discusses the supply and distribution system of iron implements in Lingnan via a perspective of regional comparison (output #7). One major result is that the PI identified, although the distribution network in Lingnan was less comprehensive and systematic than the case in the Guanzhong basin reconstructed by the PI, the distribution patterns of iron implements (and bronze objects as well) still show a relatively developed distribution network of daily items between Lingnan and other parts of the Han empire.

24607916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24607916.value: There are several potentials for further developing this current project: 1) Since the PI identified that cast iron and related steel-making technique represented by the assemblage of iron objects selected from Lingnan, whether the cast-iron tradition also had a strong presence in other adjacent regions (e.g., Hunan)? This idea could be further tested by another project. 2) Since blooomery iron was identified in Lingnan but was not local products based upon the PI's study, whether the bloomery iron technique also existed in other adjacent regions? The clarification of various types of iron techniques in a larger geographical-scale would eventually provide a comprehensive picture about the economic structure of the Han empire. 3) The distribution study iron and bronze objects (output #7) in Lingnan identified that the distribution of these two types of objects shows various patterns, and the supply system of bronze objects in Lingnan seems to be more developed. Since bronze was also an important type of materials in the Han period, the PI suggests studying the manufacturing and distribution system of bronze objects in Lingnan in the future may provide an important piece of information complimenting the current project about the metal economies in the Han’s peripheries.

24607916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24607916.value: This project generates articles that comprehensively discussed the production and distribution systems of iron implements in Lingnan and other parts of the Han empire for the first time. Since the analytical results suggest that, quite contradictory to the common-sense idea, the supply of iron objects relied heavily on the transportation of iron materials from external sources, the results indicated that a relatively developed transportation network for daily-goods between Lingnan and other parts of the Han empire must exist in the Han period. The information not only enhances our textual knowledge about the communication system of the Han Empire but also sheds new light on an important mechanism underlying the unified material culture of the Han study. In other words, this project generated new data for researchers exploring the way through which the Han empire consolidated its sovereignty in its peripheries from a new perspective.

24608116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24608116.value: This research investigates the critics and reception of Chinese Versification Studies in 17th to 19th Japan. The versification of Chinese Poetry, consisting of the binary opposition of the level (ping, 平) and deflected (ze, 仄) tones, has gained prominence in the study of versification. Through the classification (bifurcation) of the four tones and the imposition of tonal rules on couplets, certain prosodic patterns exclusive to the Recent Style 近體Prosody are thus formed. The prosodic rules of the Old Style Poetry 古詩, on the other hand, are ambiguous and arbitrary, leaving room for further examination for later scholars. As Classical Chinese is not the mother tongue of Japanese poets and sinologists, they were initially very careful when following the tonal rules established by Chinese poets. Nevertheless, in the 17th century, for phonological and academic reasons, they were more confident in starting their own research on Chinese versification. They criticized the rigidity and inadequacy of versification studies of Chinese scholars, particularly Li Panlong 李攀龍 (1514-1570) who was once the role model of prosodic rules in Japan. Additionally, previous work has overlooked the uniqueness, complexity and achievements of Chinese Versification Studies as found in the Japanese Corpus. They treated Japanese Corpus as the extension of Chinese Shihua 詩話 (text discussing poetry), without considering the cultural context of Japan. The Japanese poets and sinologists in the 17th -19th centuries have contributed a lot in the realm of Chinese Versification, especially with respect to the discussion of asanren下三連 (the use of three consecutive level tones) and Old Style Poetry Versification. This research investigates the attitude of Japanese critics towards versification, and re-evaluates the research value of Chinese Versification Studies of 17th-19th century Japan and China. The methodology and debate among Japanese scholars of different literary schools are also key issues. By investigating the Shihuas and other relevant literature, this research will examine how the prosodic rules (especially Old Style Prosody) were discovered and theorized in Japan. This research will provide a solid foundation for reinterpreting the history of Chinese Versification, particularly with respect to how the Japanese responded to Li Panlong, Wang Shizhen 王士禎, Shen Deqian 沈德潛 and Weng Fanggang翁方綱. The research output will provide students and amateurs comprehensive and comprehensible guidelines on the versification of Old Style Poetry. 本研究考察十七至十九世紀日本文獻對中國詩律的評論與接受。中國詩歌中的平仄對立於詩律研究中尤為突出，通過四聲二分及各種聲調配搭，近體詩特有的格律規定於焉產生。相形之下，古體詩格律則顯得含混而隨意，尚待後人研究之處尚多。 由於古典漢語並非日本漢詩人及漢學者的母語，他們學習中國詩人的聲律規則時原本亦步亦趨；到了十七世紀，因為語音與學術等變化，日人對發展其詩律研究漸覺自信。他們批評中國學者在詩律研究上的固守與不足，尤其是在聲律運用方面備受日人推崇的李攀龍(1514-1570)。此外，前人研究忽略了日本評論中所呈現的獨特、複雜性質以至其研究成果，將之視為中國詩話的延伸，沒有考慮日本的文化脈絡：十七至十九世紀的日本詩人與漢學者在漢語詩律學上(尤其在下三連與古詩詩律方面)貢獻良多。 本研究探討日本文獻對漢語詩律的評論與態度，重新評價十七至十九世紀中國與日本漢語詩律研究的價值。本研究亦關注日本各文派之間就詩律的論辯及其方法論，通過詩話及相關文獻考索日本如何發現並理論化漢詩(尤其是古體詩)詩律。 本研究將成為重新詮釋中國詩律史的重要基礎，尤其著墨於日人如何回應王士禎、沈德潛、翁方綱等人的詩律理論。本研究成果將為學生及業餘愛好者提供綜合且易於理解的古詩詩律法則。

24608116.label: Realisation of objectives
24608116.value: To investigate the critics and reception of Chinese Versification Studies in 17th to 19th Japan, the PI has carefully examined all 10 volumes of Nihon Shihua Jyusho. The PI has put extra effort to identify the major arguments and trend of Chinese versification in the Edo period. To examine the uniqueness, complexity and achievements of Chinese Versification Studies as found in Japanese Corpus, the PI has focused on the case study of Li Pan Long. As the localization of Japanese Sinology occured, opposition to the authority of Chinese scholarship grew, and the Japanese started to criticize the inadequacy of versification studies of Li and the Kobunji Gakuha which supported Li. By studying Sekihi and Somei Kintai Seiritsuko, this project examined how DAZAI Shundaiand TAKIGAWA Nankoku disapproved of the Kobunji Gakuha in terms of Chinese Versification. The research stated that achievement of Chinese Versification Studies in ancient Japan is indeed a mirror for Ming-Qing Literary critics. The PI also focused on the study of hexasyllabic poems as seen in the Japanese versification corpus. The Japanese scholars have succeeded in identifying the distorted xy system as well as the caesura of hexasyllabic poems. This constitutes definite evidence for the universal nature of the xy system, the contribution and standard of Japanese study as compared to the Qing scholars. To explore the formation and diversity of Chinese Versification, as well as the prosodic preferences of Tang and Song poets, and to re-examine how the history of Chinese Versification was constructed, the PI has turned to the reevaluation of different prosodic models proposed by Edo, Qing and modern scholars. Attempts to explain the Recent Style Prosody from a modern linguistic perspective, e.g. Chen 1979, Yip 1980, Xue 1989, Fabb and Halle 2008, are found flawed. The PI has shown that Downer and Graham 1963 is still the most reliable analysis of Recent Style Prosody. The PI has quoted certain Japanese and Chinese versification corpora, which are highly relevant to this application. This research also stated that Wang Li 1958 has scientifically demonstrated the prosodic preferences of Tang poets, approving Dong Wenhuan’s argument of single deviant and double deviant lines. To re-examine how the history of Chinese Versification was constructed, and to re-evaluate the research value of Chinese Versification Studies of the Ming and Qing Dynasties, this project analyzed Bunkyōhifuron, Yingkui Lüsui and Shihua corpus in the Tang and Song Dynasties, and proved the existence of the xy system as well as its relationship with deviant lines. With reference of Yuan Jing's "prosodic skills (tiaosheng shu)", the PI showed that the Y sub-system was the first to be established (no later than the Mid-6th century), while the X sub-system and x≠y rule was established at a later stage in the Tang Dynasty. This is highly coherent to the "eight defects" adopted in the Yongming Era. These two objectives are not fully achieved as some of the background of Chinese Versification in Ming-Qing Periods are not known to us. In contrast to pre-Meiji kanshi poets who denied the existence of Old Style Prosody, the Qing scholars were passionate about the study of Old Style Prosody. How should we explain the passion of Qing scholars in exploring the Old Style Prosody? What was their ultimate goal? Various definitions of deviant prosodic patterns (aoti), coincidence of these patterns and the xy system proposed by Downer & Graham in 1963 and consequently, the prosodic rules related to the xy system which emerged in the Qing Dynasty are yet to be further investigated. However, as this is not completely relevant to the key issues of this project, they are neglected by the PI in this project. However, by reading the research output, one can clearly appreciate the research value of Chinese Versification, especially the need of a critical edition of Chinese Versification Corpus in the Qing Dynasty, and the institutionalization of prosody in the ing Dynasty so that ts influence is still tangible in textbooks up to the present day. Due to the complexity of the content, and the need to re-analyse the vast amount statistic data on Versification provided by Du Xiaoqin 2017, 2018, the PI has decided to steadily disseminate the research output. 2 edited version of the manuscripts have been submitted to peer-reviewed academic journals, and are still under review; 1 manuscript is still under preparation, with a draft attached in this report. The PI will publish the papers as soon as possible with proper acknowledgements to the UGC, and will continue to disseminate relavant manuscripts by means of the measures mentioned in session 6.2.

24608116.label: Major findings and research outcome
24608116.value: The PI stated how the Edo Kanshi poets evaluated the values of Chinese Versification, and how they supported and refuted the prosody rules found in Li Pan Long's poems, in order to re-evaluate the canonical poetry and Ken'en School. By investigating Wang Shizhen's Gushi Pingze Lun and Mori Kainan's commentary, it is found that the study of Old Style Prosody in Japan is not popular until early 19th Century. Mori's adoption of new methodologies and terminology should be acknowledged in the history of Versification Studies. The PI provided a new definition of symmetry (nian, placement of opposite tones in xy system only), antisymmetry (dui, placement of opposite tones in both ABA and xy systems) and deviant (ao, x=y) prosodic patterns. These findings help examine how the findings of Edo and Qing scholars coincide with the xy system. The PI also illustrated how Wang Li 1958 has adopted the versification (particularly Old Style Prosody) treatises in the Qing Dynasty, and how the Japanese corpus is useful for a re-evaluation of Wang’s model. The PI has carefully analyzed the arguments found in Shogaku Shiho, Shiho Seigi , Shitetsu, Shikaku Shusei , especially in the deviant lines of Hexasyllabic poems, which serves as a “control experiment” of heptasyllabic and pentasyllabic poems.

24608116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24608116.value: The PI will apply for new GRF grant on Chinese Versification Studies in the Qing Dynasty. The 2 research projects will combine to exhibit the differences in methodology, euphonic preferences, development and application of versification studies in 17th-19th century East Asia, under the context of Literature, Linguistics and East Asian Studies.The ABA and xy systems advocated by the PI will serve as an important means to justify the feasibility of various prosodic theories proposed by ancient scholars. Shiritsu Cho could be further investigated to shed light on the combination of prosodic patterns of major Tang and Song poets. The PI plans to teach a new course “Chinese Versification Studies” for both undergraduate and MA students.

24608916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24608916.value: 以不貞名義合法處決妻子的丈夫大有人在，文藝復興時期的韋諾薩親王卡洛•傑蘇阿爾多(Carlo Gesualdo)便是其中一位，從未有誰像他那般臭名昭著，一方面他是音樂家親王，另一方面，他創作了諸多有關性虐的韵文和音樂。身為重要的大主教、異教徒和學者般的人物的後代，傑蘇阿爾多與教會的關係亦好亦壞，一方面他的名字出現在於今看來具有傳奇色彩的羅馬裁判所諭令之中，但另一方面，傑蘇阿爾多那些色情詩詞和音樂，在他於1613年辭世後不久，卻能從位於羅馬巴貝里尼宮的宗教裁判所長辦公室中聽到。事實上，巴貝里尼家族（當中包括教宗烏爾班八世馬費奧•巴貝里尼 (Maffeo Barberini)、宗教裁判所長弗朗西斯科•巴貝里尼 (Francesco Barberini)，以及眾多高級神職人員）一直借贊助作曲家和音樂學者，來鼓勵傑蘇阿爾多的音樂在羅馬的傳播。自從弗雷德里克•哈蒙德 (Frederick Hammond)在巴貝里尼對「伽利略事件」的干預研究中發現並首次披露此事後，這種似乎不得體的行為一直令學者感到驚訝。然而梵蒂岡這種新興的對傑蘇阿爾多的愛好，一直因為來自羅馬的寥落原始資料互相矛盾，而未能得到合理解釋。最不可思議的是，傑蘇阿爾多音樂的初版並沒有獲得由羅馬宗教裁判所簽發的必不可少的許可證，但卻又從未被列入《禁書目錄》當中；後續的版本則得到了出版許可證。此外，傑蘇阿爾多的教會音樂明顯從未在羅馬接受過審查——試想一下，傑蘇阿爾多為聖週寫作的音樂幾乎與梵蒂岡翹首期盼的羅馬天主教禮拜儀式的格里高利聖詠同時出現，這是一件多麼諷刺的事情！雖然梵蒂岡最初對傑蘇阿爾多提出過一些指控，但這些指控似未經裁決便已撤銷，沒有任何理據記錄在案。 本研究發現了一份早認為失傳了，於羅馬巴貝里尼完成的一篇音樂論文手稿，增進了前人就傑蘇阿爾多那隱約不明的接納歷史所做的檔案研究。《當代音樂與古代音樂之比較研究》是由羅馬天主教格里高利大學的院長萊昂內• 辛迪 (Leone Santi)完成，論文展示了那些與傑蘇阿爾多音樂相關但迄今為止不為人知的方面，以及以人道主義、神學和天主教教義為之所作的辯護。此外，論文中引用的音樂促使一位廣被忽視的羅馬作曲家安東尼奧•塞弗拉 (Antonio Cifra)受到了應有關注，他曾經審查和改編傑蘇阿爾多的音樂作品。這些資料，配合就傑蘇阿爾多對格里高利聖詠的應用和濫用的批判研究，將有助完成一本有關傑蘇阿爾多身後的接納歷史的專著。最終，我們甚至可能將音樂融入於有關羅馬宗教裁判所的龐大史料當中。

24608916.label: Major findings and research outcome
24608916.value: The most important and promising finding I made over the course of this project's research was that Carlo Gesualdo--arguably--staged his infamous "honour killing" (the killing of his wife and her lover) according to the liturgy of the Roman Church. By checking the precise date of Gesualdo's killing against the Roman Breviary, I found that he acted on a day in the liturgical calendar in which the Bible lesson (Old Testament) sanctioned honour killing. In so doing, Gesualdo tried to 'Christianize' his killing and save himself (and his family) from the burden of sin. The finding is unexpected, given the original stated research objectives, but stands to make the highest research impact of all of my findings in the past 3 years. I submitted a substantial article (15000 words) to a top journal in the summer of 2020 and, pending the inevitable revisions needed, I expect it to generate much scholarly discussion. I intend to even explore making a new documentary video about Gesualdo's life and works (a common topic that reaches a wide audience outside the academy). In addition I have under review several other articles under review (on plainchant, the Roman madrigals of Antonio Cifra) and a complete working transcription of a treatise by Leone Santi. I'm confident these will be published in the not-too-distant future. Related articles on Gesualdo's reception in the writings of the Roman Jesuit Athanasius Kircher and the unique tuning system he (and other modernist composers) was using in his music were more readily published (having been already underway). These received the highest mark (world leading) in the mock RAE for 2020. There are some areas I was not able make as many inroads as hoped for--chiefly the identification of the Roman inquisitors responsible for censoring music. I trimmed the planned archival research trip to Italy to just one month in the summer of 2019, in deference to family needs during the civil unrest in HK and to be on hand for the department. As seeking to identify inquisitors of music would be a painstaking exercise (with no guaranteed results), I therefore set a finite and feasible goal of conducting archival work on Antonio Cifra in Rome and Loreto. However, the Vatican archives will be open again and anything I did not find this time around may yet be discovered next time. All in all, I expect this project has made and will continue to make major contributions to the field.

24608916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24608916.value: There is much room for further development on Gesualdo-related research and I have already submitted one successful GRF grant proposal on an off-shoot from this project. Given the extensive resources in Italian Renaissance history needed for this research, I have also been under discussion about returning to Villa I Tatti, The Harvard University Center for Italian Renaissance Studies for a year-long fellowship to ensure that the research is polished for publication. In Hong Kong, it is best to bring this research here, but we can not yet claim these specialized Italian resources in a post-colonial city in China. (One of the original peer reviewers of this project rightly, in my view, raised a concern about the relevance to HK). One promising avenue here I found is to share this research with the monastic community in HK, some members of which indeed have degrees in music and liturgy. Given the on-going circumstances (Covid and local civil situation), it is best to connect this research to Greater China as a priority. Some related scholars and I have been brainstorming about musical research on the recent accord between the Vatican and China.

24608916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24608916.value: This project consisted of archival research and scholarly writing on one of the most infamous characters in Western music history: Carlo Gesualdo (16th c.), a Renaissance prince who executed his wife (for adultery) and composed some of the most extravagant music of his times. The research centered on this prince's religious relationship to Rome, and his reception history in the Vatican and its jurisdictions. Because the prince was related to several archbishops and event saints, there has been much speculation about how he worked to save face within the Church--especially after the Council of Trent. To answer some of the lingering questions, this project is revealing how Gesualdo used familiar melodies from sacred music to craft his own idiosyncratic music. The results include scholarly journal articles and working manuscripts that will be published as critical editions for wider scholarly study. At the same time, a new video documentary is being envisioned to continue reaching wider audiences.

24609016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24609016.value: Fall represents one of the leading causes of accidental injuries and death among the older population. With a fast growing aging population, prevalence of falls is expected to increase. In comparison to other countries, Hong Kong older adults were found to have lower muscular strength and impaired balance control, which are key risk factors for falls. Traditionally, fall prevention exercise tended to focus on strength training (ST); however, recently there is an increased awareness that muscle power training (PT) should be involved to increase the effectiveness of fall prevention programs. Specifically, muscle power is required to produce fast ballistic limb movement, which plays crucial role in the execution of rapid stepping and grasping balance-recovery reactions when exposed to unexpected balance disturbances. Previous studies of PT often relied on the use of weight machine; however, many Hong Kong older adults do not have access to such facilities. Furthermore, the effectiveness of PT on restoring the capacity to execute rapid balance-recovery reactions to prevent falls has yet to be established. Therefore, the objectives of this study are to: (1) develop a cost-effective muscle training interventions using Thera-band, and (2) compare the effectiveness of PT and ST on the restoration of rapid stepping and grasping balance-recovery reactions in older adults. Sixty older adults with some balance impairment will be recruited to participate in a randomized control trial with a 6-months follow-up. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: 1) power training (PT), 2) strength training (ST), and 3) flexibility training (FT) as control. All participants will be trained 24 sessions within 12 weeks and will be evaluated at three time-points (pre-training, post-training and 6-months follow-up) on balance and gait control, muscle strength and power, fear of falling, activities of daily-living, and 6-months fall history. We hypothesize that PT will lead to the greatest improvement in the capacity to restore postural stability from suddenly balance perturbation evoked by a “lean-and-release” balance assessment system. Repeated-measure ANOVA and post-hoc multiple comparisons with Bonferroni correction will be performed to test the main and interaction effects of intervention (PT vs. ST vs. FT) and time-point (pre vs. post vs. retention). Such cost-effective intervention, if proven effective, can be easily incorporated into older adults’ daily routines, or into the existing fall prevention programs. Moreover, our study can potentially provide more evidence that PT can improve balance-recovery reactions, as well as reduce the number of falls.

24609016.label: Realisation of objectives
24609016.value: Two main objectives were listed in the research proposal: 1. To develop a cost-effective group-based exercise program aimed to improve muscle power with the use of Thera-band 2. To examine the benefits of such intervention in the execution of compensatory stepping and grasping balance-recovery reactions and fall prevention. The first objective was achieved. We have developed an effective muscle power training intervention using Theraband as the resistance. Among the 26 subjects allocated to the muscle power training group, 21 of them completed the training, in contrast to only 18 of the 27 subjects completed the muscle strength training. All of those who dropped out from the study were due to personal reasons (e.g. getting sick/injured, lacking time to commit to the training sessions, etc.), and no one was injured because of our training. In addition, most of the dropout cases were among the first batch of participants, as we were still fine-tuning our training protocol and learning ways to motivate the unfit individuals to train with us. As we gained more experience, the dropout rate decreased significantly in the second half of the study. Based on our observation, we noticed that it was easier for older adults in the muscle power group to train their muscles because of the lower resistance. Furthermore, we have identified muscles groups that were important for maintaining static and dynamic balance, as well as in balance-recovery. One early challenge was to find a way to choose an appropriate resistance for each individual for each muscle group but that was solved by doing some simple and short assessments without the need of any specialized equipment to measure their One Repetition Maximum. Having this simple method is essential if we would like to promote this intervention in community settings. As for the second objective, originally we intended to recruit 60 participants and randomized them into three groups of approximately 20 participants each for (1) muscle power training, (2) muscle strength training, and (3) flexibility training as the control. At the end, we have successfully recruited 71 participants (i.e. 26 in power, 27 in strength, and 18 in flexibility). Although a total of 16 dropped out from our study, we still have 55 participants (i.e. 21 in power, 18 in strength, and 16 in flexibility) who have completed the training and the post-assessment. However, we would also want to collect their 6-months follow-up but due to (1) the departure of the PI from his position, (2) the ending of the funding period, and (3) malfunctioning of the a key equipment to assess balance-recovery reactions towards the end of the project, only 31 participants (i.e. 6 in power, 14 in strength, 11 in flexibility) were able to complete the 6-months follow-up. We ordered the replacement unit but it took over 2 months to arrive and we were unable to complete the follow-up assessment. With so few participants completing the follow-up assessment, we were unable to use that data for analysis. Nevertheless, with just the pre- and post-assessment data, we were able to see the effectiveness of such training on balance control among our participants.

24609016.label: Major findings and research outcome
24609016.value: Our study has shown that a 12 weeks Theraband-based muscle power training was effective in improving balance control among community-dwelling older adults with some balance impairment (Berg Balance Scale score < 52/56). In general, participants had significantly improved balance control (Berg Balance Scale [BBS]: pre=49.14 vs. post=51.99; p<0.0001; Static body sway – anteroposterior [SwayAP]: pre=31.95mm vs. post=29.01mm; p=0.044; Static body sway – mediolateral [SwayML]: pre=41.05mm vs. post=32.53mm; p=0.001), gait control (Timed Up and Go test [TUG]: pre=13.33s vs. post=12.42s; p=0.001) and speed (6 Meters Walk Test [6MWT]: pre=7.60s vs. post=7.01s; p=0.012), balance confidence (Activity-based Balance Confidence [ABC]: pre=75.14 vs. post=78.02; p=0.009), physical activity level (International Physical Activity Questionnaire [IPAQ]: pre=18.34MET vs. post=18.96MET; p=0.008), muscle power (5 Chair Sit-to-Stand [5CSTS]: pre=13.89s vs. post=11.81s; p<0.001), muscle strength in upper (Grip strength: pre=18.42kg vs. post=19.56kg; p=0.003) and lower (Knee extension: pre=14.4kg vs. post=16.3kg; p<0.001) limbs, as well as reaction time (Simple reaction time: pre=275.3ms vs. post=249.1ms; p=0.003) after receiving our training. As expected, significant group x time interaction showed that muscle power training led to the greatest improvement of their lower limb muscle power relative to the other two groups (5CSTS: power=-4.09s vs. strength=-1.99s vs. flexibility=-0.18s; p<0.001). Furthermore, there were strong trends that muscle power group also had greater improvement in their balance control (BBS: power=+4.54 vs. strength=+2.52 vs. flexibility=+1.50), gait control (TUGS: power=-1.66s vs. strength=-1.07s vs. flexibility=-0.01s), knee extension strength (power=+3.54kg vs. strength=+2.00kg vs. flexibility=+0.25kg), as well as simple reaction time (power=-53.98ms vs. strength=-18.66ms vs. flexibility=-5.97ms) than those in the conventional muscle strength training group and flexibility group. Although the small sample size and short study period would not allow us to draw conclusion on whether our intervention was effective in reducing the number of actual falls, having significant improvement in almost all of our assessment is a strong indicator that our intervention was effective in reducing older adults’ fall risk. Such simple and cost-effective intervention can be easily incorporated into older adults’ daily training routine or into the existing fall prevention programs.

24609016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24609016.value: As the PI of this project has left his previous job position, the team has yet to finish analyzing the kinematic results from the simulated falls and publish our results in peer-reviewed journals. It is our intention to finish analyzing our data within the next few months during the COVID-19 outbreak period and hopefully publish our results by the end of this year. Furthermore, our muscle power training protocol has been used in another study funded by Health Care and Promotion Scheme (Project title: Promoting to Tackle Sarcopenia by Combined Elastic-band Resistance Exercise or Vibration Treatment with Hydroxylmethylbutyrate (HMB) Supplement for Older People; Project number: 02180118). If proven successful, we will try to promote our training intervention to the community daycare centers for elderly in Hong Kong.

24609016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24609016.value: Muscle mass loss is common among older adults. As a result, this population is at increased risk of falls due to impaired balance and mobility control. Traditional muscle strength training often relied on weight machines and dumbbells, which often deterred older adults from engaging in strength training due to their perceived difficulty in using these equipment. Alternatively, Theraband can be used as a source of resistance for muscle training. These resistance bands are easy to store and carry, and older adults appeared to be more comfortable using these instead of the abovementioned equipment. Furthermore, unlike traditional resistance trainings that focus on improving muscle strength, greater emphasis should be placed on improving muscle power, as muscle power is required to effectively perform various ballistic movements in daily activities such as standing from chair, starting to walk, turning, braking, as well as taking large steps or grasping nearby objects to prevent falls. Our results showed that muscle power and strength training for 12 weeks are both effective in improving balance and gait control, though muscle power training can have even greater benefits than traditional strength training. Therefore, older adults should engage in more Theraband-based muscle power training to reduce their fall risk.

24609316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24609316.value: 本研究探討在日本近來興起的、有關治療不育問題的話語（discourse）和實踐（practice）。生殖治療在日本一般稱為「爭取懷孕」（妊活 ninkatsu）。本研究以正在接受生殖治療的男女為研究對象，運用民族誌 (ethnographic research)及訪談的研究方式，旨在瞭解這些男女在面對「非自願無子女」 (“involuntary childlessness”)的經歷，以及夫婦們在爭取懷孕過程中所面對的挑戰。本研究探討各種家庭的形成過程和存在意義。透過分析在面臨低生育率的日本社會中夫婦們如何反思及磨合對生育及家庭的規範觀念和理想、婚姻伴侶關係的各種形態(marital companionship) 和性態（sexuality），闡明在社會文化層面上的生育力問題。 在當今的東亞國家，例如香港、南韓和新加坡，就業境況和家庭結構正急速轉變。日本也不例外，其社會正處於人口結構轉變 (demographic transformation) 過程之中，逐步走向人口老齡化、生育率極低的國家。女性就業率急劇增長，婚齡不斷推遲，都影響到了生育的時機和節奏。與此相隨，大眾對不育問題的瞭解逐漸增加，對治療不育問題的需求也在增長。從2001年至2010年的十年間，對 治療不育問題的需求增加了三倍。然而，儘管有著上述經濟、人口和社會的變化，關於家庭與懷孕的「自然主義」（“naturalistic”）規範根深蒂固，仍然把生殖問題歸於女性私密、沉默的領域。因此，雖然生育與婚姻的關聯逐漸削弱，但是建立家庭的意欲卻同時變得更為急切和劇烈。儘管公眾的注意力正被引向婚姻與生育的「危機」，但建立家庭卻越發成為「私領域」的掙扎努力，而且此種努力莫不與現今日本社會和個人層面上的問題息息相關。 本研究透過與非牟利機構和臨床專業人士合作進行民族誌研究，調查正積極接受生殖治療的當代日本男女如何面對「非自願無子女」這種有口難言的挑戰，以釐清關於生育的醫療問題與社會問題的關聯性。本研究對於以下範疇做出貢獻﹕1) 生殖人類學的發展﹔2) 有關家庭、親密關係 (intimacy) 和性態(sexuality) 的各種論述﹔及3) 東亞社會在面臨低生育率所帶來的各種緊急的法律、經濟、醫療及社會局面所需的政策研究。

24609316.label: Realisation of objectives
24609316.value: Objective 1: To pursue anthropological research on the sociocultural aspects of fertility treatments. This was achieved via: 1) Literature review of comparative anthropological work on infertility in Japan, North America, Europe, and the Middle East; 2) Ethnographic fieldwork at two infertility clinics in Tokyo; 3) Interviews with fertility specialists and ART recipients, including both women and men. Through this combination of comparative analysis, fieldwork, and interviews, I was able to apprehend a comprehensive perspective on the sociocultural context of infertility and fertility treatments in Japan, specifically: 1) the impact of delayed marriage and childbirth which pushes many women past the most fertile childbearing years; 2) the culture of “overwork” that leads many couples to postpone having children and/or causes lifestyle-related infertility; 3) the gendered division of labor which makes reproductive issues framed as “women’s” issues and thus makes it difficult for men to become actively included in discussions about (in)fertility. Objective 2: To employ queer theory to engage theoretical debates on family, intimacy, and sexuality, for both women and men. This was achieved in two ways: 1) Interviews with non-heterosexual individuals about ideals of family: Specifically, I conducted in-depth interviews with gay/lesbian individuals, including lesbian-identified women who have undergone infertility treatment overseas in order to conceive children. I also interviewed gay-identified men about desires for children/family. 2) Theoretical analysis: By unpacking the process/context of infertility treatments, I identified three spheres of desire for infertility recipients: 1. Desires for family (partner/children); 2. Desires for intimacy (non-sexual); 3. Desires (or lack thereof) for sexual intimacy. Employing queer theory analysis of these spheres revealed that assumptions about pronatalist “patriarchal” compulsions for marriage and childbirth can be misleading—often, women/men themselves desire marriage/children and are not motivated by social pressure, but by individual desires for their own families, even if these are “non-heteronormative” families. Objective 3: To contribute to policy studies on legal, economic, medical, and social ramifications of fertility treatments in low-fertility societies around the world. I achieved this objective via comparative policy analysis regarding the sociocultural influences on the legal, economic, medical, and social dimensions of infertility. Thereby, I identified key areas for fertility-related policy improvement. First, early education for both men and women is necessary to raise awareness of potential impacts of lifestyle choices on future family options. Second, greater economic support and treatment flexibility is necessary to enable affordable and effective treatments. Third, greater social awareness of the impact of long working hours on reproductive health is necessary to obtain support both at the workplace and at home. I discussed these issues with scholars and policymakers from Asia, Europe, and North America through informal meetings and by presenting my research at the New York Conference on Asian Studies (September 2017). Objective 4: To offer a voice for the many individuals struggling with “involuntary childlessness” in Japan and around the world by communicating their concerns and desires in public lectures, academic presentations, and journal publications. I accomplished this objective in two ways: 1) Through in-depth interviews with men and women, I have woven their stories into my analysis of the personal and social effects of infertility in Japan and presented their voices at the New York Conference on Asian Studies. Ethnographic stories gives life to the dry statistics usually used to discuss infertility. Informants agreed to share their experiences for my research in order to empower others around the world with their stories. 2) I am preparing two manuscripts for publication in international journals. These showcase the challenges and desires behind infertility in Japan, and will contribute to international dialogue on how to support those striving for families around the world.

24609316.label: Major findings and research outcome
24609316.value: There are four major research findings. First, my research revealed a seeming paradox in that Japan is one of the most technologically advanced countries in terms of assisted reproductive technologies (ART), but it has one of the most culturally conservative policy systems of utilizing ART. The root of this paradox lies in: 1) The policy level, wherein the dominant strength of the Japan Society for Obstetrics and Gynecology sets rules and censures “rogue” doctors; 2) The technological level, in which advanced technologies enable cutting-edge research; and 3) The sociocultural level, in which individuals do not have religious or cultural aversion to ART, yet there is a strong desire for pursuing pregnancy that is as close to “natural” as possible—using one’s own gametes, and carrying the child in one’s own body—as well as an emerging skepticism for adoption than in other societies. Second, this research revealed three important experiences for individuals struggling from infertility: 1) the impact of delayed marriage and childbirth which pushes many women past the most fertile childbearing years; 2) the culture of “overwork” that leads many to postpone having children and/or causes lifestyle-related infertility; 3) the gendered division of labor which makes frames reproduction as “women’s” issues and thus makes it difficult for men to be included in discussions about (in)fertility. Moreover, I identified three areas for fertility-related policy improvement. First, early education is necessary to raise awareness of potential impacts of lifestyle choices on future family options. Second, greater economic support and treatment flexibility is necessary to enable affordable and effective treatments. Third, greater social awareness of the impact of overwork on reproductive health is necessary for support at the workplace and at home. Third, my research revealed how the technologies of ART are conceptualized as assisting nature rather than as “unnatural” or “anti-nature”: “nature” in the form of the desire to produce a biologically related child (i.e. using one’s own body, as opposed to surrogacy) “naturalizes” the advanced technology involved in ART (in “Nature vs. Technology” (See Part C)). Fourth, while statistics on ART in Japan show that Japanese women undergo a higher number of ART cycles on average compared with other countries, my research reveals that one of the key reasons behind this high number is the particular cultural ethos of “effort” which contributes to the tenacity and dedication with which couples pursue ART (in “The Pursuit of Pregnancy” (see Part C)).

24609316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24609316.value: This research opens up new avenues for longitudinal research into the divergent experiences and lifeways of individuals who eventually give up on having a child after prolonged ART. Specifically, the present project offers opportunities to further develop research on three aspects of long-term infertility: 1) How do unsuccessful women make decisions to stop ART? 2) How does this decision impact their marital relationships? 3) How do these new forms of childless families in turn impact broader social perceptions and attitudes toward marriage and family in Japan? In order to address these new areas of research, I plan to continue long-term research with individuals who are currently pursuing ART as well as with those who stop ART without having children. Through longitudinal interviews with such individuals as well as continued fieldwork at fertility clinics, I aim to document the long-term experiences and effects of repeated ART treatments and their impacts on families (husband/wife as well as extended families). The time frame for this research is at least an additional five years, in order to acquire sufficient longitudinal data. To pursue this research I will apply for additional outside grants, and eventually compile and analyze the long-term research in a full-length book manuscript.

24609316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24609316.value: Japan has one of the lowest birth rates in the world. This has been caused by late marriage and delayed childbirth, as well as more women in the workforce, which has led to increasing lifestyle-related illnesses, often resulting in infertility. Against this backdrop, there are increasing numbers of women pursuing treatments for infertility, leading to the highest number of infertility clinics in the world and the highest ratio of infertility treatments per person in the world. Based on ethnographic research and interviews with men and women undergoing treatments for infertility (i.e., Assisted Reproductive Treatments (ART)) in Tokyo during 2016-2018, this project analyzes the experiences and challenges of women and men struggling with infertility. While recent work on infertility in Japan explains the high use of ART as a state-driven pronatalist, patriarchal ideology, my research reveals women’s strong wish to have children. Moreover, women are now enabled to pursue both career and family, which was neither possible nor socially acceptable before. Thus, ART offers women agency and control in a situation where they would have had little in the past while also giving them the new challenge of choosing when to stop, which produces new worries for couples.

25105416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25105416.value: Background. Influenza virus shows a clear winter peak in temperate regions, but its seasonality is less clear in subtropical/tropical regions where viruses can be isolated throughout the year. This seasonal pattern could not be fully explained by the findings of experimental studies that cold temperature and low relative humidity facilitate the survival and transmission of influenza viruses in environment. Based on the previous studies by others and our recent studies, we hypothesize that indoor environmental factors (temperature and relative/absolute humidity), together with outdoor environmental factors, could affect the risk of influenza infections in the older population. Objectives. 1) To estimate the independent effects of indoor environment factors on self-report influenza-like symptoms, outpatient visits and hospitalizations of acute respiratory diseases in the community dwelling elderly in Hong Kong; 2) To investigate the seasonal pattern of exposed indoor environment (including temperature and humidity) in older people and assess the relationship of indoor and outdoor environmental factors; 3) To develop a simulation model for influenza virus activity during 2004-2015, by incorporating observed outdoor meteorological data and extrapolated indoor environment factors. Methodology. A cohort of elderly participants who are 65 years or over and dwelling in the community will be recruited from four districts of Hong Kong Island (HKI). Digital data loggers will be installed in the residential homes of recruited participants and the elderly centers they often visit, to continuously collect daily data of indoor temperature and relative humidity. Self-report episodes of acute respiratory symptoms and average daily hours staying indoors and outdoors will be recorded. The case-crossover design with conditional logistic regression models will be applied to estimate the effects of different indoor environmental parameters on the risk of self-report influenza like symptoms, outpatient visits and hospitalization of acute respiratory diseases, respectively. The susceptible-infected-recovered (SIR) model will be adopted to simulate the daily incidence data of laboratory confirmed cases in the elderly population of HKI during 2004-2015, by incorporating outdoor meteorological data and indoor environment factors extrapolated from this proposed study. Implications. Our study will be the first to comprehensively assess the impacts of indoor environments on influenza like illness in a subtropical city. The findings will provide key evidence to elucidate the mechanism of influenza transmission, which will help refine the control measures in warm climates. The relationship between outdoor and indoor environmental factors could also be used to extrapolate the individual indoor exposure data in future environmental studies. 研究背景 流感病毒在溫帶地區通常冬季達到高峰，但在亞熱帶或熱帶地區季節性并不確定。實驗研究證明較低的溫度和相對濕度更適合流感病毒在環境中的生存和傳播，但不能完全解釋流感在不同地區的季節性變化。基於之前的研究發現，我們推測室內環境因素(如溫度和相對/絕對濕度)和室外的環境因素可能共同影響長者感染流感的風險。 研究目的 1)估計室內環境因素對香港社區居住長者流感類疾病症狀，求診和入院風險的影響;2)調查長者居住的室內環境(包括溫度和濕度)的季節性，評估室內和室外環境因素的相關關係;3)結合室外和室內環境數據，建立模擬流感病毒活動的模型。 研究方法 本研究的目標人群為居住港島四個地區的65 歲或以上的長者。每位參與者的家中和他們經常活動的老年中心將會安裝數據資料記錄器，以收集每日的室內溫度和相對濕度。每位參與者將要求記錄流感類疾病症狀和室內/室外的平均停留時間。本研究將採用病例交叉設計，以回歸模型分別估計不同室內環境參數對流感類疾病症狀，求診和入院風險的影響。我們亦將室外和室內環境數據加入SIR模型，模擬港島地區2004年-2015年長者的每日流感發病率。 研究應用 本研究將首次全面評估室內環境在亞熱帶的城市中對流感樣病例的影響。調查結果將提供關鍵證據解釋流感傳播機制，幫助政府部門檢討在熱帶氣候下對流感應採取的控制措施。同時在後續研究中還可根據室外和室內環境數據的關聯推算出室內環境數據。

25105416.label: Realisation of objectives
25105416.value: Objective 1 and 2 have been 100% achieved from the following research activities: - Participant recruitment: The PI and research assistants contacted 42 community centers located on the Hong Kong Island, of which 17 centers agreed to let the team to recruit participants from their members. The first-year recruitment was from December 2016 to April 2017 and the second-year recruitment from January to May 2018. Snowball sampling was also adopted by asking the participants to invite their friends to join the study. At recruitment, the research team obtained signed consent form from eligible older people. The first home visit was scheduled at recruitment and the residential address was obtained from individual participants. - Data collection: The proposed study period was March 2017 – June 2018. The PI obtained one small grant (total amount $122,450) to extend the follow-up period from one year to two years. The first-year participant recruitment was conducted from December 2016 to April 2017 and 231 participants were successfully recruited. Of them, 60 dropped out by the end of the first-year follow-up and the rest 171 participants continued the second-year follow-up. We conducted the second round from January to May 2018 and 54 new participants were enrolled. The second follow-up ended in May 2019. In total, 285 participants were enrolled in the cohort and the average follow-up period was 608 days. At the first home visit, research assistants conducted baseline questionnaire (demographical information, lifestyle factors, health condition, demographical data of household members and house characteristics), and indoor air quality data. Digital data loggers for indoor temperature and humidity were installed in the living room of their apartments. --Environmental data: One digital data logger (HOBO Data Logger UX100-003) was installed in the living room of each recruited household to collect the hourly indoor temperature and relative humidity (RH) during the study period. All loggers were calibrated at time of manufacture. The sites of logger installation were carefully chosen to avoid frequently touching areas, strong ventilation, direct sunlight exposure, near window or any heating/cooling sources. The loggers were fixed at height of 1.0 - 1.8 meters. Batteries were replaced at the end of the first-year follow-up, or within two days if participants reported low battery of their data loggers. Ambient daily temperature, RH, precipitation, particulate matters less than 2.5 μm in diameter (PM2.5) and ozone (O3) during the study period were retrieved from the Hong Kong Observatory and the Environmental Protection Department, respectively. --Indoor air quality: Indoor fine particulate matter (PM2.5), carbon dioxide (CO2) and total volatile organic compounds (TVOC) in the living room and bedroom respectively were measured for 20 minutes at the first time of home visit. All instruments were calibrated before home visit. --Follow-up: Acute respiratory illness (ARI) was used as the primary outcome instead of influenza-like illness (ILI) in the original plan, because the definition of ILI was found less sensitive in older adults. The original plan to collect the incidence of acute respiratory symptoms were to encourage self-report by participants via an online survey. However, we found most participants had difficulty in using smart phones or lacked access to the internet. Therefore, we made phone calls to each participant every 3-4 week to check the incidence of respiratory symptoms. Participants were encouraged to report immediately after having any acute respiratory symptoms. If these symptoms occurred within seven days of symptoms onset, research assistants would ask for their consent of giving nasal and throat specimens for reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) tests of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). During the study period, a total of 4971 follow-up phone calls were made; 332 acute respiratory symptoms episodes were reported from the participants; 68 specimen samples were collected by research assistants; 67 participants dropped out and 5 participants died from non-respiratory related diseases or an accident. - Data analysis: Data processing: The hourly environmental data was converted to daily average data for analyses. Absolute humidity (AH) was calculated from RH and temperature data and transformed through Clausius-Clapeyron equation. Descriptive analysis: The basic characters of participants and overall indoor and outdoor environmental factors were summarized in table. A map was generated to indicate the geographic locations of participants’ households, weather and air pollutant monitor stations. Time-series plots were created for the daily average of indoor and outdoor environmental factors, and daily indoor environmental factors variation across households. Multivariate analysis: A case-crossover design with time-stratified methods and conditional logistic regression were used to evaluate the excess risk (ER) of ARI incidence associated with one unit increase of indoor and outdoor environmental factors. The single and cumulative lag-day patterns were evaluated up to 7 days prior to the onset date. The regression models evaluated the indoor and outdoor environmental factors separately, and controlled for precipitation, PM2.5 and O3 Stratified analyses by warm (May - October) and cool seasons (November - April) were subsequently conducted. All data analyses were performed by R software (version 3.6.2). The above results have been published: Han L, et al. Indoor environmental factors and acute respiratory illness in a prospective cohort of community-dwelling older adults. The Journal of infectious diseases. 2020. Research objective 3 has been 100% achieved: - Data collection: We obtained the laboratory test results of influenza A (H1N1, H3N2) and B from the Queen Mary Hospital during 2004-2019. The daily data of outdoor temperature, RH and rainfall in Hong Kong were retrieved from the Hong Kong Observatory. The daily mean concentrations of PM2.5 and ozone were obtained from the Environmental Protection Department. - Retrospective projections of indoor AH during 2004-2015 Based on the results of objectives 1 and 2, we retrospectively projected indoor AH for the simulation model. We combined the 2016-2019 data of indoor temperature and RH collected from individual households in our study, and matched to the ambient temperature and AH data in the nearest weather station in the same date. We developed a generalized linear model (GLM) to retrospective project daily mean of indoor AH, using the predictors of daily mean outdoor temperature, RH, AH, rainfall, PM2.5 and ozone. Based on the AIC criteria, we found the model with the predictors of daily mean outdoor temperature, RH, rainfall, PM2.5 and ozone yielded the best fit. But generally the predicted indoor AH values were similar between different models (overall mean ranging from 23.17 to 23.21). - Correlations between indoor AH and influenza transmission rate We calculated Pearson's product moment correlation coefficients for paired daily transmission rates of influenza and different weather data (outdoor temperature, AH, RH and indoor AH). The significant negative correlations were found between indoor AH and transmission rates (ρ=-0.22,p<0.001). We then included indoor AH together with outdoor temperature and RH as predictors for influenza virus activities. - Prediction of influenza virus activities during 2004-2015 We compared the performance of five modeling approaches for prediction of influenza virus activities: GLM, generalized additive model (GAM), linear mixed effects model (LMER), seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average model (SARIMA) and boosted regression trees (BRT). We first used the 2004-2015 data as training dataset and those of 2016-2019 as test dataset. The results showed that BRT model achieved the best goodness-of-fit and prediction accuracy among all the models, whereas SARIMA had the worst performance.

25105416.label: Major findings and research outcome
25105416.value: Two hundred and eighty-five participants have been successfully recruited and followed up for 608 days on average. During the study period, 168 ARI episodes (75 in warm season and 93 in cool season) were reported from 112 participants. Among 68 specimens collected for laboratory test, six were tested positive for influenza A and 4 were positive for RSV. Participants had a median age of 77.0 years, ranged from 65 to 95 years at the recruitment. Indoor and outdoor temperature, RH and AH showed clear seasonal pattern during the study period. In cool season, indoor temperatures were higher than outdoor temperature, indoor AH were similar with outdoor AH, indoor RH were lower than outdoor RH across seasons. In warm season, outdoor temperature and AH were higher than indoors’. Findings from Spearman correlation coefficients showed indoor temperature, RH and AH were highly correlated with corresponding outdoor variables in cool seasons (r > 0.7). The correlations were moderate in warm season (0.5 < r < 0.7). In addition, there were variations of indoor environmental factors across households. The variations were larger in warm season than they were in cool season. We observed a negative association between indoor AH and ARI incidence in cool season. For single lag day models, the ERs peaked at lag 3 day for both indoor and outdoor AH. The cumulative lag effect of indoor AH was greatest on lag 0-5 days, with an ER estimate of -9.0% (95% confidence interval, -15.9% to -1.5%). The corresponding cumulative ER for outdoor AH was -6.8% (95%CI -13.5% to 0.4%). There were negative associations between indoor/outdoor temperature and RH, but less consistent in statistical significance across warm and cool seasons. The above results have been published: “Han L, et al. Indoor environmental factors and acute respiratory illness in a prospective cohort of community-dwelling older adults. The Journal of infectious diseases. 2020.” We did a retrospective projection on daily mean of indoor AH during 2004-2015, based on the indoor data collected from individual households during 2016-2019and outdoor data from the Hong Kong Observatory and Environmental Protection Department during 2004-2019. The significant negative correlations were found between indoor AH and influenza transmission rates. We compared the performance of five modeling approaches for prediction of influenza virus activities, and found a novel machine learning method, boosted regression trees (BRT), outperformed the others in terms of model goodness-of-fit and prediction accuracy.

25105416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25105416.value: This was the first prospective cohort study to evaluate the association between indoor environmental factors and the risk of ARI. Our findings added evidence to support that increasing indoor AH could be a feasible way to help older adults reduce their risk of getting ARI infection. Further studies such as intervention studies are needed to elucidate the mechanisms and the optimal ranges of indoor environmental factors. Our study protocol can be easily applied to other age groups to validate the generalizability of our findings. The association between environmental factors and ARI incidence warrants further investigations, especially in warm season. There are a lot of factors that could affect indoor environmental factors, such as daily use of air-conditioners, ventilation behavior and other activities. It is also interesting to extend our study to other climate zones to further investigate the impact of daily activities on ARI incidence. The BRT model developed from this study can be applied to make prospective projections on influenza virus activities from routinely collected meteorological data. This model will be a useful tool for early preparedness of seasonal influenza epidemics. The modeling strategy can be applied to other seasonal diseases such as respiratory syncytial viruses.

25105416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25105416.value: During December 2016 to May 2019, we continuously collected household temperature and humidity among 285 community-dwelling older adults in Hong Kong, and recorded the date of each time that participants reporting their onset of acute respiratory illness (flu like symptoms such as cough, sore throat, fever, headache, muscle pain). Household temperature and humidity were found strongly correlated with ambient temperature and humidity in cool season (November - April), but less correlated in warm season (May - October). Per unit (1mb) decrease of absolute humidity was associated with 9% increase of ARI incidence risk among older adults in cool season. The association between environmental factors and ARI was less evident in warm season, which could be due to widely usage of air conditioning in warm season. Based on our findings, older people are advised to keep their apartments warm and humid to reduce the risk of acute respiratory infections in cool season. We also explored the possibility of developing a prediction model for influenza virus activities based on publically available meteorological data and retrospectively projected indoor data. We found a machine learning approach, boosted regression trees, could achieve satisfactory performance in model goodness-of-fit and prediction accuracy.

25105616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25105616.value: 智能手機的使用在近年來迅速增長。在2012年，全球智能手機用戶數為十億，在2015年這數字增加了一倍。智能手機在香港尤其普及，它擁有全世界最高的智能手機普及率。另外，超過50％的小學生和超過90％的中學生擁有智能手機。雖然使用智能手機可以提高我們的生活質量，但是過度使用有可能影響健康。幾項研究發現，過度使用智能手機與久坐，心理健康問題，以及睡眠問題相關。然而，這些研究有一個共同的、主要的限制，就是依賴自我報告的智能手機使用量，而這些自我報告可能導致回憶偏差，而且有效性和可靠性不明。另外，智能手機使用量、睡眠質量、以及活動量每天都會改變。事實上，我們可以直接監察智能手機獲得客觀的使用情況，但暫時沒有人研究客觀的智能手機使用量和健康狀況的關係。於本研究，我們建議監察及記錄參加者的智能手機的使用情況，以建立一個全面的、香港青少年和年輕成年人的客觀智能手機的使用量數據，以及分析白天和睡前的智能手機使用量，當晚的睡眠質量，以及翌日的活動量的關係。參加者將會連續七天安裝由研究人員開發的智能手機使用情況監察軟件，他們用於各類型的應用程序的時間（網絡瀏覽、多媒體、遊戲和漫畫、工具、攝錄、即時通訊、社交網絡、健康）和使用的頻率將被記錄。同時，參與者將於手腕上佩戴活動記錄器，以評估他們的睡眠質量和活動量。這項研究結果能夠幫助編寫控制使用智能手機的應用程序，例如限制玩遊戲的時間。另外，為了比較使用智能手機與其他活動的幸福感，我們將隨機提示參與者回答關於日常生活中的細節以收集他們日常的幸福感。作為二次分析，我們將以參加者客觀量度的智能手機使用量驗證他們自我報告的使用量。自我報告智能手機使用量的有效程度可以幫助利益相關者判斷在規模大至不可能使用客觀測量的研究結果的可靠性。

25105616.label: Realisation of objectives
25105616.value: Objective 1: We have collected 7-day smartphone usage data on 187 Hong Kong adolescents and young adults aged 11-25. Of these, 32 were from Tai Po Sam Yuk Secondary School and 155 were from Hong Kong Polytechnic University and Education University of Hong Kong. The participants spent nearly 3 hours per day on their smartphone. Secondary school students on average spent 40 more minutes per day on smartphones than university students. The most common type of usage among secondary school students and university students were games and comics apps (1 hour 30 minutes per day) and instant messaging apps (1 hour 13 minutes per day), respectively. Objective 2: Multilevel regression was used to examine the association between smartphone usage and sleep quality. Among secondary school students, one minute of daytime smartphone usage was associated with 0.12 minute decrease in total sleeping time that night (p=0.042, 95% CI: -0.23, -0.007). Broken down for different usage purposes, only social network (β=-0.39, p=0.03, 95% CI: -0.73, -0.04) was associated with total sleeping time. One minute of bedtime smartphone usage was associated with 0.32 minute increase in wake after sleep onset that night (p=0.04, 95% CI: 0.02, 0.62). One minute of smartphone usage during sleep was associated with sleep efficiency (β=0.013%, p=0.01, 95% CI: 0.003%, 0.023%) and wake after sleep onset (WASO) (β=-0.05, p=0.04, 95% CI: -0.10, -0.005). Among university students, smartphone usage during daytime, bedtime, and sleep were insignificantly associated with sleep quality. Broken down for different usage purposes, daytime tools usage (β=0.32, p=0.02, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.60) and bedtime social network usage (β=2.38, p=0.02, 95% CI: 0.37, 4.39) was associated with total sleeping time, while instant messaging (β=0.04, p=0.048, 95% CI: 0.001, 0.07), web browsing (β=0.47, p=0.02, 95% CI: 0.09, 0.84), and camera usage (β=25.79, p=0.01, 95% CI: 6.22, 45.36) during sleep were associated with WASO. Multilevel regression was also used to examine the association between smartphone usage and physical activity level. One minute of daytime smartphone usage was associated with 7.15 steps increase in the number of steps (p=0.02, 95% CI: 1.02, 13.28) among secondary school students and 3.52 steps increase in the number of steps (p=0.03, 95% CI: 0.37, 6.668) among university students on the next day. Social network, instant messaging, tools, and multimedia usage were positively associated with the time spent on moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical activity (MVPA). Smartphone usage during bedtime and sleep were insignificantly associated with physical activity level, except web browsing during sleep was associated with number of steps (β=1153.07, p=0.04, 95% CI: 57.92, 2248.22) among secondary school students. For both secondary school students and university students, better sleep quality was associated with higher volume of physical activity level on the next day, except that one percent increase in sleep efficiency was associated with 2.29 minutes decrease in time spent on MVPA (p=0.02, 95% CI: 0.34, 4.25) among secondary school students. Objective 3: The correlation between self-reported and objectively-measured total smartphone usage time was insignificant (ρ=-0.10, p=0.18), in three out of the four usage domains, namely social network (ρ=0.21, p=0.005), instant messaging (ρ=0.27, p<0.001), and games (ρ=0.64, p<0.001), the correlations were positively significant. The participants over-reported the total time spent on smartphone for around 760 min per week (self-reported 1930.3 min/wk vs objectively-measured 1170.7 min/wk, p<0.001), or an over-report of 64.9%. Most of the over-reporting was contributed by the web browsing domain (self-reported 447.8 min/wk vs objectively-measured 33.3 min/wk, p<0.001). Note that the self-reported time spent on the four domains (2124.5 min/wk) did not add up to the self-reported total time spent (1930.3 min/wk), as the participants may own more than one smartphone. To conclude, our results showed that self-reported smartphone usage had large discrepancies with objectively-measured smartphone usage. Objective 4: We obtained state positive and negative affect data from 2 random prompts from 8am to 8pm on each day of the 7-day monitoring period. 204 (57.1%) of them provided at least one valid response and were included in the present analysis. More than 85% (n=174) of the participants were university students. A total of 1032 responses were provided by them. Multilevel regression showed that the net affect score during work was significantly lower then the score during all other activities. The regression on all response records showed that, compared with not using smartphone, participants had higher net affect score (difference = 0.10, p = 0.03) when using smartphone. The regression on response records with smartphone usage showed that the duration of smartphone usage was insignificantly associated with the net affect score (p=0.09), while the regression on response records without smartphone usage showed that one hour of not using smartphone was associated a reduced net affect score of 0.03 (p=0.006).

25105616.label: Major findings and research outcome
25105616.value: Objective 2 of this study is to examine the association between smartphone usage in daytime and bedtime, sleeping quality that night, and physical activity level in the following day. Multilevel regression showed that, among secondary school students, one minute of daytime smartphone usage was associated with 0.12 minute decrease in total sleeping time that night (p=0.042, 95% CI: -0.23, -0.007). One minute of bedtime smartphone usage was associated with 0.32 minute increase in wake after sleep onset that night (p=0.04, 95% CI: 0.02, 0.62). One minute of smartphone usage during sleep was associated with sleep efficiency (β=0.013%, p=0.01, 95% CI: 0.003%, 0.023%) and WASO (β=-0.05, p=0.04, 95% CI: -0.10, -0.005). One minute of daytime smartphone usage was associated with 7.15 steps increase in the number of steps (p=0.02, 95% CI: 1.02, 13.28) among secondary school students and 3.52 steps increase in the number of steps (p=0.03, 95% CI: 0.37, 6.668) among university students on the next day. For the results of Objective 2, we have drafted a paper titled “Objectively-measured smartphone usage, sleep quality, and physical activity among Chinese adolescents and young adults” and it is currently under review in Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. Objective 3 of this study is to evaluate the validity of self-reported smartphone usage against objectively-measured data. We found that the participants over-reported the total time spent on smartphone for around 760 min per week (self-reported 1930.3 min/wk vs objectively-measured 1170.7 min/wk, p<0.001), or an over-report of 64.9%. Most of the over-reporting was contributed by the web browsing domain (self-reported 447.8 min/wk vs objectively-measured 33.3 min/wk, p<0.001). For the results of Objective 3, we have drafted a paper titled “Validation of self-reported smartphone usage against objectively-measured smartphone usage in Hong Kong Chinese adolescents and young adults” and it is currently under review in Mobile Media & Communication. Objective 4 of this study is to compare the subjective well-being of using smartphone and other daily activities. The regression on all response records showed that, compared with not using smartphone, participants had higher net affect score (difference = 0.10, p = 0.03) when using smartphone. The regression on response records without smartphone usage showed that one hour of not using smartphone was associated a reduced net affect score of 0.03 (p=0.006). The paper for the results of Objective 4 is under preparation.

25105616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25105616.value: We are collaborating with Dr Uichin Lee from the Department of Knowledge Service Engineering of the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology on smartphone usage pattern of university students. Dr Uichin Lee had concurrently collected smartphone usage data on 63 university students in his institute. A preliminary analysis showed that Korean students spent more than 12 hours per day in smartphone while Hong Kong students spent only 2 hours. Further comparison analysis of our data will be conducted.

25105616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25105616.value: This study was conducted from March 2017 to May 2018. The participants were recruited from one secondary school (Tai Po Sam Yuk Secondary School) and two universities (Hong Kong Polytechnic University and Education University of Hong Kong) in Hong Kong. We installed a smartphone usage tracking app on the smartphone of all of the participants' smartphone for seven consecutive days. This app tracked the opening and closing of all apps in the smartphone. During the seven-day monitoring period, all of the participants concurrently wore an ActiGraph GT3X accelerometer. This is a wrist-worn, water-proof accelerometer that has been validated for measuring sitting time, physical activity, and sleeping time. We found that (1) time spent on social network apps and games and comics apps was associated with total sleeping time, and time spent on social network apps, instant messaging apps, and multimedia apps were associated with the number of steps and MVPA among Hong Kong Chinese adolescents and young adults; (2) self-reported smartphone usage had large discrepancies with objectively-measured smartphone usage; and (3) participants had higher net affect score when using smartphone.

25200616.label: Project Objectives
25200616.value: to understand the air trapping process in drainage pipelines under different stormwater drainage conditions based on numerical modeling and experimental tests. The modified SPH-based 2D model and laboratory experiments are adopted for this investigation; to study the physical mechanism and evolution process of transient water-air flows in drainage pipelines under different system and ventilation conditions through numerical simulations and experimental tests, with the results used for characterizing key factors affecting transient water-air flows and establishing appropriate relationships of transient water-air interactions such as interfacial pressure function and motion; to apply the validated model and experimental tests to the situations of drainage pipelines with different configurations and operation conditions, so as to facilitate the understanding and modeling of transient water-air flows in USDS (e.g., transient water-air flow responses at junction); to integrate the results of this project into usable program packages for purposes of education activities and practical applications in terms of urban drainage hydraulics.

25200616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200616.value: Urban stormwater drainage system (USDS) becomes more important to urban flooding control and management under the influences of global climate change and rapid urbanization. The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNISDR) reported over 100 urban flooding disasters per year worldwide during 1980~2008 and these events have resulted in more than 6,700 deaths. Many of these accidents are caused or exacerbated by drainage problems due to the occurrence of transient water-air two-phase flows within USDSs. During times of high flows, air is easily trapped in poorly ventilated drainage pipelines and these air pockets act as blockages that severely reduce the system drainage capacity. In addition, the complex dynamics of the air-water interaction can cause dangerous geysering, where water is expelled from the system with great force, as seen in many USDSs worldwide including Hong Kong. Previous experimental and numerical studies have demonstrated that the interaction between water and air in transient drainage process is complicated due to the large differences in fluid densities and viscosities, pipe topology changes and pressure oscillations at water-air interfaces. Because of these complexities, current measurements and models are unable to capture and predict the potentially dangerous transient water-air interactions and flow process in USDS. Significant exploration and fundamental research on the formation mechanism and evolution of transient water-air pipe flows is needed to fill the gap of this theory and practice. This proposed research will: (1) investigate the air trapping and propagation processes in drainage pipelines during transient stormwater events; (2) study the behavior and evolution of transient water-air interface (e.g., pressure and motion) and flow geysering in drainage pipelines under different system and ventilation conditions; (3) examine and characterize transient water-air flows in complex multiple-pipeline drainage networks under different geometrical and hydraulic conditions. To achieve these objectives, the novel deliverables of this research will include: (1) develop a two-dimensional (2D) model based on the modified meshless Smoothed-Particle-Hydrodynamics (SPH) scheme to effectively simulate transient water-air flows under different drainage conditions; (2) carry out an extensive laboratory experimental program for calibrating and validating the developed 2D model; (3) apply the validated model and experimental program to complex drainage systems including single, branched and vent pipelines; (4) investigate key factors/relationships governing the transient water-air interactions and flow process in stormwater drainage pipelines. This project will make scientific advances in the understanding and modeling of transient air-water flows as well as practical contributions in the design and management of USDS. 隨著全球氣候變暖和城市化節奏的日益加快，城市雨洪排水系統的管理面臨更加嚴峻的挑戰，雨洪控制變得愈發舉足輕重。聯合國減輕災害風險部門（UNISDR）的調查發現，在1980~2008期間，世界範圍內平均每年逾百起重大洪澇災害并造成6700例死亡事故。事實上，這些事故的發生與排水系統中的氣水兩相流的瞬變作用密切相關。當水流急速匯入排水管網時，極易攜帶氣泡捲入，而在排氣不通暢的管道中，留存的氣泡則相當程度地阻礙了水體流動，嚴重降低了管網的排水能力。此外，錯綜複雜的氣水交互動態過程可能導致更加危險的井噴（間歇泉）現象，而產生巨大的作用力將洪流從管道的檢查井等處噴出，包括香港在內的許多城市已有相關報導。 前期的實驗及數值模擬研究發現，氣水瞬變過程中的水動力複雜性與氣水兩相流體的密度以及粘性的巨大差異、管道拓撲結構的變化、以及氣水交界面的壓力震盪密切相關。對此，基於目前現有的測量手段和相關數值模型，還無法模擬類比並預測氣水瞬變的動態變化，更無法重現排水管道中潛在而危險的井噴等複雜現象。因此，對於氣水瞬變流的動態演變及形成機理的初步研究和探索已迫在眉睫，研究成果有利於填補該領域在理論和實踐方面的空缺。 為此，本研究將致力於： (1) 探討排水管道中氣水瞬變過程中氣泡在水體中的交互運動過程； (2) 研究在不同的管道系統和排氣工況下，氣水接觸介面的壓力、張力等參數變化的動態過程及井噴現象的演變過程； (3) 測試在複雜多變的排水管道系統中，不同的幾何水力條件下的氣水瞬變流的特徵。 本研究的創新成果包括：(a) 建立基於改進的無網格光滑粒子法（SPH）的數值模型，從而高效模擬不同排水工況下的氣水瞬變流；(b) 搭建相應的物理實驗平臺，通過完善的實驗論證來校核本項目發展的數值模型；(c) 將校驗好的數值模型應用於複雜條件下的排水管網系統，並與實驗結果相比較；(d) 探究在排水管網中影響氣水兩相瞬變流的交互過程的核心因素及因素之間的相互關係。該項目的研究成果可進一步推動氣水兩相流的理論發展及模型構建，也為現實的城市排水系統雨洪設計和管理工程提供理論基礎與實用工具。

25200616.label: Realisation of objectives
25200616.value: The objectives of this project listed in section 5.2 have been well achieved through the numerical simulations and laboratory experiments planned for this research. In details: (1) the 2D numerical models were established by the modified SPH scheme, which could improve greatly the computational efficiency of the pipeline flows, especially under fast changing (transient) conditions. The established model has been well validated by benchmark cases from the literature, with the results published in the key & top journals in this field (e.g., ASME journal of fluids engineering; ASCE Journal of Hydraulics Engineering & Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management; IAHR Journal of Hydraulics Research; Water Resources Management; etc., with more details referred to the outputs in Part C). (2) a laboratory experimental test system was designed and set up for transient water-air two phase flows, in which the air entrapping and air-water interactions can be visualized by high-speed camera and video facilities equipped in the PI’s hydraulics laboratory. The pressure data have been secured by the high-resolution transducers (with a sampling frequency of 1024 Hz), which could be stored and treated by the equipped computer and software (embedded software for the transducers). Before its application, thorough calibrations have been performed on this system based on the benchmark cases from the references. Afterwards, the obtained data were used for validating and verifying the 2D model, as well as for systematic analysis for this project. (3) based on the validated 2D model and established experimental system, various application cases were carried out for data integration and analysis, so as to provide the fundamental understanding and practical application of transient water-air flows in drainage systems. Meanwhile, the developed model and experimental test data from this project have been well packaged for future use. (4) all the key results and findings from this project have been published on the important journals in this field as well as presented in the professional conferences in the community. The details refer to the outputs in Part C of this report. Finally, it is also noted that, due to the limitation of experimental test space and facilities, the complex drainage pipe systems were not well achieved, for example the influence of junction configurations and flow confluences on the transient water-air flows proposed in the original application. This might be the potential difficulty encountered for achieving project. However, such issues have been successfully addressed through the numerical simulations and theoretical analysis which are not confined by the space limit and facility capacity. From this perspective, the objectives of this project have been well achieved (100%) during the project period.
