25200616.label: Major findings and research outcome
25200616.value: This project has been achieved to investigate the transient water-air two-phase flows in the urban stormwater drainage system (USDS), with aims to: (a) understand the air entrapping and propagation processes in drainage pipelines during transient stormwater events; (b) exmaine the behavior and evolution of transient water-air interface (pressure and motion) and flow geysering in drainage pipelines under different system and ventilation conditions; and (c) characterize transient water-air flows in drainage pipelines under different geometrical and hydraulic conditions. With achieving these objectives, the main findings mainly include: (1) development of two-dimensional (2D) model based on the modified meshless Smoothed-Particle-Hydrodynamics (SPH) scheme, with great improvement for the computational efficiency for the simulations of transient water-air flows; (2) establishment of a laboratory experimental system for extensive tests for calibrating and validating the developed 2D model under different conditions; (3) applications of the validated model to complex drainage processes so as to examine the key influence factors and relationships governing transient water-air interactions and flow process in stormwater drainage pipelines. Based on these results and findings, the main outcomes of this research can be summarized as follows: (i) in total 14 journal papers have been published directly from this project in key/top journals of hydraulics and water resources, which have provided substantial progress on this research topic (e.g., ASCE Journal of Hydraulics Engineering; IAHR Journal of Hydraulics Research; Water Resources Management; ASME journal of fluids engineering; etc.). (ii) the results and findings have also been presented in front of peers and experts in this field in the international conferences and workshops, so as to gain essential feedback and connections with other research groups. (iii) two PhD students have been successfully trained and graduated during the project period, and seven undergraduate students (4 part-time student assistants and 3 final year project students) have been educated through participating this research project, which is also one of key objectives and outcomes for this project (i.e., young generation education and training purpose). (iv) external collaborations have been carried out for the research plans of this project, which has led to both international and national connections on this research. More details on the findings and outcome of this research project, including publication outputs, young research students training and external collaborations, can be found in the Part C of this report.

25200616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25200616.value: As stated in the objectives in Section 5 and achievements in Section 6.1, all the key tasks of this project have been well achieved. Through the implementation process of this project, it has been also found that there are potentials for the further development of this research topic can be performed for future work, including (but not limited to): (1) more complex drainage pipeline configurations and surrounding environmental conditions, for example pipe networks, surface drainage and runoff process, elevation variation of pipeline, open and closed channel conditions as well as the outfalls into coastal waters. (2) water quality issues raised by the transient water-air two-phase flows in urban drainage systems, such as air-waters-solid three-phase flows and environmental pollution. To extend such research work, it will involve more practical factors and urban conditions, which requires more collaboration with local government department and authorities so as to gain enough geographical and hydrological/hydraulic information. To this end, an engineering R&D project and/or technology transfer project may be more suitable to continue and extend the results and findings of current project to more realistic and practical systems.

25200616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25200616.value: With the influences of global climate change and rapid urbanization, extreme rainstorm events are increasing in intensity and frequency worldwide, causing significant economic losses as well as social and environmental problems. In particular, the flooding risks and drainage disasters have become more severe in the urban stormwater drainage system (USDS). To this end, this project has been motivated to investigate and develop fundamental theories and methods for transient water-air interactions in drainage pipelines during rapid and severe storm surge events that may causes flooding risks. Through the outputs (e.g., publications and presentations) and deliverables (models and datasets) directly from this project, this research project could make significance and value in both scientific and practical fields. Regarding scientific significance, the results of this research are useful to the in-depth understanding and modeling of transient water-air flows in USDS, mitigating flooding and explosive disasters in such systems. Regarding the practical values, the integrated modeling tools and various test datasets from this research could lead to better design and operate the USDS projects conducted in Hong Kong and elsewhere in the world. Furthermore, the achievement of this research project can provide support for relevant public policy developments for the USDS in Hong Kong.

25201416.label: Project Objectives
25201416.value: Models and principles of the developed single-pixel optical encryption systems are illustrated, and the applicability of various single-pixel optical imaging architectures, such as interference and computer-generated hologram, is analyzed. Design flexibility or system variety of single-pixel imaging configurations is demonstrated. Feasibility of the designed big data environment is analyzed, and it will be studied how big data can be generated in the developed single-pixel optical encryption systems. The big-data environment or concept will be clearly defined in the context of optical encryption. One or multiple marks are further encoded by using optical encryption approach, and their corresponding security keys or one-dimensional ciphertexts are compressed and embedded into the designed big data environment. These marks, acting like watermarks, can be recovered by using compressive sensing algorithms, or can be directly authenticated by using correlation algorithms to identify the targeted security keys or ciphertexts from the designed big data environment during the decoding. It will be illustrated that the developed optical cryptosystems can achieve much higher security compared with conventional optical encryption methods, since big data concept is designed and applied. The characteristics (i.e., sensitivity, robustness and security) of each developed single-pixel optical big-data encryption system are illustrated, and system performance against various attacks is studied, such as against known-plaintext attack and chosen-ciphertext attack. It will be demonstrated that big-data compression algorithms (such as anamorphic transformation) and software platform (such as based on C++) can be developed to facilitate applications of the proposed systems. In addition, fundamental principles of connection interface to single-mode or multi-mode fiber communication are illustrated.

25201416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25201416.value: Information security has become one of the most serious concerns in our modern society, and much research has been going on the development of various algorithms and technologies to protect information. Since traditional schemes may not be provably secure and feasible in all applications, there is a continued need to utilize every possible technology to enhance the security and flexibility. In recent years, optical encryption approach is considered as a promising alternative, and has been rapidly developed. However, there are still some major concerns as follows: 1) Two-dimensional recording method is usually applied in optical encryption systems, and design flexibility of optical encryption systems is restricted by conventional imaging principles and setups. 2) Some optical encryption systems have been proven vulnerably to the attacks. 3) Conventional optical encryption systems have not been effectively investigated and integrated with the related areas for an interdisciplinary study to explore new applications. These concerns motivate the applicant to investigate new optical encryption architectures. In this research proposal, single-pixel optical big-data encryption systems are developed for securing information. Instead of conventional two-dimensional recording methods, single-pixel imaging principles and configurations, i.e., using single-pixel bucket detector, are systematically investigated by using wave interference and diffraction theories to enhance design flexibility or system variety. Big data environment is clearly defined in the context of optical encryption, and is further designed and integrated into the developed single-pixel optical encryption architectures to enhance the security. Either virtual-optics (i.e., digital) or optical approach can be employed to implement the proposed systems, which effectively guarantees the applicability. High design flexibility and high security are achieved in the developed single-pixel optical big-data encryption systems, and an interface to electronic cryptography is also designed for an interdisciplinary study. The developed single-pixel optical big-data encryption systems can endure various attacks. In addition, big-data compression algorithms are investigated and applied to facilitate the transmission and storage. The existing concerns, such as low system flexibility using only two-dimensional recording method and low security using few-input processing approach, are fully resolved. There will be a long-term benefit that an effective and powerful alternative using single-pixel imaging and big data is applicable to encrypt information. The applicant has conducted extensive research related to optical encryption over the past several years, and the related work is widely recognized. The research experience and well-equipped laboratory can assist the applicant to achieve the objectives of this research proposal. 信息安全已經成為當今社會最令人擔心的問題之一。針對信息安全問題，許多學者已經開展了大量的科學研究並且開發了各種加密算法和技術。由於傳統的加密策略不能在所有的應用情況下都具有較高的安全性與可行性，所以很有必要研究其它的潛在技術從而能夠增強安全性和靈活度。近年來，光學加密方法被認為是較有前景的方法之一，並且已經得到了迅速地發展。但是，它仍然存在著一些嚴重問題：1) 由於光學加密系統通常使用二維採集方法，所以傳統光學加密系統的設計靈活度將會受限於二維成像原理和結構。 2) 一些光學加密系統已經被證明容易受到攻擊。 3) 許多傳統的光學加密系統還沒有得到有效的研究以使之能夠與相關領域進行融合，因此還不能開展跨學科的研究以探索新的應用課題。針對這些問題，本項目將研究新的光學加密架構。將研究面向信息安全的單像素光學大數據加密系統。不同於傳統的二維採集方法，本項目將會基於光干涉和衍射理論來系統性地研究單像素成像原理和結構(即使用單像素採集器)，從而能夠提高系統設計的靈活度或多樣性。將會在光學加密系統中明確地定義大數據環境，並且將它融合到單像素光學加密架構中從而增強系統安全性。本項目將使用虛擬光學方法(即數字方法)或者實際光學方法來執行所設計的系統，從而能夠有效地保障系統的適用範圍。所設計的單像素光學大數據加密系統具有高度的設計靈活度與安全性。也將設計一個與電子加密方法相連的接口，從而能夠開展跨學科的研究。所設計的單像素光學大數據加密系統能夠承受各種攻擊。除此之外，也將研究大數據壓縮算法從而有利於傳輸和存儲。本項目將能夠充分地解決一些現有的科學問題，比如基於二維採集的低靈活度問題以及基於少量數據採集的低安全性問題。從長遠發展來看，本項目所研究的基於單像素成像和大數據的光學系統能夠為信息安全領域提供一種有效的、強大的方法。在過去的幾年裡，項目負責人已經開展了大量有關於光學加密的科學研究，而且許多研究工作得到了廣泛地認可。項目負責人擁有豐富的研究經驗，而且所在的顯微及傳感實驗室具有良好的儀器設備。這些基礎將有助於項目負責人實現所設定的研究目標。

25201416.label: Realisation of objectives
25201416.value: All objectives of this RGC ECS research project have been fully realized. Research work has been successfully conducted to obtain significant research results and realize all objectives. (1) In this research project, we have successfully designed and illustrated the models and principles of single-pixel optical encryption, and various single-pixel optical imaging architectures, e.g., interference and computer-generated hologram, have been designed and applied for optically securing information. Interferometric and non-interferometric imaging based optical security systems have been fully investigated and illustrated. In this research project, high design flexibility and high variety have been achieved using different single-pixel imaging configurations. (2) In this research project, big data environment has been designed and investigated, and how big data can be generated using single-pixel optical encryption has been analyzed and successfully completed. In this research project, big data environment has been successfully applied to configure optical security systems in order to achieve high security. We found and illustrated how to correctly identify or retrieve the plaintexts hidden in big data environment, e.g., via optical authentication. During the project implementation, we also found that the designed big data environment can be applied by combing with the state-of-the-art deep learning technologies to attack other existing optical security systems. In this research project, we have realized the objectives that the developed optical cryptosystems can achieve much higher security compared with conventional optical encryption methods, since big data concept has been designed and applied. (3) We have completed the analyses of characteristics (i.e., sensitivity, robustness and security) of each developed single-pixel optical big-data encryption system, and system performance against various attacks has been fully studied. Data compression algorithms and authentication strategies have been developed to be applied in the designed big data environment. In addition to the hardware used in optical setups, various algorithms have been developed to facilitate applications of the proposed optical security systems. Fundamental principles about the distribution of security keys and ciphertext, e.g., the transmission, have also been fully investigated.

25201416.label: Major findings and research outcome
25201416.value: In this RGC ECS research project, the major findings are as follows: (1) We find that various single-pixel imaging principles and configurations can be systematically investigated and designed in big data environment for optically securing information. In this research project, big data concept has been clearly defined in the context of optical encryption for the first time. (2) In this research project, we find that single-pixel detection or imaging can be flexibly explained from quantum or classical domain, and a number of input data can be encoded into one-dimensional ciphertext. (3) We find that when the big data environment is properly designed and applied, various optical setups, e.g., interference and single-path optical diffraction, can be flexibly applied during single-pixel optical encoding. The low design flexibility problem existing in conventional optical security systems is fully resolved, and optical encryption architectures are greatly enriched. (4) We find that much higher security has been fully achieved in the developed optical encryption systems using big data environment and single-pixel detection, and effective strategies can be designed to fully withstand various attacks. (5) We find that the designed big data environment is not only suitable to configure optical security systems using single-pixel detection approaches, but also can be combined with the state-of-the-art machine learning approaches to dramatically enlarge the key space, e.g., a large number of optimized weights and biases. In this research project, research outcomes are as follows: (i) Supported by this RGC ECS research project, 19 peer-reviewed high-quality international journal papers, e.g., Optics Express and Optics Letters etc, have been published, and 12 international conference papers have been published and delivered. (ii) Supported by this RGC ECS research project, one Ph.D. student Ms. Zhou Lina has been trained. The oral examination of Ms ZHOU Lina’s Ph.D. thesis has already been held on 24 March 2021 in The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Ms Zhou Lina’s Ph.D. degree is expected to be confirmed in June or July 2021 in The Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

25201416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25201416.value: In this RGC ECS research project, we have successfully designed and applied big data environment into single-pixel optical encryption area, and significant advantages, e.g., high security and high system flexibility, have been demonstrated. It is expected that in addition to single-pixel detection, CCD camera can also be applied with various imaging methods in order to explore the wider applications using big data concept designed in this research project. Big data environment has been designed and applied for single-pixel optical encryption, and intelligent distribution of ciphertext and security keys is worth investigating. In addition, the interdisciplinary study using metasurface is also suggested.

25201416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25201416.value: Information security has been well recognized as one of the most serious concerns in our society. It is believed that when important or confidential information is not secured, there would be a great threat. Compared to electronic methods, optical technology has been explored as one of the most promising alternatives for securing information, and has attracted much attention in many application areas. Optics can provide many degrees of freedom to handle parameters, and optical technology possesses inherent nature of optical signal processing, e.g., parallel and multi-dimensional capabilities. In this RGC ECS research project, we have successfully designed and integrated big data environment into single-pixel optical encryption, and compared to conventional methods the higher security, higher robustness and higher design flexibility have been achieved. We illustrated how to correctly identify or retrieve multiple plaintexts hidden in big data environment, e.g., via optical authentication. We have fully completed the analysis of characteristics (i.e., sensitivity, robustness and security) of the developed single-pixel optical big-data encryption systems, and system performance against various attacks has been fully studied. More application areas can be continuously explored by using the single-pixel optical big-data encryption systems completed in this research project.

25202416.value: To design, fabricate and characterize a new type of yarn-based strain sensor based on a tri-coaxial yarn architecture that offers good elasticity, repeatability and durability, low hysteresis, high sensitivity as well as a good match in mechanical property with rest of the yarns in the elastic fabric. 25202416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25202416.value: Fabric-based sensors are soft, flexible, deformable, durable and washable, so that they are appropriate for applications on the human body. The elastic woven fabrics have a stable structure, the durability and the elasticity and deformability of knitted fabric if designed properly. In order to fully utilize the sensing potentials of elastic woven fabrics, three key issues need to be addressed: (i) Yarn strain sensing elements for fabric should have good elasticity, repeatability and durability, low hysteresis, high sensitivity as well as a good match in mechanical property with rest of the yarns in the elastic fabric. Lack of such kind of yarn sensing elements has been the one of obstacles to achieving desired sensing performance of fabrics. (ii) Fabric structures are critical to reduce interfiber friction thus decrease hysteresis and enhance repeatability of sensing fabric. Woven constructions with elastic yarn have a highly potential to overcome these difficulties. Yet, up to date very little studies have been reported on the design and fabrication of such fabrics. (iii) The design and fabrication of such sensing fabrics depend on a scientific understanding of their electro-mechanical properties and the influential factors. However, there is a lack of reported work on elastic woven sensing fabrics and the scientific mechanisms remain unclear. To address the aforementioned issues, this project proposes to systematically perform a theoretical analysis and experimental study on the electro-mechanical properties and sensing mechanism of elastic woven strain sensing fabrics as well as effects of the yarn sensing element and fabric structure. A new yarn strain sensor will be developed to achieve above sensing performance through a proposed tri-coaxial yarn architecture for the elastic core, conductive and insulation layers. Elastic sateen and honeycomb woven sensing fabrics featured with long yarn floats and less binding points will be fabricated by integrating the yarn sensing element via weaving technology. An experimental study will be conducted to investigate the electro-mechanical property and sensing mechanism of the fabric by investigating its deformation and corresponding deformation of the yarn sensing elements. A model on the electro-mechanical properties of the fabric will be established by using the micromechanical modeling. The verified model will reveal the effect of the yarn sensing elements and fabric structure on the fabric sensing property and then be applied to fabricate improved sensing fabrics. In the long term, the proposed project could provide engineering guidance to the design and fabrication of woven sensing fabrics. 織物傳感器具有柔性、可變形性和穿戴性等特點，所以非常適合用於人體。為了充分利用彈力機織物的傳感特性，其研發需要解決三個問題：1. 紗線傳感元件必須具有優良的彈性和重複性，以及低的滯後性。2. 織物結構對於減少纖維間的摩擦力，從而降低滯後性和提高傳感織物的重複性是至關重要的。3.設計和製作這樣的傳感織物必須充分理解他們的機電性能和影響因素。為了解決上述問題，該項目將對彈性傳感機織物的機電性能和傳感原理，以及紗線傳感元件和織物結構的影響進行系統性的理論分析和實驗研究。將研發新的紗線傳感元件並在此基礎上通過織造技術開發彈性機織物傳感器並進行實驗研究，探討該織物的機電性能和傳感原理。從長遠來看，該項目將為機織傳感織物的設計和研發提供工程化指引。

25202416.label: Realisation of objectives
25202416.value: Objective 1: The objective 1 has totally been achieved. New yarn piezoresistive strain sensors with good mechanical and electromechanical properties were designed and fabricated based on a tri-coaxial structure that comprises polyurethane (PU) yarn core, graphene/poly(vinyl alcohol) or Ag-nanoparticles/graphene-microsheets composite sheath as well as the outer polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) insulation layer using layer-by-layer assembly method. During the fabrication, we found that mussel-inspired polydopamine (PDA) is a unique adhesive and skin-friendly material for packaging the sensing structure. Therefore, PDA was introduced into the sensor system, leading to an enhancement of the interfacial adhesion between the PU yarn core and conductive sheath, the stability of the sensing layer and the integrality of the sensor. The effects of important influential factors on the sensing performance of sensors were investigated, including concentration of graphene dispersion and number of graphene coatings; on that basis, the optimized material and fabrication parameters were identified. The yarn strain sensors developed were characterized in terms of their morphological structure, mechanical and electromechanical properties as well as thermal properties, including the surface and cross-section, tensile, resistivity, sensitivity, linearity, repeatability as well as hysteresis. Objective 2: The objective 2 has totally been achieved. Various elastic woven fabric substrates were designed for fabricating the sensing fabrics wherein the specially designed 2D sateen, modified sateen/double-weave as well as 3D honeycomb structures feature weft yarn with a long float length and have less binding points with warps or even weft yarns with a straight configuration and no binding in the fabric. Based on these structures, the strain sensing fabrics with very good sensing performance were successful developed through the incorporation of the yarn-based strain sensors developed in Objective 1 into fabric structures using a Dobby weaving machine. The developed strain sensing yarn was integrated as a weft yarn into intended positions in the fabric structures, thus retaining a straight configuration for obtaining enhanced linearity and reduced hysteresis of the resultant strain sensing fabrics. The structure parameters were varied to fabricate sensing fabrics to obtain different electromechanical properties and optimized parameters, including fabric density, linear density of elastic yarn as well as tension applied on the yarn during the weaving process. Objective 3: The objective 3 has totally been achieved. The experimental investigation was conducted on the mechanical and electro-mechanical properties of the above woven strain sensing fabrics integrated with the yarn strain sensor under unidirectional tension. The load-displacement and electro-mechanical resistance-strain curves were generated. Based on these curves, the strain sensing woven fabrics developed were characterized in terms of sensing properties, including gauge factor, repeatability, linearity, hysteresis and fatigue. The geometry changes of the fabric and corresponding yarn deformation within both the plane and cross-section of the fabric were examined and analyzed by using an in-situ photography system and encapsulation method. As a result, the relationships between fabric strain and resultant strain and electrical resistance of yarn sensor were established. The effects of yarn linear density, elastic core yarn linear density and fabric weft density and weave structure on the mechanical and electromechanical properties of sensing fabrics were investigated for obtaining the optimized sensing performance. Objective 4: The objective 4 has totally been achieved. The geometry models of elastic sateen and honeycomb fabrics have been developed. Based on these models, micromechanical and finite element models of fabrics have been established, which can elaborate on the relationship among the applied load on the fabric and the resultant fabric displacement as well as local deformation of yarn sensors in the elastic weft direction. Furthermore, a parametric study was conducted to investigate the effects of structural parameters of fabric on the relationship between the applied fabric strain and the resulting yarn strain, including warp yarn spacing and diameter as well as fabric structure phase. Based on these analyses and the measured electromechanical properties of the yarn sensing element, the models which can be used to predict the electromechanical properties of the sensing fabrics were successfully established. Objective 5: The objective 5 has totally been achieved. The comparisons between experimental and simulated yarn strains as well as resultant electrical resistance subjected to the fabric strains were conducted. A series of simulations were also carried out for understanding the deformation mechanism and thus optimizing the tensile properties and thus the electromechanical properties of elastic sensing fabrics. Based on the developed strain sensing fabrics, the application of such sensing fabrics on detecting various human motions was explored and the sensing performance was also evaluated for fabricating enhanced versions of sensing fabrics.

25202416.label: Major findings and research outcome
25202416.value: 1. New yarn-based strain sensors with good mechanical and electromechanical properties developed by using elastic polyurethane yarn as a sensing yarn core, graphene/poly(vinyl alcohol) or Ag-nanoparticles/graphene-microsheets composite as a sensing yarn sheath layer as well as the polydimethylsiloxane as an insulation outer layer. It is found that the introduction of polydopamine into the sensor system can greatly enhance the interfacial adhesion between the polyurethane yarn core and conductive sheath and stability of the sensing layer. This study has provided a new approach to fabricate yarn sensors with a simple and scalable way. (Part C: Publications 1-2) Besides, this method has been further developed to deposit silver nanoparticles on cotton fabric/paper assisted by polydopamine to fabricate mechanically and electrically durable e-textiles, including sensing fabrics. (Part C: Publications 5-6). 2. New woven structure-based sensing fabrics developed through the incorporation of yarn-based strain sensors by using existing weaving technologies, which feature with very good and stable sensing performance without interfering with the exceptional properties and comfort of the fabric. The experimental studies have confirmed that woven structures featured with long yarn ﬂoats and less interlacing yarn points enable the reduced interﬁber friction between yarns and sensors, leading to the enhanced sensing properties including low hysteresis and outstanding repeatability. It is also found that the yarn sensor embedded in the sateen substrate experienced different evolution stages. Besides, the yarn sensor within the modiﬁed sateen can deform in a very similar lever with the fabric extension. This study has developed a technical-feasible and cost-effective method based on a new integration of yarn sensor and weaving technology for fabricating wearable fabric-based strain sensors. (Part C: Publications 1-3). 3. The geometrical, micromechanical and finite element models established to elaborate on the relationship among the applied load on the fabric and the resultant fabric displacement as well as local deformation of yarn sensors in the elastic weft direction. Based on these models and analyses on the measured electromechanical properties of the yarn sensing element subjected to the applied fabric strain, the models can be used to predict the electromechanical properties of the sensing fabrics. (Part C: Publications 3-4). 4. Finite element model developed to simulate the yarn strain within the woven fabric subjected to the fabric strain with varied fabric structural parameters for fabricating sensing fabrics with desired sensing performance. (Part C: Publication 4). 5. Six refereed journals, and two presentations and one best poster award at an international conference.

25202416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25202416.value: The proposed project concerns a systematic investigation of elastic woven strain sensing fabrics. New yarn-based strain sensors are first designed and fabricated based on a tri-coaxial yarn architecture, which can offer good elasticity and repeatability, low hysteresis, high sensitivity as well as easy fabrication and integration into the structure of fabric for strain sensing. With the yarn sensor used as the strain sensing element, new elastic woven strain sensing fabrics are easily and effectively developed through weaving technology. A theoretical analysis and experimental study has be carried out on the mechanical and electro-mechanical properties of the woven strain sensing fabrics. For the first time, research work on the strain sensing mechanism of woven sensing fabrics and determining the effect of yarn sensing elements and fabric structure on the sensing performance can be carried out. Models are finally developed to predict the electromechanical properties of the fabric sensor. The study will provide engineering guidance to the design and fabrication of woven strain sensing fabrics. The investigation will promote the new development of textile-based wearable electronics for applications in health care, rehabilitation, and sports and occupational wear and thus increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile and electronic industries.

25202616.label: Realisation of objectives
25202616.value: This project investigated the effects of thermo-acoustic devices and vibration-based energy harvesting techniques. The proposed four objectives have been fully addressed over the 3-year project period. The major achievements of this project included: (i) a broadband thermo-acoustic device and its applications [objectives 1 and 2]; (ii) a thermo-acoustic line array loudspeaker and its interference effect [objectives 1 and 2]; (iii) a nonlinear multi-stable piezomagnetoelastic harvester array that can work well within 3 m/s2 and 20 Hz [objectives 3 and 4]; (iv) a tri-hybrid energy harvester, coupled with the piezoelectric, electromagnetic and triboelectric approaches, with a septuple-stable nonlinearity-enhanced mechanical frequency up-conversion mechanism to operate at 2-12.5 Hz [objectives 3 and 4]; (v) a magnetic levitation-based tri-stable energy harvester that can work well under 3-8 Hz [objectives 3 and 4]; (vi) a force-amplified piezoelectric stack energy harvester under pressure fluctuations in hydraulic pipeline systems [objectives 3 and 4]; and (vii) an ultra-low-frequency multi-stable tri-hybrid energy harvester that can perform under 1-11 Hz. The proposed energy harvesters have shown promising applications in various engineering fields (e.g., railway vibration, biomechanical energy, and motorized equipment) to enable as a sustainable power source for wearable/portable electronics and wireless monitoring systems. Both theoretical and experimental studies have been conducted, the present outcomes are beyond the scope of the objectives. In addition to the aforementioned results, there are some relevant research studies under the support of this project.

25202616.label: Major findings and research outcome
25202616.value: The major findings and outcome of this project have been reported in seven research publications [1, 2, 6-10]. The first two papers [1, 2] mainly investigated the performance of thermo-acoustic transducers. This is a next generation of sound speakers without any mechanical vibration system to exhibit an extremely wide frequency response range. In these studies, acoustic field responses to broadband input signals applied to free-standing, nano-thinfilm-substrate, and phased-array-type thermo-acoustic devices were theoretically developed. The characteristics of pressure and angular distributions in a space were also examined. Besides, both frequency- and power-dependent pressure responses were compared with the available experimental results to validate the accuracy of these analytical models, an excellent agreement between analytical solutions and published experimental results has been reported. Potential applications of the thermo-acoustic transducers were also presented in an international conference (Railway Engineering 2017). On the other hand, various new vibration-based hybrid energy harvesters [6-10], using the piezoelectric, electromagnetic and triboelectric approaches, have been successfully developed to increase the working performance under broadband, random and low-frequency sources. The prime concern of these research studies focused on the exploration of mechanical nonlinearities in vibration-based energy harvesting, and the electromechanical coupling between mechanical transducers and adaptive electronic circuits for maximizing power output and minimizing energy loss during the power management. The PI and his research team firstly proposed the septuple-stable nonlinearity-enhanced mechanical frequency up-conversion mechanism (published in Nano Energy [7]) that not only enhances the output performance of the frequency up-conversion via inter-well motions, and also offers a wide and highly efficient operating bandwidth at low acceleration through the combination of resonant inter-well oscillation behavior and non-resonant behavior. The dynamic behavior of the inter-well jumping phenomenon under different external excitations and parameter turning strategies was investigated. An adaptive electronic circuit (rectifier bridge circuit) was connected to the energy harvesters to study their power gain and consumption. Furthermore, bifurcation instabilities and chaotic motions of the nonlinear systems in energy harvesting were also examined. All these studies involved the proof-of-concept, prototype design, theoretical analysis and experimental work to verify the working efficiency of the proposed energy harvesting techniques in real-engineering conditions (e.g., structural/mechanical vibration and human motions). A series of comparison studies were also carried out to show the power density of such newly proposed devices with other recently reported harvesters in the literature. Other relevant outputs (i.e., [3-5]) are the research spinoffs under the support of this project.

25202616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25202616.value: Evolving the IoT and artificial intelligence in smart cities leads to the tremendous development of wireless sensor networks, the demand for mobile or distributed power supplies is thus of paramount importance. To address these technical demands, scavenging energy from vibration-induced sources has been the subject of studies to develop built-in energy harvesters for various potential applications. To further enhance the energy conversion efficiency, how to optimize the design of dedicated electronic circuits for vibration-based hybrid energy harvesters is still a crucial issue. In the future study, the design of optimized electronic circuits will be explored to improve the working performance of such self-powered devices with a low-load dependence.

25202616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25202616.value: The rapid development of vibration-based energy harvesting techniques has become a challenging topic, because the capture of renewable energy from the ambient environment offers a promising platform to support the explosive growth of a wide range of technical demands. The working principle of such techniques is to convert vibrational energy into electrical energy. Due to the limitations of a single working mechanism under low-amplitude, low-frequency, and time-varying ambient sources, a hybrid system design that couples the piezoelectric, electromagnetic and other mechanisms together has emerged as a new direction to increase the working performance of vibration-driven energy harvesters. By integrating multiple transduction mechanisms, more electrical energy can be converted from vibrational motions and the advantages of different transduction mechanisms can be compacted into a single hub. In addition, the application of multi-stable nonlinearity-enhanced mechanisms in energy harvesting plays a critical role in improving the working performance of such energy harvesters under low excitations. The research outcomes of the present work will offer practical applications in various engineering fields.

25202916.label: Project Objectives
25202916.value: To develop a multi-channel spectral-tuneable LED lighting platform. The platform will include a lighting system, a measurement system, and a viewing booth. The lighting system will have better performances than the state-of-art system in different aspects, allowing comprehensive investigation of visual responses to light stimuli. To investigate the white region in object mode under various lighting conditions generated by the lighting system. To develop a new metric to characterize the perceived whiteness of a material under an arbitrary light source. The development of such a metric includes a) the investigation of the direction and magnitude of chromaticity shift for enhanced whiteness appearance; b) the investigation of the trade-off between luminance and chromaticity shift for whiteness perception. To develop a metric characterizing the capability of a light source to render FWA-enhanced white objects. Typical white objects around us will be collected and measured. A subset of these objects will be carefully selected as test colour samples in the metric. To investigate whiteness perception in object mode from the perspective of vision science, so that the phenomenon can be explained physiologically.

25202916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25202916.value: LED is making a new revolution for architectural lighting, creating white light with much less energy consumption. The improvement of energy efficiency, however, has been achieved at the expense of other lighting qualities including colour and whiteness rendition. Unlike the efforts made on investigating how to render colours properly, the rendition of white objects has received little attention. In order to make white objects look whiter and to mitigate the yellowness of a white material, manufacturers have been adding whiteners, known as fluorescent whitening agents (FWAs), to plastics, paper, cosmetics, fabrics, and detergents for decades. The amount of the FWAs is modulated to provide different degrees of whites. Thus, the appearance of these whites with different amounts of FWAs becomes part of our visual experience every day. The optical radiation produced by a light source affects the appearance of these whites, because these whiteners absorb ultraviolet and violet radiations and re-emit blue light, making the object brighter and less yellow. If you change the incandescent or fluorescent lamps in your house or office to LEDs, your white shirts may look dirty, the appearance of white objects may look unnatural or unfamiliar, and objects with different degrees of whites may look similar. Daylight, incandescent, and fluorescent lamps have radiations to excite the whiteners, but typical LEDs in the market do not produce any radiation to excite the whiteners. The failure to excite the whiteners cannot be solved by simply adding an ultraviolet or violet diode. When manufacturers design the spectrum of a product, the CIE Colour Rendering Index (CRI) is always employed as a guidance for colour rendition; no metric can be used as a guidance for whiteness rendition. Without such a metric to guide product development, the unnatural and unfamiliar appearance of white objects may discourage consumers or designers to replace conventional light sources with LEDs regardless how energy efficient they are, which may become a barrier for promoting LEDs in general lighting and for realizing Hong Kong’s energy saving plan. This project aims to develop a metric for characterizing the ability of a light source to render whiteness. It will advance the industry by guiding manufacturers in designing products that render whites properly, helping designers to evaluate and specify products, and promoting LEDs with good lighting quality and higher energy efficiency to the public. This metric can also be included in future regulations and standards to guarantee the quality of lighting products. 人们生活环境中绝大部分的白色物体（包括人造和自然物体）都含有不同含量的荧光增白剂，它能吸收紫外或者小于400nm的辐射并产生荧光效应，从而通过提升物体亮度并产生一定的蓝色色调来提升物体白度。不同荧光增白剂含量所引起的不同白度已经成为人类生活中非常重要的视觉感受。由荧光增白剂的原理可知，照明光谱直接影响荧光增白剂的激发与效果，从而影响物体白度。虽然现有的CIE白度指数是使用最为广泛的评价指标，但其缺陷却广为人所知，例如：它只可以用来评价物体在CIE D65标准光源下的白度；它对于白色物体的限定范围也不准确，许多白色物体因在其限定范围外而无法评价其白度。对于照明行业而言，缺乏一个能够准确评价光源对物体白度显色能力的指标将影响LED照明产品的研发、评价及应用。 本研究将利用多通道光谱可调的LED照明平台，系统地研究不同光谱对于含有荧光增白剂的白色物体的白度显色能力，来建立一个能够准确评价光源对物体白度显色能力的指标。这一指标不仅可以帮助LED照明生产商对LED产品进行光谱优化、帮助照明设计师以及工程师衡量LED的颜色品质与光品质，更可以作为衡量LED产品光品质的指标之一被相关标准和法规采用。

25202916.label: Realisation of objectives
25202916.value: This project aims to investigate how to characterize the ability of a light source used for general illumination in rendering whiteness of surface colors. A customized multi-channel spectrally tunable LED device was designed for allowing the adjustment of spectral power distribution (SPD) of the light setting in the viewing booth. In particular, the device contains three channels between 350 and 450 nm, so that the excitation of the fluorescent whitening agents (FWAs) contained in the color samples can be carefully manipulated. A series of color samples, including fabric and paper samples, were prepared. They contained different amounts of FWAs, so that they had different degrees of whiteness appearance under the same illumination. The optical properties, in terms of the Donaldson matrix, of some samples were measured using a monochrometer and a spectroradiometer, so that the reflectance and fluorescence effects can be numerically calculated. Based on the calculations, it was found that the existing whiteness metric (i.e., CIE whiteness formula) does not accurately characterize the whiteness appearance of surface colors under arbitrary light sources. Also, the metamerism index cannot be used to characterize the ability of light sources to render whiteness in comparison to a daylight simulator. Experiments were performed using the scaling method and the magnitude estimation method to investigate how whiteness of surface colors appear under different light settings. Based on the judgements made by the observers whether a sample appeared white or not, we were able to define the chromaticity range for samples to appear nominally white. In other words, samples with the chromaticities in the defined range can be classified as white, while those outside the range cannot be classified as white. Then the magnitude estimation and scaling methods were used to derive scales to numerically characterize the whiteness appearance of a surface color under an arbitrary light source. It was found that using the chromaticities of the samples under the light setting, together with the chromatic adaptation transform (i.e., CAT02), can correctly rank order the whiteness of samples under the light settings having a similar white point (i.e., Correlated Color Temperature). When comparing the whiteness across different light source white points, the metric was found to have poor performance. Samples under a lower correlated color temperature was found to have lower whiteness. This actually reveals a lower degree of chromatic adaptation under a lower CCT light setting, and merits further investigations. Based on the findings developed above, we proposed a new metric to characterize the ability of a light source to render whiteness. The new metric will be included in the technical report of the CIE technical committee, which is under preparation. Moreover, we also tried to investigate how human beings perceive white stimulus from a vision science perspective. We analyzed the collected using the cone fundamentals (i.e., LMS cones) to understand how the photoreceptors in the human visual system actually respond to the stimuli produced by the samples under different light settings. In short, the project has been completed and all the objectives have been achieved.

25202916.value: Based on the experiments, we were able to define the chromaticity range for samples to appear nominally white. In other words, samples with the chromaticities in the defined range can be classified as white, while those outside the range cannot be classified as white (see Research Output 1 and Conference article 1). Then the magnitude estimation and scaling methods were used to derive scales to numerically characterize the whiteness appearance of a surface color under an arbitrary light source. It was found that using the chromaticities of the samples under the light setting, together with the chromatic adaptation transform (i.e., CAT02), can correctly rank order the whiteness of samples under the light settings having a similar white point (i.e., Correlated Color Temperature). When comparing the whiteness across different light source white points, the metric was found to have poor performance. Samples under a lower correlated color temperature was found to have lower whiteness. This actually reveals a lower degree of chromatic adaptation under a lower CCT light setting, and merits further investigations (see Research Output 3). Based on the findings developed above, we proposed a new metric to characterize the ability of a light source to render whiteness. The new metric will be included in the technical report of the CIE technical committee, which is under preparation (see Conference article 2). Moreover, we also tried to investigate how human beings perceive white stimulus from a vision science perspective. We analyzed the collected using the cone fundamentals (i.e., LMS cones) to understand how the photoreceptors in the human visual system actually respond to the stimuli produced by the samples under different light settings.

25202916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25202916.value: The incomplete chromatic adaptation found in this project is a very important phenomenon, which actually affects various aspects of color science and management. The PI is planning to further investigate this by applying for a new GRF project.

25202916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25202916.value: White objects are widely exist in our daily life. Most of white objects contain fluorescent whitening agents (FWAs) which are purposely added to increase the whiteness appearance by absorbing short-wavelength radiation and emitting blue light. Therefore, different amounts of FWAs can be used to modulate the whiteness appearance. The existing metric (i.e., the CIE whiteness formula) generally characterize the whiteness of surface under a daylight illuminant, which works generally well for conventional light sources (e.g., incandescent, fluorescent). LED sources, however, contain little short-wavelength radiation, so they cannot render whiteness well. This needs to be characterized for the color quality of LED sources. In this project, we developed customized LED devices and carried out a series of psychophysical experiments. The experiment results helped us to develop a new formula to accurately characterize the whiteness appearance of surface colors under an arbitrary light source, which was then used to characterize the ability of a source in rendering whiteness. The findings and outcomes of the project can be used for better characterizing the quality of LED sources, which can be used for guiding the development of LED sources and also for developing codes and regulations for LED sources to be used in the market.

25204016.value: 通過一個機械和介電泳的生物打印系統來三維製作血管化組織

25204016.label: Project Objectives

25204016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25204016.value: Advanced additive manufacturing has opened up new possibilities in the biomedical industry for the fabrication of 3D tissue constructs for clinical transplantation. To date, one common practice is to dispense cell-encapsulated hydrogels and crosslink them to form the constructs. Nevertheless, the hydrogels compatible with this practice usually possess poor mechanical properties, which limit their use for applications such as bone tissues. In this research project, we propose an integrated bio-printing system to fabricate 3D vascularized tissue constructs. The system will employ a new printing approach that can manipulate and pattern two or more cell types onto a single substrate via dielectrophoresis. A substrate with its mechanical properties mimicking the outer (compact) and the inner (spongy) layers of a bone will be synthesized and characterized. The cell-patterned substrates will be stacked precisely through a robotic manipulator to assemble into a 3D vascularized bone tissue construct. In this proposed research, the following three important issues will be addressed in the development of the bio-printing system. First, we will design a programmable chip that manipulates bone and endothelial cells via electric fields (dielectrophoresis) to construct the desired tissue pattern with an integrated vascular network on the substrate. Modeling and computational simulations will be conducted to optimize the chip design as well as experimental parameters in order for printing cells on the substrate with high quality and resolution. Second, we will develop a technique to synthesize a new hydrogel biomaterial of tunable stiffness gradient in the radial direction, enabling fabrication of delicate substrates mimicking micro-environments of different tissues. The effects of fabrication conditions and the use of different bioactive agents will be investigated so that the fabricated hydrogel can be tailored to mechanically resemble different native tissues while enabling efficient cell attachment and proliferation in culture. Third, we will develop automated algorithms for 3D assembly of the construct in a submerged environment. Visual images will be utilized to coordinate two robotic arms for grasping and re-orientating the arbitrarily-located substrates. Hydrodynamics forces acting on the substrate will be integrated in the control algorithm for precise manipulation of the substrate with the two arms. Our proposed bio-printing system can precisely define cellular patterns from different cell types on a customized substrate, offering flexibility for tissue construct fabrication. This combined printing and assembly approach will benefit the biomedical industry facilitating the development of complicated 3D vascularized tissues and organs. 先進的增量製造對生物醫藥行業開創了新的可能性，用於製作三維組織作臨床移植用。至今，一般的做法是將細胞混在水凝膠中擠出， 然後把它形結。 但是，可兼容的水凝膠通常具有比較差的特性，限制了它們的用途，如作骨骼組織。在這個研究項目中，我們提出一個綜合的生物打印系統製作三維血管化的組織結構。該系統將採用新的打印方法，可以把兩個或更多的細胞類型，通過介電泳，排列好在一個模板上。這個模板的特性是按骨外層（緊密）和骨內層（海綿狀）作模仿和分析。排列好細胞的模板會通過一個機器系統組裝成一個三維血管骨骼組織結構。在此擬議的研究中，以下三個重要問題將在發展生物打印系統中解決。 首先，我們將設計一個可編程芯片，使用介電泳來操縱骨骼和血管內皮細胞，排列成特定組織圖案和血管網絡。通過計算模型與電腦模擬，芯片的設計以及實驗參數會進行優化，把細胞打印質量提高。 其次，我們將開發一個新的水凝膠生物材料的製作，其韌性在徑向方向是可作調整，從而實現製造模仿不同組織微環境的模板。其製作條件和使用不同的生物活性劑的影響將會進行研發，從而製造出水凝膠可調整至類似不同天然組織的特性，但同時可讓細胞有效的附著和在培養中繁殖。 第三，我們將開發自動化算法可用於水中環境作三維組裝。通過視頻圖像，兩個機械手臂可以協調，把隨意放的模板調好位置及抓緊。流體動力施於模板上將加入控制算法從而使兩臂能作精確操縱。 我們提出的生物打印系統可以精確地打印細胞圖案，把不同的細胞類型印在特制的模板上，提供在製造組織構建的靈活性。這種綜合打印和組裝方式的系統對生物醫藥行業有益，促進複雜的三維血管化組織和器官發展。

25204016.label: Realisation of objectives
25204016.value: Objective 1 has been successfully achieved. In order to develop a non-contact approach to pattern a group of cells onto any substrate, we first designed a micro-chip with multiple electrodes arranged in an array. This micro-chip was mounted on a motorized platform so that it can enable relative motion (displacement) between the micro-chip and the substrate. When the electrodes were energized, electric fields were generated to trap cells near the electrodes via dielectrophoresis. Each electrode can be selectively turned on/off so that different patterns can be created, and each electrode can trap one or multiple cells at a time, providing higher flexibility to create single-cell or cell-cluster patterns. This method was tested to be effective to trap small (e.g. 4um in diameter yeast cells) and large (e.g. 70um in diameter embryo cells). This micro-chip had been tested to construct patterns like “POLYU” or “ring” shapes to illustrate the patterning capability. To extend the micro-chip for constructing patterns with multiple cell types, the micro-chip can be displaced to different cell reservoirs and transferred the trapped cells onto the substrate one by one (i.e. cell A first and then cell B). This technique can allow the substrate to be patterned with multiple cell types easily. Since many of the cell types are usually transparent and similar in size, for better visualization, red and green fluorescent beads were also considered in the experiments and colored patterns were successfully constructed. Objective 2 has also been achieved. This printing system can allow different substrates to be placed underneath of the micro-chip for cell patterning. The substrates examined were polymeric based substrates (e.g. Polyvinyl Alcohol and Polydimethylsiloxane) and their mechanical property (i.e. stiffness) needed to be adjusted. To enhance the stiffness, increasing the amount of crosslinking in the substrate through methods such as the use crosslinking agent and rapid freezing-thawing help to improve the overall strength by 50%. In addition, nanoparticles can also be added during the synthesis to increase the stiffness by a larger degree, and the different polymer-nanoparticle ratios can be set on the same substrate to enable stiffness variation. The surface condition of the substrate is key to the patterning efficiency. When the stiffness was changed, the patterned cells could be easily disrupted. To resolve that, calcium chloride was used in some experiments to provide additional force between the cells and the substrate surface to hold the cell pattern in place during micro-chip manipulation. Micro-well design was also added on the substrate surface to help preserve the cell pattern. Objective 3 has also been achieved. Two robot manipulators with a probe tip installed at the end-effector were setup to serve as the fingers for handling the patterned substrates, and the tips were monitored through the microscope. Vision-based algorithms were first developed to locate and evaluate the 2D information of the tip from the images, and such information was combined with a Kalman filter to estimate the tip position in the out-of-plane direction. With the 3D information of the tips, the two tips were manipulated to the two sides of the substrate for pick and place. For simple substrate stacking, a trajectory-fee algorithm was first developed, where control algorithms were generated based on minimization of the position error from the initial position to the final position. While many of the substrates are relatively soft and deformable, the substrates should be handled delicately. A trajectory-based method through demonstration was also developed. After demonstration, the trajectory was modeled using dynamic movement primitive and constraints such as over-stretching and collision were added so that the two robot manipulators can repeat the stacking procedure accordingly and the trajectories are robust against perturbations. Different trajectories, such as straight, circular and parabolic paths had been examined. The modeled trajectory can also be applied on a larger substrate that is double in size without any problem.

25204016.label: Major findings and research outcome
25204016.value: In this project, one of the major findings is to extend the capability of dielectrophoresis through a motorized platform. Dielectrophoreis has widely been employed for cell manipulation and patterning, but the pattern constructed is usually very small (microns), mainly limited by the microfluidic environment. Also, the cell pattern is pre-determined by the electrode layout and could not be changed after fabrication. The methods introduced in this project offer a higher flexibility for cell patterning. The electrode array on the micro-chip design can be used to form different cell patterns (C1), and a number of substrates can be selected for patterning (J2). To overcome the limitation of cell patterning in a confined environment, the integration of the micro-chip with a motorized platform can enable cells to be displaced over a long distance to different parts of the substrate for larger cell pattern construction (in centimeters) (C2). The quality of the cell pattern is influenced by the number of cells available for the micro-chip. In some applications, it is desirable to arrange cells in an organized matter (e.g. in cell assay). Since the dielectrophoretic forces are opposite in sign between the inner and outer parts of electrode, the boundary of the electrode can be used to separate nearby cells (C4), allowing more cells for the selection. In addition, optimization algorithms were also developed to find the shortest path in pairing the available cells with the electrodes (J4). The orientation of the cell can also be controlled with the micro-chip. While translation on the trapped cells can be achieved via the motorized platform, cell rotation can be realized through multiple electrodes with a phase difference. The micro-chip serves as a Tweezers to pick up cells that are randomly oriented, and then properly align them and place to the designated locations (J3). Finding the tip immersed in medium is an important task in order to grasp the substrate properly. With only 2D information available from the image, Kalman filter was employed to predict the third information (C3). Based on the selected points, a trajectory can be planned online with an iterative update to find required control inputs for the manipulator using images (C5). Demonstration can also be used to show the desired trajectories for the required operation. A coupling term was added to the governing equations to avoid causing potential damages to the substrates (J5 and J6).

25204016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25204016.value: The proposed micro-chip system aims to construct larger cell patterns through the motorized micro-chip. The micro-chip only contains a total of 16 electrodes as the proof of concept, which requires manipulating the micro-chip many times to form the pattern. In the future, more electrodes should be added and the size of the electrodes should be reduced to improve the resolution and the patterning time. Another potential development of this research is to enhance the accuracy (repeatability) of positioning the micro-chip with respect to the substrate. Since most substrates are clean, the system relies on the motor (open-loop control) to accurately place the micro-chip right next to the previous location (to continue patterning with new cells). In the future, the constructed cell pattern could be used for guiding and aligning the micro-chip to avoid causing significant distortion to the overall pattern. Static and moving obstacles are quite common in many robotic applications. Although it may not be the case in substrate manipulation and stacking, it is also worthwhile to examine the performance of the proposed algorithm in formulating the required trajectory and its robustness under different scenarios, enabling a more comprehensive algorithm for use in various applications.

25204016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25204016.value: Seeding cells on a planar substrate is the first step in constructing artificial tissues in-vitro. To allow better tissue ingrowth, cells should be organized into a pattern similar to their native tissues and cultured on a favorable substrate. This research project offers a new and flexible method to construct large-scale cell patterns on various substrates. The dielectrophoresis-based micro-chip can enable cells to group into a specific pattern as needed for subsequent patterning, and different substrates can be placed underneath of the micro-chip. Through the use of a motorized platform, the micro-chip with the cell pattern can be transferred to different parts of the substrate to construct a larger cell pattern, overcoming the size limitation in many conventional cell patterning practices. While the pattern constructed on the substrate is only 2D, 3D cell structure can be realized through substrate stacking with a robotic manipulator. Proper constraints can be added to avoid causing damages to the soft and deformable substrates. The complete bio-printing system can enable easy construction of artificial tissues with high flexibility on the cell pattern and the substrate selection to suit various application needs.

25204216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25204216.value: 隨著電子計算機與物理世界越來越緊密地融合，實時系統在我們的日常生活中扮演著越來越重要的角色。違背時間約束可能會導致諸如危及人的生命安全等嚴重後果。同時，實時系統對計算能力的需求也變得越來越高。例如，無人駕駛汽車中的障礙識別系統即要滿足嚴格的實時性約束又對計算能力有很高的要求。這一趨勢使實時系統將更多地采用多核體系結構。 由於對各種共享資源的爭奪，多核平台上軟件的時間行為可預測性是非常差的。這對系統設計者提出了全新的挑戰。現有的多核實時系統設計方法要麼無法提供硬實時保證，要麼會嚴重地浪費硬件資源。 本項目旨在研究如何設計多核平台上的軟件系統來同時滿足實時與高性能兩方面的需求。現有的多核實時系統方面工作大部分只考慮整個系統開發過程中的某一個特點步驟或方面，而對其他步驟或方面進行過度簡化的假設。因此，很難講這些現有技術整合到一個統一的框架中去。相比之下，本項目將提供一個完整而一致技術框架來覆蓋整個系統開發周期。本項目的成果體現為一個完整的軟件棧，其中包括編譯器，設計與分析工具以及運行時環境。本項目的技術創新可以概括為以下三方面： 可預測性執行模型。大部分現有技術采用面向單核系統的執行模型，因此無法充分利用多核處理器的計算能力。少數現有工作采用面向多核的執行模型，但是卻忽略了共享資源競爭的問題，因此無法保證系統的時間可預測性。本項目將采用一個創新性的執行模型，既充分挖掘程序的並行性又保證時間可預測性。 基於接口的設計方。對多核系統進行時間分析所面臨的一個主要困難是並行執行的程序之間因為對共享資源的競爭而產生的相互干擾。雖然現有工作在干擾分析方面有一些進展，仍然無法滿足實際應用的需要。本項目將從一個不同的角度來解決上述問題，通過使用基於接口的時間方法來規範系統的行為，提高系統的可分析性。 運行時優化。現有工作使用簡單的監控機制進行運行時優化，而本項目將廣泛地對多種運行時信息進行監控並使用它們對系統行為進行預測並對系統的平均性能進行優化。此外，本項目所采用的運行時性能優化方法需要以保證系統的實時性能為前提。 多核處理器的發展趨勢觸發了將軟件市場重新洗牌的歷史性機遇。許多國家都投入了很大的力量來保持或建立其在這一重要領域競爭力。本項目將對在多核平台上開發高性能可預測的軟件系統起到推進作用。這對香港科研與工業領域產生重要意義。

25204216.label: Realisation of objectives
25204216.value: The objective of the project is mostly achieved. During the project period, we have been working on establishing a framework to build multi-core software systems with both real-time constraints and high-performance requirements. We have worked on both the fundamental theory and key enabling techniques in both the off-line design supporting tools and the on-line runtime systems. We have conducted extensive experiments with synthetic workload as well as workload derived from realistic applications to evaluate the proposed techniques. We not only perform research with homogeneous multi-core processors, but also with heterogeneous multi-cores which utilize the strength of different architectures for executing particular types of workload, and usually offer higher performance and energy efficiency. We study the worst-case response time (WCRT) analysis of typed scheduling of parallel tasks on heterogeneous multi-cores, where the workload of each vertex in the DAG is only allowed to execute on a particular type of cores. The only known WCRT bound for this problem is grossly pessimistic and suffers the non-self-sustainability problem. We propose two new WCRT bounds. The first new bound has the same time complexity as the existing bound, but is more precise and solves its non-self-sustainability problem. The second new bound explores more detailed task graph structure information to greatly improve the precision, but is computationally more expensive. We prove that the problem of computing the second bound is strongly NP-hard if the number of types in the system is a variable, and develop an efficient algorithm which has polynomial time complexity if the number of types is a constant. Capacity augmentation bound is a widely used quantitative metric in theoretical studies of schedulability analysis for directed acyclic graph (DAG) parallel real-time tasks, which not only quantifies the suboptimality of the scheduling algorithms, but also serves as a simple linear-time schedulability test. Earlier studies on capacity augmentation bounds of the sporadic DAG task model were either restricted to a single DAG task or a set of tasks with implicit deadlines. We consider parallel tasks with constrained deadlines under global earliest deadline first policy. We first show that it is impossible to obtain a constant bound for our problem setting, and derive both lower and upper bounds of the capacity augmentation bound as a function with respect to the maximum ratio of task period to deadline. Our upper bound is at most 1.47 times larger than the optimal one. To optimize the runtime execution efficiency, we also studied multi-shot transition strategy to utilize the slack time on multi-core systems. The existing mixed-criticality real-time task models assume that once any high-criticality task overruns, all high-criticality jobs execute up to their most pessimistic WCET estimations simultaneously in a one-shot manner. This is very pessimistic in the sense of unnecessary resource overbooking. We propose a more generalized mixed-critical real-time task model, called flexible MC model with multiple-shot transitions (FMC-MST), to address this problem. In FMC-MST, high-criticality tasks can transit multiple intermediate levels to handle less pessimistic overruns independently and to non-uniformly scale the deadline on each level. We develop a run-time schedulability analysis for FMC-MST under EDF-VD scheduling, in which a better tradeoff between the penalties of low-criticality tasks and the overruns of high-criticality tasks is achieved to improve the service quality of low-criticality tasks. Moreoever, we study the scheduling problem of the imprecise mixed-criticality model under earliest deadline first with virtual deadline (EDF-VD) scheduling upon uniprocessor systems. Two schedulability tests are presented. The first test is a concise utilization-based test which can be applied to the implicit deadline IMC task set. The suboptimality of the proposed utilization-based test is evaluated via a widely-used scheduling metric, speedup factors. The second test is a more effective test but with higher complexity which is based on the concept of demand bound function (DBF). The proposed DBF-based test is more generic and can apply to constrained deadline IMC task set. Moreover, in order to address the high time cost of the existing deadline tuning algorithm, we propose a novel algorithm which significantly improve the efficiency of the deadline tuning procedure. We proposed the semi-federated scheduling approach to significantly improve the real-time performance of parallel real-time tasks. The federated scheduling is a promising approach to schedule parallel real-time tasks on multi-cores, where each heavy task exclusively executes on a number of dedicated processors, while light tasks are treated as sequential sporadic tasks and share the remaining processors. However, federated scheduling suffers resource waste since a heavy task with processing capacity requirement slightly larger than x (where x is an integer) needs x+1 dedicated processors. In the extreme case, almost half of the processing capacity is wasted. In this paper we propose the semi-federate scheduling approach, which only grants x dedicated processors to a heavy task with processing capacity requirement slightly larger than x, and schedules the remaining part together with light tasks on shared processors. We develop new scheduling algorithms and analysis techniques for parallel real-time tasks based on the OpenMP framework. OpenMP is a promising framework for developing parallel real-time software on multi-cores. Although similar to the DAG task model, OpenMP task systems are significantly more difficult to analyze due to constraints posed by the OpenMP specification. An important feature in OpenMP is tied tasks, which must execute on the same thread during the whole life cycle. Although tied tasks enjoy benefits in simplicity and efficiency, it was considered to be not suitable to real-time systems due to its complex behavior. In this project, we study the realtime scheduling and analysis of OpenMP task systems with tied tasks. First, we show that under the existing scheduling algorithms in OpenMP, tied tasks indeed may lead to extremely bad timing behaviors where the parallel workload is sequentially executed completely. To solve this problem, we proposed a new scheduling algorithm and developed two response time bounds for it, with different trade-off between simplicity and analysis precision. In this project also presents a benchmark suite, ompTGB, to support research on real-time scheduling of OpenMP-based parallel tasks. ompTGB does not only collect realistic OpenMP programs, but also models them into task graphs so that the real-time scheduling researchers can easily understand and use them. We also present a new response time bound for a subset of OpenMP programs and use it to demonstrate the usage of ompTGB.

25204216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25204216.value: Potential further development of the research includes the following aspects. First, we will continue to conduct research on fundamental theory of real-time scheduling of parallel task systems on multi-core platforms, and include the design and analysis of resource sharing protocols and data sharing strategies. 25204216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25204216.value: Real-time systems are playing a more and more important role in our daily life as computing is closely integrated to the physical world. Violating timing constraints may lead to catastrophic consequences such as loss of human life. At the same time, real-time systems are also becoming more and more computation-demanding. This trend pushes real-time systems to multi-core architectures. However, the timing behavior of software on multi-core platforms is very unpredictable due to the contention on various shared resources. This raises fundamental challenges which cannot be solved by existing design and analysis techniques established on the basis of single-core processors. The current practice in real-time system design on multi-core platforms either provides no hard real-time guarantees, or significantly under-utilize hardware resources to gain predictability at the price of low performance. This project studied design and analysis techniques for high-performance real-time applications, especially those need to be processed in parallel, on modern multi-core processors.
