25204416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25204416.value: Light in many ways is an ideal form of electromagnetic waves to probe and treat biological tissue, and optical methods play increasingly important roles in biomedicine. Many of these methods rely on the ability to deliver light to the investigation sites with high spatial resolution. This resolution, however, declines precipitously as light travels beyond about 1 mm into tissue due to strong scattering (think about how a flashlight beam diffuses through your palm). Efficient delivery of focused light beyond this limit has long been one of the greatest challenges in biomedical optics. Prior to this proposal, using ultrasonic encoding or photoacoustic sensing as virtual internal guide star, approaches based on optical phase conjugation and iterative wavefront shaping have successfully achieved optical focusing inside a phantom or dead tissue. But implementations so far are either inefficient in delivered energy at the focus or slow in terms of focusing speed, making them unsuitable for wide applications. To overcome these barriers, we propose an innovative scheme—fast nonlinear photoacoustically guided wavefront shaping (PAWS)—to achieve intense and tight optical-resolution focusing in deep living tissue. We will employ unique approaches to generate strong nonlinear photoacoustic (PA) signals in tissue as reliable feedback. Maximizing the strength of nonlinear PA signals can focus diffuse light to a single bright speckle grain within scattering media—this feasibility has been most recently published by the primary investigator in Nature Photonics. To determine the optimum wavefront compensation rapidly, a high-speed digital micromirror device (DMD) will be used for shaping the wavefront of light, and a field programmable gate array (FPGA) will be used for high-speed onboard data processing and transfer. Moreover, a stepwise drilling strategy will be developed to deepen the focal position, reaching tissue regions where no usable feedback can be generated directly. After that, we will explore high-resolution optical applications, such as fluorescence and photoacoustic microscopies, in deep biological tissue. If successfully developed, fast nonlinear PAWS would bring revolutionary advances to many applications that require high resolution, high contrast localized light delivery in deep tissue. For example, with intense optical focusing, nonlinear PAWS can be potentially applied to non-invasive neuron-resolution imaging and single-neuron optogenetic activation, as well as to killing single cancer cells in highly scattering deep tissues. Many in vivo optical microscopic imaging technologies can be brought from the ballistic regime (about 1 mm) to the diffusive regime (up to 10 cm in tissue), or even beyond. 光學技術在現代生物醫學中發揮著越來越重要的作用，但由于光被生物组织散射受到很多限制。如何在生物組織深處實現光的無創聚焦是人們期盼已久但被認爲是很有挑戰性的目標。本項目擬探索基于光聲引導的快速波前整形技術，將有望首次在活體生物組織深處實現高分辨率的無創光學聚焦。此外，我們還將探索深穿透光聲顯微技術並將之試用于癌症的早期診斷。一旦研制成功，本項目將有望爲很多生物醫學光學技術在活體中的應用開辟新天地。

25204416.label: Realisation of objectives
25204416.value: The research objectives of this proposal have been mostly (say, more than 90%) obtained, if not 100%. For example, for the first objective, we proposed a stimulated Raman scattering in optical fibers to generate nanosecond-scale time delay to input laser pulse. When such delayed pulse is recombined with the original laser pulse, we can create a laser burst containing two pulses that are nanosecond-order away (the time scale is adjustable based on the length of the fiber). Such a laser burst is able to generate very strong Grueneisen effect-based nonlinear photoacoustic signals. This method is different from the approaches designed initially, but much stronger nonlinear photoacoustic signals can be generated. One paper (Publication 13 in Part 8) has been published to describe the implementation setup and the method to separate the two photoacoustic signals that are overlapped partially in time. Another paper is still under exploration to characterize the nonlinear performance and its novel applications in imaging and sensing. For the second objective, we have built a high-speed wavefront shaping platform incorporating the use of a fast digital micromirror device (DMD) for light modulation and a field programmable gate array (FPGA) for high-speed on-board data processing and transfer. A series of optimization algorithms and have been developed to increase the speed, efficiency, robustness and adaptability of wavefront shaping operations (Publications 3, 6, 15, 18, 20, and 21). Moreover, artificial intelligence methods have also been introduced to overcome the limitation of current mathematical and physical models (Publications 7, 11, and 19). Currently, an optical focus can be formed within seconds, and the focus can be scanned within a relatively large field of view at ~23 kHz, which has already exceeded the regular speckle decorrelation time in vivo. For the third objective, the “optical drilling” approach proposed initially was proved to be unpractical in application at each depth there is need for re-optimization, which is really time consuming. Alternatively, we have come up a new solution by using multimode optical fiber as the light guide. Typically, light pattern from multimode fiber (MMF) is a seemingly random speckle pattern in vision, which is quite similar to that from a regular scattering medium, such as biological tissue. With wavefront shaping, however, the speckle pattern can be focused down to one point, and the point can be scanned with high speed in the field of view (Publication 5). As the size of the MMF is usually less than 100 µm, being smaller than many interspaces amongst neurons or blood vessels, major trauma or damage to deep tissues can be minimized or bypassed when inserting the MMF carefully and slowly- of course, practice or sufficient experience are necessary. More importantly, there is no depth limitation theoretically. Such an MMF-based method paves a practical way to achieve optical drilling into deep tissue with minimal invasion, which is not ideal but is promising in many biomedical application scenarios. For the last objective, we have achieved high-resolution photoacoustic imaging at depths, based on which a few interesting applications have been explored (Publications 10, 12, 13, and 14). Explorations are undertaken for deep neuron stimulation and imaging with a single multimode fiber empowered by wavefront shaping. Up to now, we have demonstrated a spatiotemporally engineered neuron stimulation by using an ultra-thin multimode fiber, which is empowered by optical wavefront shaping to achieve light focusing and raster scanning with high spatiotemporal resolution at the distal end of the multimode fiber and even through a mouse skull. With this method, primary neurons expressing Chr2 can be regulated spatiotemporally in experiment. Moreover, propagation of calcium waves (synaptic transmission) could be detected in a plain manner and beneficial for wide applications such as brain mapping. An US patent has most recently granted (See the 2nd item in Part 12) about the method and the system, and a manuscript reporting these exciting findings on deep-tissue single neuron is currently under review (Tianting Zhong, Zhihai Qiu, Jinghui Guo, Huanhao Li, Zhipeng Yu, Shengfu Cheng, Yingying Zhou, Jiejun Zhu, Jie Tian, Lei Sun, and Puxiang Lai, “Spatiotemporally engineered neuron stimulation through mouse skull with a wavefront shaping-empowered multimode fiber”). High-resolution fluorescence imaging of deep neuron with wavefront shaping-empowered multimode fiber is still being explored these days. Although still in infancy, we believe the work, with continuous improvement, may open up venues for noninvasive or minimally invasive all-optical investigation and imaging of neural circuits in used-to-be optically inaccessible brain regions. For more details about the major findings and research outcome, please refer to Part 6.

25204416.label: Major findings and research outcome
25204416.value: First, we are able to generate stronger nonlinear PA signals with stimulated Ramen scattering in optical fibers. The nanosecond-level time delay between the laser pulses (Publication 13) allows more energy to accumulate at the target site to excite stronger PA feedback signals, thus enhancing the optimization efficacy. Second, we have developed a high-speed wavefront shaping system with a digital micromirror device (DMD) for input wavefront modulation and a field programmable gate array (FPGA) for high-speed on-board data processing and transfer. Optical focusing through a scattering medium can be achieved within several seconds and the output plane can be scanned at a speed of 23 kHz, enabling efficient optical control with a large field of view. Third, we have proposed a novel feedback-based algorithm called dynamic mutation algorithm (DMA) for optical focusing in scattering media (Publication 18). The algorithm is based on a theoretically derived error rate that implies the status of the optimization in real time. Thus, the optimization can reliably adapt to perturbations and maintain the optical focusing under moderate environment variations. Together with the strong nonlinear PA signals and the high-speed wavefront shaping system, the tissue’s speckle decorrelation issue due to physiological motion can be overcome and in vivo deep-tissue optical focusing by PAWS can hopefully be realized. Fourth, based on the concept of error rate and dynamic mutation, we have proposed several hybrid/modified iterative algorithms suitable for various scenarios. For example, we have proposed a parameter-free algorithm, a combination of a traditional genetic algorithm (GA) and bat algorithm (BA) (Publication 20). It has robust optimization performance without a time-consuming parameter tuning process. On the other hand, we have also shown the feasibility to incorporate the dynamic mutation into other algorithms, such as particle swarm optimization (PSO), to improve their focusing performance and noise adaptability (Publication 21). Fifth, we have combined traditional optimization algorithms with deep learning to further improve the efficiency and robustness of optical focusing at depths (Publication 5). Deep learning networks have been successfully trained to deal with phase modulation. A deep learning-empowered framework has also been proposed to achieve adaptive optical focusing in dynamic media (Publications 11 and 19). All the above findings have laid the foundation for PAWS towards in vivo applications. With strong PA signals, efficient wavefront shaping system, and highly adaptive optimization algorithms, our PAWS system is believed to have a great application prospect from biomedical imaging, sensing, therapy, to manipulation.

25204416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25204416.value: The high-speed wavefront shaping system and algorithms we developed have a wide range of applications. For example, in addition to typical scattering media, such as biological tissues, the system can also be used to control the light transmission through a multimode fiber (MMF), in which speckle patterns arise due to intermodal interference and mode dispersion when light passes through. Thus, our wavefront shaping advancement can be seamlessly applied to many MMF-based biomedical applications, especially optogenetics, which is an emerging research topic in the biomedical field. The tight and intense focused light generated by PAWS can be delivered through the multimode fiber and mouse skull, precisely stimulating a single neuron in the brain without affecting other neurons nearby. The small diameter of the multimode fibers also allows the whole operation to be non-invasive or minimally invasive, providing a promising and safe tool to study the deep-brain neuron activities at high resolution. Related study is recently under exploration, covering both neuron stimulation and imaging with a single multimode fiber empowered by wavefront shaping. A manuscript reporting the exciting preliminary findings on deep-tissue single neuron is currently under review.

25204416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25204416.value: Optical methods have a growing importance in biomedicine nowadays as they are radiation-free and have low invasiveness. However, the drawback is that light is heavily scattered when passing through the biological tissue due to the inherent refractive index inhomogeneities and can hardly reach a millimeter below the skin unless resolution is sacrificed. This has hindered a wider application of biomedical optics in deep tissue. To solve this problem, we propose a novel technique, fast nonlinear photoacoustically guided wavefront shaping, to achieve deep-tissue optical focusing. The input optical wavefront is modulated with photoacoustic signals as the feedback to compensate for the scattering effect, forming an intense and tight focal point inside the scattering medium. With strong nonlinear PA feedback signals, high-speed wavefront shaping system, and highly adaptive optimization algorithms, the implementation can hopefully be realized efficiently in the in vivo environment. It also has great potential to become a universal and promising tool that will bring revolutionary advances to many biomedical applications, including imaging, sensing, therapy, and manipulation, wherever high resolution, high contrast, and localized light delivery is required. In particular, non-invasive neuron-resolution deep-tissue imaging and single-neuron optogenetic stimulation may become possible with our fast wavefront shaping platform.

25302116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25302116.value: 不少最新的金融市场投资组合优化问题都涉及到动态决策的路径依赖性。控制决策的历史路径影响给金融建模和数学方法都带来了全新的挑战。在此大前提下，我们将侧重研究两类不完全市场中路径依赖限制的效用函数的优化问题。其中第一类问题综合考虑投资者在生活标准限制下的消费行为和投资决策。具体而言，我们研究的是非上瘾性的消费行为习惯对最优投资和消费决策的影响，为此我们假设效用函数同时定义在当前消费水平和过去长期历史消费模式上。第二类问题探索在对冲基金高净值业绩表现费用框架下，如何进行最优的投资选择。为鼓励基金经理加倍努力，如果当前的业绩表现优于历史高净值，对冲基金公司常常会根据胜出的差额部分的一定比例来收取客户的业绩费。 对于这两类路径依赖的优化问题，很多经典的数学方法并不适用于广泛的市场模型，因此我们决定采用非传统的对偶问题研究方法。该新方法的核心思想是在建立相关的对偶问题过程中，人工引进新的辅助随机过程用以消除最优决策的路径依赖性。回到具体问题中，我们在第一类问题上将消费控制过程和历史消费过程的差距定义为新的辅助控制过程， 而在第二类问题中，我们定义辅助过程为当前状态到缴费业绩费用的距离。借助辅助随机过程，我们首先对辅助问题建立对偶定理。在数学方法上，为了成功建立基于随机过程的双极性定理，研究员及其合作者们在第一类问题中将在有限可加测度的大框架下进行相关工作， 而在第二类问题中则会借助带有双界反射的对偶随机过程完成证明。原始优化问题最优解的存在和唯一性都可以由辅助问题下的对偶定理进行后续的推导和论证。这两类问题的研究方法具有相当广泛的适用性，研究过程中新的结果及其方法都可以帮助我们去了解和探究众多其它类似的控制决策依赖性下的金融优化问题并为其建立更为通用的广泛对偶理论。

25302116.label: Realisation of objectives
25302116.value: We have fully addressed all proposed objectives in our research outputs. In our original proposal, we introduced two path-dependent optimal consumption and optimal investment problems, in which the auxiliary process and convex duality approach can be applied. The first problem studies the investor's consumption utility maximization with non-addictive habit formation preference. The utility function depends on the difference between the current consumption rate and the reference process that records the historical impact by the past consumption path. In particular, we consider this habit formation reference as the historical running maximum of the consumption control so that this formulation allows us to examine how the current consumption decision will be affected by the past spending peak. We choose to work with exponential utility that allowing the current consumption to fall below the historical reference, indicating that this habit impact is non-addictive. This path-dependent stochastic control problem is consistent with the psychological viewpoint that the consumer's satisfaction level and risk tolerance depend on recent changes instead of the absolute rate. We can depict the scenario that a striking decline in future consumption plan may result in intolerable disappointment and discomfort. Meanwhile, the exponential utility enables us to consider the practical case that the investor can bear a negative gap between the consumption level and the reference level and the investor may strategically lower the consumption budget to fall below the historical maximum level so that more wealth can be accumulated from the financial market. We introduced the consumption running maximum process as the key auxiliary process in the control problem to make the value function two dimensional. This auxiliary process enables us to define the dual value function of the original control problem only with respect to the wealth variable x. The duality relationship can help us to linearize the HJB equation and our focus is to study the piecewise linear dual PDE that eventually admits the unique explicit solution. This part of dual transformation 100% addressed our Objective 1. As a consequence of the explicit dual value function, we can obtain the optimal consumption and investment controls in the feedback form based on the dual process from the market model. By applying some novel stochastic analysis, convex analysis and some probabilistic convergence results, we can prove that the feedback controls using the dual process are indeed the optimal controls for the original optimization problem. Moreover, by using the inverse transform, we can further express the optimal consumption and investment using the primal state processes, namely the wealth process and the introduced auxiliary process. The duality gap can be successfully closed, and we can numerically illustrate several important financial properties and implications of the optimal consumption behavior. This part of work fully addressed our Objectives 2 and 3. The second project considers a dynamic portfolio management problem under the running maximum cost of the state process, which is motivated by the optimal tracking portfolio problem with nondecreasing benchmark. In particular, we assume that the fund manager can dynamically inject capital into the fund account such that the total fund capital dominates the non-decreasing benchmark floor process at each intermediate time. We can transform the original problem into an unconstrained control problem, however, under a running maximum cost. The path-dependence feature comes from the past maximum of the controlled state process, which is very similar to high-water mark fees in the practical hedge fund management. As the objective function is the running maximum of the state process, we have to introduce a smart auxiliary process as a reflection process to make the control problem Markovian and tractable. The dual problem and dual PDE for the auxiliary control problem can be defined and studied carefully using Feynman-Kac representation, some novel convergence in probability and stochastic flow analysis. This part of work 100% addressed Objective 4. To decribe the optimal portfolio control using the dual value function, we verify that the convex duality holds using some martingale properties and bipolar relationship similar to super-hedging theorem. We also prove that the constructed feedback control is indeed the optimal portfolio for the original control problem with a running maximum cost. In the special case when the model has infinite horizon, the duality relationship and the optimal control can be described in an explicit manner. Some numerical illustrations are also presented. This part of work fully addressed our Objective 5 and 6.

25302116.label: Major findings and research outcome
25302116.value: In the first problem of optimal consumption under non-addictive habit reference, we can introduce the auxiliary process as the running maximum of consumption control. The dual value function and the dual PDE problem can be defined and the duality gap can be closed. As the dual PDE can be explicitly solved, we obtain the optimal consumption and portfolio controls in the piecewise feedback form across different regions. All boundary curves separating different regions can also be explicitly characterized as nonlinear functions of the auxiliary variable. We can therefore determine the consumption in each region to satisfy: (i) no consumption; (ii) consumption below the reference level; (iii) consumption above the reference but below the historical maximum level; (iv) consumption sitting on the previously attained maximum level; (v) consumption creating the new global maximum. The verification theorem of the optimality and the duality relationship are carefully proved using some versatile stochastic analysis and convergence results. This is a joint work with Shuoqing Deng (University of Michigan), Xun Li (Hong Kong Polytechnic University) and Huyen Pham (University of Paris). Our paper, entitled "Optimal consumption with reference to past spending maximum", has been submitted to Finance and Stochastics on 7 July, 2020. In the second problem of optimal portfolio under a running maximum cost, we can introduce the auxiliary process as a reflection process. The dual value function and dual PDE problem can also be defined and studied by using Feynman-Kac representation and stochastic flow analysis. The existence and uniqueness of the classical solution to the dual PDE can be obtained. The verification theorem of the feedback optimal portfolio and the convex duality relationship can be carefully proved using some novel convergence analysis, bipolar relationship, SDE analysis. In the case of infinite horizon, the optimal portfolio and the value function can be expressed in an explicit manner. This is the joint work with Lijun Bo (USTC) and Huafu Liao (NUS). This paper, entitled "Optimal tracking portfolio with a ratcheting capital benchmark", has been revised and resubmitted to SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization on 8 Dec, 2020, and it is under 2nd round of review.

25302116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25302116.value: I found the idea of introducing auxiliary process and duality relationship can also be employed in many other applications. For instance, we have successfully established the convex duality in general market models for utility maximization under transaction costs and random endowments and also utility maximization under transaction costs and model uncertainty. We can also apply the similar approach in other financial applications such as optimal bail-out dividend control in Levy market models, risk sensitive portfolio management under default contagion and regime-switching, risk sensitive portfolio under default contagion and partial information, optimal dividend for an insurance group under contagious default risk, the lifetime ruin under high-water mark fees and drift uncertainty, stochastic control under path-dependent expectation constraints and etc. We believe that the auxiliary process and the convex duality approach for the auxiliary control problem can be further widely applied in many other financial and insurance applications under certain path-dependent preferences or path-dependent constraints. The duality relationship can significantly help the analysis of the associated PDE analysis or can be used to prove the existence of the optimizer by studying the dual optimization problem.

25302116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25302116.value: Our proposed research aims to provide remedies in some complicated stochastic control problems under path-dependent preference or path-dependent constraints. By introducing some auxiliary state processes to enlarge the dimension of the value function, we are able to establish the convex duality result for the auxiliary control problems instead of the original control problems. Mathematically speaking, we can focus on the dual problem of each auxiliary control problem afterwards. The optimal control of the original path-dependent problem can eventually be represented by the dual optimizer and the duality relationship. By applying our proposed approach, we can understand the structure of the optimal control strategy even when the problem depends on the past information of the control or the state process. In financial applications, we are capable to describe the consumption behavior and portfolio decision in the feedback form using the state process and the auxiliary process, which faciliate the practical implementations and model calibrations.

25302316.label: Project Objectives
25302316.value: Establish a more comprehensive version of the smooth parameter estimation framework. In particular, as kernel-smoothing method plays an important role in the proposed framework, it is of interests to explore how would bandwidths, dimension and sample size affect the estimation errors. Study the asymptotic behavior of our proposed rules. In particular, we intend to (i) explore the conditions needed for our rules to obtain variable selection and estimation consistency; (ii) derive the misclassification rates of our rules and obtain error bounds between the optimal Bayes risk and the misclassification rates of our rules. Develop efficient algorithms for computing the proposed dynamic discriminant rules. This is particularly important for the quadratic rules as it involves of the estimation of the difference of two high dimensional concentration matrices, which can be computationally intensive when the dimension is large. Conduct numerical analysis with comparison to other approaches. In addition to some LDA/QDA based approaches introduced in the literature review, it will also be interesting to compare our rules with some machine learning approaches such as (i) k-nearest neighbor and (ii) neural networks with many hidden layers, which has become a very hot topic in recent research (Schmidhuber, 2015).

25302316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25302316.value: Discriminant analysis that aims to allocate objects into one of the two predefined classes has been a central topic in statistical learning and data analysis. Due to their simplicity and optimality, linear discriminant analysis (LDA) and quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA) have become important rules in discriminant analysis. However, in the era of big data, as one often encounters datasets with complex structures (e.g. high dimensionality, non-stationarity, composite variables), classical LDA and QDA rules are no longer appropriate. It is important to develop new discriminant rules that take into account the complex structures of the data. In this project, we first propose a smooth parameter estimation framework and based on this framework we propose novel discriminant rules for the following two problems: 1. High dimensional dynamic LDA and QDA. Modern data are predominantly featured by complexity in terms of dimensionality and non-stationarity. For discriminant analysis, recent years have seen increasing emphasis to address the former, while the dynamic nature of many complex data is ignored. To address both challenges, we propose a dynamic linear discriminant rule and a dynamic quadratic discriminant rule for binary classification. Both rules allow the means and covariance matrices of the two populations to vary as functions of covariates of interest for very high dimensional data. 2. Discriminant analysis with high dimensional mixed data Discriminant analysis with discrete and continuous data under finite dimension assumptions has been well studied since the 80's. However, no paradigmatic approach exists for discriminant analysis with high dimensional discrete and continuous variables. By linking our proposed dynamic discriminant rules to the location model, we further propose novel rules for discriminant analysis with discrete and continuous variables under high dimensional assumptions. 判别分析，作为统计学习和数据分析中心议题，旨在把对象分配到两个预定义的类中的一个。由于线性判别分析（LDA）和二次判别分析（QDA）的简单性和最优化性质， 这两个方法一直是判别分析里的重要规则。然而，在大数据时代，由于人们常常遇到复杂的结构（例如高纬度，非平稳性，复合变量），经典LDA和QDA法则已不再适用。因此重新研究以及开发新的考虑到这些复杂结构的判别法则就变得很重要。在这个项目中，我们首先提出了一个平滑的参数估息框架，并在此基础上架构，我们提出以下两个问题的判别法则： （1）高维动态LDA和QDA。现代数据主要是有高维度和非平稳性方面的特点。对判别式分析，近年来，人们越来越重视解决前者，而许多复杂的数据的动态性质被忽略。在这个项目里，我们提出了动态的一次和二次判别法则，用以解决高纬情况下非平稳均值和方差的情况。 （2）有限维假设离散和连续数据的混合数据判别分析自上世纪80年代得到很好的研究。但是，高维的混合数据的判别分析还没有得到充分的研究。根据我们提出的高纬动态判别法则，我们进一步提出了高维假设下复合变量的判别分析的新方法。

25302316.label: Realisation of objectives
25302316.value: We have constructed a dynamic LDA rule and provided comprehensive theoretical studies to evaluate how the sample size, dimension and the bandwidths would affect the dynamic rule. Upper bounds for the estimation errors, minimax lower bounds and evaluation of the misclassification rate have been well established; see our publications in Bernoulli, and Electronic Journal of Statistics. A quadratic classifier is also constructed and an efficient ADMM algorithm is designed for implementation; see our paper published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research. Extension to regression and variations of the ADMM algorithms are also explored; see our publications in Statistics Sinica and Computational Statistics & Data Analysis.

25302316.label: Major findings and research outcome
25302316.value: We have developed several discriminant rules for classifying contemporary datasets that are characterized with non-stationarity, heterogeneity or with mixing type of variables. Related research outputs have been written into papers and published in decent journals. Techniques developed in this project are also applied to some related projects.

25302316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25302316.value: The proposed framework are built on Bayes' rule under Gaussian assumptions or its variations. It would be interesting to extend the framework to other type of data such as survival data with high dimensionality and/or mixed variables. On the other hand, as classification and regression are closely related, the modeling idea can also be explored under the context of regression analysis.

25302316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25302316.value: We have developed new classification rules for modern data with complex structures. The proposed classifiers are novel, with very good potential for further extensions and applications. Research funded or partially funded by this project were published in eight journal papers and related results were presented in international conferences.

25302616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25302616.value: The development of highly controllable and energy efficient novel persistent luminescence materials is imporant in the feld of luminescence science. Lanthanide oxide materials demonstrated tremendous potential in this regard due to their novel electronic structures. Their upconverted energy transfer dynamics and persistent luminescence mechanisms as well as performance improvenemts require extensive studies. This project will focus on electronic and optical properties of lanthanide oxide materials modulated by defect and impurity levels responsible for persistent luminescence. The chemical trends of modulations are predicted by orbital-corrected ab-inito theoretical studies. By selective doping and/or native point defects engineering, we design the tailor-made materials to obtain the specific electronic structures responsible for the luminescence. Their photochemical properties and factors governing the persistent luminescence will be analyzed. The chemical trends to improve the energy conversion will also be established based on physical approaches. Based on the energy conversion modelling to dictate their persistent luminescence performance, we will unveil the physicochemical nature and improve the design of the new generation upconverted persistent luminescence materials with higher intensity, longer duration time and improved greener energy efficiency. 项目摘要 高度可控性和节能的新颖长效发光材料的开发在发光科学领域中是极其重要的。镧系元素氧化物材料由于其新颖的电子结构在这方面表现出巨大的潜力。然而它们的上转换式的动态能量转移以及长效发光机制以及性能改进方面需要大量的研究。 本项目将重点关注针对与长效发光相关本征缺陷和杂质能级调控稀土氧化物电子和光学性质的机制。该调控的化学趋势将通过基于轨道自能修正的ab-initio理论研究进行预测。通过选择性掺杂和/或本征点缺陷能级调控，我们可以设计并量身定制相关材料，以获得与长效发光紧密相关的特殊电子结构。该项目还将针对它们的光化学性质以及控制长效法官性能的影响因素进行分析。基于该项目中的物理研究方法，有关提高能量转化的化学趋势将会得以建立。 通过基于能量转换建模以支配其持久发光性能的思路，我们将揭示有关的物理化学本质并改进新一代上转换式的长效发光材料的设计，以期获得更强的发光强度，更长的时效，以及更高的环保能源效率。

25302616.label: Realisation of objectives
25302616.value: To achieve the objectives of this project, we have carried out research in five main fields. The corresponding research works in these fields not only facilitate the fundamental research method developments but also accomplish the objective in the targeted fields. Beyond the target material systems, we have also extended our works in more material systems to supply significant references for our understanding in energy conversion processes. All these works are significant for us to accomplish this research project. (1) Theoretical calculation method developments In normal DFT calculations, the lanthanides suffer from the error of self-energy and wavefunction relaxations in the orbitals at the excited state. During this project, we have proposed the two-way crossover linear response approach to self-consistently correct the self-energy and wavefunction relaxations. The returned self-consistent parameters can directly apply to the DFT+U calculation systems without dependence on the choice of functionals. This method has been successfully applied to the cross-iteration correction of self-energy and wavefunction relaxations of the electron levels in both ground states and excited states of many materials. rows: Through previous researches and studies, we confirm that it is a key challenging task to describe the d/f-orbital based electron-electron interaction and solve related electronic structures. It is also a key to fully understand the correlation properties of d/f strongly coupled solids. With the theoretical efforts, we demonstrate that the challenge comes from the incomplete cancellation of the electron-electron Coulomb repulsion energy under external perturbation. This conventional method induced issue has been found in both partially and fully occupied d/f orbitals of lanthanide contained solids. Accordingly, we successfully applied the modeled first-order of second charge perturbation, denoted the “pseudo-charge” linear response model, to offset orbital-electronic-self-interactions related residue effects. During the first stage of the objectives, we have successfully developed this two-way crossover linear response method towards optimally searching the self-consistent parameters to minimize the electronic-electronic interaction calculation error. These are successfully used in ground- and excited- state DFT calculations.

Through our theoretical studies, we have uncovered many energy conversion mechanism models valid for interpreting the persistent luminescence of nanosized solid functional lanthanide materials. Especially, targeting on some upconverted persistent luminescence materials, the electronic structures have been all accurately reflected with a consistent band gap close to the experimental reported values. By applying our developed method, we have discovered the hidden levels of doping ions within those luminescence materials. This finding directed our understanding of current energy transfers model towards a descent level and brought forward the possibilities of modification on energy-migration-upconversion model. Based on these achievements, we newly proposed an inverse energy transfer path from shell to core assisted by the interface band offset engineering to realize UC luminescence with self-sensitization. Hence, we have paved a novel route for future investigation and demonstration on the interface energy transfer and potential interface quench states of the UC assisted persistent luminescence.

We have preliminarily started some testing works on "inverte-design" for tailoring the materials optical properties towards newer generation unconverted persistent luminescence interfaced with multi-scaled solid functional systems.

25302616.label: Major findings and research outcome
25302616.value: Major Findings: During this project, we have successfully applied the self-developed two-way crossover linear response approach in revealing the ground state and excited states of different materials including both the lanthanide-based materials and other functional luminescence materials. These approaches have fully confirmed the general application of our theoretical exploration method, which are able to accurately reveal the electronic structures of different materials, leading to an in-depth understanding of the electron transfer process. Meanwhile, based on the accurate description of the electronic structures, we have also comprehensively investigated the formation of native defects and their influence on luminescence properties. In particular, we have focused on the formation process of both simple point defects and defect complexes, strengthening the conventional understanding of defect-assisted luminescence process. Then, we have also calculated the energy levels, excited states associated with both native defects and external dopings, which significantly facilitate the descriptions of electron transfer pathways and the corresponding energy conversion process during the luminescence of different materials. Besides the lanthanide oxides, we have extended such an investigation strategy to more types of functional materials to study their electronic properties and applications in different fields such as mechanoluminescence, multi-modal luminescence, electrochemical reactions, energy harvesting and conversion devices, etc., which fully prove the universality of our theoretical exploration strategies. Depending on the successful experience in different solid state materials, we have further achieved the rational design of functional materials based on the efficient screening methods through both theoretical explorations. We have successfully designed the rare-earth based fluoride materials to achieve the intrinsic nanophotonic storage effect, where we have proposed that the surface electronic process can be modulated by an intrinsic level-matching induced surface resonant quantum tunneling (LM-SRQT) effect. For low dimensional oxide materials, we have established the criteria of promising candidates for realizing efficient nanogenerators in the future. Moreover, we have accomplished the successful screening of graphdiyne based atomic catalysts based on the detailed investigation of both stability and electroactivity of the materials. Therefore, through our theoretical explorations, we have successfully accomplished the research objectives of the proposal. Major Outcome: 1) Published over 140 peer-reviewed papers; 2) Attend over 30 international conferences during the project; 3) Cultivate one MPhil student; 4) Collaborate with frontier research groups from different countries. Detailed research output are listed in Part C of the concluding report.

25302616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25302616.value: In the future, we will further focus on two development directions including (1) optimizations of theoretical approaches and (2) the extended applications of the theoretical approach in designing more functional solid materials. Currently, the self-developed two-way crossover linear response approach has been applied in some solid-state materials to obtain accurate descriptions of electronic structures and lattice properties. These are the key to guarantee an in-depth understanding of the different properties of functional materials. To further extend the current theoretical calculation method to more type of materials, we will combine our theoretical calculations with advanced machine-learning technique to improve the calculation efficiency and accuracy. Moreover, based on the developments of the theoretical calculation method, we aim to apply it to more functional materials, especially the luminescence materials, which facilitates the exploration of the detailed electron transfer and energy conversion processes in a broad range of materials. In addition, we will establish close collaborations with the experimental groups to design and synthesize the luminescence materials with remarkable properties. The collected data from the experimental groups can further supply feedback to our theoretical explorations to further improve the algorithm and accuracy.

25302616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25302616.value: Persistent luminescence is a phenomenon in which luminescence is maintained for minutes to hours without an excitation source. Owing to their unique optical properties, various kinds of persistent luminescence materials (PLMs) have been developed and widely employed in numerous areas, such as bioimaging, phototherapy, data storage, and security technologies. Therefore, understanding the electron transfer and energy conversion process supplies significant information to further develop the desired materials with improved performances in tenability, intensity and duration time of the luminescence materials. However, owing to the limitation of characterization techniques, the experiments cannot fully reveal such processes in luminescence materials. Thus, applying the theoretical calculations supplies a feasible method for scientists to explore the in-depth origins and factors that determines the material properties. Our theoretical calculations are able to supply more site-to-site microstructure information than the experimental, which are essential for modulating the persistent luminescence materials or even other functional materials. During this project, we use theoretical method to modelling different solid functional materials regarding their lattice structures, electronic modulations, electron transfer pathways, energy conversion efficiency, etc. With such information, we further propose the possible mechanisms to explain the physicochemical phenomenon in different solid functional materials.

25501716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25501716.value: 香港居民對中國大陸遊客的定型: 評估干預措施對減弱先見看法的成效

25501716.label: Project Objectives
25501716.value: Identify stereotypes of MC tourists held by HK residents. Develop a measurement scale for assessing these stereotypes. Examine the effectiveness of the PCSM intervention on reducing these stereotypes.
rows: Identify stereotypes of MC tourists held by HK residents.
Develop a measurement scale for assessing these stereotypes.
Examine the effectiveness of the PCSM intervention on reducing these stereotypes.

25501716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25501716.value: The stereotyping of tourists can have damaging impact on tourism businesses. Locally, recent protests by Hong Kong (HK) residents against Mainland Chinese (MC) tourists have brought significant economic challenges to local businesses. Internationally, in destinations such as France and Ireland, there are also anecdotal signs that residents are forming stereotypes towards MC tourists as their visitation numbers continue to rise. Although anecdotal indications suggest that preconceptions of MC tourists are evaluative in nature, the researcher is unaware of any study that has empirically assessed the stereotyping of MC tourists. Furthermore, no study to-date has experimentally examined interventions that could be adopted by tourism practitioners to reduce the stereotyping of tourists. In light of this research gap, this project identifies and develops a scale to measure positive and negative preconceptions held by HK residents of MC tourists (Study 1) and considers recent research from psychology to assess a stereotype-reducing intervention to mitigate these preconceptions through four experiments (Study 2a-d). The proposed intervention is informed by group norm theory, social identity theory, and social comparison theory. The intervention conveys collective efforts of people trying to overcome their stereotypes, thereby highlighting the prevalence of a counterstereotyping message (PCSM). This project contributes to broader research efforts in this area by: 1) assessing the effectiveness of PCSM in reducing residents’ preconceptions against MC tourists, a stereotyped group that is growing in impact on destinations worldwide; 2) investigating the implications of PCSM when residents’ identities are primed as similar or dissimilar to the stereotyped group; and 3) examining the effectiveness of PCSM towards reducing positive stereotypes, a boundary condition that was not investigated in earlier work. The findings from this project are relevant and significant for tourism practitioners. For local policymakers, there is a need to gain a broader understanding of the preconceptions from residents both within and beyond that of those directly involved in tourism businesses; in this regard, this project measures the stereotyping of MC tourists from HK residents across all districts of the city. Policymakers at international destinations could also benefit by using the measurement scale developed in this project to assess the stereotypes held by their own residents towards MC tourists. Finally, results from the interventions would make a valuable contribution to education and communication initiatives, helping policymakers design messages that can help residents reduce their preconceptions towards MC tourists. 對遊客的定型會對旅遊產業造成嚴重影響。近來香港居民發起幾次針對大陸遊客的示威抗議活動，為本地經濟帶來了嚴峻的挑戰。而在國際上，隨著中國大陸遊客來訪數量上漲，在法國、愛爾蘭等旅遊目的地也有跡象表明當地居民針對大陸遊客的定型逐漸形成。儘管已有證據表明這些針對中國大陸遊客的先見看法在本質上屬評估性，但是我們並未發現有對大陸遊客定型的實證研究。此外，至今亦沒有研究驗證用來減弱對遊客定型的干預措施。有見及這研究缺口，本研究將制定一個檢驗香港居民對大陸遊客正面及負面先見看法的衡量體系，並引入近期心理學的研究，以評估干預措施對減弱先見看法和定型的成效。該干預措施參考了群體規範理論（group norms theory)、社會性認定理論（social identity theory)及社會比較理論 (social comparison theory)。這個干預措施體現出人們協力反擊外界對其群體的定型，同時強調反對定型信息的普及。 本研究的成果對旅遊從業者有重要意義。本研究透過調查香港所有地區的居民對大陸遊客的定型，讓本地政策制定者更廣泛地了解本地居民（包括旅遊及非旅遊從業者）針對遊客的先見看法。而其他國家的政策制定者也可以利用本研究提出的衡量系統來了解當地居民對中國大陸遊客的定型。最後，本研究在干預措施方面的成果有著教育和傳播意義，可幫助政府設計有關減弱對大陸遊客先見看法的宣傳訊息。

25501716.label: Realisation of objectives
25501716.value: All project objectives have been fully achieved. More specifically: 1. A refereed article was published in the Journal of Travel Research based on the outcomes of objectives 1 and 2 (see Tung, King, & Tse, 2020). In this article, a multi-stage scale development procedure was used to identify and measure stereotypes of Mainland Chinese tourists held by Hong Kong residents. An initial pool of positive and negative attributes frequently used in stereotype research was compiled based on the stereotype content model and the Princeton trilogy. The Princeton trilogy is a list of attributes that individuals may use to describe a social group. The stereotype content model suggests that stereotypes can be measured along two dimensions: warmth and competence. This list was supplemented by the literature on Chinese stereotypes. Additionally, an exploratory study of Chinese tourist stereotypes was further conducted via a free response task. In summary, the study retained 41 initial items (i.e., 22 positive and 19 negative). An online questionnaire was distributed to Hong Kong residents to measure the extent to which they (dis)agreed with a word list of positive (e.g., friendly, sincere) and negative tourist stereotypes (e.g., loud, rude) based on a 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree). Item-to-total correlations were computed for all items and items that were poorly correlated were eliminated. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was performed to assess dimensionality and factors with eigenvalues greater than one were extracted and items with low factor loading, communality, or high cross loading were removed. A two factor model emerged for positive stereotypes with three items in each factor. Factor 1 and 2 involved items that viewed tourists as approachable (i.e., friendly, good, and sincere), and competent (i.e., industrious, competent, and intelligent), respectively. For negative stereotypes, a two-factor model also emerged, with six items. Factor 1 and 2 involved items that viewed tourists as rude (i.e., immoral, rude, uncivilized, and unreasonable), and boastful (i.e., materialistic and loud), respectively. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was conducted to assess the full factor structure. A number of goodness-of-fit statistics were used to evaluate the model. The ratio of χ2 to maximum degrees of freedom was less than 2, with CFI and NNFI greater than .9 and RMSEA lower than .7. The reliability for all factors were above .7, which suggested acceptable internal consistency of indicators in the model. Convergent validity was assessed via factor loadings and average variance extracted. The AVE of factors exceeded the unexplained variance and the factor loading for individual items were greater than .4. In terms of discriminant validity, the AVE exceeded the square of the intercorrelations between any two constructs. Overall, the measurement model showed strong evidence of reliability and validity. 2. A second refereed article was published in the Journal of Travel Research based on the outcomes of objective 3 (see Tung, 2020). In this article, the effects of the “prevalence of counter-stereotyping message” (PCSM) was assessed through three related studies. Study 1 examined the initial effects of the stereotype-reduction strategies via a between-subjects experimental design with three levels (e.g., stereotype-reduction: prevalence of stereotype message (PSM), PCSM, or control). Posters with different messages for the PSM and PCSM conditions were prepared. The messages were informed by psychology research on stereotype-reduction but modified to suit the context of this study. The message in the PSM condition read: “Majority of residents have stereotypes of tourists. Avoid stereotyping.” The message in the PCSM condition read: “Majority of residents are trying to overcome the stereotyping of tourists. Avoid stereotyping.” All participants, including those in the control condition, completed the six-item measure of negative stereotypes against Mainland Chinese tourists based on the tourist stereotype model by Tung, King and Tse (2020) on a 7-point Likert-type scale (1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree). The six items were loud, materialistic, immoral, uncivilized, rude, and unreasonable. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to assess negative tourist stereotypes across the three conditions (i.e., control, PSM, and PCSM). The results indicated a significant effect and participants who were exposed to the stereotype-reduction strategies reported lower ratings of negative tourist stereotypes than participants in the control group. However, there was no significant difference between PSM and PCSM strategies in stereotype-reduction. While Study 1 evaluated the effects of the strategies, the tone of the messages casted residents as ‘we’ and tourists as ‘they’. Building on Study 1, Study 2 sought to facilitate an understanding of common identity between residents and tourists. The objective was to examine whether doing so could strengthen these stereotype-reduction effects. Study 2 added two scenarios. The first scenario casted tourists as residents by suggesting that tourists are temporary ‘residents’. The second scenario casted residents as tourists by reminding residents that they are also tourists in others’ communities when they travel. These messages were combined with the PSM and PCSM conditions in Study 1 via a 2 (stereotype-reduction: PSM vs. PCSM) x 2 (identity: tourists as residents vs. residents as tourists) between-subjects experimental design. Participants who were exposed to stereotype-reduction strategies reported lower ratings of negative tourist stereotypes. Casting tourists as temporary residents of the destination as well as reminding residents that they are also tourists when they travel also elicited lower extents of biases. However, the interaction effect was also nonsignificant. Study 2 provided further support for Study 1 as participants exposed to stereotype-reduction strategies reported lower extents of negative tourist stereotypes. However, adding a common identity message did not strengthen the effects of the PSM and PCSM strategies for stereotype-reduction. While Studies 1 and 2 examined the effects of common identity and PSM and PCSM strategies, these studies focused on the biases from the dominant community; that is, the majority group of Cantonese-speaking Hong Kong residents. A community is comprised of a diverse mix of residents who also identify with other subgroup; for example, there are a number of Hong Kong residents in the community who are non-locally born and from Mainland China (i.e., subgroup residents). The objective of Study 3 was to investigate a boundary condition, and the potentially unintended effects of applying the stereotype-reduction strategies. In study 3, Putonghua-speaking residents of Hong Kong that were not born in the city and did not speak the dominant local language, Cantonese, as their mother tongue were recruited. They were asked to assess their negative tourist stereotypes against other Mainland Chinese tourists based on the tourist stereotype model as per Studies 1 and 2 (Tung, King, & Tse 2020). Participants were randomly assigned to a 2 (stereotype-reduction: PSM vs. PCSM) x 2 (identity: tourists as residents vs. residents as tourists) between-subjects experimental design. Participants who were exposed to stereotype-reduction strategies reported significantly higher ratings of negative tourist stereotypes. Casting a common identity within the strategies also inflated negative biases. Collectively, all strategies inflated negative tourist stereotypes.

25501716.label: Major findings and research outcome
25501716.value: The first article by Tung, King and Tse (2020) used a multi-stage scale development procedure to identify and measure stereotypes of Mainland Chinese tourists held by Hong Kong residents. An initial pool of attributes frequently used in stereotype research was compiled based on the stereotype content model and the Princeton trilogy. This list was supplemented by the literature on Chinese stereotypes. Additionally, an exploratory study of Chinese tourist stereotypes was further conducted via a free response task. Six positive stereotypes were identified across two dimensions (i.e., Approachable: friendly, sincere, and good; and Competent: intelligent, industrious, and competent) as well as six inappropriate biases across two factors (i.e., Boastful: materialistic and loud; Rude: unreasonable, immoral, rude, and uncivilized). Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was conducted to assess the full factor structure. A number of goodness-of-fit statistics were used to evaluate the model. Overall, the measurement model showed strong evidence of reliability and validity. The second article by Tung (2020) investigated the effectiveness of messaging strategies to reduce negative tourist stereotyping across three related studies. Study 1 examined the effects of the stereotype-reduction strategies via a between-subjects experimental design with three levels (e.g., stereotype-reduction: prevalence of stereotype message (PSM), prevalence of counter-stereotyping message (PCSM), or control). Participants who were exposed to the stereotype-reduction strategies reported lower ratings of negative tourist stereotypes than participants in the control group. Study 2 added two scenarios. The first scenario casted tourists as residents by suggesting that tourists are temporary ‘residents’. The second scenario casted residents as tourists by reminding residents that they are also tourists in others’ communities when they travel. These messages were combined with the PSM and PCSM conditions in Study 1 via a 2 (stereotype-reduction: PSM vs. PCSM) x 2 (identity: tourists as residents vs. residents as tourists) between-subjects experimental design. Casting tourists as temporary residents of the destination as well as reminding residents that they are also tourists when they travel elicited lower extents of biases. Study 3 investigated the potentially unintended effects of applying the stereotype-reduction strategies. Putonghua-speaking residents of Hong Kong that were not born in the city and did not speak the dominant local language, Cantonese, as their mother tongue were recruited. Participants were randomly assigned to a 2 (stereotype-reduction: PSM vs. PCSM) x 2 (identity: tourists as residents vs. residents as tourists) between-subjects experimental design. Participants who were exposed to stereotype-reduction strategies reported significantly higher ratings of negative tourist stereotypes.

25501716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25501716.value: Future studies may further assess the antecedents to, and outcomes from, the scale that was developed in Tung, King, and Tse (2020). Future studies might examine residents’ previous interactions with tourists as well as their exposure to media coverage. These elements could potentially act as antecedents that shape their stereotypes toward tourists. The assessment of residents’ prosocial behaviors, such as willingness to help tourists, as possible outcomes that could be influenced by their positive or negative stereotypes of tourists is also an area for further research. With regards to Tung (2020), an avenue for future research is to consider the extent of travel experience as a possible variable to stereotype reduction because those who traveled more would likely have had more contact with Mainland Chinese tourists. Contact situations could potentially serve as a decategorization or learning process that allows people to view each other as individuals rather than just as members of another social group. Additionally, future research can examine the perspective of tourists rather than residents. Tourists may also have stereotypes against residents at a destination that could influence how they behave and interact with locals.

25501716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25501716.value: This research presented a model to evaluate the positive and negative tourist stereotypes that Hong Kong residents hold toward Chinese outbound tourists. Six positive stereotypes (i.e., Approachable: friendly, sincere, and good; and Competent: intelligent, industrious, and competent) as well as six inappropriate biases (i.e., Boastful: materialistic and loud; Rude: unreasonable, immoral, rude, and uncivilized) were identified. Additionally, this research examined the effectiveness of messaging strategies to reduce negative tourist stereotyping by residents given the negative impacts of stereotyping on host–tourist relations. The findings show that stereotype reduction efforts through communication messages could reduce biases against tourists by residents.

25503716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25503716.value: 為香港酒店業開發一個新的社會企業責任績效量表：模糊層次分析法的應用

25503716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25503716.value: The purpose of this research is to provide a framework for developing a new corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance measure for hotels in Hong Kong. Although previous studies have addressed the need to develop a standardized CSR performance measure in the hotel industry, little research has been conducted in this area. Recent studies have also criticized the shortcomings of global CSR measures that provide a universal index that does not reflect different business environments in different countries. Therefore, this study attempts to examine current Hong Kong hotel CSR performance and develop a new CSR performance measure using the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (AHP). The measure incorporates four CSR dimensions (environmental, social/philanthropic, ethical/corporate governance, and economic) based on various stakeholder voices in the hotel industry in Hong Kong. Two sets of data will be collected to gather information on (a) important indicators of each CSR dimension in measuring CSR performance and (b) the relative importance and actual performance information of the indicators selected in (a) to measure CSR performance. As a result, hotels’ CSR performance scores and rankings will be determined. This study intends to show a practical and realistic way to measure hotels’ current CSR performance and help them determine future CSR goals. Hotels can use the CSR performance index to improve the areas in which they are lacking in comparison with other hotels in Hong Kong. 本研究旨在為香港酒店业提供一個社會企業責任績效量表的框架。盡管已有文獻表達了對此的需求，但關於這方面的研究仍屈指可數。近期亦有研究指出常用的社會企業責任量表不能反映出不同國家商業環境的差異。因此，本研究旨在分析香港酒店當前的社會企業責任績效，並利用模糊層次分析法（AHP）提出新的社會企業責任績效量表。基於香港酒店業相關人士的不同角度，此量表包含了社會企業責任的四個方面（環境；社會/慈善；道德/企業管治；經濟)。兩組數據會被采集，根據 a) 以上四頂社會企業責任每個方面的重要指標; b) 這些指標在檢測社會企業責任績效時的相對重要性和實際表現。本研究因此推斷出香港酒店的社會企業責任績效的分數及排名。本研究提供了衡量酒店當前社會企業責任績效的實際方法，並幫助其決策日後目標。酒店亦可利用本文提出的社會企業責任績效指標來改善本港其他酒店這方面不足的地方。

25505516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25505516.value: Crowdfunding, as a nascent financing channel for early stage ventures, has grown rapidly in the recent years. It is characterized by a large number of backers (i.e. the “crowd”) pledging a small amount of money individually in exchange for products and souvenirs (reward-based), or an equity stake (i.e. equity-based). Crowdfunding projects, however, are highly risky and hard to monitor. It is unclear whether entrepreneurs can rationally assess their ability and their ventures’ future payoffs, and whether crowds can rationally make investment decisions. By exploring a sample of UK equity-based crowdfunding projects, in which entrepreneurs forecast up-to-three-year future financials, this study intends to shed light on these issues. Specifically, I ask the following questions: 1) to what extent are financial forecasts biased? 2) does entrepreneurs’ human capital help alleviate forecast bias? 3) are less biased financial forecasts associated with better funding outcomes? 4) is there an easy rule-of-thumb for investors to detect biased forecasts beforehand? Crowdfunding projects, as other early stage ventures, tend to have high failing rate. Entrepreneurs’ overconfidence is a likely explanation (Astebro et al., 2014). Entrepreneurs might also feel motivated to overstate their forecasts to attract more funding. In the first hypothesis, I will try to establish that entrepreneurs’ financial forecasts are on average optimistically biased. In the second hypothesis, I will examine whether entrepreneurs’ human capital counteracts their overconfidence and alleviates forecast bias. Because a rational crowd should be able to filter out some of entrepreneurs’ forecast bias and invest in projects with less bias, in the third hypothesis I will associate forecast bias with funding outcomes. I further investigate whether the relationship between forecast bias and funding outcomes depends on entrepreneurs’ human capital. In the final hypothesis, I intend to explore whether forecasts with certain characteristics are more likely to be biased ex post and whether investors can detect the bias ex ante. These characteristics help serve as a rule-of-thumb to single out biased forecasts. Realized financial statement information is shown to be value-relevant in the venture capital market (Hand, 2005; Armstrong et al., 2006). The timelier forecasted financial information is arguably even more useful. Given the uncertain and opaque nature of early stage ventures, financial forecasts can mitigate information asymmetry and should weigh heavily on investors’ decision-making. 眾籌作為早期階段風險投資的新興融資渠道近幾年發展迅速。眾籌的特點是大量投資者每人投資較少的金額來換取商品、紀念品（回報眾籌），或者股票（股權眾籌）。然而眾籌項目風險很大而且很難監督。我們不清楚創業者能否理性評估他們個人的能力或者他們項目未來的回報，也不清楚眾籌投資者能否理性做出投資決策。通過研究壹批英國眾籌項目中創業者對未來三年或以上做出的財務預測，這篇論文旨在回答這些問題。具體來講，這篇論文想要回答如下問題：1) 創業者的財務預測對比事後實現的財務狀況有多大偏差? 2) 創業者的人力資源可不可以降低財務預測的偏差? 3) 財務預測偏差較小的項目可不可以獲得更多的融資? 4) 有沒有簡單的方法可以在項目沒有實施之前就看出某些財務預測將會有很大偏差？ 眾籌項目作為早期階段的風險投資很容易失敗。壹種解釋是創業者過分自信(Astebro et al., 2014). 創業者可能會通過誇大財務預測來吸引資金。在第壹個假設，我將首先證明創業者的財務預測壹般會高於事後實現的財務數據。在第二個假設，我將檢測創業者的人力資源能否削弱創業者的過分自信，從而降低他們的財務預測偏差。理性的群體應該可以在壹定程度上估計到創業者的財務預測會有偏差，從而選擇投資財務預測更準的項目，所以在第三個假設中我將研究財務預測的偏差會不會影響融資結果。更進壹步，我將研究財務預測偏差和融資結果的關系會不會受到創業者人力資源的影響。在最後壹個假設，我將調查具有某些特征的財務預測是否更容易在事後出現較大偏差，以及投資者能否挑出這些特征。這些特征可以在項目還沒有實施之前就提示投資者這些財務預測是不現實的。 實現的財務信息在風險投資市場對投資者是有價值的(Hand, 2005; Armstrong et al., 2006). 更及時的財務預測對投資者應該更有用。因為早期風險投資不確定性大，信息模糊，財務預測可以降低信息不對稱，從而對投資者的決策產生重大影響。

25505516.label: Major findings and research outcome
25505516.value: The paper finds that entrepreneurs systematically overestimate sales, earnings, profit margin, and assets, and underestimate leverage. Despite the poor forecast quality, investors incorporate forecasted sales, subsequent equity and debt financing, and dividend payments in their investment decisions, but they do not react strongly to other signals. Some evidence suggests that investors are able to detect ex-post optimistically biased forecasts among funded projects. However, none of the forecast signals investors react to can predict a higher likelihood of a venture’s survival. The paper is forthcoming in Journal of Accounting, Auditing and Finance.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25505516.value: This paper finds that entrepreneurs on an equity-based crowdfunding cite provide largely optimistic forecasts. Investors choose projects that promise large future sales, subsequent financing and low dividends, but none of these signals is predictive of a project's future survival. However, funded projects with very optimistic forecasts do attract less funds and fewer investors. Overall, investors do not take all forecasts at face value, but they do react to some forecasts that cannot predict the future.

25505616.label: Project Objectives
25505616.value: To provide an explanation for the distress risk puzzle from the perspectives of analyst forecast optimism, forecast revisions and post-revision price drifts. To examine whether financial analysts make earnings, sales and profit margin forecasts that are generally more optimistic for firms with high distress risk at the beginning, and whether underreaction to the negative information and/or overreaction to the apparent good shape of those firms are the drivers behind. To investigate whether downward forecast revisions, revision price responses, and post-revision price drifts are more pronounced for firms with high distress risk.

To examine whether financial analysts make earnings, sales and profit margin forecasts that are generally more optimistic for firms with high distress risk at the beginning, and whether underreaction to the negative information and/or overreaction to the apparent good shape of those firms are the drivers behind.

25505616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25505616.value: This study investigates if analyst forecast optimism provides some explanations to the Distress Risk Puzzle: the phenomenon that high distress risk firms deliver anomalously low subsequent returns. There is general consensus in literature that financial analysts make optimistic forecasts: they tend to underreact to negative but overreact to positive information (Easterwood and Nutt, 1999). In this study, we investigate if the under-reaction to negative information provides an explanation for distress risk puzzle: Because the market respond to analyst forecasts, it is likely that investors will initially overvalue the high distress risk firms as guided by the financial analyst forecasts. Later on, when distressed firms report less than expected performance, these firms will experience lower returns. It is also likely that analysts will gradually recognize the poor status of those firms and revise their forecasts which will cause the high distress risk firms to earn low future returns. Although evidence indicates that analysts underreact to the negative information of firms, it is not clear if this relation exists for firms with high distress risk. This study will first provide such evidence. That is: our first research question will ask if analysts make forecasts that are more optimistic (or less pessimistic) for high distress risk firms than those for low distress risk firms. Prior studies investigate factors that explain the cross-sectional variations in forecast revisions and the associated market responses. For instance, some studies document that downward revisions trigger stronger and more prolonged post-revision price drifts than upward ones. However, little is known about how distress risk levels affect the magnitudes of subsequent forecast revisions and the associated price drifts. If analysts initially make more optimistic forecasts for high distress risk firms, the downward forecast revisions, revision price responses, and post-revision price drifts should be more pronounced. This will be my second research question. To sum, our study will provide new evidence for explaining the distress risk puzzle from the perspective of analyst forecast optimism. 本研究將探索是否可以用“分析師預測的普遍樂觀性”來解釋“財困風險之迷思” -- 高風險的財務困難（財困）公司只能提供低回報。 過去的文獻普遍認同金融分析師的預測常常過於樂觀：他們過度反映好消息，卻對壞消息認知不足（Easterwood 和 Nutt, 1999）。在本研究中，我們測試對負面消息的認知不足是否可以解釋“財困風險之謎”：因為分析師的預測一般能影響股票價格，過分樂觀的預測很可能導致投資者在事前高估了高風險公司的股票價值。事後當這些公司公佈低於預期的業績，投資回報率就會收低。當中很可能的原因是金融分析師逐漸意識到財困公司的真實表現而向下調整他們的預測及最終導致該類公司的價格向下(回報率收低)。 雖然證據指出分析師常常弱化公司的壞消息，我們尚不清楚這個關係是否也存在於高財困風險公司的預測上。本研究會將首次提供相關證據。我們要問的第一個研究問題是：分析師對高財困公司所做的預測是否要比低財困公司的樂觀。 過往的研究也探討關於金融分析師的預測調整及其所引起的市場反應。例如，有研究證實向下調整的預測要比向上的導致更強更持久的價格變化。但學術界尚不清楚財困風險是如何影響事後預測的調整及其引起的價格浮動。如果分析師在事先做了過分樂觀的預測及事後向下調整，那麼調整後的價格下降將會更加顯著。這是我們所要問的第二個研究問題。 總的來說，我們另闢蹊徑，從“分析師的普遍樂觀性”的角度來為“財困公司高風險、低迴報之迷思”提供新的證據和解釋。

25505616.label: Realisation of objectives
25505616.value: A full research paper was generated to completely answer the stated research objectives: how over-optimistic analyst earnings per share and sales forecasts explain the low abnormal returns of firms with high distress risk. The finding is as hypothesized that analysts make more optimistic forecasts for higher distress firms, but later on analysts also revise their forecasts more downwards that drive more negative 3-day abnormal revisions returns and post-revision price drifts of the higher distress risk firms. It is the low 3-day abnormal revisions returns and post-revision price drifts that constitute the low abnormal returns of the high distress risk firms. We further find that (quarter) earnings announcement directly drive roughly more than 60% of analyst forecast revisions and 30% of the revision-related stock returns.

25505616.label: Major findings and research outcome
25505616.value: Four logically-linked hypotheses are proposed that lay out the whole argument for explaining the distress risk puzzle. First, analysts make over-optimistic forecasts for firms with higher distress risk. Then the analysts revise their forecasts more downwards for the higher distress risk firms to drive down the stock prices. Finally, market respond to the forecast revisions incompletely and prices continue to drift downwards after the forecast revisions. Empirical evidences are generally supportive for the four hypotheses, namely, we observed significant negative relations between (EPS and sales) forecast errors (revisions) and distress risk levels of the firms. The within-fiscal-year averages of 3-day abnormal returns (CAR) are positively related to the EPS forecast revisions. Finally, the within-fiscal-year averages of post-forecast-revision price drifts are more pronounced for higher distress risks firms. The 3-day immediate market responses and the post-forecast-revision price drifts constitute the low abnormal returns of higher distress risk firms.

25505616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25505616.value: Further research topic can be: Why analysts underreact to the distress risk information to make over-optimistic earnings per share and sales forecasts?; do the behind reasons overlap with the other reasons that drive analysts to make over-optimistic forecasts as documented by prior literature?

25505616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25505616.value: Our paper contributes to the analyst forecast and mis-pricing literature. We provide evidences that analysts underreact to the distress risk status of firms, and that analyst EPS and sales forecasts are more biased for the higher distress risk firms. We show that both EPS and sales forecast revisions explain the 3-day abnormal returns around forecast revisions and the post-forecast-revision price drifts; and most importantly distress risk information is a determinant of the cross-sectional variations in the post-forecast-revision price drifts associated with analyst (EPS and sales) forecast revisions. Finally, we document that (quarter) earnings announcements convey substantial amount of information that roughly drive more than 60% of the analyst forecast revisions and 30% of the revision-related market responses.

25505716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25505716.value: Media is an important information intermediary that generates and disseminates a wide range of information to the public. However, very little research has been conducted using it as a source of valuation, as compared to information generated by other information intermediaries, such as analysts (Bushee, Core, Guay, and Hamm 2010). Different from concurrent studies that assess if the market responds to media coverage, I focus on applying fundamental valuation model to evaluate the informativeness of media. I propose to examine whether media coverage contains information about a firm’s fundamental value incremental to earnings, book value, and analyst forecasts. I am also interested in how different characteristics of media affect its role of assessing firm value. Ohlson (1995) connects firm value with earnings, book value, and the other information. The other information is the information that reflects a firm’s fundamental value which is not reflected in earnings or book value. Most empirical studies that implement Ohlson’s (1995) proposed residual income model mainly rely on using analyst forecasts to measure the other information (e.g., Frankel and Lee 1998; Dechow et al 1999; Bryan and Tiras 2007). In this study, I will use the tone of firm performance-related news articles to measure the other information and examine whether it can improve the model’s ability to measure firm value beyond earnings, book value, and analyst forecasts. I assess the accuracy of firm value measurement by testing the valuation model’s future earnings predictability, correlation with concurrent stock prices, and future stock returns predictability. I also investigate how different characteristics of media coverage affect the role of media in assessing firm value. First, I examine whether media coverage that has a different tone from concurrent firm press releases measures firm value more accurately. I propose when media reports investigative articles, which are identified by the difference in tones from the concurrent press leases, media coverage measures firm value more accurately. Second, I examine the role of media in assessing frim value when media creates diverse opinions about a firm (i.e., media dispersion). I measure media dispersion as the standard deviation of tones of the articles about a firm’s performance in any given fiscal year. Prior studies show when analyst forecast dispersion increases, the other information that contains information about fundamentals becomes more uncertain (e.g., Shan, Taylor, and Walter 2014). I will examine whether media dispersion improves or decreases the accuracy in measuring firms’ fundamental values. 媒体通过其自身信息渠道挖掘信息，解读信息，并且加速信息的广泛传播，已然成为资本市场中重要的信息中介。然而，已有的研究对于传统的信息中介（例如金融分析师）在公司基本面估值中所扮演的角色进行了广泛检验(Bushee, Core, Guay, and Hamm 2010)，但是极少有研究探讨媒体在公司估值中的作用。不同于关注市场对媒体报道如何反应的同期研究，本研究项目将运用基本面估值模型来评估媒体信息质量。在控制了会计利润、账面价值和分析师预测等信息后，本研究将检验媒体报道在评估公司基本面价值中的信息增量，以及检验不同的媒体特征如何影响其在公司价值评估中的作用。 Ohlson (1995)开创性地提出了基于会计利润、账面价值和其他信息的估值模型。其他信息指未能体现在利润和账面价值中的其他能够反映公司基本面价值的信息。大多数应用Ohlson(1995) 剩余收益模型的实证研究采用分析师预测来衡量模型中的其他信息(例如， Frankel and Lee 1998; Dechow et al 1999; Bryan and Tiras 2007)。本研究将会使用与公司业绩相关的新闻报道的语调作为估值模型中其他信息的替代变量，检验其是否能在利润、账面价值及分析师预测信息的基础上，进一步提高模型衡量公司价值的能力。本研究将从以下三个角度测量估值模型的价值评估准确性：检验模型对未来利润的预测能力，与同期股价的相关性，对未来股价的预测能力。 本项目还将研究媒体报道的特征如何影响其在公司价值评估中的作用。首先，本研究将检验不同语调的媒体报道是否比同期公司新闻稿能更能准确衡量公司价值。本研究提出当媒体发布调查性报道时（定义为与同期公司新闻稿不同语调的报道），媒体覆盖率更能准确衡量公司价值。其次，本项目将检验当媒体报道存在意见分歧时（即媒体意见分歧度），媒体在评估公司价值中的作用。本研究将媒体意见分歧度定义为在一个财政年度中与公司业绩相关的新闻报道的语调标准差。已有学者发现对于包含公司基本面信息的其他信息， 其信息不确定性会随着分析师的意见分歧而增加 (例如 Shan, Taylor, and Walter 2014)。本项目将会检验媒体意见分歧度是否会改善或降低其在衡量公司价值中的准确性。

25505716.label: Realisation of objectives
25505716.value: 1. To examine whether media coverage has explanatory power of fundamental value incremental to earnings and book value. The project objective has been achieved. Using Ohlson’s (1995) residual income model, we show that media coverage helps predict firm future earnings, and stock prices of firms with more media coverage are more aligned with firm fundamental values. This means that media contains incremental information to measure firms’ fundamental values. In addition, we examine whether the market corrects the mispricing if the market price deviates from the firm fundamental value. We find that market price does correct itself in the subsequent period if the price deviates from the fundamental value. 2. To examine whether media coverage has explanatory power of fundamental value incremental to earnings, book value, and analyst forecasts. The project objective has been achieved. Using Ohlson’s (1995) residual income model, we show that media coverage helps predict firm future earnings, and stock prices of firms with more media coverage are more aligned with firm fundamental values. We find that the media coverage has similar explanatory power with analyst forecasts. This result implies that both analysts and journalists provide value relevant information to evaluate firms’ fundamental values. 3. To examine whether media coverage contains more information about firm value when the media creates independent news and when the media creates more or less diverse news. The project objective has been achieved partially. Using Ohlson’s (1995) residual income model, we show that media coverage helps predict firm future earnings, and stock prices of firms with more media coverage are more aligned with firm fundamental values. We also show that our results are strengthened when the content of the media coverage is more investigative. We show when media reports investigative articles, which are identified by the difference in tones from the concurrent press releases, media coverage measures firm value more accurately. We find when media’s tone is more different from the firms’, Ohlson’s (1995) model is better at predicting the firm’s future earnings and the value estimated from Ohlson’s model is more aligned with the firm’s market value. We did not find that when media create more or less diverse news, media coverage contains more information. However, we find that when the media coverage is not relevant to firms’ fundamentals our results are strengthened.
