25505716.label: Major findings and research outcome
25505716.value: Media is an important information intermediary. In this study, we examine whether media coverage contains information about a firm’s fundamental value incremental to earnings, book value, and analyst forecasts. Using Ohlson’s (1995) residual income model, we show that media coverage helps predict firm future earnings, and stock prices of firms with more media coverage are more aligned with firm fundamental values. We also show that our results are strengthened when the content of the media coverage is more investigative and when the media coverage is not relevant to firms’ fundamentals.

25505716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25505716.value: We can look into the characteristics of the media articles and examine the different impact they may have on the incremental explanatory power of fundamental firm values.

25505716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25505716.value: This study contributes to the literature on media and capital market by examining media as a source of valuation. Instead of using stock prices as a benchmark to examine whether investors react to information disseminated or created by media, this study uses an accounting model to examine whether media coverage contains information about firm value incremental to earnings, book value and analyst forecasts.

25505916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25505916.value: 对冲基金行动的本质是对冲基金经理人本身对公司提供外部监管的强大财务动机。为了使这样的监管得以有效的实行，行动者雇佣内部的分析师分析出对公司最好的战略并对市场进行公布，从中获利。本研究的目的在于回答一个直接而重要的问题: 对冲基金会不会在已经有买房分析师的情况下同时在决策中关注卖房分析师？ 具体地来说，卖方分析师的股票关注对对冲基金的决策和回报有没有影响？ 我们觉得卖房分析师关注对对冲基金行动的影响体现在两个方面。首先，较少的卖房分析师关注削弱了公司治理并降低了公司价值，从来使得对冲基金的行动回答更高。其次，卖房分析师将关于公司的公开和非公开信息向大众披露，从而促进投资者的交易活动。较少的卖房分析师关注导致向市场披露的信息也越少，以至于交易活动变少，从来导致对冲基金退出成本上升。 在本研究中，我们将会用两个外生的卖方分析师关注的变化，以及工具变量来回答我们的主要研究问题。我们手动搜集了从1996至今所有对冲基金行动的数据，以及这段时间内分析师预测和交易公司关张和兼并数据。用这样一个独特的数据，我们研究卖方分析师关注下降对于对冲基金发起行动的概率以及行动回报的影响。基于我们的研究结果，我们进一步研究其产生机制并探讨不同的解释。对那些发起了的行动，我们将研究行动结果和持股回报如何在行动发起后被分析师关注影响。最后，我们对于这种影响在不同行动要求间的差异进行研究。 之前的研究关注点在于对冲基金行动对于公司绩效的影响，而不是行动者在行动中的战略行为。交易公司的关闭和兼并提供了一个自然的情境来研究这样的战略动机如何被监管和股票流动性所影响。更准确地说，研究这个问题有两个原因。 首先，更高的分析师关注提供了更好的公司监管。这样的监管更好地将公司管理层和股东的利益结合起来，并激励管理层研发出提升股东利益的公司战略。这可能会进一步影响行动者提出方案的价值，因为管理层也许已经这么做了。与之相对应的是，更少的卖房分析师关注提升了这些方案的价值以及行动的效益。其次，较少的透明度降低了股票流动性。较少的分析师关注增加了市场和公司之间的信息不对称性并降低了流动性。对于行动者来说，这样就使得积累股权和出卖股权成本更高，从而降低了整体的利润。总体来说，分析师关注通过影响行动者法案的价值以及发起行动退出行动的成本影响了行动者的期望收益。 行动者法案的价值和目标公司股票流动性对行动的收益是非常重要的。在本研究中，我们对现有对冲基金行动的文献的贡献在于我们研究了在监管和股票流动性影响受分析师关注影响时对冲基金的战略动机。本研究的发现将会对对冲基金行动提供新的角度和理解。

25505916.label: Realisation of objectives
25505916.value: The original analytical framework is to analyze the effect of analyst coverage on the value creation by hedge fund activists. And to identify such effect, I planned to use the merger and closure of brokerage house as the identification strategy. I have explored and conducted relevant analyses for each objective. However, after I matched the dataset of brokerage house merger and closure with the sample of activist campaigns, the resulting sample is too small to conduct any regression analyses, which is the key to drawing conclusions. In light of the situation, I have changed the research question slightly to study the effect of hedge fund activist campaign on analyst coverage and forecast properties. The new plan is as follows. 1. We first explore whether the hedge fund activist campaign affects analyst coverage. 2. Based on our results, we further conduct cross-sectional analyses to see whether the effect is stronger when the information uncertainty is stronger; when the analysts have stronger reputation concerns or when the activist has stronger power to change the firm 3. Finally, we examine the forecast properties before and after the activist intervention. The main hypothesis is that because the intervention of hedge fund activists creates uncertainty in the future prospects, analysts are more likely to drop their coverage of the firm due to career concerns. Moreover, because of the uncertainty, analysts’ forecast errors become bigger.

25505916.label: Major findings and research outcome
25505916.value: In this paper we investigate the effect of hedge fund activism on analyst coverage. We argue that because hedge fund activism creates uncertainty about firms’ future prospects, analysts avoid covering these firms that are attacked by activists. We find that in the three years after the activist campaign, the number of analysts following a target firm decreases by two. We also find that the decrease in analyst coverage is stronger when the firm itself has larger information uncertainty, when analysts have less experienced and more reputation concerns, and when activists have stronger power to change the firm. These analyses confirm that analysts cease the coverage due to higher uncertainty associated with the campaign as well as career concerns. Finally, we also find that for those analysts who keep on covering the firms, analysts issue forecasts less frequently and their forecasts are less optimistic and more disperse.

25505916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25505916.value: This paper tries to understand how active shareholders' intervention affects the information intermediaries' role in providing information to investors. The main finding is that because of the uncertainty surrounding the active shareholders' campaign, information intermediaries tend to refrain from providing information. Meanwhile, the information quality provided to investors worsens.

25506016.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25506016.value: 優化長線慈善捐款：解釋隱含的其他選擇和建議金額表

25506016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25506016.value: Requests from charities have become a part of everyday life: people are asked for donations at physical locations such as stores and churches, by direct mail, and through different media such as radio, television, and the Internet. According to Giving USA, the number of public charitable organizations reached about 1.5 million in 2014 in the United States alone, and the total amount of giving in the US was nearly $360 billion, fully 2.2% of its GDP. Similarly, the average annual household contribution was $2,974 (including non-donating households), over 5% of median household income. Individual giving was in fact the largest source of charitable donations, reaching $258 billion – 72% of the national total. Consequently, enticing individual donors is a crucial task for charities to help them reach or surpass their annual drive goals. An overwhelmingly popular method for soliciting donations from individuals involves presenting them with an “appeals scale,” a list of suggested amounts (i.e., scale points) selected by fundraisers. An appeals scale typically consists of multiple suggested amounts and an “Other” category (e.g., $5, $10, $20, $50, $100, Other). Donors can simply select one of the suggested scale point amounts, or instead some other quantity of their own choosing. Scale manipulation effects have been studied by many researchers over the last two decades. Although their experimental settings and individual results vary, these studies generally conclude that scale manipulation effects do exist. However, a statistical methodology that can provide rigorous guidance in designing optimal appeals scales has not yet been developed. The proposed project will tackle this question using unique data from large-scale field experiments. Based on theory in marketing, psychology, and other areas, I will develop a conjoined statistical model that accounts for 1) donation decision and donation amount simultaneously; 2) preference differences across donors; and 3) the fact that donors may construct an idiosyncratic set of candidate amounts before they settle on a specific donation. Ultimately, I will provide rigorous guidance to charities on how to individually tailor appeals scales that maximize the total expected donation amount for each donor over time. That is, the project seeks implementable guidelines for charitable and non-profit organizations seeking to enhance the effectiveness of their charitable campaigns, based on well-designed field test data and state-of-the art methods in discrete choice modeling. 慈善機構的呼籲已經成為了日常生活的一部分。有人在商店和教堂募捐，有人使用直郵或通過廣播電台、電視、互聯網等媒體募捐。根據Giving USA的統計，2014年美國共有公共慈善組織150萬個，全國慈善捐款金額接近3,600億元，達到本地生產總值的2.2%。（包括沒有捐款家庭在內的）家庭平均捐獻是每年2,974元，高於家庭收入中位數的5%。事實上，個人捐獻是最主要的捐款來源，達到2,580億元，相當於全國總數的72%。因此，向個人徵集捐款對於慈善組織完成甚至超越年度目標至關重要。 向個人徵集捐款十分常用的一種方法就是提供一個建議金額表，由募捐者列出提議的金額。金額表上一般都提供多個金額和一個其他金額的選擇（例如$5, $10, $20, $50, $100, 其他）。捐款者可以簡單的選擇列出的其中一個數額，或者自定一個。 過去二十年有不少研究人員探討過使用金額表的成效。這些研究的實驗設定和結果各異，但基本上結論都是肯定金額表的作用。雖則如此，目前還未有一種計算方法，可以為設計最優化的建議金額表提供切實的指引。 建議中的研究使用大型現場實驗來探討這個課題，所開發的結合統計模型將會建基於市場營銷學、心理學和其他領域的理論，所包含的因素為1）捐獻和金額的同時決定；2）不同捐款者的優次選擇；和3）捐款者可能使用各自的計算數字來決定一項捐獻。 這項研究的最終成果將會關係到長遠來說如何為個別捐款人編制建議金額表，以便徵集得最高的可能捐款額。研究使用實地測試數據和自主選擇模型的嶄新方法，提供切實可行的指引，將有助於慈善和非盈利組織提高募捐行動的成效。

25602816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25602816.value: 聲調語言是指用聲調來區分詞義的語言，漢語屬於聲調語言。由於發音機制的限制，升調和降調的發音存在時長限制，並且聲調語言和非聲調語言發音者所需時長有所不同。目前尚未有研究從語言感知角度探討時長的效應。 語言背景是影響言語感知的重要因素之一，因此本研究對聲調語言母語者和非聲調語言母語者都將進行探索。該研究不僅從心理語言學和理論語言學的角度闡釋發音與感知的關係及範疇感知發生的條件，同時研究成果也能應用在第二語言習得中。 針對不同語言背景的發音者，該項目旨在探討以下三個研究問題： 1） 能夠有效感知線性升調和線性降調的最短時長是多少？ 本研究提出了針對聲調語言和非聲調語言發音者的最短時長的公式，並與發音的最短時長的結果進行比較。 2） 實驗中的刺激信號時長是如何影響範疇感知的？ 當面對連續的音高變化時，聲調語言母語者可以對聲調範疇做出判斷，因此他們對于每個範疇中絕對音高的差異相對不敏感。非聲調語言母語者對聲調的感知不如聲調語言母語者範疇感強。該研究設計了不同時長的刺激，同時假設較短時長中範疇感知的特征對非聲調語言發音者將會更加明顯。 3） 在識別高元音和低元音的聲調時最短時長是否存在差異？聽者在感知過程 中是否會調整多種語音因素？由此是否可以解釋為何一些語音因素不受聲音變化影響？ 無論是在發音還是感知中，元音音質和聲調都是相互作用的。發音時高元音通常伴隨較高的音高值，反之亦然。由於補償機制，上述兩個因素在言語感知中表現出相反的關係。我們將考察音高曲線與元音高度是否存在相互作用， 從而影響感知升調和降調的時長。研究結果可能可以解釋為何部分語音因素不受聲音變化的影響。 此外，此研究有助於理解時長對範疇感知的影響、聲調與元音音質的相互作用以及二語習得的相關應用。該項目還試圖從統計建模的角度，加強關於言語感知研究的最優模型的選擇。

25602816.label: Realisation of objectives
25602816.value: 1. To offer formulae for duration needed for effective perception of linear rising and falling tones by tonal and non-tonal speakers A PhD student, research assistant and undergraduate student were hired to conduct experiments of both identification and same-different discrimination tasks. We have obtained formulae of perceiving linear rising and falling tones by tonal and non-tonal speakers. The formula is in the form of t = b0 + b1d, where t is the duration needed for perceiving d semitone differences from level tones. The linear formula is chosen because we need to compare our formulae to linear formulae proposed for speech production in the literature summarizing the time needed to produce various semitone differences in pitch (Xu & Sun, 2002). They obtained the formula by fitting simple linear regression models between production time and falling and rising semitone changes. In order to fit the linear formulae, we recorded all the duration values, where the tones can be identified more accurately than a guess level, and the corresponded semitones of rising or falling. Specifically, we recorded all the cut-off steps where the identification rate was 0.5. The step number was then transformed back to semitone values. We then fitted regression models to offer the formulae for the stimuli duration needed for effectively perceiving rising and falling tones. 2. To explore the relatively under-examined relationship of two aspects of speech, production and perception We analyzed the relationship between speech production and perception from two perspectives. First, we have designed the perceptual experiment based on quantitative modeling of the Mandarin Chinese corpus (Prom-On, Xu & Thipakorn, 2009). The underlying pitch target of the Mandarin rising tone has a slope of 93.4st/sec and an intercept of -2.2st. We created seven-step continua for both rising and falling pitch directions based on the estimated underlying pitch target from the Mandarin corpus. We also tried to control the slopes of steps to be the same across various stimuli duration for a better comparison across duration values. After comparing the formulae proposed for speech production, we found that the minimum stimuli duration required for accurate perception of pitch directions is usually shorter than the time needed to produce them in most cases. We also compared the properties found in speech production to those in perception. In speech production, speakers take longer to produce a rising tone than a falling one, which is similar to the case in speech perception. Also, in speech production, the surprising results were found by Xu and Sun (2002) that native Chinese speakers were in fact slower in producing a pitch direction change than native English speakers. However, our results in speech perception showed the opposite, where English speakers required longer stimuli duration to process a pitch direction change in most cases. Second, in speech production, the well-known intrinsic F0 effect (IF0) refers to the fact that high vowels are usually correlated with higher F0 values, and low vowels with lower F0 values. We analyzed the effect from vowel quality in our perceptual experiment and showed that the effect from vowel quality is quite limited in categorical perception as it only has some effects in within-category discrimination. In addition, we found that the duration needed for perception of high and low vowels is different. In most cases, a rising and falling tone required longer stimuli duration to be effectively perceived if a low vowel bears than if a high vowel bears it. We thus compared the results and our original hypotheses about the role of vowel quality played in categorical perception. 3. To investigate the effect of duration in categorical perception by speakers with different linguistic backgrounds We recruited speakers who speak tonal or non-tonal languages as their native languages, and we tested whether stimuli duration has a significant effect, and whether the effect is different among speakers with different linguistic background. We statistically tested whether duration significantly contributed to sharpness of category boundary, between-category discrimination and within-category discrimination. We also modeled and tested the differences of the duration effect across tonal and non-tonal speakers in sharpness of category boundary, between-category discrimination and within-category discrimination. We found that duration played a significant role in both tonal and non-tonal listeners, though tonal listeners were better in employing extra stimulus duration in context coding. 4. To explore phonetic factors such as vowel height and its interaction with pitch contours in explaining factors immune to sound changes We included both low and high vowels in our experiments to test whether there is any interaction between vowel quality and perception of pitch contours. Specifically, we tested the effect of vowel quality in categorical perception by testing whether within-category discrimination, between-category discrimination, the sharpness of category boundary and the location of category boundary and peakedness showed any difference on low vs. high vowels. We further tested our hypotheses about the compensatory mechanism in perception. We also tested whether a falling or a rising pitch on a low vowel requires more, less or equal amount of time to be accurately identified than on a high vowel. The asymmetry of vowel quality effect on falling vs. rising tones was also examined. Moreover, the interaction between vowel quality and pitch perception was also examined cross linguistically. The results showed that vowel height played a limited role in listeners with little musical background and musicians were more sensitive to the interaction between vowel height and tone perception. 5. To improve research methodology of speech perception by involving statistical model comparison and optimal model selection We improved on the research methodology of speech perception experiments. In our analysis, we used generalized linear mixed models to model multiple effects of pitch directions, vowel quality and linguistic backgrounds of speakers. In discrimination tasks, we obtained the correct (hits) and incorrect responses (false alarms) in the same-different task, and fit a generalized linear mixed model with three factors: duration, language group, and vowel quality, as well as all of the two-way and three-way interactions. We also improved modeling of underlying pitch targets for future experimental designs, and tested the methods on modelling existing small corpora. 6. To shed light on theories and applications of second language acquisition We conducted experiments on both tonal and non-tonal listeners and compared tone perception results. Our results confirm that non-tonal speakers showed weak categorical perception tones, which might lead to their difficulty in learning tones. We also calculated the duration needed to effectively perceive tones, and found some differences across tonal and non-tonal speakers. The long duration of stimuli helped tonal speakers better identify the stimuli more than non-tonal speakers. We argue this finding may shed light on the mechanism used in tonal speakers. Tonal listeners benefitted more from longer duration than non-tonal listeners, which suggests that their long-term linguistic experience with tones facilitated tone perception and they might benefit from their long-term categorical representations in their encoding of short-term categorical memory. An increase in stimuli duration values may not help the non-tonal listeners as much as tonal listeners in categorizing tones more effectively.

25602816.label: Major findings and research outcome
25602816.value: We calculated the stimuli duration needed for listeners to perceive pitch falling and rising directions cross-linguistically. The results were also compared to speech production. We found a minimum duration required to effectively perceive tones is usually shorter than to produce them. Similar to the fact that rising tones need longer time to be produced in speech production, a rising tone usually needs a longer duration to be perceived than a falling pitch. Contrary to the findings in speech production that native Chinese speakers are in fact slower in pitch production than native English speakers, we found that tonal speakers required lesser stimuli duration to effectively perceive the stimuli perception time. It is likely that linguistic experience with lexical tones lead to perceptual sensitivity to a tone change. In addition, we found that for both speech production and perception, longer duration is needed for a rising pitch than a falling pitch. Similar to previous findings, we confirmed that Mandarin listeners showed stronger categorical perception of pitch directions. Moreover, although both Mandarin and English listeners showed significant effects of stimuli duration on tone perception (e.g. on the sharpness of category boundary, between- and within-category discrimination), the degree of the effects was different among tonal and non-tonal speakers. Native Chinese listeners increased in category boundary sharpness faster than English listeners as the stimuli duration increased. Similarly, the effects on between- and within- category discrimination and peakedness were also greater than English listeners. Therefore, we tried to argue that due to long-term categorical representation, Chinese listeners benefited more from stimuli duration since they had more time for context encoding. Our results also showed some significant interaction between intrinsic F0 effect and pitch perception. However, the effect of vowel quality was limited in categorical perception for listeners with little or no musical background. Musicians turned out to be more sensitive to vowel quality. We examined many characteristics of categorical perception, including the sharpness of category boundary, the location of category boundary, between-category discrimination, and peakedness, but the vowel quality demonstrated its effects more in within-category discrimination.

25602816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25602816.value: This project has resolved all the objectives. For future research, the interaction between examined factors such as music experience and linguistic experience in learning tones of a second language can be further investigated. So the formulae of stimuli duration needed for perception can be further adjusted based on more data including various population. We expect to further improve our understanding on the interaction between stimuli duration, vowel quality and linguistic and music experience in tone perception. Since more factors will be included in the study including bilingual experience, we believe the future results can better contribute to theories and applications of second language acquisition. In addition, we would like to provide a fuller picture on the relationship between speech production and perception and more evidence of supporting our hypothesis about the role vowel quality can play. We also aim to further advance the methodology and include analysis on reaction time.

25602816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25602816.value: Pitch is used in many languages to differentiate word meanings. We investigated perception of rising and falling pitch contours by speakers with various linguistic and music background. Specifically, we determined minimum durations needed to perceive both contours and compared the results to those of production, how stimuli duration affects their perception, whether there is an intrinsic F0 effect, and how first language background, musical experience, duration, directions of pitch and vowel quality interact with each other. Continua of fundamental frequency based on statistical modelling of Mandarin corpus were created for identification and discrimination tasks. Less time is generally needed to effectively perceive a pitch direction than to produce it. Overall, tonal listeners' perception is more categorical than non-tonal listeners. Stimuli duration plays a critical role for both groups, but tonal listeners showed a stronger duration effect, and may benefit more from the extra time in longer stimuli for context-coding. Finally, vowel quality plays a limited role for non-musicians and only interacts with duration in perceiving falling pitch directions. These findings further our understanding on models of categorical perception, the relationship between speech perception and production, and the interaction between the perception of tones and vowel quality.

25603916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25603916.value: About half of the world’s languages are tonal languages (Yip, 2002). Among tonal languages, Chinese is a typical one spoken by the largest population in the world. Due to the systematic use of pitch to distinguish word meanings in Chinese, being able to accurately perceive lexical tones is necessary for successful acquisition of Chinese. Although most Chinese speakers are able to perceive lexical tones accurately, some native speakers actually find them difficult. An important factor affecting tone perception is congenital amusia, a neurodevelopmental disorder primarily influencing pitch processing in about 3~4% of the population (Peretz et al., 2008). It is found that a significant portion of adult Mandarin speakers with congenital amusia showed marked deficits in identification and discrimination of Mandarin tones (Nan, Sun and Peretz, 2010). It is proposed that those speakers have lexical agnosia, an inability to recognize tones. Though amusia leads to lexical agnosia, it remains unclear which level of lexical tone processing is affected by amusia in the brain: low-level auditory processing of pitch or high-level processing of lexical tones. Understanding this question is important for identifying the most efficient intervention for amusia. Previous studies show that Mandarin-speaking amusics are behaviorally impaired in categorical perception of tones (Jiang et al., 2012b). It hints that the neural deficits might lie in high-level categorical processing of tones. However, it is difficult to segregate different levels of processing using behavioral methods. Event-related potentials (ERPs), which have fine time resolution, are better suited to examine this question. Nonetheless, there are few ERP studies on Chinese-speaking amusics. To fill in the gap, I propose to identify the levels of processing deficits in Cantonese-speaking amusics using ERPs. I focus on Cantonese, because Cantonese is a major tone language spoken by a large population in southern China and it is under-studied. I shall first establish whether Cantonese-speaking amusics show impairment in the categorical perception of Cantonese tones. I shall then examine how acoustic variation affects the perception of tones, to distinguish further between low-level and high-level processing. Findings of this project will shed light on the influence of congenital amusia on lexical tone processing, providing insights into the neural deficits of Cantonese-speaking amusics. It will pave the way for future projects on the link between language impairment and music impairment. The identified neural deficits can guide the intervention. More broadly, unveiling the relationship of language and music will lead to a deeper understanding of human cognition.

25603916.label: Realisation of objectives
25603916.value: All the stated objectives have been successfully achieved as of the date of the completion report. Regarding the 1st objective – To investigate whether Cantonese-speaking amusics are impaired in lexical tone processing, we have carried out a behavioral study to examine tone identification and discrimination performance in a group of Cantonese subjects with congenital amusia and a group of musically intact control subjects. We found that Cantonese-speaking amusics demonstrated reduced accuracy of tone identification, and less accurate and slower discrimination of Cantonese tones, though their impairment in tone discrimination was less severe compared to that in tone identification. The impairment of amusics in tone discrimination is most noticeable in tone pairs that are acoustically similar (e.g., mid level tone vs. low level tone; high rising tone vs. low rising tone.) The results confirmed that Cantonese-speaking amusics are impaired in lexical tone processing. The results were published in a conference paper (Interspeech). Regarding the 2nd objective – To identify the level of neural processing deficits of Cantonese-speaking amusics (low-level pitch processing or high-level tone processing), we have examined this issue from two angles: (1) categorical perception, and (2) tone normalization. Both studies included manipulations to induce low-level to high-level tone processing. In the categorical perception study, we found that Cantonese-speaking amusics exhibited less benefit in between-category discriminations than controls in speech contexts (lexical tone and vowel), suggesting reduced categorical perception; on the other hand, they performed inferiorly compared to controls regardless of between- and within-category discriminations in the nonspeech context (pure tone), suggesting impaired general auditory pitch processing. The finding of a phonological processing deficit is further confirmed by a second study on tone normalization. In the latter study, we found that amusics showed reduced context effects in anomalous and meaningful speech contexts relative to musically intact controls, but largely comparable context effects in nonspeech and reversed speech contexts, indicating a deficit of amusics in tone normalization through phonological cues contained in native speech contexts. These results thus confirm a phonological processing deficit in parallel to an auditory pitch impairment in Cantonese-speaking amusics. These studies were published in three journal papers (PLOS ONE, JASA and JASA Express Letters). Regarding the 3rd objective – To identify the effects of acoustic variation on neural processing of tones in Cantonese-speaking amusics, we have carried out a behavioral and an ERP study to examine the effects of syllable and talker variation on lexical tone perception in Cantonese-speaking amusics. We found that amusics demonstrated poorer performance in tone discrimination compared to controls, but the group difference was more obvious in low talker/syllable variation conditions, where more acoustic constancy was provided. Besides, controls exhibited a greater increase in discrimination sensitivity from high to low variation conditions, implying a stronger benefit of acoustic constancy. The findings suggested that amusics’ lexical tone perception abilities, in terms of both low-level pitch processing and high-level phonological processing, as measured in low and high variation conditions, are impaired. Furthermore, amusics were more impaired in taking advantage of low acoustic variation contexts, and thus less efficiently sharpened their perception of tones when perceptual anchors in talker/syllable were provided, suggesting a possible ‘anchoring deficit’ in congenital amusia. Electrophysiologically, the amusics were intact in the auditory processing of talker normalization processes, as reflected by the comparable N1 amplitude to controls, but exhibited reduced automatic attentional switch to tone changes in the blocked-talker condition, as captured by the reduced P3a amplitude, which presumably underlies a previously reported perceptual “anchoring” deficit in amusics. These results were published in two journal papers (JSLHR and NeuroImage: Clinical). Regarding the 4th objective – To examine the effect of attention on neural processing of tones in Cantonese-speaking amusics, we examined the neural activities underlying lexical tone processing in both pre-attentive (MMN) and attentive (P300) conditions in 24 Cantonese-speaking amusics and 24 matched controls. We found that at the pre-attentive level, Cantonese-speaking amusics exhibited normal MMN responses to lexical tone changes, even for tone pairs with small pitch differences (mid level vs. low level tone; high rising vs. low rising tone). However, at the attentive level, amusics exhibited reduced P3a amplitude for all tone pairs, and further reduced P3b amplitude for tone pairs with small pitch differences. These results suggest that the amusic brain shows impairment in consciously detecting the same tone differences, providing support for the consciouc pitch disorder hypothesis in the speech domain. These findings were published in a journal paper (Scientific Reports). Regarding the last two objectives (Objective 5 - To help provide evidence-based guidance on intervention of Cantonese-speaking amusics; Objective 6 - To shed light on the relationship between language and music), these are general objectives that will be informed by the combined findings of the project instead of by individual studies. With regard to intervention strategies, our results suggest that amusia not only affects lower-level auditory pitch processing, but prevails to higher-level phonological processing related to the access of phonological representations of lexical tones in Cantonese speakers with amusia. Furthermore, amusia is primarily a conscious pitch disorder (in music and speech domain) with largely intact preattentive auditory pitch processing. These findings imply that intervention on amusia should focus on active pitch perception training instead of passive pitch exposure; furthermore, phonological processing is a weak area of Cantonese amusics that should receive special attention. With regard to the relationship between language and music, the current results imply that language and music processing overlaps to some extent in the auditory processing pathway, as evidenced by the cross-domain transfer of amusia – a musical disorder on linguistic pitch processing. This finding further implies that language and music might not be autonomous modules as some theories claimed.

25603916.label: Major findings and research outcome
25603916.value: Three major findings emerged from various studies conducted under this project. First, there is a parallel phonological deficit and auditory pitch deficit in Cantonese speakers with congenital amusia. Second, several dimensions of speech pitch processing are impaired in Cantonese speakers with congenital amusia. In addition to the aforementioned phonological processing deficit, we replicated the finding of emotional prosody recognition deficit and reported a new discovery that talker recognition and discrimination are also problematic in Cantonese amusics. Third, we tested the conscious pitch disorder hypothesis for the first time in speech (lexical tone) perception and reported convergent finding with prior studies on musical perception. These findings not only expanded our understanding of the nature and underlying neural mechanisms of speech impediments in amusia, but also shed some new light on the neurobiology of language and music and their interaction, informing theories on the co-evolution of language and music. In total we have published 13 papers in international peer-reviewed journals, one academic monograph and numerous conference presentations thanks to the funding of this project.

25603916.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25603916.value: The findings of the current study provided foundation for an ensuing intervention study on Cantonese speakers with congenital amusia. These findings have advanced our understanding of the neurocognitive deficiencies of Cantonese speakers with congenital amusia and consequently provide guidance for the intervention strategies. An intervention study will not only further verify the discovered neurocognitive deficiencies, but also shed more light on the language-music relationship. A GRF proposal on the intervention of amusia has been submitted to the RGC for consideration of funding.

25603916.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25603916.value: Chinese is spoken by the largest population in the world. As Chinese uses systematic pitch differences to distinguish word meanings, namely lexical tones, it is important for native speakers to have sufficient pitch discrimination abilities in order to successfully learn the tones. Although most native Chinese speakers can acquire the tones without any problem, some speakers actually find them difficult. A not-well-understood factor that affects tone perception is congenital amusia (tone deafness), a neurodevelopmental pitch disorder that affects about 1.5~4% of the population. Among native Putonghua speakers, a significant portion of them with amusia have a problem in identifying and discriminating Mandarin tones. However, there are few studies on amusia among Cantonese speakers. Cantonese is particularly interesting for its complex tonal system. Another unresolved problem is which level of lexical tone processing is affected: low-level auditory pitch processing, high-level phonological processing of lexical tones, or both. In a series of behavioral and electroencephalography (EEG) studies, we have generated convergent evidence that both auditory pitch and phonological processing are impaired in Cantonese speakers with amusia. Intriguingly, the amusical listeners’ brain can track pitch changes when they do not pay attention to the sounds, but fail to do so when they have to actively judge the pitch.

25610316.value: 最近的研究經常探討決策時兩個選項之間的決擇會否受到第三個干擾選擇的出現而影響。在傳統心理學和經濟學的理性決策理論，這種干擾選擇應當對決策不會構成影響。七十年多年以來這種理論被奉為「免於無關選擇的公理」(independence of irrelevant alternatives, IIA)。然而，這一觀點最近受到Louie, Glimcher和同事主張的divisive normalization模型和我所主張的attractor network模型所挑戰。Divisive normalization模型預測，當干擾選擇價值變差，決策會變得更準確。相反，attractor network模型預測，當干擾選擇價值變差，決策會變得不準確。本研究旨在排解IIA，divisive normalization模型和attractor network模型的差異。 基於決策神經學的文獻，我提出了一個框架，當中包括多個並行的腦神經系統作多項選擇的決策。在此框架內，與attractor network 模型相關的額葉皮層 ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC)，主要參與需要整合多項因素時的決策。與divisive normalization 模型相關的頂葉皮層intraparietal sulcus (IPS)，主要參與單項因素的決策。與IIA相關的額蘂皮層ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC) ，主要抑制第三個選擇的影響，以促進理性決策。 我將進行一項決策實驗以測試我的多項決策框架。首先，通過有系統地改變第三個選擇的價值，我將分析divisive normalization 模型和attractor network模型可否分別預測單因素和多因素決策。其次，我會收集眼動數據，並分析不同的眼動模式是否與不同的決策系統相關。第三，我將探討在vlPFC和IPS上使用經顱磁刺激對決策和眼動的影響。這項研究的結果將可能有助於改善精神病治療，經濟模型和營銷戰略的發展。

25610316.label: Realisation of objectives
25610316.value: Objective 1. To test the multiple decision system framework proposed in this study. This objective is the primary objective, where as Objectives 2-4 are the sub-objectives under this. We have conducted three studies described in three manuscripts to address this and two of which are published in eLife (impact factor=7.080) and Journal of Neuroscience (impact factor=5.673). These studies involved computational modelling, behavioural testing in healthy individuals, behavioural testing in neurological patients, applying transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and eye tracking. In brief, we provided evidence supporting the multiple decision system framework, in which the prefrontal cortex and parietal cortex involve different signals during decision making. Objective 2. To investigate how a third distracting option affect multiple attribute and single attribute decisions. This has been addressed in the eLife paper (Chau et al., 2020) and the Journal of Neuroscience paper (Noonan et al., 2017). In Experiments 1-6 of the eLife paper, they showed that the effect of the distracting option on decision making varied as a function of choice difficulty. On scenarios where the choices were hard, more appealing distractors were associated with more optimal choices. The distractor effect was opposite when the choices were easy. The Journal of Neuroscience paper also demonstrated that the distractor effect on hard choices was disrupted in patients with lesion in the prefrontal cortex. Objective 3. To investigate how different types of eye movement strategies for evaluating options are related to different decision systems. This has been addressed in the eLife paper (Chau et al., 2020). In Experiment 8 of the paper, it showed that more gazes at the distractor was associated with slowing down of the choices and resulted in more optimal decisions. Objective 4. To disrupt different decision systems using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and test the effects on decision making and eye movement strategies. This has been addressed in a study that involved TMS and eye-tracking. The results are now reported in an unpublished manuscript. The results showed that a distractor effect was disrupted after TMS was applied to the parietal cortex. In addition, the impact of eye movement on choices also was modulated after TMS.

25610316.label: Major findings and research outcome
25610316.value: This research has generated two publications (Chau et al., eLife, 2020; Noonan et al., Journal of Neuroscience, 2017), one unpublished manuscript (Kohl et al., in preparation), and two conference abstracts. We provided evidence supporting the multiple decision system framework, in which the prefrontal cortex and parietal cortex involve different signals during decision making. In the eLife paper, we showed in a series of eight experiences that effect of the distracting option on decision making varied as a function of choice difficulty. On scenarios where the choices were hard, more appealing distractors were associated with more optimal choices (i.e. positive distractor effect). The distractor effect was opposite when the choices were easy (i.e. negative distractor effect). The Journal of Neuroscience paper also demonstrated that the positive distractor effect was disrupted in patients with lesion in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC). In addition, we showed that the positive distractor effect is modulated by overt attention, as measured by people’s eye movement. In contrast, the unpublished manuscript showed that the negative distractor effect was disrupted after the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) was inhibited using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). These findings show that the vmPFC and IPS are both involved in decision making in parallel, however, they are subjected to opposite distractor effects. To conclude, in a series of studies we provided evidence supporting the view that decision making is guided by multiple parallel systems in the brain, in which the prefrontal cortex and parietal cortex are influenced by distracting options in opposite ways.

25610316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25610316.value: This research has inspired a new research idea that investigate neural mechanisms of multiple option decision making when there is plenty of information to consider. I have written a research proposal about this new idea and it has been supported by the General Research Fund in 2017.

25610316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25610316.value: Recently there has been great interest in whether decision making between two options can be affected by the presence of a third distractor option. Traditional rational choice theory assumes that such distractors should have no impact on decision making. For more than seventy years this has been enshrined in the axiom of independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA). However, this view has been challenged recently by neuroeconomics studies showing that irrational choices could be emerged as a result of the dynamics of brain activity. The current research showed that multiple parallel systems in the brain are involved in multiple choice decision making. First, we ran computational simulations and showed that irrational choices can be observed in a “dual route model”. Next, we ran a series of experiments that involved testing the behaviour of healthy people, neurological patients and people that received brain stimulation. The findings show the prefrontal cortex and parietal cortex of the brain are causally related to different aspects of irrational choices predicted by the dual route model. These results support the notions that (1) decision making are guided by multiple brain systems, and (2) irrational choices are made as a result of the dynamics of brain activity.

25612116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25612116.value: 語塊習得對以英語為外語(EFL)的學習者是一大難題。詞組搭配nice and easy, easy and nice 及 fine and easy看似相通，事實上只有前者才是以英語母語者的慣用搭配(亦稱為語塊)。要培養出這種識別語塊的語感，可能比學習第二語言詞彙及語法更難，甚至連高階英語學習者也會被難到。很多學者正著手解決語塊習得這個問題 。其中一說(Lin, 2012)，認為英語學習者在識別語塊方面的弱點，源於第二語言習得過程中過份偏重於讀寫材料，而相對忽略聽講材料。 英語語塊的特殊韻律結構使語塊在口語語篇中突出，因此口語輸入模態應比書面輸入模態更有助第二語言語塊習得。 這項實驗將首次探索輸入模態對第二語言語塊習得影響。三百位本地EFL學習者將獲隨機分派從書面、口語或韻律經修飾過的口語文本輸入學習英語語塊。透過比對三組實驗對象於學習前後的語塊知識，研究員可以量化輸入模態對語塊習得及記憶的影響，特別著重回答兩個問題：（一）哪一個輸入模態更有助第二語言語塊習得？（二）自然語言的韻律結構是否有助第二語言語塊習得？ 這項研究對第二語言詞彙習得研究的發展有以下貢獻。首先，早前文獻皆認為書面輸入模態比口語輸入模態更有助第二語言詞彙習得。可是，這些研究只針對英語單詞習得，而忽略了英語語塊習得。這項實驗正好填補了這個空白。這實驗亦是同類研究中首次能做到量度並排除學習者在語音處理能力方面的個別差異。在共變數分析(ANCOVA)中，由語音處理能力的個別差異及第二語言能力引起的變異都會被排除。最後，這實驗首次探討自然語言的韻律結構在成人第二語言詞彙習得的角色。究竟自然語言的韻律結構會否如推動幼童第一語言習得一樣推動成人第二語言習得呢？ 這項研究，將會就口語及書面輸入在第二語言習得中所應佔的比重提供實驗證據，並為第二語言語塊教學帶來新方向。

25612116.label: Realisation of objectives
25612116.value: This project set out to test the predictions of my theory about the optimal mode of input for learning English phrases (Lin, 2012). Following the observation that English-as-a-Foreign-Language (EFL) learners have great difficulties learning lexicalised word combinations (aka formulaic sequences), the theory traced the root cause of the problem to the mode of input EFL learners predominantly receives. It predicted that spoken input is more conducive to the acquisition of second language (L2) formulaic sequences than written input because these sequences are prosodically salient. The objectives of this project revolve around testing the predictions of this theory. To accomplish these objectives, a controlled experiment was conducted. In the experiment, 213 local EFL learners were required to learn, out of context, novel phrases (e.g. silent and sleepy, spirit and angel) delivered in three input modes, i.e. written, spoken with natural prosody and spoken with word-by-word prosody. Their knowledge gains were compared within subject and analysed statistically along with the results of a vocabulary size test, a test of L2 proficiency, a test of phonological short-term memory and a test of prosodic sensitivity. To achieve objective 1, knowledge gains from written and spoken input with natural speech prosody were compared within subject using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. To achieve objective 2, knowledge gains from spoken input with natural speech prosody and with word-by-word prosody were compared within subject also using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Finally, objective 3 was achieved by a logistic regression analysis with success in learning the phrase as the binary response variable and vocabulary size, L2 proficiency, phonological short-term memory capacity and prosodic sensitivity as the predictor variables.

25612116.label: Major findings and research outcome
25612116.value: This project pushed the boundaries of L2 vocabulary acquisition research in three ways. Firstly, previous studies argued for the superiority of written input for L2 vocabulary acquisition without considering the case of FSs. This project has been the first to address this gap and provide the much-needed empirical evidence that spoken input is more conductive to L2 FS acquisition than written input. This finding is striking because now the field acknowledges that the optimal input mode differs for L2 word versus L2 FS learning. Secondly, this project has been the first to delve into the role of prosodic cues in adult L2 vocabulary acquisition. The statistically significant difference observed between gains from spoken input with natural speech prosody and gains from spoken input with word-by-word prosody indicates that prosodic cues in the input are a factor of successful learning not only in child L1 vocabulary acquisition, but also in adult L2 FS acquisition. Learners are more likely to learn an FS that is prosodically salient in the sense that every constituent word is accentuated. Finally, this project has been the first to explore how individual differences in verbal processing ability affect success in L2 FS learning. L2 vocabulary size was found to be a significant predictor of success in L2 FS learning. Put simply, learners who know more L2 words will learn L2 FSs more readily than learners who know fewer words.

25612116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25612116.value: This study has provided the much-needed empirical evidence for Lin’s theory about the effect of input modality on L2 FS learning. The empirical evidence was collected from an experiment in which subjects learned novel phrases out of context. As such, the study tapped into one of three aspects of the prosodic salience of FSs (i.e. tonality) and explored how it affected FS learning. Looking ahead, further research can be conducted on how the other two aspects of prosodic salience of FSs (i.e. tonality and tones) affect L2 FS learning. To do this, the subjects will learn novel phrases in short paragraph contexts. The study’s finding that spoken input is more conducive to L2 FS learning than written input can potentially transform practices in ELT. Written input traditionally dominates in EFL syllabi and most resources have been allocated to facilitating the learning of reading. This study, however, has shown how spoken input is fundamental and indispensable to L2 vocabulary learning. Looking head, further research is needed to identify ways of maximising the proportion of spoken input in EFL syllabi (e.g. through online videos) and understand the science of L2 auditory input processing (see my other GRF project: 15602017).

25612116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25612116.value: Formulaic sequences (FSs), such as nice and easy, cooking on gas, and believe you me, have been considered the last hurdle to nativelike proficiency. These phrases are difficult to learn for even advanced learners of English because there often is no grammatical explanation for their composition: nice and easy is formulaic, while easy and nice is not. Lin (2012) traced the cause of this difficulty with learning FSs to the mode of input that dominates many EFL syllabi and argued that more spoken input should be provided to EFL learners. This project tested the predictions of Lin's (2012) theory in a laboratory setting. Two hundred and thirteen adult local EFL learners participated in the experiment which required them to learn novel phrases from written and spoken input. As the theory predicted, learners learned phrases much more readily from spoken than written input. The phrases were also more readily learned when they were prosodically salient. These findings challenged the longstanding belief that written input is more conducive to L2 vocabulary learning than spoken input. The optimal input mode indeed differs for L2 word versus L2 FS learning. The findings also provided evidence for the role of prosodic cues in adult L2 FS acquisition.

25614016.value: This project aims to address the following issues: How was the CR discourse interpreted by different political groups in Hong Kong newspapers and journals? How did right-wing newspapers and journals interpret the CR from the perspective of cultural nationalism, particularly during the period in the outbreak of the anti-colonial activities? How did it contribute to building an image of the Chinese nation in Hong Kong? How did the “neutral” newspapers and journals analyze and interpret the CR? How did they use the colonial Hong Kong’s locality as a platform to cultivate a sense of identity for the Chinese living in Hong Kong? How did the “New Left” discuss the CR and how did they adapt the CR to Hong Kong local affairs? What were the interactions between the CR and patriotic activities, e.g. Chinese Language Movement, the Defending the Diaoyu Islands, and the “Learning about China; Caring about society” movement? How did it contribute to a distinctive local Hong Kong identity formation?

25614016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25614016.value: Existing studies on the Chinese Cultural Revolution (the CR) in Hong Kong have largely viewed it as a social-political movement, the 1967 riots, but have rarely discussed the ideological conflict relating to the CR in Hong Kong newspapers and journals. Considering “the CR in Hong Kong” as a discourse, and closely examining various interpretations by Hong Kong newspapers and journals of different political groups, this project aims to delineate the CR discourse between 1966 and 1976 through printed media. It examines how the CR discourse has transformed the identity of Hong Kong people, particularly how a distinctive local Hong Kong identity began to emerge in the 1960s and 1970s. From the outbreak of the CR, the Left anticipated a utopian image of China projected from the CR against colonialism. The Right, however, considered the CR a destruction of traditional Chinese culture. The neutralists saw from the CR a power struggle within the Chinese Communist Party. In the 1970s, the CR was acclaimed by post-war born youth and students (the “New Left”) as a successful means to reshape China into a powerful nation and spread communism to Hong Kong against the colonial government’s capitalist doctrines. Their contention generated ambivalent narratives of the Chinese nation. The CR created an impression that the Chinese nation was different politically, culturally, ethnically and ideologically from Hong Kong, a British colony. Hong Kong has played an important role in shaping the CR discourse. On one hand, as a British colony, it allows different interpretations of the national identity to coexist. The CR then influenced how Hong Kong people perceive the colonial government. On the other hand, Hong Kong developed as a place to cater for Maoist practice against capitalism in the 1970s. This rising concern for Hong Kong local affairs helped foster the emergence of a local consciousness. The formation of Hong Kong identity is an interaction between nationalism, local consciousness and a colonial setting. The CR discourse serves as a channel to explore the multi-dimensions of Hong Kong identity formation in the 1960s and 1970s. The project will employ untapped newspapers, journals and archives in Hong Kong and London; oral histories, memoirs, selected writings; interviews with editors and contributors, and produce four academic articles illustrating 1) the emergence of a distinctive local Hong Kong identity in the 1960s and 1970s and 2) the uniqueness of Hong Kong in the study of the CR. 歷來學界研究中國文化大革命（下稱「文革」）對香港的影響，偏重討論「六七暴動」這場運動的起因、經過、結果以及影響，卻忽視了「文革」在香港報刊媒體中所引起的意識形態論爭。本研究計劃將「文革在香港」視為一種論述話語，分析不同政治立場的報刊對「文革」的詮譯及挪用。自從「文革」爆發後，左派報刊在香港宣傳其為烏托邦之願景，用以攻擊港英殖民政府。右派則視之為對中華文化之破壞，而所謂「中間派」將「文革」等同於中共的權力鬥爭。「文革」思潮於1970年後，獲得一批愛國青年及學生的推崇，認為「文革」成功改革中國，並嘗試以共產主義來對抗港英政府所奉行的資本主義。由此可見，在港英殖民政府管治下之香港，為「文革」提供了多元的論述空間，而在左中右報刊詮譯「文革」之背後，牽引出政治、文化、種族以及意識形態等不同面向的國家想像與認同。 香港在左中右報刊討論「文革」的過程之中，一直扮演著重要角色。一方面，香港作為英國殖民地，容許不同國族認同的並存。反過來，香港人對「文革」認同的變化，同時影響自身對港英殖民政府的接受。另一方面，香港人在1970年代開始對本土事務的關注﹐並嘗試運用毛主義去解決本土問題。如此說來，香港人身份形成的過程是，是一場國族主義、本土意識以及殖民主義之間的角力。本研究計劃通過分析這個「文革」話語，來揭示在 1960年代至1970年代香港人身份認同的複雜性與曖昧性。 本研究計劃分析大量未被發掘的報刊資料，參考香港和倫敦的檔案資料、相關人物的口述史、回憶錄和文集，訪問報刊編輯及作家，寫成四篇學術論文，針對兩方面作出學術貢獻： 1) 在1960年代至1970年代香港人身份認同形成的爭議；2) 「香港」在「文革研究」的獨特性。

25614016.label: Realisation of objectives
25614016.value: The ECS project’s objectives have been achieved completely as of June 2021. The discovery of new materials: The PI and research assistant collected and analysed related editorials, commentaries and news reports from over 1000 volumes of Hong Kong periodicals (e.g. Panku magazine, The Undergrad, Chinese Student Weekly, Zuguo yuekan, Daxue shenghuo, Chinese University Student Press, the 70s and Ming Pao monthly) and two major local newspapers (Wen Wei Po and Ming Pao). Most of them have been rarely discussed. The unearthed materials allows the PI to understand the complexity and diversity of the Cultural Revolution discourse. Further, the PI continues to delve into archives in the United Kingdom and Hong Kong and has discovered over 150 sources related to the project. The PI also interviewed key figures in the local print media. They provided invaluable information and helped the PI to link up the relationship between the ideological meaning of the Cultural Revolution discourse and the cultural production of local newspapers. All in all, the data collection helped the PI achieve the objective 1 (i.e. how was the Cultural Revolution discourse interpreted by different political groups in Hong Kong newspapers and journals) mentioned in the ECS project. Publications and Conference presentations : the ECS project resulted in five publications and eight conference presentations The first publication achieved the objectives 1 and 2 mentioned in the ECS project. The preliminary finding on the effect of the Cultural Revolution on the construction of Hong Kong identity has been published in a book chapter titled “National Identity” in an edited volume titled “Hong Kong Keywords” (The Chinese University of Hong Kong Press). The PI successfully answers the questions raised in the objectives 1 and 2 by showing the symbiotic relationship between the formation of local/national identity in her discussion on New Left periodicals’ understanding on the Cultural Revolution. The second publication achieved the objectives 1, 2 and 6 mentioned in the ECS project. The journal article titled “Imagining a national/local identity in the colony: the Cultural Revolution discourse in Hong Kong youth and student journals, 1966-1977” (Cultural Studies) explores the New Left’s interpretation on the Cultural Revolution and Communism. The article was presented at conferences #1, #2, #4 and #6. The PI at conference #1 presented the preliminary findings on The Undergrad and discussed HKU students’ attitudes towards to the Cultural Revolution since the 1967 riots. At conferences #2, #4 and #6, the PI added more case studies (i.e. Pan Ku magazine and Chinese University Student Press). It demonstrates the similarities and differences between educated youths’ understandings of the Cultural Revolution. In the published essay, the PI successfully illustrates that Chinese nationalism, along with Maoism and the Cultural Revolution, played an important role in the formation of Hong Kong identity in a colonial setting. In particular, the PI documents how the 1967 riots and Cultural Revolution can be a catalyst for the rise of local/national awareness among the Hong Kong educated youth in local social movements and at critical moments, i.e. Chinese Language Movement, the Defending the Diaoyu Islands movement, when China replaced Taiwan as a United Nation member, and the “Learning about China; Caring about Society” movement. Through exploring the New Left’s Cultural Revolution discourse, it shows that nationalism and Maoism was used as an ideological force to nurture a sense of belonging in Hong Kong. The third publication achieved objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4 mentioned in the ECS project. The journal article titled “Inscribing the Cultural Revolution in the Hong Kong Everyday: Lü Da, Wen Wei Po, and the Question of Hong Kong Literary History”. The article was presented at conference #3, where the PI discussed the left’s tactics of spreading the Cultural Revolution ideology in Hong Kong everyday (this answers some of the questions raised in objective 3). After finishing the conference, the PI revised the article and added a concrete case study showing the localization tactics used by the leftist newspaper, Wen Wei Po. In this sense, the PI answered the questions in objectives 2 and 3 by showing Wen Wei Po’s localization strategy to promote a national mission (i.e. the Cultural Revolution as ideological and literary discourse) to Hong Kong readers. The article also answered the questions raised in the objectives 2 and 3 by showing how the formation of local identity occurs in the localization process. Moreover, in order to compare the different strategies used to represent "the Cultural Revolution", the PI also discussed the right-wing newspapers’ interpretation and strategies on anti-Cultural Revolution ideology in the run-up to the 1967 riots. The PI also explained the way the right-wing newspapers promote nationalistic discourse in Hong Kong (this answered the questions raised in objective 4). The article will soon be published by in the 2021 Spring issue of Modern Chinese Literature and Culture. The fourth article achieved the objectives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 mentioned in the ECS project. The journal article titled “Liminality, Chinese Nationalism and Place Identity: Cultural Revolution Discourse in Ming Pao” has been completed and will be submitted to an international journal published by Cambridge University Press (e.g. Modern Asian Studies). The article was first presented at conference #5, where I discussed Ming Pao’s interpretation on the Cultural Revolution in the mid 1960s. I then situate the Ming Pao case study in the ideological conflict between left and the right-wing newspapers in Hong Kong at conference #8. The final draft now includes both left, right and neutral understandings of the Cultural Revolution in order to show the uniqueness of Ming Pao’s tactics of constructing a counterbalanced identity in the liminal space of the Hong Kong Cold War era (This answered the questions raised in objectives 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6). The fifth article is an updated version of “the second publication” in Chinese. I added new materials from the 70s magazine to highlight the similarities and differences between different New Left journals on the issue of the Cultural Revolution. I also added the New Left journal’s understanding on the outbreak of Cultural Revolution in the mid-1966, so as to delineate the educated youth changing attitude toward Communist China in a more detailed manner. The article will be included in an edited volume on Hong Kong Literature and Culture. Through including new materials, the objective 6 can be further realised. The edited volume will be under review by a university press in Hong Kong.

25614016.label: Major findings and research outcome
25614016.value: The major findings and contributions of my ECS is shown as below: 1. This is the first comprehensive study of Hong Kong journalist discourse on "the Cultural Revolution in Hong Kong" in the Cold War period. Not only new primary sources have been discovered, but also new perspectives on understanding Hong Kong identity have been developed. The project shows the "Cold War" ideological conflicts were expressed through different representations of the Cultural Revolution by left-, neutral and right-wing print media to construct a national/local identity for their audience. For example, research output 4 illustrates the distinctiveness of Hong Kong during the Cold War period by showing different newspapers' interpretations on the Cultural Revolution. Output 4 also points out Hong Kong as a liminal space where ideological concepts e.g. Chinese nationalism (in various forms), Communism, and colonialism coexisted, transcending the conventional opposition between communism and capitalism. Hence, the project makes a contribution to the studies of Hong Kong and Cold War. 2. The dominant view that Maclehose’s social policies was the main contributing factor to the formation of Hong Kong identity in the 1960s and 1970s. The project shows the 1960s and 1970s Hong Kong identity formation to be more complex. The formation of Hong Kong identity was an interaction of Chinese nationalism, Communism, colonialism and local awareness. The publication output 2 shows that the identity formation process is not exclusively the result of the colonial government. The Maclehose's social policies were more or less a response to the radical movements in the 1970s. Further, Communism and Chinese nationalism were ideological forces to nurture the growth of local awareness. 3. Not much research has explored the effect of the Cultural Revolution in local newspapers. The project fills the research gap and makes a contribution to the studies of global Maoism. It documents many stories on "Cultural Revolution in Hong Kong" published in different newspapers of different political groups. Publication output 3 documents the local response to the outbreak of Cultural Revolution and local propaganda tactics. 4. Theoretically, the project attempts to establish "a local approach" (bottom-up approach, rather than top-down approach ) to understand the local transformation of the Cultural Revolution ideology in local newspaper. For example, output 3 shows this bottom-up approach, allowing us to see the local and sophisticated applications of the Cultural Revolution as a condition for developing the colonial city's culture.

25614016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25614016.value: 1. GRF proposal: The PI extends the scope of study to include pro-KMT and extreme-right journals. Including these extreme-right journals will allow us to understand the heterogeneity of the Cultural Revolution discourse in Hong Kong print media. The PI has submitted a GRF application last year. 2. Book proposal: The PI further situates the discussion of the Cultural Revolution discourse in the setting of Hong Kong Cold War era and will submit a book proposal to an international press later this year.

25614016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25614016.value: The project considers “the Cultural Revolution in Hong Kong” as an ideological conflict amongst different newspapers by different political groups, which is distinct from the current understanding that focuses on the 1967 riots and considers it to be a socio-political movement. The ideological conflicts were expressed through different representations of the Cultural Revolution by left-, neutral and right-wing print media to construct a national/local identity for their audience in the setting of the Cold War. Through exploring “the Cultural Revolution discourse”, my project has demonstrated the formation of local/national identity in a colonial setting in terms of politics, culture, ethnicity, geography and ideology. The localization of the Cultural Revolution’s ideological influence in the city, either convergence with or divergence from Communist and Cultural Revolution ideology, can be seen as ideological sources to develop Hong Kong identity. Such ideological dialectic illustrates the complexity of Hong Kong identity formation in the negotiation between Chinese nationalism, Communism, colonialism and localism. In short, the research results shown in the PI’s research, publications and public activities, and teaching materials successfully re-examines the dominant view that Maclehose’s social policies was the main contributing factor to the formation of Hong Kong identity in the 1960s and 1970s.

25614116.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25614116.value: 退場、發聲與中國及越南已婚移民工廠工人的家庭/工作互動

25614116.label: Project Objectives
25614116.value: To explore how the state, market and family impact on migrant workers’ strategies, work/life balance and workplace relations; To compare China and Vietnam in these terms and to explore the reasons underpinning the differences, to gain additional insights through comparison; To identify limitations of existing household registration policies and suggest ways to help migrant workers integrate into cities; To develop a post-socialist perspective to analyse work/family dynamics, and to explore the future pathways which industrial and family relations in China and Vietnam may develop.

To compare China and Vietnam in these terms and to explore the reasons underpinning the differences, to gain additional insights through comparison;
To identify limitations of existing household registration policies and suggest ways to help migrant workers integrate into cities;
To develop a post-socialist perspective to analyse work/family dynamics, and to explore the future pathways which industrial and family relations in China and Vietnam may develop.

25614116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25614116.value: Most migrant workers in China and Vietnam are young and single, but an increasing number are past their mid-20s and are married. Since the mid-2000s, a rapidly increasing number of these migrant workers have been moving along with their spouses and children from the countryside to industrial cities in places like China’s Pearl River Delta (PRD) and Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC) area (Liang 2007, Waibel 2007). This phenomenal shift in migration patterns has led the Vietnamese and Chinese governments to reform their household registration systems respectively in 2007 and 2014 (Chi 2015, Li 2015). How does the migration of their families affect workers’ perspectives to their working and family lives? These Chinese and Vietnamese workers are experiencing new patterns in their everyday life and family relations. They are encountering new modes of housing arrangements, new forms of community relations, integration into new social networks in cities, and new household organization strategies. Yet these major sets of shifts have barely been studied. Nor has research been done on how the new surge in married migrant couples with children affects labor relations at factories. To conceptualize the changes underway, this research project uses Albert O. Hirschman’s notion of Exit (quitting a job) vs. Voice (staying and demanding a change) to analyse workers’ reactions to job dissatisfaction. Previous studies have shown that Chinese and Vietnamese migrant workers have reacted to dissatisfaction with factory conditions in different ways—while Chinese workers normally have quit a factory and seek employment elsewhere, Vietnamese workers have chosen to stay and demand change by engaging in strike actions (Chan 2011, Pringle and Clarke 2011). However, alongside changing labour market conditions and aging migrant workforce, with more Chinese workers settling in cities with their children, it is uncertain whether Chinese workers can still be so mobile in changing jobs. The same set of interviews that will explore changes in their family life will ask questions about their perspectives on their jobs, work mobility, and labor protest. I will use Shenzhen and HCMC as my major field sites to conduct this comparative study. The methodology includes documentary research, in-depth interviews, and observations. One hundred and twenty families (sixty for each country) will be interviewed. This research will contribute to the current debates regarding family change, community development, worker attitudes and industrial relations in China and Vietnam. The research findings will result in several articles in internationally ranking journals. 在中國和越南，雖然大多農民工都是單身年輕人，但愈來愈多的農民工是二十五歲以上及已婚的 。自二零零五年開始，兩國的農民工與其伴侶和子女一同從農村搬到城市定居的數目急劇。他們大多移居至中國的珠江三角洲和越南的胡志明市地區（Liang 2007, Waibei 2007）。此外，他們的遷徙模式亦出現重大的改變。這都促使中國和越南政府分別在二零零七年和二零一四年改革戶籍登記制度（Chi 2015，Li 2015）。究竟工人家庭的遷徙如何影響他們對工作和家庭生活的看法呢？ 這些中國和越南的工人正經歷新的日常生活和家庭關係模式。他們正面對新的住房安排、社會關係、融入城市裡的新人際關係問題及家庭組織策略。可是，這些重大的轉變至此鮮有人探究。結婚生子的農民工數字激增，這如何影響工廠裡的勞動關係，亦從沒得到研究。為了掌握這些變遷，本研究用到阿爾伯特・赫希曼（Albert O. Hirschman）提出的「退場」（即辭職）與「發聲」（即留下並要求改變）的概念，以分析工人對工作不滿的反應。過往的研究指出，不滿工作條件的中國和越南工人都以不同的方式應對── 中國工人一般會辭職，然後在別的工廠求職；相反，越南工人會選擇留下，參與罷工行動，以求變革（Chan 2011, Pringle and Clarke 2011）。然而，面對就業市場急劇變動，農民工人口 老化，再加上愈來愈多中國農民工及其子女一同在城市定居，中國工人能否仍然如此自由的轉換工作，仍是未知之數。本研究會在同一系列的調查中，探討中國和越南家庭生活轉變的同時，也會問及他們如何看待自己的工作、流動性及工人示威。 本研究會以深圳巿和胡志明市為主要考察地區，進行是次比較研究。研究方法包括文獻研究、深入訪談及田野考察。筆者將會訪問一百二十個家庭（每個國家各六十個家庭）。本研究將有助了解現時中國和越南的家庭變化、社會發展、工人態度和勞資關係的討論。研究結果將刊載於不同的國際知名期刊中。

25614116.label: Realisation of objectives
25614116.value: All research objectives have been achieved. Since this project focuses on exploring how the state, market and family impact on migrant workers’ strategies, work/life balance and workplace relations (objective 1), as well as comparing China and Vietnam in these terms and exploring the reasons underpinning these differences in order to gain additional insights through comparison (objective 2), the PI has conducted extensive fieldwork research and intensive case studies in several cities in Guangdong province in southern China and in northern and southern cities in Vietnam. The PI has conducted ethnographic fieldwork by residing with a group of male Chinese migrant workers for nine months; conducted a factory gate survey with a sample size of 700 workers; and engaged in in-depth interviews with over a hundred workers, factory owners, managers, government officials, trade unionists and labour NGO organizers. Many of these informants met with me on multiple occasions over many years, allowing me to delve deeper into issues as time went on. The PI has also collected voluminous archival materials written by workers and statistics published by 2 local governments. This research has culminated in the PI’s recent three journal publications. Through intensive interviews with migrant families in comparable industrial cities (e.g. Shenzhen City, Ho Chi Minh City, etc.) as well as interviewing local government officials in China and Vietnam, the PI has been able to understand how different state policies have been influencing migrant workers’ strategies, especially how local governments have different degrees of discretions in including or excluding migrant workers into their cities within a socialist country, and how the Chinese and Vietnamese governments have different national state policies in handling migration flows from the countryside to urban centres. Having discovered this major differences, the PI specifically has looked at how the household registration policies—unique feature of socialist countries in regulating rural-to-urban migration flows—have been impacting on migrants’ strategies and livelihoods in cities (objective 3). It has been found that the pre-2014 Chinese and pre-2007 Vietnamese household registration systems had already had substantial differences in terms of discriminating migrant workers in integrating into urban centres. In particular, the PI has found that there has been an inclination for the Chinese system favouring individual migration, whereas the Vietnamese system favouring family migration. This contrasted feature has still continued and existed in the post-2014 Chinese and post-2007 Vietnamese household registrations, resulting in specifically Chinese migrant children moving with their parents from the countryside to cities having great difficulties in accessing local, affordable and quality public education, whereas Vietnamese migrant children being much easier to get into public education system in urban centres. Apart from the state influences, the PI has also observed that market forces have also been shaping migrant workers’ strategies and workplace relations substantially. Particularly, due to rising labour costs in coastal cities in China, many transnational corporations have been moving to inland provinces or other Asian or southeast Asian countries to seek cheaper labour. This capital flight has impacted on Chinese migrant workers’ migration strategies greatly. Unlike the migration patterns between the early 1990s and late 2000s where most rural migrants migrated afar from the countryside in inland Chinese provinces to coastal provinces, today increasing amount of Chinese migrant workers have been favouring shorter distance migration and moving from rural to urban areas within a province, especially those provinces having new industrial complexes being newly set up. Comparatively, similar situation happens only in northern Vietnam where most migrants travelled shorter distance from Hanoi’s nearby provinces to Hanoi, whereas majority of Vietnamese migrants still travelled afar from all different places crossing provincial borders to Ho Chi Minh City. All these have changed workers’ work/life balance and workplace relations. For example, those Chinese migrant workers having within-province migration now can have more time to spend with their families, unlike the previous situation where they could only return home in spring festivals once a year. Additionally, factory owners also did not need to build factory dormitory to house rural-migrants, and thus migrant workers having more freedom and less restriction in their leisure time. Comparatively, this did not worry factory owners in Vietnam because since the economic reform in the 1980s, Vietnamese migrant workers have been used not to reside in factory dormitories; they usually rented private apartments in industrial communities near their working factories. As for how family impacted on workers’ strategies, work/life balance and workplace relations, the PI has found that Vietnamese migrant workers had greater household responsibilities to shoulder, relative to Chinese migrant workers. This partly is due to the fact that Vietnamese usually favor family migration and bring along elderly and children with them, whereas Chinese migrant workers usually opt for individual migration, leaving elderly and children behind in the countryside. Because of this, labour time that factory owners can demand from Vietnamese migrant workers are much lower than that of the Chinese workers. In other words, Vietnamese workers, though still toiling hard in their work life, have better work/life balance than Chinese workers. Through investigations in this project, the PI has been able to develop a post-socialist perspective to analyze work/family dynamics (objective 4), especially how the characteristic socialist household registration system impacted on workers’ livelihoods, which does not exist in other capitalist societies. Furthermore, these investigation and research findings also enable the PI to explore the future pathways which industrial and family relations in China and Vietnam may develop (objective 4). Particularly, through observing Chinese and Vietnamese migrant workers’ migration flow and directions, as well as the locus of capital flight, the PI has been able to explore different new patterns of industrial relations and family relations in China and Vietnam, which has great research significances in enriching the literature in terms of diversity of industrial models and family migration patterns in China and Vietnam.
