25614116.label: Major findings and research outcome
25614116.value: China is not the only Asian society that has undergone rapid industrialization in the past century. When comparing the Chinese case with Vietnam, the PI has demonstrated the two Asian neighbours are undergoing different developmental trajectories. The Vietnamese state has a different strategy for post-socialist modernization that encourages more family/work integration, less inequality between urban-born and migrant rural workers, and more community integration. In terms of state intervention into workers’ mobility, the Vietnamese policy showed a cultural concern to sustain the family as an integral part of daily life even when workers have to migrate to an unfamiliar place to work. A more relaxed household registration system (in Vietnamese, hokhau) has enabled continuation of workers’ familial and community networks. A better work/life balance was found in Vietnam. Because Vietnamese workers could bring their families to the urban communities where they work, they often had daily family responsibilities to care for children and the elderly. These family responsibilities acted as a check on factory management’s assignment of overtime work. Although similar mixed payment systems and production facilities were found in south Vietnam’s and south China’s large garment factories, the factory managers in Vietnam could not compel workers to work as long as Chinese workers, and a substantial difference in monthly work hours was found between the two countries. Since the mid-2000s, a rapidly increasing number of migrant workers are married and have moved with their spouses and children from the countryside to industrial cities in China and Vietnam. This major shift in migration patterns has led the Vietnamese and Chinese governments to reform their household registration systems in 2007 and 2014 respectively. The PI argues that even though China and Vietnam possess similar legacies of socialist transformation and have household registration regulations that on paper restrict rural migrants’ access to urban social services and impede their settlement in cities, there exist marked differences in Guangdong and Ho Chi Minh City in migration patterns, factory work conditions and migrant worker family livelihoods. Particularly, while migrant families in Ho Chi Minh City tend to settle there permanently, married migrant workers in Guangdong normally still need to split up their families and remain trapped in circular rural-urban migration. The most important factor contributing to this marked difference has to do with the two countries’ policies in migrant children’s access to education in urban centres.

25614116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25614116.value: The research findings of this project have great potential for further development. Most of the existing empirical studies about the situation of Chinese migrant workers are based on research findings collected in China’s coastal regions. However, as living costs and labour costs in China’s coastal regions increase year by year many factories have been relocating into China’s inland provinces, and many Chinese workers therefore no longer travel afar from inland Chinese provinces to coastal regions to work. Similarly, over the past half decade, the PI have witnessed similar developmental patterns in Vietnam. Thus, it is interesting to investigate how the circumstances of factory workers who work in inland provinces near to their rural homes differ from those who work in coastal regions in China and Vietnam, and to understand the ramifications of these differences.

25614116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25614116.value: Since the mid-2000s, an increasing number of migrant workers have been moving along with their spouses and children from the countryside to industrial cities in places like China’s Pearl River Delta and Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC) area. This project discovers that although China and Vietnam possess similar legacies of socialist transformation and have household registration regulations on paper restricting rural migrants’ access to urban social services and impeding their settlement in cities, there exist marked differences in Guangdong and HCMC in migration patterns, work conditions and migrant family livelihoods. While migrant families in HCMC tend to settle there permanently, married migrant workers in Guangdong still need to split up their families and remain trapped in circular rural-urban migration. The factor contributing to this difference has to do with two countries’ policies in migrant children’s access to education in urban centres. A better work/life balance was found in Vietnam. Because Vietnamese workers could bring their families to urban communities, they had daily family responsibilities to care for children and the elderly. These responsibilities acted as a check on factory management’s assignment of overtime work, causing managers in Vietnam unable to compel workers to work as long as Chinese workers.

25614216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25614216.value: 重繪二戰記憶地圖：當代中國大陸、台灣和香港的紀念建築

25614216.label: Project Objectives
25614216.value: First, it aims to display the unspoken politics of Chineseness, legacies of western/Japanese colonialism and their influence on the narratives of war memory in the region. It illustrates and compares how the three Chinese societies are struggling to come to terms with their own, and each other’s past. Second, as monuments are fundamentally a form of visual and haptic artifact in public realm, the project aims to examine the relations between their visual forms and the way they shape broad public political acquiescence. Unlike studies that focus on written narratives of war memory, this project tries to open up new sensual possibilities for understanding the formation of collective (un)consciousness through the lens of the everydayness of public environment. Thirdly, it asks how we can redefine the idea of “war monument” in the region. While they were designed and made by the authority with a designated intention, the actual monuments change and obscure their original meaning and spiritual structure constantly as they renegotiate ideals, status, and entitlement. The project thus endeavors to animate the specific experience of modernity in Mainland China, Taiwan and Hong Kong by showing the intricate tension the object and the subject, the elite and the mass, the sacred and the profane.

25614216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25614216.value: This research explores five cases of monument and public commemorative space related to World War II (WWII) in Mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan. All of them were built either prior to or right after the end of the War and their physical existence still remains. They are/were dedicated or adapted to commemorating the heroes or victory of WWII. They are (1) the Cenotaph in Hong Kong, (2) the War Victory Stele in Chongqing, (3) the Army Number One India-Burma Corps Memorial Military Cemetery in Guangzhou (4) the National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine in Taipei and (5) Shanghai Sihang Warehouse. Despite their historical affinities, the three major Chinese societies in question, namely, Mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, vary in their own ways of telling, remembering and forgetting WWII. These divergences are not only rooted in their different political circumstances and social experiences, but also in their current competitions, confrontations and integrations. While most of the existing literatures are focusing on narratives of historical or war memory in one of the three Chinese societies, few researches have been done on connecting the three societies as a dynamically interrelated and contradictory whole. Moreover, even less researches are concerned about the role of art and visual existence of public monuments with regards to the debates on the formations of the feeling, knowledge and action in the three Chinese societies. Thus, this project hopes to fill in the gap in the studies of commemorative culture in the region by focusing on the visual and spatial manifestation of war memories. In this way, the careful selection of the five representative cases serves three major objectives of the study: first, it aims to observe the competitions, contradictions and confrontations of the war narratives, and in turn the various narratives of the modern Chinese nation-state, nationalism and Chineseness. Second, as monuments are fundamentally a form of visual and haptic artifact in public realm, the project aims to examine the relations between their visuality and the way they shape broad political acquiescence of the public in the three societies. Thirdly, it asks how these monuments can have a dialogue with each other and how we can redefine the idea of “Chinese war monument”. The project thus endeavors to animate the specific experience of modernity in the region by showing the intricate tension between the object and the subject, the elite and the mass, the sacred and the profane. 本研究探索五個與第二次世界大戰相關並分別位於中國大陸、香港和台灣的紀念碑和公共紀念空間。這五個案例中的紀念建築和空間都建造於戰爭時期或者戰爭結束初期，並且至今仍然存在。這五個紀念建築都是為了紀念戰爭英雄或者戰爭勝利而建，它們是（1）香港和平紀念碑，（2）重慶抗戰勝利紀念碑（今解放碑），（3）廣州新一軍印緬陣亡將士公墓, （4）台北忠烈祠，（5）上海四行倉庫抗戰紀念館。 儘管這五個案例之間有相當密切的歷史關係，它們所在的三個華人社會，即中國大陸、香港和台灣在敘述、記憶和遺忘這場戰爭的方式上卻不盡相同。這些差異不僅根植於這三個社會不同的歷史環境和社會經驗，也同它們互相之間在當下的競爭、對立和融合相關。 以往大部分關於歷史敘述和戰爭記憶的研究通常只關注這三個社會之其一，而不會將這三者當作一個聯動但也充滿矛盾的整體來看待。而以這三個社會中的藝術和公共建築的視覺形態去探討有關戰爭記憶和情感、知識和行動的研究則更加缺乏。因此，本研究希望可以通過戰爭記憶的視覺和空間表現以及探討這個地區的紀念文化來填補這一空缺。 因此，通過這五個經過慎重挑選的案例，本研究將以三個主要的方向作為目的：首先，研究希望可以觀察並描繪出大中華地區戰爭記憶之間的競爭、矛盾和對立，並以此來梳理中國現代民族國家、民族主義和中國性的不同敘事方法；第二，由於紀念碑從本質上來說是一種視覺和觸覺的公共人造景觀，本研究希望去探討視覺性是如何在這三個社會中塑造大眾政治意識的；第三，本研究試圖理解這些紀念碑之間是如何進行對話，而它們在什麼程度上可以重新來定義“中國戰爭紀念碑”的。綜上，本研究希望可以通過對主體和客體、精英和大眾、神聖和世俗之間複雜張力的研究，用新的角度來審視這個地區特有的現代性經驗。

All of them addresses, through one or multiple cases in question, the three objectives I was planning to tackle with. 1. The first objective was addressed particularly in Chapter 2 and 3 in my monograph, on war monuments in Hong Kong and Taiwan. 2. All chapters addressed the visual aspects of the monuments. 3. The idea of war monument in the region was elaborated on in the Introduction and Conclusion chapters of the book.

25614216.label: Major findings and research outcome
25614216.value: Even though WWII in the region was among the bloodiest and most significant historical happenings for all three societies in the 20th century, intriguingly and ironically, the war monuments and the war memories they intended to evoke among the public are constantly being marginalized and suspended, making ways for updated purposes of mobilizing public sentiment and sometimes leaving little space and time for the monuments to play their role in healing the wounds and trauma left by the war. All of the five cases have their own kind of marginality and uncertainty in their meaning. They underwent ups and downs, remembrance and forgetfulness. At certain moments, they are iconic representations of national memory while at other moments they were ruins, torn between high visibility and total invisibility, and visited by intended and unintended audience. The research outcomes include two journal articles, one book chapter and one monograph: 1. journal article: "Between Iconic Image and (Artificial) Ruins: Shanghai Sihang Warehouse and WWII Memory in China", in Visual Communication, 2020, forthcoming 2. journal article: "(Forgotten) Landscape of Imperial War Memories in a Colonial City: Hong Kong’s Cenotaph and beyond (1920s – 1960s) ", in China Historical Review, under review 3. book chapter: "Iconizing Taipei Yuanshan: Shinto Jinja, Grand Hotel and Martyrs’ Shrine", in Frontiers of Memory in Contemporary Asia: Difficult Heritage and the Cross-border Politics of Postcolonial Nationalism, Editors: Shu-Mei Huang, Hyun Kyung Lee, Edward Vickers, HKU Press, under review 4. monograph: Image, Imagination and Imaginarium: Remapping World War II Commemorative Artefacts in Greater China. London: Palgrave MacMillian, 2021, forthcoming

25614216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25614216.value: The research offers a base for an art project that gathers twelve artists from Mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan and South Korea, who will form a group of research team, whose research started with visiting each other's WWII monuments and commemorative spaces. They explore the idea of war monument in East Asia and the war per se first by making a documentary video of the visits. They will go on to make installation, photography, literary texts, music/audio works, performance, and participatory workshop after the trips. These works will be shown to the public for further discussions through publications, screenings and exhibitions. They will use these media as a way of being actively engaged with the seemingly frozen monument with presubscribed meanings. With their respective concerns on gender, body, narrative, spectacle, fantasy and representation, their works illustrates and compares how various East Asian societies are struggling to come to terms with their own, and each other’s past. They ask: what is the role of art in forming monuments? How can these monuments have a dialogue with each other? What are the relations between the commemorative artifacts and the public life?

25614216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25614216.value: Through the study on five war monuments, the research illustrates past and ongoing controversies and contestations over the Chinese nation, sovereignty, modernism and identity. Despite their historical affinities, the three major Chinese (huaren) societies in question, namely, Mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, vary in their own ways of telling, remembering and forgetting WWII. These divergences are not only rooted in their different political circumstances and social experiences, but also in their current competitions, confrontations and integrations. The research fills in the gap in the studies of commemorative culture in the Great China area by focusing on the visual and spatial manifestations of war memories. It not only unfolds the complexity of the war memories in the region in the post-Cold War years, but also positions war monuments in the relations between public space and history, art and memory, experience and representation, visual culture and war experience.

25614816.value: 病人、醫療工作者、政府研究、大眾傳媒和相當的學術研究皆認同溝通對醫療護理起重要的作用。病人與醫護人員互動與其醫療效果的關係更被受關注（Duggan & Thompson, 2011:414）。病人與醫護人員合作共同參與醫療過程可被稱為「以關係為本護理」，並在很多研究中證明對醫療結果起正面作用（例如Street et al., 2009; Iezzoni, 2006）。雖然以關係為本護理的重要性日漸被認同，卻缺乏有系統而詳細的語言學縱向研究，以探討如何在醫療過程體現以關係為本護理。學者提出不同的模范，大都不是以語言溝通分析為本（Elwyn et al., 2001; de Haes & Bensing, 2008），並沒有顧及關係發展的累積性，而探討此特性則需要縱向研究。因此，本研究計劃目的在於辨別與闡明和以關係為本護理有關的溝通特徵，並以詳細的語言學分析病人與醫護人員互動，追蹤病人與醫護人員關係的累積性改變。此研究計劃採用的分析方法已被應用於其他環境，（Lam & Webster, 2009; Lam, 2010; Forey & Lam, 2012; Lam & Yu, 2013），以體現溝通和關係發展的累積性，而不限於個別的溝通技巧。除此之外，本研究計劃會檢視以關係為本護理和病人滿意度與配合治療的程度之間的關係，以訂立以關係為本的護理溝通模范，從而促進醫療成效。在急診室，因為病人焦慮程度和醫護人員繁重工作等環境因素，病人與醫護人員的關係尤其複雜（Slade et al., 2008: 290）。此令急診室成為以關係為本護理獨特研究場所。此研究計劃為香港理工大學與悉尼科技大學的國際醫療溝通研究中心的研究項目之一，並利用數據分享和累積研究的概念（Sieber, 1991），使用一個香港理工大學於2001年在香港最繁忙之一的公立醫院急診室進行的直接觀察與人種學研究（Slade et al., 2015a, 本研究計劃的研究人員參與其中）所收集的豐富，稀有和獨特的數據。除了確定數據的質素和可用性，此研究計劃能對本地醫療體系的進步有所貢獻。為將研究轉化為實踐（Woolf, 2008），此研究計劃的發現將會以論文和學術會議的文章發表，並轉化成教學材料，教育醫療專業和專業環境溝通研究的學士學生，和醫護人員專業發展的訓練手冊，以提升他們對以關係為本護理相關的互動方式和溝通方法的認知和敏感度。國際醫療溝通研究中心與香港醫院管理局有恆常合作，以實行醫護人員的專業訓練。本研究計劃採用的真實數據能令學生和醫護人員更能體會實際面對的溝通挑戰。

25614816.label: Realisation of objectives
25614816.value: According to the research plan stated in the proposal, the first year of the project (i.e. the reporting period) was devoted to achieving Research Objective 1 and 2. The relevant research activities are described below. The transcripts of patient-practitioner communication collected from the previous project were not standardised and the data were stored in an unanalysable format. In the reporting period, the transcripts have been standardised in terms of data representation and format, particularly in enhancing the accuracy of Cantonese transcription using specific Chinese characters defined by the Hong Kong SAR Government, and transferring to file formats that enable linguistic and statistical analysis. The data of post-journey interviews were also standardised to more systematically present patients' degree of satisfaction and adherence (for achieving Research Objective 3). To achieve Research Objective 1, text and discourse analysis of patient-practitioner communication has been conducted to describe and track the development of patient- practitioner relationships through patients' journeys. With this work, a communication-based model for describing patients' journeys have been developed to complement existing descriptions that are largely based on medical knowledge, and the findings have been disseminated with a paper submitted to the journal Health Communication (Taylor & Francis). To achieve Research Objective 2, meta-analysis of 439 research articles on relationship- centred care has been conducted to develop an integrated model of relationship-centred care. This work will be disseminated as a systematic review paper to be submitted to the journal Patient Education and Counselling (Elsevier). This meta-analysis has informed the analysis of the communicative features of the described patients’ journeys that are relevant to relationship-centred care, particularly in terms of the control on the exchange of information, the typology of responses and patients’ activeness in engaging dialogue. The meta-analysis has also laid the foundation for the development of the modal of relationship-centred communication (for achieving Research Objective 4). Finally, the project objectives were achieved with the publication of a journal article in Word.

25614816.label: Major findings and research outcome
25614816.value: A patient’s journey refers to the series of events experienced by a patient in the process of receiving care. Most of the existing descriptions presuppose medical knowledge and may not capture a patient’s experience because patients are often not well-informed on the medical aspects of care. This project proposes a communication-based model to describe journeys as series of socio-semiotic activities, which were identified by linguistic analysis of authentic patient– practitioner communication. The model offers new granularity in characterizing the communicative unfolding of journeys, which reflects the participants’ roles and informational responsibilities. Practitioners’ communicative workload is largely concerned with information rather than actions or procedures, with doctors doing most of the communicative work. This study unpacks the communicative complexity within what would be considered as single steps from the medical point of view with a new sense of length of journeys in terms of communicative load instead of time.

25614816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25614816.value: The study serves as the basis of follow-up studies to correlate patients’ experience described with the proposed model and the patients’ levels of satisfaction and adherence, and to compare patients’ journeys from different parts of the world described by the same model.

25614816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25614816.value: This project describe patient's journey in emergency department from the communication perspective instead of the conventional medical perspective. This allows a deeper understanding of what is going on when patients are receiving care. The study found that healthcare practitioners were by and large giving information, instead of making commands or talking about procedures, and doctors are the ones doing most of the communication work. This study unpacks the complexity of communication in patient's journey, which would otherwise be considered as single steps from the medical point of view.

26101016.label: Project Objectives
26101016.value: To develop microfluidic methods, molecular biology protocols, and next-generation sequencing bioinformatics workflows, in order to achieve DNA-seq and RNA-seq from the same single cell. We will (a) design a microfluidic device and biochemistry protocol that captures single cells, performs reverse-transcription on cellular RNA without disrupting the cell nucleus, then co-amplifies cDNA with nuclear DNA, generating next-generation sequencing-compatible c/DNA fragments. Simultaneously, (b) construct computational pipelines to decompose sequenced reads into fragments that are from DNA vs. those from RNA. To validate the method developed in Objective 1 using cultured colon cancer cell line HCT116. To generate pilot data for a unified model for tumor heterogeneity generation in colon adenocarcinoma. We will perform simultaneous DNA-seq and RNA-seq on ~3000 individual cells isolated from (a) healthy colon tissue, as well as paired colon tumor from the same patient, in order to assess the phenotypic heterogeneity within each genetic clone of the tumor. We will also (b) develop bioinformatics tools to infer genetic clonality lineage from DNA, lineage phenotype from RNA, and for each single cell, superimpose the two to create an overall visualization of the tumor hierarchy.

26101016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26101016.value: Cancer cells within a tumor are often thought of as identical genetically and functionally, each cell having equal potential to grow and advance the tumor. In reality, at the single cell level, cancers are heterogeneous masses formed by cells with varying genetic traits and in different stages of differentiation. Some have studied tumor heterogeneity in the context of genetic mutations, and found that cancers evolve over time, with the dominating cells being those having mutations that confer a survival advantage. This process of tumor evolution in a Darwinian-like manner, in which more fit subpopulations of cancer cells grew to be the more dominant ‘clone’, was termed Clonal Evolution. Others have observed that some cells in the cancer were unique because they displayed characteristics similar to those of normal stem cells. This subset of cancer cells displays stem-cell-like surface markers, is capable of self-renewal, and can differentiate into a host of different cancer cell types. Phenotypically, many tumors recapitulate the normal tissue development in their hierarchical organization, with the cancer stem cells being the only cells that have the ability to re-populate the entire tumor with cancer cells of varying differentiated states. This model of tumorigenesis is known as the Cancer Stem Cell model. The two models both describe tumorigenesis, and both may contribute to intratumoral heterogeneity, but currently there is no way to investigate the relationship between the two processes. This is because one is framed in the context of genotype (DNA and mutation information), and the other is framed in the context of phenotype (gene expression, proteins, etc). There has been no study to reconcile clonal evolution and cancer stem cells in a unified model of tumorigenesis. Colon cancer, one of the leading causes of mortality in the developed world, is a cancer for which evidence exists for both clonal evolution and the cancer stem cell models. We propose to perform single cell DNA and RNA profiling to study the tumor heterogeneity in colon cancer. By measuring both the genotype and phenotype from the same single tumor cells, and mapping each cell to their genetic clones while superimposing their phenotype information within each clone, we can shed light on the mechanism of tumorigenesis in colon cancer. A deeper view of how tumor heterogeneity is generated, both in genotype and phenotype, will shed light on why current therapies sometimes fail, why there is relapse and metastasis, and reveal new therapeutic targets. 一个肿瘤中的所有癌细胞在基因与功能方面通常被认为是相同的，并具有相等的增长与促进肿瘤的潜力。但事实上，在单细胞层面来看，一个肿瘤是由具有不同的遗传性状和处于不同分化阶段的细胞形成的异质块组织。过去某些对于肿瘤异质性的研究，在检测癌细胞的基因突变时发现随着时间的推移肿瘤细胞会逐渐衍变，并且其中的主导细胞是那些被基因突变所赋予了生存优势的群体。在这种肿瘤演化模型中，这些生存力更优的癌细胞亚群逐渐成为肿瘤中的主导‘克隆’，因此这种类似于达尔文式的肿瘤发展过程被称为‘单克隆演化模型’。 但是在另一类肿瘤异质性的研究中，人们发现有一些癌细胞是独一无二的，因为它们拥有与正常干细胞相似的特征——这种癌细胞亚群有类似干细胞的表面标记、拥有自我更新能力、并能分化成多种不同的癌细胞类型。 许多肿瘤在其细胞层次结构和组织上与正常组织发育近似重演，而之前所描述的‘癌干细胞’是唯一具有以不同分化状态的癌细胞重建整个肿瘤的能力的细胞亚群。 这种肿瘤发展过程被称为‘癌干细胞模型’。 单克隆演化和癌干细胞这两种模型都试图解释肿瘤的起因与发展机理，两者都能导致瘤内异质性，但目前无法得知两者之间的关系。这是因为，前者存在于基因型（也就是DNA和突变信息）的框架中，后者则存在于表型（也就是基因表达，蛋白质等）的框架中。目前还没有任何研究将克隆演化和癌干细胞调和成为一个统一的、更全面的肿瘤生成发展模型。 结肠癌是发达国家的主要死因之一，它也是克隆演化和癌干细胞模型证据同时存在的癌症。我们提议进行单细胞DNA和RNA同时分析来研究结肠癌肿瘤异质性。通过从单个肿瘤细胞同时测量基因型和表型，我们可以先利用基因型将每个细胞分划到所属的克隆亚群，然后再利用表型信息确定细胞亚型，将两者叠加，从而阐明结肠癌肿瘤的发生机制。通过这次的研究我们会对肿瘤异质性的生成过程，无论是在基因型或表型层面，得到更深的了解，并且有助于揭示为何目前的癌症治疗方法有时会失败、为什么会出现复发和转移，甚至发现新的治疗靶点。

26104216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26104216.value: The majority of mammalian genomes consist of non-coding sequences that were once mistakenly defined as “junk-DNA”. In recent years, advancements in DNA sequencing technologies have revealed that these regions contain repetitive sequences and key regulatory elements. One particular class of non-coding elements is the endogenous retroviruses (ERVs), relics of invading retroviruses, which have colonized all higher eukaryotic genomes. If deregulated, they can have deleterious consequences and affect the expression of nearby coding genes. Furthermore, they have the capacity to create mutations and damage genomic integrity. Hence, stringent regulation of such elements via epigenetic modifications is critical to the fitness of the host. Intriguingly, throughout evolution, particular ERVs have been co-opted into carrying out endogenous functions. For instance, many ERVs behave as transcriptional promoters or enhancers for genes in both mouse and human genomes. These sequences help shape the distinct gene expression programs that give rise to the identities of different cell types. However, the pervasiveness of this phenomenon and the mechanism behind it remain poorly understood. Therefore, understanding the role of ERVs under normal physiological conditions allows for insight into how cells function. Taking an approach that combines bioinformatic analyses of publicly available epigenomic datasets and molecular biology experiments, we first aim to elucidate the role of ERVs in modulation of gene transcription in the human genome. Subsequently, we aim to delineate the epigenetic mechanisms responsible for such ERV-mediated transcriptional regulation using mouse cells in vitro. Moreover, we will investigate the epigenetic pathways that repress unwanted ERV activities. My previous work has shown that Setdb1, a histone methyltransferase, epigenetically silences ERVs. Interestingly, its function is required for cell viability in some cell types including mouse embryonic stem cells but not others. Therefore, we hypothesize that Setdb1 is necessary for ERV regulation in cells undergoing epigenome reprogramming, such as stem cells and progenitor cells. Employing molecular biology approaches, we aim to identify the cell types in which Setdb1-mediated ERV silencing pathway functions. These findings may have important clinical implications. In fact, cancer cells potentially require Setdb1 to stay viable, as many cancers have notably unstable epigenomes. Taken together, these studies will shed light on the epigenetic regulation of ERVs and their diverse properties, revealing the significance of these non-coding sequences in cellular processes. 大多數哺乳類動物基因組內的非編碼序列曾經錯誤地被定義為“垃圾DNA”。近年來由於DNA測序技術的進步，我們發現這些區域含有重複序列和關鍵的調控元件。其中一個特別的非編碼元素是內源性逆轉錄病毒（ ERVs ），其形成是由過去逆轉錄病毒入侵高等真核生物基因組時所留下的遺物。如果它們失調會導致有害的後果，例如影響附近的基因表達。此外它們亦有製造基因突變和令基因組完整性受損的能力，因此細胞通過表觀遺傳修飾來嚴格監管這些非編碼序列來維持其健康狀況。 有趣的是在整個進化過程中，ERVs在細胞中漸漸成為不可或缺的存在。因為在老鼠和人的細胞裡，許多ERVs已變成可以影響基因表達的轉錄啟動子或增強子。這些序列通過控制基因的表達程序而促使不同類型細胞的形成，然而這種現象的普遍性和其背後的機制仍然知之甚少，因此我們才要更加深入了解ERVs在正常生理條件下的作用並從中洞察細胞功能。結合公開的表觀數據集、分子生物實驗和生物信息的分析，我們會首先解開ERVs在人類基因組基因轉錄裡所負責的調節作用；隨後我們會利用老鼠細胞來解讀由ERVs介導下基因轉錄調控的表觀遺傳修飾機制。總而言之，這些研究將闡明ERVs和它們與別不同的表觀遺傳調控的性質；並對於了解這些非編碼序列在生命現象基本過程具有重要的意義。

26104216.label: Realisation of objectives
26104216.value: 1. Determining the role of endogenous retroviruses in human embryonic stem cells The human genome consists of a larger proportion of repetitive elements. Among which, human endogenous comprise of approximately 8% of all sequence. In the last several year, increasing evidence has shown that HERVs have the capacity to function as cis-regulatory elements and are tightly regulated by epigenetic mechanisms. Therefore, we aimed to apply a variety of epigenomic and genome engineering methods to study their functions in pluripotent stem cells. Moreover, to circumvent the issues of multiple alignment of HERVs, we developed a method termed CARP-seq to define the precise genomic locations of repetitive elements. Taken together, these experiments aimed to elucidate how HERVs influence the epigenomic and transcriptome of pluripotent stem cells. Details of the outcomes are provided below. 2. Elucidating cis-regulatory mechanisms of endogenous retroviruses in mouse embryonic stem cells Unlike human endogenous retroviruses, murine ERVs have retained a higher rate of retrotransposition activity. It was previously reported that ERVs are responsible for ~10% of all somatic mutations that occur in the mouse genome. While polymorphic elements have been described, how they impact the epigenome has not been studied in detail. Here, we employed a range of genomic and epigenomic editing techniques to show how a polymorphic ERV element functions as a unique cis-regulatory element, which gives rise to differential phenotypes between widely used laboratory mouse strains. Details of the outcomes are provided below.

26104216.label: Major findings and research outcome
26104216.value: In objective 1, we aimed to study how HERVs were epigenetic regulated and how their activities impact the epigenome and transcriptome of human pluripotent stem cells. Utilizing human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) and expanded potential stem cells (EPSCs) as model systems, we have identified several novel aspects of HERV function and regulation. Firstly, we developed the ChIP Assisted Repeat Pinpointing by Sequencing (CARP-seq) approach. This method could significantly improve the detection rate of difficult to map repetitive elements. For instance, comparing H3K27ac ChIP-seq datasets from the Roadmap Epigenome project, CARP-seq was able to capture substantially more LTR12C elements (n=1,721 vs n=2,413). However, as sequencing technologies improve, the mappability issue can also be overcome by longer reads and deeper coverage. Nevertheless, CARP-seq is an efficient way to validate the positions of highly repetitive sequences. We plan to include this method in a future publications. We had previously noted that LTR12C elements possessed cell-type specific features of cis-regulatory elements. In our detailed analysis, we discovered that a subset functioned as hESC-specific promoters. These elements were enriched with differential 3D chromatin interactions. Integrative analysis of the generated data will be useful to further elucidate their functions. Most strikingly, we discovered that the chromatin regulator RIF1 functioned to silence HERVs in hESCs, including LTR12C elements. Intriguingly, the mechanism was exclusive to hESCs. We collaborated with Prof David Gilbert (Florida State University) on defining epigenomic impacts of RIF1 depletion in hESCs. The manuscript is under review at Science. All the results relating to HERV regulation in the manuscript originated from this objective. For objective 2, we focused on delineating the impact of polymorphic ERVs on the epigenome and transcriptome. When analyzing the genomes of commonly used laboratory mouse strains, we discovered a polymorphic element from the GLN subfamily, which integrated upstream of the Klhdc4 gene in C57Bl/6 but not 129SvJ genomes. This element possessed unique epigenetic signatures. Through genetic and epigenetic editing approaches, we showed that the GLN element functioned as an enhancer and regulated the chromatin organization of the region. Moreover, this led to differential expression of stress-response genes that give rise to a strain specific-phenotypes. We further demonstrate that the scale of polymorphic ERVs in the mouse genome and their influence are larger than previously appreciated. The manuscript of these findings is currently under review at Nature Communications.

26104216.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26104216.value: Our findings demonstrate how retrotransposons can influence the epigenome and transcriptomes of pluripotent stem cells in previously unappreciated ways. Building upon these results, we have two follow up studies, which aim to further attempt to decipher molecular functions of ERVs. Firstly, we plan to continue the investigation of the role of LTR12C elements in the EPSC system and determine whether their promoter activity and differential higher-order chromatin interactions are important for the totipotent stem cell’s functions. Some of the datasets generated in the current project will be incorporated into the subsequent integrative bioinformatic analysis. Furthermore, we have discovered that trophoblast stem cells (TSCs) possess distinct HERV-derived cis-regulatory elements that are differentially active as compared to ES cells. This prompted us to ask whether such elements influence how TSC functions. We have generated some intriguing preliminary data, which were the subject of a separate GRF application. Furthermore, our findings have led to a number of local and international collaborations to study the role of HERVs in diverse development and disease contexts. Details on these collaborations will be mentioned below.

26104216.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26104216.value: Mammalian genomes comprise of mostly non-coding DNA sequences. The most abundant of which are the retrotransposons. These sequences, including endogenous retroviruses (ERVs), are the remnants of invading retroviruses that integrated in a specie’s ancestral germline. Such elements make up approximately 10% and 8% of the mouse and human genomes, respectively. Notably, if left unchecked, ERVs are capable of affecting the host’s genome structure and proper gene regulation. Our research aims to understand how ERVs are regulated and how a subset of elements evolved to contribute to important host functions. Using human and mouse embryonic stem cells as experimental models, we discovered a new mechanism of how ERVs are repressed. Moreover, among those that escape silencing, several serve to regulate the activity of host genes. Strikingly, we discovered elements are present in particular mouse strains and absent in others. These ERVs change the activity and regulation of the nearby DNA, which contribute to distinct physiological traits between strains. Taken together, the results of our study shed light on how ERVs influence hosts genes, which may provide further insights into how our cells deal with and exploit these elements in development and disease processes.

26200316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26200316.value: Materials with strong first-order phase transformations between crystalline phases have emerging applications for medical devices, microelectronics, and energy conversion. A major problem with these materials is the lack of phase reversibility, i.e. the gradual loss of latent heat during cycling, the decrease of superelastic strain and the associated accumulation of plastic deformation upon cyclic loading. Very recent discoveries [Song et. al, Nature (2013) and Chluba et al. Science (2015)] strongly suggest that the conditions of compatibility called the Cofactor Conditions (CC) [Chen et al, JMPS (2013)] play an unprecedented role in enhancing reversibility. The alloys exhibit nearly zero functional fatigue upon multi-million full transformation cycles, when their lattice parameters are tuned to satisfy CC closely. These results are in sharp contrast to ordinary martensitic materials, which degrade significantly only after several hundred cycles. These results point to a revolution in understanding of martensitic materials and inspiring potential applications. The alloy Zn45Au30Cu25 with satisfaction of CC, shows unusual microstructure: curved austenite/martensite interfaces irreproducible in consecutive transformation cycles. These phenomena are unlike any common martensite microstructure. Based on the geometrically non-linear theory, we have proven that the satisfaction of CC will result in curved interfaces and absence of elastic transition layers. We conjecture that the flexibility in constructing CC interfaces leads to the exceptional reversibility, yet the quantitative justification for this relationship is needed. In this proposal, we will systematically investigate the microstructure-reversibility relationship for the alloy Zn45Au30Cu25 and its nearby compositions. Both thermal and micro-mechanical reversibility will be quantified. The quantitative microstructure characterization will be done by Synchrotron X-ray Laue Microdiffraction at the Advance Light Source Beamline 12.3.2, Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, with which the PI has long-term affiliation: 1) measuring precisely the lattice parameters and symmetries for austenite and martensite; 2) constructing the spatial orientation distribution in situ at phase transformation. Quantitative morphologies and interface coherencies will be quantified from the orientation mapping. Based on a suite of algorithms developed by the PI, we will check the conditions of compatibility with the experimental data. Finally we will establish the relation how the formation of compatible microstructure improves the macroscopic properties in material. Success of the project will underlie new rules for development of functional materials. The exploited methodology gives the first demonstration for quantifying the morphology of interface in situ at phase transformation. In addition, the investigation opens up the possibility to a universal strategy for theory-based material design. 具有體積變化的一級固態可逆相變被廣泛應用於醫療微設備，微電子器件和能量轉化器。但是，此類材料有個普遍的問題，就是相變的可逆性隨著相變循環次數的增加而降低。主要體現在相變潛熱的減小，超彈形變降低而最終導致材料塑性變形，甚至破壞。 最近的關於開發新型形狀記憶材料的研究成果表明，材料內部的晶體結構的相容性條件，即Cofactor Conditions，對於相變材料的相容性起著重要作用。某些實驗結果表明，當材料的晶格常數滿足相容性條件時，材料的熱滯減小為零，並且其功能性經歷上百萬次循環而保持不變。在相變過程中，材料的微觀結構表現出異於常規馬氏體結構，即呈現出彎曲的相界面，並且此類微觀結構的組合在每次的相變過程中都不會重複出現。基於非線性馬氏體幾何理論，我們可以推算出，此類微觀結構的形成是材料晶體參數滿足Cofactor Conditions的結果。而且我們推斷，正是這些特殊微觀結構導致材料的超可逆性。 在此項目申請中，我們將要系統並全面的研究微觀結構與固體可逆相變的可逆性之間的關係。研究對象是形狀記憶合金Zn45Au30Cu25及其相近的化學組分。我們將要定量的逕行熱學和微，納米尺度的力學研究。並且結合同步輻射X射線Laue微區衍射進行微觀結構的定量研究。此實驗將在美國勞倫茲國家實驗室的先進光源中心進行。通過精確的測量材料的晶格參數而計算出相容性條件的每項指標。通過結合熱學實驗的結果，準確控制相變進程，通過微區掃描測量相變界面的力學和晶體學參量。最終建立材料相容性條件，相容微觀結構以及材料宏觀物理，力學性能之間的關係。此項課題的成功，將從根本上改變傳統材料開發的模式，從而建立基於理論的新材料合成與開發的鏈式方法。

26200316.value: We successfully synthesized a series of Zn-Au-Cu alloys and its nearby compositions and sibling ternary alloys. Both thermal and micromechanics analysis have been conducted to characterize the functional degradation upon cyclic martensitic phase transformation. We performed synchrotron X-ray microdiffraction at ALS, Lawrence Berkeley National Lab to characterize the lattice parameters and symmetries of the austenite and martensite, and examined the cofactor conditions for them by calculating the symmetry-related transformation stretch tensors. Our development strategy has been proven very effective to improve the reversibility of phase-transforming materials, not only in Zn-Au-Cu alloy system, but also in other alloy systems and ceramic systems.

26201616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26201616.value: Autonomous micro aerial vehicles (MAVs) have cost and mobility benefits, making them ideal robotic platforms for applications including aerial photography, surveillance, and search and rescue. Most successful commercial autonomous aerial robots utilize Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) for estimation and control, limiting their operations to outdoor spaces. But the power of MAVs lies in their ability to operate in GNSS-denied environments that are inaccessible or dangerous for human. In the event of disasters such as earthquakes, mining accidents, or chemical explosions, there is a huge demand for an aerial robot to navigate autonomously through cluttered and unknown environments, carrying out tasks such as searching for survivors and identifying potential hazards. Appropriate sensors are required to replace GNSS to enable autonomous operations under these conditions. Although smaller platforms are better for operation in confined environments, they also introduce tight size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints. As the platform scales down, a monocular visual-inertial system (VINS), consisting only of an inertial measurement unit (IMU) and a camera, becomes the only viable sensor suite because of its ultra-light weight and small footprint. In fact, it is the minimum sensor suite allowing both autonomous flight and sufficient environmental awareness. Challenges exist in two important aspects when using monocular VINS for autonomous navigation, namely estimation (determining position, velocity, orientation, etc) and mapping (detecting obstacles) problems. Due to the lack of direct distance measurements, metric scale must be obtained by fusion of camera and IMU measurements, which requires reliable visual tracking under sufficiently excited motions. This dilemma situation motivates the development of robust estimation algorithms. The mapping problem comes from the requirement of dense scene modeling for guaranteed obstacle detection. State-of-the-art VINS approaches that relies on sparse features are insufficient for navigation purposes, while existing offline dense reconstruction methods requires tremendous computational power. A real-time monocular VINS dense mapping method will be a revolution for visual navigation in cluttered 3D environments. In this project, we will develop a unified framework to jointly solve robust estimation and dense mapping problems. We will develop a robust visual tracking method using direct, semi-dense, geometric image alignment, with subsequent optimization-based fusion of IMU measurements. Under this fusion framework, we will develop a method for dimensionality reduction of dense 3D range data to enable real-time dense 3D mapping. We will conduct online experiment in real-world environments for performance verification. 小型無人機在造價和移動性上的優勢使其成為航拍、監控、搜救等任務的一個理想平台。多數成功的商業無人機利用衛星導航系統進行位置估計和控制。由於這種對衛星導航系統的依賴，無人機的活動範圍被限制在開闊的室外空間。但真正可以發揮無人機的優勢的環境往往無法使用衛星導航系統，這些環境通常很危險，人類難以接近。 在地震、礦難、化學物質洩露等災難事件中，人們需要無人機在復雜和未知的環境中自主地導航飛行，並完成倖存者搜索和潛在危險探測等任務。為此，我們需要選擇在這種條件下能支持自主飛行的傳感器來取代衛星導航系統。 小型平台在復雜環境中更具靈活性，但它在尺寸、重量和能源方面受到的限制也更嚴格。隨著平台的尺寸縮小，由一個攝像頭和一個慣性測量單元組成的單目視覺-慣性導航系統就成為了唯一的傳感器選擇，因為這種傳感器套件重量非常輕，安裝非常簡便。事實上，這是可以同時滿足自主飛行和足夠的環境感知能力的最簡化傳感器配置。 單目視覺-慣性導航系統的主要挑戰有兩個：狀態估計（測算位置、速度、姿態等）和地圖構建（檢測障礙物）。由於缺乏可以直接測量距離的傳感器，需要融合視覺觀測和慣性觀測來獲得尺度信息。這種信息融合的必要條件是傳感器有充分的運動並同時保持穩定的視覺追踪。不幸的是，充分的運動和穩定的視覺追踪是矛盾的，這就要求狀態估計算法有很高的魯棒性。地圖構建問題的出發點是用稠密的場景重建來滿足避障的需求。目前最好的視覺-慣性導航系統使用的特徵點很稀疏，不能滿足導航的需求，而一些離線的稠密重建方法對計算資源的需求極高。對於在復雜的三維環境中的視覺導航，一個實時的單目的稠密建圖算法是一個革命性的進步。 在本項目中，我們將提出一個統一的框架，同時完成魯棒的狀態估計和稠密的地圖構建。我們將基於直接、半直接和幾何的圖像配准開發一個魯棒的視覺追踪系統，然後使用優化理論融合慣性測量。在這個信息融合的基礎上，我們將設計一種算法對三維數據進行降維，使得實時的稠密三維建圖成為可能。我們將在真實的環境中進行在線實驗以評價算法的性能。

26201616.label: Realisation of objectives
26201616.value: 1. We built a system on a customized quadrotor testbed equipped with a fisheye camera, a low-cost IMU, and heterogeneous onboard computing resources. The backbone of our system is a highly accurate optimization-based monocular visual-inertial state estimator with online initialization and self-extrinsic calibration. An onboard GPU-based monocular dense mapping module that conditions on the estimated pose provides wide-angle situational awareness. Finally, an online trajectory planner that operates directly on the incrementally built three dimensional map guarantees safe navigation through cluttered environments. Extensive experimental results are provided to validate individual system modules as well as the overall performance in both indoor and outdoor environments. The system-level contribution is the proof of the feasibility of using the minimum monocular VINS and fully onboard processing to achieve safe navigation through unknown cluttered environments. At the level of software modules, our contributions are embedded into the choice of suitable real-time algorithms that are either developed specifically for this work, or are improved from our previous works. 2. We presented VINS-Mono: a robust and versatile monocular visual-inertial state estimator. Our approach starts with a robust procedure for estimator initialization. A tightly coupled, nonlinear optimization-based method is used to obtain highly accurate visual-inertial odometry by fusing pre-integrated IMU measurements and feature observations. A loop detection module, in combination with our tightly coupled formulation, enables re-localization with minimum computation. We additionally perform 4-DOF pose graph optimization to enforce the global consistency. Furthermore, the proposed system can reuse a map by saving and loading it in an efficient way. The current and previous maps can be merged together by the global pose graph optimization. (Tong Qin, T-RO 2018) We proposed an online approach for calibrating temporal offset between visual and inertial measurements. Our approach achieves temporal offset calibration by jointly optimizing time offset, camera and IMU states, as well as feature locations in a SLAM system. Furthermore, the approach is a general model, which can be easily employed in several feature-based optimization frameworks. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the high accuracy of our calibration approach even compared with other state-of-art offline tools. The source code of temporal calibration is integrated into our public project “VINS-Mono” and received 2.6k “stars” on GitHub. 3. We proposed a novel dense surfel mapping system that scales well in different environments with only CPU computation. Using a sparse SLAM system to estimate camera poses, the proposed mapping system can fuse intensity images and depth images into a globally consistent model. The system is carefully designed so that it can build from room-scale environments to urban-scale environments using depth images from RGB-D cameras, stereo cameras or even a monocular camera. The main contributions of our mapping method are the following: 1) We use superpixels extracted from both intensity and depth images to model surfels in the system. Superpixels enable our method to fuse low-quality depth maps. Run-time efficiency and memory efficiency are also gained by using superpixel-based surfels. 2) We further organize surfels accordingly to the pose graph of the sparse SLAM systems. Using this organization, locally consistent maps are extracted for fusion, and the fusion time maintains O(1) regardless of the reconstruction scale. Fast map deformation is also proposed based on the optimized pose graph so that the system can achieve global consistency in real-time. 3) We implement the proposed dense mapping system using only CPU computation. We evaluate the method using public datasets and demonstrate its usability using autonomous aggressive flights. To the best of our knowledge, the proposed method is the first online depth fusion approach that achieves global consistency in urban-scale using only CPU computation.

26201616.label: Major findings and research outcome
26201616.value: We presented a complete system solution which is built on a customized quadrotor testbed equipped with a fisheye camera, a low-cost IMU, and heterogeneous onboard computing resources. The backbone of our system is a highly accurate optimization-based monocular visual-inertial state estimator with online initialization and self-extrinsic calibration. The system-level contribution is the proof of the feasibility of using the minimum monocular VINS and fully onboard processing to achieve safe navigation through unknown cluttered environments. At the level of software modules, our contributions are embedded into the choice of suitable real-time algorithms that are either developed specifically for this work, or are improved from our previous works. Moreover, we developed “VINS-Mono”, a robust and versatile monocular visual-inertial state estimator, which contains following features: 1) robust initialization procedure that is able to bootstrap the system from unknown initial states; 2) tightly coupled, optimization-based monocular VIO with camera–IMU extrinsic calibration and IMU bias correction; 3) online re-localization and four degrees-of-freedom (DOF) global pose graph optimization; 4) pose graph reuse that can save, load, and merge multiple local pose graphs. Among these features, robust initialization, re-localization, and pose graph reuse are our technical contributions. Engineering contributions include open-source system integration, real-time demonstration for drone navigation, and mobile applications.

26201616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26201616.value: Although feature-based VINS estimators have already reached the maturity of real-world deployment, we still see many directions for future research. Monocular VINS may reach weakly observable or even degenerate conditions depending on the motion and the environment. We are interested in online methods to evaluate the observability properties of monocular VINS, and online generation of motion plans to restore observability. Another research direction concerns the mass deployment of monocular VINS on a large variety of consumer devices, such as Android phones. This application requires online calibration of almost all sensor intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, as well as the online identification of calibration qualities. Finally, we are interested in producing dense maps given results from monocular VINS. Our first results on monocular visual inertial dense mapping with application to drone navigation was presented in paper Lin, Y, Gao, F, Qin, T, et al. Autonomous aerial navigation using monocular visual-inertial fusion. J Field Robotics. 2018; 35: 23- 51. However, extensive research is still necessary to further improve the system accuracy and robustness.

26201616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26201616.value: We presented VINS-Mono: a robust and versatile monocular visual-inertial state estimator for localization in a GPS-denied and unknown environment. Our approach starts with a robust procedure for estimator initialization. A tightly coupled, nonlinear optimization-based method is used to obtain highly accurate visual-inertial odometry by fusing pre-integrated IMU measurements and feature observations. A loop detection module, in combination with our tightly coupled formulation, enables re-localization with minimum computation. We additionally perform 4- DOF pose graph optimization to enforce the global consistency and further reduce the drift. Furthermore, the proposed system can reuse a pre-built map in an efficient way. The current and previous maps can be merged together online by the global pose graph optimization. We validate the performance of our system on public datasets and real-world experiments and compare against other state-of-the-art algorithms. We also perform an onboard closed loop autonomous flight on the micro aerial-vehicle platform and port the algorithm to an iOS-based for AR application. We highlight that the proposed work is a reliable, complete, and versatile system that is applicable for different applications that require high accuracy in localization. We open source our implementations for both PCs (https://github.com/HKUST-Aerial-Robotics/VINSMono) and iOSmobile devices (https://github.com/HKUST-Aerial-Robotics/VINS-Mobile).

26202016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26202016.value: Health care systems worldwide are facing the challenge of delivering high quality care with limited resources. As one of the most critical and expensive resources in a hospital, operating rooms (ORs) have received extensive attention in improving their service quality. One of the most important performance indicators is on-time start performance. In the US, only 27% of surgeries start on schedule, while in Hong Kong, 24% of surgeries are delayed by more than 60 minutes. The aim of this project is to re-evaluate the scheduling models in ORs based on real data to help enhance the service quality, specifically, improve on-time start performance. This project will focus primarily on the sequencing and scheduling problem when the surgery time is uncertain. In particular, given a group of surgeries within a day, how can a schedule be created to minimize the risk of tardiness? We begin with the case of a single OR, then extend to the scheduling problem in multiple ORs. We will first motivate a new performance measure based on convex risk measures for evaluating on-time start performance, instead of minimizing the expected costs of waiting time and overtime, as most literature does. If successful, this performance measure can control the tardiness probability at any delay level and help deliver a tractable model. Furthermore, with more than 1,000 types of surgeries and insufficient data points, it is unrealistic to fit each type with a probability distribution. We plan to use a distributionally robust optimization framework to describe the uncertain surgery durations by assuming that its true probability distribution belongs to an ambiguity set. This ambiguity set will be characterized by descriptive statistics estimated from real data and will also incorporate correlations between different types of surgeries. We will optimize the worst-case performance among all possible distributions to protect against data varation. After formulating a sequencing and scheduling model and developing its solution algorithms, we will explore several simple heuritics and implement them in practice to collect feedback. Assuming promising results, this project will not only enrich the current literature on scheduling and robust optimization, but also enhance patients’ experience and improve ORs’ efficiency. 全球医疗系统正面临着如何利用有限的资源提供高质量服务的挑战。手术室，作为医院里最关键而昂贵的资源之一，也吸引了很多学术界的关注。在如何提高其服务质量方面，其中一个最重要的性能指标是准时性。在美国，只有27％的手术准时开始，而在香港，24％的手术有超过60分钟的延迟。 此项目的目的是基于实际数据，重新评估手术室排程模型以提高服务质量，尤其是提高准时性。此项目将主要关注手术时间不确定下的排序和调度问题。给定固定时间内的一组手术，如何创建时间表以减少等待的风险。我们会先讨论单个手术室的排程问题，然后将其扩展至多个手术室。首先，我们会提出基于凸风险度量理论的新的绩效指标用于衡量手术开始的准时性。这个目标函数与大多数文献中等待时间和加班时间最小化的目标函数不同，可以帮助控制任何延迟时间的概率而且易解。此外，由于手术种类繁多，每类手术的数据点不足，我们不可能估计每类手术的手术时间的概率分布。我们计划使用分布式鲁棒性优化框架，通过假设其真正的概率分布属于一个模糊集来描述不确定的手术时间。我们可以通过真实的数据得到手术时间的描述性统计和不同类型手术时间的相关性来构造此模糊集。在此基础上，我们将优化所有可能分布的最坏情况以使得决策免受数据不确定性的影响。最后，我们会提出求解算法并探讨几种简单的启发式算法。 此项目不仅将丰富现有的调度和鲁棒优化的文献，也能够提升患者体验和提高手术室的工作效率。

26202016.label: Realisation of objectives
26202016.value: 1. To motivate a performance measure that can evaluate the risk of tardiness and also help develop a tractable model. The first objective is achieved. We have proposed a new performance measure named entropic tardiness index to evaluate the risk of tardiness. We motivate this index from several axioms, including monotonicity, on-time satisficing, delay intolerance, convexity and positive homogeneity and define this index based on the certainty equivalent of the exponential function. This index can capture the risk of delay and idle time and allow us to develop a tractable model. 2. To establish a distributionally robust optimization framework based on real data under the specific context of Operating Room (ORs) to help decisions immune against the data variation. The second objective is achieved. We have collected real data from the ORs ranging from January 3, 2012 to April 9, 2014. In total, 8 ORs are involved. We have analysed the distribution of start-time-delay of surgery and calculated the descriptive statistics about the surgery duration for each type of surgeries. The surgery duration varies significantly and most of them are right-skewed. To build a tractable model, we establish a distributionally robust optimization framework by considering two different distributional uncertainty set. The first one is based on descriptive statistics, including support, mean and mean absolute deviation. The second one is based on the empirical distribution and the Wasserstein distance. 3. To build a sequencing and scheduling model and develop efficient algorithms. The third objective is achieved. With the proposed performance measure and established distributional uncertainty set, we formulate a sequencing and scheduling model to solve the problem. We further reformulate the model as a mixed-integer optimization problem and adopt Benders decomposition to solve it. Given sequencing decisions, the problem can be solved in polynomial time. We further show that when the surgery duration follows the dilation order, the optimal sequencing decision can have closed-form solutions. 4. To provide simple sequencing and scheduling rules that can be implemented in real OR practice while improving ORs’ on-time start performance. The fourth objective is achieved. We develop simple heuristics to solve the problem and show that the heuristics perform quite well compared with the optimal solution in the numerical studies. We can implement the heuristic in practice without solving the complicated mathematical models.

26202016.label: Major findings and research outcome
26202016.value: In this project, we mainly study the OR scheduling problem to improve the efficiency of OR and service level for patients. In total, we have three main findings. 1. Empirical findings. From the analysis of real data, we have several findings that have not been discussed in the scheduling literature. First, we observe the “to follow” policy, in which surgeries are conducted immediately after another according to a scheduled sequence. Although widely implemented in many hospitals in various countries, this practice has been ignored and underrepresented in previous research, which assumes that the surgery cannot start before the scheduled starting time. Second, most of the surgery durations are right-skewed. We believe that these two findings are significant and should guide our model building. 2. Theoretical models. Incorporating these empirical findings, we have built optimization models to solve the scheduling problem. It is powerful for several reasons. First, we propose a new performance measure that balances the risk for both delays and idle time. This performance measure can further be utilised in other contexts to evaluate the risk. Second, the model can deliver robust solutions that can immune to uncertainties. Third, we develop algorithms to solve the problem efficiently, and the closed-form solutions are derived under certain special cases. We also propose simple heuristics for OR managers to implement in practice. Based on the above findings, we have finished one paper studying the OR scheduling problem (Research Output No. 1). The paper was initially submitted to the journal of Management Science, in which we got two referee reports. One is positive and one is negative. We are now revising the paper and submitting it to the journal of Manufacturing and Service Operations Management. This is also part of the PhD student’s thesis. 3. Further, inspired by this model, we found an attractive property in the scheduling model, namely the property of supermodularity. This concept is important in economics as it represents the substitution relationship. For this scheduling model, since the total duration is fixed, each surgery competes for the surgery time. Hence, supermodularity is embedded in the model. We utilize this grant to investigate more theoretical results on the supermodularity and write the second paper (Research output No. 2). This paper provides a systematic way to verify the property of supermodularity. It quickly received positive feedback from referees and published in Operations Research.

26202016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26202016.value: There are two directions for further development of this research. 1. Extension on multiple ORs. Our current model investigates the scheduling problem in a single OR. Whether we can extend this model to multiple ORs is a possible direction. However, we have to highlight that the scheduling problem is single OR is already a complex problem since it involves binary decisions. For the scheduling in multiple ORs, one possible way is to generalize our heuristics, and we can build an optimization to optimize the heuristics’ performance. The second possible way is to explore multiple valid inequalities to expedite the computation progress. 2. Extension on the dynamic setting. Another possible direction is to consider the dynamic scheduling problem. In reality, surgeries are booked in advance and their scheduled time may not be easily changed. With an unknown number of surgeries, how do we determine the scheduled starting time is a exciting but also a challenging question.

26202016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26202016.value: In this project, we consider how to sequence and schedule surgeries in Operating Rooms. The aim is to reduce the idle time of ORs and the delay of surgeries. We have several findings from the actual practice and data. First, many hospitals implement the “to follow” policy, in which surgeries are conducted immediately after another according to a scheduled sequence. Second, for most surgeries, there are a few surgeries that have much longer durations than the normal ones. Based on these two findings, we build an optimization model to decide the optimal sequence and scheduled starting time. Our solutions can balance the risk of delay and idle time and are robust when facing uncertain surgery durations. Further, the model can be solved efficiently and several simple heuristics are provided for the implementation in practice. With these heuristics, OR managers can make the sequence and scheduling decisions without complicated calculations. We further investigate an important property embedded in this scheduling problem, namely, supermodularity, which describes the relationship on substitution. We then develop theoretical results and a systematic way to verify this property.

26202116.label: Realisation of objectives
26202116.value: We have successfully developed and validated a flight performance analysis procedure that can simultaneously evaluate the fuel consumption (fuel burn) and landing and takeoff (LTO) noise of an aircraft. To achieve this objective, a flight mission analysis that can perform segment-by-segment analysis of aircraft operations (from take-off to landing). Here, a ‘segment’ is defined as a phase in a flight mission, i.e., take-off, accelerated climb, constant velocity climb, constant Mach climb, cruise (with step-climb procedures), constant Mach descent, constant velocity descent, decelerated descent, and landing. To analyze each flight, the procedure takes inputs pertaining to aircraft and engine performance, mission parameters, and atmospheric conditions. To make the flight performance analysis computationally tractable, surrogate models are built to approximate the aerodynamic and engine performances. The International Standard Atmosphere (ISA) is modeled to provide information on standard temperature, pressure, density, and speed of sound at any given altitude. Given a flight mission time and landing weight information, the flight performance analysis procedure can compute the corresponding fuel consumption for the flight by following an iterative procedure to solve the basic range equation. The equation is derived for each segment, to meet the relevant requirements and constraints for each segment. The noise modeling was primarily focused on the trailing-edge noise, which is considered a dominant source in aircraft operations. The direct Computational AeroAcoustics (CAA) methods are accurate yet difficult, because of the scale difference between the aerodynamics and aeroacoustics related phenomena. To reduce the computational cost, a hybrid method was selected, which was composed of three components: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), a semi-empirical wall-pressure fluctuation (WPF) spectrum model, and an acoustic propagation model. The Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equation was solved to simulate flow (as inputs to the WPF spectrum model) and yield aerodynamic coefficients. The Kamruzzaman’s model was chosen to predict the WPF spectrum. The propagation prediction followed the Howe’s method, which can calculate the far-field noise from WPF spectra under low-Mach-number flows with an observer position perpendicular above the trailing edge. We used the A-Weighted overall sound pressure level (OASPL) as the source noise metric. We validated this method using a NACA0012 airfoil case from the Benchmark Problems for Airframe Noise Computations (BANC) workshop, which showed a good agreement to the experimental measurement. Due to timing mismatch, we could not validate our optimization results by comparing them with wind tunnel experiment data as mentioned in the proposal. Instead, the flight mission analysis results were validated against actual flight data recorded by airlines. On the hindsight, this change in direction was a good decision, since we could validate our model against actual aircraft operations, which is more realistic and relevant compared to wind tunnel experiments. To offer a realistic flight performance analysis, we further developed a hybrid data-driven physics-based model, which mapped flight operational data to the aforementioned flight performance analysis. Through the developed mission parameterization process, nominal parameters were substituted by the extracted mission and speed profiles, i.e., fusing real flight operations into the physics-based analyses. There are two main sources of data used in this work: the radar-based flight data from the open source FlightRadar24 and the post flight information system (PFIS) data shared by our airline partner. PFIS also provides fuel burn information, i.e., total fuel consumption for the flight mission, which was used for validation purposes. The developed flight performance analysis procedure was demonstrated and validated with flights pertaining to three sectors flown by our airline partner, Hong Kong to New York (HKG-JFK), Hong Kong to Singapore (HKG-SIN), and Hong Kong to Taipei (HKG-TPE). The three selected sectors represented different types of flights, i.e., long-, medium-, and short-haul, respectively. Finally, we performed multiobjective optimizations to simultaneously minimize aircraft fuel consumption and noise. In this optimization, we considered shape variables as our design variables and included mission range and payload requirements as constraints. An airfoil parameterization approach was adopted to obtain the shape variables of the airfoil. We also used these shape variables as inputs of surrogate models to substitute the computationally expensive CFD and CAA analysis, thereby reducing the overall computational cost. We also employed the proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) based Class-Shape function transformation (CST) method, which could significantly reduce the number of input variables. The construction of the proposed parameterization could be divided into two steps. First, a CST parameterization was performed to identify the parameters in the mathematical expression, which could represent the target airfoil accurately. After setting the bounds of each variable, the design space could be determined. Then, the POD analysis was performed to find a set of ordered orthonormal basis vectors in a subspace and the order was determined based on the ability of the model to represent the generality of the predefined design space. Following the developed parameterization algorithm, we used eight geometry variables to represent the airfoil design in the optimization. The fuel burn objective function was evaluated directly from the flight performance analysis. We adopted the mini-max scheme to evaluate the noise objective function, to minimize the maximum noise during the takeoff, climb, descent, and landing phase (i.e., below 10000 ft). Three flight sectors (HKG-JFK, HKG-SIN, HKG-TPE) were selected to perform the optimization, represented by their most dominant scenario selected from data. Three surrogate models for lift coefficient, drag coefficient, and OASPL were built to run the mission analysis with root mean square errors less than 4%. The classic Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm, type II (NSGA-II) algorithm was selected to solve the multiobjective problem. The optimizations revealed that different optimum airfoils were obtained for different flight route scenarios. However, the results can generally be categorized into three groups, as will be described briefly below. The first category corresponds to optimization results that put more emphasis on fuel reduction. The cruise fuel consumption is dramatically reduced. However, in the low-Mach region, both lift and drag coefficients are smaller than the baseline airfoil, whereas the OASPL is comparable to that of the original airfoil. The second category corresponds to optimization results that put more emphasis on noise reduction. In the low-Mach-number region, lift coefficient increases while drag coefficient decreases. The corresponding AOA is smaller, which results in lower OASPL. Nevertheless, lift coefficient decreases and drag coefficient increases in the transonic region, which increases the cruise fuel consumption compared to the baseline case, especially in the long- and medium-haul flights. For short-haul flights, on the other hand, both fuel and noise can be reduced since the fuel consumption in the cruise phase becomes less dominat. The third category seeks to balance the fuel-noise minimization. Both lift and drag coefficients are bigger than those of the baseline airfoil in the low-Mach-number region, the lift-to-drag ratio is also higher, but the OASPL slightly lower. In contrast with the first category, the required AOA is smaller, which in turn reduces noise. In the transonic region, the trends of lift and drag coefficients are similar to those in the low-Mach-number region. With a higher lift-to-drag ratio, the fuel consumption in the cruise phase can also be decreased. Our results show that incorporating a detailed flight mission analysis into optimization formulation can reveal design trade-offs between fuel and noise minimizations under different scenarios. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to develop such an integrated approach.

26202116.label: Major findings and research outcome
26202116.value: We have developed a hybrid, data-driven flight performance analysis procedure that can simulate aircraft operation for more realistic analyses and optimization. The hybrid model combined the strength of data and detailed physics-based model to accurately estimate aircraft fuel consumption, given a set of flight mission parameters. The performance of the developed model was demonstrated in three cases (for short-, medium-, and long-haul flight sectors), which represented the variations of real-world aircraft operations. The fuel estimation accuracy was compared against actual airline data, with root mean square errors less than 3%. To assess the benefits of incorporating actual flight operational data in fuel burn estimation, we ran four scenarios with different levels of data integration. The first scenario was the nominal case, assuming that no flight information is available. The second scenario used PFIS data to characterize different flights. The wind effects were added in the third scenario, and in the final scenario, a fully parameterized mission profile was used in the analysis. The significant improvements in fuel burn estimation accuracy were evident as we added more features in the flight performance analysis procedure. The developed flight performance analysis procedure could address the limitation of most existing models that relied on simplifications of aircraft performance analyses with assumptions on nominal conditions. A journal article detailing these research outcomes is attached in this completion report. A noise prediction model has been added to the framework, which enables evaluating fuel burn and noise simultaneously. We focused on the trailing edge noise and used a hybrid method including CFD simulations and CAA models. The model was validated against existing literature with discrepancies less than 0.3 dB(A), which were deemed sufficient. Multiobjective optimizations to minimize fuel and noise have been performed under different flight scenarios. The optimization results revealed that incorporating detailed flight mission analysis, which could represent aircraft operations more realistically, could yield deeper insights into the design trade-offs between fuel and noise minimizations. Existing literatures are focused only on a fixed flight condition, typically during cruise, which cannot comprehensively analyze the trade-offs between different flight segments, e.g., cruise, climb, and descent. Integrating flight mission analysis and real operation data in the optimization formulation has been shown to make the optimization more realistic and practical, which would contribute to advancing aircraft design process towards a truly environmentally-friendly air transportation system. A journal article on the fuel-noise optimization is currently under preparation.

26202116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26202116.value: Using the developed flight performance analysis module, we can extract detailed flight-condition distributions that would not be possible by solely relying on pure data-based models, or on physics-based models with simplified mission representation. We will use the generated flight-condition distribution to derive new multipoint aerodynamic shape optimization (ASO) formulations to minimize the expected value of drag of a transport aircraft by adopting a numerical quadrature approach (GRF Project 16210621, 2022-2024). We will also extend the simultaneous fuel and noise minimization problem to optimize flight trajectories during departures. The conference paper on this preliminary work is attached in this report. In the current formulation, we use a high-fidelity model to estimate fuel burn, while only relying on semi empirical models for the noise estimation. We will enhance the noise modeling by collaborating with a colleague with research expertise in aeroacoustics. We have had several discussions on this new research direction and will pursue it soon to obtain preliminary results and seek funding. We believe that incorporating a data-enhanced flight simulation module in aircraft design optimization framework can establish a more systematic link between aircraft design and air transportation, to optimize next-generation aircraft design and operations.

26202116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26202116.value: Environmental considerations, especially in terms of fuel consumption, emission, and noise, have gained importance in designing aircraft and the operation. In this research, we develop an integrated framework that can be used to design low-noise and low-emission aircraft by performing an optimization. The framework is realized by integrating a noise prediction model into a detailed mission analysis procedure, which can efficiently emulate aircraft operation from take-off to landing and compute the flight-mission range, time, and fuel burn. To use this framework in optimization and ensure that it is computationally tractable, surrogate models are built to approximate the aerodynamic performance and noise metrics of the aircraft, thus eliminating the needs to perform the computationally expensive computational fluid dynamics and aeroacoustics simulations. Incorporating a detailed flight simulation in the optimization framework enables considering a wide range of flight conditions that can represent realistic aircraft operations and therefore minimize reliance on simplified nominal-condition assumptions, which is a drawback of existing formulations. By coupling the developed flight simulation module with a multiobjective optimization algorithm, we can simultaneously minimize fuel burn and noise of the aircraft operation. Lastly, designing environmentally-friendly aircraft will support global efforts to achieve sustainable aviation, benefitting society as a whole.

26300316.label: Project Objectives
26300316.value: Calculate quasi-single field (QSF) inflation in the case where the massive direction is strongly coupled to density fluctuations. For the impact of the massive field to be observable, the fluctuation in the massive field needs to be converted to the density fluctuations, through mixing terms between the two. The size of such mixing is model dependent and may be large. For large mixing, the current calculation technique is not applicable, and the corrections require a resummation. Explicitly calculate QSF with massive loops. The majority of the currently known particles carries gauge charges. If the massive field carries a gauge charge that the inflaton does not carry, then the massive field has to appear in loops. Moreover, if the massive field is Fermionic, it also has to appear in loops in order to continue the Fermion line. This project extends the interaction, spin and interaction spectra of QSF. Calculate and classify the amplitude of the clock signal in different models of the quantum primordial standard clock (QPSC). Although the shape of the clock signal in QPSC is model independent, the amplitude depends on models. Calculate the signals of the QPSC in explicit models of alternative-to-inflation. The PI and the collaborators have shown that in a wide spectra of alternative-to-inflation scenarios, the shape of the massive oscillatory non-Gaussianity appears in a model independent way. However, the amplitude of the non-Gaussianity, together with some model dependent details, are not yet understood. Understanding those details helps greatly in relating the predictions of alternative-to-inflation models to observational data. Construct the shape templates of the non-Gaussianity from QPSC, to simplify future data analysis. Performing data analysis of non-Gaussianities is computationally highly intensive. Simplified shape templates help to reduce the required computational power. Summarize helpful analytical and numerical techniques of the cosmological in-in formalism. We have developed a lot of technical improvements for the calculation of the in-in formalism, including techniques for exact analytical calculation, approximation schemes and improvements on numerical calculation. Some of those techniques are mentioned in publications as technical details (often in appendices) and some remains unpublished. To summarize those techniques is helpful for lowering the barrier for novice to enter this research field and pushing forward the research program.
