27100416.value: 骨質疏鬆症是一個多因素疾病, 而代謝途徑是其中一個會影響其發病機制的重要因素。在TwinsUK研究的初步數據中, 我們發現有四個血清代謝物是會影響到骨密度, 它們包括prolyl-hydroxy-proline, epiandrosterone sulphate, 4-androsten-3β,17β-diol disulphate, 及 pipecolic acid。由於不同人群有著不同生活習慣及基因背景, 因此血清代謝物在不同人群中對骨密度之影響亦有機會會有所不同。另外, 由於骨密度及代謝途徑同樣是受到基因的影響, 究竟在不同骨密度的人群中, 基因對代謝途徑的調控是否會有所不同呢? 在這個研究中, 我們將會研究不同人群中的血清代謝組之分別; 了解在南方中國人中有那些血清代謝物會與骨密度有關聯; 與及研究在不同骨密度的人群中 基因對代謝途徑的調控的分別。 總括而言，我們的研究將有機會發現骨質疏鬆症的代謝標誌物，並增加我們對遺傳變異，代謝物，和骨質疏鬆症之間的關係和理解。

27100416.label: Realisation of objectives
27100416.value: Summary: In this project, we have completed all the objectives stated. In general, we generated four publications in this ECS grant. In brief, we profiled circulating metabolome in 624 unrelated participants from Hong Kong Osteoporosis Study (HKOS) baseline study (cohort 1) and follow-up study (cohort 2) and evaluated its relationship with bone mineral density (BMD) in Hong Kong Chinese. In addition to single metabolite analysis, we also adopted pathway analysis to see if a particular metabolic pathway was enriched in the association. To improve the robustness of the findings, all results were either replicated “internally” (e.g., analysed HKOS cohorts 1 and 2 separately) or “externally” (e.g., TwinsUK used as the discovery cohort, and HKOS used as the replication cohort). Among four studies, two studies collaborated with international institutes, namely King’s College London (TwinsUK) and Harvard Medical School (Framingham Osteoporosis Study). Collaboration with Caucasian cohorts allowed us to compare the association and evaluate the generalisability of the findings in Caucasians and Chinese. Given that cross-sectional study cannot infer causality, we used Mendelian Randomization (MR) approach to evaluate the casual association. In MR analysis, we first need to identify the genetic instrument of the metabolites by conducting genome-wide association study. Those genetic variants showing genome-wide significant association with metabolites will be used as the genetic instruments. Using 1-sample (in Study 1) and 2-sample MR analyses, we showed that genetic instruments affecting circulating metabolites were also significantly associated with BMD, and therefore causal associations were also established. The clinical outcome of osteoporosis is fragility fracture. It is important to evaluate if circulating metabolites are associated with or predictive of fracture risk. Thus, we assessed whether BMD-associated metabolites were predictive of fracture. Using cox-regression, we observed that the selected metabolites were significantly associated with fracture. Most importantly, adding the selected metabolites to the model consisting of conventional risk factors could further improve the accuracy of predicting fracture risk. These findings highlighted the clinical importance of the role of circulating metabolites in osteoporosis. Osteoporosis is a multi-factorial disease, we also evaluated the relationship of circulating metabolome with bone-related factors, including vitamin D and coffee intake. We, for the first time, delineated the relationship of circulating metabolome with vitamin D and habitual coffee intake in Chinese. A brief discussion of results in each publication generated from the ECS grant: Study 1: Metabolomic Pathways to Osteoporosis in Middle-Aged Women: A Genome-Metabolome-Wide Mendelian Randomization Study (JBMR) In 2018, we reported the first large-scale metabolomic study of bone mineral density (BMD) using the metabolomic data from the TwinsUK and the Hong Kong Osteoporosis Study (HKOS). We first showed that metabolites belonging to the pathway of adrenal-secreted sulfated steroids were significantly associated with BMD in both UK and HK cohorts (see Table 1). Given that cross-sectional observation cannot infer causality, we next investigated the causality of these metabolites with BMD using the MR approach. We first reported that metabolites belonging to the adrenal-secreted sulfated steroids were casually associated with BMD. The findings were published in JBMR, the top-ranked journal in the bone field. Study 2: Serum metabolomic profiling and its association with 25-hydroxyvitamin D (Clinical Nutrition) Knowing that calcium metabolism plays an important role in BMD determination, we next evaluated the metabolomics of vitamin D in Chinese for the first time. Using the analytical approach mentioned earlier, we showed that 13 metabolites were significantly associated with 25(OH)D after correction for multiple testing (Table 2). The majority of metabolites identified were lipid in nature. Docosahexaenoylcarnitine and eicosapentaenoylcholine showed the strongest associations, with effect estimates of 0.2554 and 0.1682 per 1 SD increase in metabolite, respectively. These findings indicate that there may be a close relationship between circulating vitamin D and lipid metabolism. This study was published in the top-tier journal in nutrition – Clinical Nutrition. Study 3: Serum Metabolome of Coffee Consumption and its Association With Bone Mineral Density: The Hong Kong Osteoporosis Study (JCEM) Caffeine has long been known to play a role in calcium metabolism. Coffee is a widely consumed caffeine-rich beverage, which was previously shown to affect bone metabolism adversely. Given that coffee contains caffeine and other bioactive molecules. Thus, we aimed to evaluate the metabolomics of coffee and its association with BMD. Using the same analytical approach mentioned earlier, we showed that 12 metabolites were significantly associated with habitual coffee intake (Table 3). The most associated metabolite is quinate, which is a known chemical implicated in the perceived acidity of coffee. This finding highlights the validity of the food frequency questionnaire and the metabolomic platform. In addition, we also showed that habitual coffee intake was significantly associated with higher BMD in Hong Kong Chinese, while coffee-associated metabolites, 5-Acetylamino-6-Formylamino-3-Methyluracil, Trigonelline, and 3-hydroxyhippurate, were found to be positively associated with BMD. This study identified metabolites representing coffee intake, while some may explain the positive association between coffee intake and BMD. This study was published in the top-tier journal in endocrinology – JCEM. Study 4: Metabolomics Insights into Osteoporosis Through Association With Bone Mineral Density (JBMR) In this study, we collaborated with the Framingham Osteoporosis Study (FOS) to evaluate the relationship of circulating metabolome with BMD and fracture. In general, 27 metabolites identified in the FOS were successfully replicated in the HKOS. Three metabolites further showed causal associations with BMD in the MR analysis. In addition, we showed that these 27 metabolites could further increase the prediction and reclassification of the risk of hip fracture in participants from the FOS and HKOS (Table 4). These studies showed that circulating metabolites could potentially predict fracture that is incremental to conventional risk factors. This study was published in the top-ranked journal in the bone field – JBMR. Future study: As demonstrated in the last annual report, we also conducted our metabolomic study of BMD in Chinese and identified KMV as a causal factor affecting bone metabolism. Since metabolite could be developed as a nutritional supplement for improving bone health, we evaluated the functional role of KMV in bone metabolism and found that it is an inhibitor of osteoclastogenesis using cell and animal studies. Upon further evaluation, we aim to conduct a clinical trial in humans to see if KMV supplementation could improve bone mass in humans.

27100416.label: Major findings and research outcome
27100416.value: Study 1. We first showed that metabolites belonging to the adrenal-secreted sulfated steroids were cross-sectionally and causally associated with BMD in both Caucasians (TwinsUK) and Chinese (HKOS). These included androsterone sulfate, epiandrosterone sulfate, 5alpha-androstan-3beta17beta-diol disulfate, and 4-androsten-3beta17beta-diol disulfate. Given that supplementation of DHEA, a member belonging to adrenal-secreted sulfated steroids was shown to increase bone mass in humans in a clinical trial, our findings highlighted the importance of metabolomic research in the discovery of novel nutritional supplements in improving chronic diseases, including osteoporosis. This study has been published in the JBMR (IF: 6.74) Study 2. Among 835 known metabolites, 102 metabolites showed significant correlation with 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25[OH]D) levels at baseline visit. Of these metabolites, 27 were validated in the follow-up visit. In meta-analysis of data from these two visits, 13 metabolites were highly correlated with 25(OH)D. The majority of metabolites identified were lipid in nature. Docosahexaenoylcarnitine and eicosapentaenoylcholine had the highest correlations. Our study demonstrated the close relationship of lipid metabolism with 25(OH)D. Given that vitamin D has not only been implicated in bone metabolism but also in other diseases, whether lipids mediate in such a relationship requires further studies. This study has been published in Clinical Nutrition (IF: 7.32). Study 3. We identified 12 serum metabolites positively correlating with coffee consumption after correction for multiple testing, with quinate, 3-hydroxypyridine sulfate, and trigonelline (N’-methylnicotinate) showing the strongest association. Among these metabolites, 11 known metabolites were previously identified to be associated with coffee intake and 6 of them were related to caffeine metabolism. Habitual coffee intake was positively and significantly associated with BMD. The metabolite 5-acetylamino-6-formylamino-3-methyluracil, 3-hydroxyhippurate, and trigonelline were significantly associated with BMD. This study has been published in JCEM (IF:5.96). Study 4. We identified 27 metabolites associated with FN-BMD or LS-BMD by LASSO regression with internal validation. Incorporating selected metabolites significantly improved the prediction and the classification of osteoporotic fracture risk beyond conventional risk factors. We replicated significant improvement in fracture prediction by incorporating selected metabolites in 634 participants from the HKOS. The glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism pathway was significantly enriched. Furthermore, three causally related metabolites (glycine, phosphatidylcholine [PC], and triacylglycerol [TAG]) were negatively associated with FNBMD, whereas PC and TAG were negatively associated with LS-BMD through MR analysis. In summary, metabolites associated with BMD are helpful in osteoporotic fracture risk prediction. Our findings may provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of osteoporosis.

27100416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27100416.value: As mentioned above, findings from metabolomic study could provide insight into the causal association, develop a risk score in predicting fracture, and develop a nutritional supplement for improving bone mass. We conducted our metabolomic study of BMD in Chinese and identified KMV as a causal factor affecting bone metabolism. Since metabolite could be developed as a nutritional supplement for improving bone health, we evaluated the functional role of KMV in bone metabolism and found that it is an inhibitor of osteoclastogenesis using cell and animal studies. Upon further evaluation, we aim to conduct a clinical trial in humans to see if KMV supplementation could improve bone mass in humans. This may lead to the identification of a novel nutritional supplement for osteoporosis, in addition to calcium and vitamin D supplements.

27100416.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27100416.value: Metabolomics is a systematic study of a large number of small molecules called metabolites. In this grant, we evaluated the relationship of circulating metabolites with osteoporosis. We identified a number of metabolites showing cross-sectional and causal associations with bone mass in humans. Some further showed a potential role in predicting fracture risk. Knowing that control of bone mass is multifactorial, we also studied two bone mass-related traits, namely serum vitamin D and habitual coffee intake. Our study further delineated the relationship of circulating metabolites with these traits. In short, we demonstrated the important role of circulating metabolites in bone mass determination, either directly or indirectly. We also showed that circulating metabolites could be exploited as a biomarker in predicting fracture risk.

27100816.label: Project Objectives
27100816.value: To characterize the metabolic activities of PIKE-A in muscle cells. PIKE-A is a novel regulator of energy homeostasis. However, the functional detail of PIKE-A-mediated metabolic changes is unknown. Therefore, we will measure the cellular fatty acid oxidation and AMPK kinase activity in PIKE-A overexpressed or depleted C2C12 myotubes. Moreover, we will test if PIKE-A blocks upstream kinase-induced AMPK phosphorylation. Results obtained will provide the molecular details of PIKE-A-initiated metabolic change. To identify the metabolic factors that regulate PIKE-A/AMPK association. PIKE-A interacts with AMPK in obese muscles, yet the hormonal signals or intracellular events that govern the protein complex formation remain unexplored. To address this issue, we will examine the effect of TNFα on PIKE-A/AMPK interaction in C2C12 cells. We will also determine if the presence of PIKE-A is critical for TNFα-provoked AMPK inhibition in cultured myotubes. These data will provide a new mechanistic insight on obesity-induced PIKE-A/AMPK association. To study the impacts of PIKE-A/AMPK dissociation on energy metabolism. We will use muscle-specific PIKE knockout (MPKO) mice as the in vivo model to assess the role PIKE-A/AMPK complex in systemic glucose and energy metabolisms. Physiological parameters including growth rate, body composition, blood biochemistry, insulin sensitivity, lipid oxidation and energy expenditure profiles of high-fat-diet-fed Flox/Flox and MPKO mice will be studied.

27100816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27100816.value: 雖然肥胖症與各種組織中的葡萄糖與脂肪利用率受損有密切關係，但引致這個問題的分子機制卻糢糊不清。其中的例子包括肥胖肌肉中的脂肪酸因受到未知原因影響而不能全面氧化。我們之前已報導過磷酸肌醇激酶強化蛋白A（PIKE-A）是一種末受重視的肝臓葡萄糖代謝調控蛋白。 我們在組織特定基因剔除小鼠的前期研究中更發現如將PIKE基因於肌肉剔除會提高腺苷酸活化蛋白激酶（AMPK）的活性，從而保護這些小鼠免於患上因過度進食而引致的肥胖症與糖尿病。我們亦發現PIKE-A 與AMPK有物理性的接觸。此相互作用並會在肥胖肌肉或有高脂肪含量的肌肉細胞中有所增加。因此，PIKA-A與AMPK或代表了一種聯繫細胞中脂肪含量，能量代謝與發展肥胖症的新訊號通路。我門的長期研究目標是要找出肥胖症的致病分子機制。作為其中的一部份，我們提議研究PIKE-A與AMPK於肥胖症引起的脂肪酸氧化下調中的作用。在此研究計劃中，我們將會（1）找出PIKE-A的代謝功能；（2）找出導致PIKE-A與AMPK接觸的代謝訊號；（3）用肌肉特定基因剔除小鼠去研究阻止PIKE-A 與AMPK接觸的代謝後果。總括而言，此項研究會找出一個新的能量代謝調節蛋白，並提供一個可解釋為何肥胖會引致脂肪與葡萄糖代謝失衡的機制。這些發現對發展新的肥胖症及其拼發症治療方法有重要的意義。

27100816.label: Realisation of objectives
27100816.value: In this project, we hypothesized that obesity provokes the interaction of PIKE-A GTPase and AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) in the skeletal muscle. Formation of the PIKE-A/AMPK complex hinders AMPK phosphorylation. Thus, the kinase activities of AMPK are disrupted, leading to insulin resistance, diminished lipid oxidation and reduced energy expenditure. To test this hypothesis, we have performed a variety of molecular, biochemical and cellular assays in cultured muscle cells. Moreover, the physiological parameters, energy and glucose homeostasis, and signaling mechanism were examined in mice. Specific assays done are listed below: We have characterized the metabolic activities of PIKE-A in muscle cells (Specific Aim 1). Using C2C12 myotubes that overexpressed or depleted PIKE-A as the study model, we have assessed the enzymatic activities of AMPK using immunoblotting and ELISA; measured the mitochondrial respiration and lipid oxidation using extracellular flux analysis, and determine the inhibitory mechanism of PIKE-A on AMPK activities using a combination of immunoblotting and enzymatic activity measurements. In order to identify the regulatory factors that control PIKE-A/AMPK interaction (Specific Aim 2), we have tested the effect of fatty acids (palmitic acid and oleic acid) and metabolic hormones [tumor necrosis factor α (TNFα), insulin and irisin] on endogenous PIKA-A and AMPK association in C2C12 myotubes. Signaling cascades induced by these challenges have also been examined by immunoblotting and real-time PCR. Moreover, the effect of chow diet or high fat diet (HFD) feeding and TNFα infusion on their interaction in mouse muscle have also been determined. Lastly, we have studied the impacts of PIKE-A/AMPK dissociation on energy metabolisms using our home-made muscle-specific PIKE knockout (MPKO) mice. Body composition, tissue weights, blood glucose and lipids [triacylglycerides, (TG), free fatty acid (FFA), and cholesterol], various hormones (leptin, insulin and TNFα), tissue metabolites (TG, FFA, cholesterol, and glycogen) were measured in chow diet- or HFD-fed Fl/Fl and MBKO mice. Systemic energy metabolism including O2 consumption, CO2 production, energy expenditure, food intake, water uptake, locomotion and lipid oxidation were also determined using indirect calorimetry and immunoblotting. We have measured the insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism in MBKO mice using hyperinsulinic-euglycemic clamp and immunoblotting. In summary, we have performed a large number of assays that fully addressed all Specific Aims set in the proposal.

27100816.label: Major findings and research outcome
27100816.value: In this project, we proved that PIKE-A is a novel effector of TNFα to facilitate its metabolic modulation in the skeletal muscle. Depletion of PIKE-A in C2C12 myotubes diminished the inhibitory activities of TNFα on mitochondrial respiration and lipid oxidation, whereas PIKE-A overexpression exacerbated these cellular responses. We also found that TNFα promoted the interaction between PIKE-A and AMPK to suppress its kinase activity cultured muscle cells and in C57BL/6 mice. Mechanistically, PIKE-A interaction prevented the phosphorylation of AMPK by its upstream activator LKB1. As a result, animals with PIKE ablation in the skeletal muscle displayed an upregulation of AMPK phosphorylation and a higher preference to utilize lipid as the energy production substrate under HFD feeding, which mitigated the development of diet-induced hyperlipidemia, ectopic lipid accumulation, and muscle insulin resistance. Hence, our data reveal PIKE-A as a new signaling factor that is important for TNFα-initiated metabolic changes in skeletal muscle. During the search of metabolic regulators that control PIKE-A/AMPK interaction, we found that irisin was able to suppress PIKE-A/AMPK interaction. Moreover, irisin stimulation could promote lipid oxidation in skeletal muscle, which fits with the functional outcome of PIK-A/AMPK association. The results of these data were reported in two international journals in “Diabetes” (2017) and “Cellular Physiology and Biochemistry” (2018). Moreover, the projects have provided training opportunities to one PhD candidate and 4 undergraduate students at the University of Hong Kong.

27100816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27100816.value: We found in this project that PIKE-A is a novel regulator of AMPK, and that PIKE-A/AMPK interaction is important to regulate lipid oxidation and cellular respiration in skeletal muscle of obese mice. Since AMPK is a multifunctional kinase, the identification of PIKE-A/AMPK interaction and its functional significance might provide insight on the dysregulation of AMPK activity in other diseases in addition to obesity. Indeed, data generated in this project have inspired our collaborator to initiate a study of PIKE-A/AMPK interaction in glioblastoma proliferation, which has published the results in 2019 (Zhang et al Cell Death Dis 2019 10: 222). Hence our findings provide a solid foundation to further study the functional outcomes of PIKE-A/AMPK interaction in physiological (e.g. appetite control, cell differentiation) and pathological (e.g. cancer progression) conditions.

27100816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27100816.value: Obesity is the major risk factor of type 2 diabetes but the underlying mechanism is not well-understood. In this project, we identified the role of a protein called phosphoinositide 3-kianse enhancer A (PIKE-A) that links obesity and insulin resistance in skeletal muscle. Using a variety of experimental methods including cell culture assay, gene expression measurement, biochemical analysis, and knockout mice phenotyping, we demonstrated that PIKE-A is a new inhibitor of insulin signaling via blocking the activity of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) in response to the high inflammatory cytokine levels of obese subjects. This finding has profound implications in designing new therapeutic strategies against obesity and its-related disorders.

27102316.label: Realisation of objectives
27102316.value: During neuronal development, nerve growth cones of axons use actin-based motility to extend and navigate to their specific targets for brain wiring. Dynamic assembly and disassembly of actin filaments (F-actin) from monomeric globular actin (G-actin) generate actin-based protrusions that, coupled with selective adhesion, steer and drive the growth cone forward. The peripheral domain of growth cones is highly enriched in actin and contains the hallmark membrane protrusions in lamellipodia and filopodia made up of distinct actin filamentous structures. The dynamic regulation of these actin-based structures is believed to play a crucial role in how the growth cones respond to the gradients of extracellular diffusible guidance molecules. The responses could be turning towards or away from the source of guidance molecules, and promoting or inhibiting neuronal outgrowth. While the signalling mechanisms underlying distinct guidance molecules are different, it is conceivable that the actin cytoskeleton serves as a convergent target of different intracellular signalling pathways in translating into growth cone turning responses. Over the last few decades, significant progress has been made to understand the regulation of F-actin assembly and treadmilling by a wide range of signalling cascades and accessory molecules. However, very little is known about the role of G-actin, the building blocks of F-actin, in spatiotemporally regulated actin dynamics underlying growth cone motility during neuronal outgrowth and axonal guidance. In this ECS grant project, we have explored the molecular regulation of actin dynamics in neuronal motility and gained a better understanding of the spatiotemporal localization of F-actin and G-actin with ADF/cofilin and profilin in growth cone motility and guidance. Through the overexpression of Xenopus ADF/cofilin (XAC) in Xenopus embryos via microinjection, our findings showed that ADF/cofilin is highly enriched throughout the growth cone during neuronal motility. While the wild-type form of ADF/cofilin was localized mainly at the central region of the growth cones, however, it was intriguing to observe that both active and inactive mutants of ADF/cofilin were in abundance at the peripheral regions, suggesting the spatial depolymerization of F-actin by ADF/cofilin at the peripheral regions of growth cones. Overexpression of ADF/cofilin and active ADF/cofilin resulted in a slight increase in growth cone motility. However, inactive ADF/cofilin did not cause any effects, suggesting that the endogenous amount of ADF/cofilin proteins is sufficient in the regulation of actin dynamics in growth cones. On the other hand, molecular manipulation to the endogenous expression level of profilin, an actin-sequestering protein, by anti-sense morpholino caused a significant reduction in G-actin localization at the leading edges of growth cones, which was associated with reduced neuronal outgrowth. Finally, in the neurite severing assay, our data indicated that the ability of axonal regeneration is influenced by dynamic actin turnover at the sites of neurite lesions. Cultured neurons of ADF/cofilin mutants and profilin knockdown exhibited a reduced rate of neurite extension after severing. These findings indicate a promising approach to promote axonal regeneration by tightly controlled actin dynamics in severed neurons. In addition, we have made another important observation related to this project that the transition from axonal outgrowth to synaptogenesis is mediated by neuronal membrane-type 1 matrix metalloproteinase (MT1-MMP) activity. Firstly, we showed that agrin deposition along the neurites can be strongly detected in 1- or 2-day-old Xenopus spinal neuron cultures, but not in young cultures at which the neuronal outgrowth phase is dominant. MMP-mediated extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation allows the spatial deposition of agrin along the neurites. We further demonstrated that the application of polystyrene beads coated with recombinant neural agrin proteins focally induces presynaptic differentiation in cultured spinal neurons, as reflected by clustering a panel of different presynaptic markers, through Lrp4-dependent mechanisms. Next, we identified that endogenous MT1-MMP is required for ECM degradation along the neurites and agrin bead-induced presynaptic differentiation. Time-lapse imaging further showed the dynamic axonal transport of MT1-MMP vesicles, followed by the local capture and surface delivery of vesicular MT1-MMP proteins at the agrin bead-contacted sites. Finally, we further showed that MT1-MMP mRNA is spatially enriched and locally translated at sites induced by agrin beads. In summary, this study has identified a previously unappreciated role of agrin in presynaptic differentiation and a novel role of axonal MT1-MMP mRNA translation and its spatially localized MT1-MMP proteins in regulating agrin deposition and signaling.

27102316.label: Major findings and research outcome
27102316.value: In this project, we have started by proving that the modulation of actin dynamics by ADF/cofilin activity and profilin expression are tightly correlated to the axonal outgrowth in cultured Xenopus spinal neurons. Next, we established the neurite severing assay and identified the ability of axonal regeneration is influenced by dynamic actin turnover at the sites of neurite lesions as cultured neurons of ADF/cofilin mutants and profilin knockdown exhibited a reduced rate of neurite extension after severing. Importantly, these observations led to an unexpected discovery of the intrinsic transition from axonal outgrowth to synaptogenesis via the expression of neuronal MT1-MMP (Oentaryo et al., J. Cell. Sci. 2020). In cultured Xenopus spinal neurons, agrin is secreted along the neurites of mature neurons but is absent during their outgrowth phase; this deposition correlates with an increase in MT1-MMP-mediated ECM degradation. Through the local application of agrin-coated beads along the neurites, we were able to induce presynaptic differentiation, as confirmed by the accumulation of different presynaptic markers. Agrin-induced presynaptic differentiation was found to be dependent on the neuronal expression of its receptor, the low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 4 (Lrp4) and MT1-MMP. The latter is responsible for not only promoting agrin deposition by modulating ECM remodelling, but also activating agrin signalling by mediating the necessary proteolytic cleavage of Lrp4. Together, this study identified a new role for agrin in early synaptogenesis, as well as a regulatory function for MT1-MMP in presynaptic differentiation. Interestingly, we also showed that axonal MT1-MMP translation, on top of the well-recognized long-range transport of MT1-MMP proteins synthesized from neuronal cell bodies, is required in mediating agrin-induced presynaptic differentiation (Yu et al., Development 2021).

27102316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27102316.value: Based on our recently published work demonstrating the local translation of mRNA in agrin-induced presynaptic development (Yu et al., Development 2021), it would be of interest to further investigate how the local protein synthesis of MT1-MMP and other presynaptic proteins are regulated along the axons in growing and severed axons. Specifically, as N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification has recently been recognized as one of the post-transcriptional regulatory markers in different types of RNAs. We plan to test if m6A modification is involved to regulate the stability of MT1-MMP mRNA at the presynaptic nerve terminal. If so, we will further investigate the regulation of m6A mRNA modification by its writer, eraser, and reader proteins in axonal growth and presynaptic development. Pilot experiments will be carried out to collect preliminary data for our future GRF or HMRF grant application.

27102316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27102316.value: The ability of cells to sense the environment and to move in a defined direction is fundamental not only for embryonic development but also for a wide range of physiological and pathological events. In brain development, directed neuronal migration sets up the laminar layers for the ordered brain architecture and guided extension by the motile growth cones. Both cell locomotion and growth cone migration utilize a shared mechanism that drives membrane protrusions. The actin cytoskeleton is believed to be the major target of different intracellular signaling pathways that leads to specific motile behaviors of the growth cone. The actin cytoskeleton is targeted by many signaling cascades and a complex network of actin accessory molecules are known to act on distinct aspects of filament assembly, disassembly, and their organization into distinct networks. In this project, we have elucidated the precise mechanisms underlying ADF/cofilin-regulated actin dynamics in cell motility and neuronal outgrowth. Additionally, we have demonstrated the dynamic remodelling of extracellular matrix proteins by actin-rich invadopodium-associated membrane-type 1 matrix metalloproteinase in the transition of neuronal outgrowth to synaptogenesis. Our project outcomes have provided a better understanding on how actin dynamics are spatiotemporally regulated to drive directed cell movements during development and diseases.

27103616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27103616.value: 癌細胞藉著基因組異常所驅動之失調信號通路得以持續增殖和/或存活。靶向治療藥物能阻斷通路而引致細胞死亡, 這亦是靶向治療的基礎。靶向治療可以改善抗腫瘤效力，同時亦降低引起的副作用。癌基因異常對下游信號傳導通路的影響能改變對藥物的反應。這些異常亦可作為患者分層的標記。透過患者基因組圖譜整合所作出的治療決策已取得實在的臨床效果。 PIK3R1基因編碼出 PI3K通路裡的p85α調節亞基。 於各腫瘤類型中，PIK3R1是第十二最常發生變異的基因。本人及其他新近的研究表明了小規模PIK3R1突變對信號通路激活和靶向治療敏感性的作用。除了參與典型的PI3K通路，部份PIK3R1的突變能意外激活其他信號如MAPK通路。這些發現強調著功能上註釋個別的靶基因變異的重要性，以便鑑定出正確的治療及避免錯配的治療策略。 除了小規模的突變，大規模PIK3R1基因拷貝數減少於各類型腫瘤中亦很常見。以卵巢癌為例，純合性缺失佔3.3%，而異質性缺失則佔70.14%。卵巢癌是最致命的婦科惡性腫瘤。大部份卵巢癌患者因對一般化療呈抗藥性而嚴重地限制了治療成果。為了提高患者的存活率，嶄新療法的研究是極其重要。基於患者的高頻PIK3R1基因拷貝數減少，以及我們的初步數據，我們假設PIK3R1基因拷貝數減少和所引起的p85α表達下降促進卵巢癌的形成及其所驅動的信號能調控癌細胞對治療藥物的敏感度。是項提案目標旨在解開卵巢癌中PIK3R1基因拷貝數減少引起的功能後果及其對治療的影響。具體來講，此項研究會通過癌症組學，細胞生物學和癌症治療的綜合分析，去解開PIK3R1基因拷貝數減少在卵巢癌中對腫瘤形成，下游信號及藥物敏感度之影響。事實上，PIK3R1基因拷貝數減少的功能表徵尚未於任何類型的腫瘤中得以探索。研究結果將會為帶有PIK3R1基因拷貝數減少的卵巢癌甚或其他類型的癌病患者的治療策略發展帶來積極顯著的影響。

27103616.label: Realisation of objectives
27103616.value: Objective 1: to examine the biological phenotypes as a consequence of PIK3R1 copy number loss. PIK3R1 deletion enhances a spectrum of tumorigenic hallmarks. To evaluate the functional role of PIK3R1 deletion, classical in vitro and in vivo functional assays were conducted. Compared with wild-type cells, PIK3R1 depletion markedly promoted cell proliferation of ovarian cancer cell lines. Similar results were captured with PIK3R1 shRNA-expressing stable cells in colony formation assay. Moreover, cell cycle analysis showed that depletion of PIK3R1 could promote the entrance of SKOV3 cells into S and G2/M phases, reflecting progression of cell cycle. Concordantly, deletion of PIK3R1 also granted cells an ability to resist starvation-induce apoptosis. In addition to growth-related properties, in vitro abilities of migration and invasion were also augmented in PIK3R1-depletion cells, compared with wild-type cells. Our data also demonstrated that loss of PIK3R1 promoted malignant phenotypes in vivo. In nude mice models with intra-peritoneal injection of SKOV3 cells stably expressing PIK3R1 shRNA, the peritoneal dissemination of tumors was significantly higher than vector-expressing counterparts as reflected by the number and weight of tumor nodules. Collectively, these enhanced phenotypes indicate that PIK3R1 copy number loss in ovarian cancer cells leads to enhanced tumorigenic hallmarks, indicating a functional capability-based evidence of the frequent PIK3R1 copy number loss in ovarian cancer patients. Objective 2: to investigate the signaling alteration resulted from PIK3R1 copy number loss. To investigate the alteration of downstream signaling upon PIK3R1 loss, reverse phase protein array (RPPA) that detects the levels of 302 cancer-related proteins were performed with seven ovarian cancer cell lines. Being downstream of canonical PI3K pathway, the phosphorylation levels of AKT and its downstream effector ribosomal protein S6 were elevated by the downregulation of PIK3R1 cells. Unexpectedly, the phosphorylation level of STAT3 was upregulated in PIK3R1-depleted cell lines, suggesting a pathway activation beyond the canonical AKT axis. To evaluate the clinical significance of these observations, we examined the signaling activation in ovarian cancer patient samples. Remarkably, the activation of both AKT and STAT3 could be confirmed in a set of p85α-low ovarian cancer patient sections by immunohistochemistry staining. Among all 43 cancer samples, 31 (72%) of them showed decreased p85α level. In p85α-low samples, 18 (58%) and 22 (71%) of the tumors exhibited stronger STAT3 and AKT signals respectively, with 12 (39%) of them presented a high level of both molecules. Echoing to these tumor specimens, similar phenomena were also observed in a publicly available ovarian cancer dataset (The Cancer Genome Atlas TCGA). In stratified sample groups with highest quartile and lowest quartile PIK3R1 mRNA levels (n=103 in each group), STAT3 phosphorylation level and AKT phosphorylation levels were higher in PIK3R1-low group than in PIK3R1-high group. STAT3 is a transcription factor. Our data showed an elevated STAT3 translocation to the nucleus from the cytoplasm by PIK3R1 siRNA treatment. In addition to translocation, the transcription activities of STAT3 was examined by firefly luciferase assay. A STAT3 binding site-containing reporter plasmid was transfected into SKOV3 cells. The transcriptional activity of STAT3 was elevated by 3-fold in PIK3R1 downregulated cells. In line with the transcription activity, the mRNA levels of STAT3 targets, which are known to involve in cell cycle (CCNB1), anti-apoptosis (BLC2, BLC6), angiogenesis (VEGFA), metastasis (MMP9) and transcriptional factor (JUNB) were increased by PIK3R1 siRNA treatment and abolished by STAT3 inhibitor Stattic. Collectively, the data indicated that STAT3 was activated upon PIK3R1 deletion by promoting STAT3 translocation and downstream targets transcription. Objective 3: to delineate the mechanism of Stat3 activation and potential crosstalk with other pathways upon PIK3R1 copy number loss. We examined whether STAT3 and AKT activation by PIK3R1 downregulation is independent or interdependent by blocking these two pathways individually. Inhibition of AKT was observed as expected by AKT inhibitor MK-2206, but elevated JAK2 and STAT3 phosphorylation levels induced by PIK3R1 siRNA were not attenuated by MK-2206. Likewise, JAK2 inhibitor AZD480 effectively blocked STAT3 activation, but PIK3R1 loss still led to significantly activated AKT phosphorylation. These results indicated that the activation of STAT3 and AKT by PIK3R1 loss is independent. To determine whether STAT3 activation is p110-dependent, a pan PI3K inhibitor (PIK-90) was utilized to treat ovarian cancer cell lines with PIK3R1 siRNA. The results indicated that PIK-90 did not change the phosphorylation levels of STAT3 and JAK2. This finding showed a p110-independent STAT3 activation. The kinases that mediates STAT3 activation was examined. Western blotting data showed that the phosphorylation of JAK, but not Src, was increased in PI3KR1 loss cell lines, suggesting a JAK2-dependent but Src-independent activation of STAT3. Gab2 is a docking protein that interacts with pathway molecules including p85α to regulate signaling. Our finding showed that Gab2 is a mediator between p85α downregulation and STAT3 activation. The elevation of phosphorylated STAT3 as well as JAK2, in the context of PIK3R1 loss, was fully suppressed by GAB2 siRNA. Intriguingly, enhanced binding of Gab2 with STAT3 and JAK2 were observed in PIK3R1 downregulated cells, indicating an augmented signalosome assembly that may facilitate signal activation. Collectively, the results indicated the pivotal role of Gab2 in mediating PIK3R1 loss-induced STAT3 signaling. Gab2 contains multiple tyrosine and serine/threonine phosphorylation sites to regulate signaling transmission. We identified three phosphorylation sites that were altered in PIK3R1 loss-bearing cells, including S210, S405 and S623. By detailed downstream experiments such as mutagenesis, we confirmed a positive role of Gab2 S623 in PIK3R1-loss mediated JAK2/STAT3 activation. Objective 4: to determine the therapeutic vulnerability engendered by the copy number loss. Building on the results that PIK3R1 loss induces AKT and STAT3 activation in ovarian cancer cells, we speculated that cells with downregulated PIK3R1 would be more sensitive to inhibitors targeting these two pathways. Pharmacological inhibitors targeting AKT (GDC-0068 and MK-2206), JAK2 (AZ960 and AZD1480) and STAT3 (C188-9 and Stattic)were adopted to treat SKOV3 and OVCAR8 cells in the presence or absence of PIK3R1 siRNA. Notably, more significant decreases were observed in spheroids with PIK3R1 loss than control and mock cells. Given AKT and STAT3 activation upon PIK3R1 loss was independent, and PIK3R1 loss cells were sensitive to their respective inhibitors, the combination effects of drugs targeting these two pathways were then evaluated. Interestingly, the combination of AKT with JAK2 or STAT3 inhibitors led to a significant decreased cell viability than single drug. Co-targeting AKT with JAK2 or STAT3 could achieve synergistic effects in SKOV3 and OVCAR8 cells with PIK3R1-depletion. We also assessed the drug response in ovarian cancer xenograft models. The in vivo data demonstrated that single AKT and STAT3 blockade represses tumor burden in PIK3R1-depleted tumors and that dual inhibition achieves more significant anti-tumor effect.

27103616.label: Major findings and research outcome
27103616.value: Here we established that PIK3R1 loss is an oncogenic driver in ovarian cancer using multiple types of functional assays. Mechanistically, PIK3R1 loss activated not only AKT but also unexpectedly STAT3 signaling consistently in ovarian cancer cell lines and ovarian tumor samples. We demonstrated a previously unknown mechanism underlying the AKT activation which involves the docking protein Gab2 phosphorylation (Ser210, a site that was not known to be regulated by p85α) and relief of negative feedback regulation of AKT. Activation of JAK2/STAT3 signaling associated with p85α or p85α downregulation has never been reported. Our data showed that JAK2/STAT3 signaling is independent of crosstalk with AKT, but is dependent on Gab2 involving another phosphorylation site (Ser623) that again had not been linked to p85α previously. In short, the activation of two pathways was through two independent mechanisms but the same mediator, i.e. Gab2. Apart from the solid evidence on signaling activation and the underlying mechanisms, we were able to show that AKT and STAT3 inhibitors exerted synergistic anti-tumor effects in ovarian cancer cell lines in vitro and xenografts in vivo. The findings have been published in Nature Communications, which received a Faculty Outstanding Research Output Prize. A review paper stemming from the concept of combination therapy in this study was also published. A PhD study supported by this fund has successfully graduated. The thesis entitled ‘Functional Characterization of PIK3R1 Aberrations in Gynecological Cancers’ was rated ‘outstanding’ (top 5%) by the thesis examining committee.

27103616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27103616.value: The data underscores the potential use of PIK3R1 gene copy number as biomarker of responses to inhibition of AKT and STAT3. Future steps to take these findings to the next level include examination of drug responses using patient-derived cancer models.

27103616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27103616.value: Ovarian cancer is a leading cause of cancer deaths among women worldwide. An unmet need in ovarian cancer care is to develop therapeutic strategies that can tackle this life threatening disease. This study aims to identify novel biomarker and the corresponding therapies. The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) pathway is one of the most hyperactivated pathways in cancers. The regulatory subunit of PI3K p85α encoded by PIK3R1 is thought to primarily engage in AKT signaling because it regulates p110. Deletion of the PIK3R1 gene (also known as PIK3R1 loss) is highly frequent in ovarian cancer. However, the functional consequences, downstream signaling and the therapeutic implication of PIK3R1 loss in ovarian cancer had never been investigated. In this study, we showed that PIK3R1 loss goes beyond the classical AKT pathway because the genomic defect also caused activation of the STAT3 pathway. Therapeutically, PIK3R1 loss drove sensitivity to STAT3 and AKT inhibitors in cell culture and xenograft mouse models. This research describes for the first time PIK3R1 gene deletion as a potential marker to guide the combined use of AKT and STAT3 inhibitors in ovarian cancer treatment. The proposed targeted treatment approach could be applicable to large proportion of ovarian cancer patients.

27104116.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27104116.value: Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized by positive, negative and disorganization symptoms. Relapse, the re-emergence of these psychotic symptoms, is common amongst patients with schizophrenia. Naturalistic studies have shown that up to 80% of patients relapse within 5 years. Besides being associated with significant disturbances in functioning and social behavior, relapse may mean patients will need to stay on their medication for a considerably longer period of time or even on a long-term basis. Each relapse increases the probability of drug-resistant symptoms or residual symptoms. Relapse prevention is one of the primary objectives in the long-term management of patients with psychotic disorders. A key approach to relapse prevention is maintenance treatment or continuing to take existing medication. Unfortunately, data suggest that 40% of patients relapse despite maintenance treatment. Other than dis/continuing medication, we have little other information to help identify which patients will be more likely to relapse. To resolve this, scientists should work towards finding ‘suitable markers’ that can accurately predict who will be more likely to relapse, and then modify these markers to prevent a relapse from occurring. A ‘suitable marker’ should ideally be a variable that can be clearly defined, objectively measured, reproducible, and relatively easy to monitor in the daily clinical setting. A possible marker that fulfils these criteria is neurocognitive testing, namely one’s ability to perform memory, attention, and problem solving tasks. Our group found that patients who relapsed often had preceding neurocognitive decline (particularly in the visual working memory domain) compared to those who had not relapsed. In other words, patients who performed poorly in the visual working memory test during consecutive assessments could be at risk of relapse. This innovative but potentially important finding needs to be replicated in a naturalistic clinical sample to evaluate its clinical relevance. We propose to conduct a multi-site, prospective, 1-year follow-up study involving 220 first-episode psychosis patients to test the link between visual working memory decline and relapse. We also aim to explore the underlying neural mechanisms involved in visual working memory deficit underlying relapse using a longitudinal functional imaging paradigm in patients and healthy participants. Data from this study would help clinicians and healthcare workers to identify patients who are at risk of relapse and help them make decisions about maintenance therapy. 精神分裂是一種精神疾病，主要有陽性，陰性和言語混亂的症狀。精神分裂的復發指這些症狀重新出現。復發在精神分裂患者中十分常見；研究顯示，高至八成患者會在首次發病後的五年內復發。除了影響到日常生活功能及社交，復發亦令患者要較長的時間服用藥物，甚至要長期服用藥物。另外，每次復發都增加有抗藥性症狀或殘餘症狀的可能。所以，預防復發是治療的其中一個主要長期目標。 預防復發的關鍵是維持治療或繼續服用藥物。不幸地，數據指出有四成患者即使持續服用藥物，仍然會復發。現時尚未有充夠資訊去分辨哪些患者有較大可能復發。要解決這個問題，科學家應要找出能準確預測復發可能性的適當標記，再作修改以有效預防復發。一個適當標記最好能清潔定義，可客觀和重複測量，及容易作日常臨床監測。 其中一個符合上述標準的是認知功能，即是記憶力，注意力及問題解決的能力。本研究小組發現到，和沒有復發的患者比較，患者在復發前經常都會經歷認知功能的下降，特別在視覺工作記憶方面。換句話說，在連續的視覺工作記憶測試中表現下降的患者可能有較高的復發風險。這創新而有潛在重要性的發現需要一個自然的臨床樣本去評估其臨床意義。 我們提議要進行一個多地點及前瞻性的研究，用一年時間跟進一班首發思覺失調患者，測試視覺工作記憶衰退和復發的關係。研究的另一目標是探索視覺工作記憶衰退與復發背後的神經機制。此研究數據可以幫助醫生及醫護人員分辦有復發風險的患者，並幫助他們就持續治療作合適的決定。

27104116.label: Realisation of objectives
27104116.value: Objectives 1&2 We have completed recruitment of 176 stable psychosis patients from the Queen Mary Hospital (QMH) and Kwai Chung Hospital (KCH) in Hong Kong. These patients are to be followed-up with for either a year or until relapse, whichever earlier. During this follow-up period, participants completed monthly clinical, cognitive, and psychological assessments via phone interviews, a mobile application (“app”) named ReMind developed specifically for this purpose, or face-to-face interviews. Data analysis has been completed among the patients who have completed the 1 year follow up. We have examined the relationship between cognitive performance, other clinical and psychosocial factors, and relapse. Cognitive performance was measured by the Letter Number Sequencing (LNS) task and the Visual Patterns Test (VPT), whereas psychosocial assessments included those for stressful life events, expressed emotions, quality of life, subjective recovery, resilience, and stigma. Relapse was defined using two scales: the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) and the Clinical Global Impression Scale (CGI). Participants were identified to have relapsed if 1) their scores on PANSS subitems exceeded the threshold for at least one item (P1 Delusion ≥3, P2 Conceptual disorganization ≥4, P3 Hallucinatory behavior ≥3, P6 Suspiciousness / persecution ≥5, or G9 Unusual thought content ≥4); and 2) their CGI severity and improvement subscale scores reached 3 (“mildly ill”) and 5 (“minimally worse”) or above respectively. The findings from our data analysis so far have been detailed in Section 6.1, and are also currently being written up for publication, which we aim to achieve in the first quarter of 2022. As for the app, the rationale behind it, as well as its implementation and implications, has been detailed in a published peer-reviewed manuscript in the Early Intervention in Psychiatry (DOI: 10.1111/eip.1310) in 2020. In summary, we anticipate that this app will greatly facilitate the collection of monthly data over a longer follow-up period, which could also have potential in the monitoring and prediction of psychotic relapse. Objective 3 We have completed brain imaging scanning for 40 patients and 20 healthy controls. Each session, lasting around 1.5 hours, included both MRI and fMRI scanning. During the fMRI scans, participants were required to complete verbal and visual working memory tasks, both of which included a 0-back and a 2-back condition. For the verbal task, participants indicated whether the displayed letter was “X” or “x” (0-back), or whether it was the same as the one shown two letters ago (2-back). In the visual task, they indicated the position of the circle that lit up out of an array of four possible places (0-back), or the position of the circle shown two stimuli ago (2-back). Analysis of this imaging data is also underway. Data preprocessing procedures including slice timing, motion correction, spatial smoothing, linear trend removal and low pass filtering have already been done. The change in behavioural responses, anatomical data and BOLD (Blood oxygen level dependent) signal activation in response to the spatial and verbal n-back working memory task will first be compared between patients vs. healthy participants. Comparisons between relapsers and non-relapsers will follow. Further discussion will also be made with our collaborators (Professor Peter McKenna and Dr Edith Pomarol-Clotet) concerning the above data analyses and data interpretation. Since this data analysis process is still underway, it would be remiss to provide any concrete conclusions at this point.

27104116.label: Major findings and research outcome
27104116.value: Of the 176 recruited participants, 120 (68.18%) completed the study either upon/without relapse. The rest are being followed-up with, and 23 of them (41.07%) completed more than six-months’ worth of follow-ups. After removing 10 drop-outs, 110 participants were included in this main analysis, of which 18 (16.36%) relapsed. We first compared the profile of those who relapsed and those who did not. No significant differences were found in their demographics (age, gender, education level, etc.,) and clinical variables like duration of untreated psychosis and PANSS scores. For our first objective, working memory deterioration was calculated separately for VPT and LNS – by taking scores at termination/relapse, and subtracting from them the scores two months back. A negative raw change score suggests deterioration in working memory performance, and participants were categorised into “deteriorators”/“non-deteriorators”. The major finding is that “deteriorators”, specifically those who showed worsened performance in LNS longest level passed, were significantly larger in proportion in relapsers compared to non-relapsers, χ2 = 7.718, p = .005. This indicates that psychotic relapse is preceded by verbal working memory deterioration in the previous two months. Although this differs from previous findings (Hui et al., 2016), since it was verbal and not visual working memory deterioration that predicted relapse, this could be explained by differences in study design (naturalistic follow-up vs. RCT) and participant characteristics (concurrent medication use vs. off-medication). Therefore, current findings generated from a naturalistic setting where patients were not entirely off medication are relevant and adds to previous findings from a controlled setting. Other cognitive, clinical, and psychosocial predictors were examined for the second objective. Relapsers and non-relapsers displayed significant differences at baseline/pre-termination, i.e., premorbid social isolation, resilience, perceived risk of relapse, perceived level of recovery, self-stigma, and the proportion of deterioration on LNS longest level passed. Alongside medication adherence (not stopping medication on one’s own) at pre-termination, previous relapse history, and illness duration, these variables were entered into a binary multiple logistic (stepwise) regression. Three variables remained significant, LNS deterioration (longest level passed), p = .036; pre-termination medication adherence, p = .014; and resilience, p = .010; whereas a fourth variable remained marginally significant, previous relapse history, p = .098. Together, these predictors explained around 60% of variance in relapse (Nagelkerke R2 = .590). Given the current predictor variables are raw data where missing values have not been imputed, careful planning and further analyses will be conducted to handle empty data. Hui, C. L. M., Li, Y. 27104116.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27104116.value: Our study has two directions for future research: 1) to elucidate possible pathways or interactions between medication, cognitive deterioration, and relapse; and 2) to investigate whether this predictive power of verbal working memory deterioration in relapse is a general phenomenon of psychosis, or whether it only represents certain remitted psychosis patients. We believe this study could have far-reaching implications for the clinical care of psychosis, particularly in relapse prevention. For one, by highlighting the potential of cognitive function monitoring in informing a patient’s propensity to relapse, healthcare professionals may even adopt this into routine management. Cognitive variables, as opposed to other clinical or psychosocial variables, are advantageous due to its relative objectivity and ease to measure. In response to recent years’ rising interest and technological advances in mobile health, the monitoring of cognitive function could even be done through more accessible means such as apps, as alluded to in our published paper. In addition, this study provides preliminary support for the effects of cognitive remediation in improving patients’ clinical state. While little is known about how modifying cognitive performance may affect relapse itself, we hope the current study can add to the ongoing discussion regarding cognitive remediation therapy in psychosis.

27104116.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27104116.value: This naturalistic, observational study followed-up with remitted psychosis patients for a year, during which patients completed monthly clinical, cognitive, and psychosocial assessments. Our main outcome was relapse (i.e., the reappearance or exacerbation of positive psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations or delusions). By comparing psychosis patients who relapsed (n = 18) versus those who did not (n = 92), we found three variables to be relevant in relapse prediction. Firstly, worsened cognitive function in two preceding months, specifically in verbal working memory, was more likely observed in relapsers than non-relapsers. Secondly, low resilience (i.e., the ability to adapt to and cope with adversity) at baseline was also more likely observed in relapsers than non-relapsers. Thirdly, relapsers displayed more medication non-adherence behaviours, as indicated by their increased likelihood to stop medication on their own compared to non-relapsers. We believe that this study’s importance lies in the emphasis it puts on cognitive function in psychosis. It points towards two directions for clinical application: 1) to consider improving cognitive function as an alternative or adjunctive therapy to medication; and 2) to monitor cognitive function deterioration as an early sign of relapse.

27104616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27104616.value: Memory dysfunction is the main symptom of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), and no effective therapies are known that can cure or delay the symptom. This project aims to evaluate Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) as a potential therapy for AD. The success of this study would be seen as the first critical step toward the application of DBS in AD patients. If DBS is effective in reducing symptoms of AD, then this could hold significant promise for both patients and caregivers. Although preliminary investigations of DBS in certain brain regions have demonstrated beneficial effects on memory function, some fundamental issues remain concerning which brain target(s) and what stimulation parameters should be used to achieve the desirable therapeutic effects. In addition, the mechanisms by which DBS improves memory functions remain poorly understood. The main objective in this research proposal is to test the hypothesis that DBS induces memory enhancement in transgenic AD and age-related dementia animal models. The transgenic 5XFAD mice model rapidly develops the major characteristics of amyloid pathology with accumulation of intraneuronal beta-amyloid 42 and cognitive impairment around 4 months of age. We will electrically stimulate six potential brain regions utilizing a range of stimulation parameters (frequency, current, duration) to enhance memory, and test for the specificity of the site and stimulation parameters. The animal subjects with DBS or with sham-surgery will be subject to a variety of behavioural tests, including memory-tasks for the therapeutic effects, and motor and non-motor tasks to evaluate possible side-effects. After the final behavioural experiments, the subjects will be sacrificed and their brains processed for cellular and biochemical analyses. Our secondary objective is to study the functional brain connectivity and identify the molecular mechanisms and biomarkers of neuroplasticity on DBS-induced memory enhancement using functional neuroanatomical, combined brain microdialysis-behavioural and biochemical approaches. Finally, we will investigate the electrophysiological properties of hippocampal neuronal firing, local field potential, and cellular models of long-term potentiation process due to DBS-induced memory enhancement. The experimental approach will consist of different inter-related sections, which together provide a multi-level, interdisciplinary investigation of how DBS affects the neural circuit of memory-related behaviours. The hypotheses in these objectives will be tested independently, irrespective of the outcome results from the individual experimental studies. Overall, this research proposal aims to explore new scientific opportunities of using DBS as a potential therapeutic tool in combination with molecular and electrophysiological methods to unravel the neural mechanisms underlying memory dysfunction. 記憶功能障礙是阿爾茨海默氏病(AD)的主要症狀，且沒有已知的有效治療方法可以治愈或延緩此症狀。本研究的目的是評估腦深部電刺激作為AD潛在療法的可能性。本研究的成功將開啟將電刺激應用於AD患者的關鍵一步。如果腦深部電刺激能夠有效地減少AD症狀，那麼這可能會為患者和護理人員帶來重大希望。雖然一些初步研究已證實對某些腦區進行腦深部電刺激對記憶功能有幫助，但仍然存在一些基本問題，如什麼腦區域應作為刺激目標和應用什麼刺激參數來實現理想的治療效果。另外，關於腦刺激改善記憶功能的機制仍然知之甚少。 本研究計劃的主要目標是在轉基因AD動物模型和衰老相關的癡呆症動物模型中，驗証腦刺激會誘發記憶增強的假說。轉基因5XFAD小鼠在四個月左右迅速發展出澱粉樣蛋白病理的主要特徵，包括神經元內β-澱粉樣蛋白42的積累和認知功能障礙。我們將運用一系列的刺激參數(頻率､電流､時間)刺激六個有潛質的大腦區域以增強動物記憶力，並測試刺激位置和參數的特異性。被電刺激的動物和接受假手術的動物會接受各種行為學測試，包括執行記憶任務以評測治療效果，以及運動和非運動的任務以評估可能產生的副作用。最後的行為實驗後，受試動物會被處死，牠們的大腦會被處理作細胞和生化分析。 我們的第二個目標是利用功能神經解剖學，結合腦微透析､行為學和生物化學等方法，研究大腦的功能性聯結以及探究電刺激誘發記憶增強的分子機制和神經可塑性的生物標誌物。 最後，我們將研究電刺激誘發的記憶增強中，海馬體的神經元放電，局部場電位，以及細胞模型的長時程增強現象等電生理特性。實驗方法將包括不同但互相關連的部分，它們一起提供了多層次而跨學科的研究，以揭示電刺激是如何影響記憶相關行為的神經通路。本項目的各假說將被獨立測試，不受項目內其他研究結果的影響。總體而言，本研究計劃旨在探討使用電刺激作潛在治療工具的科學機遇，並結合分子和電生理學方法，揭示記憶障礙的神經機制。

27104616.label: Realisation of objectives
27104616.value: Objective 1: In this objective, we implanted Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) electrodes bilaterally into the prelimbic cortex (PrL), perifornical area, and/or entorhinal cortex, structures known to be effective targets for DBS for memory improvement. We subjected the aged rats or 5xFAD mice to a protocol of DBS and evaluated the effects on hippocampal-dependent memory using Morris water maze (MWM), and various behavioural tests for evaluation of possible side effects (anxiety and locomotion). Interestingly, we found that DBS induced significant memory improvements and/or antidepressant-like behaviours in the experimental models of dementia in rodents. Additionally, we have used a modified plus-maze discriminative task and showed that DBS of the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) was able to disrupt consolidation, but not acquisition or retrieval of fear memories. We validated these results using a tone-footshock fear conditioning paradigm. We further demonstrated short-term changes in dopaminergic receptor and c-Fos expression in the ventral hippocampus (vHPC) and established a partial casual role of dopamine 2 receptors in this effect. Lastly, we showed changes in neurotransmitter levels in the vHPC. This study highlights the potential therapeutic effect of vmPFC DBS to treat anxiety disorders. Objective 2: We then attempted to unravel some of the mechanisms underlying the memory enhancements using several neuroanatomical and biochemical approaches, e.g. immunohistochemistry, microscopic imaging, flow-cytometry, western-blotting, microarrays, and gene expression methods. Particularly, microarrays, which can harness advancements in omics technologies and computational power, to probe key molecular signalling mechanisms mediating the observed effects. Our microarray analysis revealed distinct patterns of changes in gene expression in the hippocampus, with G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) being a key focus. Based on our microarray data, we further investigated changes in neurotransmitters and metabolites in the hippocampus, which we previously described as a potential mechanism by which DBS can enhance memories. We also found that changes in monoamines corroborated our microarray data, which partly explained some of the mechanisms behind the observed effects. Overall, we found that DBS of the PrL, perifornical area, and/or entorhinal induced memory improvements in aged rats associated with distinct patterns of change in the hippocampus. Objective 3: We studied the morphological changes of the hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity in experimental animal model. Objective Achievement/Completed Works: 1. DBS of the PrL in animal models of aging (Published - DOI: 10.1007/s13311-020-00913-7; DOI: 10.3389/fnagi.2020.00273) and fear conditioning memory (Under review process - DOI: 10.1101/537514). 2. DBS of the perifornical area in aged animal model. (Manuscript under preparation; see also published Conference Abstract - DOI:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.brs.2018.12.412) 3. DBS of the entorhinal cortex in aged animal model. (Manuscript under preparation; see also published Conference Abstract - DOI:https://doi.org/10.1016/j.brs.2018.12.412) 4. DBS of the hippocampus in 5xFAD transgenic mouse model of Alzheimer's disease. (Manuscript under preparation) 5. Extensive literature reviews of the present research have been published in Aging & Disease (DOI: 10.14336/AD.2020.0602; DOI: 10.14336/AD.2019.1026; DOI: 10.14336/AD.2019.1125), Neuroscience & Biobehavioural Reviews (DOI: 10.1016/j.neubiorev.2020.07.040; DOI: 10.1016/j.neubiorev.2019.12.022), Experimental Neurology (DOI: 10.1016/j.expneurol.2019.01.004), BMC Medical Ethics (https://doi.org/10.1186/s12910-020-00532-z), and Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences (DOI: 10.1111/nyas.14458; DOI: 10.1111/nyas.14373). Attempts to overcome problems: 1. We encountered difficulties of obtaining the aged animal model as aging studies are lengthy, resource intensive, and require long-term planning. Also, the death rate of animals was high, e.g. out of 40 animals, 12 died between 23 and 24 months of age (see Neurotherapeutics, https://doi.org/10.1007/s13311-020-00913-7). 2. Although electrophysiological study of the long-term potentiation process on hippocampal synaptic plasticity was performed in Objective 3, unfortunately, we obtained no significant results between the stimulated and non-stimulated sham animals. In this regard, we carried out alternative studies on the morphological characteristic of the hippocampal neurogenesis (immunohistochemistry of BrdU labeling, doublecortin, anti-Microtubule-Associated Protein 2, Ki-67) and neuro/synaptic plasticity (Golgi-Cox staining). Non-surprisingly, we found that electrical stimulation increased the expression of these markers as compared to non-stimulated group, which was accordingly to our hypothesis. Summary: 1. 27104616.label: Major findings and research outcome
27104616.value: (a) In this study, we used a Morris water maze (MWM) to determine the effects of prelimbic cortex (PrL) Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) on memory in aged rats. To investigate the underlying mechanisms of the effects of DBS, we carried out microarray, quantitative PCR analysis, and mass spectrometry to detect gene expression and neurotransmitter changes in the hippocampus. We showed PrL DBS improved the performance in MWM, with related distinct patterns of gene expression involving G protein–coupled receptor pathways. We further found neurotransmitter changes in the dorsal hippocampus, which corroborated and extended the microarray findings. (DOI: 10.1007/s13311-020-00913-7) (b) Next, we hypothesized that disruption and enhancement of memory through neuromodulation can be explained by the dropout of engram nodes. We used a convolutional neural network to classify handwritten digits and letters and applied dropout at different stages to simulate DBS effects on engrams. We showed that dropout applied during training improved the accuracy of prediction, whereas dropout applied during testing dramatically decreased the accuracy of prediction, which mimics enhancement and disruption of memory, respectively. We further showed that transfer learning of neural networks with dropout had increased the accuracy and rate of learning. Dropout during training provided a more robust “skeleton” network and, together with transfer learning, mimicked the effects of chronic DBS on memory. (DOI: 10.3389/fnagi.2020.00273) (c) Additionally, we have also demonstrated that perifornical stimulation enhanced spatial memory in the Morris water-maze without affecting anxiety levels in an aged rat model. The microarray profiling showed a distinct pattern of signalling mechanisms involving the neurotransmission and neuroplasticity-related functions of perifornical (PeFLH) stimulation. These results were further supported by protein changes associated with neurotransmission and neuroplasticity markers measured by western-blotting, mass-spectrometry, and FACS-based methods. (Unpublished data, manuscript is currently under preparation stage) (d) Finally, we have consolidated findings and conclusions from the current research on the effects of DBS on memory in attempt to make sense of the bidirectional nature of DBS in disrupting and enhancing memory. We propose a consolidated model of how DBS can both disrupt and enhance memory. (DOI: 10.14336/AD.2019.0511) We further highlight some of the issues involved in implementing these suggestions and argue that willpower of the research community, and emphasis on the need for interdisciplinary research in Alzheimer’s disease and suggest that international societies should play a huge role in this endeavour. (Aging and Disease, DOI: 10.14336/AD.2020.0602; BMC Medical Ethics, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12910-020-00532-z).

27104616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27104616.value: Ageing is a major predicting risk factor for dementia and no treatment is currently available for this disorder. Although promising outcome has been reported for electrical stimulation on dementia, the molecular mechanisms remain abstruse. Our present study identified a broad range of molecular pathways involved in prelimbic/ventromedial prefrontal cortex, perifornical area, and entorhinal cortex stimulation-induced memory enhancement, which could potentially be a promising therapeutic strategy for dementia. Our results suggest that both neurogenesis and non-neurogenesis pathways play roles in the effects of DBS. Further studies are needed to investigate the effects of DBS on memory beyond neurogenesis and to consider the highlighted pathways suggested by our data.

27104616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27104616.value: In this study, we showed the potential of DBS (Deep Brain Stimulation) in enhancing memory in aged animals. We anticipate that DBS technology could eventually be applied in aged-related disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease. Using a more aetiologically relevant model (aged animals) and harnessing high-throughput omics techniques such as microarray, we highlighted major molecular mechanisms related to the observed effects. We showed that mechanisms beyond neurogenesis might underlie the memory enhancement effects of DBS. Overall, it is likely that a complex interplay between changes in neurogenesis and non-neurogenesis genes/proteins contribute to the effects of DBS. Although we focused on the major changes in dopamine transmission in hippocampus, the observed changes in glutamate regulation and serotonin metabolism could also be contributing factors. This study has only begun to uncover some of the mechanisms of how DBS enhances memories in aged animals and the findings are preliminary in nature; they provide a first step and a foundation for further research to uncover the mechanisms of the effects of DBS. Therefore, this research serves as a call for more studies on the effects of DBS on memory that look beyond neurogenesis and to investigate the pathways highlighted in our data.
