27105716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27105716.value: Multiple biological mechanisms contribute to cancer cell growth, such that treatment with only a single drug is less efficacious for long-term successful cancer therapy. Combinatorial drug therapies that act on multiple cellular targets simultaneously emerge to be more effective for cancer cell elimination, and could suppress the emergence of resistance due to the activation of compensatory pathways for cancer survival. Bromodomain and extra terminal protein (BET) inhibitors are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutic agents in treating various cancers, including ovarian cancer, via reprogramming gene transcription. Cellular mechanisms that may be involved in the acquired resistance towards BET inhibitor treatment were investigated, and could be co-targeted to improve the therapeutic efficacy. However, conventional approaches for discovering the specific therapeutic combinations are low-throughput and expensive, thus impeding the progress towards developing new therapies including drug combinations for optimizing the efficacy of BET inhibitors. Our goal here is to discover new combinatorial sets of drugs that inhibit ovarian cancer cell growth, with the aim to tackle the urgent need for new and effective treatments for human ovarian cancer. We have developed a powerful and scalable technology, termed Combinatorial Genetics En Masse (CombiGEM), to enable highly multiplexed studies linking multifactorial genetic perturbations to complex biological phenotypes (Wong et al., Nat. Biotechnol., 2015). The time, cost and effort required for constructing and analyzing the effects of genetic combinations with CombiGEM are orders of magnitude less than those of other existing strategies. We have validated the CombiGEM technology in the human cell system by identifying microRNA combinations that suppress the growth and drug resistance of ovarian cancer cells. Here, we will move beyond prior studies in this proposal by using CombiGEM to inhibit combinatorial sets of druggable genes, and systematically identify those that block the proliferation of human ovarian cancer cells either with or without BET inhibitor treatment. We will functionally profile genetic combinations for rendering ovarian cancer cells sensitive to BET inhibitors. By targeting the combinatorial gene sets from various pathways with multiplexed clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based gene perturbation system, our work will provide new insights into how rewiring of gene regulatory networks may enhance the efficacy of therapies that include BET inhibitors. Importantly, by focusing our perturbation on druggable genes, our work will be able to readily translate these gene combinations into novel drug combinations for advancing therapeutic development towards treating human ovarian cancer. 癌細胞生長牽涉到眾多生物學機制，因而單一藥物處理的長期療效往往不佳。藥物聯合療法在同時作用於細胞內多個靶標，能夠更有效的殺滅癌細胞並且抑制癌細胞內因代償性信號通路的啟動引起的耐藥性。然而，尋求特定聯合治療的傳統方法通常低效且昂貴，難免阻礙了包括藥物聯合優化藥效在內的新療法的發展。我們的目標是探索新的抑制卵巢癌細胞生長的藥物聯合療法，期望滿足對人類卵巢癌新型且有效治療的迫切需要。

27105716.label: Realisation of objectives
27105716.value: We have successfully achieved all the objectives in this project. First, we built the CombiGEM-CRISPR library to knock out druggable genes (Aim 1), and performed massively parallel studies with the CombiGEM-CRISPR library to systematically profile the effects of combinatorial gene knockouts on human ovarian cancer cell proliferation (Aim 2). We applied the Azimuth 2.0 model to design sgRNAs that target the list of 52 druggable genes with maximal on-target and minimal off-target effects. We compared the on-target efficacy score obtained from the Azimuth 2.0 model and the indel generation efficiency of gRNAs, and observed that the on-target efficacy score largely predicts the efficiency of gRNAs in OVCAR8-ADR-Cas9 cells. To generate combinatorial gene knockouts at a high rate, we have selected gRNAs with an on-target efficacy score of at least 0.64. The gRNA target sites were restricted to 5 to 65% of the length of the coding sequences to generate a higher proportion of null mutations. Only gRNAs that have the low off-target rank (i.e., less than 100) were selected. We then used CombiGEM to assemble multiplexed CRISPR libraries with the sgRNA constructs to target the druggable genes. We created the initial barcoded sgRNA library targeting against the 52 druggable genes (i.e., 3 sgRNAs per gene) plus 3 control sgRNAs from the GeCKOv2 library that do not have on-target loci in the human genome as internal controls. An array of 159 oligo pairs encoding a library of barcoded sgRNA target sequences was synthesized, pooled in equal ratios, and cloned downstream of a U6 promoter in the storage vector. The scaffold sequence for the sgRNAs was inserted into the storage vector library in a single-pot ligation reaction. We applied CombiGEM for scalable assembly of the one-wise and pair-wise gRNA plasmid libraries using highly competent E. coli. We also created pooled lentiviruses harboring the pair-wise gRNA library. Using Illumina Hi-Seq, we confirmed the high coverage (>99%), as well as a relatively even distribution of barcoded gRNA combinations, for the pairwise library (i.e., 159 x 159 = total of 25,281 gRNA combinations) within both the plasmid and infected cell pools. Furthermore, we observed a high correlation of barcode representation between the plasmid and infected cell pools, and as well as within biological replicates for the infected cell pools. We further delivered this barcoded combinatorial gRNA library into OVCAR8-ADR-Cas9 cells via lentiviruses to search for gRNA combinations that inhibit cell proliferation. Lentiviruses were titrated to a multiplicity of infection of ~0.3 to facilitate single-copy integration in most infected cells. We used >300-fold more cells for lentiviral infection than the size of the library being tested to ensure high-quality screens with a high-coverage library representing most combinations. We extracted genomic DNA for unbiased amplification and quantification of the integrated barcodes for cells cultured for 15 and 21 days post-infection. We performed this experiment in two biological replicates. Illumina HiSeq was performed to quantify the representation of individual barcoded combinations in infected cell pools. Bioinformatics analysis was also completed to isolate candidate gRNA combinations targeting druggable genes that inhibit the proliferation of OVCAR8-ADR-Cas9 cells. Using selection criteria that required a mean log2 ratios of <-1 (i.e., based on data obtained from two biological replicates with at least 50% fewer barcode counts in day 21- versus day 15-cultured cells) and a P-value of <0.05, we isolated 31 gRNA combinations that inhibit OVCAR8-ADR cell proliferation. At a P-value of at least <0.1, 80 gRNA combinations were found to have mean log2 ratios of <-1. Of these, two combinations (i.e., PARP1 + DNMT1 and CDK2 + FKBP1A) were identified via multiple gRNAs targeting the same gene pair as top hits in our profiling. In addition, the antiproliferative effects brought by these double knockouts were not observed when only one of these genes in the combination was knocked out. We also performed CombiGEM-CRISPR in an attempt to identify interacting druggable genetic factors to enhance the anti-cancer effect of BET inhibitors (Aim 4). We delivered the barcoded combinatorial gRNA library into OVCAR8-ADR-Cas9 cells via lentiviruses to search for druggable factors that render those cells sensitive to BET inhibitors JQ1. We titrated the lentivirus to a multiplicity of infection of ~0.3 to facilitate single-copy integration in most infected cells. We used >300-fold more cells for lentiviral infection than the size of the library being tested to ensure a high-coverage library representing most combinations. The profiling work was completed and we compared the profiling results obtained from cell pools treated with vehicle control or the BET inhibitor. Our results indicated that none of the gRNA combinations have >2 gRNA combos that showed >-1 and P<0.05), meaning no strong hit was identified. Enhancing the efficacy of JQ1 and tackling its resistance emerged from the cancer cells may require perturbation of other factors or alternative strategies. With the overall goal to identify effective therapeutic combinations for treating ovarian cancer, here, we decided to focus on validating all two screen hits identified in Aim 2. We moved on to validate combinatorial gene knockout phenotypes using individual non-pooled CRISPR and drug combinations (Aim 3). We built individual combinatorial CRISPR constructs that recapitulate the putative anti-proliferative gene knockout combinations from the top candidates (i.e., PARP1 + DNMT1 and CDK2 + FKBP1A), and performed MTT assays to validate their anti-proliferative effect in OVCAR8-ADR. We confirmed combinatorial knockout of the targeted genes via sequencing of the targeted loci. To translate the genetic combinations into therapeutic candidates, we set up experiments to evaluate the anti-proliferative effects of the matching drug combinations in OVCAR8-ADR cells. Olaparib, Azacitdine, Roscovitine, and Rapamycin were selected as the matching drugs to target PARP1, DNMT1, CDK2, and FKBP1A, respectively. These drug molecules have been reported to have potent effects on their targets. Olaparib, Azacitdine, and Rapamycin are Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drugs, while Roscovitine is being experimented for the treatment of several diseases including non-small cell lung cancer and leukemia. In addition, Phase I and II clinical trials are in progress to evaluate the efficacy of various PARP1 inhibitors, DNMT1 inhibitors, Rapamycin and its derivatives, when used in combination with other drugs in ovarian cancer patients (https://clinicaltrials.gov). Our results using MTT and colony formation assays indicated that Olaparib and Azacitdine work synergistically to inhibit the growth of OVCAR8-ADR cells. For example, the cotreatment led to a large reduction in cell growth (i.e., >60% decrease in viable cell numbers on day 5). Combined treatment with Roscovitine and Rapamycin exerted an additive effect that renders the proliferation of OVCAR8-ADR cells (i.e., >60% decrease in viable cell numbers on day 5). We quantified drug synergy using the Bliss independence model and the Highest Single Agent model. We further completed Aim 3 by validating the drug combination (i.e., Olaparib + Azacitdine, as well as Roscovitine + Rapamycin) effects in suppressing the growth of multiple ovarian cancer cell lines. We tested them in KURAMOCHI and OVSAHO that were reported to be more closely resembling the molecular signatures detected in patients’ HGSOC tumor samples. By using a combination of drug doses, we quantified the drug synergy using the Bliss independence model and the Highest Single Agent model. Our results thus confirmed the growth-inhibiting effects brought by our hit combinations in multiple independent HGSOC cell lines.

27105716.label: Major findings and research outcome
27105716.value: This work has successfully applied a CRISPR-based dual-gene knockout screen to identify drug pairs that inhibit ovarian cancer cell growth. We have identified the druggable genetic combinations (i.e., PARP1 + DNMT1 and CDK2 + FKBP1A) and validated the matching drug combination regimens (i.e., Olaparib + Azacitdine, as well as Roscovitine + Rapamycin) for suppression of cancer cell growth in a panel of ovarian cancer cell lines. This work contributes to in part a paper published in Cell Reports, an experimental protocol published at STAR Protocols, as well as several talks and poster presentations at international conferences. (Please refer to Part C for the details).

27105716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27105716.value: We applied a CRISPR-based dual-gene knockout screening platform to address the unmet need for rapid identification of effective therapeutic combinations. Pairing drug mechanisms of action to specific genes helps to accelerate identification of effective combinations for directing secondary screens and narrows a vast number of possible combinations down to few top-performing hits for further testing. We demonstrated that systematic characterization of combinations using CRISPR-based screening discovers rare ones with synergistic interactions because most of them showed buffering or no interactions, and we were able to validate all two screen hits with strong growth inhibition effects. Our platform has broad utility because it can also be used to identify two-drug regimens that inhibit cancer cell growth and enhance protection against other disease phenotypes. In future, this platform is also versatile and can be used together with dCas9-based CRISPR interference systems to partially lower target gene expressions to mimic drug inhibitor effects and minimize any spurious effects caused by large deletions and genomic rearrangements. This platform could be coupled with other technologies, like single-cell RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), to explore different cell signatures and contribute to generation of druggable gene interaction networks using existing knowledge.

27105716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27105716.value: Studying druggable gene interactions that mimic the actions of targeted drug combinations is practically challenging. We applied the CombiGEM-CRISPR system for screening dual-gene combinations, leading to identification of two-drug combination regimens that suppress ovarian cancer growth.

27106016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27106016.value: 由於運動創傷的發生率及其相關的經濟和公共衛生費用, 運動安全被認為是許多國家的重要問題。年輕人應該要了解運動安全, 並要意識到預防運動創傷在人生中的重要性。因此，在香港教育局的體育科裏，運動安全是核心課程之一。但是, 學生在課堂上學到了運動安全後，是否會主動在課餘時間去學以致用呢？目前，並沒有研究去探討。因此，本研究旨在利用一個社會心理學的理論去建立運動安全的教學材料。 研究計劃會包括三個階段與多個定性和定量的研究。研究結果可以提高中學生在課餘時間預防運動創傷的動機和意圖。第一個階段會有十二個小組訪談, 內容包括運動安全教學, 和在課餘時間防止運動創傷的想法和行為。第一階段的定性數據會用於建立基礎理論的問卷。在第二階段，問卷會派發給中學生作為一個前瞻性研究 (例如, 學生在體育課的學習動機和在課餘時間預防運動創傷之間的關係)。第三階段會利用前期所收集的數據，建立理論為本的教育材料及網上學習系統，從而提高運動安全教育的有效性。研究將會測試這些教育材料，在提交給體育教師後, 會否能夠有效地改變到學生的學習動機，意圖，和預防運動創傷的行為 。這個計劃會在香港運動安全教育的理論與實踐有顯著貢獻。

27106016.label: Realisation of objectives
27106016.value: 1. Objective 1 has been achieved as expected. We have developed the theory-driven smartphone application for PE-teachers to enhance students’ motivation toward, and adherence to, behaviours to prevent sport injury. To examine the effectiveness of this smartphone application, we conducted a 3-month randomised controlled trial (Study 3) among 1168 secondary school students (the sample size is substantially more than what we proposed (N = 250) in our initial proposal). The results supported the effectiveness of the smartphone application on students’ motivation and decision-making factors associated with sport injury prevention. 2. Objective 2 has been achieved as expected. We conducted a prospective study (Study 2) among 1566 secondary school students (the sample size is substantially more than what we proposed (N = 300) in our initial proposal) to examine the psychological process of learning sport safety, including the relationship between motivation of sport injury prevention in-school and out-of-school contexts. 3. Objective 3 has been achieved as expected. The findings of Study 2 and Study 3 supported the tenets of the Trans-Contextual Model, the psychological model behind the smartphone application we developed. In addition, we have obtained qualitative data (Study 1) from 17 focus group interviews among 128 secondary school students (the sample size is more than what we proposed N = 72 - 96) that examined the content of the variables in the Trans-Contextual Model in the context of sport injury prevention among secondary school students. Overall, we have successfully completed the three proposed studies for a preliminary application of the trans-contextual model in the context of sport safety education.

27106016.label: Major findings and research outcome
27106016.value: Study 1: From seventeen groups semi-structured interviews among 128 secondary school students, we identified 7 higher order themes and 16 lower-order themes about in-school and out-of-school motives and social cognitive factors that were aligned with the conceptualisation of the trans-contextual model. Our qualitative findings contribute to a better understanding on secondary school students’ motivation and social cognitive factors of sport injury prevention, and the way in which sport safety education could be promoted in school setting. Study 2: Data from a prospective study among 1566 secondary school students supported the effects of perceived autonomy support from PE teachers on in-school autonomous motivation toward injury prevention, the trans-contextual relationship between students’ ‘in-school’ and ‘out-of-school’ autonomous motivation toward injury prevention, and the effects of autonomous motivation toward injury prevention on social cognitive variables and prospectively-measured injury prevention behaviour. The findings supported the utility of the trans-contextual model in predicting students’ ‘in-school’ and ‘out-of-school’ autonomous motivation toward sport injury prevention. The results underscore the potential importance of autonomy support from PE teachers in facilitating students’ sport injury prevention behaviours. Study 3: Findings of a 3-month randomised control trial among 1168 secondary school students showed that the evidence-based smartphone application we developed had positive and significant direct and indirect effects on the key psychological and behavioural variables of sport injury prevention, including perceived psychological need support, motivation, and social cognition variables, and intention of sport injury prevention. The evidence-based smartphone application developed based on the trans-contextual model is effective in promoting sport injury prevention among secondary school students.

27106016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27106016.value: Given the supportive evidence on the effectiveness of the theory-driven smartphone application, we can introduce this smartphone application to more secondary schools in Hong Kong, so students and PE teachers may have better awareness to risk of sport injury, and better behavioural adherence and motivation regarding sport injury prevention. The current institution of the principal investigator, The Education University of Hong Kong, has a number of knowledge transfer grants that will be sought for disseminating the findings of the current project to these stakeholders via public seminars, press releases, and reports in news or social media. Future research should also explore other possibilities of extending the application of this theory-driven smartphone phone to other sampling population (e.g., primary school, pre-schools), or the promotion of other health behaviours (e.g., rehabilitation adherence, physical activity, healthy diet).

27106016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27106016.value: Sport safety is regarded as a critical public health concern in many countries. It is important that young people learn about safety in sport, and be aware of the importance of preventing sport injury throughout their life. Therefore, this project applied the trans-contextual model to develop a theory-driven smartphone application for promoting sport injury prevention among Hong Kong secondary school students. In this project, we conducted 3 studies, including a qualitative study (sample = 128 secondary school students), a prospective study (sample = 1566 secondary school students), and a randomised controlled trial (sample = 1168 secondary school students), for the development and testing of the smartphone application. The findings supported the utility of the smartphone application, and the trans-contextual model, in understanding and promoting secondary school students’ motivation and decision-making factors of sport injury prevention. This project had significant contributions to theory and practice because we successfully applied the trans-contextual model in a sport safety education setting, and the smartphone application developed by the model has shown to be effective for promoting the motivation and decision-making factors of sport injury prevention among secondary school students.

27200916.label: Project Objectives
27200916.value: [To develop a general, rigorous concurrency attack model]. We will conduct an extensive study on real-world multithreaded programs, summarize general elements on how concurrency bugs propagate to attacks, and leverage our expertise on precise program analysis methods to develop the first concurrency attack model. This approach will leverage recent automated program analysis techniques to identify concurrency bugs in program source code and vulnerable instructions these bugs may propagate to. 27200916.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27200916.value: Driven by the rise of multi-core hardware, multithreaded programs become a mainstream of software. Unfortunately, despite much effort, these programs are still notoriously difficult to get right; they are plagued with concurrency bugs (e.g., data races on memory). Worse, recent research reveals that many real-world concurrency bugs have led to “concurrency attacks”: hackers have leveraged concurrency bugs to corrupt the critical memory of a program, to bypass security authentications, and to construct various vulnerabilities (e.g., privilege escalations). Moreover, concurrency attacks weaken or even completely bypass most existing security defense techniques, because these techniques are mainly designed for single-threaded programs. State-of-the-art neither has a rigorous model to describe how concurrency attacks manifest nor has any detection or defense approach. This FALCON project tackles concurrency attacks by pursuing three objectives. First, we will develop a general, rigorous model to describe how concurrency attacks manifest. A main challenge for this model is figuring out how the memory corrupted by concurrency bugs propagates to vulnerable instructions. To address this challenge, we will conduct an extensive study on real-world concurrency attacks, summarize general elements on how bugs propagate to attacks, and leverage our expertise on program analysis methods to develop our model. Second, following the model, we will construct a systematic approach for detecting attacks during the testing phase. A main challenge for this detection approach is precisely identifying several diverse types of vulnerable instructions in program source code. To tackle this challenge, we have presented a preliminary algorithm to identify one type of vulnerable instructions in our ASPLOS 2013 paper. Third, to deal with concurrency attacks that may be missed by detection tools, we will construct a runtime defense infrastructure to protect general programs during their deployment phase. This infrastructure requires several reliability techniques, including replication techniques for tolerating program failures, and checkpoint techniques for recovering program execution state (e.g., memory) from failures. In preparation for this infrastructure, we have presented an easy-to-use replication technique in our SOSP 2015 paper. We envision that our expertise on program analysis algorithms and our preliminary results on replication techniques will help us achieve all the three objectives. By greatly improving the reliability and security of multithreaded programs, this project will benefit almost all computer users and software service companies. This project will also spur new research questions, ideas, and tools in broad areas, including reliability, security, and concurrency. 随着多核硬件的流行，多线程程序已经成为了主流软件之一。但是，虽然过去人们投入了很多努力，多线程程序仍然容易出错：它们充斥了各种并行差错（比如对共享内存的竞争访问）。更糟糕的是，最近有研究表明并行差错会导致“并行攻击”：黑客可以利用并行差错来弄乱一个软件的关键内存，避开安全认证，并构建各种安全危害（比如软件的权限倒置）。更糟糕的是，并行攻击可以削弱甚至完全避开目前已有的绝大多数安全技术，因为这些技术主要是为单线程软件而设计的。目前人们并没有对并行攻击进行建模的严谨方法，也缺乏有效的检测和防御技术。 这个FALCON项目以三个研究目标来应对并行攻击。首先，我们将会研发一个普适、严谨的模型来描述并行攻击是如何发生的。为达到这个目标，一个主要的研究挑战，就是要识别出被弄乱的内存是如何传播到易受攻击的软件指令的。为了应对这个挑战，我们将会对现实世界中的并行攻击进行广泛的调研，总结这个传播渠道的主要元素，并且利用我们已掌握的程序分析的专业方法来构建这个模型。 第二个目标，就是在这个模型基础上，我们将会构建一个系统化的方法来检测并行攻击。一个主要的挑战，就是要在软件的程序之中，精准地定位多种已受攻击的指令。为了应对这个挑战，我们已经发明了一个初步的算法来定位其中一种易受攻击的指令，这个算法的初步结果被发表在了ASPLOS 2013国际会议之上。 第三个目标，就是为了应对那些躲过了检测的并行攻击，我们将会构建一个运行时防御体系结构来保护普遍的软件。这个体系结构需要几个关键技术，包括软件容错的技术，以及软件状态保存和回复的关键技术。为了构建这个体系结构，我们已经研发了一种容易使用的软件容错技术，这个技术的初步结果发表了在SOSP 2015国际会议之上。 我们期待我们在程序分析方面的专业技术以及我们在容错技术上面的初步成果，将会帮助我们达成这三个目标。通过极大地提高多线程程序的可靠性和安全性，这个项目将会为几乎所有的计算机用户和软件公司提供益处。这个项目将会激发更多的关于并行攻击的学术新问题，新理念，新技术，将会吸引包括软件可靠性、安全性和并行领域的科研人员来加入我们的研究。

27200916.label: Realisation of objectives
27200916.value: I achieved all three objectives. My PhD students and I have invented a series of software systems and tools for improving concurrency security of real-world software. Regarding paper publications funded by this ECS project, my PhD students and I have published top venue journal/conference papers in EuroSys, TDSC, ATC, NSDI, SOCC, DSN, AsiaCCS, ACSAC, SRDS, TPDS, and JSAC. I received a best paper award on software security from ACSAC 2017. Regarding real-world impact, my PhD students and I have detected five new concurrency attacks in real-world production software, including the latest Linux kernel, MySQL, Apache, SSDB. These attacks makes industries (e.g., RedHat, Android, and Ubuntu) fix most severe security vulnerabilities immediately in numerous deployed Linux instances. For instance, CVE-2017-7533, a Linux root privilege escalation attack firstly detected by my Owl [IEEE DSN 2018] project in Jul 2017 and reported to RedHat, made most Linux vendors (e.g., RedHat, Android, and Ubuntu) patch all their deployed OS instances between Linux-3.14 (released in Mar 2014) and Linux-4.12 (released in Jul 2017) immediately in Jul 2017. CVE-2017-12193, another Linux kernel panic attack firstly detected by Owl [IEEE DSN 2018] in Nov 2017, again, made almost all these Linux vendors patch all their deployed OS instances between Linux-3.13 (released in Jan 2014) and Linux-4.13 (released in Sep 2017) immediately in Nov 2017. Due to the extreme severity of CVE-2017-12193, Mr. Linus Torvalds, the father of Linux, worked with my research team via emails to generate the patch.

27202516.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202516.value: Thermoelectric materials are extremely attractive to energy industries due to their ability to directly convert heat into electricity. While these materials are being considered for practical applications such as waste heat recovery system in vehicles, large-scale deployment requires improvements in energy conversion efficiency. Unprecedentedly high thermoelectric efficiency has recently been discovered in distorted rock-salt crystal SnSe. This efficiency has been found to come primarily from its intrinsic ultra-low thermal conductivity, which is attributable to the strong lattice anharmonicity. Follow-up theoretical studies have failed to reproduce the thermal conductivity of SnSe; experimental result is overestimated by more than 2.5 times from the theory. With conventional theoretical approaches, anharmonic interactions can be calculated up to the third order, nonetheless, the large discrepancy between theory and experiment indicates that higher-order terms are crucial for SnSe due to its giant lattice anharmonicity. To solve this thermal transport problem, more sophisticated approaches need to be developed. On the other hand, alloying effects have been shown to be extremely important in manipulating the transport properties of thermoelectric materials. The alloying effects on SnSe have been studied only for a few elements including S, Te, I and Ag, while the mechanisms remain mysterious due to the lack of understanding of the compound’s intrinsic thermal transport. In the proposed project, we will calculate the anharmonic interactions in SnSe beyond conventional third-order approximation based on our newly proposed slave-mode method. A new set of slave-mode expansions, i.e., variables that transform like irreducible representations of the point group and satisfy free space homogeneity, will be developed for SnSe to allow accurate calculations of anharmonic interactions beyond the cubic terms. Electronic and bipolar contributions to thermal conductivity as well as alloying effects will also be investigated from first-principles calculations. Following the theoretical study, we will carry out experimental measurements on thermal conductivity and Hall mobility to provide validations. In addition, electrical conductivity and Seebeck coefficient of selected SnSe alloys will be measured to obtain the thermoelectric figure of merit. The aim of this project is to carry out in-depth investigation of lattice anharmonicity in SnSe and to explore the alloying effects on its thermal and electrical transports. The established slave-mode expansions will be readily applicable to other IV-VI compounds with similar distorted rock-salt crystal structure. Deeper understanding of the transport behaviors of SnSe based alloys will pave the way for new engineering strategies to enhance the thermoelectric performance. 熱電材料由於可以將熱能直接轉換為電能，因此在能源領域受到廣泛重視。汽車運行過程中產生的大量廢棄熱能有望通過熱電材料加以回收再利用，然而由於熱電材料的能量轉換效率較低，目前仍然無法實現大規模應用。最新研究發現斜方晶系SnSe具有極高的熱電能量轉換效率。實驗上所得到的SnSe優異的熱電性能主要歸咎於該材料強烈的晶格非簡諧性與極低的熱導率。然而進一步研究發現，熱導率的理論計算值遠高於實驗測量值。理論和實驗之間的明顯差異表明理論計算所基於的三階近似並不足以描述SnSe中強烈的晶格非簡諧性。為了使計算更加合理，現有的理論方法需要進一步發展。大量研究結果表明通過摻雜合金元素可以有效地調控熱電材料的輸運性質。合金元素對SnSe的影響目前仍然缺乏系統的認識；已有的報道包括了S、Te、I和Ag的摻雜效應。由於SnSe中的熱傳導機制尚缺乏理論解釋，因此合金元素的調控效應也有待進一步深入研究。 在此項目中，我們將基於新發展的slave-mode方法研究SnSe中的非簡諧相互作用。通過對SnSe構建滿足其晶格點群對稱性與空間平移、旋轉對稱性的slave-mode變量，我們將計算原子間的高階非簡諧相互作用。此外，我們還將通過第一性原理計算電子與雙極熱導率並研究合金元素的摻雜效應。理論計算的可靠性將通過與熱導率以及霍爾遷移率的實驗測量值進行對比驗證。為了獲得摻雜SnSe體系的熱電能量轉換效率，特定合金體系的電導率與塞貝克系數也將從實驗測量中得到。此項目旨在研究SnSe中的晶格非簡諧振動並探索合金元素摻雜對其熱電輸運性能的影響。基於SnSe構建的slave-mode展開式將同樣適用於IV-VI族中其它屬於斜方晶系的化合物。對SnSe合金體系輸運性質的深入理解將為進一步提升熱電材料的能量轉換效率奠定基礎。

27202516.label: Realisation of objectives
27202516.value: Objective 1: We have performed lattice dynamics calculations for SnSe using the small displacement method and density functional theory and obtained the phonon dispersions. We have also implemented a computational scheme which allows the calculation of phonon lifetimes originated from three phonon and four phonon scatterings. Lattice dynamics at elevated temperatures are studied by calculating the anharmonic interactions up to the fourth order. Phonon spectra including the coupling effects are obtained based on perturbation theory and molecular dynamics simulations. Lattice thermal conductivity of SnSe have been calculated using the Boltzmann transport equation based on the relaxation time approximation. Our theoretical results are in good agreement with experimental measurements. Furthermore, molecular dynamics simulations based on accurate machine learning interatomic potentials have been performed. The phonon lifetimes obtained from perturbation theory and molecular dynamics are carefully compared and the origins of anharmonic interactions and their contributions to the lattice thermal conductivity are identified. Objective 2: The effects of various alloying elements including some of the boron group, the carbon group and the pnictogen group elements on the electronic structures and transport properties of SnSe have been studied from first-principles calculations. It is found that Sb induces a significant improvement of the normalized power-factor along the out-of-plane direction. The improvement originates from the coexistence of resonant states and additional electrical conductive pathways. The enhancement of the electrical transport properties also leads to an increase of the electronic component of the thermal conductivity. Laser flash experiments have been performed to study the thermal conductivities of SnSe based alloys across a wide temperature range. The lattice and electronic components of the thermal conductivity have been obtained. The suppressed thermal transport of SnSe is found to be related to the strong bonding anisotropy and lattice anharmonicity. Seebeck coefficients, electrical conductivity and Hall coefficients of SnSe alloys have been experimentally measured to determine the thermoelectric figure of merit as a function of temperature.

27202516.label: Major findings and research outcome
27202516.value: A theoretical scheme which allows the computation of four phonon scattering rates from first principles has been successfully implemented, enabling in-depth investigations of anharmonic lattice dynamics at elevated temperatures. We have also found that the interaction between the px orbitals of tin and those of the pnictogen group elements induce obvious resonant states and significant charge delocalization near the conduction band minimum, resulting in simultaneous enhancements of Seebeck coefficient and electrical conductivity in the out-of-plane direction of n-type SnSe. This insight provides an important guideline for designing efficient SnSe based thermoelectric materials. We also found that there is a relatively non-dispersive valence band valley in SnSe, while this feature does not exist in the closely related SnS compound. We demonstrated that the suppressed lattice thermal transport and the electronic structure features of SnSe alloys facilitate the realization of high thermoelectric efficiency.

27202516.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27202516.value: Four phonon scatterings have been found to be important for the lattice thermal transport in strongly anharmonic materials. However, most of the existing studies of thermoelectric materials, which usually have low thermal conductivity and strong phonon scatterings, only include anharmonicity up to the third order. Further consideration of four phonon scatterings may be critical for a more complete understanding of the lattice dynamics and better designs for enhanced thermoelectric efficiencies.

27202516.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27202516.value: A large amount of energy is wasted in the form of heat in various industrial processes. Efficient recycling of the wasted thermal energy is thus critical for enhancing energy efficiency. Thermoelectric materials can convert heat into electricity or vice versa, and they have attracted significant research interest for their potential applications in waste heat recycling. In this project, we study the fundamental thermal and electrical transport mechanisms of SnSe, and design alloys to enhance its thermal energy conversion efficiency.

27203016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27203016.value: It is expected that the total number of buildings in Hong Kong will reach 58,000 in 2050. Existing buildings aged from 5 to 35 years are nearly 75% of the total buildings, and more than 2000 buildings in Hung Hom area are over 50 years old. The existing buildings have been operated and maintained using traditional Operations and Maintenance (O&M) strategies and methods. However, building O&M has been notoriously known for its inefficient and ineffective practice, which often causes tragic accidents, and is consequently unsatisfactory to building occupants and owners. The industry has started to recognize that the ineffective and inefficient O&M could be addressed by adopting state-of-the-art computing technologies currently available in the market. Building Information Modeling (BIM) provides an intelligent digital platform, aiming to support activities throughout the building lifecycle, and has been frequently used for new building construction projects. Despite growing use of BIM and improvement in as-is information recording technologies, information used to operate and maintain existing buildings is often incomplete or even incorrect, not to mention the lack of meaningful building information models. As-is BIM modeling for existing buildings and updating the models thereafter is considered to be a time-consuming process that requires great effort, high cost and skilled workers. This research aims at investigating and developing an integrated approach to highly efficiently construct as-is BIM models of existing buildings in Hong Kong at low cost. The research will extensively investigate technologies available to process diverse types of building data and develop mechanisms to extract necessary data and effectively integrate them to construct an as-is BIM model of the target building. The functional performance of the proposed approach will be evaluated using a set of representative types of university buildings. The primary implication of this research is to improve efficiency and effectiveness of O&M and emergency responses, and furthermore support refurbishment of a building by enabling O&M personnel and owners to construct, update and use a BIM model of their buildings in a cost-effective manner and access BIM-based state-of-the-art O&M tools, including the possibility of integrating the proposed system with computational maintenance management systems and big data analytics platforms for further effective monitoring of the performance and conditions of their facilities. Knowledge gained from this research and the design of the computational system proposed in this research will form a solid foundation and a computational platform for researchers to further develop their own computational systems. 2050年香港建築總量預計將達到58,000幢。其中，房齡在5到35年的既有建築數量將占建築總量的75%；在紅磡區，房齡超過50年的建築數量將超過2000幢。目前，既有建築的運營管理與維護大多採用傳統的策略和方法。然而，此種方法效率低下且存在發生安全意外的隱患，故而常導致業主及住戶對此表示十分不滿。建築行業開始採用市場上先進的計算機技術來解決建築運營管理及維護效率低下的問題。 建築信息模型技術（BIM）为建築生命週期各項建造管理活動提供了一個智能數字平臺。該技術已廣泛應用於新建建築中。針對既有建築，雖然越來越多的建築項目開始採用BIM並積極開發現有信息記錄和維護技術，但是建築運營管理與維護中的信息缺失甚至錯誤的問題仍然十分严重。目前，既有建築普遍缺乏可實際使用的、有“意義”的建築信息模型。此外，為既有建築重建“基於現狀”的BIM模型或者持續更新現有BIM模型也被認為是費時、費力、高成本並需要專業技術人員支持的複雜過程。 因此，本研究旨在開發高效、低成本的、适用于香港既有建築的 BIM 模型的綜合重建方法。本研究將全面分析可處理不同種類建築信息的現有技術方法，進開發新的建築信息提取機制，通過現有技術與新機制的有效結合，實現既有建築 BIM 模型的高效、低成本的重建。此外，本研究還將選取有代表性的學校建築來驗證此綜合方法的作用和效果。 本研究主要意義在於：使建築運營管理維護人員和業主能夠高效率、低成本的重建、更新和使用 BIM 模型，為基於 BIM 的先進建築運營管理維護工具的開發提供基礎（如在本研究提出的“基於現狀” BIM 重建技術基礎上，整合可計算的建築運營維護系統和大數據分析平臺，可實現建築設施的狀態和性能的有效監測），從而提高建築運營管理以及應急響應的有效性，並為建築翻新工程提供決策和技術支持。此外，本研究成果和相關計算系統的開發還將為日後相關領域的研究提供堅實的理論基礎和技術平臺支持。

27203016.label: Realisation of objectives
27203016.value: Despite the growing use of BIM for new construction projects in recent years, most existing buildings today often do not have complete as-is information documents, nor existed meaningful BIM. Thus, incomplete or even incorrect information in as-is records is still one of the main reasons for the low efficiency in facilities management for existing buildings. To better understand the practice and major problems of as-is BIM implementation in building O&M, the study first conducted a comprehensive and comparative analysis of the current building O&M practice without and with BIM assists in a systematic and dynamic way based on the activity theory. The study then identified the drivers with recommendations to facilitate the implementation of BIM in O&M. Two process models under different statuses (i.e., without BIM and with BIM) have been established, and the corresponding activity system models (ASMs) have been established for the two statuses. Moreover, the ASM-based driver model of evolution has been developed to clearly depict the mechanism of how the internal and external drivers trigger and accelerate the transition from the traditional O&M to the BIMassisted O&M. Furthermore, 26 primary contradictions have been identified, which were represented as the readiness of factors and explained by the readiness of information as the internal drivers within elements, and 6 secondary contradictions have been identified and examined as the external drivers between elements. With the context of social, political, and technical influences, the study has proposed 21 recommendations based on ASM from the general to specific perspectives, which can further enhance and intensify the determined drivers of evolution. These recommendations aim to achieve successful BIM-assisted O&M eventually. Next, since as-is BIM modeling for existing buildings is a time-consuming and expensive process, which requires great effort, time, cost and skilled workers, it is essential to develop convenient, efficient and economical approaches with high accuracy in order to construct an as-is BIM for effective O&M of existing buildings. This study categorized and analyzed the state-of-the-art technologies in image-based BIM construction processes in different areas (i.e., image processing, computer vision, and applications of those technologies in civil engineering). A general framework for image-based as-is BIM construction processes has been developed with the following key steps: 1) data capturing and processing; 2) object recognition; and 3) as-is BIM modeling. Detailed comparative analyses of methods commonly used in each step were conducted and a prospective model has been proposed. Based on the prospective model, knowledge gaps and future development of image-based as-is BIM construction processes have been identified. Following are some of the lessons learned during this study: 1) data capturing processes should be at low cost and user-friendly since few O&M workers are properly trained to understand the technologies and can use the tools developed based on the technologies; 2) managing data (i.e., fill in missing data and filter noisy data) in an effective way is an important concern because as-is data from existing buildings may be incomplete and/or cluttered; 3) decision making in the object recognition step requires methods designed to work in different use case scenarios in civil engineering; 4) full automation of as-built/asis BIM construction is imperative but still remained as one of major challenges. The image-based as-is BIM construction processes identified from the first objective is adopted for the development of the image-driven integrated system proposed in this study. Two independent systems have been developed to construct as-is IFC BIM for existing buildings. The first system is semi-automated and uses images collected by handheld cameras and existing CAD drawings as inputs. Three modules have been developed. The building framework construction module (Module 1) supports to construct building framework and extract structural geometry information, and further provide the coordinate system of constructing IFC BIM from CAD drawings using OCR techniques and the mathematical morphology theory. The building information complementary module (Module 2) has two sub-systems, namely the NFS-based object recognition subsystem and the material recognition sub-system, based on the image classification procedures and the texture library. Specifically, 31 fuzzy rules with membership functions generated by the training process of sample images in NFS were implemented as a critical process in the as-is BIM generation, and the system performance has been evaluated in terms of accuracy and robustness. The information integration and IFC BIM creation module (Module 3) integrates the information from Module 1 and Module 2 and then automatically transforms recognized objects with materials and location information into the complete IFC BIM. This semi-automated system systematically streamlines the process of constructing as-is IFC BIM from images and CAD drawings. It has been proved to be robust and effective enough to create as-is IFC BIM through constructing building framework and further enriching building objects even encountering the changes of surroundings or under complex environments with poorly-textured features. The second system is fully automated and consumes digital images of buildings and associated “location” data collected by a cost-effective data collection equipment system specifically developed. This system also consists of three modules. The Mask R-CNN-based building object segmentation module automatically recognize and segment all building component instances contained in each building image and then extract their surface geometry information. The building surface model (BSM) creation module automatically merge all the building component instances segmented from the first module into a complete BSM in a same coordinate system by using the collected “location” data of each image. The semantic enrichment module further automatically enriches the BSM with all semantic information required by the IFC specifications and geometric modeling requirements of building energy models and finally generate a syntactically valid IFC BIM. Last, the study demonstrated the usage of as-is BIM in supporting the intelligent operations and maintenance of existing buildings, taking building energy modeling (BEM) for energy retrofits of existing buildings as an example. This objective is achieved by the developed IFC BIM-to-BEM geometry transformation (IBGT) system, which consists of two essential parts: a novel IBGT approach and a rule-based IFC second-level SB validation system. The IBGT approach provides a highly practical solution to transform an IFC model to an EnergyPlus IDF model for energy simulation. It consists of three successive steps: 1) pre-processing an input IFC model by detecting and faceting curved objects that are essential to BEM; 2) generating second-level space boundaries (SBs), which are the exact geometric data required by BEM, from the pre-processed IFC model; and 3) converting the generated IFC second-level SBs into a building energy model in the EnergyPlus IDF format. This approach is featured by: 1) tolerating certain geometric errors and building object classification errors that commonly exist in IFC models; 2) enabling the transformation of IFC curved building objects that are essential to BEM; and 3) high efficiency to process very large-scale IFC models by using the algorithmic strategy of multiple geometry representations (MGRs). The developed SB validation system provides an automatic, reliable, and user-friendly means to validate second-level SBs in an IFC model systematically and rigorously.

27203016.label: Major findings and research outcome
27203016.value: Despite the growing use of BIM for new construction projects in recent years, most existing buildings today often do not have complete as-is information documents, nor existed meaningful BIM. Thus, incomplete or even incorrect information in as-is records is still one of the main reasons for the lowlevel efficiency in facilities management for existing buildings. Furthermore, as-is BIM modeling for existing buildings is a time-consuming and expensive process, which requires great effort, time, costs, and skilled workers. Convenient, efficient, and economical approaches with high accuracy to construct an as-is BIM would be essentially the foremost step for effective operations and maintenance of existing buildings. This study investigated and developed a highly efficient and lowcost mechanism to construct as-is building information models to support the intelligent operations and maintenance of existing buildings, especially focusing on energy-related use-case scenarios. To pursue this aim, this research was conducted to achieve the following outcomes successfully. The study developed detailed processes and corresponding computing systems equipped with a set of mechanisms for the construction of as-is BIM objects with their meanings and information. Two independent image-driven integrated systems have been developed to construct as-is IFC BIM for existing buildings. The first system is semi-automated and uses images collected by handheld cameras and existing CAD drawings as inputs. It consists of the NFS-based object recognition module, the material recognition module based on the image classification procedures and the texture library, and the information integration & IFC BIM creation module that first integrates the information from the two sub-systems and then automatically transforms recognized objects with materials and location information into the complete IFC BIM. The second system is fully automated and consumes digital images of buildings and associated “location” data collected by a cost-effective data collection equipment system specifically developed. This system also consists of three modules: the Mask RCNN-based building object segmentation module that automatically recognize and segment all building component instances contained in each building image and then extract their surface geometry information, the building surface model (BSM) creation module that automatically merges all the building component instances segmented from the first module into a complete BSM in a same coordinate system by using the collected “location” data of each image, and the semantic enrichment module that further automatically enriches the BSM with all semantic information required by the IFC specifications and BEM geometric modeling requirements and finally generates a syntactically valid IFC BIM.

27203016.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27203016.value: From the aspect of automatically creating a BIM from images and CAD drawings: 1) The Mask R-CNN based building object segmentation approach can be further improved from the perspectives of object recognition accuracy, recognizing more diverse types of building objects and building materials, and developing a more flexible and accurate dimension measure method; 2) The building surface model creation approach can be improved to handle non-flat building element surfaces in arbitrary poses and complex non-rectangular surface shapes; 3) Application areas of the semantic enrichment approach can be extended to other domains. From the aspect of transforming IFC BIM to building surface geometry model: 1) The curved object detection and faceting step can be improved to handle curved building objects defined with a non-footprint based representation (e.g., solid shapes with B-spline surfaces) and building objects that have a footprint bounded by other parametric curves or nonparametric arbitrary curves; 2) The second-level SB enrichment step needs to be improved to handle building elements defined with a collection of components with different materials; 3) The system can be extended to handle transformation of other input data, such as construction material, HVAC systems, and operation schedules, to generate a complete and ready-to-run building energy model.

27203016.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27203016.value: The research aims to investigate and develop a highly efficient and low-cost mechanism to construct as-is building information models to support the intelligent operations and maintenance of existing buildings. To this end, the research first identified current issues of BIM implementation in the O&M phase and analyzed merits and limitations of existing techniques and methods to construct as-is BIMs, especially state-of-the-art technologies and algorithms to construct BIM by processing images. Then, the research developed a framework for image-based as-is BIM construction process with the following steps: data capturing and processing, object recognition, BIM modeling, and enriching the BIM model with semantic information. The research further implemented the framework by developing detailed processes and corresponding computing systems equipped with a set of mechanisms for the construction of as-is BIM objects. The research demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed system in supporting the intelligent O&M of existing buildings, taking building energy modeling for energy retrofits of existing buildings as a representative use-case study. The research has significant implications for BIM-assisted O&M by providing both researchers and practitioners with a consolidated way to have more detailed insight into constructing asis BIMs for existing buildings and promote the evolution to the BIM-assisted O&M

27300616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27300616.value: 当今科学和工程中的一类重要研究课题是通过建立数学模型来描述复杂的现象。人们通常利用偏微分方程来建立数学模型从而进行数值模拟，例如波动、热量和污染物在不均匀多孔介质中的传播，由随机外力驱动的流动问题等等。人们假设在这些数学模型中，偏微分方程的方程系数、求解区域、初始条件和/或边界条件、以及源项都已经完全确定，然后进行数值计算。然而在实际应用中，人们从来无法完全得到这些信息。例如，在油藏数值模拟中，工程师们只能得到非常有限的关于多孔介质的测量数据，比如渗透率，孔隙度和毛细管属性。因此，油藏模型中存在很大的不确定性。 量化分析这些偏微分方程模型中的不确定性因素、以及它们对模型预测量的影响，可以帮助人们作出更好的决策。不确定性量化正逐渐变为一个热门研究领域，来研究和解决这类问题。 随机偏微分方程，是偏微分方程的自然推广。由于带有随机变量或随机过程，它可以被用来模拟更加复杂的具有不确定性的现象。在过去的几十年中，在数学家的不懈努力下，随机偏微分方程的数值计算领域有了快速发展。然而，高维随机偏微分方程的数值计算仍然是一个很具有挑战性的课题。 最近几年，通过探索高维问题中蕴含的低维结构，从而设计更加有效的数值算法，引起了人们的广泛关注。利用这类想法，人们设计出了很多计算稳态随机偏微分方程和扩散占优的时间演化随机偏微分方程的方法。然而，对于对流占优和具有多尺度特征的随机偏微分方程的计算方法却发展很缓慢。本质困难在于，由于对流作用、非线性作用、以及多尺度相互作用，问题的解空间增长很快。当我们需要计算问题的长时间解时，问题变得更加困难、更具挑战性。 在这个研究课题中，针对以上指出的若干研究难点，我们旨在研究对流占优和多尺度型随机流体问题的高效数值计算方法。此外，我们将对这些新算法的收敛性和稳定性进行分析。最后，我们将对一些来自工程的模型问题，包括两相流在非均质多孔介质中的流动和燃烧的传播，进行数值模拟，以评估我们的新算法的计算精度和有效性。 我们期待着这个课题的研究结果能够为当前的随机偏微分方程的计算领域提供一些新的算法。利用这些新算法，科学家和工程师们可以在数值模拟工程领域中解决很多具有挑战性的问题，例如油藏数值模拟以及湍流燃烧模拟。这项研究课题的顺利完成能够在快速发展的不确定性量化研究领域做出一些新的贡献。

27300616.label: Realisation of objectives
27300616.value: We have made tremendous efforts for the objectives proposed in this project, and are very pleased that the objectives of the proposal are fully achieved. Nine papers have been published. We developed several very efficient numerical methods to solve multiscale elliptic PDEs with random coefficients, including the cluster-based generalized multiscale finite element method [2], optimization-based model reduction method [4], asymptotic expansions method [5], the proper orthogonal decomposition-based method [8], and multiscale multilevel Monte Carlo based method [9]. We also develop efficient numerical methods to solve time-dependent SPDEs, including the adaptive dynamically low-dimensional approximation method for multiscale stochastic diffusion equations [3], proper orthogonal decomposition method to nonlinear filtering problems [6], where we solved a Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation. We have studied the numerical accuracy, convergence, and stability of the proposed numerical methods. For example, in [4] we obtained the convergence analysis of the proposed model reduction method and in [1] we got the convergence of the model reduction method in computing eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of Schrodinger equations. Moreover, we also use our methods to study some application problems arising from engineering. For example, in [7], we developed a numerical method to estimate exciton diffusion lengths of organic semiconductors in random domains, which is a very important research topic in material science, and in [6] we used our model reduction method to solve nonlinear filtering problems, which is very useful in tracking and signal processing. Some research outputs were presented by PI and his student in their invited talks at five international conferences. One Ph.D. student, Mr. Dingjiong Ma, was trained with support from the project.

27300616.label: Major findings and research outcome
27300616.value: We have developed several efficient numerical methods to solve some typical model problems arising from the uncertainty quantification, i.e., multiscale elliptic PDEs with random coefficients and time-dependent SPDE problems. Moreover, we studied the convergence and stability of the proposed numerical methods. Multiscale elliptic PDEs with random coefficients have many applications, such as reservoir simulation and composite material simulation. Due to the multiscale and random features in the problems, it requires tremendous computational resources to solve them. By exploring low-dimensional structures in the solution space, we propose several model reduction methods to solve them efficiently. In [4], we developed an optimization approach to construct a set of localized multiscale data-driven stochastic basis functions that give an optimal approximation property of the solution operator. In addition, we provide rigorous convergence analysis for our method and verify it by numerical experiments. In [8], we proposed a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) based method to address the same challenging problem. By studying the continual dependence of the solution on the coefficient of the elliptic operator, we give guidance on how to choose samples in constructing POD basis functions, in order to guarantee the accuracy of the model reduction method. We find that many time-dependent high-dimensional SPDE problems have certain low-dimensional structures, e.g., in the sense of Karhunen-Loeve expansion, which suggests the existence of reduced-order models and better formulations for efficient numerical methods. Based on this observation, we developed an adaptive dynamically low-dimensional approximation method to solve multiscale stochastic diffusion equations [3] and proper orthogonal decomposition method to solve Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation. The latter provides a very efficient method to solve nonlinear filtering problems [6]. We also study some application problems arising from engineering that involve uncertainty quantification. Specifically, we developed numerical methods to estimate exciton diffusion lengths of organic semiconductors in random domains, which plays a vital role in the function of optoelectronic devices [7]. We find that when one uses a random field to model the uncertainty in the domain boundary, the correlation length of randomness is important to determine whether a 1D reduced model is a good surrogate for the 2D model. This discovery suggests that for some materials where both small molecules and polymers can form crystal structures, exciton diffusion can be well described by the 1D model, but for other organic materials with low crystalline order, the reduced 1D model is not sufficiently accurate for diffusion length estimation.

27300616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27300616.value: Based on this project, there are several possible research problems in the future: (1) develop efficient model reduction methods to solve other types of PDEs where the regularity of the solution is not as smooth as the elliptic PDEs, such as wave propagation in random media (e.g. Helmholtz equation with random refractive index) and semiclassical Schrodinger equation with random potential; (2) develop adaptive low-dimensional approximation methods to solve nonlinear problems, such as stochastic Burgers equation or stochastic Navier-Stokes equation with small diffusion parameter; (3) reduce the computational cost in solving the inverse problem (using the Bayesian framework), since our methods can be viewed as fast solvers for the forward problems.

27300616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27300616.value: Stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), which contain randomness in terms of random variables or stochastic processes, provide a powerful tool to model complex phenomena with uncertainties. e.g. wave, heat, and pollutant propagation through a heterogeneous porous medium, and flow driven by stochastic force. In this project, by exploring the intrinsic low-dimensional structures in the solutions, we have developed several efficient numerical methods to solve multiscale elliptic PDEs with random coefficients and time-dependent SPDE problems. Moreover, we provide rigorous convergence and stability analysis for these new methods and conduct numerical simulations to verify the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed methods. With these new methods, we can compute many challenging real-world problems, such as reservoir simulation. By solving multiscale elliptic PDEs with random coefficients, we can analyze the uncertainties in the reservoir models and to quantify the influence of the randomness in the permeability filed on the oil production, and help engineers make better decisions. Therefore, the results obtained in this project will have a broad scientific impact on the fast-developing UQ field.

27301816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27301816.value: Particle physics is the study of fundamental particles and their interactions. Fundamental particles are basic elements of matter and fundamental force carriers. The standard model (SM) describing the law of the fundamental particles and their interactions has been very successful in explaining and predicting various experimental results. However, it is not the ultimate theory of particle physics because it fails to answer some fundamental questions: What is the cause of electroweak symmetry breaking? Can strong, weak and electromagnetic forces be unified? What are dark matter and dark energy? Why is there more matter than anti-matter in the universe? In order to answer these questions, new physics is required. Supersymmetry (SUSY) is one of the most promising new physics theory because it overcomes many of the SM’s limitations. in addition, other new physics models such as models with an extended Higgs sector or extra dimensions, are also proposed to address the open questions in the SM A particle accelerator, a very important tool in particle physics, is to produce the heavy fundamental particles. In a scientific breakthrough in 2012, the Higgs boson was discovered at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the world’s largest and highest-energy particle accelerator, which is located at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). Since that discovery, searching for new physics has been the primary task of the LHC. The PI proposes to perform searches for new physics in final states with the same-sign lepton pairs using data to be collected from the ATLAS experiment during Run II of the LHC (from 2015 to 2017). 粒子物理是一門研究基本粒子以及它們之間相互作用的學科。基本粒子能夠組成物質以及傳播基本作用力。 粒子物理標準模型成功描述了基本粒子以及相互作用的物理定律，並且它預言了很多實驗結果。但是， 標準模型因為不能夠解釋一些基本問題，所以還不是一個完備的理論，例如什麼是電弱破缺德起源？強弱和電磁作用力是否能被統一？什麼是暗物質和暗能量？ 為什麼宇宙中的物質比反物質跟多？我們需要在新物理中尋找答案。超對稱物理模型以及一些其他的新物理模型因為能夠解釋標準物理模型不能夠解釋的問題成為粒子物理研究的熱點。 粒子加速器是一個能夠幫助我們尋找這些新物理模型預言的基本粒子的工具。 在2012年希格斯粒子在世界上最大的粒子加速器，位於歐洲核子中心的大型強子對撞機上被發現。尋找新物理是大型強子對撞機的重要任務。 本研究計劃是利用大型強子對撞機的ATLAS實驗RUN II收集的數據中在一對同電荷輕子末態尋找新粒子。

27301816.label: Realisation of objectives
27301816.value: 1. To search for SUSY in a final state with same-sign lepton pairs and missing transverse energy with data to be collected by the ATLAS detector during Run II of the LHC. We published a journal paper “Search for chargino and neutralino production in final states with a Higgs boson and missing transverse momentum at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector” Phys. Rev. D 100 (2019) 012006. Charginos and neutralinos are the mass eigenstates formed of linear superpositions of the SUSY partners of the Higgs and of the electroweak gauge bosons. Before the spontaneous breaking of the electroweak symmetry, these correspond to the charged and the neutral higgsinos, the charged and the neutral winos and the bino, collectively known as the electroweakinos. Naturalness requires the lighter chargino and neutralinos (and both partners of the top quark and one of the bottom quark partners) to have masses in the hundreds of GeV range. Recent searches of sparticles produced at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) via strong interactions suggest that first and second generation squark masses and the gluino masses are larger than 1 TeV, while the third generation squark masses are excluded over ranges of several hundreds of GeV, but still allowed for masses below the TeV-level. In this case, the direct production of electroweak gauginos may be the dominant SUSY process at the LHC. We deliver a search for electroweak gauginos with final states containing two same-sign leptons. We find that backgrounds to this search are dominated by fake leptons, which are estimated via a data-driven matrix method. The irreducible background is dominated by diboson processes, in particular WZ. These background processes, taken from Monte Carlo simulation, are validated in validation regions which show a good agreement with data. Two signal regions separated in jet multiplicity are defined in an event-cut-based analysis. The event selections are optimized according to the signal efficiency. To derive limits, a simultaneous model-dependent fit in the two signal regions is performed. The resulting CLs values are obtained, which are combined with the results of the other searching channel e.g. 3 lepton channel. 2. To search for heavy Higgs bosons in a final state with same-sign lepton pairs, jets and missing transverse energy with data to be collected by the ATLAS detector during Run II of the LHC. We have setup an analysis team to search for the associated production of a heavy (pseudo)scalar Higgs boson A/H with a top-antitop quark pair with the subsequent decay A/H→ttbar leading to a 4-top final state. The same-sign lepton pair final state is our focus. Multivariate techniques are used to enhance the sensitivity of the search in the mass region between 400 and 1000 GeV. The search is on-going using full ATLAS Run II data. My post-doc Daniela Paredes Hernandez is the analysis contact. We aim for a paper publish early next year. 3. To perform studies on other searches with similar or related final states at the high luminosity LHC. With a higher luminosity, we also extend our studies to an analysis with similar final state. We published a journal paper “Search for squarks and gluinos in final states with same-sign leptons and jets using 139 fb−1 of data collected with the ATLAS detector" JHEP 06 (2020) 46. Final states with two same-sign leptons or three leptons and multiple jets are sensitive to a variety of new physics scenarios. In supersymmetric models in particular, such final states can be produced in the decays of heavy superpartners involving massive gauge bosons, sleptons or top quarks. Depending on the nature of the particles accompanying the leptons in the final states, a large variety of signatures can be obtained, notably in terms of the numbers of jets and b-tagged jets in the final state. We chose to illustrate the analysis versatility by evaluating its sensitivity to three R-parity-conserving (RPC) SUSY scenarios with the lightest neutralino χ ̃01 as lightest and stable superpartner, featuring gluino, bottom or top squark pair production with various exclusive decay modes, as well as one R-parity-violating (RPV) SUSY scenario with gluino or neutralino decays via violating λ′ couplings. . These scenarios were used as benchmarks to identify regions of the phase space where the analysis can bring particularly useful complementarity to other SUSY searches, and subsequently define our signal regions with a particular focus on these regions. We compared data to SM expectations in five signal regions with various requirements on the number of b-tagged jets, the number of leptons, the missing transverse momentum, and the global energy scale of the event. No significant excess in data over the SM prediction was observed in any of the signal regions, and exclusion limits are set on the masses of gluinos, bottom squarks, top squarks, and neutralinos in four different benchmark scenarios, extending significantly the limits set previously.

27301816.label: Major findings and research outcome
27301816.value: Based on 36.1 fb−1 of sqrt(s) = 13 TeV proton-proton collision data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider, we conduct the search for the electroweak pair production of a chargino and a neutralino pp → χ ̃±1 χ ̃02, where the chargino decays into the lightest neutralino and a W boson, χ ̃±1 → χ ̃01 W, while the neutralino decays into the lightest neutralino and a Standard Model-like 125 GeV Higgs boson, χ ̃02 → hχ ̃01. My group is the primary contributor to the final state with the same-sign lepton pairs which together with fully hadronic, semileptonic, diphoton, and multilepton final states with missing transverse momentum are included in the paper. Higgs bosons in the final state are identified by leptons from the decay modes h → WW, h → ZZ or h → ττ. We find that the observations are consistent with the Standard Model expectations, and 95% confidence-level limits of up to 680 GeV in χ ̃±1 =χ ̃02 mass are set in the context of a simplified supersymmetric model. One Ph.D. student graduated with thesis on this topic. In addition, we also conducted the search for supersymmetric partners of gluons and quarks, involving signatures with jets and either two isolated leptons (electrons or muons) with the same electric charge, or at least three isolated leptons. A data sample of proton–proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV recorded with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider between 2015 and 2018, corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 139 fb−1, is used for the search. No significant excess over the Standard Model expectation is observed. The results are interpreted in simplified supersymmetric models featuring both R-parity conservation and R-parity violation, raising the exclusion limits beyond those of previous ATLAS searches to 1600 GeV for gluino masses and 750 GeV for bottom and top squark masses in these scenarios.

27301816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27301816.value: My research group joined the ATLAS as a new group in 2014. We build up our strengths on searching for new physics in the final state with same-sign lepton pair via the analyses mentioned above. We are carrying out a couple of analyses in this channel including searching for SUSY particles and heavy Higgs. Based on our previous experiences, we will further improve background estimate, introduce Multivariate analysis and reduce systematic uncertainties. We will update relevant searches with more ATLAS data and improved analysis strategies. We also plan to develop more new physics searches in the similar final state since we have accumulated experiences in this channel. More publications are expected in the coming years.

27301816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27301816.value: The standard model (SM) describing the fundamental particles and their interactions has been very successful in explaining and predicting various experimental results. However, it is not the ultimate theory of particle physics because it fails to answer some fundamental questions. Many new models that extend the SM have been proposed, of which Supersymmetry (SUSY) models are the most promising extensions. Our research target in this project is to search for super particles predicted by the SUSY, which can provide good opportunity to answer some open questions in the SM. For example, the lightest neutralinos could be dark matter candidates. We are also motived by generating extra CP-phases to explain matter and anti-matter asymmetry in the universe, and unifying the three fundamental forces. Though we have not found those new particles so far, our results provide the best constraints on the mass of the super particles under study in the involved searching channels. The results will guide relevant theory and experiment in future.

27302016.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27302016.value: In the past decade, several key processes of global society, such as communication, transport, media and defense, have turned digital. Companies, individuals and governments routinely collect massive amounts of structured and unstructured data--text, images, videos, bookmarks, links--and this is done at unprecedented scales. Moreover, with advances in technology, it is becoming increasingly cheaper to collect and store raw data. All of these changes have brought us into the era of Big Data, which brims with both challenges and opportunities. Extracting information and insights from data has the potential to inform and enrich numerous aspects of our daily lives, and to affect fundamental processes in science, industry, business, social media, healthcare and defense. For the opportunities to bear some fruit, we must be able to transform the data into information--and this needs to be done at scales never encountered before. Many information extraction problems of interest can be cast as optimization problems and solved by optimization algorithms. However, traditional optimization algorithms relying on expensive iterations are not scalable to handle data of today's magnitude. Coordinate algorithms have attracted much attention in recent years due to their wide success in various data-driven application fields, including especially computational statistics and machine learning. Although the coordinate approach has been in use for many years among some practitioners, a systematic study on theoretical convergence analysis only emerged very recently. The deeper understanding helped a great deal in the development of many improvements and new variants of coordinate methods, featuring in particular randomized coordinate methods. The current study of randomized coordinate methods is mostly limited to problems with separable constraints. However, problems with non-separable constraints can be found in many data-related applications, such as the support vector machine (SVM) problem, which is broadly used in classification. Besides, the randomization has been invariably assumed to have the same distribution throughout the iterations, while it is unlikely that we should use the same distribution when we are close to the solution as in the beginning of the algorithm. Furthermore, the existing randomized block coordinate methods all separate the space into non-overlapping blocks of subspaces, which in all likelihood is not the optimal way to deal with huge-scale and badly conditioned problems. This project aims to address the above three issues. More precisely, the PI proposes to develop randomized coordinate methods for a more general class of problems, using adaptive sampling distribution and overlapping block of coordinates. 随着数字时代的全面到来，过去十年的社会发展产生了相应的变化。采集和存储成本的降低带来了大量的数据：大到政府小至个人，每个社会单元每分钟都在以文本，图像，录像等形式产生或者记录着各种不同的数据。这些变化带领我们进入了充满挑战与机遇的“大数据时代”。如何从纷繁复杂甚至很多时候杂乱无章的数据中提取可利用的信息，是数据分析中至关重要的一步。提取信息的过程大部分时候是通过建立一个优化模型来实现的。因此，解决数据处理相关的优化问题便自然地成为工业界和科研界共同关心的问题。数据量的增多自然地带来了优化问题规模的扩大。传统的优化方法处理起当今的大规模优化问题时往往有些捉襟见肘。新兴的算法中，随机坐标下降算法在数据处理中表现得尤为突出，因此也得到很多关注。对随机坐标下降算法的研究主要集中在有可分离约束条件的凸优化问题。但是很多数据处理中的问题都带有不可分离约束条件，比如在机器监督学习中广泛应用的支持向量机算法。此外，随机算法中的随机分布普遍是不随迭代变化的。但是很明显固定任何一种随机分布都不会是最优的。另外，随机块坐标算法普遍把空间分为不相交的块，更好的算法应该是允许块与块相交的。这个研究项目主要针对以上提出的三个问题。更具体地说：一，在统一的框架下设计可以解决带有不可分离项的随机坐标法；二，构造随迭代变化的随机分布，提高随机算法的收敛速度；三，研究可相交块随机坐标法。

27302016.label: Realisation of objectives
27302016.value: Achievements: -For the first objective as in the original application, we proposed an inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian framework with explicit inner problem termination rule for composite convex optimization problems. The latter covers the problems involving Lipschitzian, proximable and linear composite terms that are considered in the application. Moreover, it also covers problems with nonlinear composite terms. -For the second objective as in the original application, we developed and analyzed a new family of nonaccelerated and accelerated loopless variance-reduced methods for finite sum optimization problems. Our convergence analysis relies on a novel expected smoothness condition which upper bounds the variance of the stochastic gradient estimation by a constant times a distance-like function. This allows us to handle with ease arbitrary sampling schemes as well as the nonconvex case. -For the third objective as in the original application, we proposed new framework allowing arbitrary linearly convergent inner solver including in particular randomised algorithms, making the resulting framework more scalable facing the ever-increasing problem dimension. The novel methods that we propose achieves the state of the art complexity bound and exhibits superior numerical performance over many existing methods for large-scale problems. Under-achievements: The second objective is not fully achieved. The search of an adaptive sampling strategy requires further study on the convergence properties of the iterates. The approach proposed in the application can lead to some heuristic methods but without rigorous theoretical support.

27302216.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27302216.value: 随机偏微分方程及其相关问题

27302216.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27302216.value: The theory of partial differential equations has had a long history and has been successful in describing a large variety of deterministic dynamical phenomena in different areas, such as physics, chemistry, and so on. In the mid-1960s, by adding noises into partial differential functions, stochastic partial differential equations were introduced to describe dynamics with random influence. The PI proposes to carry out a systematic investigation for a class of stochastic partial differential equations, which describes a variety of phenomena, such as the parabolic Anderson model and the model of directed polymers in random medium. More precisely, the PI plans to investigate the existence and uniqueness of the solutions, obtain (generalized) Feynman-Kac formula for the solutions, and then explore the properties of the solutions. Furthermore, the PI will investigate the rescaled discrete long-range polymers in colored random medium, and then try to deduce a stochastic partial differential equation to describe the continuum long-range directed polymer in colored random medium. The results in this project are expected to contribute to a better understanding of the class of stochastic partial differential equations and the phenomena they describe. 偏微分方程理论已经发展了相当长的时间，它成功描述了包括物理、化学等领域的多种确定性动态系统里的现象。上世纪60年代中叶，为了描述受到随机扰动的动态系统，人们在偏微分方程中引入了随机项，从而产生了随机偏微分方程。 申请人计划对一类随机偏微分方程展开系统的研究。这类方程可以用来解释抛物型的Anderson模型以及在随机环境中的聚合物的行为等随机现象。具体来说，申请人将会研究这类方程解的存在唯一性，方程解的Feynman-Kac公式，以及解的各种性质等。更进一步，申请人计划研究在带颜色噪声的随机环境中聚合物的行为，并试图将其与一类随机偏微分方程建立联系。这项研究的结果预计将会使人们对这一类随机偏微分方程及其相关的现象有一个更好的理解。
