27609816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27609816.value: Driving on the freeway is a daily and often unhealthy activity for tens of millions of people worldwide. The World Health Organization reported road traffic accidents caused approximately 1.24 million deaths worldwide in 2010. This means one person died every 25 seconds. Also, the stress, mental fatigue, and negative moods that drivers often experience can lead to chronic diseases, providing additional burdens on society (Frumkin & Frank, 2004). Although plenty of studies have examined safety issues of freeway systems, they have rarely investigated the impacts of freeway landscapes on drivers' mental states. This setting is especially important because drivers often experience mental fatigue, stress and negative moods on the road. These mental problems can lead to risky driving behaviors, traffic accidents, and chronic diseases. It is plausible that green freeway landscapes may help drivers from mental fatigue, stress, and negative moods, but few empirical studies have proven and quantified their impacts. This lack of knowledge prevents developers, managers, and designers of freeway landscapes from making rational decisions on efficiently using limited public resources to create safe and healthy driving environments. To what extent do various freeway landscapes help drivers recover from mental stress, fatigue, and negative moods? To answer this crucial question, we plan to conduct an experimental study by using the advanced driving simulation technology. We will recruit 208 subjects and randomly assign them to one of 13 simulated driving environments. Each driving environment has an identical freeway infrastructure but a distinctive landscape setting. We will use hormonal, behavioral, physiological, and psychological measures to examine the restoration effects of different freeway landscapes on mental fatigue, stress, and negative mood status. We aim to summarize key physical features of restorative freeway landscapes and provide specific design advice for freeway management and design practice. 對於全球範圍內數千萬計的駕駛員來說，在高速公路駕駛是一項日常卻非健康的行為。世界健康組織報告交通事故在2010年導致約124萬人死亡。這一數字意味著每25秒就有一人死於交通事故。此外，與駕駛相關的慢性疾病已經成為社會的巨大負擔。 儘管有許多的關於高速公路安全性的研究發表，但極少有人關注高速公路景觀對駕駛員精神狀況的影響。理論上高速公路景觀可能非常重要，因為駕駛員常常經歷精神疲勞、壓力、和負面情緒的困擾。這些精神問題會導致冒險性的駕駛行為、交通事故、和慢性疾病。綠色景觀理應能夠幫助駕駛員舒緩這些精神問題，但並沒有實證研究證實這一猜測并將其效應量化。這一知識的匱乏將阻止高速公路開發者、管理者、設計師就如何高效地運用有限的公共資源來創造安全和健康的駕駛環境做出理性的決定。 不同類型的高速公路景觀在何種程度能夠幫助駕駛員舒緩精神疲勞、壓力、和不良情緒？為了回答這個關鍵的問題，我們計劃開展一項基於模擬駕駛技術的實驗性研究項目。我們將征集208位志願者（普通市民）參與測試。每一位受測者會被隨機分配到13種不同的駕駛環境中的一種進行模擬駕駛。每一個駕駛環境由一個相同的高速公路基礎設施和一種特定的綠色景觀環境組成。我們會使用荷爾蒙類、行為類、生理類、心理類的測量方式來研判每種駕駛環境對駕駛員的精神疲勞、壓力、和負面情緒水平地影響。我們期望總結出關鍵的有助於精神舒緩的特征景觀，并為高速公路管理和設計實踐提供具體的建議。

27609816.label: Realisation of objectives
27609816.value: The project has been fully completed. 1. The first objective has been fully achieved. We successfully built up a simulated freeway loop (40 km) with different types of the curbside landscape; We used multiple devices to measure drivers' mental states and driving performance when they were assigned to drive in different freeway environments, including eye-tracking device, automatic and continuous record of driving performance by the OpenDS system (software installed on the driving machine) , salivary cortisol, EKG, and self-reported driving performance and mental states. 2. The second objective has been fully achieved. We found the green landscape has a significantly more positive impact on driving performance and mental states, which clearly demonstrate the health benefits of green landscapes on drivers' and passengers' safety and health. Further, we found there is an interactive effect between greenness and complexity of freeway landscape. We found there is a trade-off effect between greenness and complexity. In other words, a driving environment should not only be green but also have a balance of greenness and complexity. When the driving environment is not challenging, our findings suggest a tree landscape with relatively regular form is optimal because driver’s mental state is a priority than driving performance. When the driving environment is challenging, our findings suggest a shrub landscape with relatively naturalistic from is optimal because driver’s performance is a priority than driver’s mental states. 3. The third objective has been significantly achieved. I successfully built up a lab at the Faculty of Architecture at the University of Hong Kong in 2016, which was named as Virtual Reality Lab of Urban Environments and Human Health. In the past four years, we have made significant contributions which can be demonstrated by our publications in first-tier journals in the field, a large number of lectures and talks for academia, professional, government, and public, exhibitions, and conference presentations. The lab has built up strong cooperation with leading labs and researchers in the world. 27609816.label: Major findings and research outcome
27609816.value: 1. Impacts of freeway landscapes on drivers’ mental states Few studies have investigated the impact of landscapes on humans’ mental status while they are moving at high speeds, such as driving on the freeway. This study used a simulation system to measure drivers’ mental responses to six different freeway landscapes. Each of the 33 participants completed six different 90-minute simulated driving tasks in a randomly assigned sequence. The six landscape conditions consisted of an identical freeway infrastructure, with different roadside landscapes. Results show significant differences between landscape conditions and drivers' mental responses. Landscape conditions with greater greenness, in general, had a greater positive impact on drivers’ mental status. The barren and tree regular landscapes yielded the worst and best results, respectively. Further, higher complexity was associated with a higher level of negative mental status. We argue that the speed of humans’ active movement should be considered as an essential factor in the Attention Restoration Theory and Stress Reduction Theory. 2. Driving performance: Analysis of OpenDS and Eye-Tracking data Poor driving performance can cause numerous injuries and deaths. Many previous studies have suggested that landscapes make significant impacts on human performance; however, few studies have examined whether and to what extent different types of freeway landscapes influence people’s driving performance. Without this knowledge, policy-makers, developers, and designers of freeway infrastructure in hundreds of countries lose opportunities to design landscapes that promote driving performance. In this study, a simulated driving system was used to measure the impacts of six types of freeway landscape (barren, turf, shrub-regular, shrub-random, tree-regular, tree-random) on 32 participants’ driving performance. Each participant completed six driving simulations for each of the six types of freeway landscapes in random order on six different days. Driving performance was measured continuously through OpenDS Software through seven parameters, and self-reported driving performance was measured seven times in the 90-minute experiment through Visual Analog Scale questionnaires. ANOVA analysis and it suggests that shrub and tree landscapes, in general, yielded more positive impacts than barren and turf landscapes, and there is no significant difference between the barren and turf landscapes. Repeated ANOVA analysis of shrub and tree landscapes consistently shows a trade-off effect between landscape diversity and greenness: landscape diversity has a positive effect on driving performance while landscape greenness has a negative effect. Finally, the shrub-random landscape yielded the most positive effect on driving performance, and barren and turf yielded the most negative effect.

27609816.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27609816.value: 1. In the future studies, we need to accurately quantify impacts of different driving speeds on driver’s mental status and driving performance while they are driving in different landscape settings; 2. In a future study, we may create a more immersive driving environment. For example, we may use a 360-degree VR system (Oculus VR glasses or multiple TV screens) and simulated vibration of seat (similar vibration responses as seating in a real moving vehicle). We also need to create more realistic and challenging driving environments for participants (other cars driving on the road, forced change of lanes, traffic signs, etc.). 3. After all publications are completed, we need to make a report to the transportation department of the HK SAR government to share our findings and search for opportunities to influence policy-making. We need to present our findings in conferences and meetings. We also need to share the findings with professional and public media across the world.

27609816.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27609816.value: This study is an initial effort to investigate whether and to what extent freeway landscapes can influence freeway driver’s mental states and driving performance. The study used an identical freeway infrastructure with a variety of landscape settings. The study used advanced devices and measures to quantify impacts. Thus, its findings have a high level of reliability. There are three significant findings. We found the green landscape has a significantly more positive impact on driving performance and mental states, which demonstrate the health benefits of green landscapes on drivers' and passengers' safety and health. Further, we found there is an interactive effect between greenness and complexity of freeway landscape. We found there is a trade-off effect between greenness and complexity. In other words, a driving environment should not only be green but also have a balance of greenness and complexity. When the driving environment is not challenging, our findings suggest a tree landscape with relatively regular form is optimal because the driver’s mental state is a priority than driving performance. When the driving environment is challenging, our findings suggest a shrub landscape with relatively naturalistic from is optimal because the driver’s performance is a priority than the driver’s mental states.

27610616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27610616.value: This project investigates emerging spaces for sex work by non-Chinese women that are experiencing other forms of marginalization in Hong Kong, such as migrant workers and asylum-seekers. This is a relatively new area of inquiry in Hong Kong and presents an opportunity to theoretically advance understandings of the relationship between sex, commerce and marginalization in a globalized context. An intersectional theoretical lens will be used to analyse the negotiation and management of social difference (e.g. race, class, gender, sexuality) across diverse statuses, roles and legal contexts in Hong Kong’s sex work sector. Empirically, this research explores non-Chinese women’s management of sex work in the context of other stigmatized, marginalized or precarious identities. A focus on this group also presents an opportunity to investigate evolving forms of sex work that may be relatively less visible in Hong Kong. The involvement in sex work by non-Chinese women that are negotiating other marginalized identities may reveal the ambiguous boundaries between sex work, transactional sex, compensated dating, economically motivated relationships and sexual exploitation. Given these empirical demands, qualitative methods such as ethnography, participant observation and semi-structured interviews, will be used. The empirical demands of this project include accommodating heightened privacy, security and confidentiality concerns of participants; negotiating evolving forms of sex work in Hong Kong; and centring the analyses and expertise of women in sex work. This research is grounded in collaboration with one of the primary sex worker support organizations in Hong Kong, Action for Reach Out (AFRO). As such, this project is committed to producing practical impact in addition to theoretical and empirical understanding. The practical aims for this project include the development of appropriate and effective outreach strategies for non-Chinese sex workers in Hong Kong, as well as the facilitation of dialogue across civil sector organizations in Hong Kong (e.g. organizations supporting asylum-seekers, migrant workers, etc.) on sex work and related issues. 此研究計劃會探討在香港經歷不同形式邊緣化之非華裔女性（如外地勞工及尋求庇護者）新興的性工作空間。這在香港是一個相對新的探討領域，提供了一個就性、商業與邊緣化數者之間在全球化的脈絡下的關係取得更高層次的理論上的了解的一個機會。研究會運用交叉的理論視角以分析香港性工作者界別中，跨越不同地位、角色及法律脈絡的社會差異（如種族、階級、性別及性身份）的交涉協商與管理。在實證上，此研究會探討非華裔女性在其他被污名化、邊緣化或不安全的身份背境下、就著性工作的管理。將焦點放在此一社群上亦提供了探討香港一種可能較不為人注意、新發展的性工作形式的機會。這些需就其他邊緣身份持續作交涉協商的非華裔女性涉足於性工作，可能揭示了性工作、跨境的性、援助交際、以經濟為誘因之關係，與性剝削之間曖昧模糊的界線。基於這些實證要求，質性研究方法（如民族志、參與式觀察及半結構訪談）將會被應用。此研究的實證要求包括為參與者就高度隱私性、安全性及保密性的關注作出適切調節，就香港新發展的性工作形式作協商，以及將性工作中女性的分析及專長置於核心。此研究將確立於與青鳥－－香港其中一個主要的性工作者支援團組織－－的合作上，因此除理論與實證上的發現外，亦旨在產生實質的影響。此研究的實際目標包括發展出適切有效的、以香港非華裔性工作為對象的外展策略，以及促進不同民間組織（如尋求庇護者支援組織、外勞組織等等）之間關於性工作及有關議題的對話。

27610616.label: Realisation of objectives
27610616.value: Objective 1: This was achieved. The main research findings that relate to this objective were published in an article titled ‘Scripting pragmatic intimacies in sex work, migration and intimate-material exchanges’ (Ham & Gheorghiu, 2020). Specifically, the article conceptualizes ‘intimate-material exchanges’ within ‘intimate economies’ in which material support is provided in exchange for intimate relations. The article discusses the implications of this conceptualization for sex work research which more often attends to visibly commercial enterprises, such as brothels, street-based sex work and online escorting, to name a few examples. The sphere of ‘intimate-material exchanges’ has particular relevance for women with migrant status who may otherwise be prohibited from formal employment, even in stigmatized and criminalized industries such as sex work. The findings were drawn from: (1) 39 semi-structured interviews with women and men involved in intimate economies and sex work, (2) ethnography in Wanchai and Tsim Sha Tsui, and (3) 14 semi-structured interviews with representatives of diverse civil society organizations that have engaged with sex work issues. Objective 2: This was achieved. The main research findings that relate to this objective were or will be published in: (1) a journal article in Culture, Health & Sexuality, titled ‘Scripting pragmatic intimacies in sex work, migration and intimate-material exchanges’ (Ham & Gheorghiu, 2020), (2) a book chapter, titled ‘Migrant domestic workers, asylum-seekers and premonitions of anti-trafficking in Hong Kong’ (Ham, Gheorghiu & Lestari, in press) for the upcoming volume, Race and Racism of Anti-Trafficking (eds. Kempadoo & Shih, in press), and (3) a journal article submitted to Qualitative Research, titled ‘Situated accounts and biographical labor in the sex work interview’ (Gheorghiu & Ham, under review). The first publication listed examines how women’s migrant status shapes their definition and understanding of sex work, particularly visa-related prohibitions against various forms of employment and the risks in labelling their activities as labour. The second publication analyses the implications of the emerging anti-trafficking framework in Hong Kong for asylum-seekers who have engaged in sex work or intimate-material exchanges and the difficulties in effectively supporting persons who have been trafficked if they are asylum-seekers engaging in sex work or intimate-material exchanges. The third publication focuses on how women define their engagement in sex work within the context of stigma and criminalization. The findings were drawn from: (1) 39 semi-structured interviews with women and men involved in intimate economies and sex work, (2) ethnography in Wanchai and Tsim Sha Tsui, and (3) 14 semi-structured interviews with representatives of diverse civil society organizations. Objective 3: This was achieved. The main research findings that relate to this objective were published in ‘Scripting pragmatic intimacies in sex work, migration and intimate-material exchanges’ (Ham & Gheorghiu, 2020). The research findings that relate to this objective are similar to those that relate to the first objective discussed above. Specifically, the article discusses ‘intimate-material exchanges’ within ‘intimate economies’ that may occur beyond more visibly commercial establishments in the sex industry. The ambiguity of ‘intimate-material exchanges’ and its liminality between the intimate and economic affords some opportunities and protection from law enforcement interference, particularly for women whose migrant status may prohibit particular forms of employment. However, research participants shared experiences and lives that are often characterized by legal precarity and economic insecurity. The findings were drawn from: (1) 39 semi-structured interviews with women and men involved in intimate economies and sex work, (2) ethnography in Wanchai and Tsim Sha Tsui, and (3) 14 semi-structured interviews with representatives of diverse civil society organizations that have engaged with sex work issues. Objective 4: This was achieved although understanding of the objective had to be adjusted to fit the organizational approach of Action for Reach Out (AFRO), a sex worker support organization and a collaborating organization on the project. An impetus of the project was to increase AFRO’s reach to non-Chinese women through an exploration of their needs and experiences. Community engagement and outreach to non-Chinese women, particularly from communities that may not have been as familiar with AFRO, was successful and AFRO reported throughout the project that more non-Chinese women were accessing their services and asking for assistance on various matters. Assistance to non-Chinese women was strengthened through an organic, evolving response to cases rather than a diagrammable outreach and support model. The cases and issues that non-Chinese women brought to AFRO often reflected intersecting issues that related not only to health, but to migrant status, concerns about law and regulation in Hong Kong, economic insecurity, and other issues. The intersecting issues raised by women in some ways challenged a standardized outreach and support model, but rather, necessitated more tailored, individualized approaches or strategies for women. A more reflective objective that captures what was achieved would be the development of outreach and support strategies or approaches rather than a diagrammable model. Community resources were also developed to disseminate research findings and to enable sharing of research participants’ knowledge with others in the sex industry. A series of five leaflets on (1) law and regulation, (2) money management, (3) sexual health, (4) safety and (5) accessing support was produced that included advice, observations and experiences from sex workers and women in intimate economies. Information about these resources will be shared on the website, Mobile Methodologies and Migrant Knowledges (https://www.mmmk.hku.hk/). Distribution of the leaflets to women in the sex industry and related sectors will occur through AFRO. Objective 5: This was achieved through 14 of interviewees from civil society organizations working on issues relating to migrant workers, asylum-seekers and refugees, women, trafficked persons and health. The role of civil society organizations in assisting women engaging in sex work and intimate economies is also explored further in two publications. The role of sex worker rights organizations in addressing the particular needs of migrant women is discussed in the article, ‘Scripting pragmatic intimacies in sex work, migration and intimate-material exchanges’ (Ham & Gheorghiu, 2020). The barriers presented by the anti-trafficking framework in addressing trafficking experienced by asylum-seekers who have engaged in sex work and intimate economies is discussed in the book chapter, titled ‘Migrant domestic workers, asylum-seekers and premonitions of anti-trafficking in Hong Kong’ (Ham, Gheorghiu & Lestari, in press) for the upcoming volume, Race and Racism of Anti-Trafficking (eds. Kempadoo & Shih, in press). Objective 6: This was achieved. The main project findings that relate to this objective are discussed in a journal article submitted to Qualitative Research, titled ‘Situated accounts and biographical labor in the sex work interview’ (Gheorghiu & Ham, under review). The article seeks to challenge the primacy of truth seeking as the determinative aim of research interviews and instead examines the biographical labour or self-making that is done by interviewees. As women working in stigmatized and criminalized industries and managing other marginalized identities (e.g. as asylum-seekers, as domestic workers), the article reveals the labour that is done in interviews to present the participant as someone whose voice and account is deserving of dignity and respect. This does not entail fabricating a socially desirable history for the interviewer but rather the use of the interview as an interactive encounter where stigma can be challenged by authoring one’s experiences on one’s own terms.

27610616.label: Major findings and research outcome
27610616.value: This study found that migration policy and migration status necessitate the deployment of sexual, emotional, or romantic intimacy for economic security in and beyond commercial sex work establishments (e.g. brothels), even when such engagement may be stigmatized or criminalized. For instance, the prohibition against particular forms of labour for various migrant groups results in a criminalization of income generation activities which may exclude migrant women from working in commercial sex work establishments due to their migrant status, race and ethnicity. This resulted in what the research team termed ‘intimate-material exchanges’ (Ham & Gheorghiu, 2020). Intimate-material exchanges, and intimate economies more broadly, blur the boundaries between the intimate and economic. Intimate-material exchanges, while designated as beyond the sphere of formal labour, nevertheless often involves a strategic pragmatism, resourcefulness and intentionality. Many of the women, primarily migrant women, in this study demonstrated a savvy pragmatism and resourcefulness in lives that were nevertheless often marked by legal, social and economic precarity. The experiences and needs of non-Chinese women, primarily migrant women, in sex work and intimate economies also presented needs and concerns that can challenge organizations that provide support or assistance. Women’s intersectional identities (as migrant workers, as members of ethnic minority communities, as asylum-seekers) revealed experiences that spoke to the intersections between migration, health and various bodies of law. Accessing support could present a challenge when a woman’s experiences defied easy categorization (Ham, Gheorghiu & Lestari, in press). The research findings in this study speak to the need to carefully attend to how research participants frame and understand their experiences (Gheorghiu & Ham, under review).

27610616.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27610616.value: The linkages between intimacy and migration that were explored in this study have the potential to bridge and advance sex work research and migration studies. Migration policy and migration status are mechanisms that reveal the increasingly blurred boundaries or interdependencies between the intimate and the economic. The findings in this study contribute to a growing literature that examines the use of intimacy in managing migration and the role of migration policy in necessitating, facilitating or criminalizing particular intimacies (Ham & Gheorghiu, 2020). This literature includes research on migrant sex work, marriage migration, and the role of reproductive status in managing labour migration, to name a few examples. The findings in this study also point to the need for sex work researchers to engage with migration law as one of the factors that shape how sex work and other intimate economies occur (Ham & Gheorghiu, 2020). The use of intimate-material exchanges for economic security also points to a need for sex work researchers to broaden their scope beyond visible or explicitly commercial establishments (such as brothels) to consider other interactions that trade intimacy for compensation or material support.

27610616.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27610616.value: This study explored the experiences of non-Chinese women, primarily migrant women, in sex work and intimate-material exchanges in which financial or material compensation is provided in exchange for sexual, emotional or romantic intimacy. Migration-related factors, such as migrant status, shaped the leveraging of intimacy for economic security, in and beyond commercial sex work establishments. For some women, engaging in intimate-material exchanges outside of commercial sex work establishments was necessitated by migration policy, such as work prohibitions for particular groups of migrants. This research demonstrates the use of intimacy in managing migration (other examples include analyses of migrant sex work, marriage migration, reproductive status and labour migration) and the role of migration policy in managing, necessitating or criminalizing particular forms of intimacy. This research also affirms the need for sex work researchers to engage with migration law as one of the forces that shapes workers’ experiences in sex work and intimate economies. For some women, experiences in and out of sex work and intimate-material exchanges presented a range of complex needs that were challenging to address within existing support structures, given the multiple identities and issues that women presented.

27611716.label: Project Title(Chinese)
27611716.value: 中日争端与国际危机中的观众成本

27611716.label: Project Objectives
27611716.value: To study whether and to what extent Chinese leaders would suffer "domestic audience costs" if they back down in a Sino-Japanese territorial dispute. To investigate the underlying drivers of audience costs: To what extent are they driven by an instrumental concern about the state's credibility, or by a normative concern about national honor and image? How does the activation of nationalism affect the public costs of backing down? To uncover the factors and strategies that can effectively reduce the public costs of backing down - in particular, do the real-life framing devices and strategies used by Chinese leaders (based on our background study of Chinese crisis behavior reported by the state media) actually help to reduce domestic audience costs?

27611716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27611716.value: This project studies the dynamics of crisis deescalation in the Chinese context. An international crisis can escalate unless one state backs down, but backing down can generate “domestic audience costs” (Fearon 1994) - the public political costs for backing down after making an international threat, when leaders are faulted by domestic constituencies for compromising their nation’s prestige and reputation. Domestic audience costs make it costly for leaders to back down, which sharpens the risk of war. Our project investigates domestic audience costs in the Chinese context and tests different strategies and devices for controlling these costs. The current conventional wisdom is that China's willingness to compromise in territorial disputes with Japan and other neighbors is highly constrained by leadership fears of popular nationalist backlash. The proposed project focuses specifically on domestic audience costs in the context of a territorial dispute between China and Japan. Audience costs are measured by the loss in domestic public approval for the national leader based on experimental scenarios embedded in a large-scale national survey (Tomz 2007; Trager and Vavreck 2011; Levendusky and Horowitz 2012). The project addresses three main issues: 1) To what extent will Chinese leaders suffer domestic audience costs if they back down in the context of Sino-Japanese conflict? How large are these costs? 2) What are the underlying drivers of domestic audience costs? In particular, how does the activation of nationalism and ethnocentrism affect the public costs of backing down? To what extent does nationalism drive audience costs? 3) What strategies and devices are effective in controlling the public costs of backing down? In particular, are the real-life framing devices and strategies used by the Chinese government (based on our background study of Chinese crisis behavior) effective in reducing audience costs? 本研究以中国为研究对象，探究有关国际危机化解的相关课题。 一般而言， 除非有其中一方让步，国际危机大有升级恶化的可能性。然而，在国际危机中让步又常常会引起“国内观众成本” (Fearon 1994)。所谓 “国内观众成本” 指的是如果国家领导人对别国做出公开的威胁， 却没有兑现， 而是选择退让， 那么这领导人往往会因为使国家的声誉和形象受损而遭到国内民众（政治观众）的指责。这种政治观众成本可以使领导人在国际危机中退让的可能性大大减小，与此同时也增大了危机升级以致爆发战争的风险。 研究的目的在于探究上述国内观众成本并对可控制该成本的各类策略的实际作用展开实证检验。在当前的普遍认识中，由于潜在的强烈民族主义反冲的担忧，中国领导人在处理与日本以及其他邻国的领土争端中愿意做出妥协的可能性被极大地限制。本课题将着重关注中日领土争端中所涉及的国内政治观众成本。研究将包含实验性的情景问题并以应答者在相关情景下的支持程度来测量所产生的政治观众成本 (Tomz 2007; Trager and Vavreck 2011; Levendusky and Horowitz 2012)。 本研究包含三个主要问题： 1. 假设中国领导人在中日有关冲突中做出退让，他们将在何种程度上承担国内观众成本？这些成本又将有多高？ 2. 国内观众成本的深层次动因是什么？尤其是， 民族主义和民族优越感是如何影响在国际危机中做出退让的观众成本？民族主义在何种程度上能引发观众成本？ 3. 哪些策略和方法能有效控制在国际危机中做出让步的观众成本？尤其是，中国政府在现实中所采取的策略是否能有效控制所谓的观众成本？

27611716.label: Realisation of objectives
27611716.value: All three objectives are achieved (see Section 6 below on "Research Outcomes"). At the same time, we believe that our discoveries represent a beginning -- rather than the end -- of a new and exciting area of research, which we continue to build on and extend further.

27611716.label: Major findings and research outcome
27611716.value: [For Objective 1] We highlight that "domestic audience costs" do not only exist in a democratic context, but can also exist in an authoritarian context such as in China under some conditions. We show experimentally that the government can incur significant costs in the form of a public approval backlash if it backs down in a territorial dispute with Japan after threatening the use of force. Many policy elites and pundits have argued that the prospect of a nationalistic backlash makes it difficult for China to de-escalate an international crisis, especially over territorial disputes. We use experimental methods to quantify for the first time the existence and magnitude of the domestic nationalistic backlash. [For Objective 2] We find that nationalism, conflict salience, and concerns over national self-image can be important underlying drivers of the public costs of backing down. Instrumental and normative concerns can co-exist in different degrees, depending on respondent traits such as their type and level of nationalism/nativism. [For Objective 3] We theorize and test different conditions and strategies that can effectively reduce the public costs of backing down in an international crisis. Our results show how the substitutive use of economic sanctions, the prospect of third-party mediation, and propaganda-frames based on China’s identity (as a peace-loving nation) and interests (as a growing economy) can be configured into effective strategies for de-escalating a territorial crisis with Japan.

27611716.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27611716.value: Our discoveries help to lay the foundation for a new and exciting area of research, which we continue to build on, and which other researchers have subsequently contributed and extended. The use of experimental methods to study the causes and consequences of Chinese foreign policy is extremely new, but also very promising. While our results indicate that nationalism, conflict salience, and concerns over national self-image can be important drivers of the public costs of backing down, the deeper determinants of these drivers -- and the heterogeneity of their effects across different people -- remain to be investigated, and we have continued on this line of research.

27611716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27611716.value: How China manages its disputes and how it de-escalates international crises in the shadow of domestic nationalistic backlash are extremely important questions in today's world. We theorize and test different conditions and strategies that can effectively reduce the public costs and nationalistic backlash from retreating in an international crisis. Using original data from randomised experiments, we show how the substitutive use of economic sanctions, the prospect of third-party mediation, and propaganda-frames based on China’s identity (as a peace-loving nation) and interests (as a developing economy) can be configured into useful strategies for de-escalating a territorial crisis with Japan.

27612816.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27612816.value: Over half of the self-harm patients (N=59,473) had presented themselves to the Accident & Emergency Departments (AED) in Hong Kong (2002-2010), imposing substantial costs on the healthcare system. About 45% of them defaulted psychiatric treatment and 16.7% re-attempt. Their low treatment compliance suggests a need for community-based intervention to help reduce hospital readmissions and the related disease burden. Follow-up contacts had significantly reduced repetition of self-harm. The interpersonal-psychological theory of suicide suggests that thwarted belongingness (TB) and perceived burdensomeness (PB) contribute to suicidal ideation, subsequent suicide attempts, and death, particularly when these two factors are perceived hopelessly as stable and unchanging. It is thus possible that enhancing social connectedness and self-assurance could buffer against self-harm by reducing TB and PB. Many mental healthcare mobile apps have been developed for mental illness management and prevention of behavioral health problems. Integrating the concept of social connectedness into a mobile app’s pre-programmed caring features for individuals at risk of self-harm is a potentially effective intervention for young people. On the other hand, trained volunteers have been widely used worldwide to answer suicide-crisis calls from the public; they provide personalized engagement with service users, and have shown promising signs in reducing hopelessness and depression among self-harm young adults. The proposed study will determine whether community-based caring contact via a mobile app connection with or without volunteer support in addition to treatment as usual (TAU; psychiatric and psychosocial treatments) is effective in reducing suicidal ideation, and hopelessness among post-discharge self-harm young adults, and if personalized contact by volunteers has additional effects on engaging self-harm individuals. 108 participants aged 18-39 with an index self-harm episode will be recruited from the AED of five local public hospitals, and randomized into the TAU, mobile app group with, and without volunteer support. Each participant will complete a questionnaire at the 4 measurement time points at baseline, during the 6-month observation and at post-intervention. The primary outcomes include suicidal ideation, interpersonal needs, hopelessness, and self-reported treatment compliance. For data analysis, intention to treat strategy will be used. Growth models are selected to capture both fixed and random effects of data collected. Safety measures will be specifically developed for this study to ensure participants’ safety and privacy will be fully protected. This study will generate empirical evidence on the novel use of mobile app and volunteer support as engagement tools among this high-risk group, and the theoretical development of self-harm prevention. 據香港2002至2010年醫院管理局的數據顯示，超過半數的自傷病人(N＝59,473)曾向急症室求診，對醫療服務的整體成本構成重大壓力。當中約百分之四十五的病人未有返回醫院接受門診精神科療程，而百分之十六點七的病人更試圖再次自傷。回流社區的病人對治療的低依從性，反映了相應的干預方法需要以社區為基礎，以減低病人再次入院的數字及減輕相關的疾病負擔。 跟進性的聯絡可明顯減少自傷重複發生。根據自殺的人際關係心理學理論，「挫敗歸屬感」和「感知負擔感」都能構成自殺念頭，及隨之而來的企圖自殺行為和死亡；當病人無助地把這兩個因素視為不會改變的時候，情況就尤其嚴重。因此，增加與社會連繫和個人信心，均能有機會緩和因「挫敗歸屬感」和「感知負擔感」引致的自傷行為。 很多與心理健康相關的手機應用程式都具有疾病管理及預防問題行為的功能。綜合連繫社會的概念，這些手機應用程式對自傷的高危人士會有一定的潛在幫助；將預切的關懷功能引進手機應用程式內，對相關的自傷青少年人，更為奏效。另一方面，由接受過專業培訓的義務人士去接聽市民因自殺而求助的來電，在世界各地已相當普及；義務人士可以為服務使用者提供個人化的連繫，有效減低自傷青少年的絕望感和抑鬱情緒。 本研究擬判斷，在因為自傷而需要接受常規醫療服務(TAU)的年輕病人當中，接受手機應用程式，或額外再透過義務人士所提供的關懷干預，能否有效地減低病人於離院後的自殺念頭和絕望感；其中更會分析義務人士所提供的個人化連繫的效果。 我們將於醫院管理局轄下的數間醫院急症室，召募108位年齡介乎18至39 歲因自傷而求診的人士參與是次究研。參加者會被隨機分派到1) 只接受TAU、2) TAU和手機應用關懷程式、或3) TAU、手機應用關懷程式及義務人士支援的干預組群。每位參加者都須在研究開始時、六個月的觀察期間和及後的跟進期，分別完成四次的問卷調查。問卷會問及參加者的自殺意向，人際關係需要，絕望感和自我報告的治療依從情況。數據會以「意圖治療」分析，以達致最公平結果；分析亦會以「增長模式」進行，以捕捉固定和隨機的數據效應。本研究的安全措施會特地為是次參加對象訂定，以保證參加者的安全和私隱能得到全面保護。這項研究會為以手機應用程式和義務人士連繫自傷人士提供實證，建立預防自傷的理論。

27613316.label: Project Objectives

27613316.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613316.value: The key goal of this project is to contribute to a better understanding of the development of languages spoken in highly diverse, multilingual linguistic ecologies. Specifically, this project seeks to account for the differentiation of the young linguistic family of Afro-Caribbean English-lexifier Creoles (AECs), which emerged in the early 17th century. The individual AEC varieties are today spoken across a vast geographical space covering West Africa and the Caribbean and show a fascinating diversity in their grammars in spite of their common origins. Much of the work on language contact and change in the AECs is founded on the ideal of the bilingual contact scenario. The development through time of the English-lexifier Creoles is seen to have been influenced primarily by contact with English, the language that has provided the AECs with the bulk of the lexicon. However, the linguistic communities that have used these languages since their emergence are notoriously multilingual, and manifest a high degree of tolerance for linguistic variation. If we want to understand how the Afro-Caribbean English-lexifier Creoles have developed apart, we therefore have to factor in the diverse range of settings these languages are today spoken in. The objective of the project is to provide a comprehensive description of the development of the English-lexifier Creoles of Africa and the Caribbean, while producing a corpus of first-hand data that will be made available to interested researchers. Based on empirical approaches, the project also seeks to contribute to the methodology and terminology for the description and analyses of language change in typologically diverse, multilingual settings in general. The study of the AECs also offers a unique window into the evolution of languages in the context of fast-paced and far-reaching social, economic and political change brought about by colonialism and globalization in the past four hundred years or so. 本項目的主要目的是幫助我們更好地理解在高度多樣化的語言生態中語言的發展狀況。研究對象是非裔加勒比人群所使用的以英語為上層語的克里奧語（Afro-Caribbean English-lexifier Creoles or AECs），這些克里奧語出現於17世紀初，形成了一個年輕的語系，本項目正是旨在解釋這些克里奧語之間存在的區別。AECs的使用範圍很廣，在西非及加勒比地區的大片區域都可以找到它們的變體。儘管這些變體的起源相同，但語法上呈現出有趣的區別。目前有關AECs在語言接觸及語言變化方面的許多研究都是在理想的雙語環境下進行的。有關AECs的歷時發展，目前認為對其產生影響的主要途徑是通過與英語發生接觸，英語為AECs提供了大量的詞彙。然而，使用這些克里奧語的語言社區自身語言高度多樣化，而且對語言變化具有很高的容忍度。如果我們想要了解AECs是如何分化的，我們必須將這些語言在當下使用的種種環境考慮進去。本研究的目的就是對AECs的發展進行綜合描述，並且建立一手語料庫，供對此有興趣的研究者使用。通過實證的方法，在多語環境下，本研究還希望對語言變化的描寫和分析所使用的方法和術語有所貢獻。過去四百多年的殖民主義及全球化給社會、經濟和政治帶來了深遠快速的影響，在這種背景下，對AECs的研究還可以為語言演化提供一個獨特的視角。

27613316.label: Realisation of objectives
27613316.value: The research objectives can be grouped under (a) data collection and handling (objectives 3, 4), (b) data analysis (objectives 1, 2) and (c) publication output (objectives 5, 6). All objectives relating to (a) and (c) have been realised above target, while objectives under (b) are yet ongoing and should be realised by the end of this year. Here follow details on the achievement of objectives grouped under (a) data collection and handling: During field research in Ghana and Cameroon in 2016 and 2017, I collected a substantial corpus of two of the five object languages with support from local research assistants. I collected about twenty hours of recorded speech in Ghanaian Pidgin English in Ghana. During research in Cameroon, I collected about 30 hours of data on Cameroon Pidgin in Buea, Limbe and other locations. Data collection on the Caribbean object languages Tobagonian Creole (Trinidad and Tobago) and Sranan (Suriname) was outsourced to competent research assistants in the two countries with my guidance and supervision. This led to the collection of thirty hours of Tobagonian Creole and about fifteen hours of complementary data on Sranan collected in addition to an existing corpus from a previous research project. Field research on Pichi, the fifth object language, turned out to be unnecessary because an existing corpus of about forty hours of recordings proved to be rich enough to be mined for this project without spending time and material resources on additional field research. The entire corpus has been transcribed by research assistants who I trained either in the field locations or in communication and coordination from my desk. The corpus is presently being curated (i.e. checked for inconsistencies, standardised, glossed) and I am aiming for the corpus to be ready for submission to the language archive of the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics by the end of 2019. Objective four of the research project (data collection and handling) is therefore the only one to extend beyond the official project completion date of 31 Aug 2019. However, this was predicted in the mid-term progress report, since data curation constitutes the most tedious and most expansive part of the project in terms of (wo)man hours of work. The curation of data and preparation for archiving is known to consume substantial amounts of time and resources. Regarding (b) data analysis, the following can be concluded with respect to the realisation of research objectives. The project relied on the methodological apparatus of descriptive linguistics, areal-typology, historical linguistics, contact linguistics and the linguistic data sciences. Exclusively drawing on primary data collected during field research, I examined specific functional domains in a group of creoles with known historical connections, the same lexifier, and substrates and adstrates with areal and genealogical linkages. Data analysis took place with support from research assistants at HKU. Patterns were uncovered with support from the linguistic annotation software FLEx and specific functional areas were investigated in the object languages. The choice of structural features in the individual languages was guided by the criterion of typological markedness. The data analysed focused on under- and unstudied functional domains that allowed reconstructing the evolutionary trajectories of individual AECs, including but not limited to: (1) the AEC prosodic systems, i.e. tone systems vs. stress systems, (2) modality, (3) asymmetric negation systems, (4) split copular systems, (5) spatial relations. The analyses were very succesful in that they allowed me to develop a new model of the speciation of the AECs, which I term the “areal-stratal model of creole differentiation”. Data collection (a) and data analyses (b) as fed into the completion of significant publication outputs. These consist in eight conference paper including keynote speeches/invited talks in prestigious institutions (e.g invited talks/keynotes at the Universities of Chicago, Berkeley and Oslo) four major research works and ongoing work on an additional major work: (1) “A Grammar of Pichi” (2019) constitutes the most extensive treatment to date of any English-lexifier creole spoken in the world. The 600-page grammar was praised by three anonymous reviewers as “one of the best grammars of a creole language ever written”, “exhaustive” and of “very high quality”. The book contains a wealth of structural and sociolinguistic information of great use for creole and contact research, typology, research on varieties of English, and African linguistics. The publication of this book with the highly prestigious full open access publisher “Language Science Press” (Berlin, Germany) ensures that this work is also accessible for free for researchers, speakers of the language, students and institutions in countries of the Global South. (2) The journal article “Inheritance, contact, convergence: Pronominal allomorphy in the African English-lexifier Creoles” (2019) has appeared in the most highly ranked journal dedicated to the study of varieties of English (WoS impact factor 2.1). The article is the first to provide a comparative analysis of a specific unstudied structural feature across five AEC varieties. The paper was lauded by a reviewer as a “very nice piece of descriptive work, with a clever analysis”. Major output (3) is an article submitted to the prestigious linguistics journal Language (WoS impact factor 2.3), which has undergone a successful first review and has been invited for resubmission. I am currently revising the article with my co-author (Guri Bordal Steien, MultiLing, Univ. of Oslo). Revisions will be completed by the end of May 2019 and publication of the article is anticipated in early 2020. Output (4) is a second single-authored monograph resulting from research on this project and is currently in preparation. The manuscript of the single-authored book “The English Creoles of Africa and the Americas: Contact, differentiation, expansion” is due in Dec. 2019. A publishing contract with the Routledge series Studies in World Englishes has been signed. The monograph synthesizes the various research strands of this project in a new theoretical framework and aims to achieve significant scientific advances in the study of the AECs, contact languages, and multilingualism in fulfillment of objectives 5 and 6.

27613316.label: Major findings and research outcome
27613316.value: The principal research outcomes are twofold: (1) This project has enabled me to compile the largest existing corpus of comparative data of Caribbean and African English-lexifier Creoles (AECs) to date collected by a unified methodology and consolidated theoretical framework. The corpus is currently being curated and will be made available to the public in an online language archive. This will provide further opportunities to other researchers working on the AECs. (2) The project has explained core aspects of the complex interaction of genealogical, areal, typological, and social forces in the differentiation of the AECs. The published outputs of this project have cumulatively developed and argued the “stratal-areal model of creole differentiation”, the first comprehensive model of language change in the AECs that can be generalised to other groupings of contact languages. The in-depth study “A Grammar of Pichi” now provides a comprehensive typologically oriented framework for the description of Afro-Caribbean English-lexifier Creoles, and provides the basis for comparative and areal-typological investigation. The articles in English World-Wide (2019) and Language (under second review) also provide orientation in terms of content and methodolgy for future studies on the speciation and differentiation of creole languages. The findings support some of the hypotheses advanced in the ECS proposal: (a) contact with English has led to more structural and lexical transfer of English features to an AEC than when a non-lexifier is the superstrate of a creole; (b) contact with African adstrates has reinforced African substrate features, while the absence of contact with African adstrates has led to the weakening of such features. Furhter findings provide evidence for (c) parallel convergence: non-contiguous creole ecologies as different as Tobago and Cameroon show numerous parallellisms due to convergence towards the shared lexifier superstrate English. The analysis of primary field data from creoles in both Africa and the Americas has allowed me to assess degrees of typological alignment with an areal “Macro-Sudan” and a “Standard Average European” pole respectively. The project has therefore cleared new ground and contributed significantly to the advancement of our understanding of the evolution of contact languages that continue to evolve rapidly and acquire new speakers.

27613316.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27613316.value: The present ECS project has contributed to an understanding of the linguistic structure and diachronic evolution of the AECs. Altogether four further articles not listed under outputs are aimed at high impact venues and currently in the manuscript stage. Further, a GRF project has been submitted for the 2019-20 exercise that would complement this project by turning to the synchronic social dynamics of the AECs. The GRF would be the first to document, compare and analyze standardization processes in the AECs on the backdrop of the ongoing rapid expansion of AEC speaker numbers.

27613316.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27613316.value: This project has investigated the evolution of the Afro-Caribbean English-lexifier Creoles (AECs) the largest group of related creole languages of the world. Research was focused on five AECs spoken in West Africa and the Caribbean: Krio (Sierra Leone), Cameroon Pidgin, Pichi (Equatorial Guinea), Tobagonian (Trinidad & Tobago), and Sranan (Suriname). The findings show that these languages have adapted and changed in the respective places they are spoken in since they emerged in a few centuries ago. Specifically, the AECs have undergone influences from the European colonial languages (the “superstrates”), and from the African languages spoken alongside them (the “adstrates”). This has led to divergence among the AECs, such that each of them has developed specific characteristics. One of the main goals of this project was to find out where the exact differences between the varieties lie, and how much this may have changed their grammar towards a more “European” or more “African” type. The data collected and the publications resulting from this project both constitute a valuable repository of new knowledge on these languages. This project has also had valuable spin-offs in the form of training and education of undergraduate and postgraduate students.

27613416.value: - to produce the first full-length scholarly monograph on the aesthetics, history, and cultural practices of a transnational genre of popular music called garage rock. - to carry out new research into aspects of cultural memory in popular music, with particular focus on retro-nostalgia and the processes through which past genres are recycled and revived in popular culture.

27613416.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613416.value: The tendency to think of pop culture as moving along a linear trajectory of novelty and innovation masks a more complicated cultural logic at work in the case of popular music, where past musics either persist at the fringes of the pop culture landscape, or disappear only to reappear years later as “revivals”. In the case of rock music, in particular, the lateral expansion of underground music into a vast terrain of local scenes has enabled past musics to live on as niche cultures, sustained by fans who peddle in the memorabilia, ephemera, and vintage goods of bygone days. Recent scholarship on music revivalism, however, has largely overlooked rock music and related genres, instead tending to limit the study of revival phenomena to folk, heritage, and traditional musics. In this research, I ask, how do the parameters of revivalism change when discussing rock and pop revivalism? How do popular musics complicate the well-worn models of revivalism, which are so grounded in notions of tradition and heritage? This project explores these questions by drawing on the example of garage rock, a transnational genre of popular music rooted in the sound and style of 1960s rock and roll. Garage rock began in the 1970s in the United States within niche communities of record collectors and critics who sought to revive obscure, amateur rock and roll music of the mid-1960s. Today garage rock continues to flourish as a particular niche in underground rock, with thriving scenes in such urban centres as New York, London, and Tokyo. This project is multi-sited, drawing on ethnographic fieldwork conducted in Japan and the United States. I seek to highlight the particular forms of cultural memory that undergird garage music and culture, particularly focusing on the ways in which fans and musicians recycle the past as retro-nostalgic style. I argue that the role of retro-nostalgia in popular music more generally challenges us to rethink the concept of revivalism as an analytic tool in music scholarship. 以新奇和創新的線性發展史觀思索流行文化，會遮蔽流行音樂複雜的文化邏輯運作。過去的音樂要不是持續存在於流行文化地景的邊緣，就是消失，然後幾年後復興。以搖滾音樂為例，地下音樂橫向擴展成一個個本地音樂場景，使過去的音樂繼續以小眾文化的形式存在，並由買賣昔日復古紀念品的樂迷維繫。然而，近年有關音樂復興主義的研究，很大程度上忽略了搖滾音樂及相關類型，研究傾向受限於民謠、遺產音樂和傳統音樂的復興現象。在這項研究中，我問，討論搖滾和流行音樂復興主義時，復興主義的參數如何變化？流行音樂如何複雜化建立在傳統、遺產觀念上的陳舊復興主義模型？ 這項研究以車庫搖滾為例探索以上問題。車庫搖滾作為跨國流行音樂類型根植於60年代搖滾的聲響與風格。車庫搖滾開始於美國70年代，當時唱片收藏家和樂評組成的小眾社群，企圖復興60年代中期冷門、業餘的搖滾樂。今時今日，車庫搖滾作為小眾類型，繼續在城市中心如紐約，倫敦和東京的地下搖滾場景蓬勃發展。這是多場域的研究，在日本和美國進行民族誌田野調查。我嘗試強調文化記憶裡鞏固車庫音樂與文化的特別形式，尤其側重樂迷和音樂家如何回收過去，形成復古-懷舊風格。我認為，復古-懷舊在流行音樂中扮演的角色，促使我們重新思考音樂研究中作為分析工具的復興主義概念。

27613416.label: Realisation of objectives
27613416.value: The primary objective of this grant has been to produce a monograph on a genre of underground music called “garage rock”. This objective has been achieved, in so far as I have a completed a manuscript on contemporary garage rock, focusing on the case of the Tokyo garage rock scene. The book is tentatively entitled “Back from the Grave: Pop Nostalgia and Garage Rock and Roll in the Tokyo Underground”, and is currently being shopped around to several presses for publication. In addition to the monograph, I am also currently developing an article that is under consideration for a special issue of the journal Popular Music History (notably, the proposed special issue is still under review with the journal). This article is focused on the history of the garage rock in the United States from the 1970s through to the present, particularly as it concerns practices of recovering obscure media of the mid-1960s rock and roll era through the practice of producing reissue compilation albums. The project thus has so far exceeded the initial goal in that I am working to publish an article in addition to the monograph. I have also presented on this work at several conferences and events, including the International Musicological Society (IMS) congress in Tokyo, Japan in March 2017, and the International Association for the Study of Popular Music (IASPM) conference in Kassel, Germany in June 2017. In the fall of 2016, I was invited to participate on a panel on orientalism and music, as part of the M+ series of the Hong Kong Arts Festival. In the coming months, I am going to present a conference paper at the IASPM-Canada conference in May 2018, and I have also been invited to present a paper at an upcoming symposium at the Chinese University of Hong Kong on the theme of mobilities in Asian music in April 2018. My primary research activities over the period of the ECS grant include the following: 1) conducting interviews with key figures in the garage rock revival. I met several interlocutors in the United States and Germany, for which I conducted in-depth formal interviews. This research has directly led to an article on the reissuing of 1960s rock music through compilation albums, and has also initiated new research on the history of the compilation album as a unique media form in Anglo-American popular music. 2) As this project is ethnographic in orientation, I have also conducted participation-observation fieldwork on several occasions, most particularly at several live music events in Japan. On three occasions between the fall of 2016 and 2017, I attended live music events of garage rock in Tokyo, Japan. This fieldwork has allowed me to reconnect with my interlocutors, to conduct follow-up research, and to establish new contacts among musicians in the scene; and 3) I have conducted archival research as well as various forms of media documentation, most particularly focused on the history of the garage rock revival in the United States between the 1970s and 1980s. This entailed archival work in the New York public library, as well as research at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. This research has produced valuable information on the early history of the genre, and the processes of genre formation through which garage rock came to be a unique music form. In addition this research, I also spent the past 18 months writing and revising the manuscript. I was able to complete the manuscript, partly due to the generous teaching relief support that I received through the ECS grant. The scope of the project has changed in some ways from the initial proposal. In particular, the initial proposal was focused on the theme of revivalism, but after having conducted more research over the past two years, I have broadened the focus of the monograph to encompass the general theme of cultural memory. The project, thus, has expanded its theoretical scope beyond the narrower analytic concept of “revivalism” to speak more broadly to questions of nostalgia, curatorial aesthetics, and collective memory. Secondly, while the book project is focused on the genre of garage rock, my initial plan was to produce a monograph on the genre as it is practiced in the United States and Japan. After careful consideration—and after discussing my options with potential publishers—I have opted to focus the book on the garage rock scene in Japan. Instead, the research that I conducted on the history of the genre in the United States is currently being developed into an article, tentatively entitled “The Rise of the Amateur Rock Archivist and the Hidden Histories of American Garage Bands”. This work has also led to a second major project on the anthology compilation album as a unique form of popular music media (see section 6.2).

27613416.label: Major findings and research outcome
27613416.value: The book project is an ethnography of popular music in Japan, focusing on aspects of cultural memory in the Tokyo garage rock scene. I argue that scholarship on cultural memory has tended to overemphasize notions of cultural loss and identity, and thus we need new ways to conceptualize the sociocultural dynamics of memory in popular music scholarship. Rooted in the sound and style of mid-1960s American rock and roll, garage rock is an especially nostalgic genre of rock music characterized by a strong orientation towards lowbrow American popular culture of the pre-“Summer of Love” era of rock. It manifests variously as a fetish for obscure rock and roll, vintage goods, B-movie films of the 1950s-60s, pinup iconography, and burlesque, among other forms of obscure retro culture. The Tokyo garage rock scene thus forms an example of what Arjun Appadurai calls “nostalgia without memory”—that is, a cultural practice that supposedly appropriates a “foreign” past. Here, memory works according to the logics of media circulation and pop culture consumption rather than nostalgic longing for the irrevocable, as in the case of traditional and heritage cultures. Instead, participants in the Tokyo garage rock scene consume memory as an autoletic object to be recycled and reworked in idiosyncratic and playful ways. In the book, I proffer that cultural memory should be understood not as a “thing” to be recalled or evoked in the service of meaning-making, but rather as a social force of mediation. By tracing the poetics of pop nostalgia across its various social registers—from the particulars of musical style and live music performance to broader questions of cultural production and the formations of genre and scene—the book will show that cultural memory is more complex than the mere interplay of past and present in contemporary life, but should be understood as a dynamic force that mediates all aspects of the production and consumption of popular music. As I argue, the overemphasis on representations of identity and place in nostalgic forms of popular culture often tends to neglect the somatic and affective dimensions of musical experience, and thus we need new ways to approach the pleasurable aspects of cultural memory as embedded in and constitutive of the broader social processes that are generative of contemporary popular culture.

27613416.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27613416.value: The research conducted with the support of the Early Career Scheme grant has directly led to my next major research project, which will focus on the practice of reissuing “lost” or “obscure” popular music recordings through the production of anthology compilation albums. The anthology compilation album is a unique form of popular music media that has been mostly overlooked in popular music scholarship. This research will explore the curatorial aesthetics of producing anthology compilations, and the role of these compilations in the cultural production of alternative and underground popular music cultures. I plan to examine this media culture through the lens of a particular anthology compilation album called "Nuggets: Original Artyfacts from the First Psychedelic Era, 1965-1968", which has been especially influential in rock music history. This project has emerged from my research on garage rock due to the fact that amateur historians and archivists played a key role in the emergence of garage rock as a unique genre.

27613616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613616.value: The new set of Sustainable Development Goals by the United Nations clearly recognizes the importance of modern energy in poverty reduction, particularly the seventh goal concerning energy access. The fastest way to help developing countries make the energy transition is to transfer adequate technologies. Although many public reports from governments and international agencies emphasize the need for such transition, scholarly works on how to facilitate it have just begun to accumulate. Motivated by PI’s prior work (Kim et al., 2013), the proposed research will explore foreign aid as a way to enhance recipients’ energy capacity and make the energy transition. By emphasizing capacity, the research will focus on variations in foreign aid contracts in terms of different types of donors: bilateral contracts and multilateral contracts. I will attempt to validate the link between aid contracts and recipients’ perceived degree of ownership, and examine how variations in contract structures affect capacity-building. I will conduct cross-country analysis to model the link between aid ownership and capacity building. Given the rare focus on energy aid, studies on capacity-building largely focus on individual cases. Although case studies present rich information on individual settings, simplifying the aforementioned link will enhance scholarly understanding of an important determinant of capacity-building. In order to validate the outcome, a meta-evaluation on project evaluation studies will also be conducted. This research will contribute to the aid literature by filling the gap on aid disaggregation with respect to sector-specific and donor-type analyses. It will also contribute to the technology transfer literature by demonstrating foreign aid as an effective transfer mechanism for small developing countries. The outcome of the analyses will have important implications for the aid community in terms of future aid design in the energy sector, as well as insight into the true impact of recipients’ ownership arrangements. With the rise of multiple climate change-related multilateral funds, the outcome of the proposed research will also shed light on aid contract structures. The research will also analyze the stages of recipient ownership in aid projects as recipients progress toward graduating from the aid recipient community. 27613716.label: Project Objectives
27613716.value: To demonstrate that the emergence of modern Japanese literature was not the result of a clear-cut historical break, brought about by the influx of Western ideas, discourses and translations in the Meiji period, but also relates back to discourses and narrative practices in the early modern period (Edo period). To investigate the continuous significance of the writing of emotions and desires in the production of literature in Japan from the early 19th to the early 20th century. To examine how notions of emotionality and desire – such as the traditional concept of “human feeling” (ninjô) – shaped major 19th century literary genres. For example, what was the continuity between late Edo-period yomihon (“books for reading”) or ninjôbon (“books of human feeling”) and the Meiji-period novel (shôsetsu)? To explore how emotions and desires, in particular sexual desire, are represented as a potentially excessive and dangerous force in 19th century Japanese literary texts. What narrative strategies or plot and gender dynamics did texts use to negotiate that force? To shed new light on 19th century discussions about the socio-cultural and political significance of narrative fiction, for instance as a didactic tool or, in the Meiji period, as a medium able to advance the nation toward civilization and enlightenment. To investigate how Japanese texts from the late-Edo to the Meiji period reflect and dramatize the ambiguity of literature as a medium that represents potentially dangerous emotions while simultaneously claiming social and political significance. How did these textual negotiations over the meaning and function of literary writing shape the formation of literary modernity in 19th century Japan? To offer a case study to rethink the specific temporality of modernity in Japan and East Asia, as well as to resituate the study of 19th century Japanese literature and culture within the burgeoning scholarship on emotionality as a dominant paradigm in modern (global) culture.

27613716.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27613716.value: The primary aim of this project is to investigate the significance of the writing of emotions and desires in the production of literature in Japan from the early 19th to the early 20th century. The massive influx of new Western ideas about literature and translations in the Meiji period (1868-1912) has been generally seen as the key factor for bringing about the formation of modern literature in Japan. This study, however, will challenge this view and demonstrate that literature in Japan was continuously defined by notions of emotionality and desire – such as the traditional concept of “human feeling” (ninjô) – from the early modern period (Edo period, 1600-1868) well into the Meiji period. How did notions of emotionality and desire shape major narrative genres in 19th century Japan? One of the fundamental goals of this project is to provide a radically new understanding of the formation of modern literature in 19th century Japan. Many studies still view the decade of the 1880s as the moment of a radical historical break that brought about the emergence of literary modernity. Drawing on a broad variety of contemporary critical discourses and literary texts (including late Edo-period narrative fiction and Meiji-period novels) my study will investigate the hitherto unexamined continuities in the production of literature in Japan throughout the 19th century. I will highlight how the writing of morally problematic emotions and desires, for instance erotic desire, continuously shaped literary texts as well as the notion of literature itself across the Edo-Meiji transition. This approach will allow me to fundamentally retheorize the nature of literary-historical change from the early modern to the modern period in Japan. I expect the outcome of this project, when published as a monograph, to be a contribution that will transform the field of Japanese literary studies. Moreover, my study will be an intervention in the recently expanding scholarly field that investigates the significance of emotions for the production of modern culture and modernity in East Asia and beyond. This will also be the first major research project on pre-20th century Japanese literature and culture to be conducted in Hong Kong.

I also disseminated my findings through numerous international conference presentations and invited lectures at major universities in the US, Asia, and Europe. To achieve my project objectives with my ECS funding, I engaged in in-depth archival research at relevant research libraries in Japan and the US, such as Waseda University Library and Harvard University Library. 27613716.label: Major findings and research outcome
27613716.value: Research outcome: - 1 single-authored monograph published by Columbia University Press (2020) - 3 single-authored articles in top-tier peer-reviewed journals: Monumenta Nipponica (2018), Japanese Language and Literature (2019); and Japan Forum (2021). - numerous international conference presentations and invited talks at major institutions in the US, Asia, and Europe, including Harvard University, Oxford University, the KU Leuven, and HKU. Major research findings: Through my research, I have been able to demonstrate that nineteenth-century Japanese critical discourse and literary practice, across the early modern-modern divide or the transition from the Edo (1600–1868) to the Meiji period (1868–1912), was continuously marked by a strong concern with potentially transgressive emotions and desire. I demonstrate how notions such as ninjō (human emotion)—a key term referring to love and sexual desire—were at the core of critical discourses surrounding literature in Japan. These discourses shaped the narrative dynamics in such genres as the early nineteenth-century ninjōbon (books of human emotion) and yomihon (books for reading) as well as the Meiji-period novel, influenced by Western models of fiction. My research has provided a radically new perspective on the emergence of literary modernity in Japan in the nineteenth century and it has highlighted the crucial significance of emotion as a critical category shaping literary narratives and the understanding of literature in Japan. My findings have been pathbreaking in the field of Japanese literary studies, as they bridge the still prevalent academic divide between early modern and modern studies and showcase key continuities that warrant a more integrative perspective on this crucial period of transition. At the same time, my research findings provide an important case study to rethink the significance of emotion and modernity in a unique nineteenth-century framework that sheds new lights on the more thoroughly studied developments in the twentieth century, thus providing an important comparative lens to rethink the temporality of modernity in other East Asian literatures and beyond.

My research has provided fundamentally new impulses to develop an integrated critical field of nineteenth-century studies in Japan. I envision further research building on my work studying, for instance, the important continuities between Edo- and Meiji-period narrative genres with regard to representation, emotion, institutional frameworks, etc. This further expanding research field will fundamentally alter conceptualizations of Japanese literary modernity in the Meiji period and well into the twentieth century. - research on emotion and modernity. The history of emotion is a newly expanding academic field. I envision my work to stimulate new research that will investigate how traditional notions of emotion and desire—such as the Japanese concept of ninjō (human emotion)—complicate narratives of a global modernity that have hitherto been largely dominated by a Euro-American critical framework.

27613716.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27613716.value: My research project is the first to have brought to light the significance of critical concepts of emotion and desire, such as ninjō (literally "human emotion," but more specifically love and sexual desire), in continuously shaping narrative fiction and the novel in nineteenth-century Japan. The project has been pathbreaking in bridging the artificial academic divide between early modern (Edo) and modern (Meiji) studies and in also highlighting important continuities with Chinese literary discourse and fiction. Against previous scholarly narratives that have emphasized emotional interiority and individualism, the publications arising out of my research have fundamentally reassessed the role of emotion for the emergence of literary modernity in Japan. Providing context and close textual analysis for innumerable writings, literary and non-literary, produced from the seventeenth to the early twentieth century, my publications demonstrate how traditional concepts such as ninjō (human emotion) continuously shaped literary practice in Japan, even after the influx of new Western ideas of literature and emotion. My project thus constitutes a valuable case study to rethink the interplay of critical categories such as literature, emotion, and modernity not only in Japan, but also in other East-Asian and non-Western historical contexts more broadly.

27615616.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27615616.value: This research project examines how new ways of thinking about epidemics shaped Japanese understandings and treatments of disease during the 18th and 19th centuries. This period of Japanese medical history is generally recognized as one of rapid changes in ideas and practices, but the origins of this innovation are often attributed to the early stages of the importation of European medicine. By taking a fresh look at how Japanese doctors and the broader Japanese public understood the nature of epidemics in this period, I will show how styles of medical thought derived from China remained a vital part of Japanese medical practice well into the 19th century, providing important sources of new medical thinking and innovative responses to disease. This project will use a combination of qualitative and quantitative analyses to examine how new medical ideas about epidemics imported from China and Europe or originating within Japan developed and spread through networks of medical practitioners as they tried to find ways to respond to the challenges posed by new diseases they encountered in practice. By studying these doctors writings on the topic of epidemics and interpreting them in the context of local historical circumstances, it will reveal the wide variety of social groups involved in responding to epidemics, collecting and distributing information about their characteristics and about appropriate methods of treatment, and contributing to the provision of medical care. Besides elucidating the specific history of Japanese responses to epidemics in the 18th and 19th centuries, this research will contribute to a better understanding of the history of medical innovation in comparative perspective. The significance of epidemic diseases for stimulating new ways of thinking about the body and disease in Europe and its colonies since the late medieval period are widely recognized, but the importance of epidemics as focal points for medical debate and innovation has only recently begun to attract the attention of historians studying East Asian contexts. 日本江戶時代中後期（18-19世紀）是醫療具有豐富創新的一個時代。一般認為這個時期的醫學發展是所謂「蘭學家」將荷蘭文醫籍翻成日文而推廣西方醫學知識所導致，但其實是「蘭學」只是當時日本醫療創新的一方面。此研究計畫檢視當時日本醫生關於疫病的新理論如何形塑了他們對於醫療創新的態度，而且解釋當時傳統東亞醫學如何能夠面對新的流行病。

Because of these problems, the PI has reoriented towards greater use of digitally available resources, developing software tools to scrape bibliographic data from online library catalogues and digital images of early modern Japanese books where these are available. This shift in methodology has been made possible by the rapid growth of support in Japan for digitization projects and the standardization of digital image repositories searchable through the portal website of the National Institute of Japanese Literature (NIJL). Achieved milestones in this aspect of the project include the following: (1) Transcription of nine sets of book catalogue records (shojaku mokuroku 書籍目録) published during the period 1670–1699, containing 3433 total records. Together, these catalogues present a comprehensive view of the growing number of medical books available in Japan, from 183 books listed in the earliest catalogue (ca. 1670) to 578 books listed in the largest catalogue (1692). Further analysis of these catalogues will resolve ambiguities in the title listings and clarify the authorship and composition dates, serving as the basis for a quantitative analysis. - Compilation and preliminary analysis of a reference title database of printed medical works listed in the NIJL database. This reference database, composed primarily of books by Japanese authors includes 1271 unique titles. Further analysis will integrate this list with the Chinese titles previously catalogued by Kosoto Hiroshi (1999). - Compilation of publishers' advertisements for medical books (zōhan mokuroku 蔵版目録) from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century.
